002bf0720404e5dc6bf43eff64f116ec755b405f.title: SciMON: Scientific Inspiration Machines Optimized for Novelty
002bf0720404e5dc6bf43eff64f116ec755b405f.research_question: Can neural language models generate novel scientific directions grounded in literature, moving beyond traditional binary link prediction to produce expressive, contextually rich hypotheses? How can the generation of scientific ideas be systematically optimized for novelty while maintaining relevance to existing literature?
002bf0720404e5dc6bf43eff64f116ec755b405f.hypothesis: Explicitly grounding language model outputs in retrieved inspirations from past scientific literature and iteratively optimizing for novelty will enable the generation of more novel, relevant, and technically detailed scientific ideas compared to standard language model approaches.
002bf0720404e5dc6bf43eff64f116ec755b405f.proposed_method: A modeling framework, SCIMON, is proposed to generate novel scientific ideas by combining literature-grounded inspiration retrieval with iterative novelty optimization. The method begins by extracting background contexts (e.g., problems, motivations, experimental settings) and salient seed terms from scientific papers using information extraction (IE) systems. For each input, the system retrieves 'inspirations'—related problems and solutions—from a large corpus using semantic similarity graphs, knowledge graphs, and citation networks. These inspirations, along with the background context, are provided to a large language model (LLM) for idea generation. To explicitly optimize for novelty, an iterative process is introduced: the generated idea is compared to prior literature using similarity metrics, and if it is found to overlap strongly with existing work, the model is prompted to revise its output to be more novel. This process repeats until a predefined novelty threshold is achieved. Additionally, a contrastive learning objective is incorporated during training to discourage copying from the input context and further boost novelty.
002bf0720404e5dc6bf43eff64f116ec755b405f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a large-scale dataset of scientific papers (e.g., 67,408 ACL Anthology papers from S2ORC for NLP/AI, and PubMed papers for biomedical domain), with data split temporally to avoid contamination. The system will be evaluated in both in-context learning (using GPT-3.5 and GPT-4) and fine-tuning setups (e.g., T5, Meditron). Baselines will include standard LLM generations, few-shot prompting, and retrieval-augmented methods. Evaluation will be performed through comprehensive human annotation by domain experts, assessing outputs for relevance, utility, novelty, and technical depth. Automated metrics (ROUGE, BERTScore, BARTScore) will also be used for supplementary analysis. Experiments will include ablation studies on the effect of inspiration retrieval sources, contrastive objectives, and iterative novelty boosting. Additional case studies will test generalization to the biomedical domain.
002bf0720404e5dc6bf43eff64f116ec755b405f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach departs from traditional literature-based discovery by generating open-ended, natural language scientific ideas rather than binary concept links, and by explicitly optimizing for novelty through iterative refinement. The framework introduces a novel combination of inspiration retrieval from multiple literature-based sources and an iterative novelty-boosting mechanism. It also presents a new in-context contrastive training objective to discourage copying and encourage genuine innovation. Comprehensive human evaluation protocols for scientific idea generation are developed, and the methodology is demonstrated to generalize across scientific domains.

00339a85aba1defcf1b3bc94f644973e897b0773.title: Learning with Explanation Constraints
00339a85aba1defcf1b3bc94f644973e897b0773.research_question: How can machine learning models be trained to incorporate a priori explanation constraints, and under what conditions do such constraints improve generalization and model performance compared to standard learning approaches?
00339a85aba1defcf1b3bc94f644973e897b0773.hypothesis: Incorporating explanation constraints into the training of machine learning models reduces the hypothesis class complexity, leading to improved generalization, higher accuracy, and better satisfaction of desired model behaviors, especially in settings with limited labeled data.
00339a85aba1defcf1b3bc94f644973e897b0773.proposed_method: A learning-theoretic framework is developed for training models with explanation constraints, formalizing explanations as functionals that impose constraints on model behavior for specific inputs. Explanation constraints are integrated into an empirical risk minimization (ERM) objective, using a surrogate loss to quantify constraint satisfaction. A variational optimization method is proposed, which alternates between minimizing supervised loss on labeled data and projecting the model onto the set of models that satisfy the explanation constraints (CEmodels). The variational objective decouples the supervised loss from the explanation constraint satisfaction, allowing for efficient optimization and the use of both labeled and unlabeled data. The method supports noisy or imperfect explanations and can be instantiated for various explanation types, such as gradient-based constraints for linear models and neural networks.
00339a85aba1defcf1b3bc94f644973e897b0773.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic tasks include regression with linear models and two-layer neural networks, where ground-truth gradients are available as explanations. Real-world tasks involve weak supervision benchmarks (e.g., YouTube and Yelp datasets), where explanations are derived from heuristic weak labelers providing noisy gradient information. Baselines for comparison include standard supervised learning, Lagrangian-regularized methods that penalize explanation constraint violations, and self-training approaches. Evaluation metrics include mean squared error (MSE) for regression, classification accuracy for real-world tasks, and the degree of satisfaction of explanation constraints (e.g., gradient matching). Experiments will systematically vary the number of labeled, unlabeled, and explanation-annotated data points to assess performance under limited supervision.
00339a85aba1defcf1b3bc94f644973e897b0773.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a formal learning-theoretic framework for learning with explanation constraints, providing generalization bounds that quantify the benefit of such constraints in terms of reduced Rademacher complexity. It develops a practical variational optimization algorithm that efficiently incorporates explanation constraints, outperforming standard Lagrangian and self-training methods. The approach supports both perfect and noisy explanations, and the theoretical analysis is instantiated for canonical explanation types, such as input gradients for linear and neural models. This work bridges the gap between explainability and learning theory, offering both theoretical guarantees and practical algorithms for explanation-constrained learning.

003ef1cd670d01af05afa0d3c72d72228f494432.title: LLM+P: Empowering Large Language Models with Optimal Planning Proficiency
003ef1cd670d01af05afa0d3c72d72228f494432.research_question: How can large language models be empowered to reliably solve complex, long-horizon planning problems specified in natural language, particularly in robotics and related domains?
003ef1cd670d01af05afa0d3c72d72228f494432.hypothesis: Integrating large language models with classical symbolic planners via a structured translation pipeline will enable the generation of correct and optimal plans for complex tasks specified in natural language, outperforming LLMs used in isolation for planning.
003ef1cd670d01af05afa0d3c72d72228f494432.proposed_method: A framework is developed that combines large language models (LLMs) with classical planning algorithms to solve planning problems described in natural language. The method first uses an LLM to translate a natural language problem description into a Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL) problem file, leveraging in-context learning by providing the LLM with example (problem, PDDL) pairs. The generated PDDL problem file, along with a fixed domain PDDL file, is then input to a classical planner (such as FAST-DOWNWARD) to compute an optimal or feasible plan. Finally, the resulting plan is translated back into natural language using the LLM, making the solution accessible and actionable for robotic agents or human users. This pipeline does not require any fine-tuning or retraining of the LLM, and is designed to be generalizable across domains where a sound and complete solver exists.
003ef1cd670d01af05afa0d3c72d72228f494432.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on seven benchmark robot planning domains (BLOCKSWORLD, BARMAN, FLOORTILE, GRIPPERS, STORAGE, TERMES, TYREWORLD), each with 20 automatically generated tasks. For each domain, a domain PDDL file and example (problem, PDDL) pairs are provided as context to the LLM. The GPT-4 model is used with deterministic settings (temperature 0) to generate PDDL files, which are then solved using the FAST-DOWNWARD planner with both optimal and sub-optimal search aliases (SEQ-OPT-FDSS-1 and LAMA), with a maximum search time of 200 seconds. Baseline comparisons include LLMs used directly for planning (LLM-AS-P), Tree of Thoughts (ToT) reasoning, and ablation studies without context. Evaluation metrics include success rate (correct/optimal plan generation), feasibility of generated plans, and performance on a real-world robot tidy-up task.
003ef1cd670d01af05afa0d3c72d72228f494432.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first framework that systematically integrates LLMs with classical planners to achieve optimal planning proficiency from natural language descriptions, without modifying or fine-tuning the LLMs. The method leverages the strengths of both LLMs (for translation and generalization) and classical planners (for correctness and optimality), enabling reliable long-horizon planning that LLMs alone cannot achieve. The framework is demonstrated to be general across diverse planning domains and is validated on both simulated benchmarks and a real-world robotic task. The approach also highlights the critical role of in-context learning for accurate translation from natural language to PDDL.

0042426b8904df6d3cfc882d1729a0bffbf25a57.title: Online Learning of Neural Networks
0042426b8904df6d3cfc882d1729a0bffbf25a57.research_question: What are the fundamental conditions and quantitative bounds that govern the online learnability of feedforward neural networks with sign activation functions, and how can these bounds be improved under additional structural or margin-based assumptions?
0042426b8904df6d3cfc882d1729a0bffbf25a57.hypothesis: Online learnability of neural networks with sign activation functions can be quantitatively characterized by geometric properties of the input space, such as the totally-separable-packing number, and improved mistake bounds can be achieved under multi-index or strong margin assumptions.
0042426b8904df6d3cfc882d1729a0bffbf25a57.proposed_method: The proposed research will develop a theoretical framework for online learning of feedforward neural networks with sign activation functions, focusing on adversarial, non-i.i.d. data streams. The approach will characterize the mistake bound in terms of the (d, γ)-totally-separable-packing number, which captures the geometric separability of the input space under margin constraints. The methodology will include constructing meta-learners using a multiclass version of the Weighted Majority algorithm, with expert classes tailored to the neural network's structure and the input sequence's properties. Additional specialized algorithms will be designed for two restricted settings: (1) the multi-index model, where the target function depends only on a low-dimensional subspace, and (2) the extended margin assumption, where all neurons in all layers classify with a margin bounded away from zero. Adaptive strategies will also be developed to handle unknown margin and model parameters.
0042426b8904df6d3cfc882d1729a0bffbf25a57.experiment_details: Theoretical analysis will be conducted to derive upper and lower mistake bounds for online learning in the general case, as well as under the multi-index and extended margin assumptions. The bounds will be expressed in terms of the totally-separable-packing number, input dimension, margin, and network depth. Lower bounds will be established by constructing adversarial input sequences and corresponding neural networks that force any learner to make a provably large number of mistakes. Comparative analysis will be performed against existing regret bounds for online neural network learning, particularly under convex and Lipschitz loss settings. The evaluation will focus on the tightness of the derived bounds, their dependence on dimension, margin, and network architecture, and their applicability to both realizable and agnostic settings. No empirical datasets are specified, as the work is primarily theoretical.
0042426b8904df6d3cfc882d1729a0bffbf25a57.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a near-complete quantitative characterization of online learnability for neural networks with sign activation functions using the totally-separable-packing number, a geometric quantity not previously central in this context. It provides the first dimension-free mistake bounds in the multi-index and extended margin settings, and develops new pruning-based analytical techniques to reduce the effective network size for learning. The approach enables adaptive online learning without prior knowledge of key parameters and extends to agnostic settings via regret bounds. The methods and bounds are novel in their explicitness, independence from input dimension in certain regimes, and applicability to non-convex 0/1 loss functions.

005173328f409ca2495aa891eaf3699973985231.title: Distribution-Aware Data Expansion with Diffusion Models
005173328f409ca2495aa891eaf3699973985231.research_question: How can data expansion for deep learning be improved to generate synthetic samples that are both highly diverse and closely aligned with the real data distribution, without requiring additional model training?
005173328f409ca2495aa891eaf3699973985231.hypothesis: A training-free data expansion framework that leverages distribution-aware diffusion models guided by hierarchical prototypes can generate synthetic data that is both diverse and distribution-consistent, leading to improved downstream model performance compared to existing transformation- and synthesis-based augmentation methods.
005173328f409ca2495aa891eaf3699973985231.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a distribution-aware data expansion framework utilizing a pre-trained diffusion model, specifically Stable Diffusion, to generate synthetic samples. The method begins by extracting instance features from the original dataset using an image encoder, then constructs hierarchical prototypes at both class and group levels via agglomerative clustering to approximate the real data distribution. During the diffusion sampling process, a residual multiplicative transformation is applied to latent features, introducing controlled stochastic perturbations. Hierarchical energy guidance is then employed at intermediate denoising steps, optimizing the latent features to minimize distributional distance to the prototypes using custom energy functions. This process ensures that generated samples maintain both high fidelity to the original distribution and increased diversity, without the need for retraining the diffusion model.
005173328f409ca2495aa891eaf3699973985231.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on six diverse image classification datasets, including Caltech-101, CIFAR100-Subset, ImageNette, Cars, DTD, and PathMNIST, covering general, fine-grained, textual, and medical imaging tasks. The proposed method is compared against traditional transformation-based augmentations (e.g., AutoAugment, RandAugment, MixUp, CutMix) and state-of-the-art synthesis-based approaches (e.g., Stable Diffusion, LECF, GIF-SD). Evaluation metrics include classification accuracy and Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) to assess both downstream model performance and distributional alignment. Models are trained from scratch or fine-tuned from strong pre-trained baselines, and ablation studies are performed to analyze the impact of hierarchical prototypes, optimization steps, and group-level prototype numbers. All experiments are repeated with multiple random seeds, and computational efficiency is measured by generation time per sample.
005173328f409ca2495aa891eaf3699973985231.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is training-free and introduces a novel distribution-aware energy guidance mechanism within the diffusion process, leveraging hierarchical prototypes to approximate the real data distribution at multiple scales. Unlike prior methods, optimization is performed at intermediate denoising steps rather than only on final outputs, leading to improved distributional alignment and diversity. The approach is compatible with existing augmentation strategies, efficient in computation, and demonstrates superior performance across datasets and model architectures. The method avoids overfitting and additional training costs associated with fine-tuning, and provides a generalizable solution for data expansion in both low-data and large-scale scenarios.

0053f9529c11a98ee907d26b062d73227195aca6.title: Smooth p-Wasserstein Distance: Structure, Empirical Approximation, and Statistical Applications
0053f9529c11a98ee907d26b062d73227195aca6.research_question: How can smoothing the p-Wasserstein distance with a Gaussian kernel improve its structural and statistical properties, particularly in terms of empirical convergence rates, and how can these improvements be leveraged for statistical applications such as two-sample testing and generative modeling in high-dimensional settings?
0053f9529c11a98ee907d26b062d73227195aca6.hypothesis: Smoothing the p-Wasserstein distance via Gaussian convolution will preserve key metric and topological properties while enabling faster, dimension-independent empirical convergence rates, thereby facilitating more efficient and robust statistical inference and learning in high dimensions.
0053f9529c11a98ee907d26b062d73227195aca6.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that defines the smooth p-Wasserstein distance W_p^(σ) by convolving input probability distributions with an isotropic Gaussian kernel of variance σ^2, then computing the standard p-Wasserstein distance between the smoothed distributions. Theoretical analysis will establish that W_p^(σ) retains the metric and topological structure of the classic W_p, is stable under perturbations of σ, and converges to W_p as σ approaches zero. A key technical component involves relating W_p^(σ) to a smooth p-th order Sobolev integral probability metric (IPM), d_p^(σ), which is shown to be efficiently computable as a maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) with an explicit reproducing kernel. The empirical convergence of W_p^(σ) will be analyzed using tools from empirical process theory applied to d_p^(σ), and limit distributions for the empirical smooth Sobolev IPM will be derived under sub-Gaussian assumptions.
0053f9529c11a98ee907d26b062d73227195aca6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted to empirically validate the theoretical claims, focusing on p = 2 for computational tractability. Synthetic datasets such as uniform and Gaussian distributions in varying dimensions will be used to estimate the convergence rate of W_2^(σ) between empirical and true distributions. The MMD formulation for d_2^(σ) will enable efficient computation of empirical convergence rates and upper bounds. Two-sample testing procedures based on the smooth Wasserstein statistic will be implemented using bootstrap-calibrated critical values, and their empirical false alarm rates will be evaluated across different dimensions and sample sizes. For generative modeling, minimum distance estimation using W_p^(σ) will be performed, and the convergence of parameter estimates will be assessed by fitting parametric models (e.g., Gaussian mixtures) to target distributions and analyzing the scaling of estimation error with sample size.
0053f9529c11a98ee907d26b062d73227195aca6.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a comprehensive theoretical and empirical analysis of the Gaussian-smoothed p-Wasserstein distance for arbitrary p ≥ 1 and dimension d, establishing for the first time that smoothing yields a parametric empirical convergence rate of n^{-1/2} independent of dimension, in contrast to the curse of dimensionality for the unsmoothed case. The method provides new limit distribution results for the empirical smooth Sobolev IPM in all dimensions, and demonstrates efficient computation via an explicit MMD formulation. Applications to two-sample testing and generative modeling are developed with provable asymptotic guarantees, extending the applicability of Wasserstein-based inference to high-dimensional and practical machine learning scenarios.

008a428e049003fe768068a0f1fa1416af5c4982.title: Masked Feature Prediction for Self-Supervised Visual Pre-Training
008a428e049003fe768068a0f1fa1416af5c4982.research_question: How can self-supervised learning methods be improved for visual pre-training, particularly for video understanding, without relying on external supervision or large-scale labeled datasets?
008a428e049003fe768068a0f1fa1416af5c4982.hypothesis: Predicting hand-crafted feature descriptors, such as Histograms of Oriented Gradients (HOG), for masked regions in visual data enables effective self-supervised pre-training of large-scale vision models, leading to improved performance on downstream video and image recognition tasks compared to previous methods that use pixel prediction, discrete tokenization, or deep network features.
008a428e049003fe768068a0f1fa1416af5c4982.proposed_method: A self-supervised pre-training framework is developed in which a vision Transformer backbone processes visual input (video or image) with a portion of the input randomly masked out. The model is tasked with regressing feature representations of the masked regions, where the features are extracted from the original, unmasked data. Five types of target features are considered: pixel colors, HOG descriptors, discrete tokens from a dVAE, deep network features (from self-supervised or supervised models), and pseudo-labels. The approach primarily focuses on HOG as the prediction target due to its balance of performance and efficiency. Masking is performed on space-time cubes for videos or spatial patches for images, and the model is trained to minimize the L2 loss between predicted and target features for the masked regions. The method is scalable to both image and video domains and is compatible with minimal data augmentation.
008a428e049003fe768068a0f1fa1416af5c4982.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on large-scale video datasets (Kinetics-400, Kinetics-600, Kinetics-700) and image datasets (ImageNet-1K) using MViT and ViT architectures. The pre-training protocol involves masking 40% of input patches or cubes and using cube masking for videos. Baselines include training from scratch, supervised pre-training on large labeled datasets (e.g., IN-21K, JFT-300M), and previous self-supervised methods such as BEiT, DINO, and MoCo. Evaluation metrics include top-1 and top-5 accuracy for classification tasks, mean Average Precision (mAP) for action detection (AVA), and top-1 accuracy for human-object interaction classification (SSv2). Fine-tuning is performed on downstream tasks, with ablations on masking strategies, masking ratios, feature targets, and pre-training schedules.
008a428e049003fe768068a0f1fa1416af5c4982.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces masked feature prediction using hand-crafted descriptors, specifically HOG, as a simple and effective self-supervised pre-training objective that does not require external tokenizers or additional model weights. This method demonstrates that continuous feature regression is sufficient for masked visual prediction, outperforming pixel prediction and discrete tokenization. The approach achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple video and image benchmarks without external supervision, scales efficiently to large models and datasets, and generalizes across both video and image domains. The findings highlight the importance of local contrast normalization and show that strong performance can be achieved with minimal augmentation and computational overhead.

008a858ed75c50af068709c77c273ea98ea51fe4.title: DOPL: Direct Online Preference Learning for Restless Bandits with Preference Feedback
008a858ed75c50af068709c77c273ea98ea51fe4.research_question: Can efficient reinforcement learning algorithms be developed for restless multi-armed bandit problems when only preference (pairwise comparison) feedback is available, rather than scalar rewards, and can such algorithms achieve sublinear regret under online learning constraints?
008a858ed75c50af068709c77c273ea98ea51fe4.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a direct online preference learning approach can be designed for restless bandit problems with preference feedback, enabling efficient exploration and decision-making while achieving sublinear regret, despite the reduced information content of preference signals compared to scalar rewards.
008a858ed75c50af068709c77c273ea98ea51fe4.proposed_method: A new episodic reinforcement learning algorithm, Direct Online Preference Learning (DOPL), will be developed for restless multi-armed bandits with preference feedback (PREF-RMAB). The method will maintain confidence sets for unknown transition functions using empirical counts and the Hoeffding inequality, and will estimate preferences between arms using a Bradley-Terry model based on observed pairwise comparisons. A novel preference inference mechanism will be introduced to infer unobserved preferences via transitivity, reducing the number of required comparisons per epoch from O(B^2) to B-1. The algorithm will further encourage exploration by overestimating preferences using confidence intervals. For decision-making, a low-complexity direct index policy will be constructed by solving a linear programming relaxation in terms of occupancy measures and preference feedback, ensuring the instantaneous activation constraint is satisfied at each decision epoch.
008a858ed75c50af068709c77c273ea98ea51fe4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world environments. The synthetic environment, AppMarketing, simulates user engagement and retention dynamics. Real-world applications include CPAP therapy for sleep apnea patient adherence and the ARMMAN maternal healthcare intervention. Baselines for comparison will include an oracle (optimal index policy with full information), several maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) based algorithms (MLE_WIBQL, MLE_LP, MLE_QWIC) that estimate rewards from preference data and apply standard RL algorithms, and a random activation policy. Evaluation metrics will include episodic reward and cumulative regret, with a focus on demonstrating sublinear regret and computational efficiency. The experimental setup will track latent rewards and use the same preference feedback model for all algorithms.
008a858ed75c50af068709c77c273ea98ea51fe4.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first formal framework and algorithm for online restless multi-armed bandits with preference feedback (PREF-RMAB), rather than scalar rewards. The DOPL algorithm is novel in its direct use of online preference learning, its efficient preference inference mechanism that reduces comparison complexity, and its direct index policy based on preference feedback. Theoretical analysis provides the first sublinear regret guarantee for this setting, matching the regret order of standard RMABs despite the harder feedback model. The approach eliminates the need for explicit reward modeling and demonstrates significant computational and empirical advantages over existing methods that rely on reward estimation from preferences.

008c9dd5d978808aa6ec218b4de7c3b2540f6049.title: A parallel rank-adaptive integrator for dynamical low-rank approximation
008c9dd5d978808aa6ec218b4de7c3b2540f6049.research_question: How can a parallel and rank-adaptive integrator be developed to improve the efficiency and robustness of dynamical low-rank approximation for large matrix differential equations, particularly in the presence of small singular values and high curvature of the low-rank manifold?
008c9dd5d978808aa6ec218b4de7c3b2540f6049.hypothesis: A parallel, rank-adaptive integrator that solves all arising differential equations for basis and coefficients in parallel, and incorporates a robust step rejection strategy, will achieve comparable or superior accuracy and robustness to existing methods (such as the BUG and projector-splitting integrators) while significantly reducing computational cost and maintaining error bounds insensitive to small singular values.
008c9dd5d978808aa6ec218b4de7c3b2540f6049.proposed_method: A novel matrix integrator will be constructed for dynamical low-rank approximation, enabling both the basis updates and Galerkin coefficient updates to be computed in parallel. The method will start from a factored low-rank matrix and, at each time step, simultaneously integrate matrix differential equations for the left and right basis matrices (K-step and L-step) and for the coefficient matrix (S-step). The augmented basis matrices will be constructed via QR decompositions, and the coefficient matrix will be assembled from the results of the parallel steps. After each step, a singular value decomposition (SVD) will be performed, and the rank will be adaptively truncated according to a user-specified tolerance. A step rejection strategy will be employed, based on the norm of the normal component of the vector field with respect to the tangent space, to ensure robustness and accuracy, especially in cases where the required rank increases steeply or the normal component is not sufficiently small. The method will avoid the costly sequential update of large augmented coefficient matrices required by previous approaches, instead relying on parallel r×r Galerkin steps and efficient error control.
008c9dd5d978808aa6ec218b4de7c3b2540f6049.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on benchmark problems from radiative transfer and radiation therapy, including the plane-source and line-source test cases. The radiative transfer equation will be discretized in space and angle, resulting in large matrix ODEs, and the proposed integrator will be applied to these systems. The performance of the parallel integrator will be compared against the rank-adaptive BUG integrator, with both methods evaluated in terms of solution quality, rank evolution, computational runtime, and robustness to small singular values. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy of the scalar flux, rank adaptivity, and computational efficiency (measured in runtime). Tolerance parameters for rank truncation and step rejection will be systematically varied, and the impact on both accuracy and computational cost will be assessed. The experiments will utilize large-scale discretizations (e.g., 1000 spatial cells, 500 angular moments) to demonstrate scalability and efficiency.
008c9dd5d978808aa6ec218b4de7c3b2540f6049.novelty_claims: The proposed integrator is the first to enable full parallelization of all differential equations arising in rank-adaptive dynamical low-rank approximation, eliminating the need for costly sequential coefficient updates with augmented bases. The method introduces a new step rejection strategy that efficiently controls low-rank error and enhances robustness, particularly in challenging regimes with small singular values or rapidly increasing rank requirements. The integrator maintains robust error bounds comparable to the best existing methods while achieving significant computational speedup. The approach is expected to generalize to tensor decompositions, offering potential for further computational gains in higher-dimensional problems.

0095acc4f2c3255cf38fdf844003c97858adb418.title: OUTFOX: LLM-generated Essay Detection through In-context Learning with Adversarially Generated Examples
0095acc4f2c3255cf38fdf844003c97858adb418.research_question: How can the robustness of detectors for identifying LLM-generated essays be improved, particularly against adversarial attacks that adapt to the detector's outputs, and how can such detectors maintain high performance on both attacked and non-attacked texts?
0095acc4f2c3255cf38fdf844003c97858adb418.hypothesis: Jointly training or prompting both the detector and the adversarial attacker to consider each other's outputs in an in-context learning framework will significantly improve the robustness and accuracy of LLM-generated essay detection, even under strong adversarial attacks, without sacrificing performance on non-attacked texts.
0095acc4f2c3255cf38fdf844003c97858adb418.proposed_method: A novel adversarial in-context learning framework, OUTFOX, is proposed to enhance the detection of LLM-generated essays. In this framework, both the detector and the attacker leverage each other's outputs as in-context examples within their respective prompts. The detector uses a mixture of human-written, standard LLM-generated, and adversarially generated essays as labeled examples to improve its classification capabilities. The attacker, in turn, generates essays specifically designed to evade the detector by conditioning on the detector's predictions and examples. Both components operate in a few-shot, prompt-based manner using large language models (e.g., ChatGPT) without parameter updates, relying solely on in-context learning. The process involves retrieving semantically similar essay prompts and essays, constructing input prompts with labeled examples, and iteratively generating adversarial essays and updating detection prompts to simulate a realistic arms race between attacker and detector.
0095acc4f2c3255cf38fdf844003c97858adb418.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in the domain of student essay writing, using a newly constructed dataset containing 15,400 triplets of essay problem statements, native student-written essays, and LLM-generated essays. The dataset will be split into train, validation, and test sets (14,400/500/500). The evaluation will focus on both non-attacked and adversarially attacked essays, with attacks generated by both the proposed OUTFOX attacker and a strong paraphrasing baseline (DIPPER). Detection baselines will include statistical outlier methods (e.g., entropy, log probability, DetectGPT), supervised classifiers (e.g., RoBERTa-based classifiers, HC3 detector), and the proposed OUTFOX detector. Evaluation metrics will include F1-score, HumanRec, MachineRec, and AvgRec, with thresholds determined on the validation set. The robustness of the detector will be assessed by its performance on both attacked and non-attacked test essays, and semantic similarity analyses will be performed using BERT-based embeddings.
0095acc4f2c3255cf38fdf844003c97858adb418.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to enable both the detector and the attacker to adapt to each other's outputs via in-context learning without parameter updates, simulating a realistic adversarial setting. The OUTFOX attacker generates adversarial essays that are semantically closer to human-written texts than standard LLM outputs, making detection more challenging. The OUTFOX detector achieves state-of-the-art detection performance on both attacked and non-attacked essays, with significant improvements in robustness against strong attacks compared to prior methods. The framework demonstrates that considering adversarial attacks in training or prompting does not degrade, and may even improve, performance on standard (non-attacked) texts. The approach is model-agnostic and can be extended to other domains such as fake news or academic paper generation.

00961426bef856073e7a57d785883b1b0a2f6050.title: Packed-Ensembles for Efficient Uncertainty Estimation
00961426bef856073e7a57d785883b1b0a2f6050.research_question: How can uncertainty estimation in deep neural networks be made more computationally efficient, while preserving or improving predictive accuracy, calibration, out-of-distribution detection, and robustness to distribution shifts, particularly under hardware and memory constraints?
00961426bef856073e7a57d785883b1b0a2f6050.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a novel ensemble architecture leveraging grouped convolutions to create multiple independent subnetworks within a single neural network can achieve uncertainty estimation and predictive performance comparable to traditional Deep Ensembles, but with significantly reduced computational and memory costs.
00961426bef856073e7a57d785883b1b0a2f6050.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces an ensemble framework termed Packed-Ensembles, which constructs multiple independent subnetworks within a single neural network by employing grouped convolutions. Each subnetwork operates on a distinct subset of the encoding space, with independence enforced by non-shared parameters and group-specific convolutional masks. The architecture is parameterized by three hyperparameters: the number of subnetworks (M), an expansion factor (α) that scales the width of the encoding dimension to compensate for reduced subnetwork capacity, and the number of subgroups per subnetwork (γ) to control sparsity. The method ensures that subnetworks are trained in parallel, leveraging GPU acceleration and mixed-precision computation for efficiency. During inference, predictions from all subnetworks are averaged to produce the final output, closely mimicking the behavior of traditional Deep Ensembles.
00961426bef856073e7a57d785883b1b0a2f6050.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification benchmarks including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet, using architectures such as ResNet-18, ResNet-50, and WideResNet-28-10. The method will be compared against baselines including Deep Ensembles, BatchEnsemble, MIMO, Masksembles, and single-model baselines. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, negative log-likelihood (NLL), expected calibration error (ECE), area under the precision-recall curve (AUPR), area under the ROC curve (AUC), and false positive rate at 95% recall (FPR95) for out-of-distribution (OOD) detection. OOD datasets such as SVHN (for CIFAR), ImageNet-O, and Texture (for ImageNet) will be used, and robustness to distribution shift will be assessed using ImageNet-R. Hyperparameters will be tuned for trade-offs between computational cost and performance, and ablation studies will be performed to analyze the impact of the method's parameters.
00961426bef856073e7a57d785883b1b0a2f6050.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new ensemble framework that leverages grouped convolutions to efficiently create and train multiple independent subnetworks within a single neural network, enabling parallelization and significant reductions in memory and computational requirements. This method preserves the diversity and uncertainty estimation properties of traditional Deep Ensembles, while offering flexible trade-offs between accuracy and resource usage. The approach is claimed to achieve state-of-the-art uncertainty quantification and predictive performance with lower computational cost, and provides a formalization of structured sparsity for deep ensembles. Additional contributions include a thorough analysis of the method's properties (diversity, sparsity, stability), extensive empirical validation, and an open-source implementation.

00a8081f3c03b38146dd742e344f08c371c15044.title: SPARTA ALIGNMENT: Collectively Aligning Multiple Language Models through Combat
00a8081f3c03b38146dd742e344f08c371c15044.research_question: How can the collective alignment of multiple large language models (LLMs) through competitive and collaborative mechanisms improve model alignment, generalization, and output diversity compared to single-model self-alignment approaches?
00a8081f3c03b38146dd742e344f08c371c15044.hypothesis: Collectively aligning multiple LLMs via a competitive, game-theoretic framework—where models generate, judge, and learn from each other's outputs—will yield superior alignment, greater generalization to unseen tasks, and enhanced output diversity compared to single-model self-alignment methods.
00a8081f3c03b38146dd742e344f08c371c15044.proposed_method: A novel algorithm, SPARTA ALIGNMENT, will be developed to collectively align a pool of LLMs through iterative competitive and collaborative processes. In each iteration, a prompt is sampled and two models are selected for a head-to-head 'combat', generating responses to the prompt. The remaining models in the pool act as judges, evaluating the responses and assigning scores. These scores are aggregated using a reputation-weighted scheme, where each judge's influence is proportional to its dynamically updated reputation. The outcome of each combat is used to update the reputation scores of the competing models, rewarding winners and penalizing losers, and to generate preference pairs for preference learning. At the end of each iteration, all models are fine-tuned using Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) based on the accumulated preference pairs, enabling iterative self-evolution and collective improvement of the model pool.
00a8081f3c03b38146dd742e344f08c371c15044.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a pool of 10 Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct models, each independently fine-tuned on different data domains to ensure diversity. The evaluation will span 12 datasets across 8 tasks, including domain-specific QA (MedQA-US, Normad), reasoning (GSM8K, Knowledge Crosswords, COM2, MATH), instruction following (Alpaca), and safety (TruthfulQA). Baselines will include the best initial model, SELF-REWARD, META-REWARD, SPIN, and SPPO, representing state-of-the-art self-alignment and self-play methods. Evaluation metrics will be task-specific: pass@1 accuracy for discrete and mathematical tasks, LLM-as-a-Judge scores for open-ended generation, and log-probability-based metrics for safety. Experiments will also analyze the effects of model pool size and diversity, and ablation studies will assess the impact of each algorithmic component.
00a8081f3c03b38146dd742e344f08c371c15044.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a game-theoretic, multi-agent alignment framework that leverages both competition and collaboration among diverse LLMs, moving beyond single-model self-alignment. Key innovations include a dynamic reputation system for judge weighting, a probabilistic match-making strategy to encourage meaningful and diverse pairings, and the use of cross-model preference learning. The method enables unsupervised, scalable, and robust alignment without reliance on external reward models or human annotations, and demonstrates improved generalization, output diversity, and alignment effectiveness across a wide range of tasks.

00c85c78a67dceb33621e36adef08b5d05c5251d.title: On the Reliability of Watermarks for Large Language Models
00c85c78a67dceb33621e36adef08b5d05c5251d.research_question: How reliable are watermarking techniques for detecting machine-generated text from large language models in realistic, adversarial, and mixed-content scenarios, including paraphrasing by humans or other models and insertion into larger human-written documents?
00c85c78a67dceb33621e36adef08b5d05c5251d.hypothesis: Watermarks embedded in machine-generated text remain reliably detectable under a wide range of realistic modifications, including paraphrasing by humans or other language models and mixing with human-written content, provided that a sufficient quantity of text is available for analysis.
00c85c78a67dceb33621e36adef08b5d05c5251d.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation will be conducted on the robustness of combinatorial watermarking schemes for large language models, focusing on both the watermark generation and detection pipelines. The watermarking method will involve seeding a pseudo-random function with a context window of preceding tokens to generate a 'greenlist' of favored tokens, then biasing the model's output logits to favor these tokens during generation. Several parameterizations will be explored, including different context widths and hashing schemes (e.g., LeftHash, SelfHash), and detection will be performed using both global and windowed z-score tests (WinMax) to identify watermarked regions, even when embedded in larger documents. The method will be tested against a variety of attacks, including strong machine paraphrasing, human paraphrasing, and copy-paste scenarios, to assess detection reliability as a function of observed token count.
00c85c78a67dceb33621e36adef08b5d05c5251d.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize the Colossal Common Crawl Cleaned corpus (C4) for open-ended prompt generation and the Long-Form Question Answering (LFQA) dataset for human paraphrasing studies. Watermarked text will be generated using state-of-the-art models such as Llama-7B and Vicuna. Attacks will include paraphrasing by GPT-3.5-turbo, the Dipper paraphrasing model, and human volunteers incentivized to remove watermarks, as well as synthetic copy-paste attacks embedding watermarked spans into human-written documents. Baselines will include post-hoc statistical detectors (DetectGPT), retrieval-based detection, and adversarially trained classifiers (RADAR). Evaluation will be based on ROC-AUC, true positive rates at low false positive rates, and detection performance as a function of token count, with experiments carefully controlling for sequence length and including over 500 positive and negative samples per setting.
00c85c78a67dceb33621e36adef08b5d05c5251d.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a systematic, empirical evaluation of watermark reliability under realistic adversarial conditions, including strong human and machine paraphrasing and mixed-content scenarios. It proposes novel detection enhancements such as the WinMax windowed z-score test for identifying short spans of watermarked text within larger documents. The study will provide the first comprehensive comparison of watermarking against state-of-the-art detection paradigms (retrieval, loss-based, and adversarial classifiers) in terms of sample complexity and robustness to attacks, establishing watermarking as the most reliable approach for in-the-wild detection of machine-generated text.

00e18c603e60d861c4e99c541e4d65ef442d5945.title: LLM in a flash: Efficient Large Language Model Inference with Limited Memory
00e18c603e60d861c4e99c541e4d65ef442d5945.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be efficiently run for inference on devices with limited DRAM capacity, particularly when the model size exceeds available memory, by leveraging flash memory and hardware-aware algorithmic optimizations?
00e18c603e60d861c4e99c541e4d65ef442d5945.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by storing LLM parameters in flash memory and employing hardware-informed strategies to minimize data transfer and maximize throughput, it is possible to enable efficient inference of models larger than available DRAM, with significant reductions in latency and memory usage compared to naive loading approaches.
00e18c603e60d861c4e99c541e4d65ef442d5945.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a hardware-aware framework for LLM inference where model parameters are stored in flash memory and selectively loaded into DRAM on demand. An inference cost model is constructed to account for flash memory characteristics, guiding optimizations in two main areas: (1) reducing the volume of data transferred from flash by leveraging activation sparsity and a low-rank predictor to identify and load only the necessary weights for each inference step, and (2) increasing data transfer throughput by reading larger, more contiguous chunks from flash, using techniques such as row-column bundling in the feed-forward network layers. A sliding window strategy is employed to cache only the most recently needed neuron weights in DRAM, incrementally loading and evicting data as new tokens are processed. Efficient memory management data structures are pre-allocated to minimize DRAM overhead and support fast insertion and deletion of neuron weights, further reducing inference latency.
00e18c603e60d861c4e99c541e4d65ef442d5945.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several LLMs, including OPT-6.7B, Falcon-7B (sparsified), Phi-2, Persimmon-8B, and Llama2-7B (sparsified), using a subset of the C4 validation dataset. The evaluation will be performed on multiple hardware configurations: Apple M1 Max and M2 Ultra (CPU and GPU/Metal), and NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU, with approximately half the model size available in DRAM or GPU memory. Baselines will include naive on-demand loading, hybrid approaches with partial model persistence, and theoretical optimal I/O scenarios. Evaluation metrics will focus on inference latency (broken down into I/O, memory management, and compute), throughput (GB/s), and memory usage. Additional analyses will include ablation studies on window size, generation length, and speculative decoding, as well as power consumption profiling.
00e18c603e60d861c4e99c541e4d65ef442d5945.novelty_claims: The proposal claims several innovations: (1) enabling efficient inference of LLMs up to twice the size of available DRAM by storing parameters in flash memory and selectively loading them on demand; (2) introducing a hardware-informed cost model to guide algorithmic optimizations specific to flash memory constraints; (3) developing the windowing technique for neuron reuse and row-column bundling to increase data transfer chunk size and throughput; (4) integrating activation sparsity and low-rank predictors for context-adaptive loading; and (5) demonstrating significant speedups (up to 4x on CPU and 20x on GPU) and memory savings over naive and hybrid baselines, paving the way for practical LLM deployment on memory-constrained devices.

00e5a1db842eed1ed7d5804d5a5eab0c552fafad.title: R2-T2: Re-Routing in Test-Time for Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts
00e5a1db842eed1ed7d5804d5a5eab0c552fafad.research_question: How can the performance and generalization of multimodal mixture-of-experts (MoE) models be improved on diverse and challenging downstream tasks, particularly by addressing suboptimal expert routing at test time without retraining base model parameters?
00e5a1db842eed1ed7d5804d5a5eab0c552fafad.hypothesis: Optimizing the routing weights of multimodal MoE models at test time, by leveraging information from similar correctly predicted samples, will significantly improve model performance and generalization on a wide range of downstream tasks without requiring any additional training of base model parameters.
00e5a1db842eed1ed7d5804d5a5eab0c552fafad.proposed_method: A novel test-time re-routing framework, R2-T2, is introduced to dynamically optimize the routing weights of multimodal MoE models for each test sample. The method utilizes a reference set of samples where the model predictions are correct, and for each new test instance, it identifies similar samples in a task embedding space. Three core strategies are proposed: (1) Neighborhood Gradient Descent (NGD), which updates routing weights by minimizing a surrogate loss computed from neighbors' outputs; (2) Kernel Regression, which estimates optimal routing weights as a kernel-weighted average of neighbors' routing weights and refines them via binary search; and (3) Mode Finding, which iteratively shifts routing weights toward the densest region in the routing weight space. All strategies operate without modifying base model parameters and are designed to be computationally efficient for inference-time deployment.
00e5a1db842eed1ed7d5804d5a5eab0c552fafad.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two recent multimodal MoE models, MoAI and MoVA, each equipped with specialized expert modules for vision-language reasoning. Evaluation will span eight challenging benchmarks across general visual understanding, knowledge-based reasoning, and optical character recognition, including MMBench, MME-P, SQA-IMG, AI2D, TextVQA, GQA, CVBench2D/3D, and PhysBench. Baselines will include the original base models and state-of-the-art vision-language models of varying parameter scales (7B, 8B, 13B, 34B). Evaluation metrics will primarily be accuracy, with specific metrics for multi-question benchmarks (e.g., MME-P's combined score). Hyperparameters will be fixed across tasks, and ablation studies will examine the impact of neighborhood selection, kernel choice, embedding models, and optimization steps. Computational efficiency will be measured in FLOPs to assess the trade-off between accuracy gains and inference cost.
00e5a1db842eed1ed7d5804d5a5eab0c552fafad.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first training-free, test-time re-routing mechanism for multimodal MoE models, enabling dynamic adaptation of expert routing weights based on local neighborhood information in a task embedding space. The approach is model-agnostic and does not require any finetuning or retraining of base model parameters, making it highly efficient and practical for deployment. Three distinct optimization strategies are developed and systematically compared, providing new insights into expert re-routing. The method is claimed to unlock significant performance improvements, allowing smaller models to match or surpass much larger vision-language models on diverse benchmarks, and to approach oracle-level routing performance without access to ground-truth labels at inference.

00e6500616920a25ecd95d0d3ad6f7764266b31b.title: Pride and Prejudice: LLM Amplifies Self-Bias in Self-Refinement
00e6500616920a25ecd95d0d3ad6f7764266b31b.research_question: How does self-bias manifest and amplify in large language models (LLMs) during iterative self-refinement and self-rewarding pipelines across multiple tasks and languages, and what strategies can effectively mitigate this bias to improve downstream performance?
00e6500616920a25ecd95d0d3ad6f7764266b31b.hypothesis: LLMs exhibit a measurable self-bias during self-refinement and self-rewarding processes, which can be amplified through iterative feedback and larger candidate pools, but this bias can be significantly reduced by increasing model size and incorporating external, accurate feedback.
00e6500616920a25ecd95d0d3ad6f7764266b31b.proposed_method: A formal definition of self-bias in LLMs will be established using two statistical measures: bias (the mean difference between LLM self-evaluation and human or reference-based evaluation) and distance skewness (the asymmetry of the distribution of these differences). The methodology involves prompting LLMs to generate initial outputs for various tasks, then iteratively refining these outputs using self-generated feedback. At each step, the LLM's self-assessment will be compared to human or high-quality automatic metrics. The process will be repeated across multiple LLM architectures, languages, and tasks. To mitigate self-bias, two interventions will be tested: (1) increasing model size and (2) replacing or supplementing self-feedback with external feedback from an oracle or reference-based model.
00e6500616920a25ecd95d0d3ad6f7764266b31b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six LLMs (GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Gemini, LLaMA2, Mixtral, DeepSeek) across three tasks: machine translation (using Flores-200 for four low/medium-resource language pairs), constrained text generation (using CommonGen Hard), and mathematical reasoning (using the MATH dataset). For evaluation, both human annotations and reference-based metrics (such as BLEURT and UniEval) will be used to establish ground truth. The iterative self-refinement process will be analyzed for bias and skewness at each step. Baselines will include self-refinement with only self-feedback, with external feedback, and with varying model sizes and sample pool sizes. Additional experiments will assess the impact of paraphrasing and sample pool size on self-bias, as well as the effect of external feedback and model scaling.
00e6500616920a25ecd95d0d3ad6f7764266b31b.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a principled, quantitative framework for defining and measuring self-bias in LLMs using bias and distance skewness statistics. It proposes the first comprehensive, cross-task, and cross-language analysis of self-bias amplification in both self-refinement and self-rewarding pipelines. The approach systematically investigates the impact of model size and external feedback on mitigating self-bias, providing actionable strategies for improving LLM self-correction and downstream performance. The work also highlights the unintended consequences of self-bias, such as false positive optimization and reduced diversity, and demonstrates that larger models and external feedback can elicit genuine self-correction.

0104949e68695546c6987dc4e457e5108eda0712.title: Sample-Efficient Learning of POMDPs with Multiple Observations In Hindsight
0104949e68695546c6987dc4e457e5108eda0712.research_question: How can sample-efficient learning be achieved in partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) when the learner receives multiple observations per latent state in hindsight, and what structural conditions on the POMDP enable such efficiency?
0104949e68695546c6987dc4e457e5108eda0712.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that providing multiple additional observations per encountered latent state in hindsight enables sample-efficient learning for broader classes of POMDPs than previously possible under standard feedback, specifically for subclasses with relaxed structural assumptions such as k-MO-revealing and distinguishable POMDPs.
0104949e68695546c6987dc4e457e5108eda0712.proposed_method: A new feedback model, termed k-MOMDP, is introduced where after each episode, the learner receives k-1 additional observations from the latent states encountered, without direct access to the latent states themselves. The methodology involves defining two new subclasses of POMDPs: (α, k)-MO-revealing POMDPs, which generalize the revealing POMDPs by requiring the augmented observation matrix to be well-conditioned, and distinguishable POMDPs, which require only that emission distributions from different latent states are separated in total variation distance. For (α, k)-MO-revealing POMDPs, the k-OMLE algorithm is proposed, adapting optimistic maximum likelihood estimation to the augmented observation setting. For distinguishable POMDPs, an Optimism with State Testing (OST) algorithm is developed, leveraging distribution testing techniques to cluster observations and infer latent state identities up to permutation, followed by model estimation and policy optimization.
0104949e68695546c6987dc4e457e5108eda0712.experiment_details: Experiments are designed to evaluate the proposed algorithms on both tabular and low-rank POMDPs under the k-MOMDP feedback model. Theoretical sample complexity guarantees are derived for both k-OMLE and OST, with detailed analysis of how the number of required samples scales with problem parameters such as the number of states, actions, observations, and the separation parameter α. Baselines for comparison include existing algorithms for standard and hindsight observable feedback models. Evaluation metrics focus on the number of samples required to achieve ε-optimal policies with high probability, and the experiments are structured to compare the efficiency of the proposed methods against prior approaches under varying structural assumptions and feedback models.
0104949e68695546c6987dc4e457e5108eda0712.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel enhanced feedback model (k-MOMDP) for POMDPs that provides multiple observations per latent state in hindsight, enabling sample-efficient learning for new, broader subclasses of POMDPs. The definition of (α, k)-MO-revealing and distinguishable POMDPs systematically relaxes previous structural requirements, expanding the set of tractably learnable POMDPs. Two new algorithms, k-OMLE and OST, are developed, with OST leveraging explicit distribution testing for sharper sample complexity. Theoretical results establish that any distinguishable POMDP can be learned efficiently under k-MOMDP feedback, and OST achieves improved sample efficiency compared to reduction-based approaches. These contributions advance the understanding of when and how POMDPs can be efficiently learned with enhanced feedback.

012639570b097f7700e3d0767336338eef84dc3d.title: Learning a Restricted Boltzmann Machine using biased Monte Carlo sampling
012639570b097f7700e3d0767336338eef84dc3d.research_question: How can the efficiency and stability of Restricted Boltzmann Machine (RBM) training and sampling be improved, particularly for low-dimensional, clustered, or multimodal datasets where standard Monte Carlo methods exhibit slow mixing and ergodicity breakdown?
012639570b097f7700e3d0767336338eef84dc3d.hypothesis: Biased Monte Carlo sampling techniques, specifically the Tethered Monte Carlo (TMC) method, will significantly accelerate mixing, improve the evaluation of trained RBMs, and enhance the quality and efficiency of both training and sample generation, especially for low-dimensional clustered datasets.
012639570b097f7700e3d0767336338eef84dc3d.proposed_method: A novel training and sampling framework for RBMs will be developed using the Tethered Monte Carlo (TMC) method. This approach introduces soft constraints on order parameters, such as projections along principal component directions, into the partition function, thereby enabling efficient exploration of multimodal or clustered configuration spaces. The TMC method will be used to sample the equilibrium distribution by running parallel simulations at fixed values of the constrained order parameter(s), reconstructing the effective potential and probability distribution via numerical integration. The negative phase of the log-likelihood gradient will be estimated by integrating TMC ensemble averages, replacing standard Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling. The method will be generalized to handle multiple order parameters and will be integrated into the stochastic gradient ascent training loop for RBMs.
012639570b097f7700e3d0767336338eef84dc3d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both artificial and real-world low-dimensional clustered datasets. Artificial datasets will include high-dimensional data with well-separated clusters aligned along one or two principal component directions, such as datasets with two or three clusters in 1000 dimensions. Real datasets will be selected to exhibit natural clustering after dimensionality reduction (e.g., genomics or protein sequence data). Baseline comparisons will include standard RBM training using Persistent Contrastive Divergence (PCD) and standard Glauber Heat-Bath MCMC sampling. Evaluation metrics will include mixing time, quality of generated samples (matching the true data distribution along principal components), log-likelihood estimation accuracy, and relaxation dynamics. The experimental setup will involve discretizing order parameter ranges, running parallel TMC simulations, and comparing the reconstructed distributions and training dynamics to those obtained with standard methods.
012639570b097f7700e3d0767336338eef84dc3d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the application of Tethered Monte Carlo sampling to RBM training and evaluation, enabling efficient sampling and gradient estimation in the presence of multimodal or clustered data distributions. The method allows for accurate recovery of the free-energy profile and probability distribution of trained RBMs, facilitating improved sample generation and model assessment. It addresses the ergodicity and mixing time limitations of standard MCMC-based training, particularly for low-dimensional clustered datasets, and provides a practical framework for integrating biased sampling into RBM learning. The approach also generalizes to multiple order parameters and demonstrates significant improvements in training speed and sample quality over traditional methods.

0127ff209c2ee559c0a68daefc3fc9f263a6941f.title: Spike-driven Transformer
0127ff209c2ee559c0a68daefc3fc9f263a6941f.research_question: Can the spike-driven paradigm of Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) be fully integrated into the Transformer architecture to achieve high task accuracy and extreme energy efficiency, making the model suitable for deployment on neuromorphic hardware?
0127ff209c2ee559c0a68daefc3fc9f263a6941f.hypothesis: A Transformer architecture that is entirely spike-driven, using only sparse addition and binary spike communication, can achieve state-of-the-art accuracy on large-scale tasks while drastically reducing energy consumption compared to both conventional Transformers and existing spiking Transformer hybrids.
0127ff209c2ee559c0a68daefc3fc9f263a6941f.proposed_method: A novel Transformer architecture is proposed in which all core computations, including self-attention and multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs), are re-designed to operate in a spike-driven manner. The key innovation is the Spike-Driven Self-Attention (SDSA) module, which replaces energy-intensive matrix multiplications, softmax, and scaling operations with element-wise masking (Hadamard product) and sparse addition, leveraging binary spike representations. All residual connections are restructured to operate between membrane potentials rather than spike outputs, ensuring that all spike tensors remain binary and that all weight-spike multiplications can be implemented as additions. The architecture employs Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) spiking neurons throughout, and patch splitting, position embedding, and classification head modules are adapted to maintain the spike-driven property. Surrogate gradient methods are used for direct training of the network.
0127ff209c2ee559c0a68daefc3fc9f263a6941f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale static image datasets such as ImageNet-1K, as well as smaller static (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100) and neuromorphic event-based datasets (CIFAR10-DVS, DVS128 Gesture). The proposed model will be compared against state-of-the-art SNNs (e.g., SEW-Res-SNN, MS-Res-SNN), spiking Transformers (e.g., SpikFormer), and conventional Transformer baselines. Evaluation metrics include top-1 classification accuracy and theoretical energy consumption, estimated via spike firing rates and operation counts. Standard data augmentation and training protocols will be followed, with ablation studies performed to assess the impact of the SDSA module and membrane shortcut design. The model will be evaluated at various network scales and input resolutions to demonstrate scalability and efficiency.
0127ff209c2ee559c0a68daefc3fc9f263a6941f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first Transformer architecture that is fully spike-driven, eliminating all multiply-and-accumulate operations in favor of sparse addition, making it highly compatible with neuromorphic hardware. The Spike-Driven Self-Attention (SDSA) module is a novel self-attention mechanism that achieves linear complexity in both token and channel dimensions and operates with negligible energy consumption. The residual connection design ensures binary spike communication throughout the network, further optimizing energy efficiency. The approach is claimed to achieve state-of-the-art accuracy in the SNN field on ImageNet-1K and other benchmarks, while reducing energy consumption by up to 87.2× compared to conventional self-attention mechanisms.

017010b941d902a467f6d329ae5e74fd67e67912.title: LLM-Pruner: On the Structural Pruning of Large Language Models
017010b941d902a467f6d329ae5e74fd67e67912.research_question: How can large language models be structurally pruned in a task-agnostic manner to reduce computational and memory requirements, while minimizing reliance on the original training data and preserving general-purpose language understanding and generation capabilities?
017010b941d902a467f6d329ae5e74fd67e67912.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a dependency-based structural pruning framework, combined with efficient importance estimation and rapid post-training using limited external data, can significantly compress large language models without substantial loss in their multi-task and generative performance.
017010b941d902a467f6d329ae5e74fd67e67912.proposed_method: A novel framework, LLM-Pruner, is proposed for task-agnostic structured pruning of large language models. The method consists of three main stages: (1) Discovery of all coupled and interdependent structures within the model by constructing a dependency graph, ensuring that pruning respects the inherent structural dependencies of the network; (2) Estimation of the importance of each group of coupled structures using both first-order (gradient-based) and second-order (Hessian-based) approximations, leveraging small, publicly available datasets or manually created samples for calibration; (3) Rapid recovery of the pruned model via low-rank adaptation (LoRA), where only a small subset of parameters are optimized using a limited external dataset, thus minimizing the data and time required for post-pruning fine-tuning. The framework automates the identification of pruning groups and importance ranking, and supports multiple aggregation strategies for group importance.
017010b941d902a467f6d329ae5e74fd67e67912.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three open-source large language models: LLaMA-7B, Vicuna-7B, and ChatGLM-6B. The evaluation will focus on zero-shot classification and generation tasks using nine datasets, including BoolQ, PIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-easy, ARC-challenge, OpenbookQA, as well as WikiText2 and PTB for perplexity analysis. Baseline comparisons will include magnitude-based pruning (L2), random pruning, and existing data-free pruning algorithms, as well as comparisons with models such as DistilBERT and StableLM-3B. The pruned models will be post-trained using approximately 50,000 samples from the Alpaca dataset, with tuning performed for only 3 hours on a single GPU. Key evaluation metrics will include zero-shot classification accuracy, perplexity, model size, memory usage, and inference latency. Ablation studies will assess the impact of different importance estimation and aggregation strategies, as well as the effect of dependency-based pruning versus independent pruning.
017010b941d902a467f6d329ae5e74fd67e67912.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to enable fully automatic, dependency-based structural pruning of large language models in a task-agnostic setting. It introduces a novel algorithm for identifying and grouping coupled structures, minimizing manual intervention. The method significantly reduces the need for the original training corpus, requiring only a small external dataset for rapid post-pruning recovery. LLM-Pruner achieves substantial model compression (e.g., 20% parameter reduction) while maintaining over 94% of the original model's performance on diverse zero-shot tasks, and completes the entire compression and recovery process in only a few hours. The approach demonstrates superior efficiency and effectiveness compared to existing pruning and distillation baselines.

017435814af0e52375306012018535a3b286cf85.title: Pareto Front-Diverse Batch Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization
017435814af0e52375306012018535a3b286cf85.research_question: How can multi-objective optimization of expensive black-box functions be performed efficiently in batch settings to discover high-quality and diverse Pareto fronts, particularly when diversity in the output space is critical?
017435814af0e52375306012018535a3b286cf85.hypothesis: A principled approach that adaptively selects acquisition functions and leverages determinantal point processes (DPPs) to select diverse batches in the output space will yield Pareto fronts that are both higher in quality and more diverse than those produced by existing batch multi-objective Bayesian optimization methods.
017435814af0e52375306012018535a3b286cf85.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a framework called Pareto front-Diverse Batch Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization (PDBO). At each iteration, PDBO builds independent Gaussian process (GP) surrogate models for each objective function and constructs a portfolio of acquisition functions (e.g., EI, UCB, TS, ID). A multi-arm bandit strategy with a discounted cumulative reward is employed to adaptively select the most promising acquisition function from the portfolio. For each acquisition function, a 'cheap' multi-objective optimization problem is solved to generate candidate Pareto sets. From each candidate set, a batch of B inputs is selected using a determinantal point process (DPP) configured as a convex combination of the GP kernels, with the combination weights fitted to maximize the likelihood of selecting points with high individual hypervolume contribution (HVC), thereby promoting diversity in the output (objective) space. The batch nominated by the selected acquisition function is then evaluated, and all model and selection parameters are updated for the next iteration.
017435814af0e52375306012018535a3b286cf85.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a suite of synthetic and real-world multi-objective optimization benchmarks, including ZDT and DTLZ series, gear train design, SWL-LVM, and UAV power system design, covering varying input and output dimensions. The method is compared against state-of-the-art batch MOO baselines such as DGEMO, qEHVI, qPAREGO, USEMO-EI, NSGA-II, and random selection. Evaluation metrics include the hypervolume indicator (for Pareto front quality) and a newly introduced Diversity of the Pareto Front (DPF) metric, which measures average pairwise distances in the output space. Experiments are repeated multiple times (e.g., 25 runs), with results reported as averages and standard deviations. Batch sizes are varied (e.g., B ∈ {2, 4, 8, 16}), and all methods are initialized with a fixed number of random evaluations. Additional ablation studies isolate the impact of adaptive acquisition function selection and DPP-based batch selection.
017435814af0e52375306012018535a3b286cf85.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to combine adaptive acquisition function selection via a multi-arm bandit with a DPP-based batch selection mechanism specifically configured for output-space diversity in multi-objective Bayesian optimization. It introduces a new metric (DPF) for quantifying Pareto front diversity in the output space, addresses the challenge of diversity beyond input space, and provides theoretical regret bounds for the adaptive selection strategy. The method is demonstrated to be effective and scalable across a range of input/output dimensions and batch sizes, outperforming prior methods in both diversity and quality of discovered Pareto fronts.

018a1db1ced37c332d58ba785d9debc1cc80d141.title: Learning in POMDPs is Sample-Efficient with Hindsight Observability
018a1db1ced37c332d58ba785d9debc1cc80d141.research_question: Can learning in partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) become sample-efficient when the true latent states are revealed to the learner in hindsight during training, and what are the fundamental sample complexity limits and algorithmic strategies for this setting?
018a1db1ced37c332d58ba785d9debc1cc80d141.hypothesis: Hindsight observability, where latent states are revealed after each episode during training, enables sample-efficient learning of near-optimal policies in POMDPs without reliance on traditional observability conditions, and achieves minimax-optimal sample complexity in terms of latent state and observation space sizes.
018a1db1ced37c332d58ba785d9debc1cc80d141.proposed_method: A novel framework, the Hindsight Observable Markov Decision Process (HOMDP), is introduced, where the learner interacts with a partially observable environment but receives the true latent states in hindsight at the end of each training episode. For finite (tabular) latent and observation spaces, a model-based algorithm called HOP-B is developed, which estimates transition and emission models using empirical counts and augments rewards with optimism-based bonuses to encourage exploration. The algorithm iteratively updates these models and computes optimistic history-dependent policies using a POMDP planner, leveraging the hindsight state information for efficient learning. For large or infinite state/observation spaces, an extension called HOP-V is proposed, which employs function approximation and version space elimination over candidate transition and emission models, combined with optimistic planning and uniform exploration to ensure generalization and sample efficiency.
018a1db1ced37c332d58ba785d9debc1cc80d141.experiment_details: Theoretical analysis is conducted to derive sample complexity and regret bounds for both the tabular (HOP-B) and function approximation (HOP-V) settings. The sample complexity is characterized in terms of the number of latent states, observations, actions, and planning horizon, with explicit upper and lower bounds established. Theoretical lower bounds are constructed using information-theoretic arguments and hard instance constructions to demonstrate minimax optimality. Evaluation metrics include PAC sample complexity guarantees (number of episodes to achieve near-optimal policy with high probability) and regret over training episodes. Comparisons are made to standard POMDP learning, MDP learning, and recent latent MDP benchmarks, with analysis of dependence on observability parameters and structural assumptions.
018a1db1ced37c332d58ba785d9debc1cc80d141.novelty_claims: The proposed HOMDP framework formalizes a practically motivated learning setting where latent states are revealed in hindsight, bridging the gap between MDPs and POMDPs. The HOP-B algorithm achieves sample complexity bounds that are independent of traditional observability parameters, relying only linearly on the number of latent states and observations, and is shown to be minimax optimal in these quantities. The HOP-V algorithm extends these results to settings with large or infinite state and observation spaces via function approximation, maintaining sample efficiency without additional structural assumptions on the emission function. The work establishes both upper and lower bounds, demonstrating that hindsight observability fundamentally alters the sample efficiency landscape for learning in partially observable environments.

01c12d59d9e3e7282514bdc75ba4f9d9b3e9fd57.title: Magnetic Preference Optimization: Achieving Last-iterate Convergence for Language Models Alignment
