01c12d59d9e3e7282514bdc75ba4f9d9b3e9fd57.research_question: How can large language models be aligned with complex, potentially non-transitive human preferences in reinforcement learning from human feedback, while ensuring efficient and robust convergence to optimal policies?
01c12d59d9e3e7282514bdc75ba4f9d9b3e9fd57.hypothesis: A novel optimization framework that achieves last-iterate convergence to the Nash equilibrium of the original preference-based game will enable more accurate and efficient alignment of large language models with diverse human preferences, overcoming the limitations of existing average-iterate or regularized approaches.
01c12d59d9e3e7282514bdc75ba4f9d9b3e9fd57.proposed_method: A new algorithm, Magnetic Preference Optimization (MPO), will be developed to achieve last-iterate convergence to the Nash equilibrium (NE) of a two-player constant-sum game modeling human preferences. The method adapts Magnetic Mirror Descent (MMD) to the RLHF setting, introducing a periodically updated 'magnet' policy that guides the optimization towards the NE of the original (unregularized) game. The approach involves iteratively solving a sequence of regularized games, updating the reference (magnet) policy at fixed intervals, and using a KL-divergence-based trust region to stabilize policy updates. The algorithm will be implemented efficiently by leveraging the symmetry of the game, requiring only a single model to be maintained and updated, and employing practical reward estimation and advantage calculation techniques suitable for large language models.
01c12d59d9e3e7282514bdc75ba4f9d9b3e9fd57.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using open-source large language models such as Gemma-2B and Llama-3-8B. The models will first undergo supervised fine-tuning on datasets like Alpaca and SFT-OpenHermes-2.5-Standard. Preference models will be trained on mixtures of open-source preference datasets, and self-play fine-tuning will be performed using prompts from datasets such as PKU-SafeRLHF, HH-Harmless, UltraFeedback, HelpSteer, OpenOrca, UltraInteract, and Capybara. Evaluation will use both cost model-based metrics and GPT-4o-based human preference comparisons for safety alignment, as well as MixEval and OpenLLMLeaderboard v2 for general capability assessment. Baselines will include supervised fine-tuning, RLHF with Bradley-Terry models, and ablations such as fixed reference policies and alternative trust region enforcement. Multiple self-play iterations will be compared, and ablation studies will assess the contribution of each algorithmic component.
01c12d59d9e3e7282514bdc75ba4f9d9b3e9fd57.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to guarantee last-iterate convergence to the Nash equilibrium of the original preference-based game in RLHF, eliminating the need for storing and averaging multiple historical policies. The method achieves linear convergence rates, significantly improving computational and storage efficiency. Unlike prior approaches that converge only to regularized games or require average-iterate solutions, this approach directly aligns a single model with true human preferences, effectively handling non-transitive and complex preference structures. The algorithm is theoretically grounded, practically efficient, and demonstrates substantial empirical improvements in both safety and general capabilities of large language models.

01c2ba3b8f3c28e1d6f67e40d0ae0e32a4ac54a3.title: Unifying Appearance Codes and Bilateral Grids for Driving Scene Gaussian Splatting
01c2ba3b8f3c28e1d6f67e40d0ae0e32a4ac54a3.research_question: How can photometric inconsistencies in multi-view, dynamic autonomous driving scenes be effectively addressed to improve both appearance fidelity and geometric accuracy in 3D scene reconstruction using neural rendering techniques?
01c2ba3b8f3c28e1d6f67e40d0ae0e32a4ac54a3.hypothesis: A multi-scale bilateral grid framework that unifies global appearance codes and localized bilateral grids will provide superior modeling capability and optimization efficiency, resulting in improved photometric consistency and geometric accuracy in dynamic driving scene reconstructions compared to existing single-scale or code-based methods.
01c2ba3b8f3c28e1d6f67e40d0ae0e32a4ac54a3.proposed_method: A novel multi-scale bilateral grid architecture is proposed to address photometric inconsistencies in dynamic driving scenes. This method constructs a hierarchical pyramid of bilateral grids at three scales: coarse (2×2×1×12), intermediate (4×4×2×12), and fine (8×8×4×12), each capturing photometric variations at different spatial granularities. The approach uses luminance-based guidance maps derived from rendered images to perform slicing operations at each grid level, retrieving affine transformation coefficients via trilinear interpolation. These transformations are hierarchically fused from coarse to fine, enabling the model to adaptively correct both global and local photometric variations. The framework is integrated into a Gaussian Splatting-based 3D scene representation, with joint optimization of appearance and geometry through a composite loss function that includes reconstruction, SSIM, depth, and regularization terms. Additional regularization, such as adaptive total variation and circle regularization loss, is employed to enhance image fidelity and prevent artifacts.
01c2ba3b8f3c28e1d6f67e40d0ae0e32a4ac54a3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four large-scale autonomous driving datasets: Waymo, NuScenes, Argoverse, and PandaSet, each featuring diverse sensor configurations and environmental conditions. The proposed method will be compared against baselines including appearance codes, standalone bilateral grids, and state-of-the-art neural rendering frameworks such as OmniRe, ChatSim, and StreetGS. Evaluation metrics will include PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS for appearance fidelity, and Chamfer Distance (CD), RMSE, and Median Squared Depth Error for geometric accuracy. All models will be trained with identical hyperparameters and hardware (NVIDIA L40 GPU), and ablation studies will assess the impact of grid scale, guidance map resolution, and loss functions. Additional experiments will test generalization by integrating the proposed module into other neural rendering pipelines and evaluating on challenging scene subsets with severe photometric inconsistencies.
01c2ba3b8f3c28e1d6f67e40d0ae0e32a4ac54a3.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified multi-scale bilateral grid framework that bridges the gap between global appearance codes and pixel-wise bilateral grids, enabling patch-wise photometric transformations. This hierarchical approach overcomes optimization challenges of single-scale grids and enhances both modeling capacity and convergence stability. The method demonstrates significant improvements in both appearance and geometric metrics across multiple real-world datasets, and is shown to be a generalizable module for various Gaussian Splatting-based neural rendering systems. The approach is particularly effective in challenging scenarios with severe photometric inconsistencies, reducing geometric artifacts such as floaters and achieving state-of-the-art results.

01de6d0c00e7e77050a90945246b2b4acde497a2.title: NodeFormer: A Scalable Graph Structure Learning Transformer for Node Classification
01de6d0c00e7e77050a90945246b2b4acde497a2.research_question: How can node classification on large-scale graphs be improved by learning adaptive, latent graph structures in a scalable and efficient manner, especially in scenarios with heterophily, long-range dependencies, incomplete or missing input graphs?
01de6d0c00e7e77050a90945246b2b4acde497a2.hypothesis: Learning layer-wise, adaptive latent graph structures via an efficient, differentiable operator will enable scalable, accurate node classification on large graphs, outperforming existing graph neural network and structure learning methods, particularly in challenging settings such as heterophily, long-range dependencies, and absent or incomplete input graphs.
01de6d0c00e7e77050a90945246b2b4acde497a2.proposed_method: A new framework is proposed that introduces a scalable, Transformer-style graph neural network for node classification, named NODEFORMER. The core component is a kernelized Gumbel-Softmax operator that enables efficient, differentiable learning of discrete, layer-specific latent graph structures with linear complexity in the number of nodes. Message passing is performed over all node pairs using a random feature approximation of positive-definite kernels, and the Gumbel-Softmax trick provides a continuous relaxation for sampling discrete edges, allowing end-to-end optimization. Optional components include a relational bias to incorporate observed input graphs and an edge-level regularization loss to encourage learning of meaningful edge probabilities. The overall architecture supports both the presence and absence of input graphs, and is optimized via a combination of supervised classification loss and edge-level regularization.
01de6d0c00e7e77050a90945246b2b4acde497a2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of node classification benchmarks, including small/medium-sized graphs (Cora, Citeseer, Deezer, Actor), large-scale graphs (OGB-Proteins, Amazon2M), and graph-enhanced applications such as semi-supervised image and text classification (Mini-ImageNet, 20News-Groups) where input graphs are artificially constructed or missing. Baselines will include standard GNNs (GCN, GAT), advanced GNNs (JKNet, MixHop), scalable GNNs (SGC, GraphSAINT), and state-of-the-art graph structure learning methods (LDS-GNN, IDGL). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy and ROC-AUC, with additional measurements of training/inference time and GPU memory usage. Experiments will use random splits and mini-batch training for large datasets, and ablation studies will assess the impact of stochastic components, edge regularization, and relational bias.
01de6d0c00e7e77050a90945246b2b4acde497a2.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first Transformer-based graph network that scales all-pair message passing to graphs with millions of nodes via a kernelized Gumbel-Softmax operator, reducing complexity from quadratic to linear in node count. The method enables efficient, differentiable learning of layer-wise latent graph structures, supports both the presence and absence of input graphs, and achieves significant improvements in accuracy, scalability, and resource efficiency over existing GNNs and structure learning baselines. Theoretical analysis guarantees the well-posedness and approximation properties of the kernelized Gumbel-Softmax operator, and empirical results demonstrate superior performance on both homophilic and heterophilic graphs, as well as on large-scale and graph-absent scenarios.

01e863776846ebd1a9a7acc4a9ca24217f953aa2.title: Data Interpreter: An LLM Agent For Data Science
01e863776846ebd1a9a7acc4a9ca24217f953aa2.research_question: How can large language model (LLM) agents be designed to autonomously and robustly solve end-to-end data science workflows, including complex, interconnected tasks that require dynamic adaptation to evolving data and task dependencies?
01e863776846ebd1a9a7acc4a9ca24217f953aa2.hypothesis: A hierarchical graph-based framework that decomposes data science workflows into dynamically managed subproblems, combined with programmable node generation for iterative code refinement and tool integration, will significantly improve the robustness, adaptability, and overall performance of LLM agents on complex data science tasks compared to existing methods.
01e863776846ebd1a9a7acc4a9ca24217f953aa2.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a hierarchical graph modeling framework for LLM-based data science agents. The workflow is decomposed into a task graph, where each node represents a major subproblem (e.g., data exploration, feature engineering, model training), and dependencies are represented as edges. Each task node is further decomposed into an action graph comprising executable code snippets (action nodes), which can be independently executed and verified. The system incorporates iterative graph refinement, allowing dynamic updates to the task and action graphs in response to real-time execution feedback and failures. Programmable node generation integrates context-aware tool selection and code synthesis, enabling seamless incorporation of external libraries and domain-specific tools within the generated code. The agent leverages LLMs for both high-level planning and low-level code generation, with runtime reflection and debugging to ensure robust execution.
01e863776846ebd1a9a7acc4a9ca24217f953aa2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several benchmarks: InfiAgent-DABench (257 data analysis challenges across 52 CSV files), ML-Benchmark (8 real-world machine learning datasets from Kaggle), an open-ended task benchmark (20 tasks including OCR, web crawling, and multimodal tasks), and the MATH dataset (level-5 problems from 4 categories). Baselines will include XAgent, AutoGen, OpenInterpreter, TaskWeaver, OpenDevin, and MathChat. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, comprehensive score, and completion rate, with results averaged over multiple runs where applicable. The experimental setup will use state-of-the-art LLMs (e.g., GPT-4o, GPT-4-0613, GPT-4-1106-preview) and systematically compare the proposed method against baselines in terms of performance, adaptability, and efficiency.
01e863776846ebd1a9a7acc4a9ca24217f953aa2.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a unified, hierarchical graph-based framework for end-to-end data science automation with LLM agents, enabling dynamic decomposition, real-time task refinement, and robust execution. Programmable node generation allows for seamless, context-aware integration of external tools and libraries within generated code, surpassing the isolated function-calling paradigm of prior LLM agents. The approach supports iterative feedback-driven optimization at both the planning and execution levels, providing fine-grained adaptability to evolving data and task dependencies. Extensive benchmarking across diverse, real-world data science and mathematical tasks demonstrates significant improvements in accuracy, robustness, and efficiency over existing open-source LLM agent frameworks.

01fc730e06c4d3d02840af2ebae083634998b566.title: GeoCLIP: Clip-Inspired Alignment between Locations and Images for Effective Worldwide Geo-localization
01fc730e06c4d3d02840af2ebae083634998b566.research_question: How can the alignment between images and their corresponding geographic locations be improved to enable accurate and scalable worldwide geo-localization, especially in the absence of dense image galleries and with limited training data?
01fc730e06c4d3d02840af2ebae083634998b566.hypothesis: A CLIP-inspired image-to-GPS retrieval framework that directly aligns image features with continuous GPS location embeddings, using hierarchical positional encoding and contrastive learning, will achieve more accurate and data-efficient worldwide geo-localization than existing classification-based or image-to-image retrieval methods.
01fc730e06c4d3d02840af2ebae083634998b566.proposed_method: A novel image-to-GPS retrieval approach is proposed, where the task is formulated as matching a query image to a gallery of GPS coordinates rather than to a gallery of images. The method consists of two main components: an image encoder based on a frozen CLIP Vision Transformer (ViT-L/14) backbone with two additional trainable linear layers, and a location encoder that transforms 2D GPS coordinates into high-dimensional embeddings. The location encoder first applies Equal Earth Projection to minimize geographic distortions, then uses Random Fourier Features (RFF) for positional encoding at multiple frequency scales, and finally aggregates hierarchical representations via multiple MLPs with different sigma values to capture spatial information at varying resolutions. Contrastive loss is employed to align image and GPS features, leveraging a dynamic queue of negative GPS samples for robust representation learning. The architecture supports both image and text queries by leveraging the CLIP backbone, enabling semantic geo-localization from textual descriptions.
01fc730e06c4d3d02840af2ebae083634998b566.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on several benchmark datasets for worldwide geo-localization, including MediaEval Placing Task 2016 (MP-16) for training, and Im2GPS3k, Google World Streets 15k (GWS15k), and YFCC26k for evaluation. During testing, image-to-GPS retrieval is performed by matching query images against a large gallery of sampled GPS coordinates (100K for Im2GPS3k, 500K for GWS15k). Performance is evaluated using geodesic distance thresholds (1km, 25km, 200km, 750km, 2500km), reporting the percentage of predictions within each threshold. Baselines include state-of-the-art classification and retrieval methods such as PlaNet, CPlaNet, ISNs, Translocator, and GeoDecoder. Ablation studies assess the impact of each component in the location encoder, and experiments are also conducted in limited-data settings (using 20%, 10%, and 5% of training data) to evaluate data efficiency. Additional experiments demonstrate the utility of the learned GPS embeddings for image classification on the NUS-WIDE dataset and the ability to perform geo-localization with text queries.
01fc730e06c4d3d02840af2ebae083634998b566.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to frame worldwide geo-localization as an image-to-GPS retrieval problem by explicitly aligning image features with continuous GPS embeddings. The location encoder introduces a hierarchical positional encoding scheme using Random Fourier Features at multiple resolutions, overcoming spectral bias and enabling fine-grained and coarse-grained localization simultaneously. The method demonstrates strong data efficiency, maintaining high accuracy even with significantly reduced training data. The approach also enables text-based geo-localization by leveraging the CLIP backbone, and the learned GPS embeddings are shown to be useful for downstream tasks such as image classification, highlighting the versatility and generality of the representation.

0231f2aed9a96cb516242fb57f2cb63f5651c4d8.title: Safe Latent Diffusion: Mitigating Inappropriate Degeneration in Diffusion Models
0231f2aed9a96cb516242fb57f2cb63f5651c4d8.research_question: How can the generation of inappropriate or biased content in text-to-image diffusion models be systematically measured and effectively mitigated, while preserving image quality and text alignment?
0231f2aed9a96cb516242fb57f2cb63f5651c4d8.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging the internal representations and learned concepts of pre-trained diffusion models, without additional training or external classifiers, enables effective suppression of inappropriate content during image generation, thereby reducing undesired degeneration without degrading overall image fidelity or text alignment.
0231f2aed9a96cb516242fb57f2cb63f5651c4d8.proposed_method: A novel safety guidance mechanism, termed Safe Latent Diffusion (SLD), will be developed for text-to-image diffusion models. SLD operates during inference by manipulating the latent space of the diffusion process, using classifier-free guidance to steer generations away from user-defined inappropriate concepts (expressed in natural language) and towards the original prompt. The approach computes three noise estimates at each diffusion step: unconditioned, prompt-conditioned, and safety-concept-conditioned. The unconditioned estimate is shifted towards the prompt and away from the inappropriate concept, with the degree of suppression controlled by hyperparameters such as safety guidance scale, threshold, warm-up period, and momentum. This method requires no additional training, no external classifiers, and relies solely on the model's pre-trained knowledge. Fine-grained control is achieved by adjusting the strength and timing of the safety intervention, allowing for minimal alteration of appropriate content while rigorously suppressing inappropriate elements.
0231f2aed9a96cb516242fb57f2cb63f5651c4d8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a newly curated benchmark, the Inappropriate Image Prompts (I2P) dataset, which contains over 4,700 real-world text prompts likely to elicit inappropriate content across categories such as hate, harassment, violence, self-harm, sexual content, shocking images, and illegal activity. For each prompt, multiple images will be generated using Stable Diffusion with and without SLD, as well as with negative prompting as a baseline. Automated evaluation will be performed using a combination of the Q16 and NudeNet classifiers to detect inappropriate content, with metrics including the probability of inappropriate generation and expected maximum inappropriateness over prompt batches. Additional experiments will assess the impact on image fidelity (using FID-30k on COCO) and text alignment (using CLIP distance and a user study on DrawBench). Comparative analysis will include different SLD hyperparameter configurations, negative prompting, and models trained on filtered datasets (e.g., Stable Diffusion v2.0).
0231f2aed9a96cb516242fb57f2cb63f5651c4d8.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel, inference-time safety guidance mechanism for diffusion models that requires no additional training or external classifiers, leveraging only the model's own learned representations of inappropriate concepts. It provides the first systematic testbed (I2P) for evaluating inappropriate degeneration in text-to-image models using real-world prompts. The method offers fine-grained, user-configurable control over the suppression of undesired content, and demonstrates mitigation of both explicit inappropriate content and dataset-induced biases (e.g., ethnic bias in nudity generation). The approach is computationally efficient, preserves overall image quality and text alignment, and can be flexibly adapted to evolving definitions of inappropriateness or fairness.

0234aa9ca4ad23a38d2d324e6b1ff0115306dded.title: ReinFlow: Fine-tuning Flow Matching Policy with Online Reinforcement Learning
0234aa9ca4ad23a38d2d324e6b1ff0115306dded.research_question: How can online reinforcement learning be leveraged to fine-tune flow matching policies for continuous robotic control, particularly in scenarios with limited or imperfect demonstration data, minimal inference steps, and challenging exploration requirements?
0234aa9ca4ad23a38d2d324e6b1ff0115306dded.hypothesis: Injecting learnable noise into the trajectories of flow matching policies and optimizing them with online reinforcement learning will enable stable and efficient fine-tuning, resulting in improved task performance and sample efficiency compared to existing diffusion- and flow-based RL methods, especially at very few or even a single denoising step.
0234aa9ca4ad23a38d2d324e6b1ff0115306dded.proposed_method: A novel online reinforcement learning framework, ReinFlow, is proposed to fine-tune pre-trained flow matching policies for continuous robotic control. The method introduces a learnable noise injection network that perturbs the deterministic flow path, converting it into a discrete-time Markov process with Gaussian transition probabilities. This transformation enables exact and tractable likelihood computation for policy gradients, even with minimal denoising steps. The policy and noise networks are jointly optimized using a clipped surrogate loss (e.g., PPO), and various regularization techniques, such as Wasserstein-2 and entropy regularization, are incorporated to enhance training stability and promote exploration. After fine-tuning, the noise network can be discarded, recovering a deterministic flow policy suitable for fast inference.
0234aa9ca4ad23a38d2d324e6b1ff0115306dded.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of simulated robotic control tasks, including locomotion (OpenAI Gym: Hopper, Walker2d, Ant, Humanoid) and manipulation (Franka Kitchen, Robomimic visual tasks: PickPlaceCan, NutAssemblySquare, TwoArmTransport). Pre-trained flow policies will be fine-tuned using ReinFlow and compared against strong baselines such as DPPO (diffusion policy policy optimization) and FQL (FlowQ-Learning). Evaluation metrics include episode reward, task success rate, wall-clock time, and sample efficiency. Experiments will systematically vary the number of denoising steps, pre-training data scale, noise network conditioning, noise magnitude, and regularization strength to analyze their effects on performance.
0234aa9ca4ad23a38d2d324e6b1ff0115306dded.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first online RL algorithm specifically designed for stable fine-tuning of flow matching policies, particularly at very few or even a single denoising step. It introduces a learnable noise injection mechanism that transforms deterministic flows into Markov processes, enabling exact likelihood computation and built-in exploration. The method is broadly applicable to various flow model variants, including Rectified Flow and Shortcut Models, and achieves significant improvements in task performance and wall-time efficiency compared to state-of-the-art diffusion RL methods. Comprehensive sensitivity analyses provide new scientific insights into the key factors affecting flow policy fine-tuning.

023d462ec6ff84cee0d0716a34d11efc7cde8534.title: Reward Model Ensembles Help Mitigate Overoptimization
023d462ec6ff84cee0d0716a34d11efc7cde8534.research_question: Can ensemble-based conservative optimization methods effectively mitigate the problem of overoptimization in reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) for language model fine-tuning, especially under realistic conditions such as label noise?
023d462ec6ff84cee0d0716a34d11efc7cde8534.hypothesis: Ensemble-based conservative optimization objectives, such as worst-case optimization (WCO) and uncertainty-weighted optimization (UWO), will significantly reduce or eliminate overoptimization in RLHF pipelines, outperforming single reward model optimization, even in the presence of label noise.
023d462ec6ff84cee0d0716a34d11efc7cde8534.proposed_method: The proposed approach involves training an ensemble of proxy reward models, each initialized with different random seeds but trained on the same dataset and with identical hyperparameters. During policy optimization, three ensemble-based objectives are considered: (1) mean optimization, which averages the outputs of the ensemble; (2) worst-case optimization (WCO), which selects the minimum reward across the ensemble to provide a conservative estimate; and (3) uncertainty-weighted optimization (UWO), which combines the mean reward with a penalty proportional to the variance among ensemble members, controlled by a hyperparameter λ. These objectives are integrated into two policy optimization methods: best-of-n sampling (BoN) and proximal policy optimization (PPO). For PPO, a KL penalty term is also considered to regularize policy updates and further prevent overoptimization.
023d462ec6ff84cee0d0716a34d11efc7cde8534.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the AlpacaFarm dataset, which contains 52,000 instruction-response pairs with human preference annotations. Both noiseless and 25% label noise conditions will be tested to simulate real-world annotator disagreement. The policy and reward models are based on the Pythia suite of pretrained language models, with proxy reward models of various sizes (7M, 44M, 1.3B parameters) and a 7B-parameter gold reward model serving as the 'true' reward. The RLHF pipeline includes supervised fine-tuning, preference generation with the gold model, proxy reward model training, ensemble creation, and policy optimization via BoN (up to n=12,500 samples) and PPO (up to 3,000 steps). Baselines include single reward model optimization and mean ensemble optimization, with evaluation metrics focusing on gold reward model scores, KL divergence, and policy win-rate. Robustness to ensemble size and uncertainty penalty hyperparameters will also be assessed.
023d462ec6ff84cee0d0716a34d11efc7cde8534.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first systematic study of ensemble-based conservative optimization methods for mitigating overoptimization in RLHF-based language model fine-tuning. The approach demonstrates that WCO and UWO objectives can nearly eliminate overoptimization and yield substantial performance improvements, especially under label noise. The method is computationally efficient, as it only requires fine-tuning multiple copies of existing pretrained models rather than training larger models from scratch. Additional contributions include robustness analyses with respect to ensemble size and uncertainty penalty, as well as the demonstration that ensemble-based gains are orthogonal to those achieved by scaling model or dataset size.

024006d4c2a89f7acacc6e4438d156525b60a98f.title: Continuous control with deep reinforcement learning
024006d4c2a89f7acacc6e4438d156525b60a98f.research_question: How can reinforcement learning algorithms be extended to effectively solve complex, high-dimensional continuous control tasks, including those with raw sensory (pixel) inputs, in a stable and scalable manner?
024006d4c2a89f7acacc6e4438d156525b60a98f.hypothesis: A model-free, off-policy actor-critic algorithm leveraging deterministic policy gradients, combined with deep neural network function approximators, experience replay, target networks, and batch normalization, can learn effective policies for high-dimensional continuous control problems, including those using raw pixel observations, with stability and generality across diverse tasks.
024006d4c2a89f7acacc6e4438d156525b60a98f.proposed_method: A novel reinforcement learning framework will be developed based on the deterministic policy gradient (DPG) algorithm, enhanced to operate with deep neural network function approximators for both actor and critic. The method will incorporate an experience replay buffer to break temporal correlations and enable efficient minibatch learning, as well as target networks for both actor and critic, updated via soft updates to stabilize learning. Batch normalization will be applied to all layers of the actor and critic networks to handle varying input scales and facilitate generalization across tasks. Exploration will be handled by adding temporally correlated noise (e.g., Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process) to the policy output, and the entire system will be trained end-to-end, including from raw pixel observations using convolutional neural networks.
024006d4c2a89f7acacc6e4438d156525b60a98f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of over 20 simulated physics control environments, including classic tasks (e.g., cartpole swing-up, pendulum), dexterous manipulation, legged locomotion, and driving (e.g., Torcs racing simulator), using both low-dimensional state vectors and high-dimensional pixel inputs. All experiments will use the same network architecture and hyperparameters to test generality. Performance will be evaluated against two baselines: a naive random policy and a planning-based algorithm (iLQG) with full access to the environment's dynamics. Evaluation metrics will include normalized return scores (random=0, planner=1), learning curves, and accuracy of value function estimation. Policies will be periodically evaluated without exploration noise, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of target networks and batch normalization.
024006d4c2a89f7acacc6e4438d156525b60a98f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to demonstrate stable, scalable, and generalizable learning of continuous control policies in high-dimensional environments using deep neural networks, experience replay, and target networks, with the same architecture and hyperparameters across diverse tasks. It enables end-to-end policy learning directly from raw pixel inputs and achieves performance competitive with, or superior to, planning-based methods that have full model access. The method introduces a simple yet robust actor-critic architecture that can be easily implemented and scaled, and provides empirical evidence of stable learning in challenging domains where previous methods were unstable or impractical.

02520b20a97b3d65ed381c9840797c3ca97c0260.title: Register and CLS tokens yield a decoupling of local and global features in large ViTs
02520b20a97b3d65ed381c9840797c3ca97c0260.research_question: How do register tokens and [CLS] tokens affect the relationship between local and global feature representations in large Vision Transformer (ViT) models, and what are the implications for model interpretability and the validity of the patch integration assumption?
02520b20a97b3d65ed381c9840797c3ca97c0260.hypothesis: In large ViT models, the introduction of register tokens or the use of [CLS] tokens with residual connections leads to a decoupling of local patch features from global representations, thereby violating the patch integration assumption and reducing the interpretability of attention maps.
02520b20a97b3d65ed381c9840797c3ca97c0260.proposed_method: A systematic analysis will be conducted on Vision Transformer models of varying sizes, both with and without register tokens, to quantify the degree to which global representations rely on local patch features versus register or [CLS] tokens. The methodology involves probing the attention distributions of the final layer [CLS] token, partitioning attention between patch and register tokens, and constraining the self-attention mechanism to attend exclusively to one token type at a time. Linear centered kernel alignment (CKA) will be used to measure the similarity between global representations derived from all tokens, only patch tokens, or only register tokens. Additionally, the influence of residual connections in the [CLS] token will be assessed by analyzing the L2-norm contributions of skip connections and patch features, as well as by measuring the cosine similarity of [CLS] token representations across layers.
02520b20a97b3d65ed381c9840797c3ca97c0260.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed using publicly available DINOv2 ViT models of different sizes ('small', 'base', 'large', and 'giant'), with and without register tokens. The MSCOCO validation set and the ImageNet test set will serve as primary datasets for probing attention distributions and feature similarities. Baseline comparisons will include models trained with different supervision strategies (e.g., DeiTIII, CLIP, iBOT). Evaluation metrics will include the partitioning of attention weights, CKA similarity scores between different feature extraction strategies, cosine similarity between feature vectors, and one-shot classification accuracy using global, patch-based, and register-based outputs. The experimental setup will involve both qualitative (visualization of attention maps) and quantitative (statistical analysis of feature alignment and classification performance) assessments.
02520b20a97b3d65ed381c9840797c3ca97c0260.novelty_claims: The proposed research identifies and characterizes a fundamental disconnect between local and global features in large ViT models induced by register and [CLS] tokens, challenging the widely held patch integration assumption. It demonstrates that, contrary to expectations, cleaner attention maps resulting from register tokens do not guarantee faithful attribution of global representations to local image regions. The analysis further reveals that residual connections in the [CLS] token can independently cause similar decoupling effects, even in the absence of explicit register tokens. This work provides actionable design recommendations for constructing more interpretable vision models and offers new insights into the interplay between model overparameterization, token design, and representation geometry in transformer-based architectures.

025d6f7a4f96dc4a68ea814cd10ff261a7cd604c.title: Variational Data Assimilation with a Learned Inverse Observation Operator
025d6f7a4f96dc4a68ea814cd10ff261a7cd604c.research_question: How can the optimization process in variational data assimilation for dynamical systems be improved to enhance forecast quality, particularly in the presence of non-invertible and nonlinear observation operators?
025d6f7a4f96dc4a68ea814cd10ff261a7cd604c.hypothesis: A learned approximate inverse observation operator, when integrated into the variational data assimilation pipeline, will improve the initialization and reformulation of the optimization problem, resulting in more accurate forecasts for chaotic dynamical systems.
025d6f7a4f96dc4a68ea814cd10ff261a7cd604c.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves augmenting a traditional variational data assimilation algorithm with a machine-learned inverse observation operator. This operator is parameterized as a fully-convolutional neural network (in space and time) trained to map observation trajectories to corresponding physical states using simulated data. The learned inverse is used in two key ways: (1) to provide an effective initialization for the non-convex optimization of the initial state, and (2) to reformulate the assimilation objective function in the physics state space, rather than the observation space, thereby improving the optimization landscape. A hybrid optimization approach is also proposed, where the assimilation first minimizes the reformulated objective in physics space and then refines the solution in observation space, leveraging the strengths of both formulations.
025d6f7a4f96dc4a68ea814cd10ff261a7cd604c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two canonical chaotic systems: the Lorenz96 model and a two-dimensional turbulent fluid flow (Kolmogorov flow). For each system, simulated datasets of independent observation trajectories will be generated for training and evaluation. The learned inverse observation operator will be implemented as a fully-convolutional neural network (with architecture details specified for each system) and trained using the Adam optimizer. Baseline methods will include traditional observation-space optimization with standard initialization (e.g., averaging or bicubic interpolation for unobserved points). Evaluation metrics will include the mean L1 forecast error relative to a random evolution of the system, measured over a sample of 100 test trajectories. The experimental setup will compare the impact of different initialization schemes and optimization strategies (observation space only vs. hybrid physics/observation space) on forecast accuracy, with all models and optimizations run on a single NVIDIA V100 GPU.
025d6f7a4f96dc4a68ea814cd10ff261a7cd604c.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel integration of a machine-learned inverse observation operator into the variational data assimilation process, enabling both improved initialization and reformulation of the optimization objective in physics space. This approach addresses the challenges posed by non-invertible and nonlinear observation operators, leading to a more tractable optimization problem and enhanced forecast quality. The use of fully-convolutional architectures for the inverse operator and the hybrid optimization strategy are innovative contributions that demonstrate significant improvements over traditional data assimilation methods in chaotic systems.

02634cfbd3882f51ca74a4e0939edc958449bd13.title: Unlocking the Potential of Model Calibration in Federated Learning
02634cfbd3882f51ca74a4e0939edc958449bd13.research_question: How can model calibration be effectively integrated into federated learning to ensure reliable confidence estimates across heterogeneous client data distributions, without sacrificing model accuracy?
02634cfbd3882f51ca74a4e0939edc958449bd13.hypothesis: Dynamically adjusting the calibration penalty for each client in federated learning, based on the statistical similarity between local and global models, will improve both the calibration and accuracy of the global model across heterogeneous data distributions.
02634cfbd3882f51ca74a4e0939edc958449bd13.proposed_method: A novel framework, Non-Uniform Calibration for Federated Learning (NUCFL), is developed to integrate model calibration into federated learning (FL) by introducing a dynamic, client-specific calibration penalty during local training. The approach augments the standard FL loss with an auxiliary calibration loss (such as DCA or MDCA), weighted by a penalty term that is automatically determined for each client based on the similarity between the client's local model and the global model. The similarity is measured using metrics such as cosine similarity or Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA), and the penalty is set higher for clients whose local models are more similar to the global model, aligning local calibration objectives with global needs. This non-uniform penalty ensures that calibration is prioritized where it most benefits the global model, while maintaining accuracy in more heterogeneous clients. The framework is compatible with any auxiliary-based calibration loss and can be integrated into a wide range of FL algorithms without additional hyperparameter tuning.
02634cfbd3882f51ca74a4e0939edc958449bd13.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on four image classification datasets: MNIST, FEMNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100, using standard convolutional neural network architectures (e.g., CNN, AlexNet, ResNet-34). Both IID and non-IID data distributions are simulated across 50 clients, with non-IID splits generated via a Dirichlet distribution (α=0.5). The framework is evaluated on five federated learning algorithms: FedAvg, FedProx, Scaffold, FedDyn, and FedNova. Baselines include standard cross-entropy (uncalibrated), various centralized and train-time calibration methods (Focal Loss, Label Smoothing, Brier Score, MMCE, FLSD, MbLS, DCA, MDCA), and the state-of-the-art FL calibration method FedCal. Evaluation metrics include classification accuracy, Expected Calibration Error (ECE), and Static Calibration Error (SCE), with results averaged over multiple random seeds. The impact of different auxiliary losses and similarity measures is systematically studied, and the compatibility with post-hoc calibration (e.g., Temperature Scaling) is also assessed.
02634cfbd3882f51ca74a4e0939edc958449bd13.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to systematically address model calibration in federated learning by dynamically adjusting calibration penalties based on the relationship between local and global models, thereby directly accounting for data heterogeneity. The method is generic, compatible with any auxiliary-based calibration loss and any FL algorithm, and requires no additional hyperparameter tuning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the approach consistently improves both calibration and accuracy across diverse FL settings, outperforming existing calibration methods and providing a flexible foundation for future extensions in FL calibration.

0268225b5c7f12f3d980ccc4311e488e613b60f4.title: Learning to Clarify: Multi-turn Conversations with Action-Based Contrastive Self-Training
0268225b5c7f12f3d980ccc4311e488e613b60f4.research_question: How can large language models be adapted to function as mixed-initiative conversational agents capable of effectively handling ambiguity and disambiguation in multi-turn conversations, particularly in data-scarce settings?
0268225b5c7f12f3d980ccc4311e488e613b60f4.hypothesis: A quasi-online contrastive self-training approach that leverages action-based preference optimization can enable large language models to more efficiently learn dialogue policies for ambiguity recognition and clarification, outperforming standard supervised fine-tuning and preference optimization baselines in multi-turn conversational tasks.
0268225b5c7f12f3d980ccc4311e488e613b60f4.proposed_method: A novel framework, Action-Based Contrastive Self-Training (ACT), will be developed to adapt large language models for mixed-initiative conversational settings. The method models dialogue action planning as an implicit subtask of response generation, focusing on contrasting pragmatic conversational actions such as 'clarify' versus 'answer.' ACT consists of two main phases: (1) constructing a contrastive dataset of winning and losing action-response pairs for each conversation turn, where actions are inferred via a classifier or annotation agent, and losing responses are generated by a high-capacity LLM; (2) performing quasi-online self-training using on-policy response sampling, multi-turn trajectory simulation, and iterative policy updates with a DPO-based objective. On-policy responses are evaluated for action correctness and task completion via user simulation and task-specific heuristics, enabling dynamic updating of contrastive pairs and robust policy learning.
0268225b5c7f12f3d980ccc4311e488e613b60f4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three diverse multi-turn conversational tasks: PACIFIC (tabular conversational QA), Abg-CoQA (machine reading comprehension QA), and AmbigSQL (ambiguous conversational text-to-SQL generation). For each task, datasets will be constructed or adapted to include ambiguous user queries and corresponding clarifying or direct answer responses. Baselines will include supervised fine-tuning (SFT), Iterative Reasoning Preference Optimization (IRPO), and prompt-based approaches using frontier LLMs such as Gemini Pro and Claude Sonnet. Evaluation metrics will include Macro F1 for ambiguity recognition, content-level metrics such as token overlap (DROP F1), semantic similarity (SentenceBERT), and task-specific execution match for SQL queries. Both single-turn and multi-turn (trajectory-level) evaluations will be performed, with particular focus on post-clarification task success and data efficiency under limited conversation samples.
0268225b5c7f12f3d980ccc4311e488e613b60f4.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first contrastive learning framework that operates on conversational actions within multi-turn trajectories, rather than single-turn response optimization. ACT enables data-efficient adaptation of LLMs for dialogue policy learning without requiring explicit action labels, leveraging self-generated contrastive pairs and user simulation. The method is designed for pragmatic skill acquisition, specifically targeting ambiguity recognition and clarification in conversation, and demonstrates substantial improvements in multi-turn conversational modeling and task completion over existing tuning and alignment strategies.

026b3396a63ed5772329708b7580d633bb86bec9.title: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era
026b3396a63ed5772329708b7580d633bb86bec9.research_question: How can a neural network architecture be designed to combine the efficient, linear-scaling inference of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with the parallelizable and expressive training capabilities of Transformers, in order to improve scalability and performance on large-scale sequence modeling tasks such as natural language processing?
026b3396a63ed5772329708b7580d633bb86bec9.hypothesis: A novel architecture that integrates linear attention mechanisms with recurrent structures, enabling both parallelized training and efficient, linear-time inference, will achieve performance comparable to state-of-the-art Transformers while significantly reducing computational and memory costs, especially for long sequences.
026b3396a63ed5772329708b7580d633bb86bec9.proposed_method: A new model architecture, termed Receptance Weighted Key Value (RWKV), will be developed that reformulates the attention mechanism using a channel-wise, time-decay vector, allowing it to function as either a Transformer or an RNN. The architecture consists of stacked residual blocks, each containing time-mixing and channel-mixing sub-blocks, which leverage past information through a recurrent structure. The WKV operator is introduced to compute attention-like scores with linear complexity, and a token shift mechanism is implemented to interpolate between current and previous timestep inputs. Layer normalization and custom initialization strategies are incorporated to stabilize training and address vanishing/exploding gradients. The model supports both time-parallel (Transformer-like) training and time-sequential (RNN-like) inference, with additional optimizations such as custom CUDA kernels for efficient computation.
026b3396a63ed5772329708b7580d633bb86bec9.experiment_details: The proposed architecture will be benchmarked by training models ranging from 169 million to 14 billion parameters on the Pile dataset (an 800GB diverse text corpus) for one epoch (330 billion tokens). Evaluation will be conducted on a suite of NLP tasks, including ARC, BoolQ, COPA, HeadQA, HellaSwag, LAMBADA, OpenBookQA, PIQA, ReCoRD, SciQ, and Winogrande, using zero-shot performance as the primary metric. Baselines will include similarly sized Transformer models such as Pythia, OPT, and BLOOM, with comparisons made on a FLOP-matched basis. Additional experiments will assess scaling laws, long-context modeling (including finetuning to context lengths up to 8192 tokens), and performance on the Long Range Arena benchmark for long-sequence tasks. Inference speed and memory requirements will be measured on both CPU and GPU platforms.
026b3396a63ed5772329708b7580d633bb86bec9.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel architecture that unifies the benefits of RNNs and Transformers, achieving linear computational and memory complexity during inference while supporting parallelized training. The RWKV model is claimed to be the largest dense RNN ever trained (up to 14B parameters) and demonstrates performance on par with state-of-the-art Transformers on a wide range of NLP benchmarks. The architecture enables efficient handling of long sequences, supports both Transformer-like and RNN-like modes, and is backed by extensive empirical evaluation and the release of large-scale pretrained models. Additional innovations include custom initialization, a new WKV operator, and optimizations for both training and inference.

026bb8a1066f50ddc8797e1341353603149a8cb8.title: Gradient Descent on Neural Networks Typically Occurs at the Edge of Stability
026bb8a1066f50ddc8797e1341353603149a8cb8.research_question: How does full-batch gradient descent behave when training neural networks, particularly with respect to stability, sharpness of the loss landscape, and the validity of conventional optimization assumptions?
026bb8a1066f50ddc8797e1341353603149a8cb8.hypothesis: Full-batch gradient descent on neural network objectives typically operates in a regime where the sharpness (maximum Hessian eigenvalue) hovers at or just above a critical threshold (2/step size), resulting in non-monotonic but overall decreasing training loss. Conventional assumptions such as L-smoothness and monotonic descent may not accurately describe this regime.
026bb8a1066f50ddc8797e1341353603149a8cb8.proposed_method: The proposed research will systematically investigate the dynamics of full-batch gradient descent on a variety of neural network architectures and tasks. The approach involves monitoring the evolution of the sharpness, defined as the maximum eigenvalue of the training loss Hessian, throughout training at various step sizes. Both mean squared error and cross-entropy losses will be considered, and experiments will include architectures with and without batch normalization, as well as networks of varying depth and width. The method will also extend to momentum-based variants of gradient descent, such as Polyak and Nesterov momentum, analyzing the corresponding maximum stable sharpness thresholds. Numerical integration (e.g., Runge-Kutta) will be used to approximate gradient flow trajectories for comparison.
026bb8a1066f50ddc8797e1341353603149a8cb8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard datasets such as CIFAR-10, using subsets and the full dataset, as well as on synthetic regression tasks, deep linear networks with Gaussian data, and language modeling with Transformers on WikiText-2. A variety of architectures will be tested, including fully-connected networks, convolutional networks, VGG, and ResNet, with different activation functions (tanh, ReLU, ELU, softplus, hardtanh). For each configuration, the training loss and sharpness will be tracked across iterations and compared to theoretical stability thresholds (2/step size or maximum stable sharpness for momentum). Baseline comparisons will include different step sizes, loss functions, and the use of batch normalization. Evaluation metrics will include training accuracy, loss curves, sharpness evolution, and convergence speed (number of iterations to reach target accuracy). Key experimental setups will also involve step size drops to observe the resumption of progressive sharpening.
026bb8a1066f50ddc8797e1341353603149a8cb8.novelty_claims: The proposed research claims to provide a precise empirical characterization of the 'Edge of Stability' regime in neural network training with gradient descent, where sharpness hovers at or just above the theoretical stability threshold. This regime is shown to be the default for reasonable step sizes in standard architectures, contradicting conventional optimization assumptions such as L-smoothness and monotonic descent. The work extends analysis to a broad range of architectures and tasks, demonstrates the inadequacy of stable step sizes for practical training, and highlights the need for revised theoretical frameworks for optimization in deep learning.

0286b2736a114198b25fb5553c671c33aed5d477.title: Training a Helpful and Harmless Assistant with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
0286b2736a114198b25fb5553c671c33aed5d477.research_question: How can large language models be trained to act as helpful and harmless assistants using human feedback, and what are the effects of such alignment training on model performance, robustness, and the ability to integrate specialized skills?
0286b2736a114198b25fb5553c671c33aed5d477.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), combined with preference modeling for helpfulness and harmlessness, can align large language models to be both helpful and harmless without degrading, and potentially improving, their performance on standard NLP and specialized skill evaluations.
0286b2736a114198b25fb5553c671c33aed5d477.proposed_method: The proposed method involves collecting separate datasets of human preferences for helpfulness and harmlessness through open-ended dialogue interactions with crowdworkers. Preference models (PMs) are trained on these datasets to evaluate model responses for helpfulness and harmlessness. These PMs are then used as reward models in a reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) framework, where large language models are fine-tuned using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) to maximize the PM scores. An iterated online RLHF approach is adopted, where PMs and RLHF policies are updated on a weekly cadence with new human feedback, allowing for continuous improvement of both models and datasets. The method also explores the integration of alignment training with specialized skills such as code generation and summarization, as well as the application of out-of-distribution (OOD) detection to filter harmful or strange requests.
0286b2736a114198b25fb5553c671c33aed5d477.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using large language models of varying sizes (up to 52B parameters). Datasets for helpfulness and harmlessness are collected via crowdworker interactions, with three main tranches: initial, rejection-sampled, and online RLHF-enhanced data. Evaluations include standard NLP benchmarks (MMLU, Lambada, HellaSwag, OpenBookQA, ARC, TriviaQA), code generation (HumanEval), summarization, and static alignment tasks (HHH Evaluations, TruthfulQA, BBQ-Lite, gender bias, sentiment analysis). Baselines include plain language models, context-distilled models, and RLHF models trained on static datasets. Evaluation metrics include mean accuracy on benchmarks, Elo scores from crowdworker preferences, and calibration/robustness studies (e.g., overfitting via PM train/test splits, KL divergence analysis). Additional human evaluations compare model outputs to those of professional writers.
0286b2736a114198b25fb5553c671c33aed5d477.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a comprehensive framework for training language models to be both helpful and harmless using RLHF with separate preference modeling for each objective. It claims to be the first to explicitly study the tension and trade-offs between helpfulness and harmlessness in alignment training, and to demonstrate that alignment can be combined with specialized skills without performance degradation. The iterated online RLHF approach, with regular updates to both PMs and policies based on fresh human feedback, is presented as a novel method for dataset and model improvement. The work also claims to provide new insights into the robustness and scaling behavior of RLHF, and to show the effectiveness of OOD detection for filtering harmful requests.

029d309dd1f3a93ff74740ceca32da8c09c63e5c.title: BOND: Aligning LLMs with Best-of-N Distillation
029d309dd1f3a93ff74740ceca32da8c09c63e5c.research_question: How can large language models be aligned to emulate the high-quality outputs of Best-of-N sampling strategies, while avoiding the significant computational overhead at inference time associated with sampling and ranking multiple generations?
029d309dd1f3a93ff74740ceca32da8c09c63e5c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that aligning the policy of a large language model to match the distribution of outputs produced by Best-of-N sampling, using a distribution matching approach based on Jeffreys divergence and iterative distillation, will enable the model to generate outputs of comparable quality to Best-of-N sampling with only a single sample at inference time, thus achieving superior reward/KL trade-offs and improved alignment with human preferences.
029d309dd1f3a93ff74740ceca32da8c09c63e5c.proposed_method: A novel RLHF algorithm, Best-of-N Distillation (BOND), will be developed to align the policy of a large language model with the distribution induced by Best-of-N sampling from a reference policy. The approach begins by analytically deriving the Best-of-N distribution, then formulates policy alignment as a distribution matching problem. Jeffreys divergence—a weighted combination of forward and backward KL divergences—will be minimized between the current policy and the Best-of-N distribution, balancing mode-covering and mode-seeking behaviors. An iterative distillation procedure will be employed, where the policy is repeatedly aligned to the Best-of-n (e.g., n=2) distribution of a moving anchor policy, which is updated via exponential moving average (EMA) from the current policy. The J-BOND algorithm will implement this procedure, using minimal anchor samples per prompt and incorporating additional KL regularization to ensure stability.
029d309dd1f3a93ff74740ceca32da8c09c63e5c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both abstractive summarization (using the XSum dataset) and conversational alignment tasks with Gemma (2B and 7B) models. The reward model will be a large, pretrained model reflecting human preferences. Baselines will include standard RLHF algorithms such as REINFORCE with KL regularization and supervised fine-tuning. Evaluation metrics will include reward/KL Pareto front analysis, average reward, log quantile statistics, and performance on academic benchmarks and side-by-side comparisons with open-source models like Mixtral. Training will use batch sizes of 128, Adam optimizer, and learning rates of 3e-6 with warm-up steps. Quantile estimation for the BOND objective will use Monte Carlo sampling, and ablations will be performed on anchor update strategies and KL regularization strength.
029d309dd1f3a93ff74740ceca32da8c09c63e5c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a theoretically grounded, practical algorithm for distilling the Best-of-N sampling distribution into a policy, enabling single-sample inference with Best-of-N quality. The use of Jeffreys divergence for distribution matching in RLHF is novel and shown to inherit the strengths of both mode-covering and mode-seeking objectives. The iterative BOND procedure allows for exponential scaling to large N with minimal sample complexity and improved training stability. The J-BOND algorithm further innovates by employing an EMA anchor and a calibrated reward function for robust and efficient policy updates. Collectively, these innovations enable superior reward/KL trade-offs and improved alignment compared to existing RLHF methods.

029dd3e4045bb605dae95c549fd13e8dcee254d3.title: Auto-differentiable Ensemble Kalman Filters
029dd3e4045bb605dae95c549fd13e8dcee254d3.research_question: How can sequential state estimation and unknown dynamical system learning be effectively combined and scaled for high-dimensional data assimilation problems when the underlying dynamics are partially known, fully unknown, or inaccurately modeled?
029dd3e4045bb605dae95c549fd13e8dcee254d3.hypothesis: Integrating ensemble Kalman filters with automatic differentiation and machine learning-based surrogate modeling will enable efficient, scalable, and accurate joint learning of latent states and dynamical system parameters, outperforming existing expectation-maximization and particle filter-based approaches, especially in high-dimensional and partially observed settings.
029dd3e4045bb605dae95c549fd13e8dcee254d3.proposed_method: A novel auto-differentiable ensemble Kalman filter (AD-EnKF) framework will be developed that iteratively co-learns the parameters of the underlying dynamical system and recovers the latent state sequence from observations. The method will alternate between (i) running an ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) to estimate the data log-likelihood using an ensemble of particles, (ii) employing automatic differentiation (autodiff) to compute gradients of the log-likelihood with respect to the model parameters, and (iii) performing gradient ascent updates to optimize the parameters, including those of neural network surrogate models or corrections to inaccurate models. The framework will utilize the reparameterization trick to enable unbiased gradient estimation through the stochastic EnKF steps, and will leverage autodiff capabilities of modern machine learning libraries. To address long time series, truncated backpropagation through time (TBPTT) will be incorporated, dividing the data into manageable subsequences and updating parameters sequentially. Additionally, advanced EnKF techniques from the data assimilation literature, such as localization and covariance inflation, will be integrated to enhance performance in high-dimensional regimes.
029dd3e4045bb605dae95c549fd13e8dcee254d3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both linear-Gaussian state-space models and the nonlinear Lorenz-96 model, a standard benchmark in geophysical data assimilation. The evaluation will cover three scenarios: parameterized dynamics with unknown parameters, fully unknown dynamics modeled by neural networks, and correction of inaccurate models using neural network-based corrections. Baseline comparisons will include expectation-maximization approaches using EnKF or ensemble Kalman smoothers, as well as differentiable particle filter (PF) and variational sequential Monte Carlo (VSMC) methods. Performance will be assessed using metrics such as data log-likelihood, state estimation accuracy, and parameter recovery error. The impact of high-dimensionality and partial observability will be systematically analyzed, and the role of EnKF-specific enhancements (e.g., localization) will be evaluated. Implementation will utilize autodiff-enabled libraries such as PyTorch, JAX, or TensorFlow.
029dd3e4045bb605dae95c549fd13e8dcee254d3.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to enable end-to-end auto-differentiation through the ensemble Kalman filter for joint learning of states and dynamical system parameters, including neural network surrogates, in high-dimensional settings. The approach provides new theoretical convergence guarantees for EnKF-based log-likelihood gradient estimation in linear-Gaussian models. By integrating TBPTT and EnKF-specific enhancements, the method addresses scalability and stability for long sequences and large state spaces. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior accuracy and robustness compared to EM-based and differentiable particle filter methods, particularly in challenging, high-dimensional, and partially observed scenarios.

02ad9f3fefe33cb9ca546591bec65dbdf7766c80.title: Ring Attention with Blockwise Transformers for Near-Infinite Context
02ad9f3fefe33cb9ca546591bec65dbdf7766c80.research_question: How can the memory constraints of Transformers be overcome to enable efficient training and inference on extremely long sequences, scaling context length linearly with the number of devices, without incurring additional communication or computation overheads or resorting to attention approximations?
02ad9f3fefe33cb9ca546591bec65dbdf7766c80.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by distributing blockwise self-attention and feedforward computations across multiple devices in a ring topology, and overlapping the communication of key-value blocks with computation, it is possible to scale Transformer context length linearly with device count, achieving near-infinite context size without additional overhead or loss of performance.
02ad9f3fefe33cb9ca546591bec65dbdf7766c80.proposed_method: A novel framework, Ring Attention with Blockwise Transformers, is proposed to address the memory bottleneck in large-context Transformer models. The method splits input sequences into blocks, assigning each block to a separate device in a ring topology. Each device computes blockwise self-attention and feedforward operations for its assigned block, while key-value blocks are communicated in a ring fashion to neighboring devices. Communication of key-value blocks is fully overlapped with the computation of blockwise attention and feedforward, ensuring no additional communication or computation overhead. The approach leverages the permutation invariance of blockwise attention, enabling devices to process their blocks concurrently and scale context length proportionally to the number of devices, with memory requirements dependent only on block size rather than total sequence length.
02ad9f3fefe33cb9ca546591bec65dbdf7766c80.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on language modeling and reinforcement learning tasks using models based on the LLaMA architecture, with sizes ranging from 3B to 30B parameters. The method will be evaluated on various hardware configurations, including multi-GPU (A100) and TPU (v3, v4, v5e) clusters, using both fully sharded data parallelism (FSDP) and tensor parallelism. Baselines will include vanilla Transformers, memory-efficient attention, and blockwise parallel Transformers. Evaluation metrics will include maximum supported context length, model FLOPs utilization (MFU), throughput, and task-specific metrics such as cumulative return on the ExoRL RL benchmark and retrieval accuracy on long-context line retrieval tasks. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by using consistent batch sizes and precision settings across methods.
02ad9f3fefe33cb9ca546591bec65dbdf7766c80.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a memory-efficient Transformer architecture that enables context length to scale linearly with the number of devices, eliminating the memory bottleneck imposed by individual devices. By overlapping communication and computation in a ring topology, the approach achieves zero-overhead scaling of context size, supporting sequences up to device count times longer than prior state-of-the-art memory-efficient Transformers. The method does not require approximations to attention and is compatible with existing memory-efficient Transformer implementations. Extensive experiments are planned to demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach in enabling training and inference with context lengths exceeding 100 million tokens, as well as improved performance on both language modeling and reinforcement learning tasks.

02b8a21f5d586cfc37fde8534d8e79aebf2ea6bd.title: Investigating the Impact of Model Misspecification in Neural Simulation-based Inference
02b8a21f5d586cfc37fde8534d8e79aebf2ea6bd.research_question: How do neural simulation-based inference (SBI) methods perform when the data-generating process does not coincide with the assumed model, and what strategies can improve their robustness to model misspecification?
02b8a21f5d586cfc37fde8534d8e79aebf2ea6bd.hypothesis: Neural SBI methods are hypothesized to provide accurate posterior approximations under well-specified models, but their performance is expected to degrade under various types and degrees of model misspecification. It is further hypothesized that mitigation strategies such as ensemble posteriors and robust optimization techniques like sharpness-aware minimization (SAM) may improve robustness, but may not fully resolve failures in all scenarios.
02b8a21f5d586cfc37fde8534d8e79aebf2ea6bd.proposed_method: A systematic evaluation of neural SBI algorithms will be conducted under controlled model misspecification. Three main classes of neural SBI—neural posterior estimation (NPE), neural likelihood estimation (NLE), and neural ratio estimation (NRE)—will be benchmarked. Misspecification will be introduced by applying a series of controlled, parameterizable transforms to the observed data, simulating increasing levels of discrepancy between the simulator and the data-generating process. Two mitigation strategies will be tested: (1) ensemble posteriors, where multiple independently trained models are averaged to form a mixture posterior, and (2) robust optimization using sharpness-aware minimization (SAM) to encourage flatter minima in the loss landscape and thus potentially better out-of-distribution generalization. All methods will be implemented using the sbi package, with flow-based models (neural spline flows) for NPE and NLE, and fully connected networks for NRE.
02b8a21f5d586cfc37fde8534d8e79aebf2ea6bd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three benchmark models with known analytical or exact posterior solutions: a toy Gaussian model (with and without summary statistics), a stochastic volatility model, and at least one additional task (details in supplement). For each model, 50 independent observations will be generated and subjected to five levels of misspecification via additive noise or other transforms. Each neural SBI method will be trained on 10^5 samples, and performance will be compared to a rejection ABC baseline (retaining the best 1% of 10^5 samples). Evaluation will focus on coverage metrics, assessing both the accuracy and calibration of posterior approximations across varying degrees of misspecification. Ensemble and SAM-based variants will be systematically compared to single-model and ABC baselines. The impact of architectural choices and flow types will be checked for robustness but not varied systematically.
02b8a21f5d586cfc37fde8534d8e79aebf2ea6bd.novelty_claims: This proposal aims to provide the first comprehensive benchmark of neural SBI methods under model misspecification, extending prior work that focused only on well-specified models. It introduces a systematic framework for generating and quantifying misspecification, and rigorously evaluates both standard and robustified neural SBI algorithms. The study will also assess the effectiveness of ensemble posteriors and sharpness-aware minimization as mitigation strategies, providing new insights into the limitations and potential improvements for neural SBI in realistic, imperfect modeling scenarios.

02bc11de9d2f75bad48166098aa6b30fffee4d70.title: Preserve Your Own Correlation: A Noise Prior for Video Diffusion Models
02bc11de9d2f75bad48166098aa6b30fffee4d70.research_question: How can text-to-video diffusion models be efficiently trained to generate photorealistic and temporally coherent videos, especially in the context of limited large-scale video datasets and high computational costs?
02bc11de9d2f75bad48166098aa6b30fffee4d70.hypothesis: Introducing a temporally correlated noise prior, rather than the conventional i.i.d. noise prior, during the fine-tuning of pretrained image diffusion models on video data will significantly improve the photorealism and temporal consistency of generated videos, while also enabling efficient knowledge transfer from image to video generation tasks.
02bc11de9d2f75bad48166098aa6b30fffee4d70.proposed_method: A novel video diffusion noise prior will be developed to better align with the temporal correlations present in real video data. The approach involves fine-tuning a state-of-the-art pretrained text-to-image diffusion model (such as eDiff-I) jointly on large-scale image and video datasets. The conventional i.i.d. Gaussian noise prior will be replaced with either a mixed or progressive noise model, where the noise injected into each video frame is correlated along the temporal axis. In the mixed noise model, each frame's noise is a linear combination of a shared noise vector and an independent noise vector, controlled by a hyperparameter α. In the progressive noise model, noise for each frame is generated autoregressively by perturbing the previous frame's noise, also modulated by α. The model architecture will consist of a cascade of four networks: a base model for low-resolution, low-frame-rate generation, a temporal interpolation model, and two spatial super-resolution models, all adapted from image-based U-Nets with added temporal attention layers.
02bc11de9d2f75bad48166098aa6b30fffee4d70.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both small-scale and large-scale video generation tasks. For small-scale experiments, the UCF-101 dataset will be used for unconditional and text-conditional video generation, following established protocols for metrics such as Inception Score (IS) and Fréchet Video Distance (FVD). For large-scale experiments, a combination of public and proprietary datasets will be used, including 1.2 billion text-image pairs and 22.5 million text-video pairs, filtered for quality. Zero-shot evaluations will be performed on UCF-101 and MSR-VTT benchmarks, using metrics such as IS, FVD, FID, and CLIP-FID. Baselines will include prior state-of-the-art video diffusion models (e.g., Make-A-Video, CogVideo, VideoLDM, VDM), and ablation studies will be conducted to assess the impact of the noise prior and the correlation hyperparameter α. Model sizes and training times will also be compared.
02bc11de9d2f75bad48166098aa6b30fffee4d70.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a temporally correlated noise prior specifically designed for fine-tuning image diffusion models on video data, which preserves inter-frame correlations and enables more effective transfer of image-based knowledge to video generation. This approach allows for state-of-the-art zero-shot text-to-video synthesis with significantly reduced computational resources and model size compared to prior art. The method demonstrates that careful design of the noise prior leads to substantial improvements in both photorealism and temporal consistency of generated videos, outperforming existing baselines on standard benchmarks.

02bd62e468f1d5db1ce5cf7044e0202d5663e060.title: A theory of continuous generative flow networks
02bd62e468f1d5db1ce5cf7044e0202d5663e060.research_question: Can generative flow networks (GFlowNets) be extended to sample from unnormalized target distributions over general state spaces, including continuous and hybrid (discrete-continuous) domains, and what are the theoretical and practical implications of such a generalization for probabilistic inference and modeling tasks?
02bd62e468f1d5db1ce5cf7044e0202d5663e060.hypothesis: Generalized GFlowNets, equipped with appropriate theoretical foundations and training objectives, can efficiently and accurately sample from unnormalized target distributions over arbitrary state spaces, including those with continuous and hybrid structures, thereby retaining or surpassing the advantages observed in discrete GFlowNets.
02bd62e468f1d5db1ce5cf7044e0202d5663e060.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical framework for generalized GFlowNets will be developed, extending existing flow-matching, detailed balance, and trajectory balance conditions to measurable pointed graphs that encompass both discrete and continuous state spaces. The methodology will formalize the necessary mathematical structures, such as reference measures and transition kernels, and derive practical training losses based on Radon-Nikodym derivatives for density-based learning. The approach will include the design of parametric forward and backward policies (kernels) that can be learned via gradient-based optimization, and will specify the conditions under which sampling from the learned forward kernel yields samples from the desired target distribution. Special attention will be paid to ensuring the soundness of these objectives in infinite or hybrid spaces, including the handling of Jacobian terms and the reachability and boundedness of trajectories.
02bd62e468f1d5db1ce5cf7044e0202d5663e060.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a variety of domains to validate the theoretical claims and demonstrate the practical utility of generalized GFlowNets. These include synthetic continuous environments inspired by the hypergrid domain, low-dimensional stochastic control tasks (such as learning discretizations of stochastic differential equations to sample from black-box densities), and modeling reward densities on manifolds like the 2D torus for molecular conformer generation. Additional experiments will address Bayesian structure learning with mixed discrete and continuous posteriors, and connections to diffusion models will be explored by training GFlowNets to maximize likelihood on datasets such as ImageNet-32. Baselines will include standard variational inference methods, stochastic control algorithms, and diffusion models. Evaluation metrics will comprise Jensen-Shannon divergence, log-partition function estimation bias, root mean square error for marginal distributions, negative log-likelihood, and Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for generative modeling. Both on-policy and off-policy training regimes will be tested, and the impact of learning backward policies versus using fixed ones will be systematically assessed.
02bd62e468f1d5db1ce5cf7044e0202d5663e060.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first unified and rigorous theory for GFlowNets over general state spaces, encompassing both discrete and continuous domains. It establishes the mathematical foundations for flow-matching, detailed balance, and trajectory balance objectives in arbitrary measurable spaces, and provides practical loss functions for training density-based samplers.
