The work claims to generalize and subsume existing discrete GFlowNet methods, demonstrates the transferability of their advantages to continuous and hybrid settings, and empirically validates these claims across a diverse set of challenging tasks. Furthermore, the approach enables new applications in probabilistic inference, molecular design, Bayesian structure learning, and generative modeling, including connections to diffusion models and simulation-based inference.

02ddfe4c6da5890fcba72e2273ccdab156e5c654.title: TIPS: Text-Image Pretraining with Spatial Awareness
02ddfe4c6da5890fcba72e2273ccdab156e5c654.research_question: How can general-purpose image-text pretraining be enhanced to produce representations that are effective for both dense spatial understanding tasks and global vision tasks, enabling strong off-the-shelf performance in a wide variety of computer vision applications?
02ddfe4c6da5890fcba72e2273ccdab156e5c654.hypothesis: Combining high-quality synthetic image captions with noisy web captions, together with integrating self-distillation and masked image modeling losses into a contrastive image-text pretraining framework, will result in image-text models that achieve spatially-aware and discriminative representations, leading to improved performance on both dense and global vision tasks.
02ddfe4c6da5890fcba72e2273ccdab156e5c654.proposed_method: A new pretraining framework, Text-Image Pretraining with Spatial awareness (TIPS), will be developed to jointly optimize for spatially-aware and globally discriminative image representations. The approach will enhance weak textual supervision by generating synthetic image captions using state-of-the-art captioning models, and combine these with noisy web captions via a dual embedding strategy in the vision transformer, introducing separate [CLS] tokens for each caption type. The method will further integrate self-distillation, where local crops of the input image are encouraged to match the global embedding via a teacher-student setup with exponential moving average updates, and masked image modeling, where patch embeddings are trained to reconstruct masked regions using prototype-based losses. The total loss will be a weighted sum of dual contrastive losses, self-distillation, and masked image modeling objectives. The architecture will leverage a scalable Vision Transformer backbone, with adaptations for efficient training and spatial feature extraction.
02ddfe4c6da5890fcba72e2273ccdab156e5c654.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a curated dataset of approximately 117 million image-text pairs, sourced and filtered from large-scale web data (WebLI), with near-duplicates to evaluation sets removed. The TIPS models will be evaluated off-the-shelf (frozen features) across 8 tasks and 16 datasets, including semantic segmentation (PASCAL VOC, ADE20k), monocular depth estimation and surface normal estimation (NYUv2, NAVI), image classification (ImageNet-1K), fine-grained and instance-level retrieval (Universal Embeddings Dataset), and multimodal retrieval (Flickr30K, COCO, DOCCI). Baselines will include state-of-the-art self-supervised, weakly-supervised, and supervised models such as DINOv2, MAE, iBOT, CLIP, OpenCLIP, SigLIP, MaskCLIP, SILC, EVA-CLIP, and ViT-g trained on JFT-3B. Evaluation metrics will include mean Intersection over Union (mIoU), RMSE for depth, angular RMSE for normals, recall@1 for retrieval, and top-1 accuracy for classification. Ablation studies will isolate the effects of synthetic captions, dual embedding, self-distillation, and masking losses.
02ddfe4c6da5890fcba72e2273ccdab156e5c654.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a dual embedding strategy that leverages both synthetic and noisy web captions in image-text pretraining, enabling the model to learn both object-centric and spatially-aware representations. It is the first to combine contrastive image-text learning with both self-distillation and masked image modeling within a unified framework, demonstrating positive synergies for dense prediction tasks. The approach shows that synthetic captions significantly enhance spatial understanding, and the dual embedding with dedicated loss functions allows flexible adaptation to different downstream tasks. The method achieves state-of-the-art or highly competitive results across a broad spectrum of dense and global vision tasks, surpassing existing image-text and self-supervised models in several cases, and enabling strong off-the-shelf performance for both image-only and image-text applications.

02f4516502bc0d05fb8971687f37c5f319ca2704.title: Diffusion for World Modeling: Visual Details Matter in Atari
02f4516502bc0d05fb8971687f37c5f319ca2704.research_question: Can diffusion models, when adapted for world modeling, improve the fidelity of visual details and agent performance in reinforcement learning environments compared to existing discrete latent variable approaches?
02f4516502bc0d05fb8971687f37c5f319ca2704.hypothesis: Employing diffusion models as world models for reinforcement learning will enable more accurate modeling of environment dynamics, particularly in preserving critical visual details, leading to improved agent performance and sample efficiency relative to world models based on discrete latent variables.
02f4516502bc0d05fb8971687f37c5f319ca2704.proposed_method: A diffusion-based world model will be developed, leveraging the EDM (Elucidated Diffusion Models) framework for stable and efficient generation of future environment observations conditioned on past observations and actions. The model will use a U-Net architecture, conditioning on a buffer of past frames and actions, and will be trained with an adaptive loss that mixes signal and noise based on the noise schedule, as per Karras et al. (2022). The reverse diffusion process will be used to generate next-step observations in an autoregressive manner, enabling long-horizon imagination. A separate reward and termination model will be trained using CNN-LSTM architectures to predict scalar outcomes, and an actor-critic RL agent will be trained entirely within the imagined trajectories generated by the diffusion world model. The method will also explore practical trade-offs in the number of denoising steps and sampling schemes to balance visual fidelity and computational efficiency.
02f4516502bc0d05fb8971687f37c5f319ca2704.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Atari 100k benchmark, encompassing 26 diverse games, with agents limited to 100,000 real environment steps before evaluation. The proposed diffusion world model will be compared against state-of-the-art world model baselines such as STORM, DreamerV3, IRIS, TWM, and SimPLe, using mean and interquartile mean human-normalized scores as primary evaluation metrics. Each experiment will be run with multiple random seeds, and the computational setup will be standardized (e.g., single Nvidia RTX 4090 GPU). Additional qualitative and quantitative analyses will be performed to compare visual consistency and compounding error against discrete latent world models. The approach will also be tested on a large-scale static dataset from Counter-Strike: Global Offensive (CS:GO) to assess scalability and generalization, with upsampling diffusion models employed for higher resolution outputs.
02f4516502bc0d05fb8971687f37c5f319ca2704.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first use of diffusion models as world models for online reinforcement learning in imagination, demonstrating that such models can preserve critical visual details and improve agent performance over discrete latent variable approaches. The method achieves state-of-the-art results on the Atari 100k benchmark for agents trained entirely within a world model, and provides a stable, efficient framework for long-horizon imagination with minimal denoising steps. Additionally, the approach enables the creation of interactive neural game engines from static gameplay data, showcasing the scalability and versatility of diffusion-based world models.

02f6240cab482a2d559a2b1fc85ba25051abebc6.title: Norm-guided latent space exploration for text-to-image generation
02f6240cab482a2d559a2b1fc85ba25051abebc6.research_question: How can the structure of the latent seed space in text-to-image diffusion models be better exploited to improve the quality and efficiency of image generation, particularly for rare concepts and few-shot learning scenarios?
02f6240cab482a2d559a2b1fc85ba25051abebc6.hypothesis: Guiding latent space exploration in text-to-image diffusion models using a norm-based prior derived from the statistical properties of the seed distribution will result in higher-quality image generation, improved semantic fidelity for rare concepts, and more efficient data augmentation for few-shot and long-tail learning tasks.
02f6240cab482a2d559a2b1fc85ba25051abebc6.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed for latent space exploration in text-to-image diffusion models, leveraging a norm-based prior derived from the chi distribution of high-dimensional Gaussian seed vectors. The method will introduce a new interpolation technique between latent seeds by formulating an optimization problem that maximizes the likelihood of the interpolation path under the norm-based prior, resulting in a non-Euclidean metric structure over the seed space. This approach will be extended to define centroids (Fréchet means) for sets of seeds, again using the new metric, and solved via discretized optimization with constraints on step size. The resulting centroids and interpolation paths will be used to generate new seeds for image synthesis, and can serve as improved initializations for further seed optimization algorithms such as SeedSelect. The entire optimization will be implemented efficiently using gradient-based methods (e.g., Adam optimizer) and soft penalty terms for constraints.
02f6240cab482a2d559a2b1fc85ba25051abebc6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Stable Diffusion model as the primary text-to-image diffusion framework. Evaluation will include direct assessment of image quality and semantic content for images generated via the proposed interpolation and centroid methods, using metrics such as FID (Fréchet Inception Distance) and classification accuracy with a pre-trained classifier. Benchmarks will include rare concept generation (using ImageNet1k classes with varying prevalence in LAION2B), few-shot classification (on CUB-200, miniImageNet, and CIFAR-FS), and long-tail classification (using ImageNet-LT). Baselines will include standard Euclidean and spherical interpolation/centroid methods, as well as SeedSelect and other state-of-the-art semantic data augmentation and long-tail learning methods. Experimental protocols will involve generating synthetic samples from few real images, training classifiers on both real and synthetic data, and measuring performance in terms of accuracy, FID, and generation speed. Additional experiments will test the impact of the proposed method as initialization for SeedSelect, measuring convergence time and final image quality.
02f6240cab482a2d559a2b1fc85ba25051abebc6.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a closed-form, norm-based prior for guiding latent space exploration in high-dimensional seed spaces of diffusion models, enabling efficient and effective interpolation and centroid computation without requiring additional data or model retraining. The method defines a new non-Euclidean metric structure over the latent space, leading to improved image quality and semantic fidelity, especially for rare concepts. The approach achieves state-of-the-art results on few-shot and long-tail learning benchmarks, while also significantly reducing generation and optimization time compared to prior methods. The framework is simple, generalizable, and can be applied to pre-trained diffusion models without fine-tuning.

02fa77e4f355198cb4270f6d4a07517bf09c46dd.title: Chronos: Learning the Language of Time Series
02fa77e4f355198cb4270f6d4a07517bf09c46dd.research_question: Can a general-purpose, pretrained language model framework be developed for probabilistic time series forecasting, leveraging large-scale data and minimal architectural changes, to achieve strong in-domain and zero-shot forecasting performance across diverse datasets?
02fa77e4f355198cb4270f6d4a07517bf09c46dd.hypothesis: A language modeling framework that tokenizes time series data via scaling and quantization, and trains standard transformer-based language models on these tokenized sequences, will enable effective probabilistic forecasting and strong zero-shot generalization, rivaling or surpassing both classical and deep learning baselines without requiring time-series-specific architectural modifications.
02fa77e4f355198cb4270f6d4a07517bf09c46dd.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a framework that adapts existing transformer-based language models for probabilistic time series forecasting by tokenizing real-valued time series into discrete tokens. This is achieved through a two-step process: first, each time series is normalized using mean scaling to address varying scales; second, the normalized values are quantized into a fixed number of bins, forming a finite vocabulary suitable for language modeling. The resulting token sequences, augmented with special tokens (PAD, EOS), are used to train encoder-decoder or decoder-only transformer architectures (e.g., T5, GPT-2) using a standard cross-entropy loss over the categorical distribution of tokens. During inference, the model autoregressively samples token sequences, which are then dequantized and unscaled to produce probabilistic forecasts. The approach deliberately omits explicit time or frequency features, treating time series as generic sequences.
02fa77e4f355198cb4270f6d4a07517bf09c46dd.experiment_details: Experiments will involve pretraining models of varying sizes (20M to 710M parameters) on a large, curated collection of public time series datasets, supplemented by synthetic data generated via Gaussian processes and data augmentation techniques such as TSMixup. Evaluation will be conducted on a benchmark suite of 42 datasets, covering both in-domain (datasets seen during training) and zero-shot (unseen) forecasting tasks. Baselines will include classical local models (e.g., ARIMA, ETS), deep learning models (e.g., DeepAR, TFT, PatchTST), and recent LLM-based forecasters. Metrics will focus on probabilistic forecasting accuracy, such as quantile-based scores and likelihood-based measures. Key experimental details include uniform quantization, use of both encoder-decoder and decoder-only architectures, and comprehensive ablation studies on tokenization and augmentation strategies.
02fa77e4f355198cb4270f6d4a07517bf09c46dd.novelty_claims: The proposed framework claims novelty by demonstrating that minimal modifications—specifically, scaling and quantization for tokenization—allow standard language models to serve as effective probabilistic time series forecasters. Unlike prior work, the method requires no time-series-specific architectural changes, explicit time features, or task-specific fine-tuning, and achieves strong zero-shot performance with relatively modest model sizes. The approach also introduces a scalable data augmentation pipeline (TSMixup and KernelSynth) to address the scarcity of diverse time series data, and establishes a new benchmark for generalist, pretrained time series models.

030eddc0177a4569bf01925d6d43871636fab993.title: Learning from Interval Targets
030eddc0177a4569bf01925d6d43871636fab993.research_question: How can regression models be effectively trained when only interval targets, rather than precise target values, are available? What theoretical guarantees and practical algorithms can enable learning in this weakly supervised setting, especially when standard regression loss functions are not directly applicable?
030eddc0177a4569bf01925d6d43871636fab993.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that regression models can achieve strong generalization and low error when trained with loss functions specifically designed for interval targets, particularly by leveraging smoothness constraints on the hypothesis class. Furthermore, incorporating minmax formulations and smoothness-aware constraints can yield improved performance and tighter error bounds compared to naive interval-based approaches.
030eddc0177a4569bf01925d6d43871636fab993.proposed_method: The proposed methodology consists of two main approaches for learning from interval targets. First, a projection loss is introduced, where for each input, the model's prediction is penalized only if it falls outside the provided interval, using a loss function evaluated at the nearest interval boundary. This projection loss is minimized empirically, and theoretical analysis is conducted to derive non-asymptotic generalization bounds that depend on the smoothness (Lipschitz constant) of the hypothesis class and the quality of the intervals. Second, a novel minmax learning formulation is developed, where the model minimizes the maximum possible loss with respect to the worst-case label within each interval. This is further refined by restricting the worst-case labels to those generated by smooth hypotheses, leading to a constrained minmax problem. Alternative optimization strategies, such as regularization and pseudo-labeling with a finite set of smooth hypotheses, are proposed to make the minmax objective tractable.
030eddc0177a4569bf01925d6d43871636fab993.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five public datasets from the UCI Machine Learning Repository and 18 additional tabular regression benchmarks. Interval targets will be generated using various algorithms to simulate different real-world scenarios. Models to be evaluated include standard multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs), Lipschitz-constrained MLPs (using spectral normalization to control smoothness), and the proposed projection loss, minmax, PL(Mean), and PL(Max) methods. Baselines will include naive midpoint regression and standard supervised learning where possible. Evaluation metrics will primarily be mean absolute error (MAE) on held-out test sets. The effect of varying the Lipschitz constant will be systematically studied to validate theoretical predictions about the relationship between smoothness and generalization.
030eddc0177a4569bf01925d6d43871636fab993.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretically grounded framework for regression with interval targets, including new generalization bounds that relax prior restrictive assumptions such as small ambiguity degree and realizability. The projection loss and minmax formulations are shown to be compatible with gradient-based optimization and provide practical learning objectives for interval supervision. The analysis reveals how hypothesis class smoothness can reduce effective interval size, leading to tighter error bounds and improved empirical performance. The approach also demonstrates that constraining worst-case labels to smooth hypotheses can outperform unconstrained minmax methods, and that Lipschitz-constrained neural networks can significantly enhance learning from interval targets.

03630ef6f249b9945c40da9c5cf6b76621ae7a4f.title: Interactive fingerprinting codes and the hardness of preventing false discovery
03630ef6f249b9945c40da9c5cf6b76621ae7a4f.research_question: What are the fundamental computational limits for accurately answering a large number of adaptively chosen statistical queries based on a finite sample from an unknown distribution, and how do these limits relate to privacy guarantees in data analysis?
03630ef6f249b9945c40da9c5cf6b76621ae7a4f.hypothesis: Assuming the existence of one-way functions, no computationally efficient algorithm can accurately answer more than O(n^2) adaptively chosen statistical queries given n samples from an unknown distribution, and any such algorithm that achieves this threshold is necessarily vulnerable to privacy breaches.
03630ef6f249b9945c40da9c5cf6b76621ae7a4f.proposed_method: A new approach will be developed that leverages interactive fingerprinting codes (IFPCs) to establish hardness results for answering adaptively chosen statistical queries. The methodology involves constructing a challenge distribution and an adaptive analyst who, by interacting with any efficient oracle, can reconstruct the sample set, thereby exposing the oracle's limitations. The IFPCs are constructed with a new Fourier-analytic analysis that enables robust tracing of colluding users with optimal code length O(n^2) and robustness to up to a 1/2 fraction of errors. The analysis ensures both soundness (few false accusations) and completeness (all colluding users are eventually identified), and the construction is generalized to handle various parameter regimes. The connection between IFPCs and adaptive data analysis will be formalized, and the resulting framework will be used to derive computational and information-theoretic lower bounds.
03630ef6f249b9945c40da9c5cf6b76621ae7a4f.experiment_details: Theoretical experiments will be conducted by designing adversarial analysts and challenge distributions within the statistical query model, where the dimensionality of the data grows with the sample size. The analysis will compare the number of queries that can be answered accurately by computationally efficient oracles versus information-theoretically unbounded oracles. Evaluation metrics include the number of adaptively chosen queries answered accurately, the robustness of the fingerprinting code (fraction of errors tolerated), and the rate of false accusations. Baselines for comparison include previous constructions of non-interactive and interactive fingerprinting codes, as well as differentially private algorithms capable of answering O(n^2) queries. Theoretical proofs will be provided to demonstrate the tightness of the bounds and the privacy implications.
03630ef6f249b9945c40da9c5cf6b76621ae7a4f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces interactive fingerprinting codes as the key combinatorial object for establishing computational hardness in adaptive data analysis, analogous to the role of non-interactive codes in differential privacy. A new Fourier-analytic method is developed for analyzing both interactive and non-interactive fingerprinting codes, yielding simpler, more flexible, and stronger hardness results, including optimal robustness to up to a 1/2 fraction of errors. The approach closes the gap between previous upper and lower bounds, establishing a nearly tight O(n^2) threshold for computationally efficient algorithms. The results demonstrate a sharp phase transition: below this threshold, differential privacy is achievable, while above it, even minimal privacy is impossible for efficient algorithms.

0369023acce546aa8ceabbbc36a17a2f2845ebe3.title: Proactive Privacy Amnesia for Large Language Models: Safeguarding PII with Negligible Impact on Model Utility
0369023acce546aa8ceabbbc36a17a2f2845ebe3.research_question: How can large language models be protected from leaking personally identifiable information (PII) under adversarial attacks, while maintaining high model utility and performance?
0369023acce546aa8ceabbbc36a17a2f2845ebe3.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that selectively forgetting only the key elements within memorized PII sequences, identified through sensitivity analysis, and compensating for any resulting performance loss via memory implanting, can effectively safeguard PII in large language models without significantly degrading their utility.
0369023acce546aa8ceabbbc36a17a2f2845ebe3.proposed_method: A novel framework, Proactive Privacy Amnesia (PPA), will be developed to proactively protect PII in large language models. The method consists of three main components: (1) Sensitivity Analysis, which identifies the key elements within memorized PII sequences by calculating a memorization factor for each token based on its contribution to the model's retention of the sequence; (2) Selective Forgetting, which applies targeted unlearning (via loss maximization) to only those key elements, rather than the entire PII sequence, thereby minimizing collateral damage to model performance; and (3) Memory Implanting, which introduces fabricated or substitute non-sensitive information to compensate for any utility loss caused by forgetting, ensuring the model retains its general capabilities. The approach allows for flexible adjustment of the number of forgotten elements to balance privacy and utility.
0369023acce546aa8ceabbbc36a17a2f2845ebe3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using fine-tuned LLaMA2-7b and LLaMA3-8b models on two datasets: the Enron email dataset and the Fraud email dataset. The evaluation will involve defending against multiple PII-targeted attacks, including input rephrasing, probing, and soft prompt attacks, targeting phone numbers and physical addresses. Baseline defense methods for comparison will include Empty Response, Error Injection, Unlearning, and DEPN (memory editing). Evaluation metrics will comprise a custom PII risk score (using Levenshtein distance for phone numbers and a structured scoring table for addresses), exact match score, model perplexity, and an email completion score assessed by GPT-4o. Ablation studies will be performed to analyze the contributions of each stage and the effect of varying the number of forgotten elements.
0369023acce546aa8ceabbbc36a17a2f2845ebe3.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the concept of the memorization factor to identify key elements within PII sequences that are most critical for model retention, enabling targeted forgetting. PPA is the first method to combine sensitivity analysis, selective forgetting, and memory implanting in a unified framework to proactively defend against PII extraction while preserving model utility. The method provides a flexible trade-off between privacy protection and performance by tuning the number of forgotten elements. Extensive experiments demonstrate that this approach achieves superior defense against PII-targeted attacks with negligible impact on model utility, outperforming existing state-of-the-art defensive techniques.

036aef17a8c2c03202170aa85fd7be1dba974202.title: MACE: Higher Order Equivariant Message Passing Neural Networks for Fast and Accurate Force Fields
036aef17a8c2c03202170aa85fd7be1dba974202.research_question: How can fast and accurate force fields for atomistic simulations be developed using neural network architectures that overcome the scalability and computational limitations of existing message passing neural networks, while maintaining or improving predictive accuracy and generalization?
036aef17a8c2c03202170aa85fd7be1dba974202.hypothesis: Employing higher order equivariant message passing in neural network architectures enables the construction of force fields that are both computationally efficient and highly accurate, reducing the number of required message passing iterations and improving generalization compared to traditional two-body message passing approaches.
036aef17a8c2c03202170aa85fd7be1dba974202.proposed_method: A novel neural network architecture, termed MACE, will be developed based on the message passing neural network (MPNN) framework. The core innovation is the hierarchical expansion of messages to include higher body order interactions, specifically up to four-body messages, using equivariant features under the O(3) group. Message construction will involve embedding edges with learnable radial bases, spherical harmonics, and chemical element embeddings, followed by pooling and tensor product operations to efficiently generate higher order features. The architecture will employ efficient parameterizations and tensor contractions to circumvent the exponential scaling typically associated with many-body interactions. The update step will use linear functions with residual connections, and the readout phase will hierarchically decompose site energies using invariant features to ensure physical invariance. The model will be designed for computational efficiency, parallelizability, and scalability to systems with multiple chemical elements.
036aef17a8c2c03202170aa85fd7be1dba974202.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several benchmark datasets for molecular force fields, including rMD17 (revised MD17), 3BPA (3-(benzyloxy)pyridin-2-amine), and AcAc (acetylacetone). The model will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as NequIP, BOTNet, Allegro, GemNet, and PaiNN, using metrics like mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean square error (RMSE) for energies and forces. Evaluation will include both in-domain and out-of-domain generalization (e.g., extrapolation to higher temperatures and dihedral slices), as well as computational efficiency measured by evaluation latency on NVIDIA A100 GPUs. Ablation studies will assess the impact of body order, equivariance, and number of message passing layers. Hyperparameters and training details will be specified for reproducibility, and multiple random seeds will be used to report standard deviations.
036aef17a8c2c03202170aa85fd7be1dba974202.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a systematic and computationally efficient method for higher order equivariant message passing in neural networks for atomistic simulations. By disentangling body order from the number of message passing iterations, the method achieves high accuracy with only two layers, enabling faster training and evaluation as well as improved parallelizability. The architecture efficiently incorporates many-body interactions without incurring exponential computational cost, and demonstrates superior generalization and extrapolation capabilities on challenging benchmarks. The method achieves or exceeds state-of-the-art accuracy while being significantly faster than existing models.

03755613d50e1958a97bfaad2efb976f786fbb70.title: VALOR: Vision-Audio-Language Omni-Perception Pretraining Model and Dataset
03755613d50e1958a97bfaad2efb976f786fbb70.research_question: How can a unified pretraining framework be developed to enable comprehensive understanding and generation across vision, audio, and language modalities, and what are the benefits of leveraging large-scale, strongly correlated tri-modal datasets for such models?
03755613d50e1958a97bfaad2efb976f786fbb70.hypothesis: Jointly modeling relationships among vision, audio, and language in an end-to-end framework, using strongly correlated tri-modal data and novel pretraining tasks, will significantly improve generalization and performance on a wide range of multimodal downstream tasks compared to dual-modality or weakly correlated approaches.
03755613d50e1958a97bfaad2efb976f786fbb70.proposed_method: A novel omni-perception pretraining model, VALOR, will be constructed to jointly encode and align vision, audio, and language modalities. The architecture will consist of three separate encoders for each modality (vision, audio, and text) and a multimodal decoder for conditional text generation. Two pretext tasks will be designed: Multimodal Grouping Alignment (MGA), which projects all three modalities into a common space and establishes fine-grained alignment via contrastive learning; and Multimodal Grouping Captioning (MGC), which reconstructs masked text tokens conditioned on vision, audio, or both using cross-attention in the decoder. The model will leverage a modality grouping strategy to enable flexible adaptation to various input combinations, supporting both discriminative and generative downstream tasks.
03755613d50e1958a97bfaad2efb976f786fbb70.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a newly constructed large-scale tri-modal dataset, VALOR-1M, containing one million videos with human-annotated audiovisual captions, as well as public dual-modality datasets such as WebVid-2.5M, CC3M, CC14M, and HD VILA 10M. The model will be evaluated on a broad range of downstream tasks, including text-to-video, text-to-audio, and text-to-audiovisual retrieval, video/audio/audiovisual captioning, and question answering, using benchmarks such as MSRVTT, DiDeMo, ActivityNet, LSMDC, VATEX, ClothoV1, AudioCaps, and the proposed VALOR-32K. Baselines will include state-of-the-art dual- and tri-modal models, with evaluation metrics such as Recall@K for retrieval, BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, and SPICE for captioning, and accuracy for question answering. Ablation studies will assess the contributions of each modality, pretraining task, and dataset.
03755613d50e1958a97bfaad2efb976f786fbb70.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first large-scale, high-quality, human-annotated tri-modal dataset (VALOR-1M) for vision-audio-language pretraining, and a unified model architecture capable of end-to-end learning across all three modalities. The modality grouping strategy and dual pretraining tasks (MGA and MGC) enable flexible adaptation to a variety of input combinations and downstream tasks. The method claims to achieve new state-of-the-art results across a wide range of cross-modal benchmarks, demonstrating superior generalization and efficiency compared to previous dual-modality or weakly correlated tri-modal approaches.

037613dd9c9cb48cdfd9deb6023795a5aa1fb837.title: Labeling Neural Representations with Inverse Recognition
037613dd9c9cb48cdfd9deb6023795a5aa1fb837.research_question: How can neural representations within deep neural networks be systematically labeled and interpreted in terms of human-understandable concepts, without reliance on segmentation masks or high computational cost, and with statistical significance guarantees?
037613dd9c9cb48cdfd9deb6023795a5aa1fb837.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that neural representations can be effectively and efficiently explained by identifying compositional concepts that maximize their discriminative capacity, as measured by a robust similarity metric, and that these explanations can be made statistically significant and interpretable without requiring segmentation masks.
037613dd9c9cb48cdfd9deb6023795a5aa1fb837.proposed_method: A scalable framework is developed for labeling neural representations by leveraging their ability to discriminate between human-understandable concepts, using only labeled data. The method defines neural representations as scalar functions over the data domain and concepts as binary functions corresponding to labeled attributes. The core approach involves searching for compositional concepts—logical combinations of atomic concepts (using AND, OR, NOT)—that maximize the Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic (AUC) similarity between the representation and the concept. Beam search is employed to efficiently explore the space of compositional concepts up to a predetermined formula length, with constraints on the fraction of data points covered by the concept to balance precision and generality. Statistical significance of the resulting explanation is assessed using the Mann–Whitney U test, reporting p-values to ensure the robustness of the explanation.
037613dd9c9cb48cdfd9deb6023795a5aa1fb837.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on multiple deep neural network architectures, including ResNet18, GoogleNet, EfficientNetB0, ViT B16, MaskRCNN ResNet50 FPN, FCN ResNet50, and DenseNet161, using datasets such as ImageNet 2012 and MS COCO. For classification models, explanations are generated for output neurons corresponding to known classes, while for segmentation models, pixel-wise confidences are aggregated. Baselines include Network Dissection and Compositional Explanations of Neurons (CompExp), with evaluation metrics focusing on explanation accuracy (matching identified classes to ground truth), AUC similarity, and computational cost (runtime). Additional experiments include auditing for spurious correlations by augmenting datasets with new concepts, explaining model circuits, and constructing handcrafted circuits using fuzzy logic operators. Statistical significance of explanations is routinely tested, and the trade-off between explanation simplicity and precision is systematically explored.
037613dd9c9cb48cdfd9deb6023795a5aa1fb837.novelty_claims: The proposed approach eliminates the need for segmentation masks and is applicable to diverse neuron types, reducing computational complexity compared to prior methods. It introduces an interpretable similarity metric (AUC) for explanation quality, incorporates statistical significance testing for explanation robustness, and supports compositional explanations using logical operators. The method enables efficient model auditing for spurious correlations, facilitates circuit-level interpretability, and allows for the manual construction of symbolic-like circuits from neural representations. Empirical results demonstrate superior or comparable explanation accuracy and significantly reduced computational cost relative to established baselines.

0399533de2d1d21f456663d1bd5355c8b3c32a58.title: Unlearn What You Want to Forget: Efficient Unlearning for LLMs
0399533de2d1d21f456663d1bd5355c8b3c32a58.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) efficiently and effectively remove the influence of specific user-requested data (such as privacy-related or erroneous data) without retraining the entire model, while maintaining predictive quality and supporting sequences of unlearning operations?
0399533de2d1d21f456663d1bd5355c8b3c32a58.hypothesis: It is possible to efficiently unlearn specific data from LLMs by introducing lightweight, parameter-efficient unlearning layers trained with a selective teacher-student objective, and by fusing multiple such layers to handle sequential deletion requests, thereby preserving model performance on retained data and tasks.
0399533de2d1d21f456663d1bd5355c8b3c32a58.proposed_method: A novel unlearning framework for LLMs will be developed by integrating lightweight unlearning layers into transformer architectures. These layers will be trained using a selective teacher-student objective: the student model (augmented with unlearning layers) is optimized to mimic the teacher (original model) on retained data while diverging on data to be forgotten, balancing this with the original task and language modeling objectives. Only the unlearning layers are updated during this process, leaving the main model parameters unchanged, thus enabling efficient adaptation. To handle multiple or sequential unlearning requests, a fusion mechanism will be designed to merge the weights of different unlearning layers, using a regression-based approach to create a unified layer that forgets all requested data. This fusion is performed without extra training, relying on precomputed hidden representations of the forgotten data, ensuring privacy and efficiency.
0399533de2d1d21f456663d1bd5355c8b3c32a58.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both classification and generation tasks using the IMDB sentiment classification dataset and the SAMSum dialogue summarization dataset. The approach will be evaluated on T5-base and T5-3B models, with unlearning requests simulated by removing data associated with specific entities (e.g., names of people or movies) or mislabeled examples. Baseline methods will include re-training, fine-tuning, SISA (sharded, isolated, sliced, and aggregated training), reverse-gradient, and model editing (MEND). Evaluation metrics will encompass task performance on test, retained, and forgotten sets, masked language modeling loss on forgotten data, updating time, and resistance to member inference attacks. Experiments will also assess the ability to handle sequences of unlearning requests and perform ablation studies on the objective components.
0399533de2d1d21f456663d1bd5355c8b3c32a58.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a parameter-efficient, dynamic unlearning framework for LLMs that avoids full-model retraining by leveraging selective teacher-student objectives and adapter-based unlearning layers. The fusion mechanism for merging multiple unlearning layers to handle sequential or compound deletion requests is novel, enabling efficient and scalable unlearning. The approach is claimed to outperform state-of-the-art baselines in both forgetting effectiveness and computational efficiency, while maintaining or improving performance on retained and test data.

039c0f0b4142823fe214ddf2470230e211c7b8ee.title: STAR: A Benchmark for Situated Reasoning in Real-World Videos
039c0f0b4142823fe214ddf2470230e211c7b8ee.research_question: How can machine intelligence be evaluated and advanced in its ability to perform situated reasoning in real-world video scenarios, specifically involving dynamic, compositional, and logical understanding of human-object interactions, temporal sequences, action prediction, and feasibility inference?
039c0f0b4142823fe214ddf2470230e211c7b8ee.hypothesis: Current state-of-the-art visual reasoning and video question answering models are insufficient for robust situated reasoning in real-world videos, and a benchmark that combines structured situation abstraction with logic-grounded question answering will reveal key challenges and guide the development of more capable reasoning systems.
039c0f0b4142823fe214ddf2470230e211c7b8ee.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark will be constructed to evaluate situated reasoning in real-world videos, focusing on four core reasoning skills: interaction understanding, temporal sequence reasoning, action prediction, and feasibility inference. The methodology involves curating a large-scale dataset of trimmed video clips sourced from human activity datasets, with each video annotated using situation hypergraphs that capture entities (persons, objects), actions, and relationships. Questions and answers will be procedurally generated using templates and functional programs grounded in these hypergraphs, ensuring explicit, step-by-step reasoning logic. Distractor answers will be carefully designed to break statistical shortcuts and balance answer distributions, while grammar and rationality will be validated through automated tools and human annotation. Additionally, a diagnostic neuro-symbolic model will be developed, integrating modules for visual perception, situation abstraction via transformer-based action transition modeling, language parsing to functional programs, and symbolic program execution on predicted hypergraphs.
039c0f0b4142823fe214ddf2470230e211c7b8ee.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the proposed benchmark, which consists of approximately 22,000 video clips, 144,000 situation hypergraphs, and 60,000 multi-choice situated reasoning questions with aligned programs and answers. Multiple baseline models will be trained and evaluated, including language-only models (LSTM, BERT), vision-language models (CNN-LSTM, CNN-BERT), and state-of-the-art video question answering models (LCGN, HCRN, ClipBERT), all trained from scratch on the benchmark's training and validation sets. Evaluation metrics will primarily involve average answer accuracy across four question types, with detailed analysis of model performance on each reasoning skill. The neuro-symbolic diagnostic model will be assessed under various controlled conditions (oracle, perfect perception, perfect abstraction, etc.) to isolate bottlenecks and challenges in visual perception, structured abstraction, and reasoning.
039c0f0b4142823fe214ddf2470230e211c7b8ee.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces a real-world, large-scale, and systematically controlled evaluation platform for situated reasoning, uniquely combining dynamic video situations, structured hypergraph-based situation abstraction, and logic-grounded, programmatic question answering. The benchmark covers a wider range of reasoning tasks than prior datasets, including interaction, sequence, prediction, and feasibility questions, and employs rigorous debiasing and balancing strategies to break common statistical shortcuts. The diagnostic neuro-symbolic model provides a modular, interpretable framework for disentangling and analyzing the contributions of perception, abstraction, language understanding, and reasoning, offering new insights and directions for the development of robust situated reasoning systems.

03a281a176413ed4d140293edc5bf04a3ad7a1f1.title: DragDiffusion: Harnessing Diffusion Models for Interactive Point-Based Image Editing
03a281a176413ed4d140293edc5bf04a3ad7a1f1.research_question: How can interactive point-based image editing be made more accurate, controllable, and generalizable across diverse image domains using large-scale generative models?
03a281a176413ed4d140293edc5bf04a3ad7a1f1.hypothesis: Harnessing large-scale pretrained diffusion models and optimizing the latent at a single, carefully selected diffusion step, combined with identity-preserving fine-tuning and reference-latent-control, will enable accurate, efficient, and robust interactive point-based image editing that generalizes well to both real and synthetic images.
03a281a176413ed4d140293edc5bf04a3ad7a1f1.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed for interactive point-based image editing by leveraging pretrained diffusion models, specifically Stable Diffusion. The method begins with identity-preserving fine-tuning of the diffusion model's UNet using LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) to ensure the model encodes the input image's features accurately and maintains identity during editing. Next, given user-specified handle and target points (and optionally a mask), the diffusion latent at a single, empirically selected step (e.g., t=35) is optimized via gradient descent to move the handle points to their targets while preserving unmasked regions. This optimization alternates between motion supervision (using UNet feature maps to guide the movement) and point tracking (updating handle point locations in feature space). Finally, a reference-latent-control technique is employed during the denoising process: self-attention modules in the UNet are guided by the original image's latent, replacing key and value vectors to maintain coherence and identity in the edited result.
03a281a176413ed4d140293edc5bf04a3ad7a1f1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Stable Diffusion 1.5 model and several of its variants (e.g., Counterfeit-V2.5, Majicmix Realistic, Interior Design Supermix). The proposed method will be evaluated on a newly introduced benchmark, DRAGBENCH, which contains diverse real and synthetic images with annotated drag instructions (handle/target points and editable masks). Baseline comparisons will be made against DRAGGAN, a GAN-based interactive editing method, using an ensemble of pretrained StyleGANs selected by CLIP similarity for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics will include Image Fidelity (IF, based on LPIPS) to measure identity preservation and Mean Distance (MD) to quantify the accuracy of point movement. Ablation studies will be performed on the number of inversion steps, fine-tuning steps, and UNet feature map selection, with both qualitative and quantitative analyses.
03a281a176413ed4d140293edc5bf04a3ad7a1f1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable interactive point-based image editing using diffusion models, overcoming the generalization limitations of GAN-based methods. It introduces a novel latent optimization strategy at a single diffusion step, significantly improving editing efficiency and spatial control. Two new techniques—identity-preserving fine-tuning via LoRA and reference-latent-control during denoising—are proposed to robustly preserve image identity and quality. Additionally, the first dedicated benchmark dataset for this task, DRAGBENCH, will be created to facilitate systematic evaluation and future research.

03ba7286bc9053c3441e8ab03538447b06bc6ecc.title: Diverse Prototypical Ensembles Improve Robustness to Subpopulation Shift
03ba7286bc9053c3441e8ab03538447b06bc6ecc.research_question: How can machine learning models be made more robust to subpopulation shifts in data distributions, particularly when explicit subgroup annotations or knowledge of subpopulation structure are unavailable?
03ba7286bc9053c3441e8ab03538447b06bc6ecc.hypothesis: Introducing a diversified ensemble of prototypical classifiers, each capturing different latent subpopulations within classes, will improve worst-group accuracy and overall robustness to subpopulation shifts, even in the absence of explicit subgroup annotations.
03ba7286bc9053c3441e8ab03538447b06bc6ecc.proposed_method: The proposed approach consists of a two-stage training pipeline. First, a feature extractor (e.g., ResNet-50 or BERT) is trained using standard empirical risk minimization (ERM) on the full training set to obtain robust feature representations. In the second stage, the linear classification head is replaced with a Diversified Prototypical Ensemble (DPE), which consists of multiple (N) distance-based prototype classifiers per class. Each prototype classifier is trained on a different class-balanced subset of the validation data, and predictions are aggregated across the ensemble. To ensure diversity among prototypes, an inter-prototype similarity (IPS) loss is introduced to decorrelate the representations of different prototypes within the same class, and bootstrap aggregation is used to further encourage diversity by exposing each prototype to different data distributions. The ensemble is trained end-to-end by sequentially optimizing the joint prototype and IPS loss for each new ensemble member, with all prototypes associated with previous stages kept fixed.
03ba7286bc9053c3441e8ab03538447b06bc6ecc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on nine real-world datasets spanning multiple domains and types of subpopulation shift, including WATERBIRDS, CELEBA, METASHIFT, IMAGENETBG, NICO++, LIVING17, CHEXPERT, CIVILCOMMENTS, and MULTINLI. Both scenarios with and without subgroup annotations will be evaluated. Baselines for comparison include ERM, CRT, ReWeightCRT, DFR, JTT, CnC, RWY, AFR, GroupDRO, SSA, and GAP, among others. The main evaluation metric is worst-group accuracy (WGA), with additional reporting of average accuracy to assess trade-offs. Hyperparameters will be tuned using a held-out subset of the validation set, and each experiment will be repeated with multiple random seeds to ensure stability. Ablation studies will investigate the effect of ensemble size, prototype diversification strategies, and sensitivity to hyperparameters.
03ba7286bc9053c3441e8ab03538447b06bc6ecc.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel, differentiable, end-to-end framework for subpopulation shift robustness that does not require explicit subgroup annotations or prior knowledge of subpopulation structure. The use of a diversified prototypical ensemble, with explicit diversity regularization and bootstrap aggregation, enables the automatic discovery and classification of latent subpopulations. This approach is claimed to outperform prior state-of-the-art methods in worst-group accuracy across a wide range of datasets and subpopulation shift scenarios, including challenging cases such as attribute imbalance and attribute generalization. The method is modular, scalable, and computationally efficient, providing a practical solution for robust machine learning in real-world settings where subgroup information is unavailable.

03e385b1a6fdb7bef5612feea44e44d5efd45bcc.title: Accelerating RL for LLM Reasoning with Optimal Advantage Regression
03e385b1a6fdb7bef5612feea44e44d5efd45bcc.research_question: Can reinforcement learning algorithms for large language model (LLM) reasoning be made more computationally efficient and scalable, particularly for long-context and complex reasoning tasks, without sacrificing performance?
03e385b1a6fdb7bef5612feea44e44d5efd45bcc.hypothesis: Directly approximating the optimal advantage function using offline sampling from a reference policy, followed by on-policy updates via least-squares regression with a single generation per prompt, will enable efficient and effective RL-based fine-tuning of LLMs for reasoning tasks, reducing computational overhead and memory usage while maintaining or improving performance.
03e385b1a6fdb7bef5612feea44e44d5efd45bcc.proposed_method: A novel two-stage policy optimization framework, termed A⋆-PO (Policy Optimization via Optimal Advantage Regression), will be developed. In the first stage, the optimal value function V⋆ for each training prompt will be estimated by generating N independent samples from a fixed reference policy and computing a closed-form expression involving the log-sum-exp of the rewards. This stage is performed entirely offline and can be parallelized without gradient computation. In the second stage, on-policy updates will be performed by collecting a single generation per prompt from the current policy and regressing the log-ratio of the policy and reference policy to the optimal advantage using a least-squares regression loss. The KL-regularized RL objective will be optimized without the need for explicit critic networks, multiple generations per prompt, or complex exploration strategies, and only a single regularization term based on KL divergence to the reference policy will be used.
03e385b1a6fdb7bef5612feea44e44d5efd45bcc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of mathematical reasoning benchmarks, including GSM8K (grade school math), MATH (high school competition problems), and competition-level datasets such as AMC, AIME, and HMMT. Multiple LLM sizes (Qwen2.5-1.5B, 3B, 7B) will be evaluated. Baselines for comparison will include PPO, GRPO, and REBEL, with evaluation metrics covering test accuracy, KL divergence to the base model, peak GPU memory usage, and total training time. For long-context reasoning, experiments will use the DeepSeek-R1 distilled Qwen-1.5B model with a context length of 16,384, and results will be reported on AIME and HMMT benchmarks using Avg@32 and Pass@32 metrics. Ablation studies will investigate the effect of the number of generations for value estimation, prompt filtering, and KL regularization coefficients.
03e385b1a6fdb7bef5612feea44e44d5efd45bcc.novelty_claims: The proposed method eliminates the need for explicit critic networks and multiple online generations per prompt, enabling a highly efficient RL training regime for LLMs. The approach uniquely leverages offline estimation of the optimal value function and a simple regression-based on-policy update, resulting in significant reductions in training time (up to 2×) and memory usage (over 30%) compared to leading baselines. Theoretical analysis provides formal performance guarantees, showing near-optimality without requiring sophisticated exploration or strong policy completeness assumptions. The method is also demonstrated to generalize well to out-of-domain and long-context reasoning tasks, and supports efficient filtering of unsolvable prompts.

03e57a54b5d12f7245ea449c8cf8153d84118021.title: NETS: A Non-Equilibrium Transport Sampler
03e57a54b5d12f7245ea449c8cf8153d84118021.research_question: How can unbiased and efficient sampling from unnormalized probability distributions, particularly in high-dimensional and non-log-concave settings, be achieved using non-equilibrium transport dynamics?
03e57a54b5d12f7245ea449c8cf8153d84118021.hypothesis: Introducing a learnable additional drift term into the non-equilibrium sampling dynamics, estimated via novel objective functions, will reduce the variance of importance weights and improve the effective sample size, enabling unbiased and efficient sampling from complex target distributions.
03e57a54b5d12f7245ea449c8cf8153d84118021.proposed_method: A novel sampling algorithm, the Non-Equilibrium Transport Sampler (NETS), will be developed to sample from unnormalized probability distributions. The method augments standard annealed Langevin dynamics with a learnable additional drift term, which is optimized to minimize the lag between the evolving sample distribution and the target distribution. The drift is estimated by minimizing objective functions derived from manipulations of the Fokker-Planck equation, including a physics-informed neural network (PINN) loss and an action-matching (AM) loss. These objectives can be estimated without backpropagating through the simulation of the stochastic differential equations (SDEs), allowing for scalable training. The algorithm supports post-training adaptation by tuning the diffusion coefficient and integration time-step to maximize the effective sample size.
03e57a54b5d12f7245ea449c8cf8153d84118021.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard sampling benchmarks, including a 40-mode Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) in 2 dimensions, high-dimensional GMMs, and statistical lattice field theory models with up to 400 dimensions. The performance of NETS will be compared against established baselines such as Annealed Importance Sampling (AIS), Flow Annealed Bootstrap (FAB), and Controlled Monte Carlo Diffusions (CMCD), among others. Evaluation metrics will include effective sample size (ESS), Wasserstein-2 distance (W2), and variance of importance weights. The experimental setup will involve annealing schedules, empirical estimation of objectives, and, where appropriate, the use of resampling strategies to control weight variance.
03e57a54b5d12f7245ea449c8cf8153d84118021.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new framework for unbiased sampling from unnormalized distributions by augmenting non-equilibrium Langevin dynamics with a learnable drift, optimized via novel objective functions that do not require backpropagation through SDE solutions. The PINN-based objective is shown to control both the Kullback-Leibler divergence and the variance of importance weights, and can be used off-policy. The method allows for post-training adaptation of diffusion parameters to further improve sampling efficiency. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior statistical efficiency and scalability compared to existing baselines, especially in high-dimensional and challenging settings.

03e8b6224ef5ec8bce483a139709b16ebe30cf34.title: Repetita Iuvant: Data Repetition Allows SGD to Learn High-Dimensional Multi-Index Functions
03e8b6224ef5ec8bce483a139709b16ebe30cf34.research_question: Can data repetition during training improve the efficiency of stochastic gradient descent (SGD) in learning high-dimensional multi-index functions, and what are the theoretical and practical implications for representation learning in neural networks under realistic training scenarios?
03e8b6224ef5ec8bce483a139709b16ebe30cf34.hypothesis: Allowing repeated processing of data samples during SGD training will significantly improve the computational efficiency and sample complexity required to learn high-dimensional multi-index functions, surpassing previously established theoretical limitations based on the Information and Leap exponents.
03e8b6224ef5ec8bce483a139709b16ebe30cf34.proposed_method: A detailed analytical and empirical investigation will be conducted into the training dynamics of two-layer (shallow) fully connected neural networks when trained with gradient-based algorithms that allow for data repetition. The method will implement a training routine where each data point is processed multiple times (specifically, at least twice) per epoch, as opposed to the idealized one-pass SGD scenario. The core algorithm will update the first-layer weights using a variant of extragradient or Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) steps, parameterized by a mixing coefficient (rho) that controls the influence of the current gradient. Theoretical analysis will focus on the evolution of the overlap between learned weights and the low-dimensional relevant subspace, with rigorous characterization of sample complexity scaling in terms of the input dimension and properties of the target function. Initialization will be fully agnostic, with first-layer weights drawn uniformly from the unit sphere and second-layer weights from a symmetric binary distribution.
03e8b6224ef5ec8bce483a139709b16ebe30cf34.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on high-dimensional synthetic datasets where inputs are drawn from Gaussian distributions and target functions are constructed as multi-index models with a small number of relevant directions. Both single-index and multi-index target functions, including polynomials and sparse parities, will be considered. Baseline comparisons will include standard one-pass SGD and variants with and without data repetition. Evaluation metrics will focus on the cosine similarity between learned weights and ground-truth relevant directions (weak recovery), as well as the number of iterations (sample complexity) required to achieve a specified correlation threshold. Experiments will systematically vary input dimension, minibatch size, and target function structure, with detailed numerical illustrations validating the theoretical predictions.
03e8b6224ef5ec8bce483a139709b16ebe30cf34.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a rigorous theoretical and empirical framework demonstrating that data repetition in SGD training enables efficient learning of high-dimensional multi-index functions, overcoming previously established limitations based on the Information and Leap exponents. It generalizes the concept of generative exponents to multi-index settings and shows that all polynomial multi-index functions can be learned with O(d) or O(d log d) sample complexity without any preprocessing or warm start. The approach identifies new classes of hard functions and reveals hierarchical learning mechanisms that emerge only when data repetition is permitted, extending beyond the classical staircase phenomena. This work challenges the prevailing consensus on SGD limitations and provides new insights into the representation learning capabilities of shallow neural networks under realistic training regimes.

03ec8d1d8f91dd727371512f9079cad31e202f66.title: (Predictable) performance bias in unsupervised anomaly detection
03ec8d1d8f91dd727371512f9079cad31e202f66.research_question: How does the composition of training datasets with respect to protected demographic attributes (such as gender, age, and race) affect the fairness and performance of unsupervised anomaly detection (UAD) models in medical imaging, and can performance disparities be systematically quantified and predicted?
03ec8d1d8f91dd727371512f9079cad31e202f66.hypothesis: Performance disparities in UAD models for medical imaging are systematically related to the representation of demographic subgroups in the training data, and these disparities persist even under balanced data conditions. Furthermore, it is hypothesized that some subgroups are inherently harder for UAD models to learn, leading to predictable bias patterns that can be quantified using appropriate metrics.
03ec8d1d8f91dd727371512f9079cad31e202f66.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical investigation will be conducted using state-of-the-art unsupervised anomaly detection models applied to large-scale public chest X-ray datasets. The methodology involves constructing training, validation, and test sets with controlled and varying proportions of protected attribute subgroups (gender, age, race), while maintaining consistent sample sizes and ensuring no patient overlap between splits. The study will introduce and utilize a novel evaluation metric, subgroup-AUROC (sAUROC), which quantifies subgroup-specific performance by computing the area under the ROC curve where the false positive rate is calculated per subgroup and the true positive rate across the whole population. Experiments will be repeated across multiple random seeds to ensure statistical robustness, and intersectional subgroup analyses will be performed to assess compounding effects of multiple protected attributes.
03ec8d1d8f91dd727371512f9079cad31e202f66.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three large public chest X-ray datasets: MIMIC-CXR-JPG, ChestX-ray14 (CXR14), and CheXpert, each containing extensive demographic metadata. Two state-of-the-art UAD models, the Structural Feature Autoencoder (FAE) and the Reverse Distillation (RD) model, will be trained on datasets with systematically varied subgroup representation ratios. The evaluation will focus on the proposed sAUROC metric, as well as traditional metrics such as anomaly scores, FPR@0.95TPR, and standard AUROC, with particular attention to their ability to capture fairness-related disparities. Intersectional subgroup analyses will be performed by constructing balanced test sets for all combinations of two protected attributes, and all experiments will be run with ten different random seeds to compute confidence intervals and perform statistical significance tests.
03ec8d1d8f91dd727371512f9079cad31e202f66.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a novel empirical framework for quantifying and predicting fairness in unsupervised anomaly detection models, including the development of the subgroup-AUROC (sAUROC) metric tailored for subgroup-specific performance assessment. The research claims the discovery of empirical 'fairness laws'—linear relationships between subgroup representation in training data and model performance—which enable a priori estimation of subgroup outcomes and guide optimal dataset composition for fairness. Additionally, the study provides the first large-scale, systematic evaluation of intersectional fairness in UAD models and demonstrates that balanced data representation alone is insufficient to eliminate performance disparities.

03fab98a9be74a253688840dba9144737a8ca92d.title: Survey on Factuality in Large Language Models: Knowledge, Retrieval and Domain-Specificity
03fab98a9be74a253688840dba9144737a8ca92d.research_question: How can the factuality of large language models (LLMs) be comprehensively characterized, evaluated, and enhanced, particularly with respect to knowledge storage, retrieval mechanisms, and domain-specific requirements?
03fab98a9be74a253688840dba9144737a8ca92d.proposed_method: A systematic framework will be developed to analyze and address the factuality of LLMs, focusing on both standalone and retrieval-augmented configurations. The approach will include: (1) defining and categorizing types of factual errors and their causes at the model, retrieval, and inference levels; (2) surveying and benchmarking existing evaluation metrics, such as rule-based, neural, human, and LLM-based methods; (3) investigating the mechanisms of knowledge storage, completeness, and contextual influence in LLMs; and (4) proposing strategies for enhancing factuality, including continual pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, model editing, multi-agent debate, and retrieval-based augmentation. Special emphasis will be placed on domain-specific LLMs and the challenges posed by outdated or incomplete information.
03fab98a9be74a253688840dba9144737a8ca92d.experiment_details: Experiments will involve evaluating LLM factuality across a variety of benchmarks, including MMLU, TruthfulQA, C-Eval, AGIEval, RealTimeQA, and FreshQA, as well as domain-specific datasets such as FLARE (Finance), CMB (Medicine), GeneTuring (Gene), and EcomInstruct (E-commerce). Baselines will include both general-purpose and domain-specific LLMs, with and without retrieval augmentation. Evaluation metrics will encompass accuracy, precision, recall, F-measure, calibration, Brier score, BLEU, ROUGE, METEOR, BERTScore, BLEURT, FActScore, GPTScore, and human/LLM-based assessments. Comparative analysis will be conducted to assess the impact of different enhancement strategies and to identify the root causes of factual errors.
03fab98a9be74a253688840dba9144737a8ca92d.novelty_claims: The proposed research offers the first comprehensive, structured taxonomy and analysis of factuality in LLMs, spanning knowledge storage, retrieval augmentation, and domain-specific challenges. It integrates a wide spectrum of evaluation metrics and benchmarks, systematically categorizes error types and their origins, and proposes a unified framework for both analysis and enhancement of factuality. The work uniquely addresses the intersection of hallucination, outdated information, and domain specificity within the broader factuality problem, providing actionable guidance for future LLM development and deployment.

0416373646c97e18ef395fcbc61845e7b9993b34.title: Provably Efficient Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning: Iterated CVaR and Worst Path
0416373646c97e18ef395fcbc61845e7b9993b34.research_question: How can reinforcement learning agents efficiently optimize risk-sensitive objectives that tightly control the risk of catastrophic outcomes at every decision stage in episodic Markov Decision Processes, and what are the fundamental limits of such learning under tail-focused risk measures?
0416373646c97e18ef395fcbc61845e7b9993b34.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that novel algorithms leveraging iterated Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) and minimum-reward (worst path) criteria can achieve provably efficient regret and sample complexity bounds for risk-sensitive reinforcement learning, outperforming existing approaches in safety-critical applications.
0416373646c97e18ef395fcbc61845e7b9993b34.proposed_method: A new framework for risk-sensitive episodic reinforcement learning is developed based on the Iterated CVaR criterion, which maximizes the worst-case (tail) reward-to-go at each step. Two main algorithms are proposed: ICVaR-RM for regret minimization and ICVaR-BPI for best policy identification. Both algorithms employ CVaR-adapted value iteration, incorporating exploration bonuses that focus on rare but potentially catastrophic states, and use empirical CVaR calculations over observed transitions. For the limiting case where the risk level approaches zero (Worst Path RL), a specialized algorithm, MaxWP, is introduced, which optimizes the minimum possible cumulative reward by planning over the empirically discovered state connectivity. The methodology includes novel analytical techniques for bounding the change in CVaR due to value function shifts and for decomposing regret via a distorted visitation distribution that emphasizes risky states.
0416373646c97e18ef395fcbc61845e7b9993b34.experiment_details: Experiments are designed to validate the theoretical regret and sample complexity bounds of the proposed algorithms. The setup includes synthetic episodic Markov Decision Processes with varying parameters such as risk level (alpha), horizon length (H), state and action space sizes (S, A), and number of episodes (K). Baselines include classical RL algorithms and existing CVaR-based methods. Evaluation metrics are cumulative regret for regret minimization and sample complexity (number of episodes to identify an epsilon-optimal policy with high probability) for policy identification. The experiments systematically analyze the influence of risk sensitivity and problem parameters on algorithm performance, with empirical results compared against theoretical predictions.
0416373646c97e18ef395fcbc61845e7b9993b34.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first provably efficient algorithms for Iterated CVaR RL in the model-free setting, providing nearly matching upper and lower bounds for both regret minimization and best policy identification. It develops new analytical tools for handling the unique challenges of risk-sensitive RL, including bounding CVaR changes under value shifts and decomposing regret via distorted visitation distributions. The approach also addresses the previously unsolved limiting case of Worst Path RL with a constant-regret algorithm, and the techniques are broadly applicable to other risk-sensitive decision-making problems.

042e67f66d1dc02aad6f5985d5f79b98729ae9c1.title: Generating Graphs via Spectral Diffusion
042e67f66d1dc02aad6f5985d5f79b98729ae9c1.research_question: How can graph generative models be designed to efficiently and accurately generate graphs that capture complex structural characteristics, node features, and spectral properties, while scaling to large graphs and enabling conditioning on desired spectral attributes?
042e67f66d1dc02aad6f5985d5f79b98729ae9c1.hypothesis: A generative model that operates in the spectral domain by learning to generate eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the graph Laplacian via a diffusion process, followed by a permutation-invariant graph predictor, will enable efficient, scalable, and accurate graph generation, including the ability to condition on spectral properties and handle node features.
042e67f66d1dc02aad6f5985d5f79b98729ae9c1.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a graph generative model that leverages the spectral decomposition of the graph Laplacian and a denoising diffusion process. The method represents graphs using a subset of eigenvectors and eigenvalues of the Laplacian, which are generated via a neural diffusion model composed of multi-head cross-attention layers that allow eigenvectors and eigenvalues to condition each other. Node features can be incorporated by concatenating them to the eigenvectors. The diffusion process is designed to be permutation-invariant and operates on a truncated spectrum, reducing computational complexity from quadratic to linear in the number of nodes. After generating the spectral components, a Provably Powerful Graph Network (PPGN) is employed as a deterministic graph predictor to reconstruct the binary adjacency matrix from the (possibly noisy) Laplacian, using both reconstruction and adversarial losses to refine the output.
042e67f66d1dc02aad6f5985d5f79b98729ae9c1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets, including Community-small, Planar, and Stochastic Block Model (SBM) for synthetic data, and Proteins and QM9 for real-world graphs. Evaluation will utilize metrics such as Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) over degree distribution, clustering coefficient, Laplacian spectrum, and 4-node orbit frequencies, as well as validity, uniqueness, and novelty for molecular graphs. Baseline comparisons will include classical and deep graph generative models such as GraphRNN, GRAN, DiGress, SPECTRE, GDSS, GSDM, and GraphVAE. The experimental setup will ensure robust evaluation by generating large test sets and using cross-validation folds where appropriate. Ablation studies will assess the contributions of the diffusion and predictor components, and additional experiments will evaluate the ability to condition generation on target spectral properties.
042e67f66d1dc02aad6f5985d5f79b98729ae9c1.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel spectral diffusion framework for graph generation that directly generates both eigenvalues and eigenvectors, enabling efficient and scalable generation with linear complexity in the number of nodes. The approach is permutation-invariant, naturally incorporates node features, and allows conditioning on desired spectral properties at inference time. The use of a transformer-based architecture for the diffusion process and a PPGN-based graph predictor further distinguishes the method, providing robust handling of noisy spectral reconstructions and outperforming state-of-the-art baselines in both accuracy and flexibility.

0430dbcbfed0a737881d22340fb044028ed851a9.title: Continual Test-Time Domain Adaptation
0430dbcbfed0a737881d22340fb044028ed851a9.research_question: How can a pre-trained model be continually adapted to a non-stationary, continually changing target domain at test time, without access to source data, in order to maintain high performance and avoid error accumulation and catastrophic forgetting?
0430dbcbfed0a737881d22340fb044028ed851a9.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that combining weight-averaged and augmentation-averaged pseudo-labels for self-training, along with stochastic restoration of a subset of network parameters to their source pre-trained values, will enable continual test-time adaptation in non-stationary environments, reducing error accumulation and catastrophic forgetting while improving long-term performance.
0430dbcbfed0a737881d22340fb044028ed851a9.proposed_method: A continual test-time adaptation framework will be developed that operates on off-the-shelf pre-trained models without requiring access to source data. The method will employ a weight-averaged teacher model to generate pseudo-labels for the current target data, leveraging exponential moving averages of model weights to improve prediction quality. Augmentation-averaged predictions will be used for samples with low confidence, applying multiple random augmentations and averaging the teacher’s outputs to further refine pseudo-labels under large domain shifts. To combat catastrophic forgetting, a stochastic restoration mechanism will be introduced, periodically restoring a small, random subset of network parameters to their original source pre-trained values during adaptation. All trainable parameters, not just normalization layers, will be updated, enabling the approach to be broadly applicable across architectures.
0430dbcbfed0a737881d22340fb044028ed851a9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several benchmarks for continual test-time adaptation, including CIFAR10-to-CIFAR10C, CIFAR100-to-CIFAR100C, ImageNet-to-ImageNet-C for classification, and Cityscapes-to-ACDC for semantic segmentation. For classification tasks, pre-trained models such as WideResNet-28 and ResNeXt-29 will be used, while Segformer-B5 will be used for segmentation. Target data will be presented sequentially in a continually changing order of corruption types and severity levels, mimicking real-world non-stationary environments. Baselines will include source-only models, batch normalization statistics adaptation, pseudo-labeling, and state-of-the-art test-time adaptation methods such as TENT. Evaluation metrics will include classification error rate and mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) for segmentation. The adaptation will be performed online, with models updated after each test sample without access to the full test set or source data.
0430dbcbfed0a737881d22340fb044028ed851a9.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a continual test-time adaptation setting where the target domain changes continually and source data is unavailable, a scenario not addressed by prior methods. The method enables adaptation of all network parameters, not just normalization layers, and does not require retraining or architectural modifications of the source model. The combination of weight-averaged and augmentation-averaged pseudo-labels for robust self-training, together with stochastic restoration for long-term knowledge preservation, constitutes a novel framework for mitigating error accumulation and catastrophic forgetting in continual adaptation. The approach is designed to be simple, broadly applicable, and effective across both classification and segmentation tasks, outperforming existing baselines in long-term adaptation scenarios.

0462a5fa13b10e9d57ab95223002e781fad62c4a.title: Toward Extreme Image Compression With Latent Feature Guidance and Diffusion Prior
0462a5fa13b10e9d57ab95223002e781fad62c4a.research_question: How can extreme image compression at very low bitrates (below 0.1 bits per pixel) be achieved while maintaining high perceptual quality and fidelity in reconstructed images, particularly by leveraging advanced generative models?
