0462a5fa13b10e9d57ab95223002e781fad62c4a.hypothesis: Incorporating a two-stage framework that combines compressive variational autoencoders with pre-trained diffusion models, guided by latent feature alignment and conditional diffusion decoding, will enable realistic and high-fidelity image reconstruction at extremely low bitrates, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods.
0462a5fa13b10e9d57ab95223002e781fad62c4a.proposed_method: A novel two-stage extreme image compression framework is developed. In the first stage, a VAE-based latent feature-guided compression module (LFGCM) is employed to compress images and generate content variables, using the latent representation of images in the diffusion space as external guidance to correct intermediate features and content variables. The second stage introduces a conditional diffusion decoding module (CDDM), which leverages a fixed, pre-trained stable diffusion model as a decoder, injecting content information via a lightweight, trainable control module. A space alignment loss is designed to enforce alignment between the content variables and the diffusion space, providing necessary constraints for end-to-end optimization. The framework is trained to optimize a combined objective including rate loss, noise estimation loss, and space alignment loss, with careful balancing of these terms.
0462a5fa13b10e9d57ab95223002e781fad62c4a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the LSDIR dataset for training, with evaluation on the Kodak, Tecnick, and CLIC2020 datasets. The method will be compared against traditional codecs (BPG, VVC), VAE-based, GAN-based, and other diffusion-based compression methods, using both perceptual (LPIPS, NIQE, DISTS, FID, KID) and fidelity (PSNR, MS-SSIM) metrics. The experimental setup includes random cropping of images to fixed resolutions, use of stable diffusion 2.1-base as the generative prior, and spaced DDPM sampling with varying denoising steps for inference. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of latent feature guidance, the number of denoising steps, and the channel width of the control module. Encoding and decoding speed, as well as bitrate allocation, will be reported to assess computational efficiency.
0462a5fa13b10e9d57ab95223002e781fad62c4a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to integrate compressive VAEs with pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models in an end-to-end manner for extreme image compression. A latent feature-guided compression module is introduced to adaptively select and correct information essential for reconstruction, improving fidelity at extremely low bitrates. The conditional diffusion decoding module fully exploits the generative power of stable diffusion while maintaining its fixed parameters, enabling realistic reconstructions. A space alignment loss is designed to enforce alignment between compressed content variables and the diffusion space, providing effective optimization constraints. The method achieves superior perceptual quality and fidelity compared to state-of-the-art approaches, especially at very low bitrates.

0466bc84931796bb550c92d1dbe5493796a66413.title: Lagrangian operator inference enhanced with structure-preserving machine learning for nonintrusive model reduction of mechanical systems
0466bc84931796bb550c92d1dbe5493796a66413.research_question: How can nonlinear reduced-order models (ROMs) of mechanical systems be learned nonintrusively from data while preserving the underlying Lagrangian structure, without requiring prior knowledge of the mathematical form of nonlinearities?
0466bc84931796bb550c92d1dbe5493796a66413.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a two-step approach combining Lagrangian operator inference with structure-preserving machine learning can learn accurate and generalizable nonlinear reduced-order models of mechanical systems solely from data, while preserving the physical structure and properties inherent to the original system.
0466bc84931796bb550c92d1dbe5493796a66413.proposed_method: The proposed methodology consists of a two-step process. First, proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) is used to project high-dimensional snapshot data onto a low-dimensional subspace, forming the basis for reduced-order modeling. In the first step, linear reduced operators (mass, damping, and stiffness matrices) are inferred using a structure-preserving Lagrangian operator inference method, formulated as a constrained linear least-squares problem to ensure symmetric positive-definite properties. In the second step, structure-preserving machine learning (SpML) is employed to learn the nonlinear components of the reduced potential energy and dissipation functions. These nonlinearities are parameterized using a combination of polynomial terms and multilayer perceptrons (MLPs), with constraints to maintain physical properties such as non-negativity and positive-definiteness. The overall reduced model is trained by minimizing the residuals of the forced Euler-Lagrange equations in the reduced space, using unsupervised learning and modern stochastic optimization techniques.
0466bc84931796bb550c92d1dbe5493796a66413.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three datasets: (1) simulated data from a one-dimensional conservative rod model with spatially isolated elastic nonlinearities, (2) simulated data from a two-dimensional geometrically nonlinear membrane model with internal damping, and (3) experimental data from digital image correlation measurements of a lap-joint beam structure. For each case, high-dimensional snapshot data will be generated or collected, and then projected to reduced spaces of varying dimensions (e.g., r=4, 6, 8). Baseline comparisons will include intrusive Lagrangian ROMs and linear operator inference ROMs. Evaluation metrics will include prediction accuracy on test data outside the training regime, energy error bounds, and the ability to capture nonlinear characteristics such as amplitude-dependent frequency and damping. The training process will use a split of data into training, validation, and test sets, with hyperparameters such as learning rate, batch size, and number of epochs specified for reproducibility.
0466bc84931796bb550c92d1dbe5493796a66413.novelty_claims: The proposed approach enables the nonintrusive learning of nonlinear, structure-preserving reduced-order models directly from data, without requiring explicit knowledge of the nonlinear terms' analytic forms. By integrating Lagrangian operator inference with structure-preserving neural networks, the method ensures that learned ROMs retain key physical properties, such as energy and momentum conservation, and generalize well to unseen data. The framework is applicable to both simulated and experimental datasets, including high-dimensional systems, and demonstrates accurate long-time predictions and bounded energy errors outside the training data regime.

046e9c3275b3614ccdb22f9cf1f358e1f09e1220.title: Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning with Classifier-Free Diffusion Generation
046e9c3275b3614ccdb22f9cf1f358e1f09e1220.research_question: How can data augmentation methods be improved to better align generated data with the online policy distribution in offline-to-online reinforcement learning, thereby enhancing the performance and stability of RL agents during online fine-tuning?
046e9c3275b3614ccdb22f9cf1f358e1f09e1220.hypothesis: Utilizing classifier-free guidance within a diffusion model to simultaneously augment both offline and online data will generate higher-quality, better-aligned samples, leading to improved performance and stability in offline-to-online reinforcement learning compared to existing data augmentation methods.
046e9c3275b3614ccdb22f9cf1f358e1f09e1220.proposed_method: A novel data augmentation framework is proposed that employs classifier-free guidance in diffusion models to generate synthetic data for both offline and online distributions in offline-to-online reinforcement learning (O2O RL). The method treats offline and online data as distinct labels, enabling a single diffusion model to conditionally generate both types of data without the need for additional classifier training. During the online phase, the diffusion model is updated using samples from both offline and online buffers, and synthetic data is generated and added to corresponding synthetic buffers. A reweighting strategy is applied to prioritize synthetic data that is more closely aligned with the current online policy, increasing the weight of online synthetic data to better support policy adaptation. The approach is designed to be modular and can be integrated into existing O2O RL algorithms, with data utilization strategies tailored to different algorithmic paradigms.
046e9c3275b3614ccdb22f9cf1f358e1f09e1220.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the D4RL benchmark, focusing on Locomotion (hopper, halfcheetah, walker2d) and AntMaze tasks, using multiple dataset qualities (random, medium, medium-replay, medium-expert, etc.). The proposed method will be integrated with state-of-the-art O2O RL algorithms such as IQL, PEX, and APL. Baseline comparisons will include these algorithms without augmentation, as well as with existing model-based augmentation methods like SynthER and EDIS. Evaluation metrics will include normalized return scores, with results averaged over 5 random seeds. The experimental setup will ensure consistent buffer sizes, update frequencies, and synthetic data ratios across all tasks and methods. Additional analyses will include divergence measures (e.g., Jensen-Shannon divergence) to quantify alignment between generated and online data distributions, and ablation studies to assess the impact of classifier-free guidance and dual-data augmentation.
046e9c3275b3614ccdb22f9cf1f358e1f09e1220.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces classifier-free guidance into diffusion-based data augmentation for O2O RL, enabling simultaneous and efficient generation of both offline and online synthetic data without additional classifier overhead. By treating data types as distinct labels within a single model, the method reduces training complexity and adapts dynamically to changing policy distributions. The reweighting mechanism further enhances alignment with the online policy, leading to significant empirical improvements over existing data augmentation methods. The framework is versatile, easily integrates with various O2O RL algorithms, and demonstrates a notable average performance boost (e.g., 15% improvement) across standard RL benchmarks.

04983bbf48ab9649e3e6dcb7f4fadd7d04c89bbd.title: Ring-A-Bell! How Reliable are Concept Removal Methods for Diffusion Models?
04983bbf48ab9649e3e6dcb7f4fadd7d04c89bbd.research_question: How reliable are current concept removal and safety mechanisms in text-to-image diffusion models at preventing the generation of inappropriate or forbidden content, and can their limitations be systematically exposed through automated prompt-based evaluation?
04983bbf48ab9649e3e6dcb7f4fadd7d04c89bbd.hypothesis: Existing safety mechanisms and concept removal methods in text-to-image diffusion models are insufficiently robust and can be circumvented by systematically crafted adversarial prompts, even without access to the underlying model parameters.
04983bbf48ab9649e3e6dcb7f4fadd7d04c89bbd.proposed_method: A model-agnostic red-teaming framework, Ring-A-Bell, will be developed to evaluate the effectiveness of safety mechanisms in text-to-image diffusion models. The approach begins by extracting holistic representations of sensitive concepts (e.g., nudity, violence) using prompt pairs that differ only in the target concept, leveraging a general text encoder such as CLIP. The empirical concept vector is computed by averaging the embedding differences between these prompt pairs. To generate problematic prompts, the target prompt's embedding is infused with the concept vector, and an optimization procedure (such as a genetic algorithm) is used to find discrete prompts whose embeddings closely match the desired target in the embedding space. This process is performed offline and does not require access to the internal weights or architecture of the target diffusion model, relying only on the text encoder.
04983bbf48ab9649e3e6dcb7f4fadd7d04c89bbd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the I2P dataset, focusing on prompts related to nudity and violence. The method will be evaluated against a range of state-of-the-art concept removal models, including Erased Stable Diffusion (ESD), Safe Latent Diffusion (SLD) in multiple configurations, Stable Diffusion with negative prompts (SD-NP), Concept Ablation (CA), and Forget-Me-Not (FMN). Online text-to-image services such as Midjourney, DALL·E 2, Gen-2, and Stable Diffusion XL will also be tested. Baselines will include the QF-Attack method. Evaluation metrics will primarily be the Attack Success Rate (ASR), defined as the proportion of successful generations of inappropriate images, with detection performed via automated classifiers (e.g., NudeNet for nudity, Q16 for violence). Ablation studies will assess the impact of prompt length, concept vector strength, number of prompt pairs, and choice of optimizer.
04983bbf48ab9649e3e6dcb7f4fadd7d04c89bbd.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a fully model-agnostic, offline prompt-based evaluation tool for systematically probing the reliability of concept removal and safety mechanisms in diffusion models. Unlike prior approaches, it does not require white-box access to the model or its parameters, relying solely on a general text encoder. The method enables the automated generation of adversarial prompts that can expose vulnerabilities in both open-source and commercial T2I systems, providing a practical and scalable red-teaming tool for risk assessment and safety improvement.

04a96b66705858c988edfcb73191c1da7d54abfb.title: Studying Large Language Model Generalization with Influence Functions
04a96b66705858c988edfcb73191c1da7d54abfb.research_question: How can the generalization behavior of large language models be systematically analyzed by attributing model outputs to specific training data, and what patterns of generalization, abstraction, and memorization emerge as model scale increases?
04a96b66705858c988edfcb73191c1da7d54abfb.hypothesis: Influence functions, when efficiently scaled to large language models, can reveal meaningful and interpretable patterns of generalization, abstraction, and memorization by identifying which training sequences most affect specific model behaviors.
04a96b66705858c988edfcb73191c1da7d54abfb.proposed_method: A scalable framework will be developed for computing influence functions in large transformer-based language models using the Eigenvalue-corrected Kronecker-Factored Approximate Curvature (EK-FAC) approximation to efficiently estimate inverse-Hessian-vector products (IHVPs). To address the computational bottleneck of gradient computation for candidate training sequences, two algorithmic enhancements will be employed: TF-IDF filtering to pre-select relevant training examples and query batching to amortize the cost of gradient calculations across multiple influence queries. The method will enable both scalar and fine-grained (layerwise and tokenwise) attribution of model outputs to training data, allowing for detailed analysis of where and how knowledge is stored and generalized within the network. The approach will focus on the multilayer perceptron (MLP) layers of pretrained transformer models, with the potential for future extension to fine-tuned models.
04a96b66705858c988edfcb73191c1da7d54abfb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale transformer language models with up to 52 billion parameters. Validation of the EK-FAC-based influence estimates will be performed against traditional iterative methods such as LiSSA and the proximal Bregman response function (PBRF). Analyses will include both quantitative (e.g., distribution and sparsity of influence scores, power-law fitting) and qualitative (e.g., case studies of influential sequences for specific queries) evaluations. The setup will involve searching a substantial subset of the pretraining corpus using TF-IDF filtering, and comparisons will be made across models of different sizes to assess abstraction and generalization patterns. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy of influence estimation, computational efficiency, and interpretability of identified influential sequences, with additional human crowdworker studies to assess the semantic relevance of top influential examples.
04a96b66705858c988edfcb73191c1da7d54abfb.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a scalable and efficient method for applying influence functions to extremely large language models, overcoming prior computational barriers by leveraging EK-FAC and novel batching/filtering techniques. It enables unprecedented analysis of generalization, abstraction, and memorization in LLMs at scale, including fine-grained attribution to layers and tokens. The approach provides new empirical insights into how generalization patterns evolve with model size, reveals limitations such as sensitivity to word order, and offers a practical tool for auditing and interpreting LLM behaviors.

04ac11f8db83406b03d92aa4571fc3e6c176c1e3.title: Understanding over-squashing and bottlenecks on graphs via curvature
04ac11f8db83406b03d92aa4571fc3e6c176c1e3.research_question: How do structural properties of graphs, specifically bottlenecks, impact the propagation of information in message passing graph neural networks, and can geometric notions such as curvature be leveraged to better understand and alleviate the over-squashing phenomenon?
04ac11f8db83406b03d92aa4571fc3e6c176c1e3.hypothesis: Negatively curved edges in a graph are responsible for bottlenecks that cause over-squashing in message passing neural networks, and targeted curvature-based graph rewiring can alleviate this issue, improving information propagation and downstream GNN performance.
04ac11f8db83406b03d92aa4571fc3e6c176c1e3.proposed_method: A new edge-based combinatorial curvature, termed Balanced Forman curvature, will be introduced to quantify local geometric properties of graphs and identify negatively curved edges responsible for bottlenecks. The relationship between this curvature and the over-squashing phenomenon will be formally established through sensitivity analysis of node representations via the Jacobian of GNN outputs. Building on this, a curvature-based graph rewiring algorithm, Stochastic Discrete Ricci Flow (SDRF), will be developed. SDRF iteratively modifies the graph by adding edges to support the most negatively curved edges and removing edges with maximal positive curvature, with the goal of homogenizing curvature and reducing bottlenecks. The rewiring process is designed to be local and surgical, preserving overall graph structure while targeting problematic regions.
04ac11f8db83406b03d92aa4571fc3e6c176c1e3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on nine standard node classification benchmarks, including datasets with varying levels of homophily such as Cornell, Texas, Wisconsin, Chameleon, Squirrel, Actor, Cora, Citeseer, and Pubmed. The base model will be a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN), and the proposed SDRF method will be compared against baselines including no preprocessing, undirected conversion, fully connected last layer (+FA), and diffusion-based graph rewiring (DIGL/PPR). Evaluation metrics will include node classification accuracy, changes in graph topology (degree distribution, edge addition/removal rates), and the impact on the Cheeger constant as a measure of bottleneckedness. Hyperparameters will be optimized via random search over multiple data splits, and results will be reported as average accuracies with confidence intervals. Additional analysis will include the preservation of graph structure and the effect on the Jacobian of node predictions.
04ac11f8db83406b03d92aa4571fc3e6c176c1e3.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a novel combinatorial curvature (Balanced Forman curvature) for graphs that provides a sharp, computable lower bound to Ollivier curvature and directly links local geometric properties to over-squashing in GNNs. The proposed Stochastic Discrete Ricci Flow (SDRF) is a new curvature-based graph rewiring algorithm that surgically targets bottlenecks, in contrast to existing diffusion-based methods, and is theoretically and empirically shown to better preserve graph structure while alleviating over-squashing. The approach establishes a new geometric framework for understanding and mitigating information bottlenecks in message passing neural networks.

04b0c289607d408f5c89743552157c3c20ec3d3b.title: Guidance with Spherical Gaussian Constraint for Conditional Diffusion
04b0c289607d408f5c89743552157c3c20ec3d3b.research_question: How can the sample quality and time efficiency of training-free conditional diffusion models be improved by addressing the manifold deviation problem that arises during loss-guided sampling?
04b0c289607d408f5c89743552157c3c20ec3d3b.hypothesis: Introducing a spherical Gaussian constraint to the guidance step in conditional diffusion models will mitigate manifold deviation, enabling larger guidance steps and resulting in improved sample quality and faster inference without significant computational overhead.
04b0c289607d408f5c89743552157c3c20ec3d3b.proposed_method: A novel training-free guidance method, Diffusion with Spherical Gaussian constraint (DSG), will be developed for conditional diffusion models. The approach constrains the guidance step within the intermediate data manifold by leveraging the concentration phenomenon of high-dimensional Gaussian distributions, effectively approximating the intermediate distribution as a hypersphere. The guidance is formulated as an optimization problem with a spherical Gaussian constraint, ensuring that the updated sample remains within a high-confidence region of the unconditional diffusion step. A closed-form solution for the constrained optimization is derived, allowing the method to be implemented as a plug-and-play module with minimal code changes and negligible computational overhead. The approach will also incorporate an adaptive step size mechanism, enabling the use of larger guidance steps while maintaining sample fidelity.
04b0c289607d408f5c89743552157c3c20ec3d3b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of conditional generative tasks, including image inpainting, super-resolution, Gaussian deblurring, text-segmentation guidance, style guidance, text-style guidance, and face ID guidance. Datasets such as FFHQ, ImageNet, CelebA-HQ, and WikiArt will be used, with pre-trained diffusion models (e.g., Stable Diffusion, LDM) serving as the backbone. The proposed method will be integrated into existing training-free conditional diffusion baselines such as DPS, UGD, and Freedom. Evaluation metrics will include LPIPS, FID, SSIM, PSNR, KID, and task-specific losses (e.g., CLIP-based perceptual loss, cross-entropy for segmentation, ArcFace for face ID). Experiments will systematically compare sample quality, alignment with conditions, and inference speed under varying numbers of denoising steps, with ablation studies to assess robustness and diversity.
04b0c289607d408f5c89743552157c3c20ec3d3b.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a spherical Gaussian constraint to the guidance step in conditional diffusion models, addressing the manifold deviation problem theoretically and empirically for the first time. A closed-form solution for the constrained optimization is derived, enabling seamless integration into existing training-free methods with almost no computational overhead. The approach allows for significantly larger guidance steps, improving both sample quality and inference speed across diverse conditional generation tasks. The method is broadly applicable as a plug-and-play module and demonstrates superior adaptability and performance compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

04c24e80c137cd0694a86f94634ba0db207d7831.title: Scaling Exponents Across Parameterizations and Optimizers
04c24e80c137cd0694a86f94634ba0db207d7831.research_question: How can the scaling behavior of neural network training be made robust and predictable across different parameterizations and optimizers, particularly as model width increases, and what are the optimal prescriptions for per-layer learning rates and optimizer hyperparameters to ensure stable and effective training at scale?
04c24e80c137cd0694a86f94634ba0db207d7831.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that all common parameterizations, not just maximal update parameterization (muP), can achieve effective hyperparameter transfer and stable scaling when equipped with appropriately derived per-layer learning rate prescriptions. Furthermore, it is posited that the epsilon hyperparameter in adaptive optimizers like Adam must be scaled correctly to avoid gradient underflow, and that a scale-invariant optimizer can eliminate this issue entirely.
04c24e80c137cd0694a86f94634ba0db207d7831.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted into the scaling exponents governing neural network training across a broad set of parameterizations (including standard, NTK, muP, and mean-field) and optimizers (SGD, Adam, Adafactor). The method will derive general stability and nontriviality constraints as a function of alignment between parameters and data, relaxing key assumptions from prior work. A novel metric for quantifying alignment during training will be introduced and measured empirically. Per-layer learning rate prescriptions will be theoretically derived for each parameterization-optimizer pair under varying alignment assumptions, and a new scale-invariant version of Adam (Adam-atan2) will be developed to eliminate the epsilon hyperparameter. Extensive experiments will be conducted to validate theoretical predictions and to optimize per-layer learning rate constants for practical performance.
04c24e80c137cd0694a86f94634ba0db207d7831.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training tens of thousands of Transformer language models on the C4 dataset, spanning all combinations of three optimizers, four parameterizations, multiple alignment assumptions, over a dozen learning rates, and fourteen model sizes up to 26.8 billion parameters. Each model will be trained for 50,000 steps with a fixed batch size, context length, and depth, and learning rate schedules will include linear warmup and cosine decay. The empirical investigation will measure alignment metrics throughout training, compare global versus per-layer learning rate prescriptions, and tune per-layer learning rate constants. Baselines will include global learning rate approaches and established parameterization methods, with evaluation metrics focused on validation loss and hyperparameter transferability across scales.
04c24e80c137cd0694a86f94634ba0db207d7831.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a general theoretical framework for scaling exponents that explicitly quantifies the role of alignment between parameters and data, relaxing restrictive assumptions from prior work. It provides the first comprehensive empirical measurement of alignment dynamics across parameterizations, optimizers, and model sizes. A novel per-layer learning rate prescription for standard parameterization is proposed and shown to outperform muP. The work further demonstrates that all parameterizations can achieve hyperparameter transfer, not just muP, and highlights the critical importance of scaling the epsilon parameter in Adam. The introduction of Adam-atan2, a numerically stable, scale-invariant optimizer that eliminates the need for the epsilon hyperparameter, represents a significant innovation in adaptive optimization.

04d64be16fb402f28348faffef484bd419c8bd8f.title: Self-Rewarding Language Models
04d64be16fb402f28348faffef484bd419c8bd8f.research_question: Can language models be aligned and improved through a self-rewarding, iterative training process in which the model itself generates and evaluates its own instruction-following data, thereby overcoming the limitations of fixed, human-trained reward models?
04d64be16fb402f28348faffef484bd419c8bd8f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a language model trained to both follow instructions and act as its own reward model, through iterative self-generated feedback and preference optimization, will achieve superior alignment and instruction-following performance compared to models trained with static, human-derived reward models.
04d64be16fb402f28348faffef484bd419c8bd8f.proposed_method: A self-rewarding language model framework will be developed, starting from a pretrained base model and a small set of human-annotated instruction-following and evaluation data. The model will be fine-tuned to perform both instruction following and response evaluation (LLM-as-a-Judge) tasks. In each iteration, the model will generate new prompts, produce multiple candidate responses, and evaluate these responses using its own learned reward model via a structured, multi-criteria scoring prompt. Preference pairs will be constructed from the highest and lowest scoring responses and used to further fine-tune the model using Direct Preference Optimization (DPO). This iterative process will be repeated, with each new model generation using augmented training data created by the previous iteration, enabling continual improvement in both instruction following and reward modeling capabilities.
04d64be16fb402f28348faffef484bd419c8bd8f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using Llama 2 70B as the base model, fine-tuned initially on 3,200 high-quality instruction-following examples and 1,630 evaluation examples from the Open Assistant dataset. The iterative training process will generate additional preference pairs (e.g., 3,964 and 6,942 pairs in subsequent iterations) for DPO-based fine-tuning. Evaluation will be performed on multiple axes: instruction following (using GPT-4 as an evaluator on 256 test prompts, AlpacaEval 2.0 leaderboard with 805 prompts, MT-Bench, and nine NLP benchmarks), and reward modeling (measuring pairwise accuracy, exact match, Spearman and Kendall correlation with human rankings). Baselines will include the SFT baseline (supervised fine-tuning only) and previous iterations of the self-rewarding model. Both automatic (GPT-4) and human evaluations will be used for comprehensive assessment.
04d64be16fb402f28348faffef484bd419c8bd8f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified, self-rewarding language model that simultaneously learns to generate and evaluate instruction-following data, eliminating the need for a separate, frozen reward model. The iterative, self-alignment process enables the reward model to improve alongside the language model, potentially surpassing the performance ceiling imposed by human-labeled data. This framework demonstrates the feasibility of continual self-improvement in both instruction following and reward modeling, and achieves state-of-the-art results on public leaderboards using only a small amount of seed human data and self-generated feedback.

04dd447d9f174bcd0659fe80de7f3400365035ec.title: Proximal Policy Gradient Arborescence for Quality Diversity Reinforcement Learning
04dd447d9f174bcd0659fe80de7f3400365035ec.research_question: How can reinforcement learning algorithms be enhanced to efficiently discover and optimize a diverse set of high-performing behaviors in complex, high-dimensional, and stochastic environments, particularly for challenging continuous control tasks?
04dd447d9f174bcd0659fe80de7f3400365035ec.hypothesis: Integrating on-policy reinforcement learning, specifically Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), with Differentiable Quality Diversity (DQD) frameworks and introducing algorithmic innovations such as Markovian Measure Proxies, vectorized policy optimization, and Natural Evolution Strategies will enable more efficient and robust discovery of diverse, high-quality policies compared to existing QD-RL approaches.
04dd447d9f174bcd0659fe80de7f3400365035ec.proposed_method: A novel algorithm, Proximal Policy Gradient Arborescence (PPGA), will be developed by combining PPO with the Differentiable Quality Diversity (DQD) framework, specifically building on the CMA-MAEGA algorithm. The method will introduce Markovian Measure Proxies (MMPs) to transform typically non-Markovian behavioral diversity measures into Markovian, RL-optimizable proxies, enabling the use of PPO for both objective and diversity gradient estimation. A vectorized PPO (VPPO) implementation will be designed to jointly optimize the RL objective and multiple MMPs using a single actor and multiple value functions, allowing efficient computation of policy gradients for branching and archive exploration. The search distribution over gradient coefficients will be maintained and updated using Natural Evolution Strategies (xNES) instead of CMA-ES to improve stability in noisy, non-stationary environments. The search policy will be iteratively 'walked' through the archive by optimizing a multi-objective reward function constructed from the dot product of the xNES mean coefficient vector and the objective/measure proxies, enabling targeted exploration of unexplored regions.
04dd447d9f174bcd0659fe80de7f3400365035ec.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four continuous control locomotion tasks derived from the Mujoco suite: Ant, Walker2d, Half-Cheetah, and Humanoid, using the Brax simulator for GPU-accelerated, massively parallelized environment rollout. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art QD-RL baselines including Policy Gradient Assisted MAP-Elites (PGA-ME), Quality Diversity Policy Gradient (QDPG), CMA-MAEGA (with TD3 and ES), and separable CMA-MAE, as well as an ablation using TD3 in place of PPO. Evaluation metrics will include QD-score (sum of scores of all nonempty archive cells), coverage (percentage of nonempty cells), best reward (highest-performing discovered policy), and the complementary cumulative distribution function (CCDF) of archive rewards to assess both diversity and quality. Post-hoc analysis will involve re-evaluating archive policies over 50 runs to construct corrected metrics and assess robustness to stochasticity. All experiments will use consistent archive resolutions, network architectures, and shared hyperparameters across baselines.
04dd447d9f174bcd0659fe80de7f3400365035ec.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to successfully leverage on-policy RL (PPO) within a Differentiable Quality Diversity framework for QD-RL, achieving state-of-the-art results and solving the challenging Humanoid domain with a 4x improvement in best reward over baselines. Key innovations include the introduction of Markovian Measure Proxies for RL-optimizable diversity measures, a vectorized PPO implementation for efficient joint optimization of multiple objectives, and the use of Natural Evolution Strategies (xNES) for stable search distribution updates in noisy environments. The method achieves equivalent or superior best-policy performance to standard RL while maintaining or improving diversity, and demonstrates robust policy discovery in highly stochastic, high-dimensional tasks.

04e541391e8dce14d099d00fb2c21dbbd8afe87f.title: Prompt-to-Prompt Image Editing with Cross Attention Control
04e541391e8dce14d099d00fb2c21dbbd8afe87f.research_question: How can intuitive, fine-grained, and high-fidelity image editing be achieved using only textual prompts, without requiring spatial masks or additional manual input, in large-scale text-to-image diffusion models?
04e541391e8dce14d099d00fb2c21dbbd8afe87f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that controlling and manipulating the internal cross-attention maps within text-conditioned diffusion models enables prompt-to-prompt image editing, allowing localized and global modifications to generated or real images using only textual changes, while preserving the structure and content of the original image.
04e541391e8dce14d099d00fb2c21dbbd8afe87f.proposed_method: A novel prompt-to-prompt image editing framework is proposed that operates by intervening in the cross-attention layers of pre-trained text-conditioned diffusion models. The method injects or modifies cross-attention maps during the diffusion process to control the correspondence between image pixels and prompt tokens. Three main editing operations are supported: (1) word swap, where attention maps from the original prompt are injected into the generation process with a modified prompt to preserve structure while changing content; (2) phrase addition, where attention maps are aligned and injected only for common tokens between the original and edited prompts, enabling global or attribute-based edits; and (3) attention re-weighting, where the influence of specific words is amplified or attenuated by scaling their attention maps, providing fine-grained control over semantic attributes. The algorithm synchronizes the diffusion process for both source and target prompts, applying attention-based manipulations at each step, with the ability to control the number and timing of attention injections for optimal fidelity and editability.
04e541391e8dce14d099d00fb2c21dbbd8afe87f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Imagen text-guided diffusion model as the backbone, focusing on both synthetic and real images. Editing tasks will include localized object replacement, global style transfer, attribute modification, and real image editing via inversion techniques. Baselines will include standard text-to-image generation with prompt modification (without attention injection), as well as existing mask-based and text-only editing methods. Evaluation metrics will encompass qualitative visual fidelity, preservation of original image structure, and alignment with edited prompts, supplemented by user studies for subjective assessment. Additional technical details include using deterministic diffusion (e.g., DDIM) for reproducibility, and leveraging attention map-derived masks for real image editing without user guidance.
04e541391e8dce14d099d00fb2c21dbbd8afe87f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a cross-attention control mechanism for prompt-to-prompt image editing that requires only textual input, eliminating the need for spatial masks or retraining. The method enables both localized and global edits, supports fine-grained semantic control via attention re-weighting, and can be applied to both generated and real images using inversion. The approach provides an intuitive, flexible, and high-fidelity editing interface, advancing the state of the art in text-driven image manipulation.

04ecc94e50a9127eded7d9c49736f19b0ea7b8ee.title: SAMRefiner: Taming Segment Anything Model for Universal Mask Refinement
04ecc94e50a9127eded7d9c49736f19b0ea7b8ee.research_question: How can the quality of coarse segmentation masks be universally and efficiently refined to serve as reliable training data for segmentation models across diverse tasks and datasets, thereby reducing annotation costs?
04ecc94e50a9127eded7d9c49736f19b0ea7b8ee.hypothesis: A universal mask refinement framework that leverages a promptable segmentation model with a noise-tolerant, multi-prompt excavation strategy, combined with an IoU adaptation step, will significantly improve the quality of coarse masks and generalize across segmentation tasks and datasets without requiring additional annotations.
04ecc94e50a9127eded7d9c49736f19b0ea7b8ee.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a universal mask refinement framework by adapting a prompt-driven segmentation model (SAM) for the mask refinement task. The core technique is a noise-tolerant prompting scheme, which excavates diverse prompts—distance-guided points, context-aware elastic bounding boxes, and Gaussian-style masks—from initial coarse masks. These prompts are collaboratively used to mitigate the effects of noise and defects in the coarse masks, generating multiple candidate refined masks. For semantic segmentation with multi-object cases, a split-then-merge (STM) pipeline is employed to split coarse masks into connected regions and iteratively merge them based on area and occupancy heuristics. An optional IoU adaptation step (SAMRefiner++) is introduced, where a LoRA-style adaptor is added to the IoU prediction head and trained with a ranking loss using coarse masks as priors, enhancing mask selection accuracy in a self-boosted, annotation-free manner.
04ecc94e50a9127eded7d9c49736f19b0ea7b8ee.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a wide range of benchmarks, including DAVIS-585 (mask refinement), COCO (instance segmentation), and PASCAL VOC (semantic segmentation), under various supervision settings (unsupervised, semi-supervised, weakly-supervised). The method is evaluated both as a standalone mask refiner and as a post-processing tool for different segmentation models (e.g., Mask R-CNN, SOLOv2, DeepLabV2). Baselines include dense CRF, CascadePSP, CRM, SegRefiner, and others. Evaluation metrics comprise IoU, boundary IoU, mask AP, boundary AP, and mIoU. Ablation studies assess the impact of different prompt types, STM, and IoU adaptation. The framework's efficiency is benchmarked in terms of inference time and batch processing capability.
04ecc94e50a9127eded7d9c49736f19b0ea7b8ee.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to adapt the Segment Anything Model (SAM) for universal mask refinement, introducing a noise-tolerant, multi-prompt excavation strategy that robustly handles defects in coarse masks. The split-then-merge pipeline addresses multi-object semantic segmentation, and the IoU adaptation step enables self-boosted, annotation-free enhancement of mask selection. The method is model- and task-agnostic, generalizes across datasets, and demonstrates significant improvements in both mask quality and efficiency compared to state-of-the-art refinement techniques.

04ed1d9c81cd6304d21a88d7aae9ba7cde802f50.title: Model merging with SVD to tie the Knots
04ed1d9c81cd6304d21a88d7aae9ba7cde802f50.research_question: How can the merging of multiple LoRA-finetuned models, each specialized on distinct tasks but sharing a common pretrained checkpoint, be improved to yield a single general model that performs well across all tasks without requiring additional retraining or access to training data?
04ed1d9c81cd6304d21a88d7aae9ba7cde802f50.hypothesis: Aligning the task-updates (parameter changes) of LoRA-finetuned models into a shared representation space will significantly improve the effectiveness of gradient-free model merging methods, resulting in merged models that better preserve the capabilities of the original task-specific models.
04ed1d9c81cd6304d21a88d7aae9ba7cde802f50.proposed_method: A novel, data-free and gradient-free method, termed KnOTS (Knowledge Orientation Through SVD), is developed to align the parameter updates (task-updates) from multiple LoRA-finetuned models before merging. For each layer, the method concatenates the low-rank update matrices from all models column-wise and applies singular value decomposition (SVD) to decompose them into shared orthonormal bases (U), scaling factors (Σ), and task-specific components (V). Existing gradient-free merging methods (such as Task Arithmetic, TIES, or DARE) are then applied directly to the aligned V matrices, producing a merged V(merged). The final merged update for each layer is reconstructed as UΣV(merged) and added to the pretrained model's parameters. This process is repeated layer-wise, enabling the construction of a merged model whose representations are functionally aligned across tasks.
04ed1d9c81cd6304d21a88d7aae9ba7cde802f50.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both vision and language domains. For vision, ViT-B/32 and ViT-L/14 models pretrained as CLIP vision encoders will be finetuned with LoRA on eight distinct image classification datasets (Cars, DTD, EuroSAT, GTSRB, MNIST, RESISC45, SUN397, SVHN). For language, Llama3-8B models will be finetuned on six different natural language inference tasks (SNLI, MNLI, SICK, QNLI, RTE, SCITAIL). Merging baselines will include RegMean, Task Arithmetic (TA), TIES, and DARE, with KnOTS applied as a preprocessing step to each. Evaluation metrics will include normalized per-task accuracy (merged model accuracy divided by finetuned model accuracy), as well as Hits@k (top-k accuracy) in a new 'joint-task' benchmark where merged models must classify samples across the union of all datasets and labels. Hyperparameters for merging methods will be tuned on held-out validation sets, and robustness will be assessed across varying numbers of merged models and LoRA ranks.
04ed1d9c81cd6304d21a88d7aae9ba7cde802f50.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new SVD-based alignment technique (KnOTS) for LoRA model merging that is both data-free and gradient-free, enabling more effective application of existing merging methods. It is claimed to significantly improve the alignment of task-updates between LoRA models, addressing a key challenge that limits the performance of prior merging strategies. Additionally, a novel benchmark is introduced for evaluating the generality of merged models by requiring classification across the union of all task labels, rather than per-task evaluation. The method is demonstrated to consistently improve merging performance by up to 4.3% across diverse vision and language tasks, and scales robustly with model size, number of tasks, and LoRA rank.

052df22955b06d93a88edc72be09ba9f94c2e548.title: Improving the Training of Rectified Flows
052df22955b06d93a88edc72be09ba9f94c2e548.research_question: Can rectified flow models for generative tasks be trained to achieve competitive or superior performance to knowledge distillation-based diffusion models in the low function evaluation (NFE) regime, and what training techniques can maximize their efficiency and sample quality?
052df22955b06d93a88edc72be09ba9f94c2e548.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that rectified flow models, when trained with improved techniques such as a U-shaped timestep distribution and perceptual loss functions, can achieve state-of-the-art performance in low-NFE settings, rivaling or surpassing knowledge distillation methods while retaining the qualitative advantages of neural ODE-based generative models.
052df22955b06d93a88edc72be09ba9f94c2e548.proposed_method: A new training framework for rectified flow models will be developed, focusing on optimizing performance in the low-NFE regime. The approach will replace the standard multi-round Reflow training with a single, well-optimized round, based on the insight that additional rounds offer diminishing returns under realistic data distributions. Key innovations include adopting a U-shaped timestep distribution to focus training on the most challenging interpolation points and introducing a composite loss function that combines the Pseudo-Huber loss with the LPIPS perceptual similarity metric (LPIPS-Huber), weighted to emphasize perceptual quality at critical timesteps. The method will also leverage initialization from pre-trained diffusion models (such as EDM or DDPM) with appropriate time and scale conversion, and optionally incorporate real data pairs for fine-tuning. The overall training pipeline is designed to minimize computational overhead while maximizing generative quality and efficiency.
052df22955b06d93a88edc72be09ba9f94c2e548.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image generation benchmarks, including CIFAR-10, AFHQ 64x64, FFHQ 64x64, and ImageNet 64x64. The proposed rectified flow models will be compared against a comprehensive set of baselines: classical diffusion models, distilled diffusion models (e.g., consistency distillation, progressive distillation), GANs, and previous rectified flow variants. Evaluation metrics will include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS), precision, and recall, with a focus on 1- and 2-NFE settings. Ablation studies will assess the impact of each proposed technique (timestep distribution, loss function, initialization, and real data incorporation). The computational cost will be analyzed in terms of forward passes and storage requirements, and qualitative analyses will cover inversion, interpolation, and image-to-image translation capabilities.
052df22955b06d93a88edc72be09ba9f94c2e548.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces several innovations: (1) a demonstration that a single round of Reflow is sufficient for near-optimal rectified flow training in practical settings, eliminating the need for costly multi-stage procedures; (2) a novel U-shaped timestep distribution tailored to the training dynamics of rectified flows; (3) a composite LPIPS-Huber loss that enhances perceptual quality in few-step generation; (4) a principled method for initializing rectified flows from pre-trained diffusion models with precise time and scale conversion; and (5) empirical evidence that these techniques enable rectified flows to achieve or surpass state-of-the-art results in the low-NFE regime, while maintaining the unique advantages of neural ODE-based generative models, such as efficient inversion and flexible trade-offs between quality and computational cost.

053e9cacea6ff66f0343fc7b17fca01005a31dec.title: Delay-adaptive step-sizes for asynchronous learning
053e9cacea6ff66f0343fc7b17fca01005a31dec.research_question: How can asynchronous optimization algorithms for large-scale machine learning be improved by adapting step-sizes to actual, time-varying information delays, rather than relying on conservative upper bounds on delays?
053e9cacea6ff66f0343fc7b17fca01005a31dec.hypothesis: Delay-adaptive step-size policies that utilize real-time measurements of system delays will accelerate convergence of asynchronous optimization algorithms compared to traditional fixed step-size methods based on worst-case delay bounds, without sacrificing theoretical guarantees.
053e9cacea6ff66f0343fc7b17fca01005a31dec.proposed_method: A framework will be developed for asynchronous optimization algorithms that dynamically adjusts the step-size at each iteration based on the actual observed delays in the system. This approach will be instantiated for two prominent distributed optimization algorithms: Proximal Incremental Aggregated Gradient (PIAG) in a parameter server architecture and Asynchronous Block Coordinate Descent (Async-BCD) in a shared memory setting. Delay-tracking mechanisms will be implemented using time-stamping or local counters to record the delay associated with each update. Two adaptive step-size policies will be formulated: one that uses a weighted maximum of recent step-sizes and another that scales the step-size inversely with the current delay, ensuring that the step-size is automatically reduced when delays increase. Theoretical analysis will establish convergence guarantees under these adaptive policies, without requiring knowledge of the maximal delay.
053e9cacea6ff66f0343fc7b17fca01005a31dec.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on regularized logistic regression for classification tasks using the rcv1 and MNIST datasets. For PIAG, data will be partitioned into batches and distributed to multiple workers in a parameter server setup; for Async-BCD, the variable will be split into blocks and updated asynchronously by multiple workers in a shared memory environment. The proposed delay-adaptive step-size policies will be compared against state-of-the-art fixed step-size rules that require knowledge of the worst-case delay. Evaluation metrics will include objective error and convergence speed (number of iterations to reach a target objective value). Delay distributions will be analyzed to illustrate the adaptivity and efficiency of the proposed methods under realistic, heterogeneous system delays.
053e9cacea6ff66f0343fc7b17fca01005a31dec.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first general convergence results for asynchronous optimization algorithms using step-sizes that adapt to actual, time-varying delays, eliminating the need for conservative delay upper bounds. Practical delay-tracking algorithms are developed for both PIAG and Async-BCD, and new step-size policies are designed that guarantee convergence regardless of unknown or variable system delays. Theoretical analysis provides explicit convergence rate guarantees for both convex and non-convex objectives under these adaptive policies. Experimental results are expected to demonstrate substantial speed-ups over existing fixed step-size approaches, particularly in environments with non-uniform or bursty delays.

05506581cade1a8ef6372616cec20b81a3d5c366.title: GSM-Symbolic: Understanding the Limitations of Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
05506581cade1a8ef6372616cec20b81a3d5c366.research_question: How reliably can large language models perform mathematical reasoning, and what are the limitations of current evaluation methodologies in assessing their true reasoning capabilities?
05506581cade1a8ef6372616cec20b81a3d5c366.hypothesis: Current large language models do not perform genuine logical reasoning in mathematical tasks; instead, they rely on probabilistic pattern-matching, resulting in high sensitivity to superficial changes in input and a lack of robustness to increased complexity or irrelevant information.
05506581cade1a8ef6372616cec20b81a3d5c366.proposed_method: A new benchmark, GSM-Symbolic, will be developed by generating diverse mathematical word problem variants using symbolic templates derived from the GSM8K dataset. These templates will allow systematic control over variables such as names, numerical values, and the number of logical clauses, enabling the creation of multiple question instances with varying complexity and superficial features. Automated and manual validation checks will ensure the correctness and diversity of generated questions. Additionally, a GSM-NoOp dataset will be constructed by augmenting questions with seemingly relevant but operationally irrelevant clauses to test the models' ability to discern pertinent information for reasoning. The evaluation protocol will include Chain-of-Thought prompting with multiple shots and greedy decoding to simulate realistic usage scenarios.
05506581cade1a8ef6372616cec20b81a3d5c366.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on over 25 state-of-the-art open and closed large language models, including models ranging from 2B to 27B parameters and proprietary models such as GPT-4o and o1-preview. The primary datasets will consist of 100 symbolic templates, each generating 50 variants, resulting in 5000 examples per benchmark. Multiple experimental conditions will be tested, including changes to proper names, numerical values, and the addition or removal of logical clauses to modulate difficulty. Baseline performance will be measured on GSM8K, with comparative evaluation on GSM-Symbolic, GSM-Symbolic variants (with altered difficulty), and GSM-NoOp. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy distributions across instances, performance variance, and robustness to irrelevant information, with results analyzed for both mean accuracy and variance across different experimental setups.
05506581cade1a8ef6372616cec20b81a3d5c366.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a benchmark that enables fine-grained, controllable evaluation of mathematical reasoning in language models, moving beyond single-point accuracy metrics. The methodology allows for systematic investigation of model robustness to superficial and substantive changes in problem statements, as well as the impact of irrelevant information on reasoning. The GSM-NoOp dataset provides a novel diagnostic tool to expose models' inability to filter out inconsequential information, revealing critical flaws in their reasoning processes. Overall, this framework offers deeper and more reliable insights into the limitations of current LLMs in mathematical reasoning and establishes a foundation for future research into developing models with genuine logical reasoning capabilities.

057f18b6baa4efbaa33ea1ca148c71787dbebc47.title: Regularization of the policy updates for stabilizing Mean Field Games
057f18b6baa4efbaa33ea1ca148c71787dbebc47.research_question: How can policy optimization methods be adapted to stabilize learning and improve convergence in non-cooperative Mean Field Games (MFG) with large populations of agents?
057f18b6baa4efbaa33ea1ca148c71787dbebc47.hypothesis: Introducing a double proximal regularization to policy updates in Mean Field Games will stabilize learning dynamics and improve convergence to the Mean Field Nash Equilibrium (MFNE) compared to existing value-based and averaging methods.
057f18b6baa4efbaa33ea1ca148c71787dbebc47.proposed_method: A novel algorithm, Mean Field Proximal Policy Optimization (MF-PPO), will be developed to address instability in learning within Mean Field Games. The approach extends Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) by incorporating a double proximal regularization: one constraining policy updates within each episode (intra-iteration) and another constraining updates between iterations (inter-iteration). The MF-PPO objective function combines these two regularization terms, weighted by a hyper-parameter α, to balance the proximity of the policy between intra- and inter-iteration updates. The algorithm proceeds by iteratively updating the mean-field distribution, collecting trajectories under the current policy, estimating advantages, and optimizing both the policy and value networks while enforcing the proximal constraints. This regularization is designed to prevent large, destabilizing policy shifts and to smooth the learning process toward the MFNE.
057f18b6baa4efbaa33ea1ca148c71787dbebc47.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the OpenSpiel framework, focusing on crowd modeling scenarios with congestion, specifically the Four-Rooms (10x10 grid, 40-step horizon) and Maze (20x20 grid, 100-step horizon) environments. The state space is represented as a two-dimensional grid, and the action space consists of five discrete actions. The reward function penalizes distance from the goal, unnecessary movement, and crowding. The proposed MF-PPO algorithm will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines: Deep-Munchausen Online Mirror Descent (D-MOMD) and Deep Average-Network Fictitious Play (D-ANFP). Evaluation will use the exploitability metric to measure convergence to the MFNE, and results will be averaged over multiple random seeds. Additional analysis will be performed on the impact of hyper-parameters, including the regularization weight α and clipping factors for intra- and inter-iteration updates. Computational efficiency (CPU time) will also be reported.
057f18b6baa4efbaa33ea1ca148c71787dbebc47.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to introduce a policy-based optimization method, specifically a double proximal regularization strategy, for stabilizing learning in general Mean Field Games with deep reinforcement learning. Unlike prior methods that rely on value-based learning or averaging techniques, MF-PPO directly regularizes policy updates both within and across iterations, leading to improved convergence rates and lower exploitability. This innovation broadens the spectrum of scalable algorithms for MFG to include policy optimization, which is especially advantageous in environments with large or continuous action spaces.

057f8de4c6702f20fef90d31ab6d54a555739e66.title: Hierarchical Fine-grained Preference Optimization for Physically Plausible Video Generation
057f8de4c6702f20fef90d31ab6d54a555739e66.research_question: How can physically plausible video generation be improved to better align with the laws of physics and human preferences, while efficiently utilizing existing data resources?
057f8de4c6702f20fef90d31ab6d54a555739e66.hypothesis: Hierarchical, fine-grained preference optimization across multiple levels (instance, state, motion, semantic) combined with automated selection of real-world, diverse, and physically faithful data will significantly enhance the physical plausibility and overall quality of generated videos compared to existing methods.
057f8de4c6702f20fef90d31ab6d54a555739e66.proposed_method: A novel framework, PhysHPO, is proposed for hierarchical cross-modal direct preference optimization in video generation. The method introduces four levels of preference alignment: (1) Instance-level, ensuring overall video content matches the input prompt; (2) State-level, anchoring physical states at the start and end frames for temporal consistency; (3) Motion-level, modeling and aligning motion trajectories using structural information such as optical flow; and (4) Semantic-level, maintaining logical and narrative consistency between textual prompts and generated visuals. The optimization objective integrates these levels into a unified loss function with adjustable weights. Additionally, an automated data selection pipeline is developed to filter large-scale text-video datasets for real-world, physically faithful, and diverse samples using vision-language models and large language models for scoring and diversity enforcement, thus maximizing the utility of existing data.
057f8de4c6702f20fef90d31ab6d54a555739e66.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using advanced video generation models (e.g., CogVideoX-2B and CogVideoX-5B) as the base, with PhysHPO applied as a post-training optimization. The selected dataset will be derived from OpenVidHD-0.4M, filtered for real-world and physically plausible content, and further diversified using embedding-based cosine distance criteria. Baselines for comparison include PhyT2V, vanilla DPO, SFT, and the respective base models. Evaluation will be performed on physics-focused benchmarks (VideoPhy, PhyGenBench) and general capability benchmarks (VBench), using metrics such as physical plausibility, semantic adherence, visual quality, and motion quality. Implementation details include training with AdamW optimizer, a batch size of 8, and experiments run on 8 NVIDIA H100 GPUs. Ablation studies and user studies will be conducted to assess the contribution of each hierarchical level and alignment with human preferences.
057f8de4c6702f20fef90d31ab6d54a555739e66.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first hierarchical, fine-grained cross-modal direct preference optimization framework for video generation, targeting physical plausibility at multiple granularities. It pioneers automated data selection for video generation, leveraging real-world videos and large-scale datasets to efficiently identify high-quality, physically faithful, and diverse samples without the need for costly new dataset construction. The synergy of strategic data selection and multi-level preference optimization is claimed to yield superior physical fidelity, general quality, and data efficiency compared to existing supervised fine-tuning and DPO approaches.

05877e76088d0f7d1363f287f44e359708667579.title: Internal Causal Mechanisms Robustly Predict Language Model Out-of-Distribution Behaviors
05877e76088d0f7d1363f287f44e359708667579.research_question: Can internal causal mechanisms identified within language models be leveraged to robustly predict model output correctness, particularly under out-of-distribution (OOD) conditions, across a diverse set of language modeling tasks?
05877e76088d0f7d1363f287f44e359708667579.hypothesis: Internal causal features that play a distinctive causal role in a model's behavior can serve as robust predictors of output correctness, outperforming causal-agnostic features and confidence-based methods, especially under distribution shifts.
05877e76088d0f7d1363f287f44e359708667579.proposed_method: A two-stage framework is developed for predicting language model output correctness under distribution shifts. First, high-level abstract causal mechanisms relevant to task performance are identified and localized within the model using techniques such as Distributed Alignment Search (DAS), which maps high-level variables to neural representations via distributed interchange interventions. Second, two methods are proposed for correctness prediction: (1) counterfactual simulation, which checks if the model implements the identified causal mechanisms by simulating interventions and measuring whether key causal variables are realized; and (2) value probing, which uses the values of localized causal variables to predict correctness via learned decision boundaries, typically using linear classifiers. These methods are compared to baselines using output probabilities (confidence scores) and causal-agnostic internal features, with all approaches evaluated for both in-distribution and OOD settings.
05877e76088d0f7d1363f287f44e359708667579.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on five language modeling tasks spanning symbolic manipulation (Indirect Object Identification, PriceTag), knowledge retrieval (RAVEL, MMLU), and instruction following (UnlearnHP), covering both tasks with fully known and partially known internal mechanisms. For each task, both in-distribution and multiple OOD settings are constructed by perturbing input variables, templates, or background conditions. The primary evaluation metric is AUC-ROC, measuring the ability to distinguish correct from incorrect model outputs. Baselines include confidence score-based methods (with temperature scaling), causal-agnostic probing of internal activations, and correctness probing using both background and causal variables. The main model evaluated is Llama-3-8B-Instruct, with additional experiments on other model sizes for generalization.
05877e76088d0f7d1363f287f44e359708667579.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel application of internal causal analysis for predicting language model output correctness under distribution shifts, demonstrating that causal features localized via mechanistic interpretability techniques are significantly more robust predictors than traditional confidence scores or causal-agnostic features. The two proposed methods—counterfactual simulation and value probing—provide new, principled approaches for leveraging internal causal mechanisms in correctness prediction, outperforming existing baselines in OOD settings. This work establishes a predictive use case for causal interpretability, suggesting a path from mechanistic understanding to improved model reliability and safety.

0597e979716c2488f82e607fbf4fae37d14b8a30.title: Deep Symbolic Regression for Physics Guided by Units Constraints: Toward the Automated Discovery of Physical Laws
0597e979716c2488f82e607fbf4fae37d14b8a30.research_question: How can the automated discovery of physical laws from data be improved by incorporating physical units constraints into deep symbolic regression frameworks?
0597e979716c2488f82e607fbf4fae37d14b8a30.hypothesis: Incorporating in situ physical units constraints into the symbolic expression generation process will significantly reduce the search space, improve the physical plausibility, interpretability, and accuracy of discovered equations, and enhance robustness to noise compared to existing symbolic regression methods.
0597e979716c2488f82e607fbf4fae37d14b8a30.proposed_method: A novel symbolic regression framework, termed Physical Symbolic Optimization (Φ-SO), will be developed to recover analytical symbolic expressions from physics data using deep reinforcement learning. The method will encode physical units information directly into the expression generation process by maintaining a tree representation of the evolving mathematical expression and computing local units constraints at each step. A recurrent neural network (RNN), specifically an LSTM, will generate candidate expressions in prefix notation, with the categorical distribution over tokens masked in real-time to enforce units consistency. The RNN will be trained via a risk-seeking policy gradient reinforcement learning strategy, where only the top-performing candidate expressions (according to a reward function based on normalized RMSE and optionally complexity) are reinforced. Free constants in candidate expressions will be optimized using gradient-based methods (e.g., L-BFGS) within PyTorch, leveraging auto-differentiation. The approach will allow for the inclusion of additional grammatical or domain-specific priors and will be parallelized for computational efficiency.
0597e979716c2488f82e607fbf4fae37d14b8a30.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a standard benchmark of 120 equations drawn from the Feynman Lectures on Physics and other physics textbooks. The proposed Φ-SO framework will be compared against 17 popular symbolic regression algorithms, including both classical genetic programming-based and modern deep learning-based methods. Evaluation metrics will include exact symbolic recovery rate, normalized RMSE, robustness to varying levels of noise (including up to 10%), and the physical plausibility of discovered expressions. Additional ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of units constraints and other priors. The framework's capabilities will also be demonstrated on a suite of astrophysical test cases. Computational efficiency will be measured in terms of parallelized constant optimization and overall runtime on different hardware configurations.
0597e979716c2488f82e607fbf4fae37d14b8a30.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a deep symbolic regression framework that, for the first time, enforces physical units constraints in situ during the generation of candidate expressions, ensuring that only physically plausible equations are produced by construction. This approach drastically reduces the combinatorial search space, improves interpretability and accuracy, and enables state-of-the-art performance in the presence of noise. Unlike previous methods that render variables dimensionless prior to regression, this framework leverages dimensional analysis as a grammatical constraint, guiding the neural network to learn and respect physical laws. The method is fully generalizable to any symbolic regression approach and is designed for extensibility to additional domain-specific priors.

05b15934d837dc84afa96824742d3dcc7ec88e09.title: Drag Your GAN: Interactive Point-based Manipulation on the Generative Image Manifold
05b15934d837dc84afa96824742d3dcc7ec88e09.research_question: How can interactive, precise, and flexible point-based manipulation of images be achieved on the manifold of generative adversarial networks (GANs), allowing users to control spatial attributes such as pose, shape, expression, and layout across diverse object categories?
05b15934d837dc84afa96824742d3dcc7ec88e09.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging the discriminative feature space of a pre-trained GAN, combined with an iterative optimization process for latent codes and feature-based point tracking, will enable accurate, flexible, and efficient point-based image manipulation that generalizes across object categories and supports multiple simultaneous constraints.
05b15934d837dc84afa96824742d3dcc7ec88e09.proposed_method: A novel interactive image manipulation framework will be developed that enables users to specify pairs of handle points and target points on a GAN-generated image, optionally with a mask to restrict the editable region. The method will iteratively optimize the latent code of the GAN using a feature-based motion supervision loss, which shifts patches in the generator's intermediate feature space to move handle points toward their targets. After each optimization step, a point tracking algorithm based on nearest neighbor search in the GAN's feature space will update the handle points to follow the object as it deforms. The process repeats until all handle points reach their corresponding targets, supporting multiple points and precise spatial control. The approach will be implemented efficiently to support live, interactive editing sessions, and will include a GUI for user interaction.
05b15934d837dc84afa96824742d3dcc7ec88e09.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of datasets using pre-trained StyleGAN2 models, including FFHQ (faces), AFHQCat, SHHQ, LSUNCar, LSUNCat, LandscapesHQ, microscope images, and self-distilled animal datasets (Lion, Dog, Elephant). Baseline comparisons will include UserControllableLT for point-based editing and RAFT and PIPs for point tracking. Evaluation metrics will include mean distance (MD) between manipulated and target landmarks (for face landmark manipulation), FID for image quality, MSE and LPIPS for paired image reconstruction, and qualitative assessment of editing fidelity and realism. Both qualitative and quantitative results will be reported, including ablation studies on feature selection and mask effects, and the system's ability to perform out-of-distribution manipulations and real image editing via GAN inversion.
05b15934d837dc84afa96824742d3dcc7ec88e09.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a general and efficient framework for interactive point-based manipulation on the GAN image manifold, supporting multiple simultaneous handle-target constraints with pixel-level precision. Unlike prior methods, it does not require additional neural networks for motion supervision or tracking, relying instead on the discriminative power of GAN feature spaces. The method enables flexible, precise, and generalizable control over spatial attributes across diverse object categories, supports region masking, and achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and realism in both in-distribution and out-of-distribution editing scenarios. The approach also demonstrates superior performance in point tracking for GAN-generated images compared to existing tracking algorithms.

05bad81069c8b11202e90ac16c543efc774e2800.title: NoMaD: Goal Masked Diffusion Policies for Navigation and Exploration
05bad81069c8b11202e90ac16c543efc774e2800.research_question: How can a single, unified policy enable both goal-conditioned navigation and undirected exploration for mobile robots in previously unseen environments, using only visual observations and optional goal specifications?
05bad81069c8b11202e90ac16c543efc774e2800.hypothesis: A unified diffusion policy model, equipped with goal masking and trained on diverse real-world navigation data, can achieve superior performance in both goal-conditioned navigation and undirected exploration compared to separate or traditional models, while maintaining computational efficiency and robustness in unseen environments.
05bad81069c8b11202e90ac16c543efc774e2800.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops a unified policy, NoMaD, based on a Transformer backbone with dual EfficientNet-B0 encoders for processing sequences of RGB observations and an optional goal image. Goal masking is introduced as a binary mechanism to flexibly condition the policy on the presence or absence of a goal, enabling the same model to switch between goal-directed and undirected behaviors. The action distribution is modeled using a conditional diffusion process, where a 1D conditional U-Net predicts noise over future action sequences, trained with a square cosine noise scheduler and 10 denoising steps. The policy is integrated with a topological graph-based episodic memory for long-horizon planning, allowing the robot to plan and execute trajectories in large, previously unseen environments. Training is performed end-to-end with supervised learning, using a combination of mean squared error losses for both action prediction and temporal distance to goal, and goal masking is sampled with a 0.5 probability to ensure balanced exposure to both behaviors.
05bad81069c8b11202e90ac16c543efc774e2800.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six distinct real-world indoor and outdoor environments using mobile robot platforms. The training dataset will comprise the GNM and SACSoN datasets, totaling over 100 hours of diverse real-world navigation trajectories. The unified policy will be compared against six baselines, including latent variable models (VIB), goal-conditioned navigation transformers (ViNT), autoregressive action models, subgoal diffusion models, and random subgoal selection, with all baselines trained on the same data for 20 epochs. Evaluation metrics will include mean success rate for both undirected exploration and goal-conditioned navigation, as well as the mean number of collisions per experiment. Additional ablation studies will assess the impact of visual encoder architecture and goal masking strategies on performance.
05bad81069c8b11202e90ac16c543efc774e2800.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to instantiate a goal-conditioned diffusion policy capable of both task-agnostic exploration and task-oriented navigation within a single unified model. Key innovations include the use of goal masking for flexible policy conditioning, direct action modeling with diffusion processes (rather than subgoal image generation), and integration with topological memory for scalable long-horizon planning. The approach claims significant improvements over state-of-the-art baselines in both efficiency (15× fewer parameters) and performance (over 25% higher success rates), while maintaining real-time operation on edge hardware.

05c7eabf85ab246fa30beb191c6b13cf1181d1ba.title: Stable VITON: Learning Semantic Correspondence with Latent Diffusion Model for Virtual Try-On
05c7eabf85ab246fa30beb191c6b13cf1181d1ba.research_question: How can semantic correspondence between clothing and the human body be effectively learned to enable high-fidelity, detail-preserving, and generalizable image-based virtual try-on using pre-trained diffusion models?
05c7eabf85ab246fa30beb191c6b13cf1181d1ba.hypothesis: Integrating a zero cross-attention block within the latent space of a pre-trained diffusion model, combined with a novel attention total variation loss and targeted augmentation, will enable precise semantic correspondence between clothing and the human body, resulting in superior preservation of clothing details and high-quality virtual try-on images, even in complex backgrounds and cross-dataset scenarios.
05c7eabf85ab246fa30beb191c6b13cf1181d1ba.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces StableVITON, an end-to-end virtual try-on framework that leverages the latent space of a pre-trained diffusion model. The method incorporates a spatial encoder that processes the clothing image and conditions the U-Net backbone using zero cross-attention blocks, aligning intermediate clothing features with the human body representation. The input to the U-Net is expanded to include the noisy image, a clothing-agnostic person representation, an agnostic mask, and a dense pose condition, all concatenated and processed in the latent space. To further enhance semantic alignment and detail preservation, a novel attention total variation loss is introduced, which encourages sharper and more localized attention maps, and targeted augmentation is applied during training to improve robustness and generalization. The architecture is designed to operate without impairing the pre-trained diffusion model, enabling high-quality synthesis even for images with complex backgrounds.
