05c7eabf85ab246fa30beb191c6b13cf1181d1ba.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the VITON-HD, DressCode, and SHHQ-1.0 datasets, covering both single-dataset and cross-dataset evaluation settings. The method is compared against several baselines, including GAN-based models (VITON-HD, HR-VITON, GP-VTON) and diffusion-based models (LADI-VTON, DCI-VTON, Paint-by-Example, ControlNet). Evaluation metrics include SSIM and LPIPS for paired (reconstruction) settings, and FID and KID for unpaired (realism) settings. The model is trained at 1024x768 resolution but evaluated at 512x384 for fair comparison. Ablation studies are conducted to assess the impact of the zero cross-attention block, augmentation, and attention total variation loss. User studies with human participants are performed to assess perceptual quality across criteria such as fidelity, person attributes, clothing identity, and background consistency.
05c7eabf85ab246fa30beb191c6b13cf1181d1ba.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first end-to-end virtual try-on method that fine-tunes a pre-trained diffusion model without relying on an independent warping process. A novel zero cross-attention block is developed to learn semantic correspondence between clothing and the human body in the latent space, enabling precise alignment and detail preservation. The attention total variation loss and targeted augmentation are newly designed to sharpen attention maps and further enhance semantic correspondence learning. The approach demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in both qualitative and quantitative evaluations, including challenging cross-dataset scenarios, and shows strong generalization and real-world applicability.

05f9997d61460fea9b586f98722c4be32f4a8b22.title: Simple Guidance Mechanisms for Discrete Diffusion Models
05f9997d61460fea9b586f98722c4be32f4a8b22.research_question: How can controllable generation be effectively achieved with discrete diffusion models across various discrete data domains, and what mechanisms enable improved guidance and performance in such models compared to autoregressive and existing diffusion baselines?
05f9997d61460fea9b586f98722c4be32f4a8b22.hypothesis: Discrete diffusion models equipped with simple and tractable classifier-free and classifier-based guidance mechanisms, especially when leveraging uniform noise processes and improved variational bounds, will enable more effective and controllable generation in discrete domains than autoregressive models or prior discrete diffusion approaches.
05f9997d61460fea9b586f98722c4be32f4a8b22.proposed_method: The proposed methodology develops two guidance mechanisms for discrete diffusion models: Discrete Classifier-Free Guidance (D-CFG) and Discrete Classifier-Based Guidance (D-CBG). D-CFG adapts classifier-free guidance by training both conditional and unconditional denoising diffusion networks, using a temperature parameter to interpolate between them, and factorizes the guided distribution across sequence tokens for efficient sampling. D-CBG adapts classifier-based guidance by training a classifier on noised latent sequences and combining its outputs with an unconditional denoising network, employing a tractable normalization by restricting summation to per-token alternatives and using a first-order Taylor approximation for efficiency in large vocabularies or long sequences. Additionally, the method introduces Uniform Diffusion Language Models (UDLM), which use a uniform noise corruption process and a continuous-time variational lower bound (NELBO) to tighten the training objective and allow for repeated editing of tokens during denoising, improving both guidance and generation quality. The denoising process is parameterized to predict clean data from noisy latents, and the continuous-time NELBO is analytically derived and extended to sequence modeling.
05f9997d61460fea9b586f98722c4be32f4a8b22.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of discrete data domains, including genomic sequences (Species10), small molecule design (QM9, using SMILES strings), discretized images (CIFAR10), and natural language datasets (text8, Amazon Review, LM1B). For language modeling, perplexity and bits-per-character (BPC) will be used as evaluation metrics, while for image generation, Frechet Inception Distance (FID) and Inception Score (IS) will be measured. Guidance experiments will compare the proposed methods to autoregressive baselines (including FUDGE and PPLM) and previous diffusion guidance methods (e.g., NOS), evaluating controllability (e.g., F1, AUROC for class-conditional generation), validity, novelty, and property maximization (e.g., QED, ring count for molecules). Hyperparameters such as guidance strength and sampling steps will be varied, and ablations will be performed to assess the impact of the continuous-time formulation and faster sampling regimes.
05f9997d61460fea9b586f98722c4be32f4a8b22.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first simple and tractable adaptations of classifier-free and classifier-based guidance mechanisms for discrete diffusion models, enabling efficient and effective controllable generation in discrete domains. It presents a novel class of Uniform Diffusion Language Models (UDLM) with a continuous-time variational lower bound, significantly improving the performance of uniform noise diffusion and closing the gap to state-of-the-art absorbing-state models, especially in small vocabulary settings. The guidance mechanisms are shown to outperform both autoregressive and prior diffusion-based baselines in terms of controllability and generation quality across multiple domains. The approach also demonstrates robustness to faster sampling and enables repeated editing of tokens, which is not possible with previous discrete diffusion models.

060e0df71620f1844839f6a993dfa5fb8e4c3bf6.title: Android in the Wild: A Large-Scale Dataset for Android Device Control
060e0df71620f1844839f6a993dfa5fb8e4c3bf6.research_question: How can large-scale, diverse datasets of human demonstrations for Android device control advance the development and evaluation of systems that interpret natural language instructions and execute them via direct manipulation of device user interfaces?
060e0df71620f1844839f6a993dfa5fb8e4c3bf6.hypothesis: A large-scale, realistic dataset of human-annotated Android device interactions, encompassing diverse tasks, applications, and device versions, will enable the training and evaluation of device-control agents that generalize better to novel instructions, applications, and UI variations compared to agents trained on existing, smaller datasets.
060e0df71620f1844839f6a993dfa5fb8e4c3bf6.proposed_method: A comprehensive dataset, Android in the Wild (AITW), will be constructed by collecting over 715,000 episodes of human demonstrations on Android devices, spanning more than 350 applications and websites, four Android versions, and eight device types. Each episode will consist of a natural language instruction and a sequence of observation-action pairs, where observations are screenshots and actions are precise gestures (taps, drags, text entry) recorded at arbitrary screen coordinates. Data collection will use a two-stage pipeline: first, raters will perform full tasks on emulated devices, and second, hindsight language relabeling will be applied to annotate single-step sub-tasks. Post-processing will extract UI elements from screenshots using OCR and icon detection, providing pixel-based screen features. The dataset will be organized to facilitate robustness and generalization analysis, including splits for unseen tasks, instructions, applications, and Android versions.
060e0df71620f1844839f6a993dfa5fb8e4c3bf6.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training and evaluating device-control agents using the AITW dataset. Baseline agents will include a Transformer-based behavioral cloning model (BC) that predicts action types and gestures from screen features and instructions, and a large language model (LLM, e.g., PaLM 2) that predicts actions based on a text-based screen representation. Evaluation will use both standard train/validation/test splits and specialized out-of-distribution splits: unseen Android version, unseen instruction subject/verb templates, and unseen domains (apps/websites). Metrics will include partial and complete action matching scores, computed by comparing predicted actions to ground truth based on action type and spatial proximity, as well as human validation for a subset of episodes. The experimental setup will test the agents' ability to generalize to new instructions, UI layouts, and device contexts.
060e0df71620f1844839f6a993dfa5fb8e4c3bf6.novelty_claims: The proposed dataset is orders of magnitude larger and more diverse than existing device-control datasets, providing realistic, multi-step, high-level task instructions and execution paths across a wide range of Android environments. The dataset uniquely captures precise gesture actions at arbitrary screen locations, rather than relying on UI metadata or element-based actions, and supports robust evaluation of generalization to new tasks, language patterns, applications, and platform versions. The methodology for data collection and annotation, including hindsight language relabeling and pixel-based UI element extraction, represents a significant advancement in enabling research on natural language-driven device control.

06353b9112ab14c26ce9d3c851c01ebe4b798177.title: TimeMixer: Decomposable Multiscale Mixing for Time Series Forecasting
06353b9112ab14c26ce9d3c851c01ebe4b798177.research_question: How can time series forecasting models be improved to better handle intricate temporal variations by leveraging information present at multiple temporal scales?
06353b9112ab14c26ce9d3c851c01ebe4b798177.hypothesis: Disentangling and separately mixing seasonal and trend components across multiple temporal scales, and aggregating predictions from multiple scale-specific predictors, will enhance the accuracy and efficiency of time series forecasting for both long-term and short-term tasks.
06353b9112ab14c26ce9d3c851c01ebe4b798177.proposed_method: A fully MLP-based architecture, named TimeMixer, is proposed to address multiscale temporal variations in time series forecasting. The method begins by generating multiscale representations of the input series through average downsampling, producing a set of time series at different resolutions. Past-Decomposable-Mixing (PDM) blocks are then applied, which decompose each scale into seasonal and trend components using a series decomposition module. Seasonal components are mixed in a bottom-up fashion (fine-to-coarse), while trend components are mixed top-down (coarse-to-fine), each via dedicated linear layers with GELU activations. For prediction, a Future-Multipredictor-Mixing (FMM) block ensembles the outputs of multiple scale-specific predictors, each regressing the future sequence from its respective scale's mixed representation, and combines their outputs to form the final forecast. This architecture is designed to capture both detailed and macroscopic temporal patterns and to integrate complementary forecasting capabilities from different scales.
06353b9112ab14c26ce9d3c851c01ebe4b798177.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 18 real-world benchmarks covering both long-term and short-term forecasting tasks. Long-term forecasting datasets include ETT (ETTh1, ETTh2, ETTm1, ETTm2), Weather, Solar-Energy, Electricity, and Traffic, while short-term forecasting uses PeMS (PEMS03, PEMS04, PEMS07, PEMS08) and the M4 dataset. The model will be compared against 15 state-of-the-art baselines such as PatchTST, TimesNet, SCINet, Crossformer, MICN, FiLM, DLinear, FEDformer, and others. Evaluation metrics include MSE, MAE, RMSE, MAPE, SMAPE, MASE, and OWA, depending on the dataset. All experiments will use aligned input lengths and repeated runs for fair comparison, and will be implemented in PyTorch on NVIDIA A100 GPUs. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of each architectural component.
06353b9112ab14c26ce9d3c851c01ebe4b798177.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel multiscale mixing framework for time series forecasting that goes beyond traditional decomposition and multiperiodicity analysis. Key innovations include the separate bottom-up mixing of seasonal components and top-down mixing of trend components across multiple scales, as well as the ensemble of multiple scale-specific predictors for future forecasting. This design enables effective disentanglement and integration of micro- and macro-level temporal patterns, leading to consistent state-of-the-art performance and superior computational efficiency across a wide range of benchmarks.

064ccebc03d3afabaae30fe29a457c1cfcdff7e3.title: DiffEdit: Diffusion-based semantic image editing with mask guidance
064ccebc03d3afabaae30fe29a457c1cfcdff7e3.research_question: How can semantic image editing be performed using text-conditioned diffusion models in a way that localizes edits to relevant regions of an input image, without requiring user-provided masks, while preserving the original image content as much as possible?
064ccebc03d3afabaae30fe29a457c1cfcdff7e3.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by automatically inferring editing masks through the comparison of noise predictions from text-conditioned diffusion models under different prompts, and by leveraging DDIM-based latent encoding of the input image, it is possible to achieve precise, localized, and natural semantic edits that outperform existing mask-based and mask-free diffusion editing methods in terms of edit quality and preservation of input image content.
064ccebc03d3afabaae30fe29a457c1cfcdff7e3.proposed_method: The proposed method, termed DIFFEDIT, introduces a three-step framework for semantic image editing. First, a mask is automatically generated by contrasting the noise predictions of a diffusion model conditioned on the target text query and a reference text (or no text), identifying regions of the input image that should be edited. Second, the input image is encoded into the latent space using DDIM encoding, preserving its content in a manner that facilitates subtle and natural edits. Third, the editing process is performed by DDIM decoding conditioned on the text query, with the inferred mask guiding the denoising process such that only the masked region is edited, while the rest of the image is reconstructed from the latent encoding. The mask is computed by averaging spatial differences in noise predictions over multiple noise samples, rescaling, and binarizing the result. The mask-guided DDIM update replaces pixel values outside the mask with those from the encoded latent, ensuring minimal deviation from the original image outside the edited region.
064ccebc03d3afabaae30fe29a457c1cfcdff7e3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three datasets: ImageNet (for class-based edits), COCO (for complex, caption-based edits), and synthetic images generated by Imagen (for compositional edits). The method will use latent diffusion models, including a class-conditional model trained on ImageNet and the Stable Diffusion model trained on LAION-5B. Baselines for comparison will include SDEdit, FlexIT, ILVR, and Cross Attention Control, with all methods evaluated using the same diffusion backbone where possible. Evaluation metrics will include LPIPS (perceptual similarity to the input), CSFID (class-conditional FID for ImageNet), FID (image realism), and CLIPScore (alignment with text query). Trade-off curves between edit strength and preservation of the input image will be analyzed by varying the encoding ratio parameter. Ablation studies will assess the contributions of mask inference and DDIM encoding, and the impact of mask binarization thresholds will be explored.
064ccebc03d3afabaae30fe29a457c1cfcdff7e3.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is novel in that it enables fully automatic, mask-free semantic image editing by leveraging the internal behavior of text-conditioned diffusion models to infer editing regions. It combines mask inference with DDIM-based latent encoding to achieve highly localized and natural edits, outperforming prior mask-based and mask-free diffusion editing methods. The method is efficient, requiring no model fine-tuning or optimization at inference, and is compatible with large-scale pre-trained diffusion models. Theoretical analysis is provided to justify the use of DDIM encoding over noise-based approaches, and extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on multiple challenging benchmarks.

06550f40fc1bf67b2ca7d7f85f16a2bc141be45e.title: Neural Genetic Search in Discrete Spaces
06550f40fc1bf67b2ca7d7f85f16a2bc141be45e.research_question: How can the evolutionary search capabilities of genetic algorithms be integrated directly into the generation process of deep generative models to improve solution quality, diversity, and robustness across a wide range of discrete optimization tasks?
06550f40fc1bf67b2ca7d7f85f16a2bc141be45e.hypothesis: Incorporating problem-agnostic genetic operators, such as crossover and mutation, directly into the sequential generation process of pretrained deep generative models will enable more effective and robust search in discrete spaces, outperforming traditional search and decoding methods in terms of solution quality and diversity.
06550f40fc1bf67b2ca7d7f85f16a2bc141be45e.proposed_method: A novel test-time search algorithm, Neural Genetic Search (NGS), will be developed to combine the population-based exploration of genetic algorithms with the expressive power of pretrained sequential generative models. The method will initialize a population of candidate solutions using the generative model, then iteratively select parent solutions based on their rewards using rank-based prioritized sampling. Offspring will be generated via a parent-conditioned crossover, where the generative model's vocabulary is restricted to tokens present in the parents, and mutation will be introduced by occasionally relaxing this restriction to promote diversity. The population will be updated by replacing low-reward individuals with newly generated offspring, and this evolutionary cycle will repeat for a fixed number of iterations. The approach will be designed to be model-agnostic and easily integrated with any sequential generative model.
06550f40fc1bf67b2ca7d7f85f16a2bc141be45e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across three distinct domains: combinatorial routing problems (including TSP, CVRP, PCTSP, and OP), automated red-teaming of language models, and de novo molecular design. For routing problems, pretrained graph neural networks and autoregressive models will serve as the generative backbone, and performance will be compared against sampling, beam search, Monte Carlo Tree Search, and ant colony optimization baselines using standard benchmarks (e.g., TSPLib, CVRPLib). Evaluation metrics will include optimality gap, solution diversity, and computational efficiency. In red-teaming, the method will be applied to generate attack prompts for language models, with toxicity and diversity measured using classifier-based scoring and embedding-based diversity metrics, and transferability tested across multiple victim models. For molecular design, the method will be benchmarked on the Practical Molecular Optimization (PMO) suite, comparing top-10 property scores and validity rates against specialized genetic algorithms such as GraphGA, SMILESGA, STONED, and SynNet, using LSTM or GFlowNet-based generative policies.
06550f40fc1bf67b2ca7d7f85f16a2bc141be45e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a problem-agnostic, model-agnostic genetic search framework that integrates genetic operators directly into the generative process of deep models, eliminating the need for hand-crafted, domain-specific crossover and mutation rules. The method enables iterative, population-based refinement at inference time, providing improved robustness to distribution shifts and enhanced solution quality and diversity. Unlike prior works that chain genetic algorithms and deep models or rely on post-hoc search, this approach unifies evolutionary search and generative modeling in a single, flexible framework applicable to any sequential generative model and a wide range of discrete domains.

06582e8ed167c3ce73a630c2e8102b0e905baf1f.title: A Closer Look at the Robustness of Contrastive Language-Image Pre-Training (CLIP)
06582e8ed167c3ce73a630c2e8102b0e905baf1f.research_question: How robust are contrastive language-image pre-training (CLIP) models to variations in specific visual factors, and how do they perform in terms of predictive uncertainty and out-of-distribution (OOD) detection compared to other vision models? What are the key factors influencing these safety-related properties across diverse architectures, training distributions, and evaluation conditions?
06582e8ed167c3ce73a630c2e8102b0e905baf1f.hypothesis: CLIP models exhibit superior robustness to certain visual factor variations, competitive OOD detection, and reliable predictive uncertainty estimation compared to conventional ImageNet models, but their performance on these safety-related properties is significantly influenced by training source, fine-tuning procedures, and evaluation prompts.
06582e8ed167c3ce73a630c2e8102b0e905baf1f.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical study will be conducted on a large collection of CLIP models and ImageNet classifiers, systematically evaluating their robustness to visual factor variations, OOD detection capability, and predictive uncertainty. The methodology involves analyzing 83 CLIP models (including both zero-shot and fine-tuned variants) and 127 ImageNet classifiers, spanning diverse architectures (ResNet, ConvNeXt, ViT, MLP-Mixer), training sources (WIT, LAION), and dataset sizes (80M to 2B samples). Robustness will be assessed using ImageNet-X with 10 annotated visual factors, while OOD detection will be evaluated using established benchmarks and metrics such as AUROC and FPR@95. Predictive uncertainty will be measured using calibration metrics (ECE, NLL) on both in-distribution and OOD datasets, with and without temperature scaling. The study will further analyze the impact of model architecture, training distribution, dataset quantity, fine-tuning strategies, and test-time prompt selection on all three safety objectives.
06582e8ed167c3ce73a630c2e8102b0e905baf1f.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize 51 zero-shot CLIP models and 32 ImageNet fine-tuned CLIP models, compared against 127 diverse ImageNet models. Robustness will be evaluated on ImageNet-X, focusing on 10 visual factors (e.g., pose, background, shape, color, texture), as well as on cue-conflict stimuli and Stylized-ImageNet for bias analysis. OOD detection will be tested using ImageNet as the in-distribution set and five OOD datasets: iNaturalist, SUN, PLACES, TEXTURE, and ImageNet-O, with performance measured by AUROC and FPR@95. Calibration and predictive uncertainty will be assessed on ImageNet validation (ID) and multiple OOD datasets (ImageNet-V2, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-Sketch, ObjectNet, ImageNet-Vid-Robust) using ECE and NLL, both before and after temperature scaling. The influence of test-time prompts will be investigated by varying prompt sets (1, 5, 30, 80 prompts) and analyzing their effects on all safety objectives.
06582e8ed167c3ce73a630c2e8102b0e905baf1f.novelty_claims: The proposed study offers the first comprehensive, large-scale analysis of CLIP models' robustness, OOD detection, and predictive uncertainty across a wide range of architectures, training sources, and evaluation conditions. It introduces a detailed factor-level robustness assessment using ImageNet-X, uncovers the critical influence of training source and fine-tuning on safety-related properties, and challenges previous assumptions about CLIP's calibration superiority. The investigation into prompt effects and the systematic comparison with a broad set of baseline models provide new insights for designing more robust and reliable vision-language models.

0671fd553dd670a4e820553a974bc48040ba0819.title: Reflexion: language agents with verbal reinforcement learning
0671fd553dd670a4e820553a974bc48040ba0819.research_question: How can language agents based on large language models be enabled to learn efficiently from trial-and-error interactions with external environments, without requiring extensive training samples or expensive model fine-tuning?
0671fd553dd670a4e820553a974bc48040ba0819.hypothesis: Providing language agents with verbal, self-generated feedback stored in episodic memory will enable more efficient and effective learning from experience, leading to improved decision-making, reasoning, and programming performance across diverse tasks compared to agents relying solely on scalar rewards or in-context learning.
0671fd553dd670a4e820553a974bc48040ba0819.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed in which a language agent is composed of three modular components: an Actor (an LLM-based policy that generates actions and text), an Evaluator (which scores the agent's output using environment feedback or task-specific heuristics), and a Self-Reflection model (an LLM that generates verbal feedback based on the agent's trajectory, reward, and memory). After each trial, the agent receives a reward signal, which is amplified into a natural language self-reflection summary and stored in a long-term memory buffer. In subsequent episodes, the Actor conditions its decisions on both short-term (trajectory) and long-term (self-reflection) memory, enabling iterative improvement. The framework supports various feedback types (binary, scalar, or free-form language) and sources (external or internally simulated), and is designed to be lightweight, requiring no model fine-tuning.
0671fd553dd670a4e820553a974bc48040ba0819.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across three domains: sequential decision-making (using the AlfWorld suite of text-based environments), reasoning (using the HotPotQA question-answering dataset), and programming/code generation (using HumanEval, MBPP, and the newly introduced LeetcodeHardGym benchmarks in Python and Rust). Baseline agents will include ReAct, Chain-of-Thought, and other state-of-the-art LLM-based approaches without self-reflection. Evaluation metrics will include task completion rates, pass@1 accuracy for code generation, and exact match for question answering. Ablation studies will be performed to isolate the contributions of self-reflection, episodic memory, and test generation components. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by using consistent prompting, memory limits, and evaluation protocols across all agent variants.
0671fd553dd670a4e820553a974bc48040ba0819.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces verbal reinforcement learning for language agents, enabling policy optimization through natural language self-reflection rather than weight updates or fine-tuning. The method provides a flexible and interpretable mechanism for incorporating nuanced feedback and episodic memory into LLM-based agents. It claims significant improvements over strong baselines and state-of-the-art results on code generation benchmarks, and introduces a new code-generation RL benchmark (LeetcodeHardGym). The framework is language-agnostic, supports both interpreted and compiled languages, and offers new insights into the role of self-reflection and memory in autonomous agent learning.

067fe55559c4c5a6f39e17ddbfcbb3c9dec93dba.title: Revisiting Ensembling in One-Shot Federated Learning
067fe55559c4c5a6f39e17ddbfcbb3c9dec93dba.research_question: How can federated learning achieve high model accuracy under high data heterogeneity while maintaining low communication costs, particularly in one-shot federated learning scenarios?
067fe55559c4c5a6f39e17ddbfcbb3c9dec93dba.hypothesis: A two-phase federated ensembling scheme that combines one-shot local model training with a lightweight, collaboratively trained aggregator model can approach the accuracy of iterative federated learning while retaining the communication efficiency of one-shot federated learning, especially under high data heterogeneity.
067fe55559c4c5a6f39e17ddbfcbb3c9dec93dba.proposed_method: The proposed method, FENS, consists of two main phases. In the first phase, each client independently trains a local model on its private data and sends the fully trained model to a central server in a single communication round, as in one-shot federated learning. In the second phase, instead of using simple aggregation (e.g., averaging), the server constructs an ensemble by stacking a trainable aggregator model (such as a shallow neural network) atop the locally trained models. This aggregator model is then collaboratively trained among the clients using an iterative federated learning protocol, but only the aggregator's parameters are exchanged, not the full local models. The aggregator learns to combine the predictions of the local models in a data-driven, potentially non-linear manner, effectively correcting for biases and improving ensemble performance. The overall approach leverages the strengths of both one-shot and iterative federated learning, with the aggregator phase being lightweight in terms of communication.
067fe55559c4c5a6f39e17ddbfcbb3c9dec93dba.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, and AG-News, as well as the FLamby healthcare benchmark (Fed-Camelyon16, Fed-Heart-Disease, Fed-ISIC2019) to evaluate performance under varying data heterogeneity. Local data will be partitioned using Dirichlet distributions with different concentration parameters to simulate different levels of non-IID data. Baselines will include state-of-the-art one-shot federated learning methods (e.g., FEDAVG one-shot, FEDENS, FEDKD, FED-ET, FEDCVAE-ENS, Co-Boosting) and iterative federated learning algorithms (e.g., FEDAVG, FEDPROX, FEDNOVA, SCAFFOLD, FEDYOGI, FEDADAM), as well as communication-efficient variants (e.g., FEDAVGSTC). Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy, area under the curve (AUC), balanced accuracy, and total communication cost (measured in GiB). Experiments will also assess the impact of the number of clients, the size of local datasets, and the choice of aggregator model (e.g., averaging, weighted averaging, voting, linear, neural network, mixture-of-experts). Additional studies will explore memory efficiency via quantization and model downsizing, and the feasibility of distilling the ensemble into a single model for inference.
067fe55559c4c5a6f39e17ddbfcbb3c9dec93dba.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a hybrid federated ensembling scheme that, for the first time, leverages a shallow, trainable aggregator model to bridge the accuracy gap between one-shot and iterative federated learning under high data heterogeneity. This approach achieves near-iterative FL accuracy with communication costs close to one-shot FL, outperforming existing one-shot methods by up to 26.9% in accuracy while incurring only a modest increase in communication. The method supports model heterogeneity, enables rapid client unlearning, and can be efficiently distilled for inference. Extensive empirical evaluation across vision, language, and real-world healthcare datasets demonstrates the method's effectiveness and its superior accuracy-communication trade-off compared to both one-shot and iterative baselines.

0681d80cd58b6135534cf279a69f5f999f47ebca.title: L1: Controlling How Long A Reasoning Model Thinks With Reinforcement Learning
0681d80cd58b6135534cf279a69f5f999f47ebca.research_question: How can the reasoning length of language models be precisely controlled to enable fine-grained trade-offs between computational cost and reasoning accuracy across a variety of tasks, including mathematical and general reasoning benchmarks?
0681d80cd58b6135534cf279a69f5f999f47ebca.hypothesis: A reinforcement learning-based approach that directly optimizes for both reasoning accuracy and adherence to user-specified length constraints will enable language models to generate outputs that precisely match desired lengths, resulting in improved efficiency and competitive or superior performance compared to existing length control methods.
0681d80cd58b6135534cf279a69f5f999f47ebca.proposed_method: A reinforcement learning framework, Length Controlled Policy Optimization (LCPO), will be developed to train reasoning language models for precise and adaptive length control. The method will augment each training prompt with a user-specified target length instruction and optimize a reward function that balances answer correctness with adherence to the target output length. Two constraint modes will be explored: LCPO-Exact, which requires the generated reasoning to match the target length exactly, and LCPO-Max, which enforces a soft upper bound on output length. The RL objective will use a correctness indicator and a length penalty, with a trade-off parameter to balance the two. The approach will be implemented using GRPO (Generalized Reinforcement Policy Optimization) and will be compatible with other RL algorithms.
0681d80cd58b6135534cf279a69f5f999f47ebca.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by fine-tuning a 1.5B-parameter reasoning language model (based on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B) on the DeepScaleR-Preview-Dataset, which contains 40K math question-answer pairs from AIME, AMC, Omni-Math, and STILL. Evaluation will be performed on test sets from AIME2025, MATH, AMC, Olympiad-Bench, as well as out-of-domain datasets GPQA, LSAT, and MMLU. Baselines will include DeepSeek-R1-1.5B, DeepScaleR-24K, DeepScaleR-4K, and S1 (a budget-forcing length control method). Metrics will include mean deviation from target length, problem-solving accuracy at various token budgets (512, 1024, 2048, 3600), and budget violation rates. Multiple random seeds and temperature settings will be used to assess robustness, and additional ablation studies will be conducted to evaluate reward function design and scaling to larger models.
0681d80cd58b6135534cf279a69f5f999f47ebca.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first reinforcement learning-based approach for precise and adaptive length control in reasoning language models, enabling outputs to match user-specified length constraints. It claims to achieve state-of-the-art reasoning accuracy under fixed token budgets, outperforming existing length control methods such as S1 by large margins. The approach generalizes robustly to out-of-domain tasks and demonstrates that models trained for long chain-of-thought reasoning can also serve as highly effective short reasoning models, surpassing much larger models like GPT-4o at equivalent generation lengths. The method provides a flexible mechanism for calibrating inference compute, opening new avenues for efficient and scalable reasoning models.

069ca59d23011b9ad18d2e58807ffba6ba2c9f63.title: Physics-Driven Deep Learning for Computational Magnetic Resonance Imaging: Combining physics and machine learning for improved medical imaging
069ca59d23011b9ad18d2e58807ffba6ba2c9f63.research_question: How can the integration of physics-based models and deep learning architectures improve the reconstruction quality and efficiency of computational magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for both linear and non-linear inverse problems?
069ca59d23011b9ad18d2e58807ffba6ba2c9f63.hypothesis: Physics-driven deep learning methods that explicitly incorporate known MRI acquisition physics into neural network architectures or training objectives will yield superior reconstruction accuracy, improved k-space consistency, and better generalization to unseen pathologies compared to purely data-driven or classical model-based approaches.
069ca59d23011b9ad18d2e58807ffba6ba2c9f63.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed that integrates physics-based forward models directly into deep learning architectures for MRI reconstruction. The approach will encompass several strategies: (1) enhancement networks that enforce k-space consistency either as a post-processing step or as a loss term during training; (2) plug-and-play (PnP) methods where deep convolutional neural network (CNN) denoisers are used as proximal operators within iterative optimization schemes; (3) generative models, including Deep Image Prior (DIP) and generative adversarial networks (GANs), where the generator is constrained by the known MRI encoding operator; and (4) unrolled optimization networks that mimic classical iterative solvers but replace regularization steps with learned neural modules. The framework will address both linear (e.g., parallel imaging, compressed sensing) and non-linear (e.g., motion, relaxation mapping) forward models, and will include domain-specific adaptations for real- and complex-valued data and non-Cartesian sampling.
069ca59d23011b9ad18d2e58807ffba6ba2c9f63.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on publicly available and proprietary MRI datasets, covering a range of anatomical regions and acquisition protocols. Datasets will include both linear and non-linear forward models, with various undersampling patterns (Cartesian and non-Cartesian) and acceleration rates. Baseline comparisons will include classical parallel imaging (e.g., SENSE, GRAPPA), compressed sensing, and purely data-driven deep learning methods. Evaluation metrics will comprise quantitative measures such as peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity index (SSIM), and k-space consistency error, as well as qualitative radiologist assessments. Experimental setups will systematically vary the incorporation of physics-driven components to assess their impact on reconstruction fidelity, artifact suppression, and generalization to unseen data.
069ca59d23011b9ad18d2e58807ffba6ba2c9f63.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified framework for physics-driven deep learning in computational MRI that systematically integrates domain knowledge at multiple levels of the reconstruction pipeline. Innovations include the explicit enforcement of k-space consistency within deep learning architectures, the use of deep denoisers as plug-and-play proximal operators, and the adaptation of generative models to MRI inverse problems with both linear and non-linear physics. The approach addresses domain-specific challenges such as handling complex-valued data and non-Cartesian sampling, and aims to bridge the gap between classical model-based and modern data-driven methods for robust and generalizable MRI reconstruction.

06a8f2e3c4266196b008851f1ec7ef9f340809da.title: Advancing Regular Language Reasoning in Linear Recurrent Neural Networks
06a8f2e3c4266196b008851f1ec7ef9f340809da.research_question: Can linear recurrent neural networks (LRNNs) effectively learn and generalize the underlying rules of regular languages, particularly under challenging length extrapolation settings?
06a8f2e3c4266196b008851f1ec7ef9f340809da.hypothesis: Existing LRNN architectures lack sufficient expressiveness to model regular languages, especially for tasks involving arithmetic operations such as subtraction and modular arithmetic. Introducing a block-diagonal and input-dependent transition matrix will enable LRNNs to successfully model and extrapolate regular language rules.
06a8f2e3c4266196b008851f1ec7ef9f340809da.proposed_method: A new LRNN architecture will be developed that incorporates a block-diagonal, input-dependent transition matrix. The transition matrix at each timestep is constructed as a block-diagonal matrix, where each block is a function of the current input, allowing the network to simulate the transition function of a finite state automaton (FSA). To ensure numerical stability and control expressiveness, a p-norm constraint is imposed on the columns of each block, with p chosen close to 1.2. The model will be implemented using a parallel scan (PScan) algorithm to efficiently compute state transitions, enabling fast parallel training and inference while maintaining equivalence with sequential computation. Multiple layers of the proposed LRNN can be stacked to increase modeling capacity for more complex tasks.
06a8f2e3c4266196b008851f1ec7ef9f340809da.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on regular language transduction tasks, specifically Sum(5), EvenPair(5), and ModArith(5), which require the model to perform arithmetic operations and recognize patterns in sequences. The training set will consist of sequences of length 40 (or 39 for ModArith), while extrapolation will be evaluated on much longer sequences (length 500 or 499). Baseline models will include S4, S4D, and Liquid-S4, all of which are established LRNN architectures with varying transition matrix parameterizations. Evaluation metrics will focus on accuracy in the length extrapolation setting, measuring the model's ability to generalize to much longer sequences than seen during training. Computational efficiency will also be assessed by comparing the runtime of the parallel scan implementation against sequential processing.
06a8f2e3c4266196b008851f1ec7ef9f340809da.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a block-diagonal, input-dependent transition matrix for LRNNs, which is theoretically and empirically shown to overcome the expressiveness limitations of prior LRNNs in modeling regular languages. This is the first LRNN architecture capable of successful length extrapolation on challenging regular language tasks such as modular arithmetic. The approach also provides an efficient parallel scan implementation for fast training and inference, while maintaining stability through p-norm constraints. These innovations collectively enable LRNNs to simulate finite state automata and learn complex regular language rules.

06cae16b055c92713bbf7ed5a0067c6c394a88cf.title: Aligning Individual and Collective Objectives in Multi-Agent Cooperation
06cae16b055c92713bbf7ed5a0067c6c394a88cf.research_question: How can individual and collective objectives be effectively aligned in mixed-motive multi-agent cooperation scenarios, particularly in environments where individual and group interests are not fully aligned?
06cae16b055c92713bbf7ed5a0067c6c394a88cf.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a gradient-based optimization method that incorporates both individual and collective objectives can guide agents toward stable fixed points of the collective objective, thereby achieving improved cooperation and fairness without neglecting individual interests.
06cae16b055c92713bbf7ed5a0067c6c394a88cf.proposed_method: A novel optimization framework, termed Altruistic Gradient Adjustment (AgA), will be developed to address the alignment of individual and collective objectives in differentiable mixed-motive games. The approach models mixed-motive multi-agent interactions as differentiable games, where each agent's loss is at least twice differentiable, and both individual and collective gradients are computed. AgA modifies the standard gradient update by introducing an adjustment term: the update direction is given by the sum of the individual gradient and a scaled combination of the collective gradient and its Hessian-vector product. The sign and magnitude of the adjustment parameter are theoretically chosen to ensure that the update pulls the system toward stable fixed points of the collective objective and pushes away from unstable ones. The method is designed for compatibility with centralized training and decentralized execution (CTDE) frameworks, and computational efficiency is maintained by using Hessian-vector products rather than explicit Hessian computation.
06cae16b055c92713bbf7ed5a0067c6c394a88cf.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a spectrum of environments, including the two-player public goods matrix game, sequential social dilemma environments (Cleanup and Harvest) with five homogeneous agents, and a newly developed large-scale mixed-motive environment (Selfish-MMM2) based on the StarCraft II MMM2 map featuring 10 heterogeneous agents and 11 adversaries. Baseline comparisons will include simultaneous individual and collective optimization, consensus gradient adjustment (CGA), symplectic gradient adjustment (SGA), Social Value Orientation (SVO), and the selfishness level (SL) method. Evaluation metrics will include individual and collective rewards, social welfare, equality (Gini-based), and win rate (in Selfish-MMM2). Multiple random seeds and statistical confidence intervals will be used to ensure robustness, and ablation studies will assess the impact of the sign alignment mechanism and parameter choices.
06cae16b055c92713bbf7ed5a0067c6c394a88cf.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first modeling of mixed-motive games as differentiable games for the explicit purpose of analyzing and aligning learning dynamics at both the individual and collective levels. The Altruistic Gradient Adjustment (AgA) algorithm is a novel optimization method that theoretically guarantees alignment toward stable fixed points of the collective objective while accounting for individual interests. Additionally, a new large-scale mixed-motive environment (Selfish-MMM2) is introduced, enabling the study of cooperation in complex, high-dimensional, and heterogeneous agent settings. The approach is claimed to outperform existing baselines in both cooperation and fairness, and to provide a theoretically grounded and computationally efficient alternative to hand-crafted or purely reward-shaping methods.

06cfecfb904bb9d813ef9f1040ef784cdf151a54.title: Partitioned Variational Inference: A Framework for Probabilistic Federated Learning
06cfecfb904bb9d813ef9f1040ef784cdf151a54.research_question: How can variational inference be generalized and adapted to the federated learning setting to enable probabilistic modeling and uncertainty quantification while respecting data privacy and decentralization constraints?
06cfecfb904bb9d813ef9f1040ef784cdf151a54.hypothesis: Partitioned variational inference (PVI) enables effective and principled probabilistic inference in federated learning environments, achieving global variational inference solutions while accommodating data heterogeneity, communication constraints, and privacy requirements.
06cfecfb904bb9d813ef9f1040ef784cdf151a54.proposed_method: A framework called partitioned variational inference (PVI) will be developed to extend variational inference (VI) to the federated learning setting. The method decomposes the global variational objective into a series of local free-energy optimization problems, each solved by an individual client using only its local data. The approximate posterior is represented as a product of the prior and client-specific approximate likelihoods, which are iteratively refined through local optimization and coordinated updates. Three variants of PVI will be implemented: sequential (one client updates at a time), synchronous (all clients update in parallel), and asynchronous (clients update as they become available), each with specific communication and convergence properties. Damping and normalization strategies will be incorporated to ensure stability and proper probabilistic interpretation, especially in the presence of inhomogeneous data partitions and unreliable communication.
06cfecfb904bb9d813ef9f1040ef784cdf151a54.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on federated learning benchmarks, including logistic regression models and Bayesian neural networks, with datasets partitioned across clients to simulate varying degrees and forms of data heterogeneity. The PVI framework will be evaluated against existing federated and distributed inference methods, such as expectation propagation, global and local VI, and Bayesian committee machines. Evaluation metrics will include the accuracy of posterior approximation, predictive performance, robustness to data partitioning, and communication efficiency. Both homogeneous and highly inhomogeneous data splits will be considered, and the impact of different PVI variants and damping strategies will be systematically analyzed.
06cfecfb904bb9d813ef9f1040ef784cdf151a54.novelty_claims: The proposed framework unifies and generalizes a broad spectrum of existing variational inference methods under a single federated paradigm, providing new theoretical insights and practical algorithms for probabilistic federated learning. PVI enables principled uncertainty quantification in decentralized settings, supports flexible communication protocols, and offers provable connections to global variational inference solutions. The approach addresses key limitations of prior methods, such as lack of uncertainty estimation and inefficiency in heterogeneous or unreliable environments, and introduces new strategies for stable and efficient distributed inference.

06d79953e85f7981f8a2cabad2165ca739af35af.title: AdaptiGraph: Material-Adaptive Graph-Based Neural Dynamics for Robotic Manipulation
06d79953e85f7981f8a2cabad2165ca739af35af.research_question: How can a unified predictive model be developed to enable robots to accurately manipulate and adapt to a wide variety of objects made from different materials with unknown and varying physical properties?
06d79953e85f7981f8a2cabad2165ca739af35af.hypothesis: A graph-based neural dynamics model conditioned on both material type and continuous physical property variables, combined with an online few-shot adaptation mechanism, will enable accurate prediction and manipulation of diverse objects with unknown physical properties, outperforming non-adaptive and non-parameterized baselines.
06d79953e85f7981f8a2cabad2165ca739af35af.proposed_method: A material-adaptive graph-based neural dynamics framework will be developed, in which objects are represented as particles within a graph structure. Each particle node is encoded with both discrete material type and continuous physical property variables (such as stiffness, granularity, or center of pressure), which are propagated and updated during model training. A graph neural network (GNN) will serve as the core dynamics predictor, taking as input the current state, action, material type, and physical property variables to predict the next state. At deployment, an online few-shot adaptation procedure will be used: the robot will interact with previously unseen objects, observe their responses, and estimate their physical properties by minimizing the prediction error (e.g., Chamfer Distance) between predicted and observed states via inverse optimization. The adapted model will then be used for closed-loop model-based planning in downstream manipulation tasks.
06d79953e85f7981f8a2cabad2165ca739af35af.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four categories of objects: rigid boxes, ropes, granular piles, and cloths, each with varying physical properties (e.g., stiffness, granularity, center of pressure). Datasets will be generated in simulation (using NVIDIA FleX and Pymunk) with randomized object properties and robot interactions, and real-world evaluations will be performed using a 6-DoF robot arm equipped with specialized end effectors and multiple RGB-D cameras. Baselines will include a GNN without physical property conditioning (trained per material) and an ablated version of the proposed model without online adaptation. Evaluation metrics will include forward dynamics prediction error (e.g., mean squared error, Chamfer Distance), physical property estimation accuracy, and task success rates in closed-loop planning. Both qualitative and quantitative comparisons will be made across all material types and tasks.
06d79953e85f7981f8a2cabad2165ca739af35af.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a unified, material- and property-conditioned graph-based neural dynamics model capable of generalizing across diverse materials and intra-class physical property variations without retraining. The integration of a few-shot online adaptation mechanism enables real-time estimation of unknown physical properties through robot-object interaction, providing interpretable and consistent parameter estimates. This approach allows for accurate dynamics prediction and efficient model-based planning for objects with out-of-distribution or extreme physical properties, surpassing prior methods limited to single materials or requiring extensive retraining.

0707f0bd29ba2cc787820f7f6b3b911f00257845.title: Universal approximation property of Banach space-valued random feature models including random neural networks
0707f0bd29ba2cc787820f7f6b3b911f00257845.research_question: Can random feature models, extended to Banach space-valued settings, provide universal approximation capabilities for learning elements in general function spaces, including infinite-dimensional and non-compact domains, and what are the associated approximation rates and computational complexities?
0707f0bd29ba2cc787820f7f6b3b911f00257845.hypothesis: Banach space-valued random feature models, including random neural networks with randomly initialized weights and biases and only trained linear readouts, possess the universal approximation property in a wide class of function spaces, and their approximation error and computational cost can be quantitatively characterized.
0707f0bd29ba2cc787820f7f6b3b911f00257845.proposed_method: A Banach space-valued extension of random feature learning will be developed, where the feature maps are randomly initialized and only the linear readout is trained. The method will treat random feature models as Banach space-valued random variables, leveraging the strong law of large numbers in Bochner spaces to establish universal approximation properties. The framework will encompass random trigonometric/Fourier regression and random neural networks, with the latter constructed as single-hidden-layer feedforward networks with random inner parameters and trained linear output layers. Explicit algorithms will be derived for learning elements in Banach spaces, and the approach will be generalized to function spaces such as weighted Lp and Sobolev spaces, including the approximation of weak derivatives.
0707f0bd29ba2cc787820f7f6b3b911f00257845.experiment_details: Experiments will include both theoretical and empirical components. Theoretical analysis will establish universal approximation theorems and derive explicit approximation rates, relating the number of features to the tolerated error and the input/output dimensions. Empirical validation will be conducted via numerical examples, such as learning solutions to the heat equation, comparing the performance of random feature models to deterministic counterparts. Datasets will include synthetic or standard PDE benchmarks, and evaluation metrics will comprise approximation error (in relevant Banach space norms), generalization error, and computational cost (number of features/neurons required). Baselines will include deterministic neural networks and kernel methods.
0707f0bd29ba2cc787820f7f6b3b911f00257845.novelty_claims: The proposed framework generalizes random feature models to Banach space-valued settings, enabling learning of infinite-dimensional objects and extending universal approximation results to non-compact domains and broader function spaces. It provides explicit approximation rates and computational complexity bounds, including cases where random neural networks overcome the curse of dimensionality. The approach unifies and extends prior results for random trigonometric/Fourier features and random neural networks, and demonstrates empirical advantages over deterministic models.

0733b0b90a17e84acc927b4f81f851a7bd106ff7.title: Have We Learned to Explain?: How Interpretability Methods Can Learn to Encode Predictions in their Interpretations
0733b0b90a17e84acc927b4f81f851a7bd106ff7.research_question: How can interpretability methods for machine learning be quantitatively evaluated to ensure that their explanations faithfully reflect the true data-generating process, and how can new explanation methods be developed to avoid encoding predictions or omitting critical control flow features in their interpretations?
0733b0b90a17e84acc927b4f81f851a7bd106ff7.hypothesis: Amortized explanation methods that decouple the learning of feature selector and predictor models, and that are evaluated using a model trained to approximate the true conditional distribution of the target given feature subsets, will yield more faithful and high-fidelity explanations that do not encode predictions or omit control flow features, compared to existing joint amortized methods.
0733b0b90a17e84acc927b4f81f851a7bd106ff7.proposed_method: A novel evaluation framework, EVAL-X, will be developed to quantitatively assess the fidelity of instance-wise feature selection explanations by learning an evaluator model that approximates the true conditional distribution of the target given any subset of input features. This evaluator will be trained using random feature masks to ensure it generalizes to arbitrary feature subsets and avoids out-of-distribution issues. Building on this, a new amortized explanation method, REAL-X, will be proposed, which learns a global selector model to identify minimal subsets of important features for each instance. The predictor model in REAL-X will be trained independently from the selector, ensuring that predictions cannot be encoded in the selection mask. The selector is optimized to maximize the likelihood of the data under the evaluator's estimated conditional distribution, with regularization to encourage sparsity in feature selection. REBAR gradients or similar low-variance estimators will be employed to optimize over discrete feature selections.
0733b0b90a17e84acc927b4f81f851a7bd106ff7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic datasets with known generative processes and control flow features, the MNIST handwritten digit dataset, and a real-world chest X-ray dataset for cardiomegaly detection. For each dataset, the proposed REAL-X method will be compared against established joint amortized methods (L2X, INVASE) and a baseline (BASE-X) that mimics the optimization of REAL-X but without its decoupling. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy (ACC), area under the ROC curve (AUROC), true positive rate (TPR), false discovery rate (FDR), and control flow feature selection rate (CFSR). Critically, explanations will be evaluated both by standard post-hoc predictive performance and by EVAL-X, which measures how well selected features alone predict the target under the evaluator model. For the chest X-ray data, expert radiologists will rank the quality of explanations to assess clinical relevance. Hyperparameters controlling the number of features selected will be tuned to balance interpretability and predictive performance, with models selected to retain high accuracy while minimizing feature subset size.
0733b0b90a17e84acc927b4f81f851a7bd106ff7.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces EVAL-X, a new quantitative evaluation procedure for interpretability methods that addresses the problem of out-of-distribution masking and detects when explanations encode predictions. REAL-X is presented as a novel amortized explanation method that avoids the pitfalls of joint training by decoupling the predictor and selector models, ensuring explanations do not encode predictions or omit control flow features. The approach is claimed to yield higher-fidelity, more faithful, and clinically meaningful explanations, as demonstrated by both quantitative metrics and expert evaluation. The methodology also generalizes to different data modalities and can be extended to various forms of feature attribution.

073b30f4604c0869231eea08b776f02414b19fce.title: TensoIR: Tensorial Inverse Rendering
073b30f4604c0869231eea08b776f02414b19fce.research_question: How can inverse rendering from multi-view images under unknown lighting conditions be made more accurate and efficient, enabling high-quality reconstruction of scene geometry, materials, and illumination for applications such as novel view synthesis and relighting?
073b30f4604c0869231eea08b776f02414b19fce.hypothesis: A tensor factorization-based scene representation, combined with neural fields and joint optimization of radiance field and physically-based rendering models, will enable more accurate and efficient inverse rendering than existing MLP-based neural field methods, particularly in modeling secondary shading effects and supporting multi-light conditions.
073b30f4604c0869231eea08b776f02414b19fce.proposed_method: A novel inverse rendering framework is developed that extends tensor factorization-based radiance field representations to jointly estimate scene geometry, surface reflectance (BRDF parameters), and environment illumination from multi-view images captured under unknown lighting. The method models the scene as a neural voxel feature grid, factorized into low-rank tensor components, and applies multiple lightweight MLPs to regress volume density, view-dependent color, normals, and material properties. Both radiance field rendering (for view synthesis) and physically-based rendering (for inverse rendering) are performed, with joint supervision from captured images. The approach enables explicit and efficient computation of visibility and indirect illumination via online second-bounce ray marching, leveraging the efficiency of the tensor representation. Furthermore, an additional lighting dimension is incorporated into the tensor factorization, allowing the method to handle multi-light input efficiently and exploit photometric cues across varying lighting conditions.
073b30f4604c0869231eea08b776f02414b19fce.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on several challenging synthetic and real-world datasets, including three Blender scenes and one from the Stanford 3D Scanning Repository, with ground-truth images, BRDF parameters, and normal maps. Both single-light and multi-light settings are evaluated, with multi-light data rendered in rotated and general configurations. The method is compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as NeRFactor and InvRender, using evaluation metrics including MAE for normals, PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS for albedo, novel view synthesis, and relighting. Reconstruction speed is also measured, with the proposed approach achieving high-quality results in significantly less time than baselines. Ablation studies assess the impact of indirect illumination and visibility modeling. Additional regularization terms are applied to normals, BRDF parameters, and tensor factors to ensure robust optimization.
073b30f4604c0869231eea08b776f02414b19fce.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a tensor factorization-based inverse rendering framework that jointly reconstructs radiance fields and physically-based scene models, enabling efficient and accurate modeling of secondary shading effects such as shadows and indirect lighting. The method supports multi-light input by extending the tensor representation with an additional lighting dimension, allowing for efficient and scalable reconstruction under arbitrary lighting conditions. Explicit online computation of visibility and indirect illumination is achieved without the need for costly pre-computation or auxiliary MLPs, resulting in state-of-the-art reconstruction quality and significantly faster optimization compared to previous neural field-based methods.

073fd972ead074b9898ecb443670edc233f78cec.title: Improving Ensemble Distillation With Weight Averaging and Diversifying Perturbation
073fd972ead074b9898ecb443670edc233f78cec.research_question: How can ensemble distillation be improved to produce a single student network that matches or exceeds the predictive accuracy and uncertainty calibration of deep ensembles, while maintaining low inference cost and effectively transferring the diversity of teacher ensembles?
073fd972ead074b9898ecb443670edc233f78cec.hypothesis: A student network trained with multiple subnetworks and weight averaging, combined with a perturbation strategy that considers both student and teacher diversity, will more effectively absorb ensemble teacher diversity and achieve superior predictive accuracy and uncertainty calibration compared to existing ensemble distillation methods, without increasing inference cost.
073fd972ead074b9898ecb443670edc233f78cec.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a novel ensemble distillation framework, termed LatentBE, in which a student network is trained with multiple subnetworks differentiated by rank-one factors, as in BatchEnsemble. During training, each subnetwork is guided to mimic a corresponding teacher in a one-to-one fashion, with all subnetworks sharing most parameters but maintaining individual low-rank factors. After training, the rank-one factors are averaged to produce a single student network for inference, ensuring no additional inference cost. To further enhance diversity transfer, a new input perturbation strategy is developed that seeks input directions maximizing the diversity among teacher outputs while minimizing diversity among student subnetworks, computed via pairwise KL-divergence. This perturbation is applied during training to focus learning on examples where student diversity lags behind teacher diversity, thus improving the transfer of ensemble diversity.
073fd972ead074b9898ecb443670edc233f78cec.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification benchmarks including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, and ImageNet-1k, using architectures such as WideResNet and ResNet. The proposed LatentBE method will be compared against baselines including standard knowledge distillation (KD), adaptive ensemble KD, Proxy-EnD2, and BatchEnsemble-based distillation methods. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy, negative log-likelihood (NLL), expected calibration error (ECE), and their calibrated variants, as well as robustness to common corruptions and out-of-distribution detection via predictive entropy. Both training and inference runtimes will be measured to assess computational efficiency. Experiments will also include ablation studies on the effect of the proposed perturbation strategy and the impact of the number of teacher models.
073fd972ead074b9898ecb443670edc233f78cec.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new ensemble distillation framework that leverages weight averaging of rank-one factors to produce a single student network with no additional inference cost, while retaining the benefits of ensemble diversity. Additionally, a novel perturbation strategy is proposed that explicitly considers both teacher and student diversity, enabling more effective diversity transfer during distillation. The combination of these techniques is claimed to yield state-of-the-art performance in both predictive accuracy and uncertainty calibration, outperforming existing ensemble distillation methods, especially in resource-constrained settings.

076f35d58d26ac74c71e6e849dfffc0707aa8a6f.title: AHA: A Vision-Language-Model for Detecting and Reasoning Over Failures in Robotic Manipulation
076f35d58d26ac74c71e6e849dfffc0707aa8a6f.research_question: How can vision-language models be developed to autonomously detect and reason over failures in robotic manipulation tasks, providing detailed and adaptable natural language explanations across diverse robots, tasks, and environments?
076f35d58d26ac74c71e6e849dfffc0707aa8a6f.hypothesis: A vision-language model, instruction-tuned on a large-scale, procedurally generated dataset of robotic manipulation failures, will outperform existing state-of-the-art models in both failure detection and reasoning, and will enhance downstream robotic applications by providing detailed failure feedback.
076f35d58d26ac74c71e6e849dfffc0707aa8a6f.proposed_method: A novel vision-language model (VLM) will be developed and instruction-tuned to detect and reason about failures in robotic manipulation. The methodology involves the creation of a scalable data generation pipeline, FailGen, which procedurally perturbs successful robotic task demonstrations in simulation to synthesize diverse failure trajectories based on a formalized taxonomy of failure modes. The resulting AHA dataset, comprising over 49,000 image-query pairs across 79 tasks, will be used for instruction-tuning the VLM. The model architecture will include a pre-trained image encoder, a linear projection layer, and a transformer-based language model, where only the projector and transformer are fine-tuned. The model will be prompted with temporally and viewpoint-concatenated images and sub-task descriptions, predicting binary task success and generating free-form natural language explanations for failures.
076f35d58d26ac74c71e6e849dfffc0707aa8a6f.experiment_details: Experiments will benchmark the proposed VLM against six state-of-the-art open-source and proprietary VLMs, including models such as GPT-4o and LLaVA, across three diverse evaluation datasets: the AHA test set (11k image-question pairs from RLBench tasks), ManiSkill-Fail (130 pairs from ManiSkill simulator), and RoboFail (real-world robot failures). Evaluation metrics will include ROUGE-L, Cosine Similarity, LLM Fuzzy Match (using an external LLM), and Binary Success Rate. Additional experiments will assess generalization to out-of-domain tasks, unseen environments, and real-world embodiments. Downstream integration will be tested in reinforcement learning (reward synthesis), task and motion planning, and zero-shot trajectory generation, comparing task success rates and qualitative feedback improvements against GPT-4o baselines.
076f35d58d26ac74c71e6e849dfffc0707aa8a6f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first open-source VLM specifically designed for free-form failure detection and reasoning in robotic manipulation, moving beyond binary classification to detailed natural language explanations. The FailGen pipeline enables scalable, procedural generation of large-scale failure datasets across multiple simulators and tasks, supporting robust instruction-tuning. The method demonstrates superior generalization to unseen domains, tasks, and real-world settings, and provides actionable failure feedback that significantly improves downstream robotic application performance. Integration into reinforcement learning, planning, and verification pipelines shows measurable improvements in task success rates over leading commercial models.

07745b1f400dbeec0fb4646a80091837a4b36a2b.title: OMLT: Optimization & Machine Learning Toolkit
07745b1f400dbeec0fb4646a80091837a4b36a2b.research_question: How can trained machine learning models, such as neural networks and gradient-boosted trees, be efficiently and flexibly integrated into larger mathematical optimization problems to enable advanced decision-making in computer science and engineering applications?
07745b1f400dbeec0fb4646a80091837a4b36a2b.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a general-purpose toolkit can be developed to automate the transformation of trained machine learning models into optimization-ready formulations, thereby streamlining the integration process and enabling seamless experimentation with alternative optimization formulations.
07745b1f400dbeec0fb4646a80091837a4b36a2b.proposed_method: A comprehensive open-source toolkit will be developed that accepts high-level representations of trained neural networks and gradient-boosted trees, primarily through ONNX and Keras interfaces. The toolkit will automatically translate these models into algebraic optimization formulations compatible with the Pyomo modeling language, leveraging Pyomo blocks to encapsulate surrogate models as components within larger optimization problems. Multiple mathematical formulations, including both full-space and reduced-space approaches for smooth and non-smooth activation functions, will be implemented, allowing users to switch between formulations such as big-M, complementarity, and partition-based methods for ReLU networks. The system will support variable scaling, bound specification, and flexible linking of surrogate model inputs/outputs to user-defined optimization variables and constraints.
07745b1f400dbeec0fb4646a80091837a4b36a2b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of decision-making and verification tasks, including neural network verification on the MNIST dataset using both dense and convolutional architectures, and engineering optimization problems such as process design with surrogate models derived from process simulation data (e.g., using IDAES-PSE). The toolkit's performance will be benchmarked against existing specialized tools and alternative optimization formulations, with comparisons made in terms of formulation size (number of constraints), ease of use, and solution quality. Evaluation metrics will include computational efficiency, formulation flexibility, and the ability to address problems not solvable by dedicated verification tools. Baselines will include existing libraries such as MeLOn, JANOS, reluMIP, OptiCL, and direct solver interfaces.
07745b1f400dbeec0fb4646a80091837a4b36a2b.novelty_claims: The proposed toolkit offers a unified and extensible framework for embedding both neural networks and gradient-boosted trees into mathematical optimization problems, supporting a wide variety of input model formats and activation functions. Unlike prior tools, it enables seamless switching between competing optimization formulations and supports both dense and convolutional neural network layers. The block-based abstraction in Pyomo simplifies integration and experimentation, making it possible to compare and develop new formulations with minimal user effort. The toolkit generalizes and extends the capabilities of existing solutions by automating the translation of machine learning surrogates into optimization-ready components, thus broadening the applicability of optimization-based decision-making with machine learning models.

07756bd662565b61a04fc2dfca7d6f5236b24326.title: 4Real-Video-V2: Fused View-Time Attention and Feedforward Reconstruction for 4D Scene Generation
07756bd662565b61a04fc2dfca7d6f5236b24326.research_question: How can high-quality, consistent, and efficient 4D scene generation be achieved from text prompts, enabling synchronized multi-view video outputs and explicit 4D representations suitable for dynamic and complex scenes?
07756bd662565b61a04fc2dfca7d6f5236b24326.hypothesis: A parameter-efficient, fused view-time attention mechanism within a large-scale video diffusion model, combined with a feedforward reconstruction network, will enable state-of-the-art 4D scene generation in terms of visual quality, consistency, and reconstruction accuracy, outperforming existing sequential and parallel attention architectures.
07756bd662565b61a04fc2dfca7d6f5236b24326.proposed_method: A two-stage framework is developed for 4D scene generation. In the first stage, a novel 4D video diffusion model is constructed based on a large-scale Diffusion Transformer (DiT) backbone. This model fuses cross-view and cross-time attention into a single masked self-attention layer, enabling each latent token to attend to others sharing either the same view or timestamp. The attention mask is implemented efficiently using sparse attention techniques, and 4D positional embeddings are mapped to 3D to maintain compatibility with pretrained video models. The model is conditioned on reference videos (fixed-view and freeze-time) and trained using a rectified flow objective, with only self-attention layers fine-tuned. In the second stage, a feedforward reconstruction network extends a pretrained transformer-based model (VGGT) to predict both camera parameters and time-varying Gaussian splats from the generated multi-view video frames. This network incorporates temporal attention, camera token replacement for temporal consistency, and a Gaussian head to predict ellipsoid parameters, all trained with a reconstruction loss combining MSE and perceptual metrics.
07756bd662565b61a04fc2dfca7d6f5236b24326.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a combination of synthetic and real-world datasets, including Objaverse (animated 3D assets), the NVIDIA Dynamic Dataset (real-world multi-view videos), and generated videos using Veo2. The model is compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as TrajectoryCrafter, ReCamMaster (two variants), SynCamMaster, 4Real-Video, and SV4D. Evaluation metrics include PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS for reconstruction quality, Met3R for multi-view consistency, and VBench metrics for video quality. The training set comprises synthetic 4D data, 2D-transformed videos, and static scene videos, with ablation studies performed to assess the impact of training data and architectural components. The feedforward reconstruction model is evaluated on both static (Tanks&Temples, LLFF) and dynamic (Neural3DVideo, dynamic Kubric) datasets, compared to GSLRM, BTimer, and Splatt3r, using standard novel view synthesis metrics.
07756bd662565b61a04fc2dfca7d6f5236b24326.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first parameter-efficient fused view-time attention mechanism for 4D video diffusion, eliminating the need for additional parameters or synchronization modules and enabling effective fine-tuning of large pretrained video models. The framework supports conditioning on reference videos without explicit camera pose embeddings, improving usability for 3D animation tasks. The feedforward reconstruction model is the first to jointly predict camera parameters and dynamic Gaussian splats from synchronized multi-view videos, incorporating temporal attention and camera token replacement for temporal consistency. The overall system achieves state-of-the-art results in 4D scene generation, multi-view consistency, and reconstruction accuracy, outperforming prior sequential and parallel attention architectures and existing feedforward reconstruction methods.

077c4f979ac6a369318c59ff8c5df8d6f681d8b5.title: Temporal Dependencies in Feature Importance for Time Series Predictions
077c4f979ac6a369318c59ff8c5df8d6f681d8b5.research_question: How can feature importance in time series prediction models be more accurately and robustly explained, particularly accounting for temporal dependencies and the varying importance of features over time?
077c4f979ac6a369318c59ff8c5df8d6f681d8b5.hypothesis: A feature removal-based explainability method that explicitly models temporal dependencies and aggregates feature importance over a window of time steps will provide more accurate, robust, and interpretable explanations for time series prediction models compared to existing explainability techniques.
077c4f979ac6a369318c59ff8c5df8d6f681d8b5.proposed_method: A new explainability framework, Windowed Feature Importance in Time (WinIT), will be developed to address the temporal dependencies inherent in time series data. The method will assign importance to each feature observation by quantifying its impact on model predictions over a specified window of subsequent time steps, rather than treating each observation as independent. Importance will be computed as the difference in prediction outcomes when a feature is removed over intervals [a, b] and [a+1, b], capturing delayed and distributed effects.
