Feature removal will be implemented using a conditional generative model, which generates plausible counterfactuals for masked features based on past observations, ensuring realistic imputations. The final importance score for each feature at each time step will be aggregated over the window, providing a temporally-aware and granular explanation of feature contributions.
077c4f979ac6a369318c59ff8c5df8d6f681d8b5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world time series datasets. Synthetic datasets, including Spike, Delayed Spike, and State (based on NARMA processes and Hidden Markov Models), will be used to provide ground truth for feature importance and to evaluate the method's ability to capture shifted and delayed dependencies. The MIMIC-III clinical dataset will serve as a real-world benchmark for mortality prediction tasks. Baselines will include gradient-based methods (DeepLIFT, DeepSHAP, Integrated Gradients), feature occlusion methods (FO, AFO), Feature Importance in Time (FIT), and Dynamask. Evaluation metrics will include Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve (AUPRC), mean rank of ground truth important features, AUC drop, and average prediction change after masking important features. Multiple masking strategies (END, STD, STD-BAL) will be systematically compared to assess robustness and bias in evaluation. All experiments will use GRU-based models for both prediction and generative counterfactuals, with hyperparameters and training procedures standardized for fair comparison.
077c4f979ac6a369318c59ff8c5df8d6f681d8b5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel feature removal-based explainability method that explicitly accounts for temporal dependencies in time series data, allowing for the attribution of feature importance across a window of future predictions. Unlike prior methods, WinIT aggregates the impact of each observation over multiple time steps, capturing delayed and distributed effects. The use of a generative model for counterfactual feature removal ensures realistic imputations and avoids out-of-distribution artifacts. Additionally, the proposal includes a comprehensive evaluation framework with multiple masking strategies to provide a more robust and unbiased assessment of explainability methods in time series settings.

07955e96cbd778d0ae2a68f09d073b866dd84c2a.title: Decomposed Prompting: A Modular Approach for Solving Complex Tasks
07955e96cbd778d0ae2a68f09d073b866dd84c2a.research_question: How can complex tasks be more effectively solved using large language models (LLMs) when few-shot prompting struggles with increased task complexity or hard-to-learn reasoning steps?
07955e96cbd778d0ae2a68f09d073b866dd84c2a.hypothesis: Decomposing complex tasks into simpler sub-tasks, each handled by dedicated prompting-based LLMs or symbolic functions, will improve the accuracy, generalization, and modularity of solutions compared to standard few-shot or chain-of-thought prompting.
07955e96cbd778d0ae2a68f09d073b866dd84c2a.proposed_method: A modular framework, termed Decomposed Prompting (DECOMP), is developed to address complex tasks by decomposing them into a sequence of simpler sub-tasks. A decomposer LLM generates a prompting program that specifies the order and nature of sub-queries, each delegated to a sub-task handler. Sub-task handlers may be prompting-based LLMs with their own few-shot prompts, further decomposed prompts, or symbolic functions such as external APIs. The system supports hierarchical and recursive decomposition, enabling sub-tasks to be further broken down or handled by reusable modules. An imperative controller orchestrates the execution, passing intermediate results between the decomposer and sub-task handlers until the final answer is produced.
07955e96cbd778d0ae2a68f09d073b866dd84c2a.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on eight challenging datasets, including symbolic reasoning tasks (e.g., kth letter concatenation, list reversal), long-context multi-hop QA (CommaQA-E), and open-domain multi-hop QA (2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, HotpotQA). Baselines include standard chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting, least-to-most prompting, and strong retrieval-based systems. Evaluation metrics include Exact Match (EM) and F1 score, with model variants such as GPT-3 (text-davinci-002, code-davinci-002) and Flan-T5 (Large, XL, XXL) used for both decomposition and sub-task handling. Experimental setups include testing generalization to longer input sequences, new delimiters, and compositional splits, as well as ablation studies on prompt granularity and post-processing for error correction.
07955e96cbd778d0ae2a68f09d073b866dd84c2a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a modular, decomposable prompting paradigm that allows each sub-task to be independently optimized, further decomposed, or replaced with symbolic or learned functions. This framework enables hierarchical and recursive decomposition, supports integration of external APIs, and facilitates targeted error correction. The method claims improved performance and generalization over existing few-shot and chain-of-thought prompting techniques, especially on tasks with increased complexity, longer input contexts, or knowledge-intensive requirements.

07975b0df907e775908cec198cade7ff2a6154c5.title: Rethinking Confidence Calibration for Failure Prediction
07975b0df907e775908cec198cade7ff2a6154c5.research_question: How can the reliability of confidence estimates in deep neural networks be improved for failure prediction in safety-critical applications, and what factors or training strategies contribute to better separability between correct and incorrect predictions?
07975b0df907e775908cec198cade7ff2a6154c5.hypothesis: Flat minima in the loss landscape of deep neural networks are beneficial for failure prediction by enhancing the separability of confidence scores between correct and incorrect predictions.
07975b0df907e775908cec198cade7ff2a6154c5.proposed_method: A new approach will be developed that leverages the connection between flat minima and confidence separation to improve failure prediction. The method will involve training deep neural networks with techniques specifically designed to find and maintain flat minima in the loss landscape. This may include the use of explicit regularization strategies, such as sharpness-aware minimization or stochastic weight averaging, and the combination of multiple flatness-inducing techniques. The training procedure will be carefully designed to preserve high confidence for correct predictions while reducing confidence for misclassified samples, thereby increasing the margin between them. The resulting models are expected to yield confidence distributions that are more robust and better separated for the purpose of failure prediction.
07975b0df907e775908cec198cade7ff2a6154c5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification benchmarks such as CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet, using a variety of deep neural network architectures including ResNet110, WideResNet, DenseNet, ConvMixer, and ResNet-18. The evaluation will focus on failure prediction metrics including AURC, E-AURC, AUROC, FPR-95%TPR, AUPR-Success, and AUPR-Error. The proposed method will be compared against established baselines and popular confidence calibration techniques such as mixup, label smoothing, focal loss, CS-KD, L1 regularization, and temperature scaling. Each experiment will be repeated multiple times to report mean and standard deviation, and standard training protocols (SGD with momentum, learning rate schedules, weight decay, and validation splits) will be followed for reproducibility.
07975b0df907e775908cec198cade7ff2a6154c5.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel perspective by identifying and addressing the negative impact of popular confidence calibration methods on failure prediction, which has been largely overlooked in the literature. By hypothesizing and empirically validating the beneficial role of flat minima for confidence separability, the approach offers a principled and effective strategy for improving failure prediction in deep neural networks. The combination of multiple flatness-inducing techniques to directly target confidence separation represents an innovative contribution to the field of trustworthy AI and selective classification.

079be8c8a93fc80274ff22251a3dac9804bec66a.title: RTLLM: An Open-Source Benchmark for Design RTL Generation with Large Language Model
079be8c8a93fc80274ff22251a3dac9804bec66a.research_question: How can the evaluation and benchmarking of large language models (LLMs) for automatic RTL (Register Transfer Level) hardware design generation from natural language instructions be systematically advanced, particularly in terms of design complexity, scale, and design quality?
079be8c8a93fc80274ff22251a3dac9804bec66a.hypothesis: A comprehensive, open-source benchmark with diverse and complex RTL design tasks, combined with a structured evaluation protocol and advanced prompt engineering techniques, will enable more rigorous, fair, and informative assessment of LLM-based RTL generation solutions, and will facilitate measurable improvements in both correctness and design quality.
079be8c8a93fc80274ff22251a3dac9804bec66a.proposed_method: A new open-source benchmark, RTLLM, will be developed to evaluate LLMs on the task of generating RTL code from natural language descriptions. The benchmark will consist of 30 diverse digital hardware designs, spanning a wide range of complexities and scales, each accompanied by a standardized natural language description, a comprehensive testbench, and a human-crafted reference RTL implementation. The evaluation framework will define three progressive goals: syntax correctness (successful synthesis), functionality correctness (passing all testbench cases), and design quality (measured by PPA: power, performance, area). To further enhance LLM performance, a novel prompt engineering technique called self-planning will be introduced, which decomposes the code generation process into a planning step (reasoning and error-avoidance advice) followed by code synthesis, all without human intervention. The entire evaluation process, including synthesis and simulation, will be automated to ensure reproducibility and fairness.
079be8c8a93fc80274ff22251a3dac9804bec66a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using five LLM-based solutions: GPT-3.5, GPT-4.0, an academic fine-tuned CodeGen model, StarCoder, and versions of GPT-3.5 and GPT-4.0 augmented with the self-planning prompt technique. Each model will be tasked with generating RTL for all 30 benchmark designs, with five independent runs per design to account for stochasticity. The generated RTL will be evaluated for syntax correctness (synthesizability), functionality (testbench pass rate), and design quality (PPA metrics) using Synopsys Design Compiler and VCS tools. Baseline comparisons will include human-crafted reference designs and prior academic datasets. The evaluation will report both aggregate success rates and detailed per-design results.
079be8c8a93fc80274ff22251a3dac9804bec66a.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark, RTLLM, is the first open-source, large-scale, and systematically diverse dataset for evaluating LLM-based RTL generation, supporting multiple HDL formats and providing automated, multi-level evaluation metrics. The benchmark covers significantly more and larger designs than previous datasets, enabling more rigorous and scalable assessment. The self-planning prompt engineering technique is introduced as a novel, automated method to substantially improve LLM performance in code generation tasks, reducing syntax and functionality errors without human intervention. The framework enables fair, reproducible, and quantitative comparison of both commercial and academic LLMs on realistic hardware design tasks.

079f720a2d66074f1c83dd2c2c90d7b5aad8448c.title: Context-Based Trit-Plane Coding for Progressive Image Compression
079f720a2d66074f1c83dd2c2c90d7b5aad8448c.research_question: How can progressive image compression be improved to achieve better rate-distortion performance, fine-grained scalability, and efficient context modeling, while maintaining low computational complexity?
079f720a2d66074f1c83dd2c2c90d7b5aad8448c.hypothesis: Integrating context-based rate reduction and distortion reduction modules into a trit-plane coding framework, along with a decoder retraining scheme, will significantly improve the rate-distortion performance of progressive image compression compared to existing methods, while incurring only marginal increases in computational complexity.
079f720a2d66074f1c83dd2c2c90d7b5aad8448c.proposed_method: A novel progressive image compression framework is developed based on trit-plane coding, which decomposes quantized latent tensors into multiple trit-planes for fine-grained scalable compression. The method introduces two key context modules: a context-based rate reduction (CRR) module and a context-based distortion reduction (CDR) module. CRR exploits already decoded information, including previously reconstructed latent tensors, entropy parameters, and expected latent values, to refine trit probability estimates and reduce entropy before entropy encoding. CDR operates after entropy decoding, using entropy parameters and the partially reconstructed latent tensor to regress and correct quantization errors, thereby improving the quality of reconstructed images. Additionally, a decoder retraining scheme is proposed, where the decoder is retrained using the refined latent tensors from CDR to further enhance reconstruction quality across all progressive stages. All modules are implemented using convolutional neural networks for efficient parallel processing.
079f720a2d66074f1c83dd2c2c90d7b5aad8448c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using standard image compression benchmarks, including the Kodak Lossless True Color Image Suite, the CLIC professional validation dataset, and the JPEG-AI test set. The proposed method will be trained on the Vimeo-90K dataset, with 256x256 image patches, using the Adam optimizer and a staged training procedure for the encoder, hyper-encoder, CRR, CDR, and decoder retraining. Baselines for comparison include traditional codecs (JPEG2000, BPG, VTM), state-of-the-art learning-based fixed-rate, variable-rate, and progressive codecs (such as Minnen et al., Cheng et al., Lee et al., and Lu et al.). Evaluation metrics will include bits per pixel (bpp), PSNR, MS-SSIM (in dB), and BD-rate savings. Encoding and decoding time complexities, as well as parameter counts, will be measured to assess computational efficiency. Ablation studies will be performed to isolate the contributions of CRR, CDR, and decoder retraining.
079f720a2d66074f1c83dd2c2c90d7b5aad8448c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first context models specifically designed for trit-plane-based progressive image compression, enabling both rate reduction and distortion reduction in a fine-grained scalable setting. The CRR and CDR modules exploit context information in a parallel, convolutional manner, overcoming the limitations of autoregressive models in progressive scenarios. The decoder retraining scheme is a novel strategy for adapting to refined latent tensors, further improving rate-distortion tradeoffs. The overall framework achieves significant bitrate savings over state-of-the-art progressive codecs, with only marginal increases in computational complexity, and delivers competitive or superior performance to leading non-progressive codecs.

07be0ec1f45e21a1032616535d0290ee6bfe0f6b.title: Structure and Content-Guided Video Synthesis with Diffusion Models
07be0ec1f45e21a1032616535d0290ee6bfe0f6b.research_question: How can video synthesis and editing be performed in a controllable, efficient, and temporally consistent manner, allowing users to modify the content of existing videos based on text or image prompts while preserving the underlying structure of the original footage?
07be0ec1f45e21a1032616535d0290ee6bfe0f6b.hypothesis: Joint training of a latent diffusion model on both images and videos, with explicit conditioning on structure (e.g., depth estimates) and content (e.g., CLIP embeddings), will enable fine-grained, inference-time control over video editing, achieving high temporal consistency, spatial detail, and user-guided customization without the need for per-video retraining.
07be0ec1f45e21a1032616535d0290ee6bfe0f6b.proposed_method: A conditional latent video diffusion model will be developed, operating in a compressed latent space for efficiency. Structure will be represented by monocular depth estimates extracted from input videos and processed with varying levels of detail via blurring and downsampling. Content will be encoded using CLIP image embeddings, with the option to convert text prompts to image embeddings via a learned prior. The model architecture will extend an image-based UNet by introducing temporal layers (1D temporal convolutions and self-attention) to capture spatio-temporal dependencies. Conditioning mechanisms will concatenate structure representations and apply cross-attention for content, allowing explicit control over structure and appearance. A novel guidance method, inspired by classifier-free guidance, will be introduced to control temporal consistency during inference by interpolating between image and video model predictions.
07be0ec1f45e21a1032616535d0290ee6bfe0f6b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a large-scale internal dataset of 240M images and 6.4M video clips, with additional evaluation on public datasets such as DAVIS and various stock footage. The model will be compared against several baselines, including Text2Live, SDEdit (per-frame and with propagation), depth-conditioned Stable Diffusion, and few-shot video stylization methods. Evaluation metrics will include frame consistency (measured by CLIP cosine similarity between consecutive frames) and prompt consistency (CLIP similarity between frames and edit prompts). A user study on Amazon Mechanical Turk will be conducted to assess subjective preference for edit quality and prompt faithfulness. Ablation studies will examine the effects of structure fidelity and customization via finetuning on small image sets.
07be0ec1f45e21a1032616535d0290ee6bfe0f6b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first structure and content-guided latent video diffusion model that enables inference-time editing of arbitrary videos without per-video retraining. It provides explicit, user-controllable trade-offs between temporal consistency, structure preservation, and content fidelity through novel conditioning and guidance mechanisms. The method supports both text- and image-based editing, allows for fine-grained customization via few-shot finetuning, and demonstrates superior user preference and quantitative performance over existing baselines. The use of depth-based structure conditioning with variable fidelity and joint image-video training for temporal control are key innovations.

07c2c3b4af7e4ff1577f36f47f1c93398a6df648.title: Successor Heads: Recurring, Interpretable Attention Heads In The Wild
07c2c3b4af7e4ff1577f36f47f1c93398a6df648.research_question: How do large language models internally represent and perform incrementation tasks on tokens with natural orderings, such as numbers, days, and months, and to what extent are these mechanisms interpretable and shared across different model architectures and scales?
07c2c3b4af7e4ff1577f36f47f1c93398a6df648.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that large language models develop recurring, mechanistically interpretable attention heads—termed successor heads—that implement incrementation over ordinal token sequences using compositional and abstract numeric representations, including mod-10 features, and that these mechanisms are present across a wide range of model sizes and architectures.
07c2c3b4af7e4ff1577f36f47f1c93398a6df648.proposed_method: The proposed research will systematically identify and characterize attention heads in large language models that perform incrementation on tokens from ordinal sequences (e.g., numbers, days, months). This will involve constructing a succession dataset comprising various ordinal token sets and evaluating attention heads using an effective OV circuit to quantify their ability to increment tokens, measured by a defined succession score. The internal representations of these heads will be analyzed using sparse autoencoders to uncover abstract features, such as mod-10 periodicities, and linear probes will be trained to assess the compositionality and transferability of these features across tasks and token domains. Additionally, vector arithmetic experiments will be conducted to manipulate token indices within the learned numeric subspaces, and ablation studies will be performed to determine the causal importance of identified features and neurons.
07c2c3b4af7e4ff1577f36f47f1c93398a6df648.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of transformer-based language models, including Pythia (31M to 1.4B parameters), GPT-2 (up to 12B parameters), and Llama-2 (up to 7B parameters). The succession dataset will include tasks such as numbers, number words, cardinal words, days, day prefixes, months, month prefixes, and letters, with multiple token forms per word to account for tokenizer variations. Baseline comparisons will involve random and non-successor attention heads, as well as ablations of identified successor heads. Evaluation metrics will include the succession score (proportion of tokens correctly incremented), top-1 output-space decoding accuracy, and the impact on next-token prediction loss in natural language datasets (e.g., The Pile) using direct effect mean ablation. Further, the interpretability and transferability of discovered features will be validated through linear probing, neuron ablation, and vector arithmetic tests on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution token sequences.
07c2c3b4af7e4ff1577f36f47f1c93398a6df648.novelty_claims: This research introduces the concept of successor heads as recurring, interpretable attention heads responsible for incrementation in language models, and provides the first systematic evidence of their existence across diverse architectures and scales. It uncovers a compositional numeric subspace, including mod-10 features, that underlies incrementation and demonstrates that these features are causally important and transferable across tasks. The work also proposes novel methodologies for mechanistic interpretability, such as the use of sparse autoencoders and vector arithmetic in the numeric subspace, and reveals interpretable polysemanticity in attention heads operating in natural language contexts.

07db8d33845ca3034f623a5bddf4c4816056d3ba.title: V2V4Real: A Real-World Large-Scale Dataset for Vehicle-to-Vehicle Cooperative Perception
07db8d33845ca3034f623a5bddf4c4816056d3ba.research_question: How can the development and evaluation of vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) cooperative perception systems for autonomous driving be advanced through the creation of a large-scale, real-world, multi-modal dataset, and what are the impacts of such data on key perception tasks such as 3D object detection, object tracking, and domain adaptation?
07db8d33845ca3034f623a5bddf4c4816056d3ba.hypothesis: A large-scale, real-world, multi-modal dataset specifically designed for V2V cooperative perception will enable the development of more robust and accurate cooperative perception algorithms, improve performance on 3D object detection and tracking tasks, and facilitate effective domain adaptation from simulation to real-world scenarios.
07db8d33845ca3034f623a5bddf4c4816056d3ba.proposed_method: A comprehensive real-world dataset will be constructed by equipping two vehicles with synchronized multi-modal sensors, including LiDAR, RGB cameras, and GPS/IMU systems, and collecting data while driving in diverse scenarios and road types. The dataset will be annotated with 3D bounding boxes for multiple vehicle classes and high-definition maps, with careful alignment of coordinate systems and object identities across vehicles. Three cooperative perception tasks will be defined: (1) 3D object detection using multi-vehicle LiDAR data with various fusion strategies (early, intermediate, late), (2) multi-object tracking by leveraging cooperative detection results and established tracking algorithms, and (3) Sim2Real domain adaptation by training on simulated data and adapting to real-world data using domain adaptation techniques such as feature-level and object-level adversarial training. Benchmarking protocols will be established for each task, including evaluation under synchronization and communication delay scenarios.
07db8d33845ca3034f623a5bddf4c4816056d3ba.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize the newly collected V2V4Real dataset, which covers 410 km of driving, 20K LiDAR frames, 40K RGB frames, and 240K annotated 3D bounding boxes across five vehicle classes. Baseline and state-of-the-art cooperative perception algorithms will be implemented and evaluated, including NoFusion, Early Fusion, Late Fusion, F-Cooper, V2VNet, AttFuse, V2X-ViT, and CoBEVT. Evaluation metrics will include Average Precision (AP) at IoU 0.5/0.7 for detection, Multi-Object Tracking Accuracy (MOTA), AMOTA, AMOTP, and sAMOTA for tracking, and AP drop for domain adaptation. Experiments will be conducted under both synchronous and asynchronous (100 ms delay) settings to assess robustness to communication delays. For domain adaptation, models will be trained on the OPV2V simulated dataset and adapted to V2V4Real using adversarial domain adaptation methods, with performance compared to direct transfer and real-data baselines.
07db8d33845ca3034f623a5bddf4c4816056d3ba.novelty_claims: The proposed dataset is the first large-scale, real-world, multi-modal dataset dedicated to V2V cooperative perception, covering a broader range of road types and driving scenarios than existing datasets. It provides comprehensive annotations, including 3D bounding boxes and HD maps, and supports multiple cooperative perception tasks with public benchmarks and baseline implementations. The dataset enables rigorous evaluation of state-of-the-art cooperative perception algorithms under realistic conditions, including asynchrony and bandwidth constraints, and facilitates research on Sim2Real domain adaptation. This work addresses the critical gap in real-world data for V2V perception and is positioned to accelerate progress in robust, scalable autonomous driving systems.

07faa238c8fad8e8213260dae37dc8a9114971c7.title: Neural Fields Meet Explicit Geometric Representations for Inverse Rendering of Urban Scenes
07faa238c8fad8e8213260dae37dc8a9114971c7.research_question: How can high-fidelity 3D reconstruction and intrinsic decomposition (geometry, spatially-varying materials, and HDR lighting) of large-scale urban scenes be achieved from posed camera images, in a way that supports photorealistic relighting and virtual object insertion for downstream applications such as AR and VR?
07faa238c8fad8e8213260dae37dc8a9114971c7.hypothesis: A hybrid approach that combines neural fields for high-resolution intrinsic property estimation with explicit mesh-based representations for efficient physics-based rendering of higher-order lighting effects will enable accurate inverse rendering of large urban scenes, supporting photorealistic relighting and object insertion under varied illumination conditions.
07faa238c8fad8e8213260dae37dc8a9114971c7.proposed_method: A novel hybrid inverse rendering framework, FEGR, is proposed to jointly reconstruct scene geometry, spatially-varying materials, and HDR lighting from posed RGB images (with optional depth). The method represents intrinsic scene properties using a neural field that encodes signed distance, surface normals, base color, and material parameters at each 3D location. Lighting is modeled as a neural HDR sky dome, allowing for relighting and object insertion. Primary rays are rendered volumetrically through the neural field, producing a G-buffer containing geometry and material information. Secondary rays, responsible for higher-order effects such as cast shadows and specular highlights, are ray-traced using an explicit mesh extracted from the neural field via marching cubes. The entire hybrid deferred rendering pipeline is fully differentiable, enabling end-to-end optimization of geometry, materials, and lighting through reconstruction and regularization losses.
07faa238c8fad8e8213260dae37dc8a9114971c7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple large-scale outdoor urban datasets, including NeRF-OSR (with multi-illumination sessions and ground-truth environment maps) and autonomous driving datasets such as Waymo Open Dataset and RoadData (with single-illumination captures and LiDAR depth supervision). Baselines for comparison include NeRF-OSR for relighting, Nvdiffrecmc for intrinsic decomposition, and state-of-the-art lighting estimation methods for object insertion. Evaluation metrics will include PSNR and MSE for relighting accuracy, as well as qualitative and user-study-based assessments for virtual object insertion realism. The experimental setup will leverage semantic segmentation masks to mask out dynamic or irrelevant regions, and will use both single and multi-illumination settings to test the generality of the approach.
07faa238c8fad8e8213260dae37dc8a9114971c7.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a hybrid neural-explicit scene representation that enables efficient and accurate inverse rendering of large urban scenes, overcoming scalability and fidelity limitations of prior volumetric and mesh-based approaches. The framework supports both single and multi-illumination data, disentangles geometry and materials from lighting, and enables photorealistic relighting and virtual object insertion with ray-traced shadows. The method achieves significant improvements over state-of-the-art baselines in both quantitative and qualitative evaluations, and is the first to demonstrate high-quality inverse rendering and scene manipulation at city-block scale using only posed images.

0812f6b841a99b6ffb4fb114c04a090de956de6e.title: VLM2Vec: Training Vision-Language Models for Massive Multimodal Embedding Tasks
0812f6b841a99b6ffb4fb114c04a090de956de6e.research_question: Can a universal multimodal embedding model be developed that generalizes across a wide range of vision-language tasks, domains, and modality combinations, and how can such a model be effectively evaluated and benchmarked?
0812f6b841a99b6ffb4fb114c04a090de956de6e.hypothesis: A vision-language model, when adapted with instruction-following contrastive training on a large, diverse multimodal benchmark, will produce universal embeddings that outperform existing multimodal embedding models across a wide range of tasks, including out-of-distribution and zero-shot scenarios.
0812f6b841a99b6ffb4fb114c04a090de956de6e.proposed_method: A contrastive training framework will be designed to convert state-of-the-art vision-language models (VLMs) into universal embedding models. The approach will leverage deeply fused transformer-based VLMs (such as Phi-3.5-V and LLaVA-1.6) as backbones, enabling the model to process any combination of images and text, guided by explicit task instructions. Task-specific instructions will be incorporated into the input, and both queries and targets (which may be images, text, or image-text pairs) will be encoded into fixed-dimensional vectors using the last layer representation of the model. The model will be trained using a temperature-scaled InfoNCE contrastive loss over in-batch negatives and hard negatives, with GradCache employed to enable large batch sizes and efficient memory usage. LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) will be explored for parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and the impact of training parameters (batch size, number of sub-image crops, training steps) will be systematically studied.
0812f6b841a99b6ffb4fb114c04a090de956de6e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Massive Multimodal Embedding Benchmark (MMEB), which includes 36 datasets spanning four meta-tasks: classification, visual question answering, retrieval, and visual grounding. 20 in-distribution datasets will be used for training, and 16 out-of-distribution datasets will be reserved for evaluation. All tasks will be reformulated as ranking problems with 1,000 candidates per query, and Precision@1 will be used as the primary evaluation metric. The proposed method will be compared against a comprehensive set of baselines, including CLIP, BLIP2, SigLIP, OpenCLIP, UniIR, MagicLens, and E5-V, both with and without fine-tuning. Training will be performed on 8 H100 GPUs, with a batch size of up to 1,024 and a maximum text length of 256 tokens. Ablation studies will investigate the effects of full fine-tuning versus LoRA, batch size, number of sub-image crops, and the inclusion of task instructions.
0812f6b841a99b6ffb4fb114c04a090de956de6e.novelty_claims: A novel universal multimodal embedding benchmark (MMEB) is introduced, covering a uniquely broad set of tasks and datasets for both training and evaluation. The proposed VLM2VEC framework enables any vision-language model to be transformed into a universal embedding model capable of instruction-following and handling arbitrary modality combinations. Deep integration of vision and language features within the transformer backbone, combined with instruction-guided contrastive training, is claimed to significantly improve generalization and zero-shot performance. The method demonstrates substantial improvements over existing baselines, including both fine-tuned and non-fine-tuned models, and provides new insights into the benefits of instruction-following and diverse task training for universal multimodal embeddings.

0816ee42aa1c84ad929bbfd46dd6d41d8e9b9a19.title: AdaptDiffuser: Diffusion Models as Adaptive Self-evolving Planners
0816ee42aa1c84ad929bbfd46dd6d41d8e9b9a19.research_question: How can the generalization and planning performance of diffusion-based offline reinforcement learning models be improved, particularly when facing insufficiently diverse training data and novel, unseen tasks?
0816ee42aa1c84ad929bbfd46dd6d41d8e9b9a19.hypothesis: Integrating a self-evolving, reward-guided synthetic data generation process with selective fine-tuning will enable diffusion-based planners to achieve higher performance and better generalization to unseen tasks without requiring additional expert data.
0816ee42aa1c84ad929bbfd46dd6d41d8e9b9a19.proposed_method: A novel adaptive framework, AdaptDiffuser, is developed to enhance diffusion-based planners for offline reinforcement learning. The method iteratively generates diverse synthetic expert trajectories for goal-conditioned tasks using reward gradient guidance during the diffusion denoising process. A rule-based or neural discriminator selects high-quality synthetic data based on reward and dynamics consistency, filtering out infeasible or low-quality samples. The selected trajectories are then used to fine-tune the diffusion model, improving its mean and covariance estimates and thus its planning capabilities. This self-evolving process is repeated over multiple iterations, continually enriching the training dataset and enhancing both planning performance and adaptability to new tasks.
0816ee42aa1c84ad929bbfd46dd6d41d8e9b9a19.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on two widely-used offline RL benchmarks: Maze2D (navigation tasks with sparse rewards and varying maze layouts) and MuJoCo (locomotion tasks with continuous control and several dataset types, including medium, random, and medium-expert). Additional adaptation experiments are performed on custom-designed unseen tasks, including a KUKA industrial robot arm pick-and-place scenario and Maze2D environments with auxiliary objectives (e.g., coin collection). Baselines include model-free RL algorithms (IQL, CQL), return-conditioned models (Decision Transformer, Trajectory Transformer), model-based planners (MPPI, MOPO, MOReL, MBOP), and the prior diffusion-based Diffuser. Evaluation metrics include normalized average return, success rates, and qualitative trajectory analysis. Ablation studies assess the impact of iterative self-evolution and varying amounts of expert data.
0816ee42aa1c84ad929bbfd46dd6d41d8e9b9a19.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a self-evolving planning framework for diffusion models that iteratively generates and selects high-quality synthetic expert data using reward-guided diffusion and discriminator-based filtering. This approach enables diffusion-based planners to generalize to unseen tasks without requiring additional expert data, overcoming limitations of prior methods that rely on fixed offline datasets. The integration of reward gradients directly into the diffusion sampling process, combined with iterative fine-tuning, is claimed to significantly improve both planning performance and adaptability, as demonstrated by superior results on standard benchmarks and novel task settings.

083bab4a967c2221d9f4da9110fe37d8ca679078.title: DynamiCrafter: Animating Open-domain Images with Video Diffusion Priors
083bab4a967c2221d9f4da9110fe37d8ca679078.research_question: How can open-domain still images be effectively animated into videos that exhibit natural, logical dynamics and high visual conformity to the input image, leveraging the capabilities of modern generative video models?
083bab4a967c2221d9f4da9110fe37d8ca679078.hypothesis: Incorporating a dual-stream image injection paradigm—combining text-aligned context representation with direct visual detail guidance—into a video diffusion model will enable the generation of animated videos from still images that are both visually faithful to the input and exhibit plausible, natural dynamics across a wide range of content domains.
083bab4a967c2221d9f4da9110fe37d8ca679078.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that animates open-domain still images by leveraging pre-trained text-to-video (T2V) diffusion models. The approach introduces a dual-stream image injection paradigm: (1) the input image is projected into a text-aligned context representation space using a pre-trained CLIP image encoder and a learnable query transformer, facilitating semantic understanding and dynamic synthesis; (2) the full image is also concatenated with the initial noise input to the diffusion model, providing direct visual detail guidance. The two streams are fused within the denoising U-Net via adaptive gating mechanisms that modulate the influence of each stream across different network layers. The training procedure involves a staged strategy: first, the context representation network is trained on a T2I model, then adapted to the T2V model, and finally jointly fine-tuned with the visual detail guidance stream to ensure both semantic alignment and high-fidelity visual preservation.
083bab4a967c2221d9f4da9110fe37d8ca679078.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the open-source VideoCrafter T2V model and Stable-Diffusion-v2.1 T2I model. The model will be trained on the WebVid-10M dataset, sampling 16 frames per video at 256x256 resolution. Evaluation will include zero-shot generation on UCF-101 and MSR-VTT datasets, comparing against baselines such as VideoComposer and I2VGen-XL, as well as commercial systems like Gen-2 and PikaLabs. Metrics will include Frechet Video Distance (FVD), Kernel Video Distance (KVD), and a custom Perceptual Input Conformity (PIC) score based on DreamSim. User studies will assess motion quality, temporal coherence, and input conformity. Ablation studies will investigate the impact of each stream and training strategy, and additional experiments will explore text-based motion control using a filtered and re-annotated dataset for dynamic captioning.
083bab4a967c2221d9f4da9110fe37d8ca679078.novelty_claims: The proposed method pioneers a dual-stream image injection paradigm for animating open-domain images, combining semantic context and direct visual detail guidance within a video diffusion framework. It introduces a dedicated training strategy for harmonizing these streams, enabling both high visual fidelity and natural dynamic synthesis. The approach is the first to demonstrate effective text-based motion control for image animation in open domains, and it is shown to outperform existing open-source and commercial competitors in both quantitative and qualitative evaluations. The framework is also adaptable to related applications such as storytelling video generation, looping video synthesis, and generative frame interpolation.

084bc25747b92be54134d4e4257789b4b6c33c10.title: Rank-DETR for High Quality Object Detection
084bc25747b92be54134d4e4257789b4b6c33c10.research_question: How can object detection transformers (DETRs) be enhanced to achieve higher quality object detection, particularly by improving the ranking accuracy of bounding box predictions under high IoU thresholds?
084bc25747b92be54134d4e4257789b4b6c33c10.hypothesis: Integrating rank-oriented architectural components and optimization strategies into DETR-based object detectors will improve the alignment between classification confidence and localization accuracy, resulting in superior detection performance, especially at high IoU thresholds.
084bc25747b92be54134d4e4257789b4b6c33c10.proposed_method: A novel object detection framework, Rank-DETR, is proposed, which incorporates rank-oriented architectural and optimization designs into the DETR pipeline. The method introduces a rank-adaptive classification head after each Transformer decoder layer, which adjusts classification scores using learnable logit bias vectors that are aware of query ranking. Additionally, a query rank layer is inserted before each of the last L-1 Transformer decoder layers to sort and regenerate content and positional queries based on the latest ranking information, ensuring that ranking cues are propagated throughout the decoding process. On the optimization side, a GIoU-aware classification loss is employed, supervising the classification head with normalized GIoU scores to couple localization quality with classification. Furthermore, a high-order matching cost is used during Hungarian matching, prioritizing predictions with both high classification confidence and high IoU by raising the IoU term to a higher power, thus emphasizing accurate localization in the matching process.
084bc25747b92be54134d4e4257789b4b6c33c10.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the COCO object detection benchmark using the detrex toolbox. The proposed method will be evaluated with various backbones, including ResNet-50, Swin-Tiny, and Swin-Large, and compared against strong DETR-based baselines such as H-DETR and DINO-DETR. Evaluation metrics will include mean Average Precision (AP), AP at different IoU thresholds (AP50, AP75), and Average Recall (AR), as well as error metrics such as oLRP for false positives and false negatives. Ablation studies will systematically assess the contribution of each proposed component. Computational efficiency, including FLOPs, parameter count, training time, and inference speed, will also be measured to ensure practical viability.
084bc25747b92be54134d4e4257789b4b6c33c10.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a comprehensive rank-oriented design for DETR-based object detectors, including the first use of a rank-adaptive classification head and a query rank layer that propagate ranking information throughout the decoding process. The method further innovates by integrating a GIoU-aware classification loss and a high-order matching cost, directly aligning classification confidence with localization quality. These contributions collectively enable more accurate ranking of predictions, leading to significant improvements in detection performance, particularly at high IoU thresholds, and demonstrate generalizability across multiple DETR variants and backbone architectures.

08695fdaa5544e22742a8aea1ddeb9808ab20ab2.title: AutoMix: Unveiling the Power of Mixup for Stronger Classifiers
08695fdaa5544e22742a8aea1ddeb9808ab20ab2.research_question: How can data mixing augmentation strategies be improved to directly serve the classification objective, achieving both high accuracy and computational efficiency in deep neural network training for image classification?
08695fdaa5544e22742a8aea1ddeb9808ab20ab2.hypothesis: A parameterized, learnable mixup policy that integrates mixed sample generation and classification within a unified, end-to-end optimization framework will yield stronger classifiers with improved generalization and efficiency compared to existing hand-crafted or optimization-based mixup methods.
08695fdaa5544e22742a8aea1ddeb9808ab20ab2.proposed_method: A new automatic mixup framework, AutoMix, is proposed to unify mixed sample generation and mixup classification as bi-level sub-tasks within a single optimization pipeline. The core of AutoMix is the Mix Block (MB), a lightweight, cross-attention-based module that generates pixel-wise mixup masks by modeling patch-wise relationships between paired feature maps and embedding the mixing ratio. The MB dynamically selects discriminative regions from input pairs to produce semantically meaningful mixed samples, directly supervised by the classification loss. To address instability and gradient entanglement in bi-level optimization, a Momentum Pipeline (MP) is introduced, decoupling the training of the mixup generator and the classifier using a teacher-student (EMA) strategy, thereby stabilizing and accelerating convergence.
08695fdaa5544e22742a8aea1ddeb9808ab20ab2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a wide range of image classification benchmarks, including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, ImageNet-1k, CUB-200, FGVC-Aircraft, iNaturalist2017/2018, and Places205. The method will be evaluated across eight popular network architectures, such as ResNet, Wide-ResNet, ResNeXt, MobileNetV2, EfficientNet, ConvNeXt, DeiT, and Swin Transformer. Baselines will include both hand-crafted mixup methods (e.g., MixUp, CutMix, ManifoldMix, AugMix, AttentiveMix, SaliencyMix, FMix, ResizeMix) and optimization-based methods (e.g., PuzzleMix, Co-Mixup, SuperMix). Evaluation metrics will include top-1 classification accuracy and expected calibration error (ECE). Standardized training procedures, data augmentations, and hyperparameter settings will be used for fair comparison, and results will be averaged over multiple trials.
08695fdaa5544e22742a8aea1ddeb9808ab20ab2.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified, end-to-end bi-level optimization framework for mixup training, explicitly decoupling mixed sample generation and classification. The Mix Block offers a novel, parameterized, cross-attention-based approach to generate pixel-wise mixup masks, enabling adaptive and semantically meaningful mixing policies. The Momentum Pipeline innovatively stabilizes bi-level optimization by decoupling generator and classifier training, mitigating gradient entanglement and trivial solutions. The approach claims significant improvements in accuracy, calibration, and efficiency over state-of-the-art mixup methods across diverse datasets and architectures.

086f2c280dbb8331ee1bdcac2fee8dc9a390d44f.title: Does equivariance matter at scale?
086f2c280dbb8331ee1bdcac2fee8dc9a390d44f.research_question: Does incorporating explicit equivariance into neural network architectures provide benefits in terms of data efficiency and compute scaling compared to non-equivariant models, especially at large scale? How do these models compare in terms of optimal allocation of compute resources between model size and training duration, and what role does data augmentation play in bridging any performance gaps?
086f2c280dbb8331ee1bdcac2fee8dc9a390d44f.hypothesis: Explicitly equivariant neural network architectures will demonstrate superior data and compute efficiency compared to non-equivariant architectures, even at large scale. Data augmentation may reduce but not fully eliminate the advantages of equivariant models, and the optimal allocation of compute resources will differ between the two model classes.
086f2c280dbb8331ee1bdcac2fee8dc9a390d44f.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical study will be conducted comparing E(3)-equivariant and non-equivariant transformer architectures on a benchmark task involving the prediction of rigid-body interactions in 3D mesh-based physical simulations. The equivariant model will be based on the Geometric Algebra Transformer (GATr), which utilizes multivector representations and an E(3)-equivariant dot-product attention mechanism, while the baseline will use a standard pre-LN transformer with multi-query attention. Both models will process mesh faces as tokens and employ a hierarchical attention mechanism, with half of the attention heads restricted to intra-object attention and the other half attending globally. Object rigidity will be enforced by averaging predicted translation and rotation outputs per object, ensuring consistent rigid-body transformations. Hyperparameters such as depth, width, and number of attention heads will be tuned to define comparable model families for both architectures.
086f2c280dbb8331ee1bdcac2fee8dc9a390d44f.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize a large-scale synthetic dataset of rigid-body interactions generated with the Kubric simulator, recreating the MOVi-B dataset parameters. The dataset will consist of 400,000 trajectories with 96 time steps each, involving 3-10 objects per scene and up to 2160 mesh faces per object. Two main experimental series will be performed: (1) scaling with compute, where model size and number of training tokens are varied across three orders of magnitude in compute budget (10^16 to 10^19 nominal FLOPs), and (2) scaling with data, where the number of unique training samples is varied over five orders of magnitude while fixing compute budget and model size. Baselines will include the non-equivariant transformer, the equivariant transformer, and the non-equivariant transformer with data augmentation (applying symmetry transformations per epoch). Evaluation will be based on mean squared error of predicted mesh vertex positions. Empirical scaling laws will be fitted to the results, and optimal compute allocation strategies will be derived.
086f2c280dbb8331ee1bdcac2fee8dc9a390d44f.novelty_claims: The proposed study will provide the first systematic, large-scale empirical comparison of equivariant and non-equivariant transformer architectures in the context of geometric, symmetry-rich problems, focusing on scaling laws with respect to both data and compute. It will introduce a rigorous methodology for analyzing the interplay between architectural inductive biases, data augmentation, and scaling behavior. The work will offer novel insights into the persistent benefits of equivariance even in the large-data, large-compute regime, and will characterize how optimal compute allocation strategies differ between model classes. The use of the Geometric Algebra Transformer and the hierarchical attention mechanism in this context represents an innovative approach to isolating the effects of equivariance.

087fa49d28506726c337ea3862275462149fc1f9.title: The Geometry of Categorical and Hierarchical Concepts in Large Language Models
087fa49d28506726c337ea3862275462149fc1f9.research_question: How are categorical and hierarchical semantic concepts geometrically encoded in the representation spaces of large language models, particularly in the absence of natural binary contrasts?
087fa49d28506726c337ea3862275462149fc1f9.hypothesis: Semantic concepts, including categorical and hierarchical structures, are encoded as specific geometric objects—such as vectors and polytopes—in the representation spaces of large language models, and hierarchical relationships are reflected as orthogonality between these representations.
087fa49d28506726c337ea3862275462149fc1f9.proposed_method: A formal framework will be developed to extend the linear representation hypothesis from binary concepts with natural contrasts to general features and categorical concepts, enabling their representation as vectors and polytopes in the unified representation space of large language models. The approach will leverage a causal inner product to align embedding and unembedding spaces, transforming them via a whitening operation to ensure the Euclidean inner product reflects semantic relationships. Vector representations for binary features will be estimated using a variant of Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), optimizing for separation between concept-related tokens and the rest of the vocabulary while minimizing within-class variance. The method will further formalize how hierarchical relationships between concepts are encoded as orthogonality between their vector representations, and categorical concepts will be represented as convex polytopes (simplexes) formed from their constituent vectors.
087fa49d28506726c337ea3862275462149fc1f9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large language models such as Gemma-2B and LLaMA-3-8B. A large set of binary and categorical concepts will be extracted from the WordNet hierarchy, encompassing over 900 hierarchically related noun and verb synsets. For each concept, vector representations will be estimated using LDA on the unembedding vectors, with the vocabulary split into training and test sets to assess generalization. Baseline comparisons will include analyses with randomly shuffled unembedding vectors to control for the effects of high-dimensional geometry and set inclusion. Evaluation metrics will include the separation of concept-related tokens in projection space, changes in logit differences when intervening on context embeddings, and cosine similarity matrices to assess alignment with the semantic hierarchy. Additional controls will test the robustness of orthogonality claims by breaking set inclusion and comparing to random baselines.
087fa49d28506726c337ea3862275462149fc1f9.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled extension of the linear representation hypothesis to encompass general features and categorical concepts, enabling their representation as vectors and polytopes rather than mere directions. It formalizes and proves that hierarchical semantic relationships are encoded as orthogonality in the representation space, providing a direct geometric interpretation of semantic hierarchy. The approach unifies embedding and unembedding spaces via a causal inner product, allowing for precise estimation and manipulation of concept representations. Empirical validation on state-of-the-art language models and large-scale concept hierarchies provides new evidence for the existence and structure of these geometric representations, offering foundational insights for future interpretability and feature extraction methods in language models.

087fb7f1c25d3af48fb2603db6586184fe447cfc.title: Preventing False Discovery in Interactive Data Analysis Is Hard
087fb7f1c25d3af48fb2603db6586184fe447cfc.research_question: What are the fundamental computational limitations of preventing false discovery in interactive data analysis, particularly when answering a large number of adaptively chosen statistical queries using a finite sample from an unknown distribution?
087fb7f1c25d3af48fb2603db6586184fe447cfc.hypothesis: Assuming the existence of standard cryptographic primitives such as one-way functions, no computationally efficient algorithm can provide statistically valid answers to more than a cubic number of adaptively chosen statistical queries given n samples from an unknown distribution.
087fb7f1c25d3af48fb2603db6586184fe447cfc.proposed_method: The proposed approach formalizes interactive data analysis in the statistical query (SQ) model, where an oracle is given n samples from an unknown distribution over a high-dimensional space and must answer adaptively chosen statistical queries accurately with respect to the underlying distribution. The methodology involves constructing a challenge distribution and designing an efficient adaptive analyst that, through a sequence of carefully crafted queries, is able to reconstruct nearly all of the oracle's sample points if the oracle provides accurate answers to more than n^3 queries. The attack leverages robust fingerprinting codes to generate challenge queries and tracing algorithms, and employs cryptographic encryption schemes to hide query definitions outside the sample, ensuring the attack works against all computationally bounded oracles. The analysis incorporates measure concentration properties to ensure that the sample and the distribution agree on the challenge queries with high probability, using robust fingerprinting codes to tolerate approximation errors.
087fb7f1c25d3af48fb2603db6586184fe447cfc.experiment_details: Theoretical experiments are proposed in which the oracle is given n samples from a distribution over {0,1}^d, with d growing polynomially in n. The adaptive analyst issues up to n^3+o(1) queries, using robust fingerprinting codes and cryptographic tools to reconstruct the sample. The evaluation metric is the ability of the analyst to reconstruct almost all sample points and to find queries on which the oracle's answers are blatantly inaccurate with respect to the underlying distribution. Baselines include non-adaptive query settings, where exponentially many queries can be answered accurately, and previously known upper bounds for adaptive queries using differentially private mechanisms. The setup also considers both computationally efficient and unbounded oracles, and compares the number of queries that can be answered accurately in each case.
087fb7f1c25d3af48fb2603db6586184fe447cfc.novelty_claims: The proposal establishes a fundamental computational barrier to preventing false discovery in adaptive data analysis, showing for the first time that statistical validity alone can be a source of computational intractability in interactive settings. The approach introduces a novel combination of robust fingerprinting codes and cryptographic encryption to construct efficient reconstruction attacks against oracles answering adaptive queries. The results demonstrate tight lower bounds (up to linear factors) on the number of adaptively chosen queries that can be answered accurately by efficient algorithms, and reveal an inherent trade-off between sample size, data dimensionality, and computational feasibility. This work provides the first computational hardness result specific to adaptively chosen statistical queries, highlighting the intrinsic difficulty of maintaining statistical validity in modern collaborative and adaptive research environments.

088ab579bf490691eea7ac92e122ee11c9b9d131.title: JudgeBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLM-based Judges
088ab579bf490691eea7ac92e122ee11c9b9d131.research_question: How can the reliability and reasoning abilities of LLM-based judges be objectively evaluated, especially on complex tasks where human preference is an unreliable indicator of correctness?
088ab579bf490691eea7ac92e122ee11c9b9d131.hypothesis: A benchmark constructed from challenging response pairs with objectively verifiable correctness labels will more rigorously and accurately assess the reasoning capabilities of LLM-based judges than existing benchmarks focused on human preference alignment.
088ab579bf490691eea7ac92e122ee11c9b9d131.proposed_method: A hierarchical evaluation framework will be established, prioritizing instruction following, factual and logical correctness, and then stylistic alignment. A novel pipeline will be developed to transform any dataset with ground truth labels and verification algorithms into challenging response pairs, each consisting of one correct and one subtly incorrect response. Candidate responses will be generated using a strong LLM (e.g., GPT-4o), and correctness will be verified both by automated checkers and a secondary LLM to filter out format-based errors. The resulting JudgeBench dataset will span categories such as knowledge, reasoning, mathematics, and coding, and will be designed to minimize stylistic cues and self-enhancement bias by using a single model for response generation. Evaluation protocols will include positional bias mitigation by presenting response pairs in both orders and aggregating results.
088ab579bf490691eea7ac92e122ee11c9b9d131.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate a wide range of LLM-based judges, including prompted, fine-tuned, and multi-agent judges, as well as reward models, using the JudgeBench dataset. The dataset will consist of 350 challenging response pairs across knowledge, reasoning, math, and coding, sourced from MMLU-Pro, LiveBench, and LiveCodeBench. Baselines will include existing benchmarks such as MTBench, LLMEval, FairEval, LLMBar, and RewardBench. Evaluation metrics will focus on accuracy in distinguishing correct from incorrect responses, with additional analysis of positional bias, model size effects, and ablation studies comparing judge and solver performance. The evaluation protocol will require each judge to assess each pair twice with swapped order, and aggregate decisions to account for ties and inconsistencies.
088ab579bf490691eea7ac92e122ee11c9b9d131.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled, hierarchical evaluation framework that objectively prioritizes factual and logical correctness over stylistic preferences. The JudgeBench benchmark is constructed to be significantly more challenging than prior benchmarks, with response pairs that are difficult for both humans and LLM-based judges to reliably distinguish. The pipeline for generating response pairs is novel in its use of a single strong LLM for both correct and incorrect responses, minimizing stylistic bias and enabling objective ground truth labeling. The benchmark provides a robust, unsaturated testbed for evaluating and advancing reasoning-enhanced LLM-based judges, addressing a critical gap as AI systems surpass human evaluators in complexity.

08901f2f5b363f28660f401afafccc2e6c9373d5.title: Cross Entropy versus Label Smoothing: A Neural Collapse Perspective
08901f2f5b363f28660f401afafccc2e6c9373d5.research_question: How do different loss functions, specifically cross-entropy and label smoothing, influence the convergence behavior and geometric properties of deep neural networks during the terminal phase of training, as characterized by the neural collapse framework?
08901f2f5b363f28660f401afafccc2e6c9373d5.hypothesis: Label smoothing, compared to standard cross-entropy loss, induces faster convergence to neural collapse, achieves a more pronounced simplex ETF structure in features and classifier weights, and improves model calibration and generalization by introducing an implicit inductive bias that regularizes the network's output distributions.
08901f2f5b363f28660f401afafccc2e6c9373d5.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical and theoretical investigation will be conducted to analyze the effects of cross-entropy loss and label smoothing on deep neural network training. The approach will involve training neural networks with both loss functions on balanced datasets, monitoring the evolution of last-layer features and classifier weights, and quantifying neural collapse metrics (NC1, NC2, NC3) throughout training. The unconstrained feature model (UFM) will be leveraged to derive closed-form expressions for the global minimizers under both loss functions, explicitly parameterized by the label smoothing hyperparameter. A conditioning number analysis of the optimization landscape around these minimizers will be performed to explain differences in convergence speed. The impact of label smoothing on model calibration will be examined, including the interaction with temperature scaling and the effect of varying the smoothing parameter.
08901f2f5b363f28660f401afafccc2e6c9373d5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification datasets including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, STL-10, and Tiny ImageNet. ResNet-18 will be used as the backbone for CIFAR-10, and ResNet-50 for CIFAR-100, STL-10, and Tiny ImageNet. Training will be performed using stochastic gradient descent with momentum, a batch size of 128, and multi-step learning rate decay. The training period will be extended (e.g., 800 epochs for most datasets) to fully observe terminal phase training. Standard preprocessing will be used without data augmentation to isolate the effects of the loss functions. Baselines will include models trained with cross-entropy and with varying levels of label smoothing. Evaluation metrics will include training and test error rates, nearest centroid classifier performance, neural collapse metrics (NC1, NC2, NC3), and expected calibration error (ECE) both before and after temperature scaling. The influence of the label smoothing hyperparameter on these metrics will also be systematically explored.
08901f2f5b363f28660f401afafccc2e6c9373d5.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel perspective by systematically comparing cross-entropy and label smoothing losses through the lens of neural collapse, both empirically and theoretically. Closed-form solutions for the global minimizers under both loss functions are derived within the unconstrained feature model, providing new insights into the optimization landscape and convergence properties. The work claims to reveal that label smoothing not only accelerates convergence to neural collapse but also induces a more pronounced simplex ETF structure (NC2), which is hypothesized to enhance generalization. Additionally, the proposal investigates the nuanced effects of label smoothing on model calibration, including the interplay with temperature scaling, and provides a theoretical explanation for observed empirical phenomena.

08a80cb34d785258c770acecd302ab41ead46eed.title: WizardLM: Empowering Large Pre-Trained Language Models to Follow Complex Instructions
08a80cb34d785258c770acecd302ab41ead46eed.research_question: How can large pre-trained language models be empowered to follow complex and diverse open-domain instructions without relying on expensive and labor-intensive human annotation, and what impact does instruction complexity have on the performance of instruction-tuned LLMs?
08a80cb34d785258c770acecd302ab41ead46eed.hypothesis: Automatically evolving and generating open-domain instructions of varying complexity using large language models, rather than humans, will produce instruction-following datasets that significantly improve the performance of fine-tuned LLMs on complex tasks.
08a80cb34d785258c770acecd302ab41ead46eed.proposed_method: A novel framework, Evol-Instruct, will be developed to automatically generate large-scale, open-domain instruction datasets with varying levels of complexity. The process begins with an initial set of seed instructions, which are iteratively evolved using two main strategies: In-Depth Evolving (increasing instruction complexity through operations such as adding constraints, deepening, concretizing, increasing reasoning steps, and complicating input) and In-Breadth Evolving (increasing diversity by generating new instructions inspired by existing ones). Each evolution step is performed by prompting a strong LLM (e.g., ChatGPT-3.5) with carefully designed prompts, and corresponding responses are generated by the same LLM. An elimination step filters out failed or low-quality evolutions using automated criteria. The resulting evolved instructions, along with their responses, are merged and shuffled to form a balanced fine-tuning dataset for LLMs.
08a80cb34d785258c770acecd302ab41ead46eed.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by initializing the instruction pool with the Alpaca dataset (52k instructions) and performing four rounds of evolution, resulting in a dataset of 250k instructions. For fair comparison, 70k samples will be randomly selected to match the training size of competitive baselines (e.g., Vicuna). The LLaMA-13B model will be fine-tuned on this data using standard hyperparameters (Adam optimizer, learning rate 2e-5, batch size 4 per GPU, 3 epochs, 8 V100 GPUs with DeepSpeed Zero-3). Evaluation will be performed on a suite of benchmarks, including MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag, TruthfulQA, HumanEval (code), GSM8k (math), AlpacaEval, MT-Bench, and a new human-curated, difficulty-balanced test set called WizardEval. Baselines for comparison include Alpaca-13B, Vicuna-13B, ChatGPT-3.5, Baize-13B, CAMEL-13B, and Tulu-13B. Both automatic metrics and human evaluations (blind pairwise ranking by annotators on WizardEval) will be used to assess performance.
08a80cb34d785258c770acecd302ab41ead46eed.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces an automated, scalable method for generating open-domain instruction data of controlled complexity and diversity using LLMs, reducing reliance on human annotation. The Evol-Instruct framework enables fine-grained control over instruction difficulty and topic coverage, resulting in instruction datasets that better prepare LLMs for complex, real-world tasks. The resulting WizardLM model is expected to significantly outperform existing open-source instruction-tuned LLMs across a wide range of benchmarks, especially in code, math, and reasoning tasks. The research also provides new insights into the importance of instruction complexity for supervised fine-tuning of LLMs and demonstrates the generalizability of the method across different pre-trained model bases.

08b85bce712168998004ee80ce4e475390413c74.title: A Prompt Pattern Catalog to Enhance Prompt Engineering with ChatGPT
08b85bce712168998004ee80ce4e475390413c74.research_question: How can prompt engineering for large language models be systematically enhanced to improve the quality, reliability, and adaptability of LLM outputs across diverse domains, particularly in software development tasks?
08b85bce712168998004ee80ce4e475390413c74.hypothesis: Systematically documenting and applying reusable prompt patterns—analogous to software design patterns—will improve the effectiveness, transferability, and efficiency of prompt engineering for conversational LLMs, leading to higher quality and more reliable outputs.
08b85bce712168998004ee80ce4e475390413c74.proposed_method: A comprehensive catalog of prompt patterns will be developed, each documented in a standardized format including name, classification, intent, motivation, structure, example implementation, and consequences. Patterns will be categorized into areas such as Input Semantics, Output Customization, Error Identification, Prompt Improvement, Interaction, and Context Control. Each pattern will be defined by fundamental contextual statements that guide LLM behavior in specific scenarios, such as automating outputs, adopting personas, refining questions, and managing interaction flow. The methodology will emphasize the creation of a reusable framework for prompt pattern documentation, enabling adaptation to various domains and tasks. The catalog will be validated through iterative prompt creation, application to real-world software engineering tasks, and empirical testing with ChatGPT.
08b85bce712168998004ee80ce4e475390413c74.experiment_details: Experiments will involve applying the prompt pattern catalog to a range of software development tasks using ChatGPT, leveraging both independently created prompts and those sourced from the community. Outputs will be evaluated on criteria such as correctness, relevance, efficiency, and user satisfaction. Baseline comparisons will be made against ad hoc or non-patterned prompts to assess improvements in output quality and interaction efficiency. Evaluation metrics will include task completion rates, number of user interactions required, and qualitative user feedback. All experiments will be conducted using ChatGPT+ due to its accessibility and popularity, with patterns tested in new conversation sessions to avoid context contamination.
08b85bce712168998004ee80ce4e475390413c74.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the concept of a reusable prompt pattern catalog for LLMs, analogous to software design patterns, providing a systematic framework for prompt engineering. The approach codifies prompt engineering knowledge in a transferable format, enabling reuse across domains and tasks. The framework emphasizes the use of fundamental contextual statements rather than formal grammars, making it accessible to users with varying technical backgrounds. The catalog includes novel pattern categories and combinations, such as integrating question refinement with persona or cognitive verification, and provides detailed guidance on structuring and applying prompt patterns for enhanced LLM interaction.

08d438f041b18de0ef256939d885a7d044e438c8.title: Memorization in Self-Supervised Learning Improves Downstream Generalization
08d438f041b18de0ef256939d885a7d044e438c8.research_question: How can memorization be formally defined and measured in self-supervised learning (SSL) without reliance on labels, and what is the relationship between memorization and downstream generalization performance across diverse tasks and datasets?
08d438f041b18de0ef256939d885a7d044e438c8.hypothesis: Memorization in self-supervised learning encoders, as measured by a method-independent alignment-based metric, is essential for achieving superior generalization on downstream tasks, even across different data distributions and task types.
08d438f041b18de0ef256939d885a7d044e438c8.proposed_method: A new framework, SSLMem, will be developed to define and quantify memorization in SSL encoders. The method will measure memorization as the difference in alignment loss between representations of augmented views of a data point, comparing encoders trained with and without that data point. Specifically, for each data point, the alignment loss (the expected distance between representations of two augmentations) will be computed for encoders trained on the full dataset and for encoders trained with the data point left out. The memorization score will be the difference between these two alignment losses, averaged over multiple random augmentations and multiple independently trained encoders. This approach is designed to be independent of SSL training objectives, encoder architectures, and downstream tasks, relying solely on the representations produced by the encoder.
08d438f041b18de0ef256939d885a7d044e438c8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard vision datasets including CIFAR10, SVHN, STL10, and ImageNet, using various SSL methods (e.g., MAE, DINO, SimCLR) and encoder architectures (e.g., ViT, ResNet50). The memorization score will be evaluated by partitioning the training data into shared, candidate, independent, and extra sets, training encoders on different combinations, and measuring alignment-based memorization on candidate points. Downstream generalization will be assessed by removing the most-memorized or random data points from the pre-training set and evaluating linear probing accuracy and semantic segmentation performance (mIoU) on multiple downstream tasks and datasets. Additional experiments will include the effect of limiting alignment via regularization and the impact of differential privacy (DP-SGD) on memorization and downstream accuracy. Statistical significance of memorization differences will be tested using t-tests.
08d438f041b18de0ef256939d885a7d044e438c8.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the first formal, label-independent definition of memorization for SSL that is applicable across different methods, architectures, and downstream tasks. The alignment-based memorization metric operates directly on encoder representations and does not require class labels or specific augmentations. The research will empirically demonstrate that memorization is not only present in SSL but is a key factor in achieving strong downstream generalization, including for tasks and distributions not seen during pre-training. The work will also show that reducing memorization (e.g., via regularization or differential privacy) harms downstream performance, establishing memorization as a necessary property for effective self-supervised feature learning.

0907d616383b18ff4a9973ce012b97ea51c9e7ab.title: Emerging Safety Attack and Defense in Federated Instruction Tuning of Large Language Models
0907d616383b18ff4a9973ce012b97ea51c9e7ab.research_question: How can the safety alignment of large language models trained via federated instruction tuning be compromised by adversarial attacks, and what effective defense mechanisms can be developed to safeguard against such threats in decentralized collaborative learning environments?
0907d616383b18ff4a9973ce012b97ea51c9e7ab.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that malicious clients in federated instruction tuning can significantly compromise the safety alignment of large language models by training on automatically generated unaligned data, and that a post-hoc, automated defense mechanism at the server side can effectively restore safety alignment without significant loss of helpfulness.
0907d616383b18ff4a9973ce012b97ea51c9e7ab.proposed_method: A two-pronged approach is proposed: (1) A novel safety attack in federated instruction tuning (FedIT) where malicious clients generate and train on unaligned instruction-response pairs, either by extracting unsafe samples from public datasets or by leveraging off-the-shelf LLMs to automatically generate harmful instructions and responses. These compromised local models are then aggregated with benign models, thereby poisoning the global model's safety alignment. (2) To counteract this, a post-hoc defense method is introduced, in which the server, after model aggregation, automatically generates a defense dataset comprising both normal and safety-aligned instruction-response pairs. This dataset is constructed using prompt-based data generation pipelines, either with external LLMs or the target model itself. The aggregated global model is then fine-tuned on this defense dataset for a small number of steps, aiming to restore or enhance safety alignment while maintaining helpfulness.
0907d616383b18ff4a9973ce012b97ea51c9e7ab.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the OpenFedLLM framework with Llama2-7B as the base model, employing LoRA for parameter-efficient fine-tuning. Four benign instruction tuning datasets (LMSYS-Chat, WildChat, Dromedary-verbose, Wizard-evol) and two malicious datasets (Beavertails and automatically generated MaliciousGen) will be used. The federated setup involves 10 clients (7 benign, 3 malicious), each with 500 samples, over 100 communication rounds. Evaluation will be performed on three safety benchmarks (AdvBench with Rule, MD-Judge, and RM metrics) and one helpfulness benchmark (MT-Bench). Baselines will include standard FedAvg and six representative FL defense methods (Median, Trimmedmean, Krum, DnC, FoolsGold, Residual). Additional scalability experiments with up to 100 clients and ablation studies on defense data generation and fine-tuning steps will be included.
