0907d616383b18ff4a9973ce012b97ea51c9e7ab.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first systematic safety attack targeting federated instruction tuning of large language models, demonstrating that simple, automated data poisoning can drastically reduce safety alignment in collaborative LLM training. It further presents a novel, automated post-hoc defense mechanism that operates at the server level, decoupling defense from model-level operations and enabling robust safety restoration even against stealthy attacks undetectable by existing FL defense methods. The approach is validated to be scalable, plug-and-play with existing FL frameworks, and effective across various datasets and LLM architectures.

091c5297a3ef491fc3957709c7c7953d42e50cd1.title: Online Class Incremental Learning on Stochastic Blurry Task Boundary via Mask and Visual Prompt Tuning
091c5297a3ef491fc3957709c7c7953d42e50cd1.research_question: How can online class-incremental learning be effectively performed in scenarios where task boundaries are stochastic and blurry, and data distributions dynamically change as in real-world streams?
091c5297a3ef491fc3957709c7c7953d42e50cd1.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a combination of instance-wise logit masking, contrastive visual prompt tuning, gradient similarity-based focal loss, and adaptive feature scaling will significantly improve continual learning performance by mitigating intra- and inter-task forgetting as well as class imbalance in stochastic, blurry task boundary scenarios.
091c5297a3ef491fc3957709c7c7953d42e50cd1.proposed_method: A novel online continual learning framework will be developed for the Stochastic Incremental Blurry (Si-Blurry) scenario, which simulates real-world data streams with dynamically varying classes and stochastic task boundaries. The method will utilize a pre-trained Vision Transformer (ViT) as a frozen feature extractor, augmented with a pool of learnable visual prompts. Instance-wise logit masking will be applied to the classification logits to facilitate easier learning by masking irrelevant classes, while a contrastive visual prompt tuning loss will be used to ensure effective prompt selection and knowledge retention. To address class imbalance, a gradient similarity-based focal loss will emphasize learning from underrepresented (minor) classes by dynamically scaling the loss based on how much a sample is ignored during training. Additionally, adaptive feature scaling will be employed to regularize learning on major classes by adjusting feature magnitudes according to their marginal benefit, thus preventing overfitting. The entire system will be trained end-to-end with a composite loss function that balances these components.
091c5297a3ef491fc3957709c7c7953d42e50cd1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, and ImageNet-R datasets, each configured under the proposed Si-Blurry scenario with stochastic class and task boundaries. The experimental setup will include varying disjoint class ratios and blurry sample ratios to simulate different real-world streaming conditions. Baseline comparisons will be made against state-of-the-art continual learning methods, including replay-based, regularization-based, and prompt-based approaches (e.g., ER, Rainbow Memory, CLIB, LwF, EWC++, L2P, DualPrompt). Evaluation metrics will include anytime inference accuracy (AUC) and final accuracy after training (ALast), with results averaged over multiple independent seeds. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the contribution of each proposed component, and experiments will be repeated with and without memory buffers to assess robustness.
091c5297a3ef491fc3957709c7c7953d42e50cd1.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the Si-Blurry scenario, a new and more realistic continual learning benchmark that captures the stochastic and dynamic nature of real-world data streams. The method is the first to combine instance-wise logit masking and contrastive visual prompt tuning for mitigating intra- and inter-task forgetting in blurry, stochastic task settings. Additionally, the gradient similarity-based focal loss and adaptive feature scaling are novel techniques for addressing class imbalance and overfitting in online incremental learning. The integrated framework is claimed to outperform existing state-of-the-art methods under challenging, realistic conditions, as demonstrated by extensive empirical evaluation.

092245d86b77181c36f972b1b7a17a59cd989c4a.title: Guiding Instruction-based Image Editing via Multimodal Large Language Models
092245d86b77181c36f972b1b7a17a59cd989c4a.research_question: How can instruction-based image editing be improved to better follow human commands, especially when instructions are brief or ambiguous, by leveraging advances in multimodal large language models?
092245d86b77181c36f972b1b7a17a59cd989c4a.hypothesis: Integrating multimodal large language models to derive expressive, visual-aware instructions will provide more explicit and effective guidance for image editing, resulting in improved alignment with user intent and higher-quality edited images compared to existing methods.
092245d86b77181c36f972b1b7a17a59cd989c4a.proposed_method: A novel framework, termed MLLM-Guided Image Editing (MGIE), is proposed to enhance instruction-based image editing by jointly leveraging a multimodal large language model (MLLM) and a diffusion-based image editing model. The MLLM is trained to generate concise, expressive instructions from human-provided commands and input images, using a summarization module to ensure the guidance is explicit yet succinct. These expressive instructions are augmented with trainable visual tokens ([IMG]) that bridge language and vision modalities. An edit head, implemented as a multi-layer Transformer, transforms these tokens into latent visual guidance, which is then injected into a latent diffusion model via cross-attention mechanisms. The entire system is trained end-to-end, optimizing both the instruction generation and image editing objectives, enabling the model to learn to extract and utilize relevant visual guidance for precise image manipulation.
092245d86b77181c36f972b1b7a17a59cd989c4a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of instruction-based image editing datasets, including IPr2Pr for pre-training, and EVR, GIER, MA5k, and MagicBrush for comprehensive evaluation across Photoshop-style modifications, global photo optimization, and local object alteration. Baseline comparisons will include InsPix2Pix (CLIP-based) and a language-only LLM-guided editing model (LGIE). Evaluation metrics will encompass pixel-level differences (L1), visual feature similarity (DINO, CVS), structural similarity (SSIM), perceptual similarity (LPIPS), and text-image alignment (CTS). Both zero-shot and fine-tuned scenarios will be assessed, with all models trained or adapted on the same splits. Human evaluations will also be performed to assess instruction quality and editing results, and inference efficiency will be measured on NVIDIA A100 GPUs.
092245d86b77181c36f972b1b7a17a59cd989c4a.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first end-to-end framework that leverages multimodal large language models to generate expressive, visual-aware instructions for image editing, bridging the gap between ambiguous human commands and precise visual manipulation. The approach jointly optimizes instruction derivation and image editing, enabling the model to learn explicit, contextually relevant guidance that significantly improves editing performance across diverse tasks. The use of trainable visual tokens and a Transformer-based edit head to connect language and vision modalities is a novel architectural contribution. Extensive experiments demonstrate that this framework achieves superior results in both automatic and human evaluations while maintaining competitive inference efficiency.

0938d0ccc1c633fa0f8c067d914358b1ef53a44b.title: Vid2Seq: Large-Scale Pretraining of a Visual Language Model for Dense Video Captioning
0938d0ccc1c633fa0f8c067d914358b1ef53a44b.research_question: How can dense video captioning—requiring both temporal localization and natural language description of multiple events in untrimmed videos—be improved using large-scale pretraining on multi-modal data, particularly when annotated datasets are limited or expensive to obtain?
0938d0ccc1c633fa0f8c067d914358b1ef53a44b.hypothesis: Pretraining a unified visual language model on large-scale, unlabeled narrated videos using transcribed speech and corresponding temporal boundaries as weak supervision will significantly improve the performance and generalization of dense video captioning models across multiple benchmarks and tasks.
0938d0ccc1c633fa0f8c067d914358b1ef53a44b.proposed_method: A novel multi-modal encoder-decoder architecture will be developed that jointly predicts event boundaries and captions as a single sequence of tokens, interleaving text and special time tokens for temporal grounding. The model will process both video frames and transcribed speech, using a visual encoder (frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 backbone for frame-level features and a transformer for temporal modeling) and a text encoder (tokenizing speech with SentencePiece, augmented with time tokens). The decoder, initialized from T5-Base, will autoregressively generate event sequences by cross-attending to both visual and speech embeddings. Pretraining will leverage two objectives: a generative task predicting transcribed speech from video inputs, and a denoising task reconstructing masked spans of speech from corrupted input, enabling the model to learn cross-modal and temporal dependencies from weakly aligned narrated video data.
0938d0ccc1c633fa0f8c067d914358b1ef53a44b.experiment_details: Experiments will pretrain the model on the YT-Temporal-1B dataset, comprising 18 million untrimmed narrated YouTube videos, and optionally on HowTo100M for domain transfer. Downstream evaluation will be conducted on dense video captioning datasets (YouCook2, ViTT, ActivityNet Captions), video paragraph captioning (YouCook2, ActivityNet Captions), and video clip captioning (MSR-VTT, MSVD). Baselines will include state-of-the-art two-stage and joint localization-captioning models, as well as models pretrained only on text or trimmed clips. Evaluation metrics will include CIDEr, METEOR, SODA_c, and event-level precision, recall, and F1 scores across multiple IoU thresholds. Ablation studies will assess the effects of pretraining objectives, input modalities, model size, and pretraining data scale. Few-shot experiments will fine-tune the pretrained model on small fractions of labeled data to evaluate generalization.
0938d0ccc1c633fa0f8c067d914358b1ef53a44b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified sequence-to-sequence framework for dense video captioning that interleaves text and time tokens, enabling simultaneous event localization and captioning in a single output. It leverages large-scale pretraining on unlabeled narrated videos by reformulating transcribed speech boundaries as pseudo event boundaries, thus bypassing the need for expensive manual annotation. The approach demonstrates that integrating temporal information via time tokens and using untrimmed videos for pretraining yields significant improvements. The model generalizes across dense, paragraph, and clip-level video captioning tasks, and excels in few-shot settings, establishing new state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks.

09609bd28855fd9b27f043b4dbf509615229bd08.title: HQ-Edit: A High-Quality Dataset for Instruction-based Image Editing
09609bd28855fd9b27f043b4dbf509615229bd08.research_question: How can a large-scale, high-quality dataset for instruction-based image editing be constructed to improve the performance and evaluation of image editing models, particularly in terms of alignment between instructions and edits, and the overall coherence of edited images?
09609bd28855fd9b27f043b4dbf509615229bd08.hypothesis: Leveraging advanced foundation models such as GPT-4V and DALL-E 3 in a scalable, synthetic data generation pipeline will produce a more diverse, higher-resolution, and better-aligned instruction-based image editing dataset than existing approaches, thereby enabling improved training and evaluation of image editing models.
09609bd28855fd9b27f043b4dbf509615229bd08.proposed_method: A novel data generation pipeline will be developed to create a large-scale instruction-based image editing dataset. The process begins with collecting a small, diverse set of seed triplets (input/output image descriptions and edit instructions) from online sources, which are then expanded to approximately 100,000 instances using GPT-4 to ensure diversity and coverage. In the generation phase, GPT-4 is used to refine and merge these triplets into detailed diptych prompts for DALL-E 3, which generates side-by-side input-output image pairs (diptychs) at high resolution. Post-processing decomposes diptychs into paired images using a retrained YOLOv8 object detector, aligns them with DIFT-based warping, and filters out misaligned samples. Edit instructions are further refined and augmented (including inverse edits) using GPT-4V to maximize alignment and detail, resulting in a dataset of nearly 200,000 high-quality edit pairs.
09609bd28855fd9b27f043b4dbf509615229bd08.experiment_details: The resulting dataset will be evaluated both quantitatively and qualitatively. Two new evaluation metrics, Alignment (semantic consistency with the edit prompt) and Coherence (aesthetic quality, including lighting, style, and edge smoothness), will be introduced and computed using GPT-4V. The dataset's quality will be benchmarked against existing datasets such as InstructPix2Pix, HIVE, and MagicBrush by sampling 500 data points from each and comparing their Alignment and Coherence scores. Additionally, downstream experiments will involve fine-tuning state-of-the-art instruction-based image editing models (e.g., InstructPix2Pix) on the new dataset, with performance assessed using the proposed metrics and human evaluation on selected samples.
09609bd28855fd9b27f043b4dbf509615229bd08.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a scalable, synthetic data generation pipeline leveraging the latest foundation models (GPT-4V and DALL-E 3) to create a high-resolution, diverse, and well-aligned instruction-based image editing dataset. The method innovates by generating diptychs for improved image pair correspondence, employing advanced post-processing for precise alignment, and augmenting instructions with both forward and inverse edits. Two novel evaluation metrics, Alignment and Coherence, are proposed for comprehensive quantitative assessment of edit quality. The resulting dataset is claimed to significantly outperform existing datasets in both alignment with instructions and overall image coherence, enabling superior training and evaluation of instruction-based image editing models.

0965a1c7e2b64889ab7f9d69d42b465414378ab2.title: SPRINT: Enabling Interleaved Planning and Parallelized Execution in Reasoning Models
0965a1c7e2b64889ab7f9d69d42b465414378ab2.research_question: How can large reasoning models be enabled to dynamically identify and exploit opportunities for parallelization during complex reasoning tasks, thereby reducing inference latency without sacrificing accuracy across diverse domains?
0965a1c7e2b64889ab7f9d69d42b465414378ab2.hypothesis: Fine-tuning large reasoning models on curated datasets that explicitly structure reasoning trajectories into interleaved planning and parallel execution rounds will enable these models to autonomously identify independent subtasks and execute them concurrently, resulting in significant reductions in sequential inference time while maintaining or improving task accuracy.
0965a1c7e2b64889ab7f9d69d42b465414378ab2.proposed_method: A novel framework, SPRINT, will be developed to restructure the inference and training of large reasoning models. At inference time, the method introduces two distinct modules: a planner, which receives the cumulative context and generates sets of independent plans, and a pool of executors, which concurrently execute these plans. The process is organized into iterative rounds, where each round consists of planning, parallel execution, and synchronization of results. For training, a data curation pipeline will extract reasoning steps from existing model trajectories, decompose them into planning and execution phases, construct dependency graphs (DAGs), and pack steps into stages that maximize parallelization. Only trajectories with high parallelization potential will be used to fine-tune the model, teaching it to dynamically propose and execute parallelizable tasks based on context.
0965a1c7e2b64889ab7f9d69d42b465414378ab2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a curated dataset of approximately 1,700 samples derived from 6,000 reasoning trajectories generated on the MATH dataset, filtered for correctness and processed through the data curation pipeline. The primary evaluation will use the MATH-500 benchmark, with additional out-of-domain evaluations on GPQA-diamond (covering biology, physics, and chemistry) and Countdown (a synthetic arithmetic reasoning task). Baselines will include a base reasoning model (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B), a reasoning fine-tuned model (RFT), Skeleton-of-Thought (SoT), and repeated sampling with self-consistency. Evaluation metrics will include final answer accuracy and the number of sequential tokens generated, with sequential token count serving as a proxy for inference latency. Additional analysis will examine efficiency gains on longer reasoning trajectories and generalization to out-of-domain tasks.
0965a1c7e2b64889ab7f9d69d42b465414378ab2.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a generalizable post-training and inference-time framework that enables dynamic, context-driven parallelization of reasoning steps in large models, rather than relying on predefined or heuristic structures. The data curation pipeline is novel in its use of dependency-based staging and explicit plan/execution tagging to maximize parallelism during both training and inference. SPRINT is claimed to uniquely support adaptive search, model optimization, inference-time parallelism, and multi-step sequential reasoning within a unified framework. The method demonstrates state-of-the-art efficiency, achieving substantial reductions in sequential inference tokens (up to 39% on long trajectories) while matching or exceeding the accuracy of strong reasoning baselines, and generalizes effectively to out-of-domain tasks.

09879f7956dddc2a9328f5c1472feeb8402bcbcf.title: Density estimation using Real NVP
09879f7956dddc2a9328f5c1472feeb8402bcbcf.research_question: How can a generative probabilistic model be designed for high-dimensional continuous data that enables tractable and exact learning, sampling, inference, and evaluation, while also providing an interpretable latent space?
09879f7956dddc2a9328f5c1472feeb8402bcbcf.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by constructing a class of stably invertible, learnable, and expressive bijective transformations, it is possible to achieve efficient and exact log-likelihood computation, sampling, and inference for high-dimensional data, resulting in both high-quality generative modeling and interpretable latent representations.
09879f7956dddc2a9328f5c1472feeb8402bcbcf.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed based on real-valued non-volume preserving (real NVP) transformations, which are bijective mappings between data space and a latent space (typically Gaussian). The approach leverages a sequence of affine coupling layers, each updating a subset of variables conditioned on the others, ensuring invertibility and tractable computation of the Jacobian determinant. These coupling layers are implemented using deep convolutional neural networks for the scale and translation functions, and are composed in alternating patterns with spatial checkerboard and channel-wise masking to ensure all variables are transformed. A multi-scale architecture is employed, where at each scale, some variables are factored out and modeled as Gaussians, while the remaining variables undergo further transformation, reducing computational and memory costs. Batch normalization and residual connections are incorporated to stabilize and accelerate training, and the model is trained via maximum likelihood using the change of variable formula.
09879f7956dddc2a9328f5c1472feeb8402bcbcf.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four natural image datasets: CIFAR-10, ImageNet (32x32 and 64x64 downsampled), LSUN (bedroom, tower, church outdoor categories), and CelebA (64x64). The model will be trained using data augmentation (horizontal flips) and a logit transformation of pixel values to mitigate boundary effects. The multi-scale architecture will be implemented with deep convolutional residual networks in the coupling layers, and hyperparameters such as number of residual blocks and feature maps will be tuned per dataset. The prior in latent space will be an isotropic unit Gaussian. Baseline comparisons will include PixelRNN, ConvDRAW, and IAF-VAE, with evaluation metrics focusing on bits per dimension (log-likelihood) and qualitative assessment of generated samples. The experimental setup will also include latent space manipulations to assess the semantic structure of the learned representations.
09879f7956dddc2a9328f5c1472feeb8402bcbcf.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a class of invertible, expressive, and tractable transformations for density estimation, enabling exact and efficient log-likelihood computation, inference, and sampling in high-dimensional spaces. The multi-scale architecture and use of affine coupling layers with deep convolutional networks provide both flexibility and computational efficiency. The method achieves competitive generative modeling performance while offering interpretable and semantically meaningful latent spaces, bridging the gap between auto-regressive models, variational autoencoders, and GANs. Additionally, the approach allows for parallelized sampling and does not require fixed-form reconstruction losses, resulting in sharper generated samples.

09b2df29327a5d26b4fac7d155ce5de7b96e8245.title: Propagation of chaos: A review of models, methods and applications. I. Models and methods
09b2df29327a5d26b4fac7d155ce5de7b96e8245.research_question: How can the propagation of chaos phenomenon in large systems of interacting particles be rigorously modeled, analyzed, and proved across a range of stochastic particle systems, including mean-field and Boltzmann-type models, and what are the fundamental mathematical tools and methods for establishing such results?
09b2df29327a5d26b4fac7d155ce5de7b96e8245.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that for a broad class of exchangeable interacting particle systems, including McKean-Vlasov diffusions, mean-field jump processes, and Boltzmann models, the propagation of chaos can be rigorously established using a combination of probabilistic and analytical techniques, and that these results can be quantitatively characterized and extended to new domains beyond classical statistical physics.
09b2df29327a5d26b4fac7d155ce5de7b96e8245.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed to analyze large systems of interacting particles through the lens of exchangeable stochastic processes. The methodology will include the formalization of particle systems via generators and stochastic differential equations, with a focus on models such as McKean-Vlasov diffusions, mean-field jump processes, and Boltzmann-type interactions. Key mathematical tools will be employed, including coupling methods (such as synchronous and reflection coupling), compactness and martingale techniques, large deviation principles, and analysis in Wasserstein spaces. The approach will also involve the study of empirical measures, convergence of probability measures, and the use of entropy and concentration inequalities to obtain quantitative and uniform-in-time propagation of chaos results.
09b2df29327a5d26b4fac7d155ce5de7b96e8245.experiment_details: Theoretical experiments will be conducted by applying the developed methods to canonical models, including the McKean-Vlasov diffusion, mean-field jump processes, and various Boltzmann models (both parametric and classical collisional kinetic theory). The effectiveness of each method will be evaluated by deriving propagation of chaos results and comparing the rates and strengths of convergence under different assumptions and interaction mechanisms. Quantitative metrics such as Wasserstein distances, total variation, and relative entropy will be used to assess convergence and chaos propagation. Where applicable, the framework will be extended to recent applications in mathematical biology, social sciences, mean-field games, and data sciences, with models tailored to the specific constraints and randomness present in these domains.
09b2df29327a5d26b4fac7d155ce5de7b96e8245.novelty_claims: The proposed research aims to unify and extend the mathematical theory of propagation of chaos by systematically reviewing and developing both classical and modern methods for a wide variety of particle systems. Novel contributions include the integration of probabilistic and analytic tools for both old and new models, the introduction of quantitative and uniform-in-time chaos propagation techniques, and the adaptation of these methods to emerging applications outside traditional statistical physics. The framework is designed to be flexible and broadly applicable, providing new insights and tools for the rigorous analysis of large stochastic systems in diverse scientific fields.

0a1bf4740dc9f02c292d5489c5097cc8da7f4368.title: Unexpected Improvements to Expected Improvement for Bayesian Optimization
0a1bf4740dc9f02c292d5489c5097cc8da7f4368.research_question: How can the numerical optimization of improvement-based acquisition functions in Bayesian Optimization be made more robust and efficient, particularly as problem dimensionality, number of constraints, or number of observations increases?
0a1bf4740dc9f02c292d5489c5097cc8da7f4368.hypothesis: Reformulating improvement-based acquisition functions, such as Expected Improvement (EI) and its variants, in log-space and employing numerically stable smoothing approximations will mitigate issues of vanishing gradients and values, thereby enabling more effective gradient-based optimization and improving Bayesian Optimization performance across a wide range of problem settings.
0a1bf4740dc9f02c292d5489c5097cc8da7f4368.proposed_method: A new family of acquisition functions, termed LogEI, will be developed by transforming canonical improvement-based acquisition functions (such as EI, constrained EI, parallel EI, and Expected Hypervolume Improvement) into log-space. For analytic EI, a numerically stable log-transformation of the core function will be implemented, ensuring non-vanishing gradients throughout the domain. For Monte Carlo-based batch and multi-objective settings, smooth approximations (such as softplus and p-norm or fat-tailed non-linearities) will be used to replace discrete max and indicator operations, and all computations will be performed in log-space to ensure numerical stability. These reformulations will be extended to constrained and multi-objective cases, with careful attention to stable computation of log-probabilities and log-hypervolumes. The approach will be implemented in a modular fashion, allowing drop-in replacement of standard acquisition functions in existing Bayesian Optimization frameworks.
0a1bf4740dc9f02c292d5489c5097cc8da7f4368.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of benchmark problems, including single-objective, constrained, parallel, and multi-objective optimization tasks. Test functions will include the Ackley, Michalewicz, and Sum-of-Squares functions for varying dimensionalities, as well as real-world-inspired engineering design problems with black-box constraints, high-dimensional synthetic problems (e.g., Hartmann6 embedded in 100D, 100D rover trajectory, 103D SVM hyperparameter tuning), and multi-objective tasks such as DTLZ2 and cell network design. Baselines will include canonical EI, constrained EI, qEI, qEHVI, Max-Value Entropy Search (GIBBON), and Joint Entropy Search (JES). All methods will be implemented in BoTorch, using multi-start L-BFGS-B optimization with random or heuristic initializations. Evaluation metrics will include best observed objective value (regret), hypervolume for multi-objective tasks, and convergence speed. Multiple replicates will be run, and results will be reported as means with error bars.
0a1bf4740dc9f02c292d5489c5097cc8da7f4368.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled family of log-space acquisition functions that are mathematically equivalent or near-equivalent to their canonical counterparts but are substantially easier to optimize numerically. The method systematically addresses and remedies the issue of vanishing gradients and values in improvement-based acquisition functions, a pervasive but underappreciated problem in the literature. The approach generalizes across analytic, constrained, batch, and multi-objective settings, and enables effective joint batch optimization that is competitive with or superior to sequential greedy strategies. The reformulations do not incur meaningful additional computational cost and reduce dependence on brittle initialization heuristics, offering robust and scalable improvements for Bayesian Optimization.

0a20bfad9cd5f800c2f64c9feb5457f074059c98.title: Valid Conformal Prediction for Dynamic GNNs
0a20bfad9cd5f800c2f64c9feb5457f074059c98.research_question: How can valid uncertainty quantification be achieved for predictions made by graph neural networks on dynamic graphs, particularly in settings where standard assumptions such as exchangeability do not hold?
0a20bfad9cd5f800c2f64c9feb5457f074059c98.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that representing dynamic graphs using a dilated unfolding of their tensor structure, and applying standard GNNs to this representation, enables the construction of valid conformal prediction sets across various inference regimes, including those lacking exchangeability, and improves predictive accuracy and uncertainty quantification compared to existing approaches.
0a20bfad9cd5f800c2f64c9feb5457f074059c98.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a dynamic graph representation based on the dilated unfolding of the tensor of adjacency matrices, concatenating node-time pairs and global nodes into a single, symmetric adjacency matrix. This unfolded representation is compatible with any standard GNN architecture, requiring no architectural modifications. Node and node-time pair attributes are concatenated accordingly, and the GNN is trained on this representation to produce embeddings for each node-time pair. Conformal prediction is then performed using adaptive non-conformity scores, such as those from the Adaptive Prediction Sets (APS) algorithm, to construct prediction sets with guaranteed coverage. The method is designed to be modular, allowing independent selection and optimization of the GNN and conformal prediction modules, and is theoretically analyzed for validity in transductive, temporal transductive, and semi-inductive regimes, with specific attention to the assumptions required in each scenario.
0a20bfad9cd5f800c2f64c9feb5457f074059c98.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both simulated and real-world dynamic graph datasets, including a dynamic stochastic block model (SBM), a primary school social contact network, the OpenSky flight network, and an agricultural trade network. Each dataset will be evaluated under transductive and semi-inductive regimes, using standard GNNs (GCN and GAT) applied to both the unfolded and block-diagonal representations. Prediction sets will be computed using the APS algorithm, and performance will be measured in terms of accuracy, coverage (targeted at ≥0.9), and prediction set size. Multiple random splits and permutations of calibration and test sets will be used to ensure robust evaluation, with results averaged over thousands of conformal inference instances per model and dataset. Baseline comparisons will include block-diagonal GNNs and existing conformal prediction routines.
0a20bfad9cd5f800c2f64c9feb5457f074059c98.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the use of tensor unfoldings for dynamic graph representation in supervised GNN-based prediction tasks, enabling valid conformal prediction in both transductive and semi-inductive regimes. This approach is claimed to be the first to apply unfoldings to conformal inference on dynamic graphs, providing a modular interface between GNNs and conformal prediction that allows for independent optimization. The method is shown to achieve valid coverage with smaller prediction sets and improved accuracy compared to block-diagonal baselines, especially in challenging semi-inductive settings. Theoretical contributions include a careful analysis of the assumptions required for validity in different inference regimes, and empirical results demonstrate the method's robustness and practical advantages.

0a2814fafd99b105e7f5633487284840ce2e4ec2.title: Homotopy Relaxation Training Algorithms for Infinite-Width Two-Layer ReLU Neural Networks
0a2814fafd99b105e7f5633487284840ce2e4ec2.research_question: How can the training efficiency and convergence speed of infinite-width two-layer ReLU neural networks be improved by modifying the activation function during training?
0a2814fafd99b105e7f5633487284840ce2e4ec2.hypothesis: Introducing a homotopy-based relaxation of the activation function, transitioning from linear to ReLU and beyond, will increase the smallest eigenvalue of the training kernel, thereby accelerating convergence and improving training efficiency for infinite-width two-layer neural networks.
0a2814fafd99b105e7f5633487284840ce2e4ec2.proposed_method: A novel training algorithm, termed the Homotopy Relaxation Training Algorithm (HRTA), is proposed for infinite-width two-layer neural networks. The method constructs a homotopy activation function that interpolates between the identity (linear) activation and the ReLU activation, parameterized by a homotopy parameter s. Training is performed in stages, each corresponding to a different value of s, starting from s=0 (linear) and gradually increasing to s=1 (ReLU), with the possibility of over-relaxation (s>1 up to s=2) to further enhance convergence. At each stage, the neural network is trained using gradient descent on the current homotopy-parameterized activation, and the parameters from the previous stage are used to initialize the next. The approach leverages the evolving energy landscape induced by the changing activation function to avoid poor local minima and accelerate loss decay.
0a2814fafd99b105e7f5633487284840ce2e4ec2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on supervised learning tasks and the numerical solution of partial differential equations using two-layer neural networks. The experimental setup will include networks of varying widths, with a focus on large-width (infinite-width) regimes. The proposed HRTA will be compared against traditional training methods such as standard gradient descent and Adam using fixed ReLU activations. Evaluation metrics will include convergence speed (measured by loss decay rate), final training loss, and possibly generalization error. Datasets will be sampled from high-dimensional functions defined on [0,1]^d, with input samples drawn i.i.d. from a uniform distribution. Theoretical analysis will be validated by empirical results, particularly in the regime of large network width.
0a2814fafd99b105e7f5633487284840ce2e4ec2.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a homotopy relaxation framework for neural network training that allows the activation function to evolve continuously from linear to ReLU and beyond, rather than fixing it throughout training. This method is claimed to increase the smallest eigenvalue of the training kernel, leading to provably faster convergence rates. The relaxation of the homotopy parameter beyond the standard [0,1] interval is a novel contribution, enabling further acceleration of training. The approach is generalizable to other activation functions and potentially to deeper network architectures. Theoretical analysis is provided to support the convergence claims, and empirical results validate the effectiveness of the method.

0a29c21484fa1fe4722bd76ab075840580ba2abe.title: Realizable H-Consistent and Bayes-Consistent Loss Functions for Learning to Defer
0a29c21484fa1fe4722bd76ab075840580ba2abe.research_question: What surrogate loss functions can be developed for learning to defer that simultaneously achieve strong theoretical guarantees, such as Bayes-consistency, realizable H-consistency, and H-consistency bounds, and how do these losses perform empirically compared to existing baselines across various cost functions and hypothesis sets?
0a29c21484fa1fe4722bd76ab075840580ba2abe.hypothesis: A broad family of surrogate loss functions parameterized by a non-increasing function Ψ can be constructed for learning to defer, and under mild conditions on Ψ and the hypothesis set, these losses will achieve Bayes-consistency, realizable H-consistency, and H-consistency bounds, outperforming or matching existing surrogate losses in both theoretical guarantees and empirical performance.
0a29c21484fa1fe4722bd76ab075840580ba2abe.proposed_method: A new family of surrogate loss functions for learning to defer will be constructed, parameterized by a non-increasing function Ψ. The method involves deriving loss functions from first principles by replacing indicator functions in the deferral loss with smooth surrogate losses, specifically using comp-sum losses and their variants. The surrogate loss for each instance will be a convex combination of a standard comp-sum loss and a modified comp-sum loss that incorporates the deferral option, weighted by the instance-specific deferral cost. Theoretical analysis will establish conditions under which these losses are Bayes-consistent, realizable H-consistent, and admit H-consistency bounds, with special attention to the properties of the hypothesis set (such as symmetry and completeness). The approach will also generalize to arbitrary cost functions by appropriate choices of Ψ, such as the mean absolute error loss.
0a29c21484fa1fe4722bd76ab075840580ba2abe.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three real-world datasets: CIFAR-10H, HateSpeech, and COMPASS. Each dataset will be split into training, validation, and test sets using a 70/10/20 split. The model class will match that used in prior work for comparability. The cost function will primarily be the expert's classification error, but general cost functions will also be considered. The proposed surrogate losses will be compared against four established baselines: the cross-entropy surrogate, the one-vs-all surrogate, and other recent consistent surrogates. Evaluation metrics will include deferral loss and standard classification accuracy, with results reported on held-out test data. Experimental protocols will ensure fair comparison by using identical data splits and model architectures.
0a29c21484fa1fe4722bd76ab075840580ba2abe.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified and flexible family of surrogate loss functions for learning to defer that, for the first time, simultaneously achieve Bayes-consistency, realizable H-consistency, and H-consistency bounds under mild and practical conditions. The approach resolves an open question regarding the Bayes-consistency of a previously proposed surrogate loss and extends consistency guarantees to general cost functions, not just classification error. The theoretical analysis establishes new relationships between different consistency notions in the learning-to-defer setting, and the empirical evaluation demonstrates the practical effectiveness of the new surrogates compared to existing methods.

0a2f2836285b7c035eb9131508c11f1534642662.title: Towards Understanding and Improving GFlowNet Training
0a2f2836285b7c035eb9131508c11f1534642662.research_question: How can the training and generalization capabilities of Generative Flow Networks (GFlowNets) be improved to better match target reward distributions, particularly in high-dimensional discrete spaces with compositional reward functions?
0a2f2836285b7c035eb9131508c11f1534642662.hypothesis: Modifying GFlowNet training through prioritized replay of high-reward samples, relative edge flow policy parametrization, and guided trajectory balance objectives will improve sample efficiency, credit assignment to important substructures, and convergence to the target distribution, especially in tasks with compositional rewards.
0a2f2836285b7c035eb9131508c11f1534642662.proposed_method: The proposed approach involves three main innovations to enhance GFlowNet training. First, prioritized replay training (PRT) is introduced, where training batches are constructed to include a higher proportion of high-reward samples, thereby focusing learning on more informative data points. Second, a relative edge flow policy parametrization (SSR) is developed, where a neural network models the transition probabilities based on both parent and child states, allowing the model to generalize action preferences more flexibly across the state space. Third, a guided trajectory balance (GTB) objective is proposed, which uses a dynamically updated guide distribution to assign credit preferentially to trajectories passing through empirically important substructures, thus addressing the substructure credit assignment problem inherent in compositional reward settings. The GTB objective is implemented in a two-phase optimization: first, a backward policy is trained to approximate the guide, and then the forward policy is trained using trajectory balance with this fixed backward policy.
0a2f2836285b7c035eb9131508c11f1534642662.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of discrete generative tasks with enumerable state spaces, including multiset (Bag), DNA sequence design (SIX6, PHO4), and molecular graph generation (QM9, sEH). Each task uses either real-world or proxy reward functions, some with compositional structure. Baselines include standard trajectory balance (TB) and maximum entropy (MaxEnt) GFlowNets. The proposed methods (PRT, SSR, GTB with substructure guidance) are evaluated individually and in combination. Evaluation metrics include the Anderson-Darling statistic for goodness-of-fit between sampled and target reward distributions, convergence of sampled mean reward to the target mean, sample efficiency (number of rounds to reach target mean), mode discovery, and diversity (e.g., Tanimoto diversity for molecules). Training curves and ablation studies are used to assess the impact of each proposed modification.
0a2f2836285b7c035eb9131508c11f1534642662.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first guided trajectory balance objective for GFlowNets, enabling flexible and targeted credit assignment to important substructures, which addresses a previously unaddressed substructure credit assignment problem. The use of relative edge flow parametrization allows for more expressive and generalizable policy representations. Prioritized replay training is adapted to the GFlowNet setting to improve sample efficiency. Together, these innovations are claimed to substantially improve GFlowNet training, sample efficiency, and convergence on challenging biochemical and combinatorial design tasks, with up to 10-fold improvements in some settings. The work also establishes a new framework for evaluating and understanding the impact of flow distribution and generalization in GFlowNet training.

0a646808002d3a629c60330178cb5b85fa6c77dd.title: Thinking in Character: Advancing Role-Playing Agents with Role-Aware Reasoning
0a646808002d3a629c60330178cb5b85fa6c77dd.research_question: How can large language models be enhanced to generate deep, character-consistent internal reasoning processes for role-playing agents, thereby improving the depth, consistency, and believability of their role-play in dialogue and social interaction tasks?
0a646808002d3a629c60330178cb5b85fa6c77dd.hypothesis: Incorporating explicit role identity activation and dynamic reasoning style optimization into large language models will significantly improve the ability of role-playing agents to maintain character consistency, prevent attention diversion, and adapt reasoning styles to context, resulting in more believable and effective character portrayals.
0a646808002d3a629c60330178cb5b85fa6c77dd.proposed_method: A novel Role-Aware Reasoning (RAR) framework will be developed for large language models, consisting of two key modules: Role Identity Activation (RIA) and Reasoning Style Optimization (RSO). RIA will continuously inject character-specific constraints—such as personality, emotions, experiences, standpoints, and motivations—into the model's reasoning process by generating explicit, rule-like prompts from character profiles. This ensures the model maintains a strong awareness of its assigned role throughout multi-turn dialogues and complex reasoning. RSO will enable the model to dynamically adapt its internal reasoning style to match both the character and the current dialogue context. This will be achieved by constructing positive and negative training pairs using system prompts that enforce either fact-based or character-knowledge-based reasoning styles, and optimizing the model via contrastive learning to prefer contextually appropriate styles. The overall approach will distill reasoning capabilities from large reasoning models into more efficient LLMs, ensuring both logical rigor and vivid, in-character thought processes.
0a646808002d3a629c60330178cb5b85fa6c77dd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the LLaMA-3-8B model as the base, with all models quantized to 4-bit precision and trained using LoRA adapters. The primary training dataset will be RoleBench-Train, derived from scripts of 940 films and TV shows, providing 137,920 high-quality role-playing samples with detailed character profiles. Evaluation will be performed on two public benchmarks: SocialBench, which assesses social intelligence across multiple dimensions (e.g., role knowledge, style, emotion detection, memory), and CharacterBench, which evaluates persona consistency, memory, fact accuracy, emotional regulation, and engagement using both automated and human-annotated metrics. Baselines will include vanilla supervised fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation, distillation from large reasoning models, various reasoning strategies (e.g., ZeroThink, MoreThink), and specialized role-playing models such as Neeko and CharacterGLM. Ablation studies will isolate the effects of RIA and RSO. Additional analyses will include reasoning trace quality (coherence, relevance, effectiveness, conciseness), t-SNE visualization of hidden states for style adaptation, and case studies for qualitative assessment.
0a646808002d3a629c60330178cb5b85fa6c77dd.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first explicit framework for role-aware reasoning in large language models, combining continuous role identity activation with dynamic, context-sensitive reasoning style optimization. This approach uniquely addresses the dual challenges of attention diversion and style drift in role-playing agents, enabling deep, human-like internal thought processes that are both logically sound and character-consistent. The method leverages contrastive learning on positive and negative style-context pairs and distills advanced reasoning capabilities from large reasoning models into more efficient LLMs. Extensive benchmarking and ablation studies are planned to demonstrate significant improvements over state-of-the-art baselines in both persona consistency and social intelligence.

0a67ab901a541a1445c6814d0241715454619b15.title: Rethinking Benign Overfitting in Two-Layer Neural Networks
0a67ab901a541a1445c6814d0241715454619b15.research_question: How can the phenomenon of benign overfitting in overparameterized two-layer neural networks be theoretically explained, particularly in the presence of heterogeneous, class-dependent noise as commonly found in long-tailed data distributions?
0a67ab901a541a1445c6814d0241715454619b15.hypothesis: Incorporating class-dependent heterogeneous noise into the feature-noise data model will reveal that overparameterized neural networks can leverage data noise to learn implicit features, thereby improving generalization and classification accuracy for long-tailed data, contrary to predictions made by models assuming homogeneous noise.
0a67ab901a541a1445c6814d0241715454619b15.proposed_method: A refined feature-noise data model will be developed by introducing class-dependent, heterogeneous noise patches in the data generation process. Theoretical analysis will be conducted on the training dynamics of two-layer ReLU convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained via gradient descent, focusing on both explicit feature learning and implicit feature learning from class-dependent noise. The method will derive test loss bounds and characterize phase transitions between benign and harmful overfitting, utilizing singular value and covariance analyses to address the randomness of noise activation. Additionally, a training-free metric based on the covariance structure of class distributions will be proposed to evaluate the influence of individual data points on test performance.
0a67ab901a541a1445c6814d0241715454619b15.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets, including MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100. Synthetic datasets will be generated according to the proposed heterogeneous feature-noise model, with controlled variations in feature strength, noise correlation ratios, and class sample sizes. Baselines will include models trained under homogeneous noise assumptions and standard overparameterized neural networks. Evaluation metrics will focus on test accuracy, particularly for long-tailed and atypical data, as well as the impact of removing high- and low-influence samples as measured by the proposed training-free metric. The experimental setup will involve training two-layer CNNs with fixed neuron counts and learning rates, and analyzing the effects of dataset composition and noise structure on generalization.
0a67ab901a541a1445c6814d0241715454619b15.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a generalized feature-noise data model that accounts for class-dependent, heterogeneous noise, extending beyond prior work limited to homogeneous noise. It provides the first theoretical explanation for why memorization of long-tailed, atypical data can enhance generalization in overparameterized neural networks. The approach establishes new phase transition results for benign versus harmful overfitting in the context of heterogeneous noise, and offers a simple, training-free metric for quantifying data influence on test performance. These contributions bridge the gap between empirical observations and existing theory, and offer practical tools for data selection and evaluation.

0ad5a074865cfdcf49ef19958c2dc53cf12d64b0.title: Standardizing Structural Causal Models
0ad5a074865cfdcf49ef19958c2dc53cf12d64b0.research_question: How can synthetic datasets generated by structural causal models (SCMs) be improved to avoid artifacts that bias the benchmarking of causal structure learning algorithms, and what are the theoretical and empirical implications of such improvements for causal discovery and identifiability?
0ad5a074865cfdcf49ef19958c2dc53cf12d64b0.hypothesis: Introducing internal standardization into the generative process of SCMs will remove exploitable covariance and variance artifacts, leading to more reliable benchmarking of causal discovery algorithms and preventing partial identifiability and degeneracy present in post-hoc standardized SCMs.
0ad5a074865cfdcf49ef19958c2dc53cf12d64b0.proposed_method: A novel class of internally-standardized structural causal models (iSCMs) is proposed, in which a standardization operation (z-score normalization) is applied to each variable during the generative process rather than post-hoc. The generative process involves, for each variable, computing its value as a function of the standardized values of its parents and additive noise, followed by standardizing the result to have zero mean and unit variance. This ensures that all observed variables are unit-less and the scale of the causal mechanism and noise is consistent throughout the system, independent of the variable's position in the causal ordering. Theoretical analysis will focus on linear iSCMs with additive Gaussian noise, deriving properties such as bounded cause-explained variance and non-degeneracy with increasing graph depth. Identifiability results will be established by comparing the observational distributions of iSCMs and post-hoc standardized SCMs, particularly in the context of Markov equivalence classes and forest DAGs.
0ad5a074865cfdcf49ef19958c2dc53cf12d64b0.experiment_details: Experiments will generate synthetic datasets using both standard SCMs, post-hoc standardized SCMs, and iSCMs across a variety of random graph structures (e.g., Erdős-Rényi and scale-free graphs) and weight distributions. The evaluation will employ popular causal structure learning algorithms, including NOTEARS, GOLEM, CAM, PC, GES, and AVICI, as well as baseline methods exploiting variance and R2 artifacts (Var-SORTNREGRESS, R2-SORTNREGRESS). Datasets will be assessed for the presence of variance and R2-sortability artifacts, and structure learning performance will be measured using F1 scores and structural Hamming distance. The identifiability of causal graphs from observational data will be empirically tested, and the noise statistics of the implied SCMs will be analyzed to understand their impact on algorithm performance. Experiments will be repeated across different system sizes, noise distributions, and weight ranges to ensure robustness of findings.
0ad5a074865cfdcf49ef19958c2dc53cf12d64b0.novelty_claims: The proposed iSCM framework is the first general method for generating synthetic causal data that eliminates both variance and correlation artifacts without restricting the strength or nature of causal dependencies. Theoretical results provide, for the first time, partial identifiability results for post-hoc standardized linear SCMs and demonstrate that iSCMs avoid degeneracy and partial identifiability even under strong prior knowledge of weight distributions. Empirical findings show that iSCMs produce artifact-free datasets, enabling fairer benchmarking of causal discovery algorithms and disentangling the effects of data artifacts from algorithmic performance. Additionally, iSCMs offer a stable, scale-free modeling approach that is invariant to units and may be useful for modeling large, temporal, or physical systems beyond benchmarking.

0ad90df9d692dfb040a9aa6dab1e6065de0cae4a.title: Provably Bounding Neural Network Preimages
0ad90df9d692dfb040a9aa6dab1e6065de0cae4a.research_question: How can the set of neural network inputs that provably lead to a specified set of outputs, defined by linear constraints, be tightly and efficiently over-approximated, enabling formal guarantees for safety, robustness, and out-of-distribution detection in neural network-driven systems?
0ad90df9d692dfb040a9aa6dab1e6065de0cae4a.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a generalized bound propagation framework, which incorporates output constraints into the tightening of intermediate neural network bounds and leverages efficient GPU-accelerated algorithms without requiring linear programming solvers, can yield significantly tighter and faster over-approximations of neural network preimages than existing methods.
0ad90df9d692dfb040a9aa6dab1e6065de0cae4a.proposed_method: A novel algorithm, INVPROP, will be developed to compute convex over-approximations of neural network preimages corresponding to linearly constrained output sets. The approach formulates the inverse verification problem as a constrained optimization, first encoding it as a Mixed Integer Linear Program (MILP), then relaxing to a Linear Program (LP), and finally deriving a highly structured Lagrangian dual that enables efficient bound propagation. The method iteratively tightens bounds on all intermediate neurons by leveraging both input and output constraints, propagating these bounds through the network in multiple passes to achieve high precision. The algorithm is designed to be GPU-accelerated and implemented using standard deep learning frameworks, supporting further refinement via input-space branching and integration with existing verification tools such as α,β-CROWN.
0ad90df9d692dfb040a9aa6dab1e6065de0cae4a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several benchmarks, including backward reachability analysis for neural feedback loops (e.g., Double Integrator and 6D Quadrotor control systems), adversarial robustness verification on MNIST classifiers and the large-scale YOLO object detector from VNN-COMP'23, and out-of-distribution (OOD) detection using neural classifiers with abstention logits. Datasets will include standard control benchmarks, MNIST, and YOLO, with evaluation metrics such as approximation ratio (volume of over-approximation divided by true preimage volume), number of verified properties, and runtime. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art methods such as ReBreach-LP, DeepSRGR, and α,β-CROWN, with experiments measuring both tightness and computational efficiency, including scalability to large networks (up to 167k neurons) and high-dimensional inputs.
0ad90df9d692dfb040a9aa6dab1e6065de0cae4a.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first efficient, GPU-accelerated bound propagation framework for inverse neural network verification that directly incorporates output constraints into the tightening of intermediate bounds. Unlike prior approaches, the method does not require LP solvers, supports iterative refinement across all network layers, and generalizes existing forward verification frameworks. The approach enables orders-of-magnitude tighter preimage over-approximations and faster runtimes on challenging benchmarks, scales to large and high-dimensional networks, and unifies forward and inverse verification under a single framework. Integration with α,β-CROWN extends its capabilities, resulting in the verification of more properties and improved performance on standard benchmarks.

0ae247216ef2ca38aff6015d7b900e8f156c0201.title: Enhancing Zeroth-order Fine-tuning for Language Models with Low-rank Structures
0ae247216ef2ca38aff6015d7b900e8f156c0201.research_question: How can memory-efficient zeroth-order fine-tuning methods for large language models be improved to better capture the low-rank structure of gradients and achieve performance comparable to first-order optimization, while maintaining low memory overhead?
0ae247216ef2ca38aff6015d7b900e8f156c0201.hypothesis: Incorporating a low-rank structure into zeroth-order gradient estimators will enable more accurate approximation of true gradients in large language model fine-tuning, resulting in improved empirical performance and memory efficiency compared to existing zeroth-order methods.
0ae247216ef2ca38aff6015d7b900e8f156c0201.proposed_method: A novel low-rank zeroth-order gradient estimator (LGE) will be developed, where the gradient is approximated using finite differences along low-rank directions defined by random matrices U and V, sampled from standard normal distributions with rank r much smaller than the parameter dimensions. The update rule will use these low-rank perturbations to ensure that the estimated gradient remains low-rank, closely matching the structure of true first-order gradients in language model fine-tuning. A lazy sampling strategy will be employed, where one of the low-rank matrices (V) is resampled only every ν iterations, allowing the optimizer to explore a fixed low-rank subspace for several steps and preventing abrupt parameter changes. The method will be extended to support momentum (LOZO-M), where momentum is accumulated in the low-rank space, incurring negligible additional memory overhead. Theoretical convergence guarantees will be established by framing the approach as a zeroth-order subspace optimization method.
0ae247216ef2ca38aff6015d7b900e8f156c0201.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of large language models, including RoBERTa-large and OPT models (13B, 30B, 66B parameters), across multiple downstream tasks such as classification, multiple-choice, and generation, using benchmarks like SuperGLUE. Baselines will include existing zeroth-order methods (MeZO, MeZO-LoRA), full fine-tuning (FT), LoRA, zero-shot, and in-context learning (ICL) approaches. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy and memory usage, with results averaged over multiple random seeds for robustness. Hyperparameters such as the low-rank dimension r and the lazy sampling interval ν will be tuned, and memory consumption will be measured during training to assess efficiency. Convergence speed and loss curves will also be analyzed to compare optimization dynamics.
0ae247216ef2ca38aff6015d7b900e8f156c0201.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first low-rank matrix-wise zeroth-order gradient estimator tailored for large language model fine-tuning, enabling the gradient approximation to retain the low-rank structure observed in true gradients. The lazy sampling strategy for subspace exploration is novel in the context of zeroth-order optimization, improving both stability and performance. The momentum extension (LOZO-M) is designed to maintain memory efficiency, overcoming the typical overhead associated with momentum in zeroth-order methods. Theoretical convergence guarantees are provided by interpreting the method as a zeroth-order subspace optimization algorithm. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior performance and memory efficiency compared to state-of-the-art zeroth-order baselines, and to approach the accuracy of first-order fine-tuning.

0af4359948693c7aa60caf5e13aaab9d32fced92.title: R1-VL: Learning to Reason with Multimodal Large Language Models via Step-wise Group Relative Policy Optimization
0af4359948693c7aa60caf5e13aaab9d32fced92.research_question: How can the reasoning capabilities of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) be enhanced to move beyond passive imitation of successful reasoning paths, particularly in complex, step-by-step reasoning tasks involving both visual and textual modalities?
0af4359948693c7aa60caf5e13aaab9d32fced92.hypothesis: Introducing dense, step-wise, rule-based reward mechanisms into the reinforcement learning process will enable MLLMs to self-improve their reasoning abilities, resulting in more accurate, structured, and logically consistent reasoning trajectories compared to models trained with only outcome-level rewards or supervised fine-tuning.
0af4359948693c7aa60caf5e13aaab9d32fced92.proposed_method: A novel online reinforcement learning framework, Step-wise Group Relative Policy Optimization (StepGRPO), will be developed to address the sparse reward issue in MLLM reasoning. The method consists of two phases: (1) a policy warm-up phase using supervised fine-tuning on multimodal chain-of-thought (CoT) data to provide basic reasoning ability, and (2) a step-wise online policy optimization phase where the model generates multiple reasoning paths per question and receives dense, step-wise rewards. Two rule-based reward mechanisms are introduced: Step-wise Reasoning Accuracy Reward (StepRAR), which uses soft key-step matching to reward reasoning paths containing essential intermediate steps, and Step-wise Reasoning Validity Reward (StepRVR), which evaluates reasoning completeness and logical structure. The overall reward for each path is a combination of these two, and group relative advantage is estimated for policy optimization using KL-regularized loss.
0af4359948693c7aa60caf5e13aaab9d32fced92.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using Qwen2-VL-7B as the base MLLM, with Mulberry-260k as the primary dataset for supervised warm-up and 10,000 samples from Mulberry-260k for online RL training. Evaluation will be performed on eight multimodal reasoning benchmarks: MathVista, MMStar, Math-Vision, ChartQA, DynaMath, HallusionBench, MathVerse, MME, and MMReason, covering mathematical reasoning, chart understanding, visual hallucination, and general visual understanding. Baselines will include both open-source and closed-source MLLMs, as well as models trained with outcome-level rewards and supervised fine-tuning. Main evaluation metrics will be accuracy and benchmark-specific scores. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of each reward mechanism and the number of generated reasoning paths per question.
0af4359948693c7aa60caf5e13aaab9d32fced92.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new reinforcement learning framework (StepGRPO) for MLLMs that provides dense, step-wise, rule-based rewards without requiring process reward models, thus reducing computational overhead and improving training stability. The method is the first to combine soft key-step matching for intermediate reasoning steps and logical structure evaluation for multimodal reasoning. StepGRPO is claimed to effectively mitigate the sparse reward problem, leading to more robust, interpretable, and accurate step-by-step reasoning in MLLMs, as demonstrated by superior performance across multiple challenging benchmarks.

0b0debb710366cdff461938c80763eace1651af6.title: Code Llama: Open Foundation Models for Code
0b0debb710366cdff461938c80763eace1651af6.research_question: How can large language models be effectively specialized and scaled for code generation, infilling, and instruction-following tasks across multiple programming languages and long input contexts?
0b0debb710366cdff461938c80763eace1651af6.hypothesis: Specializing large language models through code-focused pretraining, infilling objectives, long-context adaptation, and instruction fine-tuning will yield state-of-the-art performance on code generation and infilling benchmarks, while maintaining strong multilingual and instruction-following capabilities.
0b0debb710366cdff461938c80763eace1651af6.proposed_method: A family of large language models will be developed by initializing from a strong general-purpose language model and applying a cascade of specialization steps. The first step involves further pretraining on a near-deduplicated, code-heavy dataset (500B–1T tokens), with a small proportion of natural language and code-related natural language to retain general language understanding. For select model sizes, a multitask infilling objective will be used, employing causal masking and special tokenization schemes to enable fill-in-the-middle capabilities. Long-context fine-tuning will be performed by increasing the maximum sequence length (up to 16,384 tokens during training and extrapolating to 100,000 tokens at inference) and modifying rotary positional embeddings to support longer contexts. Instruction-following variants will be created by further fine-tuning on a mix of proprietary human-annotated instruction data, machine-generated self-instruct datasets (including question-test-solution triplets), and a small rehearsal proportion of code and natural language data to preserve general capabilities.
0b0debb710366cdff461938c80763eace1651af6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of code generation and infilling benchmarks, including HumanEval, MBPP, APPS, and MultiPL-E, covering Python and multiple other programming languages (C++, Java, PHP, TypeScript, C#, Bash). Models of various sizes (7B, 13B, 34B, 70B parameters) and specializations (general, Python-focused, instruction-tuned) will be evaluated. Baselines will include Llama 2, StarCoder, Codex, CodeGen, and other state-of-the-art open and proprietary models. Evaluation metrics will primarily be pass@k (k=1,10,100) for code generation, exact match for infilling, and perplexity for long-context handling. Both zero-shot and few-shot settings will be used, and ablation studies will assess the impact of each specialization stage (e.g., infilling, long-context fine-tuning, instruction tuning).
0b0debb710366cdff461938c80763eace1651af6.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a comprehensive pipeline for specializing large language models for code, including support for infilling, long input contexts up to 100,000 tokens, and robust instruction-following. It provides the first open models to combine state-of-the-art code generation, infilling, and multilingual capabilities at scale, outperforming all other publicly available models on major code benchmarks. The method also demonstrates that smaller, specialized models can match or exceed the performance of much larger general-purpose models, and that instruction fine-tuning with machine-generated self-instruct data can significantly improve safety and helpfulness without major losses in code generation performance. All models and code are released under a permissive license, facilitating both research and commercial use.

0b1b08ddde3093c4b26d4d0ef0599754f2602fd4.title: Wasserstein Quantum Monte Carlo: A Novel Approach for Solving the Quantum Many-Body Schrödinger Equation
0b1b08ddde3093c4b26d4d0ef0599754f2602fd4.research_question: How can the optimization of ground-state solutions to the quantum many-body Schrödinger equation be improved by reformulating the energy minimization process in the space of probability distributions, and by employing alternative geometric metrics beyond the traditional Fisher–Rao metric?
0b1b08ddde3093c4b26d4d0ef0599754f2602fd4.hypothesis: Employing the Wasserstein metric to define the gradient flow in the space of Born probability distributions will result in faster and more stable convergence to the ground state of quantum many-body systems compared to conventional approaches based on the Fisher–Rao metric.
0b1b08ddde3093c4b26d4d0ef0599754f2602fd4.proposed_method: The proposed approach reformulates the energy minimization problem for the quantum many-body Schrödinger equation as a gradient flow in the space of Born probability distributions, which are constrained to be (anti-)symmetric under particle permutations. Instead of the Fisher–Rao metric, the method introduces the Wasserstein metric (or a general c-Wasserstein metric) to define the gradient flow, resulting in a density evolution governed by optimal transport principles. At each iteration, the non-parametric density evolution is projected onto a parametric manifold defined by a deep neural network ansatz for the wavefunction, using a Kullback-Leibler divergence minimization step. The parameter updates are computed by taking the inner product between the projected gradient flow and the score function of the parametric model, and are preconditioned using the Fisher information matrix (with K-FAC approximation) to exploit the geometry of the parameter space. Practical enhancements include the use of coordinate-wise tanh nonlinearity on gradients and robust sample selection to stabilize optimization.
0b1b08ddde3093c4b26d4d0ef0599754f2602fd4.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on electronic structure problems for several molecular systems (Be, B, Li2, and H10) under the Born–Oppenheimer approximation, where the wavefunction is parameterized by a deep neural network architecture ('psiformer') incorporating Slater determinants for fermionic antisymmetry. The proposed Wasserstein Quantum Monte Carlo (WQMC) method is compared against the baseline Quantum Variational Monte Carlo (QVMC) using identical architectures and hyperparameters. Evaluation metrics include the relative error of the estimated ground-state energy, the variance of the local energy, and the median gradient norm of the local energy, with convergence monitored over 10,000–20,000 optimization steps. Monte Carlo sampling is used for configuration generation, and optimization is performed using natural gradient descent with K-FAC preconditioning. Additional stabilization techniques such as gradient clipping and sample filtering are applied.
0b1b08ddde3093c4b26d4d0ef0599754f2602fd4.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new theoretical and algorithmic framework for quantum Monte Carlo optimization by recasting energy minimization as a gradient flow in the space of Born distributions under the Wasserstein metric, rather than the conventional Fisher–Rao metric. This results in a principled method that regularizes the evolution of probability densities, forbidding non-local mass teleportation and promoting local, physically meaningful updates. The approach is claimed to yield significantly faster and more stable convergence to the ground state in quantum chemistry benchmarks, and provides a generalizable perspective that can be extended to other generative modeling tasks by altering the objective functional.

0b4f027cd01e52f8cc63d2e59e87d4792261f497.title: Flexible Tails for Normalising Flows, with Application to the Modelling of Financial Return Data
0b4f027cd01e52f8cc63d2e59e87d4792261f497.research_question: How can normalizing flows be enhanced to more accurately model heavy-tailed distributions, particularly for applications such as financial return data where extreme events are critical?
0b4f027cd01e52f8cc63d2e59e87d4792261f497.hypothesis: Introducing a flexible, non-Lipschitz tail transformation as the final layer in a normalizing flow, motivated by extreme value theory, will enable the model to capture a wider range of tail behaviors—including heavy and asymmetric tails—thereby improving fit and synthetic data generation for heavy-tailed distributions compared to existing approaches that rely on heavy-tailed base distributions.
0b4f027cd01e52f8cc63d2e59e87d4792261f497.proposed_method: A novel transformation is developed to modify the tail properties of a distribution, inspired by extreme value theory and the generalized Pareto distribution (GPD). This transformation is parameterized to allow separate control over the upper and lower tail weights, enabling the modeling of asymmetric and tunable heavy tails. The transformation is designed to be the final layer in a normalizing flow with a standard Gaussian base distribution, and can be implemented as either a multivariate (autoregressive) or marginal (component-wise) transformation. The method also supports an extension to allow lighter-than-GPD tails via a smooth power transformation, ensuring flexibility across a range of tail behaviors. Efficient computation of the transformation, its inverse, and derivatives is ensured through the use of special functions (e.g., complementary error function), and the transformation is integrated with standard flow architectures (e.g., rational quadratic spline layers and trainable linear layers).
0b4f027cd01e52f8cc63d2e59e87d4792261f497.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on high-dimensional financial return data derived from the daily closing prices of the top traded S&P 500 stocks, converted to log returns and treated as independent observations. The method will be evaluated for various data dimensions (d = 10, 100, 200, 300) using a 40/20/40 train/validation/test split, with repeated runs (10 per configuration) and early stopping based on validation loss. Baselines will include state-of-the-art normalizing flows with heavy-tailed base distributions (e.g., gTAF with Student's T base), flows with standard Gaussian bases (RQS), and several variants of the proposed tail transformation (multivariate, marginal, and GPD-only). Evaluation will focus on density estimation performance, measured by negative log-likelihood on held-out test data, to assess the ability to capture extreme events and overall fit.
0b4f027cd01e52f8cc63d2e59e87d4792261f497.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a flexible, parameterized tail transformation layer that can be composed with existing normalizing flows to induce a wide range of heavy-tail behaviors, including asymmetric and non-GPD tails, without requiring heavy-tailed base distributions. This enables more accurate modeling of extremes and tail dependencies in multivariate data. The method also provides efficient and tractable computation for both sampling and density evaluation, and demonstrates superior performance over existing baselines in modeling the tails of financial return data.

0b58f4ec8cbf6f63fb65b7e3c368cf511eadecd3.title: Grounding Large Language Models in Interactive Environments with Online Reinforcement Learning
0b58f4ec8cbf6f63fb65b7e3c368cf511eadecd3.research_question: How can large language models be effectively grounded in interactive environments to improve their functional competence for decision-making tasks, and what are the impacts of online reinforcement learning on their sample efficiency and generalization abilities?
0b58f4ec8cbf6f63fb65b7e3c368cf511eadecd3.hypothesis: Large language models, when grounded through online reinforcement learning in interactive environments, will exhibit improved sample efficiency and enhanced generalization to new objects and tasks compared to non-grounded or offline-trained baselines.
0b58f4ec8cbf6f63fb65b7e3c368cf511eadecd3.proposed_method: A new approach is developed that grounds large language models (LLMs) in interactive, text-based environments using online reinforcement learning. The method, named GLAM, employs an LLM as the agent's policy, where the model receives prompts composed of the current goal, recent observations, and available actions. At each step, the LLM computes the conditional probability of each possible action given the prompt, and an action is sampled according to a softmax distribution over these probabilities. The agent interacts with the environment, receives rewards, and the LLM is fine-tuned online using the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm, with a value head added to the model for value estimation. To address computational challenges, distributed inference and training are implemented via a custom library, allowing scalable and efficient policy updates.
0b58f4ec8cbf6f63fb65b7e3c368cf511eadecd3.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted in BabyAI-Text, a procedurally generated, text-only environment adapted from the BabyAI platform, focusing on spatial and navigation tasks. The primary model evaluated is Flan-T5 (780M parameters), compared to several baselines: a non-pretrained Flan-T5 with action heads, a DRRN agent (1M parameters), and a Symbolic-PPO agent using symbolic observations. Evaluation metrics include average success rate and sample efficiency, measured over multiple seeds and a variety of tasks such as navigation, object manipulation, and compositional reasoning. Generalization is assessed through zero-shot tests on new objects (including out-of-vocabulary and invented words), new task compositions, and synonym substitutions, with performance compared to random and zero-shot LLM baselines.
