0b58f4ec8cbf6f63fb65b7e3c368cf511eadecd3.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first systematic study of functional grounding for LLMs via incremental online reinforcement learning in interactive environments. Key innovations include using LLMs directly as agent policies in text-based RL settings, leveraging online PPO for continual grounding, and demonstrating robust sample efficiency and generalization. The approach also provides a scalable distributed framework (Lamorel) for RL practitioners to utilize LLMs in interactive decision-making tasks, and establishes new benchmarks for grounding and generalization in language-conditioned RL.

0b5b753aa23be12f24b4592429514df6e53289bc.title: Structure-CLIP: Towards Scene Graph Knowledge to Enhance Multi-Modal Structured Representations
0b5b753aa23be12f24b4592429514df6e53289bc.research_question: How can multi-modal models be enhanced to better capture and utilize structured representations, such as objects, attributes, and relationships, for improved image-text matching and understanding tasks?
0b5b753aa23be12f24b4592429514df6e53289bc.hypothesis: Integrating scene graph knowledge into multi-modal learning frameworks and leveraging semantic negative sampling will significantly improve the ability of models to learn and utilize structured representations, leading to superior performance on tasks requiring fine-grained semantic understanding.
0b5b753aa23be12f24b4592429514df6e53289bc.proposed_method: A novel end-to-end framework is proposed that incorporates Scene Graph Knowledge (SGK) to enhance multi-modal structured representations. The approach begins by parsing captions into scene graphs, which explicitly represent objects, attributes, and relationships. These scene graphs are used to guide the construction of semantic negative samples by swapping key entities or attributes, ensuring that negative samples are compositionally similar but semantically distinct. A Knowledge-Enhanced Encoder (KEE) is introduced, which processes both the original text and its scene graph-derived triples using a multi-layer Transformer initialized from BERT. The encoder fuses standard text embeddings with structured knowledge embeddings, enabling the model to jointly learn general and structured semantic representations. Training uses a combination of contrastive learning objectives that pull together matched image-text pairs and push apart mismatched pairs, with special emphasis on distinguishing fine-grained structured differences.
0b5b753aa23be12f24b4592429514df6e53289bc.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using the MSCOCO dataset for pre-training, with approximately 100k image-text pairs filtered for rich object, attribute, and relationship content. Downstream evaluation is performed on the Visual Genome Relation (VG-Relation) and Visual Genome Attribution (VG-Attribution) datasets, which probe the model's ability to distinguish between captions with identical word compositions but different structured semantics. Baselines include state-of-the-art multi-modal models (CLIP, NegCLIP, VILT, FLAVA, BLIP) and large language models (BART, FLAN-T5, OPT). Evaluation metrics include Recall@1 for image-to-text and text-to-image retrieval, as well as accuracy on structured matching tasks. Ablation studies examine the impact of semantic negative sampling, the Knowledge-Enhanced Encoder, and various fusion strategies. All experiments are performed on NVIDIA A100 GPUs with consistent hyperparameters and training protocols.
0b5b753aa23be12f24b4592429514df6e53289bc.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to systematically integrate scene graph knowledge for the explicit enhancement of structured representations in multi-modal models. The semantic negative sampling method, guided by scene graphs, produces high-quality negatives that better target fine-grained semantic distinctions than previous random or hard negative approaches. The Knowledge-Enhanced Encoder uniquely fuses structured knowledge with textual representations at the input level, enabling the model to capture both general and detailed semantics. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on structured representation tasks, outperforming both prior multi-modal and large language models, while maintaining strong general representation capabilities.

0b5f27a5766c5d1394a6282ad94fec21d620bd6b.title: GroupViT: Semantic Segmentation Emerges from Text Supervision
0b5f27a5766c5d1394a6282ad94fec21d620bd6b.research_question: Can semantic segmentation models be trained using only text supervision, without any pixel-level annotations, such that they can generalize to different sets of object categories in a zero-shot manner?
0b5f27a5766c5d1394a6282ad94fec21d620bd6b.hypothesis: Semantic segmentation models trained solely with large-scale image-text paired data and hierarchical grouping mechanisms can learn to generate meaningful semantic segments and transfer to new segmentation tasks in a zero-shot fashion, without requiring pixel-level supervision.
0b5f27a5766c5d1394a6282ad94fec21d620bd6b.proposed_method: A novel hierarchical Grouping Vision Transformer (GroupViT) architecture will be developed, which partitions input images into progressively larger, arbitrary-shaped visual segments using a multi-stage grouping mechanism within the Transformer framework. The model will be trained end-to-end with contrastive losses between image and text embeddings, where the image encoder (GroupViT) and a text encoder (Transformer) are jointly optimized from scratch. Visual tokens are grouped via learnable group tokens and a differentiable Grouping Block that assigns and merges segment tokens using Gumbel-Softmax-based hard assignment. Multi-label contrastive losses will be employed, leveraging text prompting to generate additional positive text pairs for each image, thus enhancing the model's ability to associate image regions with semantic concepts. During inference, the model will assign semantic labels to image segments by computing similarity between segment embeddings and text embeddings of class names, enabling zero-shot semantic segmentation.
0b5f27a5766c5d1394a6282ad94fec21d620bd6b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by training the model on large-scale, noisy public image-text datasets such as Conceptual Captions (CC12M) and Yahoo Flickr Creative Commons (YFCC), totaling approximately 30 million image-text pairs. The model's zero-shot semantic segmentation performance will be evaluated on the PASCAL VOC 2012 and PASCAL Context datasets, using mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) and boundary mIoU as evaluation metrics. Baseline comparisons will include zero-shot segmentation using standard Vision Transformers (ViT) with non-parametric grouping methods (e.g., k-means, mean-shift, spectral clustering) and fully supervised transfer-learning baselines (e.g., ViT models pre-trained with supervised or self-supervised objectives and fine-tuned with segmentation labels). Ablation studies will analyze the effects of hard vs. soft assignment, single-stage vs. multi-stage grouping, and the impact of multi-label contrastive losses and varying numbers of group tokens.
0b5f27a5766c5d1394a6282ad94fec21d620bd6b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a hierarchical grouping mechanism into Vision Transformers, enabling arbitrary-shaped semantic segments to emerge without pixel-level supervision. This is the first method to achieve zero-shot semantic segmentation across different label vocabularies using only text supervision, without any mask or pixel-wise annotations. The model demonstrates competitive or superior performance to state-of-the-art transfer-learning methods that require significantly more supervision. The framework establishes a strong baseline for text-supervised zero-shot semantic segmentation and demonstrates that text supervision can be effectively leveraged for fine-grained vision tasks beyond classification.

0b6eea72dcbe3257cac62afb0db9ec28505ede0b.title: SafeDiffuser: Safe Planning with Diffusion Probabilistic Models
0b6eea72dcbe3257cac62afb0db9ec28505ede0b.research_question: How can diffusion probabilistic models for data-driven planning be equipped with formal safety guarantees to ensure satisfaction of safety specifications in safety-critical applications such as robotics and manipulation?
0b6eea72dcbe3257cac62afb0db9ec28505ede0b.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that embedding control-theoretic invariance, specifically through control barrier functions (CBFs) and finite-time diffusion invariance, into the denoising diffusion process will enable diffusion models to generate safe trajectories that satisfy specified safety constraints without significantly compromising model performance.
0b6eea72dcbe3257cac62afb0db9ec28505ede0b.proposed_method: A new framework, SafeDiffuser, will be developed to enforce safety specifications within diffusion probabilistic models by leveraging control barrier functions (CBFs) and the concept of finite-time diffusion invariance. The approach will embed invariance constraints directly into the diffusion (denoising) process, rather than only in planning time, ensuring that generated trajectories remain within safe sets throughout the diffusion steps. Three variants will be implemented: (1) Robust-SafeDiffuser, which enforces hard invariance constraints via a quadratic program (QP) at each diffusion step; (2) Relaxed-SafeDiffuser, which introduces relaxation variables and time-varying weights to address local trap problems and allow soft constraint satisfaction; and (3) Time-Varying-SafeDiffuser, which modifies safety specifications over diffusion time using a differentiable time-varying function. At each diffusion step, a QP will be solved to minimally deviate from the original diffusion dynamics while satisfying the CBF-based safety constraints, updating the trajectory iteratively.
0b6eea72dcbe3257cac62afb0db9ec28505ede0b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of safe planning tasks, including maze path generation, legged robot locomotion (e.g., Walker2D and Hopper in MuJoCo), and 3D space manipulation (e.g., in Pybullet). Publicly available datasets, such as those from Janner et al. (2022), will be used for training and evaluation. Baseline methods will include standard diffusion models (Diffuser), truncation-based approaches, and classifier-guided diffusion. Evaluation metrics will include satisfaction scores for simple and complex safety specifications, task performance scores, and computation time per diffusion step. Both quantitative and qualitative analyses will be performed to assess the ability of the proposed methods to guarantee safety, preserve planning performance, and address local trap issues compared to baselines.
0b6eea72dcbe3257cac62afb0db9ec28505ede0b.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first formal framework for equipping diffusion probabilistic models with specification guarantees via control-theoretic invariance. The concept of finite-time diffusion invariance is developed and incorporated into the diffusion process using a class of CBFs, enabling safety guarantees throughout the generative procedure. Three distinct SafeDiffuser variants are proposed to address both hard and soft constraint satisfaction and to mitigate local trap problems. The approach is general and can handle complex, differentiable safety specifications, providing robust and trustworthy data generation for safety-critical planning tasks.

0b73a37c06f3d79a1cb5fd61e3556676634b9d2f.title: Data Determines Distributional Robustness in Contrastive Language Image Pre-training (CLIP)
0b73a37c06f3d79a1cb5fd61e3556676634b9d2f.research_question: What are the primary factors that determine the distributional robustness of contrastively trained language-image models, such as CLIP, under natural distribution shifts?
0b73a37c06f3d79a1cb5fd61e3556676634b9d2f.hypothesis: The diversity of the training data distribution is the main determinant of robustness in contrastive language-image models, while other factors such as language supervision, contrastive loss, and training set size contribute minimally.
0b73a37c06f3d79a1cb5fd61e3556676634b9d2f.proposed_method: A comprehensive experimental framework will be established to systematically isolate and evaluate five potential contributors to robustness in contrastive language-image models: (i) training set size, (ii) training distribution, (iii) language supervision at training time, (iv) language supervision at test time, and (v) the contrastive loss function. A new dataset, ImageNet-Captions, will be constructed by augmenting a subset of the ImageNet 2012 training set with original Flickr-sourced text metadata (titles, descriptions, tags), enabling controlled comparisons between language-image and standard classification training on identical images. Additional experiments will involve converting the YFCC-15M dataset into a classification dataset using simple text matching for label assignment, and training models using both contrastive and classification objectives. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of different caption constructions, language encoder initializations, and template usage.
0b73a37c06f3d79a1cb5fd61e3556676634b9d2f.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize datasets including ImageNet, ImageNet-Captions (463,622 images with paired text), and YFCC-15M (a subset of YFCC-100M filtered for English captions, with 14.8M images). Models will be evaluated on in-distribution accuracy (ImageNet) and out-of-distribution robustness using natural distribution shift benchmarks: ImageNet-V2, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-Sketch, ObjectNet, and ImageNet-A. Baselines will include standard supervised models, contrastive models, and models with minimal language supervision (e.g., SimCLR pre-training followed by classification with text-matched labels). Evaluation metrics will focus on top-1 accuracy and effective robustness, defined as accuracy gains under distribution shift beyond what is explained by in-distribution accuracy. Key experimental setups will control for confounding factors by ensuring identical image distributions between compared models and by systematically varying only one factor at a time.
0b73a37c06f3d79a1cb5fd61e3556676634b9d2f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new dataset, ImageNet-Captions, enabling controlled experiments on the effect of language supervision versus training distribution. A novel baseline is established by demonstrating that image-only contrastive pre-training followed by simple text-based classification can nearly match the robustness of full language-image models, suggesting that robustness arises primarily from data diversity rather than language supervision or contrastive loss. The experimental design provides the first systematic disentanglement of the contributions of data, supervision, and loss function to distributional robustness in large-scale contrastive language-image models.

0b7bb1e0c34e2a0106c6103f6e6d7cfc3307c240.title: CLIPood: Generalizing CLIP to Out-of-Distributions
0b7bb1e0c34e2a0106c6103f6e6d7cfc3307c240.research_question: How can vision-language pre-trained models be effectively adapted to downstream tasks while maintaining strong out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization, particularly in scenarios involving both domain shifts and open classes?
0b7bb1e0c34e2a0106c6103f6e6d7cfc3307c240.hypothesis: Fine-tuning vision-language models using a training objective that incorporates semantic relationships between classes and an optimization strategy that balances pre-trained and adapted knowledge will improve OOD generalization performance compared to existing methods.
0b7bb1e0c34e2a0106c6103f6e6d7cfc3307c240.proposed_method: A novel fine-tuning approach, termed CLIPood, is proposed for adapting pre-trained vision-language models (specifically CLIP) to downstream tasks with enhanced OOD generalization. The method introduces Margin Metric Softmax (MMS), a training objective that adds class-adaptive margins to the metric softmax loss, leveraging semantic distances in the pre-trained text embedding space to enforce stronger image-text alignment and exploit inter-class relationships. During fine-tuning, only the image encoder is updated, while the text encoder is frozen to preserve semantic knowledge. To further balance the contributions of the pre-trained zero-shot model and the fine-tuned model, a Beta Moving Average (BMA) strategy is employed, maintaining a temporal ensemble of model checkpoints weighted by a Beta distribution, thus integrating both generalization and task-specific adaptation. The final model used for inference is the BMA-averaged model, which is updated online during training.
0b7bb1e0c34e2a0106c6103f6e6d7cfc3307c240.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple benchmarks covering domain shift (DomainBed suite: PACS, VLCS, OfficeHome, TerraIncognita, DomainNet; ImageNet and its variants), open class (ImageNet, Caltech101, OxfordPets, StanfordCars, Flowers102, Food101, FGVCAircraft, SUN397, UCF101, DTD, EuroSAT), and combined domain shift plus open class scenarios (OfficeHome, DomainNet). Standard protocols such as leave-one-domain-out and class splits for base/new classes will be followed. Baselines for comparison include zero-shot CLIP, standard fine-tuning, and state-of-the-art generalization methods (e.g., MIRO, DPL, CoOp, CoCoOp, SWAD, WiSE-FT). Evaluation metrics will primarily be classification accuracy, reported on both in-distribution and OOD test sets, with harmonic mean used to assess the trade-off between base and new class performance. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of MMS, BMA, and alternative ensembling strategies.
0b7bb1e0c34e2a0106c6103f6e6d7cfc3307c240.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new fine-tuning objective (Margin Metric Softmax) that adaptively incorporates semantic distances between classes from the text modality, which is not considered in standard metric softmax or cross-entropy losses. The Beta Moving Average optimization strategy is also novel, providing a principled way to ensemble pre-trained and fine-tuned models by leveraging the Beta distribution, unlike conventional exponential or uniform averaging. The approach is designed to address both domain shift and open class OOD scenarios simultaneously, a more general and challenging setting than those considered in prior work. The method is simple, efficient, and requires minimal additional computation or storage compared to standard fine-tuning.

0ba0091c60c0346493b9ffb46ac682eee5453a53.title: Exploring the Limits of Differentially Private Deep Learning with Group-wise Clipping
0ba0091c60c0346493b9ffb46ac682eee5453a53.research_question: Can differentially private deep learning be made as computationally efficient as non-private learning, and can the privacy-utility trade-off be improved when scaling to large pretrained models by leveraging novel group-wise gradient clipping strategies?
0ba0091c60c0346493b9ffb46ac682eee5453a53.hypothesis: Group-wise clipping strategies, specifically adaptive per-layer clipping and per-device clipping, will enable differentially private deep learning to achieve computational efficiency comparable to non-private learning and improve the privacy-utility trade-off, especially when scaling to large pretrained models.
0ba0091c60c0346493b9ffb46ac682eee5453a53.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves two main group-wise gradient clipping strategies within differentially private stochastic gradient descent (DP-SGD): adaptive per-layer clipping and per-device clipping. Adaptive per-layer clipping assigns and dynamically adjusts separate clipping thresholds for each neural network layer based on privately estimated statistics (e.g., quantiles of per-layer gradient norms), allowing clipping to be performed in conjunction with backpropagation and minimizing memory and time overhead. The quantile estimation for each layer is privatized using a small fraction of the privacy budget, and noise is allocated either globally or per-layer based on the chosen strategy. For large-scale distributed models (e.g., GPT-3), per-device clipping is employed, where each device clips gradients of its hosted model partition using a local threshold and adds noise independently, thereby avoiding costly inter-device communication. Both approaches are implemented efficiently to ensure that per-example gradients are not materialized in memory, and all privacy accounting is performed according to standard DP mechanisms.
0ba0091c60c0346493b9ffb46ac682eee5453a53.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of tasks and architectures, including training Wide ResNet (WRN16-4) from scratch on CIFAR-10, fine-tuning RoBERTa-base and RoBERTa-large on GLUE benchmark tasks (SST-2, QNLI, QQP, MNLI), and fine-tuning GPT-2 and GPT-3 on table-to-text generation (E2E, DART) and dialog summarization (SAMSum). Baselines will include standard flat clipping DP-SGD and previously published results. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy for classification tasks and BLEU/ROUGE scores for generation tasks. Experiments will compare memory usage, training throughput, and task performance under various privacy budgets (e.g., ε = 1, 3, 8; δ = 10^-5 or 1/n^1.1), and will be repeated across multiple random seeds. For large models, distributed training will be implemented using pipeline parallelism, and the impact of per-device clipping on efficiency and utility will be measured.
0ba0091c60c0346493b9ffb46ac682eee5453a53.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces an efficient implementation of adaptive per-layer clipping that enables memory- and time-efficient differentially private training, nearly matching non-private training efficiency for small to moderate scale workflows. It demonstrates that adaptively setting per-layer thresholds eliminates the performance losses associated with fixed thresholds and matches or outperforms flat clipping under fixed training epoch constraints. Furthermore, the research pioneers the use of per-device clipping to enable scalable, efficient, and private fine-tuning of extremely large models such as GPT-3, achieving improved privacy-utility trade-offs compared to prior approaches. These innovations collectively advance the scalability and practicality of differentially private deep learning.

0bea974897420b053a5a79f5710ad3724d2c70d4.title: How Does Sequence Modeling Architecture Influence Base Capabilities of Pre-trained Language Models? Exploring Key Architecture Design Principles to Avoid Base Capabilities Degradation
0bea974897420b053a5a79f5710ad3724d2c70d4.research_question: How do different sequence modeling architectures influence the base capabilities of pre-trained language models, and what architectural design principles can prevent degradation of these capabilities?
0bea974897420b053a5a79f5710ad3724d2c70d4.hypothesis: Sequence modeling architectures that support full-sequence arbitrary selection, real relation computation, and non-uniform attention distribution will preserve or enhance the base capabilities of pre-trained language models, whereas architectures lacking these properties will exhibit degradation in base capabilities.
0bea974897420b053a5a79f5710ad3724d2c70d4.proposed_method: A comprehensive experimental framework will be established to analyze the impact of sequence modeling architectures on the base capabilities of pre-trained language models. The approach involves designing a limited domain pre-training regime, where models are trained on a restricted set of domains and evaluated on out-of-distribution (OOD) domains to better reveal architectural differences. Ablation studies will be conducted on stateful architectures (such as Mamba, RWKV, and Gated DeltaNet) to isolate the effects of architectural components like data-dependent decay, convolution, and position encoding. Key architectural factors—full-sequence visibility, real relation calculation, and non-uniform attention distribution—will be systematically tested. Novel architectures, including a minimalist Top-1 Element Selection and a scalable Top-1 Chunk Selection mechanism (with efficient GPU kernel implementations), will be developed and empirically validated to test the proposed design principles.
0bea974897420b053a5a79f5710ad3724d2c70d4.experiment_details: Experiments will pre-train language models with approximately 110M and 1.3B parameters on subsets of the SlimPajama dataset, using cc and c4 domains for training and arxiv, github, and stack for OOD evaluation. Baselines will include standard Transformer, Transformer++ (with variants), Mamba-1/2, RWKV-5/6/7, DeltaNet, and Gated DeltaNet. Evaluation metrics will focus on OOD language modeling loss, few-shot learning accuracy on established NLP benchmarks (e.g., SWDE, SQuAD, FDA, MMLU, OBQA, ARC, BoolQ, RACE, SIQA, SCIQ, HellaSwag, COPA, PIQA, Winograd, WSC), and retrieval tasks. Long-sequence (up to 100k tokens) performance and time efficiency will also be assessed, with custom GPU kernels implemented for the proposed architectures. Comparative analysis will be performed against both attention-based and stateful baselines.
0bea974897420b053a5a79f5710ad3724d2c70d4.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled evaluation framework using limited domain pre-training with OOD testing to expose architectural impacts on base capabilities, which is more sensitive than conventional mixed-domain or few-shot evaluations. It identifies and empirically validates the necessity of full-sequence arbitrary selection, real relation calculation, and non-uniform attention distribution as critical architectural properties for preserving base capabilities. The work proposes and implements the Top-1 Element Selection and Top-1 Chunk Selection architectures as minimalist, efficient sequence modeling alternatives that adhere to these principles, accompanied by open-source GPU kernels for practical deployment. These findings provide actionable guidelines for future sequence modeling architecture design and improvement.

0bf68448099b138d179f8402721d502ec4c4b833.title: FRUGAL: Memory-Efficient Optimization by Reducing State Overhead for Scalable Training
0bf68448099b138d179f8402721d502ec4c4b833.research_question: How can the memory overhead of optimizer states be reduced during the training of large language models (LLMs) without sacrificing model performance, and what strategies allow for scalable, memory-efficient optimization applicable to both pre-training and fine-tuning tasks?
0bf68448099b138d179f8402721d502ec4c4b833.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that splitting the parameter space into state-full and state-free subspaces—using advanced optimizers (such as Adam) for a low-dimensional subspace and state-free optimizers (such as SGD or signSGD) for the complementary subspace—will enable memory-efficient training of large models while maintaining or improving convergence and performance compared to existing low-rank or blockwise memory-efficient methods.
0bf68448099b138d179f8402721d502ec4c4b833.proposed_method: A novel optimization framework, FRUGAL (Full-Rank Updates with GrAdient spLitting), is proposed to reduce optimizer state memory by partitioning model parameters into two subspaces: a state-full subspace, updated with advanced optimizers like Adam or AdamW, and a state-free subspace, updated with lightweight optimizers such as SGD or signSGD. The method leverages gradient splitting, where gradients are projected onto a low-dimensional subspace (using techniques such as SVD, random, or blockwise projections) for state-full updates, while the residual gradients are handled by state-free optimizers. The framework supports various projection strategies and allows for dynamic or fixed assignment of parameters to each subspace. The optimizer states are managed such that only the state-full subspace requires storage of optimizer statistics, significantly reducing memory usage. Theoretical convergence guarantees are established for the case where SGDM is used for the state-full subspace and SGD for the state-free subspace, with formal analysis of the impact of projection and update frequency.
0bf68448099b138d179f8402721d502ec4c4b833.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both pre-training and fine-tuning tasks. For pre-training, LLaMA-like models of various sizes (60M, 130M, 350M, 1B, and 3B parameters) will be trained on the Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus (C4) dataset, with training durations aligned with practical convergence rather than minimal scaling law recommendations. Comparisons will be made against baselines including full-rank AdamW, GaLore, and BAdam, with all methods evaluated under matched memory budgets (e.g., same density of state-full parameters). Evaluation metrics will include validation perplexity and memory consumption (measured in GB for weights, gradients, and optimizer states). For fine-tuning, RoBERTa-base will be evaluated on the GLUE benchmark, and LLaMA-8B will be fine-tuned on commonsense reasoning tasks, with accuracy as the primary metric. Ablation studies will explore the impact of projection type, update frequency, optimizer choice, and precision (mixed vs. pure bf16). Additional experiments will assess the sensitivity of specific model modules (e.g., Output layer) to optimizer selection.
0bf68448099b138d179f8402721d502ec4c4b833.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a novel approach to memory-efficient optimization by combining state-full and state-free updates within a single training process, enabling full-rank parameter exploration without the memory overhead of storing optimizer states for all parameters. Unlike prior low-rank or blockwise methods, FRUGAL leverages the entire gradient information by updating all parameter directions—using advanced optimizers where memory allows and state-free methods elsewhere—thus overcoming the information loss inherent in strictly low-rank updates. The method is general, supporting integration with various projection and optimizer strategies, and is accompanied by theoretical convergence guarantees for hybrid optimizer settings. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in both pre-training and fine-tuning tasks, with substantial memory savings and practical scalability to billion-parameter models.

0bfc804e31eecfd77f45e4ee7f4d629fffdcd628.title: ToolLLM: Facilitating Large Language Models to Master 16000+ Real-world APIs
0bfc804e31eecfd77f45e4ee7f4d629fffdcd628.research_question: How can open-source large language models be empowered to effectively use a vast array of real-world APIs to fulfill complex human instructions, including multi-tool and multi-step scenarios, and how can their tool-use capabilities be robustly evaluated and generalized to unseen APIs and domains?
0bfc804e31eecfd77f45e4ee7f4d629fffdcd628.hypothesis: Fine-tuning open-source large language models on a large-scale, diverse, and realistic tool-use instruction dataset, combined with advanced reasoning strategies and automated API retrieval, will enable these models to match or exceed the tool-use capabilities of state-of-the-art closed-source models, including robust generalization to unseen APIs and domains.
0bfc804e31eecfd77f45e4ee7f4d629fffdcd628.proposed_method: A comprehensive tool-use framework will be developed, consisting of three main components: (1) Construction of a large-scale instruction-tuning dataset (ToolBench) covering over 16,000 real-world RESTful APIs across 49 categories, with instructions generated for both single-tool and multi-tool scenarios using automated prompting and solution path annotation via a depth-first search-based decision tree (DFSDT) algorithm. (2) Fine-tuning of a large language model (e.g., LLaMA-2) on the ToolBench dataset, with context length extended to accommodate long API responses, and integration of a neural API retriever trained to recommend relevant APIs for each instruction using dense retrieval techniques. (3) Development of an automated evaluation framework (ToolEval) based on LLM-assisted metrics to assess both the executability (pass rate) and quality (win rate) of tool-use solutions. The approach emphasizes multi-step reasoning, error recovery, and generalization to unseen APIs through reliance on API documentation.
0bfc804e31eecfd77f45e4ee7f4d629fffdcd628.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ToolBench dataset, which includes 126,486 instruction-solution pairs spanning single-tool, intra-category multi-tool, and intra-collection multi-tool scenarios. Evaluation will compare the proposed model (ToolLLaMA) against strong baselines such as ChatGPT, GPT-4, Claude-2, Text-Davinci-003, Vicuna, and Alpaca, using both oracle and neural API retrievers. Metrics will include pass rate and win rate as measured by the ToolEval evaluator, with additional assessment of API retrieval performance using NDCG. Out-of-distribution generalization will be tested on the APIBench dataset (domains: TorchHub, TensorHub, HuggingFace), reporting AST accuracy and hallucination rates, and comparing to the Gorilla model under zero-shot and retrieval-aware settings. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by controlling for API set availability and context length.
0bfc804e31eecfd77f45e4ee7f4d629fffdcd628.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the largest and most diverse open-source tool-use instruction dataset to date, covering over 16,000 real-world APIs and supporting both single-tool and complex multi-tool scenarios. The depth-first search-based decision tree (DFSDT) algorithm is proposed as a novel reasoning and annotation strategy that enables efficient exploration of reasoning paths and error recovery, outperforming prior methods such as ReACT. The integration of a neural API retriever enables scalable and automated API selection from a massive pool, removing the need for manual curation. The ToolEval framework provides a scalable, LLM-based automatic evaluation method with high agreement to human judgments. The overall framework demonstrates strong generalization to unseen APIs and out-of-distribution domains, matching or surpassing closed-source models in tool-use tasks.

0c26bfc15a7caecce0ed4567dc2f2909b80e5bdd.title: Hard Prompts Made Easy: Gradient-Based Discrete Optimization for Prompt Tuning and Discovery
0c26bfc15a7caecce0ed4567dc2f2909b80e5bdd.research_question: How can hard, discrete, human-interpretable prompts for generative models be automatically discovered and optimized, enabling effective prompt engineering for both text-to-image and text-to-text applications without manual intervention?
0c26bfc15a7caecce0ed4567dc2f2909b80e5bdd.hypothesis: Gradient-based discrete optimization methods can efficiently discover hard prompts that are both interpretable and effective, matching or surpassing the performance of existing hand-crafted or soft prompt techniques in generative and classification tasks.
0c26bfc15a7caecce0ed4567dc2f2909b80e5bdd.proposed_method: A novel gradient-based discrete optimization algorithm, termed PEZ, is proposed for learning hard prompts. The method maintains a continuous embedding representation of the prompt, which is iteratively updated using gradients computed with respect to a task-specific loss. At each optimization step, the continuous embeddings are projected onto the nearest valid token embeddings from the model's vocabulary, ensuring the prompt remains discrete and interpretable. The approach leverages a broadcast function to handle batch optimization, and can incorporate additional constraints such as fluency regularization for language tasks. For vision-language models, the method optimizes prompts to maximize semantic similarity between image and text embeddings (e.g., using CLIP), while for language models, it optimizes for task accuracy and optionally fluency.
0c26bfc15a7caecce0ed4567dc2f2909b80e5bdd.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on four diverse image datasets (LAION, MSCOCO, Celeb-A, Lexica.art) for text-to-image tasks, using Stable Diffusion v2 as the generative model and OpenCLIP-ViT/H for prompt optimization. The quality of learned prompts is evaluated by generating images and measuring CLIP similarity scores between generated and target images, using OpenCLIP-ViT/G as a reference. Baselines include CLIP Interrogator (with and without BLIP), AutoPrompt, FluentPrompt, and soft prompts, with ablations on prompt length and keyword bank usage. For text-to-text tasks, experiments are performed on sentiment analysis (SST-2, Amazon Polarity) and news classification (AGNEWS), using GPT-2 Large for prompt optimization and testing transferability to larger models (GPT-2 XL, T5-LM-XL, OPT-2.7B, OPT-6.7B). Evaluation metrics include classification accuracy and prompt transferability, with further analysis on few-shot learning and prompt distillation.
0c26bfc15a7caecce0ed4567dc2f2909b80e5bdd.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple yet effective gradient-based discrete optimization framework for hard prompt discovery, enabling automatic generation of interpretable prompts for both text-to-image and text-to-text tasks. Unlike previous approaches, the method combines the flexibility and automation of soft prompt optimization with the interpretability and portability of hard prompts, supporting transfer across models and applications. The approach is demonstrated to outperform or match specialized baselines while using fewer tokens and requiring no hand-crafted components. Additional innovations include prompt distillation, style transfer via hard prompts, and compositionality through prompt concatenation.

0c30784a70be60e6f1a0bf42b420130957cb5a08.title: Whispering Experts: Neural Interventions for Toxicity Mitigation in Language Models
0c30784a70be60e6f1a0bf42b420130957cb5a08.research_question: How can the generation of toxic language by large language models be mitigated through neural interventions, while preserving model performance and requiring minimal changes to the model architecture or inference procedure?
0c30784a70be60e6f1a0bf42b420130957cb5a08.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that neurons responsible for generating toxic language can be identified by their ability to discriminate toxic content, and that proportionally dampening their activations will significantly reduce toxicity in language model outputs without substantially degrading model performance or increasing perplexity.
0c30784a70be60e6f1a0bf42b420130957cb5a08.proposed_method: A new intervention, AUROC Adaptation (AURA), is proposed to mitigate toxicity in pre-trained large language models (LLMs). The method first identifies 'expert' neurons whose activations are highly predictive of toxic content, using the area under the ROC curve (AUROC) as a measure of each neuron's expertise. For each neuron with AUROC > 0.5, its activation is dampened by a factor proportional to its expertise, with the Gini coefficient used to rescale the AUROC so that non-expert neurons remain unaffected and highly toxic experts are strongly suppressed. This intervention is hyperparameter-free, model-agnostic, and can be implemented as a permanent modification to the model's weights and biases, thereby requiring no additional fine-tuning or changes to the inference process. The approach is designed to preserve the model's ability to perform on non-toxic content and maintain zero-shot reasoning abilities.
0c30784a70be60e6f1a0bf42b420130957cb5a08.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of publicly available LLMs, including GPT2-XL (1.5B), Falcon-7B, Falcon-40B, MPT-7B, MPT-30B, Mistral-7B, and Llama-v2 (7B), as well as instruction-tuned models. Toxicity mitigation will be evaluated using several benchmarks: Jigsaw 2018 (Wikipedia comments labeled for toxicity), HONEST (hurtful language completions), and RealToxicityPrompts (RTP), with toxicity measured via a robust RoBERTa-based classifier. Baselines for comparison include DExperts, CTRL, Detzero (zeroing expert neurons), and pre-prompting strategies. Evaluation metrics include toxicity reduction (on both toxic and non-toxic prompts), perplexity on a fixed Wikipedia dataset, and zero-shot performance on common-sense reasoning tasks (PIQA, SIQA, TriviaQA, TruthfulQA, Hellaswag). Both automated and human evaluations will be performed, and the robustness of the method will be tested against adversarial pre-prompts designed to elicit toxic content.
0c30784a70be60e6f1a0bf42b420130957cb5a08.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a hyperparameter-free, model-agnostic neural intervention for toxicity mitigation in LLMs that operates by proportionally dampening the activations of toxicity-related expert neurons. This approach eliminates the need for fine-tuning or additional inference-time computation, and is shown to be effective across a wide range of model scales and architectures. AURA is claimed to preserve non-toxic model capabilities, maintain low perplexity, and robustly counteract both standard and adversarial pre-prompting strategies. The method advances the state of the art by providing a practical, efficient, and generalizable solution for safer language model deployment.

0c311d188f2708e2f3a90ac03cfdd68c5523009b.title: Sharpness Minimization Algorithms Do Not Only Minimize Sharpness To Achieve Better Generalization
0c311d188f2708e2f3a90ac03cfdd68c5523009b.research_question: Does the flatness (sharpness minimization) of neural network loss landscapes always correlate with or imply better generalization across different neural network architectures and data distributions? What are the underlying mechanisms by which sharpness minimization algorithms achieve generalization, and are there scenarios where sharpness minimization alone does not explain generalization performance?
0c311d188f2708e2f3a90ac03cfdd68c5523009b.hypothesis: The relationship between sharpness minimization and generalization is not universal; it depends on specific neural network architectures and data distributions. Sharpness minimization algorithms may generalize well even when not all flattest minimizers generalize, suggesting that mechanisms beyond sharpness reduction contribute to generalization.
0c311d188f2708e2f3a90ac03cfdd68c5523009b.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted to analyze the relationship between sharpness minimization and generalization in overparameterized neural networks. The study will focus on several two-layer neural network architectures, including variants with and without bias, as well as with simplified BatchNorm and LayerNorm. Theoretical analysis will derive generalization bounds and construct explicit examples of both generalizing and non-generalizing flattest minimizers. Empirical experiments will implement sharpness minimization algorithms, specifically Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) with batch size 1 (1-SAM), and compare their performance to standard gradient descent with weight decay. Sharpness will be quantified using the trace of the Hessian of the loss, and the interplay between architecture, data distribution, and generalization will be systematically explored.
0c311d188f2708e2f3a90ac03cfdd68c5523009b.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed on synthetic datasets, primarily the parity XOR problem with inputs sampled uniformly from the hypercube {−1,1}^d and labels y = x[1]x[2]. Multiple neural network architectures will be evaluated: 2-layer MLPs with and without bias, with simplified BatchNorm, and with simplified LayerNorm. Training will use mean squared error loss, and generalization will be assessed using zero-one classification error on unseen data. Baselines will include standard gradient descent with weight decay, while the primary sharpness minimization algorithm will be 1-SAM. Evaluation metrics will include training and test accuracy, sharpness (trace of Hessian), and interpretability of learned features. Experimental setups will vary network width, input dimension (e.g., d=30), and training set size (e.g., n=100), and will also explore the effect of different activation functions such as ReLU and Softplus.
0c311d188f2708e2f3a90ac03cfdd68c5523009b.novelty_claims: The proposed research identifies and characterizes regimes where sharpness minimization does and does not imply generalization, demonstrating that the relationship is highly sensitive to architectural and data distribution choices. The work provides new theoretical constructions showing the existence of both generalizing and non-generalizing flattest minimizers, and empirically reveals scenarios where sharpness minimization algorithms generalize well even when some flattest minimizers do not. This challenges the prevailing assumption that sharpness alone explains generalization and motivates the search for additional explanatory mechanisms. The research also highlights the architectural dependence of generalization from sharpness and offers interpretable examples of feature extraction in flat minimizers.

0c43750030198dbe7fe164e1ce743ec64427bca1.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization in Direct Alignment Algorithms
0c43750030198dbe7fe164e1ce743ec64427bca1.research_question: How does over-optimization, including reward hacking, manifest in Direct Alignment Algorithms (DAAs) for aligning large language models with human feedback, and what are the scaling laws and underlying causes of this phenomenon across different objectives, training regimes, and model scales?
0c43750030198dbe7fe164e1ce743ec64427bca1.hypothesis: Direct Alignment Algorithms, despite bypassing explicit reward modeling, are susceptible to over-optimization and reward hacking phenomena similar to those observed in classical RLHF pipelines, with the degree and nature of over-optimization being influenced by model scale, KL-divergence constraints, and the choice of training objective.
0c43750030198dbe7fe164e1ce743ec64427bca1.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical and theoretical investigation will be conducted to characterize and formalize the over-optimization problem in Direct Alignment Algorithms (DAAs), such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), IPO, and SLiC. The approach will unify recent DAA methods under a common framework and systematically vary key hyperparameters, including KL-divergence budgets and model sizes, to observe their effects on over-optimization. Scaling laws relating KL divergence and model performance will be derived and fitted to experimental data. Theoretical analysis will explore the under-constrained nature of DAA objectives, including the existence of multiple global optima and the tendency to place probability mass on out-of-distribution responses, supported by both language modeling and simplified MDP experiments.
0c43750030198dbe7fe164e1ce743ec64427bca1.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed using the Reddit TL;DR summarization dataset and the Pythia family of language models at scales of 1B, 2.8B, and 6.9B parameters. Additional tests will be conducted on the Gemma2-2b model and the Anthropic Helpfulness-Harmlessness dataset. The study will compare DPO, IPO, and SLiC objectives across seven KL-divergence (beta) settings, tracking model win-rates as judged by GPT-4, KL divergence metrics, and intra-epoch performance. Baselines will include standard RLHF procedures and models with and without length regularization. Evaluation metrics will focus on win-rates, KL divergence, reward model accuracy, and extrapolation to out-of-distribution responses. Toy MDPs will be used to illustrate theoretical findings regarding the non-strict convexity and OOD behavior of DAAs.
0c43750030198dbe7fe164e1ce743ec64427bca1.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a unified empirical and theoretical framework for analyzing over-optimization in Direct Alignment Algorithms, extending the concept of reward hacking beyond classical RLHF. It formulates and validates new scaling laws for DAA over-optimization, demonstrates the existence of multiple global optima leading to OOD behavior, and provides the first comprehensive empirical evidence of over-optimization dynamics in DAAs across objectives, model scales, and KL budgets. The work also highlights the limitations of current DAA objectives and the necessity for more robust alignment techniques.

0c4cdd4a22477807cbdc95ba5837458b54dcc1d2.title: Online Learning in the Random Order Model
0c4cdd4a22477807cbdc95ba5837458b54dcc1d2.research_question: How can online learning algorithms be effectively adapted to the random-order input model, and what are the fundamental limits and characterizations of learnability and regret in this setting across various online learning problems?
0c4cdd4a22477807cbdc95ba5837458b54dcc1d2.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that stochastic online learning algorithms can be systematically adapted to the random-order model to achieve regret guarantees comparable to those in the i.i.d. stochastic setting, and that the learnability in online classification under random order is characterized by the VC dimension rather than the Littlestone dimension.
0c4cdd4a22477807cbdc95ba5837458b54dcc1d2.proposed_method: A general template, termed Simulation, is proposed to adapt stochastic online learning algorithms for the random-order model. The method partitions the time horizon into blocks of geometrically increasing length. In each block, a distribution is constructed from past observed data (e.g., by uniform sampling), and the stochastic algorithm is trained on simulated i.i.d. samples from this distribution without incurring real loss. The empirical action frequencies from this training phase are then used to determine the actions played in the current block on the actual instance. For settings with delayed feedback, an additional buffer is introduced to ensure that feedback from previous blocks is available before constructing the next training distribution. The approach leverages concentration properties of sampling without replacement to ensure that empirical gaps in past and future blocks are close to the true mean, thus preserving regret guarantees.
0c4cdd4a22477807cbdc95ba5837458b54dcc1d2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several canonical online learning problems: prediction with delayed feedback, online learning with constraints, and bandits with switching costs. For each setting, the Simulation template will be instantiated with appropriate stochastic algorithms (e.g., Follow-The-Leader, successive elimination). Datasets will be constructed by generating adversarial loss sequences and applying random permutations to simulate the random-order model. Baselines will include standard algorithms for both the stochastic i.i.d. and adversarial models. Evaluation metrics will focus on regret (including minimax regret rates), constraint violations (where applicable), and learnability characterizations (e.g., VC vs. Littlestone dimension in online classification). The experimental setup will include varying parameters such as the delay in feedback, the number of actions, and the time horizon, with results compared across input models.
0c4cdd4a22477807cbdc95ba5837458b54dcc1d2.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a general and systematic reduction (Simulation) for adapting stochastic online learning algorithms to the random-order model, preserving regret guarantees up to logarithmic factors. It demonstrates that minimax regret rates in the random-order model essentially match those of the stochastic i.i.d. model across multiple online learning problems, including settings with delayed feedback, constraints, and switching costs. Furthermore, it establishes a new characterization of online classification in the random-order model, showing that learnability is determined by the VC dimension rather than the Littlestone dimension, thereby separating the random-order model from the fully adversarial model. The approach also provides practical implications for algorithm designers, suggesting that dataset shuffling can recover stochastic regret rates in practice.

0c72450890a54b68d63baa99376131fda8f06cf9.title: The Rise and Potential of Large Language Model Based Agents: A Survey
0c72450890a54b68d63baa99376131fda8f06cf9.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) serve as the foundation for constructing general and adaptable AI agents capable of perceiving, reasoning, acting, and interacting in diverse environments and social contexts?
0c72450890a54b68d63baa99376131fda8f06cf9.hypothesis: LLMs, when equipped with expanded perception and action modules, can serve as a powerful and generalizable foundation for AI agents, enabling them to exhibit autonomy, reactivity, pro-activeness, and social ability across a wide range of tasks and environments.
0c72450890a54b68d63baa99376131fda8f06cf9.proposed_method: A general conceptual framework for LLM-based agents will be developed, consisting of three key components: brain, perception, and action. The brain module will leverage a large language model to handle memory, knowledge storage, reasoning, planning, and decision-making. The perception module will be designed to extend the agent's input space from text-only to multimodal, incorporating textual, visual, and auditory information to enable richer environmental understanding. The action module will expand the agent's output capabilities beyond text generation to include tool use and embodied actions, allowing the agent to interact with and influence its environment. This modular framework will be adaptable to various application scenarios, supporting single-agent, multi-agent, and human-agent cooperative settings.
0c72450890a54b68d63baa99376131fda8f06cf9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across multiple domains to evaluate the generality and effectiveness of the proposed LLM-based agent framework. Datasets will include text-based tasks, simulated exploration environments, and multimodal benchmarks, with scenarios ranging from task-oriented deployments to innovation-driven and lifecycle-oriented applications. Baseline comparisons will involve symbolic agents, reactive agents, reinforcement learning agents, and existing LLM-based systems. Evaluation metrics will include task success rate, reasoning and planning accuracy, adaptability, generalization across tasks, and measures of social interaction such as cooperation and competition in multi-agent settings. Additional experiments will assess emergent social phenomena and human-agent collaboration paradigms in both virtual and physical environments.
0c72450890a54b68d63baa99376131fda8f06cf9.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified and extensible framework for constructing general-purpose AI agents grounded in LLMs, systematically integrating multimodal perception and diverse action capabilities. The approach aims to bridge the gap between specialized agent architectures and general intelligence by leveraging the emergent properties of LLMs. Novel contributions include the formalization of a modular agent architecture, the exploration of agent societies and emergent behaviors, and the identification of open challenges and risks in scaling LLM-based agents for real-world and social applications.

0c9796f5f6716ffdd40e2a8158221f5b631c44f6.title: One Diffusion Step to Real-World Super-Resolution via Flow Trajectory Distillation
0c9796f5f6716ffdd40e2a8158221f5b631c44f6.research_question: How can efficient and high-quality real-world image super-resolution be achieved using large-scale diffusion models, while minimizing computational costs and inference latency?
0c9796f5f6716ffdd40e2a8158221f5b631c44f6.hypothesis: A one-step diffusion-based super-resolution model, distilled from a large pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model via flow trajectory distillation and enhanced with specialized loss functions, can generate realistic high-resolution images with reduced artifacts and computational overhead, outperforming existing one-step and multi-step diffusion-based super-resolution methods.
0c9796f5f6716ffdd40e2a8158221f5b631c44f6.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a one-step diffusion model for real-world image super-resolution (Real-ISR), leveraging a large pre-trained diffusion model (FLUX.1-dev) as the base. The core of the method is Flow Trajectory Distillation (FTD), which aligns the flow from low-resolution (LR) to high-resolution (HR) images with the original noise-to-image flow of the teacher model, preserving generative capabilities and photo-realism. A large model friendly training strategy is adopted, where noise-image pairs are generated offline by the teacher model, allowing the student model to be trained without requiring the teacher to be present during training, thus reducing memory and computational costs. The method incorporates two novel loss functions: TV-LPIPS, a perceptual loss combining total variation and LPIPS to emphasize high-frequency detail restoration and suppress artifacts, and Attention Diversification Loss (ADL), which regularizes transformer attention to reduce repetitive patterns and periodic artifacts. The final model is parameterized to support efficient one-step inference, using only a single flow model.
0c9796f5f6716ffdd40e2a8158221f5b631c44f6.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using 2400 noise-image pairs of size 1024x1024 generated by FLUX.1-dev for training, with corresponding low-resolution images created via the RealESRGAN degradation pipeline. Evaluation is performed on the DIV2K-val synthetic dataset and two real-world datasets: RealSR and RealSet65. The method is compared against both one-step and multi-step diffusion-based Real-ISR baselines, including StableSR, DiffBIR, SeeSR, ResShift, AddSR, SinSR, OSEDiff, and TSD-SR. Metrics include full-reference (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, DISTS) and no-reference (MUSIQ, MANIQA, TOPIQ, Q-Align) image quality measures. Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of FTD, TV-LPIPS, and ADL. The evaluation protocol includes both quantitative and qualitative comparisons, with all models tested on full-size images to reflect real-world performance.
0c9796f5f6716ffdd40e2a8158221f5b631c44f6.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to achieve one-step diffusion-based real-world image super-resolution using a large-scale model (over 12B parameters). Flow Trajectory Distillation (FTD) is introduced to explicitly align the LR-to-HR flow with the original noise-to-image flow, preserving the generative distribution and photo-realism of the teacher model. The large model friendly training strategy eliminates the need for the teacher model during online training, significantly reducing memory and computational requirements. The introduction of TV-LPIPS and ADL addresses high-frequency artifacts and repetitive patterns, leading to more realistic and artifact-free super-resolved images. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that the approach outperforms existing one-step diffusion-based Real-ISR methods on multiple benchmarks and metrics.

0caf98b5f5ff8e9476d55027473e15fca54292ff.title: All in One and One for All: A Simple yet Effective Method towards Cross-domain Graph Pretraining
0caf98b5f5ff8e9476d55027473e15fca54292ff.research_question: How can a unified pretraining framework be developed to enable effective cross-domain knowledge transfer and generalization for graph neural networks, particularly in few-shot learning scenarios across diverse graph domains?
0caf98b5f5ff8e9476d55027473e15fca54292ff.hypothesis: Introducing learnable virtual nodes (coordinators) to connect and align multiple heterogeneous graph datasets during pretraining will mitigate negative transfer and enhance the generalization and transferability of graph neural networks to downstream tasks, especially under few-shot settings.
0caf98b5f5ff8e9476d55027473e15fca54292ff.proposed_method: A novel cross-domain graph pretraining framework, named Graph Coordinators for Pretraining (GCOPE), will be developed to unify multiple graph datasets from different domains. The method begins by projecting node features from each source graph into a shared feature space using a non-parametric operation such as singular value decomposition (SVD), ensuring consistent feature dimensions. Virtual nodes, termed 'coordinators', are introduced for each graph and are fully connected to all nodes within their respective graphs, as well as interconnected across graphs, forming a joint adjacency matrix that enables information flow between otherwise isolated datasets. These coordinators are learnable parameters and facilitate both intra-graph and inter-graph alignment. The pretraining objective combines a contrastive loss (e.g., GraphCL or SimGRACE) for learning robust node and graph representations, with an auxiliary feature reconstruction loss to preserve original node information. The framework is designed to be compatible with both fine-tuning and prompt-based transferring techniques for downstream tasks.
0caf98b5f5ff8e9476d55027473e15fca54292ff.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on ten real-world graph datasets, including five homophilic (Cora, Citeseer, Pubmed, Computers, Photos) and five heterophilic (Wisconsin, Texas, Cornell, Chameleon, Squirrel) graphs, covering a range of structural and semantic diversity. The evaluation will focus on few-shot node classification tasks under C-way-K-shot settings, using 10-fold cross-validation where nine datasets serve as sources for pretraining and the remaining one as the target for transfer. Baselines will include supervised GNNs (GCN, GAT, BWGNN, FAGCN), isolated pretraining with fine-tuning (GraphCL, SimGRACE), and prompt-based transfer methods. Metrics such as accuracy, AUC-ROC, and F1-score will be used for quantitative comparison. Ablation studies will assess the impact of inter-coordinator connectivity, the reconstruction loss coefficient, and different feature projection operations (SVD vs. attention).
0caf98b5f5ff8e9476d55027473e15fca54292ff.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the concept of learnable coordinators as virtual nodes to unify and align multiple graph datasets during pretraining, enabling effective cross-domain knowledge transfer. Unlike previous approaches that pretrain on isolated or domain-specific graphs, this method constructs a joint graph structure with inter-dataset connectivity, addressing both structural and feature alignment challenges. The approach is compatible with various pretraining and transfer paradigms, including prompting, and demonstrates significant improvements in few-shot transfer learning scenarios, mitigating the negative transfer phenomenon commonly observed in cross-domain graph pretraining.

0ccc4f409c3630c4a3d68170a12fc72e15906559.title: HybridNorm: Towards Stable and Efficient Transformer Training via Hybrid Normalization
0ccc4f409c3630c4a3d68170a12fc72e15906559.research_question: How can normalization strategies be improved to enhance the stability and efficiency of training deep transformer models, particularly for large language models, without sacrificing final model performance?
0ccc4f409c3630c4a3d68170a12fc72e15906559.hypothesis: A hybrid normalization strategy that combines QKV normalization within the attention mechanism and Post-Norm in the feed-forward network will provide more stable training dynamics and improved downstream performance compared to using only Pre-Norm or Post-Norm approaches.
0ccc4f409c3630c4a3d68170a12fc72e15906559.proposed_method: A novel hybrid normalization framework, termed HybridNorm, will be developed for transformer architectures. In this approach, the query, key, and value (QKV) matrices in the attention mechanism are each normalized individually before the attention computation, a process referred to as QKV-Norm. The output of the attention mechanism is then combined with the input via residual connection. In the feed-forward network (FFN) sub-layer, normalization is applied after the residual connection, following the Post-Norm paradigm. Additionally, a variant (HybridNorm*) will be explored where the first transformer block uses Pre-Norm in both MHA and FFN, combined with QKV-Norm in MHA, to further stabilize early training. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to study gradient flow and the decoupling effects of QKV-Norm, and ablation studies will investigate the impact of normalization placement and initialization schemes.
0ccc4f409c3630c4a3d68170a12fc72e15906559.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both dense and Mixture of Experts (MoE) transformer models, with model sizes ranging from 151M to 7B parameters. Dense models (550M, 1.2B, and 7B) will follow architectures similar to LLaMA 3.2, while MoE models will utilize the OLMoE framework with up to 64 experts. All models will be trained from scratch on the OLMoE Mix dataset and evaluated on a diverse suite of benchmarks, including ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, PIQA, SciQ, CoQA, Winogrande, MMLU, BoolQ, COPA, CSQA, OBQA, and SocialIQA, using the LM Eval Harness for standardized evaluation. Baselines will include Pre-Norm, Post-Norm, and Mix-LN, with performance assessed via training loss, validation perplexity, and task accuracy. Hyperparameters such as optimizer (AdamW), learning rate schedules, and initialization schemes (Normal, Depth-Scaled, Megatron) will be systematically varied, and ablation studies will analyze the effects of normalization position and first-block treatment.
0ccc4f409c3630c4a3d68170a12fc72e15906559.novelty_claims: The proposed HybridNorm framework is the first to systematically integrate QKV normalization in the attention mechanism with Post-Norm in the FFN within each transformer block, leveraging the strengths of both Pre-Norm and Post-Norm strategies. This approach is claimed to provide more stable and efficient training, improved gradient flow, and superior downstream performance across a range of model sizes and architectures, including both dense and MoE transformers. The method is further distinguished by its theoretical analysis of gradient decoupling and its empirical validation across extensive benchmarks, outperforming existing normalization strategies such as Pre-Norm, Post-Norm, and Mix-LN.

0cee098244c9978032702862a43a09f468f691a4.title: Unlocking Efficiency in Large Language Model Inference: A Comprehensive Survey of Speculative Decoding
0cee098244c9978032702862a43a09f468f691a4.research_question: How can inference efficiency in large language models (LLMs) be improved by leveraging speculative decoding paradigms, and what are the key design choices, trade-offs, and evaluation criteria for such methods across diverse application scenarios?
0cee098244c9978032702862a43a09f468f691a4.hypothesis: Speculative decoding, which drafts multiple future tokens and verifies them in parallel, can substantially reduce inference latency in LLMs without compromising output quality, provided that key factors such as drafter selection, verification strategy, and behavior alignment are optimally addressed.
0cee098244c9978032702862a43a09f468f691a4.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework for speculative decoding will be developed, wherein each decoding step consists of two main substeps: (1) a drafter model (either an independent smaller language model, a non-autoregressive model, or a self-drafting mechanism within the target LLM) efficiently generates multiple candidate tokens in parallel; (2) the target LLM then verifies all drafted tokens in parallel using a specified verification criterion, such as greedy matching, speculative sampling, or token tree verification. The framework will support both independent and self-drafting strategies, allowing for flexible integration of knowledge distillation or alignment techniques to maximize speculation accuracy while minimizing drafting latency. The methodology will also include mechanisms for correcting or discarding drafted tokens that fail verification, and will investigate the impact of various drafting and verification strategies on speedup and output fidelity.
0cee098244c9978032702862a43a09f468f691a4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a unified benchmark, Spec-Bench, which covers a range of application scenarios including multi-turn conversation, translation, summarization, question answering, mathematical reasoning, and retrieval-augmented generation. Datasets such as MT-bench, WMT14 DE-EN, CNN/DailyMail, Natural Questions, GSM8K, and DPR will be used, with 80 samples per task. The proposed speculative decoding methods will be evaluated on open-source LLMs (e.g., Vicuna-7B, LLaMA, T5-XXL) under controlled hardware settings (e.g., single 3090 GPU, FP16 precision) to ensure fair comparison. Baselines will include standard autoregressive decoding and leading speculative decoding variants. Evaluation metrics will focus on inference speedup (tokens per second), output quality (e.g., exact match, BLEU, ROUGE), and acceptance rate of drafted tokens. Additional experiments will assess the impact of sampling temperature, batch size, and integration with advanced techniques such as continuous batching.
0cee098244c9978032702862a43a09f468f691a4.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a systematic and extensible framework for speculative decoding in LLMs, encompassing a formal taxonomy of drafting and verification strategies, and supports both independent and self-drafting paradigms. It will establish a comprehensive and reproducible benchmark (Spec-Bench) for fair and holistic evaluation of speculative decoding methods across diverse tasks and model architectures. The research will also explore novel alignment and knowledge distillation techniques to improve speculation accuracy, and investigate the integration of speculative decoding with batched inference and other efficiency-oriented methods, addressing key open challenges in the field.

0d04b5fe637e34de7b79fa4a03aaf9d9bc5c5b8e.title: Look Inside for More: Internal Spatial Modality Perception for 3D Anomaly Detection
0d04b5fe637e34de7b79fa4a03aaf9d9bc5c5b8e.research_question: How can the utilization of internal spatial information within 3D point clouds improve the effectiveness and reliability of anomaly detection in complex structures, and what new frameworks can be developed to better align and extract both global and local features for this task?
0d04b5fe637e34de7b79fa4a03aaf9d9bc5c5b8e.hypothesis: Leveraging internal spatial modality features within 3D point clouds, in addition to external structural information, will significantly enhance the accuracy and robustness of anomaly detection by providing more comprehensive and discriminative feature representations.
0d04b5fe637e34de7b79fa4a03aaf9d9bc5c5b8e.proposed_method: A novel framework, Internal Spatial Modality Perception (ISMP), will be developed to fully exploit internal spatial features of 3D point clouds for anomaly detection. The approach will consist of three main modules: (1) a Spatial Insight Engine (SIE) that abstracts complex internal information into essential global features by projecting the point cloud into multiple internal and external slices; (2) an enhanced keypoint feature extraction module that uses Farthest Point Sampling (FPS), PointMAE, and Fast Point Feature Histograms (FPFH) to amplify local spatial structure representations; and (3) a feature filtering module based on a Laplacian transform to suppress noise and redundant features, thereby improving feature alignment and quality. During training, memory banks for features and coordinates will be constructed, and during inference, anomaly scores will be computed by comparing test samples to these banks using nearest neighbor searches and re-weighting strategies.
0d04b5fe637e34de7b79fa4a03aaf9d9bc5c5b8e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two large-scale 3D anomaly detection datasets: Real3D-AD (12 categories, 1,254 samples) and Anomaly-ShapeNet (40 categories, over 1,600 samples). For each dataset, only a small number of normal samples will be used for training, with both normal and anomalous samples included in the test set. The method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as BTF, M3DM, PatchCore, CPMF, RegAD, and IMRNet, using both object-level AUROC (O-AUROC) and pixel-level AUROC (P-AUROC) as evaluation metrics. Additional ablation studies will be performed to assess the contribution of each module, and the generalization of SIE will be evaluated on point cloud classification (ModelNet40) and segmentation (ShapeNet-Part) tasks. All experiments will be run on an RTX 3090 GPU, and implementation details such as parameter settings and pre-trained weights will be specified.
0d04b5fe637e34de7b79fa4a03aaf9d9bc5c5b8e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to systematically focus on extracting and leveraging internal structural features of point clouds for 3D anomaly detection, rather than relying solely on external or pseudo-modal information. The introduction of the Spatial Insight Engine (SIE) enables comprehensive internal feature abstraction via multi-slice projections, while the enhanced feature extraction and Laplacian-based filtering modules further improve local and global feature alignment. The method demonstrates strong generalization across tasks and achieves significant improvements over state-of-the-art baselines in both object- and pixel-level anomaly detection metrics. The framework also provides a theoretically grounded and empirically validated approach for integrating internal spatial modality into 3D vision tasks.

0d1a6bdbbc7dfa5d26667503b6b1e3598c2ede42.title: Certifying the Absence of Spurious Local Minima at Infinity
0d1a6bdbbc7dfa5d26667503b6b1e3598c2ede42.research_question: How can one certify the absence of spurious local minima at infinity in nonconvex unconstrained optimization problems, particularly in cases where classical tools such as the gradient and Hessian are insufficient?
0d1a6bdbbc7dfa5d26667503b6b1e3598c2ede42.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that for a broad class of locally Lipschitz, lower-bounded functions with finitely many critical values and admitting a chain rule, the boundedness of subgradient trajectories is both necessary and sufficient to certify the absence of spurious local minima at infinity.
0d1a6bdbbc7dfa5d26667503b6b1e3598c2ede42.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed to extend the concept of setwise local minima by removing the boundedness assumption, thereby enabling the definition and analysis of spurious local minima at infinity. The approach will leverage the properties of subgradient trajectories for locally Lipschitz functions, utilizing the Clarke subdifferential to handle nonsmoothness. The main result will establish that, under the assumptions of local Lipschitz continuity, boundedness below, existence of a chain rule, and finitely many critical values, the absence of spurious local minima is equivalent to the absence of spurious setwise local minima, provided that all subgradient trajectories are bounded. The method will also provide practical criteria for checking these conditions in applications such as deep linear neural networks, matrix sensing, and certain matrix factorization problems.
0d1a6bdbbc7dfa5d26667503b6b1e3598c2ede42.experiment_details: Theoretical analysis will be complemented by case studies on several representative optimization problems, including deep linear neural networks, one-dimensional deep neural networks with sigmoid activation, matrix recovery with the restricted isometry property, and nonsmooth matrix factorization with rank-one matrices. For each application, the proposed criteria will be checked to confirm the absence of spurious local minima at infinity. Numerical experiments, such as gradient descent runs on matrix completion problems, will be conducted to illustrate scenarios where classical analysis fails and to empirically validate the theoretical predictions. Evaluation will focus on the presence or absence of spurious local minima at infinity, convergence behavior of first-order methods, and the boundedness of subgradient trajectories.
0d1a6bdbbc7dfa5d26667503b6b1e3598c2ede42.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified theoretical device for certifying the absence of spurious local minima at infinity in a broad class of nonconvex optimization problems, including nonsmooth cases. By generalizing the notion of setwise local minima and linking it to the boundedness of subgradient trajectories, the approach overcomes the limitations of classical gradient and Hessian-based landscape analysis. The method provides easily checkable conditions for practical problems in machine learning and optimization, and establishes new connections between landscape properties and the convergence of first-order methods.

0d1c76d45afa012ded7ab741194baf142117c495.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
0d1c76d45afa012ded7ab741194baf142117c495.research_question: How can language models be fine-tuned to align with human preferences in a stable, efficient, and scalable manner, avoiding the complexity and instability of traditional reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) pipelines?
0d1c76d45afa012ded7ab741194baf142117c495.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a direct optimization of language model policies using a preference-based classification loss, bypassing explicit reward modeling and reinforcement learning, can achieve alignment with human preferences as effectively or better than existing RLHF methods, while being more stable and computationally efficient.
0d1c76d45afa012ded7ab741194baf142117c495.proposed_method: A new algorithm, Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), is proposed for fine-tuning language models directly from human preference data. DPO leverages a closed-form reparameterization of the reward model, enabling direct optimization of the policy using a simple binary cross-entropy loss derived from the Bradley-Terry preference model. The method eliminates the need for explicit reward model fitting and reinforcement learning by analytically mapping the reward function to the optimal policy, allowing the language model to implicitly represent both the policy and reward. The DPO loss increases the log-probability of preferred responses relative to dispreferred ones, weighted by a dynamic importance factor that prevents model degeneration. The approach is theoretically grounded, ensuring equivalence to the optimal policy under standard preference models, and is implemented as a single-stage supervised learning procedure.
0d1c76d45afa012ded7ab741194baf142117c495.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three open-ended text generation tasks: sentiment-controlled generation (using the IMDB dataset), summarization (using the Reddit TL;DR dataset with human preference annotations), and single-turn dialogue (using the Anthropic Helpful and Harmless dataset). For each task, models will be fine-tuned using DPO and compared against several baselines, including supervised fine-tuning on preferred completions, unlikelihood training, PPO-based RLHF (with both learned and ground-truth rewards), and the 'Best of N' sampling strategy. Evaluation metrics include the frontier of achieved reward versus KL-divergence from the reference policy (where ground-truth reward is available), as well as win rates against baseline completions as judged by GPT-4 and human raters.
