Hyperparameter sweeps (e.g., for KL constraint and loss coefficients) will be performed, and robustness to sampling temperature and generalization to out-of-distribution inputs (e.g., CNN/DailyMail for summarization) will be assessed.
0d1c76d45afa012ded7ab741194baf142117c495.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a theoretically justified, RL-free approach to preference-based fine-tuning of language models, reducing the complexity and instability associated with RLHF. DPO enables direct policy optimization from preference data via a closed-form objective, eliminating the need for explicit reward modeling, policy sampling during training, and extensive hyperparameter tuning. The approach is claimed to be computationally lightweight, stable, and at least as effective as state-of-the-art RLHF methods, with empirical results showing superior or comparable alignment with human preferences across multiple tasks and datasets. DPO also demonstrates improved robustness to sampling temperature and generalizes well to out-of-distribution data.

0d23e85bd975f3f2401f5b76d13c1cc120374fee.title: Differentiable Euler Characteristic Transforms for Shape Classification
0d23e85bd975f3f2401f5b76d13c1cc120374fee.research_question: How can a topological shape descriptor be made differentiable and efficiently integrated into deep learning models for shape classification across diverse data modalities such as point clouds, graphs, and meshes?
0d23e85bd975f3f2401f5b76d13c1cc120374fee.hypothesis: A differentiable formulation of the Euler Characteristic Transform (ECT) can be developed that enables end-to-end learning of topological shape representations, resulting in scalable, efficient, and expressive models for shape classification tasks, potentially matching or surpassing the performance of more complex topological deep learning layers.
0d23e85bd975f3f2401f5b76d13c1cc120374fee.proposed_method: A novel computational layer, termed the Differentiable Euler Characteristic Transform (DECT), will be developed by reformulating the ECT as a sum of differentiable functions. The standard ECT, which is based on indicator functions and thus non-differentiable, will be approximated by replacing indicator functions with sigmoid functions, controlled by a sharpness parameter. This enables gradients to be computed with respect to both the filter directions and the input coordinates, allowing the ECT to be used as a trainable layer or loss term in neural networks. The DECT will be integrated into neural architectures by embedding individual Euler Characteristic Curves (ECCs) using a permutation-equivariant multilayer perceptron (MLP), followed by a pooling operation to obtain permutation-invariant representations, and a final classification MLP. The approach will be fully vectorized and parallelizable, leveraging GPU acceleration for scalability.
0d23e85bd975f3f2401f5b76d13c1cc120374fee.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of datasets, including MNIST (as point clouds and superpixel graphs), ModelNet40 (3D shape point clouds), and standard graph classification benchmarks (e.g., BZR, COX2, DHFR, Letter datasets). The DECT-based models will be compared against baseline methods such as MLPs, convolutional neural networks, and established graph neural networks (GAT, GCN, GIN, GraphSage). Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy and runtime per epoch. The experimental setup will involve preprocessing to normalize and center coordinates, an 80/20 train/test split with a validation set, and training with the ADAM optimizer. Hyperparameters such as the number of directions and discretization steps for the ECT will be systematically varied to study their impact on classification performance and scalability. Additional experiments will demonstrate the ability to optimize both filter directions and input coordinates in an end-to-end differentiable manner, including shape matching and topological regularization tasks.
0d23e85bd975f3f2401f5b76d13c1cc120374fee.novelty_claims: The proposed method constitutes the first differentiable and end-to-end trainable formulation of the Euler Characteristic Transform, enabling its seamless integration into deep learning models as a layer or loss term. The approach is highly scalable, computationally efficient, and applicable to various data modalities, including point clouds, graphs, and meshes, without restrictions on object size or connectivity. DECT achieves performance on par with or superior to more complex topological deep learning layers while being orders of magnitude faster. The method also provides new capabilities for topological optimization and interpretability by allowing the learning of filter directions and input coordinates in a differentiable fashion.

0d24c5680efe9769e6d7ea579db0499ec819a8c7.title: Scaling and evaluating sparse autoencoders
0d24c5680efe9769e6d7ea579db0499ec819a8c7.research_question: How can sparse autoencoders be scaled and evaluated to reliably extract interpretable features from large language model activations, and what are the best practices for controlling sparsity, preventing dead latents, and measuring feature quality at scale?
0d24c5680efe9769e6d7ea579db0499ec819a8c7.hypothesis: Directly controlling sparsity in autoencoders using k-sparse activation functions, combined with targeted initialization and auxiliary losses, will enable the training of extremely large and sparse autoencoders with minimal dead latents, improved reconstruction-sparsity tradeoffs, and enhanced interpretability of extracted features.
0d24c5680efe9769e6d7ea579db0499ec819a8c7.proposed_method: A methodology will be developed for training extremely wide and sparse autoencoders on the residual stream activations of large language models, such as GPT-2 small and GPT-4. The approach will employ k-sparse autoencoders with a TopK activation function, which retains only the k largest latent activations per input, thereby directly controlling sparsity and eliminating the need for L1 penalties. Encoder weights will be initialized as the transpose of the decoder, and an auxiliary loss will be added to model reconstruction error using the top-k dead latents, which helps prevent dead latents even at large scales. The training loss will be mean squared error (MSE) between input and reconstruction, and hyperparameters such as learning rate will be systematically tuned or extrapolated for large models. Additional techniques, such as Multi-TopK losses, will be explored to ensure progressive coding properties.
0d24c5680efe9769e6d7ea579db0499ec819a8c7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the residual stream activations of both GPT-2 small and a series of increasingly large models sharing the GPT-4 architecture, including GPT-4 itself. Autoencoders will be trained at various layers (e.g., layer 8 for GPT-2 small, layer 5/6 for GPT-4) with a context length of 64 tokens. The number of latents and sparsity levels will be systematically varied, with models trained up to 16 million latents on 40 billion tokens. Baselines will include ReLU, ProLU, Gated, and other activation functions. Evaluation metrics will include normalized reconstruction MSE, downstream cross-entropy and KL divergence (by substituting reconstructions into the language model), probe loss on 61 binary classification tasks, explainability via n-gram-based NeurontoGraph (N2G) explanations, and sparsity of downstream effects measured by ablation. Scaling laws relating model size, sparsity, and reconstruction error will be characterized, and the effect of different activation functions and mitigation strategies for dead latents will be compared.
0d24c5680efe9769e6d7ea579db0499ec819a8c7.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a scalable recipe for training extremely large and sparse autoencoders with minimal dead latents, enabled by the use of k-sparse TopK activation functions and targeted initialization and auxiliary losses. Clean scaling laws for autoencoder size and sparsity are established. Several new metrics for evaluating feature quality are proposed, including recovery of hypothesized features, explainability of activation patterns, and sparsity of downstream effects. The approach demonstrates the ability to train a 16-million-latent autoencoder on GPT-4 activations and provides open-source code, pretrained models, and a visualizer for interpretability research.

0d2adcddccd72de47c263b6e4e0aab3dd0582a52.title: ReLoRA: High-Rank Training Through Low-Rank Updates
0d2adcddccd72de47c263b6e4e0aab3dd0582a52.research_question: Can parameter-efficient training techniques be developed to enable efficient pre-training of large-scale neural networks, particularly transformer language models, without sacrificing model performance or requiring full-rank updates?
0d2adcddccd72de47c263b6e4e0aab3dd0582a52.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a sequence of low-rank updates, when properly aggregated and combined with appropriate optimization strategies, can effectively train high-rank neural networks, achieving performance comparable to full-rank training while significantly reducing memory and computational requirements.
0d2adcddccd72de47c263b6e4e0aab3dd0582a52.proposed_method: A novel training framework, ReLoRA, will be developed to train high-rank neural networks through a series of low-rank updates. The approach begins with a brief full-rank 'warm start' training phase, after which all linear layers are replaced with low-rank adapters following the LoRA methodology. During training, ReLoRA periodically merges the accumulated low-rank updates into the main model weights, resets the low-rank parameters, and partially resets the optimizer state using magnitude pruning. A jagged cosine learning rate schedule is employed, with the learning rate set to zero and quickly warmed up after each reset to stabilize training. This process is repeated multiple times, enabling the effective rank of the updates to increase over time, thereby approximating full-rank training dynamics while maintaining parameter efficiency.
0d2adcddccd72de47c263b6e4e0aab3dd0582a52.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on transformer-based language models with sizes ranging from 60M to 1.3B parameters, using the C4 dataset for pre-training. The experimental setup will include comparisons against full-rank training, standard LoRA, LoRA with warm start, and a control baseline with the same number of trainable parameters as ReLoRA. Evaluation metrics will include language modeling perplexity and downstream task performance on the GLUE benchmark. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of key components such as restarts, optimizer resets, learning rate scheduling, and warm starts. Hardware efficiency will be evaluated across different GPU setups, measuring training speed, memory consumption, and throughput.
0d2adcddccd72de47c263b6e4e0aab3dd0582a52.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new approach for parameter-efficient pre-training of large neural networks by leveraging the rank-of-sum property to achieve high-rank updates through multiple low-rank steps. Unlike existing low-rank training techniques, ReLoRA combines periodic merging of low-rank adapters, partial optimizer resets, and a jagged learning rate schedule to stabilize and enhance training dynamics. This framework enables substantial reductions in memory usage and training time, especially for multi-billion-parameter models, without significant loss in model performance. The approach is demonstrated to outperform standard low-rank methods and closely match full-rank training, representing a significant advancement in scalable, efficient neural network training.

0d3a331e7e91392cd2422a5c57ab4fd7fc1b3518.title: Optimal Stochastic Non-smooth Non-convex Optimization through Online-to-Non-convex Conversion
0d3a331e7e91392cd2422a5c57ab4fd7fc1b3518.research_question: How can the complexity of optimizing non-smooth, non-convex stochastic objectives be improved, and what are the fundamental limits of first-order algorithms for finding approximate stationary points in this setting?
0d3a331e7e91392cd2422a5c57ab4fd7fc1b3518.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by reducing non-smooth, non-convex stochastic optimization to an online learning problem with shifting regret, it is possible to achieve an improved and optimal complexity rate for finding approximate stationary points, specifically (δ,ϵ)-stationary points.
0d3a331e7e91392cd2422a5c57ab4fd7fc1b3518.proposed_method: A novel reduction from non-smooth, non-convex stochastic optimization to online learning with shifting regret is proposed. The approach involves designing an optimization algorithm where each update direction is determined by an online learning algorithm, which is fed linear losses constructed from stochastic gradients of the objective function. The method leverages randomized perturbations to handle non-smoothness, ensuring that gradients are evaluated at points along line segments between iterates. Online learning algorithms, such as Online Gradient Descent (OGD) with periodic resets, are employed to minimize shifting regret, and the update step is clipped to maintain bounded movement. Theoretical analysis connects the regret bounds of the online learning algorithm to the convergence rate for finding (δ,ϵ)-stationary points.
0d3a331e7e91392cd2422a5c57ab4fd7fc1b3518.experiment_details: The proposed algorithms will be analyzed through theoretical complexity bounds, focusing on the number of stochastic gradient evaluations required to find (δ,ϵ)-stationary points. The analysis considers both stochastic and deterministic settings, as well as smooth and second-order smooth objectives. The primary evaluation metric is the expected norm of the averaged gradient over a finite subset of points within a δ-ball around the iterate, as defined by the (δ,ϵ)-stationarity criterion. Baseline comparisons include existing complexity results for stochastic gradient descent and other first-order methods under various smoothness assumptions. Theoretical lower bounds are established to demonstrate optimality.
0d3a331e7e91392cd2422a5c57ab4fd7fc1b3518.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new reduction from non-smooth, non-convex stochastic optimization to online learning, enabling the use of advanced online learning algorithms to accelerate non-convex optimization. This yields an improved complexity of O(ϵ⁻³δ⁻¹) stochastic gradient evaluations for finding (δ,ϵ)-stationary points, surpassing the previous best-known rate of O(ϵ⁻⁴δ⁻¹). The method is shown to be optimal, and the framework recovers or improves all optimal or best-known results for smooth and second-order smooth objectives in both stochastic and deterministic settings. The approach also generalizes to directional gradient oracles and provides new insights into the relationship between online learning and non-convex optimization.

0d4a5161b6ac6d19f473d67e63050a15b5eb70f7.title: Classically Approximating Variational Quantum Machine Learning with Random Fourier Features
0d4a5161b6ac6d19f473d67e63050a15b5eb70f7.research_question: Can classical machine learning methods efficiently approximate the functions learned by variational quantum circuits (VQCs) in quantum machine learning, and under what conditions does a quantum advantage persist?
0d4a5161b6ac6d19f473d67e63050a15b5eb70f7.hypothesis: Random Fourier Features (RFF) can efficiently approximate the output of VQCs for a wide range of encoding strategies, particularly when the quantum feature space exhibits redundancy or limited complexity. Quantum advantage may only persist for VQCs with highly complex, non-diagonalizable encoding Hamiltonians or very high input dimensions.
0d4a5161b6ac6d19f473d67e63050a15b5eb70f7.proposed_method: A classical approximation framework will be developed to mimic the behavior of VQCs by leveraging the equivalence between VQCs and large Fourier series. The approach will analyze the encoding gates of a given VQC to extract its frequency spectrum, then employ Random Fourier Features (RFF) to sample a tractable subset of these frequencies. Three RFF-based sampling strategies will be implemented: (1) Distinct sampling, which samples directly from the set of distinct frequencies derived from the VQC architecture; (2) Tree sampling, which samples paths through the eigenvalue tree of the encoding Hamiltonians, naturally weighting redundant frequencies; and (3) Grid sampling, which constructs a regular frequency grid when the spectrum is unknown or intractable. Theoretical bounds will be derived for the number of samples required to approximate the VQC output within a specified error, considering the structure and redundancy of the quantum spectrum.
0d4a5161b6ac6d19f473d67e63050a15b5eb70f7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real datasets. Synthetic experiments will include random VQCs with various encoding strategies (Pauli encoding, complex Hamiltonians, and scaled Pauli gates) and varying input dimensions, with datasets constructed to satisfy the Shannon sampling criterion for the relevant frequency spectra. The RFF-based classical models will be trained on the same datasets as the VQCs, and performance will be compared using training and test loss metrics. Baselines will include direct kernel ridge regression using the full quantum spectrum (when tractable) and standard VQC training. Evaluation metrics will focus on approximation error between the RFF model and the VQC output, as well as the number of frequency samples required to achieve a given error threshold. Additional experiments will explore the impact of spectrum redundancy, input dimension, and encoding complexity on the efficiency of the classical approximation.
0d4a5161b6ac6d19f473d67e63050a15b5eb70f7.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a systematic framework for classically approximating VQCs using Random Fourier Features, supported by new theoretical bounds on sample complexity that account for the structure and redundancy of the quantum frequency spectrum. The approach identifies regimes where classical approximations are efficient and highlights specific conditions—such as complex, non-diagonalizable Hamiltonians or high input dimensionality—where quantum advantage may persist. This work narrows the conditions for quantum advantage in variational quantum machine learning and provides practical tools for benchmarking and understanding the expressive power of VQCs relative to classical methods.

0d59d7a86c822a671e4ef1eabae0846e5f6edfb7.title: Linear bandits with limited adaptivity and learning distributional optimal design
0d59d7a86c822a671e4ef1eabae0846e5f6edfb7.research_question: What is the minimum amount of adaptivity required to achieve minimax-optimal regret in linear contextual bandits under limited adaptivity models, and how can optimal experiment design be extended to stochastic context settings to enable efficient learning?
0d59d7a86c822a671e4ef1eabae0846e5f6edfb7.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that minimax-optimal regret in linear contextual bandits can be achieved with substantially limited adaptivity, specifically O(d log d log T) policy switches for adversarial contexts and O(log log T) batches for stochastic contexts, and that a distributional extension of optimal experiment design can facilitate efficient learning in stochastic settings.
0d59d7a86c822a671e4ef1eabae0846e5f6edfb7.proposed_method: A comprehensive study will be conducted on linear contextual bandits under two limited adaptivity models: batch learning and rare policy switches. For stochastic contexts, a batch elimination framework will be developed, leveraging a novel distributional optimal design approach that generalizes the classical G-optimal experiment design to stochastic context sets. This involves constructing a mixed-softmax policy parameterized by O(d^3 log d) real values, learned via a CoreLearning algorithm that identifies a core subset of empirical samples and iteratively prunes insufficiently explored directions. For adversarial contexts, a rarely switching algorithm will be devised by combining OFUL and SupLinUCB, maintaining only O(log d) information matrices and employing a determinant-based doubling trick to control the number of policy switches. Theoretical analysis will establish the existence and learnability of near-optimal policies under these constraints.
0d59d7a86c822a671e4ef1eabae0846e5f6edfb7.experiment_details: Experiments will be designed to evaluate the regret performance of the proposed algorithms under both adversarial and stochastic context settings. Synthetic datasets will be generated for both types of context generation, with varying dimensionality d, number of actions K, and time horizon T. Baselines will include standard fully adaptive linear bandit algorithms, batch algorithms for multi-armed bandits, and previous batch linear bandit methods with restrictive assumptions. Evaluation metrics will focus on cumulative regret, number of policy switches or batches, and computational efficiency. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by aligning context distributions and reward models across methods.
0d59d7a86c822a671e4ef1eabae0846e5f6edfb7.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the distributional optimal design framework, extending classical experiment design to stochastic context sets and enabling efficient batch learning in linear contextual bandits. It establishes tight adaptivity-regret trade-offs for both adversarial and stochastic settings, demonstrating that minimax-optimal regret can be achieved with significantly fewer policy switches or batches than previously known. The CoreLearning algorithm and the mixed-softmax policy provide statistically and computationally efficient solutions for learning optimal designs from finite samples. These contributions present a nearly complete characterization of adaptivity requirements in linear contextual bandits and offer new algorithmic tools for parallel and collaborative online learning.

0d777e8fce96a559b794976aceede98ea508c77f.title: Can In-context Learning Really Generalize to Out-of-distribution Tasks?
0d777e8fce96a559b794976aceede98ea508c77f.research_question: Can in-context learning (ICL) in large language models generalize to out-of-distribution (OOD) tasks, and what mechanisms underlie ICL's performance on such tasks?
0d777e8fce96a559b794976aceede98ea508c77f.hypothesis: ICL in large language models is limited to implementing functions within the pretraining hypothesis space and does not inherently generalize to OOD tasks; instead, it tends to select or retrieve pretraining functions that minimize test error or match input distributions in the downstream context.
0d777e8fce96a559b794976aceede98ea508c77f.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical and theoretical investigation will be conducted to analyze the generalization capabilities of ICL on OOD tasks. Synthetic experiments will be designed where GPT-2 models are pretrained on specific mathematical function classes (e.g., linear regression, quadratic regression, ReLU neural networks) and then evaluated on both in-distribution and OOD function classes. Additional experiments will probe the ability of ICL to perform classification with abstract labels, using both synthetic retrieval tasks and real-world LLMs (e.g., Llama-2, Llama-3) on tasks with unseen label mappings. Theoretical analysis will be developed to characterize the algorithm selection mechanism in ICL, focusing on the preference for pretraining functions with low test error and similar input distributions. Empirical validation of these theoretical predictions will be performed using both synthetic and real-world tasks, including ambiguous sentence classification in natural language.
0d777e8fce96a559b794976aceede98ea508c77f.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training GPT-2 models from scratch on various function classes, then evaluating their ICL performance on both seen and unseen (OOD) function classes using synthetic datasets where input vectors are sampled from Gaussian distributions. Baselines will include models trained via gradient descent on the same function classes using the in-context examples. Additional experiments will use pretrained Llama-2-7B and Llama-3-8B models on synthetic word classification and retrieval tasks, as well as ambiguous sentence classification tasks with abstract label mappings. Evaluation metrics will include test squared error for regression tasks and top-1/top-5 accuracy for classification tasks. Key experimental setups will control for the number of in-context examples, the diversity of pretraining tasks, and the distributional shifts between training and testing functions.
0d777e8fce96a559b794976aceede98ea508c77f.novelty_claims: The proposed research claims to provide a unified empirical and theoretical framework for understanding the limitations of ICL on OOD tasks. It introduces novel synthetic experiments demonstrating that ICL performance is constrained to the pretraining hypothesis space and does not represent true OOD generalization. The research further elucidates that ICL's ability to handle abstract labels is a consequence of retrieval capabilities acquired during pretraining, not genuine new-task learning. Theoretical contributions include formalizing the algorithm selection mechanism in ICL, showing a preference for pretraining functions with lower test error or similar input distributions, and empirically validating these mechanisms in both synthetic and real-world LLM settings.

0d7ed4a2e9e02d46a938319d2a5ea44b8344e773.title: Weighted Point Set Embedding for Multimodal Contrastive Learning Toward Optimal Similarity Metric
0d7ed4a2e9e02d46a938319d2a5ea44b8344e773.research_question: How can multimodal contrastive learning frameworks be enhanced to better capture complex similarity structures and relationships among real-world instances, moving beyond single-point embeddings to achieve more optimal similarity metrics for downstream tasks?
0d7ed4a2e9e02d46a938319d2a5ea44b8344e773.hypothesis: Utilizing weighted point set embeddings, where each instance is represented as a set of weighted vectors and similarity is computed via a kernel function, will enable multimodal contrastive learning models to more closely approximate the optimal similarity metric (pointwise mutual information), resulting in improved representation capacity and downstream task performance compared to traditional single-point, cosine similarity-based approaches.
0d7ed4a2e9e02d46a938319d2a5ea44b8344e773.proposed_method: A new multimodal contrastive learning framework is developed in which each input (e.g., image or text) is encoded into a weighted point set, consisting of multiple pairs of scalar weights and vector embeddings. The similarity between two instances is defined as the sum over all pairs of weights multiplied by a kernel function applied to their respective vectors, allowing for both linear and nonlinear similarity measures. Encoders are implemented using Transformer architectures (e.g., Vision Transformer for images and Transformer for text), modified to output all token vectors and corresponding weights, rather than a single pooled vector. The kernel function is a linear combination of a linear kernel and a nonlinear kernel (such as Gaussian or IMQ), with random Fourier features (RFFs) used to efficiently approximate the nonlinear component. The overall model is trained using a symmetric InfoNCE contrastive loss, with the kernel-based similarity replacing the standard cosine similarity.
0d7ed4a2e9e02d46a938319d2a5ea44b8344e773.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted by pretraining text-image representation models on large-scale datasets such as Conceptual Captions 3M (CC3M) and Conceptual Captions 12M (CC12M). The base architectures include ViT-B/16 for images and a small CLIP-style Transformer for text, both modified to output weighted point sets. The proposed method is compared against standard CLIP models trained from scratch, using both zero-shot and linear classification evaluations on 13 benchmark datasets (including ImageNet, CIFAR-10/100, STL-10, Food-101, Caltech-101, Stanford Cars, FGVCAircraft, Oxford Flowers, EuroSAT, DTD, Oxford Pets, and SUN397). Evaluation metrics include mean per-class accuracy and top-1 accuracy, with prompt ensembling used for zero-shot classification. Hyperparameters for the kernel and RFFs are tuned via search, and ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of kernel choice and weight constraints.
0d7ed4a2e9e02d46a938319d2a5ea44b8344e773.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the use of weighted point set embeddings for multimodal contrastive learning, enabling richer and more flexible similarity structures than traditional single-point, cosine similarity-based methods. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that this method can consistently approximate the optimal similarity (pointwise mutual information) under mild assumptions, overcoming representational limitations of inner-product-based similarities. The framework is implemented efficiently using Transformer encoders and random Fourier feature approximations, and empirical results show superior performance on standard benchmarks. The method also provides new theoretical insights linking optimal similarity in contrastive learning to improved downstream linear classification performance.

0d88e13ccdbfd4a060d9c29f20b9dcb54097cacd.title: Grammars of Formal Uncertainty: When to Trust LLMs in Automated Reasoning Tasks
0d88e13ccdbfd4a060d9c29f20b9dcb54097cacd.research_question: How can uncertainty in large language model (LLM) outputs for automated formal reasoning tasks be systematically quantified and leveraged to improve the reliability of LLM-driven formal artifact generation and verification workflows?
0d88e13ccdbfd4a060d9c29f20b9dcb54097cacd.hypothesis: Probabilistic context-free grammar (PCFG)-based modeling of LLM-generated formal artifacts provides more precise and actionable uncertainty quantification than conventional token-level or ensemble-based uncertainty metrics, enabling selective verification that significantly reduces error rates in automated reasoning tasks.
0d88e13ccdbfd4a060d9c29f20b9dcb54097cacd.proposed_method: A probabilistic framework is developed that models the distribution of LLM-generated formal artifacts—specifically, SMT-LIB programs—using probabilistic context-free grammars (PCFGs). Ensembles of LLM outputs are parsed into PCFGs, and rule probabilities are estimated via maximum likelihood estimation, with optional Bayesian or neural extensions for richer context modeling. Multiple uncertainty metrics are derived from the PCFGs, including grammar entropy, Rényi entropy, perplexity, KL divergence, and a novel composite metric (NSUI) that combines normalized entropy with structural complexity (spectral radius). These metrics are used to characterize and diagnose uncertainty in the formalization process. Additionally, lightweight, model-agnostic fusion techniques (such as unweighted/weighted metric ensembles and meta-machine learning models) are employed to combine uncertainty signals for improved calibration and error detection.
0d88e13ccdbfd4a060d9c29f20b9dcb54097cacd.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on four widely used formal reasoning datasets: StrategyQA, ProntoQA, ProofWriter, and FOLIO. Five frontier LLMs (o3-mini, DeepSeekR1, DeepSeek-v3-04-21, GeminiFlash2.0, GeminiFlash2.0Lite) are evaluated, with each model generating five samples per question. Both direct text outputs and SMT-LIB formalizations (solved by Z3) are compared. Evaluation metrics include accuracy, AUROC, AURC, ECE, Brier score, and error reduction rates, assessing both ground truth correctness and consistency between SMT and text outputs. Baselines include conventional uncertainty quantification methods (e.g., token entropy, perplexity) and ensemble-based predictors. Selective verification is tested by applying uncertainty thresholds to abstain from low-confidence predictions, and ablation studies examine the effect of sampling temperature and metric calibration.
0d88e13ccdbfd4a060d9c29f20b9dcb54097cacd.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a PCFG-based uncertainty quantification framework for LLM-generated formal artifacts, offering a mathematically grounded and interpretable approach that bridges neural generative models and formal verification. It develops a comprehensive taxonomy of uncertainty, distinguishing between epistemic-knowledge, epistemic-procedural, recursive-complexity, and capacity-limited sources. The approach demonstrates that localized, grammar-derived uncertainty metrics can outperform conventional methods in error detection and calibration, and that lightweight fusion of these signals enables substantial error rate reductions with minimal abstention. The method is model-agnostic, incurs minimal computational overhead, and provides new diagnostic insights into LLM reasoning failures, paving the way for more reliable neurosymbolic systems.

0d91913396469ecd016caaebc86ef70fd11fd3c8.title: IF-GUIDE: Influence Function-Guided Detoxification of LLMs
0d91913396469ecd016caaebc86ef70fd11fd3c8.research_question: How can toxic content in the training data of large language models be identified and proactively suppressed to prevent the emergence of toxic behaviors in model outputs, without relying on human-preference data or reactive alignment methods?
0d91913396469ecd016caaebc86ef70fd11fd3c8.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging influence functions to identify and penalize the most toxicity-promoting tokens in the training data will substantially reduce both explicit and implicit toxicity in large language models, while preserving fluency and task performance, and improving robustness to adversarial prompts.
0d91913396469ecd016caaebc86ef70fd11fd3c8.proposed_method: A novel framework, IF-GUIDE, is developed to proactively detoxify large language models by leveraging influence functions to identify and suppress harmful tokens in the training data. The method first computes token-level influence scores by contrasting the effect of training examples on toxic versus non-toxic queries, using an efficient Hessian approximation (EK-FAC) and differential attribution. Token-level attribution is performed to localize toxic content within documents, and a document-based importance ranking is used to select tokens most responsible for toxicity, including their surrounding context. A penalty-based training objective is then introduced, which penalizes the model for assigning high probability to identified toxic tokens during both pre-training and fine-tuning, while rewarding accurate prediction of benign tokens. The approach is designed to be computationally efficient by employing proxy models for influence computation and batching techniques.
0d91913396469ecd016caaebc86ef70fd11fd3c8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple open-source LLMs (Pythia 160M–12B, Llama-3.2-1B) using a one-billion-token subset of OpenWebText for training, with four epochs per run. Toxicity reduction will be evaluated on RealToxicityPrompts (RTP), BOLD, and AttaQ benchmarks, using up to 10,000 prompts per benchmark and generating 25 completions per prompt with nucleus sampling. Toxicity will be measured using the Detoxify classifier (for explicit toxicity) and ToxiGen-RoBERTa (for implicit toxicity), reporting Expected Maximum Toxicity (EMT) and Toxicity Probability (TP). Fluency will be evaluated by perplexity (PPL) on OpenWebText and accuracy (Acc.) on LAMBADA. Baselines will include word filtering, toxicity filtering, Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), and Reward Augmented Decoding (RAD). Additional experiments will assess robustness to adversarial prompts, the impact of proxy model size, and mechanistic interpretability of internal model representations.
0d91913396469ecd016caaebc86ef70fd11fd3c8.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first proactive, influence-function-guided method for identifying and suppressing toxicity-promoting training tokens at scale, with token-level attribution and a penalty-based training objective that does not require human-preference data. The approach is model-agnostic, computationally efficient, and scalable to billion-parameter LLMs using proxy models and efficient Hessian approximations. IF-GUIDE enables substantial reductions in both explicit and implicit toxicity, preserves model fluency, and improves robustness to adversarial prompts, outperforming existing filtering and alignment-based baselines. The method also provides a unified framework compatible with existing alignment techniques, yielding additive benefits.

0d9276843992471971a56729f4b8c5aaf0208571.title: Learning Distribution-Wise Control in Representation Space for Language Models
0d9276843992471971a56729f4b8c5aaf0208571.research_question: How can more effective and robust control over language model behavior be achieved by leveraging interventions in the representation space, particularly at the distribution level rather than pointwise interventions?
0d9276843992471971a56729f4b8c5aaf0208571.hypothesis: Distribution-wise interventions in the representation space of language models, which learn and manipulate distributions rather than single points, will enable finer-grained, more robust, and more controllable steering of model behavior compared to traditional pointwise interventions.
0d9276843992471971a56729f4b8c5aaf0208571.proposed_method: A novel intervention framework is developed that replaces deterministic nodes (e.g., standard MLP layers) in language models with stochastic nodes capable of learning a distribution over latent representations. This is achieved by introducing two parallel neural networks to independently predict the mean (μ) and log-variance (logσ²) of the latent distribution at selected layers. The reparameterization trick is employed to allow efficient gradient-based optimization, enabling the model to sample from the learned distribution during training while maintaining differentiability. Model-specific clamping is applied to ensure numerical stability by restricting the range of sampled values based on adjacent layer weights. The approach is designed as a drop-in replacement for existing intervention-based methods and is evaluated in both layer-wise and all-layer configurations, with a focus on early-layer interventions and mixed strategies combining stochastic and deterministic nodes.
0d9276843992471971a56729f4b8c5aaf0208571.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on Llama-family language models (Llama-7B/13B, Llama-2-7B, Llama-3-8B) using a single NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU with mixed precision. The evaluation spans eight commonsense reasoning benchmarks (e.g., BoolQ, PIQA, SIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-e, ARC-c, OBQA) and seven arithmetic reasoning benchmarks (e.g., AddSub, SingleEQ, MultiArith, AQuA, GSM8K, MAWPS, SVAMP). Baselines include pointwise intervention methods (MLP, RED, SwiGLU, ReFT) and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods (Prefix-tuning, Adapter, LoRA, DoRA). The proposed method is compared in both layer-wise and all-layer settings, with ablation studies on the proportion of layers replaced, the effect of noise scaling, and the number of intervention parameters. Evaluation metrics are primarily accuracy on the respective benchmarks, with additional robustness tests involving adversarial input perturbations (e.g., random word deletion) and analysis of test-time stochasticity via temperature scaling.
0d9276843992471971a56729f4b8c5aaf0208571.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces distribution-wise interventions in the representation space of language models, enabling the learning and manipulation of latent distributions rather than single-point transformations. This method provides a principled, information-theoretic framework for intervention, leverages the reparameterization trick for efficient optimization, and demonstrates that early-layer stochastic interventions yield significant improvements in controllability, robustness, and performance across a wide range of reasoning tasks. The approach is shown to outperform both existing pointwise intervention methods and state-of-the-art PEFT techniques, while maintaining parameter efficiency and offering enhanced robustness to input perturbations.

0da325499eed6086bde470f2f2f6fb4b5d009a94.title: Sequential Neural Score Estimation: Likelihood-Free Inference with Conditional Score Based Diffusion Models
0da325499eed6086bde470f2f2f6fb4b5d009a94.research_question: How can likelihood-free Bayesian inference in simulator-based models be improved by leveraging conditional score-based diffusion models, particularly in terms of simulation efficiency, scalability, and posterior estimation accuracy?
0da325499eed6086bde470f2f2f6fb4b5d009a94.hypothesis: Conditional score-based diffusion models, when trained to estimate the score of the posterior and embedded within a sequential simulation-guided procedure, will enable more accurate, efficient, and scalable likelihood-free Bayesian inference compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.
0da325499eed6086bde470f2f2f6fb4b5d009a94.proposed_method: A novel framework, Sequential Neural Posterior Score Estimation (SNPSE), is developed for likelihood-free Bayesian inference in simulator-based models. The approach utilizes conditional score-based diffusion models to generate samples from the posterior distribution of interest. The model is trained using a score-matching objective that directly estimates the gradient of the log-posterior, leveraging samples from the simulator and the prior. To improve simulation efficiency, a sequential training procedure is embedded, where each round adaptively guides simulations toward informative regions of the parameter space using the current posterior approximation. The preferred sequential variant, Truncated Sequential NPSE (TSNPSE), employs a series of truncated proposals based on the highest-probability regions of the learned posterior, thereby reducing the need for importance corrections and maintaining the loss minimizer at the true posterior score.
0da325499eed6086bde470f2f2f6fb4b5d009a94.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on eight benchmark simulation-based inference tasks, including Lotka-Volterra, SLCP, Gaussian Linear, Uniform, Bernoulli GLM, Two Moons, and Gaussian Mixture, using simulation budgets of 1,000, 10,000, and 100,000. The evaluation metric is the classification-based two-sample test (C2ST) score, with lower values indicating better posterior estimation. Both non-sequential (NPSE) and sequential (TSNPSE) variants are compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as NPE, SNPE-C, TSNPE, and FMPE, using consistent neural network architectures and hyperparameters across all tasks. Additionally, the method is validated on a challenging real-world neuroscience simulator (the pyloric network of the stomatogastric ganglion), where the percentage of valid summary statistics and posterior predictive accuracy are assessed and compared to other sequential inference methods.
0da325499eed6086bde470f2f2f6fb4b5d009a94.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first comprehensive application of conditional score-based diffusion models to simulation-based inference, including the development of sequential variants that adaptively guide simulations. The TSNPSE algorithm is claimed to be the first to use truncated sequential proposals in the context of score-based diffusion models for SBI, eliminating the need for importance corrections and enabling efficient, accurate posterior sampling. Empirical results demonstrate that the method achieves comparable or superior performance to existing state-of-the-art approaches, particularly in high-dimensional and real-world inference problems. The approach is robust to hyperparameter settings and demonstrates scalability and flexibility not present in prior SBI methods based on normalizing flows or adversarial training.

0da731fc37dbb16115458d2b3e7f5e89c57e89a6.title: Poseidon: Efficient Foundation Models for PDEs
0da731fc37dbb16115458d2b3e7f5e89c57e89a6.research_question: Can a scalable, general-purpose foundation model be developed to efficiently learn solution operators for a wide variety of partial differential equations (PDEs), enabling accurate and sample-efficient generalization to unseen and unrelated PDEs and data distributions?
0da731fc37dbb16115458d2b3e7f5e89c57e89a6.hypothesis: A multiscale operator transformer-based foundation model, when pretrained on a diverse set of PDE solution operators and equipped with a novel training strategy leveraging the semi-group property of time-dependent PDEs, will achieve superior accuracy and sample efficiency in learning new PDE tasks, including those not seen during pretraining.
0da731fc37dbb16115458d2b3e7f5e89c57e89a6.proposed_method: A foundation model, termed POSEIDON, will be constructed using a scalable Operator Transformer (scOT) architecture. This model will employ a hierarchical, multiscale vision transformer backbone with shifted-window (SwinV2) attention, tailored for operator learning tasks. Time-conditioning will be incorporated through a lead-time-conditioned layer normalization, enabling continuous-in-time evaluations. A novel 'all2all' training strategy will be introduced to exploit the semi-group property of time-dependent PDEs, allowing quadratic scaling of training samples per trajectory. The model will be pretrained on a large, diverse dataset of solution operators for compressible Euler and incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, and subsequently fine-tuned on downstream tasks using a parameter decomposition strategy that enables efficient transfer and adaptation.
0da731fc37dbb16115458d2b3e7f5e89c57e89a6.experiment_details: The pretraining phase will utilize a dataset comprising 6 distinct PDE operators (4 from compressible Euler and 2 from incompressible Navier-Stokes equations), resulting in approximately 77,840 trajectories and over 5 million training examples via the all2all strategy. Downstream evaluation will be conducted on 15 challenging tasks representing a broad spectrum of PDE types (linear/nonlinear, time-dependent/independent, elliptic/parabolic/hyperbolic/mixed), with many tasks being out-of-distribution relative to pretraining data. Baselines will include standalone neural operators (FNO, CNO, scOT), as well as foundation models (MPP, CNO-FM), with all models evaluated using relative L1 error at final time and scaling curves plotting error versus number of task-specific training samples. Additional metrics will quantify accuracy and efficiency gains relative to FNO. Multiple POSEIDON model sizes (T, B, L) will be compared, and ablation studies will assess the impact of pretraining dataset size and diversity.
0da731fc37dbb16115458d2b3e7f5e89c57e89a6.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first general-purpose foundation model for PDEs capable of significant sample efficiency and accuracy gains across a wide range of PDE types, including those not encountered during pretraining. Key innovations include the multiscale operator transformer architecture with time-conditioned normalization for continuous-in-time evaluation, and the all2all training strategy that leverages the semi-group property of time-dependent PDEs to scale up training data. The method demonstrates, for the first time, that pretraining on a small set of diverse PDEs enables generalization to unseen and unrelated PDEs. The model and datasets will be open-sourced, providing a new benchmark and resource for the field.

0da780687ca68105117d572601c6b69055016740.title: Making Pre-trained Language Models Great on Tabular Prediction
0da780687ca68105117d572601c6b69055016740.research_question: How can pre-trained language models be effectively adapted for prediction tasks on tabular data, overcoming challenges posed by heterogeneous feature types and the incompatibility between text-based representations and numerical feature values?
0da780687ca68105117d572601c6b69055016740.hypothesis: A pre-trained language model, specifically adapted with novel numerical feature tokenization and feature organization strategies, will achieve competitive or superior performance compared to existing deep neural networks and gradient boosted decision trees on typical tabular prediction tasks, particularly when categorical features are prevalent.
0da780687ca68105117d572601c6b69055016740.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops a tabular prediction-adapted language model (TP-BERTa) based on RoBERTa, introducing two key innovations. First, a novel Relative Magnitude Tokenization (RMT) discretizes numerical feature values using a target-aware C4.5-based binning process, mapping each value to a high-dimensional 'magnitude token' that is incorporated into the language model's vocabulary and regularized with a magnitude-aware triplet loss. Second, an Intra-Feature Attention (IFA) module is introduced, which applies a shared multi-head self-attention mechanism to fuse each feature's name and value into a single vector, ensuring feature order-agnostic prediction and preventing interference between features. The overall architecture concatenates these refined feature vectors and feeds them, along with a [CLS] token, into a shared RoBERTa encoder, followed by a task-specific prediction head. The model is pre-trained in a supervised manner on large collections of tabular datasets, with both classification and regression objectives.
0da780687ca68105117d572601c6b69055016740.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the TabPertNet database, selecting 101 binary classification and 101 regression datasets (each with at least 10,000 samples and no more than 32 features) for pre-training, and 80 binary classification plus 65 regression datasets (with fewer than 10,000 samples) for downstream evaluation. The model will be compared against classical gradient boosted decision trees (XGBoost, CatBoost), advanced deep tabular models (MLP, TabNet, AutoInt, DCNv2, FT-Transformer, SAINT), and recent cross-table/pre-trained tabular models (TransTab, XTab). Evaluation metrics include average model ranks and AUC for classification tasks, with experiments stratified by feature type distributions (categorical vs. numerical) and data volume. Ablation studies will assess the impact of numerical encoding strategies (RMT vs. value-as-string and value-multiplied embeddings), the IFA module, and the number of magnitude tokens. Hyperparameter tuning will be performed for baselines, while TP-BERTa will use fixed hyperparameters across downstream tasks.
0da780687ca68105117d572601c6b69055016740.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel relative magnitude tokenization technique for numerical feature representation in language models, enabling the model to capture relative value magnitudes in the language space. The intra-feature attention module is a new mechanism for fusing feature name and value information prior to language model processing, ensuring feature order-agnostic and interference-free representations. The approach demonstrates, for the first time, that pre-trained language models tailored with these adaptations can outperform existing deep neural networks and rival gradient boosted decision trees on typical tabular data, especially when categorical features are dominant. Extensive ablation and comparative studies provide new insights into the necessity of bespoke numerical encoding and feature organization for language model-based tabular prediction.

0dadc12d7e048d3390b9857e7bd346eec9ab3227.title: Online Sparsification of Bipartite-Like Clusters in Graphs
0dadc12d7e048d3390b9857e7bd346eec9ab3227.research_question: How can efficient, online algorithms be developed to sparsify large graphs while preserving the structure of bipartite-like clusters, for both undirected and directed graphs, and how can these sparsified graphs be leveraged to accelerate existing clustering algorithms without loss of effectiveness?
0dadc12d7e048d3390b9857e7bd346eec9ab3227.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that it is possible to design nearly-linear time online sparsification algorithms that preserve the structure and cut values of bipartite-like clusters in both undirected and directed graphs, such that the sparsified graphs retain the essential clustering properties and enable significant speedup of existing clustering algorithms without compromising clustering quality.
0dadc12d7e048d3390b9857e7bd346eec9ab3227.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed for online graph sparsification that targets the preservation of bipartite-like clusters. For undirected graphs, the method will sample edges based on probabilities derived from dual Cheeger constants and spectral properties, ensuring that the cut values between pairs of vertex sets (A, B) are maintained. For directed graphs, a reduction to an undirected semi-double cover will be constructed, where bipartite-like clusters correspond to low-conductance sets, followed by sparsification using edge sampling and then mapping back to a directed graph via a reverse operation. The algorithms will be designed to operate online, only requiring local access to the graph (e.g., degree oracles), and will avoid reliance on Laplacian solvers by using random sampling and combinatorial techniques. The approach will ensure that the number and quality of bipartite-like clusters are preserved in the sparsified output.
0dadc12d7e048d3390b9857e7bd346eec9ab3227.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic graphs will be generated using stochastic block models with controlled parameters to create known bipartite-like cluster structures. Real-world datasets will include the Dyadic Militarised Interstate Disputes dataset and the US Migration dataset, where graphs are constructed from domain-specific relationships. The proposed sparsification algorithms will be evaluated as preprocessing steps for existing local clustering algorithms (e.g., LOCBIPARTDC, EVOCUTDIRECTED), and compared against these baselines in terms of runtime and clustering quality metrics such as bipartiteness ratio and flow ratio. Evaluation will include varying the number of vertices, cluster sizes, and edge probabilities, with multiple runs to assess stability. All experiments will be performed on standard hardware, and results will be reported as averages over multiple trials.
0dadc12d7e048d3390b9857e7bd346eec9ab3227.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first online sparsification algorithms specifically designed to preserve bipartite-like clusters in both undirected and directed graphs. The methodology departs from traditional sparsification, which typically preserves cuts between sets and their complements, by instead targeting inter-set cut values relevant to bipartite-like structures. The approach is applicable to directed graphs via a novel reduction to undirected semi-double covers, and the algorithms are implementable online with only local access. The resulting sparsifiers enable significant speedup of existing clustering algorithms while maintaining clustering effectiveness, and the techniques are broadly applicable across domains and graph types.

0e0e706e13f160e74cac9556f28ab9a358c148d2.title: Fine-tuning Aligned Language Models Compromises Safety, Even When Users Do Not Intend To!
0e0e706e13f160e74cac9556f28ab9a358c148d2.research_question: What are the safety risks associated with custom fine-tuning of safety-aligned large language models (LLMs) by end-users, and how robust are current safety alignment mechanisms to both adversarial and benign fine-tuning practices?
0e0e706e13f160e74cac9556f28ab9a358c148d2.hypothesis: Fine-tuning safety-aligned LLMs, even with a small number of adversarial or benign examples, can significantly degrade their safety alignment, potentially circumventing existing safety guardrails and leading to increased harmful outputs.
0e0e706e13f160e74cac9556f28ab9a358c148d2.proposed_method: A systematic investigation will be conducted into the effects of custom fine-tuning on the safety alignment of state-of-the-art LLMs, such as Llama-2-7b-Chat and GPT-3.5 Turbo. The methodology involves fine-tuning these models on three types of datasets: (1) explicitly harmful instruction-response pairs, (2) implicitly adversarial 'identity-shifting' examples designed to induce unconditional obedience, and (3) widely used benign instruction-following datasets (e.g., Alpaca, Dolly, LLaVA-Instruct). For each scenario, fine-tuning will be performed using both full-parameter and parameter-efficient techniques, adhering to official recipes and varying hyperparameters such as learning rate, batch size, and number of epochs. Safety evaluation will be carried out using a comprehensive benchmark of harmful instructions spanning 11 categories derived from official LLM usage policies, with automated scoring by a GPT-4-based judge and corroboration by other moderation tools.
0e0e706e13f160e74cac9556f28ab9a358c148d2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both open-source (Llama-2-7b-Chat) and closed-source (GPT-3.5 Turbo via OpenAI API) LLMs. Fine-tuning datasets will include (a) 10–100 adversarially crafted harmful instruction-response pairs from the Anthropic red team dataset, (b) 10 manually constructed identity-shifting conversations that induce the model to adopt an 'absolutely obedient' persona, and (c) benign datasets such as Alpaca, Dolly, and LLaVA-Instruct. Each model will be fine-tuned for up to 10 epochs, with ablation studies on hyperparameters. Safety will be evaluated using a benchmark of 330 harmful instructions across 11 policy categories, with outputs scored by GPT-4 (harmfulness score 1–5 and harmfulness rate). The same system prompts will be used for fair comparison, and additional moderation tools (OpenAI API, Perspective API, Detoxify) will be tested for their detection efficacy.
0e0e706e13f160e74cac9556f28ab9a358c148d2.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a comprehensive, policy-oriented safety evaluation benchmark that directly reflects contractual prohibited use categories, enabling fine-grained analysis of safety degradation across multiple harm types. It systematically demonstrates that both adversarial and benign fine-tuning can compromise LLM safety alignment, even with minimal data and cost, and reveals the limitations of current moderation and alignment strategies. The work highlights the emergence of new threat vectors, such as implicit identity-shifting attacks and unintended safety loss from benign fine-tuning, and provides detailed ablation studies on the impact of fine-tuning hyperparameters. The findings motivate the need for improved technical and policy-based mitigations for safe LLM customization.

0e2f8491b7af5f715c8ac7e3a7fd96494bd417d8.title: Rewarded soups: towards Pareto-optimal alignment by interpolating weights fine-tuned on diverse rewards
0e2f8491b7af5f715c8ac7e3a7fd96494bd417d8.research_question: How can deep learning foundation models be aligned more effectively with diverse and potentially conflicting human preferences or objectives, particularly in settings where only imperfect proxy rewards are available for reinforcement learning fine-tuning?
0e2f8491b7af5f715c8ac7e3a7fd96494bd417d8.hypothesis: 1) Weights fine-tuned from a shared pre-trained initialization on diverse proxy rewards remain linearly connected in weight space, such that linear interpolation between these weights yields models whose rewards exceed the interpolated rewards (Linear Mode Connectivity). 2) The set of models obtained by interpolating these weights forms a Pareto-optimal coverage set with respect to the diverse rewards, allowing for optimal trade-offs between objectives.
0e2f8491b7af5f715c8ac7e3a7fd96494bd417d8.proposed_method: A multi-policy alignment strategy, termed 'rewarded soup', is proposed for fine-tuning foundation models. The approach begins with a shared pre-trained model, which is then fine-tuned independently on N diverse proxy rewards, resulting in N expert networks. These expert weights are then linearly interpolated in weight space, forming a continuous set of models parameterized by interpolation coefficients. At test time, the interpolation coefficients can be selected according to user preferences or application-specific trade-offs, enabling a posteriori adaptation without additional training. The method leverages the empirical property that weights fine-tuned from a common initialization on different rewards remain linearly connected, thus enabling effective interpolation and Pareto-optimal trade-offs.
0e2f8491b7af5f715c8ac7e3a7fd96494bd417d8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a range of tasks, including text-to-text generation (summarization, Q&A, conversational assistants, review generation) using LLaMA-7b fine-tuned with RLHF and diverse reward models, image captioning on COCO with statistical rewards (BLEU, ROUGE, METEOR, CIDEr), text-to-image generation with diffusion models and aesthetic reward models, visual grounding on RefCOCO+ with object size-based rewards, visual question answering (VQAv2) with BLEU and METEOR, and continuous control (locomotion) in Brax with engineered rewards. Baselines will include standard single-policy RLHF and multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) with reward scalarization. Evaluation metrics will be task-appropriate (e.g., ROUGE, BLEU, accuracy, hypervolume for Pareto fronts), and the effectiveness of the proposed method will be assessed by comparing the Pareto fronts and reward trade-offs achieved by weight interpolation versus reward scalarization. Efficiency gains in terms of the number of required fine-tuning runs will also be quantified.
0e2f8491b7af5f715c8ac7e3a7fd96494bd417d8.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a flexible and efficient multi-policy alignment strategy for deep foundation models by leveraging linear interpolation in weight space after independent RL fine-tuning on diverse rewards. This approach enables a posteriori selection of trade-offs, approximates the Pareto front of possible solutions with far fewer training runs than traditional MORL, and empirically demonstrates that weight interpolation yields Pareto-optimal or near-optimal models across a variety of tasks and reward types. The method is compatible with any RLHF system and scales to an arbitrary number of objectives, offering improved transparency, fairness, and adaptability in model alignment.

0e4e899e8d4de9bd8d0ea43e32afd0baca7b6bf0.title: OccWorld: Learning a 3D Occupancy World Model for Autonomous Driving
0e4e899e8d4de9bd8d0ea43e32afd0baca7b6bf0.research_question: How can the evolution of 3D driving scenes and ego vehicle trajectories be jointly modeled in a unified, fine-grained, and efficient representation to improve autonomous driving forecasting and planning?
0e4e899e8d4de9bd8d0ea43e32afd0baca7b6bf0.hypothesis: A world model based on 3D occupancy space, using discrete scene tokenization and spatial-temporal generative transformers, can more accurately and efficiently forecast future scene evolutions and ego trajectories than conventional object-centric or segmentation-based approaches, without requiring instance-level or map supervision.
0e4e899e8d4de9bd8d0ea43e32afd0baca7b6bf0.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops a 3D occupancy world model, OccWorld, that represents the driving scene as a dense 3D occupancy grid, capturing both structural and semantic information. A vector-quantized variational autoencoder (VQ-VAE) is trained to encode the 3D occupancy into discrete high-level scene tokens in a self-supervised manner. These tokens, along with an ego token representing the vehicle's position, are input into a GPT-like spatial-temporal generative transformer that autoregressively predicts future scene and ego tokens. The transformer architecture incorporates spatial aggregation and multi-scale token mixing to capture both local and global dependencies, followed by temporal causal self-attention to model scene evolution over time. A U-net structure integrates predictions at multiple scales, and the decoder reconstructs the predicted 3D occupancy and ego trajectory from the tokens.
0e4e899e8d4de9bd8d0ea43e32afd0baca7b6bf0.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the nuScenes benchmark, focusing on the challenging task of 4D occupancy forecasting, which requires predicting the 3D occupancy for future frames given a sequence of past frames. The method is evaluated under different supervision settings, including oracle 3D occupancy, camera-based self-supervised occupancy, and semantic LiDAR. Baselines include copy-paste and other occupancy forecasting variants. Evaluation metrics include mean Intersection over Union (mIoU), IoU at multiple future time steps (1s, 2s, 3s), and L2 trajectory error for planning. The experimental setup compares OccWorld's performance against baselines in terms of forecasting accuracy and planning quality, and tests the model's ability to generalize without instance or map supervision.
0e4e899e8d4de9bd8d0ea43e32afd0baca7b6bf0.novelty_claims: The proposal claims novelty in introducing a unified world model operating in the 3D occupancy space, enabling joint prediction of scene evolution and ego trajectory. The approach leverages a self-supervised scene tokenizer and a spatial-temporal generative transformer tailored for the autonomous driving domain, moving beyond conventional object-centric or segmentation-based pipelines. The method is designed to be modality-agnostic, efficient, and scalable, and does not require instance-level or map annotations. The framework is claimed to provide more expressive, versatile, and interpretable predictions, and demonstrates competitive or superior performance in forecasting and planning tasks compared to existing baselines.

0e52059a6a42e1c6a3d388fefc4221f88b63b059.title: Continual Learning in Linear Classification on Separable Data
0e52059a6a42e1c6a3d388fefc4221f88b63b059.research_question: How can continual learning be theoretically understood and improved in the context of linear classification on sequences of separable binary tasks, particularly with respect to catastrophic forgetting, convergence, and the effects of regularization and task recurrence?
0e52059a6a42e1c6a3d388fefc4221f88b63b059.hypothesis: Continual learning of linear classifiers on separable data, when trained with weak regularization, can be theoretically characterized as a sequential max-margin projection process, and this characterization enables the derivation of upper bounds on forgetting and convergence under various task orderings and regularization schemes.
0e52059a6a42e1c6a3d388fefc4221f88b63b059.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed for continual learning in linear classification settings, focusing on sequences of binary classification tasks with jointly-separable datasets. The method will analyze the dynamics of sequentially training linear classifiers with weak regularization, showing that this process reduces to a sequential max-margin projection scheme, which is a special case of the Projection Onto Convex Sets (POCS) framework. The approach will rigorously derive the equivalence between weakly-regularized continual learning and sequential projections, and will further extend the analysis to cases with recurring tasks (cyclic and random orderings), as well as to different regularization strength schedules and weighted regularization schemes. Theoretical guarantees will be established for convergence, optimality, and bounds on forgetting, leveraging tools from convex analysis and the POCS literature.
0e52059a6a42e1c6a3d388fefc4221f88b63b059.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic datasets of binary classification tasks where each task's data is linearly separable and the tasks are jointly separable. The setup will include varying the number of tasks, dimensionality, and task orderings (cyclic, random, adversarial). Baselines will include standard batch learning, vanilla SGD, and continual learning with different regularization strengths and weighting schemes (such as Fisher-information-based regularization). Evaluation metrics will focus on forgetting (measured by hinge loss on previous tasks), distance to the offline feasible set, and convergence to minimum-norm solutions. Both theoretical analysis and empirical simulations will be used to validate the derived bounds and claims.
0e52059a6a42e1c6a3d388fefc4221f88b63b059.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel theoretical connection between weakly-regularized continual learning in linear classification and the POCS framework, specifically through sequential max-margin projections. It provides the first analytic upper bounds on forgetting and convergence for continual linear classification with recurring tasks, including cyclic and random orderings. The analysis reveals fundamental differences between continual classification and regression, demonstrates the limitations of popular regularization weighting schemes (such as Fisher-information-based methods), and uncovers the impact of regularization scheduling on convergence and optimality. The work also highlights algorithmic biases in continual learning and provides new insights into the effects of early stopping versus explicit regularization.

0ed53dfee261f5d74f6981cb207534966e61c8c9.title: Homomorphism Counts for Graph Neural Networks: All About That Basis
0ed53dfee261f5d74f6981cb207534966e61c8c9.research_question: How can the expressive power of graph neural networks (GNNs) be systematically increased to capture a broader class of graph motif parameters, including but not limited to subgraph and homomorphism pattern counts, without incurring additional computational overhead?
0ed53dfee261f5d74f6981cb207534966e61c8c9.hypothesis: Injecting the homomorphism counts of all basis structures (the homomorphism basis) for a target pattern into GNNs will result in strictly more expressive architectures than using only subgraph or homomorphism counts of the pattern itself, and this can be achieved without additional computational complexity.
0ed53dfee261f5d74f6981cb207534966e61c8c9.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed for enriching GNNs by injecting features corresponding to the homomorphism counts of all graphs in the homomorphism basis (Spasm) of a target motif parameter. This approach leverages recent results in graph theory, which show that many graph motif parameters can be expressed as linear combinations of homomorphism counts. The method will compute the homomorphism counts for each basis element and provide these as additional node- or graph-level features to the GNN. The framework will also include mechanisms to avoid redundant information by precisely identifying which homomorphism counts are necessary for the desired expressivity, and will extend naturally to both node-level and graph-level tasks. Efficient algorithms for computing these counts will be employed, ensuring that the computational complexity matches or improves upon existing subgraph counting approaches.
0ed53dfee261f5d74f6981cb207534966e61c8c9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of standard graph learning benchmarks, including molecular property prediction tasks (ZINC, QM9), link prediction on large-scale social networks (COLLAB), and expressiveness evaluation using the BREC benchmark. Baseline models will include GAT, GCN, GIN, and higher-order architectures such as BasePlanE and PPGN. Comparisons will be made against models enriched with subgraph counts, homomorphism counts of specific patterns, and the proposed homomorphism basis features. Evaluation metrics will include mean absolute error (MAE) for regression tasks, Hits@50 for link prediction, and the percentage of correctly distinguished graph pairs for expressiveness benchmarks. Additional ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of feature encoding strategies (e.g., positional encoding vs. MLP) and the incremental inclusion of basis elements.
0ed53dfee261f5d74f6981cb207534966e61c8c9.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled and fine-grained method for increasing GNN expressiveness by injecting the homomorphism basis of motif parameters, strictly subsuming both subgraph and homomorphism count augmentation. It provides a unified and computationally efficient mechanism for targeted expressivity gains, avoids redundant feature injection, and generalizes beyond fixed pattern counting to a broad class of logical and motif-based graph parameters. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art expressivity and significant improvements on real-world tasks, establishing a new foundation for the design of expressive GNN architectures.

0ee08563d545333d6ee7e7d27123ff1051cae933.title: Introduction to Haar Measure Tools in Quantum Information: A Beginner's Tutorial
0ee08563d545333d6ee7e7d27123ff1051cae933.research_question: How can the mathematical tools associated with the Haar measure be made accessible and practical for quantum information applications, particularly for beginners with only linear algebra background, and how can these tools be utilized in quantum information tasks such as quantum machine learning and classical shadow tomography?
0ee08563d545333d6ee7e7d27123ff1051cae933.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by developing and presenting Haar measure tools using only linear algebra and diagrammatic techniques, the essential concepts and calculations relevant to quantum information can be made accessible to a broader audience, enabling practical computations and applications without requiring advanced representation theory.
0ee08563d545333d6ee7e7d27123ff1051cae933.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed to introduce and operationalize Haar measure tools for quantum information, relying solely on linear algebraic concepts and intuitive diagrammatic representations. The approach will begin by formally defining the Haar measure and characterizing the moment operator, which is central to computing integrals over the Haar measure. The properties of the symmetric and antisymmetric subspaces will be explored, and the use of tensor network diagrams and vectorization formalism will be incorporated to simplify and visualize complex calculations. The framework will further introduce the concepts of unitary designs and approximate unitary designs, providing equivalent definitions and elucidating their relationships. Practical calculation recipes, such as the use of permutation operators and Weingarten calculus, will be provided for explicit Haar integrals. The methodology will be illustrated through detailed examples, including the derivation of twirling formulas and concentration inequalities.
0ee08563d545333d6ee7e7d27123ff1051cae933.experiment_details: Experiments will involve the application of the proposed Haar measure tools to a range of quantum information problems. Example calculations will include the twirling of quantum channels, computation of average gate fidelity, average purity of reduced states in bipartite systems, and Haar averages of observable expectation values. Further, the framework will be applied to analyze phenomena such as barren plateaus in quantum machine learning and protocols in classical shadow tomography, both of which rely on properties of k-designs. Evaluation will be conducted by comparing the accessibility, correctness, and computational efficiency of the proposed methods against traditional approaches that require representation theory. Standard quantum information datasets and simulation environments will be used to validate the practical utility of the tools, and results will be benchmarked using metrics such as calculation accuracy, computational complexity, and user comprehension.
0ee08563d545333d6ee7e7d27123ff1051cae933.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces an accessible, linear-algebra-based toolkit for Haar measure calculations in quantum information, eliminating the need for advanced representation theory. The integration of tensor network diagrammatic notation and explicit calculation recipes for moment operators and permutation operators provides a novel, visual, and practical approach. The framework bridges foundational mathematical concepts with practical applications in quantum machine learning and classical shadow tomography, enabling broader adoption and understanding of Haar measure tools among quantum information practitioners and students.

0eebd8adc57d6aa6a3964eecc2f3a9450169f917.title: SemCoT: Accelerating Chain-of-Thought Reasoning through Semantically-Aligned Implicit Tokens
0eebd8adc57d6aa6a3964eecc2f3a9450169f917.research_question: How can chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning in large language models be accelerated for efficiency-critical applications while preserving the semantic fidelity and effectiveness of the reasoning process?
0eebd8adc57d6aa6a3964eecc2f3a9450169f917.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a semantically-aligned implicit CoT framework, which jointly optimizes for semantic preservation and token-level generation speed, can significantly improve the efficiency of CoT reasoning in LLMs without sacrificing answer accuracy.
0eebd8adc57d6aa6a3964eecc2f3a9450169f917.proposed_method: A novel framework, SemCoT, is proposed to address the dual challenges of semantic misalignment and inefficiency in implicit CoT reasoning. The approach consists of two main components: (1) a customized sentence transformer, trained via contrastive learning, that measures and enforces semantic alignment between implicit reasoning embeddings and ground-truth explicit reasoning; and (2) a lightweight language model, distilled or pruned from the original LLM, which efficiently generates implicit reasoning tokens. The sentence transformer is constructed by extracting intermediate layers from the LLM, applying pooling and linear projection to obtain semantic embeddings, and is trained on pairs of ground-truth and condensed reasoning texts. The lightweight generator produces implicit reasoning embeddings, which are linearly projected into the LLM's embedding space and optimized using a combined loss function that balances answer accuracy and semantic alignment, controlled by a hyperparameter. Training is staged, with the sentence transformer trained first and then frozen, followed by the training of the implicit reasoning generator.
0eebd8adc57d6aa6a3964eecc2f3a9450169f917.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on five benchmark datasets spanning mathematical (GSM8K, SVAMP, MultiArith), commonsense (CommonsenseQA), and symbolic (CoinFlip) reasoning. Two open-source LLMs (Llama-2-7b-chat-hf and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2) are evaluated, with corresponding lightweight models (Sheared-LLaMA-1.3B and mistral-1.1b-testing) used for implicit reasoning generation. Baselines include Pause, ICoT-SI, COCONUT, CODI, and SoftCoT, representing state-of-the-art implicit CoT efficiency methods. Evaluation metrics include answer accuracy (percentage of correct answers) and average wall-clock inference time per query. Implementation details specify a semantic embedding dimension of 768, use of AdamW optimizer, and up to 30 answer tokens generated per query. Ablation studies and parameter sensitivity analyses are performed to assess the contribution of each component and the effect of hyperparameters.
