0eebd8adc57d6aa6a3964eecc2f3a9450169f917.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to jointly optimize for both token-level generation speed and semantic alignment in implicit CoT reasoning. SemCoT introduces a customized sentence transformer specifically designed to measure and enforce semantic alignment between implicit and explicit reasoning within the LLM embedding space. The integration of a lightweight, knowledge-distilled language model for efficient implicit reasoning generation, guided by semantic alignment objectives, represents a significant advancement over prior methods. Extensive empirical results demonstrate that SemCoT achieves superior trade-offs between efficiency and effectiveness compared to existing baselines, providing a scalable solution for deploying CoT reasoning in real-world, efficiency-critical scenarios.

0f0d757e764a7f21d7aaa329c835571b247dd937.title: QServe: W4A8KV4 Quantization and System Co-design for Efficient LLM Serving
0f0d757e764a7f21d7aaa329c835571b247dd937.research_question: How can quantization and system co-design be leveraged to significantly improve the efficiency and throughput of large language model (LLM) serving on modern GPU hardware, especially in large-batch, cloud-based scenarios?
0f0d757e764a7f21d7aaa329c835571b247dd937.hypothesis: A co-designed quantization algorithm and serving system that utilizes 4-bit weights, 8-bit activations, and 4-bit KV cache (W4A8KV4), along with progressive group quantization, SmoothAttention, and compute-aware system optimizations, will enable higher throughput and lower latency for LLM serving on GPUs compared to existing quantization and serving approaches, without incurring significant accuracy degradation.
0f0d757e764a7f21d7aaa329c835571b247dd937.proposed_method: A novel quantization algorithm, termed QoQ (W4A8KV4), will be developed that quantizes LLM weights to 4 bits, activations to 8 bits, and KV cache to 4 bits. The method introduces progressive group quantization, which first applies per-channel symmetric INT8 quantization with a protective range, followed by per-group asymmetric INT4 quantization to ensure all intermediate values remain within the INT8 range. To address accuracy loss from low-bit KV cache quantization, SmoothAttention will be employed to scale and smooth outlier channels in the Key cache, shifting quantization difficulty away from the most problematic activations. The system component, QServe, will implement compute-aware weight reordering to minimize pointer arithmetic overhead on CUDA cores, enable register-level parallelism for efficient dequantization, and optimize the computation order (subtraction after multiplication) to reduce main loop overhead in GEMM operations. Additional optimizations such as activation-aware channel reordering, block input rotation, and block output smoothing will further improve quantization robustness and system throughput.
0f0d757e764a7f21d7aaa329c835571b247dd937.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on seven widely-used LLMs, including Llama-3-8B and Qwen1.5-72B, using both NVIDIA A100 and L40S GPUs. The proposed system will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as TensorRT-LLM (in FP16, W8A8, and W4A16 configurations), Atom (W4A4), and QuaRot (W4A4). Evaluation metrics will include maximum achievable serving throughput (tokens/sec), latency, and model accuracy (e.g., perplexity on standard datasets like Wikitext-2). Detailed profiling will be performed to analyze the impact of main loop overhead, memory bandwidth utilization, and kernel efficiency. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by matching batch sizes and sequence lengths across systems, and by using dynamic, per-head quantization for KV caches to maintain accuracy at low bit precision.
0f0d757e764a7f21d7aaa329c835571b247dd937.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first quantization and system co-design that enables practical, high-throughput LLM serving using W4A8KV4 precision on modern GPUs. Key innovations include progressive group quantization with a protective range for register-level parallelism, SmoothAttention for mitigating accuracy loss from 4-bit KV quantization, and compute-aware weight reordering to eliminate pointer arithmetic bottlenecks. The system achieves substantial measured speedups (up to 3.5×) over leading baselines and demonstrates that low-bit quantization can outperform higher-precision systems even on less expensive hardware. The approach also provides new insights into the interplay between quantization granularity, hardware architecture, and system-level bottlenecks in LLM serving.

0f11cf87f63b9f147eae2a280a25033a04e634f9.title: Introducing Competition to Boost the Transferability of Targeted Adversarial Examples Through Clean Feature Mixup
0f11cf87f63b9f147eae2a280a25033a04e634f9.research_question: How can the transferability of targeted adversarial examples across different deep neural network models be improved, especially under black-box settings, while maintaining computational efficiency?
0f11cf87f63b9f147eae2a280a25033a04e634f9.hypothesis: Introducing competition into the optimization process of targeted adversarial attacks, by simulating interference from both adversarial perturbations towards other target classes and friendly perturbations towards the correct class in feature space, will encourage the use of more diverse features and significantly enhance the transferability of adversarial examples.
0f11cf87f63b9f147eae2a280a25033a04e634f9.proposed_method: A novel method, Clean Feature Mixup (CFM), will be developed to enhance the transferability of targeted adversarial examples. The approach involves attaching CFM modules to selected deeper convolutional and fully connected layers of a pre-trained source model. During inference, these modules store clean feature representations and then randomly mix them with current input features in a stochastic, channel-wise manner, using linear interpolation. The mixing process incorporates both the clean features of the same image (simulating friendly perturbations) and those from other images in the batch (simulating adversarial perturbations towards other target classes), with randomization applied to the selection and mixing ratios. This design aims to prevent overfitting to the source model's features, thereby encouraging adversarial perturbations to exploit a broader set of features and improving transferability to unseen target models. The method is designed for computational efficiency, requiring only a single additional forward pass for feature storage and minimal overhead for mixup operations.
0f11cf87f63b9f147eae2a280a25033a04e634f9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ImageNet-Compatible and CIFAR-10 datasets, following established protocols for targeted adversarial attacks. Multiple source models, including standard and adversarially trained convolutional neural networks as well as Transformer-based classifiers, will be used to generate adversarial examples. The proposed CFM method will be compared against strong baseline methods such as Diverse-Inputs (DI), Resized-Diverse-Inputs (RDI), Scale-Invariant (SI), Variance Tuning (VT), Admix, and Object-based Diverse Input (ODI), with and without combinations of input diversification, gradient stabilization, and advanced loss functions. Evaluation metrics will include targeted attack success rates across a variety of target models (including robust and ensemble models), as well as computational time per adversarial example. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of different components of the CFM module, such as mixing probability, channel-wise ratios, and feature shuffling. Batch size sensitivity and compatibility with other attack techniques will also be investigated.
0f11cf87f63b9f147eae2a280a25033a04e634f9.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the concept of competition in the feature space during adversarial example generation, efficiently simulating both friendly and adversarial competitor noises without requiring additional backward passes. Clean Feature Mixup (CFM) is the first to leverage random mixing of stored clean features at multiple network layers to diversify feature utilization in targeted attacks, substantially boosting transferability. The method is computationally efficient, easy to integrate into existing models, and compatible with a wide range of attack techniques. Extensive experiments are expected to demonstrate significant improvements in transfer success rates over state-of-the-art baselines, including on robust and ensemble models.

0f170ef970b4febb9115b5b142123cce5a1c6396.title: Large Motion Model for Unified Multi-Modal Motion Generation
0f170ef970b4febb9115b5b142123cce5a1c6396.research_question: How can a single, unified model be developed to perform a wide range of human motion generation tasks across multiple modalities and data formats, while achieving strong generalization and performance on diverse benchmarks?
0f170ef970b4febb9115b5b142123cce5a1c6396.hypothesis: A unified, large-scale, multi-modal motion generation model, trained on a comprehensive and standardized dataset with advanced attention mechanisms and pre-training strategies, can achieve competitive or superior performance across a variety of motion generation tasks compared to specialist models.
0f170ef970b4febb9115b5b142123cce5a1c6396.proposed_method: A unified motion generation framework will be developed by first consolidating 16 diverse motion datasets into a single benchmark, MotionVerse, which covers 10 tasks and standardizes all motion data into a common intermediate representation based on the TOMATO format. The model architecture will be a transformer-based diffusion model enhanced with a novel ArtAttention mechanism, which incorporates both spatial (body part-aware) and temporal attention, enabling fine-grained control and robust handling of missing or variable body parts. Multi-modal condition signals (text, speech, music, video) will be encoded into unified feature vectors using a modality-agnostic encoder (e.g., ImageBind), and dataset-dependent read-in/read-out layers will map between the unified representation and dataset-specific formats. The training regime will include both unsupervised pre-training (with random frame rate augmentation and masking strategies) and supervised fine-tuning, allowing the model to leverage large-scale, heterogeneous data while learning both general and task-specific motion knowledge.
0f170ef970b4febb9115b5b142123cce5a1c6396.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on nine widely used motion generation benchmarks spanning tasks such as text-to-motion (HumanML3D), action-to-motion (KIT-ML, HumanAct12, NTU-RGBD120), music-to-dance (AIST++), speech-to-gesture (BEAT, TED-Gesture++), motion prediction (Human3.6M, AMASS, 3DPW), and others. The unified model will be compared against state-of-the-art specialist models for each task using standard evaluation metrics such as FID (Fréchet Inception Distance), FGD (Fréchet Gesture Distance), and avg-MPJPE (mean per-joint position error). Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of the unified representation, ArtAttention mechanism, and pre-training strategies. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparisons by using the same data splits and evaluation protocols as prior work.
0f170ef970b4febb9115b5b142123cce5a1c6396.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first large-scale, unified, multi-modal motion generation benchmark (MotionVerse) with standardized data representation across 16 datasets and 10 tasks. The model architecture features a novel ArtAttention mechanism for body part-aware and temporally-aware motion generation, supporting multi-modal conditioning and missing data. The pre-training strategy leverages random frame rates and masking to enhance robustness and knowledge transfer. The unified model demonstrates strong generalization, competitive or superior performance across diverse tasks, and the ability to handle unseen multi-modal motion generation scenarios.

0f322ac4f9f12b11fe5d042508497148a84fe8a5.title: Dynamic Sparse Training with Structured Sparsity
0f322ac4f9f12b11fe5d042508497148a84fe8a5.research_question: How can dynamic sparse training methods be adapted to learn structured sparsity patterns that enable both efficient training and real-world acceleration on modern hardware, without sacrificing the generalization performance of dense neural networks?
0f322ac4f9f12b11fe5d042508497148a84fe8a5.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that imposing a constant fan-in structured sparsity constraint within a dynamic sparse training framework, combined with a neuron ablation mechanism, will enable the learning of highly sparse neural networks that maintain generalization performance comparable to unstructured sparse methods, while also achieving significant real-world speedups on both CPUs and GPUs.
0f322ac4f9f12b11fe5d042508497148a84fe8a5.proposed_method: A novel dynamic sparse training algorithm, Structured RigL (SRigL), will be developed to enforce a constant fan-in constraint during training, such that each neuron (or filter) retains the same number of non-zero incoming weights. The method will periodically update the sparse mask by pruning weights with the smallest magnitude and regrowing connections with the largest gradient magnitude, but will do so at the neuron level to maintain the structured constraint. To address the limitation that constant fan-in can inhibit neuron ablation (which is beneficial at high sparsity), a dynamic neuron ablation mechanism will be incorporated: neurons with fewer than a threshold proportion of salient weights will be ablated, and their connections redistributed. The algorithm will include a hyperparameter to control the ablation threshold, allowing flexibility across architectures and sparsity regimes. The resulting sparse mask will be learned end-to-end during training, enabling both structured and unstructured sparsity patterns to be exploited for acceleration.
0f322ac4f9f12b11fe5d042508497148a84fe8a5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification benchmarks, including CIFAR-10 (using ResNet-18 and WideResNet-22) and ImageNet (using ResNet-50, MobileNet-V3, and ViT-B/16). The proposed method will be compared against dense baselines and a range of dynamic sparse training (DST) methods such as RigL, SET, DeepR, DSR, Top-KAST, MEST, DSB, and SR-STE. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 test accuracy and real-world inference speed (wall-clock time) on both CPUs and GPUs. Real-world speedups will be measured using a PyTorch implementation for CPU online inference and a CUDA-based implementation for GPU batched inference, with timings compared across structured, unstructured, and dense representations. Hyperparameters will be tuned via sweeps, and experiments will be repeated with multiple random seeds to ensure statistical significance.
0f322ac4f9f12b11fe5d042508497148a84fe8a5.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a dynamic sparse training framework that enforces constant fan-in structured sparsity, enabling both parameter and memory efficiency as well as real-world acceleration without specialized hardware. The integration of a neuron ablation mechanism within the structured DST setting is novel and allows the method to match or exceed the generalization performance of state-of-the-art unstructured DST methods, even at extreme sparsity levels. The approach is broadly applicable across architectures and sparsity regimes, and the condensed sparse representation enables immediate and significant speedups for both online and batched inference on commodity hardware.

0f3575f63b67f257b740751587a5658e3b6ad454.title: Analyzing Neural Scaling Laws in Two-Layer Networks with Power-Law Data Spectra
0f3575f63b67f257b740751587a5658e3b6ad454.research_question: How do neural scaling laws manifest in two-layer neural networks when the data covariance matrix exhibits a power-law spectrum, and what are the theoretical underpinnings of generalization error dynamics under such data distributions?
0f3575f63b67f257b740751587a5658e3b6ad454.hypothesis: Neural networks trained on data with power-law spectral covariance matrices will exhibit distinct scaling regimes in their generalization error, including transitions from exponential to power-law convergence, and the structure of these regimes will depend on the number of distinct eigenvalues and hidden units.
0f3575f63b67f257b740751587a5658e3b6ad454.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed using statistical mechanics to analyze one-pass stochastic gradient descent in a student-teacher setup, where both student and teacher are two-layer neural networks. The student network will be trained on outputs generated by the teacher, with Gaussian-distributed inputs whose covariance matrix follows a power-law spectrum with a tunable number of distinct eigenvalues. Analytical solutions for the generalization error will be derived for both linear and non-linear activation functions, focusing on the dynamics of order parameters that describe the relationships between student and teacher weights. The methodology will involve deriving and solving coupled differential equations for these order parameters, employing the Cayley–Hamilton theorem to close the system, and using asymptotic and perturbative analysis to characterize learning regimes and plateau behaviors.
0f3575f63b67f257b740751587a5658e3b6ad454.experiment_details: Experiments will involve both synthetic and real datasets. Synthetic data will be generated as Gaussian vectors with covariance matrices exhibiting a controlled power-law spectrum, varying the number of distinct eigenvalues and the power-law exponent. Real-data experiments will use the CIFAR-5m dataset, with empirical estimation of the data spectrum. Baseline comparisons will include isotropic (white noise) data and varying numbers of trainable features. Evaluation metrics will focus on the generalization error, tracked as a function of training time (measured by the ratio of examples to input dimension), number of hidden units, and number of distinct eigenvalues. Both analytical predictions and numerical simulations (averaged over multiple random initializations) will be used to validate theoretical results and scaling laws.
0f3575f63b67f257b740751587a5658e3b6ad454.novelty_claims: The proposed research will provide the first comprehensive theoretical analysis of neural scaling laws in two-layer neural networks with power-law data spectra, deriving exact analytical expressions for the generalization error in both linear and non-linear regimes. It will identify and characterize the transition from exponential to power-law convergence in generalization error, elucidate the dependence of plateau length and height on the number of distinct eigenvalues and hidden units, and establish new scaling laws for feature learning and parameter scaling. The approach extends previous work by fully incorporating feature learning (all pre-activation weights trainable) and by closing the dynamical system for arbitrary numbers of distinct eigenvalues, offering new insights into the optimization of neural network learning under realistic data structures.

0f3b6cb07a8edb78a40ee478708eedcd03242503.title: Understanding Gradient Descent on Edge of Stability in Deep Learning
0f3b6cb07a8edb78a40ee478708eedcd03242503.research_question: How does deterministic Gradient Descent behave in deep learning when operating at the Edge of Stability, and what are the underlying mechanisms of implicit regularization and trajectory dynamics in this regime?
0f3b6cb07a8edb78a40ee478708eedcd03242503.hypothesis: Gradient Descent, when operating at the Edge of Stability with finite learning rates, exhibits a deterministic implicit regularization mechanism that drives iterates along the manifold of minimizers in a manner that reduces sharpness, even in the absence of stochasticity or infinitesimal updates.
0f3b6cb07a8edb78a40ee478708eedcd03242503.proposed_method: The proposed research will mathematically analyze the dynamics of deterministic Gradient Descent (GD) in deep learning settings where the loss landscape is non-smooth or the learning rate is effectively adaptive. The study will focus on two key settings: (1) Normalized Gradient Descent, where the learning rate is scaled by the gradient norm, and (2) GD on a transformed loss (such as the square root of the original loss). The analysis will assume that the set of minimizers forms a submanifold and that the Hessian at these points has a fixed rank with a positive eigengap. The methodology involves deriving and studying the limiting flow of GD iterates on the manifold, using projection operators and Taylor expansions to characterize the trajectory and its alignment with the top eigenvector of the Hessian. Occasional negligible noise may be injected to ensure technical smoothness in the analysis, but the primary focus remains on deterministic dynamics.
0f3b6cb07a8edb78a40ee478708eedcd03242503.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic and real-world deep learning models, including quadratic losses and neural networks with smooth activation functions. The empirical study will track the behavior of sharpness, loss, and trajectory alignment during training with both Normalized GD and GD on transformed losses. Baselines will include traditional GD and possibly stochastic variants for comparison. Evaluation metrics will include the largest eigenvalue of the Hessian (sharpness), loss oscillation patterns, and the degree of alignment between the gradient and the top Hessian eigenvector. Experiments will be designed to corroborate theoretical predictions, such as the stabilization of sharpness around 2/LR, non-monotonic loss decrease, and movement toward flatter minima.
0f3b6cb07a8edb78a40ee478708eedcd03242503.novelty_claims: This research proposes the first rigorous mathematical framework for analyzing deterministic GD at the Edge of Stability in deep learning, demonstrating a new form of implicit regularization that does not rely on stochasticity or infinitesimal step sizes. The approach reveals that GD iterates evolve along a deterministic flow on the manifold of minimizers, reducing sharpness in a manner not captured by previous implicit bias results. The analysis introduces new technical tools for proving alignment between the gradient and the top Hessian eigenvector in both quadratic and general loss settings, and provides formal guarantees for the two-phase dynamics observed empirically in deep learning optimization.

0f71a43a5cd29368bcc2f2ff5e8769f69c20fff6.title: A Novel Framework for Policy Mirror Descent with General Parametrization and Linear Convergence
0f71a43a5cd29368bcc2f2ff5e8769f69c20fff6.research_question: How can policy optimization in reinforcement learning be achieved with general policy parameterizations, including neural networks, while providing strong theoretical guarantees such as linear convergence for policy-gradient-based methods?
0f71a43a5cd29368bcc2f2ff5e8769f69c20fff6.hypothesis: A mirror descent-based policy optimization framework that accommodates arbitrary policy parameterizations and mirror maps will achieve linear convergence rates under appropriate conditions, extending theoretical guarantees beyond tabular and log-linear settings.
0f71a43a5cd29368bcc2f2ff5e8769f69c20fff6.proposed_method: A novel framework, Approximate Mirror Policy Optimization (AMPO), will be developed that generalizes policy mirror descent to arbitrary policy parameterization classes and mirror maps. The method defines a new policy class based on Bregman projections induced by a chosen mirror map and a parameterized function, enabling the recovery of known policy classes (e.g., softmax) and the creation of new ones. The optimization procedure consists of two main steps: (1) solving a regression problem to approximate the Q-function and the gradient of the mirror map using a parameterized function (e.g., neural network), and (2) updating the policy via a Bregman projection onto the probability simplex. The framework is designed to be compatible with a wide range of mirror maps, including negative entropy, squared Euclidean norm, Tsallis entropy, and hyperbolic entropy, and supports efficient computation for a large class of mirror maps (ω-potential mirror maps). Theoretical analysis will be conducted to establish convergence guarantees for any parameterization and mirror map.
0f71a43a5cd29368bcc2f2ff5e8769f69c20fff6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on classic control tasks such as CartPole and Acrobot using the AMPO framework with various mirror maps (e.g., negative entropy, hyperbolic entropy, squared Euclidean norm, Tsallis entropy). The policy parameterization will include shallow neural networks, and the Q-function will be estimated using generalized advantage estimation. The performance of AMPO will be compared against established baselines such as PPO, with evaluation metrics including average episodic return and convergence rate. Step-size schedules (constant and geometrically increasing) will be explored, and empirical results will validate the theoretical claims regarding convergence and the impact of different mirror maps.
0f71a43a5cd29368bcc2f2ff5e8769f69c20fff6.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to guarantee linear convergence for policy-gradient-based methods with general policy parameterizations and arbitrary mirror maps. It unifies and generalizes existing results for tabular, log-linear, and neural policy classes, and introduces a flexible approach that can generate new algorithms by varying the mirror map. The method provides improved or matching convergence rates compared to prior works, supports efficient implementation for a broad class of mirror maps, and offers new sample complexity results for neural network parameterizations. The framework enables off-policy updates and relaxes several technical assumptions required by previous approaches.

0f7308fbcae43d22813f70c334c2425df0b1cce1.title: Safe RLHF: Safe Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
0f7308fbcae43d22813f70c334c2425df0b1cce1.research_question: How can large language models be aligned with human values to simultaneously maximize helpfulness and minimize harmfulness, while effectively balancing the inherent tension between these two objectives during training?
0f7308fbcae43d22813f70c334c2425df0b1cce1.hypothesis: Explicitly decoupling human preferences for helpfulness and harmlessness, and optimizing with separate reward and cost models under a constrained reinforcement learning framework, will enable large language models to achieve higher levels of both helpfulness and safety compared to conventional RLHF or static multi-objective balancing methods.
0f7308fbcae43d22813f70c334c2425df0b1cce1.proposed_method: A novel Safe Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (Safe RLHF) framework will be developed, which formalizes safety alignment as a constrained optimization problem. Human annotation will be explicitly decoupled into two dimensions: helpfulness and harmlessness, with independent labeling for each QA pair across 14 predefined harm categories. Two preference models will be trained: a Reward Model (RM) for helpfulness and a Cost Model (CM) for harmlessness, each using pairwise preference data and, for the CM, additional binary safety labels. During policy optimization, the LLM will be fine-tuned by maximizing expected reward (helpfulness) while enforcing a constraint on expected cost (harmlessness), using the Lagrangian method to dynamically adjust the trade-off between objectives. The optimization will be performed iteratively, updating both the LLM parameters and the Lagrange multiplier to maintain the desired safety threshold without over-optimizing either objective.
0f7308fbcae43d22813f70c334c2425df0b1cce1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by iteratively fine-tuning an initial SFT model (Alpaca-7B, instruction-tuned from LLaMA-7B using the Alpaca dataset) through three rounds of Safe RLHF. In each round, prompts will be sourced from open datasets and augmented with human red-teaming to ensure coverage of safety-related scenarios. For each prompt, multiple model responses will be generated and labeled by crowdworkers for both helpfulness and harmlessness, creating decoupled preference datasets. Baselines will include conventional RLHF and static reward shaping methods with various weighting schemes. Evaluation will be performed using a custom prompt set covering 14 safety categories, with assessments from both unified preference models (reward and cost) and human/GPT-4 pairwise Elo scoring for helpfulness and harmlessness. Key metrics will include ranking accuracy, safety classification accuracy, Elo scores, and the proportion of harmful responses.
0f7308fbcae43d22813f70c334c2425df0b1cce1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first integration of Safe RL (constrained RL) with RLHF for LLM alignment, featuring explicit decoupling of helpfulness and harmlessness in both annotation and modeling. The method leverages separate reward and cost models and dynamically balances objectives using the Lagrangian method, overcoming the limitations of static multi-objective balancing. The framework is designed to improve both safety and utility, with empirical protocols for iterative red-teaming, annotation, and evaluation. This approach enables more robust and scalable safety alignment for LLMs and can be generalized to other multi-objective alignment scenarios.

0f80c534cd3191142af9c1ab521b85263daf43fe.title: CLARIFY: Contrastive Preference Reinforcement Learning for Untangling Ambiguous Queries
0f80c534cd3191142af9c1ab521b85263daf43fe.research_question: How can preference-based reinforcement learning be improved to better handle ambiguous queries, where human labelers struggle to distinguish between highly similar trajectory segments, in order to enhance label efficiency and practical applicability in offline settings?
0f80c534cd3191142af9c1ab521b85263daf43fe.hypothesis: Integrating contrastive learning into trajectory embedding and query selection will enable the identification and prioritization of unambiguous queries, resulting in improved label efficiency, more meaningful trajectory representations, and superior policy performance compared to existing offline preference-based reinforcement learning methods.
0f80c534cd3191142af9c1ab521b85263daf43fe.proposed_method: A new offline preference-based reinforcement learning (PbRL) framework is developed that leverages contrastive learning to construct a trajectory embedding space which incorporates human preference information. The method introduces two key loss functions: an ambiguity loss that maximizes the distance between embeddings of clearly distinguished segment pairs while minimizing the distance between ambiguous ones, and a quadrilateral loss that regularizes the embedding space by modeling preference relationships as geometric quadrilaterals among segment pairs. The embedding space is trained using a bi-directional decision transformer architecture, with additional constraints to prevent representation collapse. Query selection is performed via rejection sampling in the learned embedding space, prioritizing queries with large embedding distances (i.e., more clearly distinguished segment pairs), thereby increasing the proportion of unambiguous queries presented to human labelers. The overall training process alternates between embedding learning, query selection, preference data collection, and policy optimization using a standard offline RL algorithm.
0f80c534cd3191142af9c1ab521b85263daf43fe.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a suite of complex robotic manipulation tasks from the Metaworld benchmark and continuous control tasks from DMControl, using an offline dataset with no reward signals. Both scripted non-ideal teachers (with a skip mechanism for ambiguous queries) and real human labelers are used to provide preference feedback. Baseline comparisons include state-of-the-art offline PbRL methods such as Markovian Reward (MR), Preference Transformer (PT), OPRL, OPPO, and LiRE. Evaluation metrics include policy success rates, episodic returns, query clarity ratio (proportion of queries with clear human preferences), and label accuracy. Additional analyses include embedding space visualizations, ablation studies on loss components and query selection strategies, and assessments of label efficiency under varying query budgets.
0f80c534cd3191142af9c1ab521b85263daf43fe.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel combination of contrastive learning and preference-based reinforcement learning to address the challenge of ambiguous queries in offline settings. Key innovations include the ambiguity and quadrilateral losses for constructing a preference-aware trajectory embedding space, a rejection sampling-based query selection mechanism that maximizes the proportion of unambiguous queries, and theoretical guarantees on the geometric properties of the learned embeddings. The method demonstrates improved label efficiency, higher-quality trajectory representations, and superior policy performance under both non-ideal and real human feedback, advancing the practical applicability of PbRL.

0f900b9876d03cc2b09b8c113121e749ccddd698.title: Label Noise SGD Provably Prefers Flat Global Minimizers
0f900b9876d03cc2b09b8c113121e749ccddd698.research_question: How does stochastic gradient descent (SGD) with label noise influence the implicit regularization and convergence behavior in overparameterized models, and what are the global effects on the loss landscape and generalization?
0f900b9876d03cc2b09b8c113121e749ccddd698.hypothesis: SGD with label noise induces an implicit regularization effect that biases optimization toward flat, global minimizers by penalizing sharp regions of the loss landscape, and this effect is controlled by the learning rate, batch size, and strength of label noise.
0f900b9876d03cc2b09b8c113121e749ccddd698.proposed_method: A theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted on the implicit regularization properties of SGD when label noise is injected during training. The approach involves formalizing the SGD with label noise algorithm, where at each iteration, random noise is added to the labels before computing the gradient update. The method will derive and analyze the explicit form of the induced regularizer R(θ), which penalizes sharp minima, and will characterize the effective regularization parameter λ as a function of learning rate, batch size, and noise variance. Theoretical analysis will establish convergence properties to stationary points of a regularized loss L(θ) + λR(θ), including extensions to general loss functions, momentum, and general noise covariance. The analysis will also employ coupling arguments and Taylor expansions to rigorously quantify the effect of label noise on the optimization trajectory and stationary points.
0f900b9876d03cc2b09b8c113121e749ccddd698.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both real and synthetic datasets to empirically validate the theoretical findings. The setup will involve training overparameterized models using SGD with varying levels of label noise, learning rates, and batch sizes. Baselines will include standard SGD without label noise and other regularization techniques such as dropout and batch normalization. Evaluation metrics will include training loss, test loss, sharpness of the loss landscape (e.g., Hessian eigenvalues), and generalization gap. Key experimental details will involve systematic variation of hyperparameters to assess the strength of the implicit regularization and its effect on convergence to flat minima.
0f900b9876d03cc2b09b8c113121e749ccddd698.novelty_claims: The proposed research provides a global characterization of the implicit regularization effect induced by label noise in SGD, extending prior local analyses to global convergence and accommodating large learning rates. The explicit form of the regularizer R(θ) is derived for general models and loss functions, revealing an additional regularization effect for large learning rates that more strongly penalizes sharp minima. The analysis also generalizes to SGD with momentum and arbitrary noise covariance, offering a comprehensive theoretical framework for understanding the role of label noise in modern deep learning optimization.

0f900f07158d0abf9d7a419c392e33531f3eebae.title: Word Embeddings Are Steers for Language Models
0f900f07158d0abf9d7a419c392e33531f3eebae.research_question: How can the internal word embedding space of language models be leveraged to flexibly and efficiently steer the generative behavior of these models, such as controlling style, sentiment, or toxicity, without retraining or extensive fine-tuning?
0f900f07158d0abf9d7a419c392e33531f3eebae.hypothesis: Linear transformations of output word embeddings in language models are sufficient to induce controlled shifts in generation style, sentiment, or toxicity, enabling efficient, interpretable, and transferable control over language model outputs.
0f900f07158d0abf9d7a419c392e33531f3eebae.proposed_method: A novel approach, LM-Steer, is proposed that applies a learnable linear transformation matrix W to the output word embeddings of a fixed, pre-trained language model. Specifically, each word embedding e_v is replaced with e_v' = (I + ϵW)e_v, where ϵ is a scalar steering value that controls the intensity and polarity of the desired style or attribute. The matrix W is trained using maximum likelihood on labeled data corresponding to the target style (e.g., positive/negative sentiment, toxic/non-toxic), with only W being updated and all other model parameters kept fixed. During generation, the user specifies a steering value ϵ, and the model decodes as usual, enabling continuous and compositional control by interpolating or combining multiple steering matrices. The method is parameter-efficient (typically requiring less than 0.2% of the original model size) and can be transferred between models via explicit linear mapping of embedding spaces.
0f900f07158d0abf9d7a419c392e33531f3eebae.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on tasks such as language model detoxification and sentiment control using several backbone models, including GPT-2 (various sizes), Pythia, GPT-J, and Llama-2. For detoxification, the Jigsaw Unintended Bias in Toxicity Classification dataset will be used for training, and the RealToxicityPrompts dataset for evaluation. For sentiment control, the Stanford Sentiment Treebank (SST-5) will be used for training, with evaluation on prompts filtered by a sentiment classifier. Baselines include DExperts, DAPT, PPLM, GeDi, PromptT5, MuCoLa, LoRA, and a soft-blacklist method. Evaluation metrics include maximal toxicity, toxicity probability, fluency (perplexity), and diversity (Dist-n). Human evaluation will also be conducted for subjective assessment of detoxification, fluency, and topicality. Additional experiments will assess parameter/data efficiency, transferability of LM-Steer between models, and the ability to provide continuous and compositional control.
0f900f07158d0abf9d7a419c392e33531f3eebae.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a theoretically grounded, simple, and highly parameter-efficient approach to controlled language generation by directly manipulating output word embeddings. LM-Steer enables continuous and compositional control over generation attributes, is transferable between language models via explicit linear mapping, and provides interpretability by revealing which embedding dimensions correspond to specific styles or biases. Unlike prior methods, LM-Steer does not require retraining the full model or external classifiers, and achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on detoxification and sentiment control tasks while maintaining fluency and diversity.

0fb982323f107aa07824c259ff19bb63236f7f56.title: Improving the Variance of Differentially Private Randomized Experiments through Clustering
0fb982323f107aa07824c259ff19bb63236f7f56.research_question: How can the variance of causal effect estimation in differentially private randomized experiments be reduced without compromising privacy guarantees, particularly by leveraging available cluster structures in the data?
0fb982323f107aa07824c259ff19bb63236f7f56.hypothesis: Incorporating non-sensitive clustering information into differentially private mechanisms will improve the privacy-variance trade-off in causal effect estimation, resulting in lower estimator variance compared to standard differentially private baselines, without weakening privacy guarantees.
0fb982323f107aa07824c259ff19bb63236f7f56.proposed_method: A novel differentially private mechanism, CLUSTER-DP, will be developed to privatize user-level outcomes in randomized experiments while leveraging known, non-sensitive cluster structures within the data. The method operates by, for each cluster and treatment group, estimating the empirical response distribution, adding Laplace noise to ensure privacy, truncating and renormalizing the resulting probabilities, and then privatizing each individual response by either retaining the true value or resampling from the privatized cluster distribution with a specified probability. The mechanism is parameterized by a truncation threshold, noise scale, and resampling probability, which together control the privacy-variance trade-off. The approach is designed to be label-differentially private and supports both (ε, δ)-DP and pure ε-DP guarantees. The method generalizes to a cluster-free version (CLUSTER-FREE-DP) when no clustering is available, and reduces to a uniform prior mechanism under specific parameter choices.
0fb982323f107aa07824c259ff19bb63236f7f56.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both simulated and real-world datasets. Simulated data will include Gaussian mixture models with varying cluster homogeneity, where potential outcomes are quantized and clusters are of varying sizes. Real-world evaluation will use a subset of the YouTube social network dataset, leveraging natural user communities as clusters and generating synthetic potential outcomes based on cluster features. The proposed CLUSTER-DP mechanism will be compared against baselines including UNIFORM-PRIOR-DP (both stratified and unstratified) and CLUSTER-FREE-DP. Evaluation metrics will include the variance of the average treatment effect estimator under fixed privacy loss (ε, δ), and the privacy-variance trade-off will be explored by varying mechanism parameters. Additional experiments will analyze the impact of cluster quality and demonstrate unbiasedness and consistency of the estimators.
0fb982323f107aa07824c259ff19bb63236f7f56.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new user-level differentially private mechanism that leverages non-sensitive clustering information to reduce estimator variance in causal inference tasks. It generalizes existing baselines, including uniform prior and cluster-free mechanisms, and provides theoretical guarantees on both privacy and variance. The method is the first to explicitly quantify and exploit cluster homogeneity to improve the privacy-variance trade-off in differentially private causal effect estimation. Empirical and theoretical results demonstrate that the approach achieves lower variance than prior user-level and aggregation-based mechanisms for the same privacy guarantees, especially when high-quality clusters are available.

0fff3b43bfe041111e75acf5341c9667568e32ce.title: Multicalibration as Boosting for Regression
0fff3b43bfe041111e75acf5341c9667568e32ce.research_question: How can the concepts of multicalibration and boosting be unified for regression tasks, and under what conditions does multicalibration with respect to a function class imply Bayes optimality in squared error regression?
0fff3b43bfe041111e75acf5341c9667568e32ce.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a simple iterative algorithm, leveraging a squared error regression oracle over a function class H closed under affine transformations, can achieve both multicalibration and Bayes optimality under a weak learning assumption on H, without requiring realizability assumptions.
0fff3b43bfe041111e75acf5341c9667568e32ce.proposed_method: A new algorithm is proposed that iteratively constructs a regression function f over a discretized range by repeatedly partitioning the data into level sets based on current predictions. For each level set, a squared error regression oracle is called on the subset of data corresponding to that level set to find the function in H that minimizes squared error. The model is then updated by replacing predictions in each level set with the output of the corresponding regressor and rounding to the discretized range. This process is repeated until the overall squared error ceases to decrease by a specified threshold. The method relies on a 'swap regret'-like characterization of multicalibration and only requires standard regression oracles on subsets of the data, not relabeling or classification oracles. The approach is analyzed both as a multicalibration algorithm and as a boosting algorithm, with convergence guarantees provided under a weak learning condition.
0fff3b43bfe041111e75acf5341c9667568e32ce.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using both synthetic two-dimensional datasets for visualization and real-world data derived from the US Census via the Folktables package. The proposed algorithm's performance will be evaluated in terms of its convergence to Bayes optimality, as well as its accuracy and multicalibration guarantees. Baselines will include existing multicalibration algorithms (such as split-and-merge) and standard regression boosting methods. Evaluation metrics will include mean squared error, calibration error, and multicalibration error. The implementation will be optimized for speed and parallelizability, and code will be made available as open source.
0fff3b43bfe041111e75acf5341c9667568e32ce.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a novel, exceedingly simple boosting algorithm for regression that unifies multicalibration and boosting under a weak learning assumption, without requiring realizability. It provides a new 'swap regret'-like characterization of multicalibration for function classes closed under affine transformations. The method avoids the need for relabeling or classification oracles, using only standard regression oracles on subsets of the data. It establishes necessary and sufficient conditions under which multicalibration with respect to a function class implies Bayes optimality, and generalizes the weak learning condition to allow for competitive performance relative to arbitrary constrained function classes.

10044d70ffefdfc57ebc69ae6d52e1f5178bb775.title: Lower Bounds and Nearly Optimal Algorithms in Distributed Learning with Communication Compression
10044d70ffefdfc57ebc69ae6d52e1f5178bb775.research_question: What are the fundamental limits of convergence rates for distributed stochastic optimization algorithms under communication compression, and can nearly optimal algorithms be designed that approach these limits for smooth, non-convex objectives using either unbiased or contractive compressors in unidirectional or bidirectional settings?
10044d70ffefdfc57ebc69ae6d52e1f5178bb775.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that there exist theoretical lower bounds on the convergence rates of distributed learning algorithms with communication compression, and that it is possible to design algorithms that match these lower bounds up to logarithmic factors, regardless of whether unbiased or contractive compressors are used, and whether compression is applied unidirectionally or bidirectionally.
10044d70ffefdfc57ebc69ae6d52e1f5178bb775.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical framework will be developed to establish minimax lower bounds on the convergence rates of distributed stochastic optimization algorithms with communication compression. The analysis will consider both unbiased and contractive compressor classes, as well as unidirectional (worker-to-server only) and bidirectional (both directions) compression schemes. Building on these lower bounds, a new algorithm—referred to as NEOLITHIC—will be designed, which incorporates a fast compressed communication (FCC) module. FCC iteratively compresses and transmits residuals over multiple rounds to reduce compression error exponentially, and can be flexibly applied at both worker and server sides. NEOLITHIC will be compatible with both unbiased and contractive compressors, and will be analyzed to ensure its convergence rate matches the established lower bounds up to logarithmic factors under mild assumptions.
10044d70ffefdfc57ebc69ae6d52e1f5178bb775.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard distributed learning benchmarks with smooth, non-convex loss functions. The experimental setup will include multiple parallel workers communicating with a central server, with data heterogeneity and stochastic gradient noise modeled as per the theoretical assumptions. Both unidirectional and bidirectional compression will be evaluated, using representative unbiased (e.g., stochastic quantization) and contractive (e.g., top-k sparsification) compressors. Baseline algorithms will include state-of-the-art distributed SGD variants with compression, such as Q-SGD, MEM-SGD, Double-Squeeze, CSER, and EF21-SGD. Evaluation metrics will focus on convergence rate (measured as expected squared gradient norm), communication cost (number of rounds or gradient queries), and transient complexity (iterations to reach linear speedup). Extensive experiments will validate the theoretical findings and compare the proposed method against baselines.
10044d70ffefdfc57ebc69ae6d52e1f5178bb775.novelty_claims: The proposal establishes, for the first time, tight minimax lower bounds on the convergence rates of distributed stochastic optimization algorithms with communication compression for smooth, non-convex objectives, applicable to both unbiased and contractive compressors and both unidirectional and bidirectional compression. A novel algorithm, NEOLITHIC, is introduced that provably matches these lower bounds up to logarithmic factors, closing the gap between theory and practice. The analysis reveals that contractive bidirectional compression can achieve convergence rates comparable to unbiased unidirectional compression, challenging prior assumptions. The fast compressed communication module provides an efficient and generalizable approach to reducing compression error in distributed systems.

10150f543c54a74746056ac6ae558353ada200eb.title: General framework for online-to-nonconvex conversion: Schedule-free SGD is also effective for nonconvex optimization
10150f543c54a74746056ac6ae558353ada200eb.research_question: Can schedule-free stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and a general online-to-nonconvex conversion framework provide optimal iteration complexity and theoretical guarantees for nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization problems, particularly in the context of training large neural networks?
10150f543c54a74746056ac6ae558353ada200eb.hypothesis: Schedule-free SGD, when analyzed through a novel online-to-nonconvex conversion framework, achieves optimal iteration complexity for nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization problems, matching or exceeding the performance of existing optimizers even without learning rate scheduling.
10150f543c54a74746056ac6ae558353ada200eb.proposed_method: A general framework for converting online learning algorithms into optimization algorithms for nonconvex losses will be developed. The method maintains three sequences of iterates (x_t, y_t, z_t), where z_t follows the base SGD trajectory, x_t is a weighted average of z_t, and y_t is an interpolation between x_t and z_t. Stochastic gradients are computed at y_t, and updates are performed using parameterized interpolation weights and step sizes. The framework allows arbitrary choices for x_t at each iteration, enabling the design of both existing and novel conversion schemes. Theoretical analysis will focus on the (λ, ε)-stationarity criterion, targeting approximate Goldstein stationary points, and will leverage discounted regret bounds from online learning to derive nonconvex optimization guarantees. Special attention will be given to parameter selection, such as setting interpolation weights close to 1 and using larger-than-usual step sizes.
10150f543c54a74746056ac6ae558353ada200eb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization benchmarks, including large-scale neural network training tasks. The proposed schedule-free SGD and its variants derived from the general conversion framework will be evaluated against established baselines such as SGD with momentum and Adam. Evaluation metrics will include iteration complexity (number of stochastic gradient oracle calls to reach a (λ, ε)-stationary point), convergence rates, and empirical loss reduction. Theoretical results will be validated by comparing empirical performance with predicted optimal rates. Parameter sweeps (e.g., for interpolation weights and step sizes) will be performed to confirm theoretical insights regarding optimal choices.
10150f543c54a74746056ac6ae558353ada200eb.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a general online-to-nonconvex conversion framework that not only recovers existing conversion schemes but also enables new, theoretically optimal algorithms for nonconvex optimization. A novel conversion is identified that directly corresponds to schedule-free SGD, establishing its optimality in nonsmooth, nonconvex settings for the first time. The analysis provides new theoretical insights into parameter selection for schedule-free methods, explaining empirical phenomena previously unaccounted for by convex theory. The framework unifies and extends prior work, offering a principled approach to designing and analyzing optimizers for challenging nonconvex problems.

101914972192c4fa0c7eab6ffc72f13d3ae1dde0.title: State-Free Inference of State-Space Models: The Transfer Function Approach
101914972192c4fa0c7eab6ffc72f13d3ae1dde0.research_question: How can state-space models for deep learning be designed and parameterized to enable highly efficient, parallel, and memory-efficient inference for long sequence modeling tasks, without sacrificing expressivity or downstream performance?
101914972192c4fa0c7eab6ffc72f13d3ae1dde0.hypothesis: State-space models parameterized via their rational transfer function representation, and equipped with a state-free, frequency-domain parallel inference algorithm, can achieve superior computational efficiency and memory usage while maintaining or improving performance on long-range sequence modeling tasks compared to existing state-space and convolutional models.
101914972192c4fa0c7eab6ffc72f13d3ae1dde0.proposed_method: A new approach is developed that parameterizes state-space models (SSMs) using their rational transfer function (RTF) representation, which fully captures the functional space of any linear time-invariant SSM, including those with dense state transition matrices. The method introduces a state-free parallel inference algorithm that leverages the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to compute the spectrum of the convolutional kernel directly from the transfer function coefficients, bypassing the need to materialize or scan over the state dimension. The RTF is defined by numerator and denominator polynomial coefficients, and the impulse response is computed efficiently in the frequency domain, enabling O(ℓ) space and O(ℓ log ℓ) time complexities for sequence length ℓ, regardless of the state size n. For autoregressive and single-step inference, the method provides a recurrent companion form, and a stable parameterization scheme is proposed to ensure numerical stability during training.
101914972192c4fa0c7eab6ffc72f13d3ae1dde0.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a range of sequence modeling tasks, including the Long Range Arena (LRA) benchmark (with tasks such as ListOps, Text, Retrieval, Image, Pathfinder, and Path-X), language modeling on WikiText-103, and synthetic memorization tasks like Copying and Delay. The proposed method is compared against strong baselines, including S4, S4D, S5, SpaceTime, Hyena, Transformers, and other attention-free models. Evaluation metrics include classification accuracy, perplexity for language modeling, root mean squared error for synthetic tasks, and empirical measurements of GPU memory usage and inference/training latency. Models are tested across varying state sizes and sequence lengths to assess scalability and efficiency. Additional experiments include distillation of MLP-based filters into the proposed RTF-based SSMs and ablation studies on initialization schemes for stability.
101914972192c4fa0c7eab6ffc72f13d3ae1dde0.novelty_claims: The proposed method claims several innovations: (1) a complete and expressive parameterization of SSMs via rational transfer functions, (2) a state-free, FFT-based parallel inference algorithm that achieves O(ℓ) space and O(ℓ log ℓ) time complexity, independent of state size, (3) improved computational and memory efficiency over existing scan-based and time-domain SSMs, (4) empirical demonstration of state-of-the-art or superior performance on long-range sequence modeling tasks and language modeling, and (5) a stable initialization scheme for high-order polynomial parameterizations, enabling robust training of deep SSMs.

10301766e5686bda76722ef2af1362213b934cc0.title: SpatialVLA: Exploring Spatial Representations for Visual-Language-Action Model
10301766e5686bda76722ef2af1362213b934cc0.research_question: How can spatial representations be effectively integrated into vision-language-action (VLA) models to enable generalist robot policies that exhibit strong 3D scene understanding, cross-embodiment generalization, and efficient adaptation to new robot setups and tasks?
10301766e5686bda76722ef2af1362213b934cc0.hypothesis: Injecting 3D spatial information into both the observation and action spaces of VLA models, via egocentric 3D position encoding and adaptive action grids, will significantly improve the generalization, spatial reasoning, and transferability of robot policies across diverse tasks, embodiments, and environments.
10301766e5686bda76722ef2af1362213b934cc0.proposed_method: A novel VLA model, SpatialVLA, will be developed that augments a vision-language backbone with two key spatial modules: Ego3D Position Encoding and Adaptive Action Grids. Ego3D Position Encoding will integrate depth information and camera intrinsics to generate egocentric 3D spatial representations from 2D images, eliminating the need for robot-camera calibration and enabling universal applicability. The Adaptive Action Grids module will discretize continuous robot actions (translation, rotation, gripper) into data-driven, adaptive spatial grids, fitting Gaussian distributions to action statistics and enabling token-based action prediction. During training, the model will be pre-trained on large-scale, heterogeneous robot datasets to learn generalizable spatial knowledge, and post-training will involve adapting the action grids and embeddings to new robot-specific distributions via efficient re-discretization and trilinear interpolation. The model will predict spatial action tokens autoregressively, which are then de-tokenized into continuous actions for robot control.
10301766e5686bda76722ef2af1362213b934cc0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both simulation and real-world robot platforms, including Google Robot, WidowX, and Franka, covering 24 real-robot tasks and 3 simulation environments. The model will be pre-trained on a mixture of large-scale datasets (OXE and RH20T, totaling 1.1 million episodes) and evaluated in zero-shot and fine-tuning scenarios. Baselines will include state-of-the-art generalist robot policies such as RT-1, RT-1-X, RT-2-X, Octo, OpenVLA, TraceVLA, RoboVLM, and Diffusion Policy. Evaluation metrics will include visual matching, variant aggregation, and task success rates, with comprehensive ablation studies on grid discretization, spatial encoding, and fine-tuning strategies (full, LoRA, spatial embedding adaptation). Special spatial understanding tasks and LIBERO benchmarks will be used to assess 3D spatial reasoning and generalization.
10301766e5686bda76722ef2af1362213b934cc0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a universal, robot-agnostic framework for spatial representation in VLA models by combining egocentric 3D position encoding and adaptive action grids. This enables efficient and transferable spatial knowledge learning across heterogeneous robots and tasks. The method provides a new mechanism for post-training adaptation via action grid re-discretization and spatial embedding interpolation, supporting rapid transfer to new robot embodiments. The approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in both zero-shot and fine-tuning settings, especially on tasks requiring complex spatial reasoning, and demonstrates significantly faster inference with fewer action tokens per step.

10302f3cb84315efbbe1c528c8902cacad49d98a.title: ALMGuard: Safety Shortcuts and Where to Find Them as Guardrails for Audio-Language Models
10302f3cb84315efbbe1c528c8902cacad49d98a.research_question: How can audio-language models (ALMs) be robustly defended against jailbreak attacks that exploit vulnerabilities unique to their multimodal nature, while preserving their utility on benign tasks?
10302f3cb84315efbbe1c528c8902cacad49d98a.hypothesis: Well-aligned audio-language models inherently possess latent safety shortcuts—input sensitivities or pathways—that, if efficiently and harmlessly activated at inference time, can steer the model toward safer behavior and mitigate jailbreak attacks without significantly degrading performance on benign tasks.
10302f3cb84315efbbe1c528c8902cacad49d98a.proposed_method: A defense framework, ALMGuard, will be developed to systematically discover and activate inherent safety shortcuts in ALMs. The method will identify universal Shortcut Activation Perturbations (SAPs)—lightweight, universal acoustic perturbations—that are applied to the input Mel-spectrogram to trigger these safety pathways during inference. To minimize utility loss, a Mel-Gradient Sparse Mask (M-GSM) will be constructed by analyzing gradient sensitivities across Mel-frequency bins, selecting only those bins that are highly influential for jailbreak mitigation but largely inconsequential for benign speech understanding. The SAP will be optimized using Projected Gradient Descent, constrained to the masked frequency bins, ensuring robust defense with minimal impact on benign inputs. The approach requires no model retraining and is designed for efficient, near zero-cost deployment.
10302f3cb84315efbbe1c528c8902cacad49d98a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four state-of-the-art ALMs (Qwen2-Audio, LLaMA-Omni, Lyra-Base, Qwen2.5-Omni) using the AdvBench-Audio dataset, which contains 520 audio queries derived from standard jailbreak benchmarks. Six representative jailbreak attacks will be evaluated: three acoustic-based (AdvWave, AdvWave-P, Gupta et al.) and three semantic-based (PAIR-Audio, ICA, PAP-Audio). Baseline defenses will include traditional audio adversarial defenses (Gaussian Noise, Local Smoothing, Downsampling) and text-based jailbreak defenses (Self-Reminder, In-Context Defense). Evaluation metrics will include Success Rate of Attack (SRoA) for robustness, Word Error Rate (WER) on LibriSpeech for ASR utility, and Response Quality Score (RQS) on AIR-Bench-Chat for interaction quality. Adaptive (white-box) attacks will also be considered to assess robustness under strong threat models. Hyperparameter ablations and utility impact analyses will be performed to validate the method’s effectiveness and efficiency.
10302f3cb84315efbbe1c528c8902cacad49d98a.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the concept of leveraging inherent safety shortcuts in ALMs for defense, representing the first systematic approach to discover and activate such latent pathways for robust and generalizable jailbreak mitigation. The universal SAP, precisely guided by the novel M-GSM technique, targets sparse, security-critical acoustic regions, maximizing defense effectiveness while minimizing utility loss. The method demonstrates strong generalization to unseen attacks and models, achieves state-of-the-art robustness against ALM-specific jailbreaks, and preserves model utility with negligible inference overhead. The approach is lightweight, requires no model retraining, and is theoretically justified to generalize and bound utility degradation.

104b0bb1da562d53cbda87aec79ef6a2827d191a.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
104b0bb1da562d53cbda87aec79ef6a2827d191a.research_question: How can large language models be pretrained and fine-tuned to achieve high performance, helpfulness, and safety in dialogue applications, while providing open access to the research community?
104b0bb1da562d53cbda87aec79ef6a2827d191a.hypothesis: Large language models trained on a diverse, high-quality dataset and fine-tuned with supervised instruction data and reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF), including explicit safety alignment, will outperform existing open-source chat models on benchmarks of helpfulness and safety, and approach the performance of closed-source models.
104b0bb1da562d53cbda87aec79ef6a2827d191a.proposed_method: A new family of large language models will be pretrained using an optimized auto-regressive transformer architecture on a large, carefully curated corpus of publicly available online data, with robust data cleaning and up-sampling of factual sources to reduce hallucinations. The pretraining will utilize architectural improvements such as increased context length and grouped-query attention for scalability, and employ advanced optimization techniques (AdamW, cosine learning rate schedule, RMSNorm, SwiGLU, RoPE). Fine-tuning will proceed in two stages: first, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with high-quality, manually annotated instruction-following data focused on dialogue, helpfulness, and safety; second, iterative RLHF using binary preference data collected from human annotators, with separate reward models for helpfulness and safety. Additional techniques such as Ghost Attention will be explored to improve multi-turn dialogue consistency. Safety will be further enhanced through targeted annotation, safety-specific fine-tuning, and adversarial red-teaming.
104b0bb1da562d53cbda87aec79ef6a2827d191a.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate pretrained and fine-tuned models at multiple scales (7B, 13B, 34B, 70B parameters) on a comprehensive suite of academic benchmarks, including code generation (HumanEval, MBPP), commonsense reasoning (PIQA, SIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC, OpenBookQA, CommonsenseQA), world knowledge (NaturalQuestions, TriviaQA), reading comprehension (SQuAD, QuAC, BoolQ), mathematics (GSM8K, MATH), and aggregated benchmarks (MMLU, BBH, AGIEval). Baselines will include previous Llama models, MosaicML MPT, Falcon, and closed-source models such as GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and PaLM. Evaluation metrics will include pass@1, accuracy, and human evaluations for helpfulness and safety, using both direct human raters and model-based (e.g., GPT-4) assessments. Safety will be assessed with adversarial prompts and red-teaming, and carbon footprint of training will be measured and reported.
104b0bb1da562d53cbda87aec79ef6a2827d191a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new open family of large language models with up to 70B parameters, trained on a significantly larger and cleaner dataset than prior models, and incorporating architectural advances for scalability. The fine-tuning pipeline combines high-quality, vendor-annotated instruction data, large-scale human preference collection, and explicit separation of helpfulness and safety reward models during RLHF. The method includes novel techniques for multi-turn dialogue consistency and a comprehensive, transparent safety alignment process, including red-teaming and iterative safety evaluation. The open release of both base and fine-tuned models, along with detailed methodology and responsible use guidelines, aims to democratize access to high-quality LLMs and support responsible AI development.

10667c1ae4b49808772b5a377c5b52196701267f.title: When and why vision-language models behave like bags-of-words, and what to do about it?
10667c1ae4b49808772b5a377c5b52196701267f.research_question: How well do vision-language models (VLMs) encode compositional relationships, such as object-attribute associations, inter-object relations, and word order, and how can their deficiencies in these areas be systematically identified and improved?
10667c1ae4b49808772b5a377c5b52196701267f.hypothesis: Vision-language models trained with standard contrastive objectives on large-scale retrieval datasets do not adequately encode compositional and order information, but incorporating composition-aware hard negatives into the training process will significantly enhance their ability to understand and represent such information.
10667c1ae4b49808772b5a377c5b52196701267f.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark, Attribution, Relation, and Order (ARO), will be developed to systematically evaluate VLMs on their understanding of object attributes, inter-object relations, and order sensitivity. The benchmark will consist of large-scale datasets derived from Visual Genome and GQA for relation and attribution tasks, and from COCO and Flickr30k for order sensitivity tasks, with carefully constructed test cases that require distinguishing between correct and perturbed captions or image compositions. To address observed deficiencies, a novel training modification will be introduced: composition-aware hard negative mining. This involves generating targeted negative captions by swapping linguistic elements (such as nouns, adjectives, or verb phrases) and sampling visually similar images as hard negatives within each training batch. The modified contrastive learning objective will incorporate these hard negatives, encouraging the model to learn fine-grained compositional distinctions and order sensitivity.
10667c1ae4b49808772b5a377c5b52196701267f.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate state-of-the-art VLMs (e.g., CLIP, BLIP, Flava, X-VLM) on the ARO benchmark, measuring their accuracy in distinguishing between correct and perturbed captions or image compositions. The datasets used include Visual Genome (for relation and attribution tasks), COCO, and Flickr30k (for order sensitivity and retrieval tasks), with over 50,000 test cases for robust statistical analysis. Baselines will include standard contrastive pretraining and retrieval-based evaluation, as well as ablations with and without the proposed hard negative mining. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on the ARO tasks, Recall@1 and Recall@5 for retrieval, and standard image classification benchmarks (e.g., CIFAR10/100, ImageNet) to ensure downstream performance is not compromised. Experiments will also test the impact of removing order and compositional cues from captions and images to assess model reliance on these structures.
10667c1ae4b49808772b5a377c5b52196701267f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the largest and most fine-grained benchmark to date for evaluating compositional and order understanding in VLMs, addressing limitations of prior small-scale or mixed-phenomena datasets. It provides a systematic analysis revealing that high retrieval performance does not imply compositional understanding. The composition-aware hard negative mining strategy is a simple yet effective modification to contrastive learning, shown to substantially improve VLM performance on compositional and order-sensitive tasks without degrading downstream task performance. This approach offers a new direction for enhancing VLMs' compositional reasoning capabilities through targeted training interventions.

107fb6eec2febbae12db29bf3e311aaf5680027c.title: Video-LLaVA: Learning United Visual Representation by Alignment Before Projection
107fb6eec2febbae12db29bf3e311aaf5680027c.research_question: How can a large language model be enabled to simultaneously and effectively understand both images and videos by learning from a unified visual representation, and what are the benefits of aligning visual modalities before projection into the language model?
107fb6eec2febbae12db29bf3e311aaf5680027c.hypothesis: Aligning image and video features into a unified visual representation before projection into a large language model will enable improved multi-modal reasoning, allowing the model to outperform modality-specific or separately trained models on both image and video understanding tasks.
107fb6eec2febbae12db29bf3e311aaf5680027c.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that first aligns image and video features into a shared visual feature space using modality encoders derived from LanguageBind, which are pre-trained to map both images and videos into the language feature space. This unified visual representation is then passed through a shared projection layer and combined with tokenized textual queries before being input to a large language model (LLM), such as Vicuna. The training pipeline consists of two stages: (1) understanding pretraining on large-scale image-text and video-text pairs to teach the model basic visual interpretation, and (2) instruction tuning using multi-turn, instruction-based conversations to develop advanced visual reasoning abilities. Joint training is performed with mixed batches of image and video data, allowing the LLM to learn from both modalities simultaneously.
107fb6eec2febbae12db29bf3e311aaf5680027c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of image and video understanding benchmarks. For video question-answering, datasets such as MSVD-QA, MSRVTT-QA, TGIF-QA, and ActivityNet-QA will be used, with performance evaluated using accuracy and GPT-Assistant-based scoring. For image understanding, benchmarks include VQAv2, GQA, VisWiz, ScienceQA-IMG, TextVQA, POPE, MMBench, LLaVA-Bench, and MM-Vet, with metrics such as accuracy and F1-score. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art LVLMs such as Video-ChatGPT, Video-LLaMA, InstructBLIP, MiniGPT-4, and others. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of unified versus separated visual representations and the effects of joint training. Training utilizes Vicuna-7B as the LLM, LanguageBind encoders for visual modalities, and a shared projection layer, with images resized to 224x224 and videos sampled at 8 frames per clip.
107fb6eec2febbae12db29bf3e311aaf5680027c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified visual representation for both images and videos by aligning features before projection into the LLM, addressing the misalignment issue present in prior multi-modal models. Joint training on both modalities enables the LLM to learn complementary visual concepts, leading to mutual performance gains in both image and video understanding tasks. The framework demonstrates that a single LVLM can surpass or match the performance of expert models specialized for either images or videos, and extensive ablation validates the benefits of alignment before projection and joint training. This approach provides a robust baseline and new insights for unified multi-modal learning in large language models.

10923e416d15ab36161f4ab9ad40aa15bb91f541.title: Self-supervised learning of Split Invariant Equivariant representations
10923e416d15ab36161f4ab9ad40aa15bb91f541.research_question: How can self-supervised learning be advanced to jointly learn invariant and equivariant representations that are suitable for a wide range of downstream tasks, especially in complex scenarios where both types of information are valuable?
10923e416d15ab36161f4ab9ad40aa15bb91f541.hypothesis: Splitting representations into invariant and equivariant components, combined with a hypernetwork-based predictor that leverages knowledge of group transformations, will enable the learning of richer, more generalizable representations that outperform existing methods on both invariant and equivariant tasks.
10923e416d15ab36161f4ab9ad40aa15bb91f541.proposed_method: A novel self-supervised learning framework is proposed that introduces a split in the learned representations: one part is optimized for invariance to transformations, while the other is optimized for equivariance. The method employs a hypernetwork-based predictor that takes group transformation parameters as input and outputs the weights for a transformation in the latent space, enabling the learning of equivariant representations without collapsing to invariance. The architecture is based on a joint-embedding framework, where two augmented views of an image are encoded and split into invariant and equivariant parts, each processed by separate projection heads. The equivariant part is further processed by the hypernetwork-based predictor, which is trained to map representations according to the applied transformation. A combined loss function, based on VICReg, enforces similarity for invariant components, equivariance for the equivariant components, and regularizes the variance and covariance of the embeddings to avoid representational collapse.
10923e416d15ab36161f4ab9ad40aa15bb91f541.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using 3DIEBench, a newly introduced large-scale dataset of 3D object renderings with over 2.5 million images across 55 classes, where full control over object and scene transformations is available. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art invariant (e.g., VICReg, SimCLR, SimCLR+AugSelf) and equivariant (e.g., EquiMod, SEN) self-supervised learning baselines, using both their original and the proposed hypernetwork-based predictors. Evaluation will be performed on both invariant tasks (linear classification) and equivariant tasks (rotation and color prediction) using frozen representations and linear or MLP heads. Metrics such as top-1 classification accuracy, R^2 for regression tasks, Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR), Hit@k, and Prediction Retrieval Error (PRE) will be used. All models will use a ResNet-18 encoder and be trained for 2000 epochs with Adam optimizer, and ablations will assess the impact of the predictor and representation split.
10923e416d15ab36161f4ab9ad40aa15bb91f541.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new benchmark dataset (3DIEBench) that enables controlled evaluation of both invariant and equivariant representation learning at scale. It proposes a hypernetwork-based predictor architecture that avoids collapse to invariance and enables effective equivariant learning without prior knowledge of the group action in latent space. The method further innovates by splitting representations into invariant and equivariant components, demonstrating that this split, combined with the hypernetwork predictor, significantly improves performance on equivariant tasks while maintaining strong invariance.
