The approach is shown to outperform existing methods on both qualitative and quantitative metrics, providing a general framework for learning richer representations in self-supervised settings.

10b238f8b0da6edaa24008448e3f0b7a01d7c268.title: Point Transformer V3: Simpler, Faster, Stronger
10b238f8b0da6edaa24008448e3f0b7a01d7c268.research_question: How can the trade-off between accuracy and efficiency in 3D point cloud transformer backbones be overcome to enable scalable, high-performance 3D perception across diverse tasks and datasets?
10b238f8b0da6edaa24008448e3f0b7a01d7c268.hypothesis: Model performance in 3D point cloud perception is more significantly influenced by scaling (in terms of data, receptive field, and model size) than by intricate architectural details, and prioritizing simplicity and efficiency in backbone design will enable superior scalability, speed, and memory efficiency without sacrificing accuracy.
10b238f8b0da6edaa24008448e3f0b7a01d7c268.proposed_method: A new framework, Point Transformer V3 (PTv3), is proposed that restructures unstructured point clouds into serialized, structured formats using space-filling curves (such as Z-order and Hilbert curves and their variants). This serialization enables efficient patch-based attention mechanisms, replacing computationally expensive KNN-based neighborhood construction and relative positional encoding with streamlined, scalable alternatives. Patch grouping and interaction are handled via various strategies (Shift Dilation, Shift Patch, Shift Order, Shuffle Order), maximizing receptive field and feature integration while maintaining efficiency. The method introduces an enhanced conditional positional encoding (xCPE) by prepending a sparse convolutional layer with skip connections before attention, further improving performance with minimal latency overhead. The overall architecture follows a U-Net style encoder-decoder with scalable depth and width, leveraging grid pooling and batch normalization for stability and efficiency.
10b238f8b0da6edaa24008448e3f0b7a01d7c268.experiment_details: Extensive experiments are proposed across more than 20 indoor and outdoor 3D perception tasks, including semantic segmentation (ScanNet, ScanNet200, S3DIS, nuScenes, SemanticKITTI, Waymo), instance segmentation (ScanNet, ScanNet200), and object detection (Waymo). Both training from scratch and multi-dataset joint training paradigms will be used. Baselines include state-of-the-art sparse convolutional networks (MinkUNet, Cylinder3D), previous point cloud transformers (PTv1, PTv2, OctFormer, FlatFormer, SphereFormer, Swin3D), and other recent architectures. Evaluation metrics include mean Intersection over Union (mIoU), mean Average Precision (mAP), accuracy, inference latency, and memory consumption. Ablation studies will be conducted to assess the impact of serialization patterns, patch interaction strategies, positional encoding methods, patch size scaling, normalization layers, and block structures. Efficiency will be measured on real-world hardware (e.g., RTX 4090 GPU), and data efficiency will be evaluated under limited annotation and reconstruction scenarios.
10b238f8b0da6edaa24008448e3f0b7a01d7c268.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled scaling strategy for point cloud transformers, breaking the conventional trade-off between accuracy and efficiency. Key innovations include the use of serialization-based point cloud structuring via space-filling curves, efficient patch-based attention mechanisms, and a highly scalable conditional positional encoding. The method achieves a 3.3× increase in inference speed and a 10.2× reduction in memory usage compared to prior transformers, while expanding the receptive field from 16 to 1024 points. PTv3 demonstrates state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of 3D perception benchmarks, with superior scalability, speed, and memory efficiency, and provides a unified backbone suitable for both indoor and outdoor tasks. The framework also opens new avenues for multimodal and large-scale 3D representation learning.

10b9ca173c665e3f2c322c2d5ce9b9d433fe4629.title: The Effects of Reward Misspecification: Mapping and Mitigating Misaligned Models
10b9ca173c665e3f2c322c2d5ce9b9d433fe4629.research_question: How does reward misspecification in reinforcement learning environments lead to misaligned agent behavior as agent capabilities increase, and what methods can be developed to detect and mitigate such misalignment in the absence of reliable true reward signals?
10b9ca173c665e3f2c322c2d5ce9b9d433fe4629.hypothesis: As the optimization power of reinforcement learning agents increases, agents are more likely to exploit misspecified reward functions, resulting in higher proxy rewards but lower true rewards, and that phase transitions in agent behavior may occur at certain capability thresholds. Furthermore, anomaly detection methods can be developed to identify misaligned policies even when true rewards are not directly observable.
10b9ca173c665e3f2c322c2d5ce9b9d433fe4629.proposed_method: A comprehensive suite of reinforcement learning environments will be constructed, each featuring carefully designed misspecified proxy reward functions that differ from the true task objectives through misweighting, ontological errors, or scope limitations. Agents will be trained using state-of-the-art RL algorithms (such as PPO, SAC, and IMPALA) with systematically varied capabilities, including model size, training duration, action space resolution, and observation fidelity. The relationship between agent optimization power and the emergence of reward hacking will be quantitatively and qualitatively analyzed, with particular attention paid to phase transitions in agent behavior. To address the challenge of detecting misalignment without access to true rewards, an anomaly detection benchmark (POLYNOMALY) will be developed, leveraging trusted reference policies and empirical action distributions to flag aberrant agent behaviors using statistical distance measures.
10b9ca173c665e3f2c322c2d5ce9b9d433fe4629.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across four diverse RL environments: traffic control (Flow/SUMO simulator), COVID-19 response (SEIR-based simulation), blood glucose monitoring (FDA-approved simulator), and the Atari Riverraid game (OpenAI Gym). For each environment, multiple misspecified proxy reward functions will be defined and agents will be trained using the proxy rewards, with performance evaluated on both proxy and true rewards. Agent capabilities will be varied by adjusting neural network size, number of training steps, action space granularity, and observation noise. Baseline anomaly detectors, such as mean Jensen-Shannon divergence and Hellinger distance between action distributions of trusted and candidate policies, will be evaluated using metrics like AUROC and maximum F-1 score. The anomaly detection task will be benchmarked on labeled policy datasets, with policies categorized as acceptable or problematic based on true reward performance.
10b9ca173c665e3f2c322c2d5ce9b9d433fe4629.novelty_claims: The proposed research systematically investigates the phenomenon of reward hacking as a function of agent capabilities across multiple realistic RL environments and reward misspecification types. It introduces the concept of phase transitions in agent behavior due to increased optimization power, highlighting the risks of abrupt misalignment. A novel anomaly detection benchmark (POLYNOMALY) is developed to identify misaligned policies without access to true rewards, accompanied by baseline detectors and empirical evaluation. The work aims to provide foundational insights and tools for safer RL deployment in real-world settings where reward misspecification and emergent misalignment are critical concerns.

10bd38673951f5d7729568284093cbd80482ab16.title: Vision Transformers Need Registers
10bd38673951f5d7729568284093cbd80482ab16.research_question: How can the presence of artifacts in feature maps of vision transformers be understood and mitigated to improve interpretability and performance on dense visual prediction and object discovery tasks?
10bd38673951f5d7729568284093cbd80482ab16.hypothesis: Large and sufficiently trained vision transformer models repurpose tokens from low-informative image regions as internal registers for computation, leading to undesirable artifacts in feature maps. Introducing explicit register tokens into the input sequence will isolate this behavior, eliminate artifacts, and enhance downstream performance and interpretability.
10bd38673951f5d7729568284093cbd80482ab16.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a set of additional learnable tokens, referred to as register tokens, into the input sequence of vision transformers after the patch embedding layer. These tokens are not associated with any specific image region and are intended to serve as computational registers during the transformer's forward pass. The output representations of these register tokens are discarded after processing, and only the class ([CLS]) token and patch tokens are used for downstream tasks. The number of register tokens is ablated to determine the optimal configuration for artifact removal and performance improvement. This architectural modification is applied during pretraining and can be integrated into supervised, text-supervised, and self-supervised transformer training regimes.
10bd38673951f5d7729568284093cbd80482ab16.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using three state-of-the-art training paradigms: supervised (DeiT-III on ImageNet-22k), text-supervised (OpenCLIP on a Shutterstock-based corpus), and self-supervised (DINOv2 on ImageNet-22k). Models will be trained with and without register tokens, and their performance will be evaluated on downstream tasks such as ImageNet classification (linear probing), ADE20k semantic segmentation, and NYUd monocular depth estimation. Evaluation metrics include top-1 accuracy, mean IoU, and RMSE for depth. Additionally, unsupervised object discovery will be assessed using the LOST algorithm on VOC2007, VOC2012, and COCO20k, with corloc as the metric. Qualitative and quantitative analyses of feature and attention maps will be performed to assess artifact removal and interpretability.
10bd38673951f5d7729568284093cbd80482ab16.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the use of explicit register tokens in vision transformers as a simple yet effective architectural modification to eliminate high-norm artifact tokens from feature maps. The approach generalizes across different training paradigms and model sizes, leading to smoother and more interpretable feature and attention maps. The method improves performance on dense prediction and object discovery tasks, and provides a new perspective on the internal computation mechanisms of vision transformers by isolating register-like behavior into dedicated tokens.

10d3c1cfb98f4e547f579a30b31f2361297983f1.title: MMT-Bench: A Comprehensive Multimodal Benchmark for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models Towards Multitask AGI
10d3c1cfb98f4e547f579a30b31f2361297983f1.research_question: How can large vision-language models (LVLMs) be comprehensively evaluated across a broad range of multimodal tasks to better track progress toward multitask artificial general intelligence (AGI)?
10d3c1cfb98f4e547f579a30b31f2361297983f1.hypothesis: A benchmark that covers a diverse and extensive set of multimodal tasks, including both in-domain and out-of-domain scenarios, will reveal significant performance gaps in current LVLMs and provide actionable insights for their advancement toward multitask AGI.
10d3c1cfb98f4e547f579a30b31f2361297983f1.proposed_method: A comprehensive multimodal benchmark, termed MMT-Bench, will be constructed to evaluate LVLMs across a wide spectrum of tasks. The benchmark will be organized hierarchically, comprising 32 meta-tasks and 162 subtasks, resulting in over 31,000 multi-choice visual questions. Data will be collected from a variety of publicly available datasets, spanning 13 image types (e.g., natural scenes, synthetic images, depth maps, medical images, point clouds), and will be unified into a standardized metadata format. Question and answer pairs will be generated using a combination of manual rules and large language models (e.g., ChatGPT), ensuring high-quality and task-relevant content. The evaluation protocol will include both single-image and multi-image prompts, as well as visual referring prompts, to test a wide range of multimodal capabilities such as recognition, localization, reasoning, OCR, counting, 3D perception, and temporal understanding.
10d3c1cfb98f4e547f579a30b31f2361297983f1.experiment_details: Experiments will involve evaluating 30 publicly available LVLMs, including both open-source and proprietary models (e.g., InternVL-Chat, GPT-4V, GeminiProVision), using the MMT-Bench dataset. Baselines such as random and frequent choice will be included for reference. Accuracy will serve as the primary evaluation metric, with performance reported at both the meta-task and subtask levels. Additional analyses will be conducted to assess the impact of different prompting strategies (e.g., multi-image vs. single-image, visual vs. text-based prompts) and to perform error analysis by categorizing model mistakes (e.g., perception, reasoning, knowledge errors). Taskonomy analysis will be performed using task vectors and hierarchical clustering to identify in-domain and out-of-domain task clusters, and Kendall's tau will be used to measure ranking consistency across tasks.
10d3c1cfb98f4e547f579a30b31f2361297983f1.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces the most extensive and diverse multimodal evaluation suite to date, with over 31,000 questions spanning 162 subtasks and 13 image types. It enables systematic identification of both in-domain and out-of-domain tasks for LVLMs, supports a wide variety of multimodal capabilities, and provides a task map for detailed taskonomy analysis. The benchmark is designed to reveal nuanced performance gaps in current LVLMs, especially in fine-grained perception and reasoning, and to guide future model development toward multitask AGI. The methodology also incorporates innovative prompting strategies and error analysis frameworks not present in prior benchmarks.

10d3e2b5d7b17f6eab363100ae33f62c7820ac34.title: MeshAnything: Artist-Created Mesh Generation with Autoregressive Transformers
10d3e2b5d7b17f6eab363100ae33f62c7820ac34.research_question: How can high-quality, artist-created meshes be automatically generated from arbitrary 3D representations in a way that matches the topology and efficiency of human-created meshes, and can be seamlessly integrated into 3D industry pipelines?
10d3e2b5d7b17f6eab363100ae33f62c7820ac34.hypothesis: Formulating mesh extraction as a shape-conditioned generation problem using autoregressive transformers, combined with a learned mesh vocabulary and robust decoding, will enable the automatic production of artist-quality meshes from diverse 3D representations, resulting in meshes with superior topology, fewer faces, and comparable shape fidelity to human-created meshes.
10d3e2b5d7b17f6eab363100ae33f62c7820ac34.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a shape-conditioned mesh generation framework, MeshAnything, which consists of two main components: a VQ-VAE for learning a discrete vocabulary of mesh face embeddings, and a decoder-only autoregressive transformer conditioned on shape features. During training, high-quality artist-created meshes are paired with shape conditions represented as point clouds (including normals), sampled from coarsened versions of the meshes to match the domain of automatically generated assets. The VQ-VAE encodes each mesh as a sequence of tokens, which the transformer learns to generate conditioned on the point cloud features, encoded via a pretrained point cloud encoder and projected into the mesh token space. To address imperfections in token sequences during inference, a novel noise-resistant decoder is developed by fine-tuning the VQ-VAE decoder with injected noise and auxiliary shape information, enhancing robustness and mesh quality.
10d3e2b5d7b17f6eab363100ae33f62c7820ac34.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a combined dataset of filtered artist-created meshes from Objaverse and ShapeNet, with approximately 56,000 meshes after quality filtering. The training set will comprise 90% of the data, with the remainder used for evaluation. MeshAnything will be compared against both mesh generation baselines (e.g., PolyGen, MeshGPT) and mesh extraction baselines (e.g., Marching Cubes, ShapeAsPoints, Pengetal.), using both user studies and quantitative metrics such as Coverage (COV), Minimum Matching Distance (MMD), 1-Nearest Neighbor Accuracy (1-NNA), Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), and Kernel Inception Distance (KID). User studies will involve participants rating shape and topology quality, while quantitative metrics will be computed on generated meshes. Implementation details include the use of BERT-based encoders/decoders for the VQ-VAE, OPT-350M for the transformer, and a pretrained point cloud encoder, with training on 8 A100 GPUs.
10d3e2b5d7b17f6eab363100ae33f62c7820ac34.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first formulation of mesh extraction as a shape-conditioned generation problem, enabling the direct generation of artist-created meshes aligned with arbitrary 3D shapes. The method incorporates a novel noise-resistant decoder that leverages shape conditions for robust mesh reconstruction, addressing domain gaps between training and inference. The approach is designed for broad applicability, supporting integration with any 3D asset production pipeline and generalizing to unlimited shape categories. Experimental results are expected to demonstrate significant improvements in mesh topology, efficiency (orders of magnitude fewer faces), and shape fidelity compared to both traditional and recent neural mesh extraction/generation methods.

10feab31bb9e71a0f1094fb00c0554abfb992c4d.title: ProRL: Prolonged Reinforcement Learning Expands Reasoning Boundaries in Large Language Models
10feab31bb9e71a0f1094fb00c0554abfb992c4d.research_question: Can prolonged reinforcement learning (RL) training meaningfully expand the reasoning boundaries of large language models, enabling them to develop novel reasoning strategies and generalize to out-of-distribution and complex tasks beyond the capabilities of their base models?
10feab31bb9e71a0f1094fb00c0554abfb992c4d.hypothesis: Prolonged RL training, when combined with techniques such as KL divergence control, reference policy resetting, and diverse task coverage, enables language models to discover new reasoning strategies and expand their reasoning boundaries beyond what is accessible to the base model, even under extensive sampling.
10feab31bb9e71a0f1094fb00c0554abfb992c4d.proposed_method: A novel training methodology, ProRL, is developed to enable extended RL training for language models. The approach is built on Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), which estimates advantages using group scores rather than a value model. To address entropy collapse and maintain exploration, the method incorporates decoupled clipping (with separate upper and lower bounds), dynamic sampling to focus on intermediate-difficulty prompts, and explicit KL divergence regularization between the current and reference policies. Periodic reference policy resets are performed to a recent snapshot of the online policy, preventing premature convergence and enabling continued policy improvement. The training is conducted on a diverse suite of tasks, including math, code, STEM, logic puzzles, and instruction following, with verifiable reward signals for each task.
10feab31bb9e71a0f1094fb00c0554abfb992c4d.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using a 1.5B parameter language model, trained via ProRL on a dataset of 136,000 problems spanning five domains. Training is performed using verl, with a batch size of 256, a mini-batch size of 64, a high rollout temperature (1.2), and up to 16 responses per prompt. The training runs for approximately 16,000 GPU hours on 48 NVIDIA H100 nodes, with periodic resets and validation monitoring. Evaluation is performed on a wide range of benchmarks: for math (AIME24, AIME25, AMC, MATH, Minerva, Olympiad), coding (APPS, Codecontests, Codeforces, TACO, HumanevalPlus, LiveCodeBench), STEM (GPQA Diamond), instruction following (IFEval), and logic puzzles (Reasoning Gym), as well as out-of-distribution tasks (acre, boxnet, game_of_life_halting). Metrics include pass@1, pass@16, and pass@128, as well as the Creativity Index to assess novelty. Baselines include the base model (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B), a larger model (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B), and domain-specialized models (DeepScaleR-1.5B for math, DeepCoder-1.5B for code). Inference uses vllm with a sampling temperature of 0.6 and nucleus sampling (top_p=0.95).
10feab31bb9e71a0f1094fb00c0554abfb992c4d.novelty_claims: The proposed methodology enables stable, prolonged RL training for language models, overcoming previous limitations such as entropy collapse and premature convergence. ProRL demonstrates that extended RL can elicit genuinely new reasoning strategies and expand reasoning boundaries, particularly in domains where the base model initially struggles. The approach achieves state-of-the-art results for a 1.5B parameter model, matching or surpassing much larger models and domain-specialized baselines across diverse tasks. The method also enables strong generalization to out-of-distribution and more complex problems, with empirical evidence of increased novelty in reasoning trajectories as measured by the Creativity Index. These findings challenge prior assumptions that RL merely amplifies existing capabilities and establish that, with sufficient training and methodological advances, RL can meaningfully expand the reasoning capabilities of language models.

1104739f75df7edc7fc9c5cc18615dc837c25c7e.title: GeoComplete: Geometry-Aware Diffusion for Reference-Driven Image Completion
1104739f75df7edc7fc9c5cc18615dc837c25c7e.research_question: How can reference-driven image completion be improved to achieve higher geometric consistency and visual fidelity, especially when the target view differs significantly from the reference images?
1104739f75df7edc7fc9c5cc18615dc837c25c7e.hypothesis: Incorporating explicit 3D geometric cues and a targeted masking strategy into a diffusion-based generative framework will significantly improve the geometric consistency and perceptual quality of reference-driven image completion compared to existing image-only or geometry-agnostic approaches.
1104739f75df7edc7fc9c5cc18615dc837c25c7e.proposed_method: A geometry-aware image completion framework is proposed that integrates explicit 3D structural guidance into a dual-branch diffusion architecture. The method begins by generating a 3D point cloud from both reference and target images using the Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer (VGGT) for camera pose and depth estimation, with dynamic regions segmented and filtered out using LangSAM based on text prompts. The dual-branch diffusion model consists of a target branch, which encodes the masked target image, and a cloud branch, which processes the projected point cloud; both branches are fused via joint self-attention, allowing geometric cues to inform the synthesis of missing regions. A target-aware masking strategy is introduced, where informative regions (visible in references but missing in the target) are selectively masked in both reference images and point clouds during training, guiding the model to focus on complementary cues. Conditional cloud masking and a specialized attention mask ensure robust integration of geometric and visual information, even in the presence of noisy or incomplete geometric estimates.
1104739f75df7edc7fc9c5cc18615dc837c25c7e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two challenging reference-driven image completion datasets: RealBench and QualBench. RealBench contains 33 scenes with 1–5 reference images per scene, a masked target image, and ground truth completions, while QualBench includes 25 scenes without ground truth, evaluated via user studies. Baselines for comparison include prompt-based methods (SDInpaint, GenerativeFill), reference-based methods (Paint-by-Example, TransFill, RealFill), and geometry-aware approaches. Evaluation metrics encompass low-level (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS), mid-level (DreamSim), and high-level (DINO, CLIP) measures, as well as user study scores (1–5) for perceptual quality. The diffusion model is fine-tuned with LoRA on Stable Diffusion 2 Inpainting, using a batch size of 16 and 2,000 iterations per scene, with all images resized to 512×512. Ablation studies will assess the contributions of the dual-branch architecture, joint self-attention, and target-aware masking, while robustness tests will simulate noisy or sparse point clouds and segmentation errors.
1104739f75df7edc7fc9c5cc18615dc837c25c7e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a geometry-aware dual-branch diffusion model that explicitly conditions image completion on projected 3D point clouds, enabling strong geometric consistency in the generated content. A novel target-aware masking strategy is developed to guide the model toward informative, non-redundant reference cues, improving performance in challenging scenarios with large viewpoint or content differences. The integration of joint self-attention between visual and geometric branches ensures coherent fusion of cues, and conditional cloud masking enhances robustness to upstream geometric estimation errors. The framework achieves substantial improvements over state-of-the-art methods, with a reported 17.1% PSNR gain and superior perceptual quality on benchmark datasets.

1122b654f8b47c1aa9c04ff6bbe7561c798e2ad0.title: Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning in Large Language Models with One Training Example
1122b654f8b47c1aa9c04ff6bbe7561c798e2ad0.research_question: To what extent can the training dataset for reinforcement learning with verifiable reward (RLVR) be reduced while maintaining or improving the mathematical reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs), and what are the mechanisms and generalization properties underlying such data efficiency?
1122b654f8b47c1aa9c04ff6bbe7561c798e2ad0.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that RLVR can achieve substantial improvements in LLM reasoning performance using only one or a few carefully selected training examples, and that policy gradient-based RL with verifiable rewards is sufficient to stimulate generalization and advanced reasoning behaviors, even in the extreme low-data regime.
1122b654f8b47c1aa9c04ff6bbe7561c798e2ad0.proposed_method: A reinforcement learning framework will be developed for fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) on mathematical reasoning tasks using RLVR with extremely limited training data, including as few as one example (1-shot RLVR). The method will utilize policy gradient-based RL algorithms such as GRPO or PPO, with a reward function based on the correctness of the model's final answer to mathematical problems. The loss function will include a policy gradient term, KL divergence to a reference model for language quality, and an entropy term to encourage diverse exploration in model outputs. A data selection strategy based on historical variance of training accuracy will be used to identify impactful training examples, and ablation studies will be conducted to dissect the contributions of each loss component and the effects of label correctness. The approach will also analyze phenomena such as post-saturation generalization, cross-category transfer, and increased self-reflection in model outputs.
1122b654f8b47c1aa9c04ff6bbe7561c798e2ad0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several LLMs, including Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B, Qwen2.5-Math-7B, Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B. The primary datasets will be a 1.2k DeepScaleR-Preview subset (DSR-sub) and the 7.5k-instance MATH training set, with additional evaluation on six mathematical reasoning benchmarks: MATH500, AIME2024, AMC2023, MinervaMath, OlympiadBench, and AIME2025. Non-mathematical reasoning tasks (ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge) will also be included. Baselines will include format-reward RLVR and full-dataset RLVR. Evaluation metrics will be pass@1 accuracy and average performance across benchmarks. The experimental setup will control for batch size, prompt/response length, rollout temperature, and loss coefficients. Detailed ablations will compare the effects of different loss components, data selection methods, and label correctness on both training and test performance.
1122b654f8b47c1aa9c04ff6bbe7561c798e2ad0.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first systematic investigation of RLVR in the extreme low-data regime, demonstrating that a single training example can match or exceed the performance of RLVR with thousands of examples on complex reasoning benchmarks. It identifies and analyzes novel phenomena such as post-saturation generalization, cross-category transfer, and increased self-reflection induced by 1-shot RLVR. The work provides new insights into the mechanisms of RLVR, showing that policy gradient loss is the primary driver of generalization, distinct from grokking, and that entropy-based exploration further enhances performance. The proposal also establishes a simple yet effective data selection criterion based on historical variance, and offers comprehensive ablations on loss components and label robustness.

112b228210d5ec50a1c4da7a8d76db8b6392be81.title: A Sharp Convergence Theory for The Probability Flow ODEs of Diffusion Models
112b228210d5ec50a1c4da7a8d76db8b6392be81.research_question: What are the precise non-asymptotic convergence rates for the probability flow ODE sampler in diffusion models, particularly in high-dimensional settings and under minimal assumptions on the target data distribution?
112b228210d5ec50a1c4da7a8d76db8b6392be81.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the probability flow ODE sampler can achieve nearly linear iteration complexity in the data dimension and target accuracy, under minimal assumptions on the data distribution and with access to sufficiently accurate score function estimates.
112b228210d5ec50a1c4da7a8d76db8b6392be81.proposed_method: A new non-asymptotic theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the convergence of the probability flow ODE sampler in discrete time, decoupling the score estimation and generative sampling phases. The analysis will assume access to ℓ2-accurate estimates of the (Stein) score functions and their Jacobians at each diffusion step. The reverse process will be constructed deterministically, starting from Gaussian noise and iteratively applying a mapping based on the estimated score, with a carefully designed two-phase learning rate schedule. The framework will directly analyze the discrete-time process, avoiding reliance on stochastic differential equation (SDE) or ordinary differential equation (ODE) toolboxes, and will quantify how estimation errors in the score and its Jacobian propagate to the total variation distance between the generated and target distributions.
112b228210d5ec50a1c4da7a8d76db8b6392be81.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic and real-world datasets in high-dimensional Euclidean spaces, with the data distribution only assumed to have bounded second moments and no smoothness or log-concavity requirements. The evaluation will focus on the total variation distance between the generated samples and the true data distribution, with iteration complexity measured as a function of the data dimension d and target accuracy ε. Comparisons will be made to existing theoretical bounds for both deterministic and stochastic diffusion samplers, including those with polynomial and exponential dependencies on d and ε. The impact of score and Jacobian estimation errors will be systematically varied to assess their influence on convergence rates.
112b228210d5ec50a1c4da7a8d76db8b6392be81.novelty_claims: The proposed research establishes, for the first time, a nearly linear dependency of iteration complexity on the data dimension d and accuracy ε for the probability flow ODE sampler, improving upon prior results with quadratic or worse dependencies. The analysis requires only minimal assumptions on the target distribution and explicitly quantifies the effect of both score and Jacobian estimation errors. The theoretical framework is fully non-asymptotic and elementary, directly addressing discrete-time processes without resorting to SDE/ODE theory, thus lowering technical barriers and broadening applicability. The results demonstrate that the deterministic sampler can achieve convergence rates previously only shown for stochastic samplers, and provide sharper bounds than all existing deterministic sampler analyses.

112d8385aa3f362e15ffdc35ac2a083e99b77485.title: Plug-in Performative Optimization
112d8385aa3f362e15ffdc35ac2a083e99b77485.research_question: Can explicit models of performative feedback, even when potentially misspecified, be leveraged to improve the optimization of performative risk in predictive systems, compared to model-agnostic approaches?
112d8385aa3f362e15ffdc35ac2a083e99b77485.hypothesis: Models of performative feedback, even if misspecified, can enable significantly faster convergence and lower excess performative risk than model-agnostic strategies, provided the degree of misspecification is not extreme.
112d8385aa3f362e15ffdc35ac2a083e99b77485.proposed_method: A plug-in performative optimization protocol will be developed that utilizes a parametric family of models (distribution atlas) to approximate the unknown performative feedback map. The protocol consists of three main steps: (1) deploying a sequence of predictors according to a chosen exploration distribution and collecting the resulting data; (2) fitting the parameters of the feedback model to the observed data using empirical risk minimization or maximum likelihood estimation; and (3) computing the plug-in performative optimum by minimizing the estimated performative risk under the fitted model. The method explicitly quantifies and analyzes two sources of error: irreducible misspecification error due to model mismatch, and statistical error from finite sample estimation. Theoretical analysis will provide excess risk bounds in terms of these errors, under both total-variation and Wasserstein distances, and under regularity conditions on the model-fitting procedure.
112d8385aa3f362e15ffdc35ac2a083e99b77485.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several performative prediction settings, including strategic regression, binary strategic classification, and location-family models. Synthetic datasets will be generated according to known performative feedback mechanisms, with varying degrees of model misspecification. The plug-in performative optimization protocol will be compared against model-agnostic baselines such as bandit algorithms, derivative-free optimization, and greedy retraining (SGD), as well as specialized algorithms like PerfGD. Evaluation metrics will include excess performative risk (difference between achieved and optimal performative risk), convergence rates, and robustness to model misspecification. Experimental setups will ensure sufficient exploration of the predictor space and control for sample size to observe statistical error decay.
112d8385aa3f362e15ffdc35ac2a083e99b77485.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a general and principled protocol for leveraging possibly misspecified models in performative prediction, providing theoretical guarantees on excess risk that decompose into misspecification and statistical error. It demonstrates that even imperfect models can yield substantial improvements over model-agnostic methods, due to faster statistical rates. The analysis extends to both total-variation and Wasserstein misspecification, and covers a broad class of performative feedback scenarios, including strategic classification and location families. The work provides new insights into the trade-offs between model complexity, misspecification, and statistical efficiency in performative optimization.

11665dbecb17ef4d3d71b75b8666ce0e61bd43fa.title: LGM: Large Multi-View Gaussian Model for High-Resolution 3D Content Creation
11665dbecb17ef4d3d71b75b8666ce0e61bd43fa.research_question: How can high-resolution, high-fidelity 3D models be efficiently generated from text prompts or single-view images, overcoming the limitations of current 3D representations and computational bottlenecks?
11665dbecb17ef4d3d71b75b8666ce0e61bd43fa.hypothesis: Employing a multi-view Gaussian feature representation, combined with an asymmetric U-Net backbone and robust data augmentation, will enable efficient, high-resolution 3D content creation from text or single-view image inputs, surpassing the quality and speed of existing methods.
11665dbecb17ef4d3d71b75b8666ce0e61bd43fa.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that utilizes multi-view Gaussian features as a compact and expressive 3D representation. An asymmetric U-Net architecture is designed to process multi-view images, each paired with camera pose embeddings, to predict and fuse 3D Gaussians. The U-Net incorporates cross-view self-attention at deeper layers to enhance information sharing across views, and outputs a lower-resolution feature map to allow for high-resolution input images while limiting the number of generated Gaussians. Differentiable rendering is used to supervise the fused Gaussians at novel viewpoints, and robust training is achieved through targeted data augmentations simulating multi-view inconsistencies and camera pose jitter. Additionally, a pipeline is developed to convert generated 3D Gaussians into smooth, textured polygonal meshes via NeRF-based reconstruction and mesh extraction.
11665dbecb17ef4d3d71b75b8666ce0e61bd43fa.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a filtered subset of the Objaverse dataset, consisting of approximately 80,000 high-quality 3D objects rendered from 100 camera views at 512×512 resolution. The model will be trained on four input views per object, with supervision from eight rendered views per batch. Baseline comparisons will include existing feed-forward and optimization-based 3D generation methods such as LRM, Instant3D, and triplane-based NeRF models. Evaluation metrics will include mean square error (MSE), LPIPS perceptual similarity, and qualitative visual assessments of generated 3D models. The model will be trained on 32 A100 GPUs, and inference will leverage off-the-shelf multi-view diffusion models to generate input images from text or single-view images.
11665dbecb17ef4d3d71b75b8666ce0e61bd43fa.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a high-resolution, feed-forward 3D generation framework that fuses multi-view Gaussian features via an asymmetric U-Net, enabling efficient and detailed 3D content creation from text or image inputs. Key innovations include the use of a multi-view Gaussian representation for expressiveness and rendering efficiency, an asymmetric U-Net with cross-view self-attention for scalable high-resolution training, robust data augmentation strategies to bridge the domain gap between real and synthesized multi-view images, and a general pipeline for converting sparse 3D Gaussians into high-quality polygonal meshes. This method is expected to achieve state-of-the-art quality and speed in both text-to-3D and image-to-3D tasks.

1190c204564459b46171e2e179816deb40320769.title: AdaWorld: Learning Adaptable World Models with Latent Actions
1190c204564459b46171e2e179816deb40320769.research_question: How can world models be designed to efficiently adapt to novel environments and heterogeneous action spaces using limited interaction data, thereby enabling effective action transfer and planning across diverse domains?
1190c204564459b46171e2e179816deb40320769.hypothesis: Incorporating action information during the pretraining of world models via self-supervised extraction of latent actions from videos will significantly enhance the adaptability, transferability, and controllability of world models in new environments, even with minimal labeled data and fine-tuning.
1190c204564459b46171e2e179816deb40320769.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces AdaWorld, a framework for highly adaptable world model learning. The method consists of two main components: a latent action autoencoder and an autoregressive world model. The latent action autoencoder, based on a spatiotemporal Transformer architecture, extracts compact, context-invariant latent actions from pairs of consecutive video frames using an information bottleneck and a β-VAE objective to balance expressiveness and disentanglement. These latent actions represent the most critical transitions between frames and are used as unified conditions for pretraining the world model. The autoregressive world model, initialized from a latent diffusion model (e.g., StableVideoDiffusion), is conditioned on historical frames and the extracted latent actions, enabling frame-level control and autoregressive rollout. During adaptation, the control interface can be initialized with averaged latent actions or a lightweight MLP for continuous action spaces, allowing efficient fine-tuning with minimal action-latent action pairs.
1190c204564459b46171e2e179816deb40320769.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a wide range of environments, including simulated games (Procgen, Gym Retro), real-world robot datasets (OpenX-Embodiment, RoboSuite, RoboDesk), and driving scenarios (nuScenes). The training dataset will comprise approximately 2 billion frames from over 1000 diverse environments. Baselines will include action-agnostic pretraining, optical flow-based action conditioning, and discrete latent action (VQ-VAE) variants. Evaluation metrics will include Frechet Video Distance (FVD), Embedding Cosine Similarity (ECS), Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), LPIPS, and human evaluation for action transfer. Experiments will assess action transfer, world model adaptation (with limited samples and fine-tuning steps), and visual planning performance using model-predictive control (MPC) and reinforcement learning baselines (Q-learning). Ablation studies will analyze the impact of data diversity, initialization strategies, and hyperparameter choices.
1190c204564459b46171e2e179816deb40320769.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel framework for extracting context-invariant latent actions from unlabeled videos in a self-supervised manner and using them as unified conditions for action-aware world model pretraining. This enables efficient adaptation to new environments and action spaces with minimal labeled data and fine-tuning. The method demonstrates superior performance in action transfer, world model adaptation, and visual planning compared to conventional action-agnostic and alternative action-aware baselines. Additionally, the latent action space supports semantic action composition and flexible control interface initialization, highlighting its generality and scalability across diverse domains and world model architectures.

11ba4fc174d7a571e9f8ea16b3c6e814fac44c14.title: Meta-Query-Net: Resolving Purity-Informativeness Dilemma in Open-set Active Learning
11ba4fc174d7a571e9f8ea16b3c6e814fac44c14.research_question: How can the trade-off between purity and informativeness be optimally balanced in open-set active learning, where unlabeled data contains both in-distribution and out-of-distribution (open-set noise) examples, to maximize model performance and labeling efficiency?
11ba4fc174d7a571e9f8ea16b3c6e814fac44c14.hypothesis: An adaptive meta-learning framework that dynamically balances purity and informativeness in query selection will outperform existing active learning and open-set active learning methods by more effectively selecting informative and relevant examples, leading to higher model accuracy and robustness across varying noise ratios.
11ba4fc174d7a571e9f8ea16b3c6e814fac44c14.proposed_method: A meta-model, termed Meta-Query-Net (MQ-Net), will be developed to learn a meta-score function that adaptively balances purity (likelihood of being in-distribution) and informativeness (potential to improve the model) for each unlabeled example. MQ-Net will be parameterized as a monotonic multi-layer perceptron (MLP) with non-negative weights to enforce a skyline constraint, ensuring that examples with higher purity and informativeness receive higher meta-scores. The meta-model will be trained in a supervised manner using a self-validation set generated from each active learning round's query set, leveraging ground-truth labels obtained from the oracle. The training objective will include a ranking loss to align meta-scores with masked loss values (which ignore OOD examples) and a skyline regularization term to enforce clear dominance relationships. Purity and informativeness scores will be computed using state-of-the-art OOD detection and active learning methods, normalized and converted to positive values for meta-model input. The overall procedure alternates between updating the target model and MQ-Net across active learning rounds.
11ba4fc174d7a571e9f8ea16b3c6e814fac44c14.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on benchmark datasets including CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and ImageNet, using both class-split and cross-dataset open-set noise setups. Each dataset will be divided into in-distribution (IN) and out-of-distribution (OOD) subsets, with noise ratios varying from 10% to 60%. MQ-Net will be compared against random selection, four standard active learning baselines (CONF, CORESET, LL, BADGE), and two recent open-set active learning methods (CCAL, SIMILAR). Purity and informativeness scores will be derived from methods such as CSI and LL, with ablation studies using alternative scoring combinations (e.g., ReAct, CONF). Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy over active learning rounds, robustness to varying OOD labeling costs, and the effect of different meta-inputs and regularization strategies. Each experiment will be repeated over multiple random splits, and results will be averaged. The labeling budget and costs will be set as per prior open-set AL literature, and all models will be trained from scratch without pre-training.
11ba4fc174d7a571e9f8ea16b3c6e814fac44c14.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first meta-learning framework that adaptively balances purity and informativeness in open-set active learning, resolving the previously unaddressed purity-informativeness dilemma. MQ-Net leverages a self-validation set generated from the active learning process, eliminating the need for a separate clean validation set. The method incorporates a novel skyline constraint in the meta-model architecture to guarantee monotonicity and effective prioritization of examples. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent and significant improvements in test accuracy (up to 20.14% over state-of-the-art methods) across multiple datasets and noise levels. The framework is shown to generalize across different scoring functions and is robust to varying OOD labeling costs.

11c659af49165e641f98ac35e21bd1ca2da29b20.title: PF2ES: Parallel Feasible Pareto Frontier Entropy Search for Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization Under Unknown Constraints
11c659af49165e641f98ac35e21bd1ca2da29b20.research_question: How can multi-objective Bayesian optimization be made more efficient and accurate, particularly for problems with unknown constraints and the need for batch (parallel) query, by improving the acquisition function to better characterize the mutual information between candidate evaluations and the feasible Pareto frontier?
11c659af49165e641f98ac35e21bd1ca2da29b20.hypothesis: A variational lower bound approach to estimating the mutual information between candidate evaluations and the feasible Pareto frontier will yield a computationally efficient and accurate acquisition function for multi-objective Bayesian optimization, outperforming existing information-theoretic methods in both sequential and batch settings, especially when handling unknown constraints.
11c659af49165e641f98ac35e21bd1ca2da29b20.proposed_method: A novel information-theoretic acquisition function, Parallel Feasible Pareto Frontier Entropy Search ({PF}2ES), will be developed for multi-objective Bayesian optimization with support for unknown constraints and batch (parallel) query. The method will use a variational lower bound to directly approximate the mutual information between batches of candidate evaluations and the feasible Pareto frontier, leveraging a variational approximation of the conditional distribution of observations given the Pareto frontier. The output space will be partitioned using a hypervolume-based decomposition, and the acquisition function will be evaluated using Monte Carlo samples of the Pareto frontier generated from Gaussian process (GP) surrogate models. For batch optimization, a parallelization strategy will be implemented by extending the mutual information calculation to batches, using a sample average approximation and a differentiable relaxation to enable efficient optimization.
11c659af49165e641f98ac35e21bd1ca2da29b20.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of synthetic benchmarks and real-world design problems, including both unconstrained and constrained multi-objective optimization tasks. Datasets will include standard test functions (e.g., DTLZ, Four Bar Truss, Disc Brake Design) with varying input and output dimensionalities. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art acquisition functions such as EHVI, PFES, MESMO, PESMO, MESMOC+, PPESMOC, and random search. Both sequential and batch (parallel) optimization scenarios will be evaluated. Evaluation metrics will primarily focus on the log-hypervolume difference and uncertainty calibration of the inferred Pareto frontier, with performance assessed over multiple independent runs. GP surrogate models with Matérn 5/2 kernels will be used, and acquisition functions will be optimized using multi-start L-BFGS-B. Batch sizes, initial design, and other experimental parameters will be systematically varied to assess robustness.
11c659af49165e641f98ac35e21bd1ca2da29b20.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new acquisition function for multi-objective Bayesian optimization that efficiently and accurately estimates mutual information using a variational lower bound, overcoming the limitations of existing methods that rely on crude approximations or expensive inference. The approach supports both unknown constraints and batch query, and provides theoretical links to the multi-objective probability of improvement (MOPI) acquisition function. A new taxonomy for comparing output-space information-theoretic acquisition functions is established, and a practical parallelization strategy for batch optimization is developed. The method is claimed to achieve competitive or superior empirical performance across a range of synthetic and real-world problems, without requiring a reference point configuration as in EHVI, and demonstrates robust uncertainty calibration of the Pareto frontier.

1206b05eae5a06ba662ae79fb291b50e359c4f42.title: Stable Video Diffusion: Scaling Latent Video Diffusion Models to Large Datasets
1206b05eae5a06ba662ae79fb291b50e359c4f42.research_question: How can latent video diffusion models be effectively scaled to large datasets to achieve state-of-the-art performance in text-to-video and image-to-video generation, and what is the impact of systematic data curation and multi-stage training strategies on the quality and versatility of generative video models?
1206b05eae5a06ba662ae79fb291b50e359c4f42.hypothesis: Pretraining latent video diffusion models on large, systematically curated video datasets, followed by high-quality finetuning, will significantly improve the quality, motion consistency, and versatility of generated videos compared to models trained on uncurated or less systematically processed data. Furthermore, such models will provide strong motion and 3D priors, enabling superior performance on downstream tasks such as multi-view synthesis and camera motion control.
1206b05eae5a06ba662ae79fb291b50e359c4f42.proposed_method: A comprehensive three-stage training pipeline is developed for latent video diffusion models. The first stage involves initializing the model with a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model to provide robust visual representations. The second stage consists of large-scale video pretraining using a systematically curated dataset, where data processing includes cut detection, optical flow analysis for motion filtering, optical character recognition to remove text-heavy clips, and aesthetic scoring using CLIP embeddings. Captioning is performed using a combination of image and video captioners, with further summarization via LLMs. The third stage involves high-resolution finetuning on a smaller, high-quality video dataset to optimize the model for downstream tasks. Technical innovations include micro-conditioning on frame rate, adoption of the EDM noise schedule with higher noise values for high-res finetuning, and the use of LoRA modules for camera motion control.
1206b05eae5a06ba662ae79fb291b50e359c4f42.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using a curated video dataset (LVD-F) comprising up to 152 million annotated video clips, with additional high-quality finetuning on a 250K-sample dataset. Baselines include models trained on uncurated datasets, as well as established datasets such as WebVid-10M and InternVid-10M. Evaluation metrics include human preference studies, FVD (Fréchet Video Distance), LPIPS, PSNR, and CLIP-Similarity scores. The model is benchmarked on tasks such as zero-shot text-to-video generation (UCF-101), image-to-video generation, frame interpolation, and multi-view synthesis, with comparisons against state-of-the-art models like GEN-2, PikaLabs, Zero123XL, and SyncDreamer. Ablation studies assess the impact of each training stage and data curation strategy. Large-scale training is performed on high-performance GPUs, with batch sizes and training steps optimized for each stage.
1206b05eae5a06ba662ae79fb291b50e359c4f42.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a systematic, scalable data curation workflow for generative video modeling, enabling the transformation of massive, noisy video collections into high-quality training datasets. A unified three-stage training strategy is established, separating image pretraining, video pretraining, and high-quality finetuning, and its impact is empirically validated. The resulting models achieve state-of-the-art results in text-to-video and image-to-video generation, outperforming prior models in both human and quantitative evaluations. The approach further demonstrates that pretrained video diffusion models serve as strong motion and 3D priors, facilitating advanced applications such as multi-view synthesis and camera motion control with minimal additional training. The method achieves these advances with significantly reduced computational requirements compared to existing approaches.

12074bba0ac7a5683228718c0a61e1b0976920c1.title: Rethinking Residual Distribution in Locate-then-Edit Model Editing
12074bba0ac7a5683228718c0a61e1b0976920c1.research_question: How can the precision and effectiveness of model editing in large language models be improved, particularly in locate-then-edit frameworks, while minimizing negative side effects such as loss of general capabilities and representation shifts?
12074bba0ac7a5683228718c0a61e1b0976920c1.hypothesis: Directly updating only the first and last critical layers of a large language model, without distributing residuals across all critical layers, will reduce weight shift errors, improve editing efficacy, and better preserve the model's general capabilities compared to traditional residual distribution approaches in locate-then-edit model editing.
12074bba0ac7a5683228718c0a61e1b0976920c1.proposed_method: A new strategy, Boundary Layer UpdatE (BLUE), will be developed to enhance locate-then-edit model editing methods. Instead of distributing residuals evenly across all identified critical layers, BLUE will compute and apply residual updates only to the first and last critical layers. The method involves using causal tracing to identify critical layers, directly optimizing residuals for these boundary layers using least-squares solutions, and updating their weights accordingly. This approach is designed to minimize information loss and weight shift errors that arise from residual distribution, while maintaining the efficiency and applicability of multi-layer locate-then-edit frameworks. BLUE will be integrated with existing locate-then-edit methods such as MEMIT, RECT, PRUNE, and AlphaEdit to assess its generalizability and effectiveness.
12074bba0ac7a5683228718c0a61e1b0976920c1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three large language models: Llama3-8B-Instruct, GPT-J (6B), and GPT2-XL. Two datasets, CounterFact and zsRE, will be used for evaluation. The experimental setup will include sequential batch editing tasks, where 2,000 samples are edited in batches of 100, and long-form editing scenarios using the UnKEBench benchmark. Baselines will consist of state-of-the-art locate-then-edit methods (MEMIT, PRUNE, RECT, AlphaEdit) both with and without the BLUE enhancement. Evaluation metrics will include efficacy, generalization, specificity, fluency, and consistency, as well as downstream task performance on GLUE benchmark tasks to assess general capability retention. Additional analyses will measure hidden state shifts using t-SNE visualizations and ablation studies will determine the optimality of updating only the boundary layers.
12074bba0ac7a5683228718c0a61e1b0976920c1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel boundary-layer update strategy that discards residual distribution in favor of direct residual computation at only the first and last critical layers. This method is claimed to significantly reduce weight shift errors, improve editing efficacy, and better preserve the general capabilities of large language models after editing. Empirical and theoretical analyses support the claim that BLUE outperforms existing locate-then-edit methods across multiple models, datasets, and editing scenarios, including long-form and sequential batch editing. The strategy also demonstrates improved efficiency and mitigates representation shifts in post-edit models.

1208eb150c819b281e5afbfd8d6b2db4ea0d6a47.title: CQ-DINO: Mitigating Gradient Dilution via Category Queries for Vast Vocabulary Object Detection
1208eb150c819b281e5afbfd8d6b2db4ea0d6a47.research_question: How can object detection systems be made scalable and effective for vast vocabulary scenarios, where the number of object categories is extremely large, while addressing the optimization and efficiency challenges inherent to such settings?
1208eb150c819b281e5afbfd8d6b2db4ea0d6a47.hypothesis: Reformulating object classification as a contrastive task between object queries and learnable category queries, combined with dynamic image-guided query selection and explicit modeling of category relationships, will mitigate gradient dilution issues and enable efficient, scalable, and accurate object detection in vast vocabulary settings.
1208eb150c819b281e5afbfd8d6b2db4ea0d6a47.proposed_method: A novel object detection framework will be developed that encodes each category as a learnable query embedding, initialized using a large-scale text encoder (e.g., CLIP). An image-guided query selection module will be designed to dynamically select the top-K most relevant category queries for each image using cross-attention between image features and category queries, thereby reducing the negative search space and rebalancing gradient distributions. The selected category queries will interact with image features via a feature enhancer and a cross-modality decoder to generate object queries, which are then used for bounding box prediction and contrastive classification. For datasets with explicit category hierarchies, a hierarchical tree construction strategy will be implemented to encode semantic relationships, while for datasets without such structure, a self-attention mechanism will be used to learn implicit correlations among categories. The overall training objective will combine asymmetric classification loss, contrastive loss, bounding box regression, and generalized IoU loss, with a two-stage training paradigm for stability and efficiency.
1208eb150c819b281e5afbfd8d6b2db4ea0d6a47.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the V3Det dataset (13,204 categories, 183k training and 30k validation images) as the primary benchmark for vast vocabulary detection, and on COCO val2017 (80 categories, 118k training and 5k validation images) for standard detection scenarios. Multiple Swin Transformer backbones (Swin-B, Swin-B-22k, Swin-L) will be used, with category queries initialized from CLIP-ViT-L text embeddings. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art classification-head-based, text-prompted, and generative detection methods such as DINO, Prova, and GenerateU. Evaluation metrics will include average precision (AP), AP at different IoU thresholds, and category-level average recall with selected queries (ARC). Ablation studies will assess the impact of image-guided query selection, hierarchical tree construction, self-attention, and adaptive weighting strategies. Scalability and memory efficiency will be measured by per-category parameter count, GPU memory usage, and maximum supported category capacity.
1208eb150c819b281e5afbfd8d6b2db4ea0d6a47.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first systematic theoretical analysis of gradient dilution in vast vocabulary object detection and addresses it by dynamically selecting a sparse, image-relevant subset of category queries, which rebalances gradients and enables adaptive hard negative mining. The framework flexibly models category correlations via explicit hierarchical tree construction or implicit self-attention, depending on dataset structure. The image-guided query selection mechanism significantly reduces computational complexity and memory usage, enabling scalability to over 100,000 categories. The method achieves superior performance over state-of-the-art baselines on vast vocabulary benchmarks, demonstrating both effectiveness and practical scalability.

122a7e217fe70d5a1a44a6e2b67e859d1fc8e28d.title: On Memorization in Diffusion Models
122a7e217fe70d5a1a44a6e2b67e859d1fc8e28d.research_question: What are the conditions and influential factors that govern memorization behaviors in diffusion models, and how do data distribution, model configuration, and training procedures affect the tendency of diffusion models to memorize training data instead of generalizing?
122a7e217fe70d5a1a44a6e2b67e859d1fc8e28d.hypothesis: Diffusion models are more likely to exhibit memorization behaviors when trained on smaller datasets, and the extent of memorization is significantly influenced by factors such as data diversity, model architecture, training procedure, and conditioning information. Conditioning on uninformative random labels can also trigger memorization.
122a7e217fe70d5a1a44a6e2b67e859d1fc8e28d.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical framework will be established to systematically investigate memorization in diffusion models. The approach will introduce and utilize a new metric, effective model memorization (EMM), which quantifies the maximum training dataset size at which a diffusion model closely replicates its training data, approximating the theoretical optimum. The study will involve training state-of-the-art diffusion models (such as EDM and Stable Diffusion) under varying conditions, including different dataset sizes, data dimensionalities, class diversities, model widths and depths, time embedding strategies, and skip connection configurations. The impact of training hyperparameters (e.g., batch size, weight decay, EMA rate) and conditioning mechanisms (e.g., class labels, random labels, unique labels, text prompts) will also be systematically explored. For each configuration, the memorization ratio will be measured using a nearest-neighbor-based criterion, and EMM will be estimated via interpolation across dataset sizes.
122a7e217fe70d5a1a44a6e2b67e859d1fc8e28d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted primarily on the CIFAR-10 dataset, with additional studies on FFHQ and Imagenette for broader validation. Diffusion models will be trained with varying dataset sizes (ranging from 1k to 50k samples), image resolutions (8x8, 16x16, 32x32), and class diversities. Model architecture variations will include changes in width, depth, time embedding (positional vs. Fourier), and skip connection design. Training procedures will be varied in terms of batch size, weight decay, and EMA rates, following standard recipes and scaling rules. Both unconditional and conditional (class and text) generation settings will be evaluated, including scenarios with true, random, and unique labels. Baselines will include unconditional models and models with standard configurations. Evaluation metrics will include the memorization ratio (based on nearest neighbor ℓ2 distance thresholds), Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for image quality, and alternative memorization metrics for robustness. Fine-tuning experiments will be performed on Stable Diffusion using full and LoRA-based approaches on Imagenette, with both plain and class-based text prompts.
122a7e217fe70d5a1a44a6e2b67e859d1fc8e28d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the effective model memorization (EMM) metric as a principled way to quantify memorization in diffusion models and systematically analyzes the impact of data, model, and training factors on memorization. It provides the first comprehensive empirical study that reveals how conditioning on random or unique labels can dramatically increase memorization, even in large state-of-the-art diffusion models. The findings are expected to offer practical guidance for diffusion model users and inform theoretical research on privacy, generalization, and memorization in deep generative models.

123acfbccca0460171b6b06a4012dbb991cde55b.title: Large Language Models Are Zero-Shot Time Series Forecasters
123acfbccca0460171b6b06a4012dbb991cde55b.research_question: Can large language models (LLMs), when provided with appropriately tokenized numerical sequences, serve as effective zero-shot forecasters for time series data across a variety of domains and data characteristics?
123acfbccca0460171b6b06a4012dbb991cde55b.hypothesis: Large language models, when time series data are encoded as strings of numerical digits and appropriate tokenization and rescaling procedures are applied, can perform zero-shot time series forecasting at a level comparable to or exceeding traditional and deep learning-based time series models, without any fine-tuning on the target data.
123acfbccca0460171b6b06a4012dbb991cde55b.proposed_method: The proposed methodology frames time series forecasting as a next-token prediction problem in text by encoding numerical time series values as strings of digits. Careful tokenization strategies are developed to ensure that each digit is treated as a separate token, with spaces and commas used to separate digits and timesteps, respectively. Rescaling procedures are applied to normalize values and optimize token efficiency, tuning scaling parameters on validation log-likelihoods. For forecasting, multiple samples are drawn from the LLM using temperature scaling and nucleus sampling, with point estimates and probabilistic forecasts derived from the sample statistics. To bridge the gap between the discrete output space of LLMs and the continuous nature of time series, a method is introduced to convert discrete token distributions into flexible continuous densities by treating each sequence of digits as a bin and placing a uniform distribution within each bin. This enables the use of LLMs for high-resolution, multimodal, and heavy-tailed probabilistic forecasting.
123acfbccca0460171b6b06a4012dbb991cde55b.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on several benchmark time series datasets, including Darts (8 real univariate datasets), Monash (30 public datasets, with a subset used for computational feasibility), and Informer (multivariate datasets). The proposed method is evaluated in a zero-shot setting using pretrained LLMs such as GPT-3 and LLaMA-2 (70B parameters), without any fine-tuning on the target datasets. Baselines include classical statistical models (ARIMA, ETS), neural network models (TCN, N-BEATS, N-HiTS, DeepAR, WaveNet), and competing LLM-based methods (PromptCast). Evaluation metrics comprise deterministic measures (MAE) and probabilistic metrics (log-likelihood, CRPS), with additional analysis on sample efficiency and robustness to missing data. Hyperparameters for tokenization, rescaling, and sampling are tuned on validation data, and experiments address potential data leakage concerns. The method is also tested for its ability to handle missing values natively and to incorporate textual side information.
123acfbccca0460171b6b06a4012dbb991cde55b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel zero-shot framework for time series forecasting that leverages pretrained LLMs without any downstream fine-tuning, relying solely on encoding numerical data as text and careful tokenization. It claims the ability to outperform or match dedicated time series models on standard benchmarks, to naturally handle missing data and incorporate textual side information, and to provide flexible, well-calibrated probabilistic forecasts. The approach uniquely bridges the gap between language modeling and time series forecasting, demonstrating that LLMs' inherent biases and generative capabilities align well with the structure of time series data. Additionally, the method highlights the impact of model alignment and tokenization choices on forecasting performance, and provides a scalable path for leveraging advances in LLMs for time series tasks.

1243e13254bb4ea1f71b4be8a3e4e54ffd02d2fe.title: Scaling Autoregressive Models for Content-Rich Text-to-Image Generation
1243e13254bb4ea1f71b4be8a3e4e54ffd02d2fe.research_question: How can autoregressive models be effectively scaled to generate high-fidelity, content-rich images from complex and detailed text descriptions across diverse domains?
1243e13254bb4ea1f71b4be8a3e4e54ffd02d2fe.hypothesis: Scaling autoregressive sequence-to-sequence models with advanced image tokenization and large parameter counts will significantly improve the fidelity, compositionality, and alignment of generated images with complex text prompts, outperforming existing benchmarks.
1243e13254bb4ea1f71b4be8a3e4e54ffd02d2fe.proposed_method: A two-stage text-to-image generation framework will be developed. First, a Transformer-based image tokenizer (ViT-VQGAN) will encode images into sequences of discrete visual tokens, leveraging techniques such as l2-normalization codes and factorized codes for improved codebook utilization and reconstruction quality. Second, a large-scale encoder-decoder Transformer will be trained to map text token sequences to image token sequences, treating the task as a sequence-to-sequence modeling problem. The model will be scaled up to 20 billion parameters, with architectural choices such as conv-shaped masked sparse attention, large decoder depth, and pretraining of the text encoder on large corpora. Additional techniques, including classifier-free guidance for improved conditional generation and contrastive reranking for enhanced image-text alignment, will be incorporated. A super-resolution module will be used to upsample generated images to higher resolutions.
1243e13254bb4ea1f71b4be8a3e4e54ffd02d2fe.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a combination of large-scale image-text datasets, including LAION-400M, FIT400M, and JFT-4B, for model training. Evaluation will be performed on MS-COCO (2014), Localized Narratives (COCO subset), and the newly introduced PartiPrompts (P2) benchmark, which contains over 1600 diverse English prompts spanning 12 categories and 11 challenge dimensions. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art models such as DALL-E, CogView, and diffusion-based approaches. Evaluation metrics will include zero-shot and finetuned Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) scores, as well as human evaluations for image-text alignment and compositionality. The experimental setup will utilize distributed training on TPU clusters with advanced parallelism strategies to enable efficient scaling.
1243e13254bb4ea1f71b4be8a3e4e54ffd02d2fe.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a highly scalable autoregressive text-to-image generation model that achieves state-of-the-art FID scores on both MS-COCO and Localized Narratives. The method demonstrates that scaling model size and improving image tokenization directly enhance image fidelity and compositionality. The introduction of the PartiPrompts (P2) benchmark provides a comprehensive and challenging evaluation suite for open-domain text-to-image generation. Additional innovations include the use of classifier-free guidance and contrastive reranking in the autoregressive setting, as well as detailed analyses of model limitations and error types.

1244fd52eb23246dbef2ef6c6bf58dbf361550cf.title: Building Efficient Universal Classifiers with Natural Language Inference
1244fd52eb23246dbef2ef6c6bf58dbf361550cf.research_question: How can efficient and universal text classifiers be built that generalize to a wide range of classification tasks, while requiring fewer computational resources than generative large language models?
1244fd52eb23246dbef2ef6c6bf58dbf361550cf.hypothesis: Universal text classifiers based on Natural Language Inference (NLI), when trained on a mixture of NLI and diverse non-NLI classification datasets reformulated as NLI tasks, will achieve improved zero-shot and few-shot classification performance across a broad range of tasks compared to NLI-only models, while being significantly more efficient than generative LLMs.
1244fd52eb23246dbef2ef6c6bf58dbf361550cf.proposed_method: A universal text classification framework will be developed by leveraging the Natural Language Inference (NLI) task as a generalizable formulation for any text classification problem. The approach involves harmonizing and preprocessing multiple datasets, including five large-scale NLI datasets and 28 diverse non-NLI classification datasets (covering topics such as sentiment, emotion, intent, toxicity, and more), by verbalizing class labels as hypotheses and converting all data into a binary entailment vs. not-entailment format. The method includes automated data cleaning using CleanLab to remove noisy labels, downsampling to balance classes and avoid overfitting, and careful hypothesis formulation in simple language. The resulting combined dataset will be used to fine-tune encoder-only transformer models (e.g., DeBERTaV3) for the binary NLI task, enabling the model to generalize to unseen tasks via zero-shot classification. The pipeline will be implemented with reusable Jupyter notebooks and designed for compatibility with the Hugging Face ZeroShotClassificationPipeline.
1244fd52eb23246dbef2ef6c6bf58dbf361550cf.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by training three types of models: (1) a universal classifier trained on all NLI and non-NLI datasets (deberta-v3-zeroshot-v1.1-all-33), (2) a baseline model trained only on NLI datasets, and (3) 28 models each trained on all datasets except one held-out non-NLI dataset to evaluate zero-shot generalization. The training data will consist of approximately 900,000 hypothesis-premise pairs, with a maximum of 500 examples per class and 5,000 per dataset for non-NLI data. Evaluation will use balanced accuracy as the primary metric due to class imbalance, and performance will be assessed both on tasks seen during training and on held-out tasks. All models will be trained and evaluated on a single A100 40GB GPU, and inference will be benchmarked for efficiency. Detailed metrics and model cards will be provided for reproducibility.
1244fd52eb23246dbef2ef6c6bf58dbf361550cf.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a practical and efficient universal classifier framework that combines NLI with a diverse set of non-NLI tasks reformulated as NLI, improving zero-shot performance by 9.4% over NLI-only models. It provides a step-by-step, reproducible pipeline with reusable code and harmonized datasets, enabling users to build, adapt, and fine-tune universal classifiers for their own domains. The approach demonstrates that encoder-only models, when trained with a mixture of NLI and diverse classification data, can achieve competitive performance with much lower computational requirements than generative LLMs. The methodology also highlights the importance of data diversity, label verbalization, and automated cleaning for robust generalization, and sets the stage for future foundation models tailored to universal classification.

124d4d374fbef2016fa9880489871a58a7450644.title: Improved Baselines with Visual Instruction Tuning
124d4d374fbef2016fa9880489871a58a7450644.research_question: What are the most effective and data-efficient design choices for training large multimodal models (LMMs) to achieve state-of-the-art performance across a broad range of visual instruction-following and academic visual question answering tasks, and how can these models be scaled to higher resolutions and improved for compositionality and reduced hallucination?
124d4d374fbef2016fa9880489871a58a7450644.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that (1) a simple architectural modification—replacing the linear vision-language connector in LMMs with a multi-layer perceptron (MLP)—combined with targeted response-format prompting and the inclusion of academic-task-oriented VQA data, will significantly improve model performance and data efficiency across diverse benchmarks; (2) scaling input image resolution via a grid-based encoding approach will further enhance detailed perception and reduce hallucination without requiring large-scale retraining.
124d4d374fbef2016fa9880489871a58a7450644.proposed_method: A new approach will be developed that systematically investigates the impact of architectural, data, and prompt design choices for LMMs within a controlled framework. The method will replace the standard linear vision-language connector with a two-layer MLP to enhance cross-modal representation power. Response-format prompting will be introduced, appending explicit instructions to VQA-type questions to regularize output formats and balance short- and long-form answers. The training data will be augmented with academic-task-oriented VQA, OCR, and region-level datasets, using only publicly available sources.
