For scaling to higher image resolutions, a grid-based encoding strategy will be implemented: input images will be divided into patches matching the vision encoder's native resolution, encoded independently, and merged into a single feature map, with global context features concatenated to mitigate split artifacts. The approach will also explore data efficiency via sub-sampling and compositional generalization by mixing tasks of varying complexity.
124d4d374fbef2016fa9880489871a58a7450644.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a comprehensive suite of 12 benchmarks, including both academic-task-oriented datasets (VQAv2, GQA, VizWiz, ScienceQA, TextVQA) and instruction-following LMM benchmarks (POPE, MME, MMBench, MMBench-CN, SEED-Bench, LLaVA-Bench-in-the-Wild, MM-Vet). Baselines will include leading models such as BLIP-2, InstructBLIP, Shikra, IDEFICS, and Qwen-VL, with both 7B and 13B parameter LLM backbones. Evaluation metrics will cover accuracy, F1, and GPT-4-based response quality scoring, with additional analysis on hallucination rates, compositionality, and multilingual generalization. Ablation studies will examine the effects of connector type, data mixture, prompt format, LLM backbone, and data sub-sampling ratios. Training will be performed using only publicly available data, with compute tracked (e.g., single 8xA100 node, ~1 day for full training).
124d4d374fbef2016fa9880489871a58a7450644.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first systematic, controlled study of LMM design choices under a unified framework, demonstrating that a simple MLP connector and response-format prompting can yield state-of-the-art results with orders-of-magnitude less data and compute than prior art. The approach establishes new, fully reproducible baselines that are more accessible to the community. Additional innovations include a scalable grid-based high-resolution encoding method that does not require retraining the vision encoder, empirical findings on data efficiency (showing strong performance even with 50% data), and new insights into compositional generalization and hallucination mitigation in LMMs.

1262758538525835d918007d15726794e19a07b7.title: Squeeze, Recover and Relabel: Dataset Condensation at ImageNet Scale From A New Perspective
1262758538525835d918007d15726794e19a07b7.research_question: How can large-scale image datasets be efficiently condensed into compact synthetic datasets that retain essential information for high-performance model training, while reducing computational and memory requirements, and supporting arbitrary image resolutions and model architectures?
1262758538525835d918007d15726794e19a07b7.hypothesis: Decoupling the optimization of model training and synthetic data generation through a multi-stage process—comprising information extraction, data recovery, and relabeling—enables scalable, efficient, and effective dataset condensation at large scales, outperforming bilevel optimization approaches in both accuracy and resource efficiency.
1262758538525835d918007d15726794e19a07b7.proposed_method: A novel three-stage dataset condensation framework is proposed, consisting of Squeeze, Recover, and Relabel stages. In the Squeeze stage, a deep neural network is trained from scratch on the original dataset to encapsulate critical information, with careful consideration of training strategies and data augmentation. The Recover stage synthesizes condensed images from Gaussian noise by aligning the batch normalization (BN) statistics of the pre-trained model with those of the synthetic data, using regularization terms and multi-crop optimization to enhance semantic content. The Relabel stage assigns soft labels to the synthetic data using the pre-trained model, ensuring label-data alignment, particularly through temperature-scaled softmax outputs. This decoupled approach eliminates the need for simultaneous real and synthetic data in memory, significantly reducing computational and memory costs, and is compatible with a wide range of model architectures, including ConvNets and ViTs.
1262758538525835d918007d15726794e19a07b7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale datasets, specifically Tiny-ImageNet and full-resolution ImageNet-1K, using various backbone architectures such as ResNet-18, ResNet-50, ResNet-101, ViT-Tiny, and a BN-modified ViT. The quality of the condensed datasets will be evaluated by training models from scratch on the synthetic data and measuring top-1 validation accuracy on real validation sets. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art dataset condensation methods such as MTT, TESLA, and DM, with metrics including accuracy, synthesis time per image, and peak GPU memory usage. Ablation studies will analyze the effects of squeezing budget, data augmentation, recovery budget, regularization terms, multi-crop optimization, relabeling strategies, and temperature settings. Cross-architecture generalization and continual learning scenarios will also be evaluated to assess robustness and applicability.
1262758538525835d918007d15726794e19a07b7.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to enable condensation of the full ImageNet-1K dataset at standard resolution (224×224) using widely available GPUs, while achieving state-of-the-art accuracy under strict image-per-class constraints. The decoupling of model training and synthetic data optimization introduces a scalable, resource-efficient alternative to bilevel optimization, supporting arbitrary image resolutions and network architectures. The use of BN-statistics alignment for data recovery and multi-crop optimization for enhanced semantic content are innovative contributions. Comprehensive ablation and generalization studies provide new insights into the design of large-scale dataset condensation methods.

126a4776ff8315fd506766cb8f3c722cf746ad9e.title: Teaching Small Language Models to Reason
126a4776ff8315fd506766cb8f3c722cf746ad9e.research_question: Can the reasoning capabilities of large language models be effectively transferred to smaller language models through fine-tuning, and what are the trade-offs between model size, dataset size, and task performance across arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning tasks?
126a4776ff8315fd506766cb8f3c722cf746ad9e.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that fine-tuning smaller language models on chain-of-thought (CoT) outputs generated by large language models will significantly improve their reasoning abilities across various tasks, and that the effectiveness of this transfer will depend on both the size of the student model and the amount of CoT-annotated data used.
126a4776ff8315fd506766cb8f3c722cf746ad9e.proposed_method: A two-step knowledge distillation pipeline will be developed to transfer reasoning capabilities from large language models (LLMs) to smaller models. First, existing supervised datasets will be annotated with chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning generated by LLMs such as PaLM 540B and GPT-3 175B, using few-shot prompting with 8 exemplars and providing the target answer in the prompt to guide the generation. Incorrect CoT examples will be filtered out based on the target answer to ensure data quality. In the second step, student models of various sizes (e.g., T5 base, XL, XXL) will be fine-tuned using teacher forcing, where the input is the question and the target is the generated CoT and answer. This approach eliminates the need for CoT prompting at inference time and allows for systematic investigation of model and dataset size effects.
126a4776ff8315fd506766cb8f3c722cf746ad9e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of reasoning benchmarks, including arithmetic (GSM8K, MAWPS, ASDiv), commonsense (StrategyQA), and symbolic reasoning tasks (last letter concatenation, coinflip). For arithmetic datasets, official splits and 5-fold cross-validation will be used, with accuracy measured both directly and with an external calculator to correct arithmetic mistakes. For commonsense and symbolic tasks, custom train/validation/test splits will be created to ensure reproducibility and to test generalization to out-of-distribution examples. Baselines will include student models fine-tuned on original targets and on golden CoT annotations, with comparisons to few-shot performance of teacher LLMs. Evaluation metrics will focus on task accuracy, and ablation studies will assess the impact of providing the target in CoT generation, model size, and dataset size.
126a4776ff8315fd506766cb8f3c722cf746ad9e.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces an extensive and systematic exploration of CoT knowledge distillation from LLMs to smaller language models across multiple architectures and reasoning domains. Key innovations include the adaptation of few-shot CoT prompting to provide the target answer for improved CoT quality, rigorous filtering of incorrect CoT examples, and comprehensive analysis of the effects of both student model size and dataset size on reasoning performance. The approach aims to demonstrate significant improvements in small model reasoning abilities, establish data efficiency gains, and provide practical recommendations for deploying reasoning-capable small language models.

127ebdb7b87fe5c8c8ff1bb9173584b75eec8f47.title: RankMe: Assessing the downstream performance of pretrained self-supervised representations by their rank
127ebdb7b87fe5c8c8ff1bb9173584b75eec8f47.research_question: How can the downstream performance of pretrained self-supervised representations be assessed without relying on labeled data, and can a simple, unsupervised criterion reliably predict the quality of learned representations across different datasets and tasks?
127ebdb7b87fe5c8c8ff1bb9173584b75eec8f47.hypothesis: A smooth, unsupervised measure of the effective rank of the embedding matrix, computed from the singular value distribution (RankMe), is sufficient to predict the downstream performance of joint-embedding self-supervised learning (JE-SSL) representations, even across different datasets and without access to labels.
127ebdb7b87fe5c8c8ff1bb9173584b75eec8f47.proposed_method: A new approach is developed that introduces RankMe, a numerically stable, hyperparameter-free, and unsupervised metric for evaluating the quality of JE-SSL representations. RankMe is defined as the exponential of the Shannon entropy of the normalized singular values of the embedding matrix, providing a smooth estimate of the effective rank. The method involves extracting embeddings from the encoder (optionally before the projector for methods like DINO), computing the singular value decomposition (SVD) of the embedding matrix using a large but fixed sample size (e.g., 25,600 samples), normalizing the singular values, and then calculating the entropy-based rank. RankMe is then used to compare different runs of a given JE-SSL method, select hyperparameters, and assess the likelihood of successful downstream performance without any access to labels or supervised validation.
127ebdb7b87fe5c8c8ff1bb9173584b75eec8f47.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using five representative JE-SSL methods: SimCLR (contrastive), VICReg (covariance-based), VICReg-exp, VICReg-ctr (variants), and DINO (clustering-based). Models are trained on ImageNet and iNaturalist18 using a ResNet-50 backbone and a large MLP projector, with variations in key hyperparameters such as temperature, loss weights, learning rate, and weight decay. Downstream evaluation is performed on multiple datasets, including ImageNet, iNaturalist18, Places205, EuroSat, SUN397, Stanford Cars, CIFAR10, CIFAR100, Food101, VOC07, and CLEVR-count. Both linear and non-linear probing (using MLP and k-NN classifiers) are used to assess the correlation between RankMe and downstream accuracy. Hyperparameter selection is performed using RankMe, and results are compared to supervised oracle selection and the α-ReQ baseline. Evaluation metrics include top-1 classification accuracy, AP50 for object detection, and average performance across out-of-distribution datasets.
127ebdb7b87fe5c8c8ff1bb9173584b75eec8f47.novelty_claims: The proposed method provides the first theoretically motivated, hyperparameter-free, and label-free criterion (RankMe) for assessing the quality of JE-SSL representations and selecting hyperparameters. RankMe enables reliable prediction of downstream performance on both in-domain and out-of-domain datasets without any access to labels, surpassing or matching supervised oracle selection and previous unsupervised baselines. The approach is computationally efficient, robust to architectural and method variations, and applicable to both linear and non-linear evaluation protocols, thus facilitating the deployment of self-supervised learning in domains where labeled data is scarce or unavailable.

12910786da7a34c9ee26798fd81b0ed7b0e38789.title: Finding Neurons in a Haystack: Case Studies with Sparse Probing
12910786da7a34c9ee26798fd81b0ed7b0e38789.research_question: How are high-level, human-interpretable features represented within the internal neuron activations of large language models, and how does the sparsity and localization of these representations vary with model scale and feature type?
12910786da7a34c9ee26798fd81b0ed7b0e38789.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that certain features are represented sparsely or even monosemantically in specific neurons, particularly in middle layers for high-level contextual features, while early layers exhibit superposition with polysemantic neurons. Additionally, as model scale increases, representational sparsity increases on average, but the dynamics differ by feature type.
12910786da7a34c9ee26798fd81b0ed7b0e38789.proposed_method: A k-sparse linear probing framework will be developed to systematically study the localization and sparsity of feature representations in transformer-based large language models (LLMs). The approach involves training linear classifiers (probes) constrained to use at most k neurons from a given layer to predict the presence of over 100 interpretable features spanning multiple categories. Both optimal sparse probing (OSP) using cutting-plane algorithms for small k and adaptive thresholding for larger k will be employed, with initial neuron selection based on mean activation differences. Probing datasets will be carefully constructed to maximize conceptual separation between features and minimize confounds, and both elementwise and aggregated activation statistics will be used depending on the feature granularity. The methodology will also include ablation studies to assess the functional role of identified neurons and further analyses to distinguish between superposition and compositionality.
12910786da7a34c9ee26798fd81b0ed7b0e38789.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the EleutherAI Pythia suite of autoregressive transformer language models, covering seven model sizes from 70 million to 6.9 billion parameters. Probing will be performed across ten feature collections, including linguistic, programming, factual, and structural properties, with over 100 binary classification tasks derived from these features. For each model, feature, layer, and probing method, probes will be trained for a range of k values and evaluated on held-out test sets using F1 score as the primary metric, along with precision, recall, and Matthews Correlation Coefficient. Baseline comparisons will include different sparse feature selection methods and random neuron selection. Additional analyses will include activation distribution studies, co-occurrence analysis for compositionality, and ablation experiments to measure the impact of neuron removal on language modeling loss.
12910786da7a34c9ee26798fd81b0ed7b0e38789.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a systematic, scalable sparse probing methodology capable of provably optimal neuron selection for small k, enabling precise localization of feature representations in LLMs. It addresses key shortcomings of prior probing work by disentangling ranking and classification quality, leveraging sparsity as an inductive bias for interpretability, and providing granular insight into both monosemantic and polysemantic neurons. The research will provide the first large-scale empirical evidence of superposition and monosemanticity in real LLMs, characterize how representational sparsity evolves with model scale, and offer new tools and analyses to refine and verify neuron-level interpretations.

129d9e9d51ff33dddf9118dd70bfca995899168b.title: Test-time Adaptation for Cross-modal Retrieval with Query Shift
129d9e9d51ff33dddf9118dd70bfca995899168b.research_question: How can robust cross-modal retrieval be achieved in the presence of query shift, where online queries originate from distributions different from the source domain?
129d9e9d51ff33dddf9118dd70bfca995899168b.hypothesis: Endowing test-time adaptation methods with mechanisms to explicitly manipulate modality uniformity and modality gap, along with noise-robust adaptation, will enable cross-modal retrieval models to maintain high performance under query shift conditions.
129d9e9d51ff33dddf9118dd70bfca995899168b.proposed_method: A novel test-time adaptation framework for cross-modal retrieval, termed Test-time adaptation for Cross-modal Retrieval (TCR), will be developed to address the query shift problem. The method will incorporate a query prediction refinement module that selects the most similar gallery samples for each query, forming query-candidate pairs and filtering out irrelevant gallery samples to stabilize adaptation. A joint objective function will be introduced, comprising three loss components: intra-modality uniformity learning (which contrasts queries with their centers to enhance discrimination), inter-modality gap learning (which rectifies the modality gap between query and gallery embeddings to match the source model's alignment), and a noise-robust adaptation loss (which uses a self-adaptive threshold to amplify high-confidence predictions and suppress noisy ones). Constraint estimation will be performed by adaptively selecting source-domain-like query-candidate pairs to guide the adaptation process.
129d9e9d51ff33dddf9118dd70bfca995899168b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on widely-used image-text retrieval benchmarks, including COCO, Flickr, Fashion-Gen, CUHK-PEDES, ICFG-PEDES, and Nocaps, under both Query Shift (QS) and Query-Gallery Shift (QGS) settings. The evaluation will involve introducing various types of corruptions and distribution shifts to the query and/or gallery modalities. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art test-time adaptation methods such as Tent, EATA, SAR, READ, and DeYO. Performance will be measured using Recall@1 for both image-to-text and text-to-image retrieval tasks. The adaptation will be performed online, updating only the normalization layers of pre-trained models (e.g., CLIP and BLIP) using the AdamW optimizer, with batch sizes and hyperparameters fixed across experiments. Ablation studies and analytic experiments will be conducted to assess the contribution of each component and the effects of intra-modality uniformity and inter-modality gap.
129d9e9d51ff33dddf9118dd70bfca995899168b.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces one of the first online adaptation methods specifically designed for cross-modal retrieval under query shift, addressing both intra-modality uniformity and inter-modality gap. The framework uniquely combines query prediction refinement, adaptive constraint estimation, and a joint objective with noise-robust adaptation, enabling robust performance without access to source data during adaptation. The approach is generalizable to various pre-trained models and demonstrates superior robustness and adaptability compared to existing test-time adaptation methods.

12abb16eabeb321c579c2bbdcb3e37f6bbf90262.title: SoftPatch: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection with Noisy Data
12abb16eabeb321c579c2bbdcb3e37f6bbf90262.research_question: How can unsupervised anomaly detection methods be made robust to noisy training data, particularly in image sensory anomaly detection tasks where label-level noise is present?
12abb16eabeb321c579c2bbdcb3e37f6bbf90262.hypothesis: Incorporating patch-level denoising and soft re-weighting strategies into the memory-based coreset construction process will significantly improve the robustness and accuracy of unsupervised anomaly detection methods in the presence of noisy training data.
12abb16eabeb321c579c2bbdcb3e37f6bbf90262.proposed_method: A novel unsupervised anomaly detection framework, SoftPatch, will be developed to address the challenge of noisy training data. The method operates at the patch level, employing noise discriminators to assign outlier scores to individual image patches based on their feature distributions. Three types of noise discriminators will be explored: nearest neighbor distance, multi-variate Gaussian modeling, and Local Outlier Factor (LOF), with LOF hypothesized to provide the best trade-off between robustness and capacity. Patches with the highest outlier scores (top τ%) will be removed before constructing the coreset memory bank, and the remaining patches' outlier scores will be stored as soft weights. During inference, anomaly scores for test samples will be computed using nearest neighbor search in the denoised, re-weighted memory bank, with soft weights modulating the final anomaly score to down-weight the influence of hard-to-remove noisy patches.
12abb16eabeb321c579c2bbdcb3e37f6bbf90262.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the MVTecAD and BTAD benchmarks, which are standard datasets for industrial image anomaly detection. To simulate realistic noisy conditions, anomalous samples will be injected into the training set at varying noise ratios, creating both 'Nooverlap' (injected anomalies not present in the test set) and 'Overlap' (injected anomalies also in the test set) scenarios. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art methods such as PatchCore, PaDiM, and CFLOW, with consistent backbone architectures (e.g., Wide-ResNet50) and coreset sampling ratios. Evaluation metrics will include image-level and pixel-level AUROC, with additional analysis of performance gaps between clean and noisy training conditions. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of different noise discriminators, soft weighting, and hyperparameter choices (LOF-k, threshold τ). All experiments will be repeated multiple times for statistical reliability.
12abb16eabeb321c579c2bbdcb3e37f6bbf90262.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to systematically address label-level noise in unsupervised image sensory anomaly detection. By introducing patch-level denoising and soft re-weighting in coreset construction, the method improves data utilization and model robustness compared to conventional sample-level denoising. The framework establishes a new baseline for unsupervised anomaly detection under noisy conditions and demonstrates superior robustness and accuracy over existing state-of-the-art methods, even in challenging noise scenarios. The approach also provides insights into the practical deployment of anomaly detection systems in real-world industrial settings, where noisy data is unavoidable.

12ad6e798487223f4c17aac69c9853bca8bc7830.title: Test-Time Prompt Tuning for Zero-Shot Generalization in Vision-Language Models
12ad6e798487223f4c17aac69c9853bca8bc7830.research_question: How can zero-shot generalization in vision-language models be improved without relying on hand-crafted or task-specific training data, particularly under natural distribution shifts, cross-dataset scenarios, and context-dependent visual reasoning tasks?
12ad6e798487223f4c17aac69c9853bca8bc7830.hypothesis: Adaptive prompt tuning at test time, using only the test sample and without any additional training data or annotations, can enhance the zero-shot generalization performance of vision-language models such as CLIP across a range of tasks and distribution shifts.
12ad6e798487223f4c17aac69c9853bca8bc7830.proposed_method: A novel test-time prompt tuning (TPT) framework is developed, which adaptively optimizes the text prompt for a vision-language model using only a single test sample. For image classification, multiple augmented views of the test image are generated, and the prompt is tuned by minimizing the marginal entropy of the model's predictions across these views, encouraging prediction consistency. A confidence selection mechanism is introduced to filter out augmented views with high prediction entropy, ensuring that only high-confidence predictions contribute to the prompt optimization. For context-dependent visual reasoning tasks (e.g., Bongard-HOI), both the prompt and class tokens are jointly optimized using the support images in each test sample, employing a cross-entropy loss to better differentiate between positive and negative contexts. The method operates entirely at test time, requiring no access to training data or annotations.
12ad6e798487223f4c17aac69c9853bca8bc7830.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on several benchmarks to evaluate robustness to natural distribution shifts (ImageNet-V2, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-Sketch), cross-dataset generalization (Flower102, OxfordPets, SUN397, DTD, Food101, StanfordCars, Aircraft, UCF101, EuroSAT, Caltech101), and context-dependent visual reasoning (Bongard-HOI). Baselines include zero-shot CLIP with hand-crafted prompts, prompt ensemble, and few-shot prompt tuning methods such as CoOp and CoCoOp. Evaluation metrics primarily involve top-1 classification accuracy. For TPT, prompts are initialized with a default template (e.g., 'a photo of a'), and optimized for one or more steps per test sample using AdamW. Data augmentations (random resized crops, AugMix) are applied, and confidence selection retains the top 10% most confident augmented views for entropy minimization. For Bongard-HOI, prompt and class tokens are optimized for 64 steps per test sample using support images.
12ad6e798487223f4c17aac69c9853bca8bc7830.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to perform prompt tuning on a single test sample in a zero-shot manner, without any training data or annotations. The introduction of confidence selection as a plug-and-play module for filtering noisy augmentations during entropy minimization is novel and shown to improve performance. The method demonstrates that test-time prompt tuning can match or surpass the performance of existing prompt tuning methods that require additional training data, across natural distribution shifts, cross-dataset generalization, and context-dependent visual reasoning tasks.

12cce6a8af34ff35286b92959f1cd49e38b600bf.title: The Memory Perturbation Equation: Understanding Model's Sensitivity to Data
12cce6a8af34ff35286b92959f1cd49e38b600bf.research_question: How can the sensitivity of machine learning models to perturbations in their training data be efficiently and accurately estimated, unified across a wide variety of models and algorithms, and utilized to predict generalization performance without costly retraining?
12cce6a8af34ff35286b92959f1cd49e38b600bf.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a unified, Bayesian-derived equation—leveraging natural gradients within the Bayesian learning rule framework—can generalize and improve upon existing sensitivity measures, enabling efficient, accurate, and interpretable estimation of model sensitivity to data perturbations during training, and that these sensitivity estimates can reliably predict generalization performance on unseen data.
12cce6a8af34ff35286b92959f1cd49e38b600bf.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed based on the Memory-Perturbation Equation (MPE), which is derived from Bayesian principles and the Bayesian learning rule (BLR). The MPE expresses the deviation in model parameters due to removal or perturbation of data examples as a sum of their natural gradients, allowing sensitivity estimation for a broad class of algorithms, including those using non-differentiable losses or discrete parameter spaces. The method will provide closed-form or efficiently computable approximations for sensitivity, applicable both at convergence and during training, and will generalize existing influence function approaches. Technical implementation will include adapting the MPE to various algorithms (e.g., SGD, Newton's method, RMSprop, Adam) by matching their update rules and preconditioners, and extending the approach to handle arbitrary perturbations, such as leave-one-out or leave-group-out scenarios. The framework will also analyze the causes of high sensitivity, linking them to prediction error and variance, and will enable efficient computation of cross-validation and generalization estimates using quantities already available during training.
12cce6a8af34ff35286b92959f1cd49e38b600bf.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification datasets such as MNIST, FMNIST, and CIFAR-10, using a range of neural network architectures including MLPs, LeNet, CNNs, and ResNet-20. The proposed sensitivity estimates will be empirically validated by comparing estimated deviations (from data removal or perturbation) to true deviations in model predictions, using both individual and grouped example removals. Baselines will include traditional influence functions, leave-one-out retraining, and ad-hoc sensitivity measures (e.g., TracIn, gradient norms, Hessian-based approximations). Evaluation metrics will focus on the correlation between estimated and true deviations, the accuracy of predicted generalization error (e.g., test negative log-likelihood, LOO-CV error), and computational efficiency. Additional experiments will assess the evolution of sensitivity during training and the utility of sensitivity estimates for hyperparameter tuning and class-level data removal.
12cce6a8af34ff35286b92959f1cd49e38b600bf.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the Memory-Perturbation Equation as a unifying and generalizing framework for sensitivity analysis in machine learning, subsuming and extending existing influence-based methods. It enables efficient, closed-form sensitivity estimation for a wide variety of models and algorithms, including those with non-differentiable losses or discrete parameters, and provides new theoretical insights into the causes of model sensitivity. The method allows for faithful prediction of generalization performance during training, eliminates the need for costly retraining or brute-force cross-validation, and offers practical tools for robust and adaptive learning. The framework also facilitates algorithm-specific sensitivity measures and highlights the importance of high-sensitivity examples in characterizing model memory.

1311944e1ac408fd4a7829b254f25a6560b66e07.title: Maximize to Explore: One Objective Function Fusing Estimation, Planning, and Exploration
1311944e1ac408fd4a7829b254f25a6560b66e07.research_question: Can a sample-efficient and easy-to-implement reinforcement learning (RL) framework be developed that effectively balances exploration and exploitation under general function approximation, and is applicable to both Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) and two-player zero-sum Markov games (MGs)?
1311944e1ac408fd4a7829b254f25a6560b66e07.hypothesis: A single-objective RL framework that fuses estimation and planning into an unconstrained maximization problem can automatically balance exploration and exploitation, achieve sublinear regret under general function approximation, and be efficiently implemented in both model-free and model-based RL settings.
1311944e1ac408fd4a7829b254f25a6560b66e07.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a reinforcement learning framework, Maximize to Explore (MEX), which optimizes a single unconstrained objective function combining the expected total return (planning) and the negative estimation error (estimation) of a hypothesis. The method operates episodically: in each episode, a hypothesis is selected by maximizing a weighted sum of the optimal expected return and the negative loss (estimation error), with the weight parameter η controlling the exploration-exploitation trade-off. For model-free RL, the loss is based on a generalized Bellman error; for model-based RL, it is the negative log-likelihood of the transition model. The selected hypothesis determines the policy for data collection and prediction, and the process iterates, updating the loss with new data. This framework is designed to be compatible with general function approximators, including deep neural networks, and avoids computationally expensive constrained optimization or sampling-based procedures.
1311944e1ac408fd4a7829b254f25a6560b66e07.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of MuJoCo environments with sparse rewards to evaluate the practical effectiveness of the MEX framework. Both model-free and model-based deep RL baselines, such as TD3 and MBPO, will be adapted to instantiate practical versions of MEX. Performance will be compared against standard baselines using metrics such as cumulative reward and sample efficiency. The experimental setup will include varying the complexity of the environments and the sparsity of rewards, and computational cost will be measured to demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed approach. Additional experiments may extend to tabular and partially observable settings, as well as two-player zero-sum Markov games.
1311944e1ac408fd4a7829b254f25a6560b66e07.novelty_claims: The proposed framework unifies estimation, planning, and exploration into a single unconstrained maximization objective, eliminating the need for data-dependent level-set optimization or complex sampling procedures. It provides theoretical guarantees of sublinear regret under general function approximation, which extends to both MDPs and two-player zero-sum MGs. The method is computationally efficient, compatible with modern deep RL techniques, and achieves similar or better sample efficiency compared to existing algorithms, while being easier to implement and less computationally intensive.

1318baab56565e6684fc864ec721f512dfcf8d83.title: Unimodal Bandits: Regret Lower Bounds and Optimal Algorithms
1318baab56565e6684fc864ec721f512dfcf8d83.research_question: How can the unimodal structure of expected rewards in stochastic multi-armed bandit problems be optimally exploited to minimize regret, particularly in both stationary and non-stationary environments, and how does this extend to continuous or very large discrete action spaces?
1318baab56565e6684fc864ec721f512dfcf8d83.hypothesis: Optimal exploitation of unimodal structure in multi-armed bandit problems enables algorithms to achieve regret bounds that do not depend on the total number of arms, and such algorithms can outperform existing methods in both stationary and smoothly varying non-stationary environments.
1318baab56565e6684fc864ec721f512dfcf8d83.proposed_method: A novel algorithm, OSUB (Optimal Sampling for Unimodal Bandits), will be developed to leverage the unimodal structure of expected rewards defined over a partially ordered set of arms (represented as a graph or a continuous interval). The method will use KL-divergence-based upper confidence bounds to define an index for each arm, but restricts exploration to the neighborhood of the current empirical leader, thus efficiently focusing sampling on promising regions. In non-stationary environments, a sliding window version (SW-OSUB) will be implemented, where decisions and statistics are computed over a recent window of observations to adapt to smoothly evolving reward distributions. For continuous or very large discrete arm sets, the approach will combine an adaptive discretization scheme with UCB-like algorithms, reducing the effective decision space to a manageable size while maintaining order-optimal regret.
1318baab56565e6684fc864ec721f512dfcf8d83.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic stationary and non-stationary environments, including discrete bandits with varying numbers of arms (e.g., 17, 129, up to 7500) and continuous-armed bandits with unimodal reward functions. Baselines will include KL-UCB, UCB, UCB-U (UCB restricted to leader neighborhoods), and LSE (Line Search Elimination). Evaluation metrics will focus on cumulative regret and regret per unit time, with performance averaged over multiple independent runs. For non-stationary settings, environments will be constructed where expected rewards evolve smoothly (e.g., moving triangles), and window sizes for sliding window algorithms will be tuned according to theoretical guidelines. The impact of the number of arms and the speed of non-stationarity on regret will be systematically analyzed.
1318baab56565e6684fc864ec721f512dfcf8d83.novelty_claims: The proposed approach provides the first regret lower bounds for unimodal bandits that are independent of the number of arms, and introduces an algorithm (OSUB) that matches these lower bounds asymptotically, achieving optimal performance. The method is shown to outperform existing algorithms such as LSE and classical UCB variants, especially in regimes where the number of arms is large or the environment is non-stationary. For continuous action spaces, the combination of discretization and UCB is demonstrated to be order-optimal and practically superior to previous methods. New concentration inequalities and regret analyses are developed for both stationary and non-stationary unimodal bandit settings.

131ba9932572c92155874db93626cf299659254e.title: FLatten Transformer: Vision Transformer using Focused Linear Attention
131ba9932572c92155874db93626cf299659254e.research_question: How can the computational efficiency of self-attention mechanisms in vision Transformers be improved without sacrificing their expressive power and performance across various vision tasks?
131ba9932572c92155874db93626cf299659254e.hypothesis: A novel linear attention mechanism that enhances focusability and feature diversity can achieve comparable or superior performance to Softmax-based self-attention in vision Transformers, while maintaining lower computational complexity.
131ba9932572c92155874db93626cf299659254e.proposed_method: A new Focused Linear Attention (FLatten) module will be developed to address the limitations of existing linear attention methods in vision Transformers. The approach involves two key innovations: (1) a focused mapping function that adjusts the feature direction of queries and keys, sharpening the attention distribution to better distinguish informative features and improve focusability; and (2) a rank restoration module that applies depthwise convolution to the attention matrix, thereby increasing its rank and enhancing feature diversity among output tokens. The module will be integrated into multiple stages of advanced vision Transformer architectures, replacing standard Softmax attention blocks, and will be designed to maintain linear computational complexity with respect to sequence length. The method will be implemented with simple, efficient operators to minimize additional overhead and will be compatible as a plug-in for a variety of Transformer models.
131ba9932572c92155874db93626cf299659254e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard benchmarks for image classification (ImageNet-1K), semantic segmentation (ADE20K), and object detection/instance segmentation (COCO). The proposed module will be integrated into several state-of-the-art vision Transformer backbones, including DeiT, PVT, PVT-v2, Swin Transformer, and CSwin Transformer. Baselines will include the original models with Softmax attention and several recent linear attention variants (e.g., Hydra Attention, Efficient Attention, Linear Angular Attention, Enhanced Linear Attention). Evaluation metrics will include Top-1 accuracy for classification, mean Intersection-over-Union (mIoU) and mean Accuracy (mAcc) for segmentation, and Average Precision (AP) for detection and segmentation. FLOPs, parameter count, and inference latency on both CPU and GPU will be measured to assess efficiency. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of the focused mapping function, depthwise convolution, receptive field size, and the stages at which the module is applied.
131ba9932572c92155874db93626cf299659254e.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple yet effective focused mapping function that sharpens attention distributions in linear attention, addressing the lack of focusability in prior approaches. It further innovates by restoring the rank of the attention matrix via depthwise convolution, overcoming the feature diversity limitations of existing linear attention modules. The resulting module achieves linear computational complexity while matching or surpassing the expressive power and performance of Softmax-based attention. The approach is broadly applicable as a plug-in to various vision Transformer architectures and demonstrates consistent improvements across multiple vision tasks and benchmarks, with superior efficiency and state-of-the-art results among linear attention methods.

13263ec6b83e59442aafe1b45b7554bbba57b680.title: Brax - A Differentiable Physics Engine for Large Scale Rigid Body Simulation
13263ec6b83e59442aafe1b45b7554bbba57b680.research_question: How can a differentiable, high-performance physics engine be designed to enable large-scale, efficient, and scalable rigid body simulation for reinforcement learning on modern accelerators, while supporting seamless integration with learning algorithms and providing open, extensible interfaces for environment creation and experimentation?
13263ec6b83e59442aafe1b45b7554bbba57b680.hypothesis: A differentiable, accelerator-optimized physics engine implemented with auto-vectorization, device-parallelism, and just-in-time compilation can dramatically accelerate reinforcement learning experiments, enable new classes of optimization techniques, and democratize access to high-fidelity physical simulation for control and robotics research.
13263ec6b83e59442aafe1b45b7554bbba57b680.proposed_method: A new open-source physics engine will be developed using JAX, focusing on maximal coordinate rigid body simulation with support for auto-differentiation, vectorization, and device-parallelism. The core simulation loop will be structured around a QP data primitive representing positions, velocities, and orientations, with modular transformations for joints, actuators, and colliders applied in a parallelizable fashion. The engine will provide a ProtoBuf-based system specification for defining physical scenes and a gym-like API for constructing sequential decision-making environments. The framework will also include JAX-based implementations of popular reinforcement learning algorithms (PPO, SAC, ES, APG), allowing both the environment and learning algorithm to run on the same accelerator, with all data processing and optimization steps compiled and executed without host-device context switches.
13263ec6b83e59442aafe1b45b7554bbba57b680.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of environments inspired by standard OpenAI Gym MuJoCo tasks (Ant, Humanoid, Halfcheetah), as well as custom environments for dexterous manipulation (Grasp) and goal-directed locomotion (Fetch). Performance will be benchmarked in terms of simulation throughput (environment steps per second) and training wall-clock time, using both single and multi-accelerator setups (e.g., TPUv2, TPUv3 clusters). Baseline comparisons will include standard MuJoCo-based environments and non-accelerator-optimized RL algorithm implementations. Evaluation metrics will include training speed, sample efficiency, reward progression, and physical fidelity (momentum and energy conservation diagnostics). Hyperparameter sweeps will be performed to identify performant configurations, and qualitative comparisons of learning curves and simulation quality will be reported.
13263ec6b83e59442aafe1b45b7554bbba57b680.novelty_claims: The proposed engine combines differentiability, high performance, and seamless accelerator integration in a single open-source library, enabling reinforcement learning experiments to be run orders of magnitude faster than existing CPU-based or non-differentiable simulators. The method supports end-to-end differentiable policy optimization, parallelizes simulation and learning across hundreds of accelerators, and provides a unified JAX-based stack for both environments and algorithms. The engine is extensible, open, and designed for rapid iteration, lowering the barrier to entry for RL research and enabling new classes of optimization and control techniques previously impractical due to computational constraints.

132957bbe335808a42a0d50f7d6c93576af0e2f5.title: Federated Dynamical Low-Rank Training with Global Loss Convergence Guarantees
132957bbe335808a42a0d50f7d6c93576af0e2f5.research_question: How can federated learning be made more efficient in terms of client computation and communication costs, while ensuring global loss convergence guarantees, particularly in scenarios where model weights can be well-approximated by low-rank matrices?
132957bbe335808a42a0d50f7d6c93576af0e2f5.hypothesis: A federated learning scheme that dynamically maintains a globally consistent low-rank basis for model weights, combined with variance correction, can significantly reduce client computation and communication costs without sacrificing global model accuracy or convergence guarantees.
132957bbe335808a42a0d50f7d6c93576af0e2f5.proposed_method: A federated dynamical low-rank training (FeDLRT) algorithm will be developed, leveraging dynamic low-rank approximation (DLRA) and a Galerkin-type operator splitting to restrict model weight updates to a low-rank manifold. The method maintains a globally shared orthonormal basis for the low-rank factors, which is dynamically augmented and truncated on the server based on training dynamics. Clients perform local optimization only on a small coefficient matrix, significantly reducing their computational and memory footprint. Variance correction, inspired by FedLin, is incorporated to bound client drift and guarantee convergence to a stationary point. The server handles all basis augmentation, orthonormalization, and rank truncation, ensuring that clients only perform lightweight updates and communicate compact low-rank factors.
132957bbe335808a42a0d50f7d6c93576af0e2f5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic tests include homogeneous and heterogeneous linear least squares regression problems, where target matrices of known low rank are used to evaluate convergence speed, rank adaptation, and global loss. Real-world benchmarks include training the fully connected head of ResNet18 on CIFAR10, with data partitioned equally among varying numbers of clients (e.g., 1 to 32). Baselines for comparison include FedAvg, FedLin, and several existing federated low-rank methods. Evaluation metrics will include validation accuracy, communication cost (in floats), client/server memory and compute footprint, and convergence rate. Multiple random initializations will be used to ensure statistical robustness, and hyperparameters such as learning rate, local steps, and singular value truncation thresholds will be systematically varied.
132957bbe335808a42a0d50f7d6c93576af0e2f5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first federated low-rank method to combine (1) efficient communication via low-rank factor sharing, (2) low client compute and memory requirements, (3) automatic server-side rank adaptation and compression during training, and (4) global loss convergence guarantees via variance correction. The method ensures a globally consistent low-rank manifold across clients, enabling robust optimization and eliminating the need for full-rank matrix reconstruction or SVD on the server. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate order-of-magnitude reductions in client costs with minimal impact on accuracy, and the approach is designed to be broadly applicable to neural networks where low-rank structure is present.

1334a47e8f4e4ffd04ff534329d76a5e5cc16f46.title: Goal-Conditioned Imitation Learning using Score-based Diffusion Policies
1334a47e8f4e4ffd04ff534329d76a5e5cc16f46.research_question: How can general-purpose, goal-conditioned policies be learned from large, uncurated, reward-free play datasets in a way that effectively captures the multimodal nature of human demonstrations and enables fast, expressive, and robust behavior generation for long-horizon robotic tasks?
1334a47e8f4e4ffd04ff534329d76a5e5cc16f46.hypothesis: Score-based diffusion models, when used as the core of a policy representation and combined with efficient sampling and classifier-free guidance, can enable expressive, multimodal, and fast goal-conditioned imitation learning from play data, outperforming existing state-of-the-art approaches without the need for hierarchical architectures or additional clustering.
1334a47e8f4e4ffd04ff534329d76a5e5cc16f46.proposed_method: A novel policy representation, termed BEhavior generation with ScOre-based Diffusion Policies (BESO), will be developed for goal-conditioned imitation learning. This method will leverage a score-based diffusion model (SDM) as the policy, where a neural network is trained to approximate the score function of the action distribution conditioned on current state and goal. The diffusion process will be formulated as a stochastic differential equation (SDE), and the reverse process will be solved using a probability flow ODE with fast, deterministic samplers (e.g., DDIM). The architecture will use a Transformer-based score model with specialized noise preconditioning and skip connections to handle a wide range of noise levels. Classifier-free guidance will be incorporated to simultaneously enable both goal-dependent and goal-independent policy learning within the same model, allowing flexible conditioning at inference time.
1334a47e8f4e4ffd04ff534329d76a5e5cc16f46.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several challenging simulation benchmarks, including the CALVIN benchmark (language-conditioned, long-horizon manipulation with 6 hours of play data), the Block-Push environment (robotic block manipulation with 1000 demonstrations), and the Relay Kitchen environment (multi-task kitchen manipulation with 566 human-collected trajectories). The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as Goal-conditioned Behavior Cloning (GCBC), Relay Imitation Learning (RIL), Latent Motor Plans (LMP), Conditional Implicit Behavior Cloning (C-IBC), Conditional-Behavior Transformer (C-BeT), and Diffusion-X (CX-Diff). Evaluation metrics will include task success rate, cumulative reward, and computational efficiency (e.g., inference time per action). Ablation studies will systematically analyze the impact of architectural choices, conditioning methods, sampling algorithms, and the number of denoising steps. All models will be evaluated over multiple random seeds and hundreds of rollouts per environment to ensure statistical robustness.
1334a47e8f4e4ffd04ff534329d76a5e5cc16f46.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to represent a behavior policy using a decoupled score-based diffusion model for goal-conditioned imitation learning from play data. It introduces a method to simultaneously learn goal-dependent and goal-independent policies using classifier-free guidance within a single diffusion framework. The method achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple challenging benchmarks while requiring significantly fewer denoising steps (as few as three) compared to previous diffusion-based policies. The architecture eliminates the need for hierarchical policies or explicit clustering, and demonstrates robustness, computational efficiency, and the ability to capture the multimodal nature of play data.

133b97e40017a9bbbadd10bcd7f13088a97ca3cc.title: Dissecting Recall of Factual Associations in Auto-Regressive Language Models
133b97e40017a9bbbadd10bcd7f13088a97ca3cc.research_question: How are factual associations internally recalled and extracted during inference in auto-regressive transformer-based language models, and what are the mechanisms and pathways through which subject-relation queries lead to the prediction of correct attributes?
133b97e40017a9bbbadd10bcd7f13088a97ca3cc.hypothesis: Factual associations are stored and enriched in early MLP sublayers and are extracted primarily via multi-head self-attention (MHSA) heads, which encode subject-attribute mappings in their parameters.
133b97e40017a9bbbadd10bcd7f13088a97ca3cc.proposed_method: A comprehensive analysis will be conducted on auto-regressive transformer-based language models to dissect the internal mechanisms of factual recall. The methodology involves targeted interventions, such as 'attention knockout,' which blocks specific attention edges at various layers to trace the flow of information from subject and relation tokens to the prediction position. Additionally, the enrichment of subject representations will be analyzed by zeroing out MLP and MHSA sublayer outputs at key positions and layers. Projections of hidden states and attention head parameters into the vocabulary space will be used to interpret the semantic content and mapping capabilities of internal representations. The approach will also include patching and gradient-based attribution to assess the necessity and sufficiency of subject enrichment for attribute extraction.
133b97e40017a9bbbadd10bcd7f13088a97ca3cc.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed on two large-scale, decoder-only language models: GPT-2 XL (1.5B parameters, 48 layers) and GPT-J (6B parameters, 28 layers), using factual open-domain question-answering queries derived from Wikipedia triplets. For each model, a sample of over 1,200 subject-relation-attribute queries will be constructed where the model predicts the correct attribute. Baseline measurements will include the attribute rate in static embeddings and intermediate representations. Interventions will be systematically applied across layers and positions, and the effects on prediction probabilities and attribute extraction rates will be measured. Evaluation metrics will include the change in prediction probability, attribute extraction rate (agreement between intermediate and final predictions), and the rank of the correct attribute in projected representations. Comparisons will be made between MLP and MHSA contributions, and the role of specific attention heads will be quantified.
133b97e40017a9bbbadd10bcd7f13088a97ca3cc.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a fine-grained, intervention-based framework for tracing and dissecting the internal recall process of factual associations in transformer LMs. It claims to reveal a previously uncharacterized three-step mechanism involving subject enrichment in early MLP layers, propagation of relation information, and attribute extraction via MHSA heads. The study will demonstrate that factual knowledge is not only stored in mid-layer MLPs but is also encoded and extracted by attention heads, which often act as knowledge hubs. This work is expected to provide new insights into model transparency, knowledge localization, and the design of more effective knowledge editing techniques.

133e0fcb3a3a903e765844ae98d367795b8f3d8d.title: Do LLMs "know" internally when they follow instructions?
133e0fcb3a3a903e765844ae98d367795b8f3d8d.research_question: How do large language models internally represent and process instruction-following, and can these internal representations be leveraged to improve adherence to user-provided instructions across diverse tasks and instruction types?
133e0fcb3a3a903e765844ae98d367795b8f3d8d.hypothesis: Large language models encode a specific dimension within their input embedding space that is predictive of instruction-following success, and manipulating model representations along this dimension can improve instruction adherence without degrading response quality. Furthermore, this dimension is hypothesized to be more sensitive to prompt phrasing than to task familiarity or instruction complexity.
133e0fcb3a3a903e765844ae98d367795b8f3d8d.proposed_method: A systematic approach will be developed to analyze the internal representations of large language models (LLMs) during instruction-following tasks. Linear probing will be applied to the input embedding space of several LLMs to identify a direction—termed the instruction-following dimension—that correlates with successful adherence to instructions. The methodology will involve disentangling the effects of task content and instruction type by pairing multiple instruction types with a fixed set of tasks, using a specially constructed dataset (IFEval-simple). Representation engineering will then be employed to manipulate model activations along the identified dimension, with the goal of converting failure cases into successes. Sensitivity analysis will be conducted to interpret the nature of this dimension by systematically perturbing prompt phrasing, task familiarity, and instruction complexity, and measuring their alignment with the instruction-following direction.
133e0fcb3a3a903e765844ae98d367795b8f3d8d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four open-source LLMs (LLaMA-2-7B-chat, LLaMA-2-13B-chat, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, and Phi-3-mini-128k-instruct) using the IFEval-simple dataset, which contains five practical instruction types paired with 100 diverse tasks. Linear probes will be trained and evaluated on model representations from various tokens (first, middle, last) and layers (early, middle, last) to assess generalization across unseen tasks (via 70-30 train-test split) and unseen instruction types (via leave-one-out cross-validation). Evaluation metrics will include Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUROC) for classification, instruction-following success rate (SR), and response quality ratio (QR) as scored by GPT-4. Baselines will include random direction manipulations in representation space. Additional experiments will perform sensitivity analysis by perturbing prompts and measuring cosine similarity to the instruction-following dimension.
133e0fcb3a3a903e765844ae98d367795b8f3d8d.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the identification and practical use of a specific instruction-following dimension within LLM input embedding spaces, enabling direct manipulation of model behavior to improve instruction adherence. The approach extends linear probing and representation engineering to the domain of instruction-following, rather than truthfulness or hallucination mitigation. The methodology disentangles task and instruction effects, demonstrates generalization across tasks but not instruction types, and provides empirical evidence that prompt phrasing, rather than task difficulty or familiarity, is most closely linked to instruction-following success. These insights offer a new, interpretable mechanism for improving and understanding LLM reliability in instruction-based applications.

1367dcff4ccb927a5e95c452041288b3f0dd0eff.title: Tune-A-Video: One-Shot Tuning of Image Diffusion Models for Text-to-Video Generation
1367dcff4ccb927a5e95c452041288b3f0dd0eff.research_question: Can text-to-video generation be achieved using only a single text-video pair by leveraging pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models, thereby eliminating the need for large-scale video datasets and extensive computational resources?
1367dcff4ccb927a5e95c452041288b3f0dd0eff.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models, when appropriately adapted and fine-tuned with a single text-video pair, can generate temporally consistent and semantically accurate videos from edited text prompts, matching or surpassing the quality of models trained on large-scale video datasets.
1367dcff4ccb927a5e95c452041288b3f0dd0eff.proposed_method: The proposed method adapts a pre-trained text-to-image (T2I) latent diffusion model to the text-to-video (T2V) domain through a process called 'One-Shot Video Tuning.' The approach involves inflating the 2D convolutional and attention layers of the T2I model into the spatio-temporal domain, introducing a sparse spatio-temporal attention mechanism that only attends to the first and previous frames to maintain temporal consistency while keeping computational complexity manageable. During fine-tuning, only the projection matrices in the attention blocks are updated, while most of the pre-trained model parameters remain frozen, ensuring efficient adaptation and preservation of learned visual concepts. At inference, DDIM inversion is employed to extract latent noise from the input video, which is then used as the starting point for DDIM sampling, guided by edited text prompts to generate new videos that preserve the structure and motion of the source video.
1367dcff4ccb927a5e95c452041288b3f0dd0eff.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using 42 representative videos from the DAVIS dataset, with 32 frames sampled per video at a resolution of 512x512. The proposed method will be fine-tuned for 500 steps per video, and inference will use the DDIM sampler with classifier-free guidance. Baselines for comparison include CogVideo (a large-scale T2V model), Plug-and-Play (an image editing model applied frame-wise), and Text2LIVE (a text-driven video editing approach). Evaluation metrics will include frame consistency (measured by average pairwise CLIP similarity between frames), textual alignment (average CLIP score between frames and prompts), and user preference studies for both temporal consistency and semantic faithfulness. Additional ablation studies will assess the impact of spatio-temporal attention, DDIM inversion, and selective fine-tuning.
1367dcff4ccb927a5e95c452041288b3f0dd0eff.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first framework for one-shot text-to-video generation using pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models, eliminating the need for large-scale video datasets. Key innovations include a sparse spatio-temporal attention mechanism for efficient temporal modeling, an efficient tuning strategy that updates only a subset of attention parameters, and the use of DDIM inversion for structural guidance during inference. The method is inherently compatible with personalized and conditional T2I models, enabling a wide range of controllable and personalized video generation and editing applications.

137073a4059f7d46f58b1f530557855f4d124ebd.title: Registration is a Powerful Rotation-Invariance Learner for 3D Anomaly Detection
137073a4059f7d46f58b1f530557855f4d124ebd.research_question: How can robust, rotation-invariant, and locally discriminative features be learned for effective 3D anomaly detection in point cloud data, particularly under spatial misalignment and geometric transformations?
137073a4059f7d46f58b1f530557855f4d124ebd.hypothesis: Integrating point cloud registration directly into the feature learning process will yield rotation-invariant and locally discriminative representations, thereby improving the reliability and accuracy of 3D anomaly detection compared to conventional memory bank-based or reconstruction-based approaches.
137073a4059f7d46f58b1f530557855f4d124ebd.proposed_method: A unified framework will be developed that embeds registration-induced feature learning into the 3D anomaly detection pipeline. The approach will generate paired point clouds via random rigid transformations and employ multi-scale voxel downsampling to construct hierarchical patch and point groupings. A feature extractor combining RIConv++, KPConv-FPN, and a Geometric Transformer will be used to encode both local and global geometric structures, ensuring rotation invariance and fine-grained discrimination. The training objective will jointly optimize geometric alignment and multi-scale feature consistency using a combination of negative log-likelihood and overlap-aware circle losses, enforced via optimal transport and Sinkhorn algorithms. During inference, the model will align test samples to a prototype via estimated rigid transformations, extract normalized features, and compute anomaly scores by comparing to a coreset-sampled memory bank.
137073a4059f7d46f58b1f530557855f4d124ebd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Anomaly-ShapeNet and Real3D-AD datasets, covering both synthetic and real-world 3D anomaly detection scenarios. Evaluation will use object-level and point-level Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (O-AUROC, P-AUROC) as metrics. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines, including both reconstruction-based (IMRNet, R3D-AD, PO3AD) and memory bank-based (BTF, M3DM, PatchCore, CPMF, Reg3D-AD, ISMP, Group3AD) methods. The experimental setup will include adaptive voxelization, feature normalization, and coreset sampling for memory bank construction, with training performed for 100k iterations using the Adam optimizer and a single RTX4090D GPU. Ablation studies will be performed on registration strategy, loss components, memory bank feature composition, and robustness to noise.
137073a4059f7d46f58b1f530557855f4d124ebd.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a novel integration of point cloud registration and feature learning, enabling the extraction of rotation-invariant and locally discriminative features tailored for 3D anomaly detection. Unlike prior methods that treat registration as a preprocessing step, this approach jointly optimizes alignment and representation learning within a unified objective. The method leverages multi-scale hierarchical grouping, advanced feature extraction modules, and optimal transport-based matching to achieve robust spatial correspondence and anomaly localization. Experimental results are expected to demonstrate significant improvements over existing baselines in both detection accuracy and generalizability, particularly within memory bank-based frameworks.

139a84c6fc4887ce2374489d79af0df9e1e7e4d6.title: Craftax: A Lightning-Fast Benchmark for Open-Ended Reinforcement Learning
139a84c6fc4887ce2374489d79af0df9e1e7e4d6.research_question: How can a reinforcement learning benchmark be designed to enable efficient, large-scale experimentation in complex, open-ended environments that require deep exploration, long-term planning, and continual adaptation, while remaining accessible to researchers with limited computational resources?
139a84c6fc4887ce2374489d79af0df9e1e7e4d6.hypothesis: A JAX-based, procedurally generated, open-ended RL environment with increased complexity and speed will enable meaningful research into generalization, exploration, and continual learning, and will expose limitations of current RL algorithms that are not apparent in simpler or slower benchmarks.
139a84c6fc4887ce2374489d79af0df9e1e7e4d6.proposed_method: A new reinforcement learning benchmark, Craftax, will be developed as a JAX-based environment featuring procedurally generated, multi-floor worlds inspired by games like Crafter and NetHack. The environment will support both pixel-based and symbolic observations, with a discrete action space and a rich set of achievements grouped by difficulty. Craftax will introduce new mechanics such as multiple floors, diverse creatures, complex combat, potions with randomized effects, enchantments, and a final boss floor, all designed to require deep exploration, memory, and long-term planning. The environment will be highly optimized for speed, allowing up to 250x faster training than previous benchmarks, and will expose the full environment state to facilitate unsupervised environment design research. Two main evaluation protocols will be established: a 1 billion step challenge for open-ended learning and a 1 million step challenge for sample efficiency.
139a84c6fc4887ce2374489d79af0df9e1e7e4d6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a suite of RL algorithms, including PPO, PPO-RNN (with memory), and state-of-the-art exploration methods such as Random Network Distillation (RND), Intrinsic Curiosity Module (ICM), and E3B. Unsupervised environment design (UED) methods like Prioritized Level Replay (PLR), Robust PLR, ACCEL, and Domain Randomization (DR) will also be evaluated. The primary dataset is the procedurally generated Craftax environment, with experiments run for up to 1 billion environment interactions per agent, using both symbolic and pixel-based observations. Baselines will be compared on reward (percentage of maximum achievable reward), achievement success rates, and episode length, with results averaged over multiple seeds and evaluated on fixed sets of levels. The experimental setup will leverage massive parallelism (up to 4096 workers) and single-GPU training to ensure accessibility.
139a84c6fc4887ce2374489d79af0df9e1e7e4d6.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces a significantly more complex and diverse open-ended RL environment than existing benchmarks, while being orders of magnitude faster due to its JAX-based implementation. Craftax combines the procedural complexity of games like NetHack with the accessibility and speed of modern RL pipelines, enabling experiments that previously required large compute clusters to be run on a single GPU. The environment exposes the full state for advanced research in unsupervised environment design and supports both symbolic and pixel-based observations. The benchmark is designed to challenge current RL methods in deep exploration, long-term planning, and continual adaptation, and provides standardized evaluation protocols for both open-ended and sample-efficient learning.

13c85adfa950651ffcd91ef3018fa30801b74472.title: Prompting and Evaluating Large Language Models for Proactive Dialogues: Clarification, Target-guided, and Non-collaboration
13c85adfa950651ffcd91ef3018fa30801b74472.research_question: Are large language model (LLM)-based conversational systems equipped to handle proactive dialogue problems, specifically in the areas of clarification, target-guided, and non-collaborative dialogues?
13c85adfa950651ffcd91ef3018fa30801b74472.hypothesis: LLM-based conversational systems can be enhanced to exhibit proactivity in dialogues—such as asking clarifying questions, guiding conversations toward designated targets, and strategically handling conflicting goals—through the use of advanced prompting schemes that incorporate planning and reasoning capabilities.
13c85adfa950651ffcd91ef3018fa30801b74472.proposed_method: A proactive chain-of-thought prompting (ProCoT) scheme will be developed to augment LLM-based conversational systems with planning and decision-making capabilities. This method involves instructing the LLM to first generate descriptive reasoning about intermediate steps needed to reach the conversational goal, followed by the selection of appropriate dialogue acts or strategies, and finally the generation of the response based on the planned action. The approach will be systematically applied to three proactive dialogue scenarios: (1) clarification dialogues, where the system must identify ambiguity and ask clarifying questions; (2) target-guided dialogues, where the system proactively shifts the conversation toward a hidden target topic; and (3) non-collaborative dialogues, where the system must negotiate or reach consensus despite conflicting goals. The prompting schemes will be evaluated in both zero-shot and few-shot (in-context learning) settings, and compared to standard and proactive (action-selection) prompting baselines.
13c85adfa950651ffcd91ef3018fa30801b74472.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using both proprietary (ChatGPT/gpt-3.5-turbo-0301) and open-source (Vicuna-13B) LLMs. For clarification dialogues, the Abg-CoQA (general domain) and PACIFIC (finance domain) datasets will be used, evaluating both clarification need prediction (CNP) and clarification question generation (CQG) with metrics such as F1, BLEU-1, ROUGE-2, and human helpfulness ratings. For target-guided dialogues, turn-level evaluation will use the OTTers dataset (next-topic prediction and transition response generation, with hits@k, BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE-L), and dialogue-level evaluation will use TGConv (success rate, average turns, contextual coherence, and human ratings). For non-collaborative dialogues, the CraigslistBargain dataset will be used to assess negotiation strategy prediction, dialogue act prediction, and response generation (F1, ROC AUC, BLEU, BERTScore), as well as human evaluations of persuasiveness, coherence, naturalness, and negotiation outcome (sale-to-list ratio). Baselines will include fine-tuned state-of-the-art dialogue models, and both automatic and human evaluations will be performed.
13c85adfa950651ffcd91ef3018fa30801b74472.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first comprehensive evaluation of LLM-based dialogue systems on proactive dialogue capabilities, encompassing clarification, target-guided, and non-collaborative scenarios. The proactive chain-of-thought prompting scheme is a novel method that endows LLMs with explicit planning and reasoning abilities for dialogue management, going beyond standard instruction-following or action-selection prompts. The approach systematically benchmarks LLMs against fine-tuned baselines and provides detailed empirical analysis across multiple domains and dialogue types, highlighting both the strengths and current limitations of LLMs in proactive conversational AI.

13df1025968bd89f204a3a526a712919b929a832.title: One Prompt Fits All: Universal Graph Adaptation for Pretrained Models
13df1025968bd89f204a3a526a712919b929a832.research_question: How can graph prompt learning be made universally adaptable to any pretrained graph model, effectively bridging the adaptation gap between upstream pretraining and diverse downstream tasks, especially under distribution shifts and few-shot learning scenarios?
13df1025968bd89f204a3a526a712919b929a832.hypothesis: Input-level prompt mechanisms that adapt the graph topology, when combined with a learnable classifier, will more effectively unleash the capabilities of pretrained graph models and improve generalization across in-domain and cross-domain tasks compared to existing prompt strategies or simple fine-tuning.
13df1025968bd89f204a3a526a712919b929a832.proposed_method: A universal input-level graph prompt learning framework, UniPrompt, will be developed to adapt any pretrained graph model to downstream tasks. The method constructs a k-nearest neighbor (kNN) prompt graph with learnable edge weights, initialized based on feature similarity, and integrates it with the original graph topology using a bootstrapped iterative fusion mechanism controlled by a temperature coefficient. This prompt graph is fed into the frozen pretrained encoder, and a lightweight, learnable classifier (projection head) is jointly optimized with the prompt parameters on labeled nodes. The edge weights in the prompt graph are adaptively gated using a scaled and shifted ELU activation to ensure non-negativity and selective amplification or pruning of topological information. The optimization objective is the cross-entropy loss over labeled nodes, jointly updating the prompt parameters and classifier while keeping the pretrained encoder fixed.
13df1025968bd89f204a3a526a712919b929a832.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on nine node classification datasets, including both homophilic (Cora, CiteSeer, PubMed) and heterophilic (Cornell, Texas, Wisconsin, Chameleon, Actor, Squirrel) graphs. Three pretrained models (DGI, GRACE, GraphMAE) will be used for in-domain settings, while FUG will be used for cross-domain scenarios. Baselines will include fine-tuning, linear probing, and a range of state-of-the-art graph prompt learning methods (e.g., GPPT, GraphPrompt, GPF, EdgePrompt), as well as supervised and self-supervised baselines (GCN, GAT, DGI, GraphCL) and multi-domain graph foundation models (GCOPE, MDGPT, MDGFM). Performance will be evaluated under 1/3/5-shot settings, with accuracy as the primary metric. Each experiment will be repeated 20 times over 5 fixed random seeds (100 trials total) for statistical reliability. Hyperparameter sensitivity (e.g., prompt fusion coefficient, k in kNN) will also be analyzed.
13df1025968bd89f204a3a526a712919b929a832.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a universal, input-level prompt mechanism that is compatible with any pretrained graph model, addressing both the lack of mechanistic consensus and limited scenario adaptability in existing graph prompt learning. The method provides a theoretically grounded distinction between prompt learning and fine-tuning, demonstrating that representation-level prompts are equivalent to linear probing, and thus advocates for input-level prompting to truly leverage pretrained knowledge. The bootstrapped integration of a learnable prompt graph with the original topology is novel, preventing overfitting and model collapse in few-shot settings. Extensive experiments are designed to show consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines in both in-domain and cross-domain scenarios, including challenging distribution shifts.

13fba50e2c707b30e17defd93c040e837c29921e.title: Variational Information Pursuit for Interpretable Predictions
13fba50e2c707b30e17defd93c040e837c29921e.research_question: How can predictive machine learning models be designed to provide interpretable predictions by sequentially querying interpretable features, while avoiding the computational and modeling challenges of full generative models?
13fba50e2c707b30e17defd93c040e837c29921e.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a variational approach, which directly optimizes a KL-divergence-based objective over query selection and classification functions, can efficiently and effectively produce interpretable predictions with short query-answer chains, competitive accuracy, and significantly reduced computational cost compared to generative modeling and reinforcement learning approaches.
13fba50e2c707b30e17defd93c040e837c29921e.proposed_method: A variational framework for interpretable prediction, termed Variational Information Pursuit (V-IP), will be developed. This framework will parameterize both the query selection strategy (querier) and the classifier as deep neural networks. The objective is to minimize the expected KL-divergence between the true label distribution and the predicted label distribution conditioned on the current history of query-answer pairs and the next query. The querier network will sequentially select the most informative query given any history, while the classifier network will estimate the posterior over labels. Training will involve adaptive sampling of query-answer histories, initially random and then biased towards those encountered under the current querier, and optimization will be performed end-to-end using stochastic gradient descent. Differentiable approximations such as the straight-through softmax estimator will be used to enable gradient-based optimization through the query selection process.
13fba50e2c707b30e17defd93c040e837c29921e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of vision, NLP, and medical diagnosis datasets, including CUB-200 (bird attributes), Huffington News (headline word presence), MNIST, KMNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10/100 (image patches), and several medical symptom datasets (SymCAT-200/300/400, MuZhi, Dxy).
