For each dataset, a user-defined interpretable query set will be used, and the proposed method will be compared against baselines including generative-model-based Information Pursuit (G-IP), reinforcement learning approaches (RAM, RAM+, REFUEL), and random query selection. Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy, area under the accuracy vs. explanation length curve (AUC), and computational efficiency (inference time per query). Both fixed-budget and adaptive stopping criteria will be explored, and ablation studies will be performed to assess architectural and sampling choices.
13fba50e2c707b30e17defd93c040e837c29921e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a variational characterization of the Information Pursuit framework that eliminates the need for explicit generative modeling and MCMC-based inference. By jointly learning the querier and classifier networks via a KL-divergence objective, the method enables efficient, end-to-end optimization and inference. The approach is claimed to be 10-100x faster than prior generative-model-based methods, to produce shorter and more interpretable query chains than reinforcement learning baselines, and to achieve competitive or superior predictive performance across a variety of complex tasks. Additionally, the framework provides a principled, interpretable-by-design prediction process, with theoretical guarantees aligning the variational solution with the optimal information pursuit strategy.

13fc67cf6fa303d31c41c5c814cbd3d42f2f8504.title: JetFormer: An Autoregressive Generative Model of Raw Images and Text
13fc67cf6fa303d31c41c5c814cbd3d42f2f8504.research_question: How can a unified, end-to-end trainable generative model be developed to jointly understand and generate both raw images and text, without relying on separately pretrained modality-specific components?
13fc67cf6fa303d31c41c5c814cbd3d42f2f8504.hypothesis: A generative model that combines a normalizing flow-based image representation with an autoregressive transformer, trained end-to-end on raw image and text data, will achieve competitive performance in both image generation and vision-language understanding tasks, while eliminating the need for separately pretrained encoders or decoders.
13fc67cf6fa303d31c41c5c814cbd3d42f2f8504.proposed_method: A novel generative framework is proposed that integrates a normalizing flow model with a decoder-only autoregressive transformer. The normalizing flow is used to encode raw images into continuous 'soft-token' representations, which are lossless and invertible, allowing for both image encoding and decoding. These soft tokens, along with text tokens, are modeled jointly by the transformer, which is trained to maximize the log-likelihood of the raw data using a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) loss for image tokens and a categorical loss for text tokens. The entire system is trained end-to-end from scratch, with no reliance on pretrained or frozen modality-specific encoders or decoders. Additional enhancements include a noise curriculum during training, where Gaussian noise is added to images and gradually reduced, and the factoring out of redundant latent dimensions to improve efficiency and sample quality.
13fc67cf6fa303d31c41c5c814cbd3d42f2f8504.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on class-conditional image generation using the ImageNet-1k dataset and on large-scale multimodal generation using the WebLI dataset of image-text pairs. The model is evaluated on image generation quality using FID, precision, and recall metrics, and on vision-language understanding tasks such as zero-shot ImageNet classification, COCO captioning (CIDEr), and VQAv2 visual question answering (accuracy). Baselines include VQ-VAE and VAE-based transformer models, as well as diffusion models. Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of the normalizing flow, noise curriculum, dimensionality reduction, and other architectural choices. Training details include the use of the Adam optimizer, large batch sizes, and a cosine noise decay schedule for image augmentation.
13fc67cf6fa303d31c41c5c814cbd3d42f2f8504.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable fully end-to-end joint modeling of raw images and text with a single autoregressive transformer and a normalizing flow, without any separately pretrained or frozen modality-specific components. The method introduces a noise curriculum as a training augmentation to prioritize high-level image structure, and demonstrates that lossless, invertible flow-based image representations can be learned jointly with the transformer for both generation and understanding. The model achieves competitive or superior performance to prior VQ-VAE and VAE-based baselines, particularly in vision-language understanding, and provides explicit log-likelihood bounds for raw images, which is rare among high-fidelity image generators.

14003bb8b5236f4abb12963745c04a6c6610cc5d.title: KVTuner: Sensitivity-Aware Layer-wise Mixed Precision KV Cache Quantization for Efficient and Nearly Lossless LLM Inference
14003bb8b5236f4abb12963745c04a6c6610cc5d.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be made more efficient in inference by compressing the key-value (KV) cache using mixed-precision quantization, while maintaining high accuracy across diverse models and hardware constraints?
14003bb8b5236f4abb12963745c04a6c6610cc5d.hypothesis: Layer-wise sensitivity to KV cache quantization is an inherent property of LLMs, and by adaptively tuning the precision of key and value caches at the layer level—prioritizing higher precision for keys in sensitive layers—it is possible to achieve nearly lossless model accuracy with significantly reduced memory usage and improved inference throughput.
14003bb8b5236f4abb12963745c04a6c6610cc5d.proposed_method: A novel framework, KVTuner, will be developed to automatically search for optimal, hardware-friendly, layer-wise mixed-precision KV cache quantization configurations for LLMs. The method will begin with a theoretical and empirical analysis of the sensitivity of transformer layers to KV cache quantization, establishing that key caches are generally more critical than value caches for maintaining accuracy. The approach will employ a two-stage search space reduction: first, intra-layer pruning will identify Pareto-efficient KV precision pairs within each layer based on quantization error and memory trade-offs; second, inter-layer clustering will group layers with similar sensitivity profiles, further reducing the combinatorial search space. Multi-objective optimization algorithms will then be used offline to find Pareto-optimal layer-wise KV precision pairs that balance memory footprint and accuracy loss under user-specified constraints. The resulting quantization configurations will be directly loaded during inference, incurring no online decision-making overhead.
14003bb8b5236f4abb12963745c04a6c6610cc5d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of LLMs, including Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, and others, using mathematical reasoning datasets such as GSM8K and scientific reasoning benchmarks like GPQA Extended. Baselines will include uniform precision quantization methods (e.g., KIVI-8, KIVI-4, per-token-asym) and prior mixed-precision approaches. Evaluation metrics will encompass model accuracy (e.g., word perplexity, reasoning accuracy), memory usage (average equivalent quantization bits), and inference throughput (tokens per second). The experimental setup will include both few-shot and multi-turn reasoning tasks, as well as long-context generation scenarios, with calibration datasets designed to amplify error accumulation and distinguish the impact of different quantization settings. Ablation studies will assess the impact of search space pruning and sensitivity-aware tuning.
14003bb8b5236f4abb12963745c04a6c6610cc5d.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the first sensitivity-aware, layer-wise mixed-precision KV cache quantization method for LLMs that is both hardware-friendly and plug-and-play. Key innovations include a theoretical analysis of why key cache precision is more critical than value cache, a two-stage search space reduction (intra-layer pruning and inter-layer clustering) to enable efficient offline optimization, and an automatic, multi-objective search for Pareto-optimal precision pairs. The method achieves nearly lossless quantization (as low as 3.25 bits) for strong models and outperforms existing baselines in both memory efficiency and inference throughput, with up to 21.25% throughput improvement over state-of-the-art uniform quantization. The framework generalizes across LLM architectures and is compatible with existing inference acceleration systems.

1406bb4cb6801bc4767b661308118c888a9b09da.title: MMLU-Pro: A More Robust and Challenging Multi-Task Language Understanding Benchmark
1406bb4cb6801bc4767b661308118c888a9b09da.research_question: How can a new benchmark be developed to more robustly and discriminatively evaluate multi-task language understanding and reasoning capabilities of large language models, overcoming the limitations of existing benchmarks such as performance saturation, lack of reasoning focus, and sensitivity to prompt variations?
1406bb4cb6801bc4767b661308118c888a9b09da.hypothesis: A benchmark that integrates more challenging, reasoning-focused questions, expands the number of answer choices, and removes trivial or noisy items will provide a more robust, discriminative, and reliable evaluation of advanced language models, better tracking progress and differentiating model capabilities.
1406bb4cb6801bc4767b661308118c888a9b09da.proposed_method: A new multi-task language understanding benchmark will be constructed by aggregating and curating questions from diverse sources, including the original MMLU dataset, STEM educational websites, TheoremQA, and SciBench. The dataset will be filtered to remove trivial, overly simple, or erroneous questions using multiple language models as filters, and the subject categories will be consolidated for broader coverage. Each question will be augmented to have ten answer options, with additional distractors generated using advanced language models (e.g., GPT-4-Turbo) and validated for plausibility and distinctiveness. A two-phase expert review process will be implemented: first, human experts will verify correctness and appropriateness of questions and answers; second, advanced models (e.g., Gemini-1.5-Pro) will help identify false negatives among distractors, which will then be manually reviewed. The final dataset will emphasize reasoning and professional-level problem-solving across 14 disciplines, ensuring high quality and minimal noise.
1406bb4cb6801bc4767b661308118c888a9b09da.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate over 50 large language models, both open-source and closed-source, on the proposed benchmark using a 5-shot Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting strategy, with select models also evaluated using direct answering for comparison. The evaluation will span 14 disciplines and over 12,000 questions, with accuracy as the primary metric. Robustness will be assessed by measuring model performance variability under 24 different prompt styles. Baselines will include performance on the original MMLU benchmark, and detailed error analysis will be conducted on leading models to identify reasoning, knowledge, and calculation errors. The experimental setup will ensure consistent answer extraction and fair comparison across models.
1406bb4cb6801bc4767b661308118c888a9b09da.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces several innovations: (1) a substantial increase in reasoning-focused, college-level exam questions, (2) expansion of answer choices from four to ten to reduce guesswork and increase difficulty, (3) rigorous multi-phase expert review to minimize dataset noise and annotation errors, (4) demonstrated improved discriminative power and robustness to prompt variations compared to existing benchmarks, and (5) a design that necessitates advanced reasoning strategies such as Chain-of-Thought, thus better reflecting professional-level language understanding and reasoning.

141c137db6bd8f12fa0ce81968a4a8370d36ca74.title: On the Identifiability of Nonlinear ICA: Sparsity and Beyond
141c137db6bd8f12fa0ce81968a4a8370d36ca74.research_question: Can nonlinear independent component analysis (ICA) models be made identifiable, up to trivial indeterminacies, in the fully unsupervised setting without auxiliary variables, by imposing structural assumptions on the mixing process? What structural or simplicity-based constraints on the mixing function are sufficient to guarantee identifiability of latent sources from nonlinear mixtures, and how do these compare to existing approaches relying on auxiliary information?
141c137db6bd8f12fa0ce81968a4a8370d36ca74.hypothesis: Imposing structural sparsity or related simplicity constraints on the mixing process enables the identifiability of nonlinear ICA models with unconditional priors, allowing recovery of independent latent sources up to component-wise invertible transformations and permutations, even in the absence of auxiliary variables.
141c137db6bd8f12fa0ce81968a4a8370d36ca74.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed for nonlinear ICA that leverages structural sparsity in the mixing process to achieve identifiability. The approach formalizes sparsity as a condition on the support of the Jacobian matrix of the nonlinear mixing function, requiring that for each latent source, there exists a set of observed variables influenced only by that source. Estimation will be performed via a regularized maximum-likelihood objective, incorporating a sparsity-inducing penalty (e.g., L1 norm of the Jacobian) to promote minimal support in the estimated mixing function. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to establish identifiability results under these structural conditions, including extensions to the undercomplete case (more observed variables than sources) and reductions of indeterminacy under additional assumptions such as volume-preservation or factorial Jacobian determinants. Alternative simplicity-based constraints, such as independence of influences and orthogonality of the Jacobian columns, will also be explored both theoretically and empirically.
141c137db6bd8f12fa0ce81968a4a8370d36ca74.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic data and real-world-inspired image datasets to validate the theoretical claims. Synthetic datasets will be generated according to specified structural sparsity, independent influences, and volume-preserving constraints, with ablation studies comparing models with and without these assumptions. The 'Triangles' image dataset will be used to assess the applicability of the proposed conditions to practical data-generating processes, with sources corresponding to interpretable semantic factors. Baseline methods will include vanilla nonlinear ICA without structural constraints and models incorporating independent mechanism analysis (IMA) or orthogonality. Evaluation metrics will primarily be the mean correlation coefficient (MCC) between true and estimated sources, along with visualizations of Pearson correlation matrices. The stability of the method will be assessed by varying the number of sources, and the effectiveness of alternative regularizations (e.g., orthogonality, factorial Jacobian) will be empirically compared.
141c137db6bd8f12fa0ce81968a4a8370d36ca74.novelty_claims: The proposed research provides, for the first time, identifiability results for nonlinear ICA with unconditional priors based solely on structural assumptions of the mixing process, without requiring auxiliary variables or conditional independence. The structural sparsity condition enables recovery of latent sources up to trivial indeterminacies, even in cases previously thought unsolvable (e.g., linear ICA with Gaussian sources). The framework extends to undercomplete settings and offers a general approach to identifiability in unsupervised learning. Additionally, the exploration of alternative simplicity-based constraints (such as independent influences and orthogonality) broadens the theoretical and empirical understanding of identifiability in nonlinear ICA.

142ebbf4760145f591166bde2564ac70c001e927.title: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
142ebbf4760145f591166bde2564ac70c001e927.research_question: Can large language models accurately evaluate the validity of their own outputs and predict which questions they are able to answer correctly, thereby demonstrating self-knowledge and calibrated confidence in their responses across a diverse range of tasks?
142ebbf4760145f591166bde2564ac70c001e927.hypothesis: Large language models, when prompted appropriately, are capable of producing well-calibrated confidence estimates regarding the correctness of their own answers and can be trained to predict their own knowledge state (i.e., whether they know the answer to a question), with performance improving as model size increases.
142ebbf4760145f591166bde2564ac70c001e927.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation framework will be developed to assess language models' ability to self-evaluate their outputs. The approach will involve two main components: (1) prompting models to generate answers to open-ended and multiple choice questions, then asking them to assign a probability P(True) to the correctness of each answer; and (2) training a value head on top of the language model to predict P(IK), the probability that the model knows the answer to a given question, without reference to a specific answer. Calibration will be assessed by comparing predicted probabilities to empirical frequencies, using metrics such as Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Brier Score. The effect of providing multiple model-generated samples ('brainstorming') before self-evaluation will also be investigated to determine its impact on calibration and discriminative performance.
142ebbf4760145f591166bde2564ac70c001e927.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a suite of language models ranging from 800M to 52B parameters, pretrained on 850B tokens with approximately 10% code. Evaluation will span diverse datasets, including multiple choice tasks from BIG Bench, MMLU, TruthfulQA, LogiQA, and QuALITY, as well as open-ended generation tasks such as TriviaQA, Lambada, GSM8k, Codex HumanEval, arithmetic problems, and web-scraped Python function synthesis. Both zero-shot and few-shot settings will be tested, with few-shot contexts constructed from within-task examples. Baselines will include standard answer selection, 'none of the above' options, and true/false reformulations. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, AUROC, ECE, and Brier Score, with calibration curves and conditional accuracy analyses. Out-of-distribution generalization will be assessed by training P(IK) on one task and evaluating on others, and the impact of source materials and hints will be measured.
142ebbf4760145f591166bde2564ac70c001e927.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a systematic methodology for eliciting and quantifying self-knowledge and calibrated confidence in large language models, extending beyond token-level calibration to open-ended and generative tasks. It proposes the use of model-internal probability estimates (P(True) and P(IK)) for self-evaluation and knowledge prediction, and demonstrates that model size and prompting strategies significantly affect calibration and generalization. The approach also explores the impact of providing multiple model-generated samples prior to evaluation, and investigates generalization of self-knowledge across tasks and with the inclusion of external information such as source materials and problem hints. This work lays the groundwork for developing more honest and trustworthy AI systems capable of expressing reliable confidence in their outputs.

143e18bfd7c356592e7c1439738a3525d3e16279.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
143e18bfd7c356592e7c1439738a3525d3e16279.research_question: Does reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) genuinely incentivize large language models (LLMs) to develop novel reasoning abilities that exceed those of their base models, or does RLVR merely improve the efficiency of sampling correct responses without expanding the underlying reasoning capacity?
143e18bfd7c356592e7c1439738a3525d3e16279.hypothesis: Current RLVR methods do not elicit fundamentally new reasoning patterns in LLMs beyond what is already present in the base model; instead, RLVR primarily increases the likelihood of sampling correct responses from existing reasoning paths, potentially narrowing the model's overall reasoning coverage.
143e18bfd7c356592e7c1439738a3525d3e16279.proposed_method: A systematic evaluation framework will be established to probe the reasoning capacity boundaries of RLVR-trained LLMs compared to their base models. Multiple LLM families and sizes will be considered, and a variety of RLVR algorithms (such as PPO, GRPO, Reinforce++, RLOO, ReMax, and DAPO) will be implemented. The evaluation will utilize the pass@k metric at both small and large k values, which measures the proportion of problems solvable within k samples, thereby providing a robust assessment of reasoning coverage. Additional analyses will include manual inspection of chain-of-thought (CoT) outputs for correctness, perplexity analysis to determine whether RLVR-generated reasoning paths are present in the base model's output distribution, and comparison with distillation approaches that transfer reasoning patterns from stronger teacher models. Controlled ablations will examine the effects of RL algorithm choice, training steps, rollout numbers, KL regularization, entropy, and model scaling.
143e18bfd7c356592e7c1439738a3525d3e16279.experiment_details: Experiments will span mathematics, code generation, and visual reasoning tasks using benchmarks such as GSM8K, MATH500, Minerva, Olympiad, AIME24, AMC23, LiveCodeBench, HumanEval+, MBPP+, MathVista, and MathVision. Both zero-shot and instruction-tuned base models will be compared to their RLVR-trained counterparts, with consistent prompt templates and sampling parameters (e.g., temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, max tokens 16,384). Pass@k will be computed for a range of k values (from 1 up to 1024 or 128, depending on the benchmark), and manual validation of CoTs will be performed for challenging problems to distinguish genuine reasoning from lucky guesses. Baselines will include base models, RLVR-trained models, and distilled models. Additional metrics such as accuracy distributions, sampling efficiency gap (difference between RLVR pass@1 and base model pass@k), and perplexity of generated responses will be analyzed. Ablation studies will control for RL algorithm, training hyperparameters, and entropy.
143e18bfd7c356592e7c1439738a3525d3e16279.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a rigorous, multi-faceted evaluation protocol for assessing whether RLVR expands the reasoning capacity of LLMs or merely improves sampling efficiency. The approach extends pass@k metrics to a broad set of reasoning tasks and includes in-depth manual and quantitative analyses of reasoning paths and coverage. The research will clarify the limitations of current RLVR paradigms, highlight the distinction between RLVR and distillation in expanding reasoning boundaries, and provide actionable insights for developing improved RL algorithms that can genuinely unlock new reasoning abilities in LLMs.

14476c7ddcd7844d74dbd54bd20fb86ed1ae2a8d.title: Steering Masked Discrete Diffusion Models via Discrete Denoising Posterior Prediction
14476c7ddcd7844d74dbd54bd20fb86ed1ae2a8d.research_question: How can discrete diffusion models be steered to generate samples that satisfy arbitrary, potentially non-differentiable reward functions or downstream metrics, enabling controllable generation in domains such as images, proteins, and text?
14476c7ddcd7844d74dbd54bd20fb86ed1ae2a8d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that steering pre-trained masked discrete diffusion models can be effectively formulated as a probabilistic inference problem, where fine-tuning is achieved by learning to sample from a reward-modulated Bayesian posterior, and that this approach will enable scalable, simulation-free alignment with general reward models, including non-differentiable ones.
14476c7ddcd7844d74dbd54bd20fb86ed1ae2a8d.proposed_method: A novel framework, Discrete Denoising Posterior Prediction (DDPP), will be developed to steer pre-trained Masked Diffusion Models (MDMs) by casting the steering task as Bayesian posterior sampling. The target posterior is defined as the product of the pre-trained MDM and a reward model, representing the desired property or metric. DDPP introduces a family of simulation-free objectives that match the denoising trajectories or endpoints of the fine-tuned model to those of the reward-induced posterior, leveraging the denoising posterior parameterization inherent to MDMs. Three concrete algorithmic variants will be implemented: (1) DDPP-IS, which uses Monte Carlo importance sampling to estimate the partition function; (2) DDPP-LB, which parameterizes and amortizes the partition function as a learnable head; and (3) DDPP-KL, which minimizes the reverse KL divergence using discrete gradient estimators when the reward is differentiable. The approach allows fine-tuning with arbitrary reward functions and supports both trajectory-level and single-step endpoint matching.
14476c7ddcd7844d74dbd54bd20fb86ed1ae2a8d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across multiple domains: (1) synthetic discrete grid tasks and binarized MNIST for controlled evaluation, (2) pixel-level image modeling using CelebA (64x64) with discretized pixels, (3) protein sequence generation using discrete protein language models (DPLMs) with tasks such as high β-sheet content and protein shrinking, and (4) text generation tasks including toxic story generation (Tinystories dataset) and product review sentiment control (Amazon reviews). Baselines will include Best-of-N sampling, Relative Trajectory Balance (RTB), SVDD, and the base pre-trained MDM. Evaluation metrics will be tailored to each domain: log-reward, Fréchet distance, bits-per-dimension (BPD) for images, ESMFold pLDDT/pTM and TM-Score for proteins, and log-reward and GPT-2 perplexity (GenPPL) for text. For protein design, wet-lab validation will be performed to assess expression and structural fidelity. Experimental setups will ensure fair comparison by using the same pre-trained MDMs and reward models across methods.
14476c7ddcd7844d74dbd54bd20fb86ed1ae2a8d.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first scalable, simulation-free method for steering and aligning masked discrete diffusion models with arbitrary, potentially non-differentiable reward models. DDPP introduces a principled Bayesian inference perspective for fine-tuning discrete diffusion models, enabling efficient and generalizable control without requiring full trajectory simulation or differentiable rewards. The approach is broadly applicable across domains and supports both amortized and inference-time steering. Empirical validation, including wet-lab protein expression, demonstrates the practical impact and versatility of the method.

144cc108f0072f78c67fa97a17972d3ac5da894d.title: SORTeD Rashomon Sets of Sparse Decision Trees: Anytime Enumeration
144cc108f0072f78c67fa97a17972d3ac5da894d.research_question: How can the enumeration of Rashomon sets of sparse decision trees be made scalable, efficient, and flexible to support anytime retrieval, ordered solution generation, and analysis under diverse objectives in high-stakes, real-world applications?
144cc108f0072f78c67fa97a17972d3ac5da894d.hypothesis: Enumerating Rashomon sets of sparse decision trees in objective-value order using a dynamic programming-based framework will significantly improve runtime and memory efficiency, enable anytime solution retrieval, and support flexible post-hoc evaluation under various objectives compared to existing methods.
144cc108f0072f78c67fa97a17972d3ac5da894d.proposed_method: A novel framework, SORTD (Sorted Rashomon Sets of Trees using Dynamic Programming), will be developed to enumerate sparse decision trees within the Rashomon set in non-decreasing order of their objective values. The method will first identify the optimal tree and set a Rashomon bound, then iteratively construct the Rashomon set by maintaining sorted lists of solutions at each node in a search tree. Each search node will aggregate solutions from its helper nodes (branching or leaf), and a lazy enumeration strategy will be employed to generate new solutions only as needed, reducing computation time. To further enhance scalability, a specialized subroutine for efficiently enumerating all depth-two trees will be integrated, leveraging precomputed frequency counts for rapid misclassification calculations. The framework will support any separable and totally ordered objective for computation and allow post-hoc evaluation with separable and partially ordered objectives, such as fairness metrics.
144cc108f0072f78c67fa97a17972d3ac5da894d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 30 benchmark binary classification datasets, as well as standard regression and fairness datasets, to evaluate runtime, scalability, and flexibility. The proposed method will be compared against the state-of-the-art TreeFARMS algorithm, with both methods enumerating Rashomon sets under identical Rashomon multipliers and varying tree depth budgets (d ∈ {3,4,5}) and complexity costs (λ ∈ {0.001, 0.01, 0.1}). Evaluation metrics will include runtime, memory usage, and the stability of variable importance analysis (using LOFO scores and ranking stability via Jaccard index and Kendall's τ). Additional experiments will demonstrate the method's ability to enumerate Rashomon sets for regression objectives and to support post-hoc evaluation with fairness metrics such as equality of opportunity. All experiments will be run single-threaded with a fixed time and memory budget, and the implementation will be made available as a Python package.
144cc108f0072f78c67fa97a17972d3ac5da894d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first framework for enumerating Rashomon sets of sparse decision trees in objective-value order, enabling anytime retrieval of the highest-quality models. The method achieves substantial improvements in runtime and memory efficiency, scaling to larger feature sets and deeper trees than previous methods. It generalizes Rashomon set computation to any separable and totally ordered objective and uniquely supports post-hoc evaluation with separable and partially ordered objectives, such as multi-objective fairness criteria. The integration of a specialized depth-two solver further enhances scalability, and the ordered enumeration facilitates downstream tasks such as variable importance analysis and flexible model selection.

144eca44e250cc462f6fc3a172abb865978f66f5.title: Multi-Concept Customization of Text-to-Image Diffusion
144eca44e250cc462f6fc3a172abb865978f66f5.research_question: How can a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model be efficiently customized to represent new user-provided concepts from a few images, and how can multiple such new concepts be composed together in novel settings without catastrophic forgetting or overfitting?
144eca44e250cc462f6fc3a172abb865978f66f5.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that fine-tuning only a small subset of parameters in the cross-attention layers of a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model, combined with targeted regularization and data augmentation, is sufficient to efficiently and effectively embed new concepts and enable their composition, while preserving prior knowledge and minimizing overfitting.
144eca44e250cc462f6fc3a172abb865978f66f5.proposed_method: The proposed method, termed Custom Diffusion, augments a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model by fine-tuning only the key and value projection matrices in the cross-attention layers, along with a new modifier token for each novel concept. For each new concept, a small set of user-provided images and corresponding text prompts are used for training. To prevent overfitting and language drift, a regularization dataset of real images with captions similar to the target concept is retrieved and incorporated into the training process. Data augmentation is performed by randomly resizing images and appending size-related prompts. For multi-concept composition, either joint training on multiple concepts or a closed-form constrained optimization is used to merge the fine-tuned parameters, allowing coherent generation of scenes containing multiple new concepts.
144eca44e250cc462f6fc3a172abb865978f66f5.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using Stable Diffusion as the backbone model. The method is evaluated on multiple datasets, including user-personalized objects, animals, and rare categories, with as few as four training images per concept. Baselines include DreamBooth, Textual Inversion, and full-model fine-tuning. Evaluation metrics comprise CLIP-based image- and text-alignment, Kernel Inception Distance (KID) against real validation images, and human preference studies. Both single-concept and multi-concept scenarios are tested, with quantitative and qualitative comparisons, as well as ablation studies on regularization, augmentation, and parameter subsets. Training is performed for 250–500 steps with a batch size of 8, and inference uses DDPM sampling with 50–200 steps and a guidance scale of 6.
144eca44e250cc462f6fc3a172abb865978f66f5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a highly efficient method for customizing text-to-image diffusion models by updating only a small fraction (approximately 3%) of the model parameters, specifically in the cross-attention layers. It enables rapid fine-tuning (approximately 6 minutes per concept) and requires minimal storage per concept. The method supports both joint and optimization-based composition of multiple new concepts, outperforming or matching existing baselines in both fidelity and compositionality, while being significantly more memory- and compute-efficient. The use of a regularization dataset and targeted data augmentation further mitigates overfitting and catastrophic forgetting, enabling seamless integration of new concepts with existing model knowledge.

1460d33f547ee40c560174dc0f6898f4802f4cf8.title: Calibrated Language Models Must Hallucinate
1460d33f547ee40c560174dc0f6898f4802f4cf8.research_question: What are the fundamental statistical limits on the rate of hallucinations produced by calibrated language models, and how do these limits depend on the nature of the facts (arbitrary versus systematic) present in the training data?
1460d33f547ee40c560174dc0f6898f4802f4cf8.hypothesis: For language models that are statistically calibrated and trained on ideal, error-free data, there exists an inherent lower bound on the rate of hallucination for arbitrary facts whose veracity cannot be determined from the training data. This lower bound is closely related to the fraction of such facts that appear exactly once in the training set, and cannot be eliminated solely by improving model architecture or data quality.
1460d33f547ee40c560174dc0f6898f4802f4cf8.proposed_method: A mathematical framework will be developed to analyze the relationship between calibration, factoid frequency in training data, and the rate of hallucination in generative language models. The approach will define a semantic-level calibration criterion for generative models, extending beyond token-level calibration, and will model the generation of arbitrary factoids as a probabilistic process. The analysis will employ the Good-Turing estimator to quantify the 'missing mass'—the proportion of plausible facts not observed in the training data—and derive lower bounds on hallucination rates as a function of this missing mass and model miscalibration. Theoretical results will be established under assumptions such as i.i.d. sampling, one factoid per document, and a clear distinction between facts and hallucinations.
1460d33f547ee40c560174dc0f6898f4802f4cf8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in both synthetic and real-world data settings. Synthetic datasets will be constructed to allow precise control over the distribution of arbitrary factoids and the frequency with which they appear in training data, enabling direct measurement of hallucination rates under varying calibration and data regimes. Real-world experiments will analyze large-scale language model training corpora, such as web-scale text datasets, to empirically estimate the fraction of factoids appearing exactly once and the corresponding hallucination rates. Baselines will include language models with varying degrees of calibration and post-training alignment. Evaluation metrics will include the hallucination rate (fraction of generated factoids not present in training data), calibration error (e.g., expected calibration error, ECE), and the accuracy of the Good-Turing estimator in predicting missing mass.
1460d33f547ee40c560174dc0f6898f4802f4cf8.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a formal statistical lower bound on hallucination rates for calibrated language models, independent of model architecture or data quality, and provides a semantic-level calibration definition tailored to generative models. The analysis distinguishes between arbitrary and systematic facts, showing that hallucinations are statistically inevitable for the former but not for the latter. The use of the Good-Turing estimator to connect factoid frequency in training data to hallucination rates is novel in the context of language model analysis. The results offer theoretical guidance for designing post-training procedures and highlight the limitations of pretraining in addressing hallucinations for certain types of facts.

14640831f152dcf93b61ae364ef5e8ad8ffe8a4a.title: Time-Embedded Algorithm Unrolling for Computational MRI
14640831f152dcf93b61ae364ef5e8ad8ffe8a4a.research_question: How can the performance and generalization of algorithm unrolling methods for computational MRI be improved, particularly in data-limited regimes, while avoiding overfitting and excessive parameter growth?
14640831f152dcf93b61ae364ef5e8ad8ffe8a4a.hypothesis: Incorporating time-embedding into both the proximal operator and data fidelity steps of algorithm unrolling frameworks will enable iteration-dependent adaptation, leading to improved reconstruction quality, reduced artifacts, and better generalization in limited data settings, without significantly increasing the number of learnable parameters.
14640831f152dcf93b61ae364ef5e8ad8ffe8a4a.proposed_method: A novel time-embedded algorithm unrolling framework is proposed for solving inverse problems in computational MRI. The approach introduces time-embedding into the neural network-based proximal operator, allowing the regularizer to adapt dynamically at each unrolling iteration. Sinusoidal encodings of the iteration index are processed through learned functions and integrated into the network using feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM) and group normalization, modulating the network's behavior over time. Additionally, the data fidelity weights and Onsager correction terms are parameterized as time-dependent learnable scalars, enabling the model to adjust its fidelity and correction strategies at each step. The framework is compatible with various optimization algorithms (e.g., VSQP, ADMM) and neural network architectures (e.g., U-Net, ResNet), and can be extended to other unrolling-based inverse problem solvers.
14640831f152dcf93b61ae364ef5e8ad8ffe8a4a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the NYU fastMRI dataset, including coronal proton density (PD), PD with fat suppression (PD-FS), and axial T2-weighted brain MRI scans. Datasets will be retrospectively undersampled using both uniform (equispaced) and random sampling masks at acceleration rates of R=4, 6, and 8. Training will use 300 slices from 10 subjects, with testing on 380 slices from separate subjects for knee data, and 300 slices each for brain data. The proposed method will be compared against standard algorithm unrolling baselines (VSQP and ADMM) with both shared and unshared proximal operator weights, using matched network architectures (U-Net and ResNet) and training protocols. Evaluation metrics will include PSNR and SSIM for quantitative assessment, as well as qualitative expert radiologist review for artifact and sharpness evaluation. Ablation studies will analyze the effect of the number of unrolls, parameter count, and time-embedding hyperparameters. Additional comparisons will be made to diffusion-based MRI reconstruction models.
14640831f152dcf93b61ae364ef5e8ad8ffe8a4a.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to explicitly incorporate time-embedding into both the proximal operator and data fidelity steps of algorithm unrolling for MRI, inspired by VAMP and diffusion models. It enables iteration-dependent adaptation without requiring a separate network for each unroll, thus minimizing parameter growth and overfitting risk. The method generalizes across different unrolling algorithms and network architectures, and demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in artifact reduction and image sharpness, especially in limited data regimes. The approach also extends to existing unrolling frameworks, improving reconstruction quality with minimal computational overhead.

14683cef8489618e2ad1c3280272aea3d23f2f74.title: Action Sensitivity Learning for Temporal Action Localization
14683cef8489618e2ad1c3280272aea3d23f2f74.research_question: How can temporal action localization in videos be improved by accounting for the varying importance of individual frames for both action classification and localization tasks across diverse video scenarios?
14683cef8489618e2ad1c3280272aea3d23f2f74.hypothesis: Modeling and leveraging frame-level action sensitivity, disentangled for classification and localization sub-tasks, and incorporating this sensitivity into both training and feature enhancement will improve the accuracy and robustness of temporal action localization.
14683cef8489618e2ad1c3280272aea3d23f2f74.proposed_method: A novel Action Sensitivity Learning (ASL) framework will be developed for temporal action localization. The approach will begin by extracting video features using a pre-trained 3D-CNN, followed by a feature encoder that utilizes a transformer-based architecture with parallel temporal and channel attention mechanisms. An Action Sensitivity Evaluator (ASE) module will be introduced to assess the importance (sensitivity) of each frame for both classification and localization, using a combination of class-level (via learnable Gaussian-like weights) and instance-level (via temporal convolution and quality supervision) modeling. These sensitivities will be used to dynamically reweight training losses for each frame, ensuring that more informative frames contribute more to learning. Additionally, an Action Sensitive Contrastive Loss (ASCL) will be designed to enhance feature discrimination by contrasting sensitive frames for classification and localization, as well as distinguishing between actions and backgrounds.
14683cef8489618e2ad1c3280272aea3d23f2f74.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six benchmark datasets representing densely-labeled, egocentric, and single-labeled video scenarios: MultiThumos, Charades, Ego4D-MomentQueries v1.0, Epic-Kitchens 100, Thumos14, and ActivityNet1.3. Pre-extracted features (e.g., I3D, EgoVLP, Slowfast, Omnivore) will be used as inputs. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines including both two-stage and one-stage temporal action localization methods. Evaluation will be performed using mean Average Precision (mAP) at multiple temporal Intersection-over-Union (tIoU) thresholds, with average mAP over specified tIoU ranges as the main metric. Ablation studies will be conducted to assess the impact of class-level and instance-level sensitivity modeling, the contrastive loss, and the number and type of Gaussian weights. Hyperparameters such as the weight of the contrastive loss and the sampling ratio for sensitive frames will also be tuned.
14683cef8489618e2ad1c3280272aea3d23f2f74.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a lightweight, dual-level Action Sensitivity Evaluator that models frame importance separately for classification and localization, combining class-level (learnable, category-aware Gaussian weights) and instance-level (prediction-aware) sensitivity. The method dynamically reweights training based on frame sensitivity, improving both efficiency and effectiveness. A novel Action Sensitive Contrastive Loss is designed to enhance feature discrimination and mitigate misalignment between classification and localization sub-tasks. The approach is applicable across various types of temporal action localization scenarios, including densely-labeled, egocentric, and single-labeled datasets, and demonstrates superior performance over existing state-of-the-art methods.

14699ddf1297c33bed77524ee823b20c831a05bd.title: MVMoE: Multi-Task Vehicle Routing Solver with Mixture-of-Experts
14699ddf1297c33bed77524ee823b20c831a05bd.research_question: How can a unified neural solver be developed to efficiently and effectively solve a wide range of vehicle routing problem (VRP) variants, including previously unseen combinations of constraints, while maintaining strong generalization and computational efficiency?
14699ddf1297c33bed77524ee823b20c831a05bd.hypothesis: A multi-task neural solver based on a mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture, equipped with a hierarchical gating mechanism, can achieve superior zero-shot and few-shot generalization across diverse VRP variants, outperforming existing neural and traditional baselines in both empirical performance and computational efficiency.
14699ddf1297c33bed77524ee823b20c831a05bd.proposed_method: A multi-task vehicle routing solver is proposed, leveraging a mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture within both the encoder and decoder of an attention-based neural network. The method incorporates a unified set of static and dynamic features that encompass all relevant attributes across VRP variants, enabling the model to learn shared representations. Each MoE layer consists of multiple independent experts (e.g., feed-forward networks), and a gating network determines which experts are activated for each input, employing node-level and hierarchical gating strategies. The hierarchical gating mechanism selectively routes inputs to either a sparse MoE layer or a dense layer based on problem-level representations, balancing computational cost and empirical performance. Training is conducted in a multi-task fashion, where each batch samples a different VRP variant, and the model is optimized using reinforcement learning with an auxiliary loss to encourage balanced expert utilization.
14699ddf1297c33bed77524ee823b20c831a05bd.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on 16 VRP variants, generated by combining five practical constraints, with training and evaluation on problem sizes n = 50 and n = 100. The solver is compared against traditional solvers (HGS, LKH3, OR-Tools) and neural baselines (POMO, POMO-MTL), using metrics such as objective value, optimality gap, and computational time. Zero-shot generalization is assessed on 10 previously unseen VRP variants, while few-shot generalization is evaluated by fine-tuning on a small set of new instances. Additional ablations investigate the impact of MoE configurations (number of experts, gating mechanisms, layer positions), and out-of-distribution generalization is tested on real-world benchmark datasets (e.g., CVRPLIB). Training utilizes reinforcement learning (REINFORCE), with greedy rollout and instance augmentation for inference, and experiments are run on high-performance GPU hardware.
14699ddf1297c33bed77524ee823b20c831a05bd.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to introduce mixture-of-experts architectures to combinatorial optimization problems in the context of vehicle routing, enabling a single neural solver to handle multiple VRP variants concurrently. The hierarchical gating mechanism is novel in this domain, providing an effective trade-off between empirical performance and computational complexity. The method demonstrates strong zero-shot and few-shot generalization to unseen VRP variants, outperforming both multi-task and single-task neural baselines, and achieves competitive results on real-world benchmarks. Extensive ablation studies offer new insights into the application of MoEs for combinatorial optimization, including the impact of gating strategies and expert configurations.

146e9e1238ff6caf18f0bd936ffcfbe1e65d2afd.title: Data Distributional Properties Drive Emergent In-Context Learning in Transformers
146e9e1238ff6caf18f0bd936ffcfbe1e65d2afd.research_question: What distributional properties of training data and model architectures drive the emergence of in-context few-shot learning in large transformer-based models, and how can these properties be manipulated to promote both in-context and in-weights learning in domains beyond language?
146e9e1238ff6caf18f0bd936ffcfbe1e65d2afd.hypothesis: In-context learning in transformers emerges when the training data exhibits certain distributional properties, such as burstiness, a large number of rarely occurring classes, and dynamic item meanings. Furthermore, a skewed (Zipfian) class distribution enables the co-existence of in-context and in-weights learning within a single model, and these effects are architecture-dependent.
146e9e1238ff6caf18f0bd936ffcfbe1e65d2afd.proposed_method: A comprehensive experimental framework will be developed to systematically manipulate the distributional properties of training data and assess their effects on in-context learning in neural sequence models. Training sequences will be constructed using the Omniglot dataset, with controlled variations in burstiness (the clustering of item occurrences), the number and rarity of classes, label multiplicity (dynamic meanings), and within-class variation. Both transformer and recurrent architectures (RNNs, LSTMs) will be trained on these sequences, with image and label tokens embedded via a ResNet and standard embedding layers, respectively, and processed through a causal transformer or recurrent network. The training objective will be to minimize softmax cross-entropy loss on predicting the label of a query image following a context of image-label pairs. Additionally, the marginal distribution over classes will be varied from uniform to Zipfian to test the emergence and coexistence of in-context and in-weights learning.
146e9e1238ff6caf18f0bd936ffcfbe1e65d2afd.experiment_details: Experiments will use the Omniglot dataset, which contains 1623 character classes with 20 handwritten examples per class, and will be augmented via rotations and flips to increase the number of classes up to 12,800. Training data will consist of sequences of 8 image-label pairs (context) followed by a query image, with systematic variation in burstiness, class rarity, label multiplicity, and within-class variation (including Gaussian noise and exemplar diversity). Evaluation will be performed on two types of sequences: (1) few-shot in-context learning on holdout classes with randomly assigned labels, and (2) in-weights learning on trained classes with fixed labels but no context support. Baselines will include both transformer and recurrent architectures, matched for number of parameters and depth. Performance will be measured by classification accuracy on the query image, with chance levels computed based on the number of possible labels. Additional experiments will vary the Zipf exponent of the class distribution to identify conditions under which both learning modes co-exist.
146e9e1238ff6caf18f0bd936ffcfbe1e65d2afd.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a systematic investigation of how naturalistic data properties—such as burstiness, class rarity, dynamic meanings, and Zipfian distributions—drive the emergence of in-context learning in transformers, distinguishing these effects from those of model architecture. The approach demonstrates that in-context learning is not solely a product of transformer architecture but critically depends on specific data distributions, and it identifies conditions under which both in-context and in-weights learning can co-exist. This work provides actionable insights for designing datasets and training regimes to induce rapid adaptation capabilities in models across domains, and offers a new perspective on the interplay between data structure and neural network learning dynamics.

146efd9ed4ce53d9da48d302f95a8f597bc22b8b.title: SwitchTab: Switched Autoencoders Are Effective Tabular Learners
146efd9ed4ce53d9da48d302f95a8f597bc22b8b.research_question: How can self-supervised representation learning methods be adapted to effectively capture latent dependencies and improve downstream performance on tabular data, which lacks explicit spatial or semantic dependencies found in other domains?
146efd9ed4ce53d9da48d302f95a8f597bc22b8b.hypothesis: Introducing a self-supervised framework that explicitly decouples mutual and salient features among tabular data samples will yield more representative embeddings, leading to improved performance in downstream tasks and enhanced explainability.
146efd9ed4ce53d9da48d302f95a8f597bc22b8b.proposed_method: A novel self-supervised learning framework, SwitchTab, is proposed for tabular data. The method employs an asymmetric encoder-decoder architecture, where each data sample is first corrupted and then encoded into a general embedding. Two separate projectors are used to decouple the embedding into mutual (shared) and salient (distinctive) feature vectors. During decoding, a switching mechanism swaps mutual and salient features between pairs of samples, enforcing the encoder to learn structured and disentangled representations. The model is trained to reconstruct both the original and switched data samples, optimizing a loss that combines mean squared error for reconstruction and, when labels are available, a classification or regression loss. The salient embeddings can also be extracted and used as plug-and-play features for traditional machine learning models.
146efd9ed4ce53d9da48d302f95a8f597bc22b8b.experiment_details: Comprehensive experiments will be conducted on a wide range of tabular datasets, including standard benchmarks (e.g., California Housing, Adult, Higgs, ALOI, Epsilon, Year, Covertype, Yahoo, Microsoft, Helena, Jannis) and additional public datasets (e.g., Bank, Blastchar, Arrhythmia, Arcene, Shoppers, Volkert, MNIST). Datasets will be preprocessed using backward difference encoding for categorical features, mean/mode imputation for missing values, and min-max scaling. The encoder will be a three-layer transformer, with linear projectors and a simple decoder. Baselines will include traditional models (Logistic Regression, XGBoost, Random Forest, LightGBM, CatBoost) and deep learning methods (MLP, TabNet, NODE, ResNet, FT-Transformer, TabTransformer, SAINT, VIME, ReConTab). Evaluation metrics will be accuracy for classification and RMSE for regression, with results averaged over multiple seeds. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the switching mechanism and feature corruption ratio. Plug-and-play experiments will test the utility of salient features as additional inputs to traditional models.
146efd9ed4ce53d9da48d302f95a8f597bc22b8b.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to explicitly decouple and organize mutual and salient embeddings for tabular data using a switching autoencoder framework. The approach introduces a novel switching mechanism in the latent space, enabling the extraction of structured, explainable representations. The method demonstrates versatility by supporting both self-supervised and supervised pre-training, and by providing salient embeddings that can enhance traditional models as plug-and-play features. Visualization of the learned embeddings further highlights the model's explainability and the clear separation of mutual and salient information.

14d52d4ec14eba80c267e39f2b28442c726046c0.title: SizeShiftReg: a Regularization Method for Improving Size-Generalization in Graph Neural Networks
14d52d4ec14eba80c267e39f2b28442c726046c0.research_question: How can the generalization ability of graph neural networks (GNNs) be improved when classifying graphs whose sizes differ significantly from those seen during training, particularly when only training data is available and no assumptions about the generative process or access to test data are possible?
14d52d4ec14eba80c267e39f2b28442c726046c0.hypothesis: A regularization strategy that simulates size shifts in training graphs and enforces robustness to these shifts will improve the size-generalization performance of GNNs, enabling them to better classify larger graphs after being trained on smaller ones.
14d52d4ec14eba80c267e39f2b28442c726046c0.proposed_method: A model-agnostic regularization framework is developed that can be applied to any GNN architecture. The method simulates size shifts in the training data by applying graph coarsening techniques to generate smaller versions of each training graph at various coarsening ratios. For each original graph and its coarsened versions, node embeddings are computed using the GNN. The regularization loss is defined as the Central Moment Discrepancy (CMD) between the distributions of node embeddings from the original and coarsened graphs, encouraging the GNN to produce similar representations regardless of graph size. The total training loss combines the standard supervised loss (e.g., cross-entropy) with the regularization loss, weighted by a tunable coefficient. Coarsened graphs are precomputed for efficiency, and the approach is compatible with any existing coarsening method and GNN model.
14d52d4ec14eba80c267e39f2b28442c726046c0.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on standard benchmark datasets from the TUDataset library (NCI1, NCI109, PROTEINS, DD) and the Deezer social network dataset. The evaluation protocol splits the data such that models are trained on the 50% smallest graphs and tested on the 10% largest graphs, with the test graphs being 3-9 times larger on average than the training graphs. Baselines include standard GNNs (GCN, GIN, PNA), more expressive models (RPGNN), graph kernels (WL, GC), and methods using invariant risk minimization (IRM) and E-invariant models. Performance is measured using Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) due to class imbalance. Hyperparameters for the regularization coefficient and coarsening ratios are tuned on a validation set for one model/dataset and then fixed for all others to demonstrate robustness. Results are averaged over 50 runs to account for variance.
14d52d4ec14eba80c267e39f2b28442c726046c0.novelty_claims: The proposed regularization strategy is model-agnostic and can be applied to any GNN without requiring access to test data or assumptions about the data's generative process. Unlike prior approaches, it does not require domain-specific inductive biases or additional computation at inference time. The method leverages graph coarsening and CMD-based regularization to directly address size-shift robustness, leading to significant improvements (up to 30%) in size-generalization performance across multiple datasets and outperforming or matching more complex or domain-specific models. The approach is robust to the choice of coarsening method and hyperparameters, and requires no additional test-time computation.

14e8c201e42e8372def8919fa104ff835556e58c.title: Model-Based Imitation Learning for Urban Driving
14e8c201e42e8372def8919fa104ff835556e58c.research_question: How can a model-based imitation learning framework be developed to jointly learn a world model and a driving policy for autonomous urban driving, using only high-dimensional camera observations and expert demonstrations, without requiring online interaction or access to reward signals?
14e8c201e42e8372def8919fa104ff835556e58c.hypothesis: A model-based imitation learning approach that leverages 3D geometric inductive biases and learns a compact latent space from high-resolution visual expert demonstrations can enable accurate, robust, and generalizable autonomous driving policies in complex urban environments, outperforming existing methods even without access to privileged information or online interaction.
14e8c201e42e8372def8919fa104ff835556e58c.proposed_method: A novel model-based imitation learning architecture is proposed that jointly learns a probabilistic world model and an action policy using only offline expert demonstrations from urban driving. The approach encodes high-resolution camera images by first lifting features to 3D using predicted depth distributions and camera parameters, then pooling them into a bird’s-eye view (BeV) representation, which is further compressed to a low-dimensional latent vector. The latent dynamics are modeled with a recurrent neural network (gated recurrent cell) and parameterized Gaussian transitions, conditioned on both past latent states and predicted actions. The model is trained via deep variational inference, matching prior and posterior distributions over latent states, and is supervised by reconstructing observations, BeV semantic segmentations, and expert actions. The policy is learned directly from the latent state, and the model is capable of generating diverse future trajectories by iteratively predicting latent states and actions in imagination mode.
14e8c201e42e8372def8919fa104ff835556e58c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the CARLA urban driving simulator, with training data collected from four towns and four weather conditions, totaling 2.9 million frames (32 hours) of expert driving. The model will be evaluated in a previously unseen town and weather conditions, using standard CARLA challenge metrics: driving score, route completion, infraction penalty, cumulative reward, and normalized reward. Baselines will include state-of-the-art camera-only and LiDAR-based approaches such as CILRS, LBC, TransFuser, Roach, and LAV, with public pre-trained weights. Ablation studies will assess the impact of 3D geometric encoding, probabilistic modeling, and latent state dimensionality. Additional experiments will evaluate the model’s ability to plan and drive in imagination mode, as well as its computational efficiency in recurrent deployment.
14e8c201e42e8372def8919fa104ff835556e58c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first camera-only model-based imitation learning method that jointly models static scene, dynamic scene, and ego-agent behavior in urban driving environments. It introduces a scalable architecture that leverages 3D geometry as an inductive bias, enabling high-fidelity latent dynamics modeling from high-resolution images. The method achieves state-of-the-art driving performance in the CARLA simulator, surpassing even LiDAR-based approaches, and demonstrates the ability to predict diverse, plausible futures and execute complex maneuvers from imagined plans. The framework operates entirely offline, requiring no online environment interaction or reward access, and provides interpretable predictions through BeV semantic segmentation.

14e8cf5a5e6a7b35e618b08f5cf06f572b3a54e0.title: Tree of Attacks: Jailbreaking Black-Box LLMs Automatically
14e8cf5a5e6a7b35e618b08f5cf06f572b3a54e0.research_question: How can automated, black-box, and interpretable methods be developed to efficiently and effectively generate jailbreak prompts that bypass the safety and alignment mechanisms of state-of-the-art large language models (LLMs)?
14e8cf5a5e6a7b35e618b08f5cf06f572b3a54e0.hypothesis: Incorporating branching and pruning strategies within an automated, black-box prompt generation framework will significantly improve the success rate and query efficiency of jailbreaking attacks on LLMs, even in the presence of advanced guardrails.
14e8cf5a5e6a7b35e618b08f5cf06f572b3a54e0.proposed_method: A novel framework, Tree of Attacks with Pruning (TAP), will be developed to automate the generation of jailbreak prompts for black-box LLMs. TAP is initialized with two auxiliary LLMs: an attacker LLM that generates multiple candidate prompt variations and an evaluator LLM that assesses and prunes these candidates based on their likelihood to elicit undesired information from the target model. The process iteratively branches by generating several prompt refinements at each step, prunes off-topic or low-potential prompts in two phases, and queries the target LLM with the most promising candidates. The evaluator further scores the responses to determine jailbreak success, and the process continues until a jailbreak is found or a maximum number of iterations is reached. Key parameters such as branching factor, tree width, and depth are tuned to balance success rate and query efficiency.
14e8cf5a5e6a7b35e618b08f5cf06f572b3a54e0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two datasets: the AdvBench Subset (50 harmful prompts across 32 categories) and a newly constructed dataset of 123 harmful requests generated via WizardVicuna30B-Uncensored. TAP will be compared to state-of-the-art baselines, including the Prompt Automatic Iterative Refinement (PAIR) method for black-box attacks and GCG for white-box attacks. Target LLMs will include Vicuna-13B-v1.5, Llama-2-Chat-7B, GPT3.5-Turbo, GPT4, GPT4-Turbo, GPT4o, PaLM-2, Gemini-Pro, and Claude3 Opus, with some experiments also evaluating models protected by LlamaGuard. Evaluation metrics will include the fraction of prompts successfully jailbreaking the target (using both automated GPT4-based and human-judged criteria), as well as the number of queries required per prompt. Hyperparameters such as branching factor, tree width, and depth will be carefully controlled to ensure fair comparisons.
14e8cf5a5e6a7b35e618b08f5cf06f572b3a54e0.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a fully automated, black-box, and interpretable attack framework that leverages both branching and pruning strategies to achieve significantly higher jailbreak success rates and improved query efficiency compared to prior methods. TAP is capable of jailbreaking state-of-the-art LLMs, including those protected by advanced guardrails, and generates prompts with natural language meaning, making them harder to detect. The method generalizes and enhances previous iterative refinement frameworks by introducing tree-based exploration and selective pruning, and demonstrates transferability of generated jailbreaks across different LLMs.

14e8f3c72fc07b793fe18c2e116d84ee4a83ff6e.title: Distilling a Powerful Student Model via Online Knowledge Distillation
14e8f3c72fc07b793fe18c2e116d84ee4a83ff6e.research_question: How can online knowledge distillation be improved to produce a single, high-performing student model without relying on cumbersome teacher models or increasing deployment costs, while maximizing the use of information available from multiple collaboratively trained student models?
14e8f3c72fc07b793fe18c2e116d84ee4a83ff6e.hypothesis: Integrating feature fusion and self-distillation modules into an online knowledge distillation framework will enable a leader student model to absorb richer and more diverse knowledge from peer students, resulting in superior generalization and accuracy compared to existing online and traditional knowledge distillation methods.
14e8f3c72fc07b793fe18c2e116d84ee4a83ff6e.proposed_method: A novel online knowledge distillation framework is developed, termed FFSD, which introduces two main components: feature fusion and self-distillation. Multiple student models with identical architectures are trained collaboratively, with a designated leader student and a set of common students. The feature fusion module, inspired by an autoencoder, concatenates and encodes the last-layer feature maps of all common students into a compact representation, which is then distilled into the leader student via supervised learning. To enhance the diversity of the common students, a diversity enhancement strategy is applied by shifting attention in feature maps, ensuring that the fused representation contains richer information. Additionally, a self-distillation module is designed to map high-order supervision information (from deeper layers and fused features) to lower-order cues for shallower layers, promoting attention consistency and improved generalization. After training, only the leader student is retained for deployment, eliminating the need for ensemble inference or teacher models.
14e8f3c72fc07b793fe18c2e116d84ee4a83ff6e.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the CIFAR-100 and ImageNet datasets, using a variety of network architectures including ResNet, WideResNet, GoogLeNet, and DenseNet. The proposed method is compared against strong baselines such as traditional knowledge distillation (KD, AT), mutual learning (DML, AMLN), ensemble-based online distillation (ONE, FFL, KDCL, OKDDip), and other state-of-the-art online distillation techniques. Evaluation metrics include top-1 classification accuracy, with additional analysis of feature diversity (e.g., cosine similarity of feature maps), and ablation studies on the impact of feature fusion, diversity enhancement, and self-distillation modules. Training time and computational overhead are also measured. Hyperparameters are tuned via grid search, and all experiments are repeated multiple times to report mean and standard deviation.
14e8f3c72fc07b793fe18c2e116d84ee4a83ff6e.novelty_claims: The proposed FFSD framework is the first to combine feature fusion and self-distillation in an online knowledge distillation setting, enabling a single leader student to integrate the collective knowledge of multiple peers without increasing inference costs. The method introduces a novel diversity enhancement strategy to ensure richer, non-redundant feature representations among students, and a self-distillation module that addresses attention inconsistency across network layers. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FFSD achieves superior accuracy and generalization compared to both traditional and online distillation methods, with lower deployment overhead.

14ef3ca91d73b404e476df81b8b1877528fde73c.title: Radar: Fast Long-Context Decoding for Any Transformer
14ef3ca91d73b404e476df81b8b1877528fde73c.research_question: How can inference for pre-trained Transformer models be accelerated for long-context data without sacrificing generation quality or requiring retraining, while maintaining efficient use of context information?
14ef3ca91d73b404e476df81b8b1877528fde73c.hypothesis: A training-free, dynamic context selection approach can significantly reduce the inference time complexity for any pre-trained Transformer model on long-context tasks, while preserving or improving generation quality compared to existing context reduction and efficient attention methods.
14ef3ca91d73b404e476df81b8b1877528fde73c.proposed_method: A novel, training-free framework named Radar is developed to accelerate long-context decoding for any pre-trained Transformer. The method organizes context tokens into hierarchical segments, where each segment is represented by a 'summarization representation' constructed via random feature projections (attention kernelization). During inference, for each query token, Radar computes the importance of each segment by calculating the inner product between the query's random feature and the segment's averaged random features. Only tokens from the top-k most important segments are selected for attention computation, reducing the number of tokens processed at each step. A dynamic restructuring schedule is introduced to adaptively adjust segment sizes as context grows, ensuring amortized sub-quadratic time complexity. Theoretical analysis guarantees that, with high probability, the most important tokens are selected, and the overall time complexity is reduced to O(t^1.5) for generating t tokens.
14ef3ca91d73b404e476df81b8b1877528fde73c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of long-context tasks and benchmarks, including language modeling (PG-19 dataset), code generation (The Stack), and the LongBench benchmark suite covering single-doc QA, multi-doc QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic, and code tasks. Pre-trained models such as Llama-7b, Llama-2-7b-chat-hf, and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 will be evaluated. Baselines will include vanilla dot-product attention, StreamingLLM, Landmark attention, H2O, SnapKV, and SubGen. Evaluation metrics will include perplexity, ROUGE scores, accuracy, and average percentile rankings across tasks. Experiments will be run on A100 GPUs, and ablation studies will be performed to analyze the effects of hyperparameters and segment selection strategies.
14ef3ca91d73b404e476df81b8b1877528fde73c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is training-free and compatible with any pre-trained Transformer, requiring no model modification or retraining. Unlike prior methods that heuristically evict tokens or require specialized architectures, this method dynamically selects context segments based on principled importance estimation using random feature projections. Theoretical guarantees are provided for the correctness and reliability of segment selection. The method achieves state-of-the-art performance on long-context benchmarks with significantly reduced inference time complexity, offering a practical and general solution for efficient long-context processing in Transformers.

14f2e7a63cf43c41e7dc6a4a527243422d5e3c36.title: Simple Hierarchical Planning with Diffusion
14f2e7a63cf43c41e7dc6a4a527243422d5e3c36.research_question: How can hierarchical planning be effectively integrated with diffusion-based generative models to improve efficiency, generalization, and performance in long-horizon and offline reinforcement learning tasks?
14f2e7a63cf43c41e7dc6a4a527243422d5e3c36.hypothesis: Incorporating a hierarchical structure into diffusion-based planning, where high-level 'jumpy' subgoals are generated and refined by a low-level planner, will improve planning efficiency, generalization to out-of-distribution tasks, and overall performance compared to flat diffusion-based or traditional hierarchical methods.
14f2e7a63cf43c41e7dc6a4a527243422d5e3c36.proposed_method: A novel hierarchical planning framework, termed Hierarchical Diffuser, is proposed that leverages two diffusion models: a high-level diffusion model for generating temporally sparse subgoals and a low-level diffusion model for planning actions between subgoals. Training involves splitting each trajectory into equal-length segments, treating segment boundaries as subgoals, and training both diffusion models in parallel. The high-level planner operates on subsampled trajectories (every K-th state) to generate subgoals with a larger receptive field and lower computational cost, while the low-level planner models dense trajectory segments to achieve fine-grained control. At test time, the high-level model first generates a sequence of subgoals, and the low-level model plans the detailed actions to transition between these subgoals, with all segments generated in parallel. An optional enhancement incorporates dense actions in the high-level planner's input to improve return prediction accuracy.
14f2e7a63cf43c41e7dc6a4a527243422d5e3c36.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard offline reinforcement learning benchmarks, including D4RL Maze2D, Multi2D, AntMaze, Gym-MuJoCo, and FrankaKitchen datasets. The proposed method will be compared against flat learning methods (e.g., MPPI, IQL, Diffuser), hierarchical learning methods (e.g., IRIS, HiGoC, HDMI), and other state-of-the-art model-free and model-based baselines (e.g., BC, BCQ, BEAR, CQL, Decision Transformer, MoReL, Trajectory Transformer, RvS-G). Evaluation metrics include average task return, success rate, cosine similarity, and mean squared error (MSE) for compositional out-of-distribution tasks. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of kernel size, subgoal interval K, and the inclusion of dense actions. Computational efficiency will be measured by wall-clock training and planning times.
14f2e7a63cf43c41e7dc6a4a527243422d5e3c36.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple yet effective hierarchical diffusion-based planning framework that enables efficient and scalable planning for long-horizon tasks. Key innovations include the use of a 'jumpy' high-level diffusion model for subgoal generation, parallel training and inference of high- and low-level planners, and the integration of dense actions to improve value prediction. The approach achieves superior performance and efficiency compared to both flat and hierarchical baselines, demonstrates enhanced generalization to compositional out-of-distribution tasks, and provides theoretical analysis of the generalization-performance tradeoff. The method also offers significant speedups in training and planning due to its hierarchical structure.

14fdab35cc6288083a38a92392af3f1da0b95a90.title: KAN: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
14fdab35cc6288083a38a92392af3f1da0b95a90.research_question: Can a new neural network architecture, inspired by the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem and featuring learnable activation functions on edges instead of fixed activations on nodes, serve as a more accurate and interpretable alternative to traditional Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) for function approximation and scientific discovery tasks?
14fdab35cc6288083a38a92392af3f1da0b95a90.hypothesis: Replacing fixed activation functions on nodes with learnable, spline-parametrized activation functions on edges in a fully-connected neural network will yield models that are both more accurate and more interpretable than standard MLPs, particularly for tasks with compositional structure and in scientific domains.
14fdab35cc6288083a38a92392af3f1da0b95a90.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs), which are fully-connected neural networks where each edge is associated with a learnable univariate activation function, parameterized as a B-spline. Unlike MLPs, KANs have no linear weights; instead, each connection between nodes is a non-linear function that can be adapted during training. The architecture allows for arbitrary depth and width, generalizing the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation to modern deep learning settings. Each KAN layer is a matrix of univariate spline functions, and the network output is obtained by composing these layers. Training is performed using backpropagation, and special techniques are introduced for initialization, residual connections (using silu as a basis), and dynamic grid extension to refine spline resolution as training progresses. Interpretability is enhanced by network simplification and pruning methods.
