14fdab35cc6288083a38a92392af3f1da0b95a90.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on small-scale AI and scientific tasks, including synthetic function fitting (e.g., functions with compositional structure such as f(x, y) = exp(sin(πx) + y^2)), partial differential equation (PDE) solving (e.g., Poisson equation), and scientific discovery tasks in mathematics and physics (e.g., knot theory, Anderson localization). KANs will be compared against standard MLPs of varying sizes, with baselines matched for parameter count where possible. Evaluation metrics will include training and test root mean squared error (RMSE), scaling laws (test loss vs. parameter count), and qualitative interpretability assessments. Grid extension experiments will be used to study the effect of spline resolution on accuracy and generalization. Training dynamics, interpolation thresholds, and scaling exponents will be analyzed to assess the efficiency and expressiveness of KANs relative to MLPs.
14fdab35cc6288083a38a92392af3f1da0b95a90.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a fundamentally new neural network architecture that places learnable, spline-based activation functions on edges rather than fixed activations on nodes, eliminating the need for linear weights. This design enables KANs to learn both compositional structure and univariate function details, resulting in superior accuracy and interpretability compared to MLPs. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that KANs can overcome the curse of dimensionality for functions with compositional structure, achieving faster neural scaling laws. Practical techniques for grid extension and network simplification further enhance accuracy and interpretability, making KANs promising alternatives for scientific machine learning and symbolic discovery.

151fb7efaf53ff01abd00d06a64d05a71b20ed68.title: Wan-Move: Motion-controllable Video Generation via Latent Trajectory Guidance
151fb7efaf53ff01abd00d06a64d05a71b20ed68.research_question: How can precise and scalable motion control be achieved in image-to-video generation models, enabling fine-grained and high-quality manipulation of object and camera motion in generated videos?
151fb7efaf53ff01abd00d06a64d05a71b20ed68.hypothesis: Injecting motion guidance directly into the latent condition features of an image-to-video generation model, using dense point trajectories mapped into latent space, will enable precise, high-fidelity, and scalable motion control without requiring auxiliary motion encoders or architectural modifications.
151fb7efaf53ff01abd00d06a64d05a71b20ed68.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed that represents object and camera motions using dense point trajectories, allowing for fine-grained control over scene dynamics. These trajectories are spatially mapped from pixel space into the latent space of a pretrained VAE, aligning with the latent representations used by the image-to-video (I2V) backbone. The first-frame latent features are then replicated along each trajectory across subsequent frames, producing a spatiotemporal feature map that encodes both appearance and motion. This updated latent condition is concatenated with the latent noise and injected into the I2V diffusion model (e.g., Wan-I2V-14B) as motion guidance, requiring no changes to the model architecture. The approach supports both single- and multi-object motion, as well as complex camera movements, and is compatible with scalable fine-tuning.
151fb7efaf53ff01abd00d06a64d05a71b20ed68.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using a large-scale, high-quality dataset of 2 million 720p videos, filtered for visual and motion consistency. The method is evaluated on the newly introduced MoveBench benchmark, which contains 1,018 videos (480x832 resolution, 5 seconds each) with rich, hybrid-verified motion annotations (point trajectories and masks) across 54 content categories, as well as on public datasets such as DAVIS. Baselines include state-of-the-art academic and commercial motion-controllable video generation methods (e.g., ImageConductor, LeviTor, Tora, MagicMotion, Kling1.5Pro). Evaluation metrics include FID, FVD, PSNR, SSIM for visual quality, and end-point error (EPE) for motion accuracy. Both quantitative and qualitative comparisons are performed, including ablation studies on motion guidance strategies, condition fusion, and the number of point trajectories. Human studies (2AFC) are conducted to assess motion and visual quality.
151fb7efaf53ff01abd00d06a64d05a71b20ed68.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple yet effective approach for motion control in video generation by directly editing latent condition features, eliminating the need for auxiliary motion encoders or fusion modules. It enables scalable fine-tuning and seamless integration with existing I2V backbones. The framework supports diverse and complex motion control tasks, including multi-object and camera motion, with high fidelity and precision. A comprehensive benchmark, MoveBench, is also introduced, providing a rigorous evaluation platform with detailed motion annotations and diverse scenarios. The method achieves state-of-the-art results in both motion accuracy and video quality, rivaling commercial solutions while remaining open-source.

152e7ff98ad99ba07bfe773f319076e23b715805.title: A Theoretical Analysis of the Learning Dynamics under Class Imbalance
152e7ff98ad99ba07bfe773f319076e23b715805.research_question: How does class imbalance affect the learning dynamics of gradient-based optimization algorithms in supervised classification, and can modifications to these algorithms guarantee improved convergence and per-class performance under imbalance?
152e7ff98ad99ba07bfe773f319076e23b715805.hypothesis: Class imbalance leads to suboptimal learning dynamics for minority classes in gradient-based optimization, but per-class normalization of gradients can mitigate these effects and improve both convergence and per-class loss behavior. However, in stochastic settings, additional factors such as directional noise must be addressed for effective mitigation.
152e7ff98ad99ba07bfe773f319076e23b715805.proposed_method: A theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted into the learning dynamics of gradient-based optimization algorithms, specifically gradient descent (GD) and stochastic gradient descent (SGD), under class imbalance. The approach will involve analyzing the per-class loss trajectories and the conditions under which these losses decrease monotonically. A novel algorithm, per-class-normalized gradient descent (PCNGD), will be developed, which normalizes the contribution of each class's gradient to ensure equal magnitude in updates, thereby relaxing restrictive conditions on gradient angles and mitigating the minority initial drop (MID). For stochastic settings, the study will extend to per-class-normalized SGD (PCNSGD) and introduce further corrections to address directional noise, including rescaling based on the projection of stochastic gradients onto full-batch gradients and the use of oversampling strategies to balance both gradient norms and directions.
152e7ff98ad99ba07bfe773f319076e23b715805.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using several neural network architectures (e.g., Mod1, Mod2, Mod3) and a variety of imbalanced binary and multiclass datasets (such as Bi7a, Bi7b, Bi60, Mul10, Mul100). Both training and balanced test sets will be used to evaluate the methods. Baseline algorithms will include standard GD, SGD, and their per-class normalized variants, as well as combinations with oversampling. Evaluation metrics will focus on per-class loss, recall, and overall performance, with particular attention to the presence or absence of the minority initial drop (MID) and the rate of convergence for each class. The experimental setup will include varying imbalance ratios, batch sizes, and step sizes to systematically assess the impact of the proposed methods.
152e7ff98ad99ba07bfe773f319076e23b715805.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretical framework for understanding the impact of class imbalance on the convergence of gradient-based learning algorithms, providing formal convergence guarantees for both GD and SGD under imbalance. The per-class normalization approach (PCNGD/PCNSGD) is shown to guarantee monotonic per-class loss decrease under milder conditions than standard GD, and the analysis identifies the role of directional noise in stochastic settings, which has not been previously formalized. The work also clarifies why heuristic methods like oversampling are effective, offering a unified perspective on imbalance mitigation strategies and highlighting the need to address both gradient norm and direction in stochastic optimization.

153471389d70a1ead6a3848673aa42ed554da900.title: On the convex hull of convex quadratic optimization problems with indicators
153471389d70a1ead6a3848673aa42ed554da900.research_question: What is the precise convex hull characterization for convex quadratic optimization problems with indicator variables and arbitrary constraints on the indicators, and how can this characterization be leveraged to develop tractable formulations and relaxations for mixed-integer quadratic optimization problems?
153471389d70a1ead6a3848673aa42ed554da900.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the convex hull of the feasible set for convex quadratic optimization problems with indicator variables can be described compactly in an extended space using a single positive semidefinite constraint and linear constraints, and that this description enables the development of efficient mixed-integer linear and conic formulations whose solutions correspond to the vertices of the underlying polyhedral set.
153471389d70a1ead6a3848673aa42ed554da900.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed to characterize the convex hull of mixed-integer sets arising from convex quadratic optimization problems with indicator variables. The approach involves constructing an extended formulation by introducing a quadratic number of additional variables and enforcing a single positive semidefinite constraint alongside linear constraints. The method reduces the convexification of the original set to the description of a polyhedral set in the extended space, for which a compact mixed-integer linear formulation will be derived. Additionally, in the original variable space, the convex hull will be described using an infinite but finitely generated family of conic-quadratic inequalities, and criteria will be established to determine the necessity of each inequality. The relationship between this new convex hull description and existing relaxation techniques based on matrix decomposition will also be analyzed.
153471389d70a1ead6a3848673aa42ed554da900.experiment_details: The proposed formulations will be evaluated on a range of benchmark problems, including best subset selection in regression, portfolio optimization, and other applications where the mixed-integer quadratic structure with indicator variables is prominent. Experiments will compare the new formulations against state-of-the-art convex relaxations and extended formulations, focusing on the number of variables and constraints required, the tractability for large-scale instances, and the tightness of the relaxation. Evaluation metrics will include solution quality, computational time, and the ability to generate necessary inequalities dynamically using mixed-integer linear optimization techniques. Both synthetic and real-world datasets will be considered, with special attention to cases where the indicator set Z is large or complex.
153471389d70a1ead6a3848673aa42ed554da900.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified and compact convex hull characterization for a broad class of convex quadratic optimization problems with indicator variables, requiring only a quadratic number of additional variables and a single positive semidefinite constraint in the extended space. The approach enables the derivation of a compact mixed-integer linear formulation whose solutions correspond exactly to the vertices of the underlying polyhedral set, overcoming the exponential complexity of explicit vertex enumeration. In the original variable space, the method provides a finitely generated conic-quadratic description, allowing for precise identification of necessary inequalities. This framework generalizes and unifies several previously known results, and offers a tractable alternative to existing disjunctive programming and decomposition-based relaxations, especially for problems with large or complex indicator sets.

153d544db44e0bffa8d3739c548848a899442b43.title: Convergence rates of deep ReLU networks for multiclass classification
153d544db44e0bffa8d3739c548848a899442b43.research_question: How rapidly do the estimated conditional class probabilities produced by deep ReLU neural networks converge to the true conditional class probabilities in multiclass classification problems, particularly when class membership probabilities approach zero?
153d544db44e0bffa8d3739c548848a899442b43.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the convergence rates of deep ReLU networks for estimating conditional class probabilities in multiclass classification depend critically on the behavior of these probabilities near zero, and that introducing a truncation to the cross-entropy loss will enable the derivation of meaningful convergence rates without requiring the probabilities to be bounded away from zero.
153d544db44e0bffa8d3739c548848a899442b43.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the convergence rates of sparse deep ReLU neural networks with softmax output layers in multiclass classification settings. The approach will focus on minimizing the cross-entropy loss, with a novel truncation applied to the Kullback-Leibler divergence to handle cases where conditional class probabilities are near zero. The analysis will introduce an 'alpha-small value bound' (SVB) condition to quantify the behavior of conditional class probabilities close to zero and relate this to convergence rates. The method will further assume the true conditional probability functions are Hölder-smooth and will derive risk bounds that explicitly depend on the SVB index and smoothness parameters. Theoretical results will be established for both the truncated and standard Kullback-Leibler risk, with explicit rates as functions of network architecture, smoothness, and the SVB index.
153d544db44e0bffa8d3739c548848a899442b43.experiment_details: The investigation will be conducted through rigorous mathematical analysis rather than empirical experiments. Theoretical risk bounds will be derived for multiclass classification models with input space [0,1]^d and K classes, assuming i.i.d. data. The function class will consist of s-sparse deep ReLU networks with bounded parameters and softmax output, and the true conditional class probabilities will be assumed to be Hölder-smooth and satisfy the alpha-SVB condition. The evaluation will focus on convergence rates of the estimated probabilities to the true probabilities, measured by the (possibly truncated) Kullback-Leibler divergence and, by extension, the Hellinger distance. Theoretical comparisons will be made to existing results for regression and density estimation, and the impact of network architecture (depth, width, sparsity) and problem parameters (number of classes, input dimension, smoothness, SVB index) on the rates will be systematically analyzed.
153d544db44e0bffa8d3739c548848a899442b43.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel analysis of convergence rates for deep ReLU networks in multiclass classification that accounts for the behavior of conditional class probabilities near zero, a regime where standard risk bounds can become infinite. The use of a truncated Kullback-Leibler divergence in the cross-entropy loss is proposed to overcome this limitation, enabling meaningful convergence rates without requiring lower bounds on probabilities. The introduction and use of the alpha-small value bound (SVB) condition is a new contribution, allowing the derivation of risk rates that interpolate between regimes with and without small probabilities. The results provide explicit, non-asymptotic convergence rates as functions of network architecture, smoothness, and the SVB index, and establish connections between the truncated Kullback-Leibler risk and the Hellinger distance in the context of deep learning.

1548e6f03f933ee3ee248bdb4710b9f0e0da551c.title: Towards Scalable 3D Anomaly Detection and Localization: A Benchmark via 3D Anomaly Synthesis and A Self-Supervised Learning Network
1548e6f03f933ee3ee248bdb4710b9f0e0da551c.research_question: How can scalable and effective 3D anomaly detection and localization be achieved in point cloud data, given the scarcity of diverse, high-quality 3D anomaly datasets and the limitations of current deep learning approaches?
1548e6f03f933ee3ee248bdb4710b9f0e0da551c.hypothesis: A synthetic, diverse 3D anomaly dataset combined with a self-supervised, geometry-aware iterative mask reconstruction network will significantly improve the scalability, accuracy, and localization capabilities of 3D anomaly detection in point clouds compared to existing methods.
1548e6f03f933ee3ee248bdb4710b9f0e0da551c.proposed_method: A comprehensive 3D anomaly detection framework will be developed, consisting of two main components: (1) a synthetic dataset generation pipeline that augments existing large-scale 3D model repositories (such as ShapeNet) with realistic, diverse 3D anomalies using mesh subdivision, defect carving via industrial design tools (e.g., Blender), and ground-truth annotation; and (2) a self-supervised Iterative Mask Reconstruction Network (IMRNet) for anomaly detection and localization. IMRNet will employ a Geometry-aware Point-cloud Sampling (GPS) module to prioritize sampling of points with high geometric variation, followed by a Point-patch Mask Reconstruction (PMR) module that reconstructs masked patches using a transformer-based autoencoder. During inference, the point cloud will undergo multiple reconstruction iterations, and a Dense Feature Concatenation and Comparison (DFC) module will compare both the reconstructed and original point clouds at feature and point levels to produce anomaly scores. Template regularization will be used to mitigate false positives from excessive reconstruction.
1548e6f03f933ee3ee248bdb4710b9f0e0da551c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both the newly created Anomaly-ShapeNet dataset (40 categories, 1600 samples, 6 anomaly types, 8K-30K points per sample) and the Real3D-AD dataset (12 categories, 1254 samples, 35K-780K points per sample). The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines including BTF, PatchCore (with FPFH and PointMAE features), M3DM, CPMF, and RegAD. Evaluation metrics will include image-level AUROC (I-AUC) for anomaly detection, pixel-level AUROC for segmentation, and AUPRO for per-region overlap, with additional analysis of computational efficiency and ablation studies on sampling strategies and masking ratios. The model backbone will be based on Point-MAE, with fine-tuning and ablation on the GPS module and iterative reconstruction parameters.
1548e6f03f933ee3ee248bdb4710b9f0e0da551c.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first large-scale, diverse, and realistic synthetic 3D point cloud anomaly dataset (Anomaly-ShapeNet) with accurate ground-truth annotations and a wide range of anomaly types. It also presents a novel self-supervised iterative mask reconstruction framework (IMRNet) that leverages geometry-aware sampling and iterative transformer-based reconstruction for effective anomaly detection and localization. The approach enables scalable representation learning in 3D, outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods on both synthetic and real 3D anomaly datasets, and provides a new benchmark and baseline for future research in 3D anomaly detection.

1574586ae94dbeecd6649784f4cfcf77c44e6b19.title: Embedding Principle of Loss Landscape of Deep Neural Networks
1574586ae94dbeecd6649784f4cfcf77c44e6b19.research_question: What is the general structural relationship between the loss landscapes of deep neural networks (DNNs) of different widths, and how does this relationship inform the understanding of critical points, optimization dynamics, and implicit regularization in wide DNNs?
1574586ae94dbeecd6649784f4cfcf77c44e6b19.hypothesis: The loss landscape of a wide DNN contains all critical points of all narrower DNNs of the same depth, and these embedded critical points contribute to the prevalence of highly degenerate critical points in wide networks, potentially explaining the ease of optimization and implicit regularization observed in overparameterized DNNs.
1574586ae94dbeecd6649784f4cfcf77c44e6b19.proposed_method: A formal embedding operation, termed 'critical embedding', will be developed to map any critical point (including local or global minima and saddle points) of a narrower fully-connected DNN into a critical point or critical affine subspace of a wider DNN, while preserving the network output function. The embedding is constructed via a sequence of one-step operations, each splitting a neuron in a hidden layer into two, copying input weights and splitting output weights according to a parameter alpha. This process is iteratively applied to embed the parameter set of a narrow network into the parameter space of a wider network, ensuring the preservation of criticality (i.e., the gradient of the loss remains zero) and increasing the degree of degeneracy (number of zero eigenvalues in the Hessian). The method is mathematically formalized for differentiable loss and activation functions, and is shown to generalize to other architectures such as convolutional neural networks by analogous feature/channel splitting.
1574586ae94dbeecd6649784f4cfcf77c44e6b19.experiment_details: Empirical validation will be conducted using fully-connected two-layer neural networks of varying widths on both synthetic data and real datasets such as the Iris dataset and MNIST. Networks will be trained to critical points using full-batch gradient descent (for 1D fitting tasks) or Adam optimizer (for classification tasks), with parameters initialized from a Gaussian distribution. After identifying empirical critical points in narrow networks, these points will be embedded into wider networks using the proposed embedding operation, and the Hessian spectrum at the embedded points will be analyzed to quantify the increase in degeneracy. Additional experiments will visualize the loss landscape and critical points in width-3 networks, and a reduction experiment will be performed on a width-400 network trained on MNIST, where neuron groups with highly similar input weights are merged to validate the embedding principle and its implications for pruning. Evaluation metrics include loss value, Hessian eigenvalue spectrum, degree of degeneracy, and prediction agreement between original and reduced networks.
1574586ae94dbeecd6649784f4cfcf77c44e6b19.novelty_claims: The proposed research establishes a general embedding principle for DNN loss landscapes, rigorously proving that the loss landscape of any wide DNN contains all critical points of all narrower DNNs of the same depth, independent of data or loss function. This principle reveals the ubiquitous existence of highly degenerate critical points in wide networks and provides a new theoretical framework for understanding implicit regularization and the optimization dynamics of overparameterized DNNs. The embedding operation is shown to preserve network function and criticality, and the methodology is extendable to other architectures such as CNNs. The work offers a foundational perspective for future research on loss landscapes, generalization, and pruning in deep learning.

15e1fc71bd0a664a4d8c01d2498f03b1de19f80a.title: Long-Context Inference with Retrieval-Augmented Speculative Decoding
15e1fc71bd0a664a4d8c01d2498f03b1de19f80a.research_question: How can long-context inference for large language models be accelerated while simultaneously enhancing generation quality, particularly in scenarios where traditional retrieval-augmented generation and speculative decoding face efficiency and performance limitations?
15e1fc71bd0a664a4d8c01d2498f03b1de19f80a.hypothesis: Integrating retrieval-augmented generation with speculative decoding—by employing a retrieval-augmented drafter operating on compressed, relevant contexts and introducing a retrieval-augmented target distribution for inference-time knowledge transfer—will enable significant speedups in long-context inference and improve generation quality over existing approaches.
15e1fc71bd0a664a4d8c01d2498f03b1de19f80a.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces Retrieval-Augmented Speculative Decoding (RAPID), which leverages a RAG drafter—a draft LLM operating on a compressed, selectively retrieved context—to generate speculative candidate tokens for a long-context target LLM. The RAG drafter processes only the most relevant context segments, identified via dense embedding and cosine similarity, to maintain computational efficiency. During inference, RAPID employs a retrieval-augmented target distribution that incorporates knowledge transfer from the RAG drafter to the target LLM, using a distillation-inspired logit shift controlled by a hyperparameter. The speculative decoding process is modified so that candidate tokens are validated against this enriched target distribution, allowing for higher acceptance rates and improved output quality. The approach supports both self-speculation (drafter and target of same scale) and upward-speculation (larger drafter), and can dynamically adapt the influence of the drafter via a tunable parameter.
15e1fc71bd0a664a4d8c01d2498f03b1de19f80a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using LLaMA-3.1 (8B, 70B) and Qwen2.5 (7B, 72B) as both target and drafter LLMs, evaluating both self-speculation and upward-speculation settings. Benchmarks include ∞Bench (covering long-book QA, multi-choice QA, and summarization with contexts >100K tokens) and LongBench v2 (multi-choice tasks with context lengths up to 2M words), using metrics such as F1, accuracy, ROUGE-L-Sum, and overall throughput (tokens/sec). Baselines for comparison include standard long-context LLM inference, RAG-only generation, naive speculative decoding, and MagicDec (a KV cache compression method). Efficiency is measured via prefill time and speedup ratios, and robustness is assessed under varying retrieval quality and knowledge transfer strengths. Additional real-world evaluation is performed on multi-turn dialogue tasks with extended chat histories, using LLM-as-a-Judge protocols for quality assessment.
15e1fc71bd0a664a4d8c01d2498f03b1de19f80a.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new paradigm for speculative decoding in long-context LLMs by leveraging retrieval-augmented drafters that operate on compressed, relevant contexts, thus overcoming memory-bound inefficiencies of traditional SD. The retrieval-augmented target distribution enables inference-time knowledge transfer from potentially stronger drafters, improving both acceptance rates and generation quality. RAPID supports both same-scale and larger-scale drafters, allowing for flexible and efficient acceleration of long-context inference. The approach demonstrates robust performance across varying retrieval qualities and context lengths, and achieves emergent capabilities beyond those of individual target or drafter models.

15e318ceb6b972098590fc3b7214fe49fb3e3de4.title: Pre-Trained Model Guided Fine-Tuning for Zero-Shot Adversarial Robustness
15e318ceb6b972098590fc3b7214fe49fb3e3de4.research_question: How can the zero-shot adversarial robustness of large-scale pre-trained vision-language models, such as CLIP, be improved without sacrificing their generalization ability and clean accuracy?
15e318ceb6b972098590fc3b7214fe49fb3e3de4.hypothesis: Incorporating supervision from the original pre-trained model during adversarial fine-tuning will mitigate overfitting and enhance both zero-shot adversarial robustness and clean accuracy of large-scale vision-language models.
15e318ceb6b972098590fc3b7214fe49fb3e3de4.proposed_method: A novel adversarial fine-tuning strategy, Pre-trained Model Guided Adversarial Fine-Tuning (PMG-AFT), is developed to enhance zero-shot adversarial robustness. The method introduces an auxiliary generalization information branch that leverages the frozen pre-trained model to guide the target model during fine-tuning. Specifically, adversarial examples are generated using PGD, and the target model is trained with a composite loss: (1) a cross-entropy loss on adversarial examples for robustness, (2) a KL-divergence loss that minimizes the distance between the adversarial example outputs of the target and pre-trained models to preserve generalization, and (3) a regularization loss that encourages the features of adversarial and clean images in the target model to be similar. Only the image encoder parameters are updated, while the text encoder remains frozen, and the adversarial example generation alternates with parameter updates.
15e318ceb6b972098590fc3b7214fe49fb3e3de4.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted by fine-tuning the CLIP model on the TinyImageNet dataset and evaluating on 15 additional zero-shot datasets spanning general object recognition, fine-grained recognition, scene recognition, domain-specific data, and medical images. Evaluation metrics include robust accuracy under PGD-10 and AutoAttack with various perturbation bounds, as well as clean accuracy. Baselines include the original CLIP, standard fine-tuning, FT-TeCoA (the current SOTA), and visual prompt-based adaptations. The ViT-B/32 architecture is used, with SGD optimization, and all models are trained for 10 epochs. Ablation studies assess the impact of loss components, feature layers, and distance metrics.
15e318ceb6b972098590fc3b7214fe49fb3e3de4.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a dual-branch adversarial fine-tuning framework that leverages the pre-trained model's generalization features to mitigate overfitting and improve zero-shot adversarial robustness. Unlike prior approaches that focus on parameter space constraints, this method enforces constraints in the feature space and incorporates a regularization loss to further enhance generalization. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in both robust and clean accuracy over state-of-the-art methods across a wide range of zero-shot datasets, achieving a superior trade-off between robustness and generalization.

15f87ce1634093c8760e534bf2dd5daf66c7b54b.title: Untargeted Backdoor Watermark: Towards Harmless and Stealthy Dataset Copyright Protection
15f87ce1634093c8760e534bf2dd5daf66c7b54b.research_question: How can dataset copyright protection be achieved for open-sourced image datasets in a manner that is both harmless to model security and stealthy, while enabling reliable ownership verification?
15f87ce1634093c8760e534bf2dd5daf66c7b54b.hypothesis: Untargeted backdoor watermarks, designed to induce non-deterministic abnormal model behaviors, can provide effective, stealthy, and harmless dataset copyright protection, and enable robust ownership verification without introducing significant security risks.
15f87ce1634093c8760e534bf2dd5daf66c7b54b.proposed_method: A new untargeted backdoor watermarking (UBW) framework will be developed for image classification datasets, supporting both poisoned-label and clean-label settings. The UBW-P (poisoned-label) variant will randomly shuffle the labels of poisoned samples and apply an adversary-specified image transformation, ensuring that poisoned images do not share a deterministic target label and thus increasing prediction dispersibility. The UBW-C (clean-label) variant will use bi-level optimization to maximize the entropy (dispersibility) of model predictions on poisoned samples while keeping their labels unchanged, leveraging differentiable surrogate metrics for sample-wise and class-wise dispersibility. Both variants will be designed so that models trained on the watermarked datasets behave normally on benign data but exhibit highly dispersed, non-deterministic predictions on poisoned samples. Dataset ownership verification will be enabled by querying suspicious models with poisoned samples and applying a hypothesis-testing procedure (pairwise T-test) to detect the presence of the untargeted backdoor.
15f87ce1634093c8760e534bf2dd5daf66c7b54b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on benchmark image classification datasets, specifically CIFAR-10 and a 50-class subset of ImageNet, using ResNet-18 as the model architecture. The proposed UBW methods will be compared against established poison-only backdoor watermarking baselines, including BadNets, Blended, WaNet, Label-Consistent, and SleeperAgent attacks. Evaluation metrics will include benign accuracy (BA), attack success rate on all and correctly classified samples (ASR-A, ASR-C), and averaged prediction dispersibility (D_p). Ownership verification effectiveness will be assessed using the confidence score (ΔP) and p-value from hypothesis testing in various scenarios (independent trigger, independent model, and malicious/unauthorized dataset usage). Additional experiments will evaluate the resistance of the proposed UBW methods to backdoor defenses such as fine-tuning and model pruning, as well as the effects of poisoning rate and trade-off hyperparameters.
15f87ce1634093c8760e534bf2dd5daf66c7b54b.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first untargeted backdoor watermarking paradigm for dataset copyright protection, addressing the security risks of targeted backdoor watermarks by ensuring non-deterministic model behaviors on poisoned samples. The approach supports both poisoned-label and clean-label settings, with the clean-label variant leveraging bi-level optimization and surrogate dispersibility metrics for stealthiness. The verification method is designed to be harmless, stealthy, and robust to existing backdoor defenses, including those that assume sample-agnostic triggers. The framework enables reliable dataset ownership verification without compromising model security or dataset usability.

160820bb80922cfc3ff47a0c9b3a2bb369bb97b9.title: SPC: Evolving Self-Play Critic via Adversarial Games for LLM Reasoning
160820bb80922cfc3ff47a0c9b3a2bb369bb97b9.research_question: How can the reliability of large language model (LLM) step-by-step reasoning processes be automatically evaluated and improved, particularly in the absence of high-quality step-level human annotations?
160820bb80922cfc3ff47a0c9b3a2bb369bb97b9.hypothesis: A self-evolving adversarial framework, in which a generator creates challenging erroneous reasoning steps and a critic model learns to detect these errors through self-play and reinforcement learning, can surpass existing process reward models and LLM-based critics in step-level error detection and enhance LLM mathematical reasoning performance.
160820bb80922cfc3ff47a0c9b3a2bb369bb97b9.proposed_method: A novel self-play adversarial framework is proposed, involving two models initialized from a base LLM: a 'sneaky generator' and a 'step-level critic.' The sneaky generator is fine-tuned to transform correct reasoning steps into subtle, impactful erroneous steps using supervised learning on correct-incorrect step pairs, with error types guided by predefined categories. The step-level critic is initialized by fine-tuning on human-annotated critiques, ensuring concise and standardized feedback on step correctness. These models engage in adversarial games: the generator attempts to create errors that are both impactful (verified by a drop in LLM problem-solving success rate) and hard for the critic to detect, while the critic strives to accurately identify all errors. Reinforcement learning is applied iteratively, with rewards based on the outcome of each confrontation, and a balanced evolution strategy is used to avoid overfitting and ensure both models improve through competition.
160820bb80922cfc3ff47a0c9b3a2bb369bb97b9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three human-annotated mathematical reasoning process benchmarks: ProcessBench, PRM800K, and DeltaBench. The evaluation focuses on the critic's ability to assess the correctness of individual reasoning steps, using recall, average, and harmonic mean metrics. Baselines include state-of-the-art process reward models (e.g., Math-Shepherd, Qwen2.5-Math-7B-PRM800K) and various LLMs prompted as critics (e.g., Llama, Qwen, GPT-4o, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B). The impact of the critic on LLM reasoning will be further evaluated by integrating it into the test-time search process on MATH500 and AIME2024 datasets, measuring problem-solving accuracy. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the effects of different adversarial training strategies and reward structures.
160820bb80922cfc3ff47a0c9b3a2bb369bb97b9.novelty_claims: The proposed approach eliminates the need for manual step-level annotation by generating high-quality adversarial training data through self-play. It introduces a dual-model adversarial game at the reasoning step level, enabling both the error generator and the critic to evolve iteratively via reinforcement learning. The method leverages automated validation of step impact on LLM problem-solving success, ensuring that generated errors are both realistic and challenging. The critic model is designed to provide actionable, step-level critiques that can be used in real-time to guide LLM reasoning, rather than only post-hoc scoring. The framework demonstrates superior generalization to both short and long chain-of-thought styles and outperforms strong baselines in both step-level error detection and overall mathematical reasoning accuracy.

160fff3ad3611c9f16e1ec8dd168882e98c4fcf2.title: AugGen: Synthetic Augmentation using Diffusion Models Can Improve Recognition
160fff3ad3611c9f16e1ec8dd168882e98c4fcf2.research_question: Can synthetic data augmentation using class-conditional diffusion models, trained solely on a target dataset without external resources, improve the performance of discriminative models in data-limited, privacy-sensitive recognition tasks such as face recognition?
160fff3ad3611c9f16e1ec8dd168882e98c4fcf2.hypothesis: A generative model, when appropriately conditioned and sampled, can augment a limited real dataset with synthetic samples in a way that significantly boosts the performance of a downstream discriminator, even surpassing gains from architectural improvements and reducing the need for additional real data.
160fff3ad3611c9f16e1ec8dd168882e98c4fcf2.proposed_method: A self-contained synthetic augmentation framework will be developed using a class-conditional diffusion model trained exclusively on the target face recognition dataset. The approach involves training both a generator (diffusion model) and a discriminator from scratch on the same real dataset. A novel sampling strategy will be implemented, where new synthetic samples are generated by interpolating between class condition vectors (using parameters alpha and beta), effectively creating 'mixed' classes that increase inter-class separation and intra-class compactness. A grid search will be conducted over alpha and beta to maximize dissimilarity from source classes while maintaining coherence within the synthetic class, using cosine similarity and feature space metrics. The synthetic samples will be combined with the original real data to train the discriminator, with no reliance on external datasets or pre-trained models.
160fff3ad3611c9f16e1ec8dd168882e98c4fcf2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard face recognition datasets, including CASIA-WebFace and a subset of WebFace4M (WebFace160K), with approximately 10,000 identities and 160K images. The discriminative model will use an IR50 backbone with AdaFace margin loss, and architectural comparisons will include IR101. The generative model will be a latent or pixel-space diffusion model, trained from scratch on the target dataset. Synthetic datasets will be generated using the proposed class-mixing strategy, and compared against state-of-the-art synthetic data generation methods (e.g., DCFace, IDiff-Face, DigiFace1M). Evaluation will be performed on eight face recognition benchmarks, including LFW, CFP-FP, CPLFW, CALFW, AgeDB, IJB-B, IJB-C, and TinyFace, using verification accuracy (TAR) at various FPR thresholds and rank-1 accuracy. Experiments will also compare the impact of adding synthetic versus additional real data, and all models will be trained and evaluated with standardized augmentations and multiple random seeds for statistical reliability.
160fff3ad3611c9f16e1ec8dd168882e98c4fcf2.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to demonstrate that synthetic augmentation via class-conditional diffusion models, trained solely on the target dataset without any auxiliary models or external data, can consistently improve recognition performance across multiple benchmarks. The approach introduces a novel class-mixing sampling strategy that generates beneficial synthetic samples, often yielding gains comparable to or exceeding those from architectural enhancements. The method is shown to be as effective as increasing the real dataset size by up to 1.7×, thus alleviating data collection challenges in privacy-sensitive domains. Additionally, the work highlights that traditional generative metrics (e.g., Frechet Distance) poorly correlate with downstream discriminative performance, emphasizing the need for new proxy metrics.

161273d7f1c4a7302be2937f14ac48ed557e6dae.title: HarsanyiNet: Computing Accurate Shapley Values in a Single Forward Propagation
161273d7f1c4a7302be2937f14ac48ed557e6dae.research_question: How can exact Shapley values for input variables in deep neural networks be computed efficiently, without incurring the high computational cost typically associated with existing approximation methods?
161273d7f1c4a7302be2937f14ac48ed557e6dae.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a novel neural network architecture can be designed to simultaneously perform model inference and compute exact Shapley values for each input variable in a single forward propagation, by leveraging the theoretical connection between Shapley values and Harsanyi interactions.
161273d7f1c4a7302be2937f14ac48ed557e6dae.proposed_method: A new neural network architecture, termed HarsanyiNet, will be developed to encode Harsanyi interactions at the level of intermediate neurons, called Harsanyi units. Each Harsanyi unit is designed to represent an AND relationship among a specific subset of input variables, ensuring that its activation is exclusively determined by its receptive field and is deactivated if any variable in that field is masked. The network output is constructed as a weighted sum of all Harsanyi units across multiple layers. The architecture includes cascaded Harsanyi blocks, each composed of linear, AND, and ReLU operations, with learnable child node selection to flexibly encode higher-order interactions. The exact Shapley value for each input variable is then computed as a uniform redistribution of the contributions from all Harsanyi units containing that variable, using a closed-form equation derived from the network's forward activations.
161273d7f1c4a7302be2937f14ac48ed557e6dae.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both tabular and image datasets, including Census Income, Yeast, TV news commercial detection, MNIST, and CIFAR-10. Two variants of HarsanyiNet will be implemented: Harsanyi-MLP for tabular data and Harsanyi-CNN for image data, each adapted to the respective data modality. The accuracy of computed Shapley values will be quantitatively evaluated using root mean squared error (RMSE) against ground-truth Shapley values (computed exactly for small n), and classification accuracy will be reported. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art Shapley value approximation methods such as DeepSHAP, FastSHAP, KernelSHAP, and ShapNet (both shallow and deep variants). The computational cost, measured in the number of network inferences required, will also be compared. Visualization of attribution maps and receptive fields will be performed to qualitatively assess the faithfulness and interpretability of the attributions.
161273d7f1c4a7302be2937f14ac48ed557e6dae.novelty_claims: The proposed approach enables the exact computation of Shapley values for all input variables in a single forward propagation, overcoming the NP-hard computational barrier of traditional methods. Unlike prior architectures, the method does not restrict the order or number of variable interactions that can be encoded, thus providing greater flexibility and representation power. The architecture is theoretically guaranteed to produce exact Shapley values, and experimental results are expected to demonstrate both negligible computational error and superior classification performance compared to existing methods. The method also introduces a general framework for designing neural networks that can simultaneously perform inference and attribution, applicable to both tabular and image data.

162325cf35e26f32c3dfc88bf04bcbb599741ab3.title: Quamba2: A Robust and Scalable Post-training Quantization Framework for Selective State Space Models
162325cf35e26f32c3dfc88bf04bcbb599741ab3.research_question: How can post-training quantization be made robust and scalable for selective State Space Models (SSMs) across a variety of bit-width configurations and deployment scenarios, including both cloud and edge platforms, while minimizing performance degradation and maximizing efficiency?
162325cf35e26f32c3dfc88bf04bcbb599741ab3.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging intrinsic properties of SSMs, such as channel order preservation and activation persistence, and applying specialized quantization techniques (e.g., sort-and-cluster and per-state-group quantization), will enable robust post-training quantization at low bit-widths (e.g., W4A8, W4A16, W8A8) for SSMs, achieving significant memory and latency reductions with minimal accuracy loss.
162325cf35e26f32c3dfc88bf04bcbb599741ab3.proposed_method: A robust post-training quantization framework will be developed for selective SSMs, supporting multiple bit-width configurations (W8A8, W4A8, W4A16) and both Mamba1 and Mamba2 architectures. The method will exploit channel order preservation and activation persistence in SSMs by first sorting and clustering head channels based on offline-calibrated channel maxima, then applying unsupervised clustering to group heads and channels for shared quantization scaling factors. For input-dependent parameters (B and C), per-state-group quantization will be used, assigning a single scaling factor per group to enhance precision where value ranges are small. Offline cluster-aware weight reordering will be performed to align model weights with the new channel and head sequences, and Hadamard matrix fusion will be integrated into input and output projections to further smooth activation distributions and ensure compute-invariance. The framework will provide efficient CUDA kernels for 4/8-bit quantization throughout the model, including embedding and output head, enabling head-to-toe quantization for maximal memory and latency savings.
162325cf35e26f32c3dfc88bf04bcbb599741ab3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using both Mamba1 and Mamba2 SSM backbones, with quantized models evaluated on a suite of zero-shot downstream tasks including LAMBADA, HellaSwag, PIQA, ARC, and WinoGrande, as well as the large multitask MMLU benchmark to assess generalizability and robustness. Baselines will include state-of-the-art SSM quantization methods such as MambaQuant and Quamba, with comparisons across multiple bit-width settings. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, memory usage, latency (time-per-output-token, time-to-first-token), and throughput, with tests performed on both high-end GPUs (Nvidia A5000) and resource-constrained edge devices (Nvidia Orin Nano 8G). Ablation studies will analyze the impact of each quantization component, and mixed-precision strategies will be explored using evolutionary search to optimize accuracy-latency tradeoffs.
162325cf35e26f32c3dfc88bf04bcbb599741ab3.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a novel combination of sort-and-cluster quantization for SSM input activations and per-state-group quantization for input-dependent parameters, specifically tailored to the unique properties of SSMs. Offline cluster-aware weight reordering and Hadamard matrix fusion are integrated to maximize quantization precision and maintain compute-invariance. The approach supports a wide range of bit-widths and full head-to-toe quantization, enabling deployment of large SSMs on both cloud and edge platforms with up to 4× memory reduction, 1.3–3× speedup, and minimal accuracy loss. The framework also demonstrates improved generalizability and robustness on challenging multitask datasets and provides automated mixed-precision support for optimal tradeoffs.

163b4d6a79a5b19af88b8585456363340d9efd04.title: GPT-4 Technical Report
163b4d6a79a5b19af88b8585456363340d9efd04.research_question: How can large-scale, multimodal language models be developed to achieve human-level performance across a wide range of professional, academic, and reasoning tasks, while ensuring predictable scaling, improved factuality, and safe deployment?
163b4d6a79a5b19af88b8585456363340d9efd04.hypothesis: A Transformer-based, multimodal model pre-trained on large-scale text and image data, and subsequently aligned via reinforcement learning from human feedback, will demonstrate human-level or superior performance on diverse academic and professional benchmarks, exhibit predictable scaling properties, and show improved factuality and adherence to desired behaviors compared to prior models.
163b4d6a79a5b19af88b8585456363340d9efd04.proposed_method: A large-scale Transformer-based architecture will be pre-trained to predict the next token in a document, using a mixture of publicly available and licensed datasets containing both text and images. The model will be designed to accept interlaced text and image inputs and produce text outputs, enabling multimodal reasoning. Post-training alignment will be performed using Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) to improve factual accuracy and adherence to user intent. Infrastructure and optimization methods will be developed to ensure predictable model behavior across a wide range of scales, enabling reliable extrapolation of performance from smaller models to the final large-scale model. Scaling laws will be fitted to loss and capability metrics to predict final model performance prior to full-scale training.
163b4d6a79a5b19af88b8585456363340d9efd04.experiment_details: The model will be evaluated on a diverse set of academic and professional benchmarks, including simulated human exams (e.g., Uniform Bar Exam, LSAT, SAT, GRE, AP exams, AMC, Leetcode, HumanEval) and traditional NLP benchmarks (e.g., MMLU, HellaSwag, ARC, WinoGrande, DROP, GSM-8K). For each exam, real-world conditions and scoring rubrics will be simulated, and contamination checks will be performed to ensure test data integrity. Baselines will include previous large language models (e.g., GPT-3.5, Chinchilla, PaLM) and state-of-the-art systems with benchmark-specific training. Evaluation metrics will include exam scores, percentiles, accuracy, F1 score, pass rates, and human preference ratings. Multilingual capabilities will be assessed by translating benchmarks into multiple languages. Factuality and safety will be evaluated using internal adversarial factuality tests and public benchmarks such as TruthfulQA.
163b4d6a79a5b19af88b8585456363340d9efd04.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a large-scale, multimodal language model capable of processing both text and image inputs, achieving human-level or superior performance on a broad range of academic and professional tasks. The methodology includes a novel approach to predictable scaling, enabling accurate performance prediction from small-scale experiments. The model demonstrates substantial improvements in factuality, multilingual performance, and adherence to user intent compared to prior models. Additionally, the research contributes new infrastructure for scalable training and open-sources a framework for comprehensive model evaluation.

163f8f91005c6844f2617e1e33ef484b30e08f2a.title: Context-Alignment: Activating and Enhancing LLM Capabilities in Time Series
163f8f91005c6844f2617e1e33ef484b30e08f2a.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be effectively activated and enhanced for time series (TS) tasks, overcoming the limitations of token-level alignment and leveraging their inherent strengths in linguistic logic and structure?
163f8f91005c6844f2617e1e33ef484b30e08f2a.hypothesis: Aligning time series data with linguistic context at the structural and logical level within environments familiar to LLMs will significantly improve LLMs' ability to understand, process, and generalize across diverse TS tasks, especially under few-shot and zero-shot scenarios.
163f8f91005c6844f2617e1e33ef484b30e08f2a.proposed_method: A new paradigm, Context-Alignment, will be developed to align time series data with linguistic components in a manner that leverages LLMs' strengths in logic and structure. This will be operationalized through Dual-Scale Context-Alignment Graph Neural Networks (DSCA-GNNs), which perform both structural alignment (using dual-scale nodes to represent hierarchical structures in TS-language multimodal inputs) and logical alignment (using directed edges to encode semantic relationships). The method will include a learnable interaction mechanism to transfer macroscopic information between coarse- and fine-grained representations. Furthermore, a Few-Shot Prompting Context-Alignment (FSCA) approach will be instantiated, integrating demonstration examples as prompts and enabling flexible, repeated insertion of DSCA-GNNs into various LLM layers to enhance logical and structural awareness.
163f8f91005c6844f2617e1e33ef484b30e08f2a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a wide range of TS tasks, including long-term and short-term forecasting, few-shot and zero-shot forecasting, and classification. Datasets such as ETTh1, ETTh2, ETTm1, ETTm2, Weather, Electricity, Traffic, ILI, and the M4 and UEA classification datasets will be used. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art Transformer-based models (iTransformer, FEDformer, Non-stationary Transformer, ETSformer, PatchTST), non-Transformer models (TimesNet, DLinear), and advanced LLM-based approaches (GPT4TS, Time-LLM, S2IP-LLM), all utilizing GPT-2 as the LLM backbone for consistency. Evaluation metrics will include MSE, MAE, SMAPE, MASE, OWA, and classification accuracy. Experimental protocols will follow established standards, with ablation studies to assess the impact of DSCA-GNNs, the number and position of LLM layers, and the inclusion of coarse- and fine-grained branches.
163f8f91005c6844f2617e1e33ef484b30e08f2a.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first context-level alignment paradigm for TS-language multimodal inputs, moving beyond token-level alignment to fully activate LLMs' potential for TS tasks. The Dual-Scale Context-Alignment GNNs framework is novel in its dual-scale node and directed edge design, enabling both structural and logical alignment. The FSCA method further innovates by integrating few-shot prompting within this framework, allowing flexible and repeated enhancement of LLMs. The approach claims significant improvements over existing methods, particularly in data-scarce settings, and demonstrates generality across forecasting and classification tasks.

164c61ff8bcb2bc70fde03fa6a45f23c3d391c50.title: Loss Functions and Operators Generated by f-Divergences
164c61ff8bcb2bc70fde03fa6a45f23c3d391c50.research_question: How can loss functions for classification and language modeling be systematically generalized beyond the classical cross-entropy, and what are the effects of using losses generated by general f-divergences with potentially non-uniform reference measures in various training regimes and tasks?
164c61ff8bcb2bc70fde03fa6a45f23c3d391c50.hypothesis: Loss functions generated from f-divergences, particularly those based on the α-divergence with α=1.5, will outperform or match the classical cross-entropy loss (KL divergence) across a range of tasks and training regimes, including pre-training, supervised fine-tuning, and distillation, for both image classification and language modeling.
164c61ff8bcb2bc70fde03fa6a45f23c3d391c50.proposed_method: A framework will be developed to construct convex loss functions for multiclass classification and language modeling by leveraging Fenchel–Young losses generated from general f-divergences. The method generalizes the logistic loss by replacing the KL divergence with arbitrary f-divergences and by allowing for non-uniform reference measures (class priors). For each f-divergence, a corresponding operator, termed f-softargmax, will be defined to map logits to probability distributions. A novel, parallelizable bisection algorithm will be designed to efficiently compute the f-softargmax for any f-divergence, supporting both dense and sparse probability outputs. The approach will be instantiated for several known divergences (KL, Chi-square, α-divergence, Jensen-Shannon, Squared Hellinger), recovering existing losses (logistic, sparsemax, entmax) and generating new ones. The method will also support learning or specifying the reference measure q, and will provide closed-form solutions in the binary case.
164c61ff8bcb2bc70fde03fa6a45f23c3d391c50.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both image classification and language modeling tasks. For image classification, ResNet50 will be trained on the ImageNet-2012 dataset using various f-divergence-generated losses, with SGD optimization and standard data augmentation and learning rate schedules. For language modeling, decoder-only transformer models will be pre-trained, fine-tuned (SFT), and distilled using next-token prediction losses generated by different f-divergences, with experiments on the C4 and XSum datasets. Baselines will include the standard cross-entropy (KL divergence) loss, and comparisons will be made to losses generated by Chi-square, α-divergence (with varying α), Jensen-Shannon, and Squared Hellinger divergences. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy for ImageNet and ROUGE-2 scores for summarization tasks. The effect of using different f-softargmax operators at decoding time will also be assessed.
164c61ff8bcb2bc70fde03fa6a45f23c3d391c50.novelty_claims: The proposed framework systematically generalizes loss functions for classification and language modeling by generating them from arbitrary f-divergences, supporting both uniform and non-uniform reference measures. A novel, parallelizable bisection algorithm is introduced for efficiently computing the f-softargmax operator for any f-divergence, including those that produce sparse probability distributions. The approach unifies and extends existing losses (logistic, sparsemax, entmax) and enables the creation of entirely new loss functions. Empirical results suggest that the α-divergence with α=1.5 yields robust improvements across tasks, and the framework supports direct application to pre-trained models and various training regimes without requiring changes to inference code.

166b8c2ee52794c46615c5c52d0390d896b79794.title: Training-free Diffusion Model Adaptation for Variable-Sized Text-to-Image Synthesis
166b8c2ee52794c46615c5c52d0390d896b79794.research_question: How can text-to-image diffusion models be adapted to generate high-fidelity images of variable sizes and aspect ratios, while maintaining visual quality and semantic alignment, without requiring additional training or fine-tuning?
166b8c2ee52794c46615c5c52d0390d896b79794.hypothesis: Modifying the scaling factor in the attention layers of diffusion models, based on a statistical relationship between attention entropy and token count, will enable effective adaptation to variable image resolutions, mitigating common defects in low and high resolution synthesis without retraining.
166b8c2ee52794c46615c5c52d0390d896b79794.proposed_method: A novel approach is proposed that replaces the conventional scaling factor in the attention modules of diffusion models with a new scaling factor proportional to the logarithm of the token count. This scaling factor is derived from a statistical analysis of the relationship between attention entropy and the number of tokens, ensuring that the entropy remains stable across varying image resolutions. The method involves analytically determining the optimal scaling constant such that, for any inference token count N, the scaling factor is set as λ = (1/√d) * (log N / log T), where d is the token dimension and T is the training token count. This adjustment is implemented in a training-free, plug-and-play manner by modifying a single parameter in the model's attention layers, requiring no additional model training or fine-tuning.
166b8c2ee52794c46615c5c52d0390d896b79794.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on subsets of the LAION-400M and LAION-5B datasets, using both Stable Diffusion (trained on LAION-5B, default 512x512 resolution) and Latent Diffusion (trained on LAION-400M, default 256x256 resolution) models. The evaluation will include generating images at multiple resolutions (including lower, default, and higher than training resolutions) and aspect ratios. Baselines will use the original scaling factor (λ = 1/√d). Performance will be quantitatively assessed using Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for image quality and diversity, and CLIP scores for text-image semantic alignment. Human evaluation will be conducted via pairwise preference tests for text-image consistency. Additional analysis will measure attention entropy across layers and resolutions to validate the theoretical claims.
166b8c2ee52794c46615c5c52d0390d896b79794.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a training-free, theoretically grounded scaling factor for attention layers in diffusion models, enabling robust adaptation to variable image sizes and aspect ratios. This approach is the first to leverage the statistical relationship between attention entropy and token count for this purpose, mitigating incomplete object depiction at low resolutions and repetitive artifacts at high resolutions. The method is efficient, requiring only a single parameter change, and outperforms existing upsampling and super-resolution techniques in both semantic richness and computational efficiency for variable-sized image synthesis.

166d1e5361465f8e235747d14641249cbb3b6fd2.title: A Paradigm Shift in Machine Translation: Boosting Translation Performance of Large Language Models
166d1e5361465f8e235747d14641249cbb3b6fd2.research_question: How can the translation performance of moderate-sized large language models (LLMs) be significantly improved for machine translation tasks, especially without relying on large amounts of parallel data?
166d1e5361465f8e235747d14641249cbb3b6fd2.hypothesis: A two-stage fine-tuning approach—first on monolingual data in relevant languages, followed by fine-tuning on a small set of high-quality parallel data—will substantially boost the translation capabilities of moderate-sized LLMs, surpassing both their zero-shot performance and existing state-of-the-art translation models.
166d1e5361465f8e235747d14641249cbb3b6fd2.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a two-stage fine-tuning paradigm for decoder-only LLMs such as LLaMA-2 (7B and 13B parameters). In the first stage, the model is fine-tuned using monolingual data from all languages involved in the translation tasks, with English data included to prevent catastrophic forgetting. This stage aims to enhance the model’s general linguistic proficiency across languages. In the second stage, the model undergoes further fine-tuning on a small, high-quality parallel dataset, curated from human-written sources such as WMT test sets and Flores-200 development/test sets. Both full-weight and parameter-efficient (LoRA) fine-tuning strategies are explored, with LoRA applied to the down-projection layers of the feed-forward networks. The entire process is designed to avoid overfitting and knowledge dilution that can result from excessive parallel data.
166d1e5361465f8e235747d14641249cbb3b6fd2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 10 translation directions involving English, German, Czech, Icelandic, Chinese, and Russian, using WMT’21 and WMT’22 test datasets. The method will be evaluated against strong baselines, including prior LLM-based translation systems (e.g., BigTranslate, TIM, SWIE, BayLing) and state-of-the-art supervised models (NLLB-54B, GPT-3.5, GPT-4). Evaluation metrics include BLEU and COMET, with a focus on COMET for its stronger correlation with human judgment. Ablation studies will assess the impact of monolingual data volume, parallel data quality, and fine-tuning strategies. The training setup involves full-weight fine-tuning with batch size 256, sequence length 512, and up to 20B monolingual tokens, using 16 MI200 GPUs. Both full-weight and LoRA-based fine-tuning will be compared.
166d1e5361465f8e235747d14641249cbb3b6fd2.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a paradigm shift in LLM-based machine translation by demonstrating that high translation performance can be achieved with minimal parallel data, leveraging a novel two-stage fine-tuning strategy. The approach challenges the prevailing assumption that large volumes of parallel data are necessary for strong translation models, and provides empirical evidence that moderate-sized LLMs can outperform much larger models and supervised systems. The method also establishes efficient training recipes with low computational cost and highlights the critical role of monolingual data and data quality in LLM translation.

169fd6c457d99a21c32b6f23bbfd1e09a2513684.title: Relay Diffusion: Unifying diffusion process across resolutions for image synthesis
169fd6c457d99a21c32b6f23bbfd1e09a2513684.research_question: How can the diffusion process for image synthesis be unified and optimized across different resolutions to improve the efficiency, quality, and flexibility of high-resolution image generation?
169fd6c457d99a21c32b6f23bbfd1e09a2513684.hypothesis: A cascaded diffusion framework that transfers a low-resolution image or noise into an equivalent high-resolution representation via patch-wise blurring diffusion and block noise will enable seamless continuation of the diffusion process across resolutions, reducing distribution mismatch and improving both efficiency and image quality in high-resolution image synthesis.
169fd6c457d99a21c32b6f23bbfd1e09a2513684.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces the Relay Diffusion Model (RDM), a cascaded diffusion pipeline where each stage continues the diffusion process from the output of the previous stage, rather than restarting from pure noise. At each transition, the low-resolution image is upsampled and a patch-wise blurring diffusion process is applied, with block noise introduced to match the frequency characteristics of the upsampled image to those of high-resolution images. The forward process uses a series of patch-wise blurring matrices, and the corrupted sample is modeled as a mixture of blurred image, block noise, and independent Gaussian noise. The high-resolution stage is trained with a loss function that incorporates these noise components, and a stochastic sampler adapted from EDM is developed to handle the modified forward process, including a weighted sum of block noise and Gaussian noise in the sampling steps.
169fd6c457d99a21c32b6f23bbfd1e09a2513684.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on CelebA-HQ and ImageNet datasets, focusing on 256×256 image generation. The architecture will utilize a UNet backbone for both low- and high-resolution stages, with the first stage trained on 64×64 images and the second on 256×256 images. Baselines for comparison include state-of-the-art diffusion models such as ADM, LDM, DiT, MDT, and StyleSwin. Evaluation metrics will include FID, sFID, IS, Precision, and Recall, computed on 50,000 samples for ImageNet and 30,000 for CelebA-HQ. Ablation studies will assess the impact of block noise, the scale of stochasticity in the sampler, and the allocation of sampling steps (NFE) between stages.
169fd6c457d99a21c32b6f23bbfd1e09a2513684.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a unified framework for continuing the diffusion process across resolutions without restarting from pure noise, leveraging patch-wise blurring diffusion and block noise to address frequency-domain mismatches. This approach eliminates the need for low-resolution conditioning and associated augmentation tricks, reduces training and sampling steps, and allows for correction of low-resolution artifacts in later stages. The method claims improved efficiency, simplicity, and potential for higher performance compared to both traditional cascaded and end-to-end diffusion models, achieving state-of-the-art results on standard benchmarks.

16a44d0782699b43057151225773f3ebe2cd5918.title: BayesDAG: Gradient-Based Posterior Inference for Causal Discovery
16a44d0782699b43057151225773f3ebe2cd5918.research_question: How can scalable and accurate Bayesian posterior inference over causal models, specifically Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs), be achieved for both linear and nonlinear settings, while quantifying epistemic uncertainty and ensuring computational efficiency?
16a44d0782699b43057151225773f3ebe2cd5918.hypothesis: A gradient-based Bayesian inference framework that combines stochastic gradient Markov Chain Monte Carlo (SG-MCMC) and variational inference (VI) in an augmented parameter space can enable direct sampling of DAGs from the posterior, improve inference quality, and scale to high-dimensional, nonlinear causal discovery tasks.
16a44d0782699b43057151225773f3ebe2cd5918.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a novel parameterization of the DAG space using an augmented space of binary edge masks and node potentials, inspired by the NoCurl characterization, but modified to enable valid Bayesian inference without explicit DAG regularization. Bayesian inference is performed in this (W, p) space, where W is a binary adjacency matrix and p is a vector of node potentials, using a combination of SG-MCMC for continuous parameters and VI for discrete edge variables. A key technical innovation is the derivation of an equivalence between this augmented space and permutation-based DAG learning, enabling the use of differentiable gradient estimators such as the Sinkhorn operator for efficient optimization. The functional relationships between variables are modeled using neural networks under an additive noise model, with weight sharing and node embeddings to improve scalability. The overall inference procedure alternates between SG-MCMC updates for continuous parameters (node potentials and neural network weights) and variational updates for the binary edge variables, using a Gibbs sampling scheme.
16a44d0782699b43057151225773f3ebe2cd5918.experiment_details: Experiments are proposed on both synthetic and real-world datasets to evaluate posterior inference quality, scalability, and causal discovery accuracy. Synthetic data will be generated using randomly sampled DAGs from Erdős–Rényi and scale-free graph models, with both linear and nonlinear functional relationships, and varying numbers of variables (including high-dimensional settings with up to 100 nodes). Baselines for comparison include Bootstrap GES, BCD Nets, DDS, and DIBS, covering both variational and sampling-based Bayesian causal discovery methods. Evaluation metrics will include Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) to the true posterior, expected Structural Hamming Distance (E-SHD), edge orientation F1 score, and negative log-likelihood (NLL) on held-out data. Additional experiments will be conducted on semi-synthetic (SynTReN) and real-world (Sachs Protein Cells) datasets to assess practical applicability and robustness to model misspecification. Ablation studies will investigate the impact of initialization, number of SG-MCMC chains, and injected noise levels.
16a44d0782699b43057151225773f3ebe2cd5918.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to enable gradient-based MCMC sampling for Bayesian causal discovery in both linear and nonlinear models, directly sampling DAGs from the posterior without requiring DAG regularization. The method introduces a novel equivalence between augmented edge/potential space and permutation-based DAG learning, allowing the use of efficient, differentiable gradient estimators. The approach is model-agnostic, scalable to high-dimensional settings, and provides improved inference quality and computational efficiency compared to state-of-the-art baselines. Empirical results demonstrate superior performance in terms of posterior accuracy and scalability, including settings with up to 100 variables and nonlinear relationships.

16b459de55727171aff6ea674535bea499e58261.title: Simple is Effective: The Roles of Graphs and Large Language Models in Knowledge-Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
16b459de55727171aff6ea674535bea499e58261.research_question: How can knowledge graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (KG-based RAG) be improved to efficiently and effectively retrieve relevant subgraphs for large language model (LLM) reasoning, particularly for complex multi-hop question answering, while balancing retrieval effectiveness, efficiency, and explainability?
16b459de55727171aff6ea674535bea499e58261.hypothesis: Integrating a lightweight, parallelizable subgraph retriever that encodes directional structural distances, combined with prompt-based LLM reasoning over flexible subgraph forms, will yield superior retrieval effectiveness, efficiency, and explainability compared to existing KG-based RAG frameworks, without requiring LLM fine-tuning.
16b459de55727171aff6ea674535bea499e58261.proposed_method: A novel KG-based RAG framework will be developed that first extracts a relevant subgraph from the knowledge graph for each query and then employs an LLM to reason over the extracted subgraph. The subgraph retriever will be implemented as a lightweight multilayer perceptron (MLP) that scores triples in parallel using both semantic embeddings (from pre-trained text encoders) and directional distance encoding (DDE) features, which capture the structural relationship between candidate triples and query topic entities. The retriever will factorize the subgraph selection over triples, allowing for flexible and size-adjustable subgraph forms tailored to the LLM's context window and reasoning capacity. Retrieved triples will be linearized and incorporated into a dedicated prompt template for the LLM, which will generate both answers and knowledge-grounded explanations without requiring any LLM fine-tuning.
16b459de55727171aff6ea674535bea499e58261.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two challenging multi-hop KGQA benchmarks, WebQSP and CWQ, both based on Freebase. The evaluation will include both retrieval (triple/entity recall, wall-clock time) and question-answering (Macro-F1, Micro-F1, Hit@1, and a truth-grounded hallucination score) metrics. Baselines will include structure-free retrievers (cosine similarity), path-based retrievers, GNN-based retrievers, and recent KG-based RAG methods such as RoG, G-Retriever, and GNN-RAG. The proposed method will be paired with various LLMs (e.g., Llama3.1-8B-Instruct, Llama3.1-70B-Instruct, ChatGPT, GPT-4o) in a prompt-based, in-context learning setup. Ablation studies will examine the impact of retrieval size, structural encoding, and retriever variants. Generalization will be assessed by training retrievers on one dataset and evaluating on another.
16b459de55727171aff6ea674535bea499e58261.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a parallel triple-scoring subgraph retriever that combines semantic and directional structural features for efficient and flexible subgraph extraction. Unlike prior methods, the retriever supports arbitrary subgraph forms and size adjustment, enabling adaptation to different LLMs and query complexities. The use of directional distance encoding (DDE) for structural feature construction is claimed to outperform GNN-based and heuristic approaches in multi-hop reasoning. The approach is fully LLM-agnostic, requires no LLM fine-tuning, and is shown to provide state-of-the-art accuracy, efficiency, and explainability, including robust reduction of hallucinations and improved grounding of LLM responses.

16bcdb78924501f87e36881701f2383410f18e2d.title: Detecting Anomalies in Blockchain Transactions using Machine Learning Classifiers and Explainability Analysis
16bcdb78924501f87e36881701f2383410f18e2d.research_question: How can machine learning classifiers, enhanced with explainability techniques, be used to effectively detect anomalies in blockchain transaction data, particularly in the presence of extreme class imbalance?
16bcdb78924501f87e36881701f2383410f18e2d.hypothesis: Integrating advanced data balancing techniques and explainable AI methods into tree-based ensemble classifiers will significantly improve the detection accuracy and interpretability of anomalous blockchain transactions compared to traditional approaches.
16bcdb78924501f87e36881701f2383410f18e2d.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed for anomaly detection in blockchain transactions, focusing on Bitcoin data. The methodology begins with extensive data preprocessing and feature selection, including statistical testing (e.g., T-tests) to identify the most relevant transaction features. To address severe class imbalance, a novel under-sampling algorithm, XGBCLUS, based on eXtreme Gradient Boosting, will be introduced, iteratively selecting impactful majority class samples to balance the dataset. Multiple data balancing strategies will be explored, including established under-sampling (Random Under Sampling, Near-Miss) and over-sampling (SMOTE, ADASYN, SMOTEENN, SMOTETOMEK) techniques. The balanced data will be used to train both single and ensemble tree-based classifiers (Decision Tree, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, AdaBoost, XGBoost), with ensemble approaches including stacking (using Logistic Regression as a meta-classifier) and voting. To enhance transparency, eXplainable AI (XAI) methods, particularly SHAP, will be employed to analyze feature contributions and derive interpretable anomaly detection rules.
16bcdb78924501f87e36881701f2383410f18e2d.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize a large-scale Bitcoin transaction dataset from the IEEE Data Portal, containing over 30 million samples with only 108 labeled as anomalous. After preprocessing and feature selection, the dataset will be split into training and independent test sets (80/20 split). Data balancing will be applied exclusively to the training set.
