The performance of various single and ensemble classifiers will be evaluated under different balancing techniques, with comparisons made across baselines such as Random Under Sampling, Near-Miss, SMOTE, and ADASYN. Evaluation metrics will include Accuracy, True Positive Rate (TPR), False Positive Rate (FPR), and ROC-AUC, with 10-fold cross-validation used to ensure robustness. SHAP analysis will be conducted to interpret model predictions and identify key features influencing anomaly detection.
16bcdb78924501f87e36881701f2383410f18e2d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces XGBCLUS, a novel XGBoost-based under-sampling algorithm that iteratively selects majority class samples with significant impact on model performance, aiming to minimize the loss of important instances during balancing. The approach systematically compares a wide range of under-sampling, over-sampling, and combined balancing techniques for blockchain anomaly detection. Furthermore, the integration of tree-based ensemble classifiers with explainable AI (SHAP) provides both high detection performance and interpretability, addressing the lack of transparency in prior models. The proposal also derives explicit anomaly detection rules from decision trees, enhancing practical interpretability for blockchain transaction monitoring.

16d6e1ed1cf72212f6154644f3aa59d18bc95fda.title: DeepSeekMoE: Towards Ultimate Expert Specialization in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
16d6e1ed1cf72212f6154644f3aa59d18bc95fda.research_question: How can expert specialization in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models be maximized to improve parameter efficiency and performance, while maintaining or reducing computational costs compared to conventional MoE and dense architectures?
16d6e1ed1cf72212f6154644f3aa59d18bc95fda.hypothesis: Implementing fine-grained expert segmentation and shared expert isolation within MoE architectures will significantly enhance expert specialization, reduce knowledge redundancy, and result in improved performance and parameter efficiency compared to existing MoE models such as GShard, without increasing computational costs.
16d6e1ed1cf72212f6154644f3aa59d18bc95fda.proposed_method: A novel MoE architecture, DeepSeekMoE, will be developed to achieve ultimate expert specialization through two principal strategies: (1) Fine-grained expert segmentation, where each standard expert FFN is split into multiple smaller experts by reducing the intermediate hidden dimension, and a proportionally larger number of these fine-grained experts are activated per token, maintaining constant parameter and computational budgets; (2) Shared expert isolation, wherein a subset of experts is designated as shared and always activated for every token, capturing common knowledge and reducing redundancy among routed experts. The architecture will also incorporate expert-level and device-level balance losses to prevent routing collapse and ensure balanced computation across devices. All FFNs in the Transformer backbone will be replaced with MoE layers, and the routing will be managed by a top-k gating mechanism, with the number of nonzero gates adjusted according to the segmentation and shared expert strategies.
16d6e1ed1cf72212f6154644f3aa59d18bc95fda.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted at multiple model scales (e.g., 2B, 16B, and 145B parameters), using a large-scale multilingual corpus (primarily English and Chinese, with other languages included) for pretraining. Tokenization will employ byte pair encoding with vocabulary sizes scaled to model size. Baseline comparisons will include dense Transformer models, Hash Layer MoE, Switch Transformer, and GShard, with all models trained on the same data and under matched hyperparameters. Evaluation will be performed on a suite of zero-shot and few-shot benchmarks, including The Pile (language modeling, cross-entropy loss), HellaSwag, PIQA, ARC-easy, ARC-challenge (accuracy), RACE-high, RACE-middle (accuracy), HumanEval, MBPP (code generation, Pass@1), TriviaQA, and NaturalQuestions (exact match). Performance, parameter efficiency, and computational cost (FLOPs) will be measured, and ablation studies will be conducted to isolate the effects of each architectural innovation.
16d6e1ed1cf72212f6154644f3aa59d18bc95fda.novelty_claims: The proposed architecture introduces fine-grained expert segmentation and shared expert isolation as new strategies to maximize expert specialization in MoE language models. This approach enables more flexible and targeted expert activation, significantly reduces knowledge hybridity and redundancy, and approaches or surpasses the upper-bound performance of dense models with substantially lower computational cost. The method demonstrates superior scalability and parameter efficiency compared to existing MoE architectures, and supports deployment on single GPUs without quantization. Additionally, the architecture is validated across a wide range of tasks and model scales, and is made publicly available to foster open research.

16de2006e2960ba410772c6b6d460b83c0a5cc4b.title: Reproducible Scaling Laws for Contrastive Language-Image Learning
16de2006e2960ba410772c6b6d460b83c0a5cc4b.research_question: How do model size, dataset scale, and training compute affect the performance and scaling laws of contrastive language-image pre-training models across a variety of downstream tasks, and how can these scaling laws be systematically and reproducibly studied using open-source data and models?
16de2006e2960ba410772c6b6d460b83c0a5cc4b.hypothesis: Performance of contrastive language-image models will follow predictable power law scaling trends with respect to model size, data scale, and compute, but the scaling coefficients and trends will be influenced by the choice of pre-training dataset and task. Open-source datasets and models can enable reproducible and generalizable scaling law studies.
16de2006e2960ba410772c6b6d460b83c0a5cc4b.proposed_method: A comprehensive scaling law investigation will be conducted for contrastive language-image pre-training by systematically varying model architectures (e.g., ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16, ViT-L/14, ViT-H/14, ViT-g/14), dataset sizes (LAION-80M, LAION-400M, LAION-2B), and the number of samples seen during training (3B, 13B, 34B). All models will be trained using the OpenCLIP framework with distributed training across up to 1520 GPUs, employing large batch sizes (up to 88K), mixed precision (float16 or bfloat16 as appropriate), and the InfoNCE loss with AdamW optimization. Training schedules will be adapted to the number of samples seen using cosine annealing, and hyperparameters will be tuned to optimize validation loss and prevent instabilities. The methodology will closely follow standard CLIP procedures, with careful controls for batch size and training duration to ensure valid scaling comparisons.
16de2006e2960ba410772c6b6d460b83c0a5cc4b.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize the open-source LAION-400M and LAION-2B datasets for pre-training, with control experiments to validate subset equivalence. Models will be evaluated on a suite of downstream tasks: zero-shot classification (ImageNet, ImageNet-V2, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-Sketch, ObjectNet, ImageNet-A, VTAB), zero-shot retrieval (MS-COCO, Flickr30K), linear probing (ImageNet, CIFAR-100, VTAB, in both few-shot and full regimes), and end-to-end fine-tuning (ImageNet, ImageNet-22k, and eight diverse datasets). Baselines will include OpenAI CLIP models trained on private WIT-400M, with matched architectures and training recipes where possible. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy, Recall@K, and error rates. Scaling laws will be fit using power law relationships on the Pareto frontier of model performances, and bottleneck effects will be analyzed by varying data and sample scales independently.
16de2006e2960ba410772c6b6d460b83c0a5cc4b.novelty_claims: The proposed study will provide the first fully reproducible and open-source scaling law analysis for contrastive language-image models using public datasets and code. It will systematically disentangle the effects of model size, data scale, and compute on downstream task performance, revealing how scaling trends differ by task and pre-training dataset. The open release of all models, code, and evaluation workflows will enable the community to extend and validate scaling law research, addressing reproducibility challenges posed by prior work relying on private data and models. The study will also highlight the critical role of dataset design in scaling behavior and generalization, offering actionable insights for future dataset and model development.

16e57ac3e26f6b2ff083c86c3876077a2a2ec727.title: Gradient-based Bi-level Optimization for Deep Learning: A Survey
16e57ac3e26f6b2ff083c86c3876077a2a2ec727.research_question: How can gradient-based bi-level optimization frameworks be systematically formulated and applied to a wide range of deep learning problems, including hyperparameter optimization, meta-knowledge extraction, and tasks with complex nested structures?
16e57ac3e26f6b2ff083c86c3876077a2a2ec727.hypothesis: Gradient-based bi-level optimization, when properly formulated and equipped with efficient solvers, enables more effective and scalable solutions to deep learning problems involving nested or hierarchical objectives compared to classical or non-gradient-based approaches.
16e57ac3e26f6b2ff083c86c3876077a2a2ec727.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework for gradient-based bi-level optimization will be developed, encompassing both single-task and multi-task formulations. The approach will formalize the identification of inner and outer variables, establish criteria for when a problem is suitable for bi-level optimization, and provide guidelines for structuring objectives and constraints. The method will include detailed procedures for constructing differentiable relationships between inner and outer variables, and will implement multiple solver strategies for hypergradient computation, such as explicit gradient update, proxy update, implicit function update, and closed-form update. Special attention will be given to parameterization techniques for high-dimensional or discrete outer variables, including continuous relaxations and neural network-based parameterizations.
16e57ac3e26f6b2ff083c86c3876077a2a2ec727.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of deep learning tasks, including hyperparameter optimization (e.g., regularization, learning rate), neural architecture search, data distillation, adversarial attack generation, label learning, instance reweighting, and meta-learning (e.g., model initialization). Standard datasets such as CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet, and domain-specific datasets (e.g., for molecular conformation or protein structure) will be used. Baselines will include classical methods (random search, Bayesian optimization, evolutionary algorithms), alternate optimization, and state-of-the-art meta-learning algorithms. Evaluation metrics will be task-specific, such as validation/test accuracy for classification, mean squared error for regression, and downstream performance for meta-learning. Experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by controlling for computational resources, number of optimization steps, and hyperparameter search spaces.
16e57ac3e26f6b2ff083c86c3876077a2a2ec727.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified taxonomy and practical guide for formulating and solving gradient-based bi-level optimization problems in deep learning, covering both single-task and multi-task scenarios. It systematically categorizes bi-level problems based on the mathematical relationship between inner and outer objectives and the source of hypergradients. The framework supports efficient optimization of high-dimensional and discrete hyperparameters through advanced parameterization and solver techniques. Additionally, the proposal identifies and addresses open challenges in data optimization for scientific applications and the development of accurate explicit proxy updates, paving the way for future research directions in the field.

16f01c1b3ddd0b2abd5ddfe4fdb3f74767607277.title: Time-LLM: Time Series Forecasting by Reprogramming Large Language Models
16f01c1b3ddd0b2abd5ddfe4fdb3f74767607277.research_question: Can large language models (LLMs) be effectively adapted for general time series forecasting tasks, achieving high accuracy, data efficiency, and generalizability across domains without requiring fine-tuning or task-specific model design?
16f01c1b3ddd0b2abd5ddfe4fdb3f74767607277.hypothesis: Large language models, when reprogrammed through modality alignment and guided prompting, can serve as effective, general-purpose time series forecasters that outperform specialized models, particularly in few-shot and zero-shot learning scenarios.
16f01c1b3ddd0b2abd5ddfe4fdb3f74767607277.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed to reprogram frozen large language models (LLMs) for time series forecasting. The approach begins by partitioning multivariate time series into univariate series, which are normalized and segmented into patches. These patches are embedded and then reprogrammed into the LLM's input space using a small set of learned text prototypes, selected via a multi-head cross-attention mechanism to align time series and language modalities. To further enhance the LLM's reasoning abilities, a Prompt-as-Prefix (PaP) strategy is employed, enriching the input with dataset context, task instructions, and statistical summaries, all formulated in natural language. The LLM processes the combined prompt and reprogrammed patches, and the output is projected through a lightweight layer to generate the final forecasts. Only the input transformation and output projection parameters are trained; the backbone LLM remains frozen, ensuring efficiency and broad applicability.
16f01c1b3ddd0b2abd5ddfe4fdb3f74767607277.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a suite of mainstream time series forecasting benchmarks, including ETTh1, ETTh2, ETTm1, ETTm2, Weather, Electricity (ECL), Traffic, ILI, and the M4 dataset, covering both long-term and short-term forecasting tasks. The proposed method is compared against a comprehensive set of baselines, including state-of-the-art Transformer-based models (e.g., PatchTST, FEDformer, Autoformer), recent LLM-based approaches (e.g., GPT4TS, LLMTime), and other competitive models (e.g., DLinear, TimesNet, N-HiTS, N-BEATS). Evaluation metrics include mean square error (MSE), mean absolute error (MAE), symmetric mean absolute percentage error (SMAPE), mean absolute scaled error (MASE), and overall weighted average (OWA). Both few-shot (using 10% and 5% of training data) and zero-shot (cross-domain adaptation) scenarios are tested, with unified experimental configurations and seeds for fair comparison. Ablation studies are performed to assess the contributions of patch reprogramming, prompting, and various prompt components.
16f01c1b3ddd0b2abd5ddfe4fdb3f74767607277.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the concept of reprogramming frozen LLMs for time series forecasting by aligning modalities through learned text prototypes and augmenting reasoning via Prompt-as-Prefix, all without fine-tuning the backbone model. This approach demonstrates that time series forecasting can be cast as a 'language' task, enabling off-the-shelf LLMs to achieve or surpass state-of-the-art performance on diverse forecasting benchmarks. The method excels in few-shot and zero-shot settings, highlighting its data efficiency and generalizability. Additionally, the framework is highly parameter-efficient, requiring only minor trainable components, and offers extensibility for broader multimodal and sequential data tasks.

172069c1e484c342be4a6df04c6ec645993b4817.title: Closed-Form Diffeomorphic Transformations for Time Series Alignment
172069c1e484c342be4a6df04c6ec645993b4817.research_question: How can time series alignment be improved using highly expressive, differentiable, and invertible warping functions that preserve temporal topology, and can efficient, closed-form solutions for such transformations and their gradients be developed to enhance both accuracy and computational efficiency in joint alignment and classification tasks?
172069c1e484c342be4a6df04c6ec645993b4817.hypothesis: Closed-form expressions for the solution and gradient of diffeomorphic transformations under continuous piecewise-affine (CPA) velocity functions will enable more efficient, accurate, and generalizable time series alignment compared to existing numerical or discretization-based approaches.
172069c1e484c342be4a6df04c6ec645993b4817.proposed_method: A novel closed-form solution for the ordinary differential equation (ODE) governing one-dimensional diffeomorphic transformations will be derived under the assumption of continuous piecewise-affine (CPA) velocity functions. This approach will also provide a closed-form expression for the gradient of the transformation with respect to model parameters, enabling efficient and precise sensitivity analysis compatible with automatic differentiation frameworks. The method will be implemented as a highly optimized library (Diffeomorphic Fast Warping, DIFW) supporting both CPU (NumPy, PyTorch with C++) and GPU (PyTorch with CUDA) backends. The closed-form integration and its gradient will be incorporated into a temporal transformer network (TTN) architecture for time series alignment and classification, where the localization network outputs the parameters of the CPA velocity field for each input signal, and a differentiable sampler applies the learned diffeomorphic transformation.
172069c1e484c342be4a6df04c6ec645993b4817.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 84 datasets from the UCR Time Series Classification Archive, covering a wide variety of real-world time series alignment and classification tasks. The proposed method will be compared against several baselines, including Euclidean averaging, DTW Barycenter Averaging (DBA), SoftDTW, Diffeomorphic Temporal Alignment Nets (DTAN), and ResNet-TW. Evaluation will use Nearest Centroid Classification (NCC) accuracy as the primary metric, with additional analysis of computational efficiency (forward and backward pass times) and integration/gradient precision. Hyperparameters such as tessellation size, regularization strength, number of transformer layers, and scaling-and-squaring iterations will be tuned via grid search, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the trade-off between expressiveness and computational complexity.
172069c1e484c342be4a6df04c6ec645993b4817.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first closed-form expression for both the solution and gradient of CPA-based one-dimensional diffeomorphic transformations, providing significant improvements in computational efficiency, speed, and precision over existing numerical and adjoint-based methods. The method enables exact and efficient gradient computation, facilitating faster and more stable optimization in deep learning frameworks. The integration of these closed-form transformations into a temporal transformer network allows for highly expressive, generalizable, and scalable joint alignment of time series data, outperforming existing methods in both accuracy and efficiency across a large benchmark suite.

1733eb7792f7a43dd21f51f4d1017a1bffd217b5.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
1733eb7792f7a43dd21f51f4d1017a1bffd217b5.research_question: How effectively can language models utilize information distributed throughout long input contexts, particularly when relevant information is located at different positions within the context, and what factors influence their ability to robustly access and use such information for downstream tasks?
1733eb7792f7a43dd21f51f4d1017a1bffd217b5.hypothesis: Current language models do not robustly utilize information in long input contexts, with performance significantly affected by the position of relevant information; specifically, models are hypothesized to perform best when relevant information is at the beginning or end of the context and to struggle when it is in the middle, regardless of context window size.
1733eb7792f7a43dd21f51f4d1017a1bffd217b5.proposed_method: A comprehensive experimental framework will be developed to evaluate language models on tasks requiring retrieval and reasoning over long input contexts. The methodology involves controlled manipulation of input context length and the position of relevant information within the context. Two primary tasks will be used: multi-document question answering, where only one document contains the answer among distractors, and synthetic key-value retrieval, where the model must extract a value given a key from a large JSON object with randomly ordered pairs. Both open-source and proprietary language models, including decoder-only and encoder-decoder architectures, will be evaluated. Additional experiments will systematically vary architectural features (e.g., model type), prompt structure (e.g., query-aware contextualization), and fine-tuning strategies to isolate their effects on context utilization.
1733eb7792f7a43dd21f51f4d1017a1bffd217b5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using datasets such as NaturalQuestions-Open for multi-document question answering, with input contexts constructed from Wikipedia passages and distractors retrieved via a fine-tuned retrieval system. The key-value retrieval task will use randomly generated UUIDs to eliminate linguistic confounds. Model performance will be measured as a function of the position of relevant information (e.g., start, middle, end) and context length (ranging from a few thousand to over 100,000 tokens). Baseline models will include both standard and extended-context versions of state-of-the-art LLMs (e.g., GPT-3.5-Turbo, Claude-1.3, MPT-30B-Instruct, LongChat-13B, Flan-T5-XXL, Flan-UL2). Evaluation metrics will primarily be accuracy (correct answer extraction), with additional analysis of performance curves (e.g., U-shaped trends) and comparison to closed-book and oracle settings. Further, open-domain QA case studies will assess the trade-off between context length and downstream task performance.
1733eb7792f7a43dd21f51f4d1017a1bffd217b5.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces rigorous, position-controlled evaluation protocols for assessing long-context utilization in language models, revealing systematic positional biases (primacy and recency effects) that persist even in models with large context windows. The methodology isolates the impact of context position, model architecture, prompt structure, and fine-tuning, providing new insights into the limitations of current LLMs. The work establishes that extended context capacity does not guarantee robust use of information throughout the context and that simple architectural or prompting changes may not suffice to address these limitations. The proposal also provides new benchmarks and open-source evaluation resources to facilitate future research on long-context language modeling.

17501175894aa402b6bd93117aa04b24e909db8d.title: Dynamical Low-Rank Compression of Neural Networks with Robustness under Adversarial Attacks
17501175894aa402b6bd93117aa04b24e909db8d.research_question: How can neural networks be compressed to operate efficiently on resource-constrained devices while maintaining high accuracy and robustness against adversarial attacks?
17501175894aa402b6bd93117aa04b24e909db8d.hypothesis: Introducing a spectral regularizer that controls the condition number of low-rank core matrices in each neural network layer during dynamic low-rank training will mitigate the sensitivity of compressed models to adversarial perturbations without sacrificing accuracy on clean data.
17501175894aa402b6bd93117aa04b24e909db8d.proposed_method: A dynamic low-rank training scheme is proposed, in which each weight matrix in the neural network is factorized into orthonormal bases and a small core matrix. A novel, computationally efficient spectral regularizer is integrated into the training objective, penalizing deviations of the core matrix from a well-conditioned form by minimizing the distance of its Gram matrix to a scaled identity. The regularizer acts only on the small core matrices, ensuring minimal overhead. The training algorithm is rank-adaptive, allowing the rank of each layer to be automatically adjusted based on training dynamics, and maintains orthogonality of the bases throughout. The method is compatible with both fully connected and convolutional layers, using appropriate tensor decompositions, and supports integration with adversarial training and other robustness defenses.
17501175894aa402b6bd93117aa04b24e909db8d.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on multiple standard neural network architectures, including VGG11, VGG16, and ViT-16b, across datasets such as UCM, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet1k. The method is evaluated under various adversarial attack scenarios, including FGSM (ℓ1 and ℓ2), Jitter, and Mixup attacks, with a range of perturbation strengths. Baselines include uncompressed networks, standard low-rank training without regularization, and other state-of-the-art compression and robustness methods from the literature. Evaluation metrics include clean accuracy, adversarial accuracy, and compression rate (percentage of parameters pruned). Multiple training runs are performed to report mean and standard deviation, and experiments include both white-box and black-box attack settings as well as adversarial training.
17501175894aa402b6bd93117aa04b24e909db8d.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new spectral regularizer for low-rank neural network training that explicitly controls the condition number of compressed layers, leading to improved adversarial robustness. The approach is model- and data-agnostic, computationally efficient, and supports rank adaptivity, removing the need for manual rank selection. Theoretical guarantees are provided for the condition number bound and stability of the regularized dynamics. Empirical results demonstrate that the method achieves up to 94% compression while matching or surpassing the adversarial robustness and clean accuracy of uncompressed baselines, outperforming existing methods in both compression and robustness metrics.

17586f46d3d93c1c266ad5e57a09e4cb1f0a8617.title: On the Optimality of Misspecified Spectral Algorithms
17586f46d3d93c1c266ad5e57a09e4cb1f0a8617.research_question: Are spectral algorithms minimax optimal for nonparametric regression in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHS) when the true regression function lies in a less-smooth interpolation space, particularly for all smoothness parameters s in (0,1), and under what conditions on the RKHS embedding index and eigenvalue decay rate does this optimality hold?
17586f46d3d93c1c266ad5e57a09e4cb1f0a8617.hypothesis: Spectral algorithms achieve minimax optimal convergence rates for the generalization error in nonparametric regression for all smoothness parameters s in (0,1), provided that the RKHS embedding index and eigenvalue decay rate satisfy specific conditions, and without requiring additional boundedness assumptions on the true regression function.
17586f46d3d93c1c266ad5e57a09e4cb1f0a8617.proposed_method: A novel theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the minimax optimality of spectral algorithms in misspecified settings, where the true regression function lies in an interpolation space [H]^s of an RKHS H with s in (0,1). The approach will leverage real interpolation theory to establish Lq-embedding properties of these interpolation spaces, thereby enabling the removal of the boundedness assumption on the true function that was required in previous analyses. The convergence rates of spectral algorithms will be derived with respect to both the L2-norm and the more general [H]^γ-norm generalization error, using advanced operator-theoretic techniques. The methodology will be applied to a broad class of RKHSs, including those with specific eigenvalue decay rates and embedding indices, and will provide explicit characterizations of the regimes where minimax optimality is achieved.
17586f46d3d93c1c266ad5e57a09e4cb1f0a8617.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic and real-world datasets where the input space X is a compact subset of R^d and the output space Y is a subset of R. Various RKHSs will be considered, including those with uniformly bounded eigenfunctions, Sobolev RKHSs, shift-invariant kernels, and dot-product kernels on the sphere, each with known eigenvalue decay rates and embedding indices. Baseline methods will include state-of-the-art spectral algorithms such as kernel ridge regression, gradient flow, and spectral cut-off, with regularization parameters selected according to theoretical prescriptions. Evaluation metrics will focus on the excess risk, measured in both L2-norm and [H]^γ-norm, and results will be compared to known minimax lower bounds to assess optimality. Experimental setups will ensure sufficient sample sizes to observe asymptotic behaviors and will include statistical significance analysis for the observed convergence rates.
17586f46d3d93c1c266ad5e57a09e4cb1f0a8617.novelty_claims: The proposed research removes the previously necessary boundedness assumption on the true regression function for minimax optimality of spectral algorithms in the misspecified regime, by introducing and leveraging the Lq-embedding property of interpolation spaces. It extends the minimax optimality results to all smoothness parameters s in (0,1) for a broad class of RKHSs, including those with embedding index α = 1, such as Sobolev spaces and RKHSs with shift-invariant or dot-product kernels. The framework generalizes convergence rate analyses to the [H]^γ-norm, subsuming the L2-norm as a special case, and provides explicit characterizations of the optimality regime in terms of RKHS structural parameters. These contributions resolve a longstanding open problem in the theory of misspecified spectral algorithms.

1759d78e00b811b2b4b35b49e22f7ec11694f5ad.title: Simple linear attention language models balance the recall-throughput tradeoff
1759d78e00b811b2b4b35b49e22f7ec11694f5ad.research_question: Can language model architectures be designed to achieve high recall performance while significantly improving efficiency, particularly in terms of memory consumption and throughput, compared to traditional attention-based models?
1759d78e00b811b2b4b35b49e22f7ec11694f5ad.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that combining linear attention with small-window sliding window attention in a single architecture will enable language models to effectively balance the tradeoff between recall accuracy and efficiency, achieving recall performance comparable to full attention while substantially reducing memory and computational overhead.
1759d78e00b811b2b4b35b49e22f7ec11694f5ad.proposed_method: A new architecture, BASED, is proposed that integrates two key components: (1) global linear attention using a hardware-efficient 2nd-order Taylor approximation of the softmax function as the feature map, and (2) local exact softmax attention applied within small sliding windows (e.g., 64-128 tokens wide). The linear attention component enables modeling of long-range dependencies with a fixed-size recurrent state, while the sliding window attention provides precise local token interactions. The architecture allows for tuning of the window size and linear attention feature dimension to navigate the Pareto frontier between recall and memory usage. IO-aware CUDA algorithms are developed for both linear and sliding window attention to optimize for real-world GPU hardware, minimizing memory movement and maximizing throughput during both prefill and recurrent generation phases. Additional enhancements include the use of short gated convolutional layers to further improve local modeling.
1759d78e00b811b2b4b35b49e22f7ec11694f5ad.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training language models up to 1.3 billion parameters on the Pile dataset, with models evaluated on both overall language modeling perplexity and recall-intensive tasks, such as synthetic Multi-Query Associative Recall (MQAR), information extraction (SWDE, FDA), and question answering (SQuAD). Baselines will include Transformer++ (with modern improvements), Mamba, Hyena, H3, RWKV, and other efficient architectures. Evaluation metrics will include perplexity, recall accuracy, F1 scores, and average accuracy on the LM-Eval Harness suite. Efficiency will be measured in terms of throughput (tokens/ms) for both prefill and recurrent generation, with detailed microbenchmarks on NVIDIA H100 GPUs. Ablation studies will assess the impact of feature map choice, feature dimension, and window size on quality and efficiency.
1759d78e00b811b2b4b35b49e22f7ec11694f5ad.novelty_claims: The proposed architecture claims to expand the Pareto frontier of the recall-throughput tradeoff for language models by combining linear and sliding window attention in a simple, hardware-aware framework. BASED is designed to match or outperform state-of-the-art sub-quadratic models in perplexity and recall-intensive tasks, while providing up to 24× higher generation throughput compared to optimized attention implementations. The work introduces novel IO-aware CUDA algorithms for efficient linear attention, demonstrates that recall-memory tradeoffs are fundamental across architectures, and provides empirical and theoretical analysis supporting the design choices. The approach enables efficient navigation of the recall-efficiency tradeoff, achieving high recall with significantly reduced memory and computational requirements.

177741af2c2d93096ac8a10b3ea37a8ff8dc2fac.title: Improved Certified Defenses against Data Poisoning with (Deterministic) Finite Aggregation
177741af2c2d93096ac8a10b3ea37a8ff8dc2fac.research_question: How can certified defenses against general data poisoning attacks be improved to provide stronger pointwise robustness guarantees without sacrificing clean accuracy, particularly in deep learning models trained on data from diverse and potentially untrusted sources?
177741af2c2d93096ac8a10b3ea37a8ff8dc2fac.hypothesis: Strategically reusing training samples across multiple overlapping base classifiers in an aggregation-based defense will reduce the worst-case impact of poisoned samples, thereby improving certified robustness bounds against data poisoning attacks while maintaining clean accuracy.
177741af2c2d93096ac8a10b3ea37a8ff8dc2fac.proposed_method: A novel deterministic aggregation-based defense, termed Finite Aggregation, will be developed to improve certified robustness against data poisoning. The method first splits the training set into smaller disjoint subsets using a hash function, then spreads each subset to multiple larger, overlapping subsets via a balanced spreading function. Each of these larger subsets is used to train a base classifier, and the final prediction is made by majority voting across all base classifiers. The approach introduces two hyperparameters: k, controlling the number of partitions (and thus the sensitivity of each classifier), and d, controlling the spreading degree (i.e., how many base classifiers each sample is used in). The method is designed to ensure that every sample is reused in a structured manner, enabling finer-grained certification of robustness and reducing the adversary's ability to manipulate predictions through poisoning.
177741af2c2d93096ac8a10b3ea37a8ff8dc2fac.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification benchmarks including MNIST, CIFAR-10, and GTSRB. The evaluation will use deep neural networks as deterministic base classifiers, with training data sorted and hash functions fixed for reproducibility. Certified robustness will be measured in terms of certified fraction (the proportion of test samples robust to a given number of poisoning attacks), and clean accuracy will be tracked to ensure no degradation. Finite Aggregation will be compared directly against Deep Partition Aggregation (DPA) using the same base classifiers, and improvements in certified fraction and certified radius will be reported. Hyperparameters k and d will be varied to analyze the trade-offs between robustness, accuracy, and computational cost.
177741af2c2d93096ac8a10b3ea37a8ff8dc2fac.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a 'split & spread' protocol that enables strategic reuse of training samples across overlapping base classifiers, resulting in finer-grained certified robustness against data poisoning. This approach bridges deterministic and stochastic aggregation-based defenses, providing a new theoretical and practical framework that unifies prior methods. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art pointwise certified robustness on multiple benchmarks, with improvements in certified fraction up to 3-5% over previous methods, all while maintaining clean accuracy. The method also offers a deterministic and computationally efficient alternative to stochastic aggregation approaches, avoiding estimation errors and scaling issues.

177b49a8fac501645d9110226c55510e724e4929.title: Physically Consistent Learning of Conservative Lagrangian Systems with Gaussian Processes
177b49a8fac501645d9110226c55510e724e4929.research_question: How can data-driven modeling approaches be developed to learn uncertain Lagrangian systems in a manner that is physically consistent, ensuring properties such as energy conservation, positive definiteness, and equilibrium preservation, while accommodating noisy and partial measurements?
177b49a8fac501645d9110226c55510e724e4929.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a Gaussian Process-based modeling framework, explicitly structured to encode the energy components and differential equation structure of Lagrangian systems, can achieve physically consistent learning of conservative dynamics, guaranteeing properties such as energy conservation, positive definiteness, and equilibrium preservation, even in the presence of noisy and partial measurements.
177b49a8fac501645d9110226c55510e724e4929.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed for learning Lagrangian systems using Gaussian Processes (GPs) that are structurally tailored to the energy components (kinetic and potential) and the differential equation structure of the system. The method will introduce composite GPs for the Lagrangian, kinetic, and potential energies, with means and covariance functions designed to enforce quadratic forms and positive definiteness. Cholesky-decomposed matrix kernels will be employed to probabilistically guarantee the positive definiteness of the learned inertia and stiffness matrices. The approach will analytically embed the structure of the Euler-Lagrange equations using Nabla operators, enabling the GP to model the mapping from state variables to system torques while preserving physical properties such as energy conservation, passivity, and equilibrium. The method will accommodate noisy measurements in torques, velocities, and accelerations, and will require only differential input-to-output measurements, thus allowing for practical data collection.
177b49a8fac501645d9110226c55510e724e4929.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a two-link robotic manipulator, a standard benchmark for Lagrangian system identification. The method will be trained on a small set of input-output data pairs, with noisy torque and acceleration measurements, and noiseless position and velocity data. The learned model's performance will be evaluated in closed-loop control scenarios, comparing a standard PD controller with its L-GP-augmented counterpart for trajectory tracking tasks. Evaluation metrics will include tracking accuracy, energy conservation, and the preservation of physical properties such as positive definiteness of the learned inertia matrix. Additional analyses will assess the eigenvalue manifolds of the estimated inertia matrix and the accuracy of the potential energy estimates across the state space.
177b49a8fac501645d9110226c55510e724e4929.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a physically consistent, data-driven modeling framework for Lagrangian systems that analytically guarantees key physical properties such as energy conservation, quadratic form, and positive definiteness via Cholesky-decomposed matrix kernels. The method extends Gaussian Processes from scalar to symmetric matrix-valued functions and embeds the structure of the Euler-Lagrange equations directly into the GP model. It is the first to provide probabilistic guarantees for positive definiteness and equilibrium preservation in learned Lagrangian dynamics, while accommodating noisy and partial measurements. The framework enables reliable and physically consistent learning for control applications, bridging the gap between flexible data-driven models and physics-based constraints.

1784c987e681d60c634765fe64c8d9c26f73d5ff.title: SnapKV: LLM Knows What You are Looking for Before Generation
1784c987e681d60c634765fe64c8d9c26f73d5ff.research_question: How can the memory and computational efficiency of large language models (LLMs) be improved for long-context inference without significant loss in generation accuracy, particularly by optimizing the key-value (KV) cache used in attention mechanisms?
1784c987e681d60c634765fe64c8d9c26f73d5ff.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that only a subset of prompt tokens are essential for accurate response generation in LLMs, and that these critical attention features can be identified prior to generation. By selectively compressing the KV cache to retain only the most important features, it is possible to significantly reduce memory and computational overhead while maintaining comparable model performance.
1784c987e681d60c634765fe64c8d9c26f73d5ff.proposed_method: A novel, fine-tuning-free algorithm, SnapKV, will be developed to automatically compress the KV cache in LLMs. The method identifies crucial attention features for each attention head by analyzing attention allocation patterns within an 'observation window' at the end of the prompt. A voting mechanism aggregates attention weights from this window to select the most important prefix positions, which are then clustered using a pooling operation to preserve contextual integrity. The compressed KV cache is formed by concatenating the selected prefix features with the full observation window features, and this reduced cache is used during generation. This approach requires minimal code changes and does not alter the underlying model weights or architecture.
1784c987e681d60c634765fe64c8d9c26f73d5ff.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a variety of LLMs, including LWM-Text-Chat-1M, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2, LongChat-7b-v1.5-32k, Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1, and Command-R, with context lengths ranging from 16K to 1M tokens. Evaluation will utilize benchmarks such as LongBench (covering single/multi-document QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion), Needle-in-a-Haystack (testing retrieval in extremely long contexts), LongEval-Lines (for key-value retrieval in noisy contexts), and RAG tasks (retrieval-augmented generation). Baselines will include full KV caching and state-of-the-art compression methods like H2O. Metrics will include accuracy, F1-score, hit rate of selected features, decoding speed (latency), memory usage, and maximum processable sequence length. Ablation studies will assess the impact of pooling and clustering on retrieval accuracy.
1784c987e681d60c634765fe64c8d9c26f73d5ff.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a context-aware, observation window-based KV cache compression strategy that is both fine-tuning-free and minimally invasive to existing LLM implementations. Unlike prior methods, SnapKV targets prompt KV cache compression (not just generation-phase cache), leverages dynamic attention allocation patterns for feature selection, and employs clustering to maintain contextual integrity. The approach achieves substantial improvements in decoding speed (up to 3.6x), memory efficiency (up to 8.2x), and enables processing of up to 380K tokens on a single GPU with negligible performance degradation. SnapKV demonstrates robust performance across diverse tasks and models, outperforming existing baselines in both efficiency and accuracy.

1784cd42207a12bdc4061bb0f78bc8d5c82f61dd.title: Information Flow Routes: Automatically Interpreting Language Models at Scale
1784cd42207a12bdc4061bb0f78bc8d5c82f61dd.research_question: How can the internal information flow within large language models be automatically and efficiently interpreted at scale, in a way that is generalizable across predictions, domains, and model architectures?
1784cd42207a12bdc4061bb0f78bc8d5c82f61dd.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that an attribution-based, top-down extraction of information flow routes can efficiently and comprehensively reveal the most important internal circuits and model components responsible for specific predictions, outperforming existing activation patching methods in speed, generality, and informativeness.
1784cd42207a12bdc4061bb0f78bc8d5c82f61dd.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed to automatically construct information flow graphs for language model predictions, where nodes represent token representations and edges correspond to model computations (such as attention heads and feed-forward blocks). The method will extract the most important subgraph for each prediction by tracing information backwards from the output, retaining only the nodes and edges with the highest attribution-based importance. Edge importance will be quantified using a modified version of the ALTI (Aggregation of Layer-Wise Token-to-Token Interactions) attribution method, which measures the contribution of each edge to the final prediction. The approach will operate in a top-down manner, starting from the output residual stream and recursively including only those upstream components whose contributions exceed a tunable threshold. This process will require only a single forward pass per prediction, making it highly scalable for large models.
1784cd42207a12bdc4061bb0f78bc8d5c82f61dd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on transformer-based language models, including Llama2-7B, OPT-125M, and GPT2-Small. The evaluation will include both general and task-specific analyses, using datasets such as C4, FLORES-200 (English, Russian, Italian, Spanish), CodeParrot (code), and arithmetic tasks (addition/subtraction). Baseline comparisons will be made against activation patching workflows, including ACDC, for tasks like Indirect Object Identification (IOI) and Greater-Than, using both original and contrastive templates. Evaluation metrics will include the accuracy and interpretability of extracted circuits, activation frequency of model components, computational efficiency (runtime), and the ability to recover known circuits. Additional analyses will explore component specialization across domains and part-of-speech, using t-SNE visualizations and singular value decomposition of attention head outputs.
1784cd42207a12bdc4061bb0f78bc8d5c82f61dd.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces an attribution-based, fully automated approach to extracting information flow routes in language models, eliminating the need for human-designed templates and multiple forward passes required by activation patching. It enables efficient, scalable, and general interpretation of model behavior for any prediction, achieving approximately 100x speedup over existing methods. The approach provides new insights into model component specialization (e.g., attention heads for subword merging and previous token handling), reveals domain- and task-specific circuits, and supports fine-grained analysis of information flow patterns that were previously inaccessible. This framework is the first to systematically analyze and generalize the importance of attention heads and feed-forward blocks across both general and domain-specific settings in large language models.

17a1e1a7db6d3694874ee32d84c4825a244241ad.title: Reducing Tool Hallucination via Reliability Alignment
17a1e1a7db6d3694874ee32d84c4825a244241ad.research_question: How can the reliability of large language models (LLMs) in interacting with external tools be systematically evaluated and improved, particularly with respect to reducing tool hallucinations that negatively impact task performance and system efficiency?
17a1e1a7db6d3694874ee32d84c4825a244241ad.hypothesis: Expanding the tool-use action space of LLMs to include indecisive actions, combined with reliability-focused alignment techniques and specialized evaluation metrics, will significantly reduce tool hallucinations, improve task reliability, and enhance the efficiency of LLM tool interactions.
17a1e1a7db6d3694874ee32d84c4825a244241ad.proposed_method: A comprehensive reliability alignment framework, named Relign, will be developed to address tool hallucinations in LLMs. The method will first systematically define and categorize tool hallucinations into selection and usage types, and introduce an automated evaluation pipeline combining rule-based and LLM-based evaluators for accurate detection. The action space for tool-use will be expanded to include indecisive actions, such as deferring tool use, seeking clarification, or dynamically adjusting tool selection, allowing models to avoid unnecessary or erroneous tool calls. Training will involve a two-stage process: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on reliability-focused data to teach the model to handle indecisive actions, followed by Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) using preference pairs generated from sampled tool-use trajectories and hallucination evaluations. Specialized data synthesis pipelines will generate training data that simulate challenging tool-use scenarios, such as missing parameters and tool-task mismatches.
17a1e1a7db6d3694874ee32d84c4825a244241ad.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using three main datasets: ToolBench, StableToolBench, and the newly constructed RelyToolBench, which includes additional subsets specifically designed to test tool selection and usage hallucinations. Models such as LLaMA-3.1, Qwen2.5, and ToolLLaMA will be evaluated, with training performed on 10,000 samples and batch sizes of 32, using standard hyperparameters. Baselines will include RLHF, StepTool, SFT, DPO, and their combinations. Evaluation metrics will include the Reliable Pass Rate (RePR), Benefit-Cost Utility, tool hallucination rate, and average number of tool calls. Additional out-of-distribution generalization tests will be performed on APIBench to assess robustness. All evaluations will utilize GPT-4O as an LLM-based evaluator, and experiments will be run on Nvidia A800 GPUs.
17a1e1a7db6d3694874ee32d84c4825a244241ad.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a systematic definition and categorization of tool hallucinations, along with an automated hybrid evaluation framework. It presents the first reliability alignment framework for tool-augmented LLMs that expands the action space to include indecisive actions, enabling models to defer tool use or seek clarification. The RelyToolBench benchmark and novel reliability-aware metrics (Reliable Pass Rate and Benefit-Cost Utility) are proposed for rigorous, hallucination-aware evaluation. The approach integrates preference-based optimization and data synthesis pipelines to align LLM behavior with reliability objectives, demonstrating significant reductions in tool hallucinations and improvements in efficiency and reliability over existing methods.

17a6116e5bbd8b87082cbb2e795885567300c483.title: Quantifying Language Models' Sensitivity to Spurious Features in Prompt Design or: How I learned to start worrying about prompt formatting
17a6116e5bbd8b87082cbb2e795885567300c483.research_question: How sensitive are large language models to meaning-preserving variations in prompt formatting, and how can this sensitivity be systematically quantified and reported to ensure fair and robust evaluation of model performance?
17a6116e5bbd8b87082cbb2e795885567300c483.hypothesis: Large language models exhibit significant and unpredictable sensitivity to semantically equivalent but differently formatted prompts, and this sensitivity is not eliminated by increasing model size, number of few-shot examples, or instruction tuning. Systematic exploration and reporting of performance across plausible prompt formats will reveal substantial variance that is currently underreported.
17a6116e5bbd8b87082cbb2e795885567300c483.proposed_method: A novel algorithm, FORMATSPREAD, will be developed to efficiently estimate the performance spread of language models across a space of semantically equivalent prompt formats. This approach will use a manually constructed grammar to define the space of plausible prompt formats, ensuring semantic equivalence by restricting modifications to features such as separators, casing, and enumeration. FORMATSPREAD will employ Bayesian optimization, specifically Thompson sampling, to search for the highest and lowest performing formats within a user-specified computational budget, without requiring access to model weights. The method will evaluate sampled prompt formats on a target task and report the interval of expected model performance, enabling robust and fair model comparisons.
17a6116e5bbd8b87082cbb2e795885567300c483.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse subset of 53 tasks from the Super-NaturalInstructions benchmark, covering both multiple-choice and classification tasks. Several widely used open-source LLMs, including LLaMA-2 (7B, 13B, 70B), Falcon-7B, Falcon-7B-Instruct, and GPT-3.5-Turbo, will be evaluated in few-shot learning settings. For each task, prompt templates will be constructed using the grammar, and a fixed set and order of few-shot examples will be used to control for confounding factors. Evaluation metrics will include ranking accuracy and exact prefix matching. Baselines will include naive and UCB sampling for estimating performance spread, and the efficiency and accuracy of FORMATSPREAD will be compared against these baselines under various computational budgets. Additional analyses will quantify the impact of individual formatting features and assess the identifiability of prompt formats via model embeddings.
17a6116e5bbd8b87082cbb2e795885567300c483.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first systematic framework for quantifying LLM sensitivity to meaning-preserving prompt formatting choices using a formal grammar and Bayesian optimization. FORMATSPREAD enables efficient estimation of performance spread without access to model internals, making it applicable to API-gated models. The approach provides actionable recommendations for reporting performance intervals rather than single-format results, challenging current evaluation practices. The proposal also offers new insights into the non-monotonicity and unpredictability of prompt format effects, and demonstrates that individual formatting changes can yield large and non-intuitive performance differences.

17b0637c32a0b67b69f7c8e90146af37ca6f3789.title: Iterative Nash Policy Optimization: Aligning LLMs with General Preferences via No-Regret Learning
17b0637c32a0b67b69f7c8e90146af37ca6f3789.research_question: How can large language models be aligned with general human preferences in reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF) settings, without relying on restrictive assumptions about preference transitivity or the Bradley-Terry model?
17b0637c32a0b67b69f7c8e90146af37ca6f3789.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a no-regret learning algorithm, formulated from a game-theoretic perspective and leveraging only binary preference signals, can effectively learn a Nash policy that aligns large language models with general human preferences, outperforming existing RLHF methods based on the Bradley-Terry model.
17b0637c32a0b67b69f7c8e90146af37ca6f3789.proposed_method: A novel online algorithm, Iterative Nash Policy Optimization (INPO), will be developed to align large language models with general preferences. The approach formulates the alignment problem as a symmetric two-player game, where the Nash equilibrium corresponds to the optimal policy. The method employs online mirror descent (OMD) as a no-regret learning algorithm, iteratively updating the policy by minimizing a new population loss objective that does not require explicit estimation of expected win rates for individual responses. At each iteration, the current policy generates response pairs for prompts, and a preference oracle provides binary feedback indicating which response is preferred. The policy is then updated to minimize the population loss over the collected preference dataset, incorporating KL regularization to maintain stability and prevent reward hacking. The algorithm is designed to be practical, requiring only binary preference signals and sampling from the current policy, thus avoiding computationally expensive normalization or win rate estimation.
17b0637c32a0b67b69f7c8e90146af37ca6f3789.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a supervised fine-tuned LLaMA-3-8B model as the backbone, following an online RLHF workflow. At each iteration, the current policy will generate responses to a set of prompts, and preference signals will be obtained using either a BT reward model or a general preference model. The best and worst responses will be selected via a tournament strategy, requiring only O(K) preference queries per prompt. The proposed method will be evaluated on widely used benchmarks including AlpacaEval2.0, Arena-Hard v0.1, and MT-Bench, using win rate and length-controlled win rate as primary metrics, with GPT-4Turbo as the judge model. Additional evaluations will be performed on academic benchmarks such as IFEval, GPQA, MMLU, Hellaswag, TruthfulQA, and GSM8K to assess reasoning and factual accuracy. Baselines for comparison will include iterative DPO, SPPO, and other state-of-the-art online RLHF algorithms, as well as open- and closed-source LLMs. Ablation studies will be conducted to assess the impact of KL regularization.
17b0637c32a0b67b69f7c8e90146af37ca6f3789.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a game-theoretic, no-regret learning framework for RLHF that does not rely on the Bradley-Terry model or transitive preference assumptions. The new population loss objective enables direct learning from binary preference signals without estimating expected win rates, reducing annotation and computational costs. The algorithm achieves last-iterate convergence to the Nash policy, is practical to implement, and demonstrates substantial improvements over state-of-the-art online RLHF algorithms on multiple benchmarks. The approach also shows robustness when evaluated with both BT-based and general preference models, and maintains or improves performance on academic reasoning and factuality benchmarks.

17d068e78e6f25e65cb08319b19b58279bb8b214.title: Understanding Diffusion Models: A Unified Perspective
17d068e78e6f25e65cb08319b19b58279bb8b214.research_question: How can diffusion models be understood and unified within the broader context of probabilistic generative modeling frameworks, such as variational autoencoders and hierarchical VAEs, and what are the mathematical and algorithmic implications of this unified perspective for generative modeling?
17d068e78e6f25e65cb08319b19b58279bb8b214.hypothesis: Diffusion models can be rigorously interpreted as a special case of Markovian Hierarchical Variational Autoencoders with linear Gaussian transitions, and this perspective enables a principled derivation of their training objectives, optimization strategies, and connections to other generative models.
17d068e78e6f25e65cb08319b19b58279bb8b214.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that formalizes diffusion models as Markovian Hierarchical Variational Autoencoders (MHVAEs) with specific restrictions: the latent dimension matches the data dimension, encoder transitions are fixed linear Gaussians, and the noise schedule is chosen to ensure the final latent is standard Gaussian. The joint and posterior distributions will be mathematically derived, and the Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO) will be decomposed into interpretable terms: reconstruction, prior matching, and consistency (or denoising matching). The approach will leverage the reparameterization trick and Monte Carlo estimates for tractable optimization. Theoretical derivations will be provided to show equivalence between the proposed diffusion model framework and existing score-based and likelihood-based generative models.
17d068e78e6f25e65cb08319b19b58279bb8b214.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image datasets such as CIFAR-10, CelebA, and ImageNet to evaluate the generative quality and likelihood estimation capabilities of the proposed unified diffusion model framework. Baselines will include traditional VAEs, hierarchical VAEs, and state-of-the-art diffusion models. Evaluation metrics will comprise negative log-likelihood, Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), and Inception Score (IS) for sample quality, as well as ablation studies to assess the impact of different noise schedules and parameterizations. The experimental setup will involve training models with varying numbers of diffusion steps (T), analyzing the variance of Monte Carlo estimates, and comparing optimization stability and sample diversity.
17d068e78e6f25e65cb08319b19b58279bb8b214.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified mathematical perspective that rigorously connects diffusion models to hierarchical variational inference, providing clear derivations of training objectives and optimization strategies. The framework decomposes the ELBO for diffusion models into interpretable components, enabling lower-variance estimation and principled analysis of the denoising process. This approach clarifies the relationship between diffusion models and other generative modeling paradigms, and offers new insights for designing and optimizing future generative models.

17f75f98cb3c331c048fcbb1eaa59c094f65e696.title: Hierarchical Decomposition of Prompt-Based Continual Learning: Rethinking Obscured Sub-optimality
17f75f98cb3c331c048fcbb1eaa59c094f65e696.research_question: How can continual learning with prompt-based methods be improved, especially under realistic self-supervised pre-training scenarios, to better incorporate task-specific knowledge and overcome sub-optimality in downstream tasks?
17f75f98cb3c331c048fcbb1eaa59c094f65e696.hypothesis: Explicit hierarchical decomposition and optimization of continual learning objectives—specifically within-task prediction, task-identity inference, and task-adaptive prediction—using ensembles of task-specific prompts and statistical modeling of representations, will significantly improve continual learning performance and robustness across pre-training paradigms, particularly in self-supervised settings.
17f75f98cb3c331c048fcbb1eaa59c094f65e696.proposed_method: A novel framework, termed Hierarchical Decomposition Prompt (HiDe-Prompt), will be developed to explicitly optimize three hierarchical components of continual learning: within-task prediction (WTP), task-identity inference (TII), and task-adaptive prediction (TAP). The method will construct an expandable pool of task-specific prompts, leveraging a prompt ensemble strategy to incorporate and transfer knowledge across tasks while freezing previous prompts to prevent forgetting. Statistical modeling of both uninstructed and instructed representations will be performed, typically using Gaussian approximations for each class, to facilitate TII and TAP. A contrastive regularization strategy will be introduced to coordinate and align the hierarchical components, ensuring compatibility and reducing inter-task overlap in the representation space. The framework will employ auxiliary output layers for TII and TAP, trained with cross-entropy losses on sampled pseudo-representations, and will be computationally efficient due to the lightweight nature of these layers.
17f75f98cb3c331c048fcbb1eaa59c094f65e696.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple class-incremental learning (CIL) benchmarks, including Split CIFAR-100, Split ImageNet-R, 5-Datasets, and Split CUB-200. Both supervised (ImageNet-21K) and several state-of-the-art self-supervised pre-training paradigms (iBOT, DINO, MoCo) will be evaluated using pre-trained ViT-B/16 backbones. Baselines for comparison will include L2P, DualPrompt, S-Prompt++, and CODA-Prompt, with consistent training regimes and hyperparameters (e.g., Adam optimizer, batch size 128, learning rates as per baseline requirements). Evaluation metrics will include final average accuracy (FAA), cumulative average accuracy (CAA), and final forgetting measure (FFM), with results averaged over multiple runs and random splits. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the contribution of each hierarchical component and the effect of contrastive regularization. Additional analyses will investigate memory and computational efficiency, as well as robustness to pre-training data disjointness.
17f75f98cb3c331c048fcbb1eaa59c094f65e696.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a theoretically grounded hierarchical decomposition of the continual learning objective, enabling explicit and synergistic optimization of within-task prediction, task-identity inference, and task-adaptive prediction. The method leverages statistical modeling of both uninstructed and instructed representations, coordinated by a novel contrastive regularization mechanism, to overcome the sub-optimality of existing prompt-based continual learning methods—especially under self-supervised pre-training. The framework achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse benchmarks and pre-training paradigms in a rehearsal-free setting, demonstrates superior robustness and efficiency, and generalizes to other parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques.

17fbffb05fa14e21d1c506fd5f0f568b955fe983.title: Do All Languages Cost the Same? Tokenization in the Era of Commercial Language Models
17fbffb05fa14e21d1c506fd5f0f568b955fe983.research_question: Do commercial language model APIs provide equitable cost and utility across different languages, or do tokenization practices lead to disparities in pricing and model performance for speakers of various languages and scripts?
17fbffb05fa14e21d1c506fd5f0f568b955fe983.hypothesis: Tokenization strategies in commercial language models, particularly those based on byte-level subword segmentation, result in non-uniform fragmentation rates across languages, causing higher costs and lower model utility for speakers of underrepresented or non-Latin script languages.
17fbffb05fa14e21d1c506fd5f0f568b955fe983.proposed_method: A systematic analysis will be conducted to quantify the impact of tokenization on cost and utility across languages in commercial language model APIs. The approach will involve measuring the average number of tokens needed to represent the same information in a parallel multilingual corpus using the APIs' tokenizers. Further, the study will evaluate the downstream effects on model utility by performing in-context learning experiments on a range of multilingual NLP tasks, such as classification, span prediction, and summarization, across diverse languages and scripts. The methodology will also include training custom BBPE tokenizers on controlled parallel corpora to disentangle the effects of training data proportion and inherent language/script properties on fragmentation rates. Finally, the analysis will correlate these findings with socio-economic indicators of language communities to assess the broader implications of pricing disparities.
17fbffb05fa14e21d1c506fd5f0f568b955fe983.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize two major language models: ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo) via OpenAI's API and BLOOMZ via Huggingface's API. The FLORES-200 parallel corpus will be used to measure tokenization fragmentation rates across 22 typologically diverse languages. For downstream utility and cost analysis, tasks will include XNLI (cross-lingual inference), XFACT (fact verification), XQUAD (question answering), CrossSum, and XLSUM (summarization), covering a broad spectrum of languages and scripts. Evaluation will be performed in a k-shot in-context learning setup, with English instructions and varying numbers of demonstrations, constrained by the token limits of each API. Baselines will include relative cost and performance in English versus other languages, and evaluation metrics will comprise standard task-specific scores (e.g., F1, exact match) and the average number of tokens per sequence. Socio-economic analysis will involve correlating API costs and model utility with the Human Development Index (HDI) of countries where the languages are spoken.
17fbffb05fa14e21d1c506fd5f0f568b955fe983.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a comprehensive, empirical framework for evaluating the fairness of commercial language model API pricing and utility across a wide range of languages and scripts. It uniquely combines tokenization analysis, downstream task performance, and socio-economic impact assessment, highlighting systemic inequities in current token-based pricing models. The approach goes beyond prior work by controlling for content with parallel corpora, training custom tokenizers to isolate contributing factors, and directly linking technical disparities to real-world economic accessibility. The findings are expected to inform more equitable API pricing policies and raise awareness of the overlooked role of tokenization in multilingual NLP accessibility.

1827dd28ef866eaeb929ddf4bcfa492880aba4c7.title: A Stitch in Time Saves Nine: Detecting and Mitigating Hallucinations of LLMs by Validating Low-Confidence Generation
1827dd28ef866eaeb929ddf4bcfa492880aba4c7.research_question: How can hallucinations in large language models (LLMs) be effectively detected and mitigated during the text generation process to improve their reliability and trustworthiness across diverse domains and tasks?
1827dd28ef866eaeb929ddf4bcfa492880aba4c7.hypothesis: Actively detecting low-confidence concepts during generation using model uncertainty signals, validating these concepts with external knowledge, and repairing hallucinated content in real-time will significantly reduce the rate and propagation of hallucinations in LLM outputs without introducing new errors.
1827dd28ef866eaeb929ddf4bcfa492880aba4c7.proposed_method: A two-stage framework is proposed, consisting of active hallucination detection and mitigation during LLM text generation. In the detection stage, each generated sentence is analyzed to identify key concepts using an instruction-based approach, which does not require external tools. Model uncertainty for each concept is quantified using logit output values, specifically the minimum softmax probability across concept tokens, to flag low-confidence candidates. For these uncertain concepts, validation questions are generated (preferably yes/no), and relevant knowledge is retrieved via web search APIs to answer the questions. If a hallucination is detected, the mitigation stage repairs the sentence by removing or substituting the hallucinated information, leveraging the retrieved evidence, and the repaired sentence is appended to the prompt for continued generation. This iterative process prevents the propagation of hallucinations in subsequent sentences.
1827dd28ef866eaeb929ddf4bcfa492880aba4c7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using GPT-3.5 (text-davinci-003) and Vicuna-13B as LLMs, evaluated on an 'article generation' task across 150 topics from diverse domains (sports, politics, music, literature, etc.). For each topic, the first five generated sentences will be manually annotated for sentence-level and concept-level hallucinations using web search as the reference. Baselines will include the unmodified LLM outputs and post-hoc detection/mitigation methods. Evaluation metrics will include hallucination rate reduction, recall and precision of detection, and the success rate of mitigation (i.e., percentage of hallucinations successfully repaired without introducing new errors). Additional studies will assess performance on multi-hop and false premise questions.
1827dd28ef866eaeb929ddf4bcfa492880aba4c7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces an active, in-generation hallucination detection and mitigation framework that leverages model uncertainty and external knowledge retrieval, rather than relying solely on post-hoc filtering. The method uniquely combines uncertainty-based candidate selection, instruction-driven concept and validation question generation, and real-time sentence repair to prevent hallucination propagation. Experiments demonstrate substantial reductions in hallucination rates across models and domains, with high recall and minimal introduction of new errors, establishing the approach as a robust and generalizable solution for improving LLM reliability.

182c7b40ff7560a5545764814338f55a2098e441.title: Reinforced Self-Training (ReST) for Language Modeling
182c7b40ff7560a5545764814338f55a2098e441.research_question: How can large language models be efficiently aligned with human preferences in generative language tasks, such as machine translation, while reducing computational costs and maintaining or improving output quality compared to existing reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) methods?
182c7b40ff7560a5545764814338f55a2098e441.hypothesis: Iterative application of a reinforced self-training (ReST) algorithm, which alternates between generating new training data from the current policy and improving the policy using offline reinforcement learning with filtered high-reward samples, will yield language models that are better aligned with human preferences and more computationally efficient than traditional online RLHF approaches.
182c7b40ff7560a5545764814338f55a2098e441.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces Reinforced Self-Training (ReST), a growing-batch reinforcement learning framework for aligning language models with human preferences. The approach begins with a supervised policy trained via negative log-likelihood on a dataset of input-output pairs. In each iteration, a Grow step generates new output samples from the current policy, augmenting the training set with synthetic data. These samples are scored using a learned reward model trained on human preferences, and only those above a dynamic threshold are retained. The Improve step then fine-tunes the policy on this filtered dataset using an offline RL objective, such as reward-weighted behavioral cloning or other offline RL losses. Multiple Improve steps with increasing thresholds are performed per Grow step to incrementally raise data quality, and the process is repeated for several Grow-Improve cycles, with hyperparameters such as the number of steps and thresholds tuned empirically.
182c7b40ff7560a5545764814338f55a2098e441.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on established machine translation benchmarks, including IWSLT 2014, WMT 2020, and a high-fidelity internal Web Domain dataset, each with distinct language pairs. The evaluation will use both automated metrics (e.g., Metric X, BLEURT, COMET, BLEU) and human preference ratings. Baselines will include supervised learning (behavioral cloning), various offline RL algorithms (Offline Actor Critic, BVMPO, GOLD), and online RL (PPO). Key experimental variables include the number of Grow and Improve steps, filtering thresholds, and loss functions. The impact of Best-of-N sampling at inference will also be assessed. Performance will be measured in terms of average reward model scores, BLEU scores, and human evaluation differences, with careful tracking of computational efficiency and sample diversity.
182c7b40ff7560a5545764814338f55a2098e441.novelty_claims: The proposed approach offers a novel decoupling of data generation and policy improvement in RLHF for language models, enabling efficient reuse of synthetic data and iterative policy refinement. Unlike standard online RLHF, ReST amortizes the cost of data generation across multiple policy updates, reducing computational burden. The method supports flexible integration of various offline RL losses and filtering mechanisms, and demonstrates that iterative filtering with increasing thresholds leads to higher quality models. ReST is claimed to outperform both supervised and online RL baselines in terms of alignment with human preferences and reward model scores, while being more stable, interpretable, and hyperparameter-efficient.

184d6cc92ed61679f5f500289c782a7d83451c05.title: Basis Sharing: Cross-Layer Parameter Sharing for Large Language Model Compression
184d6cc92ed61679f5f500289c782a7d83451c05.research_question: How can parameter sharing across layers be leveraged to achieve more effective compression of large language models (LLMs) without significant loss in performance, and what are the optimal strategies for selecting which weight matrices and layers to share?
184d6cc92ed61679f5f500289c782a7d83451c05.hypothesis: Parameter sharing across selected layers and weight matrix types, using a shared set of basis vectors and unique coefficients derived via SVD and input-aware scaling, will enable higher compression ratios for LLMs while maintaining or improving performance compared to state-of-the-art SVD-based and parameter sharing methods.
184d6cc92ed61679f5f500289c782a7d83451c05.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a cross-layer parameter sharing framework for compressing LLMs, termed Basis Sharing. Weight matrices from selected types and layers are horizontally concatenated and then decomposed using singular value decomposition (SVD) after scaling with a matrix S that reflects input data statistics. The decomposition yields a set of shared basis vectors (basis matrix) and layer-specific coefficient matrices. During inference, the original weight matrices are reconstructed as linear combinations of the shared basis and unique coefficients, with the scaling matrix applied to preserve the effect of input data. The method includes a systematic procedure for selecting which types of weight matrices and which groups of layers are suitable for sharing, based on minimizing Frobenius loss and empirical evaluation of compression error.
184d6cc92ed61679f5f500289c782a7d83451c05.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple LLMs, including the LLaMA family (LLaMA-7B, LLaMA-13B, LLaMA-30B, LLaMA2-7B), OPT-6.7B, Mistral-7B, and GPT-2. Evaluation will use language modeling datasets such as WikiText-2, PTB, and C4, as well as seven reasoning datasets (OpenbookQA, WinoGrande, HellaSwag, PIQA, MathQA, ARC-e, ARC-c), with zero-shot evaluation via the LM-Evaluation-Harness framework. Baselines will include SVD, FWSVD, ASVD, SVD-LLM, and Dynamic Tying. Metrics will include perplexity for generation tasks and accuracy for reasoning tasks, under compression ratios ranging from 20% to 50%. Additional experiments will investigate the impact of grouping different numbers of layers for basis sharing, the effect of LoRA and full parameter fine-tuning, and real hardware throughput on NVIDIA A100 GPUs.
