184d6cc92ed61679f5f500289c782a7d83451c05.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to systematically exploit cross-layer parameter sharing in pretrained LLMs via SVD, representing weight matrices as combinations of shared basis vectors and unique coefficients. It introduces an input-aware scaling mechanism to align the decomposition with inference-time data distributions, and provides principled criteria for selecting matrix types and layer groupings to optimize compression and performance. The method achieves superior compression ratios and performance compared to state-of-the-art SVD-based and parameter sharing techniques, particularly under high compression ratios, and is demonstrated to be effective across multiple LLM architectures and scales without requiring retraining from scratch.

18594d3f15b39385bace39657d14f0c8c7479db1.title: LLM2Vec: Large Language Models Are Secretly Powerful Text Encoders
18594d3f15b39385bace39657d14f0c8c7479db1.research_question: Can decoder-only large language models (LLMs) be effectively transformed into strong, universal text encoders for word- and sequence-level natural language processing tasks, without requiring extensive supervised data or expensive adaptation procedures?
18594d3f15b39385bace39657d14f0c8c7479db1.hypothesis: Decoder-only LLMs, when modified to support bidirectional attention and adapted through masked next token prediction and unsupervised contrastive learning, can achieve or surpass the performance of traditional encoder-based models on text embedding tasks, in both unsupervised and supervised settings.
18594d3f15b39385bace39657d14f0c8c7479db1.proposed_method: The proposed method, termed LLM2Vec, consists of three main steps to convert any pre-trained decoder-only LLM into a universal text encoder. First, the causal attention mask is replaced with a fully bidirectional attention mask, allowing each token to attend to all others in the sequence. Second, the model is adapted to this new attention pattern using masked next token prediction (MNTP), where a fraction of tokens in each sequence are masked and the model is trained to predict these tokens based on both past and future context, with the loss computed from the representation of the previous token. Third, unsupervised contrastive learning (SimCSE) is applied: each input sentence is passed through the model twice with independently sampled dropout masks, and the model is trained to maximize the similarity between these two representations while minimizing similarity with other sentences in the batch. The approach is parameter-efficient, requires no labeled data, and leverages LoRA for fine-tuning.
18594d3f15b39385bace39657d14f0c8c7479db1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several decoder-only LLMs ranging from 1.3B to 8B parameters, including S-LLaMA-1.3B, LLaMA-2-7B, Mistral-7B, and Meta-LLaMA-3-8B. The adaptation steps (MNTP and SimCSE) will use English Wikipedia data, specifically Wikitext-103 for MNTP and a Wikipedia sentence subset for SimCSE. Evaluation will cover both word-level tasks (chunking, named-entity recognition, part-of-speech tagging) using the CoNLL-2003 benchmark, and sequence-level tasks using the Massive Text Embeddings Benchmark (MTEB), which spans 56 datasets across seven categories. Baselines will include encoder-only models such as DeBERTa-v3-large, unsupervised BERT models, and Echo embeddings. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy for word-level tasks and MTEB average scores for sequence-level tasks. Supervised contrastive learning will also be tested using a public subset of the E5 dataset, with performance compared to state-of-the-art models trained on public data.
18594d3f15b39385bace39657d14f0c8c7479db1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a simple, unsupervised, and parameter-efficient method to transform any decoder-only LLM into a universal text encoder, requiring only minimal adaptation and no labeled data. LLM2Vec achieves state-of-the-art results on the MTEB benchmark for unsupervised models and, when combined with supervised contrastive learning, sets a new performance record among models trained solely on publicly available data. The method is computationally efficient, does not require synthetic data or full model fine-tuning, and is compatible with a wide range of LLM architectures. Additionally, the analysis reveals novel insights into the behavior of Mistral-7B under bidirectional attention, suggesting unique pre-training characteristics.

185e88645dfc07d6ca81a55dfc66bd3452400276.title: ZipLoRA: Any Subject in Any Style by Effectively Merging LoRAs
185e88645dfc07d6ca81a55dfc66bd3452400276.research_question: How can independently trained subject and style LoRAs be effectively merged to enable the generation of any user-provided subject in any user-provided style, while maintaining high fidelity to both subject and style in diffusion models?
185e88645dfc07d6ca81a55dfc66bd3452400276.hypothesis: A hyperparameter-free, optimization-based approach that minimizes interference between LoRA weight matrices by reducing column-wise cosine similarity, while preserving the generative capabilities of the original subject and style LoRAs, will enable robust and high-fidelity merging of independently trained LoRAs for arbitrary subject-style combinations.
185e88645dfc07d6ca81a55dfc66bd3452400276.proposed_method: The proposed method, ZipLoRA, introduces a novel framework for merging independently trained subject and style LoRAs for diffusion models such as Stable Diffusion XL (SDXL). The approach leverages the sparsity and alignment properties of LoRA update matrices, learning column-wise merger coefficients that minimize cosine similarity between columns of subject and style LoRAs to reduce signal interference. An optimization objective is formulated that (1) preserves the ability of the merged LoRA to generate each reference subject and style independently by minimizing the difference between outputs of the merged and original LoRAs, and (2) enforces orthogonality between columns of the two LoRA matrices. Only the merger coefficients are updated during optimization, while the base model and original LoRA weights remain frozen. This process is hyperparameter-free and does not require manual tuning or grid search.
185e88645dfc07d6ca81a55dfc66bd3452400276.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using the SDXL v1.0 diffusion model as the backbone. Subject LoRAs are obtained via DreamBooth fine-tuning on the DreamBooth dataset (30 subject image sets), and style LoRAs are trained on single-image exemplars from the StyleDrop dataset. All LoRAs are trained with rank 64, using Adam optimizer for 1000 steps, batch size 1, and learning rate 0.00005. ZipLoRA optimization is run until cosine similarity between columns drops to zero or for a maximum of 100 steps. Baselines include direct arithmetic merging of LoRAs, joint training of subject and style, and the DreamBooth+StyleDrop approach. Evaluation metrics include user preference studies, CLIP-based style and text alignment, and DINO-based subject alignment, as well as qualitative assessment of stylization and subject fidelity.
185e88645dfc07d6ca81a55dfc66bd3452400276.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to introduce a hyperparameter-free, optimization-based approach for merging independently trained subject and style LoRAs, enabling arbitrary subject-style generation with diffusion models. Key innovations include the use of column-wise merger coefficients to minimize alignment-induced interference, leveraging the sparsity of LoRA matrices, and preserving the generative capabilities of both subject and style LoRAs. The approach is computationally efficient, requires no manual tuning, and consistently outperforms existing merging and joint training baselines in both qualitative and quantitative evaluations.

186c2b2386799fa599e2d77bc6945f7da66e5fab.title: Zero123++: a Single Image to Consistent Multi-view Diffusion Base Model
186c2b2386799fa599e2d77bc6945f7da66e5fab.research_question: How can a single input image be used to generate high-quality, consistent multi-view images that accurately reflect underlying 3D structure, leveraging pretrained 2D diffusion models while minimizing fine-tuning effort?
186c2b2386799fa599e2d77bc6945f7da66e5fab.hypothesis: Integrating advanced conditioning techniques, optimized noise scheduling, and multi-view joint modeling into a diffusion framework based on pretrained Stable Diffusion models will enable the generation of highly consistent, high-quality multi-view images from a single input image, outperforming existing approaches in both visual fidelity and geometric consistency.
186c2b2386799fa599e2d77bc6945f7da66e5fab.proposed_method: A new image-conditioned diffusion model will be developed for generating 3D-consistent multi-view images from a single input view. The approach will tile six novel views in a fixed 3x2 layout, enabling the model to learn the joint distribution of multi-view images rather than generating each view independently. The method will incorporate advanced conditioning strategies, including scaled reference attention for local conditioning and a trainable global conditioning mechanism based on FlexDiffuse, leveraging CLIP image embeddings to maximize the reuse of Stable Diffusion priors. The noise schedule will be carefully selected and adapted, switching from the default scaled-linear to a linear schedule, and the Stable Diffusion 2 v-prediction model will be used as the base for fine-tuning to ensure stability and consistency. Training will be phased, initially tuning only attention layers and later the full UNet, with Min-SNR weighting to improve efficiency. Additionally, a depth-controlled variant using ControlNet will be developed to allow explicit geometric guidance.
186c2b2386799fa599e2d77bc6945f7da66e5fab.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Objaverse dataset, using rendered images of 3D objects with random HDRI lighting, and will include both real-world photos and out-of-domain images such as AI-generated content and 2D illustrations. Baselines for comparison will include Zero-1-to-3, Zero-1-to-3 XL, SyncDreamer, and MVDream. Evaluation metrics will focus on multi-view consistency and perceptual quality, with LPIPS used as the primary quantitative metric by comparing tiled generated views to ground truth renderings. Qualitative comparisons will be performed on diverse input types, and ablation studies will assess the impact of different conditioning and noise scheduling strategies. For the depth-controlled variant, ControlNet will be trained on paired RGB and depth images, and its performance will be evaluated using the same LPIPS metric.
186c2b2386799fa599e2d77bc6945f7da66e5fab.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel joint multi-view generation strategy by tiling multiple views into a single training target, enabling consistent modeling of the joint distribution of object appearances. It maximizes the reuse of pretrained Stable Diffusion priors through advanced local and global conditioning mechanisms, including scaled reference attention and FlexDiffuse-based global image conditioning. The method systematically addresses issues of noise scheduling and model stability, allowing high-resolution training and improved adaptation to new tasks. The integration of a depth-controlled variant further extends the model’s capabilities to explicit geometric guidance. Overall, the approach claims to achieve superior multi-view consistency, quality, and generalization compared to current state-of-the-art methods.

18764a7cf55b5d0be599cf4442dede7394959afb.title: Computation vs. Communication Scaling for Future Transformers on Future Hardware
18764a7cf55b5d0be599cf4442dede7394959afb.research_question: How will the relative scaling of computation and communication impact the efficiency of distributed training for future large-scale Transformer models on evolving hardware platforms, and what are the implications for system and model design?
18764a7cf55b5d0be599cf4442dede7394959afb.hypothesis: As Transformer models and hardware continue to scale, communication overhead will become a critical bottleneck in distributed training, potentially exceeding computation time and limiting overall training efficiency unless new strategies or technologies are adopted.
18764a7cf55b5d0be599cf4442dede7394959afb.proposed_method: A comprehensive multi-axial analysis will be conducted to study the scaling behavior of computation versus communication (Comp-vs.-Comm) for future Transformer models on anticipated hardware. The methodology will include: (1) algorithmic analysis to derive system-agnostic scaling laws for compute and communication operations in Transformer architectures, focusing on key hyperparameters such as hidden dimension, sequence length, batch size, and degrees of parallelism; (2) an empirical strategy leveraging operator-level performance models and targeted profiling of regions of interest (ROIs) to project execution times for hundreds of model/hardware configurations, thereby reducing the need for exhaustive end-to-end profiling; and (3) hardware evolution modeling, using historical and projected trends in compute throughput and network bandwidth to estimate future bottlenecks. The approach will systematically sweep relevant hyperparameters and parallelism degrees, and utilize high-fidelity operator models to extrapolate performance for unseen scenarios.
18764a7cf55b5d0be599cf4442dede7394959afb.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed on a cluster of AMD Instinct MI210 GPUs, each with 64GB HBM and connected via high-bandwidth Infinity Fabric links. The study will consider a wide range of Transformer model hyperparameters (e.g., hidden sizes from 1K to 64K, sequence lengths up to 8K, batch sizes down to 1) and distributed training setups (data and tensor parallelism degrees up to 256). Operator-level profiling and modeling will be used to project compute and communication times for hundreds of future model/hardware configurations, with validation against measured runtimes showing <15% error. Baselines will include current state-of-the-art Transformer models (e.g., BERT, T5, GPT-3, MT-NLG, PaLM) and their distributed training performance. Evaluation metrics will include the fraction of training time spent on communication versus computation, the ability to overlap communication with computation (slack), and the impact of hardware scaling (compute FLOPS vs. network bandwidth) on these fractions.
18764a7cf55b5d0be599cf4442dede7394959afb.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a principled, multi-axial framework for analyzing and projecting the interplay between computation and communication scaling in distributed training of future Transformer models. Key innovations include a system-agnostic algorithmic analysis that generalizes across models and hardware, an empirical strategy that reduces profiling costs by over three orders of magnitude via operator-level modeling and ROI extraction, and a forward-looking evaluation of hardware evolution trends. The work claims to provide the first comprehensive quantification of when and how communication will become a dominant bottleneck, and offers actionable insights for the design of both future models and distributed training systems.

188336f606e76fda9e219b954d1750ad26646fdb.title: ReLU Strikes Back: Exploiting Activation Sparsity in Large Language Models
188336f606e76fda9e219b954d1750ad26646fdb.research_question: How can activation sparsity be effectively exploited in large language models to improve inference efficiency without compromising model performance, particularly through the use of ReLU or related activation functions?
188336f606e76fda9e219b954d1750ad26646fdb.hypothesis: ReLU activations, when incorporated into large language models either during pretraining or via architectural modifications and finetuning, will induce significant activation sparsity, leading to substantial reductions in inference computation and memory requirements, while maintaining comparable performance to models using smoother, more complex activation functions.
188336f606e76fda9e219b954d1750ad26646fdb.proposed_method: The proposed approach involves systematically replacing or augmenting the activation functions in large language models (LLMs) such as Llama, Falcon, and OPT with ReLU activations, a process termed 'relufication.' This will be conducted in two stages: first, by replacing non-ReLU activations (e.g., GELU, SiLU) in the feedforward layers with ReLU, and second, by inserting additional ReLU layers after normalization layers to further enhance sparsity throughout the model. The method also explores the use of shifted ReLU activations, where a constant bias is subtracted from the preactivation before applying ReLU, to increase sparsity even further. Technical implementation will include architectural surgery on existing pretrained models, followed by targeted finetuning to recover any lost performance. The approach will also analyze the reuse of activated neurons across token generations (aggregated sparsity) and leverage this property to optimize speculative decoding and reduce memory and I/O overhead.
188336f606e76fda9e219b954d1750ad26646fdb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using open-source pretrained LLMs (OPT, Llama, Falcon) with both pretraining from scratch and finetuning on the RefinedWeb dataset (a high-quality CommonCrawl subset). Validation will use WikiText for sparsity measurements and preactivation analysis. The evaluation will cover zero-shot and few-shot performance on a suite of tasks from the Language Model Evaluation Harness (e.g., ARC, HellaSwag, BoolQ, PIQA, LAMBADA, TriviaQA, WinoGrande, SciQ) and the MMLU benchmark. Baselines will include models with original activation functions (GELU, SiLU) and models with relufied architectures. Key metrics will be activation sparsity (percentage of zeroed activations), FLOPS (as a proxy for inference efficiency), and standard accuracy metrics for each task. The experimental setup will also assess the impact of relufication on speculative decoding speedup and the effectiveness of weight reuse strategies enabled by aggregated sparsity.
188336f606e76fda9e219b954d1750ad26646fdb.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a systematic and practical framework for exploiting activation sparsity in LLMs via relufication, demonstrating that ReLU activations can be retrofitted into existing pretrained models with minimal performance loss and substantial computational savings. It claims that activation sparsity induced by ReLU is more hardware-friendly and leads to structured computation reductions (e.g., skipping entire matrix rows), unlike unstructured weight pruning. The work is among the first to show that activation function choice has negligible impact on LLM performance at scale, while offering significant efficiency gains. Additionally, it proposes novel applications such as leveraging aggregated sparsity for faster token generation and speculative decoding, and introduces the shifted ReLU as a simple yet effective way to further increase sparsity without architectural complexity.

188d1ad5acbbb8678560e5dc6ff7b0de25a9e53b.title: Rethinking Complex Queries on Knowledge Graphs with Neural Link Predictors
188d1ad5acbbb8678560e5dc6ff7b0de25a9e53b.research_question: How can complex existential first-order logic queries with a single free variable be effectively and faithfully answered on knowledge graphs, overcoming the limitations of existing query embedding methods and datasets?
188d1ad5acbbb8678560e5dc6ff7b0de25a9e53b.hypothesis: Equipping neural link predictors with a principled fuzzy logic inference mechanism will enable accurate, end-to-end learning and reasoning over a broader class of complex queries—including those not representable by existing operator-tree-based approaches—while providing theoretical guarantees of faithfulness and perfectness under certain conditions.
188d1ad5acbbb8678560e5dc6ff7b0de25a9e53b.proposed_method: A novel neural-symbolic framework, Fuzzy Inference with Truth value (FIT), will be developed to answer complex existential first-order (EFO_1) queries on knowledge graphs. FIT will integrate neural link predictors (which provide a 'truth value' for any triple) with strict fuzzy logic theory to enable differentiable, end-to-end reasoning over arbitrary EFO_1 queries. The method will represent queries as general multigraphs, allowing for features such as existential leaves, multigraphs, and cycles, which are not captured by prior operator-tree-based methods. FIT will construct neural matrices for each relation using calibrated neural link predictor outputs, and will recursively compute answer vectors for queries by propagating fuzzy truth values through the query graph structure, supporting all logical operations (conjunction, disjunction, negation, existential quantification) as defined in fuzzy logic. The approach will be fully differentiable, allowing for fine-tuning of the neural link predictor parameters using cross-entropy loss between predicted and true answer sets.
188d1ad5acbbb8678560e5dc6ff7b0de25a9e53b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both a newly constructed dataset of ten real EFO_1 query types—designed to cover properties and complexities not present in existing benchmarks—and on standard Tree-Form query datasets (e.g., BetaE, FB15k-237, NELL). Baseline methods will include state-of-the-art query embedding and neural link prediction models such as BetaE, LogicE, ConE, QTO, CQD, and LMPNN. Evaluation will use Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) as the primary metric, with results reported separately for deductible (faithful) and generalizable answers. The experimental protocol will ensure fair comparison by using the same pretrained neural link predictor checkpoints across methods. The effectiveness of FIT will be assessed by its performance on both the new complex queries and traditional Tree-Form queries, as well as its ability to achieve perfect faithfulness on deductible answers.
188d1ad5acbbb8678560e5dc6ff7b0de25a9e53b.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a principled, theoretically grounded neural-symbolic method (FIT) that extends the scope of complex query answering on knowledge graphs to the full class of existential first-order queries with a single free variable. FIT is the first approach to systematically support queries with features such as existential leaves, multigraphs, and cycles, which are not representable by existing operator-tree-based query embedding methods. The research also provides a new, comprehensive dataset of complex EFO_1 queries, enabling more thorough empirical evaluation. The FIT framework offers provable guarantees of faithfulness and perfectness under reasonable assumptions, and empirical results are expected to demonstrate significant improvements over prior methods on both new and existing benchmarks.

1891c3756f870d902a0b793a1dcd5cc34c778612.title: VideoCrafter1: Open Diffusion Models for High-Quality Video Generation
1891c3756f870d902a0b793a1dcd5cc34c778612.research_question: How can open-source diffusion models be developed to enable high-quality, high-resolution video generation from text and/or image prompts, with strong content preservation, temporal consistency, and semantic alignment?
1891c3756f870d902a0b793a1dcd5cc34c778612.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging large-scale joint image and video training, incorporating temporal attention into a Stable Diffusion-based UNet, and introducing a dual cross-attention mechanism for text and image embeddings will enable the development of open-source diffusion models capable of generating cinematic-quality videos from text and image prompts, while preserving content and structure and achieving temporal coherence.
1891c3756f870d902a0b793a1dcd5cc34c778612.proposed_method: The proposed approach involves developing two diffusion-based video generation models: a text-to-video (T2V) model and an image-to-video (I2V) model. The T2V model builds upon a Stable Diffusion 2.1 UNet backbone, augmented with temporal attention layers to capture temporal consistency across video frames. A joint image and video training strategy is employed to prevent concept forgetting, utilizing both large-scale image and video datasets. The I2V model extends the T2V architecture by incorporating an additional image prompt; image features are extracted using the CLIP image encoder and projected into a text-aligned embedding space via a learnable projection network. Both text and image embeddings are injected into the UNet through dual cross-attention layers, enabling the model to synthesize videos that strictly adhere to the reference image's content and structure. Motion speed control is facilitated via an FPS embedding, and the models are trained progressively from low to high resolution.
1891c3756f870d902a0b793a1dcd5cc34c778612.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize the LAION COCO 600M image dataset, WebVid-10M video dataset, and an additional proprietary high-resolution video dataset with 10 million clips. The T2V model will be trained in stages, starting at 256x256 resolution and progressing to 1024x576, with large batch sizes and extensive iterations. Baselines for comparison will include both open-source (e.g., I2VGen-XL, Zeroscope V2 XL, VideoComposer) and commercial (e.g., Gen-2, Pika Labs) video generation models. Evaluation will be conducted using the EvalCrafter benchmark, which includes both quantitative metrics and human preference studies, assessing visual quality, text-video alignment, temporal consistency, and motion quality. Qualitative comparisons will be provided through visual examples, and user studies will be conducted to further validate performance.
1891c3756f870d902a0b793a1dcd5cc34c778612.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first open-source generic image-to-video (I2V) foundation model capable of strict content and structure preservation from a reference image while animating it into a video. The text-to-video (T2V) model is claimed to achieve state-of-the-art visual and cinematic quality among open-source models at a resolution of 1024x576. The dual cross-attention mechanism for fusing text and image embeddings in the UNet is a novel component, as is the joint image-video training strategy for robust concept retention. The open-sourcing of these high-quality video generation models is positioned as a significant contribution to the research community, enabling further advancements in open-domain video synthesis.

189fde3f4dfa105bb51472a8945618f395919560.title: Repeat After Me: Transformers are Better than State Space Models at Copying
189fde3f4dfa105bb51472a8945618f395919560.research_question: What are the fundamental differences in the ability of transformer architectures and generalized state space models (GSSMs) to perform tasks that require copying or retrieving information from the input context, and how do these differences impact practical performance on memory-intensive sequence modeling tasks?
189fde3f4dfa105bb51472a8945618f395919560.hypothesis: Transformer architectures possess a fundamentally greater capacity than GSSMs to copy and retrieve arbitrary-length sequences from input context, due to their attention-based mechanisms, whereas GSSMs are limited by their fixed-size latent state.
189fde3f4dfa105bb51472a8945618f395919560.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted to compare the representational and practical capabilities of transformers and GSSMs on tasks requiring copying and retrieval from input context. Theoretically, the representational limits of both model classes will be analyzed by constructing explicit algorithms and proofs for the copy task, demonstrating that transformers can copy sequences of exponential length relative to their size, while GSSMs are limited by the size of their latent state. Empirically, both model types will be trained from scratch on synthetic tasks such as string copying and n-gram lookup, with careful control of model size and parameter count. The study will also introduce and evaluate a novel positional encoding (Hard-ALiBi) to enhance transformer generalization. Finally, pretrained large language models (transformers and GSSMs) will be evaluated on real-world tasks, including copying natural language strings, phone-book lookup, and question answering, to assess practical relevance.
189fde3f4dfa105bb51472a8945618f395919560.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training transformer and GSSM models (including LSTM and Mamba variants) with approximately 160 million parameters on synthetic copy tasks, using a vocabulary of 30 tokens and context lengths up to 1000 tokens. Baselines will include standard positional encodings (RoPE, Alibi, NoPE) and the proposed Hard-ALiBi. Evaluation metrics will focus on string-level and character-level accuracy, as well as F1 score for question answering. Pretrained models (Pythia transformers and Mamba GSSMs) ranging from 410M to 2.8B parameters will be compared on tasks such as copying natural language strings from C4, shuffled string copying, phone-book lookup, and SQuAD question answering, with performance measured as a function of input length. Experiments will assess both in-distribution learning efficiency and out-of-distribution generalization to longer sequences.
189fde3f4dfa105bb51472a8945618f395919560.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a rigorous theoretical separation between transformers and GSSMs on the copy task, providing explicit constructions and lower bounds. It proposes a novel positional encoding (Hard-ALiBi) that enables transformers to generalize copying behavior far beyond the training context. The empirical study is the first to systematically compare transformers and state space models of similar scale on memory-intensive tasks, revealing a fundamental gap in their ability to copy and retrieve information. The work also demonstrates that transformer-based models outperform GSSMs on practical retrieval tasks, even when GSSMs achieve lower language modeling perplexity, thus highlighting architectural biases that influence downstream performance beyond standard metrics.

18a65d3136df8429b63e9a6352151d4d7374d8eb.title: Prediction without Preclusion: Recourse Verification with Reachable Sets
18a65d3136df8429b63e9a6352151d4d7374d8eb.research_question: How can the responsiveness of machine learning model predictions to actionable changes in input features be formally verified, particularly in high-stakes decision-making domains such as lending and hiring, to ensure that individuals are not precluded from access due to fixed predictions under realistic actionability constraints?
18a65d3136df8429b63e9a6352151d4d7374d8eb.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a model-agnostic verification procedure based on constructing and querying reachable sets—representing all feature vectors attainable through permissible actions—can reliably certify whether recourse is feasible for individuals, even under complex, discrete, and non-separable actionability constraints.
18a65d3136df8429b63e9a6352151d4d7374d8eb.proposed_method: A model-agnostic framework will be developed to verify recourse by constructing reachable sets for each individual, where a reachable set comprises all feature vectors that can be attained through actions allowed by specified actionability constraints. The method will encode actionability constraints—including immutability, monotonicity, integrality, categorical encodings, and deterministic causal effects—into a mixed-integer programming (MIP) formulation. For each individual, the procedure will enumerate all reachable points by iteratively solving the MIP and excluding previously found solutions, thus fully characterizing the space of feasible actions. To address scalability, decomposition techniques will be applied to partition features into independent subsets, allowing parallel and more efficient construction of reachable sets. The verification process will then query the model's predictions over the reachable set to determine if recourse is feasible (i.e., if any reachable point achieves the desired prediction), infeasible (no reachable point achieves the desired prediction), or indeterminate (if the reachable set cannot be fully enumerated).
18a65d3136df8429b63e9a6352151d4d7374d8eb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three consumer finance datasets (HELOC, German Credit, and GiveMeCredit), each processed to encode categorical features and discretize continuous ones. For each dataset, multiple classification models (logistic regression, XGBoost, and random forests) will be trained using standard train/test splits and hyperparameter tuning. Inherent actionability constraints, reflecting indisputable and dataset-wide limitations (e.g., physical limits, feature encoding, deterministic causal effects, and protected attribute immutability), will be specified for each dataset. Reachable sets will be constructed for all individuals, and recourse verification will be performed by querying model predictions over these sets. The reliability of the proposed method will be benchmarked against existing recourse and counterfactual generation methods (e.g., AR and DiCE), with evaluation metrics including the proportion of individuals for whom recourse is certified infeasible, the prevalence of loopholes (actions violating constraints), blindspots (failure to find recourse when it exists), and overall correctness of recourse determination.
18a65d3136df8429b63e9a6352151d4d7374d8eb.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a formal, model-agnostic verification procedure for recourse that is capable of certifying infeasibility under complex, discrete, and non-separable actionability constraints, which existing methods cannot reliably handle. The method provides exhaustive and reliable certification by enumerating all reachable points in feature space, overcoming the limitations of prior recourse provision algorithms that may return infeasible or inconclusive results due to blindspots or loopholes. The framework is generalizable to any model class and supports practical auditing in high-stakes applications, enabling practitioners to detect and mitigate preclusion effects before model deployment. Additionally, a Python package will be developed to facilitate the specification of complex actionability constraints and to automate the recourse verification process for practitioners.

18b028072673f1caad4a76e88f022c022c997709.title: Understanding Model Ensemble in Transferable Adversarial Attack
18b028072673f1caad4a76e88f022c022c997709.research_question: What are the theoretical foundations underlying the transferability of adversarial examples generated via model ensemble attacks, and how can these insights guide the design of more effective transferable adversarial attack algorithms?
18b028072673f1caad4a76e88f022c022c997709.hypothesis: Transferability error in model ensemble adversarial attacks can be theoretically decomposed and bounded using concepts of vulnerability, diversity, and ensemble complexity, and can be minimized by increasing the number of surrogate models, enhancing their diversity, and controlling their complexity.
18b028072673f1caad4a76e88f022c022c997709.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed to analyze model ensemble adversarial attacks by introducing three key definitions: transferability error (the gap in expected loss between an adversarial example and the optimal transferable example), diversity (quantified as the variance in ensemble model predictions), and empirical model ensemble Rademacher complexity (a measure of the flexibility of the ensemble). The transferability error will be decomposed into vulnerability and diversity components, and upper bounds will be derived using advanced mathematical tools from information theory, specifically leveraging the Hellinger integral and Rademacher complexity. The methodology will further establish practical guidelines for minimizing transferability error, including increasing the number of surrogate models, maximizing their diversity, and reducing model complexity in cases of overfitting. Theoretical results will be validated through extensive empirical experiments.
18b028072673f1caad4a76e88f022c022c997709.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification datasets including MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100, with additional demonstrations on ImageNet. A total of 54 deep neural network models (MLPs and CNNs with varying architectures, regularization, and data transformations) will be trained as surrogates, and a ResNet-18 will serve as the target model for transferability evaluation. Attacks will be crafted using MI-FGSM with cross-entropy loss, and metrics such as attack success rate (ASR), loss value, and prediction variance will be tracked across attack steps and varying ensemble sizes. Baseline comparisons will include attacks with different numbers of surrogate models, levels of diversity, and model complexities. Evaluation will focus on the relationship between theoretical bounds and empirical transferability, as well as the trade-off between diversity and complexity.
18b028072673f1caad4a76e88f022c022c997709.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first comprehensive theoretical framework for understanding transferable model ensemble adversarial attacks, including novel definitions of transferability error, ensemble diversity, and empirical model ensemble Rademacher complexity. It rigorously decomposes transferability error into vulnerability and diversity, providing actionable theoretical guidelines for attack design. The approach leverages recent advances in information theory to derive upper bounds on transferability error and validates these insights with large-scale empirical studies, representing a significant advance in the theoretical and practical understanding of transferable adversarial attacks.

18b1c6181ce6d3ec9486d0183b62e523a04c098e.title: MPO: An Efficient Post-Processing Framework for Mixing Diverse Preference Alignment
18b1c6181ce6d3ec9486d0183b62e523a04c098e.research_question: How can large language models be efficiently aligned with diverse and potentially competing human preferences without incurring the high computational costs and instability associated with traditional multi-objective reinforcement learning from human feedback?
18b1c6181ce6d3ec9486d0183b62e523a04c098e.hypothesis: A post-processing framework that aggregates single-objective policies using a principled optimization approach can achieve balanced alignment with diverse human preferences, matching or surpassing the performance of existing multi-objective RLHF methods while significantly reducing computational cost.
18b1c6181ce6d3ec9486d0183b62e523a04c098e.proposed_method: The proposed method, Mixing Preference Optimization (MPO), introduces a post-processing framework that log-linearly combines multiple single-objective policies into a unified policy. Each policy is trained to optimize for a distinct human preference using standard RLHF or Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) pipelines. The aggregation weights for each policy are computed via Batch Stochastic Mirror Descent (BSMD), which solves for the optimal preference vector by minimizing a convex objective derived from the normalized rewards of each policy. The normalization operator projects reward functions onto a shared scale, ensuring comparability and stability during aggregation. The final policy is formed as a weighted product of the single-objective policies, where the weights reflect the learned balance among competing objectives. This approach eliminates the need for additional reinforcement learning or reward model training during aggregation, enabling efficient and scalable alignment.
18b1c6181ce6d3ec9486d0183b62e523a04c098e.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on text generation tasks, including sentiment and conciseness alignment using the IMDB dataset and a three-objective 'Helpful Assistant' task using the HH-RLHF dataset. Single-objective policies are trained on preference-specific data splits using LLaMA 3.2-3B or Qwen 2.5-7B as reference models, and DPO or RLHF as the training method. Baselines include single-reward RLHF, Reward Soups (uniform linear combination), and MaxMin-RLHF, with reward models normalized using Z-normalization. Evaluation metrics include average win rate against a reference model as judged by GPT-3.5 and GPT-4, as well as normalized reward scores for each objective. Ablation studies assess the impact of excluding individual objectives, and computational cost is measured in GPU hours. The experimental setup explores the effect of different KL regularization strengths and compares the scalability and robustness of MPO against baselines.
18b1c6181ce6d3ec9486d0183b62e523a04c098e.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is novel in that it achieves multi-objective alignment entirely through post-processing, bypassing the need for additional reinforcement learning or reward model training. It establishes a theoretical connection between reward aggregation and policy aggregation, providing a closed-form solution for policy mixing. The method is computationally efficient, scalable, and integrates seamlessly with existing RLHF and DPO pipelines. Empirical results demonstrate that the approach achieves balanced performance across diverse objectives, often matching or exceeding the effectiveness of state-of-the-art multi-objective RLHF methods at a fraction of the computational cost.

18b91948fe1aa1ccacbaff4ee110dbdd5b790fb1.title: DreamDistribution: Learning Prompt Distribution for Diverse In-distribution Generation
18b91948fe1aa1ccacbaff4ee110dbdd5b790fb1.research_question: How can diverse, high-quality, and controllable in-distribution images be generated from a small set of reference images that share abstract visual attributes, using text-to-image diffusion models, without overfitting to specific instances or losing diversity?
18b91948fe1aa1ccacbaff4ee110dbdd5b790fb1.hypothesis: A learnable distribution of soft prompts, optimized in the text encoder feature space of a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model, can effectively capture both the commonalities and variations present in a set of reference images, enabling the generation of diverse, high-quality, and controllable novel images that remain faithful to the visual attributes of the references.
18b91948fe1aa1ccacbaff4ee110dbdd5b790fb1.proposed_method: A novel prompt distribution learning approach is developed for text-to-image diffusion models, leveraging prompt tuning with a set of learnable soft prompt embeddings. Instead of fine-tuning the diffusion model parameters, only the prompt embeddings are optimized, allowing the pretrained model to remain fixed and preventing catastrophic forgetting. The method maintains a set of K learnable prompts, which are used to estimate a Gaussian distribution in the CLIP text encoder feature space, capturing the mean and variance of the reference images' semantic attributes. During training, a reparameterization trick is applied to enable differentiable sampling from this prompt distribution, and an orthogonal loss is incorporated to encourage diversity among the learned prompts. At inference, new prompts are sampled from the learned distribution to guide the diffusion model, enabling the generation of diverse images that follow the visual traits of the reference set. The approach also supports text-guided editing, variance scaling for diversity control, and interpolation between multiple prompt distributions.
18b91948fe1aa1ccacbaff4ee110dbdd5b790fb1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using Stable Diffusion 2.1 as the backbone model, with all model parameters except the prompt embeddings kept fixed. The method will be evaluated on a custom dataset of 12 scenarios, each containing 20 reference images with shared visual attributes but not representing the same instance. Baselines will include Textual Inversion, DreamBooth, Custom Diffusion, and prompt engineering methods using short and long captions. Evaluation metrics will comprise CLIP-I, CLIP-T, DINO, FID, Density, and Coverage for automatic assessment, as well as human evaluation for diversity and similarity to references. Additional experiments will demonstrate controllability (e.g., text-guided editing, variance scaling, distribution composition), transferability to text-to-3D generation using MVDream, and utility for synthetic dataset generation, including training classifiers on synthetic ImageNet-100 images and evaluating on various ImageNet variants.
18b91948fe1aa1ccacbaff4ee110dbdd5b790fb1.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a distribution-based prompt tuning framework for text-to-image diffusion models, enabling the modeling of abstract visual attributes and their variations from a small set of reference images. Unlike prior instance-level personalization methods that rely on fixed token embeddings, this approach learns a distribution of prompts, providing greater diversity and controllability in generated images. The method is parameter-efficient, prevents catastrophic forgetting, and supports flexible manipulation such as text-guided editing, variance scaling, and distribution interpolation. It is also readily adaptable to other text-guided generation tasks, such as text-to-3D, and demonstrates superior performance in both automatic and human evaluations compared to existing baselines.

18d750263f1dfe43374e8791cefa580a511c2098.title: Few-Shot Preference Learning for Human-in-the-Loop RL
18d750263f1dfe43374e8791cefa580a511c2098.research_question: How can the query efficiency of preference-based reinforcement learning be improved to enable practical human-in-the-loop training of complex robotic policies, especially in multi-task settings where reward functions are unknown and must be learned from limited human feedback?
18d750263f1dfe43374e8791cefa580a511c2098.hypothesis: Pre-training reward models on data from multiple prior tasks using meta-learning will enable rapid adaptation to new tasks with only a small number of human preference queries, thereby significantly reducing the amount of online feedback required to train effective reinforcement learning policies.
18d750263f1dfe43374e8791cefa580a511c2098.proposed_method: A novel few-shot preference-based reinforcement learning framework will be developed that leverages meta-learning (specifically, Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning, MAML) to pre-train a reward function across a family of tasks using pairwise trajectory segment comparisons. During pre-training, artificial or offline data from previous tasks will be used to train a reward model to predict human preferences over trajectory segments, optimizing a Bradley-Terry paired comparison objective via cross-entropy loss. For a new task, the pre-trained reward model will be quickly adapted online using a small number of human-provided preference queries, updating the model parameters with a few gradient steps. The adapted reward model will then be used to relabel transitions in a Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) RL algorithm, enabling policy optimization with the learned reward. An ensemble of reward models will be used to select the most informative queries based on disagreement, and the reward model will be re-initialized to pre-trained weights and re-adapted after each feedback session to maximize adaptation efficiency.
18d750263f1dfe43374e8791cefa580a511c2098.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Meta-World benchmark, which includes a variety of robotic manipulation tasks such as door opening, window closing, and block pushing. The method will be evaluated on both seen and unseen tasks, with reward models pre-trained on data from 10 prior tasks and adapted to 6 new tasks using only a fraction (1/20th) of the queries required by previous methods. Baselines will include Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) with ground-truth rewards (oracle), PEBBLE (a feedback-efficient RL method without pre-training), and a pre-trained initialization baseline without re-adaptation. Evaluation metrics will include task success rate and distance to goal (for real-robot experiments), with experiments also conducted using real human feedback on both simulated and real-world robotic platforms (e.g., Franka Panda robot). Additional experiments will address human query difficulty, label noise, and the impact of query selection strategies.
18d750263f1dfe43374e8791cefa580a511c2098.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to leverage multi-task meta-learning for preference-based reinforcement learning, enabling significant reductions in human query complexity (up to 20× fewer queries) while maintaining or exceeding the performance of state-of-the-art methods. The framework introduces a meta-learned reward adaptation mechanism that is agnostic to reward function structure, supports expressive reward models, and is practical for real human-in-the-loop training. The method also demonstrates, for the first time, the feasibility of training complex robotic manipulation policies from real human feedback with minimal queries, and provides algorithmic innovations in query selection and reward model adaptation.

18d82f2a4aa1e2c1c4b447876c95b8f7e717e1a1.title: Offline RL with No OOD Actions: In-Sample Learning via Implicit Value Regularization
18d82f2a4aa1e2c1c4b447876c95b8f7e717e1a1.research_question: How can offline reinforcement learning be improved to avoid errors caused by out-of-distribution (OOD) actions, and is it possible to design a general framework that enables robust in-sample learning through implicit value regularization?
18d82f2a4aa1e2c1c4b447876c95b8f7e717e1a1.hypothesis: Implicit value regularization, when applied in a fully in-sample manner, will enable offline RL algorithms to achieve robust and state-of-the-art performance by avoiding OOD actions and reducing value estimation errors, especially in noisy or small data regimes.
18d82f2a4aa1e2c1c4b447876c95b8f7e717e1a1.proposed_method: A general implicit value regularization (IVR) framework will be developed for offline reinforcement learning, where a behavior regularization term is added to the policy learning objective. The framework will be mathematically analyzed to derive closed-form solutions for the optimal policy and value functions under certain assumptions, ensuring that learning is performed only on in-sample actions from the dataset. Two practical algorithms, Sparse Q-Learning (SQL) and Exponential Q-Learning (EQL), will be instantiated from this framework. SQL leverages a sparsity-inducing regularizer based on the chi-squared divergence, filtering out low-value actions, while EQL uses a reverse KL divergence-based regularizer for exponential weighting. Both methods iteratively update Q-functions, V-functions, and policies using only dataset samples, and employ convex optimization or approximations to efficiently solve for normalization terms.
18d82f2a4aa1e2c1c4b447876c95b8f7e717e1a1.experiment_details: The proposed algorithms will be evaluated on the D4RL benchmark suite, which includes MuJoCo locomotion tasks (e.g., halfcheetah, hopper, walker2d), AntMaze, and Kitchen datasets, as well as high-dimensional image-based Atari datasets from RL Unplugged. Baselines for comparison will include Behavior Cloning (BC), BCQ, Decision Transformer (DT), TD3+BC, One-step RL, CQL, and IQL. Evaluation metrics will include normalized return scores and Bellman error, with experiments conducted under standard, noisy (mixed expert/random), and small data regimes (simulating limited state coverage). Multiple random seeds and repeated runs will be used for statistical significance, and performance will be measured both in terms of final policy quality and robustness to data imperfections.
18d82f2a4aa1e2c1c4b447876c95b8f7e717e1a1.novelty_claims: The proposed IVR framework provides a unified theoretical foundation connecting behavior-regularized and in-sample learning methods in offline RL. The SQL and EQL algorithms are the first to implement complete in-sample value learning with implicit regularization, avoiding OOD actions entirely. SQL introduces a sparsity mechanism in value learning, enhancing robustness to noisy data, while both SQL and EQL demonstrate superior or state-of-the-art performance on challenging offline RL benchmarks, particularly in regimes with suboptimal, noisy, or limited data. The approach also offers improved stability and reduced Bellman error compared to existing regularized offline RL methods.

18e1648e16311d4f345b2704aec00a98fa29db94.title: Temperature-Annealed Boltzmann Generators
18e1648e16311d4f345b2704aec00a98fa29db94.research_question: How can efficient and scalable sampling of unnormalized probability densities, such as the Boltzmann distribution of complex molecular systems, be achieved without mode collapse and with improved computational efficiency, especially in data-scarce domains?
18e1648e16311d4f345b2704aec00a98fa29db94.hypothesis: Training normalizing flows with the reverse Kullback-Leibler divergence at elevated temperatures, followed by an iterative reweighting-based annealing strategy, will enable accurate and efficient sampling from complex, multimodal Boltzmann distributions without mode collapse, while reducing the number of target energy evaluations compared to existing variational sampling methods.
18e1648e16311d4f345b2704aec00a98fa29db94.proposed_method: A temperature-annealed Boltzmann generator (TA-BG) framework is proposed, which consists of two main phases. First, a normalizing flow is trained at a high temperature using the reverse Kullback-Leibler divergence, leveraging the increased mode connectivity to avoid mode collapse. Second, the learned distribution is iteratively annealed to the desired lower (target) temperature using a reweighting-based training objective: at each annealing step, samples are drawn from the current flow, reweighted to the next lower temperature, and the flow is further trained using the forward KLD on the reweighted dataset. This process is repeated over a geometrically scheduled sequence of temperatures until the target temperature is reached. The flow architecture is based on monotonic rational-quadratic spline coupling layers with internal coordinate representations, and regularization strategies are employed to stabilize training.
18e1648e16311d4f345b2704aec00a98fa29db94.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three molecular systems of increasing complexity: alanine dipeptide, alanine tetrapeptide, and alanine hexapeptide, each presenting challenging metastable regions. The method will be benchmarked against baselines including forward KLD-trained flows (using MD data), reverse KLD-trained flows at target temperature, and Flow Annealed Importance Sampling Bootstrap (FAB). Evaluation metrics will include negative log-likelihood (NLL) on ground truth MD datasets, reverse effective sample size (ESS), Ramachandran Kullback-Leibler divergence (RAMKLD) for backbone dihedral angles, and the number of target energy evaluations. Multiple independent runs will be performed to assess robustness, and ablations on annealing schedules and fine-tuning steps will be included.
18e1648e16311d4f345b2704aec00a98fa29db94.novelty_claims: The proposed approach demonstrates that reverse KLD training at high temperatures can reliably avoid mode collapse in normalizing flows for molecular systems, a result contrary to prevailing literature. The iterative reweighting-based annealing strategy enables the flow to be transitioned to arbitrary target temperatures without requiring MD data at those temperatures. The method is shown to scale to significantly larger and more complex molecular systems than previously addressed by variational sampling methods, achieving superior sampling efficiency and accuracy while reducing computational cost. Additionally, the introduction of new, more complex molecular benchmarks advances the field's evaluation standards.

18e204166b5b458fba3dd6a648780f42a9654d02.title: Bivariate Causal Discovery using Bayesian Model Selection
18e204166b5b458fba3dd6a648780f42a9654d02.research_question: How can causal direction be identified between two variables within a Markov equivalence class, especially in scenarios where strong model restrictions for identifiability do not hold, and can a Bayesian model selection framework enable reliable causal discovery under more realistic and flexible modeling assumptions?
18e204166b5b458fba3dd6a648780f42a9654d02.hypothesis: Bayesian model selection, when equipped with appropriately designed priors that encode causal assumptions, can effectively distinguish causal direction between two variables even in the absence of hard model restrictions, outperforming existing methods that rely on strict identifiability conditions.
18e204166b5b458fba3dd6a648780f42a9654d02.proposed_method: A Bayesian model selection framework will be developed for bivariate causal discovery, treating each possible causal direction (X→Y and X←Y) as a separate Bayesian model. Each model will encode the Independent Causal Mechanisms (ICM) assumption through separable priors over the causal factorization. The approach will employ a highly flexible, non-parametric model for the joint distribution, specifically a Gaussian Process Latent Variable Model (GPLVM), to avoid rigid restrictions and reduce model misspecification. Marginal likelihoods for each causal direction will be computed by integrating over the priors, and the direction with the higher marginal likelihood will be selected as the inferred cause. The methodology includes a statistical test to estimate the probability of error and quantify overlap between models, ensuring robustness even under mild model misspecification.
18e204166b5b458fba3dd6a648780f42a9654d02.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of benchmark datasets, including both real and synthetic data, with varying data-generating assumptions. The proposed Bayesian GPLVM-based method will be compared against a comprehensive suite of baselines, including methods with strict identifiability assumptions (e.g., LiNGAM, ANM, PNL) and more flexible approaches (e.g., CGNN, GPI, CDCI). Evaluation will use the ROC AUC metric to measure the accuracy of causal direction inference, ensuring balanced representation of both causal directions in each dataset. Additional analysis will estimate the probability of error using repeated sampling and the proposed statistical test, and the robustness of the method will be assessed under model misspecification scenarios.
18e204166b5b458fba3dd6a648780f42a9654d02.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a Bayesian causal discovery framework that removes the need for hard model restrictions, enabling the use of highly flexible, non-parametric models for causal inference. It provides a principled way to encode causal assumptions via priors and demonstrates that Bayesian model selection can distinguish causal direction even when maximum likelihood fails due to model flexibility. The approach includes a new statistical test to quantify the probability of error and overlap between models, and empirically outperforms existing methods across a wide range of data-generating processes, highlighting its practical applicability to real-world datasets where standard identifiability assumptions may not hold.

18edf06b3df19a66cf6edbc884f27a46c40f891e.title: On the Local Complexity of Linear Regions in Deep ReLU Networks
18edf06b3df19a66cf6edbc884f27a46c40f891e.research_question: How does the distribution and local density of linear regions in deep ReLU networks relate to representation learning, adversarial robustness, and the optimization process? Can a theoretically grounded measure of local complexity provide insights into the geometric properties of learned functions and their implications for learning dynamics?
18edf06b3df19a66cf6edbc884f27a46c40f891e.hypothesis: Networks that learn low-dimensional feature representations will exhibit lower local complexity, as measured by the density of linear regions near the data distribution. This reduced local complexity will correlate with increased adversarial robustness and can be influenced by optimization dynamics and implicit regularization.
18edf06b3df19a66cf6edbc884f27a46c40f891e.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed to quantify the local complexity of deep ReLU networks by defining and computing the density of linear regions over the input data distribution. The local complexity will be formalized as the expected density of non-linearities (i.e., boundaries between linear regions) in the vicinity of data points, using a robust measure that averages over small perturbations of the network's bias parameters. Analytical tools such as the co-area formula and Kac-Rice formula will be leveraged to derive explicit formulas and bounds for local complexity, connecting it to the rank of learned representations (via the Jacobian of intermediate layers) and to the total variation of the network function. Theoretical results will be complemented by empirical algorithms that estimate local complexity using gradient computations at each neuron and by analyzing the effect of parameter noise.
18edf06b3df19a66cf6edbc884f27a46c40f891e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real datasets, including multivariate Gaussian data and subsets of MNIST images, to empirically estimate the local complexity and its evolution during training. Fully connected multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) with ReLU activations and varying widths and depths will be trained, with local complexity estimated numerically via gradient-based sampling and noise-perturbed parameter ensembles. Baselines will include measurements of local rank, total variation, and adversarial robustness (e.g., via PGD attacks). Evaluation metrics will include the density of linear regions, the rank of intermediate representations, total variation over the data distribution, and adversarial accuracy. Ablation studies will assess the impact of initialization scale and weight decay on local complexity.
18edf06b3df19a66cf6edbc884f27a46c40f891e.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretically grounded and robust measure of local complexity for ReLU networks, connecting geometric properties of the function (linear region density) to representation learning and robustness. Explicit connections are established between local complexity, the rank of learned features, and total variation, providing new insights into how feature learning and implicit regularization during optimization drive networks toward simpler, more robust solutions. The framework offers new theoretical and empirical tools to analyze the interplay between network architecture, training dynamics, and function complexity, and suggests practical implications for improving adversarial robustness and generalization.

18f6691def4672a5ecea02464b9649b7a103cf61.title: MOTO: Offline Pre-training to Online Fine-tuning for Model-based Robot Learning
18f6691def4672a5ecea02464b9649b7a103cf61.research_question: How can model-based reinforcement learning be effectively adapted for offline pre-training and online fine-tuning in high-dimensional robotic tasks, particularly when learning directly from pixel observations?
18f6691def4672a5ecea02464b9649b7a103cf61.hypothesis: A model-based actor-critic algorithm that leverages model-based value expansion, ensemble-based epistemic uncertainty estimation, and policy regularization can enable efficient and robust offline pre-training and online fine-tuning for robot learning from high-dimensional observations, outperforming existing model-free and model-based baselines.
18f6691def4672a5ecea02464b9649b7a103cf61.proposed_method: A novel model-based reinforcement learning algorithm, MOTO, is proposed for the offline-to-online fine-tuning setting. The method utilizes a recurrent variational autoencoder (VAE) world model (based on RSSM/DreamerV2) to encode high-dimensional observations into latent states, and trains an ensemble of such models to estimate epistemic uncertainty. Policy optimization is performed via model-based value expansion, where Monte Carlo rollouts in the latent space are used to compute value estimates for actor-critic updates, mixing real and model-generated data without requiring large replay buffers. Epistemic uncertainty is penalized in the reward function to prevent model exploitation, and policy regularization is applied using behaviour cloning on successful demonstration snippets to ensure safe and stable learning, especially in the early stages. The entire system is trained end-to-end, with joint updates to the world model, actor, and critic during both offline pre-training and online fine-tuning.
18f6691def4672a5ecea02464b9649b7a103cf61.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on ten tasks from the MetaWorld benchmark and two tasks from the Franka Kitchen environment, both using only 64x64 RGB image observations and sparse rewards. Offline datasets will consist of a small number (9-10) of demonstration episodes per task. The proposed method will be compared against prior vision-based offline model-based RL algorithms (LOMPO, COMBO, DreamerV2), model-free offline RL baselines (CQL, IQL, SAC), and behaviour cloning. All methods will undergo 10,000 offline gradient steps followed by 500,000 environment steps of online fine-tuning. Evaluation metrics will include task success rates and sample efficiency. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the contribution of model-based value expansion, uncertainty penalties, and policy regularization.
18f6691def4672a5ecea02464b9649b7a103cf61.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first model-based RL method to successfully solve the Franka Kitchen benchmark tasks directly from pixel observations. Key innovations include the integration of model-based value expansion without replay buffers, ensemble-based epistemic uncertainty penalties for robust policy learning, and behaviour-prior regularization for safe exploration. The method empirically demonstrates superior performance and sample efficiency compared to state-of-the-art baselines, and provides the first empirical validation of theoretical performance bounds for offline-to-online model-based RL in high-dimensional domains. The approach is designed to scale to large models and is suitable for future extensions to imitation learning, multi-task, and transfer learning.

18fb344c9bfd019014996e57c465aa279b7e0151.title: FastIF: Scalable Influence Functions for Efficient Model Interpretation and Debugging
18fb344c9bfd019014996e57c465aa279b7e0151.research_question: How can influence functions be made scalable and efficient for large-scale model interpretation and debugging tasks, enabling their practical use for model analysis, explanation, and error correction in modern deep learning models and datasets?
18fb344c9bfd019014996e57c465aa279b7e0151.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a combination of fast nearest neighbor search to restrict the candidate set, optimized hyperparameters for Hessian-vector product estimation, and parallel computation can significantly accelerate influence function computation without substantial loss in quality, thereby enabling efficient model interpretation and debugging at scale.
18fb344c9bfd019014996e57c465aa279b7e0151.proposed_method: A novel framework, FASTIF, is proposed to accelerate the computation of influence functions for deep learning models. The method first employs fast k-nearest neighbor (kNN) search to select a small, promising subset of training data points likely to be influential for a given test point, reducing the search space by orders of magnitude. Next, the approach optimizes the estimation of the inverse Hessian-vector product (HVP) by using mini-batch stochastic approximations, a Neumann series expansion, and carefully chosen hyperparameters (number of iterations, batch size, and repetitions) to balance speed and estimation quality. The method further leverages parallelization, distributing the computation of influence scores across multiple GPUs, with asynchronous computation and efficient aggregation of results. This framework is model-agnostic and can be applied post-hoc to any trained model without requiring retraining or modification of the original training process.
18fb344c9bfd019014996e57c465aa279b7e0151.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on several large-scale NLP datasets, including MultiNLI, HANS, ANLI, and Amazon-WILDS, using BERT-base models fine-tuned for each task. The evaluation includes runtime analysis, recall of influential points using kNN, and quality of influence estimation compared to full influence function computation. Baselines include the original influence function computation (full enumeration, serial HVP estimation), random selection, and direct fine-tuning on anchor data points. Evaluation metrics include computation time, correlation (Pearson, Spearman, Kendall) between fast and full influence values, recall of influential points, and downstream task performance (accuracy, loss) after model correction or data augmentation. The experimental setup uses V100 GPUs, with parallelization across up to 4 GPUs, and includes ablation studies on hyperparameters (batch size, number of iterations, repetitions) and their impact on speed and quality.
18fb344c9bfd019014996e57c465aa279b7e0151.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces three key innovations: (1) the use of fast kNN search to drastically reduce the candidate set for influence computation, (2) an optimized, parallelizable stochastic approximation for inverse Hessian-vector product estimation that balances speed and quality, and (3) a scalable, parallel implementation that enables influence function computation on large models and datasets previously considered intractable. The method achieves up to 80x speedup over standard influence function computation while maintaining high correlation with original influence values. Additionally, the framework enables new applications of influence functions, including efficient model explanation, visualization of influence interactions, and targeted model correction or data augmentation, demonstrating practical utility for model interpretation and debugging.

191a82f6b059c0d847d2e390dbb4c8b424388025.title: Mixture of LoRA Experts
191a82f6b059c0d847d2e390dbb4c8b424388025.research_question: How can multiple trained Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) modules be dynamically and efficiently composed to preserve their individual characteristics and enhance performance across diverse domains such as Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Vision & Language (V&L)?
191a82f6b059c0d847d2e390dbb4c8b424388025.hypothesis: A hierarchical, learnable gating mechanism that assigns layer-specific composition weights to multiple trained LoRA modules will enable more effective, flexible, and computationally efficient composition, preserving individual LoRA characteristics and improving downstream task performance compared to existing linear or reference-based composition methods.
191a82f6b059c0d847d2e390dbb4c8b424388025.proposed_method: The proposed method, Mixture of LoRA Experts (MOLE), treats each layer of multiple trained LoRA modules as a distinct expert and introduces a learnable gating function within each layer to determine optimal composition weights. For each transformer block in the pre-trained model, the outputs of all candidate LoRAs are concatenated and normalized. A gating function, parameterized by a learnable vector and temperature, computes a softmax distribution over the LoRA experts, producing layer-specific weights. The final output of each block is the sum of the pre-trained model's output and the weighted sum of LoRA outputs, where weights are dynamically learned to optimize for a domain-specific objective. The method includes a gating balancing loss to encourage balanced utilization of all experts and supports both full and masked inference modes for flexible composition.
191a82f6b059c0d847d2e390dbb4c8b424388025.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in both the V&L and NLP domains. In V&L, MOLE will be evaluated on multi-subject text-to-image generation tasks using DreamBooth (based on Stable Diffusion V2.1), composing 3-6 LoRA modules per experiment, with training at 512x512 resolution, a learning rate of 1e-5, and 400 iterations per composition. Evaluation metrics include CLIP-based text-image alignment and image-image alignment, with comparisons against normalized linear arithmetic composition and SVDiff, as well as full-parameter baselines like Custom and Textual Inversion. In NLP, MOLE will be tested using Flan-T5 as the base model, composing LoRAs trained on datasets such as WMT, CommonGen, DART, E2ENLG, WebNLG, ARC, NQ, TQA, ANLI, QNLI, and BBH. Metrics include BLEU, ROUGE, and Exact Match, with 800 training iterations per composition and batch size 12. Baselines include LoRAHub and PEMs. Additional analyses will examine scalability to larger numbers of LoRAs, generalization to new datasets, and the impact of gating granularity.
191a82f6b059c0d847d2e390dbb4c8b424388025.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel hierarchical gating mechanism for LoRA composition, enabling dynamic, layer-wise control of expert weights. This method preserves individual LoRA characteristics, supports flexible inference (including masking of experts), and achieves superior performance with minimal computational overhead compared to existing linear and reference-based composition methods. The approach is validated across both NLP and V&L domains, demonstrating improved alignment, generalization, and scalability, and offers a lightweight alternative to full-parameter training methods.

191f7ed65bb52d703afed822736f703acd15838d.title: Representational Difference Explanations
191f7ed65bb52d703afed822736f703acd15838d.research_question: How can the differences between two learned model representations be effectively identified and explained in a way that is interpretable and useful for model comparison, particularly in settings where existing explainable AI techniques are insufficient?
191f7ed65bb52d703afed822736f703acd15838d.hypothesis: A method that directly contrasts two learned representations by isolating and visualizing their unique similarity structures will provide more meaningful and interpretable explanations of model differences than existing dictionary learning-based explainable AI approaches.
191f7ed65bb52d703afed822736f703acd15838d.proposed_method: The proposed approach, Representational Difference Explanations (RDX), constructs an affinity matrix that highlights pairs of inputs considered similar by one model representation but not by the other. This is achieved by first computing pairwise normalized distance matrices for two sets of embeddings, then forming a difference matrix using a locally-biased difference function that emphasizes local similarity changes. Spectral clustering is applied to the resulting difference matrix to extract clusters of inputs that are uniquely grouped in one representation. These clusters are visualized as explanation grids, where each grid contains a set of semantically related samples that define a concept unique to one model. Optionally, a representational alignment step using centered kernel alignment (CKA) can be performed to account for global transformations before difference extraction.
191f7ed65bb52d703afed822736f703acd15838d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets, including modified MNIST (digits 3, 5, 8), CUB (Caltech-UCSD Birds) with concept bottleneck models, and challenging subsets of ImageNet and iNaturalist. Model comparisons will involve checkpoints with known architectural or training differences, as well as state-of-the-art models such as DINO, DINOv2, CLIP, and CLIP-iNat. Baselines for comparison will include dictionary learning methods (sparse autoencoders, non-negative matrix factorization, principal component analysis, KMeans), convex NMF, and non-linear multi-dimensional concept discovery. Evaluation metrics will include the proposed Binary Success Rate (BSR) for difference explanations, as well as Redundancy, Clarity, and Polysemanticity metrics from SemanticLens. Experimental setups will include both aligned and unaligned representations, and qualitative analysis will be performed via visualization of explanation grids.
191f7ed65bb52d703afed822736f703acd15838d.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel framework for directly contrasting two model representations to isolate and visualize their substantive differences, rather than explaining each model independently. RDX requires no additional training and can be applied to any embedding-based model, offering flexibility and ease of use. The approach leverages a locally-biased difference function and spectral clustering to extract interpretable, concept-level explanations of representational differences. A new evaluation metric, Binary Success Rate, is proposed to quantitatively assess the quality of difference explanations. Experiments demonstrate that RDX reveals meaningful and fine-grained differences between models where existing XAI techniques fail, supporting both knowledge discovery and model debugging.

19261c6ad20c6c1e5585a8afcb88196173cbc8a6.title: WebVoyager: Building an End-to-End Web Agent with Large Multimodal Models
19261c6ad20c6c1e5585a8afcb88196173cbc8a6.research_question: How can a large multimodal model-based web agent autonomously complete complex, real-world web tasks end-to-end by interacting with live websites, and how can such agents be reliably evaluated at scale?
19261c6ad20c6c1e5585a8afcb88196173cbc8a6.hypothesis: A web agent that leverages both visual (screenshots) and textual (HTML elements) modalities, powered by large multimodal models, will outperform text-only or tool-based agents in completing real-world web tasks. Furthermore, an automated evaluation protocol using a multimodal LLM can achieve high agreement with human judgment for assessing open-ended web agent performance.
19261c6ad20c6c1e5585a8afcb88196173cbc8a6.proposed_method: The proposed method develops an end-to-end web agent, WebVoyager, that operates directly on the open web using a large multimodal model (LMM) such as GPT-4V, Claude-3-Opus, or GPT-4o as its backbone. The agent receives both webpage screenshots (with overlaid bounding boxes and numeric labels for interactive elements) and auxiliary textual information (element type, content, aria-labels) as input at each step. Actions are generated in a two-stage process: first, the agent produces a natural language 'thought' reflecting its reasoning, then outputs an executable action (e.g., click, input, scroll, wait, back, jump to search, answer) that is performed in a Selenium-powered browser. The agent maintains a context of the last three observations and the full history of thoughts and actions. Interactive elements are identified using a rule-based JavaScript tool (GPT-4V-ACT), and the agent iteratively interacts with the environment until the task is completed or a step limit is reached.
