19261c6ad20c6c1e5585a8afcb88196173cbc8a6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a newly constructed benchmark of 643 real-world web tasks sampled from 15 popular websites spanning diverse domains (e.g., Amazon, Apple, BBC News, Google services, GitHub, Booking, etc.), as well as on 90 tasks from the GAIA dataset and 50 tasks from the SeeAct evaluation set. Baselines will include GPT-4 (All Tools) and a text-only version of WebVoyager using the accessibility tree as input. The primary evaluation metric is Task Success Rate, defined as the proportion of tasks completed successfully. Both human evaluation (binary success/failure) and an automated evaluation protocol using GPT-4V (and other LMMs) as evaluators will be employed, with agreement and kappa statistics reported to measure consistency between human and automatic judgments. The browser window size and agent step limits will be fixed for consistency.
19261c6ad20c6c1e5585a8afcb88196173cbc8a6.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first end-to-end web agent that leverages both visual and textual modalities to interact with live, real-world websites, rather than simulators or static snapshots. A new, diverse benchmark of real-world web tasks is constructed for comprehensive evaluation. An automated evaluation protocol using a multimodal LLM (GPT-4V) is developed, achieving high agreement (85.3%) with human annotators, enabling scalable and reliable assessment of open-ended web agent performance. The approach demonstrates significant improvements over existing baselines, highlighting the importance of multimodal understanding for web automation.

192c71e66832deb1598118c955c969914effef27.title: Optimal Transport-Guided Conditional Score-Based Diffusion Models
192c71e66832deb1598118c955c969914effef27.research_question: How can conditional score-based diffusion models be effectively trained for conditional generation tasks when only unpaired or partially paired datasets are available, particularly in image-to-image translation and super-resolution applications?
192c71e66832deb1598118c955c969914effef27.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging optimal transport to estimate a coupling relationship between condition and target data enables effective training of conditional score-based diffusion models in unpaired or partially paired settings, resulting in high-quality conditional generation.
192c71e66832deb1598118c955c969914effef27.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that integrates optimal transport (OT) with conditional score-based diffusion models (SBDMs) for scenarios where paired data is scarce or unavailable. The method first estimates a soft coupling between condition and target data using L2-regularized unsupervised OT for unpaired settings, or semi-supervised OT when some paired data is available. This coupling is encoded as a compatibility function, which is then used to define a new training objective for the conditional score-based model, generalizing the standard denoising score-matching loss to unpaired or partially paired data. To address instability in mini-batch training, a 'resampling-by-compatibility' strategy is introduced, where target samples are selected for each condition sample in proportion to their OT-derived compatibility, ensuring that training focuses on high-quality pseudo-pairs. The conditional score-based model is trained using this objective, and sample generation is performed via the reverse-time SDE conditioned on the input.
192c71e66832deb1598118c955c969914effef27.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on unpaired super-resolution (using the CelebA dataset) and semi-paired image-to-image translation tasks (using Animal Faces HQ and MNIST/Chinese-MNIST datasets). For unpaired super-resolution, the method will use L2-regularized unsupervised OT with mean squared L2 distance as the cost, while for semi-paired translation, semi-supervised OT with cosine feature distance (using CLIP embeddings) will be used. Baselines will include adversarial OT methods (W2GAN, OT-ICNN, OTM, NOT, KNOT), diffusion-based unpaired I2I methods (EGSDE, DDIB), flow-based methods (ReFlow), and SCONES, as well as the semi-paired I2I method TCR. Evaluation metrics will include FID (Fréchet Inception Distance) for image quality, SSIM for structural similarity, and classification accuracy for translation correctness. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the resampling-by-compatibility strategy and the number of paired samples.
192c71e66832deb1598118c955c969914effef27.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable conditional score-based diffusion models to be trained directly on unpaired or partially paired datasets by leveraging optimal transport to estimate a soft coupling between domains. The introduction of the OT-guided conditional denoising score-matching objective and the resampling-by-compatibility training strategy are novel contributions that address the challenges of instability and lack of explicit pairing in the data. The method theoretically and empirically demonstrates the ability to approximate the optimal conditional transport plan, achieving state-of-the-art results in both unpaired and semi-paired image translation tasks, and providing a scalable solution for data transport in large-scale OT settings.

193955704f66923ac20a664bd184ed4663b2bdf9.title: Continual Pre-Training of Large Language Models: How to (re)warm your model?
193955704f66923ac20a664bd184ed4663b2bdf9.research_question: How can large language models be efficiently updated with new data through continual pre-training, while maintaining performance on both new and previously seen data, and what strategies for learning rate scheduling and warm-up phases optimize this process?
193955704f66923ac20a664bd184ed4663b2bdf9.hypothesis: Re-increasing the learning rate (re-warming) during continual pre-training on new data can improve compute efficiency and downstream performance, potentially outperforming models trained from scratch, while careful tuning of learning rate schedules can balance adaptation to new data and retention of past knowledge.
193955704f66923ac20a664bd184ed4663b2bdf9.proposed_method: A systematic investigation will be conducted into the effects of various warm-up strategies and learning rate schedules during continual pre-training of large language models. The approach involves resuming training of a pre-trained model (initially trained on a large dataset, such as the Pile) on a new, similarly large dataset (such as SlimPajama), using linear warm-up followed by cosine decay learning rate schedules. Experiments will vary the length of the warm-up phase, the maximum learning rate, and the choice of pre-trained checkpoint (including earlier and later stages of pre-training). The method will also assess the impact of re-warming on both data with and without distribution shift, and compare continual pre-training to training from scratch.
193955704f66923ac20a664bd184ed4663b2bdf9.experiment_details: Experiments will use the Pythia 410M language model architecture, initially pre-trained on the Pile dataset (300B tokens), and then continually pre-trained on the SlimPajama dataset (297B tokens). The same tokenizer as in prior Pythia work will be used, and training will be conducted with the AdamW optimizer (β1=0.9, β2=0.95, ε=1e-8, weight decay=0.1), cosine learning rate decay (to 10% of max LR), and gradient clipping at 1.0. Validation perplexity will be measured on both upstream (Pile) and downstream (SlimPajama) datasets. Baselines will include models trained from scratch on SlimPajama and models using constant learning rates. Key variables include warm-up length (0%, 0.5%, 1%, 2% of data), maximum learning rate (1.5e-4, 3e-4, 6e-4), and checkpoint selection. Additional experiments will test re-warming on the same data (no distribution shift) and evaluate the effect of starting from earlier pre-training checkpoints.
193955704f66923ac20a664bd184ed4663b2bdf9.novelty_claims: The proposal aims to provide the first systematic study of the influence of warm-up phase strategies in the context of continual pre-training for large language models. It introduces the concept of re-warming the learning rate as a scalable, compute-efficient alternative to full retraining, and investigates the trade-offs between adaptation to new data and retention of prior knowledge. The approach is novel in its scale (hundreds of billions of tokens, large model sizes), in its detailed analysis of learning rate scheduling, and in its comparison of continual pre-training to training from scratch on similarly large datasets.

195dc158fa820c70f9d9892b7f2a150ca0cfc939.title: DYffusion: A Dynamics-informed Diffusion Model for Spatiotemporal Forecasting
195dc158fa820c70f9d9892b7f2a150ca0cfc939.research_question: How can diffusion models be adapted and enhanced for efficient, accurate, and probabilistic forecasting of high-dimensional spatiotemporal dynamics, particularly for long-range and multi-step prediction tasks?
195dc158fa820c70f9d9892b7f2a150ca0cfc939.hypothesis: Incorporating temporal dynamics directly into the diffusion process via a dynamics-informed, time-conditioned framework will improve the stability, accuracy, and computational efficiency of probabilistic spatiotemporal forecasting compared to standard Gaussian noise-based diffusion models and conventional autoregressive approaches.
195dc158fa820c70f9d9892b7f2a150ca0cfc939.proposed_method: A novel framework, DYffusion, is developed that reimagines the forward and reverse processes of diffusion models as temporal interpolation and forecasting, respectively. The forward process is implemented as a stochastic, time-conditioned interpolator neural network that learns to interpolate between initial and future states, introducing a temporal inductive bias. The reverse process is realized as a deterministic forecaster network that predicts future states conditioned on interpolated intermediate states and time indices, mimicking the denoising process in standard diffusion models. Training is performed in two stages: first, the interpolator is trained to stochastically interpolate between data snapshots; second, the forecaster is trained with the interpolator frozen, optimizing a loss that combines direct forecasting and a one-step look-ahead to mitigate error accumulation. Monte Carlo dropout is used in the interpolator to enable stochasticity, and the framework supports flexible, continuous-time sampling trajectories, allowing trade-offs between accuracy and inference speed.
195dc158fa820c70f9d9892b7f2a150ca0cfc939.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on three benchmark datasets: Sea Surface Temperatures (SST) from NOAA OISSTv2, Navier-Stokes fluid flow, and Spring Mesh particle systems. The same neural network backbones are used for all baselines and for both the interpolator and forecaster in DYffusion, with UNet architectures for SST and Navier-Stokes, and a CNN for Spring Mesh. Baselines include DDPM (standard diffusion), MCVD (video diffusion), Dropout and Perturbation ensemble methods, and barebone multi-step forecasters. Evaluation metrics include Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS), Mean Squared Error (MSE), and Spread-Skill Ratio (SSR), with ensembles of 20-50 samples generated for each test case. Models are evaluated on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution test sets, with a focus on long-range, multi-step forecasting (up to 804 steps for Spring Mesh and 7 days for SST), and experiments include ablations on stochasticity, sampling schedules, and training data size.
195dc158fa820c70f9d9892b7f2a150ca0cfc939.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a dynamics-informed diffusion process that directly couples diffusion steps with the temporal evolution of the underlying system, imposing a strong inductive bias and reducing computational complexity. Unlike standard diffusion models, the forward process is realized via a stochastic interpolator rather than Gaussian noise, and the reverse process operates in the data space at all times, enabling efficient, stable, and flexible multi-step forecasting. The framework naturally supports continuous-time sampling and long-range rollouts, and can be interpreted as implicitly learning the solutions to the underlying dynamical system. Empirical results demonstrate improved computational efficiency and competitive or superior probabilistic forecasting performance, particularly for long-range and high-dimensional spatiotemporal tasks, compared to both standard diffusion and ensemble-based baselines.

198fb07ae84ca36f98a362058fb8a90e214bea06.title: Rep ViT: Revisiting Mobile CNN From ViT Perspective
198fb07ae84ca36f98a362058fb8a90e214bea06.research_question: Can the architectural designs and principles from lightweight Vision Transformers (ViTs) be systematically integrated into lightweight Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to improve their performance and efficiency for deployment on resource-constrained mobile devices across a range of computer vision tasks?
198fb07ae84ca36f98a362058fb8a90e214bea06.hypothesis: Integrating efficient architectural designs from lightweight ViTs into lightweight CNNs will result in pure CNN architectures that outperform existing state-of-the-art lightweight ViTs and CNNs in terms of accuracy and latency on mobile devices, while maintaining or improving transferability to downstream vision tasks.
198fb07ae84ca36f98a362058fb8a90e214bea06.proposed_method: A new family of lightweight CNNs, termed RepViT, will be developed by incrementally enhancing a standard lightweight CNN (MobileNetV3-L) with architectural elements inspired by lightweight ViTs. The process involves: (1) separating token mixer and channel mixer modules using structural re-parameterization to mimic the MetaFormer block structure found in ViTs; (2) reducing the expansion ratio in the channel mixer and increasing network width for improved efficiency; (3) optimizing macro-architecture by employing early convolutional stems, deeper downsampling layers, a simplified classifier, and an aggressive stage ratio; (4) refining micro-architecture through the use of 3x3 convolutions and strategic, cross-block placement of squeeze-and-excitation (SE) layers. Multiple RepViT variants will be constructed by varying the number of channels and blocks per stage to target different latency and performance trade-offs.
198fb07ae84ca36f98a362058fb8a90e214bea06.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard computer vision benchmarks, including ImageNet-1K for image classification, MS COCO 2017 for object detection and instance segmentation, and ADE20K for semantic segmentation. The models will be trained from scratch for 300 or 450 epochs using a consistent training recipe (AdamW optimizer, cosine learning rate schedule, data augmentations, and label smoothing), with and without knowledge distillation from a strong teacher (RegNetY-16GF). Latency will be measured on an iPhone 12 using CoreMLTools, with batch size 1 and GeLU activations to ensure hardware compatibility. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art lightweight ViTs (e.g., EfficientFormerV2, FastViT, SwiftFormer), lightweight CNNs (e.g., MobileNetV3, MobileOne), and hybrid models. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy, latency (ms), throughput (images/sec), APbox, APmask, and mIoU. Additional experiments will assess transferability by integrating RepViT into the Segment Anything Model (SAM) framework and evaluating zero-shot transfer tasks.
198fb07ae84ca36f98a362058fb8a90e214bea06.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a pure CNN architecture that systematically incorporates efficient design principles from lightweight ViTs, resulting in the RepViT family. This is the first time a lightweight CNN achieves over 80% top-1 accuracy with 1.0 ms latency on a real mobile device (iPhone 12). RepViT demonstrates superior accuracy-latency trade-offs compared to both lightweight ViTs and CNNs, and achieves state-of-the-art results across multiple vision tasks. The method also enables the creation of RepViT-SAM, which provides nearly 10× faster inference than MobileSAM while maintaining competitive transfer performance. The work highlights the promising potential of pure lightweight CNNs for edge deployment and provides a strong baseline for future research.

19cb32d761a9ca76dec86e69d6ad8ff5d27c2562.title: Symplectic model reduction of Hamiltonian systems using data-driven quadratic manifolds
19cb32d761a9ca76dec86e69d6ad8ff5d27c2562.research_question: How can model reduction techniques for high-dimensional Hamiltonian systems be improved to better preserve the underlying geometric (symplectic) structure and achieve higher accuracy and efficiency, especially in cases where the Kolmogorov N-width decays slowly, such as in wave-type problems?
19cb32d761a9ca76dec86e69d6ad8ff5d27c2562.hypothesis: Introducing data-driven quadratic manifolds into symplectic model reduction frameworks will enable more accurate and stable reduced-order models for Hamiltonian systems, preserving the geometric structure and improving predictive capability beyond the range of training data compared to conventional linear subspace approaches.
19cb32d761a9ca76dec86e69d6ad8ff5d27c2562.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed for symplectic model reduction of Hamiltonian systems by constructing data-driven quadratic manifolds for the state approximation. Two main approaches will be implemented: (1) the Quadratic Manifold Cotangent Lift (QMCL) method, which constructs a symplectic, nonlinear approximation mapping using quadratic terms and applies the Symplectic Manifold Galerkin (SMG) projection to derive a reduced Hamiltonian system that strictly preserves the symplectic structure; and (2) the Blockwise-Quadratic (BQ) approximation mapping, which augments the linear symplectic approximation with quadratic terms and applies a Galerkin projection to yield an approximately Hamiltonian reduced-order model with improved computational efficiency. Both methods involve learning quadratic manifolds from high-dimensional snapshot data via regularized least-squares optimization, ensuring orthogonality and interpretability of the reduced basis. The reduced-order operators are precomputed offline for efficient online simulation.
19cb32d761a9ca76dec86e69d6ad8ff5d27c2562.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on high-dimensional Hamiltonian systems arising from the semi-discretization of partial differential equations, specifically including a one-dimensional linear wave equation and a two-dimensional nonlinear wave equation. The proposed reduced-order models (ROMs) will be trained on snapshot data collected over various time intervals and parameter settings. Baseline comparisons will include classical symplectic model reduction methods using linear subspaces. Evaluation metrics will comprise relative state error, energy conservation error, and long-time stability, with additional studies on extrapolation to unseen parameter values and time intervals to assess predictive performance. All models will be integrated using structure-preserving numerical integrators, and the dimensionality of the reduced models will be systematically varied to analyze accuracy and stability.
19cb32d761a9ca76dec86e69d6ad8ff5d27c2562.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first strictly structure-preserving symplectic model reduction methods for Hamiltonian systems using data-driven quadratic manifolds. The QMCL approach guarantees symplecticity and interpretability in the reduced-order mapping, while the BQ method offers a computationally efficient, physics-preserving augmentation of linear ROMs. Both approaches are claimed to yield more accurate and stable predictions than existing linear symplectic ROMs, especially for systems with slowly decaying Kolmogorov N-widths, and to provide robust extrapolation capabilities beyond the training regime.

19db2d61f20a6c439cc79f28ef4c9e4bf26cd20e.title: Preference Ranking Optimization for Human Alignment
19db2d61f20a6c439cc79f28ef4c9e4bf26cd20e.research_question: How can large language models be efficiently and effectively aligned with human preferences using direct optimization methods that overcome the complexity and instability of reinforcement learning from human feedback?
19db2d61f20a6c439cc79f28ef4c9e4bf26cd20e.hypothesis: Directly optimizing language models using preference rankings of arbitrary length, rather than relying on pairwise contrasts and reinforcement learning, will yield more stable, efficient, and effective human alignment, leading to improved performance on human preference metrics.
19db2d61f20a6c439cc79f28ef4c9e4bf26cd20e.proposed_method: A novel supervised fine-tuning (SFT) algorithm, Preference Ranking Optimization (PRO), is developed to directly align large language models (LLMs) with human preferences. PRO generalizes the traditional pairwise contrastive approach to handle preference rankings of any length by iteratively contrasting the top-ranked response against the remaining candidates, then recursively proceeding down the ranking. The method employs a multi-positional, multi-dimensional objective inspired by the Plackett-Luce model, optimizing the LLM to match the probability ranking of n responses to the human-provided preference order. The approach also integrates a dynamic temperature mechanism to modulate penalties based on reward model scores, and can flexibly incorporate additional responses—either from other LLMs or self-bootstrapped generations—into the ranking set. The final objective combines the PRO alignment loss with a standard supervised loss to maintain both alignment and text quality.
19db2d61f20a6c439cc79f28ef4c9e4bf26cd20e.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the HH-RLHF dataset, which contains human-annotated rankings of conversational responses, with both raw and augmented versions (the latter expanded by adding responses from models such as Alpaca and ChatGPT). The main backbone is LLaMA-7B, and baselines include SFT, RLHF, CoH, DPO, RRHF, and best-of-n sampling, as well as zero-shot evaluations from LLaMA, Curie, Alpaca, ChatGLM, and ChatGPT. Evaluation metrics include BLEU for text quality, reward model scores for alignment, and both GPT-4 and human preference judgments. Experiments systematically vary the ranking length and diversity of candidate responses, and ablation studies assess the impact of key components such as the PRO loss, dynamic temperature, and ranking depth. Implementation details specify hyperparameters, batch sizes, and the use of open-source reward models for both training and evaluation.
19db2d61f20a6c439cc79f28ef4c9e4bf26cd20e.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a direct, efficient, and scalable framework for human alignment that extends beyond pairwise preference optimization to arbitrary-length rankings, fully leveraging available human feedback. PRO eliminates the need for complex reinforcement learning loops, reward model approximation, and trial-and-error sampling, instead providing a differentiable, single-stage objective that can be flexibly integrated with additional ranking data. The approach demonstrates superior or competitive performance to state-of-the-art baselines, including RLHF and DPO, and achieves results comparable to ChatGPT with significantly smaller models. Additional innovations include the integration of dynamic temperature scaling based on reward model gaps, and the demonstration that increased ranking length and candidate diversity lead to better alignment outcomes.

19df5eb2c74606414ed93633b4c61947cc42dbbb.title: Some things are more CRINGE than others: Preference Optimization with the Pairwise Cringe Loss
19df5eb2c74606414ed93633b4c61947cc42dbbb.research_question: How can language models be more effectively aligned with human preferences using pairwise preference data, and can existing binary feedback optimization methods be generalized to this setting to improve performance on instruction-following and alignment tasks?
19df5eb2c74606414ed93633b4c61947cc42dbbb.hypothesis: Generalizing the Cringe Loss, originally designed for binary feedback, to the pairwise preference setting with a margin-based extension will result in more effective preference optimization and improved model alignment compared to state-of-the-art methods such as PPO and DPO.
19df5eb2c74606414ed93633b4c61947cc42dbbb.proposed_method: A novel Pairwise Cringe Loss is introduced by extending the Cringe Loss from binary feedback to pairwise preference data. The method defines a margin between the log-likelihoods of the preferred and non-preferred responses for a given input, and applies a sigmoid-gated Cringe Loss to penalize the less preferred response when the margin is small. The loss combines sequence-level and token-level optimization by updating the model to increase the likelihood of the preferred response and decrease the likelihood of the non-preferred one, using contrastive sampling of alternative tokens. Iterative training is proposed, where after an initial round of training on human-labeled pairwise preferences, new responses are generated by the improved model, labeled with a reward model, and used to further fine-tune the model in subsequent iterations. The approach is efficient, straightforward to implement, and can be applied with or without a reward model.
19df5eb2c74606414ed93633b4c61947cc42dbbb.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on two main tasks: a repetition mitigation task and general instruction following using the AlpacaFarm benchmark. For repetition mitigation, GPT2-Medium is fine-tuned on a large web-based corpus and evaluated on a test set for n-gram repetition and F1 score against human responses. Preference pairs are constructed by comparing outputs from beam-blocking and greedy decoding. For instruction following, the Llama-7b model is fine-tuned using 10k instruction-following demonstrations and 10k pairwise human preference annotations from AlpacaFarm, with additional unlabeled instructions for iterative training. Baselines include SFT, PPO, DPO, Binary Cringe Loss, and best-of-n methods. Evaluation uses LLM-based win rates over 805 prompts, with results averaged over multiple seeds. Ablation studies compare soft versus hard margin gating and the impact of iterative training.
19df5eb2c74606414ed93633b4c61947cc42dbbb.novelty_claims: The proposed method generalizes the Cringe Loss to the pairwise preference setting with a novel margin-based, sigmoid-gated loss, combining sequence-level and token-level optimization. Iterative preference optimization is introduced for both Pairwise Cringe Loss and DPO, leading to improved performance. The approach is simple, efficient, and outperforms state-of-the-art preference optimization algorithms such as PPO and DPO on the AlpacaFarm benchmark. The method is also versatile, supporting both binary and pairwise feedback in a unified framework.

19e499d76a2e49574b499cd9ebd31304880d33d6.title: Language Model Cascades: Token-level uncertainty and beyond
19e499d76a2e49574b499cd9ebd31304880d33d6.research_question: How can adaptive inference strategies be improved for generative language model cascades to achieve better cost-quality tradeoffs, particularly through more effective deferral rules that leverage uncertainty estimates?
19e499d76a2e49574b499cd9ebd31304880d33d6.hypothesis: Incorporating token-level uncertainty information and learned post-hoc deferral rules, potentially augmented with intermediate model embeddings, will yield more effective and consistent cost-quality tradeoffs in language model cascades than traditional sequence-level uncertainty aggregation methods.
19e499d76a2e49574b499cd9ebd31304880d33d6.proposed_method: A novel framework for language model cascades will be developed, focusing on deferral rules that exploit token-level uncertainty. Rather than relying on aggregate sequence-level uncertainty (such as sum or average log-probabilities), the method will compute multiple quantiles over the per-token uncertainty vector produced by the small model for each generated sequence. These quantile features, along with aggregate scores (e.g., Chow-Sum and Chow-Average), will be used as inputs to a post-hoc trained deferral rule, implemented as a feedforward neural network. The deferral rule will be trained to predict whether deferring to a larger model would improve quality, using supervised targets derived from model performance differences. Optionally, the approach will be extended to incorporate intermediate embeddings from both the small and large models as additional features, further enriching the deferral decision process.
19e499d76a2e49574b499cd9ebd31304880d33d6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using FLAN-T5 models of varying sizes (e.g., Base and Large) in two-model cascades. Evaluation will span a diverse set of NLP tasks, including classification (MNLI, IMDb, SuperGLUE, ANLI), question answering (TriviaQA, NaturalQA, TyDiQA), reading comprehension (Lambada, SQuAD), translation (WMT14 EN→FR, WMT19 DE→FR, WMT14 FR→EN), and commonsense reasoning (Winogrande). For each task, the cascade's performance will be measured by the area under the deferral curve (AUC-DF), which plots the tradeoff between deferral rate and cascade quality as the deferral threshold is varied. Baselines will include traditional sequence-level uncertainty aggregation methods (sum and average), as well as various quantile-based rules. The post-hoc deferral rule will be trained on held-out data, with evaluation on separate test sets. For translation tasks, BLEURT score differences will be used as training targets; for classification, correctness labels will be used.
19e499d76a2e49574b499cd9ebd31304880d33d6.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the use of token-level uncertainty quantiles as features for deferral in language model cascades, addressing the limitations of traditional sequence-level aggregation methods which suffer from length bias. It further innovates by learning post-hoc deferral rules that combine multiple quantile features, enabling adaptation to diverse tasks and datasets. The integration of intermediate embeddings from both small and large models into the deferral rule represents an additional novel contribution, offering a richer decision basis and further improving cost-quality tradeoffs. This approach systematically advances the understanding and practical effectiveness of adaptive inference in generative language models.

19edd41688c844d4ffd5230b417b99b5fd041cf1.title: Efficient Bayesian Learning Curve Extrapolation using Prior-Data Fitted Networks
19edd41688c844d4ffd5230b417b99b5fd041cf1.research_question: How can Bayesian learning curve extrapolation be made both computationally efficient and flexible enough to accurately predict the future performance of machine learning models across diverse architectures and datasets?
19edd41688c844d4ffd5230b417b99b5fd041cf1.hypothesis: Prior-data fitted networks (PFNs), when trained on a suitably informative generative prior over learning curves, can approximate the posterior predictive distribution for learning curve extrapolation more efficiently and accurately than traditional MCMC-based Bayesian methods.
19edd41688c844d4ffd5230b417b99b5fd041cf1.proposed_method: A novel approach will be developed that leverages prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) for Bayesian learning curve extrapolation. The method involves training a transformer-based PFN on artificial learning curves generated from a parametric prior designed to reflect realistic model training dynamics, including bounded support and constraints to ensure valid curve shapes. The PFN is meta-trained to predict the posterior predictive distribution (PPD) of future model performance, conditioned on observed partial learning curves, by minimizing the cross-entropy between its predictions and the true PPD over many sampled tasks. The architecture encodes each observed epoch and performance pair as a token, uses permutation-invariant attention masking, and outputs a discretized predictive distribution over future epochs. Hyperparameters such as embedding size, number of layers, and number of training samples will be tuned to optimize performance.
19edd41688c844d4ffd5230b417b99b5fd041cf1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in two phases: first, controlled tests will be performed using 10,000 synthetic learning curves sampled from the defined prior, comparing the PFN-based approach to a strong MCMC baseline (with extensive hyperparameter tuning) using log-likelihood of the true curve under the inferred PPD as the main metric. Second, the method will be evaluated on 20,000 real-world learning curves from four diverse benchmarks (LCBench, NAS-Bench-201, Taskset, and PD1), covering MLPs, CNNs, RNNs, and Transformers across tabular, image, text, and protein data. Baselines will include MCMC with both the new and original priors, and evaluation metrics will include log-likelihood and mean squared error (MSE) of the predicted medians. Additionally, the practical utility of the method will be assessed in a model selection scenario, using early stopping criteria based on the extrapolated PPD, and comparing against standard heuristics (e.g., Patience) and no-stopping baselines. All experiments will be run with careful control of computational resources and reproducibility ensured by open-sourcing code and data.
19edd41688c844d4ffd5230b417b99b5fd041cf1.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first application of prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) to Bayesian learning curve extrapolation, enabling efficient and accurate approximation of the posterior predictive distribution in a single forward pass. The approach is claimed to be over 10,000 times faster than MCMC-based baselines while achieving equal or superior probabilistic extrapolation quality. It is further claimed that the method generalizes well across a wide range of model architectures and data modalities, and that it enables practical early stopping in model selection, yielding significant speed-ups with negligible computational overhead. The open-sourcing of all code, data, and models is also highlighted as a contribution to reproducibility and future research.

19f4d1533d8f7c4c13e9732c36fb374edd5ad470.title: Manifold Preserving Guided Diffusion
19f4d1533d8f7c4c13e9732c36fb374edd5ad470.research_question: How can conditional image generation be improved to be more efficient, generalizable, and training-free, while maintaining high sample quality across a broad range of tasks?
19f4d1533d8f7c4c13e9732c36fb374edd5ad470.hypothesis: Incorporating manifold-preserving guidance into the diffusion process, by projecting guidance gradients onto the data manifold using pretrained autoencoders, will enable efficient, training-free conditional generation that maintains or improves sample quality and reduces computational cost compared to existing training-free guided diffusion methods.
19f4d1533d8f7c4c13e9732c36fb374edd5ad470.proposed_method: A novel framework, Manifold Preserving Guided Diffusion (MPGD), is developed to enable training-free conditional image generation using pretrained diffusion models and off-the-shelf neural networks. The method leverages the manifold hypothesis, positing that real data lies on a lower-dimensional manifold within the ambient space, and refines the diffusion process by projecting guidance gradients onto the tangent space of this manifold at each step. Two practical manifold projection strategies are proposed: (1) projecting the guidance onto the manifold using a pretrained autoencoder (MPGD-AE), and (2) manipulating the latent representation directly (MPGD-Z), both ensuring that updates remain on the data manifold. For latent diffusion models, the method exploits the natural alignment between the latent space and the data manifold, allowing efficient manifold-preserving guidance (MPGD-LDM). The framework also incorporates a shortcut algorithm that reduces the need for repeated gradient computations, and supports multi-step optimization for further performance gains.
19f4d1533d8f7c4c13e9732c36fb374edd5ad470.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of conditional image generation tasks, including noisy linear inverse problems (such as super-resolution and Gaussian deblurring), FaceID-guided face generation, and text-to-image generation with style guidance. Datasets used include FFHQ, ImageNet, CelebA-HQ, WikiArt, and PartiPrompts. Baseline methods for comparison include DPS, LGD-MC, MCG, and FreeDoM, with pretrained diffusion models provided by prior works. Evaluation metrics will include Kernel Inception Distance (KID) for fidelity, Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity (LPIPS) for guidance quality, FaceID loss for identity preservation, inference time, and GPU memory usage. Experiments will be run on standard GPUs (e.g., NVIDIA RTX 2080 Ti, RTX 3090 Ti, A100), and results will be reported for different numbers of diffusion steps to assess the trade-off between quality and efficiency.
19f4d1533d8f7c4c13e9732c36fb374edd5ad470.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a training-free, manifold-preserving guidance framework for conditional generation that leverages pretrained autoencoders to project guidance gradients onto the data manifold. It provides a shortcut algorithm that significantly reduces inference time and memory usage while maintaining or improving sample quality. The approach is generalizable to both pixel-space and latent diffusion models, supports a broad range of conditional generation tasks, and achieves consistent speed-ups (up to 3.8×) over existing baselines. The method also offers a principled analysis of the manifold hypothesis within the diffusion process and demonstrates practical strategies for manifold projection using imperfect, off-the-shelf autoencoders.

19fe975249d368d29dfe60d2ffd07e5438d7ec1f.title: Contrastive Localized Language-Image Pre-Training
19fe975249d368d29dfe60d2ffd07e5438d7ec1f.research_question: How can vision-language pre-training be enhanced to improve the localization capabilities of image encoders for fine-grained region-level understanding, while maintaining strong image-level performance and scalability for integration into multimodal large language models?
19fe975249d368d29dfe60d2ffd07e5438d7ec1f.hypothesis: Incorporating explicit region-text alignment and promptable embedding mechanisms into contrastive language-image pre-training will yield image encoders with superior localization capabilities, enabling improved performance on region-level recognition and retrieval tasks as well as downstream multimodal applications.
19fe975249d368d29dfe60d2ffd07e5438d7ec1f.proposed_method: A new pre-training framework, Contrastive Localized Language-Image Pre-Training (CLOC), will be developed to enhance the localization capability of vision encoders. The method introduces a region-text contrastive loss in addition to the standard image-text contrastive objective, enabling the encoder to learn promptable embeddings that can be transformed into region-specific representations given spatial cues such as bounding boxes or text prompts. A lightweight Prompter module, implemented as a single-layer transformer encoder, will be attached to the image encoder to extract region-aware features from the image embedding, conditioned on spatial hints. To support large-scale training, a Visually-Enriched and Spatially-Localized (VESL) captioning pipeline will be designed, combining open-vocabulary detectors and advanced captioners to pseudo-label billions of images with high-quality region-text pairs. All components will be trained end-to-end from scratch using the combined image-text and region-text datasets.
19fe975249d368d29dfe60d2ffd07e5438d7ec1f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a wide range of tasks, including standard image-level benchmarks (e.g., ImageNet classification, COCO image-text retrieval) and newly constructed region-level tasks such as region classification and region-text retrieval using datasets like COCO, LVIS, and GRIT. The pre-training will utilize large-scale datasets, including WiT-300M and a 2B-image subset of DFN-5B, with region annotations generated by the VESL pipeline. Baselines will include standard CLIP models and variants with alternative region extraction mechanisms (e.g., RoI-Align). Evaluation metrics will include recall@K for retrieval, mean accuracy for classification, and IoU-based metrics for grounding and referring tasks. The proposed encoder will also be integrated into multimodal large language models (e.g., Ferret, LLaVA-1.5, Open-LLaVA-NeXT) to assess improvements in referring, grounding, and general VQA tasks.
19fe975249d368d29dfe60d2ffd07e5438d7ec1f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces promptable embeddings as a new learning objective, enabling image encoders to flexibly produce region-specific features conditioned on spatial or textual prompts. The framework augments the standard CLIP loss with a region-text contrastive loss and employs a lightweight, transformer-based Prompter for efficient and flexible region feature extraction. A scalable VESL captioning pipeline is designed to generate high-quality region-text annotations at web scale, overcoming the lack of large-scale region-level datasets. The resulting encoder is intended as a drop-in replacement for CLIP, offering competitive image-level performance while unlocking emergent zero-shot region-level capabilities and improved fine-grained understanding in multimodal language models.

1a3763f38e84bf5a43c34df10a381a4449146acc.title: Large Language Models Effectively Leverage Document-level Context for Literary Translation, but Critical Errors Persist
1a3763f38e84bf5a43c34df10a381a4449146acc.research_question: How can large language models be leveraged to improve the quality of literary translation at the document or paragraph level across diverse language pairs, and what are the strengths and limitations of such approaches compared to sentence-level and commercial machine translation systems?
1a3763f38e84bf5a43c34df10a381a4449146acc.hypothesis: Providing large language models with paragraph-level or document-level context will result in higher-quality literary translations, with fewer errors in coherence, style, and context-dependent expressions, compared to sentence-level translation and commercial baselines.
1a3763f38e84bf5a43c34df10a381a4449146acc.proposed_method: A comprehensive methodology is proposed to evaluate the capabilities of large language models, specifically GPT-3.5, for literary translation at the paragraph level. Three translation strategies will be implemented: (1) sentence-level translation without context, (2) sentence-level translation with paragraph context, and (3) full paragraph-level translation, all using few-shot prompting with carefully curated demonstration examples for each language pair. The method will utilize a novel dataset of 360 aligned source-target literary paragraphs from recently published novels, spanning 18 language pairs and three target languages (English, Japanese, Polish). Human translators fluent in both source and target languages will be recruited to provide span-level error annotations and comparative preference judgments, using an error taxonomy inspired by Multidimensional Quality Metrics (MQM). Baseline comparisons will be made against Google Translate outputs for the same paragraphs.
1a3763f38e84bf5a43c34df10a381a4449146acc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a dataset of 360 aligned literary paragraphs, extracted from 18 recent novel translations, covering eight source languages and three target languages. For each language pair, 20 paragraphs will be translated using all three GPT-3.5 strategies and Google Translate. Human evaluation will involve 13 professional translators annotating span-level errors (mistranslation, grammar, untranslated, inconsistency, register, format), identifying omissions/additions, and providing pairwise preference judgments for each translation method. Automatic evaluation metrics (COMET, BLEURT, BERTSCORE, COMET-QE) will also be computed, though human evaluation will be prioritized due to the limitations of automatic metrics for literary and document-level translation. Statistical analysis will be performed to compare error rates and preference outcomes across all methods and language pairs.
1a3763f38e84bf5a43c34df10a381a4449146acc.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a rigorous, fine-grained human evaluation framework for document-level literary translation using large language models, addressing a gap in current evaluation methodologies. It leverages a newly curated, publicly released dataset of aligned literary paragraphs across a diverse set of languages, and systematically compares paragraph-level, sentence-level, and commercial translation systems. The approach provides new insights into the discourse-level capabilities and persistent limitations of LLM-based translators, particularly in capturing literary style and context, and sets a new benchmark for future research in document-level machine translation evaluation.

1a3efe3595ca2f31da443e57d1b2dba585dba6b8.title: A Survey on Dataset Distillation: Approaches, Applications and Future Directions
1a3efe3595ca2f31da443e57d1b2dba585dba6b8.research_question: How can the field of dataset distillation be systematically categorized, and what are the key approaches, data modalities, and applications that define its current landscape and future directions?
1a3efe3595ca2f31da443e57d1b2dba585dba6b8.proposed_method: A comprehensive taxonomy of dataset distillation will be developed, organizing the field by approaches (learning frameworks and enhancement methods), data modalities (such as image, audio, text, and graph), and applications (including computationally intensive tasks, privacy, and robustness). The methodology will involve a detailed analysis and categorization of existing dataset distillation techniques, including meta-learning (back-propagation through time, kernel ridge regression), surrogate objectives (parameter matching, distribution matching), and enhancement strategies (parameterization, augmentation, label distillation). Representative methods will be systematically compared, and technical details such as optimization strategies, computational trade-offs, and integration of regularization or privacy mechanisms will be documented. The proposal will also include a review of challenges and open problems, such as computational efficiency, performance scaling, and adaptation to new modalities.
1a3efe3595ca2f31da443e57d1b2dba585dba6b8.experiment_details: The proposed study will survey and analyze a wide range of dataset distillation methods using publicly available benchmarks and datasets, including MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, TinyImageNet, Speech Commands, and various text and graph datasets. Baselines will include traditional coreset selection, random sampling, and state-of-the-art distillation algorithms such as DC, DSA, KIP, FRePo, MTT, and others. Evaluation metrics will cover model accuracy on test sets, generalization across architectures, computational cost, privacy leakage (e.g., resistance to membership inference attacks), and robustness to adversarial or poisoning attacks. The review will systematically document experimental setups, including the number of images per class, augmentation strategies, and privacy mechanisms, to enable fair comparison and reproducibility.
1a3efe3595ca2f31da443e57d1b2dba585dba6b8.novelty_claims: The proposed work introduces the first systematic taxonomy of dataset distillation, providing a holistic categorization of learning frameworks, enhancement methods, data modalities, and applications. It offers a comprehensive comparison of existing approaches, highlights underexplored areas such as text and graph distillation, and identifies key challenges and future research directions. The taxonomy and analysis are intended to guide researchers in understanding the landscape, selecting appropriate methods, and identifying promising avenues for advancing dataset distillation.

1a4a0033fffb3e01315eebd43915bcbc3e1cba23.title: Accelerated Sampling from Masked Diffusion Models via Entropy Bounded Unmasking
1a4a0033fffb3e01315eebd43915bcbc3e1cba23.research_question: How can sampling from masked diffusion models for language and reasoning tasks be made more efficient without sacrificing performance, particularly by adaptively unmasking multiple tokens per step?
1a4a0033fffb3e01315eebd43915bcbc3e1cba23.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that adaptively unmasking multiple tokens per sampling step, based on entropy-bounded criteria that control joint dependence error, can significantly accelerate sampling from masked diffusion models without degrading generation quality.
1a4a0033fffb3e01315eebd43915bcbc3e1cba23.proposed_method: A novel adaptive sampling algorithm, termed Entropy Bounded Sampler (EB-Sampler), will be developed for masked diffusion models. At each sampling step, the method will sort masked tokens according to a local model error proxy (such as entropy or confidence) and then dynamically determine how many tokens to unmask by bounding the cumulative entropy difference within a predefined threshold (gamma). This approach seeks to unmask as many tokens as possible in parallel, provided their joint dependence remains below the set entropy bound, thus minimizing both model error and joint dependence error. The EB-Sampler will be implemented as a drop-in replacement for existing Top-k and greedy samplers, requiring no retraining of the underlying diffusion model. The method will be theoretically analyzed within a general family of adaptive multi-token samplers, with error decomposition into model and joint dependence components to justify the entropy-bounded selection.
1a4a0033fffb3e01315eebd43915bcbc3e1cba23.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard code and math reasoning benchmarks, including HumanEval, MBPP, GSM8K, and MATH, using state-of-the-art masked diffusion models such as LLaDa 8B and Dream 7B. Additional evaluations will be performed on structured logic puzzles, specifically maze navigation and Sudoku, using smaller discrete diffusion models. The EB-Sampler will be compared against Top-k samplers using confidence, entropy, and margin as error proxies. Evaluation metrics will include pass@1 accuracy and average number of function evaluations (NFE) required to generate a complete output, with efficiency measured under both fixed-length and generate_until stopping criteria. Experimental setups will control for temperature and sequence length, and results will be reported as Pareto frontiers of accuracy versus NFE, as well as speed-up factors relative to standard samplers.
1a4a0033fffb3e01315eebd43915bcbc3e1cba23.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces an adaptive, entropy-bounded multi-token unmasking strategy for masked diffusion models, enabling significant acceleration (2-3x speed-up) of sampling without loss of accuracy. Unlike prior approaches, the number of tokens unmasked per step is dynamically determined based on model-predicted entropy, rather than being fixed. The method is theoretically justified via a novel error decomposition and is compatible with existing models without retraining. This approach is the first to provide a practical, theoretically grounded solution for efficient sampling in large-scale masked diffusion models for language and reasoning tasks.

1a5a79b393b3f00eb5a47243ee031ad799d2f641.title: MM-SafetyBench: A Benchmark for Safety Evaluation of Multimodal Large Language Models
1a5a79b393b3f00eb5a47243ee031ad799d2f641.research_question: How can the safety of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) be systematically evaluated and improved, particularly with respect to their vulnerability to image-based manipulations in malicious scenarios?
1a5a79b393b3f00eb5a47243ee031ad799d2f641.hypothesis: MLLMs are susceptible to safety breaches when presented with query-relevant images, and introducing targeted safety prompts can significantly reduce the success rate of such attacks.
1a5a79b393b3f00eb5a47243ee031ad799d2f641.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark, MM-SafetyBench, will be constructed to evaluate the safety of MLLMs against multimodal attacks. The methodology involves generating a large dataset of malicious queries across 13 safety-critical scenarios, extracting key phrases from these queries, and converting them into images using three methods: Stable Diffusion-based image generation, typographic rendering, and a combination of both. Each malicious query will be paired with these images, and the queries will be rephrased to align with the visual content, aiming to provoke unsafe responses from MLLMs. The evaluation protocol will include both attack success rate (ASR) and refusal rate (RR) metrics, and a concise safety prompt will be designed to instruct models to refuse unsafe queries, with its effectiveness systematically tested.
1a5a79b393b3f00eb5a47243ee031ad799d2f641.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 12 state-of-the-art open-source MLLMs, including LLaVA, IDEFICS, InstructBLIP, MiniGPT-4, mPLUG-Owl, Otter, LLaMA-AdapterV2, CogVLM, MiniGPT-5, MiniGPT-V2, Shikra, and Qwen-VL, using zero-shot evaluation. The MM-SafetyBench dataset will comprise 5,040 text-image pairs spanning 13 scenarios such as illegal activity, hate speech, fraud, and professional advice, with both default and tiny versions for scalability. Baselines will include text-only queries and queries with irrelevant images, while attack variants will use query-relevant images generated by the three proposed methods. Evaluation will use the attack success rate (ASR) to quantify how often models generate unsafe responses and the refusal rate (RR) to measure explicit rejection of malicious queries. Both manual and GPT-4-aided evaluations will be employed to ensure reliability of safety assessments.
1a5a79b393b3f00eb5a47243ee031ad799d2f641.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel multimodal safety benchmark specifically targeting the vulnerabilities of MLLMs to image-based attacks, covering a broader range of safety scenarios than existing benchmarks. The method innovatively combines text-to-image generation and typographic techniques to craft query-relevant visual prompts that can bypass current safety mechanisms. The benchmark provides a systematic, large-scale, and scenario-diverse evaluation framework, and the proposed safety prompt offers a simple yet highly effective defense mechanism that does not require model retraining. This work aims to set a new standard for safety evaluation and enhancement in the rapidly evolving field of multimodal language models.

1a638e5752e386612406d0479b7bad94877be8cb.title: Model Merging in LLMs, MLLMs, and Beyond: Methods, Theories, Applications, and Opportunities
1a638e5752e386612406d0479b7bad94877be8cb.research_question: How can model merging techniques be systematically advanced and applied to efficiently integrate knowledge from multiple expert models across diverse machine learning domains, including large language models, multimodal models, and other subfields, without requiring access to original training data or incurring high computational costs?
1a638e5752e386612406d0479b7bad94877be8cb.hypothesis: Advanced model merging methods, when systematically classified and developed, can enable the creation of universal models that retain the capabilities of multiple expert models, reduce storage and computational overhead, and address challenges such as task interference, architectural heterogeneity, and representation bias.
1a638e5752e386612406d0479b7bad94877be8cb.proposed_method: A comprehensive taxonomy of model merging methods will be developed, dividing approaches into pre-merging and during-merging phases. Pre-merging methods will include merger-friendly fine-tuning to disentangle weight spaces, architectural transformation to homogenize model structures, and weight re-basin or alignment to ensure models are in compatible parameter spaces. During-merging methods will encompass basic parameter averaging, weighted merging based on parameter or model importance, subspace-based merging using sparse or low-rank projections, optimization-based merging with data-free objectives to minimize task interference, routing-based dynamic merging conditioned on input samples, and post-calibration techniques to correct representation bias in merged models. Each method will be technically detailed and implemented for empirical evaluation.
1a638e5752e386612406d0479b7bad94877be8cb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of foundation models, including large language models (LLMs), multimodal large language models (MLLMs), and visual generative models, as well as across more than ten machine learning subfields such as continual learning, multi-task learning, federated learning, and adversarial learning. Publicly available model checkpoints from repositories like Huggingface, torchvision, and timm will be utilized. Baselines will include independent expert models, ensemble methods, federated learning, and standard multi-task learning. Evaluation metrics will include task accuracy, knowledge retention, catastrophic forgetting, model storage efficiency, and computational cost. Empirical comparisons will be performed to assess performance gaps, generalization, and robustness of merged models.
1a638e5752e386612406d0479b7bad94877be8cb.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified and exhaustive taxonomy of model merging methods, covering both pre-merging and during-merging strategies, and systematically addresses architectural heterogeneity, parameter alignment, and dynamic inference. It extends model merging applications to a broad set of machine learning domains, including foundation models and specialized subfields, and highlights novel calibration and optimization-based approaches for mitigating knowledge loss and interference. The work also identifies and addresses open challenges such as scalability, theoretical understanding, and trustworthy guarantees, offering a roadmap for future research and cross-disciplinary applications.

1a67d1123d824757fbb22366cdd85421006cb8a1.title: Image Restoration Through Generalized Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Bridge
1a67d1123d824757fbb22366cdd85421006cb8a1.research_question: How can a unified and mathematically principled diffusion bridge model be developed to improve the restoration of high-quality images from low-quality inputs across diverse image restoration tasks, without relying on task-specific prior knowledge or costly iterative approximations?
1a67d1123d824757fbb22366cdd85421006cb8a1.hypothesis: A diffusion bridge model based on the Generalized Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (GOU) process, enhanced with Doob’s h-transform, will enable direct and optimal point-to-point mappings between low-quality and high-quality images, resulting in superior restoration performance across various tasks compared to existing bridge and diffusion models.
1a67d1123d824757fbb22366cdd85421006cb8a1.proposed_method: A novel image restoration framework will be developed by formulating the restoration process as a Generalized Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Bridge (GOUB), leveraging the mean-reverting property of the GOU process. The method will apply Doob’s h-transform to the GOU process, modifying the stochastic differential equation (SDE) to directly connect the high-quality (HQ) and low-quality (LQ) image states, thereby eliminating terminal noise and enabling precise point-to-point mapping. The forward process will use the closed-form solution of the GOU bridge for efficient sampling, while the reverse process will be learned via maximum likelihood estimation, allowing for stable and effective restoration. Additionally, a Mean-ODE variant will be introduced, parameterizing the mean trajectory of the reverse process to better capture pixel-level details and structural information, and trained using an L1 loss for enhanced image quality.
1a67d1123d824757fbb22366cdd85421006cb8a1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three major image restoration tasks: image inpainting (using CelebA-HQ dataset with thin masks), image deraining (using Rain100H dataset), and image super-resolution (using DIV2K dataset for 4× upscaling). The proposed GOUB and Mean-ODE models will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as PromptIR, DDRM, IR-SDE, MPRNet, M3SNet-32, MAXIM, MHNet, and other bridge models (VEB, VPB). Evaluation metrics will include Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity (LPIPS), and Fréchet Inception Distance (FID). The experimental setup will ensure consistent hyperparameters across models, and ablation studies will be performed to analyze the impact of the Mean-ODE variant and different bridge processes.
1a67d1123d824757fbb22366cdd85421006cb8a1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a mathematically unified diffusion bridge model (GOUB) that generalizes and subsumes existing bridge models as special cases, providing a closed-form and optimal solution for image restoration. The use of Doob’s h-transform on the GOU process enables direct elimination of terminal noise and efficient point-to-point mapping, overcoming limitations of prior methods that require task-specific priors or expensive iterative approximations. The Mean-ODE variant further advances the field by enabling superior pixel-level and structural restoration. Empirical results demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across multiple restoration tasks, validating both the theoretical and practical advantages of the approach.

1a6f3fbbbcb60ec742a034bc8d3ad5242a422f4c.title: Fourier Head: Helping Large Language Models Learn Complex Probability Distributions
1a6f3fbbbcb60ec742a034bc8d3ad5242a422f4c.research_question: How can large language models be improved to better model complex, continuous, and multi-modal probability distributions, particularly in non-linguistic domains such as decision making and time series forecasting?
1a6f3fbbbcb60ec742a034bc8d3ad5242a422f4c.hypothesis: Incorporating a neural network layer based on Fourier series as a replacement for the standard linear classification head in large language models will enable the models to better capture the underlying continuous structure of the data, resulting in improved modeling of complex probability distributions and enhanced performance on tasks where output tokens have a natural ordering or continuity.
1a6f3fbbbcb60ec742a034bc8d3ad5242a422f4c.proposed_method: A new neural network layer, termed the Fourier head, will be developed to replace the standard linear classification head in large language models. The Fourier head will input a feature vector and use a linear layer to learn the coefficients of a truncated Fourier series with N frequencies over a fixed interval (e.g., [-1, 1]). The interval will be quantized into m bins corresponding to output tokens, and the learned Fourier probability density function (PDF) will be evaluated at the bin centers to produce a categorical distribution. Regularization on the Fourier coefficients will be applied to control smoothness and prevent overfitting to high-frequency noise. Hyperparameters such as the number of frequencies and binning strategies (including mixed-precision binning) will be explored to optimize performance for different tasks.
1a6f3fbbbcb60ec742a034bc8d3ad5242a422f4c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic experiments will involve learning conditional distributions (e.g., Gaussian, GMM, Beta) using MLPs with different classification heads (linear, Gaussian mixture, and Fourier) and evaluating performance using KL divergence, smoothness, and MSE metrics. Large-scale experiments will be performed in two domains: (1) offline reinforcement learning using the Decision Transformer on Atari games (Seaquest, Bank Heist, Double Dunk, Gravitar) with returns as the main metric, and (2) probabilistic time series forecasting using the Chronos foundation model on a benchmark of 20 unseen datasets, evaluated with MASE, WQL, and smoothness metrics. Baseline comparisons will include standard linear heads and alternative parameterizations, with ablations on model size, dataset size, number of frequencies, and regularization strength.
1a6f3fbbbcb60ec742a034bc8d3ad5242a422f4c.novelty_claims: The proposed Fourier head introduces a principled, modular approach to infusing continuity inductive bias into large language models, enabling them to better model complex, multi-modal, and continuous probability distributions. The method leverages Fourier series as universal function approximators, providing a flexible trade-off between expressivity and smoothness, formalized by a new scaling law. The Fourier head is shown to be easily integrated into existing architectures, outperforming standard linear heads in both synthetic and large-scale real-world tasks, and yielding smoother, higher-quality output distributions. The approach also extends prior work on Fourier-based density modeling to conditional and autoregressive settings relevant for LLMs.

1a71f7b216b710b936da666027014adb83af8e7a.title: LLaVA-OneVision: Easy Visual Task Transfer
1a71f7b216b710b936da666027014adb83af8e7a.research_question: How can a single large multimodal model be designed to achieve strong performance and transfer learning capabilities across diverse visual tasks, including single-image, multi-image, and video scenarios, using open-source components and cost-efficient training strategies?
1a71f7b216b710b936da666027014adb83af8e7a.hypothesis: A unified large multimodal model, trained with carefully curated high-quality instruction data and a flexible visual representation strategy, will enable strong cross-modal transfer and achieve state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of visual tasks spanning images, multi-image sequences, and videos.
1a71f7b216b710b936da666027014adb83af8e7a.proposed_method: A family of large multimodal models will be developed by integrating a strong open-source language model (Qwen-2) with a high-performing vision encoder (SigLIP) via a 2-layer MLP projector. The architecture will support flexible visual input representations using a novel Higher AnyRes strategy with bilinear interpolation, allowing for scalable token allocation across single-image, multi-image, and video scenarios. Training will follow a curriculum learning approach in three stages: (1) aligning visual and language embeddings, (2) injecting high-quality knowledge via synthetic and curated datasets, and (3) instruction tuning on a diverse set of visual tasks. Visual instruction tuning will be performed in two phases: first on a large single-image dataset, then on a mixed dataset of single-image, multi-image, and video samples, enabling emergent cross-scenario capabilities.
1a71f7b216b710b936da666027014adb83af8e7a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a comprehensive suite of benchmarks covering single-image, multi-image, and video tasks. Datasets include COCO, BLIP, CC3M, UReader, ShareGPT4V, Evo-Instruct, and a curated collection of instruction-tuning datasets spanning general QA, OCR, document understanding, math reasoning, and language tasks. Baselines will include state-of-the-art open-source and proprietary models such as GPT-4V, GPT-4o, InternVL, Cambrian, and others. Evaluation metrics will consist of accuracy, reasoning scores, and task-specific metrics as defined by each benchmark, with all models evaluated under standardized, zero-shot, and greedy decoding settings. Multiple model sizes (0.5B, 7B, 72B parameters) will be trained and compared to assess scalability and performance trade-offs.
1a71f7b216b710b936da666027014adb83af8e7a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first open-source large multimodal model family that achieves strong, transferable performance across single-image, multi-image, and video tasks within a single architecture. Key innovations include a flexible Higher AnyRes visual representation strategy for efficient cross-modal token allocation, a cost-effective curriculum learning training recipe, and the demonstration of emergent video and cross-scenario capabilities via task transfer from image-based training. The project also contributes a large, carefully curated multimodal instruction dataset and open-sources all code, models, and data to facilitate further research.

1a80429448d7379ca1157a33a36bd5130257e3e9.title: Jumping Ahead: Improving Reconstruction Fidelity with JumpReLU Sparse Autoencoders
1a80429448d7379ca1157a33a36bd5130257e3e9.research_question: How can the trade-off between sparsity and reconstruction fidelity in sparse autoencoders for language model activations be improved, while maintaining or enhancing the interpretability of the learned features?
1a80429448d7379ca1157a33a36bd5130257e3e9.hypothesis: Introducing a discontinuous JumpReLU activation function, combined with direct L0 sparsity penalties and principled use of straight-through estimators for gradient estimation, will enable sparse autoencoders to achieve higher reconstruction fidelity at a given sparsity level without sacrificing interpretability, compared to existing methods such as Gated and TopK sparse autoencoders.
1a80429448d7379ca1157a33a36bd5130257e3e9.proposed_method: A novel sparse autoencoder architecture, termed JumpReLU SAE, will be developed by replacing the standard ReLU activation in the encoder with a JumpReLU activation function. This function applies a learnable threshold to pre-activations, zeroing out values below the threshold and passing through values above it, thus providing independent control over feature activation and magnitude estimation. The training objective will directly penalize the L0 norm of the feature activations, encouraging true sparsity without the shrinkage or reparameterization issues of L1-based penalties. To enable gradient-based optimization despite the discontinuities in the JumpReLU and L0 penalty, straight-through estimators (STEs) will be analytically derived and applied to provide meaningful gradient signals for the threshold parameters. The method will be implemented efficiently, requiring only elementwise operations and avoiding computationally expensive procedures such as partial sorting.
1a80429448d7379ca1157a33a36bd5130257e3e9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on activations from the Gemma 2 9B language model, specifically targeting residual stream, MLP output, and attention output activations at multiple layers (e.g., layers 9, 20, and 31). Multiple 131k-width autoencoders of each type (JumpReLU, Gated, TopK) will be trained over 8 billion tokens, with sparsity controlled via the L0 penalty coefficient or TopK parameter. Baselines will include Gated SAEs (with both original and reparameterization-invariant L1 penalties) and TopK SAEs (with auxiliary loss to reduce dead features). Evaluation metrics will include mean L0-norm (sparsity), delta LM loss (increase in cross-entropy when SAE reconstructions are spliced into the LM), fraction of variance unexplained, and both manual and automated interpretability assessments. Human raters will evaluate feature monosemanticity, and language model-based automated metrics will assess the correlation between simulated and ground truth feature activations. Feature activation frequency and the proportion of dead features will also be analyzed.
1a80429448d7379ca1157a33a36bd5130257e3e9.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the use of a discontinuous JumpReLU activation function in sparse autoencoders for language model activations, enabling independent thresholding for feature activation. Direct optimization of L0 sparsity, rather than L1 proxies, is made feasible through analytically derived straight-through estimators, allowing efficient and principled gradient-based training. The method claims to achieve state-of-the-art reconstruction fidelity at a given sparsity level, while maintaining or improving interpretability relative to existing Gated and TopK SAE methods. Additionally, the approach is computationally efficient, requiring only elementwise operations and no auxiliary loss terms or resampling procedures.

1a9b8c545ba9a6779f202e04639c2d67e6d34f63.title: Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models
1a9b8c545ba9a6779f202e04639c2d67e6d34f63.research_question: How can the instruction-following abilities of large language models be evaluated in a standardized, objective, and reproducible manner using prompts that minimize subjectivity and ambiguity?
1a9b8c545ba9a6779f202e04639c2d67e6d34f63.hypothesis: A benchmark based on verifiable, objectively checkable instructions enables more reliable, scalable, and unbiased evaluation of large language models' instruction-following capabilities compared to human or LLM-based evaluators.
1a9b8c545ba9a6779f202e04639c2d67e6d34f63.proposed_method: A new evaluation framework will be developed that centers on a set of 'verifiable instructions'—atomic directives that can be checked for compliance using deterministic, interpretable programs. A comprehensive list of 25 verifiable instruction types will be curated, covering categories such as keyword inclusion, word/letter frequency, language constraints, formatting, and structural requirements. Around 500 prompts will be synthesized, each embedding one or more verifiable instructions, with prompt diversity ensured through few-shot prompting, rephrasing, and manual curation to avoid conflicts and increase coverage. For each prompt, large language models will generate responses, and automated scripts will verify adherence to each instruction using both strict and loose criteria, the latter incorporating response transformations to account for common output variations.
1a9b8c545ba9a6779f202e04639c2d67e6d34f63.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on widely used large language models, such as GPT-4 and PaLM 2 Small, using the constructed set of 541 prompts. Each model's responses will be collected via API calls, and evaluated for instruction-following accuracy at both the prompt and instruction levels, using both strict (exact match) and loose (with output normalization) criteria. Baseline comparisons will be established between the models, and performance will be analyzed by instruction category to identify strengths and weaknesses. Evaluation metrics will include prompt-level and instruction-level strict and loose accuracy, and detailed results will be reported per instruction type.
1a9b8c545ba9a6779f202e04639c2d67e6d34f63.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces a fully automatic, objective, and reproducible evaluation methodology for instruction-following in LLMs, focusing exclusively on verifiable instructions that can be programmatically checked. The approach eliminates human subjectivity and LLM-based evaluator bias, and provides granular insights into which types of instructions models struggle with. The framework is designed to be easily extensible to new instruction types and multi-modal tasks, and the code and data will be released for community use and further development.

1aa206426a20b0b549cda5068b90b8da353b3434.title: Repository-Level Prompt Generation for Large Language Models of Code
1aa206426a20b0b549cda5068b90b8da353b3434.research_question: How can repository-level context be leveraged to automatically generate effective prompts for large language models of code, particularly in scenarios with only black-box access to the LLM? What is the impact of incorporating structured, cross-file context on code autocompletion performance compared to standard file-level prompting?
1aa206426a20b0b549cda5068b90b8da353b3434.hypothesis: Automatically generating prompts that incorporate structured, repository-level context—such as information from imports, parent classes, sibling files, and other relevant files—will significantly improve the performance of large language models on code autocompletion tasks, even when only black-box access to the LLM is available.
1aa206426a20b0b549cda5068b90b8da353b3434.proposed_method: A framework, Repo-Level Prompt Generator (RLPG), will be developed to generate example-specific prompts for code completion tasks. The method will define a set of discrete prompt proposals, each specifying a combination of prompt source (e.g., current file, parent class, imports, sibling files, similar name files) and prompt context type (e.g., method names, identifiers, field declarations, method bodies). For each code completion instance (target hole), a neural Prompt Proposal Classifier (PPC) will be trained to select the most effective prompt proposal based on the code context and repository structure. The selected prompt proposal's context will be dynamically combined with the default file-local context to form the final prompt. The approach will operate without access to LLM weights, making it suitable for black-box LLM APIs.
1aa206426a20b0b549cda5068b90b8da353b3434.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a single-line code autocompletion task using Java repositories scraped from the Google Code archives, with careful deduplication and train/validation/test splits at the repository level. The primary evaluation metric will be exact match accuracy (success rate) of the predicted code segment, with additional evaluation using normalized character-level edit distance. Baselines will include standard Codex prompting, random and BM25-based context retrieval, identifier usage windows, and fixed prompt proposals. The RLPG framework will be compared to these baselines using the OpenAI Codex API (code-davinci-001 and code-cushman-001) in a black-box setting, with prompt lengths and completion lengths controlled. Ablation studies will assess the impact of different prompt sources, context types, and the number of prompt attempts.
1aa206426a20b0b549cda5068b90b8da353b3434.novelty_claims: The proposed framework enables automatic, example-specific prompt generation for code LLMs using repository-level context, without requiring access to model weights. It introduces a comprehensive taxonomy of prompt proposals that systematically incorporate cross-file and structural information from code repositories. The approach is the first to address prompt generation for code LLMs in a black-box setting, demonstrating substantial improvements over standard prompting and retrieval-based baselines. The method provides a flexible mechanism for integrating domain and project-specific knowledge into LLM prompting, and is extensible to new prompt proposals and programming languages.

1ad85b1a902cd37c855dbedf5bd17c536628b611.title: Optimal Goal-Reaching Reinforcement Learning via Quasimetric Learning
1ad85b1a902cd37c855dbedf5bd17c536628b611.research_question: How can reinforcement learning agents be enabled to efficiently and accurately learn optimal goal-reaching value functions in multi-goal environments, leveraging the inherent geometric structure of value functions?
1ad85b1a902cd37c855dbedf5bd17c536628b611.hypothesis: Constraining the value function to the space of quasimetrics and directly optimizing for quasimetric structure will enable more accurate and sample-efficient learning of optimal goal-reaching value functions compared to unconstrained or contrastive approaches.
