1ad85b1a902cd37c855dbedf5bd17c536628b611.proposed_method: A novel reinforcement learning framework is developed that parameterizes the goal-conditioned value function as a quasimetric, leveraging recent advances in differentiable quasimetric models. The method, termed Quasimetric Reinforcement Learning (QRL), formulates the learning objective as a constrained maximization: maximizing the quasimetric distance between state-goal pairs while ensuring local distances do not exceed observed transition costs, and enforcing the triangle inequality globally. The quasimetric model is implemented using Interval Quasimetric Embeddings (IQE), which consist of a deep encoder mapping states to a latent space and a differentiable quasimetric head. Optimization is performed via dual gradient descent, jointly updating model parameters and Lagrange multipliers to satisfy the cost constraints. The approach is extended to learn Q-functions and policies by incorporating a learned latent transition model and optimizing a transition loss that ensures consistency between predicted and actual next-state latents under the quasimetric.
1ad85b1a902cd37c855dbedf5bd17c536628b611.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on discretized MountainCar and maze2d environments, as well as FetchReach, FetchPush, and FetchSlide benchmarks with both state-based and image-based observations. Offline datasets are collected using random or hand-coded policies, and online learning is evaluated in continuous control settings. Baselines include standard Q-Learning, Q-Learning with quasimetric models, Contrastive RL, Conservative Q-Learning (CQL), Model Standard-deviation Gradients (MSG), Diffuser trajectory models, and planning methods such as MPPI. Evaluation metrics include normalized episode return, success rate, and qualitative analysis of learned value function structures. The experimental setup includes ablations on symmetry, optimality, and objective formulation, and comparisons are made in both single-goal and multi-goal settings.
1ad85b1a902cd37c855dbedf5bd17c536628b611.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a principled framework for learning optimal goal-reaching value functions by directly exploiting the quasimetric structure inherent in multi-goal RL. Unlike prior approaches, QRL enforces both local cost consistency and global triangle inequality, providing strong theoretical recovery guarantees and provable optimality. The method demonstrates significant improvements in sample efficiency, accuracy, and generalization across diverse environments and observation modalities. Additionally, QRL enables seamless integration with planning and trajectory modeling methods, further enhancing their performance. This approach establishes a new direction for geometric RL by unifying value function learning with quasimetric modeling.

1af0ad4f5c1b44042fe9eac5aef68507a9cffe2a.title: OVTrack: Open-Vocabulary Multiple Object Tracking
1af0ad4f5c1b44042fe9eac5aef68507a9cffe2a.research_question: How can multiple object tracking be extended to handle arbitrary, open-vocabulary object categories, including those not seen during training, in a data-efficient manner while maintaining high tracking, classification, and association accuracy?
1af0ad4f5c1b44042fe9eac5aef68507a9cffe2a.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging vision-language models for knowledge distillation, combined with a novel data hallucination strategy using generative models, will enable a multiple object tracker to generalize to open-vocabulary settings and track arbitrary object classes with high accuracy, even when trained only on static images.
1af0ad4f5c1b44042fe9eac5aef68507a9cffe2a.proposed_method: A new open-vocabulary multiple object tracking framework, OVTrack, will be developed. The method decomposes tracking into localization, classification, and association modules. Localization will be performed using a class-agnostic Faster R-CNN, enabling generalization to unseen object categories. For classification, the standard classifier will be replaced with an embedding head supervised via knowledge distillation from a large-scale vision-language model (CLIP), aligning region-of-interest features with both image and text embeddings for open-vocabulary recognition. Association will rely on robust appearance features learned through contrastive instance similarity objectives, using appearance embeddings for track association. To address the scarcity of annotated video data, a data hallucination strategy based on denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) will be employed, generating positive and negative training samples and simulating realistic appearance variations from static images.
1af0ad4f5c1b44042fe9eac5aef68507a9cffe2a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the TAO benchmark, a large-scale, large-vocabulary multiple object tracking dataset, with a split into base (seen) and novel (unseen) classes as defined by LVIS taxonomy. The tracker will be trained solely on static images from LVIS, with hallucinated counterparts generated per image. Baseline comparisons will include both closed-set trackers (e.g., TETer, QDTrack) and open-vocabulary baselines (e.g., DeepSORT and Tracktor++ with ViLD or RegionCLIP detectors). Evaluation metrics will include TETA (tracking-every-thing accuracy), which separately assesses localization, association, and classification, as well as TrackmAP for overall tracking performance. Ablation studies will assess the contributions of CLIP-based distillation and the data hallucination strategy, and additional experiments will evaluate zero-shot transfer to datasets such as BDD100K.
1af0ad4f5c1b44042fe9eac5aef68507a9cffe2a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first open-vocabulary multi-object tracker capable of tracking arbitrary object classes, including those unseen during training, by leveraging vision-language model distillation for both classification and association. A novel data hallucination strategy using DDPMs is proposed to generate realistic training samples from static images, addressing the data scarcity problem in open-vocabulary tracking. The method enables data-efficient training without requiring video annotations and achieves state-of-the-art results on challenging large-vocabulary tracking benchmarks, demonstrating strong generalization to novel categories.

1b2355c3c674b26a977768a91a164384ad51bbb1.title: ImageReward: Learning and Evaluating Human Preferences for Text-to-Image Generation
1b2355c3c674b26a977768a91a164384ad51bbb1.research_question: How can human preferences be effectively modeled and integrated into the training and evaluation of text-to-image generative models to improve alignment with human values and preferences?
1b2355c3c674b26a977768a91a164384ad51bbb1.hypothesis: A reward model trained on systematically collected and annotated human preference data can more accurately capture human judgments for text-to-image synthesis than existing automatic metrics, and direct optimization of diffusion models using this reward feedback will yield generations that are more aligned with human preferences.
1b2355c3c674b26a977768a91a164384ad51bbb1.proposed_method: A comprehensive annotation pipeline will be developed to collect large-scale, high-quality human preference data for text-to-image pairs. This pipeline will include prompt selection using a graph-based algorithm for diversity, expert annotation involving rating and ranking images on alignment, fidelity, and harmlessness, and rigorous quality control. A reward model, ImageReward, will be trained using these annotations by formulating the problem as preference learning, leveraging a BLIP-based backbone with cross-attention and an MLP head to output scalar preference scores. To address overfitting, a portion of the backbone will be frozen and hyperparameters will be optimized via grid search. Building on this, a direct fine-tuning algorithm, Reward Feedback Learning (ReFL), will be developed to optimize latent diffusion models by backpropagating gradients from ImageReward scores at randomly selected late denoising steps, with regularization from the pre-training loss and careful loss reweighting to stabilize training.
1b2355c3c674b26a977768a91a164384ad51bbb1.experiment_details: Experiments will use a dataset of 137k expert-annotated image comparisons across 8,878 prompts, with a test set of 466 prompts for model evaluation. Baselines will include CLIP score, Aesthetic score, and BLIP score, with evaluation metrics such as preference accuracy, recall, and filter rates, as well as human win rates in image selection tasks. For model improvement, Stable Diffusion v1.4 will be fine-tuned using ReFL and compared against methods such as dataset filtering, reward-weighted loss, and RAFT, using both real user prompts from DiffusionDB and challenging prompts from MTBench. Evaluations will include both automatic metrics and human rankings, with experiments conducted on high-performance GPUs and using consistent training settings across methods for fair comparison.
1b2355c3c674b26a977768a91a164384ad51bbb1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first general-purpose human preference reward model for text-to-image generation, trained on a large-scale, systematically annotated dataset. The annotation pipeline is specifically designed to address the unique challenges of text-to-image preference collection, ensuring high-quality and diverse data. ImageReward is claimed to outperform existing metrics in aligning with human judgment and distinguishing image quality. The ReFL algorithm is the first to provide direct gradient-based optimization of diffusion models using reward feedback from a human preference model, offering more effective and stable improvement over prior indirect methods such as data filtering and loss reweighting. The combined system enables both improved automatic evaluation and generation of images more closely aligned with human values.

1b312cbe72d8790a9db613e0dce6091da1a6d778.title: TopoTune : A Framework for Generalized Combinatorial Complex Neural Networks
1b312cbe72d8790a9db613e0dce6091da1a6d778.research_question: How can a principled, flexible, and standardized framework be developed to generalize neural network architectures for modeling higher-order interactions in complex systems beyond the limitations of traditional graph neural networks?
1b312cbe72d8790a9db613e0dce6091da1a6d778.hypothesis: Generalized Combinatorial Complex Neural Networks (GCCNs), constructed via a systematic graph-based expansion and equipped with flexible neighborhood and aggregation mechanisms, will match or outperform existing combinatorial complex neural networks (CCNNs) and graph neural networks (GNNs) in modeling higher-order interactions, while reducing model complexity and increasing accessibility.
1b312cbe72d8790a9db613e0dce6091da1a6d778.proposed_method: A novel methodology will be developed to systematically generalize any neural network architecture to its topological deep learning (TDL) counterpart by expanding combinatorial complexes into ensembles of strictly augmented Hasse graphs, each corresponding to a specific neighborhood function. For each neighborhood, a base neural architecture (such as a GNN, Transformer, or MLP) will be applied independently to the corresponding graph, and the outputs will be aggregated rank-wise and updated using learnable functions. The framework will allow for per-rank neighborhoods, enabling fine-grained control over which cells (nodes, edges, faces, etc.) communicate, and will support arbitrary neighborhood message functions, not limited to message-passing. The resulting Generalized Combinatorial Complex Neural Networks (GCCNs) will be implemented in a lightweight, modular software package (TopoTune) that integrates with existing TDL benchmarking tools.
1b312cbe72d8790a9db613e0dce6091da1a6d778.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of benchmark datasets spanning graph-level and node-level tasks, including MUTAG, PROTEINS, NCI1, NCI09, ZINC, Cora, Citeseer, and PubMed. Datasets will be lifted to higher-order topological domains (simplicial and cellular complexes) using standardized procedures. GCCNs will be instantiated with various neighborhood structures (including both regular and per-rank neighborhoods) and base architectures (GCN, GAT, GIN, GraphSAGE, Transformer), imported from established libraries. Baselines will include top-performing CCNNs and GNNs as reported in standardized benchmarks (TopoBench). Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy for classification tasks and mean absolute error (MAE) for regression tasks, with model size and parameter efficiency also reported. Experiments will be run with multiple random seeds, and training configurations will be harmonized to ensure fair comparison.
1b312cbe72d8790a9db613e0dce6091da1a6d778.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the first method to systematically generalize any neural network to its topological counterpart with minimal adaptation, enabling the generation of a broad class of TDL architectures (GCCNs) that formally generalize and subsume CCNNs. The methodology supports per-rank and arbitrary neighborhood functions, allowing unprecedented flexibility and expressivity. The accompanying software, TopoTune, is the first lightweight, modular tool for defining, building, and training GCCNs, fully integrated with standardized TDL benchmarking infrastructure. The approach enables controlled benchmarking across architectures, datasets, and topological domains, and demonstrates that GCCNs can outperform or match existing CCNNs with reduced model complexity, thereby accelerating and democratizing research and application in topological deep learning.

1b3a6efc7c68e8a2b350b4d07cdb50b6a48c6e3b.title: Occ3D: A Large-Scale 3D Occupancy Prediction Benchmark for Autonomous Driving
1b3a6efc7c68e8a2b350b4d07cdb50b6a48c6e3b.research_question: How can large-scale, high-quality benchmarks and advanced models be developed to improve 3D occupancy prediction for autonomous driving, enabling detailed geometric and semantic scene understanding, including out-of-vocabulary objects, from multi-view camera inputs?
1b3a6efc7c68e8a2b350b4d07cdb50b6a48c6e3b.hypothesis: A rigorously constructed 3D occupancy benchmark, coupled with a transformer-based coarse-to-fine occupancy prediction network, will enable more accurate and detailed 3D scene understanding, outperforming existing methods in both geometric fidelity and semantic coverage, particularly for general and irregularly shaped objects.
1b3a6efc7c68e8a2b350b4d07cdb50b6a48c6e3b.proposed_method: A comprehensive label generation pipeline will be developed to produce dense, visibility-aware 3D occupancy annotations from multi-view camera and LiDAR data. The pipeline consists of three main stages: voxel densification (including multi-frame aggregation, KNN-based label assignment, and mesh reconstruction), occlusion reasoning (using ray-casting from both LiDAR and camera perspectives to determine voxel visibility and occupancy state), and image-guided voxel refinement (leveraging 2D semantic segmentation masks to correct misaligned or noisy voxels). Building on these annotations, a transformer-based Coarse-to-Fine Occupancy (CTF-Occ) network will be designed. This model extracts 2D features from multi-view images, aggregates them into 3D voxel space via cross-attention, and employs a pyramid voxel encoder with incremental token selection and spatial cross-attention to progressively refine voxel features. An implicit occupancy decoder will be used to produce arbitrary-resolution semantic occupancy outputs.
1b3a6efc7c68e8a2b350b4d07cdb50b6a48c6e3b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two newly constructed benchmarks, Occ3D-Waymo and Occ3D-nuScenes, derived from the Waymo Open Dataset and nuScenes, respectively. Each benchmark provides surround-view images, high-resolution voxel grids, and semantic labels, including a general object (GO) class for out-of-vocabulary objects. Baseline methods such as MonoScene, TPVFormer, BEVDet, OccFormer, and BEVFormer will be re-implemented and evaluated for comparison. Evaluation metrics include Intersection-over-Union (IoU) and mean IoU (mIoU), computed only on observed voxels as determined by both LiDAR and camera visibility. The experimental setup will feature ablation studies on key components such as incremental token selection and OHEM loss, and will compare camera-only, LiDAR-only, and fusion-based approaches. Hyperparameters, voxel sizes, and model architectures will be detailed for reproducibility.
1b3a6efc7c68e8a2b350b4d07cdb50b6a48c6e3b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first large-scale 3D occupancy prediction benchmarks with surround-view images, high-resolution voxel grids, and explicit labeling of general objects. The label generation pipeline addresses sparsity, occlusion, and 3D-2D misalignment through a validated, multi-stage process. The CTF-Occ network pioneers a coarse-to-fine transformer-based approach with incremental token selection and spatial cross-attention, enabling efficient and detailed 3D occupancy prediction. The proposed benchmarks and model are expected to set new standards for 3D scene understanding in autonomous driving, particularly in handling irregular and out-of-vocabulary objects.

1b3f1fc36ef84e90e837df474121f5d67afd13d9.title: Transformers, parallel computation, and logarithmic depth
1b3f1fc36ef84e90e837df474121f5d67afd13d9.research_question: What are the fundamental computational capabilities and limitations of transformers with logarithmic depth, particularly in comparison to other neural sequence models and parallel computation frameworks, and how does parallelism distinguish transformers in solving algorithmic tasks?
1b3f1fc36ef84e90e837df474121f5d67afd13d9.hypothesis: Transformers with logarithmic depth can efficiently simulate and be simulated by a constant number of rounds of Massively Parallel Computation (MPC), enabling them to solve certain computational tasks more efficiently than other neural sequence models and sub-quadratic transformer approximations.
1b3f1fc36ef84e90e837df474121f5d67afd13d9.proposed_method: A formal connection will be established between the transformer architecture and the Massively Parallel Computation (MPC) model by constructing bidirectional simulations: (1) any R-round MPC protocol will be simulated by a transformer of depth O(R), and (2) any depth-L transformer will be simulated by an O(L)-round MPC protocol. The methodology involves designing transformer layers to mimic the communication and computation rounds of MPC, including the routing and aggregation of messages using self-attention mechanisms. Theoretical constructions will be provided for both general graph problems and specific sequential tasks, such as the k-hop induction heads task, with proofs of optimality and conditional lower bounds based on established conjectures in distributed computing. Empirical studies will be conducted to verify whether transformers trained on synthetic tasks exhibit the predicted depth-efficiency and to analyze the interpretability of learned models.
1b3f1fc36ef84e90e837df474121f5d67afd13d9.experiment_details: Experiments will focus on the k-hop induction heads task, where transformers of varying depths and parameter counts (ranging from 500K to 5M) are trained to solve the task for different values of k, using context lengths of N=100 and an alphabet size of 4. Training will be performed in a multi-task setting with auto-regressive prediction, and models will be evaluated on token-wise classification error across a range of k values. Baselines will include recurrent neural networks (RNNs), state-space models (such as Mamba), graph neural networks (GNNs), and transformers with sub-quadratic attention mechanisms (e.g., Performer, Longformer). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, depth/width trade-offs, and computational efficiency. Additional analysis will be performed on attention patterns and model interpretability to compare learned solutions with theoretical constructions.
1b3f1fc36ef84e90e837df474121f5d67afd13d9.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a rigorous, bidirectional simulation between transformers and the MPC model, establishing that logarithmic-depth transformers can efficiently solve a broad class of parallelizable algorithmic tasks, including some that are provably hard for other neural architectures and sub-quadratic transformer approximations. It provides tight upper and lower bounds on transformer depth for key problems, conditional on well-known conjectures in distributed computing. The k-hop induction heads task is proposed as a new synthetic benchmark to empirically and theoretically separate the representational power of transformers from other models. The work claims to identify parallelism as a fundamental property distinguishing transformers and to provide the first detailed characterization of the algorithmic tasks that benefit exponentially from transformer depth.

1b50041bc6cc3b517b1de0b9d5c76a67f8ae2fe7.title: Facilitating Multi-turn Function Calling for LLMs via Compositional Instruction Tuning
1b50041bc6cc3b517b1de0b9d5c76a67f8ae2fe7.research_question: How can large language models be effectively aligned and instruction-tuned to perform multi-turn function calling, enabling them to plan, decompose, and execute compositional real-world tasks that require multiple sequential or parallel function calls?
1b50041bc6cc3b517b1de0b9d5c76a67f8ae2fe7.hypothesis: Synthetic compositional instruction tuning data, generated through a structured bottom-up and top-down pipeline, can significantly enhance the multi-turn function calling abilities of large language models, enabling improved planning and execution of complex, real-world queries.
1b50041bc6cc3b517b1de0b9d5c76a67f8ae2fe7.proposed_method: A novel data generation pipeline, termed BUTTON (Bottom-Up Then Top-dOwN), will be developed to create high-quality synthetic instruction tuning data for multi-turn function calling. The bottom-up phase involves extracting real-world scenarios, constructing atomic tasks that are simple and solvable in one step, and composing these into more complex tasks using heuristic strategies such as sequential and parallel-then-sequential composition. For each compositional task, corresponding function definitions are generated with attention to generality, descriptiveness, and consistency. The top-down phase simulates multi-turn interaction trajectories in a multi-agent environment, where user, assistant, and tool agents (all simulated by LLMs with curated prompts) interact to solve the compositional tasks using the generated functions. These interaction trajectories, along with function definitions, are formatted into instruction tuning data suitable for supervised fine-tuning of LLMs.
1b50041bc6cc3b517b1de0b9d5c76a67f8ae2fe7.experiment_details: Experiments will involve fine-tuning multiple open-source LLMs (e.g., Llama3-8B/70B, Qwen2-7B/72B) using the generated BUTTONInstruct dataset, which contains 8,000 multi-turn function calling data points. Evaluation will be conducted on established multi-turn function calling benchmarks, including GTA (General Tool Agents) and Tool-Query, which feature real-world tasks requiring sequential and parallel tool use. Baselines will include both API-based LLMs (e.g., GPT-4o, GPT-4-Turbo, GPT-3.5-Turbo) and original instruction-tuned versions of the open-source models. Metrics will cover instruction accuracy, tool selection, argument accuracy, summary accuracy, F1 scores for different task categories, grounding accuracy, process rate, and final answer success rate. Ablation studies will assess the necessity of the bottom-up and top-down procedures, and data scaling experiments will evaluate the impact of dataset size.
1b50041bc6cc3b517b1de0b9d5c76a67f8ae2fe7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a structured, two-phase synthetic data generation pipeline specifically tailored for multi-turn function calling, addressing the lack of compositional, multi-turn datasets for LLM alignment. The method ensures task compositionality, function compatibility, and high-quality multi-turn trajectories through a combination of atomic task decomposition and multi-agent simulation. Unlike prior works that focus on single-turn function calling or rely on existing APIs, this proposal generates tasks and functions in a function-agnostic, bottom-up manner, followed by realistic simulation of multi-turn interactions. The resulting dataset and methodology are expected to significantly improve LLMs' planning and execution abilities in complex, real-world function calling scenarios.

1b5db3170c195508ff24fee8eda0d4987e806f0b.title: EAGLE: Speculative Sampling Requires Rethinking Feature Uncertainty
1b5db3170c195508ff24fee8eda0d4987e806f0b.research_question: How can speculative sampling for large language model (LLM) inference be accelerated while maintaining the output text distribution, and what are the limitations of current feature-level autoregression approaches in this context?
1b5db3170c195508ff24fee8eda0d4987e806f0b.hypothesis: Autoregression at the feature (second-to-top-layer) level, when combined with a token sequence advanced by one time step, can significantly reduce uncertainty in speculative sampling, enabling more accurate and efficient draft generation and verification, thus accelerating LLM inference without altering the output distribution.
1b5db3170c195508ff24fee8eda0d4987e806f0b.proposed_method: A new speculative sampling framework, EAGLE (Extrapolation Algorithm for Greater Language-model Efficiency), will be developed to accelerate LLM inference. The method will perform draft generation autoregressively at the feature (second-to-top-layer) level, rather than at the token level, leveraging the regularity of feature sequences. To address the inherent uncertainty in feature-level autoregression, the draft model will incorporate a token sequence advanced by one time step as an additional input, allowing the model to condition on actual sampling outcomes. The draft model will consist of an embedding layer, a lightweight autoregression head (composed of a fully connected layer and a transformer decoder layer), and will reuse the LM head of the target LLM for token prediction. Training will use a combination of regression (SmoothL1) and classification (cross-entropy) losses, and data augmentation will be applied by injecting noise into feature representations. The verification phase will employ tree-structured attention to validate multiple tokens per forward pass, ensuring the output distribution matches that of the original LLM.
1b5db3170c195508ff24fee8eda0d4987e806f0b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of LLMs, including Vicuna (7B, 13B, 33B), LLaMA2-Chat (7B, 13B, 70B), and Mixtral 8x7B Instruct, across tasks such as dialogue (MT-bench), code generation (HumanEval), mathematical reasoning (GSM8K), and instruction following (Alpaca). Baselines will include speculative sampling with small draft models, Lookahead, Medusa, and DistillSpec, with all methods compared under both greedy (temperature=0) and non-greedy (temperature=1) decoding. Evaluation metrics will focus on walltime speedup ratio, average acceptance length (number of tokens accepted per forward pass), and acceptance rate (accuracy of draft tokens). All models will be tested in zero-shot/few-shot settings, using fixed weights trained on the ShareGPT dataset, and no fine-tuning of the backbone LLMs will be performed. Additional ablation studies will examine the impact of tree attention, input modalities for the draft model, and training data sources. Throughput and memory usage will also be measured for different batch sizes and hardware configurations.
1b5db3170c195508ff24fee8eda0d4987e806f0b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel feature-level speculative sampling framework that directly addresses the uncertainty in feature autoregression by conditioning on advanced token sequences. EAGLE requires only a lightweight plug-in (single transformer decoder layer) and does not require fine-tuning or modification of the original LLM, ensuring theoretical preservation of the output distribution for both greedy and non-greedy settings. The method achieves higher draft accuracy and acceptance rates than prior feature-based speculative sampling methods, and demonstrates robust, generalizable acceleration across multiple LLM architectures and tasks. EAGLE is also compatible with other acceleration techniques such as quantization and compilation, offering further reductions in inference latency and operational cost.

1b6341b05471bb961b4e76467444d7b70c66bbb5.title: Revisiting the Minimalist Approach to Offline Reinforcement Learning
1b6341b05471bb961b4e76467444d7b70c66bbb5.research_question: To what extent can incorporating recent minor design and implementation choices improve the performance of minimalist offline reinforcement learning algorithms across a diverse set of tasks and domains?
1b6341b05471bb961b4e76467444d7b70c66bbb5.hypothesis: Integrating key design choices such as deeper networks, LayerNorm, larger batch sizes, decoupled actor and critic penalization, and adjusted discount factors into a minimalist offline RL algorithm will yield significant performance improvements over established baselines, achieving or surpassing state-of-the-art results in both offline and offline-to-online settings.
1b6341b05471bb961b4e76467444d7b70c66bbb5.proposed_method: A new offline reinforcement learning algorithm, ReBRAC, will be developed by systematically integrating several recent design choices into the TD3+BC baseline. The method will employ deeper neural networks with three hidden layers for both actor and critic, and LayerNorm will be applied between each layer of the critic network to improve convergence and prevent value extrapolation. Larger batch sizes (e.g., 1024 samples) will be used to accelerate training, and the learning rate will be scaled accordingly. The actor and critic regularization penalties will be decoupled, allowing independent tuning of their respective coefficients, and Mean Squared Error (MSE) will be used as the divergence function for both. The discount factor will be increased (e.g., from 0.99 to 0.999) for tasks with sparse rewards, such as AntMaze, to better propagate training signals. The method will include ablation studies to isolate the impact of each modification.
1b6341b05471bb961b4e76467444d7b70c66bbb5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 51 datasets spanning both proprioceptive and visual state spaces using the D4RL and V-D4RL benchmarks, covering Gym-MuJoCo, AntMaze, Adroit, and image-based tasks. The proposed method will be compared against ensemble-free baselines such as TD3+BC, IQL, CQL, and SAC-RND, as well as ensemble-based methods where appropriate. Evaluation metrics will include normalized scores, cumulative regret for offline-to-online transitions, and Expected Online Performance (EOP) under varying policy selection budgets. Hyperparameters will be tuned over multiple random seeds for fair comparison, and extensive ablation studies will be performed to assess the contribution of each design choice. Sensitivity analyses will be conducted on regularization parameters and network depth.
1b6341b05471bb961b4e76467444d7b70c66bbb5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach systematically distills and integrates a set of impactful, yet often overlooked, design and implementation choices into a minimalist offline RL algorithm, demonstrating that such modifications can yield state-of-the-art performance among ensemble-free methods. The work provides a comprehensive ablation and sensitivity analysis at scale, clarifying the individual and combined effects of each design choice. The resulting algorithm offers a strong, reproducible baseline for offline and offline-to-online RL, highlighting the importance of non-algorithmic factors in advancing the field.

1b6b5db09381de42cf09ae8c7ea5183c2600ab78.title: Frame In-N-Out: Unbounded Controllable Image-to-Video Generation
1b6b5db09381de42cf09ae8c7ea5183c2600ab78.research_question: Can unbounded, controllable image-to-video generation be achieved such that objects can be made to enter or exit the visible scene in a temporally coherent and identity-preserving manner, with explicit user control over motion trajectories and object identities?
1b6b5db09381de42cf09ae8c7ea5183c2600ab78.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a unified video Diffusion Transformer architecture, conditioned on first-frame images, text prompts, motion trajectories, identity references, and an unbounded canvas region, can generate videos where objects can plausibly enter or leave the scene, surpassing existing methods in controllability, temporal coherence, and fidelity.
1b6b5db09381de42cf09ae8c7ea5183c2600ab78.proposed_method: A novel video Diffusion Transformer framework will be developed that unifies multiple conditioning signals: a first-frame image, user-specified motion trajectories, optional identity reference images, text prompts, and an unbounded canvas region extending beyond the initial frame. The architecture will encode these conditions using a shared VAE and concatenate them at both channel and frame levels, leveraging flexible position embeddings to support arbitrary canvas sizes. Motion trajectories will be represented as pixel-aligned images with semantic color coding, and the model will be trained with a two-stage process: first on motion control, then jointly on Frame In and Frame Out scenarios with unbounded canvas conditioning. A full-field loss will be used to supervise the entire canvas, and identity reference signals will be integrated via frame-wise concatenation, with random augmentation for robustness.
1b6b5db09381de42cf09ae8c7ea5183c2600ab78.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a curated dataset combining OpenVid-1M, VidGen-1M, and a subset of Webvid-10M, with additional filtering and annotation to create dedicated Frame In and Frame Out benchmarks. The evaluation will use metrics such as FID, FVD, LPIPS for generative quality, as well as specialized metrics: Trajectory Error (for motion controllability), Video Segmentation MAE (for semantic accuracy), Vision-Language Model (VLM) accuracy (for subjective success), and Relative DINO (for identity preservation). Baselines will include state-of-the-art motion-controllable and elements-to-video models (e.g., DragAnything, Image Conductor, ToRA, Phantom, SkyReels-A2), with all models evaluated on the same curated test sets. Training will be performed at 384x480 resolution, with 12 FPS videos, and classifier-free guidance will be used during inference.
1b6b5db09381de42cf09ae8c7ea5183c2600ab78.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first unified framework for unbounded controllable image-to-video generation with explicit Frame In and Frame Out capabilities. Key innovations include: (1) a new dataset and curation pipeline for Frame In and Frame Out patterns, (2) a video Diffusion Transformer architecture that integrates spatiotemporal motion, identity reference, and unbounded canvas conditions, (3) a comprehensive evaluation protocol tailored for the new task, and (4) empirical demonstration of significant improvements over existing baselines in both controllability and video quality.

1b6c33edca944c871ba40b165803e16241d9e33c.title: Restoring Pruned Large Language Models via Lost Component Compensation
1b6c33edca944c871ba40b165803e16241d9e33c.research_question: How can the performance of pruned large language models be effectively restored without compromising their sparsity or inference efficiency, particularly by addressing the unique information loss characteristics induced by pruning?
1b6c33edca944c871ba40b165803e16241d9e33c.hypothesis: Selective compensation of pruning-induced lost components in attention head activations can substantially restore the performance of pruned large language models, outperforming existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods while preserving model sparsity and inference speed.
1b6c33edca944c871ba40b165803e16241d9e33c.proposed_method: A new restoration framework, RestoreLCC, will be developed to target pruned large language models. The approach consists of two main modules: (1) Contrastive probing, which uses activation editing to construct contrastive sample pairs and identify the most critical attention heads for performance recovery; and (2) Lost Component Compensation (LCC), which estimates the principal and minor components of information lost due to pruning by decomposing the activation differences between dense and pruned models. For each important attention head, the method learns scalar magnitudes for each orthogonal component direction, as well as a bias vector, to optimally reconstruct the lost information. The learned compensation vectors are then injected as constant biases into the pruned model's attention heads, restoring their functional capacity. The method is designed to be plug-and-play, compatible with structured, semi-structured, and unstructured pruning schemes, and introduces negligible parameter and computational overhead.
1b6c33edca944c871ba40b165803e16241d9e33c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of large language models, including LLaMA-7B/13B/30B, LLaMA-2-7B/13B, LLaMA-3-8B, Vicuna-7b-v1.5, Tulu-2-7B, Qwen-3-8B/14B, and DeepSeek-R1-Qwen3-8B, across multiple pruning strategies (unstructured, semi-structured, structured) and sparsity levels. Pruning will be performed using state-of-the-art methods such as Wanda, SparseGPT, and SlimGPT, with calibration on the C4 dataset. Restoration effectiveness will be evaluated using zero-shot language modeling perplexity (WikiText) and accuracy on commonsense reasoning benchmarks (BoolQ, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-easy, ARC-challenge, RTE, OpenBookQA) via the lm-eval-harness. Both general recovery (using Alpaca for tuning) and task-specific recovery (using 100–1000 target task samples) settings will be tested. Baselines will include LoRA, DoRA, FLAP, EoRA, and LoFiT. Key metrics are accuracy, perplexity, parameter overhead, and inference speed, with ablation studies to assess the impact of each module and hyperparameter sensitivity.
1b6c33edca944c871ba40b165803e16241d9e33c.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a targeted restoration strategy that explicitly compensates for pruning-induced information loss by identifying and reconstructing critical lost components in attention head activations. Unlike existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods, which are designed for dense models and do not account for the unique characteristics of pruned models, this approach leverages contrastive probing to select important heads and learns both the direction and magnitude of lost information for effective recovery. The method is compatible with all major pruning schemes, maintains model sparsity and inference efficiency, and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both general and task-specific recovery scenarios. Additional innovations include minimal parameter overhead, seamless integration with quantized models, and empirical validation across a wide range of model sizes and tasks.

1b6e810ce0afd0dd093f789d2b2742d047e316d5.title: Chain of Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
1b6e810ce0afd0dd093f789d2b2742d047e316d5.research_question: How can the reasoning abilities of large language models be enhanced to solve complex tasks such as arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning, using only in-context learning without additional fine-tuning or large annotated datasets?
1b6e810ce0afd0dd093f789d2b2742d047e316d5.hypothesis: Providing large language models with exemplars that include explicit chains of intermediate reasoning steps (chain-of-thought prompting) will elicit improved multi-step reasoning capabilities and lead to higher performance on complex reasoning tasks compared to standard prompting approaches.
1b6e810ce0afd0dd093f789d2b2742d047e316d5.proposed_method: A new prompting strategy, termed chain-of-thought prompting, will be developed wherein few-shot exemplars are augmented with explicit, natural language descriptions of intermediate reasoning steps leading to the answer. For each task, prompts will consist of triples: <input, chain of thought, output>, enabling the model to observe and mimic step-by-step reasoning. This approach will be applied to a variety of large language models (e.g., GPT-3, LaMDA, PaLM) at different parameter scales, using manually composed or sampled chains of thought for few-shot exemplars. The method will be systematically compared to standard prompting (input–output pairs only) and several ablations, such as equation-only or variable-compute prompting, to isolate the effects of natural language reasoning steps.
1b6e810ce0afd0dd093f789d2b2742d047e316d5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple benchmarks spanning arithmetic reasoning (GSM8K, SVAMP, ASDiv, AQuA, MAWPS), commonsense reasoning (CSQA, StrategyQA, BIG-bench Date Understanding, Sports Understanding, SayCan), and symbolic reasoning (last letter concatenation, coin flip tasks). For each benchmark, a consistent set of few-shot exemplars with chains of thought will be used, with variations for task format (e.g., multiple choice). Baselines will include standard few-shot prompting and prior state-of-the-art models, including fine-tuned systems. Evaluation metrics will include solve rates or accuracy, with additional analysis of robustness to different annotators, exemplar orders, and model scales. Both in-domain and out-of-domain (longer sequence) generalization will be assessed for symbolic tasks.
1b6e810ce0afd0dd093f789d2b2742d047e316d5.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces chain-of-thought prompting as a simple yet broadly applicable method for eliciting multi-step reasoning in large language models without fine-tuning. It claims that reasoning abilities emerge at sufficient model scale when models are prompted with explicit reasoning steps, resulting in significant performance gains on challenging reasoning tasks. The approach is shown to be robust across annotators, exemplars, and model architectures, and to facilitate out-of-domain generalization in symbolic reasoning. This work expands the known capabilities of large language models and demonstrates that standard prompting underestimates their reasoning potential.

1b88ff25523e21628672e6e0d77b4f2aede14bbc.title: Robust low-rank training via approximate orthonormal constraints
1b88ff25523e21628672e6e0d77b4f2aede14bbc.research_question: How can neural network training be made both resource-efficient and robust to adversarial perturbations, particularly when using low-rank weight parameterizations?
1b88ff25523e21628672e6e0d77b4f2aede14bbc.hypothesis: Imposing approximate orthonormal (well-conditioned) constraints on low-rank weight matrices during training will yield neural networks that are both computationally efficient and robust to adversarial attacks, without sacrificing accuracy.
1b88ff25523e21628672e6e0d77b4f2aede14bbc.proposed_method: A robust low-rank training algorithm is developed that parameterizes each layer's weight matrix as W = USV⊤, where U and V have orthonormal columns and S is a small invertible matrix. The training process is formulated as a constrained optimization problem, enforcing that the singular values of S remain within a narrow band around a target value, thereby bounding the condition number of each layer to a desired tolerance (1+τ). The method employs projected gradient flows for U, S, and V, using geometric integration theory to ensure updates remain on the appropriate low-rank and Stiefel manifolds. At each iteration, U and V are updated and projected onto the Stiefel manifold, S is updated and projected onto the set of matrices with nearly constant singular values, and the tolerance τ is tuned to control robustness. The algorithm is implemented efficiently, never forming full weight matrices, and supports parallel updates for all factors.
1b88ff25523e21628672e6e0d77b4f2aede14bbc.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on MNIST and CIFAR10 datasets using LeNet5 and VGG16 architectures, respectively. The proposed method is compared against full-rank baselines, orthogonality-promoting methods (Cayley SGD, Projected SGD), and several low-rank training baselines (DLRT, SVD prune, Vanilla). Compression ratios of 50% and 80% are tested, with the number of parameters reduced accordingly. Evaluation metrics include standard test accuracy and robust accuracy under adversarial perturbations generated by the Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM) at varying perturbation strengths. All models are trained for 120 epochs using stochastic gradient descent with fixed learning rates and batch sizes, and results are reported for both natural and adversarially perturbed test sets.
1b88ff25523e21628672e6e0d77b4f2aede14bbc.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to combine low-rank training with explicit, tunable conditioning constraints to ensure both efficiency and adversarial robustness. The method introduces a novel projected gradient flow formulation on the low-rank manifold with bounded singular values, enabling robust training without increased computational cost. Theoretical guarantees are provided, showing that the method approximates the ideal full model up to a first-order error when a well-performing low-rank sub-network exists. Experimental results demonstrate state-of-the-art robustness and accuracy trade-offs at significant compression rates, outperforming both standard low-rank and orthogonality-based baselines.

1b93ebee92672c7f8d8245e56fd5f9f853acf7c3.title: Spike-driven Transformer V2: Meta Spiking Neural Network Architecture Inspiring the Design of Next-generation Neuromorphic Chips
1b93ebee92672c7f8d8245e56fd5f9f853acf7c3.research_question: How can a general, high-performance, and energy-efficient Transformer-based Spiking Neural Network (SNN) architecture be developed to serve as a versatile backbone for various vision tasks and inspire the design of next-generation neuromorphic chips?
1b93ebee92672c7f8d8245e56fd5f9f853acf7c3.hypothesis: A meta-architecture that integrates spike-driven self-attention mechanisms with both convolutional and Transformer-based SNN blocks, leveraging sparse addition operations and optimized shortcut connections, will outperform existing CNN-based SNNs in accuracy, versatility, and energy efficiency across multiple vision tasks, while providing a scalable blueprint for neuromorphic hardware co-design.
1b93ebee92672c7f8d8245e56fd5f9f853acf7c3.proposed_method: A meta Transformer-based SNN architecture, termed Meta-SpikeFormer, will be developed by combining Conv-based and Transformer-based SNN blocks within a unified framework. The architecture will employ spike-driven self-attention (SDSA) modules, which replace energy-intensive operations like softmax and scaling with sparse addition, and generate spiking Query, Key, and Value tensors using re-parameterized convolutions. The macro-level design will follow a hybrid Conv+ViT structure, with early stages using separable convolutional SNN blocks and later stages using pyramid-structured Transformer-based SNN blocks. At the micro-level, new SDSA operators with varying computational complexities will be designed, and membrane-based shortcut connections will be used to ensure identity mapping and spike-driven computation. Direct training with surrogate gradients will be used to optimize the network for spatio-temporal dynamics.
1b93ebee92672c7f8d8245e56fd5f9f853acf7c3.experiment_details: Comprehensive experiments will be conducted on four major vision tasks: image classification (ImageNet-1K), event-based action recognition (HAR-DVS), object detection (COCO), and semantic segmentation (ADE20K, VOC2012). The architecture will be evaluated at multiple scales by varying channel sizes, and both direct training and fine-tuning strategies will be employed. Baselines will include state-of-the-art CNN-based SNNs, ANN2SNN models, and Transformer-based SNNs, as well as leading ANN architectures such as ResNet, ViT, and PVT. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy for classification, mean Average Precision (mAP) for detection, and mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) for segmentation, along with parameter count and estimated energy consumption (using FLOPs and spike firing rates). Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of architectural components such as SDSA variants, shortcut types, and block configurations.
1b93ebee92672c7f8d8245e56fd5f9f853acf7c3.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first meta-architecture for Transformer-based SNNs that supports direct training and unifies classification, detection, and segmentation tasks within a single backbone. It pioneers the use of spike-driven self-attention modules with only sparse addition, eliminating the need for energy-intensive operations. The design achieves state-of-the-art accuracy in the SNN domain on ImageNet-1K (80% top-1), surpassing previous SNN baselines with fewer parameters and lower power consumption. The architecture's versatility and performance provide a blueprint for future Transformer-based neuromorphic chip design, facilitating algorithm-hardware co-design and enabling scalable, energy-efficient neuromorphic computing.

1b9d53349420bb6970095898a5d2960ab8653713.title: Is Large-Scale Pretraining the Secret to Good Domain Generalization?
1b9d53349420bb6970095898a5d2960ab8653713.research_question: How does large-scale pretraining influence the domain generalization ability of models, and can domain generalization methods be developed that generalize well to target domains that are not well aligned with pretraining data?
1b9d53349420bb6970095898a5d2960ab8653713.hypothesis: The Alignment Hypothesis: Domain generalization performance is high if and only if the alignment between image and class label text embeddings, as established during pretraining, is high. In other words, pretraining alignment is a stronger predictor of domain generalization success than perceptual similarity alone.
1b9d53349420bb6970095898a5d2960ab8653713.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation framework is proposed to analyze the dependence of domain generalization (DG) methods on pretraining alignment. The methodology involves computing an Alignment Score for each sample in standard DG datasets, defined as the cosine similarity between the pre-trained image embedding and its corresponding class label text embedding. Based on this score, datasets are split into In-Pretraining (IP, high alignment) and Out-of-Pretraining (OOP, low alignment) subsets, after filtering out mislabeled and OCR-dominated samples. Multiple state-of-the-art DG algorithms, especially those leveraging CLIP-based backbones, are then trained on the original, unsplit source domains and evaluated separately on the IP and OOP splits of the target domain. This approach enables a fine-grained analysis of where DG methods succeed or fail, particularly in relation to pretraining alignment.
1b9d53349420bb6970095898a5d2960ab8653713.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on five widely-used DomainBed datasets: VLCS, PACS, OfficeHome, TerraIncognita, and DomainNet. For each dataset, the Alignment Score is computed for all samples using the OpenCLIP ViT-B/16 backbone, and data is split into IP and OOP subsets with a threshold of 0.21 after filtering for label noise and OCR artifacts. DG methods evaluated include explicit regularization approaches (e.g., MIRO, VL2V-SD, CLIPood, MPA), domain invariance methods (e.g., CORAL), flat optima methods (e.g., SWAD, SAGM), and baselines such as ERM and zero-shot CLIP. Models are trained on source domains and tested on IP, OOP, and the original test splits, with accuracy averaged across all target domains. Evaluation metrics focus on classification accuracy, and the experimental setup follows DomainBed's leave-one-domain-out protocol, ensuring comparability and robustness.
1b9d53349420bb6970095898a5d2960ab8653713.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the Alignment Hypothesis as a new, empirically validated predictor of domain generalization performance, surpassing the previously established Image Similarity Hypothesis. A novel evaluation framework is developed by splitting standard DG datasets into IP and OOP subsets based on pretraining alignment, enabling more diagnostic benchmarking. The approach exposes that current DG methods excel only on pretraining-aligned data and struggle on misaligned samples, highlighting a critical gap in existing methods. The release of DomainBed-IP/OOP splits provides a new resource for the community to develop and evaluate DG methods that can generalize beyond the limitations of pretraining alignment.

1bba2a9c6db3b356b8ae6ef2efff5645e4d96c2b.title: Text-to-Image Diffusion Models are Zero-Shot Classifiers
1bba2a9c6db3b356b8ae6ef2efff5645e4d96c2b.research_question: Can text-to-image diffusion models be effectively leveraged as zero-shot image classifiers, and how do their learned representations compare to those of contrastively trained models on downstream discriminative tasks such as classification, robustness to confounding cues, and attribute binding?
1bba2a9c6db3b356b8ae6ef2efff5645e4d96c2b.hypothesis: Text-to-image diffusion models, when repurposed as generative classifiers, can achieve competitive or superior zero-shot classification performance compared to contrastively trained models, demonstrate robustness to misleading textural cues, and exhibit enhanced compositional generalization such as attribute binding.
1bba2a9c6db3b356b8ae6ef2efff5645e4d96c2b.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed to utilize text-to-image diffusion models as zero-shot image classifiers. The approach involves conditioning the diffusion model on text prompts corresponding to class labels and repeatedly denoising a noised version of the input image for each class prompt. The denoising ability, quantified via a re-weighted variational lower bound (VLB) or diffusion loss, serves as a proxy for the likelihood of the image belonging to each class. Monte Carlo estimation is used to approximate the expectation over noise and timesteps, with a heuristic or learned weighting function applied to improve accuracy. To address computational inefficiency, shared noise sampling across classes and a candidate class pruning strategy based on paired statistical tests are introduced, significantly reducing the number of model evaluations required per classification.
1bba2a9c6db3b356b8ae6ef2efff5645e4d96c2b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models (Imagen and Stable Diffusion) and compared against CLIP (ViT-L/14) as a strong contrastive baseline. Evaluation will be performed on a suite of zero-shot classification datasets, including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, STL-10, MNIST, DTD, Camelyon, SVHN, EuroSAT, Stanford Cars, ImageNet, Caltech101, OxfordPets, and Food101. Additional robustness experiments will utilize the Cue-Conflict dataset to assess shape vs. texture bias, and synthetic datasets based on CLEVR will be used to probe attribute binding capabilities. Datasets are preprocessed to appropriate resolutions for each model, and accuracy is measured as the primary evaluation metric. For efficiency, reduced dataset sizes and prompt templates are used, and multiple runs are performed to ensure statistical significance. Baselines include both supervised and zero-shot models, with attention to input resolution and model size differences.
1bba2a9c6db3b356b8ae6ef2efff5645e4d96c2b.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to directly use text-to-image diffusion models as zero-shot classifiers via generative classification, enabling quantitative evaluation of their learned representations on discriminative tasks. The approach introduces substantial computational efficiency improvements through shared noise sampling and candidate class pruning. Experiments demonstrate that diffusion models can match or exceed the performance of contrastive models like CLIP on standard classification benchmarks, achieve state-of-the-art robustness to misleading textural cues, and uniquely exhibit attribute binding abilities not present in contrastive models. The findings suggest generative pre-training as a compelling alternative to contrastive pre-training for vision-language tasks.

1bc9865ebf52b59abac7f5ee4456ff2ac37fcff3.title: ST-MoE: Designing Stable and Transferable Sparse Expert Models
1bc9865ebf52b59abac7f5ee4456ff2ac37fcff3.research_question: How can large-scale sparse expert neural network models be designed and trained to achieve stable and high-quality performance, particularly in transfer learning and fine-tuning across diverse natural language processing tasks, while maintaining computational efficiency?
1bc9865ebf52b59abac7f5ee4456ff2ac37fcff3.hypothesis: Introducing targeted architectural modifications, stability techniques such as the router z-loss, and fine-tuning protocols will enable sparse Mixture-of-Experts models to achieve both stable training and state-of-the-art transfer learning performance, matching or exceeding dense models at a fraction of the computational cost.
1bc9865ebf52b59abac7f5ee4456ff2ac37fcff3.proposed_method: A novel framework for sparse expert models, termed Stable and Transferable Mixture-of-Experts (ST-MoE), will be developed with a focus on stabilizing training and improving transferability. The methodology will involve a large-scale empirical study of stability-quality trade-offs for various stabilization techniques, including the introduction of the router z-loss to penalize large logits in the routing network, thereby reducing roundoff errors and improving numerical stability. The architecture will use top-k routing with a carefully tuned capacity factor, and will replace every fourth feedforward layer with a sparse MoE layer containing multiple experts. Mixed precision training will be employed, with float32 precision for critical routing operations to mitigate instability. Fine-tuning protocols will be systematically analyzed, including dropout and expert dropout regularization, and hyperparameter sensitivity studies will be conducted to optimize generalization on downstream tasks.
1bc9865ebf52b59abac7f5ee4456ff2ac37fcff3.experiment_details: Experiments will pre-train sparse models with up to 269B parameters on large-scale multilingual corpora such as mC4, using masked language modeling objectives. Models will be FLOP-matched to strong dense baselines (e.g., T5-XL, T5-Large) and evaluated on a wide range of NLP benchmarks, including SuperGLUE, ARC Easy/Challenge, XSum, CNN-DM, WebQA, Natural Questions, Winogrande, and ANLI R3. Stability techniques will be benchmarked using multiple random seeds, and the impact of architectural and optimization changes will be measured via negative log perplexity and task-specific metrics (e.g., accuracy, F1). Fine-tuning experiments will analyze overfitting, regularization, and hyperparameter sensitivity, with ablations for dropout rates and expert dropout. The computational cost and hardware efficiency will be compared between sparse and dense models.
1bc9865ebf52b59abac7f5ee4456ff2ac37fcff3.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the router z-loss as a principled and effective stabilization technique for large-scale sparse expert models, enabling stable training without sacrificing model quality. The work systematically characterizes the stability-quality trade-off space for sparse architectures, provides a design guide for Pareto efficient sparse models, and demonstrates—for the first time—state-of-the-art transfer learning performance from a sparse model across a diverse set of NLP tasks at a fraction of the computational cost of dense models. Additional contributions include detailed analyses of fine-tuning protocols, architectural design principles for distributed sparse models, and qualitative studies of expert specialization and token routing.

1bc9fd4f2f36fb1355d34c2ec8b15ed1be98b8ec.title: Sharp Spectral Rates for Koopman Operator Learning
1bc9fd4f2f36fb1355d34c2ec8b15ed1be98b8ec.research_question: How can the spectral properties (eigenvalues and eigenfunctions) of the Koopman operator associated with time-reversal-invariant stochastic dynamical systems be learned from data with sharp, non-asymptotic statistical guarantees, and what are the fundamental limits and practical implications of different kernel-based operator regression algorithms?
1bc9fd4f2f36fb1355d34c2ec8b15ed1be98b8ec.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that sharp, non-asymptotic learning bounds can be established for the estimation of Koopman operator spectra using kernel-based regression algorithms, and that the interplay between operator norm error and a newly introduced metric distortion functional is crucial for understanding estimator performance and the emergence of spurious eigenvalues.
1bc9fd4f2f36fb1355d34c2ec8b15ed1be98b8ec.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops a theoretical framework for learning the spectral decomposition of the Koopman operator from data, focusing on time-reversal-invariant stochastic dynamical systems (such as Langevin dynamics). The methodology analyzes two mainstream kernel-based operator regression algorithms: Principal Component Regression (PCR, also known as Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition, EDMD) and Reduced Rank Regression (RRR). Both methods approximate the Koopman operator on a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), using empirical covariance and cross-covariance operators constructed from observed state transitions. The proposal introduces a novel metric distortion functional to quantify the discrepancy between the RKHS and the ambient space, and derives non-asymptotic minimax optimal bounds for the operator norm error. The spectral estimation error is then bounded by combining the operator norm error and the metric distortion, providing a comprehensive analysis of both eigenvalue and eigenfunction estimation. Additionally, the method proposes empirical estimators for the metric distortion and spectral bias, enabling practical model selection and detection of spurious eigenvalues.
1bc9fd4f2f36fb1355d34c2ec8b15ed1be98b8ec.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and realistic dynamical systems, including the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process and Langevin dynamics with multi-well potentials. Multiple kernel functions (including well-matched and deliberately misspecified kernels) will be used to fit PCR/EDMD and RRR estimators on datasets of consecutive state pairs. Evaluation will focus on the accuracy of estimated eigenvalues and eigenfunctions compared to ground truth, using metrics such as eigenvalue estimation error, empirical spectral bias, and root mean squared error (RMSE) for forecasting tasks. Baseline comparisons will include both PCR/EDMD and RRR under various kernel choices and rank constraints. Additional experiments will assess the utility of the empirical spectral bias as a model selection criterion on realistic molecular dynamics datasets (e.g., Alanine Dipeptide), with performance measured by forecasting accuracy and the ability to avoid spurious eigenvalues.
1bc9fd4f2f36fb1355d34c2ec8b15ed1be98b8ec.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first non-asymptotic, minimax-optimal learning bounds for the spectral estimation of Koopman operators, explicitly accounting for both operator norm error and a novel metric distortion functional. The analysis reveals that RRR and PCR/EDMD have similar variance but different bias properties, with PCR/EDMD potentially suffering from larger and irreducible bias depending on the kernel choice. The work provides a theoretical explanation for the empirical phenomenon of spurious eigenvalues in Koopman spectral estimation and proposes a new, data-driven criterion for model and kernel selection based on empirical spectral bias. These contributions advance the statistical understanding of Koopman operator learning and offer practical tools for reliable spectral estimation in data-driven dynamical systems.

1bd57f00a1cb85c1242924e0e80c6b2c0de9a9ab.title: Revisiting Random Walks for Learning on Graphs
1bd57f00a1cb85c1242924e0e80c6b2c0de9a9ab.research_question: How can random walk-based neural network models be systematically designed and analyzed to achieve isomorphism invariance, universal approximation, and improved information propagation for graph-level and vertex-level prediction tasks on graphs, including large and attributed graphs?
1bd57f00a1cb85c1242924e0e80c6b2c0de9a9ab.hypothesis: Random walk neural networks (RWNNs) can be designed to be isomorphism invariant and achieve universal approximation of graph functions in probability by appropriately choosing the random walk algorithm and recording function, while leveraging powerful neural network architectures (such as language models) as readers. These models will overcome limitations of message passing neural networks (MPNNs), such as over-smoothing and over-squashing, and provide strong empirical performance on challenging graph learning tasks.
1bd57f00a1cb85c1242924e0e80c6b2c0de9a9ab.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops a class of models called Random Walk Neural Networks (RWNNs), which operate by generating random walks on input graphs, recording the walks using invariant recording functions (such as anonymization or anonymization with named neighbors), and processing these records with a deep neural network reader. The random walk algorithm is chosen to be invariant in probability, with options such as uniform walks, minimum degree local rule (MDLR) walks, and non-backtracking walks, potentially augmented with restarts for locality. The recording function ensures isomorphism invariance by anonymizing vertex identities and, optionally, recording named neighbors to efficiently capture subgraph structures. The reader neural network is unconstrained in architecture and can include powerful models such as transformers or pre-trained language models, which process the recorded walks (in formats such as plain text) to make predictions. For vertex-level tasks on large or infinite graphs, random walks are localized using restarts to guarantee finite cover times and effective information capture.
1bd57f00a1cb85c1242924e0e80c6b2c0de9a9ab.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world graph datasets. Synthetic experiments will use lollipop, clique, and barbell graphs to measure edge and vertex cover times, and to evaluate over-smoothing and over-squashing phenomena, with baselines including MLP, GCN, SAGE, GAT, NSD, BuNN, and other RWNN variants. For graph isomorphism learning, datasets such as CSL, SR16, and SR25 (containing strongly regular graphs where WL tests fail) will be used, with accuracy compared to state-of-the-art baselines like GIN, PPGN, AgentNet, and CRaWl. For large-scale, real-world transductive classification, the ogbn-arxiv citation network (with 170k+ nodes and textual attributes) will be used, comparing RWNNs with language models (Llama3, DeBERTa, GPT-3.5), MPNNs, and label propagation, using accuracy as the main metric. Evaluation will include ablation of walk types, recording functions, and reader architectures, with attention visualizations to interpret model behavior.
1bd57f00a1cb85c1242924e0e80c6b2c0de9a9ab.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled framework for designing RWNNs that decouples random walk generation, walk recording, and neural network reading, enabling systematic incorporation of isomorphism invariance via probabilistic invariance of walks and records. It establishes universal approximation guarantees for RWNNs in probability, surpassing the expressive power of the Weisfeiler-Lehman hierarchy under suitable conditions. The method introduces the use of anonymization with named neighbors for efficient subgraph recording, and demonstrates the compatibility of plain-text walk records with powerful language models for graph learning. The analysis reveals that RWNNs inherently avoid over-smoothing and shift the challenge of over-squashing to probabilistic under-reaching, which can be mitigated by walk design. Empirical results are expected to show state-of-the-art performance on challenging graph isomorphism and transductive classification tasks, including settings where traditional MPNNs and WL-based methods fail.

1bed8c7541381b1f79027c240b64c9276573fc3c.title: Simplified and Generalized Masked Diffusion for Discrete Data
1bed8c7541381b1f79027c240b64c9276573fc3c.research_question: How can masked diffusion models for discrete data be simplified and generalized to improve generative modeling performance across text and image domains, and what are the effects of state-dependent masking schedules on such models?
1bed8c7541381b1f79027c240b64c9276573fc3c.hypothesis: A simplified and generalized continuous-time masked diffusion framework, with a loss based on a weighted integral of cross-entropy terms and the option for state-dependent masking schedules, will improve the performance and training stability of discrete diffusion models, surpassing previous discrete diffusion and autoregressive models in likelihood-based and zero-shot generative tasks.
1bed8c7541381b1f79027c240b64c9276573fc3c.proposed_method: A continuous-time masked diffusion framework for discrete data is developed, where the forward process progressively replaces each token with a mask token according to a time-dependent or state-dependent masking schedule. The reverse generative model is parameterized via a neural network that predicts the mean of the original data given masked inputs, and is trained using an Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO) objective that is shown to be a weighted integral of cross-entropy losses over time. The method is extended to allow state-dependent masking schedules, where the masking probability for each token can depend on its value, and the corresponding ELBO is derived. For multidimensional data, the forward and reverse processes factorize across tokens, and the loss is computed as a sum over masked tokens. Sampling is performed via ancestral sampling from the reverse process, with careful selection of discretization grids (e.g., cosine schedules) to improve sample quality.
1bed8c7541381b1f79027c240b64c9276573fc3c.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both text and image modeling tasks. For text, models are trained on datasets such as text8, OpenWebText, and FineWeb-Edu, and evaluated using bits-per-character (BPC), perplexity, and zero-shot accuracy on benchmarks including LAMBADA, WikiText2, PTB, WikiText103, IBW, and Hellaswag. For images, pixel-level modeling is performed on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet 64x64, treating each pixel as a discrete token, and evaluated using bits-per-dimension (BPD) and Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for sample quality. Baselines include prior discrete diffusion models (e.g., D3PM, SEDDAbsorb), autoregressive models (e.g., GPT-2, PixelCNN, PixelSNAIL), and continuous diffusion models (e.g., VDM, Plaid, BFN). The effect of different masking schedules (linear, cosine, geometric, polynomial) and discretization strategies is systematically compared. Additional experiments assess the impact of state-dependent masking schedules and the generalization capabilities of the proposed models.
1bed8c7541381b1f79027c240b64c9276573fc3c.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified and simplified continuous-time framework for masked diffusion on discrete data, deriving a closed-form ELBO as a weighted integral of cross-entropy losses. It generalizes masked diffusion to allow state-dependent masking schedules, enabling more flexible modeling. The method clarifies the relationship between mean and score parameterizations and demonstrates that the proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art likelihoods and zero-shot performance among discrete diffusion models, outperforming prior discrete and autoregressive baselines on several benchmarks. The framework also provides new insights into the design of masking schedules and their impact on generative quality and training stability.

1bf8c4f93a8663b424f0d132a169344c93ec5a5c.title: Faster Minimum Bayes Risk Decoding with Confidence-based Pruning
1bf8c4f93a8663b424f0d132a169344c93ec5a5c.research_question: How can the computational efficiency of minimum Bayes risk (MBR) decoding in conditional language generation tasks, such as neural machine translation, be improved without sacrificing accuracy?
1bf8c4f93a8663b424f0d132a169344c93ec5a5c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that an iterative pruning algorithm, which incrementally increases the number of samples and prunes unlikely hypotheses using confidence estimates derived from bootstrap sampling, can significantly reduce the computational cost of MBR decoding while maintaining comparable accuracy to standard MBR methods.
1bf8c4f93a8663b424f0d132a169344c93ec5a5c.proposed_method: A novel iterative pruning algorithm for MBR decoding is proposed, wherein the hypothesis set is gradually reduced while the number of pseudo-references (samples) used to estimate expected utility grows according to a predefined schedule. At each iteration, a pruning function evaluates the probability that each hypothesis is the true MBR winner, using nonparametric bootstrap resampling to estimate confidence. Hypotheses with an estimated probability below a confidence threshold (1-α) of being the top candidate are pruned. This process continues until either a maximum number of iterations is reached or only one hypothesis remains, at which point the hypothesis with the highest expected utility is selected. The method reuses previously computed utility values to minimize redundant computation and supports early termination when only one candidate remains.
1bf8c4f93a8663b424f0d132a169344c93ec5a5c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on neural machine translation models trained on WMT18 datasets for German-English, English-Estonian, and Turkish-English language pairs. The models will use the Transformer architecture and standard preprocessing, with beam top-k (k=256) for hypothesis generation and up to 1024 pseudo-references generated via epsilon sampling. Both chrF++ and COMET will serve as utility and evaluation metrics, and pruning parameters will be tuned based on validation set performance. Baseline comparisons will include standard sampling-based MBR and a utility-based pruning baseline. Evaluation will consider automatic metrics (score, accuracy, reciprocal rank), computational metrics (number of utility calls, pseudo-references), and human evaluation for indistinguishability. Multiple random trials will be run for statistical robustness, and runtime comparisons will be performed against standard MBR and beam search.
1bf8c4f93a8663b424f0d132a169344c93ec5a5c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a confidence-based, bootstrap-driven pruning strategy for MBR decoding that drastically reduces the number of utility function calls and required samples compared to standard MBR, without statistically significant loss in accuracy. The method is model-agnostic, requires no changes to the underlying model or utility function, and can terminate early, further improving efficiency. Empirical results demonstrate that the approach achieves substantial computational savings—up to 15x fewer utility calls—while maintaining accuracy on par with standard MBR, and is validated across multiple language pairs, metrics, and both automatic and human evaluations.

1bfc6f9c9db5c6646f0f3e0213d407ae14d8f7bf.title: Beta-CROWN: Efficient Bound Propagation with Per-neuron Split Constraints for Neural Network Robustness Verification
1bfc6f9c9db5c6646f0f3e0213d407ae14d8f7bf.research_question: How can neural network robustness verification be made both highly efficient and capable of fully encoding per-neuron split constraints, particularly in the context of branch-and-bound (BaB) based complete verification frameworks?
1bfc6f9c9db5c6646f0f3e0213d407ae14d8f7bf.hypothesis: Introducing optimizable per-neuron split constraint parameters into bound propagation methods will enable neural network verifiers to achieve verification tightness comparable to or better than LP-based approaches, while significantly improving computational efficiency and scalability on modern hardware.
1bfc6f9c9db5c6646f0f3e0213d407ae14d8f7bf.proposed_method: A novel bound propagation framework, named Beta-CROWN, will be developed to efficiently encode per-neuron split constraints introduced by BaB in neural network verification. The method introduces optimizable parameters (beta) derived from either the primal or dual space, corresponding to Lagrangian multipliers for neuron split constraints. These beta parameters will be jointly optimized with traditional bound propagation variables (alpha) using (super)gradient ascent, leveraging automatic differentiation and GPU acceleration. The approach will support joint optimization of intermediate layer bounds, allowing for tighter relaxations than typical LP-based verifiers, and will be compatible with any BaB branching strategy. The overall algorithm will be implemented to exploit parallelism, enabling large-scale verification tasks.
1bfc6f9c9db5c6646f0f3e0213d407ae14d8f7bf.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard robustness verification benchmarks, including CIFAR-10 models (Base, Wide, Deep) and various MNIST and CIFAR-10 convolutional and MLP architectures. The method will be evaluated in both complete and incomplete verification settings. Baseline comparisons will include LP-based BaB verifiers, MIP solvers, abstract interpretation methods, dual-space verifiers, and state-of-the-art incomplete verifiers such as kPoly, OptC2V, PRIMA, and SDP-based approaches (e.g., SDP-FO). Evaluation metrics will include average verification time, number of branches, timeout rates, and verified accuracy. Experiments will utilize GPU acceleration, and both BaBSR and FSB branching heuristics will be tested. The method will also be assessed for its ability to provide tight lower bounds and to outperform convex barrier-breaking incomplete verifiers in runtime and tightness.
1bfc6f9c9db5c6646f0f3e0213d407ae14d8f7bf.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first efficient bound propagation method capable of fully encoding per-neuron split constraints via optimizable parameters, bridging the gap between the efficiency of bound propagation and the tightness of LP-based verifiers. The method enables joint optimization of intermediate layer bounds and split constraint parameters, resulting in tighter relaxations than fixed-bound LP approaches. GPU-friendly implementation allows for orders-of-magnitude speedup over existing LP and SDP-based verifiers, with demonstrated improvements in both verification tightness and scalability. The approach is generalizable to any BaB branching strategy and can function as both a complete and an efficient incomplete verifier.

1c13af186d1e177b85ef1ec3fc7b8d33ec314cfd.title: Paraphrasing evades detectors of AI-generated text, but retrieval is an effective defense
