1c13af186d1e177b85ef1ec3fc7b8d33ec314cfd.research_question: How robust are current AI-generated text detection methods to paraphrasing attacks, and can retrieval-based approaches provide an effective defense against such attacks?
1c13af186d1e177b85ef1ec3fc7b8d33ec314cfd.hypothesis: Existing AI-generated text detectors are vulnerable to paraphrasing attacks that preserve semantics but alter surface form, while retrieval-based detection leveraging a database of previously generated outputs will be significantly more robust to such attacks.
1c13af186d1e177b85ef1ec3fc7b8d33ec314cfd.proposed_method: A large-scale, controllable discourse-level paraphraser (DIPPER) will be developed by fine-tuning a sequence-to-sequence Transformer model (initialized from T5-XXL, 11B parameters) on a parallel corpus of paragraph-level paraphrases. The paraphraser will be trained to handle long-form text, leverage context (such as prompts), and provide fine-grained control over lexical diversity and content reordering via scalar control codes. Paraphrasing attacks will be conducted by passing AI-generated outputs from various LLMs through DIPPER, systematically varying the degree of lexical and order diversity. To defend against these attacks, a retrieval-based detection system will be implemented: all outputs from the LLM API will be stored in a database, and candidate texts will be compared for semantic similarity (using BM25 or neural embedding methods like P-SP) against this database to identify AI-generated or paraphrased content.
1c13af186d1e177b85ef1ec3fc7b8d33ec314cfd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on long-form text generation tasks, including open-ended generation and question answering, using models such as GPT2-XL, OPT-13B, and GPT-3.5-davinci-003. Datasets include WikiText-103 for prompts and continuations, as well as the PAR3 dataset for paraphrase training. Baseline detectors to be evaluated and attacked include watermarking, DetectGPT, GPTZero, OpenAI’s text classifier, and RankGen. Evaluation metrics will include detection accuracy at a fixed 1% false positive rate, semantic similarity (using P-SP), and ROC curves. The retrieval-based defense will be tested at scale with a corpus of up to 15 million LLM generations, measuring detection rates for both original and paraphrased outputs, and monitoring false positive rates on human-written text.
1c13af186d1e177b85ef1ec3fc7b8d33ec314cfd.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a controllable, discourse-level paraphraser capable of attacking AI-generated text detectors at the paragraph level with fine-grained control over output diversity. It systematically demonstrates the vulnerability of state-of-the-art detectors to such paraphrasing attacks while preserving semantics. As a novel defense, it proposes and empirically validates a retrieval-based detection method that leverages a large-scale database of LLM outputs, showing high effectiveness and scalability against paraphrased attacks. The approach is claimed to outperform existing detectors and to provide a practical, scalable solution for LLM API providers.

1c1d1b4e1edae9dca84ea655624a4c8dc7fef2a7.title: Conformal Language Modeling
1c1d1b4e1edae9dca84ea655624a4c8dc7fef2a7.research_question: How can reliable, distribution-free uncertainty quantification and performance guarantees be achieved for language model outputs in generative, combinatorial output spaces, including both full responses and their subcomponents, across diverse NLP tasks?
1c1d1b4e1edae9dca84ea655624a4c8dc7fef2a7.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a calibrated sampling and rejection procedure, inspired by conformal prediction and tailored to language models, can produce prediction sets that provably contain at least one acceptable response with high probability, while also identifying independently correct subcomponents within generated outputs.
1c1d1b4e1edae9dca84ea655624a4c8dc7fef2a7.proposed_method: A novel conformal prediction framework will be developed for language models, leveraging a calibrated sampling procedure that iteratively grows a set of candidate outputs. At each step, candidate responses are sampled from the language model and subjected to both a quality threshold and a diversity criterion, ensuring only high-quality and diverse samples are included. A set-based confidence function is used to determine when the output set is likely to contain at least one acceptable response, at which point sampling stops. The method also incorporates a calibrated rejection rule to remove low-quality or redundant candidates, maintaining both statistical validity and output set precision. Additionally, an extension will be implemented to identify and select independently correct subcomponents (such as sentences or phrases) within generated outputs, using component-level admission functions and confidence estimators, all calibrated to provide formal guarantees.
1c1d1b4e1edae9dca84ea655624a4c8dc7fef2a7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three tasks: radiology report generation (using the MIMIC-CXR dataset with a ViT-GPT2 model), news summarization (using the CNN/DM dataset with a T5-XL model), and open-domain question answering (using the TriviaQA dataset with LLaMA-13B in a few-shot setting). For each task, appropriate admission functions will be defined (e.g., Clinical Efficacy metric for radiology, ROUGE-L for summarization, exact match for QA), and both set-level and component-level prediction sets will be evaluated. Baselines will include uniform sampling (FIRST-K), likelihood-based scoring (MAX, SUM), and rejection-augmented variants. Evaluation metrics will include set loss (risk), relative excess samples, and output set size, with results aggregated over multiple trials and normalized AUCs computed over achievable risk levels. Calibration and hyperparameter selection will be performed using a held-out calibration set and the Learn-Then-Test (LTT) framework.
1c1d1b4e1edae9dca84ea655624a4c8dc7fef2a7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach bridges the gap between conformal prediction and generative language models by calibrating a sampling-based algorithm rather than relying on enumeration of the output space. It extends multi-label conformal prediction to the identification of confident subcomponents within long generations, providing formal, distribution-free guarantees at both the set and component level. The method is model-agnostic, applicable to any language model supporting sampling, and introduces a dynamic stopping rule and rejection mechanism to ensure efficient, precise, and reliable uncertainty quantification for open-ended text generation tasks.

1c3c531fc0fbe79f97f367ed3648de8467caeeaa.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
1c3c531fc0fbe79f97f367ed3648de8467caeeaa.research_question: How can the design of agent-computer interfaces (ACIs) be optimized to enable language model agents to autonomously and effectively perform complex software engineering tasks in digital environments?
1c3c531fc0fbe79f97f367ed3648de8467caeeaa.hypothesis: Custom-designed agent-computer interfaces tailored to the needs and limitations of language model agents will significantly improve their performance on real-world software engineering tasks compared to traditional human-centric interfaces such as the Linux shell.
1c3c531fc0fbe79f97f367ed3648de8467caeeaa.proposed_method: A novel agent-computer interface (ACI) will be developed to facilitate language model (LM) agents in performing software engineering tasks. The ACI will provide a set of LM-friendly commands for repository navigation, file viewing, code editing, and context management, with guardrails such as syntax checking and concise, informative feedback to prevent and recover from errors. The interface will consolidate complex operations into simple, efficient actions, minimizing the cognitive and context window load on the LM. The LM agent will interact with the environment iteratively, generating both thoughts and actions at each step, and the ACI will manage the formatting and delivery of environment state and feedback to the LM. The system will be built atop a Linux shell but will abstract away low-level details, offering a higher-level, LM-centric interaction paradigm.
1c3c531fc0fbe79f97f367ed3648de8467caeeaa.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the SWE-bench dataset, which comprises 2,294 real-world software engineering tasks from 12 popular Python repositories, and on HumanEvalFix, a code debugging benchmark. The proposed system will be evaluated using leading language models such as GPT-4 Turbo and Claude 3 Opus, with additional tests on other models for comparison. Baselines will include a non-interactive retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system and an interactive shell-only agent. Evaluation metrics will include %Resolved (pass@1), which measures the proportion of tasks for which all tests pass after the agent's patch is applied, and average API inference cost per resolved instance. Ablation studies will be performed to analyze the impact of different ACI design choices, such as search and editing interfaces, file viewer window sizes, and context management strategies.
1c3c531fc0fbe79f97f367ed3648de8467caeeaa.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the concept of an agent-computer interface (ACI) specifically designed for language model agents, unifying tool use, prompting, and code execution within a single framework. The method claims to substantially improve LM agent performance on end-to-end software engineering tasks without modifying the underlying LM weights. The approach is distinct in its LM-centric design principles, such as compact actions, informative feedback, and integrated guardrails, and demonstrates state-of-the-art results on challenging software engineering benchmarks. The system is also claimed to be portable across different LMs and to provide insights into the behavioral differences between human and artificial agents in digital environments.

1ca4456a9e1802ac9332fc984ae0df83980629f5.title: Label differential privacy via clustering
1ca4456a9e1802ac9332fc984ae0df83980629f5.research_question: How can the privacy of training labels in machine learning datasets be protected while maintaining high model utility, particularly when only the labels (and not features) are considered sensitive? What mechanisms can be developed to achieve label differential privacy efficiently in both centralized and distributed (peer-to-peer) settings, and how do these mechanisms compare to existing approaches in terms of privacy-utility trade-offs?
1ca4456a9e1802ac9332fc984ae0df83980629f5.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that clustering examples based on non-private features and applying cluster-based label randomization can significantly improve the privacy-utility trade-off for label differential privacy, outperforming uniform randomized response and standard differentially private stochastic gradient descent (DP-SGD), especially when clusters are large and have low heterogeneity.
1ca4456a9e1802ac9332fc984ae0df83980629f5.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces two mechanisms for achieving label differential privacy: a centralized mechanism and a peer-to-peer distributed mechanism. In the centralized approach, examples are clustered using their non-private feature vectors. Within each cluster, empirical label distributions are computed and perturbed with Laplace noise. Labels are then randomized by resampling from the noisy cluster label distribution, and a modified loss function is constructed to correct for the bias introduced by label randomization. In the peer-to-peer setting, each user adds noise to their own label, then replaces it with the noisy label of a randomly selected user from the same cluster, followed by optional subsampling. The approach leverages cluster size and heterogeneity to balance privacy and utility, with theoretical guarantees on excess risk and privacy parameters. Both mechanisms are designed to be practical, relying on empirical risk minimization and simple label manipulation rather than computationally expensive procedures.
1ca4456a9e1802ac9332fc984ae0df83980629f5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard benchmark datasets including MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10. The proposed cluster-based randomized response mechanism (ClusterRR) and uniform randomized response (UniformRR) will be implemented using KMeans clustering (100 clusters per dataset) and multinomial logistic regression (SAGA solver) for classification. These methods will be compared against DP-SGD, a widely used differentially private learning algorithm. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy, excess risk, and the privacy-utility trade-off. Experimental setups will ensure that clustering is performed on unlabeled data, and that all mechanisms are evaluated under comparable privacy budgets (b) and cluster heterogeneity conditions.
1ca4456a9e1802ac9332fc984ae0df83980629f5.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel cluster-based label randomization framework for label differential privacy that generalizes randomized response by leveraging feature-based clustering. This approach provides improved privacy-utility trade-offs, particularly when clusters are large and homogeneous, and extends theoretical guarantees to multi-class settings. The centralized mechanism incorporates a modified loss function for bias correction, and the peer-to-peer mechanism achieves privacy amplification without a trusted server. Theoretical analysis establishes new upper bounds on excess risk and demonstrates the necessity of large, high-quality clusters for strong privacy and utility. Empirical results are expected to show significant improvements over uniform randomized response and DP-SGD, especially in practical, large-scale learning scenarios.

1ca5618423c64f0656d13c2bc0d387cc2006f7b2.title: ZeRO++: Extremely Efficient Collective Communication for Giant Model Training
1ca5618423c64f0656d13c2bc0d387cc2006f7b2.research_question: How can collective communication overhead in large-scale model training be significantly reduced to improve throughput and scalability, especially on low-bandwidth clusters and with small per-GPU batch sizes, without sacrificing model accuracy or usability?
1ca5618423c64f0656d13c2bc0d387cc2006f7b2.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a combination of communication volume reduction techniques—specifically, block-based quantized weight communication, hierarchical partitioning of model weights, and a novel all-to-all based quantized gradient averaging protocol—can substantially reduce the communication overhead in large-scale model training, leading to improved throughput and scalability while maintaining model convergence and accuracy.
1ca5618423c64f0656d13c2bc0d387cc2006f7b2.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a comprehensive system, ZeRO++, that integrates three key communication optimizations targeting the main collective operations in ZeRO-based distributed training. First, quantized weight communication (qwZ) applies block-based INT8 quantization to model weights during the forward all-gather, reducing communication volume by half while preserving accuracy through fine-grained quantization granularity. Second, hierarchical partitioning (hpZ) trades additional GPU memory for communication efficiency by maintaining a full replica of model weights within each node, thereby eliminating inter-node all-gather communication during the backward pass and leveraging high intra-node bandwidth. Third, a novel quantized gradient communication protocol (qgZ) replaces the standard reduce-scatter with a two-stage hierarchical all-to-all collective using block-based INT4 quantization, reducing cross-node gradient communication by 75% while ensuring full-precision reduction to avoid accuracy loss. The system further incorporates optimized CUDA kernels for quantization, dequantization, and tensor slice reordering, as well as kernel fusion and overlapping of communication and computation to minimize overhead and maximize throughput.
1ca5618423c64f0656d13c2bc0d387cc2006f7b2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on up to 384 NVIDIA V100 GPUs across 24 DGX-2 nodes, with varying inter-node InfiniBand bandwidths (from 100Gbps to 800Gbps) to simulate both low and high bandwidth scenarios. The evaluation will use GPT-style transformer models ranging from 18B to 138B parameters, with microbatch sizes of 1K and 2K tokens per GPU. Baselines will include ZeRO-3 and, for certain comparisons, MiCS. Key evaluation metrics will be sustained throughput (TFLOPs), percentage of peak GPU performance, and model convergence (measured by validation loss on the Pile dataset). Ablation studies will assess the impact of each communication optimization and kernel implementation. The experiments will also analyze memory usage, communication volume, and the effect of kernel fusion and overlapping strategies.
1ca5618423c64f0656d13c2bc0d387cc2006f7b2.novelty_claims: The proposal claims several innovations: (1) the introduction of block-based quantized weight communication that reduces all-gather communication by 50% without accuracy loss; (2) a hierarchical partitioning strategy that eliminates inter-node all-gather in the backward pass with minimal memory overhead; (3) a novel all-to-all quantized gradient communication protocol that reduces cross-node gradient communication by 75% while preserving model accuracy; (4) optimized CUDA kernels and kernel fusion for efficient quantization and communication; and (5) the first end-to-end system that achieves up to 4x reduction in communication volume for ZeRO-based training, translating into up to 2.4x throughput improvement and enabling large-scale training on low-bandwidth clusters without code refactoring.

1ca67cc763a38c9c10daf79c857e1fef17e97ecb.title: Lossy Compression with Gaussian Diffusion
1ca67cc763a38c9c10daf79c857e1fef17e97ecb.research_question: How can lossy compression be achieved with perfect realism constraints using generative models, and what are the rate-distortion trade-offs and practical performance characteristics of such an approach compared to existing state-of-the-art methods?
1ca67cc763a38c9c10daf79c857e1fef17e97ecb.hypothesis: A lossy compression framework based on unconditional Gaussian diffusion generative models, which communicates corrupted pixels directly and reconstructs data via diffusion-based denoising, can achieve state-of-the-art rate-distortion performance and perfect realism, outperforming existing generative compression schemes and traditional codecs.
1ca67cc763a38c9c10daf79c857e1fef17e97ecb.proposed_method: A novel lossy compression scheme is proposed that utilizes an unconditionally trained Gaussian diffusion generative model. The method encodes data by adding isotropic Gaussian noise directly to the pixels, producing a corrupted version of the original data. This corrupted sample is then efficiently communicated using reverse channel coding, with the number of bits required bounded by the mutual information between the original and corrupted data. At the decoder, the reconstruction is performed by either ancestral sampling (DiffC-A) or a deterministic flow-based approach (DiffC-F) that inverts the diffusion process via a probability flow ODE, leveraging the learned score function of the diffusion model. The same model supports arbitrary bitrates by varying the noise level and enables progressive decoding from partial bitstreams.
1ca67cc763a38c9c10daf79c857e1fef17e97ecb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the downsampled ImageNet 64x64 dataset, with careful deduplication to ensure a clean validation set. The proposed method (DiffC) will be compared to strong baselines including BPG (a non-neural codec) and HiFiC (a state-of-the-art GAN-based neural generative compression model), with HiFiC retrained for the specific image size and multiple target bitrates. Evaluation metrics will include FID (Fréchet Inception Distance) for perceptual quality and PSNR (Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio) for distortion, with bitrates estimated using theoretical upper bounds for the proposed coding scheme. Both ancestral and flow-based reconstructions will be evaluated across a range of bitrates, and additional experiments will assess progressive coding capabilities.
1ca67cc763a38c9c10daf79c857e1fef17e97ecb.novelty_claims: The proposed approach eliminates the need for a separate encoder transform, entropy model, and adversarial loss, relying solely on a single unconditional diffusion model for both encoding and decoding. It introduces the use of reverse channel coding for communicating exact Gaussian-corrupted samples, enabling efficient and theoretically bounded bitrates. The method supports progressive coding and arbitrary bitrate control with a single model. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the flow-based reconstruction achieves up to a 3 dB SNR gain over ancestral sampling at high bitrates, and empirical results show significant improvements in both perceptual quality and rate-distortion performance compared to existing generative and traditional codecs.

1cade8d7001579059949a36e92c0af382113c8ce.title: Training Unbiased Diffusion Models From Biased Dataset
1cade8d7001579059949a36e92c0af382113c8ce.research_question: How can diffusion models be trained to generate unbiased data distributions when only biased datasets are available, particularly under weak supervision and in the presence of latent or unannotated bias factors?
1cade8d7001579059949a36e92c0af382113c8ce.hypothesis: Time-dependent importance reweighting, utilizing a time-dependent density ratio between perturbed biased and unbiased distributions, enables diffusion models to converge to the true unbiased data distribution even when trained predominantly on biased data.
1cade8d7001579059949a36e92c0af382113c8ce.proposed_method: A novel training framework for diffusion models is proposed, leveraging time-dependent importance reweighting (TIW) to mitigate dataset bias. The method estimates a time-dependent density ratio between the perturbed biased and unbiased distributions using a neural network-based discriminator conditioned on both data and diffusion time. This density ratio is employed both as a sample reweighting factor and as a score correction term within the denoising score-matching objective, resulting in a tractable loss function. The approach theoretically guarantees equivalence to classical score-matching on the unbiased distribution and ensures convergence to the unbiased data distribution, even when only a small reference set from the unbiased distribution is available. The framework is designed to operate under weak supervision, requiring only knowledge of data origin (biased or reference) without explicit bias annotations.
1cade8d7001579059949a36e92c0af382113c8ce.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard generative modeling benchmarks, including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, FFHQ, and CelebA, with various artificially constructed and real-world bias settings. The evaluation will use the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) to measure the similarity between generated and true unbiased data distributions, and additional metrics will assess the mitigation of bias in generated samples. Baselines for comparison include naive diffusion model training on biased and reference data, as well as time-independent importance reweighting (IW-DSM). The proposed method (TIW-DSM) will be compared under identical training configurations, with ablation studies to assess the impact of reweighting and score correction components, and sensitivity analyses on density ratio scaling. Experiments will also analyze the effectiveness of the method under varying reference set sizes and bias intensities.
1cade8d7001579059949a36e92c0af382113c8ce.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first time-dependent importance reweighting framework for diffusion models, addressing the density-chasm problem in density ratio estimation by leveraging the forward diffusion process to improve estimation accuracy. The method uniquely combines time-dependent reweighting and score correction in the loss function, providing both theoretical guarantees of convergence to the unbiased distribution and empirical improvements over existing baselines. The approach is designed for weak supervision and is shown to outperform time-independent reweighting and naive baselines across diverse datasets and bias settings.

1cd8373490efc2d74c2796f4b2aa27c7d4415ec9.title: VoxPoser: Composable 3D Value Maps for Robotic Manipulation with Language Models
1cd8373490efc2d74c2796f4b2aa27c7d4415ec9.research_question: How can abstract, free-form language instructions be grounded into robust, closed-loop 3D robotic manipulation trajectories for a wide variety of tasks and objects, without relying on pre-defined motion primitives or extensive task-specific data collection?
1cd8373490efc2d74c2796f4b2aa27c7d4415ec9.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that large language models (LLMs), when combined with vision-language models (VLMs) and code-generation capabilities, can be leveraged to compose 3D value maps that encode affordances and constraints from language instructions, enabling zero-shot synthesis of robust robot manipulation trajectories for open-set tasks and objects.
1cd8373490efc2d74c2796f4b2aa27c7d4415ec9.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a framework that extracts language-conditioned affordances and constraints from large language models and grounds them in the robot's perceptual space using vision-language models. The approach prompts LLMs to generate Python code that interacts with perception APIs (e.g., open-vocabulary object detectors, segmentation models) to obtain spatial information about relevant objects or parts. This information is then used to compose dense 3D voxel value maps representing task-specific rewards and costs in the observation space. These value maps serve as objective functions for a model-based motion planner, which synthesizes closed-loop robot trajectories by optimizing over the value maps. The framework supports additional trajectory parameterizations, such as rotation, gripper actions, and velocity, and can be extended to learn environment dynamics efficiently from online experience for contact-rich tasks.
1cd8373490efc2d74c2796f4b2aa27c7d4415ec9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in both real-world and simulated environments, covering a diverse set of everyday manipulation tasks specified by open-set, free-form language instructions and involving open-set objects. The evaluation will include tasks such as opening drawers, sorting objects, and interacting with appliances. Baselines for comparison will include methods that use LLMs to parameterize pre-defined motion primitives and approaches that learn cost maps via supervised learning (e.g., U-Net-based predictors). Success rates, robustness to dynamic disturbances, and generalization to unseen instructions and object attributes will be measured. Additional experiments will assess the efficiency of dynamics model learning using zero-shot synthesized trajectories as priors, with metrics including task success rate and learning time.
1cd8373490efc2d74c2796f4b2aa27c7d4415ec9.novelty_claims: The proposed approach claims novelty in leveraging LLMs to compose dense, language-conditioned 3D value maps for robotic manipulation, enabling direct grounding of abstract instructions in the robot's observation space without additional training or reliance on pre-defined motion primitives. The method enables zero-shot, closed-loop trajectory synthesis for a broad range of manipulation tasks and demonstrates efficient dynamics learning from online experience. The framework offers significant generalization capabilities for open-set instructions and objects, outperforming existing baselines in both robustness and flexibility.

1ce81d64eefe5915c6ef9719915efa5f4079a6c1.title: Deformable 3D Gaussians for High-Fidelity Monocular Dynamic Scene Reconstruction
1ce81d64eefe5915c6ef9719915efa5f4079a6c1.research_question: How can high-fidelity, real-time reconstruction and rendering of monocular dynamic scenes be achieved from a set of multi-view images and camera poses, overcoming the limitations of existing implicit neural representations in terms of detail, speed, and robustness to pose inaccuracies?
1ce81d64eefe5915c6ef9719915efa5f4079a6c1.hypothesis: A deformable 3D Gaussian splatting framework, which models dynamic scenes by learning 3D Gaussians in canonical space and leveraging a deformation field, can outperform existing implicit and hybrid neural rendering methods in both rendering quality and speed for monocular dynamic scene reconstruction, while also providing robustness to pose inaccuracies through an annealing smoothing training mechanism.
1ce81d64eefe5915c6ef9719915efa5f4079a6c1.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that represents dynamic scenes using a set of 3D Gaussians, each parameterized by position, rotation, scale, and opacity, and learns these Gaussians in a canonical space. A deformation field, modeled by a multi-layer perceptron (MLP), takes as input the spatial position and time (with positional encoding) and outputs offsets to the canonical Gaussians, enabling them to deform over time. The method employs a differentiable Gaussian rasterization pipeline to render 2D images from the deformed 3D Gaussians, allowing for efficient joint optimization of both the Gaussian parameters and the deformation field. An adaptive density control mechanism is implemented to prune or densify Gaussians as needed, ensuring geometric detail and efficient rendering. Additionally, an annealing smoothing training (AST) mechanism is introduced, injecting decaying Gaussian noise into the time input during early training to mitigate the effects of pose inaccuracies and improve temporal smoothness without extra computational overhead.
1ce81d64eefe5915c6ef9719915efa5f4079a6c1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets, including the D-NeRF synthetic dataset and real-world datasets from HyperNeRF and NeRF-DS. The evaluation will use standard metrics such as PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS to assess rendering quality, with all methods tested at full image resolution (800x800). Baselines for comparison include 3D-GS, D-NeRF, TiNeuVox, Tensor4D, K-Planes, HyperNeRF, and NeRF-DS. The experimental setup will involve training for 40k iterations with a warm-up phase for the Gaussians, followed by joint optimization, and all experiments will be performed on an NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPU. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of the annealing smoothing training mechanism and positional encoding choices.
1ce81d64eefe5915c6ef9719915efa5f4079a6c1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to extend 3D Gaussian splatting to dynamic scenes via a deformation field, enabling the learning of 3D Gaussians in canonical space for monocular dynamic scene reconstruction. The method introduces a novel annealing smoothing training mechanism that ensures temporal smoothness and robustness to pose inaccuracies without increasing computational complexity. The framework achieves real-time rendering speeds and high-fidelity scene reconstruction, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines in both synthetic and real-world settings. The explicit point-based representation also enhances editability and post-production flexibility compared to implicit methods.

1d0a9158accfa497d3bf25b2dbb47172afd7bdfa.title: Mixed Autoencoder for Self-Supervised Visual Representation Learning
1d0a9158accfa497d3bf25b2dbb47172afd7bdfa.research_question: How can data augmentation strategies, specifically image mixing, be effectively integrated into masked image modeling frameworks to improve self-supervised visual representation learning for various downstream vision tasks?
1d0a9158accfa497d3bf25b2dbb47172afd7bdfa.hypothesis: Incorporating a homologous recognition pretext task into a mixed autoencoder framework will mitigate the negative effects of naive image mixing in masked image modeling, leading to more effective and object-aware self-supervised visual representations that outperform existing methods on downstream tasks.
1d0a9158accfa497d3bf25b2dbb47172afd7bdfa.proposed_method: A novel self-supervised learning framework, termed Mixed Autoencoder (MixedAE), will be developed by integrating image mixing augmentation into a masked autoencoder architecture. The method will introduce an auxiliary pretext task called homologous recognition, where each patch in a mixed image is required to explicitly recognize homologous patches (i.e., patches originating from the same source image) using a TopK-based attention mechanism. The encoder processes mixed samples, and homologous attention is applied to enforce each patch to attend only to its homologous counterparts, while a homologous contrastive loss encourages the similarity of homologous patch features and dissimilarity of heterologous ones. The decoder reconstructs the original images from unmixed encoder features. The overall training objective is a weighted sum of the standard reconstruction loss and the homologous contrastive loss, enabling object-aware representation learning without additional specialized modules.
1d0a9158accfa497d3bf25b2dbb47172afd7bdfa.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale and diverse datasets, including ImageNet-1K for image classification, ADE20K for semantic segmentation, and COCO for object detection and instance segmentation. The proposed MixedAE will be compared against strong baselines such as MAE, BEiT, MixMIM, CIM, and iBOT, using standard Vision Transformer (ViT) backbones. Evaluation metrics will include Top-1 accuracy for classification, mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) for segmentation, and Average Precision (AP) for detection and segmentation tasks. Ablation studies will be performed to analyze the effects of mixing ratio, attention mechanism, and loss components. Additional transfer learning experiments will be conducted on 11 downstream classification datasets to assess the generalizability of the learned representations.
1d0a9158accfa497d3bf25b2dbb47172afd7bdfa.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to systematically incorporate image mixing as a data augmentation strategy for masked image modeling from the perspective of pretext task design. The introduction of homologous recognition as an auxiliary task addresses the mutual information increase caused by naive mixing, enabling object-aware self-supervised pre-training without specifically designed modules. MixedAE achieves state-of-the-art transfer performance among masked image modeling augmentations, with significant efficiency gains and improved results on dense perception tasks. The method also provides theoretical insights into the differences between mixing in supervised, contrastive, and masked image modeling frameworks.

1d3539a8d94bd3ab78993d7cc584efc06ed0e460.title: Synthetic Benchmarks for Scientific Research in Explainable Machine Learning
1d3539a8d94bd3ab78993d7cc584efc06ed0e460.research_question: How can the evaluation and benchmarking of feature attribution methods in explainable machine learning be made more efficient, reliable, and comprehensive, especially in the absence of ground-truth explanations in real-world datasets?
1d3539a8d94bd3ab78993d7cc584efc06ed0e460.hypothesis: Synthetic datasets with configurable parameters and known ground-truth distributions can enable efficient, accurate, and flexible benchmarking of feature attribution methods across a wide range of evaluation metrics, potentially revealing failure modes and improving the robustness of explainability techniques.
1d3539a8d94bd3ab78993d7cc584efc06ed0e460.proposed_method: A suite of synthetic datasets will be developed, each with configurable parameters such as feature distribution (e.g., multivariate Gaussian, mixture of Gaussians, multinomial), feature correlation, and label generation functions (e.g., linear, piecewise constant, nonlinear additive, piecewise linear). These datasets will be paired with a benchmarking library that enables efficient computation of conditional expectations and exact ground-truth Shapley values, as well as other empirical evaluation metrics such as faithfulness, monotonicity, remove-and-retrain (ROAR), and infidelity. The methodology includes the ability to simulate real-world datasets by estimating empirical covariances and generating synthetic analogs, allowing for controlled experiments on data realism and robustness. The library will provide APIs for researchers to benchmark new or existing explainability algorithms under a variety of data and model conditions, and will support both observational and interventional conditional expectations for metric computation.
1d3539a8d94bd3ab78993d7cc584efc06ed0e460.experiment_details: Experiments will benchmark a diverse set of feature attribution methods (e.g., SHAP, SHAPR, Kernel SHAP, LIME, MAPLE, L2X, breakDown, and a random baseline) across multiple synthetic datasets with varying feature correlations, dataset types, and machine learning models (such as linear regression, decision trees, and multilayer perceptrons). Evaluation will be conducted using five key metrics: faithfulness, monotonicity, ROAR, GT-Shapley, and infidelity. The experimental setup includes parameter sweeps over feature correlation (rho), dataset type, and model class, with results averaged over multiple trials. Additionally, real-world datasets (such as wine quality and forest fires) will be simulated using synthetic data generated from empirical statistics, and the similarity between real and synthetic distributions will be quantified using metrics like Jensen-Shannon Divergence. Performance of explainers on these simulated datasets will be compared using the same suite of evaluation metrics.
1d3539a8d94bd3ab78993d7cc584efc06ed0e460.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a comprehensive library of synthetic datasets with known ground-truth distributions and configurable parameters, enabling exact and efficient computation of multiple evaluation metrics for feature attribution methods. Unlike prior work, this approach supports a broader range of metrics (including exact Shapley values and ROAR), allows for controlled simulation of real-world data, and facilitates systematic identification of explainer failure modes (e.g., sensitivity to feature correlation). The library is designed to accelerate the development and deployment of robust explainability methods by providing a flexible, extensible, and open-source benchmarking platform.

1d36dd3d333659d72df8eb5666edfd5cde54c84f.title: Stop Regressing: Training Value Functions via Classification for Scalable Deep RL
1d36dd3d333659d72df8eb5666edfd5cde54c84f.research_question: Can the scalability and performance of deep reinforcement learning (RL) methods be improved by replacing traditional regression-based value function training with a classification-based approach, particularly when using large neural network architectures such as Transformers, ResNets, and Mixture-of-Experts?
1d36dd3d333659d72df8eb5666edfd5cde54c84f.hypothesis: Training value functions in deep RL using categorical cross-entropy classification losses, rather than mean squared error regression, will yield improved performance, robustness, and scalability, especially as model capacity increases.
1d36dd3d333659d72df8eb5666edfd5cde54c84f.proposed_method: A new approach is developed that frames value function learning in deep RL as a classification problem rather than a regression problem. The method replaces the mean squared error (MSE) loss typically used for temporal difference (TD) learning with a categorical cross-entropy loss. Value targets are represented as categorical distributions over a fixed set of bins, with several strategies for constructing these distributions: (1) Two-Hot encoding, which places probability mass on the two nearest bins; (2) HL-Gauss, which uses a Gaussian distribution centered at the TD target and projects it onto the bins, effectively smoothing the label; and (3) a distributional RL approach (C51), which models the full return distribution and projects it onto the categorical support. The neural network outputs logits for each bin, and the expected value is computed as the mean of the resulting categorical distribution. The cross-entropy loss is then minimized between the predicted and target distributions, with hyperparameters such as bin width and Gaussian variance tuned for optimal smoothing.
1d36dd3d333659d72df8eb5666edfd5cde54c84f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a diverse set of RL domains, including single-task and multi-task Atari 2600 games (both online and offline RL), language-agent tasks (Wordle), chess (distilling Stockfish evaluations into a Transformer), and large-scale robotic manipulation tasks. For Atari, both DQN and IMPALA architectures will be used, scaling from standard CNNs to large ResNets and Mixture-of-Experts (SoftMoE) modules. Transformers with up to 270M parameters will be tested on language and chess tasks. Baselines will include standard regression-based (MSE) value function training and, where applicable, distributional RL (C51) and one-hot classification targets. Evaluation metrics will include interquartile mean (IQM) normalized scores, human-normalized scores, success rates, and accuracy on held-out tasks or puzzles. Multiple random seeds and extensive hyperparameter sweeps (e.g., for label smoothing) will ensure robustness of results.
1d36dd3d333659d72df8eb5666edfd5cde54c84f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a simple yet powerful shift from regression to classification for value function training in deep RL, enabling reliable scaling to high-capacity neural networks such as Transformers and large ResNets. The HL-Gauss cross-entropy loss, in particular, is claimed to outperform both standard regression and existing distributional RL methods across a wide range of domains and architectures. The approach is positioned as a 'drop-in' replacement for regression losses, requiring minimal changes to existing RL algorithms while yielding substantial gains in performance, stability, and scalability. The method also provides new insights into the benefits of classification losses in mitigating issues like noisy targets and non-stationarity in RL.

1d603b03bb083a2c3e2e3b6f116cf196d637e6b6.title: Label-Free Concept Bottleneck Models
1d603b03bb083a2c3e2e3b6f116cf196d637e6b6.research_question: How can interpretable neural network models be constructed without requiring labeled concept data, while maintaining high predictive accuracy and scalability to large and complex datasets?
1d603b03bb083a2c3e2e3b6f116cf196d637e6b6.hypothesis: It is possible to transform any neural network into an interpretable concept bottleneck model without the need for labeled concept data, by leveraging large language models and multimodal foundation models, and that such models can achieve accuracy comparable to standard neural networks.
1d603b03bb083a2c3e2e3b6f116cf196d637e6b6.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a label-free framework for constructing Concept Bottleneck Models (CBMs) that does not require labeled concept data. The approach begins by automatically generating an initial set of human-interpretable concepts for each class using GPT-3, followed by filtering to remove redundant, irrelevant, or overly similar concepts via embedding-based similarity measures and activation thresholds. Next, the method learns a projection from the neural network backbone's feature space to the concept space using CLIP-Dissect, optimizing projection weights to maximize the correlation between neuron activations and target concepts through a differentiable similarity function (coscubed similarity). After filtering out uninterpretable concepts, a sparse linear predictor is trained on top of the concept bottleneck layer using an elastic net objective, ensuring interpretability and efficiency. The entire process is automated, scalable, and can be applied to any neural network architecture.
1d603b03bb083a2c3e2e3b6f116cf196d637e6b6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five diverse datasets: CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, CUB-200, Places365, and ImageNet, covering general image classification, fine-grained species recognition, and scene recognition tasks. The method will be evaluated using standard backbone architectures such as CLIP (RN50) and ResNet-18/50, with the number of concepts proportional to the number of output classes. Baselines for comparison will include standard neural networks (with and without sparse final layers) and existing CBM variants, including post-hoc CBMs and those using expert-provided concept sets. Evaluation metrics will focus on classification accuracy, interpretability of decision rules (via visualization of final layer weights), and the ability to explain individual predictions. Training efficiency, scalability, and the impact of manual model editing will also be assessed.
1d603b03bb083a2c3e2e3b6f116cf196d637e6b6.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to enable fully automated, label-free construction of Concept Bottleneck Models that scale to large datasets such as ImageNet. It eliminates the need for human-annotated concept labels by leveraging large language models for concept generation and multimodal foundation models for concept alignment. The method achieves high accuracy comparable to standard neural networks while providing fully interpretable decision rules and supporting manual model editing for debugging and improvement. The approach is efficient, requiring minimal human intervention and enabling rapid deployment across diverse tasks and architectures.

1d6d84463357d635a537093c9bae12d5ab78a6be.title: ViSpec: Accelerating Vision-Language Models with Vision-Aware Speculative Decoding
1d6d84463357d635a537093c9bae12d5ab78a6be.research_question: How can inference acceleration for vision-language models (VLMs) be substantially improved through speculative decoding techniques, while maintaining high multimodal generation quality across diverse tasks and model architectures?
1d6d84463357d635a537093c9bae12d5ab78a6be.hypothesis: Incorporating vision-aware mechanisms—specifically, compressed image embedding integration and persistent global visual feature augmentation—into speculative decoding frameworks will enable shallow draft models to efficiently process multimodal sequences, resulting in significant inference speedup for VLMs without loss of output quality.
1d6d84463357d635a537093c9bae12d5ab78a6be.proposed_method: A novel speculative decoding framework, Vision-Aware Speculative Decoding (ViSpec), will be developed for VLMs. The approach introduces a lightweight vision adaptor module inspired by Q-Former, which compresses high-dimensional image tokens into a compact set of visual embeddings using a Transformer encoder with fixed learnable query vectors. These compressed tokens are integrated into the draft model's attention mechanism, preserving the original image's positional information. Additionally, a global visual feature vector is extracted from the compressed image tokens and injected into the hidden states of all subsequent text tokens during generation, ensuring persistent access to holistic visual context. The training strategy involves generating synthetic multimodal datasets with extended assistant responses by repurposing and augmenting existing datasets, and employing multi-token prediction with randomized target model sampling to prevent shortcut learning and overfitting.
1d6d84463357d635a537093c9bae12d5ab78a6be.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four open-source VLMs: LLaVA-v1.6-Vicuna-7B, LLaVA-v1.6-Vicuna-13B, Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, using their official weights and configurations. The method will be evaluated on eight multimodal benchmarks, including ScienceQA, MM-Vet, MME, TextVQA, COCO Captions, VizWiz, GQA, and SEED-Bench, covering tasks such as visual question answering and image captioning. Baseline comparisons will include Medusa and EAGLE-2, adapted for multimodal input. Evaluation metrics will focus on acceleration performance, specifically average acceptance length (number of tokens accepted per speculative cycle) and speedup ratio (relative to standard autoregressive decoding). Draft models will be trained in two stages: initial text-only pretraining on ShareGPT, followed by multimodal fine-tuning with both original and synthetically-extended datasets.
1d6d84463357d635a537093c9bae12d5ab78a6be.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to achieve substantial and practical inference acceleration for VLMs through speculative decoding, surpassing previous approaches that yielded only marginal speedups. Key innovations include the integration of a vision adaptor for image token compression, persistent global visual feature augmentation for enhanced multimodal coherence, and a synthetic dataset generation strategy for long-response multimodal tasks. Ablation studies will demonstrate the synergistic contributions of these components, establishing a new state-of-the-art for speculative decoding in vision-language models.

1d803f07e4591bd67c358eef715bcd443e821894.title: BC-Z: Zero-Shot Task Generalization with Robotic Imitation Learning
1d803f07e4591bd67c358eef715bcd443e821894.research_question: How can a vision-based robotic manipulation system be enabled to generalize to novel tasks without requiring additional demonstrations for those tasks, particularly through scalable and flexible imitation learning approaches?
1d803f07e4591bd67c358eef715bcd443e821894.hypothesis: A large-scale, interactive imitation learning system that conditions on flexible task specifications—such as natural language commands or videos of humans—will enable a robot to generalize zero-shot or few-shot to new, unseen manipulation tasks, even when those tasks involve novel combinations of objects and actions.
1d803f07e4591bd67c358eef715bcd443e821894.proposed_method: A multi-task imitation learning framework will be developed that collects a large-scale dataset of robot demonstrations and human videos across a diverse set of manipulation tasks using a VR-based teleoperation system with shared autonomy. The policy will be conditioned on task specifications provided as either natural language or human demonstration videos, using a modular architecture with a task encoder (for language or video) and a visuomotor control policy. Pre-trained sentence encoders will be used for language commands, while a ResNet-18-based convolutional network will process video inputs, with an auxiliary language regression loss to align video and language embeddings. The control policy will be trained with behavior cloning, using state differences as actions and open-loop auxiliary predictions to improve robustness and interpretability.
1d803f07e4591bd67c358eef715bcd443e821894.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a real robot platform using a dataset of 25,877 demonstrations spanning 100 diverse manipulation tasks, with additional 18,726 human videos for the same tasks. The system will be evaluated on 29 held-out tasks, including both tasks with new object combinations and tasks requiring cross-object set generalization. Baselines will include single-task policies, multi-task policies without adaptive state differences, and policies trained with and without HG-DAgger (human-gated DAgger) interventions. Evaluation metrics will include task success rate, intervention rate during shared autonomy, and qualitative analysis of policy behavior. Ablation studies will assess the impact of multi-task training, adaptive state differences, and the use of HG-DAgger.
1d803f07e4591bd67c358eef715bcd443e821894.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a scalable imitation learning system capable of zero-shot task generalization to entirely new manipulation tasks based on natural language or video commands, without requiring robot demonstrations for those tasks. The method leverages a combination of shared autonomy data collection, flexible task conditioning, and large-scale multi-task training to achieve generalization across a wide range of skills and objects. The integration of pre-trained language embeddings and an auxiliary language regression loss for video encoders is claimed to facilitate the organization of the task embedding space and improve generalization. The system is empirically validated on a uniquely large and diverse real-world dataset, demonstrating significant advances in zero-shot robotic task generalization.

1d82f61ee52331a94141a50b59b186ccf105f6a9.title: Building Math Agents with Multi-Turn Iterative Preference Learning
1d82f61ee52331a94141a50b59b186ccf105f6a9.research_question: How can large language models be effectively trained to solve complex mathematical reasoning tasks that require multi-turn interactions and integration with external tools, leveraging preference learning beyond traditional supervised fine-tuning and synthetic data generation?
1d82f61ee52331a94141a50b59b186ccf105f6a9.hypothesis: Incorporating multi-turn, trajectory-level preference learning—especially with online iterative training and feedback from external tools—will significantly improve the mathematical problem-solving abilities of large language models compared to models trained solely with supervised fine-tuning or single-turn preference learning.
1d82f61ee52331a94141a50b59b186ccf105f6a9.proposed_method: A novel multi-turn online iterative direct preference learning framework will be developed for training large language models in mathematical problem-solving tasks that require both intrinsic reasoning and external tool usage. The method will formalize the learning process as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), enabling trajectory-level preference optimization rather than single-turn feedback. The approach will derive and implement multi-turn variants of direct preference learning algorithms, such as Multi-turn DPO (M-DPO) and Multi-turn KTO (M-KTO), which incorporate external tool feedback and mask out irrelevant tokens during training. Online iterative training will be employed, where the model generates new trajectories and updates its policy in cycles, allowing for continual improvement based on preference signals derived from final answer checking, outcome-supervised reward models, or process-supervised reward models. The framework will also address the deterministic nature of tool-integrated environments, ensuring that the preference learning loss is unbiased and optimal for these settings.
1d82f61ee52331a94141a50b59b186ccf105f6a9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using augmented prompt sets derived from the GSM8K and MATH datasets, which are standard benchmarks for mathematical reasoning. Various base models, including Gemma-1.1-it-7B, Gemma-2-it-9B, CodeGemma, and Mistral, will be trained and evaluated. Baseline comparisons will include supervised fine-tuned models and models trained with traditional single-turn preference learning algorithms. Evaluation metrics will focus on accuracy of final answers on GSM8K and MATH, with additional analysis of trajectory quality and error rates. The experimental setup will involve both offline and online iterative training regimes, and ablation studies will be performed to isolate the impact of multi-turn preference learning and tool integration.
1d82f61ee52331a94141a50b59b186ccf105f6a9.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first comprehensive multi-turn direct preference learning framework tailored for tool-integrated mathematical reasoning in large language models. Key innovations include the derivation of multi-turn DPO and KTO algorithms for trajectory-level preference optimization, rigorous handling of deterministic tool feedback, and the integration of online iterative training in a multi-turn setting. The approach extends preference learning beyond single-turn chat tasks, enabling more effective alignment of LLMs with complex reasoning objectives and external tool usage. The framework is expected to set new performance benchmarks on standard mathematical reasoning datasets and provide a practical recipe for future research in agent-based LLM training.

1dbd58bd8768ba0dada2e7c84aa2fe0b9f418ebc.title: Solving Challenging Math Word Problems Using GPT-4 Code Interpreter with Code-based Self-Verification
1dbd58bd8768ba0dada2e7c84aa2fe0b9f418ebc.research_question: How can the mathematical reasoning and problem-solving abilities of large language models be further enhanced, particularly in solving challenging math word problems, by leveraging code generation, execution, and self-verification mechanisms?
1dbd58bd8768ba0dada2e7c84aa2fe0b9f418ebc.hypothesis: Incorporating explicit code-based self-verification and verification-guided weighted majority voting into large language models with code execution capabilities will significantly improve their accuracy and reliability in solving complex mathematical word problems compared to existing prompting and verification strategies.
1dbd58bd8768ba0dada2e7c84aa2fe0b9f418ebc.proposed_method: A novel prompting framework will be developed that explicitly instructs a code-capable large language model (such as GPT-4 Code Interpreter) to not only generate step-by-step code solutions for math word problems, but also to verify its final answers through additional code-based checks. If the verification fails (i.e., the answer is marked as False), the model will be prompted to automatically revise its reasoning and solution, iterating until a verified solution is found or an uncertain state is reached. The verification outcome (True, False, or Uncertain) will be recorded for each solution path. To further enhance answer reliability, a verification-guided weighted majority voting mechanism will be introduced, where multiple solution paths are sampled, and each answer is assigned a voting weight based on its verification status (e.g., True > Uncertain > False). The final answer will be selected based on the highest weighted score, thereby integrating both solution diversity and verification confidence.
1dbd58bd8768ba0dada2e7c84aa2fe0b9f418ebc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several challenging math word problem datasets, including MATH, GSM8K, and MMLU-Math. The proposed method will be evaluated in a zero-shot setting using GPT-4 Code Interpreter as the base model. Baseline comparisons will include standard GPT-4, GPT-3.5, chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting, program-aided language models (PAL), and previous code-based approaches without explicit self-verification. Evaluation metrics will focus on accuracy across overall and subtopic-specific benchmarks. The experimental setup will also include ablation studies on code usage frequency, the impact of code-based versus natural language self-verification, and hyperparameter tuning for the weighted majority voting scheme. The number of sampled solution paths (e.g., k=16) and the weights assigned to verification outcomes will be systematically varied to assess their effect on performance.
1dbd58bd8768ba0dada2e7c84aa2fe0b9f418ebc.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first systematic analysis of code generation, execution, and self-debugging mechanisms in mathematical problem-solving with LLMs. It pioneers an explicit code-based self-verification (CSV) prompting strategy that enables autonomous answer verification and correction within a single model, without reliance on external verifiers or few-shot examples. The verification-guided weighted majority voting framework further innovates by integrating verification confidence into the answer aggregation process, leading to substantial improvements in accuracy and reliability. Additionally, the creation of new instruction-following datasets with detailed code-based solutions is expected to facilitate future research and fine-tuning of open-source models.

1dc6c476e6a48cf9c11dc1307de2b844fb1824ba.title: Hard Patches Mining for Masked Image Modeling
1dc6c476e6a48cf9c11dc1307de2b844fb1824ba.research_question: How can masked image modeling (MIM) be enhanced by enabling models to not only solve given reconstruction tasks but also autonomously generate more challenging pretext tasks, thereby improving learned visual representations?
1dc6c476e6a48cf9c11dc1307de2b844fb1824ba.hypothesis: Empowering a model to identify and mask 'hard' patches—those that are more difficult to reconstruct—during MIM pre-training, rather than relying solely on pre-defined or random mask strategies, will lead to richer and more transferable visual representations for downstream tasks.
1dc6c476e6a48cf9c11dc1307de2b844fb1824ba.proposed_method: A novel training framework, Hard Patches Mining (HPM), is proposed for masked image modeling. The method introduces both a student and a teacher network, each composed of an encoder, an image reconstructor, and a loss predictor. During each training iteration, the teacher network predicts patch-wise reconstruction losses for an input image, which are then used to generate a binary mask that preferentially selects the most challenging (hard) patches to be masked. The student is then trained to reconstruct these masked patches and to predict the relative reconstruction loss for each patch. The loss predictor is optimized using a binary cross-entropy objective that focuses on the relative difficulty between patches, rather than absolute loss values, to avoid overfitting and to encourage learning of discriminative features. An easy-to-hard mask generation schedule is employed, gradually increasing the proportion of hard patches masked as training progresses.
1dc6c476e6a48cf9c11dc1307de2b844fb1824ba.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard computer vision benchmarks, including ImageNet-1K for classification, COCO for object detection and instance segmentation, and ADE20k for semantic segmentation. The main backbone will be Vision Transformer (ViT) architectures (e.g., ViT-B/16 and ViT-L). Baselines will include conventional MIM methods such as MAE, BEiT, SimMIM, and contrastive learning methods like MoCo v3 and DINO. Evaluation metrics will include Top-1 accuracy for classification, AP for detection/segmentation, and mIoU for semantic segmentation. Ablation studies will explore the effects of different mask strategies, loss formulations (absolute vs. relative), reconstruction targets (pixels vs. features), and the easy-to-hard masking schedule. The experimental setup will ensure consistent input resolutions and training epochs for fair comparison.
1dc6c476e6a48cf9c11dc1307de2b844fb1824ba.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to explicitly integrate a loss predictor for patch-wise reconstruction difficulty into the MIM pre-training loop, enabling the model to act as both a teacher and a student. This approach introduces a dynamic, learnable mask generation mechanism that adaptively focuses on the most challenging regions of an image, rather than relying on fixed or random mask patterns. The use of a relative loss prediction objective further distinguishes the method by emphasizing inter-patch difficulty relationships, and the easy-to-hard masking schedule provides a principled way to increase task difficulty over time. The method is demonstrated to be plug-and-play, improving performance across a variety of MIM targets and downstream tasks.

1dd20f5d548555a863164824ef225b27f8ff8f8d.title: R-Bench: Graduate-level Multi-disciplinary Benchmarks for LLM & MLLM Complex Reasoning Evaluation
1dd20f5d548555a863164824ef225b27f8ff8f8d.research_question: How can a comprehensive, graduate-level, multi-disciplinary benchmark be developed to rigorously evaluate the complex reasoning abilities of both large language models (LLMs) and multimodal large language models (MLLMs) across multiple languages and modalities?
1dd20f5d548555a863164824ef225b27f8ff8f8d.hypothesis: A benchmark that is multi-disciplinary, multimodal, and multilingual, with carefully calibrated difficulty and rigorous filtering, will provide a more challenging and discriminative evaluation of complex reasoning skills in LLMs and MLLMs than existing benchmarks, revealing current limitations and guiding future model improvements.
1dd20f5d548555a863164824ef225b27f8ff8f8d.proposed_method: A new benchmark, R-Bench, will be constructed by collecting reasoning-focused questions from over 100 graduate-level courses across 19 departments, ensuring coverage of a wide range of disciplines. The question collection process will involve recruiting 51 experts from various fields to curate and filter out knowledge-based or memory-recall questions, focusing only on those requiring deep reasoning. The dataset will be digitized, standardized, and further filtered through three rounds: expert review, model-based filtering using reasoning token counts from a leading LLM, and manual review for completeness, clarity, and subject balance. All questions will be converted to single-choice format with six options, and each will be translated and validated in both English and Chinese. The benchmark will include both text-only and multimodal (text + image) questions, enabling evaluation of both LLMs and MLLMs.
1dd20f5d548555a863164824ef225b27f8ff8f8d.experiment_details: Experiments will involve evaluating a diverse set of both proprietary and open-source LLMs and MLLMs (e.g., OpenAI o1, GPT-4o, DeepSeek-R1, Gemini, Claude, Qwen2.5, Llama3, etc.) on the R-Bench benchmark in both English and Chinese. Models will be tested in zero-shot settings, with and without chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting, using official APIs or local deployment with standardized parameters. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy, reasoning time (tokens), and consistency across languages. Baselines such as MMLU and MMMU will be used for comparison, and expert/user studies will be conducted to validate the benchmark's difficulty and reasoning requirements. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by using default hyperparameters and consistent evaluation protocols across all models.
1dd20f5d548555a863164824ef225b27f8ff8f8d.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark is the first to combine graduate-level, multi-disciplinary, multimodal, and multilingual reasoning evaluation in a single, rigorously curated dataset. It addresses the limitations of existing benchmarks that are either saturated or lack coverage in modality or language. The benchmark introduces a systematic multi-stage filtering process to ensure high difficulty and subject balance, and provides both English and Chinese versions for each question. R-Bench enables more discriminative assessment of advanced models' reasoning abilities, particularly in complex and real-world problem-solving scenarios, and reveals significant gaps in current model performance, especially in multimodal and cross-lingual reasoning.

1dd7abaa839bc69b27bc5bdeb99a8e65ba47feff.title: Second-Order Fine-Tuning without Pain for LLMs: A Hessian Informed Zeroth-Order Optimizer
1dd7abaa839bc69b27bc5bdeb99a8e65ba47feff.research_question: How can fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) be made more memory-efficient and stable, particularly in the presence of heterogeneous parameter curvatures, without relying on first-order gradient information?
1dd7abaa839bc69b27bc5bdeb99a8e65ba47feff.hypothesis: Incorporating diagonal Hessian information into a zeroth-order optimizer will improve convergence speed and model accuracy during LLM fine-tuning, while maintaining low memory usage.
1dd7abaa839bc69b27bc5bdeb99a8e65ba47feff.proposed_method: A novel diagonal Hessian-informed zeroth-order optimizer (HiZOO) is proposed for fine-tuning large language models. The method estimates the diagonal of the Hessian matrix using an additional forward pass per optimization step, enabling curvature-aware parameter updates without requiring backpropagation. The optimizer leverages stochastic perturbations and exponential moving average (EMA) to denoise the Hessian estimates, maintaining O(d) memory complexity. Additionally, a low-rank variant (HiZOO-L) is introduced, which further reduces Hessian memory consumption to 10% of comparable methods by maintaining the Hessian in a low-rank subspace, inspired by Adafactor. Theoretical analysis is provided to guarantee unbiased Hessian estimation and convergence properties.
1dd7abaa839bc69b27bc5bdeb99a8e65ba47feff.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of LLMs, including RoBERTa-large (350M), Phi-2 (2.7B), Llama3 (8B), OPT (13B, 30B, 66B), and across various downstream tasks such as classification, multiple-choice, and generation. Both full-parameter fine-tuning and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA, prefix-tuning) will be evaluated. Baselines will include first-order optimizers (Adam, AdamW), zeroth-order optimizers (MeZO, ZO-SGD, ZO-Adam, and other ZO variants), and memory-efficient approaches. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, F1 score (for non-differentiable objectives), convergence speed (number of steps to target loss/accuracy), memory usage, and wall-clock time. Multiple runs will be averaged for robustness, and both differentiable and non-differentiable objectives will be tested.
1dd7abaa839bc69b27bc5bdeb99a8e65ba47feff.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first zeroth-order optimizer for LLM fine-tuning that leverages diagonal Hessian information, enabling curvature-aware updates without backpropagation. The method achieves significant reductions in training steps and improves model accuracy compared to existing zeroth-order and first-order methods. The low-rank variant (HiZOO-L) further reduces memory consumption, allowing fine-tuning of much larger models on the same hardware. The approach is theoretically grounded with convergence guarantees and is empirically validated across a wide range of models, tasks, and settings, including non-differentiable objectives.

1ddbd08ad8cf22a5c66c4242194c4286328533bf.title: MiniGPT-v2: large language model as a unified interface for vision-language multi-task learning
1ddbd08ad8cf22a5c66c4242194c4286328533bf.research_question: How can a single large language model be designed to serve as a unified interface for a broad range of vision-language multi-task learning scenarios, such as image description, visual question answering, visual grounding, and related tasks, using simple multi-modal instructions?
1ddbd08ad8cf22a5c66c4242194c4286328533bf.hypothesis: Introducing explicit task identifiers into the training of a unified vision-language model will improve its ability to distinguish and perform diverse vision-language tasks efficiently, resulting in state-of-the-art or competitive performance across multiple benchmarks.
1ddbd08ad8cf22a5c66c4242194c4286328533bf.proposed_method: A unified vision-language model will be developed by integrating a frozen high-capacity ViT-based visual backbone (EVA) with a large language model (LLaMA-2-chat, 7B parameters) via a linear projection layer. Visual features from high-resolution images (448x448) will be extracted, and adjacent visual tokens will be concatenated to reduce sequence length and improve efficiency. The model will be trained using a multi-task instruction template that incorporates explicit task identifier tokens (e.g., [vqa], [caption], [grounding]) to disambiguate task intent. Training will proceed in three stages: (1) pretraining on a mixture of weakly-labeled and fine-grained image-text datasets, (2) focused multi-task training on high-quality, fine-grained datasets, and (3) multi-modal instruction tuning with conversational and instructional datasets to enhance chatbot and multi-task capabilities. The language model will be fine-tuned using LoRA for parameter-efficient adaptation.
1ddbd08ad8cf22a5c66c4242194c4286328533bf.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a wide range of vision-language tasks, including visual question answering (VQA), image captioning, grounded captioning, referring expression comprehension (REC), referring expression generation (REG), and object parsing/grounding. Datasets used will include LAION, CC3M, SBU, GRIT-20M, COCO Caption, Text Captions, RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, RefCOCOg, GQA, VQA-v2, OCR-VQA, OK-VQA, AOK-VQA, LLaVA, Flickr30k, and Unnatural Instructions. Baselines for comparison will include MiniGPT-4, InstructBLIP, LLaVA, Shikra, OFA, and specialist models like UNINEXT and G-DINO. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy for VQA, IOU-based accuracy for visual grounding, and CHAIR scores for hallucination assessment. The model will be trained and evaluated using multi-modal instruction templates, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of task identifiers.
1ddbd08ad8cf22a5c66c4242194c4286328533bf.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified multi-modal large language model that leverages explicit task identifier tokens to resolve multi-task ambiguity and improve learning efficiency. The method enables efficient high-resolution image processing through visual token concatenation and supports a broad spectrum of vision-language tasks within a single model. The three-stage training strategy, including targeted instruction tuning and conversational data, enhances both task performance and chatbot capabilities. The approach achieves state-of-the-art or competitive results on multiple vision-language benchmarks and demonstrates reduced hallucination compared to prior models, validating the effectiveness of task-oriented instruction training.

1df2b4378938361788aeea8ca0e304c58b2c4eb3.title: A Walsh Hadamard Derived Linear Vector Symbolic Architecture
1df2b4378938361788aeea8ca0e304c58b2c4eb3.research_question: How can a new linear vector symbolic architecture be developed to improve computational efficiency, numerical stability, and performance in both classical symbolic AI tasks and modern differentiable deep learning systems?
1df2b4378938361788aeea8ca0e304c58b2c4eb3.hypothesis: A vector symbolic architecture derived from the Walsh-Hadamard transform, with appropriate initialization and binding/unbinding operations, will achieve superior computational efficiency, numerical stability, and performance compared to existing VSAs in both classical and deep learning tasks.
1df2b4378938361788aeea8ca0e304c58b2c4eb3.proposed_method: A novel vector symbolic architecture, termed Hadamard-derived Linear Binding (HLB), will be developed by replacing the Fourier transform in classic binding/unbinding operations with the Walsh-Hadamard transform. The binding operation will be defined as element-wise multiplication in the Hadamard domain, and unbinding will be performed via element-wise division, leveraging the self-inverse property of the Hadamard matrix for computational simplicity. To address numerical stability, a Mixture of Normal Distributions (MiND) will be used for vector initialization, ensuring zero mean and non-zero absolute mean, thus avoiding values near zero that could destabilize unbinding. A projection step in the Hadamard domain will be introduced to further reduce retrieval noise, and a similarity augmentation correction will be applied to maintain accurate cosine similarity scores when multiple items are bound together. The overall method will achieve linear computational complexity for binding and unbinding operations.
1df2b4378938361788aeea8ca0e304c58b2c4eb3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both classical VSA benchmark tasks and deep learning applications. For classical tasks, a pool of 1000 random vectors will be used to create bundles of up to 25 bound pairs, and retrieval accuracy will be measured over 50 trials, comparing HLB against HRR, VTB, and MAP baselines. Sequential binding/unbinding tasks will also be performed to assess similarity preservation and vector norm stability. For deep learning, two applications will be targeted: (1) Connectionist Symbolic PseudoSecrets (CSPS) for privacy-preserving inference, evaluated on MNIST, SVHN, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Mini-ImageNet datasets, using accuracy and Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) for clustering resistance; (2) Extreme Multi-Label (XML) classification on eight datasets (e.g., BIBTEX, DELICIOUS, MEDIAMILL, EURLEX-4K, WIKI10-31K, AMAZON-13K, DELICIOUS-200K), using nDCG and PSnDCG as evaluation metrics. All experiments will use standardized vector sampling and be run on a single NVIDIA TESLA PH402 GPU with 32GB memory.
1df2b4378938361788aeea8ca0e304c58b2c4eb3.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new linear VSA based on the Walsh-Hadamard transform, achieving linear computational complexity for binding/unbinding while maintaining or improving performance over prior VSAs. The method provides enhanced numerical stability through a novel initialization scheme and a Hadamard-domain projection step that reduces retrieval noise. A theoretically justified similarity correction is introduced for accurate retrieval in composite representations. Empirical results demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in both classical symbolic tasks and differentiable deep learning applications, including privacy-preserving inference and extreme multi-label classification, surpassing existing VSA methods in accuracy, stability, and information security.

1dff6b1b35e2d45d4db57c8b4e4395486c3e365f.title: Token Merging: Your ViT But Faster
1dff6b1b35e2d45d4db57c8b4e4395486c3e365f.research_question: How can the throughput of existing Vision Transformer (ViT) models be increased across multiple modalities (images, video, audio) without significant accuracy loss and without requiring retraining?
1dff6b1b35e2d45d4db57c8b4e4395486c3e365f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that merging similar tokens within transformer blocks using a lightweight, parallelizable matching algorithm can significantly increase throughput of ViT models with minimal impact on accuracy, and that this approach will generalize across image, video, and audio modalities.
1dff6b1b35e2d45d4db57c8b4e4395486c3e365f.proposed_method: A novel token merging framework is proposed for Vision Transformers, where, within each transformer block, a fixed number of the most similar tokens are merged using a fast bipartite soft matching algorithm. Token similarity is determined by computing cosine similarity between the attention keys of tokens, and merging is performed by partitioning tokens into two sets, matching each token in one set to its most similar counterpart in the other, and averaging their features weighted by token size. Proportional attention is introduced to account for merged token sizes, ensuring correct softmax scaling. The merging schedule can be constant or decreasing across layers, and the method is designed to be a drop-in module for both inference and training, requiring no architectural changes or retraining for off-the-shelf models.
1dff6b1b35e2d45d4db57c8b4e4395486c3e365f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard benchmarks for images (ImageNet-1k), video (Kinetics-400), and audio (AudioSet-2M) using a variety of ViT models pretrained via different strategies (e.g., AugReg, MAE, SWAG, DeiT). The method will be evaluated both off-the-shelf and with fine-tuning, comparing throughput and accuracy against state-of-the-art ViT variants and token pruning methods such as DynamicViT, A-ViT, and SP-ViT.
