Evaluation metrics include Top-1 accuracy for images, mAP for audio, and clip-level accuracy for video, with throughput measured in images/s, samples/s, or clips/s on V100 GPUs. Ablation studies will analyze design choices for token similarity, merging algorithms, and merging schedules.
1dff6b1b35e2d45d4db57c8b4e4395486c3e365f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable significant throughput gains for ViT models via token merging without requiring retraining, maintaining competitive accuracy across images, video, and audio. The bipartite soft matching algorithm is both fast and parallelizable, outperforming previous clustering and pruning-based reduction methods in speed-accuracy trade-off. The method is modality-agnostic, can be used during both inference and training, and enables real-world speedups including up to 2x faster training and inference with negligible accuracy drop. Additionally, the approach provides a natural hierarchical structure within pure transformer architectures, with potential applications beyond classification such as segmentation and part tracking.

1e05c5427d6a35a3b1bf37fb955f2ea94995a71d.title: Effective Data Augmentation With Diffusion Models
1e05c5427d6a35a3b1bf37fb955f2ea94995a71d.research_question: How can data augmentation methods be improved to generate diverse, high-fidelity synthetic images that enhance few-shot image classification performance, especially for novel or fine-grained visual concepts not present in the training data of generative models?
1e05c5427d6a35a3b1bf37fb955f2ea94995a71d.hypothesis: Leveraging pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models, combined with learned pseudo-prompts for novel concepts and image-to-image editing, will produce semantically meaningful and diverse augmentations that significantly improve few-shot classification accuracy across common, fine-grained, and previously unseen visual categories.
1e05c5427d6a35a3b1bf37fb955f2ea94995a71d.proposed_method: A novel data augmentation framework, DA-Fusion, will be developed that utilizes pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models (such as Stable Diffusion) to generate synthetic images for training classifiers. The approach adapts the diffusion model to new domains by learning new word embeddings (pseudo-prompts) for each class using a small set of labeled images via Textual Inversion, enabling the model to generate images for concepts outside its original vocabulary. Augmentation is performed by splicing real images into the reverse diffusion process at a randomly selected timestep, allowing control over the intensity of semantic modification. Synthetic images are mixed with real data during classifier training, with the ratio of real to synthetic images controlled by a sampling hyperparameter. The method includes mechanisms to prevent training data leakage from the generative model, both by erasing class knowledge from the model weights (model-centric) and by removing class names from prompts (data-centric).
1e05c5427d6a35a3b1bf37fb955f2ea94995a71d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on seven datasets: Caltech101, Flowers102, FGVC Aircraft, Stanford Cars, COCO, PASCAL VOC, and a newly contributed Leafy Spurge aerial imagery dataset. Few-shot classification tasks will be set up by varying the number of labeled examples per class. The proposed method will be compared against RandAugment (a standard augmentation baseline) and Real Guidance (an SDEdit-based generative augmentation method), using consistent hyperparameters for fair comparison. A ResNet50 classifier pre-trained on ImageNet will be fine-tuned on mixtures of real and synthetic images, and validation accuracy will be measured. Ablation studies will analyze the effects of augmentation intensity randomization and the balance between real and synthetic data. Evaluation metrics include classification accuracy and normalized scores across domains, with additional analysis on the impact of leakage prevention strategies.
1e05c5427d6a35a3b1bf37fb955f2ea94995a71d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a universal, controllable, and performant data augmentation strategy that enables semantic modification of images using diffusion models, even for concepts not present in the model's original training data. The method is the first to systematically analyze synthetic data augmentation for previously unseen concepts using diffusion models, and it incorporates learned pseudo-prompts for novel class adaptation. DA-Fusion demonstrates robustness to data balance and augmentation intensity, and provides practical defenses against training data leakage from large generative models. The framework outperforms both standard and existing generative augmentation baselines, particularly in few-shot and fine-grained classification settings.

1e0cf0e78bc145c0096b19b80ec2603c9cf03247.title: Procedural Image Programs for Representation Learning
1e0cf0e78bc145c0096b19b80ec2603c9cf03247.research_question: Can large-scale collections of procedural image programs be leveraged to train neural networks for effective image representation learning, reducing reliance on real image data and overcoming the limitations of curated generative processes?
1e0cf0e78bc145c0096b19b80ec2603c9cf03247.hypothesis: Training neural networks on a diverse and extensive dataset of procedural image programs will yield image representations that approach or surpass the performance of models pre-trained on real images, especially when combined with advanced data mixing strategies.
1e0cf0e78bc145c0096b19b80ec2603c9cf03247.proposed_method: A large dataset of over 21,000 unique procedural image programs, implemented as short OpenGL fragment shaders, will be collected from public sources such as Twitter (TwiGL shaders) and Shadertoy. Each program will be used to generate diverse synthetic images by varying a stochastic timestep parameter, enabling both supervised and unsupervised representation learning. Neural networks will be pre-trained using both supervised classification (cross-entropy), supervised contrastive learning (SupCon), and unsupervised contrastive learning (SimCLR, MoCo v2) on images generated from these shaders. To address shortcut learning and improve transferability, pixel-space mixing strategies such as MixUp and CutMix will be applied to create interpolated samples, with hyperparameters optimized using FID scores. The methodology includes both offline and online (on-the-fly) image generation to assess the impact of sample diversity and volume.
1e0cf0e78bc145c0096b19b80ec2603c9cf03247.experiment_details: Experiments will involve pre-training ResNet-18 and ResNet-50 models on datasets generated from the procedural shaders at resolutions of 256x256 and 384x384. Both supervised and unsupervised learning paradigms will be evaluated, with linear evaluation protocols applied to downstream tasks. The primary evaluation datasets are ImageNet-100, ImageNet-1k, and the Visual Task Adaptation Benchmark (VTAB), covering natural, specialized, and structured tasks. Baseline comparisons will include models pre-trained on real images (ImageNet-1k, Places365) and other procedural datasets (FractalDB, Dead-Leaves, StyleGAN Oriented). Evaluation metrics include top-1 accuracy, FID, LPIPS intra-image distance, and 5-NN retrieval accuracy. Additional analyses will investigate the effect of the number and diversity of shaders, the impact of mixing strategies, and the properties of high-performing shaders using shallow predictors and feature analysis.
1e0cf0e78bc145c0096b19b80ec2603c9cf03247.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first large-scale, diverse collection of procedural image programs for representation learning, enabling scalable and high-throughput synthetic image generation. It demonstrates that increasing the number of generative programs, rather than samples per program, leads to improved downstream performance without saturation at current scales. The approach achieves state-of-the-art results in representation learning without real images, significantly narrowing the gap with real-image pre-training. The work also provides new insights into the properties of effective generative programs and proposes practical strategies (such as MixUp) to mitigate shortcut learning in contrastive frameworks.

1e20aa9a52ea92b3107c4de372c7a0e4c1bfb324.title: Fast Inference of Mixture-of-Experts Language Models with Offloading
1e20aa9a52ea92b3107c4de372c7a0e4c1bfb324.research_question: How can inference speed and efficiency of large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models be improved on consumer-grade hardware with limited GPU memory, without sacrificing model quality?
1e20aa9a52ea92b3107c4de372c7a0e4c1bfb324.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging the locality and predictability of expert usage patterns in MoE language models, combined with mixed quantization and optimized offloading strategies, can significantly accelerate inference on resource-constrained hardware while maintaining competitive model performance.
1e20aa9a52ea92b3107c4de372c7a0e4c1bfb324.proposed_method: A novel MoE-centric offloading framework will be developed that exploits two key properties of MoE language models: (1) the temporal locality of expert usage, and (2) the predictability of future expert selection from current hidden states. The method will implement a least-recently-used (LRU) cache to retain recently activated experts in GPU memory, reducing redundant host-to-device transfers. Additionally, speculative expert loading will be employed, where the system predicts and preloads likely-to-be-used experts for upcoming layers by applying the next layer's gating function to the current hidden states. Mixed quantization will be applied, using lower bit-width quantization for expert layers and higher precision for shared layers, to further reduce memory footprint and transfer times. The system will be engineered to support asynchronous expert loading and efficient buffer management, enabling practical deployment on hardware with 12-16GB VRAM and limited RAM.
1e20aa9a52ea92b3107c4de372c7a0e4c1bfb324.experiment_details: Experiments will focus on the Mixtral-8x7B and Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct MoE language models, targeting interactive inference scenarios (batch size 1) on hardware including NVIDIA T4, RTX 3060, RTX 3080 Mobile, and A100 GPUs. The OpenAssistant Conversations dataset will be used to evaluate caching and prefetching strategies by measuring cache hit ratios and recall of speculative loading. Model quality will be assessed using WikiText2 and C4 perplexity, as well as 5-shot MMLU accuracy. Multiple quantization schemes (FP16, 4-bit, 3-bit, 2-bit) will be compared for both expert and shared layers. Inference speed will be benchmarked in tokens per second across hardware setups, and ablation studies will isolate the impact of LRU caching and speculative loading. Baselines will include naive offloading and existing offloading frameworks.
1e20aa9a52ea92b3107c4de372c7a0e4c1bfb324.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a MoE-specific offloading strategy that combines LRU caching and speculative expert loading, tailored to the unique access patterns of MoE models. This approach enables efficient inference of large MoE LLMs on consumer hardware with limited GPU memory, a scenario where existing offloading and quantization techniques perform suboptimally. The integration of mixed quantization and asynchronous buffer management further distinguishes the method, providing a practical solution for interactive, low-latency inference without requiring architectural changes or retraining. The proposed system is claimed to significantly outperform naive offloading and to enable near state-of-the-art MoE models to run interactively on affordable hardware.

1e2a82ef5e0325a26ca0344c4f8c256c52fae7ec.title: π0.5: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization
1e2a82ef5e0325a26ca0344c4f8c256c52fae7ec.research_question: How can a vision-language-action (VLA) model be developed to enable mobile robots to generalize and perform complex, long-horizon manipulation tasks in entirely new, unseen real-world environments?
1e2a82ef5e0325a26ca0344c4f8c256c52fae7ec.hypothesis: A VLA model co-trained on a heterogeneous mixture of robot data, high-level semantic subtask prediction, web-based multimodal data, and verbal instructions will achieve broad open-world generalization, enabling mobile robots to perform complex, multi-stage tasks in novel environments not seen during training.
1e2a82ef5e0325a26ca0344c4f8c256c52fae7ec.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a hierarchical VLA model, π0.5, which leverages a two-stage training process. In the pre-training stage, the model is trained on a diverse set of data sources, including mobile and non-mobile robot demonstrations, high-level subtask annotations, and large-scale web data (image captioning, VQA, object localization), using discrete token representations for all modalities. The post-training stage specializes the model for mobile manipulation by incorporating flow matching to enable efficient, real-time inference of continuous action sequences and by integrating verbal instruction demonstrations for improved high-level reasoning. The model architecture consists of a unified transformer backbone with modality-specific tokenizers and expert weights for action tokens, enabling both high-level semantic inference (subtask prediction) and low-level action generation. At inference time, the model first predicts a high-level subtask from the current observation and instruction, and then generates the corresponding low-level action chunk, allowing for flexible, multi-stage task execution.
1e2a82ef5e0325a26ca0344c4f8c256c52fae7ec.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in both controlled mock home environments and real homes that are entirely unseen during training. The evaluation will focus on multi-stage household tasks such as cleaning kitchens and bedrooms, with tasks including placing dishes in sinks, putting items in drawers, and making beds. The dataset for training includes approximately 400 hours of mobile manipulator data from around 100 homes, additional data from static robots in diverse settings, laboratory cross-embodiment data, high-level subtask annotations, and multimodal web data. Baselines will include models trained only on robot data, models without web or cross-embodiment data, and prior VLA models (π0 and π0-FAST+Flow). Evaluation metrics will include task completion rate, language following accuracy (for both in-distribution and out-of-distribution objects), and success rate in executing multi-stage tasks. Ablation studies will assess the contribution of each data source and the importance of hierarchical inference.
1e2a82ef5e0325a26ca0344c4f8c256c52fae7ec.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to demonstrate that a co-trained VLA model can enable mobile robots to perform long-horizon, dexterous manipulation tasks in entirely new, real-world homes, generalizing far beyond the training distribution. The method introduces a unified architecture for both high-level semantic and low-level action inference, leverages a hybrid discrete-continuous training regime for efficient and expressive action generation, and systematically integrates diverse supervision sources—including web-scale multimodal data, cross-embodiment robot data, and verbal instructions—to achieve open-world generalization. Empirical results are expected to show that this combination of co-training ingredients is essential for robust, scalable generalization in real-world robotics.

1e30ef403b1a90d512e8503d7ae2bf87a3a2a1ba.title: A Riemannian Framework for Learning Reduced-order Lagrangian Dynamics
1e30ef403b1a90d512e8503d7ae2bf87a3a2a1ba.research_question: How can physically-consistent, data-efficient, and interpretable reduced-order models of high-dimensional Lagrangian dynamical systems be learned, enabling accurate long-term predictions for both rigid and deformable systems?
1e30ef403b1a90d512e8503d7ae2bf87a3a2a1ba.hypothesis: Jointly learning a structure-preserving nonlinear latent space and associated low-dimensional dynamics within a Riemannian geometric framework will yield physically-consistent, interpretable, and data-efficient reduced-order models that accurately capture the behavior of high-dimensional Lagrangian systems.
1e30ef403b1a90d512e8503d7ae2bf87a3a2a1ba.proposed_method: A novel geometric deep network architecture will be developed to learn reduced-order Lagrangian dynamics from high-dimensional physical systems. The approach integrates a constrained autoencoder (AE) to learn a nonlinear, structure-preserving latent space and its embedding, ensuring projection properties via biorthogonal layers optimized on the biorthogonal manifold using Riemannian optimization. The reduced-order dynamics in the latent space are modeled using a geometric Lagrangian Neural Network (LNN), where the mass-inertia matrix is parameterized as a symmetric positive-definite (SPD) network operating directly on the SPD manifold, and the potential energy is learned via a standard multilayer perceptron. The entire system—including AE and LNN parameters—is trained jointly, leveraging Riemannian optimization to respect the intrinsic geometry of the parameter spaces and guarantee physically-plausible, energy-conserving dynamics. Both acceleration-based and multi-step integration training regimes will be explored to enhance long-term prediction accuracy.
1e30ef403b1a90d512e8503d7ae2bf87a3a2a1ba.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on simulated high-dimensional physical systems, including a 16-DoF pendulum, a 192-DoF rope, and a 600-DoF thin cloth. Datasets will consist of trajectories generated under varying initial conditions and actuation scenarios. The proposed method will be compared against full-order LNNs, linear structure-preserving model order reduction (MOR) methods such as Lagrangian operator inference (L-OpInf), and variants using different geometric parameterizations. Evaluation metrics will include reconstruction error, acceleration prediction error, and long-term trajectory prediction accuracy for both positions and velocities. Both single-step and multi-step (over multiple integration steps) prediction regimes will be evaluated, with ablation studies on the impact of latent space dimension, joint versus sequential training, and the use of Riemannian optimization for biorthogonal AE weights.
1e30ef403b1a90d512e8503d7ae2bf87a3a2a1ba.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a unified Riemannian geometric approach to jointly learn nonlinear structure-preserving latent spaces and reduced-order Lagrangian dynamics, enabling physically-consistent and interpretable models for high-dimensional systems. Key innovations include the use of constrained autoencoders with biorthogonal layers optimized on the biorthogonal manifold, SPD neural networks for mass-inertia matrix parameterization, and joint Riemannian optimization of all parameters. The method extends structure-preserving model order reduction to cases with unknown high-dimensional dynamics and demonstrates superior data efficiency, generalization, and long-term prediction accuracy compared to existing approaches.

1e41434841c880821300a9e24e29109ca6689de4.title: Surgical Robot Transformer (SRT): Imitation Learning for Surgical Tasks
1e41434841c880821300a9e24e29109ca6689de4.research_question: Can imitation learning be effectively used to train surgical robots to perform fundamental surgical manipulation tasks using only approximate kinematics data, and what design choices in action representation and sensory input are critical for robust and generalizable policy learning in this domain?
1e41434841c880821300a9e24e29109ca6689de4.hypothesis: Modeling policy actions as relative motions, rather than absolute poses, enables robust imitation learning on surgical robots with inaccurate kinematics, and the inclusion of wrist camera imagery further improves policy performance and generalization.
1e41434841c880821300a9e24e29109ca6689de4.proposed_method: A novel imitation learning framework will be developed for surgical robots, specifically targeting the da Vinci Research Kit (dVRK), which suffers from inaccurate forward kinematics. The method will collect demonstration data consisting of synchronized stereo endoscope and wrist camera images, along with approximate kinematics, during teleoperated execution of surgical tasks. Policies will be trained using transformer-based architectures (e.g., ACT) and diffusion models, with action representations explored in three forms: camera-centric (absolute pose), tool-centric (relative to end-effector), and hybrid-relative (translation relative to a fixed frame, rotation relative to end-effector). The hybrid-relative action representation will be emphasized, as it grounds translation to a stable frame and rotation to the tool, mitigating errors from kinematic inconsistencies. Wrist camera inputs will be incorporated to enhance depth perception and robustness to visual occlusions.
1e41434841c880821300a9e24e29109ca6689de4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the dVRK platform across three fundamental surgical tasks: tissue lifting, needle pickup and handover, and knot-tying. For each task, hundreds of teleoperated demonstrations will be collected, with randomized initial conditions to encourage generalization. Policies using different action representations and sensory inputs (with/without wrist cameras) will be compared. Evaluation will include trajectory tracking repeatability under robot configuration shifts, task success rates, and robustness to novel scenarios such as animal tissue backgrounds and unseen suture pads. Metrics will include root mean squared error (RMSE) for trajectory tracking and binary success rates for task completion. Baseline comparisons will include camera-centric and tool-centric action representations, as well as policies omitting wrist camera input.
1e41434841c880821300a9e24e29109ca6689de4.novelty_claims: The proposed approach enables effective imitation learning for surgical robots using only approximate kinematics data, eliminating the need for precise calibration or post-processing corrections. The hybrid-relative action representation is introduced to improve robustness to kinematic errors and challenging rotations, outperforming traditional absolute and tool-centric approaches. The use of removable wrist cameras is systematically evaluated, demonstrating their critical role in enhancing policy performance and generalization to out-of-distribution scenarios. The framework is validated on complex bimanual surgical tasks, including knot-tying, and shows the potential to leverage large-scale clinical demonstration datasets for scalable autonomous surgery.

1e66b2d2a56842f07e5d6bf4ac0dbe5da829d052.title: DetectLLM: Leveraging Log Rank Information for Zero-Shot Detection of Machine-Generated Text
1e66b2d2a56842f07e5d6bf4ac0dbe5da829d052.research_question: How can zero-shot methods be improved for detecting machine-generated text, particularly by leveraging internal statistics of large language models (LLMs), and what are the efficiency–performance trade-offs of such methods?
1e66b2d2a56842f07e5d6bf4ac0dbe5da829d052.hypothesis: Leveraging log rank information, either alone or in combination with log-likelihood and perturbation-based techniques, will yield more accurate and efficient zero-shot detection of machine-generated text compared to existing zero-shot baselines.
1e66b2d2a56842f07e5d6bf4ac0dbe5da829d052.proposed_method: Two novel zero-shot detection methods are proposed that utilize log rank statistics from LLMs in a white-box setting. The first method, Log-Likelihood Log-Rank Ratio (LRR), computes the ratio between the average per-token log-likelihood and the average per-token log rank for a given text, hypothesizing that this ratio is higher for machine-generated text. The second method, Normalized Perturbed log-Rank (NPR), applies small perturbations (minor rewrites) to the input text and measures the normalized change in log rank, based on the intuition that machine-generated texts are more sensitive to such perturbations. LRR is designed to be fast and efficient, requiring only a single pass over the text, while NPR is more accurate but computationally intensive due to the need for multiple perturbations and evaluations. Both methods are fully zero-shot and require no additional training data.
1e66b2d2a56842f07e5d6bf4ac0dbe5da829d052.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three benchmark datasets: XSum (news articles), SQuAD (Wikipedia paragraphs), and WritingPrompts (prompted stories), covering domains where LLM misuse is plausible. For each dataset, 300 human-written and 300 machine-generated texts will be evaluated, with machine-generated samples produced by prompting several LLMs (GPT2-xl, Neo-2.7B, OPT-2.7B, GPT-j, OPT-13B, Llama-13B, NeoX-20B) using the first 30 tokens of human-written texts. Baseline zero-shot methods (log probability, rank, log rank, entropy, DetectGPT) and supervised detectors (RoBERTa-base, RoBERTa-large) will be compared. The primary evaluation metric is AUROC, measuring the ability to distinguish machine-generated from human-written text. Additional experiments will analyze the impact of decoding strategies (top-k, top-p), temperature settings, perturbation functions (T5-large, T5-3B, etc.), and number of perturbations on detection accuracy and computational efficiency.
1e66b2d2a56842f07e5d6bf4ac0dbe5da829d052.novelty_claims: The proposed methods introduce the use of log rank statistics, both directly and in combination with log-likelihood and perturbation-based approaches, for zero-shot detection of machine-generated text. LRR offers a fast, efficient, and effective perturbation-free detector, while NPR achieves higher accuracy with fewer perturbations than prior perturbation-based methods such as DetectGPT. The methods demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art zero-shot baselines across multiple datasets and LLMs, and provide new insights into the efficiency–performance trade-offs in practical detection scenarios. The proposal also includes a comprehensive analysis of computational costs and guidelines for selecting detection strategies based on user constraints.

1e71ec1e27804f1eb0f60cade2d86f7fd34fac9d.title: On the Adversarial Risk of Test Time Adaptation: An Investigation into Realistic Test-Time Data Poisoning
1e71ec1e27804f1eb0f60cade2d86f7fd34fac9d.research_question: What is the realistic adversarial risk of test-time adaptation (TTA) methods under test-time data poisoning scenarios, and how can both attack and defense strategies be developed and evaluated under practical threat models?
1e71ec1e27804f1eb0f60cade2d86f7fd34fac9d.hypothesis: Test-time adaptation methods are less vulnerable to adversarial test-time data poisoning than previously believed when evaluated under realistic threat models that do not assume white-box access or access to benign data; furthermore, new attack and defense strategies tailored to these constraints can more accurately characterize and improve TTA robustness.
1e71ec1e27804f1eb0f60cade2d86f7fd34fac9d.proposed_method: A novel, realistic test-time data poisoning (RTTDP) protocol is proposed, which operates under a grey-box threat model where the adversary has access only to the model architecture and initial weights, but not to real-time model parameters or benign user data. A surrogate model is distilled from the online model using only adversarial queries, enabling gradient-based synthesis of poisoned samples. The poisoning objective is formulated as an in-distribution attack with feature consistency regularization, ensuring that the feature distribution of poisoned samples matches that of clean data, thus improving transferability of the attack. Two TTA-aware attack objectives are developed: a high-entropy attack (NHEAttack) that maximizes prediction entropy except for the ground-truth class, and a balanced low-entropy attack (BLEAttack) that targets the most probable non-ground-truth class in a class-balanced manner. Optimization is performed using Projected Gradient Descent with constraints, and the attack is injected online during TTA.
1e71ec1e27804f1eb0f60cade2d86f7fd34fac9d.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on standard TTA benchmarks: CIFAR10-C, CIFAR100-C, and ImageNet-C, each with strong distribution shifts and using pre-trained WideResNet-28, ResNeXt-29, and ResNet-50 models, respectively. The proposed attacks are compared against established poisoning baselines such as Unlearnable Examples, Adversarial Poisoning, DIA, TePA, and MaxCE, with all methods adapted to the realistic RTTDP protocol. Evaluation metrics include attack success rate (classification error on benign samples) and average ranking across various state-of-the-art TTA methods (e.g., TENT, RPL, EATA, TTAC, SAR, CoTTA, ROID). Ablation studies investigate the contributions of the surrogate model, feature consistency regularization, and attack objectives. Defense strategies such as entropy thresholding, data augmentation, EMA updating, and stochastic parameter restoration are also evaluated for their effectiveness against the proposed attacks.
1e71ec1e27804f1eb0f60cade2d86f7fd34fac9d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a comprehensive and realistic threat model for test-time data poisoning that eliminates unrealistic assumptions such as white-box access and access to benign user data. It develops a surrogate model-based attack framework with feature consistency regularization, enabling effective in-distribution poisoning without requiring benign data. Two new TTA-aware attack objectives are designed, and the protocol provides the first extensive evaluation of TTA robustness under these realistic conditions. Additionally, the study identifies practical defense strategies that empirically improve adversarial robustness in TTA, offering actionable insights for future robust TTA method design.

1e909e2a8cdacdcdff125ebcc566f37cb869a1c8.title: A Survey on Hallucination in Large Language Models: Principles, Taxonomy, Challenges, and Open Questions
1e909e2a8cdacdcdff125ebcc566f37cb869a1c8.research_question: What are the principles, taxonomy, causes, detection methods, and mitigation strategies for hallucination in large language models, and what open challenges and future research directions exist in this area?
1e909e2a8cdacdcdff125ebcc566f37cb869a1c8.proposed_method: A comprehensive research plan will be developed to systematically investigate hallucinations in large language models (LLMs). The approach will begin with the construction of a refined taxonomy of hallucination types, specifically tailored to LLMs, distinguishing between factuality and faithfulness hallucinations and their subtypes. The research will analyze the multifaceted causes of hallucination, categorizing them into data, training, and inference-related sources, and will provide detailed case studies and examples to illustrate each cause. Detection methodologies will be reviewed and benchmarked, including both automated and human-in-the-loop approaches, and a survey of existing evaluation datasets and metrics will be conducted. Mitigation strategies will be proposed and categorized according to their target stage (data, training, inference), with particular attention to retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems and their limitations. The research will also identify and discuss open questions and promising future directions, such as hallucinations in vision-language models and the boundaries of LLM knowledge.
1e909e2a8cdacdcdff125ebcc566f37cb869a1c8.experiment_details: The research will involve a thorough review and analysis of existing benchmarks for hallucination detection and evaluation, such as TruthfulQA, HalluQA, HaluEval-2.0, SelfCheckGPT-Wikibio, and FELM. Comparative studies will be conducted using these benchmarks to assess the prevalence and types of hallucinations across different LLMs, including models like GPT-3, GPT-4, LLaMA, Claude, and Gemini. Baseline methods for detection and mitigation will be identified and compared, including data filtering, model editing, and decoding strategies. Evaluation metrics will include factual consistency, faithfulness, and logical coherence, as well as human evaluation where appropriate. Experimental setups will be designed to test the effectiveness of mitigation strategies in both standard and retrieval-augmented LLM architectures.
1e909e2a8cdacdcdff125ebcc566f37cb869a1c8.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a nuanced and layered taxonomy of hallucinations specific to LLMs, distinguishing between factuality and faithfulness errors and their subtypes. It provides a holistic analysis linking the causes of hallucination to targeted mitigation strategies, offering a coherent framework for addressing the problem. The research will deliver a comprehensive synthesis of detection methods and benchmarks, and will critically analyze the unique challenges faced by retrieval-augmented generation systems. Additionally, the proposal outlines new research directions, including the study of hallucinations in multimodal models and the exploration of knowledge boundaries in LLMs, paving the way for future advancements in trustworthy AI.

1e97342906e53e1977ae409185da699da8091877.title: A Unifying Framework for Online Optimization with Long-Term Constraints
1e97342906e53e1977ae409185da699da8091877.research_question: How can online optimization problems with long-term, possibly non-convex, time-varying constraints be addressed in both stochastic and adversarial environments, while ensuring high reward and minimal cumulative constraint violation?
1e97342906e53e1977ae409185da699da8091877.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a unified online optimization framework can be developed that achieves sublinear regret and sublinear cumulative constraint violation with respect to the best fixed strategy satisfying long-term constraints, under both stochastic and adversarial selection of rewards and constraints, provided a strictly feasible solution exists.
1e97342906e53e1977ae409185da699da8091877.proposed_method: A meta-algorithm is proposed that leverages pairs of regret minimizers (RMs) operating in primal and dual domains, interacting through repeated Lagrangian games. The method is structured in two phases: a play phase, where the primal RM seeks to maximize reward while balancing constraint violations, and a recovery phase, where the focus shifts to making 'safe' decisions to reduce any excessive cumulative constraint violation. The framework is highly modular, allowing the use of different regret minimizers as black-box components, which enables handling both full-information and bandit-feedback settings, as well as non-convex reward and constraint functions. The algorithm is designed to work with minimal assumptions, only requiring a lower bound on the feasibility parameter (the margin by which constraints can be strictly satisfied), and includes mechanisms to estimate this parameter from data in the stochastic case.
1e97342906e53e1977ae409185da699da8091877.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets that feature time-varying, possibly non-convex, constraints and reward functions. The proposed framework will be instantiated with various regret minimizers suitable for convex and non-convex settings, and both full and bandit feedback. Baselines will include state-of-the-art algorithms for online convex optimization with static, stochastic, and adversarial constraints, such as those by Yu et al. and Mahdavi et al. Evaluation metrics will include cumulative regret with respect to the best fixed feasible strategy, cumulative constraint violation, and the fraction of optimal reward achieved. The framework's adaptability to budget-management scenarios in repeated auctions, including non-packing constraints like ROI, will also be empirically validated.
1e97342906e53e1977ae409185da699da8091877.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to provide best-of-both-worlds guarantees for online optimization with arbitrary, time-varying, long-term constraints in both stochastic and adversarial settings, including non-convex cases. It achieves sublinear regret and constraint violation with respect to the optimal fixed strategy mixture, and is the first to provide such guarantees in the adversarial setting with respect to this strong baseline. The modular use of regret minimizers allows seamless adaptation to various feedback and function structures. The method also introduces a principled approach to handling unknown feasibility parameters, and extends applicability to constraint types and settings previously considered intractable.

1ea243f1b697aae22e6f0349fa64857780a6108a.title: Generalization or Memorization: Data Contamination and Trustworthy Evaluation for Large Language Models
1ea243f1b697aae22e6f0349fa64857780a6108a.research_question: How can data contamination in large language models be reliably detected and mitigated, especially when training data and model internals are opaque, and how can trustworthy evaluation of LLMs be ensured in the presence of potential contamination?
1ea243f1b697aae22e6f0349fa64857780a6108a.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that data contamination alters the output distribution of LLMs, resulting in increased peakedness and duplication in generated texts, and that these distributional changes can be detected and corrected using only sampled outputs, without requiring access to model probabilities or training data.
1ea243f1b697aae22e6f0349fa64857780a6108a.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that leverages the output distribution of LLMs to detect and mitigate data contamination. The approach introduces Contamination Detection via output Distribution (CDD), which models the edit distance distribution among multiple sampled outputs for a given prompt to quantify the peakedness of the distribution. A high degree of peakedness is used as an indicator of contamination, with thresholds set for detection. For mitigation, Trustworthy Evaluation via output Distribution (TED) is developed, which corrects the evaluation by excluding peaked outputs (likely memorized or contaminated) and removing duplicate generations, thereby approximating the uncontaminated performance. Both methods operate in a black-box setting, requiring only access to generated texts and not to model parameters or training data.
1ea243f1b697aae22e6f0349fa64857780a6108a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using two newly constructed benchmarks: DETCON for data contamination detection and COMIEVAL for contamination mitigation evaluation. DETCON covers 2224 detection tasks across code generation and logical reasoning domains, simulating various contamination scenarios (explicit and implicit forms, different mixing ratios, learning rates, and contamination occurrences) by fine-tuning base LLMs (CodeLlama, CodeGen, Llama2, Bloom) with LoRA. COMIEVAL comprises 560 tasks for evaluating mitigation methods. Baselines for detection include n-gram overlap, embedding similarity, perplexity, Min-k% probability, and LLM Decontaminator, while evaluation metrics include Accuracy, F1 Score, AUC, and Pass@1. Hyperparameters for CDD and TED are empirically set, and ablation studies are performed to assess component contributions. Real-world validation is performed on ChatGPT using HumanEval, HumanEval_R (rephrased/translated), and CodeForces2305 (post-training data) datasets.
1ea243f1b697aae22e6f0349fa64857780a6108a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to detect and mitigate data contamination in LLMs by modeling output distribution peakedness using only sampled texts, without requiring access to model probabilities, parameters, or training data. It is capable of detecting both explicit and implicit contamination, including variants and paraphrases of test data. Two new benchmarks, DETCON and COMIEVAL, are introduced for systematic evaluation of contamination detection and mitigation. The method demonstrates substantial improvements over existing baselines and provides evidence of real-world data contamination in widely used LLMs such as ChatGPT.

1ea6fd882be428f7a98220599edf19c113c24bd3.title: AttriBoT: A Bag of Tricks for Efficiently Approximating Leave-One-Out Context Attribution
1ea6fd882be428f7a98220599edf19c113c24bd3.research_question: How can the computational cost of context attribution in large language models be drastically reduced while maintaining high fidelity to leave-one-out (LOO) error-based attributions, enabling scalable and interpretable analysis of model outputs in real-world settings?
1ea6fd882be428f7a98220599edf19c113c24bd3.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a combination of key-value caching, hierarchical attribution, and proxy modeling can be composed to efficiently approximate LOO context attributions in large language models, achieving significant speedups while maintaining high faithfulness to the original model's attributions.
1ea6fd882be428f7a98220599edf19c113c24bd3.proposed_method: The proposed method, AttriBoT, integrates several complementary techniques to approximate LOO context attribution efficiently. First, key-value (KV) caching is employed to avoid redundant computation by reusing attention key and value tensors for shared input prefixes, reducing the number of floating-point operations required. Second, hierarchical attribution is introduced, where the context is partitioned into groups (e.g., paragraphs), and LOO scores are first computed at the group level to prune low-importance groups before performing fine-grained attribution within retained groups. Third, proxy modeling leverages smaller models from the same family to approximate the LOO attributions of a larger target model, using the target model's response as input for the proxy. Additionally, proxy model pruning is used to further improve efficiency by using the proxy to identify and retain only the most contributive sources, which are then rescored with the target model. These methods are composable, allowing for a flexible trade-off between efficiency and accuracy.
1ea6fd882be428f7a98220599edf19c113c24bd3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using state-of-the-art open large language models, specifically the 70B-parameter Llama3.1 and 72B-parameter Qwen2.5 models as targets, with smaller variants from the same families serving as proxies. Evaluation will focus on open-book question answering (OBQA) tasks using three datasets: SQuAD 2.0 (sentence-level attribution, paragraph groups), HotpotQA (sentence-level attribution, paragraph groups), and QASPER (paragraph-level attribution, section groups). Baselines will include attention weights, gradient norm, sentence embedding similarity, and ContextCite. The primary evaluation metric will be mean Average Precision (mAP) for recovering highly contributive sources as identified by the target model's LOO attributions, with efficiency measured in GPU-seconds and theoretical FLOPs. Experiments will be run on multi-GPU servers, and both practical and theoretical speedups will be reported.
1ea6fd882be428f7a98220599edf19c113c24bd3.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel composition of key-value caching, hierarchical attribution, and proxy modeling for efficient LOO context attribution in large language models. This method achieves over 300× speedup compared to naive LOO computation, making attribution up to 30× faster than response generation itself, while maintaining higher faithfulness to target model attributions than prior efficient attribution methods. The composability of techniques allows for Pareto-optimal trade-offs between speed and accuracy, and the approach is validated across multiple datasets and model families. The resulting system enables scalable, interpretable LLM analysis suitable for real-world applications.

1ea72d659bf48a0f50e4d6f7f7b34e9d4850d7be.title: Improved Diffusion-based Generative Model with Better Adversarial Robustness
1ea72d659bf48a0f50e4d6f7f7b34e9d4850d7be.research_question: How can the distribution mismatch between training and inference stages in diffusion-based generative models, including both Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DPMs) and Consistency Models (CMs), be effectively mitigated to improve generation quality and robustness, particularly under adversarial conditions?
1ea72d659bf48a0f50e4d6f7f7b34e9d4850d7be.hypothesis: Applying adversarial training (AT) grounded in distributionally robust optimization (DRO) to both DPMs and CMs will alleviate the distribution mismatch between training and inference, thereby improving the robustness and quality of generated data across various generative tasks.
1ea72d659bf48a0f50e4d6f7f7b34e9d4850d7be.proposed_method: A novel adversarial training framework is developed for diffusion-based generative models, targeting both DPMs and CMs. The approach reformulates the training objective using distributionally robust optimization (DRO), which is shown to be equivalent to adversarial training with theoretically justified error bounds. For DPMs, the method introduces adversarial perturbations to the noisy inputs during training, optimizing the model to be robust to these perturbations within a bounded range. For CMs, adversarial perturbations are applied to the ODE-based data transformation process, ensuring the model's robustness to numerical approximation errors. Efficient adversarial training algorithms are designed to minimize computational overhead, utilizing a small number of gradient ascent steps per update and integrating adversarial example generation directly into the training loop.
1ea72d659bf48a0f50e4d6f7f7b34e9d4850d7be.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on standard image generation benchmarks, including CIFAR-10 (32×32) and ImageNet (64×64), as well as zero-shot text-to-image generation on MS-COCO (512×512) using Latent Consistency Models (LCM) with Stable Diffusion v1.5. The proposed adversarial training methods are evaluated against baselines such as original pretrained models, standard fine-tuning, and ADM-IP (a method that adds Gaussian perturbations). Evaluation metrics include Frechet Inception Distance (FID) for image quality, Classification Accuracy Score (CAS), CLIP score for text-image alignment, and additional metrics such as sFID, Inception Score, Precision, and Recall. Fine-tuning is performed from pretrained models for efficiency, and various diffusion samplers (IDDPM, DDIM, DPM-Solver, ES) are tested under different numbers of network function evaluations (NFEs). Hyperparameters such as adversarial learning rate and number of adversarial steps are systematically explored. All models are trained with the same computational budget for fair comparison.
1ea72d659bf48a0f50e4d6f7f7b34e9d4850d7be.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first theoretically grounded connection between distributionally robust optimization and adversarial training in the context of diffusion-based generative models. It provides a unified adversarial training framework applicable to both multi-step DPMs and single-step CMs, supported by new theoretical results that quantify error bounds and robustness guarantees. The adversarial training algorithms are designed to be computationally efficient, avoiding the high cost of standard projected gradient descent methods. Empirical results demonstrate consistent improvements over existing baselines and state-of-the-art methods across multiple datasets and sampling regimes, particularly in scenarios with few sampling steps where distribution mismatch is most severe.

1eab09d29fa9e7ff08e8c82166b9faf4463e84d5.title: The Illusion of Thinking: Understanding the Strengths and Limitations of Reasoning Models via the Lens of Problem Complexity
1eab09d29fa9e7ff08e8c82166b9faf4463e84d5.research_question: What are the fundamental strengths and limitations of current Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) in solving problems of varying complexity, and how do their reasoning processes and performance compare to standard language models under controlled experimental conditions?
1eab09d29fa9e7ff08e8c82166b9faf4463e84d5.hypothesis: Current Large Reasoning Models exhibit distinct performance regimes depending on problem complexity, with reasoning advantages manifesting at intermediate complexity, but both reasoning and non-reasoning models ultimately failing at high complexity due to inherent scaling limitations in their reasoning mechanisms.
1eab09d29fa9e7ff08e8c82166b9faf4463e84d5.proposed_method: A systematic evaluation framework will be developed using controllable puzzle environments that allow precise manipulation of problem complexity while maintaining consistent logical structures. The approach involves comparing LRMs equipped with explicit reasoning mechanisms (such as extended chain-of-thought and self-reflection) to their non-reasoning counterparts, ensuring equivalent inference compute (token budget) across all models. Both final answers and intermediate reasoning traces will be analyzed using simulator-based verification to assess correctness, reasoning effort, and self-correction behaviors. The methodology will include fine-grained extraction and analysis of intermediate solutions within the reasoning traces, tracking their position, correctness, and evolution as problem complexity increases.
1eab09d29fa9e7ff08e8c82166b9faf4463e84d5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four puzzle environments—Tower of Hanoi, Checkers Jumping, River Crossing, and Blocks World—each offering fine-grained control over compositional and planning complexity. Multiple state-of-the-art LRMs (e.g., Claude 3.7 Sonnet Thinking, DeepSeek-R1, o3-mini) and their non-reasoning variants will be evaluated, using a consistent token budget (up to 64k tokens) and sampling 25 instances per model per complexity level. Baseline comparisons will include both reasoning-enabled and standard LLMs with matched model backbones. Evaluation metrics will include final answer accuracy, pass@k, reasoning token usage, and detailed analysis of intermediate reasoning traces using custom puzzle simulators. The setup will enable rigorous, controlled comparisons and facilitate in-depth failure analysis across low, medium, and high complexity regimes.
1eab09d29fa9e7ff08e8c82166b9faf4463e84d5.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a controlled experimental testbed leveraging algorithmic puzzle environments to systematically manipulate problem complexity and analyze both final answers and internal reasoning traces of LRMs. The approach moves beyond conventional math benchmarks, enabling precise, contamination-free, and simulator-verified evaluation of reasoning processes. Novel insights will be generated regarding the scaling limits of LRMs, the existence of distinct performance regimes, and the inefficiencies and failure modes in their reasoning traces, including phenomena such as overthinking and collapse. The work aims to provide a deeper quantitative and qualitative understanding of the self-correction mechanisms and computational behaviors of modern reasoning models.

1ec293c86e9a7a494759c7e20293d20d7a1e656e.title: Why Robust Generalization in Deep Learning is Difficult: Perspective of Expressive Power
1ec293c86e9a7a494759c7e20293d20d7a1e656e.research_question: What are the fundamental limitations of robust generalization in deep learning, particularly in terms of the expressive power required by neural networks to achieve low robust test error under adversarial perturbations, even when data exhibits favorable structural properties such as separability or low intrinsic dimensionality?
1ec293c86e9a7a494759c7e20293d20d7a1e656e.hypothesis: Robust generalization in deep learning is fundamentally limited by the expressive power of neural networks, such that achieving low robust test error requires exponentially large models in the data dimension or intrinsic manifold dimension, even for well-separated or linearly separable data.
1ec293c86e9a7a494759c7e20293d20d7a1e656e.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the expressive power required for robust classification by deep neural networks, focusing on binary classification tasks with data that is well-separated or lies on a low-dimensional manifold. The approach will involve deriving upper and lower bounds on the size of ReLU neural networks needed to achieve zero robust training error and low robust test error, under various structural assumptions about the data. The analysis will extend to general function classes with VC-dimension polynomial in the number of parameters, and will consider both the ambient data dimension and the intrinsic dimension of data manifolds. Theoretical constructions will be supported by rigorous proofs, leveraging concepts from VC-dimension theory, Lipschitz continuity, and manifold approximation.
1ec293c86e9a7a494759c7e20293d20d7a1e656e.experiment_details: The proposal centers on theoretical analysis rather than empirical experiments; however, the theoretical results will be illustrated using synthetic constructions of well-separated datasets in high-dimensional spaces and on low-dimensional manifolds. Theoretical baselines will include standard non-robust classifiers (e.g., linear classifiers) and robust classifiers constructed via Lipschitz functions. Evaluation metrics will focus on robust training error and robust test error, as defined by adversarial perturbation radii in various norms (e.g., L2, L-infinity). Key experimental setup details include the explicit construction of adversarially robust classifiers, analysis of network size requirements, and comparison to existing sample complexity and memorization results.
1ec293c86e9a7a494759c7e20293d20d7a1e656e.novelty_claims: The proposal claims a novel theoretical explanation for the persistent gap between robust training accuracy and robust test accuracy in deep learning, attributing it to the exponential expressive power required for robust generalization. It establishes exponential lower bounds on neural network size for robust test error, even for linearly separable and well-separated data, and provides matching upper and lower bounds for data lying on low-dimensional manifolds. The analysis generalizes to a broad class of models with polynomial VC-dimension, and introduces new techniques for bounding the VC-dimension and function approximation on manifolds in the context of robust classification.

1ec3a3ff77cb4b424499b3805ecc90182ecd8f8b.title: What Algorithms can Transformers Learn? A Study in Length Generalization
1ec3a3ff77cb4b424499b3805ecc90182ecd8f8b.research_question: Under what conditions can Transformer models learn true algorithmic solutions to symbolic reasoning tasks and exhibit strong length generalization beyond the training distribution?
1ec3a3ff77cb4b424499b3805ecc90182ecd8f8b.hypothesis: Transformer models are likely to length-generalize on algorithmic tasks if and only if the task can be solved by a short, simple program in the RASP-L programming language, which is specifically tailored to the computational model of Transformers.
1ec3a3ff77cb4b424499b3805ecc90182ecd8f8b.proposed_method: A unifying framework will be developed to predict when and how Transformers can exhibit strong length generalization on algorithmic tasks. This framework will leverage the RASP-L programming language, a restricted and learnable subset of RASP, which allows for the specification of algorithms that can be directly mapped to Transformer architectures. The approach involves formalizing the RASP-Generalization Conjecture, which states that length generalization is likely when a task's next-token function is representable by a simple RASP-L program, and the training data is sufficiently diverse to avoid learning spurious solutions. The methodology will include constructing a standard library of RASP-L functions and systematically analyzing which algorithmic tasks admit short RASP-L solutions. Empirical validation will be performed by training standard decoder-only Transformers from scratch on various algorithmic tasks and evaluating their out-of-distribution generalization to longer sequences.
1ec3a3ff77cb4b424499b3805ecc90182ecd8f8b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of algorithmic tasks, including counting, mode, sorting, and copy (with unique tokens), as well as harder tasks such as addition, parity, and copy with repeating tokens. For each task, models will be trained on sequences of varying lengths up to a maximum training length, with the training context packed and shifted to mirror standard LLM training practices. Evaluation will focus on exact match accuracy (EM) for test sequences that are significantly longer than those seen during training, providing a measure of length generalization. Baselines will include tasks with and without simple RASP-L solutions, and additional ablations will examine the impact of training data diversity and scratchpad formats. Standard decoder-only Transformer architectures with learned positional embeddings will be used, and all models will be trained to convergence on their respective training distributions.
1ec3a3ff77cb4b424499b3805ecc90182ecd8f8b.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a predictive theory for Transformer length generalization based on the existence of short RASP-L programs, providing a unifying perspective that explains both the surprising successes and failures of Transformers on symbolic reasoning tasks. The approach offers a principled method for identifying which tasks are amenable to length generalization and demonstrates, for the first time, strong length generalization on traditionally hard tasks such as parity and addition by leveraging insights from the RASP-L framework. Additionally, the work highlights the limitations of existing simplicity-based models and establishes RASP-L complexity as a more accurate predictor of Transformer generalization behavior.

1eceebdeffb153e4de9e71b6b3d7b1de3d338798.title: On the Finite-Time Complexity and Practical Computation of Approximate Stationarity Concepts of Lipschitz Functions
1eceebdeffb153e4de9e71b6b3d7b1de3d338798.research_question: Can practical algorithms be developed to compute approximately stationary points for general nonconvex, nonsmooth Lipschitz functions in finite time, and can these methods be extended to broader function classes beyond weakly convex functions, including those that are Clarke irregular, with provable finite-time complexity guarantees?
1eceebdeffb153e4de9e71b6b3d7b1de3d338798.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a practical, finite-time algorithmic scheme can be constructed to compute Goldstein approximate stationarity (GAS) and, under certain new regularity conditions, near-approximate stationarity (NAS) for a broad class of nonconvex, nonsmooth Lipschitz functions, including those not covered by weak convexity, with dimension-independent complexity guarantees.
1eceebdeffb153e4de9e71b6b3d7b1de3d338798.proposed_method: A novel algorithmic framework will be developed for computing approximate stationary points of general Lipschitz functions, focusing on two stationarity notions: Goldstein approximate stationarity (GAS) and near-approximate stationarity (NAS). The method replaces impractical subgradient oracle assumptions with a practical oracle that only requires gradients at differentiable points, leveraging automatic differentiation tools. The core algorithm employs a random conic perturbation scheme, iteratively sampling directions and updating points based on gradients or stochastic gradients, ensuring that almost everywhere differentiability (via Rademacher’s theorem) is exploited. For NAS, a new function class with outer Lipschitz continuity (OLC) of the subdifferential mapping is isolated, and a calculus of OLC is established to enable finite-time computation of NAS points for functions beyond weakly convex ones. The algorithms are analyzed in both deterministic and stochastic settings, with explicit stopping rules and complexity bounds.
1eceebdeffb153e4de9e71b6b3d7b1de3d338798.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of machine learning models that are not weakly convex and are Clarke irregular, such as ρ-margin SVMs, 1-layer, and 2-layer ReLU neural networks. The proposed algorithms will be evaluated for their ability to compute ((ε, δ)-GAS and ((ε, δ)-NAS points within finite time. Baselines will include existing gradient sampling and subgradient methods, particularly those requiring impractical oracles or exhibiting dimension-dependent complexity. Evaluation metrics will focus on the number of oracle calls required to reach approximate stationarity, the quality of the stationary points (measured by the distance to the subdifferential), and the practical feasibility of the oracle implementation. Theoretical guarantees will be validated empirically by checking convergence rates and the applicability of the method to models with non-weakly convex objectives.
1eceebdeffb153e4de9e71b6b3d7b1de3d338798.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first practical, dimension-free, finite-time algorithm for computing Goldstein approximate stationary points of general nonconvex, nonsmooth Lipschitz functions using only gradients at differentiable points. It removes the unrealistic subgradient selection oracle assumption present in prior work, making the method implementable with modern automatic differentiation tools. A new class of functions with outer Lipschitz continuous subdifferential mappings is identified, enabling finite-time computation of near-approximate stationary points for models beyond the weakly convex regime, including Clarke irregular functions. Additionally, a comprehensive calculus for OLC is developed, allowing explicit determination of regularity parameters for complex machine learning models such as ReLU neural networks and robust SVMs.

1ede15a0aa5204de1f3013d7616a93dbd46fd849.title: Equiformer: Equivariant Graph Attention Transformer for 3D Atomistic Graphs
1ede15a0aa5204de1f3013d7616a93dbd46fd849.research_question: How can Transformer-based neural network architectures be adapted to effectively model 3D atomistic graphs, such as molecules and materials, while respecting the underlying geometric symmetries of these systems?
1ede15a0aa5204de1f3013d7616a93dbd46fd849.hypothesis: Incorporating SE(3)/E(3)-equivariant operations and irreducible representation-based features into Transformer architectures, along with a novel equivariant graph attention mechanism, will enable effective learning on 3D atomistic graphs and outperform existing models in quantum property prediction tasks.
1ede15a0aa5204de1f3013d7616a93dbd46fd849.proposed_method: A novel graph neural network architecture, termed Equiformer, will be developed by replacing standard Transformer operations with their SE(3)/E(3)-equivariant counterparts and integrating tensor products for handling irreducible representation (irreps) features. The architecture will embed input 3D graphs using atom and edge-degree embeddings, followed by a stack of Transformer blocks that include equivariant graph attention and feedforward networks. The equivariant graph attention mechanism will replace traditional dot product attention with a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) attention and incorporate non-linear message passing, leveraging tensor products and spherical harmonics to encode both content and geometric information. Additional modules such as equivariant layer normalization, gate activations for non-linearities, and depth-wise tensor products will be implemented to maintain equivariance throughout the network. The final output head will aggregate node features to predict scalar properties such as energy.
1ede15a0aa5204de1f3013d7616a93dbd46fd849.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three benchmark datasets: QM9 (quantum properties of ~134k small molecules), MD17 (molecular dynamics trajectories for small organic molecules), and OC20 (Open Catalyst 2020, large atomic systems for catalysis). For each dataset, the model will be trained to minimize mean absolute error (MAE) between predictions and ground truth, with additional metrics such as energy within threshold (EwT) for OC20. Baselines will include state-of-the-art equivariant and invariant GNNs and Transformer-based models such as SchNet, DimeNet++, SE(3)-Transformer, NequIP, SEGNN, TorchMD-NET, and Graphormer. Ablation studies will be performed to isolate the effects of dot product vs. MLP attention and linear vs. non-linear message passing. Hyperparameters, architecture details, and training times will be carefully documented, and model performance will be compared across all tasks and molecules in each dataset.
1ede15a0aa5204de1f3013d7616a93dbd46fd849.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a minimal yet effective modification of Transformer architectures to achieve SE(3)/E(3)-equivariance using irreps-based features and tensor products, enabling the encoding of geometric symmetries without complicating the graph structure. A novel equivariant graph attention mechanism is proposed, combining MLP-based attention with non-linear message passing, which is more expressive than previous linear or dot product-based attention mechanisms and supports higher-order tensor interactions. The method is claimed to achieve state-of-the-art or competitive results on multiple challenging datasets, with improved training efficiency and scalability compared to existing equivariant and invariant models.

1ee2d51749bb6cd12bbfb61c38762c857d9ec112.title: Reconstructing Training Data with Informed Adversaries
1ee2d51749bb6cd12bbfb61c38762c857d9ec112.research_question: Can an adversary reconstruct individual training data points from a machine learning model when given access to the model and all training data except one, and what factors influence the success of such reconstruction attacks? Additionally, what mitigations, such as differential privacy, are effective against these attacks?
1ee2d51749bb6cd12bbfb61c38762c857d9ec112.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a powerful adversary, informed with all but one training data point and white-box access to the model, can reconstruct the remaining data point with high fidelity, even for complex models such as neural networks. Furthermore, it is posited that differential privacy can effectively mitigate such reconstruction attacks with appropriate parameter settings.
1ee2d51749bb6cd12bbfb61c38762c857d9ec112.proposed_method: A reconstruction attack framework will be developed for both convex and non-convex machine learning models. For convex models, such as logistic regression, a closed-form solution will be derived by solving a system of equations relating the model parameters, known training data, and the unknown target point. For general models, including neural networks, a reconstructor network (RecoNN) will be trained by the adversary. This network will take as input the weights of the target model and output a reconstruction of the missing data point. The adversary will generate a set of shadow models by training on the known dataset plus various candidate points, using these to train the RecoNN to invert the mapping from model parameters to training data. The approach will also investigate the impact of side knowledge, model architecture, training hyperparameters, and randomness in the training process. Differential privacy mechanisms, such as DP-SGD, will be incorporated into the training pipeline to evaluate their effectiveness as mitigations.
1ee2d51749bb6cd12bbfb61c38762c857d9ec112.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification datasets such as MNIST and CIFAR-10. Released models will include both multi-layer perceptrons and convolutional neural networks, trained on subsets of these datasets. The adversary will have access to all but one training point, the model parameters, and the training algorithm (with or without knowledge of internal randomness). Baselines will include nearest neighbor oracles and reconstructions using only available data. Evaluation metrics will include mean squared error (MSE), LPIPS (perceptual similarity), and KL divergence between classifier outputs on targets and reconstructions. The effect of various factors—such as the size of the known dataset, model architecture, training hyperparameters, and the use of differential privacy—will be systematically investigated. The robustness of the attack will be tested under different adversarial knowledge scenarios, including out-of-distribution shadow data and limited access to model parameters.
1ee2d51749bb6cd12bbfb61c38762c857d9ec112.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a general and practical reconstruction attack framework that does not rely on access to model gradients or generative model outputs, making it applicable to a wide range of models and settings. The use of reconstructor networks to invert model parameters to data points is a novel approach for non-convex models. The work systematically analyzes which factors in standard machine learning pipelines affect the success of reconstruction, providing actionable insights for model developers. Furthermore, the research establishes theoretical and empirical connections between differential privacy parameters and resistance to reconstruction, demonstrating that differential privacy can mitigate such attacks in regimes with minimal utility loss. This framework enables a new standard for assessing individual data memorization and privacy leakage in machine learning models.

1f03ef1c0461bd60de904c8626157fe7d89fc465.title: Learning from Memory: Non-Parametric Memory Augmented Self-Supervised Learning of Visual Features
1f03ef1c0461bd60de904c8626157fe7d89fc465.research_question: How can the stability and effectiveness of self-supervised learning (SSL) for visual feature learning be improved without relying on parametric prototypes or additional regularizers, while reducing computational resources and maintaining or enhancing transferability and robustness of learned representations?
1f03ef1c0461bd60de904c8626157fe7d89fc465.hypothesis: Augmenting a neural network with a non-parametric memory component that stores and stochastically samples previous image representations, combined with a consistency-enforcing loss between image views and memory blocks, will yield more stable SSL training, avoid mode collapse without explicit regularizers, and produce highly transferable and robust visual representations with reduced computational cost.
1f03ef1c0461bd60de904c8626157fe7d89fc465.proposed_method: A memory-augmented self-supervised learning framework will be developed, where a neural network encoder is equipped with a non-parametric memory bank that stores a FIFO queue of previously encountered image representations. During training, for each image, multiple augmented views are encoded by student and teacher networks (the latter updated by exponential moving average). Each view's representation is compared to randomly sampled blocks from the memory, computing similarity distributions via cosine similarity and softmax. The learning objective enforces consistency between the similarity distributions of different views of the same image with respect to the memory block, using a cross-entropy loss. Stochastic sampling of memory blocks is employed to regularize training and break ordering bias, and the method operates in a prototype-free manner, requiring no explicit negative sampling or additional regularization terms to avoid collapse. Only the [CLS] token of a Vision Transformer (ViT) backbone is used, reducing memory and computational requirements.
1f03ef1c0461bd60de904c8626157fe7d89fc465.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a wide range of computer vision benchmarks, including linear probing, transfer learning, low-shot classification, image retrieval, clustering, and robustness to background changes. Datasets such as ImageNet-1M, ImageNet-LT, Oxford-5k, Paris-6k, INRIACopydays, CIFAR-10, and IM-9 will be used. Baselines will include state-of-the-art SSL methods such as DINO, iBOT, MOCO-v3, MAE, and supervised ViT models. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy (for k-NN, logistic regression, and linear probing), mean average precision (mAP) for retrieval and copy detection, normalized mutual information (NMI), adjusted mutual information (AMI), and adjusted rand index (ARI) for clustering, as well as training time and GPU memory usage. Ablation studies will assess the effect of memory size, block size, and sampling strategy. The experimental setup will use ViT-S/16 and ViT-B/16 backbones, with standardized training protocols and batch sizes.
1f03ef1c0461bd60de904c8626157fe7d89fc465.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a non-parametric, prototype-free memory augmentation for SSL that formulates learning as consistency over memory-view similarity distributions, eliminating the need for explicit regularizers or negative sampling. Stochastic memory block sampling is used as a novel regularization strategy to improve training stability and representation quality. The method achieves state-of-the-art or competitive results on multiple transfer, retrieval, and robustness benchmarks, while requiring less computational time and memory compared to leading SSL methods. The framework is simple, efficient, and generalizes well across tasks and data regimes, including low-shot and long-tailed scenarios.

1f1b58e92d7a5a6f70eb5b406d30183675e2a732.title: (S)GD over Diagonal Linear Networks: Implicit bias, Large Stepsizes and Edge of Stability
1f1b58e92d7a5a6f70eb5b406d30183675e2a732.research_question: How do stochasticity and large stepsizes influence the implicit regularization and solution properties of gradient descent (GD) and stochastic gradient descent (SGD) when training overparameterized two-layer diagonal linear networks, particularly in sparse regression settings?
1f1b58e92d7a5a6f70eb5b406d30183675e2a732.hypothesis: Large stepsizes and stochasticity in SGD and GD will induce distinct implicit regularization effects, leading to qualitatively different solutions, especially in the recovery of sparse predictors. Specifically, large stepsizes will consistently benefit SGD in sparse recovery, while potentially hindering GD, with these effects being amplified near the edge of stability regime.
1f1b58e92d7a5a6f70eb5b406d30183675e2a732.proposed_method: The proposed research will analyze the dynamics of GD and mini-batch SGD with macroscopic (large) stepsizes on overparameterized two-layer diagonal linear networks (DLNs) in regression tasks. The method involves formulating the training process as a non-convex optimization problem with a specific diagonal parametrization, and deriving a trajectory-dependent implicit regularization characterization for the solutions of both GD and SGD. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to prove convergence of the iterates to global minima under macroscopic stepsizes, and to explicitly characterize the recovered solution via a Bregman divergence minimization involving a hyperbolic entropy potential. The influence of stepsize and minibatch size will be analytically linked to an effective initialization parameter, which modulates the implicit bias of the optimization trajectory. Additional analysis will be performed to connect these findings to the edge of stability phenomenon, where stepsizes approach the divergence threshold.
1f1b58e92d7a5a6f70eb5b406d30183675e2a732.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic noiseless sparse regression tasks, where input features are drawn from a standard Gaussian distribution and targets are generated using a fixed s-sparse ground truth vector. The setup will vary the number of samples, input dimension, sparsity level, and initialization scale. Both GD (full-batch) and SGD (mini-batch, including single-sample) will be evaluated across a wide range of stepsizes, including those near the edge of stability. Baselines will include gradient flow (infinitesimal stepsize) and classical linear regression. Evaluation metrics will include training loss convergence, test loss, and the sparsity and structure of the recovered predictors. The experiments will systematically compare the impact of stepsize and batch size on the implicit bias and generalization performance of GD and SGD, with particular attention to the scale and shape of the effective regularization induced.
1f1b58e92d7a5a6f70eb5b406d30183675e2a732.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel, trajectory-dependent implicit regularization characterization for both GD and SGD with large stepsizes on diagonal linear networks, extending beyond the continuous-time (gradient flow) regime. It provides the first explicit analysis of how stepsize and stochasticity jointly affect the implicit bias and solution structure in overparameterized settings, including the edge of stability regime. The work offers new theoretical insights into why SGD with large stepsizes can outperform GD in sparse recovery, and establishes a direct connection between optimization hyperparameters and the qualitative nature of the recovered solutions. The findings are expected to bridge gaps between empirical observations and theoretical understanding of implicit regularization in deep learning optimization.

1f29cc45de4cc92302d62b161185465e8e3321f5.title: Cascade of phase transitions in the training of energy-based models
1f29cc45de4cc92302d62b161185465e8e3321f5.research_question: How does the feature encoding process unfold during the training of energy-based generative models, specifically Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs), and what are the underlying dynamics and phase transitions associated with the progressive learning of data features in high-dimensional datasets?
1f29cc45de4cc92302d62b161185465e8e3321f5.hypothesis: The training dynamics of energy-based models such as RBMs involve a cascade of second-order phase transitions, each corresponding to the acquisition of new data features, and these transitions are governed by the alignment of the model's weight matrix with the principal components of the data distribution.
1f29cc45de4cc92302d62b161185465e8e3321f5.proposed_method: The proposed research will analytically and numerically investigate the learning dynamics of Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs) by tracking the evolution of the weight matrix through its singular value decomposition (SVD) during training. Theoretical analysis will be conducted using simplified high-dimensional models, such as the Mattis and Hopfield models, to characterize the emergence of phase transitions as the RBM encodes new data features. The methodology will include deriving dynamical equations for the weight matrix and analyzing the conditions under which phase transitions occur, using both Binary-Gaussian and Binary-Binary RBMs. The analysis will be extended to real-world training scenarios, where the alignment of the RBM's singular vectors with the principal components of the dataset will be monitored over the course of training. Additionally, a mean-field finite-size scaling hypothesis will be formulated and tested to characterize the universality class of the observed transitions.
