1f29cc45de4cc92302d62b161185465e8e3321f5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by training Binary-Binary RBMs with varying numbers of hidden nodes on several real datasets, including the Human Genome Dataset (HGD), MNIST, and CelebA. Datasets will be resized to different dimensions to investigate the effect of system size on the sharpness of phase transitions. The evolution of the RBM's weight matrix will be tracked via SVD, with the alignment of singular vectors to principal components and the growth of singular values monitored throughout training. Baselines will include theoretical predictions from the Mattis and Hopfield models, as well as mean-field finite-size scaling laws. Evaluation metrics will include the susceptibility associated with magnetizations along singular vectors, the divergence of susceptibility at critical points, and the scaling behavior of these quantities with system size. MCMC relaxation times will also be measured to assess the impact of phase transitions on model thermalization.
1f29cc45de4cc92302d62b161185465e8e3321f5.novelty_claims: The proposed research claims that the training of RBMs is governed by a cascade of second-order phase transitions, each linked to the progressive encoding of principal data features. This process is analytically characterized and numerically validated, revealing that each new feature learned corresponds to a critical transition in the model's parameter space. The research further establishes that these transitions belong to the mean-field universality class and demonstrates a mean-field finite-size scaling hypothesis for the observed phenomena. The work provides new insights into the hierarchical and stepwise nature of feature learning in energy-based models, with implications for understanding training dynamics, model expressivity, and the computational challenges posed by critical slowing-down near phase transitions.

1f2a20a6efaf83214861dddae4a38a83ae18fe32.title: DeepSeek-Coder: When the Large Language Model Meets Programming - The Rise of Code Intelligence
1f2a20a6efaf83214861dddae4a38a83ae18fe32.research_question: How can open-source large language models be advanced to achieve state-of-the-art code intelligence, rivaling or surpassing closed-source models in code generation, code completion, cross-file reasoning, and program-based mathematical reasoning tasks across diverse programming languages?
1f2a20a6efaf83214861dddae4a38a83ae18fe32.hypothesis: Training large language models from scratch on a high-quality, repository-level, deduplicated, and multi-lingual code corpus, combined with advanced objectives such as fill-in-the-middle and extended context windows, will significantly improve code intelligence performance, closing the gap with or surpassing leading closed-source models.
1f2a20a6efaf83214861dddae4a38a83ae18fe32.proposed_method: A series of open-source large language models will be developed with parameter sizes ranging from 1.3B to 33B, trained from scratch on a 2 trillion token corpus spanning 87 programming languages. The data pipeline will include repository-level organization, dependency parsing for cross-file context alignment, repository-level deduplication, and rigorous quality screening and decontamination to remove test set leakage. Pre-training will employ both next-token prediction and a fill-in-the-middle (FIM) objective, with a 50% FIM rate using the Prefix-Suffix-Middle (PSM) mode, to enhance both code completion and infilling abilities. The models will utilize a decoder-only Transformer architecture with Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE), Grouped-Query Attention (for larger models), and FlashAttention v2 for efficient training and inference. Context windows will be extended to 16K tokens to enable handling of long code sequences, and instruction tuning will be performed using high-quality, human-curated instructional data.
1f2a20a6efaf83214861dddae4a38a83ae18fe32.experiment_details: Extensive experiments will be conducted on public code-related benchmarks, including code generation (HumanEval, MBPP), fill-in-the-middle code completion (HumanEval-FIM), cross-file code completion, and program-based math reasoning (GSM8K, MATH). The models will be compared against state-of-the-art open-source models such as CodeGeeX2, StarCoder, and CodeLlama, as well as closed-source models like Codex (code-cushman-001), GPT-3.5, and GPT-4. Evaluation metrics will include pass@1 accuracy and other standard metrics relevant to each benchmark. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of FIM rates and training strategies. Training and evaluation will be conducted on high-performance GPU clusters with parallelism strategies for scalability.
1f2a20a6efaf83214861dddae4a38a83ae18fe32.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first open-source code LLMs trained from scratch on a 2 trillion token, repository-level deduplicated corpus spanning 87 languages, with explicit modeling of cross-file dependencies. The method pioneers repository-level data construction and deduplication, and systematically investigates the impact of FIM objectives and long-context adaptation for code models. The resulting models are claimed to achieve state-of-the-art performance among open-source code LLMs and, in several benchmarks, surpass leading closed-source models such as Codex and GPT-3.5, while being released under a permissive license for both research and commercial use.

1f346f74e8eabececa4896d734ab9b261f30830d.title: Modular Deep Learning
1f346f74e8eabececa4896d734ab9b261f30830d.research_question: How can modular deep learning architectures be systematically designed to enable effective transfer learning, mitigate negative task interference, and achieve systematic generalization across diverse and non-identically distributed tasks?
1f346f74e8eabececa4896d734ab9b261f30830d.hypothesis: Explicitly modular deep learning architectures, which separate computation, routing, and aggregation functions, will enable positive transfer, compositionality, parameter efficiency, and systematic generalization, outperforming monolithic models in multi-task and transfer learning scenarios.
1f346f74e8eabececa4896d734ab9b261f30830d.proposed_method: A modular deep learning framework will be developed, where models are constructed from autonomous, parameter-efficient modules. The approach will explore various module implementations, including sparse subnetworks, adapter layers, and prefix tuning, integrated into a shared base architecture. A routing function will be designed to select active modules per input or task, with both fixed and learned (hard and soft) routing strategies considered. Aggregation functions will be investigated to combine module outputs, using deterministic operations (e.g., weighted averaging) or learnable neural networks (e.g., attention mechanisms). The training protocol will support joint multi-task learning, continual learning, and post-hoc modularization of pre-trained models, allowing modules to be updated locally and asynchronously.
1f346f74e8eabececa4896d734ab9b261f30830d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a range of transfer learning tasks in natural language processing, computer vision, and speech processing. Benchmarks will include machine translation, cross-lingual transfer, domain adaptation, and cross-modal learning, utilizing standard datasets such as multilingual corpora and image-text datasets. Baselines will consist of monolithic pre-trained models, fully shared multi-task models, and existing parameter-efficient transfer learning methods (e.g., in-context learning, prompt tuning). Evaluation metrics will include task accuracy, sample efficiency, robustness to distribution shift, and parameter/time efficiency. The experimental setup will systematically vary module design, routing, and aggregation strategies to assess their impact on transfer, interference, and generalization.
1f346f74e8eabececa4896d734ab9b261f30830d.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified taxonomy and framework for modular deep learning, systematically decomposing architectures along computation, routing, aggregation, and training dimensions. This approach enables flexible composition and reuse of modules, supports conditional computation, and facilitates positive transfer and systematic generalization. The framework connects and extends previously independent lines of research, providing new insights into the design of modular architectures for scalable, robust, and efficient transfer learning across modalities and tasks.

1f454157062dd48b6065e75cd3fc97d4cd906a04.title: DeepCache: Accelerating Diffusion Models for Free
1f454157062dd48b6065e75cd3fc97d4cd906a04.research_question: How can the computational overhead of diffusion models be significantly reduced at inference time without requiring retraining, while maintaining high image generation quality across diverse datasets and model architectures?
1f454157062dd48b6065e75cd3fc97d4cd906a04.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the temporal redundancy present in the high-level features of diffusion models' denoising steps can be exploited through a caching mechanism, enabling substantial acceleration of inference without the need for retraining, and with minimal degradation in generation quality.
1f454157062dd48b6065e75cd3fc97d4cd906a04.proposed_method: A novel training-free acceleration framework, DeepCache, is proposed to enhance the efficiency of diffusion models during inference. The method leverages the temporal consistency of high-level features across adjacent denoising steps in the reverse diffusion process. By strategically caching these slowly-evolving features within the U-Net architecture, redundant computations are eliminated: high-level features are computed once and reused in subsequent steps, while only low-level features are updated at each step. DeepCache introduces both uniform and non-uniform 1:N caching strategies, where full inference is performed at selected intervals and partial inference (with cached features) is performed in between, with the non-uniform strategy adapting the cache update frequency based on feature similarity dynamics. The approach is compatible with existing fast samplers and does not require any retraining or modification of the original model weights.
1f454157062dd48b6065e75cd3fc97d4cd906a04.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of pre-trained diffusion models, including DDPM, LDM, and Stable Diffusion, across datasets such as CIFAR-10, LSUN-Bedroom, LSUN-Churches, ImageNet, MS-COCO 2017, and PartiPrompts. Evaluation metrics will include FID, sFID, IS, Precision-and-Recall, and CLIP Score. Baselines will consist of state-of-the-art pruning and distillation methods (e.g., Diff-Pruning, BK-SDM, Spectral Diffusion), as well as fast sampling techniques (e.g., DDIM, PLMS). The experimental setup will systematically vary the caching interval N and compare both uniform and non-uniform caching strategies, reporting computational cost (MACs), throughput, speedup ratios, and generation quality. Ablation studies will assess the impact of caching and shallow network inference, and visualizations will illustrate qualitative effects of different caching intervals.
1f454157062dd48b6065e75cd3fc97d4cd906a04.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a training-free, architecture-level acceleration paradigm for diffusion models that exploits temporal feature redundancy, enabling significant speedups (up to 7x) without retraining. DeepCache is the first to dynamically compress diffusion models at runtime by caching high-level features, and it is compatible with existing fast sampling methods. The method achieves superior or comparable generation quality to retraining-based compression and fast sampling baselines, and provides a new perspective for efficient inference in large-scale pre-trained diffusion models.

1f46546393d138c3953523c16883ede511c6be01.title: Revisiting Realistic Test-Time Training: Sequential Inference and Adaptation by Anchored Clustering
1f46546393d138c3953523c16883ede511c6be01.research_question: How can models be effectively adapted to target domains under distribution shift in realistic deployment scenarios where source data is unavailable and test samples arrive sequentially, requiring instant inference and adaptation?
1f46546393d138c3953523c16883ede511c6be01.hypothesis: Anchored clustering of target domain features to source domain statistics, combined with pseudo label filtering and global feature alignment, enables more effective and efficient test-time adaptation than existing methods, even under strict sequential inference protocols.
1f46546393d138c3953523c16883ede511c6be01.proposed_method: A novel test-time adaptation framework is proposed based on anchored clustering, where both source and target domain feature distributions are modeled as mixtures of Gaussians, each component corresponding to a category. During deployment, target domain clusters are matched to source domain anchors by minimizing the KL-Divergence between corresponding Gaussian components, enabling category-wise alignment. Pseudo labels for target samples are generated and filtered using temporal consistency and posterior probability thresholds to reduce the impact of noisy predictions. An exponential moving average strategy is used to iteratively update target cluster statistics for efficient online adaptation. Additionally, a global feature alignment loss is introduced by minimizing the KL-Divergence between the global feature distributions of source and target domains, ensuring that all target samples contribute to adaptation.
1f46546393d138c3953523c16883ede511c6be01.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six benchmark datasets for test-time training, including CIFAR10-C, CIFAR100-C, CIFAR10.1, VisDA-C, ImageNet-C, and ModelNet40-C, covering both image and 3D point cloud domains. The evaluation will follow four categorized test-time training protocols, with a focus on the most realistic sequential one-pass protocol (sTTT), where test samples are streamed and predictions must be made instantly. Baselines for comparison include direct testing, batch normalization adaptation, entropy minimization (TENT), classifier prototype adjustment (T3A), source-free domain adaptation (SHOT), and prior test-time training methods (TTT-R, TTT++). Evaluation metrics include classification error rates and cumulative error over the test stream. Ablation studies will assess the contributions of anchored clustering, pseudo label filtering, global feature alignment, and compatibility with contrastive learning branches. Computational efficiency will be measured in terms of per-sample wall-clock time under various queue and update epoch settings.
1f46546393d138c3953523c16883ede511c6be01.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new sequential test-time training protocol (sTTT) that enforces instant inference and prohibits modification of the source training objective, addressing confusion in prior TTT evaluations. Anchored clustering is developed to enable category-wise alignment between source and target domains at test time, a capability not present in existing methods. The method further innovates by integrating lightweight pseudo label filtering based on temporal consistency and posterior thresholds, as well as an efficient iterative updating mechanism for online adaptation. The approach is shown to be complementary to existing TTT techniques and achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple datasets and protocols.

1f5c1e202e0bb2e8f6d627eb896adcd4cf8e323b.title: Perplexed by Perplexity: Perplexity-Based Data Pruning With Small Reference Models
1f5c1e202e0bb2e8f6d627eb896adcd4cf8e323b.research_question: Can small language models be used to effectively perform perplexity-based data pruning on large-scale text datasets to improve the downstream performance and training efficiency of much larger language models, and how does the domain composition of the dataset and training regime affect the efficacy of such pruning?
1f5c1e202e0bb2e8f6d627eb896adcd4cf8e323b.hypothesis: Small reference language models can identify high-quality subsets of large-scale text datasets via perplexity-based data pruning, leading to improved downstream task performance and training efficiency for significantly larger language models, with the effectiveness of pruning dependent on dataset domain composition and training regime.
1f5c1e202e0bb2e8f6d627eb896adcd4cf8e323b.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves training a small reference language model (e.g., 125 million parameters) on a random subset of a large pretraining dataset. The reference model is then used to compute the perplexity of each sample in the remaining training split of the dataset. Samples are selected for pruning based on their perplexity values, using criteria such as selecting the lowest, median, or highest perplexity samples, and a specified selection rate (e.g., top 50%). The pruned dataset is then used to train a much larger language model (e.g., 1B or 3B parameters) from scratch using the standard next-token prediction objective. This approach is systematically evaluated across different dataset compositions and training regimes, including over-training and data-constrained scenarios.
1f5c1e202e0bb2e8f6d627eb896adcd4cf8e323b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using two large-scale text datasets with distinct domain compositions: The Pile (diverse, curated domains) and Dolma (web-scrape skewed). Reference models with 125M parameters will be used for pruning, while final models will have 1B and 3B parameters, all based on the MPT transformer architecture. Models will be trained to Chinchilla-optimal token budgets and evaluated on 33 downstream question-answering tasks using the MosaicML evaluation gauntlet, reporting normalized accuracy against random guessing. Baselines will include training on unpruned data, and comparisons will be made for different pruning criteria and selection rates. Additional experiments will assess performance in over-trained (5x token budget) and data-constrained (varying data repetition) regimes, as well as the impact of pruning on domain composition and the reliability of upstream perplexity as an evaluation metric.
1f5c1e202e0bb2e8f6d627eb896adcd4cf8e323b.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a systematic investigation of using small reference language models for perplexity-based data pruning to improve the performance of much larger language models, demonstrating that such pruning can yield significant downstream gains and increased training efficiency even when the reference model is up to 30x smaller. The approach is evaluated across multiple dataset compositions, revealing that optimal pruning strategies are highly sensitive to domain makeup. The method is further validated in non-standard regimes, such as over-training and data-constrained settings, and challenges the common practice of using upstream perplexity as a proxy for downstream performance, showing that it can be misleading. The work provides new insights into the transferability of pruning parameters and the effects of pruning on domain representation within datasets.

1f8786ee58b5957039cdaf0dd70df62586bbcff4.title: Asynchronous Local-SGD Training for Language Modeling
1f8786ee58b5957039cdaf0dd70df62586bbcff4.research_question: How can asynchronous Local-SGD be made as effective and efficient as synchronous Local-SGD for large-scale language modeling, especially in the presence of heterogeneous worker hardware and varying model sizes?
1f8786ee58b5957039cdaf0dd70df62586bbcff4.hypothesis: Introducing a delayed Nesterov momentum update and dynamically adjusting local training steps based on worker speed will enable asynchronous Local-SGD to match or surpass the convergence and time efficiency of synchronous Local-SGD for language modeling tasks.
1f8786ee58b5957039cdaf0dd70df62586bbcff4.proposed_method: A novel asynchronous Local-SGD framework will be developed for distributed language model training. The approach will incorporate two main innovations: (1) a Delayed Nesterov (DN) momentum update, which buffers pseudo-gradients and updates the server-side momentum only after aggregating a set number of updates, thereby mitigating the negative effects of stale gradients and excessive momentum amplification; and (2) Dynamic Local Updates (DyLU), which assigns each worker a number of local training steps proportional to its computational speed, ensuring more synchronized progress and reducing the impact of stragglers. The method will also employ per-shard learning rate scheduling with linear warmup and cosine decay, and a grace period mechanism for model synchronization to further balance update staleness. The framework will allow for flexible data shard allocation and adaptive learning rate schedules per worker.
1f8786ee58b5957039cdaf0dd70df62586bbcff4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the C4 dataset for language modeling, using models ranging from 20M to 150M parameters. The evaluation will include scenarios with varying numbers of workers (4, 8, 16) and different levels of hardware heterogeneity. Baselines will include single-worker finetuning with enlarged batch size, synchronous Local-SGD (DiLoCo), and naive asynchronous Local-SGD with various optimizer combinations (e.g., AdamW+Nesterov, AdamW+SGD). Additional comparisons will be made against asynchronous Local-SGD variants employing polynomial discounting, thresholding, delay compensation, and buffer-based aggregation. Evaluation metrics will include perplexity versus update steps and perplexity versus wall-clock time. Experiments will also include ablation studies on the effect of the momentum blending parameter and the number of local steps per worker.
1f8786ee58b5957039cdaf0dd70df62586bbcff4.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new combination of delayed Nesterov momentum updates and dynamic local step adjustment tailored for asynchronous Local-SGD in language modeling. This approach addresses the unique optimization challenges of asynchronous distributed training, such as momentum amplification and gradient staleness, which are not adequately handled by existing methods. The framework is claimed to match the convergence of synchronous Local-SGD in terms of perplexity per update, while significantly improving wall-clock efficiency, especially in heterogeneous environments. The method is also the first to systematically analyze and mitigate the impact of asynchrony-induced momentum effects in large-scale language model training.

1f898d66acabff511a3871b82799aa73c0055402.title: A Reparameterized Discrete Diffusion Model for Text Generation
1f898d66acabff511a3871b82799aa73c0055402.research_question: How can discrete diffusion probabilistic models be improved to enhance the quality and efficiency of natural language text generation, particularly in comparison to existing discrete and continuous diffusion approaches?
1f898d66acabff511a3871b82799aa73c0055402.hypothesis: Explicitly reparameterizing the sampling process in discrete diffusion models to incorporate a routing mechanism for selective token denoising will yield more effective training objectives, enable more flexible and discriminative decoding strategies, and result in significant improvements in text generation quality and efficiency over existing diffusion-based and non-autoregressive baselines.
1f898d66acabff511a3871b82799aa73c0055402.proposed_method: A novel family of Reparameterized Discrete Diffusion Models (RDMs) will be developed, leveraging an alternative yet equivalent formulation of the discrete diffusion backward process. The key idea is to explicitly model a routing mechanism at each diffusion step, where each token is either denoised or reset to a noisy state according to a stochastic routing variable. The joint generative process will be parameterized such that the routing and denoising decisions are modeled separately, with the routing variable following a Bernoulli distribution whose parameter can be adaptively set. Training will be based on a reweighted cross-entropy loss, where only noisy tokens are considered and the loss is weighted by the routing probabilities, greatly simplifying the objective compared to standard KL-based diffusion training. During sampling, an adaptive routing strategy will be employed, where tokens are selectively denoised based on model confidence scores, allowing for more expressive and efficient decoding.
1f898d66acabff511a3871b82799aa73c0055402.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several standard text generation benchmarks, including machine translation (IWSLT14 DE-EN, WMT14 EN-DE, WMT16 EN-RO), question generation (Quasar-T), and paraphrasing (Quora Question Pairs). The proposed RDMs will be compared against vanilla discrete diffusion models (multinomial and absorbing), continuous diffusion models (e.g., DiffuSeq, CDCD), non-autoregressive baselines (CMLM, Levenshtein Transformer, DisCo), and autoregressive models (Transformer, GPT2). Evaluation metrics will include BLEU, ROUGE-L, BERTScore, and Dist-1. The experimental setup will control for model size (90-110M parameters) and measure both generation quality and decoding speed, with ablations on training reweighting strategies and decoding mechanisms. All models will be implemented in the FairSeq toolkit, and decoding will be performed with varying numbers of diffusion steps to assess trade-offs between quality and efficiency.
1f898d66acabff511a3871b82799aa73c0055402.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a reparameterized formulation of discrete diffusion models that explicitly models a routing mechanism for token-level denoising, resulting in a greatly simplified and more flexible training objective. The method enables adaptive, discriminative decoding strategies that significantly improve both the quality and speed of text generation compared to prior discrete and continuous diffusion models. The framework generalizes various discrete diffusion processes and allows for shared training objectives across a broad family of routing distributions, facilitating extensibility and advanced search methods in sampling. Extensive empirical results demonstrate substantial improvements over existing baselines, including achieving competitive or superior performance to autoregressive models with much faster decoding.

1f9cda9ea4d320beebfb3263d42fd694fe49aac8.title: Understanding Self-Distillation in the Presence of Label Noise
1f9cda9ea4d320beebfb3263d42fd694fe49aac8.research_question: How does self-distillation affect model performance in supervised learning tasks when the training labels are corrupted by noise, and under what conditions does self-distillation outperform standard regularization or teacher-only training?
1f9cda9ea4d320beebfb3263d42fd694fe49aac8.hypothesis: Self-distillation, especially with an appropriately chosen imitation parameter, can provide superior generalization and robustness to label noise compared to standard regularization or teacher-only training, and in high-noise regimes, the optimal imitation parameter may exceed the conventional range.
1f9cda9ea4d320beebfb3263d42fd694fe49aac8.proposed_method: The proposed research will theoretically and empirically investigate self-distillation in supervised learning with noisy labels. The methodology involves first training a teacher model on noisy data using regularized loss (squared loss for regression, cross-entropy for classification), then training a student model of identical architecture using a weighted combination of the teacher's predictions and the original noisy labels. The imitation parameter (ξ) controlling this weighting will be analytically optimized, and its range will be extended beyond the conventional [0,1] interval to explore potential benefits of 'anti-learning' the noisy labels. Theoretical analysis will include bias-variance decomposition for linear regression and population accuracy characterization for logistic regression under random label corruption, leveraging tools such as singular value decomposition and first-order Maclaurin expansion for non-linearities. Conditions under which self-distillation outperforms optimal regularization will be formally derived.
1f9cda9ea4d320beebfb3263d42fd694fe49aac8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. For linear regression and multi-class classification, datasets with controlled amounts of label corruption (e.g., 30% and 50% randomly flipped labels) will be used. The student model's performance will be compared against the teacher and standard regularization baselines, with the imitation parameter ξ varied and optimized (including values ξ > 1). Evaluation metrics will include expected estimation error for regression and classification accuracy for classification tasks. For logistic regression, balanced binary classification datasets with random label flipping will be used, and population accuracy will be measured for both teacher and student models. Empirical results will be corroborated with theoretical predictions, and the utility of the teacher's predictions as a function of noise level will be quantified.
1f9cda9ea4d320beebfb3263d42fd694fe49aac8.novelty_claims: This research proposes the first theoretical characterization of self-distillation with cross-entropy loss in the presence of label noise, including explicit bias-variance tradeoff analysis and conditions for superiority over optimal regularization. It introduces the novel insight that the optimal imitation parameter can exceed one in high-noise regimes, suggesting practical benefits from 'anti-learning' noisy labels. The work also provides the first provable results showing when a self-distilled student can outperform its teacher in classification accuracy under label corruption, and quantifies the regimes where this occurs. These contributions extend the theoretical understanding of self-distillation beyond prior work limited to squared loss and offer actionable recommendations for robust model training in noisy environments.

1fa298e3f745099d39ca5bd088fcb62f87e8cc2f.title: HunyuanVideo: A Systematic Framework For Large Video Generative Models
1fa298e3f745099d39ca5bd088fcb62f87e8cc2f.research_question: How can an open-source video generative model be developed to achieve performance on par with or surpassing leading closed-source video foundation models, while enabling high visual quality, motion dynamics, text-video alignment, and advanced filming techniques?
1fa298e3f745099d39ca5bd088fcb62f87e8cc2f.hypothesis: A systematically designed large-scale open-source video generative model, leveraging advanced data curation, hierarchical filtering, structured captioning, scalable architecture, and progressive training strategies, can match or exceed the performance of state-of-the-art closed-source video generation models in terms of visual quality, motion dynamics, and text-video alignment.
1fa298e3f745099d39ca5bd088fcb62f87e8cc2f.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed for large-scale video generation, comprising several key components. First, a rigorous data curation and hierarchical filtering pipeline will be implemented for both images and videos, ensuring high quality, diversity, and compliance with privacy standards. Structured, multi-dimensional captions will be generated for all training data using an in-house vision-language model, and camera movement classifiers will be trained to enrich metadata. The model architecture will utilize a Causal 3D Variational Autoencoder (VAE) to compress videos and images into a latent space, enabling efficient training at high resolutions and long durations. A unified Transformer-based diffusion model with a dual-stream to single-stream design will be employed, integrating advanced multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for text encoding and leveraging rotary position embeddings for spatiotemporal understanding. Neural scaling laws will be empirically established for both image and video domains to guide optimal model and dataset sizing, and a progressive multi-stage training regime will be adopted, including pretraining on images, joint image-video training, and human-annotated fine-tuning.
1fa298e3f745099d39ca5bd088fcb62f87e8cc2f.experiment_details: Extensive experiments will be conducted using large-scale, internet-sourced datasets of both images and videos, curated and filtered through the proposed hierarchical pipeline. The model will be compared against leading closed-source and open-source video generative models, including Runway Gen-3, Luma 1.6, and top-performing commercial Chinese models. Over 1,500 representative text prompts will be used for evaluation, with a group of 60 human evaluators providing professional assessments. Evaluation metrics will include visual quality, motion dynamics, text-video alignment, and advanced filming techniques, with both quantitative and qualitative analyses performed. Ablation studies will be conducted to assess the impact of data quality, captioning strategies, and architectural choices.
1fa298e3f745099d39ca5bd088fcb62f87e8cc2f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the largest open-source video generative model to date, featuring a systematic framework that integrates advanced data curation, structured captioning, and a scalable, unified architecture. Key innovations include a hierarchical data filtering pipeline, structured multi-dimensional captioning for improved generalization, a Causal 3D VAE for efficient latent compression, and empirically derived neural scaling laws for optimal resource allocation. The approach enables high-quality, controllable video generation and aims to bridge the gap between closed-source and open-source communities, fostering broader innovation and accessibility in video foundation models.

1fa674b4e1c82cf648868be2568637fdfb5fb1b3.title: What's "up" with vision-language models? Investigating their struggle with spatial reasoning
1fa674b4e1c82cf648868be2568637fdfb5fb1b3.research_question: Can vision-language models reliably perform fine-grained spatial reasoning, such as distinguishing basic spatial relations (e.g., 'left of', 'right of', 'on', 'under') between objects in images, and what are the underlying causes of their limitations in this area?
1fa674b4e1c82cf648868be2568637fdfb5fb1b3.hypothesis: Current vision-language models struggle with basic spatial reasoning due to insufficient and ambiguous spatial relationship data in large-scale pretraining corpora, and simple modeling interventions or finetuning are not sufficient to overcome these limitations.
1fa674b4e1c82cf648868be2568637fdfb5fb1b3.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation framework will be developed to assess vision-language models' capacity for spatial reasoning using three newly curated benchmarks: What’sUp (tightly controlled real-world photographs with minimal background and balanced spatial relations), COCO-spatial (curated from COCO validation data with mutually exclusive spatial captions), and GQA-spatial (filtered from GQA validation data for unambiguous spatial questions). Each benchmark will present images paired with captions that differ only in spatial prepositions, requiring models to select the correct caption. The methodology includes a detailed corpus analysis of large-scale pretraining data (e.g., LAION-2B) to quantify the frequency and ambiguity of spatial prepositions, as well as targeted modeling interventions such as re-normalizing caption priors, substituting more frequent spatial terms, and various finetuning strategies (including hard negative mining and up-weighting preposition-containing instances). Linear analogy tests in image representation space will be used to probe whether spatial concepts are encoded similarly to other visual attributes like color.
1fa674b4e1c82cf648868be2568637fdfb5fb1b3.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate 18 vision-language models spanning a variety of architectures (one-stack vs. two-stack), training objectives (contrastive vs. generative), and pretraining datasets. Each model will be tested in a zero-shot setting and, where applicable, after finetuning on downstream tasks or curated spatial datasets. The primary evaluation metric will be accuracy in selecting the correct caption among distractors, with additional pairwise and setwise accuracy metrics for What’sUp. Human performance will be estimated as an upper bound by expert annotation. Baselines will include random and text-only models. Further experiments will analyze the impact of finetuning on spatially enriched subsets of LAION, as well as the effect of hard negative caption generation. Linear analogy accuracy in the representation space will be measured for both spatial relations and color attributes as a control.
1fa674b4e1c82cf648868be2568637fdfb5fb1b3.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces three new, tightly controlled benchmarks specifically designed to isolate and evaluate spatial reasoning in vision-language models, overcoming the confounds and biases present in existing datasets. The approach systematically investigates the root causes of spatial reasoning failures by combining corpus analysis, targeted interventions, and diagnostic probing of model representations. The work provides the first comprehensive evidence that current large-scale pretraining corpora lack sufficient spatial relationship data, and that simple modeling or data interventions are insufficient, thus charting a path for future research on more effective spatial supervision and model architectures.

1fa945c69d2b67d49af88734d3b5fa527d24f910.title: Better by Default: Strong Pre-Tuned MLPs and Boosted Trees on Tabular Data
1fa945c69d2b67d49af88734d3b5fa527d24f910.research_question: How can the performance and usability of machine learning models for classification and regression on tabular data be improved by developing stronger neural network architectures and optimizing default hyperparameters for both neural and tree-based models, without relying on extensive dataset-specific hyperparameter tuning?
1fa945c69d2b67d49af88734d3b5fa527d24f910.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that (1) enhancing the multilayer perceptron (MLP) architecture with targeted architectural, preprocessing, and initialization improvements will yield neural models that are competitive with or superior to gradient-boosted decision trees (GBDTs) on tabular data benchmarks; and (2) meta-tuning default hyperparameters for both MLPs and GBDTs across a large, diverse set of datasets will result in default configurations that perform nearly as well as dataset-specific hyperparameter optimization, thus reducing the need for expensive tuning.
1fa945c69d2b67d49af88734d3b5fa527d24f910.proposed_method: A novel MLP architecture, termed RealMLP, will be developed by integrating a suite of architectural and training improvements, including robust feature preprocessing (robust scaling and smooth clipping), advanced numerical and categorical embeddings (such as periodic bias linear DenseNet embeddings for numerical features), learnable feature scaling layers, parametric activation functions (e.g., SELU/Mish with learnable parameters), and data-driven initialization schemes. Training strategies will incorporate AdamW optimization with nonstandard momentum parameters, multi-cycle learning rate schedules, dropout and weight decay scheduling, and label smoothing for classification. Default hyperparameters for both RealMLP and leading GBDT implementations (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) will be meta-optimized using a large meta-train benchmark of diverse tabular datasets, employing semi-automatic search and manual refinement. The resulting tuned defaults will be evaluated on disjoint meta-test benchmarks to assess generalization.
1fa945c69d2b67d49af88734d3b5fa527d24f910.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a comprehensive suite of tabular datasets, with a meta-train benchmark of 118 datasets for hyperparameter tuning and a disjoint meta-test benchmark of 90 datasets for evaluation, covering both classification and regression tasks. Additional evaluation will be performed on the GBDT-friendly benchmark by Grinsztajn et al. (2022). Each model configuration (library defaults, tuned defaults, and hyperparameter-optimized) will be assessed using repeated random splits (10 per dataset), with metrics including shifted geometric mean classification error, normalized RMSE, and AUROC. Baselines will include standard MLPs, ResNet, FT-Transformer, TabR, and leading GBDTs, as well as model selection and ensembling strategies. Training times and time-accuracy tradeoffs will be systematically measured, and ablation studies will be performed to isolate the impact of individual architectural improvements.
1fa945c69d2b67d49af88734d3b5fa527d24f910.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a robustly improved MLP architecture (RealMLP) with a novel combination of preprocessing, embedding, scaling, activation, and initialization techniques tailored for tabular data. It establishes a meta-learning framework for tuning default hyperparameters across a large and diverse set of datasets, providing strong out-of-the-box performance for both neural and tree-based models. The approach demonstrates that carefully meta-tuned defaults can rival or surpass hyperparameter optimization on new datasets, significantly reducing the computational burden of model selection. Additionally, the improvements are shown to be transferable to other neural architectures, and the methodology enables efficient algorithm selection and ensembling with superior time-accuracy tradeoffs.

1fcaafeb72142fe3d1a5d698a072d69778d244b0.title: Search-R1: Training LLMs to Reason and Leverage Search Engines with Reinforcement Learning
1fcaafeb72142fe3d1a5d698a072d69778d244b0.research_question: How can large language models be trained to autonomously and effectively leverage search engines for improved reasoning and up-to-date information retrieval during complex question answering tasks?
1fcaafeb72142fe3d1a5d698a072d69778d244b0.hypothesis: Training large language models with reinforcement learning frameworks that interleave reasoning and search engine interactions will enable more effective multi-turn retrieval and reasoning, resulting in improved performance on complex question answering tasks compared to existing retrieval-augmented and tool-use approaches.
1fcaafeb72142fe3d1a5d698a072d69778d244b0.proposed_method: A novel reinforcement learning framework, SEARCH-R1, will be developed to enable large language models (LLMs) to autonomously generate and execute multiple search queries during step-by-step reasoning. The method will model the search engine as part of the environment, allowing LLMs to interleave token generation with real-time retrieval in a multi-turn fashion. Special tokens will be used to demarcate reasoning (<think>...</think>), search queries (<search>...</search>), retrieved information (<information>...</information>), and final answers (<answer>...</answer>). The RL objective will be optimized using either Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) or Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), with loss masking applied to exclude retrieved tokens from policy gradient updates, ensuring stable training. A simple outcome-based reward function, such as exact match with ground truth, will be used to guide learning without the need for complex or neural reward models.
1fcaafeb72142fe3d1a5d698a072d69778d244b0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on seven benchmark datasets covering general and multi-hop question answering: NQ, TriviaQA, PopQA, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, Musique, and Bamboogle. Two LLMs, Qwen-2.5-3B and Qwen-2.5-7B (both base and instruction-tuned variants), will be used. The retrieval component will utilize the 2018 Wikipedia dump as the knowledge source and E5 as the retriever, with three passages retrieved per query for all retrieval-based methods. Baselines will include direct inference, chain-of-thought, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), IRCoT, Search-o1, supervised fine-tuning, RL-based fine-tuning without search, and rejection sampling. Evaluation will be performed using the Exact Match (EM) metric, and all methods will be compared under identical retrieval, training data, and LLM initialization conditions.
1fcaafeb72142fe3d1a5d698a072d69778d244b0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a reinforcement learning framework that explicitly integrates search engine interactions into LLM reasoning, supporting multi-turn, interleaved search and reasoning steps. The method leverages retrieved token masking for stable RL optimization and employs a simple outcome-based reward function, avoiding the need for complex reward models or large-scale annotated trajectories. This framework enables autonomous, strategic search query generation and real-time information utilization, achieving significant improvements over existing retrieval-augmented and tool-use baselines. Additionally, the approach provides new empirical insights into RL optimization strategies, LLM model selection, and response dynamics in retrieval-augmented reasoning.

1fd31aad1efb7a17d56ee65d6b7b589980102b15.title: Quantized Spike-driven Transformer
1fd31aad1efb7a17d56ee65d6b7b589980102b15.research_question: How can spike-driven Transformer architectures be made more energy-efficient and compact through quantization, while maintaining high performance on visual tasks such as image classification, object detection, semantic segmentation, and transfer learning?
1fd31aad1efb7a17d56ee65d6b7b589980102b15.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a bi-level optimization strategy, combining an information-enhanced spiking neuron model and a fine-grained distillation scheme, can mitigate the performance degradation typically caused by low-bit quantization in spike-driven Transformers, thereby achieving both high energy efficiency and competitive accuracy.
1fd31aad1efb7a17d56ee65d6b7b589980102b15.proposed_method: A quantized spike-driven Transformer (QSD-Transformer) will be developed by quantizing synaptic weights from 32-bit to low-bit representations (e.g., 2, 3, or 4 bits) throughout the model, including convolutional, fully connected, and self-attention layers. To address the spike information distortion (SID) problem arising from quantization, a bi-level optimization strategy will be employed. At the lower level, an information-enhanced Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (IE-LIF) neuron will be introduced, which uses multi-bit outputs during training to maximize information entropy and then converts to binary spikes for inference, preserving spike-driven characteristics. A membrane potential rectify function will be applied within the Q-SDSA module to align the attention score distributions with those of ANN Transformers. At the upper level, a fine-grained distillation (FGD) scheme will be implemented, minimizing the norm distance between the attention matrices of the QSD-Transformer and a full-precision ANN Transformer teacher, thus aligning their information distributions. The overall training objective will combine cross-entropy loss with the proposed distillation loss.
1fd31aad1efb7a17d56ee65d6b7b589980102b15.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of computer vision tasks. For image classification, the ImageNet-1K dataset will be used, with comparisons against state-of-the-art SNN and ANN models. Object detection will be evaluated on the COCO 2017 dataset using Mask R-CNN as the detection head, and semantic segmentation will be tested on ADE20K with SemanticFPN. Transfer learning capabilities will be assessed on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and CIFAR10-DVS datasets. Baselines will include various spike-driven and ANN Transformer models, with ablations on quantization bit-width, the presence of IE-LIF and FGD modules, and activity bit configurations. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy, mean average precision (mAP@0.5), mean Intersection over Union (MIoU), parameter count, and estimated power consumption. All models will be initialized with pre-trained weights where appropriate, and training will use standard optimization and initialization techniques.
1fd31aad1efb7a17d56ee65d6b7b589980102b15.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a quantized spike-driven Transformer architecture that achieves state-of-the-art accuracy in the SNN domain while drastically reducing model size and power consumption. The bi-level optimization strategy is novel in its combination of an information-enhanced spiking neuron (IE-LIF) and a fine-grained distillation scheme, specifically designed to address the spike information distortion problem unique to quantized spike-driven self-attention. The method demonstrates robust applicability across multiple vision tasks and architectures, and establishes new benchmarks for energy-efficient, high-performance SNN Transformers.

1fdf449c96fbac0789cf8dfae15b788905407fd3.title: Evaluating the Ripple Effects of Knowledge Editing in Language Models
1fdf449c96fbac0789cf8dfae15b788905407fd3.research_question: How can the evaluation of knowledge editing in language models be extended to systematically assess the broader, logically implied changes—'ripple effects'—that result from editing a single factual statement, and how well do current editing methods integrate such edits into the model's knowledge base?
1fdf449c96fbac0789cf8dfae15b788905407fd3.hypothesis: Current knowledge editing methods for language models are effective at locally updating individual facts but often fail to propagate logically necessary changes to related facts, resulting in inconsistent or incomplete updates to the model's knowledge. A comprehensive evaluation framework that tests for ripple effects will reveal these limitations and guide the development of more robust editing techniques.
1fdf449c96fbac0789cf8dfae15b788905407fd3.proposed_method: A novel evaluation framework will be developed to systematically assess the ripple effects of factual edits in language models. This framework will define six evaluation criteria—Logical Generalization, Compositionality I and II, Subject Aliasing, Preservation, and Relation Specificity—each targeting a distinct type of logical or compositional implication that should be updated following a factual edit. A large-scale diagnostic benchmark, RIPPLEEDITS, will be constructed, comprising 5,000 factual edits (including both real and synthetic edits) and a set of natural language test queries for each edit, generated from Wikidata triplets and manually crafted templates. The methodology will include both the creation of edits (modifications and injections) and the generation of corresponding test queries that probe the model's ability to update, retain, or preserve related facts as dictated by logical rules and knowledge graph structure.
1fdf449c96fbac0789cf8dfae15b788905407fd3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several recent autoregressive language models of varying sizes, including GPT-2, GPT-J, GPT-NeoX, LLaMA, and GPT-3, using state-of-the-art knowledge editing algorithms such as ROME, MEMIT, and MEND, as well as a simple in-context editing (ICE) baseline. The evaluation will filter for successfully applied edits and pre-edit correct answers to ensure meaningful assessment. Each model-method combination will be tested on the full RIPPLEEDITS benchmark, with accuracy measured for each evaluation criterion. Baselines will include both parameter-editing and non-parametric (in-context) approaches. Metrics will include average accuracy per criterion, overall accuracy, and error type analysis, with additional breakdowns by entity popularity and model size.
1fdf449c96fbac0789cf8dfae15b788905407fd3.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a comprehensive evaluation framework and benchmark (RIPPLEEDITS) specifically designed to assess the ripple effects of factual edits in language models, addressing a critical gap in current knowledge editing evaluation. The framework formalizes and operationalizes multiple types of logical and compositional implications that should be updated after an edit, going beyond existing benchmarks that focus only on local or paraphrased edits. The approach enables fine-grained analysis of model behavior post-edit and highlights the limitations of current editing methods, while also demonstrating that in-context editing can outperform parametric approaches on ripple effect consistency. The benchmark and methodology are intended to set a new standard for evaluating and developing knowledge editing techniques.

204008df9e9d4e6499f48add49291c12f3aa1ffc.title: Barren plateaus in variational quantum computing
204008df9e9d4e6499f48add49291c12f3aa1ffc.research_question: What are the fundamental causes of barren plateaus in variational quantum computing, and how can their detrimental effects on trainability be understood, avoided, or mitigated through algorithmic design, circuit architecture, and initialization strategies?
204008df9e9d4e6499f48add49291c12f3aa1ffc.hypothesis: Barren plateaus in variational quantum computing arise primarily due to the curse of dimensionality, circuit expressiveness, and the interplay of initial state, measurement operators, and noise; by carefully constraining circuit expressiveness, leveraging problem-inspired inductive biases, and employing shallow circuits or tailored initialization, it is possible to avoid or mitigate barren plateaus and improve trainability.
204008df9e9d4e6499f48add49291c12f3aa1ffc.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted to analyze the origins and mechanisms of barren plateaus in variational quantum algorithms. The approach will involve formalizing the relationship between circuit expressiveness (as quantified by the dynamical Lie algebra), the structure of initial states and measurement operators, and the scaling of gradient variance with system size. Analytical tools such as representation theory, Weingarten calculus, and Markov chain analysis will be used to derive scaling laws for gradient concentration under various circuit architectures and noise models. The study will also design and evaluate new circuit architectures that encode problem-specific symmetries or restrict expressiveness, as well as initialization and measurement strategies that align with polynomially large subspaces, to empirically test their impact on gradient scaling and trainability.
204008df9e9d4e6499f48add49291c12f3aa1ffc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using both simulated and, where feasible, real quantum hardware. A variety of variational quantum circuits will be implemented, including hardware-efficient ansatzes, problem-inspired ansatzes (such as QAOA and UCCSD), and circuits with reduced expressiveness (e.g., matchgate circuits, symmetry-constrained circuits). Datasets will include standard quantum chemistry Hamiltonians, combinatorial optimization problems, and synthetic benchmarks designed to probe specific aspects of barren plateau formation. Baselines will include randomly initialized deep circuits, shallow circuits, and circuits with various initialization and measurement schemes. Evaluation metrics will focus on the scaling of gradient variance, success probability of optimization, number of measurement shots required, and classical simulability. Key experimental variables will include circuit depth, number of qubits, noise strength, and the presence or absence of problem-specific inductive biases.
204008df9e9d4e6499f48add49291c12f3aa1ffc.novelty_claims: The proposed research will systematically unify and extend the theoretical understanding of barren plateaus by connecting them to the curse of dimensionality, circuit expressiveness, and the algebraic structure of variational circuits. It will introduce new analytical tools for diagnosing and predicting barren plateaus, and propose concrete algorithmic and architectural strategies—such as symmetry-constrained circuits, shallow architectures, and tailored initialization—that can provably avoid or mitigate barren plateaus. The work will also clarify the trade-off between avoiding barren plateaus and maintaining quantum advantage, highlighting the link between barren plateau avoidance and classical simulability. These contributions will provide actionable guidelines for the design of scalable and trainable variational quantum algorithms.

205c04ed3f3a4442e60eca41e15d29ef40b56b55.title: Grokfast: Accelerated Grokking by Amplifying Slow Gradients
205c04ed3f3a4442e60eca41e15d29ef40b56b55.research_question: How can the generalization phase in neural networks exhibiting the grokking phenomenon be accelerated, particularly by manipulating the training dynamics to reduce the delay between overfitting and generalization across diverse tasks and architectures?
205c04ed3f3a4442e60eca41e15d29ef40b56b55.hypothesis: Amplifying the slow-varying (low-frequency) components of the gradient signal during training will accelerate the onset of generalization in models that exhibit the grokking phenomenon, reducing the number of training iterations required after overfitting.
205c04ed3f3a4442e60eca41e15d29ef40b56b55.proposed_method: A new optimizer augmentation, GROKFAST, is proposed to accelerate grokking by decomposing the sequence of parameter gradients during training into fast- and slow-varying components via spectral analysis. The method applies a low-pass filter (either a moving average or an exponential moving average) to the gradient signal, amplifying the slow-varying component and adding it back to the original gradient at each optimization step. This filtered gradient is then used in the parameter update, and the approach is compatible with standard first-order optimizers such as SGD, Adam, and AdamW. Two variants are developed: GROKFAST-MA, which uses a windowed moving average, and GROKFAST-EMA, which uses an exponential moving average, each with tunable hyperparameters for filter width, amplification factor, and momentum. The method is designed to be simple to implement, requiring only a few additional lines of code, and is applicable to a wide range of model architectures and tasks.
205c04ed3f3a4442e60eca41e15d29ef40b56b55.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on tasks and models known to exhibit grokking, including modular arithmetic with a two-layer Transformer, image classification on MNIST with a three-layer MLP, molecular property prediction on QM9 with a GCN, and sentiment analysis on IMDb with a two-layer LSTM. Baseline training with standard optimizers will be compared to training with the GROKFAST-augmented optimizers. Evaluation metrics include validation accuracy and loss, as well as the number of training iterations required to reach a specified generalization threshold (e.g., 95% validation accuracy). Hyperparameters for the gradient filters (amplifier gain, window size, momentum) will be selected via grid search, and ablation studies will examine the effects of filter parameters and weight decay. Additional analyses will include parameter trajectory visualization using PCA and measurement of parameter space distances between key training states.
205c04ed3f3a4442e60eca41e15d29ef40b56b55.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel optimizer augmentation that accelerates grokking by amplifying slow gradient components, reducing the delay to generalization by up to 50-fold across diverse tasks. The method is general, lightweight, and compatible with existing first-order optimizers, requiring minimal code changes. It provides a new state-space and frequency-domain interpretation of training dynamics under grokking, supported by comprehensive empirical validation and analysis of parameter trajectories. The approach also demonstrates synergistic benefits when combined with weight decay and offers insights into the necessity of both fast and slow gradient components for stable and accelerated generalization.

205e33202d83a87300e2cf719b60943cf53508e3.title: Separating Knowledge and Perception with Procedural Data
205e33202d83a87300e2cf719b60943cf53508e3.research_question: How can the separation of perception and knowledge in visual models be achieved to enable efficient data unlearning, privacy guarantees, and strong generalization, while minimizing reliance on real-world data?
205e33202d83a87300e2cf719b60943cf53508e3.hypothesis: Training visual embedding models exclusively on procedurally generated data, and introducing real-world knowledge only through a visual memory of reference image embeddings, will enable full compartmentalization of real data, efficient data unlearning, and strong performance on downstream tasks such as classification and segmentation.
205e33202d83a87300e2cf719b60943cf53508e3.proposed_method: A vision transformer embedding model will be trained using self-supervised learning (DINO) on procedurally generated image datasets created via OpenGL shader programs. The procedural data generation process will be enhanced by introducing novel methods such as ShadersKML and ShadersKMLMixup, which increase data diversity by extracting mixing masks from shader images using K-Means clustering and combining them with Mixup strategies. After training, the model will not be further updated with real-world data; instead, a visual memory—a database of reference image embeddings from real images—will be constructed. Downstream tasks (such as classification, similarity search, and segmentation) will be performed by retrieving k-nearest neighbors from this memory, enabling explicit control over all real data and facilitating efficient addition or removal of samples.
205e33202d83a87300e2cf719b60943cf53508e3.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate the procedural embedding models on a range of tasks. For visual similarity, the NIGHTS dataset will be used with a human visual similarity benchmark (2AFC), comparing model judgments to human responses. For classification, KNN accuracy will be measured on fine-grained datasets (Flowers102, CUB200, Food101) and ImageNet-1K, with baselines including models trained on real datasets (Places, ImageNet) and prior procedural data methods. Segmentation abilities will be assessed using PCA-based features on COCO, ADE20K, and Pascal VOC, with metrics such as R2 (explained variance) and qualitative analysis of zero-shot and in-context segmentation. Additional experiments will analyze privacy and unlearning by measuring the impact of removing samples from the visual memory and evaluating on sensitive datasets (CelebA, MedMNIST). Model scaling and Gestalt perception will also be investigated. Evaluation metrics include KNN classification accuracy, R2 for segmentation, and alignment with human similarity judgments.
205e33202d83a87300e2cf719b60943cf53508e3.novelty_claims: The proposed approach achieves full separation between perception (feature extraction) and knowledge (visual memory) by training embeddings solely on procedural data, allowing all real-world data to be controlled at the memory level. The introduction of ShadersKML and ShadersKMLMixup procedural data processes yields stronger and more diverse embeddings than previous procedural methods. The method enables perfect and efficient data unlearning and privacy guarantees with respect to all real data, while retaining strong performance on classification and segmentation tasks—often matching or exceeding models trained on real data in fine-grained settings. Furthermore, the approach provides new insights into the limitations and generalization abilities of procedural models, and demonstrates practical advantages for privacy-sensitive and regulated domains.

206400aba5f12f734cdd2e4ab48ef6014ea60773.title: Evaluating Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models
206400aba5f12f734cdd2e4ab48ef6014ea60773.research_question: How can object hallucination in large vision-language models (LVLMs) be systematically evaluated, and what factors influence the prevalence of hallucinated objects in model outputs?
206400aba5f12f734cdd2e4ab48ef6014ea60773.hypothesis: Object hallucination in LVLMs is influenced by the frequency and co-occurrence of objects in visual instruction datasets, and current evaluation methods are inadequate for robustly measuring hallucination. A polling-based evaluation method can provide more stable and flexible assessment of hallucination in LVLMs.
206400aba5f12f734cdd2e4ab48ef6014ea60773.proposed_method: A novel evaluation framework, Polling-based Object Probing Evaluation (POPE), will be developed to assess object hallucination in LVLMs. POPE reformulates hallucination evaluation as a binary classification task by prompting LVLMs with simple Yes/No questions about the presence of specific objects in images. The method constructs evaluation triples for each image, pairing ground-truth and sampled nonexistent objects with templated questions (e.g., 'Is there a <object> in the image?'). Three negative sampling strategies—random, popular (frequent in dataset), and adversarial (frequent co-occurrence with present objects)—will be used to probe model tendencies toward hallucination. POPE can leverage either human annotations or automatic segmentation tools (e.g., SEEM) to identify objects, enabling application to both annotated and unannotated datasets.
206400aba5f12f734cdd2e4ab48ef6014ea60773.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the MSCOCO dataset and extended to A-OKVQA and GQA datasets, using both human-annotated and automatically segmented images. Five representative LVLMs (mPLUG-Owl, LLaVA, MultiModal-GPT, MiniGPT-4, and InstructBLIP) will be evaluated. Baselines will include traditional instruction-based evaluation metrics such as CHAIR, with POPE compared for stability and reliability. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and the proportion of 'Yes' responses. Additional analyses will examine the correlation between hallucinated objects and their frequency/co-occurrence in training data, and the impact of hallucination on downstream tasks such as VQA and image captioning.
206400aba5f12f734cdd2e4ab48ef6014ea60773.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first systematic, polling-based evaluation framework (POPE) for object hallucination in LVLMs, addressing limitations of existing caption-based metrics. The method enables stable, prompt-invariant, and scalable assessment, including applicability to unannotated datasets via automatic segmentation. The research also provides empirical insights into how object distributions in instruction datasets drive hallucination, and demonstrates the flexibility of POPE to probe model behavior under varied negative sampling strategies.

206ac9b41d419be0da5acc198f574e5bfa3c6548.title: Conformal prediction with conditional guarantees
206ac9b41d419be0da5acc198f574e5bfa3c6548.research_question: How can distribution-free prediction sets be constructed to provide finite-sample conditional guarantees that interpolate between marginal and conditional validity, especially in the presence of covariate shifts or subgroup structures, without making assumptions on the underlying data-generating process?
206ac9b41d419be0da5acc198f574e5bfa3c6548.hypothesis: It is possible to design a conformal prediction framework that, by leveraging augmented quantile regression over appropriate function classes, achieves finite-sample conditional coverage guarantees for a broad spectrum of conditional targets, including group-conditional and covariate-shifted scenarios, while remaining assumption-free and computationally efficient.
206ac9b41d419be0da5acc198f574e5bfa3c6548.proposed_method: A novel conformal prediction framework will be developed that generalizes split conformal prediction by introducing a flexible relaxation of conditional coverage, formulated as coverage over a class of covariate shifts. The method will employ augmented quantile regression, where the quantile function is fit over a finite or infinite-dimensional function class F (e.g., linear functions, subgroup indicators, or reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces), and the new test point is incorporated into the fit as an augmented data point. The prediction set for a new instance will be defined as the set of values whose conformity scores fall below the estimated conditional quantile threshold, with the quantile regression objective including both calibration and test points. For finite-dimensional F, exact or nearly exact finite-sample conditional coverage will be provided; for infinite-dimensional F, the method will quantify and control coverage errors via interpretable hyperparameters. The approach can be implemented as a wrapper around any black-box machine learning model, using its predictions to define conformity scores, and can be randomized to achieve exact coverage in discrete settings.
206ac9b41d419be0da5acc198f574e5bfa3c6548.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both simulated and real datasets to evaluate the proposed method. Simulated datasets will include settings with known group structures and covariate shifts, such as univariate and high-dimensional regression problems with overlapping subgroups or Gaussian-tilted covariate distributions. Baselines will include standard split conformal prediction and quantile regression-based conformal methods (e.g., Jung et al., 2023). Evaluation metrics will focus on empirical coverage (marginal, group-conditional, and under covariate shift), miscoverage rates, and prediction set lengths. Experiments will systematically vary calibration set sizes, function class complexity, and hyperparameters to assess finite-sample performance, tightness of coverage, and robustness to model misspecification.
206ac9b41d419be0da5acc198f574e5bfa3c6548.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a spectrum of conditional coverage guarantees interpolating between marginal and exact conditional validity, unifying and generalizing prior group-conditional and covariate-shifted conformal methods. It achieves tighter finite-sample coverage than existing group-conditional methods, requires no assumptions on the data-generating distribution (including for discrete outcomes), and extends coverage guarantees to infinite-dimensional function classes with quantifiable error. The method is computationally efficient, can be implemented as a wrapper around arbitrary black-box predictors, and allows practitioners to flexibly control the trade-off between coverage tightness and conditionality via interpretable hyperparameters.

206ee73f4e3187b5a71c3569bb1d443b8cce9351.title: Towards Understanding the Generalization of Graph Neural Networks
206ee73f4e3187b5a71c3569bb1d443b8cce9351.research_question: What are the key factors that determine the generalization gap of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) in node classification tasks, and how can theoretical guarantees be established for their generalization performance under realistic transductive learning and stochastic optimization settings?
206ee73f4e3187b5a71c3569bb1d443b8cce9351.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the generalization gap of GNNs is significantly influenced by architecture-specific factors such as the Lipschitz continuity and smoothness constants, the choice of optimization algorithm, and the properties of the graph structure (e.g., node degree distribution). Furthermore, it is expected that sharper and more realistic generalization bounds can be derived by analyzing GNNs under transductive learning with stochastic gradient descent.
206ee73f4e3187b5a71c3569bb1d443b8cce9351.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the generalization properties of GNNs in the transductive node classification setting, explicitly considering stochastic optimization algorithms such as stochastic gradient descent (SGD). High-probability upper bounds on the generalization gap and gradient differences between training and test nodes will be established by leveraging complexity-based techniques and properties of the GNN architecture, such as Lipschitz continuity and Hölder smoothness. The analysis will be extended to popular GNN architectures, including both linear and nonlinear models (e.g., GCN, GCNII, SGC, APPNP, GPR-GNN), by deriving architecture-specific constants that govern their generalization capability. Theoretical results will be supported by a detailed case study of these models, with explicit computation of the relevant constants and discussion of their implications.
206ee73f4e3187b5a71c3569bb1d443b8cce9351.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on widely used benchmark datasets for node classification, such as Cora, Citeseer, and Pubmed. For each dataset, a standard transductive learning setup will be used: 30% of nodes will be randomly sampled as the training set, with the remainder used for testing. Each experiment will be repeated 10 times with different random seeds, and results will be reported as mean and standard deviation. The evaluation metrics will include the generalization gap in terms of both loss and accuracy (i.e., the absolute difference between training and test performance), as well as test accuracy. Baseline models for comparison will include GCN, GCNII, SGC, APPNP, GPR-GNN, and GAT, with both shallow and deep variants where appropriate. The number of SGD iterations will be fixed, and the effect of network depth and architecture-specific factors on generalization will be systematically analyzed.
206ee73f4e3187b5a71c3569bb1d443b8cce9351.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified theoretical framework for analyzing the generalization of GNNs under realistic transductive learning and stochastic optimization, addressing key limitations of prior work that relied on unrealistic independence assumptions or slow-order bounds. The derived high-probability generalization bounds are sharper and more applicable to large-scale node classification scenarios. The analysis reveals how specific architectural choices and optimization parameters affect generalization, providing theoretical justification for practical techniques such as early stopping and edge dropout. The work also explains, from a learning theory perspective, why linear GNNs can sometimes outperform nonlinear ones and offers guidance for designing new GNN architectures with improved generalization.

2091dcd7c80bc27ba7d1fdc0087748bb1e293e2f.title: Depth Anything V2
2091dcd7c80bc27ba7d1fdc0087748bb1e293e2f.research_question: How can a monocular depth estimation model be developed to achieve robust and fine-grained depth predictions across diverse real-world scenarios, while maintaining high efficiency and generalization capability for downstream tasks?
2091dcd7c80bc27ba7d1fdc0087748bb1e293e2f.hypothesis: Replacing all labeled real images with high-quality synthetic images for initial training, scaling up the teacher model, and leveraging large-scale pseudo-labeled real images for student training will result in a monocular depth estimation model that is both more accurate and robust than models trained on conventional real or synthetic datasets alone.
2091dcd7c80bc27ba7d1fdc0087748bb1e293e2f.proposed_method: A new framework for monocular depth estimation will be developed, consisting of three main stages. First, a large-capacity teacher model based on the DINOv2-G encoder will be trained exclusively on a curated set of highly precise synthetic images, ensuring the capture of fine-grained details and accurate depth for challenging objects such as transparent and reflective surfaces. Second, this teacher model will be used to generate pseudo-depth labels for a massive collection of unlabeled real images, effectively bridging the domain gap and increasing scene diversity. Third, a series of student models of varying sizes (from 25M to 1.3B parameters) will be trained solely on these pseudo-labeled real images, using a combination of scale-and-shift-invariant loss and gradient matching loss to optimize depth sharpness and semantic alignment. The approach will also include a feature alignment loss to preserve semantic information from the pre-trained encoder.
2091dcd7c80bc27ba7d1fdc0087748bb1e293e2f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using five precise synthetic datasets (totaling 595K images) for teacher training and eight large-scale pseudo-labeled real datasets (totaling 62M images) for student training. The models will be evaluated on both conventional benchmarks (e.g., KITTI, NYU-D, Sintel, ETH3D, DIODE) and a newly constructed DA-2K benchmark, which features high-resolution images and diverse scenarios with triple-checked sparse depth annotations. Baseline comparisons will include leading discriminative and generative depth models such as MiDaS, Depth Anything V1, Marigold, and others. Evaluation metrics will include AbsRel, delta accuracy thresholds, RMSE, and accuracy on relative depth discrimination. Ablation studies will assess the impact of synthetic versus pseudo-labeled data and the necessity of each training stage.
2091dcd7c80bc27ba7d1fdc0087748bb1e293e2f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a data-centric training pipeline that eliminates the reliance on noisy real labeled data by leveraging only synthetic images for teacher training and large-scale pseudo-labeled real images for student training. This method achieves both fine-grained detail and robust generalization without requiring complex model architectures or loss functions. Additionally, a new, versatile evaluation benchmark (DA-2K) is constructed to address the limitations of existing test sets, providing high-resolution, diverse, and precisely annotated images. The framework supports models across a wide range of sizes, enabling deployment in various real-world applications, and demonstrates superior performance and efficiency compared to state-of-the-art generative and discriminative baselines.

20a93646a95156b07f1212932d4aa5ad34ad8ad6.title: Are Random Decompositions all we need in High Dimensional Bayesian Optimisation?
20a93646a95156b07f1212932d4aa5ad34ad8ad6.research_question: How can high-dimensional Bayesian optimization be effectively scaled without relying on data-driven decomposition learning, and what are the theoretical and empirical benefits of using data-independent, random decomposition strategies?
20a93646a95156b07f1212932d4aa5ad34ad8ad6.hypothesis: Random, data-independent tree-based decompositions can provide superior theoretical guarantees and empirical performance in high-dimensional Bayesian optimization compared to data-driven decomposition learning methods, by effectively trading off maximal information gain and functional mismatch.
20a93646a95156b07f1212932d4aa5ad34ad8ad6.proposed_method: A novel Bayesian optimization algorithm, Random Decomposition Upper Confidence Bound (RDUCB), will be developed that employs a random tree-based decomposition sampler at each optimization round. The method will use additive kernel Gaussian processes as surrogate models, where the decomposition of the input dimensions is sampled independently of the data, specifically as random trees to ensure sparsity and tractable information gain. At each iteration, a new tree decomposition is sampled, a GP is fitted using the additive kernel corresponding to the decomposition, and an additive UCB acquisition function is maximized using message passing for efficient query selection.
