The approach is designed to be plug-and-play, allowing integration with existing BO frameworks, and is theoretically justified by new regret bounds that account for both information gain and functional mismatch.
20a93646a95156b07f1212932d4aa5ad34ad8ad6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of benchmarks, including high-dimensional synthetic functions (e.g., 20-d Rosenbrock, 20-d Hartmann, 250-d Styblinski-Tang), neural architecture search hyperparameter tuning (NAS) with mixed discrete and continuous spaces, mixed integer programming (MIP) solver tuning with up to 74 dimensions, and high-dimensional Lasso regression (up to 180 dimensions). Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art tree-based decomposition learners, random embedding BO (REMBO), Hashing-enhanced Subspace BO (HeSBO), Coordinate LineBO, and random search. Evaluation metrics will focus on best regret (difference between the queried function value and the theoretical or empirical minimum) over a fixed budget of queries, with multiple random seeds for statistical significance. Additional experiments will test scalability as dimensionality increases and demonstrate the plug-and-play nature of the method by integrating it with HEBO and evaluating on the Bayesmark suite.
20a93646a95156b07f1212932d4aa5ad34ad8ad6.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first theoretically grounded, data-independent random decomposition strategy for high-dimensional Bayesian optimization, providing new regret bounds that explicitly quantify the trade-off between information gain and functional mismatch. The method is simple, scalable, and nearly plug-and-play, enabling easy integration with existing BO frameworks. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate significant improvements over prior state-of-the-art decomposition learners, especially as dimensionality increases, and to validate the practical benefits of random decompositions in both synthetic and real-world tasks.

20c4c597835ee9696241c1c08a3fc380a7f75401.title: An Evidence-Based Post-Hoc Adjustment Framework for Anomaly Detection Under Data Contamination
20c4c597835ee9696241c1c08a3fc380a7f75401.research_question: How can anomaly detection models trained on contaminated datasets be effectively adapted at test time, without access to training data, training pipelines, or prior knowledge of anomaly proportions, to improve robustness and performance across diverse domains and contamination levels?
20c4c597835ee9696241c1c08a3fc380a7f75401.hypothesis: A post-hoc adjustment framework that integrates evidence collected at test time with the outputs of anomaly detection models trained on contaminated data will improve anomaly detection performance and robustness, even when training data, pipelines, or contamination ratios are inaccessible.
20c4c597835ee9696241c1c08a3fc380a7f75401.proposed_method: A novel test-time adaptation framework, EPHAD (Evidence-based Post-Hoc Adjustment for Anomaly Detection), is proposed to refine the outputs of pre-trained anomaly detection (AD) models that may have been trained on contaminated datasets. The method operates by combining the prior knowledge encoded in the AD model with an evidence function T(x), which is computed at test time and can be derived from multimodal foundation models (e.g., CLIP), classical AD methods (e.g., Local Outlier Factor), or domain-specific knowledge. The adjustment is mathematically formulated as an exponential tilting of the contaminated model's output, producing a revised score or density that upweights samples deemed more likely to be normal by the evidence function. A temperature parameter β controls the trade-off between reliance on the original model and the evidence; an adaptive, unsupervised strategy (EPHAD-Ada) is also developed to select β based on entropy minimization of inlier probabilities. The framework is compatible with both density-based and score-based AD models, enabling post-hoc correction without retraining or access to internal model components.
20c4c597835ee9696241c1c08a3fc380a7f75401.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a wide range of datasets, including eight visual anomaly detection benchmarks (such as MVTecAD, MPDD, ViSA, RealIAD, CIFAR-10, Fashion-MNIST, MNIST, and SVHN), twenty-six tabular anomaly detection datasets from ADBench, and a real-world industrial AD dataset. Controlled contamination is introduced into the training data to simulate realistic scenarios, with contamination ratios typically set at 10% but varied in ablation studies. The framework is evaluated with multiple state-of-the-art unsupervised AD baselines (e.g., PatchCore, PaDiM, CFLOW, FastFlow, DRÆM, Reverse Distillation, ULSAD, DeepSVDD, ECOD, COPOD, IForest, LOF), both with and without EPHAD integration. Evidence functions include CLIP for images and LOF/IForest for tabular data. Performance is measured using AUROC, averaged across categories and repeated across contamination levels. Ablation studies systematically assess the impact of contamination ratio and the β parameter, and an adaptive variant (EPHAD-Ada) is evaluated for unsupervised hyperparameter selection.
20c4c597835ee9696241c1c08a3fc380a7f75401.novelty_claims: The proposed framework enables post-hoc, test-time adaptation of anomaly detection models trained on contaminated data without requiring access to training pipelines, data, or contamination ratios, making it highly practical for real-world deployments. EPHAD is flexible in its integration of diverse evidence sources, including foundation models and domain-specific knowledge, and is compatible with both density-based and score-based AD models. The method introduces a principled exponential tilting formulation and an unsupervised, adaptive approach for hyperparameter selection. Extensive experiments demonstrate improved robustness and performance across a wide range of datasets, AD models, and contamination scenarios, establishing EPHAD as a versatile and effective solution for anomaly detection under data contamination.

20d8448cf1efea10e5ddb3ca8bc8beaef874c51e.title: Pushdown Layers: Encoding Recursive Structure in Transformer Language Models
20d8448cf1efea10e5ddb3ca8bc8beaef874c51e.research_question: How can explicit modeling of recursive syntactic structure be incorporated into Transformer language models to improve their syntactic generalization, sample efficiency, and performance on downstream language understanding tasks?
20d8448cf1efea10e5ddb3ca8bc8beaef874c51e.hypothesis: Introducing a stack-based memory mechanism into Transformer language models, via Pushdown Layers that track recursive syntactic state, will enable more effective learning and generalization of recursive structures, leading to improved syntactic generalization, greater sample efficiency, and enhanced performance on both synthetic and natural language tasks compared to standard self-attention mechanisms.
20d8448cf1efea10e5ddb3ca8bc8beaef874c51e.proposed_method: A novel self-attention layer, termed Pushdown Layer, will be developed to augment Transformer language models with an explicit stack-based memory. This memory is realized as a stack tape that tracks the estimated syntactic depth of each token in the incremental parse of the observed prefix. At each step during autoregressive generation, the model predicts both the next token and a probabilistic attachment decision, updating the stack tape by either shifting (assigning depth 0) or reducing with a prior constituent (incrementing depth). The stack tape is used to generate depth embeddings, which are additively incorporated into the attention keys, softly biasing the attention mechanism towards syntactically relevant tokens (e.g., headwords of constituents) and away from irrelevant or closed constituents. Training is performed on corpora annotated with constituency parses, jointly supervising both token prediction and attachment decisions using gradient descent. The approach is designed as a drop-in replacement for standard self-attention, enabling parallel training and compatibility with existing Transformer architectures.
20d8448cf1efea10e5ddb3ca8bc8beaef874c51e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and natural language datasets. For synthetic evaluation, models will be trained and tested on Dyck languages (well-nested bracket strings) to assess generalization to deeper recursive structures and longer-range dependencies. For natural language, models will be trained on the BLLIP-LG dataset (annotated with constituency parses) and evaluated on syntactic generalization test suites (SG), BLIMP, and perplexity metrics. Additional large-scale experiments will use a newly constructed WIKITREES dataset (100M+ tokens from Wikipedia, automatically parsed), comparing sample efficiency and syntactic generalization between Pushdown-augmented and standard Transformer LMs. Baselines will include standard Transformer LMs and prior structured models such as PLM, PLM-Mask, and Transformer Grammars (TG). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on syntactic generalization suites, perplexity, and performance on downstream GLUE text classification tasks (RTE, SST5, MRPC, STS-B) via staged finetuning. Experimental setups will control for model size, training regime, and data splits, and will include ablations to isolate the effect of the Pushdown Layer.
20d8448cf1efea10e5ddb3ca8bc8beaef874c51e.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a stack-based memory mechanism into Transformer self-attention, enabling explicit modeling of recursive syntactic state without altering the output space or requiring hard constraints on attention. Pushdown Layers provide a soft, learnable syntactic bias that is compatible with gradient-based optimization and parallel training. The approach achieves dramatically improved and more sample-efficient syntactic generalization compared to standard Transformers and prior structured models, while maintaining or improving perplexity and downstream task performance. This represents the first integration of a stack-based, parse-tracking mechanism as a drop-in replacement for self-attention in large-scale Transformer language models.

20de79ec4fe682b68930eb4dcd91b1801b8d4731.title: Towards Understanding Grokking: An Effective Theory of Representation Learning
20de79ec4fe682b68930eb4dcd91b1801b8d4731.research_question: What are the underlying mechanisms and conditions that govern the phenomenon of delayed generalization (grokking) in neural networks, and how do representation learning dynamics, dataset size, and hyperparameter choices influence generalization performance across different learning phases?
20de79ec4fe682b68930eb4dcd91b1801b8d4731.hypothesis: Generalization in neural networks, particularly in the context of grokking, arises from the emergence of structured representations in the learned embeddings, and the transition between learning phases (comprehension, grokking, memorization, confusion) can be predicted and controlled through an effective theory of representation learning that incorporates dataset size and hyperparameter tuning.
20de79ec4fe682b68930eb4dcd91b1801b8d4731.proposed_method: A comprehensive investigation will be conducted using both simplified toy models and more complex neural architectures (such as transformer-based models) to study the dynamics of representation learning. The approach will involve formalizing a quantitative measure of representation quality (e.g., parallelogram structure and Representation Quality Index) and developing a physics-inspired effective theory to model the learning dynamics of embeddings. The effective theory will be used to predict critical training set sizes, phase transitions, and training trajectories. Phase diagrams will be constructed by systematically varying key hyperparameters, such as learning rates and weight decay for both encoder and decoder components, to map out the regions corresponding to different learning phases. The methodology will be extended to mainstream benchmarks (e.g., MNIST) to test the generality of the findings.
20de79ec4fe682b68930eb4dcd91b1801b8d4731.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed on both algorithmic datasets (e.g., modular addition, permutation group operations) and standard benchmarks like MNIST. In the toy model, datasets will consist of pairs of integers and their binary operations, with controlled splits for training and validation. Neural architectures will include simple MLPs and decoder-only transformers with learnable embeddings. A grid search over hyperparameters such as representation and decoder learning rates, decoder weight decay, and dropout rates will be conducted to generate phase diagrams. Evaluation metrics will include training and validation accuracy, Representation Quality Index (RQI), and the entropy of explained variance in PCA of embeddings. Baselines will include models with varying degrees of regularization and overparameterization. The number of optimization steps to reach high accuracy or high RQI will be recorded, and the effect of hyperparameters on the emergence and duration of grokking will be analyzed.
20de79ec4fe682b68930eb4dcd91b1801b8d4731.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a quantitative, physics-inspired effective theory for representation learning that predicts the onset of generalization and the critical training set size required for structured embeddings. A novel phase diagram framework is developed to classify learning dynamics into four distinct phases and to elucidate the conditions under which grokking occurs. The approach demonstrates that delayed generalization can be systematically controlled and even eliminated through appropriate hyperparameter tuning. Furthermore, the research extends the study of grokking beyond algorithmic tasks to mainstream datasets, providing the first evidence that grokking is a general phenomenon in machine learning. The use of representation quality metrics and phase diagrams offers new tools for understanding and predicting neural network generalization.

21032d1669b7e6fc58ef3a272e6a2f1f4ba15f10.title: Variance-reduced Zeroth-Order Methods for Fine-Tuning Language Models
21032d1669b7e6fc58ef3a272e6a2f1f4ba15f10.research_question: How can memory-efficient optimization methods be developed to enable stable and effective fine-tuning of large language models when backpropagation is prohibitively expensive or infeasible?
21032d1669b7e6fc58ef3a272e6a2f1f4ba15f10.hypothesis: Incorporating variance reduction techniques into zeroth-order optimization methods will improve the stability, convergence, and memory efficiency of large language model fine-tuning, outperforming existing zeroth-order approaches and approaching the performance of first-order methods.
21032d1669b7e6fc58ef3a272e6a2f1f4ba15f10.proposed_method: A new memory-efficient zeroth-order optimization algorithm, termed MeZO-SVRG (Memory-Efficient Zeroth-Order Stochastic Variance-Reduced Gradient), will be developed for fine-tuning large language models. The method combines full-batch and minibatch information to construct asymptotically unbiased, low-variance gradient estimators using only forward passes and loss differences, thus eliminating the need for backpropagation. Efficient gradient estimation is achieved by perturbing the entire batch in a single direction, leveraging data parallelism and in-place operations to minimize memory usage. The algorithm periodically computes a full-batch gradient estimator and uses it to correct minibatch updates, following a variance-reduced update rule. Additional design choices include the use of separate learning rates for full-batch and minibatch updates and compatibility with parameter-efficient fine-tuning and non-differentiable objectives.
21032d1669b7e6fc58ef3a272e6a2f1f4ba15f10.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of masked and autoregressive language models (up to 7B parameters), including DistilBERT, RoBERTa-large, GPT2, OPT-2.7B, and OPT-6.7B. Fine-tuning tasks will be drawn from GLUE and SuperGLUE benchmarks (e.g., MNLI, QNLI, SST-2, CoLA, BoolQ), using both full- and partial-parameter fine-tuning in FP32 and BF16 precision. Baselines will include the MeZO zeroth-order optimizer and first-order methods such as SGD and Adam. Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy, fine-tuning loss, GPU memory usage, and GPU-hours to convergence. Experimental setups will vary batch sizes and context lengths to profile memory and computational efficiency, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of algorithmic parameters.
21032d1669b7e6fc58ef3a272e6a2f1f4ba15f10.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first variance-reduced zeroth-order optimizer specifically tailored for large-scale language model fine-tuning, achieving significant improvements in stability and convergence over prior zeroth-order approaches. MeZO-SVRG enables fine-tuning with memory requirements comparable to inference, achieving up to 2× reduction in memory usage relative to first-order methods and up to 20% higher test accuracy than existing zeroth-order baselines. The method is compatible with non-differentiable objectives and parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and offers substantial reductions in computation time (up to 2× fewer GPU-hours) while maintaining or improving performance. The proposal also establishes theoretical convergence guarantees for the new algorithm.

21091f8133ab034baacb92fdb958e14989eb427f.title: Language Modeling Is Compression
21091f8133ab034baacb92fdb958e14989eb427f.research_question: Can large language models, when viewed through the lens of lossless compression, serve as general-purpose compressors across diverse data modalities, and what insights does this compression perspective provide into scaling laws, tokenization, and in-context learning?
21091f8133ab034baacb92fdb958e14989eb427f.hypothesis: Large language models, despite being primarily trained on text, are hypothesized to function as powerful general-purpose compressors for various data modalities, outperforming traditional domain-specific compressors. Furthermore, analyzing these models from a compression perspective is expected to yield novel insights into model scaling, tokenization strategies, and in-context learning capabilities.
21091f8133ab034baacb92fdb958e14989eb427f.proposed_method: The proposed research will systematically evaluate the lossless compression capabilities of large language models (LLMs) by utilizing arithmetic coding in conjunction with the probabilistic outputs of these models. Both pretrained foundation models (such as Chinchilla and Llama2) and custom-trained vanilla Transformers will be employed. The method involves applying these models, without further training, to compress datasets from multiple modalities (text, image, audio) and comparing their performance to classical compressors (gzip, LZMA2, PNG, FLAC). The study will also investigate the impact of tokenization strategies (e.g., ASCII vs. byte-pair encoding with varying vocabulary sizes) on compression rates, and analyze the trade-off between model size and dataset size for optimal compression. Additionally, the equivalence between prediction and compression will be leveraged to use compressors as generative models, sampling data sequences based on compression-derived probability distributions.
21091f8133ab034baacb92fdb958e14989eb427f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three 1GB datasets representing different modalities: enwik9 (text), ImageNet (image patches converted to grayscale), and LibriSpeech (audio). The compression performance of LLMs with arithmetic coding will be benchmarked against standard compressors (gzip, LZMA2, PNG, FLAC) using both raw and adjusted compression rates (the latter accounts for model parameter size). For neural models, both in-distribution and out-of-distribution evaluations will be performed by training on enwik8 and testing on enwik8, enwik9, and other modalities. The effect of context length, chunking strategies, and tokenization will be systematically varied and analyzed. Evaluation metrics will include compression rate (compressed size/raw size), adjusted compression rate (including model size), and qualitative assessment of generative samples produced by treating compressors as sequence models.
21091f8133ab034baacb92fdb958e14989eb427f.novelty_claims: This research proposes a comprehensive empirical investigation of large language models as general-purpose lossless compressors across multiple data modalities, demonstrating that such models can outperform specialized compressors even on non-text data. The compression viewpoint is further claimed to provide new insights into model scaling laws, revealing a fundamental trade-off between model and dataset size for optimal compression. The study also explores the impact of tokenization as a form of pre-compression, showing its nuanced effects on model performance. Finally, the research leverages the theoretical equivalence between compression and prediction to demonstrate that any compressor can be used as a conditional generative model, thus unifying the perspectives of language modeling and compression.

210b0a3d76e93079cc51b03c4115fde545eea966.title: GPQA: A Graduate-Level Google-Proof Q&A Benchmark
210b0a3d76e93079cc51b03c4115fde545eea966.research_question: How can a benchmark be developed to evaluate the ability of both human experts and advanced AI systems to answer graduate-level, domain-specific questions that are resistant to web search and accessible resources, thereby enabling realistic experiments in scalable oversight and model alignment?
210b0a3d76e93079cc51b03c4115fde545eea966.hypothesis: A carefully constructed benchmark of graduate-level, domain-specific multiple-choice questions, validated for objectivity and difficulty, will expose significant performance gaps between experts, non-experts (even with internet access), and state-of-the-art AI models, thus providing a robust platform for evaluating scalable oversight methods.
210b0a3d76e93079cc51b03c4115fde545eea966.proposed_method: A new benchmark will be created by soliciting graduate-level multiple-choice questions from domain experts in biology, physics, and chemistry, with each question designed to be answerable by in-domain experts but highly challenging for non-experts, even with unrestricted internet access. The data collection pipeline will involve several stages: question writing by experts, initial expert validation with feedback, question revision, a second round of expert validation, and non-expert validation by individuals with PhD-level expertise in other domains. Questions will be filtered and categorized based on expert agreement and non-expert performance to ensure objectivity and difficulty. Detailed explanations for correct and incorrect answer choices will be included to support post-hoc analysis and further validation.
210b0a3d76e93079cc51b03c4115fde545eea966.experiment_details: Experiments will involve administering the curated question sets to three groups: in-domain experts, skilled non-experts (experts in other domains with full internet access except LLMs), and advanced AI models (such as GPT-4, GPT-3.5-turbo, and Llama-2-70B-chat) under both closed-book and open-book (with internet search tools) conditions. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy rates for each group, with additional analysis of expert post-hoc agreement and time spent per question. Baseline comparisons will be made between human and AI performance, and across different domains and question subsets (main set, diamond set, extended set). The setup will also track abstention rates and the impact of prompting strategies (e.g., few-shot chain-of-thought).
210b0a3d76e93079cc51b03c4115fde545eea966.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces a unique combination of graduate-level, domain-expert-authored questions that are explicitly designed to be 'Google-proof' and objectively answerable only by true experts. The multi-stage validation pipeline, including both expert and incentivized non-expert validators, ensures high question quality and difficulty. This resource fills a gap by enabling realistic, high-stakes scalable oversight experiments where neither non-experts nor current AI models can reliably solve the tasks, thus providing a critical testbed for future research in model alignment, human–AI collaboration, and oversight protocols.

211a6800a4cc0c7ab863037b9efb53e7d7801a34.title: Near-Optimal Differentially Private k-Core Decomposition
211a6800a4cc0c7ab863037b9efb53e7d7801a34.research_question: How can k-core decomposition, densest subgraph, and low out-degree ordering be performed on graphs while ensuring strong differential privacy guarantees, and what are the optimal trade-offs between privacy and utility in these settings?
211a6800a4cc0c7ab863037b9efb53e7d7801a34.hypothesis: It is possible to design differentially private algorithms for k-core decomposition, densest subgraph, and low out-degree ordering that achieve near-optimal additive error and eliminate or significantly reduce multiplicative error, thereby improving upon existing privacy-utility trade-offs.
211a6800a4cc0c7ab863037b9efb53e7d7801a34.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that adapts the classical iterative peeling algorithm for k-core decomposition to the differentially private setting using a multidimensional generalization of the sparse vector technique, termed the Multidimensional AboveThreshold (MAT) mechanism. This approach enables threshold-based graph algorithms to be executed under both central and local edge differential privacy models with strong utility guarantees. The MAT mechanism injects carefully calibrated Laplace noise into threshold checks for each vertex, allowing the algorithm to privately determine core numbers without incurring large errors from repeated composition. The method is further extended to related problems, including densest subgraph and low out-degree ordering, by leveraging the connection between these problems and k-core decomposition, and by designing specialized private thresholding and orientation procedures.
211a6800a4cc0c7ab863037b9efb53e7d7801a34.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard benchmark graph datasets, including both synthetic and real-world networks of varying sizes and densities. The proposed algorithms will be evaluated against state-of-the-art differentially private baselines, such as previous (2+η)-approximate k-core decomposition methods and private densest subgraph algorithms. Evaluation metrics will include additive and multiplicative approximation error of core numbers, subgraph density, and out-degree, as well as computational efficiency (running time and round complexity). Both central and local edge differential privacy models will be considered, and results will be reported with high-probability accuracy guarantees. Parameter sweeps over privacy budget ε and graph size n will be performed to empirically validate theoretical bounds.
211a6800a4cc0c7ab863037b9efb53e7d7801a34.novelty_claims: The proposed approach eliminates the multiplicative error in differentially private k-core decomposition, achieving a (1, O(log(n)/ε))-approximation, which is nearly tight with respect to known lower bounds. The multidimensional AboveThreshold technique generalizes the sparse vector method to multidimensional, threshold-based graph algorithms, enabling efficient and accurate private computation. The method also improves additive error guarantees for private densest subgraph and low out-degree ordering, surpassing prior results by significant factors. The framework strengthens the theoretical and practical connection between distributed/parallel graph algorithms and differentially private computation, and provides the first near-linear time, near-optimal utility algorithms for these fundamental graph problems under strong privacy constraints.

2130adb9d49db51c49639105c49de33df02ff85b.title: ID3: Identity-Preserving-yet-Diversified Diffusion Models for Synthetic Face Recognition
2130adb9d49db51c49639105c49de33df02ff85b.research_question: How can synthetic face datasets be generated such that they preserve identity consistency within each identity group, promote diversity across different identities, and ensure diversity within each identity by varying facial attributes, in order to enable effective and privacy-preserving training of face recognition models? What sampling strategies can be employed to generate synthetic face datasets that allow state-of-the-art face recognition models to perform well on real-world benchmarks?
2130adb9d49db51c49639105c49de33df02ff85b.hypothesis: A conditional diffusion model that jointly leverages identity embeddings and facial attribute conditioning, optimized with a loss function explicitly enforcing identity preservation, can generate synthetic face datasets with high inter-class and intra-class diversity while maintaining identity consistency. Such datasets will enable face recognition models trained on them to achieve performance comparable to those trained on real-world data.
2130adb9d49db51c49639105c49de33df02ff85b.proposed_method: A conditional diffusion model, termed ID3, will be developed to generate face images conditioned on both identity embeddings and facial attribute vectors. Identity embeddings are extracted using a pretrained face recognition model, while facial attributes (such as age and pose) are predicted using pretrained attribute estimators. The denoising network is trained with a novel loss function comprising a denoising term, a one-step reconstruction term, and an inner-product term that explicitly encourages the generated image’s embedding to match the target identity embedding. Theoretical analysis shows that minimizing this loss is equivalent to maximizing a lower bound of an adjusted conditional log-likelihood over identity-preserving data. An ID-preserving sampling algorithm will be designed, operating over an adjusted gradient vector field that incorporates both the original and a reversed likelihood score, to guide the generation of identity-consistent and diverse face images. To ensure inter-class diversity, anchor identity embeddings will be distributed on the hypersphere by solving the Tammes problem, and intra-class diversity will be promoted by perturbing these embeddings and varying attribute conditions.
2130adb9d49db51c49639105c49de33df02ff85b.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training the proposed model on large-scale face datasets such as FFHQ and CASIA-WebFace. The generated synthetic datasets will be used to train face recognition models (e.g., LResNet50-IR), which will then be evaluated on standard face verification benchmarks including LFW, CFP-FP, CPLFW, AgeDB, and CALFW. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art synthetic face recognition generative models such as IDiff-Face, ID-Net, DigiFace, SFace, SynFace, and DCFace. Evaluation metrics will focus on face verification accuracy across these benchmarks. The experimental setup will ensure fairness by generating synthetic datasets with the same number of identities and samples per identity for all methods. Ablation studies will be conducted to assess the impact of key components, such as the reversed likelihood score, attribute conditioning, and anchor selection strategy.
2130adb9d49db51c49639105c49de33df02ff85b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a theoretically grounded loss function and sampling algorithm that jointly enforce identity preservation and diversity in synthetic face generation. The method leverages a novel combination of identity and attribute conditioning within a diffusion model, and employs a dataset generation strategy based on hyperspherical anchor separation (Tammes problem) to maximize inter-class diversity. The ID-preserving sampling algorithm, which operates over an adjusted vector field combining original and reversed likelihoods, is claimed to improve both the quality and identity consistency of generated faces. The overall framework enables fully automated synthetic face dataset generation without manual filtering or auxiliary real data during sampling, and achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple challenging face recognition benchmarks.

2141ed804636a1cf339d606cd03fd3b3e9582133.title: VILA: On Pre-training for Visual Language Models
2141ed804636a1cf339d606cd03fd3b3e9582133.research_question: How do different design choices in the pre-training process of visual language models (VLMs) affect their downstream performance, including multi-modal reasoning, in-context learning, and preservation of text-only capabilities?
2141ed804636a1cf339d606cd03fd3b3e9582133.hypothesis: Fine-tuning the language model backbone during visual language pre-training, using interleaved image-text corpora, and blending in text-only instruction data during supervised fine-tuning will significantly improve downstream visual language task performance, in-context learning, and maintain or enhance text-only capabilities compared to approaches that freeze the language model or rely solely on image-text pairs.
2141ed804636a1cf339d606cd03fd3b3e9582133.proposed_method: A comprehensive pre-training and fine-tuning pipeline will be developed for auto-regressive visual language models (VLMs) that augments a pre-trained text-only large language model (LLM) with visual input support. The architecture will consist of a visual encoder (e.g., ViT), a linear projection layer to map visual embeddings to the LLM input space, and the LLM itself. The methodology involves: (1) initializing the visual encoder and LLM with pre-trained weights while randomly initializing the projector; (2) pre-training the model on large-scale, interleaved image-text corpora (such as MMC4) and image-text pairs (such as COYO), with ablations on freezing vs. updating the LLM and on the structure of the training data; (3) performing supervised fine-tuning (SFT) using a blend of visual instruction datasets (converted to instruction-following style) and text-only instruction data (e.g., FLAN), to recover and enhance text-only capabilities and instruction-following performance. The pipeline will include ablation studies on projector capacity, image resolution, and data blending ratios.
2141ed804636a1cf339d606cd03fd3b3e9582133.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using large-scale datasets: interleaved image-text corpora (MMC4, ~25M images), image-text pairs (COYO, ~25M images), and diverse visual instruction datasets for SFT. The evaluation will cover a wide range of visual language benchmarks, including VQAv2, GQA, VisWiz, TextVQA, OKVQA, COCO, Flickr, ScienceQA-IMG, POPE, MME, MMBench, MMBench-Chinese, SEED-Bench, LLaVA-Bench, and MM-Vet. Baselines will include models with frozen LLMs, models using only image-text pairs, and state-of-the-art VLMs such as LLaVA-1.5, InstructBLIP, and Qwen-VL. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy (for VQA-style tasks), CIDEr (for captioning), and text-only benchmarks (MMLU, BBH, DROP) to assess both multi-modal and unimodal capabilities. Both zero-shot and few-shot (in-context) learning settings will be tested, and qualitative analyses will be performed to assess multi-image reasoning, in-context learning, and chain-of-thought reasoning.
2141ed804636a1cf339d606cd03fd3b3e9582133.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a systematic study and practical recipe for VLM pre-training, highlighting the importance of updating the LLM backbone (rather than freezing), leveraging interleaved image-text corpora for better modality alignment and in-context learning, and blending in text-only instruction data during SFT to recover and enhance text-only performance. The approach demonstrates that these design choices unlock superior multi-modal reasoning, in-context learning, and world knowledge capabilities, achieving consistent improvements over state-of-the-art VLMs across diverse benchmarks without increasing model size or complexity. Additionally, the method enables efficient on-device deployment and provides new insights into the architectural and data-centric factors critical for effective VLM pre-training.

2169e2c251785288eb9bbd4217922c43b10f0dde.title: Distribution Free Prediction Sets for Node Classification
2169e2c251785288eb9bbd4217922c43b10f0dde.research_question: How can distribution-free prediction sets with rigorous uncertainty quantification be constructed for node classification tasks in graph-structured data, particularly in inductive learning scenarios where data points are dependent due to the graph structure?
2169e2c251785288eb9bbd4217922c43b10f0dde.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by leveraging local graph structure and homophily, conformal prediction methods can be adapted to provide valid, well-calibrated, and tighter prediction sets for node classification, even in the presence of non-exchangeable data dependencies induced by the graph.
2169e2c251785288eb9bbd4217922c43b10f0dde.proposed_method: A new approach, termed Neighbourhood Adaptive Prediction Sets (NAPS), will be developed to construct distribution-free prediction sets for node classification in graphs. This method adapts conformal prediction by localizing the calibration process to the K-hop neighborhood of each test node, assigning weights to calibration points based on their graph distance from the test node. The conformal score function will be based on Adaptive Prediction Sets (APS), and the method will use weighted quantiles to account for the non-exchangeable nature of graph data. Several variants will be explored, including unweighted, hyperbolic, and geometric decay weighting schemes for neighbors at increasing graph distances. The method will be applicable in inductive settings where test nodes or graphs are unseen during training, and theoretical coverage guarantees will be derived based on the local homophily of the graph.
2169e2c251785288eb9bbd4217922c43b10f0dde.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large, real-world node classification datasets such as Reddit2, Flickr, and Amazon Computers. Multiple popular GNN architectures, including GraphSAGE (with mean and max aggregation) and ShaDow-based GCNs, will be used as base models. The evaluation will compare NAPS variants to naive split-conformal APS baselines, measuring empirical coverage, average prediction set size, and conditional coverage properties. Metrics such as Size-Stratified Coverage Violation (SSCV) and Partition Conditional Coverage Violation (PCCV) will be used to assess calibration and fairness across graph partitions. Experiments will use inductive splits, with calibration and evaluation performed on disjoint sets of nodes, and results will be averaged over multiple random splits to ensure statistical reliability.
2169e2c251785288eb9bbd4217922c43b10f0dde.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first distribution-free conformal prediction framework for node classification in graphs that accounts for non-exchangeable dependencies via local neighborhood calibration. It provides theoretical coverage guarantees under homophily and demonstrates improved calibration and tighter prediction sets compared to naive conformal methods. The approach is model-agnostic, incurs minimal computational overhead, and can be flexibly adapted to various GNN architectures and weighting schemes. Additionally, new evaluation metrics are proposed to assess conditional coverage in the context of graph topology.

218ed67834bd1968fdbdfb3be114e5e3f193c976.title: Category Query Learning for Human-Object Interaction Classification
218ed67834bd1968fdbdfb3be114e5e3f193c976.research_question: How can human-object interaction (HOI) classification be improved by better modeling interaction categories, rather than focusing solely on human-object feature learning?
218ed67834bd1968fdbdfb3be114e5e3f193c976.hypothesis: Explicitly learning category-specific queries associated with interaction categories and using them as adaptive classification weights will improve HOI classification performance, particularly on challenging images with dense human-object interactions.
218ed67834bd1968fdbdfb3be114e5e3f193c976.proposed_method: A new framework is developed that introduces category-specific queries, each corresponding one-to-one with an interaction category. These queries are learnable embedding vectors that interact with image features via a transformer decoder, producing image-specific category representations. The learning of both the queries and decoder weights is supervised by an auxiliary image-level multi-label classification task, employing asymmetric loss to address label imbalance. For HOI classification, the cosine similarity between the updated category query and human-object instance features is used as the classification score, replacing the traditional static classifier weights. An additional score integration step modulates instance scores based on image-level classification probabilities, further enhancing performance.
218ed67834bd1968fdbdfb3be114e5e3f193c976.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on two major HOI benchmarks: HICO-DET and V-COCO. The proposed method is integrated into three representative HOI baselines: two transformer-based methods (QPIC and GEN-VLKT) and a traditional two-stage method (SCG). Evaluation metrics include mean Average Precision (mAP) under default and known object settings for HICO-DET, and role mAP for V-COCO. Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of each component, including the category query learning, the use of adaptive classification weights, loss functions, decoder structure, and the score integration step. The method is compared against state-of-the-art baselines, with model size and inference speed also reported.
218ed67834bd1968fdbdfb3be114e5e3f193c976.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces, for the first time in HOI classification, the concept of category-specific queries as adaptive classification weights, learned via an auxiliary image-level classification task. This approach is complementary to existing human-object feature learning methods and can be integrated with most off-the-shelf HOI detectors with minimal modification. The method is lightweight, general, and achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks. It is particularly effective on images with dense human-object interactions, a property not previously addressed in the HOI community.

21a6d78c683b17680a5823b3a702a1f4ac3e0dd7.title: Regularized Langevin Dynamics for Combinatorial Optimization
21a6d78c683b17680a5823b3a702a1f4ac3e0dd7.research_question: How can the exploration and efficiency of sampling-based combinatorial optimization solvers be improved to better escape local optima and achieve high-quality solutions across diverse problem instances?
21a6d78c683b17680a5823b3a702a1f4ac3e0dd7.hypothesis: Regularizing the expected distance between sampled and current solutions during the search process will enhance the ability of Langevin dynamics-based solvers to escape local optima in combinatorial optimization, leading to improved solution quality and computational efficiency compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.
21a6d78c683b17680a5823b3a702a1f4ac3e0dd7.proposed_method: A novel sampling framework, Regularized Langevin Dynamics (RLD), is developed for combinatorial optimization. RLD modifies discrete Langevin dynamics by enforcing a fixed expected Hamming distance between the current and proposed solutions at each step, thus controlling the update magnitude and encouraging broader exploration of the solution space. This regularization is incorporated into both simulated annealing (SA) and neural network (NN)-based solvers, resulting in two algorithms: Regularized Langevin Simulated Annealing (RLSA) and Regularized Langevin Neural Network (RLNN). RLSA leverages closed-form gradients for problems where available, while RLNN trains a neural network to approximate the gradient or proposal distribution, using a local unsupervised objective that regularizes the expected update distance. The method is designed to be simple, parallelizable, and compatible with GPU acceleration.
21a6d78c683b17680a5823b3a702a1f4ac3e0dd7.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on three classic combinatorial optimization problems: Maximum Independent Set (MIS), Maximum Clique (MCl), and Maximum Cut (MCut). Benchmark datasets include RB and BA graphs (small: 200–300 nodes; large: 800–1200 nodes) and ER graphs (small: 700–800 nodes; large: 9000–11000 nodes). Baselines span classical operations research solvers (Gurobi, KaMIS, SDP), heuristic methods (Greedy, MFA, iSCO), and state-of-the-art supervised, reinforcement, and unsupervised learning-based solvers (e.g., INTEL, DGL, PPO, DIMES, DIFUSCO, LTFT, DiffUCO, EGN). Evaluation metrics include the mean achieved objective value (e.g., set size, clique size, cut size) and total runtime across test instances. Hyperparameters are matched for fair comparison, and both the number of sampling steps and parallel trials are controlled. Ablation studies examine the effect of regularization and compare with standard discrete Langevin dynamics.
21a6d78c683b17680a5823b3a702a1f4ac3e0dd7.novelty_claims: The proposed RLD framework introduces a simple yet effective regularization of the expected update magnitude in discrete Langevin dynamics, specifically tailored to address the challenges of local optima in combinatorial optimization. RLD is broadly applicable to both simulated annealing and neural network-based solvers, offering significant improvements in solution quality and computational efficiency. RLSA achieves state-of-the-art or superior performance compared to previous SA and NN-based methods, reducing runtime by up to 80% while maintaining or improving solution quality. RLNN enables efficient unsupervised training without the need for labeled data or long-term return estimation, outperforming or matching the best existing diffusion models with dramatically reduced training time. The framework is simple to implement, highly parallelizable, and demonstrates strong generalization across multiple CO problem types and scales.

21b786b3f870fc7fa247c143aa41de88b1fc6141.title: Glow: Generative Flow with Invertible 1x1 Convolutions
21b786b3f870fc7fa247c143aa41de88b1fc6141.research_question: How can generative flow-based models be improved to achieve more efficient, high-quality, and scalable synthesis and manipulation of high-dimensional data such as large images, while maintaining tractable exact log-likelihood and latent-variable inference?
21b786b3f870fc7fa247c143aa41de88b1fc6141.hypothesis: Introducing an invertible 1×1 convolution as a learnable and efficient channel permutation within a flow-based generative model, combined with actnorm and affine coupling layers in a multi-scale architecture, will improve log-likelihood performance, synthesis quality, and scalability to high-resolution images compared to previous flow-based models.
21b786b3f870fc7fa247c143aa41de88b1fc6141.proposed_method: A novel generative flow model is developed that integrates three key components in each step of the flow: actnorm (activation normalization) layers with data-dependent initialization, invertible 1×1 convolutions for learned channel mixing, and affine coupling layers for expressive reversible transformations. The actnorm layer performs per-channel affine transformations initialized to zero mean and unit variance using a minibatch, then learned during training. The invertible 1×1 convolution replaces fixed or random permutations with a learnable linear transformation, parameterized efficiently via LU decomposition to reduce computational cost. Affine coupling layers split the input tensor along the channel dimension and apply a neural network to one half to generate scale and shift parameters for the other half, initialized to perform identity mappings for stable training. These steps are composed in a multi-scale architecture, enabling the model to capture dependencies at different resolutions and scales.
21b786b3f870fc7fa247c143aa41de88b1fc6141.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on standard image modeling benchmarks including CIFAR-10, ImageNet (32×32 and 64×64), and LSUN (bedroom, tower, church outdoor), as well as high-resolution CelebA-HQ (256×256). The model is compared to RealNVP and other flow-based models, using bits per dimension as the primary evaluation metric. Training uses consistent preprocessing and architecture settings, with three-layer convolutional neural networks in coupling layers, and experiments are averaged over multiple random seeds. Additional qualitative experiments include synthesis, latent space interpolation, and attribute manipulation on CelebA-HQ, with temperature scaling explored for sample quality. Batch sizes, model depth (number of flow steps and levels), and computational efficiency are systematically varied and reported.
21b786b3f870fc7fa247c143aa41de88b1fc6141.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the invertible 1×1 convolution as a learnable and efficient generalization of channel permutations within flow-based models, enabling improved mixing of information across channels. The actnorm layer with data-dependent initialization addresses challenges in training deep flows with small batch sizes. The overall architecture achieves state-of-the-art log-likelihoods on multiple image benchmarks and demonstrates, for the first time, efficient and high-quality synthesis of high-resolution natural images using a likelihood-based model. The method also enables meaningful latent space manipulations and efficient parallelizable synthesis and inference.

21bf133b44ae682589b76d75acce296cded2b49e.title: Neural Congealing: Aligning Images to a Joint Semantic Atlas
21bf133b44ae682589b76d75acce296cded2b49e.research_question: How can a set of images with shared semantic content, but potentially large variations in appearance, pose, and background, be automatically and jointly aligned into a unified semantic space without requiring additional training data or domain-specific models?
21bf133b44ae682589b76d75acce296cded2b49e.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging pre-trained DINO-ViT features as dense semantic descriptors, combined with a self-supervised, test-time optimization framework, enables robust and accurate joint alignment of diverse image sets into a shared semantic atlas, even under significant intra-set variations and without the need for domain-specific training.
21bf133b44ae682589b76d75acce296cded2b49e.proposed_method: A novel self-supervised framework will be developed that, given a set of images, constructs a unified 2D latent semantic atlas representing the common content in DINO-ViT feature space. Each image is mapped to this atlas via a composition of rigid and non-rigid transformations, both parameterized by Spatial Transformer Networks (STNs). The method extracts DINO-ViT features and initial saliency masks for each image, then jointly optimizes the atlas features, atlas saliency, and transformation parameters to align the images in feature space. The optimization objective includes a semantic matching loss weighted by atlas saliency, a saliency voting loss to robustly estimate shared regions, regularization terms to encourage plausible transformations and sparse, localized atlas features, and a centering loss to anchor the shared object in the atlas. The approach is fully automatic, operates at test-time on arbitrary image sets, and does not require any additional training data or fine-tuning of the DINO-ViT backbone.
21bf133b44ae682589b76d75acce296cded2b49e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of image sets, including those from LSUN, AFHQ, Pixabay, Shutterstock, and Internet collections, with set sizes ranging from 5 to 25 images. The method will be evaluated on semantic point correspondence benchmarks such as SPair-71K and CUB-200-2011, using the PCK-Transfer metric (percentage of keypoints transferred within a threshold of the ground truth). Baselines for comparison will include GANgealing (a GAN-supervised method requiring domain-specific training), as well as state-of-the-art supervised, weakly-supervised, and self-supervised correspondence methods. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the contribution of each loss term. Qualitative results will demonstrate alignment quality, robustness to clutter and domain variation, and the ability to propagate edits across the set via the learned atlas.
21bf133b44ae682589b76d75acce296cded2b49e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to leverage pre-trained DINO-ViT features for dense, joint alignment of in-the-wild image sets in a zero-shot, test-time optimization setting. Unlike prior methods, it does not require domain-specific generative models or large-scale training, and can handle diverse domains and mixed-category sets. The framework introduces a robust, self-supervised loss formulation that isolates shared semantic content and enables automatic edit propagation across the set. This method is claimed to outperform or match state-of-the-art methods on challenging benchmarks, while being significantly more flexible and data-efficient.

22274d28d90df56167d59f04d6f1106fe2f1c97a.title: DualPrompt: Complementary Prompting for Rehearsal-free Continual Learning
22274d28d90df56167d59f04d6f1106fe2f1c97a.research_question: How can a continual learning framework be developed that enables a single model to learn a sequence of tasks without catastrophic forgetting, while avoiding the use of rehearsal buffers and maintaining high performance in challenging class-incremental settings?
22274d28d90df56167d59f04d6f1106fe2f1c97a.hypothesis: A continual learning method that leverages complementary prompt-based modules to encode both task-invariant and task-specific knowledge can achieve state-of-the-art performance without requiring rehearsal buffers, thereby overcoming memory and privacy limitations of existing methods.
22274d28d90df56167d59f04d6f1106fe2f1c97a.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces DualPrompt, a rehearsal-free continual learning framework that attaches two types of learnable prompts—G(eneral)-Prompt and E(xpert)-Prompt—to a pre-trained transformer-based backbone (e.g., Vision Transformer). The G-Prompt encodes task-invariant knowledge and is shared across all tasks, while the E-Prompt encodes task-specific knowledge and is associated with a learnable task key for each task. During training, both prompt types are attached at selected layers of the transformer, with their positions determined via empirical search on a validation set. The E-Prompt for each input is selected through a query function based on feature similarity to task keys, and both prompt sets are trained jointly with a classification head using a combination of cross-entropy and matching losses. The method supports configurable prompting functions, such as Prompt Tuning and Prefix Tuning, to control how prompts interact with backbone representations.
22274d28d90df56167d59f04d6f1106fe2f1c97a.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on challenging continual learning benchmarks, including Split ImageNet-R (derived from ImageNet-R, split into 10 tasks of 20 classes each) and Split CIFAR-100 (split into 10 tasks of 10 classes each). The evaluation follows the class-incremental setting, where task identity is unknown at test time and no rehearsal buffer is used. DualPrompt is compared against state-of-the-art regularization-based, rehearsal-based, and prompt-based baselines, including EWC, LwF, ER, GDumb, BiC, DER++, Co2L, and L2P. Performance is measured using average accuracy and forgetting metrics. Experimental protocols include using pre-trained vision transformers, empirical search for prompt attachment positions, and validation on both average accuracy and forgetting across tasks.
22274d28d90df56167d59f04d6f1106fe2f1c97a.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a dual-prompt mechanism that explicitly decouples the learning of task-invariant and task-specific knowledge via G-Prompt and E-Prompt, respectively, providing a lightweight and memory-efficient alternative to rehearsal-based methods. The approach is the first to empirically demonstrate that the placement and configuration of complementary prompts in pre-trained models are critical for effective rehearsal-free continual learning. Additionally, the introduction of the Split ImageNet-R benchmark offers a more challenging and realistic testbed for rehearsal-free continual learning research.

22552dd0e7789f175a302055f06444a12e22b652.title: Video-MME: The First-Ever Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark of Multi-modal LLMs in Video Analysis
22552dd0e7789f175a302055f06444a12e22b652.research_question: How can a comprehensive and challenging benchmark be developed to evaluate the capabilities of multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) in video analysis, with respect to diverse video types, temporal durations, and multi-modal input modalities?
22552dd0e7789f175a302055f06444a12e22b652.hypothesis: A benchmark that incorporates a wide spectrum of video types, durations, and modalities (including video frames, subtitles, and audio), with high-quality expert annotations, will enable more rigorous and holistic evaluation of MLLMs and reveal current limitations in their video understanding abilities.
22552dd0e7789f175a302055f06444a12e22b652.proposed_method: A new evaluation benchmark, Video-MME, will be constructed to systematically assess MLLMs on video analysis tasks. The methodology involves curating a dataset of 900 videos sourced from YouTube, spanning six primary domains and 30 sub-categories, with durations ranging from 11 seconds to 1 hour. Each video will be annotated with three multiple-choice QA pairs, resulting in 2,700 high-quality questions designed by expert annotators to require multi-modal and temporal reasoning. The dataset will include associated subtitles and audio tracks to enable evaluation of models under different modality settings. A rigorous quality review process will ensure that questions are challenging, unanswerable by text alone, and closely tied to video content. The benchmark will be designed to support evaluation across short, medium, and long video durations, and will include detailed metadata and certificate length analysis to quantify temporal reasoning requirements.
22552dd0e7789f175a302055f06444a12e22b652.experiment_details: Experiments will involve benchmarking a broad set of state-of-the-art MLLMs, including both commercial (e.g., Gemini 1.5 Pro, GPT-4V, GPT-4o) and open-source models (e.g., VILA-1.5, LLaVA-NeXT-Video, VITA-1.5), as well as advanced image-based MLLMs (e.g., Qwen-VL-Max, InternVL-Chat-V1.5). Models will be evaluated on the multiple-choice QA task using the Video-MME dataset, under varying input modalities: video frames only, frames plus subtitles, and frames plus audio. Performance will be measured by accuracy, with results reported across different video durations (short, medium, long) and domains. Additional analyses will assess the impact of subtitles and audio on model performance, and examine how performance degrades with increasing video length. Baseline comparisons will be made to prior video QA benchmarks, and certificate length analysis will be used to quantify the temporal complexity of questions.
22552dd0e7789f175a302055f06444a12e22b652.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark is the first to offer a full-spectrum, multi-modal evaluation of MLLMs in video analysis, covering a uniquely broad range of video types, durations, and modalities. It introduces rigorous, expert-annotated, multi-choice QA pairs that require deep temporal and compositional reasoning, and includes a detailed certificate length analysis to quantify temporal difficulty. The benchmark enables systematic evaluation of both video and image-based MLLMs, and provides new insights into the limitations of current models, especially in handling long-range temporal dependencies and multi-modal information. The inclusion of subtitles and audio as standard modalities for evaluation is also a novel contribution.

226df707ea2ba59ccf72def048c379a65783107e.title: Bayesian Prediction-Powered Inference
226df707ea2ba59ccf72def048c379a65783107e.research_question: How can statistical estimates be improved when only limited human-labeled data is available, by leveraging larger amounts of data labeled by an automatic system that may be biased or imperfect? What general frameworks can be developed to enable task-appropriate combination of human and automatic labels for more precise inference across a variety of evaluation tasks?
226df707ea2ba59ccf72def048c379a65783107e.hypothesis: By employing a Bayesian inference framework that flexibly combines small amounts of human-labeled data with large amounts of automatic (potentially biased) labels, it is possible to construct estimators that yield tighter and more reliable confidence intervals for key evaluation metrics than classical or previously proposed PPI methods.
226df707ea2ba59ccf72def048c379a65783107e.proposed_method: A Bayesian framework for prediction-powered inference (PPI) will be developed, enabling the design of new proxy estimands that combine human and automatic labels in a statistically principled manner. The method will utilize Monte Carlo integration to compute credible intervals for arbitrary functions of means and proportions derived from both human and automatic ratings. Several novel PPI estimators will be introduced: (1) Bayesian variants of the difference estimator and its 'powertuned' extension, (2) stratified estimators that partition the data based on autorater predictions to correct for non-uniform bias, and (3) chain rule estimators designed for discrete or abstaining autoraters, as well as for side-by-side (paired) evaluation tasks. Each estimator will be constructed to ensure unbiasedness and reduced variance by exploiting the structure of the available data and the properties of the autorater.
226df707ea2ba59ccf72def048c379a65783107e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple natural language processing evaluation datasets, including the Seahorse dataset for multilingual summarization quality and attributed question answering (AQA) datasets. Each dataset contains a limited set of human-labeled examples and a larger set of autorater-labeled examples. The proposed methods will be compared to classical confidence interval estimation and prior PPI baselines, such as the difference estimator and powertuning. Evaluation metrics will include the width of the confidence/credible intervals and their empirical coverage rates. Experiments will systematically vary the number of human-labeled samples and assess performance across different tasks, autorater calibration levels, and partitioning strategies (e.g., equal-frequency bins and regression tree-based partitions).
226df707ea2ba59ccf72def048c379a65783107e.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a general Bayesian framework for PPI that simplifies the design of new estimators for diverse evaluation tasks, leveraging Monte Carlo integration for efficient and flexible inference. Several new PPI estimators are proposed, including stratified estimators that address non-uniform autorater bias and chain rule estimators for discrete and abstaining autoraters, as well as for paired comparison tasks. The approach enables tighter and more reliable confidence intervals than classical or previous PPI methods, and supports easy adaptation to new metrics and tasks. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate substantial improvements in confidence interval width and coverage across a range of realistic evaluation scenarios.

227a616814355c3b8765d09a224a9c08fb260559.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of State Space Models
227a616814355c3b8765d09a224a9c08fb260559.research_question: How can parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods be effectively applied to state space model (SSM)-based architectures, and what strategies or new methods can optimize adaptation of SSM modules for downstream tasks across diverse domains?
227a616814355c3b8765d09a224a9c08fb260559.hypothesis: Existing PEFT methods, such as LoRA and its variants, are suboptimal for SSM modules, and a specialized approach that selectively tunes key dimensions within SSMs will yield superior performance and efficiency.
227a616814355c3b8765d09a224a9c08fb260559.proposed_method: A new parameter-efficient fine-tuning method, Sparse Dimension Tuning (SDT), will be developed specifically for SSM modules. SDT operates by first performing a warmup phase to estimate the importance of each channel and state dimension within the SSM, then categorizes dimensions as pruned, frozen, or trainable based on their magnitude and contribution. Only a small subset of the most relevant channels and state dimensions are updated during fine-tuning, while the rest are either frozen or effectively set to zero. SDT will be combined with LoRA (or its variants) applied to linear projection matrices, leveraging LoRA’s strengths for those components while addressing the unique structure of SSMs. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to guarantee that SDT, when combined with LoRA, can match the expressivity of a target model with significantly fewer trainable parameters.
227a616814355c3b8765d09a224a9c08fb260559.experiment_details: Experiments will benchmark six popular PEFT methods, including prompt tuning, prefix-tuning, BitFit, Additional-scan, LoRA, and DoRA, across SSM-based models (Mamba) and hybrid models (Jamba) on a diverse set of tasks: natural language understanding (GLUE), RDF-to-text generation (DART), summarization (SAMSum), text-to-SQL (Spider), and computer vision (CIFAR-10, CelebA). Each method will be applied to different target modules (SSM, linear projections, both), with parameter budgets capped (e.g., <1% for Mamba, <0.15% for Jamba). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE, and task-specific scores. Additional synthetic regression experiments will validate theoretical claims by matching the outputs of a smaller target SSM with a larger frozen SSM using various fine-tuning strategies. Hyperparameter tuning and ablation studies will be conducted to ensure fair comparison and to analyze the impact of dimension selection in SDT.
227a616814355c3b8765d09a224a9c08fb260559.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces Sparse Dimension Tuning (SDT), the first PEFT method specifically designed for SSM modules, which selectively updates only the most relevant channels and state dimensions. Theoretical guarantees are established for the expressivity and efficiency of SDT when combined with LoRA on linear projections, showing that any smaller target SSM can be matched by a larger frozen model with minimal parameter updates. Comprehensive benchmarking demonstrates that SDT, when paired with LoRA, achieves state-of-the-art performance on SSM-based models, outperforming all existing PEFT methods for SSM modules. The approach also provides a practical and computationally efficient alternative to existing methods, with reduced memory and training overhead.

227feac3b9e56063e8e086d11193865ce21381f9.title: Robust Evaluation of Diffusion-Based Adversarial Purification
227feac3b9e56063e8e086d11193865ce21381f9.research_question: How can the robustness of diffusion-based adversarial purification methods be reliably evaluated, and what strategies can improve their defense against strong adaptive adversarial attacks?
227feac3b9e56063e8e086d11193865ce21381f9.hypothesis: A carefully designed evaluation framework and a novel gradual noise-scheduling purification strategy will yield more accurate robustness assessments and improved adversarial defense performance for diffusion-based purification methods compared to current practices.
227feac3b9e56063e8e086d11193865ce21381f9.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation framework will be developed for diffusion-based adversarial purification methods, focusing on white-box attacks. The method will recommend direct back-propagation through the full purification process to compute gradients for attacks; if memory constraints prevent this, a surrogate process will be used to approximate gradients more effectively than adjoint or BPDA methods. For defense, a gradual noise-scheduling strategy will be introduced for multi-step purification, where the number of forward noise steps varies across purification iterations to maximize robustness. Extensive hyperparameter analysis will be conducted, including the number of forward steps, denoising steps, and purification iterations, to empirically determine optimal configurations. The approach will also consider ensemble purification runs and test the transferability of attacks using different diffusion samplers.
227feac3b9e56063e8e086d11193865ce21381f9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on CIFAR-10, ImageNet, and SVHN datasets using pretrained classifiers such as WideResNet-28-10, WideResNet-70-16, and ResNet-50. Diffusion models including DDPM, DDPM++, and Guided Diffusion will be used for purification. Robustness will be evaluated against strong white-box attacks (PGD+EOT, AutoAttack, BPDA) and black-box attacks (Square Attack), with attack strengths set to ℓ∞ (ϵ = 8/255) and ℓ2 (ϵ = 0.5). Baselines will include adversarial training methods and state-of-the-art purification defenses (e.g., DiffPure, ADP, GDMP, SODEF, DISCO). Evaluation metrics will be standard and robust accuracy, with experiments reporting mean and standard deviation over multiple runs. The impact of hyperparameters and the proposed gradual noise-scheduling strategy will be systematically compared to existing approaches.
227feac3b9e56063e8e086d11193865ce21381f9.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a robust evaluation guideline tailored specifically for diffusion-based purification, highlighting limitations of current practices such as reliance on adjoint and BPDA methods. A novel gradual noise-scheduling strategy for multi-step purification is proposed, empirically shown to improve robustness over previous diffusion-based defenses. The work provides the first comprehensive analysis of hyperparameter effects in this context and demonstrates that direct gradient-based attacks (using surrogate processes when needed) are more effective for evaluating these defenses. The proposed evaluation and defense strategies are expected to set new standards for reliable robustness assessment and improved adversarial purification.

2286f32d98211caac715ee9087a9192d9c3241a0.title: 4+3 Phases of Compute-Optimal Neural Scaling Laws
2286f32d98211caac715ee9087a9192d9c3241a0.research_question: How do data complexity, target complexity, and model parameter count interact to determine compute-optimal neural scaling laws in the regime where compute is the primary constraint and data is effectively infinite? What are the distinct phases of scaling behavior that emerge as a function of these parameters, and how can the optimal model size be selected to minimize loss under a fixed compute budget?
2286f32d98211caac715ee9087a9192d9c3241a0.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, in a solvable neural scaling model with three parameters (data complexity, target complexity, and model parameter count), there exist distinct phases in the compute-optimal scaling law regime, each characterized by different dominant factors (model capacity, optimizer noise, feature embedding), and that these phases can be mathematically delineated. Furthermore, it is anticipated that universal scaling laws may emerge in certain regions of parameter space.
2286f32d98211caac715ee9087a9192d9c3241a0.proposed_method: A three-parameter power-law random features (PLRF) model will be analyzed, where data and target complexities are parameterized by exponents α and β, and model capacity is controlled by the parameter count d. The model will be trained using one-pass stochastic gradient descent (SGD) on a mean-squared error loss, with the data vector embedded via a random Gaussian matrix W. The expected loss trajectory under SGD will be characterized by deriving and solving a convolution-type Volterra equation, using deterministic equivalents from random matrix theory to replace random quantities with their asymptotic deterministic counterparts. Explicit asymptotic forms for the loss components will be derived, allowing the identification of the dominant terms in different regions of the (α, β) phase plane. Analytical expressions for the compute-optimal model size and scaling law exponents will be extracted by solving for the tradeoff points between these terms, under the constraint of a fixed compute budget.
2286f32d98211caac715ee9087a9192d9c3241a0.experiment_details: Experiments will involve numerical simulations of the PLRF model, varying data complexity (α), target complexity (β), and model parameter count (d), with large ambient and model dimensions (v, d) to approach the asymptotic regime. One-pass SGD will be run with fixed batch size and learning rate, and the loss trajectory will be recorded as a function of floating point operation budget (flops). Empirical scaling law exponents and optimal model sizes will be measured and compared against theoretical predictions derived from the Volterra equation and the deterministic equivalents. Baselines will include both population gradient descent and alternative parameter regimes to isolate the effects of SGD noise and feature embedding. Evaluation metrics will focus on the achieved loss at fixed compute, the scaling law exponents, and the agreement between empirical and theoretical phase boundaries.
2286f32d98211caac715ee9087a9192d9c3241a0.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a mathematically rigorous framework for analyzing compute-optimal scaling laws in neural models, delineating four distinct phases (with three subphases) in the data/target complexity plane and providing explicit analytical expressions for the optimal model size and loss scaling exponents in each phase. The approach leverages deterministic equivalents and Volterra equations to accurately capture SGD dynamics, including the effects of optimizer noise and feature embedding, which are often neglected in prior scaling law analyses. The identification of universal scaling regimes and the precise characterization of phase transitions represent significant innovations, as does the demonstration that SGD noise and feature embedding can fundamentally alter compute-optimal behavior. The framework also offers new insights into the limitations of empirically derived scaling laws and suggests directions for algorithmic improvements.

229b45e022634586218d3c0abc29874d8560f5a4.title: Understanding while Exploring: Semantics-driven Active Mapping
229b45e022634586218d3c0abc29874d8560f5a4.research_question: How can a mobile robot autonomously and efficiently explore and semantically map unknown 3D environments, achieving high-fidelity geometric and semantic understanding with minimal observations and robustness to noisy semantic predictions?
229b45e022634586218d3c0abc29874d8560f5a4.hypothesis: Integrating semantic and geometric uncertainty quantification with a sparse, high-dimensional semantic representation into an active mapping framework will enable robots to select informative viewpoints, resulting in more complete, accurate, and robust semantic maps with fewer observations, even when semantic predictions are noisy.
229b45e022634586218d3c0abc29874d8560f5a4.proposed_method: A novel active semantic mapping framework, termed Active Semantic Gaussian Mapping (ActiveSGM), will be developed by building upon a 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) backbone. The method will encode geometric, photometric, and semantic properties within each 3D Gaussian, using a sparse semantic representation that retains only the top-k most probable semantic categories per Gaussian to reduce memory overhead. Semantic predictions will be obtained from a state-of-the-art segmentation model (e.g., OneFormer) and incorporated as probability distributions. The mapping process will be optimized via differentiable rendering, employing a combined Hellinger distance and cosine similarity loss between rendered and predicted semantic distributions, with entropy-based masking to filter uncertain supervision. A keyframe selection strategy will balance local and global coverage, and the pipeline will decouple semantic and geometric optimization for stability.
229b45e022634586218d3c0abc29874d8560f5a4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in simulated photorealistic environments using the Habitat simulator, with evaluation on the Replica, ReplicaSLAM, and Matterport3D (MP3D) datasets. Semantic predictions will be generated by fine-tuning OneFormer on each dataset, and the system will be evaluated on both seen and novel views. Baselines will include state-of-the-art NeRF/3DGS-based semantic SLAM methods (e.g., SGS-SLAM, NIDS-SLAM, DNS-SLAM, SNI-SLAM), as well as passive semantic mapping and geometry-based active mapping approaches. Evaluation metrics will cover semantic segmentation (mean Intersection over Union, Top-1/Top-3 accuracy, mean Average Precision, F1-score), geometric reconstruction (accuracy, completeness, completeness ratio), and photometric quality (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, Depth L1). Ablation studies will assess the impact of the number of retained semantic categories and different loss functions.
229b45e022634586218d3c0abc29874d8560f5a4.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first dense active semantic mapping system built on a 3D Gaussian Splatting backbone, integrating semantic-aware mapping and planning for active reconstruction. Key innovations include a semantics-driven exploration criterion that jointly leverages geometric and semantic uncertainty, a sparse top-k semantic representation for efficient storage and rendering of high-dimensional distributions, and robustness to noisy semantic predictions without reliance on ground-truth labels. The closed-loop system enables efficient, adaptive exploration and mapping, achieving high-quality semantic and geometric reconstruction with fewer observations compared to existing methods.

22ab4219371366a4e890382bc0ca606130840ca7.title: Statistical Rejection Sampling Improves Preference Optimization
22ab4219371366a4e890382bc0ca606130840ca7.research_question: How can the alignment of large language models with human preferences be improved using scalable, stable, and efficient offline preference optimization methods that do not rely on online reinforcement learning from human feedback?
22ab4219371366a4e890382bc0ca606130840ca7.hypothesis: A statistical rejection sampling approach that generates preference pairs from an estimated optimal policy, combined with a unified preference optimization framework, will yield more accurate and effective alignment of language models with human preferences compared to existing offline methods such as SLiC and DPO.
22ab4219371366a4e890382bc0ca606130840ca7.proposed_method: A novel offline preference optimization framework will be developed that leverages statistical rejection sampling to construct preference pairs from an estimated optimal policy. The method begins by training a pairwise reward-ranking model on human preference data. Using this reward model and a supervised fine-tuned (SFT) policy as a proposal distribution, statistical rejection sampling is performed to generate response pairs that approximate samples from the optimal policy.
