These sampled pairs are then labeled using the reward model, and the language model is fine-tuned using classification losses, with both logistic (sigmoid-norm) and hinge-based (SVM-like) loss functions considered. The framework also unifies and extends the loss functions used in SLiC and DPO, providing a comprehensive recipe for preference pair generation and optimization.
22ab4219371366a4e890382bc0ca606130840ca7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple generative tasks, including Reddit TL;DR summarization and Anthropic Helpful and Harmless (HH) dialogue datasets. The policy model will be initialized from a T5-large (770M) or T5-XXL (11B) supervised fine-tuned checkpoint, and a T5-XXL pairwise reward-ranking model will be used for preference labeling. Various baselines will be compared, including DPO, SLiC, RAFT, and ReST, with ablations over loss functions and preference pair construction strategies. Evaluation will be performed using proxy reward models, gold reward models (e.g., PaLM2-S), automated side-by-side (AutoSxS) comparisons with large language models, and human evaluations via crowd-sourcing. Hyperparameters such as the rejection sampling temperature (β), loss scaling (γ), and sampling strategies (number of candidates, ranking procedures) will be systematically varied and analyzed.
22ab4219371366a4e890382bc0ca606130840ca7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a scalable and practical statistical rejection sampling algorithm for generating preference pairs from an estimated optimal policy, enabling more accurate offline preference optimization. The method unifies and extends the theoretical foundations of existing offline preference optimization techniques (SLiC and DPO) by providing a statistical perspective on their loss functions and sampling distributions. Comprehensive experimental results demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines in both automated and human evaluations across multiple tasks. The approach also provides insights into the importance of explicit reward models and the trade-offs in preference pair sampling and ranking strategies.

22ae20f20d0b4e6451ae41cc76e58a9221e90df9.title: LEACE: Perfect linear concept erasure in closed form
22ae20f20d0b4e6451ae41cc76e58a9221e90df9.research_question: How can specified concepts be perfectly and efficiently erased from neural network embeddings, such that all linear classifiers are unable to detect the concept, while minimally altering the original embedding and preserving downstream task performance?
22ae20f20d0b4e6451ae41cc76e58a9221e90df9.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a closed-form, least-squares optimal affine transformation exists which can provably erase all linearly available information about a target concept from an embedding, and that applying this transformation at every layer of a deep neural network will effectively remove the concept without significant collateral damage to other features or downstream tasks.
22ae20f20d0b4e6451ae41cc76e58a9221e90df9.proposed_method: A novel closed-form method, Least-squares Concept Erasure (LEACE), is proposed to remove all linearly available information about a specified concept from an embedding. LEACE is derived by identifying the unique affine transformation that minimizes the mean squared distance between the original and transformed embeddings, subject to the constraint that all linear classifiers are unable to predict the concept (i.e., zero cross-covariance between features and concept labels). The method involves centering and whitening the data, projecting onto the subspace orthogonal to the concept, and then unwhitening, ensuring minimal distortion. For deep networks, a procedure termed 'concept scrubbing' is introduced, which sequentially applies LEACE at each layer, fitting the transformation based on the current hidden state and immediately updating activations before proceeding to the next layer. This approach allows for efficient, layer-wise removal of concept information throughout the network.
22ae20f20d0b4e6451ae41cc76e58a9221e90df9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several tasks and models. To evaluate intrinsic erasure, the method will be applied to BERT embeddings using the biographies dataset, removing gender information and measuring the ability of linear classifiers to recover the erased concept, as well as the impact on the main task of profession prediction. Comparisons will be made against baselines such as RLACE, INLP, and random projections, using metrics like classification accuracy, mean squared error, and TPR-GAP for fairness. For deep language models, concept scrubbing will be evaluated on autoregressive models (e.g., EleutherAI's Pythia and Meta's LLaMA) using part-of-speech tags from the Universal Dependencies dataset, with perplexity and cross-entropy loss as evaluation metrics. The effect of erasure at each layer will be analyzed, and the method's efficiency and collateral damage will be compared to prior approaches such as SAL and INLP.
22ae20f20d0b4e6451ae41cc76e58a9221e90df9.novelty_claims: The proposed method provides the first closed-form, provably optimal affine transformation for perfect linear concept erasure, minimizing distortion under all inner-product-induced norms. The approach generalizes and improves upon prior linear erasure methods by guaranteeing both perfect erasure and minimal change to the embedding. The concept scrubbing procedure enables, for the first time, efficient and practical removal of concepts from every layer of deep neural networks, overcoming limitations of iterative or gradient-based approaches. The method is computationally efficient, scalable, and causes significantly less collateral damage to useful features than existing techniques.

22e2d9505e64c4725e9f868ee6886a9c8356d1e3.title: Adam Can Converge Without Any Modification on Update Rules
22e2d9505e64c4725e9f868ee6886a9c8356d1e3.research_question: Can the original Adam optimization algorithm, without any modifications to its update rules, be theoretically and empirically shown to converge under practical settings, and what are the precise conditions on its hyperparameters that govern its convergence and divergence behavior?
22e2d9505e64c4725e9f868ee6886a9c8356d1e3.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, contrary to prior theoretical claims of divergence, the vanilla Adam optimizer can provably converge to critical points or their neighborhoods for a broad range of hyperparameters, provided that the optimization problem is fixed before hyperparameter selection and that the second-order momentum parameter is sufficiently large.
22e2d9505e64c4725e9f868ee6886a9c8356d1e3.proposed_method: A rigorous theoretical analysis will be conducted on the convergence properties of the original Adam algorithm under the setting where the optimization problem (i.e., the data and objective function) is fixed prior to hyperparameter tuning. The analysis will focus on the relationship between the first-order (β1) and second-order (β2) momentum parameters, establishing sufficient and necessary conditions for convergence and divergence. The methodology will avoid imposing bounded gradient or bounded momentum assumptions, instead leveraging novel stochastic process analysis techniques to handle the intricate dependencies between Adam's momentum and adaptive stepsizes. Theoretical results will be complemented by the construction of explicit counterexamples to characterize divergence regions, and new proof techniques will be developed to analyze the stochastic nonlinear dynamics inherent in Adam's updates.
22e2d9505e64c4725e9f868ee6886a9c8356d1e3.experiment_details: Empirical validation will be performed on both synthetic and real-world tasks. Experiments will include optimization of convex functions with and without the strong growth condition, as well as standard machine learning benchmarks such as MNIST and CIFAR-10 for image classification, and WikiText-103 for language modeling with TransformerXL. For each task, Adam will be run with a grid of (β1, β2) hyperparameter combinations, with the optimization problem and batch size fixed prior to hyperparameter selection. Baselines will include different regions of the (β1, β2) parameter space, particularly those previously identified as divergent. Evaluation metrics will include optimality gap, training loss, and gradient norm, with careful tracking of convergence or divergence behavior across settings.
22e2d9505e64c4725e9f868ee6886a9c8356d1e3.novelty_claims: The proposed research claims to provide the first theoretical proof that vanilla Adam can converge without any modification to its update rules for a wide range of hyperparameters, including those commonly used in practice. The analysis removes the need for bounded gradient or bounded momentum assumptions, which are prevalent in prior work. The study introduces a non-asymptotic characterization of the convergence and divergence regions in the (β1, β2) hyperparameter space, revealing a phase transition governed by the second-order momentum parameter. New analytical techniques are developed to handle the stochastic nonlinear dependencies in Adam, and the results offer practical guidance for hyperparameter tuning in real-world applications.

22ee3aab390c3adeb8cf08eacf079e9445e222da.title: SA-Solver: Stochastic Adams Solver for Fast Sampling of Diffusion Models
22ee3aab390c3adeb8cf08eacf079e9445e222da.research_question: How can the efficiency and sample quality of diffusion probabilistic models (DPMs) be improved for generative tasks, particularly by developing fast, training-free stochastic solvers for diffusion stochastic differential equations (SDEs)?
22ee3aab390c3adeb8cf08eacf079e9445e222da.hypothesis: Introducing a variance-controlled family of diffusion SDEs and solving them with a high-order stochastic Adams method, augmented with predictor-corrector steps and data-prediction model parameterization, will yield more efficient and higher-quality sampling from DPMs compared to existing deterministic and stochastic solvers, especially under limited function evaluations or inaccurate score estimation.
22ee3aab390c3adeb8cf08eacf079e9445e222da.proposed_method: A new stochastic solver, termed SA-Solver, will be developed for fast sampling from diffusion SDEs in DPMs. The approach introduces a family of variance-controlled diffusion SDEs parameterized by a noise scale function τ(t), allowing explicit control over the magnitude of stochasticity during sampling. The solver is based on the stochastic Adams method, leveraging linear multi-step integration with Lagrange interpolation of previous model evaluations for high-order accuracy. Predictor-corrector steps are incorporated to refine solution estimates at each timestep, and the data-prediction model parameterization is used to improve sample quality. The method analytically computes the variance and integrates the stochastic and deterministic terms, ensuring theoretical convergence guarantees.
22ee3aab390c3adeb8cf08eacf079e9445e222da.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of benchmark image generation datasets, including CIFAR10 (32x32), ImageNet (64x64 and 256x256), and LSUN Bedroom (256x256), utilizing both pixel-space and latent-space diffusion models such as ADM, EDM, Latent Diffusion, and DiT. The evaluation metric will be Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), measured under varying numbers of function evaluations (NFEs), typically sampling 50,000 images per experiment. Comparisons will be made against state-of-the-art deterministic and stochastic samplers, including DDIM, DPM-Solver, UniPC, Heun, and EDM samplers, using their recommended hyperparameters and timesteps. Ablation studies will assess the impact of predictor/corrector steps, noise scale τ, and model parameterization. Additional experiments will evaluate robustness under inaccurate score estimation and limited training.
22ee3aab390c3adeb8cf08eacf079e9445e222da.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretically grounded, high-order stochastic Adams solver for diffusion SDEs, which incorporates variance control via a tunable noise scale and predictor-corrector refinement. This method generalizes and subsumes several existing solvers as special cases, provides explicit analytical solutions for the semi-linear SDE structure, and achieves state-of-the-art FID scores across diverse datasets and models. The approach is training-free, efficient for few-step sampling, and demonstrates superior robustness when the underlying score model is imperfect or undertrained.

23525374cfd3af714f3ffb7a203b1ef3253333fe.title: WebShop: Towards Scalable Real-World Web Interaction with Grounded Language Agents
23525374cfd3af714f3ffb7a203b1ef3253333fe.research_question: How can scalable, real-world interactive environments be developed to train and evaluate grounded language agents capable of complex web-based tasks, such as online shopping, using natural language instructions?
23525374cfd3af714f3ffb7a203b1ef3253333fe.hypothesis: Grounded language agents trained in a large-scale, realistic web-based environment with programmatically defined rewards and diverse, real-world linguistic instructions will achieve higher task success and better generalization to real-world web tasks than rule-based or non-grounded baselines.
23525374cfd3af714f3ffb7a203b1ef3253333fe.proposed_method: A simulated e-commerce environment will be constructed, containing over one million real-world products and thousands of crowd-sourced natural language instructions. The environment will be designed as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP), where agents receive natural language instructions and must navigate, search, select, and purchase products by interacting with various types of web pages. The agent architecture will combine pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT for action choice, BART for search query generation) and visual models (e.g., ResNet for image features), with an attention fusion layer to integrate multi-modal information. Agents will be trained using a combination of imitation learning from human demonstrations and reinforcement learning with automatically computed rewards based on product attributes, options, and price matching the instruction.
23525374cfd3af714f3ffb7a203b1ef3253333fe.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the WebShop environment, which includes 1.18 million products scraped from Amazon across five categories and 12,087 crowd-sourced instructions. Human demonstrations (over 1,600 trajectories) will be collected for imitation learning and evaluation. Baselines will include rule-based heuristics (e.g., searching the instruction text and buying the first result), as well as agents trained with imitation learning, reinforcement learning, and ablated architectures. Evaluation metrics will include average reward (Task Score) and Success Rate (portion of instructions fully satisfied). Additional experiments will test sim-to-real transfer by deploying trained agents on real-world Amazon and eBay websites, comparing performance to human users and rule-based baselines.
23525374cfd3af714f3ffb7a203b1ef3253333fe.novelty_claims: The proposed environment introduces the first large-scale, realistic, and scalable web-based benchmark for grounded language agents, featuring a diverse set of real-world products, linguistically rich instructions, and a programmatically defined reward function that eliminates the need for human-in-the-loop evaluation. The modular design supports both imitation and reinforcement learning, multi-modal input (text and images), and high-level, context-based action spaces. The approach demonstrates non-trivial sim-to-real transfer, showing that agents trained in the simulated environment can generalize to real-world web tasks, outperforming rule-based baselines and providing a foundation for future research in grounded language understanding and decision making on the web.

235303a8bc1e4892efd525a38ead657422d8a519.title: Transformers are Sample Efficient World Models
235303a8bc1e4892efd525a38ead657422d8a519.research_question: Can reinforcement learning agents achieve high sample efficiency and strong performance in visually complex, partially observable environments by learning entirely within a world model, and what architectural choices enable such efficiency?
235303a8bc1e4892efd525a38ead657422d8a519.hypothesis: A world model architecture combining a discrete autoencoder for image tokenization and an autoregressive Transformer for environment dynamics modeling will enable reinforcement learning agents to achieve state-of-the-art sample efficiency and competitive or superhuman performance in challenging visual domains, such as Atari 100k, without the need for lookahead search.
235303a8bc1e4892efd525a38ead657422d8a519.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops a reinforcement learning agent that learns exclusively within the imagination of a world model. The world model consists of two main components: a discrete autoencoder that encodes high-dimensional image observations into a compact set of tokens, and a GPT-like autoregressive Transformer that models the temporal dynamics of these tokens conditioned on actions. The discrete autoencoder is trained with a combination of reconstruction, commitment, and perceptual losses to ensure high-fidelity tokenization and reconstruction of images. The Transformer is trained in a self-supervised manner to predict next-frame tokens, rewards, and episode terminations, using cross-entropy and mean-squared error losses as appropriate. Policy and value functions are learned entirely in the simulated environment generated by the world model, using actor-critic objectives and bootstrapping with a value network for long-horizon returns.
235303a8bc1e4892efd525a38ead657422d8a519.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Atari 100k benchmark, which consists of 26 Atari games with a strict limit of 100,000 environment steps (approximately two hours of gameplay per game). The proposed method will be compared against several strong baselines, including SimPLe, CURL, DrQ, and SPR, as well as search-based methods like MuZero and EfficientZero. Evaluation metrics include mean, median, and interquartile mean of human-normalized scores, optimality gap, and the number of games achieving superhuman performance. Each agent will be evaluated over multiple runs (e.g., 5 for the proposed method and SimPLe, 100 for CURL, DrQ, and SPR), and results will be reported with stratified bootstrap confidence intervals. The evaluation protocol will involve collecting average scores over 100 episodes at the end of training for each game.
235303a8bc1e4892efd525a38ead657422d8a519.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel world model architecture for reinforcement learning that leverages a discrete autoencoder and an autoregressive Transformer to enable highly sample-efficient learning in complex visual environments. Unlike prior approaches, the agent learns entirely in imagination without lookahead search, yet achieves state-of-the-art performance on the Atari 100k benchmark, including superhuman results on a substantial subset of games. The approach demonstrates that Transformers, when combined with discrete image tokenization, can serve as powerful and scalable world models for reinforcement learning, offering a new direction for efficient policy learning in high-dimensional domains.

23540cc01ce11f686cd3eb854ceff3ba4b3f2ec6.title: Quantum speedups for stochastic optimization
23540cc01ce11f686cd3eb854ceff3ba4b3f2ec6.research_question: Can quantum algorithms provide provable speedups over classical algorithms for stochastic optimization problems, specifically in minimizing Lipschitz convex functions and finding critical points of smooth non-convex functions, when given access to quantum generalizations of stochastic gradient oracles?
23540cc01ce11f686cd3eb854ceff3ba4b3f2ec6.hypothesis: Quantum algorithms that leverage quantum variance reduction and quantum mean estimation techniques can achieve improved query complexity for stochastic convex and non-convex optimization compared to the best-known classical methods, particularly in low-dimensional settings.
23540cc01ce11f686cd3eb854ceff3ba4b3f2ec6.proposed_method: The proposed research will develop new quantum algorithms for stochastic optimization by utilizing quantum stochastic gradient oracles (QSGOs) and quantum variance reduction techniques. The approach will build upon quantum multivariate mean estimation and multilevel Monte Carlo (MLMC) methods to construct unbiased, low-variance estimators of gradients in the quantum setting. Two main algorithms will be designed for minimizing Lipschitz convex functions: a quantum accelerated stochastic approximation (Q-AC-SA) method and a quantum stochastic cutting plane (Q-SCP) method, each targeting different dimension-accuracy trade-offs. For non-convex optimization, the research will extend these quantum variance reduction techniques to develop quantum analogs of state-of-the-art classical algorithms (such as SPIDER and SGD) for finding critical points, ensuring improved dependence on the target accuracy parameter. The methodology will also establish quantum lower bounds to characterize the optimality of the proposed algorithms.
23540cc01ce11f686cd3eb854ceff3ba4b3f2ec6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by implementing the proposed quantum algorithms and evaluating their query complexity on benchmark stochastic optimization problems. The evaluation will focus on two main settings: (1) minimizing Lipschitz convex functions and (2) finding critical points of smooth non-convex functions, both under quantum oracle access. The performance of the quantum algorithms will be compared against optimal classical baselines such as stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and SPIDER, using metrics such as the number of queries required to reach a specified accuracy (epsilon-optimality or epsilon-criticality). The experimental setup will consider varying problem dimensions and accuracy levels to empirically validate the theoretical dimension-accuracy trade-offs. Additionally, theoretical lower bounds will be established and compared to the achieved rates to demonstrate optimality in certain regimes.
23540cc01ce11f686cd3eb854ceff3ba4b3f2ec6.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a general quantum variance reduction technique that enables unbiased and low-variance estimation of gradients using quantum oracles, which is of independent interest beyond stochastic optimization. The proposed quantum algorithms achieve dimension-dependent query complexities that are provably unattainable by classical algorithms, offering quadratic speedups in low-dimensional settings. The research also establishes new quantum lower bounds, demonstrating the asymptotic optimality of one of the algorithms for low-dimensional convex optimization. Furthermore, the approach extends quantum speedups to non-convex optimization, improving upon the best-known classical rates for critical point computation.

236be8f587472dbdc7ff6a2ce7f11893bc558641.title: Lossy Image Compression with Quantized Hierarchical VAEs
236be8f587472dbdc7ff6a2ce7f11893bc558641.research_question: How can hierarchical variational autoencoders be adapted to enable practical, efficient, and high-performance lossy image compression, while bridging the gap between generative modeling and compression frameworks?
236be8f587472dbdc7ff6a2ce7f11893bc558641.hypothesis: A quantization-aware hierarchical VAE, equipped with redesigned latent variable models and efficient network architectures, will outperform existing hand-crafted and learning-based lossy image compression methods in terms of rate-distortion performance and computational efficiency.
236be8f587472dbdc7ff6a2ce7f11893bc558641.proposed_method: A novel lossy image compression framework will be developed based on hierarchical variational autoencoders (VAEs), specifically leveraging a ResNet-based architecture with multiple latent blocks. The latent variable model will be redesigned to use a quantization-aware posterior (uniform distribution) and a prior modeled as a Gaussian convolved with a uniform distribution, enabling straightforward quantization and entropy coding at test time. The network will consist of a bottom-up path for feature extraction and a top-down path for reconstruction, with each latent block adding information in a coarse-to-fine manner. The method will employ patch embedding for downsampling, sub-pixel convolutions for upsampling, and ConvNeXt blocks for residual connections, supporting parallel encoding and decoding for fast execution on GPUs. The training objective will minimize a rate-distortion loss, balancing the bit rate and reconstruction error via a tunable parameter, and separate models will be trained for different bit rates.
236be8f587472dbdc7ff6a2ce7f11893bc558641.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several standard datasets, including COCO (train2017, 256x256 patches), Kodak (24 images, 768x512), CLIC 2022 test set (30 high-resolution images), and CelebA (64x64). The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art learned image compression baselines such as VVC intra (VTM 12.1), Minnen et al. (2018, 2020), Cheng et al. (2020), and others, using open-source implementations where available. Evaluation metrics will include bits per pixel (bpp), peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), and BD-rate (average bitrate savings over VVC intra). Computational complexity will be assessed via parameter count, FLOPs, and encoding/decoding latency on both CPU and GPU. Ablation studies will examine the impact of architectural choices such as the number of latent blocks and residual block types.
236be8f587472dbdc7ff6a2ce7f11893bc558641.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a quantization-aware probabilistic model for hierarchical VAEs, enabling practical and efficient entropy coding for lossy image compression. The method supports parallel encoding and decoding, resulting in significantly faster execution compared to autoregressive models, and achieves state-of-the-art rate-distortion performance on natural image datasets. Additionally, the framework narrows the gap between image compression and generative modeling, providing a unified perspective and new insights for the design of future image compression systems.

23a921483746b8b3c828bd601f54d485bec32014.title: Mechanistic Unlearning: Robust Knowledge Unlearning and Editing via Mechanistic Localization
23a921483746b8b3c828bd601f54d485bec32014.research_question: How can knowledge editing and unlearning in large language models be made more robust and precise, particularly to prevent the recovery of unwanted knowledge and minimize unintended side effects, while preserving general language modeling capabilities?
23a921483746b8b3c828bd601f54d485bec32014.hypothesis: Localizing edits and unlearning to model components associated with mechanistically interpretable fact lookup mechanisms, rather than output-tracing or non-localized approaches, will yield more robust, precise, and parameter-efficient knowledge removal or modification, with greater resistance to adversarial relearning and reduced side effects on unrelated model capabilities.
23a921483746b8b3c828bd601f54d485bec32014.proposed_method: A novel framework for knowledge editing and unlearning will be developed that leverages mechanistic interpretability to identify and localize model components—specifically MLP layers—responsible for factual recall via the fact lookup (FLU) mechanism. The approach will involve training probes to map internal activations to factual associations, using techniques such as logistic regression to pinpoint layers where latent representations encode target knowledge. Editing or unlearning will be performed by fine-tuning only the weights of these localized components, using a composite loss function that encourages the model to forget or replace specific facts while retaining general language modeling ability. The method will be compared to output-tracing (OT) localization techniques (e.g., Causal Tracing, Attribution Patching) and various baselines, including random and non-localized parameter updates. Additional analyses will include probing internal representations post-editing and employing weight masking to control for parameter count and assess the specificity of edits.
23a921483746b8b3c828bd601f54d485bec32014.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large language models such as Gemma-7B, Gemma-2-9B, and Llama-3-8b. Two main datasets will be used: the Sports Facts dataset (subject-sport relations for 1567 athletes) and the CounterFact dataset (factual associations with ground-truth and alternative answers). Editing and unlearning tasks will include Sports-Athlete-Editing, Full-Sports-Editing, Sports-Unlearning, CounterFact-Editing, and Sequential-CounterFact-Editing, with varying forget set sizes. Evaluation will involve prompt-based accuracy (including multiple-choice and paraphrase formats), adversarial relearning (using LoRA retraining on half of the forget set), and probing of latent knowledge via linear classifiers. Baselines will include output-tracing localizations, random and all-MLP localizations, and non-localized editing. General language modeling side effects will be measured using MMLU accuracy. Parameter efficiency and the specificity of edits will be assessed via weight masking and analysis of the affected mechanisms.
23a921483746b8b3c828bd601f54d485bec32014.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a mechanistic unlearning framework that targets fact lookup mechanisms for localized editing and unlearning, rather than relying on output-tracing or non-localized approaches. This approach is claimed to yield more robust and precise knowledge removal, greater resistance to adversarial relearning, and fewer unintended side effects. The method also provides a principled way to identify and edit the internal representations responsible for factual recall, and demonstrates parameter efficiency by minimizing the number of weights that need to be updated. Comprehensive evaluations across multiple models, datasets, and robustness scenarios support the claim that mechanistic localization is superior to existing baselines.

23c2e21b6a5789724715f2986fdc586a517ffe57.title: Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention
23c2e21b6a5789724715f2986fdc586a517ffe57.research_question: How can a sparse attention mechanism be designed to efficiently support long-context modeling in large language models, while aligning with modern hardware constraints and enabling end-to-end trainability without sacrificing model performance?
23c2e21b6a5789724715f2986fdc586a517ffe57.hypothesis: A natively trainable, hardware-aligned sparse attention mechanism that integrates hierarchical token modeling—combining coarse-grained compression, fine-grained selection, and local sliding windows—will achieve substantial computational efficiency gains for long-context language modeling, while maintaining or improving model performance compared to full attention and existing sparse attention baselines.
23c2e21b6a5789724715f2986fdc586a517ffe57.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a Native Sparse Attention (NSA) mechanism that replaces the standard full attention with a hierarchical, dynamically constructed sparse attention framework. NSA processes input sequences through three parallel branches: (1) compressed coarse-grained tokens generated by aggregating sequential blocks via a learnable MLP, (2) blockwise-selected fine-grained tokens identified using importance scores derived from intermediate attention computations, and (3) a sliding window branch that preserves local context. Each branch computes attention outputs independently, which are then combined using a learned gating mechanism. The architecture is specifically optimized for hardware efficiency by aligning memory access and computation patterns with modern GPU architectures (e.g., GQA/MQA), and custom Triton kernels are developed to maximize arithmetic intensity and minimize memory bottlenecks. The design ensures that all components are differentiable and trainable end-to-end, supporting both efficient training and inference.
23c2e21b6a5789724715f2986fdc586a517ffe57.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a 27B-parameter transformer backbone with Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE), trained on 270B tokens of 8k-length texts, followed by continued training and supervised fine-tuning on 32k-length texts. NSA will be compared against a full attention baseline and state-of-the-art sparse attention methods such as H2O, infLLM, Quest, and Exact-Top. Evaluation will cover general language benchmarks (e.g., MMLU, CMMLU, BBH, GSM8K, MATH, DROP, MBPP, HumanEval), long-context tasks, and chain-of-thought reasoning. Performance metrics will include accuracy on these benchmarks, training convergence, and computational speedup ratios (decode, forward, backward) on 64k-length sequences, with kernel-level speed measured on A100 GPUs using optimized Triton implementations.
23c2e21b6a5789724715f2986fdc586a517ffe57.novelty_claims: The proposed NSA framework is novel in its integration of hierarchical sparse attention with hardware-aligned design, enabling both substantial practical speedups and native end-to-end trainability. Unlike prior sparse attention methods that focus on inference-only sparsity or post-hoc pruning, NSA achieves efficient computation across all stages (training, prefilling, decoding) and is compatible with advanced attention architectures (GQA/MQA). The blockwise selection and compression strategies are specifically engineered for optimal GPU utilization, and the entire mechanism is differentiable, overcoming the limitations of non-trainable or inefficient prior approaches. NSA is claimed to deliver superior or comparable model performance to full attention while significantly reducing computational costs for long-context processing.

23e261a20a315059b4de5492ed071c97a20c12e7.title: Imagic: Text-Based Real Image Editing with Diffusion Models
23e261a20a315059b4de5492ed071c97a20c12e7.research_question: How can complex semantic edits, including non-rigid changes and multi-object manipulations, be performed on a single real image using only a natural language text prompt, while preserving image fidelity and structure?
23e261a20a315059b4de5492ed071c97a20c12e7.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model, combined with optimized text embeddings and model fine-tuning, enables high-fidelity, text-driven semantic editing of single real images, including complex non-rigid transformations, without requiring auxiliary inputs.
23e261a20a315059b4de5492ed071c97a20c12e7.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a three-stage framework for text-based editing of real images using diffusion models. First, the target text prompt is encoded and its embedding is optimized to reconstruct the input image, aligning the embedding with the image's content. Second, the pre-trained generative diffusion model is fine-tuned on the input image, conditioned on the optimized embedding, to improve fidelity and capture image-specific appearance. Third, a linear interpolation is performed between the optimized embedding and the target text embedding, producing a latent representation that balances image fidelity and semantic alignment with the desired edit. This interpolated embedding is then used to generate the edited image via the fine-tuned diffusion process, with auxiliary super-resolution models applied as needed for high-resolution outputs.
23e261a20a315059b4de5492ed071c97a20c12e7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of real images collected from sources such as Unsplash and Pixabay, covering multiple domains and editing categories (e.g., style, appearance, color, posture, and composition). The method will be evaluated using both Imagen and Stable Diffusion as the underlying generative models. Baseline comparisons will include leading single-image text-based editing methods such as SDEdit, DDIB, and Text2LIVE, using consistent diffusion hyperparameters and best practices for each. Evaluation metrics will include CLIP score for text alignment, LPIPS for image fidelity, and extensive human perceptual studies (2AFC) on the newly introduced TEdBench benchmark, which consists of 100 image-text pairs targeting complex non-rigid edits.
23e261a20a315059b4de5492ed071c97a20c12e7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable complex, non-rigid, text-driven semantic edits on a single real image without requiring auxiliary inputs such as masks or multiple views. It introduces a novel combination of text embedding optimization, model fine-tuning, and semantic interpolation in the embedding space, resulting in high-fidelity edits that preserve the original image's structure and composition. Additionally, a new benchmark (TEdBench) is introduced for evaluating non-rigid text-based image editing, and the method demonstrates strong compositional capabilities and smooth semantic interpolation between image and text representations.

23f33654b05927b0b09e7b020a7cedc50508a4f4.title: Reasoning Models Hallucinate More: Factuality-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Large Reasoning Models
23f33654b05927b0b09e7b020a7cedc50508a4f4.research_question: How can the prevalence of hallucinations in large language models optimized for reasoning tasks via reinforcement learning be reduced, while maintaining or improving reasoning accuracy?
23f33654b05927b0b09e7b020a7cedc50508a4f4.hypothesis: Incorporating explicit step-wise factuality verification and reward shaping into the reinforcement learning fine-tuning process will reduce hallucinations in large reasoning models without compromising, and potentially improving, their reasoning performance.
23f33654b05927b0b09e7b020a7cedc50508a4f4.proposed_method: A novel reinforcement learning fine-tuning algorithm, Factuality-aware Step-wise Policy Optimization (FSPO), will be developed to address hallucinations in large reasoning models. FSPO integrates explicit factuality verification at each reasoning step by employing an automated verifier to determine whether each generated reasoning sentence is entailed by provided evidence. Step-wise factuality rewards are assigned as +1 (entailed), 0 (neutral), or -1 (contradicted) for each reasoning step, and are combined with traditional answer correctness rewards to form a denser, more informative reward signal. The Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) framework is adopted for policy optimization, with factuality-aware advantage adjustment re-weighting token-level advantages based on the factuality of their corresponding reasoning steps. This approach ensures that factually correct reasoning tokens are encouraged, while incorrect ones are penalized, providing non-zero gradients even when the overall answer is incorrect and enabling the model to escape spurious local optima.
23f33654b05927b0b09e7b020a7cedc50508a4f4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using Qwen2.5-7B-Base/Instruct and Llama3.1-8B-Instruct as backbone models. Training will utilize a mixture of complex reasoning datasets, including subsets of HotpotQA and 2WikiMultiHopQA (2K examples), as well as the SimpleRL dataset (8K mathematical problems). Hallucination reduction will be evaluated on TruthfulQA, HaluEval, and HalluQA benchmarks, using metrics such as the ratio of truthful outputs and accuracy in discriminating hallucinated answers. Reasoning performance will be measured on GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME2024, and AIME2025 using Pass@1 accuracy. Baselines will include API-based models (DeepSeek-V3, DeepSeek-R1, GPT-4o, GPT-o1), reasoning models (QwQ-32B, Distill-Qwen, Distill-Llama), and open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B-Base/Instruct, Llama3.1-8B-Instruct). Implementation will use the verl framework, with detailed hyperparameters specified (e.g., batch size, rollout count, learning rate, KL loss coefficient, clip ratio). Ablation studies and analyses of sample size, RL algorithm variants, and factuality improvement will be performed.
23f33654b05927b0b09e7b020a7cedc50508a4f4.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a factuality-aware, step-wise reinforcement learning algorithm that integrates explicit factuality verification into the policy optimization process for large reasoning models. By combining step-wise factuality rewards with answer correctness rewards and re-weighting token-level advantages, the approach provides denser and more informative feedback, directly addressing the high-variance gradient, entropy-induced randomness, and spurious local optima that lead to hallucinations in standard RL fine-tuning. This method is claimed to be among the first to systematically analyze and mitigate hallucinations in RL-trained reasoning models through step-wise factuality feedback, achieving substantial improvements in both hallucination reduction and reasoning accuracy across multiple benchmarks.

23f4c8d980d8288131f80cbdb4173f05a21e8724.title: RePrompt: Automatic Prompt Editing to Refine AI-Generative Art Towards Precise Expressions
23f4c8d980d8288131f80cbdb4173f05a21e8724.research_question: How can the emotional expressiveness of AI-generated images be improved through automatic refinement of text prompts, and how effective are such methods compared to manual or naïve approaches?
23f4c8d980d8288131f80cbdb4173f05a21e8724.hypothesis: Automatic, explainable prompt editing based on interpretable text features will significantly improve the emotional expressiveness of AI-generated images, particularly for complex or negative emotions, compared to original, manually edited, or label-appended prompts.
23f4c8d980d8288131f80cbdb4173f05a21e8724.proposed_method: A novel automatic prompt editing pipeline, RePrompt, is developed to refine text prompts for text-to-image generative models to enhance emotional expressiveness in generated images. The method begins with feature curation, extracting interpretable word-level features such as the number and concreteness of nouns, adjectives, and verbs from prompts. A proxy machine learning model (e.g., LightGBM) is trained to predict image-emotion alignment (IEA) scores, using a large dataset of emotional texts and generated images. Explainable AI techniques (SHAP and partial dependence plots) are applied to analyze feature importance and identify optimal value ranges for key features. Based on these insights, a rubric is curated to algorithmically revise prompts by adding or removing words to optimize salient features, ensuring edits are human-readable and contextually consistent. The refined prompts are then used to generate images with improved emotional alignment.
23f4c8d980d8288131f80cbdb4173f05a21e8724.experiment_details: Experiments include a simulation study and a user evaluation. The simulation study uses 10,000 emotional texts from the Empathetic Dialogues dataset, generating images with VQGAN-CLIP and assessing alignment using CLIPScore for both image-emotion (IEA) and image-text (ITA) metrics. The user study involves 197 participants evaluating images generated from four prompt conditions: original, manually edited, label-appended, and RePrompt-edited, using DALL·E2 as the generative model. Evaluation metrics include both objective CLIPScore measures and external validator ratings for emotional and textual alignment. Statistical analysis is performed using linear mixed-effects regression and ANOVA to compare the effectiveness of each prompt editing method.
23f4c8d980d8288131f80cbdb4173f05a21e8724.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces an interpretable, explainable, and automatic prompt editing pipeline for refining text prompts to optimize emotional expressiveness in AI-generated art. Unlike prior heuristic or black-box prompt engineering methods, this method leverages data-driven feature analysis and explainable AI to derive actionable, human-readable editing rules. The approach is validated on both open-source and state-of-the-art generative models, demonstrating significant improvements in emotional alignment, especially for negative emotions, and providing a generalizable framework for prompt refinement in creative AI applications.

240103933ffe3dac2179cc160a2bd91299357a53.title: Retentive Network: A Successor to Transformer for Large Language Models
240103933ffe3dac2179cc160a2bd91299357a53.research_question: How can a new neural network architecture be designed to simultaneously achieve efficient training parallelism, low inference cost, and strong performance for large language models, overcoming the limitations of existing Transformer-based and recurrent models?
240103933ffe3dac2179cc160a2bd91299357a53.hypothesis: A novel retention-based sequence modeling mechanism, which unifies parallel, recurrent, and chunkwise recurrent computation paradigms, will enable large language models to achieve efficient training, low-cost and scalable inference, and competitive or superior performance compared to Transformer architectures.
240103933ffe3dac2179cc160a2bd91299357a53.proposed_method: A new architecture, termed Retentive Network (RetNet), will be developed to replace the standard multi-head attention mechanism in Transformers with a multi-scale retention (MSR) module. This retention mechanism is mathematically derived to connect recurrence and attention, supporting three computation paradigms: (1) parallel representation for efficient training via GPU parallelism, (2) recurrent representation for O(1) memory and computation cost during inference, and (3) chunkwise recurrent representation for efficient long-sequence modeling with linear complexity. The MSR module will employ multiple retention heads, each with distinct decay rates (gamma), and incorporate group normalization and a swish gating function to enhance non-linearity and training stability. The overall architecture will alternate MSR and feed-forward modules, with careful parameter allocation to ensure fair comparison with Transformers. Training will utilize parallel and chunkwise recurrent modes, while inference will leverage the recurrent mode for maximum efficiency.
240103933ffe3dac2179cc160a2bd91299357a53.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale language modeling tasks using models of various sizes (1.3B, 2.7B, 6.7B parameters), trained from scratch on a composite corpus including The Pile, C4, and The Stack. Training will be performed with up to 100B tokens, using large batch sizes and sequence lengths up to 8k. Baselines will include standard Transformer, Transformer with FlashAttention, and efficient Transformer variants such as Linear Transformer, RWKV, H3, and Hyena. Evaluation metrics will include language modeling perplexity (in-domain and out-of-domain), zero-shot and few-shot accuracy on downstream tasks (e.g., HellaSwag, BoolQ, COPA, PIQA, Winograd, Winogrande, StoryCloze), as well as detailed measurements of training/inference memory consumption, throughput, and latency. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of architectural components such as swish gating, group normalization, multi-scale decay, and head dimension.
240103933ffe3dac2179cc160a2bd91299357a53.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a retention mechanism that unifies the benefits of parallel and recurrent computation, achieving the so-called 'impossible triangle' of training parallelism, low inference cost, and strong performance. Unlike previous approaches, the method supports O(1) inference complexity, linear memory scaling for long sequences, and efficient chunkwise training, all within a single architecture. The retention mechanism is mathematically derived to generalize and improve upon both attention and recurrence, and the use of multi-scale decay, group normalization, and swish gating further enhances stability and expressiveness. Experimental results are expected to demonstrate that the proposed architecture outperforms both standard Transformers and recent efficient variants in terms of perplexity, downstream task accuracy, and resource efficiency.

240300b1da360f22bf0b82c6817eacebba6deed4.title: What Makes Convolutional Models Great on Long Sequence Modeling?
240300b1da360f22bf0b82c6817eacebba6deed4.research_question: What are the minimal and essential design principles that enable convolutional models to effectively capture long-range dependencies in sequence modeling tasks, and can a simpler, more efficient global convolutional model be developed based on these principles to outperform existing state-of-the-art methods across diverse domains?
240300b1da360f22bf0b82c6817eacebba6deed4.hypothesis: A global convolutional model that employs efficient parameterization (with parameter count scaling sub-linearly with sequence length) and incorporates a decaying kernel structure (assigning greater weights to closer neighbors) will achieve superior or comparable performance to current state-of-the-art models on long sequence modeling tasks, while being simpler and more computationally efficient.
240300b1da360f22bf0b82c6817eacebba6deed4.proposed_method: A novel global convolutional architecture, Structured Global Convolution (SGConv), will be developed based on two key principles: (1) efficient parameterization of the convolution kernel such that the number of parameters grows logarithmically with input sequence length, and (2) a decaying structure in the kernel, where weights decrease with distance from the center, prioritizing local information. The convolution kernel will be constructed as a weighted combination of multiple upsampled sub-kernels, each parameterized by a fixed-size vector and upsampled to increasing scales. The decaying property will be enforced by applying a decay coefficient (e.g., α=1/2) to the weights of each scale. Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) will be utilized to efficiently compute the global convolution in O(L log L) time, and normalization will ensure stable training. The design will allow easy integration into existing architectures and support both depth-wise and channel-wise convolutions.
240300b1da360f22bf0b82c6817eacebba6deed4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Long Range Arena (LRA) benchmark, which includes tasks spanning text, images, and synthetic data with sequence lengths up to 16K tokens, as well as the Speech Commands dataset for both 10-class and 35-class spoken word classification. Baseline comparisons will include standard Transformers, efficient Transformer variants (e.g., Linformer, BigBird, Reformer), S4, and other state-space models. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy, perplexity (for language modeling), inference speed, and GPU memory usage. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of the decay speed and kernel dimension. Further, SGConv will be integrated into language models (e.g., Transformer-XL, BERT) and vision models (e.g., ConvNeXt), with performance evaluated on WikiText-103 and ImageNet, respectively, to demonstrate generalizability and efficiency gains.
240300b1da360f22bf0b82c6817eacebba6deed4.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple yet effective global convolutional model that captures long-range dependencies using a logarithmic parameterization and an explicit decaying kernel structure. SGConv achieves state-of-the-art or competitive results on long sequence modeling benchmarks with significantly reduced computational complexity and improved speed compared to prior models such as S4. The approach offers a more intuitive, easily implemented alternative to complex state-space models, and demonstrates versatility as a drop-in module for both language and vision tasks, outperforming or matching specialized architectures while improving efficiency.

241083edff572026db88a922733571515be7d361.title: Function Classes for Identifiable Nonlinear Independent Component Analysis
241083edff572026db88a922733571515be7d361.research_question: Under what conditions can nonlinear Independent Component Analysis (ICA) be made identifiable by restricting the class of mixing functions, and which specific function classes enable identifiability or local identifiability of the underlying sources in unsupervised latent variable models?
241083edff572026db88a922733571515be7d361.hypothesis: Constraining the class of mixing functions in nonlinear ICA to conformal maps or orthogonal coordinate transformations (OCTs) enables identifiability or local identifiability of the latent sources, whereas more general nonlinear or volume-preserving transformations do not guarantee such identifiability.
241083edff572026db88a922733571515be7d361.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the identifiability of nonlinear ICA under different function classes of mixing functions. The approach will focus on characterizing the properties of conformal maps, orthogonal coordinate transformations (OCTs), and volume-preserving maps, using tools from differential geometry, rigidity theory, and partial differential equations. Identifiability will be formally defined in terms of the ability to recover the true sources up to certain symmetry groups, and new notions such as local identifiability under smooth invariant deformations will be introduced. Theoretical proofs will be constructed to establish identifiability results for conformal maps in dimensions d ≥ 2, local identifiability for OCTs, and the existence of spurious solutions for volume-preserving and general nonlinear maps.
241083edff572026db88a922733571515be7d361.experiment_details: The research will primarily involve mathematical analysis and theoretical proofs rather than empirical experiments. However, illustrative constructions and counterexamples will be provided, such as explicit constructions of spurious solutions for volume-preserving and general nonlinear maps, and demonstrations of local rigidity for OCTs. Where relevant, the framework will assume the existence of latent source distributions (e.g., uniform or with smooth densities) and will analyze the effect of different symmetries and boundary conditions. Theoretical results will be compared to known results in linear ICA and prior work on identifiability in related function classes.
241083edff572026db88a922733571515be7d361.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces new identifiability results for nonlinear ICA with conformal maps in dimensions d ≥ 2, extending previous results and removing restrictive assumptions. It defines and proves a new notion of local identifiability for orthogonal coordinate transformations, showing that smooth deformations cannot generate spurious solutions within this class. The approach leverages connections to rigidity theory and global properties of partial differential equations, providing novel theoretical tools for the ICA field. Additionally, the work clarifies the limitations of volume-preserving and general nonlinear maps for identifiability, offering new counterexamples and insights into the structure of spurious solutions.

241eefc1bb11e693e0fef6977a65a0a822fb8f5e.title: LoRA+: Efficient Low Rank Adaptation of Large Models
241eefc1bb11e693e0fef6977a65a0a822fb8f5e.research_question: How can the efficiency and effectiveness of low-rank adaptation methods for fine-tuning large pretrained neural networks be improved, particularly with respect to learning rate strategies for adapter matrices?
241eefc1bb11e693e0fef6977a65a0a822fb8f5e.hypothesis: Decoupling and appropriately scaling the learning rates for the two adapter matrices in low-rank adaptation modules will improve both the performance and training efficiency of large model fine-tuning, compared to using a single shared learning rate.
241eefc1bb11e693e0fef6977a65a0a822fb8f5e.proposed_method: A new method, LoRA+, is proposed for efficient fine-tuning of large pretrained neural networks using low-rank adaptation. The approach introduces separate learning rates for the two adapter matrices (A and B) in LoRA modules, rather than using a single shared learning rate. Theoretical analysis in the infinite-width regime is conducted to derive principled scaling rules, showing that efficient feature learning is achieved when the learning rate for B is much larger than that for A (specifically, η_B = λ × η_A, with λ ≫ 1). The method is model-agnostic and applies to general neural architectures, with guidelines provided for initialization and learning rate selection. Empirical guidelines for setting the ratio λ are also developed, and the method is designed to be computationally as efficient as standard LoRA.
241eefc1bb11e693e0fef6977a65a0a822fb8f5e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several large language models, including RoBERTa-base, GPT-2, and Llama-7b, across multiple NLP benchmarks such as GLUE (MNLI, QQP, SST2, QNLI) and the Flan-v2 instruction tuning dataset. For each model and task, a grid search over pairs of learning rates (η_A, η_B) will be performed to identify optimal configurations, comparing LoRA+ (decoupled learning rates) to standard LoRA (shared learning rate). Evaluation metrics include test accuracy and training speed (epochs to convergence), with experiments run using both FP16 and full precision. Additional analysis will examine the sensitivity of the optimal learning rate ratio to model architecture, task difficulty, and initialization scheme. Results will be averaged over multiple random seeds, and stability of training will be assessed.
241eefc1bb11e693e0fef6977a65a0a822fb8f5e.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled, theoretically justified approach for setting distinct learning rates for the two adapter matrices in low-rank adaptation modules, addressing a previously unstudied source of suboptimality in standard LoRA. The method provides scaling rules derived from infinite-width analysis, validated by extensive empirical results across multiple models and tasks. LoRA+ is claimed to improve both fine-tuning performance (by 1-2% in accuracy) and training speed (up to 2x faster convergence) at no additional computational cost, and offers practical guidelines for hyperparameter selection. The approach is general, model-agnostic, and compatible with existing resource-efficient fine-tuning pipelines.

243dce356173444cbdd6d3fbebb05f04429edbe6.title: Preference Optimization by Estimating the Ratio of the Data Distribution
243dce356173444cbdd6d3fbebb05f04429edbe6.research_question: How can preference optimization for aligning large language models with human feedback be generalized to achieve both theoretical optimality and practical simplicity, without relying on reward models or partition functions, and can this generalization improve both generation fidelity and diversity compared to existing methods?
243dce356173444cbdd6d3fbebb05f04429edbe6.hypothesis: A generalized preference optimization framework based on Bregman divergence and likelihood ratio estimation will enable policy models to match target policies without auxiliary reward models or partition functions, maintaining theoretical guarantees and simplicity, and will improve both generation fidelity and diversity over current direct preference optimization and its probabilistic extensions.
243dce356173444cbdd6d3fbebb05f04429edbe6.proposed_method: A novel framework, Bregman Preference Optimization (BPO), is proposed that formulates preference optimization as a ratio matching problem between the data preference ratio and the model ratio. The method leverages Bregman divergence to define a family of objective functions, allowing the policy model to match the target policy distribution solely through likelihood ratio estimation, without the need for learned reward models or partition functions. The BPO framework subsumes direct preference optimization (DPO) as a special case and provides tractable, closed-form objectives for all instances, enabling straightforward implementation. Additionally, a gradient scaling method, Scaled Basu’s Power Divergence (SBA), is introduced to control the optimization dynamics and sample prioritization within the BPO framework, enhancing training stability and performance. The framework is designed to be orthogonally applicable to existing DPO variants that can be expressed as logistic regression, further extending its flexibility.
243dce356173444cbdd6d3fbebb05f04429edbe6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on single-turn dialogue generation using the Anthropic Helpful and Harmless (HH) dataset and summarization using the Reddit TL;DR dataset. Pre-trained models such as Pythia-2.8B and GPT-J will be used, with supervised fine-tuning on preferred subsets of the datasets. The proposed BPO and its instances (including SBA) will be compared against baselines such as DPO, f-DPO, and f-PO, with careful control of training hyperparameters for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics will include win rate (as judged by GPT-4), predictive entropy, self-BLEU, and distinct-1 to measure both generation fidelity and diversity. Further large-scale experiments will be performed using Mistral-7B-Base, Llama-3-8B-Base, and Llama-3-8B-Instruct on the UltraFeedback dataset, with performance evaluated on external benchmarks such as AlpacaEval2 and Arena-Hard, using length-controlled and raw win rates.
243dce356173444cbdd6d3fbebb05f04429edbe6.novelty_claims: The proposed BPO framework uniquely retains both theoretical optimality and practical simplicity among probabilistic preference optimization extensions, enabling flexible choices of optimization objectives via Bregman divergence. It eliminates the need for auxiliary reward models and partition function estimation, distinguishing it from prior methods such as f-PO and f-DPO. The introduction of the SBA gradient scaling method further enhances optimization dynamics and sample prioritization. BPO is orthogonally applicable to existing DPO variants, allowing for broader generalization and improved performance. Empirical results demonstrate consistent improvements in both win rate and diversity, achieving state-of-the-art performance among preference-optimized models on several benchmarks.

244054a4254a2147e43a3dad9c124b9b7eb4a04a.title: Flow Straight and Fast: Learning to Generate and Transfer Data with Rectified Flow
244054a4254a2147e43a3dad9c124b9b7eb4a04a.research_question: How can data-driven transport maps between two empirical distributions be learned in a unified, efficient, and scalable manner to address generative modeling and domain transfer tasks?
244054a4254a2147e43a3dad9c124b9b7eb4a04a.hypothesis: Learning an ordinary differential equation (ODE) model that follows straight-line paths between samples from two distributions will yield efficient, scalable, and high-quality generative and transfer models, reducing transport costs and improving computational efficiency compared to existing methods.
244054a4254a2147e43a3dad9c124b9b7eb4a04a.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a rectified flow framework, where an ODE model is trained to transport samples from a source distribution π0 to a target distribution π1 by following straight-line paths as closely as possible. The drift function of the ODE is parameterized by a neural network and optimized via a nonlinear least squares objective, minimizing the difference between the network's predicted velocity and the direction of the straight line connecting sample pairs. The method is time-symmetric and can be recursively applied (reflow) to further straighten the flow paths, making them increasingly linear and thus easier to simulate. The approach includes optional distillation, where the learned flow is approximated by a direct neural mapping for extremely fast inference. The method is purely ODE-based, avoiding the complexities of SDEs, adversarial training, or intractable likelihoods.
244054a4254a2147e43a3dad9c124b9b7eb4a04a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image generation and domain transfer tasks, including datasets such as CIFAR-10 and image-to-image translation benchmarks (e.g., human and cat faces). The method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines including GANs, VAEs, denoising diffusion models, and optimal transport-based approaches. Evaluation metrics will include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), recall, and transport cost measures. The experimental setup will assess both the quality of generated samples and the computational efficiency (e.g., number of Euler steps required for inference), with ablation studies on the number of reflow steps, discretization granularity, and distillation effectiveness.
244054a4254a2147e43a3dad9c124b9b7eb4a04a.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified ODE-based framework for both generative modeling and domain transfer that learns flows following nearly straight paths, enabling fast and accurate simulation with minimal discretization steps. The rectified flow approach guarantees non-increasing convex transport costs for any input coupling and provides a theoretically grounded method for straightening flow paths through recursive application. The method avoids adversarial or variational inference, requires no additional parameters or complex hyperparameter tuning, and achieves state-of-the-art results in fast generative modeling and transfer tasks. The approach also provides a new perspective on the connection between ODE-based generative models and optimal transport.

248779b1c52abb7a10023a87e29e44bccc2fb5fd.title: MissDiff: Training Diffusion Models on Tabular Data with Missing Values
248779b1c52abb7a10023a87e29e44bccc2fb5fd.research_question: How can generative diffusion models be trained directly on tabular data containing missing values, under various missing data mechanisms, to accurately model the underlying data distribution and generate high-quality synthetic data?
248779b1c52abb7a10023a87e29e44bccc2fb5fd.hypothesis: Training diffusion models by directly incorporating missing values into the learning objective, rather than relying on imputation-based preprocessing, will yield more accurate generative models and higher-quality synthetic tabular data, even under diverse missing data mechanisms.
248779b1c52abb7a10023a87e29e44bccc2fb5fd.proposed_method: A novel diffusion-based generative modeling framework, MissDiff, is proposed for learning from tabular data with missing values. Instead of imputing missing values prior to model training, the method modifies the Denoising Score Matching (DSM) objective by masking the regression loss according to the observed data mask. This approach directly incorporates the uncertainty of missing entries into the score estimation process. For mixed-type tabular data (containing both continuous and categorical variables), missing values are represented as zeros for continuous variables and as a new category for discrete variables, with one-hot encoding applied as appropriate. The forward diffusion process uses a Variance Preserving (VP) stochastic differential equation, and the model is trained to estimate the score function only on observed (non-missing) entries, using a masked loss. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that this masked DSM objective consistently recovers the true score function and provides an upper bound on the negative log-likelihood under mild assumptions on the missing data mechanism.
248779b1c52abb7a10023a87e29e44bccc2fb5fd.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both simulated and real-world tabular datasets, including a Bayesian Network synthetic dataset, the Census dataset, and the large-scale MIMIC4ED electronic health records dataset. Various missing data mechanisms are evaluated: Missing Completely At Random (MCAR) with row, column, and independent missing patterns; Missing At Random (MAR); and Not Missing At Random (NMAR). Baseline methods include training diffusion models after deleting incomplete rows (Diff-delete), mean imputation (Diff-mean), and the state-of-the-art tabular diffusion model STaSy with corresponding data completion strategies. Evaluation metrics include fidelity (using SDMetrics, a model-agnostic library, with scores ranging from 0 to 100%) and utility (downstream classification or regression accuracy using models such as XGBoost, Decision Tree, and MLP, with accuracy, AUROC, F1, RMSE, and R2 as metrics). All experiments are repeated three times, and standard preprocessing for tabular data is applied.
248779b1c52abb7a10023a87e29e44bccc2fb5fd.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to enable direct training of diffusion models on mixed-type tabular data with missing values, without requiring prior imputation or deletion. The method provides theoretical guarantees for consistency in score estimation and establishes an upper bound on the negative log-likelihood for incomplete data. Empirical results demonstrate substantial improvements over state-of-the-art diffusion models that rely on imputation, particularly as the proportion of missing data increases. The approach is broadly applicable across various missing data mechanisms and tabular data types.

2495700b4303512784fbdbfccc58c6c4f7771ac2.title: Language Models with Conformal Factuality Guarantees
2495700b4303512784fbdbfccc58c6c4f7771ac2.research_question: How can high-probability correctness and factuality guarantees be provided for the outputs of large language models, especially in open-ended settings, without strong assumptions or extensive human annotation?
2495700b4303512784fbdbfccc58c6c4f7771ac2.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by connecting language modeling with conformal prediction and defining uncertainty sets via entailment relations, it is possible to guarantee that language model outputs are correct with any user-specified probability, while retaining most of the useful content.
2495700b4303512784fbdbfccc58c6c4f7771ac2.proposed_method: A new framework called conformal factuality is proposed, which leverages conformal prediction to provide correctness guarantees for language model outputs. The method defines uncertainty sets for each output as the set of statements that entail the output, using entailment as the correctness criterion. A back-off algorithm is developed that decomposes LM outputs into sub-claims, scores each sub-claim for reliability (using LLM-based or heuristic scoring functions), and progressively removes the least certain sub-claims to generate a sequence of less specific outputs. The conformal prediction procedure calibrates the level of specificity needed to achieve the desired correctness probability, based on a calibration dataset and split conformal prediction. This approach is model-agnostic and can be applied to any black-box language model, requiring only a small number of human-annotated samples for calibration.
2495700b4303512784fbdbfccc58c6c4f7771ac2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three datasets: FActScore (biography factuality evaluation), NaturalQuestions (open-domain QA), and MATH (math word problems for reasoning). For each dataset, the first 50 examples will be used, with manual annotation of sub-claims for factuality. The method will be instantiated with GPT-4 as the base language model, and sub-claim extraction, merging, and scoring will also use GPT-4 via prompting. Several sub-claim scoring functions will be evaluated, including random, ordinal, LLM-based confidence, frequency (self-consistency), and an oracle based on ground-truth entailment. Baselines will include the original GPT-4 outputs and various scoring strategies. Evaluation metrics will include empirical correctness (fraction of outputs/sub-claims entailed by ground truth) at different target confidence levels, as well as retention of original output content.
2495700b4303512784fbdbfccc58c6c4f7771ac2.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a principled connection between conformal prediction and language model factuality, defining uncertainty sets via entailment rather than token or sequence enumeration. The method provides the first exact, user-controllable correctness guarantees for open-ended LM outputs, rather than only for constrained or multiple-choice settings. The back-off algorithm based on sub-claim decomposition and scoring is novel and practical, enabling guarantees with minimal annotation. The approach is model-agnostic, interpretable, and can be extended to partial correctness guarantees. Empirical results demonstrate that the method can achieve 80-90% correctness guarantees while retaining most of the original LM output, outperforming the base model's factuality.

24aa8c52b062afbfcab0faccf144397503a1873e.title: Concept-based Explainable Artificial Intelligence: A Survey
24aa8c52b062afbfcab0faccf144397503a1873e.research_question: How can explanations provided by artificial intelligence models be made more interpretable and meaningful to users by leveraging human-understandable concepts rather than raw features, and how can a unified taxonomy and guidelines for concept-based explainable AI (C-XAI) methods be established?
24aa8c52b062afbfcab0faccf144397503a1873e.hypothesis: Concept-based explanations, which utilize human-understandable abstractions, can provide more interpretable, robust, and actionable insights into AI model behavior than traditional feature-level explanations. A systematic taxonomy and set of guidelines will facilitate the development and selection of effective C-XAI methods.
24aa8c52b062afbfcab0faccf144397503a1873e.proposed_method: A comprehensive research plan will be undertaken to systematically define, categorize, and evaluate concept-based explainable AI (C-XAI) methods. The approach will begin by formalizing key terms such as 'concept' and 'concept-based explanation,' identifying four primary concept types (symbolic, unsupervised, prototype, and textual) and three explanation types (class-concept relation, node-concept association, and concept visualization). A taxonomy will be constructed based on 13 analysis dimensions, including concept training, annotation, type, explanation form, scope, data modality, task, network architecture, and evaluation strategies. Guidelines will be developed to assist practitioners in selecting suitable C-XAI methods according to their constraints and goals. The methodology will also include the creation of a conversational decision framework to guide users through method selection based on model modifiability, concept annotation availability, and desired explanation outcomes.
24aa8c52b062afbfcab0faccf144397503a1873e.experiment_details: Experiments will involve a systematic review and comparative analysis of C-XAI methods published between 2017 and July 2023 across major AI conferences and journals. Methods will be characterized by their use of datasets (e.g., images, text, graphs, videos), neural architectures (CNNs, GNNs, Transformers, etc.), and tasks (primarily classification). Evaluation strategies will include the collection and comparison of metrics such as conceptual sensitivity, faithfulness, and human interpretability, as well as the reporting of datasets and code availability. User studies and human evaluations will be incorporated where possible to assess the practical interpretability and utility of concept-based explanations. The taxonomy and guidelines will be validated through case studies and application scenarios.
24aa8c52b062afbfcab0faccf144397503a1873e.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first unified taxonomy and systematic guidelines for concept-based explainable AI, addressing the lack of standardization and field definition in C-XAI. It provides a detailed categorization of methods, a formalization of concept and explanation types, and a decision framework for method selection. The research aims to bridge the gap between technical explainability and user-understandable explanations, facilitating the development and deployment of more transparent, robust, and trustworthy AI systems.

24d52678c887331b9da0368e8a2f58bec07f7203.title: Exploring Large Language Models for Communication Games: An Empirical Study on Werewolf
24d52678c887331b9da0368e8a2f58bec07f7203.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be effectively engaged in complex communication games that require natural language understanding, reasoning, and strategic behavior, without relying on parameter tuning or human-annotated data?
24d52678c887331b9da0368e8a2f58bec07f7203.hypothesis: LLMs, when equipped with mechanisms for retrieving and reflecting on historical communication and leveraging past experiences, can autonomously develop effective strategies and exhibit emergent social behaviors in communication games, even without parameter tuning or supervised fine-tuning.
24d52678c887331b9da0368e8a2f58bec07f7203.proposed_method: A tuning-free framework is proposed in which each player in the communication game is represented by an individual LLM-based agent. The method addresses LLM context length limitations by selectively retrieving recent and informative messages, as well as generating concise reflections that summarize the agent's understanding of the current situation. An experience pool is constructed by collecting tuples of responses, reflections, and performance scores from previous game rounds. During gameplay, relevant experiences are retrieved from this pool based on semantic similarity to the current reflection, and distilled into actionable suggestions that guide the agent's reasoning and decision-making. The prompting strategy includes explicit game rules, recent and informative messages, agent reflections, extracted suggestions from experience, and a chain-of-thought prompt to elicit step-by-step reasoning.
24d52678c887331b9da0368e8a2f58bec07f7203.experiment_details: Empirical evaluation is conducted on the Werewolf game, a multi-agent communication game with hidden roles and incomplete information. Each of the seven roles in the game is controlled by an LLM agent, and the framework is implemented using the Chatarena platform with GPT-3.5-turbo as the backend. Experiments are run for 50 rounds per configuration, varying the size of the experience pool (10, 20, 30, and 40 rounds) to assess the impact of learning from experience. Baselines include agents without access to the experience pool and ablation studies removing key components (e.g., informative messages, reflection, chain-of-thought). Evaluation metrics include winning rate, average game duration, and the frequency of emergent strategic behaviors such as trust, confrontation, camouflage, and leadership. Human evaluation is also performed to assess the reasonableness of agent outputs.
24d52678c887331b9da0368e8a2f58bec07f7203.novelty_claims: The proposed framework enables LLMs to play complex communication games without any parameter tuning or human-annotated data, relying solely on prompt engineering and non-parametric learning from experience. The method introduces a novel mechanism for extracting and leveraging cross-round, multi-agent experiences in multi-party games, and demonstrates the emergence of sophisticated social behaviors such as trust, confrontation, camouflage, and leadership among LLM agents. The approach is generalizable to multi-agent, multi-role scenarios and provides new insights into the potential of LLMs for natural language-based strategic reasoning in interactive environments.

24e2af60c1b01569271669687bfdbf0f02267057.title: PCEvolve: Private Contrastive Evolution for Synthetic Dataset Generation via Few-Shot Private Data and Generative APIs
