24e2af60c1b01569271669687bfdbf0f02267057.research_question: How can high-quality differentially private synthetic image datasets be generated using few-shot private data and untrusted generative APIs, particularly in specialized domains such as healthcare and industry?
24e2af60c1b01569271669687bfdbf0f02267057.hypothesis: Incorporating inter-class contrastive relationships from few-shot private data into an adapted Exponential Mechanism will improve the utility and class-discriminability of differentially private synthetic datasets generated via generative APIs, outperforming existing API-assisted and DP-based baselines in low-data regimes.
24e2af60c1b01569271669687bfdbf0f02267057.proposed_method: A novel algorithm, Private Contrastive Evolution (PCEvolve), is proposed to generate differentially private synthetic image datasets using few-shot private data and black-box generative APIs. The method begins by initializing a synthetic dataset using a text-to-image API with a simple prompt. In each iteration, private data is aggregated into class centers to reduce bias from limited samples. A contrastive filter is applied to identify synthetic samples that are class-discriminative with respect to the aggregated private class centers. A similarity calibrator normalizes and scales similarity scores to maximize the selection probability of the most similar synthetic data. These calibrated scores are used as utility values in an adapted Exponential Mechanism, which selects prototypical synthetic samples in a privacy-preserving manner. The selected samples are then used as guidance for an image-to-image API to refine the synthetic dataset iteratively, with the process repeating for a fixed number of iterations under a total privacy budget.
24e2af60c1b01569271669687bfdbf0f02267057.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four specialized datasets from healthcare and industry domains, including COVIDx, Camelyon17, KVASIR-f, and MVTecAD-l, under few-shot (K-shot) private data settings. Multiple generative APIs (Stable Diffusion, SD+IP-Adapter, OpenJourney) will be used for image synthesis. The proposed method will be compared against six baselines: text-to-image API generation, API-based filtering, DP-noise addition, and the Private Evolution (PE) algorithm, as well as ablated variants. Evaluation will focus on downstream classification accuracy (Top-1 accuracy) using various pre-trained models (e.g., ResNet, Inception, ViT), with each experiment repeated three times and mean results reported. The impact of private data quantity, synthetic data volume, API choice, and hyperparameters will be systematically analyzed.
24e2af60c1b01569271669687bfdbf0f02267057.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new privacy-preserving synthetic data generation framework that leverages inter-class contrastive relationships from few-shot private data, overcoming the limitations of prior DP-based methods in low-data regimes. The adaptation of the Exponential Mechanism with calibrated similarity scores for synthetic data selection is novel and specifically tailored to maximize utility under strict privacy constraints. The approach enables high-quality, class-discriminative, differentially private synthetic images using untrusted generative APIs, and demonstrates superior performance over existing baselines in challenging specialized domains.

25135e5dda4cd46e38b028b9f2fef28a336735ca.title: Backdoor Defense via Adaptively Splitting Poisoned Dataset
25135e5dda4cd46e38b028b9f2fef28a336735ca.research_question: How can training-time defenses be improved to effectively identify and mitigate backdoor attacks in deep neural networks when training data may be partially poisoned and only a small amount of clean data is available?
25135e5dda4cd46e38b028b9f2fef28a336735ca.hypothesis: Adaptively splitting the poisoned dataset into dynamically updated clean and polluted data pools, using loss-guided and meta-learning-inspired strategies, enables more effective separation of clean and poisoned samples, thereby improving backdoor defense performance while maintaining high model accuracy.
25135e5dda4cd46e38b028b9f2fef28a336735ca.proposed_method: A novel training-time backdoor defense framework is proposed that adaptively splits the poisoned dataset into two pools: a clean data pool and a polluted data pool. The clean pool is initialized with a small number of clean seed samples, while the polluted pool contains the remaining (potentially poisoned) data. The method proceeds in three stages: (1) Warming up with a class-aware loss-guided split, where samples with the lowest symmetric cross-entropy losses in each class are progressively added to the clean pool to prevent class imbalance. (2) Training with a class-agnostic loss-guided split, where a fixed percentage of samples with the lowest losses across the entire dataset are added to the clean pool, further refining the pools. (3) A meta-learning-inspired meta-split stage, where a virtual model is trained for one epoch and samples with the smallest loss reduction are identified as clean hard samples and added to the clean pool. Throughout training, the model is trained in a semi-supervised manner: supervised learning is applied to the clean pool (with labels), and unsupervised learning is applied to the polluted pool (without labels), leveraging methods such as MixMatch.
25135e5dda4cd46e38b028b9f2fef28a336735ca.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on benchmark datasets including CIFAR-10, GTSRB, and an ImageNet subset, using ResNet-18 as the default model. The defense is evaluated against six state-of-the-art backdoor attacks (BadNets, Blend, WaNet, IAB, Refool, and CLB) and compared to baselines such as Fine-pruning, Neural Attention Distillation, Anti-Backdoor Learning, and Decoupling-based Defense. Evaluation metrics include clean accuracy (ACC) and attack success rate (ASR). The setup involves varying the number of clean seed samples, testing resistance to adaptive attacks, and exploring transfer-based initialization using clean samples from a different dataset (e.g., ImageNet). Ablation studies are performed to assess the necessity of each stage and robustness to seed sample contamination. Training time and hyperparameter sensitivity are also reported.
25135e5dda4cd46e38b028b9f2fef28a336735ca.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified framework for training-time backdoor defenses based on adaptive dataset splitting, which enables dynamic and effective separation of clean and poisoned samples. A novel meta-split method is developed to identify clean hard samples that are otherwise difficult to distinguish from poisoned samples. The method requires only a small number of clean seed samples and can be extended to transfer-based settings, making it practical for real-world scenarios. Extensive experiments demonstrate superior performance over existing defenses in both effectiveness (lower ASR, higher ACC) and efficiency (reduced training time), as well as robustness to adaptive and transfer attacks.

251ea7c0ac48ea5a97e9f3f75a2c56a7830993e4.title: Theory, Analysis, and Best Practices for Sigmoid Self-Attention
251ea7c0ac48ea5a97e9f3f75a2c56a7830993e4.research_question: Can self-attention mechanisms in transformer architectures be effectively implemented using element-wise sigmoid activations instead of the conventional softmax, and what are the theoretical, practical, and computational implications of such a substitution across diverse domains and tasks?
251ea7c0ac48ea5a97e9f3f75a2c56a7830993e4.hypothesis: Transformers utilizing sigmoid-based self-attention, when properly normalized and stabilized, can match or exceed the performance and efficiency of softmax-based attention across language, vision, and speech tasks, while offering improved regularity and hardware efficiency.
251ea7c0ac48ea5a97e9f3f75a2c56a7830993e4.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that replaces the standard softmax operation in self-attention with an element-wise sigmoid nonlinearity, introducing a bias term proportional to the logarithm of the sequence length to stabilize attention norms. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to prove that sigmoid attention retains the universal approximation property and exhibits improved regularity, as quantified by a tighter Lipschitz constant. A hardware-aware implementation, FLASHSIGMOID, will be engineered to optimize memory access and computational throughput on modern GPUs by leveraging tiling, kernel fusion, and activation recomputation strategies. The method will also systematically explore best practices for initialization, normalization (including LayerScale and QK norm), and positional embedding choices to ensure stable and performant training across modalities.
251ea7c0ac48ea5a97e9f3f75a2c56a7830993e4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across multiple domains: supervised image classification (using ViT-B/16 on ImageNet-1k), self-supervised image representation learning (SimCLR, BYOL, MAE), automatic speech recognition (LibriSpeech 100h/960h, TED-LIUMv3), and large-scale autoregressive language modeling (RedPajama, Llama2 recipe). Baselines will include standard transformers with softmax attention and recent alternatives such as ReLU and hybrid-norm variants. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy for vision, word error rate for ASR, negative log-likelihood, and standard language modeling benchmarks (e.g., MMLU, PIQA, SciQ). Ablation studies will analyze the impact of bias initialization, normalization layers, positional embeddings, and hardware throughput, with kernel-level benchmarking on H100 and A100 GPUs to quantify speed-ups.
251ea7c0ac48ea5a97e9f3f75a2c56a7830993e4.novelty_claims: The proposed research establishes, for the first time, that sigmoid-based self-attention can serve as a universal function approximator in transformers, with provably improved regularity over softmax attention. A new hardware-aware implementation, FLASHSIGMOID, is introduced, yielding up to 17% kernel-level inference speed-up and 8% end-to-end inference speed-up over state-of-the-art FLASHATTENTION2 on H100 GPUs. The work unifies and extends prior art by providing a comprehensive theoretical foundation, empirical validation across diverse modalities, and actionable best practices for deploying sigmoid attention as a drop-in replacement for softmax in modern transformer architectures.

252088cd1e48bd81772e634ea6c5bef209ae451f.title: SUMO: Subspace-Aware Moment-Orthogonalization for Accelerating Memory-Efficient LLM Training
252088cd1e48bd81772e634ea6c5bef209ae451f.research_question: How can memory-efficient training of large language models (LLMs) be accelerated without sacrificing stability or performance, by leveraging the low-rank structure of gradients and adapting optimization steps to the anisotropic geometry of deep network loss landscapes?
252088cd1e48bd81772e634ea6c5bef209ae451f.hypothesis: Exact moment orthogonalization within a dynamically adapted low-dimensional subspace, using singular value decomposition (SVD), will accelerate convergence, improve stability, and further reduce memory requirements compared to existing low-rank and norm-induced optimization methods that rely on approximate orthogonalization.
252088cd1e48bd81772e634ea6c5bef209ae451f.proposed_method: A novel optimizer, SUMO (Subspace-Aware Moment-Orthogonalization), will be developed to perform exact SVD-based orthogonalization of the first-order moment within an adaptively selected low-rank subspace. The method begins with adaptive subspace selection using randomized SVD to efficiently identify the dominant directions of the gradient matrix, followed by transformation of the first-order moment into the new subspace. The steepest descent optimization step is then computed by applying SVD to the projected moment, yielding orthogonalized updates aligned with the spectral norm of the loss landscape. A norm-growth limiter is incorporated to constrain abrupt changes in update magnitudes, and the update step is performed in the original parameter space by combining the orthogonalized moment with the residual gradient outside the low-rank subspace. Layer-wise learning rate adaptation is achieved by scaling updates according to the root mean square magnitude, ensuring consistent effective learning rates across layers.
252088cd1e48bd81772e634ea6c5bef209ae451f.experiment_details: Experiments will include fine-tuning and pre-training of LLMs on standard benchmarks. Fine-tuning will be evaluated on the GLUE benchmark using the RoBERTa-base model across eight tasks, comparing SUMO (with both SVD and Newton-Schulz5 orthogonalization) to full fine-tuning, LoRA, and GaLore, with metrics such as accuracy, F1, Matthew's correlation, and Pearson correlation. Pre-training experiments will use the LLaMA model on the C4 dataset, reporting validation perplexity and memory usage for models up to 1B parameters. Additional evaluations will include few/zero-shot reasoning on GSM8K and long-context generalization, as well as zero-shot performance on diverse reasoning tasks using the LLaMA-350M model. Baselines will include AdamW, APOLLO, APOLLO-Mini, LoRA, and GaLore. All experiments will be conducted on high-performance GPUs (NVIDIA A100/H200), and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of orthogonalization methods and subspace ranks.
252088cd1e48bd81772e634ea6c5bef209ae451f.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces exact SVD-based moment orthogonalization within a dynamically adapted low-rank subspace for LLM optimization, eliminating the approximation errors and instability associated with iterative methods such as Newton-Schulz5. This approach leverages the observed low-rank structure of gradients and moments during LLM training, enabling both greater memory efficiency and faster, more stable convergence. The method further reduces memory usage by relying solely on first-order moments and provides theoretical convergence guarantees that explicitly account for subspace dynamics and orthogonalization accuracy. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior convergence rates, improved generalization, and state-of-the-art memory efficiency compared to existing low-rank and memory-efficient optimizers.

2535ba93741c111d06fbc33516922a8711a429d4.title: Learning to Reject with a Fixed Predictor: Application to Decontextualization
2535ba93741c111d06fbc33516922a8711a429d4.research_question: How can accurate models with a rejection option be developed for sequence-to-sequence natural language processing tasks, such as decontextualization, where the predictor is fixed and the set of correct outputs is large or ambiguous?
2535ba93741c111d06fbc33516922a8711a429d4.hypothesis: A surrogate loss function, specifically designed for learning a rejector given a fixed predictor, will enable the training of a rejection function that achieves higher precision-coverage trade-offs than traditional confidence-based or threshold-based methods, and will provide strong theoretical guarantees (H-consistency) with respect to the true rejection loss.
2535ba93741c111d06fbc33516922a8711a429d4.proposed_method: A two-step approach will be developed: first, a sequence-to-sequence predictor (e.g., a large language model) is trained using standard techniques such as cross-entropy loss. Second, a rejector function is learned, taking as input both the original input and the predictor's output, and trained on a manually labeled dataset indicating the correctness of the predictor's outputs. The rejector is optimized using a novel convex and differentiable surrogate loss function, parameterized by alpha and beta, which upper-bounds the induced rejection loss and incorporates a built-in threshold for acceptance or rejection. Theoretical analysis will establish H-consistency bounds for the surrogate loss, ensuring that minimizing this loss yields strong guarantees with respect to the original rejection loss. Hyperparameters for the surrogate loss will be set according to principled relationships derived from the theoretical analysis.
2535ba93741c111d06fbc33516922a8711a429d4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the decontextualization task, using a manually labeled dataset of 2,000 examples sampled from the English Wikipedia corpus. The predictor is a fixed, fine-tuned MT5XXL model. The dataset will be split into 1,500 training and 500 validation examples, with 4-fold cross-validation. The rejector will be trained to classify outputs as 'yes' or 'no' based on manual annotation, including a 'title' category treated as positive. Baselines will include confidence-based rejection methods such as MaxProb and thresholding on model scores. Evaluation metrics will focus on precision, coverage, and the precision-coverage trade-off, specifically measuring improvements in coverage at fixed error rates and proximity to theoretical limits.
2535ba93741c111d06fbc33516922a8711a429d4.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new problem formulation for learning to reject with a fixed predictor in sequence-to-sequence NLP tasks, along with a novel surrogate loss function tailored for this setting. The surrogate loss is proven to have strong H-consistency guarantees, providing non-asymptotic bounds on the excess rejection loss. The method eliminates the need for ad-hoc threshold selection by embedding the threshold in the loss function itself. The approach is evaluated on a challenging, manually annotated decontextualization dataset, demonstrating significant improvements in precision-coverage trade-offs over existing baselines and achieving performance close to the theoretical optimum.

2559ddde36d4a861ab54b881bbd15eb40918b159.title: Parameters vs FLOPs: Scaling Laws for Optimal Sparsity for Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
2559ddde36d4a861ab54b881bbd15eb40918b159.research_question: What is the optimal trade-off between parameter count and FLOPs per example in sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models, and how does sparsity influence scaling laws, training efficiency, and downstream performance under various compute and parameter constraints?
2559ddde36d4a861ab54b881bbd15eb40918b159.hypothesis: There exists an optimal sparsity level in MoE language models that, for a given total parameter count and compute budget, improves both training efficiency and model performance. Increasing sparsity while proportionally expanding the total number of parameters leads to better pretraining and potentially downstream performance, up to a point determined by model size and compute constraints.
2559ddde36d4a861ab54b881bbd15eb40918b159.proposed_method: A large-scale empirical study will be conducted to systematically vary the sparsity level, total parameter count, and compute budget in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Transformer language models. Sparsity will be defined as the ratio of inactive experts to total experts, controlling the ratio of total parameters to FLOPs per example. Polynomial surface fitting (in log-space) will be used to model the relationship between pretraining loss, total parameters, active parameters, and sparsity, enabling the identification of optimal configurations. Scaling law equations will be extended to include sparsity as a variable, and coefficients will be estimated using L-BFGS optimization and Huber loss. Both qualitative and quantitative analyses will be performed to derive scaling laws that disentangle the effects of total parameters and FLOPs per example.
2559ddde36d4a861ab54b881bbd15eb40918b159.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training a grid of MoE Transformer models across a range of sparsity levels, total parameter counts (from hundreds of millions to tens of billions), and compute budgets (measured in total training FLOPs). Pretraining loss will be recorded, and downstream performance will be evaluated using few-shot in-context learning on a suite of tasks from the llm-foundry benchmark, including language understanding, world knowledge, reading comprehension, and symbolic reasoning. Baselines will include dense models and MoEs with varying sparsity. Evaluation metrics will include pretraining loss (perplexity) and downstream task error rates. IsoFLOP surfaces will be fitted to empirical data, and optimal points will be identified by fixing one variable and varying others. Additional experiments will explore the impact of increasing inference-time compute (e.g., via Chain-of-Thought prompting) on downstream reasoning tasks.
2559ddde36d4a861ab54b881bbd15eb40918b159.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a generalized scaling law framework that incorporates sparsity as a key variable, enabling the prediction of optimal trade-offs between parameter count and FLOPs per example in MoE language models. The approach provides empirical evidence and parametric forms for optimal sparsity under fixed compute and parameter constraints, extending prior scaling law studies to the sparse MoE regime. The methodology allows for disentangling the effects of total versus active parameters, and demonstrates how dynamic compute allocation during inference can further enhance efficiency and performance on complex tasks. The findings offer actionable insights for designing more efficient and performant sparse architectures.

25709a50df5eb8e40dce7ffe6ecd3bfa79969c7a.title: Exploring Data Scaling Trends and Effects in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
25709a50df5eb8e40dce7ffe6ecd3bfa79969c7a.research_question: How can data scaling and prompt selection strategies be optimized in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) to overcome bottlenecks such as reward hacking and loss of response diversity, and thereby improve the alignment and performance of large language models across diverse tasks?
25709a50df5eb8e40dce7ffe6ecd3bfa79969c7a.hypothesis: Carefully constructed training prompts, particularly those that are more challenging and less susceptible to reward hacking, combined with early-stage prioritization of mathematical and coding tasks, will enhance RLHF performance, increase resistance to reward hacking, and improve response diversity and generalization in large language models.
25709a50df5eb8e40dce7ffe6ecd3bfa79969c7a.proposed_method: A comprehensive RLHF training framework will be developed that integrates a hybrid reward system and advanced prompt selection strategies. The reward system will combine Reasoning Task Verifiers (RTV), which directly validate correctness for specific tasks (e.g., code execution sandboxes for programming), and a Generative Reward Model (GenRM) trained on pairwise human preference data, with explicit use of ground-truth solutions for reasoning tasks. For prompt selection, a Pre-PPO algorithm will be designed to identify and prioritize prompts with lower reward model scores, which are inherently more challenging and less prone to reward hacking. Additionally, the training curriculum will emphasize mathematical and coding prompts in the early stages, leveraging their resistance to reward hacking and clear ground-truth evaluation, before transitioning to a broader mixed-domain dataset. The iterative RLHF optimization will be conducted using PPO, guided by the hybrid reward system and the curated prompt schedule, to maximize reward scores while maintaining policy stability.
25709a50df5eb8e40dce7ffe6ecd3bfa79969c7a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using two pre-trained language model sizes (approximately 25B and 150B parameters). The training dataset will consist of one million original prompts and five million newly collected prompts spanning mathematics, coding, instruction-following, creative writing, and other domains. The Pre-PPO prompt selection will be performed on the small model, selecting the bottom 10% of prompts by reward score, and these will be combined with the original dataset for RLHF training. Early-stage training will focus on coding and math prompts, gradually introducing other domains. Evaluation will use two comprehensive test sets (V1.0 and V2.0), covering logical reasoning, instruction-following, STEM, coding, NLP, knowledge, contextual understanding, and out-of-distribution generalization, with both automated and human-based assessments. Baselines will include standard PPO-based RLHF with the original dataset. Ablation studies will isolate the effects of Pre-PPO prompt selection and early-stage task prioritization.
25709a50df5eb8e40dce7ffe6ecd3bfa79969c7a.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a hybrid reward system that combines reasoning task verifiers and generative reward models for robust resistance to reward hacking. A novel Pre-PPO prompt selection method is developed to explicitly target challenging prompts, enhancing learning effectiveness and response diversity. The curriculum strategy of prioritizing mathematical and coding tasks early in RLHF training is shown to yield significant improvements in specialized and general capabilities. The approach provides a systematic analysis and practical methodology for overcoming data-driven bottlenecks in RLHF, offering scalable solutions for improved alignment and performance in large language models.

2589e7435b478b0389b78cafea75910c2e9460e0.title: LLM4Decompile: Decompiling Binary Code with Large Language Models
2589e7435b478b0389b78cafea75910c2e9460e0.research_question: Can large language models be effectively trained to decompile binary code into high-level source code, improving upon traditional decompilation tools in terms of readability and re-executability, and what are the best approaches for optimizing such models for this task?
2589e7435b478b0389b78cafea75910c2e9460e0.hypothesis: Large language models, when fine-tuned on large-scale, domain-specific datasets and optimized through advanced training strategies, can significantly outperform traditional decompilation tools and existing LLMs in generating readable and executable high-level source code from binaries.
2589e7435b478b0389b78cafea75910c2e9460e0.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that leverages large language models (LLMs) with parameter sizes ranging from 1.3B to 33B, specifically fine-tuned for binary code decompilation. The approach will utilize an End2end-Decompile strategy, where binaries are first disassembled into assembly code and then paired with corresponding source code for supervised training. Training optimization will involve three key steps: (1) large-scale data augmentation by compiling source code at multiple optimization levels (O0-O3), (2) rigorous data cleaning using MinHash and Locality Sensitive Hashing to remove duplicates and low-quality samples, and (3) a two-stage training regime where models are first trained on compilable (but not linkable) code and then refined on executable code. Additionally, a Refined-Decompile approach will be implemented, where LLMs are fine-tuned to enhance the output of traditional tools like Ghidra, further improving readability and correctness.
2589e7435b478b0389b78cafea75910c2e9460e0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using large-scale datasets derived from ExeBench (5 million C functions) and HumanEval-Decompile (converted from HumanEval to C), covering both compilable and executable binaries across multiple compiler optimization levels. Baselines will include state-of-the-art LLMs such as GPT-4o and DeepSeek-Coder, as well as traditional tools like Ghidra. Evaluation will focus on re-executability rates (i.e., whether the decompiled code compiles and passes test assertions) and edit similarity metrics to assess code quality. Additional experiments will measure readability using structured GPT-4o evaluations and test robustness against common binary obfuscation techniques (Control Flow Flattening and Bogus Control Flow). Training and inference will be performed on high-performance GPU clusters, with ablation studies to analyze the impact of dataset type and training strategies.
2589e7435b478b0389b78cafea75910c2e9460e0.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first and largest open-source LLM series (up to 33B parameters) specifically fine-tuned for binary code decompilation. Key innovations include a scalable and optimized End2end-Decompile training pipeline, integration of multi-stage data augmentation and cleaning, and a two-stage training process tailored for binary understanding. The research also pioneers a refined approach for leveraging LLMs to enhance outputs from traditional decompilers, achieving substantial improvements in re-executability and readability. Furthermore, the work systematically evaluates the risks and limitations of LLM-based decompilation under obfuscation, providing empirical evidence that standard obfuscation techniques remain effective barriers, thus addressing ethical concerns.

25a57ecf771dbcc839e5b2d24bb6dc09b9b0a118.title: OpenBias: Open-Set Bias Detection in Text-to-Image Generative Models
25a57ecf771dbcc839e5b2d24bb6dc09b9b0a118.research_question: How can biases, including previously unstudied and domain-specific ones, be identified and quantified in text-to-image generative models without relying on a predefined set of biases or prior data annotation?
25a57ecf771dbcc839e5b2d24bb6dc09b9b0a118.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that an open-set, modular pipeline leveraging large language models (LLMs) and vision question answering (VQA) models can effectively discover, recognize, and quantify both known and novel biases in text-to-image generative models, achieving agreement with existing closed-set methods and human judgment.
25a57ecf771dbcc839e5b2d24bb6dc09b9b0a118.proposed_method: A modular pipeline, OpenBias, will be developed to enable open-set bias detection in text-to-image generative models. The pipeline consists of three main stages: (1) A large language model (LLM) is used to analyze a dataset of real textual captions and propose possible biases, associated classes, and relevant questions for each caption, building a knowledge base of potential biases. (2) The target generative model is treated as a black box and is queried with the identified captions to synthesize images, simulating end-user interactions. (3) A state-of-the-art vision question answering (VQA) model is then used to assess the presence and extent of the proposed biases in the generated images by answering the caption-specific questions. The severity of each bias is quantified by analyzing the distribution of VQA answers, using entropy-based metrics normalized for comparability across biases. The pipeline is designed to be flexible, allowing for the replacement of LLM or VQA components as better models become available.
25a57ecf771dbcc839e5b2d24bb6dc09b9b0a118.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple text-to-image generative models, specifically Stable Diffusion 1.5, 2, and XL, using captions from large-scale multimodal datasets such as COCO and Flickr30k. The pipeline will be evaluated in both context-aware (caption-specific) and context-free (dataset-level) scenarios. For each bias, 100 captions will be selected and 10 images per caption will be generated, resulting in 1000 images per bias for analysis. Baseline comparisons will include closed-set classifier-based bias detection methods (e.g., FairFace for gender, age, and race) and human judgment via a user study. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, F1 score, and KL divergence for model agreement, as well as absolute mean error and majority class agreement for human alignment. The modular design allows for systematic comparison across model versions and datasets, and the pipeline’s outputs will be validated against both automated and human baselines.
25a57ecf771dbcc839e5b2d24bb6dc09b9b0a118.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to address open-set bias detection in text-to-image generative models at scale, without relying on any predefined list of biases or prior data annotation. The pipeline leverages LLMs to propose domain-specific and previously unstudied biases, and uses VQA models for automated, scalable bias recognition and quantification. The approach is modular and model-agnostic, enabling flexible adaptation to new foundation models and domains. The method enables the discovery of novel biases beyond traditional social categories, providing a comprehensive and extensible framework for bias assessment in generative models.

25bc06b508b2c63b9faf77881e528530b147b988.title: DayDreamer: World Models for Physical Robot Learning
25bc06b508b2c63b9faf77881e528530b147b988.research_question: Can world model-based reinforcement learning enable efficient, robust, and generalizable learning of complex robotic tasks directly in the physical world, across diverse robot platforms, sensory modalities, and action spaces, without reliance on simulators or expert demonstrations?
25bc06b508b2c63b9faf77881e528530b147b988.hypothesis: World model-based reinforcement learning, specifically leveraging latent imagination and policy optimization in learned latent spaces, can achieve sample-efficient, robust, and adaptable robot learning directly on physical hardware, outperforming or matching model-free baselines and approaching human-level performance across a variety of real-world robotic tasks.
25bc06b508b2c63b9faf77881e528530b147b988.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed that applies a world model-based reinforcement learning algorithm, such as Dreamer, to physical robots for online learning. The method involves training a deep neural network world model (based on a Recurrent State-Space Model, RSSM) to predict environment dynamics from multi-modal sensory inputs, including images and proprioceptive data. The world model fuses sensory inputs into compact latent representations using an encoder, predicts future latent states and rewards with a dynamics and reward network, and reconstructs observations with a decoder for rich learning signals. An actor-critic reinforcement learning algorithm then learns task-specific behaviors by optimizing policies from imagined rollouts in the latent space of the world model, enabling massively parallel policy updates. Data collection and model learning are decoupled and run asynchronously to meet real-time control requirements, allowing continuous improvement as the robot interacts with the environment.
25bc06b508b2c63b9faf77881e528530b147b988.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four distinct physical robots: a Unitree A1 quadruped for locomotion (rolling over, standing up, and walking), two robotic arms (UR5 and XArm) for visual pick-and-place tasks with sparse rewards, and a Sphero Ollie wheeled robot for visual navigation. Each task will use only real-world data, without simulators or demonstrations. The same set of hyperparameters will be used across all experiments to test generalizability. Baselines will include state-of-the-art model-free reinforcement learning algorithms appropriate to each task, such as SAC for continuous control, Rainbow DQN and PPO for discrete visual manipulation, and DrQv2 for visual navigation, as well as human operator performance where applicable. Evaluation metrics will include task-specific rewards (e.g., pick rate, distance to goal, successful locomotion), sample efficiency (learning time), and robustness to perturbations. Experimental setups will ensure fair comparisons, including identical sensory modalities and action spaces for each baseline.
25bc06b508b2c63b9faf77881e528530b147b988.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first comprehensive demonstration of world model-based reinforcement learning for sample-efficient, robust, and generalizable robot learning directly in the physical world, across diverse robot types and tasks, without simulators or demonstrations. The approach leverages a unified algorithm and hyperparameter setting for all experiments, demonstrating broad applicability. The method enables rapid adaptation to environmental changes and perturbations, and achieves or approaches human-level performance in challenging real-world tasks. The research will also provide an open-source infrastructure supporting multiple sensory modalities and action spaces, establishing a strong baseline and platform for future research in real-world robot learning with world models.

26218bdcc3945c7edae7aa2adbfba4cd820a2df3.title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning
26218bdcc3945c7edae7aa2adbfba4cd820a2df3.research_question: How can a general-purpose visual language model be developed to rapidly adapt to a wide range of multimodal tasks, including image and video understanding, using only a few annotated examples and without extensive task-specific fine-tuning?
26218bdcc3945c7edae7aa2adbfba4cd820a2df3.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a visual language model leveraging architectural innovations to bridge large pretrained vision and language models, and trained on large-scale interleaved multimodal web data, can achieve state-of-the-art few-shot learning performance across diverse vision-language tasks without requiring extensive task-specific fine-tuning.
26218bdcc3945c7edae7aa2adbfba4cd820a2df3.proposed_method: A novel visual language model architecture will be designed that integrates a frozen, pretrained vision encoder (such as NFNet) with a frozen, pretrained large language model (e.g., Chinchilla) via a Perceiver Resampler module and newly inserted GATED XATTN-DENSE cross-attention layers. The Perceiver Resampler will convert variable-length visual features into a fixed number of visual tokens, which are then used to condition the language model through gated cross-attention blocks interleaved between frozen language model layers. The model will be trained on a mixture of large-scale web-scraped datasets containing interleaved images, videos, and text, as well as paired image-text and video-text data. The architecture will support arbitrarily interleaved visual and textual inputs and will be optimized for in-context few-shot learning by prompting with multimodal input/output examples.
26218bdcc3945c7edae7aa2adbfba4cd820a2df3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a comprehensive suite of 16 popular multimodal benchmarks spanning image and video captioning, visual question answering, visual dialogue, and multi-choice question answering. Datasets will include COCO, OKVQA, VQAv2, MSVDQA, VATEX, VizWiz, MSRVTTQA, Hateful Memes, and others, with both development and held-out test sets to ensure unbiased evaluation. Baselines will include state-of-the-art zero-shot, few-shot, and fine-tuned models. Evaluation metrics will be task-appropriate, such as CIDEr for captioning, top-1 accuracy for classification and question answering, and other standard metrics for each benchmark. The model's few-shot learning capabilities will be assessed by prompting with varying numbers of support examples (e.g., 4 and 32 shots), and performance will be compared to models trained with orders of magnitude more task-specific data. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of architectural choices, training data composition, and optimization strategies.
26218bdcc3945c7edae7aa2adbfba4cd820a2df3.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first visual language model capable of ingesting arbitrarily interleaved images, videos, and text, and generating free-form text output in an open-ended manner. Key innovations include the Perceiver Resampler for efficient visual tokenization, GATED XATTN-DENSE layers for stable and effective visual conditioning of frozen language models, and a training regime leveraging large-scale, naturally interleaved multimodal web data. The method enables state-of-the-art few-shot adaptation to a wide range of vision-language tasks without fine-tuning, outperforming existing models that require extensive task-specific training.

263d1188541c69049ac4831332271b5acfe69b97.title: RMM: Reinforced Memory Management for Class-Incremental Learning
263d1188541c69049ac4831332271b5acfe69b97.research_question: How can memory management be dynamically optimized in class-incremental learning scenarios under strict memory constraints, in order to mitigate catastrophic forgetting and improve overall classification performance?
263d1188541c69049ac4831332271b5acfe69b97.hypothesis: A hierarchical reinforcement learning-based memory management strategy that dynamically allocates memory between old and new classes, as well as among individual classes based on recognition difficulty, will outperform static or heuristic memory allocation strategies in class-incremental learning tasks.
263d1188541c69049ac4831332271b5acfe69b97.proposed_method: A hierarchical reinforcement learning framework, Reinforced Memory Management (RMM), is proposed for class-incremental learning (CIL) under a fixed memory budget. The method consists of two levels: Level-1 determines the split of memory between exemplars of old classes and new incoming class data at each incremental phase, while Level-2 allocates the exemplar memory among individual old classes based on their recognition difficulty, measured by training entropy. The policy functions for both levels are parameterized as two-layer fully connected networks and are trained using the REINFORCE algorithm. To address the challenge that past and future data are inaccessible during CIL, policy functions are pre-trained on pseudo-CIL tasks generated from available data (e.g., data from the initial phase or from another dataset), where all data is accessible for reward computation. The learned policy is then transferred and applied to the target CIL task, enabling adaptive and class-specific memory allocation throughout the incremental learning process.
263d1188541c69049ac4831332271b5acfe69b97.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by integrating the proposed RMM framework into two state-of-the-art CIL baselines: LUCIR+AANets and POD+AANets. Evaluation will be performed on three widely used benchmarks: CIFAR-100, ImageNet-Subset (100 classes), and ImageNet-Full (1000 classes). Each dataset will be split into several incremental phases (5, 10, or 25), with a fixed total memory budget for all phases. The primary evaluation metric will be average classification accuracy across all phases, as well as last-phase accuracy to assess forgetting. Ablation studies will compare one-level versus two-level reinforcement learning, transferred policies, and oracle settings. Network architectures include a 32-layer ResNet for CIFAR-100 and an 18-layer ResNet for ImageNet, with consistent class orders and hyperparameters as in prior work. Policy networks are trained offline on pseudo-CIL tasks, and their computational overhead is measured relative to baseline training time.
263d1188541c69049ac4831332271b5acfe69b97.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a hierarchical reinforcement learning approach for memory management in class-incremental learning, enabling dynamic and class-specific allocation of memory resources. The method is the first to optimize memory allocation for CIL in a reinforced and learnable manner, rather than relying on static or heuristic strategies. A novel pseudo-task generation strategy is developed to enable policy training despite the inaccessibility of past and future data in standard CIL protocols. The approach is general and can be incorporated into any exemplar-replaying-based CIL method, with demonstrated transferability of learned policies across datasets and settings.

2651f0179874bd010f58d2c9fa7d118807c80977.title: TIES-Merging: Resolving Interference When Merging Models
2651f0179874bd010f58d2c9fa7d118807c80977.research_question: How can multiple task-specific fine-tuned models be merged into a single multitask model without additional training, while minimizing performance loss due to parameter interference across models?
2651f0179874bd010f58d2c9fa7d118807c80977.hypothesis: Interference between redundant parameters and sign disagreements in parameter updates are primary causes of performance degradation when merging models; explicitly addressing these sources of interference will yield merged multitask models with higher in-domain and out-of-domain performance compared to existing merging techniques.
2651f0179874bd010f58d2c9fa7d118807c80977.proposed_method: A new model merging approach, TIES-MERGING (TRIM, ELECT SIGN & MERGE), is proposed to resolve parameter interference when combining multiple fine-tuned models. The method operates in three key steps: (1) For each task-specific model, compute the task vector by subtracting the pre-trained initialization from the fine-tuned parameters, then trim each task vector to retain only the top-k% largest-magnitude parameter updates, resetting the rest to zero (TRIM). (2) For each parameter, resolve sign conflicts across models by electing the sign with the largest total magnitude (ELECT SIGN). (3) For each parameter, merge only the values from models whose sign matches the elected sign, averaging these values to produce the final parameter value (MERGE). The merged task vector is then scaled by a hyperparameter and added to the pre-trained initialization to yield the final multitask model. This approach is designed to prevent both magnitude shrinkage from redundant parameters and destructive interference from sign disagreements.
2651f0179874bd010f58d2c9fa7d118807c80977.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across diverse settings, including both language (T5-base, T5-large) and vision (ViT-B/32, ViT-L/14) models, and both full fine-tuning and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (e.g., (IA)3 on T0-3B). Datasets will span a variety of NLP tasks (e.g., COPA, H-SWAG, StoryCloze, ANLI, CB, RTE, WSC, Winogrande, WiC, QASC, WikiQA, QuaRTz, PAWS) and vision tasks (e.g., Cars, DTD, EuroSAT, GTSRB, MNIST, RESISC45, SUN397, SVHN). Baseline methods for comparison will include simple parameter averaging, Task Arithmetic, RegMean, and Fisher Merging. Evaluation metrics will include in-domain accuracy, out-of-domain generalization (on held-out datasets), and robustness to merging checkpoints from the same or different tasks. Both settings with and without validation sets for hyperparameter tuning will be explored, and ablation studies will assess the importance of each component of the proposed method.
2651f0179874bd010f58d2c9fa7d118807c80977.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a principled approach to model merging that explicitly addresses two key sources of parameter interference: redundancy and sign disagreement. Unlike prior methods, TIES-MERGING trims non-influential parameter updates and resolves sign conflicts before merging, resulting in improved multitask model performance across a wide range of domains, architectures, and fine-tuning regimes. The approach is simple, requires no additional training, and can be applied without access to validation data, yet consistently outperforms existing merging techniques. Detailed analysis demonstrates the critical role of sign alignment and parameter selection in successful model merging.

266311bcce6cf4cba39168f9392ca1a42ae75a71.title: What Kinds of Functions do Deep Neural Networks Learn? Insights from Variational Spline Theory
266311bcce6cf4cba39168f9392ca1a42ae75a71.research_question: What are the mathematical properties and function spaces that characterize the functions learned by deep neural networks with rectified linear unit (ReLU) activations, and how can these insights inform the design of regularization schemes and network architectures?
266311bcce6cf4cba39168f9392ca1a42ae75a71.hypothesis: Deep neural networks with ReLU activations learn functions that can be characterized as compositions of functions from Banach spaces of second-order bounded variation in the Radon domain, and regularization based on these spaces promotes sparsity, skip connections, and low-rank weight matrices, which align with effective empirical practices in deep learning.
266311bcce6cf4cba39168f9392ca1a42ae75a71.proposed_method: A variational framework will be developed to analyze deep neural networks with ReLU activations by defining a new function space that captures their compositional structure. This space will consist of compositions of functions from Banach spaces of second-order bounded variation in the Radon domain, equipped with sparsity-promoting norms. A representer theorem will be derived, showing that solutions to regularized data-fitting problems over this space are realizable by deep ReLU networks with skip connections and rank-bounded weight matrices. The regularization term will be formulated as the sum of Banach norms of each function in the composition, which can be expressed in terms of neural network parameters and is related to weight decay and path-norm regularization. The analysis will leverage techniques from variational spline theory to establish connections between deep neural networks and splines.
266311bcce6cf4cba39168f9392ca1a42ae75a71.experiment_details: Experiments will involve fitting deep ReLU networks to scattered data using the proposed variational regularization framework. The datasets will consist of synthetic or real-world data suitable for supervised learning tasks, with varying input and output dimensions to test the generality of the approach. Baseline comparisons will include standard deep ReLU networks trained with conventional regularization methods such as weight decay and path-norm regularization. Evaluation metrics will include interpolation accuracy, sparsity of the learned representations (e.g., number of active neurons), rank of weight matrices, and generalization performance. The experimental setup will allow for control over the number of layers, the rank bounds of weight matrices, and the presence of skip connections to assess their impact on learning and regularization.
266311bcce6cf4cba39168f9392ca1a42ae75a71.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a new function space for deep neural networks that captures their compositional and sparsity properties, grounded in Banach spaces of second-order bounded variation in the Radon domain. A novel representer theorem is established for deep ReLU networks, providing theoretical justification for architectural features such as skip connections and low-rank weight matrices. The variational framework leads to new, principled forms of regularization that promote sparsity and are directly related to neural network parameters. The approach also establishes new connections between deep neural networks and variational spline theory, offering a unified mathematical perspective on deep learning and classical spline methods.

26756d4327a62b1d5aef8031cc4071e243f050a3.title: I2SB: Image-to-Image Schrödinger Bridge
26756d4327a62b1d5aef8031cc4071e243f050a3.research_question: How can a scalable, mathematically principled framework be developed to directly model nonlinear diffusion processes between two arbitrary image distributions for image restoration and general image-to-image translation tasks?
26756d4327a62b1d5aef8031cc4071e243f050a3.hypothesis: Directly constructing diffusion bridges between degraded and clean image distributions, using a tractable class of Schrödinger bridge models compatible with standard diffusion model techniques, will yield more interpretable, efficient, and high-performing generative processes for image restoration compared to existing conditional diffusion models and inverse problem approaches.
26756d4327a62b1d5aef8031cc4071e243f050a3.proposed_method: A new class of conditional diffusion models, termed Image-to-Image Schrödinger Bridge (I2SB), will be developed to directly learn nonlinear diffusion bridges between two given image distributions, such as degraded and clean images. The method will leverage a tractable subclass of Schrödinger bridge models, reformulated to be compatible with the computational framework of standard score-based generative models (SGMs). The approach will analytically compute marginal distributions given boundary pairs (clean and degraded images), enabling simulation-free training and efficient sampling. Training will involve regressing a neural network (e.g., U-Net) to predict the nonlinear drift (score function) using an analytic posterior derived from the Schrödinger bridge SDEs, while generation will start from a degraded image and iteratively sample towards the clean image using DDPM-style recursive posterior sampling.
26756d4327a62b1d5aef8031cc4071e243f050a3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of image restoration tasks, including super-resolution, deblurring, inpainting, and JPEG restoration, using the ImageNet 256×256 dataset. The method will be compared against three classes of baselines: standard conditional score-based generative models (e.g., Palette, ADM), diffusion-based inverse models (e.g., DDRM, DDNM, ΠGDM), and standard Schrödinger bridge models (e.g., CDSB). Evaluation metrics will include Frechet Inception Distance (FID) and classifier accuracy (CA) using a pre-trained ResNet50. The experimental setup will match baseline implementations for fair comparison, and ablation studies will be performed to analyze sampling efficiency, interpretability, and the effect of varying the number of function evaluations (NFE). Additional experiments will extend the approach to general image-to-image translation tasks and compare efficiency and quality with GAN-based methods.
26756d4327a62b1d5aef8031cc4071e243f050a3.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first scalable, simulation-free framework for learning nonlinear diffusion bridges between arbitrary image distributions, leveraging a tractable class of Schrödinger bridge models compatible with standard diffusion model techniques. It enables direct, interpretable, and efficient image-to-image generation without requiring knowledge of corruption operators, surpassing standard conditional diffusion models and matching or exceeding the performance of inverse problem-based diffusion models. The approach provides new algorithmic opportunities for large-scale nonlinear diffusion modeling and demonstrates state-of-the-art results on multiple high-dimensional image restoration tasks.

2689fd5901abe402e67b75c7674e29c9724d5028.title: DextrAH-RGB: Visuomotor Policies to Grasp Anything with Dexterous Hands
2689fd5901abe402e67b75c7674e29c9724d5028.research_question: How can end-to-end visuomotor policies be developed to enable dexterous robotic hands to robustly grasp a wide variety of objects using only RGB image input, and how well can such policies generalize to novel objects and real-world conditions?
2689fd5901abe402e67b75c7674e29c9724d5028.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a dexterous arm-hand grasping policy trained entirely in simulation using privileged state-based reinforcement learning, and subsequently distilled into an RGB-based policy via a student-teacher framework, can achieve robust sim-to-real transfer and competitive performance on complex, contact-rich grasping tasks, even under challenging lighting and object conditions.
2689fd5901abe402e67b75c7674e29c9724d5028.proposed_method: A two-stage training pipeline is proposed. First, a state-based teacher policy is trained in simulation using reinforcement learning (PPO) with privileged geometric and proprioceptive observations, leveraging a geometric fabric controller to ensure safe, reactive, and stable dexterous grasping. The teacher policy uses an LSTM-based architecture with dense skip connections and is trained with automatic domain randomization (ADR) to improve robustness. In the second stage, the teacher policy is distilled into a student policy that receives only RGB images (monocular or stereo) and proprioceptive data. The student employs a Siamese ResNet-18 encoder for image processing, a transformer-based stereo embedding module, and an LSTM-MLP policy head. Distillation is performed using an online DAgger approach, minimizing KL-divergence between student and teacher action distributions, with an auxiliary loss for object position prediction. The student is trained with extensive photorealistic rendering, domain randomization, and data augmentation to bridge the sim-to-real gap.
2689fd5901abe402e67b75c7674e29c9724d5028.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in both simulation and real-world settings. In simulation, policies are trained and ablated using the NVIDIA Isaac Lab framework across diverse objects, with ADR applied to physics and visual parameters. Performance is evaluated via success rate, positional error, and policy robustness, comparing monocular vs. stereo input, transformer vs. non-transformer architectures, and different encoder training strategies. Real-world deployment uses a 7-DoF Kuka arm with a 16-DoF Allegro hand and stereo RGB cameras, running the trained policy at 60 Hz. Evaluation includes single-object grasping (across 11 objects, 5 poses each) and a bin-packing protocol (36 objects, measuring consecutive successes, cycle time, and success rate) under both controlled and high-dynamic-range lighting. Baselines include depth-based policies (DextrAH-G), diffusion-based grasping, and other state-of-the-art methods. Metrics include grasp success rate, cycle time, and robustness to lighting and background distractors.
2689fd5901abe402e67b75c7674e29c9724d5028.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to demonstrate robust sim-to-real transfer of end-to-end RGB-based visuomotor policies for dexterous arm-hand grasping in complex, contact-rich tasks. The method introduces a scalable student-teacher distillation framework that enables training purely in simulation with photorealistic rendering and extensive domain randomization, without reliance on depth maps or object pose estimation. The use of geometric fabric controllers provides a safe and reactive action space, and the stereo transformer-based perceptual architecture enables effective depth inference from RGB alone. The approach achieves competitive or state-of-the-art performance compared to depth-based and prior RGB-based methods, and demonstrates robustness across novel objects, textures, and challenging real-world lighting conditions.

2698fead3a09c5e3e2ebb5a020861654fc017de1.title: Preserving Node-level Privacy in Graph Neural Networks
2698fead3a09c5e3e2ebb5a020861654fc017de1.research_question: How can node-level privacy be effectively preserved in Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) while maintaining strong utility, especially under differential privacy constraints, and what are the limitations of existing approaches?
2698fead3a09c5e3e2ebb5a020861654fc017de1.hypothesis: A specialized node sampling protocol, combined with tailored sub-graph construction and differential privacy mechanisms, can achieve node-level privacy in GNNs with strong utility, outperforming existing baselines, particularly in high privacy regimes.
2698fead3a09c5e3e2ebb5a020861654fc017de1.proposed_method: A novel protocol is developed for node-level privacy in GNNs, centered around a sampling routine called HeterPoisson. This method employs a heterogeneous node sampling strategy that adjusts the probability of node selection inversely to each node's out-degree, thereby controlling individual node impact on the model. Sub-graphs are constructed by independently sampling central nodes and their neighbors, with additional steps to ensure no overlap between central and peripheral nodes across sub-graphs, which enables precise privacy accounting. Per-sub-graph gradients are computed and clipped to a bounded norm, and Gaussian noise is added to the aggregated gradients to enforce differential privacy. Privacy guarantees are derived by reducing the protocol to a mixture of Gaussians mechanism, and privacy loss is tightly accounted for using Rényi Differential Privacy (RDP) and privacy loss random variables.
2698fead3a09c5e3e2ebb5a020861654fc017de1.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on five real-world graph datasets (Facebook, Twitch, Amazon, PubMed, Reddit) with varying sizes, edge densities, and node features. The method is evaluated under both transductive and inductive settings, using standard GNN architectures (GCN, GIN, SAGE) as backbones. Baselines include naive DP-SGD, GAP, and NDP. Evaluation metrics include node classification accuracy and precision, with ablation studies on sampling parameters and design choices. Privacy audit techniques are applied to validate privacy guarantees, and membership inference attacks are performed to assess protocol resilience. Hyperparameters such as neighborhood sampling multiplier and number of sampled neighbors are varied to analyze privacy-utility trade-offs.
2698fead3a09c5e3e2ebb5a020861654fc017de1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a node-level differential privacy protocol for GNNs that does not require bounded degree assumptions or graph projection, addressing fundamental utility-privacy trade-offs overlooked by prior methods. The HeterPoisson sampling routine enables precise privacy accounting via a mixture of Gaussians mechanism, and the protocol is shown to provide strong privacy guarantees and superior utility, especially in high privacy regimes. The method also identifies and proves the impossibility of achieving both strong privacy and acceptable utility through private instance embedding, highlighting critical flaws in previous approaches. Comprehensive empirical and theoretical validation, including privacy audits and attack resistance, further establishes the innovation and robustness of the solution.

26bd84d181af3812a62bc03ba005e223471a3bad.title: Locality Alignment Improves Vision-Language Models
26bd84d181af3812a62bc03ba005e223471a3bad.research_question: How can vision-language models be improved to better capture both local and global image semantics, particularly to address spatial reasoning errors and perceptual failures in downstream tasks?
26bd84d181af3812a62bc03ba005e223471a3bad.hypothesis: Incorporating a post-training locality alignment stage that leverages self-supervision to disentangle and encode local image semantics in vision transformer backbones will improve the spatial reasoning and overall performance of vision-language models, especially on tasks requiring fine-grained spatial understanding.
26bd84d181af3812a62bc03ba005e223471a3bad.proposed_method: A novel post-training procedure, termed locality alignment, will be developed for vision transformer (ViT) backbones. This will utilize a masked embedding self-consistency approach (MaskEmbed), where the pre-trained ViT is fine-tuned by reconstructing its own outputs under various masked input patterns. Specifically, an encoder initialized from the pre-trained ViT will generate patch embeddings, and a transformer-based decoder will reconstruct the masked outputs of the frozen pre-trained model (teacher) using a reconstruction loss. The method will use random masking of image patches and train the encoder-decoder pair to ensure that each patch embedding captures localized semantic information. The procedure is designed to be efficient, requiring only a small fraction of the original pre-training compute, and does not require additional human-annotated data.
26bd84d181af3812a62bc03ba005e223471a3bad.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in two stages: (1) vision-centric probing using semantic segmentation datasets (e.g., MSCOCO, ADE20k) reformulated as patch-level multi-label classification, with macro-averaged recall as the primary metric, and (2) vision-language model (VLM) training and evaluation using the Prismatic library and a suite of benchmarks focused on spatial understanding (e.g., RefCOCO, OCID-Ref, TallyQA, VSR, AI2D), as well as holistic QA and text comprehension (e.g., VQAv2, VizWiz, TextVQA). Baselines will include standard pre-trained ViTs (e.g., CLIP, SigLIP, MoCo) and VLMs trained without locality alignment. The main backbones will be high-resolution CLIP ViT-L@336px and SigLIP SO400M@384px, paired with Llama-2 7B as the language model. Training data for locality alignment will be sourced from ImageNet-1k and ImageNet-21k, while VLMs will be trained on the Llava-1.5 and extended data mixtures. Controlled comparisons will be made, and ablations will be performed to assess the impact of key hyperparameters and design choices.
26bd84d181af3812a62bc03ba005e223471a3bad.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a scalable, self-supervised post-training stage (locality alignment) for ViTs that enables extraction of local semantics without additional human annotation or significant computational overhead. The MaskEmbed procedure generalizes previous masking-based approaches by using a transformer decoder for richer patch embeddings, and is applicable to any strong image-level supervised backbone. The approach is claimed to consistently improve both patch-level semantic extraction and downstream VLM performance on spatial reasoning benchmarks, outperforming prior methods such as CLIPSelf and feature fusion in terms of efficiency and breadth of improvement.

26c6090b7e7ba4513f82aa28d41360c60770c618.title: VideoFusion: Decomposed Diffusion Models for High-Quality Video Generation
26c6090b7e7ba4513f82aa28d41360c60770c618.research_question: How can high-quality, temporally coherent videos be generated efficiently using diffusion probabilistic models, while effectively leveraging spatial-temporal correlations and prior knowledge from large-scale pretrained image models?
26c6090b7e7ba4513f82aa28d41360c60770c618.hypothesis: Decomposing the diffusion process into a shared base noise and a frame-specific residual noise will enable more efficient and coherent video generation, and leveraging pretrained image diffusion models for the base component will further enhance video quality and training efficiency.
26c6090b7e7ba4513f82aa28d41360c60770c618.proposed_method: A novel decomposed diffusion probabilistic model for video generation is proposed, in which the noise added to each video frame during the diffusion process is split into two components: a base noise shared across all frames and a residual noise unique to each frame. The denoising process is carried out by two jointly trained neural networks: a base generator (initialized from a large pretrained image diffusion model, such as DALL-E 2) responsible for reconstructing the central or base frame, and a smaller residual generator that reconstructs the motion or differences between frames. In each denoising step, the base noise is estimated from the central frame and removed from all frames, after which the residual generator estimates the remaining noise for each frame, conditioned on frame index and latent embedding. The base generator is fine-tuned on video data with a small learning rate, and a stop-gradient operation ensures stable joint training. The method supports both unconditional and text-conditional video generation, with the prior for conditioning learned or pretrained as needed.
26c6090b7e7ba4513f82aa28d41360c60770c618.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on several benchmark datasets, including UCF101, Sky Time-lapse, TaiChi-HD, and WebVid-10M, covering both unconditional and text-conditioned video generation. The method is compared against state-of-the-art GAN-based and diffusion-based baselines such as TGAN, MoCoGAN-HD, DIGAN, StyleGAN-V, VideoGPT, TATS, VDM, and CogVideo. Evaluation metrics include Frechet Video Distance (FVD), Kernel Video Distance (KVD), and Inception Score (IS), with quantitative results reported at various resolutions (e.g., 16x128x128). Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of the decomposition parameter, pretraining, and joint training strategies. Efficiency is measured in terms of memory usage and inference latency compared to baseline diffusion models. Qualitative results include long sequence generation, content-motion disentanglement, and text-to-video synthesis.
26c6090b7e7ba4513f82aa28d41360c60770c618.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a decomposed diffusion process for video generation, where noise is split into a shared base and a residual component, enabling more effective modeling of temporal coherence. The method leverages large pretrained image diffusion models for the base generator, allowing efficient parameter allocation and improved sample quality. The framework supports both unconditional and text-conditioned video generation, and enables long sequence synthesis and explicit control over content and motion. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks, with significant improvements in both quality and efficiency over previous GAN-based and diffusion-based methods.

26d46ca94df7b11a0fb876762cb5d6d525c4e7da.title: On the expressiveness and spectral bias of KANs
26d46ca94df7b11a0fb876762cb5d6d525c4e7da.research_question: How do Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) compare to Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) in terms of expressiveness, approximation capabilities, and spectral bias, particularly for applications requiring the learning of high-frequency components?
26d46ca94df7b11a0fb876762cb5d6d525c4e7da.hypothesis: KANs possess at least equivalent, and potentially superior, expressiveness and approximation efficiency compared to MLPs, and exhibit significantly reduced spectral bias, enabling more effective learning of high-frequency components.
26d46ca94df7b11a0fb876762cb5d6d525c4e7da.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted to compare KANs and MLPs. Theoretical analysis will establish representation equivalences and parameter efficiency between KANs (with B-spline parameterized activations and grid extension) and MLPs (with ReLU or higher-order polynomial activations), including derivation of approximation rates on Sobolev spaces. Spectral bias will be analyzed by examining the Hessian of the least squares loss for shallow KANs and comparing convergence rates across frequency components. Empirical studies will implement both architectures using controlled hyperparameters (depth, width, grid size), leveraging grid extension for KANs, and will systematically evaluate learning dynamics and frequency fitting behaviors. The method will also include the use of adaptive grid refinement and analysis of overfitting tendencies.
26d46ca94df7b11a0fb876762cb5d6d525c4e7da.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed on several benchmark tasks: (1) 1D regression of functions composed of multiple sine waves with varying frequencies and amplitudes, using 200 uniformly spaced samples and full-batch ADAM optimization; (2) regression of samples from high-dimensional Gaussian random fields, generated via truncated Karhunen–Loève expansions, with 80/20 train/test splits and mean squared error loss, using both LBFGS optimization and grid extension for KANs; (3) solution of the 1D Poisson equation with high-frequency components using the DeepRitz method, comparing relative L2 and H1 errors for both architectures. Baselines will include standard MLPs (with ReLU and higher-order activations) and KANs with varying depth, width, and grid size. Evaluation metrics will focus on frequency-wise learning curves (via Fourier analysis), regression loss, and error norms. Hyperparameter sweeps will be conducted to assess the impact of architecture choices on spectral bias and overfitting.
26d46ca94df7b11a0fb876762cb5d6d525c4e7da.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a rigorous theoretical framework demonstrating that KANs can efficiently represent any function expressible by MLPs with comparable or fewer parameters, especially as grid size increases. It provides the first detailed analysis of spectral bias in finite-width KANs, showing that KANs are less biased toward low frequencies and can learn all frequencies more uniformly than MLPs. The research will clarify the practical implications of grid extension and compositional spline-based activation parameterization, offering new insights for hyperparameter selection and for scientific computing applications where high-frequency learning is critical.

26d7a95a029f91fd36d32bd5520a8cde691ffd0c.title: Mimetic Initialization of Self-Attention Layers
26d7a95a029f91fd36d32bd5520a8cde691ffd0c.research_question: Can the trainability and final performance of vanilla Transformers, particularly Vision Transformers (ViTs), be improved on small and medium-sized datasets through a structured, learning-free initialization of self-attention layers, without relying on pretraining or architectural modifications?
26d7a95a029f91fd36d32bd5520a8cde691ffd0c.hypothesis: A closed-form, mimetic initialization of self-attention weights—designed to mimic the statistical patterns observed in pretrained models—will enable vanilla Transformers to train faster and achieve higher final accuracies on small and medium-scale datasets compared to standard random initializations.
26d7a95a029f91fd36d32bd5520a8cde691ffd0c.proposed_method: A novel initialization scheme, termed 'mimetic initialization,' will be developed for the self-attention layers of Transformers. This method sets the product of the query and key weights (W_Q W_K^T) to approximate the identity matrix, and the product of the value and projection weights (W_V W_proj) to approximate the negative identity, based on empirical observations from pretrained ViTs. The initialization is achieved via a structured, learning-free, closed-form procedure using random normal matrices and singular value decomposition (SVD) to control the prominence of diagonal and off-diagonal components. Sinusoidal positional embeddings are required to interact with the initialized weights, and the method is designed to be compatible with standard Transformer architectures without any architectural modifications or pretraining steps.
26d7a95a029f91fd36d32bd5520a8cde691ffd0c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several image classification datasets, including CIFAR-10, ImageNet-1k, TinyImageNet, CIFAR-100, and SVHN, as well as on language modeling tasks such as Penn Treebank (PTB) and WikiText-103. Vanilla ViT models of varying sizes and depths will be trained from scratch using standard pipelines (e.g., ResNet-style and DeiT-style training) and compared against baselines with default initialization, GPSA (Gated Positional Self-Attention), LayerScale, and pretrained weight transfer. Evaluation metrics include classification accuracy for vision tasks and perplexity or bits-per-character for language modeling. Ablation studies will assess the importance of each initialization component, positional embedding scaling, and the interaction between initialization and architectural or training pipeline choices. Hyperparameters for the initialization (alpha, beta) will be tuned via grid search on validation splits.
26d7a95a029f91fd36d32bd5520a8cde691ffd0c.novelty_claims: The proposed mimetic initialization is a learning-free, closed-form technique that directly mimics the statistical structure of self-attention weights in pretrained models, without requiring any pretraining or architectural changes. This approach enables vanilla Transformers to achieve substantial performance gains—up to 5% higher accuracy on small-scale image classification tasks—making them competitive with or superior to methods that rely on convolutions, auxiliary losses, or pretraining. The method is simple, computationally inexpensive, and generalizes across different datasets and domains, including language modeling. The proposal introduces the broader concept of 'mimetic initialization,' suggesting that domain-informed, interpretable initializations can bridge the gap between random initialization and the benefits of pretraining.

26e5b933b8f60bd749d428b5ff813b2abcd765d8.title: Composer: Creative and Controllable Image Synthesis with Composable Conditions
26e5b933b8f60bd749d428b5ff813b2abcd765d8.research_question: How can image synthesis models be designed to provide flexible and fine-grained control over generated images using a wide range of composable conditions, while maintaining high synthesis quality and creativity?
26e5b933b8f60bd749d428b5ff813b2abcd765d8.hypothesis: A diffusion-based generative model that decomposes images into multiple independent, composable representations and recomposes them using a conditional framework will enable unprecedented controllability and flexibility in image synthesis, without sacrificing quality or generalization.
26e5b933b8f60bd749d428b5ff813b2abcd765d8.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a compositional image synthesis framework based on conditional diffusion models. First, each image is decomposed into a set of independent representations capturing different aspects, such as text captions, semantic embeddings, style, color histograms, sketches, segmentation masks, depth maps, intensity images, and editable masks. These representations are extracted using pretrained models or computer vision algorithms. During training, a multi-conditional diffusion model (with a UNet backbone) is optimized to reconstruct images from varying subsets of these representations, employing a joint training strategy with probabilistic dropout of conditions to encourage robustness to missing or novel combinations. At inference, users can flexibly specify any subset of conditions to guide image synthesis or editing, with global representations (e.g., text, style) and localized representations (e.g., sketch, segmentation) integrated through modified conditioning modules in the diffusion model. The method supports both global and localized conditioning, region-specific editing via masking, and can generate high-resolution images through hierarchical upsampling diffusion models.
26e5b933b8f60bd749d428b5ff813b2abcd765d8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale image-text datasets, including ImageNet21K, WebVision, and a filtered version of LAION (totaling around 1 billion images). The model will be trained in stages: pretraining the base diffusion model at 64x64 resolution, followed by upsampling models for 256x256 and 1024x1024 resolutions, and an optional prior model for caption-to-image embedding. Evaluation will include traditional text-to-image generation on the COCO dataset, with metrics such as FID and CLIP score, as well as a suite of image manipulation tasks (variation, interpolation, reconfiguration, style transfer, pose transfer, virtual try-on, and region-specific editing). Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art text-to-image diffusion models (e.g., unCLIP, Stable Diffusion) and multi-modal conditional generation methods. The experimental setup will use large batch sizes, probabilistic condition dropout, and classifier-free/bidirectional guidance for flexible conditioning.
26e5b933b8f60bd749d428b5ff813b2abcd765d8.novelty_claims: The proposal claims a novel compositional generation paradigm that enables exponentially large control spaces by allowing arbitrary combinations of visual conditions at inference. Unlike prior work, the method supports simultaneous conditioning on diverse representations (text, style, color, structure, region masks, etc.), providing fine-grained and region-specific control. The framework is general, supporting a wide range of classical and novel generative tasks without retraining, and introduces a unified approach to both global and localized conditioning. The method demonstrates zero-shot generalization to unseen combinations of conditions and enables new forms of image editing and synthesis not previously possible with existing models.

270a3a28be03293900aac529a517d2ef56aee0c2.title: How do Minimum-Norm Shallow Denoisers Look in Function Space?
