270a3a28be03293900aac529a517d2ef56aee0c2.research_question: What are the functional forms and generalization properties of minimum-norm (minimum representation cost) shallow ReLU neural network denoisers, particularly in the low-noise regime, and how do these solutions behave for both univariate and multivariate data under various geometric configurations of the training data?
270a3a28be03293900aac529a517d2ef56aee0c2.hypothesis: Minimum-norm shallow ReLU neural network denoisers exhibit contractive and structured interpolation properties that lead to better generalization than empirical MMSE estimators in the low-noise regime, and their functional forms can be explicitly characterized in both univariate and certain multivariate settings.
270a3a28be03293900aac529a517d2ef56aee0c2.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted to characterize the solutions of shallow (one-hidden-layer) ReLU neural network denoisers trained to interpolate noisy samples with minimal ℓ2-norm weights (representation cost), focusing on the low-noise regime where noisy clusters are well-separated. For univariate data, closed-form solutions for the minimum-norm denoiser will be derived and analyzed for contractivity and generalization. For multivariate data, the study will extend to cases where training samples lie in low-dimensional subspaces, unions of rays, or form simplexes, deriving closed-form or conjectured solutions under these geometric assumptions. The method will also involve analyzing the alignment of neural network weights with geometric structures in the data, and exploring the effect of regularization and the number of noisy samples on the learned function.
270a3a28be03293900aac529a517d2ef56aee0c2.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed on both synthetic and real datasets. For univariate settings, synthetic datasets with known clean points and controlled Gaussian noise will be used to compare the NN denoiser to the empirical MMSE (eMMSE) estimator, evaluating generalization via test MSE and visualizing the denoiser function. For multivariate settings, experiments will include synthetic configurations (e.g., points on rays, simplexes) and real image datasets such as MNIST and BSD68, with varying noise levels. Baselines will include eMMSE estimators and nearest-neighbor classifiers. Evaluation metrics will focus on test mean squared error (MSE), contractivity properties, and alignment of learned network weights with data geometry. Both online and offline training regimes will be considered, with and without explicit weight decay regularization, and the number of noisy samples per clean point will be varied to study its effect.
270a3a28be03293900aac529a517d2ef56aee0c2.novelty_claims: The proposal aims to provide the first explicit closed-form characterizations of minimum-norm shallow ReLU neural network denoisers in both univariate and several multivariate settings beyond trivial or co-linear cases. It introduces the concept of alignment phenomena, where the learned network decomposes into sums of rank-one piecewise linear interpolators aligned with edges or faces connecting training samples. The work also claims to theoretically demonstrate that minimum-norm NN denoisers generalize better than empirical MMSE estimators in the low-noise regime and to provide new insights into the contractive properties of such denoisers. Additionally, the approach enables a deeper understanding of the inductive bias of weight decay and minimal-norm solutions in neural denoising tasks.

270b95262f2100c279c4c65ef2521473841ca8ad.title: Dream to Control: Learning Behaviors by Latent Imagination
270b95262f2100c279c4c65ef2521473841ca8ad.research_question: How can reinforcement learning agents efficiently learn long-horizon behaviors from high-dimensional sensory inputs, such as images, by leveraging learned world models and latent imagination?
270b95262f2100c279c4c65ef2521473841ca8ad.hypothesis: Learning behaviors by propagating analytic gradients of multi-step value estimates through trajectories imagined in the latent space of a learned world model will enable more data-efficient, robust, and high-performing reinforcement learning agents for visual control tasks compared to existing model-based and model-free approaches.
270b95262f2100c279c4c65ef2521473841ca8ad.proposed_method: A novel reinforcement learning agent is proposed that operates entirely in the latent space of a learned world model. The method constructs a compact latent dynamics model consisting of a representation model, a transition model, and a reward model, all parameterized by neural networks. Behaviors are learned by predicting hypothetical trajectories in this latent space, where both actions and state values are optimized. An actor-critic algorithm is employed: the value model is trained for Bellman consistency on imagined rewards, while the action model is updated by backpropagating analytic gradients of value estimates through the neural network dynamics. The approach supports efficient parallel imagination of thousands of trajectories, and policy optimization is performed using reparameterization for continuous actions and straight-through gradients for discrete actions.
270b95262f2100c279c4c65ef2521473841ca8ad.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 20 challenging visual control tasks from the DeepMind Control Suite, covering a range of difficulties including sparse rewards, contact dynamics, high degrees of freedom, and 3D environments. The agent will be compared to strong baselines, including model-free (D4PG, A3C) and model-based (PlaNet) methods, using the same hyperparameters across all tasks. Evaluation metrics will include data-efficiency (performance per environment step), computation time, and final episodic return. Additional ablations will compare different representation learning objectives (pixel reconstruction, contrastive estimation, reward prediction) and the effect of imagination horizon. Implementation will utilize TensorFlow Probability on a single GPU and multiple CPU cores, with training time and resource usage tracked for comparison.
270b95262f2100c279c4c65ef2521473841ca8ad.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new actor-critic algorithm that learns behaviors purely by latent imagination, leveraging analytic gradients of multi-step value estimates through learned latent dynamics. This enables efficient, robust learning of long-horizon behaviors from high-dimensional observations. The method demonstrates superior data-efficiency, computation time, and final performance compared to state-of-the-art model-based and model-free agents. The framework is flexible to different representation learning objectives and is applicable to both continuous and discrete action spaces, as well as tasks with early termination.

2719cb215a2f1ee6fd271b1dea8dd51e69c20931.title: Monte Carlo guided Diffusion for Bayesian linear inverse problems
2719cb215a2f1ee6fd271b1dea8dd51e69c20931.research_question: How can Bayesian linear inverse problems be solved in a principled and consistent manner using modern generative priors, particularly denoising diffusion models, while enabling accurate uncertainty quantification and robust sampling from the true posterior distribution?
2719cb215a2f1ee6fd271b1dea8dd51e69c20931.hypothesis: Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) methods, when guided by the structure of score-based generative diffusion model priors, can be designed to consistently approximate the Bayesian posterior for linear inverse problems, outperforming existing diffusion-based conditional sampling techniques in both accuracy and theoretical guarantees.
2719cb215a2f1ee6fd271b1dea8dd51e69c20931.proposed_method: A novel algorithm, termed Monte Carlo Guided Diffusion (MCGdiff), is proposed to sample from the Bayesian posterior of linear inverse problems with Gaussian noise, using denoising diffusion generative model priors. The method constructs a sequence of intermediate linear inverse problems by exploiting the structure of the diffusion model prior, where the noise level is gradually decreased, causing the sequence of posteriors to approach the target posterior. At each step, an SMC sampler is employed to propagate a set of particles, using carefully designed proposal kernels and weight functions that incorporate both the backward dynamics of the diffusion model and the likelihood of the observed data. The approach is extended to handle general linear observation operators (via SVD-based basis transformation) and both noiseless and noisy observation regimes. Theoretical analysis provides non-asymptotic bounds on the bias and establishes convergence guarantees for the empirical distribution of the samples to the true posterior as the number of particles increases.
2719cb215a2f1ee6fd271b1dea8dd51e69c20931.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic tests use Gaussian Mixture (GM) and Funnel Mixture (FM) priors, with various dimensions and measurement models, where the true posterior is either analytically available or sampled via MCMC (NUTS). Competing baselines include DDRM, DPS, and RNVP, all using the same diffusion priors. Evaluation is performed using the sliced Wasserstein distance between samples from each method and the true posterior, with results averaged over multiple random seeds. For real-world imaging tasks, the method is applied to super-resolution, deblurring, and inpainting on datasets such as CIFAR-10, Flowers, Cats, Bedroom, Church, and CelebA-HQ. In these cases, 1000 samples are generated per method, and qualitative diversity is visualized. For all experiments, the number of SMC particles, diffusion steps, and other hyperparameters are systematically varied and reported.
2719cb215a2f1ee6fd271b1dea8dd51e69c20931.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to provide a provably consistent algorithm for conditional sampling from denoising diffusion model posteriors in general Bayesian linear inverse problems. The method leverages the structure of both the linear inverse problem and the diffusion prior to design an efficient and theoretically grounded SMC sampler. Unlike prior diffusion-based conditional sampling methods, this approach ensures that samples are consistent with the observed data and the true posterior, with explicit non-asymptotic bias bounds and convergence guarantees. The algorithm is versatile, handling both noiseless and noisy observations, as well as arbitrary linear operators, and demonstrates superior empirical performance compared to existing baselines.

272afc28d03890160b1f2808cc551c962ea9138c.title: ProofNet: Autoformalizing and Formally Proving Undergraduate-Level Mathematics
272afc28d03890160b1f2808cc551c962ea9138c.research_question: How can the automatic formalization and formal proving of undergraduate-level mathematics be advanced using large language models, and what benchmarks and methods are most effective for evaluating and improving these capabilities?
272afc28d03890160b1f2808cc551c962ea9138c.hypothesis: Large language models, when equipped with suitable training data and enhanced with novel techniques such as prompt retrieval and distilled backtranslation, can significantly improve the accuracy and reliability of autoformalization and formal proving of undergraduate-level mathematics compared to existing few-shot learning baselines.
272afc28d03890160b1f2808cc551c962ea9138c.proposed_method: A new benchmark, ProofNet, will be constructed to evaluate autoformalization and formal proving of undergraduate-level mathematics. ProofNet will consist of 371 parallel examples, each containing a formal theorem statement in Lean 3, a corresponding natural language theorem statement, and a natural language proof, sourced from widely used undergraduate mathematics textbooks. The methodology will include the development and open-sourcing of PROOFGPT language models, fine-tuned on a large mathematical text corpus ('proof-pile'), and the implementation of two novel autoformalization methods: prompt retrieval, which uses nearest-neighbor search in an embedding space to select the most relevant examples for in-context learning, and distilled backtranslation, which leverages synthetic parallel data generation for fine-tuning models without extensive parallel corpora. Evaluation will focus on the autoformalization and informalization of theorem statements, with human expert assessment for correctness and type-checking in Lean.
272afc28d03890160b1f2808cc551c962ea9138c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ProofNet benchmark, evaluating models on tasks such as autoformalization (natural language to Lean theorem statement) and informalization (Lean to natural language). The dataset covers a broad range of undergraduate mathematics topics, ensuring diversity and difficulty. Baseline comparisons will include in-context learning using OpenAI's Code-davinci-002 and the PROOFGPT models at 1.3B and 6.7B parameters. Evaluation metrics will include formalization accuracy (human-verified), typecheck rate (proportion of well-formed Lean statements), BLEU score, and compile rate for informalization. Additional experiments will assess the impact of prompt retrieval and distilled backtranslation on performance. The experimental setup will ensure no train-test overlap and will use human experts to judge semantic correctness where automatic verification is infeasible.
272afc28d03890160b1f2808cc551c962ea9138c.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces ProofNet, the first benchmark specifically targeting autoformalization and formal proving at the undergraduate mathematics level with parallel natural language and formal Lean data. It proposes two novel methods—prompt retrieval for context selection in in-context learning, and distilled backtranslation for generating synthetic training pairs without parallel data. The open-sourcing of PROOFGPT models fine-tuned for general mathematics is also claimed as a contribution. The benchmark and methods are designed to drive progress in autoformalization and theorem proving, addressing the lack of standard evaluation datasets and scalable training approaches in the field.

27332c540b16f454e4f37a043b4ce521433cbeb1.title: SAMPO:Scale-wise Autoregression with Motion PrOmpt for generative world models
27332c540b16f454e4f37a043b4ce521433cbeb1.research_question: How can generative world models be improved to achieve higher visual fidelity, temporal consistency, and efficient action-conditioned video prediction and control in complex, dynamic environments?
27332c540b16f454e4f37a043b4ce521433cbeb1.hypothesis: A hybrid scale-wise autoregressive framework that integrates temporal causal modeling, bidirectional spatial attention, asymmetric multi-scale tokenization, and trajectory-aware motion prompts will enhance the spatial and temporal coherence, efficiency, and generalization ability of generative world models for video prediction and model-based control.
27332c540b16f454e4f37a043b4ce521433cbeb1.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a hybrid scale-wise autoregressive framework for world modeling, termed SAMPO. This approach combines temporal autoregression across frames with coarse-to-fine spatial token generation within each frame, leveraging bidirectional spatial attention to preserve spatial locality and enable parallel decoding at each scale. An asymmetric multi-scale tokenizer based on vector quantization is employed: observed frames are densely tokenized to retain static and contextual details, while future frames are sparsely tokenized at coarser scales to focus on dynamic regions and reduce redundancy. Additionally, a trajectory-aware motion prompt module is incorporated, which extracts dynamic object and agent trajectories using a point-tracking model (e.g., CoTracker3), filters for salient motion, and overlays these as prompts to guide the model’s attention during generation. Actions are integrated via linear projection and concatenation with the token sequence, and temporal position embeddings are used to maintain temporal consistency.
27332c540b16f454e4f37a043b4ce521433cbeb1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several established benchmarks, including BAIR Robot Pushing, RoboNet, and 1X World Model for action-free and action-conditioned video prediction, as well as Robosuite and Meta-World for visual planning and model-based reinforcement learning. The evaluation will utilize metrics such as Fréchet Video Distance (FVD), PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS for perceptual quality, and task-specific success rates for planning and control. Baselines will include state-of-the-art masked modeling, diffusion-based, and autoregressive models (e.g., MaskViT, FitVid, MCVD, iVideoGPT). Ablation studies will isolate the contributions of the hybrid architecture, motion prompt, temporal embedding, and scaling. Zero-shot generalization will be assessed by pretraining on large-scale robot datasets and testing on unseen domains without fine-tuning. Inference speed and scalability will also be benchmarked.
27332c540b16f454e4f37a043b4ce521433cbeb1.novelty_claims: The proposed framework unifies temporal causal modeling and coarse-to-fine spatial autoregression with bidirectional attention, enabling efficient, scalable, and structurally coherent world modeling. The asymmetric multi-scale tokenizer is designed to balance spatial detail and dynamic modeling by differentiating between observed and future frames. The trajectory-aware motion prompt module introduces explicit spatiotemporal priors, improving the model’s ability to capture dynamic interactions and physical dependencies. The approach claims significant improvements in generation quality, temporal consistency, inference speed, and generalization over existing state-of-the-art methods in both video prediction and model-based control tasks.

2742460c702206fe19c0b5ceae97fef3499bdf76.title: Similarity of Neural Network Models: A Survey of Functional and Representational Measures
2742460c702206fe19c0b5ceae97fef3499bdf76.research_question: How can the similarity between neural network models be systematically and comprehensively measured from both functional and representational perspectives, and what are the properties, relationships, and practical implications of these similarity measures?
2742460c702206fe19c0b5ceae97fef3499bdf76.proposed_method: A unified framework will be developed to formally define and categorize similarity measures for neural network models, focusing on two complementary perspectives: representational similarity (comparing internal activations across layers) and functional similarity (comparing model outputs, particularly in classification tasks). The framework will systematically review, define, and analyze existing similarity measures, including canonical correlation analysis-based, alignment-based, representational similarity matrix-based, nearest neighbor-based, topology-based, and descriptive statistics-based approaches. Technical details such as invariance to transformations (e.g., permutations, orthogonal, affine), preprocessing requirements (e.g., centering, normalization), and metric properties will be rigorously examined. The relationships and distinctions between representational and functional similarity will be explored, and open challenges will be identified to guide future research.
2742460c702206fe19c0b5ceae97fef3499bdf76.experiment_details: A comprehensive survey and analytical comparison of similarity measures will be conducted using a variety of neural network architectures and datasets, primarily focusing on multi-class classification tasks. Benchmark datasets such as MNIST, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet will be used to extract activations and outputs from different models and layers. Baseline methods will include classical and recent similarity measures, with evaluation metrics including invariance properties, computational efficiency, interpretability, and alignment with functional performance (e.g., accuracy, robustness). Experimental setups will involve systematic preprocessing, dimensionality alignment, and statistical analysis to assess the practical applicability and robustness of each measure.
2742460c702206fe19c0b5ceae97fef3499bdf76.novelty_claims: The proposed research provides the first systematic and comprehensive review that unifies representational and functional similarity measures for neural network models. A formalized terminology and categorization of similarity measures will be introduced, enabling clearer understanding of their properties and relationships. The work will analyze practical considerations such as invariance, preprocessing, and metric properties, and will highlight unresolved challenges and research gaps, laying the groundwork for more systematic and interpretable comparison of neural network models.

274f0cee47c8a5bbc38c32de6787adee6a08f69e.title: On the Robustness of Safe Reinforcement Learning under Observational Perturbations
274f0cee47c8a5bbc38c32de6787adee6a08f69e.research_question: How can safe reinforcement learning policies be made robust to observational perturbations, such as adversarial attacks or sensor noise, while maintaining both task performance and safety constraint satisfaction? What are the vulnerabilities of current safe RL policies under such perturbations, and how can effective adversarial attackers and robust training methods be designed for this setting?
274f0cee47c8a5bbc38c32de6787adee6a08f69e.hypothesis: Safe reinforcement learning policies that are optimal in noise-free environments are vulnerable to carefully designed observational adversarial attacks, which can induce constraint violations even while maintaining high task rewards. Adversarial training with specifically designed attackers can improve the robustness and safety of RL policies under such perturbations.
274f0cee47c8a5bbc38c32de6787adee6a08f69e.proposed_method: A robust training framework for safe reinforcement learning is proposed, which incorporates adversarial observation perturbations during policy learning. Two novel adversarial attackers are designed: one that maximizes the cost (constraint violations) and another that maximizes the reward to induce stealthy, unsafe behaviors. The adversarial training objective is formulated as a constrained optimization problem, where the policy is optimized over trajectories corrupted by the strongest adversarial perturbations within a bounded set. The training procedure employs a primal-dual approach (e.g., Lagrangian methods), and the adversary is adaptively scheduled to increase perturbation strength over training epochs. The method leverages differentiable models for both the policy and value functions, allowing gradient-based optimization of adversarial observations.
274f0cee47c8a5bbc38c32de6787adee6a08f69e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on continuous control robot locomotion tasks (e.g., Car-Run, Drone-Run, Ant-Run, Car-Circle, Drone-Circle, Ant-Circle) from a public safe RL benchmark. Multiple robot types and tasks will be used to evaluate generality. Baseline comparisons will include vanilla safe RL (e.g., PPO-Lagrangian), naive adversarial training with random noise, state-adversarial algorithms using existing attackers (MAD, AMAD), and ablations with the proposed attackers. Evaluation metrics will include episode reward (task performance) and episode cost (constraint violations) under various adversarial attacks and perturbation magnitudes. Each policy will be evaluated over multiple seeds and episodes for statistical significance, and the same hyperparameters and model weights will be used for fair comparison.
274f0cee47c8a5bbc38c32de6787adee6a08f69e.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a formal analysis of policy vulnerability in safe RL under observational adversarial attacks, highlighting the unique challenge of constraint satisfaction versus reward maximization. Two new adversarial attack algorithms are developed—one maximizing cost and one maximizing reward—demonstrating that maximizing reward can be a strong and stealthy attack in the safe RL setting. A robust adversarial training framework is proposed, theoretically justified via Bellman contraction properties, and shown to outperform existing robust RL techniques in terms of safety and robustness. The approach is generalizable to various safe RL algorithms and reveals previously unrecognized vulnerabilities in safe RL policies.

2755f27185eda96cd9ab066e08659a5dfbd1639a.title: Faster Fixed-Point Methods for Multichain MDPs
2755f27185eda96cd9ab066e08659a5dfbd1639a.research_question: How can value-iteration algorithms for general (multichain) Markov decision processes (MDPs) under the average-reward criterion be designed to achieve faster convergence rates and sharper complexity measures, particularly by better addressing the navigation subproblem inherent in multichain settings?
2755f27185eda96cd9ab066e08659a5dfbd1639a.hypothesis: By introducing refined complexity measures and leveraging novel connections between average-reward and discounted MDPs, as well as developing new fixed-point methods and suboptimality decompositions, it is possible to design value-iteration algorithms that achieve improved and sometimes optimal convergence rates for multichain MDPs, outperforming existing approaches especially in handling the navigation subproblem.
2755f27185eda96cd9ab066e08659a5dfbd1639a.proposed_method: The proposed methodology develops new value-iteration algorithms for multichain average-reward MDPs by introducing sharper complexity parameters that directly capture the difficulty of the navigation subproblem. The approach includes a coupling-based analysis leveraging restricted commutativity properties of the Bellman operator, enabling the design of an 'Approximately Shifted Halpern Iteration' algorithm that splits computation into gain estimation and fixed-point refinement phases. Additionally, the method introduces a reduction from average-reward to discounted MDPs, allowing the use of discounted value iteration with a novel initialization (warm-start) strategy to rapidly reduce value error. A new 'Halpern-Then-Picard' algorithm is proposed for discounted fixed-point problems, which first applies Halpern iteration for a number of steps proportional to the effective horizon, then switches to Picard iteration, achieving optimal fixed-point error rates in Banach spaces. Theoretical analysis provides new sublinear convergence rates and refined suboptimality bounds that depend on the newly defined gain-dropping time and other structural parameters of the MDP.
2755f27185eda96cd9ab066e08659a5dfbd1639a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic and standard benchmark MDPs, including both weakly communicating and general multichain instances, to evaluate the convergence rates and suboptimality bounds of the proposed algorithms. Baseline comparisons will include prior value-iteration methods for average-reward MDPs, such as those based on Halpern iteration and discounted reductions, as well as classical value iteration and policy iteration. Evaluation metrics will include the maximum suboptimality gap (infinity norm of gain difference), convergence rate to optimal gain, and computational complexity in terms of iteration count and dependence on structural parameters (such as gain-dropping time and span seminorms). Experimental setups will vary the complexity of the navigation subproblem and the size of the MDP to test the robustness and scalability of the proposed methods.
2755f27185eda96cd9ab066e08659a5dfbd1639a.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces several innovations: (1) a refined complexity measure (gain-dropping time) that more sharply characterizes the difficulty of the navigation subproblem in multichain MDPs; (2) new algorithms for value iteration that achieve improved and sometimes optimal nonasymptotic convergence rates, including in settings where previous bounds were vacuous or overly pessimistic; (3) a novel reduction from average-reward to discounted MDPs that enables faster convergence via discounted value iteration with warm-start initialization; (4) the first optimal fixed-point error convergence rates for discounted value iteration in general Banach spaces; and (5) new suboptimality decompositions and theoretical insights that advance the understanding of value-iteration methods for general MDPs.

277dd73bfeb5c46513ce305136b0e71fcd2a311c.title: Recipe for a General, Powerful, Scalable Graph Transformer
277dd73bfeb5c46513ce305136b0e71fcd2a311c.research_question: How can a general, powerful, and scalable graph Transformer architecture be designed to efficiently handle both small and large graphs, while achieving state-of-the-art performance across diverse graph learning benchmarks?
277dd73bfeb5c46513ce305136b0e71fcd2a311c.hypothesis: A hybrid architecture that combines modular positional and structural encodings, local message-passing mechanisms, and scalable global attention layers can achieve high expressivity, efficiency, and scalability for graph representation learning, outperforming existing graph Transformer models on a wide range of benchmarks.
277dd73bfeb5c46513ce305136b0e71fcd2a311c.proposed_method: A modular graph Transformer architecture is proposed, termed GPS (General, Powerful, Scalable), which integrates three main components: (i) flexible positional and structural encodings (PE/SE) categorized as local, global, or relative, (ii) a local message-passing neural network (MPNN) layer for neighborhood aggregation, and (iii) a global attention mechanism based on linear-complexity Transformers such as Performer or BigBird. At each layer, node and edge features are updated by aggregating the outputs of the MPNN and the global attention layer, followed by a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) and residual connections. Edge features are incorporated only in the MPNN, while the global attention operates solely on node features, enabling linear scaling with the number of nodes and edges. The framework is highly modular, allowing drop-in replacement of PE/SE schemes, MPNN types, and attention mechanisms, and is implemented in an extensible software package (GRAPHGPS) for ease of experimentation and future research.
277dd73bfeb5c46513ce305136b0e71fcd2a311c.experiment_details: A comprehensive set of experiments is conducted on 16 benchmark datasets, including those from Benchmarking-GNNs (ZINC, MNIST, CIFAR10, PATTERN, CLUSTER), Open Graph Benchmark (ogbg-molhiv, ogbg-molpcba, ogbg-code2, ogbg-ppa, PCQM4Mv2), MalNet-Tiny, and the Long-Range Graph Benchmark (PascalVOC-SP, COCO-SP, Peptides-func, Peptides-struct, PCQM-Contact). Ablation studies systematically evaluate the contributions of the message-passing module, global attention module, and various PE/SE schemes. Baselines include popular message-passing GNNs (GCN, GIN, GatedGCN, PNA), recent graph Transformers (SAN, Graphormer, EGT), and other state-of-the-art models. Evaluation metrics vary by task and include MAE, accuracy, AUROC, average precision, F1 score, and mean reciprocal rank. Experimental setups ensure comparable parameter budgets and consistent hyperparameter tuning across models.
277dd73bfeb5c46513ce305136b0e71fcd2a311c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first graph Transformer architecture with linear complexity in the number of nodes and edges, enabling scalability to graphs with several thousand nodes. It establishes a unified, modular framework for integrating diverse positional and structural encodings at local, global, and relative levels, and decouples local message-passing from global attention to avoid expressivity bottlenecks. The method demonstrates universal function approximation capabilities on graphs and achieves state-of-the-art or highly competitive results across a wide range of benchmarks, surpassing previous graph Transformer models in both performance and scalability. The open-source implementation further facilitates reproducibility and future research in efficient and expressive graph Transformers.

278b08cab626c2795415ce2ba4f766ec96d2e247.title: Efficient Length-Generalizable Attention via Causal Retrieval for Long-Context Language Modeling
278b08cab626c2795415ce2ba4f766ec96d2e247.research_question: How can attention mechanisms in large language models be designed to efficiently generalize to much longer contexts than seen during training, while maintaining the ability to access and utilize distant information with manageable computational and memory costs?
278b08cab626c2795415ce2ba4f766ec96d2e247.hypothesis: An attention mechanism that enables learnable, end-to-end chunk retrieval—where relevance scores directly participate in next-token prediction—will allow language models to generalize to contexts orders of magnitude longer than those seen during training, while maintaining efficient random access to long-range information and reducing computational and memory overhead.
278b08cab626c2795415ce2ba4f766ec96d2e247.proposed_method: A novel attention mechanism, Grouped Cross-Attention (GCA), will be developed to enable efficient, length-generalizable attention for long-context language modeling. The input sequence will be divided into fixed-size chunks, and for each chunk, a learnable retriever will select the top-k most relevant past chunks based on differentiable relevance scores. These scores will be used as soft weights to fuse information from the retrieved chunks into the current chunk's representation, allowing gradients from the autoregressive loss to flow through the retrieval process. GCA will be integrated into a Transformer-based architecture (Differentiable Retrieval-based Transformer, DRT), with upper layers grouped to allow multiple retrievals and chunk-wise fusion. The method will employ Gumbel Top-k sampling to balance exploration and exploitation during training, and hardware-aware implementation (e.g., Triton) will be used for efficiency. Memory offloading strategies will be incorporated to further reduce GPU memory usage during inference.
278b08cab626c2795415ce2ba4f766ec96d2e247.experiment_details: Comprehensive experiments will be conducted on long-range language modeling benchmarks such as PG19 and arXiv-math, with models pre-trained from scratch using context lengths up to 16K tokens and evaluated on sequences up to 16M tokens (1000× the training length). Baselines will include sliding window Transformers, Retrieval-Pretrained Transformer (RPT), Landmark Attention, Block-Recurrent Transformers, and strong base LMs with comparable parameter counts and attention fields. Evaluation metrics will include perplexity for language modeling, ROUGE scores for summarization tasks (XSum, CNN/DailyMail), and accuracy on needle-in-a-haystack (NIAH) retrieval tests. Ablation studies will assess the impact of key components such as Gumbel Top-k, retriever learning, and hardware optimizations. Inference speed, memory footprint, and training throughput will be measured across a range of model sizes and context lengths.
278b08cab626c2795415ce2ba4f766ec96d2e247.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces Grouped Cross-Attention (GCA), the first attention mechanism to achieve near-perfect retrieval accuracy at context lengths 1000× longer than training, while maintaining constant attention window size and efficient random access. The method enables end-to-end, learnable chunk retrieval where relevance scores directly affect next-token prediction, overcoming the limitations of previous retrieval-based models that rely on fixed or separately trained retrievers. The approach achieves linear complexity with respect to input length, supports efficient memory offloading, and demonstrates superior extrapolation and efficiency compared to state-of-the-art baselines. The integration of GCA into Transformer architectures establishes a new paradigm for long-context language modeling.

278c3a34371b8f56ff92552b923e7a39a228ed17.title: Asymptotic theory of in-context learning by linear attention
278c3a34371b8f56ff92552b923e7a39a228ed17.research_question: What are the fundamental conditions and scaling laws governing the emergence of in-context learning (ICL) in attention-based neural architectures, specifically in terms of sample complexity, pretraining task diversity, and context length, for linear regression tasks?
278c3a34371b8f56ff92552b923e7a39a228ed17.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that there exist precise scaling regimes for input dimension, pretraining dataset size, context length, and task diversity under which linear attention modules transition from memorization to genuine in-context learning, and that these regimes can be characterized analytically using asymptotic theory.
278c3a34371b8f56ff92552b923e7a39a228ed17.proposed_method: A simplified model of in-context learning will be developed using a linear self-attention module tailored for linear regression tasks. The model will be parameterized such that pretraining can be performed via ridge regression, enabling analytical tractability. Theoretical analysis will be conducted in a joint asymptotic limit where the input dimension, number of pretraining samples, context length, and number of unique task vectors all scale together, with context length and task diversity scaling linearly with input dimension and pretraining sample size scaling quadratically. Random matrix theory will be employed to derive sharp asymptotic expressions for the generalization error of the model, distinguishing between in-context learning (ICL) and in-distribution generalization (IDG) tasks. Theoretical predictions will be validated through numerical simulations and compared to full nonlinear Transformer architectures.
278c3a34371b8f56ff92552b923e7a39a228ed17.experiment_details: Experiments will involve pretraining the linear attention model on synthetic datasets generated according to the specified linear regression task, with Gaussian-distributed inputs and task vectors, and varying levels of noise. The pretraining dataset size, context length, and task diversity will be systematically varied according to the scaling laws identified in the theoretical analysis. Baseline comparisons will include Bayes-optimal within-context estimators such as ridge regression and discrete minimum mean squared error (dMMSE) estimators. Evaluation metrics will focus on mean squared error (MSE) for both ICL (generalization to novel tasks) and IDG (memorization of training tasks). Additional experiments will be conducted on full Transformer models with softmax attention to assess the transferability of theoretical insights from the linear model.
278c3a34371b8f56ff92552b923e7a39a228ed17.novelty_claims: The proposed research provides the first asymptotically precise theory of in-context learning for linear regression using linear attention, identifying exact scaling laws for sample complexity, context length, and task diversity. The analysis reveals a double-descent phenomenon in generalization error as a function of pretraining dataset size and uncovers a phase transition from memorization to true in-context learning as task diversity increases. Theoretical results are supported by numerical experiments and shown to transfer to full nonlinear Transformer architectures, offering new insights into the mechanisms underlying in-context learning in large-scale models.

2797cbda8c845504119b62ee25deb1500ec2dfaf.title: DeepSeek-Coder-V2: Breaking the Barrier of Closed-Source Models in Code Intelligence
2797cbda8c845504119b62ee25deb1500ec2dfaf.research_question: How can open-source large language models for code intelligence be advanced to achieve or surpass the performance of state-of-the-art closed-source models in code generation, mathematical reasoning, and general language tasks, while supporting a broad range of programming languages and long-context scenarios?
2797cbda8c845504119b62ee25deb1500ec2dfaf.hypothesis: Continued pre-training of a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) code language model on a large, diverse, and high-quality multi-domain corpus—including code, mathematics, and natural language—combined with advanced alignment strategies and long-context extension, will enable open-source models to match or exceed the performance of leading closed-source models in code intelligence tasks.
2797cbda8c845504119b62ee25deb1500ec2dfaf.proposed_method: A Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) transformer-based code language model will be developed, leveraging both 16B and 236B parameter configurations with efficient activation (2.4B and 21B active parameters, respectively). The model will be initialized from an intermediate checkpoint of a strong generalist language model and further pre-trained on an additional 6 trillion tokens, comprising 60% source code (spanning 338 programming languages), 10% mathematical content, and 30% natural language. Data collection will employ rigorous filtering, deduplication, and domain-specific crawling from sources such as GitHub and Common Crawl, with iterative expansion using fastText and BPE tokenization for multilingual support. Pre-training objectives will include next-token prediction and, for the 16B model, Fill-In-the-Middle (FIM) with Prefix-Suffix-Middle (PSM) mode at a 0.5 rate. The model’s context window will be extended to 128K tokens using the YARN method, with staged training to enhance long-context capabilities. Alignment will be achieved through supervised fine-tuning on a mixed instruction dataset (code, math, and general instructions), followed by reinforcement learning using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and a reward model trained on compiler/test-case feedback.
2797cbda8c845504119b62ee25deb1500ec2dfaf.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate the model on a comprehensive suite of benchmarks covering code generation (HumanEval, MBPP+, LiveCodeBench, SWE-Bench, RepoBench), mathematical reasoning (MATH, GSM8K, AIME, Math Odyssey), and general language understanding (MMLU, MT-Bench, AlignBench). Multilingual code generation will be assessed across 338 programming languages. Baselines will include both leading open-source models (CodeLlama, StarCoder, Codestral, Llama3) and closed-source models (GPT-4-Turbo, Claude 3 Opus, Gemini 1.5 Pro, GPT-4o). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, exact match, and subjective human preference scores, with standardized evaluation pipelines (e.g., EvalPlus for MBPP+). Ablation studies will be conducted to validate data quality and training strategies, and long-context performance will be assessed using the Needle In A Haystack (NIAH) test. Fill-in-the-middle and repository-level code completion will be evaluated using Single-Line Infilling and RepoBench, respectively.
2797cbda8c845504119b62ee25deb1500ec2dfaf.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first open-source hundred-billion-parameter code model with Mixture-of-Experts architecture, supporting 338 programming languages and a 128K token context window. It pioneers large-scale, high-quality multi-domain pre-training for code intelligence and demonstrates, for the first time, open-source performance that matches or surpasses leading closed-source models in both code and math tasks. The model is released under a permissive license, enabling unrestricted research and commercial use. Key innovations include advanced data collection/filtering, long-context extension via YARN, and efficient RL-based alignment with a robust reward model.

27a91bdc94493dd0a756f67460ea162d1419fc95.title: f-Divergence Based Classification: Beyond the Use of Cross-Entropy
27a91bdc94493dd0a756f67460ea162d1419fc95.research_question: How can classification tasks be formulated and solved using a broader class of objective functions based on f-divergences, moving beyond the conventional cross-entropy approach, and what are the implications for classification accuracy and posterior probability estimation in various domains?
27a91bdc94493dd0a756f67460ea162d1419fc95.hypothesis: A class of objective functions derived from the variational representation of f-divergences, including a novel shifted log (SL) divergence, will enable more effective posterior probability estimation and lead to improved or at least competitive classification accuracy compared to cross-entropy minimization across a range of tasks and datasets.
27a91bdc94493dd0a756f67460ea162d1419fc95.proposed_method: The proposed methodology formulates classification as a maximum a posteriori (MAP) probability problem from a Bayesian perspective, where the posterior probability is estimated via density ratio learning using neural networks. Two main approaches are developed: one leverages the variational representation of f-divergences to define a family of objective functions for training discriminators, and the other introduces a bottom-up method that guides the design of new objective functions by imposing optimal convergence conditions on the discriminator’s output. A novel objective function corresponding to the shifted log (SL) divergence is introduced and theoretically analyzed. Both unsupervised (for continuous random variables) and supervised (for discrete class sets) neural network architectures are designed to estimate the posterior, with the supervised version outputting class probabilities directly. The approach enables single-stage maximization-based training, avoiding the need for dual optimization (min-max or max-max) required by some prior f-divergence-based methods.
27a91bdc94493dd0a756f67460ea162d1419fc95.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on several benchmark image classification datasets (MNIST, FashionMNIST, CIFAR10, CIFAR100) using a variety of neural network architectures (TinyNet, VGG, DLA, ResNet, MobileNetV2), where each network is trained with different objective functions derived from f-divergences (KL, reverse KL, squared Hellinger, GAN, Pearson χ2, and the proposed SL divergence). Evaluation metrics include classification accuracy (mean and standard deviation over multiple seeds). Additional scenarios include signal decoding tasks in telecommunications (e.g., 4-PAM over nonlinear channels) where symbol error rate (SER) is measured, and toy examples for continuous posterior estimation (Exponential and Gaussian models) where the estimated posterior is compared to the closed-form solution. Training utilizes standard optimizers (SGD, Adam), data augmentation, and dropout where appropriate, with hyperparameters tuned for each dataset and architecture.
27a91bdc94493dd0a756f67460ea162d1419fc95.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a general framework for classification based on the variational representation of f-divergences, extending beyond cross-entropy. A new shifted log (SL) divergence and its corresponding objective function are developed, shown both theoretically and empirically to achieve superior or competitive classification accuracy in most tested scenarios. The approach provides a single-stage training formulation for posterior estimation, generalizes to both discrete and continuous settings, and demonstrates that cross-entropy is not always the optimal choice for classification. The method also offers insights into the design of objective functions and their impact on training dynamics and convergence.

27ae70f2de4e7c4080a45925452f6382edde7890.title: Breaking the Curse of Multiagency: Provably Efficient Decentralized Multi-Agent RL with Function Approximation
27ae70f2de4e7c4080a45925452f6382edde7890.research_question: Can decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithms be developed that efficiently overcome the curse of multiagency, even in environments with large or infinite state spaces requiring function approximation?
27ae70f2de4e7c4080a45925452f6382edde7890.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that decentralized MARL algorithms utilizing novel policy replay mechanisms and function approximation can achieve polynomial sample complexity in the number of agents and other problem parameters, thereby breaking the curse of multiagency in both linear and general function approximation settings.
27ae70f2de4e7c4080a45925452f6382edde7890.proposed_method: A new decentralized meta-algorithm, V-Learning with Policy Replay (VLPR), will be developed, integrating the standard V-Learning framework with a policy replay mechanism to facilitate learning under function approximation. The algorithm will iteratively update policies by uniformly mixing previously learned policies, and at each stage, will compute approximate Coarse Correlated Equilibria (CCEs) and value functions using specialized subroutines. An accelerated version, AVLPR, will be introduced to improve sample complexity by employing infrequent policy updates via a doubling trick. Additionally, an alternative approach, Decentralized Optimistic Policy Mirror Descent (DOPMD), will be designed to learn policy-class-restricted CCEs under more general function approximation, leveraging optimistic value estimation and mirror descent in policy space. All algorithms will be constructed to allow fully decentralized execution, requiring minimal or no inter-agent communication.
27ae70f2de4e7c4080a45925452f6382edde7890.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and benchmark multi-agent Markov games, including settings with tabular and linear function approximation, as well as more general function classes with bounded Bellman-Eluder dimension. The algorithms will be evaluated on their ability to find approximate Markov CCEs, with sample complexity measured in terms of the number of episodes required to achieve a specified approximation error ε. Baselines will include existing decentralized and centralized MARL algorithms, such as V-Learning and SPoCMAR, with comparisons focused on sample efficiency, scalability with the number of agents, and dependence on state/action space size. Evaluation metrics will include CCE gap, convergence rate, and computational efficiency, with ablation studies to assess the impact of policy replay and function approximation choices.
27ae70f2de4e7c4080a45925452f6382edde7890.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first provably efficient decentralized MARL algorithms that break the curse of multiagency under function approximation, achieving polynomial sample complexity in the number of agents and other parameters. The VLPR and AVLPR frameworks generalize prior tabular MARL approaches to settings with large or infinite state spaces, and the accelerated version achieves optimal statistical rates in ε. The DOPMD algorithm extends applicability to a wider range of problems with general function approximation and bounded Bellman-Eluder dimension. In the tabular setting, the approach improves upon the best known sample complexity for decentralized Markov CCE learning. The methods are fully decentralized and require minimal communication, making them practical for large-scale multi-agent systems.

27b1d59859621b2b8a095802ca24b9d93e676f07.title: Prior-Guided Diffusion Planning for Offline Reinforcement Learning
27b1d59859621b2b8a095802ca24b9d93e676f07.research_question: How can offline reinforcement learning planners based on diffusion models be improved to generate high-value, generalizable trajectories efficiently, while mitigating issues such as distributional drift, suboptimal multi-modal actions, and high inference-time computational costs?
27b1d59859621b2b8a095802ca24b9d93e676f07.hypothesis: A learnable, behavior-regularized prior distribution, when used to guide diffusion-based planners in offline reinforcement learning, will enable efficient generation of high-value trajectories, reduce computational overhead, and improve performance over existing guided sampling strategies and planners.
27b1d59859621b2b8a095802ca24b9d93e676f07.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a guided sampling framework for diffusion-based planners in offline reinforcement learning by replacing the standard Gaussian prior with a learnable, parameterized prior distribution. This prior is optimized using a behavior-regularized objective that encourages the sampling of high-value trajectories while maintaining proximity to the behavior distribution. The approach leverages a latent-space value function, trained to approximate the value of denoised trajectories directly in the latent space, thereby avoiding costly backpropagation through the iterative denoising process. The prior is parameterized using a recurrent neural network (GRU) that outputs the parameters of a Gaussian (or Gaussian mixture) distribution conditioned on the current state, and the denoising operator learned via behavior cloning remains fixed during prior optimization. Training alternates between updating the latent value function and optimizing the prior, enabling closed-form behavior regularization and efficient computation.
27b1d59859621b2b8a095802ca24b9d93e676f07.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the D4RL offline RL benchmark suite, covering diverse domains such as MuJoCo, Kitchen, Antmaze, and Maze2D, with various dataset types (e.g., medium, replay, expert, mixed, partial, play, diverse, large, ummaze). The proposed method will be compared against a comprehensive set of baselines, including Gaussian policy methods (e.g., CQL, IQL), diffusion policies (e.g., SfBC, DQL, IDQL, QGPO, SRPO), and diffusion planners (e.g., Diffuser, AD, DD, HD, DV). Evaluation metrics will include normalized scores on benchmark tasks, training and inference time, and analysis of out-of-distribution action selection. Ablation studies will examine the impact of different regularization functions, regularization coefficients, and prior parameterizations (uni-modal vs. multi-modal Gaussian). Visualization and correlation analysis will be performed to assess the quality of the learned latent value function and the expressiveness of the learned prior.
27b1d59859621b2b8a095802ca24b9d93e676f07.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel method for guiding diffusion-based planners in offline RL by learning a behavior-regularized prior, enabling efficient and direct generation of high-value trajectories without the need for costly inference-time sampling or backpropagation through the denoising process. The method provides analytically tractable and stable behavior regularization in the latent space, which was previously infeasible due to intractable output densities of diffusion models. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on long-horizon offline RL tasks, improved computational efficiency, and reduced risk of out-of-distribution action selection compared to existing methods.

27c741e54cedfc7e648103f90b109dd58143fd34.title: VisionThink: Smart and Efficient Vision Language Model via Reinforcement Learning
27c741e54cedfc7e648103f90b109dd58143fd34.research_question: How can vision-language models dynamically and efficiently process visual inputs of varying complexity while maintaining high performance across both general and detail-sensitive (e.g., OCR-related) visual question answering tasks?
27c741e54cedfc7e648103f90b109dd58143fd34.hypothesis: A vision-language model that autonomously determines the necessary image resolution for each input, guided by reinforcement learning and an LLM-based evaluation strategy, will achieve greater computational efficiency without sacrificing accuracy, particularly by preserving performance on tasks requiring fine-grained visual details.
27c741e54cedfc7e648103f90b109dd58143fd34.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed in which the vision-language model first processes a downsampled (low-resolution) version of the input image to minimize computational cost. The model will be trained to smartly decide, on a per-sample basis, whether the available information is sufficient to answer the question; if not, it will output a special token to request the original high-resolution image and reattempt the answer. Reinforcement learning, specifically Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), will be employed to optimize this decision process, using a reward function that balances answer accuracy, output format compliance, and penalties for unnecessary high-resolution requests. An external large language model (LLM) will serve as a semantic judge to evaluate the correctness of generated answers in a flexible, human-aligned manner, enabling effective RL training even for open-ended VQA tasks. The training data will be curated to include both cases solvable at low resolution and those requiring high resolution, supporting robust learning of the resolution selection policy.
27c741e54cedfc7e648103f90b109dd58143fd34.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of general and OCR-related VQA benchmarks, including ChartQA, OCRBench, MathVista, MMVet, RealWorldQA, and MathVerse. The proposed method will be implemented on top of the Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct model, with training performed using the veRL framework and multi-turn GRPO. Baselines will include state-of-the-art open-source and closed-source VLMs, as well as previous efficient VLM methods such as FastV and SparseVLM, which use fixed visual token pruning ratios. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on VQA tasks, inference time, and the proportion of visual tokens retained. Comparative studies will assess both performance and efficiency, with particular attention to the model’s ability to preserve accuracy on detail-sensitive tasks while reducing computation on simpler queries.
27c741e54cedfc7e648103f90b109dd58143fd34.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new paradigm for visual token compression by enabling dynamic, sample-specific resolution selection rather than relying on fixed pruning ratios. The method leverages reinforcement learning with an LLM-as-Judge strategy to generalize efficient reasoning to open-ended VQA tasks, overcoming limitations of rule-based RL in diverse scenarios. A carefully designed reward and penalty mechanism ensures stable and balanced decision-making between efficiency and performance. The framework is compatible with existing efficient VLM techniques and demonstrates superior efficiency and accuracy, particularly on tasks requiring fine-grained visual understanding.

27f7aa77bf343fefd3984c6b23265af672bcc0a3.title: Attribution Patching Outperforms Automated Circuit Discovery
27f7aa77bf343fefd3984c6b23265af672bcc0a3.research_question: How can automated interpretability methods be improved to efficiently and accurately identify the computational subgraphs (circuits) responsible for specific behaviors in large neural language models?
27f7aa77bf343fefd3984c6b23265af672bcc0a3.hypothesis: A method based on attribution patching can outperform existing automated circuit discovery techniques in both accuracy and computational efficiency for identifying relevant circuits in neural networks.
27f7aa77bf343fefd3984c6b23265af672bcc0a3.proposed_method: A new approach, Edge Attribution Patching (EAP), is developed to identify important edges in the computational graph of a language model for a given task. The method estimates the importance of each edge by applying a linear approximation to the effect of corrupting that edge, using only two forward passes and a single backward pass to compute attribution scores for all edges simultaneously. The absolute value of the attribution score, derived from a first-order Taylor expansion of the task-specific metric with respect to each edge's activation, is used to rank edges by importance. The network is then pruned by retaining only the top-k edges with the highest attribution scores, forming a subgraph hypothesized to be responsible for the target behavior. This process is designed to be highly efficient compared to traditional activation patching, which requires a separate forward pass per edge.
27f7aa77bf343fefd3984c6b23265af672bcc0a3.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on several mechanistic interpretability benchmarks, including the Indirect Object Identification (IOI), Docstring, and Greater-Than tasks, using GPT-2 small models. The proposed EAP method is compared against existing automated circuit discovery methods such as ACDC (with both task-specific and KL divergence metrics) and, where computationally feasible, repeated activation patching. Evaluation is performed by measuring the area under the ROC curve (AUC) for circuit recovery, using previously identified human-labeled circuits as ground truth. The experiments also analyze the distribution of attribution scores for edges inside and outside the ground truth circuits and investigate the faithfulness of the linear approximation used in EAP.
27f7aa77bf343fefd3984c6b23265af672bcc0a3.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces Edge Attribution Patching, which enables efficient and scalable automated circuit discovery by leveraging a linear approximation for edge importance, requiring only a constant number of forward and backward passes regardless of model size. EAP is shown to outperform all previous automated circuit discovery methods in terms of circuit recovery accuracy and computational efficiency. The approach also provides a practical framework for combining EAP with existing methods, such as running ACDC on the subgraph pruned by EAP, to further refine circuit identification.

2804e9eff062efaedeca87724ebbabeeffa36522.title: Your diffusion model secretly knows the dimension of the data manifold
2804e9eff062efaedeca87724ebbabeeffa36522.research_question: How can the intrinsic dimension of a data manifold be estimated using information available from a trained diffusion model, and how does this approach compare to established statistical estimators across various types of data?
2804e9eff062efaedeca87724ebbabeeffa36522.hypothesis: A trained diffusion model implicitly encodes information about the intrinsic dimension of the data manifold, and this information can be extracted to provide accurate and robust estimates of manifold dimension, outperforming traditional statistical estimators, especially in high-dimensional and nonlinear settings.
2804e9eff062efaedeca87724ebbabeeffa36522.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves training a diffusion model on the dataset of interest, where the model learns to approximate the score function (the gradient of the log-density of noise-corrupted data) across varying levels of corruption. For a given data point, a set of nearby points is sampled by adding small Gaussian noise, and the score vectors at these points are computed using the trained diffusion model at a small diffusion time. These score vectors are assembled into a matrix, and singular value decomposition (SVD) is performed to analyze the spectrum. The number of vanishing singular values corresponds to the dimension of the tangent space, allowing estimation of the intrinsic dimension as the ambient dimension minus the number of significant singular values. This process is repeated for multiple points to obtain robust estimates, and the method is designed to handle both linear and highly nonlinear manifolds.
2804e9eff062efaedeca87724ebbabeeffa36522.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic Euclidean manifolds (such as k-spheres and non-linear curves embedded in high-dimensional spaces) and synthetic image manifolds with known intrinsic dimensions, as well as on real-world datasets like MNIST where the true dimension is unknown. For each dataset, a diffusion model will be trained, and the proposed dimension estimation method will be applied. Baselines for comparison will include nearest neighbor-based maximum likelihood estimators (MLE), local PCA, and probabilistic PCA (PPCA). Evaluation metrics will include the accuracy of estimated intrinsic dimension (compared to ground truth when available), and for datasets like MNIST, alignment with the point of diminishing returns in auto-encoder reconstruction error curves. Experimental setup details, such as the number of sampled points, diffusion times, and model architectures, will be specified and controlled for reproducibility.
2804e9eff062efaedeca87724ebbabeeffa36522.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first method for estimating the intrinsic dimension of a data manifold using diffusion models, leveraging the geometric properties of the learned score field at small diffusion times. The approach is theoretically justified and empirically shown to outperform established statistical estimators, particularly in high-dimensional and nonlinear settings. The method is robust to score approximation errors and data non-uniformity, and it provides local dimension estimates, enabling analysis of unions of manifolds with varying dimensions. The work opens new avenues for understanding and quantifying data complexity in modern machine learning datasets.

281a7a99c16ce8f53bfbfb7aeb460dbd28648d28.title: Toxicity in ChatGPT: Analyzing Persona-assigned Language Models
281a7a99c16ce8f53bfbfb7aeb460dbd28648d28.research_question: How does assigning different personas to large language models affect the toxicity and bias of their generated outputs, particularly in dialogue settings, and what are the implications for safety and fairness in real-world applications?
281a7a99c16ce8f53bfbfb7aeb460dbd28648d28.hypothesis: Assigning specific personas to large language models significantly increases the toxicity and discriminatory bias in their generated outputs, with the degree of toxicity and bias varying depending on both the persona and the target entity.
281a7a99c16ce8f53bfbfb7aeb460dbd28648d28.proposed_method: A comprehensive large-scale evaluation will be conducted to systematically measure the toxicity and bias in outputs generated by a dialogue-based large language model when assigned a variety of personas using the system-level parameter. Ninety diverse personas will be curated, including historical figures, politicians, journalists, businesspersons, sportspersons, and baseline character types, ensuring balance across gender, political affiliation, and nationality. The model will be prompted to generate responses about 123 entities (covering gender, race, religion, country, profession, sexual orientation, and more) and to complete 2,000 stratified prompts from the REALTOXICITYPROMPTS dataset. Multiple prompt templates (e.g., neutral, positive, negative) will be used to assess the impact of prompt style on toxicity. For each persona-entity and persona-prompt pair, multiple generations will be sampled using nucleus sampling (top-p=0.9, temperature=1, frequency penalty=0.02), and the toxicity of each output will be measured using the Perspective API.
281a7a99c16ce8f53bfbfb7aeb460dbd28648d28.experiment_details: The experimental setup involves generating over 500,000 outputs from the language model (gpt-3.5-turbo via the ChatGPT API, as of March 2023) across all combinations of 90 personas and 123 entities, as well as continuations for 2,000 prompts from the REALTOXICITYPROMPTS dataset. For each persona-entity pair, five generations will be sampled; for each persona-prompt pair, one generation will be sampled. Toxicity will be evaluated using the Perspective API, reporting both the maximum and average toxicity per set. Additionally, a new metric, Probability of Responding (POR), will be introduced to measure the likelihood that the model responds to prompts intended to elicit toxic behavior. Statistical significance of differences in toxicity will be assessed using unpaired t-tests with a significance level of 0.05. Baseline personas (e.g., 'a good person', 'a bad person') and various prompt styles will be included to control for prompt sensitivity.
281a7a99c16ce8f53bfbfb7aeb460dbd28648d28.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first large-scale, systematic analysis of persona-assigned toxicity in dialogue-based large language models, leveraging a diverse and balanced set of personas and entities. The approach uniquely combines entity-conditioned and prompt-continuation evaluations, introduces the Probability of Responding (POR) metric for nuanced assessment of model behavior, and provides fine-grained analysis of how toxicity varies across personas, entities, and prompt styles. The findings are expected to reveal vulnerabilities in current safety guardrails and highlight the risk of defamation and discriminatory bias, informing the design of more robust and trustworthy AI systems.

2834adc0bfcb7a6eab2895bdfcdee218a4e8f4b8.title: Aligning LLMs by Predicting Preferences from User Writing Samples
2834adc0bfcb7a6eab2895bdfcdee218a4e8f4b8.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be more effectively aligned to individual users' writing preferences and styles, using minimal user demonstrations, to enable more personalized and effective AI writing assistants?
2834adc0bfcb7a6eab2895bdfcdee218a4e8f4b8.hypothesis: Iterative refinement and consistency verification of preference descriptions inferred from user writing samples will enable LLMs to more accurately capture nuanced user preferences, resulting in improved alignment of generated text with individual user styles compared to existing preference inference methods.
2834adc0bfcb7a6eab2895bdfcdee218a4e8f4b8.proposed_method: A novel framework, PROSE (Preference Reasoning by Observing and Synthesizing Examples), is developed to infer user writing preferences from a small set of user-provided demonstrations. The method operates in two main stages: (1) iterative refinement, where an LLM generates a candidate preference description, conditions its generations on this description, compares the output to the user's demonstration, and updates the preference description over multiple steps until the generations closely match the user’s style or a maximum number of iterations is reached; (2) consistency verification, where the refined preference description is decomposed into component preferences, and each component is verified against multiple user demonstrations using LLM-as-a-Judge scoring to prune unsupported or overfitted preferences. The final, verified preference description is then used to condition the LLM for future writing tasks, and all relevant data is stored in an interaction memory for continual improvement.
2834adc0bfcb7a6eab2895bdfcdee218a4e8f4b8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two benchmarks: PRELUDE (an existing assistive writing benchmark) and PLUME (a newly proposed benchmark addressing PRELUDE's limitations). Tasks include article summarization and email writing, with multiple synthetic users (using GPT-4o as a proxy) providing demonstrations for each task. Four LLMs of varying sizes and capabilities (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, GPT-4o-mini, and GPT-4o) will be evaluated. Baselines include in-context learning (ICL), CIPHER (a state-of-the-art preference inference method), and oracle/no-preference controls. Evaluation metrics include preference similarity (LLM-as-a-Judge on a Likert scale), per preference-component match (PPCM), and generation quality, with results averaged over multiple seeds. Human evaluation will also be conducted to assess subjective alignment quality.
2834adc0bfcb7a6eab2895bdfcdee218a4e8f4b8.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel iterative refinement process for preference inference, enabling more precise alignment of LLM generations to user writing styles. The method incorporates a new consistency verification step that decomposes and validates preference components across multiple demonstrations, reducing overfitting and irrelevant preferences. A new benchmark, PLUME, is developed to address key limitations of existing datasets, providing more diverse, orthogonal, and impactful preference sets. The approach is claimed to outperform existing methods (e.g., CIPHER) by a significant margin and to be complementary to in-context learning, with combined methods achieving further improvements. The framework also offers interpretable and modifiable preference descriptions, facilitating user interaction and broader applicability.

28358e718311a6f616a97fa20f87b39ca987b06d.title: Practical Adversarial Multivalid Conformal Prediction
28358e718311a6f616a97fa20f87b39ca987b06d.research_question: How can conformal prediction methods be developed to provide robust, computationally efficient, and practically usable prediction sets with strong empirical coverage guarantees, even under adversarially chosen, non-exchangeable data and for arbitrary, possibly intersecting subgroups of the feature space?
28358e718311a6f616a97fa20f87b39ca987b06d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a novel conformal prediction algorithm can be designed to achieve target empirical coverage guarantees in sequential prediction tasks against adversarial data, without requiring a held-out validation set, and that this algorithm can provide threshold-calibrated and group-conditional coverage for arbitrary, possibly intersecting subgroups, while maintaining computational efficiency comparable to split conformal prediction.
28358e718311a6f616a97fa20f87b39ca987b06d.proposed_method: A new algorithm, termed MultiValid Prediction (MVP), will be developed to generate prediction sets for sequential prediction problems over arbitrary domains. The method will operate by, at each round, selecting a conformal score function (potentially data-dependent and adaptive), and computing a round-dependent threshold to form prediction sets. The algorithm will maintain empirical coverage statistics for each threshold and for each user-specified group (which may be arbitrary and intersecting subsets of the feature space), ensuring that coverage guarantees hold both marginally and conditionally on thresholds and group membership. The approach will discretize the threshold space and use a combinatorial update rule, inspired by online learning and multicalibration techniques, to ensure that empirical coverage rates converge to the target rate at nearly optimal statistical rates, even under adversarial ordering and distribution shift. The method will be designed to be computationally lightweight, requiring only simple enumeration and record-keeping at each round, and will not require data splitting for calibration.
28358e718311a6f616a97fa20f87b39ca987b06d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a variety of settings, including both regression and classification tasks, and will use both synthetic and real-world datasets. The evaluation will compare the proposed MVP algorithm to established baselines such as split conformal prediction, methods designed for covariate shift, conservative groupwise coverage approaches, and adversarial coverage algorithms. Evaluation metrics will include marginal and group-conditional empirical coverage, as well as the size and informativeness of prediction sets. Scenarios will be tested under both i.i.d. and adversarial data orderings, and under various forms of distribution shift, to assess robustness and adaptability. The experimental setup will ensure that all data can be used for both model training and conformal score computation, and will include extensive ablation studies to assess the impact of algorithmic choices.
28358e718311a6f616a97fa20f87b39ca987b06d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a practical, computationally efficient conformal prediction algorithm that achieves worst-case empirical coverage guarantees against adversarial data, without requiring a held-out calibration set. It provides threshold-calibrated and multivalid (group-conditional) coverage for arbitrary, possibly intersecting subgroups, a guarantee not achieved by prior practical algorithms. The method achieves nearly statistically optimal convergence rates and is applicable to both regression and classification tasks, as well as to time series and non-exchangeable data. This work advances the state of the art by combining strong theoretical guarantees with practical efficiency and flexibility.

285260b85a028524ad690ddbc096e9a58be7e896.title: Zero-Shot Trajectory Planning for Signal Temporal Logic Tasks
285260b85a028524ad690ddbc096e9a58be7e896.research_question: How can executable trajectories be generated for complex Signal Temporal Logic (STL) tasks in systems with unknown dynamics, using only task-agnostic offline trajectory data, and with the ability to generalize to new STL tasks in a zero-shot manner?
285260b85a028524ad690ddbc096e9a58be7e896.hypothesis: A hierarchical planning framework that semantically decomposes STL specifications, allocates timed waypoints using a learned dynamics-aware model, and synthesizes trajectory segments via a diffusion-based generator trained on task-agnostic data will enable zero-shot generalization to novel STL tasks and generate dynamically feasible, STL-satisfying trajectories for systems with unknown dynamics.
285260b85a028524ad690ddbc096e9a58be7e896.proposed_method: A hierarchical framework will be developed that first decomposes a given STL specification into a set of reachability and invariance progresses, each associated with specific time constraints. A search-based allocation algorithm, guided by a Time Predictor model trained on task-agnostic trajectory data, will determine a sequence of timed waypoints that satisfy the decomposed progresses and respect system dynamics. For trajectory generation, a diffusion model pre-trained on task-agnostic trajectories will be used to synthesize short trajectory segments between waypoints, ensuring that all invariance progresses are satisfied via constrained sampling (e.g., using SafeDiffuser with control barrier functions). These segments will be stitched together to form a complete trajectory, and an inverse dynamics model or controller will be used to recover the action sequence for execution, ensuring temporal alignment with STL requirements.
285260b85a028524ad690ddbc096e9a58be7e896.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in several environments, including Maze2D (U-Maze, Medium, Large), Cube (6-DoF UR5e manipulator), and AntMaze (8-DoF Ant), using only task-agnostic trajectory datasets for offline training. The framework will be evaluated on a diverse set of randomly generated STL tasks, with baselines including Robustness Guided Diffuser (RGD) and a standard optimization-based method where full system dynamics are available. Evaluation metrics will include execution success rate, average STL robustness value, total planning time, and trajectory generation time. Additional experiments will be performed in a custom environment with known dynamics to rigorously assess the feasibility and conservativeness of the planning algorithm.
285260b85a028524ad690ddbc096e9a58be7e896.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first data-driven method to achieve zero-shot generalization for complex STL tasks using only task-agnostic offline trajectory data and without requiring explicit knowledge of system dynamics. The hierarchical decomposition-allocation-generation pipeline guarantees STL satisfaction by construction, and the integration of a learned Time Predictor with constrained diffusion-based trajectory synthesis enables efficient and scalable planning for long-horizon tasks. The method also demonstrates significant improvements in planning efficiency and robustness over existing diffusion-based and optimization-based baselines, and is applicable to high-dimensional, dynamics-rich domains.

2854e5bab8e6f36e54c64456628a9559bf67019e.title: IP-Adapter: Text Compatible Image Prompt Adapter for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
