2854e5bab8e6f36e54c64456628a9559bf67019e.research_question: How can image prompt capability be effectively and efficiently enabled in pretrained text-to-image diffusion models, while maintaining compatibility with text prompts and structural controls, and without requiring extensive fine-tuning or modification of the base model?
2854e5bab8e6f36e54c64456628a9559bf67019e.hypothesis: A lightweight adapter utilizing a decoupled cross-attention mechanism for text and image features can enable pretrained text-to-image diffusion models to generate images from image prompts, achieving performance comparable to or better than fully fine-tuned models, while preserving compatibility with text prompts and structural controls.
2854e5bab8e6f36e54c64456628a9559bf67019e.proposed_method: A novel adapter, termed IP-Adapter, is introduced to enable image prompt conditioning in existing text-to-image diffusion models. The approach leverages a pretrained CLIP image encoder to extract global image embeddings, which are projected into a sequence of features via a small trainable projection network. For each cross-attention layer in the UNet of the diffusion model, an additional cross-attention layer is added specifically for image features, while the original cross-attention layers continue to process text features. During training, only the parameters of the new image-specific cross-attention layers and the projection network are updated, while the base diffusion model and text encoder remain frozen. The outputs of the text and image cross-attention layers are summed, and a weighting factor allows for flexible control of the influence of image versus text prompts during inference.
2854e5bab8e6f36e54c64456628a9559bf67019e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using approximately 10 million image-text pairs sourced from the LAION-2B and COYO-700M datasets for training. The Stable Diffusion v1.5 model will serve as the base diffusion model, and OpenCLIP ViT-H/14 will be used as the image encoder. The proposed method will be compared against baselines including models trained from scratch (e.g., OpenunCLIP, Kandinsky-2-1, Versatile Diffusion), fine-tuned models (SDImageVariations, SDunCLIP), and other adapter-based methods (Uni-ControlNet, T2I-Adapter, ControlNetShuffle). Evaluation will be performed on the COCO 2017 validation set using metrics such as CLIP-I (CLIP image embedding similarity with the prompt image) and CLIP-T (CLIPScore with prompt captions). The experimental setup includes training with 8 V100 GPUs, a batch size of 8 per GPU, AdamW optimizer, and classifier-free guidance with random dropping of text and image conditions.
2854e5bab8e6f36e54c64456628a9559bf67019e.novelty_claims: The proposed IP-Adapter introduces a decoupled cross-attention mechanism that separately processes text and image features, enabling effective image prompt conditioning without modifying or fine-tuning the base diffusion model. The adapter is lightweight (approximately 22M parameters), reusable across custom models fine-tuned from the same base, and compatible with existing structural control tools and multimodal prompts. This approach achieves performance comparable to or surpassing fully fine-tuned image prompt models, while maintaining flexibility and efficiency.

285876e4889f004a8ff9c2d5a5efb8de8839b54e.title: Language Ranker: A Lightweight Ranking framework for LLM Decoding
285876e4889f004a8ff9c2d5a5efb8de8839b54e.research_question: How can the decoding process in large language models be improved to efficiently and effectively select high-quality responses from candidate outputs, while minimizing computational overhead and enabling flexible, personalized adaptation across diverse tasks and user needs?
285876e4889f004a8ff9c2d5a5efb8de8839b54e.hypothesis: A lightweight ranking framework that leverages intermediate features extracted by the base language model can achieve response selection performance comparable to large-scale reward models, while substantially reducing computational and memory requirements during both training and inference.
285876e4889f004a8ff9c2d5a5efb8de8839b54e.proposed_method: A novel framework, Language Ranker, is proposed to enhance the decoding process of large language models by introducing a lightweight, learnable ranker module. The method extracts hidden state features from a predefined intermediate layer of the base model for both the input instruction and each candidate response. These features are projected into a low-dimensional space and processed by either a listwise or pointwise ranker architecture (using a Transformer block or MLP block, respectively) to compute relevance scores between the instruction and each candidate response. The candidate with the highest relevance score is selected as the final output. The ranker is trained using either classification or regression objectives, depending on the label format, and is designed to operate independently from the base model, allowing for flexible pairing and deployment on edge devices or user hardware.
285876e4889f004a8ff9c2d5a5efb8de8839b54e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three representative LLM tasks: mathematics (MATH dataset), coding (MBPP dataset), and function calling (xlam-function-calling-60k dataset). Multiple base models of varying scales and architectures (LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, and Gemma3-4B-it) will be used to demonstrate generality. Baselines will include traditional decoding strategies (beam search, first sample) and reward models (GPT-2-based and LoRA-finetuned models). Evaluation metrics will be task-specific accuracy measures: exact answer match for math, test case pass rate for code, and function/argument match for function calling. The ranker will be trained on features extracted from approximately the 60% depth layer of the base model, using groups of 10 candidate responses per instruction, and evaluated under zero-shot settings. Ablation studies, hyperparameter robustness analysis, and transfer experiments (cross-domain and cross-task) will further assess adaptability and efficiency.
285876e4889f004a8ff9c2d5a5efb8de8839b54e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach reinterprets LLM decoding through the lens of recommender systems, introducing a feature-shared, learnable, and lightweight ranker that eliminates redundant computation present in traditional reward model-based reranking. The framework achieves performance comparable to large-scale reward models with less than 0.5M additional parameters, supports efficient CPU-based training and inference, and enables flexible, personalized adaptation by decoupling the ranker from the base model. The method demonstrates strong cross-domain and cross-task generalization, high hyperparameter robustness, and practical scalability for real-world deployment.

285d2884ba835a62f50311b360185bb6a6b1d061.title: OmniBal: Towards Fast Instruction-Tuning for Vision-Language Models via Omniverse Computation Balance
285d2884ba835a62f50311b360185bb6a6b1d061.research_question: How can computational load imbalance in large-scale distributed training of vision-language models be systematically addressed to improve training efficiency and scalability across heterogeneous data and model architectures?
285d2884ba835a62f50311b360185bb6a6b1d061.hypothesis: A holistic framework that jointly balances data, model, and memory dimensions during distributed instruction-tuning of vision-language models will significantly reduce computational imbalance, leading to faster training without sacrificing model performance.
285d2884ba835a62f50311b360185bb6a6b1d061.proposed_method: A comprehensive training framework is developed to address computational imbalance in distributed vision-language model training by integrating three key modules: data balancing, model partitioning, and adaptive memory management. First, a balanced dynamic mini-batch method is introduced, using an iterative sampling and filtering algorithm (ISF) to group training samples into mini-batches with similar image and text sizes, minimizing padding and ensuring consistent input sizes both within and across devices. Second, a search-based balanced model partitioning strategy is employed, leveraging layer-wise profiling and heuristic search to optimally distribute the heterogeneous vision and language model components across pipeline stages, minimizing variance in computational load and communication overhead. Third, a balanced adaptive re-computation strategy is implemented, which dynamically adjusts the checkpointing of intermediate activations for each model partition based on actual memory usage, maximizing memory utilization and reducing unnecessary recomputation. These modules are tightly integrated to form an omniverse computation balance framework, enabling efficient and scalable instruction-tuning for vision-language models.
285d2884ba835a62f50311b360185bb6a6b1d061.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using large-scale open-source vision-language models, such as InternVL-Chat-1.5 (6B vision encoder + 20B/34B language model), on the InternVL-Chat-1.2 dataset (1.2M samples), with both DeepSpeed and Megatron-DeepSpeed backends to evaluate 3D parallelism. The method is benchmarked against standard open-source training pipelines, with GPU days as the primary metric for training efficiency, and model performance evaluated on five commonly used benchmarks (MMB-EN/CN, ChartQA, AI2D, MMVet, MME). Ablation studies isolate the impact of data, model, and memory balancing components. Additional experiments test generalizability across different datasets, model architectures (e.g., EVA-CLIP, Llama3, Yi-34B, Qwen1.5-110B), hardware platforms (A100, H100), image resolutions, and task types (pretraining, SFT). Overhead analyses for sampling, partitioning, and optimal solution search are reported, and the method’s scalability is validated with larger models and up to 512 GPUs.
285d2884ba835a62f50311b360185bb6a6b1d061.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to systematically identify and address the computation imbalance problem in large-scale vision-language model instruction-tuning, integrating data, model, and memory balancing into a unified framework. The dynamic mini-batch grouping algorithm enables stable and balanced input sizes, while the search-based model partitioning adapts to heterogeneous architectures and hardware. The adaptive re-computation strategy optimizes memory usage based on real-time profiling, reducing unnecessary overhead. The method achieves substantial speed-ups (up to 1.8× reduction in GPU days) without compromising model accuracy, and demonstrates robust generalizability across diverse datasets, models, hardware, and tasks.

28630034bb29760df01ab033b743e30b37f336ae.title: PaLI: A Jointly-Scaled Multilingual Language-Image Model
28630034bb29760df01ab033b743e30b37f336ae.research_question: How can a large-scale, multilingual, multimodal model be designed to jointly process and understand both language and vision inputs, enabling high performance across a wide range of vision, language, and multimodal tasks in many languages?
28630034bb29760df01ab033b743e30b37f336ae.hypothesis: Jointly scaling both the language and vision components of a multimodal model, while leveraging large-scale multilingual data and pre-trained unimodal backbones, will significantly improve performance on a diverse set of vision, language, and multimodal tasks, including those requiring cross-lingual and open-vocabulary capabilities.
28630034bb29760df01ab033b743e30b37f336ae.proposed_method: A modular, scalable encoder-decoder architecture is proposed, integrating a large pre-trained multilingual language model (mT5) and a high-capacity Vision Transformer (ViT). The model processes both images and text as input, with visual features extracted by the ViT and passed as tokens to the text encoder via cross-attention. The architecture is designed to reuse existing unimodal checkpoints for both language and vision, minimizing training costs and leveraging prior capabilities. The vision backbone is scaled up to 4 billion parameters (ViT-e), and the language component uses up to 13 billion parameters (mT5-XXL), with the model trained on a mixture of multimodal and language-only tasks using a unified text generation interface. Training employs a diverse mixture of objectives, including span corruption, captioning, OCR, VQA, and object detection, across a new large-scale multilingual dataset (WebLI) containing over 10 billion images and text in more than 100 languages.
28630034bb29760df01ab033b743e30b37f336ae.experiment_details: Experiments will involve fine-tuning and evaluating the model on a comprehensive suite of benchmarks, including image captioning (COCO Captions, NoCaps, TextCaps, VizWiz-Cap), visual question answering (VQAv2, OKVQA, TextVQA, VizWiz-QA, ST-VQA), cross-lingual and multilingual VQA (xGQA, MaXM), and language understanding (SuperGLUE, XTREME). The model will be compared against strong baselines and state-of-the-art models such as SimVLM, CoCa, GIT, BEiT-3, Flamingo, and others. Evaluation metrics will include CIDEr for captioning, accuracy for VQA, and standard metrics for language understanding. The experimental setup includes both open-vocabulary and classification settings, zero-shot image classification on ImageNet and related datasets, and ablation studies to assess the impact of scaling, data mixture, and model initialization.
28630034bb29760df01ab033b743e30b37f336ae.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a jointly-scaled, modular multimodal model that balances parameter allocation between vision and language components, demonstrating that scaling the vision backbone yields significant gains in multimodal tasks. The method leverages a new, massive multilingual image-text dataset (WebLI) covering over 100 languages, enabling robust multilingual and cross-lingual capabilities. The unified text generation interface allows seamless handling of a wide range of tasks without task-specific heads or parameters. Empirical results are expected to establish new state-of-the-art performance on multiple vision, language, and multimodal benchmarks, and provide a clear scaling roadmap for future large multimodal models.

287839feb1e302fe513c2b03754ca44ad428634a.title: Grokking as the Transition from Lazy to Rich Training Dynamics
287839feb1e302fe513c2b03754ca44ad428634a.research_question: What are the underlying mechanisms responsible for the grokking phenomenon in neural networks, and how do training dynamics, feature learning, and kernel alignment influence the delayed generalization observed during training?
287839feb1e302fe513c2b03754ca44ad428634a.hypothesis: The grokking phenomenon arises from a transition in neural network training dynamics, specifically when a network shifts from a lazy (kernel-like) regime to a rich (feature-learning) regime. This transition is controlled by parameters such as the scale of network output (laziness), the alignment between the initial neural tangent kernel and the target function, and the size of the training dataset.
287839feb1e302fe513c2b03754ca44ad428634a.proposed_method: A theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted using a two-layer neural network trained via vanilla gradient descent on a polynomial regression task. The method will systematically vary key parameters: the output scale parameter (α), which controls the rate of feature learning and induces lazy or rich regimes; and the initial alignment parameter (ϵ), which quantifies the alignment between the neural tangent kernel (NTK) at initialization and the target function. The study will track sufficient statistics of the network (e.g., weight moments and kernel alignment) throughout training to analyze the transition from lazy to rich dynamics. Additionally, the approach will be extended to more complex settings, including MNIST classification, one-layer Transformers, and student-teacher networks, to test the generality of the findings.
287839feb1e302fe513c2b03754ca44ad428634a.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed on synthetic polynomial regression tasks, where the input data is sampled from high-dimensional Gaussian distributions and the target function is a quadratic form. The two-layer neural network will be trained without regularization using vanilla gradient descent, and the effects of varying α and ϵ will be systematically explored. Baselines will include kernel regression solutions using the initial NTK and comparisons to models with fixed or varying feature learning rates. Evaluation metrics will include mean squared error (MSE) for both train and test sets, as well as centered kernel alignment (CKA) between the NTK and the target function. Additional experiments will be conducted on MNIST and modular arithmetic tasks with one-layer Transformers to demonstrate the broader applicability of the proposed mechanism.
287839feb1e302fe513c2b03754ca44ad428634a.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new conceptual framework that explains grokking as a transition from lazy (linearized) to rich (feature-learning) training dynamics, rather than attributing it to weight decay or weight norm reduction as in previous theories. It identifies and formalizes two key parameters—output scale (laziness) and NTK-task alignment—that can induce, control, or eliminate grokking. The method demonstrates that grokking can occur without regularization and with increasing weight norm, challenging prior explanations. The approach provides a general mechanism applicable across architectures, optimizers, and datasets, and offers a principled way to construct tasks that exhibit grokking.

28835fd8d4cb7b62c09fce9e85fe52afe82ba4f5.title: Bottleneck Structure in Learned Features: Low-Dimension vs Regularity Tradeoff
28835fd8d4cb7b62c09fce9e85fe52afe82ba4f5.research_question: What is the fundamental tradeoff between learning low-dimensional representations and maintaining regularity (complexity control) in deep neural networks with large depth and L2 regularization, and how does this tradeoff manifest in the structure of learned features and weight matrices as network depth increases?
28835fd8d4cb7b62c09fce9e85fe52afe82ba4f5.hypothesis: Deep neural networks with large depth and L2 regularization are biased towards learning low-dimensional representations of the input, but this bias is balanced by a regularity constraint that prevents overfitting to spurious symmetries or excessively irregular functions. The existence of a bottleneck structure in the learned features and weight matrices is expected, with most hidden representations being approximately low-dimensional, and this structure can be characterized and controlled by corrections to the representation cost.
28835fd8d4cb7b62c09fce9e85fe52afe82ba4f5.proposed_method: A theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted into the representation cost of deep, fully-connected neural networks with homogeneous nonlinearities and L2 regularization. The representation cost will be decomposed via a Taylor expansion in inverse depth, yielding a dominant low-rank term R(0) (the Bottleneck rank), and correction terms R(1) and R(2) that quantify regularity and further complexity control. Analytical results will be derived to formalize the properties of these corrections, including their behavior under function composition and addition, and their relationship to the Jacobian and pseudo-determinant of the learned function. Theoretical proofs will be provided for the existence of a bottleneck structure in the weight matrices and hidden representations, with explicit finite-depth rates. Additionally, the effect of learning rate scaling on the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) and its role in ensuring convergence of representations at infinite depth will be analyzed.
28835fd8d4cb7b62c09fce9e85fe52afe82ba4f5.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed on synthetic datasets designed to have known optimal Bottleneck rank, allowing precise control and measurement of the learned representations. Deep fully-connected networks of varying depth and sufficient width will be trained with L2 regularization, and the parameter norm, rank of weight matrices, and singular value spectra will be tracked across layers. The effect of depth on the emergence of low-rank bottleneck structures will be empirically validated. Additional experiments will focus on tasks with high-dimensional symmetries, such as learning summary statistics of high-dimensional dynamics, to test the network's ability to learn underlying symmetries and the dimensionality of hidden representations. Evaluation metrics will include training loss, parameter norm, rank and singular values of weight matrices, and the dimensionality and geometry of hidden layer activations. Comparisons will be made across different depths, regularization strengths, and learning rates.
28835fd8d4cb7b62c09fce9e85fe52afe82ba4f5.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a formal decomposition of the representation cost in deep nonlinear networks, identifying correction terms that balance the low-dimensionality bias with regularity constraints. It provides the first theoretical proof of the bottleneck structure in learned features for large-depth networks, including explicit finite-depth rates and conditions for convergence. The approach formalizes the tradeoff between dimension reduction and regularity, and connects these concepts to the behavior of the NTK under large learning rates. The work also offers new insights into why gradient descent avoids certain pathological minima and how implicit regularization shapes the structure of learned representations, extending and generalizing previous empirical observations.

28976990e107c66d33c238df88269eb12b5457ce.title: Improved Diversity Maximization Algorithms for Matching and Pseudoforest
28976990e107c66d33c238df88269eb12b5457ce.research_question: Can constant-factor approximation algorithms and composable coreset constructions be developed for diversity maximization problems under the remote-matching and remote-pseudoforest diversity measures, where only logarithmic-factor approximations were previously known?
28976990e107c66d33c238df88269eb12b5457ce.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that polynomial-time algorithms can be designed to achieve O(1)-approximation for both the remote-matching and remote-pseudoforest diversity maximization problems, and that composable coresets of size polynomial in k can be constructed for these objectives, closing the gap with other diversity measures.
28976990e107c66d33c238df88269eb12b5457ce.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves designing new algorithms for both the offline and composable coreset settings for remote-matching and remote-pseudoforest diversity measures. The approach begins with the Greedy Max-Min (GMM) algorithm to select k well-dispersed points, leveraging properties of metric spaces to ensure spread. For composable coresets, the method partitions the data, applies GMM to each partition, and constructs coresets by carefully selecting representatives and additional points to guarantee diversity objectives are met. For remote-matching, the algorithm exploits the property that duplicate or closely located points do not significantly impact the minimum-weight matching cost, allowing for coreset size reduction to O(k). For remote-pseudoforest, more intricate partitioning and selection strategies are used, involving ε-nets and dynamic programming, to achieve coreset sizes of O(k^{1+ε}) with O(1/ε)-approximation. All algorithms are designed to be deterministic and efficient, with technical innovations to ensure composability and tight approximation guarantees.
28976990e107c66d33c238df88269eb12b5457ce.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic and real-world datasets represented as vectors in metric spaces. The evaluation will compare the proposed algorithms' approximation ratios and coreset sizes against existing O(log k)-approximation baselines for remote-matching and remote-pseudoforest. Metrics will include achieved diversity (minimum-weight matching and sum-of-nearest-neighbor costs), running time, and coreset compactness. The experimental setup will involve partitioning datasets, applying the algorithms in both offline and distributed (composable) settings, and measuring the diversity of selected subsets relative to the optimum and prior methods.
28976990e107c66d33c238df88269eb12b5457ce.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first constant-factor (O(1)) approximation algorithms for the remote-matching diversity maximization problem, resolving a long-standing open question. It also presents the first constant-factor composable coreset constructions for both remote-matching and remote-pseudoforest objectives, with significant improvements in coreset size (O(k) for remote-matching and O(k^{1+ε}) for remote-pseudoforest). The methods are deterministic, simpler than prior randomized or LP-based approaches, and extend to all values of k and n. These advances close the approximation gap for all pairwise distance-based diversity measures and provide practical algorithms for large-scale, distributed, and streaming data settings.

28a35c393ed2709ed129f68d0346cf375dd7a34e.title: Enhancing Sharpness-Aware Optimization Through Variance Suppression
28a35c393ed2709ed129f68d0346cf375dd7a34e.research_question: How can the generalization ability of deep neural networks be further improved by addressing the limitations of sharpness-aware optimization methods, particularly in the presence of adversarial instability and label noise?
28a35c393ed2709ed129f68d0346cf375dd7a34e.hypothesis: Suppression of gradient variance during sharpness-aware optimization will stabilize the adversarial direction, leading to improved generalization and robustness of deep neural networks, especially under high label noise conditions.
28a35c393ed2709ed129f68d0346cf375dd7a34e.proposed_method: A novel optimization framework, Variance-Suppressed Sharpness-Aware Optimization (VaSSO), will be developed to address the instability of adversarial directions in sharpness-aware minimization (SAM). VaSSO introduces an exponentially moving average (EMA) of stochastic gradients to compute a stabilized adversarial direction at each iteration. Specifically, the adversarial perturbation is determined using a smoothed gradient direction, updated as a convex combination of the previous EMA and the current minibatch gradient, controlled by a parameter θ. The adversarial step is then computed by normalizing this EMA direction, ensuring it lies on the surface of a norm ball of prescribed radius. This approach is designed to reduce the variance in the adversarial direction, thereby providing a more reliable estimate of global sharpness and mitigating the 'friendly adversary' problem that can undermine generalization in SAM.
28a35c393ed2709ed129f68d0346cf375dd7a34e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification benchmarks (CIFAR10, CIFAR100, ImageNet) using various neural network architectures (e.g., VGG-11, ResNet-18/34/50, WRN-28-10, PyramidNet-110, ViT-S/32) and on a neural machine translation task (German-English translation on IWSLT-14 using Transformers). VaSSO will be compared against baselines including SGD, AdamW, SAM, ASAM, FisherSAM, and GSAM, with consistent data augmentation and hyperparameter tuning across methods. Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy, BLEU score (for translation), validation perplexity, and flatness measures such as Hessian eigenvalues. Additional experiments will assess robustness to label noise by randomly flipping training labels at various rates and measuring test accuracy. Hyperparameters such as the adversarial radius ρ and EMA parameter θ will be tuned for optimal performance, and all experiments will be run on NVIDIA V100 GPUs.
28a35c393ed2709ed129f68d0346cf375dd7a34e.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a principled variance suppression mechanism within sharpness-aware optimization, leading to provably more stable adversarial directions than existing approaches. Theoretical analysis provides tighter convergence guarantees and stability bounds, removing restrictive assumptions present in prior work. VaSSO is model-agnostic, memory-efficient, and can be integrated with other SAM variants. Empirical results demonstrate consistent improvements in generalization and robustness across vision and language tasks, especially under high label noise, substantiating the practical benefits of stabilized adversarial optimization.

28b5dfe6035013e9345ec4a3eef5f0c5307a3fcb.title: Atomistic Line Graph Neural Network for improved materials property predictions
28b5dfe6035013e9345ec4a3eef5f0c5307a3fcb.research_question: How can the explicit incorporation of bond angle information into graph neural network architectures improve the prediction accuracy of materials properties for both solid-state and molecular systems?
28b5dfe6035013e9345ec4a3eef5f0c5307a3fcb.hypothesis: Explicitly including bond angle information through a line graph representation in a graph neural network will lead to improved predictive performance on a wide range of atomistic materials property prediction tasks compared to models that use only bond distance information.
28b5dfe6035013e9345ec4a3eef5f0c5307a3fcb.proposed_method: A novel Atomistic Line Graph Neural Network (ALIGNN) architecture will be developed, which alternates message passing between an atomistic bond graph and its corresponding line graph. In the atomistic bond graph, atoms are nodes and bonds are edges, with node features derived from atomic properties and edge features based on interatomic distances, expanded using radial basis functions. The line graph is constructed such that its nodes represent bonds and its edges represent bond angles, with edge features derived from the cosine of bond angles, also RBF-expanded. Edge-gated graph convolution layers will be used to update both node and edge features, and ALIGNN layers will alternate between convolutions on the bond graph and the line graph, propagating angle information efficiently. The model will be trained with multiple ALIGNN and GCN layers, followed by global average pooling and a final regression or classification layer for property prediction.
28b5dfe6035013e9345ec4a3eef5f0c5307a3fcb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three major datasets: the Materials Project (MP, version 2018.6.1, 69,239 materials), JARVIS-DFT (version 2021.8.18, 55,722 materials), and QM9 (molecular dataset, 130,829 molecules). Standard train-validation-test splits will be used (e.g., 60,000-5,000-4,239 for MP; 80%-10%-10% for JARVIS-DFT; 110,000-10,000-10,829 for QM9). The ALIGNN model will be compared against baselines including CGCNN, MEGNet, SchNet, and descriptor-based methods such as CFID. Evaluation metrics will include mean absolute error (MAE) and mean absolute deviation (MAD) across a variety of properties such as formation energy, band gap, dielectric constant, modulus, and more. Hyperparameters such as number of layers, embedding size, and learning rate will be optimized via random search and hypothesis-driven experiments.
28b5dfe6035013e9345ec4a3eef5f0c5307a3fcb.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel use of line graph neural networks to explicitly incorporate bond angle information into atomistic GNNs, enabling efficient propagation of angular features alongside bond distances. This dual-graph message passing framework is claimed to outperform existing GNN architectures and descriptor-based models on a broad set of materials property prediction tasks, offering improved accuracy and comparable or better training efficiency. The method provides a generalizable and scalable solution for capturing many-body interactions critical for accurate atomistic modeling.

28c6ac721f54544162865f41c5692e70d61bccab.title: A survey on large language model based autonomous agents
28c6ac721f54544162865f41c5692e70d61bccab.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be effectively leveraged to construct autonomous agents capable of human-like decision-making, memory, planning, and action in dynamic, open-domain environments, and what unified frameworks and evaluation strategies can be developed to advance this field?
28c6ac721f54544162865f41c5692e70d61bccab.hypothesis: Integrating comprehensive profiling, memory, planning, and action modules within a unified agent architecture, and leveraging LLMs' human-like capabilities, will enable the creation of autonomous agents that exhibit more consistent, flexible, and effective behaviors across diverse tasks and environments.
28c6ac721f54544162865f41c5692e70d61bccab.proposed_method: A unified framework will be developed for constructing LLM-based autonomous agents, comprising four key modules: profiling, memory, planning, and action. The profiling module will define agent roles and characteristics using a combination of manual, LLM-generated, and dataset-aligned strategies. The memory module will implement both short-term and long-term memory structures, utilizing formats such as natural language, embeddings, databases, and structured lists, and will support operations including reading, writing, and reflection. The planning module will enable agents to decompose complex tasks into subtasks using both single-path and multi-path reasoning, with and without feedback, inspired by human cognitive processes. The action module will translate agent decisions into concrete outputs, interfacing with tools, environments, and other agents. The framework will allow for modular integration and flexible adaptation to various application domains.
28c6ac721f54544162865f41c5692e70d61bccab.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of benchmark tasks spanning social science, natural science, and engineering domains. Representative datasets such as conversational logs, game environments (e.g., Minecraft, Dungeons & Dragons), and real-world demographic datasets (e.g., ANES) will be utilized. Baseline comparisons will include traditional reinforcement learning agents, prior LLM-based agent architectures, and ablated versions of the proposed framework. Evaluation metrics will encompass both objective measures (task completion rate, reasoning accuracy, memory consistency) and subjective assessments (human-likeness, explainability, and user satisfaction). The experimental setup will include systematic ablation studies to isolate the contributions of each module and strategy.
28c6ac721f54544162865f41c5692e70d61bccab.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a comprehensive and unified framework for LLM-based autonomous agent construction, systematically integrating profiling, memory, planning, and action modules inspired by human cognition. It synthesizes and extends prior modular approaches, enabling flexible and scalable agent design. The framework supports advanced memory operations, hierarchical planning with feedback, and modular action spaces, facilitating the development of agents with enhanced reasoning, adaptability, and explainability. The work also establishes a taxonomy of evaluation strategies and identifies open challenges, laying the groundwork for future research in LLM-based autonomous agents.

28c7e583d90ccfc5c3078dfc1d6b80a9ad90248d.title: Quantifying Memorization Across Neural Language Models
28c7e583d90ccfc5c3078dfc1d6b80a9ad90248d.research_question: How can memorization in neural language models be quantitatively measured and characterized across different model architectures, dataset properties, and training configurations?
28c7e583d90ccfc5c3078dfc1d6b80a9ad90248d.hypothesis: Memorization in neural language models increases as a function of model size, data duplication, and context length, and this scaling can be quantitatively characterized using systematic evaluation methods.
28c7e583d90ccfc5c3078dfc1d6b80a9ad90248d.proposed_method: A comprehensive methodology is proposed to quantify memorization in neural language models by defining a sequence as 'extractable' if the model, when prompted with a prefix from its training data, generates the exact ground truth continuation using greedy decoding. The evaluation involves constructing two types of data subsets: a uniformly random sample and a duplicate-normalized sample, where sequences are stratified by both length and duplication count. For each sequence, the model is prompted with a prefix and its ability to reproduce the suffix is measured, allowing for the analysis of memorization as a function of model size, data duplication, and prompt length. The approach is extended to masked language models (such as T5) by adapting the extractability definition to the masked prediction task. Additional experiments explore the effects of decoding strategies and deduplication on memorization.
28c7e583d90ccfc5c3078dfc1d6b80a9ad90248d.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on several model families, including GPT-Neo (causal language models trained on The Pile), T5 (masked language models trained on C4), and OPT (trained on a modified version of The Pile), with model sizes ranging from 125M to 66B parameters. Evaluation datasets include both uniformly random and duplicate-normalized samples, with up to 500,000 sequences per experiment, stratified by sequence length and duplication count. Baselines include GPT-2 models trained on different data and models trained on deduplicated datasets. Metrics focus on the fraction of sequences for which the model exactly reproduces the ground truth continuation, with additional analysis of alternative decoding strategies (e.g., beam search) and qualitative inspection of memorized examples. Statistical significance is assessed where appropriate.
28c7e583d90ccfc5c3078dfc1d6b80a9ad90248d.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a systematic, quantitative framework for measuring memorization in neural language models, providing order-of-magnitude more precise bounds than prior qualitative or lower-bound approaches. The methodology enables the identification of log-linear scaling relationships between memorization and model size, data duplication, and context length across multiple model families and training objectives. The study also demonstrates the limitations of deduplication strategies and highlights the challenges of auditing memorization, offering new insights for privacy and dataset curation in large-scale language model training.

28ea43cfad0ad2a367096581865114b6b94a9a6e.title: MagicDec: Breaking the Latency-Throughput Tradeoff for Long Context Generation with Speculative Decoding
28ea43cfad0ad2a367096581865114b6b94a9a6e.research_question: Can both throughput and latency be simultaneously improved for large language model (LLM) inference on long-context, large-batch workloads without sacrificing output quality, and what strategies can optimize speculative decoding in this regime?
28ea43cfad0ad2a367096581865114b6b94a9a6e.hypothesis: Speculative decoding, when combined with intelligent drafting strategies such as compressed key-value (KV) cache-based drafting, can overcome traditional bottlenecks and achieve significant speedup in both throughput and latency for long-context, large-batch LLM inference without degrading accuracy.
28ea43cfad0ad2a367096581865114b6b94a9a6e.proposed_method: A novel framework, MagicDec, will be developed to optimize speculative decoding for LLMs in long-context, large-batch settings. The method will first analyze the shifting inference bottlenecks as batch size and sequence length increase, identifying the KV cache as the dominant constraint in these regimes. MagicDec will employ draft models with compressed or sparsified KV caches, leveraging both static and dynamic KV selection algorithms to maximize draft token acceptance rates while minimizing draft and verification costs. A theoretical model will guide the selection of optimal drafting strategies, balancing draft model size, KV budget, and compression method to achieve the best trade-off between speedup and accuracy. The framework will be adaptable to different LLM architectures, hardware configurations, and task requirements, and will include a bottleneck-aware formulation for drafting strategy selection.
28ea43cfad0ad2a367096581865114b6b94a9a6e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on state-of-the-art long-context LLMs such as LLaMA-3.1-8B, LLaMA-2-7B-32K, Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen2.5-32B, and Mistral-7B-v0.3, using datasets like PG-19 and various Ruler tasks (e.g., needle in a haystack, common word extraction, question answering). The evaluation will span a range of batch sizes (32 to 256+), sequence lengths (from 256 up to 100,000 tokens), and hardware platforms (e.g., 8xA100, 8xH100, L40 GPUs). Baselines will include traditional autoregressive decoding and standard speculative decoding with small draft models. Key evaluation metrics will be throughput (tokens/sec), per-token latency, acceptance rate, and end-to-end speedup. The impact of different KV compression algorithms (e.g., StreamingLLM, SnapKV, PQCache) and drafting strategies will be systematically compared, with ablation studies on KV budget, draft model size, and compression method.
28ea43cfad0ad2a367096581865114b6b94a9a6e.novelty_claims: The proposed research challenges the prevailing belief that speculative decoding is ineffective for large-batch LLM inference by demonstrating that, beyond a critical sequence length, SD can achieve increasing speedup with batch size. The introduction of KV cache compression as a drafting strategy is claimed to yield higher acceptance rates and better batch performance than parameter-efficient draft models, especially in memory-bound regimes. MagicDec provides a general, bottleneck-aware framework for selecting optimal drafting strategies based on theoretical and empirical analysis, and is extensible to various LLMs, hardware, and tasks. The approach is claimed to achieve up to 2.51x speedup over autoregressive decoding without compromising accuracy, and to generalize across multiple models and hardware configurations.

290b5017a8e574bec4d810167e711566069d64cc.title: Local Latent Space Bayesian Optimization over Structured Inputs
290b5017a8e574bec4d810167e711566069d64cc.research_question: How can Bayesian optimization be improved for black-box optimization tasks over structured, discrete, and high-dimensional input spaces, such as molecules or arithmetic expressions, by leveraging latent representations learned by deep autoencoder models?
290b5017a8e574bec4d810167e711566069d64cc.hypothesis: Jointly adapting the latent space of a deep autoencoder with a local Bayesian optimization strategy that incorporates trust-region methods will better align the structure of the latent space with the assumptions of the surrogate model, leading to significantly improved optimization performance over existing latent space Bayesian optimization approaches.
290b5017a8e574bec4d810167e711566069d64cc.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a local latent space Bayesian optimization (LOL-BO) framework for structured input spaces. This method adapts trust-region-based local Bayesian optimization (such as TuRBO) to operate within the latent space of a deep autoencoder (DAE), addressing the mismatch between local neighborhoods in latent and input spaces. The encoder of the DAE is reformulated to serve both as a standard encoder and as a deep kernel for the Gaussian process (GP) surrogate model within the trust region. A semi-supervised variational inference procedure is developed, jointly optimizing the DAE and a sparse GP surrogate, encouraging the latent space to satisfy the smoothness and locality assumptions required by trust-region BO. Additionally, a transformer-based autoencoder architecture using the SELFIES molecular representation is proposed to further improve the validity and expressiveness of the latent space for molecular design tasks.
290b5017a8e574bec4d810167e711566069d64cc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six high-dimensional structured optimization tasks, including molecular property optimization (e.g., penalized logP, Guacamol benchmarks, and DRD3 receptor docking) and arithmetic expression generation. Datasets include a standardized set of 1.27 million molecules from the Guacamol benchmark and 40,000 labeled arithmetic expressions. Both supervised and unsupervised data are used to train the autoencoders. Baselines for comparison include standard latent space BO, weighted and triplet loss retraining methods, and non-BO methods such as genetic algorithms and reinforcement learning approaches (e.g., GEGL, GraphGA). Evaluation metrics include best objective value achieved, sample efficiency, molecule validity, reconstruction accuracy, and surrogate model performance (e.g., GP test negative log-likelihood). Experimental setups ensure consistent data access and model architectures across methods, with ablation studies isolating the impact of local optimization and joint latent space adaptation.
290b5017a8e574bec4d810167e711566069d64cc.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to jointly adapt the latent space of a deep autoencoder and a local trust-region Bayesian optimization strategy for structured input spaces. It introduces a semi-supervised variational inference framework that aligns the latent space with the assumptions of the GP surrogate, resulting in improved locality and optimization performance. The use of a transformer-based SELFIES autoencoder further enhances validity and expressiveness for molecular design. Empirical results demonstrate up to 20x improvements in objective value and significant gains in sample efficiency over state-of-the-art latent space Bayesian optimization methods across multiple real-world benchmarks.

293499319bdd460cb3fca1f0f5eb330e64bf3ff9.title: Towards Making the Most of ChatGPT for Machine Translation
293499319bdd460cb3fca1f0f5eb330e64bf3ff9.research_question: How can the translation capabilities of large language models like ChatGPT be maximally elicited for machine translation tasks, particularly across diverse domains, language pairs, and resource levels?
293499319bdd460cb3fca1f0f5eb330e64bf3ff9.hypothesis: Optimizing prompt design (including task-specific and domain-specific prompts) and decoding parameters (such as temperature), as well as leveraging advanced in-context learning strategies, will significantly improve the machine translation performance of ChatGPT, especially in low-resource and non-English-centric scenarios.
293499319bdd460cb3fca1f0f5eb330e64bf3ff9.proposed_method: A systematic investigation will be conducted into the impact of prompt engineering and decoding strategies on ChatGPT's machine translation performance. The approach will involve three main components: (1) tuning the temperature parameter to identify optimal settings for translation tasks, hypothesizing that lower temperatures yield more accurate outputs; (2) designing and evaluating Task-Specific Prompts (TSP) that explicitly instruct ChatGPT to act as a translation system, and Domain-Specific Prompts (DSP) that provide explicit domain context (e.g., biomedical, news, e-commerce) to the model; and (3) exploring advanced in-context learning (ICL) strategies, including few-shot prompting with both random and similarity-based (TopK) example selection, as well as chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting adapted for translation. The methodology will include prompt template development, ablation studies on prompt components, and comparative analysis of ICL strategies.
293499319bdd460cb3fca1f0f5eb330e64bf3ff9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a variety of publicly available machine translation test sets, including Flores-200 (covering 204 languages), WMT19 Biomedical, WMT19 News, and WMT22 E-Commerce datasets. The evaluation will span both English-centric and non-English-centric language pairs, with particular attention to low-resource and distant language scenarios. Baselines will include commercial systems such as Google Translate and vanilla ChatGPT with standard prompts. Performance will be measured using neural-based metrics (COMET), as well as traditional metrics (BLEU, ChrF), and statistical significance will be assessed. Additional analyses will include hallucination detection in non-English-centric outputs and the impact of incorrect domain prompts. Few-shot ICL experiments will vary the number and selection method of examples, and CoT prompting will be evaluated for its effect on translation quality.
293499319bdd460cb3fca1f0f5eb330e64bf3ff9.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a comprehensive framework for eliciting the full translation potential of ChatGPT through optimal prompt design and decoding strategies. It is the first to systematically analyze the effects of temperature, task-specific, and domain-specific prompts in conjunction with advanced in-context learning and chain-of-thought strategies for machine translation. The work also provides new insights into hallucination phenomena in non-English-centric translation and demonstrates that domain and task guidance can close the gap with or even surpass commercial MT systems in certain settings. The approach bridges philosophies from example-based and statistical machine translation with modern LLM prompting techniques.

297a6890413050cca93e1897a318b0ffe9e520b3.title: Generalization in quantum machine learning from few training data
297a6890413050cca93e1897a318b0ffe9e520b3.research_question: How can quantum machine learning models generalize from a limited number of training data points, and what are the theoretical and practical limits of generalization error in variational quantum machine learning, especially as a function of model complexity and training data size?
297a6890413050cca93e1897a318b0ffe9e520b3.hypothesis: Quantum machine learning models with a polynomial number of trainable gates can achieve good generalization from a polynomially sized training dataset, and the generalization error can be tightly upper bounded as a function of the number of trainable parameters and the size of the training data. Furthermore, if only a subset of parameters undergo significant change during optimization, generalization can improve further.
297a6890413050cca93e1897a318b0ffe9e520b3.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the generalization performance of variational quantum machine learning models (QMLMs) trained on limited data. The approach will model QMLMs as parameterized quantum channels, considering both continuous and discrete parameters, and will derive probabilistic upper bounds on the generalization error using covering number arguments and chaining techniques from random process theory. The analysis will account for scenarios with repeated use of parameterized gates (gate-sharing), variable circuit architectures, and the effect of the optimization trajectory on parameter changes. Theoretical results will be complemented by numerical simulations on two key applications: quantum phase classification using quantum convolutional neural networks (QCNNs), and variational quantum compiling of the quantum Fourier transform using variable ansatz circuits. The methodology will include both analytical derivations and efficient classical simulations using matrix product state techniques and stochastic optimization algorithms.
297a6890413050cca93e1897a318b0ffe9e520b3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in two main settings. First, QCNNs will be trained to classify ground states of a generalized cluster Hamiltonian into different quantum phases, using training sets of varying size and system size (number of qubits), with performance evaluated by test accuracy and empirical risk. Matrix product state (MPS) methods will be used for efficient simulation and optimization. Second, the task of compiling the quantum Fourier transform (QFT) will be addressed by training variable-depth parameterized quantum circuits (using the VAns algorithm) on input-output pairs generated from QFT, with training data drawn from computational basis states, low-entangled states, or Haar random states. The generalization error will be assessed by testing the compiled circuits on unseen states and measuring the trace distance between the target and compiled unitaries. Baselines will include random guessing and existing classical compiling methods, with evaluation metrics such as test accuracy, training accuracy, and trace norm error. The effect of training data size, system size, and initialization near the solution will be systematically studied.
297a6890413050cca93e1897a318b0ffe9e520b3.novelty_claims: The proposed research will provide the first rigorous, general, and non-asymptotic upper bounds on the generalization error of variational quantum machine learning models as a function of the number of trainable gates and training data size. It will introduce new covering number bounds for quantum channels implemented by QMLMs, and demonstrate that efficient generalization is possible even with few training data points, especially when only a subset of parameters are significantly optimized. The work will establish that key applications such as quantum compiling and quantum phase recognition can be performed with polynomial or even logarithmic training data resources, significantly improving upon prior exponential data requirements. Additionally, the research will provide practical guidance for ansatz design and training strategies in quantum machine learning, and offer new insights into the scalability and efficiency of quantum algorithms for real-world applications.

298a3a4d509473ca3e82d6e16ba7a98ebc7372ae.title: All-in-one simulation-based inference
298a3a4d509473ca3e82d6e16ba7a98ebc7372ae.research_question: How can simulation-based amortized Bayesian inference be made more flexible, efficient, and broadly applicable, particularly in scenarios involving unstructured or missing data, function-valued (infinite-dimensional) parameters, and the need to sample arbitrary conditional distributions of parameters and data?
298a3a4d509473ca3e82d6e16ba7a98ebc7372ae.hypothesis: A unified amortized inference framework based on probabilistic diffusion models and transformer architectures can overcome the limitations of current simulation-based inference methods, enabling efficient and accurate inference for a wide range of simulators, data structures, and conditional queries.
298a3a4d509473ca3e82d6e16ba7a98ebc7372ae.proposed_method: A novel inference method, termed the Simformer, will be developed by integrating probabilistic diffusion models with transformer architectures. The approach models the joint distribution of simulator parameters and data using a score-based diffusion process, where a transformer network is trained to estimate the score function over tokenized representations of all variables (parameters and data). The method introduces a flexible tokenization scheme encoding variable identity, value, and condition state, and leverages attention masks to encode known or assumed dependency structures within the simulator. During training, the Simformer is optimized via denoising score matching, sampling various condition masks to enable learning of all possible conditional distributions. At inference, arbitrary conditionals—including posterior, likelihood, and conditionals with interval constraints—can be sampled efficiently using guided diffusion, allowing for flexible and interactive Bayesian inference.
298a3a4d509473ca3e82d6e16ba7a98ebc7372ae.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of benchmark simulation-based inference tasks from domains such as ecology, epidemiology, and neuroscience. Datasets will include both standard benchmarks (e.g., Gaussian linear, mixture, Two Moons, Lotka-Volterra, SIRD, Hodgkin-Huxley) and custom scenarios with unstructured or missing data, as well as function-valued parameters. Baseline methods for comparison will include neural posterior estimation (NPE), neural likelihood estimation (NLE), and other state-of-the-art amortized inference techniques. Evaluation metrics will comprise classifier two-sample test (C2ST) accuracy between inferred and ground-truth posteriors, log-likelihood, and calibration measures. Experimental setups will assess the ability to infer arbitrary conditionals, handle missing/unstructured data, and perform inference with interval constraints. Simulation budgets will be varied to assess efficiency, and attention mask configurations will be tested to evaluate the impact of incorporating dependency structure.
298a3a4d509473ca3e82d6e16ba7a98ebc7372ae.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a unified 'all-in-one' amortized inference framework that enables efficient sampling of arbitrary conditional distributions—including posterior, likelihood, and parameter/data conditionals—using a single trained network. It is claimed to be substantially more flexible than existing methods, supporting function-valued (infinite-dimensional) parameters, unstructured and missing data, and interval constraints via guided diffusion. The approach leverages transformer attention masks to encode and exploit known dependency structures, improving simulation efficiency. The Simformer is expected to outperform state-of-the-art amortized inference methods on benchmark tasks and to open new application domains for simulation-based Bayesian inference.

29b77089a0a40f46372ce2dca9c3bb2dd5d46b1d.title: Fine-Tuning can Distort Pretrained Features and Underperform Out-of-Distribution
29b77089a0a40f46372ce2dca9c3bb2dd5d46b1d.research_question: How do different transfer learning strategies, specifically full fine-tuning, linear probing, and hybrid approaches, affect in-distribution and out-of-distribution generalization when transferring pretrained models to downstream tasks under significant distribution shift?
29b77089a0a40f46372ce2dca9c3bb2dd5d46b1d.hypothesis: Full fine-tuning of pretrained models, while improving in-distribution accuracy, can distort pretrained features and result in lower out-of-distribution accuracy compared to linear probing, especially when the pretrained features are strong and the distribution shift is large. A two-step approach of linear probing followed by fine-tuning (LP-FT) can mitigate this tradeoff and improve both in-distribution and out-of-distribution performance.
29b77089a0a40f46372ce2dca9c3bb2dd5d46b1d.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical and theoretical investigation will be conducted to compare three transfer learning strategies: (1) full fine-tuning, where all model parameters are updated on the downstream task; (2) linear probing, where only the final linear classification head is trained while the feature extractor is frozen; and (3) a two-step LP-FT approach, where a linear head is first trained with the feature extractor frozen, followed by full fine-tuning of the entire model initialized with the linear probed head. Theoretical analysis will focus on overparameterized linear models to characterize how fine-tuning can distort pretrained features, particularly in directions orthogonal to the training data, thereby degrading OOD generalization. The effect of head initialization and feature extractor alignment will be rigorously analyzed, and the role of feature distortion in OOD error will be quantified. The LP-FT approach will be theoretically motivated as a means to reduce feature distortion by better aligning the head before full fine-tuning.
29b77089a0a40f46372ce2dca9c3bb2dd5d46b1d.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed on ten diverse distribution shift benchmarks, including Breeds-Living17, Breeds-Entity30, DomainNet, CIFAR → STL, CIFAR10.1, FMoW, ImageNetV2, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-A, and ImageNet-Sketch. Pretrained feature extractors from MoCo-v2 and CLIP will be used as initialization. Each method (fine-tuning, linear probing, LP-FT) will be evaluated on both in-distribution (ID) and out-of-distribution (OOD) test sets. Baselines will include training from scratch, linear probing, and full fine-tuning. Evaluation metrics will be classification accuracy for both ID and OOD splits. Additional analysis will track feature changes during training, alignment between feature extractors and data subspaces, and the effect of head initialization. The experimental setup will ensure consistent hyperparameters and comparable compute budgets across methods.
29b77089a0a40f46372ce2dca9c3bb2dd5d46b1d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a rigorous theoretical framework that explains why fine-tuning can degrade OOD performance by distorting pretrained features, a phenomenon not previously characterized in depth. It proposes and justifies a simple yet principled two-step LP-FT strategy that combines the benefits of linear probing and full fine-tuning, demonstrating both theoretically and empirically that LP-FT can outperform both standard fine-tuning and linear probing on ID and OOD accuracy. The analysis provides new insights into the tradeoff between ID and OOD generalization in transfer learning and offers practical guidance for robust model adaptation under distribution shift.

29bd550d0ab53296790ceba31dfe0a06754bcdde.title: Large Language Models Are Latent Variable Models: Explaining and Finding Good Demonstrations for In-Context Learning
29bd550d0ab53296790ceba31dfe0a06754bcdde.research_question: How can the process of in-context learning in large language models be better understood and improved through a probabilistic, latent variable framework, and how can this understanding be leveraged to systematically select effective demonstrations for few-shot learning tasks?
29bd550d0ab53296790ceba31dfe0a06754bcdde.hypothesis: Large language models implicitly infer a latent variable representing task and format information from in-context demonstrations, and selecting demonstrations that maximize the likelihood of this latent variable will lead to improved in-context learning performance.
29bd550d0ab53296790ceba31dfe0a06754bcdde.proposed_method: A two-phase approach is proposed. First, latent concept learning is performed by introducing new concept tokens into a small language model's vocabulary, with their embeddings fine-tuned via prompt tuning on a set of demonstration candidates for each task. This process aligns the latent concept variable with the token embedding space, allowing the model to represent task-specific information. Second, demonstration selection is conducted by evaluating candidate demonstrations according to the probability that they infer the optimal concept tokens, as computed by the fine-tuned small language model. The top-k demonstrations with the highest likelihood of inferring the task concept are selected and then used as demonstrations for in-context learning in larger language models, leveraging the generalizability of the selected examples.
29bd550d0ab53296790ceba31dfe0a06754bcdde.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on eight real-world text classification datasets spanning sentiment analysis (SST2, FPB), linguistic acceptability (COLA), topic classification (DBpedia), emotion classification (EmoC, Saravia), and hate speech detection (ETHOS-SO, ETHOS-R). Demonstrations are selected using GPT2-large and then transferred to a range of larger models (including GPT2, GPT3, GPT-J, OPT, LLaMA, and Llama2) for evaluation. Baselines include uniform random selection and semantic similarity-based selection using sentence transformers. Evaluation metrics focus on classification accuracy, with experiments repeated across multiple random seeds and ablation studies performed on the number of demonstrations and concept tokens. Additional experiments are conducted on the GSM8K math word problem dataset to assess generalizability to more complex reasoning tasks.
29bd550d0ab53296790ceba31dfe0a06754bcdde.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a Bayesian latent variable explanation for in-context learning in large language models that is empirically validated on real-world models and datasets, rather than synthetic or toy settings. A practical and efficient demonstration selection algorithm is developed, leveraging prompt tuning of concept tokens in a small language model and transferring the selected demonstrations to larger models. The approach does not require model parameter updates or instruction fine-tuning, and demonstrates significant improvements over established baselines. The method also provides theoretical guarantees under realistic assumptions and offers insights into the transferability and robustness of demonstration selection across different models and tasks.

29c2d3d77b6d6f24f4356d5ba20c1a6ab4229c76.title: Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation with Mask-adapted CLIP
29c2d3d77b6d6f24f4356d5ba20c1a6ab4229c76.research_question: How can open-vocabulary semantic segmentation models be improved to accurately segment images into arbitrary categories described by text, including categories not seen during training, while retaining strong generalization capabilities?
29c2d3d77b6d6f24f4356d5ba20c1a6ab4229c76.hypothesis: Adapting vision-language models such as CLIP to masked images using diverse, weakly-supervised mask-category pairs mined from image-caption datasets, combined with mask prompt tuning, will significantly improve open-vocabulary semantic segmentation performance and generalization to unseen categories.
29c2d3d77b6d6f24f4356d5ba20c1a6ab4229c76.proposed_method: A two-stage open-vocabulary semantic segmentation framework will be developed. First, a segmentation model (e.g., MaskFormer) is trained to generate class-agnostic mask proposals and corresponding embeddings compatible with a vision-language model (CLIP). Next, a large-scale dataset of mask-category pairs will be mined from image-caption datasets (such as COCO Captions) by extracting nouns from captions and aligning them with mask proposals using CLIP similarity. To address the domain gap between natural images and masked image regions, CLIP will be adapted using these mined pairs. Mask prompt tuning will be introduced, replacing blank (zero) tokens in masked image patches with learnable prompt tokens, either training only these prompts (freezing CLIP weights) or jointly with full model finetuning. This approach enables efficient adaptation for masked images and supports multi-task scenarios where CLIP weights may need to remain unchanged.
29c2d3d77b6d6f24f4356d5ba20c1a6ab4229c76.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by training on the COCO-Stuff dataset and using captions from COCO Captions to mine mask-category pairs. The adapted models will be evaluated in a zero-shot manner on multiple challenging segmentation benchmarks, including ADE20K (A-150 and A-847), Pascal Context (PC-59 and PC-459), and PASCAL VOC (PAS-20), without any dataset-specific adaptation. Baselines will include prior open-vocabulary segmentation methods such as OpenSeg, ZegFormer, and LSeg, as well as supervised specialist models like MaskFormer and DeepLab. Evaluation metrics will primarily be mean Intersection over Union (mIoU). Ablation studies will assess the impact of different sources of mask-category pairs, the effect of mask prompt tuning versus full model finetuning, and the scalability of the approach across different model backbones (e.g., ResNet-101c, Swin-Base, ViT-L/14).
29c2d3d77b6d6f24f4356d5ba20c1a6ab4229c76.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a novel adaptation of CLIP for masked images using a large, diverse, weakly-supervised mask-category dataset mined from image captions, as opposed to limited, manually annotated segmentation labels. Mask prompt tuning is proposed as a new technique for adapting CLIP to masked images without modifying its weights, enabling efficient multi-task and multi-domain usage. The approach demonstrates, for the first time, that open-vocabulary generalist models can match or surpass the performance of supervised specialist models from previous years on standard segmentation benchmarks, all without dataset-specific adaptation.

29cf62a9331d4a24c68ad31b767ee4870719fa26.title: MIBP-Cert: Certified Training against Data Perturbations with Mixed-Integer Bilinear Programs
29cf62a9331d4a24c68ad31b767ee4870719fa26.research_question: How can robust, certified training methods be developed to provide provable guarantees against data perturbations—including complex, structured, and non-standard threat models—during the training of machine learning models?
29cf62a9331d4a24c68ad31b767ee4870719fa26.hypothesis: Certified training using mixed-integer bilinear programming (MIBP) can provide tighter, more stable, and more expressive robustness guarantees against a wide range of data perturbations, including both continuous and categorical features, compared to existing interval or polyhedral relaxation-based methods.
29cf62a9331d4a24c68ad31b767ee4870719fa26.proposed_method: A certified training framework will be developed based on mixed-integer bilinear programming (MIBP) to compute deterministic, sound bounds on model parameters at each training iteration under a general threat model. The method will encode the entire training step—including forward pass, loss computation, backward pass, and parameter updates—as a single MIBP, allowing for precise per-step certification and the preservation of operand dependencies. To ensure tractability, the computational graph will be cut after each parameter update, and bounds will be computed iteration-wise, relaxing only the parameter space at each step. The framework will support arbitrary linear, bilinear, logical, and integer constraints, enabling the modeling of complex perturbation scenarios, such as structured, dataset-wide, or feature-dependent attacks, as well as both real-valued and categorical data.
29cf62a9331d4a24c68ad31b767ee4870719fa26.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on benchmark datasets, including Two Moons, Iris (both 2-class and full multi-class), Breast Cancer Wisconsin, and the National Poll on Healthy Aging (NPHA) tabular dataset. The method will be compared against state-of-the-art deterministic certified training baselines such as FullCert and Sosnin et al., using certified accuracy as the primary evaluation metric. Additional metrics will include certification rate, standard deviation of certified accuracy, and runtime/complexity analysis (e.g., number of branches explored by the solver). The evaluation will cover a range of perturbation radii and threat models, including both standard ℓ-norm bounded perturbations and complex, structured constraints on categorical features, such as missing values and reporting bias.
29cf62a9331d4a24c68ad31b767ee4870719fa26.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to formulate certified training as a mixed-integer bilinear program, enabling exact, deterministic parameter bounds and convergence guarantees. It supports a broader class of threat models—including complex, structured, and dataset-wide perturbations—than prior methods, and can handle both continuous and categorical features. The method achieves significantly tighter parameter bounds, improved certified accuracy, and greater training stability, particularly under large perturbations and expressive threat models. Additionally, the approach avoids the divergence and instability issues inherent in interval or polyhedral relaxation-based certified training.

29d3d528b8dac5e9aa8034342d41b6a48c0f0896.title: Learnable Sampler Distillation for Discrete Diffusion Models
29d3d528b8dac5e9aa8034342d41b6a48c0f0896.research_question: How can sampling efficiency in discrete diffusion models (DDMs) be improved without sacrificing generation quality, particularly when using significantly fewer sampling steps?
29d3d528b8dac5e9aa8034342d41b6a48c0f0896.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by distilling knowledge from a high-fidelity teacher sampler into a learnable student sampler—specifically by aligning intermediate score trajectories and optimizing both sampler coefficients and time schedules—DDMs can achieve high-quality generation with substantially reduced sampling steps.
29d3d528b8dac5e9aa8034342d41b6a48c0f0896.proposed_method: A novel learnable sampler distillation (LSD) framework will be developed for discrete diffusion models. The approach involves training a student sampler with a small number of steps to align its intermediate score trajectory with that of a high-quality teacher sampler that uses many steps. This alignment is achieved by optimizing a set of learnable, time-dependent coefficients that adaptively adjust the influence of the model's score at each step, compensating for errors introduced by larger step sizes. An enhanced version, LSD+, will also be proposed, which learns non-uniform time schedules in addition to the coefficients, enabling adaptive allocation of sampling steps based on the dynamics of the reverse diffusion process. The training objective will include a relaxed alignment criterion, allowing the student sampler to match the teacher's trajectory starting from perturbed initial states within a small Hamming distance, thereby improving optimization feasibility in discrete spaces.
29d3d528b8dac5e9aa8034342d41b6a48c0f0896.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across text generation, image generation, and synthetic sequence tasks. For text, pre-trained DDM backbones such as SEDD-small, SEDD-medium, and RADD (trained on OpenWebText) will be used, with generative perplexity evaluated using a GPT2-large model over 1024 samples of 1024 tokens each. For image generation, the CIFAR-10 dataset will be used, with FID scores computed on 50,000 generated samples. A synthetic countdown task will evaluate the method's ability to handle strong token dependencies, measuring error rates as the proportion of samples violating sequence rules. Baseline comparisons will include standard Euler and Tweedie samplers, the JYS method, and higher-order samplers such as θ-RK-2 and θ-trapezoidal where applicable. The number of function evaluations (NFEs) will be varied (e.g., 8, 16, 32, 64) to assess performance at different efficiency levels.
29d3d528b8dac5e9aa8034342d41b6a48c0f0896.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a distillation framework specifically tailored for discrete diffusion models, addressing the unique challenge of non-differentiability in categorical sampling by aligning intermediate score trajectories rather than final outputs. The method makes the sampler's coefficients and, in the LSD+ variant, the time schedules learnable and adaptive, enabling compensation for accumulated errors from large step sizes. The relaxed training objective using Hamming-distance-based input perturbations further improves feasibility and convergence in discrete spaces. Extensive empirical results are expected to demonstrate that these innovations enable state-of-the-art sampling quality with significantly fewer sampling steps compared to existing methods.

29dacf591970184973afb6c3ca4d0dd0b3c08693.title: GeoRanker: Distance-Aware Ranking for Worldwide Image Geolocalization
29dacf591970184973afb6c3ca4d0dd0b3c08693.research_question: How can the spatial relationships among candidate locations be effectively modeled to improve the accuracy of worldwide image geolocalization, especially at fine-grained geographic levels?
29dacf591970184973afb6c3ca4d0dd0b3c08693.hypothesis: Incorporating distance-aware ranking that leverages large vision-language models and a multi-order distance loss will enable more accurate modeling of spatial relationships among candidates, leading to improved geolocalization performance compared to existing similarity-based or pointwise methods.
29dacf591970184973afb6c3ca4d0dd0b3c08693.proposed_method: A distance-aware ranking framework, GeoRanker, will be developed to model structured spatial relationships among candidate locations for image geolocalization. The approach will leverage a large vision-language model (LVLM) to jointly encode query–candidate interactions, integrating multimodal information including images, GPS coordinates, and textual descriptions. A multi-order distance optimization objective will be introduced, combining first-order (absolute distance) and second-order (relative distance gap) losses to guide the model in ranking candidates by geographic proximity. During training, prompts will be constructed to include the query image, top-ranked candidates, and hard negatives, and LoRA modules will be used to efficiently fine-tune the LVLM. At inference, both retrieved and LVLM-generated candidates will be scored, and the candidate with the highest ranking will be selected as the predicted location.
29dacf591970184973afb6c3ca4d0dd0b3c08693.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two public benchmarks for worldwide image geolocalization: IM2GPS3K and YFCC4K. The GeoRanking dataset, specifically constructed for this study, will provide multimodal candidate sets for each query, with 100,000 samples and 2 million query–candidate pairs. Baselines for comparison will include 11 state-of-the-art methods such as [L]kNN, PlaNet, CPlaNet, ISNs, Translocator, GeoDecoder, GeoCLIP, Img2Loc, PIGEON, and G3. Evaluation metrics will report the percentage of predictions within various geodesic distance thresholds (1km, 25km, 200km, 750km, 2500km) from the ground truth. Ablation studies will assess the impact of each component, including the multi-order loss, negative samples, and multimodal information, as well as hyperparameter sensitivity and backbone model scaling. Efficiency analyses will measure inference latency and data efficiency.
29dacf591970184973afb6c3ca4d0dd0b3c08693.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a novel distance-aware ranking paradigm that explicitly models both absolute and relative spatial relationships among candidates using a multi-order distance loss. It leverages large vision-language models for joint multimodal encoding of query–candidate interactions, surpassing the limitations of independent similarity-based approaches. The GeoRanking dataset is the first to provide multimodal, spatially diverse candidate sets specifically for geographic ranking, supporting structured spatial reasoning. The method claims substantial improvements over state-of-the-art baselines at multiple geographic granularities and demonstrates superior data and time efficiency.

29db0494afb6297d2235b6a4e4358f1552bf49ad.title: On PAC-Bayesian reconstruction guarantees for VAEs
29db0494afb6297d2235b6a4e4358f1552bf49ad.research_question: What are the theoretical generalization guarantees for the reconstruction ability of variational autoencoders (VAEs), and how does the regularization effect of the VAE objective, particularly the KL term, influence generalization in terms of reconstruction on unseen data?
29db0494afb6297d2235b6a4e4358f1552bf49ad.hypothesis: Applying PAC-Bayesian theory to the VAE framework will yield computable generalization bounds on reconstruction error, and optimizing a PAC-Bayes-based objective will result in VAEs that generalize well to unseen data while providing tight risk certificates. The KL term in the VAE objective may not always serve as an effective regularizer for reconstruction generalization.
29db0494afb6297d2235b6a4e4358f1552bf49ad.proposed_method: A PAC-Bayesian framework will be developed to derive generalization bounds for the reconstruction loss of VAEs.
