The approach involves formulating both randomized and derandomized PAC-Bayes bounds on the reconstruction error, where the encoder and decoder parameters are treated as random variables with Gaussian distributions centered at learned means. The methodology includes learning a prior over the VAE parameters (encoder and decoder weights) using a subset of the data, followed by optimizing a PAC-Bayes objective that incorporates the empirical reconstruction loss and a KL divergence term between the posterior and prior over parameters. The PAC-Bayes bound is used both as a computable risk certificate and as a learning objective, with the possibility of learning the noise levels (variances) in the parameter distributions to encourage flat minima and improved generalization. A derandomized bound is also derived to provide high-probability guarantees for specific parameter instantiations.
29db0494afb6297d2235b6a4e4358f1552bf49ad.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on benchmark datasets such as binarized MNIST and Omniglot, using standard train/test splits. The encoder and decoder will be implemented as 3-layer feedforward neural networks with 400 hidden units per layer and ReLU activations, and a latent space of dimension 50. Baselines will include standard β-VAEs with varying β values, as well as PAC-Bayes VAEs with different prior learning strategies (e.g., learned with dropout, random, or zero-centered priors). The Adam optimizer will be used, and the PAC-Bayes objectives will be compared to β-VAEs in terms of test reconstruction loss, generalization gap (difference between train and test reconstruction errors), and the tightness of the computed PAC-Bayes risk certificates. The effect of techniques such as KL attenuation and dropout during prior learning will be systematically evaluated.
29db0494afb6297d2235b6a4e4358f1552bf49ad.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first PAC-Bayesian generalization bounds specifically tailored for the VAE structure, providing both theoretical and empirical insights into the reconstruction generalization properties of VAEs. The approach enables the computation of non-vacuous, data-dependent risk certificates for VAE reconstruction error, and proposes a novel PAC-Bayes-based learning objective that can be optimized directly to achieve strong generalization. The framework also clarifies the role of the KL term in VAE objectives, showing that it may not always function as an effective regularizer for reconstruction, and demonstrates that PAC-Bayes VAEs can outperform β-VAEs in terms of generalization gap while maintaining competitive reconstruction performance.

29ea8f3648264f4fa8dec627fc8726131ea72cdc.title: Spacetime Gaussian Feature Splatting for Real-Time Dynamic View Synthesis
29ea8f3648264f4fa8dec627fc8726131ea72cdc.research_question: How can dynamic scene representations be developed to enable real-time, high-resolution, photorealistic view synthesis with compact storage requirements for novel view rendering in dynamic environments?
29ea8f3648264f4fa8dec627fc8726131ea72cdc.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that extending 3D Gaussian scene representations into the spacetime domain, combined with feature-based splatting and guided sampling, will enable efficient, high-quality, real-time dynamic view synthesis while maintaining compact model size.
29ea8f3648264f4fa8dec627fc8726131ea72cdc.proposed_method: A novel dynamic scene representation will be developed based on Spacetime Gaussian Feature Splatting. The approach extends 3D Gaussians into 4D spacetime by equipping each Gaussian with temporal opacity (modeled by a temporal radial basis function), polynomially parameterized motion and rotation, and time-dependent neural features. Instead of using spherical harmonics, neural features encoding base color, view-dependent, and time-dependent information will be stored per Gaussian and rasterized to the image plane via differentiable splatting. A lightweight multi-layer perceptron (MLP) will map these splatted features to final pixel colors. Additionally, a guided sampling strategy will be introduced, leveraging training error maps and coarse depth estimates to sample new Gaussians in regions with high rendering error or sparse coverage, thus improving quality in challenging areas.
29ea8f3648264f4fa8dec627fc8726131ea72cdc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several established real-world multi-view video datasets, including the Neural 3D Video Dataset, Google Immersive Dataset, and Technicolor Dataset. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as NeRFPlayer, HyperReel, MixVoxels, K-Planes, and others, using evaluation metrics including PSNR, DSSIM, LPIPS, and rendering FPS. Both quantitative and qualitative comparisons will be performed, with model size, rendering speed, and visual fidelity as key evaluation criteria. Ablation studies will be conducted to assess the impact of temporal opacity, polynomial motion/rotation, feature-based splatting, and guided Gaussian sampling.
29ea8f3648264f4fa8dec627fc8726131ea72cdc.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces Spacetime Gaussians, extending 3D Gaussian splatting to the 4D spacetime domain with temporal opacity and parametric motion/rotation, enabling accurate modeling of static, dynamic, and transient scene content. Feature-based splatting replaces spherical harmonics with neural features, enhancing model compactness and expressiveness for time- and view-dependent appearance. A guided sampling strategy is incorporated to address sparse or challenging regions, improving rendering quality. The method claims to achieve state-of-the-art rendering quality and speed at high resolutions while maintaining a compact model size, with real-time 8K rendering demonstrated.

2a28903d52688d7bee05f1f9b8ca4ff83a825824.title: Domain-Specific Pruning of Large Mixture-of-Experts Models with Few-shot Demonstrations
2a28903d52688d7bee05f1f9b8ca4ff83a825824.research_question: How can large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models be efficiently pruned in a domain-specific manner using only a few demonstration samples, while maintaining high performance and significantly reducing memory and computational overhead?
2a28903d52688d7bee05f1f9b8ca4ff83a825824.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a small number of domain-specific demonstrations can reliably identify a sparse and stable subset of experts within large MoE models, enabling effective pruning that preserves or even enhances in-domain performance while reducing resource requirements.
2a28903d52688d7bee05f1f9b8ca4ff83a825824.proposed_method: A novel pruning framework, EASY-EP (Expert Assessment with Simple Yet-effective scoring for Expert Pruning), will be developed to enable domain-specific pruning of large MoE models. The approach begins by sampling a small set of demonstration examples from a target domain and generating model responses to form a calibration set. Two complementary components are introduced: (1) output-aware expert importance assessment, which computes the importance of each expert for each token as the product of its gating value and the L2 norm of its output; and (2) expert-level token contribution estimation, which measures the change in token representations before and after expert routing using cosine similarity, assigning higher importance to tokens with greater representational shifts. The final expert score is computed by aggregating the product of these two terms across all tokens. Top-scoring experts are retained, while others are pruned, and the process requires only a single forward pass without backpropagation.
2a28903d52688d7bee05f1f9b8ca4ff83a825824.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale MoE models, specifically DeepSeek-R1 and DeepSeek-V3-0324, across eight benchmark datasets spanning math, coding, science, finance, medicine, and agent-based task execution. For each domain, 25 demonstration samples will be used to construct the calibration set, and the top 64 or 128 experts per layer will be retained based on the EASY-EP scoring. Baseline methods will include random pruning, frequency-based pruning, gating score-based pruning, and M-SMoE expert merging. Evaluation metrics will include task-specific accuracy or performance scores, as well as throughput and memory usage. Both domain-specific and mixed-domain pruning settings will be explored, and ablation studies will assess the contribution of each component of the proposed method.
2a28903d52688d7bee05f1f9b8ca4ff83a825824.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a simple yet effective pruning method that leverages few-shot domain-specific demonstrations for expert selection in large MoE models. The method uniquely combines output-aware expert importance assessment and expert-level token contribution estimation, enabling accurate identification of critical experts with only a single forward pass. It demonstrates robust performance preservation at high compression ratios, achieves significant improvements in inference throughput under fixed memory budgets, and supports both domain-specific and mixed-domain pruning. This framework facilitates practical deployment of large MoE models by substantially reducing memory and computational requirements without sacrificing task performance.

2a3213cb3c755f036d5dfec7261d726a819c78c1.title: Muse: Text-To-Image Generation via Masked Generative Transformers
2a3213cb3c755f036d5dfec7261d726a819c78c1.research_question: How can text-to-image generation be improved in terms of efficiency, image quality, semantic alignment, and editing capabilities by leveraging masked generative transformers and discrete token representations?
2a3213cb3c755f036d5dfec7261d726a819c78c1.hypothesis: A masked generative transformer model, conditioned on embeddings from a large pre-trained language model and operating in discrete image token space, will achieve state-of-the-art text-to-image generation performance with significantly greater efficiency and enhanced editing capabilities compared to diffusion and autoregressive models.
2a3213cb3c755f036d5dfec7261d726a819c78c1.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a text-to-image generation framework based on masked generative transformers. The method utilizes a pre-trained and frozen large language model (T5-XXL) to encode text prompts into high-dimensional embeddings, which are then projected to match the hidden size of the transformer models. Images are tokenized into discrete semantic tokens using a pair of VQGAN models at different resolutions (256x256 and 512x512), enabling efficient representation and reconstruction. The base model is a masked transformer that predicts randomly masked image tokens conditioned on both the unmasked tokens and the text embedding, using cross-entropy loss for training. A super-resolution transformer further refines the output by translating low-resolution latent tokens into high-resolution tokens, again conditioned on the text embedding. The model employs variable masking rates and classifier-free guidance to improve diversity and fidelity, and utilizes iterative parallel decoding at inference for fast and efficient generation.
2a3213cb3c755f036d5dfec7261d726a819c78c1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale text-image paired datasets, including the Imagen dataset (460M pairs), CC3M, and MS-COCO. Models of varying sizes (from 632M to 3B parameters) will be trained, with the T5-XXL text encoder (4.6B parameters) kept frozen. Evaluation will be performed using Frechet Inception Distance (FID) to assess image quality and diversity, and CLIP score to measure image-text alignment. Baselines will include state-of-the-art diffusion models (e.g., Imagen, DALL-E2), autoregressive models (e.g., Parti), and other non-autoregressive and GAN-based approaches. Human evaluation will be used for qualitative assessment of prompt-image alignment. The experimental setup will also test zero-shot image editing capabilities such as inpainting, outpainting, and mask-free editing without model fine-tuning.
2a3213cb3c755f036d5dfec7261d726a819c78c1.novelty_claims: The proposed method claims significant efficiency improvements over both diffusion and autoregressive models due to the use of discrete image tokens and parallel decoding, enabling over 10x faster inference than leading alternatives. The approach achieves state-of-the-art FID and CLIP scores on standard benchmarks, demonstrating superior image quality, diversity, and semantic alignment. The architecture natively supports zero-shot, out-of-the-box image editing tasks such as inpainting, outpainting, and mask-free editing, without requiring model fine-tuning or inversion. The combination of masked modeling, discrete token space, and pre-trained language model conditioning is positioned as a key innovation enabling these advances.

2a37336354499c3170a4aaf6e72c99ca7ab04155.title: Offline Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning via Inverse Optimization
2a37336354499c3170a4aaf6e72c99ca7ab04155.research_question: How can hierarchical reinforcement learning policies be effectively learned from offline datasets, particularly when high-level actions are unobserved and the data may have been generated by arbitrary or non-hierarchical policies, in order to improve robustness, scalability, and safety in complex real-world decision-making tasks?
2a37336354499c3170a4aaf6e72c99ca7ab04155.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging structural knowledge of hierarchical policies and solving an inverse optimization problem to recover high-level actions from offline data will enable the construction of datasets suitable for standard offline RL algorithms, resulting in improved performance, robustness, and safety compared to end-to-end and traditional hierarchical RL approaches.
2a37336354499c3170a4aaf6e72c99ca7ab04155.proposed_method: A novel framework, OHIO (Offline Hierarchical reinforcement learning via Inverse Optimization), is developed to enable offline learning of hierarchical policies. The method exploits knowledge of the hierarchical policy structure, particularly the low-level policy (which may be explicit or optimization-based), to solve an inverse optimization problem that infers the most likely high-level actions responsible for observed state transitions (and optionally, low-level actions). This inversion is formulated as a regularized maximum likelihood estimation problem, utilizing either analytical or numerical optimization techniques depending on the policy class and available models. The reconstructed high-level action trajectories are then used to create a new dataset, on which standard offline RL algorithms (such as IQL, CQL, or behavioral cloning) are applied to learn the high-level policy. The approach is agnostic to the specific form of the low-level policy and can incorporate approximate or learned dynamics models as needed, ensuring applicability across a wide range of domains.
2a37336354499c3170a4aaf6e72c99ca7ab04155.experiment_details: Experiments are designed to evaluate the framework on both robotic control and real-world network optimization problems, including tasks such as goal-directed control (Reacher), robotic manipulation (RoboSuite Lift and Door), dynamic vehicle routing (NYC and Shenzhen networks), and supply chain management. Datasets are collected using a variety of behavior policies, including expert RL, optimization-based controllers, and heuristics, with both hierarchical and non-hierarchical structures. Baselines include end-to-end RL, traditional hierarchical RL, and offline RL methods without dataset reconstruction. Evaluation metrics are normalized task scores (scaled to 0-100), with additional analysis of robustness to changes in low-level policy parameters, dataset quality, and transfer to modified environments. Both direct deployment and online fine-tuning scenarios are assessed, and the impact of different inverse optimization algorithms is systematically compared.
2a37336354499c3170a4aaf6e72c99ca7ab04155.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a principled approach to offline hierarchical RL by leveraging inverse optimization to reconstruct unobserved high-level actions from arbitrary offline datasets, regardless of the original policy structure. This enables the use of standard offline RL algorithms within hierarchical policy schemes, overcoming limitations of prior methods that require matched policy structures or oracle demonstrations. The method is broadly applicable to both explicit and optimization-based low-level policies, supports both analytical and numerical inversion, and directly encodes domain-specific constraints for improved safety and robustness. Empirical results demonstrate substantial improvements in performance, scalability, and robustness over end-to-end and traditional hierarchical RL approaches, particularly in high-dimensional and safety-critical settings.

2a7a6648563e6a09e6fea6dd96e68e0563216dcb.title: Datamodels: Predicting Predictions from Training Data
2a7a6648563e6a09e6fea6dd96e68e0563216dcb.research_question: How can the relationship between training data and model predictions be systematically characterized and predicted for arbitrary machine learning algorithms and datasets?
2a7a6648563e6a09e6fea6dd96e68e0563216dcb.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a simple, parameterized surrogate model—constructed solely from knowledge of which training examples are present in a subset—can accurately predict the output of a learning algorithm on a fixed target example, even for complex models such as deep neural networks.
2a7a6648563e6a09e6fea6dd96e68e0563216dcb.proposed_method: The proposed method develops a framework called datamodeling, where for a fixed target example, a parameterized surrogate function is trained to predict the output of a learning algorithm on any subset of the training data. The surrogate function, typically instantiated as a linear model, takes as input the characteristic vector indicating the presence or absence of each training example in a subset. The output to be predicted is a continuous function of model performance on the target example, such as the correct-class margin. Training proceeds by sampling many random subsets of the training data, training models on these subsets, recording their outputs on the target example, and fitting the surrogate function via regularized least-squares regression (LASSO). The framework is designed to be scalable, with custom solvers and efficient model training pipelines, and can be extended to multiple target examples simultaneously.
2a7a6648563e6a09e6fea6dd96e68e0563216dcb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification datasets, including CIFAR-10 and Functional Map of the World (FMoW). For each dataset, a large number of deep neural networks (e.g., ResNet-9 for CIFAR-10, ResNet-18 for FMoW) will be trained from scratch on random subsets of the training data of varying sizes (e.g., α = 10%, 20%, 50%, 75%). For each target example (both from the test and training sets), datamodels will be estimated using hundreds of thousands of trained models, with separate training, validation, and test splits for the subset-output pairs. Evaluation will focus on the ability of datamodels to predict model outputs on held-out (in-distribution) and out-of-distribution subsets, using metrics such as mean squared error and Pearson/Spearman correlation. Baselines will include random selection, influence functions, and nearest-neighbor representations. Additional analyses will include counterfactual prediction (e.g., estimating the minimal set of training examples whose removal flips a prediction), identification of train-test leakage, and exploration of datamodel-based embeddings.
2a7a6648563e6a09e6fea6dd96e68e0563216dcb.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a new, general approach for modeling and predicting the behavior of machine learning algorithms in terms of their training data, applicable to arbitrary learning algorithms and datasets. The method demonstrates that even simple linear surrogate models can accurately approximate the complex mapping from training data subsets to model predictions, enabling efficient counterfactual analysis, identification of brittle predictions, detection of train-test leakage, and construction of meaningful data embeddings. This approach provides a scalable, interpretable, and practical tool for understanding and auditing the data dependence of modern machine learning systems.

2a9e7a76cfb42d1d6e47aa721833f460570712c4.title: U-KAN Makes Strong Backbone for Medical Image Segmentation and Generation
2a9e7a76cfb42d1d6e47aa721833f460570712c4.research_question: How can the integration of mathematically inspired network operators improve the accuracy, efficiency, and interpretability of backbone architectures for medical image segmentation and generative modeling, particularly in challenging and resource-constrained clinical scenarios?
2a9e7a76cfb42d1d6e47aa721833f460570712c4.hypothesis: Incorporating Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) into established encoder-decoder architectures such as U-Net will enhance the modeling of complex nonlinear patterns, leading to improved segmentation and generative performance, higher efficiency, and greater interpretability compared to conventional convolutional, transformer, or MLP-based backbones.
2a9e7a76cfb42d1d6e47aa721833f460570712c4.proposed_method: A new framework, U-KAN, will be developed by embedding tokenized Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) blocks into the U-Net backbone. The architecture will retain the standard encoder-decoder structure with skip connections, where early layers use convolutional blocks and deeper layers near the bottleneck are replaced with tokenized KAN blocks. Intermediate feature maps will be tokenized into patches, projected into a latent space, and processed through stacked KAN layers with learnable activation functions, depthwise convolutions, normalization, and residual connections. For generative tasks, time embeddings will be injected into KAN blocks to enable diffusion-based image generation, modifying the architecture to predict noise at each denoising step. The design will be scalable, with ablations on the number of KAN layers and channel widths to balance performance and computational cost.
2a9e7a76cfb42d1d6e47aa721833f460570712c4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three heterogeneous medical imaging datasets: BUSI (ultrasound breast tumor segmentation), GlaS (histology gland segmentation), and CVC-ClinicDB (colonoscopy polyp segmentation), with images resized for consistency. For segmentation, models will be trained with Adam optimizer, cosine annealing learning rate, and a combination of binary cross-entropy and dice loss, using standard data augmentations and three random splits. Baselines will include U-Net, U-Net++, Att-UNet, U-NeXt, Rolling-UNet, and U-Mamba, with evaluation metrics of Intersection over Union (IoU), F1 score, model parameters, and Gflops. For generative modeling, unconditional diffusion experiments will generate images from Gaussian noise, evaluated using Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and Inception Score (IS). Ablation studies will assess the impact of KAN layer count, replacement with MLPs, and model scaling. Qualitative and quantitative comparisons, as well as interpretability analyses using activation plausibility IoU, will be performed.
2a9e7a76cfb42d1d6e47aa721833f460570712c4.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first integration of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks into the U-Net backbone for vision tasks, providing a mathematically grounded approach to improving nonlinear modeling and interpretability. The tokenized KAN block is a novel architectural component enabling compatibility with convolutional pipelines. The method claims superior accuracy and efficiency over state-of-the-art convolutional, transformer, and MLP-based segmentation and generative models, while also enhancing model explainability. The framework is validated across diverse medical imaging tasks and demonstrates adaptability as a backbone for diffusion-based generative models, suggesting broad applicability and future extensibility to higher-dimensional and temporal data.

2abd335f39acda4ff35276ac159643b761b4c1c7.title: Deep linear networks for regression are implicitly regularized towards flat minima
2abd335f39acda4ff35276ac159643b761b4c1c7.research_question: How do the optimization dynamics of deep linear networks for univariate regression relate to the sharpness (largest Hessian eigenvalue) of minimizers, and what implicit regularization properties emerge from gradient-based training under different initialization schemes?
2abd335f39acda4ff35276ac159643b761b4c1c7.hypothesis: Gradient flow training of deep linear networks for regression implicitly regularizes solutions toward flat minima, resulting in minimizers with sharpness close to a lower bound determined by the data covariance, independent of network width or depth.
2abd335f39acda4ff35276ac159643b761b4c1c7.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted on the sharpness of minimizers in deep linear networks trained for univariate regression. The approach will analyze the landscape of the empirical risk, deriving lower and upper bounds on the sharpness of minimizers as a function of network depth and data covariance. Gradient flow dynamics will be studied under two distinct initialization schemes: small-scale Gaussian initialization and residual (identity plus Gaussian noise) initialization. For small-scale initialization, the structure of the learned weight matrices will be characterized, focusing on their rank and singular vector alignment. For residual initialization, convergence properties and the structure of the resulting minimizers will be established, leveraging high-probability bounds on singular values of products of random matrices. Theoretical results will be complemented by numerical experiments to validate the analytical findings and explore the connection to gradient descent with non-vanishing learning rates.
2abd335f39acda4ff35276ac159643b761b4c1c7.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training deep linear networks of varying depths on univariate regression tasks with quadratic loss. Synthetic datasets will be generated with controlled covariance properties to test theoretical predictions. Networks will be initialized using both small-scale Gaussian and residual schemes, with a range of initialization scales and learning rates. Baseline comparisons will include the empirical risk minimizer and theoretical sharpness bounds. Evaluation metrics will focus on the squared distance to the empirical risk minimizer, sharpness (largest Hessian eigenvalue), and convergence behavior. Key experimental setups will explore the effect of learning rate, initialization scale, and network depth on trainability and sharpness, with results visualized through training curves and sharpness evolution.
2abd335f39acda4ff35276ac159643b761b4c1c7.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces new theoretical bounds on the minimal sharpness of minimizers in deep linear regression networks, showing that sharpness grows linearly with depth but is bounded below by a function of the data covariance. It claims to establish, for the first time, that gradient flow dynamics in both small-scale and residual initialization regimes implicitly regularize toward flat minima, with sharpness close to the theoretical lower bound and independent of width or depth. The analysis provides novel characterizations of the structure of minimizers, including approximate rank-one weights and singular vector alignment for small-scale initialization, and bounded perturbations from identity for residual initialization. The work also presents new high-probability bounds for singular values of products of random matrices in the context of deep residual networks.

2ac231b9cff4f5f9054d86c9b540429d4dd687f4.title: A Practical Review of Mechanistic Interpretability for Transformer-Based Language Models
2ac231b9cff4f5f9054d86c9b540429d4dd687f4.research_question: How can mechanistic interpretability be systematically advanced to reverse-engineer and understand the internal computations of transformer-based language models, and what workflows, techniques, and evaluation methods can be developed to guide researchers in this field?
2ac231b9cff4f5f9054d86c9b540429d4dd687f4.hypothesis: Mechanistic interpretability techniques, when organized around a task-centric taxonomy and actionable workflows, can provide comprehensive, human-understandable insights into the features, circuits, and universality of transformer-based language models, thereby improving both practical understanding and application.
2ac231b9cff4f5f9054d86c9b540429d4dd687f4.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed that organizes mechanistic interpretability research into three core tasks: feature study, circuit study, and universality study. For each task, detailed, step-by-step workflows will be designed, including targeted and open-ended feature discovery, circuit localization and explanation, and systematic evaluation of universality across models and tasks. The methodology will integrate and compare a range of interpretability techniques, such as vocabulary projection, intervention-based methods, sparse autoencoders, probing, and visualization, specifying their technical details, advantages, and limitations. Actionable guidance will be provided for each workflow step, including hypothesis generation, observation, computational graph definition, and evaluation, to enable both newcomers and experienced practitioners to select and apply the most appropriate methods.
2ac231b9cff4f5f9054d86c9b540429d4dd687f4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of transformer-based language models, ranging from small-scale to state-of-the-art models, using both synthetic and real-world datasets. Baselines will include existing interpretability techniques and prior mechanistic analyses. Evaluation metrics will encompass both quantitative measures (e.g., accuracy of feature detection, circuit localization precision, cross-model generalization) and qualitative assessments (e.g., human-interpretability of explanations, practical utility in downstream tasks). Standardized benchmarks for feature and circuit interpretability will be utilized, and case studies will be performed to demonstrate the practical application of the proposed workflows.
2ac231b9cff4f5f9054d86c9b540429d4dd687f4.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a task-centric taxonomy and actionable roadmap for mechanistic interpretability, moving beyond technique-centric surveys by providing detailed, stepwise workflows for feature, circuit, and universality studies. The framework systematically integrates technical details, comparative analysis, and practical guidance, enabling both structured research and practical application. The approach also emphasizes the development and use of standardized evaluation benchmarks and metrics, as well as the potential for automated hypothesis generation and broader human-AI collaboration driven by mechanistic insights.

2ac4fb1e431276536d5eb5313ce6001cdbc7b603.title: OccFormer: Dual-path Transformer for Vision-based 3D Semantic Occupancy Prediction
2ac4fb1e431276536d5eb5313ce6001cdbc7b603.research_question: How can vision-based systems for autonomous driving achieve more accurate and efficient 3D semantic occupancy prediction from camera images, overcoming the limitations of existing BEV and 3D convolutional approaches?
2ac4fb1e431276536d5eb5313ce6001cdbc7b603.hypothesis: A dual-path transformer network that decomposes 3D feature processing into local and global pathways, combined with transformer-based mask classification and specialized pooling and sampling strategies, will enable more accurate and efficient 3D semantic occupancy prediction from camera images than existing methods.
2ac4fb1e431276536d5eb5313ce6001cdbc7b603.proposed_method: A novel dual-path transformer framework, OccFormer, will be developed for vision-based 3D semantic occupancy prediction. The method begins with an image encoder (e.g., EfficientNetB7 or ResNet-101) to extract multi-scale 2D features from monocular or multi-camera images. These features are lifted to a 3D voxel feature volume using a depth distribution and voxel pooling mechanism inspired by LSS. The dual-path transformer encoder processes the 3D volume: the local path applies shared windowed self-attention to each horizontal slice for fine-grained semantic extraction, while the global path aggregates scene-level semantics via average pooling along the height and ASPP modules. Outputs from both paths are fused using a sigmoid-weighted summation. For decoding, a transformer-based occupancy decoder adapts Mask2Former for 3D, introducing preserve-pooling (max-pooling for mask downsampling) and class-guided sampling (sampling voxels based on class frequency) to address sparsity and class imbalance. The final occupancy prediction is formulated as a set of mask classification queries over the 3D voxel grid.
2ac4fb1e431276536d5eb5313ce6001cdbc7b603.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the SemanticKITTI and nuScenes datasets. For SemanticKITTI, the model will be trained and evaluated on the semantic scene completion task using monocular images, with ground-truth occupancy represented as 256x256x32 voxel grids and 21 semantic classes. For nuScenes, the model will be trained for LiDAR semantic segmentation using multi-camera images and sparse LiDAR supervision. Baselines will include state-of-the-art monocular and multi-view methods such as MonoScene, TPVFormer, LMSCNet, and LiDAR-based segmentation models. Evaluation metrics will be mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) for both semantic scene completion and LiDAR segmentation, as well as class-agnostic IoU for scene completion. Ablation studies will examine the impact of the dual-path encoder, pixel decoder, transformer decoder, pooling and sampling strategies, and data augmentations.
2ac4fb1e431276536d5eb5313ce6001cdbc7b603.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first dual-path transformer encoder for efficient and dynamic 3D feature processing in vision-based semantic occupancy prediction. It is also the first to adapt transformer-based mask classification (Mask2Former) to 3D occupancy, with novel modifications including preserve-pooling for sparse mask downsampling and class-guided sampling to address class imbalance. The method achieves state-of-the-art performance on SemanticKITTI for semantic scene completion and on nuScenes for camera-based LiDAR segmentation, outperforming both monocular and multi-view baselines. The dual-path design and tailored decoder strategies provide significant improvements in efficiency, accuracy, and the ability to recover fine-grained and scene-level semantics from camera images.

2ac7f3e729af4f902d4fa6fe2d0e956679053277.title: DiBS: Differentiable Bayesian Structure Learning
2ac7f3e729af4f902d4fa6fe2d0e956679053277.research_question: How can Bayesian structure learning be made fully differentiable and scalable, enabling joint posterior inference over both graph structures and conditional distribution parameters for complex Bayesian networks, including those with nonlinear dependencies?
2ac7f3e729af4f902d4fa6fe2d0e956679053277.hypothesis: A continuous latent variable framework for representing directed acyclic graphs, combined with differentiable Bayesian inference techniques, enables efficient and accurate joint posterior inference over both graph structures and parameters for a wide range of Bayesian network models, including those with nonlinear relationships.
2ac7f3e729af4f902d4fa6fe2d0e956679053277.proposed_method: A fully differentiable framework for Bayesian structure learning is developed by introducing a continuous latent variable representation of directed acyclic graphs (DAGs). The method defines a latent variable Z, composed of node embeddings, which probabilistically generates the adjacency matrix of a graph via a bilinear inner product and a sigmoid function. A prior over Z is designed to softly enforce acyclicity using a Gibbs distribution penalizing expected cyclicity, while also incorporating standard graph priors (e.g., sparsity, scale-free structure) as additional factors. Posterior inference is performed in the latent space using gradient-based variational inference, specifically Stein Variational Gradient Descent (SVGD), leveraging differentiable estimators such as the Gumbel-softmax trick or score function estimators depending on the differentiability of the likelihood. The framework supports joint inference over both graph structures and conditional distribution parameters, and is agnostic to the form of the local conditionals, allowing for nonlinear parameterizations (e.g., neural networks).
2ac7f3e729af4f902d4fa6fe2d0e956679053277.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic experiments use Bayesian networks with 20 and 50 nodes, generated with Erdős-Rényi and scale-free random structures, and include both linear and nonlinear (neural network parameterized) Gaussian conditional distributions. For each graph, training, held-out, and interventional datasets are generated, with 100 observations used for inference. Evaluation metrics include expected structural Hamming distance (E-SHD), area under the ROC curve (AUROC) for edge prediction, negative (marginal) log-likelihood on held-out data, and interventional log-likelihood. Baselines include structure MCMC (MC3), bootstrap methods with PC and GES algorithms, and variants of joint parameter-structure MCMC. The method is also applied to the Sachs protein signaling dataset (11 variables, 7,466 samples), comparing both linear and nonlinear Gaussian Bayesian networks. Experiments are run for 3,000 SVGD iterations with latent dimension equal to the number of nodes, and results are averaged over multiple random restarts or synthetic graph instances.
2ac7f3e729af4f902d4fa6fe2d0e956679053277.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a general, fully differentiable framework for Bayesian structure learning that operates in a continuous latent space, enabling joint posterior inference over both graph structures and parameters. Unlike prior methods, the framework is agnostic to the form of the local conditional distributions, supporting complex and nonlinear Bayesian network models. The method integrates acyclicity constraints directly into the latent prior, allowing for scalable and efficient inference using black-box variational techniques. Experimental results demonstrate superior or competitive performance compared to existing methods, particularly in settings involving nonlinear dependencies and joint inference, and establish the feasibility of Bayesian inference for expressive, neural network-parameterized Bayesian networks.

2ad49013277354e95df6396be036a5b50341dd22.title: Knee-Deep in C-RASP: A Transformer Depth Hierarchy
2ad49013277354e95df6396be036a5b50341dd22.research_question: What are the formal expressive capabilities gained by increasing the depth of transformer architectures, and how does depth impact the ability of transformers to model sequential dependencies in language tasks?
2ad49013277354e95df6396be036a5b50341dd22.hypothesis: Deeper transformer models possess strictly greater expressive power than shallower ones, enabling them to recognize and model more complex sequential dependencies, as characterized by a formal depth hierarchy.
2ad49013277354e95df6396be036a5b50341dd22.proposed_method: A formal theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the expressive power of transformers as a function of their depth. This will be accomplished by establishing an exact equivalence between fixed-precision transformers (with rounding applied only outside attention mechanisms) and a temporal logic with counting operators, TL[#], as well as the programming language C-RASP. The depth of a transformer will be mapped to the nesting depth of logical operators in TL[#] and the corresponding depth in C-RASP programs, allowing for a precise characterization of the depth hierarchy. Theoretical results will be complemented by constructing separating languages (e.g., L_k) that require increasing depth to be recognized, and by extending the analysis to transformers with various positional encodings such as RoPE and ALiBi.
2ad49013277354e95df6396be036a5b50341dd22.experiment_details: Empirical validation will be conducted by training future-masked transformers without positional encodings on a family of formal languages (L_k) that require increasing depth to model their sequential dependencies. For each k, datasets will be generated by uniformly sampling strings of length 201–400, with training, validation, and test splits. The next-token prediction problem will be used as the evaluation task, where the model must predict the set of possible next symbols at each position. Models of varying depth will be compared, and accuracy will be measured as the percentage of strings for which the model predicts the correct next-token set at every position. Hyperparameters such as model dimension and learning rate will be tuned, and experiments will be run on a GPU cluster. Baselines will include transformer models of different depths, and results will be analyzed to determine the minimum depth required to achieve perfect accuracy for each L_k.
2ad49013277354e95df6396be036a5b50341dd22.novelty_claims: The proposed research establishes, for the first time, an exact depth-preserving equivalence between a subclass of fixed-precision transformers and a well-defined temporal logic (TL[#]) and programming language (C-RASP). It proves a strict depth hierarchy for these models, demonstrating that each additional layer enables the recognition of strictly more complex languages. The approach is parameter-uniform, meaning the results hold for transformers whose parameters are independent of input length, making them directly relevant to length generalization. The research also extends depth hierarchy results to transformers with several commonly used positional encodings and provides empirical evidence that the theoretical predictions closely match the observed depth requirements in practice.

2adbe699326679485ff22131da2d3de9aca789d1.title: Continuous Bayesian Model Selection for Multivariate Causal Discovery
2adbe699326679485ff22131da2d3de9aca789d1.research_question: How can causal discovery in multivariate systems be achieved without relying on restrictive model assumptions or infeasible interventional data, and can Bayesian model selection provide a scalable and effective solution for identifying unique causal structures in real-world settings?
2adbe699326679485ff22131da2d3de9aca789d1.hypothesis: Bayesian model selection, when combined with flexible nonparametric models and continuous optimization techniques, enables accurate and scalable multivariate causal discovery without requiring restrictive functional assumptions or exhaustive enumeration of all possible causal graphs.
2adbe699326679485ff22131da2d3de9aca789d1.proposed_method: A scalable framework for multivariate causal discovery will be developed by leveraging a continuous relaxation of the discrete model selection problem. The approach employs the Causal Gaussian Process Conditional Density Estimator (CGP-CDE) as a Bayesian nonparametric model for each variable, where the hyperparameters of the model are interpreted as a continuous adjacency matrix representing the causal graph. This adjacency matrix is optimized using the marginal likelihood (evidence) of the Bayesian model, combined with a spectral acyclicity regularizer to ensure the resulting graph is a valid Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG). Variational inference is used to approximate the marginal likelihood, enabling efficient optimization even for large numbers of variables. A prior is placed on the graph structure via the hyperparameters to encourage sparsity and avoid bias toward dense graphs.
2adbe699326679485ff22131da2d3de9aca789d1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and semi-synthetic datasets to evaluate the proposed method. Synthetic data will be generated from both the CGP-CDE model itself and from randomly initialized neural networks to assess robustness to model misspecification. Graph sizes will range from small (3 variables) to large (50 variables), with various graph densities (e.g., Erdos-Renyi and scale-free graphs). The method will also be tested on the Syntren benchmark, a semi-synthetic gene regulatory network dataset. Baseline comparisons will include non-Bayesian continuous optimization methods (e.g., NOTEARS, SDCD), order-based methods (e.g., SCORE, NOGAM, CAM), and Bayesian methods (e.g., DiBS). Evaluation metrics will include Structural Hamming Distance (SHD), Structural Intervention Distance (SID), and F1 score, with performance assessed across multiple random seeds and datasets. Ablation studies will be performed to analyze the impact of model flexibility and optimization choices.
2adbe699326679485ff22131da2d3de9aca789d1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a scalable Bayesian model selection framework for multivariate causal discovery that does not require restrictive functional assumptions or exhaustive enumeration of all possible DAGs. By leveraging a continuous relaxation of the adjacency matrix and employing a flexible nonparametric model (CGP-CDE), the method enables practical and accurate causal discovery in high-dimensional settings. The approach demonstrates that Bayesian model selection can distinguish between causal structures even when identifiability is not strictly guaranteed, offering improved real-world applicability and robustness compared to existing methods. Empirical results are expected to show superior performance over both Bayesian and non-Bayesian baselines, particularly in scenarios where model assumptions are violated.

2b14d9e190022e388476ebb24eb1a84349ca0de4.title: Silkie: Preference Distillation for Large Visual Language Models
2b14d9e190022e388476ebb24eb1a84349ca0de4.research_question: How can preference distillation be leveraged to improve the alignment, helpfulness, and visual faithfulness of large vision-language models (LVLMs) across diverse multi-modal tasks?
2b14d9e190022e388476ebb24eb1a84349ca0de4.hypothesis: Distilling AI-annotated preference data into LVLMs using direct preference optimization will enhance the models' helpfulness, visual faithfulness, and ethical alignment, leading to improved performance on multi-modal benchmarks compared to models trained with human-annotated or heuristic preference datasets.
2b14d9e190022e388476ebb24eb1a84349ca0de4.proposed_method: A large-scale vision-language feedback (VLFeedback) dataset will be constructed by aggregating multi-modal instructions from a variety of domains, including general vision-language, academic, robustness-oriented, and domain-specific tasks. For each instruction, responses will be generated by sampling from a pool of 12 diverse LVLMs. These responses will be evaluated and ranked by GPT-4V according to helpfulness, visual faithfulness, and ethical considerations using detailed annotation templates. The resulting preference rankings will be distilled into a target LVLM (Qwen-VL-Chat) using the Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) algorithm, which directly optimizes the model based on preference pairs without requiring an explicit reward model. Model fine-tuning will utilize LoRA for parameter-efficient adaptation and a cosine learning rate schedule for stable training.
2b14d9e190022e388476ebb24eb1a84349ca0de4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using Qwen-VL-Chat-v1.1 (7B) as the base model, with training performed for 3 epochs using the AdamW optimizer and LoRA tuning on 16 NVIDIA-A100 GPUs. Evaluation will be carried out on multiple multi-modal benchmarks, including MME (with perception and cognition splits), MMHal-Bench for hallucination/faithfulness, and MM-Vet for generalization. Baselines will include various LLaVA-series models, RLHF-trained models, and models fine-tuned with human-annotated or heuristic preference data. Evaluation metrics will include benchmark-specific scores for perception, cognition, and hallucination, as well as relative improvements over the base model. Agreement between AI and human annotators will also be assessed to validate annotation quality.
2b14d9e190022e388476ebb24eb1a84349ca0de4.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a scalable, AI-annotated preference dataset (VLFeedback) covering 80,000 multi-modal instructions and responses from 12 LVLMs, annotated across three curated aspects. It pioneers the application of direct preference optimization (DPO) for distilling AI preferences into LVLMs, bypassing the need for reward modeling and enabling efficient, stable training. The approach is claimed to yield more comprehensive and consistent improvements in fine-grained perception and complex cognition tasks compared to human-annotated or heuristic preference datasets, and to set new state-of-the-art results on hallucination and multi-modal evaluation benchmarks.

2b26b17fe3a909bc0f5408b3328308153b31f22e.title: Convolutions Die Hard: Open-Vocabulary Segmentation with Single Frozen Convolutional CLIP
2b26b17fe3a909bc0f5408b3328308153b31f22e.research_question: How can open-vocabulary segmentation be performed efficiently and accurately in a single-stage framework, leveraging shared multi-modal vision-language representations, to enable recognition and segmentation of arbitrary categories, including those unseen during training, across diverse environments?
2b26b17fe3a909bc0f5408b3328308153b31f22e.hypothesis: A single-stage open-vocabulary segmentation framework, built upon a shared frozen convolutional CLIP backbone, can achieve superior accuracy, efficiency, and generalization to novel categories compared to existing two-stage pipelines that separately generate masks and perform classification.
2b26b17fe3a909bc0f5408b3328308153b31f22e.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a single-stage open-vocabulary segmentation architecture, termed FC-CLIP, which utilizes a shared frozen convolutional CLIP backbone (e.g., ConvNeXt-Large CLIP pretrained on LAION-2B) for both mask generation and classification. A pixel decoder with multi-scale deformable attention enhances the backbone features, and a series of mask decoders generate class-agnostic mask proposals using object queries and masked cross-attention. For classification, two branches are employed: an in-vocabulary classifier that pools pixel decoder features and matches them with category text embeddings in a contrastive manner, and an out-of-vocabulary classifier that pools features directly from the frozen CLIP backbone to preserve open-vocabulary recognition. During inference, geometric ensembling fuses the predictions from both classifiers. The architecture is designed to maintain the alignment of image and text features, avoid feature duplication, and generalize well to high-resolution inputs due to the convolutional nature of the backbone.
2b26b17fe3a909bc0f5408b3328308153b31f22e.experiment_details: Experiments will train the model on the COCO panoptic dataset, using standard training recipes and losses (AdamW optimizer, 50 epochs, crop size 1024x1024, batch size 16). Zero-shot evaluation will be conducted on ADE20K, Cityscapes, and Mapillary Vistas for panoptic and semantic segmentation, with additional benchmarks including A-847, PC-459, A-150, and PC-59. Baselines for comparison include MaskCLIP, FreeSeg, ODISE, SAN, and other state-of-the-art open-vocabulary segmentation models. Evaluation metrics will include Panoptic Quality (PQ), Average Precision (AP), mean Intersection-over-Union (mIoU), and inference speed (FPS). The model will be compared in terms of accuracy, parameter efficiency, and runtime, with ablation studies on backbone freezing and input resolution generalization.
2b26b17fe3a909bc0f5408b3328308153b31f22e.novelty_claims: The method proposes the first single-stage open-vocabulary segmentation framework that unifies mask generation and classification using a shared frozen convolutional CLIP backbone. It demonstrates that a convolutional CLIP backbone generalizes better to high-resolution dense prediction tasks than ViT-based CLIP, enabling both efficient and effective segmentation. The approach achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple open-vocabulary segmentation benchmarks while significantly reducing computational cost, parameter count, and inference time compared to prior two-stage methods. The design also preserves open-vocabulary recognition by maintaining pretrained image-text alignment and introduces a novel dual-branch classification scheme for both seen and unseen categories.

2b2e20068f38f4ca7e46e9267306eb7fe9ee471f.title: Sampling 3D Molecular Conformers with Diffusion Transformers
2b2e20068f38f4ca7e46e9267306eb7fe9ee471f.research_question: How can diffusion transformer architectures be adapted and optimized for the generation of physically valid and diverse 3D molecular conformers, while effectively incorporating molecular graph information and Euclidean symmetries, and scaling to molecules of varying sizes and complexities?
2b2e20068f38f4ca7e46e9267306eb7fe9ee471f.hypothesis: Integrating modular conditioning strategies based on molecular graph information and employing flexible self-attention mechanisms—including both non-equivariant and SO(3)-equivariant formulations—within a diffusion transformer framework will enable accurate, efficient, and scalable generation of 3D molecular conformers that achieve or surpass state-of-the-art precision, physical validity, and generalization to larger, previously unseen molecules.
2b2e20068f38f4ca7e46e9267306eb7fe9ee471f.proposed_method: A novel diffusion transformer-based framework, DiTMC, will be developed for 3D molecular conformer generation. The architecture will separate the processing of 3D atomic coordinates from conditioning on atomic connectivity, utilizing both atom-wise and pair-wise conditioning tokens derived from molecular graphs. The model will incorporate multiple positional embedding strategies—absolute, relative, and SO(3)-equivariant Euclidean embeddings—to encode atomic positions, enabling systematic exploration of the impact of Euclidean symmetries. Self-attention mechanisms will be modular, supporting both standard and SO(3)-equivariant formulations, allowing for a trade-off between computational efficiency and sample fidelity. The generative process will be formulated as conditional flow matching, learning a time-dependent vector field that transforms samples from a base distribution to the target conformer distribution via an ODE-based probability flow.
2b2e20068f38f4ca7e46e9267306eb7fe9ee471f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the GEOM dataset, including QM9 (small molecules), DRUGS (drug-like molecules), and XL (large out-of-distribution molecules), with reference conformers generated using CREST. Evaluation will utilize metrics such as average minimum RMSD (AMR), coverage (COV) for recall and precision, and median absolute error (MAE) of ensemble properties (e.g., energy, dipole moment). Baselines will include state-of-the-art methods such as GeoMol, GeoDiff, TorsionDiff, MCF, DMT, and ET-Flow. Ablation studies will systematically compare different conditioning strategies (atom-wise, pair-wise, geodesic distances), positional embeddings, and self-attention mechanisms. Model scaling experiments will assess performance as a function of model size, and computational efficiency will be benchmarked in terms of wall clock time per generated conformer. Generalization will be tested on GEOM-XL to evaluate performance on larger, previously unseen molecules.
2b2e20068f38f4ca7e46e9267306eb7fe9ee471f.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces two complementary graph-based conditioning strategies that integrate seamlessly with diffusion transformer architectures, enabling conditioning on both atom-wise and pair-wise (including geodesic) molecular graph information. The modular design supports interchangeable self-attention blocks and positional embeddings, allowing systematic investigation of the impact of Euclidean symmetries on generative performance. The approach demonstrates that non-equivariant, scalable transformer variants can achieve state-of-the-art precision and physical validity on established benchmarks, while SO(3)-equivariant models further improve sample fidelity at increased computational cost. The method achieves superior or competitive results compared to existing baselines, particularly in terms of physical validity and generalization to larger molecules, using significantly fewer parameters.

2b6dca7caa80ff249b498cce0eabcfc2c36c76a1.title: FlexWorld: Progressively Expanding 3D Scenes for Flexiable-View Synthesis
2b6dca7caa80ff249b498cce0eabcfc2c36c76a1.research_question: How can flexible-view 3D scenes, supporting arbitrary camera trajectories such as 360° rotation and zooming, be generated from a single image in the absence of multi-view 3D data?
2b6dca7caa80ff249b498cce0eabcfc2c36c76a1.hypothesis: A progressive framework that combines a strong video-to-video diffusion model with geometry-aware 3D scene expansion can generate high-quality, flexible-view 3D scenes from single images, outperforming existing methods in visual fidelity and camera controllability.
2b6dca7caa80ff249b498cce0eabcfc2c36c76a1.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a two-stage framework. First, a video-to-video (V2V) diffusion model, fine-tuned on advanced video foundation models and accurate depth-estimated training pairs, generates high-quality novel view videos from incomplete inputs rendered from a coarse 3D scene. Second, a progressive 3D scene expansion process is employed, which involves planning camera trajectories to explore unseen regions, extracting new 3D content using dense stereo models, and integrating this content into a persistent global 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) representation. The integration step aligns and fuses new point clouds into the global scene, followed by a refinement process using image diffusion models to enhance visual quality. The entire pipeline iteratively expands the 3D scene, enabling rendering from arbitrary viewpoints.
2b6dca7caa80ff249b498cce0eabcfc2c36c76a1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the RealEstate10K and Tanks-and-Temples datasets, which are not used in training. The evaluation will compare the proposed method against several state-of-the-art baselines for both novel view synthesis (MotionCtrl, CameraCtrl, DimensionX, See3D, ViewCrafter) and 3D scene generation (LucidDreamer, DimensionX, See3D, ViewCrafter). Metrics such as FID, FVD, PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and camera pose errors (R_err, T_err) will be used to assess visual quality, similarity to ground truth, and camera controllability. The V2V model will be trained at 480×720 resolution using the DL3DV-10K dataset, with careful filtering for camera annotation quality. Ablation studies will evaluate the necessity of each pipeline component.
2b6dca7caa80ff249b498cce0eabcfc2c36c76a1.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a progressive, geometry-aware scene expansion strategy that enables flexible-view 3D scene generation from a single image. It leverages a fine-tuned video-to-video diffusion model conditioned on videos rather than images, trained with more accurate 3DGS-based depth estimation for superior consistency under large camera variations. The method integrates new 3D content into a persistent global scene representation and refines it for high-fidelity rendering, achieving superior results in both visual quality and camera controllability compared to existing baselines.

2b7b634405f02d205d12099354fe6ef0988a1c50.title: SuperCLIP: CLIP with Simple Classification Supervision
2b7b634405f02d205d12099354fe6ef0988a1c50.research_question: How can vision-language pretraining models be enhanced to better leverage fine-grained semantic signals in text, particularly for improved visual-text alignment and downstream task performance, without requiring additional annotated data or significant computational overhead?
2b7b634405f02d205d12099354fe6ef0988a1c50.hypothesis: Incorporating classification-based supervision at the token level into the contrastive learning paradigm of vision-language pretraining will enable more effective utilization of fine-grained textual semantics, resulting in improved visual-text alignment and superior performance across classification, retrieval, and purely visual tasks, while remaining efficient and annotation-free.
2b7b634405f02d205d12099354fe6ef0988a1c50.proposed_method: A new framework, SuperCLIP, is proposed that augments the standard contrastive learning objective of CLIP-style models with a classification-based supervision signal. Specifically, a lightweight linear layer is added to the vision encoder, mapping averaged image features to a vocabulary-sized classification target derived from the raw text tokens in the paired caption. Each caption is tokenized using CLIP's subword tokenizer, and an inverse document frequency (IDF) weighting is applied to emphasize discriminative tokens. The resulting weighted K-hot label distribution is used as the target for a cross-entropy classification loss, which is combined with the original contrastive loss. This approach ensures that the model is directly supervised to align image features with all semantic entities in the text, promoting fine-grained visual-text alignment. The method is designed to introduce minimal computational overhead (approximately 0.077% increase in FLOPs) and does not require any additional annotated data.
2b7b634405f02d205d12099354fe6ef0988a1c50.experiment_details: Experiments will involve pretraining the proposed method and baseline CLIP models on large-scale image-text datasets such as DataComp-1B (1.3B image-text pairs), with additional experiments using Recap-DataComp-1B for long, semantically rich captions. Evaluation will be conducted on zero-shot image classification (ImageNet-1K val/v2), image-text retrieval (COCO, Flickr30K), and purely visual tasks (semantic segmentation on PASCAL/ADE20K, depth estimation on NYUv2). Baselines will include standard CLIP, as well as other CLIP-style models such as SigLIP and FLIP. Metrics will include classification accuracy, Recall@1 for retrieval, mean IoU for segmentation, and RMSE for depth estimation. Experiments will also assess the impact of batch size, loss weighting, and IDF weighting, and the method's generalization to multi-modal LLM settings (e.g., integration into LLaVA-1.5 with Vicuna-7B).
2b7b634405f02d205d12099354fe6ef0988a1c50.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a simple yet effective classification-based supervision mechanism into the contrastive pretraining paradigm, enabling the model to recover and utilize rich semantic signals from all text tokens without additional annotations or significant computational cost. The approach achieves improved fine-grained visual-text alignment, mitigates performance degradation under small-batch training, and generalizes effectively to other CLIP-style models and multi-modal LLMs. The method is highly scalable, easy to implement, and demonstrates consistent performance gains across a wide range of vision-language and purely visual benchmarks.

2b7bec81a6ece230ae9361c22336f8a0c70ada5d.title: Simplicity Bias in 1-Hidden Layer Neural Networks
2b7bec81a6ece230ae9361c22336f8a0c70ada5d.research_question: Do 1-hidden layer neural networks exhibit a bias towards learning simple, low-dimensional features, even when more complex and robust features are available, and how can this bias be characterized and mitigated in practical and theoretical settings?
2b7bec81a6ece230ae9361c22336f8a0c70ada5d.hypothesis: 1-hidden layer neural networks trained with gradient descent will predominantly rely on the simplest, linearly separable features in the data, ignoring more complex but potentially more robust features, leading to a simplicity bias that can be rigorously defined and empirically observed. Furthermore, training successive models on orthogonalized feature subspaces will yield more diverse and robust classifiers.
2b7bec81a6ece230ae9361c22336f8a0c70ada5d.proposed_method: A rigorous definition of simplicity bias (SB) is introduced for 1-hidden layer neural networks, formalized as low-dimensional subspace dependence (LD-SB), where the network's output is primarily determined by a low-rank projection of the input. Theoretical analysis is conducted under the independent features model (IFM), demonstrating that, for linearly separable data, gradient descent converges to solutions that depend almost exclusively on the simplest (linearly separable) feature. Empirical verification is performed by training 1-hidden layer neural networks (with frozen pretrained backbones) on real datasets, extracting the effective rank of the first layer weights, and evaluating the model's dependence on low-dimensional projections. To mitigate SB, a sequential ensemble method (OrthoP) is proposed: after training an initial model, subsequent models are trained on input representations projected onto the orthogonal complement of the subspace used by previous models, encouraging feature diversity.
2b7bec81a6ece230ae9361c22336f8a0c70ada5d.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both semi-synthetic and real-world datasets, including Imagenette (binary and multiclass), Waterbirds-Landbirds, and MNIST-CIFAR. Feature representations are extracted using a pretrained ResNet-50 backbone, with only the 1-hidden layer head trained for classification. The effective rank of the first layer is monitored during training to assess low-dimensional dependence. LD-SB is empirically validated by measuring the model's accuracy and logit stability when inputs are mixed along identified subspaces. Baselines include independently trained models and ensembles, with diversity and robustness evaluated using metrics such as mistake diversity, class-conditioned logit correlation, and robustness to Gaussian noise perturbations. The OrthoP ensemble is compared to standard ensembles to demonstrate improved robustness and feature diversity.
2b7bec81a6ece230ae9361c22336f8a0c70ada5d.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a precise, general, and theoretically grounded definition of simplicity bias (LD-SB) for 1-hidden layer neural networks, moving beyond prior work limited to semi-synthetic datasets. It provides the first rigorous theoretical characterization of SB in the IFM setting and demonstrates its empirical manifestation on real datasets. The OrthoP ensemble method is proposed as a novel approach to encourage feature diversity and robustness by sequentially training models on orthogonalized subspaces, with theoretical and empirical evidence supporting its effectiveness.

2b9fd9d034d5ee3f5d83038454b6b0ef2b17285c.title: On the number of regions of piecewise linear neural networks
2b9fd9d034d5ee3f5d83038454b6b0ef2b17285c.research_question: How can the expressiveness of continuous and piecewise-linear (CPWL) neural networks be quantitatively characterized in terms of the number of linear regions, and how do depth, width, and activation complexity contribute to this expressiveness for arbitrary CPWL activation functions?
2b9fd9d034d5ee3f5d83038454b6b0ef2b17285c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the maximal number of linear regions in CPWL neural networks grows exponentially with network depth and polynomially with width and activation complexity, and that under reasonable stochastic assumptions, the average number of linear regions along a 1D path is bounded by the product of depth, width, and activation complexity, thus assigning equivalent roles to these factors in terms of expressiveness.
2b9fd9d034d5ee3f5d83038454b6b0ef2b17285c.proposed_method: A comprehensive mathematical framework will be developed to generalize existing bounds on the number of linear regions from specific architectures (such as ReLU and Maxout networks) to neural networks with arbitrary, possibly multivariate, CPWL activation functions. The approach will introduce the concept of arrangements of convex partitions, extending the classical theory of hyperplane arrangements, and derive tight upper and lower bounds on the maximal number of linear regions produced by operations such as sum, vectorization, and composition of CPWL functions. The framework will also include a stochastic analysis to estimate the expected number of linear regions along 1D paths for random CPWL neural networks. Key technical steps will involve combinatorial geometry, properties of convex partitions, and probabilistic analysis under random parameterizations.
2b9fd9d034d5ee3f5d83038454b6b0ef2b17285c.experiment_details: The experimental plan involves both theoretical analysis and empirical validation. Theoretical results will be derived for a variety of CPWL neural network architectures, including those with ReLU, Maxout, GroupSort, PWLU, and other CPWL activations, considering different depths, widths, and activation complexities. Empirical experiments will be conducted by constructing neural networks with varying architectures and randomly initialized parameters, then numerically estimating the number of linear regions (both maximal and average along 1D paths) using synthetic datasets and computational geometry tools. Baseline comparisons will include previously established bounds for ReLU and Maxout networks. Evaluation metrics will focus on the tightness of the derived bounds, the observed growth rates of region counts with respect to architectural parameters, and the agreement between theoretical predictions and empirical measurements.
2b9fd9d034d5ee3f5d83038454b6b0ef2b17285c.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a generalization of hyperplane arrangement theory to arrangements of convex partitions, enabling the derivation of tight and broadly applicable bounds on the number of linear regions in CPWL neural networks with arbitrary activation functions. It provides the first unified framework to analyze the expressiveness of such networks in terms of depth, width, and activation complexity, extending beyond the limitations of prior work focused on specific activations. The stochastic framework for estimating average region counts offers new insights into the typical expressiveness of random CPWL networks, revealing that depth does not always yield exponential growth in average cases. These contributions advance the theoretical understanding of neural network expressiveness and offer practical tools for architecture design.

2bd386807b0a0f3c987dae1d4b6326df41771df7.title: DOTA: Distributional Test-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language Models
2bd386807b0a0f3c987dae1d4b6326df41771df7.research_question: How can vision-language models be effectively and efficiently adapted at test time to new and evolving data distributions, particularly under significant distribution shifts, without incurring the computational cost and instability associated with traditional fine-tuning or cache-based adaptation methods?
2bd386807b0a0f3c987dae1d4b6326df41771df7.hypothesis: Continually estimating the underlying distribution of test data using online statistical modeling, rather than relying on limited-capacity instance-level caches or computationally expensive prompt optimization, enables more robust, adaptive, and efficient test-time adaptation of vision-language models, reducing catastrophic forgetting and improving downstream performance.
2bd386807b0a0f3c987dae1d4b6326df41771df7.proposed_method: A novel test-time adaptation framework is proposed that continuously estimates the statistical distribution of test data embeddings for each class, under the assumption that these follow a Gaussian distribution. The method employs an online Expectation-Maximization algorithm, using zero-shot predictive probabilities as soft labels to update class means and covariances incrementally as new test samples arrive in a streaming fashion. Posterior class probabilities for each test sample are then computed via Bayes’ theorem, leveraging the dynamically estimated distributions. To ensure robustness when the number of test samples is low, an adaptive fusion mechanism combines the original zero-shot classifier with the distributional classifier, weighting their influence based on the amount of observed data. Covariance estimation is regularized and shared across classes to maintain computational efficiency and stability.
2bd386807b0a0f3c987dae1d4b6326df41771df7.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a comprehensive suite of benchmarks, including cross-domain generalization (10 diverse image classification datasets such as Aircraft, Caltech101, Cars, DTD, EuroSAT, Flower102, Food101, Pets, SUN397, and UCF101) and natural distribution shift scenarios (ImageNet, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-S, and ImageNet-V2). Additional evaluations are performed on medical image datasets (KatherColon, PanNuke, WSSS4LUAD) using a pathology-pretrained foundation model. Baselines include zero-shot CLIP, prompt-based test-time adaptation methods (TPT, DiffTPT, Historical Prompt Tuning), and cache-based adaptation methods (TDA, BoostAdapter, ZERO, DMN). Evaluation metrics focus on top-1 accuracy, with additional analysis of inference time, continuous learning ability, and ablation studies on distribution estimation and fusion strategies. Experimental setups include both all-sample and last-50%-sample evaluations to assess continual adaptation and forgetting.
2bd386807b0a0f3c987dae1d4b6326df41771df7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a paradigm shift from instance-level cache-based test-time adaptation to continual distributional estimation, enabling full utilization of all test samples and mitigating catastrophic forgetting. The method is computationally efficient, requiring no gradient backpropagation, and achieves over 20 times faster inference than prompt-optimization-based approaches. Adaptive fusion of zero-shot and test-time classifiers ensures robust performance even with limited test data. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art accuracy and superior continuous learning capability compared to existing methods, with significant improvements in both performance and efficiency.

2bf4206276d5f574bbb2e13a56b29b4522fea675.title: ELITE: Enhanced Language-Image Toxicity Evaluation for Safety
2bf4206276d5f574bbb2e13a56b29b4522fea675.research_question: How can the safety evaluation of vision-language models (VLMs) be improved to more accurately and comprehensively detect harmful outputs, especially those that are implicit or ambiguous, across diverse multimodal contexts?
2bf4206276d5f574bbb2e13a56b29b4522fea675.hypothesis: Incorporating a structured, rubric-based evaluation method that explicitly includes a toxicity score will yield safety assessments for VLMs that are more closely aligned with human judgment and more effective at identifying genuinely harmful outputs than existing automated methods.
2bf4206276d5f574bbb2e13a56b29b4522fea675.proposed_method: A new rubric-based evaluation framework, termed the ELITE evaluator, will be developed to assess VLM safety. This evaluator will extend prior rubric-based methods by introducing a toxicity score, rated on a 0-5 scale, as a core component alongside specificity and convincingness of model responses. The evaluation formula will combine refusal, specificity, convincingness, and toxicity to produce a composite score that better distinguishes genuinely harmful outputs from merely descriptive or ambiguous ones. The ELITE evaluator will be used to curate a high-quality safety benchmark (the ELITE benchmark) by filtering out low-quality and ambiguous image-text pairs from existing datasets and generating new, diverse image-text pairs using multiple prompt-generation strategies (Role Playing, Fake News, Blueprint, Flowchart) across 11 hazard taxonomies. The benchmark construction pipeline will include taxonomy alignment, rigorous filtering based on the ELITE score, and balancing across taxonomies to ensure comprehensive coverage.
2bf4206276d5f574bbb2e13a56b29b4522fea675.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of proprietary and open-source VLMs, including GPT-4o, Gemini-2.0, LLaVa, DeepSeek-VL, ShareGPT4V, and others. The curated ELITE benchmark, comprising 4,587 image-text pairs across 11 safety-critical categories, will be used to evaluate model vulnerability to harmful prompts. Evaluation metrics will include the ELITE score-based Attack Success Rate (E-ASR), traditional Attack Success Rate (ASR), and alignment with human judgments via Area Under the ROC Curve (AU-ROC), accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. Human annotation will be performed on a subset of the data to establish ground truth, and the ELITE evaluator's performance will be compared to existing automated evaluators (e.g., StrongREJECT) and safeguard models (e.g., LlamaGuard3, OpenAI Moderation API). The experimental setup will also include ablation studies on the impact of different prompt-generation methods and analysis of the benchmark's coverage and diversity.
2bf4206276d5f574bbb2e13a56b29b4522fea675.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a novel rubric-based evaluation method for VLM safety that explicitly incorporates a toxicity score, enabling more precise and human-aligned assessments. The ELITE benchmark will be the first to systematically filter ambiguous and low-quality image-text pairs and to generate diverse, high-coverage multimodal safety scenarios, including all combinations of safe and unsafe image-text pairs. The methodology provides a significant advancement over prior automated evaluators by addressing their limitations in detecting implicit and ambiguous harmful content. The approach is validated through extensive experiments and human evaluation, demonstrating superior alignment with human judgments and improved detection of harmful outputs compared to existing benchmarks and evaluators.

2c33062b8f729cc000a6ac16d80dfd1d167f957a.title: Disentangling and Integrating Relational and Sensory Information in Transformer Architectures
2c33062b8f729cc000a6ac16d80dfd1d167f957a.research_question: How can neural architectures be enhanced to disentangle and integrate both relational and sensory information, thereby improving data efficiency, parameter efficiency, and generalization across a wide range of tasks and modalities?
2c33062b8f729cc000a6ac16d80dfd1d167f957a.hypothesis: Introducing explicit computational mechanisms for relational information, alongside standard sensory attention, into Transformer architectures will significantly improve performance, data efficiency, and generalization on tasks requiring relational reasoning, compared to standard Transformers that lack such mechanisms.
2c33062b8f729cc000a6ac16d80dfd1d167f957a.proposed_method: A novel architecture, the Dual Attention Transformer (DAT), is proposed, which augments the standard Transformer with two distinct attention mechanisms: sensory attention for routing sensory information (attributes of individual objects) and relational attention for routing relational information (relationships between objects).
