Relational attention is implemented by computing a series of comparisons between object pairs under learned feature maps, producing relation vectors and symbolic identifiers that tag the source object. These two types of attention are processed in parallel via multi-head attention, with outputs concatenated and integrated at each layer. The architecture supports various symbol assignment mechanisms (positional, relative, or feature-based) to tag relations, and can be configured for encoder-only, decoder-only, or encoder-decoder tasks, as well as ViT-style vision models. The computational complexity remains similar to standard Transformers, and symmetry constraints can be optionally imposed on relations.
2c33062b8f729cc000a6ac16d80dfd1d167f957a.experiment_details: The proposed DAT architecture will be empirically evaluated on a diverse set of tasks and modalities. Experiments include synthetic relational reasoning benchmarks (e.g., Relational Games), mathematical problem-solving (sequence-to-sequence tasks from the Saxton et al. benchmark), image recognition (CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 using ViT-style DAT), and large-scale language modeling (causal language modeling on the FineWeb-Edu dataset with up to 1.3B parameters). Baselines will consist of standard Transformers with comparable parameter counts and attention head configurations. Evaluation metrics include classification accuracy (for vision and relational tasks), character-level accuracy (for math tasks), and perplexity (for language modeling). Experiments will assess data efficiency, parameter efficiency, and generalization, with ablations on the composition of attention heads and symbol assignment mechanisms.
2c33062b8f729cc000a6ac16d80dfd1d167f957a.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a principled disentanglement and integration of sensory and relational information within the Transformer framework, via dual attention mechanisms. This approach enables explicit relational computation and tagging, which is not present in standard Transformers. The architecture demonstrates improved data and parameter efficiency across multiple domains, supports a wide range of task paradigms, and provides a flexible mechanism for incorporating relational inductive biases. Empirical results indicate significant performance gains on relational, symbolic, visual, and language tasks, and relational attention is shown to encode human-interpretable semantic relations.

2c70684973bc4d7b6f8404a647b8031c4d3c8383.title: Zero-1-to-3: Zero-shot One Image to 3D Object
2c70684973bc4d7b6f8404a647b8031c4d3c8383.research_question: How can novel 3D object views and full 3D reconstructions be synthesized from a single RGB image, without relying on explicit 3D supervision or multi-view data, and can such a method generalize to out-of-distribution and in-the-wild images?
2c70684973bc4d7b6f8404a647b8031c4d3c8383.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that large-scale pre-trained 2D diffusion models, when fine-tuned with synthetic viewpoint-conditioned data, possess sufficient geometric priors to enable zero-shot novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction from a single image, even for objects and styles not seen during fine-tuning.
2c70684973bc4d7b6f8404a647b8031c4d3c8383.proposed_method: A novel viewpoint-conditioned image-to-image translation framework will be developed by fine-tuning a pre-trained latent diffusion model (such as Stable Diffusion) to accept both an input RGB image and a specified relative camera transformation (rotation and translation) as conditioning. The method will use a hybrid conditioning mechanism: a CLIP embedding of the input image concatenated with the camera parameters to provide high-level semantic context, and direct channel-wise concatenation of the input image with the denoising process to preserve object identity and details. Cross-attention will be applied to inject the posed CLIP embedding into the U-Net denoiser. The model will be trained on a large-scale synthetic dataset of 3D objects, where paired images and their relative camera extrinsics are available, using a denoising objective that encourages the generated image to match the ground truth novel view. For 3D reconstruction, the trained model will be integrated into a neural field optimization framework (e.g., NeRF-style volumetric rendering), using the diffusion model to supervise the reconstruction from randomly sampled viewpoints.
2c70684973bc4d7b6f8404a647b8031c4d3c8383.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several benchmarks, including Google Scanned Objects (GSO) for high-quality scanned household items and RTMV for complex multi-object scenes, both of which are out-of-distribution relative to the synthetic training set (Objaverse). The method will be evaluated on two tasks: novel view synthesis and single-image 3D reconstruction. Baselines will include DietNeRF, Image Variations (IV), SJC-I, MCC, and Point-E, covering both neural field and diffusion-based approaches. Evaluation metrics for novel view synthesis will include PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and FID, while 3D reconstruction will be assessed using Chamfer Distance and volumetric IoU. The experimental setup will ensure that all methods operate in a zero-shot setting, using only single-view RGB images as input, and will include both quantitative and qualitative comparisons on in-the-wild images and images generated by text-to-image models.
2c70684973bc4d7b6f8404a647b8031c4d3c8383.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a zero-shot, viewpoint-conditioned diffusion framework that enables novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction from a single image without explicit 3D supervision. It leverages large-scale internet-pretrained diffusion models and demonstrates strong generalization to out-of-distribution and in-the-wild images, including artistic styles. The method establishes a generic mechanism for controlling camera viewpoint in diffusion models, and combines multi-view priors with neural field optimization for high-fidelity 3D reconstruction. Significant improvements over state-of-the-art baselines are claimed in both novel view synthesis and 3D reconstruction tasks.

2c7f80548ef03ac6b6e1e949acb02c882f8eec98.title: An Adaptive Algorithm for Learning with Unknown Distribution Drift
2c7f80548ef03ac6b6e1e949acb02c882f8eec98.research_question: How can a learning algorithm effectively adapt to unknown and potentially unbounded distribution drift in sequential data, achieving competitive error guarantees without prior knowledge of the drift magnitude, across general function families such as binary classifiers and linear regressors?
2c7f80548ef03ac6b6e1e949acb02c882f8eec98.hypothesis: It is possible to design an adaptive learning algorithm that, without prior knowledge or explicit estimation of the magnitude of distribution drift, achieves error rates comparable to or better than algorithms that assume such knowledge, by leveraging empirical data to balance statistical and drift errors.
2c7f80548ef03ac6b6e1e949acb02c882f8eec98.proposed_method: A novel adaptive algorithm is proposed for agnostic learning under unknown distribution drift. The method operates on a sequence of independent samples, where each sample may come from a different, drifting distribution. The algorithm adaptively selects the optimal window size of recent samples to use for training, based on empirical estimates of both statistical error (using uniform convergence bounds) and drift error (quantified via a discrepancy norm between empirical distributions from different time windows). Crucially, the algorithm does not require explicit estimation or prior bounds on the drift; instead, it iteratively doubles the sample window and compares empirical discrepancies until an optimal trade-off is detected. The approach is applicable to any function family for which the discrepancy norm is computable, and concrete procedures are provided for binary classification (using empirical risk minimization and VC dimension) and linear regression (using regularized least squares and trust-region optimization).
2c7f80548ef03ac6b6e1e949acb02c882f8eec98.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in two fundamental learning scenarios: binary classification and linear regression. For binary classification, the hypothesis class will be a VC-dimension-bounded family, and the algorithm will use empirical risk minimization over adaptively chosen sample windows. For linear regression, the method will use ℓ2-regularized predictors on data in the unit ball, with squared loss. The evaluation will compare the adaptive algorithm against baselines that assume known drift bounds, using metrics such as excess risk (difference between the learned function's risk and the optimal risk under the current distribution) and empirical error rates. Datasets will be constructed to simulate both stationary (i.i.d.) and drifting environments, including cases with known and unknown drift magnitudes. The experimental setup will ensure that the discrepancy norm is computable or approximable for the chosen function classes.
2c7f80548ef03ac6b6e1e949acb02c882f8eec98.novelty_claims: The proposed algorithm is the first to provably adapt to unknown distribution drift without requiring prior knowledge or explicit estimation of the drift magnitude, resolving a longstanding open problem in the literature. The method achieves error guarantees that match or improve upon those of algorithms with access to drift bounds, and it can outperform non-adaptive methods when drift bounds are loose or data is stationary. The approach is broadly applicable to any learnable function family with a computable discrepancy norm, and it provides concrete, computationally feasible procedures for both binary classification and linear regression. Theoretical analysis establishes minimax optimality (up to logarithmic factors) in the error bounds, and the algorithm is robust to both stationary and drifting data regimes.

2c988d25233d41a1535e54dc0f3cfc9f52ef2c83.title: Efficient Adversarial Training without Attacking: Worst-Case-Aware Robust Reinforcement Learning
2c988d25233d41a1535e54dc0f3cfc9f52ef2c83.research_question: How can reinforcement learning agents be efficiently trained to achieve robust long-term performance against worst-case adversarial attacks on input observations, without incurring significant additional computational or sample complexity?
2c988d25233d41a1535e54dc0f3cfc9f52ef2c83.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that directly estimating and optimizing the worst-case value of a policy under bounded adversarial attacks, without explicitly training an adversarial agent, can yield reinforcement learning agents that are both robust to a wide range of attacks and more sample- and computation-efficient than existing adversarial training methods.
2c988d25233d41a1535e54dc0f3cfc9f52ef2c83.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a robust training framework for reinforcement learning called Worst-case-aware Robust RL (WocaR-RL). This framework consists of three key mechanisms: (1) A novel worst-attack Bellman operator is developed to estimate the lower bound of a policy's value under worst-case adversarial perturbations, using only off-policy samples and convex relaxation techniques to efficiently approximate the set of vulnerable actions. (2) The policy is optimized to maximize both natural and worst-case rewards, guided by a worst-attack critic network that is trained to estimate the worst-case action values. (3) The policy network is regularized using a state importance weighting scheme, which prioritizes robustness in states that are critical for future rewards by penalizing large action divergences under state perturbations. The overall training objective combines the base RL loss with the worst-case-aware policy loss and the value-enhanced state regularization, and can be integrated with standard RL algorithms such as PPO or DQN.
2c988d25233d41a1535e54dc0f3cfc9f52ef2c83.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both continuous control tasks (MuJoCo environments: Hopper, Walker2d, Halfcheetah, Ant) and discrete action, high-dimensional state environments (Atari games: Pong, Freeway, BankHeist, RoadRunner). The proposed method will be evaluated against state-of-the-art robust RL baselines, including regularization-based (SA-PPO/SA-DQN, RADIAL-PPO/RADIAL-DQN) and adversarial training-based (ATLA-PPO, PA-ATLA-PPO) methods. Evaluation metrics will include average episodic rewards under no attack and under various strong adversarial attacks (e.g., MaxDiff, RobustSarsa, SA-RL, PA-AD for MuJoCo; PGD, MinBest, PA-AD for Atari), as well as measures of sample and computational efficiency. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the contribution of each mechanism in the proposed framework.
2c988d25233d41a1535e54dc0f3cfc9f52ef2c83.novelty_claims: The proposed framework claims several innovations: (1) It provides a principled approach to estimate the worst-case value of any policy under bounded adversarial attacks without requiring explicit attacker training or additional environment interactions. (2) The method introduces a worst-case-aware policy optimization procedure that leverages a worst-attack critic and is compatible with off-policy data, improving both robustness and efficiency. (3) A novel state importance weighting scheme is incorporated into the regularization process, enabling the policy to focus robustness efforts on critical states. (4) The framework is generic and can be applied to a wide range of RL algorithms, achieving state-of-the-art robustness and significantly improved training efficiency compared to prior robust RL methods.

2c994fadbb84fb960d8306ee138dbeef41a5b323.title: SmoothQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Large Language Models
2c994fadbb84fb960d8306ee138dbeef41a5b323.research_question: How can post-training quantization be made both accurate and hardware-efficient for large language models, enabling low-bit quantization of weights and activations without retraining or significant accuracy loss?
2c994fadbb84fb960d8306ee138dbeef41a5b323.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that migrating quantization difficulty from activations to weights through a mathematically equivalent transformation and per-channel scaling can enable accurate and efficient INT8 quantization of both weights and activations in large language models, preserving model performance and improving hardware efficiency.
2c994fadbb84fb960d8306ee138dbeef41a5b323.proposed_method: A novel post-training quantization framework is developed that introduces a mathematically equivalent per-channel scaling transformation to smooth activation outliers in large language models. The method computes per-channel smoothing factors using calibration samples from the pre-training dataset, then applies these factors offline to normalize the magnitude of activations, while inversely scaling the corresponding weights to maintain functional equivalence. A migration strength hyperparameter controls the balance of quantization difficulty between activations and weights, allowing fine-tuning for different model architectures. All compute-intensive matrix multiplications, including linear and batched matrix multiplication operations in Transformer blocks, are quantized to INT8 for both weights and activations, while lightweight element-wise operations retain higher precision to balance accuracy and efficiency. The approach is designed to be compatible with various quantization schemes and is implemented in both PyTorch and high-performance inference frameworks.
2c994fadbb84fb960d8306ee138dbeef41a5b323.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a range of large language models, including OPT, BLOOM, GLM-130B, MT-NLG 530B, Llama-1/2, Falcon, Mistral, and Mixtral. Evaluation is performed on multiple zero-shot and language modeling benchmarks such as LAMBADA, HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande, OpenBookQA, RTE, COPA, WikiText, MMLU, MNLI, and QNLI, using the lm-eval-harness and official model repositories. Baseline comparisons include naive W8A8 quantization, ZeroQuant, LLM.int8(), and Outlier Suppression, with all methods evaluated under several quantization granularities (per-tensor, per-token, per-channel, static and dynamic). Performance is measured in terms of accuracy, perplexity, inference latency, and peak memory usage, with experiments run on NVIDIA A100 GPUs using both PyTorch and FasterTransformer backends. Additional ablation studies investigate the effect of migration strength and quantization scheme granularity.
2c994fadbb84fb960d8306ee138dbeef41a5b323.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to enable lossless INT8 quantization of both weights and activations for large language models up to 530B parameters without retraining. It introduces a mathematically equivalent per-channel smoothing transformation that migrates quantization difficulty from activations to weights, overcoming the challenge of activation outliers in LLMs. The approach is training-free, hardware-friendly, and general-purpose, supporting a wide range of model architectures and quantization schemes. It achieves significant reductions in inference latency and memory usage, enabling the deployment of extremely large models on fewer GPUs and democratizing access to LLMs.

2c9c8df8e097ff06ae5741ad35f520110f264549.title: Regret Bounds for Batched Bandits
2c9c8df8e097ff06ae5741ad35f520110f264549.research_question: How can efficient algorithms be designed for batched versions of multi-armed bandit and linear bandit problems, and what are the achievable regret bounds for both stochastic and adversarial settings under batch constraints?
2c9c8df8e097ff06ae5741ad35f520110f264549.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that with a logarithmic number of batches, it is possible to achieve regret bounds in batched stochastic multi-armed and linear bandit problems that match the optimal bounds of the fully sequential setting, and that tight (up to logarithmic factors) regret bounds can be established for batched adversarial multi-armed bandits.
2c9c8df8e097ff06ae5741ad35f520110f264549.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves developing adaptive algorithms for batched stochastic multi-armed and linear bandits based on iterative arm elimination. In the stochastic multi-armed bandit setting, the method divides the time horizon into batches, pulling each active arm in parallel within a batch, estimating their means, and eliminating arms that are statistically suboptimal. For stochastic linear bandits, the approach leverages geometric properties of the action set, using approximately optimal G-designs to select informative batches and eliminate suboptimal arms based on least-squares parameter estimation. For the adversarial multi-armed bandit setting, the research will analyze non-adaptive algorithms, employing reductions to delayed feedback models and constructing hard reward sequences to establish lower bounds.
2c9c8df8e097ff06ae5741ad35f520110f264549.experiment_details: Theoretical analysis will be conducted to derive regret bounds for the proposed algorithms. For stochastic settings, the regret will be analyzed as a function of the number of batches B, the time horizon T, the number of arms K, and problem-specific parameters such as the gap between arm means or the dimensionality d. The performance will be compared to known optimal bounds from the sequential setting and to existing batched algorithms, with particular attention to the number of batches required to achieve optimal regret. For the adversarial setting, both upper and lower bounds will be established, with proofs based on reductions and adversarial constructions. Evaluation metrics will include expected regret and its scaling with respect to B, T, K, and d.
2c9c8df8e097ff06ae5741ad35f520110f264549.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first efficient algorithms for batched stochastic linear bandits, providing regret bounds that match the sequential optimum with only a logarithmic number of batches. For stochastic multi-armed bandits, the proposed adaptive batch sizing and arm elimination strategy achieves optimal regret with nearly the minimal number of batches. In the adversarial setting, the research establishes tight (up to logarithmic factors) upper and lower bounds for non-adaptive batched algorithms, revealing a polynomial relationship between the number of batches and achievable regret. These contributions extend the theoretical understanding of batched bandit problems and provide practical algorithms for parallelized exploration-exploitation trade-offs.

2ca3628968b6a0e1f625ff905c1d278cabe0357b.title: Tailoring Mixup to Data for Calibration
2ca3628968b6a0e1f625ff905c1d278cabe0357b.research_question: How can data augmentation techniques based on linear interpolation (Mixup) be adapted to improve model calibration and predictive performance in both classification and regression tasks, while maintaining computational efficiency and diversity of synthetic samples?
2ca3628968b6a0e1f625ff905c1d278cabe0357b.hypothesis: Dynamically adjusting the interpolation coefficients in Mixup according to the similarity between data points will reduce manifold mismatch and label noise, thereby improving model calibration and predictive accuracy without sacrificing computational efficiency or diversity.
2ca3628968b6a0e1f625ff905c1d278cabe0357b.proposed_method: A novel data augmentation framework, Similarity Kernel Mixup (SKMixup), is proposed, which dynamically tailors the distribution of interpolation coefficients for each pair of data points based on their similarity. The method introduces a warping function that transforms uniformly sampled interpolation coefficients into Beta-distributed coefficients, where the Beta distribution's parameter is determined by a similarity kernel. This kernel computes a normalized Gaussian function of the distance (in embedding or label space) between the two points to be mixed, such that more similar points are mixed with stronger interpolation (higher Beta parameter), and less similar points are mixed more weakly. The approach preserves the diversity of synthetic samples by allowing all pairs to be mixed, but controls the extent of mixing to minimize manifold mismatch. The framework is general and efficient, requiring only a single batch in memory and minimal computational overhead, and is applicable to both classification (using embedding distances) and regression (using label distances) tasks.
2ca3628968b6a0e1f625ff905c1d278cabe0357b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of benchmark datasets for both image classification (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, ImageNet, and their covariate/out-of-distribution variants) and regression (Airfoil, Exchange-Rate, Electricity). Multiple neural network architectures will be used, including ResNet34, ResNet50, ResNet101, Vision Transformers (ViT), MLPs, and RNNs. Baselines will include ERM, standard Mixup, ManifoldMixup, RegMixup, RankMixup, MIT-A, and other calibration-driven Mixup variants. Evaluation metrics will cover both predictive performance (accuracy, MAPE, RMSE) and calibration (ECE, AECE, NLL, Brier score, UCE, ENCE), with and without post-hoc temperature scaling. Experimental protocols will ensure reproducibility by averaging results over multiple random seeds and reporting standard deviations. Efficiency will be assessed in terms of memory usage, time per epoch, and total training time to best performance.
2ca3628968b6a0e1f625ff905c1d278cabe0357b.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a flexible and efficient framework for dynamically tailoring Mixup interpolation coefficients to the similarity between data points, addressing the manifold mismatch and label noise issues inherent in standard Mixup. Unlike previous approaches, this method preserves sample diversity while improving both calibration and accuracy, and is computationally more efficient than other calibration-driven Mixup methods. It is broadly applicable across classification and regression tasks and can be combined with existing regularization-based Mixup variants for further performance gains.

2cc1d857e86d5152ba7fe6a8355c2a0150cc280a.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering
2cc1d857e86d5152ba7fe6a8355c2a0150cc280a.research_question: How can real-time, high-quality novel view synthesis of complex 3D scenes from multi-view images be achieved using an efficient, explicit scene representation that enables both fast training and rendering?
2cc1d857e86d5152ba7fe6a8355c2a0150cc280a.hypothesis: A scene representation based on anisotropic 3D Gaussians, combined with adaptive density control and a fast, differentiable, visibility-aware GPU renderer, will enable real-time radiance field rendering with visual quality matching or exceeding state-of-the-art methods, while significantly reducing training and rendering times.
2cc1d857e86d5152ba7fe6a8355c2a0150cc280a.proposed_method: The proposed method represents a scene as a set of anisotropic 3D Gaussians, initialized from a sparse point cloud obtained via Structure-from-Motion (SfM). Each Gaussian is parameterized by its 3D position, a full covariance matrix (expressed via scale and rotation), opacity, and spherical harmonic coefficients for view-dependent color. The method interleaves stochastic gradient descent optimization of these parameters with adaptive density control, which dynamically clones or splits Gaussians based on view-space gradient magnitudes to better capture scene geometry and appearance. A novel tile-based, differentiable GPU rasterizer is developed to project the 3D Gaussians to 2D, perform fast visibility-aware alpha blending of anisotropic splats, and enable efficient backpropagation through arbitrary numbers of blended Gaussians. The entire pipeline is fully differentiable and supports real-time rendering at high resolutions.
2cc1d857e86d5152ba7fe6a8355c2a0150cc280a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several established datasets, including Mip-NeRF360, Tanks & Temples, DeepBlending, and the synthetic Blender dataset. The method will be compared against state-of-the-art radiance field approaches such as Mip-NeRF360, InstantNGP, and Plenoxels, using standard train/test splits. Evaluation metrics will include PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS for image quality, as well as training time, rendering speed (frames per second), and memory usage. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of initialization, densification strategies, anisotropic covariance, gradient computation depth, and spherical harmonics. All experiments will be run on high-end GPUs, and both quantitative and qualitative results will be reported.
2cc1d857e86d5152ba7fe6a8355c2a0150cc280a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces anisotropic 3D Gaussians as a flexible, explicit, and differentiable scene representation for radiance fields, enabling both high-quality and compact modeling of complex geometry. A new adaptive density control mechanism interleaves optimization with dynamic addition and removal of Gaussians, improving representation efficiency. The tile-based, visibility-aware GPU rasterizer allows for real-time rendering and efficient backpropagation through arbitrary numbers of blended Gaussians, overcoming limitations of previous methods. The method achieves state-of-the-art visual quality with training and rendering speeds that are orders of magnitude faster than existing approaches, and is the first to enable real-time, high-quality novel view synthesis for large, unbounded scenes at 1080p resolution.

2ccb452691a5d3e3b600caaec119df9ff44688bd.title: AdaMerging: Adaptive Model Merging for Multi-Task Learning
2ccb452691a5d3e3b600caaec119df9ff44688bd.research_question: How can multiple independently fine-tuned models for different tasks be effectively merged into a single multi-task model without access to the original training data, while maximizing performance, generalization, and robustness?
2ccb452691a5d3e3b600caaec119df9ff44688bd.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that adaptively learning task-wise or layer-wise merging coefficients for model merging, using entropy minimization on unlabeled test data as a surrogate objective, will result in superior multi-task learning performance, improved generalization to unseen tasks, and increased robustness to data distribution shifts compared to existing model merging methods.
2ccb452691a5d3e3b600caaec119df9ff44688bd.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces an adaptive model merging framework, AdaMerging, for multi-task learning without requiring original training data. AdaMerging learns merging coefficients for each task vector (task-wise) or for each layer within each task vector (layer-wise) in an unsupervised manner. The merging coefficients are optimized by minimizing the entropy of the model's prediction distribution on unlabeled test samples, serving as a proxy for loss minimization. The approach supports both direct merging of task vectors and a variant (AdaMerging++) that incorporates parameter trimming and sign consistency to further mitigate conflicts. Optimization is performed iteratively using backpropagation and automatic differentiation, and only a small fraction of unlabeled test data is required for effective coefficient learning.
2ccb452691a5d3e3b600caaec119df9ff44688bd.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on eight image classification datasets: SUN397, Cars, RESISC45, EuroSAT, SVHN, GTSRB, MNIST, and DTD. Pre-trained ViT-B/32 and ViT-L/14 architectures from CLIP are used as the backbone models. Baselines include Individual fine-tuning, Traditional MTL, Weight Averaging, FisherMerging, RegMean, Task Arithmetic, and Ties-Merging. The primary evaluation metric is average accuracy (AvgAcc) across all tasks. Additional experiments assess generalization to unseen tasks and robustness to test data distribution shifts using various corruption types. Both task-wise and layer-wise versions of AdaMerging and AdaMerging++ are evaluated, with ablation on the impact of merging coefficient granularity.
2ccb452691a5d3e3b600caaec119df9ff44688bd.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is novel in autonomously learning merging coefficients for each task or layer in an unsupervised manner, using entropy minimization as a principled and efficient surrogate objective. This method eliminates the need for grid search or access to original training data, significantly enhancing flexibility and scalability. AdaMerging demonstrates substantial improvements over state-of-the-art task vector-based model merging methods in terms of multi-task performance, generalization to unseen tasks, and robustness to distribution shifts. The framework provides a finer-grained and adaptive merging solution, bridging the performance gap between model merging and traditional multi-task learning.

2ccbafd636184c6edd83e585359514923b6cf849.title: The Unreasonable Ineffectiveness of the Deeper Layers
2ccbafd636184c6edd83e585359514923b6cf849.research_question: How is knowledge stored across the layers of large language models (LLMs), and to what extent are the parameters in deeper layers necessary for performance on various downstream tasks?
2ccbafd636184c6edd83e585359514923b6cf849.hypothesis: The deeper layers of LLMs are less essential for storing knowledge required for common question-answering tasks, but may be more important for higher-level computations such as reasoning. Shallow layers play a critical role in knowledge storage and retrieval.
2ccbafd636184c6edd83e585359514923b6cf849.proposed_method: A layer-pruning framework will be developed for decoder-only, open-weight LLMs. The method will identify blocks of consecutive layers to prune by computing the angular distance between the representations at layer ℓ and ℓ+n on a neutral pretraining or downstream dataset, selecting the block with minimal distance as the optimal pruning target. After removing the selected layers, the model will be 'healed' via parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT), specifically using QLoRA with 4-bit quantization, to mitigate the mismatch caused by pruning. An alternative, simpler strategy will also be evaluated, in which the deepest layers (excluding the final layer) are pruned directly, followed by the same healing procedure. Technical implementation will leverage efficient model surgery (e.g., modifying ModuleList in PyTorch) and will ensure all experiments are feasible on a single 40GB A100 GPU.
2ccbafd636184c6edd83e585359514923b6cf849.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of open-weight LLMs, including Llama-2 (7B, 13B, 70B), Qwen (7B, 14B), Mistral-7B, and Phi-2 (2.7B), covering models with 32 to 80 layers. Pruned models will be evaluated on Massive Multitask Language Understanding (MMLU) and BoolQ for question answering, GSM8K and HellaSwag for reasoning, and next-token prediction loss on the C4 validation set. Baselines will include unpruned models, randomly pruned models, and models pruned with and without healing. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy (for QA and reasoning), pass@1 (for GSM8K), and normalized cross-entropy loss (for C4). Ablation studies will assess the impact of pruning depth, healing strategies, and block selection heuristics.
2ccbafd636184c6edd83e585359514923b6cf849.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a similarity-informed, block-wise layer pruning strategy for LLMs, demonstrating that a substantial fraction of deeper layers can be removed with minimal degradation on QA benchmarks after efficient fine-tuning. The approach provides new empirical evidence regarding the distribution of knowledge and reasoning capabilities across model layers, and offers a practical, resource-efficient method for model compression and interpretability. The work also systematically compares similarity-based pruning to a simple heuristic of pruning deepest layers, and investigates the robustness of different task types to layer removal, highlighting a sharp distinction between knowledge retrieval and reasoning in LLMs.

2cf95cfeb7180a3a93a2cd79989090986c1a66bd.title: L2M: Mutual Information Scaling Law for Long-Context Language Modeling
2cf95cfeb7180a3a93a2cd79989090986c1a66bd.research_question: What are the fundamental information-theoretic requirements for effective long-context language modeling, and how do these requirements inform the design and scaling of neural architectures for processing long sequences?
2cf95cfeb7180a3a93a2cd79989090986c1a66bd.hypothesis: The minimum necessary capacity of a language model's latent history state for effective long-context modeling is lower bounded by the power-law scaling of bipartite mutual information in natural language; architectures whose history state dimension does not scale accordingly will be fundamentally limited in their ability to capture long-range dependencies.
2cf95cfeb7180a3a93a2cd79989090986c1a66bd.proposed_method: A universal theoretical framework will be developed to analyze long-context language modeling through the lens of bipartite mutual information scaling. The approach will rigorously define and empirically estimate the scaling law of bipartite mutual information in natural language, leveraging state-of-the-art large language models (LLMs) as density estimators to overcome the challenges of high-dimensional mutual information estimation. The framework will introduce the L2M condition, which formalizes the minimum scaling requirement for a model's latent history state (such as transformer key-value caches or SSM recurrent states) to capture the observed mutual information growth in long sequences. Theoretical derivations will relate the model's history state dimension to its capacity to express bipartite mutual information, establishing necessary conditions for MI-capability across increasing sequence lengths. The method will also analyze and compare different neural architectures (e.g., transformers, SSMs, RNNs, sparse attention) under this framework to determine their suitability for long-context modeling.
2cf95cfeb7180a3a93a2cd79989090986c1a66bd.experiment_details: Experiments will empirically verify the bipartite mutual information scaling law using both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic data will be constructed from multivariate Gaussian distributions that mimic the scaling properties of natural language, enabling tractable calculation of conditional probabilities and KL divergences. On real data, such as the PG19 dataset (a collection of pre-1919 books), bipartite and two-point mutual information will be estimated using LLaMA and other LLMs as density estimators, employing both direct and vCLUB estimators with bias correction. Model architectures including transformers (e.g., GPT-2), state-space models (Mamba, Mamba2), and varying model sizes will be trained and evaluated on these datasets. Evaluation metrics will include average per-token KL divergence and position-wise conditional negative log likelihood (NLL), with performance analyzed as a function of sequence length and the ratio of mutual information to history state size. Baselines will include fixed-size and scalable models, and results will be compared across architectures to test the theoretical predictions.
2cf95cfeb7180a3a93a2cd79989090986c1a66bd.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a universal, information-theoretic framework for understanding and quantifying the requirements of long-context language modeling, grounded in a rigorously verified bipartite mutual information scaling law. The L2M condition provides the first principled lower bound on the necessary scaling of a model's history state for capturing long-range dependencies, offering concrete, data-driven guidance for neural architecture design. The approach distinguishes itself from prior work by moving beyond two-point mutual information to capture multi-token dependencies and by providing both theoretical and empirical validation across diverse architectures and datasets. This framework enables principled comparisons of model capacity, explains the limitations of fixed-state models, and suggests new directions for efficient architecture design tailored to the true information structure of natural language and other sequential domains.

2d14697232f03661cb86246df46e52816694a97f.title: Towards Last-layer Retraining for Group Robustness with Fewer Annotations
2d14697232f03661cb86246df46e52816694a97f.research_question: How can group robustness in neural network classifiers be improved, particularly for minority groups affected by spurious correlations, while minimizing the need for group and class annotations?
2d14697232f03661cb86246df46e52816694a97f.hypothesis: Last-layer retraining, when applied with class balancing and selective data selection strategies, can significantly improve worst-group accuracy and group robustness even in the absence of group annotations and with minimal class annotations.
2d14697232f03661cb86246df46e52816694a97f.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves a comprehensive study of last-layer retraining techniques for improving group robustness in neural networks. First, class-balanced last-layer retraining will be implemented by sampling uniformly over classes to construct the reweighting dataset, avoiding the need for group annotations. Next, a 'selective last-layer finetuning' (SELF) approach will be developed, which constructs a small, more group-balanced reweighting dataset by identifying and upsampling data points based on misclassifications or model disagreements (e.g., between an ERM model and an early-stopped or dropout-regularized model). The last layer of the neural network will then be finetuned on this selectively constructed dataset, starting from the ERM-trained weights. Multiple variants of SELF will be explored, including misclassification-based and disagreement-based selection, with a focus on minimizing annotation requirements and avoiding overfitting.
2d14697232f03661cb86246df46e52816694a97f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four well-established benchmarks for group robustness: Waterbirds, CelebA, CivilComments, and MultiNLI, spanning both vision and language tasks. For each dataset, models such as ResNet-50 (for vision) and BERT (for language) will be pretrained and then subjected to the proposed retraining and finetuning procedures. Baselines will include empirical risk minimization (ERM), class-balanced ERM, deep feature reweighting (DFR), group DRO, and other recent methods such as JTT. Evaluation will focus on worst-group accuracy (WGA) as the primary metric, with additional analyses on the proportion of worst-group data in the reweighting set and the annotation efficiency of each method. Experiments will be repeated with multiple random seeds, and both hyperparameter-free and hyperparameter-tuned variants will be compared.
2d14697232f03661cb86246df46e52816694a97f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a practical and annotation-efficient framework for group robustness by demonstrating that class-balanced last-layer retraining can achieve near state-of-the-art performance without group annotations. It further claims that selective last-layer finetuning (SELF), especially when based on model disagreement, can match or surpass existing methods like DFR while using less than 3% of held-out class annotations and no group annotations. The approach provides the first empirical and theoretical evidence that model disagreement effectively upsamples worst-group data, and it identifies a 'free lunch' phenomenon where holding out a subset of training data for last-layer retraining can outperform ERM on the full dataset without additional data or annotations.

2d2bfb068e3441aaa9743043603d00f860dd0308.title: ForecastPFN: Synthetically-Trained Zero-Shot Forecasting
2d2bfb068e3441aaa9743043603d00f860dd0308.research_question: How can accurate and efficient zero-shot time-series forecasting be achieved in data-sparse settings, where only a small number of initial observations are available and no retraining on target data is possible?
2d2bfb068e3441aaa9743043603d00f860dd0308.hypothesis: A prior-data fitted network (PFN) trained exclusively on a carefully designed, diverse synthetic time-series distribution can generalize to real-world zero-shot forecasting tasks, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods even when those methods are allowed to train on additional in-distribution data.
2d2bfb068e3441aaa9743043603d00f860dd0308.proposed_method: A novel zero-shot forecasting framework, ForecastPFN, will be developed by training a transformer-based prior-data fitted network entirely on synthetic time-series data. The synthetic data generation process will incorporate multi-scale seasonal trends (weekly, monthly, yearly), linear and exponential global trends, and a Weibull-based multiplicative noise model, with parameters sampled to maximize diversity and realism. The transformer architecture will be designed to accept variable-length input sequences and arbitrary future time queries, enabling flexible prediction horizons. Robust scaling techniques will be employed to handle the wide range of scales and outliers present in both synthetic and real-world series, involving multi-step outlier removal and loss normalization. Training will be performed offline, using a large synthetic dataset, with the model learning to approximate Bayesian posterior predictive distributions for arbitrary time-series queries.
2d2bfb068e3441aaa9743043603d00f860dd0308.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on seven standard real-world time-series datasets spanning energy, economics, traffic, and weather domains (ECL, ETTh1, ETTh2, Exchange, Illness, Traffic, Weather). ForecastPFN will be evaluated in zero-shot mode, where it receives only a short input sequence (e.g., 36 points) and makes future predictions without any retraining. Comparisons will be made against a range of baselines, including traditional statistical models (ARIMA, Prophet), simple heuristics (Last, Mean, SeasonalNaive), and state-of-the-art deep learning models (FEDformer, Autoformer, Informer, vanilla Transformer), as well as the Meta-N-BEATS zero-shot model. Evaluation will consider multiple data budgets (50 to 500 points), time budgets (1 to 120 seconds), and prediction lengths (6 to 48 steps), with performance measured primarily by mean squared error (MSE) and aggregated using win counts across datasets and settings. Ablation studies will assess the impact of robust scaling and synthetic noise parameters.
2d2bfb068e3441aaa9743043603d00f860dd0308.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to train a zero-shot forecasting model purely on a synthetic time-series distribution, without any real-world pretraining. The synthetic prior is designed to be both highly diverse and representative of real-world patterns, enabling strong generalization. ForecastPFN introduces a flexible transformer architecture capable of arbitrary-length queries and robust scaling techniques tailored for extreme value and trend diversity. The method achieves superior accuracy and speed compared to existing zero-shot and non-zero-shot baselines, making accurate predictions in a single forward pass and outperforming models that require extensive retraining on target data.

2d384d1c2f46645b2808cc4bb779aeafdea927dc.title: Orthus: Autoregressive Interleaved Image-Text Generation with Modality-Specific Heads
2d384d1c2f46645b2808cc4bb779aeafdea927dc.research_question: How can a unified multimodal model be developed to effectively generate and understand interleaved image-text sequences from mixed-modality inputs, while minimizing information loss and maximizing modeling efficiency?
2d384d1c2f46645b2808cc4bb779aeafdea927dc.hypothesis: A unified autoregressive model that employs modality-specific heads—one for discrete text token prediction and another for continuous image feature generation via diffusion—will outperform existing approaches in interleaved image-text generation and multimodal understanding by reducing information loss and improving modeling flexibility.
2d384d1c2f46645b2808cc4bb779aeafdea927dc.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a unified multimodal framework, Orthus, which processes mixed-modality inputs by embedding discrete text tokens and continuous image features into a shared representation space. A transformer backbone models both intra- and inter-modality dependencies using causal attention. Two modality-specific output heads are employed: a language modeling (LM) head for predicting the next text token, and a diffusion head for generating the next image patch feature through conditional diffusion modeling. The vision embedding module is made differentiable by replacing vector quantization with a softmax-based alternative, enabling gradient-based adaptation and preserving more information from the original image features. Training involves initializing from a pre-trained autoregressive model, adapting the input and output modules, and fine-tuning primarily on image reconstruction tasks before post-training on interleaved image-text datasets to enable complex, mixed-modality generation.
2d384d1c2f46645b2808cc4bb779aeafdea927dc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of multimodal understanding and generation benchmarks. Datasets include LAION-COCO-aesthetic for image reconstruction, Instruct-Pix2Pix for image editing, and StoryStream for interleaved storybook generation, as well as mixtures of LLaVA-v1.5-665K, JourneyDB, and recaptioned ShareGPT-4v for post-training. Baselines for comparison include models such as Chameleon, Show-o, LWM, and specialized diffusion models like SDXL and DALL-E. Evaluation metrics will cover GenEval for text-to-image alignment, MME-P and POPE for multimodal understanding, VQAv2 and GQA for visual question answering, and HPS for human preference scoring. The experimental setup includes fine-tuning only the vision embedding and diffusion head on 10k images, followed by unified post-training on interleaved image-text data, with inference using greedy decoding for text and DDIM sampling for images.
2d384d1c2f46645b2808cc4bb779aeafdea927dc.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a fully autoregressive framework that directly models continuous image features without vector quantization, thereby minimizing information loss and enabling lossless cross-modal representation. The use of modality-specific heads within a single transformer backbone allows seamless alternation between text and image generation, supporting lengthy and logically coherent interleaved outputs. An efficient adaptation strategy leverages existing pre-trained autoregressive models, reducing training costs and enabling rapid instantiation of the new model. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior performance over state-of-the-art unified and specialized models on both understanding and generation tasks, highlighting the method's potential as a foundation for future multimodal systems.

2d40e31e39a7d699e0bd2c1750baf18575eb5a7c.title: Representational Similarity via Interpretable Visual Concepts
2d40e31e39a7d699e0bd2c1750baf18575eb5a7c.research_question: How can the representational similarity between two deep neural networks be measured in a way that provides interpretable insights into what makes their internal representations similar or dissimilar, particularly in terms of the visual concepts they encode?
2d40e31e39a7d699e0bd2c1750baf18575eb5a7c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a concept-based approach to measuring representational similarity will not only quantify the degree of similarity between two models but also reveal interpretable visual concepts that are shared or unique, thereby providing deeper insight into the functional differences between models.
2d40e31e39a7d699e0bd2c1750baf18575eb5a7c.proposed_method: A novel framework, Representational Similarity via Interpretable Visual Concepts (RSVC), will be developed to compare the internal representations of two neural networks. The method begins by extracting visual concepts from a specific layer of each model using a dictionary learning approach, where activations are factorized into a concept basis and a coefficient matrix. For each object class, image patches predicted by each model are used to form concept proposals, which are then passed through the network to obtain activations. These activations are decomposed into interpretable concepts, and the importance of each concept for a given image is quantified by the coefficients. To compare concepts across models, a regression-based mapping is learned to predict the concept coefficients of one model from the activations of the other, and similarity is measured using correlation metrics between the predicted and true coefficients. Additional visualization strategies are introduced to interpret both high and low similarity concepts, including over- and under-predicted concept patch analysis.
2d40e31e39a7d699e0bd2c1750baf18575eb5a7c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a range of computer vision models, including ResNet-18, ResNet-50, ViT-S, ViT-L, DINO ViT-B, and MAE ViT-B, trained on ImageNet and fine-tuned on NABirds. Four model pairs will be compared: RN18 vs. RN50, ViT-S vs. ViT-L, RN50 vs. ViT-S, and DINO vs. MAE, covering both cases with significant performance differences and those with similar accuracy. The methodology will be validated with both real-world and controlled 'toy' datasets, such as modified NABirds with synthetic visual concepts. Baselines will include within-model concept similarity and existing representational similarity metrics. Evaluation metrics will include Pearson and Spearman correlation of concept coefficients, l2-distance of activations, KL-divergence of logits, and classification accuracy. Concept importance will be measured using concept integrated gradients, and a replacement test will be used to assess the impact of concept similarity on model behavior.
2d40e31e39a7d699e0bd2c1750baf18575eb5a7c.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces an interpretable, concept-based framework for measuring representational similarity between neural networks, moving beyond single-score metrics to provide detailed insights into shared and unique visual concepts. It enables practitioners to identify which concepts drive differences in model behavior and links representational changes to functional outcomes. The approach is general, applicable across diverse architectures and training protocols, and introduces new visualization techniques for understanding both similar and dissimilar concepts between models.

2d4a853affeb0b164fc1134df612aea658f36459.title: Mixture of Cluster-conditional LoRA Experts for Vision-language Instruction Tuning
2d4a853affeb0b164fc1134df612aea658f36459.research_question: How can task conflicts arising from diverse instruction tuning in large vision-language models be mitigated to improve both task specialization and generalization across a wide range of downstream vision-language tasks?
2d4a853affeb0b164fc1134df612aea658f36459.hypothesis: Automatically clustering instructions and activating cluster-conditional parameter-efficient experts, combined with a universal expert, will reduce task conflicts during instruction tuning and enhance both specialization for similar tasks and generalization to novel tasks in large vision-language models.
2d4a853affeb0b164fc1134df612aea658f36459.proposed_method: A novel Mixture of Cluster-conditional LoRA Experts (MoCLE) framework will be developed for vision-language instruction tuning. The approach begins by encoding all training instructions using a pre-trained sentence encoder and clustering them via k-means to group similar tasks together. For each cluster, a dedicated LoRA expert is constructed, and a router dynamically dispatches input data to the appropriate expert based on the cluster assignment of its instruction. Additionally, a universal expert, trained on all instructions, is incorporated to ensure generalization to unseen tasks. The model output is computed as a weighted sum of the outputs from the selected cluster expert, the universal expert, and the original model layer, with gating controlled by a temperature-scaled softmax over cluster embeddings.
2d4a853affeb0b164fc1134df612aea658f36459.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two large vision-language models: InstructBLIP and LLaVA-1.5. The evaluation will include a wide range of held-in and held-out vision-language tasks, such as GQA, VSR, IconQA, ScienceQA, TextVQA, Visual Dialog, and MME, among others. Training datasets will cover multiple domains, including natural images, geometric tasks, and medical tasks. Baselines will include dense models, single LoRA models, and other Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) methods such as Sentence-MoLE and Dataset-MoLE. Evaluation metrics will include CIDEr, iVQA accuracy, AUC, Mean Reciprocal Rank, perception/cognition scores, F1, and top-1 accuracy, depending on the task. Ablation studies will be performed to analyze the impact of the number of clusters, experts, gating temperature, and the inclusion of the universal expert.
2d4a853affeb0b164fc1134df612aea658f36459.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first cluster-conditional mixture-of-experts architecture for parameter-efficient instruction tuning in vision-language models, automatically partitioning tasks via instruction clustering rather than manual taxonomy. It uniquely combines specialized cluster experts with a universal expert to simultaneously achieve task specialization and robust generalization. The approach addresses negative transfer and task conflicts in multi-task instruction tuning, providing a scalable and automatic solution that outperforms existing dense and MoE baselines across diverse domains and tasks.

2d5edc038a177bed2f58e5374f38a411d8538f0b.title: Watch and Match: Supercharging Imitation with Regularized Optimal Transport
2d5edc038a177bed2f58e5374f38a411d8538f0b.research_question: How can imitation learning be made more sample-efficient and robust for complex decision-making tasks, particularly in high-dimensional visual environments and real-world robotics, using only a small number of expert demonstrations?
2d5edc038a177bed2f58e5374f38a411d8538f0b.hypothesis: Combining optimal transport-based trajectory matching with adaptive regularization towards a behavior cloning policy will significantly accelerate and stabilize imitation learning, enabling efficient policy learning from few demonstrations and limited online interactions.
2d5edc038a177bed2f58e5374f38a411d8538f0b.proposed_method: A novel imitation learning framework, Regularized Optimal Transport (ROT), will be developed that integrates two phases: (1) offline behavior cloning (BC) pretraining using expert demonstrations, and (2) online fine-tuning with inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) using rewards derived from optimal transport (OT) trajectory matching. The fine-tuning phase will employ an actor-critic RL algorithm (n-step DDPG) to optimize the policy with OT-based rewards, while simultaneously regularizing the policy to remain close to the BC-pretrained policy. An adaptive regularization scheme, termed soft Q-filtering, will be introduced to automatically adjust the strength of the BC regularization based on the relative Q-values of the current and BC policies, prioritizing imitation early in training and exploration later. The approach will be designed to handle high-dimensional visual observations by employing data augmentation and a CNN encoder with Polyak averaging for stable OT reward computation.
2d5edc038a177bed2f58e5374f38a411d8538f0b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 20 simulated visual control tasks from the DeepMind Control Suite, OpenAI Robotics Suite, and Meta-World Benchmark, as well as 14 real-world robotic manipulation tasks using an xArm 7 robot. For simulated tasks, expert demonstrations will be collected using state-of-the-art RL agents (e.g., DrQ-v2), with varying numbers of demonstrations per environment. In the real-world setup, a single human demonstration and one hour of online training will be used per task. Baselines will include adversarial IRL methods (e.g., DAC), trajectory-matching IRL (e.g., Sinkhorn Imitation Learning), and behavior cloning. Evaluation metrics will include the speed to reach 90% of expert performance, average task success rates, and sample efficiency. Ablation studies will assess the impact of each component, including the adaptive regularization scheme and the choice of IRL method.
2d5edc038a177bed2f58e5374f38a411d8538f0b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces an adaptive regularization mechanism (soft Q-filtering) that dynamically balances imitation and exploration without hand-tuned schedules, enabling stable and efficient policy learning. The integration of OT-based trajectory matching with BC regularization in a unified framework allows for rapid imitation from few demonstrations, even in high-dimensional visual and real-world robotic settings. The method is compatible with image-based observations and requires minimal additional hyperparameters compared to standard IRL. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate substantial improvements in sample efficiency and success rates over prior state-of-the-art imitation learning and RL methods.

2d65798c7dcb31ce07864b35dc80f399f87ce9d0.title: HYPO: Hyperspherical Out-of-Distribution Generalization
2d65798c7dcb31ce07864b35dc80f399f87ce9d0.research_question: How can a learning algorithm be designed to achieve robust out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization by learning representations that are invariant across domains and environments, and what theoretical guarantees can be established for such an algorithm?
2d65798c7dcb31ce07864b35dc80f399f87ce9d0.hypothesis: Learning domain-invariant representations in a hyperspherical space, guided by minimizing intra-class variation and maximizing inter-class separation, will provably improve OOD generalization performance.
2d65798c7dcb31ce07864b35dc80f399f87ce9d0.proposed_method: A hyperspherical learning algorithm is developed to promote domain-invariant representations by mapping input data to a unit hypersphere using a deep neural network. For each class, a prototype vector is maintained, and the loss function consists of two terms: one that encourages feature embeddings of samples from the same class (across all training domains) to align closely with their class prototype (minimizing intra-class variation), and another that enforces maximal separation between different class prototypes (maximizing inter-class separation). The feature embeddings and prototypes are normalized to lie on the unit hypersphere, and prototypes are updated during training using an exponential moving average of class-specific embeddings. The loss can be interpreted probabilistically as maximizing the likelihood under a von Mises-Fisher distribution on the hypersphere, and the model is trained end-to-end using stochastic gradient descent. During inference, classification is performed by assigning each sample to the class whose prototype is closest in the hyperspherical space.
2d65798c7dcb31ce07864b35dc80f399f87ce9d0.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on several OOD generalization benchmarks, including CIFAR-10 (as in-distribution) and CIFAR-10-C (as OOD, with 19 corruption types), as well as multi-domain datasets such as PACS, Office-Home, and VLCS. Standard architectures are used: ResNet-18 for CIFAR-10 and ResNet-50 for PACS, Office-Home, and VLCS, with models trained using SGD with momentum and weight decay. The evaluation protocol includes leave-one-domain-out testing, and performance is measured using in-distribution and OOD classification accuracy. Baselines include ERM, IRM, GroupDRO, CORAL, DANN, and other state-of-the-art domain generalization methods, all optimized with standard SGD to isolate the effect of the loss function. Additional ablations and visualizations are performed to analyze intra-class variation and inter-class separation.
2d65798c7dcb31ce07864b35dc80f399f87ce9d0.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a theoretically justified hyperspherical learning algorithm for OOD generalization that directly optimizes for low intra-class variation and high inter-class separation. The approach provides a provable upper bound on OOD generalization error by minimizing variation in the hyperspherical embedding space, establishing a crucial link between theoretical understanding and practical algorithm design. The loss function is rigorously interpreted through the lens of the von Mises-Fisher distribution, and empirical results demonstrate superior OOD generalization compared to competitive baselines, even without specialized optimization techniques.

2db6355b1556d1e28925c8b8e2f1c0ad53f4763e.title: Sequential Subset Matching for Dataset Distillation
2db6355b1556d1e28925c8b8e2f1c0ad53f4763e.research_question: How can the process of dataset distillation be improved to more effectively condense both low-level and high-level features from real datasets, thereby enhancing the generalization and performance of deep neural networks trained on synthetic data?
2db6355b1556d1e28925c8b8e2f1c0ad53f4763e.hypothesis: Sequentially optimizing synthetic data subsets, rather than optimizing the entire synthetic dataset as a unified entity, will mitigate the coupling issue and enable more effective condensation of high-level features, resulting in improved performance and generalization in dataset distillation.
2db6355b1556d1e28925c8b8e2f1c0ad53f4763e.proposed_method: A novel dataset distillation strategy, Sequential Subset Matching (SeqMatch), is proposed to address the limitations of static optimization in current methods. The synthetic dataset is divided into multiple equally sized subsets, each of which is optimized sequentially. During the distillation phase, each subset is encouraged to acquire knowledge in the order that deep neural networks typically learn from real data, with earlier subsets focusing on low-level features and later subsets targeting high-level features. Each subset is optimized using a backbone distillation method (e.g., gradient or trajectory matching), with the optimization of each subset conditioned on the knowledge condensed by previous subsets. During evaluation, the subsets are used sequentially to train the network, emulating the sequential feature extraction observed in natural training processes.
2db6355b1556d1e28925c8b8e2f1c0ad53f4763e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of widely used datasets, including MNIST, SVHN, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny ImageNet, and subsets of ImageNet, covering various image resolutions. The evaluation metric will be classification accuracy, measured by training neural networks (e.g., 3-layer or 4-layer ConvNets) on the distilled synthetic datasets and reporting the mean and standard deviation over multiple random initializations. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art dataset distillation methods such as MTT, IDC, DC, DSA, DM, CAFE, KIP, FTD, RTP, and HaBa. Additional experiments will assess cross-architecture generalization by evaluating performance on ResNet, VGG, and AlexNet architectures. Hyperparameters such as the number of subsets (K) and images per class (ipc) will be systematically varied, and implementation details will be provided to ensure reproducibility.
2db6355b1556d1e28925c8b8e2f1c0ad53f4763e.novelty_claims: The proposed SeqMatch strategy introduces an adaptive, sequential optimization framework for dataset distillation that explicitly targets the condensation of high-level features, overcoming the coupling issue inherent in static optimization approaches. SeqMatch is designed as a plug-in method compatible with existing distillation backbones, offering easy integration and implementation. Experimental results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, particularly under high compression ratios, and improved generalization across architectures. The method also provides new insights into the sequential nature of knowledge acquisition in deep neural network training and its implications for synthetic data optimization.

2dd1c1c45ec63de38b4e37a064c9e145d027435b.title: Efficient Model-based Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning via Optimistic Equilibrium Computation
2dd1c1c45ec63de38b4e37a064c9e145d027435b.research_question: How can sample-efficient model-based multi-agent reinforcement learning be achieved in environments with unknown transition dynamics, enabling agents to effectively balance exploration and exploitation and reach equilibrium in general-sum Markov games with continuous state and action spaces?
2dd1c1c45ec63de38b4e37a064c9e145d027435b.hypothesis: A model-based multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithm that constructs high-probability confidence intervals around the unknown transition model and uses these to compute optimistic equilibrium policies will achieve sublinear dynamic regret and sample-efficient convergence to equilibria, outperforming non-optimistic and model-free exploration methods.
2dd1c1c45ec63de38b4e37a064c9e145d027435b.proposed_method: The proposed method, H-MARL (Hallucinated Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning), introduces a sample-efficient framework for model-based multi-agent reinforcement learning in general-sum Markov games with continuous state and action spaces. At each learning round, agents use observed transition data to update a statistical model (e.g., Gaussian Processes or deep ensembles) of the environment's transition function, constructing high-confidence intervals around the model predictions. Using these confidence bounds, the method hallucinates an optimistic Markov game by defining upper confidence bounds (UCB) on the agents' value functions, which are computed by maximizing over plausible next states within the confidence intervals. An equilibrium-finding subroutine is then used to compute a coarse-correlated equilibrium (CCE) of the hallucinated game, and the resulting equilibrium policies are executed in the environment to collect new data. This process is repeated, with the statistical model and confidence intervals updated after each round, enabling efficient exploration and exploitation.
2dd1c1c45ec63de38b4e37a064c9e145d027435b.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on an autonomous driving simulation benchmark (SMARTS), focusing on scenarios such as lane merging and intersection crossing with both autonomous and human-driven vehicles. The transition dynamics of human-driven vehicles are unknown and must be learned online through interaction. The proposed H-MARL method is compared against baselines including Thompson Sampling exploration, greedy exploitation using the predictive posterior mean, and an idealized benchmark with full knowledge of the environment model. Evaluation metrics include average cumulative agent rewards, completion rates, and episode completion times across learning rounds. Equilibrium policies are computed using independent DQN agents, and the hallucinated optimistic value functions are approximated via sampling. Additional comparisons are made with model-free methods to assess sample efficiency.
2dd1c1c45ec63de38b4e37a064c9e145d027435b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to provide theoretical guarantees for sample-efficient model-based multi-agent reinforcement learning in general-sum Markov games with continuous state and action spaces. It introduces a novel use of hallucinated optimistic value functions for multi-agent equilibrium computation, leveraging general statistical models for the transition function. Theoretical analysis includes dynamic regret bounds and sample complexity guarantees for convergence to approximate equilibria. Empirical results demonstrate fast convergence and superior performance compared to non-optimistic and model-free baselines in realistic autonomous driving scenarios.

2dfe824e0147ac2cd14ebdedbeebe89459552dd6.title: How Far Are We from Optimal Reasoning Efficiency?
2dfe824e0147ac2cd14ebdedbeebe89459552dd6.research_question: How can the efficiency of reasoning in large reasoning models (LRMs) be optimized, particularly in terms of balancing accuracy and response length under varying token budgets, and how close are current methods to achieving optimal reasoning efficiency?
2dfe824e0147ac2cd14ebdedbeebe89459552dd6.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a reinforcement learning-based approach, which directly targets the minimization of a unified efficiency gap metric across a sparse set of strategically selected token budgets, can significantly improve the reasoning efficiency of LRMs—reducing redundant reasoning without sacrificing accuracy—compared to existing fine-tuning and reward-based methods.
2dfe824e0147ac2cd14ebdedbeebe89459552dd6.proposed_method: A new family of reinforcement learning algorithms, Reasoning Efficiency Optimization with Reinforcement Learning (REO-RL), will be developed to enhance LRM reasoning efficiency. The core idea is to approximate the global efficiency objective—maximizing accuracy while minimizing response length across all token budgets—using numerical integration over a small, strategically selected set of token budgets. Two variants will be implemented: REO-RL(Oracle), which greedily selects token budgets based on estimated empirical reasoning efficiency frontiers, and REO-RL(Exp), which uses exponentially spaced token budgets for practical scenarios where the frontier is unknown. The RL objective will be formulated to optimize a weighted sum of length-constrained rewards, with coefficients derived from the trapezoidal rule, enabling efficient and effective training without exhaustive evaluation across all budgets.
2dfe824e0147ac2cd14ebdedbeebe89459552dd6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B/7B and Qwen3-4B/8B as base LRMs. Training will utilize a mixture of 135k mathematical problems from DeepScaleR and AReaL datasets. Evaluation will be performed on challenging mathematical reasoning benchmarks: AMC 2023, AIME 2024 & 2025, and Minerva Math. The primary evaluation metric will be the Reasoning Efficiency Gap (REG), a unified metric quantifying the area between a model's budget-accuracy curve and the empirical efficiency frontier, thus capturing both accuracy and response length. Baselines will include vanilla RL, RL with length-based rewards, RL with hard token budgets, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), preference learning (SimPO), and hybrid reasoning methods (HGPO). Each method will be evaluated under a maximum token budget (typically 16K or 32K), and results will be averaged over multiple benchmarks and runs.
2dfe824e0147ac2cd14ebdedbeebe89459552dd6.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the reasoning efficiency frontier as an empirical upper bound for LRM efficiency and the Reasoning Efficiency Gap (REG) as a unified, interpretable metric for evaluating reasoning efficiency. The REO-RL algorithm is novel in its use of numerical integration to approximate the global efficiency objective using a sparse set of token budgets, drastically reducing computational overhead while maintaining alignment with the optimal trade-off between accuracy and length. The approach is claimed to achieve substantial reductions in REG—often by 50% or more—while maintaining or only minimally reducing accuracy, outperforming existing fine-tuning and RL-based baselines. The methodology also provides a principled framework for benchmarking and advancing reasoning efficiency in LRMs.

2e0ffd2cd3d70898f48d4a059095ff117452c849.title: FedLPA: One-shot Federated Learning with Layer-Wise Posterior Aggregation
2e0ffd2cd3d70898f48d4a059095ff117452c849.research_question: How can one-shot federated learning be improved to effectively aggregate local neural network models into a global model under high statistical heterogeneity and non-IID data distributions, without requiring auxiliary datasets or exposing private label information?
2e0ffd2cd3d70898f48d4a059095ff117452c849.hypothesis: A one-shot federated learning approach that aggregates local models using layer-wise posterior approximations based on block-diagonal empirical Fisher information matrices will yield a more accurate and robust global model, particularly in non-IID settings, while preserving privacy and maintaining low communication overhead.
2e0ffd2cd3d70898f48d4a059095ff117452c849.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a one-shot federated learning framework that employs layer-wise posterior aggregation (FedLPA). Each client locally trains its neural network and computes layer-wise posterior approximations using Laplace approximation, where the empirical Fisher information matrix is estimated in a block-diagonal (layer-wise) form to capture intra-layer parameter correlations. Clients transmit the local layer-wise means and Fisher matrices (A, B, and M) to the server, without sharing raw data or label distributions. The server aggregates these local posteriors by constructing and solving a convex quadratic objective that directly trains the global model parameters, leveraging the Kronecker product structure of the Fisher matrices for efficiency. The global model is thus obtained in a single communication round, with no reliance on auxiliary datasets or server-side knowledge distillation.
2e0ffd2cd3d70898f48d4a059095ff117452c849.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard federated learning benchmarks, including MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, and SVHN, under various non-IID data partitioning schemes (e.g., Dirichlet distribution with varying beta, and class-per-client settings). The evaluation will compare FedLPA against state-of-the-art one-shot and multi-round federated learning baselines such as FedAvg, FedProx, FedNova, SCAFFOLD, and DENSE. Metrics will include test accuracy, communication overhead (in MB), and computation time (in minutes). The experimental setup will use a 5-layer CNN, with default settings of 10 clients, 200 local epochs, batch size 64, and learning rate 0.001. Additional experiments will assess scalability (varying number of clients), robustness to data sample proportion, sensitivity to hyperparameters, and performance in extreme label skew scenarios.
2e0ffd2cd3d70898f48d4a059095ff117452c849.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable effective one-shot federated learning by aggregating local models using block-diagonal empirical Fisher information matrices, capturing intra-layer parameter correlations without auxiliary data or label information. The method formulates and solves a convex quadratic objective for global parameter estimation, ensuring efficient and accurate aggregation. FedLPA demonstrates superior performance over existing one-shot FL methods, particularly under severe non-IID and label-skewed conditions, while maintaining moderate computation and communication overhead. The approach is data-free, privacy-preserving, and compatible with differential privacy and other privacy-enhancing techniques.

2e198278db9c643179db6fff5942ebd4ec2cccdf.title: Determinant Estimation under Memory Constraints and Neural Scaling Laws
2e198278db9c643179db6fff5942ebd4ec2cccdf.research_question: How can the log-determinant of extremely large, dense, and potentially ill-conditioned positive (semi-)definite matrices be accurately and efficiently estimated under severe memory constraints, particularly in the context of kernel matrices such as empirical Neural Tangent Kernels (NTKs) arising in large-scale machine learning applications?
2e198278db9c643179db6fff5942ebd4ec2cccdf.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that (1) a hierarchical, memory-constrained block-wise decomposition algorithm can enable exact log-determinant computation for matrices too large to fit in memory, and (2) for a broad class of kernel matrices, including NTKs, the ratio of successive pseudo-determinants follows a predictable scaling law, which can be exploited to accurately extrapolate log-determinants from small subsamples of the data.
2e198278db9c643179db6fff5942ebd4ec2cccdf.proposed_method: A two-pronged approach is proposed. First, a hierarchical memory-constrained algorithm (MEMDET) will be developed for exact log-determinant computation, leveraging block-wise LU, LDL, or Cholesky decompositions. The method processes the matrix in small blocks, storing only a few blocks in memory at a time and offloading intermediate computations to disk, thus enabling out-of-core computation for matrices orders of magnitude larger than available RAM. Second, a novel approximation algorithm (FLODANCE) will be constructed, based on empirically and theoretically justified scaling laws for the ratios of successive determinants of kernel matrices. FLODANCE will use linear regression on normalized log-determinants computed from small subsamples (via MEMDET) to estimate scaling parameters, and then extrapolate to predict the log-determinant for the full matrix. Non-asymptotic corrections and burn-in periods will be incorporated to improve accuracy, and the method will be robust to the ordering of data and the presence of small eigenvalues.
2e198278db9c643179db6fff5942ebd4ec2cccdf.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on empirical NTK Gram matrices generated from deep neural networks (ResNet9, ResNet18, ResNet50, and MobileNet) trained on standard datasets such as CIFAR-10 and MNIST.
