For smaller datasets, exact log-determinants will be computed using MEMDET and compared with FLODANCE, stochastic Lanczos quadrature (SLQ), block-diagonal approximations, and mixed-precision direct computations (16-, 32-, 64-bit). For large-scale settings (e.g., 500,000 x 500,000 matrices), MEMDET will serve as the ground truth, and FLODANCE's accuracy and computational efficiency will be evaluated. Evaluation metrics include absolute and relative error in log-determinant estimation, computational cost, and wall-clock time. Experiments will be run on high-performance hardware (e.g., NVIDIA H100/GH200 GPUs, multi-core CPUs) and will include robustness checks and ablation studies on subsample size, burn-in, and scaling law parameters.
2e198278db9c643179db6fff5942ebd4ec2cccdf.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first memory-constrained, hierarchical block decomposition algorithm (MEMDET) capable of exact log-determinant computation for matrices far exceeding available memory, including those with severe ill-conditioning. It further establishes and exploits new scaling laws for the ratios of pseudo-determinants in kernel matrices, enabling accurate log-determinant extrapolation (FLODANCE) from small data fractions. This approach achieves orders-of-magnitude speedup and improved accuracy over existing approximation methods, and is demonstrated at scales previously considered computationally intractable. The methodology is implemented in a high-performance, open-source Python package, facilitating reproducibility and practical adoption.

2e965b5d97c2d6fb4af284307735be39283792ba.title: Extracting Training Data from Diffusion Models
2e965b5d97c2d6fb4af284307735be39283792ba.research_question: How vulnerable are diffusion-based generative image models to training data extraction and privacy attacks, and what factors influence the memorization and leakage of training data in these models?
2e965b5d97c2d6fb4af284307735be39283792ba.hypothesis: Diffusion models are more prone to memorizing and regurgitating individual training examples than prior generative models such as GANs, and existing privacy-preserving techniques are insufficient to mitigate these vulnerabilities.
2e965b5d97c2d6fb4af284307735be39283792ba.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical study will be conducted to assess the privacy risks of state-of-the-art diffusion models. The approach involves defining rigorous metrics for image memorization and extraction, then developing and implementing a two-stage generate-and-filter pipeline to extract training data from large diffusion models. The methodology includes both black-box and white-box adversarial settings, leveraging membership inference, data extraction, and reconstruction attacks. The study will further analyze the impact of model architecture, dataset duplication, training hyperparameters, and augmentation on memorization by training hundreds of diffusion models under controlled conditions. Advanced attack strategies, such as influence-based outlier detection and shadow model-based likelihood ratio attacks, will be employed to maximize extraction success and understand privacy-utility tradeoffs.
2e965b5d97c2d6fb4af284307735be39283792ba.experiment_details: Experiments will target both publicly available and proprietary diffusion models, including Stable Diffusion and Imagen, as well as smaller models trained on CIFAR-10. For large models, millions of images will be generated using known prompts or random sampling, and candidate outputs will be filtered using CLIP-based similarity and pixel-wise (L2) distance to identify near-duplicates of training data. Membership inference attacks will be evaluated using both loss threshold and likelihood ratio (LiRA) methods, with performance measured by true positive and false positive rates. Baseline comparisons will include GANs and classifiers trained on the same datasets. The study will also investigate the effect of data duplication, augmentation, and model size on privacy leakage, and will use metrics such as precision-recall curves, ROC curves, and FID to quantify both extraction success and generative quality.
2e965b5d97c2d6fb4af284307735be39283792ba.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces new, rigorous definitions of image memorization tailored to diffusion models and develops a scalable, high-precision generate-and-filter pipeline for extracting training data. It is the first to demonstrate large-scale, successful extraction of real training images—including personally identifiable photos and copyrighted content—from state-of-the-art diffusion models. The study systematically analyzes the factors contributing to memorization, reveals that diffusion models are significantly less private than GANs or classifiers, and shows that existing privacy-enhancing methods do not provide an acceptable privacy-utility tradeoff. The findings challenge prevailing assumptions about the privacy of synthetic data from diffusion models and highlight the urgent need for new privacy-preserving training techniques in this domain.

2e99a953a34b703658cdf6a510e2bf89b823771a.title: DiLightNet: Fine-grained Lighting Control for Diffusion-based Image Generation
2e99a953a34b703658cdf6a510e2bf89b823771a.research_question: How can fine-grained and independent control over lighting conditions be achieved in text-driven, diffusion-based image generation, overcoming the limitations of current models that entangle lighting and content and lack precise lighting specification?
2e99a953a34b703658cdf6a510e2bf89b823771a.hypothesis: Incorporating radiance hints—coarse visualizations of scene geometry under target lighting—into the diffusion process, combined with neural encoding of provisional images, enables precise and independent control of lighting in generated images, without requiring exact scene geometry or real-world photographs.
2e99a953a34b703658cdf6a510e2bf89b823771a.proposed_method: A three-stage pipeline is developed for lighting-controlled, text-driven image synthesis. First, a provisional image is generated using a pretrained diffusion model based on a text prompt and content seed, under uncontrolled lighting. Second, radiance hints are computed by estimating a coarse foreground object shape via off-the-shelf segmentation and depth estimation networks; these hints represent the object's appearance under the target lighting with canonical materials. The radiance hints are channel-wise multiplied with a neural encoding of the provisional image, and the result is passed, along with the text prompt and an appearance seed, to a finetuned diffusion model (DiLightNet) using ControlNet architecture. In the third stage, the background is inpainted to be consistent with the target lighting, either by direct rendering (for environment maps) or by using a diffusion-based inpainting model. The method supports arbitrary lighting conditions and allows user control over both appearance and lighting.
2e99a953a34b703658cdf6a510e2bf89b823771a.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a variety of text prompts and lighting conditions, including both point and environment lighting. The training dataset comprises 25,000 synthetic 3D objects from the Objaverse dataset, rendered from multiple viewpoints and under diverse lighting setups (point lights, area lights, environment maps, and monochrome variants), with materials sourced from both the dataset and the INRIA-Highres SVBRDF dataset. Evaluation is performed on a held-out synthetic test set of 50 high-quality objects, rendered under multiple viewpoints and lighting conditions. Quantitative metrics include PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS, and qualitative assessment involves user studies measuring perceptual lighting accuracy and appearance consistency. Baselines include variants of the proposed architecture (e.g., direct ControlNet input, non-encoded multiplication, different numbers of radiance hints), and ablation studies assess the impact of each component and training augmentation.
2e99a953a34b703658cdf6a510e2bf89b823771a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel use of radiance hints derived from coarse depth and segmentation estimates to guide the diffusion process for lighting control, eliminating the need for precise geometry or real photographs. Unlike prior methods, this framework enables fine-grained, independent control over lighting and content in text-driven image generation, supports arbitrary lighting types, and disentangles lighting from material and shape. The method leverages a unique combination of neural encoding, channel-wise multiplication, and ControlNet-based conditioning, and demonstrates superior flexibility and control compared to language-token-based or limited-direction lighting approaches.

2e9badeda30a5e86d17b4f725ad53aa3a0b321b0.title: Variational Learning is Effective for Large Deep Networks
2e9badeda30a5e86d17b4f725ad53aa3a0b321b0.research_question: Is variational learning an effective and practical approach for training large deep neural networks, including language models and image classifiers, in terms of both predictive performance and uncertainty estimation, without incurring significant computational overhead compared to standard optimizers?
2e9badeda30a5e86d17b4f725ad53aa3a0b321b0.hypothesis: Variational learning, when implemented with an improved optimizer that directly optimizes the variational objective, can match or surpass the predictive accuracy of standard optimizers such as Adam while providing superior uncertainty estimates, scalability, and practical utility for large-scale deep networks.
2e9badeda30a5e86d17b4f725ad53aa3a0b321b0.proposed_method: A new optimizer, Improved Variational Online Newton (IVON), will be developed to directly optimize the variational objective for deep neural networks. IVON will use an Adam-like update scheme, but with modifications to estimate the Hessian efficiently and ensure the positivity of variance parameters, enabling stable and scalable variational learning even for very large models. The method will employ a reparameterization trick for efficient gradient and Hessian estimation, and incorporate practical tricks such as adaptive weight decay as the prior, initialization strategies for Hessian estimates, and gradient clipping for stability in transformer models. IVON will support both single and multi-GPU training, allowing for Monte Carlo sampling across devices to reduce variance, and can be implemented as a drop-in replacement for Adam in standard deep learning frameworks. The approach will also enable posterior averaging for improved predictive uncertainty and facilitate downstream tasks such as fine-tuning, model merging, and sensitivity analysis.
2e9badeda30a5e86d17b4f725ad53aa3a0b321b0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of large-scale deep learning tasks, including training GPT-2 language models (with up to 773M parameters) from scratch on the OpenWebText dataset, and training ResNet-50 and other architectures on ImageNet, TinyImageNet, and CIFAR-100. IVON will be compared to baselines such as AdamW, SGD, MC-Dropout, SWAG, Laplace, Bayes-by-Backprop, VOGN, and deep ensembles. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, negative log-likelihood (NLL), expected calibration error (ECE), Brier score, and out-of-domain (OOD) detection metrics such as AUROC and AUPR. Additional experiments will assess fine-tuning performance on GLUE tasks using large language models (DeBERTAv3, RoBERTa), model merging efficiency, and the ability to estimate generalization error and data sensitivity. Ablation studies will examine computational efficiency, the impact of Hessian estimation choices, and initialization strategies. Multi-GPU and low-precision (bf16) training will also be evaluated.
2e9badeda30a5e86d17b4f725ad53aa3a0b321b0.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a practical, scalable variational optimizer (IVON) that enables direct optimization of the variational objective for large deep networks at a computational cost nearly identical to Adam. IVON provides improved or comparable predictive accuracy and significantly better uncertainty estimates than existing baselines, including for large language models trained from scratch. The method demonstrates new use cases for variational learning, such as improved fine-tuning, efficient model merging, faithful generalization error prediction, and sensitivity analysis at scale. IVON's design allows for easy integration into existing deep learning workflows and supports flexible posterior forms, paving the way for further advances in Bayesian deep learning for large-scale models.

2e9db13d2f135ea4c3d85003aafc2e437b96322e.title: Prompt Tuning Strikes Back: Customizing Foundation Models with Low-Rank Prompt Adaptation
2e9db13d2f135ea4c3d85003aafc2e437b96322e.research_question: How can foundation models be efficiently customized for user-specific downstream tasks without requiring server-side storage or processing of task-specific adapters, while maintaining or surpassing the performance of existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods?
2e9db13d2f135ea4c3d85003aafc2e437b96322e.hypothesis: A prompt-tuning approach that combines task-specific and instance-specific soft prompts using a low-rank decomposition and a gating mechanism will achieve performance comparable to or better than state-of-the-art parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods and full fine-tuning, while requiring fewer parameters and eliminating the need for server-side adapters.
2e9db13d2f135ea4c3d85003aafc2e437b96322e.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces Low-Rank Prompt Adaptation (LoPA), a prompt-tuning-based framework that constructs soft prompts from two components: a task-specific element shared across instances and an instance-specific element unique to each input. These components are combined using a gating function (implemented as a sigmoid-based Hadamard product), allowing the model to balance generalization and customization. The instance-specific component is generated via a low-rank decomposition (Z_I = u × v^T), where u and v are learned through separate MLPs, significantly reducing parameter count. The soft prompt is prepended to the input embeddings, and all learning is performed via back-propagation, with the encoder network generating input representations for the instance-specific component. This design enables the soft prompt to be computed client-side, requiring no server-side model modification or storage of adapters.
2e9db13d2f135ea4c3d85003aafc2e437b96322e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six Natural Language Understanding (NLU) tasks from the GLUE benchmark (SST-2, MNLI, MRPC, QNLI, QQP, RTE) and three code-related tasks (MBPP for code generation, CruxEval-I and CruxEval-O for code understanding). Multiple foundation model backbones will be used, including RoBERTa (355M), CodeGen-mono (350M), Deepseek-Coder (1.3B, 7B), Phi-2 (2.7B), Phi-3 (3.8B), and Llama3 (8B). Baselines for comparison include full fine-tuning (FFT), LoRA, p-tuning-v2, prefix-tuning, standard prompt-tuning, S-IDPG, and DePT. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy and F1 for NLU tasks, and pass@1 for code tasks. Training configurations will be standardized across methods, with prompt length and low-rank decomposition rank tuned for optimal performance. Ablation studies will assess the effects of prompt length, rank, encoder choice, and combination functions for the soft prompt.
2e9db13d2f135ea4c3d85003aafc2e437b96322e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel instance-aware prompt-tuning strategy that combines task-specific and instance-specific soft prompts via a gating mechanism and low-rank decomposition, achieving high parameter efficiency. Unlike existing PEFT methods, LoPA eliminates the need for server-side storage or processing of adapters, enabling user-end customization. The method demonstrates performance on par with or superior to state-of-the-art PEFT techniques and full fine-tuning, while using significantly fewer parameters. Additional contributions include a comprehensive empirical evaluation across diverse tasks and model backbones, and detailed ablation studies highlighting the effectiveness and robustness of the approach.

2ea9167ca0dd536923ea0968d6b89e2b6cc34f21.title: Consistency Trajectory Models: Learning Probability Flow ODE Trajectory of Diffusion
2ea9167ca0dd536923ea0968d6b89e2b6cc34f21.research_question: How can generative diffusion models be improved to allow efficient, high-quality sampling with flexible trade-offs between speed and sample fidelity, while unifying score-based and distillation-based approaches and enabling new controllable sampling schemes?
2ea9167ca0dd536923ea0968d6b89e2b6cc34f21.hypothesis: A unified generative modeling framework that learns the full trajectory of the probability flow ODE in diffusion processes, and combines distillation, denoising score matching, and adversarial objectives, will enable efficient anytime-to-anytime sampling, improve sample quality, and provide a natural trade-off between speed and fidelity, surpassing existing score-based and distillation-based diffusion models.
2ea9167ca0dd536923ea0968d6b89e2b6cc34f21.proposed_method: A Consistency Trajectory Model (CTM) is proposed, which trains a single neural network to predict both infinitesimal and long-step jumps along the probability flow ODE (PF-ODE) trajectory of a diffusion process. The model is designed to output scores (gradients of log-density) and enables unrestricted traversal between any initial and final time, supporting both deterministic and stochastic sampling. Training leverages a soft consistency loss that matches the model's anytime-to-anytime jump predictions to those of a pre-trained teacher model, using a mixture of teacher and student predictions over randomly sampled time intervals. Auxiliary losses, including denoising score matching (DSM) and adversarial GAN losses, are incorporated to provide direct training signals from the data distribution and improve the accuracy of both small and large jumps. Adaptive weighting of loss terms is employed to stabilize training, and the architecture is based on a modified UNet with temporal and positional embeddings.
2ea9167ca0dd536923ea0968d6b89e2b6cc34f21.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image generation benchmarks, including CIFAR-10 and ImageNet at 64x64 resolution. The CTM will be trained using pre-trained diffusion models (e.g., EDM for CIFAR-10 and CM for ImageNet) as teachers, and compared against state-of-the-art GANs, score-based diffusion models, and distillation-based models. Evaluation metrics will include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS), and Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL), with sampling performed at varying numbers of function evaluations (NFE) to assess the speed-quality trade-off. Both unconditional and conditional generation settings will be tested, and ablation studies will investigate the effects of soft consistency, DSM, and GAN losses. Additional experiments will explore controllable generation and the impact of the proposed gamma-sampling scheme.
2ea9167ca0dd536923ea0968d6b89e2b6cc34f21.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified framework that generalizes both score-based and distillation-based diffusion models, enabling anytime-to-anytime trajectory learning and sampling. It is the first to enable both exact score evaluation and unrestricted time traversal along the PF-ODE, supporting new deterministic and stochastic sampling schemes (gamma-sampling) that trade off speed and quality. The method allows efficient integration of adversarial and denoising losses, leading to improved sample quality and likelihood, and achieves state-of-the-art results for single-step diffusion model sampling. The approach also facilitates controllable and conditional generation by providing access to the score function, and enables likelihood computation in a distillation-based framework.

2edccb8fa562ed52cd49ea6fc67ed32db6218247.title: From Sparse to Soft Mixtures of Experts
2edccb8fa562ed52cd49ea6fc67ed32db6218247.research_question: How can the scalability, efficiency, and stability of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures be improved for large-scale Transformer models, particularly in the context of visual recognition and transfer learning tasks?
2edccb8fa562ed52cd49ea6fc67ed32db6218247.hypothesis: A fully-differentiable, soft assignment-based Mixture-of-Experts framework for Transformers will address key limitations of sparse MoEs—such as training instability, token dropping, expert imbalance, and scaling difficulties—while maintaining or improving computational efficiency and model performance.
2edccb8fa562ed52cd49ea6fc67ed32db6218247.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces SoftMoE, a fully-differentiable MoE layer for Transformers that replaces hard, discrete token-to-expert assignments with soft, weighted combinations of all input tokens for each expert. Each SoftMoE layer computes dispatch weights via a softmax over learned parameters, producing input slots as convex combinations of tokens, which are then processed by experts (typically MLPs). The outputs from experts are recombined using another set of softmax-based combine weights to reconstruct the output tokens. Layer normalization and L2 normalization are applied to stabilize training, and the number of slots per expert is a key hyperparameter that determines computational cost. The approach is designed to be hardware-friendly by avoiding slow top-k or sorting operations, and can be distributed across multiple devices for large-scale training.
2edccb8fa562ed52cd49ea6fc67ed32db6218247.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale image classification tasks, primarily using the proprietary JFT-4B dataset (over 4 billion images, 29k classes) for pretraining, with evaluation on ImageNet-1k (both 10-shot and full fine-tuning) and additional downstream tasks. Baselines will include dense Vision Transformers (ViT) and popular sparse MoE variants such as Tokens Choice and Experts Choice. Models will be trained for up to 10 million steps, with ablations on the number of experts, slots, and routing mechanisms. Evaluation metrics will include precision-at-1 on JFT-4B, ImageNet 10-shot accuracy, and ImageNet fine-tuning accuracy, as well as inference speed (FLOPs and wall-clock time). Additional experiments will test transfer to image-text contrastive learning using the WebLI dataset (10B image-text pairs) and public LAION-400M, comparing zero-shot performance on several benchmarks.
2edccb8fa562ed52cd49ea6fc67ed32db6218247.novelty_claims: The proposed SoftMoE framework offers a fully-differentiable alternative to traditional sparse MoEs, eliminating token dropping and expert imbalance by ensuring every slot is a weighted mixture of all tokens. The method enables scaling to a large number of experts without increasing inference cost, avoids non-differentiable routing, and is significantly faster due to the absence of top-k operations. SoftMoE achieves superior performance-cost tradeoffs, outperforming both dense and sparse baselines across multiple metrics and tasks, and demonstrates strong transferability to contrastive learning and downstream applications. The approach also provides new insights into the optimal configuration of experts and slots, and is compatible with large-scale distributed training.

2eed1fad9bbf887d4395de40f20144c4fafefd7f.title: DeepSeek-R1 incentivizes reasoning in LLMs through reinforcement learning
2eed1fad9bbf887d4395de40f20144c4fafefd7f.research_question: How can large language models be incentivized to develop advanced reasoning capabilities without relying on extensive human-annotated reasoning trajectories, and how can these capabilities be systematically transferred to smaller models while maintaining alignment with human preferences and safety requirements?
2eed1fad9bbf887d4395de40f20144c4fafefd7f.hypothesis: Reinforcement learning, when used with carefully designed reward signals based solely on the correctness of final predictions and minimal structural constraints, can autonomously elicit sophisticated reasoning behaviors in large language models, surpassing models trained with conventional supervised learning on human demonstrations.
2eed1fad9bbf887d4395de40f20144c4fafefd7f.proposed_method: A multi-stage reinforcement learning framework is proposed to train large language models for advanced reasoning tasks. The initial stage employs Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) on a pre-trained base model, using rule-based rewards that evaluate both the correctness of answers and adherence to a specified reasoning format, without any supervised fine-tuning or human-annotated reasoning traces. The model is prompted to generate explicit reasoning steps and final answers, with rewards based on verifiable outcomes (e.g., mathematical correctness, passing code test cases) and structural compliance (e.g., use of <think> and <answer> tags). Subsequent stages integrate rejection sampling, supervised fine-tuning on both reasoning and non-reasoning datasets, and additional RL phases using model-based reward models that capture human preferences for helpfulness, harmlessness, and language consistency. Language consistency rewards are introduced to mitigate language mixing, and the pipeline is designed to enable distillation into smaller models.
2eed1fad9bbf887d4395de40f20144c4fafefd7f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a wide range of benchmarks, including MMLU, MMLU-Redux, MMLU-Pro, C-Eval, CMMLU, IFEval, FRAMES, GPQA Diamond, SimpleQA, C-SimpleQA, SWE-Bench Verified, Aider, LiveCodeBench, Codeforces, CNMO2024, and AIME 2024. The evaluation will compare the proposed models at various developmental stages against strong baselines, including human performance and state-of-the-art LLMs, using metrics such as exact match, pass@1, F1, accuracy, and win rates on preference-based leaderboards. The experimental setup involves large-scale RL training with batch sizes of 512, sampling 16 outputs per question, and using both rule-based and model-based reward signals. Safety and alignment are assessed using curated safety datasets and preference pairs, with comprehensive analysis on language mixing, reasoning transfer to smaller models, and ablation studies on reward design.
2eed1fad9bbf887d4395de40f20144c4fafefd7f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach eliminates the need for human-annotated reasoning trajectories by leveraging pure reinforcement learning with verifiable, rule-based rewards. The framework enables the organic emergence of advanced reasoning behaviors, such as self-reflection and verification, in LLMs. The multi-stage pipeline systematically integrates reasoning and non-reasoning capabilities, aligns model outputs with human preferences, and addresses language consistency. Additionally, the method demonstrates that strong reasoning abilities can be distilled into smaller models, providing a scalable and accessible resource for the research community.

2ef60a4ea4ea53056be811ff55679eb59fb4b586.title: Confident Adaptive Language Modeling
2ef60a4ea4ea53056be811ff55679eb59fb4b586.research_question: How can the inference-time efficiency of large Transformer-based language models be improved by dynamically allocating computation per input and generation timestep, while maintaining rigorous, user-defined quality guarantees on the generated output sequences?
2ef60a4ea4ea53056be811ff55679eb59fb4b586.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a principled, confidence-driven early-exit mechanism can be calibrated to dynamically reduce the number of layers used per generated token in autoregressive language models, achieving significant computational savings while provably maintaining global sequence-level quality constraints as specified by the user.
2ef60a4ea4ea53056be811ff55679eb59fb4b586.proposed_method: A novel framework, Confident Adaptive Language Modeling (CALM), is proposed to enable dynamic allocation of computational resources during autoregressive decoding in Transformer-based language models. The method introduces per-token early-exit decisions based on calibrated confidence measures, such as softmax response, hidden-state saturation, or a lightweight early-exit classifier. A decaying threshold function is applied to allow more aggressive early exits as decoding progresses, balancing performance and efficiency. The approach leverages a statistically rigorous calibration procedure, grounded in the Learn then Test (LTT) framework, to connect local exit decisions to global sequence-level constraints (e.g., textual or risk consistency), ensuring that user-defined tolerances are satisfied with high probability. The calibration uses only unlabeled data and supports both textual similarity and risk-based objectives, enabling flexibility across tasks.
2ef60a4ea4ea53056be811ff55679eb59fb4b586.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three diverse text generation tasks: CNN/DM for summarization, WMT15 EN-FR for machine translation, and SQuAD 1.1 for open-domain question answering. The T5 encoder-decoder architecture (8 layers) will serve as the backbone, with CALM integrated for adaptive decoding. Evaluation metrics include ROUGE-L for summarization, BLEU/BLEURT for translation, and token-level F1 for QA, with efficiency measured by average decoder layers per token, FLOPs reduction, and wall-clock speedup. Baselines will include static layer usage and alternative early-exit strategies. Calibration will be performed using an 80/20 split of validation/test data, with rigorous statistical guarantees (e.g., 95% confidence) on performance degradation, and multiple random trials to assess robustness. Comparisons will be made against both static and oracle early-exit strategies.
2ef60a4ea4ea53056be811ff55679eb59fb4b586.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a theoretically grounded, calibration-driven approach for adaptive computation in autoregressive language models, providing provable guarantees on global output quality. Key innovations include the integration of per-token confidence measures with global sequence-level constraints, a decaying threshold mechanism for fine-grained control of the performance-efficiency tradeoff, and a calibration procedure that requires only unlabeled data. The method is generalizable to any multi-layered autoregressive model and supports both textual and risk-based consistency objectives. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate substantial efficiency gains (up to 3x speedup) with minimal or controlled performance loss, establishing a new standard for controllable, efficient inference in large language models.

2f1df8c0806d5756929a09aba60ac7f43778a938.title: Why Do We Need Weight Decay in Modern Deep Learning?
2f1df8c0806d5756929a09aba60ac7f43778a938.research_question: What is the role and necessity of weight decay in modern deep learning across different training regimes, and how does it affect optimization dynamics, generalization, and training stability in both over-training and under-training scenarios?
2f1df8c0806d5756929a09aba60ac7f43778a938.hypothesis: Weight decay does not primarily act as an explicit regularizer in modern deep learning but instead modifies the optimization dynamics in a way that enhances implicit regularization, improves training loss optimization, and ensures stability, particularly in low-precision training environments.
2f1df8c0806d5756929a09aba60ac7f43778a938.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical and theoretical investigation will be conducted to analyze the effects of weight decay in both over-training (multiple passes through data, e.g., vision tasks) and under-training (few passes, e.g., large language models) regimes. In the over-training regime, experiments will focus on how weight decay interacts with large learning rates to maintain non-vanishing SGD noise, thereby enhancing implicit regularization via loss stabilization and controlling the norm of the network Jacobian. In the under-training regime, the analysis will examine how weight decay modulates the effective learning rate (ELR) in optimizers like AdamW, impacting the bias-variance tradeoff and training stability, especially under reduced precision (bfloat16) settings. The methodology will include both direct training and fine-tuning phases, as well as the use of exponential moving averages (EMA) to characterize stationary distributions in function space.
2f1df8c0806d5756929a09aba60ac7f43778a938.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed using standard deep learning architectures: ResNet18 (and variants) for image classification tasks (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet) and GPT-2 (124M parameters) for language modeling on OpenWebText. Training will be conducted under both over-training (multiple epochs, SGD) and under-training (one epoch, AdamW) regimes. Baselines will include training with and without weight decay, varying learning rates, and different regularization strengths. Evaluation metrics will include test error, training loss, parameter and Jacobian norms, and training stability (e.g., loss spikes in low-precision settings). Additional analyses will involve matching effective learning rates, using EMA and fine-tuning, and comparing the impact of weight decay versus equivalent learning rate schedules. Experiments will also assess the stability of training under bfloat16 and float32 precision.
2f1df8c0806d5756929a09aba60ac7f43778a938.novelty_claims: The proposed research provides a unifying perspective on the role of weight decay in modern deep learning, demonstrating that its primary benefit is not explicit regularization but rather the modulation of optimization dynamics. It establishes that in over-training regimes, weight decay combined with large learning rates enhances implicit regularization through loss stabilization and Jacobian norm control, while in under-training regimes, it acts as a mechanism for tuning the effective learning rate and ensuring training stability, especially in reduced precision environments. The work offers new empirical insights and practical guidelines for selecting weight decay and learning rate parameters, and clarifies the distinct mechanisms by which weight decay operates across different training paradigms.

2f28ad4a7e3208ee66b02acfd3130a727dd8fe46.title: Stochastic Encodings for Active Feature Acquisition
2f28ad4a7e3208ee66b02acfd3130a727dd8fe46.research_question: How can instance-wise, sequential feature acquisition be improved to make more effective and non-myopic decisions for prediction tasks when features are not all available at once, particularly in settings such as medical diagnosis or other domains with costly or limited feature access?
2f28ad4a7e3208ee66b02acfd3130a727dd8fe46.hypothesis: A latent variable model that leverages stochastic encodings and an information bottleneck regularization, combined with a novel acquisition objective based on gradients in the latent space and probability-weighted class likelihoods, will outperform existing reinforcement learning and conditional mutual information-based approaches for active feature acquisition in terms of predictive accuracy and efficiency.
2f28ad4a7e3208ee66b02acfd3130a727dd8fe46.proposed_method: A new framework, Stochastic Encodings for Feature Acquisition (SEFA), is proposed for active feature acquisition. The method employs an encoder-predictor architecture with a stochastic latent variable, where each feature is encoded separately into latent components, and missing features are handled via imputation and a binary mask. The model is trained in a supervised manner with a predictive loss and an information bottleneck regularization term, encouraging the latent space to encode only label-relevant information. During acquisition, a custom objective is computed by taking the expectation over multiple latent samples, using the norm of the gradient of the class probability with respect to each feature's latent components as an importance score, and weighting these scores by the current predicted class probabilities. This approach allows the model to reason about the effects of acquiring features across many possible unobserved realizations, enabling non-greedy, instance-wise, and label-focused acquisitions.
2f28ad4a7e3208ee66b02acfd3130a727dd8fe46.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of synthetic and real-world datasets, including synthetic binary and multi-class classification tasks, tabular datasets (e.g., Bank Marketing, California Housing, MiniBooNE), image datasets (MNIST, FashionMNIST), and medical datasets (METABRIC, TCGA). The method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines, including reinforcement learning approaches (Opportunistic RL, GSMRL), greedy CMI maximization methods (DIME, GDFS), generative model-based CMI estimators (ACFlow, EDDI), and standard baselines such as random and fixed feature orderings. Evaluation metrics will include AUROC for binary tasks and accuracy for multi-class tasks, with performance tracked at each acquisition step. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of each component of the method, such as latent space regularization, number of latent samples, and the use of stochastic encoders.
2f28ad4a7e3208ee66b02acfd3130a727dd8fe46.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a fundamentally new acquisition objective that operates in a regularized stochastic latent space rather than the feature space, leveraging gradient-based importance scores and probability-weighted aggregation across classes. This method addresses key limitations of existing RL and CMI-based methods, such as myopic acquisitions and training instability, by enabling non-greedy, label-focused, and instance-wise feature selection. The use of stochastic encodings allows the model to reason about unobserved features, and the information bottleneck ensures that only label-relevant information is used for acquisition. Extensive experiments and ablations are designed to demonstrate that each novel component is critical for achieving state-of-the-art performance.

2f2a430ba6c93bcfaf4818316ff8a27b1e034b1a.title: Flocks of Stochastic Parrots: Differentially Private Prompt Learning for Large Language Models
2f2a430ba6c93bcfaf4818316ff8a27b1e034b1a.research_question: How can prompt-based learning for large language models be made differentially private to protect sensitive information in prompts, while maintaining high utility and practical deployment, especially in scenarios where only black-box access to the model is available?
2f2a430ba6c93bcfaf4818316ff8a27b1e034b1a.hypothesis: It is possible to develop differentially private algorithms for both soft and discrete prompt learning in large language models that achieve utility comparable to non-private prompting, while providing rigorous privacy guarantees, even when only black-box access to the model is available.
2f2a430ba6c93bcfaf4818316ff8a27b1e034b1a.proposed_method: Two complementary methods for differentially private prompt learning will be developed. First, PromptDPSGD will be designed for soft prompts by applying differentially private stochastic gradient descent (DPSGD) to the soft prompt embeddings, keeping the underlying LLM frozen. This method leverages the small number of trainable parameters in soft prompts, enabling efficient and private adaptation to downstream tasks. Second, PromptPATE will be introduced for discrete prompts, where an ensemble of LLMs, each prompted with different private data, acts as 'teachers' whose predictions on public data are aggregated via a noisy voting mechanism (using the Confident GNMAX algorithm) to ensure differential privacy. The aggregated outputs are used to construct a 'student' prompt, which can be publicly released and used for inference. Both methods are designed to be compatible with commercial LLM APIs, requiring only black-box access for PromptPATE.
2f2a430ba6c93bcfaf4818316ff8a27b1e034b1a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple standard NLP classification benchmarks, including sst2, qnli, qqp, mnli (from the GLUE benchmark), dbpedia, agnews, and trec. For PromptDPSGD, RoBERTa models will be used, and performance will be compared to state-of-the-art private fine-tuning methods (full fine-tuning, LoRA-tuning) using accuracy as the primary metric. For PromptPATE, commercial LLM APIs such as GPT-3 (Babbage and Curie) and Claude will be utilized, with ensembles of one-shot or few-shot prompts serving as teachers. The evaluation will include both in-distribution (IID) and out-of-distribution (OOD) public data for knowledge transfer, and privacy guarantees will be reported in terms of (ε, δ)-differential privacy. Baselines will include zero-shot prompting, non-private prompting, and private ensemble accuracy. Additional ablation studies will assess the impact of public dataset size and teacher consensus on privacy-utility trade-offs.
2f2a430ba6c93bcfaf4818316ff8a27b1e034b1a.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first algorithms for differentially private prompt learning in large language models, covering both soft and discrete prompt paradigms. PromptDPSGD offers a parameter-efficient alternative to private fine-tuning by updating only soft prompt embeddings, while PromptPATE is the first method to enable differentially private prompt learning with only black-box access to commercial LLM APIs. The approach demonstrates that high downstream utility can be achieved with strong privacy guarantees, and that private prompt learning is more practical and scalable than private fine-tuning, especially as LLMs grow in size and are increasingly accessed via APIs.

2f2b2567187dfb22b1a2e2c9724cc55df80f9444.title: Label-Noise Robust Diffusion Models
2f2b2567187dfb22b1a2e2c9724cc55df80f9444.research_question: How can conditional diffusion models be trained to be robust to label noise in the conditional inputs, thereby improving the quality and condition-alignment of generated data in the presence of noisy labels?
2f2b2567187dfb22b1a2e2c9724cc55df80f9444.hypothesis: Incorporating instance-wise and time-dependent label transition information into the training objective of conditional diffusion models will enable the models to learn clean-label conditional scores, resulting in improved robustness to label noise and better generation quality under noisy label conditions.
2f2b2567187dfb22b1a2e2c9724cc55df80f9444.proposed_method: A novel objective, Transition-aware weighted Denoising Score Matching (TDSM), will be developed for training conditional diffusion models with noisy labels. The method leverages a linear relationship between noisy-label and clean-label conditional scores, expressing the noisy-label score as a convex combination of clean-label scores weighted by instance-wise and time-dependent transition probabilities. To estimate these transition-aware weights, a time-dependent noisy-label classifier will be trained, and a transition matrix—either known a priori or estimated from data—will be used. The training procedure involves evaluating the transition-aware weights for each data instance and diffusion timestep, computing the weighted sum of score network outputs for all classes, and minimizing the L2 loss between this sum and the perturbed data score. Practical implementation techniques, such as selective backpropagation and thresholding of negligible weights, will be employed to reduce computational overhead.
2f2b2567187dfb22b1a2e2c9724cc55df80f9444.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on benchmark datasets including MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and the real-world Clothing-1M dataset. Synthetic label noise will be introduced in both symmetric and asymmetric forms at varying noise rates, and real-world label noise will be evaluated using naturally noisy datasets. The primary backbone will be EDM, with additional backbones tested for robustness. Baseline comparisons will include standard Denoising Score Matching (DSM) and S-weighted DSM (SDSM), as well as state-of-the-art label-noise robust GANs and label correction methods such as VolMinNet and DISC. Evaluation metrics will include unconditional metrics (FID, IS, Density, Coverage) and conditional metrics (CW-FID, CW-Density, CW-Coverage, Classification Accuracy Score). Ablation studies will assess the impact of weight estimation methods and the integration with external label correction pipelines.
2f2b2567187dfb22b1a2e2c9724cc55df80f9444.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to introduce a theoretically grounded, instance-wise and time-dependent transition-aware weighting scheme for denoising score matching in diffusion models under label noise. The method provides a principled way to align noisy-label conditional scores with clean-label targets, leveraging a novel estimator for transition-aware weights based on a time-dependent noisy-label classifier. The framework is orthogonal and complementary to existing label correction methods, and demonstrates improved conditional and unconditional generation performance even when combined with external noisy label correctors. The approach also reveals and addresses the risk of label noise in widely used benchmark datasets.

2f3822eb380b5e753a6d579f31dfc3ec4c4a0820.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
2f3822eb380b5e753a6d579f31dfc3ec4c4a0820.research_question: How can large language models be enhanced to perform more effective general problem solving, particularly for tasks that require exploration, strategic lookahead, and global planning, beyond the limitations of token-level, left-to-right inference?
2f3822eb380b5e753a6d579f31dfc3ec4c4a0820.hypothesis: Introducing a framework that enables language models to explore multiple reasoning paths as trees of intermediate thoughts, with deliberate self-evaluation and search-based planning, will significantly improve problem-solving performance on tasks requiring non-trivial planning or search.
2f3822eb380b5e753a6d579f31dfc3ec4c4a0820.proposed_method: A novel inference framework, Tree of Thoughts (ToT), is proposed for large language models. This approach represents problem solving as a search over a tree, where each node is a 'thought'—a coherent language sequence serving as an intermediate step. The method involves decomposing the problem into thought steps, generating multiple candidate thoughts at each step using either i.i.d. sampling or sequential proposals, and evaluating these states via language model-based heuristics (either independent value assignment or comparative voting). Search algorithms such as breadth-first search (BFS) or depth-first search (DFS) are integrated to systematically explore the tree, allowing for lookahead, backtracking, and pruning of less promising paths. The framework is modular, allowing independent variation of the base language model, thought decomposition, generation, evaluation, and search procedures.
2f3822eb380b5e753a6d579f31dfc3ec4c4a0820.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three challenging tasks: Game of 24 (mathematical reasoning with arithmetic operations), Creative Writing (generating coherent multi-paragraph passages ending in specified sentences), and Mini Crosswords (filling a crossword grid from clues). For Game of 24, a dataset of 100 hard instances will be used, with success defined as producing a valid equation using all input numbers exactly once. For Creative Writing, 100 inputs will be generated, and outputs will be evaluated for passage coherency using both GPT-4 scoring (1-10 scale) and human pairwise preference. Baselines will include standard input-output prompting, chain-of-thought prompting, self-consistency, and iterative refinement. Evaluation metrics will include success rate (Game of 24), average coherency score (Creative Writing), and human preference rates. The experimental setup will use GPT-4 with a sampling temperature of 0.7, and ablations will be performed to analyze the impact of different components.
2f3822eb380b5e753a6d579f31dfc3ec4c4a0820.novelty_claims: The proposed framework generalizes and subsumes existing prompting strategies (IO, CoT, self-consistency) by enabling explicit search and deliberation over trees of thoughts, rather than single chains. It introduces language model-driven heuristics for both generation and evaluation of intermediate reasoning steps, and integrates classical search algorithms for systematic exploration. The approach is modular, adaptable to various tasks and resource constraints, and requires no additional model training. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate substantial improvements over existing methods, especially on tasks requiring planning, search, or creative reasoning.

2f4788a62ffa9929c7b399a9bc1e07917cc58b06.title: Harmful Fine-tuning Attacks and Defenses for Large Language Models: A Survey
2f4788a62ffa9929c7b399a9bc1e07917cc58b06.research_question: What are the vulnerabilities and defense mechanisms associated with harmful fine-tuning attacks on large language models (LLMs) in fine-tuning-as-a-service scenarios, and how can these attacks be systematically characterized, evaluated, and mitigated?
2f4788a62ffa9929c7b399a9bc1e07917cc58b06.hypothesis: Harmful fine-tuning attacks can compromise the safety alignment of LLMs, but robust defense strategies—applied at various stages of the fine-tuning pipeline—can improve resistance and stability against such attacks without significantly degrading downstream task performance.
2f4788a62ffa9929c7b399a9bc1e07917cc58b06.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed to systematically analyze harmful fine-tuning attacks and corresponding defenses for LLMs. The approach will include: (1) formalizing the threat model and attack surface in fine-tuning-as-a-service, including both adversarial and non-adversarial scenarios; (2) categorizing and benchmarking existing attack strategies (e.g., vanilla, advanced, covert) and defense mechanisms (e.g., alignment-stage, fine-tuning-stage, post-fine-tuning-stage); (3) proposing new evaluation methodologies and metrics, such as harmful score and fine-tune accuracy, to assess both attack effectiveness and defense robustness; and (4) designing and testing novel defense algorithms that either preserve alignment knowledge, remove or attenuate harmful knowledge, or constrain model drift during fine-tuning. The methodology will emphasize technical rigor in optimization-based defenses, data curation, and regularization strategies.
2f4788a62ffa9929c7b399a9bc1e07917cc58b06.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using standard LLMs such as Llama2-7B, with fine-tuning performed on datasets that mix benign and harmful samples (e.g., SST2 combined with curated harmful data). The evaluation will utilize metrics including harmful score (to quantify safety degradation), fine-tune accuracy (to assess task performance), alignment loss, and embedding drift. Baselines will include both aligned and non-aligned models, as well as a variety of attack and defense strategies from the literature (e.g., Vaccine, RepNoise, TAR, Booster, LDIFS, Freeze, Constrain-SFT). The setup will simulate both adversarial and non-adversarial user uploads, and will test defense effectiveness across varying ratios of harmful data and fine-tuning steps. Visualization techniques such as t-SNE will be used to analyze embedding drift, and robustness will be measured against both seen and unseen harmful prompts.
2f4788a62ffa9929c7b399a9bc1e07917cc58b06.novelty_claims: The proposed research offers a systematic and specialized framework for understanding and mitigating harmful fine-tuning attacks on LLMs, bridging gaps in current knowledge by unifying threat models, evaluation metrics, and defense taxonomies. Novel contributions include the development of comprehensive benchmarks, the introduction of new evaluation methodologies, and the design of advanced defense strategies that balance alignment preservation and downstream utility. The work aims to clarify misunderstandings in the community and provide actionable guidelines for both researchers and practitioners in the deployment of safe LLM fine-tuning services.

2f4c451922e227cbbd4f090b74298445bbd900d0.title: Elucidating the Design Space of Diffusion-Based Generative Models
2f4c451922e227cbbd4f090b74298445bbd900d0.research_question: What are the key independent design choices in diffusion-based generative models, and how can a modular framework be established to systematically improve image quality, training efficiency, and sampling speed across diverse model architectures and datasets?
2f4c451922e227cbbd4f090b74298445bbd900d0.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the components of diffusion-based generative models—specifically, the sampling process, training procedure, and network preconditioning—can be decoupled and optimized independently, leading to significant improvements in sample quality, efficiency, and robustness. Furthermore, it is expected that a principled analysis and redesign of these components will yield state-of-the-art performance with fewer model evaluations.
2f4c451922e227cbbd4f090b74298445bbd900d0.proposed_method: A unified and modular framework will be developed to disentangle and explicitly parameterize the design space of diffusion-based generative models. The approach will begin by reformulating both deterministic and stochastic sampling processes within a common ODE/SDE framework, enabling the use of advanced numerical solvers such as Heun’s 2nd order method for improved trade-offs between accuracy and computational cost. The sampling schedule, noise level parameterization, and step size distribution will be optimized empirically, with a focus on minimizing truncation errors and maximizing sample quality. For stochastic sampling, a Langevin-like noise injection mechanism will be incorporated, with heuristic controls to balance detail preservation and error correction. On the training side, the score-modeling neural network will be preconditioned using σ-dependent scaling and skip connections to stabilize input/output magnitudes, and a log-normal distribution over noise levels will be used to focus training on the most informative regions. Loss weighting will be derived to equalize effective training contributions across noise levels, and non-leaky data augmentation will be employed to further regularize training.
2f4c451922e227cbbd4f090b74298445bbd900d0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image generation benchmarks, including CIFAR-10 (32×32) and ImageNet-64, as well as FFHQ-64 and AFHQv2-64 for additional diversity. Both unconditional and class-conditional settings will be evaluated. Baselines will include widely used diffusion model variants such as DDPM, NCSN, and iDDPM, with original and reimplemented samplers for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics will primarily be Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), computed over 50,000 generated samples per experiment. The number of neural function evaluations (NFE) required for high-quality synthesis will be tracked, and the impact of each modular improvement (sampler, preconditioning, loss weighting, augmentation) will be assessed through ablation studies. Pre-trained models from prior work will also be tested with the new sampling and training procedures to demonstrate modularity and transferability.
2f4c451922e227cbbd4f090b74298445bbd900d0.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a modular, unified framework that explicitly separates and parameterizes the design choices in diffusion-based generative models, allowing independent optimization of sampling, training, and network preconditioning. It proposes the use of higher-order ODE solvers (e.g., Heun’s method) and empirically optimized noise schedules for more efficient and accurate sampling. A novel stochastic sampling procedure is developed that combines deterministic integration with controlled Langevin-like noise injection. The training process is improved through principled preconditioning, log-normal noise level sampling, and loss weighting, as well as the introduction of non-leaky data augmentation. The approach claims to achieve new state-of-the-art FID scores on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-64 with significantly fewer model evaluations, and to provide a foundation for more systematic and targeted exploration of the diffusion model design space.

2f62a1821bbf6b7b8dbc2a11fd3d900e5ebd5fe9.title: DCBM: Data-Efficient Visual Concept Bottleneck Models
2f62a1821bbf6b7b8dbc2a11fd3d900e5ebd5fe9.research_question: How can interpretable neural network models be designed to maintain high accuracy and adaptability in data-sparse and fine-grained classification domains, while relying exclusively on dataset-specific, visually-grounded concepts?
2f62a1821bbf6b7b8dbc2a11fd3d900e5ebd5fe9.hypothesis: Defining visual concepts as image regions extracted via segmentation or detection foundation models, and clustering these to form dataset-specific concept banks, enables interpretable and accurate classification in data-scarce and fine-grained domains, with improved adaptability and out-of-distribution generalization compared to text- or large-corpus-based concept bottleneck models.
2f62a1821bbf6b7b8dbc2a11fd3d900e5ebd5fe9.proposed_method: A novel framework, Data-Efficient Visual Concept Bottleneck Models (DCBMs), is proposed that generates visual concepts by applying segmentation and detection foundation models (such as SAM, Mask-RCNN, DETR, and GroundingDINO) to a small, randomly selected subset of training images per class. Each image yields multiple region proposals at varying granularities, which are then embedded using a frozen vision encoder (e.g., CLIP) and clustered (e.g., via K-Means) to reduce redundancy and form a set of dataset-specific concept centroids. These centroids serve as the interpretable concept bank. A sparse linear classifier (CBM) is trained to map concept activations (computed as normalized projections of image embeddings onto concept centroids) to class predictions, with L1 regularization to promote interpretability. Concept naming is performed by mapping visual concepts to the nearest textual features in a shared embedding space, allowing for human-understandable explanations. The method supports targeted removal of undesired concepts using text prompts and provides step-wise inspectability at each stage.
2f62a1821bbf6b7b8dbc2a11fd3d900e5ebd5fe9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of standard and fine-grained image classification datasets, including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet (and ImageNet-R for OOD evaluation), CUB, Places365, ImageNette, ImageWoof, AWA2, CelebA, MiT-States, and ClimateTV. Various segmentation and detection models will be compared for concept proposal generation. Baselines will include state-of-the-art CBMs leveraging text-aligned or large-scale visual concepts (e.g., DN-CBM, LF-CBM, LaBo, CDM, DCLIP), as well as linear probe and zero-shot CLIP classifiers. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy, error rate changes under domain shift (IID vs. OOD), and interpretability metrics such as the Grid Pointing Game (GPG) to assess concept localization. Hyperparameters (learning rate, sparsity, number of clusters) will be tuned on held-out validation splits. Qualitative analysis will investigate the semantic coherence and visual alignment of learned concepts, and attribution methods (e.g., Grad-CAM) will be used to visualize concept activations.
2f62a1821bbf6b7b8dbc2a11fd3d900e5ebd5fe9.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a data-efficient, visually-grounded framework for concept bottleneck models that eliminates the need for large-scale text or image corpora during concept generation. By leveraging segmentation and detection foundation models, DCBMs produce dataset-specific, multi-granularity concepts suitable for fine-grained and out-of-distribution tasks. The method enables flexible adaptation to new domains, supports targeted concept removal, and maintains interpretability through step-wise inspectability and concept naming. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate competitive accuracy with state-of-the-art CBMs, superior performance in data-scarce and fine-grained settings, and improved generalization to novel and OOD datasets.

2f6511c90bf4f50be8c9be77e754282089241bd1.title: Zero-Shot Offline Imitation Learning via Optimal Transport
2f6511c90bf4f50be8c9be77e754282089241bd1.research_question: How can zero-shot offline imitation learning be achieved from offline, potentially suboptimal, and partial expert demonstrations, without requiring action labels or precise timing, and while avoiding myopic behavior that undermines long-term objectives?
2f6511c90bf4f50be8c9be77e754282089241bd1.hypothesis: Directly optimizing an occupancy-matching objective using optimal transport between the agent's and expert's state (or goal) occupancies, approximated via a learned world model and value functions, will enable non-myopic, zero-shot imitation learning from offline, suboptimal, and partial expert data.
2f6511c90bf4f50be8c9be77e754282089241bd1.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed that formulates zero-shot offline imitation learning as an occupancy-matching problem, operationalized via optimal transport (OT) between the empirical occupancies of the agent and the expert demonstration. The method leverages a learned dynamics model (world model) and goal-conditioned value functions to approximate the agent's and expert's occupancies from offline data. The OT cost is defined using a distance metric derived from the learned value function, which proxies the expected first-hitting time between states and goals, thus incorporating the environment's dynamics. At inference, a model-predictive control (MPC) approach is used: a zero-order optimizer (e.g., CEM) plans over a finite horizon in the learned world model to minimize the OT cost between the planned trajectory and the expert demonstration, allowing for non-myopic planning. The approach supports rough, partial, and temporally imprecise expert demonstrations by relaxing the need for action labels and precise timing, and can be further extended with unbalanced OT and classifier-based goal filtering.
2f6511c90bf4f50be8c9be77e754282089241bd1.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a suite of 30 tasks across 5 continuous-control environments, including robotic manipulation (Fetch Push, Pick&Place, Slide), locomotion (HalfCheetah), and navigation (PointMaze). The method is compared against state-of-the-art zero-shot imitation learning baselines, including hierarchical goal-conditioned policies with classifiers, model-predictive planning with value functions, and forward-backward RL/IL methods (ER_FB, RER_FB). Evaluation metrics include the minimal Wasserstein-1 distance between the agent's and expert's trajectories (under the goal metric) and the fraction of goals achieved in sequence. Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of OT variants (unbalanced OT, classifier-based goal filtering, and alternative cost metrics). All methods use the same offline datasets, and the agent's world model and value functions are trained using TD-MPC2. Planning is performed in the latent space of the learned model, and experiments include both qualitative trajectory visualizations and quantitative performance metrics.
2f6511c90bf4f50be8c9be77e754282089241bd1.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a holistic, non-myopic approach to zero-shot offline imitation learning by directly optimizing an optimal transport-based occupancy-matching objective, rather than decomposing the problem into sequential goal-reaching tasks. It is the first to leverage OT between empirical occupancies in conjunction with a learned world model and goal-conditioned value functions for zero-shot imitation from rough, partial, and action-free demonstrations. The approach is robust to suboptimal and temporally imprecise expert data, supports practical relaxations such as unbalanced OT, and demonstrates superior performance over prior methods, especially in environments where myopic planning fails. The method also provides a principled way to incorporate the geometry and dynamics of the environment into the imitation learning objective.

2f8917d5bead2e011a00c33153e8deb2027756ee.title: Privacy Auditing of Large Language Models
2f8917d5bead2e011a00c33153e8deb2027756ee.research_question: How can privacy leakage in large language models (LLMs) be more accurately audited, particularly under realistic threat models and black-box access, and what methods can be developed to construct canaries that are most likely to be memorized by LLMs?
2f8917d5bead2e011a00c33153e8deb2027756ee.hypothesis: Carefully designed canaries, crafted using knowledge of data and model distributions, will significantly improve the effectiveness of privacy auditing in LLMs, enabling tighter empirical lower bounds on privacy leakage compared to random canary baselines.
2f8917d5bead2e011a00c33153e8deb2027756ee.proposed_method: A new framework is developed for privacy auditing of LLMs that focuses on constructing canaries—synthetic data points inserted into training—that are highly likely to be memorized by the model. The method systematically explores several strategies for canary generation: (1) unigram-based canaries that use rare tokens based on the training data distribution, (2) n-gram (e.g., bigram) canaries that use unlikely token pairs, (3) model-based canaries that select tokens or sequences the model itself deems improbable, and (4) new-token canaries that introduce tokens not present elsewhere in the training data. These canaries are inserted into the training data, and membership inference attacks (MIAs), specifically loss-thresholding attacks, are performed to detect memorization. The approach is compatible with both standard and differentially private (DP) training regimes, and is evaluated in a black-box setting where only the final model's log probabilities are accessible.
2f8917d5bead2e011a00c33153e8deb2027756ee.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a diverse set of LLMs, including GPT2, Pythia, Qwen-2.5, and Llama3, covering a range of vocabulary sizes and model scales. Models are fine-tuned on public datasets such as PersonaChat and E2E, with canaries inserted at a low sampling rate. The evaluation uses membership inference attacks measuring true positive rate (TPR) at a low false positive rate (FPR=1%), and privacy auditing is performed using the Steinke et al. (2023) method to obtain empirical lower bounds on epsilon (ε) for DP-trained models. Baselines include random canaries and prior canary-generation approaches. Ablation studies vary canary length, learning rate, and training objectives (supervised fine-tuning vs. next-word prediction). All experiments are conducted in a black-box setting, without access to model weights or intermediate checkpoints, and use a single-run audit protocol.
2f8917d5bead2e011a00c33153e8deb2027756ee.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a systematic approach to designing highly effective canaries for privacy auditing of LLMs, demonstrating that adversarially crafted canaries—especially those based on rare tokens, n-gram statistics, model-based rarity, or new tokens—dramatically improve the sensitivity of membership inference attacks and the tightness of empirical privacy leakage bounds. This is the first method to achieve nontrivial privacy audits (e.g., empirical ε ≈ 1 for analytical ε = 4) for LLMs in the black-box setting, without requiring shadow models, gradient access, or repeated training runs. The approach provides a new standard for privacy auditing in LLMs and reveals that prior reliance on random canaries may systematically underestimate privacy risk.

2f9bcfe03ed3c5827036e7a7e672f952e2d1a382.title: LongVideoBench: A Benchmark for Long-context Interleaved Video-Language Understanding
2f9bcfe03ed3c5827036e7a7e672f952e2d1a382.research_question: How can the long-context multimodal understanding capabilities of large multimodal models (LMMs) be effectively evaluated using video-language inputs that span up to an hour in duration, and what are the current limitations of existing models in detailed, temporally-grounded video-language reasoning tasks?
2f9bcfe03ed3c5827036e7a7e672f952e2d1a382.hypothesis: A benchmark featuring interleaved, hour-long video and subtitle inputs with carefully crafted referring reasoning questions will reveal significant performance gaps and challenges for current LMMs, especially in detailed and relational video-language understanding, and will drive measurable improvements in models capable of processing longer multimodal contexts.
2f9bcfe03ed3c5827036e7a7e672f952e2d1a382.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark, LONGVIDEOBENCH, will be constructed to evaluate LMMs on long-context video-language understanding. The benchmark will consist of 3,763 web-collected videos, each with aligned subtitles, spanning durations from 8 seconds to 60 minutes and covering diverse themes such as movies, news, daily life, and knowledge. For each video, human annotators will create multiple-choice questions that require models to answer based on specific referred contexts within the video, using a novel 'referring reasoning' task paradigm. Questions will be divided into 17 fine-grained categories across two levels: perception (single-moment understanding) and relation (multi-moment, temporal, or attribute-based reasoning). The interleaved input format will temporally align video frames and subtitle segments, requiring models to process both modalities jointly.
2f9bcfe03ed3c5827036e7a7e672f952e2d1a382.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate 22 LMMs, including both proprietary (e.g., GPT-4o, Gemini-1.5-Pro) and state-of-the-art open-source models (e.g., Idefics2, Phi-3-Vision-Instruct), as well as video-specific and image-based LMMs. The benchmark will be split into validation and test sets, with 752 videos (1,337 MCQs) for validation and 3,011 videos (5,341 MCQs) for testing. Models will be assessed on their ability to answer multiple-choice questions using interleaved video and subtitle inputs, with performance measured by accuracy across different video durations, question categories, and input modalities. Baselines will include existing video QA datasets (e.g., MSVD-QA, ActivityNet-QA), and models will be compared on their ability to scale with input length and integrate multimodal information.
2f9bcfe03ed3c5827036e7a7e672f952e2d1a382.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces the first large-scale, human-annotated, long-context video-language QA dataset with interleaved inputs up to an hour long, addressing the longstanding single-frame bias in video understanding evaluation. The referring reasoning task paradigm is novel in requiring explicit retrieval and reasoning over temporally distant, multimodal contexts. The benchmark covers a uniquely diverse set of video themes and durations, and provides detailed analysis of model performance with respect to context length, modality integration, and temporal reasoning. This resource is positioned to drive the development and evaluation of future-generation LMMs for real-world, long-form video-language understanding.

2fadd79679a2093c1690a2310269ecf6a0df86f8.title: Causal Inference Under Unmeasured Confounding With Negative Controls: A Minimax Learning Approach
2fadd79679a2093c1690a2310269ecf6a0df86f8.research_question: How can causal parameters be estimated from observational data when some confounders are unmeasured but negative control variables are available, and what identification and estimation strategies enable reliable inference in this setting?
2fadd79679a2093c1690a2310269ecf6a0df86f8.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that causal parameters can be identified and efficiently estimated under unmeasured confounding by leveraging negative control variables, without requiring strong completeness or uniqueness assumptions on bridge functions, through the use of minimax learning formulations.
2fadd79679a2093c1690a2310269ecf6a0df86f8.proposed_method: A new identification strategy will be developed that enables the estimation of causal parameters using negative control variables, requiring only the existence of certain bridge functions and not completeness conditions. The estimation of these bridge functions will be formulated as a minimax learning problem, introducing adversarial critic functions and allowing for the use of flexible function classes such as Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces (RKHS) and neural networks. The bridge functions will be estimated by solving conditional moment equations through minimax optimization, where the estimator minimizes the worst-case violation of these moments over a class of critic functions. These estimated bridge functions will then be plugged into inverse propensity weighting, regression-based, or doubly robust estimating equations to estimate the generalized average causal effect (GACE). The approach is designed to accommodate both discrete and continuous actions, and does not require the uniqueness of bridge functions except when stronger theoretical guarantees are desired.
2fadd79679a2093c1690a2310269ecf6a0df86f8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using both simulated datasets and real-world observational data, where the true causal effects and confounding structure are known or can be reasonably inferred. The proposed minimax estimators will be compared against existing parametric and nonparametric methods for negative control-based causal inference, including approaches that rely on completeness and uniqueness assumptions. Evaluation metrics will include finite-sample convergence rates, estimation bias, variance, and mean squared error of the estimated causal parameters. The experimental setup will consider various configurations of negative control variables, function class choices (e.g., RKHS, neural networks), and sample sizes to assess robustness and practical feasibility.
2fadd79679a2093c1690a2310269ecf6a0df86f8.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new identification strategy for causal inference with negative controls that avoids the need for completeness conditions on bridge functions, thus relaxing a key limitation of prior work. The minimax learning formulation for bridge function estimation is novel in this context, accommodating highly flexible function classes and allowing for nonunique bridge functions. Finite-sample convergence results are derived under a variety of assumptions, including settings where bridge functions are not consistently estimated, which is generally not possible with standard instrumental variable analyses. The methodology fully exploits the structure of double negative controls, offering practical and theoretical advances over existing literature.

2fc993c78cd84dafe4c36d2ac1cc25a6256aaa9d.title: Sample-Efficient Reinforcement Learning with loglog(T) Switching Cost
2fc993c78cd84dafe4c36d2ac1cc25a6256aaa9d.research_question: Can reinforcement learning algorithms be designed to achieve low policy switching costs while maintaining sample efficiency and near-optimal regret in episodic Markov Decision Processes with unknown transitions?
2fc993c78cd84dafe4c36d2ac1cc25a6256aaa9d.hypothesis: It is possible to construct reinforcement learning algorithms that achieve poly(H,S,A) sample efficiency and near-optimal regret while reducing the global policy switching cost to O(HSA loglog T), which is exponentially lower than previous methods.
2fc993c78cd84dafe4c36d2ac1cc25a6256aaa9d.proposed_method: A novel policy elimination framework, termed Adaptive Policy Elimination by Value Estimation (APEVE), is proposed. The approach divides the total exploration budget into a sequence of stages with geometrically increasing batch sizes, each corresponding to a fixed policy deployment. In each stage, the method performs a two-step exploration: (1) Crude Exploration, which constructs an absorbing MDP by identifying infrequent state-action-next-state tuples and estimating transitions using policies that maximize visitation of each tuple; and (2) Fine Exploration, which further refines the transition estimates using targeted policies. After each stage, policies are eliminated from the candidate set if their estimated value is statistically suboptimal, based on confidence bounds derived from the collected data. The schedule of policy switches is determined in advance, enabling parallel and distributed data collection, and ensuring that the total number of policy switches grows only as O(HSA loglog T).
2fc993c78cd84dafe4c36d2ac1cc25a6256aaa9d.experiment_details: Experiments are proposed to evaluate the regret and switching cost of the APEVE algorithm in finite-horizon episodic tabular MDPs with unknown transitions. The evaluation will compare APEVE against state-of-the-art baselines such as UCB2-Bernstein, UCB-Advantage, and other recent low-switching-cost RL algorithms. Metrics will include cumulative regret, global switching cost, and sample complexity. The experiments will use synthetic MDPs with varying numbers of states (S), actions (A), and horizon lengths (H), and will measure performance as a function of the total number of steps T. Lower bounds on switching cost and regret will be empirically validated, and reward-free exploration scenarios will also be considered using the LARFE variant.
2fc993c78cd84dafe4c36d2ac1cc25a6256aaa9d.novelty_claims: The proposed method achieves an exponential improvement in global policy switching cost, reducing it from O(H2SA log T) to O(HSA loglog T) while maintaining near-optimal regret bounds. The algorithm is the first to achieve loglog T switching cost in RL with poly(H,S,A) regret, and the lower bounds established show that this switching cost is information-theoretically optimal. The framework also extends to reward-free exploration with optimal switching cost, and introduces new technical tools for constructing and estimating absorbing MDPs with multiplicative error guarantees. The policy elimination schedule is predetermined, enabling parallelism and practical deployment in real-world RL applications where policy changes are costly.

2fd1e96f56794be12b02044f83eb2c2370c69037.title: Process Reward Model with Q-Value Rankings
2fd1e96f56794be12b02044f83eb2c2370c69037.research_question: How can process reward modeling for complex reasoning and decision-making tasks be improved to better capture the dependencies among intermediate steps and provide more accurate, theoretically grounded feedback throughout multi-step solution trajectories?
2fd1e96f56794be12b02044f83eb2c2370c69037.hypothesis: Modeling process rewards as a Q-value ranking problem within a Markov Decision Process, and optimizing with a comparative loss function that emphasizes the gap between correct and incorrect steps, will yield more accurate and generalizable process reward models than existing classification-based approaches.
2fd1e96f56794be12b02044f83eb2c2370c69037.proposed_method: A new framework for process reward modeling will be developed by formulating the problem as a Q-value ranking task grounded in a Markov Decision Process (MDP). For each state-action pair in a reasoning trajectory, a Q-value function will be defined to represent the probability of ultimately achieving a correct final answer. The method will derive optimal Q-value rankings among intermediate steps, showing that Q-values should ascend with correct steps and descend with incorrect steps, maintaining a significant gap between the two.
