To train the model, a novel comparative loss function will be introduced, incorporating a margin hyperparameter to emphasize the Q-value gap between correct and incorrect steps, while focusing on the relative rankings among correct steps. The approach will be implemented by adding a value head to a large language model (LLM) backbone, projecting latent representations to scalar Q-values for each step.
2fd1e96f56794be12b02044f83eb2c2370c69037.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multi-step reasoning benchmarks, including the MATH500 and GSM-Plus datasets, using 128 sampled solutions per question from three policy models: MetaMath-Mistral-7B, MuggleMath-13B, and Llama-3-70B-Instruct. The proposed method will be compared against outcome reward models (ORM), classification-based process reward models using binary cross-entropy (BCE) loss, and mean squared error (MSE) loss with both 0-1 and Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) labels. Evaluation will use the best-of-n (BON@n) metric, measuring the correctness of the most preferred trajectory selected by the process reward model from n candidates. Additional ablation studies will examine the impact of the margin hyperparameter, loss function design, and model backbone, and empirical validation will be performed for theoretical assumptions using sampled trajectories.
2fd1e96f56794be12b02044f83eb2c2370c69037.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a theoretically grounded process reward modeling framework by casting it as a Q-value ranking problem within an MDP, which generalizes and subsumes prior classification-based methods. The comparative loss function is specifically designed to capture pronounced Q-value gaps between correct and incorrect steps, addressing limitations of standard ranking losses and classification objectives. The method provides a more granular and accurate evaluation of intermediate steps, leading to significant improvements in verification accuracy and generalizability across datasets, sampling policies, and LLM backbones. Extensive ablation and empirical validation support the theoretical claims and practical efficacy of the approach.

2fec2120ecf71834513ebda481e9abebb382d5e5.title: Adapting the Linearised Laplace Model Evidence for Modern Deep Learning
2fec2120ecf71834513ebda481e9abebb382d5e5.research_question: How can the classical linearised Laplace method for model uncertainty estimation and model evidence maximisation be effectively adapted to modern deep learning architectures and training practices, particularly in the presence of stochastic optimisation and normalisation layers?
2fec2120ecf71834513ebda481e9abebb382d5e5.hypothesis: Adapting the linearised Laplace method by (1) optimising the model evidence with respect to the linearised model's loss rather than the original neural network's loss, and (2) independently parametrising regularisers for each group of normalised parameters, will yield more reliable uncertainty estimates and improved model selection performance in modern neural networks.
2fec2120ecf71834513ebda481e9abebb382d5e5.proposed_method: The proposed approach involves linearising the neural network around the parameters obtained from standard (possibly stochastic or incomplete) optimisation, constructing a feature expansion based on the Jacobian at this point. Instead of using the original neural network loss, the method minimises the loss for the linearised model, which is convex, to find an optimal set of linear model weights and regularisation hyperparameters via evidence maximisation. For networks with normalisation layers, the method introduces independent regularisers for each group of normalised parameters, ensuring that the predictive posterior is invariant to the scale of these parameters. The curvature (Hessian) is evaluated at the linearisation point to avoid expensive recomputation, and the model evidence is maximised with respect to both weights and regularisation parameters, iterating until convergence.
2fec2120ecf71834513ebda481e9abebb382d5e5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of neural network architectures, including MLPs, classic CNNs, residual networks with and without normalisation layers (such as batch norm and FixUp), generative autoencoders (U-Nets), and transformers. Datasets will include MNIST, CIFAR-10, and point cloud variants, as well as tomographic reconstruction tasks. Baselines will include naive implementations of the linearised Laplace method and standard model selection techniques such as cross-validation. Evaluation metrics will focus on negative log-likelihood (NLL) for uncertainty calibration and Wasserstein distance between predictive posteriors. Both small-scale (tractable Hessian computation) and large-scale (using KFAC Hessian approximations) settings will be tested, with results averaged over multiple random seeds.
2fec2120ecf71834513ebda481e9abebb382d5e5.novelty_claims: The proposed method identifies and addresses two key incompatibilities between the classical linearised Laplace method and modern deep learning: (1) the lack of convergence to a true loss minimum in stochastic training, and (2) the invariance introduced by normalisation layers. The approach introduces a theoretically justified, scalable procedure for adapting model evidence maximisation to the linearised model's loss and for independently regularising normalised parameter groups. These adaptations yield improved uncertainty estimates and model selection performance across a wide range of modern architectures and tasks, as validated both theoretically and empirically.

3021fa7790631e11e888315d387c0a442ef82ab6.title: UTMOS: UTokyo-SaruLab System for VoiceMOS Challenge 2022
3021fa7790631e11e888315d387c0a442ef82ab6.research_question: How can the accuracy and generalizability of automatic mean opinion score (MOS) prediction for synthetic speech be improved across both in-domain and out-of-domain conditions, especially when labeled data is limited?
3021fa7790631e11e888315d387c0a442ef82ab6.hypothesis: Integrating ensemble learning with advanced self-supervised learning models, contrastive learning, listener and domain-dependent modeling, phoneme encoding, and data augmentation will significantly enhance MOS prediction performance and robustness, particularly in low-resource and out-of-domain scenarios.
3021fa7790631e11e888315d387c0a442ef82ab6.proposed_method: A comprehensive MOS prediction system will be developed based on ensemble learning, combining strong learners—fine-tuned self-supervised learning (SSL) neural networks—and weak learners—regression models using SSL-derived features. The strong learner architecture will utilize raw speech waveforms as input, extracting frame-level features via pretrained SSL models (e.g., wav2vec2.0), followed by BLSTM and linear layers to predict frame-level MOS scores. The model will incorporate contrastive loss to leverage unlabeled data by optimizing the ranking of utterances based on MOS differences, and will include listener and domain ID embeddings to enable listener- and test-dependent predictions. Phoneme encoding will be introduced by feeding ASR-derived phoneme and reference sequences into a dedicated BLSTM encoder, capturing linguistic content and intelligibility cues. Data augmentation techniques such as speaking-rate modification and pitch-shifting will be employed to mitigate overfitting, especially in low-data regimes. For weak learners, mean embeddings from various SSL models will be used as features for simple regression models (e.g., ridge regression, SVMs, decision trees), and ensemble stacking will combine outputs from both strong and weak learners for final prediction.
3021fa7790631e11e888315d387c0a442ef82ab6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the VoiceMOS Challenge 2022 datasets, which include synthetic speech samples and MOS ratings from past Blizzard and Voice Conversion Challenges, divided into a main (in-domain, English) track and an out-of-domain (OOD, Chinese) track. The main track uses the BVCC dataset, while the OOD track includes both labeled and unlabeled data, with additional MOS labels collected for external data. Evaluation metrics will include mean squared error (MSE), linear correlation coefficient (LCC), Spearman rank correlation coefficient (SRCC), and Kendall tau (KTAU), calculated at both utterance and system levels. Baselines will include previous SSL-MOS models and other challenge participants. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of each proposed component (contrastive loss, listener/domain embedding, phoneme encoder, data augmentation, and external data usage). Hyperparameter tuning and model selection will be conducted using development sets and cross-validation, and ensemble diversity will be ensured by varying SSL model types, domains, and regression methods.
3021fa7790631e11e888315d387c0a442ef82ab6.novelty_claims: The proposed system introduces a novel ensemble framework that integrates strong SSL-based neural predictors with diverse weak regression models, leveraging both labeled and unlabeled data through contrastive learning. Listener- and domain-dependent modeling is explicitly incorporated via embedding layers, and phoneme encoding is used to capture linguistic and intelligibility information without requiring reference transcripts. The approach also systematically utilizes data augmentation and external MOS collection to address data scarcity in OOD scenarios. Extensive ablation and stacking studies are planned to demonstrate the effectiveness and complementarity of these innovations, aiming for state-of-the-art performance in MOS prediction under both in-domain and out-of-domain conditions.

302c993d9e34bd3c6eb641346d553901993c0c1c.title: Tight Bounds for Answering Adaptively Chosen Concentrated Queries
302c993d9e34bd3c6eb641346d553901993c0c1c.research_question: What are the fundamental limits and optimal algorithms for accurately answering a maximal number of adaptively chosen concentrated queries when the underlying data distribution may exhibit arbitrary correlations, and what structural or algorithmic conditions are necessary to surpass current query limits?
302c993d9e34bd3c6eb641346d553901993c0c1c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that under the current concentrated queries framework and natural algorithmic conditions, no efficient mechanism based on noise addition or subsampling can accurately answer more than a linear number of adaptively chosen concentrated queries, even when query concentration matches that of the i.i.d. case. Furthermore, it is hypothesized that a noise addition mechanism calibrated via differential privacy can match this upper bound with a simpler analysis.
302c993d9e34bd3c6eb641346d553901993c0c1c.proposed_method: The proposed research will rigorously analyze the theoretical limitations of mechanisms for answering adaptively chosen concentrated queries in the presence of data correlations. The approach will focus on two classes of mechanisms: (1) noise-addition mechanisms, which answer each query by adding independent noise to the empirical mean, and (2) subsampling mechanisms, which answer queries using the empirical mean over a randomly drawn subsample. An impossibility result will be established by constructing a correlated data distribution and an adaptive analyst strategy that forces any such mechanism to fail after a linear number of queries, even when each query is (ε,γ)-concentrated. Additionally, a positive result will be developed by analyzing a noise addition mechanism using tools from differential privacy, demonstrating that, with appropriately calibrated noise, statistical accuracy can be guaranteed for up to O(n) concentrated queries. The analysis will leverage advanced composition theorems and a hybrid mechanism argument to tightly bound the number of answerable queries.
302c993d9e34bd3c6eb641346d553901993c0c1c.experiment_details: Theoretical experiments will be conducted via adversarial constructions and proof techniques. The negative result will be demonstrated by designing a distribution over datasets and an adaptive querying strategy that exploits correlations to extract information, thereby forcing failure of any noise-addition or subsampling mechanism after O(n) queries. The positive result will be validated by analyzing the statistical accuracy of a Laplace mechanism under the concentrated queries setting, using parameters ε and γ comparable to those in the i.i.d. case. Evaluation metrics include the number of queries answered accurately (k), the statistical accuracy parameters (α, β), and the concentration parameters (ε, γ). Baselines for comparison include the known O(n^2) query bounds in the i.i.d. setting and prior typical stability and compression-based approaches.
302c993d9e34bd3c6eb641346d553901993c0c1c.novelty_claims: The proposal establishes the first tight impossibility bound for answering adaptively chosen concentrated queries under correlated data using all known efficient mechanisms (noise addition and subsampling), showing that the linear barrier is inherent under current assumptions. It also introduces a significantly simplified and sharper analysis for the best-known positive result, leveraging differential privacy rather than typical stability, and saving logarithmic factors in the bounds. The work provides a clear characterization of the gap between the i.i.d. and correlated settings and identifies the necessity of new structural or algorithmic ideas to surpass the linear query barrier.

303b4ae0e53cca8d007076778e5c17e28116ff7e.title: Learning to Decode Collaboratively with Multiple Language Models
303b4ae0e53cca8d007076778e5c17e28116ff7e.research_question: How can multiple large language models be trained to collaborate effectively at the token level during decoding, in order to leverage their complementary expertise and improve performance across a variety of tasks and domains?
303b4ae0e53cca8d007076778e5c17e28116ff7e.hypothesis: Collaborative token-level decoding between a base language model and one or more assistant models, with the decision of which model generates each token modeled as a latent variable and learned from data without direct supervision, will result in improved performance over using individual models alone, especially in cross-domain and cross-scale settings.
303b4ae0e53cca8d007076778e5c17e28116ff7e.proposed_method: A latent variable framework is developed in which a base language model is fine-tuned to decide, at each token generation step, whether to generate the next token itself or defer to an assistant model. The decision is modeled as a discrete latent variable, and the joint likelihood of the output sequence and model selection decisions is optimized via marginal likelihood training. The base model is augmented with a lightweight classification head to predict the probability of deferral at each step, using the base model's hidden state as input. During training, weak supervision is used to initialize the deferral parameters, but the model is ultimately trained in an unsupervised manner to allow organic learning of collaboration patterns. At inference, a threshold on the deferral probability controls when the assistant model is invoked, enabling flexible trade-offs between efficiency and performance.
303b4ae0e53cca8d007076778e5c17e28116ff7e.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a range of tasks, including instruction following (Tülu v2), mathematical reasoning (GSM8k, MATH), and medical question answering (BioASQ), using both generalist and domain-specific models (e.g., LLAMA-7B, LLAMA-70B, LLEMMA-34B, MEDITRON-70B). Baselines include individual fine-tuned models, contrastive decoding, proxy tuning, and ablated collaboration strategies (random and greedy switching, weak supervision). Evaluation metrics include win rate (AlpacaEval), exact match, accuracy, F1, and Rouge-2, with experiments comparing the proposed collaborative method to baselines on both in-domain and cross-domain tasks. The experimental setup also includes varying the frequency of deferral to analyze the trade-off between model collaboration and performance, and qualitative analyses are performed to interpret learned collaboration patterns.
303b4ae0e53cca8d007076778e5c17e28116ff7e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a flexible, interpretable, and unsupervised token-level collaboration mechanism for large language models, enabling modular composition of generalist and specialist models without requiring gradient access to assistants or restrictive architectural assumptions. The method allows for dynamic, data-driven learning of when to defer to assistant models, supports collaboration across different domains, model scales, and architectures, and achieves superior or comparable performance to state-of-the-art baselines while requiring fewer calls to large models during inference. The latent variable formulation also provides inference-time control over collaboration frequency, offering practical efficiency-performance trade-offs.

305941292b59d808af1f6646993747ba0f76f4ac.title: GOOD-D: On Unsupervised Graph Out-Of-Distribution Detection
305941292b59d808af1f6646993747ba0f76f4ac.research_question: Can out-of-distribution (OOD) graphs be effectively detected in an unsupervised manner using only unlabeled in-distribution (ID) graph data, without relying on ground-truth labels or supervised signals?
305941292b59d808af1f6646993747ba0f76f4ac.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a hierarchical graph contrastive learning framework, leveraging perturbation-free data augmentation and multi-level semantic agreement, can capture the latent patterns of ID graphs and accurately detect OOD graphs solely from unlabeled ID data.
305941292b59d808af1f6646993747ba0f76f4ac.proposed_method: A novel framework, termed GOOD-D, is proposed for unsupervised graph-level OOD detection. The method begins by generating two distinct graph views for each input: a feature view (using original node features) and a structure view (using pre-computed structural encodings that combine global random walk-based and local degree-based information). These views are processed by independent GNN encoders to produce node and graph embeddings. Hierarchical contrastive learning is performed at node, graph, and group (cluster) levels, maximizing agreement between the two views at each granularity. Group-level contrast is implemented by clustering graph embeddings and contrasting samples with their assigned prototypes. An adaptive loss and scoring mechanism is introduced, balancing the contributions of each level based on the variability of their errors, to robustly aggregate multi-level OOD scores.
305941292b59d808af1f6646993747ba0f76f4ac.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a comprehensive benchmark comprising 10 pairs of graph datasets from domains such as molecular chemistry, bioinformatics, and social networks. For each pair, one dataset serves as ID and the other as OOD; 90% of ID samples are used for training, with the remaining 10% and an equal number of OOD samples for testing. The evaluation metric is the Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC). Baselines include graph kernel methods with various detectors, state-of-the-art graph contrastive learning (GCL) methods with standard OOD detectors, and recent end-to-end graph anomaly detection models. Extensive ablation studies are performed to assess the contribution of each hierarchical contrastive component and the adaptive mechanism. Hyperparameters such as cluster number and adaptiveness strength are systematically varied to evaluate robustness.
305941292b59d808af1f6646993747ba0f76f4ac.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first unsupervised graph-level OOD detection framework that employs perturbation-free data augmentation, avoiding the risk of generating artificial OOD samples during augmentation. It pioneers hierarchical contrastive learning at node, graph, and group levels for OOD detection, rather than focusing solely on instance-level contrast. The adaptive training and scoring mechanism further distinguishes the approach by automatically balancing multi-level contributions, leading to superior and robust OOD detection performance across diverse real-world graph datasets.

30864e48dce502a69e05b51f5d624d2c0f5d3477.title: From Knowledge Distillation to Self-Knowledge Distillation: A Unified Approach with Normalized Loss and Customized Soft Labels
30864e48dce502a69e05b51f5d624d2c0f5d3477.research_question: How can the utilization of soft labels in both knowledge distillation (KD) and self-knowledge distillation (self-KD) be improved to enhance the performance of student models across diverse neural network architectures, including CNNs and Vision Transformers (ViTs)?
30864e48dce502a69e05b51f5d624d2c0f5d3477.hypothesis: Normalizing the non-target logits in the distillation loss and generating customized soft labels for both target and non-target classes will improve the effectiveness of knowledge transfer in both KD and self-KD, leading to superior student model performance with minimal computational overhead.
30864e48dce502a69e05b51f5d624d2c0f5d3477.proposed_method: A unified framework is developed that decomposes the standard KD loss into a normalized KD (NKD) loss and introduces customized soft labels for both target and non-target classes. For KD with a teacher, the NKD loss normalizes the non-target logits to ensure their sum is equalized between teacher and student, thereby improving the alignment of their output distributions. For self-KD, a Universal Self-Knowledge Distillation (USKD) method is proposed, where soft target labels are generated by smoothing and squaring the student’s own target logits, and soft non-target labels are derived by ranking intermediate features (using a weakly supervised linear layer) and applying Zipf’s law to assign label values. The approach is designed to be broadly applicable to both CNN and ViT architectures, requiring only a minor addition (an extra linear layer) for weak supervision in self-KD.
30864e48dce502a69e05b51f5d624d2c0f5d3477.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet datasets for both KD and self-KD scenarios. For KD, various teacher-student pairs are used, including homogeneous (e.g., ResNet34-ResNet18) and heterogeneous (e.g., ResNet50-MobileNet) architectures. Baselines include standard KD, DKD, and other state-of-the-art logit- and feature-based distillation methods. Evaluation metrics are Top-1 and Top-5 accuracy. For self-KD, the method is compared against label smoothing, Tf-KD, and Zipf’s LS, with experiments extended to lightweight and deep models (e.g., MobileNetV2, ShuffleNetV2, ResNet-101) and ViT-like models (e.g., DeiT, Swin-Transformer, RegNet). Additional experiments measure training time overhead and test generalization to object detection on COCO using Mask-RCNN. Ablation studies analyze the impact of target and non-target loss components, smoothing strategies for soft targets, and ranking strategies for soft non-targets.
30864e48dce502a69e05b51f5d624d2c0f5d3477.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple yet effective normalization of non-target logits in the KD loss, resulting in improved knowledge transfer and state-of-the-art performance. A novel approach for generating customized soft labels for both target and non-target classes in self-KD is developed, enabling effective self-distillation without a teacher and with negligible computational cost. The USKD method is the first to provide a general self-KD solution applicable to both CNNs and ViTs, overcoming limitations of prior methods that were architecture-specific or resource-intensive. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent accuracy gains and improved generalization to downstream tasks such as object detection.

30a7390ec0103684eba9fb6bde1983d706fb57b3.title: Optimal Brain Compression: A Framework for Accurate Post-Training Quantization and Pruning
30a7390ec0103684eba9fb6bde1983d706fb57b3.research_question: How can deep neural networks be efficiently and accurately compressed in the post-training setting, using only a small amount of calibration data and without any retraining, by unifying pruning and quantization in a single framework?
30a7390ec0103684eba9fb6bde1983d706fb57b3.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a unified, layer-wise, second-order optimization framework can enable highly accurate post-training compression of deep neural networks through both pruning and quantization, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy-compression trade-offs without retraining.
30a7390ec0103684eba9fb6bde1983d706fb57b3.proposed_method: A unified framework, termed the Optimal Brain Compressor (OBC), will be developed to address both weight pruning and quantization in the post-training setting. The method will begin by formulating the global compression task as a set of independent layer-wise sub-problems, each seeking to minimize the squared error between the original and compressed layer outputs given a small calibration dataset. The approach will leverage an exact, efficient realization of the Optimal Brain Surgeon (OBS) framework, extended to handle both pruning and quantization, and will introduce algorithmic innovations to reduce the computational complexity from O(d^4) to O(d_row * d_col^3) per layer, where d_row and d_col are the dimensions of the weight matrix. For pruning, the method will iteratively remove weights one at a time, updating the remaining weights using second-order information. For quantization, a new algorithm, the Optimal Brain Quantizer (OBQ), will be introduced to iteratively quantize weights based on their impact on loss, with closed-form updates to the remaining weights after each quantization step. The framework will support various sparsity patterns, including unstructured, N:M, and block sparsity, and will be implemented for efficient execution on modern hardware.
30a7390ec0103684eba9fb6bde1983d706fb57b3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard deep learning tasks and models, including image classification (ResNet on ImageNet), object detection (YOLOv5 on COCO), and language modeling (BERT on SQuAD). The evaluation will cover multiple compression scenarios: unstructured pruning, semi-structured N:M pruning, uniform and mixed-precision quantization, and joint pruning-quantization for both GPU and CPU inference. Baselines will include state-of-the-art post-training compression methods such as Global Magnitude Pruning, L-OBS, AdaPrune, AdaRound, AdaQuant, and BRECQ. Calibration datasets will consist of 1024 samples, with data augmentation applied where appropriate. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy (for classification), mean average precision (for detection), and F1 score (for language tasks), as well as FLOP reduction, BOP reduction, and actual inference speedup. Layer-wise and global compression targets will be optimized using dynamic programming based on calibration loss and hardware-specific constraints.
30a7390ec0103684eba9fb6bde1983d706fb57b3.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to provide an exact, efficient, and unified solution for both pruning and quantization in the post-training setting, leveraging second-order information without requiring retraining. The method introduces algorithmic advances that make the exact OBS approach tractable for modern DNNs, including efficient per-layer and per-row computations and support for a wide range of sparsity patterns. The approach enables accurate compound application of pruning and quantization, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy-compression trade-offs and demonstrating, for the first time, that post-training compression can be competitive with retraining-based methods. The framework is extensible to structured pruning and compatible with further compression techniques.

30bd5f9f96e262f0557fe889113f49a8bbdd8f55.title: SoK: Certified Robustness for Deep Neural Networks
30bd5f9f96e262f0557fe889113f49a8bbdd8f55.research_question: How can a comprehensive taxonomy and benchmarking framework be developed to systematically evaluate and compare certifiably robust approaches for deep neural networks (DNNs) against adversarial attacks, and what are the fundamental trade-offs, limitations, and future directions in certified robustness for DNNs?
30bd5f9f96e262f0557fe889113f49a8bbdd8f55.hypothesis: A unified taxonomy and benchmarking platform for certifiably robust approaches will enable more effective quantitative comparison, reveal key strengths and limitations, and facilitate the development of more scalable and tighter robustness verification and training methods for DNNs.
30bd5f9f96e262f0557fe889113f49a8bbdd8f55.proposed_method: A systematic taxonomy will be constructed to categorize certifiably robust approaches for DNNs, including both robustness verification and robust training methods. The taxonomy will distinguish between complete and incomplete verification, deterministic and probabilistic methods, and further subdivide by system model and core methodology (e.g., solver-based, relaxation-based, Lipschitz-based, etc.). A unified open-source evaluation toolbox will be developed to implement and standardize over 20 representative verification and training approaches. This toolbox will allow for consistent benchmarking across multiple datasets and model architectures, supporting various threat models (e.g., different lp-norm bounded adversaries). The framework will also include detailed analysis modules to assess scalability, tightness of certification, and practical deployment considerations.
30bd5f9f96e262f0557fe889113f49a8bbdd8f55.experiment_details: Experiments will involve benchmarking more than 20 state-of-the-art verification and robust training approaches on a range of datasets, including MNIST, CIFAR-10, Tiny ImageNet, and ImageNet, covering models of varying size and complexity. The evaluation will compare approaches based on scalability (e.g., maximum model size and dataset handled), tightness of certified robustness bounds, and computational complexity. Baselines will include both complete (e.g., SMT/MILP/branch-and-bound) and incomplete (e.g., IBP, polyhedra, zonotope, Lipschitz) verification methods, as well as robust training strategies (e.g., regularization-based, relaxation-based, augmentation-based). Evaluation metrics will include certified robustness radius, running time, and success rate of certification. The benchmarking platform will generate leaderboards and practical deployment guidelines based on these results.
30bd5f9f96e262f0557fe889113f49a8bbdd8f55.novelty_claims: The proposed research will deliver the first comprehensive taxonomy and large-scale benchmark specifically focused on certifiably robust approaches for DNNs, enabling standardized quantitative comparison across a wide range of verification and training methods. The unified open-source toolbox will facilitate reproducible research and practical deployment by providing reference implementations and evaluation protocols. The work will also reveal fundamental trade-offs between scalability and tightness in robustness verification, identify theoretical barriers, and outline promising future research directions for certified robustness in deep learning.

30cfdd0a02098c3589f6221e3af2c29fd335966d.title: Long-Context Linear System Identification
30cfdd0a02098c3589f6221e3af2c29fd335966d.research_question: How can the parameters of long-context linear dynamical systems, where the current state depends linearly on a window of previous states, be efficiently and accurately identified from observed trajectories? What are the statistical and computational implications of low-rank structure and context length misspecification in such models?
30cfdd0a02098c3589f6221e3af2c29fd335966d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that long-context linear system identification can achieve statistical rates comparable to the i.i.d. parametric rate, up to logarithmic factors, even in the presence of long context windows and without reliance on mixing properties. Furthermore, incorporating low-rank assumptions and allowing for context length misspecification can improve sample complexity and learning efficiency under certain stability conditions.
30cfdd0a02098c3589f6221e3af2c29fd335966d.proposed_method: A constrained least squares framework is developed for estimating the transition matrices of long-context linear autoregressive models, where the state at time t is modeled as a linear function of the previous p states plus noise. The estimation is performed by minimizing the empirical squared loss over a convex set of matrices with bounded operator norm, ensuring stability and tractability. For systems with potential low-rank structure, a rank-regularized estimator is proposed, either by imposing explicit rank constraints or by utilizing nuclear norm regularization as a convex relaxation. In the case of misspecified context length, the method restricts the estimator to use a shorter context window, with appropriate adjustments to the constraint set to ensure identifiability of the leading transition matrices. Theoretical analysis leverages empirical process theory and uniform concentration arguments to establish non-asymptotic statistical rates for the proposed estimators.
30cfdd0a02098c3589f6221e3af2c29fd335966d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic datasets generated from long-context linear autoregressive processes with varying dimensions (d), context lengths (p), and sample sizes (N, T). Both full-rank and low-rank settings will be evaluated, with the latter incorporating shared low-dimensional representations across transition matrices. Baselines will include standard OLS estimators and methods adapted from first-order system identification. Evaluation metrics will focus on the Frobenius norm error between estimated and true transition matrices, as well as the scaling of sample complexity with respect to problem parameters. Additional experiments will test the impact of context length misspecification and verify the predicted scaling laws for statistical rates. All experimental setups will ensure sub-Gaussian noise and operator norm boundedness as per the theoretical assumptions.
30cfdd0a02098c3589f6221e3af2c29fd335966d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach establishes, for the first time, non-asymptotic statistical rates for long-context linear system identification that match the i.i.d. parametric rate up to logarithmic factors, independent of the mixing time of the underlying process. A 'learning-without-mixing' phenomenon is demonstrated, showing that slow mixing does not degrade learning rates for these models. The method extends to low-rank settings, providing improved sample complexity under rank constraints, and rigorously analyzes the effect of context length misspecification, revealing that shorter contexts can offer statistical advantages in strictly stable systems. These contributions fill a significant gap in the theory of linear system identification for higher-order dependencies and provide practical guidelines for learning in high-dimensional, long-memory dynamical systems.

30e10edf8f4916c8b3ca04a43f7ec62d44b05b5d.title: Jump Your Steps: Optimizing Sampling Schedule of Discrete Diffusion Models
30e10edf8f4916c8b3ca04a43f7ec62d44b05b5d.research_question: How can the sampling schedule in discrete diffusion models be optimized to improve sampling quality and speed across various domains, while minimizing errors introduced by parallel sampling methods?
30e10edf8f4916c8b3ca04a43f7ec62d44b05b5d.hypothesis: Optimizing the allocation of discrete sampling timesteps by minimizing compounding decoding error (CDE) will significantly improve the sampling quality and efficiency of discrete diffusion models, without incurring additional computational costs or requiring changes to model architecture.
30e10edf8f4916c8b3ca04a43f7ec62d44b05b5d.proposed_method: A novel approach, termed Jump Your Steps (JYS), will be developed to optimize the allocation of discrete sampling timesteps in discrete diffusion models. The method will introduce a rigorous measure of Compounding Decoding Error (CDE) and derive a practical, efficiently computable upper bound on CDE using tools such as Girsanov’s theorem for continuous-time Markov chains (CTMCs). The optimization objective will be to minimize this upper bound (KLUB) over the sampling schedule, using a hierarchical breakdown strategy to iteratively refine timestep selection. Efficient computational techniques, including closed-form expectations and golden section search, will be employed to ensure tractable optimization and scalability to large state spaces. The approach will be designed to require no additional model training, architectural changes, or extra corrector steps.
30e10edf8f4916c8b3ca04a43f7ec62d44b05b5d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of domains, including synthetic sequential data (Countdown dataset), image generation (CIFAR-10), music generation (Lakh Pianoroll), and text modeling (OpenWebText with GPT-2 tokenizer). Pretrained discrete diffusion models with various transition kernels (uniform, Gaussian, absorbing) and parameterizations (denoising, score-based) will be used. The proposed JYS sampling schedule will be compared to uniform scheduling and, where applicable, to other fast sampling baselines such as τ-leaping and k-Gillespie. Evaluation metrics will include FID score for images, Hellinger distance for music, generative perplexity for text, and rule violation rates for synthetic data. Experiments will systematically vary the number of function evaluations (NFE) to assess the trade-off between speed and quality, and will include both unconditional and conditional generation tasks.
30e10edf8f4916c8b3ca04a43f7ec62d44b05b5d.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a theoretically grounded and computationally efficient framework for optimizing sampling schedules in discrete diffusion models by directly minimizing an upper bound on compounding decoding error. Unlike prior approaches, this method does not require additional corrector steps, specialized architectures, or increased computational budgets. The approach is generalizable across different data modalities, transition kernels, and model parameterizations, and provides a practical algorithm for schedule optimization that adapts to the underlying data distribution and token dependencies. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate significant improvements in sampling quality and efficiency, establishing the method as a versatile tool for accelerating discrete diffusion model sampling.

30eb58d687f841eaa09faa947f50b82aa79e4c32.title: Pro3D-Editor : A Progressive-Views Perspective for Consistent and Precise 3D Editing
30eb58d687f841eaa09faa947f50b82aa79e4c32.research_question: How can text-guided 3D editing be achieved with high consistency and precision across multiple views, ensuring accurate local modifications while avoiding spatial conflicts and fragmentation in the edited 3D objects?
30eb58d687f841eaa09faa947f50b82aa79e4c32.hypothesis: A progressive-views paradigm that dynamically identifies and edits the most salient view first, then propagates semantic edits to other views using disentangled feature correspondences, will yield more consistent and precise 3D editing results than existing view-indiscriminate approaches.
30eb58d687f841eaa09faa947f50b82aa79e4c32.proposed_method: A novel framework, Pro3D-Editor, is developed to address multi-view consistency and precision in text-guided 3D editing. The method comprises three main modules: (1) Primary-view Sampler, which dynamically selects and edits the most editing-salient view based on a scoring function that considers alignment with the editing prompt and penalizes missing or sparse views; (2) Key-view Render, which propagates editing semantics from the primary view to other key views using a Mixture-of-View-Experts Low-Rank Adaptation (MoVE-LoRA) mechanism that decouples feature correspondences and blocks reverse learning to avoid conflicts; (3) Full-view Refiner, which fuses edited key multi-views to iteratively repair and refine the 3D object, mitigating fragmentation and ensuring structural coherence. The pipeline includes a two-stage inference strategy to further enhance feature consistency, using editing masks to guide a second round of multi-view generation.
30eb58d687f841eaa09faa947f50b82aa79e4c32.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a 3D dataset containing 6 objects and 15 editing prompts, with each edited object rendered from 72 viewpoints at 5° intervals to comprehensively evaluate spatial consistency. Baselines for comparison include state-of-the-art methods such as MVEdit, 3D-Adapter, Tailor3D, and LGM. Evaluation metrics will encompass both editing quality (FID, PSNR, LPIPS, FVD, and GPTEval3D texture details) and editing accuracy (CLIP-T, DINO-I, GPTEval3D 3D plausibility, and text-asset alignment). Ablation studies will assess the contribution of each module (Primary-view Sampler, MoVE-LoRA, Full-view Refiner) to overall performance. The full editing pipeline will be trained on an A100 GPU, with detailed hyperparameters specified for each module.
30eb58d687f841eaa09faa947f50b82aa79e4c32.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a progressive-views paradigm for 3D editing, propagating semantic edits from salient to sparse views to ensure spatial consistency and avoid conflicts. The MoVE-LoRA mechanism is designed to decouple feature correspondences among views, enabling precise local editing and preventing entanglement. The Full-view Refiner module addresses fragmentation by integrating information from multiple edited views to repair and refine the 3D object. The approach claims significant improvements in editing quality and accuracy over existing methods, as demonstrated by both quantitative metrics and user preference evaluations.

30f9b1fd46e9192b41d2b0d877e06688d0b2e9b5.title: Multiple Instance Learning Framework with Masked Hard Instance Mining for Whole Slide Image Classification
30f9b1fd46e9192b41d2b0d877e06688d0b2e9b5.research_question: How can whole slide image (WSI) classification be improved by addressing the limitations of current multiple instance learning (MIL) frameworks, particularly the tendency to focus on easy-to-classify (salient) instances while neglecting hard-to-classify instances?
30f9b1fd46e9192b41d2b0d877e06688d0b2e9b5.hypothesis: Incorporating a masked hard instance mining strategy within a MIL framework, which emphasizes hard-to-classify instances during training, will improve the discriminative ability and generalization performance of WSI classification models compared to methods that focus primarily on salient instances.
30f9b1fd46e9192b41d2b0d877e06688d0b2e9b5.proposed_method: A novel MIL framework is proposed that employs masked hard instance mining (MHIM-MIL) using a Siamese (Teacher-Student) architecture. The method utilizes a momentum teacher network to compute attention scores for all instances (patches) in a WSI. Instances with the highest attention scores (i.e., easy instances) are masked out using several hybrid masking strategies, such as High Attention Masking (HAM), Random Masking, and Low Attention Masking, to indirectly mine and retain hard instances for training. The student model, which can be any attention-based MIL model, is trained on the remaining (hard) instances, while a consistency loss constrains the outputs of the teacher and student to encourage stable learning. The teacher network is updated via an exponential moving average (EMA) of the student’s parameters, enabling iterative and stable hard instance mining.
30f9b1fd46e9192b41d2b0d877e06688d0b2e9b5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two benchmark WSI datasets: CAMELYON-16 (breast cancer metastasis detection) and TCGA Lung Cancer (LUAD and LUSC subtypes). Standard data splits and cross-validation protocols will be followed, including 3-times 3-fold cross-validation for CAMELYON-16 and 4-fold cross-validation for TCGA. The proposed framework will be evaluated using accuracy, area under the curve (AUC), and F1-score, with AUC as the primary metric. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art attention-based MIL methods (AB-MIL, DSMIL, CLAM-SB, CLAM-MB, TransMIL, DTFD-MIL) as well as traditional pooling operations (max-pooling, mean-pooling). Computational cost (training time, memory usage, parameter count) will also be measured. Ablation studies will investigate the impact of different masking strategies, the Siamese structure, consistency loss, and teacher update mechanisms.
30f9b1fd46e9192b41d2b0d877e06688d0b2e9b5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a simple yet effective masked hard instance mining strategy for MIL-based WSI classification, enabling indirect mining of hard instances without requiring instance-level supervision. The use of a momentum teacher in a Siamese architecture, combined with hybrid masking strategies and a consistency loss, provides stable and efficient training with minimal additional computational cost. This framework is generalizable to various attention-based MIL models and demonstrates superior performance and efficiency over existing methods, particularly by improving generalization and discriminative boundaries in WSI classification.

311e87c7c0c59bf5c03efa5a01df3e8bd2122edb.title: Scaling Opponent Shaping to High Dimensional Games
311e87c7c0c59bf5c03efa5a01df3e8bd2122edb.research_question: How can opponent shaping methods be effectively scaled to high-dimensional, temporally-extended general-sum games, and what are the necessary architectural and algorithmic components to achieve robust shaping in such complex multi-agent environments?
311e87c7c0c59bf5c03efa5a01df3e8bd2122edb.hypothesis: A simplified opponent shaping algorithm that consolidates memory for context and history into a single recurrent agent, and formalizes batch averaging, will enable scalable and effective shaping in high-dimensional, temporally-extended general-sum games, leading to improved individual and collective outcomes compared to prior methods.
311e87c7c0c59bf5c03efa5a01df3e8bd2122edb.proposed_method: A new opponent shaping method, termed Shaper, will be developed to address the scalability challenges in high-dimensional general-sum games. Shaper employs a single recurrent neural network agent that retains its hidden state over multiple episodes within a trial, capturing both intra-episode (history) and inter-episode (context) information necessary for shaping co-players' learning dynamics. The method formalizes and integrates batch averaging of hidden states at each meta-step, ensuring the agent's memory reflects the diversity of experiences across parallel environments. Training will be conducted using model-free meta-learning techniques, such as Evolution Strategies (ES), optimizing the meta-agent's policy over sequences of trials and episodes, with co-players sampled from a distribution and updated via their own learning rules. The approach will be systematically compared to previous architectures, including those requiring separate agents for context and history, and will include ablations to isolate the contributions of memory and batch averaging.
311e87c7c0c59bf5c03efa5a01df3e8bd2122edb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in a suite of challenging multi-agent environments, including gridworld-based general-sum games such as 'IPD in the Matrix' and 'IMP in the Matrix' from the Melting Pot benchmark, which feature large state spaces, partial observability, and temporally-extended actions. Baselines will include prior opponent shaping methods (M-FOS, The Good Shepherd), as well as naive learners and independent learners. Evaluation metrics will include individual and collective episodic rewards, state visitation patterns, and the ability to elicit cooperative or extortionate equilibria. Additional ablation studies will test the necessity of context, history, and batch averaging by selectively removing these components. Experiments will be run over hundreds of random seeds, and both reinforcement learning (PPO) and evolutionary strategies will be used for training and comparison.
311e87c7c0c59bf5c03efa5a01df3e8bd2122edb.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to successfully scale opponent shaping to high-dimensional, temporally-extended general-sum games with long time horizons. It introduces a simplified architecture that unifies context and history memory in a single recurrent agent, removing bottlenecks present in prior methods. The formalization and empirical analysis of batch averaging as a critical component for shaping are novel, as is the demonstration that previous benchmarks (e.g., CoinGame) are inadequate for evaluating shaping in complex environments. The method is shown to achieve improved individual and collective outcomes, and the analysis provides new insights into the roles of memory and batching in multi-agent meta-learning.

315d7a58fada47c5729645f0af8ddfaa0743f82f.title: Exploiting Diffusion Prior for Real-World Image Super-Resolution
315d7a58fada47c5729645f0af8ddfaa0743f82f.research_question: How can pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models be effectively leveraged for real-world blind image super-resolution, without explicit assumptions about image degradations and while preserving generative priors?
315d7a58fada47c5729645f0af8ddfaa0743f82f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that fine-tuning a lightweight, time-aware encoder and feature modulation layers—while keeping the pre-trained diffusion model frozen—can enable effective super-resolution by adaptively guiding the generative process, balancing fidelity and perceptual quality, and supporting arbitrary output resolutions.
315d7a58fada47c5729645f0af8ddfaa0743f82f.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a novel framework, StableSR, which exploits the generative prior of a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model (e.g., Stable Diffusion) for blind image super-resolution. A time-aware encoder is fine-tuned to extract multi-scale features from the low-resolution (LR) input and modulate the intermediate features of the frozen diffusion model via spatial feature transformation (SFT) layers, with temporal (diffusion step) embeddings to adaptively control the strength of guidance. To address the stochasticity and potential fidelity loss of diffusion models, a controllable feature wrapping (CFW) module is introduced, allowing users to trade off between realism and fidelity by adjusting a scalar coefficient during inference. Additionally, a progressive aggregation sampling strategy is developed to enable processing of images at arbitrary resolutions by dividing them into overlapping patches, fusing outputs with Gaussian-weighted aggregation at each diffusion step, and dynamically adjusting overlaps to avoid boundary artifacts. Color correction is also applied, both in pixel and wavelet domains, to align the color statistics of outputs with the LR input.
315d7a58fada47c5729645f0af8ddfaa0743f82f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world benchmarks. Synthetic LR-HR pairs are generated using the Real-ESRGAN degradation pipeline on datasets such as DIV2K, DIV8K, Flickr2K, and OutdoorSceneTraining, with additional face images from FFHQ for generalization. Real-world evaluations will use datasets including RealSR, DRealSR, and DPED-iPhone, as well as a set of 40 diverse internet images. Baselines for comparison include state-of-the-art GAN-based and diffusion-based SR models (e.g., RealSR, BSRGAN, Real-ESRGAN+, DASR, FeMaSR, LDM, SwinIR-GAN, IFIII). Evaluation metrics include PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, FID, CLIP-IQA, and MUSIQ, with both reference-based and no-reference metrics, and a user study is planned for perceptual assessment. The experimental setup includes fine-tuning only the encoder and SFT layers, using Adam optimizer, and employing DDPM sampling with 200 timesteps. For arbitrary resolution images, the aggregation sampling strategy is used.
315d7a58fada47c5729645f0af8ddfaa0743f82f.novelty_claims: The proposal claims novelty in leveraging pre-trained diffusion priors for super-resolution without requiring explicit degradation assumptions or retraining the entire diffusion model. Key innovations include the time-aware encoder for adaptive step-wise conditioning, the controllable feature wrapping module for user-adjustable fidelity-realism trade-off, and the progressive aggregation sampling strategy for seamless arbitrary-resolution image generation. The approach preserves the generative prior of the original diffusion model, minimizes training cost, and demonstrates superior perceptual quality and flexibility compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

316bfdad9f6c44050b9dfc8805747ffa111cd1d9.title: Energy-Based Sliced Wasserstein Distance
316bfdad9f6c44050b9dfc8805747ffa111cd1d9.research_question: How can the effectiveness and computational efficiency of the sliced Wasserstein distance be improved by designing a more informative and optimization-free slicing distribution for comparing probability measures in high-dimensional spaces?
316bfdad9f6c44050b9dfc8805747ffa111cd1d9.hypothesis: A parameter-free, energy-based slicing distribution, with density proportional to an energy function of the projected one-dimensional Wasserstein distance, will yield a sliced Wasserstein variant that is both more discriminative and computationally efficient than existing approaches using fixed or optimized slicing distributions.
316bfdad9f6c44050b9dfc8805747ffa111cd1d9.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed for the sliced Wasserstein distance by introducing an energy-based slicing distribution. This distribution is defined such that its density at each projecting direction on the unit hypersphere is proportional to a monotonically increasing energy function (such as an exponential or polynomial) applied to the one-dimensional Wasserstein distance between the projected probability measures. The resulting metric, termed the energy-based sliced Wasserstein (EBSW) distance, will be formally defined and its theoretical properties—including metricity, bounds with respect to existing variants, and convergence—will be established. To compute the EBSW in practice, several Monte Carlo estimation techniques will be implemented: importance sampling (IS), sampling importance resampling (SIR), and Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), each leveraging the energy-based slicing distribution to efficiently approximate the expectation over projecting directions. The method will be designed to be parameter-free, avoiding the need for costly or unstable optimization over parametric families of slicing distributions.
316bfdad9f6c44050b9dfc8805747ffa111cd1d9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on tasks including point-cloud gradient flows, color transfer between images, and deep point-cloud reconstruction. Datasets such as ShapeNetCore-55 and ModelNet40 will be used for point-cloud experiments, while color transfer will utilize RGB palettes from source and target images. Baseline methods for comparison will include the conventional sliced Wasserstein (SW), max sliced Wasserstein (Max-SW), and distributional sliced Wasserstein (DSW) distances. Evaluation metrics will include Wasserstein-2 distance, sliced Wasserstein distance, and computational time. Experimental setups will involve varying the number of projections, energy functions, and sampling methods, with performance assessed in terms of both accuracy (distance to target distributions) and computational efficiency.
316bfdad9f6c44050b9dfc8805747ffa111cd1d9.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel, parameter-free energy-based slicing distribution for the sliced Wasserstein distance, eliminating the need for optimization over parametric families and enabling more discriminative projections. The EBSW distance is the first non-optimization-based variant that provides an upper bound to the conventional SW distance while maintaining desirable metric and statistical properties. The method is computationally efficient, with importance sampling estimation requiring minimal code changes compared to standard SW, and supports multiple estimation techniques. Theoretical analysis establishes topological and statistical guarantees, and empirical results demonstrate superior performance over existing projection-selection sliced Wasserstein variants across several tasks.

31b27d90c2d5732386dd3a46a7d8336c0555c6fe.title: Deep Latent State Space Models for Time-Series Generation
31b27d90c2d5732386dd3a46a7d8336c0555c6fe.research_question: How can generative models for time-series data be improved to efficiently and accurately model sequences with sharp transitions and varying temporal dynamics, particularly in the presence of irregular sampling and long sequence lengths?
31b27d90c2d5732386dd3a46a7d8336c0555c6fe.hypothesis: A generative model for time-series data that leverages a deep latent state space architecture with convolutional representations and structured state space ODEs will achieve superior modeling capacity, computational efficiency, and robustness to sharp transitions compared to existing continuous-time generative models.
31b27d90c2d5732386dd3a46a7d8336c0555c6fe.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a deep latent state space model (LS4) for time-series generation, where latent variables evolve according to structured state space ordinary differential equations (ODEs). The method parameterizes the generative, prior, and inference distributions using stacks of state space model (SSM) blocks, each implemented via convolutional representations that bypass explicit hidden state recurrence. The prior over latent variables is modeled autoregressively with SSMs, while the decoder (generative model) and inference model are constructed as parallel stacks of SSMs for each input and latent dimension, allowing efficient computation via Fast Fourier Transform (FFT)-based convolutions. The architecture is trained using a variational autoencoder (VAE) objective, optimizing the evidence lower bound (ELBO) with factorized approximate posteriors for the latent sequences. HiPPO initialization is used for SSM parameters to ensure stability and expressivity, and the model scales efficiently to high-dimensional and long sequences.
31b27d90c2d5732386dd3a46a7d8336c0555c6fe.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world time-series datasets, including the Monash Time Series Forecasting Repository (e.g., FRED-MD, NN5Daily, TemperatureRain, SolarWeekly), USHCN, and Physionet. The evaluation will include tasks such as sequence generation, interpolation, and extrapolation, with datasets selected to cover a wide range of temporal dynamics and sequence lengths (up to ~20,000 steps). Baseline comparisons will include VAE-based models (RNN-VAE, GP-VAE, ODE2VAE, LatentODE), GAN-based models (TimeGAN, SDEGAN), and autoregressive SSMs (SaShiMi/S4). Evaluation metrics will comprise marginal distribution matching, classification scores (distinguishability of real vs. generated samples), prediction scores (future step prediction), mean squared error (MSE), and continuous ranked probability score (CRPS). Computational efficiency will be measured via wall-clock runtime for both training and inference across varying sequence lengths.
31b27d90c2d5732386dd3a46a7d8336c0555c6fe.novelty_claims: The proposed method claims several innovations: (1) introduction of a deep latent state space generative model for time-series that leverages convolutional SSM representations to bypass explicit hidden state recurrence, enabling log-linear scaling in both sequence length and hidden state dimensionality; (2) ability to model highly stochastic data with sharp temporal transitions and stiff dynamics where previous ODE-based methods fail; (3) significant computational speedup (up to 100x) over existing baselines for long sequences; (4) demonstration of state-of-the-art performance on multiple real-world and synthetic benchmarks in terms of marginal distribution, classification, prediction, interpolation, and extrapolation metrics; (5) theoretical results showing that the model subsumes autoregressive SSMs (e.g., S4) as a special case, while providing greater expressivity and efficiency.

31bfe3e9e139970c469cb9d2b7ed01b648434e37.title: Zero-Shot Generalization of Vision-Based RL Without Data Augmentation
31bfe3e9e139970c469cb9d2b7ed01b648434e37.research_question: How can vision-based reinforcement learning agents achieve zero-shot generalization to novel environments and task variations without relying on data augmentation or large-scale datasets?
31bfe3e9e139970c469cb9d2b7ed01b648434e37.hypothesis: Incorporating a mechanism that jointly learns disentangled latent representations and associative memory will enable vision-based RL agents to generalize zero-shot to out-of-distribution (OOD) environments, without the need for data augmentation.
31bfe3e9e139970c469cb9d2b7ed01b648434e37.proposed_method: A novel framework, Associative Latent Disentanglement (ALDA), is proposed that integrates disentangled representation learning with an associative memory mechanism within an off-policy RL algorithm. The method employs QLAE, a state-of-the-art disentanglement model, to encode high-dimensional image observations into a low-dimensional, discrete, disentangled latent space. Each latent dimension is mapped to a separate codebook, and a commitment loss ensures stability during training. To enable association, a softmax-based attention mechanism is applied over the codebooks, functioning analogously to a modern Hopfield network, which allows the agent to map OOD latent variables back to known in-distribution values. Temporal information is incorporated by reshaping batches of latent vectors and processing them through a 1D convolutional neural network, and the resulting latent representation is used as the state input for the actor and critic networks in the RL agent.
31bfe3e9e139970c469cb9d2b7ed01b648434e37.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on four challenging tasks from the DeepMind Control Suite, evaluating zero-shot generalization on the DMControl Generalization Benchmark and the Distracting Control Suite. The evaluation environments include 'colorhard' (randomizing agent and background colors) and 'distractingcs' (camera shaking and random video backgrounds). Baseline comparisons include DARLA (disentangled representation RL), SAC+AE (autoencoder regularized RL), RePo (task-centric latent RL), and SVEA (data augmentation-based RL). Performance is measured by average return over five random seeds, with training and evaluation curves reported for both in-distribution and OOD environments. Additional analysis includes latent traversals to empirically assess disentanglement, and ablations to isolate the impact of associative memory.
31bfe3e9e139970c469cb9d2b7ed01b648434e37.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to jointly learn disentangled representations and associative memory for vision-based RL, enabling zero-shot generalization without data augmentation. The method demonstrates that data augmentation is a form of weak disentanglement and provides a formal proof of this connection. ALDA achieves competitive or superior generalization performance compared to state-of-the-art data augmentation and representation learning baselines, while requiring less data and computational overhead. The approach also offers improved interpretability by explicitly separating task-relevant and task-irrelevant factors in the latent space.

31fcbacd4874a772e77ac21e4ec7d0dff132ec4e.title: Submodular Reinforcement Learning
31fcbacd4874a772e77ac21e4ec7d0dff132ec4e.research_question: How can reinforcement learning be extended to effectively optimize non-additive, history-dependent reward functions, particularly those exhibiting diminishing returns as captured by submodular set functions, and what are the theoretical and practical limits of such approaches?
31fcbacd4874a772e77ac21e4ec7d0dff132ec4e.hypothesis: Optimizing reinforcement learning policies with respect to submodular, non-additive reward functions is theoretically hard in the worst case, but practical algorithms inspired by greedy maximization of marginal gains can achieve strong empirical performance and provable approximation guarantees under certain structural assumptions.
31fcbacd4874a772e77ac21e4ec7d0dff132ec4e.proposed_method: A new reinforcement learning framework is proposed that models rewards as monotone submodular set functions over state-action trajectories, capturing the property of diminishing returns. The core algorithm, Submodular Policy Optimization (SUBPO), parameterizes the policy (potentially with neural networks) and applies a policy gradient method that, instead of maximizing immediate rewards, greedily maximizes marginal gains at each step. The policy gradient estimator is adapted to submodular rewards by decomposing trajectory returns into marginal gains and incorporating suitable baselines to reduce variance. The method supports both Markovian and non-Markovian policies, with history-dependence captured via recurrent architectures if needed, and can be further regularized with entropy penalization to encourage exploration. Optimization is performed via stochastic gradient ascent, and in special cases, Frank-Wolfe steps are used to enforce convex constraints and achieve provable approximation ratios.
31fcbacd4874a772e77ac21e4ec7d0dff132ec4e.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted across a diverse set of environments, including informative path planning (biodiversity monitoring), item collection, Bayesian D-experimental design, building exploration, car racing, and MuJoCo Ant locomotion. Both discrete and continuous state-action spaces are considered. The proposed SUBPO algorithm is evaluated in two variants: Markovian (SUBPO-M) and non-Markovian (SUBPO-NM) policies, and is compared to a modular RL baseline (MODPO) that optimizes additive rewards. Evaluation metrics include normalized cumulative reward (J(π)), coverage, and information gain, with statistical significance assessed over multiple random seeds and environments. Neural network-based policies are trained using PyTorch, with automatic differentiation for unbiased gradient estimation, and experiments are repeated for statistical confidence. The scalability and sample efficiency of the approach are demonstrated, especially in high-dimensional continuous control tasks.
31fcbacd4874a772e77ac21e4ec7d0dff132ec4e.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first general reinforcement learning framework for optimizing submodular, non-additive, and history-dependent reward functions, establishing new theoretical hardness results for such problems. SUBPO is a novel, practical policy gradient algorithm that maximizes marginal gains and is shown to achieve constant-factor approximation guarantees under DR-submodular and bounded curvature conditions. The approach is empirically validated across a wide range of challenging environments, demonstrating versatility, sample efficiency, and scalability to high-dimensional domains. This work significantly broadens the scope of RL to encompass a rich class of real-world objectives previously inaccessible to standard methods.

32112b798f70faab00e14806f51d46058cf5e597.title: Chameleon: Mixed-Modal Early-Fusion Foundation Models
32112b798f70faab00e14806f51d46058cf5e597.research_question: How can a unified, early-fusion, token-based foundation model be developed to understand and generate arbitrarily interleaved sequences of images and text, enabling general multimodal document modeling and reasoning?
32112b798f70faab00e14806f51d46058cf5e597.hypothesis: A transformer-based architecture that represents both images and text as discrete tokens and employs early-fusion, end-to-end training from scratch on large-scale mixed-modal data can achieve state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of multimodal and unimodal tasks, while also enabling novel capabilities in mixed-modal generation and reasoning.
32112b798f70faab00e14806f51d46058cf5e597.proposed_method: A novel mixed-modal foundation model will be developed using a fully token-based approach, where both images and text are quantized into discrete tokens and processed using a single, uniform transformer architecture. Images will be tokenized via a learned codebook (e.g., 8192 tokens per 512x512 image), while text will use a BPE tokenizer with a shared vocabulary. The model will be trained end-to-end from scratch on a massive corpus of interleaved text, image, and code data, using an early-fusion strategy that projects all modalities into a shared representational space. Architectural innovations such as query-key normalization (QK-Norm), revised layer norm placement, and z-loss regularization will be incorporated to ensure stable and scalable training across modalities. The training will be staged, with an initial phase using large-scale, unsupervised data and a second phase incorporating higher-quality and instruction-tuned datasets, followed by supervised fine-tuning for alignment and safety.
32112b798f70faab00e14806f51d46058cf5e597.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate the model on a comprehensive suite of tasks, including visual question answering, image captioning, text generation, image generation, and long-form mixed-modal document generation. Datasets will include large-scale text corpora (e.g., LLaMa-2 and CodeLLaMa pretraining data), 1.4 billion text-image pairs, and 400 billion tokens of interleaved text-image data, with additional high-quality and instruction-tuned datasets for fine-tuning. Baselines will include state-of-the-art models such as Llama-2, Mixtral 8x7B, Gemini-Pro, Flamingo, IDEFICS, and Llava-1.5. Evaluation metrics will cover standard benchmarks for each modality (e.g., VQA, image captioning scores, text-only reasoning benchmarks), as well as human preference studies for long-form mixed-modal generation, where human raters compare outputs from the proposed model against leading baselines. The experimental setup will utilize large-scale distributed training on clusters of NVIDIA A100 GPUs, with careful ablation studies to assess the impact of architectural and optimization choices.
32112b798f70faab00e14806f51d46058cf5e597.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified, early-fusion, token-based transformer architecture capable of reasoning over and generating fully interleaved image-text documents, eliminating the need for modality-specific encoders or decoders. Key innovations include architectural modifications (QK-Norm, norm reordering) and a stable training recipe that enables scaling to large parameter counts and data volumes. The model is expected to achieve state-of-the-art performance across both multimodal and unimodal tasks, while unlocking new capabilities in mixed-modal document generation and reasoning. Additionally, the work pioneers large-scale human evaluation for open-ended mixed-modal generation, demonstrating the model's unique abilities in this emerging area.

321dab4a4d30192a11873d894ac6720ff3888201.title: SuperCorrect: Advancing Small LLM Reasoning with Thought Template Distillation and Self-Correction
321dab4a4d30192a11873d894ac6720ff3888201.research_question: How can the reasoning accuracy and self-correction ability of small language models be significantly improved for complex mathematical tasks, particularly by leveraging external guidance and advanced training strategies?
321dab4a4d30192a11873d894ac6720ff3888201.hypothesis: Equipping small language models with hierarchical thought templates distilled from larger teacher models, combined with cross-model collaborative direct preference optimization based on teacher correction traces, will substantially enhance their reasoning accuracy and self-correction capabilities on challenging mathematical problems.
321dab4a4d30192a11873d894ac6720ff3888201.proposed_method: A two-stage training framework is developed. In the first stage, hierarchical thought templates—comprising both high-level generalized strategies and detailed step-by-step explanations—are extracted from a large teacher LLM for a diverse set of mathematical problems. These templates are used to supervise small student LLMs via supervised fine-tuning, encouraging the generation of more fine-grained and human-like reasoning processes. In the second stage, a cross-model collaborative Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) procedure is introduced: the student LLM's erroneous reasoning steps are identified, and the teacher LLM provides explicit correction traces for these errors. The student model is then optimized to prefer the teacher's corrections over its own self-corrections, using a pairwise preference loss at the thought-step level. This approach enables the student to internalize error-driven insights and break through its reasoning bottlenecks.
321dab4a4d30192a11873d894ac6720ff3888201.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using several strong small LLMs (e.g., Qwen2.5-Math-7B, Meta-Llama3.1-8B, DeepSeek-Math-7B) as student models. Training data includes 100k hierarchical thought template samples and 10k paired correction traces, sourced from datasets such as MATH, GSM8K, GaoKao Bench, NuminaMath, and MetaMath. Evaluation will be performed on the MATH and GSM8K test sets, using chain-of-thought reasoning accuracy as the primary metric, with comparisons against state-of-the-art baselines and reflection-based methods (e.g., Reflexion). The experimental setup includes ablation studies to isolate the effects of hierarchical supervision and cross-model DPO, as well as analysis of reasoning stability and topic-wise performance.
321dab4a4d30192a11873d894ac6720ff3888201.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel two-stage framework that combines hierarchical thought template distillation from large teacher models with cross-model collaborative DPO for small LLMs. Key innovations include the use of hierarchical (high-level and detailed) thought templates for fine-tuning, the construction of a fine-grained correction dataset at the thought-step level, and a cross-model optimization strategy that leverages explicit teacher corrections rather than relying solely on self-reflection. This approach is claimed to break through the reasoning bottlenecks of small LLMs, significantly improving both accuracy and self-correction ability, and to achieve new state-of-the-art results among 7B parameter models on challenging mathematical reasoning benchmarks.

325d110aacf592b6e9f07932d896341e6c9923e0.title: CoLT: The conditional localization test for assessing the accuracy of neural posterior estimates
325d110aacf592b6e9f07932d896341e6c9923e0.research_question: How can the accuracy of neural posterior estimates be rigorously and efficiently validated across all conditioning inputs, especially in simulation-based inference settings where only limited samples from the true posterior are available for each input?
325d110aacf592b6e9f07932d896341e6c9923e0.hypothesis: A conditional localization test that adaptively learns regions of maximal discrepancy between the true and estimated posteriors, leveraging a learned embedding and localization function, will provide a more sensitive and scalable method for detecting and quantifying mismatches between conditional distributions than existing approaches.
325d110aacf592b6e9f07932d896341e6c9923e0.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces the Conditional Localization Test (CoLT), which formulates posterior validation as a search for local regions where the neural posterior estimate deviates most from the true posterior. This is achieved by learning a localization function that maps conditioning inputs to parameter space locations where discrepancies are maximized, and a trainable embedding that transforms the parameter space to better align with the geometry of distributional differences. The method constructs a ball probability rank statistic by anchoring each comparison on a single observed sample from the true posterior and comparing the conditional mass assigned by the neural posterior within adaptive metric balls. The optimization objective maximizes the divergence between the empirical distribution of these rank statistics and the uniform distribution, using differentiable approximations such as Sinkhorn divergence during training. At test time, the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test is used to assess the uniformity of the rank statistics, providing both a p-value for hypothesis testing and an integral probability metric quantifying the distance between posteriors.
325d110aacf592b6e9f07932d896341e6c9923e0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of benchmark tasks designed for neural posterior testing, including both multivariate Gaussian posteriors with data-dependent parameters and nonlinear manifold-structured posteriors. For each benchmark, a reference posterior is defined and systematically perturbed to generate families of alternative posteriors with controlled levels of discrepancy. The proposed method will be evaluated against established baselines such as classifier two-sample tests (C2ST), simulation-based calibration (SBC), and TARP, with all methods adapted to produce p-values for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics include Type I error rates and statistical power across varying perturbation severities, with experiments repeated across multiple random seeds and dimensional configurations. Each method will be trained and tested using matched sample budgets, with detailed implementation and architectural choices specified for reproducibility.
325d110aacf592b6e9f07932d896341e6c9923e0.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled and scalable framework for conditional distribution comparison that leverages adaptive localization and learned geometric embeddings, overcoming key limitations of existing classifier-based and marginal rank-based tests. The method provides both necessary and sufficient conditions for posterior equivalence, enables efficient optimization using only a single true posterior sample per conditioning input, and yields a continuous, interpretable metric for quantifying posterior mismatch. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior sensitivity and robustness, particularly in high-dimensional or geometrically complex settings where prior methods struggle.

32820e6c6b145a497c2d9f40e259e41af8ec93fa.title: RelTR: Relation Transformer for Scene Graph Generation
32820e6c6b145a497c2d9f40e259e41af8ec93fa.research_question: How can scene graph generation be improved to efficiently and accurately predict meaningful relationships between objects in an image using only visual appearance, while overcoming the limitations of dense, two-stage approaches?
32820e6c6b145a497c2d9f40e259e41af8ec93fa.hypothesis: A one-stage, end-to-end transformer-based model that directly predicts a sparse set of subject-predicate-object triplets from visual features, without reliance on prior knowledge or dense pairwise classification, will achieve competitive or superior accuracy and inference speed compared to existing two-stage and prior-knowledge-based methods.
32820e6c6b145a497c2d9f40e259e41af8ec93fa.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces Relation Transformer (RelTR), an end-to-end scene graph generation model with an encoder-decoder transformer architecture.
