33c8fde911526140a85cdfc654c8ee318f83906d.title: CollabLLM: From Passive Responders to Active Collaborators
33c8fde911526140a85cdfc654c8ee318f83906d.research_question: How can large language models be trained to move beyond passive, single-turn responses and instead actively collaborate with users over multiple conversational turns to improve user satisfaction, efficiency, and task success in complex, open-ended tasks?
33c8fde911526140a85cdfc654c8ee318f83906d.hypothesis: Training large language models with multiturn-aware rewards that estimate the long-term impact of responses, using collaborative simulation and reinforcement learning, will enable these models to more effectively uncover user intent, proactively guide conversations, and outperform standard single-turn or prompt-engineered models in multiturn collaboration tasks.
33c8fde911526140a85cdfc654c8ee318f83906d.proposed_method: A novel training framework will be developed that enhances large language models (LLMs) for multiturn human-AI collaboration. The core of the method is a collaborative simulation module that forward-samples possible future conversation trajectories with a user simulator, estimating the long-term impact of each model response using a Multiturn-aware Reward (MR) function. This reward function combines extrinsic metrics (e.g., task-specific success such as BLEU or accuracy) and intrinsic metrics (e.g., conversational efficiency, engagement, and interactivity as judged by an LLM). Reinforcement learning algorithms such as PPO and DPO will be used to fine-tune the LLM based on these multiturn-aware rewards, encouraging the model to generate responses that maximize long-term collaboration gains. Synthetic multiturn datasets will be generated via simulation for both supervised and reinforcement learning, enabling scalable training without human annotation.
33c8fde911526140a85cdfc654c8ee318f83906d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three multiturn benchmarks: document editing (MediumDocEdit-Chat), code generation (BigCodeBench-Chat), and multiturn mathematics problem solving (MATH-Chat), each constructed using publicly available data and simulated user interactions. Evaluation will use task-specific metrics (BLEU for document editing, pass rate for code, accuracy for math), as well as task-agnostic metrics such as average token count (for efficiency) and interactivity (LLM-judged engagement). Baselines will include the base Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model, proactive prompt-engineered variants, and standard RLHF-trained models. Both offline (SFT, DPO) and online (PPO, Online DPO) training variants will be compared. Additionally, a large-scale real-world user study will be conducted with over 200 participants, measuring user satisfaction, interaction quality, and time efficiency during collaborative writing tasks with anonymized AI assistants.
33c8fde911526140a85cdfc654c8ee318f83906d.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a general, multiturn-aware training paradigm for LLMs that explicitly models the long-term effects of responses through collaborative simulation and forward-sampled reward estimation. Unlike existing approaches that focus on single-turn rewards or rigid prompt engineering, this method enables proactive, adaptive, and user-centric collaboration strategies. The use of a user simulator for scalable forward sampling, the integration of both extrinsic and intrinsic rewards, and the demonstration of strong generalization to new domains and real-world user interactions are claimed as key innovations. The framework is positioned as the first to systematically align LLM training with the objectives of sustained, effective, and efficient human-AI collaboration.

33e26d4428a10f3b2803221437187c6c32778b43.title: Optimizing Temperature for Language Models with Multi-Sample Inference
33e26d4428a10f3b2803221437187c6c32778b43.research_question: How can the optimal temperature for sampling in large language models (LLMs) using multi-sample aggregation strategies be automatically determined across diverse tasks, model architectures, and aggregation methods, without relying on labeled validation data?
33e26d4428a10f3b2803221437187c6c32778b43.hypothesis: Token-level entropy exhibits a characteristic turning point with respect to temperature, which can serve as an intrinsic, model- and task-specific indicator for selecting a near-optimal sampling temperature in multi-sample inference, thereby maximizing predictive accuracy without the need for labeled validation data.
33e26d4428a10f3b2803221437187c6c32778b43.proposed_method: A novel entropy-based framework, termed Turning Point Temperature Selection (TURN), will be developed to automatically select the optimal sampling temperature for LLMs during multi-sample inference. The method involves generating candidate outputs at various temperatures, computing the token-level entropy for each, and identifying the 'entropy turning point'—the temperature at which the log-entropy curve transitions from concave to convex, indicating a sudden spike in entropy and a potential drop in sample quality. This turning point is used as the predicted optimal temperature, with a small adaptation factor added based on the aggregation strategy (e.g., majority voting or best-of-N). Additionally, a stochastic process model will be incorporated to provide interpretability and theoretical justification for the observed entropy behavior and its relationship to sample quality collapse.
33e26d4428a10f3b2803221437187c6c32778b43.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two major tasks: mathematical problem solving (using the MATH dataset) with majority voting aggregation, and code generation (using the MBPP dataset) with best-of-N aggregation. A diverse set of LLMs will be evaluated, including general-purpose, instruction-finetuned, task-finetuned, and domain-specific models. For each model and task, accuracy will be measured at various temperatures and compared against baselines using fixed temperatures and grid search. Evaluation metrics will include hit rate (whether the predicted temperature falls within an epsilon-optimal range), temperature gap, and performance drop relative to the best grid-searched temperature. The efficiency of the method will also be assessed by varying the number of samples used for entropy estimation.
33e26d4428a10f3b2803221437187c6c32778b43.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first automatic, validation-free method for temperature selection in multi-sample LLM inference, leveraging an intrinsic entropy-based metric. It eliminates the need for labeled validation data, adapts to different models, tasks, and aggregation strategies, and consistently outperforms fixed-temperature baselines. The integration of a stochastic process model provides new interpretability into the relationship between temperature, entropy, and sample quality, offering both practical and theoretical advances in optimizing LLM inference.

3404f2051763368df1613e3d9b7b787cb4a8b833.title: Larger or Smaller Reward Margins to Select Preferences for Alignment?
3404f2051763368df1613e3d9b7b787cb4a8b833.research_question: How can the quality of preference data for aligning large language models with human values be more reliably and universally evaluated, and can a new metric improve the selection and generation of high-quality data for preference optimization and alignment?
3404f2051763368df1613e3d9b7b787cb4a8b833.hypothesis: A metric that quantifies the gap between a model’s current implicit reward margin and the target explicit reward margin (alignment potential) will more effectively identify high-quality preference data, leading to improved alignment performance across various models, training objectives, and data generation scenarios.
3404f2051763368df1613e3d9b7b787cb4a8b833.proposed_method: A novel alignment potential metric (MAP) is introduced to assess the quality of preference data for large language model alignment. This metric is defined as the absolute difference between the explicit reward margin (from a reward model) and the implicit reward margin (from the current LLM policy) for each preference pair. The method involves selecting preference pairs with the highest alignment potential scores, indicating the greatest room for alignment improvement, and using these for model training. The metric is further regularized to mitigate the impact of reward model noise and is calibrated to match the directionality of typical preference optimization objectives. The approach is integrated into both static dataset selection and iterative self-play data generation frameworks, where it guides both the selection of high-quality data and the evolution of new prompts and responses.
3404f2051763368df1613e3d9b7b787cb4a8b833.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using Llama-3-8b and Gemma-2-9b instruction-tuned models, with preference datasets derived from UltraFeedback and annotated by state-of-the-art reward models (e.g., ArmoRM, PairRM). The MAP metric is compared against baselines including explicit reward margin, implicit reward margin, and uniform random selection. Evaluation is performed using open-ended instruction-following benchmarks such as AlpacaEval2 (reporting both length-controlled and raw win rates) and Arena-Hard, which assess general conversational abilities. Both single-iteration and multi-iteration (self-play) training setups are explored, with ablation studies on reward models, optimization objectives (DPO, SimPO), and dataset sizes. The impact of MAP-guided selection is measured by alignment performance improvements and noise robustness, including agreement with GPT-4 re-annotations.
3404f2051763368df1613e3d9b7b787cb4a8b833.novelty_claims: The alignment potential metric offers a theoretically grounded, universal approach to preference data quality evaluation by explicitly measuring the gap between current and optimal reward margins. This approach resolves contradictions inherent in prior metrics and is robust to reward model noise. The metric is shown to generalize to self-play data generation settings, enabling scalable and efficient expansion of high-quality preference datasets. Empirical and theoretical analyses demonstrate that MAP-guided selection accelerates convergence and consistently yields superior alignment performance over existing methods and baselines.

3422d5e0cdfdc935d6a84a1e3d3f96659265fe3a.title: Detecting Pretraining Data from Large Language Models
3422d5e0cdfdc935d6a84a1e3d3f96659265fe3a.research_question: Can it be determined whether a given piece of text was included in the pretraining data of a large language model (LLM) when only black-box access to the model is available and the pretraining data is undisclosed?
3422d5e0cdfdc935d6a84a1e3d3f96659265fe3a.hypothesis: An unseen example is likely to contain a few outlier words with low probabilities under the LLM, whereas a seen example is less likely to have words with such low probabilities. Therefore, the average log-likelihood of the least likely k% of tokens in a text can be used to distinguish between pretraining data and non-pretraining data.
3422d5e0cdfdc935d6a84a1e3d3f96659265fe3a.proposed_method: A novel, reference-free pretraining data detection method, MIN-K% PROB, will be developed. This method computes the token-level probabilities for a given text using black-box access to the target LLM. The k% of tokens with the lowest probabilities (highest negative log-likelihood) are selected, and their average log-likelihood is calculated. If this average is above a certain threshold, the text is inferred to have been seen during pretraining; otherwise, it is considered unseen. The method requires no access to the pretraining corpus or additional reference models, making it practical for large-scale LLMs where such data is unavailable or training is infeasible. The approach will be evaluated across both verbatim and paraphrased text settings, as well as across varying text lengths.
3422d5e0cdfdc935d6a84a1e3d3f96659265fe3a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the WIKIMIA benchmark, which consists of Wikipedia event articles created before (member data) and after (non-member data) a model's pretraining cutoff date, ensuring accurate ground truth. The benchmark supports both original and paraphrased versions of texts, and texts will be evaluated at multiple lengths (32, 64, 128, 256 tokens). The proposed method will be compared against several baselines, including reference-based and reference-free membership inference attacks: LOSSAttack (PPL), Neighbor (DetectGPT), Zlib compression, Lowercase, and SmallerRef (using a smaller reference model). Evaluation metrics will include AUC (area under the ROC curve) and TPR@5%FPR. Additional case studies will target real-world scenarios such as detecting copyrighted book content in pretraining data, identifying downstream dataset contamination, and auditing privacy compliance after machine unlearning. Ablation studies will examine the effects of dataset size, data occurrence frequency, and learning rate on detection difficulty.
3422d5e0cdfdc935d6a84a1e3d3f96659265fe3a.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple, effective, and reference-free approach to pretraining data detection that does not require access to the pretraining corpus or the training of reference models, overcoming a major limitation of prior membership inference techniques. The WIKIMIA benchmark is dynamic and automated, supporting continual updates and evaluation across different LLMs and time periods. The method demonstrates superior performance over existing baselines, achieving significant improvements in AUC, and is shown to be robust across paraphrased texts and varying text lengths. The approach is validated in practical, high-impact scenarios such as copyright detection, dataset contamination, and privacy auditing, providing actionable tools for ethical and regulatory compliance in LLM deployment.

34758c94b7e42cc60e83df194da26bc9566e112b.title: Accelerating Value Iteration with Anchoring
34758c94b7e42cc60e83df194da26bc9566e112b.research_question: How can the convergence rate of value iteration in reinforcement learning and dynamic programming be accelerated, particularly in terms of Bellman error, for both discounted and undiscounted Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), and can a general acceleration mechanism be developed that is robust to approximate evaluations and applicable to various value iteration variants?
34758c94b7e42cc60e83df194da26bc9566e112b.hypothesis: An anchoring-based acceleration mechanism, distinct from Nesterov's acceleration, will achieve a provably faster convergence rate for value iteration—specifically, a (1/k) rate for Bellman error when the discount factor is near or equal to one—matching a theoretical lower bound up to a constant factor, and will retain robustness under approximate and Gauss–Seidel value iteration settings.
34758c94b7e42cc60e83df194da26bc9566e112b.proposed_method: A novel value iteration algorithm, termed Anchored Value Iteration (Anc-VI), will be developed. This method iteratively computes new value function estimates as a convex combination of the output of the Bellman operator and the initial value function, with the combination coefficient (anchor term) decreasing over iterations. The update rule is Uk = βk U0 + (1 - βk) T Uk-1, where βk is a sequence determined by the discount factor and iteration count. The approach will be rigorously analyzed for both the Bellman consistency (policy evaluation) and optimality (control) operators, including the case where the discount factor γ = 1 (undiscounted MDPs). Theoretical analysis will establish convergence rates and pointwise convergence, and the method will be extended to handle approximate Bellman operator evaluations (Approximate Anc-VI) and Gauss–Seidel-style updates (GS-Anc-VI) in finite state-action spaces.
34758c94b7e42cc60e83df194da26bc9566e112b.experiment_details: Experiments will involve theoretical analysis and construction of worst-case MDPs to establish both upper and lower bounds on the convergence rate of the proposed Anc-VI algorithm. Complexity lower bounds will be derived using information-based complexity analysis, and the optimality of the accelerated rate will be demonstrated by matching the lower bound up to a constant factor. Theoretical robustness to approximation errors in the Bellman operator will be analyzed, comparing Anc-VI to standard Approximate Value Iteration. The method will also be tested in the context of Gauss–Seidel updates for finite state-action spaces. Evaluation metrics will include the Bellman error and distance to the fixed point, with rates compared against classical value iteration and existing accelerated methods. Datasets are not empirical but are based on constructed MDPs for theoretical analysis.
34758c94b7e42cc60e83df194da26bc9566e112b.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first general acceleration mechanism for value iteration that achieves a (1/k) convergence rate for Bellman error when the discount factor is near or equal to one, surpassing the classical (γ^k) rate. The anchoring mechanism is distinct from Nesterov's acceleration and is shown to be optimal up to a constant factor by matching a new complexity lower bound. The approach is robust to approximate Bellman operator evaluations and extends to Gauss–Seidel value iteration. The method also guarantees convergence in the undiscounted case (γ = 1) under mild conditions, a setting where standard value iteration may fail to converge. These contributions represent a substantive theoretical improvement over classical value iteration and prior acceleration attempts.

34774d962d6ce9684245c8b4ec9d4e0886d65222.title: Adversarial Perturbations Cannot Reliably Protect Artists From Generative AI
34774d962d6ce9684245c8b4ec9d4e0886d65222.research_question: Can adversarial perturbation-based protection tools reliably prevent unauthorized style mimicry of artists' works by generative AI models, even when faced with adaptive or low-effort circumvention techniques?
34774d962d6ce9684245c8b4ec9d4e0886d65222.hypothesis: Adversarial perturbation-based protections for digital artworks are insufficient to reliably prevent style mimicry by generative AI, as simple and accessible image processing methods can circumvent these defenses.
34774d962d6ce9684245c8b4ec9d4e0886d65222.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation protocol will be developed to assess the robustness of existing adversarial perturbation-based protection tools against a range of robust style mimicry methods. Four robust mimicry methods will be designed, prioritizing simplicity and accessibility: (1) Gaussian noising, which adds small Gaussian noise to protected images; (2) DiffPure, an image-to-image purification technique that removes adversarial perturbations using a separate diffusion model; (3) Noisy Upscaling, which first applies Gaussian noise and then upscales the image using a diffusion-based upscaler; and (4) IMPRESS++, a white-box method that builds on prior work with improved loss functions and negative prompting. These methods will be applied to images protected by state-of-the-art tools, and their effectiveness in enabling style mimicry will be systematically measured.
34774d962d6ce9684245c8b4ec9d4e0886d65222.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using artworks from 10 artists (5 historical and 5 contemporary) to ensure style diversity. For each artist, 18 images will be used for finetuning, and 10 diverse prompts will be generated per artist. The Stable Diffusion 2.1 model will be finetuned using an off-the-shelf HuggingFace script, and protection tools (Mist, Glaze, Anti-DreamBooth) will be applied using their official codebases or binaries. Each robust mimicry method will be evaluated against each protection tool, resulting in 15 scenarios. Human evaluation will be performed via Amazon Mechanical Turk, with participants comparing image pairs for both style transfer and image quality. The primary metric will be the success rate, defined as the percentage of annotators who prefer the output of robust mimicry over baseline mimicry from unprotected art. Control measures will be implemented to ensure annotation quality.
34774d962d6ce9684245c8b4ec9d4e0886d65222.novelty_claims: The proposed evaluation protocol introduces a unified, rigorous, and human-centric framework for assessing the effectiveness of style mimicry protections, addressing prior limitations such as inconsistent setups and unreliable automated metrics. The study demonstrates that even low-effort, off-the-shelf image processing techniques can reliably circumvent widely used protection tools, challenging prevailing assumptions about their robustness. The work highlights the inherent asymmetry between protection and attack in this domain, and provides the first large-scale user study showing that adversarial perturbation-based protections offer only a false sense of security for artists.

3487c12512fa41d3a4d64f00cb842525a8590ad3.title: TALLRec: An Effective and Efficient Tuning Framework to Align Large Language Model with Recommendation
3487c12512fa41d3a4d64f00cb842525a8590ad3.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be effectively and efficiently aligned with recommendation tasks, particularly in scenarios with limited recommendation data and computational resources?
3487c12512fa41d3a4d64f00cb842525a8590ad3.hypothesis: Instruction tuning of LLMs with recommendation-specific data, combined with lightweight parameter-efficient adaptation techniques, will significantly enhance the recommendation performance and generalization ability of LLMs, even in few-shot settings and across domains.
3487c12512fa41d3a4d64f00cb842525a8590ad3.proposed_method: A novel tuning framework, TALLRec, will be developed to align LLMs with recommendation tasks through a two-stage process: (1) general instruction tuning using diverse self-instruct data (e.g., Alpaca) to enhance the model's generalization, and (2) recommendation-specific instruction tuning (rec-tuning) that formats user-item interaction data as natural language instructions and responses. The framework will employ a lightweight adaptation strategy using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), which freezes the majority of the LLM's parameters and introduces trainable low-rank matrices into the Transformer layers, thus enabling efficient fine-tuning with minimal GPU resources. The backbone LLM will be an open-source model such as LLaMA-7B, selected for accessibility and data transparency. The method will support few-shot learning by enabling effective adaptation with as few as 64 tuning samples, and will be designed to generalize across different recommendation domains (e.g., movies and books).
3487c12512fa41d3a4d64f00cb842525a8590ad3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two benchmark datasets: a processed version of MovieLens 100K (movies) and BookCrossing (books), both enriched with textual item descriptions. The evaluation will focus on few-shot settings, with training sample sizes ranging from 16 to 256. Baselines will include both traditional sequential recommendation models (GRU4Rec, Caser, SASRec, DROS) and LLM-based methods using In-context Learning (Alpaca-LoRA, GPT-3.5, ChatGPT). Variants incorporating BERT for text encoding (GRU-BERT, DROS-BERT) will also be compared. The primary evaluation metric will be AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve). Ablation studies will assess the contributions of each tuning stage, and cross-domain experiments will evaluate generalization by training on one domain and testing on another. All experiments will be run multiple times with different seeds, and hyperparameters will be optimized for fairness.
3487c12512fa41d3a4d64f00cb842525a8590ad3.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a lightweight, instruction-based tuning approach that enables LLMs to rapidly acquire recommendation capabilities from limited data, outperforming both traditional and LLM-based baselines in few-shot settings. TALLRec is designed for efficiency, requiring only a single consumer-grade GPU for training, and demonstrates robust cross-domain generalization. The method uniquely combines instruction tuning with LoRA-based adaptation, and is the first to show that LLMs can be effectively aligned with recommendation tasks using minimal recommendation data, unlocking their generalization and knowledge capabilities for this domain.

348a855fe01f3f4273bf0ecf851ca688686dbfcc.title: Offline Reinforcement Learning with Implicit Q-Learning
348a855fe01f3f4273bf0ecf851ca688686dbfcc.research_question: How can offline reinforcement learning be performed to improve over the behavior policy using only previously collected data, while avoiding errors due to distributional shift and without querying values for out-of-distribution actions?
348a855fe01f3f4273bf0ecf851ca688686dbfcc.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a reinforcement learning algorithm can be developed that achieves substantial policy improvement over the behavior policy, while never querying or estimating values for out-of-distribution actions, by leveraging expectile regression and advantage-weighted behavioral cloning.
348a855fe01f3f4273bf0ecf851ca688686dbfcc.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces an offline reinforcement learning algorithm, termed implicit Q-learning (IQL), that avoids querying the value function on out-of-distribution actions. The method alternates between fitting a value function using expectile regression to estimate an upper expectile of the Q-values conditioned on actions in the dataset, and using this value function to perform Bellman backups for training the Q-function with a mean squared error loss. Specifically, the value function is trained to predict a high expectile (e.g., τ close to 1) of the Q-values, which approximates the maximum over in-distribution actions, while the Q-function is updated to match the expected return using this value function. Policy extraction is performed via advantage-weighted behavioral cloning, where the policy is trained to maximize the likelihood of dataset actions weighted by the exponential of their advantage, thus avoiding explicit policy constraints or regularization. The method employs clipped double Q-learning for stability and does not require an explicit policy during value function training.
348a855fe01f3f4273bf0ecf851ca688686dbfcc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the D4RL benchmark, which includes MuJoCo locomotion tasks, Ant Maze navigation tasks, and robotic manipulation environments (Adroit and Kitchen). The proposed method will be compared against both multi-step dynamic programming baselines (such as CQL, TD3+BC, and AWAC) and single-step approaches (such as Onestep RL and Decision Transformers). Evaluation metrics will include normalized episodic return, and experiments will assess both offline performance and the ability to fine-tune policies with online interaction after offline initialization. Hyperparameters such as the expectile parameter τ will be varied to study their effect, especially on tasks requiring trajectory stitching. Computational efficiency and runtime will also be measured and compared to baselines.
348a855fe01f3f4273bf0ecf851ca688686dbfcc.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first offline RL algorithm to combine multi-step dynamic programming with the property of never querying values for out-of-distribution actions during training. It achieves this by using expectile regression to approximate the maximum over in-distribution actions and extracting the policy via advantage-weighted behavioral cloning, thus eliminating the need for explicit policy constraints or regularization. The approach is computationally efficient, simple to implement, and demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on challenging offline RL benchmarks, particularly in environments that require stitching suboptimal trajectories.

349104be403d3debfef7c6c5ffb469608f450547.title: Understanding Robust Overfitting of Adversarial Training and Beyond
349104be403d3debfef7c6c5ffb469608f450547.research_question: What are the underlying causes of robust overfitting in adversarial training of deep neural networks, and how can robust overfitting be effectively eliminated to improve adversarial robustness without requiring additional training data?
349104be403d3debfef7c6c5ffb469608f450547.hypothesis: Robust overfitting in adversarial training is primarily caused by the presence of small-loss data that do not match the strength of the adversary, and explicitly constraining or manipulating the loss of such data during training will eliminate robust overfitting and improve adversarial robustness.
349104be403d3debfef7c6c5ffb469608f450547.proposed_method: A new adversarial training prototype, Minimum Loss Constrained Adversarial Training (MLCAT), will be developed to address robust overfitting. In each minibatch, the method distinguishes between large-loss and small-loss data using a minimum loss threshold. Large-loss data are trained as usual, while small-loss data are subjected to additional measures to increase their loss, preventing the model from fitting these easy examples too quickly and thus mitigating overfitting. Two concrete realizations of MLCAT will be implemented: (1) loss scaling, where the loss of small-loss data is multiplied by a scaling factor to meet the minimum loss threshold, and (2) weight perturbation, where targeted perturbations are applied to the model weights to increase the loss of small-loss data. The approach is designed to be general and can be flexibly integrated with existing adversarial training algorithms.
349104be403d3debfef7c6c5ffb469608f450547.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on benchmark datasets including CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and SVHN, using standard architectures such as PreActResNet-18 and WideResNet-34-10. Both L-infinity and L2 threat models will be considered, with adversarial examples generated via 10-step PGD during training. Robustness will be evaluated using 20-step PGD and AutoAttack (AA), which is an ensemble of diverse, parameter-free attacks. Baselines will include standard adversarial training (AT) and other state-of-the-art adversarial training variants. Evaluation metrics will focus on test robustness (accuracy under attack), the gap between best and last epoch robustness (to measure overfitting), and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of the minimum loss threshold and different loss adjustment strategies.
349104be403d3debfef7c6c5ffb469608f450547.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel perspective by identifying small-loss data as the primary cause of robust overfitting in adversarial training. The MLCAT framework is a general and flexible prototype that can be instantiated with different loss adjustment strategies, such as loss scaling and weight perturbation, to explicitly manipulate the loss of small-loss data. Unlike prior works, this method eliminates robust overfitting without requiring additional training data or reducing sample size, and is shown to be effective across multiple datasets, architectures, and threat models. The approach provides a new algorithmic and philosophical viewpoint on making full use of adversarial data, turning 'waste' (easy-to-fit data) into 'treasure' for robust learning.

3499082a4e936bb9fffc896f8afada30ab46a6b0.title: TRIM: Scalable 3D Gaussian Diffusion Inference with Temporal and Spatial Trimming
3499082a4e936bb9fffc896f8afada30ab46a6b0.research_question: How can the efficiency and scalability of 3D Gaussian diffusion models for text-to-3D and image-to-3D generation be improved during inference, without compromising the quality of the generated 3D assets?
3499082a4e936bb9fffc896f8afada30ab46a6b0.hypothesis: Integrating temporal and spatial trimming strategies—specifically, early trajectory reduction via a lightweight latent selector and instance mask denoising to prune redundant background regions—will significantly accelerate 3D Gaussian diffusion inference while maintaining or improving the quality of generated 3D outputs.
3499082a4e936bb9fffc896f8afada30ab46a6b0.proposed_method: A novel post-training framework, TRIM (Trajectory Reduction and Instance Mask denoising), is proposed to accelerate 3D Gaussian diffusion inference. The method consists of two main components: (1) Trajectory Reduction, which employs a lightweight latent selector trained via offline knowledge distillation to identify and retain the most promising denoising trajectory at an early timestep, thus reducing redundant computation on multiple trajectories; and (2) Instance Mask Denoising, which uses a model-free, reference-attention-based mechanism to detect and progressively mask background regions in the latent representation, reducing the number of tokens processed by the denoising transformer. The instance mask is applied in a scheduled, progressive manner to ensure stability, and after denoising, a post-processing correction sets the opacity of background Gaussian primitives to zero to eliminate rendering artifacts. Both components are designed to be model-agnostic and training-free, allowing integration with existing transformer-based 3D diffusion models.
3499082a4e936bb9fffc896f8afada30ab46a6b0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using DiffSplat as the primary 3D Gaussian diffusion backbone, trained on the G-Objaverse dataset. For text-to-3D generation, evaluation will be performed on the T3Bench benchmark (300 prompts), using CLIP Similarity, CLIP R-Precision, and ImageReward metrics to assess semantic alignment and perceptual quality. For image-to-3D generation, 300 objects from the Google Scanned Objects (GSO) dataset will be used, with PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS metrics to evaluate reconstruction fidelity. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art methods such as GVGEN, DIRECT-3D, LGM, and InstantMesh. Ablation studies will analyze the contributions of trajectory reduction and instance masking, selector architecture, and application timing. Computational efficiency will be measured in terms of FLOPs, memory usage, and throughput. Diversity analysis will use CLIP similarity, ImageReward, and Chamfer Distance metrics.
3499082a4e936bb9fffc896f8afada30ab46a6b0.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a dual trimming strategy—temporal (trajectory reduction) and spatial (instance mask denoising)—for 3D Gaussian diffusion models, enabling substantial computational savings during inference without retraining or architectural modifications. The lightweight latent selector for early trajectory pruning and the model-free, progressive instance masking mechanism are both novel in the context of 3D diffusion. The approach is model-agnostic, training-free, and can be integrated with off-the-shelf transformer-based 3D diffusion models. Experiments are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art efficiency and quality, outperforming existing methods in both semantic alignment and perceptual quality of 3D generation.

34ae91ca9c122b7cd0bd564d4b018b88c3bcfa6f.title: Sliced Wasserstein with Random-Path Projecting Directions
34ae91ca9c122b7cd0bd564d4b018b88c3bcfa6f.research_question: How can the performance and computational efficiency of sliced Wasserstein distances be improved by designing a new, optimization-free slicing distribution for projecting directions, and how does this impact applications such as gradient flows and generative modeling?
34ae91ca9c122b7cd0bd564d4b018b88c3bcfa6f.hypothesis: A novel, optimization-free slicing distribution based on random-path projecting directions, which leverages the normalized difference between samples from the two input measures, will yield more discriminative, computationally efficient, and statistically robust sliced Wasserstein distances, thereby improving performance in tasks such as gradient flows and training of denoising diffusion generative models.
34ae91ca9c122b7cd0bd564d4b018b88c3bcfa6f.proposed_method: A new slicing distribution, termed the random-path slicing distribution (RPSD), will be constructed by sampling two random vectors from the input measures, computing their normalized difference, and introducing a continuous random perturbation to ensure full support on the unit hypersphere. This random-path projecting direction (RPD) forms the basis for the RPSD. Two new sliced Wasserstein variants will be defined: Random-Path Projection Sliced Wasserstein (RPSW), which replaces the uniform slicing distribution with the RPSD, and Importance Weighted Random-Path Projection Sliced Wasserstein (IWRPSW), which further weights multiple random projections by their projected distances. Theoretical properties, including metricity, sample complexity, and computational complexity, will be established. Monte Carlo estimation will be used for practical computation, and unbiased gradient estimators will be developed for use in optimization-based applications.
34ae91ca9c122b7cd0bd564d4b018b88c3bcfa6f.experiment_details: Experiments will include comparative analysis of RPSW and IWRPSW against existing sliced Wasserstein variants (SW, Max-SW, DSW, EBSW) in both synthetic and real-world settings. Gradient flow experiments will be conducted on toy datasets and on image datasets such as MNIST, evaluating convergence speed and final Wasserstein-2 distance using a fixed number of projections and varying concentration parameters. In generative modeling, the proposed methods will be used as loss functions for training denoising diffusion models and implicit denoising models (e.g., on CIFAR-10), with evaluation metrics including Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), number of function evaluations, and generation time. Baselines will include standard and optimization-based SW variants, and computational time will be reported. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by matching projection counts and using consistent evaluation metrics.
34ae91ca9c122b7cd0bd564d4b018b88c3bcfa6f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new, optimization-free slicing distribution for sliced Wasserstein distances based on random-path projecting directions, enabling fast, parallelizable, and discriminative sampling. The resulting RPSW and IWRPSW distances are claimed to combine the statistical and computational advantages of existing methods while avoiding their drawbacks, such as expensive optimization or biased sampling. Theoretical analysis demonstrates favorable topological, statistical, and computational properties, including sample complexity that avoids the curse of dimensionality. Empirical results are expected to show improved convergence and generative quality in gradient flows and diffusion models, establishing the proposed methods as state-of-the-art among sliced Wasserstein variants.

34b66d2e67b1266f7c1ac352d5311549f107dc2f.title: Convergence of Multi-Scale Reinforcement Q-Learning Algorithms for Mean Field Game and Control Problems
34b66d2e67b1266f7c1ac352d5311549f107dc2f.research_question: How can reinforcement learning algorithms be designed and analyzed to reliably solve mean field game (MFG) and mean field control (MFC) problems in discrete-time, finite state and action spaces, and what are the theoretical guarantees for their convergence under multi-timescale learning dynamics?
34b66d2e67b1266f7c1ac352d5311549f107dc2f.hypothesis: A unified two-timescale reinforcement learning algorithm, with appropriately chosen learning rates for value function and mean field updates, will converge to solutions of either mean field games or mean field control problems, depending on the learning rate regime. The convergence can be theoretically established under suitable regularity and Lipschitz continuity assumptions on the cost function and transition kernel.
34b66d2e67b1266f7c1ac352d5311549f107dc2f.proposed_method: A unified reinforcement learning framework will be developed, employing a two-timescale Q-learning algorithm wherein the value function and the population (mean field) distribution are updated at different rates. The method will operate in discrete time with finite state and action spaces, and will be model-free, relying only on samples from the environment. For the MFG setting, the algorithm will update a single population distribution and the value function, with the value function updated on a faster timescale than the mean field. For the MFC setting, a separate population distribution will be maintained for each state-action pair, with the mean field updated on a faster timescale than the value function. Soft-min regularization will be used for policy selection to ensure smoothness and facilitate convergence analysis. Theoretical analysis will be conducted using stochastic approximation and multi-timescale ODE methods to establish convergence properties.
34b66d2e67b1266f7c1ac352d5311549f107dc2f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in environments with finite state and action spaces, focusing on infinite-horizon settings. The algorithms will be evaluated using both synchronous (expectation-based) and asynchronous (sample-based) updates. Numerical examples will be provided to illustrate convergence behavior, with performance measured by the distance to the true MFG or MFC solutions and the stability of the learned policies and distributions. Baseline comparisons may include classical Q-learning and other model-free RL methods adapted to mean field settings. Evaluation metrics will include convergence rate, approximation error to the true equilibrium, and robustness to parameter choices such as learning rates and soft-min regularization strength.
34b66d2e67b1266f7c1ac352d5311549f107dc2f.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified, model-free reinforcement learning algorithm capable of solving both mean field game and mean field control problems by tuning the ratio of learning rates. The approach generalizes classical Q-learning to multi-agent mean field settings with rigorous convergence guarantees under multi-timescale stochastic approximation. Separate algorithmic formulations and convergence proofs are provided for both MFG and MFC cases, including the handling of multiple population distributions in MFC. The use of soft-min regularization in the policy update is leveraged for theoretical tractability and practical stability. The research advances the understanding of scalable RL methods for large-population multi-agent systems.

34c9d7bb2c75c1f29730cacf78fc79d297b03040.title: Adjoint Matching: Fine-tuning Flow and Diffusion Generative Models with Memoryless Stochastic Optimal Control
34c9d7bb2c75c1f29730cacf78fc79d297b03040.research_question: How can fine-tuning of dynamical generative models, such as Flow Matching and diffusion models, be formulated and improved using theoretically sound stochastic optimal control methods to better align generated samples with reward models, while ensuring sample diversity and generalization?
34c9d7bb2c75c1f29730cacf78fc79d297b03040.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that casting reward fine-tuning as a stochastic optimal control (SOC) problem with a specifically enforced memoryless noise schedule will enable provably unbiased convergence to the desired tilted distribution, and that a novel regression-based SOC algorithm (Adjoint Matching) will outperform existing SOC methods in stability, scalability, and sample quality.
34c9d7bb2c75c1f29730cacf78fc79d297b03040.proposed_method: The proposed approach formulates reward fine-tuning of dynamical generative models as a stochastic optimal control (SOC) problem, targeting the generation of samples from a tilted distribution defined by a reward model. A critical theoretical insight is that the fine-tuning process must enforce a memoryless noise schedule, which ensures independence between the initial noise and the generated sample, thereby eliminating value function bias and guaranteeing convergence to the desired distribution. The method introduces Adjoint Matching, a new algorithm that recasts the SOC problem as a regression task by matching the control vector field to the negative adjoint gradient of the cost functional, leveraging the continuous adjoint method for efficient gradient computation. This approach avoids high-variance importance weighting and enables stable, scalable optimization of the fine-tuned generative process. The method is applicable to both Flow Matching and diffusion models, and supports both continuous- and discrete-time formulations.
34c9d7bb2c75c1f29730cacf78fc79d297b03040.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of dynamical generative models, including Flow Matching and denoising diffusion models, applied to tasks such as text-to-image generation. The evaluation will use both standard reward models (e.g., CLIPScore) and specialized human preference models to assess alignment with human preferences. Baseline comparisons will include existing SOC algorithms, KL-regularized fine-tuning, and classifier-free guidance. Metrics for evaluation will include sample realism, text-to-sample consistency, diversity, and generalization to unseen reward models. The experimental setup will involve extensive ablations of the noise schedule, including constant, zero, and the proposed memoryless schedule, as well as comparisons of optimization stability and computational efficiency.
34c9d7bb2c75c1f29730cacf78fc79d297b03040.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretically grounded memoryless noise schedule for SOC-based fine-tuning of dynamical generative models, providing provable convergence to the tilted distribution defined by reward models. It is the first to enable reward fine-tuning for noiseless Flow Matching models. The Adjoint Matching algorithm offers a novel regression-based approach to SOC, combining the scalability of gradient-based methods with the stability of least-squares objectives, and avoids the high variance of importance sampling. The method is general, simple to implement, and applicable to a broad class of generative models, with demonstrated improvements in sample quality, consistency, and generalization.

34deaa89267283ed737f620aeb86a08a85f4386f.title: All You Need is One: Capsule Prompt Tuning with a Single Vector
34deaa89267283ed737f620aeb86a08a85f4386f.research_question: How can prompt-based learning for large language models be made more parameter-efficient and effective, particularly by improving the interaction between prompts and input sequences, and eliminating the need for extensive prompt length tuning?
34deaa89267283ed737f620aeb86a08a85f4386f.hypothesis: Integrating both instance-aware and task-aware information into a single capsule prompt per layer will enhance the effectiveness of prompt-based adaptation for large language models, acting as an 'attention anchor' that improves model performance and parameter efficiency without the need for prompt length grid search.
34deaa89267283ed737f620aeb86a08a85f4386f.proposed_method: A novel prompt-based learning framework, Capsule Prompt-Tuning (CaPT), will be developed to enhance large language model adaptation by introducing a single capsule prompt per Transformer layer. Each capsule prompt is constructed by combining a learnable task-aware vector with the mean representation of the input instance or intermediate hidden states, thus encoding both instance-aware and task-aware information. At the first layer, the capsule prompt is formed by adding the learnable vector to the mean of the input embeddings; in subsequent layers, it is formed by combining the learnable vector with the mean of the previous layer's capsule prompt and hidden state outputs. This prompt can be flexibly injected, such as by prepending as a token or adding to the hidden state, and is designed to serve as an 'attention anchor' that actively interacts with key input tokens. The approach eliminates the need for grid search over prompt length and minimizes the number of trainable parameters, focusing on quality and contextual alignment rather than prompt quantity.
34deaa89267283ed737f620aeb86a08a85f4386f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six natural language understanding tasks from the SuperGLUE benchmark, including BoolQ, CB, COPA, MRC, RTE, and WiC, with datasets split into train, validation, and test sets following established protocols. The method will be evaluated using multiple large language models (T5-Base, T5-Large, Llama-3.2-1B, Qwen-2.5-1.5B) and compared against a range of baselines, including full fine-tuning, classification head adaptation, vanilla prompt-based learning, and state-of-the-art prompt tuning methods such as P-Tuning v2, XPrompt, ResPrompt, SMoP, and others. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, F1 score, and average score across tasks. The experimental setup will avoid hyperparameter grid search for prompt length, and training efficiency will be measured in terms of parameter usage and total training time. Ablation studies will explore different capsule prompt variants, prompt lengths, and prompt depths to assess robustness and design choices.
34deaa89267283ed737f620aeb86a08a85f4386f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a nearly parameter-free prompt tuning framework that integrates both instance-aware and task-aware information into a single capsule prompt per layer, eliminating the need for laborious prompt length grid search. The method leverages the concept of an 'attention anchor,' enabling strong and context-sensitive attention interactions between the prompt and input tokens, which leads to improved performance and efficiency. The design is flexible, compact, and demonstrates superior or competitive results across multiple tasks and model architectures, offering a new perspective on efficient and effective adaptation of large language models.

34e40d61b093ea3620ef76abebb8053c8038be10.title: LLM Dataset Inference: Did you train on my dataset?
34e40d61b093ea3620ef76abebb8053c8038be10.research_question: How can it be determined whether a specific dataset was used to train a large language model, particularly in scenarios where only black-box or gray-box access to the model is available, and where traditional membership inference attacks are unreliable?
34e40d61b093ea3620ef76abebb8053c8038be10.hypothesis: Aggregating and selectively combining multiple membership inference attacks (MIAs) into a statistical framework enables accurate and robust detection of whether a dataset was used to train a large language model, even when individual MIAs are unreliable and model access is limited.
34e40d61b093ea3620ef76abebb8053c8038be10.proposed_method: A new dataset inference framework is proposed for large language models (LLMs), which operates in four stages. First, the suspected dataset and a private validation set (both assumed IID and non-overlapping) are split into two partitions each. In the feature aggregation stage, both sets are passed through the LLM and a suite of diverse MIAs is applied to extract feature vectors for each example. Next, a linear regression model is trained on one partition to learn the correlation between MIA-derived features and dataset membership, with outlier values normalized to prevent skewed learning. In the final stage, the trained regressor is used to score the held-out partition, and a statistical t-test is performed on the resulting scores to determine whether the suspect dataset was likely used in training. The framework includes procedures for combining dependent p-values from multiple random splits and for robust feature pre-processing.
34e40d61b093ea3620ef76abebb8053c8038be10.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the Pythia suite of LLMs (410M, 1.4B, 6.9B, and 12B parameters) trained on the Pile dataset, which contains 20 domain-specific subsets with known train and validation splits. For each subset, 1000 examples from both train and validation sets are used to test dataset inference, while false positive rates are assessed by splitting validation sets into two. A total of 52 different MIAs, including thresholding, Min-k% Prob, perturbation-based, DetectGPT, reference model-based, and zlib ratio methods, are aggregated as features. Evaluation metrics include p-values from t-tests distinguishing train from validation splits, with a significance threshold of 0.1 and analysis of false positives. The impact of model size, data duplication, number of queries, and feature selection/pre-processing is systematically studied.
34e40d61b093ea3620ef76abebb8053c8038be10.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first comprehensive dataset inference framework for LLMs that aggregates multiple MIAs and applies statistical testing to robustly attribute training data at the dataset level, rather than at the individual instance level. This method addresses the confounding effects of distribution shift that undermine traditional MIAs, and demonstrates reliable, statistically significant detection of training datasets without false positives, even in large-scale, real-world LLM settings. The framework is operationalizable under realistic access assumptions and provides practical tools for copyright and data attribution disputes.

34efdeaf0a78d6906b4da7335afc7182df11f639.title: QuRating: Selecting High-Quality Data for Training Language Models
34efdeaf0a78d6906b4da7335afc7182df11f639.research_question: How can high-quality data be effectively selected for training language models to improve their performance, particularly under resource constraints, and what abstract qualities of text are most valuable for this selection?
34efdeaf0a78d6906b4da7335afc7182df11f639.hypothesis: Language models trained on data selected according to human-aligned quality criteria—such as writing style, required expertise, facts & trivia, and educational value—will outperform models trained on data selected by traditional heuristics or uniform sampling, both in perplexity and in-context learning performance.
34efdeaf0a78d6906b4da7335afc7182df11f639.proposed_method: A novel data selection framework, QuRating, will be developed to capture human intuitions of data quality for language model pre-training. The approach involves: (1) defining four qualitative criteria—writing style, required expertise, facts & trivia, and educational value—and designing prompts for each; (2) using a large language model (GPT-3.5-turbo) to make pairwise judgments between text samples for each criterion, collecting hundreds of thousands of such judgments; (3) training a QuRater model (a fine-tuned Sheared-Llama-1.3B) to translate these pairwise judgments into scalar quality ratings using the Bradley-Terry model; (4) annotating a large pre-training corpus (260B tokens from SlimPajama) with these quality ratings; (5) sampling subsets of data for language model training according to these ratings, using a temperature parameter to balance quality and diversity; and (6) optionally constructing training curricula by ordering data according to quality ratings.
34efdeaf0a78d6906b4da7335afc7182df11f639.experiment_details: Experiments will involve annotating a 260B-token corpus with quality ratings for each criterion and selecting 30B-token subsets for training 1.3B-parameter language models from scratch. Baselines will include uniform random sampling, perplexity filtering, and importance resampling (DSIR) based on domain resemblance (e.g., Wikipedia, Books). Evaluation will be conducted on held-out validation perplexity and in-context learning (ICL) performance across 10 diverse tasks (reading comprehension, commonsense reasoning, and knowledge-intensive tasks), using the lm-evaluation-harness. Instruction-following capabilities will be assessed via supervised fine-tuning on ShareGPT data and judged with GPT-4. Additional analyses will examine the distribution and social biases of the selected data using the AboutMe dataset.
34efdeaf0a78d6906b4da7335afc7182df11f639.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a scalable, LLM-based framework for quantifying and leveraging human-aligned abstract qualities of text for data selection, moving beyond traditional heuristics and domain proxies. It demonstrates that pairwise LLM judgments can be reliably translated into fine-grained quality ratings, which, when used for data selection and curriculum construction, yield significant improvements in both perplexity and in-context learning performance. The approach also enables detailed analysis of the impact of data selection on social and topical biases, and provides a public resource (QuRatedPajama) for further research in efficient and fair language model training.

350ddadbdc5c64c12d01ac2a5b9a2d8a9881d492.title: Stop Summation: Min-Form Credit Assignment Is All Process Reward Model Needs for Reasoning
350ddadbdc5c64c12d01ac2a5b9a2d8a9881d492.research_question: How can process reward models be leveraged to improve reinforcement fine-tuning of large language models for reasoning tasks, while avoiding reward hacking and training collapse?
350ddadbdc5c64c12d01ac2a5b9a2d8a9881d492.hypothesis: Min-form credit assignment, which defines the value function as the minimum of future process rewards, will significantly reduce reward hacking in reinforcement fine-tuning of large language models using process reward models, and will enable efficient and stable training that matches or surpasses traditional verifiable reward-based approaches, especially when supplemented with a small proportion of ground-truth signals.
350ddadbdc5c64c12d01ac2a5b9a2d8a9881d492.proposed_method: A new reinforcement learning framework, Process sUpervised Reinforcement lEarning (PURE), is proposed to fine-tune large language models using process reward models (PRMs). The key innovation is the adoption of a min-form credit assignment, where the value function at each step is defined as the minimum process reward among all future steps, rather than the traditional gamma-discounted sum. This approach is implemented by transforming process rewards in each trajectory using a softmin function, assigning higher weights to lower rewards, and then mapping these to token-level rewards for compatibility with standard policy gradient algorithms such as PPO. The framework also supports integration of sparse verifiable rewards, allowing for mixed reward signals during training. Advantage estimation is performed using robust estimators (e.g., RLOO), and token-level baselines are used to avoid bias toward shorter or degenerate responses.
350ddadbdc5c64c12d01ac2a5b9a2d8a9881d492.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three base models: Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen2.5-Math-7B, and Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B. The PRM is trained on the PRM800K dataset, a large human-annotated dataset evaluating stepwise correctness, and evaluated using Best-of-N (BoN) on GSM8K and MATH, ProcessBench, and PRMBench. Reinforcement fine-tuning is performed using three reward configurations: process rewards only, verifiable rewards only, and a combination of both (with verifiable rewards provided for 10% of training problems). Baselines include state-of-the-art RFT methods such as Eurus-2-7B-PRIME, SimpleRL-Zoo, and Qwen2.5-7B-DPO-Zero. Evaluation metrics include pass@1 accuracy on five competition-level math benchmarks (AIME24, AMC23, MATH500, MinervaMath, OlympiadBench), as well as process reward aggregation, training stability, and reward hacking analysis. Training hyperparameters are carefully controlled, and training dynamics are monitored for collapse and reward hacking.
350ddadbdc5c64c12d01ac2a5b9a2d8a9881d492.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces min-form credit assignment for reinforcement fine-tuning with process reward models, which fundamentally changes the value function from a sum to a minimum over future rewards. This approach is claimed to drastically reduce reward hacking, stabilize training, and allow PRM-based fine-tuning to achieve comparable or superior reasoning performance to verifiable reward-based methods with much greater efficiency. The method is simple to implement, requiring only a transformation of process rewards, and supports seamless integration of dense and sparse reward signals. Extensive analysis of reward hacking cases and training collapse is provided, and the approach is demonstrated to outperform or match state-of-the-art baselines on challenging mathematical reasoning benchmarks.

351a03eeeee64cba5815484eedbbc21eeddbe050.title: Brain network science modelling of sparse neural networks enables Transformers and LLMs to perform as fully connected
351a03eeeee64cba5815484eedbbc21eeddbe050.research_question: How can brain-inspired network science principles be leveraged to enable highly sparse artificial neural networks, including Transformers and large language models, to achieve or surpass the performance of fully connected architectures while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements?
351a03eeeee64cba5815484eedbbc21eeddbe050.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that integrating brain-inspired sparse connectivity initialization, efficient topology-driven dynamic sparse training, and adaptive density decay strategies will allow artificial neural networks to maintain or exceed the performance of their fully connected counterparts, even at extreme sparsity levels, across a range of tasks and architectures.
351a03eeeee64cba5815484eedbbc21eeddbe050.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a novel framework for dynamic sparse training (DST) in artificial neural networks, inspired by brain network science. First, a Bipartite Receptive Field (BRF) model is developed to initialize sparse connectivity in a manner analogous to biological receptive fields, allowing control over spatially dependent randomness and preserving desired degree distributions. Next, a matrix multiplication-based, GPU-friendly approximation of the Cannistraci-Hebb (CH) link predictor is implemented, reducing the computational complexity of link regrowth from O(N·d^3) to O(N^3), thus enabling scalability to large models. The Cannistraci-Hebb Training soft rule (CHTs) is then introduced, employing multinomial soft sampling for both link removal and regrowth, balancing exploration and exploitation of network topology and mitigating the risk of epitopological local minima. Additionally, a sigmoid-based gradual density decay strategy (CHTss) is incorporated to smoothly reduce network density during training, improving stability and performance. The overall method is designed to be gradient-free for regrowth, robust to low-precision training, and applicable to both MLPs and Transformer architectures.
351a03eeeee64cba5815484eedbbc21eeddbe050.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of tasks and architectures. For image classification, MLPs will be evaluated on MNIST, FashionMNIST, EMNIST, and CIFAR10 datasets, with all layers except the final output layer sparsified. For machine translation, Transformer models will be trained and evaluated on Multi30k en-de, IWSLT14 en-de, and WMT17 en-de datasets, using BLEU scores as the primary metric. Language modeling experiments will utilize the LLaMA model family (60M, 130M, 1B parameters) on the OpenWebText dataset, with validation perplexity as the metric, and zero-shot evaluation on GLUE and SuperGLUE benchmarks. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art DST methods such as SET, RigL, MEST, GMP, and GraNet, with both fixed sparsity and density decay variants. Key experimental setups include varying sparsity levels (as low as 1% connectivity), ablation studies on initialization and removal/regrowth strategies, and robustness tests under low-precision (bfloat16) training.
351a03eeeee64cba5815484eedbbc21eeddbe050.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces several innovations: (1) the first brain-inspired bipartite receptive field (BRF) model for sparse neural network initialization, (2) a GPU-efficient, matrix-based approximation of the Cannistraci-Hebb link predictor for scalable topology-driven regrowth, (3) a soft multinomial sampling rule for both link removal and regrowth that balances exploration and exploitation and avoids epitopological local minima, and (4) a sigmoid-based gradual density decay schedule that improves training stability and performance. Collectively, these contributions enable ultra-sparse neural networks to match or surpass the performance of fully connected models across multiple domains, while also offering significant computational and memory savings.

352f26798b07160bf10d87cf0fd67187c5a0c432.title: End-to-End Diffusion Latent Optimization Improves Classifier Guidance
352f26798b07160bf10d87cf0fd67187c5a0c432.research_question: How can classifier guidance for diffusion models be improved to provide more precise, flexible, and semantically meaningful control over image generation and editing, without requiring retraining of classifiers or relying on memory-intensive approximations?
352f26798b07160bf10d87cf0fd67187c5a0c432.hypothesis: Directly optimizing diffusion latents with respect to a model-based loss on the final generated image, using an invertible diffusion process, will enable more accurate and flexible classifier guidance compared to one-step approximations or noise-aware classifier approaches.
352f26798b07160bf10d87cf0fd67187c5a0c432.proposed_method: A new method, Direct Optimization Of Diffusion Latents (DOODL), is proposed to optimize the initial noise vectors of a diffusion model with respect to a differentiable loss computed on the final generated image. This approach leverages an invertible diffusion process (EDICT) that allows efficient backpropagation through the entire diffusion chain with constant memory cost, enabling gradients to be computed with respect to the true output rather than an approximation. The optimization is performed iteratively, using momentum and multi-crop data augmentation, and includes normalization and regularization steps to maintain latent distribution and prevent drift. The method is designed to be plug-and-play, allowing any differentiable loss function (e.g., from CLIP, fine-grained classifiers, or aesthetic scorers) to guide the generation process without retraining or modifying the diffusion model or classifier.
352f26798b07160bf10d87cf0fd67187c5a0c432.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across several guidance scenarios: (1) text-to-image generation using CLIP-based classifier guidance, evaluated on the DrawBench benchmark with both automatic (CLIP score) and human evaluation; (2) vocabulary expansion using fine-grained visual classifiers trained on datasets such as CUB-200, Stanford Dogs, and FGVC-Aircraft, with performance measured by FID between generated and real images; (3) aesthetic improvement, where real images are inverted to latents and optimized for higher or lower aesthetic scores using a CLIP-based aesthetic predictor, evaluated by human raters; and (4) visual personalization, where a specific entity is inserted into generated images using image-based CLIP guidance, with success measured by human evaluation. Baselines include standard one-step classifier guidance and vanilla Stable Diffusion generations. Multiple seeds, classifier models, and optimization hyperparameters will be tested, and both quantitative and qualitative results will be reported.
352f26798b07160bf10d87cf0fd67187c5a0c432.novelty_claims: The proposed method enables exact, memory-efficient, and flexible classifier guidance for diffusion models by directly optimizing diffusion latents with respect to any differentiable loss on the final output. This approach eliminates the need for retraining noise-aware classifiers or relying on one-step denoising approximations, and allows plug-and-play use of pretrained recognition models for a wide range of guidance signals. Novel capabilities demonstrated include vocabulary expansion for rare concepts, on-the-fly visual personalization without model retraining, and direct optimization for aesthetic improvement of both generated and real images.

3551794dcd593120a926f8529bc6492a2e0ca654.title: Stochastic Halpern iteration in normed spaces and applications to reinforcement learning
3551794dcd593120a926f8529bc6492a2e0ca654.research_question: What are the oracle complexity bounds for stochastic fixed-point iterations, specifically the stochastic Halpern iteration with minibatching, when approximating fixed-points of nonexpansive and contractive operators in general normed finite-dimensional spaces, and how can these methods be applied to reinforcement learning problems such as average and discounted reward Markov Decision Processes (MDPs)?
3551794dcd593120a926f8529bc6492a2e0ca654.hypothesis: The stochastic Halpern iteration with an appropriately designed minibatch variance reduction strategy achieves improved oracle complexity bounds for finding approximate fixed-points of nonexpansive and contractive operators in general normed spaces, and these improvements can be leveraged to design efficient, model-free reinforcement learning algorithms for both average and discounted reward MDPs.
3551794dcd593120a926f8529bc6492a2e0ca654.proposed_method: A stochastic variant of the Halpern iteration is developed, where access to the underlying operator is only available through a stochastic oracle with unbiased estimates and bounded variance. The method operates in a general normed finite-dimensional space and incorporates a minibatch strategy at each iteration to reduce the variance of the stochastic oracle's output. Each iteration computes a minibatch average of the oracle outputs at the current iterate, then updates the iterate using a convex combination of the initial point and the minibatch-averaged oracle output, with a nondecreasing stepsize sequence approaching 1. The minibatch size is increased over time to ensure that the variance of the estimator decreases sufficiently fast, enabling tight control over the fixed-point residual or distance to the true fixed-point. The methodology is extended to both nonexpansive and contractive operators, with explicit stepsize and minibatch schedules tailored to each case, and is further adapted to reinforcement learning settings by framing the Bellman operator as the target operator in MDPs.
3551794dcd593120a926f8529bc6492a2e0ca654.experiment_details: Experiments are proposed to evaluate the oracle complexity and convergence rates of the stochastic Halpern iteration with minibatching on both synthetic fixed-point problems and reinforcement learning tasks. For the RL application, model-free algorithms will be developed for average and discounted reward MDPs, assuming access to a generative model for state-action transitions. The evaluation will include measuring the number of oracle (sample) calls required to achieve a specified tolerance in fixed-point residual or Bellman error, comparing against established baselines such as stochastic Krasnoselskii-Mann iteration and other model-free RL algorithms. Metrics will include expected fixed-point residual, sample complexity to reach ε-accuracy, and, for MDPs, the Bellman error and policy optimality gap. Experiments will be conducted in both general normed spaces and standard RL benchmarks, with and without prior knowledge of system parameters.
3551794dcd593120a926f8529bc6492a2e0ca654.novelty_claims: The proposed approach establishes improved oracle complexity bounds for stochastic fixed-point iterations in general normed spaces, achieving O~(ε^{-5}) for nonexpansive operators and O(ε^{-2}(1-γ)^{-3}) for contractive operators, surpassing previous results for stochastic Krasnoselskii-Mann iteration. A matching lower bound of Ω(ε^{-3}) is provided, covering all averaged iterations with minibatching. The method is the first to provide general complexity results in the non-Euclidean setting without requiring monotonicity or additional structure on the operator. The application to reinforcement learning yields new model-free algorithms for average and discounted reward MDPs that do not require prior parameter knowledge, with sample complexity guarantees that match or improve upon existing model-free methods, and without relying on structural properties such as monotonicity of the Bellman operator.

3558d72ef6a386b3b5341789eb0f3f431cc73d93.title: 6D-Diff: A Keypoint Diffusion Framework for 6D Object Pose Estimation
3558d72ef6a386b3b5341789eb0f3f431cc73d93.research_question: How can the challenges of noise and indeterminacy in 6D object pose estimation from single RGB images be effectively addressed to improve accuracy, particularly in the presence of occlusions and cluttered backgrounds?
3558d72ef6a386b3b5341789eb0f3f431cc73d93.hypothesis: Formulating 2D keypoint detection as a reverse diffusion (denoising) process, starting from a distribution initialized by keypoint heatmaps and modeled with a Mixture-of-Cauchy (MoC) distribution, and conditioning the process on object appearance features, will yield more accurate 6D object pose estimation than existing methods.
3558d72ef6a386b3b5341789eb0f3f431cc73d93.proposed_method: A novel diffusion-based framework, 6D-Diff, is introduced for 6D object pose estimation. The method first extracts an intermediate representation in the form of 2D keypoint heatmaps from the input image, using a keypoint distribution initializer based on a ResNet-34 backbone. The initial distribution of keypoint coordinates is modeled using a Mixture-of-Cauchy (MoC) distribution, which effectively captures the complex and irregular distributions present in noisy heatmaps. The forward process diffuses the ground-truth keypoint coordinates towards this MoC-modeled distribution, generating intermediate supervision signals. The reverse process, implemented as a transformer-based diffusion model, is trained to denoise from the MoC-initialized distribution back to a determinate keypoint distribution, conditioned on both step embeddings and object appearance features extracted from the image. The final 2D keypoint predictions are combined with pre-selected 3D keypoints from the object CAD model to solve for the 6D pose using a Perspective-n-Point (PnP) algorithm.
3558d72ef6a386b3b5341789eb0f3f431cc73d93.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the challenging LM-O and YCB-V datasets, which feature significant occlusions and cluttered backgrounds. The training set will include both real and physically-based rendered (pbr) images, and the evaluation will use standard metrics such as ADD(-S), AUC of ADD-S, and AUC of ADD(-S), with a 10% model diameter threshold for correctness. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art RGB-based 6D pose estimation methods such as PVNet, GDR-Net, ZebraPose, CheckerPose, and others. The experimental setup includes using an off-the-shelf object detector (e.g., Faster RCNN) for ROI extraction, initializing distributions with heatmaps, and employing a transformer encoder-decoder diffusion model with MoC-based forward diffusion. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the denoising process, the MoC modeling, and the use of object appearance features.
3558d72ef6a386b3b5341789eb0f3f431cc73d93.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a new perspective by formulating 2D-3D correspondence estimation for 6D object pose as a reverse diffusion process, leveraging a Mixture-of-Cauchy-based forward diffusion to better model complex keypoint distributions. The method uniquely conditions the denoising process on object appearance features, enabling more robust and accurate pose estimation under challenging conditions. Extensive experiments are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art performance and validate the effectiveness of the denoising approach and MoC-based modeling.

355e7b4ec396fef5c0ae1e12b0fd2d8130b21dc2.title: Let us Build Bridges: Understanding and Extending Diffusion Generative Models
355e7b4ec396fef5c0ae1e12b0fd2d8130b21dc2.research_question: How can diffusion generative models be conceptually unified, theoretically analyzed, and extended to efficiently generate data from arbitrary domains, including discrete, structured, and non-Euclidean spaces?
355e7b4ec396fef5c0ae1e12b0fd2d8130b21dc2.hypothesis: By reinterpreting diffusion generative models as latent variable models with imputed diffusion bridge trajectories and optimizing via maximum likelihood estimation, it is possible to develop a unified framework that enables both theoretical error analysis and practical extensions to diverse data domains, including discrete and constrained spaces.
355e7b4ec396fef5c0ae1e12b0fd2d8130b21dc2.proposed_method: The proposed approach formulates diffusion generative models as latent variable models where the unobserved diffusion trajectories are treated as latent variables. The learning process is decomposed into two primary components: (1) constructing imputation mechanisms to generate latent trajectories (x-bridges) conditioned on observed data, and (2) specifying and training diffusion models (Ω-bridges) that guarantee the generated samples reside within the desired domain. The method leverages classical maximum likelihood estimation, where latent trajectories are imputed from an auxiliary distribution, and the model parameters are optimized to minimize the KL divergence between the model and the imputed trajectory distribution. The framework systematically constructs both x-bridges and Ω-bridges using tools such as time-reversal, h-transform, and mixtures of bridges, enabling decoupling of initialization and dynamics, and supporting both continuous and discrete domains. The approach also introduces a Markovization procedure to ensure the learned model matches the fixed-time marginals of the imputation process, even when the latter is non-Markov.
355e7b4ec396fef5c0ae1e12b0fd2d8130b21dc2.experiment_details: Experiments are designed to evaluate the proposed framework on a variety of data types, including integer-valued 3D point clouds, categorical semantic segmentation maps, and both discrete and continuous versions of CIFAR10 images. For point cloud generation, the method is tested on the ShapeNet chair dataset, comparing variants that generate in continuous (R^d) and integer grid domains against the PointCloudDiffusion (PCD) baseline. Neural network architectures are kept consistent with baselines for fair comparison. Standard evaluation metrics such as Minimum Matching Distance (MMD), Coverage Score (COV), and 1-Nearest Neighbor Accuracy (1-NNA) using Chamfer Distance are employed. For segmentation maps, the framework is evaluated on the ability to generate samples with categorical constraints, and qualitative results are compared to real data. The experimental setup also investigates the efficiency of the method in terms of sample quality and speed with reduced diffusion steps.
355e7b4ec396fef5c0ae1e12b0fd2d8130b21dc2.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified and theoretically grounded framework for diffusion generative models that systematically constructs and analyzes diffusion bridges for both continuous and discrete domains. It provides the first theoretical error analysis for learning diffusion models, quantifying both statistical and time-discretization errors. The approach enables a simple and universal method for generative modeling on arbitrary domains, including mixed, bounded, and categorical spaces, by decoupling the design of bridge dynamics and initialization. The method demonstrates superior performance on discrete data generation tasks and achieves efficient generation with fewer diffusion steps, addressing key limitations of existing diffusion models.
