3564562b1fd9ed8abf9aaeef0afd1d759c5e0d55.title: SoFar: Language-Grounded Orientation Bridges Spatial Reasoning and Object Manipulation
3564562b1fd9ed8abf9aaeef0afd1d759c5e0d55.research_question: How can language-grounded representations of object orientation be developed to bridge spatial reasoning and object manipulation, enabling robots to perform 6-DoF manipulation and reasoning tasks in open-world settings?
3564562b1fd9ed8abf9aaeef0afd1d759c5e0d55.hypothesis: Semantic orientation, defined as a language-grounded, reference-frame-free representation of object orientation, can enable more effective and generalizable spatial reasoning and manipulation by robots, outperforming traditional template-based orientation representations.
3564562b1fd9ed8abf9aaeef0afd1d759c5e0d55.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed that introduces the concept of semantic orientation, representing object orientations as unit vectors grounded in natural language descriptions (e.g., 'handle direction', 'plug-in direction'). To support this, a large-scale dataset, OrienText300K, will be constructed by annotating over 350,000 3D object models with diverse language-guided orientation labels, using automated filtering and annotation via GPT-4o and human validation. The core model, PointSO, will be a cross-modal 3D Transformer architecture that fuses 3D point cloud data and language embeddings (from CLIP) through token-wise addition at each layer, predicting the semantic orientation vector for a given object and language prompt. This model will be integrated into a comprehensive system (SOFAR) that combines PointSO with foundation models for segmentation (SAM, Florence-2), building a 6-DoF scene graph and enabling chain-of-thought spatial reasoning and manipulation planning in response to language instructions.
3564562b1fd9ed8abf9aaeef0afd1d759c5e0d55.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both simulated and real-world robotic manipulation tasks. The OrienText300K dataset will be used for training and validation of semantic orientation prediction, with accuracy measured at various angular thresholds and robustness tested under input corruptions (e.g., single-view, noise, random rotations). The SOFAR system will be evaluated on benchmarks such as Open6DOR V1/V2 (for 6-DoF rearrangement), SimplerEnv (for simulated manipulation), and a newly proposed 6-DoF SpatialBench (for spatial VQA), comparing against state-of-the-art VLMs and robot learning models. Metrics will include success rates in manipulation tasks, spatial reasoning accuracy, planning time, and generalization across embodiments and environments. Baselines will include models such as RT-1-X, RT-2-X, Octo, OpenVLA, RoboVLM, and others, with both zero-shot and in-domain training scenarios.
3564562b1fd9ed8abf9aaeef0afd1d759c5e0d55.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the concept of semantic orientation as a language-grounded, template-free representation for object orientation, enabling open-vocabulary and generalizable spatial reasoning. The OrienText300K dataset is claimed to be the largest and most diverse resource for 3D object orientation annotated with natural language. The PointSO model presents a novel cross-modal 3D Transformer architecture for predicting semantic orientations from point clouds and language. The SOFAR system is proposed as the first integrated framework to bridge spatial reasoning and manipulation via semantic orientation, achieving state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks and demonstrating strong zero-shot generalization across tasks, embodiments, and environments.

358b96ce1653ec489e7bf565c0f1afad81e502d0.title: BitNet: Scaling 1-bit Transformers for Large Language Models
358b96ce1653ec489e7bf565c0f1afad81e502d0.research_question: How can large language models be made more efficient in terms of memory and energy consumption without significantly sacrificing performance, particularly through extreme quantization techniques such as 1-bit weight representations?
358b96ce1653ec489e7bf565c0f1afad81e502d0.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a transformer-based large language model architecture utilizing 1-bit weights and quantized activations, trained in a quantization-aware manner from scratch, can achieve competitive performance to full-precision and state-of-the-art quantized models while drastically reducing memory and energy requirements.
358b96ce1653ec489e7bf565c0f1afad81e502d0.proposed_method: A novel transformer architecture, termed BitNet, will be developed in which all linear projection layers are replaced with a custom BitLinear module. BitLinear binarizes weights to +1 or -1 using a sign function after zero-mean centralization and applies a learned scaling factor to minimize quantization error. Activations are quantized to 8 bits using an absmax quantization scheme, with group-wise quantization and normalization to enable efficient model parallelism. Training will employ the straight-through estimator to enable backpropagation through non-differentiable quantization functions, and mixed-precision training will be used, maintaining high-precision optimizer states and gradients for stability. Sub-layer normalization (SubLN) will be applied before quantization to preserve variance and ensure stable training dynamics.
358b96ce1653ec489e7bf565c0f1afad81e502d0.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training a series of autoregressive language models with parameter counts ranging from 125M to 30B on large-scale English corpora including Pile, Common Crawl, RealNews, and CC-Stories, using a 16K vocabulary. Baselines will include FP16 Transformers and state-of-the-art post-training quantization methods such as Absmax, SmoothQuant, GPTQ, and QuIP at various bit-widths. Evaluation will be conducted using language modeling perplexity and zero-shot/few-shot accuracy on downstream tasks such as Hellaswag, Winogrande, Winograd, and Storycloze. Additional analyses will include scaling law studies, energy consumption estimation (using established hardware energy models), and ablation studies on quantization and normalization techniques.
358b96ce1653ec489e7bf565c0f1afad81e502d0.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first scalable and stable 1-bit transformer architecture for large language models, enabling quantization-aware training from scratch at extreme low precision. The BitLinear module and group-wise quantization/normalization enable efficient model parallelism without additional communication overhead. The approach demonstrates that 1-bit models can follow scaling laws akin to full-precision transformers, supporting effective scaling to larger models. Significant reductions in memory footprint and energy consumption are claimed, with competitive or superior performance to both full-precision and state-of-the-art quantized baselines, especially at low bit-widths.

35ab93f41115e860bee5e202b71061addfd0fd5d.title: Learning to (Learn at Test Time): RNNs with Expressive Hidden States
35ab93f41115e860bee5e202b71061addfd0fd5d.research_question: How can sequence modeling layers be designed to achieve both linear computational complexity and high expressive power in their hidden states, particularly for long-context tasks?
35ab93f41115e860bee5e202b71061addfd0fd5d.hypothesis: Instantiating the hidden state of RNN-like sequence modeling layers as a parametric machine learning model, and updating it via self-supervised learning steps even at test time, enables these layers to maintain linear complexity while matching or exceeding the expressive power of self-attention for long-context modeling.
35ab93f41115e860bee5e202b71061addfd0fd5d.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed in which the hidden state of a recurrent sequence modeling layer is itself a machine learning model (such as a linear model or a small neural network). The update rule for the hidden state is defined as a step of gradient descent on a self-supervised loss, applied online as new tokens are processed—even during test time. Two concrete instantiations are developed: TTT-Linear (where the hidden state is a linear model) and TTT-MLP (where the hidden state is a two-layer MLP). The self-supervised loss is formulated as a multi-view reconstruction task, with learnable linear projections for training, label, and test views, and the update is performed via mini-batch gradient descent for efficiency. A dual-form computation is introduced to exploit hardware parallelism, enabling fast training and inference on modern accelerators.
35ab93f41115e860bee5e202b71061addfd0fd5d.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted at model scales ranging from 125M to 1.3B parameters. The proposed TTT-Linear and TTT-MLP layers are evaluated on The Pile dataset, following the evaluation protocol of Kaplan et al., with context lengths up to 32k tokens. Baselines include a strong Transformer and Mamba, a modern RNN. Evaluation metrics include perplexity as a function of context length and parameter count, as well as wall-clock efficiency. All methods are trained with matched computational budgets (FLOPs), and ablations are performed on mini-batch size and efficiency optimizations.
35ab93f41115e860bee5e202b71061addfd0fd5d.novelty_claims: The framework introduces the concept of making the hidden state of a sequence modeling layer a learnable model updated by self-supervised learning at test time, enabling expressive compression of long contexts with linear complexity. The approach generalizes existing RNN and attention mechanisms, and the dual-form computation enables practical efficiency on modern hardware. Empirical results demonstrate that TTT-Linear and TTT-MLP can continue to reduce perplexity with increasing context, similar to Transformers and unlike prior RNNs, marking a significant step towards efficient and expressive long-context modeling.

35aba190f28b5c39df333c06ca21f46bd4845eba.title: Sigmoid Loss for Language Image Pre-Training
35aba190f28b5c39df333c06ca21f46bd4845eba.research_question: How can language-image pre-training be made more efficient and effective, particularly in terms of memory usage, batch size scalability, and robustness to data noise, without sacrificing model performance on downstream tasks such as zero-shot classification and cross-modal retrieval?
35aba190f28b5c39df333c06ca21f46bd4845eba.hypothesis: A pairwise sigmoid loss, applied to language-image pre-training, will enable more memory-efficient training, allow for larger and more flexible batch sizes, and improve robustness to data noise, while achieving equal or superior performance compared to traditional softmax-based contrastive losses.
35aba190f28b5c39df333c06ca21f46bd4845eba.proposed_method: A novel pairwise sigmoid loss will be introduced for language-image pre-training, replacing the standard softmax-based contrastive loss. This loss operates independently on each image-text pair, treating the task as a binary classification problem for each pair, with positive labels for matching pairs and negative labels for mismatched pairs. The method incorporates a learnable temperature and bias term, initialized to ensure stable optimization and prevent early over-correction. To address scalability and efficiency, a chunked implementation will be developed that distributes computation across devices, reducing memory requirements from quadratic to linear in batch size per device. The approach will be evaluated in two settings: SigLiT (using precomputed image embeddings and training a text tower) and SigLIP (training both image and text encoders end-to-end), with additional modifications for multilingual training and large vocabulary bottlenecking.
35aba190f28b5c39df333c06ca21f46bd4845eba.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using large-scale image-text datasets such as LiT and WebLI, including both English-only and multilingual (over 100 languages) settings. The models will be trained on various configurations of TPU-v4 chips, with batch sizes ranging from 512 up to 1 million, to systematically study the impact of batch size on performance. Baselines will include softmax-based contrastive losses as used in CLIP, ALIGN, and LiT. Evaluation metrics will include zero-shot classification accuracy on ImageNet and other benchmarks (e.g., ObjectNet, ImageNet-v2, ImageNet ReaL), as well as cross-modal retrieval recall on MSCOCO and XM3600 (for multilingual tasks). Additional ablation studies will examine the effect of batch composition, positive-to-negative ratio, learned bias initialization, and robustness to synthetic data noise. Comparisons will be made against state-of-the-art public models such as CLIP, OpenCLIP, EVA-CLIP, and CLIPA-v2.
35aba190f28b5c39df333c06ca21f46bd4845eba.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a memory- and compute-efficient pairwise sigmoid loss for language-image pre-training, enabling the use of much larger batch sizes on limited hardware resources. The approach decouples batch size from the loss normalization, allowing for flexible scaling and efficient distributed training. The method demonstrates improved robustness to data noise and achieves state-of-the-art results on both zero-shot classification and cross-modal retrieval tasks, outperforming existing models with comparable or fewer resources. Additional contributions include a scalable bottlenecked token embedding for large multilingual vocabularies and a detailed analysis of batch size effects, negative sampling strategies, and optimization stability in large-batch regimes.

35b142ea69598e6241f0011312128031df55895c.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
35b142ea69598e6241f0011312128031df55895c.research_question: How can the mathematical reasoning capabilities of open language models be advanced to approach or surpass the performance of leading proprietary models, while maintaining efficiency and broad applicability across languages and mathematical domains?
35b142ea69598e6241f0011312128031df55895c.hypothesis: Pre-training language models on a large-scale, high-quality, multilingual mathematical corpus, combined with code data and enhanced by a novel reinforcement learning algorithm, will significantly improve mathematical reasoning abilities and general reasoning skills, outperforming existing open-source models and approaching the capabilities of closed-source state-of-the-art models.
35b142ea69598e6241f0011312128031df55895c.proposed_method: A domain-specific language model will be developed by initializing from a code-pretrained base and then continually pre-training on a newly constructed, large-scale mathematical corpus (DeepSeekMath Corpus) containing 120B math-related tokens sourced and filtered from Common Crawl and other web resources using an iterative, classifier-based pipeline. The model will further incorporate code, arXiv, and general natural language data to enhance both mathematical and general reasoning abilities. After pre-training, supervised instruction tuning will be performed using a curated dataset of English and Chinese mathematical problems, annotated with chain-of-thought, program-of-thought, and tool-integrated solutions. Finally, a novel reinforcement learning algorithm, Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), will be applied to optimize instruction-following and mathematical reasoning, reducing resource requirements compared to traditional PPO by estimating baselines from group scores instead of a critic model.
35b142ea69598e6241f0011312128031df55895c.experiment_details: Experiments will include comprehensive evaluations on a suite of English and Chinese mathematical reasoning benchmarks, such as GSM8K, MATH, SAT, OCW Courses, MMLU-STEM, MGSM-zh, CMATH, Gaokao-MathCloze, and Gaokao-MathQA, covering grade-school to college-level problems. Additional assessments will be conducted on formal mathematics (miniF2F with Isabelle), general language understanding (MMLU), reasoning (BBH), and coding benchmarks (HumanEval, MBPP). Baselines will include leading open-source models (e.g., Mistral 7B, Llemma 34B) and closed-source models (e.g., Minerva 540B, GPT-4, Gemini-Ultra). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on problem-solving tasks, pass rates for code generation, and formal proof success rates. Both few-shot and zero-shot prompting will be used, and ablation studies will analyze the impact of data composition, instruction tuning, and reinforcement learning strategies.
35b142ea69598e6241f0011312128031df55895c.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the largest and highest-quality multilingual mathematical corpus to date for pre-training, demonstrating that smaller models can achieve strong mathematical reasoning through data quality and targeted training. The iterative data selection and decontamination pipeline ensures minimal benchmark contamination and broad language coverage. A novel reinforcement learning algorithm, GRPO, is proposed to enhance mathematical reasoning while reducing training resource requirements. The unified paradigm for understanding and comparing RL-based fine-tuning methods is also developed, providing insights into the effectiveness of reinforcement learning for instruction-tuned language models.

35b3979d5f824009a38f93604ef05a0d7ed09395.title: A comprehensive and FAIR comparison between MLP and KAN representations for differential equations and operator networks
35b3979d5f824009a38f93604ef05a0d7ed09395.research_question: How do Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) and their variants compare to Multilayer Perceptrons (MLPs) in representing solutions to differential equations and operator learning tasks within scientific machine learning, and what are the implications for accuracy, efficiency, robustness, and learning dynamics?
35b3979d5f824009a38f93604ef05a0d7ed09395.hypothesis: KAN-based architectures, especially those utilizing low-order orthogonal polynomials, can achieve comparable or superior accuracy and interpretability to MLP-based models for solving differential equations and operator learning tasks, but may exhibit differences in robustness and training stability depending on parameterization and initialization.
35b3979d5f824009a38f93604ef05a0d7ed09395.proposed_method: A systematic framework will be developed to construct physics-informed machine learning models (PIKANs) and deep operator networks (DeepOKANs) using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) with various parameterizations, including B-splines and low-order orthogonal polynomials such as Chebyshev polynomials. These KAN-based models will be directly compared to standard MLP-based architectures, specifically physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and DeepONets, across a suite of benchmark problems. The methodology will include the integration of advanced optimization techniques such as residual-based attention and eddy viscosity formulations to ensure fair and state-of-the-art training conditions. Learning dynamics will be analyzed using information bottleneck theory, and architectural modifications (e.g., composing Chebyshev-KAN layers with tanh activations) will be explored to address observed instabilities.
35b3979d5f824009a38f93604ef05a0d7ed09395.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on eight benchmark problems, including discontinuous function approximation, structure-preserving Hamiltonian dynamical systems, partial differential equation (PDE) solution approximation, uncertainty quantification, and operator learning tasks. Datasets will be selected from established literature, and both forward and inverse problem settings will be considered. Baseline models will include MLP-based PINNs and DeepONets, while KAN-based models will encompass vanilla KANs, Chebyshev-KANs, and modified Chebyshev-KANs. Evaluation metrics will include relative L2 error, convergence rate, runtime per iteration, and loss landscape visualization. Training will utilize the Adam optimizer, and experiments will be run on high-performance GPUs (e.g., Nvidia RTX-3090). The impact of network depth, polynomial order, and random seed initialization on stability and robustness will be systematically assessed.
35b3979d5f824009a38f93604ef05a0d7ed09395.novelty_claims: The proposed research provides the first comprehensive and FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) benchmarking of KAN versus MLP representations for differential equations and operator networks, incorporating recent advances in KAN parameterizations and optimization techniques. The study introduces modified Chebyshev-KAN architectures to address instability issues and extends information bottleneck theory analysis to KAN-based physics-informed models. By establishing reproducible benchmarks and detailed comparisons, the research aims to advance understanding of the strengths and limitations of KANs in scientific machine learning and facilitate further development in the field.

35ef8fff5c3d167b884a218f74c45c20938f100a.title: Smooth Tchebycheff Scalarization for Multi-Objective Optimization
35ef8fff5c3d167b884a218f74c45c20938f100a.research_question: How can multi-objective optimization be made more efficient and theoretically robust for differentiable problems, particularly in finding all Pareto solutions with valid trade-off preferences, while maintaining low computational complexity?
35ef8fff5c3d167b884a218f74c45c20938f100a.hypothesis: A smooth scalarization approach based on the Tchebycheff method can achieve efficient, gradient-based multi-objective optimization with strong theoretical guarantees, enabling the discovery of all Pareto solutions under mild conditions and reducing computational complexity compared to existing methods.
35ef8fff5c3d167b884a218f74c45c20938f100a.proposed_method: A novel smooth Tchebycheff (STCH) scalarization framework will be developed for gradient-based multi-objective optimization. The method replaces the non-differentiable max operator in classical Tchebycheff scalarization with a smooth approximation using a log-sum-exp function parameterized by a smoothing parameter µ. This results in a differentiable scalarization function that retains the ability to find all Pareto solutions with valid trade-off preferences. The optimization is performed using standard gradient-based algorithms, leveraging the smoothness to ensure faster convergence and lower per-iteration computational cost. The method will also be extended to Pareto set learning by training a model that maps preference vectors to Pareto-optimal solutions using the smooth scalarization as the objective.
35ef8fff5c3d167b884a218f74c45c20938f100a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of multi-objective optimization problems, including synthetic benchmarks and real-world applications such as multi-task learning (NYUv2, Office-31, QM9 datasets) and engineering design problems (Bar Truss, Hatch Cover, Disk Brake, Gear Train, Rocket Injector). Baselines will include classical scalarization methods (linear, Tchebycheff), adaptive gradient methods (MGDA, GradNorm, PCGrad, etc.), and recent hybrid and loss-adaptive techniques. Evaluation metrics will include task-specific performance, relative average improvement over single-task baselines, and hypervolume difference (∆HV) to assess Pareto front approximation quality. Both single-solution and Pareto set learning scenarios will be tested, with careful analysis of convergence speed, computational cost, and the effect of the smoothing parameter µ.
35ef8fff5c3d167b884a218f74c45c20938f100a.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a smooth, differentiable variant of the Tchebycheff scalarization that enables efficient gradient-based optimization for multi-objective problems. It provides strong theoretical guarantees for finding all Pareto solutions under mild conditions, achieves lower computational complexity per iteration compared to adaptive gradient methods, and supports efficient Pareto set learning. The approach is lightweight, easy to implement, and demonstrates superior or competitive empirical performance across a range of challenging benchmarks.

3633dba6b595fe6338df5c0b07726b4b8f349150.title: On Divergence Measures for Bayesian Pseudocoresets
3633dba6b595fe6338df5c0b07726b4b8f349150.research_question: How can small synthetic datasets, known as Bayesian pseudocoresets, be constructed to efficiently and accurately approximate the posterior distribution of high-dimensional models, such as deep neural networks, and what divergence measures are most effective for this purpose?
3633dba6b595fe6338df5c0b07726b4b8f349150.hypothesis: Minimizing alternative divergence measures, such as forward KL divergence and Wasserstein distance, in addition to the standard reverse KL divergence, will enable the construction of Bayesian pseudocoresets that better approximate the true posterior distribution in high-dimensional settings, with improved scalability, computational efficiency, and robustness compared to existing methods.
3633dba6b595fe6338df5c0b07726b4b8f349150.proposed_method: A unified framework will be developed for constructing Bayesian pseudocoresets by minimizing various divergence measures between the pseudocoreset posterior and the full-data posterior. Three divergence measures will be considered: reverse KL divergence, Wasserstein distance, and forward KL divergence. For each, a synthetic dataset (the pseudocoreset) will be parameterized and optimized such that the posterior induced by the pseudocoreset closely matches the full-data posterior. The method for reverse KL divergence will use a Laplace or Gaussian approximation for the pseudocoreset posterior, and will draw connections to gradient-matching dataset distillation algorithms. Wasserstein distance minimization will be implemented using closed-form solutions for Gaussian approximations of the posteriors. A novel algorithm will be introduced for forward KL divergence minimization, leveraging truncated backpropagation and Monte Carlo estimation to efficiently compute gradients and update the pseudocoreset. The framework will incorporate techniques from dataset distillation, such as reusing precomputed optimization trajectories and data augmentation, to enhance scalability.
3633dba6b595fe6338df5c0b07726b4b8f349150.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the CIFAR10 and CIFAR10-C datasets using a 3-layer ConvNet architecture. Bayesian pseudocoresets will be constructed using each of the three divergence-based methods (reverse KL, Wasserstein, and forward KL), and their performance will be evaluated in terms of top-1 accuracy and negative log-likelihood (NLL) on test data. Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods, specifically Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) and Stochastic Gradient Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (SGHMC), will be used for posterior inference. Baselines will include random coreset selection and comparisons across different pseudocoreset sizes (e.g., 1, 10, 20 images per class). The impact of data augmentation during training and testing will be assessed. Computational efficiency will be measured in terms of GPU memory usage and training time. Robustness to out-of-distribution data will be evaluated using the CIFAR10-C corrupted dataset, with performance averaged over multiple random seeds.
3633dba6b595fe6338df5c0b07726b4b8f349150.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unifying view that connects Bayesian pseudocoreset construction and dataset distillation via divergence minimization, establishing theoretical links between these approaches. It extends Bayesian pseudocoreset methods to high-dimensional, real-world datasets and deep neural networks, which has not been previously demonstrated. A novel algorithm for Bayesian pseudocoreset construction based on forward KL divergence minimization is proposed, offering improved computational efficiency and robustness. The approach leverages and adapts techniques from scalable dataset distillation, such as trajectory matching and data augmentation, to the Bayesian inference context. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate that the proposed methods achieve superior posterior approximation, computational efficiency, and robustness to distributional shift compared to existing baselines.

3648515cc35b517cdf60331cc4870e24616f9939.title: DeepSeek-Prover: Advancing Theorem Proving in LLMs through Large-Scale Synthetic Data
3648515cc35b517cdf60331cc4870e24616f9939.research_question: How can large-scale synthetic formal proof data generated from informal mathematical problems improve the automated theorem-proving capabilities of large language models in formal systems such as Lean 4?
3648515cc35b517cdf60331cc4870e24616f9939.hypothesis: Training large language models on a large, high-quality, synthetic dataset of formal mathematical statements and proofs, generated from informal competition-level math problems, will significantly enhance their performance in formal theorem proving compared to existing models and datasets.
3648515cc35b517cdf60331cc4870e24616f9939.proposed_method: A comprehensive pipeline is proposed to generate large-scale synthetic Lean 4 proof data from high-school and undergraduate-level mathematical competition problems. The process begins with autoformalization, where informal math problems are translated into formal Lean 4 statements using a fine-tuned large language model. Quality filtering is then applied: statements are scored for complexity and mathematical value, and a hypothesis rejection strategy is used to exclude statements with invalid or vacuous premises. For each high-quality formal statement, proofs are generated and verified within the Lean 4 environment, with a dual approach that attempts to prove both the statement and its negation in parallel to efficiently discard unprovable cases. This process is iteratively repeated, with the model being fine-tuned on the newly validated theorem-proof pairs after each cycle, progressively improving the quality and scale of the synthetic dataset and the model's capabilities.
3648515cc35b517cdf60331cc4870e24616f9939.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate the fine-tuned model on established benchmarks such as miniF2F (488 problems) and FIMO (148 problems), using the Lean 4 formal system. The base model is DeepSeekMath-Base7B, a decoder-only transformer pre-trained on 120 billion math-related tokens. Baselines for comparison include GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and state-of-the-art tree search and reinforcement learning-based theorem provers (e.g., COPRA, ProofArtifactCo-Training, ReProver, Llemma, HypertreeProofSearch). Evaluation metrics include pass@k (the probability that at least one valid proof is found in k attempts), with experiments conducted at various sample sizes (e.g., 1, 64, 128, up to 65536 generations). Ablation studies will assess the impact of dataset size, quality filtering, and iterative enhancement on theorem-proving performance.
3648515cc35b517cdf60331cc4870e24616f9939.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces an iterative, scalable method for generating over 8 million high-quality synthetic formal statements and proofs from informal mathematical problems, significantly expanding available training data for formal theorem proving. It leverages a dual proof search (for statements and their negations) to efficiently filter unprovable cases, and employs a model-driven quality assurance pipeline to ensure dataset value. The approach demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on challenging formal mathematics benchmarks, surpassing both general-purpose and specialized models. The resulting dataset and model are intended for open release, providing a valuable resource for further research in automated theorem proving and formal mathematical reasoning.

3660fb114e4047b292c8fa17fd9321c1c023a10f.title: Leveraged Weighted Loss for Partial Label Learning
3660fb114e4047b292c8fa17fd9321c1c023a10f.research_question: How can the learning process in partial label learning be improved by developing new loss functions that better balance the influence of candidate (partial) and non-candidate (non-partial) labels, and what theoretical guarantees can be established for such methods under weak assumptions about label generation?
3660fb114e4047b292c8fa17fd9321c1c023a10f.hypothesis: Introducing a leverage parameter into a family of loss functions for partial label learning will enable a principled trade-off between losses on partial and non-partial labels, leading to improved empirical performance and risk consistency under generalized, label-specific partial label generation assumptions.
3660fb114e4047b292c8fa17fd9321c1c023a10f.proposed_method: A new family of loss functions, termed Leveraged Weighted (LW) loss, will be developed for partial label learning. This approach introduces a leverage parameter β, which controls the trade-off between the losses incurred on candidate (partial) labels and non-candidate (non-partial) labels. The LW loss is constructed by combining binary loss functions for each label, weighted by parameters that reflect the likelihood of each label being the true label, and scaled by β for non-partial labels. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to establish risk consistency of the LW loss under generalized, label-specific partial label generation processes, and to provide guidance for the empirical selection of β. A practical algorithm will be designed that iteratively updates weighting parameters using an EM-like procedure, normalizing scores for both partial and non-partial labels, and optimizes the network parameters using stochastic gradient descent.
3660fb114e4047b292c8fa17fd9321c1c023a10f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both benchmark datasets (MNIST, Kuzushiji-MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10) and real-world datasets (Lost, MSRCv2, BirdSong, SoccerPlayer, Yahoo! News). Partially labeled data will be generated using both uniform and non-uniform (label-specific) procedures, with varying ambiguity levels. The proposed LW loss method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as PRODEN, RC, CC, IPAL, PALOC, and PLECOC, using consistent base models (MLP, ConvNet, or linear models) and hyperparameter tuning via validation or cross-validation. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy, with statistical significance assessed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Ablation studies will analyze the effect of the leverage parameter β and the contributions of losses on partial versus non-partial labels.
3660fb114e4047b292c8fa17fd9321c1c023a10f.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to introduce a leverage parameter into loss functions for partial label learning, enabling explicit control over the trade-off between losses on partial and non-partial labels. Theoretical contributions include a generalized risk consistency analysis under label-specific partial label generation, extending beyond uniform assumptions used in prior work. The method provides theoretical guidance for selecting the leverage parameter β, supported by empirical validation. The practical algorithm employs an iterative, data-driven approach for weighting candidate and non-candidate labels, and demonstrates superior performance over existing state-of-the-art methods on both benchmark and real-world datasets.

3691bfa5506d8eb1002100309d8b5241a6d0f90e.title: PDL: Regularizing Multiple Instance Learning with Progressive Dropout Layers
3691bfa5506d8eb1002100309d8b5241a6d0f90e.research_question: How can overfitting be effectively mitigated in multiple instance learning (MIL) frameworks, while simultaneously enhancing the discovery of intricate and impactful feature representations under weak supervision?
3691bfa5506d8eb1002100309d8b5241a6d0f90e.hypothesis: Incorporating a progressive, attention-based dropout mechanism into the intermediate layers of MIL models will reduce overfitting and promote the learning of richer, more discriminative feature representations, thereby improving both classification and localization performance.
3691bfa5506d8eb1002100309d8b5241a6d0f90e.proposed_method: A novel regularization framework, termed Progressive Dropout Layer (PDL), will be introduced and integrated into the intermediate (middle) layers of MIL models. The PDL comprises two main components: (1) a MIL-specific attention-based dropout, which utilizes a non-parametric Average-Pooling Based Attention (APBA) mechanism to assign dynamic, instance-specific dropout rates based on the relative importance of each instance within a bag, and (2) a progressive learning scheduler that gradually increases the global maximum dropout rate throughout training, preventing premature suppression of informative instances. The attention-based dropout operates by computing attention weights for each instance, assigning higher dropout rates to more important instances to encourage the network to discover alternative, latent features. The progressive scheduler ensures that dropout is initially suppressed and then progressively activated, guiding the model to robustly localize target instances and avoid misleading localizations.
3691bfa5506d8eb1002100309d8b5241a6d0f90e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several MIL benchmark datasets, including MUSK1, MUSK2 (molecule classification), and FOX, TIGER, ELEPHANT (image classification), as well as large-scale whole slide image (WSI) datasets Camelyon16 (breast cancer metastasis detection) and TCGA-NSCLC (lung cancer subtype classification). Additional experiments will be performed on MNIST-bags for further analysis. Baseline MIL models such as ABMIL, ABMIL-Gated, DSMIL, TransMIL, and DTFD-MIL will be used for comparison, both with and without the integration of PDL. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy and area under the ROC curve (AUC), with experiments run multiple times (e.g., five runs with 10-fold cross-validation for benchmarks) to report mean and standard deviation. Pre-trained feature extractors (ResNet, ImageNet, SimCLR) will be employed, and the PDL will be systematically embedded after activation functions in the middle layers. Comparative analyses with other dropout methods (vanilla Dropout, DropInstance, AttentionDropout, SpatialDropout) will also be performed.
3691bfa5506d8eb1002100309d8b5241a6d0f90e.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a MIL-specific, attention-driven progressive dropout mechanism that is orthogonal and easily integrable into existing MIL models, requiring no architectural changes. Unlike prior regularization approaches, the method dynamically assigns dropout rates at the instance level based on learned attention, and schedules the dropout progression to avoid misleading localizations. This approach both mitigates overfitting and enhances the model's ability to discover latent, discriminative features under weak supervision. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent improvements in both classification and localization accuracy across diverse MIL tasks and datasets, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines and existing dropout techniques.

369bd8479daa33df68567e93e00a52155320ed88.title: Zero-shot Model-based Reinforcement Learning using Large Language Models
369bd8479daa33df68567e93e00a52155320ed88.research_question: How can large language models be leveraged for zero-shot model-based reinforcement learning in continuous state-space environments, and what are the implications for policy evaluation, data augmentation, and uncertainty estimation in reinforcement learning tasks?
369bd8479daa33df68567e93e00a52155320ed88.hypothesis: Pre-trained large language models, when combined with a disentangling feature transformation, can serve as effective zero-shot dynamics models for continuous Markov Decision Processes, improving sample efficiency, policy evaluation accuracy, and providing well-calibrated uncertainty estimates in reinforcement learning applications.
369bd8479daa33df68567e93e00a52155320ed88.proposed_method: A novel framework, Disentangled In-Context Learning (DICL), will be developed to address the challenges of modeling continuous state-space Markov Decision Processes using large language models (LLMs). The method first projects state-action trajectories into a disentangled feature space using a transformation such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA), capturing interdependencies between state and action features and reducing dimensionality. In this latent space, each component is forecasted independently in a zero-shot manner by a pre-trained LLM via in-context learning, without any gradient-based updates to the LLM. The predictions are then mapped back to the original trajectory space using the inverse transformation. Two variants will be explored: DICL-(s,a), which operates on both states and actions, and DICL-(s), which focuses on states only, enabling flexibility for different RL tasks.
369bd8479daa33df68567e93e00a52155320ed88.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard continuous control environments such as HalfCheetah, Hopper, and Pendulum from the MuJoCo Gym suite, as well as D4RL datasets. The methodology will be evaluated in three main settings: (1) multi-step trajectory forecasting, comparing DICL to vanilla in-context learning (vICL) and MLP baselines, using metrics such as Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) statistics; (2) data-augmented off-policy RL, where DICL-generated transitions are used to augment the replay buffer in Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), with performance measured by sample efficiency and return curves; and (3) hybrid policy evaluation, where DICL predicts reward trajectories to estimate policy value, with accuracy assessed by relative error. Calibration of LLM uncertainty estimates will be evaluated using quantile calibration and reliability diagrams. Multiple LLMs (e.g., Llama 3 series) will be tested, and ablation studies will investigate the impact of feature transformation and data proportion parameters.
369bd8479daa33df68567e93e00a52155320ed88.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel methodology for applying in-context learning with pre-trained large language models to model-based reinforcement learning in continuous state spaces, overcoming previous limitations in handling multivariate data and action integration. The DICL framework enables zero-shot forecasting of environment dynamics, supports data-augmented off-policy RL with theoretical return bounds under multi-branch rollouts, and facilitates hybrid policy evaluation. Additionally, the approach provides well-calibrated uncertainty estimates from LLMs, a desirable property for model-based RL. The use of feature disentanglement (e.g., via PCA) to enable efficient and effective LLM-based dynamics modeling in RL is a key innovation.

36cae33f3c1fc0fd2c09ec7c5f54b20e250b184c.title: Cooperation and Fairness in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
36cae33f3c1fc0fd2c09ec7c5f54b20e250b184c.research_question: How can decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning systems be designed to balance efficiency and fairness in resource-constrained navigation and coverage tasks, especially when agents have only local observations and must avoid collisions and complete coverage or formation-based tasks?
36cae33f3c1fc0fd2c09ec7c5f54b20e250b184c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that integrating a fairness-driven reward function and min-max fair goal assignment into a decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning framework will enable agents to achieve more equitable task distributions without significantly sacrificing overall system efficiency.
36cae33f3c1fc0fd2c09ec7c5f54b20e250b184c.proposed_method: A decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning approach will be developed, extending the InforMARL framework, where agents operate in a 2D environment with static and dynamic obstacles. Each agent will receive local observations and communicate with neighbors within a limited sensing radius, forming an agent-entity graph processed by a graph neural network. The reward function will combine a distance-based efficiency term, a collision penalty, a goal-reaching bonus, and a fairness term based on the inverse coefficient of variation of agents' traveled distances, encouraging balanced workloads. Goal assignments during training will use a min-max fairness optimization to minimize the maximum distance any agent must travel, and the fairness metric will be incorporated into the reward via a scaled hyperbolic tangent transformation. The approach will be evaluated both for standard coverage tasks and for prescribed formation scenarios, with agents adapting to dynamic goal assignments and formation shapes using only local information.
36cae33f3c1fc0fd2c09ec7c5f54b20e250b184c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in simulated 2D environments based on the Multi-Particle Environments (MPE) suite, with varying numbers of agents, goals, and obstacles. Four model variants will be trained: random assignment (baseline), optimal distance assignment, min-max fair assignment, and min-max fair assignment with the fairness reward. Agents will be evaluated on coverage and formation tasks, with metrics including total distance traveled (efficiency), fairness (inverse coefficient of variation of distances), and goal coverage success rate. Baselines will include random and optimal assignments, and the impact of the fairness reward will be assessed by comparing efficiency-fairness tradeoffs across models. Additional experiments will test scalability, the effect of local versus global observations, and adaptability to different formation shapes.
36cae33f3c1fc0fd2c09ec7c5f54b20e250b184c.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a reward function that explicitly incentivizes fairness in decentralized multi-agent navigation, leveraging a min-max fair goal assignment and a scalable fairness metric. The approach enables agents to learn fair and efficient policies using only local observations and decentralized communication, without requiring global state information or retraining for different numbers of agents or formation shapes. The method demonstrates that significant improvements in fairness can be achieved with minimal loss in efficiency, and that agents can self-organize into arbitrary formations in a scalable and generalizable manner.

36ce239097627ffc1bcf4a45f62bb0c2579fc837.title: LMC: Fast Training of GNNs via Subgraph Sampling with Provable Convergence
36ce239097627ffc1bcf4a45f62bb0c2579fc837.research_question: How can the training of graph neural networks (GNNs) on large-scale graphs be accelerated while maintaining provable convergence and high accuracy, especially in the presence of the neighbor explosion problem?
36ce239097627ffc1bcf4a45f62bb0c2579fc837.hypothesis: Introducing a subgraph-wise sampling method that compensates for discarded messages during both forward and backward passes will enable accurate mini-batch gradient estimation, leading to provable convergence and improved training efficiency for GNNs on large-scale graphs.
36ce239097627ffc1bcf4a45f62bb0c2579fc837.proposed_method: A novel subgraph-wise sampling framework, termed Local Message Compensation (LMC), will be developed to address the neighbor explosion problem in GNN training. LMC will operate by sampling a mini-batch of nodes and constructing a subgraph for message passing, but will introduce compensation mechanisms to correct for the bias caused by discarding messages outside the mini-batch. Specifically, LMC will estimate node embeddings and auxiliary variables for out-of-batch nodes using convex combinations of incomplete up-to-date values and historical values from previous iterations. During both forward and backward passes, local message compensation terms will be computed to retrieve and incorporate the effects of discarded messages, ensuring unbiased or nearly unbiased mini-batch gradients. The method will maintain linear complexity in the number of message passing layers and neighborhood size, and will be scalable to large graphs by storing most historical values in CPU memory or disk.
36ce239097627ffc1bcf4a45f62bb0c2579fc837.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale benchmark datasets including PPI, REDDIT, FLICKR, and Ogbn-arxiv, which contain thousands to millions of nodes and edges. The proposed LMC method will be compared against a range of baselines: node-wise sampling (GraphSAGE, VR-GCN), layer-wise sampling (FASTGCN, LADIES), subgraph-wise sampling (CLUSTER-GCN, GRAPHSAINT, FM, GAS), and precomputing approaches (SIGN). Evaluation metrics will include prediction accuracy, convergence speed (epochs and runtime to reach full-batch accuracy), GPU memory usage, and relative error of mini-batch gradients. Experiments will be run on a single GPU (RTX 2080Ti), with hyperparameters selected via grid search and consistent data splits and pipelines for fair comparison. Additional ablation studies will assess the impact of the compensation mechanisms under varying batch sizes.
36ce239097627ffc1bcf4a45f62bb0c2579fc837.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first subgraph-wise sampling approach for GNNs with provable convergence guarantees. It introduces a new compensation mechanism that corrects for the bias in mini-batch gradients caused by discarding messages outside the sampled subgraph, both in forward and backward passes. LMC achieves accurate gradient estimation, accelerates convergence, and is robust to small batch sizes, outperforming state-of-the-art subgraph-wise sampling methods in terms of efficiency and stability on large-scale benchmarks.

36e8de30708d91c2089a68c830335654ba59f262.title: Adaptable Logical Control for Large Language Models
36e8de30708d91c2089a68c830335654ba59f262.research_question: How can large language models be controlled at inference time to reliably and efficiently satisfy arbitrary logical constraints during text generation, and can such control be made tractable and adaptable to a wide range of constraints and applications?
36e8de30708d91c2089a68c830335654ba59f262.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that integrating a distilled Hidden Markov Model (HMM) with a large language model (LLM), and conditioning generation on logical constraints represented as deterministic finite automata (DFA), enables tractable, scalable, and reliable control of LLM outputs to satisfy arbitrary logical constraints without sacrificing generation quality.
36e8de30708d91c2089a68c830335654ba59f262.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces an adaptable framework that couples any production-ready LLM with a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) distilled to approximate the LLM's output distribution. Logical constraints are specified as deterministic finite automata (DFA), which compactly encode the desired properties of the generated text (e.g., inclusion of keyphrases, length, order of fragments). At inference, the HMM is conditioned on the DFA-specified constraint, and the conditional probability of constraint satisfaction is efficiently computed using dynamic programming over the joint state space of the HMM and DFA. The LLM's next-token probabilities are then modulated by the likelihood of future constraint satisfaction, guiding generation toward outputs that satisfy the logical constraints. This approach supports arbitrary DFA-representable constraints and does not require retraining the HMM or LLM when constraints change.
36e8de30708d91c2089a68c830335654ba59f262.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several benchmarks, including Commonsense Generation (CommonGen), text infilling (based on ROCStories), and interactive text editing using passages from the CoAuthor dataset. The method will be applied to LLMs such as TULU2-7B (an instruction-tuned Llama2 variant) and GPT2 variants, with HMMs distilled from these models. Baselines will include state-of-the-art constrained generation methods such as FUDGE, NADO, NeuroLogic A*esque, GeLaTo, and strong LLMs like GPT3.5 and GPT4. Evaluation metrics will include BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, SPICE, constraint satisfaction rate, and human evaluation of fluency, coherence, and overall satisfaction. Human evaluations will be performed via crowd-sourcing platforms, with annotators rating the generated outputs for quality and constraint adherence. Runtime and scalability analyses will be conducted to assess computational efficiency with respect to DFA size and sequence length.
36e8de30708d91c2089a68c830335654ba59f262.novelty_claims: The proposed framework enables tractable, flexible, and reliable control of LLM outputs to satisfy arbitrary logical constraints specified as DFAs, generalizing prior work limited to specific constraint families. The approach guarantees constraint satisfaction, supports rapid adaptation to new constraints without retraining, and scales to modern large LLMs. Efficient algorithms are developed for probabilistic reasoning over logical constraints, and the method demonstrates strong generalizability and high quality on complex constrained generation tasks, outperforming existing baselines and even larger LLMs in constraint satisfaction and overall satisfaction rates.

36fff28902cfb6c99c7c98f284639ad8e0133c44.title: Segment Anything in High Quality
36fff28902cfb6c99c7c98f284639ad8e0133c44.research_question: How can the segmentation quality of large-scale, promptable segmentation foundation models be improved, especially for objects with intricate structures, while maintaining their efficiency, zero-shot generalizability, and minimal computational overhead?
36fff28902cfb6c99c7c98f284639ad8e0133c44.hypothesis: Introducing a lightweight, learnable output token and a global-local feature fusion mechanism into an existing segmentation foundation model will significantly enhance mask prediction quality, particularly for fine structures and boundaries, without compromising zero-shot transfer capabilities or efficiency.
36fff28902cfb6c99c7c98f284639ad8e0133c44.proposed_method: A novel adaptation of a promptable segmentation foundation model is proposed by integrating two key components: a learnable High-Quality Output Token and a Global-local Feature Fusion module. The High-Quality Output Token is injected into the mask decoder alongside original tokens and is trained, together with a small associated MLP, to predict high-quality segmentation masks. The Global-local Feature Fusion module combines early-layer (local detail) and final-layer (global context) features from the ViT encoder with mask decoder features, using transposed convolutions and element-wise summation after convolutional processing, to produce detail-preserving features. During training, all original model weights are frozen; only the new token, its MLP, and the fusion block are updated. The final mask is generated by combining the logits from the original and new tokens, and the output is upsampled to the desired resolution.
36fff28902cfb6c99c7c98f284639ad8e0133c44.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of 10 diverse segmentation datasets, including both image and video tasks, with 8 datasets evaluated under a zero-shot transfer protocol. The model will be trained exclusively on a newly composed HQSeg-44K dataset containing 44,320 fine-grained, manually annotated masks from six public datasets, covering over 1,000 semantic classes. Baselines for comparison include the original segmentation model, variants with context tokens, post-refinement networks, and adapter-based fine-tuning methods. Evaluation metrics will include standard mask AP, mask mIoU, boundary metrics (mBIoU, boundary AP), and stricter AP metrics for boundary accuracy. Ablation studies will assess the impact of each architectural component, and both quantitative and qualitative results will be reported.
36fff28902cfb6c99c7c98f284639ad8e0133c44.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first high-quality, zero-shot segmentation adaptation for promptable foundation models with negligible parameter and computational overhead. The approach uniquely combines a learnable output token and global-local feature fusion, enabling direct high-quality mask prediction without post-refinement or extensive fine-tuning. The method achieves significant improvements in segmentation quality, particularly for fine structures and boundaries, while fully preserving zero-shot generalization and efficiency. The training is highly data- and computation-efficient, requiring only a small, high-quality dataset and minimal additional parameters.

3707939a856655fcabf0acd5cba1a1009987b439.title: Generative Verifiers: Reward Modeling as Next-Token Prediction
3707939a856655fcabf0acd5cba1a1009987b439.research_question: How can the verification and reward modeling of large language model (LLM) outputs for complex reasoning tasks be improved by leveraging the generative capabilities of LLMs, rather than relying solely on discriminative classification approaches?
3707939a856655fcabf0acd5cba1a1009987b439.hypothesis: Training verifiers using a next-token prediction objective that unifies solution generation and verification, and incorporates chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, will result in more accurate and generalizable verification of LLM-generated solutions compared to traditional discriminative reward models and other baseline approaches.
3707939a856655fcabf0acd5cba1a1009987b439.proposed_method: A novel generative verifier framework, termed GenRM, will be developed by fine-tuning large language models using supervised next-token prediction on both solution generation and verification tasks. Verification will be formulated as predicting the probability of a 'Yes' or 'No' token in response to a prompt such as 'Is the answer correct?'. The approach will be extended to support chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning by training models to generate intermediate verification rationales before outputting the final correctness token, resulting in GenRM-CoT. During inference, multiple CoT rationales will be sampled and majority voting will be used to aggregate correctness probabilities, leveraging additional test-time computation for improved accuracy. Synthetic verification rationales, generated by prompting LLMs with reference solutions, will be used to scale training data for verification tasks.
3707939a856655fcabf0acd5cba1a1009987b439.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of reasoning tasks, including algorithmic string manipulation (Last Letter Concatenation and Word Sorting from Big-Bench), grade-school math (GSM8K), and advanced math (MATH and MMLU datasets). Verifiers will be trained using open-weight Gemma models (2B, 7B, 9B, and 29B parameters), and solutions for verification will be generated from both Gemma and Gemini 1.0 Pro models. Baselines will include discriminative reward models (binary classifiers), LLM-as-a-Judge (prompted verification), DPO (preference optimization), and self-consistency. Evaluation will focus on Best-of-N accuracy (percentage of problems solved by selecting the best out of N candidate solutions), as well as verifier classification accuracy. Majority voting with up to 32 sampled CoT rationales will be used for GenRM-CoT at inference. Additional experiments will assess generalization from easy to hard tasks, scaling with model size, and the effect of unifying solution generation and verification.
3707939a856655fcabf0acd5cba1a1009987b439.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces generative verifiers that unify solution generation and verification through next-token prediction, enabling seamless integration with instruction tuning and chain-of-thought reasoning. This method leverages the full generative capacity of LLMs for verification, supports scalable training via synthetic rationales, and allows for improved performance through inference-time majority voting. The approach claims superior accuracy and generalization over discriminative verifiers, LLM-as-a-Judge, and preference-based baselines, particularly in challenging reasoning and mathematical domains. The method also demonstrates improved sample efficiency and favorable scaling with both model size and compute.

3716224bd6b47c20d1e41681788f4b6c40f0681f.title: Optimal Rates for Random Order Online Optimization
3716224bd6b47c20d1e41681788f4b6c40f0681f.research_question: What are the optimal regret rates achievable in online convex optimization when loss functions are presented in a random order, under the assumption that the cumulative loss is (strongly) convex but individual losses may be non-convex and only smooth?
3716224bd6b47c20d1e41681788f4b6c40f0681f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, by leveraging algorithmic stability and novel sampling strategies, it is possible to achieve regret bounds in the random order online optimization model that match or improve upon the optimal rates known for the i.i.d. stochastic setting, and that these bounds can be achieved without dimension dependence and with improved scaling in the strong convexity parameter.
3716224bd6b47c20d1e41681788f4b6c40f0681f.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves the development and analysis of two algorithms for random order online convex optimization. The first algorithm utilizes a reservoir sampling-based strategy to generate unbiased gradient estimates throughout all rounds, ensuring that the expected function remains strongly convex and that algorithmic stability is maintained. This approach enables the use of stochastic gradient descent (SGD) updates with step sizes carefully chosen based on the problem's condition number, resulting in optimal regret up to additive factors. The second algorithm is designed to be memory-efficient, trading off a slightly worse dependence on the condition number for lower memory usage by maintaining only a linear-in-dimension state. Both algorithms rely on refined average stability analyses and leverage connections between stability and generalization in the without-replacement sampling setting.
3716224bd6b47c20d1e41681788f4b6c40f0681f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic and/or real datasets where the loss functions are G-Lipschitz, β-smooth, and the cumulative loss is λ-strongly convex, but individual losses may be non-convex. The algorithms will be evaluated against baselines such as online gradient descent and the previous state-of-the-art method for the random order model. Evaluation metrics will include expected regret over T rounds, with particular attention to the dependence on problem dimension d, Lipschitz constant G, smoothness β, and strong convexity λ. Key experimental setups will vary the problem dimension, condition number, and memory constraints to assess both regret performance and resource efficiency.
3716224bd6b47c20d1e41681788f4b6c40f0681f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel stability-based analysis for random order online optimization, enabling the removal of dimension dependence from regret bounds and improving scaling with respect to the strong convexity parameter compared to prior work. The use of reservoir sampling for unbiased gradient estimation in the random order setting is a key innovation, as is the extension of average stability concepts to the without-replacement online context. The resulting algorithms achieve regret rates matching the optimal rates for the individually strongly convex case, even when individual losses are non-convex, and do so with improved memory efficiency and without requiring additional smoothness assumptions such as Lipschitz Hessians.

37262eae27907fce421698c66e48e1a996c64f19.title: Is Ego Status All You Need for Open-Loop End-to-End Autonomous Driving?
37262eae27907fce421698c66e48e1a996c64f19.research_question: How does the reliance on ego vehicle status information affect the planning performance and evaluation of open-loop end-to-end autonomous driving models, and what are the limitations of current datasets and metrics in accurately assessing planning quality?
37262eae27907fce421698c66e48e1a996c64f19.hypothesis: Open-loop end-to-end autonomous driving models evaluated on current benchmarks, such as nuScenes, are overly reliant on ego vehicle status (e.g., velocity, acceleration, yaw angle), which can mask the true value of perception modules and lead to misleading conclusions about planning performance. Furthermore, current evaluation metrics do not comprehensively capture planning quality, necessitating new metrics and benchmarks.
37262eae27907fce421698c66e48e1a996c64f19.proposed_method: A comprehensive analysis will be conducted on open-loop end-to-end autonomous driving models to quantify the influence of ego status information on planning outcomes. A simple baseline model, BEV-Planner, will be developed that predicts future trajectories directly from BEV (bird's-eye view) features, optionally incorporating ego status and temporal BEV features, but without using perception annotations such as bounding boxes or HD maps. The BEV-Planner pipeline will generate BEV features from input images, concatenate features from past timesteps, and use cross-attention between BEV features and a learnable ego query, followed by MLPs to predict trajectories. Variants of the baseline will be constructed to separately analyze the effects of including or excluding ego status and map perception tasks. A new evaluation metric, Curb Collision Rate (CCR), will be introduced to measure the adherence of predicted trajectories to road boundaries, complementing traditional metrics such as L2 distance and collision rate.
37262eae27907fce421698c66e48e1a996c64f19.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the nuScenes dataset, focusing on open-loop evaluation settings where human driving logs serve as ground truth. The baseline and its variants will be compared against state-of-the-art models such as UniAD, VAD, and Ego-MLP, with and without ego status inputs. Evaluation metrics will include L2 distance, collision rate, and the newly proposed Curb Collision Rate (CCR). The experimental setup will use an R50 backbone, input resolution of 256x704, BEV resolution of 128x128, and a perception range of approximately 50 meters. Models will be trained for 12 epochs on 8 V100 GPUs with a batch size of 32 and a learning rate of 1e-4. Additional robustness experiments will introduce noise or corruption to image and ego status inputs to assess the sensitivity of planning performance to these factors.
37262eae27907fce421698c66e48e1a996c64f19.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a thorough diagnostic of the over-reliance on ego status in open-loop end-to-end autonomous driving, challenging prevailing assumptions about the necessity and utility of perception modules in current benchmarks. A new, simple baseline (BEV-Planner) is proposed that achieves competitive results without perception annotations, highlighting the limitations of existing datasets and metrics. The Curb Collision Rate (CCR) metric is introduced to better capture safety-critical aspects of planning, such as road adherence, which are overlooked by traditional metrics. The work advocates for the development of more representative datasets and comprehensive evaluation frameworks to advance the field beyond current local optima.

372c106a2c806eb28a58dd18ccfcb403835d9331.title: Explicit Preference Optimization: No Need for an Implicit Reward Model
372c106a2c806eb28a58dd18ccfcb403835d9331.research_question: How can preference optimization for large language models be improved to avoid the limitations of implicit reward models and reparameterization tricks, while ensuring better alignment with human preferences and more effective interpolation between optimal and reference policies?
372c106a2c806eb28a58dd18ccfcb403835d9331.hypothesis: Explicit preference optimization objectives, which do not rely on implicit reward models or reparameterization, can overcome the regularization and interpolation limitations of existing DPO-like methods, leading to improved alignment with human preferences and better preservation of optimal policies.
372c106a2c806eb28a58dd18ccfcb403835d9331.proposed_method: A new framework, Explicit Preference Optimization (EXPO), will be developed to directly optimize human preferences without the need for implicit reward models or reparameterization tricks. The approach introduces two main objective classes: a compositional loss (ℓc_EXPO) that combines supervised KL divergence between the model-induced and ground-truth preference distributions with an unsupervised regularization term, and a regression-based loss (ℓr_EXPO) that penalizes the squared deviation of the model's induced preference distribution from a weighted average of the ground-truth and reference distributions. Both objectives are designed to satisfy key desiderata: the ability to preserve optimal policies in regions where the reference is strong, and to interpolate smoothly between the optimal and reference policies as a trade-off parameter is varied. The methodology ensures that unbiased gradient estimates can be efficiently computed for stochastic gradient descent optimization, and the framework is constructed to be compatible with both labeled and unlabeled data.
372c106a2c806eb28a58dd18ccfcb403835d9331.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in both synthetic and real-world settings. Synthetic experiments will use a bandit setup with discrete response spaces and controlled preference distributions to test interpolation and preservation properties, comparing EXPO against DPO, IPO, and f-DPO baselines. Real-world validation will involve fine-tuning a Pythia 2.8B language model on the Anthropic Helpfulness and Harmlessness (HH) preference dataset and the IMDb dataset. The evaluation will measure win rates of generated responses using GPT-4 as a judge, with comparisons made to supervised fine-tuning, DPO, IPO, and both EXPO variants. Experimental setups will include varying the interpolation parameter λ and analyzing convergence behavior, policy preservation, and sample diversity. Additional baselines and larger LLM architectures will be considered in extended experiments.
372c106a2c806eb28a58dd18ccfcb403835d9331.novelty_claims: The proposed EXPO framework introduces explicit preference optimization objectives that eliminate the need for implicit reward models and reparameterization tricks, addressing fundamental limitations of DPO-like methods. EXPO is claimed to be the first to provably satisfy both preservation and interpolation desiderata, enabling selective preservation of optimal policies and smooth interpolation between optimal and reference policies. The approach provides unbiased, efficient gradient estimation for SGD and is compatible with both labeled and unlabeled data. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior performance in both synthetic and real-world preference alignment tasks, with improved alignment, sample diversity, and win rates over existing baselines.

373d7bc9a5ad68f915ccf9c763ecdd308f204633.title: SageAttention: Accurate 8-Bit Attention for Plug-and-play Inference Acceleration
373d7bc9a5ad68f915ccf9c763ecdd308f204633.research_question: How can attention mechanisms in transformer architectures be efficiently quantized to 8-bit precision to accelerate inference, while maintaining high accuracy and enabling plug-and-play deployment across diverse models and hardware platforms?
373d7bc9a5ad68f915ccf9c763ecdd308f204633.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a carefully designed 8-bit quantization scheme for attention—incorporating specialized handling for outlier channels, selective precision for matrix multiplications, and adaptive kernel selection—can achieve significant inference speedup with negligible loss in end-to-end model performance across a variety of tasks and hardware.
373d7bc9a5ad68f915ccf9c763ecdd308f204633.proposed_method: The proposed method, SageAttention, introduces a fast and accurate quantization framework for transformer attention. The approach applies INT8 quantization to the Q and K matrices using per-block or per-token granularity, and smooths the K matrix by subtracting its mean across tokens to address channel-wise outliers. For the PV matrix multiplication, the method retains P and V in FP16 and uses an FP16 accumulator, which balances speed and accuracy. Multiple kernel variants are implemented, allowing adaptive selection per layer based on cosine similarity thresholds to optimize the speed-accuracy tradeoff. Quantization is fused with preceding operations, such as Rotary Position Embedding (ROPE), to minimize overhead, and the implementation leverages Triton for efficient GPU execution, utilizing INT8 and FP16 tensor core instructions.
373d7bc9a5ad68f915ccf9c763ecdd308f204633.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a diverse set of models, including Llama2 (7B) for text generation, CogvideoX for text-to-video, Unidiffuser and UltraPixel for text-to-image, TIMM for image classification, and Llava1.6 for visual question answering. Evaluation spans multiple datasets: WikiText, LAMBADA, and MMLU for Llama2; open-sora prompts for CogvideoX; COCO annotations for UltraPixel and Unidiffuser; ImageNet, ImageNet-Sketch, and ImageNet-Rendition for TIMM; and TextVQA, POPE, and VQAv2 for Llava1.6. Metrics include perplexity, accuracy, FID, sFID, CLIP-based scores, ImageReward, and various video quality measures. Baselines for comparison include FlashAttention2, FlashAttention3, xformers, and standard PyTorch attention. Speed and accuracy are measured on RTX4090 and RTX3090 GPUs, with detailed throughput and latency analyses across varying sequence lengths and head dimensions.
373d7bc9a5ad68f915ccf9c763ecdd308f204633.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to systematically address 8-bit quantization for attention in transformers with a plug-and-play, post-training approach that incurs almost no end-to-end metric loss. Key innovations include smoothing the K matrix to handle channel-wise outliers, selective use of FP16 accumulators for PV multiplication to preserve accuracy, and adaptive kernel selection for optimal speed-accuracy tradeoff. The implementation achieves over 2x speedup compared to state-of-the-art baselines such as FlashAttention2 and xformers, while maintaining superior or comparable accuracy, and is compatible with widely available GPU hardware rather than being restricted to specialized architectures.

374dd173491a59a10bbb2b3519ebcfe3649f529d.title: Teaching Models to Express Their Uncertainty in Words
374dd173491a59a10bbb2b3519ebcfe3649f529d.research_question: Can large language models be trained to express their own uncertainty about answers in natural language, and how well does this verbalized uncertainty generalize to new types of questions and distribution shifts compared to traditional logit-based uncertainty measures?
374dd173491a59a10bbb2b3519ebcfe3649f529d.hypothesis: Large language models can be finetuned to express calibrated uncertainty about their own answers in natural language, and this verbalized uncertainty will generalize robustly to new question types and distribution shifts, outperforming or matching logit-based approaches and simple heuristics.
374dd173491a59a10bbb2b3519ebcfe3649f529d.proposed_method: A large pre-trained language model (such as GPT-3) will be finetuned to output, for each input question, both an answer and a verbalized confidence level (either as a probability or as a categorical descriptor like 'high' or 'medium'). The training data will be constructed by sampling questions from a suite of arithmetic tasks, generating model answers, and labeling each answer with an empirical confidence score based on the model's historical accuracy on that sub-task. The model will be trained using supervised learning to match these calibrated confidence labels. Alternative methods will also be implemented for comparison, including finetuning the model to output confidence via logits (indirect logit) and using baseline approaches such as constant confidence or heuristic-based logistic regression. The approach will also explore few-shot learning by providing the model with a small number of context examples and aggregating its predicted confidences.
374dd173491a59a10bbb2b3519ebcfe3649f529d.experiment_details: Experiments will use the CalibratedMath benchmark, a suite of 21 programmatically generated arithmetic tasks with both single-answer and multi-answer formats. The primary training set will consist of 'Add-subtract' tasks, while evaluation will be performed on two distribution-shifted sets: 'Multi-answer' (questions with multiple correct answers and different concepts) and 'Multiply-divide' (harder, unique-answer tasks). The model's calibration will be evaluated using mean squared error (MSE) and mean absolute deviation (MAD) between predicted confidences and actual correctness. Baselines will include zero-shot answer logit, indirect logit, constant confidence, and heuristic logistic regression. Additional analyses will probe whether the model's calibration is explained by logit outputs, simple heuristics, or latent representations, including linear probing on pre-trained embeddings.
374dd173491a59a10bbb2b3519ebcfe3649f529d.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the concept of training language models to express epistemic uncertainty in natural language ('verbalized probability'), rather than relying solely on model logits. It presents a new calibration benchmark (CalibratedMath) specifically designed to test generalization under distribution shift and multi-answer settings. The approach is claimed to be the first to demonstrate that a language model can express well-calibrated uncertainty about its own answers in words, and to provide evidence that such calibration is not merely a reflection of logit information or simple heuristics, but leverages latent representations developed during pre-training.

376461a2c049f6fa51a4303853fdc672e4d07a0d.title: Thinking in Space: How Multimodal Large Language Models See, Remember, and Recall Spaces
376461a2c049f6fa51a4303853fdc672e4d07a0d.research_question: Can multimodal large language models (MLLMs) develop and demonstrate visual-spatial intelligence from egocentric video data, enabling them to perceive, remember, and reason about complex real-world spaces? What are the strengths and limitations of current MLLMs in spatial reasoning, and how can their spatial intelligence be systematically evaluated and improved?
376461a2c049f6fa51a4303853fdc672e4d07a0d.hypothesis: MLLMs trained on large-scale video datasets can exhibit emerging visual-spatial intelligence, but their spatial reasoning abilities, particularly in forming global cognitive maps and performing egocentric-allocentric transformations, remain limited compared to humans. Explicitly prompting MLLMs to generate cognitive maps will enhance their spatial reasoning performance, especially for distance-related tasks.
376461a2c049f6fa51a4303853fdc672e4d07a0d.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark, VSI-Bench, will be constructed to evaluate the visual-spatial intelligence of MLLMs using over 5,000 question-answer pairs derived from nearly 290 real-world indoor scene videos. The videos will be sourced from public 3D scene reconstruction datasets (ScanNet, ScanNet++, ARKitScenes), unified into a standardized meta-information format with object-level annotations. Benchmark tasks will span configurational (object count, relative distance, direction, route planning), measurement estimation (object/room size, absolute distance), and spatiotemporal (appearance order) categories. MLLMs will be evaluated on their ability to answer questions about the spatial layout, object relationships, and navigation within these environments.
