To probe model reasoning, MLLMs will be prompted for both linguistic self-explanations and to generate explicit cognitive maps representing their internal spatial world models. The impact of advanced prompting techniques (chain-of-thought, self-consistency, tree-of-thought) and cognitive map-based reasoning will be systematically assessed.
376461a2c049f6fa51a4303853fdc672e4d07a0d.experiment_details: Experiments will involve evaluating 15 state-of-the-art video-supporting MLLMs (both proprietary and open-source, e.g., Gemini-1.5, GPT-4o, InternVL2, LLaVA-OneVision, LLaVA-Video) on VSI-Bench under zero-shot settings with default prompts. Datasets include ScanNet, ScanNet++, and ARKitScenes, providing diverse real-world indoor scenes with accurate object-level annotations. Baselines will include random and frequency-based chance levels, as well as human-level performance on a subset of the benchmark. Evaluation metrics will comprise accuracy for multiple-choice tasks and a novel Mean Relative Accuracy (MRA) for numerical estimation tasks. Additional experiments will analyze the effectiveness of linguistic prompting techniques and the impact of cognitive map generation on spatial reasoning, particularly for relative distance tasks. Error analysis will categorize model failures by capability (visual perception, linguistic intelligence, relational reasoning, egocentric-allocentric transformation).
376461a2c049f6fa51a4303853fdc672e4d07a0d.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces VSI-Bench, the first large-scale, video-based benchmark specifically designed to evaluate visual-spatial intelligence in MLLMs using real-world egocentric video. The methodology enables systematic probing of both linguistic and visual (cognitive map) reasoning in MLLMs. The research claims to reveal that standard linguistic prompting techniques do not improve—and may even harm—spatial reasoning performance, while explicit cognitive map generation significantly enhances spatial distance reasoning. The benchmark and analysis provide new insights into the bottlenecks of current MLLMs in spatial intelligence and offer a new direction for improving model performance through mental imagery and spatial world modeling.

379e42895f6d40ab9e9559609f505aba89145a5d.title: Efficiently Scaling Transformer Inference
379e42895f6d40ab9e9559609f505aba89145a5d.research_question: How can generative inference for large-scale Transformer models be made more efficient, particularly under tight latency constraints and with long sequence lengths, while optimizing for hardware utilization and scalability?
379e42895f6d40ab9e9559609f505aba89145a5d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a combination of analytically-guided multi-dimensional partitioning strategies, memory optimizations (such as multiquery attention), low-level scheduling, and quantization can significantly improve the latency and throughput of Transformer inference for large models, surpassing existing benchmarks in efficiency and scalability.
379e42895f6d40ab9e9559609f505aba89145a5d.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed to analytically determine optimal multi-axis tensor partitioning strategies for Transformer inference, tailored to specific hardware (e.g., TPU v4) and application requirements. This framework will incorporate a suite of partitioning layouts for both feedforward and attention layers, including 1D and 2D weight-stationary, weight-gathered, and hybrid strategies, with dynamic selection based on batch size and sequence length. Multiquery attention will be leveraged to reduce the memory footprint of the key-value cache, enabling support for much longer context lengths. Additional low-level optimizations will be implemented, such as concurrent communication-computation scheduling (e.g., Looped Collective Einsum), improved tensor layouts, fused matrix operations, and int8 weight quantization using the AQT library. The system will dynamically switch between partitioning and quantization strategies during prefill and generation phases to optimize for latency or throughput as required.
379e42895f6d40ab9e9559609f505aba89145a5d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the PaLM family of large language models (8B, 62B, and 540B parameters), using up to 256 Google TPU v4 chips. The evaluation will include both low-latency (interactive) and high-throughput (offline) inference scenarios, with context lengths up to 2048 tokens and batch sizes ranging from 1 to over 1000. Baselines will include the FasterTransformer suite and Megatron models, with comparisons made in terms of latency per token, model FLOPS utilization (MFU), and maximum achievable context length. Metrics will be reported for both prefill and decode phases, and detailed ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of partitioning layout, multiquery attention, and quantization. The system will be benchmarked across a Pareto frontier of latency and efficiency, and results will be normalized for hardware differences using MFU.
379e42895f6d40ab9e9559609f505aba89145a5d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a simple yet powerful analytical model for selecting optimal multi-dimensional partitioning strategies for Transformer inference, enabling intuitive tradeoff analysis and surpassing black-box search methods. The integration of multiquery attention with batch-based partitioning allows for up to 32x longer context lengths compared to standard multihead attention. The method achieves new Pareto frontiers in the latency-efficiency tradeoff for 500B+ parameter models, with empirical results demonstrating superior performance to state-of-the-art benchmarks such as FasterTransformer. Additional innovations include dynamic switching between partitioning layouts, advanced communication-computation overlap techniques, and the use of int8 quantization for low-latency inference without quality loss.

37c112454a236ab91c9c6b5cc165a6c3251e9206.title: YOLO-World: Real-Time Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
37c112454a236ab91c9c6b5cc165a6c3251e9206.research_question: How can real-time object detection systems be enhanced to support open-vocabulary detection, enabling recognition and localization of arbitrary objects specified by user-defined text prompts, while maintaining high efficiency suitable for real-world deployment?
37c112454a236ab91c9c6b5cc165a6c3251e9206.hypothesis: Integrating vision-language modeling and large-scale region-text pre-training into a lightweight, re-parameterizable YOLO-based architecture will enable efficient, real-time open-vocabulary object detection with strong generalization to novel categories, outperforming existing methods in both speed and accuracy.
37c112454a236ab91c9c6b5cc165a6c3251e9206.proposed_method: A novel object detection framework will be developed by augmenting the YOLO architecture with open-vocabulary capabilities through vision-language modeling. The approach will utilize a pre-trained CLIP text encoder to generate text embeddings for user-specified categories or prompts, which are then fused with image features using a newly designed Re-parameterizable Vision-Language Path Aggregation Network (RepVL-PAN). RepVL-PAN incorporates Text-guided Cross-Stage Partial Layers (T-CSPLayer) and Image-Pooling Attention modules to facilitate multi-level cross-modal fusion between image and text features. During training, a region-text contrastive loss will be employed to align object embeddings with corresponding text representations, leveraging large-scale region-text pairs constructed from detection, grounding, and pseudo-labeled image-text datasets. For efficient inference, a prompt-then-detect paradigm will be adopted, where user prompts are encoded offline and re-parameterized into model weights, allowing the text encoder to be removed during deployment and significantly accelerating inference.
37c112454a236ab91c9c6b5cc165a6c3251e9206.experiment_details: Experiments will involve pre-training the proposed detector on large-scale datasets, including Objects365 (detection), GQA and Flickr30k (grounding), and pseudo-labeled CC3M (image-text) to construct diverse region-text pairs. The model will be evaluated in zero-shot settings on the LVIS dataset, which contains 1203 categories, using metrics such as Fixed AP and AP for rare, common, and frequent categories. Baselines will include state-of-the-art open-vocabulary detectors such as GLIP, Grounding DINO, and DetCLIP, with comparisons made in terms of both accuracy and inference speed (FPS measured on NVIDIA V100 GPU). Additional experiments will include fine-tuning on COCO and LVIS for close-set detection, as well as open-vocabulary instance segmentation and referring detection tasks. Ablation studies will assess the impact of pre-training data composition, architectural components (e.g., RepVL-PAN), and text encoder choices.
37c112454a236ab91c9c6b5cc165a6c3251e9206.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first real-time, open-vocabulary object detector based on a lightweight YOLO framework, achieving a substantial increase in inference speed (up to 20× faster) compared to prior art while maintaining or surpassing state-of-the-art accuracy. Key innovations include the Re-parameterizable Vision-Language Path Aggregation Network for efficient cross-modal fusion, a region-text contrastive pre-training scheme unifying detection, grounding, and image-text data, and a prompt-then-detect paradigm enabling efficient deployment with offline vocabulary encoding. The approach demonstrates that small, efficient detectors can be endowed with strong open-vocabulary capabilities through large-scale vision-language pre-training, offering significant practical advantages for real-world applications.

380bebc106baa23e14189a213509b4181389c419.title: Decentralized Monte Carlo Tree Search for Partially Observable Multi-agent Pathfinding
380bebc106baa23e14189a213509b4181389c419.research_question: How can decentralized agents efficiently solve lifelong multi-agent pathfinding problems under partial observability and limited communication, achieving high throughput and robust coordination in complex, dynamic environments?
380bebc106baa23e14189a213509b4181389c419.hypothesis: A decentralized planning approach that combines neural Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) with a lightweight, learnable policy will enable agents to effectively coordinate and achieve higher throughput than existing state-of-the-art learnable MAPF solvers, even in partially observable and communication-restricted settings.
380bebc106baa23e14189a213509b4181389c419.proposed_method: A decentralized framework is developed in which each agent plans independently using a variant of neural Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) tailored to multi-agent, partially observable environments. Each agent constructs an intrinsic Markov Decision Process (IMDP) based on its local observations, which include a limited field of view of other agents and static obstacles, as well as cost-to-go information computed via breadth-first search. The MCTS search tree is grown using a compact neural network policy (COSTTRACER), pre-trained via Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), to provide action probabilities and value estimates for simulation and node evaluation. During planning, full joint actions are considered for nearby agents, while distant agents are simulated using a greedy policy, significantly reducing computational complexity. The approach does not require explicit inter-agent communication and is designed for scalability and computational efficiency.
380bebc106baa23e14189a213509b4181389c419.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on diverse environments, including random 20x20 grids with varying obstacle densities (0%-30%), maze-like maps of sizes 10x10, 20x20, and 30x30, and a large 33x46 warehouse map, with up to 192 agents. The proposed method is compared against state-of-the-art learnable MAPF solvers PRIMAL2 and SCRIMP, using their official implementations and pretrained weights. Evaluation metrics include average throughput (average number of goals reached per timestep), as well as decision time per agent. The experimental setup includes 512-timestep episodes, agents with 11x11 observation fields, and ablation studies to assess the impact of key components (e.g., number of MCTS expansions, use of COSTTRACER, proximal planning). Hyperparameters are tuned via Bayesian optimization, and the neural policy is trained using PPO with a dense reward for progress toward goals.
380bebc106baa23e14189a213509b4181389c419.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a decentralized neural MCTS framework for lifelong MAPF that operates under partial observability and without explicit agent communication. Key innovations include the use of a lightweight, learnable policy within MCTS simulations for efficient and scalable planning, the construction of intrinsic MDPs from local observations, and a proximal planning mechanism that focuses computational effort on nearby agents. The method achieves superior throughput and generalization compared to state-of-the-art learnable MAPF solvers, while maintaining computational efficiency and scalability to large agent populations and complex environments.

38115e80d805fb0fb8f090dc88ced4b24be07878.title: CodeGen: An Open Large Language Model for Code with Multi-Turn Program Synthesis
38115e80d805fb0fb8f090dc88ced4b24be07878.research_question: How can large language models be leveraged to improve program synthesis, particularly in multi-turn scenarios where user intent is specified progressively in natural language, and what are the effects of model and data scaling on synthesis performance?
38115e80d805fb0fb8f090dc88ced4b24be07878.hypothesis: Multi-turn factorization of user intent specifications enables large language models to better understand and fulfill program synthesis tasks, resulting in higher synthesis accuracy compared to single-turn specifications. Increasing model size and training data volume further enhances multi-turn program synthesis capabilities.
38115e80d805fb0fb8f090dc88ced4b24be07878.proposed_method: A family of large autoregressive transformer language models, termed CODEGEN, will be trained on a combination of natural language and programming language corpora, including THEPILE, BIGQUERY (multi-lingual code), and BIGPYTHON (Python code). Models will be trained in sequential stages, starting with natural language, followed by multi-lingual code, and finally mono-lingual Python code, with model sizes ranging from 350M to 16.1B parameters. The training objective will be next-token prediction, leveraging noisy supervision from interleaved code and natural language comments. A novel multi-turn program synthesis paradigm will be developed, where user intent is communicated in multiple natural language turns, and the model generates subprograms at each step. A custom training library (JAXFORMER) will be used to enable efficient large-scale training on TPU-v4 hardware.
38115e80d805fb0fb8f090dc88ced4b24be07878.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both single-turn and multi-turn program synthesis benchmarks. For single-turn evaluation, the HumanEval benchmark (164 hand-written Python programming problems) will be used, measuring functional correctness via pass@k metrics. For multi-turn evaluation, a new Multi-Turn Programming Benchmark (MTPB) will be constructed, containing 115 diverse problems decomposed into three or more natural language prompts per problem, each with five test cases. Models will be compared against baselines such as GPT-NEO, GPT-J, and OpenAI Codex models. Evaluation metrics will include pass rates and prompt perplexity as a proxy for user intent understanding. Sampling strategies (e.g., nucleus sampling with top-p) and temperature sweeps will be applied to generate code completions, and outputs will be validated by executing the generated code in isolated environments.
38115e80d805fb0fb8f090dc88ced4b24be07878.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first open-source family of large language models for code synthesis up to 16.1B parameters, trained on both natural and programming language data. A novel multi-turn program synthesis paradigm is proposed, enabling progressive user intent specification and subprogram generation. The Multi-Turn Programming Benchmark (MTPB) is developed to quantitatively evaluate multi-step synthesis capabilities. The approach demonstrates that multi-turn factorization of user intent significantly improves synthesis accuracy, especially for complex tasks, and that synthesis capacity scales with model and data size. All model checkpoints and the custom training library will be released as open source to foster further research.

381ab7a640f5b46b62f7e08d1af4a8e0d3eadd55.title: G-Eval: NLG Evaluation using GPT-4 with Better Human Alignment
381ab7a640f5b46b62f7e08d1af4a8e0d3eadd55.research_question: How can the evaluation of natural language generation (NLG) systems be improved to better align with human judgments, particularly for open-ended and creative tasks, without relying on costly human references?
381ab7a640f5b46b62f7e08d1af4a8e0d3eadd55.hypothesis: A large language model-based evaluation framework that incorporates chain-of-thought reasoning and a form-filling paradigm will achieve higher correlation with human quality judgments than existing reference-based, reference-free, and neural evaluation metrics.
381ab7a640f5b46b62f7e08d1af4a8e0d3eadd55.proposed_method: A novel evaluation framework, G-EVAL, will be developed utilizing large language models (LLMs) such as GPT-4 as the backbone. The method will employ a prompt-based approach, where the evaluation prompt includes a task introduction and explicit evaluation criteria tailored to the NLG task (e.g., coherence, fluency, relevance). Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting will be used to automatically generate detailed evaluation steps, providing the LLM with structured reasoning guidance. The evaluation will be conducted in a form-filling paradigm, where the LLM outputs discrete scores for each criterion, and the final metric will be computed as a probability-weighted sum of possible scores, enabling fine-grained, continuous evaluation. This approach is designed to be reference-free and adaptable to new NLG tasks.
381ab7a640f5b46b62f7e08d1af4a8e0d3eadd55.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple NLG tasks, specifically text summarization and dialogue generation. Three meta-evaluation benchmarks will be used: SummEval (for summarization, with human ratings on fluency, coherence, consistency, and relevance), Topical-Chat (for dialogue, with human ratings on naturalness, coherence, engagingness, and groundedness), and QAGS (for factual consistency in summarization). The proposed method will be compared against a range of baselines, including n-gram-based metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, METEOR), embedding-based metrics (BERTScore, MoverScore), neural evaluators (BARTScore, UniEval), and LLM-based evaluators (GPTScore). Evaluation will focus on correlation with human judgments using metrics such as Spearman, Kendall-Tau, and Pearson correlation. Additional analyses will include ablation studies on the effect of chain-of-thought prompting, probability normalization, and model size, as well as investigation of potential bias towards LLM-generated texts.
381ab7a640f5b46b62f7e08d1af4a8e0d3eadd55.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the use of chain-of-thought prompting and a form-filling paradigm for NLG evaluation with LLMs, enabling automatic generation of detailed evaluation steps and fine-grained, probability-weighted scoring. This approach is claimed to achieve substantially higher correlation with human judgments than prior reference-based, reference-free, and neural metrics, particularly for open-ended and creative NLG tasks. The method is reference-free, adaptable to new tasks, and provides insights into the behavior and potential biases of LLM-based evaluators. Preliminary analysis highlights the risk of bias towards LLM-generated texts, raising awareness of self-reinforcement issues in LLM evaluation.

381cf65c9c404caf6adaa754323646429cf456a1.title: Compositional simulation-based inference for time series
381cf65c9c404caf6adaa754323646429cf456a1.research_question: How can simulation-based Bayesian inference for time series generated by Markovian scientific simulators be made more simulation-efficient and scalable, particularly for high-dimensional or long time series data?
381cf65c9c404caf6adaa754323646429cf456a1.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging the Markovian structure of time series simulators by performing local inference on single-state transitions and composing these local results can yield accurate and simulation-efficient global posterior approximations for parameter inference, outperforming conventional amortized simulation-based inference methods that require full time series simulations.
381cf65c9c404caf6adaa754323646429cf456a1.proposed_method: A compositional simulation-based inference framework will be developed for Markovian time series simulators. The method will focus on training neural networks, such as neural posterior score estimators (FNSE), neural likelihood estimators (FNLE), and neural ratio estimators (FNRE), using datasets of single-step state transitions rather than full time series. Local posterior or likelihood information will be estimated for each transition, and a principled composition rule will be applied to aggregate these local estimates into a global posterior or likelihood for the entire time series. The approach will include the design of appropriate proposal distributions for sampling single-state transitions and will address the technical challenge of composing local scores into a global score, using covariance-based approximations and, where necessary, Jacobian-based corrections. The method will be extensible to higher-order Markov chains and partially factorized approaches that amortize over multiple transitions.
381cf65c9c404caf6adaa754323646429cf456a1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of synthetic benchmark tasks (e.g., Gaussian Random Walk, Mixture Random Walk, Periodic/Linear SDEs, Double-well SDE), as well as on established scientific simulators from ecology (Lotka-Volterra) and epidemiology (SIR model). A high-dimensional Kolmogorov flow simulator will be used to test scalability. Baselines will include non-factorized neural posterior estimation (NPE) with embedding networks, as well as other amortized SBI methods. Evaluation metrics will include sliced Wasserstein distance (sW1), classifier two-sample test accuracy (C2ST), and mean absolute error (MAE) between posterior predictive and observed data. Simulation budgets will be strictly controlled, and performance will be assessed as a function of sequence length, dimensionality, and proposal distribution design. Repeated runs with different random seeds and simulation-based calibration analyses will be performed to assess robustness and calibration.
381cf65c9c404caf6adaa754323646429cf456a1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a compositional simulation-based inference framework that leverages the Markovian structure of time series simulators, enabling local inference on single-state transitions and efficient composition into global posterior approximations. This method significantly reduces simulation costs compared to conventional amortized SBI methods that require full time series simulations. The approach is demonstrated to be scalable to high-dimensional simulators and is adaptable to various neural inference paradigms (score, likelihood, ratio estimation). The framework generalizes and extends prior i.i.d. compositional inference techniques to the Markovian time series setting, which is highly relevant for mechanistic scientific simulators.

3827f3e62e0066a4b6ebb123a64666a6dddcc14a.title: Improved Uncertainty Quantification for Neural Networks With Bayesian Last Layer
3827f3e62e0066a4b6ebb123a64666a6dddcc14a.research_question: How can uncertainty quantification in neural networks be improved, particularly in the context of safety-critical applications and extrapolation regimes, while maintaining computational efficiency and scalability?
3827f3e62e0066a4b6ebb123a64666a6dddcc14a.hypothesis: Introducing a reformulated log-marginal likelihood for neural networks with a Bayesian last layer, combined with an affine cost-based extrapolation metric and adaptive penalty parameter, will yield more accurate and calibrated uncertainty estimates—especially for extrapolation points—compared to standard Bayesian linear regression and full Bayesian neural networks trained with variational inference.
3827f3e62e0066a4b6ebb123a64666a6dddcc14a.proposed_method: A neural network architecture with deterministic weights in all hidden layers and a Bayesian (Gaussian-distributed) last linear output layer will be employed. The method reformulates the log-marginal likelihood (LML) for this network, enabling efficient gradient-based training via backpropagation by avoiding explicit matrix inversions and introducing the last-layer weights as optimization variables. To address uncertainty quantification for extrapolation points, an affine cost metric is developed, quantifying the degree of extrapolation in the learned feature space. The extrapolative uncertainty is then adaptively calibrated by tuning a scalar penalty parameter (alpha) using validation data, maximizing the log-predictive density for out-of-distribution points. The approach is extended to the multivariate output case, leveraging assumptions of independent noise and priors across outputs for computational tractability.
3827f3e62e0066a4b6ebb123a64666a6dddcc14a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on simulated regression datasets with known ground truth, including both univariate and multivariate output scenarios. Neural networks with Bayesian last layers will be compared against Bayesian linear regression using features from a trained neural network and full Bayesian neural networks trained with variational inference (Bayes by Backprop). Evaluation metrics will include mean squared error, negative log-marginal likelihood, and mean log-predictive density, with particular focus on test and extrapolation points. The effect of the adaptive penalty parameter on extrapolation uncertainty will be systematically explored, and validation data will be used to tune this parameter for optimal predictive calibration. Analytical computation of predictive distributions will be contrasted with Monte Carlo sampling required by full BNNs.
3827f3e62e0066a4b6ebb123a64666a6dddcc14a.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel, efficient reformulation of the log-marginal likelihood for neural networks with a Bayesian last layer, enabling direct gradient-based optimization without the need for sampling or matrix inversion. It further presents a new affine cost-based metric for quantifying extrapolation in the feature space and leverages this to adaptively calibrate extrapolative uncertainty. The approach provides analytical predictive distributions, improved uncertainty quantification for out-of-distribution points, and demonstrates superior log-predictive density compared to both Bayesian linear regression with fixed features and full Bayesian neural networks trained with variational inference.

382ba0c4452aab6ecdaf8a62d567bb3c4684e4f0.title: ToxiGen: A Large-Scale Machine-Generated Dataset for Adversarial and Implicit Hate Speech Detection
382ba0c4452aab6ecdaf8a62d567bb3c4684e4f0.research_question: How can large-scale, balanced datasets of implicit toxic and benign language about minority groups be generated to improve the detection of adversarial and subtle hate speech, and how can such datasets be leveraged to enhance the robustness and fairness of toxicity classifiers?
382ba0c4452aab6ecdaf8a62d567bb3c4684e4f0.hypothesis: A machine-generated, balanced dataset of toxic and benign statements about minority groups, created via demonstration-based prompting and adversarial classifier-in-the-loop decoding, will improve the ability of toxicity classifiers to detect implicit and adversarial hate speech, while reducing spurious correlations between minority mentions and toxicity.
382ba0c4452aab6ecdaf8a62d567bb3c4684e4f0.proposed_method: A novel dataset generation framework will be developed that uses demonstration-based prompting to guide a large pretrained language model (such as GPT-3) to produce both toxic and benign statements about 13 minority groups, focusing on implicit rather than explicit toxicity. To ensure the generated data is challenging for existing classifiers, an adversarial decoding algorithm (ALICE) will be implemented, which incorporates a toxicity classifier in the loop during constrained beam search decoding. This approach allows for the generation of statements that either maximize or minimize the classifier's toxicity score, depending on the prompt, thus producing both adversarial toxic and detoxified benign examples. The method will balance the dataset across groups and toxicity classes, and will include human-in-the-loop curation to ensure quality and diversity of prompts and generated statements.
382ba0c4452aab6ecdaf8a62d567bb3c4684e4f0.experiment_details: Experiments will involve generating a large-scale dataset (over 274,000 statements) using the proposed framework, with equal representation of toxic and benign statements for each of the 13 minority groups. Human validation will be conducted on a challenging subset of the data, with annotators assessing whether statements are human- or machine-generated, their perceived toxicity, intent, and group framing. The effectiveness of the dataset will be evaluated by fine-tuning state-of-the-art toxicity classifiers (e.g., HateBERT, RoBERTa-based models) on the generated data and measuring performance improvements on three publicly available human-written implicit hate speech datasets: Implicit Hate Corpus, Social Bias Frames, and DynaHate. Evaluation metrics will include AUC and agreement rates, and comparisons will be made between models trained on different subsets of the generated data (ALICE, top-k, and combined).
382ba0c4452aab6ecdaf8a62d567bb3c4684e4f0.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first large-scale, machine-generated dataset specifically targeting implicit hate speech and balanced across toxic and benign statements for multiple minority groups. The adversarial classifier-in-the-loop decoding method (ALICE) is a novel approach for generating challenging examples that can fool existing toxicity classifiers and improve their robustness. The dataset enables fine-grained control over group mentions and implicitness, addressing limitations of prior scraped datasets that suffer from spurious correlations and imbalance. Human validation demonstrates that the generated statements are indistinguishable from human-written text, and experiments show substantial improvements in classifier performance on both machine-generated and real-world human-written implicit hate speech data.

38333f6e8f0388968edc4b2ea7a683ce69677e69.title: Monte Carlo Tree Search Boosts Reasoning via Iterative Preference Learning
38333f6e8f0388968edc4b2ea7a683ce69677e69.research_question: How can the reasoning capabilities of large language models be enhanced through iterative preference learning, and what is the impact of leveraging granular, step-level feedback and search-based data collection strategies on model alignment and performance in complex reasoning tasks?
38333f6e8f0388968edc4b2ea7a683ce69677e69.hypothesis: Iterative preference learning, when combined with step-level preference data collected via Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) and direct policy optimization, will significantly improve the reasoning abilities and alignment of large language models on arithmetic and commonsense reasoning tasks compared to instance-level or offline preference learning approaches.
38333f6e8f0388968edc4b2ea7a683ce69677e69.proposed_method: A novel iterative preference learning framework is developed that integrates Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) for step-level preference data collection with Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) for policy updating. The process begins with a base language model and a prompt dataset. At each iteration, batches of prompts are sampled, and the current model policy generates candidate responses. MCTS is used to explore possible reasoning steps, assigning step-level preferences based on Q-values derived from a combination of outcome correctness and model self-evaluation. The highest and lowest Q-value steps at each reasoning depth are labeled as positive and negative samples, respectively. The model is then updated using DPO with adaptive label smoothing informed by MCTS visit counts, and this cycle is repeated, continuously refining the model's policy with on-policy, step-level preference data.
38333f6e8f0388968edc4b2ea7a683ce69677e69.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a range of arithmetic and commonsense reasoning tasks using the Mistral-7B language model as the base. Datasets include GSM8K and MATH for arithmetic reasoning, and ARC (easy and challenge splits), AI2Science (elementary and middle), OpenBookQA, CommonSenseQA, and SciQ for commonsense reasoning. Baselines for comparison include supervised fine-tuning (SFT), instance-level and offline MCTS preference learning, Self-Taught Reasoner (STaR), Crystal, Direct Tuning, LMSI, and Math-Shepherd. Evaluation metrics are primarily accuracy and pass rate on validation sets. The experimental setup ensures comparable compute budgets across methods, and ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of step-level supervision, online learning, and ground-truth guidance in the preference collection process.
38333f6e8f0388968edc4b2ea7a683ce69677e69.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the use of MCTS as a policy improvement operator for step-level preference data collection in large language models, enabling more granular and effective alignment than traditional instance-level or offline methods. The integration of outcome validation and stepwise self-evaluation within MCTS provides high-quality, adaptive feedback for preference learning. Theoretical analysis demonstrates the superiority of online, on-policy preference sampling for self-improving language models. Empirical results show substantial performance gains on both arithmetic and commonsense reasoning benchmarks, and the method achieves these improvements without the need for separate reward or value networks, highlighting its efficiency and scalability.

3841234dd49250c4fcbba79eed6593d3b57932c1.title: Language Model Crossover: Variation through Few-Shot Prompting
3841234dd49250c4fcbba79eed6593d3b57932c1.research_question: Can large language models be leveraged as general-purpose, domain-independent variation operators for evolutionary algorithms, enabling effective crossover and evolution of text-represented genotypes across diverse domains such as binary strings, mathematical expressions, natural language, image generation prompts, and code?
3841234dd49250c4fcbba79eed6593d3b57932c1.hypothesis: Large language models, when used with few-shot prompting, can serve as intelligent and effective crossover operators in evolutionary algorithms, generating high-quality, heritable, and domain-appropriate offspring from text-based parent genotypes without requiring domain-specific variation operators.
3841234dd49250c4fcbba79eed6593d3b57932c1.proposed_method: A novel crossover operator, Language Model Crossover (LMX), is developed by concatenating a small set of parent genotypes (expressed as text) into a prompt and feeding this prompt into a large pre-trained language model (LLM). The LLM, utilizing its in-context learning and pattern completion capabilities, generates new candidate solutions (offspring) as output, which are then parsed and incorporated into the evolutionary process. The method is domain-agnostic, requiring only that the genotype be representable as text, and can be integrated into standard evolutionary algorithms by replacing traditional crossover operators with LMX. The approach is simple to implement, requiring only prompt construction and output parsing, and can flexibly utilize different LLMs, including domain-specialized models, depending on the target application.
3841234dd49250c4fcbba79eed6593d3b57932c1.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted across five domains: binary strings, symbolic regression (mathematical expressions), sentiment modification in natural language, text-to-image prompt generation, and Python code synthesis. For binary strings, various Pythia LLMs (70M to 6.9B parameters) are used to assess the impact of model size and number of parents on offspring validity and novelty, as well as to compare LMX-driven evolution to classical one-point crossover on the OneMax problem. In symbolic regression, the GALACTICA-1.3B model is employed to evolve mathematical expressions on the SRBench 'banana' dataset, using R^2 and expression size as evaluation metrics, and comparing performance to existing Pareto fronts. Across all domains, baselines include traditional genetic operators or random sampling, and evaluation focuses on offspring validity, novelty, heritability, and optimization performance. The experimental setup includes prompt formatting, output parsing, population management, and fitness-based selection, with domain-specific adaptations as needed.
3841234dd49250c4fcbba79eed6593d3b57932c1.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple, domain-independent evolutionary crossover operator that leverages the in-context learning and pattern completion abilities of large language models. This approach eliminates the need for hand-designed, domain-specific variation operators and enables the evolution of semantically rich text-based genotypes across a wide range of applications. The method is highly versatile, easily integrates with existing evolutionary algorithms, and benefits from ongoing advances in language model capabilities and the growing ecosystem of specialized foundation models. Experimental results demonstrate that LMX can generate valid, novel, and heritable offspring, and can drive effective evolutionary search in domains traditionally considered challenging for generic operators.

3846545fe2082a15e8075fbfd960eaf56ce779d7.title: Label Propagation with Weak Supervision
3846545fe2082a15e8075fbfd960eaf56ce779d7.research_question: How can semi-supervised label propagation methods be enhanced by incorporating weak supervision, specifically by leveraging multiple sources of noisy prior information, to improve classification performance in settings with limited labeled data?
3846545fe2082a15e8075fbfd960eaf56ce779d7.hypothesis: Incorporating weakly supervised prior information and multiple noisy label sources into the label propagation framework will improve the accuracy and coverage of semi-supervised classification, outperforming standard label propagation and existing weakly supervised learning methods.
3846545fe2082a15e8075fbfd960eaf56ce779d7.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed to extend classical label propagation algorithms by integrating probabilistic prior information, such as hypothesized labels from weak labelers, into the propagation process. The method will formulate an optimization problem that regularizes predictions to be both smooth over a constructed graph and close to the provided priors, with a tunable parameter controlling the trade-off. To handle multiple sources of noisy information, the graph will be augmented with 'dongle' nodes representing each weak labeler, and edge weights will be determined by estimated accuracies or probabilistic models of labeler reliability. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to derive error bounds that explicitly account for graph geometry, smoothness, and prior quality, providing guidance on when to rely more on graph-based propagation versus prior information.
3846545fe2082a15e8075fbfd960eaf56ce779d7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four binary classification datasets from the WRENCH benchmark, utilizing features extracted from pretrained BERT and ResNet models for text and image data, respectively. Each experiment will use a small, randomly sampled set of 100 labeled points, with the remainder of the data treated as unlabeled. The proposed methods will be compared against standard label propagation, graph convolutional networks, and several state-of-the-art weakly supervised learning baselines, including Snorkel, FlyingSquid, Constrained Label Learning, and Liger. Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy and coverage on held-out data, as well as pseudolabel accuracy and coverage on the training set. Hyperparameters such as graph connectivity and edge weights will be tuned, and all results will be averaged over multiple random seeds to ensure robustness.
3846545fe2082a15e8075fbfd960eaf56ce779d7.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a theoretically grounded framework for label propagation that incorporates general prior information, including multiple sources of weak supervision, with a novel error bound that accounts for both graph structure and prior accuracy. The approach enables the integration of weak labelers via graph augmentation with dongle nodes and provides practical strategies for weighting multiple noisy sources. Empirical results are expected to show significant improvements over both standard semi-supervised and weakly supervised baselines, demonstrating the benefits of combining smoothness assumptions with weak supervision in a unified framework.

3849bc9782cbb69b6ac9d51aff5530536a43e406.title: Tree of Preferences for Diversified Recommendation
3849bc9782cbb69b6ac9d51aff5530536a43e406.research_question: How can recommendation systems be enhanced to provide more diversified suggestions to users while maintaining high relevance, particularly in the presence of inherent data biases that obscure underexplored user preferences?
3849bc9782cbb69b6ac9d51aff5530536a43e406.hypothesis: Leveraging large language models (LLMs) to systematically reason about user behavior through a hierarchical structure of preferences, and augmenting training data with synthetic interactions that reflect underexplored interests, will improve recommendation diversity without sacrificing relevance, even in the presence of data biases.
3849bc9782cbb69b6ac9d51aff5530536a43e406.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that constructs a global, hierarchical Tree of Preferences (ToP) to model user interests from coarse to fine granularity using LLMs. The method first encodes item attributes with a pretrained language model (e.g., BERT), clusters items to sample a representative subset, and prompts the LLM to partition the preference space into a tree. For each user, the LLM performs top-down reasoning over the ToP to identify both observed and underexplored preferences based on their interaction history and attributes. Candidate items are matched to the user's inferred preferences by assigning each item to its most relevant leaf node in the ToP using LLM-based semantic matching. Synthetic user-item interactions are generated for items covering underexplored preferences, balancing relevance (via semantic similarity) and diversity (via preference frequency), and these are integrated with observed data to train a general recommender. To improve efficiency, a dynamic user selection strategy is employed, identifying influential users for augmentation based on gradient alignment with the model's parameter trajectory.
3849bc9782cbb69b6ac9d51aff5530536a43e406.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on three real-world datasets: Twitter, Weibo, and Amazon, each containing user attributes and item metadata. The datasets are preprocessed to retain active users and informative items, and user/item textual attributes are enhanced using LLM-generated summaries. The proposed method is compared against nine baselines, including heuristic, conventional, and LLM-based diversified recommenders. Evaluation metrics include Recall@k (R@k) for relevance and Category-Entropy@k (CE@k) for diversity, with k set to 50 and 100. The backbone recommender is implemented as LightGCN, and all models are trained with Adam optimizer and evaluated using repeated runs for statistical reliability. Hyperparameters such as the number of selected leaf nodes, augmentations per user, and the diversity-relevance balancing weight are tuned. Inference latency is also measured and compared.
3849bc9782cbb69b6ac9d51aff5530536a43e406.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a global, hierarchical Tree of Preferences structure for fine-grained modeling of user interests, enabling systematic LLM-based reasoning to uncover underexplored preferences. The method integrates synthetic interaction generation based on both diversity and relevance, and employs a dynamic, gradient-based user selection mechanism for efficient augmentation. This framework is claimed to achieve superior diversity-relevance trade-offs and inference efficiency compared to both conventional and LLM-based baselines, and is applicable to generic recommender backbones.

385c74957858e7d6856d48e72b5a902b4c1aa28c.title: Encouraging Divergent Thinking in Large Language Models through Multi-Agent Debate
385c74957858e7d6856d48e72b5a902b4c1aa28c.research_question: How can large language models be encouraged to engage in more divergent and effective reasoning, particularly for complex tasks that require deep contemplation and are prone to errors from overconfidence or cognitive rigidity?
385c74957858e7d6856d48e72b5a902b4c1aa28c.hypothesis: Introducing a multi-agent debate framework, where multiple language model agents argue in a structured manner and a judge moderates the process, will mitigate the Degeneration-of-Thought problem in self-reflection and lead to more accurate and diverse solutions on challenging reasoning tasks.
385c74957858e7d6856d48e72b5a902b4c1aa28c.proposed_method: A novel Multi-Agent Debate (MAD) framework is proposed, consisting of multiple debater agents (e.g., affirmative and negative) and a judge agent. The process begins with meta prompts that introduce the debate topic, the number of debaters, and the debate rules, including a 'tit for tat' requirement to encourage disagreement and exploration of alternative solutions. In each debate iteration, debaters sequentially present their arguments based on the debate history, explicitly disagreeing and providing justifications. The judge agent monitors the debate and operates in either discriminative mode (deciding if a correct solution has emerged) or extractive mode (selecting the best answer from the debate history). An adaptive break mechanism allows the judge to terminate the debate early if an optimal answer is reached, preventing unnecessary iterations and potential performance degradation. The framework is designed to correct biases, overcome rigidity, and introduce external feedback through agent interaction.
385c74957858e7d6856d48e72b5a902b4c1aa28c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two challenging benchmarks: Commonsense Machine Translation (CommonMT), which tests ambiguity resolution and commonsense understanding in translation, and Counter-Intuitive Arithmetic Reasoning (CIAR), which requires resisting intuitive traps and performing multi-step logical reasoning. Multiple large language models (e.g., GPT-3.5-Turbo, GPT-4, Vicuna-7b, Vicuna-13b) will serve as debaters and judges. Baseline methods for comparison include standard chain-of-thought prompting, self-reflection, reranking, MAPS, and self-consistency. Evaluation metrics for translation include COMET, BLEURT, and human direct assessment (on a 1-5 scale); for arithmetic reasoning, accuracy is reported. Experiments will systematically vary the number of debaters, the intensity of disagreement ('tit for tat'), judge/debater model combinations, and debate iteration limits to analyze their effects on performance, diversity, and bias mitigation.
385c74957858e7d6856d48e72b5a902b4c1aa28c.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces and formally defines the Degeneration-of-Thought (DoT) problem in self-reflection for LLMs and addresses it with a multi-agent debate framework that explicitly encourages divergent thinking. Key innovations include the use of structured debate with a judge agent, adaptive break for optimal debate termination, and systematic analysis of agent roles and disagreement intensity. The approach is claimed to outperform strong baselines and even surpass more powerful models (e.g., GPT-4) on certain tasks when using less powerful models with the MAD framework. The study also provides new insights into LLM bias as judges and the limitations of long-context modeling in multi-agent settings.

385f0c77e72f95e7df74e98b4ff6b9ab19d52f93.title: Scaling Diffusion Language Models via Adaptation from Autoregressive Models
385f0c77e72f95e7df74e98b4ff6b9ab19d52f93.research_question: How can large-scale diffusion language models be effectively constructed by adapting existing autoregressive language models, and how do these adapted models compare to both traditional autoregressive and existing diffusion models across a range of language modeling, reasoning, and infilling tasks?
385f0c77e72f95e7df74e98b4ff6b9ab19d52f93.hypothesis: Adapting pre-trained autoregressive language models to diffusion language models using a unified training objective and architectural modifications will enable the resulting diffusion models to achieve competitive or superior performance compared to existing diffusion models and approach the capabilities of their autoregressive counterparts, especially in tasks requiring bidirectional context, infilling, and global reasoning.
385f0c77e72f95e7df74e98b4ff6b9ab19d52f93.proposed_method: A novel adaptation framework will be developed to convert pre-trained autoregressive (AR) language models into diffusion language models (DLMs). The adaptation process will unify the training objectives of AR and diffusion models by reformulating the loss functions and leveraging discrete diffusion processes. Key technical components include attention mask annealing, which gradually transitions AR models from causal (unidirectional) to fully bidirectional attention, and the retention of the shift operation to align prediction targets with the next token, preserving the training dynamics of AR models. The architecture will eschew explicit time-embedding layers, relying instead on the model's ability to infer noise levels from input structure. Training will proceed via continual pre-training on large-scale text corpora, initializing from AR model weights and optimizing the diffusion objective with the described modifications.
385f0c77e72f95e7df74e98b4ff6b9ab19d52f93.experiment_details: Experiments will involve adapting AR models of varying sizes (e.g., GPT2 at 127M and 355M parameters, LLaMA2 at 7B parameters) into diffusion models using the proposed adaptation method. Training will utilize large-scale datasets such as FineWeb, SlimPajama, and Starcoder, with up to 200B tokens for the largest models. Evaluation will be conducted on a comprehensive suite of benchmarks, including TriviaQA and Lambada for reading comprehension and long-range dependency, HellaSwag, Winogrande, SIQA, and PIQA for commonsense reasoning, GSM8K for math reasoning (with fine-tuning), ROCStories and Humaneval for infilling and code generation. Metrics will include accuracy, ROUGE scores, pass@1 for code, and perplexity for unconditional generation. Baselines will comprise both the original AR models and state-of-the-art diffusion models (e.g., SEDD, Plaid1B). Additional analyses will assess in-context learning, scaling trends, ablation of adaptation components, and inference efficiency using hardware-optimized implementations.
385f0c77e72f95e7df74e98b4ff6b9ab19d52f93.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first scalable recipe for adapting large pre-trained autoregressive language models into diffusion language models, enabling the construction of DLMs at unprecedented parameter scales (up to 7B). The adaptation method unifies AR and diffusion objectives and introduces attention mask annealing and shift operations tailored for this transition. The resulting models are expected to set new state-of-the-art performance among diffusion language models on a wide range of benchmarks, demonstrate competitive capabilities with AR models, and exhibit unique strengths in bidirectional context modeling, infilling, and efficient inference. Open-source release of models, code, and evaluation toolkits will further advance the field.

3861de24a6bfa19caac3583a68b102fe7c1ce334.title: Can Watermarked LLMs be Identified by Users via Crafted Prompts?
3861de24a6bfa19caac3583a68b102fe7c1ce334.research_question: Can users identify whether a large language model (LLM) is watermarked solely through the use of crafted prompts, and how can watermarking schemes be designed to enhance the imperceptibility of watermarked LLMs against such identification attempts?
3861de24a6bfa19caac3583a68b102fe7c1ce334.hypothesis: Watermarked LLMs introduce consistent, detectable distributional biases under repeated sampling with the same watermark key, which can be exploited by users to identify the presence of watermarks via carefully crafted prompts. Increasing the randomness of watermark key selection will enhance the imperceptibility of watermarked LLMs, making identification significantly more difficult.
3861de24a6bfa19caac3583a68b102fe7c1ce334.proposed_method: A unified black-box identification algorithm, termed Water-Probe, will be developed to detect the presence of watermarking in LLMs regardless of the specific watermarking technique used. The method constructs sets of highly correlated prompts whose output distributions are similar under the LLM. For each prompt, repeated sampling is performed under simulated fixed watermark keys, and the output distributions are estimated. The algorithm then computes the similarity of distributional differences across prompts for different watermark key pairs, using rank transformation and similarity metrics such as cosine similarity. A statistical hypothesis test (z-test) is applied to the average similarity to determine the likelihood that the LLM is watermarked. Additionally, strategies to enhance watermark imperceptibility, such as the Water-Bag approach that increases key randomness by combining multiple master keys and their inversions, will be designed and evaluated.
3861de24a6bfa19caac3583a68b102fe7c1ce334.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of LLMs, including Qwen2.5-1.5B, OPT-2.7B, Llama-3.2-3B, Qwen2.5-3B, Llama2-7B, Mixtral-7B, Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, and Llama2-13B, covering a range of model sizes. The evaluation will include both N-gram based and fixed-key-list based watermarking algorithms, such as KGW, Aar, KGW-Min, KGW-Skip, DiPMark, γ-reweighting, EXP-Edit, and ITS-Edit. Detection accuracy, false positive rates, and robustness will be assessed under various sampling temperatures and sample sizes. Metrics will include average similarity scores, z-scores for statistical significance, F1-scores for watermarked text detection, perplexity (PPL), and detection time. The impact of watermark key randomness and the effectiveness of the Water-Bag strategy will be systematically compared against baseline watermarking schemes.
3861de24a6bfa19caac3583a68b102fe7c1ce334.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first unified black-box algorithm capable of identifying all major types of watermarked LLMs through analysis of distributional consistency across crafted prompts and watermark keys. It establishes the theoretical basis for the detectability of watermarked LLMs, even for distortion-free watermarking schemes. The Water-Bag strategy is proposed as a novel approach to enhancing watermark imperceptibility by randomizing key selection, which is shown to make identification significantly more challenging while preserving detection robustness. The work also systematically analyzes the trade-offs between watermark detectability, imperceptibility, and robustness, providing new insights and practical guidelines for future watermarking algorithm design.

3864b52902f8315f21385c4a6d3ce6c0193e1ab9.title: Conformal Prediction with Large Language Models for Multi-Choice Question Answering
3864b52902f8315f21385c4a6d3ce6c0193e1ab9.research_question: How can robust, distribution-free uncertainty quantification be achieved for large language models in multiple-choice question answering tasks, particularly in high-stakes domains where formal guarantees on prediction error rates are required?
3864b52902f8315f21385c4a6d3ce6c0193e1ab9.hypothesis: Applying conformal prediction to large language models for multiple-choice question answering will yield statistically valid uncertainty estimates that are tightly correlated with prediction accuracy, and these estimates can be leveraged for selective classification and filtering of low-quality outputs, even when model retraining is not feasible.
3864b52902f8315f21385c4a6d3ce6c0193e1ab9.proposed_method: A conformal prediction framework will be adapted for use with large language models (LLMs) on multiple-choice question answering (MCQA) tasks. The approach will use the softmax outputs of an LLM (specifically, LLaMA-13B) to score each possible answer, and prediction sets will be constructed such that the true answer is included with a user-specified probability (1-α). Calibration will be performed using a held-out set, with the least ambiguous set-valued classifier (LAC) score function applied to softmax probabilities. The threshold for prediction set inclusion will be determined by the α-quantile of calibration scores, and prediction sets will be generated accordingly at inference time. The method will be model-agnostic, requiring no retraining or modification of the LLM, and will be evaluated both under the standard exchangeability assumption and when this assumption is violated (e.g., calibration and evaluation on different subject domains).
3864b52902f8315f21385c4a6d3ce6c0193e1ab9.experiment_details: Experiments will use the MMLU benchmark, which covers 57 domains, with a focus on 16 diverse subjects grouped into business, medicine, and computer science. The LLaMA-13B model will be used to generate softmax probabilities for each answer choice, with one-shot prompting and prompt variation (including GPT-4 generated and MMLU-based questions) to ensure robustness. For each subject, data will be split into equal-sized calibration and evaluation sets, and results will be averaged over 100 random trials. Evaluation metrics will include empirical coverage (the proportion of times the true answer is in the prediction set), prediction set size, top-1 accuracy stratified by set size, Expected Calibration Error (ECE), and Maximum Calibration Error (MCE). Baselines will include naive top-k softmax prediction sets and size-stratified coverage analysis. Additional experiments will assess the impact of violating the exchangeability assumption by calibrating on one subject and evaluating on another.
3864b52902f8315f21385c4a6d3ce6c0193e1ab9.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first systematic adaptation of conformal prediction to large language models for multiple-choice question answering, providing model-agnostic, distribution-free uncertainty quantification with formal coverage guarantees. The approach enables selective classification and filtering of low-confidence predictions in LLMs without requiring model retraining or internal modification. The research also investigates the robustness of conformal prediction under violations of the exchangeability assumption, which is critical for real-world deployment where calibration and evaluation data may differ. This work aims to advance trustworthy and reliable use of LLMs in safety-critical applications by offering actionable uncertainty estimates.

386cebdba39d2d5f2862a9ab43a8d807f3863dae.title: Contrastive Preference Learning: Learning from Human Feedback without RL
386cebdba39d2d5f2862a9ab43a8d807f3863dae.research_question: How can policies be efficiently and accurately learned from human preference feedback in general Markov Decision Processes, without relying on reinforcement learning or reward function inference, and in a way that scales to high-dimensional and sequential decision-making problems?
386cebdba39d2d5f2862a9ab43a8d807f3863dae.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that directly optimizing policies using a contrastive objective based on a regret-based model of human preferences, rather than learning a reward function and applying reinforcement learning, will yield policies that better align with human intent, are more computationally efficient, and can scale to high-dimensional and sequential tasks.
386cebdba39d2d5f2862a9ab43a8d807f3863dae.proposed_method: A novel framework, Contrastive Preference Learning (CPL), will be developed to learn policies directly from human preference data using a regret-based model. CPL leverages the principle of maximum entropy reinforcement learning to establish a bijection between the optimal advantage function and the optimal policy, allowing the log-probability of the policy to substitute for the advantage in the preference model. The method formulates a supervised, contrastive loss function that compares the discounted sum of log-probabilities for preferred and non-preferred behavior segments, optimizing the policy to maximize the likelihood of human-preferred behaviors. Regularization techniques, such as an asymmetric bias regularizer, will be incorporated to ensure the learned policy remains close to the data distribution, particularly when learning from finite offline datasets. Pretraining with behavior cloning may be used to initialize the policy before fine-tuning with the CPL objective.
386cebdba39d2d5f2862a9ab43a8d807f3863dae.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the MetaWorld robotics benchmark, using six tasks with both state-based and image-based (64x64 pixel) observations. Policies will be pretrained using supervised learning on suboptimal offline data, then fine-tuned with CPL using synthetic preference datasets generated by comparing segments with an oracle policy. Both dense (all pairwise comparisons) and sparse (one comparison per segment) preference datasets will be evaluated. Baselines will include supervised fine-tuning (SFT), Preference IQL (P-IQL), PPO with KL-constrained reward, and behavior cloning on top-X% of rollouts. Evaluation metrics will focus on task success rates, and computational efficiency (runtime and parameter count) will be reported. Additional experiments will test CPL on real human preference data from the D4RL benchmark, and ablations will be performed on hyperparameters and data density.
386cebdba39d2d5f2862a9ab43a8d807f3863dae.novelty_claims: The proposed approach eliminates the need for reward function learning and reinforcement learning in preference-based policy optimization, enabling fully off-policy, supervised learning from human feedback in general MDPs. CPL is the first method to directly learn optimal policies from regret-based preferences using a contrastive objective, making it simpler, faster, and more parameter-efficient than prior RLHF methods. The method is claimed to scale to high-dimensional and sequential decision-making problems, outperform RL-based baselines on complex manipulation tasks, and maintain theoretical guarantees of consistency and convergence to the optimal policy under the expert's reward function.

38865f9488b2ec41e35cb88c97598dd01b02615c.title: Dynamic Regret Reduces to Kernelized Static Regret
38865f9488b2ec41e35cb88c97598dd01b02615c.research_question: How can dynamic regret in online convex optimization be effectively minimized, particularly in unbounded domains and for arbitrary sequences of loss functions, by leveraging reductions to static regret in suitable function spaces?
38865f9488b2ec41e35cb88c97598dd01b02615c.hypothesis: Dynamic regret minimization can be reduced to static regret minimization in a suitably constructed Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RKHS), enabling the derivation of optimal or near-optimal dynamic regret guarantees for a broad class of loss functions, including linear, strongly convex, and exp-concave losses.
38865f9488b2ec41e35cb88c97598dd01b02615c.proposed_method: A novel reduction is proposed that reframes dynamic regret minimization as static regret minimization in a function space, specifically an RKHS. The approach embeds the sequence of comparator points as evaluations of a function in the RKHS, allowing the use of static regret algorithms in this infinite-dimensional space. The method involves designing translation-invariant kernels with carefully chosen spectral densities to control the trade-off between the RKHS norm of the comparator function and the kernel diagonal entries, ensuring optimal path-length dependencies. The reduction is general and holds for any sequence of loss functions, preserving curvature properties when present, and is compatible with parameter-free and second-order online learning algorithms.
38865f9488b2ec41e35cb88c97598dd01b02615c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in the online convex optimization setting, considering both linear and curved (strongly convex, exp-concave) loss functions. Synthetic and real-world datasets will be used to generate sequences of loss functions and comparator sequences with varying path-lengths and complexities. Baseline algorithms will include classic Online Gradient Descent (OGD), existing dynamic regret algorithms that require prior knowledge of the horizon or path-length, and recent kernelized approaches. Evaluation metrics will focus on dynamic regret relative to the best comparator sequence, with particular attention to path-length and horizon adaptivity, as well as computational efficiency. The impact of different kernel choices and kernel approximation techniques will also be assessed.
38865f9488b2ec41e35cb88c97598dd01b02615c.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to provide a general reduction from dynamic regret to static regret in RKHSs that holds for arbitrary loss sequences, not just linear losses. It enables the derivation of optimal path-length dependent dynamic regret bounds without prior knowledge of the time horizon or need for the doubling trick. The approach yields new scale-free and directionally-adaptive dynamic regret guarantees and can leverage the curvature of loss functions to obtain improved bounds in strongly convex and exp-concave settings. Furthermore, the method is horizon-independent and computationally feasible due to the reproducing property of RKHSs, and it unifies and extends several prior approaches under a single, general framework.

3890d82362d07064687a4b5e9024fc4c92921998.title: MCVD: Masked Conditional Video Diffusion for Prediction, Generation, and Interpolation
3890d82362d07064687a4b5e9024fc4c92921998.research_question: How can a unified, general-purpose framework be developed for high-quality video prediction, unconditional video generation, and interpolation, while maintaining computational efficiency and strong generalization across diverse video datasets?
3890d82362d07064687a4b5e9024fc4c92921998.hypothesis: A masked conditional diffusion model, trained with random masking of past and/or future frames, will enable a single neural network to perform video prediction, unconditional generation, and interpolation with state-of-the-art quality and efficiency, outperforming specialized models trained for individual tasks.
3890d82362d07064687a4b5e9024fc4c92921998.proposed_method: A probabilistic conditional score-based denoising diffusion model will be constructed for video synthesis tasks. The model will be trained to predict blocks of video frames conditioned on available past and/or future frames, with random and independent masking of all past or all future frames during training. This masking strategy allows the network to learn to handle prediction (masking only future or past), unconditional generation (masking both), and interpolation (masking neither) within a single architecture. The core architecture will be a U-Net with 2D convolutions, multi-head self-attention, and a novel conditional normalization technique called SPATIN (SPAce-TIme-Adaptive Normalization), which integrates conditional information from masked frames and noise-level positional encodings. Video generation will be performed autoregressively in a block-wise manner, enabling the synthesis of videos of arbitrary length.
3890d82362d07064687a4b5e9024fc4c92921998.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several standard video datasets of increasing complexity: Stochastic Moving MNIST (SMMNIST), KTH, BAIR, Cityscapes, and UCF-101. Video frames will be resized to 64x64 or 128x128 as appropriate for each dataset. The model's performance will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines including vRNN, Hier-vRNN, SAVP, SRVP, VideoGPT, VideoTransformer, and GAN-based methods. Evaluation metrics will include Frechet Video Distance (FVD), Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), and Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity (LPIPS). Ablation studies will assess the impact of masking strategies, architectural choices (SPATIN vs. concatenation), and block size. Training will be performed with a computational budget of up to 4 GPUs, and sampling will use DDPM or DDIM with 100 steps for efficiency.
3890d82362d07064687a4b5e9024fc4c92921998.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified masked conditional diffusion framework capable of solving video prediction, unconditional generation, and interpolation within a single model, using a simple and efficient 2D convolutional U-Net architecture. The masking-based conditioning procedure is novel in its ability to enable multi-task generalization and regularization, improving performance across all tasks compared to specialized models. The SPATIN normalization technique further enhances the model's ability to integrate spatio-temporal conditional information. The method achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple standard video benchmarks, demonstrating superior quality and diversity of generated videos while maintaining computational efficiency.

38939304bb760473141c2aca0305e44fbe04e6e8.title: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control
38939304bb760473141c2aca0305e44fbe04e6e8.research_question: Can large-scale vision-language models trained on Internet-scale data be directly incorporated into end-to-end robotic control to improve generalization and enable emergent semantic reasoning in robotic policies?
38939304bb760473141c2aca0305e44fbe04e6e8.hypothesis: Integrating pre-trained vision-language models with robotic trajectory data, by expressing robot actions as text tokens and co-fine-tuning on both Internet-scale vision-language tasks and robot data, will result in a single model that generalizes better to novel objects, environments, and instructions, and exhibits emergent semantic reasoning capabilities.
38939304bb760473141c2aca0305e44fbe04e6e8.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that transforms robot actions into discrete text tokens, allowing them to be integrated into the output space of large pre-trained vision-language models (VLMs) such as PaLI-X and PaLM-E. The method involves co-fine-tuning these VLMs on both Internet-scale vision-language datasets (e.g., visual question answering, captioning) and instruction-annotated robotic trajectory data, where each robot demonstration is paired with a natural language instruction and corresponding camera observation. During training, robot actions are discretized (e.g., 6-DoF end-effector positions, gripper extension, and termination command) and mapped to reserved tokens in the model's vocabulary. The model is trained to output either natural language or action tokens depending on the task, with output constraints ensuring valid action tokens for robot control. Real-time inference is enabled by deploying the large models as a cloud service, allowing robots to query the model over a network for closed-loop control.
38939304bb760473141c2aca0305e44fbe04e6e8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a 7-DoF mobile manipulator, leveraging a combination of Internet-scale vision-language datasets and a large-scale robot demonstration dataset collected over 17 months with 13 robots in an office kitchen environment. The evaluation will include approximately 6,000 real-world robotic trials across seen and unseen tasks, objects, backgrounds, and environments. Baselines for comparison will include RT-1 (a transformer-based policy), VC-1 and R3M (pre-trained representation models), and MOO (a VLM-based semantic mapping approach). Success rates will be measured for both in-distribution and out-of-distribution generalization, as well as for emergent semantic reasoning tasks (e.g., symbol understanding, visual reasoning, multilingual commands, and human recognition). Additional experiments will be performed in the open-source Language-Table simulation environment to assess generalization and transferability. Ablation studies will investigate the effects of model size, training strategy (from scratch, fine-tuning, co-fine-tuning), and the inclusion of chain-of-thought prompting for multi-stage reasoning.
38939304bb760473141c2aca0305e44fbe04e6e8.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the concept of vision-language-action (VLA) models by unifying the output space of vision-language models to include both natural language and robot actions, enabling direct closed-loop robotic control. Unlike prior work, this method leverages the full semantic and visual knowledge of large-scale VLMs without restricting the action space or requiring additional model components for actions. The co-fine-tuning strategy jointly exposes the model to abstract visual concepts and low-level robot actions, leading to improved generalization and emergent reasoning capabilities. The approach is scalable to models with tens of billions of parameters and supports real-time inference via cloud deployment, representing a significant advancement in the integration of web-scale knowledge into robotic control.

38c48a1cd296d16dc9c56717495d6e44cc354444.title: Vision Mamba: Efficient Visual Representation Learning with Bidirectional State Space Model
38c48a1cd296d16dc9c56717495d6e44cc354444.research_question: Can a pure state space model (SSM) backbone provide efficient and effective visual representation learning for high-resolution images and a wide range of vision tasks, without relying on self-attention or 2D inductive biases?
38c48a1cd296d16dc9c56717495d6e44cc354444.hypothesis: A bidirectional state space model with position embeddings can match or surpass the performance of Transformer-based vision backbones on classification, detection, and segmentation tasks, while achieving significantly higher computational and memory efficiency, especially for long visual sequences.
38c48a1cd296d16dc9c56717495d6e44cc354444.proposed_method: A novel vision backbone, termed Vision Mamba (Vim), will be developed based on a bidirectional state space model (SSM) architecture. The method begins by splitting input images into non-overlapping patches, which are linearly projected and embedded with positional information. The resulting patch sequence is processed by stacked Vim blocks, each incorporating bidirectional SSMs to enable data-dependent global context modeling in both forward and backward directions, as well as position embeddings for spatial awareness. The Vim block utilizes 1D convolutions, gating mechanisms, and selective state space updates for both directions, followed by a residual connection and normalization. Classification is performed using a class token or middle-class token strategy, and the architecture is designed for hardware efficiency through optimized memory and computation scheduling.
38c48a1cd296d16dc9c56717495d6e44cc354444.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard vision benchmarks, including ImageNet-1K for image classification, ADE20K for semantic segmentation, and COCO for object detection and instance segmentation. Vim will be pretrained on ImageNet and then fine-tuned or transferred to downstream tasks. Baselines will include ConvNet-based backbones (e.g., ResNet), Transformer-based models (e.g., ViT, DeiT), and other SSM-based models (e.g., S4ND-ViT). Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy for classification, mean Intersection-over-Union (mIoU) for segmentation, and Average Precision (AP) for detection and segmentation. Experiments will also benchmark inference speed (FPS) and GPU memory usage across varying image resolutions, with detailed ablation studies on bidirectionality and classification token design.
38c48a1cd296d16dc9c56717495d6e44cc354444.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first pure SSM-based vision backbone capable of handling dense prediction tasks without attention or 2D priors. It achieves subquadratic computation and linear memory complexity, enabling efficient processing of high-resolution images. The bidirectional SSM design with position embeddings provides robust global context modeling and spatial awareness. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Vim outperforms or matches state-of-the-art Transformer and ConvNet backbones in accuracy, while being significantly faster and more memory-efficient, especially for large input resolutions. The method establishes a new foundation for scalable, efficient visual representation learning suitable for next-generation vision foundation models.

38c8111873cb40d28c8bbc8aa6836a172234b5fa.title: Nash Learning from Human Feedback
38c8111873cb40d28c8bbc8aa6836a172234b5fa.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be more effectively aligned with human preferences using pairwise human feedback, and what alternative fine-tuning pipelines can better capture the diversity and complexity of human preferences compared to traditional reward-based reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) approaches?
38c8111873cb40d28c8bbc8aa6836a172234b5fa.hypothesis: A Nash equilibrium-based approach to learning from human feedback, which directly optimizes policies against a learned preference model rather than a scalar reward model, will result in LLMs that are better aligned with the diversity and richness of human preferences and are less sensitive to the data distribution used for training.
38c8111873cb40d28c8bbc8aa6836a172234b5fa.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a new framework called Nash Learning from Human Feedback (NLHF), which replaces the traditional reward model in RLHF with a pairwise preference model. This preference model is trained (via supervised learning) to predict the probability that one response is preferred over another, given a prompt, using either human or AI-generated feedback. The fine-tuning objective is to find a policy that achieves the Nash equilibrium of this preference model, i.e., a policy that cannot be outperformed by any alternative policy according to the preference scores.
