In the tabular case, a novel algorithm called Nash-MD (Mirror Descent) is developed, which iteratively updates the policy by competing against a geometric mixture of the current and reference policies, ensuring convergence to the regularized Nash equilibrium. For deep learning architectures, gradient-based algorithms (Nash-MD-PG and Nash-EMA-PG) are proposed, which extend the tabular approach to parameterized policies, enabling practical application to LLMs.
38c8111873cb40d28c8bbc8aa6836a172234b5fa.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a text summarization task using the TL;DR dataset. Several variants of the NLHF approach are implemented, including Self-Play, Best-Response, Nash-MD-PG, and Nash-EMA-PG, each corresponding to different strategies for generating the alternative policy during training. The models are evaluated using pairwise comparisons, where a large LLM (PaLM 2 Large) serves as the judge to provide preference signals between model outputs. Baselines include a standard RLHF-trained model and a supervised fine-tuned (SFT) model. Evaluation metrics focus on the pairwise win rates between models, and the impact of the mixture parameter β in Nash-MD-PG is systematically explored to assess the trade-off between self-play and best-response strategies.
38c8111873cb40d28c8bbc8aa6836a172234b5fa.novelty_claims: The proposed approach departs from traditional RLHF by directly optimizing policies with respect to a learned preference model, rather than a scalar reward model, allowing for richer and potentially non-transitive human preferences to be captured. The Nash-MD algorithm is introduced as a novel mirror descent-based method with last-iterate convergence guarantees to the Nash equilibrium, which is particularly advantageous for large models where storing mixtures of past policies is impractical. The deep learning adaptations (Nash-MD-PG and Nash-EMA-PG) enable scalable application to LLMs. The method claims reduced sensitivity to the data distribution and improved alignment with diverse human preferences compared to reward-based RLHF. Experimental results demonstrate the practical feasibility and effectiveness of NLHF on real-world LLM fine-tuning tasks.

38cb9e1786280dc517557855641323e746534611.title: On conditional diffusion models for PDE simulations
38cb9e1786280dc517557855641323e746534611.research_question: How can diffusion models be effectively adapted and conditioned to serve as flexible surrogates for partial differential equation (PDE) simulations, enabling both forecasting and data assimilation tasks, particularly in scenarios with sparse or partial observations?
38cb9e1786280dc517557855641323e746534611.hypothesis: Score-based diffusion models, when equipped with autoregressive sampling strategies, novel training procedures that amortize over history length, and hybrid conditioning mechanisms, can achieve robust and flexible performance for both forecasting and data assimilation in PDE modeling, outperforming or matching existing baselines in accuracy and adaptability.
38cb9e1786280dc517557855641323e746534611.proposed_method: The proposed approach involves developing and systematically comparing several conditional diffusion model architectures for PDE simulation tasks. First, a joint model will be trained on the full trajectory distribution, with an autoregressive (AR) sampling strategy introduced to improve information propagation and effective Markov order compared to all-at-once (AAO) sampling. Second, an amortised model will be constructed to directly learn the conditional score, with a novel training procedure that samples over a range of history lengths, thereby amortizing the conditioning dimension and improving stability across different scenarios. Third, a universal amortised model will be designed to flexibly handle any combination of predictive horizon and conditioning length, and will be further enhanced by combining architectural conditioning with reconstruction guidance, allowing for post-training conditioning on arbitrary sparse observations. All models will leverage a U-Net-based neural architecture for the score network, and sampling will be performed using advanced solvers such as DPM-Solver with appropriate guidance schedules.
38cb9e1786280dc517557855641323e746534611.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on challenging PDE benchmarks, including the 1D Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation and the 2D Kolmogorov flow, with data generated by conventional numerical solvers and discretized in space and time. The models will be evaluated on both forecasting and data assimilation (offline and online) tasks, with varying levels of observation sparsity and conditioning scenarios. Baselines will include state-of-the-art machine learning models such as MSE-trained U-Nets, Fourier Neural Operators (FNO), and PDE-Refiner. Evaluation metrics will include mean squared error (MSE), root mean squared deviation (RMSD), and Pearson correlation, with high correlation time used to assess long-term forecasting accuracy. Computational cost and scalability will also be analyzed, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of window size, guidance strength, and rollout strategies.
38cb9e1786280dc517557855641323e746534611.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces several innovations: (1) an autoregressive sampling strategy for joint diffusion models that theoretically increases the effective Markov order and empirically improves forecasting performance; (2) a novel training procedure for amortised models that amortizes over history length, resulting in stable performance across varying conditioning scenarios; (3) a universal amortised model that flexibly accommodates any combination of predictive and conditioning lengths, eliminating the need for retraining for each scenario; and (4) a hybrid approach that combines architectural conditioning with reconstruction guidance, enabling flexible post-training conditioning on arbitrary sparse observations. This work also provides the first quantitative comparison between joint and amortised diffusion models for PDE simulation under controlled experimental conditions.

38d00f8474a120c0748bbd6697481ea37e2fa390.title: FloE: On-the-Fly MoE Inference on Memory-constrained GPU
38d00f8474a120c0748bbd6697481ea37e2fa390.research_question: How can on-the-fly inference for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models be enabled on memory-constrained GPUs while minimizing inference latency and preserving generative performance?
38d00f8474a120c0748bbd6697481ea37e2fa390.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging untapped intra-expert sparsity within MoE models, combined with hybrid compression (contextual sparsification and ultra-low-bit quantization) and efficient expert prefetching, will enable significant reductions in memory footprint and inference latency on consumer-grade GPUs with minimal performance degradation.
38d00f8474a120c0748bbd6697481ea37e2fa390.proposed_method: A novel inference system, FloE, is proposed to enable efficient on-the-fly MoE inference on memory-constrained GPUs. The method introduces a hybrid compression scheme that applies contextual sparsification to the gate and down projection matrices of each expert, pruning low-magnitude activations based on offline activation statistics, while compressing the up projection matrix using ultra-low-bit quantization (e.g., INT2). Two sparsity predictors are developed: an inter-expert learning-based predictor that forecasts which experts will be activated in the next layer using the current hidden state, and an intra-expert reuse-based predictor that estimates the sparsity distribution for the up projection of the next layer. These predictors facilitate accurate prefetching and pipelining of expert weights. System-level optimizations include a specialized sparse GEMV kernel for efficient computation and a compact, asynchronous transfer mechanism that maximizes PCIe bandwidth utilization by packaging and transferring only the necessary expert weights in large contiguous chunks.
38d00f8474a120c0748bbd6697481ea37e2fa390.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Mixtral-8×7B MoE model, with evaluations on a GeForce RTX 3090 GPU (24GB VRAM) and other GPU types (H100, A100, A6000). End-to-end inference latency and throughput will be measured on the ShareGPT and C4 datasets, with varying input/output sequence lengths and VRAM constraints (down to 11GB). Baseline comparisons will include DeepSpeed-MII (with ZeRO-Infinity), Mixtral-Offloading, Fiddler, and a fully quantized Mixtral-GPU setup. Evaluation metrics will include tokens-per-second (TPS), wall-clock latency, memory footprint, and downstream task accuracy on seven benchmarks (e.g., ARC, BoolQ, SciQ, OpenBookQA, Winogrande, MMLU) using EleutherAI LM Harness. Additional ablations will assess the impact of sparsity and quantization on perplexity and task accuracy.
38d00f8474a120c0748bbd6697481ea37e2fa390.novelty_claims: The proposed approach claims several innovations: (1) the first on-the-fly MoE inference system that exploits intra-expert sparsity for memory-constrained GPUs; (2) a hybrid compression mechanism that combines contextual sparsification and selective ultra-low-bit quantization tailored to expert submatrices; (3) dual sparsity predictors enabling accurate and efficient prefetching of compressed experts, thus overlapping computation and data transfer; (4) a specialized sparse GEMV kernel and compact asynchronous transfer strategy that together maximize computational and I/O efficiency; and (5) empirical demonstration of up to 48.7× inference speedup, 9.3× parameter compression per expert, and deployment on GPUs with as little as 11GB VRAM, all with only 4.4–7.6% average performance degradation.

38d64919ba526868a850a0e5f6239d4c474b7e7e.title: Large Language Models are not Fair Evaluators
38d64919ba526868a850a0e5f6239d4c474b7e7e.research_question: How can the fairness and reliability of large language models (LLMs) as automated evaluators of generative model outputs be improved, particularly in the presence of systematic biases such as positional bias when comparing candidate responses?
38d64919ba526868a850a0e5f6239d4c474b7e7e.hypothesis: LLMs exhibit systematic positional bias when used as evaluators, but this bias can be effectively mitigated through a calibration framework that combines multiple evidence generation, balanced position aggregation, and selective human-in-the-loop intervention, resulting in evaluation outcomes that more closely align with human judgments.
38d64919ba526868a850a0e5f6239d4c474b7e7e.proposed_method: A comprehensive calibration framework will be developed to address positional bias in LLM-based evaluation. The methodology consists of three main components: (1) Multiple Evidence Calibration (MEC), where the LLM is prompted to generate multiple pieces of evaluation evidence before assigning scores, leveraging ensemble techniques to stabilize the evaluation; (2) Balanced Position Calibration (BPC), which evaluates each candidate response in both possible positions (swapping their order) and aggregates the results to compute a final, position-agnostic score; and (3) Human-in-the-Loop Calibration (HITLC), which introduces a Balanced Position Diversity Entropy (BPDE) metric to identify cases with high evaluation uncertainty or bias, selectively routing these to human annotators for adjudication. The framework is designed to be modular, allowing for automatic and semi-automatic operation depending on the difficulty and ambiguity of the evaluation case.
38d64919ba526868a850a0e5f6239d4c474b7e7e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Vicuna Benchmark, which includes 80 questions spanning 9 distinct categories, with candidate responses generated by models such as ChatGPT and Vicuna-13B. Both GPT-4 and ChatGPT will be used as evaluators under various calibration strategies. Baseline methods will include standard (vanilla) LLM evaluation and existing evidence calibration templates. Evaluation metrics will comprise accuracy and kappa correlation coefficient with respect to majority-vote human annotations, as well as conflict rate (the proportion of cases where evaluation outcomes change upon swapping response order). The experimental setup will systematically vary the number of evidence samples (k), temperature settings, and the proportion of examples routed to human annotators, with costs tracked for both human and automated evaluation. Fine-grained analysis will be performed across question categories, and ablation studies will explore the impact of key hyperparameters.
38d64919ba526868a850a0e5f6239d4c474b7e7e.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a systematic analysis of positional bias in LLM evaluators and develops a novel calibration framework that combines multiple evidence generation, balanced position aggregation, and entropy-based human-in-the-loop selection. This approach is claimed to be simple, effective, and cost-efficient, significantly improving alignment with human judgments over standard LLM evaluation pipelines. The use of BPDE for selective human intervention is a novel strategy for optimizing annotation efficiency. The framework is designed to be generalizable across evaluation templates and LLMs, and code and human annotation resources will be released to facilitate future research.

38e19b0007d7ac07e041becdb0761fedc9901c37.title: Calibrated One Round Federated Learning with Bayesian Inference in the Predictive Space
38e19b0007d7ac07e041becdb0761fedc9901c37.research_question: How can federated learning algorithms be designed to achieve well-calibrated predictive uncertainty, efficient communication (ideally in a single round), and robust performance under heterogeneous client data distributions for both regression and classification tasks?
38e19b0007d7ac07e041becdb0761fedc9901c37.hypothesis: Interpolating between a mixture and product of local Bayesian predictive posteriors using a tunable parameter will yield a global model with improved calibration and competitive accuracy, especially under varying degrees of data heterogeneity, compared to existing federated learning aggregation methods.
38e19b0007d7ac07e041becdb0761fedc9901c37.proposed_method: A new federated learning algorithm, termed β-Predictive Bayes, will be developed to aggregate local Bayesian predictive posteriors from clients by interpolating between a mixture model and a product model using a parameter β. Each client will perform local Bayesian inference (e.g., via MCMC sampling) to obtain posterior samples, which are communicated to a central server. The server aggregates the local predictive posteriors using a convex combination in the log space, controlled by β, to form an ensemble predictive model that balances calibration across heterogeneous and homogeneous data regimes. The optimal value of β will be tuned by minimizing the negative log-likelihood on a held-out public (or synthetic) dataset at the server. Finally, knowledge distillation will be applied to compress the ensemble into a single global model, which is then distributed back to clients.
38e19b0007d7ac07e041becdb0761fedc9901c37.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple regression and classification datasets, including MNIST, Fashion MNIST, EMNIST, CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and several UCI regression datasets (e.g., wine quality, air quality, forest fire, real estate, bike rental). Data will be partitioned among five clients with varying degrees of heterogeneity, controlled by a heterogeneity parameter. The evaluation will focus on calibration metrics such as negative log-likelihood (NLL) and expected calibration error (ECE), as well as predictive accuracy. Baselines will include Bayesian Committee Machine (BCM/product), mixture models, FedAvg, FedBE, EP-MCMC, OneshotFL, and other ensemble-based federated learning methods. Each method will be tested under identical experimental setups, with results averaged over multiple random seeds and statistical significance assessed where appropriate.
38e19b0007d7ac07e041becdb0761fedc9901c37.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel Bayesian federated learning aggregation framework that operates in a single communication round, interpolates between mixture and product of predictive posteriors for improved calibration, and is applicable to both regression and classification tasks. The approach provides a theoretically motivated and empirically validated solution for calibration under data heterogeneity, and leverages knowledge distillation to produce a compact global model. The method demonstrates superior calibration and competitive accuracy compared to existing baselines, particularly as data heterogeneity increases.

38f4f27bfdc6cdc4c72d714a097541f1e6ca98f2.title: Inductive Graph Alignment Prompt: Bridging the Gap between Graph Pre-training and Inductive Fine-tuning From Spectral Perspective
38f4f27bfdc6cdc4c72d714a097541f1e6ca98f2.research_question: How can the gap between graph pre-training and inductive fine-tuning be effectively bridged, especially when the fine-tuning graphs differ significantly from the pre-training graphs in both signal and structure?
38f4f27bfdc6cdc4c72d714a097541f1e6ca98f2.hypothesis: Bridging both the graph signal gap and the graph structure gap in the spectral domain using learnable prompts will enable more effective transfer of pre-trained knowledge to inductive fine-tuning tasks, resulting in improved performance on downstream graph tasks even when pre-training data is unavailable.
38f4f27bfdc6cdc4c72d714a097541f1e6ca98f2.proposed_method: A novel framework, Inductive Graph Alignment Prompt (IGAP), is developed to address the data gap between graph pre-training and inductive fine-tuning. The method first analyzes the essence of graph pre-training using spectral graph theory, revealing that pre-training predominantly aligns graph signals with low-frequency spectral components. To bridge the graph signal gap, a learnable graph signal prompt is introduced to adaptively compensate for distributional differences in node features. To address the graph structure gap, a spectral space alignment prompt is designed to align the low-frequency spectral components (the K-smallest eigenvectors) between the pre-training and fine-tuning graphs, enabling transfer of essential knowledge. Additionally, a task-specific label prompt is used to harmonize the fine-tuning objective with the pre-training task. Theoretical analysis is provided to justify the effectiveness of aligning low-frequency components and using compact spectral spaces.
38f4f27bfdc6cdc4c72d714a097541f1e6ca98f2.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both node classification and graph classification tasks under three settings: transductive, semi-inductive, and fully inductive. Datasets include Citeseer, Amazon-Photo, CoraFull/CoraFull-F, Arxiv-P/Arxiv-F, Paper100M-P/Paper100M-F, Reddit-P/Reddit-F for node classification, and Molhiv, Moltox21, Molbace, Molbbbp, Molmuv for graph classification. Baselines include supervised GNNs (GCN, GraphSAGE, GAT), pre-training plus fine-tuning methods (GraphCL, DGI), and prompt-based methods (GPPT, GraphPrompt, All-in-One). Evaluation metrics are classification accuracy for node tasks and ROC-AUC for graph tasks. The experimental setup includes freezing pre-trained GNNs during fine-tuning, training only the prompt and task-specific head, and using mean pooling for graph representations. Hyperparameter studies and ablation analyses are performed to assess the impact of each component.
38f4f27bfdc6cdc4c72d714a097541f1e6ca98f2.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to systematically bridge both the graph signal and structure gaps in the spectral domain for inductive fine-tuning, without requiring access to pre-training data. The method introduces learnable prompts in both the signal and spectral spaces, supported by theoretical analysis from spectral graph theory. The framework unifies mainstream graph pre-training paradigms and demonstrates superior performance over existing transductive and prompt-based methods, especially in challenging inductive settings where pre-training and fine-tuning graphs are disjoint.

38fe8f324d2162e63a967a9ac6648974fc4c66f3.title: PaLM-E: An Embodied Multimodal Language Model
38fe8f324d2162e63a967a9ac6648974fc4c66f3.research_question: How can a general-purpose multimodal language model be developed to enable embodied reasoning and decision-making for robots, integrating diverse sensory modalities and supporting a wide range of tasks across different embodiments?
38fe8f324d2162e63a967a9ac6648974fc4c66f3.hypothesis: A large-scale, unified multimodal language model that directly incorporates continuous sensor modalities (such as images, state vectors, and neural scene representations) into its input space can achieve effective embodied reasoning, outperforming existing vision-language models on robotic planning, perception, and general vision-language tasks, while also benefiting from transfer learning across domains.
38fe8f324d2162e63a967a9ac6648974fc4c66f3.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that injects continuous, embodied observations (e.g., images, state vectors, 3D neural scene representations) into the embedding space of a pre-trained large language model (LLM) such as PaLM. The approach will utilize specialized encoders for each modality (e.g., Vision Transformers for images, MLPs for state vectors, and Object Scene Representation Transformers for 3D scenes) to map observations into the language model's embedding space, forming 'multi-modal sentences' by interleaving these embeddings with text tokens. The model will be trained end-to-end to generate high-level textual outputs, such as plans or answers, which can be interpreted by robots or used for visual-language tasks. The architecture will support both frozen and finetuned LLM backbones, and will investigate object-centric representations and dynamic token placement for flexible multimodal integration.
38fe8f324d2162e63a967a9ac6648974fc4c66f3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across three robotic domains: task and motion planning (TAMP), tabletop pushing (Language-Table), and mobile manipulation in kitchen environments, using both simulated and real robots. The model will be trained on a mixture of robotics datasets (including expert demonstrations and embodied VQA) and large-scale internet vision-language datasets (e.g., VQA, COCO, OK-VQA). Baselines will include state-of-the-art vision-language models (such as PaLI), robotics-specific algorithms (like SayCan), and ablations with different input encoders and training regimes (single-task vs. multi-task, frozen vs. finetuned LLM). Evaluation metrics will include planning success rates, VQA accuracy, captioning scores, and general language understanding/generation benchmarks. The impact of model scale, input representation, and co-training on transfer learning and data efficiency will be systematically analyzed.
38fe8f324d2162e63a967a9ac6648974fc4c66f3.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a unified, generalist multimodal language model capable of embodied reasoning and decision-making across multiple robot embodiments and tasks. Key innovations include the direct injection of continuous sensor modalities into the LLM embedding space, the use of object-centric and 3D-aware scene representations, and dynamic multimodal token placement. The approach demonstrates positive transfer from vision-language domains to robotics, enabling high data efficiency and robust generalization. The model achieves state-of-the-art results on both embodied and general vision-language tasks, and scaling the model size is shown to mitigate catastrophic forgetting of language capabilities during multimodal training.

390b2aa03672d33c760a151bb056b1397bf40cc0.title: Efficient Test-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language Models
390b2aa03672d33c760a151bb056b1397bf40cc0.research_question: How can test-time adaptation of vision-language models be made both efficient and effective in the presence of distribution shifts, without relying on computationally intensive training or backpropagation during testing?
390b2aa03672d33c760a151bb056b1397bf40cc0.hypothesis: A training-free, cache-based dynamic adapter that leverages both positive and negative pseudo labeling can enable vision-language models to efficiently and effectively adapt to distribution shifts at test time, outperforming existing test-time adaptation methods in both accuracy and computational efficiency.
390b2aa03672d33c760a151bb056b1397bf40cc0.proposed_method: A novel training-free dynamic adapter (TDA) is proposed for test-time adaptation of vision-language models such as CLIP. The method constructs two lightweight, non-parametric key-value caches: a positive cache that stores high-confidence pseudo labels and their corresponding image features, and a negative cache that stores negative pseudo labels (indicating class absence) and associated features. During test time, the caches are dynamically updated by progressively incorporating test samples with low-entropy (high-confidence) predictions for the positive cache, and moderate-entropy (uncertain) predictions for the negative cache, while controlling the shot capacity per class. Adapted predictions are generated by combining the outputs from the positive cache, negative cache, and the original CLIP model using a weighted adaptation function. No backpropagation or prompt optimization is performed at test time, ensuring computational efficiency. The method also includes entropy-based prioritization and replacement strategies to maintain high-quality cache entries.
390b2aa03672d33c760a151bb056b1397bf40cc0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two major benchmarks: an out-of-distribution (OOD) benchmark (including ImageNet-A, ImageNet-V2, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-S) and a cross-domain benchmark (including Aircraft, Caltech101, Cars, DTD, EuroSAT, Flower102, Food101, Pets, SUN397, UCF101). The proposed method will be evaluated using pre-trained CLIP models (ResNet-50 and ViT-B/16 backbones) and compared against state-of-the-art baselines, including CLIP, CoOp, CoCoOp, Tip-Adapter, TPT, and DiffTPT. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy and testing time (efficiency). All test-time adaptation methods will be fine-tuned with streams of unlabeled test samples, using batch size 1, and no access to training data. Hyperparameters will be selected on a validation set and fixed for all datasets. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of cache design and shot capacity.
390b2aa03672d33c760a151bb056b1397bf40cc0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to address the computational efficiency of test-time adaptation for vision-language models using a training-free, dynamic cache-based adapter. It introduces a dual-cache mechanism that combines positive and negative pseudo labeling for robust adaptation, and eliminates the need for backpropagation or prompt optimization at test time. The method demonstrates superior accuracy and drastically reduced testing time compared to state-of-the-art test-time adaptation methods, making it highly suitable for real-world deployment.

390da1681d2f8c7c09368618f53ce9bfbbf3c1a1.title: InverseBench: Benchmarking Plug-and-Play Diffusion Priors for Inverse Problems in Physical Sciences
390da1681d2f8c7c09368618f53ce9bfbbf3c1a1.research_question: How can plug-and-play diffusion priors be systematically evaluated and compared for solving a diverse range of scientific inverse problems, and what are their strengths and limitations relative to domain-specific baselines across different physical science applications?
390da1681d2f8c7c09368618f53ce9bfbbf3c1a1.hypothesis: Plug-and-play diffusion prior methods, when trained on suitable datasets, will outperform conventional domain-specific baselines across a variety of scientific inverse problems, demonstrating robustness to changes in forward models and measurement sparsity, but may exhibit limitations in computational efficiency and in handling out-of-distribution sources or physically constrained forward models.
390da1681d2f8c7c09368618f53ce9bfbbf3c1a1.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmarking framework, INVERSEBENCH, will be developed to systematically evaluate plug-and-play diffusion prior (PnPDP) algorithms across five distinct scientific inverse problems: optical tomography (linear inverse scattering), compressed sensing MRI, black hole imaging, full waveform inversion, and the Navier-Stokes equation. The framework will curate domain-specific datasets for each problem, train diffusion models as priors on these datasets, and implement 14 representative PnPDP algorithms spanning guidance-based, variable-splitting, variational Bayes, and sequential Monte Carlo categories. Each algorithm will be interfaced with the corresponding physics-based forward model, which may be linear or nonlinear, closed-form or PDE-based, and will be evaluated under a standardized protocol. The modular design will allow for easy integration of new problems and algorithms, and all code, datasets, and pre-trained models will be open-sourced to facilitate reproducibility and further research.
390da1681d2f8c7c09368618f53ce9bfbbf3c1a1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on curated datasets for each inverse problem: simulated fluorescence microscopy images for linear inverse scattering, multi-coil fastMRI knee data for compressed sensing MRI, GRMHD-simulated black hole images for black hole imaging, CurveFaultB velocity maps for full waveform inversion, and numerically evolved vorticity fields for the Navier-Stokes equation. Each PnPDP method will be benchmarked against strong, domain-specific baselines (e.g., FISTA, pseudo-inverse, Adam, UNet, VarNet, EHT-Imaging, SMILI, etc.) using standardized evaluation metrics such as PSNR, SSIM, ℓ2 error, BlurPSNR, and problem-specific misfit statistics (e.g., χ2 for closure quantities in black hole imaging). Efficiency will be assessed via metrics capturing total and sequential computational cost, including the number of forward model queries. Experiments will also systematically vary measurement sparsity and forward model characteristics to assess robustness, and out-of-distribution scenarios will be tested to evaluate prior mismatch effects.
390da1681d2f8c7c09368618f53ce9bfbbf3c1a1.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces the first comprehensive, extensible framework for evaluating plug-and-play diffusion priors on a wide spectrum of scientific inverse problems beyond natural image restoration. It provides a unified, modular infrastructure for systematic comparison of 14 state-of-the-art PnPDP algorithms and strong domain-specific baselines across five challenging physical science tasks, each with unique structural and computational properties. The benchmark enables new insights into the strengths, weaknesses, and failure modes of PnPDP methods, particularly in handling nonlinear, PDE-based forward models and out-of-distribution sources. All code, datasets, and pre-trained models are open-sourced to accelerate research in this area.

3936fd3c6187f606c6e4e2e20b196dbc41cc4654.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
3936fd3c6187f606c6e4e2e20b196dbc41cc4654.research_question: How can AI systems be trained to be both helpful and harmless, minimizing harmful or evasive behaviors, using minimal human supervision and explicit, transparent behavioral principles?
3936fd3c6187f606c6e4e2e20b196dbc41cc4654.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a language model can be trained to exhibit harmless and non-evasive behavior, while remaining helpful, by leveraging a small set of explicit constitutional principles and AI-generated feedback, thereby reducing or eliminating the need for human-labeled data on harmfulness.
3936fd3c6187f606c6e4e2e20b196dbc41cc4654.proposed_method: A two-stage training process is proposed to develop a harmless and helpful AI assistant. In the first, supervised learning stage, a helpful-only language model is prompted with potentially harmful queries, generates initial responses, critiques its own outputs according to randomly sampled constitutional principles, and revises its responses in light of these critiques. This critique-revision process may be repeated multiple times per prompt, and the final revised responses are used to fine-tune the model. In the second, reinforcement learning stage, the fine-tuned model generates pairs of responses to harmful prompts, and an independent AI model evaluates which response better aligns with the constitutional principles. These AI-generated preference labels are used to train a preference model, which then serves as the reward function in reinforcement learning from AI feedback (RLAIF), further refining the assistant's policy. Chain-of-thought reasoning is incorporated throughout to improve transparency and the quality of critiques and decisions.
3936fd3c6187f606c6e4e2e20b196dbc41cc4654.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize large pretrained language models, with initial helpfulness training conducted via reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) using human-labeled helpfulness data. For harmlessness, a dataset of over 180,000 red-teaming prompts (including both human- and model-generated prompts) will be used to elicit harmful responses, which are then critiqued and revised according to a set of 16 constitutional principles. The revised responses, along with helpfulness samples, are used for supervised fine-tuning. In the RL stage, pairs of responses to harmful prompts are evaluated by an independent AI model using the constitutional principles, and the resulting preference data is used to train a preference model for reinforcement learning. Evaluation is performed using crowdworker comparisons in open-ended conversations, with Elo scores computed for both helpfulness and harmlessness. Baselines include models trained with standard RLHF on helpfulness and harmlessness, and ablations will test the effect of critique steps and the number of constitutional principles.
3936fd3c6187f606c6e4e2e20b196dbc41cc4654.novelty_claims: The proposed approach eliminates the need for human-labeled data on harmfulness by replacing it with AI-generated feedback guided by a transparent, small set of constitutional principles. The method introduces a critique-revision pipeline for self-improvement, leverages chain-of-thought reasoning for greater transparency and decision quality, and demonstrates that AI feedback can match or exceed human feedback in training harmless assistants. The approach also addresses the tradeoff between helpfulness and harmlessness by explicitly discouraging evasive responses and encouraging the assistant to explain its objections, thereby improving both transparency and utility.

3944b751c602010dc02a5dce8641852f42dcf41f.title: A unified recipe for deriving (time-uniform) PAC-Bayes bounds
3944b751c602010dc02a5dce8641852f42dcf41f.research_question: How can a unified and general framework be developed for deriving time-uniform (anytime-valid) PAC-Bayesian generalization bounds for a wide class of stochastic processes, including those with non-i.i.d. data and nonstationary loss functions?
3944b751c602010dc02a5dce8641852f42dcf41f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by systematically combining nonnegative supermartingale or reverse submartingale structures, the method of mixtures, variational representations of convex divergences, and Ville’s inequality, it is possible to derive time-uniform PAC-Bayes bounds that are broadly applicable, recover existing results as special cases, and enable the derivation of new bounds under relaxed assumptions.
3944b751c602010dc02a5dce8641852f42dcf41f.proposed_method: A unified framework will be constructed by integrating four key tools in sequence: (a) identifying or constructing nonnegative supermartingales or reverse submartingales associated with the learning process; (b) applying the method of mixtures to generate mixture processes over hypothesis distributions; (c) leveraging variational representations of convex divergences, such as the Donsker-Varadhan formula for KL divergence, to relate empirical and expected risks; and (d) applying Ville’s inequality (and its reverse-time variant) to obtain time-uniform probability bounds. The approach is designed to handle both forward and reverse-time processes, enabling the derivation of PAC-Bayes bounds that hold at all stopping times and for all data-dependent mixture distributions over hypotheses. The framework is general enough to accommodate nonstationary loss functions and non-i.i.d. data, and can be instantiated with different divergences (e.g., KL, φ-divergences, Rényi divergences) as needed.
3944b751c602010dc02a5dce8641852f42dcf41f.experiment_details: Theoretical validation will be conducted by instantiating the general framework with various choices of stochastic processes and divergences, demonstrating recovery of classical PAC-Bayes bounds (e.g., those of Seeger, McAllester, Maurer, Catoni) as well as recent and novel bounds. Comparative analysis will be performed to evaluate the tightness of time-uniform extensions relative to their fixed-time counterparts, especially for both supermartingale- and reverse submartingale-based bounds. The framework’s flexibility will be illustrated by relaxing traditional assumptions, such as requiring i.i.d. data or stationary losses, and by applying the results to settings like Gaussian process classification. Evaluation metrics will include the tightness of the derived bounds, their validity at stopping times, and their applicability to a broad class of stochastic processes.
3944b751c602010dc02a5dce8641852f42dcf41f.novelty_claims: The proposed framework offers a unified and systematic recipe for deriving time-uniform PAC-Bayesian bounds, subsuming a wide range of existing results and enabling the derivation of new bounds with minimal additional effort. It extends the applicability of PAC-Bayes theory to nonstationary and non-i.i.d. settings, relaxes traditional assumptions, and provides a clear pathway for verifying whether a process admits a time-uniform PAC-Bayes bound. The approach generalizes and unifies previous techniques by combining martingale-based tools, mixture methods, and variational representations, and introduces new anytime-valid PAC-Bayes bounds for classes of stochastic processes not previously covered.

395bfdae59f1a5fde16213cade43d2587e4565df.title: 4D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Dynamic Scene Rendering
395bfdae59f1a5fde16213cade43d2587e4565df.research_question: How can dynamic 3D scenes be efficiently represented and rendered in real time, while maintaining high image quality and minimizing training and storage costs?
395bfdae59f1a5fde16213cade43d2587e4565df.hypothesis: A compact 4D representation that combines explicit 3D Gaussians with a neural deformation field can enable real-time, high-quality rendering of dynamic scenes, outperforming existing methods in speed, quality, and storage efficiency.
395bfdae59f1a5fde16213cade43d2587e4565df.proposed_method: A holistic 4D Gaussian Splatting (4D-GS) framework will be developed to represent dynamic scenes using a single set of canonical 3D Gaussians, augmented by a Gaussian deformation field network. The deformation field network will consist of a spatial-temporal structure encoder, leveraging multi-resolution voxel planes (inspired by HexPlane/K-Planes) to efficiently encode both spatial and temporal features, and a lightweight multi-head MLP decoder to predict per-Gaussian deformations (position, rotation, scaling) at arbitrary timestamps. At each rendering time, the canonical Gaussians will be deformed according to the predicted deformation, and the resulting Gaussians will be splatted onto the image plane using differentiable splatting for novel view synthesis. The method will include a warm-up phase with 3D Gaussian initialization (using structure-from-motion points) to stabilize training and improve convergence.
395bfdae59f1a5fde16213cade43d2587e4565df.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world dynamic scene datasets. Synthetic datasets, such as D-NeRF, will be used to evaluate monocular dynamic scenes, while real-world benchmarks like HyperNeRF and Neu3D will be used for more complex, multi-camera scenarios. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines including TiNeuVox, K-Planes, HexPlane, 3D-GS, FFDNeRF, MSTH, V4D, and Im4D. Evaluation metrics will include PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, MS-SSIM, D-SSIM, rendering FPS, training time, and storage consumption. Ablation studies will assess the contributions of the spatial-temporal encoder, multi-head decoder, and initialization strategy. Rendering speed will be measured at various resolutions and Gaussian counts to validate real-time performance.
395bfdae59f1a5fde16213cade43d2587e4565df.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel 4D Gaussian Splatting framework that jointly models spatial and temporal dynamics via a compact deformation field, enabling real-time rendering of dynamic scenes at high resolutions. The approach leverages a decomposed neural voxel encoding for efficient feature extraction and a multi-head MLP decoder for flexible Gaussian deformation, resulting in significant improvements in rendering speed, storage efficiency, and training time compared to previous methods. Additional contributions include the ability to track and edit 4D objects, and a demonstration of state-of-the-art quality and speed on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

395de0bd3837fdf4b4b5e5f04835bcc69c279481.title: BART: Denoising Sequence-to-Sequence Pre-training for Natural Language Generation, Translation, and Comprehension
395de0bd3837fdf4b4b5e5f04835bcc69c279481.research_question: How can a unified pre-training framework for sequence-to-sequence models be developed to improve performance across a wide range of natural language processing tasks, including text generation, comprehension, and translation?
395de0bd3837fdf4b4b5e5f04835bcc69c279481.hypothesis: A denoising autoencoder pre-training approach, which corrupts input text using flexible noising schemes and trains a sequence-to-sequence model to reconstruct the original text, will yield representations that are broadly effective for both generative and discriminative NLP tasks.
395de0bd3837fdf4b4b5e5f04835bcc69c279481.proposed_method: A novel denoising sequence-to-sequence pre-training framework will be developed, utilizing a Transformer-based architecture with a bidirectional encoder and a left-to-right autoregressive decoder. During pre-training, input documents will be corrupted using a variety of noising functions, including token masking, token deletion, text infilling (replacing spans with a single mask token), sentence permutation, and document rotation. The model will be trained to reconstruct the original, uncorrupted text from these noised inputs by optimizing a cross-entropy loss between the decoder's output and the original document. The architecture will be designed to generalize and unify previous pre-training schemes, enabling the model to learn both bidirectional and autoregressive representations. Fine-tuning procedures will be established for a range of downstream tasks, including sequence classification, token classification, and sequence generation.
395de0bd3837fdf4b4b5e5f04835bcc69c279481.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of benchmark datasets, including SQuAD (extractive question answering), GLUE (multi-task language understanding), XSum and CNN/DailyMail (summarization), ELI5 (abstractive question answering), ConvAI2 (dialogue generation), and WMT16 Romanian-English (machine translation). The proposed model will be compared against strong baselines such as BERT, RoBERTa, XLNet, UniLM, and MASS, using evaluation metrics appropriate to each task (e.g., F1, accuracy, ROUGE, BLEU, perplexity). Both base and large model configurations will be tested, with controlled ablation studies to isolate the effects of different noising schemes and architectural choices. Pre-training will be performed on large-scale corpora (e.g., books, Wikipedia, news, web text) using byte-pair encoding and large batch sizes. Fine-tuning will be tailored to each task, and hyperparameters such as label smoothing, beam search settings, and dropout will be tuned on validation sets.
395de0bd3837fdf4b4b5e5f04835bcc69c279481.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a highly flexible denoising autoencoder pre-training objective for sequence-to-sequence models, capable of incorporating arbitrary noising functions. This approach unifies and generalizes previous pre-training methods (e.g., BERT, GPT, MASS, SpanBERT) within a single architecture, enabling effective transfer to both generative and discriminative tasks. The method demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on multiple text generation benchmarks, significant improvements in abstractive summarization and dialogue, and competitive results on comprehension and classification tasks, all with a single pre-trained model. Additionally, the approach enables improved integration of pre-trained decoders in machine translation systems, surpassing strong back-translation baselines.

3979c82601da1ab57b64a9609f94a0979641dcae.title: Noise Consistency Training: A Native Approach for One-Step Generator in Learning Additional Controls
3979c82601da1ab57b64a9609f94a0979641dcae.research_question: How can new control signals be efficiently and effectively integrated into pre-trained one-step generative models for high-quality, controllable content generation without requiring access to original training data or retraining the base diffusion model?
3979c82601da1ab57b64a9609f94a0979641dcae.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a noise consistency training framework, which operates in the noise space of a pre-trained one-step generator and employs an adapter module with a noise consistency loss and boundary loss, can enable the direct and efficient integration of new control signals, resulting in controllable generation with high fidelity and computational efficiency.
3979c82601da1ab57b64a9609f94a0979641dcae.proposed_method: A novel methodology, Noise Consistency Training (NCT), is proposed for augmenting pre-trained one-step generative models with new control signals. The approach introduces an adapter module that operates in the noise space of the generator, transforming the generator to accept both noise and control inputs. The core of the method is a noise consistency loss, which aligns the generator's outputs across noise levels that are conditionally dependent to varying degrees, thereby guiding the model to adhere to the new control. Additionally, a boundary loss is incorporated to ensure that, when the input condition matches the original generator's output, the adapted generator's output remains consistent with the uncontrollable generation, thus preventing distribution collapse. The optimization is formulated as a constrained saddle-point problem, solved via a primal-dual algorithm that dynamically balances the noise consistency and boundary losses.
3979c82601da1ab57b64a9609f94a0979641dcae.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a pre-trained one-step generator based on Stable Diffusion 1.5, further refined with Diff-Instruct. The method will be evaluated on an internally collected dataset, using four types of control signals: Canny edges, HED boundaries, depth maps, and low-resolution images. Baseline comparisons will include standard diffusion models with ControlNet, one-step generators with ControlNet, and one-step generators trained with JDM distillation. Evaluation metrics will include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for image quality, a consistency metric quantifying alignment between generated outputs and control signals, and the number of function evaluations (NFE) required for generation. Additional experiments will assess image-prompted generation using the IP-Adapter architecture and OpenCLIP ViT-H/14, with CLIP-I and CLIP-T metrics for alignment. Ablation studies will investigate the impact of noise consistency loss, boundary loss, and the primal-dual optimization scheme.
3979c82601da1ab57b64a9609f94a0979641dcae.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first native method for directly integrating new controls into pre-trained one-step generators without requiring access to original training data or additional diffusion distillation. The method is modular, data-efficient, and easily deployable, relying solely on the pre-trained generator and a control signal model. It achieves state-of-the-art controllable generation in a single forward pass, surpassing existing multi-step and distillation-based methods in both image quality and computational efficiency. The framework also supports flexible test-time composition of multiple adapters, enabling multimodal and structural control in a unified manner.

3990671bec3e7cb019dc7ae4a6d71ea0af1a49cb.title: Generalization Bounds for Adversarial Contrastive Learning
3990671bec3e7cb019dc7ae4a6d71ea0af1a49cb.research_question: How can the generalization performance of adversarial contrastive learning be theoretically characterized, particularly in terms of robustness on downstream tasks, and what are the relationships between adversarial risks in upstream and downstream settings for both linear models and multi-layer neural networks?
3990671bec3e7cb019dc7ae4a6d71ea0af1a49cb.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the average adversarial risk of downstream supervised tasks can be upper bounded by the adversarial unsupervised risk of the upstream contrastive learning task, and that robust feature extractors trained with adversarial contrastive learning will yield robust performance on downstream tasks.
3990671bec3e7cb019dc7ae4a6d71ea0af1a49cb.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed to analyze adversarial contrastive learning (ACL) using Rademacher complexity as the main tool for measuring generalization. The approach will formalize the contrastive learning setting, define adversarial risks for both unsupervised (upstream) and supervised (downstream) tasks, and introduce the notion of adversarial samples within a specified neighborhood (e.g., under an ℓ_p norm constraint). Theoretical bounds will be derived that relate the adversarial risk in the upstream contrastive task to the adversarial risk in downstream supervised tasks, for both linear models and multi-layer neural networks. The analysis will include both the standard pairwise contrastive setting and a block-based setting with multiple similar and negative samples, and will utilize covering numbers and entropy integrals to bound Rademacher complexity for the relevant hypothesis classes.
3990671bec3e7cb019dc7ae4a6d71ea0af1a49cb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted to empirically validate the theoretical findings, using standard contrastive learning benchmarks. Models will be trained using adversarial contrastive learning on large-scale unlabeled datasets, with both linear and multi-layer neural network architectures. Downstream supervised tasks will be evaluated using linear classifiers on the learned representations, and robustness will be assessed under adversarial attacks (e.g., ℓ_p norm-bounded perturbations). Baseline comparisons will include standard (non-adversarial) contrastive learning and adversarial training without contrastive objectives. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy and adversarial risk on downstream tasks, with results compared to the theoretical upper bounds derived.
3990671bec3e7cb019dc7ae4a6d71ea0af1a49cb.novelty_claims: The proposed research provides the first comprehensive theoretical analysis of adversarial contrastive learning, establishing explicit generalization bounds that connect adversarial risks in upstream and downstream tasks. The analysis extends previous work by considering both linear and multi-layer neural network models, and by rigorously addressing the more complex contrastive loss (as opposed to standard classification loss). The work introduces new techniques for bounding Rademacher complexity in the adversarial contrastive setting and demonstrates that robust feature extractors learned via ACL can guarantee robust downstream performance. The theoretical results are supported by empirical validation, offering both foundational insights and practical guidelines for robust self-supervised representation learning.

399bbcecf674a55fb1a91b178a5be4a8999bb0ac.title: The Importance of Non-Markovianity in Maximum State Entropy Exploration
399bbcecf674a55fb1a91b178a5be4a8999bb0ac.research_question: How can non-Markovian policies improve maximum state entropy exploration in reinforcement learning, particularly in finite-sample regimes, and what are the theoretical and computational implications of leveraging non-Markovianity for exploration efficiency?
399bbcecf674a55fb1a91b178a5be4a8999bb0ac.hypothesis: Non-Markovian policies are necessary to achieve optimal maximum state entropy exploration in finite-sample settings, and can outperform Markovian policies in terms of exploration efficiency and sample coverage.
399bbcecf674a55fb1a91b178a5be4a8999bb0ac.proposed_method: A novel finite-sample maximum state entropy (MSE) objective is formulated, targeting the expected entropy of state visitation frequencies within a single episode, rather than the entropy of expected state visitation frequencies over infinite samples. The approach involves recasting the exploration problem to explicitly consider the role of non-Markovian policies, which can condition actions on the full history of states and actions, rather than just the current state. Theoretical analysis is conducted to characterize the sufficiency and necessity of non-Markovian deterministic policies for this objective, and the computational complexity of finding optimal non-Markovian policies is rigorously studied. To address the NP-hardness of the general problem, several practical relaxations are proposed, including policies with finite-length history windows, compact history representations (e.g., eligibility traces), deep recurrent policies, and tree search methods for non-Markovian control.
399bbcecf674a55fb1a91b178a5be4a8999bb0ac.experiment_details: Empirical validation is performed on simple controlled Markov process (CMP) domains such as a 3-state abstraction of a two-room environment and the River Swim environment. For each domain, the expected entropy achieved by optimal Markovian and non-Markovian policies is compared over short horizons (e.g., T=9 or T=10), with results averaged over 100 runs and 95% confidence intervals reported. The experiments involve solving for optimal policies in both classes (Markovian and non-Markovian) and analyzing the resulting state visitation distributions and entropy values. The setup demonstrates that non-Markovian policies can achieve higher entropy and more uniform coverage in single trials, confirming the theoretical findings.
399bbcecf674a55fb1a91b178a5be4a8999bb0ac.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a finite-sample MSE objective that reveals the critical importance of non-Markovianity for optimal exploration, contrasting with prior work that focused solely on Markovian policies and infinite-sample objectives. It provides a rigorous theoretical analysis showing that non-Markovian deterministic policies are necessary and sufficient for the new objective, while Markovian policies incur non-zero regret in general. The computational complexity of optimizing non-Markovian policies for this objective is established as NP-hard, and several practical avenues for tractable approximations and implementations are discussed. This work motivates a shift in exploration strategy design for reinforcement learning, especially in sample-limited or single-trial settings.

39c554b7eb646d3c7bbfeac27c88572d36a4ceff.title: Fair Anomaly Detection For Imbalanced Groups
39c554b7eb646d3c7bbfeac27c88572d36a4ceff.research_question: How can anomaly detection methods be designed to ensure fairness across imbalanced groups, particularly when protected groups are under-represented compared to unprotected groups in both normal and anomalous data distributions?
39c554b7eb646d3c7bbfeac27c88572d36a4ceff.hypothesis: Incorporating a fairness-aware contrastive learning module and a re-balancing autoencoder with learnable weights into anomaly detection frameworks will improve both fairness (reducing group disparities) and overall detection performance in imbalanced group scenarios.
39c554b7eb646d3c7bbfeac27c88572d36a4ceff.proposed_method: A new anomaly detection framework, FAIRAD, will be developed to address fairness and data imbalance in unsupervised anomaly detection tasks. The method will consist of two main modules: (1) a fairness-aware contrastive learning module that maximizes the similarity between protected and unprotected groups while encouraging uniformity within each group, and (2) a re-balancing autoencoder module that reweights the reconstruction loss for protected and unprotected groups using a learnable parameter. The contrastive loss will be designed to explicitly promote group fairness by maximizing cosine similarity between group representations, while the autoencoder will be optimized with a reweighted loss to ensure both groups are adequately represented in the learned model. The overall objective will combine the reweighted reconstruction loss and the fairness-aware contrastive loss, balanced by a hyperparameter, and theoretical analysis will be conducted to guarantee group fairness.
39c554b7eb646d3c7bbfeac27c88572d36a4ceff.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both image and tabular datasets, including MNIST-USPS, MNIST-Invert, COMPAS, and CelebA, with group membership defined by sensitive attributes such as source, color, race, or gender. The proposed method will be compared against several fairness-aware anomaly detection baselines (FairOD, DCFOD, FairSVDD) and fairness-agnostic baselines (MCM, NSNMF, ReContrast). Evaluation metrics will include Recall@k, ROCAUC, and RecDiff (recall difference between groups) to assess both detection performance and fairness. Experiments will systematically vary group imbalance ratios and include ablation studies to assess the contribution of each module. Models will be trained using appropriate neural architectures for each dataset, and all experiments will be run on standardized hardware for fair comparison.
39c554b7eb646d3c7bbfeac27c88572d36a4ceff.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a fairness-aware contrastive learning loss that theoretically guarantees group fairness, and a re-balancing autoencoder with a principled, learnable weighting scheme to address data imbalance. The method is claimed to be the first to jointly address representation disparity and group imbalance in anomaly detection with both theoretical guarantees and empirical validation. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate that the method achieves superior fairness and detection performance compared to existing baselines, especially as group imbalance increases.

39d9f6db78600c4e0b8c8c124dea0e4d4e78ed09.title: Bending Graphs: Hierarchical Shape Matching using Gated Optimal Transport
39d9f6db78600c4e0b8c8c124dea0e4d4e78ed09.research_question: How can hierarchical graph-based representations and advanced optimal transport techniques be leveraged to improve dense correspondence prediction between highly deformable 3D shapes, such as meshes, in a robust and efficient manner?
39d9f6db78600c4e0b8c8c124dea0e4d4e78ed09.hypothesis: A hierarchical shape representation combining local and global graph-based features, integrated with a gated optimal transport solver that propagates confidence-weighted features, will yield more robust and accurate dense correspondences between deformable 3D meshes, even under severe deformations and with limited training data.
39d9f6db78600c4e0b8c8c124dea0e4d4e78ed09.proposed_method: A hierarchical graph-based framework will be developed for 3D shape matching, where each input mesh is represented at two levels: local graphs capturing fine-grained geometric details around sampled seed points, and a global shape graph connecting these local regions based on geodesic proximity. Local descriptors will be extracted using a multi-layer graph neural network (GNN) with topology-adaptive graph convolutions and positional encoding via Fourier feature mappings. These local features are aggregated into the shape graph, where nodes represent sampled regions and edges encode spatial relationships. For correspondence prediction, a novel Gated Optimal Transport (GOT) module will be introduced, combining a differentiable Sinkhorn algorithm for soft assignment with recurrent gated feature propagation (using GRUs) on the shape graph, guided by matching confidence. The entire pipeline will be trained end-to-end with a combination of triplet loss for descriptor learning, a soft matching loss based on geodesic distances, and a regularization term enforcing local geometric consistency via Laplacian smoothing.
39d9f6db78600c4e0b8c8c124dea0e4d4e78ed09.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on publicly available 3D shape datasets, including MPI-FAUST for human meshes and TOSCA for animal shapes. The training set will consist of synthetic shapes with varying deformations (e.g., SURREAL for humans, SMAL for animals), while testing will be performed on both seen and unseen classes to evaluate generalization. For each mesh, 200 local graphs will be sampled using farthest point sampling, and the hierarchical graph structure will be constructed as described. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art dense correspondence methods such as 3DC, DGFM, LinInv, and SRT, as well as ablations of the proposed method (e.g., without shape graphs, without GOT, without regularization). Evaluation metrics will include average geodesic error and bijectivity rate (percentage of one-to-one correspondences), with dense correspondences refined via the functional map framework. Additional qualitative analyses and ablation studies will assess the contribution of each module.
39d9f6db78600c4e0b8c8c124dea0e4d4e78ed09.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a hierarchical graph representation for deformable meshes, combining local and global structural information in a unified framework. A novel Gated Optimal Transport module is developed, integrating recurrent confidence-weighted feature propagation with the Sinkhorn algorithm to enhance soft correspondence matching. The method achieves robust performance under severe deformations with minimal training data and significantly fewer parameters than competing approaches. The framework generalizes across different shape classes and does not require extensive refinement or large-scale training, demonstrating both efficiency and adaptability.

39e0e964d6ba714584c6fd58e170fc36370da6a6.title: Towards a General Time Series Forecasting Model with Unified Representation and Adaptive Transfer
39e0e964d6ba714584c6fd58e170fc36370da6a6.research_question: How can a general time series forecasting model be developed to effectively learn unified representations from heterogeneous multi-domain data and enable adaptive transfer to diverse downstream prediction scenarios, especially under data scarcity?
39e0e964d6ba714584c6fd58e170fc36370da6a6.hypothesis: A time series forecasting model that combines decomposed frequency learning for unified representation and a register mechanism for domain-specific adaptation will achieve superior generalization and transferability across domains, outperforming existing models in full-shot, few-shot, and zero-shot settings.
39e0e964d6ba714584c6fd58e170fc36370da6a6.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a lightweight encoder-decoder architecture based on Transformers, designed for time series modeling. Decomposed Frequency Learning is employed as a pre-training task, where time series are transformed into the frequency domain using the Real Fast Fourier Transform (rFFT), and multiple frequency-based masks (randomly masking high or low frequencies) are applied to disentangle temporal patterns. The masked sequences are then reconstructed in the time domain, enabling the model to learn generalized representations from multiple frequency perspectives. Additionally, a Time Series Register (TS-Register) is incorporated to capture domain-specific information during pre-training by clustering data-dependent embeddings into register tokens. During fine-tuning, a Top-K selection strategy adaptively selects the most relevant register vectors for the target domain, and a learnable low-rank matrix further adjusts these tokens to complement downstream dataset-specific information. The model is co-trained on both supervised prediction and self-supervised reconstruction tasks to enhance generalization and transferability.
39e0e964d6ba714584c6fd58e170fc36370da6a6.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using seven real-world benchmark datasets spanning domains such as energy, nature, health, transport, web, and economics, with approximately 887 million time points in total. The evaluation covers full-shot, few-shot (10% training data), and zero-shot settings. Baselines include state-of-the-art specific models (iTransformer, PatchTST, TimesNet, DLinear) and foundation models (GPT4TS, S2IP-LLM, Timer, MOIRAI, Chronos, TimesFM, Moment). Metrics used are Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE), with a fixed look-back window of 512 and prediction lengths of 96, 192, 336, and 720. Ablation studies assess the impact of the TS-Register, prediction and reconstruction tasks, and various masking strategies. Model efficiency is analyzed by comparing parameter counts and inference times against other foundation models.
39e0e964d6ba714584c6fd58e170fc36370da6a6.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel decomposed frequency learning method that disentangles complex temporal patterns via multi-frequency masking and reconstruction, enabling robust unified representations across domains. The TS-Register mechanism is proposed to capture and adaptively transfer domain-specific information using a clustering-based register and a Top-K selection strategy, further enhanced by a low-rank adaptation matrix. The method claims to achieve state-of-the-art forecasting performance in full-shot, few-shot, and zero-shot scenarios, with significant improvements in data-scarce settings and superior computational efficiency compared to existing foundation models.

3a07a87090a061ca41dd30ac8398a9a5d9d39826.title: Dense Text Retrieval Based on Pretrained Language Models: A Survey
3a07a87090a061ca41dd30ac8398a9a5d9d39826.research_question: How can dense text retrieval systems be systematically advanced by leveraging pretrained language models, and what are the key architectural, training, indexing, and integration strategies necessary to build effective and practical dense retrieval pipelines for large-scale information retrieval tasks?
3a07a87090a061ca41dd30ac8398a9a5d9d39826.hypothesis: Dense retrieval models based on pretrained language models can significantly outperform traditional sparse and pre-BERT neural retrieval models by learning superior latent representations and semantic matching functions, provided that advances in architecture, training, indexing, and integration are systematically developed and evaluated.
3a07a87090a061ca41dd30ac8398a9a5d9d39826.proposed_method: A comprehensive research program is proposed to develop, categorize, and evaluate dense text retrieval methods utilizing pretrained language models (PLMs). The approach will systematically address four core aspects: (1) architectural design, including single- and multi-representation bi-encoders, cross-encoders, and phrase-level representations; (2) specialized training strategies such as hard negative mining, knowledge distillation, and advanced pretraining (e.g., task-adaptive, retrieval-augmented, or representation-enhanced pretraining); (3) efficient indexing mechanisms for dense vectors, including late interaction models and hybrid sparse-dense indexing; and (4) integration of dense retrievers within multi-stage retrieval pipelines, optimizing the interplay between retrievers and rerankers. The methodology will also incorporate parameter-efficient tuning, feedback mechanisms, and cross-lingual adaptations to address practical deployment challenges.
3a07a87090a061ca41dd30ac8398a9a5d9d39826.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of large-scale retrieval benchmarks, including MS MARCO, Natural Questions, BEIR, and DuReader-retrieval, covering both English and non-English (e.g., Chinese) datasets. Baselines will include classic sparse retrieval models (e.g., BM25), pre-BERT neural IR models, and state-of-the-art dense retrievers. Evaluation metrics will focus on effectiveness (Recall@k, Accuracy@k, MRR, NDCG, MAP), with additional analysis of efficiency, scalability, and robustness. The experimental setup will leverage open-source toolkits such as Tevatron, Pyserini, and SentenceTransformers, and will systematically compare architectural variants, training regimes, indexing strategies, and integration approaches. Special attention will be given to the impact of data augmentation, negative sampling strategies, and pretraining methods on retrieval performance.
3a07a87090a061ca41dd30ac8398a9a5d9d39826.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified and systematic framework for advancing dense text retrieval with pretrained language models, distinguishing itself by (1) organizing the field along four major axes—architecture, training, indexing, and integration; (2) providing a comprehensive, practical reference that bridges technical innovations and real-world deployment; (3) emphasizing practical techniques for large-scale, multilingual, and domain-specific retrieval; and (4) releasing open-source resources, toolkits, and curated benchmarks to foster reproducibility and further innovation in dense retrieval research.

3a09f8a8d64955c0bab002c08579ba3ff567b6c5.title: Contrastive Energy Prediction for Exact Energy-Guided Diffusion Sampling in Offline Reinforcement Learning
3a09f8a8d64955c0bab002c08579ba3ff567b6c5.research_question: How can diffusion models be guided by arbitrary, potentially unnormalized energy functions to enable controllable sampling in complex domains such as offline reinforcement learning and image synthesis, and how can exact energy guidance be achieved during the diffusion sampling process?
3a09f8a8d64955c0bab002c08579ba3ff567b6c5.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a novel contrastive energy prediction (CEP) objective can be used to train an energy guidance model that enables exact energy-guided diffusion sampling, guaranteeing convergence to the desired target distribution defined by an energy function, outperforming existing inexact guidance methods in offline RL and matching classifier guidance in image synthesis.
3a09f8a8d64955c0bab002c08579ba3ff567b6c5.proposed_method: A new framework is proposed that formulates the problem of sampling from a distribution proportional to q(x) * exp(-βE(x)), where E(x) is a flexible, potentially unnormalized energy function. The key innovation is the derivation of an exact, theoretically principled formulation of the intermediate energy guidance required during the diffusion process, which is shown to be intractable to compute directly. To address this, a contrastive energy prediction (CEP) objective is introduced, training a neural network to estimate the intermediate energy function by comparing the energies of noise-perturbed data samples and using their soft energy labels as supervision. The CEP objective is implemented as a contrastive loss over batches of samples, using self-normalized energy labels to ensure numerical stability. The gradients of the trained energy model are then used to guide the diffusion sampling process, ensuring that the final samples follow the desired energy-modified distribution.
3a09f8a8d64955c0bab002c08579ba3ff567b6c5.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on standard offline reinforcement learning benchmarks (D4RL), including locomotion tasks (HalfCheetah, Hopper, Walker2d) and challenging AntMaze navigation tasks. The proposed method (Q-guided policy optimization, QGPO) is compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as CQL, BCQ, IQL, Diffuser, Decision Diffuser, Diffusion-QL, and others, using normalized performance metrics as suggested by D4RL. Evaluation includes mean and standard deviation across multiple random seeds. For image synthesis, experiments are performed on ImageNet at resolutions of 128x128 and 256x256, comparing CEP-guided sampling to classic classifier guidance using metrics such as FID, sFID, precision, and recall. Additional qualitative experiments demonstrate the flexibility of CEP in controlling continuous image attributes (e.g., color appearance) via energy functions.
3a09f8a8d64955c0bab002c08579ba3ff567b6c5.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first exact formulation of intermediate energy guidance for diffusion models, enabling sampling from arbitrary energy-modified distributions. The contrastive energy prediction (CEP) objective is a novel training approach that guarantees, under unlimited model capacity and data, convergence to the exact desired distribution, unlike previous inexact or heuristic energy guidance methods. The method generalizes and subsumes prior guidance techniques (e.g., classifier guidance) and enables new forms of controllability in both offline RL and high-dimensional image synthesis. Empirical results demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in offline RL and competitive results with classifier guidance in image synthesis, while also enabling novel applications such as continuous energy-guided image manipulation.

3a0acc13399a431b20875a961fd9a11fbf135595.title: Expected Sliced Transport Plans
3a0acc13399a431b20875a961fd9a11fbf135595.research_question: Can a computationally efficient transportation plan be constructed between two discrete probability measures using the sliced transport framework, and can this plan be used to define a valid metric between the measures? Furthermore, how does this approach compare to existing optimal transport and entropic regularization methods in terms of theoretical properties and practical applications such as interpolation, classification, and embedding?
3a0acc13399a431b20875a961fd9a11fbf135595.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by averaging (taking the expectation of) lifted one-dimensional optimal transport plans across random directions, a new transportation plan can be constructed that both provides explicit coupling between measures and defines a valid metric, while retaining the computational efficiency of sliced optimal transport.
3a0acc13399a431b20875a961fd9a11fbf135595.proposed_method: A novel approach is developed that constructs transportation plans between discrete probability measures by first projecting the measures onto one-dimensional slices along random directions. For each slice, the optimal transport plan is computed in one dimension and then 'lifted' back to the original high-dimensional space. The expected sliced transport (EST) plan is then defined as the expectation (average) of these lifted plans over all directions, using a probability measure on the sphere of directions. The resulting EST plan is shown to have the correct marginals and is used to define the Expected Sliced Transport distance, which sums the weighted Euclidean costs of moving mass according to the EST plan. The method is further generalized with a temperature parameter that allows interpolation between uniform averaging and a minimum-slice approach, connecting to the min-SWGG framework.
3a0acc13399a431b20875a961fd9a11fbf135595.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets, including the PointCloudMNIST2D dataset, where each image is represented as a weighted 2D point cloud. The EST plan is compared to classical optimal transport, entropic regularized OT (with varying regularization parameters), and min-SWGG, using metrics such as transport plan visualization, interpolation quality, weak convergence behavior, and classification accuracy in a transport-based embedding framework. Evaluation includes visualizations of transport plans, interpolation between point clouds, and t-SNE plots of embeddings, as well as quantitative classification accuracy using logistic regression on the embedded representations. The impact of the temperature parameter and the number of slices is systematically studied.
3a0acc13399a431b20875a961fd9a11fbf135595.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the Expected Sliced Transport (EST) plan, a computationally efficient method for constructing explicit transportation plans between discrete probability measures within the sliced transport framework. The EST plan enables the definition of a valid metric, the EST distance, which is theoretically proven to be a metric and to induce the same topology as the Wasserstein distance for discrete measures. The approach bridges the gap between computational efficiency and explicit mass coupling, and provides a flexible parametric framework via the temperature parameter that interpolates between uniform averaging and minimum-slice strategies. The method is demonstrated to be effective in practical applications such as interpolation, classification, and embedding, and establishes connections to recent advances such as min-SWGG.

3a2daffdb7ccaf8cfe7b6c292b20a9756c0c2b1e.title: Causal Strategic Classification: A Tale of Two Shifts
3a2daffdb7ccaf8cfe7b6c292b20a9756c0c2b1e.research_question: How can predictive models be trained to be robust in strategic classification settings where users' feature modifications can causally affect true outcomes, and what are the implications of accounting for both strategic behavior and causal effects on distribution shift and predictive accuracy?
3a2daffdb7ccaf8cfe7b6c292b20a9756c0c2b1e.hypothesis: Incorporating causal relationships between features and outcomes into strategic classification will enable learning algorithms to better balance robustness to both strategic manipulation and genuine outcome changes, thereby improving predictive accuracy and reliability over time compared to methods that ignore causal effects.
3a2daffdb7ccaf8cfe7b6c292b20a9756c0c2b1e.proposed_method: A novel learning algorithm is developed for causal strategic classification, where observable features are partitioned into causal and correlative (non-causal) subsets. The method models the process by which users strategically modify their features in response to a deployed classifier, and crucially, allows these modifications to causally affect the true label through a ground-truth function involving both observed and unobserved variables. The approach replaces the unknown ground-truth function with a learned surrogate, trained on both clean and strategically-modified ('dirty') data, and utilizes a marginal density estimator to handle distributional shifts. A regularization term is introduced to encourage exploration of low-density regions, improving the estimation of the causal effect and enabling end-to-end differentiable training.
