The method is designed to operate over multiple rounds, leveraging temporally collected data to iteratively refine both the classifier and the causal surrogate.
3a2daffdb7ccaf8cfe7b6c292b20a9756c0c2b1e.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both synthetic and semi-synthetic (real) datasets. Synthetic experiments are designed to isolate and demonstrate the effects of causal and strategic shifts, including scenarios with feature partitioning, non-linear separability, and out-of-domain effects. Real data experiments use public datasets (e.g., spam detection and credit card fraud), where ground-truth causal relationships are simulated by partitioning features and training a ground-truth labeling function. The proposed method is compared against several baselines: empirical risk minimization (ERM), strategic ERM (SERM), repeated risk minimization (RRM), and oracle-like benchmarks. Evaluation metrics include predictive accuracy, improvement rates (proportion of points whose true label improves after strategic modification), movement rates (proportion of points that change features), and welfare (utility minus cost). Experiments are run over multiple rounds to assess temporal performance and sensitivity analyses are performed to test robustness to feature partitioning errors.
3a2daffdb7ccaf8cfe7b6c292b20a9756c0c2b1e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to explicitly model and address the dual distribution shifts induced by both strategic user behavior and causal effects of feature modification in classification. It introduces a flexible causal structure that generalizes standard strategic classification, a learning algorithm that decouples strategic and causal effects using density estimation and surrogate modeling, and a regularization mechanism for exploration in low-density regions. The method enables end-to-end training and demonstrates superior performance over existing baselines in both synthetic and real-world-inspired settings, providing new insights into the importance of causal reasoning in strategic machine learning environments.

3a5162590b8423c81c457be9b0f6f9194e6f970e.title: In-context operator learning with data prompts for differential equation problems
3a5162590b8423c81c457be9b0f6f9194e6f970e.research_question: Can a single neural network model be designed to learn and generalize solution operators for a wide range of differential equation problems, enabling few-shot adaptation to new, potentially out-of-distribution operators without retraining or weight updates?
3a5162590b8423c81c457be9b0f6f9194e6f970e.hypothesis: A transformer-based encoder-decoder neural network, when trained on diverse operator data using in-context prompts, will be able to learn new differential equation operators from a small number of data demonstrations and accurately apply them to novel queries without requiring weight updates.
3a5162590b8423c81c457be9b0f6f9194e6f970e.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops an In-Context Operator Network (ICON) utilizing a transformer-based encoder-decoder architecture. The method encodes 'prompts' consisting of multiple demonstrations (each a condition and its corresponding quantity of interest) and a 'question condition' into a structured matrix, with each column representing a key-value pair and index information. The encoder processes these prompts to generate an embedding representing both the operator and the query context. Queries specifying evaluation points for the question QoI are separately embedded and passed, along with the prompt embedding, to the decoder, which uses cross-attention to predict the QoI values. The model is trained using mean squared error loss over batches containing diverse operator types and parameterizations, with each batch containing randomly selected demos and queries. During inference, the trained network receives a few demos and a question condition as input and predicts the QoI for new, potentially unseen operators in a single forward pass, without any weight updates.
3a5162590b8423c81c457be9b0f6f9194e6f970e.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a suite of 19 differential equation problem types, including forward and inverse problems for ODEs, PDEs, and mean-field control problems. For each problem type, 1000 distinct operators are generated by randomizing parameters, and for each operator, 100 condition-QoI pairs are synthesized, resulting in a total of 19,000 operators and 1.9 million data pairs. During training, prompts are constructed with 1-5 demos and 41-50 key-value pairs per condition/QoI, with batching and zero-padding used for efficient computation. Evaluation metrics focus on mean squared error between predicted and true QoI values. Baselines for comparison include existing operator learning methods such as DeepONet, Fourier Neural Operator, and others, with particular attention to the ability to generalize to new operators and out-of-distribution tasks without retraining.
3a5162590b8423c81c457be9b0f6f9194e6f970e.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel in-context learning paradigm for operator learning, enabling a single neural network to learn and apply new differential equation operators from a small number of demonstrations without any weight updates. This approach leverages transformer architectures to encode variable-length, structured prompts and queries, allowing for few-shot generalization across a diverse set of operator types. The method claims to eliminate the need for retraining or fine-tuning when encountering new problems, and demonstrates the ability to generalize to operators beyond the training distribution, advancing the state-of-the-art in neural operator learning.

3aaf6a2cbad5850ad81ab5c163599cb3d523436f.title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
3aaf6a2cbad5850ad81ab5c163599cb3d523436f.research_question: Can large language models be enhanced to improve the quality of their outputs through iterative self-refinement, using their own feedback, across a diverse range of tasks without requiring additional supervised training or reinforcement learning?
3aaf6a2cbad5850ad81ab5c163599cb3d523436f.hypothesis: Large language models are capable of providing actionable and specific feedback on their own outputs, and can iteratively refine their responses using this feedback, resulting in improved performance across various tasks compared to standard single-pass generation.
3aaf6a2cbad5850ad81ab5c163599cb3d523436f.proposed_method: A novel iterative refinement framework, SELF-REFINE, is proposed, in which a single large language model (LLM) alternates between generating an initial output, providing feedback on that output, and refining the output based on the feedback. The process is guided by three types of few-shot prompts: one for initial generation, one for feedback, and one for refinement. At each iteration, the LLM is prompted to analyze its own output and produce actionable, specific feedback, which is then incorporated into the next refinement step. This loop continues for a fixed number of iterations or until a task-specific stopping criterion is met, with the model maintaining a history of previous outputs and feedback to inform further refinements. The approach requires no additional supervised training, reinforcement learning, or external feedback sources, relying solely on the in-context capabilities of the base LLM.
3aaf6a2cbad5850ad81ab5c163599cb3d523436f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on seven diverse generation tasks, including Dialogue Response Generation, Code Optimization, Code Readability Improvement, Math Reasoning, Sentiment Reversal, Acronym Generation, and Constrained Generation. The method will be instantiated with strong LLMs such as GPT-3.5, ChatGPT, GPT-4, and Codex, with both feedback and refinement steps implemented via few-shot prompting. Baseline comparisons will be made against the same base LLMs using standard single-pass generation, as well as against other strong few-shot and fine-tuned approaches. Evaluation metrics will include task-specific automated metrics (e.g., program optimization rate, math problem solve rate, coverage in constrained generation), human preference judgments, and GPT-4-based preference scores. Experiments will use greedy decoding with a temperature of 0.7, and up to four feedback-refine iterations per input. Additional ablations will assess the impact of feedback quality and the number of iterations.
3aaf6a2cbad5850ad81ab5c163599cb3d523436f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a general, training-free iterative refinement framework that leverages a single LLM as both the generator and feedback provider, eliminating the need for supervised data, additional training, or reinforcement learning. SELF-REFINE is applicable across a wide range of tasks and domains, and demonstrates that even state-of-the-art LLMs can be significantly improved at test time through self-feedback and iterative refinement. The method is distinct in using the same LLM for both feedback and refinement, and in its reliance on actionable, specific natural language feedback generated in-context. Results show consistent and substantial improvements over strong baselines, highlighting the effectiveness and generality of the approach.

3ab661db57d924f4ff1706e05ac807873ca00e0a.title: RAFT: Reward rAnked FineTuning for Generative Foundation Model Alignment
3ab661db57d924f4ff1706e05ac807873ca00e0a.research_question: How can generative foundation models be effectively aligned with human preferences and ethics, while maintaining stability, efficiency, and high-quality output across both language and vision domains?
3ab661db57d924f4ff1706e05ac807873ca00e0a.hypothesis: A reward-ranked fine-tuning framework that iteratively selects and fine-tunes on high-reward samples, as determined by a reward model, will achieve more stable, efficient, and effective alignment of generative models compared to reinforcement learning-based approaches, while preserving output quality and diversity.
3ab661db57d924f4ff1706e05ac807873ca00e0a.proposed_method: A new framework, Reward rAnked FineTuning (RAFT), is proposed for aligning generative models. The method consists of three iterative steps: (1) sampling a batch of prompts and generating multiple candidate outputs per prompt using the current generative model; (2) scoring these outputs with a reward model and selecting the highest-reward response for each prompt, thus forming a filtered dataset of high-quality samples; (3) fine-tuning the generative model on this filtered dataset using supervised learning. This process is repeated until convergence of the reward metric. The framework is flexible, decoupling data generation from model fine-tuning, and can be extended with regularization (e.g., KL divergence to the initial model) to balance reward optimization with output fluency and diversity. The acceptance ratio (number of samples per prompt), sampling temperature, and optional regularization coefficients are tunable hyperparameters.
3ab661db57d924f4ff1706e05ac807873ca00e0a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large language models (LLMs) and diffusion models, with a primary focus on the LLaMA-7B model aligned using the HH-RLHF (Helpful and Harmless Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) dataset. The setup includes fine-tuning with 112K training samples and evaluating on a 4,608-sample test set. Baseline comparisons will be made against the standard RLHF approach using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), with both methods evaluated using mean reward, perplexity, and diversity metrics (MSSTR, Distinct-1/2, Unique-1/2, output length). Additional evaluation will be performed using GPT-4 and human raters on 100 randomly sampled prompts. Hyperparameters such as batch size, learning rate, number of samples per prompt (K), sampling temperature, and KL penalty will be systematically varied to assess their impact on alignment quality, stability, and computational efficiency.
3ab661db57d924f4ff1706e05ac807873ca00e0a.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a reward-ranked, supervised fine-tuning approach that avoids the instability and inefficiency of RL-based alignment methods like PPO. RAFT decouples data generation from model fine-tuning, reducing memory requirements and enabling flexible, off-policy training. The method is robust to reward scaling and noise, requires minimal hyperparameter tuning, and can be applied to both language and vision generative models. RAFT also enables efficient distillation and alignment across models of different sizes, and supports integration of additional regularization objectives to balance reward optimization with output quality.

3ad0899e9fa71cc6c294db4e8061ff6bc9e22225.title: A Tale of Two Features: Stable Diffusion Complements DINO for Zero-Shot Semantic Correspondence
3ad0899e9fa71cc6c294db4e8061ff6bc9e22225.research_question: How can internal representations from text-to-image diffusion models and self-supervised vision transformers be leveraged and combined to improve zero-shot semantic and dense correspondence across different images and objects?
3ad0899e9fa71cc6c294db4e8061ff6bc9e22225.hypothesis: Fusing features from text-to-image diffusion models (such as Stable Diffusion) and self-supervised vision transformers (such as DINOv2) will yield a complementary representation that outperforms either feature type alone in zero-shot semantic correspondence tasks, due to their distinct and non-redundant strengths in spatial and semantic information.
3ad0899e9fa71cc6c294db4e8061ff6bc9e22225.proposed_method: The proposed method extracts multi-level features from the denoising U-Net of a pre-trained Stable Diffusion model, focusing on decoder layers that capture both semantic and textural information. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is applied to reduce the dimensionality of concatenated features from selected layers (e.g., layers 2, 5, 8), and features are aggregated to a common resolution. In parallel, features are extracted from the last token layer of a DINOv2 Vision Transformer. Both feature types are independently L2-normalized and then concatenated with a tunable weighting parameter to form a fused representation. This fused feature is used for pixel-level nearest neighbor search to establish dense or sparse correspondences between image pairs. The method is designed to operate in a zero-shot setting, requiring no task-specific fine-tuning for correspondence.
3ad0899e9fa71cc6c294db4e8061ff6bc9e22225.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on public benchmark datasets for semantic correspondence, including SPair-71k, PF-Pascal, and TSS. Both sparse and dense correspondence tasks will be evaluated. The evaluation protocol includes zero-shot nearest neighbor matching on feature maps, as well as supervised settings with a fine-tuned bottleneck layer for datasets with training splits. Baselines will include state-of-the-art supervised, unsupervised, and task-specific methods, as well as individual DINOv2 and Stable Diffusion features. Metrics such as Percentage of Correct Keypoints (PCK) at various thresholds, flow field smoothness, FID, CLIP, and quality scores for instance swapping will be used. Implementation will utilize Stable Diffusion v1-5 and DINOv2-ViT-B/14, with experiments run on high-resolution images and a single high-end GPU.
3ad0899e9fa71cc6c294db4e8061ff6bc9e22225.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a simple yet effective feature fusion strategy that combines the spatially coherent but sometimes semantically imprecise features of Stable Diffusion with the sparse but semantically accurate features of DINOv2. The fused representation is claimed to achieve state-of-the-art zero-shot performance on challenging semantic correspondence benchmarks, outperforming both prior unsupervised and supervised methods. Additional contributions include a detailed analysis of the complementary properties of diffusion and transformer features, a novel application to high-quality instance swapping without task-specific fine-tuning, and quantitative evidence of the non-redundancy and synergy between the two feature types.

3ae6ab755d9553e2b8ff656e451f2a1bfdc685e0.title: On the Relationship Between Monotone and Squared Probabilistic Circuits
3ae6ab755d9553e2b8ff656e451f2a1bfdc685e0.research_question: Can a unified probabilistic circuit model be developed that combines the strengths of monotone and squared probabilistic circuits, thereby improving expressive efficiency and tractable probabilistic modeling across a range of datasets?
3ae6ab755d9553e2b8ff656e451f2a1bfdc685e0.hypothesis: A novel probabilistic circuit architecture that generalizes both monotone and squared circuits, and incorporates complex parameters, will be strictly more expressively efficient and achieve superior density estimation performance compared to either monotone or squared circuits alone.
3ae6ab755d9553e2b8ff656e451f2a1bfdc685e0.proposed_method: A new class of probabilistic circuits, termed Inception PCs, will be constructed to generalize both monotone and squared probabilistic circuits by introducing two types of latent variables: one marginalized outside the square (1-norm latents) and one inside the square (2-norm latents). The circuit will be parameterized with complex-valued weights and input functions, and its output will be defined as a deep sum-of-square-of-sums over these latent variables. The probability distribution is computed by summing over the 1-norm latents outside the squared modulus of a sum over the 2-norm latents, ensuring tractability via smoothness and structured decomposability. An efficient tensorized architecture will be designed, grouping sum and product nodes into regions and connecting them via multi-dimensional complex-valued tensors, enabling scalable learning and inference on GPUs. Gradient descent with Wirtinger derivatives will be used for optimization, and numerical stability will be ensured using a complex log-sum-exp trick.
3ae6ab755d9553e2b8ff656e451f2a1bfdc685e0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of tabular (20 binary UCI datasets) and large-scale image datasets (downscaled ImageNet32 and ImageNet64). For tabular data, models will be compared using negative log-likelihood, and for image data, bits-per-dimension (bpd) will be used as the evaluation metric. Baselines will include monotone PCs (non-negative parameters), squared PCs (real and complex parameters), RAT-SPNs, and VAEs, as well as monotone HCLT PCs trained with EM and latent variable distillation. All models will use the same vtree structure (HCLT) for fair comparison, and hyperparameters such as the number of 1-norm and 2-norm latents will be systematically varied to study trade-offs. Training will use the Adam optimizer, and results will be averaged over multiple runs to ensure robustness.
3ae6ab755d9553e2b8ff656e451f2a1bfdc685e0.novelty_claims: The proposed Inception PC framework strictly generalizes both monotone and squared probabilistic circuits, enabling the use of both non-negative and complex parameters within a unified tractable architecture. The method introduces a deep sum-of-square-of-sums structure, providing strictly greater expressive efficiency than either monotone or squared circuits alone. The tensorized implementation allows for scalable learning and inference, and empirical results are expected to demonstrate improved density estimation performance on both tabular and image benchmarks, even when normalized for computation time.

3aee33831e0bdea1a1eaae21c7586e4f7c0396d6.title: Making Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Robust to Irrelevant Context
3aee33831e0bdea1a1eaae21c7586e4f7c0396d6.research_question: How can retrieval-augmented language models (RALMs) be made robust to irrelevant or noisy retrieved context, ensuring that retrieved information improves performance when relevant and does not harm performance when irrelevant, particularly in open-domain and multi-hop question answering tasks?
3aee33831e0bdea1a1eaae21c7586e4f7c0396d6.hypothesis: Training RALMs on a mixture of relevant and irrelevant contexts, or employing natural language inference (NLI) models to filter out irrelevant retrieved passages, will increase the robustness of RALMs to noisy or irrelevant context and maintain or improve their performance on both single-hop and multi-hop question answering tasks.
3aee33831e0bdea1a1eaae21c7586e4f7c0396d6.proposed_method: A dual approach will be developed to enhance the robustness of RALMs. First, an NLI-based filtering strategy will be implemented, where a pre-trained NLI model determines whether the retrieved context entails the question-answer pair; if not, the model falls back to using the language model without retrieval. Second, a fine-tuning procedure will be designed, where RALMs are trained on automatically generated datasets containing both relevant and irrelevant contexts. For single-hop questions, relevant and irrelevant contexts will be created by retrieving top-ranked and random/low-ranked passages, respectively. For multi-hop questions, a strong LLM will be prompted to generate decompositions, and self-consistency or intermediate answer verification will be used to ensure quality. Training examples will interleave relevant and irrelevant contexts at each reasoning step to teach the model to ignore noise and utilize useful evidence.
3aee33831e0bdea1a1eaae21c7586e4f7c0396d6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five open-domain QA benchmarks: Natural Questions (NQ) for single-hop, 2WIKIMQA and BAMBOOGLE for explicit multi-hop, and STRATEGYQA and FERMI for implicit multi-hop reasoning. Both Google Search and ColBERTv2 will be used as retrievers, with retrieval noise simulated by using top-1, low-ranked, and random passages. Baselines will include few-shot prompted Llama-2-13B and Llama-2-70B models with and without retrieval, as well as NLI-filtered variants. Evaluation metrics will be exact match (EM) for NQ and STRATEGYQA, F1 for 2WIKIMQA and BAMBOOGLE, and order-of-magnitude accuracy for FERMI. Fine-tuning will be performed with up to 1,000 training examples for single-hop and 500 for multi-hop, using parameter-efficient methods. Ablation studies will compare models trained with only relevant, only irrelevant, or mixed contexts.
3aee33831e0bdea1a1eaae21c7586e4f7c0396d6.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces an automatic data generation framework for robust RALM training that requires only a small number of examples and does not rely on manual annotation. It demonstrates that robustness to irrelevant context can be achieved with as few as 1,000 training examples, even for challenging multi-hop tasks. The approach systematically evaluates and contrasts NLI-based filtering and fine-tuning on mixed context, providing new insights into the failure modes of RALMs and the effectiveness of robustness interventions. The research also highlights that increasing model size alone does not confer robustness, and that training on a mixture of relevant and irrelevant contexts is necessary for improved performance and generalization.

3af7273d7ca20c0c63cbaa47e60b058840835052.title: VideoMamba: State Space Model for Efficient Video Understanding
3af7273d7ca20c0c63cbaa47e60b058840835052.research_question: How can video understanding models be designed to efficiently and effectively capture both local redundancy and global dependencies in short-term and long-term video data, while maintaining scalability and compatibility with multi-modal tasks?
3af7273d7ca20c0c63cbaa47e60b058840835052.hypothesis: A purely state space model (SSM)-based architecture, equipped with linear-complexity operators and enhanced by self-distillation and masked modeling strategies, will outperform existing convolutional and attention-based video understanding models in terms of efficiency, scalability, and accuracy on both short-term and long-term video tasks.
3af7273d7ca20c0c63cbaa47e60b058840835052.proposed_method: A novel video understanding framework, VideoMamba, will be developed by extending the Selective State Space Model (Mamba) to the video domain. The architecture will utilize 3D convolutional patch embedding to convert input videos into non-overlapping spatiotemporal tokens, followed by stacked bidirectional Mamba (B-Mamba) blocks adapted for 3D sequences. The model will incorporate learnable spatial and temporal position embeddings to retain spatiotemporal information. Various bidirectional scan strategies (spatial-first, temporal-first, and spatiotemporal) will be explored, with an emphasis on the spatial-first scan for efficiency. To address overfitting in larger models, a self-distillation technique will be employed, where a smaller, well-trained model serves as a teacher to guide the training of larger student models. Additionally, masked modeling strategies tailored for SSMs will be integrated to enhance temporal sensitivity and multi-modal adaptability.
3af7273d7ca20c0c63cbaa47e60b058840835052.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both image and video understanding benchmarks. For image classification, ImageNet-1K will be used, following standard training protocols with AdamW optimizer, cosine learning rate scheduling, and BFloat16 precision. For video understanding, short-term datasets such as Kinetics-400 and Something-Something V2, as well as long-term datasets like Breakfast, COIN, and LVU, will be utilized. Both supervised and self-supervised (masked modeling and distillation from CLIP-ViT) settings will be explored. Baselines will include state-of-the-art 3D CNNs, video transformers (e.g., TimeSformer, ViViT), and hybrid models (e.g., UniFormer, VMamba). Evaluation metrics will include top-1 and top-5 accuracy, throughput, and GPU memory usage. Ablation studies will assess the impact of self-distillation, scan strategies, and masking techniques.
3af7273d7ca20c0c63cbaa47e60b058840835052.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first purely SSM-based video understanding model capable of linear-complexity dynamic spatiotemporal modeling. It pioneers the use of bidirectional Mamba blocks for 3D video sequences, enabling efficient handling of high-resolution, long videos. The integration of a simple yet effective self-distillation strategy addresses scalability and overfitting without requiring large-scale pretraining. The framework also innovates in masked modeling tailored for SSMs, enhancing both temporal sensitivity and multi-modal compatibility. These contributions collectively set new benchmarks in efficiency, scalability, and performance for comprehensive video understanding.

3b21f167b07080ef9394320ea1fb69c29cee0d21.title: Moreau-Yosida f-divergences
3b21f167b07080ef9394320ea1fb69c29cee0d21.research_question: How can variational representations of f-divergences be generalized and regularized to improve their practical approximation and stability in machine learning algorithms, particularly in generative modeling tasks?
3b21f167b07080ef9394320ea1fb69c29cee0d21.hypothesis: Introducing the Moreau-Yosida approximation of f-divergences with respect to the Wasserstein-1 metric will yield variational representations that are easier to approximate in practice, provide a relaxation of hard Lipschitz constraints, and result in improved stability and performance of generative adversarial networks (GANs) compared to existing methods.
3b21f167b07080ef9394320ea1fb69c29cee0d21.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed that defines the Moreau-Yosida approximation of f-divergences with respect to the Wasserstein-1 metric, parameterized by two real numbers controlling the sharpness of the approximation and the Lipschitz constant of optimal critics. Variational formulas for these approximations will be derived, including both hard Lipschitz constraint and relaxed penalty forms, and a characterization of functions achieving the supremum in the variational representation will be provided. An algorithm compatible with automatic differentiation frameworks will be implemented to compute the tight convex conjugate of f-divergences, utilizing Newton’s method in the forward pass and implicit differentiation in the backward pass. The approach will be instantiated in the Moreau-Yosida f-GAN, where the critic and generator are parameterized by neural networks, and the variational formulas are used as training objectives.
3b21f167b07080ef9394320ea1fb69c29cee0d21.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the CIFAR-10 dataset for the task of generative modeling. The proposed Moreau-Yosida f-GAN will be implemented for a range of f-divergences, including Kullback-Leibler, reverse Kullback-Leibler, χ2, reverse χ2, squared Hellinger, Jensen-Shannon, Jeffreys, triangular discrimination, and total variation. Baselines will include standard f-GANs and Wasserstein GANs with and without gradient penalty. Evaluation metrics will be the Inception Score (IS) and Frechet Inception Distance (FID). The experimental setup will involve training the critic and generator with different regularization parameters (e.g., varying the Moreau-Yosida parameters and Lipschitz constraints), and comparing the stability, convergence, and generative quality of the models. Additional experiments will investigate the effect of quotient critics (enforcing vanishing at a base point) and the relaxation of hard Lipschitz constraints.
3b21f167b07080ef9394320ea1fb69c29cee0d21.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a generalization of the tight variational representation of f-divergences over the space of Lipschitz functions or its quotient, a practical algorithm for computing the tight convex conjugate of f-divergences compatible with automatic differentiation, and variational formulas for the Moreau-Yosida approximation of f-divergences with respect to the Wasserstein-1 metric. This includes a novel relaxation of the hard Lipschitz constraint and an unconstrained variational representation of the Wasserstein-1 metric. The approach provides a unified framework that encompasses and extends several recent results, offers new special cases of interest, and yields practical benefits such as improved stability, uniqueness of the optimal critic, and competitive performance in generative modeling tasks.

3b227285d0a4c8033d2da2b2e0bd085cf5d37e69.title: A Scale-Invariant Sorting Criterion to Find a Causal Order in Additive Noise Models
3b227285d0a4c8033d2da2b2e0bd085cf5d37e69.research_question: How can a scale-invariant criterion be developed and exploited to recover causal orderings in additive noise models (ANMs) from observational data, particularly in settings with arbitrary data scales and varying simulation parameters?
3b227285d0a4c8033d2da2b2e0bd085cf5d37e69.hypothesis: In synthetic data generated from ANMs with commonly used parameter sampling schemes, the fraction of variance explainable by other variables (as measured by the coefficient of determination, R2) tends to increase along the causal order, and this pattern (R2-sortability) can be exploited to recover the causal structure effectively, even after standardization.
3b227285d0a4c8033d2da2b2e0bd085cf5d37e69.proposed_method: A novel, scale-invariant sorting criterion based on the coefficient of determination (R2) is introduced to quantify the alignment between the causal order and the order of increasing R2 values for each variable. The proposed algorithm, R2-SortnRegress, first estimates the R2 value for each variable by regressing it onto all other variables using linear models. Variables are then sorted in ascending order of R2 to propose a candidate causal order. Subsequently, each variable is regressed onto its predecessors in this order, using penalized linear regression (with L1 regularization and model selection via Bayesian Information Criterion) to estimate the causal graph structure. This method is computationally efficient and robust to arbitrary rescaling or standardization of the data.
3b227285d0a4c8033d2da2b2e0bd085cf5d37e69.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic datasets generated from linear ANMs with randomly sampled parameters, including both Erdős–Rényi and scale-free graph structures with varying numbers of nodes and average in-degrees. Noise distributions (e.g., Gaussian) and edge weight distributions will be systematically varied to assess their impact on R2-sortability. The proposed R2-SortnRegress algorithm will be compared against established baselines such as the PC algorithm, FGES, Var-SortnRegress, and RandomRegress. Evaluation metrics will include the Structural Intervention Distance (SID) and Structural Hamming Distance (SHD) between the recovered and ground-truth graphs. Additional experiments will be performed on real-world datasets, such as the Sachs protein signaling data, to assess practical applicability and the prevalence of R2-sortability in real data.
3b227285d0a4c8033d2da2b2e0bd085cf5d37e69.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces R2-sortability as a new, scale-invariant criterion for causal order recovery in ANMs, addressing limitations of previous variance-based approaches that are sensitive to data scaling. The R2-SortnRegress algorithm is designed to exploit this property, providing a simple yet competitive baseline for causal discovery, especially in standardized or arbitrarily scaled data. Theoretical analysis links the emergence of high R2-sortability to the distribution of edge weights and graph topology, offering new insights into the implicit assumptions of synthetic ANM data generation. The work also provides practical tools and recommendations for benchmarking causal discovery algorithms with respect to R2-sortability.

3b2a675bb617ae1a920e8e29d535cdf27826e999.title: Video Diffusion Models
3b2a675bb617ae1a920e8e29d535cdf27826e999.research_question: How can high-fidelity, temporally coherent videos be generated using generative models, and what architectural and training strategies enable scalable, flexible, and effective video synthesis for both unconditional and conditional settings, including text-to-video and video prediction tasks?
3b2a675bb617ae1a920e8e29d535cdf27826e999.hypothesis: Diffusion models, when extended with 3D space-time factorized U-Net architectures and enhanced with novel conditional sampling techniques and joint image-video training, can generate high-quality, temporally coherent videos and outperform existing state-of-the-art methods on standard video generation and prediction benchmarks.
3b2a675bb617ae1a920e8e29d535cdf27826e999.proposed_method: A diffusion-based generative framework will be developed for video synthesis by extending the standard image diffusion model architecture to a 3D U-Net that factorizes computation over space and time. Each model will be trained to generate fixed-length video clips at a fixed spatial resolution, using blocks of space-only 3D convolutions and interleaved spatial and temporal attention mechanisms, with relative position embeddings for temporal ordering. The architecture will support joint training on both video and image data by masking temporal attention for image inputs, which reduces gradient variance and improves optimization. For conditional generation, a reconstruction-guided sampling technique will be introduced, leveraging the model's own reconstructions to guide the denoising process and improve temporal and spatial coherence during autoregressive extension and super-resolution. Classifier-free guidance will also be incorporated for text-conditioned generation to enhance sample fidelity.
3b2a675bb617ae1a920e8e29d535cdf27826e999.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several established benchmarks: unconditional video generation will be evaluated on the UCF101 dataset (16-frame, 64x64 resolution clips), using FVD, FID, and Inception Score metrics, with comparisons to leading GAN- and autoregressive-based methods. Video prediction will be tested on BAIR Robot Pushing (conditioning on 1 frame, generating 15) and Kinetics-600 (conditioning on 5 frames, generating 11), using I3D-based FVD and IS metrics. For text-conditioned video generation, a dataset of 10 million captioned videos will be used, with BERT-large embeddings as conditioning, and both small and large model variants will be trained. Ablation studies will assess the impact of joint image-video training, classifier-free guidance, and the reconstruction-guided sampling method. Evaluation will include both frame-averaged and first-frame FID/IS metrics, and experiments will test autoregressive extension and super-resolution capabilities.
3b2a675bb617ae1a920e8e29d535cdf27826e999.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first diffusion-based framework for high-fidelity video generation using a 3D U-Net with space-time factorized attention, enabling joint training on image and video data. A novel reconstruction-guided conditional sampling method is developed, improving temporal coherence and sample quality for autoregressive extension and super-resolution, and outperforming existing replacement/imputation methods. The approach enables scalable generation of long, high-resolution videos and demonstrates state-of-the-art results on multiple standard video generation and prediction benchmarks. The architecture's flexibility allows for seamless integration of text conditioning and classifier-free guidance, advancing the field of generative video modeling.

3b448545de12ed242638c301ddd484f591f5d74c.title: On Extending Direct Preference Optimization to Accommodate Ties
3b448545de12ed242638c301ddd484f591f5d74c.research_question: How can preference optimization methods be extended to effectively accommodate tied outcomes in pairwise comparison data, and what are the impacts of such extensions on model performance and regularization in tasks such as neural machine translation, summarization, and mathematical reasoning?
3b448545de12ed242638c301ddd484f591f5d74c.hypothesis: Explicitly modeling ties in preference optimization using extensions of the Bradley-Terry model (such as the Rao-Kupper and Davidson models) will enable the inclusion of tied data without degrading task performance, while providing stronger regularization with respect to the reference policy and improving overall model performance compared to standard DPO.
3b448545de12ed242638c301ddd484f591f5d74c.proposed_method: A novel extension to Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) is proposed by replacing the standard Bradley-Terry preference model with two established models that accommodate ties: the Rao-Kupper and Davidson models. These models introduce additional parameters to allocate probability mass to tied outcomes in pairwise comparisons, allowing the learning objective to explicitly handle both clear wins and ties. The DPO objective is reformulated to include a binary indicator for ties, and the corresponding likelihoods for wins and ties are derived from the chosen model (Rao-Kupper or Davidson). Gradient updates are adjusted to encourage the model to increase the reward margin for wins and minimize the absolute reward margin for ties, effectively learning to model both types of outcomes. Hyperparameters controlling the likelihood of ties are introduced but are shown to have minor impact when set within sensible ranges.
3b448545de12ed242638c301ddd484f591f5d74c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on neural machine translation (WMT-21 ZH-EN, IWSLT-17 FR-EN), summarization (TL;DR), and mathematical reasoning (GSM8K) tasks. Preference datasets will be constructed to include both clear preference pairs (CPs) and tied pairs (TPs), with ties identified via automatic metrics (e.g., BLEURT, XCOMET, KIWI-XXL) or by annotator disagreement. Baselines will include standard DPO trained only on CPs, as well as DPO trained on CP+TP, and other preference optimization methods such as SimPO and CPO. Evaluation metrics will include BLEURT for translation, win-rate for summarization, and exact match accuracy for mathematical reasoning, along with KL divergence to the reference policy and preservation rate. The effect of including ties on both task performance and regularization will be systematically measured, and ablation studies will assess the impact of hyperparameter choices and the proportion of ties.
3b448545de12ed242638c301ddd484f591f5d74c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first tie-compatible variants of DPO by incorporating the Rao-Kupper and Davidson models, enabling the use of tied data that is typically discarded in preference optimization. The method provides a theoretical explanation for the regularization effect of ties, demonstrates that ties can be leveraged to improve model performance and regularization without performance degradation, and introduces new data selection strategies for identifying tied pairs. The approach is validated across multiple tasks, showing consistent improvements over strong DPO baselines and offering a principled way to make fuller use of available preference data.

3b6179c293df29e31d31cea46476f104ab6950f2.title: Kosmos-2: Grounding Multimodal Large Language Models to the World
3b6179c293df29e31d31cea46476f104ab6950f2.research_question: How can multimodal large language models be enhanced to ground textual descriptions to specific regions in images, enabling more accurate and interactive vision-language understanding and generation across a wide range of tasks?
3b6179c293df29e31d31cea46476f104ab6950f2.hypothesis: Integrating explicit grounding mechanisms that link text spans to visual regions via location tokens and training on large-scale grounded image-text data will enable multimodal large language models to achieve improved performance and new capabilities in grounding, referring, and perception-language tasks.
3b6179c293df29e31d31cea46476f104ab6950f2.proposed_method: A novel multimodal large language model will be developed that incorporates grounding and referring capabilities by linking text spans (such as noun phrases and referring expressions) to corresponding image regions using discrete location tokens representing bounding boxes. The model will adopt a Transformer-based causal language modeling architecture, initialized from a strong multimodal backbone, and trained with a next-token prediction objective. A large-scale dataset of grounded image-text pairs (GRIT) will be constructed by extracting and linking text spans in image captions to spatial locations in images using a combination of natural language parsing and pretrained grounding models. The input representation will unify text and location tokens in a Markdown-like hyperlink format, enabling the model to map between textual expressions and visual regions. Instruction tuning will further align the model's outputs with human instructions using both vision-language and language-only instruction datasets, as well as grounded instruction data constructed from the GRIT dataset.
3b6179c293df29e31d31cea46476f104ab6950f2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of tasks, including multimodal grounding (phrase grounding on Flickr30k Entities, referring expression comprehension on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg), multimodal referring (referring expression generation on RefCOCOg), perception-language tasks (image captioning on Flickr30k, visual question answering on VQAv2), and language understanding/generation tasks (StoryCloze, HellaSwag, Winograd, Winogrande, PIQA, and SuperGLUE datasets). Baselines will include both finetuned and zero-shot models such as VisualBert, MDETR, GLIP, FIBER, OFA, GRILL, SLR, and previous versions of the model. Evaluation metrics will comprise recall at various thresholds (R@1, R@5, R@10) for grounding, accuracy for comprehension, METEOR and CIDEr for generation, CIDEr for captioning, VQA accuracy, and standard metrics for language tasks. The model will be trained on 256 V100 GPUs with a batch size of 419K tokens, and the training will include a mixture of text, image-text, interleaved, and grounded image-text data.
3b6179c293df29e31d31cea46476f104ab6950f2.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified framework for grounding and referring in multimodal large language models by representing links between text spans and image regions as discrete location tokens in a Markdown-like format. The construction of a massive web-scale grounded image-text dataset (GRIT) enables effective training of grounding capabilities at scale. The model demonstrates new abilities to provide visual answers (bounding boxes), ground generated text to images, and interactively refer to image regions, surpassing previous zero-shot baselines and achieving competitive or superior performance on a wide range of vision-language and language tasks. This work lays the foundation for the convergence of language, multimodal perception, and world modeling, advancing towards more general and embodied AI systems.

3b80d47e0220ecfb122e4ac00d90f7517b9a9d4d.title: GeoLoRA: Geometric integration for parameter efficient fine-tuning
3b80d47e0220ecfb122e4ac00d90f7517b9a9d4d.research_question: How can parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large-scale, pre-trained neural networks be improved to achieve adaptive parameter allocation, robustness to hyperparameters, and computational efficiency, while maintaining theoretical guarantees of convergence and local optimality?
3b80d47e0220ecfb122e4ac00d90f7517b9a9d4d.hypothesis: A dynamic, geometry-aware low-rank adaptation method that leverages matrix differential equation theory and parallel updates can achieve adaptive parameter allocation, improved robustness, and computational efficiency for fine-tuning large-scale neural networks, outperforming existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods in both accuracy and speed.
3b80d47e0220ecfb122e4ac00d90f7517b9a9d4d.proposed_method: A novel parameter-efficient fine-tuning approach, GeoLoRA, will be developed based on dynamic low-rank approximation theory and geometric integration from matrix differential equations. The method will factorize weight updates into low-rank matrices and perform parallel updates of basis and coefficient matrices using a single backpropagation pass per iteration. The algorithm will include a basis augmentation step that doubles the search space for rank adaptivity, followed by a truncation step using singular value decomposition (SVD) to prune redundant components based on a threshold. This approach ensures orthonormality of the low-rank factors, mitigates stiffness in the optimization dynamics, and provides convergence guarantees to locally optimal solutions within the low-rank parameter space. The method will be applicable to both single-layer and multi-layer neural architectures, with initialization strategies compatible with standard LoRA-type adapters.
3b80d47e0220ecfb122e4ac00d90f7517b9a9d4d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several state-of-the-art benchmarks, including the GLUE benchmark for natural language processing (using DeBERTaV3-base), Vision Transformers (Vit-base-patch16-224) on datasets such as Cifar10, Cifar100, and Tiny-Imagenet, and Stable Diffusion with Dreambooth for generative tasks. The proposed method will be compared against baselines such as full fine-tuning, LoRA, AdaLoRA, DLRT, BitFit, Houlsby and Pfeiffer adapters. Evaluation metrics will include task-specific accuracy, F1, MCC, and correlation, as well as computational efficiency measured by training and evaluation iterations per second and the number of trainable parameters. Hyperparameter robustness and ablation studies will be performed to assess sensitivity to initial rank and learning rate. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by using consistent architectures, random seeds, and reporting median results over multiple runs.
3b80d47e0220ecfb122e4ac00d90f7517b9a9d4d.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first parameter-efficient fine-tuning approach that solves the optimal geometric gradient flow for low-rank adaptation using only a single gradient evaluation per iteration, matching or surpassing the computational efficiency of standard LoRA and AdaLoRA. It provides adaptive parameter allocation across model layers, robust convergence guarantees, and theoretical error bounds. The parallel update and basis augmentation strategy enables dynamic rank adaptation without the need for hyperparameter tuning of the initial rank. The method demonstrates superior empirical performance in both accuracy and speed, with fewer trainable parameters, and maintains robustness to hyperparameter choices compared to existing PEFT methods.

3b9b1aba877ecd3f7e508cbc78a41b623349902b.title: Translation between Molecules and Natural Language
3b9b1aba877ecd3f7e508cbc78a41b623349902b.research_question: How can translation between molecular structures and natural language be enabled and improved, allowing for bi-directional tasks such as molecule captioning and text-based de novo molecule generation, especially in the context of limited annotated data in the chemistry domain?
3b9b1aba877ecd3f7e508cbc78a41b623349902b.hypothesis: Joint pretraining of a large language model on both natural language text and molecule string representations in a self-supervised manner will enable effective cross-modal translation between molecules and natural language, outperforming existing sequence-to-sequence baselines on tasks such as molecule captioning and text-based molecule generation.
3b9b1aba877ecd3f7e508cbc78a41b623349902b.proposed_method: A self-supervised learning framework, MolT5, will be developed by initializing an encoder-decoder Transformer model from a public T5 checkpoint. The model will be pretrained on large-scale, unlabeled corpora of both natural language (e.g., the C4 dataset) and molecule strings (e.g., 100 million SMILES strings from ZINC-15) using a denoising objective where random spans of tokens are corrupted and the model learns to reconstruct them. This pretraining will be performed without explicit alignment between the two modalities, treating molecules and language as distinct 'languages' in a multilingual-like setup. After pretraining, the model will be fine-tuned for two novel cross-modal tasks: (1) molecule captioning, where the input is a molecule (SMILES string) and the output is a natural language description, and (2) text-based de novo molecule generation, where the input is a natural language description and the output is a molecule (SMILES string). The framework will also incorporate a cross-modal retrieval metric based on a pretrained Text2Mol model to evaluate semantic similarity between generated and reference outputs.
3b9b1aba877ecd3f7e508cbc78a41b623349902b.experiment_details: Experiments will involve pretraining the MolT5 model on the C4 text corpus and the ZINC-15 SMILES dataset, followed by fine-tuning and evaluation on the ChEBI-20 dataset, which contains 33,010 molecule-description pairs split into train/validation/test sets. Baselines will include RNN-GRU, vanilla Transformer, and T5 models of various sizes, all trained and evaluated on the same tasks. Evaluation metrics for molecule captioning will include BLEU, ROUGE, METEOR, and the cross-modal Text2Mol similarity score. For molecule generation, metrics will include BLEU, exact string match, Levenshtein distance, multiple fingerprint-based Tanimoto similarities (MACCS FTS, RDK FTS, Morgan FTS), Fréchet ChemNet Distance (FCD), Text2Mol similarity, and validity (percentage of syntactically valid molecules). Both tasks will be evaluated on the held-out test split of ChEBI-20, and statistical significance of results will be assessed.
3b9b1aba877ecd3f7e508cbc78a41b623349902b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces two novel cross-modal tasks—molecule captioning and text-based de novo molecule generation—enabling bi-directional translation between molecules and natural language. The MolT5 framework is claimed to be the first self-supervised pretraining approach to jointly leverage large-scale unlabeled data from both modalities for these tasks. Additionally, a new cross-modal evaluation metric based on Text2Mol is proposed for more semantically meaningful assessment. The approach is expected to overcome data scarcity in the chemistry domain and to outperform existing baselines, providing a foundation for future research in multimodal molecular AI.

3bbd7f15e02dc8d844e9042136108bd3999cf8d3.title: xLSTM 7B: A Recurrent LLM for Fast and Efficient Inference
3bbd7f15e02dc8d844e9042136108bd3999cf8d3.research_question: Can a large-scale language model based on the xLSTM recurrent architecture be developed to achieve fast and efficient inference, while maintaining competitive performance on language modeling and downstream tasks compared to state-of-the-art Transformer and Mamba-based models?
3bbd7f15e02dc8d844e9042136108bd3999cf8d3.hypothesis: Scaling the xLSTM architecture to 7 billion parameters, combined with targeted architectural and training optimizations, will yield a language model that matches or exceeds the inference speed and efficiency of existing models, while maintaining comparable language modeling and downstream task performance.
3bbd7f15e02dc8d844e9042136108bd3999cf8d3.proposed_method: A 7-billion-parameter language model will be developed using an optimized xLSTM recurrent neural network architecture. The core mLSTM cell will be operated in the model's embedding dimension and integrated with position-wise feedforward MLP layers (SwiGLU) after each mLSTM layer to maximize the proportion of efficient linear operations. Channel-wise convolutions, learnable skip connections, and small projection layers will be removed to improve GPU utilization and reduce memory footprint. Training and inference efficiency will be further enhanced by employing fused GPU kernels for the mLSTM cell, chunkwise-parallel training, and multi-head mLSTM layers. Training stability will be addressed by using RMSNorm for pre-norm layers, soft-capping input and forget gates, and initializing the input gate bias to large negative values. The model will be trained on 2.3 trillion tokens with a context length of 8192, leveraging large-scale distributed training on 128 H100 GPUs.
3bbd7f15e02dc8d844e9042136108bd3999cf8d3.experiment_details: The proposed model will be evaluated on the Huggingface Open LLM Leaderboard v2 using the LMEvaluationHarness, covering a range of downstream tasks such as BBH, MMLU-PRO, MATH, MUSR, GPQA, and IFEVAL. Long-context capabilities will be assessed using the RULER benchmark, with context lengths up to 131K tokens, and compared to both Transformer (Llama-2, Llama-3) and recurrent (Mamba, RWKV) baselines. Inference speed and efficiency will be benchmarked on a single NVIDIA H100 GPU, measuring generation throughput, time to first token, memory consumption, and prefill throughput at varying batch sizes and context lengths. Ablation studies will be conducted to assess the impact of architectural choices such as memory state size, normalization layers, and gate initialization on training stability, efficiency, and performance.
3bbd7f15e02dc8d844e9042136108bd3999cf8d3.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first large-scale (7B parameter) xLSTM-based language model, demonstrating that recurrent architectures can be scaled to match or exceed the inference efficiency and speed of state-of-the-art Transformer and Mamba models. Key innovations include architectural optimizations for both training and inference (such as operating the mLSTM in embedding space, integrating efficient MLP layers, and removing inefficiencies), as well as stability enhancements through normalization and gating strategies. The approach achieves the highest inference throughput and lowest memory footprint among comparable models, establishing xLSTM as a strong foundation for future methods requiring heavy test-time computation.

3bbf541c2a3ce0ffaed3703cd486f0e1b2febb27.title: Token-Budget-Aware LLM Reasoning
3bbf541c2a3ce0ffaed3703cd486f0e1b2febb27.research_question: How can the reasoning process of large language models (LLMs) be made more efficient in terms of token usage, while maintaining high answer correctness across a variety of complex reasoning tasks?
3bbf541c2a3ce0ffaed3703cd486f0e1b2febb27.hypothesis: Incorporating token-budget awareness into the reasoning process of LLMs will significantly reduce token usage and computational costs, with only minimal impact on answer accuracy.
3bbf541c2a3ce0ffaed3703cd486f0e1b2febb27.proposed_method: A token-budget-aware reasoning framework for LLMs will be developed, featuring two main approaches: (1) Estimation & Prompting (TALE-EP), which uses zero-shot prompting to estimate a reasonable token budget for each problem and constructs a token-budget-aware prompt to guide the LLM's reasoning; and (2) Post-Training (TALE-PT), which post-trains the LLM to internalize token-budget awareness by generating target outputs under optimal token budgets and fine-tuning the model using supervised or preference-based objectives. The optimal token budget for each problem will be determined via a binary or greedy search, balancing minimal token usage and answer correctness. The TALE-EP approach leverages the LLM itself as a budget estimator, while TALE-PT uses crafted datasets from the budget search to train the model to produce concise, accurate responses without explicit budget prompts.
3bbf541c2a3ce0ffaed3703cd486f0e1b2febb27.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several challenging mathematical reasoning datasets, including GSM8K, GSM8K-Zero, and MathBench (with arithmetic, middle, high, and college-level subsets). Multiple state-of-the-art LLMs (e.g., GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Yi-lightning, o3-mini, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) will be evaluated. Baselines will include Direct Answering (no reasoning), Vanilla Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting, and other prompt engineering methods. Evaluation metrics will include answer accuracy, average output token usage, and computational expense (measured in cost per sample). The experimental setup will also assess generalization across different LLMs and analyze the trade-off between efficiency and correctness under various token budgets.
3bbf541c2a3ce0ffaed3703cd486f0e1b2febb27.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces dynamic, problem-specific token budgeting for LLM reasoning, enabling significant reductions in token usage and computational cost. The method is the first to systematically search for and internalize optimal token budgets in LLM reasoning, addressing the token redundancy problem in CoT prompting. It provides both a training-free, zero-shot estimation approach (TALE-EP) and a post-training solution (TALE-PT) that can be applied across diverse LLM architectures. The approach is shown to maintain high accuracy while reducing token usage by up to 67%, offering a practical solution for cost-effective and efficient LLM deployment.

3be60571c2befc478b37f2a0d902a8a277023423.title: Scalable Equilibrium Sampling with Sequential Boltzmann Generators
3be60571c2befc478b37f2a0d902a8a277023423.research_question: How can scalable and efficient equilibrium sampling of molecular systems at all-atom resolution be achieved, particularly for larger peptides, using generative modeling techniques in Cartesian coordinates?
3be60571c2befc478b37f2a0d902a8a277023423.hypothesis: A Transformer-based, non-equivariant, exactly invertible normalizing flow, combined with inference-time scaling via continuous-time annealed importance sampling and sequential Monte Carlo, will enable efficient and scalable equilibrium sampling of molecular systems in Cartesian coordinates, outperforming prior Boltzmann generator approaches.
3be60571c2befc478b37f2a0d902a8a277023423.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces Sequential Boltzmann Generators (SBG), which extend the Boltzmann generator framework by integrating a highly efficient Transformer-based normalizing flow (TarFlow) that operates directly on all-atom Cartesian coordinates. Instead of enforcing strict SE(3)-equivariance in the architecture, SBG employs soft equivariance through data augmentation (random rotations and center-of-mass noise) and normalization strategies, allowing for scalable and expressive model architectures. At inference, SBG performs continuous-time inference scaling using annealed Langevin dynamics to transport flow samples toward the target Boltzmann distribution, coupling this with a continuous-time variant of sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) or annealed importance sampling (AIS). The method includes theoretical adjustments for center-of-mass augmentation and energy thresholding to improve sample efficiency and stability during resampling.
3be60571c2befc478b37f2a0d902a8a277023423.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on datasets of small peptides (up to 6 alanine residues and the 10-residue chignolin peptide), generated from molecular dynamics simulations with classical force fields. The training, validation, and test splits are defined by simulation time windows, ensuring some metastable states may be underrepresented in training. SBG will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines, including exactly equivariant invertible flows and continuous normalizing flows (ECNF, SE(3)-EACF), using metrics such as effective sample size (ESS), Wasserstein-2 distances on energy and dihedral angle distributions, and overlap with molecular dynamics (MD) reference distributions. The experimental setup will include both SNIS and SMC/AIS inference for reweighting, and computational efficiency (GPU hours) will be measured as a function of system size and inference steps.
3be60571c2befc478b37f2a0d902a8a277023423.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable uncorrelated, learned equilibrium sampling in Cartesian coordinates for peptides up to six residues and demonstrates significant progress toward decapeptides, surpassing the scalability of prior Boltzmann generators. The use of a Transformer-based, non-equivariant, exactly invertible normalizing flow (TarFlow) with soft equivariance is novel in this context, allowing for efficient likelihood evaluation and inference scaling. The integration of continuous-time annealing (AIS/SMC) at inference, coupled with theoretical adjustments for center-of-mass augmentation and energy thresholding, provides improved sample efficiency, stability, and scalability compared to previous methods. The method achieves state-of-the-art performance across all evaluated metrics on challenging molecular systems.

3c185b6a2d9d2bcccd9be6e61ff8fafa91a3a638.title: Feedback Schrödinger Bridge Matching
3c185b6a2d9d2bcccd9be6e61ff8fafa91a3a638.research_question: How can distribution matching frameworks efficiently leverage partially aligned datasets to improve scalability, generalization, and training efficiency in distribution transport problems, especially when only a small fraction of optimal pairings are available?
3c185b6a2d9d2bcccd9be6e61ff8fafa91a3a638.hypothesis: Incorporating a small portion of pre-aligned sample pairs as state feedback into the transport map will significantly improve the efficiency, generalization, and robustness of distribution matching frameworks, compared to fully unsupervised or fully supervised approaches.
3c185b6a2d9d2bcccd9be6e61ff8fafa91a3a638.proposed_method: A novel semi-supervised matching framework, Feedback Schrödinger Bridge Matching (FSBM), will be developed to integrate information from partially aligned datasets. The approach begins with a static entropic optimal transport (EOT) formulation, augmented by a regularization term that encodes guidance from a small set of pre-aligned key-point (KP) pairs. This regularization is designed to preserve the relative distances of non-aligned samples to their nearest KP pairs, effectively forming regions of attraction in the source and target distributions. The static EOT objective is then recast into a dynamic formulation, enabling the use of scalable matching frameworks. The training process alternates between optimizing the intermediate path (conditioned on endpoints and KP guidance) and refining the parameterized drift, using a Bregman divergence-based variational gap objective. The method is simulation-free for the intermediate path, leveraging closed-form Gaussian path approximations and state-feedback mechanisms to steer the transport of non-aligned samples.
3c185b6a2d9d2bcccd9be6e61ff8fafa91a3a638.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of distribution matching tasks, including low-dimensional crowd navigation, high-dimensional opinion depolarization, and unpaired image translation (gender and age translation). For image translation, the FFHQ dataset (1024x1024) will be used, with translations performed in the latent space of a pre-trained ALAE autoencoder. In all cases, less than 8% of the dataset will be used as pre-aligned pairs for guidance. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art frameworks such as GSBM, DSBM, DeepGSB, and LOSBM. Evaluation metrics will include Wasserstein distance (W2), KL divergence, Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), and LPIPS for image quality, as well as training time and memory usage. Experimental setups will test generalization to perturbed initial conditions and measure robustness, efficiency, and accuracy of the generated distributions.
3c185b6a2d9d2bcccd9be6e61ff8fafa91a3a638.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first matching framework that leverages information from partially aligned datasets using a semi-supervised approach. It generalizes static entropic optimal transport to a dynamic setting with a novel guidance regularization, enabling efficient and scalable training with minimal supervision. The framework bridges the gap between fully unsupervised and fully supervised matching, achieving improved generalization, robustness to initial condition perturbations, and reduced training time. The approach is extensible to various regularization functions and demonstrates superior performance across a range of distribution matching tasks.

3c1e43b7d3f5fd42a06c65e3aafe6d8f4a606d5c.title: MC-JEPA: A Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Self-Supervised Learning of Motion and Content Features
3c1e43b7d3f5fd42a06c65e3aafe6d8f4a606d5c.research_question: How can self-supervised learning be advanced to jointly learn both motion and content features from visual data, enabling a single model to perform well on tasks requiring motion understanding (such as optical flow estimation) and content understanding (such as segmentation) across images and videos?
3c1e43b7d3f5fd42a06c65e3aafe6d8f4a606d5c.hypothesis: Jointly training a single encoder on both self-supervised optical flow estimation and self-supervised content feature learning will result in visual representations that capture both motion and content information, leading to improved or on-par performance on a wide range of downstream tasks compared to models trained on either task alone.
3c1e43b7d3f5fd42a06c65e3aafe6d8f4a606d5c.proposed_method: A multi-task self-supervised learning architecture, termed MC-JEPA, will be developed to jointly learn optical flow and content features using a shared encoder. The optical flow estimation branch will be based on a hierarchical, coarse-to-fine adaptation of PWC-Net, incorporating regression, reconstruction, smoothness, and cycle-consistency losses to learn dense pixel correspondences between consecutive video frames. The content learning branch will utilize a joint-embedding predictive approach, specifically the VICReg objective, to embed two augmented views of an image and enforce invariance, variance, and covariance regularization. Both branches will share the encoder weights, and training will alternate or combine batches from video (for flow) and images (for content), with a carefully balanced loss function. Additional stabilization techniques, such as variance-covariance regularization and layer normalization, will be employed to ensure stable multi-task training.
3c1e43b7d3f5fd42a06c65e3aafe6d8f4a606d5c.experiment_details: The model will be pretrained in a single phase on a combination of optical flow datasets (KITTI raw/2012/2015, MPI Sintel, FlyingChairs, FlyingThings, HD1K) and ImageNet-1k for content learning. Evaluation will be conducted on standard optical flow benchmarks (Sintel clean/final, KITTI 2015) using average end-point-error (EPE), and on segmentation tasks (Pascal VOC, Cityscapes, ADE20k) using mean intersection-over-union (mIoU), both in linear frozen and fine-tuning settings. Video segmentation and instance tracking will be evaluated on DAVIS 2017 using the (J&F)m metric. Baselines will include state-of-the-art self-supervised flow methods (UFlow, ARFlow, UPFlow, SMURF), correspondence learning methods (VFS, MCRW), and content feature learning methods (VICReg, VICRegL, MoCo v3, DINO). Ablation studies will be performed on dataset composition, estimator architecture, backbone choice, data sampling strategies, and loss balancing coefficients.
3c1e43b7d3f5fd42a06c65e3aafe6d8f4a606d5c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to unify self-supervised optical flow estimation and content feature learning in a multi-task joint-embedding framework with a single shared encoder. It introduces a stabilized multi-task training procedure that leverages both motion and content objectives, resulting in representations that generalize across motion and content-centric downstream tasks. The method achieves strong or state-of-the-art performance on both optical flow and segmentation benchmarks, demonstrating the mutual benefit of combining these objectives and the feasibility of a single model for diverse visual tasks.

3c2f14a28ba5e826c63c294f4cca01a8217a217e.title: Neural Combinatorial Optimization with Heavy Decoder: Toward Large Scale Generalization
3c2f14a28ba5e826c63c294f4cca01a8217a217e.research_question: How can neural combinatorial optimization methods be designed to generalize effectively to large-scale instances of combinatorial optimization problems, such as the Travelling Salesman Problem (TSP) and the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP), without relying on expert-designed algorithms or problem-specific heuristics?
3c2f14a28ba5e826c63c294f4cca01a8217a217e.hypothesis: A neural combinatorial optimization model employing a Light Encoder and Heavy Decoder (LEHD) architecture, combined with a data-efficient supervised training scheme and a flexible solution reconstruction mechanism, will achieve superior generalization and state-of-the-art performance on large-scale combinatorial optimization problems compared to existing learning-based and classical solvers.
3c2f14a28ba5e826c63c294f4cca01a8217a217e.proposed_method: A novel neural combinatorial optimization framework will be developed based on a Light Encoder and Heavy Decoder (LEHD) architecture. The encoder will consist of a single attention layer that transforms node features into initial embeddings, while the decoder will employ multiple attention layers to dynamically re-embed the starting node, destination node, and available nodes at each step of the solution construction process. This dynamic re-embedding enables the model to capture scale-independent relationships among nodes, facilitating generalization to larger problem instances. The model will be trained using a supervised learning approach that leverages data augmentation by generating and learning to construct partial solutions of varying sizes and directions, based on the property of optimality invariance. Additionally, a Random Re-Construct (RRC) mechanism will be implemented at inference time to iteratively improve solution quality by reconstructing randomly sampled partial solutions within a specified computational budget.
3c2f14a28ba5e826c63c294f4cca01a8217a217e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets for TSP and CVRP, including standard benchmarks such as TSPLib and CVRPLib. The training sets will consist of one million instances of size 100 for both TSP and CVRP, with optimal solutions generated using Concorde and HGS solvers, respectively. Test sets will include 10,000 instances for size 100 and 128 instances each for sizes 200, 500, and 1000. The proposed method will be compared against classical solvers (Concorde, LKH3, OR-Tools), state-of-the-art constructive NCO models (POMO, MDAM, EAS, SGBS, BQ), and heatmap-based methods (Att-GCN+MCTS). Evaluation metrics will include optimality gap and inference time, with ablation studies to assess the impact of the heavy decoder structure, supervised versus reinforcement learning, and the RRC mechanism. All experiments will be run on a single NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPU with 24GB memory.
3c2f14a28ba5e826c63c294f4cca01a8217a217e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new Light Encoder and Heavy Decoder (LEHD) model architecture for neural combinatorial optimization, enabling dynamic, scale-independent relationship learning among nodes and robust generalization to large-scale problem instances. A data-efficient supervised training scheme based on partial solution construction is developed, facilitating efficient and robust model training without reliance on reinforcement learning or expert-designed heuristics. The Random Re-Construct (RRC) mechanism provides a flexible and effective method for online solution improvement. The method is purely learning-based, does not require problem-specific heuristics, and achieves state-of-the-art performance on both synthetic and real-world TSP and CVRP benchmarks, outperforming existing learning-based and classical solvers on large-scale instances.

3c314149c36871bace898f3dcff03fb21de0ba64.title: PhysGen: Rigid-Body Physics-Grounded Image-to-Video Generation
3c314149c36871bace898f3dcff03fb21de0ba64.research_question: How can physically plausible and controllable videos be generated from a single image by integrating explicit physics simulation with data-driven generative models?
3c314149c36871bace898f3dcff03fb21de0ba64.hypothesis: Integrating model-based rigid-body physics simulation with data-driven generative video models will enable the generation of realistic, physically plausible, and controllable videos from a single image, outperforming existing purely data-driven approaches in terms of physical realism and user controllability.
3c314149c36871bace898f3dcff03fb21de0ba64.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed that takes a single image and user-specified physical inputs (such as force or torque) to generate a realistic video sequence grounded in rigid-body physics. The method consists of three main components: (1) a perception module that uses large pretrained visual foundation models (e.g., GPT-4V, Grounded-SAM) to infer object segmentation, geometry, and physical properties (mass, friction, elasticity) from the image; (2) an image-space rigid-body dynamics simulation module that models object motions, collisions, friction, and elasticity under Newtonian mechanics, using numerical ODE integration and 2D shape primitives; and (3) a rendering pipeline that first composites and relights the scene using intrinsic decomposition and a Lambertian shading model, then refines the output with a pretrained video diffusion model, ensuring temporal consistency, realistic lighting, and seamless object-background integration. The entire process is training-free and operates at inference time, allowing for precise user control over initial physical conditions.
3c314149c36871bace898f3dcff03fb21de0ba64.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a diverse set of images sourced from both the internet and self-captured indoor photos, covering a range of lighting conditions, object types, geometries, and physical scenarios. The proposed method is quantitatively and qualitatively compared against state-of-the-art image-to-video generation models (SEINE, I2VGen-XL, and others) and image editing baselines. Evaluation metrics include physical realism, photo-realism, and user study assessments, with ground-truth videos collected for quantitative comparison by varying input conditions. The video generation pipeline runs at a resolution of 512x512, using 120 simulation steps and sampling 16 frames per video, with a pretrained video diffusion model (SEINE) for refinement and DDIM sampling for denoising.
3c314149c36871bace898f3dcff03fb21de0ba64.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel integration of explicit rigid-body physics simulation with data-driven generative video models for image-to-video generation. It enables zero-shot inference of object physical properties from a single image using large foundation models, supports user-controllable and interactive video generation by conditioning on physical inputs, and produces videos that are both physically plausible and photo-realistic. The method is training-free, operates solely at inference time, and demonstrates superior physical realism and controllability compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

3c59f7b8ec13dee65516a1d75093fd145250e76a.title: ImageFolder: Autoregressive Image Generation with Folded Tokens
3c59f7b8ec13dee65516a1d75093fd145250e76a.research_question: How can image tokenization be improved to balance the trade-off between reconstruction quality and generation efficiency in autoregressive image generation models, particularly by reducing token sequence length without sacrificing image quality?
3c59f7b8ec13dee65516a1d75093fd145250e76a.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a semantic image tokenizer leveraging product quantization with spatially aligned and folded tokens, combined with semantic regularization and quantizer dropout, can achieve high-quality image reconstruction and generation while significantly reducing the token sequence length required for autoregressive modeling.
3c59f7b8ec13dee65516a1d75093fd145250e76a.proposed_method: A novel image tokenizer, termed ImageFolder, will be developed to tokenize images into spatially aligned semantic and detail tokens using a dual-branch product quantization approach. The method employs a vision transformer encoder to generate low-resolution features, which are then quantized in two branches: one branch is regularized with a semantic contrastive loss (using a frozen DINOv2 model) to capture semantic content, while the other captures pixel-level details. Multi-scale residual quantization is used in both branches, and a quantizer dropout strategy is introduced to encourage the model to encode images at varying bitrates, smoothing the next-scale autoregressive modeling. The quantized tokens from both branches are concatenated and can be folded for parallel prediction during autoregressive generation, effectively halving the sequence length while maintaining or improving image quality.
3c59f7b8ec13dee65516a1d75093fd145250e76a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ImageNet 256x256 dataset for both image reconstruction and generation tasks. The ImageFolder tokenizer will be compared against state-of-the-art tokenizers and generative models, including VQGAN, VAR, LlamaGen, and others, using metrics such as Frechet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS), Precision, Recall, and linear probing accuracy. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of key components such as product quantization, semantic regularization, quantizer dropout, and parallel decoding. The autoregressive generator will utilize a GPT-2-based architecture, with parallel prediction of token pairs from a single logit. Inference latency and computational efficiency will also be measured and compared to baselines.
