3c59f7b8ec13dee65516a1d75093fd145250e76a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a semantic image tokenizer that enables folding of spatially aligned tokens for parallel autoregressive prediction, reducing sequence length and computational cost without sacrificing reconstruction or generation quality. The dual-branch product quantization with selective semantic regularization and quantizer dropout is claimed to enhance the representation capacity and independence of tokens, facilitating robust and efficient image generation. The method provides new insights into the trade-off between token length and image quality, and demonstrates superior performance and efficiency over existing tokenizers and generative models.

3c5d8febc03379f5a5738eca00a6ecce4f26f996.title: COME: Adding Scene-Centric Forecasting Control to Occupancy World Model
3c5d8febc03379f5a5738eca00a6ecce4f26f996.research_question: How can future occupancy predictions for autonomous driving environments be made more accurate and controllable by disentangling ego-vehicle motion from scene dynamics in world models?
3c5d8febc03379f5a5738eca00a6ecce4f26f996.hypothesis: Explicitly separating ego-motion from scene evolution using scene-centric coordinate systems and injecting scene-consistent control features into occupancy world models will yield more spatially consistent, accurate, and controllable future occupancy predictions compared to existing methods that entangle these factors.
3c5d8febc03379f5a5738eca00a6ecce4f26f996.proposed_method: A novel three-stage framework is developed that leverages scene-centric forecasting control within an occupancy world model. First, a diffusion-based generative model predicts future occupancy maps conditioned on historical occupancy, ego-vehicle states, and optionally BEV layouts, encoding these with a variational autoencoder (Occ-VAE) and processing them through a spatial-temporal Diffusion Transformer with skip connections. Second, a scene-centric forecasting module transforms all occupancy frames into a unified scene-centric coordinate system using rigid-body transformations, enabling a U-Net to predict spatially consistent future features that are ego-motion invariant. Third, a specialized ControlNet module converts these scene-centric predictions into control features, applies a visibility-aware masking strategy to filter unreliable regions, and injects the refined features into the generative world model via residual addition and concatenation at corresponding layers. The entire system is trained in multiple stages: first the world model, then the forecasting module, and finally the ControlNet with other modules frozen.
3c5d8febc03379f5a5738eca00a6ecce4f26f996.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the Occ3D-nuScenes benchmark, which provides 3D occupancy labels for 18 categories over a large spatial range and resolution. The dataset is split into 700 training, 150 validation, and 150 test driving sequences. Evaluation metrics include semantic mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) and geometric IoU, reported at multiple future timestamps and averaged. The proposed method is compared against a comprehensive set of state-of-the-art baselines, including DOME, UniScene, OccWorld, OccVAR, OccLLaMA, and others, under diverse configurations: varying input modalities (camera, LiDAR, fusion), prediction horizons (3s, 8s), and trajectory sources (ground-truth, predicted). Ablation studies investigate the contributions of each module, training and inference setups, and the effects of masking and denoising steps. All models are trained on multiple GPUs with specified batch sizes and learning rates, and implementation details are provided for reproducibility.
3c5d8febc03379f5a5738eca00a6ecce4f26f996.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a divide-and-conquer strategy for occupancy world models by explicitly decomposing spatio-temporal prediction into ego-motion-agnostic and scene-dynamic components. The integration of a scene-centric forecasting module and a tailored ControlNet enables the injection of spatially consistent, ego-invariant control features into the generative model, enhancing both fidelity and controllability. The method empirically validates the benefits of disentangled representation learning, achieving significant and consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines across multiple settings and establishing new benchmarks for occupancy world modeling in autonomous driving.

3c6f2e0c5ff5dff6151c3e6489378a53318a75b4.title: ShortGPT: Layers in Large Language Models are More Redundant Than You Expect
3c6f2e0c5ff5dff6151c3e6489378a53318a75b4.research_question: How can large language models be compressed by identifying and removing redundant layers, while maintaining high performance across a variety of natural language understanding and reasoning tasks?
3c6f2e0c5ff5dff6151c3e6489378a53318a75b4.hypothesis: Many layers in large language models are redundant and can be removed based on a principled metric of layer importance, enabling significant reduction in model size and computational requirements with minimal impact on performance.
3c6f2e0c5ff5dff6151c3e6489378a53318a75b4.proposed_method: A new metric, Block Influence (BI), will be introduced to quantify the importance of each layer in a large language model by measuring the change in hidden states between a layer's input and output. The BI score is computed as one minus the expected cosine similarity between the input and output hidden states for each layer, using a calibration set of unlabeled text samples. Layers with the lowest BI scores, indicating minimal transformation of the hidden states, will be identified as redundant. A pruning strategy will be developed that removes these low-BI layers, with the number of layers pruned adjustable to balance performance and efficiency. The method will be evaluated for compatibility with quantization techniques and extended to both Transformer and non-Transformer architectures.
3c6f2e0c5ff5dff6151c3e6489378a53318a75b4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several popular open-source large language models, including Llama2-7B, Llama2-13B, Baichuan2-7B, Baichuan2-13B, RWKV-7B, and Mamba-2.8B. The evaluation will utilize a comprehensive suite of benchmarks covering reasoning (CMNLI, HellaSwag, PIQA), language understanding (CHID, WSC), knowledge (CoQA, BoolQ), examination (MMLU, CMMLU), and reading comprehension (Race-H/M, XSum, C3, PG19). Baseline methods for comparison will include structured pruning techniques such as LLMPruner, SliceGPT, and LaCo. Performance will be measured using metrics such as perplexity, accuracy, and average performance retention. Additional experiments will assess the effects of varying pruning ratios, the orthogonality of the approach to quantization (e.g., GPTQ), and the impact of post-training with lightweight MLP replacements for pruned layers.
3c6f2e0c5ff5dff6151c3e6489378a53318a75b4.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces Block Influence (BI), a novel, direct, and computationally efficient metric for quantifying layer importance in large language models. The proposed layer-removal pruning method is simple yet effective, outperforming previous state-of-the-art structured pruning techniques by maintaining up to 90% of model performance while reducing parameters and computation by approximately 25%. The method is shown to be orthogonal to quantization, enabling further model compression. Additionally, the approach is validated on both Transformer and non-Transformer architectures, suggesting that layer redundancy is a general property of current large language models.

3c8444cc4e96bdbe6853b886caf032afd1ee1d20.title: CausalLM is not optimal for in-context learning
3c8444cc4e96bdbe6853b886caf032afd1ee1d20.research_question: What are the theoretical and empirical differences in in-context learning performance between transformer-based prefix language models (prefixLM) and causal language models (causalLM), and how do their convergence properties affect their ability to achieve optimal solutions in various tasks?
3c8444cc4e96bdbe6853b886caf032afd1ee1d20.hypothesis: Prefix language models (prefixLM) achieve optimal in-context learning by converging to the least-squares solution in linear regression tasks, whereas causal language models (causalLM) do not guarantee optimality, even with increasing numbers of in-context examples, due to their online gradient descent-like convergence dynamics.
3c8444cc4e96bdbe6853b886caf032afd1ee1d20.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the convergence behavior of multi-layer Linear Self-Attention (LSA) transformers configured as either prefixLM or causalLM in the context of in-context learning, particularly for linear regression tasks. The analysis will formalize the relationship between multi-layer LSA transformers and multi-step gradient descent, providing proofs for the stationary points reached by each model type. Empirical validation will be conducted using both LSA-based and standard softmax attention transformers on synthetic tasks (linear and non-linear regression, multiclass classification), as well as large language models (LLMs) such as T5 and PaLM2. The methodology will include constructing input sequences with in-context examples and queries, configuring attention masks to reflect prefixLM and causalLM settings, and systematically comparing their convergence and generalization properties.
3c8444cc4e96bdbe6853b886caf032afd1ee1d20.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed in three main parts: (1) Direct verification of theoretical results using LSA-transformers on linear regression tasks, where sequences contain 40 in-context examples and 200 queries, with evaluation of mean squared error (MSE) on both training and query examples across multiple layers. (2) Evaluation of standard softmax transformers on synthetic datasets for linear regression, non-linear regression (using sigmoid activations), and multiclass classification, with 16-dimensional inputs, 24-layer models, and both shared and unshared layer configurations. Models will be trained on 64,000 sequences and evaluated on 64 holdout test sequences, using MSE for regression and classification error for multiclass tasks. (3) Large language model experiments will involve pretraining T5 decoder-only models (Base, Large, XL) with either prefixLM or causalLM attention masks on the C4 corpus, followed by FLAN-style finetuning and evaluation on MMLU (57 tasks, 5-shot) and BBH (23 tasks, 3-shot) benchmarks, reporting average test query accuracies. Additional experiments will extend to multimodal models like PaLI-X and further LLMs as detailed in appendices.
3c8444cc4e96bdbe6853b886caf032afd1ee1d20.novelty_claims: The proposal offers the first formal theoretical proof that multi-layer prefixLMs converge to the optimal least-squares solution in linear regression, while causalLMs converge to sub-optimal stationary points equivalent to online gradient descent without decaying step sizes. It establishes that causalLMs may never reach optimality in in-context learning, even with infinite data, due to architectural constraints. The empirical component systematically verifies these theoretical findings across both synthetic and real-world tasks, and demonstrates that the superiority of prefixLMs generalizes to standard transformers, large language models, and multimodal models. This comprehensive theoretical and empirical investigation provides new insights into the fundamental limitations of causalLMs for in-context learning.

3c8cc9a5ee373d51e0bf71621b6eb6901c762e8f.title: DriveLM: Driving with Graph Visual Question Answering
3c8cc9a5ee373d51e0bf71621b6eb6901c762e8f.research_question: How can vision-language models be effectively adapted for end-to-end autonomous driving, enabling multi-step reasoning and improved generalization, while supporting human-interpretable interaction through language-based question answering?
3c8cc9a5ee373d51e0bf71621b6eb6901c762e8f.hypothesis: Integrating graph-structured visual question answering with vision-language models will enable more human-like, multi-stage reasoning in autonomous driving systems, resulting in improved generalization to unseen scenarios and enhanced explainability compared to traditional end-to-end driving architectures.
3c8cc9a5ee373d51e0bf71621b6eb6901c762e8f.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that formulates autonomous driving as a Graph Visual Question Answering (GVQA) task, where the reasoning process is structured as a directed acyclic graph of question-answer (QA) pairs. Each node in the graph corresponds to a specific reasoning stage—perception, prediction, planning, behavior, and motion—with logical dependencies explicitly modeled as edges between QAs at both the object and task levels. The method leverages a large-scale vision-language model (e.g., BLIP-2) as the backbone, augmented with a graph-based prompting scheme: answers from preceding nodes are concatenated as context for subsequent questions, enabling multi-step, context-aware reasoning. For trajectory prediction, a trajectory tokenization module discretizes waypoints into bins, allowing the language model to output driving trajectories as sequences of tokens. The entire system is trained end-to-end, with fine-tuning performed separately for each reasoning stage using LoRA, and context aggregation is employed at the behavior stage to synthesize information from all prior reasoning steps.
3c8cc9a5ee373d51e0bf71621b6eb6901c762e8f.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on two newly constructed datasets: DriveLM-nuScenes, which combines manual and rule-based QA annotation on nuScenes data, and DriveLM-CARLA, which uses a fully rule-based expert (PDM-Lite) to generate QA graphs in the CARLA simulator. The evaluation protocol includes both standard trajectory prediction metrics (Average Displacement Error, Final Displacement Error, and collision rate) and language-based metrics (SPICE and GPT Score) for QA accuracy, as well as behavior classification accuracy. Baselines include a command-mean trajectory predictor, state-of-the-art driving models (e.g., UniAD), and ablated versions of the proposed method (e.g., single-stage BLIP-2, chain-based context, and full graph-based context). Experiments assess both in-domain performance and zero-shot generalization to unseen sensor configurations (e.g., training on nuScenes and testing on Waymo). Fine-tuning is performed on keyframes with batch sizes and epochs tailored to dataset size and hardware availability (e.g., 10 epochs on 8 V100 GPUs for nuScenes, 6 epochs on 4 A100 GPUs for CARLA).
3c8cc9a5ee373d51e0bf71621b6eb6901c762e8f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first graph-structured visual question answering framework for autonomous driving, explicitly modeling multi-step, object- and task-level logical dependencies in the reasoning process. It presents the largest and most comprehensive driving-language datasets to date, with dense QA annotation and logical graph structures. The method enables end-to-end vision-language models to perform interpretable, multi-stage reasoning and trajectory prediction, supporting zero-shot generalization to new sensor configurations and scenarios. The approach also provides a unified evaluation protocol combining trajectory and language metrics, and demonstrates that context-aware prompting with graph-structured QAs significantly enhances driving performance and explainability.

3c8e250026551ad5b8960de77343d13ce9050676.title: SimBa: Simplicity Bias for Scaling Up Parameters in Deep Reinforcement Learning
3c8e250026551ad5b8960de77343d13ce9050676.research_question: How can deep reinforcement learning (RL) networks be scaled up in terms of parameter count while maintaining or improving generalization and sample efficiency, and what architectural principles can be leveraged to mitigate overfitting in large-scale deep RL models?
3c8e250026551ad5b8960de77343d13ce9050676.hypothesis: Injecting architectural simplicity bias into deep RL networks enables effective scaling of network parameters, leading to improved sample efficiency and generalization across a variety of RL algorithms and environments, without incurring the overfitting typically associated with large models.
3c8e250026551ad5b8960de77343d13ce9050676.proposed_method: A novel neural network architecture, SIMBA, will be developed to embed simplicity bias into deep RL models, facilitating parameter scaling. The architecture will consist of three main components: (1) Running Statistics Normalization (RSNorm) to standardize input observations by tracking running means and variances per dimension, (2) Residual Feedforward Blocks with pre-layer normalization, providing a direct linear pathway from input to output and introducing non-linearity only when necessary, and (3) Post-Layer Normalization to stabilize activations before output layers, ensuring consistent feature magnitudes for reliable policy and value predictions. The architecture will be integrated into standard actor-critic RL frameworks, replacing conventional MLPs, and will be designed to be algorithm-agnostic. Fourier analysis will be used to quantify and validate the increase in simplicity bias at initialization, and architectural ablations will be conducted to isolate the contribution of each component.
3c8e250026551ad5b8960de77343d13ce9050676.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a diverse set of RL environments and tasks, including 51 continuous control tasks from DMC (DeepMind Control Suite), MyoSuite, and HumanoidBench, as well as open-ended and compositional tasks in Craftax. The proposed architecture will be evaluated within off-policy (SAC, TD-MPC2, DDPG), on-policy (PPO), and unsupervised RL (METRA) algorithms. Baselines will include state-of-the-art RL methods such as SAC, TD-MPC2, BRO, DreamerV3, and others, with all models using consistent input normalization for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics will include average episode return, sample efficiency, computational efficiency (measured by wall-clock time on standardized hardware), and, for unsupervised RL, state coverage. Additional analyses will assess the impact of input dimensionality, parameter scaling (width and depth), and replay ratio scaling, with ablation studies isolating the effects of normalization and architectural components. Results will be averaged over multiple random seeds to ensure statistical robustness.
3c8e250026551ad5b8960de77343d13ce9050676.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled architectural framework for scaling up deep RL networks by explicitly embedding simplicity bias, enabling large models to generalize effectively without complex regularization or training protocols. The method is algorithm-agnostic and requires only architectural modifications, not changes to loss functions or domain-specific regularizers. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate that the architecture matches or surpasses state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of RL algorithms and environments, with superior computational efficiency. The approach also provides new insights into the relationship between architectural simplicity bias and scalability in deep RL, and offers practical guidelines for parameter scaling and normalization in high-dimensional settings.

3cabe88c2ff476d35cd179525c7dfe474b4b75bb.title: BLADE: Benchmarking Language Model Agents for Data-Driven Science
3cabe88c2ff476d35cd179525c7dfe474b4b75bb.research_question: How can the analytical decision-making abilities of language model agents be rigorously evaluated on open-ended, data-driven scientific research questions using a benchmark that captures the complexity and diversity of real-world scientific analyses?
3cabe88c2ff476d35cd179525c7dfe474b4b75bb.hypothesis: A benchmark that evaluates language model agents on multifaceted, open-ended scientific analysis tasks—incorporating decision discernment, data transformation, and statistical modeling—will reveal current limitations in agents’ abilities to generate justifiable, diverse, and complex analyses, and will provide a more comprehensive assessment than existing single-answer or code-execution benchmarks.
3cabe88c2ff476d35cd179525c7dfe474b4b75bb.proposed_method: A new benchmark, BLADE, will be developed to evaluate language model agents on open-ended scientific research questions using real-world datasets. The benchmark will consist of tasks requiring agents to (1) discern justifiable analytical decisions, (2) generate end-to-end analyses including conceptual variable identification, data transformations, and statistical modeling, and (3) express these decisions in executable code and natural language. Ground truth analyses will be collected from expert annotators through a multi-stage, consensus-driven process, ensuring multiple justifiable approaches are represented. Automatic evaluation modules will be constructed to flexibly and robustly match agent outputs to ground truth using semantic equivalence for conceptual variables, data flow graphs for transformations, and natural language/model specification matching for statistical models. The evaluation framework will be designed to award partial credit for correct intermediate steps and to handle multiple valid analysis pathways.
3cabe88c2ff476d35cd179525c7dfe474b4b75bb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a suite of state-of-the-art language models (including GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Llama 3, Mixtral-8x22B, CodeLlama, and DeepSeek-Coder) and a ReAct-style agent capable of iterative reasoning in a notebook environment. The benchmark will include 12 real-world datasets and research questions, with 188 multiple choice questions and 536 ground truth analysis decisions. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy for multiple choice tasks and a decision-type-weighted F1-score (combining average precision and coverage@10) for analysis generation tasks. Baselines will be compared across both one-turn and agent-based settings, and results will be analyzed for precision, coverage, and diversity of generated analyses. The evaluation modules themselves will be validated for correctness against human expert judgments.
3cabe88c2ff476d35cd179525c7dfe474b4b75bb.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark is the first to rigorously evaluate language model agents on open-ended, data-driven scientific analyses, capturing the complexity and diversity of real-world analytical decision-making. It introduces a flexible, automatic, and decision-based evaluation framework that accounts for multiple justifiable analysis pathways and partial credit for intermediate steps. The benchmark advances beyond existing datasets by requiring comprehension of data semantics, integration of domain knowledge, multi-step reasoning, and discernment of justifiable decisions, providing a comprehensive tool for assessing and improving the scientific capabilities of language model agents.

3cb746ee9ab49920ead4bd832d94ca0bc1ee5d3b.title: Density Uncertainty Layers for Reliable Uncertainty Estimation
3cb746ee9ab49920ead4bd832d94ca0bc1ee5d3b.research_question: How can deep neural networks be designed to provide reliable and robust estimates of predictive uncertainty, particularly in safety-critical and out-of-distribution scenarios?
3cb746ee9ab49920ead4bd832d94ca0bc1ee5d3b.hypothesis: A neural network architecture that grounds its predictive uncertainty in the empirical density of the input data will yield more reliable uncertainty estimates, with higher uncertainty for inputs that are improbable in the training data and lower uncertainty for more probable inputs.
3cb746ee9ab49920ead4bd832d94ca0bc1ee5d3b.proposed_method: A new stochastic neural network architecture, termed the density uncertainty layer, will be developed to satisfy a density uncertainty criterion by design. This criterion enforces that predictive variance is proportional to an energy-based model of the input density, ensuring that uncertainty estimates reflect the empirical distribution of the training data. The architecture will incorporate energy-based generative models—such as full-rank or rank-1 mixture Gaussian energy models—at each layer, and injects noise in a manner that the variance of the network output is explicitly tied to the input's energy. The model will be trained by jointly optimizing the standard evidence lower bound (ELBO) for Bayesian neural networks and the generative objective for the energy models, using efficient parametrizations (e.g., LDL decomposition or rank-1 mixtures) to ensure scalability. The design will support both fully connected and convolutional architectures, and allow for efficient OOD detection using the learned energy statistics.
3cb746ee9ab49920ead4bd832d94ca0bc1ee5d3b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard uncertainty estimation benchmarks, including UCI regression datasets and CIFAR-10/100 image classification tasks. The proposed method will be evaluated using multilayer perceptrons (MLPs), ResNet-14, and Wide ResNet-28 architectures. Baseline comparisons will include Mean-field Variational Inference (MFVI), Monte Carlo Dropout (MCDropout), Variational Dropout, Rank-1 Bayesian Neural Networks, and last-layer Gaussian Process methods (SNGP, DUE). Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy, Expected Calibration Error (ECE), Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL), and out-of-distribution (OOD) detection performance (AUPRC, AUROC) using SVHN as the OOD dataset. Hyperparameters such as noise variances and prior standard deviations will be tuned on held-out validation sets. The robustness and scalability of the method will be assessed by varying the number of components in the rank-1 mixture energy models and by testing on both small and large network architectures.
3cb746ee9ab49920ead4bd832d94ca0bc1ee5d3b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel density uncertainty criterion that directly links predictive uncertainty to the empirical input density, a property not enforced by existing Bayesian deep learning or variational inference methods. The density uncertainty layer is a new, flexible building block for constructing uncertainty-aware neural networks, capable of providing reliable uncertainty estimates and robust OOD detection. The method enables efficient and scalable training via energy-based modeling at each layer, and demonstrates superior calibration and uncertainty estimation performance compared to state-of-the-art baselines. Additionally, the approach supports efficient low-rank approximations for large-scale architectures without sacrificing performance.

3cb8e96faba73efa027fa858e2a78cd1fc3c6e4d.title: Model-Based Offline Planning
3cb8e96faba73efa027fa858e2a78cd1fc3c6e4d.research_question: How can offline reinforcement learning be improved to generate performant, adaptable, and controllable policies for real-world systems using only logged data, without any direct interaction with the environment?
3cb8e96faba73efa027fa858e2a78cd1fc3c6e4d.hypothesis: A model-based offline planning approach that combines a learned world model, a behavior-cloned policy prior, and a fixed-horizon value function can generate policies from offline data that outperform the original behavior policy, offer improved data efficiency, and enable dynamic adaptation to new goals and constraints.
3cb8e96faba73efa027fa858e2a78cd1fc3c6e4d.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces a model-based offline planning algorithm (MBOP) that learns three key components from offline data: (1) an ensemble of neural network world models to predict environment dynamics and rewards, (2) a behavior-cloned policy network used as a prior for action sampling during planning, and (3) a fixed-horizon value function ensemble to estimate expected returns. At each decision step, Model-Predictive Control (MPC) is employed, using a particle-based trajectory optimizer that samples multiple action sequences, rolls them out in the learned model, and evaluates them using both predicted rewards and value function estimates. The optimizer leverages the behavior-cloned policy as a prior and maintains a trajectory buffer to amortize optimization over time. Trajectories are weighted by their exponentiated returns, and the resulting weighted average is used to select the next action. The approach supports dynamic conditioning on new reward functions or constraints at planning time, enabling zero-shot adaptation to novel objectives.
3cb8e96faba73efa027fa858e2a78cd1fc3c6e4d.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on standard offline RL benchmarks, including RL Unplugged (RLU) tasks (Cartpole, Quadruped, Walker) and D4RL tasks (HalfCheetah, Hopper, Walker2d, Adroit Door). Policies are trained solely from offline datasets and evaluated in the corresponding simulated environments. Baselines include behavior cloning (BC), MOPO, MBPO, and PDDM, with ablation studies performed to isolate the contributions of the policy prior and value function. Evaluation metrics include average episode return, constraint satisfaction (for constrained tasks), and adaptability to new goals. Experiments also assess data efficiency by varying dataset sizes and report results across multiple random seeds and episodes. Additional experiments demonstrate zero-shot adaptation to goal-conditioned and constrained tasks by modifying the planning objective at test time.
3cb8e96faba73efa027fa858e2a78cd1fc3c6e4d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach uniquely combines a behavior-cloned policy prior, a fixed-horizon value function, and a learned model for planning in the fully offline setting, enabling improved data efficiency and policy performance over prior model-based and model-free offline RL methods. The method supports dynamic, zero-shot adaptation to new goals and constraints without retraining, and demonstrates strong performance with limited data. Technical innovations include consistent ensemble sampling during rollouts, the use of a trajectory buffer for amortized optimization, and the integration of value function and policy priors in the planning loop. The approach is shown to outperform or match state-of-the-art baselines in several benchmark tasks and offers practical advantages in terms of controllability and explainability for real-world deployment.

3cbffab9d7981da6662d474aaa056dcbd3c1701e.title: Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
3cbffab9d7981da6662d474aaa056dcbd3c1701e.research_question: Can large language models demonstrate human-like analogical reasoning abilities across a range of zero-shot analogy tasks, and how does their performance compare to human participants in diverse analogical domains?
3cbffab9d7981da6662d474aaa056dcbd3c1701e.hypothesis: Large language models, when trained on sufficiently large and diverse corpora, will exhibit emergent analogical reasoning abilities that match or exceed human performance on a variety of zero-shot analogy tasks, including abstract, verbal, and story-based analogies.
3cbffab9d7981da6662d474aaa056dcbd3c1701e.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation will be conducted by administering a suite of analogical reasoning tasks to a state-of-the-art large language model (LLM), such as GPT-3 (text-davinci-003), and directly comparing its performance to that of human participants. The task suite will include: (1) a novel text-based matrix reasoning task (Digit Matrices) structurally modeled after Raven's Standard Progressive Matrices but using symbolic digit inputs; (2) a set of letter string analogy problems requiring identification and generalization of transformation rules; (3) four-term verbal analogy problems sourced from established human behavioral datasets; and (4) story analogy tasks probing sensitivity to higher-order relational structures. The LLM will be evaluated in a zero-shot setting, with minimal or no prompt engineering, and no in-context task examples. For each task, both generative (open-ended) and multiple-choice response formats will be used where appropriate, and qualitative analyses of error patterns and reasoning strategies will be performed.
3cbffab9d7981da6662d474aaa056dcbd3c1701e.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize several datasets: the custom-designed Digit Matrices for matrix reasoning, a novel letter string analogy set inspired by Hofstadter and Mitchell, four-term verbal analogy datasets (including the UCLA Verbal Analogy Test, Sternberg and Nigro, SAT analogies, and Jones et al.), and story analogy materials from Gentner et al. Human participant data will be collected from undergraduate students and, where available, from published behavioral studies. Baseline comparisons will include average human performance for each task and, where possible, performance distributions. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy (generative and multiple-choice), logistic regression analyses of performance across problem subtypes, and correlation analyses of error patterns between model and humans. The LLM's responses will be generated in a zero-shot manner, and contextual effects will be simulated by appending previous responses to the input context for sequential tasks.
3cbffab9d7981da6662d474aaa056dcbd3c1701e.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a direct, systematic comparison between large language models and human participants across a diverse set of analogical reasoning tasks, including a novel text-based matrix reasoning benchmark. The approach uniquely probes zero-shot analogical reasoning without task-specific training or fine-tuning, providing new insights into the emergent cognitive abilities of LLMs. The research claims to demonstrate that LLMs can acquire core analogical reasoning capabilities, including sensitivity to relational complexity and higher-order relations, rivaling or surpassing human performance in several domains.

3cebcaae3e3c20bbff0bd487488e0558d63c842b.title: From Tokens to Words: On the Inner Lexicon of LLMs
3cebcaae3e3c20bbff0bd487488e0558d63c842b.research_question: Do large language models (LLMs) internally encode word-level representations despite processing sub-word tokens, and how can this internal mechanism be leveraged to expand model vocabularies and optimize inference without finetuning?
3cebcaae3e3c20bbff0bd487488e0558d63c842b.hypothesis: LLMs possess an intrinsic detokenization process that fuses sub-word tokens into coherent word-level representations, forming a latent inner lexicon that can be accessed and manipulated to expand the model's vocabulary and reduce computational costs without degrading performance.
3cebcaae3e3c20bbff0bd487488e0558d63c842b.proposed_method: A comprehensive probing and intervention framework will be developed to analyze the internal representations of LLMs across layers, focusing on how sub-word token sequences are composed into word-level representations. The approach will utilize interpretability techniques such as logit lens and Patchscopes to decode hidden states and assess whether the last token of a word sequence encodes the full word identity. Experiments will include artificially splitting single-token words, introducing typos, and analyzing multi-token words to evaluate the robustness and coverage of the detokenization process. The role of feedforward networks (FFNs) and attention mechanisms in this process will be dissected through ablation studies and attention pattern analysis. Building on these insights, a practical method will be proposed to expand the LLM vocabulary by extracting detokenized representations for multi-token words, projecting them into embedding and unembedding spaces using learned linear maps, and refining these entries via a brief, parameter-frozen pretraining step.
3cebcaae3e3c20bbff0bd487488e0558d63c842b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several LLMs, including Llama2-7B, Llama3-8B, Mistral-7B, and Yi-6B, using datasets such as WIKITEXT-103, PUBMED abstracts, and the Arabic split of WIKI40B. A balanced dataset of real English words and artificially generated nonwords will be created, tokenized, and used to probe the model's ability to distinguish words from nonwords via k-nearest neighbors classifiers on hidden states. Retrieval rates of word identities from hidden states and FFN outputs will be measured layer-wise using logit lens and Patchscopes. Ablation studies will selectively remove FFN updates to assess their necessity in detokenization. Attention weights will be analyzed to track token aggregation dynamics. For vocabulary expansion, new embeddings for multi-token words will be constructed and evaluated in a next-word prediction setup, comparing token-level top-1 accuracy against baselines such as mean token embeddings and the original model. Reductions in token count and inference steps will also be quantified.
3cebcaae3e3c20bbff0bd487488e0558d63c842b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a detailed analysis of the internal detokenization process in LLMs, revealing the existence of a latent inner lexicon that extends beyond the tokenizer's vocabulary. It provides evidence that LLMs can reconstruct and utilize word-level representations for both in-vocabulary and out-of-vocabulary words, even under token splits and noise. The method enables practical, finetuning-free vocabulary expansion by leveraging these internal representations, reducing input length and inference iterations with minimal impact on accuracy. This approach offers a new avenue for optimizing tokenization and computational efficiency in LLMs, particularly for languages and domains with high token-per-word ratios.

3ced5335b973fa9d4e537376c02c2df22dd5631c.title: Improving Out-of-Distribution Robustness via Selective Augmentation
3ced5335b973fa9d4e537376c02c2df22dd5631c.research_question: How can machine learning models be made more robust to out-of-distribution scenarios, specifically under subpopulation shifts and domain shifts, without explicitly regularizing internal representations or predictors?
3ced5335b973fa9d4e537376c02c2df22dd5631c.hypothesis: Selective data augmentation that interpolates samples across domains or labels can lead to the learning of invariant predictors, thereby improving out-of-distribution robustness compared to existing regularization-based and augmentation-based methods.
3ced5335b973fa9d4e537376c02c2df22dd5631c.proposed_method: A novel framework, Learning Invariant Predictors with Selective Augmentation (LISA), is proposed to improve robustness under distribution shifts. The method employs a mixup-based data augmentation strategy, where pairs of training samples are linearly interpolated either across the same label but different domains (intra-label LISA) or within the same domain but different labels (intra-domain LISA). The interpolation ratio is sampled from a Beta distribution, and the choice between intra-label and intra-domain augmentation is controlled by a hyperparameter. This selective augmentation is designed to cancel out spurious correlations between domain and label, encouraging the model to learn domain-invariant predictors without explicit regularization. The approach can be adapted to different data modalities by applying mixup, CutMix, or ManifoldMixup as appropriate.
3ced5335b973fa9d4e537376c02c2df22dd5631c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on nine benchmark datasets covering both subpopulation shifts (e.g., Colored MNIST, Waterbirds, CelebA, CivilComments) and domain shifts (e.g., Camelyon17, FMoW, RxRx1, Amazon, MetaShift). Baseline methods for comparison include ERM, IRM, IB-IRM, V-REx, CORAL, GroupDRO, DomainMix, Fish, and upweighting strategies. Evaluation metrics include worst-group accuracy for subpopulation shifts and worst-domain or average accuracy for domain shifts. The same model architectures as prior work are used (e.g., ResNet-50, DenseNet-121, DistilBERT), and hyperparameters such as the strategy selection probability are tuned via cross-validation. Additional analyses include ablation studies on augmentation strategies, invariance metrics, and the effect of distribution shift magnitude.
3ced5335b973fa9d4e537376c02c2df22dd5631c.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple yet widely-applicable selective augmentation strategy that does not require explicit regularization of internal representations or predictors. LISA is claimed to consistently outperform state-of-the-art invariant learning and robust optimization methods across diverse datasets and modalities. Theoretical analysis is provided to show that LISA achieves smaller worst-group error than ERM and vanilla mixup under strong spurious correlations. The approach is also claimed to be the first to provide a theoretical framework for understanding how selective mixup strategies affect misclassification error in the context of distribution shifts.

3d0375bd2dd2ac88537ec63faad823707e6d5d46.title: InstructSAM: A Training-Free Framework for Instruction-Oriented Remote Sensing Object Recognition
3d0375bd2dd2ac88537ec63faad823707e6d5d46.research_question: How can remote sensing object recognition be performed in an instruction-oriented, open-vocabulary, open-ended, and open-subclass manner, without relying on task-specific training or confidence thresholds, while maintaining efficiency and adaptability to complex user instructions and diverse annotation rules?
3d0375bd2dd2ac88537ec63faad823707e6d5d46.hypothesis: A training-free framework that integrates large vision-language models for instruction interpretation and object counting, class-agnostic mask proposal, and a counting-constrained mask-label matching algorithm can achieve robust, scalable, and efficient instruction-driven object recognition in remote sensing imagery, matching or surpassing specialized baselines while maintaining near-constant inference time regardless of object count.
3d0375bd2dd2ac88537ec63faad823707e6d5d46.proposed_method: A novel, training-free framework named InstructSAM will be developed for instruction-driven remote sensing object recognition. The approach decomposes the task into three synergistic steps: (1) a large vision-language model (LVLM) interprets user-provided, structured natural language instructions to predict target object categories and their counts in the image; (2) SAM2 is used to generate high-quality, class-agnostic mask proposals via automated mask generation, including on image crops to improve recall for small objects; (3) a CLIP model, pre-trained or fine-tuned on remote sensing data, computes semantic similarity between mask proposals and category embeddings. The mask-label assignment is formulated as a binary integer programming (BIP) problem, where the objective is to maximize total semantic similarity subject to global counting constraints derived from the LVLM. This eliminates the need for confidence thresholds and enables efficient, instruction-oriented object recognition.
3d0375bd2dd2ac88537ec63faad823707e6d5d46.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the newly constructed EarthInstruct benchmark, which combines the NWPU-VHR-10 and DIOR remote sensing datasets, covering 20 categories with diverse annotation rules and spatial resolutions. The evaluation will span open-vocabulary, open-ended, and open-subclass scenarios for object counting, detection, and segmentation. Baseline comparisons will include both generic and remote sensing-specific vision-language models, such as GroundingDINO, OWLv2, Qwen2.5-VL, GSNet, SegEarth-OV, LAE-Label, SkySenseGPT, and others. Evaluation metrics will include mean F1-score, mean Average Precision without confidence (mAPnc), mean Intersection-over-Union (mIoU), and counting-specific metrics (precision, recall, F1) with semantic similarity matching for open-ended settings. Inference time and scalability will also be analyzed, and ablation studies will assess the impact of prompt design, model scaling, and mask-label matching strategies.
3d0375bd2dd2ac88537ec63faad823707e6d5d46.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a training-free, confidence-free paradigm for instruction-driven remote sensing object recognition, capable of handling open-vocabulary, open-ended, and open-subclass scenarios. It is the first to formulate mask-label assignment as a binary integer programming problem with global counting constraints, integrating outputs from LVLMs, SAM2, and remote sensing-specific CLIP models. The EarthInstruct benchmark is established as the first comprehensive testbed for instruction-oriented object counting, detection, and segmentation in earth observation. The method achieves near-constant inference time regardless of object count, reduces output tokens and runtime compared to direct generation approaches, and demonstrates superior or competitive performance against specialized baselines across multiple tasks.

3d28faf650805a7eecb0435658de6940b8288559.title: Complexity Matters: Dynamics of Feature Learning in the Presence of Spurious Correlations
3d28faf650805a7eecb0435658de6940b8288559.research_question: How does the relative complexity and correlation strength of spurious features, compared to core features, affect the dynamics of feature learning in neural networks, particularly in the presence of spurious correlations?
3d28faf650805a7eecb0435658de6940b8288559.hypothesis: Simpler spurious features and higher correlation strength will slow the learning of core features, lead to the formation of distinct subnetworks for core and spurious features, and result in the persistent retention of spurious features in network representations, even after core features are learned.
3d28faf650805a7eecb0435658de6940b8288559.proposed_method: A theoretical and empirical framework will be developed to investigate feature learning dynamics under spurious correlations using synthetic datasets based on Boolean function analysis. The datasets will allow precise control over the complexity and correlation strength of core and spurious features, with core and spurious features implemented as parity or staircase Boolean functions of varying degrees. Neural networks, specifically two-layer ReLU architectures, will be trained using stochastic gradient descent on these datasets. The learning process will be analyzed by tracking the evolution of weights, feature correlations, and the separation of subnetworks corresponding to core and spurious features. Theoretical analyses will be conducted to quantify the gradient dynamics and persistence of learned features, supported by empirical experiments.
3d28faf650805a7eecb0435658de6940b8288559.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic Boolean datasets where core and spurious features are defined by parity or staircase functions, with adjustable degrees to vary complexity. The confounder strength (correlation between spurious and core features) will be parameterized by a variable λ. Neural networks (primarily two-layer, width 100) will be trained with batch stochastic gradient descent and cross-entropy loss. Evaluation metrics will include core and spurious feature correlation (measured as the correlation between model output and feature functions), decoded correlation after last-layer retraining, convergence rates, and group accuracy. Baselines will include standard training, last-layer retraining, and popular debiasing algorithms such as Just Train Twice (JTT) and Spare. Additional experiments will be performed on semi-synthetic and real datasets (e.g., Waterbirds, Color-MNIST, Domino Image) to validate findings and compare learning dynamics.
3d28faf650805a7eecb0435658de6940b8288559.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a modular, theoretically-grounded synthetic dataset framework that enables fine-grained control over the complexity and correlation of spurious and core features, surpassing prior ad-hoc or limited-complexity datasets. The approach provides new insights into the learning dynamics of neural networks under spurious correlations, revealing that simpler spurious features can significantly impede core feature learning, that subnetworks specializing in core and spurious features emerge, and that spurious features are not forgotten even after core features are learned. The research also challenges key assumptions underlying popular debiasing algorithms and provides theoretical justification for the effectiveness of last-layer retraining. The framework is designed to be extensible and representative of real-world feature learning scenarios.

3d3a76a2fedccea741f34303b06358440dc2a212.title: DETRs with Collaborative Hybrid Assignments Training
3d3a76a2fedccea741f34303b06358440dc2a212.research_question: How can the training efficiency and feature discriminability of DETR-based object detectors be improved by leveraging diverse label assignment strategies, while maintaining end-to-end detection without additional inference overhead?
3d3a76a2fedccea741f34303b06358440dc2a212.hypothesis: Integrating collaborative hybrid assignments—specifically, combining one-to-one set matching with auxiliary one-to-many label assignment heads—will enhance the encoder's feature learning and the decoder's attention mechanisms, resulting in improved detection accuracy and training efficiency for DETR-based models.
3d3a76a2fedccea741f34303b06358440dc2a212.proposed_method: A collaborative hybrid assignments training scheme, termed Co-DETR, will be developed for DETR-based object detectors. The approach incorporates multiple auxiliary heads during training, each supervised by a different one-to-many label assignment strategy (such as ATSS, Faster RCNN, FCOS, or RetinaNet). The encoder's output is transformed into a multi-scale feature pyramid, which is then processed by these auxiliary heads to generate dense spatial supervisions. Additionally, customized positive queries are extracted from the positive coordinates identified by the auxiliary heads and injected into the decoder to increase the number of positive samples for attention learning. During inference, all auxiliary heads are discarded, ensuring no additional parameters or computational cost compared to the original detector, and no hand-crafted NMS is required.
3d3a76a2fedccea741f34303b06358440dc2a212.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard object detection benchmarks, including MS COCO 2017 and LVIS v1.0, with additional large-scale validation on Objects365. The method will be applied to several DETR variants, such as DAB-DETR, Deformable-DETR, and DINO-Deformable-DETR, using various backbones (e.g., ResNet-50, Swin-L, ViT-L). Baseline comparisons will include both traditional one-to-many detectors and state-of-the-art DETR variants. Evaluation metrics will focus on mean Average Precision (AP) at multiple IoU thresholds and object scales. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the number and type of auxiliary heads, the effect of customized positive queries, and optimization conflicts. Training and inference efficiency, memory usage, and convergence speed will also be measured.
3d3a76a2fedccea741f34303b06358440dc2a212.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a collaborative hybrid assignments training scheme that uniquely combines one-to-one and one-to-many label assignment paradigms within DETR-based detectors. This approach enriches encoder supervision and decoder positive samples without incurring inference overhead or requiring hand-crafted NMS. The method is plug-and-play, compatible with various DETR variants and backbones, and demonstrates significant improvements in detection accuracy, training efficiency, and model scalability. Quantitative and qualitative analyses are provided to elucidate the complementary benefits of hybrid assignments, and state-of-the-art results are achieved on COCO and LVIS with substantially fewer parameters than previous best models.

3d466cc61b248d1872539ed270fd112da2a4bd51.title: Predicting partially observable dynamical systems via diffusion models with a multiscale inference scheme
3d466cc61b248d1872539ed270fd112da2a4bd51.research_question: How can future states of partially observable, long-memory dynamical systems be accurately predicted in a probabilistic manner, especially when only limited and noisy observations are available, as in the case of solar dynamics?
3d466cc61b248d1872539ed270fd112da2a4bd51.hypothesis: A multiscale inference scheme for conditional diffusion models, which conditions on both fine-grained recent observations and coarser distant past information, will improve the accuracy, stability, and bias of probabilistic predictions for partially observable dynamical systems compared to standard autoregressive and existing hierarchical inference schemes.
3d466cc61b248d1872539ed270fd112da2a4bd51.proposed_method: A conditional diffusion model will be developed for probabilistic prediction of dynamical systems where only partial and noisy observations are available. The core innovation is a multiscale inference scheme that utilizes 'multiscale templates'—sets of time indices that are densely sampled near the present and increasingly coarsely sampled further in the past and future. At each inference step, the model generates multiple future timesteps in a single call by conditioning on both recent and distant observations, filling in the trajectory progressively by iterating over templates of varying scales and shifts. The denoising backbone will be based on a Vision Transformer architecture, adapted for spatiotemporal data, and trained to reconstruct clean data from noisy inputs with explicit conditioning masks. This approach is designed to capture long-range temporal dependencies without incurring prohibitive computational costs, and to mitigate error accumulation typical in autoregressive rollouts.
3d466cc61b248d1872539ed270fd112da2a4bd51.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic time-series data and a newly curated, large-scale solar dynamics dataset. The solar dataset consists of 8.5TB of multi-modal, high-resolution (512x512) videos of solar regions, with 12 channels including magnetic field and atmospheric observations, sampled hourly over 48-hour windows. Models will be trained and evaluated on downsampled versions for computational feasibility. Baselines will include standard autoregressive inference schemes, the 'Hierarchy-2' scheme, and existing spatiotemporal models such as AR-diff (for fluid dynamics) and AViT (deterministic transformer). Evaluation metrics will include Wasserstein distance between predicted and observed pixel distributions, mean absolute error in the isotropic power spectrum, and normalized mean absolute error for physics-based summary statistics (e.g., mean horizontal gradient of the total field). All metrics will be averaged across multiple realizations, time horizons (1-4, 4-16, 16-32 hours), and solar regions.
3d466cc61b248d1872539ed270fd112da2a4bd51.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel multiscale inference scheme for conditional diffusion models, specifically tailored to partially observable, long-memory physical systems. This method enables efficient conditioning on both recent and distant past observations, capturing long-range dependencies and reducing rollout instability and prediction bias. The approach is the first to train a multi-modal diffusion model for high-resolution solar video prediction, surpassing prior work that focused on single-modality or low-resolution data. Additionally, a new large-scale, multi-modal solar dynamics dataset is contributed to the community to facilitate further research in this area.

3d667922ad907cd88be6de92d13c308130105de4.title: Evaluating the Robustness of Interpretability Methods through Explanation Invariance and Equivariance
3d667922ad907cd88be6de92d13c308130105de4.research_question: How can the robustness of interpretability methods for neural networks be systematically evaluated and improved, particularly in the presence of model symmetries across diverse data modalities and symmetry groups?
3d667922ad907cd88be6de92d13c308130105de4.hypothesis: Interpretability methods that do not account for the symmetry invariance or equivariance properties of the underlying model may produce explanations that are inconsistent or non-robust, but robustness can be measured and improved by leveraging group-theoretic formalism and appropriate aggregation techniques.
3d667922ad907cd88be6de92d13c308130105de4.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed to evaluate the robustness of interpretability methods by formalizing the concepts of explanation invariance and equivariance with respect to a model's symmetry group using geometric deep learning and group theory. Two quantitative metrics, invariance and equivariance scores, will be defined to empirically assess how well explanations respect the symmetries of the model. Theoretical robustness guarantees for popular interpretability methods will be derived, identifying under what conditions these methods are robust. Furthermore, a systematic approach will be proposed to enforce invariance or equivariance in any interpretability method by aggregating explanations over the symmetry group, using either exact or Monte Carlo approximations depending on group size.
3d667922ad907cd88be6de92d13c308130105de4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of datasets spanning modalities such as time series (Electrocardiograms), graphs (Mutagenicity), 3D point clouds (ModelNet40), text (IMDb), and images (FashionMNIST, CIFAR100, STL10). For each dataset, models designed to be invariant under specific symmetry groups (e.g., cyclic translations, node or point permutations, dihedral group actions) will be trained. Multiple interpretability methods—including feature importance, example importance, and concept-based explanations—will be evaluated using the proposed invariance and equivariance metrics. Baselines will include both loss-based and representation-based explanation methods, and robustness will be compared across methods and model invariance levels. Monte Carlo sampling will be used to estimate metrics for large symmetry groups. The effect of enforcing invariance through aggregation and the impact of relaxing model invariance will also be systematically studied.
3d667922ad907cd88be6de92d13c308130105de4.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a rigorous, group-theoretic framework for evaluating and improving the robustness of interpretability methods with respect to model symmetries, applicable across multiple data modalities and symmetry groups. The approach formalizes explanation invariance and equivariance, provides new quantitative metrics for robustness, and supplies theoretical guarantees for commonly used interpretability methods. Additionally, a general method is proposed to enforce invariance or equivariance in any interpretability method by aggregating over group actions, leading to actionable guidelines for practitioners. This framework addresses gaps in prior work by extending robustness evaluation beyond feature importance and image data to broader interpretability methods and data types.

3d68522abfadfc8ee6b7ec9edaaf91f1b2f38e5e.title: Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context
3d68522abfadfc8ee6b7ec9edaaf91f1b2f38e5e.research_question: How does the presence of irrelevant context in problem descriptions affect the problem-solving accuracy of large language models, and what strategies can be developed to mitigate any negative effects?
3d68522abfadfc8ee6b7ec9edaaf91f1b2f38e5e.hypothesis: Large language models are highly sensitive to irrelevant information in input contexts, leading to significant decreases in problem-solving accuracy; however, their robustness can be improved through techniques such as self-consistency, explicit instructions, and exemplars that demonstrate how to ignore irrelevant context.
3d68522abfadfc8ee6b7ec9edaaf91f1b2f38e5e.proposed_method: A new benchmark, GSM-IC, will be constructed by augmenting grade-school arithmetic word problems (derived from GSM8K) with carefully controlled irrelevant sentences that do not affect the correct answer. The methodology will involve evaluating several state-of-the-art prompting techniques for large language models, including chain-of-thought (COT), zero-shot chain-of-thought (0-COT), least-to-most (LTM), and program-aided prompting, both with and without irrelevant context in the prompts. Additional strategies will be explored, such as self-consistency decoding (sampling multiple solutions and aggregating answers), adding explicit instructions to ignore irrelevant information, and including exemplars in the prompt that contain irrelevant context. The impact of various factors of the irrelevant context (topic relevance, role name overlap, and number range) will be systematically analyzed.
3d68522abfadfc8ee6b7ec9edaaf91f1b2f38e5e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using large language models such as code-davinci-002 and text-davinci-003. The primary dataset will be GSM-IC, a new benchmark of over 58,000 examples, with a 4,000-example subset (GSM-IC-4K) used for most evaluations. Baseline comparisons will include original GSM8K problems without irrelevant context. Evaluation metrics will include micro accuracy (average over all examples), macro accuracy (fraction of base problems consistently solved across all irrelevant variants), and normalized accuracy (relative to clean problem performance). Additional experiments will test the generalizability of mitigation strategies on other datasets, such as SVAMP and DROP, and will analyze the effects of prompt complexity, number of reasoning steps, and types of irrelevant context.
3d68522abfadfc8ee6b7ec9edaaf91f1b2f38e5e.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first comprehensive benchmark (GSM-IC) specifically designed to evaluate the distractibility of large language models by irrelevant context in arithmetic reasoning tasks. It systematically analyzes the sensitivity of multiple prompting techniques to irrelevant information and demonstrates that current state-of-the-art models are highly susceptible to such distractions. The proposal further claims that incorporating self-consistency, explicit instructions, and exemplars with irrelevant information can significantly improve robustness, providing actionable insights and new evaluation standards for future model development and assessment.

3d80d767a41e39c3c8bc81471bd0dbd9090ed877.title: SLCA: Slow Learner with Classifier Alignment for Continual Learning on a Pre-trained Model
3d80d767a41e39c3c8bc81471bd0dbd9090ed877.research_question: How can continual learning on pre-trained models be improved to effectively leverage pre-trained knowledge for each incremental task while maintaining generalizability and minimizing catastrophic forgetting, especially in both supervised and self-supervised pre-training scenarios across various downstream tasks?
3d80d767a41e39c3c8bc81471bd0dbd9090ed877.hypothesis: Selective reduction of the learning rate for the representation layer (slow learner) combined with post-hoc classifier alignment can mitigate progressive overfitting and sub-optimal classification, thereby significantly improving continual learning performance on pre-trained models compared to existing baselines.
3d80d767a41e39c3c8bc81471bd0dbd9090ed877.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that combines a slow learner strategy with classifier alignment for continual learning on pre-trained models. The approach involves selectively reducing the learning rate for the representation layer to prevent overfitting and maintain generalizability, while allowing a higher learning rate for the classification layer to adapt to new tasks. After each incremental task, class-wise feature statistics (mean and covariance) are collected, and a post-hoc classifier alignment step is performed by generating synthetic features from these statistics and retraining the classifier with logit normalization to prevent overconfidence. This alignment is performed using a modified cross-entropy loss with temperature scaling, ensuring balanced adaptation across all seen classes. The method is designed to be lightweight, scalable, and compatible with both supervised and self-supervised pre-training paradigms.
3d80d767a41e39c3c8bc81471bd0dbd9090ed877.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four standard continual learning benchmarks: Split CIFAR-100, Split ImageNet-R, Split CUB-200, and Split Cars-196, each split into 10 incremental tasks. Both supervised (ImageNet-21K) and self-supervised (MoCo v3, MAE, BEiT on ImageNet-1K) pre-training paradigms will be evaluated using a ViT-B/16 backbone for consistency. Baselines for comparison include regularization-based (EWC, LwF), replay-based (BiC, GDumb, DER++), and prompt-based (L2P, DualPrompt) methods, with all baselines re-implemented using the proposed slow learner for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics include Last-Acc (average accuracy after the final task) and Inc-Acc (average incremental accuracy after each task). Additional ablation studies will assess the impact of each component (slow learner, classifier alignment, logit normalization) and analyze scalability and memory efficiency.
3d80d767a41e39c3c8bc81471bd0dbd9090ed877.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a simple yet highly effective slow learner strategy that nearly eliminates progressive overfitting in the representation layer for continual learning on pre-trained models. The post-hoc classifier alignment method further addresses sub-optimal classification layers, especially in fine-grained tasks, and is combined with logit normalization to mitigate overconfidence. The approach is shown to outperform state-of-the-art prompt-based and replay-based methods, nearly closing the gap to joint training upper bounds across both supervised and self-supervised pre-training scenarios. The method is lightweight, scalable, and plug-and-play, providing a new strong baseline and critical insights for future research in continual learning with pre-trained models.

3dba4512bb7012201c07132b18d2cc22c482f667.title: Jailbreak Antidote: Runtime Safety-Utility Balance via Sparse Representation Adjustment in Large Language Models
3dba4512bb7012201c07132b18d2cc22c482f667.research_question: How can large language models be endowed with real-time, flexible control over the safety-utility trade-off during inference, enabling robust defense against jailbreak attacks without incurring computational overhead or degrading model utility?
3dba4512bb7012201c07132b18d2cc22c482f667.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that safety-related information in large language models is sparsely encoded within a small subset of internal neuron activations, and that targeted, sparse adjustments of these activations during inference can effectively enhance safety against jailbreak attacks while preserving model utility and incurring negligible computational overhead.
3dba4512bb7012201c07132b18d2cc22c482f667.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that enables runtime adjustment of safety preferences in large language models by manipulating a sparse subset of the model’s internal hidden states during inference. The method first identifies a 'safety direction' in the model’s representation space using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on hidden states derived from benign and harmful prompts, focusing on the last token position in selected layers. A mask is constructed to retain only the top k% of dimensions with the largest absolute values in the safety direction vector, leveraging the observed sparsity of safety-related representations. During inference, the hidden state of a new prompt is adjusted by adding the masked safety direction, scaled by a tunable factor α, thus enabling real-time control over the safety-utility balance. This adjustment is performed without modifying the input prompt or requiring model retraining, and the precomputed safety direction and mask ensure negligible computational overhead.
3dba4512bb7012201c07132b18d2cc22c482f667.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on nine large language models ranging from 2 billion to 72 billion parameters, including models such as Gemma-2-2B-it, Phi-3-mini-it, Qwen-1.5-7B-it, Qwen-2-7B-it, Llama-3-8B-it, Llama-3.1-8B-it, Gemma-2-9B-it, Llama-3-70B-it, and Qwen-2-72B-it. The evaluation uses JailbreakBench (100 harmful prompts) to assess safety and AlpacaEval to measure utility on benign tasks. The method is tested against ten jailbreak attack methods, including both common (e.g., BETTER DAN, AIM, DEV MODE variants) and advanced attacks (e.g., GCG, PAIR, random search, tense reformulations). Six baseline defense strategies are compared: In-Context Learning, Paraphrase and Perplexity Filter, Self-Reminder, SemanticSmoothLLM, and SmoothLLM. Evaluation metrics include Defense Success Rate (DSR) for safety and Win Rate on AlpacaEval for utility, with additional analysis of inference runtime per query to assess computational efficiency. Ablation studies are performed to analyze the impact of the scaling factor α and sparsity parameter k on the safety-utility trade-off.
3dba4512bb7012201c07132b18d2cc22c482f667.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a lightweight, scalable, and real-time mechanism for balancing safety and utility in large language models by directly manipulating a sparse subset of internal neuron activations during inference. It leverages the sparsity of safety-related representations, requiring adjustment of only about 5% of neurons to achieve performance comparable to full-state modification. Unlike existing defenses, the method does not require prompt modification, retraining, or additional tokens, and introduces negligible inference overhead. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate superior defense success rates and utility preservation compared to state-of-the-art baselines, establishing the method as a practical and adaptable solution for enhancing LLM safety in dynamic deployment scenarios.

3dd6e3dc2d7a8fa6aaa4671557e6a94e62aa1106.title: Discriminative Finetuning of Generative Large Language Models without Reward Models and Human Preference Data
3dd6e3dc2d7a8fa6aaa4671557e6a94e62aa1106.research_question: Can large language models be fine-tuned to achieve competitive or superior alignment and task performance without relying on human preference data or reward models, and how can discriminative learning paradigms be leveraged to improve upon standard supervised fine-tuning and preference optimization approaches?
3dd6e3dc2d7a8fa6aaa4671557e6a94e62aa1106.hypothesis: Discriminative fine-tuning of large language models, which explicitly models the likelihood of positive answers among all possible outputs and suppresses negative outputs using a discriminative probabilistic framework, will outperform standard supervised fine-tuning and achieve performance comparable to or better than preference optimization methods that require human preference data or reward models.
3dd6e3dc2d7a8fa6aaa4671557e6a94e62aa1106.proposed_method: A novel discriminative fine-tuning (DFT) framework is proposed for large language models, replacing the conventional generative objective with a discriminative probabilistic objective. The method introduces a scoring function based on the generative log-likelihood of output sequences, and models the conditional probability of an answer among all possible outputs using a softmax over these scores. The optimization objective maximizes the discriminative log-likelihood of observed data, increasing the score of correct outputs while suppressing the scores of other possible (potentially negative) outputs. Efficient optimization algorithms are developed, including the use of moving-average estimators and advanced sampling techniques to handle the intractable sum over all possible outputs. An approximation variant (DFT2) is also introduced, which uses a pool of outputs generated by the base model to further reduce computational costs.
3dd6e3dc2d7a8fa6aaa4671557e6a94e62aa1106.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted in two main settings: (1) fine-tuning for mathematical reasoning using the MetaMathQA dataset and evaluating on GSM8K and MATH benchmarks, and (2) general instruction-following and language understanding using the UltraFeedback dataset for training and evaluating on seven Huggingface Open Leaderboard benchmarks (MMLU, TruthfulQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, GSM8K, ARC, IFEval), as well as AlpacaEval2 with GPT-4 as a judge. Baselines include standard supervised fine-tuning (SFT), various preference optimization (PO) methods (such as DPO, SimPO, KTO, ORPO, and others), and self-play methods (e.g., SPIN, SimPO-SFT). Evaluation metrics include zero-shot test accuracy, prompt-level strict accuracy, and length-controlled win rates. The experimental setup ensures fair comparisons by using the same base model and generated negative examples across methods, and ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of algorithmic choices and hyperparameters.
3dd6e3dc2d7a8fa6aaa4671557e6a94e62aa1106.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a discriminative probabilistic framework for fine-tuning large language models without the need for human preference data or reward models, marking a shift from token-level generative objectives to data-level discriminative objectives. Efficient and scalable optimization algorithms are developed to handle the challenges of the discriminative objective, including advanced sampling and moving-average estimation techniques. The method demonstrates, through extensive experiments, that it can outperform standard supervised fine-tuning and match or exceed the performance of state-of-the-art preference optimization methods, all while eliminating the resource-intensive requirement for explicit preference data or reward modeling.

3def68bd0f856886d34272840a7f81588f2bc082.title: Survey of Hallucination in Natural Language Generation
3def68bd0f856886d34272840a7f81588f2bc082.research_question: What are the causes, definitions, evaluation metrics, and mitigation strategies for hallucination in natural language generation across various tasks, and how can a unified understanding be developed to address hallucination in NLG systems?
3def68bd0f856886d34272840a7f81588f2bc082.proposed_method: A comprehensive research framework will be developed to systematically investigate hallucination in natural language generation (NLG). This will involve (1) defining and categorizing hallucination phenomena (e.g., intrinsic vs. extrinsic) across NLG tasks such as summarization, dialogue, question answering, data-to-text, machine translation, and vision-language generation; (2) analyzing contributors to hallucination from both data (e.g., source-reference divergence, dataset artifacts) and model training/inference (e.g., exposure bias, parametric knowledge bias, decoding strategies); (3) evaluating and benchmarking existing and novel metrics for hallucination detection, including statistical, model-based (IE, QA, NLI), and human evaluation approaches; and (4) proposing and testing mitigation strategies at both data and model levels. The approach will emphasize cross-task analysis and the development of generalizable insights and tools.
3def68bd0f856886d34272840a7f81588f2bc082.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of benchmark datasets representative of major NLG tasks, such as CNN/DailyMail for summarization, WIKIBIO for data-to-text, MultiWOZ for dialogue, and WMT for machine translation. Baseline systems will include state-of-the-art Transformer-based models (e.g., BART, GPT-3, T5) and existing hallucination detection/mitigation methods. Evaluation will use both traditional metrics (ROUGE, BLEU) and advanced hallucination-specific metrics (PARENT, Knowledge F1, NLI-based entailment scores), as well as human annotation for faithfulness and factuality. Experimental setups will include ablation studies to isolate the effects of data artifacts, decoding strategies, and mitigation interventions.
3def68bd0f856886d34272840a7f81588f2bc082.novelty_claims: The proposed research offers a unified, cross-task perspective on hallucination in NLG, integrating definitions, causes, evaluation metrics, and mitigation strategies. It aims to bridge gaps between task-specific studies and provide a comprehensive taxonomy and benchmarking methodology for hallucination. The work will facilitate the development of more robust, faithful NLG systems and inform future research directions by identifying commonalities and differences in hallucination phenomena across tasks.

3df16d5c56bbb4939935351090479b3c0a65e4af.title: CycleNet: Enhancing Time Series Forecasting through Modeling Periodic Patterns
3df16d5c56bbb4939935351090479b3c0a65e4af.research_question: How can explicit modeling of periodic patterns in time series data improve the accuracy and efficiency of long-term time series forecasting across diverse domains?
3df16d5c56bbb4939935351090479b3c0a65e4af.hypothesis: Explicitly modeling inherent periodic patterns in time series data using learnable recurrent cycles, followed by residual forecasting, will significantly enhance long-term forecasting accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods, particularly in datasets with strong periodicity.
3df16d5c56bbb4939935351090479b3c0a65e4af.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that introduces the Residual Cycle Forecasting (RCF) technique. RCF utilizes learnable recurrent cycles to explicitly model the global periodic patterns present in each channel of the time series data. The method involves two main steps: (1) learning and aligning recurrent cycles of a specified length (W), which are shared across channels and trained via gradient descent, to capture the dominant periodicity; and (2) predicting the residuals after removing the learned cyclic components from the input, using a lightweight backbone such as a single-layer Linear or a dual-layer MLP model. The final forecast is obtained by adding the predicted residuals back to the cyclic components. An optional instance normalization step is incorporated to mitigate the effects of distributional shifts. The approach is designed to be plug-and-play, allowing integration with other backbone architectures.
3df16d5c56bbb4939935351090479b3c0a65e4af.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on widely-used multivariate time series forecasting benchmarks, including the ETT series (ETTh1, ETTh2, ETTm1, ETTm2), Electricity, Solar-Energy, Traffic, and Weather datasets. Each dataset exhibits stable cyclic patterns (e.g., daily or weekly), and cycle lengths will be set according to domain knowledge and confirmed via autocorrelation analysis. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as iTransformer, PatchTST, Crossformer, TiDE, TimesNet, DLinear, SCINet, FEDformer, and Autoformer. Evaluation metrics will include Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). Experiments will be implemented in PyTorch and run on a single NVIDIA RTX4090 GPU. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the RCF module, backbone choice, and cycle length parameter W, and efficiency analyses will compare parameter count, MACs, and training time.
3df16d5c56bbb4939935351090479b3c0a65e4af.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first explicit modeling of global periodic patterns in time series forecasting via learnable recurrent cycles, rather than relying on implicit extraction through deep or complex models.
