The RCF technique offers a conceptually simple, computationally efficient, and highly effective decomposition method that outperforms classical seasonal-trend decomposition approaches. The resulting CycleNet framework achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with significantly reduced parameter and computational requirements, and the RCF module is demonstrated to be a flexible, plug-and-play enhancement for existing forecasting models.

3e0972abc9939f69aa838d76fd5ce9ea3e7b2542.title: Self-Boost via Optimal Retraining: An Analysis via Approximate Message Passing
3e0972abc9939f69aa838d76fd5ce9ea3e7b2542.research_question: How can model retraining procedures optimally combine a model's own predictions with noisy observed labels to improve binary classification performance, particularly under different data generation models and high label noise conditions?
3e0972abc9939f69aa838d76fd5ce9ea3e7b2542.hypothesis: Optimal aggregation of model predictions and noisy labels, guided by a principled, theoretically derived function, will outperform heuristic retraining schemes in reducing prediction error, especially in high label noise scenarios.
3e0972abc9939f69aa838d76fd5ce9ea3e7b2542.proposed_method: A principled iterative retraining framework is developed, grounded in Approximate Message Passing (AMP), for binary classification tasks under both Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) and Generalized Linear Model (GLM) data generation settings. At each retraining iteration, the method computes soft predictions from the current model and combines them with the observed noisy labels using a Bayes-optimal aggregator function, which is analytically derived to minimize prediction error. The AMP-inspired update rules incorporate Onsager correction terms to debias the iterative process and ensure accurate asymptotic characterization. For practical deployment, the optimal aggregator is adapted for linear probing with cross-entropy loss by fitting a bimodal GMM to the distribution of model logits, enabling a closed-form computation of the retraining targets. The framework also provides a state evolution analysis that precisely tracks the evolution of model accuracy across retraining rounds.
3e0972abc9939f69aa838d76fd5ce9ea3e7b2542.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using linear probing on a ResNet-50 model pretrained on ImageNet, with retraining performed on two binary classification datasets: MedMNIST Pneumonia (medical imaging) and Food 101 (pho vs. ramen). The label noise model involves random label flipping with probability p, focusing on a high noise regime (p = 0.45). The proposed BayesMix RT method is compared against full retraining and consensus-based retraining baselines, with all methods run for 10 iterations and results averaged over 3 runs. Evaluation metrics include average test accuracy after 1 and 10 retraining iterations, and ablation studies are performed to assess robustness across different noise levels.
3e0972abc9939f69aa838d76fd5ce9ea3e7b2542.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first principled derivation of the Bayes-optimal aggregator function for combining model predictions and noisy labels in iterative retraining, under both GMM and GLM data models. The approach leverages AMP theory to provide exact asymptotic analysis and state evolution characterization of retraining dynamics. A practical adaptation for linear probing with cross-entropy loss is developed, enabling direct application to modern deep learning pipelines. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms existing heuristic retraining schemes, especially in high label noise settings.

3e1cb24198b715eb1d942df92d67d759e4591bd2.title: SQ Lower Bounds for Non-Gaussian Component Analysis with Weaker Assumptions
3e1cb24198b715eb1d942df92d67d759e4591bd2.research_question: What are the fundamental statistical query (SQ) complexity lower bounds for Non-Gaussian Component Analysis (NGCA) under weaker assumptions, specifically when only moment-matching conditions are imposed on the non-Gaussian distribution, and how do these bounds generalize to related statistical estimation and hypothesis testing tasks?
3e1cb24198b715eb1d942df92d67d759e4591bd2.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that near-optimal SQ lower bounds for NGCA can be established under the moment-matching condition alone, without requiring the previously assumed finite chi-squared distance between the non-Gaussian and Gaussian distributions.
3e1cb24198b715eb1d942df92d67d759e4591bd2.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops a rigorous framework for proving SQ lower bounds for NGCA by leveraging only the moment-matching condition on the non-Gaussian distribution. The methodology employs Fourier analysis, specifically Hermite polynomial decompositions, to analyze the behavior of bounded query functions under both the standard Gaussian and the hidden-subspace distributions. The analysis involves truncating the non-Gaussian distribution to control higher moments and bounding the difference in expectations of query functions under the two hypotheses. High-probability bounds are established for the difference in query responses using probabilistic arguments over random subspaces, and technical challenges related to infinite moments and interchange of summations are addressed via truncation and decomposition into low- and high-degree components.
3e1cb24198b715eb1d942df92d67d759e4591bd2.experiment_details: Theoretical results are validated through applications to several concrete statistical tasks, including list-decodable Gaussian mean estimation, anti-concentration detection, and learning periodic functions. For each application, the lower bounds are instantiated using specific constructions of moment-matching distributions and the corresponding hypothesis testing problems. The bounds are compared to existing results, particularly highlighting cases where previous SQ lower bounds become vacuous due to large or infinite chi-squared distances. The evaluation focuses on the accuracy and query complexity required by any SQ algorithm to succeed with high probability, and the results are parameterized by problem dimension, moment degree, and corruption or anti-concentration levels.
3e1cb24198b715eb1d942df92d67d759e4591bd2.novelty_claims: The proposed research establishes, for the first time, near-optimal SQ lower bounds for NGCA under the sole assumption of moment-matching, removing the technical requirement of finite chi-squared distance. This generalization enables the derivation of meaningful hardness results for a broader class of distributions, including discrete and heavy-tailed cases where previous techniques fail. The framework also yields sharper and non-vacuous SQ lower bounds for several related estimation and testing problems, demonstrating separations between SQ algorithms and other algorithmic paradigms (e.g., lattice-based methods). The technical innovations include new probabilistic and Fourier-analytic tools for handling unbounded chi-squared norms in the SQ model.

3e30a7ac4886b28eb50151f58e14a1d698cccd0e.title: Baseline Defenses for Adversarial Attacks Against Aligned Language Models
3e30a7ac4886b28eb50151f58e14a1d698cccd0e.research_question: How effective are standard baseline defense techniques from adversarial machine learning at mitigating algorithmically-crafted adversarial attacks (jailbreaking) against aligned large language models (LLMs), and how do robustness-performance trade-offs and threat models in the LLM domain differ from those in computer vision?
3e30a7ac4886b28eb50151f58e14a1d698cccd0e.hypothesis: Baseline defense strategies, such as perplexity-based detection, input paraphrasing, retokenization, and adversarial training, can provide meaningful robustness against adversarial attacks on LLMs, but their effectiveness and trade-offs will differ from those observed in computer vision due to the discrete and costly nature of text optimization.
3e30a7ac4886b28eb50151f58e14a1d698cccd0e.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation of three categories of baseline defenses against adversarial attacks on LLMs is proposed. First, detection defenses will be implemented using perplexity-based filters, including both global and windowed perplexity thresholds, to identify suspicious input prompts. Second, input preprocessing defenses will be explored through paraphrasing (using a generative LLM such as ChatGPT to rewrite the prompt) and retokenization (using BPE-dropout to randomly split tokens and disrupt adversarial triggers). Third, adversarial training will be conducted by injecting human-crafted adversarial prompts into the instruction fine-tuning process of LLMs, mixing these with benign prompts at various sampling rates. For each defense, both white-box and gray-box threat models will be considered, and adaptive attacks will be developed to probe the limits of each defense.
3e30a7ac4886b28eb50151f58e14a1d698cccd0e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using leading open-source LLMs, including Vicuna-7B, Guanaco-7B, Falcon-7B-Instruct, ChatGLM-6B, MPT-7B-Chat, and Alpaca-7B. The primary adversarial attack will be based on the greedy coordinate gradient optimizer (GCG) from Zou et al. (2023), which generates adversarial suffixes to bypass alignment. Evaluation metrics will include Attack Success Rate (ASR), false positive rates on benign prompts (using AlpacaEval and AdvBench datasets), and win rates on generation quality. Baseline defenses will be evaluated against both standard and adaptive attacks, with ablations on filter thresholds, paraphrasing parameters, BPE-dropout rates, and adversarial training mixing ratios. Both white-box (attacker knows defense details) and gray-box (attacker does not know defense details) scenarios will be tested.
3e30a7ac4886b28eb50151f58e14a1d698cccd0e.novelty_claims: This proposal aims to systematically benchmark and analyze the transferability and effectiveness of classical adversarial defense strategies in the context of LLMs, a domain with fundamentally different threat models and optimization challenges compared to computer vision. The work will provide the first comprehensive, comparative study of perplexity-based detection, paraphrasing, retokenization, and adversarial training as defenses against algorithmically-crafted jailbreaking attacks on aligned LLMs. It will also highlight the unique robustness-performance trade-offs and limitations of these defenses in the discrete, high-cost optimization landscape of text, and identify open challenges and directions for future research in LLM security.

3e3d89f2349e0bce3772579e91f033be1ecacdfe.title: ROS: A GNN-based Relax-Optimize-and-Sample Framework for Max-k-Cut Problems
3e3d89f2349e0bce3772579e91f033be1ecacdfe.research_question: How can large-scale Max-k-Cut problems with arbitrary edge weights be efficiently solved, while ensuring high solution quality, scalability, and generalization to both in-distribution and out-of-distribution graph instances?
3e3d89f2349e0bce3772579e91f033be1ecacdfe.hypothesis: A graph neural network-based Relax-Optimize-and-Sample (ROS) framework, which relaxes the Max-k-Cut problem to a continuous domain, optimizes it using pre-trained and fine-tuned GNNs, and then maps the solution back to the discrete domain via a theoretically grounded sampling procedure, will achieve superior scalability, efficiency, and solution quality compared to existing state-of-the-art algorithms.
3e3d89f2349e0bce3772579e91f033be1ecacdfe.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces a three-stage Relax-Optimize-and-Sample (ROS) framework for the Max-k-Cut problem. First, the discrete constraints of the Max-k-Cut problem are relaxed to a continuous probability simplex, transforming the problem into a continuous optimization task. A graph neural network (GNN) is then parameterized and trained in an unsupervised manner to optimize this relaxed problem, employing a 'pre-train + fine-tune' strategy: the GNN is pre-trained on a curated set of graphs to capture general graph structure, and subsequently fine-tuned on each specific test instance for rapid adaptation. After obtaining a high-quality continuous solution, a random sampling algorithm is applied to map the solution back to the discrete domain, with theoretical guarantees that the expected objective value is preserved. The framework integrates geometric landscape analysis and statistical theory to ensure consistency between the continuous and discrete solutions.
3e3d89f2349e0bce3772579e91f033be1ecacdfe.experiment_details: Experiments are designed to evaluate the proposed ROS framework on a variety of datasets, including random regular graphs, the Gset benchmark (with both unweighted and weighted variants), and real-world networks such as COLOR and Bitcoin-OTC. The training set consists of hundreds of regular graphs, while testing covers a broad range of graph sizes (up to 20,000 nodes) and types. Baselines include traditional algorithms (e.g., Goemans-Williamson, BQP, genetic algorithms, mirror descent, evolutionary heuristics) and learning-based methods (e.g., PI-GNN, ECO-DQN, ANYCSP). Evaluation metrics focus on solution quality (cut value) and computational time, with additional analysis on the impact of the pre-training stage and generalization to out-of-distribution instances. All experiments are conducted on GPU hardware, and the random sampling step is repeated multiple times to select the best solution.
3e3d89f2349e0bce3772579e91f033be1ecacdfe.novelty_claims: The framework introduces a scalable, learning-based approach for Max-k-Cut with arbitrary edge weights, leveraging GNNs and transfer learning to achieve rapid optimization. A novel random sampling algorithm is developed with theoretical guarantees on objective value consistency between relaxed and discrete solutions. The approach demonstrates superior scalability (solving instances with up to 20,000 nodes in seconds), outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both efficiency and solution quality, and exhibits strong generalization across diverse graph types and distributions. Theoretical contributions include rigorous analysis of the relaxation and sampling steps, ensuring the validity of the continuous-to-discrete mapping.

3e6f55f2717d0a0886179ca8172f67d426f6347d.title: FARE: Provably Fair Representation Learning with Practical Certificates
3e6f55f2717d0a0886179ca8172f67d426f6347d.research_question: How can fair representation learning methods be developed to provide practical, provable upper bounds on the unfairness of any downstream classifier trained on preprocessed data, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements and offering concrete fairness guarantees in real-world scenarios?
3e6f55f2717d0a0886179ca8172f67d426f6347d.hypothesis: Restricting the representation space of the encoder to a finite set enables the derivation of practical, high-confidence statistical certificates that tightly upper-bound the unfairness of any downstream classifier, while still maintaining favorable accuracy-fairness tradeoffs.
3e6f55f2717d0a0886179ca8172f67d426f6347d.proposed_method: A novel fair representation learning framework, FARE (Fairness with Restricted Encoders), will be developed. The approach involves designing a restricted encoder that maps input data to a finite set of representations, specifically instantiated using fair decision trees. The encoder partitions the input space into k cells, mapping all samples in a cell to the same representation. A statistical procedure will be constructed to empirically estimate the distribution of sensitive groups in each cell and compute high-confidence upper bounds on group membership probabilities. These estimates will be used to derive a finite-sample, high-probability upper bound (certificate) on the demographic parity distance of any downstream classifier trained on the representations. The method will be model- and distribution-agnostic, requiring no assumptions about the downstream classifier family or the underlying data distribution.
3e6f55f2717d0a0886179ca8172f67d426f6347d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several real-world fairness datasets, including Health, ACSIncome-CA, and ACSIncome-US. The proposed method will be compared to a range of existing fair representation learning baselines such as LAFTR, CVIB, FCRL, FNF, sIPM, and FairPath. Evaluation will focus on the tradeoff between prediction accuracy and demographic parity distance, with both empirical results and provable fairness certificates reported. Downstream classifiers (e.g., neural networks) will be trained on the learned representations, and the tightness and practicality of the computed certificates will be assessed. Additional studies will investigate the impact of dataset size, robustness to distribution shifts, sensitive attribute imbalance, and transfer learning across tasks.
3e6f55f2717d0a0886179ca8172f67d426f6347d.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first fair representation learning approach to provide practical, finite-sample, high-confidence certificates that upper-bound the unfairness of any downstream classifier, without restrictive assumptions on the data distribution or classifier family. The use of restricted encoders, particularly fair decision trees, enables efficient computation of these certificates while maintaining competitive accuracy-fairness tradeoffs. The statistical certification procedure is general and can be applied to any restricted encoder, representing a significant advancement over prior work that lacked practical or model-agnostic guarantees. The method also offers interpretability and efficiency advantages, and demonstrates robustness across various experimental settings.

3e8a7b2bd31b2e77565ecc58394889c51a0016d3.title: DISCO: learning to DISCover an evolution Operator for multi-physics-agnostic prediction
3e8a7b2bd31b2e77565ecc58394889c51a0016d3.research_question: How can the next state of a dynamical system governed by unknown and potentially varying partial differential equations (PDEs) be accurately predicted using only a short trajectory of observed states, in a manner that is agnostic to the underlying physics and scalable to high-dimensional, multi-physics scenarios?
3e8a7b2bd31b2e77565ecc58394889c51a0016d3.hypothesis: A model that decouples the estimation of governing dynamics from state prediction—by using a transformer-based hypernetwork to infer the parameters of a compact, translation-equivariant neural operator—will achieve more efficient, generalizable, and accurate multi-physics-agnostic prediction than existing transformer or meta-learning approaches, especially when pretrained on diverse physics datasets.
3e8a7b2bd31b2e77565ecc58394889c51a0016d3.proposed_method: A novel framework, DISCO, is proposed that leverages a large transformer-based hypernetwork to process a short trajectory of observed states and generate the parameters of a much smaller neural operator network. The hypernetwork encodes the context (sequence of prior states) and outputs the weights for the operator network, which is implemented as a U-Net architecture designed to preserve spatial translation equivariance and continuous-time dynamics. The operator network is then used to predict the next state through time integration, employing a third-order adaptive Runge-Kutta solver and adjoint sensitivity for efficient backpropagation. The method is trained end-to-end, with the hypernetwork learning to infer operator parameters that capture the essential dynamics of each context, thus decoupling the tasks of dynamics estimation and state evolution. The approach avoids the need for auto-encoding or explicit reconstruction, focusing instead on direct prediction in sample space, and is designed to scale across 1D, 2D, and 3D PDEs with varying boundary and initial conditions.
3e8a7b2bd31b2e77565ecc58394889c51a0016d3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two comprehensive collections of physics datasets: PDEBench and The Well, encompassing a wide range of PDEs (e.g., Burgers, Shallow Water, Diffusion-Reaction, Navier-Stokes, MHD, Supernova Explosion) across 1D, 2D, and 3D spatial domains, with spatial resolutions up to 1024 for 1D, 512x512 for 2D, and 64x64x64 for 3D. The proposed method will be pretrained on these diverse datasets and evaluated on next-step and multi-step rollout prediction tasks. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art transformer models (e.g., MPP), meta-learning frameworks (e.g., GEPS), operator learning models (e.g., FNO, U-Net), and hierarchical vision transformers (e.g., Poseidon). Evaluation metrics will primarily be normalized root mean square error (NRMSE) for next-step and rollout predictions. Experiments will assess training efficiency (epochs to convergence), generalization to unseen PDEs and initial conditions, and fine-tuning performance on downstream tasks.
3e8a7b2bd31b2e77565ecc58394889c51a0016d3.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to combine a transformer hypernetwork with a neural PDE solver for spatiotemporal prediction, enabling multi-physics-agnostic prediction with a tailored inductive bias for physical systems. The framework decouples context-driven dynamics estimation from state evolution, providing improved interpretability and alignment with classical numerical methods. It achieves state-of-the-art performance on next-step prediction across multiple physical systems with significantly fewer training epochs than baseline models, demonstrates superior numerical accuracy on multi-step rollouts, and is the first to scale to such a diverse range of PDEs in 1D, 2D, and 3D at high spatial resolutions. The approach also introduces an information bottleneck via a compact operator network, reducing overfitting and enhancing generalization to new physics and initial conditions.

3e91fd5c878b59eafea9c537f641ca045481a8f4.title: Active Exploration for Inverse Reinforcement Learning
3e91fd5c878b59eafea9c537f641ca045481a8f4.research_question: How can an agent efficiently infer an expert's reward function in inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) settings where both the environment's transition dynamics and the expert's policy are unknown, and only sequential interaction with the environment is possible?
3e91fd5c878b59eafea9c537f641ca045481a8f4.hypothesis: Active exploration strategies that leverage uncertainty estimates over both the environment's dynamics and the expert's policy can significantly reduce the sample complexity required to recover a reward function consistent with expert demonstrations, even without access to a generative model.
3e91fd5c878b59eafea9c537f641ca045481a8f4.proposed_method: A novel algorithm, Active exploration for Inverse Reinforcement Learning (AceIRL), is proposed for IRL in environments with unknown transition dynamics and expert policies. AceIRL iteratively constructs confidence intervals over plausible reward functions using observed transitions and expert actions, and then derives exploration policies that target the most informative regions of the environment. The method maintains and updates estimates of the transition model and expert policy, computes uncertainty bounds on the reward function, and solves a convex optimization problem at each iteration to select exploration policies that minimize future uncertainty about plausibly optimal policies. Two exploration strategies are considered: a greedy approach that targets current uncertainty, and a problem-dependent approach that anticipates uncertainty reduction in future iterations. The algorithm stops when the uncertainty about the optimal policy's value is below a specified threshold, ensuring PAC-style optimality guarantees.
3e91fd5c878b59eafea9c537f641ca045481a8f4.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted in simulated environments, including custom environments such as Four Paths and Double Chain, as well as standard benchmarks like RandomMDPs, Chain, and Gridworld. The evaluation metric is normalized regret, measuring the performance gap between the inferred policy and the true expert policy. AceIRL and its greedy variant are compared against baselines including uniformly random exploration, uniform sampling with a generative model, and the TRAVEL algorithm (which assumes a generative model). Sample complexity is measured as the number of samples required to achieve a normalized regret below a fixed threshold, with results averaged over 50 random seeds. The impact of the number of exploration episodes per iteration is also analyzed, and learning curves are provided for all environments.
3e91fd5c878b59eafea9c537f641ca045481a8f4.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to provide sample complexity guarantees for active IRL without requiring access to a generative model of the environment. AceIRL matches the worst-case sample complexity of active IRL methods that assume a generative model, and further introduces a problem-dependent sample complexity bound related to the suboptimality gap of the IRL problem. The method does not require a Bayesian prior over reward functions and achieves significant empirical improvements in sample efficiency over naive exploration strategies. The algorithm also introduces a new framework for combining uncertainty over both transition dynamics and expert policy to guide exploration in IRL.

3eb08f9a99eb851347a7ef8f4288d55497f0ed94.title: Constrained optimization of rank-one functions with indicator variables
3eb08f9a99eb851347a7ef8f4288d55497f0ed94.research_question: How can constrained optimization problems involving rank-one convex functions with indicator variables, subject to sign and combinatorial constraints, be reformulated to obtain strong convex hull characterizations and compact extended formulations?
3eb08f9a99eb851347a7ef8f4288d55497f0ed94.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by exploiting the conic structure induced by perspective functions, it is possible to derive compact and general extended formulations for the convex hulls of mixed-binary sets arising in rank-one convex optimization problems with indicator variables, sign restrictions, and combinatorial constraints.
3eb08f9a99eb851347a7ef8f4288d55497f0ed94.proposed_method: The proposed approach will develop a constructive methodology that leverages the hidden conic structure of perspective functions to reformulate mixed-binary convex optimization problems. Specifically, the method will analyze the epigraphs of perspective functions, establish their conic representations, and use these to characterize the convex hulls of sets involving both continuous and binary variables with complementarity constraints. The approach will generalize to both separable and non-separable (rank-one) convex functions, allowing for arbitrary sign restrictions on continuous variables and combinatorial constraints on indicator variables. The methodology will systematically reduce complex complementarity constraints to simpler forms in an extended (lifted) variable space, enabling the derivation of compact extended formulations that are amenable to standard optimization solvers.
3eb08f9a99eb851347a7ef8f4288d55497f0ed94.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on sparse nonnegative logistic regression problems with hierarchy constraints to evaluate the proposed formulations. The experimental setup will include comparisons against existing big-M and perspective-based relaxations, using standard datasets relevant to sparse regression and classification. Evaluation metrics will include the quality of continuous relaxation bounds, computational efficiency (e.g., branch-and-bound performance), and solution quality. The impact of the new formulations on solver performance and the tightness of relaxations will be systematically assessed.
3eb08f9a99eb851347a7ef8f4288d55497f0ed94.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified conic programming-based framework that simultaneously addresses sign restrictions on continuous variables and combinatorial constraints on binary variables in rank-one convex optimization problems. It provides the first compact extended formulations for the convex hulls of such problems under general settings, reducing the complexity of existing approaches and enabling direct implementation within standard integer programming solvers. The approach generalizes and extends prior results that handled these constraints separately, and offers new theoretical insights and practical tools for mixed-integer nonlinear optimization with indicator variables.

3ebdd3db0dd91069fa0cd31cbf8308b60b1b565e.title: Planning with Diffusion for Flexible Behavior Synthesis
3ebdd3db0dd91069fa0cd31cbf8308b60b1b565e.research_question: How can planning and trajectory optimization in reinforcement learning be improved by integrating the modeling and planning processes, particularly to enable flexible, long-horizon, and compositional behavior synthesis in control tasks?
3ebdd3db0dd91069fa0cd31cbf8308b60b1b565e.hypothesis: Integrating trajectory optimization directly into the generative modeling process using a diffusion probabilistic model will yield more effective, flexible, and scalable planning capabilities than traditional approaches that separate model learning from planning, especially in long-horizon and sparse-reward settings.
3ebdd3db0dd91069fa0cd31cbf8308b60b1b565e.proposed_method: A novel trajectory-level denoising diffusion probabilistic model, termed Diffuser, will be developed to generate entire sequences of state-action pairs concurrently rather than autoregressively. The model will be trained to iteratively denoise noisy trajectories, enforcing local temporal consistency at each step via temporal convolutional residual blocks, ultimately yielding globally coherent plans. Flexible conditioning will be enabled by incorporating auxiliary guide functions during sampling, such as reward gradients for reinforcement learning or constraint satisfaction for goal-reaching and inpainting tasks. The architecture will allow for variable-length plans and compositionality in both temporal and task dimensions, supporting planning for new objectives or constraints at test time without retraining.
3ebdd3db0dd91069fa0cd31cbf8308b60b1b565e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of control benchmarks, including the Maze2D environment for long-horizon planning with sparse rewards, block stacking tasks for test-time flexibility and compositionality, and the D4RL offline locomotion suite for offline reinforcement learning. The proposed method will be compared against strong baselines such as model-free offline RL algorithms (CQL, IQL, BCQ), model-based planners (MPPI), and sequence modeling approaches (Decision Transformer, Trajectory Transformer). Evaluation metrics will include task-specific returns (e.g., goal-reaching success, stacking accuracy), generalization to unseen goals, and performance under varying planning horizons and runtime budgets. The experimental setup will also assess the impact of warm-starting and the ability to handle variable-length plans.
3ebdd3db0dd91069fa0cd31cbf8308b60b1b565e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a non-autoregressive, trajectory-level diffusion model for planning, tightly coupling the modeling and planning processes such that sampling and planning become nearly identical. This enables flexible conditioning for reward maximization and constraint satisfaction, supports variable-length and compositional plans, and demonstrates superior performance in long-horizon, sparse-reward, and multi-task settings. The method departs from conventional model-based RL by subsuming trajectory optimization into the generative model, resulting in improved scalability, generalization, and test-time adaptability.

3ec5f0da304a606c5989de5b00e1246ee64b3e46.title: kNN Prompting: Beyond-Context Learning with Calibration-Free Nearest Neighbor Inference
3ec5f0da304a606c5989de5b00e1246ee64b3e46.research_question: How can large language models be leveraged for efficient and scalable inference in supervised tasks, overcoming the limitations of context length and calibration bias inherent in in-context learning?
3ec5f0da304a606c5989de5b00e1246ee64b3e46.hypothesis: Utilizing a calibration-free nearest neighbor approach that leverages distributed representations from large language models will enable scalable, robust, and more accurate inference beyond the context length limitations of standard in-context learning.
3ec5f0da304a606c5989de5b00e1246ee64b3e46.proposed_method: A novel framework, kNN Prompting, is proposed that splits the training data into a small demonstration set and a larger anchor set. For each anchor example, a prompt is constructed using the demonstration set and the anchor, and the language model is queried to obtain its output distribution, which is cached as a distributed representation in a local datastore. At inference, the test instance is similarly encoded via the language model, and its distribution is matched against the cached anchor representations using KL divergence. The final prediction is made by aggregating the labels of the k nearest neighbors in the representation space. This approach bypasses the need to directly align model outputs with task-specific label spaces, instead relying on distributional similarity for robust and scalable prediction.
3ec5f0da304a606c5989de5b00e1246ee64b3e46.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 10 established text classification datasets, including SST2, SUBJ, MPQA, AGNews, CB, CR, DBPedia, MR, RTE, and TREC. The method will be evaluated across a range of large language model scales (e.g., GPT2 0.8B/1.5B, OPT 3B-30B), with k set to 3 for nearest neighbor aggregation. Baselines will include standard in-context learning (ICL), calibration-based augmentations (e.g., Contextual Calibration, Noisy Channel), ICL ensemble, and fine-tuning approaches (BERTLargeFT, GPTLargeFT). Evaluation metrics will primarily be classification accuracy, with results averaged over multiple random seeds. The experimental setup will include few-shot, low-resource, and fully supervised scenarios, and will also compare against demonstration selection and retrieval-based prompt composition methods.
3ec5f0da304a606c5989de5b00e1246ee64b3e46.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a calibration-free, gradient-free nearest neighbor inference paradigm for large language models that is not limited by context length, enabling effective scaling with arbitrary amounts of training data. It avoids forced input-label alignment and leverages the full output distribution of the language model for distributed representation matching, resulting in superior data utility, robustness, and explainability. The approach bridges the gap between data scaling and model scaling in LLM deployment, outperforming state-of-the-art calibration-based and retrieval-based methods, and providing a scalable solution for realistic, large-scale supervised inference with LLMs.

3ed178316be914658a80e561bf00576577f34389.title: Pre-gated MoE: An Algorithm-System Co-Design for Fast and Scalable Mixture-of-Expert Inference
3ed178316be914658a80e561bf00576577f34389.research_question: How can the inference of large-scale Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models be made faster and more memory-efficient to enable cost-effective deployment of large language models (LLMs) on limited hardware resources, such as a single GPU, without sacrificing model quality?
3ed178316be914658a80e561bf00576577f34389.hypothesis: Introducing a pre-gating mechanism that decouples expert selection from expert execution, combined with hierarchical parameter storage and preemptive expert migration, will significantly reduce inference latency and GPU memory usage for MoE-based LLMs while maintaining comparable model accuracy.
3ed178316be914658a80e561bf00576577f34389.proposed_method: A novel algorithm-system co-design is proposed that introduces a pre-gate function into the MoE architecture. This pre-gate function, implemented as a compact MLP, is trained to preemptively select which experts will be activated in the next MoE block, thereby decoupling the expert selection and execution stages. The system stores all sparse MoE expert parameters in CPU memory and only migrates the subset of experts predicted to be activated to the GPU in advance of their use, overlapping this migration with the computation of the current MoE block. Dense, non-MoE parameters are kept resident in GPU memory. The pre-gate function is integrated during the fine-tuning stage, with special handling for the first and last MoE blocks to ensure seamless operation across decoder iterations. This approach enables concurrent expert migration and execution, minimizing serialization bottlenecks and optimizing both memory and compute efficiency.
3ed178316be914658a80e561bf00576577f34389.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using Google’s SwitchTransformer as the baseline MoE model, with configurations ranging from 8 to 256 experts and up to 105.6 billion parameters. The evaluation is performed on a system with an AMD EPYC CPU (1.8TB DDR4) and a single NVIDIA A100 GPU (80GB HBM), connected via PCIe Gen4. Datasets include XSum for summarization and CB Web QA and SQuAD for question answering, with evaluation metrics such as Rouge-1/2, Exact Match, and F1. Baseline comparisons include GPU-only (all parameters on GPU), MoE-OnDemand (CPU offloading with on-demand migration), and MoE-Prefetch (CPU offloading with prefetch-all strategy). Key experimental details include fine-tuning with identical configurations across methods, measurement of single-batch inference throughput, MoE block latency, peak GPU memory usage, and model accuracy across tasks.
3ed178316be914658a80e561bf00576577f34389.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a pre-gate function that eliminates the sequential dependency between expert selection and execution within MoE blocks, enabling preemptive and selective migration of only the required experts. This approach allows for significant overlap of communication and computation, reducing inference latency and peak GPU memory usage. The method enables deployment of much larger MoE-based LLMs on a single GPU than previously possible, with minimal impact on model accuracy. The co-design of algorithmic and system-level optimizations is claimed to achieve both the performance of GPU-only solutions and the memory efficiency of optimal CPU-offloading strategies, representing a scalable and cost-effective advance for real-world MoE inference.

3ed2b5a9c8e42f3bf93dfd40426e4df205420ac7.title: Towards the Generalization of Contrastive Self-Supervised Learning
3ed2b5a9c8e42f3bf93dfd40426e4df205420ac7.research_question: What are the fundamental factors that govern the generalization ability of contrastive self-supervised learning, and how can these factors be theoretically characterized and empirically validated across different contrastive losses and data augmentation strategies?
3ed2b5a9c8e42f3bf93dfd40426e4df205420ac7.hypothesis: The generalization ability of contrastive self-supervised learning is determined by three key factors: alignment of positive samples, divergence of class centers, and concentration of augmented data, and these can be theoretically quantified and empirically correlated with downstream performance.
3ed2b5a9c8e42f3bf93dfd40426e4df205420ac7.proposed_method: A novel theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the generalization of contrastive self-supervised learning (SSL). The method introduces a (σ,δ)-measure to mathematically quantify the concentration of data augmentations, defining augmented distance and main-part concentration for each latent class. Theoretical upper bounds on downstream classification error will be derived in terms of three factors: alignment of positive samples (how closely augmented views of the same sample are embedded), divergence of class centers (distance between class means in embedding space), and concentration of augmented data (how tightly augmented samples from the same class cluster). The framework will be applied to canonical contrastive losses such as InfoNCE and cross-correlation, with rigorous proofs showing how these losses achieve alignment and divergence. The role of data augmentation in determining concentration will be isolated and studied both theoretically and empirically.
3ed2b5a9c8e42f3bf93dfd40426e4df205420ac7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard computer vision datasets such as CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. Multiple contrastive SSL algorithms, including SimCLR, Barlow Twins, MoCo, and SimSiam, will be evaluated using a ResNet-18 encoder and a KNN evaluation protocol. Various combinations and strengths of data augmentations (random cropping, Gaussian blur, color dropping, color distortion, horizontal flipping) will be systematically tested to manipulate the concentration of augmented data. Baseline comparisons will include different augmentation strategies and loss functions. Evaluation metrics will focus on downstream classification accuracy and error rates, with empirical measurements of the (σ,δ)-concentration to correlate with observed performance.
3ed2b5a9c8e42f3bf93dfd40426e4df205420ac7.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a new (σ,δ)-measure to rigorously quantify the concentration of augmented data in contrastive SSL. It establishes a theoretical framework that explicitly connects alignment, divergence, and concentration to generalization guarantees, providing provable error bounds. The approach extends theoretical analysis to both InfoNCE and cross-correlation losses, demonstrating their ability to achieve alignment and divergence. Empirical studies systematically validate the theoretical predictions, revealing a strong correlation between concentration of augmented data and downstream performance. This work provides new insights into the critical role of data augmentation and unifies theoretical and empirical perspectives on contrastive SSL generalization.

3ee60ee899941c7056fc10e1b69e71bac0f11c97.title: Denoising Diffusion Samplers
3ee60ee899941c7056fc10e1b69e71bac0f11c97.research_question: How can new sampling algorithms be developed to efficiently generate approximate samples from unnormalized probability densities and estimate their normalizing constants, especially in high-dimensional and complex target distributions, without requiring direct access to samples from the target distribution?
3ee60ee899941c7056fc10e1b69e71bac0f11c97.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by leveraging the structure of denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPM) and adapting their framework to the context of unnormalized densities, it is possible to construct a new class of samplers that can provide accurate samples and normalizing constant estimates, even when score matching is not directly applicable.
3ee60ee899941c7056fc10e1b69e71bac0f11c97.proposed_method: A novel class of algorithms, termed Denoising Diffusion Samplers (DDS), will be developed by constructing a forward diffusion process that transforms the target unnormalized density into a Gaussian reference. The time-reversal of this diffusion, which cannot be directly simulated due to the inaccessibility of the target distribution, will be approximated by parameterizing the reverse dynamics with a neural network. The objective will be to minimize the reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between the proposal and the true time-reversed diffusion, using a reparameterization that leverages an auxiliary reference process for low-variance gradient estimation. The methodology will include careful design of discrete-time integrators for both the reference and proposal processes to ensure a valid evidence lower bound (ELBO) and unbiased estimation of the normalizing constant. Extensions to underdamped Langevin dynamics and continuous-time normalizing flows will also be explored.
3ee60ee899941c7056fc10e1b69e71bac0f11c97.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of challenging sampling tasks, including standard benchmark distributions (e.g., funnel distribution, log Gaussian Cox process), Bayesian logistic regression on real datasets (Ionosphere, Sonar), Brownian motion time series models, and high-dimensional targets defined by pre-trained normalizing flows (e.g., NICE on MNIST). DDS will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC), Annealed Importance Sampling (AIS), Path Integral Samplers (PIS), and Mean-Field Variational Inference (MF-VI). Evaluation metrics will include the accuracy of the estimated normalizing constant (lnZ), sample quality (e.g., Sinkhorn distance for high-dimensional targets), and computational efficiency. Hyperparameters and architectures will be carefully tuned for all methods, and ablation studies will be performed to assess stability and performance.
3ee60ee899941c7056fc10e1b69e71bac0f11c97.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new class of samplers that adapt denoising diffusion model ideas to the context of unnormalized densities, enabling sampling and normalizing constant estimation without direct score matching. The methodology leverages a novel reparameterization and auxiliary reference process to facilitate low-variance training and unbiased estimation. The framework provides theoretical guarantees on the quality of generated samples and extends to both overdamped and underdamped dynamics as well as continuous-time normalizing flows. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate improved stability and competitive or superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art Monte Carlo and variational methods, particularly on complex and high-dimensional targets.

3f03876b23b491bdc161816024044e13b02b46e5.title: LongVILA: Scaling Long-Context Visual Language Models for Long Videos
3f03876b23b491bdc161816024044e13b02b46e5.research_question: How can visual-language models be effectively scaled to handle long-context video understanding tasks, both in terms of algorithmic capability and efficient distributed system support?
3f03876b23b491bdc161816024044e13b02b46e5.hypothesis: A co-designed full-stack approach, combining a multi-stage training pipeline with a novel multi-modal sequence parallelism system, will enable visual-language models to process and understand long videos with substantially increased context length and efficiency, outperforming existing solutions in both accuracy and scalability.
3f03876b23b491bdc161816024044e13b02b46e5.proposed_method: A comprehensive solution is proposed that integrates both algorithmic and system-level innovations for long-context visual-language models (VLMs). The methodology involves a five-stage training pipeline: (1) multi-modal alignment using open-source image and video caption datasets with only the multi-modal projector trainable; (2) large-scale pre-training with relabeled datasets to enhance general multi-modal capacity; (3) supervised fine-tuning on short video and image instruction-following datasets; (4) context extension for the language model via progressive pre-training on text-only data, increasing context length up to 262,144 tokens using datasets like SlimPajama and low-rank adaptation; (5) long supervised fine-tuning on a newly constructed long video instruction-following dataset, leveraging the proposed Multi-Modal Sequence Parallelism (MM-SP) system. The MM-SP system introduces a two-stage sharding strategy and 2D-attention mechanism to efficiently distribute both visual and textual workloads across GPUs, addressing modality and network heterogeneity, and enabling context lengths up to 2 million tokens without gradient checkpointing.
3f03876b23b491bdc161816024044e13b02b46e5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale GPU clusters (e.g., 32 or 256 H100/A100 GPUs) using models based on Qwen2-1.5B and Qwen2-7B backbones. The training pipeline will utilize open-source datasets for alignment and pre-training (e.g., COYO-25M, SlimPajama), and a custom long video dataset (15,292 videos from Shot2Story) for long-context supervised fine-tuning. Baselines will include state-of-the-art VLMs such as Video-LLaVA, LongVA, Megatron-LM, and DeepSpeed-Ulysses, with comparisons on throughput, maximum supported context length, and inference latency. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on nine popular video understanding benchmarks (e.g., ActivityNet-QA, VideoMME, LongVideoBench), as well as specialized long-context tasks like needle-in-a-haystack retrieval. System-level metrics will assess training and inference speedup, scalability, and memory efficiency.
3f03876b23b491bdc161816024044e13b02b46e5.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first full-stack solution for scaling visual-language models to extremely long video contexts, combining a five-stage training curriculum with a novel multi-modal sequence parallelism system. The MM-SP system is claimed to be the first to address both modality and network heterogeneity in sequence parallelism for VLMs, enabling efficient training and inference at context lengths up to 2 million tokens. The approach also includes the construction of a new long video instruction-following dataset and demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on multiple video understanding benchmarks, with significant speedups and scalability improvements over existing distributed training and inference systems.

3f0cb40f6f8549f09748928e166bb1e8a5f500d9.title: Sparse MeZO: Less Parameters for Better Performance in Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-Tuning
3f0cb40f6f8549f09748928e166bb1e8a5f500d9.research_question: How can zeroth-order optimization methods for large language model (LLM) fine-tuning be made more memory-efficient and performant, particularly by addressing the impact of gradient estimation noise and parameter selection?
3f0cb40f6f8549f09748928e166bb1e8a5f500d9.hypothesis: Selective application of zeroth-order optimization to a carefully chosen subset of parameters, specifically those with smaller magnitudes, will mitigate the negative effects of gradient estimation noise, enabling higher learning rates, faster convergence, and improved fine-tuning performance without increasing memory overhead.
3f0cb40f6f8549f09748928e166bb1e8a5f500d9.proposed_method: A novel memory-efficient zeroth-order optimization algorithm, Sparse-MeZO, is developed for LLM fine-tuning. The method introduces a dynamic, layer-wise sparse mask that selects parameters of smaller magnitude for perturbation and update, based on a percentile-based sparsity threshold. During each training iteration, the mask is computed on-the-fly using current parameter values, and Gaussian noise is applied only to the selected parameters. The zeroth-order gradient is estimated by evaluating the loss at perturbed parameter values, and only the masked parameters are updated. A memory-optimized implementation is proposed, where the mask is computed during the forward pass, eliminating the need to store additional parameter copies or masks, thus ensuring memory usage remains at inference-level.
3f0cb40f6f8549f09748928e166bb1e8a5f500d9.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on standard LLMs including LLaMA-7b, LLaMA-30b, Mistral-7B-v0.1, and OPT-13b, across a range of NLP tasks from the SuperGLUE benchmark (e.g., SST-2, RTE, BoolQ, WIC, MultiRC, COPA) and additional commonsense reasoning (PIQA, SIQA) and mathematics (AQuA) tasks. Baselines include vanilla MeZO, MeZO with random masking (R-MeZO), first-order full fine-tuning with Adam, LoRA (a PEFT method), and other recent zeroth-order optimizers (e.g., ZO-SGD-Cons, ZO-SGD-Adam, ZO-AdaMU, AdaZeta). Evaluation metrics are primarily task accuracy and convergence speed (steps to target accuracy). Memory usage is measured and compared across methods. Experiments use consistent hyperparameters with MeZO, with higher learning rates for Sparse-MeZO, and results are averaged over multiple seeds.
3f0cb40f6f8549f09748928e166bb1e8a5f500d9.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a principled, dynamic parameter selection scheme for zeroth-order optimization based on parameter magnitude, which mitigates the adverse effects of gradient estimation noise. The memory-efficient implementation enables fine-tuning of large models (e.g., LLaMA-30b) on a single GPU with inference-level memory usage. Empirical results demonstrate consistent improvements in accuracy and convergence speed over existing zeroth-order methods, with up to 9% absolute accuracy gain and 3.5x speedup on benchmark tasks, while using no additional memory. The approach significantly narrows the performance gap between zeroth-order and first-order fine-tuning.

3f16d91bdfca925df761d27fd3b11af7d68c63d8.title: On the Role of Attention in Prompt-tuning
3f16d91bdfca925df761d27fd3b11af7d68c63d8.research_question: What is the theoretical basis for the effectiveness of prompt-tuning in attention-based architectures, and how does the attention mechanism, particularly softmax-attention, contribute to the expressivity, optimization, and generalization of prompt-tuning compared to fine-tuning and other baseline methods?
3f16d91bdfca925df761d27fd3b11af7d68c63d8.hypothesis: Prompt-tuning, when combined with softmax-attention in one-layer attention architectures, is more expressive and can outperform both fine-tuning and self-attention baselines in scenarios where context-relevant information is sparse and can be effectively isolated by the attention mechanism.
3f16d91bdfca925df761d27fd3b11af7d68c63d8.proposed_method: A novel prompt-attention framework will be developed for one-layer attention architectures, where a trainable prompt vector is appended to the input tokens and interacts with the input through a softmax-based attention mechanism. The method will model each input as a mixture of context-relevant and context-irrelevant tokens, and the prompt will be optimized jointly with a linear prediction head using gradient-based methods. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to characterize the expressivity of the prompt-attention model, the optimization trajectory of gradient descent, and the generalization properties under a contextual mixture data model. The approach will include a detailed study of the population and finite-sample dynamics of prompt-attention, with explicit consideration of the roles of sparsity, context strength, and noise.
3f16d91bdfca925df761d27fd3b11af7d68c63d8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic datasets, generated according to a contextual mixture model with controlled sparsity and noise, and real-world image classification datasets derived from CIFAR-10 with varying degrees of context relevance and distribution shift. The evaluation will compare prompt-attention models against linear, self-attention, and linear-attention baselines, as well as standard fine-tuning. Metrics will include classification accuracy, test error, and the ability to attend to context-relevant tokens, with additional analysis of optimization dynamics and sample complexity. Multiple prompt-tuning variants will be tested, and the number of trainable parameters will be varied to assess efficiency and overfitting behavior in data-rich and data-limited regimes.
3f16d91bdfca925df761d27fd3b11af7d68c63d8.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a theoretical framework for understanding the role of attention, specifically softmax-attention, in prompt-tuning and establishes provable separation results showing that prompt-attention can be strictly more expressive than self-attention and linear-attention baselines. It provides the first rigorous analysis of the optimization and generalization dynamics of prompt-tuning via gradient descent, including explicit sample complexity bounds and error rates. The work also empirically validates these theoretical insights on both synthetic and real datasets, demonstrating the ability of prompt-attention to selectively attend to context-relevant information and outperform fine-tuning in certain regimes.

3f1774d91c7c219f063f40b894e837e6c48b2bb2.title: Provable Guarantees for Self-Supervised Deep Learning with Spectral Contrastive Loss
3f1774d91c7c219f063f40b894e837e6c48b2bb2.research_question: How can self-supervised deep learning methods be equipped with provable guarantees for representation quality and downstream linear classification performance, particularly in realistic settings where positive pairs are highly correlated due to data augmentations?
3f1774d91c7c219f063f40b894e837e6c48b2bb2.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a novel contrastive loss based on spectral decomposition of the population augmentation graph can yield neural network representations with provable accuracy guarantees for downstream linear probe evaluation, even when positive pairs are not conditionally independent.
3f1774d91c7c219f063f40b894e837e6c48b2bb2.proposed_method: A new self-supervised learning framework will be developed that leverages a spectral contrastive loss, derived from the spectral decomposition of the population augmentation graph. The method constructs a graph where vertices represent augmented data points and edges connect augmentations of the same natural example, with edge weights reflecting the probability of co-occurrence via augmentation. The spectral contrastive loss is formulated as a parametric objective over neural network representations, combining attraction of positive pairs and repulsion of negative pairs, with the loss function: L(f) = -2·E[f(x)ᵗf(x+)] + E[(f(x)ᵗf(x−))²], where (x, x+) are augmentations of the same data point and (x, x−) are independent augmentations. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to show that minimizing this loss leads to representations that, under mild and realistic graph-theoretic assumptions (such as limited inter-class connectivity and sufficient intra-class connectivity), enable linear classifiers to recover ground-truth labels with high accuracy. The method will be implemented with deep neural networks, and generalization from population to empirical loss will be established using standard generalization bounds.
3f1774d91c7c219f063f40b894e837e6c48b2bb2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard benchmark vision datasets, such as ImageNet and CIFAR, using the proposed spectral contrastive loss to pretrain neural network encoders. The learned representations will be evaluated via linear probe classification, comparing accuracy against strong baselines including SimCLR, SimSiam, and BYOL. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 and top-5 classification accuracy. The experimental setup will avoid reliance on techniques such as stop-gradient, and batch sizes will be varied to assess robustness. Ablation studies will be performed to analyze the impact of representation dimension and graph connectivity assumptions. The number of unlabeled and labeled examples required for effective learning will be empirically measured to validate theoretical sample complexity claims.
3f1774d91c7c219f063f40b894e837e6c48b2bb2.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first provable analysis for contrastive learning in settings where positive pairs are not conditionally independent, closely matching practical self-supervised learning scenarios. The spectral contrastive loss is motivated by spectral clustering theory but is formulated as a practical, parametric loss suitable for deep learning. Theoretical guarantees are established for downstream linear probe performance under realistic data assumptions, and the method is shown to require only a polynomial number of unlabeled samples and a linear number of labeled samples relative to the representation dimension. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate that the method matches or outperforms established baselines without requiring specialized tricks or large batch sizes.

3f20edc750a28eaea716b894ee7f96eca391178f.title: Collaborative Mean Estimation Among Heterogeneous Strategic Agents: Individual Rationality, Fairness, and Truthful Contribution
3f20edc750a28eaea716b894ee7f96eca391178f.research_question: How can collaborative mean estimation be achieved among heterogeneous strategic agents, ensuring that all agents benefit individually, outcomes are fair, and agents are incentivized to truthfully contribute their data, even when agents have different data collection costs and may act strategically?
3f20edc750a28eaea716b894ee7f96eca391178f.hypothesis: It is possible to design a mechanism for collaborative mean estimation among heterogeneous agents that is individually rational, fair, and incentivizes truthful data contribution, while achieving near-optimal efficiency compared to the best possible individually rational solution.
3f20edc750a28eaea716b894ee7f96eca391178f.proposed_method: A mechanism is developed for collaborative mean estimation where each agent samples from a set of univariate normal distributions, incurring agent- and distribution-specific costs. The method formalizes three desiderata: individual rationality (IR), incentive compatibility (IC), and efficiency (minimizing social penalty, defined as the sum of estimation errors and data collection costs). The mechanism computes an enforceable division of work using a subroutine that adjusts the data collection scheme to ensure sufficient validation of each agent's contribution. It evaluates each agent's data by comparing it to data submitted by others, using corruption-based techniques to penalize dishonest reporting. The mechanism operates without monetary transfers and can be adapted to implement fairer divisions of work by integrating concepts from axiomatic bargaining, such as Nash or egalitarian bargaining solutions.
3f20edc750a28eaea716b894ee7f96eca391178f.experiment_details: Theoretical analysis is conducted to establish the properties of the proposed mechanism, including its Nash equilibrium, efficiency guarantees, and hardness results. The mechanism is evaluated on its ability to achieve a bounded approximation to the optimal social penalty under both worst-case and favorable conditions. Baseline mechanisms, such as the sample mean mechanism and individually rational allocations, are compared to the proposed approach. Theoretical lower bounds are established to demonstrate the impossibility of achieving certain stronger incentive or fairness properties without sacrificing efficiency. No empirical datasets or real-world experiments are specified; the evaluation is based on rigorous mathematical proofs and illustrative examples.
3f20edc750a28eaea716b894ee7f96eca391178f.novelty_claims: The proposed mechanism is the first to address collaborative mean estimation among heterogeneous agents with unequal data collection costs, ensuring individual rationality, fairness, and truthful data contribution in a strategic setting. The approach overcomes technical challenges in validating contributions when agents collect varying amounts of data from different distributions. The mechanism achieves a provable approximation to the optimal social penalty and accommodates fairer work allocations using cooperative game theory concepts. Matching hardness results are provided, showing that certain stronger incentive or fairness guarantees are fundamentally incompatible with efficiency in this setting.

3f28e8e3935c5bd2c8492d7c2724f7e98cfcfe2e.title: MetaDesigner: Advancing Artistic Typography through AI-Driven, User-Centric, and Multilingual WordArt Synthesis
3f28e8e3935c5bd2c8492d7c2724f7e98cfcfe2e.research_question: How can a user-centric, AI-driven system be developed to generate high-quality, customizable, and context-aware artistic typography (WordArt) across multiple languages and diverse stylistic preferences?
3f28e8e3935c5bd2c8492d7c2724f7e98cfcfe2e.hypothesis: A multi-agent framework that integrates large language models, controllable image synthesis, and iterative user/model feedback can effectively generate visually compelling, semantically aligned, and culturally adaptive WordArt, outperforming existing text-to-image and typographic generation methods.
3f28e8e3935c5bd2c8492d7c2724f7e98cfcfe2e.proposed_method: A novel multi-agent system will be developed, comprising four specialized agents: Pipeline Designer, Glyph Designer, Texture Designer, and Q&A Evaluation Agent. The Pipeline Designer will translate user prompts into structured workflows using visual programming and Chain-of-Thought prompting, generating enriched instructions for downstream agents. The Glyph Designer will select and render glyphs in normal, traditional, or semantic styles, leveraging font libraries and semantic transformations with differentiable rasterization and Stable Diffusion-based models. The Texture Designer will apply controllable image synthesis using a Tree-of-Thought (ToT) model selection strategy, dynamically blending from a curated library of 68 LoRA models to achieve stylistic diversity and user alignment. The Q&A Evaluation Agent will iteratively refine outputs by integrating multimodal model assessments (e.g., LLaVA) and direct user feedback, optimizing hyperparameters for text-image consistency, quality, and user preference. The entire system will operate in a closed feedback loop, continually adapting to user intent and evaluation metrics.
3f28e8e3935c5bd2c8492d7c2724f7e98cfcfe2e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a curated set of 150 prompts spanning five themes (cartoon, design, reality, sci-fi, and traditional culture), with 20 prompts selected for multilingual user studies (English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean). The proposed system will be benchmarked against state-of-the-art baselines including Stable Diffusion XL, TextDiffuser, TextDiffuser-2, Anytext, and DALL-E3. Evaluation will use both quantitative metrics (SSIM, LPIPS) and qualitative user studies assessing text accuracy, aesthetics, creativity, and semantic alignment. Additional ablation studies will investigate the effectiveness of the Tree-of-Thought model selection and the impact of iterative optimization on text-to-image consistency and visual quality.
3f28e8e3935c5bd2c8492d7c2724f7e98cfcfe2e.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a multi-agent, LLM-driven framework uniquely tailored for artistic typography synthesis, featuring an integrated feedback loop that combines automated and user evaluations for iterative refinement. The Glyph Designer’s hierarchical model tree and semantic glyph transformation enable unprecedented stylistic diversity and cultural adaptability. The Texture Designer’s Tree-of-Thought model selection and dynamic LoRA blending provide fine-grained control over visual style. Furthermore, the creation of a comprehensive, multilingual WordArt dataset supports benchmarking and future research in artistic text generation.

3f459219d75de63b5b7a26a8c6447ec1e79a985c.title: LoraHub: Efficient Cross-Task Generalization via Dynamic LoRA Composition
3f459219d75de63b5b7a26a8c6447ec1e79a985c.research_question: How can large language models be efficiently adapted to perform well on novel, unseen tasks using parameter-efficient fine-tuning modules, without requiring extensive retraining or human expertise?
3f459219d75de63b5b7a26a8c6447ec1e79a985c.hypothesis: It is possible to achieve effective cross-task generalization in large language models by dynamically composing multiple LoRA modules, each trained on different upstream tasks, using only a few labeled examples from a new target task and without additional model parameters or gradient-based optimization.
3f459219d75de63b5b7a26a8c6447ec1e79a985c.proposed_method: The proposed approach involves first training a collection of LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) modules on a diverse set of upstream tasks, each module corresponding to a specific task. For a new, unseen target task, a small set of labeled examples is provided. The method then enters a two-stage process: (1) the COMPOSE stage, where available LoRA modules are combined into a single integrated module using a set of scalar coefficients, and (2) the ADAPT stage, where these coefficients are optimized to maximize performance on the few-shot examples from the new task. Optimization is performed using a gradient-free black-box method (e.g., CMA-ES), guided by cross-entropy loss and L1 regularization. The final composed LoRA module is merged with the base LLM, yielding a model adapted to the new task without further updates.
3f459219d75de63b5b7a26a8c6447ec1e79a985c.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize the FLAN-T5-large model as the base LLM and the Big-Bench Hard (BBH) benchmark, which includes 27 challenging tasks spanning various domains. Approximately 200 LoRA modules, each trained on different upstream tasks, will serve as the candidate pool, with 20 randomly selected for each experimental run. Evaluation will be conducted using the exact match (EM) metric. Baseline comparisons will include zero-shot learning, few-shot in-context learning, full fine-tuning, LoRA tuning, IA3 fine-tuning, and a LoRA retrieval baseline. Each method will be evaluated over three runs with different few-shot example sets, and performance will be averaged. The number of tokens per example and memory usage will also be measured to assess efficiency.
3f459219d75de63b5b7a26a8c6447ec1e79a985c.novelty_claims: The proposed framework enables dynamic, data-driven composition of multiple LoRA modules for unseen tasks without requiring human expertise, additional model parameters, or gradient-based optimization. Unlike prior methods, it does not require multi-task training or manual selection of modules, and it operates efficiently in inference-only mode, significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. The approach establishes a practical platform for sharing and reusing LoRA modules, facilitating rapid and flexible adaptation of LLMs to new tasks while minimizing training and inference costs.

3f5b31c4f7350dc88002c121aecbdc82f86eb5bb.title: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models
3f5b31c4f7350dc88002c121aecbdc82f86eb5bb.research_question: How can vision-language pre-training be made more computationally efficient while leveraging the strengths of large pre-trained image encoders and large language models for a wide range of vision-language tasks?
3f5b31c4f7350dc88002c121aecbdc82f86eb5bb.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a lightweight querying transformer, when pre-trained in a two-stage process with frozen pre-trained image encoders and large language models, can effectively bridge the modality gap and achieve state-of-the-art performance on vision-language tasks with significantly fewer trainable parameters.
3f5b31c4f7350dc88002c121aecbdc82f86eb5bb.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that utilizes frozen, off-the-shelf pre-trained image encoders and large language models (LLMs) to perform vision-language pre-training. The core component is a lightweight Querying Transformer (Q-Former), which is pre-trained in two stages: (1) vision-language representation learning, where Q-Former learns to extract language-relevant visual features from a frozen image encoder using a combination of image-text contrastive, image-text matching, and image-grounded text generation objectives; and (2) vision-to-language generative learning, where Q-Former is connected to a frozen LLM and trained to project visual features into the LLM's input space via a fully-connected layer, enabling the LLM to generate text conditioned on visual input. The Q-Former acts as an information bottleneck, ensuring only the most relevant visual information is passed to the LLM, and different attention masking strategies are employed to control query-text interactions during pre-training.
3f5b31c4f7350dc88002c121aecbdc82f86eb5bb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a large-scale pre-training dataset comprising 129 million images from sources such as COCO, Visual Genome, CC3M, CC12M, SBU, and LAION400M, with synthetic captions generated and filtered for quality. The framework will be evaluated on a variety of vision-language tasks, including zero-shot visual question answering (VQAv2, OK-VQA, GQA), image captioning (COCO, NoCaps), and image-text retrieval (COCO, Flickr30K), using metrics such as VQA accuracy, CIDEr, SPICE, BLEU@4, and retrieval recall at K. Baselines will include state-of-the-art models such as Flamingo, BLIP, SimVLM, BEIT-3, and others. Both decoder-based (OPT) and encoder-decoder-based (FlanT5) LLMs, as well as different image encoders (CLIP ViT-L/14, EVA-CLIP ViT-g/14), will be explored. Fine-tuning will be performed for downstream tasks, with the LLM kept frozen and only the Q-Former and image encoder updated.
3f5b31c4f7350dc88002c121aecbdc82f86eb5bb.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a generic and compute-efficient vision-language pre-training method that leverages both frozen pre-trained image encoders and large language models, requiring significantly fewer trainable parameters than existing methods. The two-stage pre-training strategy with a lightweight Querying Transformer effectively bridges the modality gap, enabling strong cross-modal alignment and generative capabilities. The method demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on a range of vision-language tasks, including zero-shot image-to-text generation that follows natural language instructions, and shows strong generalization to out-of-domain data. The modular design allows easy adoption of advances in unimodal vision and language models, and the approach achieves substantial improvements in efficiency and scalability compared to end-to-end pre-training.

3f69fb7e93b20d04dfec182184b3c1d0a67d45ab.title: Learning to Focus: Causal Attention Distillation via Gradient-Guided Token Pruning
3f69fb7e93b20d04dfec182184b3c1d0a67d45ab.research_question: How can large language models be improved to focus on truly critical information during long-context reasoning and generation, thereby enhancing reasoning accuracy and robustness across complex tasks such as mathematical reasoning, code generation, and multi-hop question answering?
3f69fb7e93b20d04dfec182184b3c1d0a67d45ab.hypothesis: Mitigating the influence of confounding tokens—identified as spurious correlations in training data—through targeted pruning and distillation will enable student models to better capture true causal dependencies, resulting in improved reasoning accuracy, robustness, and interpretability.
3f69fb7e93b20d04dfec182184b3c1d0a67d45ab.proposed_method: A two-stage framework, Learning to Focus (LeaF), is proposed to enhance the causal attention of student language models. In the first stage, confounding tokens are identified using gradient-based comparisons between a high-capacity teacher model and a student model, focusing on instances where the student mispredicts but the teacher succeeds. Tokens with significant gradient sensitivity discrepancies are classified as confounders and are pruned using a span-based strategy to generate counterfactual training samples. In the second stage, a hybrid distillation objective is employed: the student is trained to align its output distribution with the teacher's on both the original and counterfactual samples, blending standard and counterfactual distillation losses. This composite loss encourages the student to preserve semantic knowledge while enforcing genuine causal dependencies, and can be applied at both instruction and response levels.
3f69fb7e93b20d04dfec182184b3c1d0a67d45ab.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on mathematical reasoning, code generation, and multi-hop question answering tasks. Training datasets include subsets from NuminaMath-CoT (Olympiads, AMC_AIME, GSM8K, MATH), AceCode-87k for code, and KILT datasets for multi-hop QA. Evaluation will use benchmarks such as GSM8K, MATH-500, OlympiadBench (math), HumanEval+, LeetCode, LivecodeBench (code), and HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, Musique (QA). Baselines include standard knowledge distillation without pruning, and models from the LLaMA and Qwen families at various sizes, with high-capacity teacher models (e.g., LLaMA3.3-70B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct). Models will be trained with Alpaca-LoRA, full-parameter logits distillation, and evaluated using greedy decoding and official templates. Evaluation metrics include accuracy, EM, F1, and SubEM, with detailed ablations on masking and response splitting strategies.
3f69fb7e93b20d04dfec182184b3c1d0a67d45ab.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a causal perspective to attention distillation by explicitly identifying and pruning confounding tokens using gradient-based teacher-student comparisons. Unlike prior methods that focus primarily on output imitation or self-assessment, this method leverages advanced teacher guidance to disentangle spurious correlations in both instruction and response contexts. The framework combines original and counterfactual distillation objectives, enabling more robust and interpretable reasoning. Empirical results demonstrate significant improvements over standard distillation and alternative masking strategies, establishing a new direction for enhancing LLM reasoning through causal intervention.

3f75c86479f982130e58d8c769724ca07121bd53.title: Dropout Reduces Underfitting
3f75c86479f982130e58d8c769724ca07121bd53.research_question: Can dropout, traditionally used to prevent overfitting in neural networks, be adapted to also mitigate underfitting, and how can its scheduling during training be optimized to improve model performance across different regimes of underfitting and overfitting?
3f75c86479f982130e58d8c769724ca07121bd53.hypothesis: Applying dropout selectively during specific phases of training—early dropout for underfitting models and late dropout for overfitting models—will improve model fit and generalization by reducing gradient variance and aligning mini-batch gradients with the full-dataset gradient, thereby enhancing both training loss and test accuracy.
3f75c86479f982130e58d8c769724ca07121bd53.proposed_method: A novel training strategy is proposed where dropout is applied only during the initial phase of training (early dropout) for models in underfitting regimes, and conversely, dropout is withheld in the early phase and activated later (late dropout) for models prone to overfitting. The approach involves identifying the model's regime based on whether standard dropout improves or harms generalization, then scheduling dropout accordingly. Early dropout is implemented by enabling dropout for a configurable number of initial epochs or iterations, after which it is disabled for the remainder of training. Late dropout reverses this schedule. The method also includes hyperparameter sweeps for dropout rates and the duration of dropout application, and can be extended to stochastic depth regularization. Gradient direction variance and alignment with the full-dataset gradient are measured to analyze the effects of these schedules on optimization dynamics.
3f75c86479f982130e58d8c769724ca07121bd53.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the ImageNet-1K dataset for image classification, using models such as ViT-Tiny/16, Mixer-S/32, ConvNeXt-Femto, and Swin-F for early dropout (underfitting regime), and ViT-Base and Mixer-Base for late dropout (overfitting regime). Both basic and improved training recipes are used, including variations in data augmentation, batch size, and learning rate warmup. Dropout and stochastic depth rates are tuned via hyperparameter sweeps, and results are averaged over multiple random seeds. Evaluation metrics include top-1 validation accuracy and training loss.
