Additional downstream experiments are performed on COCO for object detection and segmentation, ADE20K for semantic segmentation, and several classification datasets (CIFAR-100, Flowers, Pets, STL-10, Food-101) to assess transferability and robustness. Baselines include standard dropout, no dropout, and alternative dropout scheduling strategies (e.g., linear increase/decrease, curriculum, annealed). Gradient direction variance and error are quantitatively analyzed to support the optimization hypotheses.
3f75c86479f982130e58d8c769724ca07121bd53.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the concept of using dropout not only as a regularizer for overfitting but also as a tool to reduce underfitting, specifically through the early dropout schedule. It provides a new perspective on dropout's role in training dynamics by demonstrating its effect on gradient variance and alignment. The approach includes the first systematic study of dropout scheduling tailored to the underfitting/overfitting regime, and presents robust, easy-to-implement hyperparameter settings. Comprehensive empirical evidence is provided across multiple architectures and tasks, showing consistent improvements over standard dropout and no-dropout baselines. The work also extends the methodology to stochastic depth and demonstrates its effectiveness in both pre-training and downstream transfer scenarios.

3f7fa58806614a1f38ae760c25c1305e3a87d4ce.title: Interpretability at Scale: Identifying Causal Mechanisms in Alpaca
3f7fa58806614a1f38ae760c25c1305e3a87d4ce.research_question: How can faithful, human-interpretable causal mechanisms underlying the behavior of large language models be identified and robustly aligned with neural representations at scale?
3f7fa58806614a1f38ae760c25c1305e3a87d4ce.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that scalable, optimization-based alignment methods can efficiently uncover interpretable causal variables within large language models, and that these alignments will be robust to variations in input, instruction, and output format.
3f7fa58806614a1f38ae760c25c1305e3a87d4ce.proposed_method: A novel method, Boundless Distributed Alignment Search (BoundlessDAS), will be developed to identify interpretable causal structures in large language models by learning both the alignment and the dimensionality of linear subspaces corresponding to high-level causal variables. This approach replaces brute-force search steps in prior methods with a learnable mask-based mechanism, allowing the method to automatically determine the number of neurons needed for each causal variable. The method involves training an orthogonal rotation matrix and continuous boundary indices via gradient descent to maximize interchange intervention accuracy (IIA), a metric that quantifies the faithfulness of the alignment between neural and causal variables. Weighted distributed interchange interventions are performed by swapping aligned subspaces between examples and updating the alignment to ensure the neural model's counterfactual behavior matches that of the hypothesized causal model. The approach is designed for efficiency and scalability, enabling application to models with billions of parameters.
3f7fa58806614a1f38ae760c25c1305e3a87d4ce.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Alpaca (7B) language model, an instruct-tuned LLaMA variant, focusing on a numerical reasoning task ('Price Tagging') where the model must decide if a price falls within a specified range. Several human-interpretable causal models (e.g., LeftBoundary, Left and Right Boundary, Mid-point Distance, Bracket Identity) will be hypothesized and tested for alignment. The BoundlessDAS method will be trained and evaluated across multiple layers and token positions, using Interchange Intervention Accuracy (IIA) as the primary metric. Baselines will include random rotation matrices and randomly initialized models. Robustness will be assessed by evaluating generalization to unseen instructions, input contexts, and output formats, as well as by analyzing performance on both correct and incorrect model outputs. Multiple random seeds and control conditions will be used to ensure statistical reliability.
3f7fa58806614a1f38ae760c25c1305e3a87d4ce.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first scalable method for identifying faithful, interpretable causal mechanisms in large, general-purpose language models by learning both alignment and subspace dimensionality. BoundlessDAS transforms previously intractable brute-force search steps into a differentiable, learnable process, enabling efficient causal analysis at the scale of billions of parameters. The method provides formal guarantees of causal faithfulness when high IIA is achieved and demonstrates robust generalization of discovered alignments across diverse instructions, contexts, and output formats. This work represents a significant advance in the mechanistic interpretability of large language models and provides a publicly available tool for the research community.

3fab7327ce553c7a6dc67cd787d3926e5dac00e0.title: Scaling Stick-Breaking Attention: An Efficient Implementation and In-depth Study
3fab7327ce553c7a6dc67cd787d3926e5dac00e0.research_question: Can an alternative attention mechanism based on the stick-breaking process serve as an effective and efficient replacement for softmax-based attention in large-scale Transformer models, particularly with respect to length generalization and downstream NLP tasks?
3fab7327ce553c7a6dc67cd787d3926e5dac00e0.hypothesis: Replacing softmax-based attention with a stick-breaking process will improve length generalization and maintain or enhance performance on downstream NLP tasks, while allowing for efficient large-scale training without the need for positional embeddings.
3fab7327ce553c7a6dc67cd787d3926e5dac00e0.proposed_method: A novel attention mechanism is proposed that utilizes the stick-breaking process instead of the traditional softmax operator. For each token, the method determines a breakpoint for each preceding token, representing the proportion of attention weight to allocate, and recursively applies this process to the remaining attention 'stick' until all tokens are assigned weights. The resulting attention weights naturally encode a recency bias, obviating the need for explicit positional embeddings. The method is implemented in a numerically stable manner by operating in log-space and leveraging the softplus operation to prevent underflow and overflow. To enable large-scale and long-sequence training, the stick-breaking attention is integrated into a Triton-based kernel, adapting techniques from FlashAttention for efficient memory usage and computation, including block-wise processing and early halting optimizations.
3fab7327ce553c7a6dc67cd787d3926e5dac00e0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world NLP tasks. Synthetic tasks, such as the Multi-Query Repeated Associative Recall (MQRAR), will be used to analyze inductive biases and compare the ability of stick-breaking and softmax-based attention to handle variable tracking and repeated associations. For large-scale evaluation, 350M, 1B, and 3B parameter Transformer models will be pre-trained on the SlimPajama dataset (1T tokens) and evaluated on benchmarks including Wikitext, ARC, HellaSwag, OpenBookQA, PIQA, RACE, SciQ, Winogrande, and MMLU, using the LMevaluation Harness. Length generalization will be assessed by training on fixed context lengths (e.g., 1024 or 4096) and testing on much longer contexts (up to 64K tokens), with baselines including Softmax+RoPE, ALiBi, FIRE, NoPE, and sliding window attention. Evaluation metrics include accuracy, perplexity, and performance on retrieval tasks such as the RULER benchmark, with detailed comparisons of downstream task performance and context extrapolation.
3fab7327ce553c7a6dc67cd787d3926e5dac00e0.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a scalable, numerically stable, and efficient implementation of stick-breaking attention as a drop-in replacement for softmax-based attention in Transformers. This approach eliminates the need for positional embeddings while retaining or improving model performance, particularly in length generalization and in-context learning. The method adapts FlashAttention-style optimizations to the stick-breaking process, enabling practical large-scale training and inference. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior performance in long-context extrapolation and competitive or improved results on standard NLP benchmarks, establishing stick-breaking attention as a promising alternative to conventional attention mechanisms.

3fb26c0cf930b04635540e4815c4b8ca0581155c.title: Chain of Preference Optimization: Improving Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in LLMs
3fb26c0cf930b04635540e4815c4b8ca0581155c.research_question: How can the strategic depth and deliberative reasoning capabilities of tree-based reasoning methods be integrated into chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning in large language models (LLMs) to improve reasoning performance without incurring significant inference latency?
3fb26c0cf930b04635540e4815c4b8ca0581155c.hypothesis: Fine-tuning LLMs using preference information derived from the tree-search process of tree-of-thought (ToT) reasoning will enable CoT-style inference to achieve comparable or superior performance to ToT, while maintaining low inference latency.
3fb26c0cf930b04635540e4815c4b8ca0581155c.proposed_method: A novel training framework, Chain of Preference Optimization (CPO), is proposed to enhance LLM reasoning by leveraging preference data extracted from the tree-search process of ToT. During training, multiple candidate thoughts are generated at each reasoning step using the LLM, and each is evaluated by the LLM itself for its contribution toward solving the problem. Preferred thoughts—those included in the final selected reasoning paths—are paired with dispreferred sibling thoughts not chosen in the path. These preference pairs are used to fine-tune the LLM using the Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) objective, which maximizes the likelihood ratio of preferred over dispreferred thoughts at each step. The process is repeated for every step in the reasoning chain, enabling the model to learn fine-grained, stepwise preferences without requiring human annotations or external reward models. At inference time, the model performs standard CoT decoding, benefiting from the deliberative supervision acquired during training.
3fb26c0cf930b04635540e4815c4b8ca0581155c.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on seven datasets spanning question answering (Bamboogle, WikiMultiHopQA, HotpotQA), fact verification (Fever, Feverous, VitaminC), and arithmetic reasoning (SVAMP). The base models include LLaMA2-7B/13B and Mistral-7B, fine-tuned with LoRA adapters. Baselines for comparison are standard CoT (greedy decoding), ToT (tree-search reasoning), and TS-SFT (supervised fine-tuning on ToT-discovered paths). Evaluation metrics include accuracy and average inference latency per instance. For each dataset, 4-shot prompting is used with manually constructed CoT demonstrations. The CPO method generates 10 candidate thoughts per step, retains the top 5 after LLM-based evaluation, and uses a batch size of 32 for optimization. All experiments are repeated three times with different random seeds, and results are averaged.
3fb26c0cf930b04635540e4815c4b8ca0581155c.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new paradigm for LLM reasoning optimization by constructing and utilizing per-step preference data derived from the ToT search tree, rather than relying solely on final reasoning paths or human-annotated data. CPO uniquely leverages both preferred and dispreferred thoughts at each reasoning step, enabling more granular and effective alignment of LLMs to deliberative reasoning strategies. This approach avoids the high inference latency of tree-search methods by shifting the computational burden to training, and empirically achieves comparable or superior performance to ToT with significantly faster inference. Additionally, the method is annotation-free and does not require external reward models, representing a substantial advancement in efficient, self-supervised LLM reasoning.

3fb50a3c764d0a800af529ff9b8e359f59b1fcc2.title: Learning Multimodal Rewards from Rankings
3fb50a3c764d0a800af529ff9b8e359f59b1fcc2.research_question: How can multimodal reward functions be efficiently learned from human feedback in the form of trajectory rankings, particularly in settings where data is provided by multiple experts with diverse or task-dependent preferences, and how can the data-efficiency of this learning process be improved?
3fb50a3c764d0a800af529ff9b8e359f59b1fcc2.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that modeling reward learning as a mixture of Plackett-Luce models over rankings, combined with an active querying strategy that maximizes information gain, will enable efficient and accurate learning of multimodal reward functions from human feedback, outperforming unimodal models and standard active learning baselines in terms of data-efficiency and learning quality.
3fb50a3c764d0a800af529ff9b8e359f59b1fcc2.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed for learning multimodal reward functions by formulating the problem as a mixture model, where each mode corresponds to a different expert or preference profile. The reward for each trajectory is modeled as a linear function over known features, and the overall human feedback is represented as a mixture of Plackett-Luce models, each with unknown weights and mixing coefficients. Bayesian inference is used to maintain a posterior over the reward weights and mixing coefficients, updating this posterior as ranking queries are answered. To enhance data-efficiency, an active learning approach is employed, selecting the next ranking query by maximizing the expected information gain about the model parameters. Monte Carlo sampling and Metropolis-Hastings are used to approximate the posterior and optimize the query selection, with simulated annealing applied to efficiently search the space of possible queries.
3fb50a3c764d0a800af529ff9b8e359f59b1fcc2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in both simulated and real-world environments. The primary testbeds are a multi-task variant of OpenAI’s LunarLander (with 1000 trajectories) and a real Fetch robot performing a banana placement task (with 351 distinct trajectories). Data will be collected from multiple users, each providing rankings over sets of trajectories, with some users given different task instructions or exhibiting different preferences. The proposed method will be compared against baselines including random query selection and volume removal, a standard active learning objective. Evaluation metrics will include mean squared error (MSE) between learned and true model parameters (for synthetic experiments), log-likelihood of held-out ranking responses, and learned policy rewards on the actual tasks. Both simulation-based and user study experiments will be performed, with statistical tests used to assess significance of improvements in data-efficiency and learning quality.
3fb50a3c764d0a800af529ff9b8e359f59b1fcc2.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first approach for learning multimodal reward functions from rankings in a continuous hypothesis space, using a mixture of Plackett-Luce models. It further innovates by developing an active querying strategy based on information gain tailored for mixture models, which is shown to significantly improve data-efficiency over existing baselines. The method is applicable in settings where the number of modes is unknown and where expert identity is not labeled, addressing practical challenges in real-world human-robot interaction and reward learning.

3fc6184c72fd55b67409ef87493c333f15a33180.title: CameraCtrl: Enabling Camera Control for Text-to-Video Generation
3fc6184c72fd55b67409ef87493c333f15a33180.research_question: How can precise and flexible camera pose control be achieved in video diffusion models to enable dynamic and customized video generation from textual and camera pose inputs, while maintaining high video quality and generalizability across different video generation models?
3fc6184c72fd55b67409ef87493c333f15a33180.hypothesis: Incorporating a plug-and-play camera control module using Plücker embeddings as camera pose representations, and training it on datasets with diverse camera trajectories and similar appearance to the base model, will enable accurate and generalizable camera control in video diffusion models without sacrificing video quality.
3fc6184c72fd55b67409ef87493c333f15a33180.proposed_method: A novel camera control framework will be developed for video diffusion models by introducing a plug-and-play camera encoder that accepts Plücker embeddings as input, representing the camera pose for each frame at the pixel level. The camera encoder will be designed with temporal attention modules after each convolutional block to capture temporal relationships in camera movement throughout the video. Multi-scale camera features extracted by the encoder will be injected into the temporal attention layers of the U-Net architecture within the video diffusion model, ensuring that camera pose information is effectively fused with the generative process. The camera control module will be trained independently of the base model's appearance features, focusing solely on geometric camera information, thus enabling broad compatibility and generalization across various video diffusion backbones.
3fc6184c72fd55b67409ef87493c333f15a33180.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both text-to-video (T2V) and image-to-video (I2V) generation tasks using AnimateDiffV3 and Stable Video Diffusion (SVD) as base models. The RealEstate10K dataset, containing approximately 65,000 video clips with diverse camera trajectories and appearance similar to the base models, will be used for training, with additional ablations on Objaverse, MVImageNet, and ACID datasets to study the impact of dataset characteristics. Baselines will include AnimateDiff with MotionLoRA and MotionCtrl, with comparisons made using metrics such as Fréchet Video Distance (FVD), CLIPSIM, Frame Consistency (FC), Object Dynamic Degree (ODD), and camera control accuracy metrics (RotErr and TransErr). User studies will be conducted to assess subjective camera control quality. Ablation studies will examine the effect of different camera representations, encoder architectures, and feature injection strategies.
3fc6184c72fd55b67409ef87493c333f15a33180.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a plug-and-play camera control module for video diffusion models that enables precise, flexible, and generalizable camera pose control. The use of Plücker embeddings as the camera pose representation provides pixel-wise geometric context, leading to superior controllability compared to raw parameter inputs. The method is agnostic to the appearance of the training data, allowing seamless integration with a wide range of video diffusion models and compatibility with other video control techniques. A comprehensive analysis of training datasets is provided, highlighting the importance of camera trajectory diversity and appearance similarity for effective camera control. The approach achieves state-of-the-art camera controllability without degrading video quality.

3ff7153fd6bd47d08084c7f50f8fd70026c126e7.title: Compositional Visual Generation with Composable Diffusion Models
3ff7153fd6bd47d08084c7f50f8fd70026c126e7.research_question: How can compositionality in visual generation be improved to enable the generation of images that accurately reflect complex combinations of concepts, such as multiple objects, object relations, and attributes, beyond the capabilities of current text-guided diffusion models?
3ff7153fd6bd47d08084c7f50f8fd70026c126e7.hypothesis: Explicitly factorizing the compositional generation problem by composing multiple diffusion models—each modeling a specific concept—using compositional operators such as conjunction and negation, will enable more accurate and generalizable visual generation, particularly for complex or unseen combinations of concepts.
3ff7153fd6bd47d08084c7f50f8fd70026c126e7.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that interprets diffusion models as energy-based models (EBMs), enabling the composition of multiple diffusion models corresponding to different concepts. Each concept (e.g., object, attribute, or relation) is represented by a separate diffusion model, and compositional operators (conjunction/AND and negation/NOT) are defined to combine these models during inference. The method leverages the equivalence between the denoising score function of diffusion models and the gradient of EBMs, allowing for the construction of a composed score function that guides the generation process. The approach supports zero-shot compositional generation by combining pre-trained or independently trained diffusion models at inference time, without requiring additional training for new compositions.
3ff7153fd6bd47d08084c7f50f8fd70026c126e7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple domains, including language description composition, object and object relation composition, and human facial attribute composition. Datasets to be used include CLEVR (objects and spatial positions), Relational CLEVR (object relations), and FFHQ (human faces with annotated attributes). Baselines for comparison will include StyleGAN2-ADA, StyleGAN2, LACE, GLIDE, and energy-based models (EBMs) with compositional operators. Evaluation metrics will include binary classification accuracy (using classifiers trained on real images to assess whether generated images contain all specified concepts) and Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for image quality. Each method will generate 5,000 images per test setting, and accuracy will be measured as the percentage of images capturing all target concepts.
3ff7153fd6bd47d08084c7f50f8fd70026c126e7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled method for composing diffusion models using energy-based model interpretations, enabling explicit compositionality in generative modeling. It defines and implements compositional operators (conjunction and negation) for diffusion models, supporting zero-shot generalization to complex, unseen combinations of concepts. The method allows for the composition of pre-trained models without additional training and demonstrates substantial improvements over existing baselines in both accuracy and image quality for compositional visual generation tasks.

403ff501765762bdbf69acbb0485a48f402b4fee.title: Optimal Prediction Using Expert Advice and Randomized Littlestone Dimension
403ff501765762bdbf69acbb0485a48f402b4fee.research_question: What is the optimal expected mistake bound achievable by randomized learners in online learning, and how can it be characterized combinatorially for both realizable and agnostic settings, including the problem of prediction using expert advice?
403ff501765762bdbf69acbb0485a48f402b4fee.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a natural extension of the Littlestone dimension, termed the randomized Littlestone dimension, precisely characterizes the optimal expected mistake bound for randomized learners in online learning. Furthermore, suitable generalizations of this dimension will yield tight bounds in the agnostic (k-realizable) setting and for the expert advice problem.
403ff501765762bdbf69acbb0485a48f402b4fee.proposed_method: A new combinatorial parameter, the randomized Littlestone dimension (RL(H)), will be defined to capture the optimal expected mistake bound for randomized online learners. This dimension is based on the supremum of the expected depth of random walks on shattered trees, divided by two. The methodology will extend to the agnostic setting by introducing k-Littlestone and k-randomized Littlestone dimensions, which generalize the notion of shattering to allow up to k mistakes per branch. Optimal learning rules will be constructed as probabilistic or weighted variants of the Standard Optimal Algorithm (SOA), adapting to both deterministic and randomized scenarios. Theoretical analysis will establish tight connections between these dimensions and achievable mistake bounds, including regret bounds and explicit algorithms for the expert advice setting.
403ff501765762bdbf69acbb0485a48f402b4fee.experiment_details: Theoretical experiments will be conducted by analyzing the mistake bounds of the proposed algorithms on various hypothesis classes with known Littlestone dimensions. The framework will be applied to the prediction with expert advice problem, comparing the new bounds to those achieved by the binomial weights algorithm and other classical baselines. Evaluation metrics will include the expected number of mistakes (or regret) as a function of the number of experts n, the allowed number of mistakes k, and the Littlestone dimension d. Both bounded and unbounded horizon scenarios will be considered, and the tightness of the bounds will be established through lower and upper bound proofs, including matching lower bounds for n=2 experts.
403ff501765762bdbf69acbb0485a48f402b4fee.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the randomized Littlestone dimension as a new combinatorial parameter that exactly characterizes the optimal expected mistake bound for randomized online learners, extending the classical Littlestone dimension beyond deterministic and realizable settings. The approach yields the first tight combinatorial characterization of optimal mistake and regret bounds in the agnostic (k-realizable) setting for both deterministic and randomized learners. The method resolves longstanding open questions in prediction using expert advice, providing optimal bounds for all values of n and k, and demonstrates that the optimal expected mistake bound for randomized learners is half that of the best deterministic bound, up to negligible additive terms. The analysis unifies and generalizes prior results, offering a comprehensive framework applicable to a broad range of online learning problems.

40417133ef6de4a3bdc825d46d683f12063cd418.title: EditVal: Benchmarking Diffusion Based Text-Guided Image Editing Methods
40417133ef6de4a3bdc825d46d683f12063cd418.research_question: How can a standardized and scalable benchmark be developed to quantitatively and qualitatively evaluate the performance of diffusion-based text-guided image editing methods across a diverse set of fine-grained edit types?
40417133ef6de4a3bdc825d46d683f12063cd418.hypothesis: A modular benchmark combining a curated dataset, a diverse suite of edit types, and both automated and human evaluation pipelines will enable robust, scalable, and fair comparison of text-guided image editing methods, revealing their strengths and weaknesses across a wide range of editing tasks.
40417133ef6de4a3bdc825d46d683f12063cd418.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark, named EDITVAL, will be constructed to evaluate text-guided image editing methods. The benchmark will consist of a curated dataset of real images sourced from the MS-COCO dataset, covering 19 object classes and 92 images. For each image, a suite of 13 diverse edit types (such as object addition, replacement, positional changes, size, background, color, style, action, and viewpoint) will be defined, with specific edit operations generated using expert input and language models like ChatGPT. Standardized prompts will be created for each edit operation, and edited images will be generated using various image editing methods. Evaluation will be conducted through two complementary pipelines: (1) a large-scale human study using standardized templates to assess edit fidelity, preservation of object properties, and image context; and (2) an automated evaluation pipeline leveraging pre-trained vision-language models (e.g., OwL-ViT) to validate object-centric edits via object detection and localization rules. The modular design will allow easy extension with new edit types and operations.
40417133ef6de4a3bdc825d46d683f12063cd418.experiment_details: Experiments will involve benchmarking eight state-of-the-art diffusion-based text-guided image editing methods, including Instruct-Pix2Pix, SINE, Imagic, Null-Text, Dreambooth, Textual Inversion, SDE-Edit, and Diffedit, using their public implementations with Stable Diffusion as the backbone. Edited images will be generated for all 648 unique edit operations defined in the benchmark. Automated evaluation will use OwL-ViT for six object-centric edit types, while human evaluation will be conducted via Amazon Mechanical Turk, with annotators rating the success of edits, preservation of object properties, and overall image context. Evaluation metrics will include binary edit success rates (automated), mean human annotation scores (0-3 scale), FID scores for image quality, and DINO scores for image fidelity to the original. Correlations between automated and human evaluations will be analyzed to validate the reliability of the automated pipeline.
40417133ef6de4a3bdc825d46d683f12063cd418.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces the first standardized, extensible, and large-scale evaluation suite for diffusion-based text-guided image editing, supporting a broad range of edit types and operations. It uniquely combines automated evaluation using advanced vision-language models with a scalable, standardized human study protocol, enabling robust and fair comparison of diverse editing methods. The modular design allows for straightforward integration of new edit types and operations, and the benchmark is validated through strong alignment between automated and human evaluations. This framework is positioned to become the standard for future research and development in text-guided image editing.

40455a044a750e367e0c225cea74bf078ca73c95.title: Anyprefer: An Agentic Framework for Preference Data Synthesis
40455a044a750e367e0c225cea74bf078ca73c95.research_question: How can high-quality preference data be automatically synthesized to improve the alignment of foundation models with human values across diverse domains, while overcoming the limitations of manual annotation and self-rewarding data generation approaches?
40455a044a750e367e0c225cea74bf078ca73c95.hypothesis: A cooperative agentic framework that leverages a two-player Markov Game between a target model and a judge model, augmented with external tools and a feedback mechanism, can synthesize higher-quality, more diverse preference data than existing methods, leading to improved model alignment and performance across multiple applications.
40455a044a750e367e0c225cea74bf078ca73c95.proposed_method: The proposed approach models preference data synthesis as a cooperative two-player Markov Game, where the target model generates candidate responses to input prompts and the judge model ranks these responses using information aggregated from a suite of external tools. The judge model selects relevant tools based on the prompt to extract supplementary knowledge, which is integrated into a knowledge base for more accurate and less biased evaluation. A reward model, implemented as an LLM, evaluates the quality of generated preference pairs and provides surrogate reward signals. A feedback mechanism iteratively optimizes the prompts for both the target and judge models using policy gradient ascent, refining their cooperation and the quality of synthesized data. This process is repeated in multiple rounds, with the target model being fine-tuned using Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) on the curated preference pairs, enabling iterative self-improvement.
40455a044a750e367e0c225cea74bf078ca73c95.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted across four main applications: natural language generation, vision-language understanding, medical image analysis, and visuo-motor control. Each application uses a different target model (e.g., LLaMA2-7B-chat, LLaVA-1.5 7B, LLAVA-Medv1.5, OpenVLA) and a judge model (often GPT-4o), with domain-specific external tools (such as DuckDuckGo, BLIP-2, Grounded SAM, and specialized medical models) for knowledge extraction. Baselines include the original target models, self-rewarding, meta-rewarding, and other state-of-the-art preference data generation methods. Evaluation is performed on 21 datasets spanning the four application domains, using standard metrics such as accuracy, BLEU, ROUGE-L, METEOR, and task-specific success rates. Ablation studies assess the impact of tool augmentation and feedback mechanisms, and both manual and automated (GPT-4o) evaluations are used to assess data quality and diversity.
40455a044a750e367e0c225cea74bf078ca73c95.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to model preference data synthesis as a cooperative Markov Game between a target model and a tool-augmented judge model, introducing a dynamic feedback mechanism for prompt optimization. It uniquely integrates external tools for knowledge extraction, reducing bias and improving annotation accuracy in the rewarding process. The approach supports multi-domain preference data synthesis, resulting in the Anyprefer-V1 dataset, which demonstrates greater diversity and quality than existing datasets. Experiments show significant improvements in model alignment and self-improvement capabilities across a wide range of tasks and domains.

405f8f5f1c6df1b3343c812832479aad5180b65f.title: Inference-Time Intervention: Eliciting Truthful Answers from a Language Model
405f8f5f1c6df1b3343c812832479aad5180b65f.research_question: How can the truthfulness of large language model (LLM) outputs be enhanced during inference, particularly in cases where the model internally represents correct information but fails to express it in its generated responses?
405f8f5f1c6df1b3343c812832479aad5180b65f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that shifting model activations during inference along directions correlated with truthfulness, as identified in specific attention heads, can significantly increase the likelihood of truthful outputs from LLMs without extensive retraining or annotation requirements.
405f8f5f1c6df1b3343c812832479aad5180b65f.proposed_method: The proposed method, termed Inference-Time Intervention (ITI), involves first identifying a sparse set of attention heads within a transformer-based LLM whose activations are highly predictive of truthfulness, as determined by linear probing on a labeled dataset (e.g., TruthfulQA). For each selected attention head, a 'truthful direction' in the activation space is computed, either via the weight vector of the linear probe or by the vector connecting the means of truthful and false activations. During inference, model activations for these heads are shifted along the identified directions by a tunable strength parameter (alpha), scaled by the standard deviation of activations, at each autoregressive decoding step. This intervention is minimally invasive, computationally inexpensive, and can be applied without modifying model weights or requiring additional training. The method allows for fine-grained control over the trade-off between truthfulness and helpfulness by adjusting the intervention strength and the number of heads intervened.
405f8f5f1c6df1b3343c812832479aad5180b65f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted primarily on the TruthfulQA benchmark, which contains 817 adversarially constructed questions with binary truthfulness labels. LLaMA-7B, Alpaca, and Vicuna models will serve as the main LLMs for evaluation. Baselines will include supervised fine-tuning, few-shot prompting, and instruction fine-tuning, with and without ITI. Evaluation metrics will include the 'true*informative' score (product of truthfulness and informativeness as judged by GPT-3-based classifiers and human annotators), multiple-choice accuracy, cross-entropy loss, and KL divergence between pre- and post-intervention token distributions. Additional experiments will test generalization on Natural Questions, TriviaQA, and MMLU datasets, using closed-book settings and standard evaluation protocols. Ablations will compare different intervention directions, head selection methods, and the impact of training set size and intervention strength.
405f8f5f1c6df1b3343c812832479aad5180b65f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a minimally invasive, data-efficient, and computationally inexpensive method for increasing LLM truthfulness at inference time, requiring only a small set of labeled examples to identify effective intervention directions. Unlike reinforcement learning or weight-editing approaches, ITI operates directly on activations in selected attention heads, enabling fine-grained control and preserving model robustness. The method demonstrates significant improvements in truthfulness on challenging benchmarks and provides evidence that LLMs encode latent representations of truth that can be causally manipulated. The approach also highlights a trade-off between truthfulness and helpfulness, offering a tunable mechanism to balance these objectives.

4067b0c5e8c20e9d7bbd2196a41dba4f0e667498.title: RCCDA: Adaptive Model Updates in the Presence of Concept Drift under a Constrained Resource Budget
4067b0c5e8c20e9d7bbd2196a41dba4f0e667498.research_question: How can a lightweight, resource-aware policy for dynamic model updates be developed that effectively mitigates performance loss due to concept drift in real-time machine learning applications, while theoretically guaranteeing adherence to strict resource constraints?
4067b0c5e8c20e9d7bbd2196a41dba4f0e667498.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a threshold-based, adaptive model update policy leveraging only past loss information and a tunable drift threshold can optimize model performance under concept drift, while provably satisfying strict resource constraints in real-time, resource-limited environments.
4067b0c5e8c20e9d7bbd2196a41dba4f0e667498.proposed_method: A novel adaptive model update policy, RCCDA (Resource-Constrained Concept Drift Adaptation), is proposed to address concept drift in resource-constrained environments. The method formulates model update timing as an optimization problem, minimizing loss due to drift while adhering to a predefined resource budget. The approach leverages the Lyapunov drift-plus-penalty framework to transform the long-term optimization into a series of greedy, per-time-step decisions, balancing immediate performance improvements against resource expenditure. The policy is implemented as a threshold-based rule: at each time step, an update is triggered if the estimated performance gain (computed from historical loss data using a causal estimator) exceeds a dynamically computed resource cost threshold, which incorporates both current and accumulated resource usage. A virtual queue tracks resource debt over time, ensuring that the long-term average resource consumption does not exceed the specified budget. The algorithm is lightweight, requires no explicit drift detection, and is suitable for real-time deployment.
4067b0c5e8c20e9d7bbd2196a41dba4f0e667498.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four domain generalization datasets: PACS, DigitsDG, OfficeHome, and MEMD-ABSA, with concept drift simulated by introducing data from different domains according to various drift schedules (Burst, Step, Wave, Spikes). The model is initially pretrained on a single domain and then deployed in an environment where the data distribution shifts over time. The proposed RCCDA policy will be compared against four baseline update policies: Uniform Random, Periodic, Budget-Increase, and Budget-Threshold. Evaluation metrics include classification accuracy on a holdout dataset that evolves in parallel with the training data, and adherence to a mean update rate constraint (resource budget). The experimental setup includes tracking both model performance and update frequency over 250 time steps, with detailed architecture and parameter settings specified in supplementary materials.
4067b0c5e8c20e9d7bbd2196a41dba4f0e667498.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first theoretically grounded, adaptive threshold-based policy for model updates under concept drift that guarantees strict adherence to resource constraints. The method uniquely integrates a Lyapunov drift-plus-penalty framework with a practical, estimator-based threshold policy, enabling efficient, real-time adaptation without explicit drift detection or prior knowledge of the environment. Analytical convergence and stability bounds are established, and empirical results demonstrate superior accuracy and resource utilization compared to existing baselines across diverse drift scenarios.

40717baa413da976571bf82410ea5542b0be86db.title: Trajectory-guided Control Prediction for End-to-end Autonomous Driving: A Simple yet Strong Baseline
40717baa413da976571bf82410ea5542b0be86db.research_question: How can trajectory-based and direct control-based paradigms for end-to-end autonomous driving be effectively integrated to leverage their complementary strengths and improve overall driving performance in complex urban environments?
40717baa413da976571bf82410ea5542b0be86db.hypothesis: Integrating trajectory planning and direct control prediction into a unified, interactive framework with shared feature representations, temporal reasoning, and adaptive output fusion will outperform existing single-paradigm and naive ensemble baselines in end-to-end autonomous driving tasks, especially under challenging scenarios.
40717baa413da976571bf82410ea5542b0be86db.proposed_method: A unified framework is developed that combines two branches: a trajectory planning branch and a multi-step control prediction branch. The trajectory branch predicts future waypoints using a GRU-based auto-regressive decoder, while the control branch predicts both current and future control actions using a temporal GRU module. The control branch is guided at each step by attention mechanisms informed by the trajectory branch, allowing the model to focus on critical spatial regions relevant for future control. Both branches share a CNN-based image encoder and a measurement encoder for navigation and speed inputs, enabling efficient multi-task learning. The final control output is generated by a situation-based fusion scheme that adaptively combines the outputs from both branches according to driving context, such as whether the vehicle is turning.
40717baa413da976571bf82410ea5542b0be86db.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted in the CARLA urban driving simulator using closed-loop evaluation on challenging scenarios. The dataset comprises 420K samples collected from 8 towns under various weather conditions, with 189K samples used for ablation studies and the full set for leaderboard submission. The proposed method is compared against state-of-the-art baselines on the CARLA Leaderboard, including models using multiple cameras and LiDAR. Evaluation metrics include Driving Score (the product of Route Completion and Infraction Score), Route Completion, and Infraction Score. Ablation studies assess the contribution of each architectural component, and comparisons are made between multi-task learning, ensemble approaches, and the proposed fusion scheme.
40717baa413da976571bf82410ea5542b0be86db.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first unified framework that jointly learns and fuses trajectory planning and direct control prediction for end-to-end autonomous driving. A novel multi-step control prediction branch with temporal reasoning and trajectory-guided attention is designed to enhance temporal consistency and spatial awareness. The situation-based fusion scheme adaptively combines outputs from both paradigms, providing a simple yet strong baseline that achieves state-of-the-art performance using only a monocular camera. The approach demonstrates superior efficiency and effectiveness compared to both single-paradigm and naive ensemble baselines.

407786443475f09b94ef5c5cc0137ec4caabe04c.title: A Lie algebraic theory of barren plateaus for deep parameterized quantum circuits
407786443475f09b94ef5c5cc0137ec4caabe04c.research_question: What are the fundamental algebraic mechanisms underlying the emergence of barren plateaus in deep parameterized quantum circuits, and how can a unified theoretical framework capture the interplay between circuit expressiveness, input state entanglement, measurement operator locality, and noise?
407786443475f09b94ef5c5cc0137ec4caabe04c.hypothesis: The variance of the loss function in deep parameterized quantum circuits can be exactly characterized and unified under a Lie algebraic framework, such that all known sources of barren plateaus—circuit expressiveness, input state entanglement, measurement operator locality, and noise—can be understood as consequences of the structure and properties of the circuit's dynamical Lie algebra.
407786443475f09b94ef5c5cc0137ec4caabe04c.proposed_method: A general Lie algebraic theory will be developed to analyze the variance of the loss function in deep parameterized quantum circuits. The approach will model the quantum circuit as generating a Lie group and associated Lie algebra, and derive explicit expressions for the variance of the loss function by integrating over the Haar measure of the Lie group or its approximate designs. The theory will incorporate the effects of circuit expressiveness (via the dimension of the dynamical Lie algebra), generalized entanglement of the input state (via g-purity), generalized locality of the measurement operator, and various noise models (including SPAM and coherent errors) within a unified mathematical framework. The methodology will include rigorous derivations of variance scaling laws, bounds on the number of circuit layers required for approximate 2-designs, and the impact of noise-induced algebraic decoherence.
407786443475f09b94ef5c5cc0137ec4caabe04c.experiment_details: Experiments will consist of both analytical calculations and numerical simulations. Analytical results will be derived for representative quantum circuits with varying dynamical Lie algebra structures, including universal circuits, circuits with restricted entangling gates, and circuits subject to specific noise models. Simulations will be performed on standard quantum computing datasets and benchmarks, evaluating the variance of the loss function and its gradients as a function of circuit depth, input state entanglement, measurement operator locality, and noise strength. Baselines will include circuits forming exact and approximate 2-designs, as well as circuits with known barren plateau behavior. Evaluation metrics will focus on the scaling of the loss variance with system size, circuit depth, and Lie algebra dimension, as well as comparisons to previously established empirical and theoretical results.
407786443475f09b94ef5c5cc0137ec4caabe04c.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unifying Lie algebraic framework that precisely characterizes all known sources of barren plateaus in deep parameterized quantum circuits. It provides exact variance formulas applicable to arbitrary circuit architectures and noise models, generalizes previous results limited to specific scenarios, and rigorously connects the emergence of barren plateaus to the dimension and structure of the circuit's dynamical Lie algebra. The approach also introduces generalized notions of entanglement and locality aligned with the Lie algebraic structure, and establishes explicit bounds on circuit depth required for approximate 2-designs. This holistic theory enables precise predictions and mitigation strategies for barren plateaus across a wide range of variational quantum algorithms.

407b9e9478ba6bff43ce4b20e8b6cb2b303477d2.title: Planning with Large Language Models for Code Generation
407b9e9478ba6bff43ce4b20e8b6cb2b303477d2.research_question: Can the integration of planning algorithms with large language models improve the quality and controllability of code generation, compared to conventional Transformer decoding methods such as beam search and sampling-based approaches?
407b9e9478ba6bff43ce4b20e8b6cb2b303477d2.hypothesis: Integrating a planning algorithm that leverages test case feedback into the Transformer decoding process will yield higher-quality and more controllable code generation, outperforming standard decoding algorithms in terms of pass rates and strict accuracy on competitive programming benchmarks.
407b9e9478ba6bff43ce4b20e8b6cb2b303477d2.proposed_method: A novel decoding framework, Planning-Guided Transformer Decoding (PG-TD), will be developed to integrate a tree search-based planning algorithm with a pre-trained Transformer for code generation. The code generation process will be formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), where states are concatenations of problem descriptions and partial or complete programs, and actions are tokens from the Transformer’s vocabulary. The tree search algorithm, inspired by Monte-Carlo Tree Search (MCTS), will use the Transformer to suggest top-k likely next tokens and employ beam search to complete partial programs for evaluation. The reward signal for completed programs will be based on their pass rate on public test cases. To improve computational efficiency, mechanisms for caching tree structures and generated sequences between iterations will be implemented, allowing reuse of previously computed results.
407b9e9478ba6bff43ce4b20e8b6cb2b303477d2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on publicly available competitive programming datasets, including APPS and CodeContests, using both GPT-2 and GPT-Neo models fine-tuned on code generation tasks. Baseline methods will include Transformer beam search, sampling+filtering (where generated programs are filtered by test case pass rate), and a Sequential Monte-Carlo guided decoding algorithm. Evaluation metrics will include pass rate and strict accuracy on private test cases, with additional experiments to assess computational efficiency (e.g., number of Transformer generations, computation time) and the effectiveness of caching strategies. The framework’s versatility will be tested by optimizing alternative objectives such as code conciseness and comment density, and by using automatically generated test cases.
407b9e9478ba6bff43ce4b20e8b6cb2b303477d2.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first integration of a tree search-based planning algorithm with large language models for general-purpose code generation, enabling lookahead search guided by test case feedback during decoding. The method is model-agnostic, does not require additional training or fine-tuning of the backbone Transformer, and supports controllable code generation by modifying the reward function. Novel caching mechanisms are designed to share information between the Transformer and the planning algorithm, significantly improving computational efficiency. The framework demonstrates consistent improvements over strong baselines in both code quality and efficiency, and can further enhance Transformer models through fine-tuning with high-quality generated samples.

4085c28b18cdf7e14c2778dd212a87e0e7f2bd72.title: Moderate Dimension Reduction for k-Center Clustering
4085c28b18cdf7e14c2778dd212a87e0e7f2bd72.research_question: Can moderate dimension reduction be achieved for the k-center clustering problem and its variants, such that the optimal value and solutions are preserved within a constant-factor approximation, and can this enable more efficient algorithms in high-dimensional and streaming settings?
4085c28b18cdf7e14c2778dd212a87e0e7f2bd72.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by relaxing the approximation requirement from (1+ε) to a constant factor α > 1, the target dimension for dimension reduction in k-center clustering can be reduced below the classical O(log n) bound, specifically to O(log n + log k)/poly(α), while still preserving the problem's value and solutions within O(α)-approximation. This reduction will enable more efficient algorithms, particularly in streaming and high-dimensional scenarios.
4085c28b18cdf7e14c2778dd212a87e0e7f2bd72.proposed_method: The proposed method develops a moderate dimension reduction framework for k-center clustering and its variants by applying an oblivious random linear map, such as a matrix of iid Gaussians, to project the input data from d dimensions to a lower target dimension t = O(log n + log k)/α^2. The approach leverages the Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma and sub-Gaussian tail properties to ensure that the k-center objective value is preserved within an O(α) factor with high probability. The method introduces the concept of 'witness sets'—small subsets of the data (e.g., constructed via Gonzalez’s algorithm or robust coreset techniques)—to guarantee that the optimal value does not decrease significantly under projection. The framework is extended to handle variants such as k-center with outliers, assignment constraints (including capacitated and fair clustering), and inputs with small doubling dimension, where the target dimension can be further reduced to depend on the doubling dimension instead of d or log n.
4085c28b18cdf7e14c2778dd212a87e0e7f2bd72.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic and real-world datasets of varying sizes and dimensions to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed dimension reduction for k-center and its variants. The methodology will compare the projected data's k-center value and solution quality against the original high-dimensional data, using approximation ratio (O(α)-approximation) as the primary evaluation metric. Baseline comparisons will include the classical Johnson-Lindenstrauss reduction (O(log n) target dimension) and existing streaming algorithms for k-center. The streaming algorithm will be tested in dynamic geometric stream settings, measuring space complexity, approximation quality, and scalability as the dimension and number of clusters increase. Additional experiments will assess the impact of the input's doubling dimension on the achievable reduction and algorithmic efficiency.
4085c28b18cdf7e14c2778dd212a87e0e7f2bd72.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new regime of moderate dimension reduction for k-center clustering, achieving constant-factor approximation with target dimension below the classical O(log n) bound. This is the first framework to provide such guarantees for k-center and its challenging variants (including outliers, capacities, and fairness constraints) in both offline and streaming settings. The approach yields the first streaming algorithm for k-center in high dimensions that uses sublinear space in n, breaking the previous exponential dependence on d. The witness-based analysis and extensions to inputs with small doubling dimension further generalize the applicability and efficiency of dimension reduction for clustering problems.

40a7c44d1cfaa9faf1f731a6f93a889fab5426da.title: Who's Harry Potter? Approximate Unlearning in LLMs
40a7c44d1cfaa9faf1f731a6f93a889fab5426da.research_question: Is it possible to selectively unlearn specific subsets of training data from a large language model (LLM) without retraining the model from scratch, while preserving its general capabilities on unrelated tasks?
40a7c44d1cfaa9faf1f731a6f93a889fab5426da.hypothesis: A targeted fine-tuning procedure, leveraging reinforced models, anchor term replacement, and generation of generic predictions, can effectively erase a model's ability to recall or generate content related to a specific data subset, with minimal impact on overall performance.
40a7c44d1cfaa9faf1f731a6f93a889fab5426da.proposed_method: The proposed method consists of a multi-stage unlearning process for LLMs. First, a reinforced model is created by further training the baseline model on the unlearn target data, enhancing its association with the target content. Next, anchor terms (idiosyncratic entities and expressions unique to the unlearn target) are identified using automated entity extraction (e.g., GPT-4), and a dictionary of generic translations is constructed. Each block of the unlearn target is then processed by replacing anchor terms with their generic counterparts, and next-token predictions are generated using the baseline model. These predictions are combined with reinforcement offsets (differences in logits between baseline and reinforced models) to produce generic prediction labels. Finally, the baseline model is fine-tuned with the original text as input and the generic labels as targets, steering the model away from generating or recalling the unlearned content.
40a7c44d1cfaa9faf1f731a6f93a889fab5426da.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Llama2-7b language model, with the Harry Potter book series and synthetic related content (totaling approximately 3.1M tokens) as the unlearn target. The model will be fine-tuned for about 1 GPU hour (roughly 150 gradient steps) using 4 A100 GPUs. Evaluation will involve both qualitative and quantitative assessments: prompt completions will be compared before and after unlearning to verify the erasure of Harry Potter-related content, and performance will be measured on standard language understanding benchmarks such as Winogrande, Hellaswag, ARC, BoolQ, OpenBookQA, and PIQA to ensure minimal degradation. Next-token probability distributions for key prompts will be tracked over fine-tuning steps to monitor the shift away from target-specific completions.
40a7c44d1cfaa9faf1f731a6f93a889fab5426da.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first practical and effective technique for approximate unlearning in generative language models, enabling targeted removal of specific training data without full retraining. The method innovatively combines reinforced model training, anchor term replacement, and the generation of generic prediction labels to achieve selective forgetting. The approach is computationally efficient, scaling with the size of the unlearned target rather than the entire dataset, and preserves general model capabilities on unrelated tasks.

40c115c43adee6bc7a00ffd444ee9c045360d97d.title: What Happens after SGD Reaches Zero Loss? -A Mathematical Framework
40c115c43adee6bc7a00ffd444ee9c045360d97d.research_question: What are the implicit regularization effects of Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) in overparameterized models, particularly after reaching a manifold of zero-loss minimizers, and how can these effects be mathematically characterized in a general and global framework?
40c115c43adee6bc7a00ffd444ee9c045360d97d.hypothesis: SGD, when operating with sufficiently small learning rates and in the vicinity of a manifold of minimizers, induces an implicit regularization effect that can be globally and precisely characterized by a stochastic differential equation (SDE) whose dynamics are determined by both the loss function and the structure of the gradient noise. This implicit bias leads to improved generalization properties, potentially allowing SGD to escape regimes where gradient descent alone would be suboptimal.
40c115c43adee6bc7a00ffd444ee9c045360d97d.proposed_method: A mathematical framework will be developed to analyze the limiting dynamics of SGD near manifolds of minimizers in overparameterized models. The approach leverages stochastic differential equations (SDEs) with time rescaling to separate fast and slow dynamics, projecting the stochastic process onto the manifold of minimizers using a mapping defined by the gradient flow. The derivatives of this projection mapping will be explicitly related to the derivatives of the loss function, allowing for a closed-form characterization of the limiting diffusion process. The framework accommodates arbitrary noise covariance structures and provides both local and global analyses, extending beyond previous local-only results. Special cases, such as isotropic and label noise, will be analyzed to derive concrete forms of the implicit regularization induced by SGD.
40c115c43adee6bc7a00ffd444ee9c045360d97d.experiment_details: Experiments will focus on overparameterized linear models, particularly those with sparse ground truth vectors. Synthetic datasets will be generated using either i.i.d. Gaussian or Boolean distributions for the input features, with labels constructed via a sparse linear combination. SGD with label noise will be compared to gradient descent (GD) under various initialization regimes, including the kernel regime. Evaluation metrics will include sample complexity required to achieve a given generalization error, convergence to minimizers of specific regularizers (such as weighted l1 norm), and the ability to escape the kernel regime. Theoretical results will be validated by proving convergence properties and sample complexity bounds, with comparisons to existing upper and lower bounds from the literature.
40c115c43adee6bc7a00ffd444ee9c045360d97d.novelty_claims: The proposed framework provides a global and general mathematical characterization of the implicit bias of SGD near manifolds of minimizers, valid for Θ(η−2) steps and allowing for arbitrary noise covariance structures. This approach yields closed-form expressions for the limiting diffusion and regularization effects, surpassing previous works that only offered local analyses or required restrictive assumptions. The method demonstrates that SGD with label noise can achieve minimax-optimal sample complexity for learning sparse overparameterized linear models, even when initialized in regimes where gradient descent would fail. The framework also rigorously proves convergence properties of the limiting flow and the associated regularizer minimization, removing technical assumptions required in prior analyses.

40d92807e463c4786c644b6802a6872f23f92520.title: Flow matching for stochastic linear control systems
40d92807e463c4786c644b6802a6872f23f92520.research_question: How can an initial probability distribution be steered to a target probability distribution through deterministic or stochastic linear control systems, under the constraint that only control inputs can affect the system dynamics?
40d92807e463c4786c644b6802a6872f23f92520.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a flow matching methodology, adapted to respect the control channel constraints of linear control systems, can effectively steer the distribution of system states from a given initial distribution to a specified target distribution, even for non-Gaussian and high-dimensional cases.
40d92807e463c4786c644b6802a6872f23f92520.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed that extends the flow matching methodology to deterministic and stochastic linear control systems, where only control inputs can be manipulated. The approach constructs a probability flow that interpolates between the initial and target distributions using stochastic bridges, and derives a feedback control law characterized as the conditional expectation of the control inputs for these bridges. For special cases such as Gaussian and mixture of Gaussian distributions, explicit analytical forms for the control law are derived. In general cases, the feedback control law is numerically approximated by solving a least-squares regression problem, where the conditional expectation is learned using a neural network (specifically, a 3-block ResNet architecture) trained on samples from the interpolating process.
40d92807e463c4786c644b6802a6872f23f92520.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on several deterministic and stochastic linear control systems, including 2D, 4D, and 8D systems such as double integrators, oscillators, Nyquist-Johnson resistor models, and mass-spring systems. Initial and target distributions include standard Gaussians, mixtures of Gaussians, and uniform distributions on circles. The neural network controller is trained using the ADAM optimizer with a learning rate schedule, batch size 64, and a total of 2000 training samples. The learned controller is evaluated by simulating 2000 independent trajectories using the Euler-Maruyama method. Performance is assessed by comparing the empirical distribution of terminal states to the target distribution using kernel density estimation, Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) with Gaussian kernel, and Wasserstein-2 distance. Baseline comparisons are made to the initial and target distributions, and the scalability of the method is demonstrated in higher-dimensional settings.
40d92807e463c4786c644b6802a6872f23f92520.novelty_claims: The proposed method generalizes flow matching to the setting of linear control systems with control channel constraints, enabling distribution steering for non-Gaussian and high-dimensional cases. It provides explicit analytical solutions for Gaussian and mixture of Gaussian targets, and introduces a practical neural network-based algorithm for approximating the feedback control law in general cases. The approach demonstrates scalability and effectiveness across a range of system parameters and distribution classes, and is applicable to engineering domains where only control actions can manipulate system evolution.

40e6e64eef9721a2e1da27ef59e1aa4306a1ca47.title: Alpha-divergence Variational Inference Meets Importance Weighted Auto-Encoders: Methodology and Asymptotics
40e6e64eef9721a2e1da27ef59e1aa4306a1ca47.research_question: How can variational inference methods be improved by unifying alpha-divergence minimization and importance-weighted autoencoder frameworks, and what are the theoretical and empirical properties of such a unified approach?
40e6e64eef9721a2e1da27ef59e1aa4306a1ca47.hypothesis: A variational inference framework that generalizes the IWAE bound using alpha-divergences (the VR-IWAE bound) will enable unbiased stochastic gradient optimization for a broader class of divergences, provide better theoretical guarantees, and improve signal-to-noise ratio properties for learning both generative and inference networks compared to existing methods.
40e6e64eef9721a2e1da27ef59e1aa4306a1ca47.proposed_method: A new variational bound, the VR-IWAE bound, will be developed to interpolate between the IWAE bound and the Variational Rényi (VR) bound by introducing a tunable alpha parameter. The method will rely on unbiased Monte Carlo estimators for both the bound and its gradients, enabling theoretically sound stochastic optimization for any alpha in [0,1). The approach will provide both reparameterized and doubly-reparameterized gradient estimators, generalizing existing techniques and allowing for improved signal-to-noise ratio in gradient estimates. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to characterize the asymptotic behavior of the bound, the variational gap, and the impact of the alpha parameter in both fixed and high-dimensional regimes.
40e6e64eef9721a2e1da27ef59e1aa4306a1ca47.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic (toy) and real-world datasets to empirically validate the theoretical claims. The VR-IWAE bound will be compared against standard baselines including the Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO), IWAE, and VR bound methods. Evaluation metrics will include the tightness of the variational bound, convergence behavior, and signal-to-noise ratio of gradient estimators. The experimental setup will involve stochastic optimization with mini-batching, and both reparameterized and doubly-reparameterized gradient estimators will be implemented to assess empirical performance across different alpha values and sample sizes.
40e6e64eef9721a2e1da27ef59e1aa4306a1ca47.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the VR-IWAE bound, a novel variational inference objective that unifies and generalizes the IWAE and VR bounds, allowing unbiased gradient-based optimization for a broad class of alpha-divergences. The method provides, for the first time, unbiased estimators for the gradients of alpha-divergence-based bounds (for alpha in [0,1)), overcoming a key theoretical limitation of previous approaches. Theoretical contributions include new asymptotic analyses of the bound and its variational gap, as well as generalized signal-to-noise ratio results and doubly-reparameterized gradient estimators for the VR-IWAE framework. These innovations enable more flexible and theoretically justified variational inference methods with improved empirical properties.

40e8af970329135ec95057d73e239dab805ad128.title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models
40e8af970329135ec95057d73e239dab805ad128.research_question: How can the development of large-scale, multilingual, and multimodal foundation models be advanced to achieve state-of-the-art performance in language understanding, coding, reasoning, tool use, and safety, while scaling efficiently and supporting extended context windows?
40e8af970329135ec95057d73e239dab805ad128.hypothesis: Scaling dense Transformer-based language models with improved data curation, optimized data mixes, advanced training infrastructure, and compositional multimodal integration will yield models that match or exceed the performance of current leading language models across a wide range of tasks, including multilingual, coding, reasoning, and multimodal benchmarks.
40e8af970329135ec95057d73e239dab805ad128.proposed_method: A new herd of dense Transformer-based language models will be developed, ranging up to 405B parameters, supporting context windows up to 128K tokens. The models will be pre-trained on a curated, high-quality, multilingual corpus of approximately 15.6T tokens, with extensive filtering, de-duplication, and domain-specific pipelines for code, math, and multilingual data. Post-training will involve supervised finetuning, rejection sampling, and direct preference optimization to align models with human preferences and enable capabilities such as tool use, coding, and reasoning. Safety mitigations will be incorporated using specialized models for input and output filtering. Multimodal capabilities will be added via compositional integration of image, video, and speech encoders, with adapters trained to align these modalities with the language model, without updating the core language model parameters during adapter training.
40e8af970329135ec95057d73e239dab805ad128.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate the models on a comprehensive suite of benchmarks covering general language understanding (e.g., MMLU, ARC Challenge), coding (e.g., HumanEval), math (e.g., GSM8k, MATH), reasoning (e.g., AGIEval, BFCL), tool use (e.g., Nexus), long-context (e.g., InfiniteBench, NIH/Multi-needle), and multilingual tasks (e.g., MGSM). Comparisons will be made against leading models such as GPT-4, Gemini, Claude, and Mixtral, with results stratified by model size. Evaluation will include both automated metrics (accuracy, log-likelihood) and extensive human evaluations for helpfulness, harmlessness, and safety. Multimodal extensions will be tested on image, video, and speech recognition tasks, using compositional approaches and evaluated for competitive performance with state-of-the-art systems.
40e8af970329135ec95057d73e239dab805ad128.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a flagship 405B parameter dense Transformer model with a 128K token context window, trained on a significantly larger and higher-quality dataset than previous Llama models. It advances data curation, filtering, and domain-specific data pipelines, and employs compute-optimal scaling laws for model and data mix selection. The approach integrates multimodal capabilities via compositional adapters without retraining the language model core, and incorporates robust safety mechanisms through dedicated guard models. The open release of both pre-trained and post-trained models, including safety-optimized variants, is intended to spur further research and responsible innovation.

410d8f0451384237b054b3f06cd8eab1c9f72104.title: Theoretical Benefit and Limitation of Diffusion Language Model
410d8f0451384237b054b3f06cd8eab1c9f72104.research_question: What are the fundamental efficiency and accuracy trade-offs of Masked Diffusion Models (MDMs) for language generation, and under what conditions do they offer advantages or disadvantages compared to auto-regressive models?
410d8f0451384237b054b3f06cd8eab1c9f72104.hypothesis: Masked Diffusion Models can achieve efficient and high-quality text generation under certain evaluation metrics, but may face inherent limitations in tasks requiring high sequence-level correctness.
410d8f0451384237b054b3f06cd8eab1c9f72104.proposed_method: A rigorous theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the efficiency and accuracy of Masked Diffusion Models (MDMs) in language generation. The analysis will focus on two complementary evaluation metrics: Token Error Rate (TER), which measures token-level accuracy and fluency, and Sequence Error Rate (SER), which measures the correctness of entire generated sequences. Theoretical results will be derived using probabilistic models such as n-gram languages and Hidden Markov Models (HMMs), with formal proofs establishing upper and lower bounds on the number of sampling steps required for MDMs to achieve near-optimal performance under each metric. The analysis will also consider the computational complexity of MDM inference compared to auto-regressive models, including the impact of parallel token sampling and factorized denoising architectures.
410d8f0451384237b054b3f06cd8eab1c9f72104.experiment_details: Empirical validation will be conducted using synthetic datasets generated from formal languages, including n-gram models (with n=2,3,4) and HMMs, with sequence lengths ranging from 512 to 2048. For each language type, datasets of 1,000,000 samples will be generated, split into training and validation sets. Transformer-based architectures will be used to implement both MDMs and auto-regressive baselines, trained under identical conditions. Evaluation will be performed using TER (via generative perplexity) and SER (sequence-level accuracy), with systematic variation in the number of sampling steps. Additional experiments will be conducted on real-world benchmarks such as GSM8K and MBPP, comparing large-scale MDMs and auto-regressive models in terms of both efficiency (inference time, number of neural network executions) and accuracy.
410d8f0451384237b054b3f06cd8eab1c9f72104.novelty_claims: This proposal establishes the first comprehensive theoretical foundation for understanding the efficiency-accuracy trade-offs of Masked Diffusion Models in language generation. It rigorously proves that MDMs can achieve near-optimal token-level accuracy with a constant number of sampling steps, independent of sequence length, but require a number of steps scaling linearly with sequence length to achieve low sequence error rates. The work provides practical guidelines for selecting between MDMs and auto-regressive models based on task requirements and evaluation metrics, and systematically validates theoretical predictions with controlled experiments on both synthetic and real-world tasks.

411114f989a3d1083d90afd265103132fee94ebe.title: Mixtral of Experts
411114f989a3d1083d90afd265103132fee94ebe.research_question: How can a sparse mixture-of-experts (SMoE) architecture be leveraged to build large-scale language models that achieve high performance across a range of benchmarks, including mathematics, code generation, multilingual tasks, and long-context retrieval, while maintaining efficiency in terms of active parameter usage and inference cost?
411114f989a3d1083d90afd265103132fee94ebe.hypothesis: A transformer-based language model employing a sparse mixture-of-experts architecture, where each token at each layer is routed through a small subset of specialized feedforward blocks (experts), can outperform or match much larger dense models on a wide range of benchmarks while using significantly fewer active parameters during inference.
411114f989a3d1083d90afd265103132fee94ebe.proposed_method: A new language model architecture will be developed based on the transformer decoder, where the standard feedforward sub-block in each layer is replaced by a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layer. Each MoE layer contains 8 distinct expert feedforward blocks, and for each token at each layer, a router network selects the top 2 experts via a softmax over the top-K logits of a linear projection. The outputs of the selected experts are combined additively, weighted by the router's scores. The expert function will use the SwiGLU activation, and the model will be trained with a context window of up to 32k tokens, using a highly multilingual pretraining corpus. Efficient inference will be enabled through specialized sparse matrix multiplication kernels and expert parallelism, allowing the model to scale in total parameter count while keeping per-token compute cost low.
411114f989a3d1083d90afd265103132fee94ebe.experiment_details: The model will be pretrained on a large, multilingual dataset with a context length of 32,768 tokens. Evaluation will be conducted on a comprehensive suite of benchmarks, including commonsense reasoning (Hellaswag, Winogrande, PIQA, SIQA, OpenbookQA, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, CommonsenseQA), world knowledge (NaturalQuestions, TriviaQA), reading comprehension (BoolQ, QuAC), mathematics (GSM8K, MATH), code generation (HumanEval, MBPP), and aggregated metrics (MMLU, BBH, AGI Eval). Multilingual performance will be assessed on French, German, Spanish, and Italian subsets of ARC-Challenge, Hellaswag, and MMLU. Long-context retrieval will be tested with the passkey retrieval task and perplexity measured on the Proof-Pile dataset. Baselines for comparison will include Llama 2 (7B, 13B, 33B, 70B), GPT-3.5, and Mistral 7B. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, pass@1 for code, perplexity, and human preference scores (e.g., MT-Bench, LMSys leaderboard). Bias and sentiment will be measured using BBQ and BOLD datasets.
411114f989a3d1083d90afd265103132fee94ebe.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a sparse mixture-of-experts transformer architecture that allows for a significant increase in total parameter count while maintaining low active parameter usage per token, enabling efficient inference. The method demonstrates state-of-the-art or superior performance to much larger dense models on a wide range of tasks, including mathematics, code generation, multilingual understanding, and long-context retrieval. The model supports a 32k token context window and is the first open-weights mixture-of-experts model to surpass leading proprietary models on human evaluation benchmarks. Additional contributions include open-sourcing both base and instruction-tuned models and providing efficient inference implementations for the community.

41113411e1748a34bb80f12c761b7af1ed6dbb90.title: What Makes Good Data for Alignment? A Comprehensive Study of Automatic Data Selection in Instruction Tuning
41113411e1748a34bb80f12c761b7af1ed6dbb90.research_question: What are the key characteristics that define high-quality data for aligning large language models through instruction tuning, and how can data be automatically and effectively selected to optimize alignment performance?
41113411e1748a34bb80f12c761b7af1ed6dbb90.hypothesis: Automatically selecting instruction tuning data based on principled measurements of complexity, quality, and diversity will enable large language models to achieve state-of-the-art alignment performance with significantly less data compared to conventional approaches.
