41113411e1748a34bb80f12c761b7af1ed6dbb90.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed to measure instruction tuning data along three critical dimensions: complexity, quality, and diversity. Novel techniques will be introduced to enhance the measurement of these properties in candidate datasets. Based on these measurements, a simple yet effective data selection strategy will be implemented to automatically curate subsets of data optimized for alignment. Selected data will be used to fine-tune large language models (such as LLaMA and Mistral), resulting in a series of models termed DEITA (Data-Efficient Instruction Tuning for Alignment). Further, direct preference optimization (DPO) will be applied to refine alignment using preference data.
41113411e1748a34bb80f12c761b7af1ed6dbb90.experiment_details: Experiments will involve fine-tuning LLaMA and Mistral models using only 6,000 automatically selected instruction tuning samples, with additional DPO training on 10,000 preference samples. The evaluation will be conducted using benchmarks such as MT-Bench and AlpacaEval to assess alignment and instruction-following capabilities. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art open-source alignment models trained on substantially larger datasets (over 10 times more data). Key metrics will include MT-Bench scores and AlpacaEval percentages, with all models and datasets released for reproducibility.
41113411e1748a34bb80f12c761b7af1ed6dbb90.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled, automatic data selection strategy for instruction tuning based on multidimensional data measurement, enabling data-efficient alignment of large language models. It claims to achieve state-of-the-art or competitive results with an order of magnitude less data than existing baselines. The work also provides new tools and datasets for the research community, facilitating more efficient and effective model alignment.

4114668019552c42d1a7624bbf9b8771f961d712.title: Are Large Vision Language Models Good Game Players?
4114668019552c42d1a7624bbf9b8771f961d712.research_question: How can the cognitive and reasoning abilities of large vision-language models (LVLMs) be comprehensively evaluated in structured, dynamic environments beyond conventional benchmarks?
4114668019552c42d1a7624bbf9b8771f961d712.hypothesis: A game-based evaluation framework that leverages structured board and logic games will provide a more comprehensive and objective assessment of LVLMs' perception, reasoning, decision-making, and adversarial skills compared to traditional benchmarks.
4114668019552c42d1a7624bbf9b8771f961d712.proposed_method: A new evaluation framework, LVLM-Playground, will be developed to systematically assess LVLMs using a suite of six diverse games: Tic-Tac-Toe, Reversi, Sudoku, Minesweeper, Gomoku, and Chess. The framework will decompose evaluation into four distinct tasks—Perceiving, Question Answering, Rule Following, and End-to-End Playing—each targeting specific cognitive abilities such as visual perception, reasoning, decision-making, and adversarial play. Game simulators will generate visual and textual inputs for LVLMs, which must interpret game states, answer structured questions, follow explicit rules, and play full games against search-based AI opponents. Automated evaluators will measure performance using objective, rule-based metrics tailored to each task and game, enabling detailed analysis of model strengths and weaknesses across abilities and game complexities.
4114668019552c42d1a7624bbf9b8771f961d712.experiment_details: Experiments will involve both commercial LVLM APIs (e.g., GPT-4o, Gemini-1.5-Pro, Claude-3.5-Sonnet) and open-source models (e.g., Qwen2-VL, DeepSeek-VL, Phi-3-VL, LLaVA-1.6, Intern-VL2), all evaluated under identical conditions. For Perceiving, Question Answering, and Rule Following tasks, 2,000 samples per task will be generated using the game simulator and evaluated offline. The End-to-End Playing task will be assessed through 100 online gameplays per model, with LVLMs competing against search-based AI opponents or solving single-player games. Baselines will include random agents, and performance will be measured using accuracy, number of valid moves, game progression, and final outcomes. Aggregated scores will be computed by weighting task performance according to game difficulty and required abilities, enabling comprehensive comparison across models and tasks.
4114668019552c42d1a7624bbf9b8771f961d712.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a comprehensive, game-based benchmark for LVLMs that addresses key limitations of existing evaluations, such as inadequate assessment of detailed perception, risk of data contamination, ambiguous metrics, inconsistent prompting, and lack of multi-turn reasoning evaluation. By leveraging structured games with clear rules and objective outcomes, the framework enables consistent, reproducible, and fine-grained assessment of LVLMs' multimodal cognitive abilities. The integration of automated evaluation, diverse tasks, and a unified scoring system represents a significant innovation in benchmarking vision-language models.

411b16add23976ffcdf6422f932453f6ebcca119.title: EvoPrompting: Language Models for Code-Level Neural Architecture Search
411b16add23976ffcdf6422f932453f6ebcca119.research_question: Can language models be leveraged as adaptive operators within an evolutionary neural architecture search framework to discover novel and high-performing neural network architectures across diverse machine learning tasks?
411b16add23976ffcdf6422f932453f6ebcca119.hypothesis: Integrating large language models as adaptive mutation and crossover operators, combined with evolutionary prompt engineering and prompt-tuning, will enable the discovery of neural network architectures that outperform those designed by human experts and conventional few-shot prompting, both in terms of accuracy and model size.
411b16add23976ffcdf6422f932453f6ebcca119.proposed_method: A meta-learning framework, termed EVOPROMPTING, will be developed that utilizes a code-pretrained language model as the core mutation and crossover operator within an evolutionary neural architecture search (NAS) algorithm. The method begins by initializing the search with a small set of manually designed seed architectures. In each evolutionary round, the language model generates candidate architectures using few-shot prompts constructed from the most fit models of the previous generation, with prompts explicitly conditioning on desired performance metrics such as validation accuracy and model size. Candidate architectures are trained and evaluated on the target task, and their fitness is computed as a function of validation error and model size. The top-performing architectures are selected as in-context examples for subsequent rounds, and all evaluated architectures are used to prompt-tune the language model, thereby adaptively improving its generation capabilities over time. This iterative process continues for a fixed number of rounds, with the final output being the most fit discovered architectures.
411b16add23976ffcdf6422f932453f6ebcca119.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two main benchmarks: MNIST-1D, a lightweight image classification dataset, and the CLRS Algorithmic Reasoning Benchmark, which covers 30 classical algorithms represented as graph problems. For MNIST-1D, the search will be seeded with four baseline models (GRU, CNN, MLP, and a larger CNN), and models will be trained using the AdamW optimizer for 8000 steps on a single GPU, with fitness evaluated by best validation accuracy. For CLRS, nine seed variants of Triplet-GMPNN models will be used, and each child model will be trained for 2000 steps, with validation accuracy as the primary metric. Baselines for comparison include naive few-shot prompting, EVOPROMPTING without prompt-tuning, and EVOPROMPTING with randomly selected parents. The evaluation will focus on the Pareto frontier of model size versus test error (MNIST-1D) and out-of-distribution accuracy versus model size (CLRS), with additional analysis of sample efficiency and generalization across tasks.
411b16add23976ffcdf6422f932453f6ebcca119.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel use of language models as adaptive evolutionary operators for neural architecture search, replacing hand-crafted search spaces with the language model's code vocabulary and enabling flexible, open-ended search. The method combines evolutionary prompt engineering with prompt-tuning to iteratively improve both the prompt design and the model's generative capabilities. This framework is claimed to discover neural architectures that are both smaller and more accurate than those produced by human experts or standard few-shot prompting, and to generalize across different architecture classes and tasks. The approach is also positioned as broadly applicable to other tasks requiring in-context learning or prompt-tuning beyond neural architecture design.

412e266cddfd87c79087a88ba1e4d11b89a45a13.title: MEGABYTE: Predicting Million-byte Sequences with Multiscale Transformers
412e266cddfd87c79087a88ba1e4d11b89a45a13.research_question: How can autoregressive sequence models be scaled efficiently to handle extremely long byte-level sequences, such as high-resolution images, audio, code, or books, without relying on tokenization or incurring prohibitive computational costs?
412e266cddfd87c79087a88ba1e4d11b89a45a13.hypothesis: A multiscale transformer architecture that segments byte sequences into patches and employs separate global and local models for inter- and intra-patch dependencies will enable efficient, end-to-end differentiable modeling of million-byte sequences, achieving competitive or superior performance to tokenized models at reduced computational cost.
412e266cddfd87c79087a88ba1e4d11b89a45a13.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a multiscale transformer architecture, MEGABYTE, for efficient modeling of long byte sequences. The approach segments input sequences into fixed-size patches, each of which is embedded and processed by a global transformer model to capture inter-patch dependencies. For each patch, a smaller local transformer model is conditioned on the global representation and autoregressively predicts the bytes within the patch, allowing for efficient intra-patch modeling. This design enables sub-quadratic self-attention complexity by decomposing long sequences into shorter ones, and allows the use of large feedforward layers per patch rather than per token, significantly increasing model expressiveness for the same computational budget. Additional enhancements include optional convolutional encoders for translation invariance, cross-patch attention to extend local context, and strided inference to improve prediction quality at patch boundaries.
412e266cddfd87c79087a88ba1e4d11b89a45a13.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of long-sequence datasets, including text (PG-19, Books, Stories, arXiv, Code), images (ImageNet at multiple resolutions up to 640x640), and audio (16 kHz, 16-bit raw audio). All models will be trained under fixed compute and data budgets to ensure fair comparison of architectural efficiency. Baselines will include standard decoder-only transformers and PerceiverAR, with careful hyperparameter tuning to match compute usage. Evaluation metrics will include bits-per-byte (bpb) for density estimation and word-level perplexity for language modeling, as well as generation speed benchmarks. Ablation studies will assess the contributions of global/local models, cross-patch attention, and convolutional encoders. Additional experiments will explore the effects of patch size, model scaling, and inference techniques such as strided and sliding window inference.
412e266cddfd87c79087a88ba1e4d11b89a45a13.novelty_claims: The proposed architecture enables end-to-end, tokenization-free autoregressive modeling of sequences exceeding one million bytes, overcoming the limitations of quadratic self-attention and per-token feedforward costs in standard transformers. By decoupling local and global modeling, the method achieves sub-quadratic complexity, supports much larger and more expressive models for the same compute, and allows for parallel decoding of patches. The approach demonstrates that byte-level models can match or surpass subword models in long-context tasks, establishes state-of-the-art results in byte-level density estimation for images and audio, and provides a scalable, general-purpose solution for long-sequence modeling across modalities.

41331316e9b6cf30546793e0963a8a78d8691c86.title: TimeX++: Learning Time-Series Explanations with Information Bottleneck
41331316e9b6cf30546793e0963a8a78d8691c86.research_question: How can the explainability of deep learning models for time series data be improved to produce interpretable, in-distribution, and label-preserving explanations that avoid trivial solutions and distributional shift issues?
41331316e9b6cf30546793e0963a8a78d8691c86.hypothesis: A time series explanation framework based on a modified information bottleneck objective, which explicitly addresses compactness, informativeness, and distributional shift, will generate higher-quality, more reliable, and in-distribution explanations compared to existing methods.
41331316e9b6cf30546793e0963a8a78d8691c86.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a novel framework, TIMEX++, for generating explanations of time series model predictions. The approach leverages a modified information bottleneck (IB) objective, replacing the standard mutual information terms with tractable surrogates: compactness is enforced via a regularized mask entropy and sparsity constraint, while informativeness is quantified by a label consistency loss that measures the agreement between the original and explanation-embedded instance predictions. The method employs a parametric explanation extractor (e.g., a transformer-based encoder-decoder) to produce stochastic binary masks over the input, and an explanation conditioner (a neural network) to generate explanation-embedded instances that are both in-distribution and label-preserving. The framework includes additional losses to ensure the generated instances are close to the original data distribution (via KL divergence and Euclidean distance to a padded reference) and to promote contiguous, interpretable mask shapes. Training is performed end-to-end, optimizing a weighted sum of the label consistency, mask regularization, distributional alignment, and connectivity losses.
41331316e9b6cf30546793e0963a8a78d8691c86.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world time series datasets. Synthetic datasets (such as FreqShapes, SeqComb-UV, SeqComb-MV, and LowVar) with known ground-truth explanations will be used to quantitatively assess explanation quality using metrics such as area under precision (AUP), area under recall (AUR), and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC). Real-world datasets (including ECG, PAM, Epilepsy, Boiler, Wafer, Freezer, and a Florida water dataset) will be used for further evaluation, with occlusion experiments measuring the impact of masking salient features on model performance (e.g., AUROC drop). Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art time series explainers such as Integrated Gradients, Dynamask, WinIT, CoRTX, SGT+GRAD, and TIMEX. Evaluation will also include statistical tests (e.g., Friedman test) for significance, and distributional similarity metrics (KDE log-likelihood, KL divergence, MMD) to verify that explanation instances remain in-distribution.
41331316e9b6cf30546793e0963a8a78d8691c86.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a theoretically grounded, information-theoretic objective for time series explanation that explicitly addresses the shortcomings of prior IB-based methods, such as the signaling issue and distributional shift. TIMEX++ is the first to combine a parametric explanation conditioner with a modified IB objective to generate explanation-embedded instances that are both in-distribution and label-preserving, without requiring white-box access to the model. The approach provides a unified, end-to-end trainable solution that outperforms existing baselines in both explanation quality and distributional fidelity, as demonstrated on a diverse set of synthetic and real-world datasets.

41a3c41ba1912e1384849e6898c241af89cc4a11.title: DEPN: Detecting and Editing Privacy Neurons in Pretrained Language Models
41a3c41ba1912e1384849e6898c241af89cc4a11.research_question: How can privacy risks associated with memorization and regurgitation of private information in pretrained language models be effectively mitigated, particularly in the post-processing stage, without significantly degrading model performance?
41a3c41ba1912e1384849e6898c241af89cc4a11.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that private information is encoded in specific neurons within pretrained language models, and that detecting and editing these 'privacy neurons' can significantly reduce privacy leakage risks while maintaining model utility.
41a3c41ba1912e1384849e6898c241af89cc4a11.proposed_method: A novel framework, DEPN (Detect and Edit Privacy Neurons), will be developed to identify and mitigate privacy risks in pretrained language models. The approach consists of three main components: (1) a privacy neuron detector that uses gradient integration to compute privacy attribution scores for each neuron, identifying those most responsible for private information leakage; (2) a privacy neuron editor that erases memorized private information by setting the activations of the top-ranked privacy neurons to zero; and (3) a privacy neuron aggregator that enables batch processing by aggregating privacy attribution scores across multiple input sequences and selecting neurons for editing based on a voting mechanism. The method is designed to be efficient and applicable in the post-processing stage, requiring minimal computational overhead compared to retraining or differential privacy approaches.
41a3c41ba1912e1384849e6898c241af89cc4a11.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Enron email dataset, which contains real-world private information such as names and phone numbers. The BERT-base pretrained language model will serve as the primary testbed, with additional experiments on BERT-small and BERT-large to assess scalability. Baseline comparisons will include models trained with and without private data, as well as models trained with differential privacy (DP-SGD). Evaluation metrics will include exposure (for phone numbers), mean reciprocal rank (MRR, for names), and perplexity (PPL, for random private texts), alongside validation perplexity to assess model utility. The experimental setup will also analyze the impact of model size, training epochs, batch size, and prompt variation on privacy leakage and the effectiveness of neuron editing.
41a3c41ba1912e1384849e6898c241af89cc4a11.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces, for the first time, a model editing approach specifically tailored for privacy protection in pretrained language models. It pioneers the detection and targeted editing of privacy neurons using gradient-based attribution, enabling efficient post-hoc mitigation of privacy risks without retraining. The framework supports batch processing for scalable privacy editing and demonstrates robustness to prompt variation. Additionally, the research empirically explores the relationship between model memorization, privacy neuron distribution, and privacy leakage, offering new insights into the mechanisms of privacy risk in large language models.

41a66997ce0a366bba3becf7c3f37c9aebb13fbd.title: Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers for High-Resolution Image Synthesis
41a66997ce0a366bba3becf7c3f37c9aebb13fbd.research_question: How can rectified flow models and transformer-based architectures be scaled and improved to advance high-resolution text-to-image synthesis, achieving superior image quality, prompt fidelity, and efficiency compared to current state-of-the-art generative models?
41a66997ce0a366bba3becf7c3f37c9aebb13fbd.hypothesis: Rectified flow models, when combined with tailored noise sampling strategies and a novel multimodal transformer architecture that enables bidirectional information flow between text and image tokens, will outperform existing diffusion-based and transformer-based approaches in high-resolution text-to-image synthesis in terms of both automatic metrics and human preference ratings.
41a66997ce0a366bba3becf7c3f37c9aebb13fbd.proposed_method: A new generative modeling framework is developed based on rectified flow, which connects data and noise via straight-line trajectories, and is enhanced by introducing re-weighted noise scale sampling to emphasize perceptually relevant timesteps. The method employs a novel transformer-based architecture (MM-DiT) that uses separate, learnable streams for text and image tokens, enabling bidirectional attention and improved cross-modal comprehension. The architecture concatenates patch-embedded image latents and text representations, processes them through modality-specific transformer blocks, and employs RMS normalization of Q and K in attention layers to stabilize large-scale training. Additionally, the approach leverages improved autoencoders with increased latent dimensionality, and augments training captions with a 50/50 mix of synthetic and original annotations to enhance prompt fidelity. Resolution-dependent timestep shifting and adaptive positional encodings are incorporated to enable efficient scaling to high-resolution and variable aspect ratio outputs.
41a66997ce0a366bba3becf7c3f37c9aebb13fbd.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on large-scale datasets including ImageNet, CC12M, and COCO-2014, with models trained in the latent space of high-capacity autoencoders (16-channel, downsampling factor 8). The proposed method is compared against multiple baselines, including LDM-Linear, EDM, DiT, CrossDiT, UViT, and state-of-the-art open and closed models such as SDXL, SDXL-Turbo, Pixart-α, and DALL-E 3. Evaluation metrics include FID (both pixel and CLIP feature space), CLIP score, SSIM, PSNR, Perceptual Similarity, T2I-CompBench, GenEval, and extensive human preference studies on prompt fidelity, visual quality, and typography. Ablation studies assess the impact of noise sampling strategies, autoencoder capacity, caption augmentation, and architectural variants. Training is performed at both low (256x256) and high (up to 1024x1024) resolutions, with mixed-precision and full-precision regimes, and with careful data filtering and deduplication to ensure safe and efficient pretraining.
41a66997ce0a366bba3becf7c3f37c9aebb13fbd.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces several innovations: (1) a large-scale, systematic study and optimization of rectified flow formulations for text-to-image synthesis, including novel noise sampling strategies that bias training towards perceptually important timesteps; (2) a multimodal transformer architecture (MM-DiT) with separate, learnable streams for text and image tokens, enabling bidirectional attention and superior cross-modal integration; (3) improved autoencoder backbones with higher latent dimensionality for enhanced reconstruction fidelity; (4) the use of synthetic caption augmentation to improve prompt fidelity at scale; (5) resolution-dependent timestep shifting and adaptive positional encodings for efficient high-resolution and variable aspect ratio synthesis; and (6) demonstration of predictable scaling trends and state-of-the-art performance on both automatic metrics and human evaluations, surpassing leading open and closed text-to-image models.

41ba8127b73abd32051a89764cb976095b1dee94.title: RDT-1B: a Diffusion Foundation Model for Bimanual Manipulation
41ba8127b73abd32051a89764cb976095b1dee94.research_question: How can a scalable and generalizable foundation model be developed for bimanual robotic manipulation that effectively handles the complexity of coordinating two robot arms, multi-modal action distributions, and data scarcity, while enabling robust generalization to unseen objects, scenes, and instructions?
41ba8127b73abd32051a89764cb976095b1dee94.hypothesis: A diffusion-based Transformer model, pre-trained on large-scale heterogeneous multi-robot datasets and equipped with a physically interpretable unified action space, will enable superior generalization, dexterity, and instruction following in bimanual manipulation tasks, even under data scarcity and diverse robot embodiments.
41ba8127b73abd32051a89764cb976095b1dee94.proposed_method: A novel diffusion-based Transformer architecture, termed Robotics Diffusion Transformer (RDT), will be developed for language-conditioned visuomotor policy learning in bimanual manipulation. The method will leverage a scalable Transformer backbone with key modifications: QKNorm and RMSNorm for stable training on physical data, a nonlinear MLP decoder to capture nonlinear robot dynamics, and alternating condition injection (ACI) to balance the integration of image and language modalities. Multi-modal inputs (proprioception, action chunks, control frequency, images, and language instructions) will be encoded into a unified latent space using MLPs (with Fourier features), a fixed pre-trained vision encoder (SigLIP), and a fixed pre-trained language model (T5-XXL). A physically interpretable unified action space will be designed to map diverse robot actions into a common format, preserving physical meaning and enabling effective cross-robot pre-training. The model will be trained to predict action chunks via conditional diffusion modeling, supporting both temporal consistency and multi-modality in actions.
41ba8127b73abd32051a89764cb976095b1dee94.experiment_details: Experiments will involve pre-training the model on the largest available collection of multi-robot datasets (46 datasets, over 1 million trajectories, 21TB of data), followed by fine-tuning on a self-collected, comprehensive bimanual dataset (6,000+ trajectories, 300+ tasks, 100+ objects, 15+ rooms). Evaluation will be conducted on the ALOHA dual-arm robot across seven challenging tasks, measuring zero-shot and few-shot generalization to unseen objects, scenes, instructions, and skills, as well as dexterous manipulation. Baselines will include state-of-the-art models such as ACT (VAE-based), OpenVLA (discretization-based, 7B parameters), and Octo (diffusion-based, 93M parameters). Success rate will be the primary evaluation metric, with ablation studies examining the impact of model size, pre-training, and diffusion modeling. Real-time inference will be achieved using DPM-Solver++ for efficient diffusion sampling.
41ba8127b73abd32051a89764cb976095b1dee94.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the largest diffusion-based foundation model for robotic manipulation to date (1.2B parameters), a physically interpretable unified action space for cross-robot learning, and a scalable Transformer architecture with task-specific modifications for robotic data. The method uniquely combines large-scale multi-robot pre-training, comprehensive bimanual fine-tuning, and advanced diffusion modeling to achieve state-of-the-art generalization, instruction following, and dexterity in bimanual manipulation. The approach demonstrates significant improvements over existing baselines in zero-shot and few-shot learning, as well as in handling complex, multi-modal action distributions and heterogeneous data.

41c8a2a6ca140eeb9da52cb852e49d5ce7ffa162.title: Differentially Private Decoupled Graph Convolutions for Multigranular Topology Protection
41c8a2a6ca140eeb9da52cb852e49d5ce7ffa162.research_question: How can graph neural network (GNN) models be designed to provide rigorous, multigranular differential privacy guarantees for both node attributes and graph topology, while maintaining high utility in node classification tasks on graph-structured data?
41c8a2a6ca140eeb9da52cb852e49d5ce7ffa162.hypothesis: A decoupled graph convolution framework, together with a generalized notion of graph dataset adjacency (k-neighbor-level), enables more flexible and efficient trade-offs between privacy and utility in GNNs, outperforming standard DP-GNN approaches under various privacy requirements.
41c8a2a6ca140eeb9da52cb852e49d5ce7ffa162.proposed_method: A new framework, termed Graph Differential Privacy (GDP), will be developed to provide formal privacy guarantees for both model parameters and node-level predictions in graph learning. The approach introduces a novel k-neighbor-level adjacency definition, allowing practitioners to specify the granularity of privacy protection for graph topology independently of node attribute privacy. Building on this, a Differentially Private Decoupled Graph Convolution (DPDGC) method will be constructed, which separates the aggregation of node features and topology information to reduce sensitivity and required noise for differential privacy. The DPDGC model will employ a DP-optimized embedding module with row-normalized weights and additive Gaussian noise, followed by end-to-end training of downstream modules using both node features and privatized embeddings. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to establish GDP guarantees and to quantify the privacy-utility trade-offs enabled by the decoupled design.
41c8a2a6ca140eeb9da52cb852e49d5ce7ffa162.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on seven benchmark node classification datasets, including Facebook, Pubmed, Cora, Computers, Photo, Squirrel, and Chameleon, as well as synthetic datasets generated via contextual stochastic block models (cSBM). Various privacy settings will be evaluated, including non-private, edge-level, k-neighbor-level (for k = 1, 5, 25), and node-level GDP. Baseline methods will include DP-MLP, standard DP-GNNs such as GAP, RandEdge+SAGE, and DP-SAGE. All methods will be tuned to satisfy the same privacy budget (ε, δ) for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics will focus on node classification accuracy and the trade-off between privacy and utility under different privacy granularities. Graphs will be subsampled as needed to enforce bounded degree constraints for relevant baselines.
41c8a2a6ca140eeb9da52cb852e49d5ce7ffa162.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first formal notion of Graph Differential Privacy (GDP) that provides multigranular privacy guarantees for both node attributes and graph topology in GNNs. The k-neighbor-level adjacency definition generalizes and unifies prior edge- and node-level adjacency concepts, enabling fine-grained privacy-utility trade-offs. The DPDGC model is claimed to be the first to provably achieve GDP guarantees while decoupling graph convolutions, resulting in lower sensitivity and noise requirements that are independent of maximum node degree for k-neighbor privacy. The approach is expected to outperform existing DP-GNNs in terms of utility under the same privacy guarantees, particularly in settings where graph topology privacy requirements vary.

41e0e73cbacc7cf96f051dfbd0ce64ae1ad02b81.title: HyperDiffusion: Generating Implicit Neural Fields with Weight-Space Diffusion
41e0e73cbacc7cf96f051dfbd0ce64ae1ad02b81.research_question: How can high-fidelity, dimension-agnostic generative modeling of implicit neural fields be achieved directly in the space of neural network weights, enabling synthesis of novel 3D shapes and 4D animation sequences without reliance on explicit representations or latent encoders/decoders?
41e0e73cbacc7cf96f051dfbd0ce64ae1ad02b81.hypothesis: Modeling the weight space of overfitted implicit neural field MLPs with a diffusion process enables high-quality, diverse, and novel generative synthesis of 3D and 4D surfaces, outperforming explicit or voxel-based generative methods in fidelity and flexibility.
41e0e73cbacc7cf96f051dfbd0ce64ae1ad02b81.proposed_method: A two-phase approach is proposed. First, for each training instance (3D shape or 4D animation), an MLP is overfitted to represent the instance as an implicit neural field, with weights optimized to minimize binary cross-entropy loss on occupancy queries. These MLPs share architecture but are independently optimized, with a consistent weight initialization strategy to encourage smoothness in the resulting weight space. The optimized MLP weights are then flattened into 1D vectors and used as training data for a diffusion model. The diffusion process is modeled using a transformer-based denoising network, which operates directly on the flattened MLP weight vectors, predicting denoised weights from noisy inputs. The diffusion model is trained with a mean squared error loss between predicted and ground truth MLP weights. After training, new neural fields are synthesized by sampling random noise and applying the reverse diffusion process to generate new MLP weights, which can be decoded into 3D or 4D surfaces.
41e0e73cbacc7cf96f051dfbd0ce64ae1ad02b81.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 3D shape categories (car, chair, airplane) from the ShapeNet dataset and 4D animation sequences from the DeformingThings4D dataset. For each instance, MLPs are overfitted and their weights are used to train the diffusion model. Baselines include state-of-the-art point cloud diffusion models (PVD, DPC) and a voxel-based diffusion baseline for both 3D and 4D generation. Evaluation metrics include Minimum Matching Distance (MMD), Coverage (COV), 1-Nearest-Neighbor Accuracy (1-NNA), and Frechet PointNet++ Distance (FPD) for perceptual quality. Meshes are extracted from synthesized MLPs using Marching Cubes, and point clouds are sampled for quantitative evaluation. Ablations will be performed on MLP weight initialization and positional encoding. Experiments are run with consistent train/val/test splits and quantitative and qualitative comparisons are provided.
41e0e73cbacc7cf96f051dfbd0ce64ae1ad02b81.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first generative modeling framework that operates directly in the weight space of overfitted implicit neural field MLPs via diffusion modeling, enabling dimension-agnostic synthesis of 3D and 4D surfaces. The method eliminates the need for explicit representations or latent encoders/decoders, leverages the compactness and fidelity of neural fields, and demonstrates superior perceptual quality and generalization to novel shapes compared to voxel-based and point cloud diffusion baselines. The approach is flexible, supports arbitrary data dimensionality, and achieves state-of-the-art results in high-fidelity surface synthesis.

41f2432db166caca70386d5ded997690a0597c52.title: Data curation via joint example selection further accelerates multimodal learning
41f2432db166caca70386d5ded997690a0597c52.research_question: Can joint selection of data batches, rather than independent example selection, accelerate and improve the efficiency of large-scale multimodal contrastive pretraining, and how can model-based criteria be leveraged to optimize this process?
41f2432db166caca70386d5ded997690a0597c52.hypothesis: Joint selection of data batches based on model-based learnability criteria will yield more learnable and effective training batches, significantly accelerating multimodal pretraining and improving data efficiency compared to independent example selection. Leveraging pretrained reference models for batch scoring and employing efficient model approximation techniques will further enhance training efficiency and scalability.
41f2432db166caca70386d5ded997690a0597c52.proposed_method: A novel data curation framework is proposed that performs joint selection of training batches (JEST) for multimodal contrastive learning. The method scores candidate sub-batches from large super-batches using model-based criteria, primarily the difference in loss between a learner model and a pretrained reference model (learnability). Batch selection is performed via a sequential sampling approach inspired by blocked Gibbs sampling, where batches are constructed chunk by chunk, each time sampling examples in proportion to their conditional learnability given the current batch. To reduce computational overhead, efficient scoring is achieved by approximating the model's image encoder using multi-resolution techniques (FlexiViT), allowing low-resolution scoring during selection and full-resolution training for a subset of data. Multi-resolution training is incorporated by splitting each batch and processing halves at different resolutions, thus balancing computational efficiency and model performance.
41f2432db166caca70386d5ded997690a0597c52.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the WebLI dataset, using both large-scale (billion-scale) and strongly curated (100M–600M scale) subsets for training and reference models. The proposed methods (JEST, Flexi-JEST, JEST++, Flexi-JEST++) are compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as SigLIP, CLIP, EVA-CLIP, and OpenCLIP, using evaluation metrics including zero-shot and 10-shot ImageNet classification, and COCO image-to-text and text-to-image retrieval. Filtering ratios and batch sizes are varied to assess the impact on training efficiency and performance. Additional ablations explore the effects of different curation strategies, reference model qualities, and multi-resolution training configurations. FLOPs per iteration and total computation are measured to quantify efficiency gains, and experiments are also performed on the LAION-2B dataset to test generalizability.
41f2432db166caca70386d5ded997690a0597c52.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first tractable and scalable algorithm for joint example selection at the batch level tailored to multimodal contrastive learning objectives. It demonstrates that batch-level selection based on learnability outperforms independent example selection, leading to up to 13× fewer training iterations and 10× less computation to reach state-of-the-art performance. The method leverages recent advances in model approximation for efficient batch scoring, and shows that small, well-curated reference datasets can bootstrap the curation of much larger, uncurated datasets, exposing data curation as a new axis in neural scaling laws. The framework also simplifies data curation requirements by making pre-filtering of large datasets unnecessary for strong performance.

420f2966c574351ebc2eca50efcf5060d34a984e.title: Retrieval is Not Enough: Enhancing RAG Reasoning through Test-Time Critique and Optimization
420f2966c574351ebc2eca50efcf5060d34a984e.research_question: How can the reasoning process in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems be dynamically aligned with retrieved evidence to improve factual consistency, robustness, and generalization across diverse and noisy retrieval scenarios?
420f2966c574351ebc2eca50efcf5060d34a984e.hypothesis: Introducing an iterative, critique-driven alignment framework that leverages a dedicated, retrieval-augmented Critic Language Model (CLM) trained via contrastive critique synthesis will significantly improve the reasoning fidelity, factual reliability, and robustness of RAG systems compared to existing static or self-refinement methods.
420f2966c574351ebc2eca50efcf5060d34a984e.proposed_method: A novel framework, ALIGNRAG, is proposed to address reasoning misalignment in RAG by iteratively refining the model's reasoning process at test time. The core of the method is Critique-Driven Alignment (CDA), which employs a Critic Language Model (CLM) trained to generate evidence-grounded critiques that identify and correct reasoning steps misaligned with retrieved evidence. Training data for the CLM is constructed using contrastive critique synthesis, where expert and weak model responses are contrasted to synthesize targeted critiques, ensuring the CLM is sensitive to evidential fidelity and mitigates self-bias. During inference, the RAG system generates an initial answer, which is then iteratively critiqued and revised based on the CLM's feedback, with each iteration aiming to bring the reasoning closer to the retrieved evidence. An autonomous variant, ALIGNRAG-AUTO, is also proposed, where the CLM is trained to predict a stopping signal ([Good] token) to dynamically terminate the refinement process when sufficient alignment is achieved, enhancing efficiency and usability.
420f2966c574351ebc2eca50efcf5060d34a984e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using three instruction-tuned language model backbones: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, and LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct. The CLM will be fine-tuned using LoRA for parameter-efficient training, with strong and weak LLMs generating expert and unexpected responses, respectively. The training dataset will consist of 10,000 instances sampled from five QA benchmarks: PopQA, TriviaQA, NaturalQuestions, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and ASQA. Evaluation will be performed on these five in-domain datasets as well as two out-of-distribution benchmarks (HotpotQA and SQuAD). Baselines for comparison will include Chain-of-Thought prompting, Vanilla RAG, RetRobust, InstructRAG, Self-RAG, and Self-Refine. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy for most tasks and strict exact match (str-em) for ASQA, with additional analysis on robustness under noisy retrieval and generalization to OOD domains. Ablation studies will isolate the contributions of the CLM and contrastive critique synthesis.
420f2966c574351ebc2eca50efcf5060d34a984e.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the concept of reasoning misalignment as a fundamental, underexplored failure mode in RAG systems and reconceptualizes RAG as Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning. It presents Critique-Driven Alignment (CDA), a novel test-time iterative framework that uses a dedicated, retrieval-augmented CLM trained via contrastive critique synthesis, explicitly mitigating self-bias and enhancing evidence sensitivity. The autonomous ALIGNRAG-AUTO variant enables dynamic, domain-general refinement without manual iteration tuning. The framework is designed as a plug-and-play module compatible with existing RAG architectures, requiring no architectural modifications or task-specific fine-tuning. Extensive empirical validation demonstrates state-of-the-art performance, superior robustness under both informative and noisy retrieval, and strong generalization across diverse tasks and domains.

4211000a615716f4e2109efa5a9416102e3c2afa.title: Dual Process Learning: Controlling Use of In-Context vs. In-Weights Strategies with Weight Forgetting
4211000a615716f4e2109efa5a9416102e3c2afa.research_question: How can language models be trained to flexibly and persistently deploy both in-context learning (ICL) and in-weights learning (IWL) strategies, particularly enabling generalization to rare or unseen tokens as well as memorization of frequent tokens, across both synthetic and naturalistic tasks?
4211000a615716f4e2109efa5a9416102e3c2afa.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that targeted interventions in the training process, such as active forgetting, temporary forgetting, and probabilistic temporary forgetting, can be used to control and maintain the balance between in-context and in-weights learning strategies in language models, thereby enabling dual process learning that generalizes to unseen tokens while retaining memorized knowledge for frequent tokens.
4211000a615716f4e2109efa5a9416102e3c2afa.proposed_method: A novel training methodology will be developed that introduces and systematically studies the effects of active forgetting, temporary forgetting, and probabilistic temporary forgetting on language models. Active forgetting involves periodically re-initializing the embedding matrix during training, forcing the model to rely on in-context strategies rather than memorized embeddings. Temporary forgetting modifies this by applying active forgetting only for an initial segment of training, after which embeddings are allowed to train normally, enabling the model to memorize frequent tokens while maintaining structural in-context learning for rare or unseen tokens. Probabilistic temporary forgetting will be explored during fine-tuning by randomly replacing a subset of token embeddings with random vectors during each training step, then restoring the original embeddings after the update, to induce structural ICL in pretrained models. These interventions will be implemented in both masked and autoregressive language models, and the impact on the persistence and coexistence of ICL and IWL strategies will be evaluated.
4211000a615716f4e2109efa5a9416102e3c2afa.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and naturalistic tasks. For naturalistic evaluation, part-of-speech (POS) probing tasks will be performed using BERT-style models trained on the Penn Treebank 3 dataset, with evaluation datasets constructed to distinguish between ICL and IWL strategies (including head, tail, switch, and random token conditions). Synthetic tasks will involve masked language modeling with controlled vocabulary distributions (e.g., Zipfian and uniform) and ambiguity parameters, using custom datasets to isolate structural and conditional ICL. Baseline comparisons will include vanilla training and L2 regularization. Evaluation metrics will include probe accuracy on various token conditions (e.g., random, tail, head), with performance tracked across training checkpoints and intervention regimes. Additional experiments will replicate findings in autoregressive transformers and apply probabilistic temporary forgetting during GPT-2 fine-tuning on logical reasoning tasks using Wikitext, measuring accuracy on both seen and unseen tokens.
4211000a615716f4e2109efa5a9416102e3c2afa.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the concept of structural in-context learning (ICL) and demonstrates its transience in language models. It pioneers the use of active forgetting and, more importantly, develops temporary forgetting and probabilistic temporary forgetting as methods to induce and control dual process learning—allowing models to deploy both in-context and in-weights strategies within a single model. The approach enables persistent structural ICL for rare or unseen tokens while preserving memorization for frequent tokens, overcoming limitations of prior regularization-based methods. This framework is claimed to generalize across data distributions and model architectures, and to be applicable both during pretraining and fine-tuning, representing a significant advancement in the controllable deployment of learning strategies in language models.

42111f25167598b2bdce5af64978505c863dd913.title: Mitigating over-Exploration in Latent Space Optimization using les
42111f25167598b2bdce5af64978505c863dd913.research_question: How can over-exploration in latent space optimization for black-box discrete optimization problems be mitigated to improve the validity and quality of generated solutions across diverse generative models and structured sequence spaces?
42111f25167598b2bdce5af64978505c863dd913.hypothesis: Introducing a differentiable, decoder-based latent exploration score (LES) as a constraint in latent space optimization will reduce over-exploration, resulting in a higher proportion of valid and high-quality solutions without sacrificing objective performance, and will be computationally efficient and robust across various VAE architectures and tasks.
42111f25167598b2bdce5af64978505c863dd913.proposed_method: A novel Latent Exploration Score (LES) will be derived and incorporated as a regularization term in latent space optimization (LSO) for discrete black-box optimization tasks. LES is computed analytically from the decoder of a pre-trained Variational Autoencoder (VAE), leveraging the continuous piecewise affine (CPA) representation of neural networks to estimate the density of latent vectors under the decoder transformation. The LES score will be added as a constraint to the acquisition function during Bayesian Optimization in the latent space, encouraging exploration in regions likely to decode to valid outputs. The method requires only a pre-trained decoder, does not need access to training data, and is fully differentiable, enabling efficient gradient-based optimization. A numerically stable optimization procedure will be developed to balance the acquisition function and the LES constraint, normalizing gradients to avoid instability and tuning the regularization parameter λ for different tasks.
42111f25167598b2bdce5af64978505c863dd913.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five benchmark LSO tasks using twenty-two VAE models with varying decoder architectures (GRU, LSTM, Transformer) and latent dimensions. Datasets include arithmetic expressions, SMILES strings (ZINC250k), and SELFIES molecular representations, with both custom-trained and pre-trained VAEs. The evaluation will compare LES-constrained LSO against six baselines: unconstrained LSO, prior density regularization, likelihood-based regularization, LSO with L-BFGS, TuRBO trust region methods, and Uncertainty Censoring. Metrics will include the percentage of valid solutions, objective values (e.g., mean squared error for expressions, predicted logP for molecules, Guacamol MPO scores), AUROC for validity classification, and computational efficiency (wall clock time for score computation). Each optimization run will use realistic budgets (e.g., 500-1500 candidates, batch size 20), and results will be averaged over 10 independent runs. Hyperparameters such as step size and λ will be calibrated per dataset, and ablation studies will be performed.
42111f25167598b2bdce5af64978505c863dd913.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces LES, a differentiable, decoder-based score that identifies valid regions in latent space without requiring additional training, architectural changes, or access to training data. LES is shown to be faster to compute than existing uncertainty-based regularizers and more robust across diverse VAE architectures and sequence types. The approach enables seamless integration into existing LSO pipelines, consistently improves the validity and quality of solutions, and outperforms multiple state-of-the-art baselines in both validity and objective value across a wide range of tasks and models.

4217d99affbeab7f9fff8d13e3cf15b40e1f794e.title: RoMa: Robust Dense Feature Matching
4217d99affbeab7f9fff8d13e3cf15b40e1f794e.research_question: How can dense feature matching between images be made robust to extreme real-world changes in scale, illumination, viewpoint, and texture, while maintaining precise localization of correspondences?
4217d99affbeab7f9fff8d13e3cf15b40e1f794e.hypothesis: Integrating frozen pretrained features from a foundation model for coarse matching with specialized convolutional fine features, combined with a tailored transformer-based match decoder and improved loss formulations, will significantly improve the robustness and accuracy of dense feature matching under challenging conditions.
4217d99affbeab7f9fff8d13e3cf15b40e1f794e.proposed_method: A robust dense feature matching framework is proposed that leverages a frozen foundation model (DINOv2) to extract coarse, highly robust features, which are then combined with specialized convolutional neural network (ConvNet) fine features to form a feature pyramid capable of precise localization. A transformer-based match decoder is introduced, which predicts anchor probabilities (regression-by-classification) instead of directly regressing coordinates, enabling the model to represent multimodal matching distributions at coarse scales. For the refinement stage, a robust regression loss (generalized Charbonnier) is employed, as the conditional distribution is expected to be unimodal locally. The architecture decouples the coarse and fine feature encoders, allowing each to specialize for their respective tasks, and employs a sequence of refiners that iteratively improve the warp estimation at finer resolutions.
4217d99affbeab7f9fff8d13e3cf15b40e1f794e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of challenging benchmarks, including MegaDepth, ScanNet, IMC2022, WxBS, MegaDepth-8-Scenes, and InLoc. The evaluation will use metrics such as mean Average Accuracy (mAA), Area Under Curve (AUC) for pose estimation at various angular thresholds, and percentage of correct keypoints (PCK) at different pixel error thresholds. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art dense and sparse feature matching methods such as DKM, LoFTR, ASpanFormer, SuperGlue, and others. Ablation studies will systematically assess the impact of each component, including feature encoder choices, match decoder architectures, and loss functions. The experimental setup will use supervised correspondences derived from multi-view stereo or RGB-D data, with models trained on MegaDepth and ScanNet training splits and evaluated at resolutions up to 560x560 pixels.
4217d99affbeab7f9fff8d13e3cf15b40e1f794e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces several innovations: (1) the integration of frozen foundation model features (DINOv2) for coarse matching, which enhances robustness and reduces overfitting; (2) the combination of these robust coarse features with specialized ConvNet fine features to achieve both robustness and precise localization; (3) a transformer-based match decoder that predicts anchor probabilities, enabling effective modeling of multimodal distributions at coarse scales; and (4) a theoretically motivated loss formulation, using regression-by-classification for coarse matching and robust regression for refinement. Extensive experiments demonstrate significant improvements over previous methods, including a 36% gain on the challenging WxBS benchmark and new state-of-the-art results across multiple datasets.

42306a959a67d237e90d96b4823a98642978ea79.title: Meta-learning Parameterized Skills
42306a959a67d237e90d96b4823a98642978ea79.research_question: How can transferable, parameterized skills be meta-learned and synthesized into a hierarchical action space to enable efficient and generalizable reinforcement learning for long-horizon tasks?
42306a959a67d237e90d96b4823a98642978ea79.hypothesis: Learning parameterized skills via off-policy meta-reinforcement learning, augmented with a trajectory-centric smoothness objective, enables the creation of a structured, reusable action space that supports efficient hierarchical policy learning and improved generalization to new long-horizon tasks.
42306a959a67d237e90d96b4823a98642978ea79.proposed_method: A three-level hierarchical reinforcement learning framework is proposed to model Temporally-extended Parameterized Action Markov Decision Processes (TPAMDPs). At the lowest level, off-policy meta-RL (based on PEARL) is used to learn a set of parameterized skills, each represented as a skill-conditioned policy that takes both state and continuous skill parameters as input. A novel trajectory-centric smoothness objective is introduced to ensure that the learned skill parameter space is smooth and semantically meaningful, by minimizing the difference between latent representations of trajectories in proportion to their dynamic time warping distance. The mid-level policy selects continuous parameters conditioned on state and discrete skill, while the high-level policy selects the discrete skill label. The hierarchical actor-critic framework employs maximum entropy objectives and gumbel-softmax sampling for structured exploration, and practical constraints are imposed on the learned action space to avoid unreliable regions.
42306a959a67d237e90d96b4823a98642978ea79.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on challenging long-horizon tasks, including an Ant obstacle course domain (with tasks such as Ant-Goal, Ant-Bridge, Ant-Gather, and Ant-mix) built on OpenAI Gym, and a robotic manipulation domain (Make Coffee) from MetaWorld. The learned parameterized skills are evaluated as the action space for hierarchical policies, with comparisons to baselines including OPML+HPS (off-policy meta-RL without smoothness), MLPS+PDQN, and MLPS+HyAR. Evaluation metrics include average return, sample efficiency, and success rate on meta-test tasks. Visualization of the learned skill parameter spaces and ablation studies on the smoothness objective are provided to assess the quality and generalization of the learned skills.
42306a959a67d237e90d96b4823a98642978ea79.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel three-level hierarchical RL framework that learns both parameterized skills and their action space from scratch, rather than assuming a predefined set of skills. A new trajectory-centric smoothness objective is developed to ensure the learned skill parameter space is semantically meaningful and supports efficient policy learning. The approach demonstrates the ability to solve complex, long-horizon tasks by synthesizing a new, structured action space, and provides empirical evidence for the importance of smoothness in the learned parameterized action space for downstream hierarchical policy learning.

42585728685d7b2567e62b03463d1520f1bbe47e.title: Perception Test: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Multimodal Video Models
42585728685d7b2567e62b03463d1520f1bbe47e.research_question: How can a comprehensive diagnostic benchmark be developed to robustly evaluate the perception and reasoning skills of multimodal video models across diverse real-world scenarios, skill areas, and modalities?
42585728685d7b2567e62b03463d1520f1bbe47e.hypothesis: A purposefully designed and densely annotated real-world video benchmark, covering a broad range of perception skills and reasoning types, will expose significant gaps between current multimodal video models and human-level performance, thereby providing a more effective tool for diagnosing and guiding improvements in general perception models.
42585728685d7b2567e62b03463d1520f1bbe47e.proposed_method: A new benchmark, named Perception Test, will be constructed using 11,600 real-world videos, each averaging 23 seconds, filmed by approximately 100 diverse participants worldwide. The videos will be designed via expert-created scripts to probe four key skill areas (Memory, Abstraction, Physics, Semantics) and four reasoning types (descriptive, explanatory, predictive, counterfactual), ensuring coverage of perceptually challenging and diverse situations. Each video will be densely annotated with six types of labels: object tracks, point tracks, temporal action segments, temporal sound segments, multiple-choice video question-answers, and grounded video question-answers. The benchmark will be split into training, validation, and held-out test sets, with the majority of data reserved for evaluation to focus on generalization and transfer capabilities. An evaluation server will be provided for the held-out test set, and all data and code for the training and validation splits will be open-sourced.
42585728685d7b2567e62b03463d1520f1bbe47e.experiment_details: Experiments will involve evaluating state-of-the-art multimodal video models (such as Flamingo, SeViLA, and GPT-4) on the Perception Test benchmark in zero-shot, few-shot, and limited fine-tuning regimes. Baseline models for each computational task (object tracking, point tracking, temporal action localization, temporal sound localization, multiple-choice and grounded video QA) will be selected based on strong performance and compatibility with zero/few-shot settings; fine-tuning will be performed where necessary. Evaluation metrics will include average IoU for object tracking, Jaccard index for point tracking, mAP for temporal localization tasks, top-1 accuracy for multiple-choice QA, and HOTA for grounded QA. Human baselines will be collected for comparison, and performance will be analyzed across skill areas and reasoning types to generate diagnostic reports.
42585728685d7b2567e62b03463d1520f1bbe47e.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark uniquely combines real-world, purpose-designed videos with dense, multi-level annotations spanning both low-level and high-level perception tasks, across video, audio, and text modalities. Unlike existing benchmarks, it systematically probes a wide spectrum of skills and reasoning types, enabling comprehensive diagnostics of model capabilities and transferability. The benchmark's design, including adversarial and distractor elements, minimizes language biases and overfitting, while its open-source nature and evaluation server facilitate broad adoption and reproducibility. Initial results indicate a substantial gap between human and model performance, highlighting the benchmark's effectiveness in revealing limitations of current multimodal models.

425dbf0bb4198b630190fc582c9e658582d62817.title: Visual Haystacks: A Vision-Centric Needle-In-A-Haystack Benchmark
425dbf0bb4198b630190fc582c9e658582d62817.research_question: How can large multimodal models be rigorously evaluated and improved for their ability to retrieve and reason over relevant information in large-scale, realistic multi-image question answering scenarios, especially in the presence of visual distractors and positional biases?
425dbf0bb4198b630190fc582c9e658582d62817.hypothesis: Current large multimodal models (LMMs) are limited in their ability to retrieve and reason across thousands of images in realistic multi-image question answering (MIQA) tasks, and a retrieval-augmented, vision-centric framework with efficient token compression and query-aware retrieval will significantly improve performance and scalability on such tasks.
425dbf0bb4198b630190fc582c9e658582d62817.proposed_method: A new benchmark, Visual Haystacks (VHs), will be constructed to assess LMMs' ability to retrieve and reason about visual information in large-scale, realistic multi-image contexts. The benchmark will use in-domain, naturally annotated images (e.g., from COCO) and human-curated QA pairs that require models to find 'needle' images among thousands of distractors and answer binary questions about them. To address the observed limitations of existing LMMs, a novel retrieval-augmented generation framework, MIRAGE, will be developed. MIRAGE will employ a compressive image encoding pipeline using a frozen CLIP encoder and a Q-Former to reduce per-image token count, followed by a query-aware retriever module trained alongside the LMM to filter for relevant images before final reasoning. The model will be trained on a large-scale, instruction-tuning dataset combining synthetic and real-world MIQA data, with shuffled image order to mitigate positional biases.
425dbf0bb4198b630190fc582c9e658582d62817.experiment_details: Experiments will comprehensively evaluate both open-source and proprietary LMMs, as well as MIRAGE, on the Visual Haystacks benchmark across varying haystack sizes (from 1 to 10,000 images) and both single-needle and multi-needle settings. Baselines will include caption aggregation (captioning all images, then answering via LLM) and a detector oracle (object detection followed by reasoning). Evaluation metrics will focus on accuracy for both retrieval and reasoning, with additional analysis of positional biases and runtime efficiency. Further, MIRAGE will be benchmarked on established multi-image QA datasets (RetVQA, SlideVQA, WebQA) and single-image QA tasks (VQA-v2, GQA, TextVQA, etc.), comparing against state-of-the-art proprietary and open-source LMMs. All models will be evaluated in zero-shot settings, and robustness will be ensured via bootstrapped averages and standard deviations.
425dbf0bb4198b630190fc582c9e658582d62817.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first large-scale, vision-centric, realistic needle-in-a-haystack benchmark (Visual Haystacks) for multi-image QA, overcoming the limitations of prior text- or OCR-centric visual NIAH tasks. It presents MIRAGE, the first open-source visual retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework capable of scaling to over 10,000 images per query on a single GPU, using a novel combination of compressive image encoding and query-aware retrieval. The approach is designed to explicitly diagnose and address key challenges in long-context visual reasoning, including susceptibility to distractors, cross-image reasoning difficulty, and positional bias. MIRAGE is expected to set new state-of-the-art results on multi-image QA benchmarks while maintaining competitive performance on single-image tasks, all with significantly improved efficiency and scalability.

428854d9e75f94f0e61f37c6887c77800437d516.title: MusicLM: Generating Music From Text
428854d9e75f94f0e61f37c6887c77800437d516.research_question: How can high-fidelity, long-duration music be generated from natural language text descriptions, and how can such a system be extended to support additional conditioning signals such as melody input?
428854d9e75f94f0e61f37c6887c77800437d516.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a hierarchical sequence-to-sequence modeling approach, leveraging joint music-text embeddings and large-scale audio-only corpora, will enable the generation of coherent, high-quality music that faithfully adheres to complex text descriptions and can be further conditioned on melodic input.
428854d9e75f94f0e61f37c6887c77800437d516.proposed_method: A novel hierarchical sequence-to-sequence generative model will be developed for text-conditioned music generation. The approach will utilize independently pretrained and frozen models for audio and text representation: SoundStream for high-fidelity acoustic tokens, w2v-BERT for semantic tokens, and MuLan for joint music-text embeddings. During training, MuLan audio embeddings will be quantized and used as conditioning, while at inference, MuLan text embeddings will serve as the conditioning signal. The model will employ a multi-stage autoregressive Transformer architecture, where the first stage predicts semantic tokens conditioned on MuLan tokens, and subsequent stages predict acoustic tokens conditioned on both semantic and MuLan tokens. The method will also be extended to accept melody input by training a joint embedding model for melody and concatenating melody tokens with MuLan tokens during generation.
428854d9e75f94f0e61f37c6887c77800437d516.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a large-scale dataset of five million music audio clips (280k hours at 24kHz) for model training, with SoundStream and w2v-BERT trained on the Free Music Archive dataset. Evaluation will utilize the newly curated MusicCaps dataset, comprising 5.5k music-text pairs with detailed expert annotations. Baseline comparisons will include Mubert and Riffusion, representing state-of-the-art text-to-music systems. Evaluation metrics will include Frechet Audio Distance (FAD) for audio quality, Kullback-Leibler Divergence (KLD) and MuLan Cycle Consistency (MCC) for text faithfulness, and human listening tests for subjective assessment. Additional experiments will analyze memorization risks and the impact of semantic versus acoustic token modeling.
428854d9e75f94f0e61f37c6887c77800437d516.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a hierarchical, text-conditioned music generation framework capable of producing high-fidelity, coherent music over several minutes, outperforming existing baselines in both quality and adherence to text. The method uniquely leverages joint music-text embeddings to enable large-scale training on audio-only corpora, bypassing the need for extensive paired data. The approach supports additional conditioning on melody, allowing transformation of hummed or whistled input into music matching a text prompt. Furthermore, a new high-quality evaluation dataset (MusicCaps) will be released to support future research in text-to-music generation.

428c6bd657229d4f3360b5f5920ad3609739ecdc.title: A Training-Free Sub-quadratic Cost Transformer Model Serving Framework with Hierarchically Pruned Attention
428c6bd657229d4f3360b5f5920ad3609739ecdc.research_question: How can the computational and memory costs of serving large language models (LLMs) with extremely long context lengths be reduced, while maintaining high generation quality and requiring no retraining or fine-tuning of the underlying models?
428c6bd657229d4f3360b5f5920ad3609739ecdc.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by exploiting the locality of attention scores in pretrained LLMs and employing a hierarchical, training-free, top-k key selection algorithm, it is possible to reduce the time complexity of attention computation to sub-quadratic levels and the memory footprint to near-linear or sub-linear, all while preserving model quality and enabling practical deployment on commodity hardware.
428c6bd657229d4f3360b5f5920ad3609739ecdc.proposed_method: A novel attention mechanism, Hierarchically Pruned Attention (HiP), is developed to approximate the top-k key tokens for each query in a sequence using a tree-search-like, hierarchical approach. The method leverages the empirical observation that attention scores exhibit locality, allowing the sequence to be divided into chunks, with representative tokens used to estimate chunk importance. At each iteration, the top-k most important chunks are selected and further subdivided, recursively narrowing the search until single tokens are identified, resulting in an O(T log T) time and O(T) space complexity for attention computation. To maximize hardware efficiency, block-wise tiling and hardware-aware optimizations are incorporated, enabling efficient use of GPU matrix multiplication units (e.g., TensorCores). Additionally, a KV cache offloading strategy is introduced, storing only O(log T) frequently accessed tokens in GPU memory and offloading the remainder to host memory, with a page table or hash map for index translation, further reducing GPU memory usage while maintaining high throughput.
428c6bd657229d4f3360b5f5920ad3609739ecdc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by integrating the HiP mechanism into state-of-the-art LLM serving frameworks (such as vLLM and SGlang) and applying it to pretrained models like Llama3.1-8B. Evaluation will be performed on a suite of long-context benchmarks, including PG19 for language modeling, LongBench for long-context QA and summarization, BookSum for long document summarization, and passkey retrieval tasks such as RULER. Baselines will include FlashAttention, BigBird, StreamingLLM, HyperAttention, H2O, and AVD, among others. Metrics will include latency (prefill and decode), perplexity, ROUGE scores, retrieval accuracy, and effective context length, with experiments run on both consumer (RTX4090) and server-grade (A100) GPUs. The impact of KV cache offloading will be measured in terms of throughput and memory usage, and ablation studies will be conducted to assess trade-offs between latency, memory, and quality.
428c6bd657229d4f3360b5f5920ad3609739ecdc.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a training-free, hierarchically pruned sparse attention mechanism that achieves sub-quadratic (O(T log T)) time and O(T) space complexity for attention computation in pretrained LLMs, without requiring any retraining or fine-tuning. It further incorporates hardware-aware block-wise optimizations for maximal GPU efficiency and a novel KV cache offloading mechanism that reduces GPU memory usage to O(log T) for key-value states. The approach is mathematically proven to outperform random pruning and empirically shown to maintain high model quality while enabling long-context inference on commodity hardware. This combination of algorithmic, systems, and hardware-level innovations enables practical deployment of long-context LLMs previously considered infeasible.

42b6b7ae57b2b784be7fa78bf98b1c61d2b62751.title: Extracting Latent Steering Vectors from Pretrained Language Models
42b6b7ae57b2b784be7fa78bf98b1c61d2b62751.research_question: Can latent steering vectors be extracted from frozen, pretrained language model decoders to enable controllable text generation, and do these vectors encode semantic properties that allow for effective manipulation of generated text without fine-tuning the underlying model?
42b6b7ae57b2b784be7fa78bf98b1c61d2b62751.hypothesis: The information required to steer a pretrained language model to generate a specific target sentence is already encoded within the model, and fixed-length latent steering vectors can be extracted and used to control generation and perform semantic manipulations such as style transfer.
42b6b7ae57b2b784be7fa78bf98b1c61d2b62751.proposed_method: A methodology is proposed for extracting fixed-length steering vectors from a frozen, pretrained transformer-based language model (e.g., GPT-2). For each target sentence, a steering vector is randomly initialized and optimized via gradient descent to maximize the likelihood of the target sentence, with the language model weights kept frozen. The steering vector is injected into the hidden states of the model at specific layers and timesteps during decoding, with experiments indicating that injection into the middle layers (e.g., layers 6 or 7 of 12) is most effective. The approach allows for vector arithmetic in the latent space, enabling operations such as style transfer by computing offset vectors between groups of steering vectors corresponding to different styles. The method is fully extractive and does not require any fine-tuning or additional training of the language model.
42b6b7ae57b2b784be7fa78bf98b1c61d2b62751.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using GPT-2 (117M parameters) as the base language model. Sentence recovery is evaluated on a dataset constructed from four domains: movie dialogs (Cornell Movie Dialogs), classic books (NLTK Gutenberg), news articles (Gigaword), and Wikipedia (WikiText-103). Sentences are binned by length and sampled to assess recovery performance across a range of sequence lengths. The effectiveness of steering vectors is measured by decoding with the extracted vector and computing BLEU-4 scores between generated and target sentences. Unsupervised sentiment transfer is evaluated on the Yelp Sentiment dataset, comparing accuracy and BLEU against baselines such as autoencoder-based models and other unsupervised methods. Semantic similarity is assessed using the STS-Benchmark, correlating cosine similarities between steering vectors with human-annotated similarity scores. Additional analyses include t-SNE clustering, interpolation in latent space, sampling, and evaluation of intrinsic dimensionality and memorization effects.
42b6b7ae57b2b784be7fa78bf98b1c61d2b62751.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel extractive approach to controllable text generation by directly optimizing and injecting latent steering vectors into frozen pretrained language models, without any fine-tuning. It demonstrates that these vectors can achieve near-perfect sentence recovery, enable unsupervised style transfer via vector arithmetic, and encode semantic similarity more effectively than pooled hidden state baselines. The method provides new insights into the latent geometry of transformer models and establishes that frozen language models can be controlled through their latent steering space, offering a simple yet powerful alternative to existing controllability techniques.

42cf52baff90952944da0409ec52ff7611ed55dc.title: Representational Strengths and Limitations of Transformers
42cf52baff90952944da0409ec52ff7611ed55dc.research_question: What are the fundamental representational strengths and limitations of transformer architectures, particularly self-attention layers, in comparison to other neural network models such as recurrent and feedforward networks, with respect to intrinsic complexity parameters like width, depth, and embedding dimension?
42cf52baff90952944da0409ec52ff7611ed55dc.hypothesis: Self-attention layers in transformer architectures possess unique representational advantages for certain computational tasks, especially those involving sparse pairwise interactions, but exhibit inherent limitations when representing higher-order interactions unless their complexity parameters scale polynomially with input size.
42cf52baff90952944da0409ec52ff7611ed55dc.proposed_method: A rigorous theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the representational power of transformer self-attention layers by constructing and studying specific computational tasks, such as sparse averaging (qSA), pairwise matching (Match2), and triple-wise matching (Match3). The approach will involve formalizing these tasks and deriving upper and lower bounds on the complexity (embedding dimension, width, depth) required for transformers, recurrent neural networks, and feedforward networks to approximate these functions. Communication complexity techniques will be leveraged to establish lower bounds and impossibility results, while geometric and polytope-based constructions will be used to design efficient transformer solutions for sparse averaging. Variants of the tasks and architectural modifications, such as higher-order attention, will also be explored to delineate the boundaries of transformer expressivity.
42cf52baff90952944da0409ec52ff7611ed55dc.experiment_details: Empirical studies will be conducted to validate the theoretical findings, focusing on the sample efficiency and learnability of the qSA task using transformer-based self-attention units compared to recurrent networks and MLPs. Synthetic datasets will be generated for qSA, Match2, and Match3 tasks, with varying input sizes, sparsity levels, and embedding dimensions. Baseline models will include standard recurrent neural networks and fully-connected feedforward networks. Evaluation metrics will include approximation accuracy (e.g., mean squared error for qSA), classification accuracy for matching tasks, and sample complexity required to reach a specified accuracy threshold. Experimental setups will visualize attention matrices and convergence behavior during training.
42cf52baff90952944da0409ec52ff7611ed55dc.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a formal separation between the representational capabilities of transformers and other neural architectures for natural computational tasks, establishing that transformers can solve sparse averaging with logarithmic complexity in input size, while RNNs and MLPs require polynomial complexity. The work provides near-optimal bounds on the embedding dimension necessary for transformers to approximate sparse averaging, and rigorously characterizes the inability of standard self-attention to efficiently represent triple-wise interactions without substantial increases in complexity. The use of communication complexity as a tool for analyzing neural network expressivity, and the identification of sparse averaging as a canonical attention task, constitute key innovations. Additionally, the research offers conjectures and preliminary empirical evidence regarding the limitations of deep transformer models on higher-order tasks.

42d3b9e9111efb70a11167096738d7dd344f7e5a.title: Oscillation-free Quantization for Low-bit Vision Transformers
42d3b9e9111efb70a11167096738d7dd344f7e5a.research_question: How can quantization-aware training for low-bit Vision Transformers be stabilized to avoid weight oscillation and improve the accuracy of quantized models, particularly in resource-constrained environments?
42d3b9e9111efb70a11167096738d7dd344f7e5a.hypothesis: Weight oscillation in quantization-aware training is exacerbated by the use of learnable scaling factors and the interdependence between quantized query and key weights in self-attention layers.
