By introducing statistical scaling, confidence-guided annealing, and query-key reparameterization, it is possible to mitigate oscillation and achieve higher accuracy in low-bit quantized Vision Transformers.
42d3b9e9111efb70a11167096738d7dd344f7e5a.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces three complementary techniques to achieve oscillation-free quantization in low-bit Vision Transformers. First, statistical weight quantization (StatsQ) replaces learnable scaling factors with a statistical scaling factor computed from the weight distribution, reducing the disproportionate influence of outlier weights and stabilizing training. Second, confidence-guided annealing (CGA) is employed during fine-tuning to freeze weights that have moved outside the oscillation region, allowing only the oscillating, low-confidence weights near quantization thresholds to be updated, thus gradually eliminating oscillation. Third, query-key reparameterization (QKR) decouples the mutual influence between quantized query and key weights in self-attention layers by reordering matrix multiplications, which reduces gradient noise and prevents co-oscillation. These methods are designed to work collaboratively, ensuring stable convergence and improved quantization robustness.
42d3b9e9111efb70a11167096738d7dd344f7e5a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on DeiT-Tiny, DeiT-Small, and Swin-Tiny architectures using the ILSVRC12 ImageNet dataset. The proposed methods will be evaluated in 2-bit, 3-bit, and 4-bit quantization settings. Baseline comparisons will include LSQ (Learned Step Size Quantization), QViT, and Mix-QViT, with full-precision models serving as upper-bound references. Evaluation metrics will focus on top-1 accuracy. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the individual and combined effects of StatsQ, CGA, and QKR, as well as the sensitivity to the boundary range parameter in CGA. The experimental setup will follow standard training recipes for ViT models, with specific modifications for quantization-aware training and annealing epochs.
42d3b9e9111efb70a11167096738d7dd344f7e5a.novelty_claims: The proposal claims three main innovations: (1) the identification and analysis of the negative impact of learnable scaling factors on weight oscillation in quantization-aware training for Vision Transformers; (2) the introduction of statistical weight quantization and confidence-guided annealing to systematically eliminate oscillation and stabilize low-bit quantized models; and (3) the development of query-key reparameterization to decouple and mitigate mutual oscillation in self-attention layers. Collectively, these techniques are claimed to achieve substantial accuracy improvements over previous state-of-the-art quantization methods, particularly in the challenging low-bit regime.

42dc8e6cfd585a9fea855272269bbe3a449f134c.title: Beyond Modality Collapse: Representations Blending for Multimodal Dataset Distillation
42dc8e6cfd585a9fea855272269bbe3a449f134c.research_question: How can multimodal dataset distillation be improved to prevent excessive intra-modal similarity and poor cross-modal alignment, thereby enabling the creation of compact, effective surrogate datasets for cross-modal learning tasks?
42dc8e6cfd585a9fea855272269bbe3a449f134c.hypothesis: Introducing representation blending to enhance intra-modal diversity and employing symmetric projection trajectory matching to balance supervision across modalities will mitigate modality collapse and improve the effectiveness and efficiency of multimodal dataset distillation.
42dc8e6cfd585a9fea855272269bbe3a449f134c.proposed_method: A novel multimodal dataset distillation (MDD) framework is proposed that incorporates two key components: Representation Blending and Symmetric Projection Trajectory Matching. Representation Blending operates in the shared representation space by linearly combining representations from different synthetic instances within each modality, analogous to MixUp, to weaken overly strong cross-modal supervision and promote intra-modal diversity. Symmetric Projection Trajectory Matching introduces dedicated projection heads for both image and text modalities and aligns their optimization trajectories by minimizing the distance between the synthetic and real expert trajectories, ensuring balanced and synchronized updates across modalities. The overall pipeline involves initializing encoders with pretrained weights, optimizing only the projection heads during distillation, and iteratively updating the synthetic dataset using both representation blending and symmetric trajectory matching. This approach is designed to address both the over-concentration of intra-modal representations and the distributional gap between modalities.
42dc8e6cfd585a9fea855272269bbe3a449f134c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on widely-used image-text datasets, including Flickr-30K and MS-COCO, with additional evaluation on the AudioCaps audio-text benchmark to assess generalizability. The method will be compared against a range of state-of-the-art baselines, including coreset selection (Random, Herding, K-Center, Forgetting) and recent dataset distillation methods (MTT-VL, TESLA-VL, LoRS). Evaluation will focus on cross-modal retrieval tasks using Recall@K (R@K) metrics for both text-to-image (IR@K) and image-to-text (TR@K) retrieval. Various encoder architectures (NFNet, RegNet, ResNet-50, ViT for images; BERT, DistilBERT for text) will be tested to validate architectural robustness. Ablation studies will isolate the effects of representation blending and symmetric matching. Computational efficiency will be measured in terms of training time, memory usage, and speedup over baselines. All experiments will be run on high-end GPUs, and hyperparameters will align with those used in prior work for fair comparison.
42dc8e6cfd585a9fea855272269bbe3a449f134c.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to explicitly identify and address the modality collapse phenomenon in multimodal dataset distillation, attributing it to the interplay between over-compression and contrastive supervision. Representation Blending is introduced as a novel technique to enhance intra-modal diversity without sacrificing cross-modal alignment. Symmetric Projection Trajectory Matching is developed to synchronize and balance supervision across modalities, overcoming the limitations of prior asymmetric approaches. The method achieves substantial improvements in retrieval performance and distillation efficiency, demonstrating strong generalization across architectures and modalities, and offers significant computational advantages over existing state-of-the-art methods.

42e1790c7979796634d15920b4a08990e847243e.title: Transformers generalize differently from information stored in context vs in weights
42e1790c7979796634d15920b4a08990e847243e.research_question: How do transformer models differ in their inductive biases and generalization strategies when utilizing information stored in model weights versus information provided in-context at inference time, and how do factors such as training data and model scale influence these generalization behaviors?
42e1790c7979796634d15920b4a08990e847243e.hypothesis: Transformers generalize from information stored in weights primarily via rule-based strategies, whereas in-context information leads to exemplar-based generalization; however, large-scale pretraining on natural language or explicitly rule-based data can induce more rule-based in-context generalization, especially in larger models.
42e1790c7979796634d15920b4a08990e847243e.proposed_method: The proposed research will systematically compare the generalization behaviors of transformer models when information is encoded in model weights versus provided in-context at inference. Controlled synthetic datasets will be constructed using the 'partial exposure' paradigm, where each stimulus consists of two features but only one is predictive of the label, allowing clear differentiation between rule-based and exemplar-based generalization. Transformers will be trained from scratch on these synthetic datasets to assess both in-weights and in-context learning. Additionally, large pretrained language models of varying sizes will be evaluated using analogous tasks with natural language features (e.g., shape and color words) to assess in-context generalization. Further, transformers will be pretrained on synthetic data that explicitly requires rule-based generalization to test whether such training can induce rule-based in-context learning.
42e1790c7979796634d15920b4a08990e847243e.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize both synthetic and natural language datasets. For synthetic data, each stimulus will be a concatenation of two 32-dimensional subvectors sampled from multivariate normals, with 10 classes per feature and 100 values per class. Models will be trained using the partial exposure paradigm, where one feature predicts the label and a held-out combination is used for evaluation. In-weights generalization will be tested by training the model on fixed stimulus-label mappings, while in-context generalization will be tested by pretraining for few-shot learning and then evaluating on partial exposure sequences. For pretrained language models (1B, 7B, 70B parameters), evaluation will use sequences of shape and color words with nonsense labels, including control conditions to account for feature bias. Baselines will be established using control conditions where neither feature is predictive. Evaluation metrics include the frequency of rule-based versus exemplar-based responses on held-out combinations, with results averaged over multiple training runs and model sizes.
42e1790c7979796634d15920b4a08990e847243e.novelty_claims: This research proposes a systematic, controlled comparison of generalization from weights versus in-context information in transformers, revealing that these two sources induce distinct inductive biases. It introduces a methodology for quantifying rule-based versus exemplar-based generalization in both synthetic and natural language domains. The proposal also investigates the role of training data structure and model scale in shaping in-context generalization, providing evidence that large-scale language pretraining or explicit rule-based pretraining can induce rule-based in-context generalization. These findings have practical implications for how information should be encoded in transformer-based systems depending on desired generalization behavior.

431031af5dff30525b2ec8cdff45d21a9f78d929.title: Diffusion-based Generation, Optimization, and Planning in 3D Scenes
431031af5dff30525b2ec8cdff45d21a9f78d929.research_question: How can a unified, scene-aware, physics-based, and goal-oriented generative framework be developed to address generation, optimization, and planning tasks in complex 3D scenes, overcoming the limitations of existing modular and cVAE-based approaches?
431031af5dff30525b2ec8cdff45d21a9f78d929.hypothesis: A diffusion-based conditional generative model that jointly integrates scene-awareness, physics-based optimization, and goal-oriented planning within a unified, differentiable sampling framework will significantly improve the plausibility, diversity, and generalizability of solutions for a broad range of 3D scene understanding tasks, compared to existing modular and cVAE-based models.
431031af5dff30525b2ec8cdff45d21a9f78d929.proposed_method: A novel framework, SceneDiffuser, will be developed as a conditional generative model based on the diffusion process. This model will leverage an iterative denoising diffusion process to jointly perform scene-conditioned generation, physics-based optimization, and goal-oriented planning in 3D scenes. The method will incorporate cross-attention mechanisms to flexibly condition on scene representations (e.g., point clouds) and input trajectories, and will integrate differentiable physics-based objectives and planning objectives as guidance at each sampling step. The approach will support both explicit and learned trajectory objectives for physical plausibility (e.g., collision, contact) and goal achievement, using gradient-based sampling to steer the generation toward physically plausible and goal-reaching solutions. The architecture will include a scene encoder, cross-attention modules, and feed-forward layers to estimate the noise for the diffusion process, enabling end-to-end training and inference for diverse 3D tasks.
431031af5dff30525b2ec8cdff45d21a9f78d929.experiment_details: Comprehensive experiments will be conducted across five representative 3D scene understanding tasks: human pose generation, human motion generation, dexterous grasp generation, path planning for 3D navigation, and motion planning for robot arms. Datasets such as PROX and LEMO for human pose/motion, MultiDex for dexterous grasping, ScanNet for navigation, and custom-generated cluttered scenes for robot arms will be used. Baselines will include widely-adopted cVAE models and their variants, as well as imitation learning (Behavior Cloning) and heuristic planners for planning tasks. Evaluation metrics will cover physical plausibility (e.g., plausible rate, collision/contact scores), diversity (average pairwise distance, standard deviation), task success rates, and planning efficiency (number of steps). Both direct human evaluations and indirect quantitative metrics will be used to assess the quality and diversity of generated outputs, and ablation studies will be performed to analyze the influence of optimization guidance and model components.
431031af5dff30525b2ec8cdff45d21a9f78d929.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first unified diffusion-based framework for scene-conditioned generation, optimization, and planning in 3D scenes. It addresses the posterior collapse and module discrepancy issues inherent in cVAE-based and modular pipelines by integrating generation, physics-based optimization, and planning objectives into a single, fully differentiable sampling process. The method demonstrates superior performance and generalizability across diverse 3D tasks, achieving significant improvements in physical plausibility and task success rates, and supports flexible conditioning and guidance for both explicit and learned objectives. The framework is broadly applicable to various 3D scene understanding domains and sets a new standard for unified, scene-aware generative modeling.

4315094bec44f310d662b349aff6305b3dde9a07.title: EVEDIT: Event-based Knowledge Editing with Deductive Editing Boundaries
4315094bec44f310d662b349aff6305b3dde9a07.research_question: How can knowledge editing in large language models be made more robust and logically sound, particularly in scenarios where edits are driven by real-world events and require propagation of changes through related knowledge, while maintaining model certainty and naturalness?
4315094bec44f310d662b349aff6305b3dde9a07.hypothesis: Incorporating event-based knowledge editing with implicit deduction anchors will reduce uncertainty and improve factual consistency in edited language models compared to traditional triple-based editing approaches.
4315094bec44f310d662b349aff6305b3dde9a07.proposed_method: A novel event-based knowledge editing framework will be developed, where edits are paired with event descriptions that implicitly define deduction anchors and editing boundaries. The method involves curating a new benchmark dataset, EVEDIT, derived from COUNTERFACT, by augmenting factual edits with event context using GPT-3.5-turbo. The proposed approach, Self-Edit, leverages the pre-edit language model to generate relevant question-answer pairs for each event-based edit, including undecidable questions to delineate the editing boundary. The model is then fine-tuned on these instances, training it to recite the edit before answering and to respond with 'I don’t know' when appropriate, thus explicitly teaching the model its knowledge boundaries. This approach is compared to baseline methods that decompose events into triples and apply existing factual-association editing algorithms.
4315094bec44f310d662b349aff6305b3dde9a07.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the LLaMA2-7B-chat model as the base, evaluating both question-answering and text-completion tasks on the EVEDIT benchmark. The evaluation set will be split into 'Known' and 'Unknown' subsets to assess both factual consistency and the model's ability to recognize undecidable queries. Baselines will include ROME, MEMIT, PMET, GRACE, direct fine-tuning, and in-context learning, with edits applied in batches of N = 1, 10, 59, and 100 to test scalability. Evaluation metrics will include factual consistency (with respect to the edit), naturalness (generation quality), and precision/recall/F1 for the 'Unknown' subset. The certainty of model responses will be measured using log-likelihoods, and performance will be analyzed across both related and unrelated knowledge queries.
4315094bec44f310d662b349aff6305b3dde9a07.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces event-based knowledge editing as a more realistic and logically robust alternative to triple-based editing, addressing the issue of ambiguous editing boundaries by implicitly defining deduction anchors through event context. A new benchmark, EVEDIT, is curated to systematically evaluate this setting. The Self-Edit approach is proposed as a novel method that fine-tunes models with explicit editing boundaries, significantly improving factual consistency and boundary recognition while maintaining naturalness. The framework provides a theoretical foundation for knowledge editing with formal definitions of deduction anchors and editing boundaries, and demonstrates that event-based editing mitigates uncertainty and knowledge shrinkage in edited models.

4337200e8063bddc97c508efeb1ef81f118abe30.title: Encoding Time-Series Explanations through Self-Supervised Model Behavior Consistency
4337200e8063bddc97c508efeb1ef81f118abe30.research_question: How can interpretable and faithful explanations for time series model predictions be generated, particularly in a way that preserves the underlying temporal and relational structure of the data?
4337200e8063bddc97c508efeb1ef81f118abe30.hypothesis: A self-supervised surrogate model that enforces consistency between the latent spaces of a pretrained time series model and an explainer can produce more faithful and interpretable attribution maps, leading to superior explanation quality compared to existing interpretability methods.
4337200e8063bddc97c508efeb1ef81f118abe30.proposed_method: A novel surrogate explainer, TIMEX, will be developed to generate interpretable attribution maps for pretrained time series models. TIMEX will consist of an explanation generator that produces discrete, connected attribution masks over time-sensor pairs using a Bernoulli parameterization and Gumbel-Softmax sampling for differentiable, end-to-end training. An explanation encoder will be fine-tuned on masked input distributions, using a straight-through estimator to enforce discrete masking and avoid the pitfalls of continuous mask deformation in time series. The core training objective will be model behavior consistency (MBC), which aligns the relational structure of the explainer's latent space with that of the reference model via a distance-matching loss, supplemented by a label consistency objective based on Jensen-Shannon divergence between predicted logits. Additionally, TIMEX will learn a set of landmark explanations in the latent space, enabling aggregation and summarization of explanation patterns across samples.
4337200e8063bddc97c508efeb1ef81f118abe30.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on eight datasets, including four synthetic time series datasets with known ground-truth explanations (FreqShapes, SeqComb-UV, SeqComb-MV, LowVar) and four real-world datasets (ECG for arrhythmia detection, PAM for human activity recognition, Epilepsy for EEG seizure detection, and Boiler for mechanical fault detection). The method will be benchmarked against five baselines: Integrated Gradients (IG), Dynamask, WinIT, CoRTX, and SGT+Grad. Evaluation will use metrics such as area under the precision curve (AUP), area under the recall curve (AUR), and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) for explanation quality, as well as occlusion experiments measuring classification AUROC after masking features identified as important by the explainer. Ablation studies will assess the contribution of discrete masking, MBC, and label consistency objectives. Additional experiments will test the method's flexibility on different model architectures (e.g., LSTM, CNN) and task settings (e.g., forecasting, irregularly sampled classification).
4337200e8063bddc97c508efeb1ef81f118abe30.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces model behavior consistency (MBC), a novel self-supervised objective that preserves relational structure in the latent spaces of both the pretrained model and the explainer, enabling faithful explanations without direct alignment. TIMEX generates discrete, interpretable attribution maps using straight-through estimators, addressing the occlusion and out-of-distribution issues prevalent in time series explanation. The method uniquely learns a latent space of explanations, allowing for landmark-based aggregation and visualization of temporal patterns. Comprehensive benchmarking demonstrates that TIMEX achieves state-of-the-art or near state-of-the-art performance across all tested datasets and metrics, surpassing existing time series and general explainability methods.

435640467611474172ccf702d631bc652f6cd7a8.title: Adversarial Example Does Good: Preventing Painting Imitation from Diffusion Models via Adversarial Examples
435640467611474172ccf702d631bc652f6cd7a8.research_question: How can human-created artworks be protected from unauthorized imitation and style extraction by diffusion models used in AI-for-Art applications, particularly in the absence of existing technological safeguards against copyright infringement?
435640467611474172ccf702d631bc652f6cd7a8.hypothesis: Adversarial examples specifically crafted for diffusion models can prevent these models from extracting meaningful features or styles from protected artworks, thereby hindering unauthorized imitation and style transfer without perceptibly altering the original images.
435640467611474172ccf702d631bc652f6cd7a8.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be established to define and evaluate adversarial examples tailored for diffusion models. The approach involves formulating an optimization objective that minimizes the likelihood of a diffusion model recognizing a perturbed image as a valid input, thus preventing effective feature extraction. The core algorithm, AdvDM, utilizes a Monte Carlo estimation to optimize adversarial perturbations over different latent variables sampled from the reverse process of the diffusion model. The optimization is performed by maximizing the loss function used in diffusion model training with respect to the input image, subject to a strict perturbation norm constraint to ensure semantic fidelity. The adversarial examples are generated via iterative signed gradient ascent steps, each based on gradients estimated from multiple latent variable samples, ensuring robustness against the generative process.
435640467611474172ccf702d631bc652f6cd7a8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Latent Diffusion Model (LDM) as the backbone, reflecting its prevalence in commercial AI-for-Art applications. Datasets will include LSUN categories (cat, sheep, airplane) and WikiArt for both object and style transfer scenarios. Evaluation will focus on conditional generation pipelines, such as text-to-image and image-to-image synthesis, including style transfer via textual inversion. Metrics such as Frechet Inception Distance (FID), Precision, and Recall will be used to assess the quality and similarity of generated images relative to the originals. Baselines will include clean (unperturbed) images and various preprocessing-based adversarial defenses (JPEG compression, TVM, SR). Ablation studies will examine the effects of sampling steps and perturbation budgets on attack efficacy and computational cost.
435640467611474172ccf702d631bc652f6cd7a8.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first systematic framework for defining and generating adversarial examples specifically for diffusion models, addressing a critical gap in copyright protection for digital artworks. The AdvDM algorithm leverages Monte Carlo sampling over latent variables to craft adversarial perturbations that disrupt feature extraction in generative pipelines, a departure from existing adversarial attack paradigms focused on classification models. Extensive experimental validation across multiple datasets and commercial pipelines demonstrates the method's effectiveness in preventing unauthorized style and content imitation, establishing a new paradigm for artist-driven copyright defense in the era of generative AI.

435d459eee226fc08e6d00b08f2e61b10f40502f.title: S2AC: Energy-Based Reinforcement Learning with Stein Soft Actor Critic
435d459eee226fc08e6d00b08f2e61b10f40502f.research_question: How can reinforcement learning algorithms learn more expressive and robust stochastic policies, particularly in environments with complex, multimodal action distributions, while maintaining computational efficiency and tractable entropy estimation?
435d459eee226fc08e6d00b08f2e61b10f40502f.hypothesis: A reinforcement learning algorithm that models the policy as a parameterized Stein Variational Gradient Descent (SVGD) sampler from an energy-based model over Q-values, and leverages a closed-form entropy estimate, will yield more expressive, robust, and sample-efficient policies than existing maximum entropy RL methods.
435d459eee226fc08e6d00b08f2e61b10f40502f.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops a new actor-critic reinforcement learning algorithm, termed S2AC, which models the policy as a sampler from an energy-based model (EBM) over Q-values using parameterized Stein Variational Gradient Descent (SVGD). The actor generates action samples by iteratively transforming particles, initialized from a learnable isotropic Gaussian, towards the EBM-defined target distribution. A closed-form expression for the entropy of the resulting policy is derived using the change-of-variable formula, enabled by the invertibility of the SVGD update rule. The method alternates between policy evaluation (critic update via Bellman loss) and policy improvement (actor update to maximize expected reward plus entropy), with the SVGD-based actor enabling efficient learning of multimodal and expressive policies. To ensure scalability, the initial distribution parameters are learned end-to-end, and particle updates are bounded to avoid divergence in non-smooth Q-function landscapes. An amortized version of the SVGD policy is trained for efficient test-time inference.
435d459eee226fc08e6d00b08f2e61b10f40502f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in three main settings: (1) Evaluation of the closed-form entropy estimator on synthetic distributions with known entropy (e.g., Gaussians, Gaussian Mixture Models) to assess accuracy and sensitivity to SVGD parameters (kernel type, variance, number of steps, number of particles). (2) A custom multi-goal environment will be used to test the ability of the method to learn multimodal policies and maximize expected future entropy, with robustness assessed by introducing obstacles at test time. (3) Benchmarking on five continuous control environments from the MuJoCo suite (Hopper-v2, Walker2d-v2, HalfCheetah-v2, Ant-v2, Humanoid-v2), comparing against baselines including DDPG, PPO, SAC, SQL, and SAC-NF. Evaluation metrics will include average return, sample efficiency (convergence speed), robustness to perturbations, and statistical significance measures such as median, IQM, mean, and optimality gap. Hyperparameters and experimental details will be aligned with standard practice and provided in supplementary materials.
435d459eee226fc08e6d00b08f2e61b10f40502f.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new family of expressive variational distributions for RL policies based on parameterized SVGD samplers from EBMs, enabling tractable closed-form entropy estimation. The approach is the first to derive and utilize a closed-form entropy formula for SVGD-based policies in the RL setting, overcoming limitations of previous methods that either require high-variance sampling or restrict policy expressivity (e.g., to Gaussians or normalizing flows). The method achieves improved sample efficiency, robustness, and performance over state-of-the-art MaxEnt RL algorithms, and provides a scalable framework for learning multimodal policies in high-dimensional action spaces.

4367911d9d28d83fafbcf6c908698dd981ddbe9e.title: Inverse Preference Learning: Preference-based RL without a Reward Function
4367911d9d28d83fafbcf6c908698dd981ddbe9e.research_question: How can reinforcement learning agents be trained from human preference data without relying on an explicitly learned reward function, while maintaining or improving efficiency, performance, and robustness compared to existing preference-based RL methods?
4367911d9d28d83fafbcf6c908698dd981ddbe9e.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by leveraging the equivalence between the Q-function and the reward function under a fixed policy, it is possible to eliminate the explicit reward learning stage in preference-based reinforcement learning. Directly optimizing the Q-function to align with human preferences, with appropriate regularization, will yield competitive or superior performance and efficiency compared to traditional two-stage methods that separately learn a reward model.
4367911d9d28d83fafbcf6c908698dd981ddbe9e.proposed_method: A novel algorithm, Inverse Preference Learning (IPL), is proposed for preference-based reinforcement learning without an explicit reward function. The method utilizes the insight that for a fixed policy, the Q-function contains all information necessary to represent the reward function, allowing the reward to be expressed as a function of the Q-values and the value function via the inverse Bellman operator. IPL directly optimizes the Q-function to minimize the divergence between the preference distribution implied by the Q-function and the distribution of expert preferences, as modeled by the Bradley-Terry model. To ensure convergence and avoid degenerate solutions, a convex regularizer (such as L2 regularization) is applied to the implicit rewards. The algorithm alternates between updating the Q-function using the regularized preference loss and improving the policy or value targets using any off-policy RL algorithm, such as IQL or XQL, until convergence. The approach is general and can be instantiated with various offline or online RL algorithms, and is designed to be parameter- and hyperparameter-efficient.
4367911d9d28d83fafbcf6c908698dd981ddbe9e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard offline preference-based RL benchmarks, including D4RL Gym Locomotion and Robosuite robotics datasets with real human preference data. The proposed IPL method will be evaluated using both Implicit Q-Learning (IQL) and XQL as the underlying RL algorithms, and compared against baselines such as Markovian Reward (MR), Non-Markovian Reward (NMR) with LSTM, Preference Transformer (PT), and B-REX. Evaluation metrics will include normalized task scores, variance across random seeds, and parameter efficiency. Additional experiments will assess performance under varying amounts of preference data using MetaWorld tasks, as well as ablations on regularization, data augmentation, and network size. Hyperparameters will be matched to prior work where possible to ensure fair comparison, and all methods will be run for multiple seeds to assess consistency.
4367911d9d28d83fafbcf6c908698dd981ddbe9e.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a parameter- and hyperparameter-efficient framework for preference-based RL that completely eliminates the need for an explicit reward network. By leveraging the bijection between Q-functions and reward functions, IPL directly aligns the Q-function with human preferences, reducing computational cost, model complexity, and sources of variance. The approach is general, compatible with a wide range of RL algorithms, and achieves competitive or superior performance to state-of-the-art baselines, including those using large transformer architectures, while using significantly fewer parameters and exhibiting lower variance across runs.

43694ae3de01d0ebd730485b5890ed84094f7ad1.title: Disentanglement with Biological Constraints: A Theory of Functional Cell Types
43694ae3de01d0ebd730485b5890ed84094f7ad1.research_question: What fundamental principles underlie the emergence of disentangled neural representations in both biological and artificial neural networks, and how do biological constraints shape the selectivity and functional specialization of individual neurons?
43694ae3de01d0ebd730485b5890ed84094f7ad1.hypothesis: Imposing biologically inspired constraints such as nonnegativity and energy efficiency on neural activity and synaptic weights will promote disentangled representations, causing neurons to become selectively tuned to single factors of task variation.
43694ae3de01d0ebd730485b5890ed84094f7ad1.proposed_method: A mathematical framework will be developed to analyze the effects of nonnegativity and energy efficiency constraints on neural representations. The approach will involve formulating optimization problems for neural networks under these constraints and deriving theoretical results that predict neuron selectivity for individual task factors. The methodology will be applied to both simple and complex network architectures, including variational autoencoders, to assess the generality of the findings. Additionally, the theory will be leveraged to interpret the partitioning of biological neurons into distinct cell types and to predict when entangled versus disentangled representations should arise based on task structure.
43694ae3de01d0ebd730485b5890ed84094f7ad1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of tasks and neural network architectures, with a focus on both synthetic and biologically relevant datasets. Variational autoencoders and other standard models will be trained with and without the proposed biological constraints. Baseline comparisons will include unconstrained networks and networks with only partial constraints. Evaluation metrics will include disentanglement scores (e.g., single neuron selectivity, axis alignment with generative factors), reconstruction error, and energy usage. The experimental setup will systematically vary task structure to examine when disentanglement or entanglement emerges.
43694ae3de01d0ebd730485b5890ed84094f7ad1.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a mathematically grounded theory linking simple biological constraints to the emergence of disentangled representations, providing a unified explanation for both artificial and biological neural selectivity. It offers a new perspective on the functional partitioning of cell types in the brain and predicts when neural representations will be entangled or disentangled based on task demands. The approach is broadly applicable across architectures and tasks, bridging neuroscience and machine learning with rigorous theoretical and empirical analysis.

43737655c34a6f2a1446d1574e7830560c34bd2f.title: CFlowNets: Continuous Control with Generative Flow Networks
43737655c34a6f2a1446d1574e7830560c34bd2f.research_question: Can generative flow networks be extended to continuous control tasks, and do such methods offer advantages in exploration and performance compared to state-of-the-art reinforcement learning algorithms in continuous domains?
43737655c34a6f2a1446d1574e7830560c34bd2f.hypothesis: Generative flow networks, when adapted to continuous state and action spaces, will enable more effective exploration and improved performance in continuous control tasks compared to traditional reinforcement learning methods.
43737655c34a6f2a1446d1574e7830560c34bd2f.proposed_method: A novel framework, termed Continuous Flow Networks (CFlowNets), will be developed to generalize generative flow networks to continuous control settings. The approach will involve formulating continuous flow matching conditions, replacing summations with integrals, and defining a trajectory flow over continuous state-action trajectories. To approximate intractable integrals over inflows and outflows, importance sampling will be employed, with a deep neural network used to estimate parent states for sampled actions. The training procedure will include an action selection process where actions are sampled according to their flow values, a flow matching approximation using sampled actions, and optimization of a continuous flow matching loss function. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to establish error bounds for the flow approximation, showing that the error decreases rapidly with more samples.
43737655c34a6f2a1446d1574e7830560c34bd2f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several benchmark continuous control tasks with sparse rewards, including Point-Robot-Sparse, Reacher-Goal-Sparse, and Swimmer-Sparse environments. The CFlowNets approach will be compared against state-of-the-art reinforcement learning algorithms such as DDPG, TD3, PPO, and SAC. Evaluation metrics will include the number of valid-distinctive trajectories explored (as a measure of exploration) and average reward achieved during training. Experimental setups will involve collecting large numbers of trajectories, applying normalization and thresholding to define distinctive explorations, and reporting results with confidence intervals over multiple runs.
43737655c34a6f2a1446d1574e7830560c34bd2f.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to empirically demonstrate the effectiveness of generative flow networks on continuous control tasks. Key innovations include the extension of flow matching theory to continuous domains, the development of an efficient sampling and approximation framework for continuous inflows and outflows, and a theoretical analysis of the error bounds for flow approximation. The approach is claimed to significantly enhance exploration capabilities in continuous environments, outperforming existing reinforcement learning methods in tasks where exploration is critical.

4375a6c1053ad13e4528f9f34b6b9d0deedde638.title: Action Dubber: Timing Audible Actions via Inflectional Flow
4375a6c1053ad13e4528f9f34b6b9d0deedde638.research_question: How can the precise temporal and spatial localization of audible actions in silent videos be achieved using only visual information, and what frameworks can enable automated dubbing and sound source identification for visible, sound-producing actions?
4375a6c1053ad13e4528f9f34b6b9d0deedde638.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that abrupt kinematic changes, specifically inflectional movements detectable via the second derivative of motion (inflectional flow), serve as reliable visual priors for identifying the timing and location of audible actions in videos, even in the absence of audio input.
4375a6c1053ad13e4528f9f34b6b9d0deedde638.proposed_method: A novel framework, TA2Net, will be developed to temporally and spatially localize audible actions in silent videos by leveraging kinematic analysis. The method will estimate inflectional flow by computing the second derivative of motion (acceleration) from optical flow between video frames, under the assumption that collision-induced inflections correspond to audible events. The architecture will include three parallel encoders for visual frames, motion flow, and inflectional flow, followed by a cross-kinematics aggregation module that fuses these features using attention mechanisms. Additionally, a self-supervised auxiliary training strategy will be incorporated, employing contrastive learning and smoothness constraints to enhance spatial localization of motion regions associated with audible actions. The final prediction will be made via a spatio-temporal fusion module combining 3D convolutions and transformer-based self-attention.
4375a6c1053ad13e4528f9f34b6b9d0deedde638.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a newly curated dataset, Audible623, comprising 623 videos with frame-level annotations of audible actions, sourced from filtered subsets of Kinetics, UCF101, and YouTube. The model will be compared against eleven baselines spanning temporal action localization, repetitive action counting, action recognition, and anomaly detection, all fine-tuned under identical supervision. Evaluation metrics will include Recall, Precision, F1 score, Number Match Error (NME), Position Match Error (PME), as well as mean absolute error (MAE) and off-by-one accuracy (OBO) for counting tasks. Implementation will use a ResNet50 backbone, GMFlow for optical flow extraction, and training will be performed on an NVIDIA A800 GPU with Adam optimizer and specified hyperparameters. Ablation studies will assess the contributions of each module, and generalization will be tested on repetitive counting and sound source localization tasks.
4375a6c1053ad13e4528f9f34b6b9d0deedde638.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first dedicated framework and dataset for Audible Action Temporal Localization, focusing on visible, sound-producing actions at the frame level. The method pioneers the use of inflectional flow as a kinematic prior for detecting audible events without audio input, and integrates a self-supervised spatial localization strategy that combines contrastive and smoothness losses for enhanced spatio-temporal precision. The approach claims superior performance over existing methods in both localization and generalization to related tasks, such as repetitive action counting and sound source localization, establishing a new benchmark for automated video dubbing and editing applications.

43839821ffa50f4a24385a3519c5170c80224840.title: FAB-PPI: Frequentist, Assisted by Bayes, Prediction-Powered Inference
43839821ffa50f4a24385a3519c5170c80224840.research_question: How can statistical inference be improved by leveraging both labelled data and machine learning predictions, particularly when prior knowledge about prediction quality is available, while maintaining frequentist guarantees and robustness to poor predictions?
43839821ffa50f4a24385a3519c5170c80224840.hypothesis: Incorporating prior information about the quality of machine learning predictions into the prediction-powered inference (PPI) framework will yield more accurate estimates and tighter confidence intervals than traditional PPI or methods relying solely on labelled data, especially when predictions are generally reliable, while maintaining statistical validity and robustness in the presence of poor predictions.
43839821ffa50f4a24385a3519c5170c80224840.proposed_method: A novel framework, termed Frequentist, Assisted by Bayes, Prediction-Powered Inference (FAB-PPI), will be developed to enhance the PPI methodology by encoding prior beliefs about the quality of machine learning predictions into the inference process. The method introduces a prior (notably the horseshoe prior) over the rectifier term that quantifies the discrepancy between predictions and true labels, allowing the confidence regions to shrink adaptively when predictions are likely to be accurate and expand otherwise. The FAB construction is used to ensure that confidence intervals have exact frequentist coverage for any choice of prior, and the approach is robust: with heavy-tailed priors like the horseshoe, FAB-PPI reverts to standard PPI when predictions are poor. The method is modular and can be combined with power tuning (as in PPI++) for further efficiency. Implementation involves estimating the fit and rectifier terms from labelled and unlabelled data, applying the FAB framework to construct confidence regions, and solving for the parameter of interest using these enhanced estimators.
43839821ffa50f4a24385a3519c5170c80224840.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic experiments will involve scenarios with controlled bias and noise in predictions, varying the number of labelled and unlabelled samples, and manipulating the quality of the prediction rule to assess robustness and efficiency. Real-world experiments will use datasets such as GALAXIES, FOREST, ALPHAFOLD, HEALTHCARE, GENES, and CENSUS, covering tasks like mean estimation, odds ratio estimation, logistic regression, and quantile estimation. Baselines will include classical inference (labelled data only), standard PPI, and power-tuned PPI (PPI++). Evaluation metrics will include mean squared error (MSE) of the estimator, average confidence interval volume, and empirical coverage probability. Key setup details include using a large number of unlabelled samples, varying the number of labelled samples, and monitoring the effect of different priors (horseshoe vs. Gaussian) on the FAB-PPI procedure.
43839821ffa50f4a24385a3519c5170c80224840.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a Bayes-assisted approach to PPI that incorporates prior knowledge about prediction quality, resulting in confidence intervals that are adaptively shorter when predictions are good and robustly revert to standard PPI when predictions are poor. The use of the horseshoe prior within the FAB framework is highlighted for its ability to provide both efficiency and robustness, outperforming seemingly natural alternatives like the Gaussian prior. The method maintains exact frequentist coverage regardless of the prior and is modular, allowing integration with existing PPI enhancements such as power tuning. Empirical results demonstrate significant improvements in estimation accuracy and confidence interval tightness over existing methods, particularly in regimes with high-quality predictions.

43bb364bfad4d1adf8e7abb78d9a19608ae1181f.title: Safety Layers in Aligned Large Language Models: The Key to LLM Security
43bb364bfad4d1adf8e7abb78d9a19608ae1181f.research_question: What are the internal mechanisms by which aligned large language models (LLMs) recognize and refuse malicious queries, and how can these mechanisms be leveraged to defend against security degradation during fine-tuning attacks?
43bb364bfad4d1adf8e7abb78d9a19608ae1181f.hypothesis: A small set of contiguous layers within the middle of aligned LLMs, termed 'safety layers', are primarily responsible for distinguishing malicious from normal queries; by identifying and freezing these layers during fine-tuning, it is possible to preserve model security without sacrificing task performance.
43bb364bfad4d1adf8e7abb78d9a19608ae1181f.proposed_method: The proposed approach first conducts a detailed layer-wise analysis of aligned LLMs to identify safety layers responsible for security alignment. This involves inputting both normal and malicious queries into the model, extracting output vectors from each hidden layer, and computing cosine similarities and angular differences between vector pairs to detect where the model begins to differentiate malicious from normal inputs. The initial range of safety layers is refined by scaling the parameters of candidate layer ranges and measuring the impact on over-rejection rates using a dataset of non-malicious but potentially ambiguous queries. The most security-critical layers are those whose parameter scaling most strongly affects over-rejection. Building on this, a novel fine-tuning paradigm, Safely Partial-Parameter Fine-Tuning (SPPFT), is introduced, which freezes the gradients of the identified safety layers during downstream fine-tuning, allowing only the remaining parameters to be updated.
43bb364bfad4d1adf8e7abb78d9a19608ae1181f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four widely-used aligned LLMs: Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Llama-2-7b-chat, gemma-2b-it, and Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct, to ensure generalizability. The methodology includes evaluating the existence and localization of safety layers, followed by fine-tuning under various attack scenarios: normal data, implicit attacks, backdoor attacks, and harmful data attacks. Datasets include normal, implicit, and backdoor sets derived from Alpaca, as well as a malicious query dataset (520 samples) and an over-rejection dataset (721 samples). Baselines for comparison include full-parameter fine-tuning, neuron-freezing based on prior work, and the Lisa defense method. Evaluation metrics comprise harmful rate (proportion of malicious queries answered), harmful score (GPT-4-graded output toxicity), Rouge-L for task performance, and MMLU for general capability. Ablation studies will test the effect of freezing non-safety layers and discrete neurons.
43bb364bfad4d1adf8e7abb78d9a19608ae1181f.novelty_claims: The proposal is the first to identify and characterize 'safety layers' in the internal structure of aligned LLMs as the key mechanism for security alignment. It introduces a precise, generalizable algorithm for localizing these layers using a combination of vector similarity analysis and over-rejection phenomena. The Safely Partial-Parameter Fine-Tuning (SPPFT) method is a novel defense that preserves LLM security during fine-tuning by freezing only the safety layers, outperforming both full fine-tuning and existing neuron-freezing or parameter-freezing strategies. The approach is shown to maintain both security and downstream task performance with reduced computational cost, paving the way for safer deployment of LLMs in real-world applications.

43e624ddeed82df944a6cae0dedec3372438e243.title: Accelerating LLM Inference with Staged Speculative Decoding
43e624ddeed82df944a6cae0dedec3372438e243.research_question: How can the latency and computational efficiency of local, small-batch inference for large language models (LLMs) be improved without compromising output quality, particularly for on-device scenarios where privacy and personalization are important?
43e624ddeed82df944a6cae0dedec3372438e243.hypothesis: Introducing a staged speculative decoding algorithm, which restructures speculative batches as trees and adds an additional stage of speculation, will significantly reduce inference latency and improve computational efficiency for small-batch LLM inference while preserving output quality.
43e624ddeed82df944a6cae0dedec3372438e243.proposed_method: A novel staged speculative decoding framework will be developed to accelerate small-batch LLM inference. The method will restructure the speculative batch as a tree of possible token sequences, enabling more expected true tokens per batch, increased parallelism, and better utilization of memory bandwidth. Additionally, a second stage of speculative decoding will be introduced, wherein the draft model itself is speculatively decoded using an even smaller or faster model (e.g., an N-gram model). The approach will require partitioning self-attention into cross-attention with the KV cache and self-attention within the batch, constructing tree-structured batches via positional embeddings and causal masking, and managing KV cache updates for sampled tokens. The overall system will consist of an oracle model, a draft model, and a secondary draft (draft2) model, each contributing to a multi-stage speculative inference pipeline.
43e624ddeed82df944a6cae0dedec3372438e243.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a GPT-2-Large (762M parameters) model as the oracle, a 40M parameter GPT-2 model as the draft, and a Katz backoff trigram model as the secondary draft. All models will be fine-tuned on the Python subset of the Stack dataset. Evaluations will be performed on a consumer-grade RTX4090 GPU, using 164 prompts from the HumanEval benchmark. The proposed method will be compared against two baselines: standard token-by-token decoding and standard speculative decoding. Both deterministic (greedy) and top-k sampling regimes will be evaluated. Key metrics will include tokens per second (throughput), memory bandwidth consumption, and preservation of output quality.
43e624ddeed82df944a6cae0dedec3372438e243.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces two key innovations: (1) restructuring speculative batches as trees to increase expected tokens per batch and parallelism, and (2) adding an additional stage of speculation by speculatively decoding the draft model itself. This staged speculative decoding framework is claimed to achieve significant speedups (up to 3.16x over baseline) in small-batch LLM inference without sacrificing output quality, and to substantially reduce memory bandwidth usage. The approach is positioned as orthogonal to other inference optimization methods and particularly well-suited for on-device, privacy-preserving, and personalized LLM applications.

4411e6b32865933cab87696c2738cb7a204e4240.title: Implicit Chain of Thought Reasoning via Knowledge Distillation
4411e6b32865933cab87696c2738cb7a204e4240.research_question: Can language models be augmented to perform multi-step reasoning tasks efficiently and accurately without explicitly generating intermediate chain-of-thought steps, by leveraging their internal hidden states through knowledge distillation?
4411e6b32865933cab87696c2738cb7a204e4240.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that distilling explicit chain-of-thought reasoning from a teacher model into the internal hidden states of a student model will enable the student to perform implicit reasoning, allowing for direct answer generation on complex tasks with efficiency comparable to models without explicit reasoning steps.
4411e6b32865933cab87696c2738cb7a204e4240.proposed_method: A novel three-step methodology is proposed to enable implicit chain-of-thought reasoning in transformer-based language models. First, a student model is trained to generate final answers using the hidden states of a teacher model that has been trained to produce explicit chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning steps; this step is termed 'Mind-Reading the Teacher.' Next, an emulator is trained via knowledge distillation to predict the teacher's hidden states from the input, effectively emulating the teacher's internal reasoning process 'vertically' across layers, rather than 'horizontally' across generated tokens. Finally, the emulator and student are coupled and optimized end-to-end, allowing the student to generate answers directly from the emulated internal states, potentially developing novel internal reasoning trajectories. The method includes techniques for extracting and compressing hidden state representations (e.g., diagonal extraction, mixture modeling for multiple reasoning pathways), and supports both fixed and variable-length reasoning chains.
4411e6b32865933cab87696c2738cb7a204e4240.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two primary tasks: multi-digit multiplication (4x4 and 5x5) from the BIG-bench benchmark, and grade school math word problems using the GSM8K dataset. Synthetic data augmentation will be employed to generate large-scale training sets for both tasks, ensuring sufficient data for the proposed training paradigm. Baselines will include no chain-of-thought (NoCoT) and explicit chain-of-thought (ExplicitCoT) approaches, with models such as GPT-2 Small, Medium, and Large, as well as comparisons to ChatGPT and GPT-4 under few-shot prompting. Evaluation metrics will include exact match accuracy for final answer generation and inference throughput (examples per second), with detailed ablations on hidden state extraction strategies and mixture modeling for reasoning diversity.
4411e6b32865933cab87696c2738cb7a204e4240.novelty_claims: The approach introduces the concept of implicit chain-of-thought reasoning, where multi-step reasoning is performed internally via the model's hidden states rather than explicit token generation. The three-step strategy—mind-reading the teacher, thought emulation, and end-to-end coupling and optimization—enables efficient knowledge distillation of explicit reasoning into implicit internal processes. The method demonstrates that transformer models can be trained to solve complex reasoning tasks directly, with inference speeds significantly higher than explicit CoT models and without sacrificing much accuracy compared to traditional baselines. The proposal also presents new techniques for compressing and emulating internal reasoning states, and for handling multiple reasoning pathways through mixture modeling.

442e10a3c6640ded9408622005e3c2a8906ce4c2.title: A Unified Approach to Interpreting Model Predictions
442e10a3c6640ded9408622005e3c2a8906ce4c2.research_question: How can a unified, theoretically sound framework be developed to interpret the predictions of complex machine learning models in a way that is both accurate and consistent with human intuition?
442e10a3c6640ded9408622005e3c2a8906ce4c2.hypothesis: A unified framework based on additive feature attribution methods, uniquely determined by properties such as local accuracy, missingness, and consistency, will provide more reliable and interpretable explanations of model predictions than existing approaches.
442e10a3c6640ded9408622005e3c2a8906ce4c2.proposed_method: A novel framework is introduced that unifies and generalizes existing additive feature attribution methods for model interpretation. The approach defines explanation models as linear functions of binary variables representing feature presence, and demonstrates that only one solution within this class satisfies the properties of local accuracy, missingness, and consistency—namely, the Shapley values from cooperative game theory. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values are proposed as the unique, theoretically justified measure of feature importance for individual predictions, computed as the average marginal contribution of each feature across all possible feature orderings. Several estimation algorithms are developed, including model-agnostic (KernelSHAP, Shapley sampling) and model-specific (LinearSHAP, DeepSHAP, MaxSHAP) approximations, leveraging both regression-based and compositional strategies to improve computational efficiency and scalability.
442e10a3c6640ded9408622005e3c2a8906ce4c2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted to compare the computational efficiency, accuracy, and human-alignment of SHAP-based explanations against existing methods such as LIME, DeepLIFT, and Shapley sampling values. Datasets include decision tree models with both dense and sparse feature usage, as well as deep neural networks trained on the MNIST digit image dataset. Evaluation metrics will include sample efficiency (number of model evaluations required), agreement with human explanations (via user studies on Amazon Mechanical Turk), and the ability to discriminate between model output classes. Additional experiments will assess the impact of masking features according to different attribution methods and measure the resulting change in model predictions.
442e10a3c6640ded9408622005e3c2a8906ce4c2.novelty_claims: The proposed framework uniquely unifies six existing feature attribution methods under a single class of additive explanation models and proves that SHAP values are the only solution satisfying key desirable properties. New estimation algorithms, such as KernelSHAP and DeepSHAP, are introduced to improve computational efficiency and alignment with human intuition. The approach provides theoretical guarantees, improved sample efficiency, and empirical evidence of superior consistency with human explanations compared to prior methods.

445a134e46b2fc8c8905f8b971efed20a97e68cb.title: Isotropic Noise in Stochastic and Quantum Convex Optimization
445a134e46b2fc8c8905f8b971efed20a97e68cb.research_question: Can shape-dependent assumptions on the noise in stochastic gradient oracles, particularly isotropic noise, lead to improved algorithmic guarantees and query complexity in high-dimensional stochastic and quantum convex optimization, compared to traditional variance-based models?
445a134e46b2fc8c8905f8b971efed20a97e68cb.hypothesis: Assuming isotropic or sub-exponential noise in stochastic gradient oracles enables the development of algorithms for stochastic and quantum convex optimization that achieve improved, dimension-dependent query complexities over standard variance-bounded approaches.
445a134e46b2fc8c8905f8b971efed20a97e68cb.proposed_method: A novel stochastic cutting plane algorithm will be developed for convex optimization, leveraging a new isotropic noise model for stochastic gradient oracles. The method will formalize and utilize the notion of isotropic stochastic gradient oracles (ISGOs), where the noise is bounded in every direction with high probability, and extend to sub-exponential noise models. The algorithm will implement a marginal approximate gradient oracle (MAGO) using ISGO queries, ensuring tight control of error in specific directions, and will use mini-batching and post-processing to guarantee high-probability convergence to optimality. For the quantum setting, a quantum isotropifier subroutine will be designed to convert a quantum variance-bounded stochastic gradient oracle (QVSGO) into one with isotropic error, enabling the application of the improved cutting plane method in quantum stochastic convex optimization.
445a134e46b2fc8c8905f8b971efed20a97e68cb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic convex optimization problems, using d-dimensional Lipschitz convex functions with known minimizers and bounded domains. The proposed algorithms will be evaluated under different oracle models: ISGO, ESGO (sub-exponential), and VSGO (variance-bounded), as well as their quantum analogs. Baselines will include standard stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and existing quantum algorithms for stochastic convex optimization. Evaluation metrics will focus on query complexity (number of oracle calls to reach epsilon-optimality), dependence on dimension d, and robustness to noise structure. Lower bounds will be established via reductions to mean estimation problems, and tightness of the upper bounds will be empirically and theoretically validated.
445a134e46b2fc8c8905f8b971efed20a97e68cb.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new, shape-dependent isotropic noise model for stochastic gradient oracles and demonstrates that this model enables improved, dimension-dependent query complexity for stochastic convex optimization, outperforming traditional variance-based approaches in certain regimes. The method achieves state-of-the-art complexity for sub-exponential noise and provides matching lower bounds up to polylogarithmic factors. In the quantum setting, the introduction of a quantum isotropifier enables unbiased, isotropic mean estimation, leading to polynomial improvements in query complexity for quantum stochastic convex optimization. The approach unifies and extends existing frameworks, offering broader applicability and improved theoretical guarantees.

447b7fa233fe9b129001f0bb7f5c4a900de29e5d.title: SAEBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Sparse Autoencoders in Language Model Interpretability
447b7fa233fe9b129001f0bb7f5c4a900de29e5d.research_question: How can the evaluation of sparse autoencoders (SAEs) for language model interpretability be made more comprehensive and practically relevant, moving beyond traditional proxy metrics to better assess interpretability, feature disentanglement, and practical downstream applications?
447b7fa233fe9b129001f0bb7f5c4a900de29e5d.hypothesis: A comprehensive benchmark suite that evaluates SAEs across multiple diverse metrics—including interpretability, feature disentanglement, reconstruction fidelity, and practical applications—will provide a more accurate and actionable assessment of SAE quality than reliance on traditional sparsity-fidelity proxy metrics alone.
447b7fa233fe9b129001f0bb7f5c4a900de29e5d.proposed_method: A unified evaluation framework, SAEBench, will be developed to systematically assess sparse autoencoders on eight distinct metrics spanning four fundamental capabilities: concept detection, interpretability, reconstruction, and feature disentanglement. The methodology will include both established and novel metrics, such as automated LLM-based interpretability scoring, sparse probing, RAVEL disentanglement, feature absorption, unlearning capability, spurious correlation removal, and targeted probe perturbation. The benchmark will be designed for extensibility, automation, and reproducibility, enabling rapid and fair comparison across SAE architectures and training methodologies. Over 200 SAEs, encompassing seven recent architectures and a variety of training algorithms, will be trained and evaluated across a wide range of dictionary sizes and sparsity levels. An interactive interface will be provided for visualization and analysis of metric relationships.
447b7fa233fe9b129001f0bb7f5c4a900de29e5d.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training and evaluating more than 200 SAEs with varying architectures (including ReLU, MatryoshkaBatchTopK, TopK, BatchTopK, Gated, JumpReLU, and P-Annealing) and dictionary sizes (4k, 16k, 65k, 131k, and 1M latents). Evaluations will be conducted on residual stream activations from middle layers of large language models such as Gemma-2-2B and Pythia-160M, with sparsity levels (L0) ranging from 20 to 1000. Baselines will include direct probing of residual stream channels and existing SAE variants. Metrics will cover both unsupervised (e.g., loss recovered, automated interpretability) and supervised (e.g., sparse probing, RAVEL, unlearning) tasks, with supervised metrics using labeled datasets like WMDP-bio and MMLU. Evaluation scripts will be fully automated and deterministic to ensure reproducibility. Results will be analyzed for scaling trends, architecture comparisons, and the impact of sparsity and dictionary size on downstream performance.
447b7fa233fe9b129001f0bb7f5c4a900de29e5d.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces a comprehensive, multi-metric evaluation suite for sparse autoencoders, addressing the limitations of traditional proxy metrics by incorporating both established and novel metrics for feature disentanglement and practical applications. The framework enables systematic, reproducible, and extensible comparison across a wide variety of SAE architectures and training regimes. Novel metrics such as improved feature absorption detection, advanced unlearning evaluation, and targeted probe perturbation are adapted and generalized for broad applicability. The benchmark provides actionable insights into scaling trends, architecture-specific trade-offs, and optimal sparsity levels, offering a valuable resource for both researchers and practitioners in neural network interpretability.

44800883e82c7bc7c45c2adb6257cd0a0be42610.title: Generalized Logit Adjustment: Calibrating Fine-tuned Models by Removing Label Bias in Foundation Models
44800883e82c7bc7c45c2adb6257cd0a0be42610.research_question: How can the inherent label bias present in large pre-trained foundation models be effectively mitigated to improve downstream task performance across various fine-tuning paradigms and data regimes, including many-shot, few-shot, and long-tailed scenarios?
44800883e82c7bc7c45c2adb6257cd0a0be42610.hypothesis: Mitigating the label bias in foundation models—by estimating and removing the bias introduced by skewed pre-training distributions—will lead to improved accuracy and robustness in downstream tasks when combining fine-tuned and zero-shot models, outperforming current fine-tuning and ensembling methods.
44800883e82c7bc7c45c2adb6257cd0a0be42610.proposed_method: A novel post-hoc framework, Generalized Logit Adjustment (GLA), will be developed to address label bias in foundation models. The method consists of two main steps: (1) estimating the pre-training label distribution bias using only downstream labeled data and the zero-shot model, formulated as a constrained optimization problem that minimizes empirical risk; and (2) ensembling the fine-tuned model and the debiased zero-shot model by combining their logits and subtracting the estimated biases, resulting in a Bayes-optimal classifier for class-balanced target distributions. The estimation of the pre-training label bias is achieved without access to the original pre-training data, making the approach practical for real-world scenarios. The debiasing and ensembling are performed in logit space, and the method does not require hyperparameter tuning for the ensemble ratio.
44800883e82c7bc7c45c2adb6257cd0a0be42610.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across three real-world scenarios: many-shot learning (using datasets such as ImageNet, CIFAR100, Stanford Cars, and SUN397), few-shot learning (with 11-15 datasets including ImageNet, Caltech101, OxfordPets, and others), and long-tailed classification (using ImageNet-LT and Places365-LT). The proposed method will be compared against baselines including zero-shot models, linear probing, end-to-end fine-tuning, prompt tuning, and state-of-the-art ensembling and long-tail learning methods such as WiSE-FT, ProGrad, CoOp, PLOT, BALLAD, LWS, LA, BS, and ERM. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy and breakdowns by head, medium, and tail classes. Experimental setups will involve different backbone architectures (e.g., CLIP ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16, ResNet-50), standard fine-tuning protocols, and robust evaluation under distribution shifts. Implementation details such as optimizer choice, learning rate schedules, and training epochs will follow established best practices for each dataset and protocol.
44800883e82c7bc7c45c2adb6257cd0a0be42610.novelty_claims: The proposed approach identifies and directly addresses the overlooked issue of label bias in foundation models caused by highly imbalanced pre-training data. The method introduces a theoretically justified, optimization-based bias estimation process that does not require access to pre-training data, making it broadly applicable. GLA is proven to be Bayes-optimal for ensembling fine-tuned and zero-shot models, and it outperforms both naive ensembling and state-of-the-art methods across a wide range of tasks and data regimes. The framework is general, simple to implement, and demonstrates transferable bias estimates across different model architectures, providing consistent improvements in accuracy, especially for rare (tail) classes.

448e7e873a6e520072301b7d9c1d0d9289778418.title: InstaFlow: One Step is Enough for High-Quality Diffusion-Based Text-to-Image Generation
448e7e873a6e520072301b7d9c1d0d9289778418.research_question: Can large-scale diffusion-based text-to-image generation models be accelerated to achieve high-quality image synthesis in a single inference step, while maintaining or surpassing the image quality of existing multi-step or GAN-based approaches?
448e7e873a6e520072301b7d9c1d0d9289778418.hypothesis: Applying a text-conditioned rectified flow framework with reflow to straighten probability flow trajectories, followed by supervised distillation, enables the training of a one-step diffusion-based text-to-image generator that matches or exceeds the image quality of state-of-the-art multi-step diffusion and GAN-based models.
448e7e873a6e520072301b7d9c1d0d9289778418.proposed_method: A novel text-conditioned generative pipeline is proposed that transforms a pre-trained diffusion-based text-to-image model, such as Stable Diffusion, into a one-step generator. The approach begins by applying a text-conditioned reflow procedure to the probability flow ODE of the pre-trained model, straightening the trajectories between noise and image distributions. This is achieved by iteratively optimizing a velocity field using a mean squared error objective over linearly interpolated data pairs, conditioned on text prompts. Once the flow is sufficiently straightened, supervised distillation is performed, training a student model to approximate the one-step mapping from noise to image using a differentiable similarity loss (e.g., LPIPS) between the output of the straightened teacher flow and the student. The method incorporates classifier-free guidance for improved semantic alignment and can be scaled up by increasing model size (e.g., stacking U-Nets) and training duration.
448e7e873a6e520072301b7d9c1d0d9289778418.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using the MS COCO 2017 (5,000 images) and MS COCO 2014 (30,000 images) datasets, with text prompts sampled from laion2B-en and filtered as in Stable Diffusion. The evaluation metrics include Frechet Inception Distance (FID) for image quality and CLIP score for semantic alignment. Baselines for comparison include multi-step Stable Diffusion, progressive distillation, StyleGAN-T, GigaGAN, and other state-of-the-art diffusion and GAN-based models. Training is performed on A100 GPUs, with batch sizes of 32 and up to 199 GPU days for the largest models. The inference time per image and the effect of guidance scale are also systematically measured. Ablation studies are conducted on model architecture and the effect of reflow versus direct distillation.
448e7e873a6e520072301b7d9c1d0d9289778418.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first one-step diffusion-based text-to-image generator that achieves image quality on par with or surpassing state-of-the-art GANs and multi-step diffusion models, using only supervised learning. The method leverages a novel text-conditioned reflow procedure to straighten probability flow trajectories, enabling effective distillation into a one-step model. This framework closes the gap between continuous-time diffusion models and one-step generative models, achieving unprecedented efficiency (0.09s per image) and FID scores (e.g., 23.3 on MS COCO 2017-5k, 13.1 on MS COCO 2014-30k), and demonstrates scalability to larger model sizes with further improvements in quality.

449532187c94af3dd3aa55e16d2c50f7854d2199.title: Trust Region Policy Optimization
449532187c94af3dd3aa55e16d2c50f7854d2199.research_question: How can policy optimization in reinforcement learning be improved to achieve reliable, monotonic performance gains with scalable, sample-efficient algorithms, especially for high-dimensional, nonlinear policy classes such as neural networks?
449532187c94af3dd3aa55e16d2c50f7854d2199.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that constraining policy updates within a trust region, measured by the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between successive policies, will yield monotonic improvements in expected return and enable efficient optimization of complex, high-dimensional policies.
449532187c94af3dd3aa55e16d2c50f7854d2199.proposed_method: A novel policy optimization algorithm, Trust Region Policy Optimization (TRPO), is proposed. This method iteratively updates the policy by maximizing a surrogate objective function subject to a constraint on the average KL divergence between the new and old policies, ensuring each update stays within a 'trust region.' The surrogate objective is constructed using estimated advantage values, and two sampling schemes are considered: the single path method, which samples entire trajectories, and the vine method, which samples multiple rollouts from selected states to reduce variance. The optimization problem is solved using conjugate gradient methods with a line search, and the Fisher information matrix is computed analytically for scalability. The approach is designed to be applicable to arbitrary parameterized policies, including large neural networks, and is robust to hyperparameter tuning.
449532187c94af3dd3aa55e16d2c50f7854d2199.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a suite of challenging reinforcement learning tasks, including simulated robotic locomotion (swimming, hopping, walking) using the MuJoCo simulator, and Atari game playing from raw pixel inputs. Policy architectures include both fully connected and convolutional neural networks with tens of thousands of parameters. Baselines for comparison include natural policy gradient, cross-entropy method (CEM), covariance matrix adaptation (CMA), and other policy optimization variants. Evaluation metrics include total episodic reward, sample complexity, and learning curves averaged over multiple random seeds. The experimental setup varies the sampling method (single path vs. vine), the form of the KL constraint (average vs. maximum), and compares the effect of fixed penalty coefficients versus hard KL constraints.
449532187c94af3dd3aa55e16d2c50f7854d2199.novelty_claims: The proposed method provides the first practical, scalable algorithm for policy optimization with guaranteed monotonic improvement for general stochastic policies, including large nonlinear neural networks. It unifies and generalizes prior approaches such as policy gradient, natural policy gradient, and conservative policy iteration, and introduces a robust trust region constraint based on KL divergence. The algorithm demonstrates strong empirical performance on both continuous control and high-dimensional vision-based tasks, with minimal hyperparameter tuning and without reliance on hand-engineered policy classes or reward shaping.

44999d9bae3976d38e91b742c4541a21c7000260.title: MotionCtrl: A Unified and Flexible Motion Controller for Video Generation
44999d9bae3976d38e91b742c4541a21c7000260.research_question: How can a unified and flexible motion controller be developed to enable independent and fine-grained control of both camera and object motion in video generation models, thereby enhancing the diversity, realism, and user control of generated videos?
44999d9bae3976d38e91b742c4541a21c7000260.hypothesis: A modular framework that disentangles and independently controls camera and object motion—by integrating dedicated modules into a video diffusion model and leveraging appearance-free motion conditions—will enable more precise, flexible, and generalizable motion control in video generation compared to existing approaches.
44999d9bae3976d38e91b742c4541a21c7000260.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that introduces two specialized modules: a Camera Motion Control Module (CMCM) and an Object Motion Control Module (OMCM), each tailored to the unique properties of global (camera) and local (object) motion. The CMCM will integrate camera pose sequences (represented as rotation and translation matrices) into the temporal transformers of a latent video diffusion model (LVDM), using a lightweight fully connected network to encode pose features and inject them at the appropriate attention layers. The OMCM will spatially incorporate object movement trajectories—processed through multi-scale convolutional layers—into the convolutional layers of the video generation model, guiding object motion in each frame. A multi-step training strategy will be employed: the CMCM will be trained first using a dataset with camera pose annotations, followed by OMCM training on a dataset with synthesized object trajectories. Both modules are designed as adapter-like components to preserve the underlying model's generative quality and allow for independent or joint motion control.
