44999d9bae3976d38e91b742c4541a21c7000260.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Realestate10K dataset (augmented with captions) for camera motion control training and the WebVid dataset (augmented with object trajectories synthesized via ParticleSfM) for object motion control. Evaluation will be performed on both basic and complex camera poses, as well as diverse handcrafted object trajectories, using metrics such as Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Fréchet Video Distance (FVD), CLIP Similarity (CLIPSIM), and custom metrics for camera (CamMC) and object (ObjMC) motion control accuracy. Baselines will include AnimateDiff and VideoComposer, with comparisons made on both qualitative and quantitative grounds. Ablation studies will test module integration points, trajectory sparsity, and training order. The model will be trained on 16-frame, 256x256 resolution sequences, with optimization details specified (Adam optimizer, batch size 128, learning rate 1e-4, 8 GPUs).
44999d9bae3976d38e91b742c4541a21c7000260.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable truly independent and fine-grained control of both camera and object motion within a unified video generation model, using disentangled, appearance-free motion conditions (camera poses and object trajectories). The modular design allows for flexible and diverse combinations of motion types, and the training strategy overcomes the lack of comprehensive annotated datasets by leveraging separate, augmented sources for each motion type. The method achieves superior motion control precision and video quality compared to state-of-the-art baselines, and demonstrates generalizability to a wide range of motion conditions without the need for per-motion fine-tuning.

44a32991258416e1fb0bbc2d91a960edce960f2e.title: Optimistic Whittle Index Policy: Online Learning for Restless Bandits
44a32991258416e1fb0bbc2d91a960edce960f2e.research_question: How can online learning algorithms be developed to efficiently solve restless multi-armed bandit (RMAB) problems when the transition dynamics are unknown, while achieving low regret and maintaining computational scalability?
44a32991258416e1fb0bbc2d91a960edce960f2e.hypothesis: An online learning algorithm that leverages upper confidence bounds (UCB) to estimate transition dynamics and computes optimistic Whittle indices can achieve sublinear frequentist regret in RMABs with unknown transitions, outperforming existing online learning baselines.
44a32991258416e1fb0bbc2d91a960edce960f2e.proposed_method: A novel online learning approach is proposed for RMABs with unknown transition probabilities, based on the Whittle index policy. The method maintains empirical estimates and confidence bounds for each transition probability of every arm using observed data. At each episode, a bilinear program is formulated to compute optimistic transition probabilities within the confidence bounds that maximize the expected future value or Whittle index for each arm. These optimistic transitions are then used to calculate optimistic Whittle indices, and a Whittle index threshold policy is executed by selecting the top-K arms with the highest indices. The penalty parameter for the Lagrangian relaxation is adaptively updated using a saddle-point or heuristic rule, ensuring the policy respects resource constraints while maximizing long-term reward.
44a32991258416e1fb0bbc2d91a960edce960f2e.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted across three domains: two synthetic RMAB settings (Wide Margin and Thin Margin) and one real-world domain constructed from a maternal and child healthcare dataset (ARMMAN). Each domain involves binary-state, binary-action arms, with rewards and transitions designed to reflect realistic or challenging scenarios. The proposed method is compared to several baselines, including ExtremeWhittle (using extreme confidence bounds), WIQL (Q-learning-based), and a random policy, as well as an oracle policy with true transitions. Evaluation metrics include cumulative discounted regret over multiple episodes, with results averaged over 30 random seeds. Key experimental variables such as the number of arms, budget, episode length, and discount factor are systematically varied to assess scalability and robustness.
44a32991258416e1fb0bbc2d91a960edce960f2e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first online learning algorithm for RMABs based on the Whittle index policy that achieves sublinear frequentist regret guarantees. It introduces a bilinear program to compute optimistic Whittle indices using UCB-based confidence bounds on transition dynamics, enabling scalable and decomposable policy computation. The method provides the first frequentist regret analysis for RMABs with unknown transitions, and demonstrates empirical superiority over existing baselines across multiple domains, including a real-world healthcare application. Additionally, a computationally efficient heuristic variant is proposed that maintains strong empirical performance.

44a9d8b0314d34aff91ccff9207d38eed37216ed.title: Iterative Preference Learning from Human Feedback: Bridging Theory and Practice for RLHF under KL-constraint
44a9d8b0314d34aff91ccff9207d38eed37216ed.research_question: How can reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) for aligning large generative models be theoretically grounded and improved, particularly under KL-constraint regularization, to address challenges such as insufficient exploration, reward over-optimization, and limited coverage in preference datasets?
44a9d8b0314d34aff91ccff9207d38eed37216ed.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that formulating RLHF as a reverse-KL regularized contextual bandit problem and developing algorithms with principled theoretical guarantees in offline, online, and hybrid settings will lead to more sample-efficient, robust, and performant alignment of generative models compared to existing methods.
44a9d8b0314d34aff91ccff9207d38eed37216ed.proposed_method: The proposed approach formalizes RLHF as a reverse-KL regularized contextual bandit problem, where the objective is to maximize expected reward while constraining the learned policy to remain close to the initial (pretrained) policy via a KL-divergence penalty. The methodology involves developing efficient algorithms for three settings: (1) offline RLHF, leveraging pessimistic (conservative) reward estimation to ensure sample efficiency and robustness to distributional shift; (2) online RLHF, introducing iterative policy improvement with strategic batch exploration and continuous human feedback; and (3) hybrid RLHF, combining elements of both offline and online learning. Key algorithmic innovations include an iterative version of Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) for online settings, a multi-step rejection sampling strategy for offline learning, and robust approximations of the information-theoretical policy improvement oracle. The framework is designed to be compatible with existing planning algorithms such as PPO, DPO, and InfoNCA, and incorporates covariance-based uncertainty estimation to guide exploration and generalization.
44a9d8b0314d34aff91ccff9207d38eed37216ed.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on real-world large language model (LLM) alignment tasks, using Zephyr-SFT-7B as the initial model and evaluating on the AlpacaEval2 benchmark. The proposed algorithms will be compared against strong baselines, including standard DPO and Rejection Sampling Optimization (RSO). Evaluation metrics will include win-rate against baseline models, robustness to sampling temperature and length bias, and empirical sample efficiency. Both offline and online/hybrid learning scenarios will be tested, with ablation studies to assess the impact of online exploration, pseudo-labeling, and iterative learning. Implementation details will follow standard RLHF pipelines, with additional analysis of scaling behavior and robustness.
44a9d8b0314d34aff91ccff9207d38eed37216ed.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a rigorous mathematical formulation of RLHF as a reverse-KL regularized contextual bandit, bridging theoretical analysis and practical algorithmic design. It provides the first finite-sample theoretical guarantees for RLHF under KL-constraint in offline, online, and hybrid settings. The approach yields new algorithms, including iterative DPO for online learning and multi-step rejection sampling for offline learning, and demonstrates that these methods outperform existing strong baselines in real-world LLM alignment experiments. The framework also establishes a principled connection between information-theoretic policy improvement oracles and practical RLHF implementations.

44e4a3a50df9ec80be096c8341ac5c81ecbea3e8.title: Simplifying, Stabilizing and Scaling Continuous-Time Consistency Models
44e4a3a50df9ec80be096c8341ac5c81ecbea3e8.research_question: How can continuous-time consistency models for generative modeling be simplified, stabilized, and scaled to achieve high sample quality and efficient sampling, particularly at large model and dataset scales?
44e4a3a50df9ec80be096c8341ac5c81ecbea3e8.hypothesis: Continuous-time consistency models can be made as stable, scalable, and performant as discrete-time models by unifying and simplifying their theoretical formulation, improving parameterization, network architecture, and training objectives, thereby enabling efficient few-step sampling with high sample quality.
44e4a3a50df9ec80be096c8341ac5c81ecbea3e8.proposed_method: A novel theoretical framework, TrigFlow, will be developed to unify and simplify the parameterization of diffusion models and consistency models, allowing for straightforward expressions of the diffusion process, probability flow ODE, and model parameterization. The method will introduce improvements in network architecture, including identity time transformation for time conditioning, positional time embeddings to mitigate instability, and adaptive double normalization to stabilize normalization layers. Training objectives will be enhanced with tangent normalization or clipping to control gradient variance, and an adaptive weighting function will be jointly trained to minimize loss variance across timesteps. The approach will support both consistency training (from scratch) and consistency distillation (from a pretrained diffusion model), and will include techniques for numerically stable tangent computation and efficient Jacobian-vector product calculation in large-scale models.
44e4a3a50df9ec80be096c8341ac5c81ecbea3e8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on CIFAR-10, ImageNet 64×64, and ImageNet 512×512 datasets, scaling models up to 1.5 billion parameters. Both consistency training (sCT) and consistency distillation (sCD) will be evaluated. Baselines will include state-of-the-art diffusion models (e.g., EDM2), fast samplers, GANs, and other few-step generative models such as VSD and progressive distillation. Evaluation metrics will primarily be Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), as well as precision and recall for sample diversity and fidelity. The number of function evaluations (NFEs) will be reported to assess sampling efficiency. Experiments will ablate the impact of each proposed improvement, assess scaling behavior, and compare performance under varying guidance scales and sampling steps.
44e4a3a50df9ec80be096c8341ac5c81ecbea3e8.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces TrigFlow, a unified and simplified formulation that bridges EDM and flow matching, enabling theoretically grounded and practical continuous-time consistency models. Key innovations include principled improvements to time conditioning, normalization, and training objectives, resulting in stable and scalable training at unprecedented model sizes. The method enables few-step sampling (as low as two steps) with sample quality that closely matches or exceeds state-of-the-art diffusion models, while requiring significantly less sampling compute. Additional contributions include efficient tangent computation for large-scale models and empirical evidence that continuous-time models outperform discrete-time counterparts when properly stabilized.

451f022af13697d943d2f31b8d885e6b7274abb8.title: Nearly d-Linear Convergence Bounds for Diffusion Models via Stochastic Localization
451f022af13697d943d2f31b8d885e6b7274abb8.research_question: What are the fundamental convergence rates of denoising diffusion models for sampling from high-dimensional data distributions, under minimal smoothness assumptions, and how do these rates scale with the data dimension?
451f022af13697d943d2f31b8d885e6b7274abb8.hypothesis: Diffusion models can achieve nearly linear convergence rates in the data dimension (up to logarithmic factors) for approximating arbitrary distributions with finite second moments, without requiring strong smoothness assumptions on the data distribution.
451f022af13697d943d2f31b8d885e6b7274abb8.proposed_method: A new theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the convergence rates of denoising diffusion models by extending Girsanov-based techniques and incorporating tools from stochastic localization. The approach will focus on the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck (OU) process as the forward noising SDE, with the reverse process learned via score-based methods. The analysis will introduce a refined treatment of the time discretization error in the reverse SDE, leveraging a key lemma inspired by stochastic localization to tightly control the expected difference between drift terms at different times. The method will assume only finite second moments for the data distribution and will employ early stopping to avoid issues with non-smooth score functions near the initial time. Theoretical results will be derived to bound the KL divergence between the true and approximate distributions, with explicit dependence on the data dimension, discretization steps, and score approximation error.
451f022af13697d943d2f31b8d885e6b7274abb8.experiment_details: The proposal centers on rigorous theoretical analysis rather than empirical experiments. Theoretical 'experiments' will involve bounding the KL divergence between the generated and target distributions under various choices of discretization step sizes, number of steps, and score approximation errors. The analysis will compare the obtained bounds with existing state-of-the-art results, particularly those that are quadratic in the data dimension or require Lipschitz score assumptions. The evaluation metric will be the number of discretization steps required to achieve a given KL divergence error (ε²), with explicit scaling in the data dimension d and noise parameter δ. Theoretical baselines will include previous polynomial and superlinear convergence bounds for diffusion models.
451f022af13697d943d2f31b8d885e6b7274abb8.novelty_claims: The proposed research will establish the first convergence bounds for diffusion models that are linear in the data dimension (up to logarithmic factors) under only finite second moment assumptions, removing the need for strong smoothness or Lipschitz conditions on the score. The analysis introduces a novel application of stochastic localization techniques to control discretization error in the reverse SDE, resulting in tighter and more general convergence guarantees. The work will resolve an open question regarding the optimal scaling of iteration complexity with respect to data dimension for diffusion models, and will provide a new theoretical foundation for understanding the efficiency of these models in high-dimensional settings.

4530c25da949bb2185c50663158ef19d52e3c6b5.title: DPM-Solver: A Fast ODE Solver for Diffusion Probabilistic Model Sampling in Around 10 Steps
4530c25da949bb2185c50663158ef19d52e3c6b5.research_question: How can the sampling speed of diffusion probabilistic models (DPMs) be significantly accelerated, particularly in the few-step regime, without requiring additional training or sacrificing sample quality?
4530c25da949bb2185c50663158ef19d52e3c6b5.hypothesis: By leveraging the semi-linear structure of diffusion ODEs and analytically computing the linear part of the solution, it is possible to design high-order, training-free solvers that enable high-quality sample generation from DPMs in as few as 10 function evaluations.
4530c25da949bb2185c50663158ef19d52e3c6b5.proposed_method: A novel framework, DPM-Solver, will be developed as a dedicated high-order solver for diffusion ordinary differential equations (ODEs) underlying DPMs. The approach begins by deriving an exact solution formulation for diffusion ODEs, analytically computing the linear component and simplifying the nonlinear component to an exponentially weighted integral of the neural network noise prediction model. This integral will be efficiently approximated using numerical methods inspired by exponential integrators. Multiple solver variants will be implemented, including first-, second-, and third-order methods, each with theoretical convergence guarantees. The method will support both continuous-time and discrete-time DPMs, and will include both handcrafted (uniform in log-SNR space) and adaptive step size schedules to optimize performance across different settings.
4530c25da949bb2185c50663158ef19d52e3c6b5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of standard image generation datasets, including CIFAR-10, CelebA 64x64, ImageNet 64x64, ImageNet 128x128, and LSUN bedroom 256x256. Both continuous-time and discrete-time DPMs with various noise schedules (linear and cosine) will be evaluated. The proposed DPM-Solver will be compared against state-of-the-art training-free samplers such as DDIM, Analytic-DDIM, PNDM, FastDPM, and traditional ODE solvers like Runge-Kutta (RK45), as well as training-based methods like GGDM. Evaluation metrics will include the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) to assess sample quality, with a focus on the number of function evaluations (NFE) required to achieve competitive results. Experimental setups will include both unconditional and conditional (classifier-guided) sampling scenarios, and ablation studies will analyze the impact of solver order and step size scheduling.
4530c25da949bb2185c50663158ef19d52e3c6b5.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first dedicated high-order, training-free ODE solver for DPMs that leverages the semi-linear structure of the underlying equations. By analytically computing the linear term and directly approximating the exponentially weighted integral of the noise prediction model, the approach achieves significantly reduced discretization error compared to traditional black-box ODE solvers. The method enables high-quality sample generation in as few as 10 function evaluations, representing a 4–16× speedup over previous state-of-the-art training-free samplers. The framework is broadly applicable to both continuous- and discrete-time DPMs, does not require retraining or model modification, and provides theoretical convergence guarantees for its high-order solvers.

4538e353dd98f396c8facc29ebb72e9b1ba5f7c2.title: Synthetic Data from Diffusion Models Improves ImageNet Classification
4538e353dd98f396c8facc29ebb72e9b1ba5f7c2.research_question: Can large-scale text-to-image diffusion models, when fine-tuned for class-conditional image generation, produce synthetic data that is effective for augmenting training in challenging discriminative tasks such as ImageNet classification?
4538e353dd98f396c8facc29ebb72e9b1ba5f7c2.hypothesis: Fine-tuning large-scale text-to-image diffusion models to generate class-conditional synthetic images will yield data of sufficient quality and diversity to improve the performance of image classification models, both when used alone and in combination with real data.
4538e353dd98f396c8facc29ebb72e9b1ba5f7c2.proposed_method: A large-scale text-to-image diffusion model, such as Imagen, will be fine-tuned on the ImageNet-1K training set to produce class-conditional generative models at multiple resolutions (64×64, 256×256, and 1024×1024). The fine-tuning process will involve optimizing model weights and sampling parameters, including guidance weights, noise augmentation, and log-variance mixing coefficients, to maximize sample quality and diversity as measured by FID and Inception Score. Synthetic datasets will be generated by sampling images for each class to match the class balance of the original ImageNet dataset, with dataset sizes ranging from 1× to 10× the size of the real training set. The methodology will also include systematic sweeps over sampling hyperparameters to identify optimal settings for downstream classification tasks.
4538e353dd98f396c8facc29ebb72e9b1ba5f7c2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the ImageNet ILSVRC 2012 (ImageNet-1K) dataset, generating synthetic datasets at various resolutions and scales. Classifiers, including ResNet-50, ResNet-101, ResNet-152, ResNet-RS variants, ViT-S/16, DeiT-B, and DeiT-L, will be trained on real data, synthetic data, and combinations thereof. Baseline comparisons will include models trained on real data only and on synthetic data generated by prior state-of-the-art generative models such as BigGAN, VQ-VAE-2, and previous diffusion models (e.g., CDM). Evaluation metrics will include Frechet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS), and Classification Accuracy Score (CAS), with particular emphasis on CAS as a proxy for downstream classification performance. Experiments will assess the impact of synthetic data augmentation at different scales and resolutions, as well as the effect of merging real and synthetic data.
4538e353dd98f396c8facc29ebb72e9b1ba5f7c2.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the use of large-scale, fine-tuned text-to-image diffusion models for class-conditional image generation as a source of synthetic data for discriminative tasks. It claims to achieve state-of-the-art results in FID, Inception Score, and Classification Accuracy Score on ImageNet, surpassing previous generative models. The approach demonstrates that synthetic data from fine-tuned diffusion models can significantly boost classification accuracy when used to augment real data, across a range of convolutional and transformer-based architectures. Additionally, the methodology provides insights into optimal sampling strategies and the scaling behavior of synthetic data augmentation for large-scale image classification.

4539dcc4672a86b8f1e0bc64b92790d33518f55d.title: Why (and When) does Local SGD Generalize Better than SGD?
4539dcc4672a86b8f1e0bc64b92790d33518f55d.research_question: Under what conditions does Local SGD provide better generalization than standard SGD in large-scale distributed training, and what are the theoretical mechanisms underlying this improvement?
4539dcc4672a86b8f1e0bc64b92790d33518f55d.hypothesis: Local SGD, when used with a sufficiently small learning rate, a sufficiently long training time, and a properly tuned number of local steps, will generalize better than standard SGD due to enhanced implicit regularization effects driven by increased drift in the underlying stochastic dynamics.
4539dcc4672a86b8f1e0bc64b92790d33518f55d.proposed_method: A theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted to analyze the generalization properties of Local SGD compared to standard SGD. The approach will involve deriving a novel Stochastic Differential Equation (SDE) approximation that accurately models the long-term behavior of Local SGD in the small learning rate regime, particularly near the manifold of local minima. This SDE will be compared to the conventional SDE for SGD, focusing on the drift and diffusion terms to understand their impact on regularization and generalization. The method will also include ablation studies to empirically identify the key factors—such as learning rate, training time, and the number of local steps—that influence the generalization gap between Local SGD and SGD.
4539dcc4672a86b8f1e0bc64b92790d33518f55d.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed on standard image classification benchmarks, including CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, using architectures such as ResNet-56 and ResNet-50. Both random initialization and pre-trained models will be considered to assess the necessity of pretraining. The experimental setup will systematically vary the learning rate, number of local steps (H), and training duration to isolate their effects on generalization. Baselines will include standard (parallel) SGD and Post-local SGD, with and without momentum and learning rate decay. Evaluation metrics will focus on test accuracy, and ablation studies will be conducted to determine the interplay between hyperparameters and generalization performance.
4539dcc4672a86b8f1e0bc64b92790d33518f55d.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a new SDE framework that captures the long-term dynamics of Local SGD, revealing that Local SGD induces a stronger drift term than SGD, which enhances implicit regularization and sharpness reduction. The approach provides the first quantitative approximation bound for how well the SDE tracks Local SGD and offers theoretical insights into tuning the number of local steps for optimal generalization. The work reconciles conflicting empirical findings in the literature by identifying the joint importance of small learning rates and sufficient training time, and it establishes a rigorous theoretical foundation for the observed generalization improvements of Local SGD.

45403398688b0a7e7d125b924ffe677d066008e3.title: From noncommutative geometry to random matrix theory
45403398688b0a7e7d125b924ffe677d066008e3.research_question: How can ensembles of Dirac operators on finite noncommutative spaces, as formalized through fuzzy spectral triples, be used to construct and analytically study random matrix models relevant to quantum gravity, and what are the spectral and geometric properties of these models, including their connections to phase transitions and quantum gravity phenomena?
45403398688b0a7e7d125b924ffe677d066008e3.hypothesis: Ensembles of Dirac operators defined on fuzzy spectral triples, when equipped with suitable probability distributions and action functionals, will exhibit rich spectral behavior including phase transitions and manifold-like properties, and will allow for the analytic recovery of quantum gravity features such as Liouville quantum gravity in appropriate scaling limits.
45403398688b0a7e7d125b924ffe677d066008e3.proposed_method: The proposed research will construct random matrix models by considering ensembles of Dirac operators associated with fuzzy spectral triples, where the algebra, Hilbert space, and additional structure (charge conjugation and chirality) are fixed, and the Dirac operator is treated as a random variable with a specified probability density derived from a chosen action functional. The space of Dirac operators will be parametrized by Hermitian and skew-Hermitian matrices, enabling the translation of the problem into multi-matrix and multi-trace random matrix integrals. Various types of fuzzy spectral triples (e.g., one-dimensional, two-dimensional, and Yang-Mills-Higgs extensions) will be systematically explored, with explicit forms for the Dirac operator and associated matrix models derived for each case. Analytic techniques such as bootstrap methods, Coulomb gas approaches, and Topological Recursion (including Blobbed Topological Recursion for multi-trace potentials) will be developed and applied to study the spectral statistics, phase transitions, and geometric properties of these ensembles.
45403398688b0a7e7d125b924ffe677d066008e3.experiment_details: Experiments will involve both analytic and numerical investigations of the constructed Dirac ensembles. For analytic studies, partition functions, spectral densities, and correlation functions will be computed for various matrix models, including one-matrix, two-matrix, and Yang-Mills-Higgs-type ensembles, with quartic and higher-order polynomial potentials. The large N limit will be analyzed to reveal universal spectral properties and phase transitions. Where analytic solutions are intractable, numerical simulations will be conducted, particularly for higher-dimensional or Yang-Mills-Higgs ensembles. Comparisons will be made with classical random matrix ensembles and known results from quantum gravity, such as Liouville quantum gravity, to benchmark the models. Evaluation metrics will include spectral density, partition function behavior, phase transition points, and the ability to recover known quantum gravity phenomena in scaling limits.
45403398688b0a7e7d125b924ffe677d066008e3.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a systematic framework for constructing and analyzing random matrix models directly from noncommutative geometric data, specifically fuzzy spectral triples, thereby providing a new class of matrix ensembles with direct relevance to quantum gravity. The approach enables the study of spectral phase transitions and manifold-like behavior in noncommutative spaces, and establishes analytic connections to Liouville quantum gravity via double scaling limits. The application of advanced analytic techniques such as Topological Recursion and its generalizations to these multi-trace, multi-matrix models is innovative, as is the extension to Yang-Mills-Higgs fuzzy geometries incorporating gauge and Higgs sectors. The research opens new directions for both analytic and numerical exploration of quantum gravity models in the noncommutative geometry setting.

4544893b91b3bcae9110180dac425c7024eb1dd1.title: On the Embedding Collapse when Scaling up Recommendation Models
4544893b91b3bcae9110180dac425c7024eb1dd1.research_question: How can the scalability of deep-learning-based recommendation models be improved, particularly in the context of embedding matrix collapse, and what architectural or methodological changes can mitigate this issue while preserving model performance?
4544893b91b3bcae9110180dac425c7024eb1dd1.hypothesis: Embedding collapse, where the embedding matrix occupies a low-dimensional subspace, is a key factor limiting the scalability of recommendation models. Introducing multiple independent embedding sets with embedding-set-specific interaction modules will mitigate embedding collapse and enable consistent scalability improvements without sacrificing generalization.
4544893b91b3bcae9110180dac425c7024eb1dd1.proposed_method: A novel multi-embedding design is proposed to enhance the scalability of recommendation models. Instead of increasing the size of a single embedding matrix, the approach scales the number of independent and complete embedding sets. Each embedding set is paired with its own feature interaction module, allowing the model to jointly capture diverse interaction patterns. Non-linearities are incorporated within the interaction modules to ensure that each embedding set learns distinct representations. The model output is computed by aggregating the results from all embedding sets, and the architecture is designed to be compatible with a wide range of mainstream recommendation models. The method maintains the original feature interaction structure, thus preserving the ability to model higher-order correlations while mitigating embedding collapse.
4544893b91b3bcae9110180dac425c7024eb1dd1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale, real-world recommendation datasets such as Criteo and Avazu, using standard training/validation/test splits (8/1/1) and early stopping based on validation AUC. Baseline models will include DNN, IPNN, NFwFM, xDeepFM, DCNv2, and FinalMLP, with both single-embedding and multi-embedding variants evaluated at multiple scaling factors (2x, 3x, 4x, 10x). Evaluation metrics will focus on test AUC and information abundance (a measure of embedding matrix diversity based on singular value decomposition). Additional analyses will include ablation studies on the effect of embedding-set-specific interaction modules, measurement of embedding diversity, and the impact of varying data amounts. Online A/B testing in a large-scale commercial system (Tencent’s Online Advertising Platform) will further validate the method’s effectiveness.
4544893b91b3bcae9110180dac425c7024eb1dd1.novelty_claims: This proposal is the first to systematically identify and analyze the embedding collapse phenomenon as a primary barrier to scaling recommendation models. It introduces the interaction-collapse theory, establishing a theoretical and empirical link between feature interaction modules and embedding collapse. The proposed multi-embedding design is a simple yet effective architectural innovation that consistently improves scalability and mitigates embedding collapse across diverse recommendation models. The approach is validated both offline and in a large-scale online production system, demonstrating significant commercial impact.

457d4cffbb11666180507db21a86435941a69625.title: Pyramidal Flow Matching for Efficient Video Generative Modeling
457d4cffbb11666180507db21a86435941a69625.research_question: How can the computational and memory efficiency of high-quality, long-duration video generative modeling be improved without sacrificing generation quality or flexibility?
457d4cffbb11666180507db21a86435941a69625.hypothesis: A unified pyramidal flow matching framework that leverages both spatial and temporal pyramid representations, jointly optimized in a single model, will significantly reduce computational and memory requirements for video generation while maintaining or improving generation quality compared to existing cascaded or full-sequence approaches.
457d4cffbb11666180507db21a86435941a69625.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a pyramidal flow matching algorithm that decomposes the video generation process into multiple spatial and temporal pyramid stages. In the spatial domain, the method operates on compressed, lower-resolution representations in early denoising steps, with only the final stage using full resolution, thereby reducing redundant computation. Each pyramid stage is modeled as a piecewise flow, interpolating between noisy, pixelated latents and cleaner, higher-resolution latents, with corrective renoising at stage transitions to ensure continuity of the probability path. Temporal complexity is addressed by conditioning autoregressive video generation on a temporally compressed history, where earlier frames are represented at lower resolutions, further reducing token count and computational load. The entire framework is trained end-to-end using a unified Diffusion Transformer (DiT) architecture, with a single flow matching objective that jointly optimizes all pyramid stages.
457d4cffbb11666180507db21a86435941a69625.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a large-scale, mixed corpus of open-source image and video datasets, including subsets of LAION-5B, CC-12M, SA-1B, JourneyDB, synthetic data, WebVid-10M, OpenVid-1M, and additional high-resolution video sources, totaling approximately 10 million single-shot videos. Evaluation will employ the VBench and EvalCrafter benchmarks, which provide fine-grained and large-scale metrics for motion quality, semantic alignment, visual quality, and temporal consistency. Baselines will include state-of-the-art open-source and commercial video generation models, with comparisons made on both automated metrics and human preference studies. The model will be implemented using a 2B-parameter MM-DiT backbone, a 3D VAE for latent compression, and will be trained for up to 20.7k A100 GPU hours for 10-second, 768p, 24fps video generation. Ablation studies will isolate the contributions of spatial and temporal pyramids.
457d4cffbb11666180507db21a86435941a69625.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a unified pyramidal flow matching algorithm for video generative modeling, enabling joint optimization of spatial and temporal pyramid stages within a single model. This approach eliminates the need for separate models for each resolution or stage, facilitating knowledge sharing and end-to-end training. The integration of temporally compressed history conditions in autoregressive generation further reduces computational overhead. The framework achieves state-of-the-art efficiency, supporting high-quality, long-duration video generation at high resolutions and frame rates, with significantly reduced training and inference costs compared to existing methods.

458111ac5a0f73bb35a2acf55298268be25ccfa2.title: Ferret: Refer and Ground Anything Anywhere at Any Granularity
458111ac5a0f73bb35a2acf55298268be25ccfa2.research_question: How can a multimodal large language model be designed to enable unified, fine-grained spatial referring and grounding of any region within an image, at any granularity or shape, while supporting open-vocabulary, instruction-following, and robust interaction in both traditional and conversational settings?
458111ac5a0f73bb35a2acf55298268be25ccfa2.hypothesis: A hybrid region representation that combines discrete coordinates with continuous visual features, together with a spatial-aware visual sampler and large-scale instruction-tuning on a diverse refer-and-ground dataset, will enable a multimodal large language model to accurately refer to and ground any region in an image, outperforming existing models in both classical and conversational multimodal tasks and reducing object hallucination.
458111ac5a0f73bb35a2acf55298268be25ccfa2.proposed_method: A novel multimodal large language model will be developed, leveraging a hybrid region representation that integrates both quantized discrete coordinates and continuous visual features to represent arbitrary image regions, including points, bounding boxes, and free-form shapes. A spatial-aware visual sampler will be designed to extract continuous features from regions of varying shape and sparsity, using techniques inspired by 3D point cloud learning such as farthest point sampling, k-nearest neighbor grouping, and local feature pooling. The model architecture will consist of a pre-trained image encoder (e.g., CLIP-ViT-L/14), a trainable spatial-aware visual sampler, and a decoder-only large language model (e.g., Vicuna), with region representations embedded into the input sequence. The model will be trained end-to-end to process mixed text and region references, and to output grounded responses with explicit region coordinates.
458111ac5a0f73bb35a2acf55298268be25ccfa2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a wide range of referring and grounding tasks using established benchmarks such as LVIS (for referring object classification), RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, RefCOCOg (for referring expression comprehension), and Flickr30k Entities (for phrase grounding and grounded captioning). The model will be trained on the GRIT dataset, a 1.1M-sample instruction-tuning corpus that includes converted public datasets, GPT-generated region-based dialogues, and spatial negative mining for robustness. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art MLLMs (e.g., LLaVA, Kosmos-2, Shikra, GPT4-ROI), as well as specialized grounding models (e.g., UniTAB, MDETR). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy for referring classification, intersection-over-union (IoU) for grounding, standard captioning metrics (BLEU@4, METEOR, CIDEr, SPICE), and F1 scores for grounding alignment. Additional evaluation will be performed on a new benchmark, Ferret-Bench, designed to test region-based multimodal conversation.
458111ac5a0f73bb35a2acf55298268be25ccfa2.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first hybrid region representation for MLLMs that supports arbitrary region shapes, including free-form scribbles and polygons, rather than being limited to points or bounding boxes. A spatial-aware visual sampler is developed to robustly extract features from irregular and sparse regions. The GRIT dataset is curated to provide large-scale, instruction-following, region-based supervision, including hard negative samples for robustness. The resulting model is claimed to achieve state-of-the-art performance on both classical referring/grounding and conversational multimodal tasks, and to significantly reduce object hallucination compared to prior MLLMs.

4584dee8505ce8cdaa09d7c3f4b4ab6568b3e766.title: RealFill: Reference-Driven Generation for Authentic Image Completion
4584dee8505ce8cdaa09d7c3f4b4ab6568b3e766.research_question: How can missing regions in a target image be completed with content that is faithful to the true scene, given a small set of reference images of the same scene, even when the reference and target images differ significantly in viewpoint, lighting, style, or object arrangement?
4584dee8505ce8cdaa09d7c3f4b4ab6568b3e766.hypothesis: A generative inpainting model, personalized via fine-tuning on a small set of reference and target images, can generate image completions that are more authentic and faithful to the original scene than existing prompt-based or single-reference methods, even under challenging variations between reference and target images.
4584dee8505ce8cdaa09d7c3f4b4ab6568b3e766.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a reference-driven image completion framework that leverages a pretrained diffusion-based inpainting model. Personalization is achieved by fine-tuning the model using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) layers on up to five reference images and the target image, with randomly generated masks to simulate missing regions. The fine-tuning process is conditioned on a fixed language prompt and aims to adapt the model to the specific scene's content, lighting, and style. During inference, the adapted model fills the missing region of the target image, and a correspondence-based seed selection mechanism is used to automatically select high-quality outputs by ranking generated samples according to the number of keypoint matches with the reference images. The final output is composited with the original target image using a feathered mask to ensure seamless integration.
4584dee8505ce8cdaa09d7c3f4b4ab6568b3e766.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a newly introduced benchmark, RealBench, which contains 33 scenes (10 inpainting and 23 outpainting tasks) with significant variation in viewpoint, lighting, style, and object pose between reference and target images. Each scene includes up to five reference images, a target image, a binary mask indicating the missing region, and a ground-truth completion. The method is compared against both prompt-based (Stable Diffusion Inpainting, Photoshop Generative Fill) and reference-based (TransFill, Paint-by-Example) baselines. Evaluation metrics span low-level (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS), mid-level (DreamSim), and high-level (DINO, CLIP) image similarity. For generative methods, 64 samples per scene are generated, and correspondence-based seed selection is used to filter outputs. User studies are also conducted to assess realism and faithfulness.
4584dee8505ce8cdaa09d7c3f4b4ab6568b3e766.novelty_claims: The proposal defines and addresses the new problem of Authentic Image Completion, focusing on generating what should have been in the scene rather than plausible alternatives. The method is the first to enable multi-reference, scene-level faithful image completion using a personalized diffusion model conditioned on both reference and target images. A novel correspondence-based seed selection mechanism is introduced to automate high-quality output selection. Additionally, a new benchmark dataset, RealBench, is introduced to evaluate authentic image completion under diverse and challenging conditions.

45872b94798c3125abfb185b7926689c5e767763.title: GraphGPT: Graph Instruction Tuning for Large Language Models
45872b94798c3125abfb185b7926689c5e767763.research_question: How can large language models be effectively aligned with graph-structured data to achieve robust generalization and reasoning across diverse graph learning tasks, especially in zero-shot and low-label scenarios?
45872b94798c3125abfb185b7926689c5e767763.hypothesis: Integrating large language models with explicit graph structural information through a dual-stage instruction tuning paradigm, including self-supervised and task-specific instruction tuning, will significantly enhance the generalization, adaptability, and reasoning capabilities of language models for graph learning tasks, outperforming existing GNNs and LLMs in both supervised and zero-shot settings.
45872b94798c3125abfb185b7926689c5e767763.proposed_method: A novel framework, GraphGPT, is proposed to align large language models (LLMs) with graph-structured data using a dual-stage graph instruction tuning paradigm. The approach begins with a text-graph grounding component that encodes graph structures and aligns them with the language space via a contrastive objective, leveraging a flexible graph encoder (e.g., graph transformer or GCN) and a text encoder (e.g., vanilla transformer). In the first stage, self-supervised instruction tuning is performed using a structure-aware graph matching task, where the model learns to associate graph tokens with their corresponding textual descriptions from unlabeled graphs. A lightweight alignment projector is introduced to map graph representations to the language model's token space, with only the projector's parameters being updated while the LLM and graph encoder remain frozen. The second stage involves task-specific instruction tuning, where the model is further fine-tuned on downstream graph tasks (such as node classification or link prediction) using tailored instructions that combine graph structure and text. Additionally, chain-of-thought (CoT) distillation is incorporated to enhance the model's step-by-step reasoning abilities, using high-quality CoT data distilled from a powerful closed-source LLM.
45872b94798c3125abfb185b7926689c5e767763.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on three benchmark datasets: OGB-arxiv, PubMed, and Cora, covering diverse node classification and link prediction tasks. The evaluation includes both supervised and zero-shot transfer settings, where models are trained on one dataset and tested on another without additional fine-tuning. Baselines include state-of-the-art GNNs (e.g., GraphSAGE, GCN, GAT, RevGNN), self-supervised methods (e.g., DGI), knowledge-distillation GNNs (e.g., GKD, GLNN), recent graph transformers (e.g., NodeFormer, DIFFormer), and open-source LLMs (e.g., Baichuan-7B, Vicuna-7B). Evaluation metrics include accuracy and macro-F1 for node classification, and AUC for link prediction. Ablation studies are performed to assess the contribution of each module (graph instruction tuning, LLM reasoning, CoT distillation), and efficiency analyses measure training/inference time, parameter count, and GPU memory usage. Instruction data mixing and multitask generalization are also explored.
45872b94798c3125abfb185b7926689c5e767763.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a dual-stage graph instruction tuning paradigm that aligns LLMs with graph structural information through both self-supervised and task-specific instruction tuning, a text-graph grounding mechanism for efficient structure-to-language alignment, and a lightweight alignment projector that enables parameter-efficient adaptation. The method incorporates chain-of-thought distillation to enhance reasoning under distribution shift. The approach claims superior generalization in zero-shot and supervised graph learning tasks, efficient scalability, and the ability to handle multitask graph learning without catastrophic forgetting, surpassing both GNN and LLM baselines.

4590aa5e92037498f77f32e194ea8812b97347b9.title: Approximating Full Conformal Prediction for Neural Network Regression with Gauss-Newton Influence
4590aa5e92037498f77f32e194ea8812b97347b9.research_question: How can prediction intervals for neural network regression be constructed in a scalable, post-hoc manner that achieves well-calibrated and sharp uncertainty estimates without sacrificing statistical efficiency or requiring retraining for every test point and candidate label?
4590aa5e92037498f77f32e194ea8812b97347b9.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a scalable approximation to full conformal prediction for neural network regression can be achieved by leveraging Gauss-Newton influence to locally perturb model parameters, combined with network linearization, thereby enabling efficient and adaptive prediction intervals that maintain coverage and sharpness without the need for exhaustive retraining or sample splitting.
4590aa5e92037498f77f32e194ea8812b97347b9.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces an approximate full conformal prediction (full-CP) framework for neural network regression by utilizing Gauss-Newton influence to locally perturb the trained model parameters for each test point and candidate label. Instead of retraining the model for every possible label, the approach linearizes the neural network around the learned parameters and computes the effect of adding the test point via a rank-one update to the Gauss-Newton approximation of the Hessian. This allows the absolute residual nonconformity score to be expressed as a piecewise linear function of the candidate label, enabling efficient closed-form computation of prediction intervals. The method is further extended to support normalized (studentized) nonconformity scores, improving adaptability and efficiency, and is applicable to both single-output and multi-output regression tasks.
4590aa5e92037498f77f32e194ea8812b97347b9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of standard regression benchmarks from the UCI Machine Learning repository, including small (e.g., boston, concrete), medium (e.g., kin8nm, power), and large (e.g., bike, protein, facebook2) datasets. Additionally, a bounding box localization task using the Oxford-IIIT Pet dataset will be included, employing a VGG-19-based deep convolutional neural network. Baseline methods for comparison include Linearized Laplace (LA), split conformal prediction (SCP), conformalized residual fitting (CRF), conformalized quantile regression (CQR), and proposed variants such as SCP-GN and ACP-GN(split+refine). Evaluation metrics comprise average prediction interval width, empirical coverage, and for multi-output tasks, average confidence region volume. Experimental setups involve repeated cross-validation or multiple train-test splits, with neural networks trained to convergence using the Adam optimizer and appropriate architectural choices for each dataset. Multiple testing corrections (e.g., Bonferroni) are applied for multi-output settings.
4590aa5e92037498f77f32e194ea8812b97347b9.novelty_claims: The proposed approach eliminates the need for retraining neural networks for every test point and candidate label in full conformal prediction by introducing a Gauss-Newton influence-based approximation. It further avoids the computational burden of grid search over candidate labels by expressing nonconformity scores as linear functions, enabling closed-form interval computation. The method generalizes conformalized ridge regression to neural networks and supports normalized and studentized nonconformity scores for improved adaptability. Additionally, the approach yields a novel adaptive split-CP variant (SCP-GN) that does not require training an auxiliary network. Empirical results demonstrate that the method achieves tighter and more adaptive prediction intervals, particularly in limited-data regimes, while maintaining or improving coverage compared to existing baselines.

4591333ee08f38f2e3f50f99f70f922efb84791d.title: Ferret-UI 2: Mastering Universal User Interface Understanding Across Platforms
4591333ee08f38f2e3f50f99f70f922efb84791d.research_question: How can a multimodal large language model be developed to achieve universal user interface (UI) understanding and single-step user-centered interactions across a wide variety of platforms, including smartphones, tablets, web interfaces, and smart TVs, while addressing challenges such as platform diversity, resolution variation, and limited high-quality training data?
4591333ee08f38f2e3f50f99f70f922efb84791d.hypothesis: A multimodal large language model equipped with adaptive high-resolution image encoding, multi-platform training data, and advanced multimodal data generation techniques will achieve superior UI understanding and interaction capabilities across diverse platforms, demonstrating strong cross-platform generalization and outperforming existing models on standard benchmarks.
4591333ee08f38f2e3f50f99f70f922efb84791d.proposed_method: The proposed approach involves constructing a unified, multi-platform dataset by aggregating and harmonizing annotated UI screenshots from iPhone, Android, iPad, Webpage, and AppleTV platforms. High-quality annotations are obtained through a combination of human labeling, OCR-based text extraction, and direct parsing from HTML hierarchies. The model architecture leverages a CLIP-based image encoder to extract both global and local features from UI screenshots, with an adaptive N-gridding mechanism to optimally partition high-resolution images for efficient and information-preserving encoding. Visual features are then integrated into a large language model (LLM) backbone, enabling grounded perception and interaction. Training data for both elementary (referring and grounding) and advanced (multi-round perception and interaction QA) tasks are generated, with advanced data leveraging GPT-4o and set-of-mark visual prompting to enhance spatial and functional understanding of UI elements. The model is instruction-tuned on this diverse, multimodal dataset to support single-step, user-centered interactions across all supported platforms.
4591333ee08f38f2e3f50f99f70f922efb84791d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both custom-constructed benchmarks and established public datasets. The training set includes platform-specific and cross-platform data, with loss weighting to address class imbalance. Evaluation will be performed on 45 tasks (6 elementary and 3 advanced per platform across 5 platforms), using metrics such as GPT-4o score, Multi-IoU, BertScore, and Intersection-over-Union (IoU) for grounding. Public benchmarks include GUIDE (next-action prediction on web UIs) and GUI-World (multi-platform UI understanding). Baselines for comparison include previous versions of the model (Ferret-UI), SeeClick, GPT-4o (with and without set-of-mark prompting), and other recent multimodal agents. Ablation studies will assess the impact of adaptive gridding and improved dataset quality. Zero-shot cross-platform transfer experiments will evaluate the model's generalization when trained on one platform and tested on others.
4591333ee08f38f2e3f50f99f70f922efb84791d.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first multimodal LLM framework targeting universal UI understanding across smartphones, tablets, web interfaces, and smart TVs. Key innovations include adaptive N-gridding for efficient and high-fidelity high-resolution image encoding, a unified multi-platform dataset with improved annotation quality, and advanced multimodal training data generation using GPT-4o with set-of-mark visual prompting. The approach supports user-centered, single-step interactions rather than mechanical instruction following, and demonstrates strong cross-platform transfer and state-of-the-art performance on both custom and public benchmarks.

45977cf5dd92542c8e988c505cbf17bc14d8650f.title: Efficient Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning by Planning
45977cf5dd92542c8e988c505cbf17bc14d8650f.research_question: How can sample efficiency and computational performance in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) be improved by integrating model-based planning techniques, particularly in environments with large and complex action spaces?
45977cf5dd92542c8e988c505cbf17bc14d8650f.hypothesis: Integrating a centralized model-based planning approach with novel search and policy optimization techniques will significantly improve the sample and computational efficiency of MARL in cooperative environments, outperforming both model-free and existing model-based baselines.
45977cf5dd92542c8e988c505cbf17bc14d8650f.proposed_method: A new algorithm, MAZero, will be developed that extends the MuZero paradigm to multi-agent cooperative reinforcement learning. The approach will employ a centralized-value, individual-dynamic model with parameter sharing among agents and an attention-based communication block to facilitate cooperation during model unrolling. Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) will be adapted for policy search using a deterministic learned model, and two novel techniques will be introduced: Optimistic Search Lambda (OS(λ)), which provides optimistic value estimates to improve search efficiency in large deterministic action spaces, and Advantage-Weighted Policy Optimization (AWPO), a policy loss that leverages value information from OS(λ) to enhance policy learning. The model will be trained end-to-end using a combination of reward, value, consistency, and AWPO policy losses, enabling both centralized training and distributed execution.
45977cf5dd92542c8e988c505cbf17bc14d8650f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge (SMAC) benchmark, covering a variety of easy and hard cooperative scenarios. MAZero will be compared against both model-based (e.g., MAMBA) and model-free (e.g., QMIX, QPLEX, RODE, CDS, MAPPO) baselines. Evaluation metrics will include win rate, sample efficiency (measured by environment steps to reach a given performance), and computational efficiency (measured by runtime). Each algorithm will be executed with multiple random seeds to ensure statistical reliability. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the contributions of the OS(λ) and AWPO components, as well as the impact of network structure choices such as communication and parameter sharing.
45977cf5dd92542c8e988c505cbf17bc14d8650f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to empirically extend MuZero-style planning to multi-agent cooperative environments with demonstrated effectiveness. It introduces a centralized-value, individual-dynamic model with shared parameters and an attention-based communication mechanism tailored for multi-agent cooperation. The Optimistic Search Lambda (OS(λ)) technique enables efficient planning in deterministic environments with vast action spaces, while the Advantage-Weighted Policy Optimization (AWPO) provides a novel policy optimization loss that leverages value information for improved learning. Together, these innovations yield superior sample and computational efficiency compared to both state-of-the-art model-free and model-based MARL methods.

4599087d39184635aa1eedb1bf71839c571c3b9e.title: Provably Efficient Representation Learning with Tractable Planning in Low-Rank POMDP
4599087d39184635aa1eedb1bf71839c571c3b9e.research_question: Can a representation learning-based reinforcement learning algorithm be developed for partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) that achieves both statistical efficiency and computational tractability, particularly in subclasses such as low-rank, decodable, and γ-observable POMDPs?
4599087d39184635aa1eedb1bf71839c571c3b9e.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a reinforcement learning algorithm leveraging representation learning, combined with maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) and optimism in the face of uncertainty (OFU), can achieve statistically efficient learning and tractable planning in low-rank POMDPs, while relying only on computationally efficient supervised learning oracles.
4599087d39184635aa1eedb1bf71839c571c3b9e.proposed_method: A novel algorithm is proposed that integrates representation learning with reinforcement learning for POMDPs exhibiting low-rank latent transitions. The approach involves learning a compact representation of observation histories using a decoder function, which is updated via maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) on collected trajectory data. To balance exploration and exploitation, the method incorporates optimism in the face of uncertainty (OFU) by adding exploration bonuses derived from the learned representations. Policy updates are performed using a Least Squares Value Iteration (LSVI) algorithm adapted for L-step low-rank POMDPs (LSVI-LLR), which utilizes the learned representations and computed bonuses. The algorithm operates in episodes, alternating between data collection with a mixture of current and uniform policies, representation learning via MLE, and policy improvement via LSVI-LLR, thereby avoiding computationally intractable version-space elimination.
4599087d39184635aa1eedb1bf71839c571c3b9e.experiment_details: Experiments are to be conducted on POMDP environments characterized by low-rank transition structures and L-step decodability or γ-observability. The evaluation will utilize datasets generated from simulated POMDPs with varying state, action, and observation space sizes. Baseline comparisons will include existing algorithms for POMDPs with formal sample complexity guarantees, such as those based on version-space elimination and optimistic planning. Evaluation metrics will focus on sample complexity (number of episodes to achieve near-optimality), computational efficiency (runtime and scalability with respect to state and observation space), and policy performance (expected cumulative reward). The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by matching problem settings and hyperparameters across methods.
4599087d39184635aa1eedb1bf71839c571c3b9e.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a computationally efficient reinforcement learning algorithm for low-rank POMDPs that leverages representation learning and MLE oracles, avoiding the intractable version-space elimination used in prior work. The approach is amenable to modern function approximation techniques, including neural networks, and achieves favorable sample complexity without exponential dependence on observation or state space size. The method generalizes to both decodable and γ-observable POMDPs, providing improved scalability and practical implementability over existing algorithms.

45d613442ca75eb515de49178cd5bee6ac90fd88.title: Learning with Fantasy: Semantic-Aware Virtual Contrastive Constraint for Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning
45d613442ca75eb515de49178cd5bee6ac90fd88.research_question: How can few-shot class-incremental learning (FSCIL) be improved to better generalize to new classes with limited samples, while maintaining strong separation among base and novel class representations?
45d613442ca75eb515de49178cd5bee6ac90fd88.hypothesis: Enhancing the separation of base class representations in the embedding space during the base session, and introducing semantic diversity via virtual classes generated by pre-defined transformations, will facilitate improved generalization to novel classes and reduce overlap between old and new class distributions in FSCIL.
45d613442ca75eb515de49178cd5bee6ac90fd88.proposed_method: A novel Semantic-Aware Virtual Contrastive (SAVC) framework will be developed for FSCIL. The method constructs a 'fantasy space' by generating virtual classes through pre-defined semantic-preserving transformations (such as rotations and color permutations) applied to base session images. These virtual classes serve as placeholders for unseen classes and inject diverse semantic information into the embedding space. The framework jointly optimizes a classification loss and a supervised contrastive loss in both the original and fantasy spaces, using a shared backbone and a momentum-updated key encoder for contrastive learning. During inference, predictions from multiple transformed views are aggregated to enhance robustness and semantic coverage. Incremental sessions will leverage a nearest-class-mean classifier, with prototypes updated using both real and virtual class embeddings, and a multi-crop strategy will be used to further enrich local semantic features.
45d613442ca75eb515de49178cd5bee6ac90fd88.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three standard FSCIL benchmarks: CIFAR100, miniImageNet, and CUB200, each with a base session of sufficient data and multiple incremental sessions with few-shot samples (e.g., 5-shot per class). The proposed SAVC method will be compared against state-of-the-art FSCIL approaches, including both incremental-frozen and incremental-trainable baselines such as iCaRL, EEIL, TOPIC, SPPR, F2M, CEC, and FACT. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy across all sessions, class separation degree (inter- and intra-class distances), and confusion matrices. Ablation studies will assess the impact of virtual class fantasy, multi-crop strategies, and incremental fine-tuning. Hyperparameters such as the number and type of transformations, and the weighting of contrastive losses, will be systematically varied to analyze robustness.
45d613442ca75eb515de49178cd5bee6ac90fd88.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the concept of semantic-aware virtual classes generated via pre-defined transformations to fill the embedding space with diverse, fine-grained semantic information, which is novel in the context of FSCIL. The method enables improved base class separation and mutual separation between old and new classes, facilitating better generalization to novel classes with minimal overlap. The multi-semantic aggregated inference and joint optimization of classification and contrastive objectives in both original and fantasy spaces represent significant methodological innovations. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on multiple FSCIL benchmarks, surpassing existing methods by a substantial margin.

45e171489ecba9f667e9f0335be01029513312eb.title: A Rank Stabilization Scaling Factor for Fine-Tuning with LoRA
45e171489ecba9f667e9f0335be01029513312eb.research_question: How can the scaling factor in parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods, specifically Low-Rank Adapters (LoRA), be optimized to enable stable and effective fine-tuning of large language models across a wide range of adapter ranks?
45e171489ecba9f667e9f0335be01029513312eb.hypothesis: Replacing the conventional LoRA scaling factor (1/r) with a rank-stabilized scaling factor (1/sqrt(r)) will prevent gradient collapse, stabilize learning, and enable improved fine-tuning performance with higher adapter ranks, without increasing inference computational cost.
45e171489ecba9f667e9f0335be01029513312eb.proposed_method: A new approach is developed that analytically derives and implements a rank-stabilized scaling factor for LoRA adapters, termed rsLoRA. The method involves scaling the low-rank adapter matrix product by 1/sqrt(r) instead of the conventional 1/r, where r is the adapter rank. Theoretical analysis is conducted in the infinite-width limit to prove that this scaling ensures stability of both activations and gradients across all ranks, preventing gradient collapse and enabling effective learning with larger ranks. The rsLoRA method is implemented by modifying the scaling factor in the adapter modules during fine-tuning, while keeping the rest of the LoRA framework unchanged, ensuring no increase in inference computational cost.
45e171489ecba9f667e9f0335be01029513312eb.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted by fine-tuning the Llama 2 model on 20,000 examples from the OpenOrca instruction tuning dataset, using the AdamW optimizer with a constant learning rate. Adapters are inserted into all linear attention and feed-forward sub-modules, and a range of adapter ranks (4, 8, 32, 128, 512, 2048) is tested. Baseline comparisons are made between standard LoRA and the proposed rsLoRA, with evaluation metrics including training perplexity and average parameter gradient norm to assess learning stability and performance. Additional ablation studies are performed using different models (e.g., GPT-J on GSM8k), optimizers (e.g., Adafactor, SGD), and initialization schemes to validate the generality and robustness of the findings.
45e171489ecba9f667e9f0335be01029513312eb.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretically justified, rank-stabilized scaling factor for LoRA adapters, enabling stable and effective fine-tuning at higher adapter ranks. This approach unlocks a compute/performance trade-off not accessible with standard LoRA, allowing practitioners to leverage larger ranks for improved performance without additional inference cost. The method is validated both analytically and empirically, and is claimed to be directly applicable to other dynamic-rank PEFT methods such as AdaLoRA, potentially resulting in further improvements.

45e1c99a1c8935bf137c0b51a08a03ffb6821993.title: Demystifying Long Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in LLMs
45e1c99a1c8935bf137c0b51a08a03ffb6821993.research_question: What are the key factors and training strategies that enable large language models (LLMs) to develop robust, long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning capabilities, and how can these strategies be optimized to enhance reasoning performance across both in-domain and out-of-domain tasks?
45e1c99a1c8935bf137c0b51a08a03ffb6821993.hypothesis: Long chain-of-thought reasoning in LLMs can be systematically enhanced and stabilized through a combination of high-quality supervised fine-tuning on emergent long CoT data, carefully designed reinforcement learning (RL) reward functions (including verifiable and length-shaping signals), and the integration of diverse, noisy but verifiable data sources. Furthermore, base models may already possess latent reasoning skills that can be effectively incentivized with sufficient compute and appropriate RL incentives.
45e1c99a1c8935bf137c0b51a08a03ffb6821993.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves a multi-stage training pipeline for LLMs. First, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) is performed using high-quality, emergent long CoT trajectories distilled from strong teacher models, with rejection sampling to ensure correctness and diversity. This is followed by reinforcement learning (RL), where the model is further optimized using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and a reward function that combines correctness (verifiable by rule-based or model-based verifiers), length-shaping (e.g., a piecewise cosine reward that balances inference efficiency and reasoning depth), and repetition penalties to prevent reward hacking. The approach also explores scaling up verifiable reward signals by incorporating large-scale, noisy web-extracted datasets, filtered for short-form answers when possible, and investigates the impact of context window size and reward discount factors. Ablation studies are conducted to compare SFT initialization strategies, reward designs, and the effect of scaling compute.
45e1c99a1c8935bf137c0b51a08a03ffb6821993.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using both general-purpose and math-specialized LLMs, such as Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-Math-7B, initialized with SFT on MATH dataset (Hendrycks et al., 2021) and web-extracted datasets like WebInstruct. RL training will use PPO with various reward functions (classic, cosine length-scaling, repetition penalties) and different context window sizes (4K, 8K, 16K tokens). Evaluation will be performed on a suite of reasoning benchmarks, including MATH-500 (in-domain), AIME 2024, TheoremQA, and MMLU-Pro-1k (out-of-domain), using accuracy as the primary metric. Baselines will include models trained with short CoT SFT, SFT only, and RL from base models. Additional analyses will track emergent behaviors (e.g., branching, error correction) and the impact of reward and data scaling.
45e1c99a1c8935bf137c0b51a08a03ffb6821993.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a systematic investigation into the mechanics of long CoT reasoning in LLMs, identifying the critical role of high-quality, emergent long CoT SFT data and the importance of reward shaping (including length-scaling and repetition penalties) for stable RL training. It further claims innovation in leveraging large-scale, noisy but verifiable web data to scale up reward signals, and provides nuanced insights into the origins of long CoT abilities in base models. The work aims to demystify the emergence of complex reasoning behaviors and offers practical guidelines for optimizing training strategies to enhance long CoT reasoning, supported by extensive ablation studies and empirical analysis.

45f1dbf9ccc10fd0a46268967582c835866d788d.title: OMNI: Open-endedness via Models of human Notions of Interestingness
45f1dbf9ccc10fd0a46268967582c835866d788d.research_question: How can open-ended learning algorithms be improved to prioritize not only learnable tasks but also tasks that are interesting and worthwhile, enabling agents to continuously acquire diverse and meaningful skills in vast or infinite task spaces?
45f1dbf9ccc10fd0a46268967582c835866d788d.hypothesis: Incorporating models of human notions of interestingness, as captured by large foundation models trained on human-generated data, into open-ended learning algorithms will enable more effective selection of tasks that are both learnable and interesting, thereby accelerating the acquisition of diverse and meaningful skills compared to approaches based on learning progress or uniform task sampling alone.
45f1dbf9ccc10fd0a46268967582c835866d788d.proposed_method: A novel framework, OMNI (Open-endedness via Models of human Notions of Interestingness), is introduced to guide task selection in open-ended learning environments. The method combines a learning progress-based curriculum—which prioritizes tasks where the agent is making the most progress—with a Model of Interestingness (MoI) derived from large foundation models (FMs) such as GPT-3 or GPT-4. The FM is prompted in a few-shot or zero-shot manner to predict which tasks, given the agent's current skill set and past successes, would be considered interesting from a human perspective. Task sampling rates are first assigned according to learning progress, then filtered by the FM-based MoI, with uninteresting tasks receiving drastically reduced sampling weights. In infinite task spaces, the FM is also used to generate new candidate tasks and associated reward functions, ensuring that the agent is continually presented with novel, learnable, and interesting challenges.
45f1dbf9ccc10fd0a46268967582c835866d788d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in both finite and infinite task spaces. In finite settings, environments such as Crafter (a 2D Minecraft-like world) and BabyAI (a partially observable gridworld for language-conditioned tasks) will be used. The task set will include a mix of interesting, boring (e.g., repetitive or trivial variations), and extremely challenging tasks. Agents will be trained using PPO, and performance will be compared across three curricula: uniform sampling, learning progress only, and OMNI (learning progress plus MoI). Evaluation metrics will include average task success rate and the number of tasks with success rates above a threshold (e.g., 0.2), with experiments repeated over multiple random seeds and statistical significance assessed. In the infinite task space, the AI2-THOR embodied robotics environment will be used, with GPT-4 generating new tasks and code-based reward functions during training. Baselines will include random and learning-progress-based task generation. All experiments will be run for a fixed number of timesteps, and results will be analyzed for both the breadth and depth of skills acquired.
45f1dbf9ccc10fd0a46268967582c835866d788d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to leverage large foundation models as a proxy for human notions of interestingness in open-ended learning, enabling automated, scalable, and domain-agnostic identification of tasks that are both learnable and worthwhile. By integrating FM-based interestingness judgments with learning progress curricula, the method overcomes the limitations of prior approaches that are distracted by trivial or repetitive tasks. The framework is demonstrated to be robust across different types of boring tasks and adaptable to both finite and infinite task spaces, including the automated generation of both tasks and reward functions. This represents a significant advance towards self-improving AI and AI-generating algorithms capable of perpetual, meaningful exploration.

45f573f302dc7e77cbc5d1a74ccbac3564bbebc8.title: PEBBLE: Feedback-Efficient Interactive Reinforcement Learning via Relabeling Experience and Unsupervised Pre-training
45f573f302dc7e77cbc5d1a74ccbac3564bbebc8.research_question: How can interactive reinforcement learning be made more sample- and feedback-efficient, enabling agents to learn complex behaviors from human preferences with minimal human effort, especially in settings where reward functions are difficult to specify?
45f573f302dc7e77cbc5d1a74ccbac3564bbebc8.hypothesis: Combining unsupervised pre-training to diversify agent experience with off-policy reinforcement learning and systematic relabeling of experience based on learned reward models will significantly improve both sample and feedback efficiency in human-in-the-loop reinforcement learning, enabling agents to learn complex tasks from limited human feedback.
45f573f302dc7e77cbc5d1a74ccbac3564bbebc8.proposed_method: A feedback-efficient interactive reinforcement learning algorithm is developed that integrates unsupervised pre-training and preference-based learning via relabeling experience. Initially, the agent undergoes unsupervised exploration, maximizing state entropy using intrinsic rewards based on k-nearest neighbor distances to encourage diverse behaviors. After this pre-training phase, a human teacher provides preference feedback between pairs of behavior clips, which is used to train a reward model via the Bradley-Terry framework. The agent's policy and Q-function are then updated using an off-policy actor-critic algorithm (Soft Actor-Critic), where all past experiences in the replay buffer are relabeled with the current reward model to mitigate non-stationarity. Preference query selection is optimized using uncertainty-based sampling (ensemble disagreement or entropy-based) to maximize the informativeness of human feedback.
45f573f302dc7e77cbc5d1a74ccbac3564bbebc8.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a range of continuous control tasks, including complex locomotion and robotic manipulation environments from DeepMind Control Suite (DMControl) and Meta-world. The agent is evaluated in scenarios where ground-truth rewards are unobserved and only human (or scripted) preference feedback is available. Baselines include PreferencePPO (an on-policy preference-based RL method) and oracle agents using true task rewards with SAC and PPO. Evaluation metrics include average return (for locomotion) and success rate (for manipulation), with performance averaged over ten runs. Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of unsupervised pre-training, relabeling, and different query selection strategies. Additional experiments involve real human trainers to demonstrate the ability to learn novel behaviors and avoid reward exploitation.
45f573f302dc7e77cbc5d1a74ccbac3564bbebc8.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to demonstrate that unsupervised pre-training combined with off-policy learning and systematic relabeling can substantially improve both sample and feedback efficiency in preference-based RL.
