The approach enables learning of more complex tasks than previously possible with human-in-the-loop RL, and can utilize real-time human feedback to prevent reward exploitation and specify novel behaviors that are difficult to encode with standard reward functions. The method also introduces entropy-based query selection for preference feedback and shows that relabeling all past experiences with updated reward models stabilizes and accelerates off-policy learning in non-stationary reward settings.

45f64a0762fad89f06fd06d227a4d8e42a6b365d.title: Interacting particle Langevin algorithm for maximum marginal likelihood estimation
45f64a0762fad89f06fd06d227a4d8e42a6b365d.research_question: How can parameter estimation in latent variable models be improved by leveraging interacting particle systems and Langevin dynamics for maximum marginal likelihood estimation, particularly in scenarios where the marginal likelihood involves intractable integrals?
45f64a0762fad89f06fd06d227a4d8e42a6b365d.hypothesis: Introducing noise into the parameter dynamics within an interacting particle Langevin system will enable efficient and theoretically robust maximum marginal likelihood estimation, yielding nonasymptotic error bounds that are uniform in time and independent of the number of particles, and outperforming classical EM and standard MCMC-based approaches in both accuracy and computational efficiency.
45f64a0762fad89f06fd06d227a4d8e42a6b365d.proposed_method: A novel algorithm, termed the Interacting Particle Langevin Algorithm (IPLA), will be developed by discretizing a continuous-time interacting particle system defined over both parameter and latent variable spaces. The method introduces stochastic noise into the parameter dynamics, resulting in a coupled system of stochastic differential equations (SDEs) for both parameters and latent variables. The system is discretized using the Euler-Maruyama scheme, where at each iteration, the parameter update aggregates gradients of the negative log-likelihood across all particles, and both parameter and latent variable updates include Gaussian noise terms. The algorithm targets the stationary distribution whose parameter marginal concentrates around the maximum marginal likelihood estimator as the number of particles increases. Theoretical analysis will establish geometric ergodicity, uniform-in-time discretization error bounds, and nonasymptotic convergence rates under strong convexity and Lipschitz gradient assumptions, with extensions to settings where gradients are estimated stochastically.
45f64a0762fad89f06fd06d227a4d8e42a6b365d.experiment_details: Empirical evaluation will be conducted on latent variable models, with a primary focus on logistic regression using synthetic or real datasets that satisfy the model assumptions. The proposed IPLA will be compared against classical Expectation Maximization (EM), Monte Carlo EM (MCEM), and standard unadjusted Langevin algorithms (ULA) as baselines. Evaluation metrics will include convergence to the true parameter (measured by squared error), computational efficiency (number of gradient evaluations and runtime), and robustness to hyperparameters such as the number of particles and step size. Experiments will also investigate the impact of stochastic gradient approximations and validate theoretical error bounds under varying problem dimensions and particle counts.
45f64a0762fad89f06fd06d227a4d8e42a6b365d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new class of interacting particle Langevin algorithms for maximum marginal likelihood estimation, characterized by the injection of noise into parameter dynamics, which enables the derivation of nonasymptotic, uniform-in-time error bounds independent of the number of particles. This is the first method to provide such theoretical guarantees for interacting particle systems in the MMLE context. The framework also establishes a direct connection between the number of particles and the inverse temperature parameter in global optimization, offering a principled and scalable alternative to classical EM and MCMC-based methods. Extensions to stochastic gradient settings further broaden the applicability to large-scale and practical machine learning problems.

4637f79ddfaf923ce569996ffa5b6cda1996faa1.title: Jailbreaking Black Box Large Language Models in Twenty Queries
4637f79ddfaf923ce569996ffa5b6cda1996faa1.research_question: How can prompt-level jailbreaks be automatically and efficiently generated for black-box large language models (LLMs) without human intervention, and how effective and transferable are such attacks across a range of state-of-the-art LLMs?
4637f79ddfaf923ce569996ffa5b6cda1996faa1.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that an automated, iterative, black-box approach leveraging an attacker LLM can efficiently generate semantic, interpretable prompt-level jailbreaks for a target LLM, requiring significantly fewer queries than existing methods, while maintaining high effectiveness and transferability across different LLM architectures.
4637f79ddfaf923ce569996ffa5b6cda1996faa1.proposed_method: The proposed method, Prompt Automatic Iterative Refinement (PAIR), introduces a fully automated framework for generating prompt-level jailbreaks using only black-box access to both the attacker and target LLMs. The process involves four main steps: (1) the attacker LLM generates a candidate adversarial prompt based on a specified malicious objective; (2) this prompt is submitted to the target LLM, which returns a response; (3) a JUDGE function evaluates the prompt-response pair to determine if a jailbreak has occurred; (4) if unsuccessful, the attacker receives the conversation history and iteratively refines its prompt, incorporating chain-of-thought reasoning and improvement assessments. The attacker’s system prompt is carefully designed to encourage creativity and uses templates based on logical appeal, authority endorsement, and role-playing, with in-context examples and improvement instructions. The algorithm is parallelizable, allowing multiple conversation streams to search the prompt space efficiently.
4637f79ddfaf923ce569996ffa5b6cda1996faa1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the JailbreakBench (JBB-Behaviors) dataset, which comprises 100 behaviors across ten harmful content categories. The attacker LLM is primarily Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct, with ablations using GPT-3.5 and Vicuna. Target LLMs include both open-source (Vicuna-13B, Llama-2-7B) and closed-source (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Claude-1, Claude-2, Gemini-Pro) models, all accessed via public APIs. The evaluation metric is Jailbreak% (percentage of behaviors successfully jailbroken) and Queries per Success (average queries needed for a successful jailbreak), with LlamaGuard serving as the primary JUDGE function due to its low false positive rate and reproducibility. Baselines include the GCG white-box attack and human-crafted jailbreaks from jailbreakchat.com. Additional experiments will assess transferability of discovered jailbreaks, robustness against defenses (SmoothLLM and perplexity filters), and the impact of attacker model choice, system prompt design, and parallelization parameters.
4637f79ddfaf923ce569996ffa5b6cda1996faa1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to fully automate prompt-level jailbreak generation for black-box LLMs without human involvement, achieving orders-of-magnitude improvements in query efficiency over existing methods. PAIR produces interpretable, semantic jailbreaks with strong transferability across both open- and closed-source LLMs, including models previously not vulnerable to automated attacks. The method is highly parallelizable, cost-effective, and accessible, requiring no specialized hardware. The framework also introduces a novel use of attacker LLMs with chain-of-thought reasoning and improvement assessments, and provides a reproducible, scalable tool for red teaming and stress-testing LLM safety.

46505719a9c26625d922101f50fd8a302abfa9c7.title: Alias-Free Convnets: Fractional Shift Invariance via Polynomial Activations
46505719a9c26625d922101f50fd8a302abfa9c7.research_question: How can convolutional neural networks (CNNs) be architecturally designed to achieve true shift-invariance, including invariance to both integer and fractional (sub-pixel) translations, thereby improving robustness to adversarial image translations and common corruptions?
46505719a9c26625d922101f50fd8a302abfa9c7.hypothesis: Replacing standard non-linearities in CNNs with carefully designed polynomial activations, combined with alias-free downsampling and normalization layers, will result in CNNs that are truly shift-invariant (including for sub-pixel translations), and robust to adversarial translation attacks and common image corruptions, without significant loss in classification accuracy.
46505719a9c26625d922101f50fd8a302abfa9c7.proposed_method: A novel CNN architecture, termed Alias-Free Convnet (AFC), will be developed by modifying a state-of-the-art baseline (ConvNeXt) to eliminate aliasing at every stage. Downsampling layers will be replaced with BlurPool operations that apply ideal low-pass filtering in the Fourier domain before subsampling, ensuring that no high-frequency components cause aliasing. Standard non-linear activation functions (e.g., GeLU) will be replaced with trainable polynomial activations of degree two, wrapped in an alias-free processing scheme involving upsampling, polynomial transformation, low-pass filtering, and downsampling. Layer normalization will be adjusted to scale activations per layer rather than per pixel, maintaining shift-equivariance. Circular convolutions and padding will be used to support periodic boundary conditions, and special care will be taken in the first downsampling layer to avoid unnecessary loss of high-frequency information. The overall design ensures that both the feature extractor is shift-equivariant and the classifier is shift-invariant, even for fractional translations.
46505719a9c26625d922101f50fd8a302abfa9c7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ImageNet dataset, using the ConvNeXt architecture as the baseline and comparing against both the baseline and the Adaptive Polyphase Sampling (APS) method. Models will be trained and evaluated with circular translations, and adversarial robustness will be assessed by measuring classification accuracy under all possible integer, half-pixel, and fractional translations. Consistency metrics will quantify the percentage of predictions unchanged by translations. Additional evaluations will include adversarial translation attacks (black-box), robustness to out-of-distribution corruptions using ImageNet-C, and further tests with zero-padding and bilinear interpolation to simulate real-world translation scenarios. Evaluation metrics will include standard top-1 classification accuracy, consistency under translation, and adversarial accuracy (the fraction of samples classified correctly for all translations in a given set).
46505719a9c26625d922101f50fd8a302abfa9c7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to achieve certified shift-invariance in CNNs for both integer and fractional translations by addressing aliasing in both downsampling and non-linear layers. The method introduces the use of polynomial activations, wrapped in an alias-free processing scheme, as a practical and effective alternative to standard non-linearities for large-scale image classification. The architecture demonstrates, for the first time, competitive performance with polynomial activations on ImageNet. The resulting model achieves perfect consistency and robustness to adversarial translation attacks, outperforming existing shift-invariant and anti-aliasing methods, and maintains robustness even under severe image corruptions and non-circular translation scenarios.

4650a9593cfbb3890d314467110d2d49ef986e48.title: Shape, Light, and Material Decomposition from Images using Monte Carlo Rendering and Denoising
4650a9593cfbb3890d314467110d2d49ef986e48.research_question: How can physically-based rendering techniques, specifically Monte Carlo integration with ray tracing and advanced denoising, be leveraged to improve the decomposition of shape, material, and lighting from multi-view images for high-quality 3D scene reconstruction?
4650a9593cfbb3890d314467110d2d49ef986e48.hypothesis: Integrating Monte Carlo-based differentiable rendering with variance reduction techniques such as multiple importance sampling and differentiable denoising will enable efficient and accurate joint reconstruction of geometry, materials, and lighting from multi-view images, resulting in superior separation of material and lighting compared to existing methods.
4650a9593cfbb3890d314467110d2d49ef986e48.proposed_method: A novel inverse rendering pipeline will be developed that jointly optimizes explicit triangle mesh geometry, spatially-varying physically-based (PBR) material parameters, and high-dynamic-range environment lighting from multi-view images with known camera poses and segmentation masks. The method will utilize a differentiable Monte Carlo renderer for direct illumination, incorporating ray tracing to handle complex lighting and shadow effects. To address the high variance and noise inherent in Monte Carlo integration, the pipeline will integrate multiple importance sampling (MIS) across light, diffuse, and specular sampling strategies, and apply differentiable image denoisers, including both neural denoisers (such as OIDN) and cross-bilateral filters, to the rendered outputs. The rendering equation will be decomposed into albedo, demodulated diffuse lighting, and specular lighting, enabling targeted regularization and denoising for improved separation of material and lighting. Optimization will be performed via gradient-based methods (e.g., Adam), with gradients backpropagated through the renderer and denoiser to jointly update all scene parameters.
4650a9593cfbb3890d314467110d2d49ef986e48.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several datasets, including the NeRFactor relighting dataset, the NeRF synthetic dataset (with scenes such as Chair, Hotdog, Lego, Materials, and Mic), and custom synthetic datasets with complex geometry. Each dataset will provide multi-view images with known camera poses and segmentation masks. Baseline comparisons will be made against NVDIFFREC and NeRFactor, with evaluation focused on the quality of material and lighting separation, as well as relighting and view interpolation performance. Quantitative metrics will include PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS, computed over novel views and relit scenes. Ablation studies will assess the impact of different denoising strategies and sample counts on reconstruction quality. All relighting results will be rendered in Blender Cycles with denoising, and optimization will be performed at varying sample counts to evaluate computational efficiency and convergence behavior.
4650a9593cfbb3890d314467110d2d49ef986e48.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the integration of differentiable Monte Carlo rendering with advanced variance reduction techniques, specifically multiple importance sampling and differentiable denoising, into the inverse rendering pipeline for multi-view 3D reconstruction. This enables efficient joint optimization of explicit mesh geometry, materials, and lighting, achieving significantly improved separation of material and lighting compared to prior methods. The method demonstrates that denoising can be an integral component of high-quality inverse rendering, allowing for practical optimization at low sample counts and improved relighting capabilities. Additionally, the approach provides assets in a format directly compatible with standard DCC tools and game engines.

465471bb5bf1a945549d6291c2d23367966b4957.title: In-Context Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
465471bb5bf1a945549d6291c2d23367966b4957.research_question: How can language models be effectively augmented with external retrieval mechanisms to improve language modeling and downstream task performance, without requiring modifications or retraining of the language model architecture?
465471bb5bf1a945549d6291c2d23367966b4957.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that prepending retrieved grounding documents to the input of an unmodified, off-the-shelf language model—leveraging in-context retrieval—can yield substantial improvements in language modeling performance and downstream tasks, and that further gains can be achieved by specializing the retrieval and reranking mechanisms for the language modeling objective.
465471bb5bf1a945549d6291c2d23367966b4957.proposed_method: The proposed method, termed In-Context Retrieval-Augmented Language Modeling (In-Context RALM), augments a frozen, off-the-shelf language model by prepending relevant documents retrieved from an external corpus directly to the model's input, without any further training or modification of the language model. Retrieval is performed at regular intervals (retrieval stride) during generation, using a sparse BM25 retriever or dense neural retrievers such as BERT, Contriever, or Spider. The retrieval query consists of the most recent tokens in the input prefix, with the query length and retrieval stride treated as tunable hyperparameters. To further enhance performance, a reranking stage is introduced: either a zero-shot reranking using a small language model to select the most relevant document among the top-k retrieved candidates, or a dedicated reranker trained via self-supervision from the language modeling signal to predict which document will best support the next segment of text generation.
465471bb5bf1a945549d6291c2d23367966b4957.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five diverse language modeling datasets: WikiText-103, RealNews, and three subsets from The Pile (ArXiv, StackExchange, FreeLaw). Open-source language models from the GPT-2, GPT-Neo, OPT, and LLaMA families, ranging from 110M to 66B parameters, will be used. Baselines include standard language modeling without retrieval and In-Context RALM with various retrievers and reranking strategies. Evaluation metrics include word-level and token-level perplexity for language modeling, and exact match for open-domain question answering tasks (Natural Questions and TriviaQA). The retrieval corpora will be standardized, and contamination between training and evaluation sets will be avoided. Hyperparameters such as retrieval stride and query length will be optimized based on development set performance. Additional experiments will assess the impact of reranking, the number of retrieved documents, and the use of smaller models for reranking.
465471bb5bf1a945549d6291c2d23367966b4957.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a simple yet effective retrieval-augmented framework that requires no modification or retraining of the language model, enabling easy deployment even when only API access is available. It systematically investigates the effectiveness of off-the-shelf retrievers and demonstrates that a sparse BM25 retriever outperforms neural retrievers for in-context augmentation. The method further innovates by introducing and evaluating both zero-shot and trainable reranking mechanisms tailored to the language modeling task, showing that significant gains can be achieved through specialized document selection. The approach is broadly applicable across model sizes and domains, and provides a clean probe for developing and benchmarking retrieval strategies for language model grounding.

466785139a2270b554aa274b3d312723afce8e77.title: UMIX: Improving Importance Weighting for Subpopulation Shift via Uncertainty-Aware Mixup
466785139a2270b554aa274b3d312723afce8e77.research_question: How can model robustness to subpopulation shift be improved in machine learning, particularly in scenarios where group labels are unavailable during training?
466785139a2270b554aa274b3d312723afce8e77.hypothesis: Incorporating uncertainty-aware importance weighting into mixup-based data augmentation will mitigate overfitting in over-parameterized neural networks and improve worst-case and average accuracy across subpopulations, even without access to group labels.
466785139a2270b554aa274b3d312723afce8e77.proposed_method: A novel framework, Uncertainty-Aware Mixup (UMIX), is proposed to address subpopulation shift by integrating uncertainty-based importance weighting with the mixup data augmentation strategy. The method first estimates the epistemic uncertainty of each training sample using a trajectory-based approach inspired by Bayesian learning, leveraging predictions from multiple training epochs to approximate posterior sampling efficiently. Importance weights are assigned to each sample in proportion to its estimated uncertainty, with higher weights for samples that are more frequently misclassified (often from minority subpopulations). During training, mixup is applied probabilistically to pairs of samples, and the loss for each mixed sample is computed as a weighted linear combination of the original samples' losses, scaled by their respective uncertainty-derived weights. The framework is designed to operate in both group-oblivious and group-aware settings, but does not require group labels for training.
466785139a2270b554aa274b3d312723afce8e77.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple benchmark datasets exhibiting subpopulation shift, including Waterbirds, CelebA, CivilComments, and the Camelyon17 medical imaging dataset, which also tests domain shift. The evaluation will focus on both average and worst-case accuracy across subpopulations, with particular emphasis on worst-case performance. Baseline methods for comparison will include empirical risk minimization (ERM), focal loss, various distributionally robust optimization (DRO) methods (such as CVaR-DRO, 2-DRO, and their variants), JTT, and mixup-based approaches (vanilla and in-group mixup). In the group-aware setting, additional baselines such as IRM, IB-IRM, V-REx, CORAL, GroupDRO, DomainMix, Fish, and LISA will be used. Model selection will be performed using both average and worst-case validation accuracy, and all experiments will be repeated multiple times to report mean and standard deviation. Kernel density estimation will be used for qualitative analysis of uncertainty estimates.
466785139a2270b554aa274b3d312723afce8e77.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new uncertainty-aware importance weighting mechanism integrated with mixup, which does not require access to group labels and is robust to overfitting in over-parameterized neural networks. The uncertainty estimation leverages training trajectories for efficient and reliable epistemic uncertainty quantification. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the method achieves a tighter generalization bound than traditional importance weighting approaches, with the bound depending on subpopulation heterogeneity. Empirical results show consistent improvements in worst-case and average accuracy across diverse datasets, outperforming both group-oblivious and many group-aware baselines.

467a7d2bd809ec5d93b7951d5b8a809c2da9d6be.title: MixVPR: Feature Mixing for Visual Place Recognition
467a7d2bd809ec5d93b7951d5b8a809c2da9d6be.research_question: How can visual place recognition systems be improved to achieve higher robustness and efficiency under challenging conditions such as severe appearance changes, repetitive structures, and real-world latency constraints?
467a7d2bd809ec5d93b7951d5b8a809c2da9d6be.hypothesis: A holistic feature aggregation technique based on all-MLP architectures, which mixes global relationships across feature maps from intermediate layers of a pre-trained CNN backbone, will yield more robust and efficient global descriptors for visual place recognition compared to existing local or pyramidal aggregation methods.
467a7d2bd809ec5d93b7951d5b8a809c2da9d6be.proposed_method: The proposed method, MixVPR, introduces a novel holistic feature aggregation framework for visual place recognition. Feature maps are extracted from intermediate layers of a pre-trained CNN backbone (e.g., ResNet-50), then each 2D feature map is flattened and passed through a cascade of L identical Feature-Mixer blocks. Each Feature-Mixer block consists solely of multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) with skip connections and non-linearities, iteratively incorporating global relationships within each feature map. The output is then projected through two fully connected layers: first depth-wise (channel-wise) and then row-wise, resulting in a compact global descriptor. The architecture allows for configurable descriptor dimensionality and leverages intermediate backbone features to reduce parameter count and computational cost.
467a7d2bd809ec5d93b7951d5b8a809c2da9d6be.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple large-scale and challenging VPR benchmarks, including Pitts250k-test, Pitts30k-test, SPED, MSLS, and Nordland. All methods will be trained on the same dataset (e.g., GSV-Cities) using the same backbone architecture (ResNet-50, cropped at the second last residual block for MixVPR) to ensure fairness. Baselines for comparison will include AVG, GeM, NetVLAD, SPE-NetVLAD, GatedNetVLAD, CosPlace, as well as two-stage retrieval techniques such as Patch-NetVLAD, TransVPR, DELG, and SuperGlue. Evaluation metrics will focus on recall@k (e.g., recall@1, recall@5, recall@10) and computational latency. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of the number of Feature-Mixer blocks, descriptor dimensionality, and backbone architecture on performance.
467a7d2bd809ec5d93b7951d5b8a809c2da9d6be.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to employ an all-MLP, holistic feature mixing strategy for visual place recognition, eliminating the need for local or pyramidal aggregation and self-attention mechanisms. By leveraging intermediate backbone features and a cascade of Feature-Mixer blocks, the method achieves state-of-the-art performance on all tested benchmarks with significantly fewer parameters and orders-of-magnitude faster inference compared to two-stage and attention-based methods. The architecture is highly configurable, lightweight, and demonstrates superior robustness to viewpoint, illumination, and seasonal changes, as well as repetitive structures and occlusions.

467e17330f558809316c3f2fbb943d7f1a5eccb2.title: Beyond Scalars: Concept-Based Alignment Analysis in Vision Transformers
467e17330f558809316c3f2fbb943d7f1a5eccb2.research_question: How can the analysis of representational alignment in vision transformers be made more fine-grained and interpretable, moving beyond scalar alignment measures to reveal universal and unique concepts within and across models trained under different learning paradigms?
467e17330f558809316c3f2fbb943d7f1a5eccb2.hypothesis: Defining and discovering concepts as nonlinear manifolds in feature space, rather than relying on linear or scalar-based measures, enables a more faithful and detailed alignment analysis of vision transformer representations, revealing both universal and unique conceptual structures that correlate with model supervision and training protocols.
467e17330f558809316c3f2fbb943d7f1a5eccb2.proposed_method: A novel methodology will be developed that defines concepts in the feature space of vision transformers as nonlinear manifolds, avoiding restrictive linearity assumptions. Concept discovery will be performed by first extracting feature vectors from intermediate layers of vision transformers, then applying UMAP for dimensionality reduction to preserve local and global structure, followed by HDBSCAN for density-based clustering to identify concept manifolds. Soft cluster membership (concept proximity scores) will be computed for each feature vector, reflecting nuanced degrees of belonging to multiple concepts. Representational alignment between models or layers will be quantified using a generalized Rand index adapted for fuzzy clusterings, which allows alignment to be partitioned at the concept level, enabling fine-grained comparison of universal and unique concepts across representations.
467e17330f558809316c3f2fbb943d7f1a5eccb2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a random, stratified subset (25%) of the ImageNet-1k dataset, using four vision transformer models (ViT-base, patch size 16, input size 224) pre-trained under different paradigms: fully supervised (FS), contrastive (CLIP), knowledge distillation (DINO), and masked autoencoding (MAE). Activations will be extracted from all transformer blocks for both sequence and CLS tokens. Hyperparameters for UMAP and HDBSCAN will be tuned to maximize clustering validity (DBCV) and minimize embedding distortion (RMSE). Baseline concept discovery methods (PCA, multi-dimensional linear subspaces, KMeans) will be compared against the proposed nonlinear manifold approach. Evaluation metrics will include concept-based alignment (CBA), class label alignment, token location alignment, concept count, and intrinsic dimensionality. Robustness will be assessed by measuring alignment consistency across multiple runs.
467e17330f558809316c3f2fbb943d7f1a5eccb2.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a concept-based alignment analysis framework that moves beyond scalar similarity measures by defining concepts as nonlinear manifolds in feature space. This enables partitioning alignment into individual concepts, providing detailed insights into the structure and evolution of representations within and across vision transformers. The method leverages density-based clustering on manifold-preserving embeddings and a generalized Rand index for fuzzy clusterings, allowing for nuanced, interpretable comparisons of universal and unique conceptual structures. This framework is claimed to reveal relationships between supervision strength and semantic structure in learned representations, offering new tools for model selection and understanding of generalization and robustness in vision transformers.

467eea042debb53c031d6fa7c45902815a6d92c3.title: When Do Prompting and Prefix-Tuning Work? A Theory of Capabilities and Limitations
467eea042debb53c031d6fa7c45902815a6d92c3.research_question: What are the fundamental capabilities and limitations of context-based fine-tuning methods, such as prompting, soft prompting (prompt tuning), and prefix-tuning, in modifying the internal computation and expressiveness of pretrained transformer models?
467eea042debb53c031d6fa7c45902815a6d92c3.hypothesis: Context-based fine-tuning methods, including soft prompting and prefix-tuning, are more expressive than discrete prompting due to their use of continuous embedding space, but they are still fundamentally less expressive than full fine-tuning and cannot enable models to learn entirely new attention patterns or tasks that require them.
467eea042debb53c031d6fa7c45902815a6d92c3.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted to characterize the expressiveness and limitations of context-based fine-tuning methods. Theoretical analysis will formalize the capacity of soft prompting and prefix-tuning in both unconditional and conditional generation settings, constructing explicit transformer architectures to demonstrate the maximum achievable expressiveness. The influence of prefixes on attention patterns and attention block outputs will be mathematically analyzed, contrasting these with the effects of full fine-tuning. Empirical experiments will be designed using minimal and multi-task transformer models to validate the theoretical predictions, examining whether prefix-tuning can elicit new behaviors, combine pretrained skills, or learn entirely novel tasks. Additional experiments will compare prefix-tuning with parameter-efficient alternatives such as LoRA, using equivalent numbers of trainable parameters.
467eea042debb53c031d6fa7c45902815a6d92c3.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize small-scale transformer models, including single-layer and multi-layer architectures with varying numbers of attention heads, trained on algorithmic tasks such as sorting sequences in ascending/descending order and simple arithmetic manipulations. Pretraining will be performed on a mixture of tasks to endow the model with multiple 'skills.' Fine-tuning and prefix-tuning will then be applied to both seen and novel tasks, with accuracy measured on held-out test sets. Attention patterns and residual stream activations will be visualized to assess the impact of prefix-tuning on internal representations. Baselines will include full fine-tuning and parameter-matched LoRA adaptations. Evaluation metrics will focus on task accuracy, ability to elicit or combine skills, and the capacity to learn new attention patterns.
467eea042debb53c031d6fa7c45902815a6d92c3.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a formal theoretical framework that precisely characterizes the expressiveness of context-based fine-tuning methods in transformer models. It provides explicit constructions demonstrating the exponential capacity of soft prompts compared to discrete prompts, and rigorously proves the structural limitations of prefix-tuning in modifying attention patterns. The work reconciles empirical successes of prefix-tuning with its theoretical limitations by showing that such methods can only elicit or combine pretrained skills, not learn fundamentally new behaviors. The proposal also claims to provide the first detailed analysis of the parameter efficiency of prefix-tuning relative to other adaptation methods like LoRA, and offers new insights into the interpretability and alignment implications of context-based fine-tuning.

468992bf970c37bd1fef58b78a6c2fcd8c018868.title: Scaling Laws for Generative Mixed-Modal Language Models
468992bf970c37bd1fef58b78a6c2fcd8c018868.research_question: What are the scaling properties and empirical behaviors of generative language models trained on mixed-modal data, and how do interactions between different modalities affect model performance, training dynamics, and optimal hyperparameter selection?
468992bf970c37bd1fef58b78a6c2fcd8c018868.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the scaling laws for mixed-modal generative language models can be characterized by extending uni-modal scaling laws with additional terms that explicitly model the competition and synergy between modalities. Furthermore, it is expected that there exist predictable regimes where increasing model and data scale can overcome modality competition, leading to synergistic performance improvements.
468992bf970c37bd1fef58b78a6c2fcd8c018868.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical investigation will be conducted to derive and validate scaling laws for generative language models trained on mixed-modal data. The method involves representing all modalities (e.g., text, image, speech, code, molecules) as sequences of discrete tokens using modality-specific tokenizers such as VQGAN for images and HuBERT for speech. A unified generative model, based on a decoder-only transformer architecture with causal masking, will be trained on combinations of these modalities at varying scales (model sizes from 8 million to 30 billion parameters and datasets from 5 to 100 billion tokens). The approach will fit scaling law parameterizations to both uni-modal and multi-modal training regimes, introducing additive terms to capture modality interactions. Empirical phenomena such as coordinate ascent-like optimization, training stability, and batch size effects will be analyzed in relation to the discovered scaling law parameters.
468992bf970c37bd1fef58b78a6c2fcd8c018868.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using seven modalities: Text, Image, Image-Text, Speech, Speech-Text, Code, and Molecules. Datasets include large-scale corpora such as the OPT dataset for text, custom and public datasets for images and speech, InCoder data for code, and SMILES representations from the Zinc dataset for molecules. All data will be tokenized into a unified vocabulary, and models will be trained using the metaseq codebase with PyTorch and fairscale for memory efficiency, employing a single epoch regime and Adam optimizer. Baselines will include uni-modal models for each modality, and bi-modal/multi-modal models for selected modality pairs. Evaluation metrics will primarily be perplexity (PPL) on held-out validation sets for each modality. Scaling law fits will be compared against empirical results to validate the predictive power of the proposed laws, and key phenomena such as the competition barrier and emergent training behaviors will be systematically measured.
468992bf970c37bd1fef58b78a6c2fcd8c018868.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel set of scaling laws for mixed-modal generative language models, explicitly modeling the competition and synergy between modalities as additive terms to existing uni-modal scaling laws. It provides the first empirical recipe for selecting hyperparameters in multi-modal settings based on uni-modal optima. The research uncovers and quantifies emergent phenomena unique to mixed-modal training, such as coordinate ascent-like optimization and modality-specific training flatness, and establishes empirical connections between scaling law parameters and training dynamics. The approach enables principled prediction of the compute and data regimes required to achieve synergy between modalities, advancing the understanding and design of unified generative models.

46943551a72ab1bf608067b63cb2668049b4b199.title: Denoising Diffusion Models for Plug-and-Play Image Restoration
46943551a72ab1bf608067b63cb2668049b4b199.research_question: Can diffusion models be effectively utilized as plug-and-play priors for general image restoration tasks, and how do they compare to existing discriminative and generative denoiser-based methods in terms of restoration quality, efficiency, and flexibility?
46943551a72ab1bf608067b63cb2668049b4b199.hypothesis: Integrating denoising diffusion models as generative priors within a plug-and-play image restoration framework will enable superior reconstruction faithfulness and perceptual quality across a range of inverse problems, while maintaining computational efficiency with a limited number of neural function evaluations.
46943551a72ab1bf608067b63cb2668049b4b199.proposed_method: A novel image restoration framework, termed DiffPIR, is proposed, which integrates denoising diffusion models as plug-and-play priors within the diffusion sampling process. The methodology employs the Half-Quadratic Splitting (HQS) algorithm to decouple the data fidelity and prior terms of the restoration optimization problem. At each iteration, the data subproblem is solved analytically or via proximal gradient steps, incorporating the measurement and degradation operator, while the prior subproblem leverages an off-the-shelf diffusion model as a generative denoiser. The reverse diffusion process is adapted to incorporate measurement information at each sampling step, and a hyperparameterized noise injection strategy is used to balance reconstruction fidelity and diversity. The approach supports arbitrary degradation operators and can be accelerated using DDIM-style non-Markovian sampling for fast inference.
46943551a72ab1bf608067b63cb2668049b4b199.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the FFHQ 256×256 and ImageNet 256×256 datasets, evaluating three representative image restoration tasks: super-resolution (4×), image deblurring (Gaussian and motion blur), and image inpainting (box, random, and prepared masks). Both noisy and noiseless measurement scenarios will be considered. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines, including diffusion-based methods (DDRM, DPS) and plug-and-play methods (DPIR), using pre-trained diffusion models for all approaches to ensure fairness. Evaluation metrics will include Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Frechet Inception Distance (FID), and Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity (LPIPS). The number of neural function evaluations (NFEs) will be reported, and ablation studies will be performed to analyze the impact of sampling steps, noise injection, and guidance strength.
46943551a72ab1bf608067b63cb2668049b4b199.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to systematically integrate denoising diffusion models as generative priors within a plug-and-play image restoration paradigm, enabling flexible handling of arbitrary degradation operators. The method achieves state-of-the-art perceptual quality and faithfulness across multiple restoration tasks with significantly fewer neural function evaluations compared to prior diffusion-based approaches. The approach also supports diverse and semantically consistent reconstructions, and provides a unified, training-free solution applicable to a wide range of inverse problems.

46cbae7bf0dc2e0c9ee07567e4eba94d5e9ee8bd.title: Doubly robust calibration of prediction sets under covariate shift.
46cbae7bf0dc2e0c9ee07567e4eba94d5e9ee8bd.research_question: How can prediction sets be constructed to provide reliable uncertainty quantification under covariate shift between training and test data distributions, without requiring restrictive assumptions or prior knowledge of the covariate shift?
46cbae7bf0dc2e0c9ee07567e4eba94d5e9ee8bd.hypothesis: Prediction sets with asymptotic nominal coverage can be constructed under covariate shift using a doubly robust approach, such that correct coverage is achieved if either the propensity score (covariate density ratio) or the conditional distribution of the response is estimated sufficiently well.
46cbae7bf0dc2e0c9ee07567e4eba94d5e9ee8bd.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed for constructing prediction sets under explainable covariate shift, leveraging semiparametric efficiency theory and the efficient influence function for the quantile of the unobserved outcome in the test population. The method will estimate the quantile of a conformal score function R(X, Y) using observed data, where R can be any suitable one-dimensional function (e.g., regression residuals or conformalized quantile residuals). Two algorithmic variants will be designed: one based on sample splitting and another that avoids sample splitting for greater efficiency. Both variants will combine arbitrary machine learning prediction algorithms with doubly robust estimation, ensuring that the coverage bias of the prediction set is negligible if either the propensity score or the conditional distribution is estimated well. The approach will also allow for aggregation of prediction sets from multiple machine learning algorithms to optimize prediction accuracy.
46cbae7bf0dc2e0c9ee07567e4eba94d5e9ee8bd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using both synthetic and real-world datasets to evaluate the proposed doubly robust prediction set methods. The methods will be compared against the weighted conformal prediction approach, particularly that of Tibshirani et al. (2019), as a baseline. Evaluation metrics will include empirical coverage rates, prediction set sizes, and computational efficiency. The experimental setup will include scenarios with known and unknown covariate shift, and will assess the robustness of the methods to estimation errors in nuisance parameters. Additional experiments will explore the aggregation of prediction sets from different machine learning algorithms and the extension to individual treatment effect prediction under causal inference assumptions.
46cbae7bf0dc2e0c9ee07567e4eba94d5e9ee8bd.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a doubly robust approach to prediction set construction under covariate shift, ensuring asymptotic nominal coverage if either the propensity score or the conditional response distribution is estimated well. The product bias form of the coverage error is a key innovation, leading to improved robustness and potentially smaller coverage bias compared to existing methods. The methodology is general and can be combined with any machine learning prediction algorithm, and it supports aggregation of prediction sets for optimal accuracy. The approach also extends to prediction of individual treatment effects and allows for sensitivity analysis beyond the explainable covariate shift setting.

46e82a2c2d90361f442c19b3c19afe9751aa9553.title: How Far Can Fairness Constraints Help Recover From Biased Data?
46e82a2c2d90361f442c19b3c19afe9751aa9553.research_question: To what extent can fairness constraints in machine learning classification mitigate or recover from systematic data bias, including under-representation and label bias, across a variety of data distributions, noise models, fairness definitions, and hypothesis classes?
46e82a2c2d90361f442c19b3c19afe9751aa9553.hypothesis: Fairness constraints, such as equal opportunity or demographic parity, when applied appropriately, can recover optimally accurate and fair classifiers from systematically biased data under certain conditions on the data distribution and bias parameters, even in the presence of complex noise models and for arbitrary hypothesis classes.
46e82a2c2d90361f442c19b3c19afe9751aa9553.proposed_method: A general theoretical framework will be developed to analyze and extend the recovery capabilities of fairness constraints in classification tasks under biased data scenarios. The approach will model various forms of data bias, including under-representation and label bias, as linear fractional transformations of the regression function. The methodology will characterize optimal fair classifiers using group-dependent thresholds and Lagrange multiplier formulations, and will extend these results to settings with Massart and malicious label noise. The proposal will further generalize to arbitrary data distributions using reject option classifiers, and to arbitrary hypothesis classes by introducing a robustness criterion for the optimal classifier. Additionally, the method will be adapted to handle time-varying data bias in multi-stage machine learning pipelines, analyzing both finite and infinite time horizons.
46e82a2c2d90361f442c19b3c19afe9751aa9553.experiment_details: Theoretical results will be established via rigorous mathematical proofs, supported by illustrative synthetic data distributions that simulate under-representation and label bias. The framework will be evaluated on stylized distributions with both i.i.d. and Massart label noise, and recovery regions will be visualized for various bias parameter settings. Baselines will include standard fair classification under equal opportunity and demographic parity, with and without bias correction. Evaluation metrics will focus on the ability to recover the Bayes optimal classifier and satisfy fairness constraints under biased training data. Extensions will be demonstrated for arbitrary data distributions, hypothesis classes, and time-varying bias scenarios.
46e82a2c2d90361f442c19b3c19afe9751aa9553.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified and generalizable theoretical approach that extends previous results on fairness recovery from biased data to a broader class of fairness constraints, data bias models, noise types, and hypothesis classes. It provides necessary and sufficient conditions for recovery under both equal opportunity and demographic parity, generalizes recovery guarantees to arbitrary distributions via reject option classifiers, and establishes robustness-based recovery for arbitrary hypothesis classes. The approach also pioneers the analysis of time-varying data bias in classification pipelines, offering new insights into the interplay between fairness constraints and dynamic data bias.

46ebd8e54cd72251642899da51deb8679cd76193.title: The Benefits of Implicit Regularization from SGD in Least Squares Problems
46ebd8e54cd72251642899da51deb8679cd76193.research_question: How does the generalization performance of stochastic gradient descent (SGD) compare to that of ridge regression in least squares problems, particularly in both underparameterized and overparameterized regimes?
46ebd8e54cd72251642899da51deb8679cd76193.hypothesis: For a broad class of least squares problem instances, SGD with a properly tuned constant stepsize and a logarithmically larger sample size will generalize no worse than ridge regression with any regularization parameter. Furthermore, there exist instances where SGD can achieve comparable or better generalization performance with significantly fewer samples than ridge regression.
46ebd8e54cd72251642899da51deb8679cd76193.proposed_method: A theoretical and empirical framework will be developed to compare the generalization ability of constant-stepsize, tail-averaged SGD and optimally-tuned ridge regression in least squares problems. The analysis will focus on excess risk bounds, leveraging recent advances in instance-dependent risk analysis for both algorithms. The study will consider both one-hot and Gaussian data distributions, deriving sharp upper and lower bounds for SGD and ridge regression, respectively. The methodology will include decomposing the risk into bias and variance components in the eigenspace of the data covariance matrix, and will characterize regimes where SGD's implicit regularization matches or outperforms explicit ridge regularization. Analytical results will be complemented by empirical simulations to validate theoretical findings.
46ebd8e54cd72251642899da51deb8679cd76193.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic least squares problems with Gaussian and one-hot data distributions. Multiple problem instances will be generated by varying the covariance matrix eigenspectrum (e.g., polynomial decay rates) and the structure of the true model parameter vector. For each instance, both SGD and ridge regression will be run with hyperparameters (stepsize for SGD, regularization parameter for ridge) finely tuned to minimize excess risk. The primary evaluation metric will be the population excess risk, and the main comparison will be the sample size required by each method to achieve a given risk threshold. Results will be averaged over multiple independent runs to ensure statistical robustness.
46ebd8e54cd72251642899da51deb8679cd76193.novelty_claims: The proposed research provides the first sharp, instance-based comparison of implicit regularization from SGD and explicit regularization from ridge regression in both underparameterized and overparameterized least squares settings. It introduces new sample inflation bounds, showing that SGD is always competitive with ridge regression up to logarithmic factors, and can be significantly better in certain regimes. The work also develops new technical tools for risk decomposition and lower bounding in high-dimensional settings, and offers empirical evidence supporting the theoretical claims.

46eea7d651420e60f9b1393e3f5eda14cbff7a2a.title: Can Sensitive Information Be Deleted From LLMs? Objectives for Defending Against Extraction Attacks
46eea7d651420e60f9b1393e3f5eda14cbff7a2a.research_question: How can specific sensitive information be effectively and permanently deleted from large language models (LLMs) to defend against both blackbox and whitebox extraction attacks, while minimizing collateral damage to overall model knowledge?
46eea7d651420e60f9b1393e3f5eda14cbff7a2a.hypothesis: Directly editing model weights to remove sensitive information, combined with targeted defense objectives that address vulnerabilities in both final outputs and intermediate representations, will significantly reduce the risk of successful extraction attacks without causing unacceptable degradation of general model performance.
46eea7d651420e60f9b1393e3f5eda14cbff7a2a.proposed_method: A comprehensive attack-and-defense framework will be developed for the deletion of sensitive information from LLMs at the level of model weights. The approach will adapt and extend model editing techniques (such as ROME and MEMIT) to minimize the probability of sensitive answers both in the final output and in intermediate hidden states, using objectives like Fact Erasure, Empty Response, Head Projection Defense, and Max-Entropy Defense. Whitebox attacks will be countered by maximizing entropy and suppressing sensitive tokens in intermediate layers, while blackbox attacks will be addressed through data augmentation and paraphrase-based defenses. The methodology will also include the design of new attack strategies, such as logit lens probing of hidden states and automated input rephrasing, to rigorously test the effectiveness of the deletion and defense mechanisms.
46eea7d651420e60f9b1393e3f5eda14cbff7a2a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on publicly available LLMs, including GPT-J, Llama-2, and GPT2-XL. Evaluation will use the CounterFact and zsRE datasets, focusing on factual question-answer pairs where the model is known to possess the target information. Attacks will include both whitebox (logit lens-based probing of intermediate hidden states) and blackbox (paraphrase-based prompt rephrasing) methods. Defense effectiveness will be measured by AttackSuccess@B (the probability that the sensitive answer appears in a set of B candidates), as well as by assessing model damage using Random ∆-Acc and Neighborhood ∆-Acc metrics. Baselines will include standard model editing objectives, and comparisons will be made across different editing and defense strategies.
46eea7d651420e60f9b1393e3f5eda14cbff7a2a.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified attack-and-defense framework for information deletion in LLMs, including the first systematic evaluation of both whitebox and blackbox extraction attacks against edited models. It proposes novel defense objectives that target not only the final output but also intermediate representations, and introduces new attack metrics and threat models based on candidate set extraction. The work aims to set a higher standard for privacy and safety evaluation in LLMs by demonstrating that current state-of-the-art editing methods are insufficient and by providing improved, though not yet universally effective, defense strategies.

46f9f7b8f88f72e12cbdb21e3311f995eb6e65c5.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
46f9f7b8f88f72e12cbdb21e3311f995eb6e65c5.research_question: How can retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) frameworks be systematically advanced to enhance the factuality, adaptability, and efficiency of large language models (LLMs) in knowledge-intensive and real-world tasks, and what methodologies can be developed to optimize the retrieval, generation, and augmentation processes within these systems?
46f9f7b8f88f72e12cbdb21e3311f995eb6e65c5.hypothesis: Integrating advanced retrieval, generation, and augmentation techniques—including modular architectures, optimized indexing, adaptive query handling, and iterative retrieval—will significantly improve the factual accuracy, adaptability, and domain-specific performance of LLMs compared to conventional approaches.
46f9f7b8f88f72e12cbdb21e3311f995eb6e65c5.proposed_method: A novel RAG framework will be developed, structured around three core components: retrieval, generation, and augmentation. The retrieval module will incorporate hybrid indexing strategies (including hierarchical, metadata-enriched, and knowledge graph-based indices) and advanced embedding models, supporting both dense and sparse retrieval. Query optimization will be achieved through expansion, rewriting, transformation, and intelligent routing, leveraging LLMs for sub-query generation and semantic filtering. The generation module will feature context curation techniques such as reranking, context compression, and fine-tuning of LLMs for domain adaptation and output alignment. The augmentation process will introduce modular and iterative retrieval mechanisms, enabling multi-step reasoning, adaptive retrieval based on intermediate outputs, and integration of specialized modules (e.g., memory, search, prediction, task adapters) for enhanced flexibility and task-specific adaptation. The entire system will support end-to-end training and allow for seamless integration of external adapters and reinforcement learning signals.
46f9f7b8f88f72e12cbdb21e3311f995eb6e65c5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a diverse set of knowledge-intensive tasks, utilizing a wide range of datasets including Wikipedia, CommonCrawl, MSMARCO, BEIR, domain-specific corpora (e.g., medical, legal), and structured sources such as knowledge graphs. Baseline comparisons will include standard LLMs, naive RAG, advanced RAG, modular RAG, fine-tuning (FT), and prompt engineering approaches. Evaluation metrics will encompass factual accuracy, recall, precision, MRR, diversity, context relevance, and downstream task performance. The experimental setup will include ablation studies on retrieval granularity, indexing strategies, query optimization techniques, and augmentation modules, as well as benchmarking against state-of-the-art systems using established RAG evaluation frameworks and leaderboards (e.g., MTEB, C-MTEB).
46f9f7b8f88f72e12cbdb21e3311f995eb6e65c5.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a comprehensive and modular RAG architecture that unifies and extends prior paradigms by enabling flexible integration of advanced retrieval, generation, and augmentation modules. Key innovations include the use of dynamic and hierarchical indexing, adaptive and multi-faceted query optimization, iterative and modular retrieval processes, and seamless incorporation of external adapters and reinforcement learning signals. The framework is designed to support both sequential and end-to-end training, offering enhanced adaptability to diverse tasks and domains. Additionally, the research will provide a systematic evaluation methodology, covering a broad spectrum of tasks, datasets, and metrics, and will establish new benchmarks for RAG systems in terms of factuality, efficiency, and real-world applicability.

4702d5a163477c734a54f3ed2d171dca1504eaae.title: Your Diffusion Model is Secretly a Zero-Shot Classifier
4702d5a163477c734a54f3ed2d171dca1504eaae.research_question: Can large-scale text-to-image diffusion models be leveraged as zero-shot image classifiers, and how do their classification and compositional reasoning abilities compare to state-of-the-art discriminative and contrastive models across a variety of benchmarks and distribution shifts?
4702d5a163477c734a54f3ed2d171dca1504eaae.hypothesis: Conditional density estimates from pretrained diffusion models can be used to perform zero-shot and supervised image classification without additional training, potentially achieving competitive accuracy and superior compositional reasoning and robustness compared to discriminative models.
4702d5a163477c734a54f3ed2d171dca1504eaae.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that repurposes conditional diffusion models as classifiers by estimating class-conditional likelihoods for a given input image and set of candidate classes. The approach, termed Diffusion Classifier, computes the evidence lower bound (ELBO) for each class by repeatedly adding noise to the input image, running the diffusion model's denoising process conditioned on each class, and measuring the prediction error (epsilon-prediction loss) between the true and predicted noise. The class with the lowest average prediction error is selected as the predicted label. To improve efficiency and reduce variance, the method employs shared noise and timestep samples across all classes and introduces adaptive evaluation strategies to prune unlikely classes early. Further, the method explores different timestep sampling strategies and objective weightings to optimize classification accuracy.
4702d5a163477c734a54f3ed2d171dca1504eaae.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of zero-shot and supervised classification benchmarks, including Food-101, CIFAR-10, FGVC-Aircraft, Oxford-IIIT Pets, Flowers102, STL-10, ImageNet, and ObjectNet, as well as the Winoground compositional reasoning benchmark. The proposed method will be evaluated using Stable Diffusion 2.0 for zero-shot classification and DiT (Diffusion Transformer) for supervised classification. Baselines will include strong discriminative models (e.g., CLIP, OpenCLIP, ResNets, ViTs), as well as alternative methods for extracting classifiers from diffusion models (e.g., classifiers trained on synthetic diffusion-generated data and mid-layer diffusion features). Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy, mean-per-class accuracy, and compositional reasoning scores. Out-of-distribution robustness will be assessed on ImageNet-V2, ImageNet-A, and ObjectNet. Key experimental details include the use of adaptive inference strategies, varying the number of noise/timestep samples, and ablation studies on objective weighting.
4702d5a163477c734a54f3ed2d171dca1504eaae.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to demonstrate that pretrained text-to-image diffusion models can be directly repurposed as zero-shot and supervised image classifiers without any additional training. The method achieves competitive or superior accuracy to strong discriminative and contrastive baselines, exhibits significantly better multimodal compositional reasoning on challenging benchmarks, and demonstrates improved robustness to distribution shift (effective robustness) compared to standard discriminative models. The framework is hyperparameter-free, model-agnostic, and introduces variance reduction and adaptive inference techniques to make diffusion-based classification practical and scalable.

47030369e97cc44d4b2e3cf1be85da0fd134904a.title: Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models
47030369e97cc44d4b2e3cf1be85da0fd134904a.research_question: How can universal and transferable adversarial attacks be developed to reliably circumvent the alignment mechanisms of large language models (LLMs) and induce them to generate objectionable or harmful content across a wide range of models and prompts?
47030369e97cc44d4b2e3cf1be85da0fd134904a.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a carefully designed, automatically optimized adversarial suffix can be appended to user queries to reliably induce aligned language models to generate objectionable content, and that such attacks can be made universal and transferable across different prompts and models, including both open-source and commercial LLMs.
47030369e97cc44d4b2e3cf1be85da0fd134904a.proposed_method: A novel adversarial attack methodology will be developed that appends an optimized suffix to user queries in order to induce aligned language models to produce affirmative and objectionable responses. The optimization process will combine greedy coordinate descent and gradient-based search over discrete token spaces, leveraging gradients to identify promising token substitutions and evaluating candidate replacements in batches. The method will target the model to begin its response with an affirmative phrase that repeats the user query, thereby increasing the likelihood of generating the desired harmful content. To ensure universality and transferability, the adversarial suffix will be optimized jointly across multiple prompts representing diverse harmful behaviors and across multiple models, aggregating gradients and losses to select the most effective universal attack string. The optimization will proceed incrementally, incorporating new prompts only after finding candidates that succeed on earlier ones, and will be extended to multi-model settings when tokenizers are compatible.
47030369e97cc44d4b2e3cf1be85da0fd134904a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a newly designed benchmark, AdvBench, which includes two main settings: (1) Harmful Strings, a collection of 500 harmful or toxic strings, and (2) Harmful Behaviors, a set of 500 instructions for objectionable actions. The primary evaluation metric will be Attack Success Rate (ASR), defined as the percentage of cases where the model outputs the exact target string or makes a reasonable attempt to comply with a harmful instruction. Cross-entropy loss will be used as a secondary metric for string elicitation. The proposed method will be compared against prior baselines including PEZ, GBDA, and AutoPrompt, with all methods run under consistent configurations (e.g., 20 optimizable tokens, 500 steps, batch size 512, top-k 256). Experiments will be performed on both open-source models (Vicuna-7B, Vicuna-13B, LLaMA-2-7B-Chat, Pythia, Falcon, Guanaco) and commercial models (ChatGPT, GPT-3.5, GPT-4, PaLM-2, Claude), evaluating both direct (white-box) and transfer (black-box) attack effectiveness.
47030369e97cc44d4b2e3cf1be85da0fd134904a.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first reliable, automatically generated universal adversarial prompts capable of circumventing alignment in both open-source and commercial LLMs, achieving high transferability across models and prompt types. The method combines greedy and gradient-based discrete optimization over token sequences, and innovates by jointly optimizing over multiple prompts and models to produce a single universal attack string. The approach significantly outperforms prior automatic prompt generation methods in both attack success rate and transferability, and establishes a new state-of-the-art in adversarial attacks on aligned language models.

4706711dc4e1e16424db9f454a1f3b092b972785.title: SVD-LLM: Truncation-aware Singular Value Decomposition for Large Language Model Compression
4706711dc4e1e16424db9f454a1f3b092b972785.research_question: How can large language models be compressed post-training to significantly reduce memory and computational requirements while minimizing accuracy loss, and what new techniques can improve upon existing SVD-based compression methods?
4706711dc4e1e16424db9f454a1f3b092b972785.hypothesis: Incorporating a truncation-aware data whitening technique that establishes a direct mapping between singular values and compression loss, combined with a sequential low-rank parameter update strategy, will enable more effective post-training compression of large language models with minimal accuracy degradation, outperforming existing SVD-based, pruning-based, and quantization-based methods.
4706711dc4e1e16424db9f454a1f3b092b972785.proposed_method: A novel post-training compression framework for large language models will be developed based on singular value decomposition (SVD). The method will first employ a truncation-aware data whitening process, where calibration data is used to generate activations, and a whitening matrix is computed via Cholesky decomposition to ensure that the whitened activations are orthonormal. SVD is then performed on the product of the weight matrix and the whitening matrix, and the smallest singular values are truncated, guaranteeing that compression loss is directly tied to the truncated singular values. To further mitigate accuracy loss, a sequential low-rank approximation strategy will be introduced: the two low-rank matrices resulting from SVD will be fine-tuned in sequence using a LoRA-inspired approach, preserving their low-rank structure and enabling global accuracy recovery. This sequential update ensures that the optimization of one matrix does not interfere with the other, leading to more stable and effective fine-tuning.
4706711dc4e1e16424db9f454a1f3b092b972785.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on seven large language models from three different families (LLaMA, OPT, and Mistral) at three scales (7B, 13B, 30B), using a total of 10 datasets spanning language modeling, commonsense reasoning, and generation tasks. Baselines will include state-of-the-art SVD-based compression methods (FWSVD, ASVD), structured pruning methods (LLM-Pruner, SliceGPT, BlockPruner), and quantization methods (PB-LLM, BiLLM, OneBit), as well as smaller pre-trained LLMs. Evaluation metrics will include perplexity for language modeling, accuracy for classification tasks, BLEU score for generation, and exact match accuracy for math tasks. Calibration data will be sampled from WikiText-2, and parameter updates will use the Alpaca dataset. Inference efficiency and memory reduction will be measured on both NVIDIA A100 GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs, with ablation studies to assess the contribution of each component and sensitivity to calibration data.
4706711dc4e1e16424db9f454a1f3b092b972785.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a truncation-aware data whitening technique that, for the first time, establishes a direct and theoretically grounded mapping between truncated singular values and model compression loss, enabling optimal selection of singular values for truncation. Additionally, a sequential low-rank parameter update strategy is developed to compensate for accuracy degradation, which is not addressed by existing SVD-based methods. The approach achieves state-of-the-art compression performance, especially at high compression ratios, and is orthogonal to quantization and pruning, allowing for hybrid compression strategies. The method also enables simultaneous reduction of model weights and runtime KV cache memory without additional accuracy loss, providing practical benefits for deployment on both GPU and CPU hardware.

470e6d56ba933805a421e2a973fda193bf42a055.title: Understanding Gradient Orthogonalization for Deep Learning via Non-Euclidean Trust-Region Optimization
470e6d56ba933805a421e2a973fda193bf42a055.research_question: What are the theoretical foundations and convergence properties of optimization methods based on gradient orthogonalization for deep learning, particularly in the context of non-Euclidean trust-region optimization, and how do these methods compare to existing optimizers in various problem settings including non-convex, star-convex, and second-order smooth functions?
470e6d56ba933805a421e2a973fda193bf42a055.hypothesis: Optimization methods utilizing stochastic non-Euclidean trust-region frameworks with gradient orthogonalization and momentum, particularly when combined with weight decay and extrapolation, can achieve improved or state-of-the-art convergence rates and practical performance for training deep neural networks, surpassing or matching existing optimizers such as AdamW, normalized SGD, and signSGD under appropriate conditions.
470e6d56ba933805a421e2a973fda193bf42a055.proposed_method: A stochastic non-Euclidean trust-region gradient method with momentum will be developed for composite optimization problems, where the trust region is defined with respect to an arbitrary non-Euclidean norm, including the spectral norm for matrix-valued problems. The method will generalize and unify several existing optimizers, such as normalized SGD, signSGD, and Muon, by appropriate choice of the norm. The approach will be extended to incorporate weight decay for star-convex functions and an extrapolation step for functions with Lipschitz-continuous Hessians, resulting in improved convergence rates. Theoretical convergence guarantees will be established for non-convex, star-convex, and second-order smooth settings, with explicit iteration complexity bounds derived for each case.
470e6d56ba933805a421e2a973fda193bf42a055.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard deep learning benchmarks, including both small-scale and large-scale language modeling tasks. The proposed algorithms will be evaluated against strong baselines such as AdamW, normalized SGD with momentum, signSGD with momentum, and Orthogonal-SGDM. Evaluation metrics will include convergence speed, final objective value, and generalization performance. The experimental setup will include ablation studies on the effects of weight decay and extrapolation, as well as analysis of iteration complexity and stability in practical training scenarios. Datasets and architectures will be chosen to reflect both theoretical interest (e.g., synthetic star-convex or non-convex functions) and practical relevance (e.g., transformer-based language models).
470e6d56ba933805a421e2a973fda193bf42a055.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a new theoretical interpretation of gradient orthogonalization as a first-order trust-region method under non-Euclidean norms, specifically the spectral norm for matrix problems. The stochastic non-Euclidean trust-region gradient method with momentum is developed as a unified framework that recovers and generalizes several existing optimizers, including Muon, normalized SGD, and signSGD. Novel convergence results are established for a broad range of settings, including non-convex, star-convex, and second-order smooth functions, with improved or matching iteration complexity compared to state-of-the-art methods. The work also provides the first theoretical explanation for the empirical superiority of Muon over Orthogonal-SGDM and clarifies the role of weight decay in large-scale language model training.

472830edf3bef643fef8a6994db7dec4c2e74584.title: LlavaGuard: An Open VLM-based Framework for Safeguarding Vision Datasets and Models
472830edf3bef643fef8a6994db7dec4c2e74584.research_question: How can an open, flexible, and high-performing vision-language model (VLM)-based framework be developed to reliably safeguard vision datasets and generative models against unsafe and policy-violating visual content across diverse safety taxonomies and regulatory requirements?
472830edf3bef643fef8a6994db7dec4c2e74584.hypothesis: A vision-language model framework, trained on a carefully constructed and annotated multimodal safety dataset with guided rationales and augmented for policy flexibility, will outperform existing state-of-the-art vision safeguards and VLMs in accurately and adaptively assessing visual content safety across a range of policies and real-world applications.
472830edf3bef643fef8a6994db7dec4c2e74584.proposed_method: A comprehensive open framework will be established for vision safeguards, encompassing a customizable safety taxonomy, detailed risk guidelines, data preprocessing, policy-based data augmentation, and a robust training setup. A multimodal safety dataset will be constructed by combining human-annotated images from existing sources (e.g., SMID) and web-scraped images to balance safety categories, each labeled with a safety rating, category, and guided rationale. Data augmentation techniques will be employed to simulate policy exceptions and context-specific safety requirements, enabling the model to flexibly adapt to varying policies. Vision-language models (VLMs) of different scales (e.g., 0.5B and 7B parameters) will be fine-tuned using this dataset, with a prompt-response setup requiring structured JSON outputs including safety rating, category, and rationale. Guided rationales will be synthetically generated using conditioned prompts to ensure high-quality, policy-aligned explanations, and model training will be optimized for both accuracy and policy responsiveness.
472830edf3bef643fef8a6994db7dec4c2e74584.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a held-out, balanced test set derived from the constructed multimodal safety dataset, with additional evaluations on real-world datasets such as ImageNet, COCO, and CC12M, as well as synthetic images generated by models like Stable Diffusion. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art VLMs (e.g., Llava, InternVL, Qwen2.5-VL), proprietary moderation tools (e.g., OpenAI Omni-Moderation), and specialized safeguards (e.g., LlamaGuard-3-Vision, ImageGuard, Siglip2Guard). Evaluation metrics will include balanced accuracy, recall, precision, and a novel Policy Exception Score (PES) that harmonically combines policy exception handling with classification accuracy. Additional experiments will assess the framework's effectiveness in large-scale dataset auditing and generative model safeguarding, as well as human agreement studies to validate model outputs.
472830edf3bef643fef8a6994db7dec4c2e74584.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the first open, VLM-based vision safeguard capable of flexible, policy-driven safety assessment with structured, rationale-rich outputs. Key innovations include a vision-specific safety taxonomy aligned with current AI regulations, a multimodal safety dataset with high-quality guided rationales, advanced policy-based data augmentation for context-aware training, and a prompt-response architecture enabling automatic, transparent, and adaptable safety evaluations. The framework demonstrates superior performance over existing open-source and proprietary safeguards in both accuracy and policy responsiveness, and is validated on both real and synthetic data, supporting real-world applications such as dataset auditing and generative model moderation.

47311538ddf2f938f87140cbba474db22b7b007a.title: ESPFormer: Doubly-Stochastic Attention with Expected Sliced Transport Plans
47311538ddf2f938f87140cbba474db22b7b007a.research_question: How can a more efficient and balanced attention mechanism be developed for Transformer architectures, ensuring doubly-stochastic attention distributions without incurring high computational costs, and can such a mechanism improve performance across diverse domains such as vision, point cloud classification, sentiment analysis, and neural machine translation?
47311538ddf2f938f87140cbba474db22b7b007a.hypothesis: A doubly-stochastic attention mechanism based on Expected Sliced Transport Plans (ESP), which avoids iterative Sinkhorn normalization and leverages differentiable soft sorting, will provide more balanced attention distributions, improve computational efficiency, and yield superior or comparable performance to existing attention mechanisms across multiple domains.
47311538ddf2f938f87140cbba474db22b7b007a.proposed_method: A novel attention mechanism is proposed that enforces doubly-stochastic constraints on attention matrices using the Expected Sliced Transport Plan (ESP) framework. This approach replaces iterative Sinkhorn normalization with a fully parallelizable method based on sliced optimal transport, where attention is computed by aggregating transport plans across multiple one-dimensional slices of the key and query distributions. Differentiable soft sorting is incorporated to enable gradient-based optimization and seamless integration into deep learning models. The method introduces an inverse temperature parameter to control the sparsity and sharpness of the attention distribution, and allows for a transition from soft to hard sorting during training and inference, further improving computational efficiency. Axis-aligned or learnable slices can be used, with the method supporting both fixed and adaptive slicing strategies.
47311538ddf2f938f87140cbba474db22b7b007a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a variety of domains and tasks, including image classification (using Vision Transformers on the Cats vs. Dogs dataset), point cloud classification (using Set Transformers and Point Cloud Transformers on the ModelNet40 dataset), sentiment analysis (on IMDb and TweetEval datasets), and neural machine translation (using IWSLT’14 German-to-English). Baseline comparisons will include classic Transformers, Sinkformer (Sinkhorn-based doubly-stochastic attention), and Differential Transformer architectures. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy for vision and sentiment tasks, and BLEU scores for translation tasks.
