Experimental setups will involve both plug-and-play replacement of attention modules in pre-trained models and fine-tuning with temperature annealing schedules, as well as ablation studies on the number and type of slices and the inverse temperature parameter. Runtime and memory efficiency will be measured and compared to baselines.
47311538ddf2f938f87140cbba474db22b7b007a.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a fully parallelizable, doubly-stochastic attention mechanism based on Expected Sliced Transport Plans, eliminating the need for computationally expensive iterative Sinkhorn normalization. It leverages differentiable soft sorting to enable end-to-end training and supports a transition to hard sorting for exact doubly-stochastic matrices and improved inference efficiency. The approach establishes a new connection between sliced optimal transport and attention mechanisms, providing a principled and efficient alternative to existing methods. Experimental results are expected to demonstrate consistent improvements in accuracy and efficiency across diverse tasks, as well as robustness in low-data regimes and compatibility with recent differential attention architectures.

4744029bbaf94ea8dc3b4a3fa2644fa4730fa09c.title: What Makes a Good Diffusion Planner for Decision Making?
4744029bbaf94ea8dc3b4a3fa2644fa4730fa09c.research_question: What are the key components and design choices that make an effective diffusion planner for decision making, particularly in offline reinforcement learning tasks, and how do different architectural and algorithmic options impact planning performance across diverse domains?
4744029bbaf94ea8dc3b4a3fa2644fa4730fa09c.hypothesis: Certain design choices in diffusion planners, such as the use of Transformers as the denoising network, jump-step planning strategies, action generation via inverse dynamics, and unconditional Monte Carlo sampling with selection, can outperform conventional practices and lead to improved decision-making performance in offline reinforcement learning settings.
4744029bbaf94ea8dc3b4a3fa2644fa4730fa09c.proposed_method: A systematic empirical investigation will be conducted to identify and evaluate the essential components of diffusion planners for decision making. The study will involve training and evaluating thousands of diffusion models, varying key factors such as guided sampling algorithms (classifier guidance, classifier-free guidance, Monte Carlo sampling with selection), denoising network backbones (U-Net vs. Transformer), action generation strategies (joint state-action distribution vs. inverse dynamics), and planning strategies (dense-step, jump-step, hierarchical). Each component will be isolated and analyzed using a control variable approach, modifying one factor at a time in otherwise optimized models. The final outcome will be the development of a simple yet strong diffusion planning baseline that incorporates the most effective design choices identified through these experiments.
4744029bbaf94ea8dc3b4a3fa2644fa4730fa09c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the D4RL benchmark suite, which includes diverse offline RL tasks such as Maze2D (spatial navigation), AntMaze (robotic locomotion and planning), and Franka Kitchen (robotic manipulation). The evaluation metric will be the average total reward achieved in online testing episodes. Over 6,000 diffusion models will be trained and evaluated, systematically sweeping across the design space of key components. Baseline comparisons will include both non-diffusion offline RL methods (e.g., BC, BCQ, CQL, IQL) and state-of-the-art diffusion-based planners and policies (e.g., Diffuser, AdpDfsr, DQL, IDQL, CEP, DD, HD). Additional validation will be performed on the Adroit Hand dataset to assess generalizability. The experimental setup will involve grid search and manual tuning for hyperparameters, and results will be averaged over hundreds of episode seeds for statistical robustness.
4744029bbaf94ea8dc3b4a3fa2644fa4730fa09c.novelty_claims: The proposed research provides the first comprehensive, large-scale empirical study dissecting the design space of diffusion planners for decision making in offline RL. It challenges several prevailing assumptions, demonstrating that unconventional choices—such as unconditional sampling with selection, Transformer-based denoising networks, and jump-step planning—can yield superior performance. The work introduces a new, simple, and strong diffusion planning baseline (Diffusion Veteran) that achieves state-of-the-art results on standard offline RL benchmarks. The findings offer actionable insights and practical guidelines for future diffusion planner design, and establish a foundation for further research into the synergy between diffusion planning and diffusion policy approaches.

475df79e1e140bcde323c19b4a9a460b81584c81.title: MALinZero: Efficient Low-Dimensional Search for Mastering Complex Multi-Agent Planning
475df79e1e140bcde323c19b4a9a460b81584c81.research_question: How can efficient planning be achieved in complex multi-agent environments with exponentially large joint action spaces, particularly in the context of Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS)?
475df79e1e140bcde323c19b4a9a460b81584c81.hypothesis: By leveraging low-dimensional representational structures on joint-action returns and formulating the joint-action selection as a contextual linear bandit problem, it is possible to enable efficient exploration and exploitation in multi-agent MCTS, thereby improving planning performance and learning speed over existing model-based and model-free multi-agent reinforcement learning methods.
475df79e1e140bcde323c19b4a9a460b81584c81.proposed_method: A novel approach, MALinZero, is proposed to address the exponential growth of the joint action space in multi-agent planning. The method projects joint-action returns into a low-dimensional space by modeling them as a linear combination of latent per-agent action rewards, which are estimated as an unknown parameter vector in a contextual linear bandit setting. The contextual linear bandit problem is solved using a strongly-convex, µ-smooth loss function to prioritize accurate estimation of high-reward joint actions and mitigate representational limitations. A linear Upper Confidence Bound applied to Trees (LinUCT) is derived for action selection, balancing exploration and exploitation in the low-dimensional space. Dynamic node generation is incorporated to efficiently sample and add new child nodes during tree expansion, and joint-action selection is formulated as a submodular maximization problem, solved with a (1−1/e)-approximation algorithm.
475df79e1e140bcde323c19b4a9a460b81584c81.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on established multi-agent planning benchmarks, including MatGame (a stateless matrix game with varying numbers of agents and actions), StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge (SMAC), and SMACv2. MALinZero will be compared against both model-based (MAZero, MAZero-NP, MA-AlphaZero) and model-free (MAPPO, QMIX) baselines. Evaluation metrics will include average reward (for MatGame) and win rate (for SMAC/SMACv2), with experiments run over multiple random seeds for statistical significance. The experimental setup will involve varying the number of agents and actions to test scalability, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the contributions of dynamic node generation and the general convex loss function.
475df79e1e140bcde323c19b4a9a460b81584c81.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a low-dimensional representation of joint-action returns for multi-agent MCTS, reducing the complexity from exponential to linear in the number of agents and actions. A new LinUCT rule is derived for efficient exploration and exploitation in this reduced space, with theoretical regret bounds established for the contextual linear bandit formulation. The joint-action selection problem is shown to be submodular, enabling efficient approximate maximization. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in multi-agent planning tasks, with faster learning and superior outcomes compared to both model-based and model-free baselines.

4762a974a6326279ecc355d294b56b3928642c44.title: VideoHallu: Evaluating and Mitigating Multi-modal Hallucinations on Synthetic Video Understanding
4762a974a6326279ecc355d294b56b3928642c44.research_question: Can vision-language models (VLMs) demonstrate genuine visual understanding and critical reasoning when confronted with synthetic videos that violate physical laws and commonsense, rather than relying on superficial language-visual correlations? How can the evaluation and training of VLMs be improved to better detect and mitigate hallucinations in such out-of-distribution, counterfactual scenarios?
4762a974a6326279ecc355d294b56b3928642c44.hypothesis: Exposure to high-quality, expert-annotated synthetic videos depicting violations of physics and commonsense, combined with reinforcement learning-based post-training (such as Group Relative Policy Optimization), will improve VLMs' ability to reason about and detect abnormalities in synthetic videos without degrading their performance on real-world video understanding tasks.
4762a974a6326279ecc355d294b56b3928642c44.proposed_method: A new benchmark dataset, VideoHallu, will be constructed by generating synthetic videos using state-of-the-art video generation models (e.g., Sora, Veo2, Runway Gen2, Kling) from carefully crafted prompts designed to elicit violations of physics, commonsense, spatial-temporal consistency, and alignment. Human experts will annotate these videos with question–answer pairs that probe for counter-intuitive phenomena and critical thinking, resulting in a dataset of over 3,000 QA pairs. Multiple leading VLMs will be evaluated on this dataset to assess their ability to detect visual and logical abnormalities. Two post-training strategies will be explored: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), using a mixture of real-world and synthetic video QA data. The effectiveness of these training paradigms will be compared, and ablation studies will be conducted to assess the impact of real versus synthetic data in the training mix.
4762a974a6326279ecc355d294b56b3928642c44.experiment_details: Experiments will involve evaluating 17 state-of-the-art VLMs, including both open-source and proprietary models (e.g., Qwen-2.5-VL, Video-R1, VideoChat-R1, Gemini-2.5-Pro, GPT-4o), on the VideoHallu test set. The dataset is split into 800 training, 908 validation, and 1,525 test QA pairs, with videos averaging 96 frames (5.3 seconds) at 23 FPS and 1042×588 resolution. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy across four categories: alignment, physics, spatial-temporal consistency, and commonsense reasoning. LLM-as-a-Judge (GPT-4o-mini) will be used for automated answer evaluation, with manual validation of a subset for reliability. Fine-tuning experiments will use both SFT and GRPO on two architectures (Qwen2.5-VL-7B and LLaVA-One-Vision), training on combinations of real-world (Video-R1) and synthetic (VideoHallu) data. Additional evaluation will be conducted on real-world video understanding benchmarks (MVBench, MMVU) to assess any trade-offs in performance.
4762a974a6326279ecc355d294b56b3928642c44.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first large-scale, expert-annotated synthetic video QA benchmark specifically designed to probe VLMs' ability to detect violations of physics and commonsense in out-of-distribution scenarios. It systematically evaluates the limitations of current VLMs in abnormality and hallucination detection using negative-control synthetic videos. The approach demonstrates that reinforcement learning (GRPO) with a mixture of real and synthetic data leads to significant improvements in critical visual reasoning for synthetic videos, without sacrificing real-world performance. The work highlights the necessity of high-quality, reasoning-rich synthetic data for robust VLM training and provides a scalable framework for future research in synthetic video understanding and hallucination mitigation.

47696145b3f88c4cc3f3c22035286b5d7ebce09d.title: TimesNet: Temporal 2D-Variation Modeling for General Time Series Analysis
47696145b3f88c4cc3f3c22035286b5d7ebce09d.research_question: How can temporal variation modeling in time series be improved to enable more effective and generalizable analysis across diverse tasks such as forecasting, imputation, classification, and anomaly detection?
47696145b3f88c4cc3f3c22035286b5d7ebce09d.hypothesis: Transforming 1D time series into a 2D representation that explicitly models both intraperiod and interperiod variations, and leveraging parameter-efficient 2D vision backbones, will enable more effective learning of temporal patterns and achieve superior performance across a wide range of time series analysis tasks.
47696145b3f88c4cc3f3c22035286b5d7ebce09d.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that first analyzes the multi-periodicity present in real-world time series using frequency domain analysis via Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). The most significant periods are adaptively identified, and the 1D time series is reshaped into a set of 2D tensors, where columns represent intraperiod variations and rows represent interperiod variations. Each 2D tensor is processed using a parameter-efficient inception block with multi-scale 2D convolutional kernels, enabling simultaneous modeling of local (intraperiod) and global (interperiod) temporal dependencies. The architecture, termed TimesNet, is constructed by stacking residual TimesBlocks, each of which aggregates features from multiple period-based 2D representations using amplitude-based softmax weighting. The design allows for the replacement of the inception block with other advanced 2D vision backbones, such as ResNet, ResNeXt, or ConvNeXt, to further enhance representation learning.
47696145b3f88c4cc3f3c22035286b5d7ebce09d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five mainstream time series analysis tasks: short-term and long-term forecasting, imputation, classification, and anomaly detection. Benchmarks include ETT (4 subsets), Electricity, Traffic, Weather, Exchange, ILI, and M4 for forecasting; UEA archive for classification; SMD, MSL, SMAP, SWaT, and PSM for anomaly detection. The evaluation metrics are MSE, MAE, SMAPE, MASE, OWA, accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, depending on the task. The proposed method will be compared against over 15 strong baselines, including RNN-based (LSTM, LSTNet, LSSL), CNN-based (TCN), MLP-based (LightTS, DLinear), and Transformer-based (Informer, Autoformer, FEDformer, ETSformer) models, as well as state-of-the-art task-specific approaches. Experiments will include ablation studies and efficiency comparisons, with model configurations and hyperparameters detailed in supplementary materials.
47696145b3f88c4cc3f3c22035286b5d7ebce09d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified, task-general backbone for time series analysis that explicitly disentangles and models both intraperiod and interperiod variations by transforming 1D time series into 2D tensors. This approach enables the use of powerful 2D vision backbones for time series tasks, bridging the gap between time series and computer vision communities. The method adaptively discovers multiple periods and aggregates multi-scale temporal features in a parameter-efficient manner, leading to consistent state-of-the-art performance across a diverse set of time series analysis tasks. The framework is flexible, allowing for the integration of various advanced 2D architectures to further boost performance.

4780d0a027c5c5a8e01d7cf697f6296880ffc945.title: Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate
4780d0a027c5c5a8e01d7cf697f6296880ffc945.research_question: How can the reasoning accuracy and factual validity of large language models be improved using collaborative or interactive mechanisms among multiple model instances, as opposed to single-agent prompting techniques?
4780d0a027c5c5a8e01d7cf697f6296880ffc945.hypothesis: Engaging multiple language model agents in a structured, multi-round debate process will lead to improved reasoning accuracy and factual correctness in generated responses, compared to single-agent or majority-voting approaches.
4780d0a027c5c5a8e01d7cf697f6296880ffc945.proposed_method: A multiagent debate framework is developed in which several instances of a large language model (LLM) independently generate candidate responses to a given query. Each agent then receives as input the responses of the other agents, and is prompted to critique, update, and refine its answer based on this additional context. This debate process is repeated over multiple rounds, with agents iteratively updating their answers until a consensus or convergence is reached. The debate prompts can be tuned to encourage either rapid consensus or more prolonged, thorough deliberation, and the approach is compatible with existing prompting strategies such as chain-of-thought. The method requires only black-box access to LLMs and can be applied to both homogeneous (same model) and heterogeneous (different models) agent pools.
4780d0a027c5c5a8e01d7cf697f6296880ffc945.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of reasoning and factuality tasks, including arithmetic expression evaluation, grade school math word problems (GSM8K), chess move prediction (using PGN notation and Stockfish for evaluation), factual biography generation (using a newly constructed dataset of 524 computer scientist biographies), MMLU (Massive Multitask Language Understanding), and chess move validity (BIG-Bench Chess-State Tracking Benchmark). Baselines will include single-agent generation, single-agent reflection, and multi-agent majority voting where applicable. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy for reasoning tasks, factual agreement with ground truth for biography generation, and validity or optimality scores for chess tasks. The primary experimental setup will use three agents and two rounds of debate, with additional analysis on the effects of increasing the number of agents, debate rounds, and prompt variations.
4780d0a027c5c5a8e01d7cf697f6296880ffc945.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel multiagent debate framework for language model generation that leverages iterative, cross-agent critique and consensus-building to improve both reasoning and factuality. Unlike prior methods, this technique requires only black-box access and is orthogonal to existing prompting or retrieval-augmented strategies. The method is shown to be effective across diverse tasks and is compatible with both homogeneous and heterogeneous agent pools. Additionally, a new factuality benchmark for biography generation is introduced, and the study provides a detailed analysis of the effects of agent number, debate rounds, and prompt design on performance.

47a0c4c9332979edd3b8a127e9d957c4748bbc78.title: Indexed Minimum Empirical Divergence for Unimodal Bandits
47a0c4c9332979edd3b8a127e9d957c4748bbc78.research_question: How can the unimodal structure of multi-armed bandit problems with one-dimensional exponential family distributions be optimally exploited to minimize regret, and what algorithmic approaches can achieve asymptotic optimality in this setting?
47a0c4c9332979edd3b8a127e9d957c4748bbc78.hypothesis: A bandit algorithm that leverages the unimodal structure and adapts the Indexed Minimum Empirical Divergence (IMED) framework can achieve asymptotically optimal regret, matching the theoretical lower bounds for unimodal bandit problems.
47a0c4c9332979edd3b8a127e9d957c4748bbc78.proposed_method: A new algorithm, IMED-UB (Indexed Minimum Empirical Divergence for Unimodal Bandits), is proposed, which adapts the IMED approach to the unimodal bandit setting. The method restricts arm selection at each time step to the current empirically best arm and its immediate neighbors in the underlying unimodal graph, where the graph encodes the partial order among arms. Each arm is assigned an index based on the empirical mean and the Kullback-Leibler divergence to the current best empirical mean, plus a logarithmic exploration bonus. At each round, the arm with the minimum index among this restricted set is selected for pulling. The algorithm does not require explicit optimization procedures or a separation between exploration and exploitation phases, and its design ensures that only the neighborhood of the optimal arm is sampled at logarithmic rates, while other arms are sampled sub-logarithmically.
47a0c4c9332979edd3b8a127e9d957c4748bbc78.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic datasets generated from Bernoulli, Gaussian (with variance 0.25), and Exponential distributions, using a unimodal structure represented by a graph with a maximum degree of 2. The mean vector will be unimodal, e.g., (0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.25, 0.20, 0.15, 0.10, 0.05), and the performance will be evaluated over 500 independent runs for each distribution family. The proposed IMED-UB algorithm will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as OSUB and UTS. The primary evaluation metric will be cumulative regret, averaged over multiple runs, to assess both asymptotic and finite-time performance.
47a0c4c9332979edd3b8a127e9d957c4748bbc78.novelty_claims: The proposed algorithm is the first to adapt the IMED framework to unimodal bandits, achieving asymptotic optimality with a concise finite-time analysis. Unlike previous approaches, IMED-UB does not require explicit optimization procedures or round-based exploration/exploitation separation, and it provides explicit empirical lower and upper bounds on arm pulls. The proof techniques developed, particularly the use of concentration inequalities without additional log-log bonuses, simplify the analysis and may be of independent interest to the bandit community. Empirical results demonstrate that IMED-UB matches or outperforms existing state-of-the-art algorithms in practice.

47e7bd83c029a43cf55afd600ef067667ecc4344.title: Estimating Conditional Mutual Information for Dynamic Feature Selection
47e7bd83c029a43cf55afd600ef067667ecc4344.research_question: How can dynamic feature selection be improved to enable accurate predictions with minimal feature acquisition cost, while supporting variable budgets, non-uniform feature costs, and the incorporation of prior information across diverse data modalities?
47e7bd83c029a43cf55afd600ef067667ecc4344.hypothesis: Estimating conditional mutual information (CMI) in a discriminative fashion, rather than relying on generative models or direct argmax prediction, will enable more effective dynamic feature selection policies that achieve superior cost-accuracy tradeoffs, support flexible feature budgets and costs, and allow integration of prior information.
47e7bd83c029a43cf55afd600ef067667ecc4344.proposed_method: A novel dynamic feature selection framework will be developed that estimates the conditional mutual information (CMI) between candidate features and the response variable in a discriminative manner. Two neural networks will be jointly trained: a predictor network that outputs predictions for any subset of features, and a value network that estimates the CMI for each unobserved feature given the current feature subset. The value network is trained using a regression objective where the target is the incremental improvement in prediction loss when a new feature is added, and theoretical analysis shows that this objective recovers the true CMI at optimality. The method will be extended to incorporate prior information (such as auxiliary features or sketches) by conditioning both networks on this information, and will handle non-uniform feature costs by selecting features based on the ratio of estimated CMI to feature cost. Variable feature budgets will be supported by introducing flexible stopping criteria, including budget, confidence, or penalized CMI thresholds.
47e7bd83c029a43cf55afd600ef067667ecc4344.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of tabular and image datasets, including medical diagnosis tasks (e.g., intubation prediction, dementia onset prediction), MNIST (formulated as a tabular problem), and image classification datasets such as Imagenette, ImageNet-100, and a histopathology dataset. The proposed method will be compared against both static and dynamic feature selection baselines, including supervised Concrete Autoencoders, mRMR, CMICOT, Argmax Direct, EDDI, Hard Attention, and RL-based methods (CwCF and OL). Evaluation metrics will include AUROC for medical tasks, top-1 accuracy for image classification, and cost-accuracy tradeoff curves for varying feature acquisition budgets and costs. Experiments will also assess the impact of non-uniform feature costs, the incorporation of prior information, and the use of modern network architectures (ResNets, ViTs) for handling partial inputs.
47e7bd83c029a43cf55afd600ef067667ecc4344.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first discriminative method for directly estimating CMI for dynamic feature selection, enabling accurate and efficient feature selection without generative modeling. It supports variable per-sample feature budgets, non-uniform feature costs, and the integration of prior information, all within a unified framework. The method allows for flexible stopping criteria and leverages modern neural architectures to handle partial inputs, demonstrating superior performance and scalability compared to existing generative and discriminative baselines.

47fff0f40e52d7ad55bdfcae690bef3f889453d6.title: FIND: A Function Description Benchmark for Evaluating Interpretability Methods
47fff0f40e52d7ad55bdfcae690bef3f889453d6.research_question: How can the evaluation of automated interpretability methods for neural network submodules be systematically benchmarked using functions with known structure across diverse domains, and what are the limitations of current large language model-based approaches in generating accurate, human-legible descriptions of such functions?
47fff0f40e52d7ad55bdfcae690bef3f889453d6.hypothesis: Automated interpretability agents, particularly those leveraging large language models, can generate accurate and human-interpretable descriptions of black-box functions across numeric, string, and semantic domains when provided with a comprehensive benchmark; however, these agents may exhibit systematic limitations in capturing local details and complex behaviors without additional tools or targeted evaluation protocols.
47fff0f40e52d7ad55bdfcae690bef3f889453d6.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark suite, FIND (Function INterpretation and Description), will be constructed by procedurally generating over 2000 function interpretation problems spanning numeric operations, string manipulations, and synthetic neural modules that mimic real-world neural network behaviors. Each function will be implemented as an independent Python script, allowing black-box access for interpreters, and will include both atomic and composed functions, with complexity introduced via composition, noise, domain corruption, and approximation. Automated interpretability agents, powered by large language models, will interact with these functions by selecting inputs, observing outputs, and iteratively updating hypotheses to produce structured descriptions in both code and natural language. Evaluation protocols will include both code-based and language-based assessments, with interpreters required to approximate function behavior, identify domain-specific anomalies, and articulate underlying rules or concepts.
47fff0f40e52d7ad55bdfcae690bef3f889453d6.experiment_details: Experiments will involve running interpretability agents and non-interactive baselines (e.g., MILAN-style approaches) using off-the-shelf LMs such as GPT-4, GPT-3.5, and Llama-2 on the FIND benchmark. Datasets will include 1000 numeric functions, 1000 string functions, and a variety of synthetic neural modules constructed from Wikidata properties, with both atomic and composed variants. Evaluation metrics will include normalized mean squared error (NMSE) for code-based descriptions, exact match accuracy for string functions, and a unit-testing protocol for language-based descriptions, using a fine-tuned LM evaluator (vicuna-evaluator) to judge alignment with ground-truth function behavior. Baselines will be compared on their ability to recover function structure, describe domain corruptions, and generate accurate code or language explanations, with detailed analysis of success rates across function categories and subcategories.
47fff0f40e52d7ad55bdfcae690bef3f889453d6.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark provides the first large-scale, extensible suite for evaluating automated interpretability methods on functions with known ground-truth structure, enabling systematic and reproducible assessment of both code- and language-based explanations. The approach introduces interactive interpretability agents that autonomously generate and test hypotheses about black-box functions, moving beyond static exemplar-based evaluation. FIND supports targeted evaluation of interpreters' abilities to identify domain-specific anomalies, compositional structure, and noise models, and is designed to evolve with the field by incorporating new function types, interaction paradigms, and evaluation metrics. This work aims to drive the development of more robust, general-purpose interpretability tools and to reveal the current limitations of LM-based agents in automated model interpretation.

48034b05b18621274e5c2e46cfa31dcdab44a45b.title: ADePT: Adaptive Decomposed Prompt Tuning for Parameter-Efficient Fine-tuning
48034b05b18621274e5c2e46cfa31dcdab44a45b.research_question: How can parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods for large language models be improved to achieve better adaptation to downstream tasks without increasing inference time or the number of trainable parameters?
48034b05b18621274e5c2e46cfa31dcdab44a45b.hypothesis: Introducing adaptive, token-specific embedding offsets via a shallow, token-shared feed-forward neural network, combined with a short soft prompt, will enable more effective and expressive parameter-efficient fine-tuning than position-based or fixed-offset approaches, leading to improved performance across diverse tasks and models.
48034b05b18621274e5c2e46cfa31dcdab44a45b.proposed_method: A novel parameter-efficient fine-tuning method, Adaptive Decomposed Prompt Tuning (ADePT), will be developed. This method will utilize a short soft prompt prepended to the input token embeddings, similar to previous prompt tuning approaches, but will replace the position-based offset mechanism with a shallow, token-shared feed-forward neural network (a two-layer MLP). This neural network will compute adaptive embedding offsets for each token based on its embedding, ensuring that each token receives a unique, input-dependent offset regardless of its position in the sequence. The network will be designed to keep the total number of trainable parameters comparable to vanilla prompt tuning by adjusting the bottleneck size and soft prompt length. The updated token embeddings will be the sum of the original embeddings and the neural network-generated offsets, enabling position-independent and input-adaptive modification of the embedding space.
48034b05b18621274e5c2e46cfa31dcdab44a45b.experiment_details: The proposed method will be evaluated on a comprehensive suite of 23 natural language processing tasks, including benchmarks such as GLUE, SuperGLUE, MRQA 2019 Shared Task, MBPP, and additional datasets like WinoGrande, Yelp-2, SciTail, and PAWS-Wiki. Experiments will be conducted on four pre-trained language models of varying scales, including T5-base (220M parameters), T5-3B, CodeGen-350M, and Llama3-8B. Baselines will include full fine-tuning, vanilla prompt tuning, Decomposed Prompt Tuning (DePT), LoRA, Adapter, BitFit, LST, and prompt transfer/multi-task variants (SPoT, ATTEMPT, MPT). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, F1, Pearson correlation, and pass@1 for code generation, with results averaged over multiple runs where appropriate. Hyperparameters such as soft prompt length and MLP bottleneck size will be tuned to ensure parameter parity with vanilla prompt tuning, and inference speed will also be measured to assess efficiency.
48034b05b18621274e5c2e46cfa31dcdab44a45b.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces adaptive, token-specific embedding offsets via a shallow, token-shared neural network, overcoming the limitations of position-based offsets in previous methods. This approach enables unique and input-dependent token embeddings, enhancing expressiveness without increasing parameter count or inference time. The method is orthogonal to and can be integrated with other parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategies. Theoretical analysis demonstrates greater expressive power compared to previous prompt tuning methods, and empirical results show consistent outperformance of state-of-the-art parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques, including surpassing full fine-tuning in certain scenarios.

480e3db5b287d95c066b45c2c93f5015ec705a69.title: Log Neural Controlled Differential Equations: The Lie Brackets Make a Difference
480e3db5b287d95c066b45c2c93f5015ec705a69.research_question: How can the expressivity and efficiency of neural controlled differential equations (NCDEs) for multivariate time series modeling be improved, particularly in handling high-dimensional and irregularly sampled data, and how does leveraging mathematical tools from rough path theory impact their performance compared to state-of-the-art sequence models?
480e3db5b287d95c066b45c2c93f5015ec705a69.hypothesis: Incorporating the Log-ODE method, specifically by constructing vector fields using iterated Lie brackets of the NCDE's neural network, will significantly improve the performance and efficiency of NCDEs on multivariate time series tasks, outperforming both standard NCDEs, neural rough differential equations (NRDEs), and leading sequence models such as S5, LRU, and MAMBA.
480e3db5b287d95c066b45c2c93f5015ec705a69.proposed_method: A novel framework, termed Log Neural Controlled Differential Equations (Log-NCDEs), will be developed by integrating the Log-ODE method from rough path theory into the NCDE paradigm. The approach constructs the vector field of the controlled differential equation using the iterated Lie brackets of the neural network parameterizing the NCDE, rather than treating the vector field as a generic neural network as in NRDEs. For each interval in the time series, the truncated log-signature of the control path is computed, and the vector field is evaluated by recursively applying the Lie bracket structure, ensuring the model remains within a lower-dimensional, more expressive output space. The method enforces Lip(γ) regularity on the neural network, with γ corresponding to the truncation depth, and includes explicit regularization in the loss function to control the Lip(γ) norm during training. Efficient computation of the required iterated Lie brackets is achieved using automatic differentiation and batching techniques.
480e3db5b287d95c066b45c2c93f5015ec705a69.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of multivariate time series datasets, including a synthetic toy dataset designed to test sensitivity to higher-order path features, six large-scale benchmarks from the UEA Multivariate Time Series Classification Archive, and the PPG-DaLiA physiological signal regression dataset. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art models such as S5, LRU, S6, MAMBA, standard NCDEs, and NRDEs, all with matched architectures and hyperparameter tuning via grid search. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy for the UEA datasets and mean squared error for PPG-DaLiA, with additional reporting of GPU memory usage and runtime to assess computational efficiency. Each model will be evaluated over multiple random data splits to ensure statistical robustness, and ablation studies will investigate the impact of signature truncation depth and regularization.
480e3db5b287d95c066b45c2c93f5015ec705a69.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first application of the Log-ODE method with explicit Lie bracket computation to neural controlled differential equations, resulting in a drastic reduction in model output dimension without loss of expressivity. A new theoretical bound on the Lip(γ) norm for fully connected neural networks is established, enabling practical training of higher-regularity vector fields. The approach provides an efficient algorithm for calculating iterated Lie brackets within standard machine learning frameworks. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on challenging multivariate time series tasks, particularly for long and high-dimensional sequences, and to highlight the importance of respecting the underlying algebraic structure in rough path-based neural models.

480e756e42f065731325fc9ff38fd199889e65f1.title: PeRFlow: Piecewise Rectified Flow as Universal Plug-and-Play Accelerator
480e756e42f065731325fc9ff38fd199889e65f1.research_question: How can the sampling process of pretrained diffusion models be accelerated to enable high-quality, few-step generation across various data modalities, while preserving compatibility with existing workflows and minimizing distribution shift?
480e756e42f065731325fc9ff38fd199889e65f1.hypothesis: Dividing the sampling trajectory of pretrained diffusion models into multiple time windows and applying a piecewise rectified flow operation within each interval, combined with dedicated parameterization strategies to inherit knowledge from the original models, will enable efficient few-step generation with minimal loss in quality and compatibility.
480e756e42f065731325fc9ff38fd199889e65f1.proposed_method: A novel flow-based acceleration framework, Piecewise Rectified Flow (PeRFlow), is proposed to speed up the sampling process of diffusion models. The method divides the probability flow ODE trajectory into several time windows and applies a reflow operation within each interval to straighten the trajectory, approximating a piecewise linear flow. For each window, the starting point is generated by adding random noise to real training data, and the endpoint is computed by solving the ODE over a short interval using an ODE solver (e.g., DDIM). The PeRFlow model is parameterized to inherit knowledge from the pretrained diffusion model, supporting both epsilon-prediction and velocity-prediction schemes. The student model is initialized from the pretrained model and trained using a loss that matches the linear interpolation between the start and end points of each window. Classifier-free guidance is incorporated in two modes (CFG-sync and CFG-fixed) to further enhance generation quality and adaptability.
480e756e42f065731325fc9ff38fd199889e65f1.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on large-scale text-to-image and text-to-video diffusion models, including Stable Diffusion v1.5, v2.1, SDXL, and AnimateDiff. Images are sampled from the LAION-Aesthetics-5+ dataset for training, with resolutions ranging from 512×512 to 1024×1024 for images and 16×384×384 for video clips. The time range is divided into four windows, and the DDIM solver is used with 8 steps per window to compute endpoints. Baselines for comparison include InstaFlow, LCM-LoRA, and SDXL-Lightning. Evaluation metrics include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) on LAION-5B-Aesthetics, MSCOCO2014, and generated image sets, as well as qualitative assessments of visual quality, text-image consistency, and sampling diversity. Experiments are run on 16 NVIDIA A100 GPUs, and classifier-free guidance is applied during both training and inference.
480e756e42f065731325fc9ff38fd199889e65f1.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a divide-and-conquer strategy for flow-based acceleration, enabling the use of real training data and on-the-fly ODE simulation to avoid the drawbacks of synthetic dataset generation. The piecewise reflow operation reduces numerical errors and significantly improves training efficiency and scalability. Dedicated parameterization strategies are developed to ensure fast convergence and effective knowledge transfer from pretrained diffusion models. PeRFlow achieves state-of-the-art few-step generation quality, minimal distribution shift, and superior plug-and-play compatibility with various workflows, including ControlNets and multiview 3D generation, without requiring adversarial training or major modifications to existing pipelines.

482c496bd7c328f219fe8a75298146edd35d3f46.title: Efficient and Modular Implicit Differentiation
482c496bd7c328f219fe8a75298146edd35d3f46.research_question: How can implicit differentiation of optimization problem solutions be made efficient, modular, and accessible for practitioners across a wide range of machine learning and scientific computing applications?
482c496bd7c328f219fe8a75298146edd35d3f46.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a generic, automatic framework for implicit differentiation, which leverages autodiff and the implicit function theorem, can be constructed to efficiently and modularly differentiate through optimization problems by specifying optimality conditions, without requiring solver reimplementation or manual mathematical derivations.
482c496bd7c328f219fe8a75298146edd35d3f46.proposed_method: A framework will be developed that enables automatic implicit differentiation of optimization problem solutions by allowing users to define the optimality conditions of their problem as a Python function F. This function, representing the root or fixed point conditions (such as stationarity, KKT, or proximal mappings), is then wrapped with a custom decorator (e.g., @custom_root or @custom_fixed_point) that augments the solver with custom Jacobian-vector and vector-Jacobian product rules, leveraging autodiff and the implicit function theorem. The approach supports a broad catalog of optimality conditions, including unconstrained and constrained problems, and is compatible with state-of-the-art solvers without modification. The framework is implemented in JAX, utilizing its autodiff capabilities for higher-order derivatives and efficient linear system solvers for Jacobian computations, and is designed to be modular such that the differentiation mechanism is decoupled from the solver and optimality condition specification.
482c496bd7c328f219fe8a75298146edd35d3f46.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of machine learning and scientific computing tasks, including bi-level optimization for hyperparameter tuning of multiclass SVMs, dataset distillation with logistic regression on MNIST, task-driven dictionary learning for gene expression-based cancer survival prediction, and sensitivity analysis in molecular dynamics simulations. Datasets such as the diabetes dataset, MNIST, and gene expression data will be used. The proposed method will be compared against unrolled differentiation and existing implicit differentiation approaches, using metrics such as runtime, Jacobian estimation error, and predictive performance (e.g., AUC for classification tasks). Experimental setups will include varying problem sizes and solvers (mirror descent, proximal gradient, block coordinate descent), and the framework's flexibility in mixing solvers and fixed points for differentiation will be demonstrated. Theoretical and empirical analysis of Jacobian precision will be performed, including validation of new error bounds.
482c496bd7c328f219fe8a75298146edd35d3f46.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a generic, efficient, and modular approach to implicit differentiation that abstracts away low-level technical details and manual derivations, making it broadly accessible to practitioners. It supports a wide catalog of optimality conditions and can be applied on top of any existing solver, decoupling the differentiation mechanism from solver implementation. The approach unifies and generalizes many existing implicit differentiation methods, enables easy formulation and solution of bi-level and sensitivity analysis problems, and provides new theoretical guarantees on Jacobian precision when solutions are computed approximately. The implementation in JAX offers seamless integration with modern autodiff workflows and demonstrates significant runtime improvements over unrolling-based approaches.

4836232147bdab74106a93a23242250fe562ed95.title: Controllable Context Sensitivity and the Knob Behind It
4836232147bdab74106a93a23242250fe562ed95.research_question: How can the sensitivity of large language models to context versus prior knowledge be made controllable, and what mechanisms within model architectures enable explicit control over this trade-off?
4836232147bdab74106a93a23242250fe562ed95.hypothesis: A low-dimensional, specifically 1-dimensional, subspace within the internal representations of large language models encodes the decision to rely on context or prior knowledge, and manipulating this subspace enables explicit, robust control over context sensitivity across various model families and tasks.
4836232147bdab74106a93a23242250fe562ed95.proposed_method: A novel methodology is developed to identify and control the mechanism underlying context sensitivity in large language models. First, a controllable context sensitivity (CCS) task is designed, where models are prompted with a context, a query, and an explicit intent (to use context or prior knowledge), and are evaluated on their ability to follow the specified intent. Models are adapted to this task via fine-tuning and in-context learning. Mechanistic interpretability techniques, including activation patching and a linear-time search algorithm, are employed to identify layers and multi-head attention components critical for intent encoding and answer selection. Subsequently, a rank-1 orthogonal projection is learned to isolate a 1-dimensional subspace in the residual stream of a key layer, which encodes the context-versus-prior decision. Model behavior is then steered by manipulating the value along this subspace, enabling explicit control over context sensitivity.
4836232147bdab74106a93a23242250fe562ed95.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on intent-augmented datasets derived from BASEFAKEPEDIA, MULTIHOPFAKEPEDIA, and a synthetic ARITHMETIC dataset, each containing query-context pairs with conflicting answers and explicit intent instructions. Models evaluated include Llama-3.1-8B (instruct and base), Gemma-2 9B, and Mistral-v0.3 7B, with both fine-tuning (QLoRA) and in-context learning approaches. Baselines include zero-shot and standard instruction-following settings. Evaluation metrics focus on pair-accuracy, requiring correct answers for both context-following and prior-following intents for each example. The effectiveness and transferability of the identified subspace are tested by steering model outputs without explicit intent instructions, and performance is compared to baseline and intent-instructed models. Correlations between subspace separation and model performance are also measured.
4836232147bdab74106a93a23242250fe562ed95.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a structured recipe for identifying and controlling a fundamental, low-dimensional subspace that governs context sensitivity in large language models. It claims the discovery of a single, transferable subspace that enables explicit, robust, and generalizable control over whether a model relies on context or prior knowledge, across different model families and adaptation methods. The approach leverages mechanistic interpretability and intervention techniques to provide both understanding and actionable control, moving toward more robust and controllable language model behavior.

48362b169a235ca650918c489c8cea4c597da645.title: Beyond Human Data: Scaling Self-Training for Problem-Solving with Language Models
48362b169a235ca650918c489c8cea4c597da645.research_question: Can self-training large language models using model-generated synthetic data with external scalar feedback improve problem-solving capabilities in domains such as mathematical reasoning and code generation, and how does this approach compare to traditional fine-tuning on human-generated data in terms of effectiveness, scalability, and transferability?
48362b169a235ca650918c489c8cea4c597da645.hypothesis: Self-training large language models with model-generated synthetic data filtered by external scalar feedback will yield superior problem-solving performance compared to fine-tuning on human-generated data, particularly as model size increases, and will also enhance transferability to related tasks.
48362b169a235ca650918c489c8cea4c597da645.proposed_method: A self-training framework based on expectation-maximization (EM) is developed for large language models, termed ReST_EM. The method alternates between two key steps: (1) Generate (E-step), where the model generates multiple output samples per input context, and these samples are filtered using a binary reward function that reflects external scalar feedback (e.g., correctness for math or code tasks); (2) Improve (M-step), where the model is fine-tuned using the filtered, reward-annotated dataset, optimizing a reward-weighted negative log-likelihood loss. This process is repeated for several iterations, always fine-tuning from the base pretrained model to mitigate overfitting and maintain transferability. The approach decouples data collection and policy optimization, enabling scalable application to large models. To ensure diversity and avoid overfitting on easy problems, a cap is placed on the number of correct solutions per problem included in the training set.
48362b169a235ca650918c489c8cea4c597da645.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using PaLM 2 models of varying scales (PaLM 2-S, PaLM 2-S*, PaLM 2-L) on two primary benchmarks: Hendrycks' MATH for mathematical problem-solving and APPS (Introductory) for code generation, both of which provide binary rewards for automated evaluation. For each ReST_EM iteration, 32 solutions per problem are generated for MATH and 64 for APPS, with a maximum of 10 correct solutions per problem included in the training set. Baselines include supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on human-generated data. Evaluation metrics include test accuracy (pass@1), pass@k, and majority voting performance. Transfer performance is assessed on GSM8K, Hungarian HS finals, HumanEval, and Big-Bench Hard benchmarks. Ablation studies investigate the impact of iteration count, dataset size, and solution diversity. Sampling uses top-K (K=40, temperature=0.7) for generation and nucleus sampling (p=0.95, temperature=1.0) for evaluation.
48362b169a235ca650918c489c8cea4c597da645.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a scalable expectation-maximization-based self-training framework (ReST_EM) for large language models that leverages model-generated synthetic data filtered by external feedback, without reliance on human-generated solutions. The approach demonstrates that self-training with feedback can outperform traditional fine-tuning on human data, particularly for larger models, and enables robust transfer to held-out tasks. Comprehensive ablation studies identify critical factors for optimal performance and show that multiple iterations of self-training yield greater improvements than simply increasing data volume. The method also establishes that synthetic, in-distribution data generated by large models can be more effective for fine-tuning and distillation than human-written data.

483f9a982cca661eaf755f32e2c148d49907cede.title: Quantifying the Variability Collapse of Neural Networks
483f9a982cca661eaf755f32e2c148d49907cede.research_question: How can the variability collapse phenomenon in neural networks be quantitatively measured, and how does this measurement relate to the transferability of pretrained neural network representations across different architectures and training regimes?
483f9a982cca661eaf755f32e2c148d49907cede.hypothesis: A variability collapse metric that is invariant to invertible linear transformations and numerically stable will serve as a more reliable indicator of both the degree of representation collapse and the transferability of neural network features to downstream tasks, compared to existing metrics.
483f9a982cca661eaf755f32e2c148d49907cede.proposed_method: A new metric, the Variability Collapse Index (VCI), will be developed to quantify the degree of variability collapse in the last-layer features of neural networks. The VCI is defined as VCI = 1 - Tr[Σ_T† Σ_B] / rank(Σ_B), where Σ_B is the between-class covariance matrix and Σ_T is the total covariance matrix of the features. The metric will be derived from a loss minimization perspective, specifically leveraging the minimum mean squared error (MSE) loss in linear probing, ensuring that the metric is invariant to invertible linear transformations and numerically stable due to the properties of Σ_T. The VCI will be compared to previous metrics such as Fuzziness, Squared Distance, and Cosine Similarity, and its theoretical properties, including invariance and stability, will be rigorously analyzed.
483f9a982cca661eaf755f32e2c148d49907cede.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using various neural network architectures, including ResNet18 and ResNet50 on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-1K, as well as ViT variants (DeiT-T, DeiT-S) on ImageNet-1K. Training regimes will vary in terms of loss functions (cross-entropy, MSE), learning rate schedules, and regularization. The VCI and baseline metrics will be computed throughout training, and their trends will be analyzed. Transferability will be evaluated via linear probing on ten downstream datasets, including Oxford-IIIT Pets, Oxford 102 Flowers, FGVC Aircraft, Stanford Cars, DTD, Food-101, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Caltech-101, and SUN397. The correlation between each metric and transfer performance will be assessed using the mean log odds gain across downstream tasks. Additional experiments will manipulate training hyperparameters, such as softmax temperature and regularization strength, to test the robustness of the metric's correlation with transferability.
483f9a982cca661eaf755f32e2c148d49907cede.novelty_claims: The proposed VCI metric is the first to combine invariance to invertible linear transformations with numerical stability, addressing key limitations of previous variability collapse metrics. VCI is theoretically motivated by its direct connection to linear probing loss and is empirically shown to be a consistent and reliable indicator of both representation collapse and transferability across architectures, datasets, and training regimes. Unlike existing metrics, VCI maintains a robust positive correlation with transfer performance even under varying training conditions, making it a superior tool for analyzing and improving neural network pretraining and transfer learning.

483ff93d750003aa006dec4ff61b15a951a02729.title: TimelyFL: Heterogeneity-aware Asynchronous Federated Learning with Adaptive Partial Training
483ff93d750003aa006dec4ff61b15a951a02729.research_question: How can asynchronous federated learning be made more robust to client heterogeneity and intermittent connectivity, while improving participation rates, convergence speed, and final model accuracy in large-scale cross-device environments?
483ff93d750003aa006dec4ff61b15a951a02729.hypothesis: An asynchronous federated learning framework that adaptively adjusts local training workloads and enables partial model training based on real-time client capabilities will increase participation rates, accelerate convergence, and improve final model accuracy compared to fixed-buffer asynchronous and synchronous baselines.
483ff93d750003aa006dec4ff61b15a951a02729.proposed_method: A heterogeneity-aware asynchronous federated learning framework, TimelyFL, is proposed, which adaptively schedules the local training workload for each client based on real-time resource availability. The method introduces a wall-clock aggregation interval, set as the kth fastest local update time among all clients, allowing a flexible number of clients to participate in each global aggregation round. Clients with limited resources are assigned to train only a subset of consecutive output-side layers (partial model training), reducing both computation and communication time. The server dynamically adjusts each client's local epoch number and partial training ratio to ensure timely participation, maximizing resource utilization and inclusiveness. All local updates received within the aggregation interval are aggregated into the global model, eliminating staleness and enabling more diverse client contributions.
483ff93d750003aa006dec4ff61b15a951a02729.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three benchmark datasets: CIFAR-10 for image classification (using ResNet-20), Google Speech Commands for speech recognition (using VGG11 and a lightweight CNN-GRU model), and Reddit for next-word prediction (using ALBERT). Data will be partitioned non-iid using a Dirichlet distribution to simulate realistic federated learning scenarios. The proposed method will be compared against FedBuff (state-of-the-art asynchronous FL) and synchronous FL, using both FedAvg and FedOpt as server aggregation functions. Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy/loss, time-to-accuracy (wall-clock time to reach target accuracy/loss), and participation rate (proportion of rounds a client contributes to global updates). Simulated clients will be assigned heterogeneous computation and communication profiles based on real-world device and network measurements. Hyperparameters such as learning rates, batch sizes, and aggregation goals will be tuned for each setup. Each experiment will be repeated multiple times with different seeds, and results will be reported as mean and standard deviation.
483ff93d750003aa006dec4ff61b15a951a02729.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a heterogeneity-aware asynchronous FL framework that adaptively schedules both local epoch number and partial model training ratio per client in real time, based on device capability and network conditions. Unlike prior asynchronous methods with fixed buffer sizes, this method uses a flexible aggregation interval to maximize inclusiveness and participation. The adaptive partial model training allows even slow or intermittently connected clients to contribute timely, reducing staleness and improving both convergence speed and final model accuracy. The method demonstrates significant improvements in participation rate, time-to-accuracy, and test accuracy over state-of-the-art baselines, and is validated across multiple datasets, models, and FL tasks.

4853e1562f181e701b869611b8d07bfb5b89a8c7.title: 3D Visual Illusion Depth Estimation
4853e1562f181e701b869611b8d07bfb5b89a8c7.research_question: How can depth estimation systems be made robust to 3D visual illusions that mislead both monocular and binocular (stereo) depth estimation methods, and what unified framework can effectively combine their complementary strengths to overcome such illusions?
4853e1562f181e701b869611b8d07bfb5b89a8c7.hypothesis: Combining monocular and binocular depth cues using a vision-language model-driven fusion framework, which leverages commonsense knowledge to assess cue reliability, will significantly improve depth estimation robustness and accuracy in the presence of 3D visual illusions compared to state-of-the-art monocular, stereo, and multi-view methods.
4853e1562f181e701b869611b8d07bfb5b89a8c7.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed that integrates monocular and binocular depth estimation using a dual-branch prediction network and a vision-language model (VLM)-based fusion network. The dual-branch network will simultaneously predict monocular depth (using a pre-trained model such as DepthAnything V2) and binocular disparity (using a GRU-based iterative stereo matching module) from rectified stereo image pairs. The VLM-based fusion network will extract visual features from the left RGB image and map them, together with language prompts about material properties, into a shared embedding space using a large vision-language model (e.g., QwenVL2-7B). These embeddings will be used to generate a confidence map via a flow-matching framework, indicating the reliability of monocular and binocular cues across the image. The monocular depth will be aligned to metric scale using affine transformation guided by high-confidence regions, and final depth maps will be produced by fusing the aligned monocular and binocular predictions according to the confidence map.
4853e1562f181e701b869611b8d07bfb5b89a8c7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a newly constructed 3D-Visual-Illusion dataset, which contains nearly 3,000 scenes and over 200,000 images spanning five types of visual illusions (inpainting, picture, replay, holography, and mirror) from both virtual and real-world sources. The dataset includes high-quality ground truth depth maps obtained through a combination of LiDAR, stereo cameras, and advanced scene reconstruction techniques. The proposed method will be pre-trained on the SceneFlow dataset and fine-tuned on the virtual 3D-Visual-Illusion data, then evaluated on real-world 3D-Visual-Illusion data and the Booster dataset for generalization. Baselines will include state-of-the-art monocular depth estimation models (DepthAnything V2, Marigold, Metric3D, DepthPro), multi-view foundation models (Dust3R, VGGT), and stereo matching methods (RAFT-Stereo, Selective-IGEV, MochaStereo, StereoAnything). Evaluation metrics will comprise endpoint error (EPE), bad-pixel rates at various thresholds, absolute relative error, RMSE, and accuracy under different delta thresholds. Additional ablation studies will assess the contribution of each module and fusion strategy.
4853e1562f181e701b869611b8d07bfb5b89a8c7.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first large-scale benchmark specifically designed to evaluate depth estimation under 3D visual illusions, covering a broad range of illusion types and scene categories. The method pioneers a VLM-driven monocular–stereo fusion framework that adaptively assesses cue reliability using commonsense reasoning from vision-language models, enabling robust depth estimation in visually ambiguous and illusory regions. The approach demonstrates state-of-the-art performance across both illusion-rich and standard datasets, and provides new insights into the complementary failure modes of monocular and stereo depth estimation under illusions.

485ac73320040449bdd224f2d89732e69c585c2d.title: The First Few Tokens Are All You Need: An Efficient and Effective Unsupervised Prefix Fine-Tuning Method for Reasoning Models
485ac73320040449bdd224f2d89732e69c585c2d.research_question: How can the reasoning capabilities of large language models be improved in a data- and compute-efficient manner, without relying on labeled data or extensive rejection sampling, especially for complex reasoning tasks?
485ac73320040449bdd224f2d89732e69c585c2d.hypothesis: Fine-tuning large language models using only the initial prefix tokens of model-generated reasoning traces, in an unsupervised manner, will match or exceed the reasoning performance of supervised fine-tuning methods while drastically reducing training and sampling costs.
485ac73320040449bdd224f2d89732e69c585c2d.proposed_method: A novel fine-tuning approach, Unsupervised Prefix Fine-Tuning (UPFT), is developed to leverage the observation that initial reasoning steps (prefixes) are highly consistent across diverse solution trajectories for a given problem. The method involves generating a single model response per question and extracting only the first few tokens (prefix) as the training signal, discarding the need for labeled data or rejection sampling. Fine-tuning is performed on these prefixes using a negative log-likelihood objective, with a multi-task structure tuning component that occasionally includes full reasoning traces to preserve the model’s ability to generate complete solutions and prevent catastrophic forgetting. Prefix length and the proportion of structure tuning are treated as hyperparameters, optimized for each model and dataset. A specialized prompt template is used to guide the model to focus on initial reasoning steps during prefix fine-tuning.
485ac73320040449bdd224f2d89732e69c585c2d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using three open-source LLM backbones: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct, and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B. Four training corpora are used: PRM-12K, OMI2-60K, LIMO, and the newly curated U-Hard dataset, which focuses on challenging problems. Evaluation will be performed on four reasoning benchmarks: GSM8K, MATH500, AIME2024, and GPQA Diamond. Baselines include conventional supervised fine-tuning (SFT), Rejection Sampling Fine-Tuning (RFT), and V-STaR. Both unsupervised and supervised sampling scenarios will be tested. Metrics include accuracy on each benchmark and efficiency measures such as average training sample length, total tokens used, and training time. Ablation studies will examine the impact of prefix length and structure tuning ratio.
485ac73320040449bdd224f2d89732e69c585c2d.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the concept of Prefix Self-Consistency and demonstrates that fine-tuning on minimal, unsupervised prefixes is sufficient to achieve competitive or superior reasoning performance compared to supervised methods. UPFT eliminates the need for labeled data and costly rejection sampling, reducing training time by over 75% and sampling cost by over 99%. The approach is shown to be universally applicable across datasets and LLM architectures, and is especially effective on challenging reasoning tasks. The method also provides a scalable, resource-efficient alternative to conventional fine-tuning, with strong empirical evidence of data efficiency and versatility.

487b7090af70989dde3a0e16bc5d014eb5dfd498.title: For SALE: State-Action Representation Learning for Deep Reinforcement Learning
487b7090af70989dde3a0e16bc5d014eb5dfd498.research_question: How can representation learning be effectively leveraged in reinforcement learning environments with low-level state inputs, such as physical control tasks, to improve sample efficiency and performance in both online and offline settings?
487b7090af70989dde3a0e16bc5d014eb5dfd498.hypothesis: Jointly learning state-action embeddings that model the environment's dynamics in latent space, when integrated with policy checkpoints and other stabilization techniques, will significantly improve the performance and stability of deep reinforcement learning algorithms on low-level state tasks.
487b7090af70989dde3a0e16bc5d014eb5dfd498.proposed_method: A novel framework, State-Action Learned Embeddings (SALE), is developed to learn joint embeddings of states and actions by modeling the environment's dynamics in a latent space. SALE utilizes two encoders: one to map the state to a state embedding, and another to combine the state embedding with the action to produce a state-action embedding. These embeddings are trained online using a mean squared error loss between the state-action embedding and the embedding of the next state, with a stop-gradient operation to stabilize training. To further ensure stability, the method applies a custom normalization (AvgL1Norm) to the embeddings and input vectors, freezes embeddings during value and policy updates, and introduces a value clipping mechanism to mitigate extrapolation error from high-dimensional inputs. The learned embeddings are concatenated with the original state and action vectors and used as input to the value and policy networks, which are otherwise trained independently of the embedding encoders. Additionally, policy checkpoints are incorporated to select the best-performing policy during training, improving stability and final performance.
487b7090af70989dde3a0e16bc5d014eb5dfd498.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the OpenAI Gym MuJoCo continuous control benchmark tasks, including environments such as HalfCheetah, Hopper, Walker2d, Ant, and Humanoid. The proposed TD7 algorithm, which integrates SALE, policy checkpoints, prioritized experience replay (LAP), and a behavior cloning term for offline RL, will be compared against strong baselines: TD3, SAC, TQC, and TD3+OFE for online RL, and CQL, TD3+BC, IQL, and X-QL for offline RL, using consistent evaluation protocols and hyperparameters. Evaluation metrics will include average episode reward at various time steps (e.g., 300k, 1M, 5M) and statistical significance will be assessed using confidence intervals and Welch’s t-tests. Ablation studies will be performed to isolate the contributions of SALE, checkpoints, and other components, and runtime comparisons will be made to assess computational overhead.
487b7090af70989dde3a0e16bc5d014eb5dfd498.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a general-purpose state-action representation learning method applicable to low-level state RL environments, which is a departure from the typical focus on high-dimensional, image-based tasks. The method systematically studies and optimizes the design space for state-action embeddings, introduces a normalization technique (AvgL1Norm) tailored for decoupled representation learning, and identifies and mitigates extrapolation error through value clipping. The integration of policy checkpoints for stability in deep RL is novel in this context. The resulting TD7 algorithm achieves substantial improvements in both sample efficiency and final performance over state-of-the-art methods in both online and offline RL, without requiring per-environment hyperparameter tuning or increased architectural complexity.

48967206cd2781e2a390754a5ca79230b8735d42.title: Balanced Multimodal Learning via On-the-fly Gradient Modulation
48967206cd2781e2a390754a5ca79230b8735d42.research_question: How can multimodal learning models be improved to ensure balanced and effective optimization of all input modalities, thereby maximizing the potential of each modality in various multimodal tasks?
48967206cd2781e2a390754a5ca79230b8735d42.hypothesis: Adaptive modulation of the optimization process for each modality, based on their individual contributions to the learning objective, will alleviate optimization imbalance and lead to improved multimodal and unimodal performance. Introducing dynamically adjusted Gaussian noise will further enhance generalization ability.
48967206cd2781e2a390754a5ca79230b8735d42.proposed_method: A novel On-the-fly Gradient Modulation with Generalization Enhancement (OGM-GE) strategy is proposed to address optimization imbalance in multimodal learning. The method dynamically monitors the contribution discrepancy between modalities during training by computing a discrepancy ratio for each modality. Based on this ratio, the gradient for the dominant modality is adaptively down-weighted, allowing the under-optimized modality to receive more optimization effort. To counteract potential generalization loss due to reduced gradient noise, the method injects dynamically scaled Gaussian noise into the gradients, restoring or enhancing the stochasticity necessary for good generalization. The approach is designed to be optimizer-agnostic and can be integrated into standard stochastic gradient descent or Adam optimization routines.
48967206cd2781e2a390754a5ca79230b8735d42.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several benchmark multimodal datasets, including CREMA-D (audio-visual emotion recognition), Kinetics-Sounds and VGGSound (audio-visual event classification), and AVE (audio-visual event localization). The method will be evaluated by integrating OGM-GE into both vanilla fusion strategies (concatenation, summation, FiLM) and state-of-the-art multimodal architectures (TSN, TSM, TBN, PSP, x-vector, i-vector, MWTSM). Performance will be compared against unimodal baselines, conventional fusion methods, and other gradient modulation approaches such as Modality-Dropout and Gradient-Blending. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy and mean average precision (mAP), with ablation studies examining the effects of noise intensity, optimizer choice, and the impact on unimodal and multimodal performance.
48967206cd2781e2a390754a5ca79230b8735d42.novelty_claims: The proposed OGM-GE strategy introduces a simple yet effective mechanism for dynamically balancing the optimization of each modality in multimodal learning, without requiring additional neural modules or pre-trained unimodal classifiers. The method is versatile, serving as a plug-in for a wide range of fusion strategies and multimodal architectures. It is the first to combine on-the-fly gradient modulation with dynamically adjusted Gaussian noise for generalization enhancement, leading to consistent improvements across diverse tasks and datasets. The approach provides new insights into the optimization dynamics of multimodal models and offers a practical solution to the persistent problem of under-optimized unimodal representations.

489ab1945feb21f17b3efbcf40726c8cbb52bb75.title: Q-Diffusion: Quantizing Diffusion Models
489ab1945feb21f17b3efbcf40726c8cbb52bb75.research_question: How can the computational and memory efficiency of diffusion models be improved through quantization, while maintaining high image generation quality across both unconditional and text-guided tasks?
489ab1945feb21f17b3efbcf40726c8cbb52bb75.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a post-training quantization (PTQ) method specifically designed for the multi-timestep nature and unique architecture of diffusion models can enable aggressive quantization (e.g., 4-bit weights) without significant degradation in image generation quality.
489ab1945feb21f17b3efbcf40726c8cbb52bb75.proposed_method: A novel post-training quantization framework, Q-Diffusion, will be developed to compress the noise estimation network in diffusion models. The method introduces timestep-aware calibration data sampling, which collects calibration data across all timesteps of the denoising process to accurately reflect the diverse activation distributions encountered during inference. Additionally, a shortcut-splitting quantization technique will be employed to address the bimodal activation and weight distributions in UNet shortcut layers by quantizing deep and shallow feature channels separately before concatenation. The quantization process will use adaptive rounding for weights and tailored step size adjustments for activations, with calibration objectives designed to minimize mean squared error between quantized and full-precision outputs. The entire pipeline will be training-free and data-free, leveraging only the pretrained diffusion model for calibration data synthesis.
489ab1945feb21f17b3efbcf40726c8cbb52bb75.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both pixel-space (e.g., DDPM, DDIM) and latent-space (e.g., Latent Diffusion, Stable Diffusion) diffusion models. Datasets such as CIFAR-10 (32x32), LSUN Bedrooms (256x256), and LSUN Churches (256x256) will be used for unconditional generation, while text-guided generation will be evaluated using Stable Diffusion with prompts sampled from the MS-COCO dataset. Baselines will include naive linear quantization and state-of-the-art data-free PTQ methods such as SQuant. Evaluation metrics will comprise Frechet Inception Distance (FID) and Inception Score (IS), with additional qualitative analysis of generated images. Ablation studies will assess the impact of calibration sampling strategies and shortcut-splitting on quantization performance, and experiments will cover a range of quantization precisions (e.g., 8-bit, 4-bit weights and activations).
489ab1945feb21f17b3efbcf40726c8cbb52bb75.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first PTQ method specifically tailored to the multi-timestep inference and architectural characteristics of diffusion models, enabling quantization down to 4-bit weights while maintaining generation quality. Key innovations include timestep-aware calibration data sampling that comprehensively covers the denoising process, and shortcut-splitting quantization for handling abnormal activation and weight distributions in UNet architectures. The method is training-free and data-free, and demonstrates state-of-the-art quantization performance on both unconditional and text-guided diffusion models, outperforming existing PTQ baselines by a large margin at low bitwidths.

48c83799530dc523ee01e6c1c40ad577d5c10a16.title: DiscoveryBench: Towards Data-Driven Discovery with Large Language Models
48c83799530dc523ee01e6c1c40ad577d5c10a16.research_question: How effective are current large language models at autonomously performing multi-step, data-driven scientific discovery tasks across diverse domains, given only datasets and natural language goals?
48c83799530dc523ee01e6c1c40ad577d5c10a16.hypothesis: Current large language models, when equipped with advanced reasoning and workflow orchestration frameworks, can autonomously search for and verify scientific hypotheses from raw datasets, but their performance is limited by workflow complexity, domain knowledge requirements, and the need for semantic reasoning beyond statistical analysis.
48c83799530dc523ee01e6c1c40ad577d5c10a16.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark, DISCOVERYBENCH, will be constructed to systematically evaluate the data-driven discovery capabilities of large language models (LLMs). The benchmark will consist of two main components: (1) DB-REAL, a collection of 264 real-world discovery tasks and workflows extracted from published scientific papers across six domains, and (2) DB-SYNTH, a set of 903 synthetic tasks generated to control for task complexity and domain diversity. Each task will be defined by a dataset, metadata, and a natural language discovery goal, requiring the model to derive a hypothesis with explicit context, variables, and relationships. The methodology will formalize hypotheses as semantic trees, enabling multi-step reasoning, and will require models to generate both hypotheses and detailed workflows. Evaluation will be performed using a structured, model-based approach that decomposes predicted and gold hypotheses into sub-hypotheses and scores alignment across context, variables, and relationships.
48c83799530dc523ee01e6c1c40ad577d5c10a16.experiment_details: Experiments will benchmark state-of-the-art LLM-based reasoning agents, including closed-source models (GPT-4o, GPT-4-preview) and open-source models (Llama-3-70B), using various reasoning frameworks such as CodeGen, ReAct, DataVoyager, and Reflexion(Oracle). Each agent will receive the task description, dataset(s), metadata, and goal, and will be required to output a natural language hypothesis and workflow. Evaluation will use the Hypothesis Match Score (HMS), which measures alignment between predicted and gold hypotheses across context, variables, and relationships, using GPT-4 as an evaluator. Baselines will include both data-driven and no-data (memorization) settings. Performance will be analyzed across domains, workflow complexity, and goal types, with additional experiments assessing the impact of domain knowledge and workflow length.
