Ablation studies will examine the effects of reward discretization, number of teacher responses, KL-divergence penalty, and the impact of distillation-based initialization.
4a443c612617e88149c85d04b86fc3e3ecf28cf5.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to unify reinforcement and adversarial imitation learning for VLM training, enabling small models to mimic and even surpass large teacher VLMs without architectural changes or increased inference latency. The use of a binary-output discriminator for stable similarity rewards, combined with an LLM-as-a-Judge for flexible, context-aware answer evaluation, allows the method to generalize across diverse VLM architectures and tasks. Leveraging multiple teacher VLMs introduces a novel mechanism for enhancing the diversity and quality of student learning signals. The approach is agnostic to image embedding and tokenization strategies, and does not require a 'think-answer' phase, preserving inference efficiency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RIL-trained models achieve or exceed state-of-the-art performance on a broad spectrum of vision-language benchmarks.

4a597a081721e436e20b4e85197072e22aaecfad.title: From $r$ to $Q^*$: Your Language Model is Secretly a Q-Function
4a597a081721e436e20b4e85197072e22aaecfad.research_question: Can direct preference optimization (DPO) be theoretically and practically formulated as a token-level reinforcement learning algorithm for large language models, thereby enabling per-token credit assignment, improved decoding strategies, and deeper understanding of implicit reward dynamics in language model alignment?
4a597a081721e436e20b4e85197072e22aaecfad.hypothesis: Direct preference optimization, when reformulated within the token-level Markov Decision Process (MDP), can serve as a general inverse Q-learning algorithm that satisfies the Bellman equation, enabling language models to learn per-token credit assignment and dense reward functions, and providing a theoretical foundation for observed empirical phenomena such as improved decoding performance and implicit reward dynamics.
4a597a081721e436e20b4e85197072e22aaecfad.proposed_method: The proposed approach will derive direct preference optimization (DPO) within the token-level MDP framework used for large language models, leveraging binary preference feedback. The method will establish a bijection between reward functions and optimal Q-functions in the token MDP, showing that language model logits can be interpreted as the optimal Q-function for some reward. The DPO loss will be reformulated in terms of per-token advantage functions, allowing the model to learn dense, per-token reward assignments from preference data. Furthermore, the approach will connect likelihood-based search (e.g., beam search) and classical search algorithms (such as Monte Carlo Tree Search) to optimization over the DPO policy, providing a unified view of decoding as reward maximization. Theoretical analysis will be complemented by empirical studies to validate the practical implications of this formulation.
4a597a081721e436e20b4e85197072e22aaecfad.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Pythia 2.8B language model and the Reddit TL;DR summarization dataset. The DPO-trained models will be evaluated for their ability to perform per-token credit assignment, as visualized through implicit reward heatmaps on generated summaries. Decoding strategies will be compared by evaluating win rates of model outputs using beam search with varying beam widths, with performance measured against preferred summaries as judged by GPT-4. Additional analysis will track the evolution of implicit rewards during training, both with and without supervised fine-tuning (SFT) initialization, to understand the dynamics of likelihoods and reward assignment. Baselines will include standard DPO policies and value-function-guided search methods, with evaluation metrics such as win rate, answer length, and implicit reward trends.
4a597a081721e436e20b4e85197072e22aaecfad.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel theoretical framework that casts DPO as a general inverse Q-learning algorithm in the token-level MDP, establishing a one-to-one correspondence between reward functions and Q-functions for language models. It demonstrates, for the first time, that DPO can learn per-token credit assignment from trajectory-level feedback, and that likelihood-based search methods are equivalent to reward maximization over the DPO policy. The approach also provides the first mathematical explanation for the observed decline in implicit rewards during DPO training and unifies several recent decoding and alignment strategies under a common theoretical perspective. These contributions lay the groundwork for extending DPO to more complex tasks, such as multi-turn dialogue, agentic LLMs, and end-to-end training of multi-modal generative systems.

4a5ba3075d61f6258059dc311f761eb85848b22d.title: A Diffusion Model Framework for Unsupervised Neural Combinatorial Optimization
4a5ba3075d61f6258059dc311f761eb85848b22d.research_question: How can highly expressive latent variable models, such as diffusion models, be leveraged for unsupervised neural combinatorial optimization to enable efficient, data-free approximation and sampling from intractable discrete distributions, particularly in combinatorial optimization problems?
4a5ba3075d61f6258059dc311f761eb85848b22d.hypothesis: Latent variable models like diffusion models, when trained using a tractable upper bound on the reverse Kullback-Leibler divergence, can outperform existing exact likelihood-based and autoregressive neural methods in unsupervised combinatorial optimization by enabling more expressive modeling and efficient sampling of discrete solution spaces.
4a5ba3075d61f6258059dc311f761eb85848b22d.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed for unsupervised neural combinatorial optimization that employs discrete diffusion models as highly expressive latent variable models. The method introduces a loss function based on a tractable upper bound of the reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence, specifically the joint variational upper bound, which avoids the need for exact sample likelihoods and enables training with approximate likelihood models. The forward diffusion process iteratively adds discrete noise (using either categorical or annealed noise distributions) to the target distribution, while the reverse process is parameterized by a time-conditioned neural network (e.g., a GNN-based diffusion model) that learns to denoise and generate solutions. The model is trained via stochastic optimization (e.g., RAdam), with expectations estimated by Monte Carlo sampling, and supports conditioning on problem instances. Additionally, an efficient variant of the Conditional Expectation (CE) sampling strategy is proposed, including a subgraph tokenization approach to accelerate inference.
4a5ba3075d61f6258059dc311f761eb85848b22d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several combinatorial optimization problems, including Maximum Independent Set (MIS), Maximum Clique (MaxCl), Minimum Dominating Set (MDS), Maximum Cut (MaxCut), and Minimum Vertex Cover (MVC). Benchmark datasets will include RB-model graphs and Barabasi-Albert (BA) graphs, with both small (200-300 nodes) and large (800-1200 nodes) instances. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines, including supervised, unsupervised, and heuristic approaches such as Gurobi, KaMIS, INTEL, DGL, EGN, EGN-Anneal, LTFT, and mean-field models. Evaluation metrics will include solution quality (e.g., set size, cut size, approximation ratio), inference time, and relative error. Ablation studies will investigate the impact of the number of diffusion steps, noise distributions, annealing schedules, and the use of Conditional Expectation and subgraph tokenization during inference. All experiments will be run with multiple random seeds and repeated samples per instance to ensure statistical robustness.
4a5ba3075d61f6258059dc311f761eb85848b22d.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to enable the application of discrete diffusion models for data-free approximation of target distributions in combinatorial optimization, overcoming the limitations of exact likelihood requirements in previous neural probabilistic optimization methods. The introduction of the joint variational upper bound as a tractable loss for training approximate likelihood models in the discrete setting is novel. The method demonstrates state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of combinatorial optimization benchmarks, and introduces an efficient, scalable variant of Conditional Expectation sampling via subgraph tokenization. The approach generalizes and outperforms prior mean-field and autoregressive neural combinatorial optimization methods, and provides new insights into the benefits of variational annealing and extended diffusion steps during inference.

4a63f31c6f8e331f59a09486b588711f0db7a019.title: QiMeng-SALV: Signal-Aware Learning for Verilog Code Generation
4a63f31c6f8e331f59a09486b588711f0db7a019.research_question: How can reinforcement learning for Verilog code generation be improved by leveraging fine-grained, functionally correct signal-level information, rather than relying solely on module-level correctness or structural similarity?
4a63f31c6f8e331f59a09486b588711f0db7a019.hypothesis: Incorporating signal-level functional correctness as reinforcement learning rewards, by extracting and verifying correct signal implementations from partially incorrect Verilog modules, will provide denser and more informative feedback, resulting in superior Verilog code generation performance compared to conventional module-level or structure-based reward schemes.
4a63f31c6f8e331f59a09486b588711f0db7a019.proposed_method: A novel reinforcement learning framework is developed for Verilog code generation that operates at the signal level. The approach begins with a supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of a large language model on a cleaned Verilog dataset, followed by reinforcement learning using a signal-aware Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) algorithm. During RL training, candidate module implementations are generated for each prompt, and signal-level correctness is verified by applying random input stimuli and comparing output signals with reference modules. Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) analysis is used to extract code segments corresponding to functionally correct signals, even from otherwise erroneous modules. The signal-aware DPO loss is computed only over these verified signal-related code segments, increasing the likelihood of correct signal implementations and filtering out noise from incorrect signals. This process enables the model to learn from a broader set of partially correct samples and shifts optimization granularity from the module level to the signal level.
4a63f31c6f8e331f59a09486b588711f0db7a019.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a cleaned subset (135k samples) of the CodeV Verilog dataset for training, with five candidate module generations per prompt for RL preference data construction. The model will be evaluated on standard Verilog code generation benchmarks, including VerilogEval 1.0, VerilogEval 2.0, RTLLM v1.1, and RTLLM v2.0, using pass@k metrics (pass@1, pass@5, pass@10) under various temperature settings. Baseline comparisons will include general-purpose LLMs (e.g., GPT-3.5, GPT-4o, DeepSeek-v3), general code models (e.g., CodeQwen, Qwen2.5CoderInstruct), and Verilog-specific models (e.g., CodeV, Origen, VeriSeek, VeriPrefer). Ablation studies will analyze the impact of signal-aware DPO, dataset composition (complete vs. partial correctness), and training stage contributions. Runtime analysis will be performed to assess the efficiency of simulation and AST parsing steps.
4a63f31c6f8e331f59a09486b588711f0db7a019.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to introduce fine-grained, signal-level reinforcement learning for Verilog code generation, enabling the use of functionally correct signal implementations from partially incorrect modules as RL rewards. This approach increases the density and informativeness of functional feedback, expands the effective training dataset, and demonstrates substantial improvements over both module-level RL and SFT-only baselines. The signal-aware DPO algorithm further enhances robustness by filtering out incorrect signal segments, leading to state-of-the-art performance on multiple Verilog code generation benchmarks with significantly fewer model parameters than competing solutions.

4a7530bbaee7563ee244f3ffed6b706bd96f08a8.title: Trained Transformers Learn Linear Models In-Context
4a7530bbaee7563ee244f3ffed6b706bd96f08a8.research_question: How do transformer architectures trained on in-context examples behave when exposed to new tasks, and what are the mechanisms and limitations underlying their ability to perform in-context learning, particularly for linear models and under various distribution shifts?
4a7530bbaee7563ee244f3ffed6b706bd96f08a8.hypothesis: Transformers with a single linear self-attention layer, when trained by gradient-based optimization on in-context examples of linear regression tasks, will converge to global minima that encode linear learning algorithms, achieving prediction errors competitive with the best linear predictors. However, such models will exhibit brittleness under covariate distribution shifts, while larger, nonlinear transformers may demonstrate improved robustness.
4a7530bbaee7563ee244f3ffed6b706bd96f08a8.proposed_method: A theoretical and empirical investigation is proposed into the learning dynamics of transformers with a single linear self-attention (LSA) layer trained by gradient flow on in-context examples of linear regression tasks. The methodology involves formalizing the in-context learning setup, where prompts consist of sequences of input-output pairs sampled from Gaussian distributions with possibly anisotropic covariance, and training the transformer to minimize the population loss via gradient flow from a carefully chosen random initialization. The convergence properties of the optimization process will be analyzed, and the resulting learned algorithm will be characterized in terms of its prediction error on new prompts, including those from nonlinear tasks and under distribution shifts. Additionally, the robustness of the trained model to various types of distribution shifts—including task, query, and covariate shifts—will be systematically studied. To address brittleness under covariate shift, a generalized in-context learning setting with varying covariate distributions across prompts will be considered, and the behavior of both linear and large, nonlinear transformer architectures will be empirically evaluated.
4a7530bbaee7563ee244f3ffed6b706bd96f08a8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic datasets generated from random instances of linear regression problems, where input features are sampled from multivariate Gaussian distributions with both isotropic and anisotropic covariances. The transformer models will be trained on sequences (prompts) of labeled examples and evaluated on their ability to predict outputs for new query inputs within the same or shifted distributions. Baselines will include ordinary least squares and single-step gradient descent predictors. Evaluation metrics will focus on mean squared prediction error, both in well-specified (linear) and misspecified (nonlinear) test scenarios. Additional experiments will assess robustness to distribution shifts by varying the covariate distribution between training and test prompts, and by comparing the performance of single-layer linear self-attention transformers to larger, nonlinear transformer architectures under these conditions.
4a7530bbaee7563ee244f3ffed6b706bd96f08a8.novelty_claims: The proposed research provides a rigorous theoretical characterization of the optimization landscape and convergence properties of transformers with linear self-attention layers trained by gradient flow on in-context learning tasks. It establishes that such models provably learn linear algorithms in-context and quantifies their prediction error relative to the best linear predictor. The work further identifies and analyzes the brittleness of these models under covariate distribution shifts and extends the analysis to a generalized setting with varying covariate distributions. Empirical findings are expected to demonstrate that larger, nonlinear transformers exhibit greater robustness to such shifts, highlighting a key difference in generalization capabilities between simple and complex transformer architectures.

4a8efea3247c3d9ab458d4e2ed47d97c0661b429.title: Align Your Prompts: Test-Time Prompting with Distribution Alignment for Zero-Shot Generalization
4a8efea3247c3d9ab458d4e2ed47d97c0661b429.research_question: How can zero-shot generalization of vision-language models be improved under distribution shift between source and test domains, particularly when only a single test sample is available at test time?
4a8efea3247c3d9ab458d4e2ed47d97c0661b429.hypothesis: Explicitly aligning the feature distribution statistics of test samples with those of the source data via prompt tuning at test time will improve the zero-shot generalization performance of vision-language models under domain shift.
4a8efea3247c3d9ab458d4e2ed47d97c0661b429.proposed_method: A novel test-time adaptation strategy is proposed that leverages multi-modal prompt learning to align the feature distribution of a single test sample with that of a proxy source dataset. The method computes mean and variance statistics of token embeddings from multiple augmented views of the test sample at each layer of the vision encoder. These statistics are aligned with pre-computed source statistics (e.g., from ImageNet) using a distribution alignment loss. This alignment loss is combined with an entropy minimization loss, which encourages prediction consistency across augmented views, to jointly update both text and vision prompts in the model. The approach does not require access to the original pre-training data and is designed to be lightweight, operating on a per-sample basis at test time.
4a8efea3247c3d9ab458d4e2ed47d97c0661b429.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on domain generalization and cross-dataset benchmarks for zero-shot image classification. The domain generalization setting will use four out-of-distribution variants of ImageNet (ImageNetV2, ImageNet-Sketch, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R) and the PUG dataset, while the cross-dataset evaluation will cover 10 datasets including Caltech101, OxfordPets, Stanford Cars, Flowers102, Food101, FGVC-Aircraft, SUN397, DTD, EuroSAT, and UCF101. Baselines will include prompt learning methods such as CoOp, CoCoOp, MaPLe, and test-time prompt tuning (TPT). Evaluation metrics will focus on Top-1 accuracy. The experimental setup involves generating 63 augmented views per test sample, using a batch of 64 images, and selecting the top 10% most confident predictions for entropy minimization. Prompts are updated using the AdamW optimizer, with hyperparameters tuned per dataset and a loss scale factor for the alignment loss. Ablation studies will assess the impact of alignment loss, entropy loss, loss balancing, higher-order statistics, and prompt regularization.
4a8efea3247c3d9ab458d4e2ed47d97c0661b429.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to explicitly align token distribution statistics between source and test domains for vision-language models at test time using prompt learning. It introduces a distribution alignment loss that harmonically combines with entropy minimization, enabling effective adaptation without access to pre-training data. The method operates on a single test sample and updates both text and vision prompts, providing consistent improvements over state-of-the-art prompt learning and test-time adaptation methods in zero-shot generalization tasks. The approach is lightweight, incurs negligible computational overhead, and demonstrates robust performance across diverse datasets and domain shifts.

4adccba3bc1172b501b658d009a222948a4103f3.title: Proximal Causal Learning with Kernels: Two-Stage Estimation and Moment Restriction
4adccba3bc1172b501b658d009a222948a4103f3.research_question: How can the average treatment effect (ATE) be estimated in the presence of unobserved confounding when proxy variables for the latent confounder(s) are observed, particularly in nonlinear settings, and what are the methodological and empirical advantages of kernel-based approaches in this context?
4adccba3bc1172b501b658d009a222948a4103f3.hypothesis: Kernel-based two-stage regression and maximum moment restriction approaches can consistently and accurately estimate the ATE in the presence of unobserved confounding when suitable proxy variables are available, outperforming existing linear and non-proxy-based methods, especially in nonlinear settings.
4adccba3bc1172b501b658d009a222948a4103f3.proposed_method: The proposal introduces two kernel-based methodologies for causal effect estimation in the proximal causal learning setting with observed proxies for unobserved confounders. The first method, Kernel Proxy Variable (KPV), employs a two-stage regression approach: (1) learning the conditional mean embedding of the proxy variable given treatment, observed covariates, and a treatment-inducing proxy using kernel ridge regression, and (2) estimating the structural function mapping treatment, covariates, and the outcome-inducing proxy to the outcome, again via kernel ridge regression. The second method, Proxy Maximum Moment Restriction (PMMR), formulates the estimation as a conditional moment restriction problem and minimizes a maximum moment restriction objective in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), yielding a single-stage closed-form solution for the structural function. Both methods leverage characteristic, bounded kernels to ensure identifiability and consistency, and are designed to handle nonlinear relationships and high-dimensional proxy spaces. Theoretical consistency guarantees are derived for both approaches under regularity and completeness assumptions.
4adccba3bc1172b501b658d009a222948a4103f3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic data will be generated to simulate nonlinear treatment and outcome functions, with explicit construction of latent confounders and their proxies, ensuring that the proxies are informative but not sufficient for backdoor adjustment. Real-world case studies will include the analysis of the effect of legalized abortion on crime rates and the impact of grade retention on cognitive outcomes, using established datasets (e.g., ECLS-K panel study). Baselines for comparison will include kernel ridge regression (with and without proxy adjustment), linear two-stage methods, and finite-feature two-stage estimators. Evaluation metrics will focus on the mean absolute error (MAE) of the estimated ATE compared to ground truth (either known in synthetic data or simulated from fitted generative models in real-world cases). Hyperparameter tuning will be performed via cross-validation or leave-one-out strategies for kernel bandwidths and regularization parameters. Results will be averaged over multiple random seeds and training set sizes to assess robustness and variance.
4adccba3bc1172b501b658d009a222948a4103f3.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first kernel-based two-stage least squares and maximum moment restriction estimators for proximal causal learning with proxy variables, providing consistency guarantees in nonlinear and nonparametric settings. The methods generalize existing approaches by accommodating infinite-dimensional feature spaces and nonlinear relationships, and by offering a unified framework for solving a broader class of inverse problems characterized by Fredholm integral equations. Theoretical connections between the two-stage and moment restriction approaches are established, and empirical results demonstrate superior performance over existing linear and non-proxy-based methods, particularly in settings where proxies are available but not sufficient for standard adjustment.

4b0049e34c123e6bc4bb208ecb2ba081d06e3954.title: LuxDiT: Lighting Estimation with Video Diffusion Transformer
4b0049e34c123e6bc4bb208ecb2ba081d06e3954.research_question: How can high-dynamic-range (HDR) scene illumination be accurately estimated from casually captured images or videos, in a way that generalizes across diverse real-world conditions and supports downstream applications such as virtual object insertion?
4b0049e34c123e6bc4bb208ecb2ba081d06e3954.hypothesis: A diffusion transformer-based generative model, trained on large-scale synthetic data and adapted to real-world distributions using low-rank adaptation, can produce accurate, high-frequency, and semantically aligned HDR environment maps from single images or videos, outperforming existing lighting estimation methods.
4b0049e34c123e6bc4bb208ecb2ba081d06e3954.proposed_method: A conditional generative framework will be developed that fine-tunes a video diffusion transformer (DiT) to synthesize HDR environment maps from visual input. The approach will encode the HDR environment map using dual tone-mapped representations (Reinhard and log-intensity) to capture the wide dynamic range, and process these through a pretrained VAE to obtain latent representations. Visual input (image or video) will be encoded as tokens and conditioned into the transformer via attention-based mechanisms, with directional embeddings injected to improve angular continuity. The model will be trained in two stages: first, supervised training on a large synthetic dataset with randomized geometry, materials, and lighting to learn physically grounded cues; second, LoRA-based fine-tuning on real HDR panoramas and LDR panoramic videos to improve semantic alignment and generalization. The final HDR panorama will be reconstructed from the dual latent outputs using a lightweight MLP.
4b0049e34c123e6bc4bb208ecb2ba081d06e3954.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three benchmark datasets: Laval Indoor (289 HDR images), Laval Outdoor (116 sunny HDR panoramas), and PolyHaven (181 HDRIs not used in training), covering both indoor and outdoor scenes. Evaluation will use scale-invariant RMSE, angular error, normalized RMSE, and peak angular error for directional accuracy. Baselines will include StyleLight, DiffusionLight, NLFE, Hold-Geoffroy et al., Weber et al., and EMLight. The model will be trained on synthetic renderings (with randomized 3D scenes and HDR lighting), perspective crops from HDR panoramas, and LDR panoramic videos (WEB360 dataset). Both image and video inference will be evaluated, including temporal consistency and downstream virtual object insertion tasks, with quantitative and user study-based perceptual assessments.
4b0049e34c123e6bc4bb208ecb2ba081d06e3954.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a diffusion transformer-based generative architecture for HDR lighting estimation, leveraging dual tone-mapped HDR representations and attention-based conditioning for non-spatially aligned outputs. The method employs a two-stage training strategy combining large-scale synthetic data for physical priors and LoRA-based fine-tuning for semantic adaptation to real-world data. This results in state-of-the-art accuracy, improved high-frequency detail, robust generalization to unseen scenes, and enhanced temporal consistency for video input, outperforming existing methods in both quantitative and qualitative evaluations.

4b1b5e219fb41a7413599c3b2ca6a7fdf045d1a5.title: Generative Multimodal Models are In-Context Learners
4b1b5e219fb41a7413599c3b2ca6a7fdf045d1a5.research_question: Can scaling up generative multimodal models enhance their in-context learning abilities, enabling them to generalize to a wide range of unseen multimodal tasks and serve as a general-purpose interface for multimodal understanding and generation?
4b1b5e219fb41a7413599c3b2ca6a7fdf045d1a5.hypothesis: Scaling up generative multimodal models with unified autoregressive objectives and large-scale multimodal training data will significantly improve their in-context learning abilities, allowing them to generalize to diverse and unseen multimodal tasks with few-shot or instruction-based prompts.
4b1b5e219fb41a7413599c3b2ca6a7fdf045d1a5.proposed_method: A large-scale generative multimodal model with 37 billion parameters will be developed, trained using a unified autoregressive objective to predict the next multimodal element (either visual embeddings or textual tokens) in a sequence. The architecture will consist of a Visual Encoder (initialized from EVA-02-CLIP-E-plus), a Multimodal Transformer (initialized from LLaMA-33B), and a Visual Decoder (initialized from SDXL). Images will be tokenized into fixed-dimension embeddings, interleaved with text tokens, and modeled autoregressively. The Visual Decoder will be trained to reconstruct images or videos from embeddings, enabling both understanding and generation tasks. Instruction tuning will be applied to align the model for following specific multimodal instructions, and a controllable visual generation module will be developed to accept mixed text, location, and image inputs for grounded and subject-driven generation.
4b1b5e219fb41a7413599c3b2ca6a7fdf045d1a5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a wide range of multimodal benchmarks, including visual question answering (VQAv2, OKVQA, GQA, VizWiz, TextVQA), video question answering (MSVD, MSRVTT), and recent large multimodal model (LMM) benchmarks such as SEED-Bench, MM-Vet, TouchStone, and MMMU. Datasets for training will include LAION-2B, CapsFusion-120M, WebVid-10M, Multimodal-C4, YT-Storyboard-1B, GRIT-20M, CapsFusion-grounded-100M, Pile, and additional high-quality image-text and video-text data. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art models such as Flamingo, Kosmos, BLIP-2, IDEFICS, Shikra, Qwen-VL, LLaVA, CogVLM, and Emu. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy for question answering, CLIP-I and CLIP-T scores for image generation, and DINO for subject fidelity. Experiments will assess zero-shot, few-shot, and instruction-tuned performance, as well as controllable and subject-driven generation capabilities.
4b1b5e219fb41a7413599c3b2ca6a7fdf045d1a5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a significantly scaled-up generative multimodal model that demonstrates strong in-context learning abilities across both understanding and generation tasks. The unified autoregressive training on large-scale, interleaved multimodal data enables the model to generalize to unseen tasks with few-shot or instruction-based prompts. The model achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple multimodal benchmarks, surpassing prior models of larger or more complex architectures. Additional innovations include a robust controllable visual generation module capable of subject- and text-grounded image synthesis, and a streamlined architecture that simplifies previous designs while improving performance. The work establishes a new foundation for adaptable, general-purpose multimodal systems.

4b32b77c2503dadd11ebab026f0856e4ab3556f7.title: Fair Cooperation in Mixed-Motive Games via Conflict-Aware Gradient Adjustment
4b32b77c2503dadd11ebab026f0856e4ab3556f7.research_question: How can cooperation and fairness be simultaneously achieved in multi-agent reinforcement learning within mixed-motive environments, where agents must balance individual interests with collective goals?
4b32b77c2503dadd11ebab026f0856e4ab3556f7.hypothesis: An adaptive, conflict-aware gradient adjustment method that dynamically balances policy gradients from individual and collective objectives will promote cooperation while ensuring fairness in individual rewards, resulting in monotonic improvement and convergence of both objectives.
4b32b77c2503dadd11ebab026f0856e4ab3556f7.proposed_method: A fair and conflict-aware gradient adjustment method (FCGrad) is developed to address the trade-off between individual and collective objectives in mixed-motive multi-agent reinforcement learning. The method first computes policy gradients for both individual and collective objectives for each agent. If the gradients are aligned (i.e., their inner product is non-negative), a weighted sum of the gradients is used for the policy update, with the weighting factor β controlling the balance. If the gradients are in conflict (i.e., their inner product is negative), the gradient associated with the lower objective value is projected onto the normal plane of the other gradient, ensuring that the update direction improves the disadvantaged objective without hindering the other. This projection ensures monotonic non-decreasing improvement in both objectives and guarantees convergence to equalized individual returns across agents, thus achieving fairness. The approach is implemented in a decentralized training and execution setting, where each agent maintains separate value networks for individual and collective objectives, sharing only rewards.
4b32b77c2503dadd11ebab026f0856e4ab3556f7.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted in three environments adapted from the SocialJAX suite: Unfair Coin Game, Cleanup, and Harvest, each designed to present mixed-motive and fairness challenges. In Unfair Coin, coin appearance probabilities are skewed to induce reward asymmetry; in Cleanup and Harvest, agents are spawned in positions that create disparities in access to resources or tasks. The evaluation uses α-fairness metrics (Mean, GeoMean, Min) to jointly assess performance and fairness, with additional fairness metrics such as the Gini coefficient and Jain's index. FCGrad is compared against six baselines: collective reward optimization, individual reward optimization, inequity aversion reward restructuring, a weighted gradient combination, PCGrad, and Altruistic Gradient Adjustment (AgA). All methods use the same underlying architecture and are implemented on top of IPPO. Hyperparameters, including the weighting factor β, are tuned for each environment, and results are averaged over four random seeds.
4b32b77c2503dadd11ebab026f0856e4ab3556f7.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel conflict-aware gradient adjustment mechanism that explicitly resolves conflicts between individual and collective objectives at the gradient level, rather than relying on reward restructuring or stability-based approaches. Theoretical guarantees are provided for monotonic improvement and convergence of both objectives, ensuring fairness across agents. Empirical results demonstrate superior performance in both social welfare and fairness compared to existing baselines, as measured by α-fairness and additional fairness metrics. The approach is computationally efficient and applicable in decentralized settings.

4b4c77e60abb37894792a50649f4d6954dcdc7e6.title: Detecting, Explaining, and Mitigating Memorization in Diffusion Models
4b4c77e60abb37894792a50649f4d6954dcdc7e6.research_question: How can memorization in text-to-image diffusion models be efficiently detected, explained, and mitigated, particularly to prevent the replication of proprietary or sensitive training data in generated outputs?
4b4c77e60abb37894792a50649f4d6954dcdc7e6.hypothesis: The magnitude of text-conditional noise predictions in diffusion models serves as a reliable indicator of memorization, enabling efficient detection and mitigation of memorized prompts without significant loss in generation quality.
4b4c77e60abb37894792a50649f4d6954dcdc7e6.proposed_method: A novel detection framework will be developed that inspects the magnitude of text-conditional noise predictions during the denoising process of diffusion models. The detection metric will be computed as the average L2 norm of the difference between noise predictions conditioned on the prompt and on an empty string, across sampling steps. To explain memorization, a significance score for each token in the prompt will be calculated by measuring the gradient of the detection loss with respect to each token embedding, identifying 'trigger tokens' that contribute most to memorization. For mitigation, two strategies will be implemented: (1) inference-time mitigation by perturbing the prompt embedding to minimize the detection metric, and (2) training-time mitigation by filtering out samples with high detection metrics during training. These methods will be designed for computational efficiency and seamless integration with existing diffusion model workflows.
4b4c77e60abb37894792a50649f4d6954dcdc7e6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using Stable Diffusion v1 as the primary model, with 500 memorized prompts (identified via high SSCD similarity to training images) and 2,000 non-memorized prompts sourced from LAION, COCO, Lexica.art, and random strings. The DDIM sampler with 50 inference steps will be used for generation. Baseline comparisons will include density-based detection methods using both L2 and SSCD distances, as well as random token addition (RTA) for mitigation. Evaluation metrics will include the area under the ROC curve (AUC), TPR@1%FPR, SSCD similarity (for memorization), and CLIP score (for prompt-image alignment). Experiments will assess detection accuracy, computational efficiency, and the trade-off between memorization mitigation and generation quality, with ablation studies on the number of generations, inference steps, and hyperparameters for mitigation.
4b4c77e60abb37894792a50649f4d6954dcdc7e6.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a highly efficient, single-generation detection method for memorization in diffusion models that does not require access to the training dataset or multiple image generations. The framework provides an automated, interpretable mechanism to identify and modify trigger tokens responsible for memorization, enabling interactive prompt refinement. The mitigation strategies offer both inference-time and training-time solutions that effectively reduce memorization while preserving image quality, outperforming existing baselines in both accuracy and computational cost.

4b7d02ddfef336a2bc6d068557f39314315eed8b.title: Multimodal Data Curation via Object Detection and Filter Ensembles
4b7d02ddfef336a2bc6d068557f39314315eed8b.research_question: How can multimodal datasets, particularly large-scale web-crawled image-text datasets, be effectively curated to improve downstream model performance using advanced filtering and ensembling techniques?
4b7d02ddfef336a2bc6d068557f39314315eed8b.hypothesis: Integrating zero-shot object detection-based filters with weak supervision ensembling methods will yield more refined and higher-quality multimodal datasets, resulting in improved downstream task performance compared to existing baseline filtering approaches.
4b7d02ddfef336a2bc6d068557f39314315eed8b.proposed_method: A two-stage data curation framework will be developed for multimodal datasets. In the first stage, multiple filtering rules will be designed by leveraging both existing baseline filters (such as CLIP score thresholds) and novel object detection-based filters. Object detection filters will be constructed using a zero-shot object detection model (GroundingDINO) to extract granular information, such as the presence, number, and aspect ratio of objects mentioned in image captions. Specific heuristics will be applied, including thresholds on predicted logit scores, object counts, and object aspect ratios, to eliminate low-quality or misaligned image-text pairs. In the second stage, the outputs of these diverse filters will be aggregated using a weak supervision ensembling approach based on the Ising model, which learns filter accuracies and correlations to produce optimal inclusion labels for the curated dataset. The Snorkel framework will be used to implement the label model, allowing for flexible adjustment of class balance and robust aggregation of filter decisions.
4b7d02ddfef336a2bc6d068557f39314315eed8b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the DataComp competition's small and medium scale filtering tracks, utilizing datasets of approximately 12.8 million and 115 million image-text pairs, respectively. The curation pipeline will be evaluated by comparing the performance of curated datasets on downstream tasks, primarily using ImageNet accuracy and average performance metrics. Baseline filters from DataComp, such as various CLIP score thresholds and human heuristic rules, will be compared against the proposed object detection filters and their ensembles. The object detection model (GroundingDINO-T with Swin-T and BERT backbones) will process images resized to 400x400 pixels for computational efficiency. The Snorkel label model will be trained for 1000 epochs with learning rates and class balance parameters tuned for each dataset scale. All experiments will be run on NVIDIA A6000 GPUs, and the impact of individual and combined filters will be systematically analyzed.
4b7d02ddfef336a2bc6d068557f39314315eed8b.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the use of zero-shot object detection models to design granular, interpretable filters for multimodal data curation, enabling the identification and removal of misaligned or low-quality image-text pairs at scale. The integration of weak supervision-based ensembling, specifically using the Ising model, allows for principled aggregation of diverse filtering signals, accounting for filter accuracy and correlation. This approach demonstrates significant improvements over existing baselines, achieving up to 4% higher downstream performance in benchmark evaluations. The method is adaptable, cost-effective, and requires minimal manual intervention, making it suitable for large-scale, open-domain dataset curation.

4b89f78987e5d0dba67a4f533945a838a5428ed9.title: Constrained Variational Policy Optimization for Safe Reinforcement Learning
4b89f78987e5d0dba67a4f533945a838a5428ed9.research_question: How can reinforcement learning agents be trained to maximize task performance while ensuring satisfaction of safety constraints, particularly in settings where only constraint violation signals are available and no prior domain knowledge or expert interventions exist?
4b89f78987e5d0dba67a4f533945a838a5428ed9.hypothesis: A variational inference-based framework that decomposes safe reinforcement learning into a convex optimization phase and a supervised learning phase will yield more stable training, provable optimality guarantees, improved constraint satisfaction, and higher sample efficiency compared to existing primal-dual and Lagrangian-based approaches.
4b89f78987e5d0dba67a4f533945a838a5428ed9.proposed_method: The proposed methodology formulates safe reinforcement learning as a probabilistic inference problem, introducing an Expectation-Maximization (EM) style algorithm called Constrained Variational Policy Optimization (CVPO). In the E-step, a non-parametric variational distribution over actions is computed analytically in closed form by solving a convex optimization problem, ensuring that the distribution satisfies both safety constraints and a trust-region constraint relative to the previous policy. The dual variables for the constraints and trust region are optimized efficiently, with strong duality and uniqueness guarantees under mild conditions. In the M-step, the policy parameters are updated via supervised learning to match the optimal variational distribution, using a KL-divergence regularizer to maintain robustness and prevent overfitting. This two-phase approach enables stable, off-policy policy improvement with theoretical guarantees on constraint satisfaction and monotonic reward improvement.
4b89f78987e5d0dba67a4f533945a838a5428ed9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of continuous control robotic tasks designed to test constraint satisfaction and sample efficiency, including environments with static and dynamic obstacles as well as tasks requiring goal-reaching under safety constraints. The proposed method will be compared against both off-policy (e.g., SAC-Lag, DDPG-Lag, TD3-Lag) and on-policy (e.g., CPO, TRPO-Lag, PPO-Lag) safe RL baselines, as well as unconstrained RL baselines. Evaluation metrics will include episodic task reward, number of constraint violations (cost), convergence cost statistics, and cumulative constraint violations required to achieve a given reward. All methods will use the same network architectures and hyperparameters for fair comparison, and results will be averaged over multiple random seeds to assess stability and variance.
4b89f78987e5d0dba67a4f533945a838a5428ed9.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to formulate safe reinforcement learning as a probabilistic inference problem, enabling the use of variational inference tools to address safety constraints. The method provides a closed-form, provably optimal solution for the constrained variational distribution in the E-step, supported by strict convexity and duality guarantees. The EM-style decomposition allows for stable, sample-efficient off-policy training with monotonic reward improvement and worst-case constraint violation bounds. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate significantly improved constraint satisfaction and sample efficiency—up to 1000 times better than on-policy baselines—while maintaining high task performance.

4ba57555bef02f988f2ed3bab2f102733dc55221.title: Math-Shepherd: Verify and Reinforce LLMs Step-by-step without Human Annotations
4ba57555bef02f988f2ed3bab2f102733dc55221.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be automatically supervised and reinforced for step-by-step mathematical reasoning tasks without relying on human-annotated process-level data, and how does such supervision impact verification and reinforcement learning performance across various LLMs and mathematical benchmarks?
4ba57555bef02f988f2ed3bab2f102733dc55221.hypothesis: Automatically constructed process-level supervision, based on the potential of intermediate reasoning steps to deduce correct final answers, can effectively replace human annotation for training process reward models (PRMs), leading to improved verification and reinforcement learning outcomes for LLMs on mathematical reasoning tasks.
4ba57555bef02f988f2ed3bab2f102733dc55221.proposed_method: A novel automatic process annotation framework will be developed to generate process-level supervision for mathematical reasoning tasks without human annotation. The framework defines the quality of each intermediate reasoning step by its potential to reach the correct final answer, operationalized by using a 'completer' LLM to generate multiple continuations from each step and assessing the proportion or existence of correct completions. Two estimation strategies—hard (binary) and soft (frequency-based)—will be explored for labeling step quality. The resulting step-annotated data will be used to train a process reward model (PRM) using cross-entropy loss. The PRM will then be integrated into two scenarios: (1) as a verifier to rerank multiple candidate solutions from LLMs, and (2) as a step-level reward signal in reinforcement learning via step-by-step Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), providing feedback at each reasoning step.
4ba57555bef02f988f2ed3bab2f102733dc55221.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the GSM8K and MATH datasets, two widely used mathematical reasoning benchmarks. For verification, 256 candidate solutions per problem will be generated using various LLMs (LLaMA2-7B/13B/70B, LLemma-7B/34B, Mistral-7B, DeepSeek-67B), and the PRM will be used to rerank and select the best solution. Baselines will include self-consistency (majority voting) and outcome reward models (ORM), with accuracy of best-of-N selection as the primary metric. For reinforcement learning, LLMs will be trained with step-by-step PPO using the PRM, and their greedy decoding accuracy will be compared to models trained with ORM-based PPO and rejective sampling fine-tuning (RFT). Additional analyses will examine the impact of model size, data quantity, and out-of-distribution generalization (e.g., Hungarian national final exam dataset). Hyperparameters such as learning rates, number of epochs, and number of completions per step will be systematically varied.
4ba57555bef02f988f2ed3bab2f102733dc55221.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first fully automatic process-level annotation framework for mathematical reasoning tasks, eliminating the need for costly human annotation in training process reward models. The method leverages the potential of intermediate steps, inspired by Monte Carlo Tree Search, to construct high-quality, scalable supervision data. The resulting process reward model enables both superior verification (reranking) and reinforcement learning (step-level PPO) for LLMs, achieving state-of-the-art results on open-source models across multiple benchmarks. The approach demonstrates improved data efficiency, scalability, and generalization compared to prior human-annotated or rule-based methods.

4ba9784d73dfe8d2eb3f1126138d3815f8341121.title: Characteristic Circuits
4ba9784d73dfe8d2eb3f1126138d3815f8341121.research_question: How can probabilistic models be developed to efficiently and reliably reason under uncertainty and capture complex relationships in heterogeneous data domains, especially when closed-form density functions are unavailable?
4ba9784d73dfe8d2eb3f1126138d3815f8341121.hypothesis: A unified probabilistic modeling framework based on characteristic functions, rather than traditional density functions, will enable efficient learning and inference over heterogeneous data domains, including cases where closed-form densities do not exist, and will outperform existing state-of-the-art density estimators.
4ba9784d73dfe8d2eb3f1126138d3815f8341121.proposed_method: A new family of tractable probabilistic models, termed characteristic circuits (CCs), will be developed by representing distributions in the spectral domain via characteristic functions. The model will be structured as a rooted directed acyclic graph, with sum, product, and leaf nodes, where leaf nodes encode univariate characteristic functions (empirical, parametric, or α-stable). Sum nodes will represent mixtures, and product nodes will encode independence, following the properties of characteristic functions. Structure learning will be performed recursively using clustering for sum nodes and independence tests for product nodes, while parameter learning will minimize the squared characteristic function distance (CFD) between the circuit and the empirical characteristic function (ECF) from data. Efficient computation of densities, marginals, and moments will be enabled through recursive analytic or numerical integration at the leaves, leveraging the one-to-one correspondence between characteristic functions and probability measures.
4ba9784d73dfe8d2eb3f1126138d3815f8341121.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world heterogeneous datasets. Synthetic datasets will include mixtures of multivariate distributions and Bayesian networks with both discrete and continuous variables. Real-world evaluation will use tabular datasets from the UCI repository containing mixed data types. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art probabilistic circuit models such as Mixed Sum-Product Networks (MSPN), Automatic Bayesian Density Analysis (ABDA), and Bayesian SPNs (BSPN). Evaluation metrics will include test log-likelihood and squared characteristic function distance (CFD) to ground-truth distributions. Both random and learned circuit structures will be tested, and various types of leaf node distributions (empirical, normal, categorical, α-stable) will be evaluated for their suitability on heterogeneous data.
4ba9784d73dfe8d2eb3f1126138d3815f8341121.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified circuit-based probabilistic modeling framework in the spectral domain that can handle both discrete and continuous random variables without reliance on closed-form densities. Characteristic circuits enable efficient and exact computation of densities, marginals, and moments even for distributions lacking closed-form expressions. The method supports structure and parameter learning directly in the characteristic function space, and demonstrates superior or competitive performance to state-of-the-art density estimators on heterogeneous data, particularly when using α-stable distributions for heavy-tailed or mixed-type data.

4bc821395f101c54aa8fc6508a4a2ed3b3937fae.title: Scaling Collapse Reveals Universal Dynamics in Compute-Optimally Trained Neural Networks
4bc821395f101c54aa8fc6508a4a2ed3b3937fae.research_question: What are the universal scaling laws and dynamics that govern the training of neural networks when model size and training time are increased together under compute-optimal conditions, and how can these be leveraged to diagnose and improve scaling and hyperparameter transfer across architectures, datasets, and learning rate schedules?
4bc821395f101c54aa8fc6508a4a2ed3b3937fae.hypothesis: Compute-optimally trained neural networks exhibit a universal scaling behavior in their loss curves, such that after appropriate normalization, loss trajectories from different model sizes and architectures collapse onto a single universal curve. Furthermore, learning rate decay amplifies this effect, resulting in 'supercollapse' where the variation across normalized curves falls below the noise floor, and deviations from this collapse can serve as sensitive diagnostics for suboptimal scaling or hyperparameter choices.
4bc821395f101c54aa8fc6508a4a2ed3b3937fae.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical and theoretical investigation will be conducted into the training dynamics of neural networks under compute-optimal scaling. The approach involves training families of models (transformers and MLPs) of varying sizes on diverse datasets, with hyperparameters (such as data, initialization, and learning rate) scaled according to established scaling ladders. Loss curves will be normalized by both compute and final loss to test for universal collapse. Theoretical analysis will be developed, including power-law scaling models and stochastic differential equation (SDE) models of SGD noise dynamics, to explain and predict the observed collapse and supercollapse phenomena. The methodology will also include the development of quantitative metrics for collapse quality and the use of these metrics to diagnose scaling and hyperparameter configurations.
4bc821395f101c54aa8fc6508a4a2ed3b3937fae.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed on next-token prediction tasks using transformers (e.g., on CIFAR-5M and Lichess datasets) and on synthetic regression tasks using MLPs with power-law Fourier features. Model sizes will range from approximately 10M to 80M parameters for transformers (widths 768 to 2048) and 384 to 2048 for MLPs, with hyperparameters transferred using µP scaling. Multiple learning rate schedules, including constant and various decay schedules, will be tested. Loss curves will be averaged over multiple random seeds (typically 5) to estimate expected behavior and noise floors. Baselines will include models with suboptimal hyperparameter scaling (e.g., constant learning rates or incorrect data exponents) to test the sensitivity of the collapse phenomenon. Evaluation metrics will include the degree of collapse (collapsedeviation ∆), comparison to the per-model noise floor (σ), and fit to theoretical predictions. Additional analyses will assess the universality of gradient noise scaling and the predictive power of the proposed SDE-based loss curve models.
4bc821395f101c54aa8fc6508a4a2ed3b3937fae.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the concept of scaling collapse and supercollapse in compute-optimally trained neural networks, demonstrating that normalized loss curves from models of different sizes, architectures, and datasets collapse onto a single universal curve under proper scaling. It provides a new, practical diagnostic tool for identifying optimal scaling and hyperparameter configurations, surpassing the sensitivity of traditional scaling law fits. Theoretical contributions include a quantitative explanation of collapse and supercollapse via power-law scaling and SGD noise dynamics, and a simple, predictive model for loss curve evolution across learning rate schedules. The work establishes a new empirical and theoretical foundation for understanding and diagnosing scaling in large-scale neural network training.

4be7d1524edb0137599a5cc95f72844b85a52fe1.title: LLM.int8(): 8-bit Matrix Multiplication for Transformers at Scale
4be7d1524edb0137599a5cc95f72844b85a52fe1.research_question: How can the memory requirements for inference in large-scale transformer-based language models be significantly reduced using low-bit quantization, while maintaining full precision predictive performance across models with up to hundreds of billions of parameters?
4be7d1524edb0137599a5cc95f72844b85a52fe1.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a carefully designed quantization procedure, which combines vector-wise quantization with a mixed-precision decomposition to isolate and handle systematic large-magnitude outlier features, can enable 8-bit matrix multiplication for transformer models at scale without incurring any degradation in inference performance.
4be7d1524edb0137599a5cc95f72844b85a52fe1.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a two-part quantization framework for transformer models, termed LLM.int8(). First, vector-wise quantization is applied, assigning separate normalization constants to each inner product in the matrix multiplication, thereby improving quantization precision over standard tensor- or row-wise approaches. Second, to address the emergence of systematic large-magnitude outlier features that arise in specific feature dimensions at scale, a mixed-precision decomposition is employed: outlier feature dimensions (identified by a magnitude threshold, e.g., ≥6.0) are isolated and computed using 16-bit precision, while the remaining 99.9% of values are processed using 8-bit integer matrix multiplication. The outputs from both branches are accumulated in 16-bit floating point. This approach enables immediate conversion and inference from existing 16/32-bit checkpoints, with no need for further fine-tuning.
4be7d1524edb0137599a5cc95f72844b85a52fe1.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate the robustness and performance of the proposed quantization method across a range of publicly available pretrained transformer language models, scaling up to 175B parameters. Language modeling perplexity on the C4 validation set will serve as the primary metric for quantization degradation, while zero-shot accuracy on the EleutherAI language model evaluation harness will assess downstream task performance. Baselines will include standard 8-bit quantization methods (absmax, row-wise, vector-wise, zeropoint), as well as mixed-precision decompositions without the full LLM.int8() procedure. Models will be evaluated on NVIDIA A40 GPUs, and the impact on memory footprint, runtime, and accessibility on various hardware setups will be measured. Additional ablation studies will analyze the effect of outlier feature removal and the scaling behavior of quantization errors.
4be7d1524edb0137599a5cc95f72844b85a52fe1.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to enable immediate, degradation-free 8-bit quantization and inference for transformer models with up to 175B parameters, making such large models accessible on commodity hardware. The combination of vector-wise quantization with a novel mixed-precision decomposition for systematic outlier features is a key innovation, addressing failure modes of previous quantization techniques at scale. The approach provides both theoretical and empirical insights into the role of emergent outlier features in large transformers and demonstrates that memory usage can be halved without sacrificing predictive performance. The method is general, requires no retraining or fine-tuning, and is integrated with widely used software frameworks for broad accessibility.

4bebfab79771392aebefeab29b55e4d76c6a49a0.title: Learning from many trajectories
4bebfab79771392aebefeab29b55e4d76c6a49a0.research_question: What are the fundamental statistical limits and efficiency trade-offs for supervised learning when training data consists of many independent trajectories (sequences) of non-independent covariates, as compared to learning from independent examples or a single long trajectory, particularly in the context of linear regression and linear dynamical systems?
4bebfab79771392aebefeab29b55e4d76c6a49a0.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, under appropriate non-degeneracy conditions on the trajectories, the statistical efficiency of learning from many independent trajectories will approach that of learning from fully independent examples as the number of trajectories increases, even when each trajectory exhibits strong intra-dependence and is not ergodic or strictly stable.
4bebfab79771392aebefeab29b55e4d76c6a49a0.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical framework will be developed to analyze supervised learning from multiple independent trajectories, where each trajectory consists of a sequence of possibly correlated covariates generated by a stochastic process. The analysis will focus on the ordinary least-squares (OLS) estimator for linear regression, with covariates and responses modeled as generated from a ground truth linear model with sub-Gaussian noise. The study will introduce and leverage a 'trajectory small-ball' condition to characterize when efficient learning is possible, generalizing standard non-degeneracy assumptions from the iid setting. Special attention will be given to the case where covariates are generated by linear dynamical systems (LDS), including cases where the system is marginally unstable and non-ergodic. Theoretical upper and lower bounds on the minimax excess risk will be derived as explicit functions of the number of trajectories, trajectory length, covariate dimension, and evaluation horizon.
4bebfab79771392aebefeab29b55e4d76c6a49a0.experiment_details: Experiments will include both theoretical analysis and numerical simulations. Theoretical results will be validated through simulations using synthetic datasets generated from linear dynamical systems with varying numbers of trajectories (m), trajectory lengths (T), and covariate dimensions (n). Baselines will include learning from iid examples and from a single long trajectory. Evaluation metrics will focus on excess mean-squared prediction risk over both strict and extended evaluation horizons, as well as parameter estimation error for system identification. Key experimental setups will vary the number of trajectories and trajectory lengths to empirically confirm the predicted phase transitions in statistical efficiency and to compare with established lower bounds.
4bebfab79771392aebefeab29b55e4d76c6a49a0.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a new statistical learning framework that interpolates between classical iid learning and learning from a single auto-correlated sequence by considering many independent, non-ergodic trajectories. The analysis provides the first sharp characterization of the minimax excess risk for linear regression in this setting, revealing a phase transition in efficiency as the number of trajectories increases. The trajectory small-ball condition is introduced as a generalization of standard non-degeneracy requirements, enabling efficient learning without ergodicity or long trajectories. The results improve upon existing guarantees for linear system identification, extending them to broader regimes and providing tighter bounds, particularly in the many-trajectory setting.

4bee9cf0d3c397b1e67157eecc600f200efdce78.title: Do Vision-Language Models Really Understand Visual Language?
4bee9cf0d3c397b1e67157eecc600f200efdce78.research_question: Do large vision-language models (LVLMs) possess genuine understanding of visual language, specifically diagrams, or do their performances on diagram-based reasoning tasks reflect reliance on background knowledge and shortcuts rather than true diagram comprehension?
4bee9cf0d3c397b1e67157eecc600f200efdce78.hypothesis: LVLMs do not genuinely understand the relational structure in diagrams; instead, their apparent success in diagram reasoning tasks is primarily due to leveraging background knowledge as shortcuts, rather than parsing and reasoning about the symbolic and relational content of diagrams.
4bee9cf0d3c397b1e67157eecc600f200efdce78.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation suite will be developed to systematically assess the diagram comprehension capabilities of LVLMs. This suite will include a diverse set of both synthetic and real-world diagrams spanning multiple domains such as ecology, biology, physics, astronomy, chemistry, and geology. Diagrams will be represented as graphs, with entities as nodes and relations (explicit or implicit) as edges. The evaluation will use carefully designed multiple-choice question templates targeting both entity recognition and relation understanding, further divided into knowledge-free (KF) and knowledge-required (KR) categories. The methodology will distinguish between recognition (e.g., identifying entities or relations) and reasoning (e.g., counting entities or relations), and will control for the presence or absence of background knowledge in both the diagrams and the questions. Experiments will probe model performance under varying diagram complexity and knowledge grounding, and will include ablation studies where relational information is removed or randomized to test for knowledge shortcut reliance.
4bee9cf0d3c397b1e67157eecc600f200efdce78.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of state-of-the-art LVLMs, including open-source models (such as LLaMA-3.2-11B-Vision, LLaVA-OneVision-7B, Qwen2-VL-7B) and proprietary models (such as GPT-4V, GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro). The synthetic diagram set will be generated with controlled entity and relation structures, while the real diagram set will be curated from existing datasets (e.g., Krishnamurthy et al., 2016; Kembhavi et al., 2016), filtered for quality and complexity. Evaluation metrics will primarily be accuracy on multiple-choice QA tasks, with separate reporting for entity and relation questions, as well as for recognition and reasoning subtypes. Baselines will include zero-shot, chain-of-thought, and in-context learning prompting strategies. Additional analyses will compare model performance on diagrams with and without embedded semantic knowledge, and on questions that do or do not require background knowledge. The impact of diagram complexity and the presence of knowledge shortcuts will be quantitatively and qualitatively assessed.
4bee9cf0d3c397b1e67157eecc600f200efdce78.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a rigorous, domain-spanning test suite that isolates and evaluates the distinct capabilities of LVLMs in diagram understanding, specifically decoupling visual recognition, relational reasoning, and knowledge reliance. The methodology enables controlled analysis of whether models truly parse and reason about diagrammatic relations or simply exploit background knowledge. The approach provides new insights into the limitations of current LVLMs, challenges prevailing assumptions about their multimodal reasoning abilities, and sets a new standard for evaluating symbolic and relational understanding in vision-language models.

4c155ef1f396fd5929af9536646e77931b60a0c3.title: Implicit Bias of Gradient Descent on Reparametrized Models: On Equivalence to Mirror Descent
4c155ef1f396fd5929af9536646e77931b60a0c3.research_question: How does the implicit bias of gradient descent in overparameterized models relate to the dynamics of mirror descent, and under what conditions can gradient flow with reparametrized models be characterized as equivalent to mirror descent with respect to a Legendre function?
4c155ef1f396fd5929af9536646e77931b60a0c3.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that for a broad class of reparametrizations, specifically those termed 'commuting parametrizations,' the gradient flow in the reparametrized space is equivalent to continuous mirror descent in the original parameter space with a corresponding Legendre function. Conversely, any mirror flow can be simulated by gradient flow with an appropriate commuting reparametrization.
4c155ef1f396fd5929af9536646e77931b60a0c3.proposed_method: A general framework will be developed to analyze the dynamics of gradient flow on reparametrized models, focusing on the concept of commuting parametrizations. The approach involves formalizing the conditions under which the gradient flow in the reparametrized (x-) space simulates a mirror flow in the original (w-) space, leveraging properties of Lie brackets and vector fields. The methodology includes deriving sufficient and necessary conditions for this equivalence, characterizing the associated Legendre function, and establishing a constructive correspondence between parametrizations and mirror maps. Additionally, Nash's embedding theorem will be employed to show the existence of such parametrizations for any given mirror flow, thus providing a full characterization in both directions.
4c155ef1f396fd5929af9536646e77931b60a0c3.experiment_details: Experiments will be designed to validate the theoretical framework in the context of overparameterized linear regression and deep linear networks. Synthetic and real-world datasets will be used to instantiate various commuting and non-commuting parametrizations. Baseline comparisons will include standard gradient descent, classical mirror descent, and previously studied reparametrizations. Evaluation metrics will focus on convergence properties, the structure of the implicit bias (e.g., minimum norm or minimum Bregman divergence solutions), and the agreement between the observed optimization trajectories and the predicted equivalence to mirror descent. Additional experiments will test the generality of the framework by constructing explicit parametrizations for given mirror maps using Nash's embedding theorem.
4c155ef1f396fd5929af9536646e77931b60a0c3.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified and general framework that characterizes when and how gradient flow on reparametrized models is equivalent to mirror descent, subsuming and extending all previous results in this area. The notion of commuting parametrization is formalized and shown to be both necessary and sufficient for this equivalence. The approach provides new convergence analyses and implicit regularization results for underdetermined linear regression, filling gaps in prior work. Furthermore, the use of Nash's embedding theorem establishes, for the first time, that any mirror flow can be simulated by gradient flow with an appropriate reparametrization, offering a complete answer to open questions about the universality of this equivalence.

4c180f776e769a4be867ce35a563163143d84dd1.title: Unlocking Slot Attention by Changing Optimal Transport Costs
4c180f776e769a4be867ce35a563163143d84dd1.research_question: How can object-centric models, particularly slot attention mechanisms, be improved to effectively handle scenarios with a dynamic or ambiguous number of objects, especially in cases where set-equivariance leads to soft assignments and tie-breaking failures?
4c180f776e769a4be867ce35a563163143d84dd1.hypothesis: Introducing a cross-attention module that minimizes the entropy of the Sinkhorn operator (MESH) will enable exclusive multiset-equivariance in slot attention, allowing for effective tie-breaking between similar slots and improving object-centric learning performance in images and videos.
4c180f776e769a4be867ce35a563163143d84dd1.proposed_method: A new cross-attention module, termed MESH (Minimize Entropy of Sinkhorn), will be developed to enhance slot attention by combining the tie-breaking ability of unregularized optimal transport with the computational efficiency and differentiability of entropy-regularized optimal transport. The method will first establish a theoretical connection between slot attention and optimal transport, showing that standard slot attention approximates entropy-regularized optimal transport via a single Sinkhorn iteration. MESH will iteratively optimize the cost matrix to minimize the entropy of the resulting Sinkhorn transport map, injecting a small amount of noise to facilitate tie-breaking among similar slots. The optimization will be performed via gradient descent for a fixed number of steps, ensuring the modified cost matrix remains close to the original. The final transport map will be computed using the Sinkhorn algorithm, resulting in sparse, low-entropy assignments that enable exclusive multiset-equivariance.
4c180f776e769a4be867ce35a563163143d84dd1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple object-centric learning benchmarks, including synthetic datasets such as Random Objects Detection, CLEVR property prediction, Multi-dSprites, ClevrTex, and video-based datasets like CLEVRER-S and CLEVRER-L. Baselines will include standard slot attention (SA), slot attention with multiple Sinkhorn iterations (SA-SH), and slot attention using unregularized optimal transport (SA-EMD). Evaluation metrics will comprise normalized RMSE, average precision (AP) at various thresholds, Foreground Adjusted Rand Index (FG-ARI), Foreground mean Intersection over Union (FG-mIoU), and temporal consistency (TC) for video tasks. Experimental setups will control for the number of slots, input feature dimensions, and the presence of background elements, with multiple random seeds used for statistical robustness. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of entropy minimization, noise injection, and the number of optimization steps.
4c180f776e769a4be867ce35a563163143d84dd1.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel cross-attention module (MESH) that enables exclusive multiset-equivariance in slot attention by minimizing the entropy of the Sinkhorn operator, a property not present in standard set-equivariant attention mechanisms. This approach uniquely combines the tie-breaking ability of unregularized optimal transport with the speed and differentiability of entropy-regularized methods, overcoming the limitations of both. The method is claimed to significantly improve object-centric learning performance, particularly in challenging scenarios with dynamic object counts or ambiguous object assignments, and to offer computational efficiency suitable for practical applications.

4c4f0fcf1ce04f12290d8c876abfbe57817de430.title: TabPFN: A Transformer That Solves Small Tabular Classification Problems in a Second
4c4f0fcf1ce04f12290d8c876abfbe57817de430.research_question: Can a single, pre-trained Transformer model be developed to perform fast, accurate, and hyperparameter-free supervised classification on small tabular datasets, rivaling or surpassing state-of-the-art machine learning and AutoML methods?
4c4f0fcf1ce04f12290d8c876abfbe57817de430.hypothesis: A Transformer-based Prior-Data Fitted Network (PFN), trained offline on synthetic tabular data generated from a carefully designed probabilistic prior incorporating causal and Bayesian principles, will enable near-instant, competitive or superior classification performance on small tabular datasets without the need for hyperparameter tuning.
4c4f0fcf1ce04f12290d8c876abfbe57817de430.proposed_method: A Prior-Data Fitted Network (PFN) based on a Transformer architecture will be trained offline to approximate Bayesian posterior predictive distributions for tabular classification tasks. The training data for the PFN will be generated synthetically from a novel, probabilistic prior that combines Structural Causal Models (SCMs) and Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs), with a preference for simpler models and causal structures. The PFN will be trained to predict labels for test samples conditioned on a set of labeled training examples, using in-context learning and a set-valued input format to ensure permutation invariance. During inference, the trained Transformer will accept both training and test samples as input and output predictions for the entire test set in a single forward pass, without any further parameter updates or hyperparameter tuning.
4c4f0fcf1ce04f12290d8c876abfbe57817de430.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on small tabular datasets, primarily using the 18 numerical datasets from the OpenML-CC18 benchmark (each with up to 1000 training samples, 100 numerical features, and 10 classes), as well as an additional 67 small numerical datasets from OpenML for validation. The proposed method will be compared against standard machine learning baselines (K-nearest neighbors, Logistic Regression, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost), state-of-the-art AutoML systems (AutoGluon, Auto-sklearn 2.0), and deep learning baselines (SAINT, Regularization Cocktails). Evaluation metrics will include ROCAUC (one-vs-one for multiclass), accuracy, cross-entropy, and computational time. Each method will be evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation and multiple time budgets, with performance aggregated across datasets and splits. Additional analyses will assess the method's inductive biases, robustness to feature rotations and uninformative features, and potential for ensembling.
4c4f0fcf1ce04f12290d8c876abfbe57817de430.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a single, pre-trained Transformer model capable of performing supervised classification on small tabular datasets in less than a second, eliminating the need for hyperparameter tuning. The method leverages a novel prior over tabular data that integrates structural causal models and Bayesian neural networks, enabling the PFN to approximate Bayesian inference across a wide range of data-generating mechanisms. This results in a model with strong inductive biases toward simple and causal explanations, state-of-the-art performance on numerical tabular data, and dramatic speed improvements (up to 5700× faster on GPU) compared to leading AutoML frameworks. The approach also demonstrates unique error patterns, making it highly effective for ensembling with existing methods.

4c60ce3e5116037390b3b92866f43df83f3e9c6f.title: Pretraining task diversity and the emergence of non-Bayesian in-context learning for regression
4c60ce3e5116037390b3b92866f43df83f3e9c6f.research_question: How does the diversity of tasks in the pretraining dataset affect the ability of pretrained transformers to perform in-context learning on fundamentally new regression tasks that differ from those encountered during pretraining?
4c60ce3e5116037390b3b92866f43df83f3e9c6f.hypothesis: There exists a threshold in pretraining task diversity, beyond which pretrained transformers can perform in-context learning on new, unseen tasks by deviating from Bayesian inference based solely on the pretraining distribution, and instead approximate optimal solutions for the broader task distribution.
