4c60ce3e5116037390b3b92866f43df83f3e9c6f.proposed_method: A systematic investigation will be conducted by pretraining decoder-only transformer models on sequences of linear regression tasks, where each task is defined by a latent regression vector. The diversity of the pretraining dataset will be controlled by varying the number of unique latent regression vectors (tasks) sampled from a standard normal distribution. The transformers will be trained to minimize next-token mean squared error on sequences of data-target pairs generated from these tasks. The models' in-context learning abilities will be evaluated on both tasks seen during pretraining and on new tasks sampled from a broader, ideal Gaussian distribution. The behavior of the pretrained transformers will be compared to Bayesian estimators optimal for the pretraining and ideal task distributions, specifically the discrete minimum mean squared error (dMMSE) estimator and ridge regression estimator, respectively. Additional experiments will manipulate model capacity (number of layers, embedding size) and regularization (weight decay) to assess their influence on the emergence of in-context learning.
4c60ce3e5116037390b3b92866f43df83f3e9c6f.experiment_details: Experiments will use synthetic datasets for linear regression, with input vectors drawn from a D-dimensional standard normal and targets generated via a latent regression vector plus Gaussian noise. The number of unique regression vectors (task diversity) in pretraining will be varied systematically, with models trained using the Adam optimizer and a one-cycle learning rate schedule. Both base and small transformer architectures will be evaluated, with hyperparameters such as batch size, number of training steps, embedding dimension, and number of layers ablated. Performance will be measured using mean squared error (MSE), normalized by task dimension, on both pretraining tasks and unseen tasks from the ideal distribution. The predictions of the transformers will be quantitatively compared to those of dMMSE and ridge regression estimators. Additional analyses will include learning dynamics, scaling of the task diversity threshold with problem dimension, and the effects of regularization and model capacity.
4c60ce3e5116037390b3b92866f43df83f3e9c6f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a controlled framework for probing the emergence of in-context learning in transformers as a function of pretraining task diversity, revealing an algorithmic phase transition at a finite diversity threshold. It demonstrates that, beyond this threshold, transformers can learn fundamentally new tasks in-context by deviating from Bayesian inference on the pretraining distribution and instead approximating optimal solutions for the broader task distribution. The scaling of the diversity threshold with task dimension is shown to be much more favorable for transformers than for classical Bayesian estimators. The effects of regularization and model capacity on the emergence of in-context learning are systematically characterized, providing new insights into the mechanisms underlying this phenomenon.

4c94d04afa4309ec2f06bdd0fe3781f91461b362.title: DreamFusion: Text-to-3D using 2D Diffusion
4c94d04afa4309ec2f06bdd0fe3781f91461b362.research_question: How can high-quality 3D models be synthesized from natural language text prompts without requiring any 3D training data or modifications to existing 2D text-to-image diffusion models?
4c94d04afa4309ec2f06bdd0fe3781f91461b362.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a pretrained 2D text-to-image diffusion model can serve as an effective prior for optimizing a 3D scene representation, enabling the generation of coherent and realistic 3D models from text prompts without the need for 3D training data.
4c94d04afa4309ec2f06bdd0fe3781f91461b362.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that leverages a pretrained 2D text-to-image diffusion model as a prior for 3D synthesis. The approach introduces Score Distillation Sampling (SDS), a loss function based on probability density distillation, which enables optimization of a differentiable 3D scene parameterization (specifically, a Neural Radiance Field, or NeRF) such that its 2D renderings from random camera angles achieve low loss under the diffusion model. The NeRF is randomly initialized for each text prompt and is optimized via gradient descent, where each iteration involves rendering the NeRF from a randomly sampled camera and lighting configuration, computing the SDS loss using the pretrained diffusion model, and updating the NeRF parameters. The NeRF is enhanced with a shading model that separates albedo and geometry, and regularization techniques are applied to improve geometric fidelity and prevent degenerate solutions.
4c94d04afa4309ec2f06bdd0fe3781f91461b362.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by generating 3D models from a diverse set of text prompts, using the 64x64 base Imagen text-to-image diffusion model as the frozen prior. The proposed method will be compared against existing zero-shot text-to-3D baselines, including DreamFields and CLIP-Mesh, using the object-centric subset of the MS-COCO validation set (153 prompts). Evaluation will be performed using CLIP R-Precision, measuring the consistency of rendered images (both color and textureless) with the input captions, as well as qualitative visualizations. Ablation studies will assess the impact of key components such as view-dependent prompts, lighting, and textureless rendering. Optimization will be performed on TPU hardware for 15,000 iterations per prompt, and additional regularization and hyperparameter settings will be detailed for reproducibility.
4c94d04afa4309ec2f06bdd0fe3781f91461b362.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable high-fidelity text-to-3D synthesis using only a pretrained 2D text-to-image diffusion model, requiring no 3D training data or modifications to the diffusion model. The introduction of Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) allows direct optimization of 3D scene parameters via a 2D diffusion prior, and the integration of a NeRF-based differentiable rendering engine with advanced shading and regularization techniques enables the generation of coherent, relightable 3D assets from arbitrary text prompts. The method demonstrates significant improvements in both geometric and semantic fidelity over prior zero-shot text-to-3D methods.

4ccddac4d9cbfdb1f01f697be10d4518ff8ef2f3.title: Model Editing as a Robust and Denoised variant of DPO: A Case Study on Toxicity
4ccddac4d9cbfdb1f01f697be10d4518ff8ef2f3.research_question: How can large language models be efficiently and robustly aligned to reduce undesirable behaviors such as toxicity, without relying on computationally expensive tuning-based methods or large-scale preference data?
4ccddac4d9cbfdb1f01f697be10d4518ff8ef2f3.hypothesis: A tuning-free, sample-efficient model editing approach that identifies and projects out a low-dimensional toxic subspace in model weights can achieve effective toxicity reduction, while remaining robust to noisy preference data and preserving model capabilities.
4ccddac4d9cbfdb1f01f697be10d4518ff8ef2f3.proposed_method: The proposed method, ProFS (Projection Filter for Subspaces), is a weight-editing algorithm for transformer-based language models. First, pairs of toxic and non-toxic sentences are collected, and their embeddings are extracted from a specified set of MLP layers. The method computes the difference between toxic and non-toxic embeddings, then centers this difference by projecting out the mean direction associated with frequent, non-toxic tokens to preserve essential model functionality. Singular value decomposition (SVD) is applied to the centered difference matrix to identify the top-k singular vectors that span the toxic subspace. The model's MLP-value weight matrices are then edited by projecting out these toxic directions, resulting in a new set of weights that suppress toxic outputs. This edit is performed once, requires no architectural changes, and the resulting model can be used as a drop-in replacement.
4ccddac4d9cbfdb1f01f697be10d4518ff8ef2f3.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on several transformer language models, including GPT-2 Medium, Mistral (7B), Mistral-SFT, OPT (6.7B), and GPT-J (6B). The primary dataset for editing is a pairwise toxic/non-toxic set derived from Wikitext-2 and generated toxic continuations, with as few as 500 samples for ProFS (compared to 2000 for DPO). Toxicity is evaluated using the REALTOXICITYPROMPTS challenge set, with Detoxify as the toxicity scoring metric. Model fluency and capability are assessed via perplexity on WikiText-2 and zero-shot task performance on EleutherAI LM Harness. Baselines include DPO (Direct Preference Optimization), KTO, DexPerts, and Toxification Reversal. Robustness to label noise is tested by flipping labels in the preference data, and ablation studies are performed on layer selection and centering. Results are averaged over three random splits.
4ccddac4d9cbfdb1f01f697be10d4518ff8ef2f3.novelty_claims: The proposed approach offers a tuning-free, sample-efficient alternative to alignment that does not require large-scale preference data or gradient-based training. ProFS is robust to label noise, outperforming tuning-based methods in this regard. The method leverages factor analysis and SVD to isolate interpretable toxic subspaces, providing both theoretical and empirical connections to DPO, and can be interpreted as a denoised, single-step variant of DPO. The approach is computationally lightweight, requires only a single edit, and preserves model fluency and capabilities. ProFS demonstrates effectiveness across multiple models and tasks, and provides principled insights into leveraging interpretable directions in model activations for alignment.

4d00b4b5f19b0f9b359b01452ea4cee344cc35a2.title: Revisiting Simple Regret: Fast Rates for Returning a Good Arm
4d00b4b5f19b0f9b359b01452ea4cee344cc35a2.research_question: How can simple regret in pure exploration multi-armed bandit problems be minimized efficiently, particularly in both data-rich and data-poor regimes, without requiring parameter tuning or prior knowledge of problem-specific parameters?
4d00b4b5f19b0f9b359b01452ea4cee344cc35a2.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that improved analyses and modifications of existing algorithms, such as Sequential Halving, can yield optimal or near-optimal simple regret bounds in both data-rich and data-poor regimes, and that a new bracketing-based algorithm can outperform current state-of-the-art methods in the data-poor regime.
4d00b4b5f19b0f9b359b01452ea4cee344cc35a2.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves a detailed, instance-dependent analysis of the Sequential Halving (SH) algorithm to derive tight bounds on the probability of returning an arm whose mean reward is not within an arbitrary epsilon of the best arm, for any epsilon > 0. This analysis does not require epsilon as an input to the algorithm, enabling uniform guarantees. For the data-poor regime, a novel algorithm called Bracketing Sequential Halving (BSH) is introduced, which progressively subsamples larger sets of arms (brackets) and applies SH within each bracket, thereby avoiding the need to sample every arm at least once. BSH uses a round-robin allocation of samples across brackets, and at each timestep, outputs the arm with the highest empirical mean among all bracket representatives. Additionally, an anytime variant of SH, called Doubling SH (DSH), is proposed, which repeatedly runs SH with exponentially increasing budgets, providing strong guarantees without requiring the total budget as input.
4d00b4b5f19b0f9b359b01452ea4cee344cc35a2.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the New Yorker Cartoon Caption Contest dataset, which features thousands of arms (captions) per contest. The reward for each arm is modeled as a Bernoulli variable based on the proportion of positive crowd evaluations. The performance of BSH is compared against BUCB, a state-of-the-art baseline for the data-poor regime, across several contests with up to 6509 arms. Evaluation focuses on simple regret as a function of the number of samples, particularly in the data-poor regime where the sample budget is only modestly larger than the number of arms. Multiple values of the confidence parameter delta are tested for BUCB, and all experiments are repeated 500 times with different random seeds to ensure statistical robustness.
4d00b4b5f19b0f9b359b01452ea4cee344cc35a2.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new, tight, instance-dependent analysis of Sequential Halving that provides uniform epsilon-error probability bounds without requiring epsilon as an input, leading to optimal worst-case simple regret rates up to logarithmic factors. The Bracketing Sequential Halving (BSH) algorithm is developed for the data-poor regime, achieving non-vacuous, high-probability sample complexity bounds and outperforming existing methods on real-world tasks. The approach is parameter-free, does not require knowledge of the number of good arms or target error rates, and establishes optimality for key problem instances. Additionally, the proposal resolves several open questions regarding accelerated sample complexity in the presence of multiple good arms and provides the first such results without relying on subsampling devices.

4d1c856275744c0284312a3a50efb6ca9dc4cd4c.title: Know What You Don’t Know: Unanswerable Questions for SQuAD
4d1c856275744c0284312a3a50efb6ca9dc4cd4c.research_question: How can machine reading comprehension systems be evaluated on their ability to recognize when a question cannot be answered based on a given context, and what are the limitations of current datasets in supporting this evaluation?
4d1c856275744c0284312a3a50efb6ca9dc4cd4c.hypothesis: Incorporating a large set of adversarially-authored, context-relevant unanswerable questions into reading comprehension benchmarks will expose significant weaknesses in current models and provide a more robust evaluation of language understanding.
4d1c856275744c0284312a3a50efb6ca9dc4cd4c.proposed_method: A new dataset will be constructed by augmenting an existing reading comprehension benchmark with a substantial number of unanswerable questions, each crafted by crowdworkers to be relevant to the context and to contain plausible but incorrect answer spans. The annotation process will require workers to reference entities in the paragraph and ensure that each unanswerable question has a plausible answer present in the text, making them difficult to distinguish from answerable questions using simple heuristics. Data quality will be ensured by filtering out low-quality contributions and collecting multiple human answers per question, with majority voting to determine the final label. The resulting dataset will be split into training, development, and test sets, maintaining a balanced ratio of answerable and unanswerable questions in the evaluation splits.
4d1c856275744c0284312a3a50efb6ca9dc4cd4c.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training and evaluating several state-of-the-art extractive question answering models, including BiDAF-No-Answer and DocumentQA (with and without ELMo embeddings), on the new dataset. Evaluation metrics will include exact match and F1 scores, with models required to abstain from answering when no answer is supported by the context. Human performance will be measured by collecting multiple annotations per question and using majority voting to establish ground truth. Baselines will include always abstaining and models trained on datasets with automatically generated negative examples (e.g., TFIDF or rule-based methods). Comparative analysis will assess the difficulty of the new dataset relative to previous benchmarks and automatically generated negatives.
4d1c856275744c0284312a3a50efb6ca9dc4cd4c.novelty_claims: The proposed dataset introduces a large-scale, diverse, and adversarially-authored set of unanswerable questions that are contextually relevant and contain plausible distractor answers, addressing key shortcomings of prior benchmarks. This approach enables rigorous evaluation of a system's ability to recognize when no answer is present, a critical aspect of robust language understanding. The dataset is shown to be significantly more challenging for current models than previous datasets or those with automatically generated negatives, highlighting substantial gaps between machine and human performance and motivating further advances in reading comprehension systems.

4d1eadaa9a04e86aef2278ae13eb9fce644c9fc5.title: Learning and Leveraging World Models in Visual Representation Learning
4d1eadaa9a04e86aef2278ae13eb9fce644c9fc5.research_question: Can learning and leveraging world models improve visual representation learning, and how can such models be effectively reused for downstream vision tasks such as classification and segmentation?
4d1eadaa9a04e86aef2278ae13eb9fce644c9fc5.hypothesis: Learning capable world models in visual self-supervised learning enables the extraction of more flexible and reusable representations, which can be efficiently adapted to diverse downstream tasks through finetuning of the world model rather than the encoder.
4d1eadaa9a04e86aef2278ae13eb9fce644c9fc5.proposed_method: A novel framework, Image World Models (IWM), will be developed based on the Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA). The method will generate source and target views of images using a combination of photometric and geometric augmentations, including color jitter, destructive augmentations (grayscale, blur, solarization), and masking. Both views will be encoded using a Vision Transformer (ViT-B/16), with the predictor (the world model) conditioned on transformation parameters and mask tokens. The predictor will be trained to match the target's latent representation using a squared L2 loss. Key aspects to be systematically studied include the conditioning mechanism (sequence or feature), the complexity and strength of applied transformations, and the capacity (depth and width) of the predictor network. The approach will allow control over the abstraction level of learned representations, enabling both invariant and equivariant world models.
4d1eadaa9a04e86aef2278ae13eb9fce644c9fc5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale image datasets such as ImageNet-1k for classification and ADE20k for segmentation. The effectiveness of IWM will be evaluated against strong baselines, including contrastive methods (e.g., MoCoV3, DINO), masked image modeling (MAE), and other JEPA-based models. Evaluation protocols will include linear probing, attentive probing, and various finetuning strategies: encoder finetuning, predictor finetuning (with the encoder frozen), and end-to-end finetuning. Metrics such as ImageNet Top-1 accuracy, segmentation mIoU, and Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) for world model quality will be used. Ablation studies will examine the impact of predictor conditioning, transformation strength, and network capacity. Multi-task finetuning will also be explored to assess efficiency and versatility.
4d1eadaa9a04e86aef2278ae13eb9fce644c9fc5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a generalization of JEPA to a broader set of image corruptions and photometric transformations, moving beyond masked image modeling. It systematically studies and demonstrates the importance of conditioning, transformation complexity, and predictor capacity for learning strong world models. The method enables the reuse of the world model for downstream tasks via efficient predictor finetuning, achieving or surpassing state-of-the-art performance with fewer finetuned parameters. Additionally, it provides a mechanism to control the abstraction level of representations, interpolating between invariant (contrastive) and equivariant (masked modeling) behaviors, and supports efficient multi-task adaptation.

4d358d1684f98ea0136d4c39f8560447fb533350.title: On Least Square Estimation in Softmax Gating Mixture of Experts
4d358d1684f98ea0136d4c39f8560447fb533350.research_question: What are the statistical properties and estimation rates of least squares estimators in softmax gating mixture of experts (MoE) models under deterministic regression settings, and how do different choices of expert functions (including neural network-based, ridge, and polynomial experts) affect these rates?
4d358d1684f98ea0136d4c39f8560447fb533350.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that expert functions satisfying a strong identifiability or strong independence condition will yield faster, potentially parametric, estimation rates for the least squares estimator in softmax gating MoE models, while polynomial or input-independent experts will result in significantly slower, possibly non-polynomial, estimation rates.
4d358d1684f98ea0136d4c39f8560447fb533350.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the convergence behavior of least squares estimators (LSE) in softmax gating mixture of experts models under a deterministic regression setting. The approach will introduce and formalize a strong identifiability condition for general expert functions, and a strong independence condition for activation functions in ridge (two-layer neural network) experts. The methodology will involve deriving lower bounds on the estimation error using novel loss functions based on Voronoi cell decompositions of the parameter space, and characterizing the interaction between gating and expert parameters via partial differential equations. Theoretical analysis will be carried out for different regimes, including strongly identifiable experts, ridge experts with strongly independent activations, and polynomial (including linear) experts, to determine the corresponding estimation rates.
4d358d1684f98ea0136d4c39f8560447fb533350.experiment_details: Theoretical results will be validated through rigorous proofs and, where feasible, simulation studies. Experiments will involve generating synthetic datasets according to deterministic softmax gating MoE regression functions with varying types of expert functions (e.g., feed-forward networks with sigmoid/tanh/GELU activations, ridge experts, and polynomial experts). The performance of the least squares estimator will be compared across these settings. Evaluation metrics will include the L2 distance between the estimated and true regression functions, as well as parameter estimation error measured via the proposed Voronoi-based loss. Baselines will include maximum likelihood estimation under probabilistic MoE models and existing theoretical rates for comparison. Key experimental setup details will ensure fixed-dimensional parameter spaces, bounded input domains, and sufficient sample sizes to observe asymptotic behaviors.
4d358d1684f98ea0136d4c39f8560447fb533350.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first detailed statistical analysis of least squares estimation in deterministic softmax gating MoE models, moving beyond the restrictive Gaussian/probabilistic assumptions prevalent in prior work. It establishes a novel strong identifiability condition for expert functions and a strong independence condition for activation functions, both of which are shown to be critical for achieving fast estimation rates. The analysis reveals a surprising phenomenon: polynomial and input-independent experts can lead to estimation rates slower than any polynomial in sample size, in stark contrast to the parametric rates achievable with strongly identifiable or strongly independent experts. The findings have direct implications for expert selection and network design in practical applications, providing theoretical guidance for the choice of expert architectures in MoE models.

4d6062d49dccea1a897df1ea8d1bc768a3962b0a.title: MiDi: Mixed Graph and 3D Denoising Diffusion for Molecule Generation
4d6062d49dccea1a897df1ea8d1bc768a3962b0a.research_question: How can a generative model be designed to simultaneously generate molecular graphs and their corresponding 3D atomic arrangements in an end-to-end differentiable manner, improving the stability and validity of generated molecules for applications in drug discovery?
4d6062d49dccea1a897df1ea8d1bc768a3962b0a.hypothesis: A diffusion model that jointly generates molecular graphs and 3D conformations using a mixed discrete and Gaussian noise process, along with an adaptive noise schedule and a novel equivariant neural network architecture, will produce more stable and chemically valid molecules than existing two-stage or single-modality approaches.
4d6062d49dccea1a897df1ea8d1bc768a3962b0a.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a mixed denoising diffusion framework (MiDi) that represents molecules as attributed graphs embedded in 3D space, with node features (atom types and formal charges), edge features (bond types), and 3D coordinates. The diffusion process applies Gaussian noise to the 3D coordinates (within the zero center-of-mass subspace for SE(3) equivariance) and discrete (categorical) diffusion to atom types, formal charges, and bond types. An adaptive noise schedule is employed, adding noise to different components at different rates to prioritize early denoising of coordinates and bond types, followed by atom types and charges. The denoising network is a Transformer-based architecture incorporating a novel relaxed Equivariant Graph Neural Network (rEGNN) layer, which leverages additional rotation-invariant features and processes all graph components in an integrated manner. The model is trained end-to-end to reconstruct clean molecular graphs and conformations from noisy inputs, using mean-squared error for coordinates and cross-entropy losses for categorical features.
4d6062d49dccea1a897df1ea8d1bc768a3962b0a.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the GEOM-DRUGS dataset, which contains complex molecules with explicit hydrogens, as well as on the QM9 dataset. The proposed model is evaluated in unconditional molecule generation settings. Baselines include the Equivariant Diffusion Model (EDM) using interatomic distances for bond prediction, and EDM followed by the OpenBabel bond optimization algorithm. Evaluation metrics focus on the proportion of generated molecules that are chemically stable and valid. The experimental setup includes ablation studies on noise schedules and architectural components, and the model is assessed for its ability to generate both valid 2D graphs and consistent 3D conformations.
4d6062d49dccea1a897df1ea8d1bc768a3962b0a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first end-to-end differentiable diffusion model that jointly generates both molecular graphs and 3D conformations. It introduces a mixed noise process with component-specific adaptive schedules, and a novel rEGNN layer that enhances SE(3)-equivariant graph processing by leveraging features beyond pairwise distances. The method demonstrates a substantial improvement in the generation of stable and valid molecules over previous diffusion-based and two-stage approaches, particularly on challenging datasets with explicit hydrogens and complex structures. Additionally, the framework is versatile and can be readily extended to various drug discovery tasks.

4d673dcd58d169392357361d21ee91ed66a6adcc.title: A Nearly-Optimal Bound for Fast Regression with 𝓁∞ Guarantee
4d673dcd58d169392357361d21ee91ed66a6adcc.research_question: How can fast regression algorithms be designed to provide nearly-optimal guarantees in the infinity norm (ℓ∞) for linear and tensor regression problems, and what structural properties of sketching matrices are necessary to achieve these guarantees efficiently?
4d673dcd58d169392357361d21ee91ed66a6adcc.hypothesis: Dense sketching matrices, when designed to satisfy both oblivious subspace embedding (OSE) and oblivious coordinate-wise embedding (OCE) properties, enable fast regression algorithms to achieve nearly-optimal ℓ∞ guarantees with high probability and minimal row count, outperforming sparse sketches in this regime.
4d673dcd58d169392357361d21ee91ed66a6adcc.proposed_method: A novel analytical framework will be developed for regression with ℓ∞ guarantees by leveraging the Oblivious Coordinate-wise Embedding (OCE) property. The approach involves constructing and analyzing dense sketching matrices, such as subsampled randomized Hadamard transforms (SRHT), subsampled randomized circulant transforms (SRCT), and their tensor variants. The method establishes sufficient conditions—specifically, small pairwise column inner products and bounded column norms—that ensure the sketching matrix preserves inner products with high probability. The framework will be extended to both standard and Kronecker product (degree-2 tensor) regression, with theoretical analysis proving that solving the sketched regression yields an approximate solution close to the optimum in the ℓ∞ norm. Fast computation is enabled by utilizing the fast Fourier transform (FFT) for efficient application of the sketching matrices.
4d673dcd58d169392357361d21ee91ed66a6adcc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic and real-world datasets where the matrix A ∈ ℝ^{n×d} and vector b ∈ ℝ^n are provided, with n ≫ d. The proposed dense sketching matrices (SRHT, SRCT, TensorSRHT, TensorSRCT, Gaussian, AMS) will be evaluated against baselines such as sparse sketches (e.g., Count Sketch, OSNAP). The primary evaluation metric will be the ℓ∞ error between the approximate and optimal regression solutions, with additional metrics including computation time and row count required for a given error threshold. Experiments will measure the probability of achieving the ℓ∞ guarantee as a function of sketch size, and will compare the empirical performance to theoretical bounds. The setup will include varying n, d, and error tolerance ϵ, and will test both standard and tensor regression settings.
4d673dcd58d169392357361d21ee91ed66a6adcc.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to demonstrate that dense sketching matrices are necessary and sufficient for achieving ℓ∞ guarantees in fast regression, establishing a nearly-optimal row count up to logarithmic factors. The analysis introduces a new, simpler, and more general approach based on the OCE property, applicable to a broad class of dense sketches beyond SRHT. The method significantly improves upon prior results by reducing the required sketch size from super-linear to nearly-linear in d, and generalizes the guarantee to tensor regression. The structural insights into sketching matrices and the unified analytical technique represent key innovations.

4d6be45a51f2ab33329fe5c08939591e52dc6e6d.title: Incentivizing Honesty among Competitors in Collaborative Learning and Optimization
4d6be45a51f2ab33329fe5c08939591e52dc6e6d.research_question: How can collaborative learning and optimization be structured to incentivize honesty among participants who are also competitors, thereby preventing strategic manipulation and ensuring high-quality learning outcomes?
4d6be45a51f2ab33329fe5c08939591e52dc6e6d.hypothesis: Rational, self-interested participants in collaborative learning settings with competitive incentives are likely to manipulate their updates unless explicit incentive mechanisms are introduced; implementing peer-prediction-inspired penalties or protocol modifications can incentivize honesty and restore learning performance comparable to full cooperation.
4d6be45a51f2ab33329fe5c08939591e52dc6e6d.proposed_method: A game-theoretic framework is developed to model the interactions of multiple participants in collaborative learning, where each participant's reward depends both on the quality of their own model and the relative performance compared to others. Two key learning tasks are considered: single-round mean estimation and multi-round stochastic gradient descent (SGD) for strongly-convex objectives. For each, mechanisms are proposed to incentivize honest reporting of updates. In the mean estimation setting, both side-payment penalties (transferable utility) and protocol modifications (non-transferable utility) are introduced, penalizing deviations from honest behavior based on observable update statistics. In the SGD setting, a recursive penalty scheme is implemented, where penalties are proportional to the squared deviation of a participant's update from the group mean, and are redistributed to ensure budget balance. These mechanisms are designed to align Nash equilibria with honest participation, ensuring that rational players maximize their expected reward by behaving honestly.
4d6be45a51f2ab33329fe5c08939591e52dc6e6d.experiment_details: Empirical evaluation is conducted on the FeMNIST and Twitter datasets from the LEAF federated learning benchmark. Simulated federated SGD is performed, with participants (clients) grouped and some instructed to corrupt their gradient updates by adding noise of varying magnitudes. The effect of different penalty weights on the incentives for honesty is assessed by measuring the cross-entropy loss of the final models and the penalties incurred by each client. Baselines include standard federated SGD without penalties and with varying levels of adversarial noise. Evaluation metrics include model accuracy, cross-entropy loss, and the distribution of penalties paid by honest and dishonest clients. Experiments demonstrate that, with appropriately chosen penalty parameters, rational clients are incentivized to provide honest updates, and the overall learning performance remains high.
4d6be45a51f2ab33329fe5c08939591e52dc6e6d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a formal game-theoretic model for collaborative learning with competitive incentives, explicitly modeling strategic manipulation rather than assuming malicious behavior. Novel incentive mechanisms are developed, inspired by peer-prediction, that provably induce honest behavior as a Nash equilibrium in both mean estimation and SGD settings. The mechanisms are robust, require only observable behavior (not prior knowledge of true data distributions), and ensure budget balance and voluntary participation. Experimental results on realistic federated learning benchmarks demonstrate the practical effectiveness of the approach in non-convex settings.

4d815d722c1cb893da9b2a9cd8a1f9b1305f7b59.title: Towards Minimizing Feature Drift in Model Merging: Layer-wise Task Vector Fusion for Adaptive Knowledge Integration
4d815d722c1cb893da9b2a9cd8a1f9b1305f7b59.research_question: How can knowledge from multiple fine-tuned task-specific models be consolidated into a single unified model while minimizing performance degradation, particularly by addressing the issue of feature drift during model merging?
4d815d722c1cb893da9b2a9cd8a1f9b1305f7b59.hypothesis: Explicitly minimizing feature drift at each layer during model merging will result in a unified model that better preserves the performance of individual task experts compared to existing parameter-level or task-loss-based merging methods, and will do so efficiently without requiring retraining.
4d815d722c1cb893da9b2a9cd8a1f9b1305f7b59.proposed_method: A novel method, Layer-wise Optimal Task Vector Merging (LOTMerging), is proposed to minimize feature drift between task-specific experts and the unified model in a layer-by-layer manner. The approach formulates the merging process as a convex quadratic optimization problem, where the objective is to minimize the squared difference in feature representations for each layer across all tasks. Closed-form analytical solutions are derived for the optimal merging of linear weights, normalization scaling factors, and bias terms, enabling efficient integration via basic matrix operations. Each type of parameter (matrix multiplication, element-wise multiplication, and addition) is handled separately, and the method requires only a small set of exemplar data per task to compute the necessary feature statistics for merging. The merged model is constructed by applying the optimized task vectors to the pre-trained model parameters, with a tunable scaling factor to control the contribution of task-specific knowledge.
4d815d722c1cb893da9b2a9cd8a1f9b1305f7b59.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of vision and vision-language benchmarks. For vision tasks, eight image classification datasets will be used: SUN397, Cars, RESISC45, EuroSAT, SVHN, GTSRB, MNIST, and DTD, with CLIP-based vision encoders (ViT-B/32 and ViT-L/14) as the backbone. For vision-language tasks, three captioning datasets (COCO Caption, Flickr30k Caption, Textcaps) and three VQA datasets (OKVQA, TextVQA, ScienceQA) will be used, with BLIP as the backbone. Baselines will include state-of-the-art training-free model merging methods such as Weight Averaging, Fisher Merging, RegMean, Task Arithmetic, Ties-Merging, TATR, ConsensusMerging, AWDMerging, PCBMerging, and CATMerging. Evaluation metrics will be accuracy for classification and VQA tasks, and CIDEr for captioning tasks. The method will be evaluated with varying numbers of exemplars per task (as few as 16), and results will be averaged over multiple random exemplar sets to ensure robustness.
4d815d722c1cb893da9b2a9cd8a1f9b1305f7b59.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled, training-free, and efficient model merging framework that explicitly minimizes layer-wise feature drift, rather than relying on parameter-level averaging or costly secondary training. Closed-form solutions for optimal merging are derived for all key parameter types in transformer architectures, enabling fast and scalable consolidation. The approach is robust to limited data availability, requiring only a small number of exemplars per task, and preserves pre-trained knowledge more effectively than direct parameter merging. The method is adaptable to both vision and vision-language models, and theoretical analysis demonstrates its ability to adapt merging strategies based on task feature space dependencies.

4daf51de81e5cf3846482548196a8275369b27c4.title: Residual Denoising Diffusion Models
4daf51de81e5cf3846482548196a8275369b27c4.research_question: How can a unified and interpretable diffusion model be developed to effectively address both image generation and image restoration tasks, accommodating varying requirements for certainty and diversity across different applications?
4daf51de81e5cf3846482548196a8275369b27c4.hypothesis: A dual diffusion process that decouples residual diffusion (representing certainty and directional transformation) from noise diffusion (representing diversity and random perturbations) can provide a unified, interpretable, and effective framework for both image generation and restoration, outperforming or matching state-of-the-art methods while enabling flexible adaptation to new tasks.
4daf51de81e5cf3846482548196a8275369b27c4.proposed_method: A novel dual diffusion framework, termed Residual Denoising Diffusion Models (RDDM), is proposed to decouple the traditional single denoising diffusion process into two independent processes: residual diffusion and noise diffusion. The residual diffusion models the directional transformation from the target image to the degraded input image, explicitly guiding the reverse generation process for restoration tasks. Noise diffusion, in parallel, models random perturbations, controlling diversity in the generated outputs. The method introduces two independent coefficient schedules to separately control the speed of residual and noise diffusion, allowing for flexible adjustment and path-independent generation. The training objective includes predicting both residuals and noise using a generic UNet architecture, with an L1 loss and support for batch size of 1. The framework also incorporates an automatic objective selection algorithm to adaptively choose whether to predict residuals or noise for unknown tasks, and supports multiple sampling strategies (residual, noise, or both) for different application requirements.
4daf51de81e5cf3846482548196a8275369b27c4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of tasks, including image generation (e.g., CelebA 64x64 and 256x256), shadow removal (ISTD), low-light enhancement (LOL), and deraining (RainDrop). The proposed RDDM will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as DDPM, DDIM, InDI, I2SB, and various specialized restoration networks. Evaluation metrics will include FID and IS for generation, and MAE, PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS for restoration tasks. The experimental setup will use a generic UNet trained with L1 loss and a batch size of 1, with sampling steps ranging from 2 to 10 depending on the task. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of different coefficient schedules, sampling strategies, and the automatic objective selection algorithm. Additional qualitative experiments will include image inpainting and translation to demonstrate the generality of the framework.
4daf51de81e5cf3846482548196a8275369b27c4.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a dual diffusion process that independently models residual and noise diffusion, enabling a unified and interpretable approach for both image generation and restoration. The framework supports flexible, partially path-independent generation through independent coefficient schedules and decoupled sampling. It enables a generic UNet, trained with minimal supervision and small batch sizes, to achieve competitive or superior results compared to specialized state-of-the-art methods. The method also provides an automatic objective selection algorithm, allowing for adaptive task-specific optimization without retraining. The decoupled framework offers new insights into the roles of certainty and diversity in diffusion models and paves the way for multi-dimensional diffusion processes in image-to-image distribution transformation.

4ddd3c5fac6ec6e044a3b626ee3a6dc471499c78.title: Diffusion Bridge Implicit Models
4ddd3c5fac6ec6e044a3b626ee3a6dc471499c78.research_question: How can the sampling efficiency of denoising diffusion bridge models (DDBMs) be significantly improved for distribution translation tasks, such as image translation and restoration, without requiring additional training or compromising sample quality and diversity?
4ddd3c5fac6ec6e044a3b626ee3a6dc471499c78.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by generalizing DDBMs to a class of non-Markovian diffusion bridges defined on discretized timesteps, and introducing a deterministic or controlled-stochastic generative process, it is possible to achieve much faster sampling while maintaining or improving sample quality and diversity.
4ddd3c5fac6ec6e044a3b626ee3a6dc471499c78.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces Diffusion Bridge Implicit Models (DBIMs), which generalize the forward process of DDBMs to a family of non-Markovian diffusion bridges controlled by a variance parameter on discretized timesteps. The approach maintains the same marginal distributions and training objectives as DDBMs, enabling the reuse of pretrained models. Sampling is performed via a parameterized generative process where the variance parameter allows interpolation between fully deterministic and stochastic updates, with a booting noise introduced at the initial step to preserve diversity and avoid singularity. The deterministic case yields an ODE formulation that is theoretically equivalent to the probability flow ODE in DDBMs but is simpler and more efficient, enabling the use of high-order numerical solvers for further acceleration. The method supports both deterministic and stochastic sampling, with the variance parameter η controlling the level of stochasticity, and extends to high-order solvers by Taylor expansion and finite difference estimation of higher-order derivatives.
4ddd3c5fac6ec6e044a3b626ee3a6dc471499c78.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on image-to-image translation tasks using the Edges→Handbags (64×64) and DIODE-Outdoor (256×256) datasets, as well as image restoration (inpainting) on ImageNet (256×256) with a 128×128 center mask. Baselines will include GAN-based, diffusion-based, and bridge-based methods such as Pix2Pix, DDIB, SDEdit, I2SB, DDBM, and others. Evaluation metrics will comprise Frechet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS), Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity (LPIPS), Mean Square Error (MSE), and Classifier Accuracy (CA). The number of function evaluations (NFEs) will be varied to assess both sample efficiency and quality, with ablations on the variance parameter η and comparisons of first-order versus high-order solvers. Additional analyses will include generation diversity, reconstruction, and semantic interpolation capabilities.
4ddd3c5fac6ec6e044a3b626ee3a6dc471499c78.novelty_claims: The proposal claims the first accelerated, training-free sampling method for DDBMs, introducing a non-Markovian bridge framework that enables up to 25× faster sampling than existing DDBM samplers. The new ODE formulation is simpler and more efficient than previous probability flow ODEs, facilitating the development of high-order numerical solvers. The method preserves generation diversity via a booting noise mechanism and enables faithful encoding, reconstruction, and semantic interpolation, filling a gap in the efficient inference of diffusion bridge models. The approach is broadly applicable to pretrained DDBMs without retraining and demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on challenging high-resolution tasks.

4df52956b2801e4d216edc0ef0ea806e5ff2b59b.title: Discrete-state Continuous-time Diffusion for Graph Generation
4df52956b2801e4d216edc0ef0ea806e5ff2b59b.research_question: How can a generative model be developed to generate discrete graph-structured data while enabling flexible and efficient sampling, and preserving key invariance properties relevant to graphs?
4df52956b2801e4d216edc0ef0ea806e5ff2b59b.hypothesis: A discrete-state, continuous-time diffusion framework, grounded in continuous-time Markov chains and equipped with a neural network-based graph-to-graph backbone, will enable high-quality, efficient, and permutation-invariant graph generation, outperforming or matching existing state-of-the-art methods while providing greater sampling flexibility.
4df52956b2801e4d216edc0ef0ea806e5ff2b59b.proposed_method: A novel discrete-state continuous-time diffusion model for graph generation is proposed, leveraging continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC) dynamics to model the corruption and denoising processes of graphs. The forward process factorizes over nodes and edges, using shared or marginal rate matrices to ensure tractable computation and convergence to easy-to-sample reference distributions (e.g., uniform or empirical marginals). The reverse process is parameterized by a neural network, which predicts denoised node and edge types from noisy graphs at arbitrary continuous timepoints, using either a graph Transformer (GT) or a lightweight message-passing neural network (MPNN) as the backbone. Training is performed by minimizing a cross-entropy loss between the predicted and true node/edge types, with theoretical justification linking this loss to the approximation error in the reverse rate matrix. Sampling is implemented via a τ-leaping approximation, allowing the number of sampling steps to be flexibly chosen post-training, thus trading off quality and efficiency.
4df52956b2801e4d216edc0ef0ea806e5ff2b59b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both plain and molecular graph generation tasks, using datasets such as SBM, Planar, Community, QM9, MOSES, and GuacaMol. Evaluation metrics include relative squared Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) for degree, clustering, and orbit distributions, as well as Uniqueness, Novelty, Validity, Filter, FCD, SNN, Scaffold, and KL divergence, depending on the dataset. Baselines for comparison will include GraphRNN, GRAN, GG-GAN, MolGAN, SPECTRE, ConGress, DiGress, and other state-of-the-art graph generative models. Both the GT and MPNN backbones will be evaluated, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of reference distribution choice and sampling step count. Efficiency will be measured in terms of model parameters and training time. The experimental setup will include comprehensive hyperparameter tuning and reporting of mean and standard deviation over multiple runs.
4df52956b2801e4d216edc0ef0ea806e5ff2b59b.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first discrete-state continuous-time diffusion model for graph generation, combining the discrete nature of graph data with the flexible sampling advantages of continuous-time diffusion. The method provides a theoretically justified training objective directly tied to generation quality, supports permutation-invariant and equivariant properties crucial for graphs, and enables post-training adjustment of the sampling process for efficiency-quality trade-offs. Additionally, a new lightweight MPNN-based backbone is explored, offering a simpler and more efficient alternative to graph Transformers while maintaining competitive performance.

4e285bc0ed364a6ba6840e0426990dc455924f2e.title: Pro-KD: Progressive Distillation by Following the Footsteps of the Teacher
4e285bc0ed364a6ba6840e0426990dc455924f2e.research_question: How can knowledge distillation be improved to address the challenges of the capacity-gap and checkpoint-search problems, particularly when the best-performing teacher checkpoint is not optimal for student training, and when large teacher models do not necessarily yield better student models?
4e285bc0ed364a6ba6840e0426990dc455924f2e.hypothesis: A progressive knowledge distillation approach, in which the student model is trained by following the training trajectory of the teacher (rather than distilling solely from a fully trained teacher), combined with an adaptive temperature schedule, will yield superior student performance and mitigate both the capacity-gap and checkpoint-search problems.
4e285bc0ed364a6ba6840e0426990dc455924f2e.proposed_method: The proposed method, termed Progressive Knowledge Distillation (Pro-KD), introduces a two-phase training procedure. In Phase I, the teacher model is trained on the labeled data, and at each epoch, the student model is trained to mimic the current (not fully trained) teacher using a knowledge distillation loss with an adaptive temperature applied to the teacher's logits. The temperature starts high to provide a smoother signal and is decreased linearly as training progresses, making the student’s learning path more gradual. The number of student training epochs per teacher epoch can be adjusted, and the total student training epochs are distributed across the teacher’s training trajectory. In Phase II, after the student has learned from the teacher’s trajectory, it is further fine-tuned solely on ground-truth labels using the standard cross-entropy loss. This approach does not require training additional networks, is architecture-agnostic, and can be applied on top of existing KD variants.
4e285bc0ed364a6ba6840e0426990dc455924f2e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both image classification and natural language processing tasks. For image classification, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets will be used, with ResNet-8 as the student and ResNet-110 as the teacher, and comparisons will include TA-KD, Annealing-KD, RCO, regular KD, and training from scratch. For NLP, the GLUE benchmark and SQuAD 1.1/2.0 datasets will be employed, using BERT-based models (e.g., RoBERTa-large as teacher, DistilRoBERTa and BERT-Small as students). Baselines will include vanilla KD, TA-KD, RCO, Annealing-KD, and no-KD. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy for classification tasks and standard GLUE/SQuAD metrics (e.g., F1, EM). Hyperparameters such as maximum temperature, learning rate, and warmup epochs will be tuned per task, and ablation studies will assess the impact of the adaptive temperature schedule.
4e285bc0ed364a6ba6840e0426990dc455924f2e.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a progressive, trajectory-following distillation process that enables the student to learn from the evolving teacher, rather than a fixed, fully trained teacher. This mitigates the capacity-gap and checkpoint-search problems without requiring additional teacher-assistant networks or expensive checkpoint searches. The approach is simple, architecture-agnostic, and compatible with existing KD variants. Empirical results demonstrate consistent and significant improvements over state-of-the-art KD methods across multiple tasks and model architectures.

4e2905f3c9ec6c3625a415954e8232836a4ecb4f.title: A Fast, Well-Founded Approximation to the Empirical Neural Tangent Kernel
4e2905f3c9ec6c3625a415954e8232836a4ecb4f.research_question: How can the empirical neural tangent kernel (eNTK) for neural networks, especially those with multiple outputs and large datasets, be efficiently approximated in a theoretically justified manner to enable broader practical and theoretical applications?
4e2905f3c9ec6c3625a415954e8232836a4ecb4f.hypothesis: A specific approximation to the eNTK, referred to as the pseudo-NTK (pNTK) or 'sum of logits' approximation, converges to the true eNTK at initialization for wide neural networks, and can serve as an effective, computationally efficient surrogate for the eNTK in a variety of tasks.
4e2905f3c9ec6c3625a415954e8232836a4ecb4f.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces the pseudo-NTK (pNTK), a scalar-valued kernel computed by averaging the gradients of the output logits with respect to the network parameters, rather than constructing the full matrix-valued eNTK. Specifically, for a neural network with O output units, the pNTK between two inputs is defined as the outer product of the averaged gradients across all logits, reducing the kernel matrix size from NO×NO to N×N for N datapoints. Theoretical analysis will establish convergence rates of the pNTK to the eNTK under standard random initialization, showing that the approximation error decreases as network width increases. The method will also provide bounds on the difference in Frobenius norm and eigenvalues between the pNTK and eNTK, and will analyze the impact of this approximation on kernel regression and related learning tasks.
4e2905f3c9ec6c3625a415954e8232836a4ecb4f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a range of widely-used neural network architectures, including fully-connected networks (FCN), convolutional networks (ConvNet), ResNet18, and WideResNet, evaluated at various widths. The primary dataset for evaluation will be CIFAR-10, with additional experiments on CIFAR-100, Tiny ImageNet, and MNIST for specific applications. Baselines will include the full eNTK and existing 'single-logit' or infinite-width NTK approximations. Evaluation metrics will include the Frobenius norm difference between kernels, eigenvalue convergence, condition number, kernel regression prediction accuracy, and active learning performance. Experiments will also compare computational time and memory usage between the pNTK and eNTK, and will assess the performance of the approximation both at initialization and throughout training using stochastic gradient descent.
4e2905f3c9ec6c3625a415954e8232836a4ecb4f.novelty_claims: The proposal claims a rigorous theoretical justification for a widely used but previously unproven approximation to the eNTK, providing the first upper bounds on its convergence to the true eNTK for finite-width networks. The pNTK reduces both memory and computational complexity by orders of magnitude, enabling practical use of NTK-based methods on large datasets and multi-output tasks. The approach is validated both theoretically and empirically across diverse architectures and training regimes, and is shown to maintain or even improve performance in kernel regression and active learning tasks compared to the full eNTK. The work also provides new insights into the behavior of NTKs during training and offers resources to facilitate further research in the community.

4e2a3ddeaf5defb9318b43c364b9a9efe3847dcf.title: Compressed Context Memory For Online Language Model Interaction
4e2a3ddeaf5defb9318b43c364b9a9efe3847dcf.research_question: How can language models efficiently handle ever-growing context in online inference scenarios, such as conversation, personalization, and multi-task learning, while maintaining high performance and minimizing memory and computational overhead?
4e2a3ddeaf5defb9318b43c364b9a9efe3847dcf.hypothesis: A compressed context memory system that dynamically and recursively compresses attention key/value pairs using a lightweight, conditional LoRA adapter can enable language models to achieve performance comparable to full-context models while significantly reducing memory and computation requirements during online inference.
4e2a3ddeaf5defb9318b43c364b9a9efe3847dcf.proposed_method: A novel compressed context memory (CCM) framework will be developed to enable efficient online inference for Transformer language models. The method will introduce a specialized compression token (⟨COMP⟩) into the context, training the model to compress accumulated context into compact attention key/value representations at each time step. Memory update functions will be explored, including concatenation (scalable memory) and merging (fixed-size memory via weighted or arithmetic averages), to manage the compressed memory. A conditional LoRA adapter will be integrated, with trainable parameters affecting only the ⟨COMP⟩ tokens, ensuring that compression capabilities are learned without altering the full model weights. A parallelized training strategy will be implemented, allowing all time steps' compression and memory updates to be computed in a single forward pass, thus overcoming inefficiencies of recursive training.
4e2a3ddeaf5defb9318b43c364b9a9efe3847dcf.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three datasets representing different online inference scenarios: MetaICL (multi-task in-context learning), LaMP (personalization via user profiles), and DailyDialog (conversational modeling). The LLaMA-7B language model will be fine-tuned on each dataset, with both full-context and compressed-context variants evaluated. Baselines will include established compression techniques such as Compressive Transformer, Gisting, RMT, and AutoCompressor, as well as no-context and full-context approaches. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy for classification/recommendation tasks and perplexity for dialogue, along with memory usage (peak attention KV memory) and throughput (samples/sec, batch size). Additional analyses will assess the impact of conditional LoRA, compression overhead, and performance in streaming settings with unlimited context length.
4e2a3ddeaf5defb9318b43c364b9a9efe3847dcf.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a dynamic, online context compression mechanism for language models that operates directly on attention key/value pairs, enabling both scalable and fixed-size memory management. By leveraging a conditional LoRA adapter applied only to compression tokens, the method achieves efficient training and inference without full model fine-tuning. The parallelized training strategy allows for large-scale optimization without the recursive overhead of prior methods. The framework is claimed to achieve state-of-the-art memory efficiency and throughput, matching full-context performance with up to 5× smaller context memory, and outperforming existing baselines in both static and streaming online inference scenarios.

4e33c5756aa18d248cf50fef9382acda1e0f65da.title: VAST: A Vision-Audio-Subtitle-Text Omni-Modality Foundation Model and Dataset
4e33c5756aa18d248cf50fef9382acda1e0f65da.research_question: How can a unified foundation model be developed to effectively perceive, integrate, and understand visual, audio, subtitle, and textual modalities in videos, thereby advancing performance across a wide range of cross-modal video understanding tasks such as retrieval, captioning, and question answering?
4e33c5756aa18d248cf50fef9382acda1e0f65da.hypothesis: Integrating vision, audio, subtitle, and text modalities through large-scale pretraining on an automatically generated omni-modality video-caption dataset will significantly improve the model's ability to understand and generate multi-modal content, outperforming existing state-of-the-art models on diverse cross-modality benchmarks.
4e33c5756aa18d248cf50fef9382acda1e0f65da.proposed_method: A large-scale omni-modality video-caption dataset, VAST-27M, will be constructed by sampling 27 million open-domain video clips with complete vision, audio, and subtitle tracks. For each clip, dedicated vision and audio captioners, trained on high-quality image-text and audio-text corpora respectively, will generate multiple captions per modality. An off-the-shelf large language model (Vicuna-13b) will then integrate sampled vision and audio captions, raw subtitles, and instructional prompts into a single omni-modality caption per clip, ensuring comprehensive and human-like descriptions. Building upon this dataset, a unified foundation model (VAST) will be developed, employing a transformer-based architecture with separate vision (ViT), audio (BEATs), and text (BERT) encoders. The model will be trained end-to-end with three main objectives: omni-modality video-caption contrastive loss (OM-VCC), video-caption matching loss (OM-VCM), and caption generation loss (OM-VCG), all designed to enhance multi-modal alignment and generative capability. Modality grouping strategies will be incorporated to ensure robust performance even when certain modalities are missing at inference or adaptation time.
4e33c5756aa18d248cf50fef9382acda1e0f65da.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a wide range of public benchmarks covering vision-text, audio-text, and multi-modal video-text tasks, including COCO, Flickr30K, TGIF, MSVD, MSRVTT, Clothov1/v2, AudioCaps, YouCook2, VALOR-32K, VATEX, DiDeMo, TVC, MUSIC, and ANET. The model will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as GIT, VALUE, VALOR, BEiT-3, and BLIP-2, using evaluation metrics like Recall@1 for retrieval, CIDEr for captioning, and accuracy for question answering. Training will utilize a combination of VAST-27M, VALOR-1M, WavCaps, CC14M, and LAION-400M, with ablation studies performed to analyze the impact of different modality combinations and pretraining corpora. Implementation will leverage large-scale distributed training on 64 Tesla V100 GPUs, and both pretraining and fine-tuning configurations will be systematically varied to assess generalization and robustness.
4e33c5756aa18d248cf50fef9382acda1e0f65da.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first large-scale, automatically generated omni-modality video-caption dataset (VAST-27M) that comprehensively covers vision, audio, subtitle, and text modalities. The unified foundation model (VAST) is the first to support full omni-modality perception and understanding, enabling superior performance across vision-text, audio-text, and multi-modal video-text tasks. The approach leverages a novel automatic caption generation pipeline integrating single-modality captioners and a large language model, and employs modality grouping strategies to ensure adaptability to missing modalities. The method is expected to establish new state-of-the-art results on numerous cross-modality benchmarks, demonstrating the effectiveness and generalizability of omni-modality pretraining.

4e54d1731c089aa617880b916844e3912dbb538f.title: No-Regret Online Reinforcement Learning with Adversarial Losses and Transitions
4e54d1731c089aa617880b916844e3912dbb538f.research_question: Can online reinforcement learning algorithms be developed that achieve sublinear regret in environments with both adversarially chosen losses and adversarially changing transition functions, and can these algorithms adapt their performance guarantees based on the degree of adversarial corruption in the environment?
4e54d1731c089aa617880b916844e3912dbb538f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by introducing new algorithmic techniques and adaptive analysis, it is possible to design online reinforcement learning algorithms that achieve regret bounds which interpolate smoothly between the best-known results for fixed and fully adversarial transitions, and that these algorithms can further adapt to easier (stochastically constrained) environments for improved performance.
4e54d1731c089aa617880b916844e3912dbb538f.proposed_method: A novel online reinforcement learning framework will be developed that incorporates an enlarged confidence set for transition estimation, a log-barrier regularizer for improved stability, and an amortized bonus mechanism to control bias introduced by adversarial transitions. The method will first assume knowledge of the total corruption in transitions (CP), using a variant of Online Mirror Descent (OMD) with carefully designed loss estimators and occupancy measures. To remove the need for prior knowledge of CP, a black-box reduction will be constructed that transforms any algorithm with known-CP guarantees into one that operates without this knowledge, using a layered model selection approach (STABILISE) to ensure stability and adaptivity. Additionally, the algorithm will be refined to adapt to environments with stochastically constrained losses, employing Follow-the-Regularized-Leader (FTRL) with epoch-based restarts, optimistic transition functions, and adaptive log-barrier regularization to achieve gap-dependent regret bounds.
4e54d1731c089aa617880b916844e3912dbb538f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in episodic Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) with layered state spaces, where both the loss and transition functions can be chosen adversarially at each episode. The evaluation will involve comparing the proposed algorithms against state-of-the-art baselines for adversarial MDPs, including corruption-robust and non-stationary RL algorithms. Regret will be measured against the best fixed policy in hindsight, under both static and dynamic adversarial settings. Key metrics will include gap-independent and gap-dependent regret, as well as adaptivity to the degree of transition and loss corruption (CP and CL). Experiments will systematically vary the level of adversarial corruption to assess how regret scales with maliciousness, and will include both worst-case and stochastically constrained environments.
4e54d1731c089aa617880b916844e3912dbb538f.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first online RL algorithms that achieve regret bounds of order O(√T + CP) against adversarial losses and transitions, where the regret smoothly interpolates between the known results for fixed and fully adversarial transitions. The black-box reduction for handling unknown transition corruption is more general than prior model selection approaches, removing the need for stability in the base algorithm. The refined algorithm further achieves best-of-both-worlds guarantees, simultaneously adapting to the degree of adversarial corruption and to easier stochastic environments, with improved gap-dependent bounds and tighter dependence on problem parameters compared to previous work.

4e6244baf4236f4635e85f7dfb941a9a0a6c4a11.title: Building Normalizing Flows with Stochastic Interpolants
4e6244baf4236f4635e85f7dfb941a9a0a6c4a11.research_question: How can a continuous-time generative model be constructed to efficiently map between arbitrary base and target probability densities, enabling effective sampling and likelihood estimation, while improving computational efficiency and flexibility compared to conventional normalizing flows and diffusion models?
4e6244baf4236f4635e85f7dfb941a9a0a6c4a11.hypothesis: A generative modeling framework based on stochastic interpolants and direct velocity field estimation can enable efficient, scalable, and flexible normalizing flows that match or surpass the performance of conventional continuous-time flows and diffusion models, while reducing computational cost and providing explicit control over the transport path.
4e6244baf4236f4635e85f7dfb941a9a0a6c4a11.proposed_method: A new generative modeling framework is developed by constructing a continuous-time normalizing flow between a base and target probability density using a stochastic interpolant. The velocity field of the flow is inferred from the probability current of a time-dependent interpolant density, which is defined by sampling pairs from the base and target and passing them through a differentiable interpolant function. The velocity is estimated by minimizing a quadratic loss function, expressed as an expectation over the interpolant process, which is empirically tractable and avoids the need for backpropagation through ODE solvers. The method allows for optimization of the interpolant itself, enabling the minimization of path length in density space and paving the way for optimal transport maps. When the base is Gaussian, the velocity field can be related to the score of the interpolant density, providing a theoretical bridge to score-based diffusion models, but the approach operates directly at the ODE level for greater simplicity.
4e6244baf4236f4635e85f7dfb941a9a0a6c4a11.experiment_details: Experiments are proposed on both low-dimensional and high-dimensional datasets. For 2D density estimation, the method will be tested on toy datasets such as mixtures of Gaussians and checkerboard densities, visualizing the learned flows and comparing the generated samples to ground truth. For higher-dimensional tabular data, standard benchmarks such as POWER, GAS, HEPMASS, MINIBOONE, and BSDS300 will be used, with negative log-likelihood (NLL) as the primary evaluation metric, and comparisons made to baselines including MADE, RealNVP, Glow, FFJORD, OT-Flow, CPF, and NSP. For image generation, the method will be evaluated on CIFAR-10, ImageNet 32×32, and Oxford Flowers 128×128, using architectures such as U-Net, and reporting both NLL (in bits per dimension) and Frechet Inception Distance (FID) to assess sample quality. Training will utilize neural network parameterizations for the velocity field, optimized via stochastic gradient descent or Adam, and will employ time sampling reweighting strategies. The experimental setup will emphasize scalability, computational efficiency, and the ability to emit likelihoods.
4e6244baf4236f4635e85f7dfb941a9a0a6c4a11.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new framework for building normalizing flows using stochastic interpolants, enabling direct and efficient estimation of the velocity field via a quadratic loss that is empirically estimable. This method decouples the choice of transport path from the optimization objective, in contrast to conventional maximum likelihood-based flows, and allows for explicit control and optimization of the interpolant to achieve optimal transport. The framework provides a theoretical and practical connection to score-based diffusion models, but operates entirely at the ODE level, bypassing the need for SDEs and associated complexities. The method demonstrates scalability to high-dimensional data and large image resolutions previously unreachable by ab-initio ODE flows, and achieves competitive or superior performance to state-of-the-art continuous-time flows and diffusion models at a fraction of the computational cost.

4e6f765046cfd6e5acaf3732cf48938fa4085693.title: CODA-Prompt: COntinual Decomposed Attention-Based Prompting for Rehearsal-Free Continual Learning
4e6f765046cfd6e5acaf3732cf48938fa4085693.research_question: How can continual learning in computer vision be achieved without rehearsal of previous data, while mitigating catastrophic forgetting and improving adaptability to new tasks and distribution shifts?
4e6f765046cfd6e5acaf3732cf48938fa4085693.hypothesis: Learning a set of decomposed, attention-based prompt components that are assembled with input-conditioned weights to produce input-conditioned prompts, and optimizing these components end-to-end, will increase learning capacity, mitigate catastrophic forgetting, and improve new task accuracy in rehearsal-free continual learning settings.
4e6f765046cfd6e5acaf3732cf48938fa4085693.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that replaces traditional prompt pools with a decomposed prompt structure consisting of a weighted sum of learnable prompt components. For each input, a query is generated using a pre-trained vision transformer encoder, and this query is used to compute cosine similarities with a set of learnable keys, each associated with a prompt component. An attention mechanism is introduced, where each prompt component also has a learnable attention vector that modulates the query via element-wise multiplication before similarity calculation. The resulting similarity scores are used as weights to assemble the final prompt as a linear combination of components. This prompt is then inserted into multiple layers of a pre-trained vision transformer using prefix-tuning. The entire prompting mechanism, including prompt components, keys, and attention vectors, is optimized end-to-end with the task classification loss, augmented by an orthogonality regularization term to reduce interference between components. When a new task arrives, previously learned components are frozen and new components are added, allowing the model to expand its capacity without overwriting prior knowledge.
4e6f765046cfd6e5acaf3732cf48938fa4085693.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on established continual learning benchmarks, including ImageNet-R, CIFAR-100, and DomainNet, in the class-incremental setting. The proposed method will be compared against rehearsal-free baselines such as Learning without Forgetting (LwF), Learning to Prompt (L2P), and DualPrompt, as well as experience replay methods for context. Evaluation metrics will include average final accuracy across all tasks and average forgetting, with results averaged over multiple task orderings to ensure robustness. The method will also be evaluated on a dual-shift benchmark that introduces both semantic (class-incremental) and covariate (domain) shifts using ImageNet-R, where each task's training data includes different image styles. Hyperparameters, such as prompt length and number of components, will be tuned on validation data, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of key components such as attention, freezing, and orthogonality regularization.
4e6f765046cfd6e5acaf3732cf48938fa4085693.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a decomposed, attention-based prompt assembly mechanism for rehearsal-free continual learning, enabling end-to-end optimization of all prompting components. This method allows for scalable learning capacity by expanding the number of prompt components, rather than increasing prompt length, and inherently encourages knowledge reuse across tasks. The attention-based weighting scheme and orthogonality regularization further reduce interference and forgetting. The framework is parameter-efficient, memory-efficient, and privacy-preserving, as it does not require storage of previous training data. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on both standard and dual-shift continual learning benchmarks, outperforming existing prompting-based methods.

4e7f98ddbf849394ce8748d20146032f5e0ec903.title: DexDiffuser: Generating Dexterous Grasps With Diffusion Models
4e7f98ddbf849394ce8748d20146032f5e0ec903.research_question: How can dexterous robotic hands generate, evaluate, and refine high-quality grasp configurations for unknown objects using only partial point cloud observations?
4e7f98ddbf849394ce8748d20146032f5e0ec903.hypothesis: A conditional diffusion-based framework, when combined with a learned grasp evaluator and targeted refinement strategies, can generate and select dexterous grasps from partial point clouds that outperform existing state-of-the-art methods in both simulation and real-world scenarios.
4e7f98ddbf849394ce8748d20146032f5e0ec903.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that leverages a conditional diffusion model, termed DexSampler, to generate high-dimensional dexterous grasp candidates directly from partial object point clouds encoded with a Basis Point Set (BPS) representation. The DexSampler iteratively denoises randomly sampled grasps conditioned on the encoded observation, producing diverse and high-quality grasp poses and joint configurations. A separate neural grasp evaluator, DexEvaluator, predicts the probability of grasp success for each candidate using frequency-encoded grasp parameters and the same object encoding. Two grasp refinement strategies are introduced: Evaluator-Guided Diffusion (EGD), which steers the diffusion process toward more promising grasps using gradients from the evaluator, and Evaluator-based Sampling Refinement (ESR), which locally refines sampled grasps using a Metropolis-Hastings approach to maximize predicted grasp success. The entire pipeline is trained on a large-scale dataset of successful and unsuccessful grasps, enabling robust generalization.
4e7f98ddbf849394ce8748d20146032f5e0ec903.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both simulated and real-world setups using the 16-DoF Allegro Hand. Training and evaluation utilize a dataset of 1.7 million grasps (both successful and unsuccessful) generated with DexGraspNet across 5378 objects, with partial point clouds rendered from multiple views. The proposed method is benchmarked against state-of-the-art baselines including FFHNet (a VAE-based grasp generator) and UniDexGrasp (a contact map-based method), using both simulation (Isaacgym) and real robot hardware. Evaluation metrics include grasp success rate, diversity (entropy across joint configurations), and maximum penetration depth. Additional experiments assess the impact of the two refinement strategies and compare different point cloud encodings (BPS vs. PointNet++). Real-world tests involve grasping nine diverse objects in multiple orientations using noisy Kinect-captured point clouds, with success measured by the ability to pick and manipulate the object.
4e7f98ddbf849394ce8748d20146032f5e0ec903.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first conditional diffusion-based dexterous grasp generator for partial point clouds, capable of producing both SE(3) poses and full gripper configurations. The method incorporates a novel frequency-encoded grasp evaluator and two refinement strategies (EGD and ESR) specifically tailored for high-DoF hands. Unlike prior methods, the framework is validated extensively in both simulation and on real hardware, demonstrating significant improvements in grasp success rate, diversity, and adaptability to noisy, incomplete observations. The approach also enables direct grasp generation without requiring complete object models or shape completion, addressing a key limitation of existing techniques.

4e9a8141da2a8c603722b07d096109207f8e0b66.title: VBench: Comprehensive Benchmark Suite for Video Generative Models
4e9a8141da2a8c603722b07d096109207f8e0b66.research_question: How can a comprehensive, fine-grained, and human-aligned benchmark be developed to objectively evaluate the multifaceted quality of video generative models across diverse ability dimensions and content categories?
