4e9a8141da2a8c603722b07d096109207f8e0b66.hypothesis: A hierarchical, multi-dimensional evaluation framework that decomposes video generation quality into specific, disentangled dimensions, each with tailored prompts and objective evaluation methods, will provide more accurate, insightful, and human-aligned assessments of video generative models compared to existing single-metric approaches.
4e9a8141da2a8c603722b07d096109207f8e0b66.proposed_method: A benchmark suite will be constructed that systematically decomposes 'video generation quality' into 16 distinct, hierarchical, and disentangled evaluation dimensions, covering both video quality (e.g., temporal consistency, frame-wise quality) and video-condition consistency (e.g., semantic and style alignment with prompts). For each dimension, a dedicated prompt suite of approximately 100 carefully curated test cases will be designed to probe specific model abilities, spanning eight major content categories such as animal, human, and scenery. Each evaluation dimension will be paired with a specialized, automated evaluation pipeline leveraging state-of-the-art models (e.g., DINO for subject consistency, CLIP for background and style, GRiT for object class and color, UMT for human action, Tag2Text for scene, and RAFT for dynamic degree). Human preference annotation will be conducted for each dimension by collecting pairwise video comparisons from multiple models, with annotators instructed to focus on a single evaluation aspect per task. The resulting human annotation dataset will be used both to validate the alignment of automated metrics with human perception and to instruction-tune visual-language models for improved evaluative alignment.
4e9a8141da2a8c603722b07d096109207f8e0b66.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by evaluating several state-of-the-art text-to-video generative models (e.g., LaVie, ModelScope, VideoCrafter, CogVideo) on the proposed benchmark. For each dimension and content category, videos will be generated using the curated prompt suites, and the evaluation pipelines will compute quantitative scores. Baselines will include empirical maximum and minimum scores (estimated from real video datasets and noise clips, respectively), as well as average scores from the WebVid-10M dataset to contextualize model performance. Human preference annotations will be collected at scale for each dimension, involving pairwise comparisons of generated videos, and the correlation between automated metrics and human judgments will be statistically analyzed (e.g., using Spearman's correlation). Additional experiments will compare video generation models to image generation models (e.g., Stable Diffusion variants) on frame-wise dimensions, and performance will be analyzed across content categories to reveal strengths, weaknesses, and compositionality gaps.
4e9a8141da2a8c603722b07d096109207f8e0b66.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces the first comprehensive, hierarchical, and fine-grained evaluation suite for video generative models, decomposing quality into 16 disentangled dimensions with tailored prompts and automated evaluation pipelines. It uniquely incorporates large-scale, per-dimension human preference annotation to validate and instruction-tune evaluation methods for human alignment. The framework enables multi-dimensional, multi-categorical analysis, uncovering nuanced model strengths, weaknesses, and trade-offs, and provides actionable insights for future model development and dataset curation. The benchmark, including all prompts, evaluation methods, generated videos, and human annotations, is designed for open-sourcing to drive forward the field of video generation evaluation.

4e9e30f4702f64af5aacbb5791172c5b37510dc3.title: OpenOOD: Benchmarking Generalized Out-of-Distribution Detection
4e9e30f4702f64af5aacbb5791172c5b37510dc3.research_question: How can a unified, comprehensive, and rigorously designed benchmark be established to enable fair and systematic evaluation of generalized out-of-distribution (OOD) detection methods, including those from related fields such as anomaly detection, open set recognition, and model uncertainty?
4e9e30f4702f64af5aacbb5791172c5b37510dc3.hypothesis: A unified benchmarking framework that integrates diverse OOD detection tasks, datasets, and evaluation protocols will enable more accurate, fair, and insightful comparison of existing and future OOD detection methods, revealing strengths and weaknesses across approaches and guiding the development of more robust and generalizable OOD detectors.
4e9e30f4702f64af5aacbb5791172c5b37510dc3.proposed_method: A unified codebase and benchmarking suite, named OpenOOD, will be developed to systematically evaluate OOD detection methods under a generalized OOD detection framework. This suite will integrate over 30 representative methods spanning classification-based, density-based, distance-based, reconstruction-based, and model uncertainty/data augmentation approaches. The benchmark will encompass 9 diverse tasks, including anomaly detection, open set recognition, and OOD detection, each with carefully curated datasets and splits to prevent label leakage and ensure rigorous evaluation. The codebase will provide standardized training and evaluation pipelines, unified hyperparameter search protocols, and support for various neural architectures (e.g., LeNet, ResNet-18, ResNet-50) to ensure comparability. Both post-hoc and training-based methods, as well as those requiring external data, will be supported, and the suite will facilitate plug-and-play integration of new methods for extensibility.
4e9e30f4702f64af5aacbb5791172c5b37510dc3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 9 benchmarks: 1 for anomaly detection (MVTec-AD), 4 for open set recognition (MNIST-6/4, CIFAR-6/4, CIFAR-50/50, TinyImageNet-20/180), and 4 for OOD detection (MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet), with both near-OOD and far-OOD test sets designed for detailed analysis. Each method will be evaluated using standardized architectures (LeNet for MNIST, ResNet-18 for CIFAR/TinyImageNet, ResNet-50 for ImageNet) and common hyperparameters (SGD optimizer, learning rate 0.1, momentum 0.9, weight decay 0.0005, 100 epochs). Evaluation metrics will include AUROC, FPR@95, and AUPR, with AUROC as the main metric. Baseline comparisons will span post-hoc, training-based, and data augmentation approaches, as well as methods leveraging external data. Hyperparameter tuning will be performed using a fixed set of candidate values and validation splits, and all experiments will be run under unified computational settings to ensure fairness.
4e9e30f4702f64af5aacbb5791172c5b37510dc3.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark provides the first unified, comprehensive, and rigorously curated evaluation suite for generalized OOD detection, integrating tasks and methods from anomaly detection, open set recognition, OOD detection, and model uncertainty. It supports fair and reproducible comparison of 35+ methods across 9 benchmarks, with careful dataset curation to prevent label leakage and standardized evaluation protocols. The codebase is open-source, extensible, and designed to accommodate new methods and benchmarks, enabling the community to advance OOD detection research systematically. Insights from comprehensive experiments highlight the effectiveness of simple preprocessing and post-hoc methods, question the necessity of extra data, and reveal trends in method performance across diverse settings.

4eb3d1b4d617d010a4a5f67e345a648963bcdd84.title: Breaking the Curse of Multiagents in a Large State Space: RL in Markov Games with Independent Linear Function Approximation
4eb3d1b4d617d010a4a5f67e345a648963bcdd84.research_question: How can efficient multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithms be developed for Markov games with large state spaces and many agents, using independent function approximation, such that the curse of multiagents and large state-action spaces is overcome?
4eb3d1b4d617d010a4a5f67e345a648963bcdd84.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by employing independent linear function approximation for each agent, and by leveraging novel algorithmic techniques such as policy replay and the separation of exploration from equilibrium learning, it is possible to design multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithms whose sample complexity scales only polynomially with each agent’s own function class complexity, thereby breaking the curse of multiagents.
4eb3d1b4d617d010a4a5f67e345a648963bcdd84.proposed_method: A new model, termed the independent linear Markov game, will be introduced, allowing each agent to utilize its own independent linear function approximation for state-action value functions, marginalized over other agents' policies. The proposed methodology involves designing algorithms for learning Markov coarse correlated equilibria (CCE) and Markov correlated equilibria (CE) by employing a policy replay mechanism to address non-stationarity arising from both multi-agent interactions and function approximation. The approach separates the process of learning equilibria from exploration, enabling the use of full-information no-regret learning oracles, which are less demanding than adversarial bandit oracles. For Markov potential games, an iterative best-response algorithm will be developed to learn pure Markov Nash equilibria, leveraging reductions to linear MDPs. The algorithms will be robust to agnostic model misspecification and will be applicable to important special cases such as tabular Markov games and congestion games.
4eb3d1b4d617d010a4a5f67e345a648963bcdd84.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multi-agent Markov games with both tabular and function approximation settings, including general-sum and potential games. The evaluation will utilize standard benchmarks such as tabular Markov games and congestion games, with datasets generated according to the defined Markov game dynamics. Baselines will include state-of-the-art MARL algorithms that use global function approximation and those that operate in the tabular setting. Evaluation metrics will focus on sample complexity (number of environment interactions required to achieve a desired accuracy ǫ), accuracy in approximating Markov CCE/CE/NE, and computational efficiency. The experimental setup will include ablation studies on the effect of policy replay and the separation of exploration and learning, as well as comparisons of sample complexity scaling with respect to the number of agents and the size of the function class.
4eb3d1b4d617d010a4a5f67e345a648963bcdd84.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first provably efficient MARL algorithms for Markov games with independent linear function approximation, breaking the curse of multiagents by achieving sample complexity that depends only polynomially on each agent’s function class complexity. The policy replay mechanism is novel in its application to both multi-agent non-stationarity and function approximation, and the separation of exploration from equilibrium learning enables the use of full-information no-regret oracles. The approach also yields the first efficient algorithms for learning Markov CE in general-sum games and for learning Nash equilibria in independent linear Markov potential games, with improved sample complexity for tabular settings. The algorithms are robust to agnostic model misspecification and subsume important special cases such as congestion games.

4ed177f04136d19a7d3ba8f25318788c45ab4186.title: Minimax Optimal Algorithms for Fixed-Budget Best Arm Identification
4ed177f04136d19a7d3ba8f25318788c45ab4186.research_question: What is the minimax optimal rate for the probability of error in fixed-budget best arm identification, and can computationally efficient algorithms be developed to achieve or closely approximate this rate across all problem instances?
4ed177f04136d19a7d3ba8f25318788c45ab4186.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the minimax optimal rate for the probability of error in fixed-budget best arm identification can be tightly characterized, and that practical algorithms—potentially leveraging neural networks—can be designed to approach or match this rate, even if the exact minimax-optimal algorithm is computationally infeasible.
4ed177f04136d19a7d3ba8f25318788c45ab4186.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves first deriving tight lower bounds on the probability of error (PoE) in fixed-budget best arm identification by formulating and solving minimax optimization problems over allocation strategies and empirical distributions. Two rates, Rgo and Rgo_infty, are introduced, corresponding to different levels of oracle knowledge and trackability. To approach these rates, two algorithms are proposed: (1) Rgo-tracking, which adaptively tracks the optimal allocation based on the current empirical distribution, and is implemented efficiently using a neural network to approximate the optimal allocation mapping; and (2) Delayed Optimal Tracking (DOT), which divides the sampling budget into batches and uses delayed empirical means to guide allocation, theoretically achieving the minimax rate but at high computational cost. The neural network-based Rgo-tracking algorithm is trained via mini-batch gradient descent to minimize the worst-case PoE exponent over sampled true and empirical means, using a softmax output to ensure valid allocation probabilities.
4ed177f04136d19a7d3ba8f25318788c45ab4186.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic Bernoulli bandit problems with K=3 arms and mean parameters in [0,1], using several representative parameter settings. The total number of rounds T will be fixed (e.g., T=2000), and each experiment will be repeated a large number of times (e.g., 10^5 trials) to estimate the probability of error. The proposed neural network-based Rgo-tracking algorithm (TNN) will be compared against established baselines such as Uniform sampling and Successive Rejects (SR). Evaluation metrics will include the probability of error (PoE) over time and the tracking error between the ideal and actual allocation. Neural networks will be trained with four layers, ReLU activations, skip connections, and AdamW optimization, with hyperparameters specified for learning rate and weight decay. The complexity measure H(P) will be set as the sum of inverse squared gaps between the best and other arms.
4ed177f04136d19a7d3ba8f25318788c45ab4186.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a tight characterization of the minimax optimal rate for the probability of error in fixed-budget best arm identification, providing both a theoretical rate (Rgo_infty) and a computationally feasible approximation (Rgo-tracking via neural networks). The use of neural networks to approximate the optimal allocation mapping for best arm identification is novel and enables practical implementation of near-optimal algorithms. The DOT algorithm is the first to asymptotically achieve the exact minimax rate, albeit with high computational complexity. The approach provides new insights into the gap between theoretically optimal and practical algorithms, and offers a framework for learning allocation strategies in complex bandit settings.

4edd2d2770729380eda23826af1b78298b334a23.title: Understanding and Improving Visual Prompting: A Label-Mapping Perspective
4edd2d2770729380eda23826af1b78298b334a23.research_question: How does the quality and design of label mapping (LM) affect the effectiveness and interpretability of visual prompting (VP) for adapting pre-trained vision and vision-language models to downstream tasks, and how can this relationship be exploited to improve target task accuracy?
4edd2d2770729380eda23826af1b78298b334a23.hypothesis: A more precise and explainable label mapping, co-designed and iteratively optimized with visual prompting, will consistently improve the accuracy and interpretability of visual prompting for a wide range of downstream tasks and across both vision-only and vision-language models.
4edd2d2770729380eda23826af1b78298b334a23.proposed_method: A novel framework, Iterative Label Mapping-based Visual Prompting (ILM-VP), is proposed to jointly optimize the input prompt and the label mapping between source and target classes. The method formulates VP as a bi-level optimization problem, where the upper-level task seeks the optimal input perturbation (prompt) to maximize target task accuracy, and the lower-level task dynamically updates the label mapping based on the current prompt. Alternating optimization is employed: at each iteration, the label mapping is updated to maximize mapping precision and explanation given the current prompt, then the prompt is updated via gradient-based optimization using the current mapping. The process continues until convergence, resulting in a prompt and mapping that are mutually adapted for optimal transfer. The framework is extended to vision-language models (e.g., CLIP) by using iterative label mapping to select optimal text prompt templates for each target class, enabling improved multimodal prompt learning.
4edd2d2770729380eda23826af1b78298b334a23.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of 13 diverse target image classification datasets, including Flowers102, DTD, UCF101, Food101, GTSRB, SVHN, EuroSAT, OxfordPets, StanfordCars, SUN397, CIFAR10/100, and ABIDE, using fixed pre-trained source models such as ResNet-18, ResNet-50 (ImageNet-1K), and ResNeXt-101-32x8d (Instagram). Baselines will include random label mapping-based VP (RLM-VP), frequency-based label mapping VP (FLM-VP), and standard model fine-tuning methods (linear probing and full fine-tuning). Evaluation metrics will focus on target task accuracy, parameter efficiency, and interpretability, with explanation quality assessed via Explanation-by-Example (EBE). Additional experiments will extend the method to CLIP-based VP, comparing against fixed text prompt baselines and evaluating on datasets such as Flowers102, DTD, UCF101, Food101, SVHN, EuroSAT, StanfordCars, SUN397, CIFAR10, ImageNet-R, and ImageNet-Sketch. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of dataset scale, label space size, and iterative mapping dynamics.
4edd2d2770729380eda23826af1b78298b334a23.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first bi-level optimization framework that jointly and iteratively optimizes label mapping and visual prompting, closing the loop between mapping and prompt generation. It provides a principled approach to improve both the accuracy and interpretability of VP by explicitly modeling and optimizing the interaction between label mapping and prompt learning. The method extends to vision-language models by leveraging iterative label mapping for text prompt selection, demonstrating significant accuracy gains and enhanced semantic alignment. Empirical results are expected to show substantial improvements over existing VP baselines across a wide range of datasets and models, with additional benefits in explanation quality and parameter efficiency.

4ee8c12311f05e5b4ae82c6f83cf067677d69e5c.title: Score-based Data Assimilation
4ee8c12311f05e5b4ae82c6f83cf067677d69e5c.research_question: How can accurate and efficient data assimilation be achieved for high-dimensional, complex, and potentially long-horizon stochastic dynamical systems, particularly when the transition dynamics are intractable or the observation model is variable or unknown at training time?
4ee8c12311f05e5b4ae82c6f83cf067677d69e5c.hypothesis: Score-based generative models, when trained on short trajectory segments and equipped with a novel likelihood score approximation, can provide accurate, scalable, and flexible posterior inference over whole state trajectories in complex dynamical systems, even under zero-shot observation scenarios.
4ee8c12311f05e5b4ae82c6f83cf067677d69e5c.proposed_method: A new data assimilation framework is proposed that leverages score-based generative models to approximate the posterior distribution over state trajectories. The method decomposes the global trajectory score into a series of local scores using the Markovian structure of dynamical systems, enabling the training of local score networks on short trajectory segments rather than full trajectories. The observation model is decoupled from the training process and incorporated only at inference, allowing for zero-shot adaptation to new observation scenarios. For inference, the method combines a novel, theoretically motivated likelihood score approximation—based on an extended Kalman filter-inspired covariance—with predictor-corrector sampling using discretized reverse SDEs and Langevin Monte Carlo steps to ensure sample quality and stability.
4ee8c12311f05e5b4ae82c6f83cf067677d69e5c.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on two benchmark chaotic dynamical systems: the low-dimensional Lorenz 1963 system and the high-dimensional Kolmogorov flow (2D turbulent fluid) system. For the Lorenz system, 1024 independent trajectories are generated and split into training, validation, and evaluation sets, with various observation processes (low/high frequency, low/high noise) and comparisons against the bootstrap particle filter as a ground-truth baseline. For Kolmogorov flow, trajectories are generated using a high-resolution CFD solver, with states coarsened to 64x64 grids and observations subsampled and noise-perturbed. The method is evaluated under different observation scenarios, including sparse, noisy, and partial observations, and compared to alternative likelihood score approximations. Evaluation metrics include expected log-prior, expected log-likelihood, Wasserstein distance to the ground-truth posterior, and qualitative assessment of trajectory realism and consistency with physical models.
4ee8c12311f05e5b4ae82c6f83cf067677d69e5c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled decomposition of the global trajectory score into local scores, enabling scalable training and inference for arbitrarily long Markov chains using only short trajectory segments. A novel, stable likelihood score approximation is developed for Gaussian (linear or non-linear) observation models, improving posterior inference accuracy without the need for ad-hoc stability tricks. The framework allows for non-autoregressive, simultaneous generation of all trajectory states and supports zero-shot adaptation to new observation processes. These innovations collectively enable accurate, efficient, and flexible data assimilation in regimes where traditional methods are computationally prohibitive or inapplicable.

4f02c28bfdf43a8dd474cb8240ec9819f50ab00c.title: A Trichotomy for Transductive Online Learning
4f02c28bfdf43a8dd474cb8240ec9819f50ab00c.research_question: What are the fundamental limits on the number of mistakes that can be made by a learner in the transductive online learning setting, and how are these limits determined by combinatorial parameters of the hypothesis class such as VC dimension and Littlestone dimension? How do these limits extend to multiclass and agnostic settings?
4f02c28bfdf43a8dd474cb8240ec9819f50ab00c.hypothesis: The minimal number of mistakes in transductive online learning is determined by a trichotomy based on the VC dimension and Littlestone dimension of the hypothesis class, and this structure generalizes to multiclass and agnostic settings.
4f02c28bfdf43a8dd474cb8240ec9819f50ab00c.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical analysis will be conducted of the transductive online learning model, where the adversary fixes a sequence of instances in advance and the learner seeks to minimize mistakes under realizability constraints. The approach will involve deriving upper and lower bounds on the number of mistakes as a function of the VC dimension, Littlestone dimension, and threshold dimension of the hypothesis class. The methodology will include constructing adversarial strategies based on combinatorial structures such as Littlestone trees and threshold-shattered sets, and analyzing the learner's performance using majority-vote and halving algorithms. The analysis will be extended to the multiclass setting by replacing VC dimension with Natarajan dimension and generalizing the Littlestone dimension, and to the agnostic setting by considering regret minimization in games with incomplete information.
4f02c28bfdf43a8dd474cb8240ec9819f50ab00c.experiment_details: Theoretical results will be validated through rigorous proofs, leveraging combinatorial constructions and information-theoretic arguments. The analysis will consider all hypothesis classes with specified VC and Littlestone dimensions, and will provide tight bounds for each regime of the trichotomy. For the multiclass setting, the Natarajan dimension will be used to characterize the mistake bounds, and Ramsey-theoretic arguments will be employed. In the agnostic setting, regret bounds will be established and compared to known results in the standard online learning framework. No empirical datasets or computational experiments are involved, as the focus is on mathematical characterization and proof.
4f02c28bfdf43a8dd474cb8240ec9819f50ab00c.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a precise trichotomy for the minimal number of mistakes in transductive online learning, showing that the rate can only be n, Θ(log(n)), or Θ(1), depending on the VC and Littlestone dimensions. It provides improved lower bounds for the constant in the Θ(1) regime, strengthening previous results by showing an Ω(log(d)) lower bound where d is the Littlestone dimension. The framework is extended to multiclass classification using the Natarajan dimension, and to the agnostic setting with new regret bounds. The work also demonstrates that the DS dimension does not characterize multiclass transductive online learning, even for finite label sets, highlighting a key distinction from PAC learning.

4f03f8883838bccd638c7054f5aebf7a550176bf.title: Between Stochastic and Adversarial Online Convex Optimization: Improved Regret Bounds via Smoothness
4f03f8883838bccd638c7054f5aebf7a550176bf.research_question: How can regret bounds for online convex optimization be improved in settings that interpolate between fully stochastic (i.i.d.) and fully adversarial data, and what role does the smoothness of expected losses play in achieving these improvements?
4f03f8883838bccd638c7054f5aebf7a550176bf.hypothesis: By exploiting the smoothness of expected loss functions, it is possible to derive regret bounds for online convex optimization that depend on the variance of the gradients rather than the maximum gradient norm, and that interpolate smoothly between the stochastic and adversarial regimes, providing tight guarantees for intermediate cases.
4f03f8883838bccd638c7054f5aebf7a550176bf.proposed_method: A novel analysis of optimistic online algorithms, specifically Optimistic Follow-the-Regularized-Leader (OFTRL) and Optimistic Follow-the-Leader (OFTL), will be developed to leverage the smoothness of the expected loss functions. The proposed approach introduces a stochastically extended adversarial model, where in each round, nature selects a possibly adversarially varying distribution from which the loss is sampled. The regret analysis will introduce two key parameters: cumulative stochastic variance and cumulative adversarial variation, quantifying the interpolation between i.i.d. and adversarial settings. Adaptive step-size tuning and optimism in the algorithm will be used, along with a negative Bregman divergence term in the analysis to exploit smoothness and achieve improved regret bounds.
4f03f8883838bccd638c7054f5aebf7a550176bf.experiment_details: Theoretical experiments will be conducted by deriving upper and lower regret bounds under various settings, including fully adversarial, fully stochastic (i.i.d.), adversarially corrupted stochastic, and random order models. Theoretical datasets are modeled as sequences of convex functions over a bounded convex set, with loss distributions chosen according to the proposed stochastically extended adversarial protocol. Baselines for comparison include standard OCO regret bounds in adversarial and stochastic cases, as well as previous results for expert and bandit settings. Evaluation metrics include expected regret and its dependence on gradient variance, adversarial variation, and smoothness constants. Tightness of the bounds will be demonstrated via matching lower bounds.
4f03f8883838bccd638c7054f5aebf7a550176bf.novelty_claims: The proposed framework unifies and interpolates between stochastic and adversarial online convex optimization, providing regret bounds that depend on the variance of gradients for general convex and smooth loss functions, not just linear ones. The analysis allows for adversarially varying distributions, including adversarially corrupted rounds and random order models, and quantifies the impact of both stochasticity and adversarial variation. The regret bounds are shown to be tight in all regimes, and the approach generalizes and improves upon prior results by leveraging smoothness to replace dependence on the maximum gradient norm with variance-based terms. The method also answers open questions in the literature regarding regret under adversarial corruptions and random order models.

4f043a7311c48afd7a37cd510c4e6fc534b13bba.title: A Practical and Optimal First-Order Method for Large-Scale Convex Quadratic Programming
4f043a7311c48afd7a37cd510c4e6fc534b13bba.research_question: How can large-scale convex quadratic programming problems be solved efficiently using first-order methods that are scalable, achieve optimal convergence rates, and are suitable for modern computational architectures such as GPUs and distributed systems?
4f043a7311c48afd7a37cd510c4e6fc534b13bba.hypothesis: A restarted accelerated primal-dual hybrid gradient (rAPDHG) method, which combines acceleration and restart strategies, can achieve optimal linear convergence for convex quadratic programming, matching information-theoretical lower bounds for first-order primal-dual algorithms, and can outperform existing first-order and ADMM-based solvers on large-scale instances.
4f043a7311c48afd7a37cd510c4e6fc534b13bba.proposed_method: A new matrix-free first-order method, termed restarted accelerated primal-dual hybrid gradient (rAPDHG), is developed for convex quadratic programming. The approach reformulates the QP as a saddle-point problem and applies a two-loop scheme: an inner loop running an accelerated primal-dual hybrid gradient (PDHG) update, and an outer loop that restarts from the averaged iterates after a fixed number of inner iterations. The method leverages both acceleration (momentum) and restart mechanisms to exploit the problem structure, ensuring optimal convergence rates. Step-size parameters and restart frequency are carefully chosen based on problem data (e.g., norms of Q and A matrices) and a sharpness constant derived from the KKT system. Theoretical analysis connects the linear convergence rate to the quadratic growth of a smoothed duality gap, providing guarantees even in the absence of strong convexity.
4f043a7311c48afd7a37cd510c4e6fc534b13bba.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using both standard QP benchmark datasets and large-scale synthetic QP instances to evaluate the effectiveness of rAPDHG. The proposed solver, implemented as PDQP.jl in Julia, will be benchmarked against state-of-the-art open-source solvers such as SCS and OSQP, as well as against vanilla PDHG, restarted PDHG (without acceleration), and accelerated PDHG (without restarting). Both CPU and GPU implementations will be tested to assess scalability and performance on modern hardware. Evaluation metrics will include convergence rate, solution accuracy, and computational efficiency (runtime and memory usage). Extensive numerical studies will be performed to demonstrate the algorithm's superiority, particularly for high-accuracy and large-scale problem settings.
4f043a7311c48afd7a37cd510c4e6fc534b13bba.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first matrix-free first-order algorithm for convex QP that achieves optimal linear convergence rates, matching information-theoretical lower bounds for a broad class of primal-dual methods. The approach introduces a novel combination of acceleration and restart mechanisms tailored for QP, with theoretical guarantees linked to the sharpness of the KKT system. A practical open-source solver with both CPU and GPU support is developed, demonstrating strong empirical performance and scalability beyond existing first-order and ADMM-based solvers.

4f0bfeadd39e64456d15d400fda8ecc2197c3265.title: Direct Preference-based Policy Optimization without Reward Modeling
4f0bfeadd39e64456d15d400fda8ecc2197c3265.research_question: How can reinforcement learning agents be optimized directly from preference data, without relying on explicit reward modeling, especially in settings where reward functions are difficult to specify or human feedback is the primary supervision?
4f0bfeadd39e64456d15d400fda8ecc2197c3265.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that directly optimizing policies using preference information, formulated through a contrastive learning framework and enhanced with regularization techniques, can achieve performance competitive with or superior to existing preference-based RL methods that rely on reward modeling, particularly in high-dimensional and complex tasks.
4f0bfeadd39e64456d15d400fda8ecc2197c3265.proposed_method: A novel preference-based reinforcement learning algorithm is proposed that eliminates the need for explicit reward modeling. The method constructs a policy scoring metric based on contrastive learning principles, where the policy is encouraged to align more closely with preferred trajectory segments and distance itself from less preferred ones. The core of the approach is a policy-segment distance metric, computed as the expected L2 distance between the policy's action distribution and the actions in a trajectory segment, aggregated over the segment. This metric is incorporated into a contrastive score, which is regularized to penalize large deviations from preferred behaviors and to ensure smoothness in preference predictions across overlapping trajectory segments. The policy is optimized by maximizing this score, using both labeled preference data and a larger pool of unlabeled trajectories, with a preference predictor trained via cross-entropy loss and smoothness regularization to label new segment pairs.
4f0bfeadd39e64456d15d400fda8ecc2197c3265.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in the offline RL setting using standard benchmarks such as D4RL Gym (e.g., halfcheetah, hopper, walker2d), Adroit pen, and Kitchen tasks. Human-labeled preference datasets, ranging from 100 to 500 samples per task, will be used alongside large unlabeled datasets. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art preference-based RL methods (e.g., PreferenceTransformer with IQL and CQL for policy optimization), as well as reward-based RL methods using ground-truth rewards. Evaluation metrics will include normalized average return, variance across seeds, and ablation studies on regularization parameters. Additional experiments will assess scalability to high-dimensional tasks, robustness to dataset size, and applicability to fine-tuning large language models with human preference data.
4f0bfeadd39e64456d15d400fda8ecc2197c3265.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a direct policy optimization framework for preference-based RL that bypasses reward modeling entirely, leveraging a contrastive learning objective tailored to preference data. Key innovations include a policy-segment distance metric, a contrastive score function with regularization for conservativeness and smoothness, and a method for utilizing both labeled and unlabeled data. The method demonstrates superior scalability to high-dimensional control tasks, improved data efficiency, and applicability to large language model fine-tuning, outperforming or matching state-of-the-art baselines in empirical evaluations.

4f16e5f4793cdf2a184ae9259ea0f0c04b889eb4.title: Principled Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback from Pairwise or K-wise Comparisons
4f16e5f4793cdf2a184ae9259ea0f0c04b889eb4.research_question: How can reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF) be theoretically grounded and improved when human feedback is provided in the form of pairwise or K-wise comparisons, and what are the implications for reward model learning and policy optimization in both contextual bandit and Markov Decision Process (MDP) settings?
4f16e5f4793cdf2a184ae9259ea0f0c04b889eb4.hypothesis: Introducing a pessimistic maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) in the reward learning stage of RLHF, as opposed to standard MLE, will yield policies with improved sub-optimality bounds and sample efficiency, especially under certain coverage and regularity conditions. Additionally, directly modeling K-wise comparisons using the Plackett-Luce model will provide more efficient estimators than splitting K-wise data into pairwise comparisons.
4f16e5f4793cdf2a184ae9259ea0f0c04b889eb4.proposed_method: A principled theoretical framework for RLHF will be developed, focusing on reward learning from human feedback in the form of pairwise and K-wise comparisons. The reward function will be assumed to be linear in known features, and human preferences will be modeled using the Bradley-Terry-Luce (BTL) model for pairwise and the Plackett-Luce (PL) model for K-wise comparisons. Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) will be analyzed for learning the reward model, and a pessimistic variant of MLE will be introduced to account for limited data coverage by discounting less-represented actions. The pessimistic MLE will be implemented by constructing a confidence set around the estimated parameters and optimizing the policy with respect to the lower confidence bound of the expected reward. Both direct K-wise MLE and a splitting approach (converting K-wise to pairwise comparisons) will be studied, with theoretical analysis of their convergence and efficiency. The framework will be extended to MDPs and max-entropy inverse reinforcement learning (IRL), providing sample complexity guarantees and unifying these approaches with RLHF.
4f16e5f4793cdf2a184ae9259ea0f0c04b889eb4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on simulated datasets designed to mimic RLHF scenarios, including both contextual bandit and MDP settings. The datasets will consist of state-action pairs with rewards parameterized by known feature functions, and human feedback will be simulated according to the BTL and PL models. Baseline methods will include standard MLE, pessimistic MLE, and the splitting approach for K-wise comparisons. Evaluation metrics will focus on estimation error (in a semi-norm induced by the data covariance) and policy sub-optimality (performance gap between the learned and optimal policies). The experimental setup will test the convergence rates, sample complexity, and asymptotic efficiency of the proposed estimators under varying coverage and regularity conditions.
4f16e5f4793cdf2a184ae9259ea0f0c04b889eb4.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretical framework for RLHF that rigorously analyzes reward model learning from pairwise and K-wise human comparisons, providing the first high-probability sample complexity bounds for both RLHF and max-entropy IRL with function approximation. It establishes the failure modes of standard MLE in policy optimization and demonstrates that pessimistic MLE achieves minimax-optimal sub-optimality rates under reasonable assumptions. The analysis also reveals that direct K-wise MLE is asymptotically more efficient than the splitting approach used in current RLHF implementations. Furthermore, the framework unifies RLHF and max-entropy IRL, offering new insights for algorithm design and regularization strategies in policy training.

4f670cdbc71940119bdc1b140015041eb19fa7cf.title: Dream the Impossible: Outlier Imagination with Diffusion Models
4f670cdbc71940119bdc1b140015041eb19fa7cf.research_question: How can photo-realistic outlier data be automatically synthesized for improving out-of-distribution (OOD) detection and model reliability, using only in-distribution (ID) data and classes?
4f670cdbc71940119bdc1b140015041eb19fa7cf.hypothesis: Synthesizing photo-realistic outlier images by sampling from low-likelihood regions in a text-conditioned latent space and decoding them with diffusion models will provide effective regularization for OOD detection, outperforming existing feature-based or GAN-based outlier generation approaches.
4f670cdbc71940119bdc1b140015041eb19fa7cf.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed that first learns a text-conditioned latent space by training a feature encoder to align image embeddings with class token embeddings derived from a pre-trained diffusion model's text encoder. This is achieved by optimizing a loss that encourages compact, class-conditional von Mises-Fisher distributions on the hypersphere. Outlier embeddings are then sampled from low-likelihood regions of this latent space, specifically around the boundary of the ID data as determined by k-nearest neighbor distances, and further perturbed using a Gaussian kernel. These sampled embeddings are decoded into pixel-space images by substituting them for the original token embeddings in the diffusion model's image generation process. The resulting synthetic outlier images are incorporated into the training of the downstream classifier with an explicit OOD regularization loss, encouraging the model to separate ID and OOD samples.
4f670cdbc71940119bdc1b140015041eb19fa7cf.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using CIFAR-100 and IMAGENET-100 as in-distribution datasets, with OOD evaluation performed on datasets such as TEXTURES, SVHN, PLACES365, ISUN, LSUN, INATURALIST, SUN, and others, ensuring disjoint categories between ID and OOD sets. The classifier architecture will be ResNet-34, trained with standard SGD, cosine learning rate decay, and batch size 160. For each class, 1,000 OOD samples will be generated using Stable Diffusion v1.4, resulting in 100,000 synthetic images per dataset. Baselines for comparison include confidence-based, energy-based, distance-based, and synthesis-based (GAN, VOS, NPOS) OOD detection methods. Evaluation metrics will include FPR95 (false positive rate at 95% TPR), AUROC (area under the ROC curve), and ID accuracy. Ablation studies will investigate the effects of regularization weight, Gaussian kernel variance, and k in k-NN sampling.
4f670cdbc71940119bdc1b140015041eb19fa7cf.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable the automatic generation of photo-realistic, high-resolution outlier images for OOD detection using only ID data and classes. Unlike prior feature-based or GAN-based synthesis methods, this framework leverages off-the-shelf diffusion models to generate outliers directly in pixel space, allowing for human-interpretable inspection and understanding of the synthesized samples. The method establishes a new connection between generative modeling and discriminative OOD detection, and demonstrates improved OOD detection performance on standard benchmarks. Additionally, the framework can be extended to generate in-distribution samples, improving generalization under distribution shift.

4f861f449cc9078989b91b2bca681f58d9b3b071.title: Frustratingly Easy Test-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language Models
4f861f449cc9078989b91b2bca681f58d9b3b071.research_question: How can test-time adaptation (TTA) for vision-language models (VLMs) be made more efficient and robust, particularly in the presence of challenging, out-of-distribution, or single-sample test scenarios, without incurring significant computational overhead?
4f861f449cc9078989b91b2bca681f58d9b3b071.hypothesis: A simple, optimization-free test-time adaptation approach that leverages marginalization over confident augmented views and sets the Softmax temperature to zero can achieve or surpass the robustness and accuracy of state-of-the-art TTA methods for VLMs, while being significantly more efficient in terms of computation and memory.
4f861f449cc9078989b91b2bca681f58d9b3b071.proposed_method: The proposed method, termed ZERO (Test-Time Adaptation with 'zero' temperature), operates by first generating N augmented views of a single test image using standard augmentation techniques such as random resized crops and horizontal flips. Each view is passed through the vision encoder, and predictions are obtained via cosine similarity with precomputed text embeddings. Confidence-based filtering is applied to retain only the most confident predictions (e.g., lowest entropy, bottom 10-30% percentile). The Softmax temperature is then set to zero, effectively converting the output probabilities into one-hot vectors that only consider the argmax class per view. The final prediction is obtained by marginalizing (majority voting) over the retained confident views. This approach requires only a single batched forward pass through the vision encoder and no backward passes or parameter updates, making it highly efficient.
4f861f449cc9078989b91b2bca681f58d9b3b071.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on established benchmarks for natural distribution shifts (ImageNet, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-v2, ImageNet-Sketch) and fine-grained classification datasets (Oxford-Flowers, DTD, Oxford-Pets, Stanford Cars, UCF101, Caltech101, Food101, SUN397, FGVC-Aircraft, EuroSAT). The method will be compared against state-of-the-art TTA baselines including Test-Time Prompt Tuning (TPT), PromptAlign, and Reinforcement Learning from CLIP Feedback (RLCF), using various VLM backbones such as CLIP-ViT-B-16, MaPLe, and CLIP-ViT-L-14. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy, expected calibration error (ECE), runtime per image, and peak GPU memory usage. All methods will be run under identical hardware conditions (e.g., NVIDIA A100 GPU, FP16 precision), and results will be averaged over multiple seeds for statistical robustness.
4f861f449cc9078989b91b2bca681f58d9b3b071.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a theoretically justified, optimization-free TTA method that is hidden within the standard marginal entropy minimization paradigm. By setting the Softmax temperature to zero and marginalizing over confident augmentations, the method achieves state-of-the-art or superior accuracy compared to existing TTA methods, while being up to 10× faster and 13× more memory efficient. The approach requires only a single forward pass through the vision encoder, does not require any parameter updates, and can serve as a strong, simple baseline for future TTA research in vision-language models.

4f93f2c891f63c0711de5b50b10b8b8554b37be4.title: Scaling Laws for Floating Point Quantization Training
4f93f2c891f63c0711de5b50b10b8b8554b37be4.research_question: How do various floating-point quantization parameters—including exponent bits, mantissa bits, quantization targets, and scaling factor block size—affect the training performance of large language models, and can a unified scaling law be developed to accurately predict model performance under different low-precision configurations?
4f93f2c891f63c0711de5b50b10b8b8554b37be4.hypothesis: A unified scaling law that explicitly incorporates floating-point quantization parameters (exponent bits, mantissa bits, block size) alongside model size and data size will enable accurate prediction of large language model performance under low-precision training, and there exist optimal configurations of these parameters for cost-effective and efficient training.
4f93f2c891f63c0711de5b50b10b8b8554b37be4.proposed_method: A comprehensive methodology will be developed to empirically and theoretically investigate the impact of floating-point quantization parameters on large language model (LLM) training. The approach will involve simulating low-precision floating-point formats (with configurable exponent and mantissa bits) using QPyTorch, applying quantization to selected targets within transformer architectures, and systematically varying quantization settings such as exponent/mantissa allocation and scaling factor block size. The method will include deriving and fitting a new scaling law that models validation loss as a function of model size, data size, exponent bits, mantissa bits, and block size, capturing both classical scaling effects and additional information loss due to quantization. Parameter fitting and ablation studies will be conducted to validate the law and extract optimal quantization layouts for different compute regimes.
4f93f2c891f63c0711de5b50b10b8b8554b37be4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on LLaMA-architecture models trained on a subset of the Dolma V1.7 dataset, with model sizes ranging from 41M to 1.2B parameters and data sizes from 10B to 100B tokens. Over 350 training runs will systematically vary exponent and mantissa bit allocations, quantization targets (inputs to GEMM operations), and scaling factor block sizes. Baseline comparisons will include classical scaling laws (Chinchilla and OpenAI) and prior precision-aware scaling laws. Evaluation metrics will focus on validation loss prediction accuracy across quantization settings, with additional analysis of the marginal effects of quantization parameters, optimal bit allocations, and compute-optimal configurations. Further validation will be performed on larger models (up to 70B parameters) to test the generalizability of the scaling law.
4f93f2c891f63c0711de5b50b10b8b8554b37be4.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first unified scaling law for floating-point quantization training that explicitly models the effects of exponent bits, mantissa bits, and scaling factor block size in addition to model and data size. It provides actionable insights into optimal floating-point layouts for different bit-widths, identifies the existence of a critical data size beyond which additional training data degrades performance under low-precision, and establishes the proportional relationship between optimal quantization precision and computational power. The approach delivers a practical framework for predicting LLM performance under diverse low-precision configurations and offers guidance for hardware and algorithm co-design in future LLM training.

4f997c404e97087194d2df538deb82b2c5428c1e.title: Grounding Image Matching in 3D with MASt3R
4f997c404e97087194d2df538deb82b2c5428c1e.research_question: How can image matching be grounded in 3D to improve robustness and accuracy in camera pose estimation, camera calibration, and 3D scene reconstruction, especially under challenging conditions such as extreme viewpoint and illumination changes?
4f997c404e97087194d2df538deb82b2c5428c1e.hypothesis: Grounding image matching in 3D by jointly predicting dense local features and 3D geometry, and optimizing the matching process with efficient algorithms, will significantly improve the robustness and accuracy of image correspondence, camera pose estimation, and 3D reconstruction compared to existing 2D- or keypoint-based methods.
4f997c404e97087194d2df538deb82b2c5428c1e.proposed_method: A novel framework, MASt3R, is developed that augments a transformer-based 3D reconstruction backbone (DUSt3R) with an additional head for dense local feature prediction. This head outputs dense feature maps for each input image, trained with an InfoNCE-based matching loss to encourage precise pixel-level correspondences. The architecture jointly regresses dense 3D pointmaps, confidence maps, and local features for each pixel, enabling both 3D scene understanding and robust matching. To address the computational complexity of dense matching, a fast reciprocal matching algorithm is introduced, leveraging iterative sub-sampling and mutual nearest neighbor search to efficiently extract reliable correspondences. Additionally, a coarse-to-fine matching scheme is implemented, where matching is first performed at lower resolutions and then refined at higher resolutions using overlapping window crops, ensuring scalability to high-resolution images.
4f997c404e97087194d2df538deb82b2c5428c1e.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a diverse mixture of 14 datasets, including Habitat, ARKitScenes, BlendedMVS, MegaDepth, Static Scenes 3D, ScanNet++, CO3D-v2, Waymo, Map-free, WildRgb, VirtualKitti, Unreal4K, TartanAir, and an internal dataset, covering both indoor and outdoor scenes, synthetic and real-world imagery. The method is evaluated on multiple challenging benchmarks, such as Map-free localization, CO3Dv2, RealEstate10k, Aachen Day-Night, InLoc, and DTU for multi-view stereo. Baselines include state-of-the-art keypoint-based, dense matching, and 3D-aware methods (e.g., SIFT, SuperGlue, LoFTR, DUSt3R, RayDiff, PixSfM, COLMAP+SPSG). Evaluation metrics include Virtual Correspondence Reprojection Error (VCRE), camera pose accuracy (rotation and translation errors), mean Average Accuracy (mAA), and Chamfer distances for 3D reconstruction. The experimental setup includes training with aggressive data augmentation, random cropping, and homographic transforms, with local feature dimension set to 24 and matching loss weight of 1. Fast approximate nearest neighbor search is implemented using FAISS for high-dimensional features and K-d trees for 3D points.
4f997c404e97087194d2df538deb82b2c5428c1e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a 3D-aware dense matching framework that jointly predicts local features and 3D geometry, enabling highly accurate and robust correspondences even under extreme viewpoint and illumination changes. A fast reciprocal matching algorithm is developed, providing orders-of-magnitude speedup with theoretical guarantees and improved accuracy. The method also pioneers a scalable coarse-to-fine matching scheme for high-resolution images. Extensive experiments demonstrate significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods on multiple challenging benchmarks, including a 30% absolute gain in VCRE AUC on the Map-free localization dataset. The approach is also shown to be effective in zero-shot settings for dense multi-view stereo reconstruction.

4fa8744583a4754719fd29b295c29858a4e2ab36.title: Sum of Squares Circuits
4fa8744583a4754719fd29b295c29858a4e2ab36.research_question: How can the expressiveness and tractability trade-off in probabilistic circuits be further characterized and improved, and is it possible to construct generative models that are both more expressive and support efficient, exact inference?
4fa8744583a4754719fd29b295c29858a4e2ab36.hypothesis: Sum of squares circuits, constructed as sums of compatible squared probabilistic circuits, can be exponentially more expressive than both monotonic and squared probabilistic circuits, while maintaining tractable inference. Furthermore, complex parameters do not provide additional expressiveness beyond what can be achieved with real parameters in this framework.
4fa8744583a4754719fd29b295c29858a4e2ab36.proposed_method: A new class of probabilistic circuits, termed sum of compatible squares (SOCS) circuits, will be formalized. These circuits are constructed by summing squared probabilistic circuits that are compatible in terms of their structural properties (smoothness and decomposability). The method involves defining compatibility conditions, ensuring each squared circuit can be efficiently squared and summed while preserving tractable inference. The expressiveness hierarchy of these circuits will be theoretically analyzed, including their relationships to monotonic circuits, squared circuits, and other tractable models such as Born Machines, PSD models, and Inception PCs. Theoretical results will be established to demonstrate exponential separations in expressiveness between these classes. Additionally, the method will extend to circuits with complex and hypercomplex parameters, and reductions will be provided to show equivalence in expressiveness with real-parameterized SOCS circuits.
4fa8744583a4754719fd29b295c29858a4e2ab36.experiment_details: Empirical validation will be performed on both tabular and image datasets, including UCI datasets (Power, Gas, Hepmass, MiniBooNE) and image datasets (MNIST, FashionMNIST, CelebA). Structured monotonic PCs, squared PCs (with real and complex parameters), and SOCS circuits with varying numbers of squares will be compared in terms of distribution estimation performance. Model sizes will be controlled to ensure fair comparison. Evaluation metrics will include average test log-likelihood and bits-per-dimension (BPD) for image data. Experiments will also assess the scalability and stability of training, as well as the impact of increasing the number of squares in SOCS circuits. Baselines will include mixtures of monotonic PCs and single squared PCs.
4fa8744583a4754719fd29b295c29858a4e2ab36.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the sum of compatible squares (SOCS) circuit class, which unifies and extends several tractable probabilistic models, providing a new expressiveness hierarchy. It establishes, for the first time, exponential separations in expressiveness between monotonic, squared, and SOCS circuits, and demonstrates that SOCS circuits can efficiently simulate models with complex parameters using only real parameters. The framework also connects probabilistic circuit expressiveness to classical results in algebraic geometry and non-negative polynomial representations, and provides a rigorous theoretical foundation for the empirical success of complex-parameterized models in generative modeling.

4fbaf11a0214497e4f56f7bb2917539c5b48681e.title: Learning Mask Invariant Mutual Information for Masked Image Modeling
4fbaf11a0214497e4f56f7bb2917539c5b48681e.research_question: How can the performance and understanding of masked autoencoders (MAEs) in self-supervised visual representation learning be improved by systematically optimizing the information retained and discarded in their latent representations?
4fbaf11a0214497e4f56f7bb2917539c5b48681e.hypothesis: Optimizing the latent features of MAEs to maximize relevant information between latent representations and outputs, while minimizing irrelevant information between latent representations and inputs, will improve the quality of learned representations and downstream task performance.
4fbaf11a0214497e4f56f7bb2917539c5b48681e.proposed_method: A new masked image modeling framework, MI-MAE, is proposed based on the information bottleneck principle from information theory. The method introduces two mutual information-based losses on the latent features: (1) a mutual information maximization loss that encourages the latent features of multiple orthogonal masked views of the same image to be similar, implemented via an InfoNCE loss; and (2) a mutual information minimization loss that reduces the mutual information between the latent features and the input, estimated using a Mutual Information Neural Estimator (MINE) and an approximation network. The overall training objective combines these losses with the standard MAE reconstruction loss, weighted by hyperparameters. During training, for each image, multiple orthogonal masks are generated to ensure all image patches are covered, and the encoder, decoder, and approximation network are jointly optimized. The approximation network predicts the mean and variance of the latent feature distribution conditioned on the input, facilitating the estimation of mutual information upper bounds.
4fbaf11a0214497e4f56f7bb2917539c5b48681e.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on standard benchmarks including ImageNet-1K for image classification, COCO for object detection and instance segmentation, and ADE20K for semantic segmentation. For pre-training, four orthogonal masks per image are used, with a masking ratio of 0.75, and the number of epochs is adjusted to match the total number of mask samples with baselines. The method is compared against strong baselines such as MAE, SimMIM, BEiT, DINO, MoCov3, and others, using evaluation metrics like top-1 accuracy for classification, APbox and APmask for detection, and mIoU for segmentation. Fine-tuning and linear probing protocols follow standard practice, and ablation studies investigate the effect of loss components, loss weights, mask generation strategies, and masking ratios. All experiments are run on NVIDIA V100 GPUs, and the implementation strictly follows the official codebases of the respective baselines for fair comparison.
4fbaf11a0214497e4f56f7bb2917539c5b48681e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to systematically apply the information bottleneck principle to masked autoencoders, providing a theoretically grounded framework for optimizing latent representations. The introduction of mutual information maximization and minimization losses on the latent features is novel in the context of MAEs, enabling explicit control over the information retained and discarded. The use of multiple orthogonal masks per image for mutual information estimation and the design of a lightweight approximation network for variational estimation of mutual information are additional innovations. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements over state-of-the-art MAE-based methods across multiple vision tasks, validating the effectiveness and generality of the approach.

4fcb8b6c466937025d315be6a83b624b10e860b4.title: MAmmoTH2: Scaling Instructions from the Web
4fcb8b6c466937025d315be6a83b624b10e860b4.research_question: How can large-scale, high-quality instruction-response data be efficiently harvested from naturally occurring web sources to improve the reasoning and generalization abilities of large language models, without relying on costly human annotation or distillation from proprietary models?
4fcb8b6c466937025d315be6a83b624b10e860b4.hypothesis: Instruction-response pairs mined and refined from diverse, naturally occurring web documents can provide a scalable, high-quality dataset for instruction tuning that significantly improves the reasoning, code generation, and general language understanding abilities of large language models, rivaling or surpassing models trained on human-annotated or synthetic data.
4fcb8b6c466937025d315be6a83b624b10e860b4.proposed_method: A three-step pipeline will be developed to mine instruction-response pairs from large web corpora. First, a recall step will use a fastText classifier trained on a diverse seed dataset to identify and retrieve relevant documents from CommonCrawl, with iterative filtering using LLMs (e.g., GPT-3.5, GPT-4) to select domains likely to contain instructional content. Second, an extraction step will process the recalled documents using rule-based HTML cleaning and prompt open-source LLMs (e.g., Qwen-72B) to extract question-answer pairs, discarding documents without clear instructional content. Third, a refinement step will prompt multiple LLMs (e.g., Mixtral-22B×8 and Qwen-72B) to reformat, clarify, and add missing explanations to the extracted pairs, ensuring data quality and diversity. The resulting dataset, WEBINSTRUCT, will consist of approximately 10 million high-quality instruction-response pairs spanning diverse domains.
4fcb8b6c466937025d315be6a83b624b10e860b4.experiment_details: Large language models such as Mistral-7B, Llama-3-8B, Mixtral-8×7B, and Yi-34B will be fine-tuned on the WEBINSTRUCT dataset using standardized multi-turn instruction tuning formats and optimized training parameters (e.g., learning rates, batch size, sequence length, DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 for efficiency). Models will be evaluated on a suite of held-out reasoning benchmarks including TheoremQA, GSM8K, MATH, ARC-C, MMLU-STEM, GPQA, and BBH, with all evaluation data excluded from training. Additional experiments will assess performance on code generation (HumanEval, MBPP), general language understanding (MMLU, MMLU-Pro), and chatbot benchmarks (MT-Bench, AlpacaEval 2.0, Arena Hard). Baselines will include both official instruction-tuned models and models trained on human-annotated or synthetic datasets of comparable size. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of dataset scale, refinement strategies, domain diversity, and data sources.
4fcb8b6c466937025d315be6a83b624b10e860b4.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a scalable, cost-effective paradigm for harvesting high-quality instruction data directly from the web, eliminating dependence on human annotation or proprietary model distillation. The three-step recall-extract-refine pipeline ensures both diversity and quality, resulting in a dataset that matches or exceeds the scale of continued pre-training corpora while maintaining the high quality of supervised fine-tuning datasets. The resulting instruction-tuned models demonstrate superior generalization and state-of-the-art performance on reasoning, code generation, and general language understanding tasks, particularly for models under 10B parameters. The methodology also highlights the importance of data diversity and multi-LLM refinement for robust model performance.

4fcfffeebdc5290e2650804f3d875547264cd008.title: Multiscale transforms for signals on simplicial complexes
4fcfffeebdc5290e2650804f3d875547264cd008.research_question: How can multiscale transforms and basis dictionaries be generalized to analyze signals defined on higher-dimensional simplices (such as edges, triangles, and higher-order cells) of a simplicial complex, rather than just on nodes of a graph?
4fcfffeebdc5290e2650804f3d875547264cd008.hypothesis: Multiscale transforms and basis dictionaries constructed using hierarchical partitioning based on Hodge Laplacians and their variants can provide effective, interpretable, and localized representations for signals defined on κ-dimensional simplices of simplicial complexes.
4fcfffeebdc5290e2650804f3d875547264cd008.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops a family of multiscale transforms and overcomplete dictionaries for signals defined on κ-dimensional simplices of a simplicial complex. The method begins by constructing hierarchical bipartitions of the set of κ-simplices using spectral clustering techniques, specifically by computing Fiedler vectors of weighted random-walk Hodge Laplacians. This recursive bipartitioning yields a binary partition tree, which is then used to construct localized, piecewise-constant orthonormal bases (κ-Haar bases) and overcomplete dictionaries (κ-HGLET and κ-GHWT) for the signal space. The transforms are designed to handle the orientation and adjacency complexities unique to higher-order simplices, incorporating signed adjacency matrices and various Laplacian normalizations. The framework supports both orthonormal and overcomplete representations, and allows for data-adaptive best-basis selection.
4fcfffeebdc5290e2650804f3d875547264cd008.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Real-world simplicial complexes will be generated from sources such as co-authorship/citation networks and ocean current/flow datasets, where signals are defined on edges, triangles, or higher-dimensional cells. The proposed transforms will be evaluated on tasks including signal approximation, clustering, and supervised classification. Baselines for comparison will include existing graph-based transforms and spectral methods. Evaluation metrics will include signal reconstruction error, sparsity of representation, clustering accuracy, and classification performance. The experimental setup will involve implementation in Julia and Python, with open-source code provided for reproducibility.
4fcfffeebdc5290e2650804f3d875547264cd008.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first generalization of multiscale graph signal transforms to signals defined on κ-dimensional simplices of simplicial complexes, leveraging hierarchical partitioning via Hodge Laplacians. It provides a principled approach to constructing localized, interpretable, and orthonormal bases as well as overcomplete dictionaries for higher-order domains. The method addresses unique challenges such as orientation, signed adjacency, and multiple adjacency definitions in simplicial complexes. The framework unifies and extends prior work on graph-based wavelets and transforms, enabling new applications in signal processing, data analysis, and machine learning on complex topological domains.

4fdc32c1f7012f14b8a9748ec5dc6830a5826874.title: Discovering Spoofing Attempts on Language Model Watermarks
4fdc32c1f7012f14b8a9748ec5dc6830a5826874.research_question: How can spoofed texts generated by learning-based attacks on language model watermarks be reliably distinguished from genuinely watermarked texts, and what are the fundamental limitations of current spoofing methods?
4fdc32c1f7012f14b8a9748ec5dc6830a5826874.hypothesis: Current learning-based spoofing attacks on language model watermarks leave detectable statistical artifacts in the generated text, which can be exploited to distinguish spoofed texts from genuinely watermarked texts, regardless of the spoofing approach.
4fdc32c1f7012f14b8a9748ec5dc6830a5826874.proposed_method: A statistical framework will be developed to detect artifacts left by learning-based spoofing attacks on language model watermarks. The approach involves modeling the dependence between token color sequences (as determined by the watermarking scheme) and the context distribution, specifically focusing on Red-Green watermarking schemes but generalizing to others. The method constructs statistical tests—such as correlation-based statistics between token color and context frequency—whose distributions under the null hypothesis (genuine watermarking) are analytically or empirically characterized. Two main instantiations are proposed: one using (h+1)-gram frequency scores and another using unigram frequency scores, with appropriate statistical corrections (e.g., Spearman rank correlation, Fisher transformation) to control for outliers and non-independence. Reprompting techniques are used to estimate the null distribution when independence assumptions do not hold.
4fdc32c1f7012f14b8a9748ec5dc6830a5826874.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the KGW SumHash Red-Green watermarking scheme with varying context sizes (h ∈ {1,2,3}) and watermark parameters (γ, δ). The primary datasets for evaluation are continuations of prompts from the C4 dataset, with both spoofed and genuinely watermarked texts generated using state-of-the-art spoofing methods: Stealing (using LLAMA2-7B as the watermarked model and MISTRAL-7B as the spoofer) and Distillation (using LLAMA2-7B and PYTHIA-1.4B). For each parameter setting, 10,000 text continuations of lengths between 50 and 400 tokens are generated, concatenated to reach target lengths up to 3000 tokens. Only texts flagged as watermarked by the detector are retained for analysis. Evaluation metrics include Type 1 error (false positive rate), true positive rate (power), and empirical p-value distributions, with statistical tests validated using Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Pearson’s normality tests. Additional experiments generalize the approach to other watermarking schemes (AAR, KTH) and assess robustness to human edits.
4fdc32c1f7012f14b8a9748ec5dc6830a5826874.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first rigorous statistical tests for post-hoc discovery of spoofing attempts on language model watermarks, revealing that all current learning-based spoofing methods leave detectable artifacts. The method is general, robust across watermarking schemes and spoofing techniques, and achieves arbitrarily high detection power given sufficient text length. The approach provides new insights into the inherent limitations of existing spoofing attacks and offers a practical mitigation strategy for maintaining watermark credibility.

4ff3ec79a96c86e6deb8f71924cd6f74d124c628.title: Differentially Private Estimation of Heterogeneous Causal Effects
4ff3ec79a96c86e6deb8f71924cd6f74d124c628.research_question: How can heterogeneous causal effects be estimated in a manner that provides formal differential privacy guarantees, particularly in sensitive domains such as healthcare or social science, and what are the trade-offs between privacy and estimation accuracy in this context?
4ff3ec79a96c86e6deb8f71924cd6f74d124c628.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a general meta-algorithm leveraging sample splitting and differentially private machine learning models can enable accurate estimation of heterogeneous causal effects (CATE) while providing formal differential privacy guarantees, and that most of the accuracy loss due to privacy constraints will be attributable to increased variance rather than bias.
4ff3ec79a96c86e6deb8f71924cd6f74d124c628.proposed_method: A general meta-algorithm will be developed for estimating conditional average treatment effects (CATE) under differential privacy constraints. The approach will utilize sample splitting to partition the dataset into disjoint subsets for estimating nuisance functions (such as propensity scores and outcome regressions) and the final CATE function, enabling the use of the parallel composition property of differential privacy for tighter privacy guarantees. The method will be learner-agnostic, supporting both single-stage (e.g., S-learner) and multi-stage (e.g., DR-learner, R-learner) CATE estimators, with each sub-module implemented using differentially private algorithms. As a concrete instantiation, the method will employ differentially private Explainable Boosting Machines (DP-EBMs), which are interpretable generalized additive models, as the base learner for all regression and classification tasks within the meta-algorithm. The full pipeline will release all intermediate outputs (such as estimated nuisance functions) to facilitate transparency and diagnostic analysis, while maintaining overall differential privacy.
4ff3ec79a96c86e6deb8f71924cd6f74d124c628.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both real-world and simulated datasets. The primary real-world dataset is a modified version of the Arceneaux et al. (2006) voting dataset, where a synthetic heterogeneous treatment effect is injected to enable ground-truth evaluation. Five additional simulated datasets will be generated with varying covariate distributions, baseline functions, propensity scores, and treatment effect functions to cover a range of causal inference scenarios. Three differentially private CATE learners—DP-EBM-DR-learner, DP-EBM-R-learner, and DP-EBM-S-learner—will be evaluated. Sample splitting ratios and hyperparameters will be specified, and the DP-EBM implementation from the 'interpret' Python package will be used. Experiments will systematically vary the privacy parameter epsilon (with delta fixed at 1e-5) and training sample size, and will assess performance using mean squared error (MSE), bias, and variance decomposition on large test sets. Baselines will include non-private versions and simpler estimators such as the S-learner (ATE estimator).
4ff3ec79a96c86e6deb8f71924cd6f74d124c628.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a general, modular meta-algorithm for differentially private estimation of heterogeneous causal effects, applicable to a wide range of existing CATE learners. The method leverages sample splitting and the parallel composition property of differential privacy to provide tight, learner-agnostic privacy guarantees. The use of interpretable, high-accuracy DP-EBMs as base learners enables direct analysis of the impact of privacy noise on causal effect estimation. The research provides a comprehensive empirical study of the privacy-accuracy trade-off in CATE estimation, including decomposition of error into bias and variance, and demonstrates that most accuracy loss under differential privacy arises from increased variance rather than bias.

4ff5aa25088ad899a23e6ec0385ff5bd0e5efc68.title: Beyond Uniform Sampling: Offline Reinforcement Learning with Imbalanced Datasets
4ff5aa25088ad899a23e6ec0385ff5bd0e5efc68.research_question: How can offline reinforcement learning be improved to learn high-performing policies from imbalanced datasets, particularly when the dataset contains a predominance of suboptimal trajectories and diverse initial states?
4ff5aa25088ad899a23e6ec0385ff5bd0e5efc68.hypothesis: Re-weighting samples in offline RL training objectives to emphasize high-return state-action pairs, rather than uniformly sampling from all data, will enable the learned policy to achieve higher returns, especially in imbalanced datasets with many suboptimal trajectories.
4ff5aa25088ad899a23e6ec0385ff5bd0e5efc68.proposed_method: A new density-ratio weighting (DW) framework will be developed to re-weight state-action pairs in offline RL datasets according to their estimated importance, aiming to emulate sampling from a higher-return policy. The importance weights will be parameterized by neural networks and optimized to maximize the expected (undiscounted) return, subject to Bellman flow conservation constraints. KL-divergence regularization will be added to prevent overfitting to rare state-action pairs. The weighting function will be trained in parallel with the offline RL algorithm, and both the policy optimization and regularization terms will be weighted using these learned importance weights. The method is designed to be plug-and-play, compatible with a variety of state-of-the-art offline RL algorithms.
4ff5aa25088ad899a23e6ec0385ff5bd0e5efc68.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of 72 imbalanced datasets derived from the D4RL Gym benchmark, including both datasets with similar initial states and those with diverse initial states. Datasets will be constructed by mixing trajectories from low- and high-performing policies in varying proportions and by varying the number of trajectories to test robustness to data scarcity. The proposed method will be evaluated alongside baselines such as uniform sampling, advantage-weighting, and percentage-filtering, and will be integrated with leading offline RL algorithms including Conservative Q-Learning (CQL), Implicit Q-Learning (IQL), and TD3BC. Evaluation metrics will include the interquartile mean (IQM) of normalized returns, with performance assessed over multiple random seeds and episodes, and confidence intervals computed via bootstrapping.
4ff5aa25088ad899a23e6ec0385ff5bd0e5efc68.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a general, algorithm-agnostic density-ratio weighting framework that enables offline RL algorithms to focus on high-return data without requiring explicit knowledge of expert trajectories or task identifiers. The method leverages off-policy evaluation techniques to optimize sample weights for policy improvement, rather than for evaluation alone, and is shown to significantly outperform prior sample re-weighting and filtering methods, especially in challenging settings with diverse initial states and limited data. This represents a substantial advancement in addressing the conservativeness and suboptimality of existing offline RL methods on imbalanced datasets.

5003fdf35af631d4cb17fd3c1ce2469f665064f1.title: Common Diffusion Noise Schedules and Sample Steps are Flawed
5003fdf35af631d4cb17fd3c1ce2469f665064f1.research_question: How can the design of noise schedules and sampling procedures in diffusion models be improved to ensure consistency between training and inference, and to enable the generation of samples that accurately reflect the full range of the original data distribution?
