5003fdf35af631d4cb17fd3c1ce2469f665064f1.hypothesis: Enforcing a zero terminal signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) in the noise schedule, training with v prediction, ensuring samplers start from the last timestep, and rescaling classifier-free guidance will align the diffusion process between training and inference, thereby enabling models to generate samples with a full range of brightness and improved fidelity to the data distribution.
5003fdf35af631d4cb17fd3c1ce2469f665064f1.proposed_method: A new methodology will be developed that modifies the noise schedule in diffusion models to enforce a zero terminal SNR, ensuring that the final timestep contains only pure Gaussian noise. The method will involve rescaling existing variance-preserving schedules so that the signal component is completely removed at the last timestep. Training will employ v prediction and v loss, which remain meaningful even when SNR is zero, ensuring the model learns to predict the mean of the data distribution conditioned on the prompt. The sampling process will be adjusted so that it always starts from the last timestep, using a 'trailing' step selection strategy to maximize the utility of each sampling step, especially when the number of steps is small. Additionally, a novel rescaling technique for classifier-free guidance will be introduced to prevent over-exposure in generated images, by matching the standard deviation of the guided output to that of the unguided output using a tunable rescale factor.
5003fdf35af631d4cb17fd3c1ce2469f665064f1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by finetuning a Stable Diffusion 2.1-base model on a filtered Laion dataset, using the proposed zero terminal SNR schedule, v prediction training, trailing sample steps, and the new classifier-free guidance rescale. The training will use the same configurations as the original model (batch size 2048, learning rate 1e-4, ema decay 0.9999, 50k iterations) for fair comparison. Evaluation will include both qualitative and quantitative analyses: qualitative assessment will focus on the model's ability to generate images with diverse brightness in response to explicit prompts, while quantitative evaluation will use Frechet Inception Distance (FID) and Inception Score (IS) on 10k COCO 2014 validation captions. Baseline comparisons will include the original Stable Diffusion model and a reference model trained on the same data without the proposed fixes. Ablation studies will examine the effects of different sample step strategies, classifier-free guidance rescale factors, and alternative noise techniques.
5003fdf35af631d4cb17fd3c1ce2469f665064f1.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled approach to enforcing zero terminal SNR in diffusion noise schedules, correcting a previously overlooked flaw that causes a mismatch between training and inference. It further proposes a new classifier-free guidance rescaling technique applicable to both image-space and latent-space models, addressing over-exposure issues as terminal SNR approaches zero. The combination of these modifications enables diffusion models to generate images with a full range of brightness and improved fidelity to the data distribution, which was not possible with prior noise schedules and sampling strategies. The approach is general and can be applied to a wide range of diffusion models beyond Stable Diffusion.

500d53aa9d62fdf27a8e0572bdefca4c5254cefa.title: DEAL: Disentangle and Localize Concept-level Explanations for VLMs
500d53aa9d62fdf27a8e0572bdefca4c5254cefa.research_question: Can vision-language models (VLMs) be trained to generate disentangled and accurately localized explanations for fine-grained visual concepts in images, without relying on human annotations?
500d53aa9d62fdf27a8e0572bdefca4c5254cefa.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging self-supervised constraints on concept-level and category-level explanations can enable VLMs to disentangle and localize fine-grained visual concepts, resulting in improved explainability and prediction accuracy, even without human-annotated supervision.
500d53aa9d62fdf27a8e0572bdefca4c5254cefa.proposed_method: A novel framework, DEAL (DisEntangle and Localize), will be developed to enhance concept-level explanations in VLMs. The approach begins by prompting a large language model (LLM), such as GPT-3.5, with carefully designed in-context learning prompts to extract visually discriminative and minimally overlapping concepts for each category. These concepts are then incorporated into the VLM training pipeline as augmented text inputs. The model is trained using a standard contrastive learning objective between image and text embeddings, augmented with two self-supervised regularization terms: (1) a disentanglement constraint that encourages explanation heatmaps for different concepts within the same category to be distinct (minimizing overlap), and (2) a localization constraint that enforces the aggregated concept-level explanations to be consistent with the category-level explanation. The overall objective is formulated as a constrained optimization problem, which is solved using Lagrange multipliers to combine the contrastive, disentanglement, and localization losses. The method is designed to be plug-and-play, requiring no architectural changes or additional parameters to the underlying VLM.
500d53aa9d62fdf27a8e0572bdefca4c5254cefa.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five benchmark image recognition datasets: ImageNet, CUB (Caltech-UCSD Birds-200-2011), Food-101, Oxford-Pets, and EuroSAT. The framework will be evaluated using both ViT-B/32 and ResNet-50 vision backbones, with fine-tuning performed on top of pre-trained CLIP models. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art VLMs such as CLIP, FLAVA, DeCLIP, PyramidCLIP, and CLIPpy, using both zero-shot and fine-tuned settings. Evaluation metrics will include concept-level explanation disentanglability (measured by normalized overlap of explanation heatmaps), concept-level explanation localizability (measured by normalized area under the insertion curve, iAUC, for explanation fidelity), and standard prediction accuracy. All models will be trained and validated using standard splits, with extensive ablation studies and multiple trials to ensure robustness.
500d53aa9d62fdf27a8e0572bdefca4c5254cefa.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a self-supervised approach to disentangle and localize concept-level explanations in VLMs without requiring human annotations, addressing the supervision gap for fine-grained concept localization. The approach leverages LLMs for scalable and visually meaningful concept extraction, and introduces novel regularization terms that enforce both explanation disentanglement and localization. The method is architecture-agnostic, requiring no changes to the underlying VLMs, and demonstrates that improved explainability can also enhance prediction accuracy, contrary to the typical trade-off observed in interpretability methods.

501c02c7caa7fc2c7077405299b4cbe7d294b170.title: Normalizing Flows for Probabilistic Modeling and Inference
501c02c7caa7fc2c7077405299b4cbe7d294b170.research_question: How can flexible, expressive, and tractable probabilistic models be constructed for continuous data using invertible transformations, and what are the fundamental principles, trade-offs, and applications of such models in probabilistic modeling and inference?
501c02c7caa7fc2c7077405299b4cbe7d294b170.hypothesis: Normalizing flows, constructed as compositions of invertible and differentiable transformations applied to simple base distributions, can approximate arbitrarily complex target distributions and provide a unified, efficient framework for probabilistic modeling, inference, and generative tasks.
501c02c7caa7fc2c7077405299b4cbe7d294b170.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed for constructing probabilistic models using normalizing flows, which define complex target distributions by applying a sequence of invertible and differentiable transformations to samples from a simple base distribution (e.g., multivariate normal). Each transformation in the flow is parameterized (often by neural networks) and is designed to have a tractable inverse and Jacobian determinant, enabling efficient computation of both sampling and density evaluation. The method will support both finite compositions of simple transformations and extensions to more general domains (e.g., discrete variables, Riemannian manifolds). Model fitting will be formulated as divergence minimization (e.g., forward or reverse Kullback–Leibler divergence), allowing for maximum likelihood estimation or variational inference, with gradients computed via Monte Carlo estimation and automatic differentiation.
501c02c7caa7fc2c7077405299b4cbe7d294b170.experiment_details: Experiments will involve fitting flow-based models to a variety of target distributions, including both synthetic and real-world datasets. Standard benchmarks for density estimation, generative modeling (such as image datasets), and approximate inference tasks will be used. Baselines will include traditional probabilistic models and other deep generative models (e.g., variational autoencoders, GANs). Evaluation metrics will comprise log-likelihood, sample quality, and computational efficiency (e.g., speed of sampling and density evaluation). The experimental setup will systematically compare different flow architectures, training divergences, and implementation choices to assess expressive power, scalability, and trade-offs.
501c02c7caa7fc2c7077405299b4cbe7d294b170.novelty_claims: The proposed research provides a unified and comprehensive perspective on normalizing flows, elucidating their theoretical foundations, expressive power, and computational trade-offs. It introduces a general methodology for constructing and training flow-based models, extends the conceptual framework to broader domains, and systematically relates flows to other probabilistic modeling paradigms. The work aims to clarify enduring principles for flow design and application, and to advance the field by addressing open problems and synthesizing recent advancements in a cohesive manner.

501f8a0200a12a6f3906c1e4f3f40715e0e7d23a.title: Step-DPO: Step-wise Preference Optimization for Long-chain Reasoning of LLMs
501f8a0200a12a6f3906c1e4f3f40715e0e7d23a.research_question: How can the robustness and factuality of large language models (LLMs) be improved for long-chain mathematical reasoning tasks, particularly by addressing the limitations of current preference optimization methods in identifying detailed step-wise errors?
501f8a0200a12a6f3906c1e4f3f40715e0e7d23a.hypothesis: Optimizing LLMs using step-wise preference data—where individual reasoning steps are treated as units for preference optimization—will lead to more accurate and robust long-chain mathematical reasoning compared to holistic answer-level preference optimization.
501f8a0200a12a6f3906c1e4f3f40715e0e7d23a.proposed_method: A novel optimization framework, Step-DPO, will be developed that treats each intermediate reasoning step in a mathematical solution as the basic unit for preference optimization. Instead of comparing entire answers, the method will identify the first erroneous reasoning step in a model-generated solution and optimize the model to prefer correct steps over incorrect ones at each stage of the reasoning chain. The optimization objective will be adapted from Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) to operate on step-wise data, maximizing the probability of correct next steps and minimizing the probability of incorrect ones, conditioned on the prompt and preceding correct steps. A data construction pipeline will be implemented to generate high-quality, in-distribution, step-wise preference pairs, involving error collection from model outputs, localization of the first error, and rectification by sampling correct continuations from the model itself. This approach will enable fine-grained process supervision and facilitate the rapid localization and correction of errors in long-chain reasoning.
501f8a0200a12a6f3906c1e4f3f40715e0e7d23a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several large-scale open-source LLMs, including Qwen2, Qwen1.5, Meta-Llama-3-70B, and DeepSeekMath, with supervised fine-tuning performed on augmented mathematical datasets such as MetaMath and MMIQC. For the Step-DPO phase, a curated dataset of 10,000 step-wise preference pairs will be constructed using the proposed pipeline, with additional data from AQuA. Evaluation will be performed on standard mathematical reasoning benchmarks, including MATH (5,000 problems, multiple difficulty levels and subjects) and GSM8K (1,319 problems), using accuracy as the primary metric. Baselines will include models trained with standard supervised fine-tuning, vanilla DPO, and RLHF, as well as state-of-the-art closed-source models (e.g., GPT-4, Claude-3-Opus, Gemini-1.5-Pro). Ablation studies will compare the effectiveness of step-wise versus holistic preference optimization, and the impact of in-distribution versus out-of-distribution preference data. Implementation will use standard optimization techniques (AdamW, learning rate scheduling, DeepSpeed ZeRO3) and hyperparameters will be tuned for both small and large models.
501f8a0200a12a6f3906c1e4f3f40715e0e7d23a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a step-wise preference optimization framework (Step-DPO) that enables fine-grained process supervision for long-chain reasoning in LLMs, overcoming the limitations of holistic answer-level preference methods. A novel, data-efficient pipeline for constructing in-distribution, step-wise preference datasets is developed, facilitating effective model alignment with minimal human annotation. The method demonstrates significant improvements in mathematical reasoning accuracy, particularly for large models, and achieves state-of-the-art results on challenging benchmarks, outperforming both open-source and closed-source models. The approach is simple, scalable, and complements existing RLHF-based alignment techniques.

5040acef429108015991dc5480f1cedf6851f0b7.title: AKEW: Assessing Knowledge Editing in the Wild
5040acef429108015991dc5480f1cedf6851f0b7.research_question: How can knowledge editing in language models be more effectively evaluated and improved in practical, real-world scenarios that involve diverse and complex knowledge updates beyond well-curated structured facts?
5040acef429108015991dc5480f1cedf6851f0b7.hypothesis: Current knowledge-editing methods, which are primarily evaluated on structured, curated datasets, will exhibit significant performance declines when assessed on practical, real-world knowledge updates presented in unstructured formats or as extracted triplets. Comprehensive benchmarks that include these realistic scenarios will reveal critical limitations and motivate the development of more robust knowledge-editing approaches.
5040acef429108015991dc5480f1cedf6851f0b7.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark, AKEW (Assessing Knowledge Editing in the Wild), will be developed to evaluate knowledge-editing methods in practical scenarios. The benchmark will encompass three distinct editing settings: (1) structured facts, represented as isolated triplets; (2) unstructured facts, consisting of natural language texts such as Wikipedia-style paragraphs; and (3) extracted triplets, automatically derived from unstructured texts. Three new datasets will be constructed: two containing counterfactual knowledge updates (adapted from existing resources, with unstructured facts generated via large language models) and one featuring real-world updates sourced from Wikidata and Wikipedia. For each edit, corresponding structured, unstructured, and extracted triplet representations will be prepared, and consistency between representations will be verified both automatically and manually. The benchmark will support evaluation of both parameter-editing and retrieval-augmented knowledge-editing methods.
5040acef429108015991dc5480f1cedf6851f0b7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using multiple state-of-the-art language models, including GPT2-XL, GPT-J (6B), and Mistral (7B), as the base models for editing. Knowledge-editing methods to be evaluated include fine-tuning (FT), LoRA, locate-then-edit approaches (ROME, MEMIT), and in-context learning/retrieval-augmented methods (IKE, MeLLo). Each method will be tested on all three editing settings (structured facts, unstructured facts, and extracted triplets) across the three datasets (COUNTERFACT, MQUAKE-CF, and WIKIUPDATE). Evaluation metrics will include editing accuracy (the proportion of successful edits) and, for multi-hop scenarios, multi-hop accuracy. Special attention will be given to the performance gap between structured and unstructured settings, as well as error analysis to identify bottlenecks in current methods. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparisons by aligning the knowledge content across representations and using consistent evaluation protocols.
5040acef429108015991dc5480f1cedf6851f0b7.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces the first comprehensive evaluation framework for knowledge editing that fully incorporates practical, real-world scenarios through the inclusion of unstructured facts and extracted triplets, in addition to structured facts. It provides new datasets featuring both counterfactual and real-world knowledge updates, enabling the assessment of knowledge-editing methods under conditions that closely mirror real-world applications. The benchmark reveals substantial gaps in the performance of existing methods when faced with realistic, complex knowledge updates, thereby establishing a new standard for evaluating and motivating future research in practical knowledge editing.

5042f2d68cfdddd58fb4e0942b933b548c1c1e49.title: Towards Faster Decentralized Stochastic Optimization with Communication Compression
5042f2d68cfdddd58fb4e0942b933b548c1c1e49.research_question: How can decentralized stochastic optimization in distributed and federated machine learning be accelerated under communication constraints, particularly with compressed communication, while maintaining robustness to data heterogeneity and achieving linear speed-up with the number of clients?
5042f2d68cfdddd58fb4e0942b933b548c1c1e49.hypothesis: Integrating momentum tracking with error feedback and contractive communication compression in decentralized optimization will enable optimal convergence rates matching distributed SGD, without requiring strong assumptions on data heterogeneity or large batch sizes, and will achieve linear speed-up with the number of clients.
5042f2d68cfdddd58fb4e0942b933b548c1c1e49.proposed_method: A new decentralized optimization algorithm, MoTEF, will be developed that combines momentum tracking with error feedback and contractive communication compression. Each client will maintain local model parameters and communicate only compressed updates to neighbors over a specified communication graph. The method will use contractive compressors (such as Top-K) to reduce communication costs, and error feedback mechanisms to correct compression bias. Momentum tracking will be applied not to gradients but to a momentum term, enhancing convergence and robustness to data heterogeneity. Additionally, a variance-reduced variant, MoTEF-VR, will be designed, incorporating a STORM-type estimator for further acceleration under mean-squared-smoothness assumptions.
5042f2d68cfdddd58fb4e0942b933b548c1c1e49.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic least squares problems will be used to systematically vary the number of clients, data heterogeneity, and communication topologies (e.g., ring, star, grid, Erdös-Rènyi graphs) to assess convergence rates and robustness. Real-world experiments will include non-convex logistic regression tasks on LibSVM datasets (e.g., a9a, w8a) distributed among clients. Baselines for comparison will include BEER, CHOCO-SGD, DSGD, and D2 algorithms. Evaluation metrics will include convergence rate (gradient norm), test accuracy, and communication complexity (bits transmitted). Hyperparameters such as stepsizes, momentum, and compression ratio will be tuned for all methods. Both the effect of network topology (via spectral gap) and data heterogeneity will be systematically analyzed.
5042f2d68cfdddd58fb4e0942b933b548c1c1e49.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first decentralized algorithm supporting contractive compressors that achieves optimal asymptotic convergence rates matching distributed SGD under arbitrary data heterogeneity, without requiring large batch sizes or strong smoothness assumptions. It achieves linear speed-up with the number of clients and is robust to network topology and data heterogeneity. The variance-reduced variant further improves convergence rates under mean-squared-smoothness. Extensive theoretical analysis and empirical results are provided to support these claims.

50472d04015a28d2cd5a2608ef87330b14154ce4.title: Multiscale Graph Comparison via the Embedded Laplacian Discrepancy
50472d04015a28d2cd5a2608ef87330b14154ce4.research_question: How can structural similarities between graphs of potentially different sizes be quantified in a simple, efficient, and theoretically sound manner, particularly focusing on their community structures?
50472d04015a28d2cd5a2608ef87330b14154ce4.hypothesis: A method that embeds graphs into a common low-dimensional Euclidean space using Laplacian eigenvectors and compares them via Wasserstein-based distances will provide an effective, scalable, and theoretically robust measure of graph similarity, invariant to isomorphisms and eigenvector ambiguities.
50472d04015a28d2cd5a2608ef87330b14154ce4.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces the Embedded Laplacian Discrepancy (ELD) as a framework for multiscale graph comparison. Each graph is represented as a point cloud in a shared low-dimensional Euclidean space, constructed from the first k Laplacian eigenvectors (where k is a resolution hyperparameter). To address sign ambiguities inherent in eigenvector-based methods, a symmetrization step is applied by including both the eigenvector and its negative in the embedding. For each axis (eigenvector), the 1D Wasserstein (earth mover's) distance is computed between the empirical distributions of the two graphs, and these are averaged to yield the final discrepancy. In cases where graphs have repeated eigenvalues (basis symmetries), a small symmetric perturbation is added to the adjacency matrix to break degeneracies, and the ELD is computed on the perturbed graphs, with results averaged over multiple perturbations for stability.
50472d04015a28d2cd5a2608ef87330b14154ce4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both simulated and real-world datasets. Simulated data will include deterministic graph families such as rings of cliques, which exhibit clear community structures, and random graphs generated via stochastic block models. Real-world data will include connectome graphs from different organisms. The ELD method will be benchmarked against established multiscale graph comparison methods, specifically Network Portrait Divergence (NPD) and NetLSD, using heatmaps of dissimilarity matrices to visualize structural similarity patterns. Additionally, the method will be evaluated in a downstream graph classification task using a K-nearest neighbor classifier. Computational efficiency and scalability will be assessed, and the method will be implemented in Python with automatic switching between exact and approximate ELD depending on spectral properties.
50472d04015a28d2cd5a2608ef87330b14154ce4.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to combine spectral/Laplacian embedding with a Wasserstein-based approach for comparing collections of graphs of different sizes. It resolves eigenvector sign and basis symmetry ambiguities without costly optimization or averaging procedures common in the literature. The ELD provides a theoretically grounded, computationally efficient, and isomorphism-invariant pseudo-metric for multiscale graph comparison, with strong theoretical and empirical evidence supporting its efficacy.

506c89d92be2211b4c84448608685e1b93926595.title: Contracting with a Learning Agent
506c89d92be2211b4c84448608685e1b93926595.research_question: How can dynamic contracts be optimally designed in repeated principal-agent settings when the agent is a learning agent employing no-regret algorithms, and what are the impacts of contract structure, agent learning dynamics, and uncertainty in the time horizon on the utilities of both principal and agent?
506c89d92be2211b4c84448608685e1b93926595.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, in repeated contract settings with a no-regret (specifically, mean-based) learning agent, there exists a simple dynamic contract structure—namely, a 'free-fall' contract—that can yield higher expected utility for the principal (and potentially the agent) compared to the best static contract, and that the principal's advantage diminishes under uncertainty about the time horizon.
506c89d92be2211b4c84448608685e1b93926595.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves formalizing the repeated principal-agent problem where the agent selects actions using a no-regret learning algorithm (with a focus on mean-based algorithms such as multiplicative weights or EXP3). The principal is allowed to offer a sequence of contracts, potentially adapting them over time. The method will first analyze the canonical linear contract setting (where the agent's actions result in stochastic success/failure outcomes), and then generalize to arbitrary contract spaces with single-dimensional scaling. The approach will leverage a reduction to a continuous-time analogue of the repeated game, enabling tractable analysis of optimal contract trajectories. The optimal contract structure will be characterized, and computational procedures for determining the optimal contract sequence will be developed. The impact of uncertainty in the time horizon will be quantified by analyzing the degradation in the principal's achievable utility under various levels of uncertainty.
506c89d92be2211b4c84448608685e1b93926595.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using simulated repeated contract environments with varying numbers of actions, outcome distributions, and agent cost structures. The agent will employ mean-based no-regret learning algorithms, and the principal will implement both static and dynamic (free-fall) contract strategies. Baselines will include the optimal static contract and, where applicable, dynamic contracts without single-dimensional scaling. Evaluation metrics will include the expected utility of the principal, the agent, and total welfare over the time horizon. Additional experiments will introduce uncertainty in the time horizon to measure the robustness and degradation of the principal's advantage. Computational efficiency of the proposed contract computation procedures will also be evaluated.
506c89d92be2211b4c84448608685e1b93926595.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first tractable and optimal solution for dynamic contract design against a no-regret (mean-based) learning agent in repeated principal-agent settings. The free-fall contract structure is claimed to be both simple and optimal in a wide class of settings, including those with linear contracts and single-dimensional scaling. The approach generalizes beyond binary outcomes to richer contract spaces. Additionally, the proposal is the first to rigorously quantify the impact of time horizon uncertainty on the principal's ability to outperform static contracts, providing both upper and lower bounds on achievable utility under uncertainty. The work bridges algorithmic contract theory and learning in games, offering new insights into the interplay between contract design and learning dynamics.

50714ad97ae3a65ff15771b8ec89de47aa8311ab.title: The Transient Nature of Emergent In-Context Learning in Transformers
50714ad97ae3a65ff15771b8ec89de47aa8311ab.research_question: How does in-context learning (ICL) emerge and persist in transformer neural networks, and under what conditions does it become transient or give way to in-weights learning (IWL)? What factors in data distribution, model architecture, and training regime influence the persistence or transience of ICL, and how can persistent ICL be promoted in compact transformer models?
50714ad97ae3a65ff15771b8ec89de47aa8311ab.hypothesis: The emergence of in-context learning in transformers is not necessarily persistent and may be transient, with ICL giving way to in-weights learning during extended training. Data distribution properties, model architecture, and regularization can modulate the persistence of ICL.
50714ad97ae3a65ff15771b8ec89de47aa8311ab.proposed_method: A systematic investigation will be conducted by training transformer models on synthetic datasets specifically designed to disentangle ICL and IWL strategies. The method will utilize exemplar-label pair sequences, where both ICL and IWL can lead to correct predictions, allowing for controlled evaluation of each learning strategy. The experimental setup will include varying model sizes (depth and embedding dimension), dataset properties (number of classes, in-class variation, and distributional skew such as Zipfian distributions), and regularization techniques (e.g., L2 regularization and selective weight decay). Evaluation will be performed using tailored test sequences that isolate ICL and IWL performance, and additional experiments will probe the competition between ICL and IWL circuits by manipulating architectural and training parameters.
50714ad97ae3a65ff15771b8ec89de47aa8311ab.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic datasets derived primarily from the Omniglot benchmark for few-shot learning, with additional datasets constructed from clustered language model token embeddings (e.g., LLaMa token embeddings). Training sequences will include both bursty and non-bursty contexts to incentivize ICL, while evaluation will employ two distinct sequence types: one requiring ICL (randomized label mappings) and one requiring IWL (no matching context exemplars). Model architectures will be varied in depth (e.g., 6, 12, 18 layers) and embedding size (e.g., 32, 64, 128), and training will use the Adam optimizer. Baselines will include different dataset sizes, class distributions (uniform vs. Zipfian), and regularization strengths. Performance will be measured by accuracy on ICL and IWL evaluators, as well as training loss, with experiments run for extended iterations to observe the onset and decay of ICL.
50714ad97ae3a65ff15771b8ec89de47aa8311ab.novelty_claims: The proposed research challenges the prevailing assumption that emergent in-context learning in transformers is persistent, revealing instead that ICL can be a transient phenomenon that fades with continued training even as loss decreases. The research introduces controlled synthetic benchmarks and evaluation protocols to disentangle ICL from IWL, systematically analyzes the effect of data distribution, model size, and regularization on ICL persistence, and demonstrates that L2 regularization can mitigate or eliminate ICL transience. The work further provides evidence that competition for model capacity between ICL and IWL circuits underlies the observed transience, offering new insights and practical strategies for promoting persistent ICL in smaller, more efficient transformer models.

507465f8d46489a68a527cb5304d76bdb6c31ed9.title: Semantic Uncertainty: Linguistic Invariances for Uncertainty Estimation in Natural Language Generation
507465f8d46489a68a527cb5304d76bdb6c31ed9.research_question: How can uncertainty in natural language generation, particularly in free-form question answering, be more accurately estimated by accounting for the semantic equivalence of different generated outputs?
507465f8d46489a68a527cb5304d76bdb6c31ed9.hypothesis: Uncertainty estimation methods that operate in meaning-space—by clustering semantically equivalent outputs and measuring entropy over meanings—will provide more reliable and predictive uncertainty estimates for natural language generation tasks than existing token-level or sequence-level entropy measures.
507465f8d46489a68a527cb5304d76bdb6c31ed9.proposed_method: A novel unsupervised approach is developed to estimate uncertainty in natural language generation by introducing 'semantic entropy', which measures entropy over the distribution of meanings rather than over token sequences. The method involves three main steps: (1) sampling multiple output sequences from a large language model given a context, (2) clustering these sequences into equivalence classes based on semantic similarity using a bi-directional entailment algorithm powered by a fine-tuned Deberta-large model on the MNLI dataset, and (3) aggregating the probabilities of sequences within each semantic cluster to compute the probability of each meaning, then calculating the entropy over these meaning probabilities. This approach requires no modification or retraining of the underlying language model and leverages only a single model instance, making it broadly applicable and efficient.
507465f8d46489a68a527cb5304d76bdb6c31ed9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on free-form question answering tasks using the CoQA (open-book) and TriviaQA (closed-book) datasets, with approximately 8,000 questions each. The OPT family of language models will be used at varying scales (2.7B, 6.7B, 13B, and 30B parameters), with the primary results reported for the 30B model. Baselines for comparison include predictive entropy, length-normalised predictive entropy, p(True) (asking the model if its answer is correct), and lexical similarity among generated answers. Evaluation will focus on the AUROC metric, measuring the ability of uncertainty estimates to distinguish between correct and incorrect answers, with correctness determined by a fuzzy Rouge-L threshold. Ablation studies will explore the effects of sampling temperature, number of samples, and clustering accuracy.
507465f8d46489a68a527cb5304d76bdb6c31ed9.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces semantic entropy, a new entropy-based uncertainty measure that explicitly accounts for linguistic invariances by clustering semantically equivalent outputs. This approach leverages a novel bi-directional entailment clustering algorithm for semantic equivalence, operates in an unsupervised manner with off-the-shelf language models, and requires no additional training or data. The method is claimed to outperform strong baselines in predicting answer correctness, to scale better with model size and sample count, and to offer a reproducible, efficient, and more meaningful uncertainty quantification for natural language generation.

50b0c6ee2b3d53ba5af69d6c00b5d60888a9026f.title: Maieutic Prompting: Logically Consistent Reasoning with Recursive Explanations
50b0c6ee2b3d53ba5af69d6c00b5d60888a9026f.research_question: How can language models be prompted to perform logically consistent and robust reasoning, especially when their generated explanations are often noisy, inconsistent, or unreliable?
50b0c6ee2b3d53ba5af69d6c00b5d60888a9026f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that constructing a recursive, abductive tree of explanations and resolving their logical relationships via symbolic inference will enable language models to produce more logically consistent, robust, and interpretable answers, even when individual explanations are unreliable.
50b0c6ee2b3d53ba5af69d6c00b5d60888a9026f.proposed_method: A new inference framework, termed Maieutic Prompting, will be developed to enhance logical consistency in language model reasoning. The approach will prompt a language model to generate abductive explanations for both possible answers (e.g., True and False) to a given question, recursively expanding these explanations to form a tree structure. At each node, the logical integrity of explanations will be validated by recursively prompting the model with its own generations, pruning branches that do not yield logically integral propositions. Logical relationships (belief and consistency) between explanations will be quantified, and an external natural language inference (NLI) model will be used to further define entailment and contradiction relations between arbitrary pairs of explanations. The final inference will be formulated as a weighted MAX-SAT problem, where the most probable and consistent assignment of truth values to all propositions (including the original question) is determined by maximizing the satisfaction of logical constraints.
50b0c6ee2b3d53ba5af69d6c00b5d60888a9026f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three challenging commonsense reasoning and fact verification benchmarks: Com2Sense, CSQA 2.0, and CREAK, all in binary QA format. The method will be evaluated using GPT-3 (text-davinci-001) as the language model, with a fixed set of few-shot examples for in-context learning. Baseline comparisons will include standard prompting, Chain of Thought, Self-Consistency, Generated Knowledge Prompting (GKP), and strong supervised models such as T5, UnifiedQA, and Unicorn. Evaluation metrics will include standard accuracy, pairwise accuracy, and contrast set accuracy to assess robustness to semantic perturbations. Additional analyses will examine robustness to prompt variations and ablations on tree generation strategies, decoding methods, and the use of the NLI verifier. Human evaluation will be performed to assess the grammaticality, relevance, factuality, and helpfulness of generated explanations.
50b0c6ee2b3d53ba5af69d6c00b5d60888a9026f.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel recursive, abductive prompting framework that constructs a tree of explanations and resolves their logical relationships using symbolic inference (MAX-SAT), rather than relying on individual explanations. This approach is claimed to improve logical consistency, robustness to noisy or contradictory generations, and interpretability of language model outputs. The method is fully unsupervised, model-agnostic, and achieves state-of-the-art results among prompting methods, performing competitively with or surpassing large supervised models. Additional contributions include the integration of an NLI verifier for cross-branch logical relations and a comprehensive robustness analysis.

50c51b595dfee1df1a0506ee7acef05ba01d3aa7.title: Align Your Gaussians: Text-to-4D with Dynamic 3D Gaussians and Composed Diffusion Models
50c51b595dfee1df1a0506ee7acef05ba01d3aa7.research_question: How can dynamic, animated 3D objects and scenes be synthesized from text prompts, enabling high-quality, temporally consistent, and composable 4D (3D+time) content generation?
50c51b595dfee1df1a0506ee7acef05ba01d3aa7.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that combining dynamic 3D Gaussian representations with deformation fields, and optimizing them via a compositional score distillation framework that leverages text-to-image, text-to-video, and 3D-aware multiview diffusion models, will enable the generation of high-quality, temporally consistent, and composable 4D scenes from text prompts.
50c51b595dfee1df1a0506ee7acef05ba01d3aa7.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that represents 4D scenes using dynamic 3D Gaussians, where each Gaussian's position evolves over time according to a learnable deformation field parameterized by a multilayer perceptron. The method will disentangle the synthesis process into two stages: first, a static 3D scene is generated using a combination of text-to-image and 3D-aware multiview diffusion models via score distillation, with view guidance and canonical pose enforcement. Second, temporal dynamics are introduced by optimizing the deformation field using gradients from both a text-to-video diffusion model (which supervises motion and temporal consistency) and a text-to-image model (which ensures high visual quality at each frame). The optimization is stabilized with a novel regularization technique based on a modified Jensen-Shannon divergence that preserves the mean and variance of the Gaussian distribution over time, and a motion amplification mechanism is applied to enhance dynamic motion. An autoregressive scheme is proposed to extend 4D sequences in time and to enable seamless composition of multiple dynamic objects within a scene.
50c51b595dfee1df1a0506ee7acef05ba01d3aa7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of text prompts to synthesize dynamic 4D scenes, using a dedicated text-to-video diffusion model (trained on large-scale video datasets such as HDVG-130M and Webvid-10M), Stable Diffusion as the text-to-image model, and MVDream as the 3D-aware multiview diffusion model. Baseline comparisons will include previous state-of-the-art methods such as MAV3D, with both qualitative and quantitative evaluations. User studies will be performed to assess overall quality, 3D appearance, text alignment, motion realism, and compositional capabilities. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of key components such as the regularization method, motion amplification, compositional score distillation, and autoregressive extension. Evaluation metrics will include user preference percentages and R-Precision for text-to-4D alignment.
50c51b595dfee1df1a0506ee7acef05ba01d3aa7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a compositional generation-based framework for text-to-4D synthesis, leveraging dynamic 3D Gaussians with deformation fields as an explicit and efficient 4D representation. Key innovations include a novel regularization method based on Jensen-Shannon divergence for stable and realistic motion learning, a motion amplification technique to enhance dynamic expressiveness, and an autoregressive scheme for temporally extended and composable 4D content. The method enables seamless composition of multiple dynamic objects within large scenes, achieves state-of-the-art performance in text-to-4D synthesis, and provides exact tracking labels for synthetic data generation. These capabilities are not demonstrated by prior works and open new avenues for animation, simulation, and digital content creation.

50eb97f832ffcd2114f79957c977215176384e3d.title: Scan and Snap: Understanding Training Dynamics and Token Composition in 1-layer Transformer
50eb97f832ffcd2114f79957c977215176384e3d.research_question: How do the training dynamics of a 1-layer Transformer, specifically the self-attention mechanism, influence the emergence and composition of token representations during next-token prediction tasks?
50eb97f832ffcd2114f79957c977215176384e3d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, under certain conditions (no positional encoding, long input sequences, and a faster-learning decoder layer), the self-attention mechanism in a 1-layer Transformer will develop an inductive bias that favors distinct contextual tokens over common ones, leading to a discriminative, sparse attention pattern that stabilizes due to a phase transition in training dynamics.
50eb97f832ffcd2114f79957c977215176384e3d.proposed_method: A mathematically rigorous analysis will be conducted on the stochastic gradient descent (SGD) training dynamics of a 1-layer Transformer model, consisting of a single self-attention layer followed by a decoder layer, for the task of next-token prediction. The study will assume no positional encoding, long input sequences, and a learning rate for the decoder that is significantly higher than that of the self-attention layer. Theoretical derivations will focus on the evolution of attention weights, using reparameterization to analyze pairwise token relation matrices, and will characterize how the self-attention mechanism allocates attention to distinct versus common tokens over the course of training. The analysis will include the identification of phase transitions in attention dynamics and the impact of learning rates on the sparsity and stability of attention patterns.
50eb97f832ffcd2114f79957c977215176384e3d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic datasets (e.g., Syn-Small and Syn-Medium) and a real-world dataset (WikiText). Synthetic datasets will be constructed with controlled vocabulary sizes and sequence classes, allowing precise manipulation of distinct and common token distributions. The 1-layer Transformer will be trained using SGD (and optionally Adam) with specified initializations and learning rates, and attention patterns will be visualized and quantified (e.g., via entropy measures) over training iterations. Baseline comparisons will involve varying learning rates for the decoder and self-attention layers, and the effect of optimizer choice. Evaluation metrics will include attention sparsity, convergence speed, and the correspondence between theoretical predictions and empirical attention patterns.
50eb97f832ffcd2114f79957c977215176384e3d.novelty_claims: The proposed research offers a formal, mathematically grounded characterization of the SGD training dynamics in 1-layer Transformers, revealing a previously unstudied inductive bias in self-attention that discriminates between distinct and common tokens. The work introduces the concept of a 'scan and snap' dynamic, where attention patterns become sparse and stabilize due to a phase transition governed by learning rates. This approach provides new theoretical insights into how token combinations are formed and fixed during training, and establishes connections between learning rate schedules and the emergence of sparse, discriminative attention. The findings are validated both theoretically and empirically, and the framework sets the stage for further investigations into hierarchical token composition in multi-layer Transformers.

50ed3f80b5d8334be22b50bddba3a4c0dc9de036.title: Discrete Diffusion Models: Novel Analysis and New Sampler Guarantees
50ed3f80b5d8334be22b50bddba3a4c0dc9de036.research_question: Can discrete diffusion models be theoretically analyzed under relaxed assumptions, and can new convergence guarantees be established for practical samplers such as τ-leaping, Euler, and Tweedie τ-leaping, with improved dependence on vocabulary size and without restrictive regularity conditions?
50ed3f80b5d8334be22b50bddba3a4c0dc9de036.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a novel analytical framework based on differential inequalities can provide convergence guarantees for discrete diffusion model samplers without requiring hard-to-verify regularity assumptions, and that the convergence rates can be improved to scale linearly with vocabulary size for τ-leaping and similarly for other practical samplers.
50ed3f80b5d8334be22b50bddba3a4c0dc9de036.proposed_method: A new analytical framework will be developed to analyze discrete diffusion models, focusing on the rate-of-change of the KL-divergence between the true posterior and the sampling distribution. This approach will leverage direct application of the Kolmogorov equations for continuous-time Markov chains, rather than relying on the Girsanov change-of-measure technique, thus removing the need for regularity conditions such as path-wise local martingale assumptions. The framework will be applied to the τ-leaping sampler, as well as to the Euler and Tweedie τ-leaping methods, by constructing an approximate sampler with an explicit intermediate rate function that is asymptotically equivalent to these practical algorithms. The method will provide explicit convergence bounds in terms of the vocabulary size, data dimension, and score estimation error, and will characterize the dominant discretization error terms in expectation to achieve tighter parameter dependencies.
50ed3f80b5d8334be22b50bddba3a4c0dc9de036.experiment_details: Theoretical analysis will be conducted to derive convergence guarantees for the τ-leaping, Euler, and Tweedie τ-leaping samplers under standard score estimation and boundedness assumptions. The convergence rates will be explicitly characterized in terms of the number of steps required to achieve a target KL-divergence accuracy, with dependencies on vocabulary size (S), data dimension (d), and error tolerance (ε). Theoretical results will be compared against existing baselines from the literature, including uniformization and Kolmogorov samplers, with a focus on the order of dependence on S and d. Numerical experiments will be performed to validate the linear dependence on S and to compare the practical sampling complexity of the proposed samplers, using settings relevant to natural language processing tasks where S is large (e.g., S = 50257 for GPT-2). Evaluation metrics will include KL-divergence and total variation distance between the generated and target distributions.
50ed3f80b5d8334be22b50bddba3a4c0dc9de036.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a novel differential-inequality-based analytical framework for discrete diffusion models that eliminates the need for restrictive regularity assumptions required by previous Girsanov-based methods. It establishes the first convergence guarantees for the Euler and Tweedie τ-leaping samplers, and improves the convergence rate for τ-leaping to linear dependence on vocabulary size, which is a significant advancement over prior quadratic or higher-order results. The approach is broadly applicable to a wide class of practical samplers and may be of independent interest for the analysis of other stochastic processes.

510a068ba6ce4979202e309a0eafb82d6d89f243.title: Differentially Private Diffusion Models Generate Useful Synthetic Images
510a068ba6ce4979202e309a0eafb82d6d89f243.research_question: How can high-quality, privacy-preserving synthetic images be generated from sensitive datasets in a way that supports downstream machine learning tasks while providing formal privacy guarantees?
510a068ba6ce4979202e309a0eafb82d6d89f243.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that fine-tuning large, publicly pre-trained diffusion models with differential privacy mechanisms can produce synthetic image datasets that are both useful for downstream tasks and provably private, even under significant distribution shifts between pre-training and fine-tuning data.
510a068ba6ce4979202e309a0eafb82d6d89f243.proposed_method: A methodology will be developed to fine-tune large-scale denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs), pre-trained on public datasets such as ImageNet32, using differentially private stochastic gradient descent (DP-SGD) or DP-Adam. The approach will incorporate key strategies including virtual batching to enable large batch sizes (up to 32,768), augmentation multiplicity (combining image and timestep augmentations), and a modified timestep sampling distribution that focuses training on the most challenging phases of the diffusion process. The clipping norm and noise multiplier will be carefully tuned to balance privacy and utility, and the fine-tuning process will be adapted to handle significant distribution shifts between pre-training and target datasets. The method will also explore the impact of generating arbitrarily large synthetic datasets and ensembling downstream classifiers to maximize predictive performance.
510a068ba6ce4979202e309a0eafb82d6d89f243.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Camelyon17 datasets. For CIFAR-10 and Camelyon17, ImageNet32-pre-trained diffusion models with over 80M parameters will be fine-tuned using DP-SGD or DP-Adam under a privacy budget of (epsilon=10, delta=1e-5 or 3e-6). Synthetic datasets of varying sizes will be generated, and downstream classifiers (e.g., WideResNet, ResNet50, VGG) will be trained solely on synthetic data and evaluated on real test sets. Baselines will include state-of-the-art differentially private generative models and classifiers trained directly on real data with DP. Evaluation metrics will include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for image quality and top-1 classification accuracy for downstream utility. Additional experiments will assess the utility of synthetic data for model selection and hyperparameter tuning.
510a068ba6ce4979202e309a0eafb82d6d89f243.novelty_claims: The proposed approach enables fine-tuning of large, standard diffusion models with differential privacy to generate high-quality synthetic images that support accurate downstream classification, outperforming previous state-of-the-art results on challenging datasets such as CIFAR-10 and Camelyon17. Key innovations include the combination of public pre-training, virtual batching, augmentation multiplicity across both images and timesteps, and a novel, non-uniform timestep sampling strategy tailored for the DP setting. The method demonstrates that synthetic data can be leveraged for hyperparameter tuning and model selection without additional privacy cost, and that generating larger synthetic datasets and ensembling classifiers can further improve downstream performance.

51100655db50c0e534de188a12489324257adf60.title: Dynamic-LLaVA: Efficient Multimodal Large Language Models via Dynamic Vision-language Context Sparsification
51100655db50c0e534de188a12489324257adf60.research_question: How can the computational and memory efficiency of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) be improved throughout the entire generation process, including both the prefill and decoding stages, without degrading their vision understanding and generation abilities?
51100655db50c0e534de188a12489324257adf60.hypothesis: Dynamically sparsifying both vision and language contexts during inference in MLLMs will significantly reduce computation and memory overhead across all stages of generation, while maintaining or even improving model performance on vision understanding and text generation tasks.
51100655db50c0e534de188a12489324257adf60.proposed_method: A dynamic vision-language context sparsification framework, Dynamic-LLaVA, will be developed to reduce redundancy in both vision and language contexts during MLLM inference. The method employs two lightweight, learnable neural predictors: one for image tokens and one for output text tokens. These predictors generate binary masks that determine which tokens are retained or discarded after a selected decoder layer, with the decision shared across all subsequent layers. The framework tailors its sparsification strategy for three inference modes: prefill, decoding without KV cache, and decoding with KV cache. During training, end-to-end optimization is achieved using masked softmax in attention and Gumbel-Softmax with straight-through gradient estimation to ensure differentiability, along with regularization to control token keep rates. The approach is designed for easy integration with existing MLLMs and efficient vision encoders/projectors.
51100655db50c0e534de188a12489324257adf60.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using standard instruction-tuning datasets (e.g., 656K MixtureDataset as in LLaVA-1.5) for training. Evaluation will be performed on a comprehensive suite of vision understanding benchmarks, including VQAv2, GQA, VizWiz, SciQA, TextVQA, POPE, MMBench, SEED, MMVP, RealWorldQA, and CVBench-2D. Generation ability will be assessed using custom LVIS-VQA and ShareGPT4V-VQA benchmarks, measuring fluency (Perplexity, PPL) and answer similarity (METEOR). Baselines will include full-context MLLMs, state-of-the-art vision context sparsification methods (e.g., FastV, HiRED), efficient vision projector methods (e.g., TokenPacker), and KV cache compression approaches (e.g., H2O). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on vision tasks, PPL, METEOR, FLOPs, and GPU memory usage. Experiments will be run on 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs, with batch sizes and hyperparameters matched for fair comparison.
51100655db50c0e534de188a12489324257adf60.novelty_claims: Dynamic-LLaVA is the first framework to simultaneously sparsify both vision and language contexts in MLLMs, providing consistent efficiency gains throughout the entire generation process. The approach introduces learnable, end-to-end trainable predictors for dynamic token selection, tailored to different inference modes. It achieves up to 75% reduction in computation during prefill, and up to 50% reduction in computation and GPU memory during decoding, with negligible or even improved performance on vision and generation benchmarks. The framework is modular, easily integrates with existing MLLMs and efficient vision projectors, and supports parallel inference for practical deployment.

512fdb53eb341bc56769728274615c9bbe5bc23d.title: Flow Matching in Latent Space
512fdb53eb341bc56769728274615c9bbe5bc23d.research_question: How can flow matching generative models be made more computationally efficient and scalable for high-resolution image synthesis, and how can conditional generation tasks be effectively supported within this framework?
512fdb53eb341bc56769728274615c9bbe5bc23d.hypothesis: Applying flow matching in the latent space of pretrained autoencoders will significantly improve computational efficiency and scalability for high-resolution image synthesis, while maintaining or improving generation quality. Integrating classifier-free guidance and conditional inputs into the flow matching framework will enable effective conditional generation for tasks such as class-conditioned image generation, inpainting, and semantic-to-image synthesis.
512fdb53eb341bc56769728274615c9bbe5bc23d.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a latent flow matching framework that operates in the latent space of pretrained autoencoders (e.g., VAE from Stable Diffusion). Input images are first encoded into latent representations, and a neural network is trained to predict the velocity field that transports samples from a standard normal latent distribution to the target latent distribution, using a constant velocity ODE formulation. For conditional generation, the velocity field network is extended to accept conditional information (such as class labels, segmentation masks, or images), and classifier-free guidance is incorporated by jointly training the network with and without conditional inputs, enabling flexible control over conditional sampling without the need for a separate classifier. Sampling is performed by numerically integrating the learned ODE in latent space, and the resulting latent code is decoded to generate the output image. Theoretical analysis is provided to bound the Wasserstein-2 distance between the reconstructed and true data distributions, demonstrating that the latent flow matching objective controls this distance.
512fdb53eb341bc56769728274615c9bbe5bc23d.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on several high-resolution image datasets, including CelebA-HQ (256x256 and 512x512), FFHQ, LSUN Church, LSUN Bedroom, and Conditional ImageNet. Both unconditional and conditional generation tasks are evaluated, including class-conditioned image generation, image inpainting, and semantic-to-image synthesis. The method is benchmarked against state-of-the-art baselines such as LDM, FM, DDPM, StyleGAN, and others, using metrics like Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Recall, P-IDS, and U-IDS. Different backbone architectures (CNN-based UNet and transformer-based DiT) are tested, and various ODE solvers (adaptive, Euler, Heun) are compared for sampling efficiency. The experimental setup includes using pretrained VAE encoders/decoders, and all training and sampling are performed in the latent space.
512fdb53eb341bc56769728274615c9bbe5bc23d.novelty_claims: This proposal is the first to introduce flow matching in the latent space for high-resolution image synthesis, resulting in faster training and improved computational efficiency. It pioneers the integration of conditional inputs and classifier-free guidance into flow matching models, enabling versatile conditional generation tasks. Theoretical analysis is provided to bound the estimation error in terms of Wasserstein-2 distance, linking the latent flow matching objective to established generative model evaluation metrics. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the method achieves competitive or superior results compared to state-of-the-art diffusion and flow-based models, while significantly reducing computational requirements.

513ee6f0b00d3e4e6025df23f75c3baff9b11bce.title: Distance-Based Tree-Sliced Wasserstein Distance
513ee6f0b00d3e4e6025df23f75c3baff9b11bce.research_question: How can a new metric be developed for comparing probability measures in Euclidean spaces that preserves topological information, achieves computational efficiency, and remains invariant under Euclidean transformations, while overcoming the limitations of existing Sliced Wasserstein and Tree-Sliced Wasserstein distances?
513ee6f0b00d3e4e6025df23f75c3baff9b11bce.hypothesis: A class of distance-based, Euclidean-invariant splitting maps for projecting measures onto tree systems will yield a new Tree-Sliced Wasserstein distance that both preserves topological information and achieves computational efficiency, outperforming existing Sliced Wasserstein variants in accuracy and invariance.
513ee6f0b00d3e4e6025df23f75c3baff9b11bce.proposed_method: A novel metric, termed Distance-based Tree-Sliced Wasserstein (Db-TSW) distance, will be constructed by generalizing the splitting maps used in Tree-Sliced Wasserstein on Systems of Lines (TSW-SL). The method introduces E(d)-invariant splitting maps that depend on both the positions of data points and the configuration of tree systems, ensuring invariance under Euclidean transformations. The Radon Transform is extended to operate with these new splitting maps, and its injectivity is theoretically established under E(d)-invariance. Db-TSW is computed by projecting measures onto tree systems sampled from a distribution, using a distance-based softmax splitting map to distribute mass from points to lines, and then evaluating the closed-form Wasserstein distance on the resulting tree metric spaces. An efficient, GPU-friendly implementation is enabled by sampling tree systems with concurrent lines sharing a root, allowing for high parallelizability and linear runtime.
513ee6f0b00d3e4e6025df23f75c3baff9b11bce.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across several domains: unconditional image synthesis (using DDGAN variants on the CIFAR-10 dataset), gradient flows (on Swiss Roll and Gaussian 20d datasets), and color transfer tasks. For generative modeling, models will be trained for 1800 epochs, with consistent numbers of sampled lines across all methods, and performance will be measured using the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and per-epoch training time. In gradient flow experiments, average Wasserstein distances between source and target distributions will be tracked over multiple iterations and runs, with runtime per iteration reported. The color transfer task will evaluate Wasserstein distances between transferred and target color palettes, using both quantitative metrics and qualitative visualizations. Baselines will include vanilla Sliced Wasserstein, MaxSW, SWGG, LCVSW, TSW-SL, and recent Quasi-Sliced Wasserstein variants, with all methods using the same number of projections or tree systems for fair comparison.
513ee6f0b00d3e4e6025df23f75c3baff9b11bce.novelty_claims: Db-TSW introduces a new class of E(d)-invariant, distance-based splitting maps that generalize and improve upon prior approaches, enabling the metric to capture richer positional and topological information. The method resolves the lack of Euclidean invariance and limited positional sensitivity in previous Tree-Sliced Wasserstein distances. Theoretical contributions include a rigorous analysis of the injectivity of the new Radon Transform and proof that Db-TSW is a true metric and Euclidean invariant. The proposed tree sampling and projection mechanism enables efficient, highly parallelizable computation, matching or surpassing the runtime of vanilla SW. Empirical results demonstrate that Db-TSW achieves superior accuracy and efficiency compared to state-of-the-art Sliced Wasserstein variants across multiple tasks.

516a4c05883d4dc130bb7a638ad8e427b6756aac.title: One-Step Diffusion with Distribution Matching Distillation
516a4c05883d4dc130bb7a638ad8e427b6756aac.research_question: How can high-quality image generation be achieved in a single step using diffusion models, while maintaining fidelity comparable to multi-step diffusion models and significantly reducing computational cost?
516a4c05883d4dc130bb7a638ad8e427b6756aac.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a one-step image generator can be trained to closely match the distribution of images produced by a multi-step diffusion model, by leveraging a distribution matching distillation objective combined with a regression loss, resulting in comparable image quality at a fraction of the computational expense.
516a4c05883d4dc130bb7a638ad8e427b6756aac.proposed_method: A novel distillation framework, Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD), is proposed to transform a pretrained multi-step diffusion model into a one-step image generator. The method enforces distribution-level similarity between the outputs of the one-step generator and the original diffusion model by minimizing an approximate KL divergence, whose gradient is computed as the difference between two score functions—one for the real data distribution and one for the generator's synthetic distribution. Both score functions are parameterized by diffusion models, with the real score estimated by a fixed pretrained model and the fake score dynamically learned during training. Additionally, a regression loss is introduced, using a precomputed set of noise–image pairs from the teacher diffusion model, to regularize the generator and ensure it preserves the large-scale structure and diversity of the original model's outputs. The final training objective combines the distribution matching gradient and the regression loss, with careful weighting and noise perturbation strategies to stabilize optimization.
516a4c05883d4dc130bb7a638ad8e427b6756aac.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on class-conditional image generation tasks using CIFAR-10 and ImageNet 64×64, as well as zero-shot text-to-image generation on MS COCO 512×512. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art GANs and diffusion distillation baselines, including Consistency Models, Progressive Distillation, InstaFlow, and others, using identical teacher architectures where possible. Evaluation metrics will include Frechet Inception Distance (FID) for image quality and CLIP Score for text-image alignment. The experimental setup will involve precomputing paired datasets for regression loss, employing both Heun and PNDM solvers for teacher sampling, and testing various guidance scales and sample weighting strategies. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the distribution matching loss, regression loss, and sample weighting on performance.
516a4c05883d4dc130bb7a638ad8e427b6756aac.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled distribution matching distillation objective for training one-step diffusion generators, leveraging the difference of score functions from two diffusion models. The method uniquely combines this with a regression loss on precomputed teacher outputs, enabling high-fidelity, diverse image generation in a single forward pass. The framework is universally applicable to any pretrained diffusion model and achieves state-of-the-art results among few-step and one-step generators, with significant acceleration (up to 100× faster) and minimal quality degradation compared to the original multi-step models. The approach demonstrates, for the first time, that one-step generators can closely match the performance of large-scale diffusion models on challenging datasets and text-to-image tasks.

517f446ab3ff339459cab39cf12691d925d75a36.title: Probabilistically Robust Recourse: Navigating the Trade-offs between Costs and Robustness in Algorithmic Recourse
517f446ab3ff339459cab39cf12691d925d75a36.research_question: How can individuals adversely affected by machine learning model predictions be provided with actionable recourse options that allow for explicit control over the trade-off between implementation cost and robustness to noisy or imperfect execution of the recourse?
517f446ab3ff339459cab39cf12691d925d75a36.hypothesis: It is possible to develop an algorithmic framework that enables users to specify a desired probability of recourse invalidation, thereby generating recourses that are both cost-effective and robust to small perturbations in implementation, outperforming existing methods in terms of cost-robustness trade-offs.
517f446ab3ff339459cab39cf12691d925d75a36.proposed_method: A novel algorithmic framework, termed Probabilistically Robust Recourse (PROBE), will be developed to allow end users to specify a target recourse invalidation rate, representing the probability that a recourse becomes invalid under noisy implementation. The method introduces a new objective function that jointly minimizes the gap between the achieved and desired invalidation rates, the recourse cost (measured as the distance between the original and counterfactual instance), and ensures the recourse results in a favorable model prediction. The framework leverages theoretical results to derive closed-form or efficiently computable expressions for recourse invalidation rates for various model classes (e.g., linear, tree-based, neural networks) under Gaussian and other noise distributions. Optimization is performed via gradient-based methods, using local linear approximations where necessary, and the approach is extended to handle both differentiable and non-differentiable classifiers.
517f446ab3ff339459cab39cf12691d925d75a36.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using multiple real-world datasets, including the Adult (income prediction), Give Me Some Credit (credit scoring), and COMPAS (recidivism prediction) datasets, all normalized to [0,1]^d. Both linear (logistic regression) and non-linear (deep neural networks with ReLU activations) classifiers will be trained on these datasets. The proposed method will be compared against a range of baselines, including low-cost recourse methods (AR-LIME, Wachter, DICE, GS) and adversarially robust recourse methods (ARAR, ROAR), using implementations from the CARLA library. Evaluation metrics will include average recourse cost (ℓ1-norm), recourse accuracy (fraction of successful recourses), and average recourse invalidation rate (empirically estimated via Monte Carlo sampling with added Gaussian noise). Hyperparameters such as the invalidation target r and noise magnitude σ^2 will be systematically varied, and Pareto frontiers will be plotted to visualize the cost-robustness trade-off.
517f446ab3ff339459cab39cf12691d925d75a36.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to enable end users to explicitly navigate and control the trade-off between recourse cost and robustness by specifying a target invalidation probability. It introduces a new objective function and theoretical characterizations of recourse invalidation rates for a variety of model classes and noise distributions. The approach provides efficient optimization procedures, including closed-form solutions and local approximations, and demonstrates superior empirical performance in generating robust, low-cost recourses compared to both standard and adversarially robust baselines. The framework generalizes to both linear and non-linear models and offers practical agency to individuals seeking recourse.

5181d511526c41bc5dc160ce71f4f7f7b4bdf188.title: Attribution-based Explanations that Provide Recourse Cannot be Robust
5181d511526c41bc5dc160ce71f4f7f7b4bdf188.research_question: Can attribution-based explanation methods for machine learning simultaneously provide actionable recourse to users and maintain robustness to small changes in input features, under general conditions and utility functions?
5181d511526c41bc5dc160ce71f4f7f7b4bdf188.hypothesis: No single attribution method can, in general, be both robust (continuous) and recourse sensitive for all machine learning models and utility functions; there exists a fundamental incompatibility between these two properties.
5181d511526c41bc5dc160ce71f4f7f7b4bdf188.proposed_method: A formal theoretical framework will be developed to define and analyze the concepts of recourse sensitivity and robustness for attribution-based explanation methods. Recourse sensitivity will be formalized via a utility function that captures the user's ability to achieve a desired outcome by making limited changes to input features, constrained by a distance metric and possible feature constraints. Robustness will be defined as continuity of the attribution method with respect to the input. Theoretical impossibility results will be derived, demonstrating that for any utility function and sufficiently expressive model class, there exists a model for which no attribution method can satisfy both properties simultaneously. Analytical and empirical counterexamples will be constructed for popular attribution methods (e.g., LIME, SHAP, Integrated Gradients, SmoothGrad) and counterfactual explanations, illustrating the impossibility in practice. Sufficient conditions under which both properties can coexist will also be investigated, and potential workarounds such as set-valued attributions or restrictions on the model class will be explored.
5181d511526c41bc5dc160ce71f4f7f7b4bdf188.experiment_details: Experiments will include both analytical constructions and empirical demonstrations. Analytical examples will use simple functions (e.g., quadratic and exponential functions) in low-dimensional settings to show where attribution methods fail to be recourse sensitive or robust. Empirical experiments will be conducted on a profile picture classification task, where attribution methods generate saliency maps for images, and recourse is defined as the ability to modify the image to achieve acceptance by the classifier. Attribution methods including LIME (manual and automatic superpixel segmentation), SHAP, SmoothGrad, and Integrated Gradients will be compared. Evaluation will focus on whether the attributions provide actionable recourse and whether they are robust to small input perturbations. The setup will include varying the input images and measuring the continuity and recourse sensitivity of the resulting attributions.
5181d511526c41bc5dc160ce71f4f7f7b4bdf188.novelty_claims: The proposal establishes a general impossibility theorem showing that no attribution-based explanation method can be both robust and recourse sensitive for all models and utility functions, even for continuous models and mild user constraints. This result is shown to apply broadly, including to popular attribution methods and counterfactual explanations. The framework generalizes previous empirical and theoretical findings by formalizing the trade-off between robustness and recourse, and by providing sufficient and necessary conditions for when both properties can coexist. The work also proposes new directions, such as set-valued attributions and characterizations for special cases, to potentially circumvent the impossibility.

51a000239cda4aece95d79927f67943d819d42cd.title: Exploring and Interacting with the Set of Good Sparse Generalized Additive Models
51a000239cda4aece95d79927f67943d819d42cd.research_question: How can the set of all near-optimal sparse generalized additive models (GAMs) be efficiently approximated and explored to facilitate interactive model selection and editing by domain experts, and how can this set be leveraged to address practical challenges such as variable importance analysis, constraint satisfaction, and understanding model variability?
51a000239cda4aece95d79927f67943d819d42cd.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the Rashomon set of sparse GAMs can be efficiently and accurately approximated using ellipsoidal methods, enabling practical and interactive exploration of model space, and that this approximation will support a range of downstream tasks including variable importance analysis, constraint-based model search, and robust investigation of model shape functions.
51a000239cda4aece95d79927f67943d819d42cd.proposed_method: A novel methodology will be developed to approximate the Rashomon set—the set of all sparse GAMs whose loss is within a threshold of the optimal—using maximum-volume inscribed ellipsoids for fixed support sets. The approach involves formulating the loss function for sparse GAMs with regularization, then using gradient-based optimization to fit an ellipsoid that tightly inscribes the Rashomon set, initialized via a Hessian-based quadratic approximation. To efficiently handle multiple support sets, a blocking method will be introduced, allowing ellipsoidal approximations for smaller support sets to be derived analytically from those of larger sets by intersecting the ellipsoid with appropriate hyperplanes. These approximations will be leveraged to enable practical tasks such as variable importance range estimation (via linear and mixed-integer programming), monotonicity-constrained model search (via quadratic programming), and user-guided model editing (via projection onto the Rashomon set).
51a000239cda4aece95d79927f67943d819d42cd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four real-world datasets: COMPAS (recidivism), FICO (credit risk), Diabetes, and MIMIC-II (ICU data). The proposed Rashomon set approximation will be evaluated for precision and volume relative to the true Rashomon set, using metrics such as the proportion of approximated models within the true set (precision) and the overlap in volume (recall). Baselines will include ellipsoidal approximations based on Hessian initialization, identity matrix (spherical) approximations, and minimum-volume ellipsoids covering bootstrapped coefficient vectors from logistic regression and Explainable Boosting Machines (EBMs). Additional experiments will demonstrate the utility of the Rashomon set in estimating variable importance ranges, finding models under monotonicity constraints, and investigating the robustness of sudden changes in GAM shape functions. Sampling from the approximated Rashomon set and solving associated optimization problems will be used to support these analyses.
51a000239cda4aece95d79927f67943d819d42cd.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first method to efficiently and accurately approximate the Rashomon set for sparse generalized additive models, enabling interactive exploration and editing of interpretable models. The ellipsoidal approximation framework supports a range of practical tasks—including variable importance range analysis, constraint-based model search, and robust investigation of shape function variability—that were previously infeasible for GAMs. The blocking method for efficiently handling multiple support sets further enhances scalability and usability. This paradigm shift empowers domain experts to interact with and select from a diverse set of near-optimal models, overcoming the limitations of the classical single-model machine learning paradigm.

51b93b9a5e5e51d0846f45f54875698ccdd6c231.title: GS-IR: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Inverse Rendering
