51b93b9a5e5e51d0846f45f54875698ccdd6c231.research_question: How can the physical attributes of a 3D scene—including geometry, material properties, and illumination—be accurately and efficiently estimated from multi-view images captured under unknown lighting conditions, enabling high-quality inverse rendering, novel view synthesis, and relighting?
51b93b9a5e5e51d0846f45f54875698ccdd6c231.hypothesis: A 3D Gaussian Splatting-based scene representation, combined with forward mapping volume rendering and novel optimization schemes for normal estimation and indirect illumination modeling, can achieve efficient, high-fidelity inverse rendering and outperform existing neural field-based methods in both quality and speed.
51b93b9a5e5e51d0846f45f54875698ccdd6c231.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces GS-IR, a three-stage inverse rendering framework leveraging 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) as the core scene representation. In the initial stage, differentiable forward splatting is used to optimize 3D Gaussians for geometry reconstruction, with a depth-derivation-based regularization guiding the estimation of surface normals. The second stage precomputes occlusion information by baking it into spherical harmonics-based volumes, enabling efficient modeling of indirect illumination without backward ray tracing. In the final stage, a physically-based rendering (PBR) pipeline is integrated with the optimized 3D Gaussians, allowing for joint optimization of material properties, environment illumination, and indirect lighting. The method stores not only color and opacity but also normal and material parameters in each Gaussian, and employs loss terms for color, normal consistency, material smoothness, and illumination regularization.
51b93b9a5e5e51d0846f45f54875698ccdd6c231.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the TensoIR Synthetic dataset and the Mip-NeRF 360 real-world dataset, covering both object-level and unbounded scene-level inverse rendering tasks. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art neural field-based inverse rendering methods such as NeRFactor, InvRender, NVDiffrec, and TensoIR. Evaluation metrics will include mean angular error (MAE) for normal estimation, PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS for novel view synthesis, albedo reconstruction, and relighting quality. Training time and rendering efficiency will also be assessed. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of different depth and normal estimation strategies, as well as the contributions of occlusion and indirect illumination modeling.
51b93b9a5e5e51d0846f45f54875698ccdd6c231.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first inverse rendering framework based on 3D Gaussian Splatting, enabling fast, compact, and expressive scene representations for physically-based rendering. Key innovations include a depth-derivation-based regularization for robust normal estimation in the 3DGS context and a baking-based method for efficient indirect illumination modeling using spherical harmonics. The method achieves state-of-the-art results in novel view synthesis and material decomposition, with significant improvements in training and rendering speed compared to previous neural field-based approaches. The approach supports real-time rendering and high-quality relighting, demonstrating superior performance on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

51db4c39dc0bdf5c95c8bbe89bf4211b48d0b4df.title: SpQR: A Sparse-Quantized Representation for Near-Lossless LLM Weight Compression
51db4c39dc0bdf5c95c8bbe89bf4211b48d0b4df.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be compressed to extremely low bit-widths (3-4 bits per parameter) for efficient deployment on memory-limited devices, while maintaining near-lossless accuracy across a range of model sizes?
51db4c39dc0bdf5c95c8bbe89bf4211b48d0b4df.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a hybrid sparse-quantized representation, which isolates and stores quantization-sensitive outlier weights in higher precision while aggressively quantizing the remaining weights, can achieve near-lossless compression of LLMs at 3-4 bits per parameter, outperforming existing quantization methods in both accuracy and efficiency.
51db4c39dc0bdf5c95c8bbe89bf4211b48d0b4df.proposed_method: A novel compression framework, termed Sparse-Quantized Representation (SpQR), will be developed for LLM weight matrices. The method begins with a sensitivity analysis to identify outlier weights that contribute disproportionately to quantization error; these outliers are retained in high precision (e.g., 16 bits) and stored using a compressed sparse row (CSR) format. The remaining weights are quantized to 3-4 bits using a two-level groupwise quantization scheme: small groups of weights (e.g., 8-32) share quantization statistics, and these statistics themselves are further quantized. The quantization process is guided by a post-training quantization (PTQ) approach, leveraging calibration data to minimize the L2 error between the original and quantized model outputs. Efficient GPU inference algorithms will be implemented to decode the SpQR format, combining dense and sparse matrix multiplication for optimal performance.
51db4c39dc0bdf5c95c8bbe89bf4211b48d0b4df.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on publicly available LLMs, specifically the LLaMA (7B, 13B, 30B, 65B) and Falcon (7B, 40B) model families. Quantization will be performed using the RedPajama and RefinedWeb datasets for calibration. Baseline methods will include GPTQ and round-to-nearest (RTN) quantization, both at 4 bits per parameter. Evaluation metrics will include perplexity on WikiText2, Penn Treebank, and C4 datasets, as well as zero-shot accuracy on tasks such as WinoGrande, PiQA, HellaSwag, ARC-easy, and ARC-challenge. Inference speed will be measured on an NVIDIA A100 GPU, comparing custom SpQR kernels to standard PyTorch sparse matrix multiplication and 16-bit baselines. Ablation studies will assess the impact of group size, quantization of statistics, and outlier selection strategies.
51db4c39dc0bdf5c95c8bbe89bf4211b48d0b4df.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first near-lossless 3-4 bit quantization method for LLMs that maintains accuracy within 1% of the original 16-bit models across a wide range of model sizes. Key innovations include a sensitivity-driven outlier detection mechanism, a bilevel groupwise quantization scheme with quantized statistics, and an efficient hybrid sparse-dense inference algorithm. The method enables substantial memory compression (over 4x) and significant inference speedups (20-30%) compared to 16-bit baselines, making it feasible to deploy large LLMs on consumer hardware without accuracy degradation.

51f63473297b458041fe03a63b9697324ac341f3.title: Towards World Simulator: Crafting Physical Commonsense-Based Benchmark for Video Generation
51f63473297b458041fe03a63b9697324ac341f3.research_question: To what extent do current text-to-video (T2V) generation models demonstrate an understanding of physical commonsense, and how can their ability to represent intuitive physics be systematically evaluated?
51f63473297b458041fe03a63b9697324ac341f3.hypothesis: Current T2V models lack sufficient understanding of physical commonsense, and existing evaluation metrics and benchmarks are inadequate for assessing this aspect. A purpose-built benchmark and hierarchical evaluation framework will enable more accurate and human-aligned assessment of physical commonsense in generated videos.
51f63473297b458041fe03a63b9697324ac341f3.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark, PhyGenBench, will be constructed to evaluate physical commonsense in T2V generation. This benchmark will cover four fundamental domains—mechanics, optics, thermal, and material properties—by curating 160 prompts based on 27 distinct physical laws, each designed to elicit clear, observable physical phenomena. The construction pipeline involves conceptualizing key physical laws, manually crafting initial prompts, augmenting prompts for diversity using advanced language models, and performing rigorous quality control to ensure clarity and relevance. Alongside the benchmark, an automated evaluation framework, PhyGenEval, will be developed. PhyGenEval will employ a three-tier hierarchical evaluation strategy: (1) key physical phenomena detection using vision-language models (VLMs) and custom GPT-4o-generated questions, (2) verification of the correct temporal order of physical events, and (3) assessment of overall naturalness and realism of the physical process. Each stage will utilize state-of-the-art VLMs and tailored instructions to ensure robust and fine-grained evaluation.
51f63473297b458041fe03a63b9697324ac341f3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by generating videos from multiple state-of-the-art open-source and proprietary T2V models using the PhyGenBench prompts. The models to be evaluated include OpenSoraV1.2, Lavie, CogVideoX (2b and 5b), Vchitect2.0, Kling, Pika, and Gen-3. For each model, 64 prompts will be randomly selected to produce 512 videos in total, which will be evaluated both automatically (using PhyGenEval and existing metrics such as VideoScore, DEVIL, and VideoPhy) and by human annotators. Human evaluators will score videos on semantic and physical correctness using a four-point scale, and the correlation between human and automated scores will be measured using Kendall’s tau and Spearman’s rho. The evaluation will focus on both overall and category-specific (mechanics, optics, thermal, material) performance, and qualitative case studies will be included to highlight the strengths and limitations of each approach.
51f63473297b458041fe03a63b9697324ac341f3.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first comprehensive benchmark (PhyGenBench) specifically designed to assess physical commonsense in T2V generation, covering a broad range of physical laws and phenomena. The hierarchical evaluation framework (PhyGenEval) represents a novel approach by decomposing the assessment into semantic alignment, key physical phenomena detection, temporal order verification, and overall naturalness, leveraging advanced vision-language models and GPT-4o-generated instructions. This framework achieves high consistency with human judgments and addresses the limitations of traditional video evaluation metrics, enabling large-scale, automated, and physically grounded assessment of T2V models.

51f7f1e6658d55bce7f9cba3545f4462cae840bc.title: Fixed Design Analysis of Regularization-Based Continual Learning
51f7f1e6658d55bce7f9cba3545f4462cae840bc.research_question: How can regularization-based continual learning algorithms be theoretically analyzed in the fixed design setting, and what are the fundamental trade-offs between forgetting and intransigence when learning multiple sequential tasks with limited memory?
51f7f1e6658d55bce7f9cba3545f4462cae840bc.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that in a continual learning setting with two linear regression tasks, an ℓ2-regularized approach can provide a provable trade-off between forgetting and intransigence, and that the regularization parameter can be tuned to mitigate catastrophic forgetting when tasks are moderately dissimilar, but may be insufficient for extremely dissimilar tasks.
51f7f1e6658d55bce7f9cba3545f4462cae840bc.proposed_method: The proposed method focuses on a continual learning algorithm for two linear regression tasks in the fixed design setting, where feature vectors are fixed and labels are random variables. The approach consists of first fitting an ordinary least squares (OLS) model to the first task and storing the resulting parameter vector as long-term memory. Upon receiving the second task, the method fits a new parameter vector to the second dataset, incorporating an ℓ2-regularization term that penalizes deviation from the parameter learned on the first task. The regularization parameter µ controls the strength of this penalty, thereby adjusting the balance between retaining information from the first task (reducing forgetting) and adapting to the second task (reducing intransigence). Theoretical risk bounds are derived for the joint population risk, decomposing it into explicit terms for forgetting and intransigence, and providing conditions under which the algorithm succeeds or fails. The analysis also explores the effects of task similarity, data covariance alignment, and the limitations of the approach.
51f7f1e6658d55bce7f9cba3545f4462cae840bc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic datasets where the data covariance matrices for the two tasks are constructed with varying degrees of similarity, as controlled by their eigenvalue alignment. The dimension of the tasks is set (e.g., d = 200), and sample sizes are varied to study convergence rates. The proposed ℓ2-regularized continual learning algorithm is compared against ordinary continual learning (OCL, no regularization) and joint learning (JL, which has access to all data simultaneously and serves as an upper baseline). Evaluation metrics include the expected excess risk, as well as explicit measures of forgetting and intransigence. Results will be averaged over multiple independent runs to ensure statistical validity, and the impact of the regularization parameter µ will be systematically explored.
51f7f1e6658d55bce7f9cba3545f4462cae840bc.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a sharp theoretical analysis of regularization-based continual learning in the fixed design setting, establishing tight risk bounds that explicitly decompose performance into forgetting and intransigence components. The analysis provides a precise characterization of the trade-off between these two phenomena, controlled by the regularization parameter. The work identifies conditions under which catastrophic forgetting occurs and demonstrates that a well-tuned regularization can mitigate forgetting at the cost of intransigence. Furthermore, it highlights fundamental limitations of ℓ2-regularization, showing that for highly dissimilar tasks, no choice of regularization can simultaneously minimize both forgetting and intransigence, thus motivating the need for more advanced regularization strategies.

5214d8d22efe5629f6d146e0517604d5eabb703d.title: RanDumb: Random Representations Outperform Online Continually Learned Representations
5214d8d22efe5629f6d146e0517604d5eabb703d.research_question: Can fixed random or pretrained representations, combined with a simple linear classifier, outperform continually learned representations in online and low-exemplar continual learning scenarios, and what does this imply about the efficacy of current representation learning strategies and benchmarks in continual learning?
5214d8d22efe5629f6d146e0517604d5eabb703d.hypothesis: Fixed random or pretrained representations, when paired with a simple linear classifier, will outperform or match the performance of representations learned online in continual learning settings, particularly in exemplar-free or low-exemplar regimes.
5214d8d22efe5629f6d146e0517604d5eabb703d.proposed_method: A new approach is proposed that replaces online-learned deep feature extractors with a fixed random projection using random Fourier features, approximating an RBF kernel, to map raw input pixels into a high-dimensional space. This embedding is followed by a decorrelation step using a Mahalanobis distance metric with an online-estimated, shrinkage-regularized covariance matrix. Classification is performed via a nearest class mean (NCM) classifier in the transformed space. The method requires no exemplar storage and processes data in a strictly online, one-sample-at-a-time fashion, updating only the class means and covariance statistics. In scenarios where pretrained feature extractors are available, the method fixes the backbone and only learns the linear classifier, without further representation adaptation.
5214d8d22efe5629f6d146e0517604d5eabb703d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a comprehensive set of continual learning benchmarks, including online and offline settings, with an emphasis on exemplar-free and low-exemplar storage regimes. Datasets to be used include MNIST, CIFAR10, CIFAR100, TinyImageNet, miniImageNet, and several others in the LAMDA-PILOT suite. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art online continual learning methods (e.g., VAE-GC, SLCA, PEC, ER, iCaRL, DER, GDumb, and various prompt-tuning and network expansion methods), as well as joint training and rehearsal-based approaches. Evaluation metrics will primarily be average classification accuracy across all seen tasks after the final task, under strict online or offline continual learning constraints. Experimental setups will vary the number of classes per task, memory buffer sizes, use of augmentations, and embedding dimensionality, with ablations to assess the contribution of each component.
5214d8d22efe5629f6d146e0517604d5eabb703d.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first exemplar-free continual learning approach that leverages random Fourier feature embeddings and online Mahalanobis decorrelation, demonstrating that such fixed representations can outperform or match state-of-the-art continually learned representations. The study challenges the prevailing assumption that online representation learning is necessary for effective continual learning, especially in low-exemplar and online settings. It further provides evidence that current benchmarks may be overly restrictive and not conducive to advancing representation learning, as simple fixed representations recover most of the performance gap to joint training. The method is computationally efficient, requires no exemplar storage, and is broadly applicable across datasets and architectures.

522ac9eb08bb0c5a422700bb254ea1c44e9157de.title: Discovered Policy Optimisation
522ac9eb08bb0c5a422700bb254ea1c44e9157de.research_question: Can reinforcement learning algorithms be automatically discovered within a theoretically grounded framework, leading to improved performance and generalization compared to hand-crafted algorithms?
522ac9eb08bb0c5a422700bb254ea1c44e9157de.hypothesis: Meta-learning a drift function within the Mirror Learning framework will yield reinforcement learning algorithms that outperform existing hand-crafted methods such as PPO, while inheriting theoretical convergence guarantees and demonstrating superior robustness and generalization.
522ac9eb08bb0c5a422700bb254ea1c44e9157de.proposed_method: A meta-learning approach will be developed to discover a new reinforcement learning algorithm within the Mirror Learning framework by parameterizing the drift function as a neural network. This drift function will take as input the probability ratio between candidate and old policies, as well as the normalized advantage, and will be meta-trained using Evolution Strategies (ES) to maximize the expected return after a fixed number of training iterations. The neural network architecture will be carefully designed to ensure the drift function satisfies the necessary theoretical properties (non-negativity, zero at identity, zero gradient at identity), using shifted ReLU activations and no bias terms. To facilitate learning and generalization, the drift function may be initialized near that of PPO, allowing the meta-learning process to discover improvements over the PPO baseline. Insights gained from analyzing the learned drift function will be used to formulate a new, closed-form, parameter-free algorithm called Discovered Policy Optimisation (DPO), which captures the key features discovered during meta-learning.
522ac9eb08bb0c5a422700bb254ea1c44e9157de.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of continuous control tasks using the Brax physics simulator, leveraging its capability for highly parallelized training. The meta-training of the drift function will be performed across multiple Brax environments, with both from-scratch and PPO-initialized variants. The resulting algorithms (LPO and DPO) will be compared to PPO using the same policy architectures and training hyperparameters, with no additional tuning for the new methods. Evaluation metrics will include mean evaluation return across multiple seeds, robustness to hyperparameter changes, and generalization to unseen environments. Additional transfer experiments will be conducted on out-of-distribution tasks, such as the Minatar environments, to assess generalization. Baselines will include PPO and, where appropriate, other meta-learned or hand-crafted algorithms.
522ac9eb08bb0c5a422700bb254ea1c44e9157de.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to meta-learn a drift function within the Mirror Learning framework, resulting in algorithms that inherit theoretical convergence guarantees by construction. The method enables the discovery of both neural and closed-form algorithms (LPO and DPO) that outperform PPO in terms of performance, robustness, and generalization, without requiring hand-crafted design. The analysis of the learned drift function provides novel algorithmic insights, such as rollback for negative advantages and cautious optimism for positive advantages, which are incorporated into the closed-form DPO algorithm. DPO is claimed to be the first theoretically sound, scalable deep RL algorithm discovered via meta-learning, and can be implemented as easily as PPO.

523a1667a4815c8365b11e5c744437637474dd56.title: Compute Optimal Inference and Provable Amortisation Gap in Sparse Autoencoders
523a1667a4815c8365b11e5c744437637474dd56.research_question: How can the limitations of standard sparse autoencoders for recovering interpretable, sparse features from neural network activations be addressed, and what are the conditions under which more sophisticated sparse inference methods yield improved interpretability and accuracy in both synthetic and real-world neural data, such as large language model activations?
523a1667a4815c8365b11e5c744437637474dd56.hypothesis: Standard sparse autoencoders, due to their linear-nonlinear encoder architecture, are inherently suboptimal for accurate sparse inference, even in theoretically recoverable regimes. More expressive or optimised sparse inference methods, such as multilayer perceptrons or inference-time optimisation, can achieve superior recovery of sparse codes and more interpretable features with minimal additional computational cost.
523a1667a4815c8365b11e5c744437637474dd56.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed to decouple the encoding and decoding processes in sparse autoencoders, enabling direct comparison of multiple sparse inference strategies. Four encoding schemes will be implemented: (1) standard sparse autoencoders with linear-nonlinear encoders, (2) multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) with varying hidden layer widths, (3) sparse coding via iterative optimisation of sparse coefficients, and (4) SAE with inference-time optimisation (SAE+ITO), which uses the learned decoder but optimises the latent codes per input. Theoretical analysis will establish provable suboptimality (amortisation gap) of standard SAEs using compressed sensing theory, while empirical studies will systematically evaluate each method's ability to recover ground-truth sparse codes. Technical steps include generating synthetic datasets with known sparse codes and dictionaries, training each method under controlled conditions, and extending evaluation to real-world neural activations from large language models.
523a1667a4815c8365b11e5c744437637474dd56.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic data will be generated by projecting sparse latent codes through random dictionaries, with parameters varied across number of sources (N), measurements (M), and active components (K). Evaluation will include scenarios with known codes, known dictionaries, and fully unknown settings. Baselines will include standard SAEs, MLPs, sparse coding, and SAE+ITO. Metrics will include Mean Correlation Coefficient (MCC) for both latent code recovery and dictionary alignment, as well as reconstruction error and interpretability scores (using automated GPT-4o-based feature explanation and validation). For real-world evaluation, the methods will be applied to activations from GPT-2, with interpretability assessed via automated classification of feature semantics. Computational cost (FLOPs) and trade-offs between sparsity and performance will also be systematically measured.
523a1667a4815c8365b11e5c744437637474dd56.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretical proof of the amortisation gap for standard sparse autoencoders, demonstrating inherent limitations in their ability to achieve optimal sparse recovery. It systematically decouples encoding and decoding, enabling rigorous empirical comparison of advanced inference methods, including MLPs and inference-time optimisation, in both synthetic and large language model settings. The approach provides the first comprehensive, automated interpretability evaluation of features extracted by different sparse inference strategies, challenging the prevailing assumption that simpler encoders are necessary for interpretability. This work opens new avenues for principled evaluation and improvement of feature extraction in neural network interpretability research.

524592df63de980ea53f95b1c82fb46161d8e330.title: Can Large Language Models Understand Intermediate Representations?
524592df63de980ea53f95b1c82fb46161d8e330.research_question: Can large language models (LLMs) comprehend and reason over compiler intermediate representations (IRs) across multiple dimensions, including structural analysis, syntax and semantic understanding, and execution reasoning?
524592df63de980ea53f95b1c82fb46161d8e330.hypothesis: LLMs, when evaluated on IR-specific tasks, will exhibit limitations in instruction-level reasoning, control flow comprehension, and execution simulation, but targeted enhancements such as fine-tuning on structured IR datasets and integration of control-flow-sensitive architectures may improve their effectiveness.
524592df63de980ea53f95b1c82fb46161d8e330.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical evaluation will be conducted to systematically assess LLMs' understanding of compiler IRs. The methodology will involve designing four core tasks: (1) reconstructing control flow graphs (CFGs) from IRs to probe structural understanding, (2) decompiling IRs to high-level source code to assess syntactic comprehension, (3) generating natural language summaries of IR behavior to evaluate semantic understanding, and (4) simulating program execution by predicting assertion outcomes to test execution reasoning. Each task will utilize expert-designed meta-prompts, including few-shot and chain-of-thought prompting, to elicit detailed and structured responses from the models. Multiple state-of-the-art LLMs will be evaluated, and their outputs will be compared to ground truth using rigorous, task-specific metrics.
524592df63de980ea53f95b1c82fb46161d8e330.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a benchmark dataset derived from HumanEval, consisting of 164 C++ programs and their corresponding LLVM IRs, compiled at four optimization levels (-O0 to -O3) to ensure diversity in code structure. Six LLMs—GPT-4, GPT-3, DeepSeek, Gemma 2, Llama3, and CodeLlama—will be evaluated across all tasks. For CFG reconstruction, accuracy will be measured at both node and edge levels, including loop and conditional branch correctness. Decompilation will be assessed using metrics for syntactic validity, execution success, and assertion correctness. Code summarization quality will be evaluated with BLEU, ROUGE-L, and METEOR scores. Execution reasoning will be measured by the correctness of predicted assertion outcomes, with pass rates reported for both IR and source code inputs. Prompt engineering strategies will be iteratively refined to maximize model performance and consistency.
524592df63de980ea53f95b1c82fb46161d8e330.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first systematic, multi-dimensional evaluation of LLMs' comprehension of compiler IRs, spanning structural, syntactic, semantic, and execution reasoning tasks. It establishes a new empirical benchmark for IR understanding, identifies critical limitations in current LLMs—such as insufficient control flow awareness and reliance on heuristic reasoning—and proposes targeted directions for model improvement, including IR-specific fine-tuning and control-flow-sensitive architecture design.

524889248251669b110adf86c4380444ec5448f4.title: Fast Point Cloud Generation with Straight Flows
524889248251669b110adf86c4380444ec5448f4.research_question: How can the efficiency of 3D point cloud generation be improved to enable high-quality, real-time applications, without sacrificing sample quality compared to state-of-the-art diffusion-based methods?
524889248251669b110adf86c4380444ec5448f4.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that optimizing the generative transport trajectory from noise to data as a straight path, and distilling this process into a one-step neural flow, can enable the generation of high-quality 3D point clouds with significantly reduced computational cost and latency.
524889248251669b110adf86c4380444ec5448f4.proposed_method: A new approach, PointStraightFlow (PSF), is developed to generate 3D point clouds in a single step by learning a straight generative transport trajectory from random noise to target shapes. The method consists of three main stages: (1) training a neural velocity flow network to model the ODE-based transport from Gaussian noise to data distribution; (2) applying a reflow procedure to optimize and straighten the learned trajectory, reducing the transport cost and making the generative path as straight as possible; and (3) distilling the refined flow into a one-step generator using a permutation-invariant loss (Chamfer distance) to ensure that a single update produces samples of similar quality to multi-step methods. The final model enables direct sampling from noise to data in one forward pass, facilitating real-time applications.
524889248251669b110adf86c4380444ec5448f4.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on multiple 3D point cloud tasks, including unconditional generation, training-free text-guided generation, and point cloud completion. Standard datasets and splits from prior works (e.g., PointFlow, PVD) are used, with classes such as Airplane, Chair, Car, and a 55-class dataset. Baselines include VAE-based, GAN-based, normalizing flow, and diffusion-based models (notably PVD and PVD-DDIM). Evaluation metrics include Chamfer Distance (CD), Earth Mover's Distance (EMD), and one-nearest-neighbor accuracy (1-NNA), with sampling time measured on Nvidia RTX 3090 GPUs. The PSF model is compared against baselines in terms of both sample quality and inference speed, and ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of trajectory straightness and distillation loss choices.
524889248251669b110adf86c4380444ec5448f4.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to demonstrate that a neural flow trained with a one-step distillation strategy can generate high-quality 3D point clouds, matching or surpassing the quality of multi-step diffusion models while being orders of magnitude faster. The approach introduces a novel three-stage pipeline that straightens the generative trajectory and distills it into a single-step process, enabling real-time applications such as point cloud completion and text-guided generation. The use of a permutation-invariant loss (Chamfer distance) for distillation is specifically tailored for unordered point cloud data, further enhancing the effectiveness of the method.

525d93a382f6e7873b5d8a2e0713eb3dff7fb250.title: Transformers learn in-context by gradient descent
525d93a382f6e7873b5d8a2e0713eb3dff7fb250.research_question: What are the underlying mechanisms that enable in-context learning in Transformers, and can these mechanisms be mechanistically explained or approximated by gradient-based meta-learning algorithms?
525d93a382f6e7873b5d8a2e0713eb3dff7fb250.hypothesis: When trained on auto-regressive objectives, Transformers implement in-context learning in their forward pass via gradient-based optimization of an implicit loss constructed from in-context data, effectively performing gradient descent or its variants within their architecture.
525d93a382f6e7873b5d8a2e0713eb3dff7fb250.proposed_method: The proposed approach involves constructing explicit weights for linear self-attention layers such that the data transformations induced by these layers are mathematically equivalent to one or more steps of gradient descent on a regression loss. The methodology starts with a mechanistic construction for a single linear self-attention layer, then extends this to multi-layer (deep) Transformers, showing that stacking layers corresponds to iterative gradient-based updates, potentially with curvature correction. The method further incorporates multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) preceding self-attention to enable nonlinear regression tasks, effectively allowing the Transformer to learn linear models on deep, meta-learned data representations. Additionally, the proposal investigates how Transformers can internally construct the required token representations (e.g., by copying mechanisms) to facilitate in-context gradient-based learning, even when the input tokenization does not directly align with the required structure.
525d93a382f6e7873b5d8a2e0713eb3dff7fb250.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic regression tasks, including both linear and nonlinear (e.g., sine wave) regression, using teacher models to generate ground truth data. The experimental setup includes training Transformers with varying depths and architectures (linear self-attention only, with and without MLPs, and with softmax attention), and comparing their in-context learning performance to explicit gradient descent baselines and meta-learned MLPs with output layer adaptation. Evaluation metrics include prediction loss (mean squared error), alignment between learned models and gradient descent solutions (measured by cosine similarity and L2 distance of predictions and gradients), and generalization to out-of-distribution tasks (e.g., varying input scales or teacher weights). Additional analyses will examine the ability of Transformers to internally construct suitable token representations and the effect of architectural choices such as softmax vs. linear attention.
525d93a382f6e7873b5d8a2e0713eb3dff7fb250.novelty_claims: The proposal claims a mechanistic equivalence between in-context learning in Transformers and gradient-based meta-learning, providing explicit constructions that show how self-attention layers can implement gradient descent updates. It introduces the idea that stacking self-attention layers corresponds to iterative, potentially curvature-corrected, gradient updates, and extends this to nonlinear regression via MLPs. The work also identifies and explains the role of token construction and copying mechanisms in enabling gradient-based in-context learning. These insights offer a new perspective on the emergence of learning algorithms within Transformer architectures and suggest that in-context learning can be understood as an emergent property of meta-optimization, distinct from previously hypothesized mechanisms such as associative memory or induction heads.

526706ca6db9800d103bf87b104e98bc4ae4feed.title: Beam Tree Recursive Cells
526706ca6db9800d103bf87b104e98bc4ae4feed.research_question: How can recursive neural networks (RvNNs) be extended to better induce latent hierarchical structures from text, improving generalization to out-of-distribution cases such as longer sequences and novel argument counts, while maintaining computational efficiency and effective gradient propagation?
526706ca6db9800d103bf87b104e98bc4ae4feed.hypothesis: Incorporating beam search with a novel, partially differentiable top-k operator into RvNNs will enable more effective latent structure induction, leading to improved generalization on structure-sensitive tasks and more stable training compared to existing greedy or dynamic programming-based approaches.
526706ca6db9800d103bf87b104e98bc4ae4feed.proposed_method: A new framework, Beam Tree Recursive Cell (BT-Cell), will be developed to extend RvNNs by integrating beam search for latent structure induction. At each recursive step, the model will maintain the top-k highest scoring sub-tree representations, allowing multiple structural hypotheses to be explored in parallel. To address the non-differentiability of standard top-k operators and improve gradient propagation, a hybrid operator called OneSoftTop-k will be introduced, which combines discrete selection for the top k-1 beams with a softmax-based marginalization for the k-th beam. This approach enables gradients to propagate through more candidate structures, mitigating the bottleneck of hard selection. The BT-Cell will provide both final and intermediate constituent representations, supporting downstream tasks and interpretability.
526706ca6db9800d103bf87b104e98bc4ae4feed.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and realistic datasets. For synthetic evaluation, ListOps and a logical inference task will be used to test length and argument generalization, with training on short sequences and testing on much longer or more complex ones (e.g., ListOps splits with sequence lengths up to 1000 and argument counts up to 15). Realistic data experiments will include sentiment classification (SST5, IMDB) and natural language inference (MNLI), with additional stress tests such as contrast sets, counterfactuals, and length/negation-based splits. Baselines will include RNNs, Gumbel-Tree models, CYK-based RvNNs, Ordered Memory, and CRvNN, with evaluation metrics primarily being classification accuracy. Ablation studies will compare different cell functions, beam sizes, and top-k operator variants. Computational efficiency (runtime and memory) will also be measured across models.
526706ca6db9800d103bf87b104e98bc4ae4feed.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a backpropagation-friendly beam search framework for RvNNs, enabling more robust latent structure induction without requiring gold tree supervision. The OneSoftTop-k operator is a novel, semi-differentiable approach to top-k selection in beam search, allowing improved gradient flow compared to hard or fully soft alternatives. BT-Cell provides both final and intermediate node representations, supporting interpretability and downstream integration. The method achieves state-of-the-art results in length and depth generalization on structure-sensitive synthetic tasks, and demonstrates competitive or superior robustness on real-world NLP benchmarks and stress tests, while maintaining better computational efficiency than dynamic programming-based approaches.

5270b626feb66c8c363e93ba6608daae93c5003b.title: Modifying Memories in Transformer Models
5270b626feb66c8c363e93ba6608daae93c5003b.research_question: How can specific factual knowledge stored implicitly in large Transformer-based language models be efficiently and reliably modified, such that updated facts are incorporated without degrading the model's performance on unmodified knowledge?
5270b626feb66c8c363e93ba6608daae93c5003b.hypothesis: It is possible to explicitly modify selected factual knowledge in Transformer models through targeted parameter updates, using constrained fine-tuning techniques, in a way that maintains high accuracy on both modified and unmodified facts.
5270b626feb66c8c363e93ba6608daae93c5003b.proposed_method: A novel task is introduced that involves modifying a pre-selected subset of factual knowledge in a pretrained Transformer language model while preserving the accuracy on the remaining, unmodified facts. The approach is formulated as a constrained optimization problem: the model is fine-tuned on supporting evidence for the modified facts, with explicit constraints placed on the parameter changes (using norms such as the infinity norm) to limit interference with unmodified knowledge. Projected gradient descent is employed to solve the constrained optimization, and the method is further refined by restricting fine-tuning to specific Transformer blocks (e.g., initial or final layers), which has been found to improve the trade-off between updating targeted facts and retaining general knowledge. The approach is scalable, as its computational cost grows only with the number of modifications, and it can be extended to mixtures of modified and unmodified batches.
5270b626feb66c8c363e93ba6608daae93c5003b.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using large-scale benchmarks constructed from the T-REx and zsRE datasets, which consist of (subject, relation, object) factual triples and associated evidence sentences. The evaluation involves modifying a small subset of facts (e.g., 32, 128, 512, or 2048) by altering their objects and updating all supporting evidences accordingly. Multiple Transformer architectures are tested, including BERT-Base, BERT-Large, ALBERT-XXLarge, and the memory-augmented FaE model. Baseline methods include retraining, unconstrained fine-tuning, and fine-tuning on mixed batches. Performance is measured by accuracy on modified facts, accuracy on unmodified facts, and their average, with hyperparameters (such as the constraint strength δ) tuned to optimize this average. Ablation studies investigate the impact of fine-tuning different layers and varying the number of modified facts.
5270b626feb66c8c363e93ba6608daae93c5003b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first systematic benchmark and methodology for explicit modification of factual knowledge in Transformer models while preserving unmodified knowledge. It formulates knowledge modification as a constrained optimization problem, demonstrating that constrained, layer-wise fine-tuning is a simple yet effective solution. The work provides new insights into which Transformer components are most amenable to targeted knowledge updates and highlights the limitations of memory-augmented models for this task. The approach advances the state of the art in model editing, privacy, and bias correction for large language models.

5274e0a0445a5bfd9ff74503820a2390ba73865d.title: Bayesian Uncertainty for Gradient Aggregation in Multi-Task Learning
5274e0a0445a5bfd9ff74503820a2390ba73865d.research_question: How can uncertainty in task-specific gradients be effectively incorporated into gradient aggregation for multi-task learning to improve model optimization and generalization across diverse tasks?
5274e0a0445a5bfd9ff74503820a2390ba73865d.hypothesis: Incorporating Bayesian uncertainty estimates into the aggregation of task-specific gradients will yield more informative update directions, leading to improved optimization and generalization performance in multi-task learning compared to existing deterministic or heuristic aggregation schemes.
5274e0a0445a5bfd9ff74503820a2390ba73865d.proposed_method: A novel gradient aggregation approach for multi-task learning is developed by placing a Bayesian probability distribution over the task-specific parameters, specifically focusing on the last task-specific layer in a shared neural network architecture. This Bayesian treatment induces a distribution over the gradients for each task, enabling the quantification of uncertainty in each gradient dimension. The method computes the posterior distribution over the last-layer weights using either closed-form solutions (for regression) or Gaussian approximations (for classification), and then derives the mean and covariance of the induced gradient distributions. During aggregation, the method combines the task gradients by maximizing the joint likelihood of the update direction under all task-specific gradient distributions, resulting in a weighted combination where weights are inversely proportional to the estimated uncertainty per dimension and per example. The approach is designed to be computationally efficient by updating the prior using the full dataset once per epoch and approximating moments with either analytic expressions or Monte Carlo sampling as appropriate.
5274e0a0445a5bfd9ff74503820a2390ba73865d.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on several multi-task learning benchmarks, including QM9 (regression tasks on molecular properties), CIFAR-100 (CIFAR-MTL, binary classification tasks), ChestX-ray14 (multi-label binary classification), and UTKFace (mixed regression and classification tasks). For each dataset, standard neural network architectures are used (e.g., message-passing neural networks for QM9, convolutional networks for CIFAR-MTL, ResNet-34 for ChestX-ray14, and ResNet-18 for UTKFace). The method is compared against a comprehensive set of baselines, including single-task learning, uniform and dynamic loss weighting, uncertainty weighting, multiple-gradient descent algorithms, conflict-averse and impartial MTL methods, and recent game-theoretic and reinforcement learning-based approaches. Evaluation metrics include mean absolute error (MAE) for regression, accuracy and AUC-ROC for classification, and the average relative difference (Δm%) compared to single-task baselines. Experiments are repeated with multiple random seeds, and hyperparameters are tuned using validation splits. The computational efficiency and scalability of the method are also assessed relative to other gradient-based aggregation methods.
5274e0a0445a5bfd9ff74503820a2390ba73865d.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first Bayesian formulation for gradient aggregation in multi-task learning, leveraging uncertainty estimates in each gradient dimension for more informed aggregation. It presents a novel posterior approximation for the last-layer parameters based on a second-order Taylor expansion and derives a new aggregation rule that assigns unique, uncertainty-based weights to each gradient component per task and per example. The approach achieves state-of-the-art results on several multi-task learning benchmarks, demonstrating superior performance and computational efficiency compared to leading methods. The method is also generalizable to both regression and classification tasks and is applicable to mixed-task settings.

5278a8eb2ba2429d4029745caf4e661080073c81.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
5278a8eb2ba2429d4029745caf4e661080073c81.research_question: How can computational agents be designed to simulate believable human behavior in interactive environments, maintaining long-term coherence and emergent social dynamics?
5278a8eb2ba2429d4029745caf4e661080073c81.hypothesis: Equipping generative agents with mechanisms for memory, reflection, and planning, in conjunction with large language models, will enable the simulation of individual and emergent social behaviors that are perceived as believable by users.
5278a8eb2ba2429d4029745caf4e661080073c81.proposed_method: A novel agent architecture will be developed that integrates a large language model with three core components: a memory stream, a reflection mechanism, and a planning module. The memory stream records all agent experiences in natural language, storing observations, actions, and interactions with timestamps and importance scores. A retrieval system will be implemented to surface relevant memories for decision-making, using a weighted combination of recency, importance, and semantic relevance. The reflection mechanism will periodically synthesize higher-level inferences and abstractions from recent memories, allowing agents to generalize and form insights about themselves and others. The planning module will generate high-level action plans and recursively decompose them into detailed behaviors, conditioned on both current context and retrieved memories. All components will interact through natural language prompts to the language model, enabling dynamic, context-aware behavior generation.
5278a8eb2ba2429d4029745caf4e661080073c81.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in a custom sandbox environment inspired by The Sims, populated with 25 unique generative agents. Two main evaluations are planned: (1) a controlled evaluation to assess the believability of individual agent behaviors in isolation, using natural language 'interviews' to probe memory, planning, and reflection capabilities; and (2) an end-to-end evaluation in which agents interact freely over two simulated days, allowing for the observation of emergent social behaviors such as information diffusion, relationship formation, and group coordination. Ablation studies will be performed by disabling components (memory, reflection, planning) to measure their causal impact. Baselines will include agents with limited or no access to memory or planning. Evaluation metrics will focus on qualitative and quantitative assessments of behavioral believability, coherence, and emergent phenomena.
5278a8eb2ba2429d4029745caf4e661080073c81.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces an architecture that enables generative agents to dynamically remember, retrieve, reflect, interact, and plan through evolving circumstances, leveraging large language models for naturalistic behavior synthesis. Key innovations include the use of a comprehensive memory stream with retrieval based on recency, importance, and relevance; recursive reflection for higher-level inference; and integration of planning mechanisms for long-term coherence. The approach enables emergent social behaviors without manual scripting, supporting applications in prototyping, virtual worlds, and social simulation. The research also provides causal evidence for the necessity of each architectural component and identifies failure modes related to memory retrieval and coherence.

528302668885787968a3700524a7915cea4abb21.title: MDNS: Masked Diffusion Neural Sampler via Stochastic Optimal Control
528302668885787968a3700524a7915cea4abb21.research_question: How can efficient and scalable neural samplers be developed to generate samples from high-dimensional, multi-modal discrete distributions where the target probability mass function is known up to a normalizing constant?
528302668885787968a3700524a7915cea4abb21.hypothesis: A neural sampler framework based on stochastic optimal control of continuous-time Markov chains, combined with masked discrete diffusion models and novel learning objectives, enables accurate and scalable sampling from complex discrete distributions, outperforming existing learning-based and classical sampling methods.
528302668885787968a3700524a7915cea4abb21.proposed_method: A novel framework, Masked Diffusion Neural Sampler (MDNS), is proposed for training discrete neural samplers by aligning two path measures via a family of learning objectives grounded in stochastic optimal control of continuous-time Markov chains (CTMCs). The method parameterizes the generator of a CTMC using neural networks, leveraging a memoryless reference path measure constructed from masked discrete diffusion models. Several learning objectives are introduced, including relative-entropy with REINFORCE, log-variance, and cross-entropy, all designed to avoid differentiability requirements and backpropagation through entire trajectories. For scalable training in high dimensions, a Weighted Denoising Cross-Entropy (WDCE) loss is developed, which directly implements score learning on the target distribution using importance sampling and efficiently amortizes computation via replay buffers and resampling strategies. The framework also supports extensions to uniform discrete diffusion models and incorporates warm-up and preconditioning techniques for improved convergence.
528302668885787968a3700524a7915cea4abb21.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the Ising and Potts models on square lattices of varying sizes and temperatures, covering distributions with diverse statistical properties and challenging state space cardinalities (up to 10^122). Evaluation metrics include probabilistic divergences (KL divergence, TV distance, chi-squared divergence), statistical physics observables (magnetization, 2-point correlation), and effective sample size (ESS). The proposed MDNS is compared against learning-based baselines such as LEAPS and classical methods like Metropolis-Hastings (MH) and Swendsen-Wang (SW), with all baselines run for comparable computation time. Ablation studies assess the impact of different learning objectives and training strategies, and ground truth is estimated via long SW runs when exact computation is infeasible. Hyperparameters and metric definitions are detailed in supplementary material.
528302668885787968a3700524a7915cea4abb21.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a theoretically grounded approach for training discrete neural samplers using stochastic optimal control and masked discrete diffusion models. It presents several new learning objectives that circumvent differentiability and memory bottlenecks, and develops a scalable Weighted Denoising Cross-Entropy loss for high-dimensional training. The method demonstrates the ability to accurately sample from extremely high-dimensional and multi-modal discrete distributions, substantially outperforming existing learning-based methods. The framework is extensible to other discrete diffusion models and supports efficient estimation of the normalizing constant. Theoretical guarantees for sampling accuracy and normalizing constant estimation are provided.

529ff7d6441d244212cf2becafd12a7e67ac56d9.title: FederatedScope-LLM: A Comprehensive Package for Fine-tuning Large Language Models in Federated Learning
529ff7d6441d244212cf2becafd12a7e67ac56d9.research_question: How can large language models be efficiently and effectively fine-tuned in federated learning settings, considering challenges such as communication and computation costs, data heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and the need for extensible benchmarking and algorithmic frameworks?
529ff7d6441d244212cf2becafd12a7e67ac56d9.hypothesis: Federated fine-tuning of large language models using parameter-efficient fine-tuning algorithms and resource-optimized training paradigms can achieve competitive performance with reduced communication and computation costs, while supporting privacy and extensibility across diverse federated learning scenarios.
529ff7d6441d244212cf2becafd12a7e67ac56d9.proposed_method: A comprehensive package, FederatedScope-LLM (FS-LLM), will be developed to enable end-to-end federated fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs). The method will integrate three core modules: (1) LLM-BENCHMARKS, providing federated versions of diverse fine-tuning datasets, automated data preprocessing, and standardized evaluation pipelines; (2) LLM-ALGZOO, implementing a suite of parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) algorithms (such as LoRA, P-tuning, prompt tuning) and privacy-preserving algorithms (e.g., offsite-tuning/FedOT) with unified, extensible interfaces; and (3) LLM-TRAINER, offering a collection of accelerating and resource-efficient operators (e.g., mixed-precision, gradient accumulation, quantization, DeepSpeed integration) and hook-like functions for customizable training and interdisciplinary research (e.g., personalized FL, federated hyperparameter optimization). The system will support multiple deployment modes (simulated, distributed, clustered) and allow for plug-and-play extensibility for advanced federated learning tasks.
529ff7d6441d244212cf2becafd12a7e67ac56d9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using federated versions of several datasets: Fed-CodeAlpaca (for code generation), Fed-Dolly (for generic language tasks), and Fed-GSM8K-3 (for mathematical reasoning), each paired with a corresponding evaluation dataset (HumanEval, HELM, GSM8K-test). The LLaMA-7B model will be fine-tuned using PEFT algorithms (LoRA, P-tuning, prompt tuning) under global, federated, and local scenarios, with FedAvg as the aggregation strategy. Evaluation metrics will include task-specific scores (e.g., Pass@1 for code, accuracy for math), as well as cost-related metrics such as GPU usage, computation time, and communication overhead. Experiments will be repeated with fixed hardware (Nvidia A100 GPUs, Intel Xeon CPUs) and controlled hyperparameters, including grid search for learning rates and use of half-precision training for efficiency.
529ff7d6441d244212cf2becafd12a7e67ac56d9.novelty_claims: The proposed package introduces the first comprehensive, open-source, end-to-end benchmarking and fine-tuning pipeline for LLMs in federated learning, supporting both full-model and adapter-based fine-tuning, including scenarios where clients do not have access to the full model. It provides a unified interface for extensibility, integrates advanced resource-efficient operators and parallelization strategies, and supports interdisciplinary research such as personalized federated learning and federated hyperparameter optimization. The framework enables reproducible, scalable, and efficient federated fine-tuning of LLMs, addressing key challenges in communication, computation, privacy, and benchmarking.

52ba35523e01b1146f2519ca31bab52c4a54fe74.title: Counting Like Transformers: Compiling Temporal Counting Logic Into Softmax Transformers
52ba35523e01b1146f2519ca31bab52c4a54fe74.research_question: What is the formal expressive power of standard, future-masked softmax attention transformers with unbounded input size, and how can their capabilities be precisely characterized using logical and programming language formalisms?
52ba35523e01b1146f2519ca31bab52c4a54fe74.hypothesis: Future-masked softmax attention transformers, without additional positional embeddings, can recognize exactly the class of formal languages definable by the temporal counting logic K[#] (and equivalently, by the C-RASP programming language), establishing a tight lower bound on their expressivity.
52ba35523e01b1146f2519ca31bab52c4a54fe74.proposed_method: A new temporal counting logic, K[#], will be formally defined to capture the computational abilities of masked softmax attention transformers. In parallel, a restricted programming language, C-RASP, will be developed, designed to compile exactly into standard transformer architectures without requiring nonstandard components or positional encodings. The equivalence between K[#] and C-RASP will be established, and a constructive compilation procedure will be provided to translate any K[#] formula (or C-RASP program) into a sequence of transformer blocks. The construction will use standard transformer components, including self-attention, feed-forward layers, and layer normalization, and will store logical and counting values in specific tensor dimensions throughout the residual stream. Modal depth of formulas will be mapped to transformer depth, and all operations (counting, Boolean, arithmetic) will be simulated using combinations of masked attention and feed-forward computation.
52ba35523e01b1146f2519ca31bab52c4a54fe74.experiment_details: Theoretical constructions will be validated by demonstrating that a variety of formal languages—including regular, context-free, and context-sensitive examples such as Dyck-1 and anbncn—can be recognized by compiled transformers. Comparative analysis will be conducted against prior lower bounds (e.g., FOC[+;MOD]) and other logical characterizations, showing that K[#] strictly subsumes previous results in expressivity. No empirical experiments with real datasets are specified, but the proposal includes the development of C-RASP programs for canonical formal languages and the formal proof of their correct compilation into transformer architectures. Evaluation metrics will include logical equivalence, expressivity class coverage, and formal proof of compilation correctness.
52ba35523e01b1146f2519ca31bab52c4a54fe74.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first logic (K[#]) and programming language (C-RASP) that can be exactly and provably compiled into standard, future-masked softmax attention transformers with no input length restrictions or nonstandard architectural assumptions. This establishes the tightest known lower bound on the expressivity of such transformers. The compilation method requires no additional positional encodings and uses only standard transformer components. The equivalence between K[#] and C-RASP provides both a human-readable and a formal logical framework for understanding transformer computations, enabling both theoretical analysis and practical program synthesis.

52bca2ff9159bd9f704adffa5fd9c51a198574df.title: Proposer-Agent-Evaluator(PAE): Autonomous Skill Discovery For Foundation Model Internet Agents
52bca2ff9159bd9f704adffa5fd9c51a198574df.research_question: Can foundation model-based Internet agents autonomously discover and practice useful skills without human supervision, and can these autonomously learned skills generalize to unseen real-world tasks and environments?
52bca2ff9159bd9f704adffa5fd9c51a198574df.hypothesis: Foundation model agents equipped with an autonomous skill discovery system that leverages context-aware task proposing, self-play, and outcome-based evaluation can develop a diverse and effective skill repertoire, enabling strong zero-shot generalization to unseen tasks and websites.
52bca2ff9159bd9f704adffa5fd9c51a198574df.proposed_method: A novel Proposer-Agent-Evaluator (PAE) framework is developed for autonomous skill discovery in foundation model agents, particularly for Internet-based web navigation tasks. The system consists of three key components: (1) a context-aware task proposer that generates diverse and feasible tasks based on environment context (such as website names or user demonstration screenshots), (2) an agent policy that attempts these tasks using vision-language models (VLMs) and incorporates a chain-of-thought reasoning step before executing actions, and (3) an autonomous outcome evaluator that provides sparse binary rewards (success/failure) based on the final outcome, using only screenshots and the agent's final answer. The agent policy is optimized using Filtered Behavior Cloning, imitating successful trajectories. The task proposer and evaluator are instantiated via prompted foundation models and remain fixed during training. The framework is designed to operate in a self-play, fully autonomous setting without human-annotated instructions or supervision.
52bca2ff9159bd9f704adffa5fd9c51a198574df.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted in challenging vision-based web navigation environments, using both real-world websites from the WebVoyager benchmark and sandboxed, self-hosted websites from WebArena. The agent's observation space consists of webpage screenshots augmented with interactable element markers, and the action space includes primitive web operations (click, type, scroll, etc.). Baselines include state-of-the-art open-source VLM agents (e.g., Qwen2VL-7B/72B, LLaVa-7B/34B, InternVL2.5-8B), proprietary VLMs (Claude 3 Sonnet, Claude 3.5 Sonnet), and supervised fine-tuning (SFT) approaches. Evaluation metrics focus on task success rates, measured both on seen and unseen websites, with ground-truth success detectors and human annotations used for final assessment. Ablation studies investigate the impact of different context sources for task proposing, evaluator types, and the inclusion of chain-of-thought reasoning.
52bca2ff9159bd9f704adffa5fd9c51a198574df.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first effective learning system to enable foundation model agents to autonomously discover and practice skills in realistic web environments without any human supervision or predefined task templates. The approach leverages the asymmetric strengths of VLMs as task proposers/evaluators versus agents, incorporates a context-aware task proposing mechanism, and demonstrates robust zero-shot generalization to unseen tasks and websites. The method achieves substantial improvements over prior state-of-the-art open-source VLM agents, with more than 30% relative improvement in zero-shot generalization and over 10% absolute performance gain on challenging benchmarks. The framework is fully open-source and scalable, eliminating reliance on proprietary models or human-annotated data.

52c5ddedc205a7968e2f0a4d713f78abba4b832b.title: No Training, No Problem: Rethinking Classifier-Free Guidance for Diffusion Models
52c5ddedc205a7968e2f0a4d713f78abba4b832b.research_question: How can the benefits of classifier-free guidance (CFG) in diffusion models be achieved without requiring auxiliary training of unconditional models, and can guidance techniques be extended to improve both conditional and unconditional diffusion model generation without modifying the training process?
52c5ddedc205a7968e2f0a4d713f78abba4b832b.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the unconditional score required for classifier-free guidance can be approximated using a conditional diffusion model by substituting the conditioning vector with an independent random vector at inference time, thus eliminating the need for auxiliary unconditional model training. Furthermore, it is hypothesized that perturbing the time-step embedding during inference can provide a guidance signal that improves generation quality for both conditional and unconditional diffusion models.
52c5ddedc205a7968e2f0a4d713f78abba4b832b.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces two novel guidance techniques for diffusion models: Independent Condition Guidance (ICG) and Time-Step Guidance (TSG). ICG approximates the unconditional score by replacing the conditioning vector in a trained conditional diffusion model with an independent random vector (either sampled from a Gaussian distribution or randomly selected from the conditioning space) during inference, enabling classifier-free guidance behavior without auxiliary training. TSG leverages the time-step embedding inherent in diffusion models by perturbing it with Gaussian noise at each sampling step; the model outputs for both the clean and perturbed embeddings are combined to form a guidance signal analogous to CFG, but applicable to unconditional models as well. Both methods are designed to be implemented at inference time, require no changes to the training process, and incur the same sampling cost as standard CFG.
52c5ddedc205a7968e2f0a4d713f78abba4b832b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using pre-trained checkpoints of several diffusion models, including Stable Diffusion (text-conditional, UNet-based), DiT-XL/2 (class-conditional, Transformer-based), EDM and EDM2 (unconditional and class-conditional), and ControlNet (image-conditioned). The recommended samplers for each model will be used (e.g., EDM sampler, DPM++, DDPM). Evaluation metrics will include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for overall quality and diversity, precision and recall for quality/diversity trade-off, and FD (DINOv2) for specific models. Baselines will include standard non-guided sampling and classifier-free guidance (CFG) with auxiliary unconditional models. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of different independent condition choices in ICG and hyperparameters in TSG. Additional experiments will test the combination of ICG and TSG, as well as the effect of removing the CFG objective from training.
52c5ddedc205a7968e2f0a4d713f78abba4b832b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretically motivated and efficient method (ICG) for achieving classifier-free guidance in conditional diffusion models without requiring auxiliary unconditional model training or label-dropping during training, thus streamlining the training process and improving efficiency. It further presents a novel guidance technique (TSG) that extends the benefits of CFG to unconditional diffusion models by leveraging time-step embedding perturbations, which has not been previously explored. Both methods are model-agnostic, easy to implement, and compatible with existing architectures and guidance techniques. The combination of ICG and TSG is also proposed as a complementary approach for further improving sample quality.

52cc542b60c99e8866a7fc515c10f443089005f2.title: FastViT: A Fast Hybrid Vision Transformer using Structural Reparameterization
52cc542b60c99e8866a7fc515c10f443089005f2.research_question: How can a hybrid vision transformer architecture be designed to achieve an optimal trade-off between accuracy and latency across a wide range of computer vision tasks, while maintaining robustness to out-of-distribution samples and corruptions?
52cc542b60c99e8866a7fc515c10f443089005f2.hypothesis: A hybrid vision transformer architecture that leverages structural reparameterization to remove skip connections, employs linear train-time overparameterization, and incorporates large kernel convolutions in place of self-attention in early stages will achieve state-of-the-art accuracy-latency trade-offs and improved robustness on multiple computer vision tasks.
52cc542b60c99e8866a7fc515c10f443089005f2.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a hybrid vision transformer architecture, FastViT, which is structured into four stages operating at different spatial resolutions. The architecture utilizes a novel token mixing operator, RepMixer, which reparameterizes skip connections at inference time to reduce memory access costs and latency. Dense k×k convolutions in stem and patch embedding layers are replaced with factorized depthwise followed by pointwise convolutions, whose capacity is boosted via linear train-time overparameterization—additional branches are introduced during training and merged at inference. Large kernel depthwise convolutions are incorporated into FeedForward Network (FFN) and patch embedding layers to expand the receptive field efficiently, substituting for self-attention in early stages. Conditional positional encodings generated via depthwise convolutions are added to patch embeddings to enhance local context modeling.
52cc542b60c99e8866a7fc515c10f443089005f2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several computer vision benchmarks, including ImageNet-1K for image classification, MS-COCO for object detection and instance segmentation, ADE20K for semantic segmentation, and FreiHAND for 3D hand mesh estimation. Robustness will be evaluated on ImageNet-C, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R, and ImageNet-Sketch. Baselines for comparison include state-of-the-art models such as EfficientNet, ConvNeXt, CMT, PoolFormer, MobileOne, and various vision transformers. Evaluation metrics include Top-1 accuracy for classification, mIoU for segmentation, and AP for detection, as well as latency measured on both mobile devices (iPhone 12 Pro) and desktop GPUs (NVIDIA RTX-2080Ti). Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of RepMixer, train-time overparameterization, and large kernel convolutions. Models will be trained with standard recipes (e.g., AdamW optimizer, cosine learning rate schedule) and latency will be measured using CoreMLTools and TensorRT deployments.
52cc542b60c99e8866a7fc515c10f443089005f2.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a reparameterizable token mixer (RepMixer) that removes skip connections at inference to lower memory access cost and latency, a technique not previously applied in hybrid transformer architectures. The use of linear train-time overparameterization in factorized convolutional layers further enhances representational capacity without incurring significant inference cost. Large kernel convolutions are incorporated as efficient substitutes for self-attention in early network stages, improving both accuracy and robustness. The resulting architecture achieves superior accuracy-latency trade-offs and demonstrates strong robustness to out-of-distribution samples and corruptions across multiple vision tasks, outperforming existing state-of-the-art models.

52ee0a6dc26d0b63919b5ec77209eb2e5f12d69e.title: Simplicity Bias Leads to Amplified Performance Disparities
52ee0a6dc26d0b63919b5ec77209eb2e5f12d69e.research_question: How do machine learning models exhibit group-specific performance disparities, even when trained on balanced datasets, and what factors influence the amplification of these disparities across different groups?
52ee0a6dc26d0b63919b5ec77209eb2e5f12d69e.hypothesis: Certain machine learning models, due to a bias toward simplicity, will preferentially learn 'easier' groups at the expense of 'harder' groups, resulting in amplified performance disparities between groups, even when group sizes and label distributions are balanced.
52ee0a6dc26d0b63919b5ec77209eb2e5f12d69e.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical investigation will be conducted to quantify and analyze model-dependent performance disparities across groups of varying difficulty within balanced datasets. The methodology involves defining and measuring 'difficulty disparity' as the difference in test accuracy between groups when trained in isolation, and 'observed disparity' as the difference when trained jointly. The amplification factor will be computed as the ratio of observed to estimated disparity. Multiple neural network architectures (e.g., ResNet, LeNet, FC networks), regularization strategies (e.g., weight decay, gradient penalty), and training regimes (e.g., early stopping, varying width) will be systematically evaluated. Experiments will also explore mitigation strategies such as targeted additional data collection and oversampling for groups with higher observed disparities.
52ee0a6dc26d0b63919b5ec77209eb2e5f12d69e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic tasks will be constructed from CIFAR-100, FashionMNIST, and EMNIST Letters, where groups are defined by class pairs with known differences in classification difficulty. Real-world case studies will use FairFace (for age classification across race-annotated groups) and Dollar Street (for object classification across income quartiles), with explicit balancing and matching of group sizes and label distributions where possible. Baselines will include training models on each group in isolation and jointly, with performance measured by cross-validated test accuracy. Evaluation metrics include observed and estimated difficulty disparity, amplification factor, and the impact of mitigation strategies. Model architectures, training time, parameter count, and regularization methods will be varied to assess their influence on disparity amplification.
52ee0a6dc26d0b63919b5ec77209eb2e5f12d69e.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the concept of 'difficulty amplification'—the phenomenon where models amplify group-specific performance disparities beyond what is expected from group-wise training alone, even in balanced datasets without spurious correlations or group/label associations. The approach systematically quantifies this effect across a range of architectures and training regimes, revealing that model choice, scale, and training decisions can unpredictably exacerbate or attenuate disparities. The proposal also pioneers targeted mitigation strategies based on model-dependent audits, such as additional data collection and oversampling for underperforming groups, moving beyond traditional fairness interventions that focus solely on dataset balance.

52eff6fbdbc8adf356ecaeeeeb6ab7fc3fcb296a.title: Gradient Norm Aware Minimization Seeks First-Order Flatness and Improves Generalization
52eff6fbdbc8adf356ecaeeeeb6ab7fc3fcb296a.research_question: How can improved measures of flatness in the loss landscape of deep neural networks be leveraged to enhance model generalization, beyond current approaches that focus on zeroth-order flatness?
52eff6fbdbc8adf356ecaeeeeb6ab7fc3fcb296a.hypothesis: Optimizing for first-order flatness, defined as minimizing the maximal gradient norm within a perturbation radius, leads to flatter minima and improved generalization performance compared to optimizing zeroth-order flatness alone.
52eff6fbdbc8adf356ecaeeeeb6ab7fc3fcb296a.proposed_method: A novel training procedure, Gradient norm Aware Minimization (GAM), will be developed to explicitly seek minima with uniformly small curvature in all directions by penalizing the maximum gradient norm within a neighborhood of the model parameters. The first-order flatness regularizer will be incorporated into the training objective, combined with the standard prediction loss. The maximal gradient norm will be efficiently approximated using stochastic gradient ascent and Hessian-vector products, avoiding explicit computation of the full Hessian matrix. The method will allow integration with existing optimizers such as SGD, AdamW, and sharpness-aware minimization (SAM), and will be implemented with a tunable trade-off coefficient and perturbation radius hyperparameters.
52eff6fbdbc8adf356ecaeeeeb6ab7fc3fcb296a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of image classification benchmarks, including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet, using diverse architectures such as ResNet, WideResNet, PyramidNet, ResNeXt, and Vision Transformers (ViT). Both training from scratch and transfer learning scenarios will be evaluated, with and without advanced data augmentations. Baselines will include standard optimizers (SGD, AdamW), SAM, and their combinations with GAM. Evaluation metrics will focus on test accuracy, generalization gap, and measures of flatness such as the maximum Hessian eigenvalue and Hessian trace. Additional analysis will include computational overhead, ablation on the frequency of applying the GAM regularizer, and visualization of loss landscapes.
52eff6fbdbc8adf356ecaeeeeb6ab7fc3fcb296a.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces first-order flatness as a stronger and more discriminative measure of flatness than zeroth-order flatness, directly bounding the maximal Hessian eigenvalue and providing a tighter connection to generalization error. The GAM framework is novel in penalizing the maximum gradient norm in the neighborhood of minima, rather than just the loss value, and is shown to be compatible with and complementary to existing optimizers and sharpness-aware training methods. The method is claimed to consistently improve generalization across datasets and architectures, find flatter minima as evidenced by lower Hessian spectra, and offer a practical and efficient implementation via Hessian-vector products.

52f6003584f8b423abb0a8f2b890ae0eac660889.title: Unsupervised Learning for Combinatorial Optimization with Principled Objective Relaxation
52f6003584f8b423abb0a8f2b890ae0eac660889.research_question: How can unsupervised learning frameworks be developed to efficiently solve combinatorial optimization (CO) and proxy-based combinatorial optimization (PCO) problems, particularly when objective functions are unknown or expensive to evaluate, and without reliance on labeled data?
52f6003584f8b423abb0a8f2b890ae0eac660889.hypothesis: Entry-wise concave relaxations of objective and constraint functions, when combined with a relaxation-plus-rounding approach and neural network parameterization, enable unsupervised learning algorithms to generate valid and high-quality discrete solutions for general CO and PCO problems, with deterministic performance guarantees.
52f6003584f8b423abb0a8f2b890ae0eac660889.proposed_method: A novel unsupervised learning framework is proposed for combinatorial optimization problems, leveraging a relaxation-plus-rounding approach.
