The method first constructs continuous relaxations of the objective and constraint functions, ensuring that these relaxations are entry-wise concave (or affine) with respect to the binary optimization variables. Neural networks, particularly graph neural networks (GNNs), are used to parameterize these relaxed proxies, enabling end-to-end training via backpropagation on historical (unlabeled) data. After optimizing the relaxed objective, a deterministic sequential rounding procedure is applied to the soft solution to obtain a valid discrete solution. The entry-wise concave property is enforced in the neural network architecture or through explicit mathematical formulation, ensuring that the rounding procedure yields solutions with provable performance guarantees.
52f6003584f8b423abb0a8f2b890ae0eac660889.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Three main applications are considered: (I) feature-based edge covering and node matching in graphs (using synthetic grid graphs with MNIST-derived node attributes), (II) resource allocation in FPGA circuit design (using data flow graphs and hardware synthesis for ground-truth evaluation), and (III) imprecise functional unit assignment in approximate computing (using computation graphs with simulated error metrics). For each application, the proposed method is compared against baselines including naïve relaxation, reinforcement learning (actor-critic), Gumbel-softmax-based gradient relaxation, simulated annealing, and genetic algorithms. Evaluation metrics include the quality of the discrete solution (e.g., objective value, constraint satisfaction, relative error), approximation rate, and computational efficiency (training and inference time). Datasets are split into training, validation, and testing sets, with careful hyperparameter tuning and ablation studies on the relaxation principle.
52f6003584f8b423abb0a8f2b890ae0eac660889.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled objective relaxation framework for unsupervised learning in CO and PCO settings, grounded in the entry-wise concave relaxation principle. This approach generalizes previous probabilistic methods by providing deterministic performance guarantees for a broader class of objectives, including those learned as proxies. The method is the first to systematically address unsupervised learning for PCO problems, where objectives are not explicitly given and must be modeled. The framework demonstrates superior optimization performance and training efficiency over reinforcement learning and Gumbel-softmax-based baselines, and provides new neural network architectures for learning entry-wise concave proxies.

5306ba33d3ac5838d2b84b1d53bede563c474398.title: Quasi-Monte Carlo for 3D Sliced Wasserstein
5306ba33d3ac5838d2b84b1d53bede563c474398.research_question: How can the approximation of the Sliced Wasserstein (SW) distance between probability measures in three dimensions be improved in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency, particularly for applications involving 3D data such as point clouds and image style transfer?
5306ba33d3ac5838d2b84b1d53bede563c474398.hypothesis: Quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) based deterministic and randomized point sets on the unit hypersphere will yield lower approximation error and improved empirical performance for the Sliced Wasserstein distance in 3D, compared to conventional Monte Carlo (MC) approaches.
5306ba33d3ac5838d2b84b1d53bede563c474398.proposed_method: A new family of Quasi-Sliced Wasserstein (QSW) approximations will be developed by leveraging Quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) methods to construct low-discrepancy point sets on the 3D unit hypersphere. Several construction techniques for QMC point sets will be explored, including Gaussian-based mapping, Lambert equal-area mapping, generalized spiral points, maximizing pairwise distance, and minimizing Coulomb energy. The QSW distance will be defined as the average of 1D Wasserstein distances between projections of the measures along these deterministic directions. To enable unbiased stochastic optimization and facilitate gradient-based learning, Randomized Quasi-Sliced Wasserstein (RQSW) variants will be introduced by injecting randomness into QMC point sets, either via scrambling/shifting (pushforward from the unit cube) or random rotations on the hypersphere. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to establish asymptotic convergence and unbiasedness properties of these estimators.
5306ba33d3ac5838d2b84b1d53bede563c474398.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of 3D tasks, including point-cloud comparison, point-cloud interpolation, image style transfer, and training deep point-cloud autoencoders. The ShapeNet Core-55 dataset will be used for point-cloud tasks, and ModelNet40 will be used for evaluating autoencoder reconstruction. Baselines will include conventional Monte Carlo (MC) estimation of the SW distance. Evaluation metrics will include absolute approximation error to a high-sample MC estimate (as a population value), Wasserstein-2 distance between interpolated or reconstructed objects, and visual/qualitative assessment of style transfer and point-cloud reconstructions. Experimental setups will vary the number of projection directions (L), compare different QSW and RQSW variants, and measure computational efficiency and gradient quality in optimization tasks.
5306ba33d3ac5838d2b84b1d53bede563c474398.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first comprehensive integration of QMC methodologies for Sliced Wasserstein distance computation on the 3D unit hypersphere, including a systematic investigation of multiple QMC point set constructions and their empirical discrepancies. The approach extends QMC-based approximations to both deterministic and randomized settings, enabling unbiased and efficient gradient estimation for stochastic optimization. Theoretical guarantees of asymptotic convergence and unbiasedness are established for the proposed estimators. The methodology is validated across diverse 3D applications, demonstrating superior approximation accuracy and practical advantages over standard MC-based approaches.

5309018546f91c2a73cdadf82b801b396f37bc05.title: SQ Lower Bounds for Learning Single Neurons with Massart Noise
5309018546f91c2a73cdadf82b801b396f37bc05.research_question: Is it possible to efficiently learn single neurons (i.e., real-valued functions with a known activation function) in the presence of Massart noise, under arbitrary data distributions, using algorithms from the Statistical Query (SQ) model? What are the computational limitations of such learning tasks for various activation functions, including ReLU and other monotone nonlinear activations?
5309018546f91c2a73cdadf82b801b396f37bc05.hypothesis: No efficient Statistical Query (SQ) algorithm can achieve a constant-factor approximation to the optimal error when learning single neurons with Massart noise for a broad class of activation functions, including ReLU, under arbitrary data distributions.
5309018546f91c2a73cdadf82b801b396f37bc05.proposed_method: A rigorous lower bound construction will be developed to demonstrate the computational hardness of learning single neurons with Massart noise in the SQ model. The approach involves constructing hard instances of the learning problem by designing distributions over labeled examples such that any SQ algorithm requires either super-polynomially many queries or queries of exponentially small tolerance to achieve non-trivial approximation. The method leverages moment-matching techniques, embedding discrete distributions with carefully controlled noise properties into high-dimensional spaces, and uses combinatorial constructions on the Boolean hypercube to create families of distributions that are nearly orthogonal in the SQ sense. The construction is robust and generalizes to a wide class of activation functions, including ReLU and other fast-convergent monotone nonlinearities.
5309018546f91c2a73cdadf82b801b396f37bc05.experiment_details: The experimental validation will be theoretical and based on reductions and lower bound proofs within the SQ framework. The 'experiments' consist of constructing families of distributions and analyzing their statistical query dimension, pairwise correlations, and moment-matching properties. Theoretical evaluation will use metrics such as the number of SQ queries required, the accuracy (tolerance) of queries, and the approximation ratio achievable by any SQ algorithm. Comparisons will be made against known upper bounds for special cases (e.g., linear regression, ReLU regression under anti-concentration), and the results will be contextualized with respect to existing hardness results for agnostic and Massart noise models.
5309018546f91c2a73cdadf82b801b396f37bc05.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first super-polynomial SQ lower bounds for learning single neurons with Massart noise, ruling out any efficient constant-factor approximation for a broad class of activation functions, including ReLU, under arbitrary distributions. The construction provides a new SQ-hardness instance for low-weight halfspaces on the Boolean hypercube, addressing an open problem regarding the complexity of learning Massart halfspaces with small integer weights. The approach generalizes previous continuous and Gaussian-based constructions to the discrete setting, and extends the hardness results to both L0 and L2 variants of the Massart noise model for real-valued functions.

53132ea6c107479d4557631299d3ed525109b464.title: AFlow: Automating Agentic Workflow Generation
53132ea6c107479d4557631299d3ed525109b464.research_question: How can the generation and optimization of agentic workflows for large language models be fully automated to improve performance, scalability, and cost-effectiveness across diverse reasoning, code, and question answering tasks?
53132ea6c107479d4557631299d3ed525109b464.hypothesis: Automating the search and optimization of agentic workflows using a code-based representation and a Monte Carlo Tree Search framework will yield more effective, generalizable, and cost-efficient workflows than manually designed or existing automated methods.
53132ea6c107479d4557631299d3ed525109b464.proposed_method: A new framework, AFLOW, will be developed to automate agentic workflow generation by formulating workflow optimization as a search problem over code-represented workflows. Workflows are modeled as interconnected nodes (each representing an LLM invocation with specific parameters) and code-based edges that capture logical flows, conditions, and dependencies. The search is conducted using a variant of Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS), where each tree node represents a complete workflow. The search process iteratively applies soft mixed-probability selection for exploration, LLM-driven expansion to generate new workflow candidates, direct execution-based evaluation for performance feedback, and experience backpropagation to refine the search. Operators, defined as reusable combinations of nodes representing common agentic operations (e.g., Ensemble, Review & Revise), are integrated to enhance search efficiency and structure.
53132ea6c107479d4557631299d3ed525109b464.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six public benchmark datasets spanning code generation (HumanEval, MBPP), mathematical reasoning (GSM8K, MATH), and question answering (HotpotQA, DROP). Datasets will be split into validation and test sets using a 1:4 ratio, with random seeds fixed for reproducibility. AFLOW-optimized workflows will be compared against manually designed baselines (e.g., IO, Chain-of-Thought, Self-Refine, MedPrompt, MultiPersona) and automated workflow optimization methods (e.g., ADAS). Evaluation metrics will include solve rate for math datasets, F1 score for QA datasets, and pass@1 for code tasks. Multiple LLMs (e.g., GPT-4o-mini, DeepSeek-V2.5, Claude-3.5-sonnet) will be used as both optimizers and executors, and cost-effectiveness will be assessed by tracking token usage and constructing Pareto fronts. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of operators and workflow transferability across models.
53132ea6c107479d4557631299d3ed525109b464.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a fully automated, code-based workflow optimization framework leveraging MCTS, enabling efficient exploration of a vast workflow search space without manual intervention. Key innovations include the use of code to represent workflows for maximal expressivity, the integration of reusable operator modules to accelerate search, and a tree-structured experience mechanism to preserve and reuse exploration history. The method demonstrates the ability to generate workflows that allow smaller, less expensive LLMs to outperform larger models on certain tasks, significantly improving cost-performance trade-offs. Additionally, the framework is shown to autonomously discover effective workflow structures, even in the absence of human-designed operators, marking a substantial advance toward general-purpose, automated agentic workflow generation.

53308560ea326a432ad4f0b36f7031e9f3948971.title: Gradient-based Discrete Sampling with Automatic Cyclical Scheduling
53308560ea326a432ad4f0b36f7031e9f3948971.research_question: How can efficient and accurate sampling from highly multimodal discrete distributions, such as those arising in deep models and language models, be achieved using gradient-based methods while avoiding the issue of getting trapped in local modes?
53308560ea326a432ad4f0b36f7031e9f3948971.hypothesis: A gradient-based discrete sampling method that employs automatic cyclical scheduling of step size and balancing parameters, with adaptive hyperparameter tuning, will enable efficient exploration and exploitation of multimodal discrete distributions, outperforming existing gradient-based discrete samplers in both sampling and learning tasks.
53308560ea326a432ad4f0b36f7031e9f3948971.proposed_method: A new sampling framework will be developed that parameterizes the proposal distribution for discrete variables using two key hyperparameters: step size (α) and a balancing parameter (β). The method will employ cyclical schedules for both step size and balancing parameter, where large step sizes facilitate exploration of new modes and small step sizes enable detailed exploitation within modes. The balancing parameter will be dynamically adjusted in tandem with the step size to maintain high acceptance rates across the cycle. An automatic tuning algorithm will be designed to select optimal values for the cyclical schedules, targeting a specified Metropolis-Hastings acceptance rate and adapting to the characteristics of the target distribution with minimal manual intervention. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to establish non-asymptotic convergence and inference guarantees for the proposed Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method.
53308560ea326a432ad4f0b36f7031e9f3948971.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. For sampling tasks, the method will be evaluated on Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs) and deep convolutional Energy-Based Models (EBMs) using datasets such as MNIST, KMNIST, EMNIST, Omniglot, and Caltech. Evaluation metrics will include Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) for sample quality and convergence speed, as well as log-likelihood scores estimated via Annealed Importance Sampling (AIS) for model learning. Baselines for comparison will include Gibbs-with-Gradient (GWG), Discrete Metropolis Adjusted Langevin Algorithm (DMALA), and Any-scale Balanced sampler (AB). For text infilling tasks, the method will be tested using masked sentences and a pretrained RoBERTa model, with metrics such as perplexity, CoLA acceptability, self-BLEU, and unique n-gram counts. All experiments will be run with multiple random seeds, and hyperparameter robustness will be assessed.
53308560ea326a432ad4f0b36f7031e9f3948971.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first gradient-based discrete sampling method specifically designed to target multimodal distributions through the use of cyclical schedules for both step size and balancing parameters. The method features an automatic tuning algorithm that enables adaptive and efficient configuration of hyperparameters across diverse datasets, reducing manual effort. Theoretical contributions include the first non-asymptotic convergence and inference guarantees for gradient-based discrete samplers, explicitly quantifying the distance to the target distribution. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior performance in both sampling and learning tasks compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

5342def3dba43b35468370092afbddde9c9eff5a.title: Fast Swap Regret Minimization and Applications to Approximate Correlated Equilibria
5342def3dba43b35468370092afbddde9c9eff5a.research_question: Can swap regret in online learning be minimized in a significantly faster manner than existing algorithms, and how can such advances be leveraged to efficiently compute approximate correlated equilibria in various game-theoretic settings, including normal-form and extensive-form games?
5342def3dba43b35468370092afbddde9c9eff5a.hypothesis: It is possible to design a computationally efficient algorithm that achieves exponentially faster swap regret minimization for any constant approximation parameter, and this improvement will yield faster convergence to approximate correlated equilibria in multiple models of computation and communication.
5342def3dba43b35468370092afbddde9c9eff5a.proposed_method: A new algorithm is proposed for swap regret minimization that operates in polylogarithmic rounds with respect to the number of actions, for any fixed approximation parameter ǫ > 0. The method employs a multi-scale version of the Multiplicative Weights Update (MWU) algorithm, running multiple threads at different time scales and aggregating their strategies. Each thread restarts at intervals of increasing length, and within each interval, MWU is executed over meta-rounds, aggregating rewards over blocks of days. The final strategy at each round is a uniform mixture over all threads. This approach achieves an exponential speedup in the number of rounds required to reach ǫ-swap regret, with a dependence on ǫ that is exponential but shown to be information-theoretically optimal via a matching lower bound.
5342def3dba43b35468370092afbddde9c9eff5a.experiment_details: The proposed algorithm will be analyzed and evaluated in the context of online learning with adversarially chosen rewards, including both oblivious and adaptive adversaries. Theoretical guarantees will be established for the number of rounds required to achieve ǫ-swap regret, and lower bounds will be proven to demonstrate optimality. Applications to game theory will be explored by simulating the algorithm in multi-player normal-form games, extensive-form games, and Bayesian games. The algorithm's performance will be compared to existing baselines in terms of convergence rate to ǫ-approximate correlated equilibrium, query complexity, and communication complexity, using both synthetic and theoretically constructed instances. Evaluation metrics will include swap regret, external regret, and the approximation quality of correlated equilibrium.
5342def3dba43b35468370092afbddde9c9eff5a.novelty_claims: The proposed method achieves the first exponential improvement in the number of rounds required for swap regret minimization for constant ǫ, resolving a longstanding open problem. The approach yields the first uncoupled dynamics converging to ǫ-correlated equilibrium in polylogarithmic rounds, as well as optimal query and communication complexity protocols for computing approximate correlated equilibria in two-player and multi-player games. Additionally, the method provides a PTAS for normal-form correlated equilibrium in extensive-form games, addressing a major open computational problem in the field.

535708777863633f7cc7fd6f4a716b1483c7100f.title: Reinforcement Learning from Diverse Human Preferences
535708777863633f7cc7fd6f4a716b1483c7100f.research_question: How can reinforcement learning agents effectively learn from diverse and inconsistent human preferences, particularly when human feedback is noisy, inconsistent, or adversarial, to enable robust policy optimization in real-world tasks?
535708777863633f7cc7fd6f4a716b1483c7100f.hypothesis: Introducing a strong constraint in the latent space of the reward model and employing a confidence-based ensembling mechanism will stabilize reward learning from diverse human preferences, leading to more reliable reinforcement signals and improved policy performance compared to existing preference-based RL methods.
535708777863633f7cc7fd6f4a716b1483c7100f.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a framework for reinforcement learning from diverse human preferences by manipulating reward predictions in a latent space. First, the reward model encodes state-action pairs into a latent Gaussian distribution using deep neural networks, with the mean and covariance parameterized by multi-layer perceptrons. A strong constraint is imposed on the latent space by minimizing the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the learned latent distribution and a fixed, non-parameterized reference distribution (e.g., standard Gaussian), ensuring temporal consistency and reducing fluctuations caused by inconsistent feedback. To further enhance stability, a confidence-based reward model ensembling mechanism is developed: multiple reward models are trained, and their predictions are aggregated by weighting each model's output according to its confidence, which is measured by the divergence of its latent space from the reference distribution. This approach allows the RL agent to receive more stable and reliable reward signals, even when human feedback is noisy or adversarial.
535708777863633f7cc7fd6f4a716b1483c7100f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on complex locomotion tasks from the DeepMind Control Suite (DMControl) and robotic manipulation tasks from Meta-world. The agent will not have access to ground truth rewards; instead, a team of scripted annotators with varying rationality and error rates will provide preference feedback on trajectory segments. The method will be integrated with the PEBBLE preference-based RL algorithm and compared against baselines including PEBBLE with a single perfect annotator (oracle) and PEBBLE with diverse annotators. Evaluation metrics will include ground truth episode return for locomotion tasks and success rate for manipulation tasks. Ablation studies will investigate the effect of constraint strength, the number of annotators, and the ensembling strategy, with all results averaged over multiple runs to assess stability and robustness.
535708777863633f7cc7fd6f4a716b1483c7100f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel approach to stabilizing reward learning from diverse and inconsistent human preferences by imposing a strong constraint on the latent space of the reward model. The method further innovates by employing a confidence-based ensembling mechanism that aggregates predictions from multiple reward models based on their confidence, directly addressing the challenge of learning from noisy, inconsistent, or adversarial feedback. This approach enables preference-based RL algorithms to scale to real-world scenarios with crowd-sourced or imperfect human feedback, significantly improving robustness and performance over existing methods.

536f7361fcaff37d250a5f012c683ee39f6bdf9d.title: Learning Parameterized Skills from Demonstrations
536f7361fcaff37d250a5f012c683ee39f6bdf9d.research_question: How can parameterized skills be effectively learned from expert demonstrations to enable rapid generalization and adaptation to novel tasks in complex, multi-task robotic environments?
536f7361fcaff37d250a5f012c683ee39f6bdf9d.hypothesis: Jointly learning discrete skill selection and continuous parameterization within a hierarchical framework, combined with information-theoretic regularization and aggressive observation compression, will yield temporally extended, semantically meaningful, and generalizable parameterized skills that outperform existing baselines in generalization and data efficiency.
536f7361fcaff37d250a5f012c683ee39f6bdf9d.proposed_method: A novel end-to-end algorithm, DEPS, is proposed to discover parameterized skills from expert demonstrations using a three-level hierarchical policy. The hierarchy consists of (i) a discrete skill selector, (ii) a continuous parameter policy conditioned on the selected skill, and (iii) a low-level subpolicy conditioned on both the discrete skill and its continuous parameters. Training is performed via temporal variational inference, maximizing a variational lower bound on trajectory likelihood, with variational encoders approximating the posterior over skill sequences and parameters. To avoid degenerate solutions and encourage meaningful skill abstractions, the approach incorporates information-theoretic regularization, such as KL-divergence penalties, and aggressively compresses the observation space for the subpolicy to a one-dimensional manifold, forcing reliance on latent skill variables. The continuous parameters are predicted per skill instance to ensure temporal coherence, and a skill parameter norm penalty is introduced to prevent overfitting. The high-level policies have access to rich observations, while the subpolicy operates on compressed proprioceptive state, creating an information asymmetry that encourages generalizable skill learning.
536f7361fcaff37d250a5f012c683ee39f6bdf9d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two challenging multitask robotic manipulation benchmarks: LIBERO and MetaWorld-v2. For LIBERO, 80 tasks from LIBERO-90 will be used for pretraining, with 50 human teleoperation demonstrations per task; evaluation will be performed on out-of-distribution tasks (LIBERO-OOD), standard long-horizon tasks (LIBERO-10), and few-shot settings (LIBERO-3-shot). For MetaWorld-v2, 10 tasks will be used for pretraining with 50 expert-scripted demonstrations each, and evaluation will be on two sets of 5 unseen tasks (MW-Vanilla and MW-PRISE). Baselines for comparison include multitask behavior cloning (BC), untrained BC, and PRISE, a state-of-the-art skill learning method. Evaluation metrics include MeanSuccess (average success rate across all tasks and evaluations) and MeanHighestSuccess (best success rate per task across evaluations), with performance measured over multiple random seeds. Fine-tuning on novel tasks will be performed with limited gradient steps and demonstrations to assess rapid adaptation and data efficiency.
536f7361fcaff37d250a5f012c683ee39f6bdf9d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified, end-to-end framework for learning parameterized skills directly from demonstrations, without requiring predefined skill libraries or manual task parameterization. The method leverages temporal variational inference for skill discovery and uniquely enforces an information bottleneck by compressing the subpolicy's input to a one-dimensional manifold, conceptualizing skills as parameterized trajectory families. This aggressive compression, combined with information-theoretic regularization, compels the model to learn robust, generalizable, and interpretable skills that can be rapidly adapted to new tasks. The approach is claimed to significantly outperform existing multitask and skill-learning baselines in both generalization to out-of-distribution tasks and data efficiency, as demonstrated on diverse robotic benchmarks.

5370aa35ab6fc216284402435af6fc7940ec9677.title: Accelerating Auto-regressive Text-to-Image Generation with Training-free Speculative Jacobi Decoding
5370aa35ab6fc216284402435af6fc7940ec9677.research_question: How can the inference speed of large auto-regressive text-to-image generation models be accelerated without sacrificing the diversity and quality of generated images, particularly in scenarios that require sampling-based decoding?
5370aa35ab6fc216284402435af6fc7940ec9677.hypothesis: A training-free probabilistic parallel decoding algorithm that introduces a probabilistic convergence criterion can accelerate auto-regressive text-to-image generation models while maintaining the visual quality and diversity enabled by sampling-based decoding.
5370aa35ab6fc216284402435af6fc7940ec9677.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces Speculative Jacobi Decoding (SJD), a training-free probabilistic parallel decoding algorithm for auto-regressive text-to-image generation. SJD operates by predicting multiple tokens in parallel within a sliding window (Jacobi window) during each iteration. In each iteration, the model performs a forward pass to obtain conditional probabilities for a sequence of draft tokens. A probabilistic acceptance criterion is then applied: for each token, the ratio of its probability conditioned on the current versus previous iteration is compared to a random threshold, determining whether the token is accepted or needs to be resampled. Accepted tokens are appended to the fixed sequence, while unaccepted tokens are resampled and combined with newly initialized tokens for the next iteration. Additionally, spatial locality-aware token initialization strategies are proposed to further accelerate convergence by leveraging the spatial structure of images.
5370aa35ab6fc216284402435af6fc7940ec9677.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on recent, large auto-regressive text-to-image generation models, specifically Lumina-mGPT (7B, 768x768 images) and Anole (7B, 512x512 images). Evaluation will use the MS-COCO 2017 validation set and the Parti-prompt benchmark. Metrics will include FID and CLIP-Score for visual quality, as well as step compression ratio and latency acceleration to assess speedup. Baselines will include standard auto-regressive decoding, vanilla Jacobi decoding, and SJD with and without spatial-prior-based token initialization. The effect of sampling randomness (top-K), image resolution, window size, and token initialization strategies will be systematically studied through ablation experiments.
5370aa35ab6fc216284402435af6fc7940ec9677.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to enable acceleration of auto-regressive text-to-image generation models that rely on sampling-based decoding, through a training-free probabilistic parallel decoding algorithm. Unlike prior speculative decoding approaches for language models, this method does not require training auxiliary models or fine-tuning. The integration of spatial locality-aware token initialization further enhances acceleration in scenarios with simple or repetitive image patterns. The approach achieves significant speedup (over 2x) without sacrificing image quality or diversity.

5377943c60dac4b66665183fd7e0c98a6c4387fb.title: Model-Free Opponent Shaping
5377943c60dac4b66665183fd7e0c98a6c4387fb.research_question: How can learning agents in general-sum multi-agent reinforcement learning environments shape the learning dynamics of their opponents to achieve mutually beneficial or strategically advantageous outcomes, without requiring access to the opponents' internal learning algorithms or higher-order derivatives?
5377943c60dac4b66665183fd7e0c98a6c4387fb.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a model-free meta-learning framework can be developed to shape opponent learning over long horizons, enabling agents to discover and exploit sophisticated strategies (such as extortion or reciprocity) in general-sum games, outperforming existing methods that rely on myopic updates, white-box access, or higher-order derivatives.
5377943c60dac4b66665183fd7e0c98a6c4387fb.proposed_method: A meta-learning framework, termed Model-Free Opponent Shaping (M-FOS), will be constructed in which each meta-step corresponds to an episode of the underlying (inner) game, and the meta-state consists of the current policies of all agents. The meta-policy, parameterized by a neural network, outputs the next policy to be used in the subsequent episode. Model-free optimization techniques, such as Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Genetic Algorithms, will be employed to train the meta-policy directly, avoiding the need for higher-order derivatives or white-box access to opponent learning algorithms. For low-dimensional games, the meta-policy will operate directly on policy parameters, while for high-dimensional environments, a variant will be developed that conditions on past trajectories to meta-learn across opponent learning steps. A meta-self-play training schedule inspired by Cognitive Hierarchies will be used to ensure stable and symmetric learning dynamics.
5377943c60dac4b66665183fd7e0c98a6c4387fb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in several benchmark environments, including the Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma (IPD), Iterated Matching Pennies (IMP), the Chicken Game (matrix games), and the high-dimensional Coin Game. In matrix games, the meta-policy will observe the full state (concatenated policies), while in the Coin Game, only the effects of past actions will be available. Baselines for comparison will include Naive Learners (NL), Learning with Opponent Learning Awareness (LOLA), and Multiagent Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (M-MAML). Evaluation metrics will include average rewards in head-to-head tournaments, the ability to discover or exploit known strategies (such as Zero-Determinant extortion and Tit-for-Tat), and performance in self-play. Experiments will also assess scalability to high-dimensional settings and the stability of learning dynamics under meta-self-play.
5377943c60dac4b66665183fd7e0c98a6c4387fb.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first model-free meta-learning framework for opponent shaping that does not require higher-order derivatives or white-box access to opponent learning algorithms. It enables long-horizon opponent shaping, is consistent and symmetric in self-play, and can discover sophisticated strategies such as Zero-Determinant extortion and Tit-for-Tat without hand-coding or access to opponent rewards. The approach claims to outperform existing baselines in both exploitation and cooperation, and to scale to high-dimensional environments where previous methods fail.

5387445a58a958422a8cfd297e6a611aade0f0e8.title: 3D-Properties: Identifying Challenges in DPO and Charting a Path Forward
5387445a58a958422a8cfd297e6a611aade0f0e8.research_question: What are the fundamental challenges in reward-model-free preference learning methods, such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), for aligning large language models with human preferences, and how can these challenges be addressed to improve stability and performance relative to reward-model-based approaches?
5387445a58a958422a8cfd297e6a611aade0f0e8.hypothesis: Reward-model-free preference learning methods, particularly DPO, exhibit inherent optimization instabilities that limit their effectiveness compared to reward-model-based approaches; introducing targeted regularization techniques and analyzing the impact of preference data distribution can mitigate these limitations and enhance alignment performance.
5387445a58a958422a8cfd297e6a611aade0f0e8.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted to identify and characterize the optimization dynamics of DPO, focusing on three emergent properties: drastic drop in rejected response likelihood, degradation into response suppression, and dispersion effect on unseen responses (termed '3D-properties'). Analytical derivations of DPO's gradient behavior will be performed to explain these phenomena. To address the identified issues, two regularization strategies will be developed: (1) adaptive adjustment of the loss weighting (beta parameters) for chosen and rejected responses (Flex-DPO), and (2) augmentation of the DPO loss with a supervised fine-tuning (SFT) loss. These methods will be theoretically analyzed and empirically validated. The impact of preference data distribution, particularly on-policy versus off-policy data, will also be systematically studied.
5387445a58a958422a8cfd297e6a611aade0f0e8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic toy models and real-world large language models (Baichuan2-13B and Baichuan2-33B). Benchmarks will include mathematical reasoning (MATH dataset), out-of-distribution generalization (SuperCLUE-Math), and creative instruction-following tasks (custom poem and slogan datasets with explicit structural constraints). Preference datasets will be constructed using both on-policy and off-policy sampling strategies. Baselines will include vanilla DPO, Flex-DPO, other RM-free methods (IPO, SLiC), and RM-based alignment (RLHF-PPO). Evaluation metrics will consist of accuracy (e.g., proportion of correct preference choices), GPT-4-based scoring for mathematical tasks, and structured metrics for creative tasks (e.g., row number, rhythm, content). Experimental setups will include ablation studies on regularization parameters and detailed analysis of gradient dynamics and likelihood changes during training.
5387445a58a958422a8cfd297e6a611aade0f0e8.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled theoretical framework that identifies and explains the 3D-properties as inherent limitations of DPO and similar RM-free alignment methods. It provides the first comprehensive analysis connecting gradient dynamics to observed empirical instabilities in DPO. The proposed regularization techniques, including adaptive loss weighting and SFT augmentation, are novel in their targeted mitigation of DPO's optimization issues. The work systematically investigates the impact of preference data distribution (on-policy vs. off-policy) on DPO effectiveness, and offers actionable insights for improving the stability and performance of RM-free preference learning, aiming to bridge the gap with RM-based approaches.

539403681db02a40265b65e99fa5d3b5f928d14e.title: Multi-Player Zero-Sum Markov Games with Networked Separable Interactions
539403681db02a40265b65e99fa5d3b5f928d14e.research_question: What are the structural and computational properties of multi-player zero-sum Markov games with networked separable (polymatrix) interactions, and how can equilibrium concepts be efficiently computed or approximated in these settings?
539403681db02a40265b65e99fa5d3b5f928d14e.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that multi-player zero-sum Markov games with networked separable interactions possess unique structural properties that can be exploited to simplify equilibrium computation, but that computational hardness may persist except in special network topologies.
539403681db02a40265b65e99fa5d3b5f928d14e.proposed_method: A new class of Markov games, termed zero-sum Markov Games with Networked Separable Interactions (zero-sum NMGs), will be formally defined, where each state's auxiliary game is zero-sum and exhibits a polymatrix structure across an interaction network. Necessary and sufficient conditions for a Markov game to qualify as a zero-sum NMG will be established, focusing on decomposability of reward and transition dynamics. The relationship between Markov coarse correlated equilibrium (CCE) and Markov Nash equilibrium (NE) will be analyzed, with proofs that, in these games, marginalizing a CCE yields a NE. Computational complexity of finding stationary equilibria will be studied, including PPAD-hardness proofs for general network structures. To address these challenges, fictitious-play-type learning dynamics will be developed and analyzed for convergence in star-shaped networks, and value-iteration-based algorithms will be proposed for computing Markov non-stationary NE with finite-iteration guarantees.
539403681db02a40265b65e99fa5d3b5f928d14e.experiment_details: Numerical experiments will be conducted on several representative zero-sum NMGs, including Markov fashion games, Markov security games, and macroeconomic trading games. These experiments will utilize both synthetic and realistic network structures, such as star and triangle topologies, to evaluate the proposed algorithms. Baseline comparisons will include standard value-iteration and fictitious play methods, as well as existing approaches for general Markov games. Evaluation metrics will include convergence rate to equilibrium, computational time, and approximation error (e.g., epsilon-approximate NE/CCE). Experimental setups will vary the number of players, network connectivity, and reward/transition decomposability to assess robustness and scalability.
539403681db02a40265b65e99fa5d3b5f928d14e.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first comprehensive study of multi-player zero-sum Markov games with networked separable (polymatrix) interactions, providing a strict generalization of zero-sum polymatrix games to the Markov setting. It establishes new structural results linking CCE and NE in these games, characterizes the precise conditions under which such games can be represented, and proves computational hardness results for equilibrium computation. The development of fictitious-play-type dynamics with convergence guarantees in star-shaped networks and the design of value-iteration-based algorithms with finite-iteration guarantees for non-stationary NE computation are novel contributions. The work also provides a suite of application-motivated examples and a unified framework for analyzing networked interactions in Markov games.

5396c55bee2a2abf2207e1cc5e5ae72c9edef9fa.title: Improving and generalizing flow-based generative models with minibatch optimal transport
5396c55bee2a2abf2207e1cc5e5ae72c9edef9fa.research_question: How can the training and generalization of continuous normalizing flows (CNFs) for generative modeling be improved, particularly in terms of efficiency, stability, and applicability to arbitrary source and target distributions, including optimal transport and Schrödinger bridge problems?
5396c55bee2a2abf2207e1cc5e5ae72c9edef9fa.hypothesis: Simulation-free training objectives based on conditional flow matching (CFM), especially when combined with minibatch optimal transport (OT) couplings, will yield CNF models that are more stable, generalize better, and achieve faster and more accurate inference across a range of generative modeling tasks compared to existing CNF and diffusion-based approaches.
5396c55bee2a2abf2207e1cc5e5ae72c9edef9fa.proposed_method: A generalized conditional flow matching (CFM) framework will be developed for training CNFs, allowing regression to vector fields that generate mixtures of probability paths conditioned on arbitrary couplings between source and target distributions. The method will include a variant, optimal transport CFM (OT-CFM), where the conditioning variable is sampled from an (approximate) optimal transport plan, enabling the learned flow to approximate dynamic OT. For large datasets, minibatch OT will be used to approximate the coupling efficiently, reducing computational complexity. An entropic variant (SB-CFM) will also be implemented to address Schrödinger bridge problems, using entropy-regularized OT couplings and Brownian bridge interpolants. The approach will be implemented as a simulation-free, regression-based training objective, leveraging neural ODE parameterizations for the vector fields.
5396c55bee2a2abf2207e1cc5e5ae72c9edef9fa.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both low-dimensional synthetic datasets (such as Gaussian, 8gaussians, moons, and scurve) and high-dimensional real-world data, including single-cell trajectory interpolation tasks using CITE-seq, Multiome, and Embryoid body datasets. Baselines will include standard CNFs, regularized CNFs, flow matching (FM), rectified flow (RF), input-convex neural networks (ICNN), and diffusion-based Schrödinger bridge (DSB) methods. Evaluation metrics will comprise 2-Wasserstein distance, normalized path energy (NPE), earth mover's distance (1-Wasserstein), and runtime (training and inference time). Experiments will compare training stability, convergence speed, inference efficiency (number of ODE function evaluations), and generative modeling performance. Both exact and minibatch OT couplings will be tested, with ablations on batch size and regularization parameters.
5396c55bee2a2abf2207e1cc5e5ae72c9edef9fa.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified, simulation-free training framework for CNFs that generalizes flow matching to arbitrary source and target distributions via conditional flow matching. It is the first to systematically incorporate minibatch optimal transport couplings into CNF training, enabling efficient approximation of dynamic OT flows and Schrödinger bridges without requiring Gaussian sources or tractable densities. The approach claims improved training stability, faster convergence, and more efficient inference compared to existing CNF and diffusion-based methods. Additionally, the method supports a broad range of generative modeling tasks, including conditional and unconditional generation, image translation, and single-cell dynamics, and is accompanied by a unified open-source software package for reproducible research.

53a5b1aad1f9c211dc4e641c6933f4bc297894f7.title: Prioritizing Perception-Guided Self-Supervision: A New Paradigm for Causal Modeling in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
53a5b1aad1f9c211dc4e641c6933f4bc297894f7.research_question: How can end-to-end autonomous driving systems be trained to more robustly model causal relationships between environmental context and driving actions, thereby improving closed-loop performance and generalization in complex real-world scenarios?
53a5b1aad1f9c211dc4e641c6933f4bc297894f7.hypothesis: Prioritizing perception-guided self-supervision as the primary training paradigm, rather than relying solely on imitation learning from expert trajectories, will significantly reduce causal confusion and improve both safety and generalization in end-to-end autonomous driving.
53a5b1aad1f9c211dc4e641c6933f4bc297894f7.proposed_method: A new training paradigm for end-to-end autonomous driving is proposed, which leverages perception outputs as primary supervisory signals for the planning module. The method introduces three self-supervision mechanisms: Multi-Modal Trajectory Planning Self-Supervision (MTPS), which reformulates multi-modal decision-making as a lane selection task based on perceived lane centerlines; Spatial Trajectory Planning Self-Supervision (STPS), which aligns the planned ego trajectory with the spatial geometry of lane centerlines to reduce noise from suboptimal expert demonstrations; and Negative Trajectory Planning Self-Supervision (NTPS), which uses predicted future trajectories of surrounding agents to penalize ego trajectories that risk collisions. These self-supervision signals are integrated into a unified loss function, and the overall architecture minimally modifies a standard end-to-end network by augmenting the planning head and loss computation. The perception module provides structured representations of road topology and dynamic agents, which are used both as input features and as supervision targets for planning.
53a5b1aad1f9c211dc4e641c6933f4bc297894f7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Bench2Drive benchmark, a challenging closed-loop evaluation suite based on CARLA v2, which includes 1,000 short clips across 44 complex scenarios and 220 predefined routes. The evaluation will use official metrics such as DrivingScore, SuccessRate, Efficiency, Comfortness, and L2 Displacement Error for both open-loop and closed-loop performance. The proposed method will be compared against a range of baselines, including VAD, UniAD, DriveTransformer, and knowledge distillation-based methods, under identical network backbones and training conditions. Ablation studies will isolate the impact of each self-supervision component, and scenario-specific success rates (e.g., merging, overtaking, emergency braking) will be reported to assess generalization and safety in interactive driving contexts. Training will be performed in two stages: initial perception learning followed by joint optimization with self-supervised planning objectives, using large-scale GPU resources and standardized hyperparameters.
53a5b1aad1f9c211dc4e641c6933f4bc297894f7.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel perception-guided self-supervision paradigm that explicitly aligns both the inputs and outputs of the decision-making module with structured perception outputs, directly addressing causal confusion in end-to-end autonomous driving. The integration of MTPS, STPS, and NTPS mechanisms provides a unified framework for positive and negative causal modeling, enabling robust lane selection, trajectory alignment with road topology, and proactive collision avoidance. Unlike prior approaches that focus on suppressing input noise or rely on complex architectures, this method achieves substantial improvements in closed-loop driving performance with minimal architectural changes, establishing a new direction for causally grounded, generalizable autonomous driving systems.

53a803388e83ae89261624099d7be4287ace67cb.title: DeepSeek-V2: A Strong, Economical, and Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Language Model
53a803388e83ae89261624099d7be4287ace67cb.research_question: How can large language models be designed to achieve high performance while significantly reducing training costs and improving inference efficiency, particularly with respect to memory and throughput constraints?
53a803388e83ae89261624099d7be4287ace67cb.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that integrating a novel Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) mechanism with a high-performance Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture can enable large language models to achieve state-of-the-art performance while drastically reducing training costs and inference memory requirements.
53a803388e83ae89261624099d7be4287ace67cb.proposed_method: The proposed method involves developing a Transformer-based language model that incorporates two key innovations: Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) and DeepSeekMoE. MLA introduces a low-rank joint compression of key and value vectors, reducing the Key-Value (KV) cache size during inference without sacrificing model performance. This is achieved by projecting keys and values into a shared low-dimensional latent space, enabling efficient caching and computation. The DeepSeekMoE architecture segments experts into finer granularity and isolates shared experts to enhance specialization and reduce redundancy, while employing device-limited routing and auxiliary load balancing losses to optimize parallelism and efficiency. The model is pretrained on a large, high-quality, multi-source corpus, followed by supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning alignment to maximize performance and safety.
53a803388e83ae89261624099d7be4287ace67cb.experiment_details: Experiments will pretrain the model on an 8.1 trillion token corpus sourced from diverse and high-quality datasets, with particular emphasis on both English and Chinese data. The model will be evaluated on a wide range of benchmarks, including MMLU, AlpacaEval 2.0, MT-Bench, and AlignBench, covering tasks such as math, code, writing, reasoning, and open-ended conversation. Baselines for comparison will include previous DeepSeek models, Mixtral, LLaMA 2/3, Qwen, DBRX, and Command R+, among others. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, training cost (GPU hours per token), KV cache size per token, and maximum generation throughput (tokens/sec), with detailed ablation studies on attention mechanisms and efficiency analyses.
53a803388e83ae89261624099d7be4287ace67cb.novelty_claims: The proposal claims novelty in the introduction of Multi-head Latent Attention, which achieves superior performance to standard Multi-Head Attention while reducing KV cache requirements by over 90%. The DeepSeekMoE architecture is designed to provide stronger performance and greater efficiency than conventional MoE approaches, enabling the training of large models at significantly lower cost. The combination of these techniques allows for a model with 236B total parameters but only 21B activated per token, supporting extremely long context lengths and high throughput. Additional innovations include device-limited routing and multi-level load balancing losses, as well as the release of both large and lite model variants for the research community.

53d128ea815bcc0526856eb5a9c42cc977cb36a7.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
53d128ea815bcc0526856eb5a9c42cc977cb36a7.research_question: Can large language models autonomously learn to use external tools via simple APIs, thereby enhancing their performance on a wide range of tasks without sacrificing their core language modeling abilities?
53d128ea815bcc0526856eb5a9c42cc977cb36a7.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a language model can be trained, in a self-supervised manner and with minimal human annotation, to decide when and how to call external tools through APIs, leading to substantial improvements in zero-shot task performance while maintaining general language modeling capabilities.
53d128ea815bcc0526856eb5a9c42cc977cb36a7.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed in which a pretrained language model is equipped with the ability to call external tools (such as calculators, question answering systems, search engines, translation systems, and calendars) via API calls represented as special text tokens. The method involves three main steps: (1) sampling candidate API calls within a large text corpus using in-context learning and a handful of human-written demonstrations per API, (2) executing these API calls and filtering them based on whether their results help the model predict future tokens (using a self-supervised loss reduction criterion), and (3) fine-tuning the language model on the augmented dataset where only helpful API calls are interleaved with the original text. At inference, the model autonomously decides when and how to invoke tools, and API responses are dynamically incorporated into the text generation process.
53d128ea815bcc0526856eb5a9c42cc977cb36a7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a 6.7B parameter GPT-J model as the base language model, with fine-tuning performed on a subset of the CCNet dataset augmented with API calls. The approach will be evaluated on a variety of downstream tasks, including factual completion (LAMA), mathematical reasoning (ASDiv, SVAMP, MAWPS), question answering (Web Questions, Natural Questions, TriviaQA), multilingual QA (MLQA), and temporal reasoning (TEMPLAMA, DATESET). Baseline comparisons will include the original GPT-J, GPT-J fine-tuned without API calls, Toolformer with API calls disabled, and much larger models such as OPT (66B) and GPT-3 (175B). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy or match rates appropriate to each task, as well as perplexity on standard language modeling benchmarks (WikiText, CCNet) to assess preservation of core LM abilities. Additional analyses will examine the impact of model size and decoding strategies on tool use.
53d128ea815bcc0526856eb5a9c42cc977cb36a7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach enables language models to autonomously learn tool use in a self-supervised manner, requiring only a handful of demonstrations per tool and no extensive human annotation. Unlike prior work, the method is agnostic to the specific dataset and task, allowing the model to decide for itself when and how to use tools, thus maintaining generality. The framework achieves substantial improvements in zero-shot performance across diverse tasks, often outperforming much larger models, while preserving language modeling capabilities. The method also demonstrates that the ability to leverage tools emerges only at sufficient model scale and provides a principled, loss-based filtering mechanism to ensure only helpful tool interactions are learned.

53d12a37bc6ea511e9f59fe153df4bc8abf41cfc.title: Spectral Sparsification of Graphs
53d12a37bc6ea511e9f59fe153df4bc8abf41cfc.research_question: Can every graph be efficiently approximated by a sparse subgraph that preserves the spectral properties of its Laplacian matrix, and can such sparsifiers be constructed in nearly-linear time?
53d12a37bc6ea511e9f59fe153df4bc8abf41cfc.hypothesis: Every weighted graph admits a spectral sparsifier with nearly-linear number of edges, and such a sparsifier can be constructed in nearly-linear time while preserving the Laplacian quadratic form within a small multiplicative error.
53d12a37bc6ea511e9f59fe153df4bc8abf41cfc.proposed_method: A new algorithm will be developed to construct spectral sparsifiers by leveraging random sampling techniques guided by the conductance properties of the input graph. The method will first partition the graph into subgraphs of high conductance using a nearly-linear time graph partitioning algorithm (ApproxCut). For each high-conductance subgraph, edges will be sampled with probabilities inversely proportional to the minimum degree of their endpoints, and their weights will be scaled accordingly to ensure unbiasedness. The process will ensure that every vertex retains incident edges with high probability by setting the sampling parameter proportional to log(n). The Laplacian quadratic form of the sparsifier will be shown to approximate that of the original graph for all vectors, using refined spectral norm bounds on the difference of Laplacians. The construction will be extended to weighted graphs by adapting the sampling probabilities and partitioning steps.
53d12a37bc6ea511e9f59fe153df4bc8abf41cfc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of synthetic and real-world graphs, including complete graphs, joined complete graphs, and graphs with low and high conductance. The proposed sparsification algorithm will be evaluated by comparing the spectral similarity (measured via the Laplacian quadratic form and eigenvalue approximation) between the original and sparsified graphs. Baseline methods such as cut sparsifiers (e.g., Benczur-Karger sparsifiers) and spanners will be included for comparison. Evaluation metrics will include the number of edges in the sparsifier, the spectral approximation ratio (σ), and the runtime of the algorithm. Additional experiments will examine the utility of the sparsifiers as preconditioners for solving linear systems in diagonally-dominant matrices, measuring convergence rates and total computation time.
53d12a37bc6ea511e9f59fe153df4bc8abf41cfc.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the concept of spectral sparsification, which requires the Laplacian quadratic form of the sparsifier to approximate that of the original graph for all vectors, a stronger guarantee than previous notions such as cut sparsification. The algorithm achieves nearly-linear runtime in the number of edges, and guarantees the existence and efficient construction of sparsifiers with nearly-linear size for all graphs. The method also provides a crucial building block for nearly-linear time algorithms for solving linear systems in symmetric, diagonally-dominant matrices. The use of conductance-aware random sampling and the integration with advanced graph partitioning techniques constitute key innovations.

53d5749d04b3b1e70e88c12bc730c18bcc3ee018.title: Fairness-aware Anomaly Detection via Fair Projection
53d5749d04b3b1e70e88c12bc730c18bcc3ee018.research_question: How can group fairness be effectively ensured in unsupervised anomaly detection, particularly in scenarios involving sensitive demographic attributes, while maintaining high detection accuracy and providing robust fairness evaluation metrics?
53d5749d04b3b1e70e88c12bc730c18bcc3ee018.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that mapping data from different demographic groups to a common, simple, and compact target distribution enables unsupervised anomaly detection models to achieve group fairness without sacrificing detection accuracy. Furthermore, a threshold-free fairness metric can provide a holistic and reliable evaluation of fairness across demographic groups.
53d5749d04b3b1e70e88c12bc730c18bcc3ee018.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a fairness-aware unsupervised anomaly detection framework that learns a projection mapping data from different demographic groups into a shared target distribution, specifically a truncated isotropic Gaussian. This projection is learned via deep neural networks and optimized using a combination of Sinkhorn distance (for distribution alignment) and reconstruction error (for information preservation). The method does not require explicit fairness regularization; instead, fairness is achieved by enforcing that all groups' data distributions align with the same compact target distribution in the latent space. An anomaly score is defined based on the density in the target space, and the approach supports both a primary method (Im-FairAD) and a variant (Ex-FairAD) that further minimizes the distribution distance of anomaly scores across groups. Additionally, a novel threshold-free fairness metric, Average Demographic Parity Difference (ADPD), is proposed to evaluate group fairness holistically.
53d5749d04b3b1e70e88c12bc730c18bcc3ee018.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six publicly available real-world datasets commonly used in fairness and anomaly detection research, including datasets with various sensitive attributes such as race, gender, and age. The evaluation will compare the proposed methods against standard unsupervised anomaly detection baselines (e.g., LOF, DeepSVDD), two-stage pipelines combining fair representation learning with anomaly detection, and state-of-the-art fairness-aware anomaly detection methods (e.g., DeepFairSVDD, CFAD, FairOD). Both balanced and skewed data splitting strategies across demographic groups will be examined to assess robustness. Evaluation metrics will include detection accuracy (AUC, F1-score), threshold-dependent fairness ratios, and the proposed threshold-free ADPD metric, with additional analysis on the fairness of detected anomalies and the impact of demographic imbalance.
53d5749d04b3b1e70e88c12bc730c18bcc3ee018.novelty_claims: The proposal claims novelty in (1) introducing a fairness-aware anomaly detection framework that achieves group fairness via distributional alignment without explicit fairness regularization, (2) developing a threshold-free fairness metric (ADPD) for holistic fairness evaluation in unsupervised settings, and (3) providing a coordinated, end-to-end optimization that improves the trade-off between detection accuracy and fairness, particularly under both balanced and skewed group distributions. The method is also claimed to be robust to demographic imbalances and effective in ensuring fairness on both normal and anomalous data, despite the absence of anomalous samples during training.

53d6719e20dec6af0b1f2de159f916efb545877b.title: AnyEdit: Edit Any Knowledge Encoded in Language Models
53d6719e20dec6af0b1f2de159f916efb545877b.research_question: How can knowledge encoded in large language models be efficiently and accurately updated, especially when the knowledge is long-form and represented in diverse formats beyond structured triples?
53d6719e20dec6af0b1f2de159f916efb545877b.hypothesis: An autoregressive, multi-token editing paradigm that decomposes long-form knowledge into sequential chunks and iteratively edits key tokens in each chunk will overcome the efficacy barrier of single-token editing, enabling consistent, accurate, and scalable knowledge updates in language models regardless of knowledge length or format.
53d6719e20dec6af0b1f2de159f916efb545877b.proposed_method: A novel autoregressive editing framework, AnyEdit, will be developed to update knowledge in large language models by decomposing the target knowledge into sequential chunks, each treated as an independent sub-knowledge unit. At each step, the final token of the current chunk is located and its hidden state is perturbed to maximize the likelihood of generating the subsequent chunk, following the chain rule of mutual information. The editing process involves four main steps: (1) chunking the target output using either a sliding window or semantic segmentation, (2) locating the last token of each chunk and the influential layers via causal tracing, (3) editing the hidden state of the selected token using gradient descent to maximize the probability of generating the chunk, and (4) updating model parameters to align the hidden states with the edited states using least-squares optimization. This autoregressive process is theoretically grounded to ensure consistent and complete knowledge updates, and is designed to be plug-and-play, enabling integration with existing locate-then-edit methods.
53d6719e20dec6af0b1f2de159f916efb545877b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on widely used LLMs such as Llama3-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Chat. The evaluation will use both standard benchmarks (UnKEBench, AKEW, Counterfact, ZsRE) and a newly curated EditEverything dataset, which contains long-form, diverse-formatted knowledge entries up to 458 tokens in length across domains like mathematics, news, code, and biochemistry. Baseline comparisons will include FT-L, MEND, ROME, MEMIT, AlphaEdit, and UnKE. Evaluation metrics will include semantic similarity (BERTScore) and lexical similarity (ROUGE-L) for original, paraphrased, and sub-questions. Experiments will also assess the impact of chunk size, editing time, and the ability to boost existing editing methods by integrating the AnyEdit paradigm.
53d6719e20dec6af0b1f2de159f916efb545877b.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first autoregressive, multi-token collaborative editing paradigm for LLMs, theoretically grounded in the chain rule of mutual information. It enables efficient and precise updates to knowledge of arbitrary length and format, overcoming the efficacy barrier of single-token editing. AnyEdit is the first framework to support plug-and-play integration with existing editing methods, significantly expanding the scope and practicality of LLM knowledge editing. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate substantial improvements over strong baselines, particularly in editing long-form and diverse-formatted knowledge.

53dcf467fbded741dd08902d4203a9b57e889c87.title: Contrastive Learning as Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning
53dcf467fbded741dd08902d4203a9b57e889c87.research_question: Can reinforcement learning algorithms be designed to directly acquire effective representations for goal-conditioned tasks, without relying on auxiliary perception losses, data augmentation, or separate representation learning objectives?
53dcf467fbded741dd08902d4203a9b57e889c87.hypothesis: Contrastive learning methods, when applied directly to action-labeled trajectories in goal-conditioned reinforcement learning, can serve as effective RL algorithms by learning representations whose inner products correspond to goal-conditioned value functions, thereby achieving competitive or superior performance compared to traditional RL approaches that use auxiliary objectives or data augmentation.
53dcf467fbded741dd08902d4203a9b57e889c87.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed that casts contrastive representation learning as a goal-conditioned reinforcement learning algorithm. The approach involves learning representations of state-action pairs and goal states such that the inner product between these representations corresponds to the value function for reaching a goal. Specifically, the method uses a contrastive loss where positive pairs consist of a state-action and a future state sampled from the discounted state occupancy measure, and negative pairs are sampled from random states. The critic is parameterized as the inner product between the state-action and goal representations, and the policy is trained to select actions that maximize this inner product for a given goal. The algorithm alternates between fitting the critic using the contrastive objective and updating the policy using gradients derived from the learned critic, with implementation details optimized for efficiency using modern deep learning frameworks.
53dcf467fbded741dd08902d4203a9b57e889c87.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a suite of goal-conditioned RL tasks, including both state-based and image-based environments such as Fetch Reach, Fetch Push, Sawyer Push, Sawyer Bin, Point Spiral11x11, and Ant Umaze. Baselines include TD3+HER (actor-critic with hindsight relabeling), goal-conditioned behavioral cloning (GCBC), and model-based approaches that fit density models to future state distributions. Additional comparisons are made with representation learning techniques such as DrQ (data augmentation), autoencoder-based auxiliary losses, and CURL (augmentation-based contrastive learning). Evaluation metrics primarily focus on success rates, with experiments run across multiple random seeds to assess robustness. Offline RL experiments use the D4RL AntMaze benchmark, comparing against BC, DT, GCBC, TD3+BC, and IQL, and ablation studies explore the impact of algorithmic variants and partial observability.
53dcf467fbded741dd08902d4203a9b57e889c87.novelty_claims: The proposed approach demonstrates that contrastive representation learning can be directly used as a goal-conditioned RL algorithm, eliminating the need for auxiliary losses, data augmentation, or separate representation learning objectives. The method provides a theoretical connection between contrastive learning and value function estimation, generalizes prior methods such as C-learning, and introduces simpler yet more effective algorithms. Experimental results show that this framework achieves higher success rates than prior non-contrastive methods, particularly on challenging image-based and offline RL tasks, and is robust to partial observability and moving cameras. The work establishes a new family of contrastive RL algorithms with both theoretical and empirical advantages.

53eecd3d126a11911b53c639a7a808cac4fbf127.title: Neural-Symbolic Models for Logical Queries on Knowledge Graphs
53eecd3d126a11911b53c639a7a808cac4fbf127.research_question: How can complex first-order logic (FOL) queries be effectively and interpretably answered on incomplete knowledge graphs, combining the strengths of symbolic and neural methods?
53eecd3d126a11911b53c639a7a808cac4fbf127.hypothesis: A neural-symbolic model that decomposes FOL queries into interpretable operations over fuzzy sets, and executes relation projections using graph neural networks (GNNs) combined with fuzzy logic operations, will achieve superior accuracy and interpretability in answering logical queries on incomplete knowledge graphs compared to existing embedding-based or symbolic-only approaches.
53eecd3d126a11911b53c639a7a808cac4fbf127.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a neural-symbolic framework, Graph Neural Network Query Executor (GNN-QE), for answering complex FOL queries on knowledge graphs. The method first decomposes each FOL query into a sequence of basic operations: relation projections and logical operations (conjunction, disjunction, negation) over fuzzy sets representing sets of entities. Relation projections are parameterized by a GNN adapted from knowledge graph completion, which predicts fuzzy sets of tail entities given fuzzy sets of head entities and a relation. Logical operations are instantiated using product fuzzy logic, ensuring interpretability and adherence to logical laws. The model incorporates traversal dropout to regularize training and prevent overfitting to relation traversal patterns, and employs batched postfix expression execution to efficiently process queries of varying structures.
53eecd3d126a11911b53c639a7a808cac4fbf127.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on three standard knowledge graph datasets: FB15k, FB15k-237, and NELL995. The evaluation uses standard train/validation/test splits and a suite of FOL query types, including both existential positive and negation queries. Baselines include state-of-the-art embedding-based models (GQE, Q2B, BetaE, FuzzQE, ConE) and neural-symbolic methods (CQD-CO, CQD-Beam). Performance is measured using mean reciprocal rank (MRR) and HITS@K, with separate reporting for easy and hard answers. Additional experiments assess the model's ability to predict answer set cardinality without explicit supervision, visualize intermediate variables for interpretability, and analyze robustness to training data size and GNN architecture choices.
53eecd3d126a11911b53c639a7a808cac4fbf127.novelty_claims: The proposed method claims several innovations: (1) a neural-symbolic framework that decomposes FOL queries into interpretable operations over fuzzy sets, (2) the use of GNNs for scalable and expressive relation projection directly over fuzzy sets rather than individual entities, (3) instantiation of logical operations with product fuzzy logic, guaranteeing interpretability and logical consistency, (4) traversal dropout to enhance generalization to incomplete graphs, (5) efficient batched execution of diverse query structures, and (6) the ability to predict the number of answers and visualize intermediate reasoning steps without explicit supervision. The approach achieves significant improvements over prior state-of-the-art models in both accuracy and interpretability on complex logical queries.

53f4fb0e9972989194368faf288ff8e3cba5bd60.title: Chatbot Arena: An Open Platform for Evaluating LLMs by Human Preference
53f4fb0e9972989194368faf288ff8e3cba5bd60.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be evaluated for alignment with human preferences in a way that is robust, scalable, and reflective of real-world usage scenarios?
53f4fb0e9972989194368faf288ff8e3cba5bd60.hypothesis: A large-scale, open, crowdsourced platform that collects pairwise human preference data on LLM responses to live, user-generated prompts can provide more accurate, diverse, and robust model rankings than static, ground-truth-based benchmarks.
53f4fb0e9972989194368faf288ff8e3cba5bd60.proposed_method: A novel open-access platform will be developed where users can submit any prompt and receive responses from two anonymized LLMs. Users will compare the responses and cast a vote for the preferred answer, with options for 'tie' or 'both are bad' to account for ambiguity. The platform will employ a pairwise comparison methodology, leveraging crowdsourced votes to build a large-scale, diverse dataset of human preferences. To ensure efficient and statistically valid model ranking, advanced statistical techniques such as the Bradley-Terry model and robust confidence intervals will be used to estimate win rates and rankings. An adaptive sampling algorithm will be designed to prioritize model pairs with uncertain rankings, thereby improving sample efficiency and accelerating convergence to stable rankings. Additional mechanisms will be implemented to detect and filter out anomalous or low-quality user contributions.
53f4fb0e9972989194368faf288ff8e3cba5bd60.experiment_details: Experiments will involve deploying the platform to the public and collecting over 100,000 pairwise preference votes from a diverse user base, covering more than 50 LLMs (including both proprietary and open-source models) and over 100 languages. The dataset will include multi-turn conversations and user votes. Baselines for comparison will include traditional static benchmarks such as MMLU, HellaSwag, GSM-8K, and MT-Bench, as well as LLM-as-judge evaluations (e.g., using GPT-4 as a judge). Evaluation metrics will include win rates, agreement rates between crowd, expert, and LLM-judge votes, prompt diversity (via topic modeling), and statistical confidence in rankings. The effectiveness of the adaptive sampling algorithm will be assessed by comparing sample efficiency and ranking convergence against random sampling. Anomalous user detection will be validated using manually labeled data.
53f4fb0e9972989194368faf288ff8e3cba5bd60.novelty_claims: The proposed platform introduces the first large-scale, open, live, crowdsourced evaluation system for LLMs based on human preference, enabling dynamic, real-world benchmarking across a wide range of tasks and languages. The methodology leverages advanced statistical ranking and adaptive sampling algorithms to achieve efficient, robust, and credible model rankings. The approach addresses key limitations of static, ground-truth-based benchmarks by incorporating live, diverse prompts and real human feedback. The resulting human preference dataset and open-source platform will provide a valuable resource for the research community and industry, establishing a new standard for LLM evaluation.

54020e5fe48ebb250f27d744e20a63cac2988a84.title: Model soups: averaging weights of multiple fine-tuned models improves accuracy without increasing inference time
54020e5fe48ebb250f27d744e20a63cac2988a84.research_question: Can combining the weights of multiple independently fine-tuned models improve accuracy and robustness on downstream tasks, without increasing inference or memory costs, compared to selecting the single best model from a hyperparameter sweep?
54020e5fe48ebb250f27d744e20a63cac2988a84.hypothesis: Averaging the weights of multiple fine-tuned models, rather than selecting the single best model, will yield higher accuracy and robustness on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution data, without incurring additional inference or memory costs.
54020e5fe48ebb250f27d744e20a63cac2988a84.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves first fine-tuning a large pre-trained model (such as CLIP, ALIGN, or ViT-G) multiple times using a diverse set of hyperparameter configurations, resulting in a collection of independently fine-tuned models. Instead of selecting the single best model based on validation accuracy, the method constructs a 'model soup' by averaging the weights of selected fine-tuned models. Several strategies for model selection and averaging are considered: (1) uniform averaging of all models (uniform soup), (2) a greedy selection process where models are added sequentially to the soup only if their inclusion improves validation accuracy (greedy soup), and (3) a learned soup where interpolation weights are optimized via gradient-based methods. The greedy soup is emphasized as the primary approach due to its effectiveness and computational feasibility for large models. No additional training is required after weight averaging, and inference is performed with a single model whose weights are the average of the selected fine-tuned models.
54020e5fe48ebb250f27d744e20a63cac2988a84.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a variety of large-scale image classification and natural language processing tasks. Primary models include CLIP (ViT-B/32), ALIGN (EfficientNet-L2), and ViT-G/14 pre-trained on JFT-3B, as well as transformer models like BERT and T5 for text classification. Fine-tuning is performed with random or grid hyperparameter sweeps over learning rate, weight decay, training epochs, data augmentation, mixup, and label smoothing, resulting in dozens of fine-tuned models per experiment. Evaluation is performed on standard datasets such as ImageNet (including validation, ReaL, and multilabel splits), five natural distribution shifts (ImageNet-V2, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-Sketch, ObjectNet, ImageNet-A), WILDS benchmarks, and GLUE tasks for NLP.
