Baselines include the best single model from the sweep, logit-level ensembles, and other weight averaging techniques. Metrics include top-1 accuracy, average accuracy across distribution shifts, and task-specific metrics for NLP. Validation sets are used for greedy soup construction, and statistical significance is assessed via permutation or McNemar's tests.
54020e5fe48ebb250f27d744e20a63cac2988a84.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a simple yet effective method for improving model accuracy and robustness by averaging the weights of independently fine-tuned models, termed 'model soups.' This approach achieves ensemble-like improvements without increasing inference or memory costs, and is shown to be effective across diverse architectures, datasets, and tasks. The greedy soup strategy is highlighted as a practical and superior alternative to uniform averaging or traditional model selection. Analytical and empirical results are provided to explain the conditions under which weight averaging is beneficial, relating performance gains to the geometry of the loss landscape and the diversity of fine-tuned solutions. The method is demonstrated to set new state-of-the-art results on challenging benchmarks, and is broadly applicable to both vision and language domains.

5406129d9d7d00dc310671c43597101b0ee93629.title: An Image is Worth One Word: Personalizing Text-to-Image Generation using Textual Inversion
5406129d9d7d00dc310671c43597101b0ee93629.research_question: How can language-guided generative models be adapted to enable personalized text-to-image generation for user-specified, unique concepts, allowing for intuitive composition, appearance modification, and application in novel scenes using only a few example images?
5406129d9d7d00dc310671c43597101b0ee93629.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that new, user-specific concepts can be effectively introduced into pre-trained text-to-image generative models by learning novel pseudo-word embeddings in the model's textual embedding space, enabling high-fidelity personalized generation and flexible compositionality without retraining or fine-tuning the entire model.
5406129d9d7d00dc310671c43597101b0ee93629.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces 'Textual Inversion,' a technique for learning new pseudo-word embeddings that represent user-provided concepts within the embedding space of a frozen, pre-trained text-to-image model. Given 3-5 images depicting the target concept, a placeholder token is assigned a new embedding vector, which is optimized to minimize a reconstruction loss using the Latent Diffusion Model (LDM) framework. The optimization process keeps the generative model and text encoder weights fixed, updating only the new embedding to ensure that prompts containing the pseudo-word (e.g., 'a photo of S*') reconstruct the concept images. This embedding can then be used compositionally in natural language prompts, enabling the generation of the concept in new scenes, styles, or contexts. The method leverages the original model's semantic and visual priors, preserving generalization and editability while capturing fine visual details unique to the concept.
5406129d9d7d00dc310671c43597101b0ee93629.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the publicly available 1.4 billion parameter Latent Diffusion Model (LDM), pre-trained on the LAION-400M dataset. For each target concept, 3-5 images will be collected and used to optimize a single pseudo-word embedding. The method will be compared against several baselines, including human-captioned prompts (both short and long), image-based prompting in DALLE-2, and alternative personalization approaches such as PALAVRA (CLIP-based) and CLIP-guided test-time optimization methods (VQGAN+CLIP, Guided Diffusion). Evaluation will be both qualitative and quantitative, assessing visual fidelity, faithfulness to the concept, compositional generalization, and editability. Additional applications such as style transfer, compositional synthesis, and bias reduction will be demonstrated. For each prompt, multiple generations will be produced, and the best results may be selected manually or via automated CLIP-based curation.
5406129d9d7d00dc310671c43597101b0ee93629.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the concept of personalized text-to-image generation via direct optimization of pseudo-word embeddings in a frozen model's textual embedding space, requiring only a few example images. This method enables the expansion of a model's vocabulary to include new, user-specific concepts without retraining or fine-tuning the generative model, preserving prior knowledge and generalization. The single-word embedding is shown to capture both high-level semantics and fine-grained visual details, supporting robust compositionality and editing. The approach is further distinguished by its ability to address bias reduction and style transfer, and by its analysis of the tradeoff between distortion and editability in the embedding space, situating the method at an optimal point on this tradeoff curve.

540781d7ce994b40f026df1480e0048d06b987c4.title: How Many Tokens Do 3D Point Cloud Transformer Architectures Really Need?
540781d7ce994b40f026df1480e0048d06b987c4.research_question: How can the computational and memory efficiency of 3D point cloud transformer architectures be improved by reducing the number of tokens processed, without significantly degrading performance across diverse 3D vision tasks?
540781d7ce994b40f026df1480e0048d06b987c4.hypothesis: A substantial proportion of tokens in 3D point cloud transformer models are redundant, and a domain-specific, spatially informed token merging strategy can aggressively reduce token count—by up to 90–95%—while maintaining or even improving task performance with minimal fine-tuning.
540781d7ce994b40f026df1480e0048d06b987c4.proposed_method: A novel globally informed graph-based token merging algorithm, specifically tailored for 3D point cloud transformers, will be developed. This method computes a global energy score for each token based on its alignment with partition centroids in a bipartite graph, where tokens and partition centroids are nodes and edges represent spatial relationships. Tokens with lower energy scores, indicating higher redundancy, are merged more aggressively, while high-energy tokens are preserved to retain critical information. The merging process is adaptive, with partition-level energy thresholds guiding the degree of token reduction, and includes an unmerging step to restore original resolution for dense prediction tasks. The method is integrated into each attention layer of 3D transformer backbones (e.g., PTv3, Sonata), supporting both off-the-shelf inference and efficient fine-tuning.
540781d7ce994b40f026df1480e0048d06b987c4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple 3D vision tasks, including semantic segmentation (ScanNet, ScanNet200, S3DIS, NuScenes), 3D object reconstruction (ShapeNet, Objaverse, GSO), and language-guided object detection (SpatialLM/Waymo). The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art token reduction techniques (ToMe, PiToMe, ALGM), as well as traditional point cloud downsampling methods (Random Drop, Farthest Point Sampling, VoxelGrid Downsampling). Evaluation metrics will include mIoU, mAcc, allAcc, PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, F1 scores, GFLOPs, peak memory usage, and inference latency. Both off-the-shelf and fine-tuned scenarios will be tested, with merging rates ranging from 50% up to 99% token reduction, and ablation studies will analyze the impact of merging criteria and energy thresholds.
540781d7ce994b40f026df1480e0048d06b987c4.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first systematic analysis of token redundancy in large-scale 3D point cloud transformers and demonstrates that aggressive token merging is feasible without significant performance loss. The method leverages a 3D-specific, globally informed energy score for adaptive token merging, outperforming generic token reduction and traditional downsampling techniques in both efficiency and accuracy. The approach enables up to 90–95% token reduction, drastically lowering computational and memory requirements, and supports seamless integration with existing transformer architectures and pre-trained models. This work paves the way for lightweight, scalable, and more efficient 3D transformer designs.

54155c2977a977bf129849455dcae3a2b79b3f41.title: Simple Hardware-Efficient Long Convolutions for Sequence Modeling
54155c2977a977bf129849455dcae3a2b79b3f41.research_question: Can simple, hardware-efficient long convolutional models match or surpass the performance and efficiency of state space models (SSMs) for long sequence modeling across diverse domains, and can their runtime be improved to scale to very long sequences on modern hardware?
54155c2977a977bf129849455dcae3a2b79b3f41.hypothesis: Directly parameterizing long convolution kernels with appropriate regularization and efficient hardware-aware algorithms will achieve performance comparable to or better than SSMs on long sequence modeling tasks, while improving robustness, simplicity, and runtime efficiency.
54155c2977a977bf129849455dcae3a2b79b3f41.proposed_method: A novel approach is proposed that replaces SSM layers in sequence models with directly learned long convolution kernels. To address quality gaps, two regularization strategies are introduced: the Squash operator, which enforces sparsity and smoothness in the frequency domain by shrinking kernel weights, and the Smooth operator, which applies average pooling to kernel weights to promote smoothness. Initialization schemes, including random and geometric decay, are explored for stability and performance. For runtime efficiency, an IO-aware algorithm called FlashButterfly is developed, which fuses FFT-based convolution into a single kernel and leverages Butterfly matrix decompositions to reduce GPU memory IO and exploit matrix multiply units. An extension is proposed where the Butterfly matrices are learned from data, increasing expressivity without additional runtime cost.
54155c2977a977bf129849455dcae3a2b79b3f41.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of sequence modeling tasks and benchmarks, including the Long Range Arena (LRA) benchmark (covering text, retrieval, image, and synthetic tasks), image classification (both 1D and 2D settings, such as sequential CIFAR and CIFAR-2D), language modeling (OpenWebText and the Pile datasets), and brain fMRI sequence modeling. Baselines will include state-of-the-art SSM models (e.g., S4 variants), Transformers, and other efficient sequence models. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy for classification tasks, perplexity (PPL) for language modeling, and mean absolute error (MAE) for brain data modeling. Runtime and scaling performance will be assessed using the LRA speed benchmark and extremely long sequence tasks (e.g., Path256 with sequence length 64K), comparing throughput and training time to SSM and FFT-based baselines.
54155c2977a977bf129849455dcae3a2b79b3f41.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a simple and robust alternative to SSMs by directly learning long convolution kernels with minimal hand-crafted initialization. The Squash and Smooth regularization techniques are claimed to close the quality gap with SSMs while improving robustness. FlashButterfly is presented as a novel, IO-aware, hardware-efficient algorithm that significantly accelerates long convolutions by leveraging Butterfly matrix decompositions and kernel fusion. The learned Butterfly extension increases the model's expressivity without increasing runtime, enabling the replacement of dense layers in Transformers and outperforming them with fewer parameters. The approach is claimed to achieve state-of-the-art results on challenging long sequence tasks, with substantial speedups and improved stability.

5437e8adab596d7294124c0e798708e050e25321.title: Least-to-Most Prompting Enables Complex Reasoning in Large Language Models
5437e8adab596d7294124c0e798708e050e25321.research_question: How can large language models be enabled to perform complex reasoning and generalize to problems that are more difficult than those demonstrated in their prompts, across tasks such as symbolic manipulation, compositional generalization, and mathematical reasoning?
5437e8adab596d7294124c0e798708e050e25321.hypothesis: A prompting strategy that decomposes complex problems into sequences of simpler subproblems and solves them incrementally will enable large language models to generalize to and solve problems of greater complexity than those seen in demonstration examples.
5437e8adab596d7294124c0e798708e050e25321.proposed_method: A novel prompting methodology, termed 'least-to-most prompting,' is proposed to enhance complex reasoning in large language models. This approach operates in two stages: first, a decomposition stage prompts the model to break down a complex problem into a sequence of simpler subproblems using few-shot exemplars; second, a subproblem solving stage sequentially prompts the model to solve each subproblem, leveraging the answers to previously solved subproblems as context. Both stages are implemented purely via prompting, without any model training or finetuning. The method can be adapted to merge both stages into a single-pass prompt for certain tasks, and can be combined with other prompting techniques such as chain-of-thought or self-consistency decoding. Prompts are carefully designed to illustrate both the decomposition process and the incremental solution-building, ensuring that the model learns to build upon prior intermediate results.
5437e8adab596d7294124c0e798708e050e25321.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on tasks spanning symbolic manipulation (e.g., last-letter-concatenation), compositional generalization (e.g., SCAN benchmark), and mathematical reasoning (e.g., GSM8K and DROP datasets). For each task, least-to-most prompting will be compared against standard few-shot prompting and chain-of-thought prompting, using large language models such as code-davinci-002 and text-davinci-002. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on held-out test sets, with particular attention to generalization to more complex or longer instances than those seen in demonstration prompts (e.g., longer word lists or action sequences). Prompts will be constructed to fit within model input size constraints, sometimes using intermediate representations (such as Python expressions) and post-processing to obtain final outputs. Error analysis will be performed to identify failure modes, especially for cases requiring multiple reasoning steps.
5437e8adab596d7294124c0e798708e050e25321.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new prompting paradigm that systematically decomposes complex problems into simpler subproblems, enabling large language models to generalize to and solve problems of greater complexity than those demonstrated in prompts. Unlike prior work, this method requires no model training, finetuning, or specialized neural-symbolic architectures, and achieves state-of-the-art results on benchmarks such as SCAN with only a handful of exemplars. The approach demonstrates significant improvements over standard and chain-of-thought prompting, particularly in easy-to-hard generalization scenarios, and is broadly applicable across diverse reasoning tasks.

5451cdb7f76a97d0f6f163067e08bf850eda9997.title: EControl: Fast Distributed Optimization with Compression and Error Control
5451cdb7f76a97d0f6f163067e08bf850eda9997.research_question: How can distributed optimization algorithms be designed to achieve fast convergence with communication compression in the presence of arbitrary data heterogeneity, without relying on strong assumptions or impractical requirements?
5451cdb7f76a97d0f6f163067e08bf850eda9997.hypothesis: A distributed optimization algorithm that regulates error compensation through controlled feedback strength can achieve provable fast convergence with contractive compressors under arbitrary data heterogeneity, matching lower bounds in both convex and nonconvex regimes, and providing linear parallel speedup without requiring large batch sizes or additional communication rounds.
5451cdb7f76a97d0f6f163067e08bf850eda9997.proposed_method: A new distributed optimization algorithm, EControl, is proposed to address communication bottlenecks in distributed training with heterogeneous data. EControl introduces a mechanism that fuses the error compensation and gradient estimator updates into a single compressed message, enabling error compensation for the gradient estimator itself. The algorithm incorporates a tunable parameter η to precisely control the strength of error compensation feedback, balancing the influence of the error term and the gradient estimator. The method operates in a client-server architecture, where each client computes a local stochastic gradient, updates its error and gradient estimator terms using contractive compression, and communicates compressed updates to the server. The server aggregates the updates and synchronizes the model parameters, ensuring efficient communication and robust convergence even with arbitrary data heterogeneity.
5451cdb7f76a97d0f6f163067e08bf850eda9997.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets to evaluate the efficacy of EControl. Synthetic least squares problems are used to systematically vary data heterogeneity, number of clients, and stochastic gradient noise, with performance compared to Compressed-SGD and classic Error Compensation (EC) methods. Real-world experiments include logistic regression on the MNIST dataset and deep learning models (ResNet18, VGG13) on CIFAR-10, using Top-K contractive compression and varying the number of clients and compression ratios. Baselines include EF21, EF21-SGDM, EC, and SGD, with evaluation metrics such as convergence rate, training loss, test accuracy, and communication cost (bits sent). Hyperparameters, including stepsizes and η, are fine-tuned for each method, and experiments measure both convergence speed and robustness to data heterogeneity.
5451cdb7f76a97d0f6f163067e08bf850eda9997.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to provide provable fast convergence for distributed optimization with arbitrary contractive compressors and arbitrary data heterogeneity, without requiring strong assumptions such as bounded gradients, bounded heterogeneity, or large batch sizes. EControl achieves linear parallel speedup and matches known lower bounds in both convex and nonconvex regimes, while being practical and easily integrable into existing error compensation frameworks. The introduction of a tunable feedback parameter η enables stable and robust convergence, overcoming instability and inefficiency present in previous methods.

546d0624adfc6e18fb87d8cc77e7705bb9ea7445.title: LIMA: Less Is More for Alignment
546d0624adfc6e18fb87d8cc77e7705bb9ea7445.research_question: How much instruction tuning data is necessary to effectively align large pretrained language models to follow user instructions and produce high-quality, helpful responses? What is the relative importance of pretraining versus alignment data in achieving strong performance on diverse user prompts?
546d0624adfc6e18fb87d8cc77e7705bb9ea7445.hypothesis: The majority of a large language model's knowledge and capabilities are acquired during pretraining, and only a small, high-quality, and diverse set of instruction tuning examples is necessary to effectively align the model to user preferences and response formats.
546d0624adfc6e18fb87d8cc77e7705bb9ea7445.proposed_method: A large pretrained language model (LLaMA 65B) will be fine-tuned using a carefully curated dataset of 1,000 prompt-response pairs. The dataset will be constructed to maximize diversity and quality, drawing from community Q&A forums (StackExchange, wikiHow, Reddit) and manually authored examples, all formatted in the style of a helpful AI assistant. Fine-tuning will use supervised learning with standard hyperparameters, including AdamW optimizer, a learning rate schedule, and residual dropout. Special tokens will be introduced to differentiate between user and assistant turns. The effect of adding a small number of multi-turn dialogue examples will also be explored to enhance conversational ability.
546d0624adfc6e18fb87d8cc77e7705bb9ea7445.experiment_details: Experiments will involve evaluating the fine-tuned model on a held-out test set of 300 diverse prompts and comparing its responses to those of several strong baselines, including Alpaca 65B (trained on 52,000 examples), OpenAI's DaVinci003 (RLHF-tuned), Google's Bard, Anthropic's Claude, and OpenAI's GPT-4. Human preference studies will be conducted by presenting annotators with pairs of responses (one from the proposed model, one from a baseline) and recording preferences. Additional evaluation will be performed using GPT-4 as an annotator. Metrics will include preference rates, absolute quality ratings, and safety assessments on sensitive prompts. Ablation studies will systematically vary training data diversity, quality, and quantity (using 7B models) to assess their effects on alignment and generation quality.
546d0624adfc6e18fb87d8cc77e7705bb9ea7445.novelty_claims: The proposed approach demonstrates that fine-tuning a large pretrained language model on a small, high-quality, and diverse set of instruction-following examples is sufficient to achieve competitive performance with models trained on orders of magnitude more data and with reinforcement learning from human feedback. The work provides evidence for the 'Superficial Alignment Hypothesis,' showing that alignment primarily teaches format and style rather than knowledge or capability. Ablation studies highlight the critical roles of data diversity and quality over sheer quantity for effective alignment. The method also shows that conversational abilities can be significantly improved with only a handful of multi-turn dialogue examples.

54814744b42b06c855c97b23de1366e0bcbe775a.title: The Dawn of LMMs: Preliminary Explorations with GPT-4V(ision)
54814744b42b06c855c97b23de1366e0bcbe775a.research_question: What are the capabilities, input modalities, and effective prompting strategies for large multimodal models (LMMs) based on state-of-the-art large language models, and how can these models be evaluated and leveraged for a broad range of vision-language tasks and emerging applications?
54814744b42b06c855c97b23de1366e0bcbe775a.hypothesis: Integrating vision capabilities into large language models will enable the resulting large multimodal models to demonstrate unprecedented generality and performance across a wide spectrum of multimodal tasks, including novel forms of human-computer interaction and reasoning.
54814744b42b06c855c97b23de1366e0bcbe775a.proposed_method: A comprehensive exploration will be conducted on a state-of-the-art large multimodal model with vision capabilities, using a curated set of qualitative examples spanning diverse domains and tasks. The investigation will systematically probe the model’s input modalities (text-only, single image-text pair, and interleaved image-text sequences), working modes (zero-shot, in-context few-shot, instruction following), and prompting techniques (including visual referring prompting via pixel-space edits such as visual pointers and scene text). Special attention will be given to the design of input samples to avoid overlap with the model’s training data, ensuring the assessment of true generalization and reasoning abilities. The study will also explore the model’s performance on tasks such as open-world visual understanding, dense captioning, document reasoning, temporal and video understanding, abstract visual reasoning, emotion recognition, and application-driven scenarios.
54814744b42b06c855c97b23de1366e0bcbe775a.experiment_details: Experiments will primarily utilize a collection of original, carefully designed qualitative samples that are not present in the model’s training data, with a focus on zero-shot instruction-based prompting to minimize information leakage. The evaluation will cover a broad range of domains, including but not limited to image description, object localization, scene text understanding, document reasoning, coding with vision, temporal reasoning, and emotional intelligence tasks. While quantitative benchmarking will be limited due to potential overlap with training data and the lack of suitable next-generation benchmarks, the study will emphasize qualitative analysis and the discovery of emergent capabilities. Comparisons will be made against the expected outputs for each task, and the effectiveness of various prompting strategies will be assessed.
54814744b42b06c855c97b23de1366e0bcbe775a.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a systematic qualitative exploration of a state-of-the-art large multimodal model’s capabilities, highlighting the unprecedented generality and flexibility enabled by integrating vision with language. The study proposes and demonstrates novel prompting techniques, such as visual referring prompting, that leverage pixel-space edits for more nuanced human-computer interaction. The work aims to inspire the development of new evaluation benchmarks and task formulations for next-generation multimodal models, and to identify promising directions for future research and application scenarios.

54a02694bea2ed416d7620c3fd80c87eb626a0c4.title: Spectral Representation for Causal Estimation with Hidden Confounders
54a02694bea2ed416d7620c3fd80c87eb626a0c4.research_question: How can causal effect estimation be improved in the presence of unobserved confounders, particularly in instrumental variable (IV) regression with additional observed confounders and in proxy causal learning (PCL), using modern representation learning and optimization techniques?
54a02694bea2ed416d7620c3fd80c87eb626a0c4.hypothesis: A spectral representation framework, leveraging a low-rank assumption on conditional densities and combined with a saddle-point optimization approach, will enable more accurate and efficient causal effect estimation in settings with hidden confounders, outperforming existing methods in both IV regression (with and without observed confounders) and PCL.
54a02694bea2ed416d7620c3fd80c87eb626a0c4.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that constructs spectral representations of conditional expectation operators using singular value decomposition (SVD) under a low-rank assumption. This framework will be integrated into a saddle-point optimization formulation, enabling unbiased estimation of causal effects while avoiding double-sampling bias. The method will employ contrastive learning objectives to learn feature maps (representations) for treatments, instruments, and confounders, using neural networks trained via stochastic gradient descent. The learned representations will define explicit, finite-dimensional function classes for both the primal (causal effect) and dual (test function) variables, ensuring tractability and realizability. The approach will be extended to IV regression with observed confounders and to PCL by characterizing and learning appropriate spectral representations for these more complex conditional structures.
54a02694bea2ed416d7620c3fd80c87eb626a0c4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on benchmark datasets including dSprites (for both low- and high-dimensional IV and PCL settings) and the Demand Design dataset (for IV with observed confounders). The evaluation will use out-of-sample mean squared error (OOS MSE) as the primary metric. Baseline methods will include kernel-based IV regression (KIV), dual embedding (DE), deep neural network-based approaches (DFIV, DeepGMM), and recent PCL algorithms (DFPV, KPV, PMMR, CEVAE). The proposed method will be compared against these baselines across varying data dimensionalities and sample sizes, with careful control of representation learning and optimization phases. Experimental setup will include both fixed and learned feature representations, and runtime will also be reported to assess computational efficiency.
54a02694bea2ed416d7620c3fd80c87eb626a0c4.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a spectral representation framework for causal estimation that explicitly learns both the primal and dual function classes under a low-rank conditional density assumption, enabling efficient saddle-point optimization. Unlike prior methods, the framework provides adaptive, data-driven representations for IV regression with observed confounders and for PCL, rather than relying on fixed or augmented feature spaces. The method avoids double-sampling bias and is compatible with modern neural network architectures and large-scale datasets. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior estimation accuracy and computational efficiency compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

54caf5927a6d656bb84d2a16e16fa2b0c5d6f522.title: CogACT: A Foundational Vision-Language-Action Model for Synergizing Cognition and Action in Robotic Manipulation
54caf5927a6d656bb84d2a16e16fa2b0c5d6f522.research_question: How can a foundational vision-language-action (VLA) model be designed to synergize cognitive reasoning from vision-language models with high-precision, temporally correlated action prediction for robotic manipulation, enabling robust generalization and adaptation across diverse robots, tasks, and environments?
54caf5927a6d656bb84d2a16e16fa2b0c5d6f522.hypothesis: A componentized VLA architecture that decouples cognition (vision-language understanding) from action prediction, utilizing a large pretrained vision-language model for cognitive reasoning and a dedicated, diffusion-based transformer action module, will significantly improve task success rates, generalization to unseen objects and backgrounds, and adaptability to new robots compared to existing VLA models that directly repurpose VLMs for action prediction.
54caf5927a6d656bb84d2a16e16fa2b0c5d6f522.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a modular VLA model architecture consisting of three main components: a vision module, a language module, and a diffusion-based transformer action module. The vision module encodes raw images into perceptual tokens using powerful vision transformers (DINOv2 and SigLIP), while the language module (based on LLAMA-2) integrates these visual tokens with language instructions to produce a cognition feature. This cognition feature serves as a condition for the action module, which employs a diffusion transformer (DiT) to generate a sequence of continuous, multi-modal, and temporally correlated robot actions. The action module is trained to predict both current and multiple future actions, enhancing trajectory smoothness and task success. An adaptive action ensemble algorithm is incorporated during inference, which fuses past and current action predictions based on their similarity, further improving execution robustness and performance.
54caf5927a6d656bb84d2a16e16fa2b0c5d6f522.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Open X-Embodiment (OXE) dataset for large-scale pretraining, comprising over 1 million real-world robotic trajectories from 22 robot embodiments. Evaluation will occur in both simulation (using the SIMPLER benchmark, which closely replicates real-world robot environments for Google and WidowX robots) and real-world settings (with Realman and Franka robots). Tasks will include object picking, stacking, and placing, with both seen and unseen objects, backgrounds, and distractors. Baseline comparisons will include RT-1, RT-1-X, RT-2-X, Octo, and OpenVLA models, with all models trained or fine-tuned on similar data. Evaluation metrics will primarily be task success rates, measured across multiple trials per task and robot. Ablation studies will assess the impact of action module architecture, model scaling, multi-step prediction, and the adaptive ensemble strategy.
54caf5927a6d656bb84d2a16e16fa2b0c5d6f522.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a componentized VLA model that explicitly separates cognitive reasoning and action prediction, leveraging a large pretrained VLM for cognition and a scalable diffusion transformer for action modeling. Unlike prior works that directly quantize or regress actions from VLM outputs, this method employs a dedicated, large-scale diffusion-based action module conditioned on cognition features, resulting in superior action precision and temporal coherence. The adaptive action ensemble algorithm further enhances robustness by adaptively fusing action predictions based on similarity. The approach demonstrates favorable scaling behavior of the action module, with significant performance gains from modest parameter increases, and achieves state-of-the-art results in both simulated and real-world robotic manipulation benchmarks, exhibiting strong generalization and rapid adaptation to new robots and tasks.

54e08a49aa16e37c8f4b1a83a3c476397585e924.title: A Simple Approach to Unifying Diffusion-based Conditional Generation
54e08a49aa16e37c8f4b1a83a3c476397585e924.research_question: How can a unified, efficient diffusion-based framework be developed to flexibly support diverse conditional image generation tasks involving correlated image-condition pairs, such as controllable generation, estimation, and joint generation, without the complexity and inefficiency of existing specialized or unified approaches?
54e08a49aa16e37c8f4b1a83a3c476397585e924.hypothesis: A diffusion model that learns a joint distribution over correlated image-condition pairs, with a flexible architecture and disentangled noise-level training, will enable efficient, high-quality, and versatile conditional generation, estimation, and joint generation across multiple modalities, matching or surpassing specialized and prior unified methods while requiring fewer parameters and simpler training.
54e08a49aa16e37c8f4b1a83a3c476397585e924.proposed_method: A unified conditional diffusion model, UniCon, will be developed by adapting a large-scale pretrained diffusion model (such as Stable Diffusion) to jointly model the distribution of correlated image pairs (e.g., image-depth, image-edge, image-pose, or loosely correlated pairs like identity). The architecture will process image and condition inputs in parallel branches, linked by joint cross-attention modules that enable feature exchange between branches. Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) adapters will be used to fine-tune only a small subset of parameters, maintaining efficiency and compatibility with various base model checkpoints. Training will employ a disentangled noise-level objective, where independent noise schedules are applied to the image and condition branches, allowing the model to learn flexible conditional sampling strategies. This setup will support a wide range of inference behaviors, including controllable generation, estimation, joint generation, and coarse or partial conditioning, by varying the noise and masking schedules during sampling.
54e08a49aa16e37c8f4b1a83a3c476397585e924.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Stable Diffusion v1.5 model as the base, with UniCon models trained for different modalities: depth, soft edge, human pose, and human identity. Training datasets will include 16k images from Pascal VOC for depth and edge, 9k images for pose, 30k face images from CelebA for identity, and additional appearance models trained on 6k video frames from Panda70M. Baselines for comparison will include specialized models such as ControlNet (for depth-to-image), Marigold (for image-to-depth), LooseControl, Readout-Guidance, LDM3D, and unified models like JointNet. Evaluation metrics will include Frechet Inception Distance (FID) for image quality, Absolute Mean Relative Error (AbsRel) for depth fidelity, Edge Mean Squared Error (EMSE) for edge fidelity, and Percentage of Correct Keypoints (PCK) for pose. Depth estimation will be evaluated on NYUv2 and ScanNet benchmarks. Both quantitative metrics and user studies will be used to assess performance, and ablation studies will examine the effects of training steps, data scale, and architectural variants.
54e08a49aa16e37c8f4b1a83a3c476397585e924.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified diffusion framework that supports diverse conditional generation tasks within a single model, requiring only a single, efficient training stage and minimal additional parameters (approximately 15% of the base model). The joint cross-attention mechanism enables effective modeling of both spatially aligned and loosely correlated image pairs, surpassing the flexibility of prior unified models. The disentangled noise-level training paradigm allows for flexible conditional sampling without explicit masks or architectural complexity. The method demonstrates state-of-the-art or comparable performance to specialized methods and outperforms previous unified approaches in both efficiency and versatility. Additionally, the framework naturally supports multi-signal conditioning and seamless integration with various pretrained diffusion model checkpoints.

54f107c7cdffc43490ba18e3e4313a8b4dff4950.title: MimicGen: A Data Generation System for Scalable Robot Learning using Human Demonstrations
54f107c7cdffc43490ba18e3e4313a8b4dff4950.research_question: How can scalable and diverse datasets for robot imitation learning be generated from a small number of human demonstrations, in order to improve robot learning performance across a wide range of manipulation tasks, scene configurations, object instances, and robot hardware?
54f107c7cdffc43490ba18e3e4313a8b4dff4950.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a data generation system which adapts and reuses segments of a small set of human demonstrations to novel contexts can synthesize large, diverse, and high-quality datasets that enable effective imitation learning for robots, achieving performance comparable to or exceeding that obtained from collecting additional human demonstrations.
54f107c7cdffc43490ba18e3e4313a8b4dff4950.proposed_method: A data generation system will be developed that parses a small set of human teleoperated robot demonstrations into object-centric segments, each corresponding to a subtask within a manipulation task. For a new scene or task variant, the system will generate new demonstrations by selecting reference segments from the source dataset, transforming these segments according to the current object poses in the new context using pose transformations, and stitching them together to form a complete trajectory. The robot will execute the transformed trajectory, and only successful executions will be retained in the generated dataset. The approach is designed to be agnostic to scene configuration, object instance, and robot hardware, relying only on object and controller frames and assuming access to object pose information at the start of each subtask during data generation.
54f107c7cdffc43490ba18e3e4313a8b4dff4950.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across 18 diverse robot manipulation tasks, including pick-and-place, assembly, contact-rich interactions, and mobile manipulation, using both simulation environments (robosuite/MuJoCo and Factory/Isaac Gym) and real robot arms. For each task, a small source dataset (typically 10 human demonstrations) will be collected, and the system will be used to generate 1000 demonstrations per task variant, discarding failed attempts. Policies will be trained using Behavioral Cloning with RNNs on the generated datasets and evaluated using success rates across multiple random seeds, with both image-based and low-dimensional observations. Baselines will include policies trained on the original human demonstrations as well as on additional human-collected data, enabling direct comparison of the effectiveness of generated versus real demonstrations. Evaluation will also include generalization to novel objects, robot arms, and broader initial state distributions.
54f107c7cdffc43490ba18e3e4313a8b4dff4950.novelty_claims: The proposed system introduces a general-purpose, scalable data generation pipeline that can synthesize large and diverse imitation learning datasets from a minimal number of human demonstrations by adapting demonstration segments to new contexts. The approach is broadly applicable across tasks, objects, and robot hardware, and can generate data for unseen scene configurations and object instances. Experimental results are expected to show that agents trained on generated data achieve strong performance, often comparable to or exceeding that of agents trained on equivalent amounts of additional human demonstrations, thus offering a more economical and efficient alternative for scaling robot learning.

54fb839f621e3fe787437ab8ca5f37e7e4726bfe.title: Qwen2 Technical Report
54fb839f621e3fe787437ab8ca5f37e7e4726bfe.research_question: How can large language models be designed, trained, and aligned to achieve state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of language understanding, generation, coding, mathematics, reasoning, and multilingual tasks, while maintaining efficiency and scalability for deployment on diverse hardware platforms?
54fb839f621e3fe787437ab8ca5f37e7e4726bfe.hypothesis: Enhancing the quality and diversity of pre-training data, refining model architectures with advanced attention mechanisms and expert routing, and employing scalable alignment techniques with minimal human supervision will yield large language models that surpass existing open-weight and proprietary models in language understanding, reasoning, coding, and multilingual capabilities.
54fb839f621e3fe787437ab8ca5f37e7e4726bfe.proposed_method: A new series of large language models will be developed, based on the Transformer architecture, incorporating both dense and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) variants. The models will utilize Grouped Query Attention (GQA) to optimize inference throughput and Dual Chunk Attention (DCA) with YARN for efficient long-context processing. Pre-training will be conducted on a high-quality, multilingual dataset of over 7 trillion tokens, with extensive filtering and synthesis to enhance code, mathematics, and linguistic diversity. Post-training will involve supervised fine-tuning on a curated instruction-following dataset and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) using Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and online reward modeling, leveraging both collaborative data annotation and automated data synthesis to minimize manual labeling while maximizing data quality.
54fb839f621e3fe787437ab8ca5f37e7e4726bfe.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate models of various sizes (0.5B, 1.5B, 7B, 57B-A14B MoE, and 72B parameters) on a comprehensive suite of benchmarks. Datasets include MMLU, MMLU-Pro, GPQA, TheoremQA, BBH, HellaSwag, Winogrande, ARC-C, TruthfulQA, HumanEval, MBPP, EvalPlus, MultiPL-E, GSM8K, MATH, C-Eval, CMMLU, and a variety of multilingual benchmarks (M3Exam, IndoMMLU, ruMMLU, translated MMLU, BELEBELE, XCOPA, XWinograd, XStoryCloze, PAWS-X, MGSM, Flores-101). Baseline comparisons will be made against leading open-weight (e.g., Llama-3, Mixtral, Yi-1.5) and proprietary models. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, pass rates, and human preference scores, with both few-shot and zero-shot prompting protocols. Long-context and multilingual capabilities will be specifically assessed, and safety, responsibility, and contamination analyses will be conducted.
54fb839f621e3fe787437ab8ca5f37e7e4726bfe.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a suite of large language models with open weights, spanning a wide parameter range and including both dense and fine-grained Mixture-of-Experts architectures. Key innovations include the integration of Grouped Query Attention and Dual Chunk Attention with YARN for efficient long-context processing, a highly refined and diverse pre-training dataset, and scalable alignment strategies that minimize human annotation. The models are designed for robust multilingual proficiency (covering approximately 30 languages), efficient deployment across hardware platforms, and superior performance in coding and mathematics. Open release of model weights and training resources is intended to foster community innovation and accessibility.

550006bea81e4ccb67743dd1b82a70b86b48d93a.title: RL-VLM-F: Reinforcement Learning from Vision Language Foundation Model Feedback
550006bea81e4ccb67743dd1b82a70b86b48d93a.research_question: How can reinforcement learning agents be trained to perform a wide range of tasks using automatically generated reward functions, relying solely on a text description of the task goal and the agent's visual observations, without requiring human-crafted reward engineering or access to environment code?
550006bea81e4ccb67743dd1b82a70b86b48d93a.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging vision-language foundation models (VLMs) to generate preference-based feedback over pairs of agent visual observations, conditioned on a natural language task description, enables the automatic learning of effective reward functions, which in turn can be used to train RL agents to solve diverse tasks without human supervision.
550006bea81e4ccb67743dd1b82a70b86b48d93a.proposed_method: A novel framework, RL-VLM-F, is proposed to automate reward function generation for reinforcement learning agents. The method requires only a natural language description of the task goal and visual observations from the agent. The core approach involves sampling pairs of agent-generated images during policy rollouts and querying a vision-language foundation model (such as Gemini or GPT-4V) to provide preference labels indicating which image better achieves the task goal. A two-stage prompting strategy is employed: first, the VLM is asked to analyze and compare the images in the context of the task, and second, it is prompted to output a discrete preference label. These preference labels are then used to train a parameterized reward function via preference-based learning (using the Bradley-Terry model and a cross-entropy loss). The learned reward function is iteratively updated and used to optimize the RL policy, alternating between policy improvement and reward model updates.
550006bea81e4ccb67743dd1b82a70b86b48d93a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on seven tasks spanning classic control (CartPole), rigid and articulated object manipulation (MetaWorld: Open Drawer, Soccer, Sweep Into), and deformable object manipulation (SoftGym: Fold Cloth, Straighten Rope, Pass Water). The evaluation metrics include task-specific success rates (for MetaWorld) and episode returns (for other tasks). Baselines for comparison include direct VLM reward scoring, CLIP/BLIP-2 similarity-based rewards, RoboCLIP (text version), and ground-truth preference-based reward learning. All methods are trained with identical RL algorithms and hyperparameters, differing only in the reward function. The VLMs used are Gemini-Pro and GPT-4V, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of the prompting strategy and the accuracy of VLM-generated preference labels. The learned rewards' alignment with ground-truth task progress will also be analyzed.
550006bea81e4ccb67743dd1b82a70b86b48d93a.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a fully automated system for reward function generation that eliminates the need for manual reward engineering or human preference labeling, relying solely on task descriptions and visual observations. Unlike prior approaches, it does not require access to environment code or ground-truth state information, and it is applicable to high-dimensional, visually complex tasks, including deformable object manipulation. The use of VLMs for preference-based feedback, rather than direct reward scoring, is claimed to yield more consistent and effective reward signals. Extensive experiments demonstrate superior performance over existing methods that use large pretrained models for reward generation under similar assumptions.

550c4b70821f800cb043471d6c643df7d2a24d71.title: IRBridge: Solving Image Restoration Bridge with Pre-trained Generative Diffusion Models
550c4b70821f800cb043471d6c643df7d2a24d71.research_question: How can pre-trained generative diffusion models be effectively leveraged to improve the flexibility, efficiency, and generalization of image restoration across diverse degradation types, without requiring task-specific bridge models to be trained from scratch?
550c4b70821f800cb043471d6c643df7d2a24d71.hypothesis: A transition equation can be formulated to bridge the state distributions of image restoration diffusion processes and pre-trained generative diffusion models, enabling direct integration of generative priors into restoration bridges. This integration will enhance restoration performance, robustness, and generalization, while reducing the need for retraining for each degradation type.
550c4b70821f800cb043471d6c643df7d2a24d71.proposed_method: A novel transition equation is introduced to connect two independent diffusion processes—one for image restoration (starting from a degraded image) and one for image generation (starting from noise)—that share the same endpoint distribution of high-quality images. This equation enables state transitions between the restoration bridge and the generative model at any timestep, using a reparameterization that combines the states, known offsets, and noise terms. The IRBridge framework is then constructed, which applies a forward transition to map the restoration bridge state to the generative model's trajectory, allowing the pre-trained generative model to estimate the initial clean image. A reverse transition then maps this estimate back to the restoration bridge, enabling iterative restoration. The method supports flexible, task-specific hyperparameter selection for inference, and can incorporate conditional guidance (e.g., via ControlNet) to anchor the restoration process to the degraded input.
550c4b70821f800cb043471d6c643df7d2a24d71.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on six mainstream image restoration tasks: deraining, dehazing, desnowing, raindrop removal, low-light enhancement, and image inpainting. Stable Diffusion v1-5 is used as the pre-trained generative model, while IR-SDE and GOUB serve as the restoration bridges. ControlNet is employed to provide conditional guidance based on degraded images. The evaluation uses metrics including PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and FID, with results computed on the Y channel in the YCbCr color space and using label images decoded by the same VAE as the generative model. Baselines include both regression-based methods (e.g., WGWS-Net) and state-of-the-art bridge models (e.g., ResShift, IR-SDE, GOUB, RDDM, DiffUIR), as well as generative diffusion prior methods (e.g., GDP, TAO). Experiments are performed at 512x512 resolution, and both quantitative and qualitative comparisons are provided, including generalization tests on unseen domains and real-world degradations.
550c4b70821f800cb043471d6c643df7d2a24d71.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a transition equation that enables seamless bridging between restoration and generative diffusion processes with shared endpoints, allowing direct use of pre-trained generative priors in image restoration without retraining for each degradation. The IRBridge framework eliminates the need for task-specific bridge model training, reduces computational costs, and enhances flexibility by allowing inference-time hyperparameter customization. Extensive experiments demonstrate improved robustness, generalization, and overall restoration quality compared to both regression-based and bridge models trained from scratch, as well as methods using standard generative diffusion paradigms. The approach is the first to systematically integrate pre-trained generative diffusion models into restoration bridges via a principled transition mechanism.

553b25f1e371ae6bd7126af54206444043ee7da3.title: AnomalyCLIP: Object-agnostic Prompt Learning for Zero-shot Anomaly Detection
553b25f1e371ae6bd7126af54206444043ee7da3.research_question: How can zero-shot anomaly detection be improved to generalize across diverse domains and object types, especially when no training data from the target domain is available?
553b25f1e371ae6bd7126af54206444043ee7da3.hypothesis: Learning object-agnostic text prompts that capture generic normality and abnormality, rather than object semantics, enables more effective and generalized zero-shot anomaly detection across diverse domains.
553b25f1e371ae6bd7126af54206444043ee7da3.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that adapts large pre-trained vision-language models (such as CLIP) for zero-shot anomaly detection by learning object-agnostic text prompts. These prompts are designed to represent generic normality and abnormality, intentionally excluding object-specific semantics. The method introduces a glocal context optimization strategy, combining global and local loss functions, to jointly optimize the prompt embeddings using auxiliary datasets with anomaly annotations. The approach further refines the textual space via learnable token embeddings in the text encoder and enhances local visual feature alignment by employing a Diagonally Prominent Attention Map (DPAM) mechanism in the visual encoder. During inference, the model computes anomaly scores at both image and pixel levels by measuring the similarity between the learned text prompt embeddings and the visual embeddings from the target images.
553b25f1e371ae6bd7126af54206444043ee7da3.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on 17 publicly available datasets spanning industrial inspection and medical imaging domains, including MVTecAD, VisA, MPDD, BTAD, SDD, DAGM, DTD-Synthetic, ISIC, CVC-ClinicDB, CVC-ColonDB, Kvasir, Endo, TN3k, HeadCT, BrainMRI, Br35H, and COVID-19. The evaluation metrics include AUROC, average precision (AP) for image-level detection, and AUPRO for pixel-level segmentation. The proposed method is compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as CLIP, CLIP-AC, WinCLIP, VAND, and CoOp. Auxiliary datasets are used for prompt learning, and the model is evaluated in a zero-shot setting on unseen target datasets. Ablation studies are performed to assess the contributions of object-agnostic prompts, glocal context optimization, and DPAM strategies.
553b25f1e371ae6bd7126af54206444043ee7da3.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the concept of object-agnostic prompt learning for anomaly detection, enabling the model to focus on generic abnormality and normality rather than object semantics. The glocal context optimization jointly leverages global and local anomaly semantics for robust prompt learning. The DPAM mechanism refines local visual features for improved segmentation without additional decoder networks. The approach achieves superior zero-shot anomaly detection and segmentation performance across highly diverse domains, requiring only two learnable prompts and a single forward pass, and demonstrates strong generalization to both industrial and medical datasets.

5549dc3ceff07561d9fb59610c0f78c71617901a.title: Generative Diffusion Prior for Unified Image Restoration and Enhancement
5549dc3ceff07561d9fb59610c0f78c71617901a.research_question: How can a unified, unsupervised framework be developed to address a wide range of image restoration and enhancement tasks—including linear, non-linear, and blind inverse problems—without requiring task-specific retraining or knowledge of degradation models?
5549dc3ceff07561d9fb59610c0f78c71617901a.hypothesis: A generative diffusion model, when equipped with systematic conditional guidance and degradation parameter optimization, can serve as a universal prior to enable high-fidelity, unsupervised image restoration and enhancement across diverse tasks and arbitrary image sizes.
5549dc3ceff07561d9fb59610c0f78c71617901a.proposed_method: The proposed methodology leverages a pre-trained denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) as a generative prior for unified image restoration and enhancement. The approach introduces a protocol for conditional guidance, where the corrupted image is used to guide the reverse diffusion process, either by adding guidance at each timestep (GDP-xt) or by conditioning on the predicted clean image at each step (GDP-x0). For blind restoration tasks, the degradation model parameters are randomly initialized and optimized during the denoising process via gradient descent, allowing simultaneous estimation of both the clean image and unknown degradation. Hierarchical guidance and a patch-based generation strategy are incorporated to enable restoration of images at arbitrary resolutions. The framework also supports multi-image guidance for tasks such as HDR recovery, where multiple degraded inputs are used to guide the restoration process.
5549dc3ceff07561d9fb59610c0f78c71617901a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of image restoration and enhancement tasks, including super-resolution, deblurring, inpainting, colorization, low-light enhancement, and HDR recovery. Datasets such as ImageNet, LSUN, CelebA, LOL, VE-LOL-L, LoLi-phone, and the NTIRE HDR dataset will be used to evaluate performance. Baselines for comparison include state-of-the-art unsupervised and zero-shot methods such as RED, DGP, SNIPS, DDRM, EnlightenGAN, Zero-DCE, and others. Evaluation metrics will include PSNR, SSIM, FID, Consistency, Lightness Order Error (LOE), Perceptual Index (PI), and LPIPS. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of guidance protocols, variance removal, optimizable degradation, and patch-based tactics. The setup will also examine the generalization ability of the method to out-of-distribution images and arbitrary image sizes.
5549dc3ceff07561d9fb59610c0f78c71617901a.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to enable unified, unsupervised image restoration and enhancement across both linear and non-linear, as well as blind, inverse problems using a single unconditional DDPM pre-trained on large-scale natural images. The method introduces a practical and effective conditional guidance protocol, supports simultaneous optimization of unknown degradation models, and enables restoration of images with arbitrary resolutions via hierarchical and patch-based strategies. The approach generalizes well to images and tasks outside the training distribution and demonstrates superior or competitive performance compared to existing unsupervised and zero-shot baselines.

55791d92a0eb9de2ec97a91b7f0d662b42b8e2b4.title: Reasoning Limitations of Multimodal Large Language Models. A case study of Bongard Problems
55791d92a0eb9de2ec97a91b7f0d662b42b8e2b4.research_question: Can current multimodal large language models (MLLMs) effectively solve abstract visual reasoning tasks, such as Bongard Problems, across both synthetic and real-world domains, and what are the underlying limitations in their reasoning abilities?
55791d92a0eb9de2ec97a91b7f0d662b42b8e2b4.hypothesis: MLLMs exhibit significant limitations in abstract visual reasoning, particularly when required to generalize concepts from synthetic to real-world domains, and their performance is constrained by their ability to form and articulate abstract concepts rather than by domain specificity.
55791d92a0eb9de2ec97a91b7f0d662b42b8e2b4.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation framework will be developed to assess the abstract visual reasoning capabilities of MLLMs using Bongard Problems (BPs) as a testbed. The methodology will involve designing a diverse set of solution strategies tailored to MLLMs, including both open-ended language generation and binary classification tasks. Multiple prompting strategies will be implemented, such as Direct (whole-matrix input), Descriptive (panel-wise captioning), and Contrastive (pairwise comparison), along with their iterative and direct variants to probe reasoning and context utilization. A new dataset, Bongard-RWR, will be constructed to represent abstract BP concepts from synthetic problems using real-world images, enabling direct comparison of model performance across domains. Automated and model-based evaluation protocols will be established to assess both the correctness and semantic similarity of generated answers.
55791d92a0eb9de2ec97a91b7f0d662b42b8e2b4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three BP datasets: classic synthetic Bongard Problems, Bongard HOI (human-object interactions), and Bongard-OpenWorld (open-world concepts), as well as the newly introduced Bongard-RWR dataset. Eight MLLMs will be evaluated, including four proprietary (GPT-4o, GPT-4 Turbo, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Claude 3.5 Sonnet) and four open-access models (InternVL2-8B, LLaVA-1.6-7B, Phi-3.5-Vision, Pixtral 12B). Evaluation will span three binary classification tasks (Ground-Truth, Incorrect Label, Images to Sides) and seven prompting strategies for language generation. Datasets will be balanced and capped at 100 instances per set (except Bongard-RWR with 60). Performance will be measured using accuracy, number of correctly solved problems, and model-based ensemble voting for open-ended tasks. Additional dataset variants (e.g., greyscale, square-cropped) will be used to test robustness. Human performance will be collected for comparison, and results will be analyzed to identify failure modes and the impact of context, image modality, and model scaling.
55791d92a0eb9de2ec97a91b7f0d662b42b8e2b4.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a systematic, multimodal evaluation framework for abstract visual reasoning in MLLMs, leveraging a diverse set of solution strategies and prompting methods. It proposes the creation of Bongard-RWR, a novel dataset that bridges synthetic and real-world domains for direct concept comparison. The approach uniquely combines automated, model-based answer evaluation with human baseline studies, and provides detailed analysis of reasoning limitations, context utilization, and cross-domain generalization in MLLMs. The work aims to reveal fundamental gaps in current MLLMs' reasoning abilities and inform future model and benchmark development.

557dce8787129ca623fcb2cca2e76e9920347b69.title: Optimal and Differentially Private Data Acquisition: Central and Local Mechanisms
557dce8787129ca623fcb2cca2e76e9920347b69.research_question: How can a platform optimally acquire data from privacy-sensitive users to estimate an underlying parameter, while accounting for heterogeneous privacy costs and providing differential privacy guarantees under both central and local privacy architectures?
557dce8787129ca623fcb2cca2e76e9920347b69.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by modeling user privacy sensitivities and leveraging Bayesian-optimal mechanism design, it is possible to design efficient data acquisition mechanisms that simultaneously minimize estimation error and total user compensation, while providing heterogeneous differential privacy guarantees in both central and local settings.
557dce8787129ca623fcb2cca2e76e9920347b69.proposed_method: The proposed approach formulates the data acquisition problem as a Bayesian-optimal mechanism design task, where each user has a private, heterogeneous privacy sensitivity quantified via differential privacy. The mechanism elicits users' privacy sensitivities and data, then determines both the optimal estimator and user payments to incentivize truthful reporting. In the central privacy setting, the method constructs a linear estimator that combines a weighted average of user data with Laplace noise, where weights and noise levels are functions of reported sensitivities. In the local setting, each user privatizes their data using Laplace noise before sharing, and the platform aggregates these privatized values via a weighted average. The mechanism design problem is cast as a non-convex optimization over privacy loss allocations and estimator weights, with efficient algorithms developed: a score-based O(n log n) algorithm for the central setting and a Polynomial Time Approximation Scheme (PTAS) for the local setting.
557dce8787129ca623fcb2cca2e76e9920347b69.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted via theoretical analysis and simulation, focusing on minimax lower bounds for estimation error under both central and local differential privacy with heterogeneous user sensitivities. The effectiveness of the proposed mechanisms will be evaluated by comparing the estimation error and total payments against known baselines, such as mechanisms with homogeneous privacy guarantees or dominant-strategy truthful mechanisms. Evaluation metrics include estimation accuracy (mean squared error), total compensation, and computational efficiency. Simulations will use synthetic datasets with varying distributions of user privacy sensitivities to assess robustness and performance under different population scenarios.
557dce8787129ca623fcb2cca2e76e9920347b69.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a mechanism that endogenously determines heterogeneous differential privacy levels and payments based on user-reported sensitivities, extending prior work that assumed homogeneous privacy or fixed privacy menus. It establishes minimax lower bounds and (near-)optimal estimators for private mean estimation with heterogeneous privacy loss levels, a setting not previously addressed. The approach leverages Bayesian mechanism design to achieve incentive compatibility and efficient privacy allocation, and develops efficient algorithms for both central and local privacy architectures. The comparative analysis between central and local settings provides new insights into the trade-offs in privacy architectures and their impact on platform utility and user privacy.

5582cbd17e0b697792dd98eef89634b599c0b758.title: Learning Mean Field Control on Sparse Graphs
5582cbd17e0b697792dd98eef89634b599c0b758.research_question: How can mean field control be effectively learned and applied to large-scale multi-agent systems operating on sparse graphs, particularly those with finite expected degree and potentially diverging degree variance, such as power law networks observed in real-world applications?
5582cbd17e0b697792dd98eef89634b599c0b758.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a mean field control framework based on local weak convergence can accurately model and enable scalable learning in very sparse agent networks, outperforming existing mean field and graphon-based approaches on both synthetic and real-world networks.
5582cbd17e0b697792dd98eef89634b599c0b758.proposed_method: A novel mean field control model, termed Local Weak Mean Field Control (LWMFC), will be developed to address cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning on sparse graphs. The approach leverages the concept of local weak convergence to model graph sequences with finite expected degree, including power law networks with coefficients above two. The methodology involves a rigorous theoretical analysis of the limiting behavior of agent populations under local weak convergence, followed by the design of a two-systems approximation: one system for low-degree agents (with at most k* neighbors) and another for high-degree agents, using heuristic-based neighborhood degree distributions. Scalable learning algorithms will be constructed by reducing the large-scale interacting agent system to a single-agent mean field control Markov decision process (MFC-MDP), which is then solved using policy gradient reinforcement learning. Additionally, a model-free MARL variant will be implemented that directly interacts with real network data, bypassing the need for explicit model knowledge.
5582cbd17e0b697792dd98eef89634b599c0b758.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world networks, including datasets such as CAIDA, Cities, DiggFriends, Enron, Flixster, Slashdot, Yahoo, and YouTube, with network sizes ranging from tens of thousands to millions of nodes. The proposed LWMFC model and learning algorithms will be evaluated on a range of benchmark problems, including Susceptible-Infected-Susceptible (SIS), Susceptible-Infected-Recovered (SIR), graph coloring, and rumor spreading. Baselines for comparison will include mean field algorithms based on Lp graphons (LPGMFG) and graphexes (GXMFG), as well as scalable independent learning methods such as IPPO. Evaluation metrics will include average expected total variation distance between empirical and model-predicted mean fields, as well as objective values achieved by different learning algorithms. Experiments will assess both the accuracy of the mean field approximations and the performance of the learning algorithms in terms of convergence and achieved objectives.
5582cbd17e0b697792dd98eef89634b599c0b758.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first mean field control framework specifically designed for very sparse graphs with finite expected degree and diverging variance, a class of networks not addressed by existing graphon or graphex-based mean field models. The two-systems approximation and associated scalable learning algorithms provide a tractable and accurate approach for large-scale multi-agent systems on realistic sparse topologies. Theoretical results establish strong connections between finite and limiting systems under local weak convergence, and the proposed algorithms are rigorously justified and empirically shown to outperform state-of-the-art baselines on a variety of challenging benchmark problems and real-world networks.

55a07c708b2988d5719f8c9d19973aba6767bb92.title: Adaptive Discretization for Consistency Models
55a07c708b2988d5719f8c9d19973aba6767bb92.research_question: How can the discretization strategy for consistency models (CMs) be adaptively determined to balance trainability and stability, thereby improving training efficiency and generative performance across different noise schedules and datasets?
55a07c708b2988d5719f8c9d19973aba6767bb92.hypothesis: An adaptive discretization framework that jointly optimizes for local and global consistency, formulated as a constrained optimization problem and solved analytically, will yield improved training efficiency, stability, and generative quality for consistency models compared to manually designed or fixed discretization schemes.
55a07c708b2988d5719f8c9d19973aba6767bb92.proposed_method: A unified framework is developed for the adaptive discretization of consistency models by formulating the selection of discretization steps as a constrained optimization problem. The objective is to minimize local consistency error (the difference between model outputs at adjacent time points) while constraining global consistency error (the denoising error relative to the data distribution). This trade-off is established using a Lagrange multiplier, and the resulting optimization is relaxed and solved analytically via the Gauss-Newton method. The discretization step at each time is adaptively computed based on the current state of the neural network, leveraging the Jacobian-vector product for efficient calculation. An adaptive loss function incorporating a Pseudo-Huber metric and a dynamic weighting scheme further stabilizes training and enhances performance. The training alternates between updating the time segmentation and optimizing the network parameters, with the discretization schedule periodically recalculated based on the evolving model.
55a07c708b2988d5719f8c9d19973aba6767bb92.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on unconditional CIFAR-10 and class-conditional ImageNet 64×64 datasets, with additional scalability tests on ImageNet 512×512. Pretrained diffusion models (EDM, EDM2) are used for initialization where appropriate. The proposed method is compared against a range of baselines, including various consistency models (iCT, ECM, sCT, CCM), diffusion models (DDPM, EDM, DPM-Solver), and distillation-based approaches. Evaluation metrics include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for sample quality and the number of function evaluations (NFE) for generation speed. Training efficiency is measured by the number of images processed to reach a target FID. Ablation studies are performed on the Lagrange multiplier and loss function design, and the adaptability of the method is assessed on advanced diffusion model variants such as Flow Matching.
55a07c708b2988d5719f8c9d19973aba6767bb92.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified and adaptive discretization framework for consistency models, formulating discretization as a constrained optimization problem that balances local and global consistency. An analytical solution for the discretization step is derived using the Gauss-Newton method, enabling adaptive adjustment based on the model's state. The method generalizes and subsumes prior discretization strategies as special cases, eliminates the need for manual tuning across datasets and noise schedules, and incorporates adaptive loss and weighting functions for further stability. Experiments demonstrate significant improvements in training efficiency, generative quality, and adaptability to different model variants and resolutions.

55a0ebdc0b3fbc1f1e86e9975296d3c26f00f795.title: TypedThinker: Typed Thinking Improves Large Language Model Reasoning
55a0ebdc0b3fbc1f1e86e9975296d3c26f00f795.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be enabled to utilize diverse high-level reasoning strategies, beyond predominantly deductive reasoning, to improve their problem-solving capabilities across logical and mathematical tasks?
55a0ebdc0b3fbc1f1e86e9975296d3c26f00f795.hypothesis: Incorporating explicit selection and demonstration of diverse reasoning types (deductive, inductive, abductive, analogical) for each problem instance will enable LLMs to solve a broader range of problems more effectively than approaches relying on a single or undifferentiated reasoning strategy.
55a0ebdc0b3fbc1f1e86e9975296d3c26f00f795.proposed_method: A novel framework, TypedThinker, will be developed to diversify LLM reasoning by explicitly modeling and selecting among multiple reasoning types. The approach consists of three main components: (1) a meta-thinker, fine-tuned to predict the effectiveness of each reasoning type for a given problem based on empirical success rates; (2) an explicit demonstration collection, which stores successful solutions for each reasoning type and problem, enabling retrieval of relevant few-shot examples during inference; and (3) a reasoner, which applies the selected reasoning type to generate a detailed reasoning path for the answer, guided by retrieved demonstrations. The meta-thinker outputs effectiveness scores for each reasoning type, and the system either greedily selects the most effective type or aggregates answers across effective types using weighted voting. The reasoner and meta-thinker are further optimized via instruction tuning and supervised fine-tuning on empirical effectiveness data.
55a0ebdc0b3fbc1f1e86e9975296d3c26f00f795.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using open-source LLMs such as Mistral 7B, LLaMA3 8B, and Qwen2-7B-Instruct on two logical reasoning benchmarks (LogiQA, BBH) and two mathematical reasoning benchmarks (GSM8K, MATH). Baselines will include standard few-shot prompting, chain-of-thought selection, self-discover approaches, and mixture-of-reasoning (MoR) methods with both zero-shot and few-shot demonstrations. Evaluation will use accuracy as the primary metric, with exact match for logic tasks and mathematical equivalence for math tasks. Additional experiments will test generalization to unseen domains (e.g., Contexthub benchmark) and transferability to other LLMs (e.g., GPT-4o, MetaMath) using the pre-trained meta-thinker and demonstration memory without further fine-tuning. Ablation studies will assess the contribution of each component (meta-thinker, explicit memory, fine-tuned reasoner) to overall performance.
55a0ebdc0b3fbc1f1e86e9975296d3c26f00f795.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces an explicit mechanism for selecting and applying diverse reasoning types at the instance level, rather than relying on a single or undifferentiated reasoning strategy. TypedThinker combines a meta-thinker for reasoning type prediction, an explicit demonstration memory for retrieval of type-specific examples, and a fine-tuned reasoner for executing the selected reasoning approach. The method demonstrates improved reasoning performance over strong baselines, generalizes to new domains and LLMs without additional fine-tuning, and is orthogonal to the underlying LLM architecture. This approach enables LLMs to solve problems that are only tractable via specific reasoning types, thus expanding their effective problem-solving repertoire.

55a59dfff3e57ec551814db82225a3677411e092.title: Geometry-Informed Neural Operator for Large-Scale 3D PDEs
55a59dfff3e57ec551814db82225a3677411e092.research_question: How can the solution operator for large-scale 3D partial differential equations (PDEs) with varying and complex geometries be efficiently and accurately learned, enabling rapid prediction of physical quantities such as pressure fields and drag coefficients in computational fluid dynamics (CFD) applications?
55a59dfff3e57ec551814db82225a3677411e092.hypothesis: A neural operator architecture that combines geometry-aware encoding using signed distance functions (SDFs) and point-cloud representations with both graph-based and Fourier-based neural operator layers will enable discretization-convergent, efficient, and accurate learning of solution operators for large-scale 3D PDEs across arbitrary geometries and mesh discretizations.
55a59dfff3e57ec551814db82225a3677411e092.proposed_method: The proposed method develops a Geometry-Informed Neural Operator (GINO) framework that integrates three main components: (i) a geometry encoder using graph neural operator (GNO) layers to process irregular input point clouds and SDF features, mapping them to a latent regular grid; (ii) a global model employing a sequence of Fourier neural operator (FNO) layers operating on the regular grid to efficiently capture global interactions via fast Fourier transforms; and (iii) a geometry decoder utilizing GNO layers to project the FNO output back onto the original irregular geometry for flexible querying. The architecture is trained end-to-end to predict target functions, such as surface pressure, using loss functions computed on the geometry surface. Efficient graph construction is achieved via GPU-accelerated hash-table neighborhood search, and adaptive instance normalization is incorporated to handle varying boundary conditions such as inlet velocities. The method is designed to be discretization-convergent, supporting arbitrary mesh resolutions and enabling zero-shot super-resolution.
55a59dfff3e57ec551814db82225a3677411e092.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two large-scale 3D CFD datasets: (1) an industry-standard Ahmed-body dataset generated using GPU-accelerated OpenFOAM, comprising over 500 vehicle geometries with up to 100,000 mesh points on the surface and millions in space, and (2) the Shape-Net Car dataset, containing over 600 realistic car shapes with approximately 3,700 mesh points each. The task is to predict full pressure fields from input geometries. Baseline comparisons will include GNO, MeshGraphNet, GeoFNO, 3D UNet, and FNO models. Models will be trained for 100 epochs using the Adam optimizer and evaluated using normalized and de-normalized L2 error metrics on both training and test splits.
