Cost-accuracy trade-off analyses will be performed, including inference time versus error for drag coefficient computation, and ablation studies will investigate the effects of latent grid resolution and sampling rates. All models will be run on Nvidia V100 GPUs.
55a59dfff3e57ec551814db82225a3677411e092.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified neural operator architecture that combines the strengths of graph-based and Fourier-based operators, enabling efficient handling of both irregular and regular grids. By leveraging signed distance functions and point-cloud representations, the method supports arbitrary and complex geometries. The framework achieves discretization convergence, allowing models trained on one mesh resolution to generalize to others, including zero-shot super-resolution. The method demonstrates orders-of-magnitude speedup (up to 26,000x) over traditional CFD solvers while achieving significantly lower error rates compared to existing deep learning baselines. Efficient GPU-based graph construction and adaptive normalization for boundary conditions further distinguish the approach.

55a69beb1a754a0a7cbab1c5723a0841408725d9.title: PrefixKV: Adaptive Prefix KV Cache is What Vision Instruction-Following Models Need for Efficient Generation
55a69beb1a754a0a7cbab1c5723a0841408725d9.research_question: How can the inference efficiency of large vision-language models (LVLMs) be improved by more effectively compressing the key-value (KV) cache, while maintaining high generation quality and minimizing contextual information loss?
55a69beb1a754a0a7cbab1c5723a0841408725d9.hypothesis: Adaptive, layer-wise retention of the most important KV vectors—determined by attention-based importance metrics and optimized via a global prefix configuration—will enable significant KV cache compression, leading to faster inference and reduced memory usage without notable degradation in model performance.
55a69beb1a754a0a7cbab1c5723a0841408725d9.proposed_method: A novel KV cache compression framework, termed PrefixKV, is proposed to adaptively retain the most important KV vectors in each transformer layer of LVLMs. The method first computes an attention-based importance metric for each KV vector after the prefilling stage, normalizes and sorts these to form priority sequences, and then defines the 'prefix' as the top-ranked vectors by importance (not position). The optimal proportion of retained KV vectors per layer is determined by searching for a global prefix configuration that maximizes cumulative contextual information under a given compression budget. This search is efficiently performed using binary search over the cumulative priority sequences, ensuring that each layer preserves maximal contextual information. During decoding, the cache is dynamically pruned to maintain the derived layer-wise proportions, and offline estimation using a small number of random samples is leveraged to avoid online search overhead.
55a69beb1a754a0a7cbab1c5723a0841408725d9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using LLaVA-1.5-7B and LLaVA-1.5-13B LVLMs on the LLaVA-Description and MM-Vet instruction-following datasets. Evaluation metrics include perplexity (PPL) and ROUGE score for generation quality, as well as inference latency and throughput for efficiency. Baseline comparisons will be made against state-of-the-art KV cache compression methods such as ElasticCache, Heavy-Hitter Oracle (H2O), StreamingLLM, and PyramidKV. The experimental setup includes varying compression budgets (10% to 90%), different batch sizes, and both long and short input contexts. Additional analyses will assess robustness to domain and instruction complexity, and generalizability will be tested on Qwen-VL and LLaMA-3-8B models, including scenarios with cache quantization.
55a69beb1a754a0a7cbab1c5723a0841408725d9.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a global prefix configuration framework for adaptive, layer-wise KV cache compression, leveraging attention-based importance metrics and binary search to maximize contextual information retention. Unlike prior approaches that use uniform cache size or manually designed patterns, this method automatically tailors cache sizes per layer based on empirical importance distributions, leading to superior trade-offs between inference efficiency and generation quality. The approach demonstrates robust offline estimation, generalizes across models and domains, and eliminates the need for cache merging, providing state-of-the-art performance and practical deployment benefits.

55ad7d4007b0a5a38ce07c3fcbc3328abbd99d76.title: LobsDICE: Offline Learning from Observation via Stationary Distribution Correction Estimation
55ad7d4007b0a5a38ce07c3fcbc3328abbd99d76.research_question: How can an agent effectively learn to imitate expert behavior from state-only demonstrations in an offline setting, where the agent cannot interact with the environment and only has access to additional action-labeled transition data from agents of unknown quality?
55ad7d4007b0a5a38ce07c3fcbc3328abbd99d76.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that optimizing the stationary distribution of the agent's policy to match the expert's state-transition distribution, while regularizing against deviation from the distribution of imperfect demonstrations, will enable effective offline learning from observation, even in stochastic environments and without access to expert actions.
55ad7d4007b0a5a38ce07c3fcbc3328abbd99d76.proposed_method: A novel offline learning from observation (LfO) algorithm, LobsDICE, is proposed. The method formulates the offline LfO problem as a convex minimization that directly matches the stationary state-transition distribution of the agent's policy to that of the expert, using KL divergence. An additional regularization term penalizes deviation from the stationary distribution of available action-labeled (imperfect) demonstrations, controlled by a hyperparameter. The optimization is performed in the space of stationary distributions rather than policies, and a Lagrangian dual formulation is used to eliminate the need for nested min-max optimization. Log-ratio estimation between expert and imperfect state-transition distributions is performed via a pretrained discriminator, and a closed-form solution for the inner maximization is derived, reducing the problem to a single convex minimization. The optimal policy is then extracted using weighted behavior cloning with self-normalized importance sampling, based on the estimated stationary distribution corrections.
55ad7d4007b0a5a38ce07c3fcbc3328abbd99d76.experiment_details: Experiments are proposed on both tabular and continuous Markov Decision Processes (MDPs). For tabular MDPs, randomly generated environments with varying degrees of stochasticity will be used, and datasets will include state-only expert demonstrations and action-labeled imperfect demonstrations. Baselines for comparison will include Behavior Cloning (BC), BCO, OPOLO, and a modified DemoDICEfO. The primary evaluation metric will be the total variation distance between the state-transition stationary distributions of the expert and the learned policy, averaged over multiple random seeds. For continuous control, experiments will be conducted on MuJoCo environments (Hopper, Walker2d, HalfCheetah, Ant) using the D4RL dataset, with tasks constructed from combinations of expert, medium, and random trajectories. Baselines will include BC, BCO, OPOLO, IQ-Learn, RCE, and DemoDICEfO, and performance will be measured by normalized returns over several random seeds.
55ad7d4007b0a5a38ce07c3fcbc3328abbd99d76.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first offline LfO algorithm that directly solves the state-transition stationary distribution matching problem via a single convex minimization, eliminating the need for nested min-max optimization or inverse dynamics models. The approach is robust to stochasticity in the environment and does not require expert action labels. Empirical results demonstrate that the method can asymptotically recover expert behavior in both tabular and continuous domains, outperforming strong baselines and achieving state-of-the-art results in offline LfO tasks.

55c562c0de9d011c91965a34ba784c9d4b72fecb.title: Linearity of Relation Decoding in Transformer Language Models
55c562c0de9d011c91965a34ba784c9d4b72fecb.research_question: How are relational facts represented and decoded within transformer language models, and to what extent can these relational computations be approximated by simple, interpretable linear transformations? What are the limitations and scope of linearity in the internal knowledge representations of large language models?
55c562c0de9d011c91965a34ba784c9d4b72fecb.hypothesis: A subset of relational knowledge in transformer language models can be faithfully and causally decoded from subject representations using a single affine (linear) transformation specific to each relation, but this linearity does not universally apply to all relations.
55c562c0de9d011c91965a34ba784c9d4b72fecb.proposed_method: The proposed method involves constructing linear relational embeddings (LREs) for specific relations within transformer language models. For each relation, the method estimates an affine transformation (a matrix and bias) that maps the hidden representation of a subject entity at a chosen intermediate layer to the hidden representation of the object entity, as decoded by the model. This is achieved by computing the Jacobian of the model's output with respect to the subject representation, using a first-order Taylor approximation and correcting for underestimation of magnitude by scaling the transformation. The LRE is evaluated for both faithfulness (agreement with the model's own predictions) and causality (ability to edit subject representations to change the model's output in a controlled way). The approach is further extended to develop an 'attribute lens' tool, which visualizes the distribution over possible object tokens at each layer for a given relation.
55c562c0de9d011c91965a34ba784c9d4b72fecb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on autoregressive transformer language models, including GPT-J, GPT-2-XL, and LLaMA-13B. A manually curated dataset of 47 relations spanning factual, commonsense, linguistic, and bias-related knowledge will be used, with over 10,000 subject–object pairs and relation-specific prompt templates. For each relation, LREs will be estimated using n=8 examples, and evaluated on faithfulness (the match between LRE-based and model-based predictions) and causality (the ability to edit subject representations to control model outputs). Baselines will include direct decoding, translation-based methods, and linear regression. Additional experiments will analyze the layerwise emergence of linearity and apply the attribute lens to adversarial prompts to probe latent knowledge. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, recall at top-k, and comparison to random and oracle baselines.
55c562c0de9d011c91965a34ba784c9d4b72fecb.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a systematic method to extract and validate linear relational embeddings from transformer language models, providing a simple and interpretable approximation to a subset of relational computations. It demonstrates that for nearly half of tested relations, a single affine transformation can faithfully and causally decode relational knowledge from subject representations. The approach enables direct intervention in model representations to control outputs and introduces the attribute lens, a novel tool for visualizing latent relational knowledge at different layers. The work reveals the heterogeneous deployment of linearity in knowledge representation and provides new insights into the interpretability and manipulability of large language models.

55cad4e02614ca362b1251d0a610ff5f9d74d769.title: Towards Understanding Why Label Smoothing Degrades Selective Classification and How to Fix It
55cad4e02614ca362b1251d0a610ff5f9d74d769.research_question: How does label smoothing affect selective classification performance in neural networks, and can the negative effects be mitigated to improve reliability in uncertainty-based rejection tasks?
55cad4e02614ca362b1251d0a610ff5f9d74d769.hypothesis: Label smoothing degrades the ability of neural networks to perform effective selective classification by impairing the uncertainty ranking between correct and incorrect predictions, but post-hoc logit normalisation can recover or improve selective classification performance.
55cad4e02614ca362b1251d0a610ff5f9d74d769.proposed_method: The proposed research will conduct a comprehensive empirical and analytical investigation into the impact of label smoothing (LS) on selective classification (SC) across various neural network architectures and tasks. The methodology will include training models with varying levels of label smoothing (parameter alpha) and evaluating their selective classification performance using softmax-based uncertainty measures, particularly Maximum Softmax Probability (MSP). Analytical work will focus on deriving and interpreting the logit-level gradients of the LS loss to understand how LS alters the ranking of uncertainty between correct and incorrect predictions. Additionally, the research will implement and evaluate post-hoc logit normalisation at inference time, where logits are normalised by their p-norm, to determine its effectiveness in mitigating the negative effects of LS on SC.
55cad4e02614ca362b1251d0a610ff5f9d74d769.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale image classification (ImageNet-1k) and semantic segmentation (Cityscapes) tasks, using architectures such as ResNet-50, ViT-S-16, and DeepLabV3+ with ResNet-101 backbone. The validation and evaluation splits will be clearly defined (e.g., 10,000 validation and 40,000 evaluation images for ImageNet), and models will be trained from scratch with only the LS parameter varied to isolate its effects. Baselines will include models trained with standard cross-entropy (CE) loss. Evaluation metrics will focus on risk-coverage (RC) curves, area under the RC curve (AURC), and coverage at fixed risk levels. Additional experiments will include distribution-shifted data (ImageNet-Sketch) to test robustness. The impact of logit normalisation will be assessed by grid-searching the p-norm parameter on a validation set and comparing SC performance before and after normalisation.
55cad4e02614ca362b1251d0a610ff5f9d74d769.novelty_claims: This research proposes a detailed empirical and analytical explanation for why label smoothing degrades selective classification, attributing it to imbalanced suppression of the max logit that disrupts uncertainty ranking. The study introduces the use of post-hoc logit normalisation as an effective remedy for LS-induced degradation in SC, providing both empirical validation and theoretical insight into its mechanism. The work uniquely bridges the gap between training-time regularisation techniques and their downstream impact on uncertainty-based decision making, offering actionable recommendations for practitioners and opening new avenues for research into training enhancements and their effects on selective classification and related tasks.

55f6844c4cf5c7f2925cc7312620cd56cf275ccd.title: BOME! Bilevel Optimization Made Easy: A Simple First-Order Approach
55f6844c4cf5c7f2925cc7312620cd56cf275ccd.research_question: How can bilevel optimization be made more practical, efficient, and scalable for large-scale, non-convex machine learning problems, such as hyperparameter optimization, meta-learning, continual learning, and reinforcement learning, while avoiding the computational bottlenecks of Hessian-based or implicit differentiation methods?
55f6844c4cf5c7f2925cc7312620cd56cf275ccd.hypothesis: A fully first-order bilevel optimization algorithm, based on a value-function reformulation and dynamic barrier gradient descent, can achieve efficient, robust, and theoretically guaranteed convergence to stationary points for non-convex objectives, outperforming or matching state-of-the-art methods in both accuracy and computational efficiency.
55f6844c4cf5c7f2925cc7312620cd56cf275ccd.proposed_method: A new bilevel optimization algorithm is proposed that reformulates the bilevel problem as a single-level constrained optimization using the value-function approach. The method applies a dynamic barrier gradient descent procedure, where updates are computed by minimizing the distance to the outer objective's gradient while ensuring sufficient decrease of the constraint (the gap between the current inner objective value and its minimum). At each iteration, the inner solution is approximated by running a fixed number of gradient descent steps, and the constraint and its gradient are estimated using this approximate solution. The update direction is computed in closed form, and the method avoids differentiating through the inner optimization process, requiring only first-order gradient information. Theoretical analysis establishes non-asymptotic convergence rates to stationary points under both unimodal (PL-inequality) and multimodal settings, with robustness to initialization and hyperparameters.
55f6844c4cf5c7f2925cc7312620cd56cf275ccd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of problems, including toy examples (coreset selection, mini-max games, degenerate low-level problems) and real-world machine learning tasks such as data hyper-cleaning (on MNIST and FashionMNIST), learnable regularization (on the 20 Newsgroups dataset), and continual learning (using contextual transformation networks on PMNIST and SplitCIFAR). The proposed method will be compared against a comprehensive set of baselines, including BSG-1, BVFSM, Penalty, ITD, AID-CG, AID-FP, reverse-mode autodiff, stocBiO, and VRBO. Evaluation metrics will include convergence to optimality, test loss, computational efficiency (time to solution), and continual learning metrics such as accuracy, negative backward transfer, and forward transfer. Hyperparameters will be tuned via grid search, and robustness to key parameters (inner steps, control coefficients) will be assessed.
55f6844c4cf5c7f2925cc7312620cd56cf275ccd.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a simple, practical, and fully first-order algorithm for bilevel optimization that does not require Hessian or implicit differentiation, making it suitable for large-scale non-convex problems. It extends dynamic barrier gradient descent to general bilevel settings, including non-convex lower-level objectives, and provides the first non-asymptotic convergence guarantees for such a method. The algorithm is robust to hyperparameter choices, computationally efficient, and consistently outperforms or matches state-of-the-art baselines in both accuracy and speed across a diverse set of benchmarks.

56088d8601afdd524029c5c151f7d13ed3f1a5ee.title: MindSearch: Mimicking Human Minds Elicits Deep AI Searcher
56088d8601afdd524029c5c151f7d13ed3f1a5ee.research_question: How can AI systems more effectively perform complex web information seeking and integration tasks, particularly in scenarios where user queries are multifaceted, information is dispersed across numerous noisy web pages, and the context length limitations of large language models present challenges?
56088d8601afdd524029c5c151f7d13ed3f1a5ee.hypothesis: Mimicking human cognitive processes through a multi-agent framework that decomposes complex queries into sub-tasks and employs hierarchical web retrieval will significantly improve the depth, breadth, and factuality of AI-generated responses for information-seeking tasks, compared to existing retrieval-augmented generation approaches.
56088d8601afdd524029c5c151f7d13ed3f1a5ee.proposed_method: A novel multi-agent framework, MindSearch, will be developed to emulate human-like problem-solving in web information seeking and integration. The system will consist of two main components: a WebPlanner and multiple WebSearchers. The WebPlanner will model reasoning as a dynamic directed acyclic graph (DAG) construction process, decomposing user queries into atomic sub-questions and orchestrating their resolution through code-based planning. Each sub-question will be assigned to a WebSearcher, which will perform hierarchical information retrieval using a coarse-to-fine strategy: generating multiple similar queries, aggregating search results from multiple engines (e.g., Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo), selecting the most relevant pages, and summarizing detailed content for integration. The design will enable parallel processing of sub-tasks, efficient context management, and robust handling of long-context scenarios, leveraging the strengths of both LLMs and search engines.
56088d8601afdd524029c5c151f7d13ed3f1a5ee.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both open-set and closed-set question answering (QA) tasks. For open-set QA, a curated set of 100 real-world human queries will be used, with responses generated by MindSearch (using InternLM2.5-7B-Chat), Perplexity.ai Pro, and ChatGPT with search plugins. Five human experts will evaluate responses based on depth, breadth, and factuality, with blinded assessment to ensure fairness. For closed-set QA, established datasets such as Bamboogle, Musique, and HotpotQA will be employed, using both closed-source (GPT-4o) and open-source (InternLM2.5-7B-Chat) LLMs as backends. Baselines will include raw LLMs without search engines and ReAct-style retrieval-augmented generation. Performance will be measured using accuracy and human preference metrics, and ablation studies will assess the impact of key components such as graph-based planning, multi-query generation, context prefixing, and page selection. Inference time and scaling behavior will also be analyzed.
56088d8601afdd524029c5c151f7d13ed3f1a5ee.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a multi-agent LLM-based framework that explicitly models human-like reasoning via code-driven graph construction for query decomposition and parallel hierarchical web retrieval. This method enables efficient aggregation and integration of information from hundreds of web pages within minutes, surpassing the limitations of context length in LLMs. The framework demonstrates significant improvements in response quality (depth and breadth) over leading AI search engines and retrieval-augmented generation baselines, and provides a scalable, open-source alternative competitive with proprietary solutions. The explicit context management and modular design further facilitate robust handling of complex, long-context information-seeking tasks.

560b1bc012588731b26748e33236570df777baa0.title: Aging with GRACE: Lifelong Model Editing with Discrete Key-Value Adaptors
560b1bc012588731b26748e33236570df777baa0.research_question: How can deployed language models be efficiently and reliably edited in a lifelong, sequential manner to correct errors and adapt to new requirements, without degrading performance on unrelated or previously edited inputs and without expensive retraining or access to proprietary training data?
560b1bc012588731b26748e33236570df777baa0.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a discrete key-value adaptor mechanism, which caches and retrieves local edits in the latent space of a pre-trained model without altering its weights, can enable thousands of sequential, targeted edits while maintaining model performance and generalizing to similar future inputs.
560b1bc012588731b26748e33236570df777baa0.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces General Retrieval Adaptors for Continual Editing (GRACE), a plug-in module for transformer-based language models. GRACE wraps a chosen layer of a pre-trained model with an adaptor containing a discrete codebook of key-value pairs and a deferral mechanism. Each key is a cached activation from the previous layer, and each value is optimized to produce the desired output for an edit. The deferral mechanism uses a similarity threshold (an epsilon-ball) to determine when to activate the adaptor for a given input; otherwise, the original model output is used. Edits are made by adding or updating entries in the codebook, with codebook maintenance strategies to expand, split, or create new entries based on the proximity and label agreement of new edits. The method is parameter-efficient, model-agnostic, and does not require access to the model's training data or semantically-equivalent inputs.
560b1bc012588731b26748e33236570df777baa0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three sequential editing tasks using pre-trained T5 (question answering), BERT (document classification with label shift), and GPT-2 (language generation/hallucination correction) models. Authentic model errors will be identified and corrected in a streaming fashion, with each edit applied immediately upon error detection. Baselines will include continual finetuning, Elastic Weight Consolidation, experience replay, and state-of-the-art model editors such as MEND, Defer, ROME, and a memory network ablation. Evaluation metrics will include Edit Success (task-specific accuracy or perplexity), Test Retention Rate (performance on original test data), and Edit Retention Rate (retention of previous edits). The number of edits, codebook size, and inference time will also be tracked. Datasets include NQ and zsRE for T5, SCOTUS for BERT, and OpenWebText and SelfCheckGPT for GPT-2.
560b1bc012588731b26748e33236570df777baa0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable thousands of sequential, targeted edits to deployed language models using only streaming error inputs, without requiring retraining, finetuning, or privileged data. GRACE introduces a discrete, local codebook mechanism that preserves model weights and enables plug-and-play, parameter-efficient editing. The method generalizes edits to semantically similar inputs, maintains performance on unrelated data, and allows for transparent inspection and management of edits. New public benchmarks for lifelong model editing are also established, including tasks for mitigating LLM hallucination and addressing label shifts.

5617f04b34aafb19f19acb03a405fe6d90dffe28.title: DeepGate2: Functionality-Aware Circuit Representation Learning
5617f04b34aafb19f19acb03a405fe6d90dffe28.research_question: How can circuit representation learning be improved to more effectively and efficiently capture both structural and functional properties of digital circuits, thereby enhancing performance on downstream electronic design automation (EDA) and logic reasoning tasks?
5617f04b34aafb19f19acb03a405fe6d90dffe28.hypothesis: Incorporating pairwise truth table differences as supervision, combined with a scalable, functionality-aware loss function and a one-round graph neural network (GNN) architecture that differentiates between structural and functional embeddings, will yield more accurate and efficient circuit representations, leading to improved results on downstream EDA tasks compared to existing methods.
5617f04b34aafb19f19acb03a405fe6d90dffe28.proposed_method: A novel circuit representation learning framework is proposed that leverages pairwise truth table differences between sampled logic gates as the primary supervision signal. The methodology involves generating incomplete truth tables for each gate via rapid logic simulation, then computing the Hamming distance between pairs of gates to serve as ground-truth functional similarity. A functionality-aware loss function is designed to explicitly minimize the disparity between the embedding space distance (based on cosine similarity) and the Hamming distance of the corresponding truth tables. The approach introduces a one-round GNN architecture that separates node embeddings into functional and structural components, each initialized differently: functional embeddings for primary inputs (PIs) are uniform, while structural embeddings are orthogonal vectors to preserve unique PI identification. Information is propagated through the circuit in a single forward pass, with dedicated aggregation mechanisms for AND and NOT gates, using self-attention to prioritize controlling inputs.
5617f04b34aafb19f19acb03a405fe6d90dffe28.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a large dataset of over 10,000 And-Inverter Graphs (AIGs) extracted from standard benchmarks (ITC’99, IWLS’05, EPFL, OpenCore), with node-level sampling yielding nearly 900,000 gate pairs for training and evaluation. The proposed method will be compared against DeepGate and FGNN baselines on tasks including logic probability prediction and logic equivalence gate identification, using metrics such as prediction error, recall, precision, F1-score, and AUC. Additional experiments will integrate the learned representations into real-world EDA tools for logic synthesis (SAT sweeping) and Boolean satisfiability solving (SAT), measuring reductions in SAT calls and runtime. Model ablations will assess the impact of PI encoding and multi-stage training strategies.
5617f04b34aafb19f19acb03a405fe6d90dffe28.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a functionality-aware supervision mechanism based on pairwise truth table differences, which provides richer and more direct functional information than previous statistical or contrastive approaches. The one-round GNN architecture with separate initialization and propagation of structural and functional embeddings enables an order-of-magnitude speedup in learning and inference. The method demonstrates significant improvements in both accuracy and efficiency on practical downstream EDA tasks, and generalizes better to large-scale circuits than existing solutions.

561ecdcac76f52d8c74df916c6d49d08f10522b4.title: SEA-RAFT: Simple, Efficient, Accurate RAFT for Optical Flow
561ecdcac76f52d8c74df916c6d49d08f10522b4.research_question: How can the efficiency, simplicity, and accuracy of RAFT-based optical flow estimation methods be improved for both standard benchmarks and cross-dataset generalization?
561ecdcac76f52d8c74df916c6d49d08f10522b4.hypothesis: Incorporating a mixture of Laplace loss, direct regression of initial flow, rigid-motion pre-training, and architectural simplifications into a RAFT-style framework will yield a model that is both more efficient and more accurate than existing RAFT variants, with improved generalization across datasets.
561ecdcac76f52d8c74df916c6d49d08f10522b4.proposed_method: A novel optical flow estimation framework, SEA-RAFT, will be developed by enhancing the RAFT iterative refinement architecture with several key modifications. First, the model will be supervised using a mixture of Laplace (MoL) loss, where the network predicts parameters for a two-component Laplace mixture at each pixel, allowing explicit modeling of both ordinary and ambiguous (e.g., occluded) cases. The first component is aligned with the standard endpoint-error metric by fixing its variance, while the second accounts for uncertainty. Second, the initial optical flow field will be directly regressed from the context encoder using both input frames, replacing the standard zero initialization and reducing the number of required refinement iterations. Third, large-scale rigid-motion pre-training will be performed using the TartanAir dataset, leveraging its realistic scenes to improve generalization. Additionally, architectural simplifications will be introduced by replacing custom feature/context encoders with standard ResNet backbones and substituting the convolutional GRU with ConvNeXt blocks, streamlining the model and improving scalability.
561ecdcac76f52d8c74df916c6d49d08f10522b4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard optical flow benchmarks, including Spring, Sintel, and KITTI. The training pipeline will utilize FlyingChairs, FlyingThings3D, and HD1K for initial training, with fine-tuning on each target benchmark. Rigid-flow pre-training will be performed on TartanAir for 300k steps, followed by staged training and fine-tuning as appropriate for each dataset. Multiple model sizes (S/M/L) will be evaluated, differing in backbone depth and number of inference iterations. Baselines will include RAFT, GMA, RPKNet, DIP, SKFlow, GMFlow, Flowformer, CRAFT, and others, with comparisons based on endpoint-error (EPE), 1-pixel outlier rate (1px), Fl-score, and WAUC. Ablation studies will be conducted to assess the impact of each proposed modification. Inference speed and model size will also be measured, with latency tested on an RTX3090 GPU at 1080p resolution.
561ecdcac76f52d8c74df916c6d49d08f10522b4.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces several innovations to RAFT-style optical flow estimation: (1) a mixture of Laplace loss tailored for dense optical flow, explicitly aligning one mixture component with the endpoint-error metric; (2) direct regression of the initial flow field for faster convergence and reduced iterations; (3) large-scale rigid-motion pre-training using TartanAir to improve generalization; and (4) architectural simplifications using standard ResNet and ConvNeXt blocks. These contributions are claimed to be novel in the context of RAFT-based methods and are orthogonal to prior improvements, resulting in a model that achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and efficiency on multiple benchmarks.

5631a5e6da0c495fa14bdf1c475aa93f8bff7539.title: Parallelizing MCMC Across the Sequence Length
5631a5e6da0c495fa14bdf1c475aa93f8bff7539.research_question: How can Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms be parallelized across the sequence length to achieve sublinear time complexity, while maintaining sample quality and efficiency, especially for high-dimensional and complex probabilistic models?
5631a5e6da0c495fa14bdf1c475aa93f8bff7539.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by formulating the MCMC sampling process as a nonlinear recursion and applying parallel-in-time fixed-point solvers such as Newton's method and its variants, it is possible to parallelize MCMC sampling across the sequence length, thereby achieving significant speedups over traditional sequential approaches without sacrificing sample quality.
5631a5e6da0c495fa14bdf1c475aa93f8bff7539.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves recasting the sequence of MCMC transitions (including Gibbs, Metropolis-adjusted Langevin Algorithm (MALA), and Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC)) as a nonlinear fixed-point problem. Parallel-in-time Newton's method (DEER) and memory-efficient quasi-Newton variants (quasi-DEER, block quasi-DEER, and stochastic quasi-DEER) will be employed to iteratively solve for the entire sequence of states in parallel. For non-differentiable steps (e.g., MALA's accept-reject), differentiable relaxations such as the stop-gradient trick will be used to enable Jacobian computation. Additional techniques, such as orthogonal coordinate transformations and sliding window updates, will be incorporated to improve scalability and efficiency, particularly for high-dimensional problems. The methodology also includes early-stopping strategies to obtain high-quality approximate samples before full convergence.
5631a5e6da0c495fa14bdf1c475aa93f8bff7539.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of probabilistic models, including hierarchical Gaussian models (e.g., the eight schools problem), Bayesian logistic regression on the German Credit dataset, and high-dimensional sentiment classification using LLM embeddings from the IMDB dataset. Both synthetic and real datasets will be used. Baseline comparisons will include traditional sequential MCMC implementations and parallel chains. Evaluation metrics will include wall-clock time, number of Newton iterations to convergence, effective sample size per second (ESS/s), and sample quality assessed by Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) relative to ground-truth samples (e.g., from NUTS). Experiments will be run on modern GPU hardware (e.g., H100, A100), and various batch sizes, chain lengths, and parallelization strategies (across sequence length, across chains, and within leapfrog steps for HMC) will be explored. Additional ablations will assess the impact of memory-efficient Jacobian estimation, sliding window size, and early-stopping on performance and sample quality.
5631a5e6da0c495fa14bdf1c475aa93f8bff7539.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel framework for parallelizing MCMC algorithms across the sequence length using parallel-in-time Newton methods, enabling sublinear time complexity in chain length. New memory-efficient quasi-Newton and block quasi-Newton algorithms are developed to reduce computational and memory costs, making the approach scalable to high-dimensional problems. The methodology extends parallelization to a broad class of MCMC algorithms, including those with non-differentiable steps, and introduces practical strategies such as early-stopping and sliding window updates. This work provides new opportunities for resource allocation in parallel computing, allowing tradeoffs between parallelization across chains and sequence length, and is expected to significantly accelerate MCMC sampling in domains where sequential methods are prohibitive.

563bac1c5cdd5096e9dbf8d4f3d5b3c4f7284e06.title: FEDformer: Frequency Enhanced Decomposed Transformer for Long-term Series Forecasting
563bac1c5cdd5096e9dbf8d4f3d5b3c4f7284e06.research_question: How can long-term time series forecasting be improved in terms of accuracy and efficiency, particularly by better capturing both global and local properties of time series data?
563bac1c5cdd5096e9dbf8d4f3d5b3c4f7284e06.hypothesis: Integrating frequency-domain representations and seasonal-trend decomposition into Transformer architectures will enhance the ability to capture global properties of time series, reduce computational complexity, and improve forecasting accuracy compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.
563bac1c5cdd5096e9dbf8d4f3d5b3c4f7284e06.proposed_method: A novel forecasting framework, Frequency Enhanced Decomposed Transformer (FEDformer), will be developed by combining seasonal-trend decomposition with frequency-domain mapping within the Transformer architecture. The method will introduce Frequency Enhanced Blocks (FEB) and Frequency Enhanced Attention (FEA), which operate in both Fourier and Wavelet domains, substituting standard self-attention and cross-attention modules. The approach will randomly select a fixed number of frequency components (modes) from the Fourier or Wavelet basis, enabling a compact and information-preserving representation of time series. Additionally, a Mixture of Experts Decomposition (MOEDecomp) block will be used to extract and combine multiple trend components, allowing the model to better capture both global trends and local variations. The architecture will be designed to achieve linear computational complexity with respect to sequence length, thus enabling efficient modeling of long sequences.
563bac1c5cdd5096e9dbf8d4f3d5b3c4f7284e06.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six benchmark datasets spanning multiple domains, including energy, traffic, economics, weather, and disease. The evaluation will use both multivariate and univariate time series forecasting tasks, with input and output sequence lengths set according to established benchmarks (e.g., input length 96, prediction lengths 96, 192, 336, 720). Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art Transformer-based models such as Autoformer, Informer, LogTrans, and Reformer. Evaluation metrics will include Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). Ablation studies will assess the contributions of frequency-domain blocks, attention mechanisms, and the mode selection policy. Additional analysis will use statistical tests (e.g., Kolmogorov-Smirnov test) to compare the distributional similarity between predicted and ground truth sequences.
563bac1c5cdd5096e9dbf8d4f3d5b3c4f7284e06.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a frequency-enhanced Transformer architecture that incorporates both Fourier and Wavelet domain operations for representation learning, replacing conventional attention mechanisms. By randomly selecting a subset of frequency components, the model achieves linear computational and memory complexity, a significant improvement over standard quadratic-complexity Transformers. The integration of a Mixture of Experts Decomposition block for adaptive trend extraction further distinguishes the approach. The method is theoretically and empirically validated to preserve essential information and improve forecasting accuracy, achieving substantial error reductions over state-of-the-art baselines. This framework is the first to unify frequency-domain mapping and seasonal-trend decomposition within a Transformer for long-term time series forecasting.

567157a4722d79f5ac019142e5fb1ad10b4e86cb.title: VideoAgent: Long-form Video Understanding with Large Language Model as Agent
567157a4722d79f5ac019142e5fb1ad10b4e86cb.research_question: How can long-form video understanding be improved by leveraging interactive reasoning and planning, rather than direct processing of lengthy visual inputs, to efficiently and accurately answer complex questions about video content?
567157a4722d79f5ac019142e5fb1ad10b4e86cb.hypothesis: An agent-based system that employs a large language model to iteratively select and aggregate relevant visual information, using vision-language models and retrieval tools, will achieve superior effectiveness and efficiency in long-form video understanding compared to existing methods.
567157a4722d79f5ac019142e5fb1ad10b4e86cb.proposed_method: A novel agent-based framework is proposed in which a large language model (LLM) acts as the central agent to control an iterative process for long-form video understanding. The process begins with the LLM receiving captions of uniformly sampled frames, generated by a vision-language model (VLM), to establish an initial context. At each iteration, the LLM uses chain-of-thought prompting and self-reflection to decide whether sufficient information is available to answer the question or if further information is needed. If more information is required, the LLM formulates targeted queries to retrieve new frames using a contrastive language-image model (CLIP) at the segment level, focusing on relevant temporal regions. These retrieved frames are captioned by the VLM, and the updated textual state is fed back to the LLM for further reasoning. This iterative process continues until the agent is confident in its answer, balancing information sufficiency and computational efficiency.
567157a4722d79f5ac019142e5fb1ad10b4e86cb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two established long-form video understanding benchmarks: EgoSchema, which contains 5,000 egocentric videos and multiple-choice questions, and NExT-QA, featuring 5,440 videos and 48,000 questions categorized as temporal, causal, or descriptive. The evaluation will focus on zero-shot accuracy, using accuracy as the primary metric. Baselines will include state-of-the-art models such as LLoVi, SeViLA, and various uniform and selective sampling approaches. The experimental setup will utilize EVA-CLIP-8B-plus for frame retrieval, LaViLa and CogAgent as captioners for different datasets, and GPT-4 as the LLM agent. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of iterative frame selection, frame efficiency, and the number of reasoning rounds, while case studies will assess generalization to arbitrarily long videos.
567157a4722d79f5ac019142e5fb1ad10b4e86cb.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces an agent-based framework that mimics human cognitive processes for video understanding, emphasizing interactive, iterative reasoning and planning over direct long-context visual modeling. Key innovations include the use of a large language model as an agent to control the information-gathering process, segment-level frame retrieval guided by dynamically rewritten queries, and a multi-round self-reflective decision mechanism for efficient information aggregation. The approach achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on challenging benchmarks while using significantly fewer frames, demonstrating exceptional frame efficiency and scalability to very long videos.

56767c18bb5aaa2b6377624168bed1b6dcc4b94d.title: DistillSpec: Improving Speculative Decoding via Knowledge Distillation
56767c18bb5aaa2b6377624168bed1b6dcc4b94d.research_question: How can the alignment between a compact draft model and a larger target model be improved to accelerate large language model inference via speculative decoding, while maintaining or controlling the trade-off between generation quality and latency?
56767c18bb5aaa2b6377624168bed1b6dcc4b94d.hypothesis: Knowledge distillation, when carefully designed with model-generated data and appropriate divergence functions, can significantly improve the alignment between draft and target models, thereby increasing the efficiency and speed of speculative decoding without substantial loss in output quality.
56767c18bb5aaa2b6377624168bed1b6dcc4b94d.proposed_method: A novel framework, DistillSpec, will be developed to enhance speculative decoding by leveraging white-box knowledge distillation to better align the draft model with the target model. The method involves training the draft model using predictions from the target model as supervision, with a focus on minimizing divergence between their token distributions. Key components include: (1) generating distillation data using on-policy outputs from the draft model to ensure cost-effective and task-relevant alignment; (2) systematically exploring and tuning divergence functions (such as forward KL, reverse KL, Jensen-Shannon, and total variation distance) to optimize acceptance rates and block efficiency in speculative decoding; and (3) extending the framework to lossy speculative decoding by introducing lenience functions that allow fine-grained control over the quality-latency trade-off. The approach is designed to be compatible with existing speculative decoding infrastructures and to support transferability across tasks and model sizes.
56767c18bb5aaa2b6377624168bed1b6dcc4b94d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using both decoder-only and encoder-decoder large language models, including GPT-like models (234M and 33M parameters) and T5 v1.1 models (T5-XL at 3B and T5-Small at 77M parameters). Evaluation will cover a range of tasks and datasets: LM1B for language modeling, CNN/DM and XSum for summarization, WMT EnDe for translation, GSM8K for arithmetic reasoning, and BigBenchHard for transferability. Baselines will include standard speculative decoding with non-distilled draft models and various knowledge distillation recipes (e.g., supervised KD, SeqKD, f-Distill, GKD). Metrics will include acceptance rate, block efficiency, wall-clock latency, and downstream task performance (e.g., Rouge2, accuracy). Both greedy and non-greedy (temperature) decoding strategies will be tested, and ablation studies will analyze the impact of data generation methods and divergence choices. Additional experiments will explore lossy speculative decoding and the use of model gardens (multiple model sizes) to assess trade-offs between latency and quality.
56767c18bb5aaa2b6377624168bed1b6dcc4b94d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled and systematic framework for improving speculative decoding via white-box knowledge distillation, emphasizing the importance of model-generated (especially on-policy) data and task-specific divergence functions. The method is the first to provide a comprehensive analysis of how distillation recipes affect both alignment and downstream performance in the context of speculative decoding. DistillSpec enables substantial speedups (up to 10x) in decoding latency with minimal performance loss, offers fine-grained control over the quality-latency trade-off through lossy SD extensions, and demonstrates strong transferability across tasks and model sizes. The framework is designed to be complementary to existing speculative decoding systems and provides actionable guidelines for optimizing inference pipelines in practical, multi-model settings.

568e80ac7555266516e24830b0d325daab6fc595.title: Understanding Collapse in Non-contrastive Siamese Representation Learning
568e80ac7555266516e24830b0d325daab6fc595.research_question: What are the underlying causes and mechanisms of collapse in non-contrastive Siamese self-supervised representation learning, and how can collapse be measured, predicted, and prevented to improve downstream task performance?
568e80ac7555266516e24830b0d325daab6fc595.hypothesis: Collapse in non-contrastive Siamese networks is driven by the interplay between model capacity and dataset complexity, and can be quantitatively measured and predicted. Furthermore, modifying the training regime, such as adopting continual learning, can effectively prevent collapse and improve representation quality.
568e80ac7555266516e24830b0d325daab6fc595.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical investigation will be conducted to understand collapse in non-contrastive Siamese representation learning frameworks, such as SimSiam and BYOL. The approach will involve training models of varying architectures (e.g., different ResNet variants) on datasets of varying complexity and size, systematically altering the ratio of model capacity to dataset complexity. A novel rank-based metric, derived from the singular value decomposition (SVD) of learned representations, will be introduced to quantify the degree of partial dimensional collapse. Additionally, a linear regression model will be developed to predict downstream linear probe accuracy using both the SimSiam loss and the collapse metric, enabling label-free model selection. The effect of architectural choices (e.g., width vs. depth) and alternative training regimes, such as continual learning and hybrid continual/multi-epoch training, will be rigorously analyzed to identify strategies that mitigate collapse.
568e80ac7555266516e24830b0d325daab6fc595.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using standard self-supervised learning benchmarks, primarily ImageNet-1k, with subsets ranging from 1% to 100% of the dataset to manipulate data complexity. Multiple ResNet architectures (ResNet-18, ResNet-34, ResNet-50, and bottleneck variants) will be evaluated. Models will be trained for a fixed number of gradient steps using consistent hyperparameters (e.g., SGD with momentum, batch size 256, cosine learning rate decay). Downstream performance will be assessed via linear probe accuracy and k-nearest neighbor (k-NN) classification. Baselines will include standard SimSiam, BYOL, and MoCo-v3, with comparisons across different training regimes: multi-epoch, continual (single-pass), and hybrid. Evaluation metrics will include the proposed collapse metric (area under the cumulative explained variance curve from SVD), SimSiam loss, and downstream classification accuracy. The predictive power of the collapse metric and loss for downstream accuracy will be validated using regression analysis.
568e80ac7555266516e24830b0d325daab6fc595.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new, quantitative metric for measuring partial dimensional collapse in learned representations, capturing both obvious and subtle forms of collapse. It establishes a predictive relationship between this collapse metric, SimSiam loss, and downstream task performance, enabling label-free model selection. The research further claims that continual learning regimes, contrary to prevailing wisdom, can act as a regularizer to prevent collapse and substantially improve performance in non-contrastive SSL, especially for underparameterized models. The work provides new insights into the importance of model width over depth and demonstrates that simple changes in data ordering can yield significant gains without architectural modifications.

569140ad11310f71c5fcc0ecaa6810d12bee3416.title: Uncertainty Quantification over Graph with Conformalized Graph Neural Networks
569140ad11310f71c5fcc0ecaa6810d12bee3416.research_question: How can uncertainty quantification for predictions made by graph neural networks (GNNs) be performed with rigorous statistical guarantees, while maintaining practical efficiency in the size of prediction sets or intervals?
569140ad11310f71c5fcc0ecaa6810d12bee3416.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a conformal prediction framework, when adapted to the graph domain with permutation-invariant non-conformity scores and enhanced by a topology-aware correction model, can provide valid uncertainty quantification with guaranteed coverage and significantly improved efficiency over existing methods.
569140ad11310f71c5fcc0ecaa6810d12bee3416.proposed_method: A new framework, termed conformalized GNN (CF-GNN), is developed to extend conformal prediction to graph neural networks for uncertainty quantification. The approach first establishes a permutation invariance condition under which conformal prediction remains valid for graph-structured data, even in the transductive setting where calibration and test nodes are involved in model training. The method then introduces a topology-aware correction model, implemented as a secondary GNN, which takes the base GNN's predictions as input and aggregates information from each node's local subgraph to produce updated predictions. This correction model is trained post hoc using a differentiable inefficiency loss that simulates the conformal prediction step, directly optimizing for smaller prediction sets or intervals. The framework is designed as a generic wrapper, compatible with any pre-trained GNN, and does not alter the base model's training process.
569140ad11310f71c5fcc0ecaa6810d12bee3416.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted across 15 diverse datasets, including 8 node classification and 7 node regression tasks, spanning application domains such as citation networks, social networks, transportation, and finance. The evaluation setup involves random splits into training, validation, calibration, and test sets, with 100 random splits for robust estimation. Baselines include standard statistical calibration methods (e.g., temperature scaling, vector scaling, ensemble temperature scaling), GNN-specific calibration learners (e.g., CaGCN, GATS), and uncertainty quantification methods for regression (e.g., quantile regression, Monte Carlo dropout, Bayesian neural networks). Evaluation metrics comprise empirical marginal coverage (the fraction of test labels contained in the prediction set/interval) and inefficiency (size or length of the prediction set/interval). Conditional coverage is also assessed using the Worst-Slice metric over both input and network features. The experimental protocol fixes base GNN predictions to ensure fair comparison and isolates the effect of the uncertainty quantification method.
569140ad11310f71c5fcc0ecaa6810d12bee3416.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to provide rigorous, distribution-free uncertainty quantification for GNNs in the transductive setting, with exact characterization of test-time coverage. The introduction of a topology-aware, post-hoc correction model that directly optimizes for prediction set efficiency is novel, leveraging neighborhood correlations in inefficiency that are unique to graph data. The method achieves any pre-defined target marginal coverage while significantly reducing prediction set or interval size—by up to 74% over direct conformal prediction baselines—without sacrificing adaptivity or conditional coverage. The approach is model-agnostic, compatible with any GNN architecture, and generalizes across diverse graph types and tasks.

56b828717f32251a5e0f0be9c0113077f23c8429.title: QuIP: 2-Bit Quantization of Large Language Models With Guarantees
56b828717f32251a5e0f0be9c0113077f23c8429.research_question: How can large language models be quantized to extremely low bit-widths (e.g., 2 bits per weight) with theoretical guarantees on accuracy and without retraining, while maintaining inference performance and model quality across a range of tasks and model sizes?
56b828717f32251a5e0f0be9c0113077f23c8429.hypothesis: Enforcing incoherence in both the weight and Hessian matrices prior to quantization, combined with an optimal adaptive rounding procedure, will enable accurate and theoretically guaranteed 2-bit quantization of large language models, outperforming existing post-training quantization methods.
56b828717f32251a5e0f0be9c0113077f23c8429.proposed_method: The proposed method, Quantization with Incoherence Processing (QuIP), consists of two main steps. First, an adaptive rounding procedure (LDLQ) is employed to minimize a quadratic proxy objective for quantization error, using the Hessian of the layer inputs as a proxy for importance. This procedure iteratively quantizes weights with linear feedback based on the LDL decomposition of the Hessian, ensuring optimality among a broad class of rounding methods. Second, efficient pre- and post-processing steps are introduced to enforce incoherence in both the weight and Hessian matrices. This is achieved by multiplying these matrices with Kronecker products of random orthogonal matrices, which can be efficiently applied and reversed during inference. Additional heuristics such as diagonal rescaling, quantization range adjustment based on spectral properties, and random permutations are incorporated to further enhance performance. The entire process is designed to be efficient and scalable to models with billions of parameters.
56b828717f32251a5e0f0be9c0113077f23c8429.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large language models from the OPT (up to 66B parameters) and Llama2 (up to 70B parameters) families, using the HuggingFace implementations. Quantization will be performed post-training, one transformer block at a time, using calibration data from the C4 dataset (128 random 2048-token segments). Evaluation will be carried out on language modeling tasks (WikiText2, Penn Treebank, C4) and zero-shot tasks (LAMBADA, ARC Easy, PiQA, StoryCloze), measuring metrics such as perplexity and accuracy. Baselines will include nearest rounding, stochastic rounding, OPTQ, and variants with and without incoherence processing. Ablation studies will assess the impact of each processing step, and throughput benchmarks will compare inference speed against OPTQ. All experiments will be run on single GPUs with up to 48GB memory.
56b828717f32251a5e0f0be9c0113077f23c8429.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first quantization method for large language models that achieves viable 2-bit quantization with theoretical guarantees. It provides a novel incoherence processing technique that provably improves quantization error bounds by leveraging random orthogonal transformations. Theoretical analysis is presented for both the proposed method and the widely used OPTQ algorithm, establishing optimality within a broad class of adaptive rounding procedures. The approach is the first to demonstrate that incoherence processing enables all quantization methods, including nearest rounding, to perform well at extremely low bit-widths. Empirical results are expected to show state-of-the-art performance at 2 bits per weight across a wide range of model sizes and tasks.

56c679a0d5fce962e1c09db6d762e4024e277450.title: Clifford Group Equivariant Neural Networks
56c679a0d5fce962e1c09db6d762e4024e277450.research_question: How can neural networks be constructed to achieve equivariance with respect to orthogonal and Euclidean groups (O(n), E(n)) in a way that generalizes across dimensions and metric signatures, while efficiently representing and manipulating geometric quantities such as vectors, bivectors, and higher-grade multivectors?
56c679a0d5fce962e1c09db6d762e4024e277450.hypothesis: Neural network layers parameterized using the action of the Clifford group on Clifford algebras can achieve O(n)- and E(n)-equivariance, enabling expressive, efficient, and generalizable architectures that outperform or match existing equivariant and steerable methods across a variety of geometric and physical tasks.
56c679a0d5fce962e1c09db6d762e4024e277450.proposed_method: A novel neural network framework will be developed in which layers operate on multivectors within the Clifford algebra, parameterized to be equivariant under the action of the Clifford group. The method leverages the twisted conjugation action of the Clifford group, which acts as an orthogonal automorphism on the entire Clifford algebra, respecting both multivector grading and the geometric product. Neural network layers will be constructed as polynomials in multivectors, with grade projections and interaction terms (such as geometric products) parameterized to ensure equivariance. Both linear and higher-order (e.g., quadratic) layers will be implemented, with normalization and nonlinearity schemes designed to maintain numerical stability and equivariance. Data will be embedded into the appropriate grades of the Clifford algebra (e.g., scalars, vectors), and outputs will be projected back for comparison with ground truth.
56c679a0d5fce962e1c09db6d762e4024e277450.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of geometric and physical tasks spanning different group symmetries and dimensions. These include: (1) O(3) signed volume prediction for 3D tetrahedra, (2) O(5) convex hull volume estimation and regression tasks in five dimensions, (3) E(3) n-body simulation for charged particle dynamics, and (4) O(1,3) Lorentz-equivariant top quark jet tagging in high-energy physics. Baselines will include scalarization methods (e.g., EGNN, GVP, VN), steerable methods (e.g., SE(3)-Transformer, LGN, LorentzNet), and standard MLPs, with parameter budgets and architectures matched as closely as possible. Evaluation metrics will include mean squared error for regression tasks, classification accuracy, AUC, and background rejection rates for classification tasks. Experimental setups will ensure fair comparison by controlling for data regime and model capacity.
56c679a0d5fce962e1c09db6d762e4024e277450.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the use of the Clifford group action on Clifford algebras to construct equivariant neural network layers, enabling direct operation on multivectors without the need for alternative bases (e.g., spherical harmonics) or Clebsch-Gordan coefficients. This framework generalizes equivariant neural networks to arbitrary dimensions and metric signatures, supports expressive parameterizations via polynomials in multivectors, and allows for the modeling of exotic geometric objects (e.g., pseudovectors). The method is empirically demonstrated to achieve state-of-the-art or competitive performance on a diverse set of tasks, often surpassing specialized or highly optimized baselines.

56c88734f94fa6f9ee5ffce31df4ad004710d462.title: Acquisition Conditioned Oracle for Nongreedy Active Feature Acquisition
56c88734f94fa6f9ee5ffce31df4ad004710d462.research_question: How can a deployable, non-greedy, and data-driven oracle be developed for active feature acquisition (AFA) that efficiently determines which features to sequentially acquire in order to minimize acquisition costs while maintaining high predictive accuracy or maximizing decision outcomes, especially in high-dimensional and real-world settings?
56c88734f94fa6f9ee5ffce31df4ad004710d462.hypothesis: A nonparametric, acquisition-conditioned oracle (ACO) that operates only on acquired features and leverages conditional dependencies can outperform existing deep learning and greedy methods for active feature acquisition, both in prediction and decision-making tasks, by enabling more effective, instance-specific, and cost-aware feature selection.
56c88734f94fa6f9ee5ffce31df4ad004710d462.proposed_method: A novel, non-greedy oracle framework called the Acquisition Conditioned Oracle (ACO) will be developed for active feature acquisition. The ACO will sequentially determine which subset of features to acquire by minimizing an expected loss function (e.g., cross-entropy or MSE) plus a cost term, conditioned only on the features already acquired for a given instance. The method will avoid 'cheating' by not using unacquired features or labels during inference, instead leveraging the conditional distribution of unobserved features and labels given the observed subset. In practice, the conditional expectations required by the ACO will be approximated using nonparametric techniques such as k-nearest neighbors in the training data, and the search over possible feature subsets will be made tractable by random subsampling or discrete optimization heuristics. Additionally, a parametric policy (e.g., neural network or gradient boosted trees) will be trained via behavioral cloning to imitate the ACO policy, enabling efficient deployment without storing the full dataset.
56c88734f94fa6f9ee5ffce31df4ad004710d462.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets, including the CUBE-σ synthetic dataset, UCI ML repository datasets, and downsampled as well as full-dimensional MNIST. The ACO and its parametric student will be compared against state-of-the-art AFA baselines such as JAFA, GSMRL, EDDI, and GSM+Greedy. Evaluation metrics will include predictive accuracy as a function of the number of acquired features, acquisition cost, and, for decision-making tasks, agreement with optimal policies and estimated value functions. The experimental setup will involve varying the acquisition cost parameter to generate trade-off curves, using cross-entropy or MSE loss for prediction, and k-nearest neighbors (with k tuned per dataset) for nonparametric conditional estimation. For decision-making, contextual bandit settings and synthetic environments with known optimal policies will be used to evaluate the ability of the method to maximize expected outcomes.
56c88734f94fa6f9ee5ffce31df4ad004710d462.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first deployable, non-greedy oracle for active feature acquisition that operates only on information available to the agent, making it suitable for real-world deployment and imitation learning. It avoids the need for complex deep reinforcement learning or generative surrogate models, instead leveraging straightforward nonparametric approximations. The method generalizes AFA to decision-making tasks, not just prediction, and demonstrates superior empirical performance to state-of-the-art deep learning-based methods, even in high-dimensional settings. The framework also provides a principled way to train parametric policies via behavioral cloning from a non-cheating oracle, and extends AFA to maximize decision outcomes in contextual bandit and treatment recommendation scenarios.

56d89b44a9fbf7392a0c4a5fb46ef221f04ba5e5.title: Self-Supervised Learning of Motion Concepts by Optimizing Counterfactuals
56d89b44a9fbf7392a0c4a5fb46ef221f04ba5e5.research_question: How can motion concepts such as optical flow and occlusion be learned in a self-supervised manner from real-world videos, without relying on labeled data or hand-crafted heuristics, and how can these representations be leveraged to improve motion estimation performance in challenging, real-world scenarios?
56d89b44a9fbf7392a0c4a5fb46ef221f04ba5e5.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a self-supervised framework that optimizes learnable, context-specific counterfactual perturbations—rather than relying on fixed, hand-designed interventions or photometric heuristics—can extract motion information from pre-trained video models, enabling accurate flow and occlusion estimation from unlabeled, in-the-wild video data.
56d89b44a9fbf7392a0c4a5fb46ef221f04ba5e5.proposed_method: A novel self-supervised approach, Opt-CWM, is developed to estimate motion (optical flow) and occlusion by optimizing counterfactual probes on top of a pre-trained next-frame video prediction model. The method parameterizes a counterfactual perturbation generator as a neural network that produces image- and position-specific perturbations (modeled as colored Gaussians) for any target pixel. These perturbations are applied to the input frame, and the difference between the model's predictions on perturbed and unperturbed inputs is used to infer motion or occlusion. The perturbation generator is trained in a self-supervised fashion by coupling it with a sparse flow-conditioned next-frame predictor, optimizing both via reconstruction loss to ensure that only correct flow vectors enable accurate future frame prediction. Additional enhancements include multi-mask inference (averaging over multiple random masks) and multi-scale refinement (iteratively refining predictions on image crops) to further improve accuracy and robustness.
56d89b44a9fbf7392a0c4a5fb46ef221f04ba5e5.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on several real-world and synthetic benchmarks, including TAP-Vid DAVIS, TAP-Vid Kinetics, DAVIS, and Kubric datasets. The evaluation protocols include both the TAP-Vid First protocol (tracking points from first visibility through occlusion across large frame gaps) and a Constant Frame Gap (CFG) protocol (fixed 5-frame intervals), with metrics such as Average Jaccard, Average Distance, percentage of points within a pixel threshold, Occlusion Accuracy, and Occlusion F1. Baselines include supervised optical flow models (RAFT, SEA-RAFT), self-supervised flow models (SMURF), and recent self-supervised correspondence/point tracking methods (Doduo, GMRW, CWM). The proposed method is evaluated at high input resolutions with multi-mask and multi-scale inference, and ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of learned versus fixed perturbations, input resolution, and refinement strategies. Further, a distillation experiment is performed by training a compact RAFT-type architecture on pseudo-labels generated by Opt-CWM to demonstrate scalability and efficiency.
56d89b44a9fbf7392a0c4a5fb46ef221f04ba5e5.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a generic, learnable counterfactual perturbation generator for extracting motion information from pre-trained video models, eliminating the need for scenario-specific heuristics or labeled flow data. The approach leverages a self-supervised, end-to-end optimization framework that couples perturbation learning with a sparse flow-conditioned next-frame predictor, ensuring that perturbations are contextually appropriate and effective for motion extraction. This method achieves state-of-the-art performance on challenging real-world motion benchmarks, outperforms both supervised and unsupervised baselines in key scenarios, and demonstrates extensibility via distillation into efficient architectures. The core innovations—parameterizing and optimizing counterfactual probes and bootstrapping their learning through reconstruction objectives—are broadly applicable to extracting a variety of visual properties beyond motion.

56deece9e73c1523d467fdbbc8b7685b0a1c681e.title: Non-Adversarial Inverse Reinforcement Learning via Successor Feature Matching
56deece9e73c1523d467fdbbc8b7685b0a1c681e.research_question: Can a non-adversarial, state-only approach to inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) effectively recover expert behavior from demonstrations without requiring action labels, and how does this approach compare to existing adversarial and non-adversarial methods in terms of stability, efficiency, and performance?
56deece9e73c1523d467fdbbc8b7685b0a1c681e.hypothesis: A non-adversarial IRL method based on successor feature matching, which directly aligns the expected features of the agent and expert using policy gradients and does not require expert action labels, will achieve state-of-the-art imitation learning performance, even from a single demonstration, while offering improved stability and computational efficiency compared to adversarial approaches.
56deece9e73c1523d467fdbbc8b7685b0a1c681e.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces Successor Feature Matching (SFM), a non-adversarial IRL algorithm that leverages the linear factorization of the return as the inner product of successor features and a reward vector. The approach estimates the expected cumulative sum of features using successor features, which are learned via temporal-difference learning. The policy is optimized by direct policy gradient descent on the gap between the agent's and expert's successor features, using a closed-form witness vector derived from the difference in these features. Base feature representations are learned jointly with the policy using various unsupervised or self-supervised objectives, such as forward dynamics, inverse dynamics, autoencoding, or Hilbert representations, enabling the method to operate in state-only settings without access to expert actions. The method integrates seamlessly with off-the-shelf actor-critic RL algorithms, replacing standard actor and critic losses with SFM-specific objectives.
56deece9e73c1523d467fdbbc8b7685b0a1c681e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 10 environments from the DeepMind Control Suite, focusing on the single-demonstration imitation learning regime. The method will be compared against a range of baselines, including offline behavior cloning (BC), non-adversarial IRL (IQ-Learn), and state-only adversarial IRL methods (OPOLO, MM, GAIfO). Evaluation metrics will include mean normalized return, optimality gap, and interquartile mean (IQM), with results averaged over 10 random seeds and reported with 95% confidence intervals. The policy optimization will utilize both strong (TD7) and weaker (TD3) RL optimizers to assess robustness, and ablations will be performed to evaluate the impact of different base feature learning strategies. All methods will be trained for 1 million environment steps, with expert demonstrations collected from a TD3-trained agent.
56deece9e73c1523d467fdbbc8b7685b0a1c681e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first non-adversarial, state-only interactive IRL method capable of learning from a single expert demonstration without requiring action labels or costly bi-level adversarial optimization. The method introduces a direct policy gradient update for successor feature matching, enabling stable and efficient imitation learning with any standard RL algorithm. By jointly learning base feature representations from raw observations, the method eliminates the need for pre-specified reward function classes and extends applicability to settings where only state information is available, such as video or motion-capture demonstrations. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior performance and robustness compared to both adversarial and non-adversarial baselines.

56e952fd463accff09cf2e35432aaabd7c7c57f3.title: MQuAKE: Assessing Knowledge Editing in Language Models via Multi-Hop Questions
56e952fd463accff09cf2e35432aaabd7c7c57f3.research_question: How can knowledge editing in large language models be evaluated and improved to ensure that updates to factual knowledge propagate correctly to entailed, multi-hop questions, rather than only affecting direct recall of edited facts?
56e952fd463accff09cf2e35432aaabd7c7c57f3.hypothesis: Existing knowledge editing methods for language models are insufficient for ensuring that edits propagate to multi-hop, entailed questions, and a memory-based approach that explicitly stores and reasons over edited facts will significantly improve multi-hop consistency after edits.
56e952fd463accff09cf2e35432aaabd7c7c57f3.proposed_method: A new benchmark, MQUAKE, will be constructed to evaluate knowledge editing in language models using multi-hop questions that require reasoning over chains of facts, both before and after factual edits. The methodology involves building two datasets: MQUAKE-CF, which uses counterfactual edits, and MQUAKE-T, which uses real-world temporal updates, both based on chains of Wikidata triples. A novel memory-based editing approach, MeLLo, will be developed that keeps the base language model frozen, stores all edits in an explicit external memory, and decomposes multi-hop questions into sub-questions. At inference, MeLLo iteratively generates tentative answers to sub-questions, retrieves relevant edited facts from memory using a retrieval model, and prompts the language model to self-check for consistency and update answers as needed. This approach requires no additional training and is compatible with both white-box and black-box LMs.
56e952fd463accff09cf2e35432aaabd7c7c57f3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the MQUAKE-CF and MQUAKE-T datasets, which contain thousands of multi-hop questions constructed from Wikidata, with edits sampled either counterfactually or from real-world changes. Baseline knowledge editing methods such as fine-tuning, MEND, ROME, and MEMIT will be compared against the proposed MeLLo approach, using language models including GPT-J, Vicuna-7B, and GPT-3.5. Evaluation metrics will include edit-wise success rate (recall of edited facts), instance-wise accuracy (recall of all single-hop facts in a chain), and multi-hop accuracy (correct answers to multi-hop questions). Experiments will test both single and batched edits, and will use both standard and chain-of-thought prompting to assess reasoning abilities.
56e952fd463accff09cf2e35432aaabd7c7c57f3.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces MQUAKE, the first benchmark specifically designed to assess whether knowledge edits in language models propagate to entailed multi-hop questions. It claims that existing editing methods fail catastrophically on this task, despite high recall on direct edits. The proposed MeLLo method is novel in its use of explicit memory for storing edits, iterative sub-question decomposition, and self-consistency checking, enabling scalable, faithful knowledge editing without retraining or weight updates. MeLLo is claimed to outperform prior methods by a large margin on multi-hop consistency, especially when scaled to large LMs.

570a4a186f348ebad33816afc82c16acabd07122.title: DIMES: A Differentiable Meta Solver for Combinatorial Optimization Problems
570a4a186f348ebad33816afc82c16acabd07122.research_question: How can combinatorial optimization problems, particularly those involving large-scale graphs such as the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) and Maximal Independent Set (MIS), be solved efficiently and scalably using neural approaches without relying on costly decoding or extensive supervised data?
570a4a186f348ebad33816afc82c16acabd07122.hypothesis: A compact, continuous parameterization of the solution space, combined with a meta-learning framework for initialization and fine-tuning, enables scalable, efficient, and effective neural solvers for large-scale combinatorial optimization problems, outperforming existing deep reinforcement learning and supervised learning baselines.
570a4a186f348ebad33816afc82c16acabd07122.proposed_method: A novel framework, DIMES (Differentiable Meta Solver), is proposed to address scalability in combinatorial optimization. The method parameterizes the solution space using a continuous and differentiable vector, representing the underlying distribution over feasible solutions. This continuous representation enables massively parallel sampling and efficient REINFORCE-based training without the need for costly autoregressive decoding or iterative refinement. An auxiliary distribution is designed for each problem (e.g., chain-rule-based autoregressive models for TSP and MIS), allowing efficient sampling and gradient estimation.
