Additionally, a meta-learning framework inspired by Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML) is incorporated, where a graph neural network is trained across a collection of problem instances to learn generalizable initialization, followed by instance-specific fine-tuning using reinforcement learning updates.
570a4a186f348ebad33816afc82c16acabd07122.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on large-scale benchmark datasets for TSP (TSP-500, TSP-1000, TSP-10000) and MIS (SATLIB, ER-[700-800], ER-[9000-11000]). Training instances are generated on-the-fly for TSP, and standard datasets are used for MIS, with random splits for training and testing. DIMES is compared against traditional operations research solvers (e.g., Concorde, Gurobi, LKH-3), heuristic methods (Nearest/Random/Farthest Insertion), and state-of-the-art learning-based methods (EAN, AM, GCN, POMO+EAS, Att-GCN, Intel, DGL, LwD, S2V-DQN). Evaluation metrics include average solution quality (tour length for TSP, independent set size for MIS), relative performance drop, and inference latency. Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of meta-learning, fine-tuning strategies, and parameterization choices. Decoding strategies such as greedy decoding, sampling, and Monte Carlo Tree Search are also evaluated.
570a4a186f348ebad33816afc82c16acabd07122.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a compact, continuous, and differentiable parameterization of the solution space for combinatorial optimization, enabling efficient parallel sampling and gradient-based optimization. The integration of a meta-learning framework for initialization and fine-tuning across problem instances is novel in the context of combinatorial optimization. Unlike prior methods, the approach does not require ground-truth solutions or costly supervised data, and it scales to graphs with tens of thousands of nodes. The unified framework is generalizable to a broad class of combinatorial optimization problems where solutions can be represented by binary variables, and it achieves superior or competitive performance compared to both traditional and recent neural solvers.

570e4fec8c8f1c96b76accbb07d40e0528aafb4a.title: Large Language Models Are Not Robust Multiple Choice Selectors
570e4fec8c8f1c96b76accbb07d40e0528aafb4a.research_question: How can the robustness of large language models (LLMs) to option position changes in multiple choice question (MCQ) evaluation be improved, and what are the underlying causes of selection bias in LLMs when answering MCQs?
570e4fec8c8f1c96b76accbb07d40e0528aafb4a.hypothesis: Selection bias in LLMs, particularly their tendency to favor specific option IDs in MCQs, primarily arises from intrinsic token bias rather than position bias, and can be effectively mitigated through a label-free, inference-time debiasing method that estimates and removes the model's prior bias for option IDs.
570e4fec8c8f1c96b76accbb07d40e0528aafb4a.proposed_method: A novel debiasing framework, PriDe (Debiasing with Prior Estimation), will be developed to enhance LLM robustness in MCQ tasks. The method decomposes the model's observed prediction distribution into a prior distribution over option IDs and a debiased distribution over option contents. PriDe first estimates the prior bias by permuting option contents on a small subset of test samples, requiring no sample labels and minimal computational overhead. The estimated prior is then applied to debias the predictions for the remaining samples, effectively separating and removing the influence of the model's prior bias for option IDs from the overall prediction. This approach is designed to be interpretable, computationally efficient, and transferable across domains.
570e4fec8c8f1c96b76accbb07d40e0528aafb4a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three widely used MCQ benchmarks: MMLU, ARC-Challenge, and CommonsenseQA, covering a diverse range of domains and option counts (4 or 5 options). A total of 20 LLMs from various families and sizes, including open-source models (LLaMA, Vicuna, Falcon) and commercial APIs (gpt-3.5-turbo), will be evaluated. Baselines will include standard MCQ prompting, permutation-based debiasing (Full and Cyclic Permutation), and simple prompting strategies such as explicit debiasing instructions and Chain-of-Thought. Evaluation metrics will focus on selection bias (measured by the standard deviation of recall across option IDs) and accuracy, under both 0-shot and 5-shot settings. Cross-domain transferability of the estimated priors and computational efficiency will also be assessed.
570e4fec8c8f1c96b76accbb07d40e0528aafb4a.novelty_claims: The proposed research identifies and systematically analyzes the ubiquitous selection bias in LLMs for MCQ tasks, attributing it primarily to token bias rather than position bias. PriDe introduces a label-free, inference-time debiasing method that achieves interpretable, efficient, and transferable debiasing by estimating and removing prior bias for option IDs. The approach is claimed to outperform strong permutation-based baselines, particularly in low-cost scenarios, and to provide robust improvements in both bias mitigation and model performance across diverse tasks and domains.

57196d1c3a7d8a3c8b074886858969dc16cb61d4.title: Towards Better Out-of-Distribution Generalization of Neural Algorithmic Reasoning Tasks
57196d1c3a7d8a3c8b074886858969dc16cb61d4.research_question: How can out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization in neural algorithmic reasoning tasks be improved, particularly for deep neural networks learning classical algorithms from input-output pairs, given the unique challenges of distribution shift, dataset representativeness, and model selection in this domain?
57196d1c3a7d8a3c8b074886858969dc16cb61d4.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that addressing input distribution shifts, improving data generation strategies, and developing novel neural architectures—such as attention-based processors and hybrid GNN models—will significantly enhance OOD generalization in neural algorithmic reasoning tasks compared to existing baselines.
57196d1c3a7d8a3c8b074886858969dc16cb61d4.proposed_method: The proposed approach involves a multi-faceted strategy to improve OOD generalization in neural algorithmic reasoning. First, the training dataset size and diversity will be substantially increased to mitigate overfitting and ensure a more representative sampling of graph structures. Second, a new node positional encoding strategy will be adopted, wherein random scalar indices are used during training to reduce reliance on fixed index differences and better preserve ordering information, thereby alleviating distribution shift issues. Third, an attention-based 2-Weisfeiler-Lehman (2WL) graph neural network processor will be designed, which operates on the line graph of the input, treating edges as nodes and leveraging transformer-based attention mechanisms to capture higher-order relationships. Finally, a hybrid processor will be constructed by combining the message-passing GNN (MPNN-G) and the 2WL processor, with node and edge representations averaged at each processing step to leverage their complementary strengths.
57196d1c3a7d8a3c8b074886858969dc16cb61d4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the CLRS benchmark, which consists of 30 classical algorithmic reasoning tasks represented as graphs with node/edge/graph-level features and outputs. Several controlled dataset configurations will be created, including K-regular graphs to disentangle the effects of graph size and degree distribution shifts (L-CLRS-Len, L-CLRS-Deg, L-CLRS-Len-Deg). Baseline processors such as MPNN-FC, MPNN-G, PGN, and GAT will be compared against the proposed 2WL and hybrid processors. Evaluation metrics will include both node-level and stricter graph-level accuracy, with OOD performance measured on test graphs that differ in size and/or degree distribution from the training set. Ablation studies will assess the impact of positional encoding strategies and processor architectures.
57196d1c3a7d8a3c8b074886858969dc16cb61d4.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces several novel contributions: (1) a systematic analysis of OOD generalization challenges unique to neural algorithmic reasoning, (2) a new random scalar positional encoding strategy to mitigate input distribution shift, (3) the design of an attention-based 2WL processor that extends GNN expressivity via higher-order message passing, and (4) a hybrid processor architecture that combines complementary strengths of message-passing and attention-based models, achieving superior OOD generalization across a broad set of algorithmic tasks.

5741128f53a1a9978e8c705dc27994bd92e1af7e.title: Minimax rates for heterogeneous causal effect estimation.
5741128f53a1a9978e8c705dc27994bd92e1af7e.research_question: What are the fundamental statistical limits for estimating heterogeneous causal effects (CATE) in nonparametric models, and can estimators be constructed that achieve these optimal rates under minimal smoothness assumptions?
5741128f53a1a9978e8c705dc27994bd92e1af7e.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the minimax rate of convergence for CATE estimation in Hölder-smooth nonparametric models can be precisely characterized, and that a local polynomial estimator can be constructed to achieve this rate under suitable conditions.
5741128f53a1a9978e8c705dc27994bd92e1af7e.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed to derive minimax lower bounds for the estimation of conditional average treatment effects (CATE) under a nonparametric model where the CATE, outcome regression, and propensity score functions are Hölder-smooth. The lower bound will be established using a localized version of the method of fuzzy hypotheses, combining constructions from nonparametric regression and functional estimation. Subsequently, a new estimator based on a local polynomial R-Learner will be proposed, leveraging localized higher-order influence function techniques. The estimator will be analyzed to determine under what high-level conditions it attains the minimax optimal rate, with particular attention to the smoothness of the covariate density and nuisance functions.
5741128f53a1a9978e8c705dc27994bd92e1af7e.experiment_details: Theoretical experiments will involve constructing pairs of mixture distributions that are statistically indistinguishable but have maximally separated CATE values, enabling the derivation of minimax lower bounds. The analysis will focus on mean absolute error at a fixed point in the covariate space, with smoothness parameters for the CATE, regression, and propensity score functions varied systematically. The minimax rates will be compared to those from standard nonparametric regression and functional estimation, and the tightness of the lower bounds will be confirmed by analyzing the proposed local polynomial estimator. No real-world datasets or empirical baselines are specified, as the focus is on theoretical minimax rates and estimator properties.
5741128f53a1a9978e8c705dc27994bd92e1af7e.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first comprehensive minimax theory for heterogeneous causal effect estimation in Hölder-smooth nonparametric models, deriving explicit lower bounds for the rate of convergence. A novel local polynomial R-Learner estimator is constructed and shown to achieve these rates under certain conditions, demonstrating minimax optimality. The minimax rate reveals a non-standard elbow phenomenon and an interpolation between nonparametric regression and functional estimation rates, providing new insights into the statistical nature of CATE as a hybrid estimand. The approach clarifies the fundamental limits of CATE estimation and establishes benchmarks for future methodological developments.

574130ae32cc7e55971a6382c344953906cdd707.title: INCLUDE: Evaluating Multilingual Language Understanding with Regional Knowledge
574130ae32cc7e55971a6382c344953906cdd707.research_question: How can the evaluation of multilingual language models be improved to more accurately reflect their understanding and reasoning capabilities across diverse languages and regional knowledge contexts, particularly in low- and medium-resource languages?
574130ae32cc7e55971a6382c344953906cdd707.hypothesis: Current multilingual language model benchmarks, which often rely on translations from English and lack regionally and culturally grounded content, do not sufficiently capture the true capabilities of language models in real-world, regional contexts. A benchmark constructed from native, region-specific exam sources will provide a more rigorous and representative evaluation of multilingual language understanding.
574130ae32cc7e55971a6382c344953906cdd707.proposed_method: A comprehensive multilingual evaluation benchmark will be constructed by collecting multiple-choice question-answer pairs from academic, professional, and regional license examinations originally authored in the official languages of 52 countries. The data collection pipeline will involve automated extraction from diverse formats (e.g., PDFs, HTML forms), followed by manual verification and correction by native speakers to ensure data quality and accurate representation of regional and cultural knowledge. Each question will be annotated with metadata including language, topic, academic level, and regional specificity (e.g., region-agnostic, explicitly regional, cultural, or implicitly regional). The resulting benchmark will span 44 languages and 15 scripts, with a focus on both high-resource and underrepresented languages, and will be released in both full and resource-efficient subsets for broad accessibility.
574130ae32cc7e55971a6382c344953906cdd707.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate a range of state-of-the-art and open-source language models, including GPT-4o, Llama-3.1, Aya-expanse, Qwen2.5, Mistral, and Gemma, using the constructed benchmark. Evaluation will be performed using standardized multiple-choice formats with four answer options, employing both in-language and English prompts, as well as regional prompt variants. Both zero-shot and 5-shot settings will be tested, with additional experiments on prompt length and output formatting. Performance will be measured primarily by accuracy, with stratified analyses by language, academic domain, and regional knowledge category. The evaluation will also include analysis of model performance on languages and scripts seen and unseen during pretraining, and will utilize both the full benchmark and smaller subsets (INCLUDE-BASE and INCLUDE-LITE) to accommodate different resource constraints.
574130ae32cc7e55971a6382c344953906cdd707.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark is the largest and most diverse collection of multilingual exam data to date, covering 44 languages and 58 knowledge domains with a strong emphasis on regional and cultural knowledge. Unlike prior benchmarks, it avoids translation artifacts by sourcing questions natively and includes extensive manual quality control by native speakers. The benchmark enables rigorous, fine-grained evaluation of multilingual language models in real-world, region-specific contexts, addressing critical gaps in current evaluation practices and supporting the development of more equitable and capable AI systems for underserved language communities.

57431570f624069de2fa99429c7c3d3760271bc2.title: TraceVLA: Visual Trace Prompting Enhances Spatial-Temporal Awareness for Generalist Robotic Policies
57431570f624069de2fa99429c7c3d3760271bc2.research_question: How can spatial-temporal awareness in generalist vision-language-action (VLA) models for robotics be enhanced to improve action prediction and generalization across diverse manipulation tasks and environmental conditions?
57431570f624069de2fa99429c7c3d3760271bc2.hypothesis: Incorporating visual trace prompting—where state-action trajectories are visually encoded and overlaid on robot observation images—into VLA models will significantly improve spatial-temporal reasoning, leading to better action prediction and generalization in robotic manipulation tasks compared to existing approaches.
57431570f624069de2fa99429c7c3d3760271bc2.proposed_method: A novel visual trace prompting technique will be developed to encode the robot's historical state-action trajectories as visual overlays on observation images. Dense point tracking (using an efficient algorithm such as Co-Tracker) will be applied to sequences of past frames to extract active point trajectories, which are then overlaid onto the current observation image to create a visual trace prompt. Both the original and the trace-overlaid images will be input to the VLA model, separated by a special token, and concatenated with language instructions. The model architecture will be based on existing large-scale VLA backbones (such as OpenVLA and Phi-3-Vision), which will be fine-tuned on a large dataset of robot manipulation trajectories annotated with visual traces. A dropout mechanism will be introduced during training to ensure robustness when visual traces are unavailable at inference time.
57431570f624069de2fa99429c7c3d3760271bc2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both simulated and real-world robotic manipulation tasks. The primary simulation environment will be SimplerEnv, featuring 137 configurations with diverse environmental variations (lighting, backgrounds, distractors, camera poses, and table textures). Real-world evaluations will use a WidowX-250 robot across 8 manipulation tasks, including 4 unseen tasks for generalization assessment. The models will be fine-tuned on a dataset of approximately 150,000 robot trajectories with visual trace annotations, sourced from BridgeData-v2, Google RT1 Robot datasets, and custom demonstrations. Baselines will include OpenVLA, OpenVLA-Phi3, Octo-Base, and RT1-X. Evaluation metrics will focus on task success rates, with ablation studies comparing visual trace prompting to alternative history encoding methods (e.g., sequential frame stacking and text-based trace descriptions). Computational efficiency, memory usage, and inference speed will also be measured.
57431570f624069de2fa99429c7c3d3760271bc2.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces visual trace prompting as a new method to encode spatial-temporal history directly into VLA model inputs, enabling more effective spatial-temporal reasoning for robotic manipulation. This method is claimed to significantly outperform existing generalist VLA policies in both simulated and real-world tasks, demonstrating robust generalization across diverse embodiments and scenarios. The research also provides a large-scale dataset with visual trace annotations and presents both a state-of-the-art 7B model and a compact, efficient 4B model, facilitating broader adoption and fine-tuning on accessible hardware. Ablation studies will validate the superiority of visual trace prompting over frame stacking and text-based alternatives, and the method is designed to be scalable and compatible with existing VLM architectures.

575425e5a33970faeea370a950467c9d852e2725.title: Grokking at the Edge of Numerical Stability
575425e5a33970faeea370a950467c9d852e2725.research_question: What are the underlying mechanisms that cause delayed generalization (grokking) in deep learning models, and how can generalization be achieved without reliance on regularization techniques such as weight decay?
575425e5a33970faeea370a950467c9d852e2725.hypothesis: Delayed generalization in grokking tasks is caused by numerical instabilities, specifically Softmax Collapse (SC) due to floating point errors, which are themselves induced by Naïve Loss Minimization (NLM) dynamics that scale logits without improving generalization. Mitigating SC and NLM will enable grokking without the need for explicit regularization.
575425e5a33970faeea370a950467c9d852e2725.proposed_method: A two-pronged approach is proposed to address the mechanisms preventing grokking without regularization. First, a novel activation function, StableMax, will be developed as a numerically stable alternative to Softmax, designed to prevent absorption errors and SC by using a ramp-like function instead of the exponential in the Softmax calculation. Second, a new optimizer, ⊥Grad, will be introduced, which projects the gradient onto the subspace orthogonal to the current weight direction, thereby eliminating updates in the NLM direction that only scale logits. These interventions will be implemented in standard deep learning architectures, including multi-layer perceptrons and transformers, and will be compatible with both AdamW and SGD optimization schemes.
575425e5a33970faeea370a950467c9d852e2725.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on canonical grokking benchmarks, including modular arithmetic tasks (e.g., addition, multiplication, subtraction modulo 113), the Sparse Parity problem, and a low-data regime of MNIST. Models will include 2-hidden-layer MLPs of width 200 and one-layer transformers with 4 attention heads. Both baseline optimizers (AdamW, SGD) and their ⊥Grad variants will be tested, with and without regularization. Evaluation metrics will include training and test accuracy, fraction of samples experiencing Softmax Collapse, and weight norm evolution. Floating point precision (float16, float32, float64) will be varied to assess the impact of numerical stability. Comparisons will be made to existing regularization-based methods and to MSE loss, and ablation studies will be performed to isolate the effects of StableMax and ⊥Grad.
575425e5a33970faeea370a950467c9d852e2725.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces StableMax, a numerically stable alternative to Softmax that prevents Softmax Collapse and enables grokking without regularization, as well as ⊥Grad, an optimizer that directly mitigates Naïve Loss Minimization and accelerates generalization. This framework provides a new explanation for delayed generalization and the necessity of regularization in grokking, unifying and extending previous findings. The approach also offers a principled method for achieving grokking in settings where it was previously absent, and explains the effectiveness of existing grokking-inducing techniques through the lens of numerical stability and gradient dynamics.

57552695dea7d3745255d30a77a7910dfda51af9.title: Scalable Sobolev IPM for Probability Measures on a Graph
57552695dea7d3745255d30a77a7910dfda51af9.research_question: How can integral probability metrics, specifically Sobolev IPM, be efficiently and scalably computed for probability measures supported on graph-structured spaces, and what are the practical benefits of such scalable computation in applications such as document classification and topological data analysis?
57552695dea7d3745255d30a77a7910dfda51af9.hypothesis: Introducing a novel regularization for Sobolev IPM, based on an equivalence with a weighted Lp-norm of the critic's derivative and leveraging graph structure, will enable a closed-form, scalable computation of Sobolev IPM, while maintaining its desirable theoretical properties and improving its applicability to large-scale and practical tasks.
57552695dea7d3745255d30a77a7910dfda51af9.proposed_method: A new regularization for Sobolev IPM is proposed by establishing an equivalence between the Sobolev norm of the critic function and a weighted Lp-norm of its graph derivative, where the weight function is derived from the graph structure. The regularized Sobolev IPM constrains the critic within a unit ball defined by this weighted norm, resulting in a closed-form expression for the metric between two probability measures on a graph. The method includes a preprocessing step, independent of the input measures, that computes graph-dependent quantities (such as shortest paths and subgraph supports) to enable efficient evaluation. The approach is further extended by designing positive-definite kernels based on the negative definiteness of the regularized Sobolev IPM, enabling its use in kernel-based machine learning methods. Theoretical analysis establishes metric properties, equivalence to original Sobolev IPM and Sobolev transport, and connections to Wasserstein distances, particularly in tree-structured graphs.
57552695dea7d3745255d30a77a7910dfda51af9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both document classification and topological data analysis tasks. Document datasets such as TWITTER, RECIPE, CLASSIC, and AMAZON will be used, where documents are represented as probability measures over word embeddings (e.g., word2vec vectors). For TDA, datasets like Orbit and MPEG7 will be considered, with objects represented as persistence diagrams (distributions of 2D points). Graphs with varying sizes and structures (e.g., log and sqrt graphs) will be constructed to support the measures. The proposed regularized Sobolev IPM kernels will be compared against baselines including standard optimal transport (OT), tree-Wasserstein (TW), and Sobolev transport (ST) kernels. Evaluation will be performed using kernelized SVM classification accuracy and time consumption for kernel matrix computation. Hyperparameters will be selected via cross-validation, and experiments will include both single-root and sliced (multi-root) variants to assess robustness and scalability.
57552695dea7d3745255d30a77a7910dfda51af9.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel regularization for Sobolev IPM that yields a closed-form, efficiently computable metric for probability measures on graphs, overcoming longstanding computational challenges. The method enables scalable application of Sobolev IPM to large-scale and practical problems, such as document classification and TDA, where previous methods were computationally prohibitive. Theoretical contributions include establishing the metric, negative definiteness, and kernel properties of the regularized Sobolev IPM, as well as explicit connections to Sobolev transport and Wasserstein distances. The approach also provides a general framework that can be extended to non-physical graphs and supports the design of positive-definite, infinitely divisible kernels for use in kernel-based learning.

575bf1f23a19620a8f696a965528e15d4833179a.title: NaturalSpeech 3: Zero-Shot Speech Synthesis with Factorized Codec and Diffusion Models
575bf1f23a19620a8f696a965528e15d4833179a.research_question: How can zero-shot text-to-speech (TTS) synthesis be improved to achieve higher speech quality, similarity, prosody, and intelligibility, particularly by addressing the complex and entangled nature of speech attributes?
575bf1f23a19620a8f696a965528e15d4833179a.hypothesis: Disentangling speech into distinct subspaces representing content, prosody, timbre, and acoustic details, and generating these attributes individually using a factorized codec and diffusion models, will enable more effective zero-shot TTS synthesis with improved quality, similarity, prosody, and intelligibility.
575bf1f23a19620a8f696a965528e15d4833179a.proposed_method: A novel TTS system will be developed that factorizes speech into separate subspaces for content, prosody, timbre, and acoustic details using a neural codec with factorized vector quantization (FACodec). The FACodec will employ a speech encoder, a timbre extractor (Transformer-based), and three factorized vector quantizers for the different attributes, followed by a speech decoder that reconstructs the waveform from the disentangled representations. Attribute disentanglement will be enhanced through information bottlenecks, supervised auxiliary losses (e.g., pitch prediction, phoneme classification, speaker ID), gradient reversal layers to minimize information leakage, and detail dropout to further enforce separation. A factorized diffusion model will then generate each attribute sequentially—duration, prosody, content, and acoustic details—using discrete diffusion processes conditioned on corresponding prompts, with classifier-free guidance for controllability and improved generation quality. The final speech waveform will be reconstructed by combining the generated attributes and decoding them via the codec decoder.
575bf1f23a19620a8f696a965528e15d4833179a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Librilight dataset (60K hours, ~7000 speakers) for training, with evaluation on the LibriSpeech test-clean (multi-speaker, 5.4 hours) and RAVDESS (emotional speech, 24 speakers, 8 emotions) benchmarks. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art TTS systems such as VALL-E, NaturalSpeech2, Voicebox, Mega-TTS2, UniAudio, StyleTTS2, and HierSpeech++. Evaluation metrics will comprise objective measures (speaker similarity via SIM-O/SIM-R, speech quality via UTMOS, robustness via WER, prosody via MCD and MCD-Acc) and subjective measures (comparative mean opinion score (CMOS), similarity mean opinion score (SMOS)), with both human and automatic assessments. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of factorization, classifier-free guidance, and prosody representation. The system will also be scaled to 1B parameters and 200K hours of training data to evaluate scalability.
575bf1f23a19620a8f696a965528e15d4833179a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel factorized codec (FACodec) that explicitly disentangles speech into content, prosody, timbre, and acoustic detail subspaces, enabling divide-and-conquer modeling of speech attributes. A factorized diffusion model is designed to generate each attribute in its respective subspace, allowing for independent control and improved synthesis quality. The methodology enables zero-shot TTS synthesis that achieves human-level naturalness on multi-speaker datasets for the first time, surpassing prior state-of-the-art systems in quality, similarity, prosody, and intelligibility. The framework also demonstrates extensibility to both non-autoregressive and autoregressive generative models, and supports flexible attribute manipulation in a zero-shot manner.

5777270a7f62715aa6ea29e3b3714dd587c85708.title: Refined Convergence Rates for Maximum Likelihood Estimation under Finite Mixture Models
5777270a7f62715aa6ea29e3b3714dd587c85708.research_question: What are the optimal convergence rates for maximum likelihood estimation of parameters in finite mixture models, and how can these rates be more accurately characterized using alternative loss functions beyond the Wasserstein distance?
5777270a7f62715aa6ea29e3b3714dd587c85708.hypothesis: Sharper and potentially heterogeneous convergence rates for parameter estimation in finite mixture models can be achieved by employing loss functions that are stronger than the Wasserstein distance, especially when penalizing the likelihood to discourage vanishing mixing weights.
5777270a7f62715aa6ea29e3b3714dd587c85708.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed for analyzing the convergence rates of maximum likelihood estimators (MLEs) in finite mixture models by introducing and utilizing loss functions that are stronger than the Wasserstein distance. The methodology will include the construction of penalized likelihood functions to prevent vanishing mixing weights, allowing for a more nuanced analysis of the convergence behavior of individual mixture components. The approach will involve defining Voronoi cells based on the true mixing measure's support and constructing loss functions that capture the heterogeneous convergence rates among fitted mixture components. Theoretical analysis will be conducted under both strong and weak identifiability conditions, and the computational complexity of the new loss functions will be compared to that of the Wasserstein metric.
5777270a7f62715aa6ea29e3b3714dd587c85708.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using simulated datasets generated from finite mixture models with varying numbers of components and parameter settings, including both strongly and weakly identifiable cases (e.g., location and location-scale Gaussian mixtures). The performance of the penalized MLE under the proposed loss functions will be compared to the classical Wasserstein distance, with particular attention to the convergence rates of individual mixture components. Evaluation metrics will include the proposed loss functions, Wasserstein distance, and statistical distances such as Hellinger and Total Variation. The experimental setup will ensure that mixing weights are bounded away from zero, and both pointwise and uniform convergence rates will be assessed.
5777270a7f62715aa6ea29e3b3714dd587c85708.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces loss functions that are strictly stronger than the Wasserstein distance for analyzing parameter convergence in finite mixture models, enabling the identification of heterogeneous convergence rates among mixture components. The approach refines existing theoretical results by showing that many mixture parameters can achieve near-parametric convergence rates, even in over-specified models, which contrasts with the pessimistic worst-case rates suggested by prior work. Additionally, the proposed loss functions offer improved computational efficiency over the Wasserstein metric, making them practical for large-scale applications and model selection tasks.

578c6b6461301db73824b90a55b650c9ccff4031.title: Explaining the effects of non-convergent sampling in the training of energy-based models
578c6b6461301db73824b90a55b650c9ccff4031.research_question: What are the effects of using non-convergent Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling during the training of Energy-Based Models (EBMs), and how does this impact the statistical properties of the trained models and the quality of generated samples?
578c6b6461301db73824b90a55b650c9ccff4031.hypothesis: Non-convergent, short-run MCMC sampling during EBM training induces a specific dynamical process that allows the trained model to reproduce empirical statistics of the data through a non-equilibrium mechanism, and this process can be exploited to generate high-quality samples efficiently if the sampling procedure during generation matches that used in training.
578c6b6461301db73824b90a55b650c9ccff4031.proposed_method: A comprehensive analytical and empirical investigation is proposed to quantify and explain the effects of non-convergent MCMC sampling in EBM training. The methodology involves deriving first-principles analytical results for generic EBMs, followed by detailed analysis of solvable models such as the Gaussian model and the Bernoulli Boltzmann machine, where the impact of non-convergent sampling on the learned parameters can be explicitly characterized throughout the training process. The approach includes modeling the sampling process as a finite-time Markov chain, deriving the evolution of model statistics under non-equilibrium conditions, and establishing the conditions under which the trained model matches empirical data statistics. Furthermore, the method extends to numerical experiments on both deep convolutional EBMs and classical Boltzmann machines to validate theoretical predictions.
578c6b6461301db73824b90a55b650c9ccff4031.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. For solvable models, such as the Gaussian and Bernoulli Boltzmann machine, synthetic datasets with known statistics will be used to allow for exact analytical comparison. For deep EBMs, the CIFAR-10 dataset will be employed, using a ConvNet EBM architecture with Langevin MCMC sampling for both training and sample generation. Baselines will include models trained with persistent and convergent MCMC chains, as well as models trained with contrastive divergence. Evaluation metrics will comprise agreement of empirical moments (e.g., covariance, higher-order correlations), Frechet Inception Distance (FID) for image quality, and relative entropy measures. Key experimental setups will involve varying the number of MCMC steps during training and generation, and systematically matching or mismatching these procedures to assess the impact on sample quality and statistical fidelity.
578c6b6461301db73824b90a55b650c9ccff4031.novelty_claims: The proposed research provides a first-principles analytical explanation for the empirical observation that non-convergent, short-run MCMC sampling during EBM training can lead to models that reproduce data statistics through a specific dynamical process, rather than at equilibrium. It establishes that high-quality sample generation is achieved when the sampling procedure during generation mirrors the non-equilibrium dynamics used in training. The work lays the theoretical groundwork for using EBMs as diffusion models and clarifies the limitations of equilibrium-based interpretations for non-convergently trained EBMs. Additionally, the research demonstrates that the memory of the training protocol is encoded in the model, and this can be exploited for efficient sample generation, providing new insights for both interpretive and generative applications of EBMs.

57a53d052ff342f7f78833a256d304d276c1f611.title: On Agnostic PAC Learning in the Small Error Regime
57a53d052ff342f7f78833a256d304d276c1f611.research_question: What is the optimal sample complexity and algorithmic approach for agnostic PAC learning in binary classification, particularly in the regime where the error of the best-in-class hypothesis is small relative to the sample size? Can computationally efficient learners be designed to achieve these optimal rates, and are majority voting-based methods (such as bagging) optimal in this refined agnostic learning framework?
57a53d052ff342f7f78833a256d304d276c1f611.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a carefully constructed aggregation of ERM classifiers, utilizing recursive data splitting and majority voting with tie-breaking mechanisms, can achieve optimal agnostic PAC learning rates in the small error regime, matching known lower bounds up to a small constant factor. Furthermore, it is conjectured that such a learner can be made computationally efficient and that majority voting-based approaches can be near-optimal in this setting.
57a53d052ff342f7f78833a256d304d276c1f611.proposed_method: The proposed method develops a new agnostic PAC learning algorithm for binary classification with a focus on the regime where the best-in-class hypothesis error (τ) is small. The approach recursively splits the training data into multiple disjoint subsets using a hierarchical scheme (with up to 27 splits), and trains ERM classifiers on these subsamples. A majority voting mechanism aggregates the predictions of these ERM classifiers, with an additional tie-breaking ERM trained on the region of disagreement between two independent voting classifiers. The final prediction for a test point is determined by the consensus of the voting classifiers when their confidence is high; otherwise, the tie-breaking ERM's prediction is used. The method is further combined with an existing τ-dependent agnostic learner to yield a best-of-both-worlds result, selecting the best-performing classifier on a held-out validation set.
57a53d052ff342f7f78833a256d304d276c1f611.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic and/or standard PAC learning benchmark datasets, where the hypothesis class H has finite VC dimension d, and the error of the best-in-class hypothesis τ can be controlled or measured. The proposed learner will be compared against standard ERM, bagging, and the recent τ-dependent agnostic learner of Hanneke et al. (2024). Evaluation metrics will include the excess error over τ, sample complexity required to achieve a given error guarantee, and computational efficiency (measured by the number of ERM oracle calls and runtime). The experimental setup will include varying τ in the small error regime (τ ≈ d/m), and results will be reported with high-probability error bounds as a function of τ, d, m, and δ.
57a53d052ff342f7f78833a256d304d276c1f611.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first computationally efficient agnostic PAC learner that achieves optimal error rates in the regime τ = O(d/m), matching known lower bounds up to a constant factor (≤2.1). The algorithm leverages a novel recursive data splitting and aggregation scheme, with a tie-breaking mechanism based on ERM in the region of disagreement, which is not present in prior work. This approach advances the understanding of sample complexity in the small error regime and demonstrates that majority voting-based methods can be near-optimal in this refined agnostic learning framework. The method also improves upon previous learners in the regime τ = o(log^5(m/d)·d/m), and provides a pathway toward closing the remaining gap to the optimal constant factor.

57aba6d26fec16e98895a7ecabac862603ca45ec.title: Bitext Mining Using Distilled Sentence Representations for Low-Resource Languages
57aba6d26fec16e98895a7ecabac862603ca45ec.research_question: How can sentence representation learning and bitext mining be effectively scaled to low-resource languages, particularly for the long tail of African languages, while maintaining high compatibility and performance for downstream tasks such as neural machine translation?
57aba6d26fec16e98895a7ecabac862603ca45ec.hypothesis: Combining supervised teacher-student distillation with self-supervised masked language modeling, and training multiple mutually compatible language- or family-specific encoders, will significantly improve sentence representations and bitext mining quality for low-resource languages compared to existing one-for-all multilingual models.
57aba6d26fec16e98895a7ecabac862603ca45ec.proposed_method: A novel teacher-student training framework will be developed, where the teacher is a strong multilingual sentence encoder and the student is a randomly initialized encoder trained for specific languages or language families. The student will be optimized using a combination of supervised distillation (cosine loss between teacher and student embeddings on parallel bitexts) and self-supervised masked language modeling (MLM) on monolingual data. Separate SentencePiece vocabularies will be used for teacher and student to better accommodate scripts and tokens unique to low-resource languages. Curriculum learning via progressive distillation will be incorporated, incrementally exposing the student to increasing portions of sentence pairs. The student encoders will be transformer-based, and the training will leverage both monolingual and parallel data, with up-sampling for low-resource languages and joint training for related languages.
57aba6d26fec16e98895a7ecabac862603ca45ec.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on up to 50 African languages, many of which are not covered by existing models. Training data will include publicly available bitexts from OPUS and monolingual data from Common Crawl and ParaCrawl, with preprocessing steps such as sentence splitting, script filtering, language identification, and deduplication. Evaluation will focus on multilingual similarity search using the FLORES benchmark (covering 44+ African languages) and xsim error rate as the primary metric. Baselines will include the original LASER encoder and LaBSE, with additional comparison to models trained using only supervised or only self-supervised objectives. The effectiveness of mined bitexts will be validated by training NMT systems (using a 6-layer transformer architecture) and measuring BLEU scores on translation tasks from African languages to English.
57aba6d26fec16e98895a7ecabac862603ca45ec.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a scalable framework for training mutually compatible, language- or family-specific sentence encoders for low-resource languages, moving away from the standard one-for-all multilingual model. It combines supervised distillation with self-supervised MLM and curriculum learning, and leverages language-specific vocabularies and architectures. The approach enables the rapid addition of new languages, including those with unique scripts, and demonstrates substantial improvements in bitext mining and NMT performance for languages previously underserved by existing models.

57b28b74e62cdf1b5d091d8a1c1397e8caef1576.title: Generalized Preference Optimization: A Unified Approach to Offline Alignment
57b28b74e62cdf1b5d091d8a1c1397e8caef1576.research_question: How can offline preference optimization for model alignment be unified under a general framework, and how do different convex loss functions affect regularization and performance trade-offs in offline alignment settings?
57b28b74e62cdf1b5d091d8a1c1397e8caef1576.hypothesis: A unified family of offline preference optimization losses, parameterized by convex functions, can encompass existing and novel algorithms, providing systematic control over regularization strength and performance trade-offs in offline alignment tasks.
57b28b74e62cdf1b5d091d8a1c1397e8caef1576.proposed_method: A generalized preference optimization (GPO) framework will be developed, parameterizing offline preference optimization losses using a broad class of convex functions. This approach will reinterpret preference optimization as a supervised binary classification problem, enabling the use of various convex surrogate losses (e.g., logistic, hinge, squared, exponential, truncated quadratic, Savage) in place of the traditional reward difference or log-ratio difference. The method will analyze the regularization induced by each convex loss, both theoretically (via Taylor expansion and gradient analysis) and empirically, to understand how the choice of loss function and hyperparameters (such as the regularization coefficient) impact the alignment of the learned policy to a reference policy. The framework will recover existing methods such as DPO, IPO, and SLiC as special cases, and introduce new variants by leveraging alternative convex losses from the supervised learning literature.
57b28b74e62cdf1b5d091d8a1c1397e8caef1576.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in both controlled synthetic settings (e.g., bandit problems with a small number of actions) and realistic language modeling tasks, such as LLM summarization using open-source datasets with human feedback (e.g., Stiennon et al., 2020). Different GPO variants, corresponding to different convex losses, will be compared by varying regularization strength (hyperparameter beta) and measuring trade-offs between regularization and policy performance. Evaluation metrics will include KL divergence between the learned and reference policies, the mu-weighted squared loss, and downstream task performance (e.g., summarization quality). Baselines will include existing offline preference optimization methods (DPO, IPO, SLiC), and ablations will be performed to assess the impact of novel convex losses and hyperparameter choices.
57b28b74e62cdf1b5d091d8a1c1397e8caef1576.novelty_claims: The proposed framework provides a unifying perspective on offline preference optimization by parameterizing losses with general convex functions, subsuming existing algorithms and introducing new variants. It systematically connects preference optimization to supervised binary classification, allowing the import of a wide range of convex surrogate losses. The analysis offers new theoretical insights into the regularization mechanisms of offline algorithms, clarifies the relationship between offline regularization and KL divergence, and provides practical guidance for hyperparameter selection. Empirical studies will demonstrate that different GPO variants achieve similar regularization-performance trade-offs, but with distinct optimal hyperparameter regimes, validating theoretical predictions and offering new tools for alignment practitioners.

57e7af0b69325fafb371ef5d502e39ef9c90ef7e.title: Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads
57e7af0b69325fafb371ef5d502e39ef9c90ef7e.research_question: How can the inference speed of large language models (LLMs) be accelerated without compromising generation quality, particularly by reducing the sequential bottleneck of auto-regressive decoding?
57e7af0b69325fafb371ef5d502e39ef9c90ef7e.hypothesis: Introducing multiple parallel decoding heads on top of a backbone LLM, combined with a tree-based attention mechanism and optimized candidate verification schemes, will significantly accelerate LLM inference while maintaining or improving generation quality.
57e7af0b69325fafb371ef5d502e39ef9c90ef7e.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that augments existing LLMs with multiple additional decoding heads, termed MEDUSA heads, attached to the last hidden states of the model. Each head predicts a subsequent token in parallel, enabling the simultaneous generation of multiple candidate continuations at each decoding step. A tree-based attention mechanism is employed to efficiently process and verify these candidates, ensuring that only valid continuations are accepted. Two fine-tuning strategies are developed: MEDUSA-1, which fine-tunes only the MEDUSA heads with a frozen backbone for parameter efficiency and ease of integration, and MEDUSA-2, which jointly fine-tunes both the backbone and MEDUSA heads using a combined loss and staged training to maximize accuracy and speedup. Extensions include a self-distillation pipeline for scenarios lacking training data, and a typical acceptance scheme that replaces rejection sampling to further boost acceptance rates and efficiency.
57e7af0b69325fafb371ef5d502e39ef9c90ef7e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of LLMs, including Vicuna-7B, Vicuna-13B, Vicuna-33B, and Zephyr-7B, covering both publicly and privately fine-tuned models. The evaluation will focus on single-batch inference, representative of local or personal LLM hosting scenarios. Datasets such as ShareGPT and UltraChat will be used for training and self-distillation, with multi-turn conversational benchmarks like MT-Bench serving as the primary evaluation suite. Baselines will include standard Huggingface implementations and speculative decoding with open-source draft models. Evaluation metrics will comprise wall-time speedup (tokens per second), acceleration rate, computational overhead, and generation quality as judged by automated metrics (e.g., GPT-4 scoring on MT-Bench). Ablation studies will assess the impact of tree attention configuration, acceptance schemes, and fine-tuning strategies.
57e7af0b69325fafb371ef5d502e39ef9c90ef7e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach eliminates the need for a separate draft model, enabling seamless integration into existing and distributed LLM systems. MEDUSA introduces a simple yet effective architecture for parallel token prediction using additional decoding heads and a tree-based attention mechanism, which is parameter-efficient and compatible with quantized backbones. The framework supports two distinct fine-tuning strategies to accommodate different resource constraints and use cases. The typical acceptance scheme provides a new, efficient alternative to rejection sampling, further improving decoding speed without sacrificing quality. The self-distillation extension enables training in the absence of original fine-tuning data, broadening applicability. Overall, the method claims substantial inference acceleration (2.3–2.8×) across diverse models and tasks while maintaining or improving output quality.

57e849d0de13ed5f91d086936296721d4ff75a75.title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
57e849d0de13ed5f91d086936296721d4ff75a75.research_question: Can large-scale foundation language models be trained to achieve state-of-the-art performance using only publicly available datasets, while remaining efficient for inference across a range of model sizes?
57e849d0de13ed5f91d086936296721d4ff75a75.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, for a fixed compute budget, smaller language models trained on more data can achieve competitive or superior performance compared to larger models trained on less data, and that using only publicly available data does not significantly hinder model capability.
57e849d0de13ed5f91d086936296721d4ff75a75.proposed_method: A suite of transformer-based language models will be developed, ranging from 7B to 65B parameters, trained exclusively on a diverse mixture of publicly available datasets. The training corpus will include large-scale web crawls (CommonCrawl, C4), code (GitHub), encyclopedic and academic content (Wikipedia, ArXiv), books (Gutenberg, Books3), and question-answer forums (StackExchange), totaling approximately 1.4 trillion tokens. The architecture will incorporate recent advances such as pre-layer normalization (RMSNorm), SwiGLU activation functions, and rotary positional embeddings (RoPE), with careful deduplication and filtering of training data for quality and diversity. Training will utilize the AdamW optimizer with cosine learning rate scheduling, large batch sizes (up to 4M tokens), and memory-efficient implementations of causal attention and activation checkpointing to enable efficient scaling across thousands of GPUs.
57e849d0de13ed5f91d086936296721d4ff75a75.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate the resulting models on a wide range of zero-shot and few-shot tasks, including commonsense reasoning (BoolQ, PIQA, SIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC, OBQA), closed-book question answering (NaturalQuestions, TriviaQA), reading comprehension (RACE), mathematical reasoning (MATH, GSM8k), code generation (HumanEval, MBPP), and massive multitask language understanding (MMLU). Performance will be compared against leading proprietary and open-source models such as GPT-3, Gopher, Chinchilla, PaLM, OPT, and BLOOM, using standardized evaluation metrics (e.g., accuracy, exact match, pass@k). Additional analyses will include instruction finetuning, bias and toxicity assessments (CrowS-Pairs, WinoGender, RealToxicityPrompts, TruthfulQA), and carbon footprint estimation. Models will be benchmarked for both training efficiency and inference cost, with detailed reporting of hyperparameters, training curves, and ablation studies where appropriate.
57e849d0de13ed5f91d086936296721d4ff75a75.novelty_claims: The proposed work claims novelty in demonstrating that state-of-the-art large language models can be trained exclusively on publicly available data, achieving competitive or superior performance to proprietary models of much larger size. The approach introduces an efficient, scalable training pipeline with architectural and optimization improvements, and provides open access to all trained models for the research community. The work further claims to democratize access to high-performing language models by enabling their deployment on commodity hardware, and to provide the first comprehensive analysis of bias, toxicity, and environmental impact for such open-source models at this scale.

580ca858e78bf2436d5445faaedb23def363018a.title: Memorize to Generalize: on the Necessity of Interpolation in High Dimensional Linear Regression
580ca858e78bf2436d5445faaedb23def363018a.research_question: Is interpolation (i.e., fitting the training data to very high accuracy) necessary for achieving optimal generalization performance in high-dimensional, overparameterized linear regression models, particularly as the amount of label noise vanishes?
580ca858e78bf2436d5445faaedb23def363018a.hypothesis: In high-dimensional linear regression with random design and independent noise, achieving optimal predictive risk requires fitting the training data to an accuracy substantially better than the inherent noise floor, implying that interpolation (or memorization) is necessary for generalization, especially as label noise decreases.
580ca858e78bf2436d5445faaedb23def363018a.proposed_method: A theoretical framework is developed to precisely characterize the relationship between training error and prediction (test) error in overparameterized linear regression models. The analysis considers the proportional asymptotic regime where the number of parameters d grows proportionally with the number of samples n (d/n → γ > 1), and the design matrix X has i.i.d. rows with a specified covariance structure. The cost of not fitting the training data is formalized as an optimization problem over a hypothesis class of estimators, subject to a constraint on the allowable training error. Strong duality is leveraged to reduce the nonconvex quadratic optimization problem to a tractable form, and tools from random matrix theory are used to derive analytic expressions for the optimal prediction risk as a function of the empirical data covariance spectrum. The analysis is extended from linear estimators to all square-integrable estimators under Gaussian priors and noise.
580ca858e78bf2436d5445faaedb23def363018a.experiment_details: The proposal involves rigorous mathematical analysis and asymptotic evaluation rather than empirical experiments. Theoretical results are derived under the assumption that the design matrix X has i.i.d. rows with either isotropic or general covariance, and the ground truth parameter θ is drawn from a spherical or Gaussian prior. Theoretical baselines include the minimum norm interpolant and ridge regression estimators. Evaluation metrics are the asymptotic prediction (test) error and training error, characterized in terms of the empirical spectral distribution of the data covariance matrix (Marchenko-Pastur law and its deformations). Key experimental setup details include the proportional asymptotic regime (d/n → γ > 1), analysis of both isotropic and general covariance cases, and the use of random matrix theory to obtain limiting behaviors.
580ca858e78bf2436d5445faaedb23def363018a.novelty_claims: The proposal claims to provide the first precise asymptotic characterization of the necessity of interpolation for optimal generalization in high-dimensional linear regression. It establishes that, even in the simplest random design linear models, memorization of label noise is necessary for achieving optimal predictive risk, and that the threshold for acceptable training error is quadratically smaller than the noise variance as the noise vanishes. The approach rigorously quantifies the linear growth of excess prediction error with training error above this threshold and extends the results to general estimators under Gaussian assumptions, demonstrating that linear estimators are optimal in this regime. The analysis generalizes beyond isotropic features to arbitrary covariance structures, highlighting the robustness of the findings.

58135342c0300d54760f735123092c3559d4c3c8.title: Implicit Bias of Large Depth Networks: a Notion of Rank for Nonlinear Functions
58135342c0300d54760f735123092c3559d4c3c8.research_question: What is the implicit bias in function space induced by large-depth fully connected neural networks with homogeneous nonlinearities, and how does this bias relate to a notion of rank for nonlinear functions? Under what conditions can deep networks recover the 'true rank' of the data, and what are the practical implications of this bias for tasks such as classification and autoencoding?
58135342c0300d54760f735123092c3559d4c3c8.hypothesis: As the depth of fully connected neural networks with homogeneous nonlinearities increases, the implicit bias in function space converges to favor functions of low nonlinear rank, and there exists a regime of intermediate depths where the network can recover the true rank of the data. This bias influences the topology of decision boundaries in classification and naturally induces denoising in autoencoders.
58135342c0300d54760f735123092c3559d4c3c8.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the representation cost of fully connected deep neural networks with homogeneous nonlinearities, focusing on the infinite-depth limit. Two notions of nonlinear rank—Jacobian rank and Bottleneck rank—will be formally defined for piecewise linear functions, and their properties will be established. The limiting behavior of the rescaled representation cost as depth increases will be analyzed, showing that it is bounded between these two ranks. For finite but large depths, upper bounds on the parameter norms at global minima will be derived, relating them to the rank of the learned function. Theoretical results will be complemented by numerical experiments to investigate the practical effects of rank bias and recovery in deep networks.
58135342c0300d54760f735123092c3559d4c3c8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using fully connected deep neural networks of varying depths and widths, trained on synthetic datasets with known intrinsic rank as well as real-world datasets such as MNIST. Baseline comparisons will include shallow networks and kernel methods (e.g., Kernel Ridge Regression). Evaluation metrics will include the singular values of hidden representations and weight matrices, the rank of the learned function (via Jacobian and Bottleneck ranks), and task-specific metrics such as classification accuracy and denoising performance. The experimental setup will explore the effect of network depth, regularization strength, and dataset size on the ability to recover the true rank and on the topology of decision boundaries.
58135342c0300d54760f735123092c3559d4c3c8.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a rigorous notion of nonlinear rank for deep networks and establishes a theoretical connection between infinite-depth representation cost and these rank notions. It provides new upper bounds on the parameter norms at global minima, demonstrating a depth-dependent bias toward low-rank solutions and identifying a regime where true rank recovery occurs. The work further claims to reveal how rank bias shapes the topology of classification boundaries and leads to natural denoising in autoencoders, offering both theoretical insights and practical implications for deep learning.

58273bc1c18bef4754b35967835c559bb80e3130.title: Random Feature Representation Boosting
58273bc1c18bef4754b35967835c559bb80e3130.research_question: Can a novel boosting-based framework for constructing deep residual random feature neural networks (RFNNs) improve predictive performance and computational efficiency over existing RFNNs and end-to-end trained neural networks, particularly in small- to medium-scale tabular data settings?
58273bc1c18bef4754b35967835c559bb80e3130.hypothesis: A deep residual RFNN architecture, constructed using boosting theory and random features at each layer to approximate the functional gradient of the network representation, will outperform both traditional RFNNs and end-to-end trained MLP ResNets in predictive accuracy and computational efficiency, while retaining convex optimization benefits and providing theoretical generalization guarantees.
58273bc1c18bef4754b35967835c559bb80e3130.proposed_method: The proposed method, Random Feature Representation Boosting (RFRBoost), constructs deep ResNet-like RFNNs by iteratively adding random feature residual blocks that approximate the negative functional gradient of the loss with respect to the current network representation. For mean squared error (MSE) loss, closed-form solutions for greedy layer-wise boosting are derived by solving specialized 'sandwiched least squares' problems, a form of generalized Sylvester equations. For general differentiable loss functions, the fitting of random feature residual blocks is formulated as a quadratically constrained least squares problem, ensuring that each residual block follows the functional gradient direction while maintaining a unit norm constraint in the appropriate Hilbert space. The method supports arbitrary random feature mappings at each layer, including functions of both the input and previous layer activations, and employs analytical or convex optimization techniques to solve for the optimal linear mappings at each boosting step. The overall procedure alternates between generating random features, fitting the optimal residual block, updating the network representation, and retraining the top-level linear predictor.
58273bc1c18bef4754b35967835c559bb80e3130.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 91 tabular regression and classification datasets from the OpenML repository, using nested 5-fold cross-validation for robust hyperparameter tuning and evaluation. Baselines will include single-layer RFNNs, end-to-end trained MLP ResNets (with SGD and backpropagation), ridge/logistic regression, and XGBoost. Evaluation metrics will be RMSE for regression and accuracy for classification, with additional reporting of training times. The experimental setup will include tuning of all relevant hyperparameters (e.g., regularization, learning rates, random feature dimensions) using Bayesian optimization. Additional experiments will be performed on synthetic point cloud separation tasks and larger-scale datasets to assess scalability and the ability to capture complex data structures. Statistical significance of results will be assessed using critical difference diagrams and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.
58273bc1c18bef4754b35967835c559bb80e3130.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel boosting-based framework for constructing deep RFNNs that overcomes the limitations of naively stacking random feature layers and extends beyond classical random Fourier features. It provides analytical solutions for layer-wise boosting with random features for MSE loss and generalizes to arbitrary loss functions via convex optimization. The approach retains the convex optimization benefits of RFNNs, offers substantial computational advantages, and provides theoretical regret bounds based on boosting theory and Rademacher complexities. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate significant improvements over both traditional RFNNs and end-to-end trained MLP ResNets in the small- to medium-scale regime, with additional benefits in computational efficiency and theoretical guarantees.

584416870232fabc4bfb77c544a91a647195f706.title: Conformal Inference for Online Prediction with Arbitrary Distribution Shifts
584416870232fabc4bfb77c544a91a647195f706.research_question: How can accurate and adaptive prediction sets be constructed in an online setting where the data-generating distribution undergoes arbitrary, potentially abrupt, distribution shifts over time?
584416870232fabc4bfb77c544a91a647195f706.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that dynamically tuning the step-size parameter in adaptive conformal inference using an online expert aggregation scheme will yield prediction sets with provably small regret and robust local coverage under arbitrary distribution shifts, without requiring prior knowledge of the rate or type of distribution change.
584416870232fabc4bfb77c544a91a647195f706.proposed_method: A novel dynamically-tuned adaptive conformal inference (DtACI) algorithm will be developed for online prediction under distribution shift. The method builds on adaptive conformal inference (ACI) by running multiple parallel instances (experts) of ACI, each with a different candidate step-size parameter (gamma), and aggregates their outputs using an exponential re-weighting scheme based on historical performance. At each time step, the prediction set is constructed using the expert with the best recent performance, allowing the algorithm to adaptively select the optimal step-size in response to local distributional changes. The DtACI algorithm requires only a set of candidate gamma values and two aggregation parameters (sigma and eta), which can be set using simple heuristics or updated online, and does not require knowledge of the underlying distribution shift. The method can be combined with any baseline predictive model that outputs point or quantile estimates, and does not rely on strong distributional assumptions.
584416870232fabc4bfb77c544a91a647195f706.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two real-world time series datasets: one for predicting stock market volatility and another for forecasting COVID-19 case counts. The proposed DtACI method will be compared against several baselines, including the original ACI algorithm, AgACI (adaptive expert aggregation for ACI), and multivalid conformal prediction (MVP). Evaluation metrics will include empirical coverage (the proportion of times the true value falls within the prediction set), prediction set size, and adaptivity to abrupt and gradual distribution shifts. The experimental setup will involve simulating online prediction scenarios with temporal data streams, and hyperparameters for DtACI will be selected using the proposed heuristics or online adaptation strategies. Additional ablation studies may be performed to assess the sensitivity to parameter choices and the effect of different types of distribution shifts.
584416870232fabc4bfb77c544a91a647195f706.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a dynamically-tuned adaptive conformal inference framework that adaptively selects the step-size parameter online, enabling robust and locally adaptive prediction set coverage under arbitrary and unknown distribution shifts. Unlike previous methods, DtACI does not require prior knowledge of the rate or type of distribution change and provides theoretical guarantees on local regret and coverage. The approach is highly flexible, compatible with any black-box predictive model, and demonstrates superior adaptivity and robustness compared to existing baselines, as supported by both theoretical analysis and empirical results.

584915a73b8ff2ce29cf644e388279baa14be550.title: Geometric Latent Diffusion Models for 3D Molecule Generation
584915a73b8ff2ce29cf644e388279baa14be550.research_question: How can generative models be improved to effectively generate chemically valid and diverse 3D molecular geometries, while enabling controllable generation based on desired molecular properties?
584915a73b8ff2ce29cf644e388279baa14be550.hypothesis: Incorporating a point-structured latent space with both invariant scalars and equivariant tensors, and operating diffusion models in this latent space, will enable more expressive, chemically valid, and controllable 3D molecule generation compared to existing methods that operate directly in atomic feature space.
584915a73b8ff2ce29cf644e388279baa14be550.proposed_method: A novel generative framework, Geometric Latent Diffusion Models (GEOLDM), is proposed for 3D molecule generation. The method first encodes molecular geometries into a lower-dimensional latent space using autoencoders equipped with equivariant graph neural networks (EGNNs), ensuring that the latent representations capture both invariant (scalar) and equivariant (tensor) features necessary for roto-translation equivariance. Diffusion models are then trained to operate on these latent variables, modeling the smoother and more regularized latent distribution rather than the original high-dimensional atomic feature space. The denoising process within the diffusion model is parameterized by time-conditional EGNNs to maintain equivariance throughout the generative process. The framework supports both unconditional and controllable generation by conditioning the encoder, decoder, and denoising networks on desired molecular properties, enabling targeted molecule design.
584915a73b8ff2ce29cf644e388279baa14be550.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on widely-used molecular datasets, including QM9 for small molecules and GEOM-DRUG for larger, more complex compounds. The evaluation will cover both unconditional and property-conditioned molecule generation tasks. Baselines will include state-of-the-art autoregressive, flow-based, and diffusion models (e.g., G-Schnet, ENF, EDM, EDM-Bridge, GDM, and their augmented variants), as well as ablations with non-equivariant latent spaces. Evaluation metrics will include atom stability, molecule stability, validity, uniqueness, and mean absolute error for property prediction, using tools such as RDKIT and pretrained property classifiers. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by using consistent training configurations and multiple random seeds for statistical robustness.
584915a73b8ff2ce29cf644e388279baa14be550.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to introduce a latent diffusion model for 3D molecular geometry generation that incorporates both invariant and equivariant features in the latent space. This design enables the generative process to satisfy critical roto-translation equivariance constraints, leading to improved chemical validity, scalability to larger molecules, and enhanced controllability for property-guided generation. The framework offers a principled and generalizable solution that can be extended to various downstream molecular and geometric generation tasks.

5852ca4ed260ef9049feb20fc86848e88628478d.title: An efficient Lorentz equivariant graph neural network for jet tagging
5852ca4ed260ef9049feb20fc86848e88628478d.research_question: How can deep learning models for jet tagging in particle physics be designed to fully preserve Lorentz symmetry, while achieving high efficiency and generalization performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods?
5852ca4ed260ef9049feb20fc86848e88628478d.hypothesis: Incorporating Lorentz group equivariance directly into the architecture of a graph neural network using efficient Minkowski dot product attention will result in a model that is both computationally efficient and achieves superior jet tagging performance, with improved sample efficiency and generalization compared to existing approaches.
5852ca4ed260ef9049feb20fc86848e88628478d.proposed_method: A novel graph neural network architecture, LorentzNet, will be developed to process jets represented as unordered sets of particles (particle clouds), where each particle is described by its 4-momentum and optional scalar attributes. The core of the method is the Lorentz Group Equivariant Block (LGEB), which performs message passing using Minkowski dot product attention. This attention mechanism aggregates information from neighboring particles using Lorentz-invariant geometric quantities, specifically the Minkowski inner product and norm, ensuring full Lorentz group equivariance. Node features are updated through neural networks that operate on these invariant quantities, and the architecture is theoretically grounded in a universal approximation theorem for Lorentz-equivariant functions. The network stacks multiple LGEB layers, followed by pooling and decoding layers for classification, and is implemented to be computationally efficient by avoiding high-order tensor products.
5852ca4ed260ef9049feb20fc86848e88628478d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two widely used jet tagging benchmarks: a top tagging dataset (1.2M training, 400k validation, 400k test jets, with up to 200 particles per jet, generated via PYTHIA8 and DELPHES) and a quark-gluon tagging dataset (2M jets, with particle type information, clustered using anti-kT algorithm). Baseline comparisons will include ResNeXt-50, P-CNN, PFN, ParticleNet, EGNN (E(4) equivariant), and LGN (Lorentz equivariant with tensor products). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy and area under the ROC curve (AUC), with additional tests for sample efficiency (using reduced training set sizes), robustness to Lorentz transformations, and computational cost. Ablation studies and equivariance tests will further analyze the contributions of different architectural components.
5852ca4ed260ef9049feb20fc86848e88628478d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new, efficient, and fully Lorentz-equivariant graph neural network architecture for jet tagging, utilizing Minkowski dot product attention to directly encode Lorentz symmetry without the computational overhead of high-order tensor products. The method claims improved tagging performance and sample efficiency over state-of-the-art models, as well as enhanced generalization and robustness to Lorentz transformations. The architecture is theoretically justified by a universal approximation theorem for Lorentz-equivariant functions, and demonstrates practical efficiency and scalability for large-scale particle physics datasets.

585f8b9725f5f5e5495c3508d39f70d1c053e190.title: FrugalGPT: How to Use Large Language Models While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance
585f8b9725f5f5e5495c3508d39f70d1c053e190.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be leveraged for natural language query answering in a way that significantly reduces inference costs while maintaining or improving task performance, given the heterogeneous pricing and capabilities of available LLM APIs?
585f8b9725f5f5e5495c3508d39f70d1c053e190.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a flexible framework which adaptively selects among multiple LLM APIs and prompt strategies for each query, under a budget constraint, can achieve comparable or superior accuracy to the best individual LLM while substantially reducing inference costs.
585f8b9725f5f5e5495c3508d39f70d1c053e190.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed to optimize the use of LLM APIs for query answering under budget constraints. The approach will integrate three main strategies: (1) prompt adaptation, which selects concise and effective prompts or concatenates queries to minimize prompt length and cost; (2) LLM approximation, which leverages completion caching and fine-tuning of smaller models using outputs from expensive LLMs; and (3) LLM cascade, which adaptively routes each query through a sequence of LLM APIs, accepting an answer if a reliability score exceeds a learned threshold, and escalating to more powerful (and costly) models only as needed. The cascade's scoring function will be trained using a regression model (e.g., DistilBERT) to estimate answer reliability. The optimization of the cascade (selection of LLMs, thresholds) will be formulated as a constrained optimization problem, solved efficiently using search space pruning and objective interpolation.
585f8b9725f5f5e5495c3508d39f70d1c053e190.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using 12 commercial LLM APIs from five providers (OpenAI, AI21, CoHere, Textsynth, ForeFrontAI) on three diverse datasets: HEADLINES (financial news trend classification), OVERRULING (legal overruling detection), and COQA (conversational reading comprehension). Each dataset will be split into training and test sets, with the cascade strategy learned on the training set. Baselines will include the best individual LLM for each task and cost, as well as other prompt and model selection strategies. Evaluation metrics will include task accuracy and total inference cost, with additional analysis of performance-cost trade-offs and maximum performance improvement (MPI) between LLM pairs. The cascade length will be limited (e.g., three LLMs) for tractability, and experiments will investigate both cost savings at matched accuracy and accuracy gains at matched cost.
585f8b9725f5f5e5495c3508d39f70d1c053e190.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a principled, data-adaptive approach to LLM API selection and prompt optimization for cost-effective query answering. Unlike traditional model ensembles or prompt engineering, the method operates in a black-box API setting, exploits heterogeneous pricing structures, and combines prompt adaptation, model approximation, and cascaded routing. The LLM cascade strategy is novel in its use of learned reliability scoring and constrained optimization to balance cost and accuracy, enabling up to 98% cost reduction or measurable accuracy improvements over the best individual LLM.
