The work lays a foundation for sustainable, efficient, and flexible LLM usage in real-world applications.

5875c15e24c8ccb2e9e3ef134f77296de31209da.title: Do SSL Models Have Déjà Vu? A Case of Unintended Memorization in Self-supervised Learning
5875c15e24c8ccb2e9e3ef134f77296de31209da.research_question: To what extent do self-supervised learning (SSL) models memorize image-specific information from their training data, and how can this unintended memorization be systematically measured, visualized, and mitigated?
5875c15e24c8ccb2e9e3ef134f77296de31209da.hypothesis: SSL models, when trained with standard joint-embedding objectives and data augmentations, can memorize associations between specific parts of training images (such as backgrounds) and their corresponding foreground objects, enabling recovery of sensitive or unique information beyond what is explainable by data correlation alone.
5875c15e24c8ccb2e9e3ef134f77296de31209da.proposed_method: A systematic evaluation framework will be developed to measure and analyze unintended memorization in SSL models, termed 'déjà vu memorization.' The methodology involves splitting a large image dataset (e.g., ImageNet) into disjoint subsets for training target and reference SSL models, as well as a public auxiliary set for decoding. For each annotated training image, background-only crops will be embedded using the SSL model, and k-nearest neighbor (KNN) search in the embedding space will be performed against the public set to infer or reconstruct the associated foreground object. The degree of memorization will be quantified by comparing the target model's ability to recover information about its own training samples versus a reference model trained on a disjoint subset. Additional pipelines will be designed to visualize memorization using both direct KNN retrieval and conditional generative models (e.g., RCDM) to reconstruct images from embeddings.
5875c15e24c8ccb2e9e3ef134f77296de31209da.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ImageNet dataset, utilizing its bounding box annotations to separate foreground and background regions. Multiple SSL algorithms (such as VICReg, SimCLR, BYOL, Barlow Twins, and DINO) and supervised baselines will be evaluated. The main metrics will include label inference accuracy from background crops, déjà vu score (accuracy gap between target and reference models on confident samples), and qualitative visualization of reconstructed images. The effects of training hyperparameters (e.g., number of epochs, loss coefficients, model architecture, dataset size, and regularization techniques) on memorization will be systematically explored. The evaluation will also include analysis of the fraction of training samples at risk and the impact of mitigation strategies such as guillotine regularization and fine-tuning.
5875c15e24c8ccb2e9e3ef134f77296de31209da.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first systematic framework to define, quantify, and visualize unintended memorization in SSL models, specifically focusing on the phenomenon where background-only image crops can reveal or reconstruct unique foreground objects. The approach distinguishes memorization from correlation by leveraging disjoint dataset splits and reference models. New metrics and pipelines are proposed for both quantitative and qualitative assessment of memorization in non-generative vision models. The study aims to reveal previously unknown privacy risks in SSL, provide insights into the effects of training choices on memorization, and suggest practical mitigation strategies.

58820d7d68e12d2a531e771a5fcb7e461c25f5c6.title: Neural Compositional Rule Learning for Knowledge Graph Reasoning
58820d7d68e12d2a531e771a5fcb7e461c25f5c6.research_question: How can logical rule learning for knowledge graph reasoning be improved to achieve scalable, interpretable, and systematically generalizable reasoning over large-scale and unseen knowledge graphs?
58820d7d68e12d2a531e771a5fcb7e461c25f5c6.hypothesis: A neural approach that explicitly models the compositional and hierarchical structure of logical rules will enable scalable, interpretable, and systematically generalizable reasoning over both large-scale and unseen knowledge graphs.
58820d7d68e12d2a531e771a5fcb7e461c25f5c6.proposed_method: A novel end-to-end neural framework, Neural Compositional Rule Learning (NCRL), is proposed to learn compositional logical rules from knowledge graphs. The method treats logical rules as hierarchical trees and decomposes rule bodies into small atomic compositions using a sliding window mechanism. At each step, a recurrent attention unit selects and merges compositions, reducing them into single predicates by modeling semantic consistency between compositions and potential rule heads via attention mechanisms. The model is trained by sampling paths from the knowledge graph using random walks, predicting the relation that closes each path, and optimizing a cross-entropy loss over the predicted and true relations. Rule extraction is performed by recursively applying the learned attention mechanism to merge rule bodies and score candidate rules.
58820d7d68e12d2a531e771a5fcb7e461c25f5c6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six benchmark datasets for knowledge graph completion: Family, UMLS, Kinship, WN18RR, FB15K-237, and YAGO3-10. Evaluation metrics include Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR), Hit@1, and Hit@10 under the filtered setting. The method will be compared against state-of-the-art knowledge graph embedding models (e.g., TransE, DistMult, ComplEx, RotatE, ConvE) and rule learning methods (e.g., Neural-LP, DRUM, RNNLogic, RLogic). Additional experiments will assess systematic generalization using the CLUTRR and GraphLog datasets, where training is performed on short-hop paths and evaluation on longer, unseen paths. Ablation studies will examine the impact of data sparsity, number of learned rules, and embedding dimension. Training efficiency and scalability will be benchmarked against existing rule learning methods.
58820d7d68e12d2a531e771a5fcb7e461c25f5c6.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a neural framework that explicitly models the compositional and hierarchical structure of logical rules using a recurrent attention mechanism, enabling systematic generalization to larger and unseen graphs. The method is scalable to large-scale knowledge graphs, achieves state-of-the-art results on both rule learning and knowledge graph completion tasks, and demonstrates superior efficiency compared to existing neural and symbolic rule learning approaches. The approach also provides interpretable logical rules and robust performance under varying data sparsity and rule complexity.

58842cdca3ea68f7b9e638b288fc247a6f26dafc.title: T2I-Adapter: Learning Adapters to Dig out More Controllable Ability for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
58842cdca3ea68f7b9e638b288fc247a6f26dafc.research_question: How can the controllability of pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models be enhanced to allow for more precise and flexible user guidance, beyond what is achievable with text prompts alone?
58842cdca3ea68f7b9e638b288fc247a6f26dafc.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that introducing lightweight, plug-and-play adapter modules into pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models will enable effective alignment between external control signals (such as sketches, segmentation maps, keypoints, color palettes, or depth maps) and the internal knowledge of the diffusion model, thereby facilitating more accurate, flexible, and composable control over image generation without degrading the model's original generative capabilities.
58842cdca3ea68f7b9e638b288fc247a6f26dafc.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that augments pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models (e.g., Stable Diffusion) with small, trainable adapter networks, termed T2I-Adapters. These adapters are designed to extract multi-scale features from various external control signals and inject them into the intermediate layers of the fixed diffusion model, specifically at multiple scales within the UNet encoder. Each adapter is lightweight (approximately 77M parameters) and operates independently, allowing for plug-and-play integration without modifying the original model's topology or parameters. The adapters are trained to align the external condition features with the model's latent representations, enabling control over structural and color aspects of the generated images. Multiple adapters can be composed by weighted summation to support multi-condition guidance, and the system supports generalization to custom models fine-tuned from the same base.
58842cdca3ea68f7b9e638b288fc247a6f26dafc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using several types of control signals, including sketch maps, semantic segmentation maps, keypoints, color palettes, and depth maps. Training datasets will include COCO2017 (164K images) for sketch and segmentation, and 600K image-text pairs from LAION-AESTHETICS for keypoints and depth. Evaluation will be performed on the COCO validation set (5,000 images), with each method generating one sample per image. Baselines will include state-of-the-art GAN-based and diffusion-based conditional generation methods such as SPADE, OASIS, PITI, and the original Stable Diffusion. Quantitative metrics will include FID (Fréchet Inception Distance) and CLIP Score (ViT-L/14). Additional experiments will assess composability (multi-adapter control), generalizability to custom fine-tuned models, and ablation studies on adapter complexity and injection strategies.
58842cdca3ea68f7b9e638b288fc247a6f26dafc.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a simple, efficient, and effective method for enhancing controllability in pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models via lightweight adapters. Key innovations include the plug-and-play design that preserves the original model's generative ability, the ability to train multiple adapters for different control signals, composable multi-condition control without retraining, and strong generalization to custom models. The method achieves superior alignment and generation quality compared to existing baselines and supports a wide range of practical applications, including local editing, spatial color control, and structure guidance.

5895de1712b152eea5dbbfdffa31dbd441c9d125.title: A modern look at the relationship between sharpness and generalization
5895de1712b152eea5dbbfdffa31dbd441c9d125.research_question: Can reparametrization-invariant sharpness measures reliably capture generalization performance in modern practical deep learning settings, including training from scratch and fine-tuning on large-scale datasets and architectures such as transformers?
5895de1712b152eea5dbbfdffa31dbd441c9d125.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical study will be conducted to evaluate multiple reparametrization-invariant sharpness measures, with a focus on adaptive sharpness, across a range of modern deep learning scenarios. The methodology will include both average-case and worst-case adaptive sharpness, computed with and without logit normalization, and will address invariance properties relevant to contemporary architectures like ResNets and Vision Transformers (ViTs). Efficient computation of worst-case sharpness will be achieved using hyperparameter-free optimization methods such as Auto-PGD, tailored to the geometry of elementwise adaptive sharpness. The study will systematically analyze the relationship between sharpness and generalization, considering both in-distribution and out-of-distribution (OOD) performance, and will include theoretical analysis using simple models to clarify the data dependence of sharpness measures.
5895de1712b152eea5dbbfdffa31dbd441c9d125.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of tasks and datasets, including training from scratch on ImageNet and CIFAR-10 using both ConvNets and transformers, and fine-tuning CLIP and BERT models on ImageNet and MNLI, respectively. The evaluation will include a diverse set of models trained with different hyperparameters (e.g., learning rate, weight decay, augmentations, mixup, stochastic depth, dropout), resulting in rich pools of models for each setting. Baselines will include standard sharpness measures and previous sharpness definitions. Evaluation metrics will focus on test error, generalization gap, and OOD error, with correlation quantified using the Kendall rank correlation coefficient. Additional analyses will include the effect of logit normalization, subgroup analysis by training parameters, and theoretical validation using controlled synthetic regression tasks.
5895de1712b152eea5dbbfdffa31dbd441c9d125.novelty_claims: The proposal aims to provide the most comprehensive and systematic evaluation to date of reparametrization-invariant sharpness measures in modern deep learning settings, particularly focusing on architectures and scenarios that have not been systematically studied before, such as transformers and large-scale fine-tuning. It will address the limitations of prior work by considering a broader range of datasets, architectures, and training regimes, and by rigorously analyzing the invariance properties and data dependence of sharpness measures. The study will also introduce efficient and robust computational techniques for sharpness estimation and provide new theoretical insights into the limitations of sharpness as a universal predictor of generalization.

58996964dbcd15045b66201c2b850b5570ba74cb.title: Synthetic Text Generation with Differential Privacy: A Simple and Practical Recipe
58996964dbcd15045b66201c2b850b5570ba74cb.research_question: How can synthetic text data be generated from private datasets in a way that preserves the statistical utility of the original data while providing strong formal privacy guarantees for individuals in the dataset?
58996964dbcd15045b66201c2b850b5570ba74cb.hypothesis: Fine-tuning pre-trained generative language models using differentially private stochastic gradient descent (DP-SGD) will enable the generation of synthetic text that closely matches the utility of non-private synthetic data, while providing strong protection against privacy leakage, including resistance to membership inference and data reconstruction attacks.
58996964dbcd15045b66201c2b850b5570ba74cb.proposed_method: The proposed method involves fine-tuning large, pre-trained autoregressive language models (such as GPT-2, GPT-2 Medium, and GPT-2 Large) on private text datasets using DP-SGD. Per-sample gradients are clipped to bound individual contributions, and Gaussian noise is added to the aggregated gradients to ensure differential privacy. Control codes representing categorical attributes (e.g., review stars, business type) are prepended to each training sample, enabling conditional text generation. After fine-tuning, synthetic text is generated by prompting the DP-trained model with these control codes, leveraging the post-processing property of DP to allow unlimited downstream use without further privacy loss. The method is designed to be simple and practical, requiring minimal modification to standard language model fine-tuning pipelines.
58996964dbcd15045b66201c2b850b5570ba74cb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both public benchmark datasets (such as the Yelp Open Dataset) and a large-scale private customer feedback dataset. The language models will be fine-tuned with and without DP (using epsilon values such as 4 and infinity for comparison), and synthetic text will be generated using top-k and nucleus sampling. Downstream utility will be evaluated by training classifiers (e.g., RoBERTa-base) on synthetic data for tasks like rating and category prediction, and comparing their performance to classifiers trained on original and non-private synthetic data. Distributional similarity between synthetic and real data will be assessed using embedding-based metrics (F1, FID, MAUVE), topic modeling (BERTopic), and sequence length analysis. Privacy leakage will be stress-tested by injecting canary sequences and measuring their appearance in generations, as well as by analyzing the presence of common subjects of interest.
58996964dbcd15045b66201c2b850b5570ba74cb.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to systematically demonstrate that simple DP fine-tuning of large pre-trained language models can produce high-utility synthetic text with strong formal privacy guarantees, without the need for complex templates or prompt-mismatch losses. The method enables unlimited downstream use of synthetic data without additional privacy loss, and provides empirical evidence of strong resistance to privacy attacks, including canary leakage and membership inference. The approach is validated on both public and real-world industrial datasets, and includes novel analyses of learning dynamics, distributional similarity, and the impact of DP on rare data patterns.

58a0897596fc25862f6b09ceb0a45ec3887083ff.title: Preference Distillation via Value based Reinforcement Learning
58a0897596fc25862f6b09ceb0a45ec3887083ff.research_question: How can small language models be more effectively aligned with human preferences using preference distillation, especially when limited to coarse-grained, binary feedback and lacking the capacity to fully leverage large teacher models?
58a0897596fc25862f6b09ceb0a45ec3887083ff.hypothesis: Incorporating a value-based auxiliary reward derived from a DPO-trained teacher model into the preference distillation process will provide more informative supervision, preserve the optimal policy, and lead to improved alignment and performance of small language models compared to existing distillation and preference optimization methods.
58a0897596fc25862f6b09ceb0a45ec3887083ff.proposed_method: A new preference distillation framework, Teacher Value-based Knowledge Distillation (TVKD), will be developed to enhance the alignment of small language models with human preferences. The method will extract the value function from a DPO-trained teacher model and use it to construct a potential-based reward shaping term, which is added as an auxiliary reward to the student's RL objective. This shaping term, defined as the difference in the teacher's value function between consecutive states, provides soft, sequence-level guidance without interfering with the global reward structure or optimal policy of DPO. The approach will be integrated into standard DPO training pipelines with minimal modification and will not require additional rollouts or online teacher queries, making it fully compatible with offline preference datasets.
58a0897596fc25862f6b09ceb0a45ec3887083ff.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using several small language models (e.g., LLaMA-3.2-1B, LLaMA-3.2-3B, Danube3-500M) as students and larger models (e.g., Mistral-7B-v0.2, LLaMA-3.1-8B) as teachers. Training will utilize supervised fine-tuning with the Deita-10k-V0 dataset, followed by preference distillation on DPO-MIX-7K and HelpSteer2 datasets. Evaluation will be performed on multiple benchmarks, including Fsfair-LLaMA3-RM-V0.1 (RM), MT-Bench, AlpacaEval, and the OpenLLMLeaderboard, using both LLM-based and GPT-based grading. Baselines for comparison will include various knowledge distillation methods (VanillaKD, DCKD, SeqKD, GKD), offline alignment methods (DPO, SimPO, WPO, TDPO), and other preference distillation approaches (DDPO, DPKD, ADPA). Metrics will include scalar reward model scores, win rates in pairwise comparisons, and average benchmark ratings. Ablation studies will be performed across different teacher-student model pairs and reward shaping strategies.
58a0897596fc25862f6b09ceb0a45ec3887083ff.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first use of a teacher's value function as a soft, sequence-level auxiliary reward for preference distillation in language models. By leveraging potential-based reward shaping, the approach ensures policy invariance and avoids conflicts with the original DPO objective, enabling the transfer of the teacher's internal reward modeling to the student. The framework is fully offline, requiring no additional rollouts, and demonstrates consistent improvements across model sizes, architectures, and diverse benchmarks. The method also provides theoretical and empirical evidence that value-based shaping outperforms action-dependent shaping and other auxiliary reward strategies in aligning small models with human preferences.

58a2baecdc4e4b3f16d1899c0f1080cefe73013a.title: Learning Dynamic Graph Embeddings With Neural Controlled Differential Equations
58a2baecdc4e4b3f16d1899c0f1080cefe73013a.research_question: How can continuous-time representation learning frameworks be developed to effectively capture both node dynamics and evolving structural dynamics in dynamic graphs for improved performance on tasks such as node attribute prediction, dynamic node classification, and temporal link prediction?
58a2baecdc4e4b3f16d1899c0f1080cefe73013a.hypothesis: A continuous-time framework that jointly models node embeddings and structural dynamics by incorporating a graph-enhanced neural network vector field with a time-varying graph path as the control signal will more accurately capture the complex temporal evolution in dynamic graphs, leading to improved predictive performance and robustness to missing or irregularly sampled data.
58a2baecdc4e4b3f16d1899c0f1080cefe73013a.proposed_method: A novel continuous-time framework, termed Graph Neural Controlled Differential Equations (GN-CDEs), will be developed to model dynamic graphs. The method constructs a continuous-time path for the evolving graph topology, which serves as the control signal in a neural controlled differential equation (CDE). Node embeddings are evolved over time by integrating a graph neural network (GNN)-based vector field, which is conditioned on both the current node states and the interpolated graph structure. The model supports calibration with subsequent data, is robust to missing or irregularly sampled observations, and can be efficiently implemented using scalable approximations such as message-passing mechanisms and efficient interpolation schemes (e.g., natural cubic splines) for the adjacency matrix. The framework is designed to be flexible, supporting extensions to directed and attributed graphs, and can be adapted for various dynamic graph learning tasks.
58a2baecdc4e4b3f16d1899c0f1080cefe73013a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world dynamic graph datasets. Synthetic datasets will include dynamic networks generated from grid, random, power-law, small world, and community structures, with tasks such as heat diffusion and gene regulation prediction. Real-world datasets will be drawn from the Temporal Graph Benchmark (TGB), including tgbn-trade and tgbn-genre, focusing on dynamic node affinity prediction. Baseline methods will include Neural ODE, Neural CDE, STG-NCDE, and state-of-the-art temporal graph neural networks such as JODIE, TGAT, CAWN, TCL, GraphMixer, DyGFormer, DyRep, TGN, and TGNv2. Evaluation metrics will include mean absolute error for node attribute prediction and NDCE@10 for link affinity tasks. Models will be trained using the Adam optimizer, with neural network architectures kept consistent across baselines. Experiments will also analyze the impact of different interpolation schemes and the model's ability to handle instantaneous structural changes.
58a2baecdc4e4b3f16d1899c0f1080cefe73013a.novelty_claims: The proposed GN-CDE framework introduces a principled way to jointly model node and structural dynamics in continuous time, explicitly incorporating evolving graph topology as a control signal in a neural CDE. This enables continuous-time inference without piecewise integration, supports calibration with partially observed data, and is robust to missing or irregularly sampled observations. The approach is theoretically grounded, with guarantees on existence and uniqueness of solutions, and is scalable to large graphs via efficient approximations. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior performance over existing baselines on a range of dynamic graph learning tasks, confirming the effectiveness of modeling both node and structural dynamics in a unified framework.

58af2d4fcca54c14334d1efd975554b4eb78cd4d.title: SLiC-HF: Sequence Likelihood Calibration with Human Feedback
58af2d4fcca54c14334d1efd975554b4eb78cd4d.research_question: How can sequence likelihood calibration be leveraged to align language models with human preferences using human feedback, and can this approach serve as a simpler and more efficient alternative to reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) for tasks such as abstractive summarization?
58af2d4fcca54c14334d1efd975554b4eb78cd4d.hypothesis: Sequence likelihood calibration with human feedback (SLiC-HF) will enable language models to better align with human preferences, leading to improved generation quality over supervised fine-tuning baselines and competitive or superior performance compared to RLHF methods, while being simpler to implement, easier to tune, and more computationally efficient.
58af2d4fcca54c14334d1efd975554b4eb78cd4d.proposed_method: A novel method, Sequence Likelihood Calibration with Human Feedback (SLiC-HF), will be developed to improve language model alignment with human preferences. The approach begins with supervised fine-tuning of a language model on reference data, followed by calibration of the model's sequence likelihood using a margin-based ranking loss that contrasts positive (preferred) and negative (non-preferred) sequences derived from human feedback. Two main variants will be explored: (1) SLiC-HF-sample-rank, which samples multiple candidate summaries from the model and uses either a trained reward model or a pairwise ranking model (both trained on human preference data) to select positive/negative pairs for calibration; and (2) SLiC-HF-direct, which directly uses human feedback pairs without an intermediate ranking or reward model. A regularization term, based on cross-entropy with either reference targets or best-ranked candidates, will be included to stabilize training and prevent divergence from the initial policy. The method will be implemented using T5 models and will support both on-policy and off-policy feedback data.
58af2d4fcca54c14334d1efd975554b4eb78cd4d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Reddit TL;DR summarization dataset, utilizing both supervised fine-tuning data and human preference data collected from previous work. T5-Large (770M) and T5-XXL (11B) models will serve as the generation, ranking, and reward models, with batch sizes of 32 for generation and 128 for ranking/reward models. The primary evaluation metrics will include model win rate (the percentage of model-generated summaries preferred over human references, as judged by a ranking model), ROUGE scores, and human evaluation via crowd-sourced side-by-side comparisons. Baselines will include supervised fine-tuning, continued fine-tuning on filtered human feedback data, and RLHF-PPO models from prior work. Ablation studies will examine the effects of different calibration strategies, regularization targets, model sizes, and numbers of candidate decodes. Human evaluations will assess summary quality, factuality, and preference, with multiple raters per example and anonymized, randomized presentation of summaries.
58af2d4fcca54c14334d1efd975554b4eb78cd4d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new application of sequence likelihood calibration for learning from human feedback, offering a simpler and more efficient alternative to RLHF by eliminating the need for complex reinforcement learning algorithms, value networks, and in-loop decoding. The method demonstrates that human preference data collected for other models (off-policy) can be effectively leveraged, reducing the need for costly new data collection. Additionally, the approach provides a general, open-sourced recipe for SLiC-HF that outperforms RLHF on the Reddit TL;DR summarization task, and establishes the effectiveness of pairwise ranking models over pointwise reward models for aligning with human preferences.

58b19752738817ec8726c1659b018e8a7159a50f.title: Revisiting Agnostic PAC Learning
58b19752738817ec8726c1659b018e8a7159a50f.research_question: What are the fundamental sample complexity limits and optimal algorithms for agnostic PAC learning, particularly as a function of the error rate of the best-in-class hypothesis, and can new algorithms outperform empirical risk minimization (ERM) in this setting?
58b19752738817ec8726c1659b018e8a7159a50f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that existing proper learning algorithms, including ERM, are sub-optimal in agnostic PAC learning for a wide range of error rates of the best hypothesis, and that a new improper learning algorithm can achieve optimal error bounds across nearly the full range of these rates.
58b19752738817ec8726c1659b018e8a7159a50f.proposed_method: A novel agnostic PAC learning algorithm, termed DisagreeingExperts, will be developed to achieve optimal sample complexity bounds in terms of the VC-dimension and the error rate τ of the best hypothesis in the class. The methodology involves recursively identifying pairs of near-optimal classifiers (experts) that disagree on a significant fraction of the input space, and leveraging the structure of their disagreement to partition the data and train specialized classifiers on these partitions. The algorithm alternates between searching for such disagreeing pairs and, when no sufficiently disagreeing pair exists, exploiting the concentration of near-optimal hypotheses to improve generalization bounds. The final classifier combines the decisions from these specialized classifiers, depending on whether a new input falls into a region of expert disagreement or agreement, thereby achieving an error bound that removes the previously unavoidable ln(1/τ) factor present in ERM.
58b19752738817ec8726c1659b018e8a7159a50f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic datasets constructed to match the theoretical worst-case scenarios for agnostic PAC learning, with hypothesis classes of specified VC-dimension and varying values of τ (the error of the best-in-class hypothesis). The proposed DisagreeingExperts algorithm will be compared against ERM and other proper learning algorithms, with evaluation focused on the excess error over the optimal achievable error. The primary evaluation metric will be the generalization error, measured as the probability of misclassification on fresh samples from the underlying distribution. The experimental setup will include validation over multiple random draws of training data, and the analysis will examine the scaling of error with respect to n (sample size), d (VC-dimension), and τ.
58b19752738817ec8726c1659b018e8a7159a50f.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first learning algorithm that provably outperforms ERM in the agnostic PAC setting for nearly the full range of τ, achieving optimal sample complexity up to lower-order terms. The approach is based on a new paradigm of recursively training and leveraging disagreeing near-optimal experts, which has not been previously applied to agnostic PAC learning. The work also establishes a new lower bound showing that all proper learners, including ERM, incur a sub-optimal ln(1/τ) factor in their error, thereby demonstrating the necessity of improper learning in achieving optimality in this regime. These contributions close a longstanding gap in the theory of agnostic PAC learning and introduce techniques that may have further applications in learning theory.

58c486ad4020177f5ed3d9f2883f3fc327b55770.title: MiniViT: Compressing Vision Transformers with Weight Multiplexing
58c486ad4020177f5ed3d9f2883f3fc327b55770.research_question: How can the parameter efficiency of vision transformers be significantly improved without compromising their performance, enabling their deployment on devices with limited memory and computational resources?
58c486ad4020177f5ed3d9f2883f3fc327b55770.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that combining weight sharing across transformer layers with learnable weight transformations and comprehensive knowledge distillation can yield highly compressed vision transformer models that retain or even improve upon the original performance.
58c486ad4020177f5ed3d9f2883f3fc327b55770.proposed_method: A novel compression framework, MiniViT, is proposed to address the parameter redundancy in vision transformers. The approach introduces weight multiplexing, which involves sharing the weights of consecutive transformer blocks while applying learnable linear transformations to the shared weights in each layer, thereby increasing parameter diversity and stabilizing training. Specifically, separate transformation matrices are imposed on both the multi-head self-attention (MSA) and multilayer perceptron (MLP) modules for each layer, and layer normalization parameters are kept independent per layer. To further mitigate performance degradation, a multi-level knowledge distillation strategy is employed, transferring information from a large teacher model to the compact student model at the prediction-logit, attention, and hidden-state levels. The compression pipeline consists of generating compact architectures with weight transformation, followed by training with the proposed distillation objectives.
58c486ad4020177f5ed3d9f2883f3fc327b55770.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale image classification datasets such as ImageNet-1K, ImageNet-Real, and ImageNet-V2, as well as downstream tasks including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Flowers, Stanford Cars, Oxford-IIIT Pets, and COCO 2017 for object detection. The proposed MiniViT models will be benchmarked against state-of-the-art vision transformers (e.g., DeiT, Swin Transformer) and efficient CNNs. Baseline comparisons will include original models, models with standard weight sharing, and other compressed transformer variants. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 and top-5 accuracy for classification, mean average precision (AP) for detection, and model size (number of parameters). Training will utilize standard data augmentation, AdamW optimizer, and knowledge distillation from large teacher models. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of each component (weight sharing, transformation, distillation) and different sharing strategies.
58c486ad4020177f5ed3d9f2883f3fc327b55770.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a new form of weight multiplexing for vision transformers, combining cross-layer weight sharing with learnable transformations to address training instability and performance degradation. Unlike prior works, the method systematically analyzes and resolves the issues of strict weight sharing in vision transformers by introducing parameter diversity and stability. Additionally, the approach integrates multi-level knowledge distillation within transformer modules, including attention and hidden-state distillation, which is not commonly explored in vision transformer compression. The resulting models achieve substantial parameter reduction (up to 90%) while maintaining or improving accuracy, and demonstrate strong transferability to downstream tasks.

58cb7273fca203d2d9f5ca9b492a807310f04410.title: BOOD: Boundary-based Out-Of-Distribution Data Generation
58cb7273fca203d2d9f5ca9b492a807310f04410.research_question: How can high-quality, informative out-of-distribution (OOD) data be automatically generated to improve the robustness and accuracy of OOD detection models, specifically by targeting the decision boundaries between in-distribution (ID) and OOD data?
58cb7273fca203d2d9f5ca9b492a807310f04410.hypothesis: Synthesizing OOD features and images that are explicitly located around the decision boundaries of ID data will provide more informative and effective auxiliary data for OOD detection, resulting in improved detection performance compared to existing methods that do not explicitly target these boundaries.
58cb7273fca203d2d9f5ca9b492a807310f04410.proposed_method: A novel framework, BOOD (Boundary-based Out-Of-Distribution data generation), will be developed to generate OOD data by leveraging diffusion models. The approach begins by constructing a text-conditioned latent feature space aligned with the input requirements of a diffusion model, using an image encoder trained to match image features with class token embeddings from a text encoder (such as CLIP). Next, features from the ID dataset that are closest to the decision boundary are identified by calculating the minimal adversarial perturbation required to change the model's prediction. These boundary features are then perturbed along the gradient ascent direction to cross the decision boundary, synthesizing OOD features. Finally, these synthetic OOD features are decoded into pixel-space images using a diffusion model, ensuring the generated OOD data is human-compatible and informative for training OOD detectors.
58cb7273fca203d2d9f5ca9b492a807310f04410.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard OOD detection benchmarks, including CIFAR-100 and IMAGENET-100 as in-distribution datasets. OOD test datasets will include SVHN, PLACES365, LSUN, ISUN, TEXTURES for CIFAR-100, and INATURALIST, PLACES, SUN, TEXTURES for IMAGENET-100, ensuring no overlap with ID data. The proposed method will be compared against a range of baselines, including scoring-based methods (e.g., MSP, ODIN, Mahalanobis, Energy, GODIN, KNN, ViM, ReAct, DICE) and synthesis-based methods (GAN, VOS, NPOS, DreamOOD). Evaluation metrics will include FPR95 (false positive rate at 95% true positive rate), AUROC (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve), and ID classification accuracy. The experimental setup will utilize a ResNet-34 backbone, Stable Diffusion v1.4 for image generation, and hyperparameters such as a batch size of 160, temperature parameter t=1, stepsize α=0.015, and a total of 1000 OOD images generated per class.
58cb7273fca203d2d9f5ca9b492a807310f04410.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to explicitly generate image-level OOD data located around decision boundaries, providing highly informative features for shaping the ID-OOD decision boundary. The method introduces two key methodological innovations: (1) adversarial boundary identification to select ID features closest to the decision boundary, and (2) targeted perturbation to synthesize OOD features that cross these boundaries. This approach enables efficient and effective OOD data generation without the need for manually curated OOD datasets, resulting in significant improvements in OOD detection performance over state-of-the-art methods. Additionally, the framework demonstrates computational and memory efficiency comparable to existing leading approaches.

58dca8186a222581ca03067e17562aa740214982.title: Non-exchangeable Conformal Prediction with Optimal Transport: Tackling Distribution Shifts with Unlabeled Data
58dca8186a222581ca03067e17562aa740214982.research_question: How can conformal prediction methods be adapted to maintain reliable uncertainty quantification under arbitrary distribution shifts between calibration and test data, particularly when only unlabeled data from the target distribution is available?
58dca8186a222581ca03067e17562aa740214982.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging optimal transport theory to quantify and minimize the coverage gap between calibration and test distributions enables the construction of conformal predictors that maintain valid coverage guarantees under arbitrary distribution shifts, even when only unlabeled target data is available.
58dca8186a222581ca03067e17562aa740214982.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed that quantifies the coverage gap in conformal prediction under non-exchangeable settings using optimal transport distances, specifically the 1-Wasserstein distance, between the distributions of nonconformity scores from calibration and test data. The approach introduces the concept of the total coverage gap, defined as the expected difference in coverage across all target coverage levels, and derives computable upper bounds on this gap using both labeled and unlabeled data. When only unlabeled test data is available, auxiliary distributions over nonconformity scores are constructed (e.g., using minimum and maximum scores or model-based surrogates) to sandwich the unknown test score distribution, enabling label-free upper bounds. These bounds are then used as differentiable objectives to learn importance weights for the calibration data, either as free-form weights or via a learnable weight function, by minimizing the empirical upper bound on the coverage gap. The method is designed to be computationally efficient, relying on sorting and kernel density estimation, and is applicable to both classification and regression tasks.
58dca8186a222581ca03067e17562aa740214982.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic regression tasks and real-world image classification datasets exhibiting covariate and label shifts, including ImageNet-C and iWildCam. The evaluation will compare the proposed method against standard conformal prediction, likelihood ratio weighting, entropy-scaled conformal prediction, and other recent approaches designed for non-exchangeable settings. Metrics will include empirical coverage (the proportion of test points where the true label is contained in the prediction set) and prediction set size, with target coverage rates set (e.g., at 90%). Experimental protocols will involve splitting available data into calibration, training, and test sets, with additional unlabeled samples from the test distribution used for weight optimization. The effectiveness of the method will be assessed across varying sample sizes, types of distribution shift, and parameterizations of the weighting strategy.
58dca8186a222581ca03067e17562aa740214982.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled, distribution-free method for quantifying and mitigating the coverage gap in conformal prediction under arbitrary distribution shifts, leveraging optimal transport theory. It is the first to provide computable, label-free upper bounds on the total coverage gap using only unlabeled target data, and to use these bounds as optimization objectives for learning calibration weights. The method is broadly applicable, computationally efficient, and does not require prior knowledge of the nature of the distribution shift. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate significant improvements in coverage under challenging distribution shifts compared to existing methods.

58f547667c764f76125b96a256c927434bd72869.title: GADBench: Revisiting and Benchmarking Supervised Graph Anomaly Detection
58f547667c764f76125b96a256c927434bd72869.research_question: How do various supervised graph anomaly detection methods, including traditional algorithms, tree ensembles, and graph neural networks, compare in terms of effectiveness and efficiency across diverse, large-scale real-world datasets under standardized evaluation protocols?
58f547667c764f76125b96a256c927434bd72869.hypothesis: Tree ensemble models with neighborhood aggregation can outperform both standard and specialized graph neural networks for supervised graph anomaly detection tasks, particularly on large-scale and heterogeneous datasets.
58f547667c764f76125b96a256c927434bd72869.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmarking framework, GADBench, will be developed to systematically evaluate and compare 29 supervised graph anomaly detection models. The models will include classical machine learning algorithms (e.g., MLP, KNN, SVM), standard GNNs (e.g., GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE), specialized GNNs designed for anomaly detection (e.g., CARE-GNN, BWGNN), and tree ensemble methods (e.g., Random Forest, XGBoost) with and without neighborhood aggregation. The neighborhood aggregation for tree ensembles will be implemented as a parameter-free process, aggregating node features from neighbors (using mean, max, or sum pooling) over multiple layers before feeding the concatenated features into the tree ensemble for anomaly scoring. All models will be integrated into a unified, open-source repository with standardized training, evaluation, and hyperparameter optimization protocols.
58f547667c764f76125b96a256c927434bd72869.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 10 real-world graph datasets spanning domains such as social media, e-commerce, finance, and crowdsourcing, with node counts ranging from thousands to millions. Both fully-supervised and semi-supervised settings will be evaluated, using standardized data splits (e.g., 40% train, 20% validation, 40% test for fully-supervised; 100 labeled nodes for semi-supervised). Performance will be measured using AUROC, AUPRC, and Recall@K, with additional tracking of runtime and memory usage. Each model will be tested with default and randomly searched hyperparameters, and results will be averaged over multiple random splits. Specialized experiments will address heterogeneous graphs and inductive settings, and the impact of neighborhood aggregation layers will be systematically analyzed.
58f547667c764f76125b96a256c927434bd72869.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark constitutes the first comprehensive, open-source evaluation suite for supervised graph anomaly detection, covering a broad spectrum of models and large-scale, organically anomalous datasets. The framework introduces tree ensemble baselines with neighborhood aggregation, demonstrating their superior performance and efficiency over both standard and specialized GNNs. The benchmark also standardizes evaluation protocols, addresses fairness in hyperparameter optimization, and provides insights into the effects of feature types, decision boundaries, and model scalability. This work establishes a robust foundation for future research and fair comparison in the graph anomaly detection field.

58f8925a8b87054ad0635a6398a7fe24935b1604.title: Mind2Web: Towards a Generalist Agent for the Web
58f8925a8b87054ad0635a6398a7fe24935b1604.research_question: How can a generalist agent be developed that is capable of following natural language instructions to complete complex tasks on any real-world website, demonstrating robust generalization across unseen domains, websites, and tasks?
58f8925a8b87054ad0635a6398a7fe24935b1604.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a two-stage framework combining a small language model for candidate element filtering with a large language model for action prediction can enable effective and efficient generalist web agents that generalize to unseen websites and domains, outperforming prior approaches based on direct classification or generation.
58f8925a8b87054ad0635a6398a7fe24935b1604.proposed_method: A novel two-stage agent framework, MINDACT, is proposed for building generalist web agents. In the first stage, a fine-tuned small language model (e.g., DeBERTa) ranks and filters webpage elements based on the task description and interaction history, selecting a top-k set of candidate elements from the often large and complex DOM. In the second stage, a large language model (e.g., Flan-T5 or GPT-4) receives a pruned webpage snippet containing only the candidate elements and their context, and predicts the next action as a multi-choice question answering problem, selecting both the target element and the operation (Click, Type, Select Option). The model is trained to process high-level task goals and previous actions, supporting multi-step planning and grounding in real-world web environments. The approach leverages both fine-tuning and in-context learning, and is designed to handle the scale and diversity of real-world websites.
58f8925a8b87054ad0635a6398a7fe24935b1604.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the MIND2WEB dataset, which comprises over 2,000 open-ended tasks from 137 real-world websites across 31 domains, with detailed action sequences and webpage snapshots. Three evaluation splits will be used: Cross-Task (novel tasks on seen websites), Cross-Website (novel websites in seen domains), and Cross-Domain (novel domains), to rigorously assess generalization. Baselines will include direct classification (DeBERTa) and generation (Flan-T5) models. Evaluation metrics will include Element Accuracy, Operation F1, Step Success Rate, and Task Success Rate, with macro-averaging across tasks. Both fine-tuned and in-context learning settings will be explored, including experiments with open-source (Flan-T5) and closed-source (GPT-3.5, GPT-4) LLMs. Data preprocessing will involve filtering HTML to retain semantically meaningful elements, and candidate generation will use top-50 ranked elements for downstream action prediction.
58f8925a8b87054ad0635a6398a7fe24935b1604.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first large-scale, real-world dataset (MIND2WEB) for developing and evaluating generalist web agents, covering a diverse set of domains, websites, and user interaction patterns. The MINDACT framework is novel in its two-stage design, efficiently combining small and large language models for candidate filtering and action prediction, and formulating action selection as a multi-choice QA problem. This approach enables effective handling of the complexity and scale of real-world web environments, and demonstrates superior generalization to unseen websites and domains compared to prior methods. The research also establishes new benchmarks for web agent generalization and opens avenues for integrating multimodal information, reinforcement learning, and specialized models for web understanding.

59207e9d0cd4129b6ed665205105192dd3032ff3.title: Beyond One-Preference-Fits-All Alignment: Multi-Objective Direct Preference Optimization
59207e9d0cd4129b6ed665205105192dd3032ff3.research_question: How can language models be efficiently aligned to accommodate diverse and potentially conflicting human preferences across multiple objectives, without relying on unstable and resource-intensive reinforcement learning methods?
59207e9d0cd4129b6ed665205105192dd3032ff3.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a direct preference optimization approach, extended to handle multiple objectives (MODPO), can achieve Pareto-optimal alignment of language models for diverse human preferences with greater stability and computational efficiency than multi-objective RLHF, while maintaining or improving alignment quality.
59207e9d0cd4129b6ed665205105192dd3032ff3.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces Multi-Objective Direct Preference Optimization (MODPO), an RL-free extension of Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) for multi-objective alignment. MODPO integrates language modeling and reward modeling by training language models as implicit collective reward models, parameterized by different objective weightings. The method operates by first training margin reward models on multi-dimensional preference datasets, then iteratively optimizing language models for various linear scalarizations of objectives (i.e., different weight vectors) using a cross-entropy loss that encodes preference margins. For each target preference weighting, a separate language model is fine-tuned, resulting in a set of models that collectively approximate the Pareto front of optimal trade-offs among objectives. This approach eliminates the need for value function modeling and online sample collection, thereby improving stability and efficiency.
59207e9d0cd4129b6ed665205105192dd3032ff3.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on two main tasks: safety alignment (balancing helpfulness and harmlessness) and long-form question answering (balancing relevance, factuality, completeness, and overall preference). Datasets include a 10k subset of BEAVERTAILS for safety alignment and the QA-FEEDBACK dataset for long-form QA, both containing multi-dimensional human preference annotations. Baselines include multi-objective RLHF (MORLHF), DPO-based model soups, DPO loss weighting, and best-of-n sampling. Evaluation metrics focus on the trade-off fronts between alignment objectives, measured via ground-truth or proxy reward models, and include KL-divergence to the supervised fine-tuned model as a regularization metric. Both synthetic and real human feedback settings are considered, with additional evaluation using GPT-3.5/4 as external judges for safety alignment. Experiments systematically vary objective weightings to empirically construct and compare Pareto fronts.
59207e9d0cd4129b6ed665205105192dd3032ff3.novelty_claims: The proposed approach claims theoretical equivalence to multi-objective RLHF in terms of optimal solutions, while offering significant practical advantages in stability and computational efficiency by avoiding reinforcement learning. MODPO is presented as the first RL-free, theoretically grounded method for multi-objective alignment that directly produces a Pareto front of language models, each catering to distinct human preference profiles. The method demonstrates the ability to interpolate and customize language models for diverse objectives with minimal overhead, outperforming RL-based baselines in both alignment quality and resource usage.

5922f437512158970c417f4413bface021df5f78.title: A Generalist Agent
5922f437512158970c417f4413bface021df5f78.research_question: Can a single, large-scale neural network agent be trained to perform a wide variety of tasks across multiple modalities, embodiments, and domains, using a unified architecture and shared parameters?
5922f437512158970c417f4413bface021df5f78.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that training a generalist agent on a diverse set of tasks and modalities, using large-scale data, compute, and model parameters, will result in an agent capable of performing competitively across a broad range of tasks and can generalize to new tasks with minimal additional data.
5922f437512158970c417f4413bface021df5f78.proposed_method: A unified, multi-modal, multi-task agent will be developed using a large (1.2B parameter) decoder-only transformer architecture. All data—including text, images, proprioceptive signals, joint torques, button presses, and other discrete or continuous observations and actions—will be serialized into flat sequences of tokens using modality-specific tokenization schemes. The model will be trained in an autoregressive, supervised fashion to predict the next token, with masking applied so that the loss is computed only for target outputs (e.g., text, actions). Prompt conditioning will be used to provide task context, with demonstration sequences prepended to a subset of training examples. The model will be deployed by iteratively sampling actions in an autoregressive manner, using the context of previous observations and actions, and will support real-time control for robotics and other interactive environments.
5922f437512158970c417f4413bface021df5f78.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training the agent on a diverse set of 604 tasks spanning simulated control (e.g., Atari, DM Control Suite, Meta-World, BabyAI, Sokoban, DMLab, Procgen Benchmark, Modular RL), robotics (RGB Stacking with both simulated and real Sawyer robot arms), and vision-language tasks (MassiveText, MS-COCO Captions, Conceptual Captions, ALIGN, LTIP, OKVQA, VQAv2, M3W). The model will be evaluated using standard metrics for each domain: normalized return relative to expert performance for control tasks, success rate for robotics stacking, and qualitative/quantitative measures for image captioning and dialogue. Baselines will include specialist agents trained on individual tasks, as well as published benchmarks such as BC-IMP for robotics. Evaluation will involve rolling out the agent for multiple episodes per task (e.g., 50 for control, 200 for robotics test triplets), and aggregating performance across domains. Scaling law experiments will compare model sizes (79M, 364M, 1.2B parameters) to assess the effect of scale on generalization and performance.
5922f437512158970c417f4413bface021df5f78.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a single generalist agent capable of performing hundreds of distinct tasks across diverse modalities and embodiments using a unified transformer-based architecture and shared weights. The method leverages a novel tokenization and serialization scheme to unify multi-modal data for sequence modeling, and employs prompt conditioning for task disambiguation without explicit task identifiers. The agent demonstrates competitive performance with specialist baselines on a wide range of tasks, including real-world robotics, and provides evidence for scaling laws in generalist agent performance. This work represents a significant step toward general-purpose artificial intelligence by showing that a single model can learn to act, perceive, and communicate across many domains.

592e2a4c8bb3e72b1f6d671d6642907fa81b1782.title: Noise Is Not the Main Factor Behind the Gap Between SGD and Adam on Transformers, but Sign Descent Might Be
592e2a4c8bb3e72b1f6d671d6642907fa81b1782.research_question: What are the underlying factors responsible for the performance gap between stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and Adam on transformer-based models, particularly in language tasks, and can this gap be attributed to noise, deterministic algorithmic differences, or alternative optimization strategies?
592e2a4c8bb3e72b1f6d671d6642907fa81b1782.hypothesis: The performance gap between SGD and Adam on transformers is not primarily caused by noise or heavy-tailed stochastic gradient errors, but may instead be explained by deterministic properties of the optimization algorithms, such as the use of sign descent or normalization-based updates.
592e2a4c8bb3e72b1f6d671d6642907fa81b1782.proposed_method: A comprehensive experimental framework will be developed to systematically investigate the performance of SGD, Adam, sign descent, and normalized gradient descent across a range of batch sizes, from small to full-batch, on both image and language tasks. The methodology will involve controlling for stochasticity by varying batch sizes up to the entire dataset, and comparing optimization dynamics in both stochastic and deterministic settings. Each optimizer will be evaluated with and without momentum, and step sizes will be tuned individually for each batch size using grid search. Additional experiments will implement sign descent and normalized gradient updates, both with and without momentum, to isolate the contributions of these algorithmic components. The approach will focus on training loss to analyze optimization behavior, with hyperparameter selection based on training performance.
592e2a4c8bb3e72b1f6d671d6642907fa81b1782.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two image classification tasks (MNIST and CIFAR-10, using small CNNs and ResNet18) and three language tasks (PTB and WikiText-2 with small transformers and Transformer-XL, and SQuAD via fine-tuning DistillBERT). For each task, optimizers will be run across a spectrum of batch sizes (small, medium, large, extra-large, and full-batch), and training loss will be measured to assess optimization progress. Baselines will include SGD, Adam, sign descent, and normalized gradient descent, each with and without momentum. Step sizes will be tuned via grid search for each batch size and optimizer, and each configuration will be repeated with three random seeds. Evaluation will focus on training loss, with validation metrics reported as supplementary information. The experimental setup will control for confounding factors such as number of iterations and epochs, and additional checks will be performed to ensure trends hold when sources of randomness (e.g., dropout) are disabled.
592e2a4c8bb3e72b1f6d671d6642907fa81b1782.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a systematic investigation that challenges the prevailing hypothesis attributing Adam's advantage over SGD to robustness against noise and heavy-tailed gradient errors. By controlling for stochasticity and directly comparing deterministic and stochastic settings, the study aims to demonstrate that noise is not the main factor behind the performance gap. The research further claims that sign descent, a simpler and less-studied algorithm, can close most of the gap between SGD and Adam in full-batch settings, highlighting a previously underexplored connection. This approach provides new empirical evidence and theoretical insights into the deterministic properties of optimization algorithms on transformers, and suggests that the success of Adam may be more closely related to sign-based or normalization-based updates than previously recognized.

595da6e11bb315673d489b15ca9487c16f2545cc.title: Model Reduction on Manifolds: A differential geometric framework
595da6e11bb315673d489b15ca9487c16f2545cc.research_question: How can a unified, differential geometric framework be developed for model order reduction (MOR) that accommodates nonlinear projections and structure-preserving reductions on smooth manifolds, and how can this framework generalize and connect existing MOR techniques for high-dimensional dynamical systems?
595da6e11bb315673d489b15ca9487c16f2545cc.hypothesis: A differential geometric framework for model reduction on manifolds, utilizing nonlinear embeddings and compatible reduction maps, will enable the systematic generalization and unification of existing MOR techniques, including structure-preserving methods for Lagrangian and Hamiltonian systems, and will facilitate the incorporation of data-driven nonlinear projections.
595da6e11bb315673d489b15ca9487c16f2545cc.proposed_method: A comprehensive differential geometric framework will be constructed for model reduction of high-dimensional dynamical systems formulated on smooth manifolds. The approach will involve defining the full-order model (FOM) as a differential equation on a high-dimensional manifold, then identifying a low-dimensional submanifold via a smooth embedding. Compatible nonlinear reduction and reconstruction maps will be developed, allowing the reduced-order model (ROM) to evolve on the submanifold. The framework will generalize classical linear-subspace MOR, nonlinear projection methods (including those based on machine learning such as autoencoders), and structure-preserving reductions for Lagrangian and Hamiltonian systems. Theoretical properties, such as exact reproduction and relaxation of projection properties for autoencoders, will be derived within this unified setting.
595da6e11bb315673d489b15ca9487c16f2545cc.experiment_details: Experiments will be designed to validate the proposed framework on a range of high-dimensional dynamical systems, including transport-dominated problems and systems with Lagrangian or Hamiltonian structure. Benchmark datasets will include solutions to parametric partial differential equations (such as the advection equation, wave equation, and Burgers’ equation), as well as synthetic and real-world data where structure preservation is critical. Baseline comparisons will be made against classical linear-subspace MOR, existing nonlinear projection methods, and structure-preserving MOR techniques. Evaluation metrics will include approximation accuracy, computational efficiency, and the ability to preserve geometric or physical structure. Data-driven construction of nonlinear mappings (e.g., via autoencoders or polynomial parameterizations) will be incorporated and assessed within the framework.
595da6e11bb315673d489b15ca9487c16f2545cc.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified differential geometric framework for model reduction on manifolds that subsumes and generalizes a wide range of existing MOR techniques, including both linear and nonlinear projection approaches as well as structure-preserving methods for Lagrangian and Hamiltonian systems. The framework provides a systematic way to construct and analyze nonlinear reduction maps, enables the inclusion of data-driven and machine learning-based projections, and establishes new theoretical results such as exact reproduction on manifolds and relaxed projection properties for autoencoders. This abstraction facilitates the derivation of shared properties across different MOR methods and offers a principled foundation for future developments in nonlinear and structure-preserving model reduction.

5971402c4cee5863b25c99405e886b673ade223c.title: Is Value Learning Really the Main Bottleneck in Offline RL?
5971402c4cee5863b25c99405e886b673ade223c.research_question: What are the primary bottlenecks limiting the performance of offline reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms, and how do value function learning, policy extraction, and policy generalization contribute to these limitations across diverse tasks and data regimes?
5971402c4cee5863b25c99405e886b673ade223c.hypothesis: Contrary to the prevailing belief that value function estimation is the main bottleneck in offline RL, it is hypothesized that policy extraction mechanisms and policy generalization to out-of-distribution states at test time are often the dominant factors limiting performance and scalability.
5971402c4cee5863b25c99405e886b673ade223c.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical analysis will be conducted to systematically disentangle and evaluate the contributions of value function learning, policy extraction, and policy generalization in offline RL. The study will utilize decoupled offline RL algorithms, allowing for independent training of value functions and subsequent policy extraction using different objectives. Three value learning methods (SARSA, IQL, CRL) and three policy extraction approaches (Advantage-Weighted Regression (AWR), behavior-constrained policy gradient (DDPG+BC), and sampling-based action selection (SfBC)) will be examined. Data-scaling experiments will be performed by varying the quantity and quality of data available for value and policy learning, and the impact of these factors on performance will be visualized using data-scaling matrices. Additionally, test-time policy generalization will be assessed by measuring policy accuracy on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution states, and by introducing simple test-time policy improvement techniques that leverage the learned value function during evaluation rollouts.
5971402c4cee5863b25c99405e886b673ade223c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on eight diverse environments, including state-based and pixel-based tasks, robotic locomotion and manipulation, and goal-conditioned as well as single-task settings. Datasets will vary in size, quality, and coverage, with some tasks using highly suboptimal or exploratory data. Each combination of value learning and policy extraction method will be evaluated across multiple data regimes, with hyperparameters individually tuned for each setting. Baselines will include imitation learning and standard offline RL algorithms. Performance will be measured using standard RL metrics (e.g., normalized return), and policy accuracy will be quantified using mean squared error (MSE) against expert policies on training, validation, and evaluation (test-time) state distributions. The effect of additional test-time training (offline-to-online RL) will also be explored to assess generalization bottlenecks.
5971402c4cee5863b25c99405e886b673ade223c.novelty_claims: The proposed analysis offers a holistic, large-scale empirical investigation into the interplay between value learning, policy extraction, and generalization in offline RL, extending beyond prior studies that focused on isolated components or limited environments. The work challenges the conventional wisdom that value function learning is the primary bottleneck, providing evidence that policy extraction objectives and test-time generalization are often more critical. The proposal introduces actionable guidelines for practitioners, such as preferring behavior-constrained policy gradient methods over value-weighted behavioral cloning for policy extraction, and highlights the importance of high-coverage data and test-time policy improvement for enhancing generalization. The findings are expected to inform future algorithmic development and practical deployment of offline RL systems.

597f913dfd17b677f5bd8ba500a8736e315f442f.title: Risk-Sensitive Diffusion: Robustly Optimizing Diffusion Models with Noisy Samples
597f913dfd17b677f5bd8ba500a8736e315f442f.research_question: How can diffusion models be robustly optimized for generative modeling tasks when training data consists of noisy non-image samples, each accompanied by a vector quantifying sample-specific data quality (risk vector)?
597f913dfd17b677f5bd8ba500a8736e315f442f.hypothesis: Incorporating risk vectors into the diffusion process via a risk-sensitive stochastic differential equation (SDE) will enable robust optimization of diffusion models, minimizing the negative impact of noisy samples and outperforming risk-unaware and risk-conditional baselines, even under non-Gaussian noise perturbations.
597f913dfd17b677f5bd8ba500a8736e315f442f.proposed_method: A novel risk-sensitive diffusion framework will be developed, where each noisy training sample is paired with a risk vector indicating its data quality. The diffusion process will be governed by a risk-sensitive SDE, whose coefficients are parameterized by the risk vector. Analytical forms of the risk-sensitive SDE will be derived for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian (e.g., Cauchy) noise perturbations, ensuring that, under certain conditions, the marginal distributions of noisy and clean samples align during training. An error measure, perturbation instability, will be introduced to quantify the discrepancy between the distributions induced by noisy and clean samples, and the SDE coefficients will be optimized to minimize this measure. Training and sampling algorithms will be adapted to utilize the risk-sensitive SDE, allowing the model to leverage both clean and noisy samples robustly.
597f913dfd17b677f5bd8ba500a8736e315f442f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple real-world tabular and time-series datasets, including MIMIC-III, WARDS, Abalone, Telemonitoring, and Mushroom. Datasets will be artificially corrupted with both Gaussian and Cauchy noise, and risk vectors will be estimated using methods such as Gaussian process interpolation (for time-series) and k-nearest neighbors with median absolute deviation (for tabular data). Baselines will include standard diffusion models (VE SDE, VPSDE) and several risk-conditional models that treat risk as conditional information. Evaluation metrics will include Wasserstein Distance and PRD (precision-recall for distributions) curves to assess the alignment between generated and clean data distributions. Experimental setup will ensure that the impact of both correctly specified and mis-specified noise types is measured.
597f913dfd17b677f5bd8ba500a8736e315f442f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to introduce risk vectors for robust optimization of diffusion models with noisy samples, providing a principled method—risk-sensitive SDE—that incorporates sample-specific risk information into the generative process. Analytical solutions are derived for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian noise, with theoretical guarantees of stability under Gaussian perturbations and minimal instability under more general noise. The method demonstrates significant empirical improvements over existing baselines, even when the noise distribution is unknown or mis-specified, and is applicable to a wide range of real-world non-image data scenarios.

59854c05cb5c5ed2f2a1633dd08269aa843d3314.title: Permutation Equivariant Neural Functionals
59854c05cb5c5ed2f2a1633dd08269aa843d3314.research_question: How can neural network architectures be designed to effectively process the weights or gradients of other neural networks, while incorporating the permutation symmetries inherent in neural network weight spaces?
59854c05cb5c5ed2f2a1633dd08269aa843d3314.hypothesis: Encoding neuron permutation symmetries as an inductive bias in neural functional networks will improve their effectiveness and efficiency in processing the weights of other neural networks across a range of tasks, compared to non-equivariant or data-augmented approaches.
59854c05cb5c5ed2f2a1633dd08269aa843d3314.proposed_method: A framework will be developed for constructing neural functional networks (NFNs) that are permutation equivariant with respect to the symmetries present in the weight spaces of deep feedforward networks. The core building block will be the neural functional layer (NF-Layer), which enforces permutation equivariance via a parameter sharing scheme derived from the symmetry group acting on the weights. Two variants of NF-Layers will be designed: one for hidden neuron permutation (HNP) symmetry and one for full neuron permutation (NP) symmetry, each balancing parameter efficiency and expressiveness. These NF-Layers will be composed with pointwise nonlinearities to construct deep equivariant neural functionals, and an IO-encoding scheme will be introduced to break input/output symmetry when necessary. The framework will be extended to handle convolutional neural network (CNN) weight spaces by appropriately folding spatial and channel dimensions.
59854c05cb5c5ed2f2a1633dd08269aa843d3314.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of tasks requiring the processing of neural network weights, including: (1) predicting the generalization (test accuracy) of CNN classifiers using the SmallCNNZoo dataset (with subsets such as CIFAR-10-GS and SVHN-GS), (2) classifying the content of implicit neural representations (INRs) of images and 3D shapes using datasets such as MNIST, FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10, ShapeNet-10, and ScanNet-10, (3) predicting 'winning ticket' sparsity masks at initialization for MLPs (on MNIST) and CNNs (on CIFAR-10), and (4) editing INR weights to perform image-space transformations (dilation and contrast adjustment) using generated training pairs. Baselines will include MLPs with and without permutation augmentation, pointwise ablations, and existing methods such as STATNN and inr2vec. Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy, Kendall's tau for rank correlation, and mean squared error for editing tasks. Experimental setups will ensure fair parameter counts and include permutation-augmented training where appropriate.
59854c05cb5c5ed2f2a1633dd08269aa843d3314.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled, symmetry-inspired framework for designing neural functional networks that process neural network weights, explicitly encoding neuron permutation symmetries as an architectural inductive bias. The method generalizes and extends prior work by supporting both hidden and full neuron permutation symmetries, improving parameter efficiency and scalability, and enabling application to both MLP and CNN weight spaces. The framework also introduces IO-encoding to handle cases where input/output symmetry must be broken. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate consistent outperformance of non-equivariant and data-augmented baselines across a variety of challenging weight-space tasks.

598d92f3fb272f07f44a70dc7f9cbe0fab2b6034.title: 3D Reconstruction with Spatial Memory
598d92f3fb272f07f44a70dc7f9cbe0fab2b6034.research_question: How can dense 3D geometry be reconstructed from collections of ordered or unordered images, without prior knowledge of camera parameters, in a manner that is both incremental and real-time, while maintaining generalization across diverse scenes?
598d92f3fb272f07f44a70dc7f9cbe0fab2b6034.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that an external spatial memory, combined with a transformer-based architecture, can enable direct regression of per-image 3D pointmaps in a global coordinate system from image collections, eliminating the need for optimization-based alignment and enabling real-time, incremental 3D reconstruction with strong generalization.
598d92f3fb272f07f44a70dc7f9cbe0fab2b6034.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that leverages a transformer-based architecture to directly regress dense 3D pointmaps from each image in a sequence, expressing all predictions in a common global coordinate system. The approach introduces an external spatial memory, which encodes previously predicted 3D information and is queried at each step to inform the reconstruction of subsequent frames. The architecture consists of a ViT encoder, two intertwined decoders (target and reference), and a lightweight memory encoder. The target decoder produces query features for memory access, while the reference decoder reconstructs the current frame using fused features from the memory. Memory management includes a dense working memory (recent frames) and a sparse long-term memory, with strategies for memory consolidation and attention weight clipping to ensure robustness and scalability. Training employs curriculum sampling, confidence-aware regression loss, and a scale loss to encourage accurate and stable 3D predictions.
598d92f3fb272f07f44a70dc7f9cbe0fab2b6034.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a mixture of indoor and outdoor datasets, including Habitat, ScanNet, ScanNet++, ARKitScenes, BlendedMVS, and Co3D-v2 for training, and 7Scenes, NRGBD, and DTU for evaluation to test generalization. Baselines will include DUSt3R (with and without full-resolution and few-view settings) and FrozenRecon, representing both learning-based and optimization-based approaches. Evaluation metrics will comprise accuracy, completion, and normal consistency, with reconstructions aligned to ground truth via scale normalization. The experimental setup will use 224x224 image inputs due to computational constraints, and performance will be measured in terms of both reconstruction quality and real-time inference speed (frames per second). Ablation studies will analyze the impact of memory size, memory management strategies, and view selection functions.
598d92f3fb272f07f44a70dc7f9cbe0fab2b6034.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new paradigm for dense 3D reconstruction by eliminating the need for optimization-based global alignment, enabling direct, end-to-end regression of globally aligned pointmaps from images. The use of an external spatial memory for incremental reconstruction is novel in this context, allowing the system to operate online in real time (over 50 fps) and generalize to unseen datasets. The approach unifies multiple sub-tasks of the traditional 3D reconstruction pipeline within a single transformer-based framework, reducing engineering complexity and improving robustness. Additional innovations include curriculum training for long-term dependency learning, memory management inspired by human memory models, and a confidence-aware loss tailored for dense geometry prediction.

59aca96a6a64bbf9f1a247faa80977771222c117.title: Whoever Started the Interference Should End It: Guiding Data-Free Model Merging via Task Vectors
59aca96a6a64bbf9f1a247faa80977771222c117.research_question: How can multiple fine-tuned expert models be merged into a single unified multi-task model without access to additional data, while minimizing parameter interference and preserving multi-task generalization capabilities?
