59aca96a6a64bbf9f1a247faa80977771222c117.hypothesis: The task vectors of linear layers in neural networks form an approximate linear subspace of their corresponding input space, and leveraging this property enables effective, data-free model merging that minimizes interference among expert models.
59aca96a6a64bbf9f1a247faa80977771222c117.proposed_method: A new data-free model merging approach, WUDI-Merging, is proposed to integrate multiple expert models into a single multi-task model without requiring any additional data or rescaling coefficients. The method is based on the theoretical insight that task vectors in linear layers constitute an approximate linear subspace of the input space. The merging process involves formulating an optimization objective that minimizes the upper bound of interference between expert models, guided by their task vectors. This is achieved by sequentially optimizing the merged task vector for each linear layer using gradient descent (Adam optimizer), with a balanced weighting mechanism to account for the scale of each task vector, thereby reducing interference and ensuring robust generalization across tasks.
59aca96a6a64bbf9f1a247faa80977771222c117.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both vision and language benchmarks. For vision tasks, multi-task model merging will be evaluated across eight image classification datasets using ViT-based architectures (ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16, ViT-L/14) derived from CLIP. For discriminative language tasks, the GLUE benchmark will be used with RoBERTa-Base and RoBERTa-Large models, while generative language tasks will be tested using Llama2 and LoRA-fine-tuned models (Flan-T5-base, Qwen-14B). Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art data-free model merging methods (Weight Averaging, Fisher Merging, RegMean, Task Arithmetic, Ties-Merging, Consensus Merging, PCB Merging) as well as test-time adaptation methods (AdaMerging, Representation Surgery). Evaluation metrics will include average accuracy and normalized scores across tasks. The experimental setup will use Adam optimizer with a learning rate of 1e-5 and 300 optimization steps, focusing on linear layers for merging. Computational efficiency (time and GPU memory) will also be measured.
59aca96a6a64bbf9f1a247faa80977771222c117.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretically grounded, data-free model merging method that leverages the approximate linear subspace property of task vectors in linear layers, enabling effective minimization of interference without access to additional data or the need for rescaling coefficients. The approach is simple, computationally efficient, and general-purpose, achieving state-of-the-art performance in data-free model merging scenarios and even outperforming mainstream test-time adaptation methods in empirical evaluations. The method also demonstrates robustness to the number of tasks and model architectures, and provides a scalable solution that requires minimal computational resources.

59b7448f816908cfb49a2ab5e63b2fa5786387f7.title: Exphormer: Sparse Transformers for Graphs
59b7448f816908cfb49a2ab5e63b2fa5786387f7.research_question: How can graph transformer architectures be made more scalable and efficient for large graphs, while maintaining or improving accuracy on graph learning and representation tasks compared to existing message-passing networks and transformer-based models?
59b7448f816908cfb49a2ab5e63b2fa5786387f7.hypothesis: A sparse attention mechanism for graph transformers, leveraging expander graphs and virtual global nodes, can achieve linear complexity in the number of nodes and edges, enabling scalability to large graphs while preserving or improving accuracy relative to dense attention and message-passing baselines.
59b7448f816908cfb49a2ab5e63b2fa5786387f7.proposed_method: The proposed method develops a sparse graph transformer architecture, named EXPHORMER, which constructs the attention pattern using three main components: (1) edges from a random regular expander graph to ensure spectral approximation and efficient information propagation; (2) a small number of virtual global nodes connected to all graph nodes to provide global context and universal approximation capabilities; and (3) local neighborhood edges from the input graph to preserve local topological information. The expander graph is generated using a random permutation process to guarantee expansion properties, and learnable embeddings are used for different edge types and virtual nodes. The attention mechanism is implemented as a single unified layer that distinguishes edge types via edge features, and the architecture is modular, allowing the inclusion or exclusion of expander or global node components depending on the dataset. The EXPHORMER layer is integrated within the GraphGPS framework, replacing the standard transformer component, and combined with message-passing neural network (MPNN) layers for enhanced expressivity.
59b7448f816908cfb49a2ab5e63b2fa5786387f7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of graph learning benchmarks, including image-based graph datasets (CIFAR10, MNIST, PascalVOC-SP, COCO-SP), synthetic SBM datasets (PATTERN, CLUSTER), code graph datasets (MalNet-Tiny), molecular datasets (Peptides-Func, Peptides-Struct, PCQM-Contact), and large-scale transductive datasets (CS, Physics, ogbn-arxiv, Computer, Photo). The method will be compared against a wide range of baselines: traditional GNNs (GCN, GIN, GAT, GatedGCN, PNA, DGN), dense and sparse graph transformers (SAN, Graphormer, BigBird, Performer, NAGphormer), and the GraphGPS framework with both full and sparse attention. Evaluation metrics include accuracy, F1 score, average precision, mean absolute error, and mean reciprocal rank, depending on the dataset. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the contribution of each attention component (local, expander, global nodes), and scalability will be evaluated by training on graphs with up to hundreds of thousands of nodes and edges, monitoring memory usage and batch sizes.
59b7448f816908cfb49a2ab5e63b2fa5786387f7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a graph-centric sparse attention mechanism that achieves linear time and memory complexity by combining expander graphs and virtual global nodes, a design tailored specifically for general graphs rather than sequences. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the method spectrally approximates full attention and possesses universal approximation properties with only a logarithmic number of layers. Empirical results are expected to show state-of-the-art or highly competitive performance on a wide range of benchmarks, outperforming both existing sparse and dense transformer models as well as message-passing networks, while enabling scalability to much larger graphs than previously feasible for graph transformers.

59bcb50ca3406f2761472b5934c7b8ba1131ff81.title: Beyond Self-Repellent Kernels: History-Driven Target Towards Efficient Nonlinear MCMC on General Graphs
59bcb50ca3406f2761472b5934c7b8ba1131ff81.research_question: How can sampling efficiency and variance reduction be improved for Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods on general graphs, while maintaining computational scalability and compatibility with both reversible and non-reversible samplers, especially in large or high-dimensional discrete state spaces?
59bcb50ca3406f2761472b5934c7b8ba1131ff81.hypothesis: A history-driven target (HDT) framework that embeds self-repellent behavior into the target distribution, rather than the transition kernel, will enable efficient, unbiased, and low-variance sampling on general graphs. This approach is expected to reduce computational overhead, support both reversible and non-reversible MCMC algorithms, and maintain scalability with limited memory resources.
59bcb50ca3406f2761472b5934c7b8ba1131ff81.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a history-driven target (HDT) framework for MCMC sampling on general graphs. Instead of modifying the transition kernel as in self-repellent random walks (SRRW), the HDT approach dynamically replaces the original target distribution µ with a history-dependent target π[x], where x represents the empirical measure of past state visits. The new target π[x] is defined as π_i[x] ∝ µ_i (x_i / µ_i)^(-α), with α ≥ 0 controlling the strength of self-repellency. This design requires only local information between the current and candidate states, preserving a lightweight, sequential implementation. The framework is compatible with any MCMC sampler, including both reversible (e.g., Metropolis-Hastings, Multiple-Try Metropolis) and non-reversible (e.g., non-reversible MH, 2-cycle methods) algorithms, by simply substituting µ with π[x] in the acceptance criteria. To address memory constraints in large graphs, a Least Recently Used (LRU) cache scheme is proposed to approximate the empirical measure using only a subset of recently visited states.
59bcb50ca3406f2761472b5934c7b8ba1131ff81.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on real-world graph datasets such as Facebook and p2p-Gnutella04, evaluating the performance of HDT-enhanced MCMC samplers (e.g., HDT-MHRW, HDT-MTM, HDT-MHDA) against their base versions and SRRW. Both reversible and non-reversible MCMC algorithms will be tested. Evaluation metrics will include total variation distance (TVD) between the empirical and target distributions, and normalized root mean squared error (NRMSE) for group-size estimation tasks. Experiments will assess convergence speed, variance reduction, and computational cost under both fixed step and fixed computational budget settings. The impact of initializations, fake visit counts, and memory-efficient LRU caching will also be systematically studied, with each configuration run for 1000 independent trials and appropriate burn-in periods.
59bcb50ca3406f2761472b5934c7b8ba1131ff81.novelty_claims: The proposed HDT framework is the first to decouple self-repellent behavior from the transition kernel and embed it directly into the target distribution, enabling compatibility with both reversible and non-reversible MCMC samplers. It eliminates the computational overhead associated with SRRW by requiring only local information, and provides theoretical guarantees of unbiased sampling and O(1/α) variance reduction. The method introduces a scalable LRU cache scheme for efficient sampling in large or high-dimensional state spaces. Empirical results demonstrate consistent performance gains and robustness across various settings, outperforming existing methods in both efficiency and adaptability.

59cf4f0391430523cff7d7ca1819389476ff87a6.title: Transformers Can Do Arithmetic with the Right Embeddings
59cf4f0391430523cff7d7ca1819389476ff87a6.research_question: Can transformer-based language models be enabled to perform complex arithmetic and algorithmic reasoning tasks, such as multi-digit addition, multiplication, and sorting, with strong generalization to problem sizes far beyond those seen during training, by improving their ability to represent positional information and by modifying their architectural components?
59cf4f0391430523cff7d7ca1819389476ff87a6.hypothesis: Enhancing positional encoding for numerical tokens and incorporating architectural modifications such as input injection and recurrent (looped) layers will enable transformers to accurately perform arithmetic and algorithmic reasoning tasks, generalizing to much larger and more complex problems than those encountered during training.
59cf4f0391430523cff7d7ca1819389476ff87a6.proposed_method: A novel positional embedding scheme, termed Abacus Embeddings, will be developed to encode the position of each digit relative to the start of a number, ensuring that all digits of the same significance share the same embedding. This embedding will be combined with standard or advanced positional embeddings (such as FIRE or RoPE) to maintain compatibility with non-numerical tokens. The transformer architecture will be further enhanced by introducing input injection, where the embedded input is added to each decoder layer, and by employing looped (recurrent) transformer architectures, where one or more decoder layers are applied recurrently to increase effective depth. Progressive loss computation will be used during training, combining losses from multiple forward passes with varying numbers of recurrences to encourage generalization.
59cf4f0391430523cff7d7ca1819389476ff87a6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using decoder-only causal language models trained from scratch on synthetic datasets for addition, subtraction, multiplication, and sorting tasks. Training datasets will consist of up to 20 million samples, with operand lengths up to 20 digits for addition and up to 15 digits for multiplication, and arrays of up to 10 numbers for sorting. Models will be evaluated on in-distribution (ID), out-of-distribution (OOD), and extreme OOD (100+ digit) test sets, measuring exact match accuracy (all output digits must be correct). Baselines will include standard transformer architectures with existing positional embeddings (FIRE, NoPE, RoPE), and ablations will compare the impact of Abacus Embeddings, input injection, and recurrence. Experiments will be run on single or multiple Nvidia RTX A4000 GPUs, with training capped at 8 or 64 exaFLOP depending on task complexity. Results will be averaged over three runs for consistency.
59cf4f0391430523cff7d7ca1819389476ff87a6.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces Abacus Embeddings, a new positional embedding method specifically designed for numerical reasoning, enabling transformers to align digits of the same significance and dramatically improve length generalization in arithmetic tasks. The combination of Abacus Embeddings with architectural modifications such as input injection and looped (recurrent) transformers achieves state-of-the-art generalization, solving addition problems up to six times longer than those seen in training and achieving near-perfect accuracy on 100-digit addition. The method also demonstrates transferability to other algorithmic tasks, such as multiplication and sorting, and shows that Abacus Embeddings can be effectively combined with other positional embedding schemes for broader applicability.

5a1c1fafc07c1e9441c41d0315b55eb0eccd558a.title: A Statistical Theory of Regularization-Based Continual Learning
5a1c1fafc07c1e9441c41d0315b55eb0eccd558a.research_question: How can regularization-based continual learning algorithms be theoretically analyzed and optimized to balance forward and backward knowledge transfer, avoid catastrophic forgetting, and handle data heterogeneity in a sequence of linear regression tasks?
5a1c1fafc07c1e9441c41d0315b55eb0eccd558a.hypothesis: Properly designed generalized ℓ2-regularization with matrix-valued hyperparameters can achieve estimation error rates comparable to an oracle estimator, thereby preventing catastrophic forgetting and optimally balancing knowledge transfer in continual learning, even under task heterogeneity and overparameterization.
5a1c1fafc07c1e9441c41d0315b55eb0eccd558a.proposed_method: A statistical framework is developed for regularization-based continual learning in linear regression, focusing on a family of generalized ℓ2-regularization algorithms parameterized by matrix-valued hyperparameters. The method derives an iterative update formula for the estimation error of these estimators, enabling the identification of hyperparameters that optimize the trade-off between forward and backward knowledge transfer and adapt to data heterogeneity. The approach explicitly computes the estimation error of the optimal algorithm, showing it matches the order of the oracle estimator that has access to all data simultaneously. Theoretical analysis also establishes the equivalence between early stopping and generalized ℓ2-regularization under certain conditions, providing a unified view of regularization strategies in continual learning.
5a1c1fafc07c1e9441c41d0315b55eb0eccd558a.experiment_details: Simulation experiments are conducted to validate the theoretical findings. Two data generation settings are considered: one with and one without covariate shift, where the true parameter is fixed and features/noise are sampled from Gaussian distributions, with or without varying covariance matrices across tasks. The experiments compare the proposed generalized ℓ2-regularized estimator (GR) against the minimum norm estimator (MN), continual ridge regression (CRR), and the oracle estimator. Key evaluation metrics include estimation error as a function of task number, with repeated trials to report average results. The impact of noise level and covariate shift is systematically assessed, and regularization matrices for GR are set according to the theoretically derived practical algorithm.
5a1c1fafc07c1e9441c41d0315b55eb0eccd558a.novelty_claims: The proposal provides the first explicit statistical theory for regularization-based continual learning in linear regression, including lower bounds for existing methods and a new generalized ℓ2-regularized estimator that achieves oracle-level error rates. It introduces a principled approach to selecting matrix-valued hyperparameters that balance forward and backward transfer and adapt to heterogeneity. The work also establishes a novel equivalence between early stopping and generalized ℓ2-regularization in continual learning, extending known results from single-task learning. Theoretical insights are complemented by practical algorithms and empirical validation, offering guidance for the design of continual learning systems.

5a3d70689925df014c46d1cd50dfc8a368cb4c86.title: Federated Learning Based on Dynamic Regularization
5a3d70689925df014c46d1cd50dfc8a368cb4c86.research_question: How can communication efficiency and convergence in federated learning be improved, particularly under challenging scenarios such as device heterogeneity, partial participation, massively distributed and unbalanced data, without sacrificing model performance?
5a3d70689925df014c46d1cd50dfc8a368cb4c86.hypothesis: Introducing a dynamic regularization scheme that aligns local device objectives with the global empirical loss will enable more efficient federated learning, reducing communication costs and improving convergence rates across a variety of data distributions and device participation regimes.
5a3d70689925df014c46d1cd50dfc8a368cb4c86.proposed_method: A federated learning framework is developed in which, during each communication round, a subset of devices is randomly selected to participate. Each participating device receives the current global model from the server and optimizes a local objective that combines its empirical loss with dynamically updated linear and quadratic penalty terms. The penalty terms are constructed such that, in the limit, the stationary points of the local objectives are consistent with those of the global empirical loss. Devices update their models by minimizing this penalized objective, and send their updated models back to the server. The server aggregates these updates, adjusts a global auxiliary variable, and updates the global model accordingly. This approach is designed to be agnostic to device heterogeneity and robust to varying participation and data imbalance.
5a3d70689925df014c46d1cd50dfc8a368cb4c86.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of benchmark datasets including MNIST, EMNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Shakespeare, as well as synthetic data. Both IID and non-IID (using Dirichlet distributions for label imbalance) data splits will be considered, along with balanced and unbalanced local data settings. The proposed method will be compared against strong baselines such as FedAvg, FedProx, and SCAFFOLD, using the number of model transmissions required to reach target test accuracy as the primary evaluation metric. Experimental setups will vary the number of devices (moderate to massive), device participation rates (including partial and full participation), and the degree of data heterogeneity and imbalance. Neural network architectures will be matched to those used in prior work for fair comparison.
5a3d70689925df014c46d1cd50dfc8a368cb4c86.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel dynamic regularization mechanism that ensures asymptotic alignment between local and global optima in federated learning. The method achieves significant reductions in communication cost compared to existing baselines, is robust to device heterogeneity, partial participation, and unbalanced data, and requires less hyperparameter tuning. Theoretical analysis establishes improved convergence rates in both convex and non-convex settings, and empirical results demonstrate consistent communication savings across a wide range of federated learning scenarios.

5a47fef193484287e442d6d82af1969b5b269015.title: CORA: Adapting CLIP for Open-Vocabulary Detection with Region Prompting and Anchor Pre-Matching
5a47fef193484287e442d6d82af1969b5b269015.research_question: How can open-vocabulary object detection be improved to accurately detect and localize objects from novel categories, leveraging large-scale vision-language pre-trained models without requiring additional image-text data or extensive re-training?
5a47fef193484287e442d6d82af1969b5b269015.hypothesis: Adapting a vision-language model such as CLIP for region-level recognition through region prompting and anchor pre-matching will mitigate distribution mismatches and enable efficient, generalizable object localization and classification for open-vocabulary detection.
5a47fef193484287e442d6d82af1969b5b269015.proposed_method: A novel DETR-style framework will be developed that adapts CLIP for open-vocabulary detection via two core innovations: region prompting and anchor pre-matching. Region prompting will introduce learnable prompts directly into the pooled regional features, aligning the distribution of region-level embeddings with those of whole-image embeddings from CLIP, thereby improving classification accuracy and generalization to novel classes. Anchor pre-matching will implement a class-aware matching mechanism, where object queries are pre-matched to class name embeddings using the CLIP text encoder, enabling efficient, class-aware box regression without repetitive per-class inference. The object localization branch will use a transformer-based architecture (DAB-DETR) to refine object queries and anchor boxes, while the classification branch will use a CLIP-based region classifier with RoIAlign and attention pooling. Additional training techniques such as class dropout and CLIP-aligned labeling will be incorporated to further enhance generalization.
5a47fef193484287e442d6d82af1969b5b269015.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the COCO and LVIS open-vocabulary detection benchmarks. The COCO dataset will be split into base and novel classes, with training on base classes and evaluation on both base and novel classes using AP50 as the primary metric. The LVIS dataset will be used to evaluate large-vocabulary generalization, with mean AP reported for novel classes. Baselines will include state-of-the-art open-vocabulary detection methods such as RegionCLIP, VL-PLM, ViLD, OV-DETR, and others, ensuring fair comparison by using the same pre-trained CLIP models. Additional experiments will assess the impact of region prompting and anchor pre-matching via ablation studies, and region classification performance will be evaluated using mAP. When extra data is available, a variant (CORA+) will be trained using both ground-truth and pseudo-labeled boxes to assess performance gains.
5a47fef193484287e442d6d82af1969b5b269015.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces region prompting to directly address the distribution gap between whole-image and region-level features in CLIP, leading to improved generalization to novel classes. Anchor pre-matching enables efficient, class-aware object localization without the need for repetitive per-class inference, overcoming limitations of previous DETR-based open-vocabulary detectors. The framework achieves state-of-the-art results on COCO and LVIS open-vocabulary detection benchmarks without requiring extra image-text data or re-training for new categories. Additional training strategies such as class dropout and CLIP-aligned labeling further enhance generalization and convergence, distinguishing the approach from prior works.

5a5671b638ec64c67df3166f0cddcecb25b095b7.title: A Reductions Approach to Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning with Optimized Certainty Equivalents
5a5671b638ec64c67df3166f0cddcecb25b095b7.research_question: How can reinforcement learning algorithms be designed to optimize general risk-sensitive objectives, specifically those expressible as optimized certainty equivalents (OCE), in environments where optimal policies may be history-dependent and the underlying Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) exhibit complex structures such as exogenous block MDPs or rich observations?
5a5671b638ec64c67df3166f0cddcecb25b095b7.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by augmenting the MDP state with a scalar budget and leveraging reductions to risk-neutral RL, it is possible to develop meta-algorithms that can efficiently and optimally solve OCE-based risk-sensitive RL problems, even when optimal policies are history-dependent and the MDP structure is complex.
5a5671b638ec64c67df3166f0cddcecb25b095b7.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops two meta-algorithms for risk-sensitive reinforcement learning with OCE objectives. The first meta-algorithm is grounded in optimism and utilizes optimistic RL oracles (such as UCB-VI, Rep-UCB, or GOLF) within an augmented MDP (AugMDP) framework, where the state is extended with a budget variable that tracks cumulative rewards. This allows the use of risk-neutral RL algorithms to optimize OCE objectives by selecting both an optimal Markovian policy in the AugMDP and an appropriate initial budget. The second meta-algorithm is based on policy optimization (PO) oracles, such as natural policy gradient (NPG), and operates in the AugMDP with a discrete set of initial budgets, providing guarantees of monotone improvement and global convergence. Both methods are designed to be compatible with model-based and model-free RL oracles and are applicable to a wide class of OCE risk measures, including CVaR, entropic risk, and mean-variance.
5a5671b638ec64c67df3166f0cddcecb25b095b7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic MDPs specifically constructed to require history-dependent policies for OCE optimality, such as a two-state MDP where the optimal CVaR policy is non-Markovian. The meta-algorithms will be instantiated with various RL oracles: UCB-VI for tabular MDPs, Rep-UCB for low-rank MDPs, and GOLF for exogenous block MDPs. Baselines will include standard Markovian policies and existing risk-sensitive RL algorithms. Evaluation metrics will focus on OCE regret, convergence to the optimal OCE value, and the ability to learn history-dependent policies. The experimental setup will include both model-based and model-free settings, and results will be analyzed for both statistical and computational efficiency.
5a5671b638ec64c67df3166f0cddcecb25b095b7.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a general reductions-based framework for risk-sensitive RL with OCE objectives, unifying and extending prior work limited to specific risk measures (such as CVaR or entropic risk) and tabular MDPs. It provides the first risk-sensitive regret and PAC bounds for exogenous block MDPs and establishes the first finite-sample guarantees for gradient-based risk-sensitive RL algorithms. The approach enables efficient learning of optimal history-dependent policies by searching over Markovian policies in the AugMDP, and supports both model-based and model-free RL oracles. Additionally, the framework proves novel properties such as monotone improvement for risk-sensitive policy optimization.

5a572cdff855f771f695eaf5c05c6f2586f7a918.title: Systematic Relational Reasoning With Epistemic Graph Neural Networks
5a572cdff855f771f695eaf5c05c6f2586f7a918.research_question: How can scalable and parameter-efficient neural network architectures be developed to enable systematic relational reasoning, particularly in settings that require generalization to longer inference chains and aggregation of information from multiple relational paths, including disjunctive reasoning tasks?
5a572cdff855f771f695eaf5c05c6f2586f7a918.hypothesis: A graph neural network architecture that encodes epistemic inductive biases—by treating node embeddings as epistemic states and simulating the algebraic closure algorithm—will achieve systematic generalization and efficient relational reasoning, outperforming or matching state-of-the-art neuro-symbolic and neural baselines, especially in tasks requiring multi-path and disjunctive reasoning.
5a572cdff855f771f695eaf5c05c6f2586f7a918.proposed_method: A novel graph neural network, termed Epistemic GNN (EpiGNN), is proposed to address systematic relational reasoning. In this approach, node embeddings are interpreted as epistemic states, representing probability distributions over primitive relations, and are iteratively updated via message passing that explicitly simulates the composition of discrete relations as in the Algebraic Closure Algorithm (ACA). The message passing function is designed to handle probabilistic compositions, and the pooling operator aggregates information by simulating intersection operations, ensuring that embeddings reflect sets of possible relationships. The model incorporates both forward and backward message passing to capture different orderings of relational compositions, and supports multi-facet training to improve expressivity while maintaining parameter efficiency. The architecture is aligned with a differentiable approximation of the algebraic closure algorithm, enabling reasoning over both simple path and disjunctive rules.
5a572cdff855f771f695eaf5c05c6f2586f7a918.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several benchmarks: (1) CLUTRR and Graphlog for systematic generalization in relational reasoning, where models are trained on short inference chains and evaluated on longer, unseen chains; (2) two newly introduced benchmarks based on RCC-8 and Interval Algebra, requiring aggregation of information from multiple relational paths and handling disjunctive rules; and (3) standard inductive knowledge graph completion tasks using WN18RR and FB15k-237. Baselines will include state-of-the-art neuro-symbolic methods (such as NCRL, R5, CTP), various GNNs (NBFNet, R-GCN, GAT, GCN), edge transformers, and recurrent models. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy for relational reasoning tasks and Hits@10 for knowledge graph completion, with systematic variation of path lengths and number of paths to assess generalization. Ablation studies will analyze the importance of architectural components such as epistemic embeddings, composition functions, and multi-facet training. Parameter and time complexity will also be compared across models.
5a572cdff855f771f695eaf5c05c6f2586f7a918.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a parameter-efficient and scalable GNN architecture with an explicit epistemic inductive bias for systematic relational reasoning. It is the first GNN-based approach to simulate the algebraic closure algorithm for both simple and disjunctive relational rules, enabling reasoning over multiple relational paths and aggregation of partial information. Two new challenging benchmarks are introduced for multi-path, disjunctive relational reasoning, going beyond existing single-path benchmarks. The method achieves state-of-the-art or highly competitive results on standard and novel benchmarks, and demonstrates superior scalability and parameter efficiency compared to neuro-symbolic and neural baselines.

5a74e5f78a88c25ece84d2651b72bba67328d3b8.title: Adjoint Sampling: Highly Scalable Diffusion Samplers via Adjoint Matching
5a74e5f78a88c25ece84d2651b72bba67328d3b8.research_question: How can highly scalable and efficient diffusion-based sampling algorithms be developed to sample from complex, high-dimensional unnormalized distributions, particularly in settings where energy function evaluations are computationally expensive and ground truth samples are unavailable?
5a74e5f78a88c25ece84d2651b72bba67328d3b8.hypothesis: A novel on-policy variational inference framework, grounded in stochastic optimal control and leveraging adjoint matching with reciprocal projection, will enable significantly more gradient updates per energy evaluation and model sample, leading to efficient and scalable sampling from unnormalized densities in high-dimensional settings.
5a74e5f78a88c25ece84d2651b72bba67328d3b8.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces Adjoint Sampling, a highly efficient algorithm for learning diffusion processes that sample from unnormalized energy functions. The approach formulates the sampling task as a stochastic optimal control (SOC) problem, where the drift of a controlled stochastic differential equation (SDE) is learned to transport an initial Dirac distribution to the target distribution defined by the energy function. The method leverages a Reciprocal Adjoint Matching (RAM) objective, which allows the use of a replay buffer and decouples the expensive simulation of the controlled process from the optimization of the control function. By analytically projecting the current control onto a Schrödinger bridge using closed-form solutions for the base process, the algorithm enables multiple gradient updates per energy evaluation. The framework is further extended to incorporate geometric symmetries (e.g., graph and Euclidean invariance) and periodic boundary conditions, making it applicable to molecular modeling in both cartesian and torsional coordinates.
5a74e5f78a88c25ece84d2651b72bba67328d3b8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world molecular energy functions. Synthetic benchmarks include the 2D 4-particle Double-Well Potential (DW-4), 3D 13-particle Lennard-Jones potential (LJ-13), and 55-particle Lennard-Jones energy (LJ-55), where ground truth samples are available for evaluation. For large-scale evaluation, amortized molecular conformer generation will be performed using the eSEN neural network-based energy model across diverse molecular datasets (e.g., SPICE, GEOM-DRUGS). Baseline methods for comparison include state-of-the-art SOC-based samplers (PIS, DDS), off-policy and regression-based methods (iDEM, LogVariance), and traditional MCMC-based approaches. Evaluation metrics will include geometric 2-Wasserstein distance (accounting for molecular symmetries), 1D energy histogram distances, effective sample size (ESS), recall, precision, and coverage for conformer generation. Ablation studies will assess the impact of reciprocal projection and geometric extensions.
5a74e5f78a88c25ece84d2651b72bba67328d3b8.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first on-policy diffusion-based sampler that allows substantially more gradient updates per energy evaluation and model sample, enabling scalability to high-dimensional and computationally expensive settings. The approach is theoretically grounded in stochastic optimal control and improves upon prior adjoint matching methods by introducing a new objective that implicitly projects the model onto optimal controls without requiring corrective measures such as importance sampling or sequential Monte Carlo. The method supports the incorporation of key symmetries and periodic boundary conditions, and introduces challenging amortized molecule sampling benchmarks that directly advance progress in computational chemistry. The open-sourcing of code and benchmarks is intended to foster further research in scalable sampling methods.

5a8bab2d01bd5c0e4844909e24c19ad88f1e9f24.title: Policy Mirror Descent Inherently Explores Action Space
5a8bab2d01bd5c0e4844909e24c19ad88f1e9f24.research_question: Can online policy gradient methods for reinforcement learning achieve optimal sample complexity without incorporating explicit exploration strategies in the action space?
5a8bab2d01bd5c0e4844909e24c19ad88f1e9f24.hypothesis: Online policy gradient methods, when equipped with appropriately designed on-policy evaluation operators and analyzed with novel techniques, can achieve optimal sample complexity without the need for explicit exploration in the action space.
5a8bab2d01bd5c0e4844909e24c19ad88f1e9f24.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops two novel online policy evaluation operators—Value-Based Estimation (VBE) and Truncated On-Policy Monte Carlo (TOMC)—to be used within the stochastic policy mirror descent (SPMD) framework. VBE operates in two variants: VBE-I, which uses two independent trajectories to estimate value and Q-functions, and VBE-II, which requires only a single trajectory for estimation, enhancing implementation simplicity. TOMC modifies the standard on-policy Monte Carlo method by introducing a truncation step that provides an upper bound on the Q-function when the action's policy probability is low, thus avoiding uniform bias control for all actions. SPMD is then instantiated with these operators, using either the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence or alternative Bregman divergences (such as Tsallis divergence) for the mirror descent update. The method assumes only that the Markov chains induced by the policies are uniformly mixing and exploring over the state space, with no explicit exploration enforced over the action space.
5a8bab2d01bd5c0e4844909e24c19ad88f1e9f24.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on finite Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) with discrete state and action spaces. The evaluation will use both synthetic and standard RL benchmark datasets, where available, to assess the sample complexity and convergence properties of the proposed SPMD variants. Baseline comparisons will include online policy gradient methods with explicit exploration (such as epsilon-exploration and policy perturbation), as well as actor-critic methods that require uniform action exploration. Evaluation metrics will focus on sample complexity to achieve an epsilon-optimal policy, convergence rates, and the probability of controlling the optimality gap. Key experimental setups will include varying the size of the action space, the effective horizon, and the choice of Bregman divergence in the mirror descent step.
5a8bab2d01bd5c0e4844909e24c19ad88f1e9f24.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first online policy gradient methods that achieve O(1/epsilon^2) sample complexity without explicit exploration in the action space. The new policy evaluation operators (VBE and TOMC) enable efficient and practical policy optimization with a single trajectory, overcoming the limitations of prior methods that either require explicit exploration or suffer from poor sample complexity. The analysis demonstrates that inherent exploration can be achieved through the structure of the proposed operators and the SPMD framework, with TOMC providing high-probability control of the optimality gap. The approach also establishes new theoretical bounds that depend only linearly or polynomially on the action space and effective horizon, depending on the choice of divergence, and provides practical algorithms for the proximal policy update step.

5a9cb1b3dc4655218b3deeaf4a2417a9a8cd0891.title: DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision
5a9cb1b3dc4655218b3deeaf4a2417a9a8cd0891.research_question: Can self-supervised learning on large, diverse, and automatically curated image datasets produce robust, general-purpose visual features that transfer effectively across a wide range of computer vision tasks, without the need for supervision or textual guidance?
5a9cb1b3dc4655218b3deeaf4a2417a9a8cd0891.hypothesis: Self-supervised pretraining on a large, diverse, and carefully curated image dataset will yield visual representations that are competitive with or surpass those obtained from weakly-supervised or text-guided pretraining, enabling strong performance on both image-level and pixel-level tasks without the need for fine-tuning.
5a9cb1b3dc4655218b3deeaf4a2417a9a8cd0891.proposed_method: A discriminative self-supervised learning framework will be developed, combining elements of DINO and iBOT losses with centering techniques from SwAV, and incorporating a KoLeo regularizer to encourage feature diversity. The approach will utilize Vision Transformer (ViT) architectures, scaling up to models with over 1 billion parameters. Training will be performed on a newly constructed, diverse, and curated dataset (LVD-142M), assembled via a self-supervised image retrieval pipeline that selects images from a large pool of uncurated web data based on visual similarity to curated sources. Technical innovations will include efficient memory and compute optimizations (e.g., FlashAttention, sequence packing, improved stochastic depth, and fully-sharded data parallelism), and a short high-resolution training phase to enhance pixel-level feature quality. For smaller models, knowledge distillation from the largest trained model will be employed to transfer robust representations.
5a9cb1b3dc4655218b3deeaf4a2417a9a8cd0891.experiment_details: Experiments will involve pretraining ViT models of varying sizes on the LVD-142M dataset, with ablation studies to assess the impact of loss components, data curation, model size, and training resolution. Evaluation will be conducted on a comprehensive suite of computer vision benchmarks, including ImageNet-1k, ImageNet-V2, ImageNet-Sketch, ADE-20k (segmentation), Oxford and Paris retrieval datasets, iNaturalist 2018/2021, Cars, Food101, Places205, and video understanding tasks. Baselines will include state-of-the-art self-supervised and weakly-supervised models such as iBOT and OpenCLIP. Metrics will include top-1 accuracy for classification, mean Intersection-over-Union (mIoU) for segmentation, mean Average Precision (mAP) for retrieval, and additional task-specific metrics. Both k-NN and linear probe evaluations will be used to assess the quality of frozen features.
5a9cb1b3dc4655218b3deeaf4a2417a9a8cd0891.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a scalable, fully self-supervised visual pretraining pipeline that leverages a novel, automatic data curation and retrieval system requiring no metadata or supervision. The method combines and extends recent advances in discriminative self-supervised learning, integrates technical improvements for efficient large-scale training, and demonstrates that self-supervised models can match or exceed the performance of weakly-supervised approaches across diverse tasks. The approach also provides a practical recipe for distilling large models into smaller, more efficient ones without loss of performance, and establishes new state-of-the-art results for general-purpose visual feature learning without reliance on text or labels.

5a9ce2055a0f200fd53b7eeddf1c05f9e01ccf5a.title: Large Language Models and Games: A Survey and Roadmap
5a9ce2055a0f200fd53b7eeddf1c05f9e01ccf5a.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be systematically integrated into various roles within digital and tabletop games, and what are the opportunities, challenges, and future directions for their application in game design, gameplay, player interaction, content generation, and analysis?
5a9ce2055a0f200fd53b7eeddf1c05f9e01ccf5a.hypothesis: LLMs possess the versatility and expressive power to significantly enhance or automate diverse roles in games, including player agents, non-player characters, assistants, commentators, analysts, game masters, mechanics, automated designers, and design assistants, but their effective deployment requires addressing technical, ethical, and domain-specific challenges.
5a9ce2055a0f200fd53b7eeddf1c05f9e01ccf5a.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed to categorize and implement LLMs across multiple roles in games, including but not limited to player agents, NPCs, player assistants, commentators, analysts, game masters, game mechanics, automated designers, and design assistants. For each role, prototype systems will be designed utilizing state-of-the-art LLMs (such as GPT-3/4, Llama, Mistral, and multimodal models like GPT-4V and Llava), with tailored prompting, fine-tuning, or integration with APIs and game engines as appropriate. The methodology will include the transformation of game states and actions into LLM-compatible representations, the design of interaction protocols (e.g., dialogue management, action selection, narrative generation), and the incorporation of safety, memory, and context management strategies. Special attention will be paid to the integration of LLMs with procedural content generation pipelines, reinforcement learning, and co-creative design tools, as well as the mitigation of hallucinations and bias.
5a9ce2055a0f200fd53b7eeddf1c05f9e01ccf5a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a range of game genres and platforms, including board games (e.g., Chess, Go, Othello), text adventure games (e.g., Zork), negotiation games (e.g., Diplomacy), sandbox games (e.g., Minecraft), and custom-designed environments for NPC and social simulation (e.g., Generative Agents, AI People). Datasets will include human gameplay traces, annotated dialogue corpora, and open-source game content repositories. Baselines will consist of traditional rule-based AI, existing machine learning agents, and human performance where applicable. Evaluation metrics will include quantitative measures (e.g., win rate, puzzle solvability, diversity of generated content, clustering accuracy) and qualitative assessments (e.g., believability, engagement, narrative coherence, user satisfaction), with user studies and expert reviews supplementing automated metrics. Additional experiments will explore the effectiveness of LLMs in co-creative design settings and their ability to generalize across unseen games or tasks.
5a9ce2055a0f200fd53b7eeddf1c05f9e01ccf5a.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified, role-based framework for deploying LLMs in games, spanning both in-game and meta-game functions. It claims novelty in systematically exploring underexamined roles for LLMs, such as player assistants, commentators, analysts, and design assistants, and in integrating LLMs with procedural content generation, co-creative tools, and multimodal interfaces. The approach emphasizes the potential for LLMs to enable new forms of player interaction, emergent narrative, and automated content creation, while also addressing technical limitations and ethical considerations unique to the games domain.

5a9d73ff62967d64d9208134304b2c8946005be9.title: OASIS Uncovers: High-Quality T2I Models, Same Old Stereotypes
5a9d73ff62967d64d9208134304b2c8946005be9.research_question: How can stereotypes in text-to-image (T2I) generative models be quantitatively measured and understood in a manner that aligns with sociological definitions, and what are the origins and manifestations of such stereotypes across different models and demographic concepts?
5a9d73ff62967d64d9208134304b2c8946005be9.hypothesis: A quantitative framework that aligns with the sociological definition of stereotypes—specifically, measuring the directional over-representation of stereotypical attributes relative to real-world distributions—will more accurately identify and characterize stereotypes in T2I models than existing bias metrics. Furthermore, such a framework will reveal that even high-fidelity, modern T2I models continue to exhibit strong stereotypical predispositions, particularly for under-represented groups.
5a9d73ff62967d64d9208134304b2c8946005be9.proposed_method: A comprehensive toolbox, OASIS, will be developed to audit and analyze stereotypes in T2I models. OASIS will include two quantitative metrics: (M1) StereotypeScore, which measures the over-representation of stereotypical attributes by comparing the attribute distribution in generated images to real-world statistics, and (M2) Weighted Alignment Score (WALS), which assesses the spectral variance of generated images along specific stereotypical attributes in the feature space. Additionally, two analytical methods will be incorporated: (U1) Stereotypes from Optimized Prompts (StOP), which discovers stereotypical attributes that a T2I model internally associates with a concept by optimizing prompts to maximize alignment with image clusters, and (U2) Stereotype Propagation Index (SPI), which quantifies the emergence and propagation of stereotypical attributes in the latent space during the image generation process. The approach will leverage large language models (LLMs) to generate open-set candidate stereotypes for each concept, and use pre-trained vision-language models (e.g., CLIP) for feature extraction and attribute classification.
5a9d73ff62967d64d9208134304b2c8946005be9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several state-of-the-art open-weight T2I models, including SDv2, SDv3, and FLUX.1. For each model, datasets of 2,000 images per nationality will be generated using prompts devoid of explicit stereotypical information. Candidate stereotype attributes and their descriptions will be automatically generated using LLMs such as ChatGPT and Llama. StereotypeScore will be computed by comparing attribute distributions in generated images to real-world statistics (e.g., census data), while WALS will be calculated using singular value decomposition of CLIP image features. Baseline comparisons will include prior bias metrics based on statistical parity. Additional analyses will use StOP to identify internal model associations and SPI to track the emergence of stereotypes during generation. Evaluation metrics will include the magnitude of stereotype scores, attribute variance (WALS), and qualitative inspection of optimized prompts and generated images. The effect of Internet footprint on stereotype severity will be assessed by correlating stereotype scores with the number of Internet users per nationality.
5a9d73ff62967d64d9208134304b2c8946005be9.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a mathematically grounded, sociologically aligned quantitative definition of stereotypes for T2I models, distinguishing stereotypes from general biases by considering directionality and real-world distributions. OASIS provides the first open-set, automated auditing toolbox that combines distributional and spectral analyses with methods to uncover internal model associations and the temporal emergence of stereotypes. The approach enables nuanced, scalable, and automated auditing of stereotypes in generative models, uncovering persistent and intersectional stereotypes even in advanced T2I models, and highlighting the exacerbation of stereotypes for under-represented groups. This work advances the field by providing actionable metrics and insights for model comparison, auditing, and future mitigation strategies.

5aa3b1009955ce2c8f896e0d5e94e06155ef1e43.title: LLMRec: Large Language Models with Graph Augmentation for Recommendation
5aa3b1009955ce2c8f896e0d5e94e06155ef1e43.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be leveraged to address data sparsity and low-quality side information in recommender systems, particularly by augmenting user-item interaction graphs and enhancing user/item node attributes?
5aa3b1009955ce2c8f896e0d5e94e06155ef1e43.hypothesis: Integrating LLM-based graph augmentation strategies—specifically, reinforcing user-item interaction edges, enhancing item node attributes, and conducting user node profiling—will improve recommendation accuracy and robustness in the presence of sparse implicit feedback and low-quality side information compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.
5aa3b1009955ce2c8f896e0d5e94e06155ef1e43.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that utilizes LLMs to augment recommender system graphs in three key ways: (1) reinforcing user-item interaction edges by employing an LLM-based Bayesian Personalized Ranking (BPR) sampling algorithm to generate additional positive and negative samples from candidate item pools for each user; (2) enhancing item node attributes and user node profiles by prompting LLMs to generate or refine side information (such as genre, director, country, language, age, gender, liked/disliked genres) based on existing data and interaction histories; and (3) incorporating these augmented edges and features into the original graph using semantic projection, collaborative context injection via lightweight GNNs, and feature aggregation with normalization. To ensure the reliability of the augmented data, a denoised data robustification mechanism will be implemented, including noisy implicit feedback pruning and Masked Autoencoder (MAE)-based feature enhancement. The final model will jointly optimize the BPR loss (with noise pruning) and a feature restoration loss for masked features.
5aa3b1009955ce2c8f896e0d5e94e06155ef1e43.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on public benchmark datasets such as Netflix and MovieLens, both enriched with multi-modal side information (textual and visual). Augmentation will be performed using OpenAI's GPT-3.5-turbo and text-embedding-ada-002 models to generate additional implicit feedback and side information. The proposed method will be compared against multiple baselines, including general collaborative filtering methods (MF-BPR, NGCF, LightGCN), methods with side information (VBPR, MMGCN, GRCN), data augmentation methods (LATTICE, MICRO), and self-supervised methods (CLCRec, MMSSL). Evaluation will be based on top-K recommendation metrics: Recall@K, NDCG@K, and Precision@K, using all-ranking protocols and averaging over multiple runs. Ablation studies will assess the impact of each augmentation strategy and robustification component, and hyperparameter sensitivity analyses will be performed. Cost-effectiveness and model-agnostic applicability of the augmentation strategies will also be evaluated.
5aa3b1009955ce2c8f896e0d5e94e06155ef1e43.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to systematically employ LLMs for graph augmentation in recommendation, explicitly augmenting user-item interaction edges, item node attributes, and user node profiles. It introduces a denoised data robustification mechanism combining noisy feedback pruning and MAE-based feature enhancement to ensure data quality. The approach enables LLMs to reason over user-item interaction patterns and generate high-quality, unified semantic features, addressing both data sparsity and side information issues. The method is designed to be model-agnostic, improving performance across various recommender architectures, and demonstrates superior accuracy and robustness compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

5aae7d84f8eaa55f3386cee41d94769e7ab01e9d.title: Pushing Mixture of Experts to the Limit: Extremely Parameter Efficient MoE for Instruction Tuning
5aae7d84f8eaa55f3386cee41d94769e7ab01e9d.research_question: Can mixture of experts (MoE) architectures be adapted for extremely parameter-efficient instruction tuning, enabling robust performance on unseen tasks while updating only a small fraction of large language model parameters?
5aae7d84f8eaa55f3386cee41d94769e7ab01e9d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that integrating lightweight parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) adapters as experts within a MoE framework will enable instruction-tuned models to match or surpass the performance of full fine-tuning and standard PEFT methods, even when updating less than 1% of model parameters.
5aae7d84f8eaa55f3386cee41d94769e7ab01e9d.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed that combines the mixture of experts (MoE) architecture with parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) adapters, specifically (IA)3 vectors and LORA adapters, as lightweight experts. The method introduces two variants: Mixture of Vectors (MoV), which uses (IA)3 scaling vectors as experts, and Mixture of LORA (MoLORA), which uses LORA adapters. In this approach, the base pretrained model remains frozen, and only the experts and router layers are updated during instruction tuning. The MoE layers are integrated into Transformer blocks, where a router network computes softmax-based gating scores over experts, and a soft merging strategy is employed to combine expert outputs. The framework supports both token-level and sentence-level routing, as well as ablations on soft versus discrete (top-k) routing strategies.
5aae7d84f8eaa55f3386cee41d94769e7ab01e9d.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using T5 v1.1+LM models of varying sizes (770M, 3B, 11B parameters) as the base, fine-tuned on the Public Pool of Prompts (P3) dataset, which spans 62 diverse tasks. Evaluation is performed in a zero-shot setting on 8 held-out tasks, including ANLI, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, and 5 SuperGLUE datasets, with median accuracy across prompt templates as the primary metric. Baselines include full model fine-tuning (T0), (IA)3, and LORA PEFT methods. The experimental setup involves 500K training steps with Adafactor optimizer, batch size 32, and sequence lengths of 1024 (input) and 256 (target). Extensive ablation studies are planned to assess the impact of expert count, routing input (token vs sentence embeddings), and routing strategy (soft merging vs top-k selection), as well as scalability across model sizes.
5aae7d84f8eaa55f3386cee41d94769e7ab01e9d.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces an extremely parameter-efficient adaptation of MoE for instruction tuning by leveraging modular, lightweight PEFT adapters as experts, enabling fine-tuning with less than 1% of model parameters. The approach demonstrates that such MoEs can outperform standard PEFT methods and achieve parity with full fine-tuning on unseen tasks, all while maintaining high parameter efficiency and scalability. Additional innovations include the use of soft merging for expert routing, systematic ablations on routing strategies and expert specialization, and empirical validation across multiple model scales and diverse tasks.

5ab0b1a56ac262cf00781065f9fc0f27af145961.title: TIMING: Temporality-Aware Integrated Gradients for Time Series Explanation
5ab0b1a56ac262cf00781065f9fc0f27af145961.research_question: How can the faithfulness and interpretability of feature attribution methods for time series models be improved, particularly in capturing both the magnitude and direction of feature contributions while accounting for temporal dependencies?
5ab0b1a56ac262cf00781065f9fc0f27af145961.hypothesis: Incorporating temporality-aware segment-based masking into the Integrated Gradients framework and employing new evaluation metrics that account for directional attribution will yield more faithful, interpretable, and robust explanations for time series models compared to existing XAI methods.
5ab0b1a56ac262cf00781065f9fc0f27af145961.proposed_method: A novel explainability method, Temporality-Aware Integrated Gradients (TIMING), is developed to enhance feature attribution for time series models. TIMING extends the traditional Integrated Gradients (IG) approach by introducing segment-based random masking, which preserves or disrupts temporal dependencies in a controlled manner. Instead of scaling all points along a straight-line path from a baseline to the input, TIMING randomly retains contiguous segments of the time series, mitigating out-of-distribution (OOD) issues and enabling attribution that reflects both local and global temporal structure. The method computes attributions by aggregating results from multiple randomized segment-based paths, ensuring robustness and faithfulness. Theoretical properties such as sensitivity and implementation invariance are established, and the method is designed to be model-agnostic and computationally efficient.
5ab0b1a56ac262cf00781065f9fc0f27af145961.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both synthetic datasets (Switch-Feature, State) and a diverse set of real-world time series datasets, including MIMIC-III (healthcare), PAM (activity monitoring), Boiler, Epilepsy, Wafer, and Freezer. The proposed method is evaluated against 13 state-of-the-art XAI baselines, including both modality-agnostic (e.g., IG, SHAP, LIME, DeepLIFT) and time series-specific methods (e.g., FIT, WinIT, Dynamask, Extrmask, ContraLSP, TimeX, TimeX++). Evaluation metrics include the newly proposed Cumulative Prediction Difference (CPD) and Cumulative Prediction Preservation (CPP), as well as standard metrics such as accuracy, cross-entropy, sufficiency, and comprehensiveness. Experiments utilize single-layer GRU classifiers as the primary model, with additional tests on CNNs and Transformers for generality. Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of segment-based masking and hyperparameter sensitivity, and computational efficiency is benchmarked against other methods.
5ab0b1a56ac262cf00781065f9fc0f27af145961.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces two novel evaluation metrics, CPD and CPP, that systematically assess the directional faithfulness of attribution methods for time series, overcoming the cancel-out problem of opposing feature contributions. TIMING is the first method to incorporate temporality-aware segment-based random masking into the IG framework, enabling more accurate and robust attributions that respect temporal dependencies and mitigate OOD effects. The method preserves key theoretical properties of IG while providing improved empirical performance and interpretability. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TIMING outperforms existing XAI baselines on both synthetic and real-world time series datasets, offering a practical, efficient, and theoretically sound solution for explainable time series modeling.

5ae6fb6b5a3c7df515ff4a82ac9673bae6a8e200.title: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints
5ae6fb6b5a3c7df515ff4a82ac9673bae6a8e200.research_question: How can the memory bandwidth bottleneck during autoregressive Transformer model inference be reduced without significantly degrading model quality, and is it possible to efficiently convert existing multi-head attention models to faster attention variants with minimal retraining?
5ae6fb6b5a3c7df515ff4a82ac9673bae6a8e200.hypothesis: Existing multi-head attention language model checkpoints can be efficiently uptrained into multi-query or grouped-query attention models using a small fraction of the original training compute, resulting in models that maintain high quality while achieving significantly faster inference due to reduced memory bandwidth requirements.
5ae6fb6b5a3c7df515ff4a82ac9673bae6a8e200.proposed_method: A two-step methodology is proposed for converting multi-head attention (MHA) language model checkpoints into faster attention variants. First, the key and value projection matrices from all heads in the checkpoint are mean-pooled to create the appropriate number of key and value heads for the target attention variant—either a single head for multi-query attention (MQA) or multiple heads for grouped-query attention (GQA), where query heads are divided into groups each sharing a key-value pair. Second, the converted checkpoint is uptrained for a small proportion (e.g., 5%) of the original pre-training steps using the same data and setup as the initial model. GQA is introduced as a generalization of MQA, interpolating between MHA and MQA by varying the number of groups, thus allowing a trade-off between speed and quality. The method is applied only to the decoder self-attention and cross-attention layers, leaving encoder self-attention unchanged.
5ae6fb6b5a3c7df515ff4a82ac9673bae6a8e200.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using T5.1.1 architecture models (Large and XXL) implemented in JAX/Flax, with uptraining performed on public T5.1.1 checkpoints. The key and value heads are mean-pooled to create MQA or GQA structures, and models are uptrained for 5% of the original pre-training steps. Evaluation will be performed on summarization datasets (CNN/Daily Mail, arXiv, PubMed, MediaSum, Multi-News), a translation dataset (WMT 2014 English-to-German), and a question-answering dataset (TriviaQA), using metrics such as ROUGE, BLEU, and F1. Baselines will include original MHA models and uptrained MQA and GQA models. Timing experiments will measure inference speed per sample on TPUv4 chips, and ablation studies will examine the effects of checkpoint conversion methods, uptraining proportion, and the number of GQA groups.
5ae6fb6b5a3c7df515ff4a82ac9673bae6a8e200.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a cost-effective uptraining recipe for converting existing multi-head attention checkpoints into multi-query or grouped-query attention models using only a small fraction of original training compute. Grouped-query attention (GQA) is proposed as a novel intermediate attention mechanism that interpolates between MHA and MQA, offering a favorable trade-off between inference speed and model quality. The method demonstrates that uptrained GQA models can achieve quality close to MHA while approaching the inference speed of MQA, and provides empirical evidence on a wide range of tasks and model sizes. The approach also offers practical guidance on checkpoint conversion and uptraining stability.

5ae7ef3231f94618f5d7f1f63e659bf5de731a59.title: Variance-Dependent Regret Bounds for Linear Bandits and Reinforcement Learning: Adaptivity and Computational Efficiency
5ae7ef3231f94618f5d7f1f63e659bf5de731a59.research_question: Can computationally efficient algorithms be developed for linear bandits and reinforcement learning in the presence of heteroscedastic (unknown and time-varying) noise, such that the regret bounds adapt to the actual variance encountered, without requiring prior knowledge of the noise variance?
5ae7ef3231f94618f5d7f1f63e659bf5de731a59.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a novel algorithmic framework, utilizing adaptive variance-aware confidence sets and new concentration inequalities, can achieve minimax-optimal, variance-dependent regret bounds for linear bandits and linear mixture Markov decision processes, even when the noise variance is unknown and heteroscedastic.
5ae7ef3231f94618f5d7f1f63e659bf5de731a59.proposed_method: A new algorithm, SAVE (SupLin + Adaptive Variance-aware Exploration), will be developed for stochastic linear contextual bandits with heteroscedastic noise. The method constructs multi-layer context partitions, where each layer contains context vectors reweighted to have uniform elliptical norms, enabling tighter control of uncertainty. A weighted ridge regression estimator is employed, with weights chosen to ensure uniform uncertainty within each layer. The algorithm leverages a novel Freedman-type concentration inequality for vector-valued self-normalized martingales, allowing the construction of adaptive confidence sets whose radii are updated online based on empirical variance estimates. This approach is extended to reinforcement learning by designing a variance-adaptive algorithm for linear mixture Markov decision processes, using similar variance-aware exploration strategies and confidence set constructions.
5ae7ef3231f94618f5d7f1f63e659bf5de731a59.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard linear contextual bandit benchmarks and synthetic environments with heteroscedastic noise to evaluate the proposed SAVE algorithm. The method will be compared against existing baselines such as OFUL, Weighted OFUL, VOFUL, and other variance-dependent algorithms, both in known- and unknown-variance regimes. Evaluation metrics will include cumulative regret, computational efficiency (runtime per round), and adaptivity to changing noise variance. For reinforcement learning, experiments will be performed on linear mixture MDP environments, measuring horizon-free and problem-dependent regret, and comparing with state-of-the-art algorithms such as UCRL-VTR, VarLin, and HF-UCRL-VTR+. Key experimental setup details include varying the dimension of context/features, the number of rounds/episodes, and the distribution of noise variance across time.
5ae7ef3231f94618f5d7f1f63e659bf5de731a59.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first computationally efficient algorithm for linear bandits with unknown, heteroscedastic noise that achieves minimax-optimal, variance-dependent regret bounds. The approach is enabled by a new Freedman-type concentration inequality for vector-valued self-normalized martingales, which generalizes prior results to the heteroscedastic setting. The multi-layer context partitioning and adaptive variance-aware exploration strategy represent significant innovations, allowing the method to adapt to unknown variance without prior knowledge. Extension to linear mixture MDPs yields a variance-adaptive reinforcement learning algorithm with tight, problem-dependent, horizon-free regret bounds, improving both statistical and computational efficiency over prior methods.

5aea80d0cad8fb2d94bf3c5f163f25034aa062df.title: Causal Representation Learning from Multiple Distributions: A General Setting
5aea80d0cad8fb2d94bf3c5f163f25034aa062df.research_question: How can latent causal variables and their causal relations be recovered from observed data generated by unknown nonlinear functions, when the data arises from multiple distributions (such as heterogeneous domains or nonstationary time series), without assuming parametric models or the presence of hard interventions?
5aea80d0cad8fb2d94bf3c5f163f25034aa062df.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, under suitable sparsity constraints on the recovered graph over latent variables and sufficient change conditions on the causal mechanisms across domains, it is possible to recover the moralized graph of the underlying latent causal structure and identify the latent variables up to specific, well-defined indeterminacies, even in a completely nonparametric setting.
5aea80d0cad8fb2d94bf3c5f163f25034aa062df.proposed_method: A general, nonparametric framework will be developed for causal representation learning from multiple distributions, where observed variables are nonlinear functions of latent causal variables governed by a structural equation model (SEM). The approach will estimate a generative model that matches the observed distributions across domains, leveraging sparsity constraints on the recovered latent graph and sufficient changes in causal influences. The method will utilize properties of Markov networks and conditional independence, employing variational autoencoder (VAE) architectures or normalizing flows to learn the mapping from observations to latent variables. The prior distribution over latents will be designed to capture domain-specific changes, either nonparametrically via flow-based transformations or parametrically via structured SEMs, and sparsity regularization will be imposed to encourage recovery of the true underlying causal structure.
5aea80d0cad8fb2d94bf3c5f163f25034aa062df.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on simulated datasets where the ground truth latent variables and causal graphs are known. Data will be generated using common causal structures (such as Y-structures and chains) with latent variables modulated by random scaling and shifting across domains, and observed variables produced via invertible nonlinear transformations (e.g., MLPs with orthogonal weights and LeakyReLU activations). Both Gaussian and Laplacian noise settings will be tested. The proposed method will be compared to baselines such as standard VAE and iVAE, and evaluated using metrics such as correlation between recovered and true latent variables, and accuracy in recovering the underlying causal adjacency matrix. Sparsity regularization effects and identifiability under different noise and structural conditions will be systematically analyzed.
5aea80d0cad8fb2d94bf3c5f163f25034aa062df.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a general, nonparametric identifiability theory for causal representation learning from multiple distributions, without relying on parametric assumptions, graphical restrictions, or hard interventions. It establishes that, under sparsity and sufficient change conditions, the moralized graph of the latent causal DAG and the latent variables themselves can be recovered up to well-characterized indeterminacies. The framework unifies and generalizes previous results, provides necessary and sufficient conditions for identifiability in this setting, and offers practical algorithms that leverage only observational data with domain heterogeneity or nonstationarity.

5b1120f547d3969afc49b4a094e874d568e53aca.title: Grokked Transformers are Implicit Reasoners: A Mechanistic Journey to the Edge of Generalization
5b1120f547d3969afc49b4a094e874d568e53aca.research_question: Can transformer models acquire robust implicit reasoning abilities over parametric knowledge, and what are the mechanisms and limitations underlying their generalization—particularly in compositional and comparative reasoning tasks—when exposed to controlled mixtures of atomic and inferred facts?
5b1120f547d3969afc49b4a094e874d568e53aca.hypothesis: Transformers can learn to implicitly reason over parametric knowledge, but robust generalization—especially out-of-distribution—requires extended training (grokking), and the architecture's memory-sharing mechanisms fundamentally impact the systematicity of generalization across different reasoning types.
5b1120f547d3969afc49b4a094e874d568e53aca.proposed_method: A systematic investigation will be conducted by training standard decoder-only transformer models from scratch on synthetic datasets designed to probe implicit reasoning. The datasets will consist of atomic facts and inferred facts generated via latent rules, simulating axioms and theorems in a formal system. Two reasoning tasks—composition (multi-hop chaining of facts) and comparison (attribute comparison between entities)—will be constructed, with explicit control over the ratio of inferred to atomic facts and the distribution of knowledge between in-distribution (ID) and out-of-distribution (OOD) splits. Mechanistic analysis techniques, including logit lens and causal tracing, will be employed throughout training to identify and interpret the formation and evolution of generalizing circuits within the model. Additional experiments will explore the impact of architectural modifications, such as cross-layer memory sharing, and compare parametric-memory-based transformers to large language models (LLMs) augmented with non-parametric memory.
5b1120f547d3969afc49b4a094e874d568e53aca.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize synthetic datasets generated by sampling entities, relations, attributes, and values, with knowledge graphs constructed for composition and attribute tables for comparison. The transformer model will be trained with AdamW optimization and evaluated on both ID and OOD splits, measuring accuracy on unseen inferred facts. Key variables include the ratio of inferred to atomic facts and the total number of entities. Baselines will include state-of-the-art LLMs (e.g., GPT-4-Turbo, Gemini-1.5-Pro) tested with both direct and chain-of-thought prompting, as well as retrieval-augmented setups. Evaluation metrics will focus on accuracy, mean reciprocal rank (MRR), and systematicity of generalization. Mechanistic experiments will analyze internal activations and causal pathways using logit lens and intervention-based causal tracing.
5b1120f547d3969afc49b4a094e874d568e53aca.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a controlled, mechanistic framework for analyzing implicit reasoning and generalization in transformers, extending the study of grokking to knowledge-based reasoning tasks. It claims to reveal the critical role of data distribution (rather than size) in enabling generalization through grokking, and provides detailed mechanistic explanations for why transformers succeed or fail in systematic generalization across reasoning types. The research further demonstrates the unique power of parametric memory for complex reasoning tasks, where non-parametric memory-augmented LLMs fail, and suggests architectural improvements—such as cross-layer memory sharing—to enhance systematic generalization.

5b19bf6c3f4b25cac96362c98b930cf4b37f6744.title: DreamBooth: Fine Tuning Text-to-Image Diffusion Models for Subject-Driven Generation
5b19bf6c3f4b25cac96362c98b930cf4b37f6744.research_question: How can text-to-image diffusion models be adapted to enable high-fidelity, subject-driven image generation, allowing the synthesis of novel images of a specific subject in diverse contexts and styles, given only a few reference images?
5b19bf6c3f4b25cac96362c98b930cf4b37f6744.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that fine-tuning a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model with a small set of subject images, using a unique identifier and a class-specific prior preservation loss, will enable the model to generate novel, photorealistic images of the subject in new contexts while preserving key visual features and supporting prompt-based guidance.
5b19bf6c3f4b25cac96362c98b930cf4b37f6744.proposed_method: The proposed method involves fine-tuning a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model (such as Imagen or Stable Diffusion) using a small set (typically 3-5) of images of a specific subject. Each image is paired with a text prompt containing a unique, rare-token identifier and a class noun (e.g., 'a [V] dog'), leveraging the model's semantic prior for the class while binding the subject instance to the identifier. During fine-tuning, a class-specific prior preservation loss is introduced, which supervises the model with its own generated class samples to prevent language drift and maintain output diversity. The rare-token identifier is carefully selected to minimize prior associations in the tokenizer and model, ensuring the identifier uniquely refers to the subject. All layers of the model, including those conditioned on text embeddings, are fine-tuned to maximize subject fidelity.
5b19bf6c3f4b25cac96362c98b930cf4b37f6744.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a newly collected dataset of 30 subjects (objects and live subjects/pets), each with 3-5 reference images. A set of 25 prompts per subject will be used, covering recontextualization and property modification tasks. The evaluation protocol includes generating four images per subject per prompt, totaling 3,000 images. Baselines for comparison include Textual Inversion and standard fine-tuning approaches. Evaluation metrics will include DINO and CLIP-I (for subject fidelity), CLIP-T (for prompt fidelity), a diversity metric (LPIPS), and a prior preservation metric. User studies will be conducted to assess subjective fidelity and prompt adherence. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of the prior preservation loss and class noun selection.
5b19bf6c3f4b25cac96362c98b930cf4b37f6744.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel method for subject-driven personalization of text-to-image diffusion models using only a few reference images. Key innovations include the use of rare-token identifiers to bind new subject instances, a class-specific prior preservation loss to prevent language drift and maintain diversity, and a comprehensive evaluation protocol for subject-driven generation.
