The method enables high-fidelity synthesis of novel images of a subject in diverse contexts and styles, surpassing existing methods in both subject and prompt fidelity, and is the first to address this task with such minimal data requirements.

5b25cdc78ad437178d0231aecaa4d40402151b0d.title: DGR-MIL: Exploring Diverse Global Representation in Multiple Instance Learning for Whole Slide Image Classification
5b25cdc78ad437178d0231aecaa4d40402151b0d.research_question: How can the diversity among instances in multiple instance learning (MIL) be effectively modeled to improve whole slide image (WSI) classification performance, particularly in the context of weakly supervised learning for histopathology?
5b25cdc78ad437178d0231aecaa4d40402151b0d.hypothesis: Explicitly modeling and enforcing diversity among instances in MIL through learnable global representations and diversity-promoting mechanisms will lead to improved classification accuracy and robustness in WSI analysis compared to existing correlation-focused or prototype-based MIL approaches.
5b25cdc78ad437178d0231aecaa4d40402151b0d.proposed_method: A novel MIL aggregation framework is developed that introduces a set of learnable global vectors to summarize the diversity among instances within each bag. These global vectors interact with instance embeddings via a cross-attention mechanism, where the global vectors serve as queries and the instance embeddings as key-value pairs, reducing computational complexity compared to standard self-attention. To ensure the global vectors capture diverse and discriminative features, two mechanisms are incorporated: (1) a positive instance alignment module that encourages global vectors to align with the center of positive instances while distancing from negative centers using a triplet loss, and (2) a diversity learning paradigm based on determinantal point processes (DPP), which enforces orthogonality among global vectors by minimizing a negative log-determinant loss. Additionally, a tokenized global vector is introduced to summarize the overall bag context and facilitate robust bag-level classification.
5b25cdc78ad437178d0231aecaa4d40402151b0d.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on two benchmark datasets for WSI classification: CAMELYON-16 and TCGA-lung cancer. The proposed method is evaluated against state-of-the-art MIL aggregation models, including attention-based and transformer-based MIL approaches. Standard evaluation metrics such as classification accuracy and area under the ROC curve (AUC) are used to assess performance. The experimental setup includes the use of pre-trained feature extractors for patch embeddings, consistent bag construction protocols, and ablation studies to isolate the contributions of the positive instance alignment and diversity loss components.
5b25cdc78ad437178d0231aecaa4d40402151b0d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new perspective on modeling instance diversity in MIL by leveraging learnable global vectors and cross-attention, rather than relying solely on instance correlation or clustering-based prototypes. The method incorporates a theoretically grounded, computationally efficient diversity loss based on DPP to enforce orthogonality among global vectors. The combination of positive instance alignment and diversity-promoting mechanisms in the MIL pooling stage is claimed to yield superior performance and more descriptive global representations for WSI classification.

5b3f18492bd171e9eb69249b5a0a13d6f1717852.title: Grokking in the Wild: Data Augmentation for Real-World Multi-Hop Reasoning with Transformers
5b3f18492bd171e9eb69249b5a0a13d6f1717852.research_question: How can multi-hop reasoning capabilities in Transformer-based language models be enhanced for real-world factual datasets, particularly when knowledge is sparse and distributed, and what data augmentation strategies can enable robust, implicit multi-step reasoning?
5b3f18492bd171e9eb69249b5a0a13d6f1717852.hypothesis: Augmenting real-world knowledge graphs with carefully designed synthetic data to increase the ratio of inferred (multi-hop) facts to atomic (single-hop) facts above a critical threshold will induce the emergence of generalizing circuits in Transformers, enabling robust implicit multi-hop reasoning, even in the presence of some factually incorrect synthetic data.
5b3f18492bd171e9eb69249b5a0a13d6f1717852.proposed_method: A novel data augmentation framework will be developed to systematically increase the ratio of inferred to atomic facts (denoted as ϕ) in real-world knowledge graphs. This involves generating synthetic atomic and multi-hop facts using large language models (LLMs), ensuring that the augmented dataset surpasses empirically established thresholds necessary for grokking-based generalization in Transformers. For comparison tasks, new location-based atomic facts and corresponding multi-hop queries will be synthesized, while for compositional tasks, entity-relation chains will be expanded and converted into natural-language questions. Both structured (triplet-based) and unstructured (paragraph-based) data formats will be targeted, with LLMs used to generate and diversify the augmented facts. The methodology includes parsing and enriching knowledge graphs, avoiding cycles, and maintaining class balance, with the goal of enabling the formation of implicit reasoning circuits during prolonged Transformer training.
5b3f18492bd171e9eb69249b5a0a13d6f1717852.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the 2WikiMultiHopQA dataset, a benchmark for multi-hop question answering based on Wikipedia, which will be augmented to ensure a sufficiently high inferred-to-atomic fact ratio. Both structured (triplet) and unstructured (full paragraph) subsets will be used, focusing on comparison and compositional multi-hop tasks. A GPT-2–style Transformer (8 layers, 768 hidden units, 12 attention heads) will be trained from scratch using AdamW optimization for up to 300,000 steps, with evaluation on both in-distribution (ID) and out-of-distribution (OOD) queries. Baselines will include strong pretrained models such as GPT-4o and o1-mini, as well as non-augmented Transformer models. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on ID and OOD test sets, with particular attention to the emergence of late-phase jumps in OOD accuracy indicative of grokking. Multiple random seeds and hardware setups (e.g., A100 GPU) will be used to ensure robustness.
5b3f18492bd171e9eb69249b5a0a13d6f1717852.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to extend grokking-based data augmentation to real-world factual datasets, demonstrating that increasing the ratio of inferred to atomic facts can induce implicit multi-hop reasoning in Transformers outside of synthetic toy problems. It is claimed that even factually incorrect synthetic data can enhance reasoning circuits rather than degrade accuracy, as it encourages reliance on relational structure over memorization. The method achieves state-of-the-art or superior results on multi-hop reasoning benchmarks, and provides new insights into the internal formation of generalizing circuits as a function of data distribution. The work opens the door to more robust, interpretable, and scalable factual reasoning in large language models through principled data augmentation.

5b437e0f5353ce5ce5c599bfc778bc099185accd.title: Agent Attention: On the Integration of Softmax and Linear Attention
5b437e0f5353ce5ce5c599bfc778bc099185accd.research_question: How can an attention mechanism be designed to simultaneously achieve high computational efficiency and strong global context modeling capability in vision Transformers, without sacrificing expressive power or scalability to high-resolution inputs?
5b437e0f5353ce5ce5c599bfc778bc099185accd.hypothesis: Introducing a small set of agent tokens to mediate information aggregation and broadcast between query and key/value tokens will enable an attention mechanism that combines the efficiency of linear attention with the expressiveness of Softmax attention, resulting in improved performance and scalability for vision tasks.
5b437e0f5353ce5ce5c599bfc778bc099185accd.proposed_method: A novel attention paradigm, termed Agent Attention, will be developed by introducing agent tokens into the conventional attention module. The method is formalized as a quadruple (Q, A, K, V), where A represents a set of agent tokens, typically much fewer in number than the query tokens Q. The process consists of two sequential Softmax attention operations: first, agent tokens aggregate information from all key and value tokens (Agent Aggregation); second, the aggregated agent features are broadcast back to the query tokens (Agent Broadcast). This design avoids direct pairwise computation between all queries and keys, reducing complexity from quadratic to linear with respect to the number of tokens. Additional enhancements include the incorporation of an agent bias for positional encoding and a depthwise convolution module to restore feature diversity. Agent tokens can be obtained via pooling, learnable parameters, or other feature extraction techniques.
5b437e0f5353ce5ce5c599bfc778bc099185accd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across multiple vision tasks, including image classification (ImageNet-1K), object detection (COCO), semantic segmentation (ADE20K), and image generation (Stable Diffusion). The proposed Agent Attention module will be integrated into various state-of-the-art vision Transformer architectures such as DeiT, PVT, Swin, and CSwin, serving as a drop-in replacement for standard attention modules. Baseline comparisons will be made against original models using Softmax attention and other efficient attention variants. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy for classification, mean Average Precision (mAP) for detection, mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) for segmentation, and both generation speed and image quality for diffusion models. Ablation studies will assess the impact of agent token count, agent bias, and feature diversity modules. Inference speed will be measured on CPUs and GPUs to validate efficiency gains.
5b437e0f5353ce5ce5c599bfc778bc099185accd.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a unified attention mechanism that seamlessly integrates the strengths of Softmax and linear attention, achieving both linear computational complexity and high expressive power. The use of agent tokens as intermediaries for global information aggregation and broadcast is a novel architectural design, enabling large receptive fields without the computational burden of pairwise attention. The approach is plug-and-play, compatible with existing Transformer architectures, and demonstrates superior performance and efficiency, particularly in high-resolution scenarios and generative models, without requiring additional training.

5b529d75a09a61a8b351d1bae2c8f3a3db7c1008.title: Bisecle: Binding and Separation in Continual Learning for Video Language Understanding
5b529d75a09a61a8b351d1bae2c8f3a3db7c1008.research_question: How can continual learning for video-language understanding be improved in large multimodal foundation models, particularly under constraints of parameter efficiency and in the presence of evolving, diverse data streams?
5b529d75a09a61a8b351d1bae2c8f3a3db7c1008.hypothesis: Incorporating neurobiologically inspired mechanisms of rapid binding and pattern separation into the continual learning process for video-language models will mitigate catastrophic forgetting and update conflict, thereby improving knowledge retention and generalization across sequential tasks while maintaining parameter efficiency.
5b529d75a09a61a8b351d1bae2c8f3a3db7c1008.proposed_method: A novel continual learning framework, Bisecle, is proposed for video-language models, inspired by the hippocampus's mechanisms of rapid binding and pattern separation. The approach utilizes a multi-directional supervision module to enforce bidirectional and cross-modal associations among video, question, and answer modalities, including auxiliary objectives such as question prediction and video prediction, in addition to the standard answer prediction. Furthermore, a contrastive prompt learning scheme is introduced, where shared, task-aware learnable prompts are regularized with task-specific embeddings through a contrastive loss, effectively isolating task-specific knowledge and reducing parameter update conflicts. The backbone consists of a frozen large language model (LLM) and visual encoder, with only lightweight projection layers and prompts being updated, ensuring parameter-efficient adaptation throughout sequential tasks.
5b529d75a09a61a8b351d1bae2c8f3a3db7c1008.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on three benchmark VideoQA datasets: NExT-QA, DramaQA, and STAR. For each dataset, tasks are defined by question types or reasoning requirements, and continual learning is simulated by sequentially training on these tasks. The proposed method is compared against six strong baselines, including L2P, DualPrompt, LAE, DAM, ProgPrompt, and ColPro, with ColPro using the same backbone for a fair comparison. Evaluation metrics include average final accuracy (Avg. Acc) for task performance and average forgetting (Avg. Fog) to quantify catastrophic forgetting. The backbone model is LLaMA-Adapter with a ViT visual encoder, and all models are trained for five epochs with a batch size of 32, using fixed LLM and visual encoder weights. Additional experiments assess data efficiency, robustness to different LLM sizes, and sensitivity to the number of prompt layers.
5b529d75a09a61a8b351d1bae2c8f3a3db7c1008.novelty_claims: The proposal uniquely reframes parameter-efficient continual learning for video-language models through the lens of neurobiological mechanisms, specifically rapid binding and pattern separation. It introduces a multi-directional supervision module that extends beyond traditional single-directional objectives, enabling deeper cross-modal and causal reasoning. The contrastive prompt learning mechanism further innovates by aligning shared prompts with task-specific embeddings, reducing inter-task interference without requiring explicit task-specific parameters. The overall approach is lightweight, data-efficient, and achieves state-of-the-art performance in mitigating catastrophic forgetting and enhancing generalization across diverse continual learning scenarios.

5b5be0a0965c6f3314489b38c41c349f07fb95a1.title: FormalAlign: Automated Alignment Evaluation for Autoformalization
5b5be0a0965c6f3314489b38c41c349f07fb95a1.research_question: How can the alignment between informal mathematical statements and their formalized, machine-verifiable counterparts be automatically and robustly evaluated, reducing reliance on manual verification in the autoformalization process?
5b5be0a0965c6f3314489b38c41c349f07fb95a1.hypothesis: A dual-loss framework that jointly optimizes for both autoformalization sequence generation and representational alignment between informal and formal mathematical statements will enable more accurate and robust automated alignment evaluation than existing methods relying on logical validity or surface-form similarity alone.
5b5be0a0965c6f3314489b38c41c349f07fb95a1.proposed_method: A novel framework, FORMALALIGN, is proposed to automate the evaluation of alignment between informal (natural language) and formal (machine-verifiable) mathematical statements. The approach involves fine-tuning a large language model (LLM) using a dual-loss objective: a cross-entropy loss for the autoformalization sequence generation task and a contrastive loss to align the hidden representations of paired informal-formal statements. During training, the model is encouraged to produce similar embeddings for aligned pairs and dissimilar embeddings for misaligned pairs. At inference, an alignment evaluation score is computed by averaging a certainty score (reflecting the model's confidence in generating the formal output) and a similarity score (cosine similarity between the internal representations of the informal and formal statements). This combined metric provides a robust signal for alignment assessment.
5b5be0a0965c6f3314489b38c41c349f07fb95a1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using fine-tuned LLMs (e.g., Mistral-7B) on training data from the FormL4 and MMA datasets, which contain paired informal-formal mathematical statements sourced from Mathlib. Evaluation will be performed on four test sets: FormL4-Basic, FormL4-Random (in-domain), and MiniF2F-Valid, MiniF2F-Test (out-of-domain), the latter containing formalizations of mathematical competition problems. Each positive (aligned) example will be augmented with 21 negative (misaligned) examples generated using systematic misalignment strategies, such as constant modification, exponent modification, variable introduction, type changes, equality/inequality swaps, and random pairings. Baselines will include GPT-4 and GPT-3.5, with evaluation metrics comprising Alignment-Selection (AS), Precision, and Recall for alignment detection. Human and LLM-as-judge evaluations will also be conducted for comparative analysis.
5b5be0a0965c6f3314489b38c41c349f07fb95a1.novelty_claims: The proposed method constitutes the first automated framework for evaluating alignment in autoformalization, significantly reducing the need for manual verification. The dual-loss training approach simultaneously enhances both autoformalization and semantic alignment capabilities. The introduction of a robust, combined alignment evaluation score that integrates certainty and representational similarity is claimed to provide superior performance over existing surface-form or logical validity-based metrics. Extensive augmentation with systematically generated misaligned examples enables comprehensive and challenging evaluation, and the framework demonstrates strong generalization across multiple datasets and baseline models.

5b7f5488c380cf5085a5dd93e993ad293b225eee.title: One Fits All: Power General Time Series Analysis by Pretrained LM
5b7f5488c380cf5085a5dd93e993ad293b225eee.research_question: Can a unified, pretrained language or vision model be effectively adapted to perform a wide range of general time series analysis tasks, such as classification, anomaly detection, forecasting, imputation, and few/zero-shot learning, without requiring large-scale time series pretraining?
5b7f5488c380cf5085a5dd93e993ad293b225eee.hypothesis: A frozen, pretrained transformer model from the language or vision domain, with minimal adaptation, can achieve state-of-the-art or comparable performance across diverse time series analysis tasks by leveraging its generic learned representations and self-attention mechanisms.
5b7f5488c380cf5085a5dd93e993ad293b225eee.proposed_method: A unified framework is developed that leverages frozen pretrained transformer models (such as GPT2, BERT, or BEiT) originally trained on large-scale language or vision data for general time series analysis. The method retains the self-attention and feedforward layers of the pretrained model, freezing these components during fine-tuning. Only the input embedding layer (which projects time series data to the required model dimensions), positional embeddings, normalization layers, and output layer are fine-tuned. Data normalization (including reverse instance normalization) and patching (aggregating adjacent time steps into patch-based tokens) are incorporated to facilitate knowledge transfer and improve temporal pattern extraction. This approach enables the model to handle various time series tasks within a single architecture, relying on the generic computation capabilities of the pretrained transformer.
5b7f5488c380cf5085a5dd93e993ad293b225eee.experiment_details: Extensive experiments are conducted on a broad suite of time series tasks, including classification, anomaly detection, imputation, short/long-term forecasting, and few/zero-shot forecasting. Datasets include ETT (ETTh1, ETTh2, ETTm1, ETTm2), Electricity, Weather, ECL, Traffic, ILI, M4, M3, Tourism, and several UEA classification benchmarks. Baseline comparisons cover recent state-of-the-art models such as TimesNet, PatchTST, DLinear, FEDformer, Autoformer, Reformer, N-BEATS, and others, spanning CNN, MLP, and transformer-based architectures. Evaluation metrics include MSE, MAE, SMAPE, MASE, OWA, F1-score, and classification accuracy, depending on the task. Ablation studies examine the effects of pretraining, layer freezing, and model selection, while computational efficiency is assessed by comparing training/inference time and parameter counts. Additional experiments demonstrate cross-modality transfer by applying BERT and BEiT backbones.
5b7f5488c380cf5085a5dd93e993ad293b225eee.novelty_claims: The proposed approach provides the first unified framework for general time series analysis using frozen pretrained language or vision models, achieving state-of-the-art or comparable results across all major time series tasks without requiring large-scale time series pretraining. The method demonstrates that pretrained transformers can serve as universal compute engines for time series data, and provides both empirical and theoretical evidence that the self-attention mechanism performs a function analogous to principal component analysis (PCA), explaining the model's cross-domain adaptability. The framework is shown to be effective with different transformer backbones and modalities, highlighting its universality and transferability.

5b9bb1e2631bdb26ba41d18dd3c77aac9d12acfd.title: Reverse Diffusion Sequential Monte Carlo Samplers
5b9bb1e2631bdb26ba41d18dd3c77aac9d12acfd.research_question: How can sampling from unnormalized target distributions be improved to achieve asymptotically exact samples and unbiased normalization constant estimation, while mitigating the biases and inefficiencies of diffusion-based and classical sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) methods?
5b9bb1e2631bdb26ba41d18dd3c77aac9d12acfd.hypothesis: A sequential Monte Carlo framework that utilizes reverse diffusion processes as proposals, combined with informative intermediate target distributions constructed from Monte Carlo score estimates, will enable consistent, unbiased sampling from unnormalized target distributions without requiring additional model training or inference overhead.
5b9bb1e2631bdb26ba41d18dd3c77aac9d12acfd.proposed_method: A new algorithm, Reverse Diffusion Sequential Monte Carlo (RDSMC), is proposed to sample from unnormalized target distributions by integrating reverse diffusion dynamics into the SMC framework. The method constructs a sequence of intermediate target distributions that guide the resampling of particles at each step, progressively steering the particle population toward the final target distribution. These intermediate targets are efficiently approximated using byproducts of Monte Carlo-based score estimation, such as importance sampling or annealed importance sampling, without the need for additional model training. The proposal distribution for particle propagation is derived from the discretized reverse diffusion process, where the score function is estimated via Monte Carlo methods using the denoising score identity. The SMC weighting and resampling steps asymptotically correct for proposal bias, ensuring that the final weighted samples are consistent with the desired target distribution and that the normalization constant can be estimated unbiasedly.
5b9bb1e2631bdb26ba41d18dd3c77aac9d12acfd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of synthetic and real-world target distributions, including bi-modal Gaussian mixtures of varying dimensions, the Rings and Funnel distributions, and Bayesian logistic regression on benchmark datasets (Credit, Cancer, Ionosphere, Sonar). The proposed method will be compared against baselines such as classical SMC, Annealed Importance Sampling (AIS), Score Matching Sampler (SMS), and diffusion-based samplers RDMC and SLIPS. Evaluation metrics will include estimation bias of mode weights, log-normalization constant bias, total variation distance, sliced Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance, and test log-likelihood for Bayesian inference tasks. Each method will be tuned using validation metrics, and experiments will be repeated over multiple random seeds to report mean and standard error. Ablation studies will assess the impact of intermediate targets and resampling by comparing RDSMC to its proposal-only and importance sampling variants.
5b9bb1e2631bdb26ba41d18dd3c77aac9d12acfd.novelty_claims: The proposed method is training-free, requiring no neural network training or additional inference overhead, and extends diffusion Monte Carlo samplers to achieve asymptotically exact sampling and unbiased normalization constant estimation. The construction of intermediate target distributions using byproducts of Monte Carlo score estimation is both principled and computationally efficient, providing exact approximation to the ideal targets at each SMC step. The approach systematically corrects for discretization and score estimation biases inherent in diffusion-based samplers, and empirical results demonstrate superior or competitive performance compared to both classical and diffusion-based baselines. The method also generalizes to a nested SMC framework, inheriting strong theoretical guarantees of consistency and unbiasedness.

5bce5d4a1bf3112f7d6b3999aa4d7a521e2ff3e0.title: OmnixR: Evaluating Omni-modality Language Models on Reasoning across Modalities
5bce5d4a1bf3112f7d6b3999aa4d7a521e2ff3e0.research_question: How can the reasoning abilities of omni-modality language models (OLMs) be rigorously and comprehensively evaluated across a diverse set of modalities, including complex combinations such as text, image, audio, and video, in both synthetic and real-world scenarios?
5bce5d4a1bf3112f7d6b3999aa4d7a521e2ff3e0.hypothesis: Current omni-modality language models exhibit significant inconsistencies and performance drops when required to integrate and reason across multiple modalities, especially in complex or noisy real-world settings. A comprehensive benchmark that includes both synthetic and real-world multi-modal tasks will reveal these limitations and guide future improvements.
5bce5d4a1bf3112f7d6b3999aa4d7a521e2ff3e0.proposed_method: A novel evaluation suite, Omni×R, will be developed to systematically benchmark OLMs on their cross-modal reasoning abilities. The suite will consist of two complementary datasets: (1) Omni×R_synth, a synthetic dataset generated by programmatically translating text-based questions into multiple modalities (audio, images, video, and hybrids) using tools such as PIL for images, Google TTS for audio, and OpenCV for video; and (2) Omni×R_real, a real-world dataset curated from educational YouTube videos, with questions manually transcribed and annotated into various modalities by expert annotators. The synthetic set will ensure controlled, information-preserving modality translation, while the real-world set will introduce natural noise and complexity. Both datasets will include mixed-modality samples (e.g., video+audio, image+audio) to simulate authentic user scenarios. Evaluation protocols will include standard Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting as well as an Extract-Then-Answer (ETA) prompting strategy to assess both perception and reasoning capabilities.
5bce5d4a1bf3112f7d6b3999aa4d7a521e2ff3e0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on leading OLMs, including Gemini (1.5-Pro, 1.5-Flash), GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, and Claude-3 (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku). The models will be evaluated on both Omni×R_synth and Omni×R_real across all supported modalities: text, image, audio, video, and their combinations. The primary dataset for synthetic evaluation will be MMLU-Pro, sampled across 14 categories, while the real-world set will be constructed from 100 curated YouTube videos in math, physics, chemistry, and coding. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on multiple-choice questions, performance drops relative to pure-text baselines, reasoning path detection rates, and character error rate (CER) for perception tasks. Baselines will include both standard CoT prompting and ETA prompting. Model-specific limitations (e.g., lack of audio/video support) will be accounted for in the experimental setup.
5bce5d4a1bf3112f7d6b3999aa4d7a521e2ff3e0.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark is the first to systematically evaluate OLMs on deep cross-modal reasoning tasks involving more than two modalities and complex real-world scenarios. The dual dataset design (synthetic and real-world) enables both scalable, controlled evaluation and realistic, noisy testing. The Omnify! pipeline provides a scalable, low-cost method for generating information-preserving multi-modal data. The benchmark also introduces mixed-modality and interleaved-modality tasks, which better reflect real-world user interactions. Additionally, the evaluation protocol includes a novel ETA prompting strategy to disentangle perception and reasoning abilities, and the benchmark quantitatively measures reasoning behavior discrepancies across modalities.

5be68d1b4ec1cd8a626c52b3e40a0fd44b24f232.title: Stochastic Optimization for Spectral Risk Measures
5be68d1b4ec1cd8a626c52b3e40a0fd44b24f232.research_question: How can spectral risk measures (L-risks), which interpolate between average-case and worst-case performance, be efficiently and accurately optimized in stochastic settings for machine learning tasks, especially when the objective is non-smooth and subgradient estimates are biased?
5be68d1b4ec1cd8a626c52b3e40a0fd44b24f232.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a novel stochastic optimization algorithm can be developed for spectral risk measures that achieves convergence to the true minimum using only a constant number of function and gradient evaluations per iteration, overcoming the bias and inefficiency present in existing stochastic subgradient methods.
5be68d1b4ec1cd8a626c52b3e40a0fd44b24f232.proposed_method: A new linearly convergent stochastic optimization algorithm for spectral risk measures will be developed, leveraging a detailed characterization of the subdifferential and continuity properties of L-risk objectives. The method will adapt the SVRG (Stochastic Variance Reduced Gradient) framework to handle the non-smoothness and ordering inherent in spectral risk measures, resulting in the LSVRG algorithm. The approach will include a smoothing technique for the empirical L-statistic, enabling efficient gradient computation via isotonic regression at O(n log n) cost per epoch, and will update weights and checkpoints at regular intervals or with a fixed probability. The algorithm will be designed to require only O(1) function and gradient evaluations and O(log n) elementary operations per iteration, ensuring scalability to large datasets. Convergence analysis will be provided for both the non-smooth and smoothed variants, with theoretical guarantees on the error bound and linear convergence rate under standard convexity and Lipschitz assumptions.
5be68d1b4ec1cd8a626c52b3e40a0fd44b24f232.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world regression datasets, including simulated data, the Yacht hydrodynamics dataset, the Energy efficiency dataset, and the Concrete compressive strength dataset. The squared loss under a linear model will be used, and the regularized L-risk objective will be minimized for several spectral risk measures: empirical mean (ERM), superquantile (CVaR), extremile, and exponential spectral risk measure (ESRM). The proposed LSVRG algorithm will be compared against minibatch SGD and stochastic regularized dual averaging (SRDA), with batch sizes set to 64. Evaluation metrics will include the suboptimality gap (relative difference from the optimal risk), convergence rate, and stability of the loss ordering. Additional analyses will examine the bias and variance properties of the algorithms, and the impact of smoothing on empirical performance. Multiple random seeds will be used to assess robustness, and both training and test losses will be reported.
5be68d1b4ec1cd8a626c52b3e40a0fd44b24f232.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first linearly convergent stochastic optimization algorithm for general spectral risk measures that achieves convergence to the true minimum with only constant per-iteration gradient and function evaluations. Unlike prior methods, which suffer from bias or require full-batch computations, the new method efficiently handles the non-smoothness and ordering of losses inherent in L-risks. The smoothing technique for the empirical L-statistic and its efficient implementation via isotonic regression are novel contributions. Theoretical analysis establishes consistency, convergence rates, and error bounds under minimal assumptions, and empirical results demonstrate superior performance and scalability compared to existing baselines.

5bec2a6df12e4cc6034490e400abecfc7ae090fb.title: Broken Tokens? Your Language Model can Secretly Handle Non-Canonical Tokenizations
5bec2a6df12e4cc6034490e400abecfc7ae090fb.research_question: How robust are instruction-tuned language models to non-canonical tokenizations at inference time, and can alternative tokenization schemes be leveraged to improve model performance on specific tasks?
5bec2a6df12e4cc6034490e400abecfc7ae090fb.hypothesis: Instruction-tuned language models are robust to non-canonical tokenizations, and certain alternative tokenization schemes can improve performance on tasks that benefit from finer-grained or more meaningful segmentation.
5bec2a6df12e4cc6034490e400abecfc7ae090fb.proposed_method: The proposed research will systematically evaluate the robustness of instruction-tuned language models to non-canonical tokenizations by generating alternative tokenizations for input text using a fixed tokenizer vocabulary. Two primary non-canonical schemes will be considered: (1) random tokenization, which recursively splits tokens into valid sub-tokens, and (2) character-level tokenization, which decomposes text into individual character tokens. Additionally, task-specific tokenization strategies, such as right-aligned digit grouping for arithmetic, will be explored. The methodology will include ablation studies to identify the training phases and data formats responsible for robustness, and controlled interventions on supervised instruction-tuning procedures to pinpoint the source of generative robustness.
5bec2a6df12e4cc6034490e400abecfc7ae090fb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple instruction-tuned language models, including LLAMA-3.1-8B-INSTRUCT, OLMO-2-7B-INSTRUCT, and QWEN-2.5-7B-INSTRUCT. Evaluation will span 20 diverse benchmarks, including multiple-choice and short-answer tasks (e.g., ARC-C, COPA, MMLU, BoolQ, HellaSwag, WikidataQA, TriviaQA, AlpacaEval, MATH, GSM8K, DROP). For each benchmark, model performance under canonical, random, and character-level tokenizations will be compared. Additional constructed tasks will target string manipulation, code understanding, and arithmetic, using alternative tokenizations hypothesized to be beneficial. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, performance retention relative to canonical tokenization, spelling and grammaticality scores, and win rates as judged by AlpacaEval GPT-4. Ablation studies will manipulate instruction-tuning templates and loss masking to isolate the source of robustness.
5bec2a6df12e4cc6034490e400abecfc7ae090fb.novelty_claims: The research claims that instruction-tuned language models are far more robust to non-canonical tokenizations than previously believed, retaining high performance even with tokenizations never seen during training. It further claims that alternative tokenization schemes can be used at inference time to substantially improve performance on tasks such as code understanding and arithmetic, without any model retraining. The proposal also asserts that the source of this robustness is the separation of instruction and response during supervised instruction-tuning, rather than pretraining, and provides a systematic analysis of how and why this robustness emerges. This work challenges the assumption that language models are tightly bound to their training tokenization and demonstrates the potential for dynamic, task-adaptive tokenization strategies.

5bf89bd184891b890c693cd8e4e54e02a9c6ce10.title: MatryoshkaKV: Adaptive KV Compression via Trainable Orthogonal Projection
5bf89bd184891b890c693cd8e4e54e02a9c6ce10.research_question: How can the feature dimension of the Key-Value (KV) cache in large language models be adaptively compressed to reduce storage and memory transfer bottlenecks, while maintaining high model performance across diverse tasks and resource constraints?
5bf89bd184891b890c693cd8e4e54e02a9c6ce10.hypothesis: Jointly optimizing trainable orthogonal projection matrices for the feature dimension of the KV cache, using a hierarchical (Matryoshka) training strategy and knowledge distillation, will enable higher and more flexible compression rates with minimal performance degradation compared to traditional PCA-based or fixed low-rank projection methods.
5bf89bd184891b890c693cd8e4e54e02a9c6ce10.proposed_method: A novel adaptive KV cache compression framework is proposed, which introduces trainable orthogonal projection matrices to reduce the feature dimension of keys and values in the KV cache of large language models. The method begins with PCA-based initialization of the projection matrices, followed by joint fine-tuning using a knowledge distillation objective that minimizes the KL divergence between the outputs of the compressed and original models, with an additional language modeling loss to preserve generation quality. Orthogonality of the projection matrices is enforced throughout training via Cayley parameterization. To enable smooth trade-offs between compression level and performance, a Matryoshka training strategy is employed: during each iteration, the rank (number of columns) used from each projection matrix is randomly sampled from a predefined schedule, and different ranks are sampled per layer, head, and key/value type. After training, a greedy search algorithm is used to adaptively select heterogeneous compression rates for each layer and head, based on a small calibration dataset and a predefined tolerance for output deviation.
5bf89bd184891b890c693cd8e4e54e02a9c6ce10.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both continual pre-training and supervised fine-tuning scenarios, using LLaMA2-7B-base and Mistral-v0.3-7B-base as base models. The RedPajama dataset will be used for pre-training, and downstream tasks such as PIQA, ARC-challenge, ARC-easy, WinoGrande, HellaSwag, CommonSenseQA, GSM8K, and OpenbookQA will be used for evaluation. Baselines will include PCA-based KV cache compression, ASVD, and other recent methods. Evaluation metrics will include zero-shot accuracy on benchmarks, average accuracy across tasks, and cache utilization rates. The experimental setup will also assess compatibility with other KV cache compression techniques (e.g., H O, KIVI), and include ablation studies on the effects of the Matryoshka training strategy, orthogonality constraints, and PCA initialization. Performance will be measured at various cache budgets (e.g., 100%, 87.5%, 75%, 62.5%, 50%, 37.5%, 25%) and the impact on inference speed will be reported.
5bf89bd184891b890c693cd8e4e54e02a9c6ce10.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable adaptive, trainable orthogonal projection for KV cache compression along the feature dimension, introducing a Matryoshka training strategy that preserves a hierarchical structure in the projections for flexible compression. Unlike prior methods, it allows seamless integration with pre-trained LLMs, supports heterogeneous compression rates per layer and head, and achieves significantly higher compression rates (up to 60-75%) with minimal performance loss. The method is also compatible with other KV cache compression techniques and demonstrates high data efficiency, requiring only a small number of training samples and calibration data.

5c104f905fcacf390270f619f232a2ba4eb873f2.title: FlashFFTConv: Efficient Convolutions for Long Sequences with Tensor Cores
5c104f905fcacf390270f619f232a2ba4eb873f2.research_question: How can the efficiency and hardware utilization of long-sequence convolutional models be improved to enable faster and more scalable sequence modeling across various domains, while maintaining or improving model quality?
5c104f905fcacf390270f619f232a2ba4eb873f2.hypothesis: Optimizing the FFT convolution algorithm to better utilize specialized matrix multiply units (such as tensor cores) and reduce memory I/O through matrix decomposition and kernel fusion will significantly improve the efficiency, scalability, and quality of long-sequence convolutional models.
5c104f905fcacf390270f619f232a2ba4eb873f2.proposed_method: A new framework, FlashFFTConv, will be developed to optimize FFT-based convolutions for long sequences on modern accelerators. The method will employ an order-p Monarch decomposition of the FFT, rewriting the FFT as a series of matrix-matrix multiply operations that are efficiently mapped onto tensor cores. The decomposition order p will be dynamically selected based on sequence length and hardware characteristics to balance FLOP and I/O costs. Kernel fusion will be enabled for longer sequences by broadcasting matrix operations across the sequence dimension, reducing SRAM requirements and transforming costly permutations into efficient matrix transposes. Domain-specific optimizations will be incorporated, including a real-valued FFT algorithm to halve computation, special handling of zero-padding, and fusing additional operations (e.g., gating) to further reduce I/O. Architectural extensions will include partial convolutions (using shorter kernels) and frequency-sparse convolutions (zeroing out kernel components in frequency space), both implemented by skipping blocks in the matrix decomposition for additional memory and compute savings.
5c104f905fcacf390270f619f232a2ba4eb873f2.experiment_details: Experiments will benchmark FlashFFTConv against standard PyTorch FFT convolution and Nvidia's cuFFTdx across a range of sequence lengths (from 256 to 4 million) and modalities, including language modeling (M2-BERT-base, Hyena-GPT-s), high-resolution vision (Path-X, Path-512 from the Long Range Arena benchmark), audio (SaShiMi), and DNA modeling (HyenaDNA). Evaluation metrics will include wall-clock runtime, FLOP utilization, memory footprint, throughput (sequences or tokens per second), and downstream task quality (e.g., perplexity, GLUE score, classification accuracy). Baselines will include PyTorch FFT, cuFFTdx, and highly-optimized Transformer models using FlashAttention-v2. Ablation studies will assess the impact of kernel fusion, tensor core utilization, domain-specific optimizations, and architectural extensions (partial and frequency-sparse convolutions) on both speed and quality.
5c104f905fcacf390270f619f232a2ba4eb873f2.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel adaptation of the Monarch FFT decomposition for convolutions, enabling efficient mapping to tensor cores and kernel fusion for long sequences. FlashFFTConv is the first to enable efficient, scalable FFT convolutions across four orders of magnitude in sequence length, achieving significant speedups and memory savings over existing implementations. The framework also presents convolutional analogues to sparse/approximate attention via partial and frequency-sparse convolutions, which can be implemented efficiently within the matrix decomposition. FlashFFTConv enables longer sequence models in language, vision, and genomics, achieving state-of-the-art results on tasks previously out of reach for convolutional models and matching or surpassing models with twice the parameter count.

5c2a509f60e29a6a6bfcc39e26a95ae689f9c5b0.title: FedCal: Achieving Local and Global Calibration in Federated Learning via Aggregated Parameterized Scaler
5c2a509f60e29a6a6bfcc39e26a95ae689f9c5b0.research_question: How can both local and global model calibration be effectively achieved in federated learning systems under non-IID data distributions, without requiring access to a global validation dataset?
5c2a509f60e29a6a6bfcc39e26a95ae689f9c5b0.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that aggregating client-specific post-hoc calibration scalers via a parameterized and order-preserving architecture can simultaneously improve both local and global calibration in federated learning, even in the absence of a global validation set and under significant data heterogeneity.
5c2a509f60e29a6a6bfcc39e26a95ae689f9c5b0.proposed_method: A novel federated calibration framework, FedCal, will be developed to address calibration at both the client (local) and server (global) levels in federated learning. Each client will train a post-hoc multi-layer perceptron (MLP) scaler on its local data to calibrate the output probabilities of its model, with the scaler designed to be order-preserving to maintain prediction accuracy. These client-specific scalers will then be aggregated using a weight-matching algorithm that aligns the parameters of the MLPs, followed by parameter averaging to produce a global scaler. The global scaler will be periodically synchronized and redistributed to clients, enabling both local adaptation and global consistency. The approach is designed to be compatible with existing FL algorithms and does not require access to a global validation dataset.
5c2a509f60e29a6a6bfcc39e26a95ae689f9c5b0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four benchmark datasets (MNIST, SVHN, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100) with varying degrees of non-IIDness simulated using Dirichlet label skew. The federated setup will involve 20 clients, with 5 randomly selected per round, and models including CNNs and ResNets as base classifiers. Baselines will include standard FL without calibration, temperature scaling on a global validation set, deep ensembles, averaging of temperature scalers, and linear regression-based temperature scaling. Evaluation metrics will focus on global and local Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and test accuracy. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the MLP scaler size, order-preserving constraints, and weight matching. Additional experiments will test integration with non-IID robust FL algorithms such as FedProx.
5c2a509f60e29a6a6bfcc39e26a95ae689f9c5b0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a parameterized, order-preserving MLP scaler that can be aggregated across clients without access to global validation data, addressing both local and global calibration in federated learning. The method leverages weight matching for effective aggregation of neural scalers, ensuring robust calibration and maintaining prediction accuracy under non-IID conditions. This represents a significant advancement over prior work, which either focuses solely on accuracy, requires global validation data, or cannot simultaneously address both local and global calibration. Empirical and theoretical analysis support the claim that this approach achieves substantial improvements in calibration error over state-of-the-art baselines.

5c308e16788bb80d9a6292c05448d319928f0be5.title: See What You Are Told: Visual Attention Sink in Large Multimodal Models
5c308e16788bb80d9a6292c05448d319928f0be5.research_question: How can the allocation of attention in large multimodal models (LMMs) be optimized to enhance their focus on relevant visual information in multimodal tasks, and what are the underlying properties of consistently attended but semantically irrelevant visual tokens?
5c308e16788bb80d9a6292c05448d319928f0be5.hypothesis: The hypothesis is that certain visual tokens in LMMs, which receive consistently high attention weights but are semantically irrelevant (visual attention sink tokens), can be identified and their attention budget can be redistributed to improve the model's focus on meaningful image regions, thereby enhancing overall multimodal performance without additional training or inference steps.
5c308e16788bb80d9a6292c05448d319928f0be5.proposed_method: A novel method, Visual Attention Redistribution (VAR), will be developed to intensify image focus in LMMs by leveraging the phenomenon of visual attention sink. The approach consists of two main steps: (1) selecting image-centric attention heads based on the proportion of attention weights assigned to visual non-sink tokens, and (2) redistributing a portion of the attention weights from identified visual sink tokens to visual non-sink tokens within these selected heads. The method involves computing sink dimension values for each visual token to distinguish sink tokens, accumulating surplus attention from these tokens, and reallocating it proportionally to non-sink visual tokens based on their relative importance. This redistribution is designed to preserve the total attention weight and is applied at the attention map level, requiring no retraining or architectural changes.
5c308e16788bb80d9a6292c05448d319928f0be5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of LMMs, including LLaVA-1.5-7B, LLaVA-1.5-13B, LLaVA-1.5-HD-13B, VILA-13B, Qwen2-VL-7B, and InternVL2-8B. The evaluation will span multiple benchmark datasets across three categories: general vision-language tasks (e.g., VQAv2, GQA, VizWiz, SQAI, VQAT, MME, MMBench, SEED, LLaVAW, MM-Vet), visual hallucination tasks (CHAIR, POPE, MMHal-Bench), and vision-centric tasks (MMVP, CV-Bench2D, CV-Bench3D). Baseline comparisons will be made against the unmodified base models. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, F1 score, hallucination scores, and other task-specific metrics. Hyperparameters for VAR (sink threshold, attention redistribution ratio, head selection threshold) will be kept consistent within each task type, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of each component of the method.
5c308e16788bb80d9a6292c05448d319928f0be5.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the concept of visual attention sink in LMMs, systematically analyzes its properties, and demonstrates that attention allocated to these tokens is surplus and can be recycled. The VAR method is claimed to be model-agnostic, requiring no additional training, models, or inference steps, and can be applied to a wide range of LMMs. The approach provides a new mechanism for steering internal attention to improve multimodal capabilities, and experimental evidence suggests it achieves consistent improvements across diverse benchmarks and tasks. The method also offers insights into the inner workings of attention mechanisms in multimodal transformers.

5c32c653735b43a0a8923ca65ac191bd4bf15311.title: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels
5c32c653735b43a0a8923ca65ac191bd4bf15311.research_question: How can effective zero-shot dense retrieval systems be developed that do not require any relevance labels or supervised fine-tuning, and that generalize across diverse tasks and languages?
5c32c653735b43a0a8923ca65ac191bd4bf15311.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging instruction-following large language models to generate hypothetical documents for queries, followed by encoding these documents with unsupervised contrastive encoders, can enable precise zero-shot dense retrieval without the need for relevance labels.
5c32c653735b43a0a8923ca65ac191bd4bf15311.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a two-stage retrieval framework called HyDE. First, for each input query, an instruction-following large language model (such as InstructGPT) is prompted to generate a hypothetical document that would answer the query, capturing relevance patterns in natural language. This generated document, which may contain factual inaccuracies, is then encoded into a dense vector using an unsupervised contrastive encoder (such as Contriever or mContriever). The resulting embedding is used to search for similar real documents in the corpus by computing vector similarities in the embedding space. This approach grounds the generative output to the actual corpus, with the encoder acting as a lossy compressor that filters out hallucinated details. No additional training or fine-tuning is performed on the retrieval models; both the language model and encoder are used as-is.
5c32c653735b43a0a8923ca65ac191bd4bf15311.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of benchmark datasets, including TREC DL19 and DL20 for web search, six low-resource datasets from the BEIR benchmark (such as Scifact, Arguana, Trec-Covid, FiQA, DBPedia, and TREC-NEWS), and multilingual datasets from Mr.TyDi (covering languages like Swahili, Korean, Japanese, and Bengali). Baselines will include unsupervised dense retrievers (Contriever, mContriever), classical lexical retrievers (BM25), and supervised/fine-tuned dense retrievers (DPR, ANCE, ContrieverFT, mContrieverFT, mDPR, mBERT, XLM-R). Evaluation metrics will include nDCG@10, MAP, Recall@1k, Recall@100, and MRR@100, depending on the dataset. The retrieval experiments will be implemented using the Pyserini toolkit, and different instruction prompts will be tailored for each dataset and language.
5c32c653735b43a0a8923ca65ac191bd4bf15311.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel retrieval paradigm that pivots through hypothetical document embeddings generated by instruction-following language models, enabling dense retrieval without any relevance labels or supervised fine-tuning. This approach decouples relevance modeling from representation learning and leverages the generalization capabilities of large language models for zero-shot retrieval. The method is claimed to outperform state-of-the-art unsupervised dense retrievers and achieve performance competitive with fine-tuned models across multiple tasks and languages, all without access to relevance judgments or training on the target corpora.

5c34278c9cb0c0f7df0a8f84dfa142cf4c57fcd7.title: Frame-Voyager: Learning to Query Frames for Video Large Language Models
5c34278c9cb0c0f7df0a8f84dfa142cf4c57fcd7.research_question: How can the selection of frame combinations for Video Large Language Models (Video-LLMs) be optimized to improve performance on video understanding tasks, given the constraints of input token length and the need for effective temporal and contextual reasoning?
5c34278c9cb0c0f7df0a8f84dfa142cf4c57fcd7.hypothesis: Learning to select informative combinations of video frames, conditioned on the specific textual query, will enable Video-LLMs to achieve superior performance on video understanding tasks compared to uniform sampling or individual text-frame matching methods.
5c34278c9cb0c0f7df0a8f84dfa142cf4c57fcd7.proposed_method: A novel plug-and-play module, FRAME-VOYAGER, will be developed to learn to query and select optimal combinations of video frames based on the input textual query. The approach formulates the frame selection as a ranking task, where frame combinations are ranked according to their utility for answering the query. Training data will be generated automatically by traversing all possible T-frame combinations from a set of M candidate frames for each (video, query) pair, inputting them into a pre-trained reference Video-LLM, and ranking them based on the model's prediction losses. FRAME-VOYAGER will be trained to assign higher rewards to combinations with lower losses, leveraging both query-frame and frame-to-frame interactions via cross-modal transformer layers. During inference, the module will efficiently select the top T frames with the highest predicted rewards to form the input for downstream Video-LLMs.
5c34278c9cb0c0f7df0a8f84dfa142cf4c57fcd7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by integrating FRAME-VOYAGER with multiple state-of-the-art Video-LLMs, including VILA-8B, VILA-40B, and LLaVA-OneVision-7B, and evaluating on four widely-used video question answering benchmarks: Video-MME, MLVU, NextQA, and ActivityNet-QA. The training data for FRAME-VOYAGER will be constructed from the training sets of NextQA and VideoChatGPT, with specific values of M and T (e.g., 16 frames with 2-frame combinations for short videos, 32 frames with 4-frame combinations for longer videos). Baselines for comparison will include uniform frame sampling, rule-based shot boundary detection, clustering, and text-frame matching methods (e.g., CLIP, SigLIP, InternViT-6B). Evaluation metrics will primarily be accuracy, with additional ablation studies to assess the impact of data filtering, combination size, and model architecture choices. All models will be trained and evaluated on high-performance GPU clusters, and accuracy will be reported across all benchmarks and question types.
5c34278c9cb0c0f7df0a8f84dfa142cf4c57fcd7.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first approach to frame selection for Video-LLMs that models frame combinations holistically, rather than retrieving individual frames. It formulates the selection as a ranking problem and provides an automatic, human-free data labeling pipeline using prediction losses from a reference Video-LLM. FRAME-VOYAGER is designed as a lightweight, plug-and-play module compatible with various Video-LLM architectures, and it explicitly models both query-frame and frame-to-frame interactions. The method demonstrates significant improvements over existing frame selection strategies, especially for tasks requiring temporal reasoning and information synthesis in long videos.

5c4bbf816a6e4759b9efe5f37f9c66a603ef9e2f.title: Did You Train on My Dataset? Towards Public Dataset Protection with CleanLabel Backdoor Watermarking
5c4bbf816a6e4759b9efe5f37f9c66a603ef9e2f.research_question: How can public datasets be protected from unauthorized use, particularly for commercial purposes, by embedding robust, stealthy, and verifiable watermarks that do not degrade the utility of the data across multiple modalities such as text, image, and audio?
5c4bbf816a6e4759b9efe5f37f9c66a603ef9e2f.hypothesis: Embedding a small number of clean-label, imperceptibly perturbed samples with consistent labels into public datasets will enable the reliable detection of unauthorized model training on these datasets, without significantly impacting the original task performance or being easily detected by standard data-cleaning or outlier detection methods.
5c4bbf816a6e4759b9efe5f37f9c66a603ef9e2f.proposed_method: A novel clean-label backdoor watermarking framework will be developed that generates watermarking samples by applying human-imperceptible adversarial perturbations to a small subset of data from a target class, preserving the original labels. For each data modality, specialized perturbation and trigger strategies will be designed: synonym replacement and style transfer for text, projected gradient descent-based perturbations and trigger patterns (colorful patches or textures) for images, and impulse signals for audio. These watermarking samples will be injected into the dataset at low rates (e.g., 1-5% of the target class). Models trained on the watermarked dataset will implicitly learn a secret backdoor function, which can be verified post hoc by applying the trigger and performing statistical hypothesis testing (such as the Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test) on model predictions. The method will emphasize low distortion to task performance, high effectiveness in watermark detection, and stealthiness against common data-cleaning and outlier detection techniques.
5c4bbf816a6e4759b9efe5f37f9c66a603ef9e2f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on seven real-world datasets spanning text (SST-2, IMDB, SNLI), image (CIFAR-10, TinyImageNet, Caltech256), and audio (AudioMNIST). For each domain, state-of-the-art models will be fine-tuned or trained from scratch (e.g., BERT for text, ResNet-18 for images, RawAudioCNN for audio). Watermarking samples will be injected at various rates (1%, 5%, 10%, 20% of the target class), and models will be evaluated on both original and watermarked datasets. Baselines will include conventional backdoor insertion and direct trigger-stamped sample addition. Evaluation metrics will include Accuracy Drop (AD) to measure utility loss, Trigger Success Rate (TSR) for backdoor effectiveness, Watermark Detection Rate (WDR) using statistical hypothesis testing, and Watermarking Samples Detectability (WSD) using outlier detection (autoencoder-based, confidence-based, and grammatical error rate for text). Transferability across model architectures and robustness to data-cleaning methods will be systematically assessed.
5c4bbf816a6e4759b9efe5f37f9c66a603ef9e2f.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a clean-label, imperceptible perturbation-based watermarking approach that is applicable across text, image, and audio datasets, overcoming the limitations of prior methods that rely on mislabeled or easily detectable samples. The method enables robust and stealthy dataset watermarking with minimal impact on original task performance and demonstrates resilience to standard data-cleaning and outlier detection techniques. Additionally, the approach is validated across multiple modalities and model architectures, providing a general and practical solution for public dataset protection and ownership verification.

5c55a465aa4011bfe29b7d0ad5dbaae7d34c58b6.title: Silencer: From Discovery to Mitigation of Self-Bias in LLM-as-Benchmark-Generator
5c55a465aa4011bfe29b7d0ad5dbaae7d34c58b6.research_question: How can self-bias in large language model (LLM)-as-benchmark-generator paradigms be systematically identified, quantified, and effectively mitigated to ensure more reliable and human-aligned evaluation benchmarks across diverse tasks and models?
5c55a465aa4011bfe29b7d0ad5dbaae7d34c58b6.hypothesis: Self-bias in LLM-generated benchmarks arises from multiple sub-biases, including question domain bias, language style bias, and wrong label bias, and can be significantly mitigated by leveraging generator heterogeneity and targeted debiasing strategies at both the sample and benchmark levels.
5c55a465aa4011bfe29b7d0ad5dbaae7d34c58b6.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework, SILENCER, will be developed to neutralize self-bias in LLM-generated benchmarks. At the sample level, three strategies will be implemented: Attribute Integration to diversify and debias the question domain by integrating attribute sets across multiple generators; Cross Paraphrase to increase linguistic diversity and suppress language style bias by having generators paraphrase each other's questions; and Label Calibration to reduce wrong label bias by calibrating labels using predictions from multiple generators. At the benchmark level, a Bias-Neutralizing Ensemble algorithm will be employed, which iteratively estimates each generator's self-bias by measuring evaluation consistency with the ensembled benchmark and assigns ensemble weights inversely proportional to self-bias. The ensemble process will converge to a final benchmark with minimized self-bias, using evaluation consistency as the primary criterion for weight updates.
5c55a465aa4011bfe29b7d0ad5dbaae7d34c58b6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across three tasks—math reasoning (MATH), language understanding (MMLU-Pro), and commonsense reasoning (HellaSwag)—each paired with high-quality human-annotated benchmarks. Seven diverse LLMs, both open- and closed-source (including GPT-4o mini, Qwen-Plus, Claude 3.5 Haiku, DeepSeek-Distill-Qwen-32B, GPT-4o, QwQ-32B, and Gemini 2.0 Flash), will serve as benchmark generators. A reference set of 16 LLMs will be used for evaluation, with each experiment averaging results over 1,000 random seeds and varying the number of generators and reference models. Baseline methods will include BenchMaker and AttrPrompt, with and without the SILENCER framework. Evaluation metrics will comprise self-bias (as defined by relative performance differences), Pearson correlation with human-annotated benchmarks, label accuracy (using OpenAI o3-mini as a judge), semantic diversity (entropy and n-gram statistics), and distributional similarity (Maximum Mean Discrepancy and Wasserstein Distance). Ablation studies and parameter sweeps (e.g., number of generators, benchmark size) will further analyze the framework's effectiveness and robustness.
5c55a465aa4011bfe29b7d0ad5dbaae7d34c58b6.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a formal, quantifiable definition of self-bias in LLM-as-benchmark-generator settings and systematically decomposes it into three measurable sub-biases. SILENCER is a novel, general-purpose framework that combines sample-level debiasing (across domain, style, and label dimensions) with a benchmark-level bias-neutralizing ensemble, leveraging generator heterogeneity for robust bias suppression. The ensemble weighting algorithm based on evaluation consistency is a new approach for minimizing self-bias without requiring human-annotated benchmarks. The methodology is validated across multiple tasks, models, and generation strategies, demonstrating significant improvements in benchmark quality, evaluation reliability, and generalizability.

5c601530f798283890635475e80f57a5e5f69642.title: ManiSkill-HAB: A Benchmark for Low-Level Manipulation in Home Rearrangement Tasks
5c601530f798283890635475e80f57a5e5f69642.research_question: How can a unified, scalable, and realistic benchmark be developed to advance low-level manipulation and object rearrangement tasks in home environments for embodied AI research?
5c601530f798283890635475e80f57a5e5f69642.hypothesis: A GPU-accelerated, realistic simulation environment supporting low-level control, combined with automated trajectory filtering and extensive RL/IL baselines, will enable efficient training, evaluation, and dataset generation for complex home rearrangement tasks, leading to improved policy performance and more controlled data collection.
5c601530f798283890635475e80f57a5e5f69642.proposed_method: A holistic benchmark, MS-HAB, will be developed by implementing a GPU-accelerated version of the Home Assistant Benchmark (HAB) using the ManiSkill3 simulator. The environment will support realistic low-level control for a mobile manipulator (Fetch robot), including grasping, manipulation, and interaction with articulated objects (e.g., fridge, drawers) in apartment-scale scenes. The benchmark will provide parallelized simulation for efficient training and data generation, and will include hand-engineered dense rewards for reinforcement learning (RL) and imitation learning (IL) baselines. Automated event labeling and rule-based trajectory filtering will be incorporated to categorize demonstrations by success and failure modes, enabling scalable, controlled dataset generation. Per-object policies will be trained for manipulation subtasks to address object-specific challenges, and skill chaining will be used to solve long-horizon tasks.
5c601530f798283890635475e80f57a5e5f69642.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three long-horizon home rearrangement tasks (TidyHouse, PrepareGroceries, SetTable) using the ReplicaCAD dataset, which provides 105 apartment scenes with macro- and micro-variations. The dataset will be split into training and validation sets, with 10,000 training and 1,000 validation episode configurations per task. RL baselines will be trained using SAC and PPO algorithms with visual and proprioceptive observations, and per-object as well as all-object policies will be compared. Evaluation metrics will include subtask success once rate and progressive completion rate for long-horizon tasks, with 1,000 episodes per evaluation. Automated trajectory labeling will be used to analyze failure modes and filter demonstrations for IL baselines. Benchmarking will compare simulation speed and memory usage against Habitat 2.0, and ablations will assess the impact of per-object policies and demonstration filtering.
5c601530f798283890635475e80f57a5e5f69642.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces the first GPU-accelerated, realistic low-level control implementation of HAB, achieving over 3x the simulation speed of prior implementations with significantly reduced GPU memory usage. It uniquely supports automated event labeling and trajectory filtering for scalable, controlled dataset generation. The benchmark provides extensive RL and IL baselines, including per-object manipulation policies, and enables efficient training and evaluation for complex, long-horizon home rearrangement tasks. The combination of realistic physics, high simulation throughput, and automated data curation represents a significant advancement for embodied AI research in home environments.

5c6a37a1332ef6a49f8e3805cb52f526c97751df.title: Nonlocal Kernel Network (NKN): a Stable and Resolution-Independent Deep Neural Network
5c6a37a1332ef6a49f8e3805cb52f526c97751df.research_question: How can a deep neural network architecture be designed to achieve stability in the deep-layer limit, independence from input resolution, and the ability to capture long-range dependencies in the feature space, for tasks such as learning governing equations and image classification?
5c6a37a1332ef6a49f8e3805cb52f526c97751df.hypothesis: A neural network architecture based on nonlocal integral operators, interpreted as a discretized nonlocal diffusion-reaction equation, will provide stable, resolution-independent, and accurate performance for both operator learning and image classification tasks, outperforming existing baseline methods.
5c6a37a1332ef6a49f8e3805cb52f526c97751df.proposed_method: A novel deep neural network architecture, termed the Nonlocal Kernel Network (NKN), will be developed by modeling feature space interactions continuously via integral operators acting on the node domain. Each network layer will be interpreted as a discretized time-step of a nonlocal diffusion-reaction equation, with the limit of infinite layers corresponding to a parabolic nonlocal equation. The architecture will employ nonlocal vector calculus to guarantee stability in the deep-layer limit. Node-to-node interactions will be parameterized by learnable kernel functions, enabling the network to capture long-range dependencies and achieve resolution independence. The NKN will also leverage shallow-to-deep initialization techniques, where parameters optimized on shallow networks are used as initial guesses for deeper networks, accelerating convergence and improving generalization.
5c6a37a1332ef6a49f8e3805cb52f526c97751df.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both operator learning and image classification tasks. For operator learning, benchmark PDEs such as the 1D Poisson equation and 2D Darcy's equation will be used, with input-output function pairs sampled at varying resolutions to test resolution independence. For image classification, standard datasets such as MNIST and CIFAR will be employed, including cross-resolution training and testing scenarios. Baseline comparisons will include Graph Kernel Networks (GKNs), Fourier Neural Operators (FNOs), Nonlocal Neural Networks (NNNs), and multiscale CNNs. Evaluation metrics will include mean squared error for operator learning and classification accuracy (with cross-entropy loss) for image tasks. Experimental setups will test generalization across resolutions and network depths, and will assess stability and performance improvements enabled by the proposed architecture.
5c6a37a1332ef6a49f8e3805cb52f526c97751df.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a deep neural network architecture that is simultaneously stable in the deep-layer limit, resolution-independent, and capable of modeling long-range dependencies via nonlocal integral operators. The method unifies and extends the advantages of existing neural operator and nonlocal network architectures while overcoming their limitations, particularly instability in deep networks and lack of resolution independence. The interpretation of the network as a nonlocal parabolic equation enables theoretical guarantees of stability and supports accelerated training via shallow-to-deep initialization. The architecture is general and flexible, demonstrating superior performance in both operator learning and image classification tasks, and enabling transfer across resolutions and depths.

5c7f465d162aade4a4c0eefb02fd7aadeebdaf58.title: LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations
5c7f465d162aade4a4c0eefb02fd7aadeebdaf58.research_question: Do large language models (LLMs) exhibit a bias toward favoring their own generated outputs during evaluation, and is this bias causally linked to their ability to recognize their own generations? How does this self-recognition capability impact the reliability and neutrality of LLM-based self-evaluation, particularly in tasks such as text summarization?
5c7f465d162aade4a4c0eefb02fd7aadeebdaf58.hypothesis: LLMs demonstrate self-preference in evaluation tasks because they possess the capability to recognize their own outputs, and increasing self-recognition ability will causally increase the strength of self-preference bias.
5c7f465d162aade4a4c0eefb02fd7aadeebdaf58.proposed_method: A comprehensive experimental framework will be developed to measure and manipulate the self-recognition and self-preference capabilities of LLMs. The approach involves using both prompting and supervised fine-tuning to alter LLMs' ability to recognize their own outputs, with explicit pairwise and individual evaluation settings. LLMs will be presented with summaries generated by themselves, other LLMs, and humans, and tasked with both identifying the source and rating the quality of each summary. Fine-tuning will be conducted on a subset of data to enhance or reduce self-recognition, and additional control fine-tuning tasks (e.g., length, vowel count, readability) will be used to rule out confounders. The correlation between self-recognition and self-preference will be systematically measured, and causal relationships will be probed by varying the fine-tuning regime and introducing explicit source labels.
5c7f465d162aade4a4c0eefb02fd7aadeebdaf58.experiment_details: Experiments will focus on the text summarization domain using the XSUM and CNN/DailyMail datasets, each providing 1,000 news articles and corresponding human-written summaries. Summaries will be generated by multiple LLMs, including Llama-2-7b-chat, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4, with sampling at temperature zero and standardized formatting. Both out-of-the-box and fine-tuned versions of these models will serve as evaluators. Evaluation will use both pairwise (comparing two summaries) and individual (single summary) settings, with Likert-scale ratings and confidence-based scoring. Baselines will include human annotators and alternative LLMs. Metrics will include self-recognition accuracy, self-preference scores, and Kendall’s tau correlation between recognition and preference. Fine-tuning will be performed on 500 training articles, with separate in-domain and out-of-domain evaluation, and additional control tasks will be included to test for confounding effects.
5c7f465d162aade4a4c0eefb02fd7aadeebdaf58.novelty_claims: The proposed research establishes a direct, causal link between LLMs' self-recognition ability and their self-preference bias in evaluation tasks, a connection not previously demonstrated in the literature. The methodology introduces a systematic way to manipulate and measure self-recognition and self-preference through fine-tuning and controlled prompting, while rigorously controlling for confounders. The work provides the first evidence that self-recognition is a generalizable capability that can be amplified or reduced, and that it linearly correlates with self-preference bias. These findings have significant implications for the reliability of LLM-based self-evaluation, AI safety, and the design of unbiased evaluation protocols.

5c821763f76272b6deee95f9729107969ce0ae44.title: DiffusionPDE: Generative PDE-Solving Under Partial Observation
5c821763f76272b6deee95f9729107969ce0ae44.research_question: How can partial differential equations (PDEs) be accurately solved in both forward and inverse directions when only partial, sparse, or incomplete observations are available for the coefficients or solutions?
5c821763f76272b6deee95f9729107969ce0ae44.hypothesis: A generative diffusion model that learns the joint distribution of PDE coefficients and solutions, guided by sparse observations and PDE constraints during inference, will enable accurate recovery of both missing coefficients and solutions from partial observations, outperforming existing deterministic and generative PDE solvers.
5c821763f76272b6deee95f9729107969ce0ae44.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that leverages generative diffusion models to solve PDEs under partial observation. The approach involves pre-training a diffusion model on a family of PDEs to learn the joint distribution of coefficients (or initial states) and solutions (or final states). During inference, the model will start from Gaussian noise and iteratively denoise it, guided by both sparse observed data and the governing PDE constraints. The denoising process will be modified by incorporating gradients from observation loss (mean squared error between predictions and observed values) and PDE residual loss (enforcing the PDE equation) at each step, enabling the model to reconstruct both the coefficient and solution fields even with highly sparse data. The method is designed to handle arbitrary sparsity patterns and can be applied to both static and dynamic PDEs, unifying forward and inverse problem-solving within a single pre-trained network.
5c821763f76272b6deee95f9729107969ce0ae44.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of PDEs, including Darcy Flow, Poisson, Helmholtz, Burgers', and both bounded and unbounded Navier-Stokes equations. Datasets will be generated using finite element methods, finite difference schemes, and existing simulation scripts, with training data comprising tens of thousands of pairs of coefficients and solutions on 128x128 grids (or equivalent for 1D/temporal problems). The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art learning-based PDE solvers such as PINO, DeepONet, PINNs, FNO, GraphPDE, OFormer, and classifier-free guidance diffusion approaches. Evaluation metrics will include mean pixel-wise relative error and error rates, with experiments testing both forward and inverse problems under varying levels of observation sparsity (typically 1-3% observed points). Additional analyses will assess the impact of the number and pattern of observations, as well as the contribution of PDE loss guidance.
5c821763f76272b6deee95f9729107969ce0ae44.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a unified generative approach for solving both forward and inverse PDE problems under highly partial observations, which is not supported by existing deterministic or generative PDE solvers. By modeling the joint distribution of coefficients and solutions and guiding the diffusion process with both sparse data and PDE constraints, the method can simultaneously reconstruct missing information in both spaces. The approach is robust to arbitrary sparsity patterns and achieves significantly lower errors than state-of-the-art baselines, demonstrating the effectiveness of generative priors for physical modeling in real-world scenarios with incomplete data.
