5c9eec060bd9b7af1b8f71a18c0402de3dc98388.title: Robust Preference Optimization through Reward Model Distillation
5c9eec060bd9b7af1b8f71a18c0402de3dc98388.research_question: How can the robustness and effectiveness of language model alignment with human preferences be improved, particularly in offline settings where preference data may be biased or limited?
5c9eec060bd9b7af1b8f71a18c0402de3dc98388.hypothesis: Explicitly distilling reward models into the policy, and further incorporating pessimism over a family of plausible reward models, will yield more robust and effective preference optimization than direct preference optimization alone, especially under distribution shift or bias in preference annotations.
5c9eec060bd9b7af1b8f71a18c0402de3dc98388.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that distills the knowledge of an explicit reward model, trained on preference data, into the language model policy. The approach optimizes a squared loss that matches the pairwise differences in reward scores between generation pairs, aligning the policy's implicit reward with the explicit reward model. To address uncertainty in the reward model, a pessimistic extension is introduced: the policy is trained to maximize the worst-case improvement across a set of plausible reward models, effectively regularizing against overfitting to any single reward function. This pessimistic distillation is implemented by augmenting the distillation loss with a forward KL-divergence penalty between the policy and a reference model, and can be extended to ensembles of reward models to further enhance robustness.
5c9eec060bd9b7af1b8f71a18c0402de3dc98388.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the TL;DR summarization task, where spurious correlations between summary length and preference are introduced to simulate biased preference data. Training sets are constructed with varying degrees of length bias, and the proposed methods are compared against Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and Identity Preference Optimization (IPO) baselines. Evaluation is performed using an oracle reward model trained on the full preference dataset, measuring the average reward and advantage over a supervised finetuned reference policy. Policies and reward models are initialized from Palm-2-XS, with hyperparameters tuned on validation data. Additional experiments are performed on unbiased TL;DR and Anthropic Helpfulness datasets to assess generalization.
5c9eec060bd9b7af1b8f71a18c0402de3dc98388.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces reward model distillation for offline preference optimization, bridging the gap between supervised direct preference optimization and explicit reward modeling. The pessimistic extension, which optimizes for the worst-case reward over a set of plausible models, provides a principled mechanism for handling uncertainty and distribution shift in preference data. The approach maintains the simplicity and efficiency of offline alignment while offering improved robustness and theoretical guarantees against degeneracy and overfitting observed in prior methods. Empirical results demonstrate significant improvements over existing offline alignment techniques, especially in the presence of biased or challenging preference distributions.

5ca04cde78542b8d58c4c5b2db91ddd65b56d917.title: LazyGNN: Large-Scale Graph Neural Networks via Lazy Propagation
5ca04cde78542b8d58c4c5b2db91ddd65b56d917.research_question: How can long-distance dependencies in large-scale graphs be efficiently captured for graph neural network (GNN) representation learning without incurring the scalability issues associated with deep models and neighborhood explosion?
5ca04cde78542b8d58c4c5b2db91ddd65b56d917.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that long-distance dependencies in graphs can be effectively captured by shallow GNN models through a lazy propagation mechanism that reuses historical node embeddings across training iterations, thereby reducing the need for deep propagation layers and mitigating scalability challenges.
5ca04cde78542b8d58c4c5b2db91ddd65b56d917.proposed_method: A novel shallow GNN framework, LazyGNN, will be developed to capture long-distance dependencies in graphs using lazy forward and backward propagation. The method leverages the observation that node embeddings change slowly across training iterations, allowing for the reuse of previously propagated features and gradients. LazyGNN introduces a momentum-based correction to combine current and historical embeddings, controlled by hyperparameters, to compensate for variations introduced by dropout and stochastic training. The forward computation involves a small number of aggregation layers, while the backward computation utilizes the implicit function theorem to efficiently compute gradients without storing full computational graphs. Additionally, a mini-batch version of LazyGNN will be implemented, using subgraph sampling to further improve scalability and memory efficiency for large-scale graphs.
5ca04cde78542b8d58c4c5b2db91ddd65b56d917.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple large-scale graph datasets, including REDDIT, YELP, FLICKR, ogbn-arxiv, and ogbn-products. The proposed method will be compared against a comprehensive set of baselines, such as GCN, GraphSAGE, FastGCN, LADIES, VR-GCN, MVS-GNN, Cluster-GCN, GraphSAINT, SGC, SIGN, GNNAutoScale, and VQ-GNN. Both full-batch and mini-batch training settings will be evaluated. Evaluation metrics will include node classification accuracy, memory usage, and training time per epoch. Ablation studies will be performed to analyze the effects of propagation layers, batch size, and hyperparameters on performance, as well as to investigate over-smoothing and convergence behavior.
5ca04cde78542b8d58c4c5b2db91ddd65b56d917.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a fundamentally different perspective by capturing long-distance dependencies with shallow GNNs through lazy propagation, rather than increasing model depth. LazyGNN significantly reduces computation, memory, and communication costs by reusing historical embeddings and gradients, and it is the first GNN model to be inherently compatible with existing scalable techniques such as sampling, parallelism, and end-to-end training. The method addresses technical challenges such as over-smoothing and dropout-induced variation with innovative momentum-based corrections, and provides a scalable mini-batch variant that achieves state-of-the-art performance and efficiency on large-scale graph benchmarks.

5cbe278b65a81602a864184bbca37de91448a5f5.title: Competition-level code generation with AlphaCode
5cbe278b65a81602a864184bbca37de91448a5f5.research_question: Can an AI system be developed that generates correct and original solutions to complex, real-world competitive programming problems, achieving performance comparable to human participants in programming competitions?
5cbe278b65a81602a864184bbca37de91448a5f5.hypothesis: A large-scale transformer-based language model, pre-trained on diverse code and fine-tuned on a curated competitive programming dataset, combined with large-scale sampling and behavior-based filtering, can generate novel and correct solutions to complex competitive programming problems at a level competitive with human programmers.
5cbe278b65a81602a864184bbca37de91448a5f5.proposed_method: The proposed method involves pre-training a transformer-based encoder-decoder language model on a large corpus of open-source code from GitHub, covering multiple programming languages. The model is then fine-tuned on a newly curated dataset (CodeContests) of competitive programming problems, which includes temporally split training, validation, and test sets to prevent data leakage. For each problem, the model generates a large number of candidate program samples. These samples are filtered using example test cases from the problem description, and further clustered based on program behavior to select a small set of diverse and promising submissions. The final candidate solutions are submitted for evaluation against hidden test cases, mirroring the competitive programming environment.
5cbe278b65a81602a864184bbca37de91448a5f5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the CodeContests dataset, which includes problems and solutions scraped from Codeforces and other sources, with strict temporal splits to ensure evaluation on truly unseen problems. Additional test cases will be generated via input mutation to reduce false positives and ensure robust evaluation. The system will also be evaluated on simulated Codeforces competitions, comparing its ranking and estimated rating against thousands of human participants. Baselines will include prior program synthesis models and large language models such as Codex, with evaluation metrics including solve rate (n@k), false positive rate, and competition ranking percentile. Multiple model sizes (ranging from 300M to 41B parameters) will be tested, and ablation studies will assess the impact of dataset quality, sampling strategy, and filtering techniques.
5cbe278b65a81602a864184bbca37de91448a5f5.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel combination of large-scale transformer-based code generation, a rigorously curated and temporally split competitive programming dataset, and a unique large-scale sampling and behavior-based filtering pipeline. The approach enables the generation of original, non-copied solutions to previously unseen, complex programming problems. The evaluation protocol closely mirrors real-world programming competitions, and the system aims to achieve, for the first time, a competitive ranking among thousands of human participants in actual programming contests. The dataset and methodology significantly reduce false positive rates compared to prior benchmarks, providing a more reliable measure of progress in AI code generation.

5cd671efa2af8456c615c5faf54d1be4950f3819.title: Hallucination is Inevitable: An Innate Limitation of Large Language Models
5cd671efa2af8456c615c5faf54d1be4950f3819.research_question: Can hallucination in large language models (LLMs) be fundamentally eliminated, or is it an unavoidable limitation when LLMs are used as general problem solvers?
5cd671efa2af8456c615c5faf54d1be4950f3819.hypothesis: Hallucination is inevitable for any computable LLM, regardless of model architecture, training procedure, or input prompts, when used as a general problem solver.
5cd671efa2af8456c615c5faf54d1be4950f3819.proposed_method: A formal framework will be established to rigorously define hallucination in the context of LLMs by considering a 'formal world' of computable functions. Within this framework, LLMs are modeled as total computable functions mapping input strings to outputs, and hallucination is defined as any inconsistency between the LLM's output and a computable ground truth function. The methodology will leverage foundational results from learning theory, particularly diagonalization arguments, to prove that for any computable LLM (or any computably enumerable set of LLMs), there exists a computable function for which the LLM will inevitably hallucinate on at least some inputs, and often on infinitely many. The analysis will be extended to LLMs with practical constraints, such as polynomial time bounds, and will identify classes of problems that are inherently hallucination-prone for such models.
5cd671efa2af8456c615c5faf54d1be4950f3819.experiment_details: Empirical validation will be conducted on selected hallucination-prone problems identified through theoretical analysis, such as combinatorial listing, Presburger arithmetic, subset sum, and Boolean satisfiability (SAT). Existing LLMs will be evaluated on these tasks using benchmarks and datasets that exemplify computational hardness or undecidability. Baselines will include standard LLM architectures and configurations, with evaluation metrics focusing on factual correctness and consistency with ground truth functions. Experimental setup will involve comparing LLM outputs to the ground truth on tasks that are provably beyond the computational capabilities of the models, thereby empirically illustrating the inevitability of hallucination.
5cd671efa2af8456c615c5faf54d1be4950f3819.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a formal, learning-theoretic framework that rigorously defines and analyzes hallucination in LLMs, moving beyond empirical observations to establish fundamental limitations. It provides the first formal proof that hallucination is unavoidable for all computable LLMs, independent of implementation details, and identifies broad classes of hallucination-prone problems. The work also systematically discusses the limitations of existing hallucination mitigation strategies and delineates the boundaries of LLM capabilities, offering new theoretical insights with practical implications for safe deployment and regulation.

5cde475c3b572cf81d9b14c4fd1163c1c2c19568.title: Steering Your Generalists: Improving Robotic Foundation Models via Value Guidance
5cde475c3b572cf81d9b14c4fd1163c1c2c19568.research_question: How can the performance, precision, and robustness of generalist robotic foundation models be improved at deployment time, particularly when trained on large, mixed-quality datasets and without access to policy weights or fine-tuning?
5cde475c3b572cf81d9b14c4fd1163c1c2c19568.hypothesis: A value function learned via offline reinforcement learning can be used at test time to re-rank action proposals from pre-trained generalist robotic policies, thereby improving their downstream performance, precision, and robustness across diverse tasks and embodiments, even when the policy is accessed as a black box.
5cde475c3b572cf81d9b14c4fd1163c1c2c19568.proposed_method: A modular framework, Value-Guided Policy Steering (V-GPS), will be developed to enhance generalist robotic policies at deployment by re-ranking their action proposals using a value function. This value function will be trained offline on diverse, language-annotated robotic datasets using a conservative offline RL algorithm (Calibrated Q-Learning, Cal-QL) to ensure robustness to out-of-distribution actions and noisy data. The value function will be language-conditioned, utilizing a ResNet-34 image encoder with FiLM language conditioning and a frozen MUSE encoder for language processing. At test time, for each step, the generalist policy will propose multiple candidate actions given the current state and language instruction; these actions will be scored by the value function, and the highest-value action (or a sample from a temperature-controlled softmax over Q-values) will be executed. This approach requires no fine-tuning or access to the policy weights, and is compatible with any off-the-shelf, black-box generalist policy.
5cde475c3b572cf81d9b14c4fd1163c1c2c19568.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both real-world and simulated environments, using two different robot embodiments (WidowX250 and Google Robot) and a total of 12 manipulation tasks. The value function will be trained on a mix of the BridgeV2 dataset (45K language-annotated demonstrations across 24 environments) and the Fractal dataset (130K episodes covering 700+ tasks). The method will be evaluated on five state-of-the-art generalist policies (Octo-small, Octo-base, Octo-small-1.5, RT1-X, and OpenVLA), all accessed as black boxes. Baselines will include the original generalist policies without value guidance and, where relevant, policy fine-tuning. Evaluation metrics will focus on task success rates, with detailed analysis of failure modes (e.g., grasping precision, timing of object release). Both quantitative (success rates) and qualitative (visualizations of failure mitigation) results will be reported.
5cde475c3b572cf81d9b14c4fd1163c1c2c19568.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to leverage test-time action sampling and value-based re-ranking for real-world generalist robotic policies in a plug-and-play, black-box manner. The method is broadly compatible with diverse policy architectures and datasets, does not require policy fine-tuning or weight access, and demonstrates consistent performance improvements across multiple tasks, embodiments, and state-of-the-art generalist policies. The approach addresses key failure modes of generalist policies, such as imprecise manipulation and robustness to environmental shifts, and provides a scalable recipe for deployment-time enhancement of robotic foundation models.

5d1ca53a0b41f4f5c960cd9997556d7180d6b88d.title: FlashAttention-3: Fast and Accurate Attention with Asynchrony and Low-precision
5d1ca53a0b41f4f5c960cd9997556d7180d6b88d.research_question: How can the efficiency and accuracy of attention mechanisms in Transformer architectures be improved on modern GPU hardware, particularly for large language models and long-context applications?
5d1ca53a0b41f4f5c960cd9997556d7180d6b88d.hypothesis: Leveraging hardware asynchrony and low-precision computation, combined with algorithmic innovations such as warp-specialization, pipelined overlapping of computation and data movement, and advanced quantization techniques, will significantly improve the speed and maintain or enhance the numerical accuracy of attention mechanisms on state-of-the-art GPUs.
5d1ca53a0b41f4f5c960cd9997556d7180d6b88d.proposed_method: A new attention computation framework will be developed that exploits the asynchronous execution capabilities of modern GPUs, specifically targeting the NVIDIA Hopper architecture. The method will implement a warp-specialized producer-consumer pipeline, where data movement (via Tensor Memory Accelerator) and computation (via Tensor Cores) are overlapped using a circular shared memory buffer and pingpong scheduling between warpgroups. Softmax and matrix multiplication operations will be interleaved through a two-stage (and optionally three-stage) pipelining scheme to maximize hardware utilization. For low-precision computation, the method will introduce in-kernel transposition and register permutation to satisfy FP8 layout constraints, and will incorporate block quantization and incoherent processing (random orthogonal transformations) to minimize quantization error, especially in the presence of outlier features. The approach will be compatible with multi-head, multi-query, and grouped-query attention variants.
5d1ca53a0b41f4f5c960cd9997556d7180d6b88d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on NVIDIA H100 SXM5 GPUs, benchmarking the proposed method against standard PyTorch attention, FlashAttention-2, FlashAttention-2 implemented in Triton, and NVIDIA's cuDNN attention implementation. Evaluation will cover a range of sequence lengths (512 to 16k), head dimensions (64, 128, 256), and both FP16 and FP8 precisions, with and without causal masking. Metrics will include runtime (TFLOPs/s), GPU utilization, and numerical error (compared to FP64 reference). Ablation studies will isolate the effects of warp-specialization and GEMM-softmax pipelining. Additional experiments will validate the accuracy improvements from block quantization and incoherent processing in FP8, particularly for inputs with simulated outlier features.
5d1ca53a0b41f4f5c960cd9997556d7180d6b88d.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel combination of hardware-aware algorithmic strategies for attention computation, including asynchronous producer-consumer pipelining with warp-specialization, intra- and inter-warpgroup pipelined overlapping of softmax and GEMM operations, and efficient support for FP8 low-precision via in-kernel transposition and register permutation. The integration of block quantization and incoherent processing for FP8 attention is claimed to substantially reduce numerical error compared to standard per-tensor quantization. The approach is designed to achieve near-peak hardware utilization, delivering up to 2x speedup over prior state-of-the-art methods while maintaining or improving accuracy, and is validated across a comprehensive set of benchmarks and ablation studies.

5d1ddd775dec2fc8f7aaa40fe1aab5308b55eae1.title: FedBEns: One-Shot Federated Learning based on Bayesian Ensemble
5d1ddd775dec2fc8f7aaa40fe1aab5308b55eae1.research_question: How can a global model be effectively learned in a single round of communication in federated learning, particularly in the presence of highly heterogeneous and non-i.i.d. client data distributions?
5d1ddd775dec2fc8f7aaa40fe1aab5308b55eae1.hypothesis: A multimodal Bayesian ensemble approach that aggregates local client posteriors using mixtures of Laplace approximations will yield a more accurate and robust global model in one-shot federated learning settings, outperforming unimodal or single-point aggregation methods, especially under high data heterogeneity.
5d1ddd775dec2fc8f7aaa40fe1aab5308b55eae1.proposed_method: The proposed method, FedBEns, constructs a global posterior by aggregating local client posteriors, each approximated as a mixture of Laplace approximations centered at multiple local optima found via independent training runs with different initializations. Each client trains M models on its local data, computes the MAP estimates and corresponding precision matrices (using either diagonal or Kronecker-factored Hessian approximations), and sends these to the server. The server combines these mixtures using a principled Bayesian aggregation rule, resulting in a global multimodal posterior that captures the diversity of local loss landscapes. The final global model is represented as an ensemble, and predictions are made by marginalizing over the global posterior, effectively averaging over multiple modes. Temperature scaling and a Gaussian prior are used to improve posterior calibration and regularization.
5d1ddd775dec2fc8f7aaa40fe1aab5308b55eae1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard federated learning benchmarks, including FashionMNIST, SVHN, and CIFAR10, with varying numbers of clients (e.g., 5, 10, 20, 40) and degrees of data heterogeneity (controlled via Dirichlet sampling with different alpha values). The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art one-shot FL baselines such as FedFisher (with Kronecker approximation), RegMean, DENSE, OTFusion, and FisherMerge. Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy and standard deviation over multiple random seeds. All methods will use consistent training protocols (e.g., SGD optimizer, fixed number of local epochs, batch size, and learning rate) and hyperparameter tuning will be performed using a small server-side validation set. Ablation studies will investigate the impact of the number of mixture components and different Hessian approximations.
5d1ddd775dec2fc8f7aaa40fe1aab5308b55eae1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a fully Bayesian, multimodal aggregation framework for one-shot federated learning, leveraging mixtures of Laplace approximations to capture the inherent multi-modality of local loss surfaces. Unlike prior methods that rely on unimodal or quadratic approximations, this method enables more faithful posterior aggregation and model marginalization, leading to improved predictive performance under high data heterogeneity and with a single communication round. The method is architecture-agnostic, does not require server-side data or generative models, and allows flexible trade-offs between accuracy and computational cost by adjusting the ensemble size.

5d321194696f1f75cf9da045e6022b2f20ba5b9c.title: Video-LLaMA: An Instruction-tuned Audio-Visual Language Model for Video Understanding
5d321194696f1f75cf9da045e6022b2f20ba5b9c.research_question: How can large language models be enhanced to understand and generate meaningful responses grounded in both visual and auditory content from videos, enabling comprehensive multi-modal video understanding and instruction following?
5d321194696f1f75cf9da045e6022b2f20ba5b9c.hypothesis: Integrating pre-trained visual and audio encoders with large language models, and aligning their outputs through cross-modal pre-training and instruction tuning, will enable the resulting model to effectively comprehend and generate responses based on both visual and auditory information in videos.
5d321194696f1f75cf9da045e6022b2f20ba5b9c.proposed_method: A multi-modal framework will be developed that combines frozen pre-trained visual and audio encoders with a frozen large language model (LLM). The architecture will include two main branches: a Vision-Language Branch and an Audio-Language Branch. The Vision-Language Branch will use a pre-trained image encoder (ViT-G/14 from EVA-CLIP) and a Video Q-Former to aggregate frame-level representations, inject temporal information via position embeddings, and project the output into the LLM's embedding space. The Audio-Language Branch will utilize a pre-trained audio encoder (ImageBind), process uniformly sampled audio segments into spectrograms, and use an Audio Q-Former to aggregate and align audio features with the LLM's embedding space. Both branches will be trained to align their outputs with the LLM through multi-branch cross-modal pre-training on large-scale video/image-caption datasets, followed by fine-tuning with high-quality visual-instruction datasets.
5d321194696f1f75cf9da045e6022b2f20ba5b9c.experiment_details: Experiments will involve pre-training the Vision-Language Branch on the Webvid-2M dataset (a large-scale video-caption dataset) and the CC595k image-caption dataset, using a video-to-text generation task. The Audio-Language Branch will be trained using visual-text data due to the scarcity of audio-text data, leveraging the shared embedding space of ImageBind. Fine-tuning will be performed on high-quality instruction-following datasets, including image-detail-description data from MiniGPT-4, image-instruction data from LLaVA, and video-instruction data from Video-Chat. Baselines for comparison will include existing multi-modal LLMs such as BLIP-2, MiniGPT-4, LLaVA, mPLUG-Owl, VideoChat, AudioGPT, and Video-ChatGPT. Evaluation metrics will include the model's ability to generate accurate and meaningful responses to questions grounded in both visual and auditory content, as well as its performance on instruction-following tasks.
5d321194696f1f75cf9da045e6022b2f20ba5b9c.novelty_claims: The proposed framework uniquely enables simultaneous comprehension of both visual and auditory information in videos within a single end-to-end model, unlike prior works that focus on either visual or auditory modalities alone. The method introduces a multi-branch cross-modal pre-training approach, leveraging Q-Former modules for both video and audio to align multi-modal features with the LLM's embedding space. The use of ImageBind as a universal audio encoder and the training strategy that utilizes visual-text data to bootstrap audio-language alignment are innovative, allowing for zero-shot audio understanding. The approach is designed to be efficient and extensible, with open-source code and model weights provided for reproducibility and further research.

5d49c7401c5f2337c4cc88d243ae39ed659afe64.title: Red Teaming Language Models with Language Models
5d49c7401c5f2337c4cc88d243ae39ed659afe64.research_question: How can automated methods be developed to efficiently and comprehensively identify harmful behaviors, failures, and undesirable outputs in large language models prior to deployment, across a wide range of failure modes including offensiveness, data leakage, personal information generation, and distributional bias?
5d49c7401c5f2337c4cc88d243ae39ed659afe64.hypothesis: Automated red teaming using language models to generate adversarial test cases, combined with classifier-based detection of harmful outputs, will uncover a broader and more diverse set of failures in target language models than manual red teaming alone, and can reveal specific, actionable failure modes across multiple harm categories.
5d49c7401c5f2337c4cc88d243ae39ed659afe64.proposed_method: A three-stage automated red teaming framework will be developed. First, a 'red team' language model (red LM) generates diverse, well-formed natural language test cases using several strategies: zero-shot prompting, stochastic few-shot prompting, supervised learning on previously discovered failing cases, and reinforcement learning to maximize the likelihood of eliciting harmful outputs. Second, each test case is submitted to the target language model, which generates a response. Third, a classifier (red team classifier) evaluates each (input, output) pair to detect harmful behaviors, such as offensiveness, data leakage, or personal information generation. Prompt engineering will be used to guide the red LM toward specific harm types or groups, and clustering and analysis of discovered failures will inform targeted improvements to the target model.
5d49c7401c5f2337c4cc88d243ae39ed659afe64.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a large-scale dialogue language model (e.g., Dialogue-Prompted Gopher, 280B parameters) as the target. The red LM will be instantiated with the same or similar architecture, and a classifier fine-tuned on relevant datasets (such as Bot-Adversarial Dialogue for offensiveness) will be used for harm detection. Multiple test case generation methods (zero-shot, few-shot, supervised, RL) will be compared in terms of their ability to elicit harmful outputs, measured by the percentage of offensive or otherwise harmful replies, and the diversity of test cases (using Self-BLEU and other metrics). Baselines will include manually-written adversarial datasets (e.g., BAD). Additional experiments will probe for data leakage (by searching for verbatim training data in outputs), personal information generation (using regexes for phone numbers, emails, etc.), and distributional bias (by generating group names and question templates, then evaluating groupwise harm rates).
5d49c7401c5f2337c4cc88d243ae39ed659afe64.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a fully automated, scalable red teaming framework that leverages language models themselves to generate adversarial test cases, eliminating reliance on costly and limited manual test case creation. The method supports multiple test case generation strategies, including reinforcement learning for targeted failure elicitation and prompt engineering for controllability across harm types. The framework enables comprehensive discovery of diverse and difficult failure modes, including those not anticipated by human annotators, and facilitates the automatic identification of distributional biases across demographic groups. This approach provides actionable insights for model improvement and complements existing manual red teaming and safety evaluation practices.

5d5812c5236c5fc576ba308dd9ccbd573f5dd7ef.title: Concurrent Training of a Control Policy and a State Estimator for Dynamic and Robust Legged Locomotion
5d5812c5236c5fc576ba308dd9ccbd573f5dd7ef.research_question: How can a control policy and a state estimator be concurrently trained to enable dynamic, robust, and high-speed legged locomotion across diverse and challenging terrains, including those with unreliable state estimation and slippery surfaces?
5d5812c5236c5fc576ba308dd9ccbd573f5dd7ef.hypothesis: Concurrent training of a control policy and a state estimator in a reinforcement learning framework will produce more robust, accurate, and adaptable legged locomotion compared to sequential or implicit estimation approaches, especially in environments with unreliable or noisy state information.
5d5812c5236c5fc576ba308dd9ccbd573f5dd7ef.proposed_method: A novel end-to-end locomotion learning framework will be developed in which a control policy (actor network) and a state estimator network are trained concurrently. The estimator network will predict key robot states such as base linear velocity, foot height, and contact probability using onboard proprioceptive sensors (IMU and joint encoders), and these estimates will be fed into the policy network. The policy network will output desired joint positions, which are then converted to torques via a PD controller. Training will be performed in a fast physics simulation environment (RaiSim) using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) for the actor and critic networks, and supervised learning for the estimator. Dynamics randomization will be employed to bridge the sim-to-real gap, including randomization of observation noise, motor frictions, PD gains, foot positions, collision geometry, and ground friction. The estimator and policy will be updated together in each training iteration, ensuring the policy adapts to the estimator's characteristics.
5d5812c5236c5fc576ba308dd9ccbd573f5dd7ef.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted both in simulation and on a real quadrupedal robot (Mini Cheetah). Training will utilize 800 randomized environments with varied initial states, terrain slopes, and surface frictions, using curriculum learning to gradually increase command difficulty. Baseline comparisons will include sequentially trained estimators, implicit (latent) estimators, built-in MPC controllers, and RL policies with analytical estimators (e.g., LKF). Evaluation metrics will include command tracking error, estimation error, maximum running speed, maximum traversable slope, and foot clearance, measured on normal and slippery terrains. Ablation studies will assess the impact of each estimated state (linear velocity, foot height, contact probability), and sim-to-real transfer will be validated by deploying the trained networks on the physical robot.
5d5812c5236c5fc576ba308dd9ccbd573f5dd7ef.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the concurrent training of a control policy and an explicit state estimator for legged locomotion, eliminating the need for advanced analytical state estimation or periodic gait assumptions. The method enables robust and dynamic locomotion on highly challenging terrains, including slippery surfaces with low friction coefficients, and achieves state-of-the-art running speeds for legged robots trained via reinforcement learning. The approach also provides interpretable state estimates that can be leveraged by other control modules, and demonstrates improved sim-to-real transfer through extensive dynamics randomization.

5d6be67b99390b879e1a518dc51993bfd6704dcb.title: Accelerating Convergence of Score-Based Diffusion Models, Provably
5d6be67b99390b879e1a518dc51993bfd6704dcb.research_question: Can training-free deterministic and stochastic samplers for score-based diffusion models be designed to achieve provably faster convergence rates than standard DDIM and DDPM approaches, without imposing restrictive assumptions on the target data distribution or requiring additional training?
5d6be67b99390b879e1a518dc51993bfd6704dcb.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by leveraging higher-order approximation techniques and momentum-inspired updates, training-free deterministic and stochastic samplers can be constructed that converge faster than traditional DDIM and DDPM samplers, even when only moderately accurate score estimates are available and without log-concavity or smoothness assumptions on the data distribution.
5d6be67b99390b879e1a518dc51993bfd6704dcb.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed for accelerating both deterministic (ODE-based) and stochastic (SDE-based) samplers in score-based diffusion models. For the deterministic case, the method introduces an accelerated update rule that incorporates a mid-point prediction and a momentum-like correction term, inspired by higher-order ODE solvers such as DPM-Solver-2. This approach computes an intermediate state at each step and adjusts the update using both current and previous score function evaluations, thereby achieving a higher-order approximation to the probability flow ODE. For the stochastic case, the method augments the standard DDPM update with an additional noise-injection step, generating an intermediate sample before applying the usual score-based update, which allows for improved convergence by better capturing the stochasticity of the reverse process. Both algorithms are designed to be training-free, requiring only pre-trained score functions and no additional model training.
5d6be67b99390b879e1a518dc51993bfd6704dcb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard benchmark datasets commonly used for evaluating diffusion models, such as CIFAR-10, CelebA, or ImageNet subsets. The proposed accelerated samplers will be compared against baseline methods including the original DDIM and DDPM samplers, as well as other state-of-the-art training-free solvers like DPM-Solver-2. Evaluation metrics will include total variation distance, Kullback-Leibler divergence, and sample quality measures such as FID (Fréchet Inception Distance). Experimental setups will vary the number of sampling steps T and the accuracy of score estimates to assess convergence rates and robustness, with ablation studies to isolate the impact of the higher-order and momentum terms.
5d6be67b99390b879e1a518dc51993bfd6704dcb.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first provably accelerated, training-free deterministic and stochastic samplers for score-based diffusion models, achieving improved convergence rates of O(1/T^2) for the deterministic case and O(1/T) for the stochastic case, surpassing the best-known rates for DDIM and DDPM. The methodology accommodates only ℓ2-accurate score estimates and does not require log-concavity or smoothness of the target distribution, broadening applicability. The approach leverages higher-order approximation and momentum-inspired updates in a discrete-time setting, providing theoretical guarantees and practical acceleration without additional training overhead.

5d6c53e6aa1579754d8938d5505cb6e229005be1.title: Statistical optimal transport
5d6c53e6aa1579754d8938d5505cb6e229005be1.research_question: How can statistical optimal transport be developed and analyzed to enable robust estimation, computation, and application of Wasserstein distances, transport maps, and gradient flows in statistical and machine learning contexts?
5d6c53e6aa1579754d8938d5505cb6e229005be1.hypothesis: Statistical optimal transport methods, leveraging recent advances in optimal transport theory and computational algorithms, can provide principled and efficient solutions for estimating distances and couplings between probability measures, even in challenging scenarios such as uncoupled data or high-dimensional settings.
5d6c53e6aa1579754d8938d5505cb6e229005be1.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed that integrates foundational optimal transport theory—including Wasserstein distances, duality, and transport maps—with statistical estimation techniques. The methodology will address the estimation of Wasserstein distances from empirical data, propose algorithms for recovering optimal transport maps (including in uncoupled or partially observed scenarios), and introduce entropic regularization to improve computational efficiency and statistical rates. The approach will also extend to the study of Wasserstein gradient flows, leveraging geometric and variational perspectives to design new algorithms for sampling, inference, and learning. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to establish statistical rates, optimality, and convergence properties under various assumptions on the data and underlying measures.
5d6c53e6aa1579754d8938d5505cb6e229005be1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets, including applications in single-cell genomics, image analysis, and machine learning benchmarks. Baselines will include classical statistical estimators, standard optimal transport solvers, and recent computational optimal transport algorithms such as the Sinkhorn algorithm. Evaluation metrics will focus on estimation error (e.g., Wasserstein distance between empirical and true measures), computational efficiency, and performance in downstream tasks such as regression, clustering, and generative modeling. Experimental setups will vary dimensionality, sample size, and regularization parameters to assess robustness and scalability.
5d6c53e6aa1579754d8938d5505cb6e229005be1.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified statistical perspective on optimal transport, bridging foundational theory with practical algorithms for estimation and inference. Key innovations include new statistical rates for Wasserstein distance estimation, principled treatment of uncoupled data scenarios, integration of entropic regularization for improved rates and tractability, and novel applications of Wasserstein gradient flows to variational inference, sampling, and neural network training. The geometric analysis of Wasserstein space and barycenters further extends the applicability of optimal transport to a wide range of statistical and machine learning problems.

5d6fdecd86a143ec117def6040e4cc37699e25c3.title: Spectral risk-based learning using unbounded losses
5d6fdecd86a143ec117def6040e4cc37699e25c3.research_question: How can learning algorithms be designed to optimize a broad class of spectral risk functions, particularly under unbounded and heavy-tailed loss distributions, while maintaining computational efficiency and strong generalization performance?
5d6fdecd86a143ec117def6040e4cc37699e25c3.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a derivative-free learning procedure, combined with stochastic smoothing and confidence boosting techniques, can provide formal excess risk guarantees and robust performance for spectral risk minimization under unbounded heavy-tailed losses. Furthermore, integrating approximate first-order information can accelerate convergence and improve empirical performance compared to traditional empirical risk minimizers.
5d6fdecd86a143ec117def6040e4cc37699e25c3.proposed_method: A novel learning framework is developed for optimizing spectral risk functions, where the risk is defined via a Lipschitz-continuous spectral density over the loss distribution. The approach employs a derivative-free stochastic mirror descent algorithm, utilizing a smoothed variant of the spectral risk obtained by random perturbations in the parameter space. At each iteration, empirical estimates of the loss distribution are used to construct unbiased estimators of the spectral risk, and updates are performed using Bregman divergence-based mirror descent. To enhance practical efficiency, a modified version incorporates parametric modeling (e.g., folded Normal distribution) of the loss CDF, enabling the use of approximate gradients via the chain rule and empirical moments. Additionally, a robust confidence-boosting technique is integrated to provide high-probability guarantees by generating multiple candidate solutions and selecting the best via robust M-estimation.
5d6fdecd86a143ec117def6040e4cc37699e25c3.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a suite of standard benchmark classification datasets, including Adult, CIFAR-10, Covtype, CodRNA, EMNIST Balanced, Fashion MNIST, MNIST, and Protein. Three methods are compared: the proposed derivative-free algorithm, the fast parametric-gradient variant, and traditional empirical risk minimization (ERM). Multi-class logistic regression is used as the base model, with fixed step sizes and projection onto a convex constraint set. Each method is run for 50 epochs with 10 random initializations per dataset, and performance is evaluated in terms of empirical spectral risk and misclassification error on both training and test splits. The exponential risk spectrum is used for the spectral density, and all code and data preprocessing pipelines are made available for reproducibility.
5d6fdecd86a143ec117def6040e4cc37699e25c3.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first derivative-free learning algorithm with formal excess spectral risk guarantees under unbounded and heavy-tailed loss distributions. The method generalizes beyond CVaR to arbitrary Lipschitz-continuous spectral densities, and provides both expectation and high-probability risk bounds. The integration of stochastic smoothing, empirical CDF estimation, and robust confidence boosting is novel in the context of spectral risk minimization. The fast implementation leveraging parametric CDF modeling and approximate gradients offers practical scalability and superior empirical performance, achieving a favorable balance between spectral risk and misclassification error compared to traditional ERM approaches.

5da5c2167a85ecb5d1ea22656ae36fdf995df0f2.title: Learning robust perceptive locomotion for quadrupedal robots in the wild
5da5c2167a85ecb5d1ea22656ae36fdf995df0f2.research_question: How can quadrupedal robots achieve robust and fast locomotion in challenging, unstructured environments by effectively integrating exteroceptive (e.g., vision, LiDAR) and proprioceptive sensing, especially when exteroceptive perception is unreliable or incomplete?
5da5c2167a85ecb5d1ea22656ae36fdf995df0f2.hypothesis: A locomotion controller that seamlessly integrates exteroceptive and proprioceptive inputs using a learned, attention-based recurrent encoder will enable quadrupedal robots to achieve both high robustness and speed in diverse and challenging real-world environments, outperforming controllers that rely solely on proprioception or hand-crafted heuristics.
5da5c2167a85ecb5d1ea22656ae36fdf995df0f2.proposed_method: A novel locomotion control framework will be developed that employs an attention-based recurrent encoder to fuse proprioceptive and exteroceptive sensor data into a unified belief state. The approach consists of a two-stage training process: first, a teacher policy is trained in simulation using reinforcement learning with privileged access to ground-truth terrain and robot state information, enabling discovery of optimal behaviors under perfect perception. Second, a student policy is trained via imitation learning to mimic the teacher, using only the noisy, partial observations available to the real robot, and is structured around the belief state encoder. The student policy is trained end-to-end to reconstruct the environment state and predict optimal actions, without reliance on hand-crafted rules or heuristics. The final policy is deployed zero-shot on real hardware, receiving onboard sensor observations (e.g., elevation maps from LiDAR or stereo cameras) and desired velocity commands, and outputs joint target positions for locomotion.
5da5c2167a85ecb5d1ea22656ae36fdf995df0f2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a physical quadrupedal robot (e.g., ANYmal) across a wide range of natural and urban environments, including alpine trails, forests, underground caves, and urban stairs, over multiple seasons and conditions (e.g., snow, mud, water, fog). The controller's performance will be compared against a proprioceptive-only baseline in terms of success rate, speed, and robustness on tasks such as step climbing, obstacle courses, and a 2.2 km mountain hike with 120 m elevation gain. Evaluation metrics will include completion time, number of falls or failures, maximum traversable obstacle height, and locomotion speed (forward, lateral, and turning velocities). The robustness of the controller will be further assessed under exteroceptive perception failures (e.g., sensor occlusion, reflective surfaces, soft obstacles) and by visualizing the internal belief state during ambiguous or misleading sensory input.
5da5c2167a85ecb5d1ea22656ae36fdf995df0f2.novelty_claims: The proposed approach constitutes the first general and robust framework for integrating exteroceptive and proprioceptive perception in legged robot locomotion, enabling seamless fallback to proprioceptive control when exteroception is unreliable. The method features end-to-end learning of multi-modal sensor fusion via a recurrent encoder, eliminating the need for hand-coded heuristics. Extensive real-world experiments demonstrate unprecedented robustness and speed, including successful completion of a difficult mountain hike and traversal of environments previously inaccessible to vision-based or proprioceptive-only controllers. The approach is sensor-agnostic, supporting both LiDAR and stereo cameras without retraining, and robustly handles a wide spectrum of perception failures.

5dbffedcabe3fa43060ebbe2b1789500edfd871f.title: Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model
5dbffedcabe3fa43060ebbe2b1789500edfd871f.research_question: How can large language models be enhanced to perform more effective and human-like reasoning and planning across diverse complex tasks, such as plan generation, mathematical reasoning, and logical inference?
5dbffedcabe3fa43060ebbe2b1789500edfd871f.hypothesis: Equipping large language models with an explicit internal world model and integrating principled planning algorithms will enable more strategic, coherent, and effective reasoning, surpassing current chain-of-thought and prompting-based methods.
5dbffedcabe3fa43060ebbe2b1789500edfd871f.proposed_method: A new framework, Reasoning via Planning (RAP), will be developed that repurposes a large language model (LLM) to serve both as a world model and a reasoning agent. The LLM will be prompted to simulate world state transitions and generate possible actions, effectively modeling reasoning as a Markov Decision Process. Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) will be incorporated to efficiently explore the reasoning space, balancing exploration and exploitation by maintaining a reasoning tree of state-action trajectories. At each node, the LLM will predict next states and actions, while a reward function—composed of action likelihood, state confidence, self-evaluation, and task-specific heuristics—will guide the search toward high-reward reasoning paths. The framework will also include an aggregation mechanism to ensemble multiple reasoning traces when only final answers are needed.
5dbffedcabe3fa43060ebbe2b1789500edfd871f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of challenging reasoning tasks, including plan generation in the Blocksworld environment, mathematical reasoning using the GSM8K dataset, and logical inference with the PrOntoQA benchmark. The proposed method will be compared against strong baselines such as Chain-of-Thought (CoT), least-to-most prompting, and their self-consistency variants, as well as advanced models like GPT-4 where feasible. Evaluation metrics will include success rate for plan generation, accuracy for math and logical reasoning, and proof correctness for logical inference. The experimental setup will use LLaMA-33B and Llama-2-70B as base LLMs, with prompts and reward functions tailored to each task domain. Multiple iterations of MCTS and aggregation strategies will be tested to assess robustness and performance gains.
5dbffedcabe3fa43060ebbe2b1789500edfd871f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled and unified framework that explicitly models world state and reward within LLM reasoning, enabling deliberate planning akin to human cognition. Unlike prior approaches, RAP integrates the LLM as both a world model and agent, and leverages advanced planning algorithms (MCTS) to systematically explore reasoning alternatives. The method generalizes across open-domain tasks, supports flexible reward design, and demonstrates substantial improvements over existing prompting-based and search-guided reasoning methods. RAP is claimed to achieve state-of-the-art results on several benchmarks, outperforming even more capable LLMs under traditional reasoning paradigms.

5dc4e5fd5c9b711efc1205cd3b13b23f5e792eee.title: A Singular Woodbury and Pseudo-Determinant Matrix Identities and Application to Gaussian Process Regression
5dc4e5fd5c9b711efc1205cd3b13b23f5e792eee.research_question: How can generalized matrix identities, specifically singular forms of the Woodbury matrix identity and pseudo-determinant identities, be developed and applied to improve the theoretical understanding and computational efficiency of Gaussian process regression, particularly in scenarios involving singular or rank-deficient matrices?
5dc4e5fd5c9b711efc1205cd3b13b23f5e792eee.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that new matrix identities for generalized inverses and pseudo-determinants can be derived for singular and rank-deficient cases, and that these identities will enable more efficient and theoretically robust formulations of likelihood functions and precision matrices in Gaussian process regression, preserving key statistical properties such as conditional independence.
5dc4e5fd5c9b711efc1205cd3b13b23f5e792eee.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed to generalize the Woodbury matrix identity and matrix determinant lemma to cases where one or more matrices are singular or rank-deficient. The approach will focus on deriving explicit forms for the generalized inverse (outer inverse) and pseudo-determinant of matrices of the form M = A† - A†X(Y* A† X)† Y* A†, where A, X, and Y may be rectangular and singular. The methodology will include establishing conditions under which the kernel and cokernel of M can be expressed in terms of X and Y, and will leverage properties of EP (equal-principal) matrices and the Bott-Duffin inverse. Theoretical results will be extended to the context of Gaussian process regression, where the new identities will be used to reformulate likelihood functions and define precision matrices in terms of the Bott-Duffin inverse, ensuring preservation of conditional independence and marginal/conditional precision properties.
5dc4e5fd5c9b711efc1205cd3b13b23f5e792eee.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic and real-world datasets relevant to Gaussian process regression. The proposed matrix identities and algorithms will be implemented in Python, leveraging or extending existing packages such as detkit and glearn. Baseline comparisons will include standard approaches to Gaussian process regression that utilize the classical Woodbury identity and determinant lemma, as well as conventional definitions of the precision matrix. Evaluation metrics will focus on computational efficiency (e.g., time and memory complexity for log-determinant and inverse computations), numerical stability, and the accuracy of likelihood and predictive inference. Special attention will be given to cases where covariance matrices are singular or nearly singular, and the empirical advantages of the new identities will be quantified under these conditions.
5dc4e5fd5c9b711efc1205cd3b13b23f5e792eee.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces new matrix identities for the generalized inverse and pseudo-determinant in the singular case, extending the Woodbury identity and determinant lemma to rank-deficient matrices. The framework provides a rigorous extension of the precision matrix concept via the Bott-Duffin inverse, ensuring that key statistical properties such as conditional independence and marginal/conditional precision are preserved even in singular scenarios. The approach also yields efficient algorithms for computing log-determinant terms in Gaussian process likelihoods, with demonstrated numerical advantages in challenging cases. These contributions advance both the theoretical foundations and practical computation in Gaussian process regression and related fields.

5e07d74ec8029fe5ff4045a904ffaecdd2024c66.title: Captured by Captions: On Memorization and its Mitigation in CLIP Models
5e07d74ec8029fe5ff4045a904ffaecdd2024c66.research_question: How does memorization manifest in multi-modal models such as CLIP, and what strategies can be developed to quantify and mitigate memorization while maintaining or improving generalization performance?
5e07d74ec8029fe5ff4045a904ffaecdd2024c66.hypothesis: Memorization in CLIP models is influenced by both the supervised (caption-based) and self-supervised (contrastive) learning components, with mis-captioned and atypical samples exhibiting higher memorization. Targeted mitigation strategies, particularly in the text modality, can reduce memorization without sacrificing—and potentially improving—generalization performance.
5e07d74ec8029fe5ff4045a904ffaecdd2024c66.proposed_method: A formal metric, CLIPMem, will be introduced to quantify memorization in multi-modal vision-language models by comparing the alignment (cosine similarity) of image-text pairs in a model trained with the pair versus a model trained without it (leave-one-out). This metric will jointly consider both image and text modalities, overcoming the limitations of existing uni-modal memorization metrics. The methodology involves training two CLIP models—one on the full dataset and one with specific pairs removed—and computing the difference in alignment scores for each pair. Additional mitigation strategies will be developed, including augmenting the text modality with multiple captions or generated captions, applying Gaussian noise to text embeddings during training, and removing highly memorized samples as identified by CLIPMem. The impact of these interventions on memorization and downstream utility will be systematically evaluated.
5e07d74ec8029fe5ff4045a904ffaecdd2024c66.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using OpenCLIP models (ViT-Base and ViT-Large architectures) trained on the COCO, CC3M, and YFCC100M datasets. Memorization will be measured using the proposed CLIPMem metric, with comparisons to SSLMem and other baselines. Evaluation will include linear probing accuracy on ImageNet, and the effect of various data augmentations (multiple captions, generated images, text embedding noise) will be assessed. Baselines will include random sample removal and removal based on CLIP similarity, with performance tracked as a function of the number and type of samples removed. Additional analyses will examine the distribution of memorization across modalities and network layers, and the relationship between memorization and generalization will be explored.
5e07d74ec8029fe5ff4045a904ffaecdd2024c66.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces CLIPMem, the first formal and practical metric for quantifying memorization in multi-modal models by leveraging both image and text modalities. It demonstrates that memorization in CLIP is primarily driven by the text encoder and that mitigation strategies targeting the text domain can reduce memorization while improving generalization—a result that contrasts with traditional supervised and self-supervised paradigms. The approach provides actionable insights for data curation and model training, especially in large-scale, uncurated datasets, and offers a new lens for understanding and controlling memorization in multi-modal representation learning.

5e112d07da6e6b13d1bd447e3151391aa6ffb810.title: CoDet: Co-Occurrence Guided Region-Word Alignment for Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
5e112d07da6e6b13d1bd447e3151391aa6ffb810.research_question: How can reliable region-word alignments be discovered from large-scale image-text pairs to enable open-vocabulary object detection without relying on pre-aligned vision-language models?
5e112d07da6e6b13d1bd447e3151391aa6ffb810.hypothesis: Region-word alignments for open-vocabulary object detection can be effectively discovered by leveraging co-occurrence of objects across groups of images sharing the same concept in their captions, and by guiding region-region similarity estimation with text embeddings, thus bypassing the limitations of pre-aligned vision-language models.
5e112d07da6e6b13d1bd447e3151391aa6ffb810.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a co-occurrence guided framework, CoDet, that reformulates region-word alignment as a co-occurring object discovery problem. For each concept extracted from image captions, a group of images mentioning the concept is formed, and region proposals are generated for each image. Cross-image region-region similarities are computed, with similarity estimation re-weighted by the text embedding of the shared concept to ensure concept-awareness. A prototype feature for the co-occurring object is constructed as a weighted sum of region features, where weights are learned via a two-layer MLP over the similarity matrix. The prototype and the shared concept label form a region-word pair, which is used to supervise the training of an open-vocabulary object detector. The framework is trained end-to-end, jointly optimizing for detection and vision-language alignment using both detection data and image-text pairs.
5e112d07da6e6b13d1bd447e3151391aa6ffb810.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on open-vocabulary detection benchmarks including OV-LVIS (based on LVIS dataset with 1203 categories) and OV-COCO (based on COCO with 65 categories). The method uses web-crawled image-text pairs from CC3M (2.8M pairs) and COCO Caption as sources of weak supervision. Baselines include state-of-the-art open-vocabulary detection methods such as ViLD, RegionCLIP, Detic, VLDet, and others, with comparisons made under strict open-vocabulary settings. Evaluation metrics include mask AP for novel, common, frequent, and all categories on OV-LVIS, and box AP for novel, base, and all categories on OV-COCO. The experimental setup involves co-training on detection and caption data, varying visual backbones (ResNet50, Swin-B, EVA02-L), and ablation studies on key components such as text guidance and prototype-based discovery. Cross-dataset transfer is also evaluated by testing detectors trained on OV-LVIS on COCO and Objects365 without further fine-tuning.
5e112d07da6e6b13d1bd447e3151391aa6ffb810.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to bypass reliance on pre-aligned vision-language models by reformulating region-word alignment as a co-occurring object discovery problem. It introduces a concept-aware, text-guided region-region similarity estimation and a prototype-based strategy for discovering co-occurring objects across images. The framework demonstrates superior performance and scalability over existing methods on multiple open-vocabulary detection benchmarks, and exhibits strong generalization in cross-dataset transfer. Ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of text guidance and prototype-based discovery in improving alignment quality and detection performance.

5e25c253b0c3fb159c9581131e22b6e9f615619c.title: Latent Action Pretraining from Videos
5e25c253b0c3fb159c9581131e22b6e9f615619c.research_question: How can generalist robotic foundation models be pretrained from large-scale, unlabeled video data—such as internet or human manipulation videos—without relying on ground-truth robot action labels, and how effective are such models in downstream robot manipulation tasks requiring language and visual understanding?
5e25c253b0c3fb159c9581131e22b6e9f615619c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a robotic foundation model pretrained in an unsupervised manner on large-scale video data, by learning a quantized latent action space without ground-truth action labels, can achieve superior or comparable performance to models pretrained with labeled actions, especially in terms of generalization across tasks, environments, and embodiments.
5e25c253b0c3fb159c9581131e22b6e9f615619c.proposed_method: The proposed approach consists of three stages: (1) Unsupervised Latent Action Quantization, where a VQ-VAE-based encoder-decoder model is trained to learn discrete latent actions from pairs of consecutive video frames, using a codebook and cross-attention mechanisms to maximize semantic alignment of latent actions with observed transitions. NSVQ and codebook replacement techniques are employed to ensure robust codebook utilization and prevent representation collapse. (2) Latent Pretraining, in which a Vision-Language Model (VLM) is trained via behavior cloning to predict the learned latent actions from video observations and paired task descriptions, using a dedicated latent action prediction head while freezing the vision encoder and updating the language model. (3) Action Finetuning, where the pretrained model is further finetuned on a small set of action-labeled robot trajectories to map latent actions to executable robot actions, replacing the latent action head with a new action head and discretizing the robot action space for balanced training. This pipeline enables leveraging any video-language data for pretraining, regardless of the presence of robot action labels.
5e25c253b0c3fb159c9581131e22b6e9f615619c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of simulation and real-world robot manipulation benchmarks, including Language Table (simulated 2-DOF block manipulation), SIMPLER (simulated 7-DOF arm tasks), and real-world tabletop manipulation with a Franka Emika Panda robot. Pretraining datasets will include large-scale robot datasets (Bridgev2, Open-X) and human manipulation videos (Something-Something V2), with fine-tuning performed on small, labeled robot datasets. Baselines for comparison will include models trained from scratch, models using video diffusion (UNIPI), inverse dynamics-based pseudo-labeling (VPT), and state-of-the-art VLA models pretrained with action labels (ACTIONVLA, OPENVLA). Evaluation metrics will include average task success rate, generalization to unseen objects/instructions, and pretraining efficiency (GPU hours). Experiments will systematically test cross-task, cross-environment, and cross-embodiment transfer, as well as scaling effects with respect to model size, data size, and latent action space.
5e25c253b0c3fb159c9581131e22b6e9f615619c.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first unsupervised pretraining approach for Vision-Language-Action models that does not require ground-truth robot action labels, enabling the use of internet-scale video data for robotics. It demonstrates that learning a quantized latent action space directly from observations allows for robust generalization across tasks, environments, and embodiments, outperforming existing methods—including those using labeled actions—on several real-world and simulated benchmarks. The method also shows strong positive transfer from human manipulation videos, indicating potential for leveraging web-scale data for robotics foundation models. Additionally, the approach achieves significantly higher pretraining efficiency (over 30x) compared to state-of-the-art supervised VLA models.

5e2aa82d847f94566c9d9920edf3279fbd715c61.title: No-Regret Learning in Bilateral Trade via Global Budget Balance
5e2aa82d847f94566c9d9920edf3279fbd715c61.research_question: Can sublinear regret be achieved in the repeated bilateral trade problem under a realistic and relaxed notion of budget balance, specifically global budget balance, when the sequence of seller and buyer valuations is generated adversarially and only limited feedback is available?
5e2aa82d847f94566c9d9920edf3279fbd715c61.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by relaxing the budget balance constraint from per-round to global budget balance, it is possible to design online learning algorithms that achieve sublinear regret against the best fixed price in hindsight, even in adversarial settings and under various feedback models.
5e2aa82d847f94566c9d9920edf3279fbd715c61.proposed_method: A novel online learning framework is proposed for repeated bilateral trade, where at each time step, a learner posts prices to a newly arriving seller and buyer pair, without knowledge of their private valuations. The learner must ensure global budget balance, meaning the cumulative profit over the entire time horizon is non-negative, rather than enforcing budget balance at each round. The core methodology involves a two-phase meta-algorithm: the first phase focuses on maximizing profit using a carefully constructed multiplicative grid of candidate price pairs to accumulate budget, while the second phase reinvests this budget to maximize gain from trade using an additive grid of non-budget-balanced price pairs. The approach adapts to different feedback models (full, one-bit, and two-bit), and in the partial feedback settings, a specialized estimation technique is developed to infer gain from trade from minimal feedback. Discretization strategies for the continuous, bidimensional price space are designed to ensure that the regret with respect to the best fixed price is minimized up to poly-logarithmic factors.
5e2aa82d847f94566c9d9920edf3279fbd715c61.experiment_details: The experimental evaluation will be conducted in a simulated online setting where, at each round, adversarially chosen seller and buyer valuations are presented. The learner interacts with the environment under three feedback models: full feedback (where both valuations are revealed), two-bit feedback (where acceptance or rejection by each agent is revealed), and one-bit feedback (where only whether a trade occurred is revealed). The performance of the proposed algorithms will be measured by the regret with respect to the best fixed price in hindsight, as well as against a stronger benchmark: the best fixed feasible distribution over prices. Lower bounds will be established for each feedback model to demonstrate the optimality or limitations of the proposed algorithms. Comparisons will be made to existing baselines from the literature on bilateral trade and online learning with budget constraints.
5e2aa82d847f94566c9d9920edf3279fbd715c61.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the concept of global budget balance to the repeated bilateral trade problem, enabling the first no-regret algorithms in adversarial settings where previous impossibility results held under per-round budget balance. The two-phase learning approach, with tailored discretization of the price space and feedback-specific estimation techniques, provides optimal or near-optimal regret bounds under full and partial feedback. The work also establishes a new, stronger benchmark based on the best feasible distribution over prices, inspired by bandits with knapsacks, and proves tight lower and upper bounds for regret in this setting. The separation of regret rates between feedback models and the demonstration of a tight multiplicative gap between benchmarks further highlight the theoretical contributions.

5e2bceb56f116e98baf7e418208057bc0e1c1861.title: ConceptFusion: Open-set Multimodal 3D Mapping
5e2bceb56f116e98baf7e418208057bc0e1c1861.research_question: How can a 3D mapping system be developed that enables open-set, multimodal semantic querying and spatial reasoning, supporting diverse query modalities such as text, images, audio, and clicks, and functioning effectively in zero-shot scenarios and real-world robotic tasks?
5e2bceb56f116e98baf7e418208057bc0e1c1861.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that fusing pixel-aligned features derived from large-scale foundation models (e.g., CLIP, DINO, AudioCLIP) into 3D maps using dense SLAM and multi-view fusion techniques will enable open-set, multimodal 3D mapping. Such a system will support zero-shot semantic and spatial reasoning, outperforming supervised or finetuned counterparts, especially for long-tailed and fine-grained concepts.
5e2bceb56f116e98baf7e418208057bc0e1c1861.proposed_method: The proposed method constructs open-set, multimodal 3D maps by fusing pixel-aligned features from foundation models into a dense 3D representation during online mapping. Input RGB(-D) images are processed to generate class-agnostic object masks using universal segmentation models (e.g., SAM, Mask2Former). For each region, both global (image-level) and local (region-level) feature vectors are extracted using foundation models such as CLIP, DINO, or AudioCLIP. These features are fused into pixel-aligned embeddings by weighting local and global features based on their similarity, and then mapped to 3D points using camera pose and depth information. The resulting 3D map stores, for each point, a fused concept vector, enabling open-ended querying via cosine similarity in the shared embedding space. The system supports queries in multiple modalities (text, image, audio, click) and enables spatial reasoning by composing feature similarities and 3D spatial comparators (e.g., distance, relative position, support, containment).
5e2bceb56f116e98baf7e418208057bc0e1c1861.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of real-world and simulated datasets, including the newly introduced UnCoCo dataset (comprising 3D scans of 78 household/office objects with over 500,000 queries across modalities), ScanNet, Replica, SemanticKITTI, and AI2-THOR. Baselines will include state-of-the-art supervised and zero-shot pixel-aligned models (LSeg, OpenSeg, MaskCLIP), with features fused into 3D maps for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics will include 3D mean intersection-over-union (mIoU), detection accuracy at various IoU thresholds, and success rates on spatial reasoning tasks. Experimental setups will encompass zero-shot tabletop rearrangement with a robotic arm, open-set autonomous navigation with a self-driving platform, and integration with large language model-based planners. Ablations will assess the impact of feature fusion strategies, segmentation models, and 3D versus 2.5D reasoning.
5e2bceb56f116e98baf7e418208057bc0e1c1861.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a fundamentally open-set, multimodal 3D mapping framework that enables zero-shot semantic and spatial reasoning across diverse modalities without additional training or finetuning. A novel mechanism is developed to compute pixel-aligned features from foundation models that otherwise provide only global image-level embeddings, preserving long-tailed and fine-grained concepts. The method supports arbitrary queries in text, image, audio, and click modalities, and enables complex 3D spatial reasoning not possible with prior closed-set or 2D-centric approaches. The proposal also includes the creation of the UnCoCo dataset, the first to support large-scale multimodal 3D query evaluation. Extensive experiments demonstrate significant improvements over supervised and zero-shot baselines, particularly in open-set and long-tailed scenarios.

5e3daa74acefb695dab1d74561de67a5f2a873f1.title: Non-Exchangeable Conformal Risk Control
5e3daa74acefb695dab1d74561de67a5f2a873f1.research_question: How can conformal risk control be extended to provide formal guarantees on the expected value of arbitrary monotone loss functions in settings where the data is not exchangeable, such as in the presence of distribution drift, change points, or other real-world non-i.i.d. scenarios?
5e3daa74acefb695dab1d74561de67a5f2a873f1.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a flexible conformal risk control framework can be developed to control the expected value of any monotone loss function for non-exchangeable data by appropriately weighting calibration data based on its relevance to the test example, resulting in tighter risk bounds and improved performance in non-exchangeable settings.
5e3daa74acefb695dab1d74561de67a5f2a873f1.proposed_method: A new framework for non-exchangeable conformal risk control will be developed, combining the principles of non-exchangeable conformal prediction with conformal risk control. The method will introduce a weighted empirical risk minimization procedure, where calibration points are assigned weights reflecting their relevance to the test example. The expected risk for a new test point will be bounded by a target risk level plus a term dependent on the weights and the total variation distance between the calibration and test distributions. The procedure will include a principled approach for choosing weights, such as maximum entropy regularization or similarity-based heuristics, to balance coverage gap minimization and calibration data utilization. The method will be applicable to any bounded, monotone loss function and will provide formal guarantees even when data is not exchangeable.
5e3daa74acefb695dab1d74561de67a5f2a873f1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. For synthetic data, a multilabel classification task will be constructed with scenarios including i.i.d. data, changepoints, and distribution drift, using logistic regression models and minimizing the false negative rate as the loss. Real-world experiments will include the ELEC2 electricity usage dataset, using least squares regression and the λ-insensitive absolute loss, and the Natural Questions open-domain QA dataset, controlling the best token-level F1-score. Baselines will include standard conformal risk control (CRC) under exchangeability assumptions. Evaluation metrics will focus on the achieved risk (expected loss), prediction set sizes, and coverage relative to the predefined risk threshold. The impact of different weighting strategies and the ability to maintain risk control under non-exchangeable conditions will be systematically assessed.
5e3daa74acefb695dab1d74561de67a5f2a873f1.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to provide formal risk control guarantees for arbitrary monotone loss functions in non-exchangeable data settings, generalizing both non-exchangeable conformal prediction and conformal risk control. The method allows for flexible, data-dependent weighting of calibration points, resulting in tighter risk bounds and improved adaptation to distribution shifts, changepoints, and other forms of non-i.i.d. data. The approach is broadly applicable, requires minimal assumptions, and demonstrates superior empirical performance in both synthetic and real-world tasks compared to existing methods.

5e4125b3a2ec91e866d970498f8a138c5a5cc89b.title: When Do Neural Nets Outperform Boosted Trees on Tabular Data?
5e4125b3a2ec91e866d970498f8a138c5a5cc89b.research_question: Under what conditions do neural networks outperform gradient-boosted decision trees (GBDTs) on tabular data, and what dataset properties are predictive of the relative performance of these algorithm families?
5e4125b3a2ec91e866d970498f8a138c5a5cc89b.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the relative performance of neural networks and GBDTs on tabular data is strongly influenced by specific dataset characteristics, such as size, feature distribution irregularity, and class imbalance, and that algorithm selection may be less important than hyperparameter tuning for many datasets.
5e4125b3a2ec91e866d970498f8a138c5a5cc89b.proposed_method: A large-scale empirical study will be conducted, systematically comparing the performance of 19 diverse algorithms—including multiple GBDTs, neural networks, and baseline methods—across 176 tabular classification datasets. Each algorithm will be evaluated with up to 30 hyperparameter configurations per dataset, using random search optimization. For each dataset, 10-fold cross-validation will be employed, with separate validation splits for hyperparameter tuning. Additionally, a comprehensive set of dataset metafeatures (over 900, including statistical, information-theoretic, landmarking, and model-based features) will be extracted using automated tools. Correlation and meta-learning analyses will be performed to identify which dataset properties are predictive of algorithm performance differences.
5e4125b3a2ec91e866d970498f8a138c5a5cc89b.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize 176 tabular classification datasets sourced from OpenML, including the CC-18 and OpenML Benchmarking Suite, covering a wide range of sizes and feature types. Algorithms to be compared include CatBoost, LightGBM, XGBoost (GBDTs), multiple neural network architectures (e.g., ResNet, FT-Transformer, TabNet, TabPFN), and standard baselines (e.g., logistic regression, SVM, random forest).
