Each algorithm will be trained and evaluated using up to 30 hyperparameter settings per dataset, with a maximum training time of 10 hours per dataset and 2 hours per train/eval cycle, on a standardized hardware setup (32GiB V100 GPU). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, log loss, F1-score, and ROC-AUC, with primary focus on accuracy and log loss. Statistical significance of performance differences will be assessed using Friedman and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm-Bonferroni correction. Meta-feature correlations and meta-learning models will be used to predict which algorithms are likely to perform best on new datasets.
5e4125b3a2ec91e866d970498f8a138c5a5cc89b.novelty_claims: The proposed study represents the largest systematic comparison of neural networks and GBDTs on tabular data to date, both in terms of the number of algorithms and datasets evaluated. The methodology uniquely combines large-scale hyperparameter optimization, extensive meta-feature analysis, and rigorous statistical testing. The research will provide actionable guidelines for practitioners regarding algorithm selection and tuning, and will release the TabZilla Benchmark Suite—a curated set of the most challenging tabular datasets—along with open-source code and all experimental results, thereby enabling reproducible and accelerated research in tabular data machine learning.

5e660a9af1687603977578ac0538dd2b0e601a54.title: Optimal Transport Tools (OTT): A JAX Toolbox for all things Wasserstein
5e660a9af1687603977578ac0538dd2b0e601a54.research_question: How can a comprehensive, efficient, and differentiable computational toolbox be developed for solving a wide range of optimal transport problems, including both classical and advanced Wasserstein-related tasks, in a scalable and flexible manner?
5e660a9af1687603977578ac0538dd2b0e601a54.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging modern automatic differentiation frameworks, such as JAX, in combination with entropic regularization and low-rank approximations, enables the development of a scalable, extensible, and differentiable toolbox that can efficiently solve linear and quadratic optimal transport problems, compute barycenters, and handle advanced extensions such as Gromov-Wasserstein distances and Gaussian mixture models.
5e660a9af1687603977578ac0538dd2b0e601a54.proposed_method: A Python toolbox will be implemented using the JAX framework to provide efficient, scalable, and differentiable solutions for optimal transport (OT) problems. The toolbox will include core modules for defining OT problems (linear, quadratic, and fused), geometry abstractions to handle cost matrices implicitly, and solvers based on entropic regularization (Sinkhorn algorithm) and low-rank approximations for scalability. Advanced modules will support Gromov-Wasserstein problems, computation of regularized barycenters, differentiable sorting and ranking, and Wasserstein-type distances between Gaussian mixtures. The toolbox will exploit JAX features such as automatic differentiation, vectorization, just-in-time compilation, and hardware acceleration to enable large-scale and differentiable OT computations.
5e660a9af1687603977578ac0538dd2b0e601a54.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of datasets and problem settings to demonstrate the capabilities of the toolbox. Example applications include computing regularized Wasserstein barycenters on neuroimaging data (e.g., Voxel-Based Morphometry on the Oasis dataset), solving Gromov-Wasserstein problems for shape matching between point clouds of different dimensions (such as 2D spirals and 3D Swiss rolls), and differentiable sorting tasks. Baseline comparisons will include classical network-flow solvers and standard OT algorithms. Evaluation metrics will include computational efficiency (runtime, memory usage), scalability to large datasets, accuracy of transport plans, and differentiability properties (e.g., gradient quality). The toolbox will be validated through Jupyter Notebooks and Colab notebooks to ensure reproducibility and accessibility.
5e660a9af1687603977578ac0538dd2b0e601a54.novelty_claims: The proposed toolbox introduces a unified, extensible, and differentiable framework for a broad spectrum of optimal transport problems, leveraging JAX for high-performance and hardware-accelerated computations. It supports both classical and advanced OT tasks, including entropic and low-rank Sinkhorn solvers, Gromov-Wasserstein distances, barycenters, differentiable sorting, and Wasserstein distances between Gaussian mixtures. The modular design enables seamless integration of new algorithms and problem types, while the use of implicit geometry representations and low-rank methods addresses scalability and memory challenges. The toolbox also provides differentiable solutions for OT problems, facilitating its use in modern machine learning pipelines.

5e722562c18b6168923fcf9eb414acb8bfbb0bad.title: The Manifold Scattering Transform for High-Dimensional Point Cloud Data
5e722562c18b6168923fcf9eb414acb8bfbb0bad.research_question: How can deep feature extraction methods be effectively extended to high-dimensional point cloud data modeled as lying on low-dimensional Riemannian manifolds, particularly in settings where the manifold structure is not explicitly known and the data does not come with a predefined mesh or graph structure?
5e722562c18b6168923fcf9eb414acb8bfbb0bad.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a numerically efficient manifold scattering transform, implemented via diffusion maps and discrete approximations of the Laplace-Beltrami operator, can extract geometrically informative features from high-dimensional point cloud data, enabling effective signal and manifold classification even when the underlying manifold is not explicitly known or meshed.
5e722562c18b6168923fcf9eb414acb8bfbb0bad.proposed_method: The proposed method develops a manifold scattering transform for high-dimensional point cloud data by constructing a weighted graph from the data using affinity kernels inspired by diffusion maps. The spectral geometry of this graph is designed to approximate that of the underlying manifold. Discrete approximations of the heat semigroup are implemented either via eigendecomposition of the graph Laplacian or via matrix multiplication using Markov-normalized graph Laplacians, thus avoiding the need for explicit eigenvector computation in large datasets. Wavelet transforms are defined using these heat operators, and scattering moments (zeroth, first, and second order) are computed using pointwise nonlinearities (e.g., absolute value) followed by integration over the manifold. The resulting features are used for downstream classification tasks, with the approach supporting both signal and manifold-level embeddings.
5e722562c18b6168923fcf9eb414acb8bfbb0bad.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic experiments include mesh-based and mesh-free approaches on two-dimensional surfaces such as spherical MNIST and the FAUST human shape dataset, comparing classification accuracy with and without meshes. Real-world experiments focus on high-dimensional biomedical data, such as single-cell protein expression measurements from melanoma and COVID-19 patients, where each patient’s data is modeled as a point cloud in high-dimensional space. Baseline comparisons include K-means clustering and standard graph-based methods. Evaluation metrics include classification accuracy for both signal and manifold classification tasks. Experimental setups involve varying the number of eigenvectors, the order of scattering moments, and the use of PCA for dimensionality reduction, with classifiers such as SVMs and decision trees.
5e722562c18b6168923fcf9eb414acb8bfbb0bad.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is among the first to provide practical and scalable numerical schemes for implementing the manifold scattering transform on high-dimensional point clouds without requiring explicit knowledge of the manifold, a mesh, or a predefined graph structure. It introduces computationally efficient wavelet constructions that avoid expensive eigendecomposition, supports higher-order scattering moments for improved discriminative power, and extends spectral manifold neural network techniques beyond two-dimensional surfaces to general manifolds. The method demonstrates effectiveness in both synthetic and real-world high-dimensional biomedical applications, offering a blueprint for adapting spectral networks to complex, unstructured data domains.

5e7a795d89910634f001cc3a631023f1dd4e2e23.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
5e7a795d89910634f001cc3a631023f1dd4e2e23.research_question: How can neural architectures be designed to effectively and efficiently incorporate both short-term and long-term memory mechanisms for improved sequence modeling, generalization, and scalability to very long contexts across diverse tasks?
5e7a795d89910634f001cc3a631023f1dd4e2e23.hypothesis: Integrating a neural long-term memory module that learns to memorize and manage information at test time, alongside attention-based short-term memory and persistent memory, will enable deep learning models to outperform standard Transformers and modern recurrent models, especially in tasks requiring long-context reasoning and recall.
5e7a795d89910634f001cc3a631023f1dd4e2e23.proposed_method: A novel neural long-term memory module is developed, inspired by human memory systems, which learns to memorize historical context at test time using a meta-learning approach. The memory update is governed by a surprise metric, computed as the gradient of an associative memory loss with respect to the input, and incorporates both momentum and adaptive forgetting mechanisms to manage memory capacity. The memory module is implemented as a deep MLP (multi-layer perceptron) and is trained in parallel using chunked mini-batch gradient descent reformulated via matrix multiplications for hardware efficiency. Three architectural variants are proposed: (1) Memory as Context, where long-term and persistent memory outputs are concatenated with the input and fed to an attention module; (2) Gated Memory, where outputs from sliding window attention and the memory module are combined via a gating mechanism; and (3) Memory as a Layer, where the memory module is inserted as a layer before attention. Persistent memory is incorporated as learnable, data-independent parameters prepended to the input sequence to encode task knowledge.
5e7a795d89910634f001cc3a631023f1dd4e2e23.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a diverse set of benchmarks, including language modeling, common-sense reasoning, recall-intensive 'needle-in-haystack' tasks, time series forecasting, and genomics (DNA modeling). The proposed architectures are evaluated against standard Transformers (with both limited and full context windows) and recent state-of-the-art linear recurrent models and their hybrid variants. Evaluation metrics include accuracy, recall, and the ability to scale to large context window sizes (up to and beyond 2 million tokens). Experimental setups involve varying the depth of the memory module, context window sizes, and the use of different memory incorporation strategies to assess trade-offs between efficiency and effectiveness.
5e7a795d89910634f001cc3a631023f1dd4e2e23.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a neural long-term memory module that learns to memorize at test time, using a surprise-based meta-learning update with adaptive forgetting, which is distinct from existing recurrent and attention-based models. The approach enables fast, parallelizable training and inference, and supports scaling to extremely long context windows. The Titans family of architectures systematically integrates short-term, long-term, and persistent memory modules, offering new ways to combine memory mechanisms in deep learning. Empirical results demonstrate superior performance over both Transformers and modern linear recurrent models across a wide range of tasks, particularly in long-context and recall-intensive scenarios.

5e855f449f6813762e5a3514158c38db6886fe59.title: On Training Implicit Models
5e855f449f6813762e5a3514158c38db6886fe59.research_question: Can implicit models, which are defined by infinite-layer dynamics and typically require expensive exact gradient computation for training, be efficiently and effectively trained using approximate gradient estimators that reduce computational cost while maintaining or improving performance?
5e855f449f6813762e5a3514158c38db6886fe59.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that an approximate, well-conditioned gradient estimator can provide a valid ascent direction for optimizing implicit models, enabling faster training with comparable or superior performance to exact gradient-based methods.
5e855f449f6813762e5a3514158c38db6886fe59.proposed_method: A novel gradient estimation framework, termed the phantom gradient, will be developed for training implicit models. This method replaces the costly Jacobian-inverse term in standard implicit differentiation with a more computationally efficient approximation. Two concrete instantiations of the phantom gradient will be explored: (1) an unrolling-based phantom gradient (UPG) that differentiates through a finite number of damped fixed-point iterations, and (2) a Neumann-series-based phantom gradient (NPG) that approximates the Jacobian-inverse using a truncated Neumann series. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to establish sufficient conditions under which the phantom gradient provides a valid ascent direction and ensures convergence. Hyperparameters such as the number of steps (k) and the damping factor (λ) will be studied to balance precision and conditioning of the gradient estimator.
5e855f449f6813762e5a3514158c38db6886fe59.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of tasks and datasets, including image classification on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, language modeling on Wikitext-103, and graph classification on COX2, PROTEINS, and node classification on PPI. The proposed phantom gradient methods (UPG and NPG) will be compared against standard implicit differentiation baselines using state-of-the-art implicit models such as MDEQ and IGNN. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy for vision and graph tasks, perplexity for language modeling, and computational efficiency measured by training time and memory usage. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of hyperparameters, pretraining, and regularization techniques. Additional analyses will examine the cosine similarity between phantom and exact gradients, as well as the stability and conditioning of the training process.
5e855f449f6813762e5a3514158c38db6886fe59.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretically grounded and practically efficient gradient estimation technique for implicit models, significantly reducing the computational burden of backward passes. The phantom gradient framework provides a general condition for valid optimization and offers two practical instantiations that can be tuned for precision and stability. The method is claimed to accelerate training by 1.4–1.7× on large-scale tasks, with backward pass speedups up to 12×, while achieving performance that matches or exceeds that of exact gradient-based approaches. The approach also enables adaptive switching between pretraining and regular training phases, potentially eliminating the need for explicit pretraining schedules.

5ea64e7233c502f07d15300c7059c569dfc9a4dd.title: Benign Overfitting in Two-layer ReLU Convolutional Neural Networks
5ea64e7233c502f07d15300c7059c569dfc9a4dd.research_question: How and under what conditions does benign overfitting occur in two-layer ReLU convolutional neural networks, particularly in the presence of label-flipping noise?
5ea64e7233c502f07d15300c7059c569dfc9a4dd.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, under certain conditions on the data distribution, sample size, and signal-to-noise ratio, two-layer ReLU convolutional neural networks trained by gradient descent can interpolate noisy training data and still achieve near-optimal test error, exhibiting a sharp transition between benign and harmful overfitting.
5ea64e7233c502f07d15300c7059c569dfc9a4dd.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the learning dynamics of two-layer convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with ReLU activation functions trained by gradient descent on data containing both label-dependent signals and label-independent Gaussian noise, with additional label-flipping noise. The method will generalize the signal-noise decomposition technique to the non-smooth ReLU setting, introducing a time-invariant coefficient ratio analysis to characterize the evolution of signal and noise memorization during training. The approach will also employ an automatic balance of coefficient updates to handle the effects of label-flipping noise, ensuring that the learning process can still focus on the true signal. Algorithm-dependent risk bounds will be established to precisely characterize the conditions under which benign overfitting occurs, including the derivation of phase transition thresholds for test error based on the signal-to-noise ratio and sample complexity.
5ea64e7233c502f07d15300c7059c569dfc9a4dd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic datasets generated according to the specified data model, where each input consists of a mixture of signal and Gaussian noise, and labels are subject to random flipping with a fixed probability. The two-layer ReLU CNN will be trained using full-batch gradient descent with varying dimensions, signal strengths, and fixed label noise rates. The experimental setup will include systematic variation of the signal norm and input dimension to empirically observe the phase transition in test error predicted by the theory. Evaluation metrics will include training loss, test loss, and test error, with additional analysis of margin dynamics and coefficient evolution during training. Baselines will include the Bayes optimal classifier and previous theoretical thresholds for benign overfitting in related models.
5ea64e7233c502f07d15300c7059c569dfc9a4dd.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a rigorous theoretical analysis of benign overfitting in two-layer ReLU CNNs beyond the neural tangent kernel regime, addressing the non-smoothness of the ReLU activation and the presence of label-flipping noise. Key innovations include the development of a time-invariant coefficient ratio technique for signal-noise decomposition, an automatic balancing mechanism for coefficient updates under label noise, and algorithm-dependent risk bounds that reveal a sharp phase transition between benign and harmful overfitting. The framework removes restrictive assumptions from prior work, such as orthogonality between signal and noise or smooth activation functions, and provides new insights into the generalization behavior of over-parameterized neural networks in realistic noisy settings.

5ea9ce852b5b870f50ea5b6d371ded9426ea2d74.title: Mitigating the Impact of Outlier Channels for Language Model Quantization with Activation Regularization
5ea9ce852b5b870f50ea5b6d371ded9426ea2d74.research_question: How can the impact of outlier channels on low-bitwidth quantization of language models be mitigated to enable accurate and efficient 4-bit quantization of both weights and activations, while maintaining competitive performance with standard-precision models?
5ea9ce852b5b870f50ea5b6d371ded9426ea2d74.hypothesis: Simultaneously regularizing input activations using quantization-aware training with learned clipping values and output activations via kurtosis regularization will prevent the migration of quantization difficulty to the weights, thereby enabling accurate 4-bit quantization of both weights and activations in language models without significant performance degradation.
5ea9ce852b5b870f50ea5b6d371ded9426ea2d74.proposed_method: A novel quantization-aware training (QAT) framework will be developed for large language models, where input activations to linear layers are quantized during training using learnable clipping values. The clipping thresholds for each activation layer will be treated as trainable parameters and optimized via gradient descent, employing a straight-through estimator for the backward pass. In addition, the kurtosis of each layer's output activation distribution will be regularized by adding a kurtosis penalty term to the loss function, discouraging heavy-tailed (outlier-prone) output distributions. After training, post-training quantization (PTQ) will be applied to the weights using both round-to-nearest (RTN) and data-driven methods such as GPTQ, to achieve 4-bit quantization for both weights and activations (W4A4). This approach aims to prevent the migration of outlier effects from activations to weights and ensure that both can be quantized efficiently.
5ea9ce852b5b870f50ea5b6d371ded9426ea2d74.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on language models with up to 1 billion parameters, trained on large-scale datasets such as SlimPajama (20-50 billion tokens). Models will be evaluated on standard language modeling benchmarks including C4 and PTB, with perplexity as the primary metric. Downstream task performance will be assessed on datasets such as HellaSwag, PIQA, and ARC-easy. Baselines will include standard-precision models (W16A16), activation clamping with static clipping, kurtosis regularization alone, QAT alone, and state-of-the-art PTQ methods such as OmniQuant. Both RTN and GPTQ will be used for post-training weight quantization. Hyperparameters such as batch size, learning rate, and regularization strength will be tuned, and throughput will be measured on modern GPU hardware. Ablation studies will isolate the effects of each component (QAT, kurtosis regularization) and compare against direct weight regularization approaches.
5ea9ce852b5b870f50ea5b6d371ded9426ea2d74.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a combined activation regularization strategy that applies QAT with learned clipping values to inputs and kurtosis regularization to outputs, specifically targeting the mitigation of outlier channels in language models. This dual regularization prevents the migration of quantization difficulty from activations to weights, enabling effective W4A4 quantization with minimal performance loss. The method demonstrates, for the first time, that 4-bit integer quantization of both weights and activations can achieve perplexity and downstream performance competitive with standard-precision baselines at moderate model scales. The use of kurtosis regularization on output activations, rather than directly on weights, is a novel contribution that addresses the limitations of direct weight regularization and enhances quantization robustness.

5eac2a40422a7085cb6f03285ad08210b6f6744b.title: OpenCodeInterpreter: Integrating Code Generation with Execution and Refinement
5eac2a40422a7085cb6f03285ad08210b6f6744b.research_question: How can open-source code generation models be enhanced to support dynamic code execution and iterative refinement, thereby narrowing the performance gap with proprietary systems such as GPT-4 Code Interpreter?
5eac2a40422a7085cb6f03285ad08210b6f6744b.hypothesis: Integrating execution feedback and human-like feedback into the training and inference process of open-source code generation models will significantly improve their ability to generate, debug, and iteratively refine code, achieving performance comparable to leading proprietary systems.
5eac2a40422a7085cb6f03285ad08210b6f6744b.proposed_method: A new family of open-source code generation systems, termed OpenCodeInterpreter, will be developed to tightly integrate code generation, execution, and iterative refinement. The approach involves training large language models on a newly constructed Code-Feedback dataset, which contains 68,000 multi-turn interactions featuring both execution feedback (e.g., compiler diagnostics, runtime outputs) and human feedback (e.g., follow-up instructions, clarifications). The dataset will be assembled from a diverse pool of real-world coding queries, open-source instruction datasets, and curated LeetCode challenges, and will be augmented with simulated multi-turn dialogues and error correction scenarios. During inference, the model will be capable of executing generated code, analyzing the results, and refining its outputs in response to both automated and human-like feedback, mimicking the workflow of advanced proprietary code interpreters.
5eac2a40422a7085cb6f03285ad08210b6f6744b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using several model backbones (e.g., CodeLlama, DeepSeekCoder) at various parameter scales (7B, 13B, 34B, 70B), all fine-tuned on the Code-Feedback dataset with a blend of high-quality single-turn data (e.g., WizardCoder 110k) at optimized ratios. Evaluation will be performed on standard code generation benchmarks such as HumanEval and MBPP, as well as their augmented versions (HumanEval+ and MBPP+) using the EvalPlus framework for comprehensive coverage of edge cases. Both single-turn and multi-turn (iterative refinement) scenarios will be tested, with baselines including GPT-3.5/4-Turbo, GeminiPro, and other leading open-source models. Metrics will include pass@1 accuracy and multi-turn pass rates, with additional analysis on error correction and feedback-driven refinement. Ablation studies will assess the impact of different data sources and feedback mechanisms.
5eac2a40422a7085cb6f03285ad08210b6f6744b.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first open-source code generation framework that integrates both code execution and iterative refinement using a large-scale multi-turn dataset with execution and human feedback. The Code-Feedback dataset is uniquely constructed to simulate realistic developer interactions, including error correction and follow-up guidance. The approach enables open-source models to achieve performance on par with proprietary systems like GPT-4 Code Interpreter, especially in multi-turn, feedback-driven scenarios. The methodology also demonstrates the effectiveness of combining high-quality single-turn data with diverse multi-turn feedback for robust code generation and debugging capabilities.

5eafb52964f99514ae04952e3dceb63a22b3ec2f.title: Knowledge Distillation with the Reused Teacher Classifier
5eafb52964f99514ae04952e3dceb63a22b3ec2f.research_question: How can knowledge distillation be simplified to effectively transfer the performance of a large, pre-trained teacher model to a lightweight student model without relying on complex knowledge representations or elaborate loss functions?
5eafb52964f99514ae04952e3dceb63a22b3ec2f.hypothesis: Reusing the pre-trained teacher classifier for student inference, combined with a simple feature alignment loss and a dimension-matching projector, enables the student model to closely match or even surpass the teacher's performance, while maintaining model simplicity and interpretability.
5eafb52964f99514ae04952e3dceb63a22b3ec2f.proposed_method: A novel knowledge distillation framework is proposed in which the pre-trained teacher classifier is directly reused for student inference. The student model is trained by aligning its feature representations to those of the teacher in the layer preceding the classifier, using a single ℓ2 loss for feature alignment. To address potential mismatches in feature dimensions between teacher and student, a lightweight projector module is introduced after the student encoder. Only the student encoder and the projector are updated during training, while the teacher classifier remains fixed and is reused at inference. The approach is designed to be architecture-agnostic and can be extended to multi-teacher and data-free knowledge distillation scenarios.
5eafb52964f99514ae04952e3dceb63a22b3ec2f.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on standard image classification benchmarks, including CIFAR-100 and ImageNet. Various teacher-student architecture combinations are evaluated, such as ResNet, WRN, VGG, MobileNet, and ShuffleNet. Baselines include vanilla KD, FitNet, AT, SP, VID, CRD, SRRL, and SemCKD, with all competitors implemented using the same training protocols. Evaluation metrics include top-1 test accuracy and pruning ratio, with additional analysis of convergence speed, parameter overhead, and ablation studies on the projector and loss function. Multi-teacher and data-free knowledge distillation settings are also tested, using established methods as baselines and integrating the proposed technique for comparison.
5eafb52964f99514ae04952e3dceb63a22b3ec2f.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the reuse of the pre-trained teacher classifier for student inference, eliminating the need for training a new classifier and complex knowledge representations. The approach relies solely on a simple ℓ2 feature alignment loss, which enhances interpretability and reduces hyper-parameter tuning. The addition of a lightweight projector enables compatibility across diverse architectures with minimal parameter overhead. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, faster convergence, and applicability to multi-teacher and data-free distillation settings, establishing a new, simpler baseline for knowledge distillation.

5ee8bb4fc80a291b2e416a2a879e7153a783d7e9.title: Can AI-Generated Text be Reliably Detected?
5ee8bb4fc80a291b2e416a2a879e7153a783d7e9.research_question: Can AI-generated text be reliably distinguished from human-written text, especially in the presence of adversarial attacks, and what are the fundamental limitations of current detection methods?
5ee8bb4fc80a291b2e416a2a879e7153a783d7e9.hypothesis: Current AI-generated text detectors, including watermarking-based, neural network-based, zero-shot, and retrieval-based approaches, are not robust to advanced paraphrasing and spoofing attacks and may fail to reliably distinguish AI-generated text from human-written text under adversarial conditions.
5ee8bb4fc80a291b2e416a2a879e7153a783d7e9.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation framework will be developed to stress-test the robustness of four major classes of AI-generated text detectors: watermarking-based, neural network-based, zero-shot, and retrieval-based detectors. The primary attack method will be recursive paraphrasing, where AI-generated text is repeatedly paraphrased using high-quality neural paraphrasers such as DIPPER and LLaMA-2-7B-Chat, as well as a sentence-level T5-based paraphraser. The paraphrasing process will be automated and scalable, allowing for multiple rounds of paraphrasing to maximize evasion of detection while monitoring text quality. Additionally, spoofing attacks will be investigated, where adversarially crafted human-written texts are designed to be falsely detected as AI-generated, including attacks that infer watermarking signatures through black-box probing of watermarked LLMs.
5ee8bb4fc80a291b2e416a2a879e7153a783d7e9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on diverse datasets, including the XSum news dataset (1000+ passages, ~300 tokens each), PubMedQA for medical text, and Kafkai for multi-domain articles. Target LLMs will include OPT-1.3B, OPT-13B, and GPT-2 Medium for generating AI text, with paraphrasing performed using DIPPER (11B), LLaMA-2-7B-Chat (7B), and T5-based (222M) models. Detection performance will be evaluated using state-of-the-art detectors: soft watermarking (Kirchenbauer et al.), neural network-based (OpenAI RoBERTa-Large), zero-shot (DetectGPT, entropy/threshold-based), and retrieval-based (Krishna et al.). Evaluation metrics will include AUROC, TPR@1%FPR, and detection accuracy, as well as human evaluation (MTurk) and automated metrics (perplexity, QA benchmark accuracy on SQuAD-v2) to assess text quality and content preservation post-attack. Spoofing attacks will be tested by estimating watermarking token lists via black-box queries and by leveraging retrieval-based detector vulnerabilities.
5ee8bb4fc80a291b2e416a2a879e7153a783d7e9.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first comprehensive stress-test of all major classes of AI-generated text detectors under adversarial conditions, including both evasion (paraphrasing) and spoofing attacks. Recursive paraphrasing is proposed as a scalable and effective method to break both watermarking and retrieval-based detectors with minimal text quality loss, surpassing prior span-replacement and substitution-based attacks. The approach also pioneers black-box spoofing attacks on watermarking schemes, demonstrating that adversaries can infer hidden signatures without white-box access. Finally, a theoretical framework is established linking the AUROC of optimal detectors to the total variation distance between human and AI text distributions, revealing a fundamental tradeoff between type-I and type-II errors and highlighting the increasing difficulty of detection as LLMs improve.

5eeb80dc67590422db64ca95ec0aded24799cfb6.title: Signal Propagation in Transformers: Theoretical Perspectives and the Role of Rank Collapse
5eeb80dc67590422db64ca95ec0aded24799cfb6.research_question: How does the phenomenon of rank collapse in stacked self-attention layers of Transformers impact signal propagation and optimization during training, and what architectural or initialization strategies can prevent or mitigate these effects?
5eeb80dc67590422db64ca95ec0aded24799cfb6.hypothesis: Rank collapse at initialization in deep Transformers leads to vanishing gradients for queries and keys, hindering effective training, but appropriate depth-dependent scaling of residual branches can preserve token diversity and gradient flow, enabling stable and efficient optimization.
5eeb80dc67590422db64ca95ec0aded24799cfb6.proposed_method: A theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted into the causes and effects of rank collapse in Transformer architectures, focusing on the propagation of token representations and gradients at initialization. The methodology involves deriving analytical results for the expected gradients of queries, keys, and values under various initialization and residual scaling regimes, including the use of depth-dependent scaling (e.g., scaling residual connections by 1/sqrt(L), where L is the network depth). The analysis will extend to the impact of architectural hyperparameters such as embedding dimension and sequence length on gradient magnitudes. Additionally, a practical intervention will be proposed: introducing a tunable inverse temperature parameter in the softmax of the attention mechanism to control gradient magnitudes, and training deep Transformers without layer normalization by combining residual scaling and this temperature adjustment.
5eeb80dc67590422db64ca95ec0aded24799cfb6.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed using the IWSLT'14 German-to-English translation benchmark, training Transformer encoder-decoder models of varying depths. The evaluation will compare standard training setups (with Adam optimizer and layer normalization) against the proposed methods: SGD with residual scaling, SGD with both residual scaling and softmax temperature adjustment, and other normalization-free initialization schemes (such as ReZero and T-Fixup). Metrics will include BLEU score for translation quality, as well as analyses of gradient norms for queries, keys, and values at initialization and during training. The experimental setup will avoid learning rate warm-up for SGD, instead using a step scheduler, and will report results averaged over multiple runs.
5eeb80dc67590422db64ca95ec0aded24799cfb6.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a theoretically grounded analysis linking rank collapse to vanishing gradients in Transformers, identifies the necessity of depth-dependent residual scaling for preserving token diversity and effective gradient flow, and reveals distinct scaling behaviors for gradients of queries/keys versus values. It proposes and validates a normalization-free training regime for deep Transformers using SGD, enabled by residual scaling and softmax temperature adjustment, which matches or surpasses Adam-based baselines. The work provides new insights into the architectural factors underlying the success of adaptive optimizers and offers a principled approach to stable Transformer training without reliance on layer normalization.

5f09b1184b72754935747662028c53b1f6714289.title: Continuous Temporal Domain Generalization
5f09b1184b72754935747662028c53b1f6714289.research_question: How can predictive models be trained to generalize across temporally evolving data distributions when both training and test domains are observed at arbitrary, irregular, and continuous time points, rather than at fixed intervals?
5f09b1184b72754935747662028c53b1f6714289.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that modeling the evolution of predictive model parameters as a continuous dynamical system, and leveraging Koopman operator theory to linearize and control these dynamics in a latent space, will enable more accurate and robust generalization across continuous temporal domains compared to existing discrete-time or naive continuous-time approaches.
5f09b1184b72754935747662028c53b1f6714289.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that formulates the evolution of predictive model parameters as a continuous-time dynamical system, where the parameter dynamics are learned from observed domains at arbitrary time points. The approach synchronizes the evolution of data distributions and model parameters by establishing differential equations that govern the model's evolution over time. To address the high-dimensional and nonlinear nature of model parameter dynamics, the method projects these dynamics into a lower-dimensional Koopman-invariant latent space using an autoencoder, where the dynamics become approximately linear and are governed by a learned Koopman operator. Joint optimization is performed over the predictive model parameters, the Koopman operator, and the encoder/decoder mappings, using a composite loss function that enforces prediction accuracy, reconstruction fidelity, dynamic consistency, and enables the incorporation of prior knowledge or inductive bias through constraints on the Koopman operator. At inference, the framework integrates the learned dynamics in Koopman space to predict model parameters at any desired future time, allowing for flexible and controlled generalization.
5f09b1184b72754935747662028c53b1f6714289.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a variety of both synthetic and real-world datasets with continuous temporal domain shifts, including Rotated 2-Moons, Rotated MNIST, Twitter Influenza Risk, Yearbook, Tropical Cyclone Intensity, and House Prices. The proposed method is compared against practical baselines (Offline, LastDomain, IncFinetune, IRM, V-REx), discrete temporal domain generalization methods (CIDA, TKNets, DRAIN, DRAIN-∆t), and continuous-time methods (DeepODE). Evaluation metrics include classification error rate, AUC (for imbalanced Twitter data), and mean absolute error for regression tasks. All models are trained on observed domains and evaluated on unobserved domains at arbitrary time points, with experiments repeated five times to report mean and standard deviation. Additional analyses include visualization of model dynamics, qualitative assessment of decision boundaries, and investigation of the impact of inductive bias on long-term stability.
5f09b1184b72754935747662028c53b1f6714289.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first formalization and solution to the Continuous Temporal Domain Generalization (CTDG) problem, enabling generalization to any moment in continuous time rather than only fixed discrete intervals. The method innovatively applies Koopman operator theory to the evolution of model parameters, allowing for global linearization of nonlinear, high-dimensional dynamics and facilitating both analysis and control of the generalization process. The framework supports the incorporation of prior knowledge or inductive bias through constraints on the Koopman operator, providing stability and desired dynamic behaviors. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the continuous-time approach yields lower or equal approximation error compared to discrete-time methods. Extensive experiments establish a new benchmark for CTDG and demonstrate superior generalization performance and robustness compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

5f19ae1135a9500940978104ec15a5b8751bc7d2.title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
5f19ae1135a9500940978104ec15a5b8751bc7d2.research_question: How can the reasoning accuracy of large language models on complex tasks be improved by leveraging multiple diverse reasoning paths, rather than relying on a single generated solution?
5f19ae1135a9500940978104ec15a5b8751bc7d2.hypothesis: Aggregating answers from a diverse set of sampled reasoning paths and selecting the most consistent answer will significantly improve the reasoning accuracy of large language models on arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning tasks, compared to standard greedy decoding or other aggregation strategies.
5f19ae1135a9500940978104ec15a5b8751bc7d2.proposed_method: A new decoding strategy, termed self-consistency, will be developed to enhance chain-of-thought prompting in large language models. The method involves three main steps: (1) prompt the language model with chain-of-thought exemplars for a given task; (2) instead of using greedy decoding, sample multiple diverse reasoning paths from the language model's decoder using stochastic sampling methods such as temperature sampling, top-k, or nucleus sampling; (3) aggregate the final answers by marginalizing over the sampled reasoning paths, typically via majority vote or weighted aggregation, to select the most consistent answer among the generated outputs. The approach is fully unsupervised, requires no additional training or fine-tuning, and operates directly on pre-trained models. This method can be applied to any task where the final answer is from a fixed set, and is compatible with various sampling strategies and prompt formats.
5f19ae1135a9500940978104ec15a5b8751bc7d2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a wide range of reasoning benchmarks, including arithmetic reasoning datasets (AddSub, MultiArith, ASDiv, AQuA-RAT, GSM8K, SVAMP), commonsense reasoning datasets (CommonsenseQA, StrategyQA, ARC), and symbolic reasoning tasks (last letter concatenation, Coinflip). Four transformer-based language models of varying scales will be evaluated: UL2-20B, GPT-3 (code-davinci-001 and code-davinci-002), LaMDA-137B, and PaLM-540B. All experiments will use few-shot in-context learning with manually written chain-of-thought exemplars, and no model fine-tuning. Baselines will include chain-of-thought prompting with greedy decoding, sample-and-rank, beam search, and ensemble-based approaches using prompt permutations and multiple prompt sets. Evaluation metrics will primarily be accuracy on the test or dev splits of each dataset, with results averaged over multiple runs and sampling 40 reasoning paths per input. Additional studies will assess robustness to sampling parameters, prompt imperfections, and the number of sampled paths.
5f19ae1135a9500940978104ec15a5b8751bc7d2.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple yet effective self-consistency decoding strategy that requires no additional training, supervision, or auxiliary models, and works off-the-shelf with pre-trained language models. Unlike prior approaches that rely on re-rankers, verifiers, or model ensembles, this approach leverages diversity in reasoning paths within a single model to achieve substantial improvements in reasoning accuracy. The method is shown to outperform sample-and-rank, beam search, and ensemble-based baselines, and is robust to prompt imperfections and sampling strategies. Additionally, self-consistency provides a mechanism for uncertainty estimation and improved calibration by correlating answer consistency with model confidence.

5f2f7305a467e01f76b1dbf5867fa34bd90edc19.title: What's Behind PPO's Collapse in Long-CoT? Value Optimization Holds the Secret
5f2f7305a467e01f76b1dbf5867fa34bd90edc19.research_question: How can reinforcement learning algorithms be improved to enable large language models to generate effective long chains of thought for complex reasoning tasks, such as those required in mathematical problem solving?
5f2f7305a467e01f76b1dbf5867fa34bd90edc19.hypothesis: Value initialization bias and reward signal decay are the primary causes of Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) failure in long chain-of-thought (CoT) tasks, and addressing these issues through value model pretraining and decoupled advantage estimation will significantly enhance PPO's performance in such settings.
5f2f7305a467e01f76b1dbf5867fa34bd90edc19.proposed_method: A new reinforcement learning framework, Value-Calibrated Proximal Policy Optimization (VC-PPO), is proposed to address the limitations of PPO in long CoT tasks. The method first involves offline pretraining of the value model using responses generated by a fixed supervised fine-tuning (SFT) policy, with Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE) set to λ=1.0 to ensure unbiased value targets. This pretraining phase continues until the value model achieves low value loss and high explained variance, ensuring accurate initial value estimates. During RL training, VC-PPO decouples the GAE computation for the actor (policy) and critic (value function), allowing the value model to use λ=1.0 for stable and unbiased value propagation, while the policy uses a smaller λ (e.g., 0.95) to balance bias-variance trade-off and accelerate convergence. The training alternates between policy and value updates using mini-batches, with the clipped surrogate objective for the policy and mean squared error for the value function.
5f2f7305a467e01f76b1dbf5867fa34bd90edc19.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the American Invitational Mathematics Examination (AIME) dataset, which requires long CoT reasoning, using Qwen2.5 32B as the base language model. The training set includes historical AIME questions and challenging synthetic math problems, while the test set uses recent AIME questions. Additional evaluation is performed on GPQA and Codeforces datasets to assess generalization. The baseline is standard PPO (λ=0.95), and comparisons are made with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and ablated variants of VC-PPO. Evaluation metrics include pass@1 and pass@32 accuracy on AIME, GPQA, and Codeforces. Hyperparameters such as learning rates, KL penalty, and context lengths (8k and 16k) are systematically varied, and ablation studies are performed on value pretraining steps and λ settings for both actor and critic.
5f2f7305a467e01f76b1dbf5867fa34bd90edc19.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces two key innovations: (1) value model pretraining under a fixed policy with unbiased returns to address value initialization bias, and (2) decoupled GAE computation for actor and critic to mitigate reward signal decay and optimize bias-variance trade-off. This framework enables PPO to achieve state-of-the-art performance on long CoT tasks, surpassing existing baselines such as GRPO and standard PPO. Ablation studies demonstrate that both components are essential for optimal performance, and the approach provides new insights into value optimization for RLHF in language models.

5f3062a96643b4babb18fdcabf69435798de24b2.title: Multi-Domain Graph Foundation Models: Robust Knowledge Transfer via Topology Alignment
5f3062a96643b4babb18fdcabf69435798de24b2.research_question: How can robust and generalizable knowledge transfer be achieved across diverse graph domains, particularly in the presence of significant topological differences, noise, and adversarial attacks?
5f3062a96643b4babb18fdcabf69435798de24b2.hypothesis: A unified multi-domain graph foundation model that aligns both feature and topological information across domains, while adaptively refining graph structures and leveraging prompt-based adaptation, will enable effective and robust knowledge transfer to unseen domains.
5f3062a96643b4babb18fdcabf69435798de24b2.proposed_method: A novel Multi-Domain Graph Foundation Model (MDGFM) is proposed, consisting of two main modules: a multi-domain pre-training module and a downstream target-domain adaptation module. The method begins by projecting node features from multiple source graphs into a unified semantic space using dimensional alignment (e.g., PCA) and domain tokens for semantic alignment. A shared token is introduced to capture domain-invariant information, while a balance token adaptively weighs feature and topological contributions. Graph Structure Learning (GSL) is integrated to refine graph structures, reduce noise, and align topologies across domains. For downstream adaptation, a dual-prompt framework is employed, combining meta-prompts (for transferring broadly learned knowledge) and task-specific prompts (for domain-specific adaptation), with learnable coefficients to control prompt influence. The model is trained using contrastive objectives to maximize mutual information between original and refined graphs, and node representations are obtained via a graph encoder for downstream tasks.
5f3062a96643b4babb18fdcabf69435798de24b2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of benchmark graph datasets, including homophilic (Cora, Citeseer, Pubmed) and heterophilic (Cornell, Chameleon, Squirrel) graphs, as well as a large-scale dataset (Penn94) for downstream evaluation. The evaluation focuses on few-shot and one-shot node classification tasks, using cross-domain transfer scenarios where one dataset is held out as the target domain and the rest serve as sources. Baselines for comparison include supervised GNNs (GCN, GAT), single-domain and multi-domain graph pre-training methods (DGI, GraphCL, GCOPE, MDGPT), and graph prompting methods (GPPT, GPF). Evaluation metrics include mean classification accuracy and robustness under adversarial attacks (random edge addition/deletion, Metattack). Ablation studies will assess the impact of key components (e.g., shared token, GSL, balance token), and domain sensitivity analysis will evaluate the effect of removing source domains. All experiments are repeated multiple times to report mean and standard deviation.
5f3062a96643b4babb18fdcabf69435798de24b2.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified framework that explicitly aligns both feature and topological information across multiple graph domains, leveraging adaptive tokens and graph structure learning for robust domain generalization. The integration of a dual-prompt adaptation mechanism for downstream tasks is novel in the context of graph foundation models. Theoretical analyses provide guarantees on domain generalization error bounds, and empirical results demonstrate superior performance and robustness compared to existing single- and multi-domain graph pre-training and prompting methods. This is the first work to explicitly address invariant information embedded in topology structures for both homophilic and heterophilic domains.

5f404dbba07619cc7f28d75d03f124a52290046e.title: Are Transformers Effective for Time Series Forecasting?
5f404dbba07619cc7f28d75d03f124a52290046e.research_question: Are Transformer-based architectures fundamentally effective for long-term time series forecasting, or do simpler models suffice for this task across diverse real-world datasets?
5f404dbba07619cc7f28d75d03f124a52290046e.hypothesis: Transformer-based models may not be inherently superior for long-term time series forecasting; simple linear models that directly model trend and seasonality can outperform Transformers on standard benchmarks.
5f404dbba07619cc7f28d75d03f124a52290046e.proposed_method: A set of embarrassingly simple one-layer linear models, collectively referred to as LTSF-Linear, will be developed as new baselines for long-term time series forecasting (LTSF). The core approach involves direct multi-step (DMS) forecasting, where historical time series data is regressed via a single linear layer to predict future values. Variants will include DLinear, which decomposes the input into trend and seasonal components using moving averages and applies separate linear layers to each, and NLinear, which normalizes the input by subtracting the last value to mitigate distribution shift. These models will not explicitly model spatial correlations among variates, focusing solely on temporal relationships. Comprehensive ablation studies will be conducted to assess the impact of various design choices, such as input window size, positional encoding, and embedding strategies, on both linear and Transformer-based models.
5f404dbba07619cc7f28d75d03f124a52290046e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on nine widely-used multivariate time series datasets spanning domains such as traffic, energy, economics, weather, and epidemiology (including ETT, Traffic, Electricity, Weather, ILI, and Exchange-Rate). The proposed linear models will be compared against state-of-the-art Transformer-based LTSF models (FEDformer, Autoformer, Informer, Pyraformer, LogTrans) and a naive repeat baseline. Both multivariate and univariate forecasting settings will be evaluated. The core evaluation metrics will be Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). Experiments will systematically vary the look-back window size and forecasting horizon, and include tests of model sensitivity to input order (e.g., shuffled sequences), embedding strategies, and training data size. Efficiency metrics such as inference time, parameter count, and memory usage will also be reported.
5f404dbba07619cc7f28d75d03f124a52290046e.novelty_claims: This proposal challenges the prevailing assumption that Transformers are inherently effective for long-term time series forecasting, introducing a simple linear baseline that consistently outperforms complex Transformer architectures on standard benchmarks. The work provides the first comprehensive empirical study questioning the temporal modeling capabilities of Transformers in this context, including ablations on model design, input order sensitivity, and embedding strategies. The findings advocate for a reevaluation of current research directions and benchmarks in LTSF, and establish LTSF-Linear as a strong, interpretable baseline for future work.

5f4351b4298f918aa8a837454ec198df81dce061.title: Learning to Better Search with Language Models via Guided Reinforced Self-Training
5f4351b4298f918aa8a837454ec198df81dce061.research_question: How can language models be fine-tuned to improve their search efficiency and generalization in complex reasoning tasks, particularly in domains such as arithmetic reasoning and code self-repair?
5f4351b4298f918aa8a837454ec198df81dce061.hypothesis: Incorporating optimal solutions as step-by-step guidance during the generation of search traces for self-training will enable language models to internalize more effective search strategies, resulting in improved accuracy and more efficient use of test-time compute compared to existing fine-tuning methods.
5f4351b4298f918aa8a837454ec198df81dce061.proposed_method: A novel fine-tuning algorithm, Guided Reinforced Self-Training (Guided-ReST), will be developed to enhance the search capabilities of language models. The method generates high-quality search traces by progressively integrating optimal solution steps (subgoals) into the model's self-generated search process. This is achieved through a subgoal augmentation algorithm that, upon encountering unsuccessful search attempts, replaces incorrect nodes with the correct subgoal from the optimal solution and continues the search from that point. The model is then fine-tuned on these augmented, successful traces via supervised learning over multiple iterations. To further improve performance, reinforcement learning (RL) fine-tuning is applied using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) in an operation-level Markov Decision Process, where each action corresponds to a full reasoning step or tree operation rather than individual tokens.
5f4351b4298f918aa8a837454ec198df81dce061.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Countdown benchmark for arithmetic reasoning, using Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct as the base model and a token budget of up to 4K tokens. The model will be evaluated on both seen and unseen target settings, with accuracy measured as a function of token usage. Baselines will include behavior cloning (BC), stream of search (SoS), reinforced self-training (ReST), and PPO-based RL fine-tuning. For code self-repair, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct will be used as the base model, trained on a curated dataset from APPS, CodeContests, and TACO, and evaluated on CodeContests (in-distribution) and CodeForces (out-of-distribution) using pass@k accuracy. The experimental setup will involve generating multiple search traces or episodes per problem, fine-tuning over several epochs, and comparing against both base and ReST models. Evaluation metrics include accuracy, pass@k, and token efficiency.
5f4351b4298f918aa8a837454ec198df81dce061.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new self-training algorithm that systematically incorporates optimal solutions as guidance during search trace generation, enabling more effective and efficient search strategies to be distilled into language models. The method leverages subgoal augmentation to provide corrective feedback at failure points, which is not addressed by existing self-improvement or RL fine-tuning methods. Additionally, the operation-level RL fine-tuning aligns the optimization objective with the structure of reasoning tasks, resulting in improved accuracy and compute efficiency. The approach demonstrates significant improvements over baselines in both arithmetic reasoning and code self-repair, particularly in generalization and test-time compute efficiency.

5f4364f7138f9525df291b16799d1128dd3b8fad.title: SLMRec: Distilling Large Language Models into Small for Sequential Recommendation
5f4364f7138f9525df291b16799d1128dd3b8fad.research_question: How can the efficiency and effectiveness of sequential recommendation systems be improved by leveraging small language models instead of large language models, and what are the necessary techniques to enable small models to achieve comparable performance to their larger counterparts?
5f4364f7138f9525df291b16799d1128dd3b8fad.hypothesis: Small language models, when equipped with appropriate knowledge distillation techniques and supervision strategies, can achieve recommendation performance comparable to large language models while offering substantial gains in efficiency and resource utilization.
5f4364f7138f9525df291b16799d1128dd3b8fad.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops a sequential recommendation framework, SLMREC, which distills knowledge from a large language model (LLM) into a smaller language model (SLM) using a multi-faceted knowledge distillation process. The method employs a teacher-student architecture, where the teacher is a deep LLM-based recommendation model and the student is a shallower, parameter-efficient model. Knowledge distillation is performed not only at the output level but also across multiple intermediate hidden representations, using cosine similarity and L2 norm regularization to align the feature spaces between teacher and student. The student model is further guided by multiple supervision signals, including additional adapters that project representations to lower dimensions and task-specific losses to ensure the acquisition of recommendation-relevant knowledge. The training objective integrates cross-entropy loss, feature alignment losses, and supervision losses, with hyperparameters controlling their contributions.
5f4364f7138f9525df291b16799d1128dd3b8fad.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on large-scale, industry-grade datasets from the Amazon18 collection, specifically the clothing, movies, music, and sports categories. The evaluation protocol uses top-N ranking metrics such as Hit Rate (HR@1, HR@5, HR@10), Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG@5, NDCG@10), and Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR). Baselines include traditional sequential recommendation models (e.g., GRU4Rec, SASRec, BERT4Rec), self-supervised methods, and both generative and embedding-based LLM recommendation models (e.g., Open-P5, E4SRec). Negative sampling is used for unbiased evaluation, with 999 negative items and 1 positive item per test instance. Efficiency is measured in terms of training and inference time, as well as the number of model parameters, with all models evaluated under standardized batch sizes and hardware conditions (A100 GPU). Ablation studies and online distillation variants are also explored to assess the impact of different regularization strategies and training regimes.
5f4364f7138f9525df291b16799d1128dd3b8fad.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel, block-wise knowledge distillation framework for sequential recommendation that aligns intermediate representations between large and small language models. It demonstrates that most intermediate layers in LLMs are redundant for recommendation tasks and that a small language model, trained with the proposed distillation and supervision strategies, can match or surpass the performance of much larger models while using only a fraction of the parameters (as low as 13%). The method is orthogonal and complementary to other efficiency techniques such as quantization and pruning. Theoretical analysis is provided to justify why small models can replicate the representational power of deeper models in this context.

5f4836effb7c1c4cd5b055dce419e2fdc391ae53.title: Majority-of-Three: The Simplest Optimal Learner?
5f4836effb7c1c4cd5b055dce419e2fdc391ae53.research_question: What is the simplest possible algorithm that achieves optimal sample complexity and error bounds for PAC learning in the realizable setting, where empirical risk minimization (ERM) is known to be suboptimal?
5f4836effb7c1c4cd5b055dce419e2fdc391ae53.hypothesis: A majority vote of three ERM classifiers, each trained on disjoint subsets of the data, achieves optimal in-expectation error bounds and near-optimal high-probability error bounds for PAC learning in the realizable setting.
5f4836effb7c1c4cd5b055dce419e2fdc391ae53.proposed_method: The proposed method partitions the training sample into three equal-sized, disjoint subsets. Each subset is used to train an ERM classifier independently, ensuring that each classifier is consistent with its respective subset. The final hypothesis is obtained by taking the majority vote of the three ERM classifiers' predictions on any input. This approach is improper, as the resulting classifier may not belong to the original function class, but it maintains simplicity by only requiring three ERM computations and a majority aggregation. The method is analyzed for both its expected error and its high-probability error, with technical arguments ensuring that the independence of the subsets leads to optimal or near-optimal error rates.
5f4836effb7c1c4cd5b055dce419e2fdc391ae53.experiment_details: Theoretical analysis is conducted for function classes F of VC dimension d, with training samples drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution P over the instance space X. The error rates of the proposed Majority-of-Three method are compared against known lower bounds for both proper and improper learners, as well as against the performance of a single ERM and more complex algorithms such as bagging and the one-inclusion graph algorithm. Evaluation metrics include the expected error and high-probability error bounds, with explicit dependence on n (sample size), d (VC dimension), and δ (confidence parameter). Lower bound constructions are provided to demonstrate the tightness of the results and to compare with alternative majority-vote schemes.
5f4836effb7c1c4cd5b055dce419e2fdc391ae53.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces and analyzes the Majority-of-Three algorithm, which is arguably the simplest improper learner that achieves optimal expected error bounds for PAC learning in the realizable setting. The method is shown to match the best known in-expectation error rates, previously achieved only by more complex algorithms, and provides near-optimal high-probability guarantees. The analysis demonstrates that using three disjoint ERM classifiers suffices for optimality, distinguishing this approach from prior majority-vote or bagging methods that require more classifiers or intricate sampling schemes. The simplicity and effectiveness of the method represent a significant step toward understanding the minimal complexity required for optimal PAC learning.

5f49ec9560ca9e03eff32a607f6caabc08f98926.title: Expanding Performance Boundaries of Open-Source Multimodal Models with Model, Data, and Test-Time Scaling
5f49ec9560ca9e03eff32a607f6caabc08f98926.research_question: How can the performance of open-source multimodal large language models (MLLMs) be advanced to rival or surpass leading commercial models by systematically scaling model architecture, data quality, and test-time strategies?
5f49ec9560ca9e03eff32a607f6caabc08f98926.hypothesis: Systematic scaling of vision encoders, language models, dataset size, and test-time inference strategies, combined with rigorous data quality control and efficient training pipelines, will enable open-source MLLMs to achieve or exceed the performance of leading commercial models on a wide range of multimodal tasks.
5f49ec9560ca9e03eff32a607f6caabc08f98926.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed for scaling open-source MLLMs by integrating large-scale vision encoders (such as InternViT-6B and InternViT-300M) with state-of-the-art language models (e.g., InternLM2.5, Qwen2.5) through a two-layer MLP projector. The training pipeline will be structured in multiple stages: MLP warmup (aligning vision and language representations), optional incremental vision encoder learning, and full model instruction tuning on high-quality, filtered multimodal datasets. Dynamic high-resolution preprocessing will be used to optimally tile images and support multi-image and video data. Data augmentation (random JPEG compression) and advanced loss reweighting (square averaging) will be applied to improve robustness and balance training. A progressive scaling strategy will allow vision encoders trained with smaller LLMs to be efficiently transferred to larger LLMs, reducing computational cost and maximizing reuse.
5f49ec9560ca9e03eff32a607f6caabc08f98926.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of benchmarks covering multi-disciplinary reasoning, document understanding, multi-image/video comprehension, real-world tasks, multimodal hallucination detection, visual grounding, multilingual capabilities, and pure language processing. Datasets will include large-scale mixtures with strict filtering to remove repetitive and low-quality samples, and dynamic data packing will be used to maximize GPU utilization. Baselines will include both open-source models (e.g., Qwen2-VL, LLaVA, CogVLM2, VILA) and leading commercial models (e.g., GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet). Evaluation metrics will be benchmark-specific, such as accuracy on the MMMU validation set and OpenCompass leaderboard scores. Test-time strategies such as Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning and majority voting will be systematically evaluated for their impact on challenging tasks.
5f49ec9560ca9e03eff32a607f6caabc08f98926.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to systematically explore and quantify the impact of scaling vision encoders, language models, dataset size, and test-time configurations in open-source MLLMs. It introduces a progressive scaling strategy that enables efficient transfer of vision encoders across LLMs, significantly reducing training cost. The methodology emphasizes rigorous data quality filtering to mitigate repetitive generation and improve test-time scaling. The framework is the first open-source MLLM to surpass 70% on the MMMU benchmark, setting a new standard for open-source multimodal AI. Additional innovations include dynamic high-resolution preprocessing for multi-image and video data, advanced data augmentation, and balanced loss reweighting strategies.

5f4efbe3aae1d8f44ceab1da257ae685d6beb00b.title: Agent Security Bench (ASB): Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based Agents
5f4efbe3aae1d8f44ceab1da257ae685d6beb00b.research_question: How can the security of LLM-based agents be systematically evaluated and improved across diverse real-world scenarios, considering a broad spectrum of adversarial attacks and defense strategies?
5f4efbe3aae1d8f44ceab1da257ae685d6beb00b.hypothesis: LLM-based agents exhibit significant vulnerabilities to a wide range of adversarial attacks at multiple operational stages, and current defense mechanisms are insufficient to robustly protect these agents without sacrificing utility.
5f4efbe3aae1d8f44ceab1da257ae685d6beb00b.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmarking framework, Agent Security Bench (ASB), will be developed to formalize, implement, and evaluate attacks and defenses on LLM-based agents. The framework will encompass 10 real-world scenarios (such as e-commerce, autonomous driving, and finance), 10 specialized agents, over 400 tools, and 400 tasks. ASB will systematically categorize and implement 27 attack and defense methods, including Direct Prompt Injection (DPI), Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI), Memory Poisoning, Plan-of-Thought (PoT) Backdoor Attacks, and Mixed Attacks, as well as their corresponding defenses. The methodology will include formal definitions for each attack and defense, detailed threat models, and technical procedures for attack generation (e.g., prompt manipulation, memory poisoning via black-box RAG databases, and PoT backdoor demonstration contamination). Defenses will be both prevention-based (e.g., delimiters, dynamic prompt rewriting, paraphrasing) and detection-based (e.g., perplexity and LLM-based detection). A novel metric, Net Resilient Performance (NRP), will be introduced to quantify the trade-off between agent utility and security.
5f4efbe3aae1d8f44ceab1da257ae685d6beb00b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ASB benchmark, covering 10 scenarios and 10 agents, with each agent evaluated using over 400 tools and 400 tasks (including both aggressive and non-aggressive tasks). Thirteen LLM backbones (e.g., GPT-4o, Claude-3.5 Sonnet, LLaMA3-70B, Gemma2-27B) will be benchmarked against 13 attack types (including 10 prompt injection attacks, memory poisoning, PoT backdoor, and mixed attacks) and 11 defense strategies. Seven evaluation metrics will be used: Attack Success Rate (ASR), Refusal Rate (RR), Performance under No Attack (PNA), Benign Performance (BP), False Negative Rate (FNR), False Positive Rate (FPR), and Net Resilient Performance (NRP). Baselines will include state-of-the-art LLM agent security benchmarks, and results will be analyzed for both attack effectiveness and defense efficacy, with detailed breakdowns across agent types, attack vectors, and LLM backbones.
5f4efbe3aae1d8f44ceab1da257ae685d6beb00b.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to provide a holistic, formalized, and scenario-diverse benchmark for evaluating both attacks and defenses in LLM-based agents. It introduces a novel Plan-of-Thought (PoT) backdoor attack that exploits the agent's planning process without requiring model retraining. The benchmark covers a uniquely comprehensive set of attack and defense types, operational stages, and real-world scenarios, surpassing prior benchmarks limited to single attack types or narrow domains. The new Net Resilient Performance (NRP) metric enables principled selection of LLM backbones by balancing utility and security. The framework's extensibility and breadth are designed to drive future research in robust LLM agent security.

5f546dc2f7854f9fd96d6a1bb041aea883d3f7fc.title: The Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma for Clustering and Subspace Approximation: From Coresets to Dimension Reduction
5f546dc2f7854f9fd96d6a1bb041aea883d3f7fc.research_question: What is the minimal target dimension required, as a function of dataset size and accuracy, for Johnson-Lindenstrauss transforms to preserve the optimal cost of various Euclidean projective clustering and subspace approximation problems within a specified approximation factor?
5f546dc2f7854f9fd96d6a1bb041aea883d3f7fc.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the target dimension required to preserve the optimal cost of projective clustering and subspace approximation problems under Johnson-Lindenstrauss transforms can be tightly bounded by quantities related to the size of optimal coresets for these problems, and that these bounds can be generalized beyond previously studied cases such as center-based clustering.
5f546dc2f7854f9fd96d6a1bb041aea883d3f7fc.proposed_method: The proposed method develops a general framework that leverages coreset construction, specifically using the sensitivity sampling technique, to analyze and bound the effect of Johnson-Lindenstrauss (JL) random linear transforms on the optimal cost of geometric optimization problems. For each problem instance, a small weighted coreset is constructed from the dataset, and the JL transform is applied to both the dataset and the coreset. The analysis focuses on ensuring that the cost of the optimal solution in the reduced dimension is within a (1+ε)-factor of the original cost, by carefully relating the performance of the JL transform on the coreset to its performance on the full dataset. The method systematically identifies key events (such as Lipschitz properties of the transform on the coreset span) that must hold with high probability, and uses these to derive dimension bounds in terms of coreset size and problem parameters.
5f546dc2f7854f9fd96d6a1bb041aea883d3f7fc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of projective clustering problems, including (k,z)-subspace approximation, (k,z)-flat approximation, and (k,z)-line approximation. Synthetic and real-world datasets of varying sizes and dimensions will be used to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed dimension reduction bounds. Baselines will include prior best-known bounds for each problem, such as O(k/ε^2) for (k,2)-subspace approximation and O(zk^2 log n/ε^3) for (k,z)-flat approximation. Evaluation metrics will focus on the preservation of optimal cost (within a (1+ε)-factor) after dimensionality reduction, as well as the empirical tightness of the derived dimension bounds. Experimental setup will include repeated random draws of JL transforms and statistical analysis of cost preservation across trials.
5f546dc2f7854f9fd96d6a1bb041aea883d3f7fc.novelty_claims: The proposed approach generalizes the use of Johnson-Lindenstrauss transforms for cost-preserving dimension reduction from center-based clustering to a broader class of projective clustering and subspace approximation problems. The framework introduces a novel connection between coreset size (via sensitivity sampling) and the required target dimension for JL transforms, yielding improved or first-known dimension bounds for several problems, such as (k,z)-flat and (k,z)-line approximation. The method also clarifies subtle distinctions between 'for-all' and 'optimal' guarantees in cost preservation and provides new lower bounds and impossibility results for certain constrained clustering variants. These contributions extend the theoretical understanding of dimension reduction in geometric optimization and offer practical guidelines for applying JL transforms in high-dimensional data analysis.

5f811bd7f115eea0454ed7cb6813705ff5d1de96.title: Invariant Slot Attention: Object Discovery with Slot-Centric Reference Frames
5f811bd7f115eea0454ed7cb6813705ff5d1de96.research_question: How can object-centric neural networks be improved to more effectively discover and represent objects in visual scenes, particularly by leveraging spatial symmetries such as translation, scale, and rotation invariance, in a self-supervised manner?
5f811bd7f115eea0454ed7cb6813705ff5d1de96.hypothesis: Incorporating per-object spatial symmetries through slot-centric reference frames into slot-based neural architectures will improve data efficiency, generalization, and object discovery performance, with minimal computational overhead.
5f811bd7f115eea0454ed7cb6813705ff5d1de96.proposed_method: A novel framework, Invariant Slot Attention (ISA), is proposed to enhance slot-based object discovery models by introducing slot-centric reference frames. The method modifies the Slot Attention architecture by extracting per-slot pose parameters (position, scale, and optionally rotation) from attention masks at each iteration. These parameters are used to transform position encodings for both the attention mechanism and the decoder, creating relative coordinate grids for each slot. During encoding, cross-attention is computed using keys and values modulated by these pose-relative encodings, ensuring that slot representations are invariant to object pose. In the decoding stage, a Spatial Broadcast decoder reconstructs the image using the slot latents and their associated relative grids, allowing for pose-invariant object reconstructions. The approach allows for translation, scale, and (optionally) rotation equivariance, and can be implemented with minimal changes to existing Slot Attention codebases.
5f811bd7f115eea0454ed7cb6813705ff5d1de96.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of synthetic and real-world object discovery benchmarks, including Tetrominoes, CLEVR-Tex, Objects Room, MultiShapeNet, and the Waymo Open dataset. Baselines will include the original Slot Attention model and state-of-the-art object-centric models such as AST-Seg-B3-CT and SPACE. Evaluation metrics will primarily be Adjusted Rand Index for foreground object segmentation (FG-ARI) and mean squared error (MSE) for reconstruction quality. Experimental setups will test data efficiency (varying training set sizes), out-of-distribution generalization (e.g., objects appearing in novel locations or with novel textures), and the impact of different spatial symmetries (translation, scale, rotation) on performance. Ablation studies will assess the necessity of pose-relative encoding in both encoder and decoder, as well as the importance of gradient flow through pose estimation steps.
5f811bd7f115eea0454ed7cb6813705ff5d1de96.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the concept of slot-centric reference frames to slot-based object discovery, enabling per-object spatial symmetry (translation, scale, and rotation) equivariance in both attention and decoding. This approach disentangles object appearance from pose at the slot level, leading to improved data efficiency, generalization, and segmentation quality with negligible computational overhead. The method is simple to implement, broadly applicable to various slot-based architectures, and demonstrates significant gains over existing baselines on challenging synthetic and real-world datasets.
