Additionally, the framework allows for explicit control and manipulation of discovered object representations via their inferred pose parameters.

5f8c041cb8985ee922625b5e65bece10e646f31f.title: An optimal control perspective on diffusion-based generative modeling
5f8c041cb8985ee922625b5e65bece10e646f31f.research_question: How can principles from stochastic optimal control theory be leveraged to enhance diffusion-based generative modeling and develop improved algorithms for sampling from unnormalized densities?
5f8c041cb8985ee922625b5e65bece10e646f31f.hypothesis: By establishing a formal connection between stochastic optimal control and diffusion-based generative models, it is possible to derive new theoretical insights and practical algorithms that improve generative modeling objectives and sampling efficiency, particularly for unnormalized densities.
5f8c041cb8985ee922625b5e65bece10e646f31f.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that interprets diffusion-based generative modeling through the lens of stochastic optimal control, specifically by deriving and utilizing the Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman (HJB) equation governing the evolution of the log-density of the underlying stochastic differential equation (SDE) marginals. The approach formulates the generative modeling objective as a minimization of the Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence between suitable path space measures. Building on this, a new algorithm, termed the time-reversed diffusion sampler (DIS), will be designed for sampling from unnormalized densities. This method trains a control function, parameterized by a neural network, to minimize a reverse-time KL divergence objective, allowing for flexible choices of initial distributions and reference SDEs. The framework also allows the transfer of noise schedules, integrators, and other techniques from generative modeling to the sampling domain.
5f8c041cb8985ee922625b5e65bece10e646f31f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on high-dimensional, multimodal distributions, including Gaussian mixture models, the 10-dimensional Funnel distribution, and double well potentials relevant to molecular dynamics. The proposed DIS algorithm will be compared against the Path Integral Sampler (PIS), which is a state-of-the-art diffusion-based sampler, as well as other baselines such as Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC), No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS), Annealed Flow Transport Monte Carlo (AFT), and variational normalizing flows (VINF). Evaluation metrics will include the accuracy of estimated log-normalizing constants (using unbiased importance sampling estimators), sample quality (via Monte Carlo approximations of expectations and standard deviations), and convergence speed. The experimental setup will utilize large batch sizes, advanced neural network parameterizations, and established noise schedules for SDEs, with implementation details and hyperparameters carefully controlled for fair comparison.
5f8c041cb8985ee922625b5e65bece10e646f31f.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a rigorous connection between diffusion-based generative modeling and stochastic optimal control via the HJB equation, enabling the derivation of generative modeling objectives directly from control theory. The path space perspective allows for new interpretations and improved loss functions based on divergences between continuous-time trajectory measures. The time-reversed diffusion sampler (DIS) represents a novel, flexible, and practical algorithm for sampling from unnormalized densities, outperforming existing diffusion-based samplers in numerical experiments. The approach also enables the transfer of successful techniques from generative modeling to the sampling domain, and provides a foundation for further theoretical and algorithmic advances at the intersection of control, generative modeling, and sampling.

5f90d43e6ece5c6ee6e8186e4b57d46c85377713.title: DIFUSCO: Graph-based Diffusion Solvers for Combinatorial Optimization
5f90d43e6ece5c6ee6e8186e4b57d46c85377713.research_question: How can graph-based diffusion models be leveraged to solve NP-complete combinatorial optimization problems more effectively and efficiently, without relying on hand-crafted domain knowledge?
5f90d43e6ece5c6ee6e8186e4b57d46c85377713.hypothesis: Graph-based denoising diffusion models, when formulated to operate on discrete {0,1}-vector representations of combinatorial optimization solutions and trained with supervised denoising, can generate high-quality, feasible solutions for NP-complete problems, outperforming existing neural and probabilistic solvers in both accuracy and scalability.
5f90d43e6ece5c6ee6e8186e4b57d46c85377713.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that formulates NP-complete combinatorial optimization problems as discrete {0,1}-vector optimization tasks, where each vector encodes the selection of nodes or edges in a candidate solution. The approach will employ graph-based denoising diffusion models, investigating both continuous (Gaussian noise) and discrete (Bernoulli noise) diffusion processes. An anisotropic graph neural network (AGNN) will serve as the backbone for the denoising network, enabling efficient message passing and encoding of graph structure for both node- and edge-based problems. The diffusion process will be trained via supervised learning to maximize the likelihood of optimal or high-quality solutions, and specialized decoding strategies, including heatmap generation and greedy or MCTS-based decoding, will be designed to ensure feasible outputs. Fast inference will be enabled by employing reduced denoising step schedules, such as linear or cosine schedules, to balance computational efficiency and solution quality.
5f90d43e6ece5c6ee6e8186e4b57d46c85377713.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two well-studied NP-complete problems: the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) and the Maximal Independent Set (MIS). Datasets will include 2D Euclidean TSP instances of varying sizes (TSP-50, TSP-100, TSP-500, TSP-1000, TSP-10000) generated and labeled using Concorde and LKH-3 solvers, as well as SATLIB and Erdos-Renyi (ER) graphs for MIS, labeled by the KaMIS heuristic. Baseline comparisons will include exact solvers (Concorde, Gurobi), heuristic methods (LKH-3, 2-opt), and state-of-the-art neural and probabilistic solvers (AM, GCN, Transformer, POMO, DIMES, etc.). Evaluation metrics will include average tour length or independent set size, average relative performance gap to ground-truth, and total runtime. Both greedy and sampling-based decoding strategies will be evaluated, and ablation studies will be performed to compare continuous versus discrete diffusion, different denoising schedules, and the impact of diffusion steps versus sampling.
5f90d43e6ece5c6ee6e8186e4b57d46c85377713.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first graph-based diffusion framework for directly solving NP-complete combinatorial optimization problems, enabling explicit modeling of node/edge selection in a manner natural to graph-based tasks. The approach systematically compares continuous and discrete diffusion processes, demonstrating the superior performance of discrete (Bernoulli) diffusion for combinatorial tasks. The method also incorporates a novel, efficient inference schedule (cosine schedule) and leverages a single anisotropic GNN backbone for both node- and edge-centric problems. The framework claims to achieve state-of-the-art results on large-scale TSP and MIS benchmarks, significantly narrowing the performance gap between neural solvers and ground-truth solutions, and demonstrates strong generalization across problem scales.

5faf1ee9e2f58daac97af704920cc26ae91fd9c3.title: Federated Q-Learning with Reference-Advantage Decomposition: Almost Optimal Regret and Logarithmic Communication Cost
5faf1ee9e2f58daac97af704920cc26ae91fd9c3.research_question: Is it possible to design a model-free federated reinforcement learning algorithm for tabular episodic Markov decision processes that achieves almost optimal regret while maintaining logarithmic communication cost among multiple agents coordinated by a central server?
5faf1ee9e2f58daac97af704920cc26ae91fd9c3.hypothesis: A federated Q-learning algorithm that leverages reference-advantage decomposition, event-triggered communication and policy switching, heterogeneous communication triggering conditions, and optional forced synchronization can achieve almost optimal regret (matching the information-theoretic lower bound up to logarithmic factors) and logarithmic communication cost in federated tabular RL settings.
5faf1ee9e2f58daac97af704920cc26ae91fd9c3.proposed_method: A novel model-free federated Q-learning algorithm, termed FedQ-Advantage, will be developed for tabular episodic Markov decision processes. The approach coordinates multiple agents via a central server, where each agent independently explores the environment and periodically communicates aggregated local statistics rather than raw data. The method employs reference-advantage decomposition to reduce variance in Q-function updates, using both stage-wise (recent) and global (historical) statistics for improved sample efficiency. Communication and policy switching are triggered by event-based thresholds, with heterogeneous conditions that allow more visits in early rounds and fewer in later rounds, thus reducing communication rounds. An optional forced synchronization mechanism is included to accommodate agents with heterogeneous exploration speeds, either synchronizing all agents when one reaches a threshold or waiting for all agents to reach their thresholds before communication. Upper confidence bounds (UCB) are used to promote exploration, and Q-function and policy updates occur only at the end of each stage, which are unaligned across state-action-step tuples, further reducing policy switching and communication costs.
5faf1ee9e2f58daac97af704920cc26ae91fd9c3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic and/or standard tabular episodic MDP benchmarks, simulating multiple agents interacting with independent copies of the environment. The proposed FedQ-Advantage algorithm will be compared against state-of-the-art federated RL baselines, including FedQ-Hoeffding, FedQ-Bernstein, and concurrent Q-learning algorithms. Evaluation metrics will include total regret (difference between optimal and learned policy value), communication cost (number of scalars exchanged), and policy switching cost. Experimental setups will vary the number of agents, states, actions, and episode lengths to assess scalability, communication efficiency, and regret performance. Both versions of the algorithm—with and without forced synchronization—will be evaluated to demonstrate trade-offs between communication cost and robustness to agent heterogeneity.
5faf1ee9e2f58daac97af704920cc26ae91fd9c3.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first model-free federated reinforcement learning algorithm to achieve almost optimal regret (matching the information-theoretic lower bound up to logarithmic factors) with logarithmic communication cost in the multi-agent tabular episodic MDP setting. Key innovations include the use of reference-advantage decomposition for variance reduction in federated Q-learning, a novel event-triggered and heterogeneous communication mechanism that reduces communication rounds, and an optional forced synchronization design that accommodates heterogeneous agent speeds. The method achieves near-linear regret speedup with respect to the number of agents and matches or improves upon the best-known policy switching and communication costs in the literature.

5fb9d244d1c1595f87b8a3769936bf25864eb70d.title: Learnable Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for Multi-modal Learning with Missing Modality
5fb9d244d1c1595f87b8a3769936bf25864eb70d.research_question: How can multi-modal learning models be made robust to missing modalities, particularly in scenarios where certain modalities contribute disproportionately to task performance, such as medical image segmentation?
5fb9d244d1c1595f87b8a3769936bf25864eb70d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that adaptively identifying and distilling knowledge from the most informative modalities for each task, via a learnable cross-modal knowledge distillation framework, will enable multi-modal models to maintain high performance even when key modalities are missing during training or testing.
5fb9d244d1c1595f87b8a3769936bf25864eb70d.proposed_method: A learnable cross-modal knowledge distillation (LCKD) framework is proposed, which automatically identifies the most informative modalities for each task through a teacher election procedure based on single-modality validation performance. For each task, the best-performing modality is selected as the teacher, and knowledge is distilled from these teacher modalities to the student modalities using a pairwise feature-matching loss. The model employs an encoder-decoder architecture (e.g., 3D UNet), where each modality is encoded separately, and features from missing modalities are generated by averaging the features of available modalities. All features (real or generated) are concatenated and passed to the decoder for final prediction. Training optimizes a combined loss function that balances the main task objective (e.g., segmentation Dice and cross-entropy loss) with the cross-modal distillation loss, controlled by a trade-off parameter.
5fb9d244d1c1595f87b8a3769936bf25864eb70d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the BraTS2018 brain tumor segmentation dataset, which contains 3D multi-modal MRI scans (Flair, T1, T1c, T2) and ground-truth annotations for three tumor sub-regions. The model will be trained and evaluated on all 15 possible combinations of missing modalities, simulating real-world incomplete data scenarios. Baseline comparisons will include U-HeMIS, U-HVED, Robust-MSeg, and mmFormer. Evaluation metrics will focus on segmentation Dice scores for each tumor sub-region. The experimental setup includes stochastic gradient descent with Nesterov momentum, cosine annealing for learning rate scheduling, and random dropping of 0-3 modalities per training iteration to simulate missing data.
5fb9d244d1c1595f87b8a3769936bf25864eb70d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel, learnable cross-modal knowledge distillation mechanism that adaptively selects teacher modalities per task and distills their knowledge to student modalities, addressing the missing modality problem in a unified, non-dedicated training framework. Unlike prior methods, this method explicitly leverages modality-specific performance for teacher selection and performs cross-modal distillation, enabling robust performance even when the most informative modalities are absent at test time. The framework is the first to combine automatic teacher election with cross-modal distillation for multi-modal segmentation tasks with missing modalities.

5fbe4c92791fbecb179c1ab79bba9a59b2e155ba.title: GlyphControl: Glyph Conditional Control for Visual Text Generation
5fbe4c92791fbecb179c1ab79bba9a59b2e155ba.research_question: How can visual text generation in text-to-image models be improved to produce coherent, legible, and customizable text within generated images, while enabling user control over text content, location, and size?
5fbe4c92791fbecb179c1ab79bba9a59b2e155ba.hypothesis: Incorporating explicit glyph-level conditional information into diffusion-based text-to-image generative models will significantly improve the accuracy, legibility, and controllability of visual text generation compared to relying solely on textual prompts or character-aware text encoders.
5fbe4c92791fbecb179c1ab79bba9a59b2e155ba.proposed_method: A novel glyph-conditional control framework, GlyphControl, will be developed to enhance visual text generation in diffusion-based models. The approach will augment an off-the-shelf Stable Diffusion model with a ControlNet branch that receives rendered glyph images as additional input conditions. These glyph images, generated using an OCR engine and a glyph renderer, encode the content, location, and size of the desired text, providing explicit spatial and structural guidance to the model. The architecture will consist of a locked copy of the pre-trained Stable Diffusion model and a trainable ControlNet, connected via zero-convolution layers, enabling the model to learn to integrate glyph information without sacrificing general image generation capabilities. During inference, users will be able to specify glyph instructions to customize the generated text's content, position, and size within the output image.
5fbe4c92791fbecb179c1ab79bba9a59b2e155ba.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the newly constructed LAION-Glyph benchmark, which consists of up to 10 million image-text pairs with detailed OCR annotations and high-quality captions. The model will be trained on three dataset scales: LAION-Glyph-100K, LAION-Glyph-1M, and LAION-Glyph-10M, with varying numbers of training epochs. Evaluation will be performed on two benchmarks: SimpleBench (single-word prompts) and CreativeBench (diverse phrase prompts), using OCR-based metrics (exact match accuracy, capitalization-insensitive accuracy, Levenshtein distance), CLIP score for image-text alignment, and FID for image quality. Baselines for comparison will include Stable Diffusion v2.0, SDXL, and DeepFloyd IF (multiple sizes), with all models evaluated under consistent prompt templates and word frequency buckets. Ablation studies will be conducted to analyze the effects of font size and the amount of small text.
5fbe4c92791fbecb179c1ab79bba9a59b2e155ba.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first glyph-conditional control framework for visual text generation in diffusion models, enabling explicit and flexible user control over text content, location, and size. It leverages rendered glyph images as structural conditions, which is a significant departure from prior approaches that rely solely on textual prompts or character-aware encoders. The research also establishes the LAION-Glyph benchmark, the largest open dataset specifically tailored for visual text generation. The approach claims to achieve superior OCR accuracy, image-text alignment, and image quality compared to state-of-the-art baselines, while using significantly fewer parameters than competing models.

5fc1a3a49e8f1d106118b69d1d6be3b6caa23da0.title: Qwen Technical Report
5fc1a3a49e8f1d106118b69d1d6be3b6caa23da0.research_question: How can a scalable, high-performing, and versatile large language model series be developed to address a wide range of natural language processing, coding, and mathematical reasoning tasks, while ensuring alignment with human preferences and efficient multilingual capabilities?
5fc1a3a49e8f1d106118b69d1d6be3b6caa23da0.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a large language model series, pretrained on a massive, diverse, and high-quality multilingual dataset and further aligned through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning from human feedback, can achieve superior performance across language understanding, coding, and mathematical reasoning tasks, rivaling or surpassing existing open-source models and approaching proprietary model performance.
5fc1a3a49e8f1d106118b69d1d6be3b6caa23da0.proposed_method: A comprehensive large language model series will be developed, comprising base pretrained models, chat-aligned models, and specialized variants for coding and mathematics. Pretraining will utilize up to 3 trillion tokens from diverse, multilingual sources, with rigorous data cleaning, deduplication, and quality filtering. The architecture will be based on a modified Transformer, incorporating untied embeddings, RoPE positional embeddings, RMSNorm, SwiGLU activation, and context length extension techniques such as NTK-aware interpolation, LogN-Scaling, and windowed attention. Alignment will be achieved through supervised fine-tuning on curated conversational and safety-focused datasets using ChatML-style formatting, followed by reinforcement learning from human feedback leveraging a reward model trained on human-annotated preference data and Proximal Policy Optimization. Specialized models for code and mathematics will be pretrained and fine-tuned on domain-specific datasets and tasks.
5fc1a3a49e8f1d106118b69d1d6be3b6caa23da0.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate the models on a suite of widely-used benchmarks, including MMLU, C-Eval, GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval, MBPP, and BBH, covering language understanding, reasoning, coding, and mathematics. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art open-source models such as LLaMA, LLAMA2, MPT, Falcon, Baichuan2, ChatGLM2, InternLM, and StableBeluga2, with results reported for models of comparable parameter sizes. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, perplexity (for long-context modeling), and human preference scores. Additional experiments will assess context length extension techniques on long-sequence datasets (e.g., arXiv papers) and the effectiveness of alignment via both automatic and human evaluations. Specialized models will be benchmarked on HumanEval, MBPP, HumanEvalPack (for coding), and GSM8K, MATH (for mathematics).
5fc1a3a49e8f1d106118b69d1d6be3b6caa23da0.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a scalable, multilingual large language model series with competitive performance across diverse domains, including language, coding, and mathematics. Key innovations include the integration of advanced context length extension techniques, a robust data preprocessing and quality assurance pipeline, and a comprehensive alignment strategy combining supervised fine-tuning and RLHF. The specialized models for coding and mathematics are claimed to outperform open-source models of similar size and approach the performance of proprietary models. The tokenizer design is optimized for multilingual efficiency, and the open-sourcing of models at developer-friendly scales aims to improve accessibility and reproducibility in the LLM community.

600246c61484537e7d0c3d32cc81a983e1567fc2.title: Diversifying Policy Behaviors with Extrinsic Behavioral Curiosity
600246c61484537e7d0c3d32cc81a983e1567fc2.research_question: How can imitation learning be extended to enable agents to learn a diverse set of high-performing policies from limited demonstrations, thereby improving behavioral diversity and robustness in unpredictable real-world scenarios?
600246c61484537e7d0c3d32cc81a983e1567fc2.hypothesis: Integrating extrinsic behavioral curiosity into quality-diversity inverse reinforcement learning will encourage exploration of novel behavioral patterns, leading to the learning of more diverse and robust policy archives from limited expert demonstrations.
600246c61484537e7d0c3d32cc81a983e1567fc2.proposed_method: A novel framework, Quality Diversity Inverse Reinforcement Learning (QD-IRL), will be developed by integrating quality-diversity optimization with inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) methods. The approach introduces Extrinsic Behavioral Curiosity (EBC), which provides an episode-level curiosity reward bonus to agents when they discover novel behaviors, as judged by an external behavioral archive. The EBC reward is combined with the imitation reward learned from expert demonstrations, and the resulting reward function is used to optimize a policy archive via a gradient-arborescence-based QD-RL algorithm (such as PPGA). The method will be instantiated with several IRL algorithms (e.g., GAIL, VAIL, DiffAIL) and will support seamless integration with both QD-IRL and QD-RL settings by simply augmenting the reward function with the EBC bonus. Technical implementation involves sampling policies, updating archives, computing EBC rewards based on behavioral novelty, and using policy gradient or evolutionary strategies to optimize the policy set.
600246c61484537e7d0c3d32cc81a983e1567fc2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple MuJoCo robot locomotion environments, including Halfcheetah, Walker2d, and Humanoid, using limited diverse expert demonstrations (e.g., 4 per environment). The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art IRL baselines (GAIL, VAIL, DiffAIL, MaxEnt IRL, AIRL, GIRIL) as well as QD-RL baselines using true rewards. Evaluation metrics will include QD-Score (sum of scores in the policy archive), coverage (proportion of behavioral space explored), best reward, and average reward. Additional tests will assess the impact of demonstration diversity, measure robustness to environment perturbations (few-shot adaptation), and generalization to various behavioral metrics (e.g., jump, angle, feet contact). Statistical significance will be established via Tukey HSD tests, and results will be averaged over multiple random seeds.
600246c61484537e7d0c3d32cc81a983e1567fc2.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a generic and theoretically justified curiosity-driven reward mechanism (EBC) for behavior-level exploration in QD-IRL, enabling the learning of diverse policies from limited demonstrations. The approach is claimed to be broadly applicable to any IRL or QD-RL method by simply augmenting the reward function. The episode-level, archive-based curiosity reward is distinct from prior intrinsic curiosity modules, and the method is demonstrated to substantially improve both diversity and performance in policy archives, sometimes even surpassing expert performance. The framework provides a new paradigm for learning behavioral-diverse policies and addresses key limitations of existing imitation learning and QD-RL algorithms.

600ff4c4ae9fc506c86673c5ecce4fa90803e987.title: RLAIF vs. RLHF: Scaling Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback with AI Feedback
600ff4c4ae9fc506c86673c5ecce4fa90803e987.research_question: Can reinforcement learning from AI-generated feedback (RLAIF) serve as a scalable and effective alternative to reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) for aligning large language models with human preferences across various natural language generation tasks?
600ff4c4ae9fc506c86673c5ecce4fa90803e987.hypothesis: RLAIF can achieve comparable or superior alignment performance to RLHF, enabling scalable model alignment without dependence on expensive human preference labels. Additionally, directly using LLMs as reward providers during RL (d-RLAIF) will further improve performance and address issues of reward model staleness.
600ff4c4ae9fc506c86673c5ecce4fa90803e987.proposed_method: The proposed approach investigates two main methods for aligning language models: (1) RLAIF, where a reward model (RM) is trained on preference labels generated by an off-the-shelf large language model (LLM), and (2) direct-RLAIF (d-RLAIF), where the LLM is directly queried to provide reward scores during reinforcement learning, bypassing the need for a separate RM. The preference labeling process utilizes carefully constructed prompts, including preambles, few-shot exemplars, and chain-of-thought reasoning, to elicit high-quality preference distributions from the LLM. To mitigate position bias, each candidate pair is presented in both orders and averaged. For canonical RLAIF, the RM is trained with a cross-entropy loss on softmaxed LLM preference scores, and RL is performed using REINFORCE with the RM as the reward function. In d-RLAIF, the LLM is prompted to rate generations on a numerical scale, and these scores are normalized and used directly as rewards during RL.
600ff4c4ae9fc506c86673c5ecce4fa90803e987.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three tasks: summarization (using Reddit TL;DR and OpenAI’s Human Preferences datasets), helpful dialogue generation, and harmless dialogue generation (using Anthropic Helpful and Harmless Human Preferences). Baselines will include supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and RLHF, with policies initialized from PaLM 2 Extra-Small and reward models from PaLM 2 XS checkpoints. Human evaluation will be used to assess win rates (preference between policy outputs), harmlessness rates (percentage of safe responses), and alignment of AI-generated preferences to human labels. The impact of various prompting strategies (preamble specificity, chain-of-thought, in-context learning) and LLM labeler size on alignment will be systematically studied. Additional experiments will test the effectiveness of RLAIF when the AI labeler is the same size or checkpoint as the policy, as well as the performance of d-RLAIF compared to canonical RLAIF.
600ff4c4ae9fc506c86673c5ecce4fa90803e987.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a comprehensive evaluation of RLAIF as a scalable alternative to RLHF, including direct head-to-head comparisons across multiple tasks. It proposes and tests direct-RLAIF (d-RLAIF), a method that eliminates the need for reward model training by using LLMs as real-time reward providers, addressing reward staleness and reducing annotation costs. The proposal also explores the limits of self-improvement by using AI labelers of equal or identical size to the policy, and systematically studies prompting techniques and labeler size effects on alignment. These innovations aim to significantly reduce the cost and time of model alignment while maintaining or improving alignment quality.

60109311d6ac66ca97966d26e0f9c889b4f47bcf.title: Efficient Uncertainty Quantification and Reduction for Over-Parameterized Neural Networks
60109311d6ac66ca97966d26e0f9c889b4f47bcf.research_question: How can uncertainty quantification (UQ) for over-parameterized neural networks in regression be made both statistically rigorous and computationally efficient, particularly in the presence of procedural variability introduced by the training process?
60109311d6ac66ca97966d26e0f9c889b4f47bcf.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that procedural variability in over-parameterized neural networks can be effectively removed using a procedural-noise-correcting (PNC) predictor, and that statistically valid confidence intervals for predictions can be constructed with minimal computational overhead by combining PNC with light-computation resampling methods.
60109311d6ac66ca97966d26e0f9c889b4f47bcf.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces a Procedural-Noise-Correcting (PNC) predictor to eliminate procedural variability in over-parameterized neural networks. This involves training a standard base network on the original dataset and an auxiliary network on an artificially labeled dataset, where labels are generated to mimic the expected output of an untrained network under random initialization. The output of the PNC predictor is computed as the difference between the predictions of the base and auxiliary networks, effectively yielding an estimate equivalent to an idealized deep ensemble with infinite replications but at a fraction of the computational cost. To quantify uncertainty, the PNC predictor is integrated with light-computation resampling techniques, specifically batching and cheap bootstrap methods, which allow for the construction of asymptotically exact-coverage confidence intervals using as few as four network trainings. These approaches avoid the need for explicit variance estimation or repeated large-scale retraining.
60109311d6ac66ca97966d26e0f9c889b4f47bcf.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic regression datasets generated from known distributions, with varying data dimensionality (d = 2, 4, 8, 16) and sample sizes (n = 128, 256, 512, 1024). The base neural network architecture will consist of two fully connected layers with sufficient width to ensure over-parameterization, and all optimization and initialization details will follow the NTK parameterization. The proposed PNC-enhanced batching and cheap bootstrap methods will be evaluated for their ability to construct confidence intervals at fixed test points, with coverage rate (CR), interval width (IW), and median point (MP) as evaluation metrics. Baseline comparisons will include dropout-based Bayesian uncertainty quantification and deep ensemble methods with varying numbers of networks. Additionally, mean squared error (MSE) on held-out test data will be used to assess the reduction in procedural variability and improvement in predictive performance.
60109311d6ac66ca97966d26e0f9c889b4f47bcf.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel Procedural-Noise-Correcting (PNC) predictor that removes procedural variability in neural network predictions using only one auxiliary network, as opposed to the multiple retrainings required by deep ensembles. By leveraging neural tangent kernel (NTK) theory, the method provides a statistically principled and computationally efficient approach to uncertainty quantification. The integration of PNC with light-computation resampling methods (batching and cheap bootstrap) enables the construction of asymptotically exact-coverage confidence intervals with minimal retraining, representing a significant advance over existing ensemble and Bayesian approaches. The framework offers both theoretical guarantees and practical scalability for UQ in over-parameterized neural networks.

602407425370a578585431b9834d6ff07a7da8f8.title: Uncertainty Quantification with the Empirical Neural Tangent Kernel
602407425370a578585431b9834d6ff07a7da8f8.research_question: How can uncertainty in neural network predictions be efficiently and accurately quantified, particularly for overparameterized models, to enable trustworthy deployment in critical applications?
602407425370a578585431b9834d6ff07a7da8f8.hypothesis: A post-hoc, sampling-based method that constructs ensembles of linearized neural networks using stochastic gradient descent around trained parameters can efficiently approximate the predictive posterior distribution, matching or exceeding the performance of existing Bayesian and ensemble-based uncertainty quantification methods, while reducing computational cost.
602407425370a578585431b9834d6ff07a7da8f8.proposed_method: The proposed approach, Neural Uncertainty Quantification by Linearized Sampling (NUQLS), begins by fully training an overparameterized neural network on a given dataset. The method then linearizes the network around its trained parameters, creating a local linear surrogate model. Multiple realizations are generated by initializing stochastic gradient descent (SGD) from Gaussian-perturbed versions of the trained parameters, each time solving the linearized problem to (near) convergence. This process yields an ensemble of linear predictors, each representing a plausible model under the posterior. For a given test input, the predictive mean and uncertainty are estimated by aggregating the outputs of the ensemble. Theoretically, under certain loss functions and assumptions, these samples correspond to draws from a Gaussian Process defined by the empirical Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) of the original network.
602407425370a578585431b9834d6ff07a7da8f8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of regression and classification tasks, including standard UCI regression datasets (such as Energy, Kin8nm, and Protein) and large-scale image classification benchmarks (e.g., FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, and ImageNet). The proposed method will be compared against established baselines, including Deep Ensembles, Linearized Laplace Approximation (LLA), SWAG, MC-Dropout, and other state-of-the-art Bayesian and ensemble-based uncertainty quantification techniques. Evaluation metrics will include Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL), Expected Calibration Error (ECE), and a newly introduced metric for uncertainty quality in classification (variance of the maximum softmax probability, VMSP). Experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by matching network architectures and training protocols, and will include analysis of computational efficiency and scalability.
602407425370a578585431b9834d6ff07a7da8f8.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a lightweight, post-hoc, and embarrassingly parallel uncertainty quantification framework that leverages the empirical NTK for posterior approximation without requiring retraining or architectural modifications. It establishes a theoretical connection between ensembles of linearized neural networks and Gaussian Processes with NTK kernels, providing a new perspective on uncertainty quantification in overparameterized models. The approach achieves state-of-the-art or superior performance on both predictive accuracy and uncertainty metrics, while significantly reducing computational costs compared to deep ensembles. Additionally, a novel metric for evaluating uncertainty quality in classification is proposed, addressing gaps in current evaluation methodologies.

60263d3ef1604274e5f095803e9c437f860c511f.title: MaskLLM: Learnable Semi-Structured Sparsity for Large Language Models
60263d3ef1604274e5f095803e9c437f860c511f.research_question: How can semi-structured (N:M) sparsity be effectively and efficiently learned for large language models to reduce inference computational overhead, while maintaining or improving model quality and enabling transferability of sparsity patterns across domains and tasks?
60263d3ef1604274e5f095803e9c437f860c511f.hypothesis: A learnable, end-to-end, probabilistic framework for N:M sparsity mask selection—using differentiable sampling via Gumbel Softmax—can produce high-quality, hardware-friendly sparse masks for large language models, achieving superior model quality and transferability compared to existing one-shot or hand-crafted importance-based pruning methods.
60263d3ef1604274e5f095803e9c437f860c511f.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed to learn semi-structured N:M sparsity masks for large language models by modeling mask selection as a categorical distribution over all valid N:M patterns for each parameter block. The mask selection process is made differentiable using the Gumbel Softmax trick, allowing mask probabilities (logits) to be optimized via gradient descent with respect to the language modeling loss, while keeping the model weights frozen. A regularization term is added to encourage large magnitudes in the remaining weights, aiding both mask learning and transferability. The method supports initialization from prior masks (e.g., from magnitude or other pruning methods) to accelerate convergence and improve mask quality, and enables transfer learning of sparsity patterns to new domains or tasks by refining mask distributions based on new data.
60263d3ef1604274e5f095803e9c437f860c511f.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on multiple large language models, including LLaMA-2 (7B, 13B), Nemotron-4 (15B), and in-house GPT-3 variants (843M, 2B), with model sizes ranging from 843M to 15B parameters. The primary sparsity pattern is 2:4, but the approach is extensible to other N:M ratios. Training is performed on large-scale datasets (e.g., C4, blended datasets, and original pretraining data), with mask learning carried out for 2,000 steps without updating model weights. Evaluation is performed using perplexity (PPL) on Wikitext and task-specific datasets, as well as zero-shot evaluation via LM-Eval-Harness. Baselines include Magnitude Pruning, SparseGPT, and Wanda, with calibration sets of varying sizes. Additional experiments assess transferability to downstream tasks, storage efficiency, and inference speedup on hardware accelerators.
60263d3ef1604274e5f095803e9c437f860c511f.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to enable fully learnable, end-to-end N:M semi-structured sparsity for frozen large language models at scale, using a differentiable probabilistic framework based on Gumbel Softmax. It demonstrates the ability to learn high-quality, hardware-friendly masks directly from large datasets, outperforming state-of-the-art one-shot and importance-based pruning methods in both general and domain-specific settings. The framework uniquely supports transfer learning of sparsity masks, enabling efficient adaptation to new tasks or domains with minimal storage overhead and lossless compression. The approach also introduces a regularization strategy to maintain weight magnitudes for improved downstream performance.

603bb1eb011147bed0766c0b0c0bf4bb83ef4b9a.title: Many-Shot In-Context Learning
603bb1eb011147bed0766c0b0c0bf4bb83ef4b9a.research_question: How does scaling the number of in-context examples (shots) in large language models impact performance across a broad range of tasks, and can alternative approaches reduce reliance on human-generated outputs in the many-shot regime?
603bb1eb011147bed0766c0b0c0bf4bb83ef4b9a.hypothesis: Increasing the number of in-context examples will significantly improve large language model performance on generative and discriminative tasks, and model-generated or unsupervised prompts can mitigate the need for human-generated rationales without substantial loss in effectiveness.
603bb1eb011147bed0766c0b0c0bf4bb83ef4b9a.proposed_method: The proposed research will systematically investigate the effects of scaling in-context learning (ICL) by providing large language models with hundreds to thousands of input-output examples (shots) during inference, leveraging models with expanded context windows (up to 1M tokens). The methodology will include three main approaches: (1) standard many-shot ICL using human-generated input-output pairs, (2) Reinforced ICL, which replaces human-written rationales with model-generated rationales filtered for correctness, and (3) Unsupervised ICL, where only domain-specific inputs are provided without rationales or outputs. For Reinforced ICL, model-generated rationales will be sampled and filtered based on answer correctness, while Unsupervised ICL will use prompts consisting solely of unsolved problems and minimal output format instructions. The study will also analyze the ability of many-shot ICL to override pretraining biases and learn high-dimensional or non-natural language tasks.
603bb1eb011147bed0766c0b0c0bf4bb83ef4b9a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Gemini 1.5 Pro large language model with a 1M token context window. Tasks will span problem-solving (MATH, GSM8K), question answering (GPQA), summarization (XSum, XLSum), algorithmic reasoning (BBH), reward modeling (CodeVerifier), low-resource machine translation (FLORES-200: Bemba, Kurdish), planning (Logistics), and sentiment analysis (Financial PhraseBank). Each task will be evaluated by varying the number of in-context examples from few-shot to many-shot regimes (up to 8192 shots and 1M tokens). Baselines will include few-shot ICL, state-of-the-art fine-tuned models, and zero-shot prompts. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, ROUGE-L, chrF2++, and success rate, with multiple random seeds for reliability. Additional experiments will test the ability to overcome pretraining biases (using label flips and abstract labels) and learn high-dimensional functions (linear classification and sequential parity), comparing many-shot ICL to nearest-neighbor and models trained from scratch.
603bb1eb011147bed0766c0b0c0bf4bb83ef4b9a.novelty_claims: This research proposes the first comprehensive evaluation of many-shot in-context learning across a diverse set of tasks using extremely large context windows, demonstrating substantial performance gains over few-shot ICL. The introduction of Reinforced and Unsupervised ICL provides practical solutions to the bottleneck of human-generated outputs, showing that model-generated or input-only prompts can be highly effective, particularly for complex reasoning tasks. The study reveals that many-shot ICL can override pretraining biases, learn high-dimensional functions, and perform comparably to fine-tuning, challenging the reliance on next-token prediction loss as a performance indicator. These findings suggest new directions for leveraging LLMs in domains where labeled data is scarce or expensive.

603ce317ee153ef6f61ea02a90c187f088c51bc1.title: RLSbench: Domain Adaptation Under Relaxed Label Shift
603ce317ee153ef6f61ea02a90c187f088c51bc1.research_question: How can domain adaptation methods be robustly evaluated and improved under scenarios where both the label marginal and class-conditional distributions shift arbitrarily across domains, particularly in real-world settings spanning vision, language, and tabular data modalities?
603ce317ee153ef6f61ea02a90c187f088c51bc1.hypothesis: A meta-algorithm that combines pseudo-balancing of target data and re-weighting of the final classifier using an estimated target label marginal will significantly improve the performance of existing domain adaptation methods under relaxed label shift, especially when label marginal shifts are severe.
603ce317ee153ef6f61ea02a90c187f088c51bc1.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark, RLSBENCH, will be constructed to evaluate domain adaptation under relaxed label shift, where the label marginal can shift arbitrarily and class-conditional distributions shift naturally. The method involves simulating label marginal shifts in target domains using Dirichlet sampling with varying severity, while keeping the source label distribution fixed. A two-step meta-algorithm will be developed: (1) at each training epoch, pseudo-balance the target data using pseudo-labels generated by the current classifier, and (2) post-hoc re-weight the final classifier's predictions according to an estimate of the target label marginal, which is computed using established label shift estimation techniques. This meta-algorithm is designed to be compatible with a wide range of domain adaptation heuristics, including domain-invariant representation learning, self-training, and test-time adaptation methods.
603ce317ee153ef6f61ea02a90c187f088c51bc1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on RLSBENCH, a suite of 14 multi-domain datasets spanning vision (e.g., CIFAR-10, OfficeHome, DomainNet, Visda, BREEDS), NLP (e.g., CivilComments), and tabular modalities (e.g., Retiring Adults, Mimic Readmission), resulting in 560 source-target distribution shift pairs and approximately 30,000 trained models. Target label marginal shifts will be simulated using Dirichlet distributions with varying concentration parameters to control shift severity. Baseline comparisons will include source-only models, popular domain adaptation methods (DANN, CDANN, MCD, FixMatch, Noisy Student, SENTRY, BN-adapt, TENT), and methods specifically proposed for relaxed label shift (IW-DANN, IW-CDANN, SENTRY). Evaluation metrics will include target domain accuracy and ℓ1 error for target label marginal estimation. Model selection will be based on source validation performance, and experiments will control for data augmentation, architecture, and hyperparameter settings to ensure fair comparisons.
603ce317ee153ef6f61ea02a90c187f088c51bc1.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark, RLSBENCH, is the first large-scale, standardized testbed for evaluating domain adaptation under relaxed label shift with arbitrary label marginal shifts and natural class-conditional shifts across diverse modalities. The meta-algorithm introduces a simple yet effective combination of pseudo-balancing and re-weighting corrections that can be paired with any domain adaptation method, leading to significant improvements—often 2–10% in accuracy—under severe label marginal shifts. The study provides the first comprehensive and rigorous comparison of popular domain adaptation methods and label shift corrections under standardized, realistic conditions, highlighting the widespread vulnerability of existing methods and establishing new best practices for robust evaluation and adaptation.

6056961e0e4b5fb8bdce7aa64a8499e5a38da7df.title: UCB Momentum Q-learning: Correcting the bias without forgetting
6056961e0e4b5fb8bdce7aa64a8499e5a38da7df.research_question: How can reinforcement learning in tabular, episodic, and possibly non-stationary Markov Decision Processes be improved to achieve optimal regret bounds, particularly with respect to the dependence on the number of states and the horizon, while maintaining sample efficiency and computational tractability?
6056961e0e4b5fb8bdce7aa64a8499e5a38da7df.hypothesis: Incorporating a momentum term into Q-learning updates, combined with upper confidence bound-based exploration, will correct the bias inherent in Q-learning without increasing variance excessively, thereby achieving regret bounds that are optimal in the first-order term and only linear in the number of states in the second-order term.
6056961e0e4b5fb8bdce7aa64a8499e5a38da7df.proposed_method: A novel reinforcement learning algorithm, UCB Momentum Q-learning (UCBMQ), will be developed for tabular, episodic Markov Decision Processes, including non-stationary settings where rewards and transitions may change within an episode. The method augments standard Q-learning updates with a momentum term that leverages a bias-value function specific to each state-action pair, designed to correct the bias from using past, potentially inaccurate, Q-value estimates. Optimism in the face of uncertainty is incorporated via upper confidence bounds on Q-values, constructed using Bernstein-type bonuses to ensure tight dependence on the episode horizon. The learning rate is chosen to avoid forgetting past samples, while the momentum rate is carefully scaled with the horizon to balance bias correction and variance. The algorithm maintains and updates separate bias-value functions for each state-action pair online, ensuring computational feasibility.
6056961e0e4b5fb8bdce7aa64a8499e5a38da7df.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a grid-world environment with 50 states and 4 actions, simulating non-stationary transitions and sparse rewards. UCBMQ will be compared against several baselines, including UCBVI (a model-based algorithm), OptQL (a model-free Q-learning variant with aggressive learning rates), and Greedy-UCBVI (a model-based algorithm with real-time dynamic programming). All algorithms will use identical exploration bonuses to ensure fair comparison. Evaluation will focus on cumulative regret over multiple episodes, with results averaged over several runs. The key evaluation metric will be cumulative regret, and the experimental setup will highlight both sample efficiency and the scaling of regret with respect to the number of states and the episode horizon.
6056961e0e4b5fb8bdce7aa64a8499e5a38da7df.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to achieve a regret bound that matches the problem-independent lower bound up to polylogarithmic factors for large enough episodes, while ensuring the second-order term is only linear in the number of states. The introduction of a momentum term in Q-learning updates for bias correction, without increasing variance excessively, is a novel technical contribution. The approach resolves an open question regarding achieving linear dependence on the number of states in the second-order term for model-free algorithms in episodic MDPs. Additionally, the method provides a new analysis that avoids the exponential dependence on the horizon present in previous works, and the algorithm is computationally efficient, with time complexity linear in the number of episodes, states, actions, and horizon.

6057de346b566111994ee2bf36973cb89759bc58.title: A TRIANGLE Enables Multimodal Alignment Beyond Cosine Similarity
6057de346b566111994ee2bf36973cb89759bc58.research_question: How can multimodal alignment be improved to ensure effective and interpretable joint representation of three or more modalities, overcoming the limitations of pairwise similarity measures in current state-of-the-art models?
6057de346b566111994ee2bf36973cb89759bc58.hypothesis: A similarity measure based on the geometric area formed by three modality embeddings in high-dimensional space will provide superior alignment and interpretability compared to conventional pairwise cosine similarity, resulting in improved performance on multimodal downstream tasks.
6057de346b566111994ee2bf36973cb89759bc58.proposed_method: A novel framework, TRIANGLE (TRI-modAl Neural Geometric LEarning), is proposed to directly align three modalities—such as video, audio, and text—within the higher-dimensional space spanned by their embedding vectors. The method computes a triangle-area similarity metric, where the area is derived from the embeddings of the three modalities; a smaller area indicates better alignment. This similarity replaces pairwise cosine similarity in contrastive loss functions, ensuring that all three modalities are jointly aligned rather than just aligned to an anchor. The approach also incorporates a regularization term based on cosine similarity between the two modalities most relevant to the downstream task, balancing holistic alignment with task-specific requirements. The method is designed to be portable across different modality combinations and does not require additional fusion layers or architectural changes.
6057de346b566111994ee2bf36973cb89759bc58.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several benchmark datasets that include three modalities: MSR-VTT, DiDeMo, ActivityNet, and VATEX for video-text-audio retrieval tasks; AudioCaps and VGGSound for audio-text and audio-visual classification. The approach will be evaluated in zero-shot settings for text-to-video, video-to-text, text-to-audio retrieval, and audio-visual classification. Baselines will include state-of-the-art models such as VAST, GRAM, Symile, LanguageBind, and others, using the same encoders (BERT-B for text, BEATs for audio, EVAClip-ViT-G for video) and comparable numbers of parameters. Evaluation metrics will primarily be Recall@1 and Recall@10. Additional experiments will include training from scratch and ablation studies to assess the contribution of the triangle-area loss and regularization components.
6057de346b566111994ee2bf36973cb89759bc58.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a geometric similarity measure based on the area of the triangle formed by three modality embeddings, enabling direct and interpretable alignment in high-dimensional space. This approach eliminates the reliance on pairwise similarities and fusion layers, providing a holistic and portable solution for three-modal alignment. The method offers an intuitive geometric indicator of alignment, enhancing interpretability. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on multiple multimodal retrieval and classification tasks, with significant improvements over existing cosine-based and generic n-modal alignment methods.

605ce1aa8886eecb53bdb29fca60f1fe5ff7fd8c.title: Mechanisms that Incentivize Data Sharing in Federated Learning
605ce1aa8886eecb53bdb29fca60f1fe5ff7fd8c.research_question: How can a system be designed to incentivize rational agents to contribute their fair share of data in federated learning, thereby maximizing the accuracy of the resulting model and improving collaboration?
605ce1aa8886eecb53bdb29fca60f1fe5ff7fd8c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that mechanisms based on accuracy shaping, rather than unconditional data sharing or monetary payments, can effectively incentivize rational agents to maximize their data contributions in federated learning, thus preventing free-riding and improving overall model performance.
605ce1aa8886eecb53bdb29fca60f1fe5ff7fd8c.proposed_method: A principal-agent framework will be developed, modeling each agent as having a private, potentially verifiable cost for data generation and a utility function that balances model accuracy against this cost. The proposed mechanism will map each agent's data contribution to the accuracy of the model they receive, using a contract-theoretic approach. Specifically, an accuracy shaping mechanism will be implemented, where the accuracy of the model assigned to an agent is a function of their own contribution, with thresholds and marginal incentives tuned to ensure that agents contribute beyond their individual optimum. In the full-information setting, the mechanism will be designed to be data-maximizing, feasible, and individually rational, ensuring that no agent is worse off than acting alone. For settings with unknown costs, truth-revealing accuracy curves will be designed to elicit honest reporting of costs.
605ce1aa8886eecb53bdb29fca60f1fe5ff7fd8c.experiment_details: Experiments will involve simulations using standard accuracy functions derived from generalization bounds and power-law scaling, as well as stylized models relevant to applications such as autonomous driving. The experimental setup will compare the proposed accuracy shaping mechanism against the standard federated learning baseline (where all agents receive the model trained on the pooled data) and analyze equilibrium data contributions. Key variables will include the number of agents, marginal cost per data point, and learning task complexity. Evaluation metrics will focus on the total data collected at equilibrium, the distribution of data contributions among agents, and the resulting model accuracy. Sensitivity analyses will be conducted to assess robustness to varying agent costs and problem difficulty.
605ce1aa8886eecb53bdb29fca60f1fe5ff7fd8c.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel application of contract theory to the problem of data maximization in federated learning, focusing on accuracy shaping mechanisms rather than payment-based incentives. Unlike prior work that addresses free-rider detection or type elicitation, this approach directly incentivizes maximal data contribution without requiring monetary compensation. The mechanism is provably data-maximizing, prevents catastrophic free-riding, and enables collaborative solutions to learning problems that are infeasible for individual agents. The framework also extends to settings with unknown agent costs through the design of truth-revealing mechanisms.

607f3b3961feb19e6703f03f9e4091eee8523f17.title: Tiled Flash Linear Attention: More Efficient Linear RNN and xLSTM Kernels
607f3b3961feb19e6703f03f9e4091eee8523f17.research_question: How can the efficiency and scalability of linear recurrent neural network (RNN) kernels be improved for long-context sequence modeling, and what are the trade-offs between memory usage and computational speed on modern hardware?
607f3b3961feb19e6703f03f9e4091eee8523f17.hypothesis: Introducing a two-level sequence parallelism kernel algorithm for linear RNNs, combined with targeted architectural modifications and initialization strategies, will enable faster and more memory-efficient training and inference for long-context language modeling without sacrificing model performance.
607f3b3961feb19e6703f03f9e4091eee8523f17.proposed_method: A novel kernel algorithm, Tiled Flash Linear Attention (TFLA), will be developed for linear RNNs, specifically targeting the mLSTM architecture. TFLA introduces two levels of sequence parallelism: the first level parallelizes over chunks of the input sequence, while the second level parallelizes matrix computations within each chunk via tiling along the sequence dimension. This approach enables arbitrary large chunk sizes, increasing arithmetic intensity and balancing memory consumption with computational efficiency. The method will also include a new mLSTM variant (mLSTMsig) that replaces the exponential input gate with a sigmoid gate, reducing computational overhead and kernel complexity. Additionally, empirical transfer function analysis will guide gate bias initialization to further enhance training stability and performance.
607f3b3961feb19e6703f03f9e4091eee8523f17.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on language modeling tasks using the DCLM dataset, training models at various scales (160M, 400M, and 1.4B parameters) and context lengths (4096 and 8192 tokens). The proposed TFLA-based mLSTM kernels will be benchmarked against state-of-the-art baselines such as FlashAttention (versions 2 and 3), Mamba, and Flash Linear Attention (FLA), with runtime and memory usage evaluated on NVIDIA H100 GPUs. Evaluation metrics will include validation perplexity for language modeling and kernel execution time for both inference (forward pass) and training (forward-backward pass). The effects of input gate bias initialization and normalization layer epsilon will be systematically explored to assess their impact on training stability and final model performance.
607f3b3961feb19e6703f03f9e4091eee8523f17.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces Tiled Flash Linear Attention (TFLA), a new kernel algorithm for linear RNNs that enables two-level sequence parallelism and supports arbitrarily large chunk sizes, overcoming memory bottlenecks of previous methods. The method applies TFLA to mLSTM and introduces a computationally efficient mLSTM variant with a sigmoid input gate (mLSTMsig), achieving faster kernel runtimes without loss in language modeling performance. The proposal also claims improved training stability and performance through empirically guided gate initialization, establishing new state-of-the-art efficiency for long-context sequence modeling primitives.

60a75a440967713a1fbcc85506a3d085f46fb8c8.title: Advancing Mathematical Reasoning in Language Models: The Impact of Problem-Solving Data, Data Synthesis Methods, and Training Stages
60a75a440967713a1fbcc85506a3d085f46fb8c8.research_question: How can the mathematical reasoning abilities of large language models be most effectively enhanced through the use of problem-solving data, data synthesis methods, and training stage strategies during pre-training and fine-tuning?
60a75a440967713a1fbcc85506a3d085f46fb8c8.hypothesis: 1) Incorporating problem-solving data during the pre-training phase will enhance mathematical reasoning abilities of language models more effectively than using general mathematical corpora. 2) Synthetic problem-solving data, especially when generated via efficient synthesis methods, can further improve model performance. 3) The stage at which problem-solving data is introduced (pre-training vs. supervised fine-tuning) significantly affects the acquisition of mathematical reasoning capabilities, with pre-training offering superior benefits.
60a75a440967713a1fbcc85506a3d085f46fb8c8.proposed_method: A comprehensive training framework will be developed to systematically investigate the impact of problem-solving data, synthetic data generation methods, and training stages on mathematical reasoning in language models. The approach involves: (1) augmenting the pre-training phase with varying ratios of problem-solving data and general mathematical corpora, (2) generating synthetic problem-solving data using multiple data synthesis techniques, including response diversification, query expansion, retrospective enhancement, and tutorship amplification, and (3) comparing the effects of introducing problem-solving data during continued pre-training (CPT) versus supervised fine-tuning (SFT). The framework will include rigorous data deduplication and decontamination procedures to ensure data quality and prevent contamination. Models will be trained for a fixed number of steps with consistent hyperparameters, and checkpoints with the lowest validation loss will be selected for evaluation.
60a75a440967713a1fbcc85506a3d085f46fb8c8.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize a robust base model (e.g., Llama2 or Llama3-8B) and a diverse set of training data, including general corpora (e.g., RedPajama, Wikipedia), mathematical corpora (e.g., OpenWebMath), and curated problem-solving datasets (e.g., NuminaMath, Lila, proprietary data). Synthetic data will be generated via four distinct methods, and the impact of each will be assessed. Evaluation will be performed on multiple mathematical reasoning benchmarks, including GSM8K, MATH, GAOKAO, and ZHONGKAO, with accuracy as the primary metric. Both zero-shot and few-shot prompting will be used, and the arithmetic mean of accuracies across datasets will be reported. Baselines will include models trained with only general or mathematical corpora, as well as models fine-tuned with varying amounts and types of problem-solving data. Additional analyses will segment data by distribution (in-domain vs. out-of-domain) and difficulty (easy vs. hard problems) to assess learning dynamics.
60a75a440967713a1fbcc85506a3d085f46fb8c8.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a systematic comparison of problem-solving data versus general mathematical corpora during pre-training, identifies and benchmarks multiple synthetic data generation methods, and rigorously contrasts the effects of data introduction at different training stages. The tutorship amplification synthesis method is highlighted as a particularly effective innovation for enabling self-correction and error detection in models. The research also provides detailed insights into how data distribution and difficulty affect learning at different training stages, and demonstrates that challenging problem-solving data during pre-training yields superior reasoning capabilities. The resulting methodology enables the development of highly efficient math-specific language models that outperform existing models with fewer training tokens and less reliance on large-scale post-training.

60b35c6d68acced19b0c66edcfc0ee0a2c11efed.title: Landmark Attention: Random-Access Infinite Context Length for Transformers
60b35c6d68acced19b0c66edcfc0ee0a2c11efed.research_question: How can transformer-based language models be enabled to efficiently process and attend to arbitrarily long contexts without sacrificing the random-access flexibility of attention or incurring prohibitive computational and memory costs?
60b35c6d68acced19b0c66edcfc0ee0a2c11efed.hypothesis: Introducing landmark tokens as block representatives and training the attention mechanism to use these tokens for block-level retrieval will allow transformers to efficiently and flexibly attend to relevant information in arbitrarily long contexts, matching or exceeding the performance of existing long-context models while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements.
60b35c6d68acced19b0c66edcfc0ee0a2c11efed.proposed_method: The proposed method divides the input sequence into fixed-length blocks and inserts a special landmark token after each block. During training, the attention mechanism is modified so that each token's attention depends not only on the key of other tokens but also on the key of the corresponding block's landmark token. A GroupedSoftmax function is used to separately normalize attention within blocks and across landmark tokens, effectively gating access to blocks via their landmark. At inference, only the most relevant blocks (as determined by attention to their landmarks) are retrieved from memory, and the full attention is computed over these blocks plus the local context. This approach allows for offloading non-relevant blocks to slower memory and only swapping them in when needed, and can be further optimized using advanced data structures (e.g., FAISS) for efficient nearest-neighbor retrieval.
60b35c6d68acced19b0c66edcfc0ee0a2c11efed.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on language modeling tasks using datasets such as PG-19 (English books, 3.7B tokens) and arXiv math papers (5.6B tokens). The proposed model will be compared against baselines including standard Transformers with local attention and Transformer-XL, using comparable training regimes and architecture (e.g., GPT-2-like 12-layer, 8-head, 1024-dim models). Evaluation metrics include perplexity at various context lengths, retrieval accuracy for specific information (e.g., passphrase recovery in long prompts), and computational efficiency (FLOPs, memory usage). Both training from scratch and fine-tuning of pre-trained models (e.g., LLaMA-7B) will be explored, with context lengths during inference ranging up to 32k tokens and beyond. Ablation studies will examine the impact of retrieval granularity and memory/cache management strategies.
60b35c6d68acced19b0c66edcfc0ee0a2c11efed.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a landmark-based attention mechanism that enables random-access retrieval of relevant blocks from arbitrarily long contexts directly within the attention computation, without relying on separate retrieval modules or sacrificing attention flexibility. This method decouples training and inference context lengths, allowing efficient extrapolation to much longer contexts than seen during training. It achieves significant reductions in computation and memory usage, is compatible with advanced retrieval data structures, and can be seamlessly integrated into existing pre-trained models via fine-tuning. Additionally, the method provides interpretability by making the retrieval process transparent through attention scores.

60bdb4c44136fc452170cc65fbd9cd8ad73ca425.title: UniDepth: Universal Monocular Metric Depth Estimation
60bdb4c44136fc452170cc65fbd9cd8ad73ca425.research_question: How can monocular metric depth estimation be made universally applicable and robust across diverse domains and camera types, without relying on external camera parameters or domain-specific information at test time?
60bdb4c44136fc452170cc65fbd9cd8ad73ca425.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a monocular depth estimation model can achieve robust, universal metric 3D scene reconstruction from a single image across domains by directly predicting 3D points in a pseudo-spherical output space, leveraging a self-prompted dense camera representation and a geometric invariance loss to disentangle camera and depth features.
60bdb4c44136fc452170cc65fbd9cd8ad73ca425.proposed_method: A novel framework, UniDepth, will be developed for universal monocular metric depth estimation. The method will consist of three main components: (1) a self-promptable camera module that predicts a dense, non-parametric camera representation (azimuth and elevation per pixel) from the input image, (2) a depth module that predicts log-depth values for each pixel, conditioned on the camera representation via cross-attention, and (3) a pseudo-spherical output space (azimuth, elevation, log-depth) that orthogonally separates camera and depth information. The camera representation will be embedded using Laplace Spherical Harmonic Encoding to provide robust, high-capacity prompts to the depth module. A geometric invariance loss will be introduced, enforcing consistency between depth features conditioned on camera prompts from different geometric augmentations of the same image, thereby promoting camera-aware and domain-invariant depth estimation. The architecture will utilize a backbone encoder (e.g., ViT or ConvNext), with stop-gradient operations to prevent camera gradients from dominating the encoder training.
60bdb4c44136fc452170cc65fbd9cd8ad73ca425.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by training the model on a large, diverse ensemble of real-world datasets, including Argoverse2, Waymo, DrivingStereo, Cityscapes, BDD100K, Mapillary-PSD, A2D2, ScanNet, and Taskonomy, totaling approximately 3 million images with varying cameras and domains. Zero-shot generalization will be evaluated on ten unseen datasets: SUN-RGBD, DiodeIndoor, IBims-1, VOID, HAMMER, ETH-3D, nuScenes, DDAD, NYU-DepthV2, and KITTI. Baselines will include state-of-the-art monocular metric depth estimation methods such as BTS, AdaBins, NeWCRF, iDisc, ZoeDepth, Metric3D, and ZeroDepth. Evaluation metrics will cover both scale-invariant and scale-dependent measures, including delta accuracy (δ1), scale-invariant log error (SIlog), absolute relative error (A.Rel), root mean square error (RMS), Chamfer Distance (CD), and F-score (FA), as well as point cloud-based metrics. All methods will be evaluated in a fair, consistent zero-shot regime without test-time augmentations, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the contribution of each architectural component.
60bdb4c44136fc452170cc65fbd9cd8ad73ca425.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to address universal monocular metric depth estimation without any reliance on external camera parameters or domain-specific priors at test time. Key innovations include the introduction of a self-promptable dense camera module, a pseudo-spherical output space that orthogonally separates camera and depth, and a geometric invariance loss for robust camera-aware depth prediction. The method is designed to generalize across arbitrary domains and camera types, and is demonstrated to achieve state-of-the-art performance in zero-shot settings, even surpassing models trained on the target domains. The framework also allows for optional incorporation of external camera information at test time for enhanced performance, providing flexibility and robustness for real-world deployment.

60e4c69b0472b6f93bca393133801b912afcc414.title: Variational Bayesian Pseudo-Coreset
60e4c69b0472b6f93bca393133801b912afcc414.research_question: How can Bayesian Neural Networks be made more computationally and memory efficient for large-scale datasets, while maintaining or improving predictive performance and uncertainty estimation, through the use of pseudo-coresets?
60e4c69b0472b6f93bca393133801b912afcc414.hypothesis: Utilizing variational inference, specifically last-layer variational inference, to learn pseudo-coresets will enable efficient approximation of the posterior distribution in Bayesian Neural Networks, reducing memory and computational costs while improving predictive accuracy and uncertainty estimation compared to existing Bayesian pseudo-coreset methods.
60e4c69b0472b6f93bca393133801b912afcc414.proposed_method: A novel framework, Variational Bayesian Pseudo-Coreset (VBPC), is proposed for learning a small synthetic dataset (pseudo-coreset) that approximates the posterior distribution of Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) using variational inference. The method formulates the coreset learning as a bilevel optimization problem, where the inner problem solves a variational inference objective on the pseudo-coreset and the outer problem matches the variational posterior to that of the full dataset. To ensure computational tractability, last-layer variational inference is employed, treating only the final linear layer as random and the rest as deterministic, with Gaussian priors and variational posteriors. The approach leverages closed-form solutions for the inner optimization by using a Gaussian likelihood for the pseudo-coreset, enabling efficient gradient computation and memory savings. Additionally, a model pool strategy is incorporated to prevent overfitting the pseudo-coreset to a single feature extractor, and memory-efficient techniques are developed for both training and Bayesian model averaging inference.
60e4c69b0472b6f93bca393133801b912afcc414.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several benchmark image classification datasets, including MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and Tiny-ImageNet, with varying numbers of pseudo-coresets per class (ipc). The proposed VBPC method will be compared against multiple Bayesian pseudo-coreset baselines (BPC-rKL, BPC-fKL, FBPC, BPC-CD) and dataset distillation methods (FRePo, RCIG). Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy (ACC) and negative log-likelihood (NLL), with additional assessments on robustness to out-of-distribution data (using CIFAR10-C) and generalization to different neural network architectures and normalization layers. Ablation studies will analyze memory and computational efficiency, as well as the impact of hyperparameters and model pool strategies. All experiments will use a consistent base architecture (three-layer convolutional network with BatchNorm) unless otherwise specified.
60e4c69b0472b6f93bca393133801b912afcc414.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a variational inference-based pseudo-coreset learning approach that enables closed-form solutions for the inner optimization, eliminating the need for stop-gradient tricks and iterative weight sampling. Memory-efficient algorithms are developed for both training and inference, reducing space and computational complexity from quadratic or cubic in feature dimension to quadratic in the number of pseudo-coresets. The use of a model pool during training addresses overfitting and enhances generalization across architectures. Empirical results demonstrate superior predictive performance and uncertainty estimation, as well as improved robustness to distribution shifts, compared to existing Bayesian pseudo-coreset and dataset distillation methods.

60ee030773ba1b68eb222a265b052ca028353362.title: GIT: A Generative Image-to-text Transformer for Vision and Language
60ee030773ba1b68eb222a265b052ca028353362.research_question: How can a unified, scalable, and simplified generative vision-language model be developed to address a wide range of vision-language tasks, such as image/video captioning, visual question answering, image classification, and scene text recognition, without reliance on complex architectures or external modules?
60ee030773ba1b68eb222a265b052ca028353362.hypothesis: A generative transformer model with a single image encoder and a single text decoder, pre-trained on large-scale image-text pairs using a language modeling objective, can achieve or surpass state-of-the-art performance on diverse vision-language tasks, even without external modules such as object detectors or OCR engines.
60ee030773ba1b68eb222a265b052ca028353362.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a Generative Image-to-text Transformer (GIT) consisting of a single image encoder and a single text decoder. The image encoder is a Swin-like vision transformer pre-trained on massive image-text pairs using a contrastive loss, producing compact 2D feature maps that are projected into a shared embedding space. The text decoder is a transformer network that receives concatenated image features and text embeddings, and generates output text in an auto-regressive manner using a seq2seq attention mask, allowing each text token to attend to all image tokens and preceding text tokens. Pre-training is performed on 0.8 billion image-text pairs with a language modeling loss, and the model is fine-tuned for downstream tasks such as captioning, VQA, video tasks (by encoding multiple sampled frames with temporal embeddings), image classification (by generating class names), and scene text recognition. The architecture is designed to avoid reliance on object detectors, OCR, or pre-defined answer vocabularies, and supports both image and video modalities with minimal changes.
60ee030773ba1b68eb222a265b052ca028353362.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a comprehensive suite of benchmarks, including image captioning (COCO, Flickr30K, nocaps, TextCaps, VizWiz-Captions), visual question answering (VQAv2, TextVQA, VizWiz-VQA, ST-VQA, OCR-VQA), video captioning (MSVD, MSRVTT, VATEX, TVC), video QA (MSVD-QA, MSRVTT-QA, TGIF-Frame), image classification (ImageNet-1k), and scene text recognition (ICDAR 2013/2015, IIIT5K, SVT, SVTP, CUTE80, MJSynth, SynthText). Baselines will include state-of-the-art models such as CoCa, Flamingo, Florence, SimVLM, and others, with evaluation metrics like CIDEr, accuracy, and ANLS. The model will be pre-trained on 0.8B image-text pairs from datasets such as COCO, CC3M, CC12M, SBU, Visual Genome, ALT200M, and additional web data. Ablation studies will explore the impact of model/data scaling, attention mechanisms, and fine-tuning strategies. Few-shot and zero-shot settings will be evaluated, and the model's performance will be compared in both open- and closed-vocabulary scenarios.
