60ee030773ba1b68eb222a265b052ca028353362.novelty_claims: The proposed method claims novelty in unifying vision-language tasks with a single, simple architecture—one image encoder and one text decoder—trained end-to-end with a language modeling objective. It eliminates the need for external modules like object detectors, taggers, or OCR, and supports both image and video modalities without task-specific encoders. The approach introduces a generation-based scheme for image classification and scene text recognition, allowing open-vocabulary prediction and continual learning without modifying the model architecture. The model is designed to scale efficiently with both data and model size, and aims to establish new state-of-the-art results across a wide range of benchmarks, including surpassing human performance on challenging datasets such as TextCaps.

60eef3b81e50bbd1582bb24fc173f7d93552bb53.title: Learning Mixtures of Gaussians Using the DDPM Objective
60eef3b81e50bbd1582bb24fc173f7d93552bb53.research_question: Under what conditions can gradient-based optimization of the denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) objective efficiently and provably learn the parameters of Gaussian mixture models, and what are the theoretical connections between score-based methods, EM, and spectral approaches in this context?
60eef3b81e50bbd1582bb24fc173f7d93552bb53.hypothesis: Gradient descent on the DDPM objective can efficiently recover the ground truth parameters of mixtures of spherical Gaussians under appropriate initialization and separation conditions, leveraging connections to both EM and spectral methods.
60eef3b81e50bbd1582bb24fc173f7d93552bb53.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops a gradient descent algorithm for learning the parameters of mixtures of spherical Gaussians by directly optimizing the DDPM objective, which is a score-matching loss. For mixtures of two Gaussians, the method employs a two-stage procedure: first, gradient descent is run at a high noise level (large t) from random initialization, where the dynamics resemble power iteration and align the parameter estimate with the true direction. Second, the output is used as a warm start for further gradient descent at a low noise level (small t), where the updates closely mimic the EM algorithm and rapidly converge to the true parameters. For mixtures with more than two components (K > 2), the method generalizes by utilizing a warm start and running gradient descent at low noise, leveraging analogous theoretical guarantees from EM literature. The student network architecture is chosen to match the form of the optimal score function for mixtures of Gaussians, using a two-layer neural network with tanh activation for K=2, and a weighted sum for general K.
60eef3b81e50bbd1582bb24fc173f7d93552bb53.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic datasets generated from mixtures of spherical Gaussians in d-dimensional space, varying the number of components K, the separation between centers, and the dimensionality d. The proposed method will be compared against established baselines such as the EM algorithm and spectral methods, with evaluation metrics including parameter recovery error (Euclidean distance to ground truth centers), convergence rate, and sample complexity. Both random initialization and warm-start scenarios will be tested, and the influence of noise scale (t) and initialization quality will be systematically studied. Theoretical guarantees will be validated empirically by measuring the probability of successful recovery under specified separation and initialization conditions.
60eef3b81e50bbd1582bb24fc173f7d93552bb53.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first provably efficient gradient-based algorithm for learning mixtures of Gaussians via the DDPM objective, bridging the gap between practical score-based generative modeling and theoretical guarantees for parameter recovery. A novel analysis establishes explicit connections between score-based diffusion methods, EM, and spectral (power iteration) approaches, showing that gradient descent on the DDPM objective transitions between these regimes depending on the noise level. The method achieves polynomial time and sample complexity in relevant parameters and provides optimal or near-optimal statistical rates under certain conditions. The approach is practical, aligns with empirically successful generative modeling techniques, and extends theoretical understanding of when and how score estimation can be provably implemented for fundamental distribution families.

611397e8cb8184a3c29cf0e06a168bb01e45789a.title: Balancing Preservation and Modification: A Region and Semantic Aware Metric for Instruction-Based Image Editing
611397e8cb8184a3c29cf0e06a168bb01e45789a.research_question: How can the quality of instruction-based image editing be comprehensively and reliably evaluated, accounting for both the faithful modification of relevant regions and the preservation of irrelevant content, in a manner that aligns closely with human judgment and is scalable for large-scale benchmarking?
611397e8cb8184a3c29cf0e06a168bb01e45789a.hypothesis: A region and semantic-aware evaluation metric that explicitly disentangles editing-relevant and irrelevant regions, and separately assesses modification compliance and content preservation, will provide a more comprehensive, interpretable, and human-aligned assessment of instruction-based image editing quality than existing metrics.
611397e8cb8184a3c29cf0e06a168bb01e45789a.proposed_method: A novel evaluation metric, Balancing Preservation and Modification (BPM), will be developed for instruction-based image editing. The method first parses the editing instruction using a large language model (LLM) to identify the source and target objects, as well as required changes in size and position. Detection and segmentation tools are then used to localize editing-relevant regions in both the original and edited images. A two-tier evaluation process is conducted: the Region-Aware Judge verifies alignment of the edited region's size and position with the instruction, while the Semantic-Aware Judge assesses semantic compliance within the edited region (using directional CLIP similarity) and content preservation in irrelevant regions (using L2 distance). The final BPM score is computed as a weighted combination of semantic and region-aware scores, providing a comprehensive and interpretable evaluation.
611397e8cb8184a3c29cf0e06a168bb01e45789a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on diverse instruction-based image editing datasets, including MagicBrush for local edits and PIE-Bench for global edits, covering a variety of editing types such as object addition, replacement, action change, color change, object removal, and pattern change. Edited images will be generated using advanced editing models such as IP2P, MGIE, DALLE-2, and FTIP2P. The proposed metric will be compared against existing baselines, including preservation metrics (L2, LPIPS, CLIP-I, DINOScore), modification metrics (CLIPScore), VLM-based metrics (GPT-4o), and combined metrics (CLIPScore+CLIP-I). Evaluation will include both human alignment tests (correlation between metric and human preference rankings) and ground truth tests (ability to favor well-edited images over excessively preserved or modified ones). Additional ablation studies will assess the contribution of each component and the impact of region localization on editing quality.
611397e8cb8184a3c29cf0e06a168bb01e45789a.novelty_claims: The proposed metric introduces explicit disentanglement of editing-relevant and irrelevant regions for separate evaluation, enabling nuanced assessment of both modification and preservation in instruction-based image editing. The two-tier evaluation framework (region-aware and semantic-aware) provides comprehensive and interpretable quality scores. Integration of LLM-based instruction parsing and region localization further enhances the reliability and applicability of the metric. Additionally, the region localization process can be used to guide editing models, improving editing quality by focusing modifications on relevant regions and reducing unnecessary changes elsewhere. The metric is claimed to achieve higher alignment with human evaluation and greater practical scalability than existing approaches.

6115a34ad9dd868fe886df815071023fd432e7a1.title: Decomposing NeRF for Editing via Feature Field Distillation
6115a34ad9dd868fe886df815071023fd432e7a1.research_question: How can neural radiance field (NeRF) scene representations be decomposed semantically to enable flexible, query-based, and local editing of 3D scenes without requiring costly manual annotations or retraining?
6115a34ad9dd868fe886df815071023fd432e7a1.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that distilling the knowledge from powerful 2D image feature extractors into a 3D feature field, optimized alongside a NeRF, will enable semantic decomposition and selective editing of 3D scenes in a query-driven and annotation-free manner.
6115a34ad9dd868fe886df815071023fd432e7a1.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that jointly optimizes a neural radiance field (NeRF) and a scene-specific 3D feature field via teacher-student distillation. The 3D feature field will be trained to match the semantic features of 2D image encoders (such as CLIP-LSeg or DINO) at each 3D coordinate, using volumetric rendering to supervise the feature field with multi-view image features. The feature field will support open-set, query-based selection by allowing users to specify target regions via text, image patches, or point-and-click, leveraging the semantic space of the teacher models. Once trained, the feature field will enable semantic selection and editing of regions in the NeRF, supporting appearance and geometry modifications that are consistent across views.
6115a34ad9dd868fe886df815071023fd432e7a1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on real-world NeRF scenes, using two types of pre-trained teacher networks: LSeg (a CLIP-inspired language-driven semantic segmentation model) and DINO (a self-supervised model capturing object boundaries and correspondences). The method will be quantitatively evaluated on 3D segmentation accuracy using label queries, comparing against a supervised point-cloud segmentation baseline trained on the ScanNet dataset. Qualitative experiments will demonstrate a range of local edits (appearance and geometry) enabled by text, image, pixel, or cluster queries, with no manual segmentation annotations. Evaluation metrics will include segmentation accuracy, editability, and visual consistency of edited scenes.
6115a34ad9dd868fe886df815071023fd432e7a1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the concept of distilling 2D foundation model features into a 3D feature field for NeRFs, enabling open-set, query-based semantic decomposition and editing without retraining or manual annotations. This method leverages recent advances in vision-language models and self-supervised learning to transfer semantic understanding from 2D to 3D, supporting flexible, multi-modal queries for local scene editing. The framework achieves multi-view consistent edits and demonstrates zero-shot 3D segmentation capabilities, representing a significant advance in editable neural scene representations.

6116f4ce4ec1b3cda988e7b289eda6daea75f479.title: ManiSkill3: GPU Parallelized Robotics Simulation and Rendering for Generalizable Embodied AI
6116f4ce4ec1b3cda988e7b289eda6daea75f479.research_question: How can a GPU-parallelized simulation and rendering framework be developed to enable scalable, generalizable, and efficient embodied AI for robotic manipulation across diverse tasks and environments?
6116f4ce4ec1b3cda988e7b289eda6daea75f479.hypothesis: A unified, GPU-parallelized simulation and rendering framework with support for heterogeneous environments, efficient memory usage, and a simple API will significantly accelerate robot learning, improve generalization across tasks, and facilitate sim2real and real2sim transfer for embodied AI.
6116f4ce4ec1b3cda988e7b289eda6daea75f479.proposed_method: A new simulation framework, ManiSkill3, will be developed to support state-visual GPU-parallelized robotics simulation with contact-rich physics. The framework will enable GPU parallelization of simulation and rendering, support heterogeneous environments (where each parallel environment can have different scenes, objects, and robots), and provide a user-friendly, object-oriented API for task and robot creation. The system will leverage the SAPIEN rendering engine for efficient rasterization, maintain low GPU memory usage, and include tooling for domain randomization, trajectory replay, and controller conversion. A scalable dataset generation pipeline will be implemented, utilizing motion planning, RL, and teleoperation to collect millions of demonstration frames. The framework will also integrate a VR teleoperation system for immersive data collection and support digital twins for sim2real and real2sim evaluation.
6116f4ce4ec1b3cda988e7b289eda6daea75f479.experiment_details: Experiments will benchmark simulation and rendering speed, GPU memory usage, and learning efficiency across a comprehensive suite of 12 task categories and 20+ robot embodiments. RL algorithms (PPO, SAC, TD-MPC2) and imitation learning baselines (Behavior Cloning, Diffusion Policy, Action Chunking Transformer, PerACT) will be evaluated using both state and vision-based observations. Datasets will include large-scale demonstrations generated via motion planning, RL, and teleoperation. Evaluation metrics will include training wall-clock time, sample efficiency, real-world sim2real transfer success rates, and correlation between simulation and real-world performance. Baselines will include existing simulators such as Isaac Lab, Brax, Robocasa, AI2-THOR, and OmniGibson, with comparisons on GPU memory usage, rendering speed, and task diversity. Real-world experiments will deploy policies trained in simulation directly to physical robots (e.g., Koch arm) to assess sim2real transfer.
6116f4ce4ec1b3cda988e7b289eda6daea75f479.novelty_claims: The proposed framework will be the first open-source, general-purpose robotics simulator to support fully GPU-parallelized simulation and rendering with heterogeneous environments, enabling efficient training of visual RL policies at unprecedented speed and scale. It will provide the most comprehensive range of out-of-the-box environments and robot embodiments, support scalable dataset generation from few demonstrations, and offer a unified, object-oriented API for extensibility. The system will demonstrate superior GPU memory efficiency and training acceleration compared to existing simulators, and will enable reliable sim2real and real2sim transfer for manipulation tasks. Additionally, the integration of an immersive VR teleoperation system and digital twins for evaluation will democratize access to scalable robot learning and facilitate reproducible research.

61326b7f5ff4f574ce470217b4d6502c629191dc.title: AttentionViz: A Global View of Transformer Attention
61326b7f5ff4f574ce470217b4d6502c629191dc.research_question: How can global patterns in transformer self-attention mechanisms be effectively visualized and explored across multiple input sequences and modalities to improve interpretability, model debugging, and hypothesis generation?
61326b7f5ff4f574ce470217b4d6502c629191dc.hypothesis: A joint embedding visualization of query and key vectors from transformer attention heads enables the discovery and analysis of global attention patterns, semantic and positional trends, and anomalies across both language and vision models, thereby facilitating deeper understanding and more effective model analysis.
61326b7f5ff4f574ce470217b4d6502c629191dc.proposed_method: A novel visualization framework will be developed that constructs a joint embedding space for the query and key vectors produced by each attention head in a transformer model. High-dimensional query and key vectors will be projected into a shared low-dimensional space using dimensionality reduction techniques such as t-SNE, UMAP, or PCA, after applying normalization steps (centroid alignment and scaling) to enhance interpretability and preserve the relationship between distance and attention weights. The system will provide interactive, multi-scale visualizations (Matrix View for global head comparison, Single View for detailed head analysis, and Sentence/Image View for instance-level exploration) with customizable color encodings for semantic, positional, or norm-based patterns. The tool will support both language (e.g., BERT, GPT-2) and vision (e.g., ViT) transformers, allowing users to explore attention patterns, compare heads, and identify anomalies.
61326b7f5ff4f574ce470217b4d6502c629191dc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using pre-trained transformer models: BERT and GPT-2 for language, and ViT (with 16x16 and 32x32 patch sizes) for vision. Datasets will include Wiki-Auto and SuperGLUE AX for NLP tasks, and ImageNet, MS COCO, and synthetic images for vision tasks. The visualization tool will be evaluated through application scenarios that investigate semantic, positional, and anomalous attention patterns, as well as through structured interviews with domain experts in machine learning and interpretability. Evaluation metrics will include qualitative expert feedback, the ability to surface known and novel attention patterns, and the utility of the tool for hypothesis generation, model debugging, and cross-modal analysis.
61326b7f5ff4f574ce470217b4d6502c629191dc.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first systematic method for visualizing joint query-key embeddings at scale across all attention heads and layers in both language and vision transformers. Unlike prior attention visualization techniques, this method enables global, multi-sequence, and multi-modal analysis, revealing previously inaccessible patterns such as semantic clustering, positional spirals, norm disparities, and anomalous attention behaviors. The interactive tool is model-agnostic, extensible, and supports multi-level exploration, providing a new avenue for interpretability research and practical model debugging.

6143e809cd2e9c7a18c3bc8819419fd3b02fbcf2.title: Adversarial Robust Deep Reinforcement Learning Requires Redefining Robustness
6143e809cd2e9c7a18c3bc8819419fd3b02fbcf2.research_question: How can the robustness of deep reinforcement learning policies be more effectively defined and evaluated, particularly in the presence of both policy-dependent adversarial perturbations and policy-independent high-sensitivity directions intrinsic to the environment? What are the limitations of current adversarial training methods in providing true robustness, and how do different types of perturbations affect policy performance and perceptual similarity?
6143e809cd2e9c7a18c3bc8819419fd3b02fbcf2.hypothesis: Current adversarial training methods, which focus on robustness to worst-case, policy-dependent adversarial perturbations (typically measured by norm-bounded attacks), do not provide comprehensive robustness. Policies trained with such methods may be more vulnerable to natural, policy-independent high-sensitivity directions intrinsic to the environment than those trained with standard (vanilla) methods.
6143e809cd2e9c7a18c3bc8819419fd3b02fbcf2.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed to probe the deep neural policy manifold using both policy-dependent adversarial directions (e.g., Carlini & Wagner attacks) and policy-independent high-sensitivity directions that are intrinsic to the Markov Decision Process (MDP). Policy-independent directions will include simple semantic and geometric transformations such as brightness/contrast changes, blurring, rotation, shifting, perspective transformation, and compression artifacts. The methodology will involve measuring the impact of these perturbations on policy performance and perceptual similarity using the LPIPS metric, which approximates human perceptual similarity. Both vanilla and adversarially trained policies (using state-of-the-art methods like SA-DDQN and RADIAL) will be systematically evaluated under these perturbations to assess their robustness across a broad spectrum of distributional shifts.
6143e809cd2e9c7a18c3bc8819419fd3b02fbcf2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in the Arcade Learning Environment (ALE) across multiple games with high-dimensional visual state spaces. Policies will be trained using standard DQN with Double Q-learning and prioritized experience replay, as well as with advanced adversarial training algorithms (SA-DDQN and RADIAL). For evaluation, both policy-dependent adversarial attacks and a suite of policy-independent perturbations will be applied to the agents' observations. Performance degradation will be quantified using normalized impact metrics, and perceptual similarity will be measured with LPIPS. Baselines will include vanilla-trained policies and those trained with adversarial robustness objectives. The frequency spectrum of the perturbed states will also be analyzed to characterize the types of distributional shifts each perturbation induces.
6143e809cd2e9c7a18c3bc8819419fd3b02fbcf2.novelty_claims: The proposed research redefines robustness in deep reinforcement learning by introducing and systematically evaluating policy-independent high-sensitivity directions, demonstrating that these natural perturbations can degrade policy performance as much as or more than traditional adversarial attacks. It challenges the prevailing reliance on norm-bounded adversarial robustness as a sufficient measure, showing that adversarially trained policies may be less robust to a broader class of distributional shifts than vanilla-trained policies. The research provides a detailed frequency-domain analysis of perturbations and establishes the abundance and significance of high-sensitivity directions in the policy manifold, laying the groundwork for more generalizable and truly robust deep reinforcement learning agents.

6144237fadd0c21141d23d0200cb55998cca83e5.title: Seq-VCR: Preventing Collapse in Intermediate Transformer Representations for Enhanced Reasoning
6144237fadd0c21141d23d0200cb55998cca83e5.research_question: How can the reasoning capabilities of decoder-only Transformer models be enhanced for complex multi-step tasks, such as arithmetic reasoning and dynamic programming, without relying on explicit chain-of-thought supervision?
6144237fadd0c21141d23d0200cb55998cca83e5.hypothesis: Preventing representation collapse in intermediate layers of Transformer models by increasing the diversity and entropy of internal representations will significantly improve the models' ability to perform complex reasoning tasks, especially in arithmetic and sequential decision-making domains.
6144237fadd0c21141d23d0200cb55998cca83e5.proposed_method: A novel regularization technique, Sequential Variance-Covariance Regularization (Seq-VCR), will be developed to enforce high variance and low covariance in the intermediate representations of Transformer models. Seq-VCR adapts principles from VICReg and VCReg for sequential data, applying a loss term that encourages unit variance in each dimension and penalizes covariance between different dimensions across the batch. A linear projection is inserted before the Seq-VCR loss calculation to manage computational complexity, especially with large output spaces. Additionally, dummy pause tokens will be introduced into the input sequence to simulate the computational benefits of chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, but without requiring explicit intermediate supervision. The overall training objective will combine standard next-token prediction loss with the Seq-VCR regularization loss, promoting both accurate prediction and diverse intermediate representations.
6144237fadd0c21141d23d0200cb55998cca83e5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three tasks: multi-digit multiplication (4x4 and 5x5) from the BIG-bench benchmark, arithmetic expression evaluation, and the Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS) dynamic programming problem. Datasets will be generated or sourced as appropriate for each task, with input, CoT, and output token details carefully controlled. Two model types will be used: fine-tuning a pre-trained GPT-2 Small and training a minGPT model from scratch. Five configurations will be compared: Vanilla (no CoT or pause tokens), With CoT, Pause tokens, Seq-VCR, and Seq-VCR+Pause. Evaluation metrics will include exact match accuracy for arithmetic tasks and LIS, as well as representation entropy across layers to assess diversity. Baselines will include state-of-the-art LLMs such as GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 with and without CoT prompting, and all experiments will be run with multiple seeds and varying model depths and pause token counts for ablation.
6144237fadd0c21141d23d0200cb55998cca83e5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach identifies and directly addresses representation collapse in intermediate Transformer layers as a key limitation for reasoning tasks. Seq-VCR introduces a new form of regularization specifically adapted for sequential data in language models, extending ideas from vision-based regularization to NLP. The combination of Seq-VCR with dummy pause tokens enables high performance on complex reasoning tasks without the need for explicit chain-of-thought supervision, achieving results that surpass existing baselines and even large LLMs with CoT prompting. This framework offers a scalable, supervision-light solution to enhance Transformer reasoning capabilities.

615d80aeae843ec23155ae67ce873452d1244cb9.title: DelTA: An Online Document-Level Translation Agent Based on Multi-Level Memory
615d80aeae843ec23155ae67ce873452d1244cb9.research_question: How can document-level machine translation systems based on large language models be improved to address challenges of translation consistency, accuracy, and memory efficiency when processing entire documents, especially with respect to proper noun consistency, pronoun resolution, and context-dependent translation?
615d80aeae843ec23155ae67ce873452d1244cb9.hypothesis: Employing a multi-level memory architecture that stores and retrieves document-level information at various granularities, combined with an online, sentence-by-sentence translation strategy, will significantly improve translation consistency, accuracy, and memory efficiency for document-level machine translation using large language models.
615d80aeae843ec23155ae67ce873452d1244cb9.proposed_method: A novel document-level translation agent, DELTA, will be developed, featuring a multi-level memory structure comprising Proper Noun Records, Bilingual Summary, Long-Term Memory, and Short-Term Memory. The agent will translate documents in an online, sentence-by-sentence fashion, updating and retrieving information from these memory components in real time. Proper Noun Records will ensure consistent translation of proper nouns by maintaining a dictionary of their initial translations. Bilingual Summaries will be generated and updated periodically to capture the main content, style, and tone of both source and target documents, aiding coherence and fluency. Long-Term and Short-Term Memory modules will store contextual sentence pairs at different spans, with relevant context retrieved for each translation step using LLM-based retrievers. All memory information will be integrated into the LLM translation prompt, and after each translation, memory components will be updated using auxiliary LLM-based extractors and writers.
615d80aeae843ec23155ae67ce873452d1244cb9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two document-level translation datasets: IWSLT2017 (TED talks, covering eight language pairs such as En⇔Zh, De, Fr, Ja) and Guofeng Webnovel (Chinese-to-English web fiction). Four LLMs will be evaluated as backbones: GPT-3.5-Turbo-0125, GPT-4o-mini, Qwen2-7B-Instruct, and Qwen2-72B-Instruct. Baseline methods will include sentence-level translation, context-aware translation (with three previous source-target pairs), and a Doc2Doc approach translating multiple sentences per window. Evaluation metrics will include LTCR-1 and LTCR-1f for proper noun consistency, sCOMET and dCOMET for translation quality, as well as pronoun translation accuracy (APT) and context-dependent translation accuracy. Memory efficiency will be assessed by measuring GPU memory consumption during translation. Additional ablation studies will isolate the effects of each memory component.
615d80aeae843ec23155ae67ce873452d1244cb9.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a multi-level memory architecture for document-level machine translation, integrating proper noun tracking, bilingual summarization, and both short- and long-term context retrieval in a unified agent. This framework enables consistent and accurate sentence-by-sentence translation, reducing omissions and improving alignment. The method is claimed to outperform strong baselines in translation consistency and quality, especially for proper noun and pronoun translation, and demonstrates superior memory efficiency compared to Doc2Doc methods. The bilingual summary component is also positioned as a promising tool for query-based summarization tasks.

6178a6b71ce5846104970819321d58a4e1e6759d.title: MLPInit: Embarrassingly Simple GNN Training Acceleration with MLP Initialization
6178a6b71ce5846104970819321d58a4e1e6759d.research_question: Can the training efficiency and predictive performance of graph neural networks (GNNs) on large-scale graphs be improved by leveraging the weight space relationship between GNNs and multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs)?
6178a6b71ce5846104970819321d58a4e1e6759d.hypothesis: Initializing GNNs with the weights of a fully trained, structurally matched MLP (PeerMLP) will significantly accelerate GNN training and may also improve predictive performance compared to conventional random initialization.
6178a6b71ce5846104970819321d58a4e1e6759d.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces a two-phase training scheme called MLPInit. First, a PeerMLP is constructed to match the architecture and weight space of the target GNN, ensuring identical layer dimensions and parameter shapes. The PeerMLP is trained using only node features (ignoring graph structure) until convergence, which is computationally efficient due to the absence of sparse neighbor aggregation. Upon convergence, the optimal weights from the PeerMLP are used to initialize the target GNN. The GNN is then fine-tuned using both node features and adjacency information for a reduced number of epochs. This approach is designed to exploit the faster training dynamics of MLPs and transfer their learned representations to accelerate and potentially enhance GNN optimization.
6178a6b71ce5846104970819321d58a4e1e6759d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of large-scale node classification and link prediction benchmarks, including Flickr, Yelp, Reddit, Reddit2, A-products, OGB-arXiv, and OGB-products for node classification, and Cora, CiteSeer, PubMed, CoraFull, CS, Physics, A-Photo, and A-Computers for link prediction. Multiple GNN architectures such as GCN, GraphSAGE, GraphSAINT, and ClusterGCN will be evaluated. Baselines will include GNNs with standard random initialization and MLP-based acceleration methods. Evaluation metrics will comprise accuracy for classification and AUC, AP, and Hits@K for link prediction. The primary experimental setup will compare training epochs to convergence, total training time, and final predictive performance between MLPInit and conventional initialization, with results averaged over multiple runs to assess robustness and sensitivity to hyperparameters.
6178a6b71ce5846104970819321d58a4e1e6759d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach pioneers the use of weight transfer from a converged PeerMLP to initialize GNNs, leveraging the shared weight space between MLPs and message-passing GNNs. This method is claimed to be embarrassingly simple, easy to implement, and orthogonal to existing GNN acceleration and pre-training techniques. It offers substantial training speedup (up to 33× in some cases) with negligible computational overhead and often leads to improved predictive performance and robustness. Additionally, the approach is shown to make GNN training less sensitive to hyperparameter choices and to facilitate convergence to broader low-loss regions in the optimization landscape.

618d916306c7c5992d6c191935b4bc5e1f1b7b57.title: Fast, Expressive SE(n) Equivariant Networks through Weight-Sharing in Position-Orientation Space
618d916306c7c5992d6c191935b4bc5e1f1b7b57.research_question: How can neural networks be constructed to efficiently and expressively process 3D point clouds while maintaining equivariance to the SE(n) group, and what is the optimal approach to weight sharing and message passing in position-orientation space for such networks?
618d916306c7c5992d6c191935b4bc5e1f1b7b57.hypothesis: Conditioning message passing and convolutional kernels on bijective, group-theoretically derived invariant attributes of point pairs in position-orientation space enables efficient, expressive, and fully SE(n)-equivariant neural networks that outperform existing methods in both accuracy and computational efficiency.
618d916306c7c5992d6c191935b4bc5e1f1b7b57.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed for constructing SE(n)-equivariant neural networks by formalizing weight sharing as the sharing of message functions over equivalence classes of point pairs, defined via group actions on homogeneous spaces. Bijective invariant attributes are derived to uniquely identify these equivalence classes, ensuring both invariance and expressivity. The core architecture operates on feature maps defined over position-orientation space (R^3 × S^2), using a separable group convolution that decomposes into spatial, spherical, and channel mixing components. Kernels are parameterized by MLPs conditioned on the derived attributes, and the architecture is implemented in a fully convolutional, ConvNeXt-style stack, with specialized modules for embedding and readout between scalar/vector fields and spherical signals.
618d916306c7c5992d6c191935b4bc5e1f1b7b57.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a variety of benchmarks: (1) interatomic potential energy and force prediction using the rMD17 dataset of molecular dynamics trajectories, where the model predicts energies and computes forces as gradients; (2) molecular generation via equivariant diffusion models trained on the QM9 dataset, with joint diffusion over coordinates and atom types; (3) trajectory forecasting in N-body systems, using initial positions, velocities, and charges as input and predicting future positions. Baselines include state-of-the-art equivariant models such as SchNet, DimeNet, GemNet, NequIP, Allegro, MACE, EGNN, SE(3)-Transformers, and others. Evaluation metrics include mean absolute error (MAE) for energies and forces, negative log-likelihood (NLL), atom and molecule stability for generation, and mean squared error (MSE) for trajectory prediction. Computational efficiency is assessed via training time per epoch, and ablation is performed by comparing position-only and position-orientation feature spaces.
618d916306c7c5992d6c191935b4bc5e1f1b7b57.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a principled, group-theoretic approach to weight sharing in equivariant neural networks by deriving optimal invariant attributes for message passing and convolution. It establishes that conditioning on these attributes is sufficient for universal approximation in SE(n)-equivariant settings. The architecture achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and speed across multiple 2D and 3D benchmarks, surpassing both tensor field and invariant message passing methods, while offering a simpler and more general-purpose convolutional design that does not require specialized representation theory or intricate module wiring.

61b44738b4f3095f65436c9e6c1647366ba03aac.title: DPOT: Auto-Regressive Denoising Operator Transformer for Large-Scale PDE Pre-Training
61b44738b4f3095f65436c9e6c1647366ba03aac.research_question: How can a flexible, scalable, and robust pre-training framework for neural operators be developed to efficiently learn from large-scale, heterogeneous PDE datasets and generalize to diverse downstream operator learning tasks, especially in data-scarce or high-complexity scenarios?
61b44738b4f3095f65436c9e6c1647366ba03aac.hypothesis: An auto-regressive denoising pre-training strategy, combined with a scalable transformer architecture leveraging Fourier-based attention, will enable neural operators to robustly learn from massive, diverse PDE datasets and significantly improve generalization and performance on a wide range of downstream PDE tasks.
61b44738b4f3095f65436c9e6c1647366ba03aac.proposed_method: A novel auto-regressive denoising pre-training approach will be developed, where Gaussian noise is injected into temporal PDE data and the model is trained to predict the next timestep from noisy previous frames. This regularizes the model and enhances robustness for long trajectory prediction. The core architecture will be a transformer backbone with Fourier-based attention layers, utilizing nonlinear learnable transforms in the frequency domain to efficiently approximate kernel integral transforms for PDE solution mapping. Data preprocessing will unify spatial and channel dimensions across datasets via up/down-sampling and padding, and a balanced sampling strategy will ensure equitable representation of all PDE types during training. The model will be designed for scalability, allowing parameter counts from millions to over a billion, and will include temporal aggregation and multi-head Fourier attention layers for efficient spatiotemporal feature extraction.
61b44738b4f3095f65436c9e6c1647366ba03aac.experiment_details: Experiments will involve pre-training on a collection of over 100,000 trajectories from more than 10 diverse PDE datasets, including sources such as FNO, PDEBench, PDEArena, and CFDBench, covering equations like Navier-Stokes, diffusion-reaction, and shallow-water equations. The pre-trained model will be evaluated on multiple challenging benchmarks (e.g., PDEBench, PDEArena, CFDBench) using relative L2 error as the primary metric. Comparisons will be made against state-of-the-art baselines such as FNO, FFNO, UNet, various transformer-based neural operators, and recent large-scale pre-training approaches (e.g., MPP-AViT, FNO-m). Fine-tuning experiments will be conducted on downstream tasks, including high-resolution turbulence, 3D Navier-Stokes, and steady-state PDEs, to assess transferability and generalization. Ablation studies will examine the effects of noise injection, model size, number of attention heads, and patch size on performance.
61b44738b4f3095f65436c9e6c1647366ba03aac.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first scalable auto-regressive denoising pre-training strategy specifically designed for neural operator learning on large and diverse PDE datasets. The transformer architecture with Fourier-based attention enables efficient and expressive learning of spatiotemporal PDE dynamics, and the framework supports scaling to over a billion parameters. The method is claimed to achieve state-of-the-art results across multiple PDE benchmarks, demonstrating superior generalization, transferability to unseen tasks (including 3D and high-resolution data), and improved parameter efficiency compared to existing neural operator and transformer-based models.

61be5b2d4b73cde6b11a8b988aea95c22364c86e.title: STaR-GATE: Teaching Language Models to Ask Clarifying Questions
61be5b2d4b73cde6b11a8b988aea95c22364c86e.research_question: Can language models be improved to more effectively elicit user preferences and resolve task ambiguity by learning to ask clarifying questions, thereby generating more personalized and higher-quality responses across diverse tasks?
61be5b2d4b73cde6b11a8b988aea95c22364c86e.hypothesis: Iterative self-improvement of language models through supervised fine-tuning on simulated conversations that maximize the likelihood of high-quality, persona-specific responses will enhance the model's ability to ask effective clarifying questions and generate personalized answers.
61be5b2d4b73cde6b11a8b988aea95c22364c86e.proposed_method: A novel iterative training framework, STaR-GATE, will be developed to enhance a language model's ability to ask clarifying questions. The approach begins with the generation of a large synthetic dataset of persona-task pairs, where each persona represents a unique set of user preferences. For each task-persona pair, simulated conversations are generated between a Questioner (the model being trained) and a Roleplayer (simulating the user), with the Questioner eliciting information through questions. An Oracle model, with access to the full persona, provides gold-standard responses. The Questioner is fine-tuned iteratively on conversations that maximize the log-probability of generating these gold responses, with regularization to ensure the model retains its ability to generate high-quality answers and not just questions. The method alternates between task and persona splits to ensure generalization and prevent overfitting, and incorporates response regularization by sampling responses from previous model iterations.
61be5b2d4b73cde6b11a8b988aea95c22364c86e.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize a synthetic dataset comprising 25,500 unique persona-task-response triples, derived from open-domain human-assistant prompt datasets and GPT-4-generated personas. The Questioner will be instantiated as mistral-7b-instruct, the Roleplayer as mixtral-8x7b-instruct, and the Oracle as GPT-4. Evaluation will be conducted on held-out task and persona splits, measuring both the log-probability of gold responses and win rates in head-to-head response comparisons judged by GPT-4. Baselines will include models without elicited information, models with random persona information, and ablations such as fine-tuning on questions only or on gold responses. Additional robustness experiments will test generalization to different Roleplayer models and the feasibility of using weaker or self-oracle models.
61be5b2d4b73cde6b11a8b988aea95c22364c86e.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a new algorithm that combines active preference elicitation with iterative self-improvement, enabling language models to learn to ask more effective clarifying questions. The approach leverages a synthetic dataset and a novel reward function based on the probability of generating gold-standard, persona-specific responses. Regularization techniques are incorporated to maintain response quality and prevent the model from forgetting how to answer while optimizing for question-asking. The method is demonstrated to generalize across different user personas and Roleplayer models, and ablation studies highlight the importance of joint fine-tuning on questions and responses. This work represents a significant step toward teaching language models to proactively resolve ambiguity and personalize their outputs through dialog.

61e46884567be7cad12e999365b16a8d3414b678.title: Diffusion Posterior Sampling for General Noisy Inverse Problems
61e46884567be7cad12e999365b16a8d3414b678.research_question: How can a general and efficient framework be developed for solving noisy (including both linear and nonlinear) inverse problems in imaging, particularly under various measurement noise models such as Gaussian and Poisson, without relying on restrictive assumptions or computationally expensive operations?
61e46884567be7cad12e999365b16a8d3414b678.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a diffusion model-based posterior sampling framework, which approximates the posterior distribution via tractable surrogate likelihoods and avoids explicit projections or SVD computations, can efficiently and accurately solve a wide range of noisy linear and nonlinear inverse problems across diverse noise models.
61e46884567be7cad12e999365b16a8d3414b678.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that leverages score-based diffusion models to approximate posterior sampling for general noisy inverse problems. The method constructs a tractable surrogate for the intractable likelihood term by approximating the expectation over the posterior of the clean signal, using Tweedie's formula to estimate the posterior mean at each diffusion step. The approach incorporates the measurement model directly into the diffusion process by combining the learned score function with the gradient of the log-likelihood, which is analytically tractable for common noise models (e.g., Gaussian, Poisson). The resulting update rule blends diffusion sampling with a manifold-constrained gradient step, without requiring strict measurement consistency projections or SVD computations. The method is fully general and can be applied to both linear and nonlinear measurement operators, with gradients computed via automatic differentiation.
61e46884567be7cad12e999365b16a8d3414b678.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image datasets such as FFHQ (256x256) and ImageNet (256x256), using 1,000 validation images per dataset. The evaluation will cover a diverse set of inverse problems, including inpainting (box and random masks), super-resolution, Gaussian/motion/non-uniform deblurring, Fourier phase retrieval, and nonlinear deblurring, under both Gaussian and Poisson noise models. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art methods such as DDRM, MCG, PnP-ADMM, Score-SDE (ILVR), ADMM-TV, as well as classical phase retrieval and deblurring algorithms. Evaluation metrics will focus on perceptual quality (FID, LPIPS), with additional reporting of PSNR and SSIM. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by using the same pre-trained diffusion models across methods, and will test the method's ability to handle both linear and nonlinear, as well as signal-dependent and independent, noise.
61e46884567be7cad12e999365b16a8d3414b678.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a general and efficient diffusion posterior sampling (DPS) framework that handles both linear and nonlinear noisy inverse problems without requiring SVD computations or restrictive projection steps. It provides a unified approach for incorporating various measurement noise statistics (including Gaussian and Poisson) directly into the diffusion process. The method is capable of handling complex nonlinear measurement operators via automatic differentiation, and demonstrates superior performance across a wide range of challenging inverse problems. The approach also provides a geometric interpretation that explains its robustness in noisy settings compared to previous projection-based methods.

61e5bafb567b36960a6e1584b3753d9de09b45aa.title: Evaluating the World Model Implicit in a Generative Model
61e5bafb567b36960a6e1584b3753d9de09b45aa.research_question: How can the implicit world models learned by generative sequence models be rigorously evaluated, particularly in domains where the underlying reality can be represented as a deterministic finite automaton (DFA)?
61e5bafb567b36960a6e1584b3753d9de09b45aa.hypothesis: Existing evaluation metrics for world model recovery in generative models are insufficiently sensitive to structural incoherence, and theoretically grounded metrics inspired by the Myhill-Nerode theorem will provide a more accurate and robust assessment of world model recovery.
61e5bafb567b36960a6e1584b3753d9de09b45aa.proposed_method: A new evaluation framework will be developed for assessing the implicit world models within generative sequence models, focusing on domains where the ground-truth process can be formalized as a DFA. The approach will introduce two key metrics inspired by the Myhill-Nerode theorem: a sequence compression metric, which tests whether the model recognizes that different sequences leading to the same state should admit the same continuations, and a sequence distinction metric, which tests whether the model distinguishes between sequences leading to different states by their allowed continuations. These metrics will be computed by comparing the model-implied Myhill-Nerode boundaries to the true DFA boundaries, using model-agnostic procedures based on sequence generation and acceptance thresholds. The evaluation will be designed to be applicable to any generative model with sequence-level access, and will not require access to model internals.
61e5bafb567b36960a6e1584b3753d9de09b45aa.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in three domains: navigation (using a new dataset of New York City taxi rides converted to sequences of directions), board games (Othello), and logic puzzles (seating arrangement tasks). For navigation, generative models (transformers of varying sizes) will be trained on shortest paths, noisy shortest paths, and random walks, with data split to avoid overlap between training and test origin-destination pairs. Baselines will include untrained transformers and the true world model. Evaluation metrics will include next-token prediction accuracy, current-state probing, and the proposed compression and distinction metrics. Additional robustness tests will introduce random and adversarial detours to assess model fragility. For Othello and logic puzzles, similar protocols will be used, with models trained or prompted on legal move sequences and evaluated on both traditional and proposed metrics.
61e5bafb567b36960a6e1584b3753d9de09b45aa.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces theoretically grounded, model-agnostic evaluation metrics for world model recovery in generative models, inspired by the Myhill-Nerode theorem. These metrics go beyond existing next-token and probing diagnostics by directly measuring the structural coherence of the implicit world model, revealing deficiencies that traditional metrics miss. The approach is demonstrated across diverse domains, and a new benchmark dataset and software tools for world model evaluation are provided. The framework offers a principled path toward diagnosing and improving the fidelity of world models learned by generative models.

61e721334296ebfbbf6443b5ed9eb8c83b708c95.title: Scaling Vision Transformers to 22 Billion Parameters
61e721334296ebfbbf6443b5ed9eb8c83b708c95.research_question: How can vision transformer architectures be scaled to tens of billions of parameters while maintaining efficient and stable training, and what are the resulting effects on transfer learning, robustness, fairness, and alignment with human perception across a wide range of vision tasks?
61e721334296ebfbbf6443b5ed9eb8c83b708c95.hypothesis: Scaling vision transformers to over 20 billion parameters, with appropriate architectural and training modifications, will result in improved performance, robustness, fairness, and alignment with human visual perception on a variety of downstream vision tasks compared to smaller models.
61e721334296ebfbbf6443b5ed9eb8c83b708c95.proposed_method: A 22-billion-parameter vision transformer (ViT-22B) will be developed, based on the standard Vision Transformer architecture but incorporating key modifications for efficient and stable large-scale training. The method will employ parallel application of attention and MLP blocks within each encoder layer, query/key normalization using LayerNorm before dot-product attention to prevent training instabilities, and omission of biases in QKV projections and LayerNorms to improve hardware efficiency. The model will use a patch size of 14x14 on 224x224 images, with learned 1D positional embeddings and multi-head attention pooling. Training will leverage a highly engineered infrastructure using JAX/FLAX with explicit model and data parallelism, asynchronous parallel linear operations, and parameter sharding to maximize throughput and hardware utilization.
61e721334296ebfbbf6443b5ed9eb8c83b708c95.experiment_details: Experiments will involve pretraining ViT-22B on an extended JFT dataset containing approximately 4 billion images with a hierarchical label structure, using multi-label classification and sigmoid cross-entropy loss. Downstream evaluations will include linear probing and zero-shot transfer on ImageNet and iNaturalist 2017, semantic segmentation on ADE20K, Pascal Context, and Pascal VOC, monocular depth estimation on the Waymo Open dataset, and video classification on Kinetics 400 and Moments in Time. Baselines will include smaller ViT variants (B/16, L/16, g/14, G/14, e/14), as well as other state-of-the-art models such as CLIP, ALIGN, BASIC, and CoCa. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy, mean IoU, mean squared error, absolute relative error, and standard depth estimation metrics. Experimental setups will involve both frozen feature extraction and end-to-end fine-tuning, with careful consideration of input resolutions, data augmentations, and transfer protocols.
61e721334296ebfbbf6443b5ed9eb8c83b708c95.novelty_claims: The proposed research will introduce the largest dense vision transformer to date, demonstrating for the first time the feasibility of scaling ViTs to over 20 billion parameters with efficient and stable training. Key innovations include architectural changes such as parallel attention-MLP blocks and query/key normalization, as well as highly optimized model-parallel training infrastructure. The work will provide comprehensive empirical evidence of the benefits of extreme scale in vision transformers, including improved transfer learning performance, robustness to out-of-distribution data, fairness, and unprecedented alignment with human visual perception in terms of shape/texture bias. The approach will also set new state-of-the-art results on several benchmarks and establish a scalable recipe for future large-scale vision models.

61e7a3d5606043594a8ce377870479f77a6b58c2.title: A Survey on Offline Reinforcement Learning: Taxonomy, Review, and Open Problems
61e7a3d5606043594a8ce377870479f77a6b58c2.research_question: How can offline reinforcement learning methods be systematically categorized, improved, and evaluated to address the challenges of learning effective policies from static datasets without further environment interaction, particularly in real-world applications where online data collection is costly or dangerous?
61e7a3d5606043594a8ce377870479f77a6b58c2.hypothesis: A unified taxonomy and systematic analysis of offline reinforcement learning methods will reveal key algorithmic components, highlight effective strategies for mitigating distributional shift, and identify open problems, thereby guiding the development of more robust and generalizable offline RL algorithms.
61e7a3d5606043594a8ce377870479f77a6b58c2.proposed_method: A comprehensive research program will be undertaken to develop a novel taxonomy for offline reinforcement learning (RL) methods, distinguishing between model-based, model-free, imitation learning, and trajectory optimization approaches, as well as key algorithmic modifications such as policy constraints, regularization, uncertainty estimation, and one-step methods. The methodology will involve formalizing the mathematical foundations of offline RL, analyzing the effects of distributional shift, and systematically categorizing existing and potential algorithmic strategies using unified notation. The framework will also include a critical review of loss functions, policy evaluation and improvement steps, and the integration of auxiliary components such as uncertainty quantification and conservative model learning. The proposed approach will further identify and formalize open research problems, including off-policy evaluation, reliable offline RL workflows, and adaptive conservatism in policy learning.
61e7a3d5606043594a8ce377870479f77a6b58c2.experiment_details: Experiments will be designed to evaluate representative algorithms from each class and modification type within the proposed taxonomy. Standard offline RL benchmarks such as D4RL, Atari, and robotics datasets will be used to assess algorithm performance across diverse domains and dataset properties. Baseline comparisons will include behavior cloning, standard off-policy RL, and state-of-the-art offline RL algorithms (e.g., BCQ, BEAR, BRAC, AWR). Evaluation metrics will consist of policy return, robustness to distributional shift, generalization to unseen states, and safety. The experimental setup will include ablation studies to isolate the impact of individual algorithmic modifications and cross-benchmark analyses to determine the suitability of methods for various real-world challenges.
61e7a3d5606043594a8ce377870479f77a6b58c2.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unifying taxonomy for offline RL methods, enabling systematic classification and comparison of algorithms. It provides a detailed analysis of algorithmic components and loss terms, clarifies the distinction between direct and implicit policy constraints, and integrates uncertainty estimation and regularization into the evaluation of offline RL. The work also delivers a comprehensive review of current benchmarks and identifies open problems and future research directions, equipping researchers with tools to select and design algorithms tailored to specific offline RL challenges. This structured approach is expected to accelerate progress in the field and facilitate the development of more effective offline RL solutions.

61f329722cd94291898c2c8131606a55f7a07219.title: Broken Neural Scaling Laws
61f329722cd94291898c2c8131606a55f7a07219.research_question: How can the scaling behavior of deep neural networks across diverse architectures, tasks, and settings be accurately modeled and extrapolated, particularly in cases where existing scaling law formulations fail to capture non-monotonic transitions and inflection points?
61f329722cd94291898c2c8131606a55f7a07219.hypothesis: A smoothly broken power law functional form, referred to as a broken neural scaling law (BNSL), can accurately model and extrapolate the scaling behaviors of deep neural networks across a wide range of tasks and settings, including those exhibiting non-monotonic transitions and inflection points, outperforming existing monotonic scaling law formulations.
61f329722cd94291898c2c8131606a55f7a07219.proposed_method: A novel functional form, the broken neural scaling law (BNSL), will be developed to generalize traditional power laws into a smoothly connected, piecewise (approximately) linear function on a log-log plot. The BNSL will be parameterized by a set of constants controlling the number, location, and sharpness of 'breaks' between linear segments, as well as the slopes and offsets of each segment. Model fitting will be performed using nonlinear curve fitting techniques (e.g., SciPy's curve-fitting library) to estimate the parameters from observed (x, y) scaling data, where x is a scaling variable (such as model size, compute, dataset size, etc.) and y is a performance metric. The method will be capable of expressing non-monotonic behaviors (such as double descent) and inflection points on both log-log and linear-linear plots, which are not possible with prior monotonic scaling law formulations. The expressivity of the BNSL will be mathematically analyzed, and its ability to fit and extrapolate real-world scaling behaviors will be empirically validated.
61f329722cd94291898c2c8131606a55f7a07219.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a large and diverse set of upstream and downstream tasks, including vision, language, audio, video, diffusion, generative modeling, multimodal learning, contrastive learning, AI alignment, robotics, out-of-distribution generalization, continual learning, transfer learning, uncertainty estimation, adversarial robustness, distillation, sparsity, retrieval, quantization, pruning, fairness, molecular tasks, programming/coding, math word problems, arithmetic, supervised and unsupervised learning, and reinforcement learning (both single and multi-agent). Datasets will include established benchmarks such as JFT-300M, CIFAR-100, ImageNet, Caltech101, Birds 200, BIG-Bench, and others. The BNSL will be compared against prior functional forms (M1, M2, M3, M4) using root mean squared log error (RMSLE) as the primary evaluation metric for extrapolation accuracy. Baseline models will include standard power law and modified power law formulations. Experimental setups will include zero-shot, prompted, and fine-tuned settings, and both in-distribution and out-of-distribution scenarios. Extrapolation will be evaluated by fitting models on a subset of data and testing on held-out points, including extrapolation to scales significantly larger than those seen during fitting.
61f329722cd94291898c2c8131606a55f7a07219.novelty_claims: The proposed BNSL framework introduces a highly expressive, smoothly broken power law functional form capable of modeling and extrapolating complex, non-monotonic scaling behaviors and inflection points that are mathematically inaccessible to previous monotonic scaling law formulations. The method is demonstrated to yield considerably more accurate extrapolations across a wide range of tasks and domains, including cases of double descent and sharp phase transitions. The approach provides new insights into the predictability limits of neural scaling behavior and establishes a unified, generalizable methodology for scaling law analysis in deep learning.

61f6639768e23553b5b4ba00a5e29ea3abb2e881.title: When does compositional structure yield compositional generalization? A kernel theory
61f6639768e23553b5b4ba00a5e29ea3abb2e881.research_question: Under what conditions does compositional structure in representations enable compositional generalization in machine learning models, and how do the statistical properties of training data and representational geometry affect this generalization?
61f6639768e23553b5b4ba00a5e29ea3abb2e881.hypothesis: Compositional structure in representations is not, by itself, sufficient for compositional generalization; rather, the ability of kernel-based and deep neural models to generalize compositionally depends on both the structure of the representations and the statistical properties of the training data. Furthermore, kernel models with compositionally structured representations are fundamentally limited to conjunction-wise additive computations, which restricts the class of compositional tasks they can solve.
61f6639768e23553b5b4ba00a5e29ea3abb2e881.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed to characterize compositional generalization in kernel models with fixed, compositionally structured representations. The approach will formalize the notion of compositional structure, defining representations where input similarity depends only on the overlap of underlying components. The theory will derive constraints on the class of functions such kernel models can implement, showing they are limited to conjunction-wise additive computations. Analytical results will be complemented by introducing a metric, representational salience, to quantify how strongly different conjunctions of components are encoded in a given representation. The theoretical predictions will be empirically validated by training deep neural network architectures (including convolutional networks, residual networks, and vision transformers) on compositional tasks, and comparing their behavior to the predictions of the kernel theory.
61f6639768e23553b5b4ba00a5e29ea3abb2e881.experiment_details: Experiments will use compositional tasks such as symbolic addition, context dependence, and transitive equivalence, implemented on both synthetic and naturalistic datasets. For empirical validation, datasets will include concatenations of MNIST and CIFAR-10 images, where each component corresponds to a random sample from a particular category. Training and test splits will be designed to isolate compositional generalization, including both interpolation and extrapolation regimes. Baseline models will include kernel models with compositionally structured representations and deep neural networks trained in the kernel regime. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on held-out compositional splits, linearity of model predictions relative to ground truth, and the representational salience of different conjunctions in intermediate network layers. Experimental setups will systematically vary representational geometry (e.g., by manipulating spatial distance between components in images) and training data statistics to test theoretical predictions about memorization leak and shortcut bias.
61f6639768e23553b5b4ba00a5e29ea3abb2e881.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a general kernel-theoretic framework that precisely characterizes the limitations of compositional generalization in models with compositionally structured representations. It identifies conjunction-wise additivity as a fundamental computational constraint, partitioning the compositional task space into tasks that can and cannot be solved by such models. The research also uncovers and formalizes two novel failure modes—memorization leak and shortcut bias—arising from the interaction of representational geometry and training data statistics. Additionally, it demonstrates that these theoretical insights extend to deep neural networks trained on naturalistic data, providing a unified explanation for empirical phenomena observed in compositional generalization studies. The framework offers a principled foundation for designing new benchmarks and learning mechanisms that can overcome the identified limitations.

6247d7bb9093b4f6c222c6c224b3df4335d4b8bd.title: Causal Abstraction: A Theoretical Foundation for Mechanistic Interpretability
6247d7bb9093b4f6c222c6c224b3df4335d4b8bd.research_question: How can a unified theoretical framework be developed to provide a rigorous foundation for mechanistic interpretability in AI models, enabling the formalization, comparison, and evaluation of interpretability methods and concepts at multiple levels of abstraction?
6247d7bb9093b4f6c222c6c224b3df4335d4b8bd.hypothesis: A general theory of causal abstraction, extended to encompass arbitrary mechanism transformations and structured intervention algebras, will enable precise, flexible, and faithful mappings between low-level model mechanisms and high-level interpretable abstractions, thereby unifying and strengthening mechanistic interpretability methodologies.
6247d7bb9093b4f6c222c6c224b3df4335d4b8bd.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical framework will be constructed by generalizing the theory of causal abstraction beyond traditional hard and soft interventions to arbitrary mechanism transformations, termed 'interventionals', which are functionals mapping old mechanisms to new ones. The framework will formalize intervention algebras, capturing key algebraic properties such as commutativity and left-annihilativity, and will define exact and approximate transformations between causal models, including bijective translations and constructive causal abstractions. Key mechanistic interpretability concepts such as polysemantic neurons, the linear representation hypothesis, modular features, and graded faithfulness will be precisely defined within this formalism. The approach will unify a wide range of mechanistic interpretability methods—such as activation and path patching, causal mediation analysis, concept erasure, sparse autoencoders, and activation steering—by expressing them in the common language of causal abstraction and intervention operations.
6247d7bb9093b4f6c222c6c224b3df4335d4b8bd.experiment_details: The theoretical framework will be validated through formal proofs, illustrative examples, and case studies that demonstrate its applicability to mechanistic interpretability tasks. Example applications will include the abstraction of neural network models, the analysis of distributed and modular features, and the mapping of existing interpretability techniques to the proposed formalism. Empirical validation may involve implementing selected intervention operations (e.g., distributed interchange interventions, causal scrubbing, or concept erasure) on standard deep learning models, with evaluation metrics such as faithfulness, fidelity, and alignment accuracy. Baselines for comparison will include traditional hard/soft intervention approaches and existing interpretability techniques not grounded in the new abstraction framework.
6247d7bb9093b4f6c222c6c224b3df4335d4b8bd.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a generalization of causal abstraction theory to arbitrary mechanism transformations, enabling the formal treatment of distributed and overlapping macrovariables. It provides the first unified, mathematically precise foundation for mechanistic interpretability concepts and methods, encompassing both exact and approximate abstractions. The framework establishes intervention algebras as a structural basis for interventions, and systematically unifies a diverse set of interpretability methodologies under a single theoretical language. This approach enables rigorous comparison, evaluation, and further development of mechanistic interpretability techniques.

625d57bd52c60cd79aa4add6c4420dc2ad3b808a.title: On Distillation of Guided Diffusion Models
625d57bd52c60cd79aa4add6c4420dc2ad3b808a.research_question: How can the inference speed of classifier-free guided diffusion models be significantly improved while maintaining high sample quality and flexibility across a range of guidance strengths, for both pixel-space and latent-space models, and in applications such as text-to-image generation, image inpainting, and image-to-image translation?
625d57bd52c60cd79aa4add6c4420dc2ad3b808a.hypothesis: A two-stage distillation framework that first trains a student model to match the outputs of a classifier-free guided diffusion teacher, and then progressively distills this student into models requiring fewer sampling steps, will enable fast sampling (as few as 1-4 steps) with minimal loss in sample quality and support a wide range of guidance strengths.
625d57bd52c60cd79aa4add6c4420dc2ad3b808a.proposed_method: A novel two-stage distillation approach will be developed for classifier-free guided diffusion models. In the first stage, a student model is trained to match the combined outputs of the conditional and unconditional teacher models, with explicit conditioning on the guidance strength parameter using Fourier embeddings. The student model adopts a U-Net architecture, initialized from the teacher's conditional model, and is trained with a loss that encourages accurate prediction across a range of guidance strengths. In the second stage, progressive distillation is performed, where the student model is further distilled to require fewer sampling steps by matching the outputs of multi-step teacher samplers (e.g., DDIM) in a single step, halving the number of steps at each iteration. Both deterministic and stochastic sampling procedures are supported in the distilled models, enabling efficient and flexible inference.
625d57bd52c60cd79aa4add6c4420dc2ad3b808a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both pixel-space and latent-space diffusion models. For pixel-space models, ImageNet64x64 and CIFAR-10 datasets will be used, with U-Net architectures and v-prediction models as baselines. For latent-space models, Stable Diffusion pretrained on LAION-5B and ImageNet256x256 will be employed, including text-to-image, image inpainting, and image-to-image translation tasks. Baselines will include DDPM ancestral sampling, DDIM, DPM, DPM++, and single-guidance models. Evaluation metrics will comprise FID, Inception Score, CLIP score, and improved precision/recall, with extensive ablations on guidance strength and sampling steps. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparisons by using the same teacher models and architectures across methods, and both qualitative and quantitative analyses will be performed.
625d57bd52c60cd79aa4add6c4420dc2ad3b808a.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to enable effective distillation of classifier-free guided diffusion models for both pixel-space and latent-space domains, supporting a wide range of guidance strengths in a single distilled model. The method achieves significant acceleration (up to 256x for pixel-space and at least 10x for latent-space models), enabling high-quality image synthesis with as few as 1-4 denoising steps. The approach is demonstrated to be effective for text-guided image editing, inpainting, and style transfer, and introduces a new stochastic sampling process for distilled models. This work overcomes limitations of prior distillation and fast sampling methods, which could not handle classifier-free guidance or a range of guidance strengths in a unified model.

626d221fbd67f15f6ea04cb789073d6b01c14e34.title: Unsuitability of NOTEARS for Causal Graph Discovery when Dealing with Dimensional Quantities
626d221fbd67f15f6ea04cb789073d6b01c14e34.research_question: How robust and reliable are continuous optimization-based causal discovery methods, specifically those that optimize for sparse DAG structures from observational data, when subjected to changes in data scaling, hyperparameters, and violations of standard modeling assumptions?
626d221fbd67f15f6ea04cb789073d6b01c14e34.hypothesis: Continuous optimization-based methods for causal graph discovery, such as those using least-squares loss with sparsity and acyclicity constraints, are not robust to changes in the scale of input variables and may not reliably identify true causal relationships in real-world data.
626d221fbd67f15f6ea04cb789073d6b01c14e34.proposed_method: A systematic evaluation will be conducted on the robustness of continuous optimization-based causal discovery algorithms, focusing on methods that identify sparse DAG structures by minimizing a loss function subject to acyclicity constraints (e.g., via augmented Lagrangian approaches). The methodology will involve generating synthetic datasets from known linear structural equation models (SEMs) with varying scales and variances across variables. The algorithms will be applied to both raw and rescaled (normalized) data, and their sensitivity to changes in variable scale, as well as to hyperparameter settings (such as regularization strength), will be assessed. Comparative analysis will be performed with alternative methods, including those that use different loss functions (e.g., Mahalanobis distance or Gaussian log-likelihood) and those that explicitly account for noise variance.
626d221fbd67f15f6ea04cb789073d6b01c14e34.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize synthetic datasets generated from linear SEMs with known ground truth DAGs, varying the scale of individual variables systematically (e.g., by multiplying by different factors) to assess the impact on the learned graph structure. The primary baseline will be the NOTEARS algorithm, with additional comparisons to methods such as LiNGAM and GOLEM (both equal-variance and non-equal-variance variants). Evaluation metrics will include structural accuracy (e.g., precision, recall, and F1-score of recovered edges), correctness of edge orientation, and robustness to rescaling. The experimental setup will also include ablation studies on the effect of regularization and the use of different loss functions.
626d221fbd67f15f6ea04cb789073d6b01c14e34.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a comprehensive robustness analysis of continuous optimization-based causal discovery methods with respect to data scaling and hyperparameter changes, highlighting fundamental limitations in their ability to recover true causal relationships. It claims to provide new insights into the scale-dependence of these algorithms, demonstrates that edge orientation can be arbitrarily affected by variable variance, and establishes that such methods may not be suitable for causal inference in real-world settings without careful data preprocessing or methodological adjustments. The analysis also extends to nonlinear and alternative loss-based methods, offering a broader critique of current practices in causal structure learning.

629677e4ff2aceb951ccfdf3763956c75974c8e5.title: Wild-Time: A Benchmark of in-the-Wild Distribution Shift over Time
629677e4ff2aceb951ccfdf3763956c75974c8e5.research_question: How can machine learning models be systematically evaluated and improved for robustness to real-world temporal distribution shifts across diverse domains and tasks?
629677e4ff2aceb951ccfdf3763956c75974c8e5.hypothesis: Existing approaches to domain generalization, continual learning, self-supervised learning, and ensemble learning do not consistently provide robustness to gradual, in-the-wild temporal distribution shifts, and a unified benchmark will reveal the limitations and gaps in current methods.
629677e4ff2aceb951ccfdf3763956c75974c8e5.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark, Wild-Time, will be curated to systematically evaluate machine learning models under naturally occurring, gradual temporal distribution shifts. The benchmark will include five real-world datasets spanning six tasks (e.g., facial recognition, healthcare, news, and scientific article classification) with timestamp metadata, ensuring that training and test splits reflect realistic temporal progression. Two evaluation protocols will be established: Eval-Fix (fixed train/test time split) and Eval-Stream (incremental evaluation on future timestamps), measuring both average and worst-time performance. A suite of 13 representative algorithms from empirical risk minimization, continual learning (e.g., fine-tuning, EWC, SI, A-GEM), invariant learning (e.g., CORAL, IRM, LISA, GroupDRO, and their temporal adaptations), self-supervised learning (SimCLR, SwaV), and ensemble learning (SWA) will be systematically adapted and benchmarked under these protocols. Temporal adaptation of invariant learning methods will be achieved by constructing domains via sliding time windows over the data stream, allowing for direct application of domain-invariant algorithms to temporal settings.
629677e4ff2aceb951ccfdf3763956c75974c8e5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five datasets: Yearbook (gender classification from yearbook photos, 1930-2013), FMoW-Time (land use classification from satellite images, 2002-2017), MIMIC-IV (ICU readmission and mortality prediction, 2008-2019), HuffPost (news tag classification, 2012-2022), and arXiv (paper category classification, 2007-2022). For each task, models will be trained on earlier timestamps and evaluated on future timestamps, with splits designed to ensure observable performance drops due to temporal shift. Baselines will include ERM, continual learning methods, invariant learning (with temporal adaptation), self-supervised, and ensemble methods. Evaluation metrics will be accuracy for most tasks and ROC-AUC for mortality prediction, with results averaged over three random seeds. Hyperparameters will be tuned via cross-validation on held-out validation sets from the training period. Both average and worst-time out-of-distribution (OOD) performance will be reported, and comparisons will be made to in-distribution (ID) performance to quantify robustness gaps.
