629677e4ff2aceb951ccfdf3763956c75974c8e5.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark provides the first comprehensive, multi-domain evaluation framework specifically targeting gradual, real-world temporal distribution shifts. It introduces systematic protocols (Eval-Fix and Eval-Stream) for assessing temporal robustness, adapts domain-invariant learning methods to temporal settings using sliding window domains, and enables direct comparison of a wide range of algorithms under unified conditions. The benchmark reveals significant gaps in current methods' ability to handle temporal shifts and provides a foundation for future research on temporally robust machine learning.

62a3f6b69b4fee54b7a65cb2f3acbec81af75404.title: Local Manifold Approximation and Projection for Manifold-Aware Diffusion Planning
62a3f6b69b4fee54b7a65cb2f3acbec81af75404.research_question: How can diffusion-based generative planning methods for long-horizon, sparse-reward tasks be made more reliable and robust, particularly by mitigating the risk of generating infeasible or off-manifold trajectories in high-dimensional, safety-critical applications?
62a3f6b69b4fee54b7a65cb2f3acbec81af75404.hypothesis: Introducing a training-free, local manifold approximation and projection step into the diffusion planning process will significantly reduce the generation of infeasible trajectories by constraining samples to a low-rank subspace approximated from offline data, thereby improving planning reliability and performance.
62a3f6b69b4fee54b7a65cb2f3acbec81af75404.proposed_method: A novel, training-free module called Local Manifold Approximation and Projection (LoMAP) is integrated into the diffusion planning process. At each reverse diffusion step, the current sample is first denoised using Tweedie’s formula and a learned noise predictor. The k nearest neighbors of this denoised sample are retrieved from the offline dataset, and these neighbors are forward-diffused to the current timestep. Principal component analysis (PCA) is then performed on these locally relevant samples to construct a low-dimensional subspace that approximates the local data manifold. The current sample is projected onto this subspace, ensuring that the sample remains close to the feasible manifold and reducing off-manifold deviations. This projection step is applied after each reward-guided update, and the method is fully compatible with existing diffusion planners, requiring no additional training or model modifications.
62a3f6b69b4fee54b7a65cb2f3acbec81af75404.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on standard offline reinforcement learning benchmarks, including Maze2D (single-task and multi-task), MuJoCo locomotion tasks (HalfCheetah, Hopper, Walker2d), and the challenging AntMaze domain. Baselines include model-free algorithms (IQL, CQL), model-based planners (MOPO, MOReL), sequence modeling approaches (Decision Transformer, Trajectory Transformer), and prior diffusion-based planners (Diffuser, RGG, TAT, Decision Diffuser, Hierarchical Diffuser). Evaluation metrics include normalized average return, artifact ratio (fraction of infeasible trajectories), and success rates over multiple planning seeds. The experimental setup involves comparing the proposed LoMAP-augmented planners against baselines in terms of both reliability (artifact reduction) and planning performance, with additional analysis on the ability to generate minority samples and integration into hierarchical planning frameworks.
62a3f6b69b4fee54b7a65cb2f3acbec81af75404.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first training-free, plug-and-play module for diffusion planners that constrains each reverse diffusion step to a locally approximated low-rank manifold using only offline data. LoMAP addresses the critical issue of manifold deviation in high-dimensional, long-horizon planning tasks, providing a theoretically grounded and empirically validated solution that significantly reduces infeasible trajectory generation. The approach is easily integrable into both standard and hierarchical diffusion planners, and demonstrates superior reliability and performance across diverse offline RL benchmarks, including challenging domains such as AntMaze. Additionally, LoMAP enhances the ability to generate feasible minority samples in low-density regions, supporting broader exploration without sacrificing validity.

62ad7ea9467bbcdbfe325b9ee561cab3908e4583.title: MEGA: Multilingual Evaluation of Generative AI
62ad7ea9467bbcdbfe325b9ee561cab3908e4583.research_question: How can the multilingual capabilities and limitations of generative large language models (LLMs) be systematically evaluated across a wide range of languages and NLP tasks, and what factors influence their performance in non-English and low-resource languages?
62ad7ea9467bbcdbfe325b9ee561cab3908e4583.hypothesis: Generative LLMs exhibit significant disparities in performance between high-resource (especially English) and low-resource languages, particularly for non-Latin scripts, and that prompt-based strategies such as translate-test can partially bridge this gap but are insufficient to achieve parity. Furthermore, tokenizer quality and pre-training data size are hypothesized to be key factors explaining these disparities.
62ad7ea9467bbcdbfe325b9ee561cab3908e4583.proposed_method: A comprehensive multilingual evaluation framework will be developed, benchmarking generative LLMs on 16 standard NLP datasets spanning 70 typologically diverse languages and covering five major task families: classification, question answering, sequence labeling, summarization, and responsible AI (toxicity/bias). The evaluation will include multiple prompting strategies: monolingual prompting, zero-shot cross-lingual prompting, and translate-test (machine translating test inputs to English before prediction). Few-shot in-context learning will be systematically varied, and prompt templates will be selected based on English validation performance, then applied across languages. Both generative LLMs (such as GPT-3.5, GPT-4, BLOOMZ) and fine-tuned state-of-the-art baselines (e.g., TULRv6, XLM-R, mBERT, mT5, MuRIL) will be compared. Additional analyses will examine the impact of tokenizer fertility and pre-training data size on model performance, as well as potential test data contamination.
62ad7ea9467bbcdbfe325b9ee561cab3908e4583.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 16 multilingual NLP datasets, including XNLI, Indic-XNLI, GLUECos NLI, XCOPA, XStoryCloze, PAWS-X, EN-ES-CS, XQuAD, MLQA, TyDiQA-GoldP, IndicQA, PAN-X, UDPOS, XL-Sum, Jigsaw, and Wino-MT, covering 70 languages from 21 language families. Generative LLMs (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, BLOOMZ) will be evaluated using prompt-based approaches with varying few-shot examples (typically k=8, k=4 for longer contexts), and compared to fine-tuned baselines (TULRv6, XLM-R, mBERT, mT5, MuRIL). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, F1, EM, and ROUGE-L depending on the task. Prompting strategies will be systematically compared, and the effect of prompt language, few-shot size, and explanations will be analyzed. Tokenizer fertility and pre-training data size will be correlated with performance. Test data contamination will be investigated by probing model knowledge of dataset cards and checking dataset release dates and online availability.
62ad7ea9467bbcdbfe325b9ee561cab3908e4583.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark represents the first large-scale, systematic evaluation of generative LLMs across 70 languages and 16 diverse NLP tasks, providing a comprehensive blueprint for multilingual benchmarking. The framework introduces a rigorous comparison of prompting strategies (including translate-test) and analyzes the impact of tokenizer quality and pre-training data on performance disparities. The study also pioneers an initial investigation into test data contamination in LLMs and provides actionable insights and directions for improving multilingual generative AI, particularly for low-resource and non-Latin script languages.

62b18cc55dcc7ffe52c28e1086aee893b7bc4334.title: Gated Linear Attention Transformers with Hardware-Efficient Training
62b18cc55dcc7ffe52c28e1086aee893b7bc4334.research_question: Can a hardware-efficient, data-dependent gated linear attention mechanism be developed that enables efficient training and inference in Transformers, while achieving competitive performance with state-of-the-art models on language modeling and recall-intensive tasks, and supporting strong length generalization?
62b18cc55dcc7ffe52c28e1086aee893b7bc4334.hypothesis: A hardware-aware, chunkwise parallel implementation of gated linear attention with data-dependent gates will enable efficient training and inference on modern GPUs, and when integrated into Transformers, will yield models that match or outperform existing linear and softmax attention baselines in both language modeling and recall-intensive tasks, while providing superior length generalization.
62b18cc55dcc7ffe52c28e1086aee893b7bc4334.proposed_method: A novel algorithm for linear attention, FLASHLINEARATTENTION, will be designed to optimize memory movement and parallelizability for modern GPU architectures. This method will employ chunkwise parallelism, dividing sequences into non-overlapping chunks, and will utilize I/O-aware strategies to minimize high bandwidth memory (HBM) access by maximizing on-chip SRAM usage. The linear attention mechanism will be extended with a data-dependent gating mechanism, forming a Gated Linear Attention (GLA) layer, where the gating factor is parameterized efficiently via low-rank projections and sigmoid activations applied to the input. The GLA layer will support both recurrent and parallel forms, and a secondary-level chunking strategy will be introduced to enable the use of half-precision matrix multiplications (matmuls) on tensor cores for most computations, while maintaining numerical stability with log-space computations for critical components. The resulting GLA layer will be integrated into a multi-head Transformer architecture, interleaved with feed-forward networks and modern normalization and activation techniques.
62b18cc55dcc7ffe52c28e1086aee893b7bc4334.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on moderate-scale language modeling benchmarks using the SlimPajama dataset tokenized with the Mistral tokenizer, training models at 340M and 1.3B parameter scales on 15B and 100B tokens, respectively. The GLA Transformer will be compared against strong baselines including Transformer++ (LLaMA architecture with modern enhancements), RetNet, and Mamba, all trained under identical conditions for fair comparison. Evaluation will include perplexity on Wikitext and LAMBADA, as well as accuracy on a suite of downstream tasks (e.g., PIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-easy, ARC-challenge), with additional focus on recall-intensive tasks such as FDA, SWDE, SQUAD, and synthetic MQAR. Training efficiency will be measured in terms of throughput and memory usage on single H100 GPUs, and length generalization will be assessed by training on shorter sequences and evaluating on much longer contexts (up to 20K tokens). Ablation studies will explore the impact of gating parameterization and head dimension choices.
62b18cc55dcc7ffe52c28e1086aee893b7bc4334.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a hardware-efficient, I/O-aware chunkwise algorithm for linear attention that outperforms existing optimized softmax attention implementations, even at moderate sequence lengths. It generalizes linear attention to a more expressive, data-dependent gated form while maintaining efficient training and inference. The method enables the use of half-precision tensor core operations for most computations, significantly improving training throughput and scalability. The GLA Transformer demonstrates superior length generalization and strong performance on recall-intensive tasks, addressing known weaknesses of prior linear attention models. The approach also provides a practical path for scaling linear attention models to larger hidden states and longer contexts without prohibitive memory or compute costs.

62b368417eca18fe68d209e5a077392748450a29.title: Ablating Concepts in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
62b368417eca18fe68d209e5a077392748450a29.research_question: How can specific concepts, such as copyrighted styles, object instances, or memorized images, be efficiently removed from large-scale pretrained text-to-image diffusion models without retraining from scratch, while preserving the model's ability to generate related or surrounding concepts?
62b368417eca18fe68d209e5a077392748450a29.hypothesis: It is possible to ablate (remove) specific target concepts from pretrained text-to-image diffusion models by fine-tuning the model to match the output distribution of the target concept to that of a user-specified anchor concept, thereby preventing generation of the target concept while minimally affecting related concepts.
62b368417eca18fe68d209e5a077392748450a29.proposed_method: A novel concept ablation framework will be developed for pretrained text-to-image diffusion models. The approach involves fine-tuning the model such that, when conditioned on a target concept prompt, the model's output distribution matches that of an anchor concept prompt. Two variants will be explored: (1) model-based ablation, where the model is trained to minimize the difference between its predictions for the target and anchor prompts using KL divergence between their conditional distributions, and (2) noise-based ablation, where the model is fine-tuned on pairs of target prompts and images generated from anchor prompts, using the standard diffusion loss. Regularization with the standard diffusion loss on anchor concept pairs will be included to preserve related concepts. The method will experiment with updating different parameter subsets, such as cross-attention layers, text embeddings, or the full U-Net weights, to balance effectiveness and robustness.
62b368417eca18fe68d209e5a077392748450a29.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Stable Diffusion model, targeting 16 ablation tasks including specific object instances (e.g., Grumpy Cat, R2D2), artistic styles (e.g., Van Gogh, Monet), and memorized images identified from prior work. For each task, prompts will be generated using ChatGPT or CLIP-based retrieval, and images will be synthesized for both target and anchor concepts. Baselines will include a loss maximization approach inspired by prior unlearning methods. Evaluation metrics will comprise CLIP Score and CLIP Accuracy (measuring similarity and classification accuracy in CLIP feature space), KID (Kernel Inception Distance) for distributional similarity, and SSCD for memorization rate. Additional analyses will assess robustness to prompt misspellings, the effect of anchor concept choice, and the ability to ablate multiple concepts simultaneously.
62b368417eca18fe68d209e5a077392748450a29.novelty_claims: The proposed method enables efficient ablation of specific concepts from large-scale pretrained text-to-image diffusion models without requiring retraining from scratch or access to the original training data. It introduces a principled distribution-matching objective for concept removal, supports flexible parameter subset fine-tuning, and demonstrates robustness to prompt variations. The approach is scalable, computationally efficient (requiring only minutes per concept), and preserves the model's ability to generate related concepts, addressing key challenges in model unlearning and responsible AI deployment.

62b66f2fec242fa9e5b1071a625643a9fcd5a8e9.title: Near-Optimal Algorithms for Gaussians with Huber Contamination: Mean Estimation and Linear Regression
62b66f2fec242fa9e5b1071a625643a9fcd5a8e9.research_question: How can robust mean estimation and linear regression be performed efficiently and accurately for high-dimensional Gaussian distributions in the presence of Huber contamination?
62b66f2fec242fa9e5b1071a625643a9fcd5a8e9.hypothesis: It is possible to design algorithms for robust mean estimation and linear regression under Huber contamination that achieve optimal error rates with near-optimal sample complexity and almost-linear runtime.
62b66f2fec242fa9e5b1071a625643a9fcd5a8e9.proposed_method: A novel algorithmic framework is proposed for robust mean estimation and linear regression with Gaussian covariates under Huber contamination. The approach combines multi-directional filtering—leveraging projections onto multiple nearly-orthogonal directions—with fast filtering techniques that use random directions derived from the empirical covariance matrix. The method iteratively identifies directions of large variance, filters outliers more aggressively in these directions, and ensures that the remaining sample set has controlled covariance structure. For robust linear regression, a reduction is performed by conditioning on the response variable and applying the robust mean estimation algorithm to the resulting conditional distribution, which is shown to be nearly spherical with mean proportional to the true regressor. The algorithm is carefully designed to run in almost-linear time by restricting expensive operations to low-dimensional subspaces and using efficient linear algebraic techniques.
62b66f2fec242fa9e5b1071a625643a9fcd5a8e9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic datasets generated according to the Huber contamination model, where a fraction of samples are replaced by arbitrary outliers. For mean estimation, samples will be drawn from d-dimensional isotropic Gaussians with varying contamination levels. For linear regression, labeled examples will be generated with Gaussian covariates and additive Gaussian noise, with a fraction of responses corrupted. Baseline methods will include previous robust mean estimation and regression algorithms, such as those achieving O(ε log(1/ε)) error or requiring higher sample complexity. Evaluation metrics will include ℓ2 estimation error of the mean or regressor, runtime, and sample complexity. Experiments will systematically vary dimension, contamination fraction, and sample size to assess scalability and robustness.
62b66f2fec242fa9e5b1071a625643a9fcd5a8e9.novelty_claims: The proposed algorithms are the first to achieve both optimal error guarantees (O(ε) for mean estimation and O(σ ε) for regression) and almost-linear runtime with near-optimal sample complexity for Gaussian distributions under Huber contamination. The methodology introduces a new multi-directional filtering approach that enables stronger concentration and more effective outlier removal, overcoming limitations of prior single-directional or brute-force methods. The reduction from robust regression to robust mean estimation is novel and enables the first polynomial-time algorithm with optimal error for robust Gaussian linear regression in the Huber model. The framework is also amenable to streaming settings with optimal memory up to poly(1/ε) factors.

62d6e95e60ba36abacc5de85078d053316bd1942.title: UniPC: A Unified Predictor-Corrector Framework for Fast Sampling of Diffusion Models
62d6e95e60ba36abacc5de85078d053316bd1942.research_question: How can the sampling process of diffusion probabilistic models (DPMs) be accelerated to achieve high-quality image generation with extremely few function evaluations, while maintaining or improving sample quality and diversity across both unconditional and conditional tasks?
62d6e95e60ba36abacc5de85078d053316bd1942.hypothesis: A unified predictor-corrector framework that supports arbitrary order and can be applied in a training-free manner to existing DPM samplers will significantly improve sampling quality and convergence speed, especially in scenarios with very few sampling steps, without increasing computational or memory costs.
62d6e95e60ba36abacc5de85078d053316bd1942.proposed_method: A unified predictor-corrector (UniPC) framework will be developed for fast sampling of diffusion probabilistic models. The method consists of two main components: a unified corrector (UniC), which can be applied after any existing DPM sampler to increase the order of accuracy without extra model evaluations, and a unified predictor (UniP) that supports arbitrary order as a byproduct of the corrector's formulation. Both components share a unified analytical form based on exponential integrators in the half-log-SNR domain, allowing for simple and explicit computation of higher-order solvers. The framework enables both multistep and singlestep updates, is method-agnostic, and can be customized for arbitrary order schedules. UniPC is designed to be plug-and-play, improving the accuracy of off-the-shelf fast samplers and supporting both pixel-space and latent-space DPMs, as well as conditional and unconditional sampling tasks.
62d6e95e60ba36abacc5de85078d053316bd1942.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of datasets, including CIFAR10, FFHQ, LSUN Bedroom, ImageNet 256×256, and MS-COCO2014, covering both pixel-space and latent-space DPMs. Both unconditional and conditional (classifier-guided and classifier-free) sampling tasks will be evaluated. Baseline methods for comparison will include DDIM, DPM-Solver, DPM-Solver++, DEIS, and PNDM, with particular focus on DPM-Solver++ as the state-of-the-art. Evaluation metrics will include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for sample quality, Inception Score (IS) for diversity, and L2 distance to reference solutions for convergence analysis. Experiments will systematically vary the number of function evaluations (NFE), the order of the solver, and the choice of hyperparameters such as B(h). Ablation studies will assess the impact of different components and configurations, and inference time and memory usage will be measured to ensure practical efficiency.
62d6e95e60ba36abacc5de85078d053316bd1942.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a unified, analytical, and training-free predictor-corrector approach for arbitrary-order fast sampling of DPMs, which can be applied to any existing sampler to boost accuracy without additional model evaluations. Unlike previous methods, UniPC supports explicit forms for any order, enabling easy customization and efficient implementation. The method achieves state-of-the-art sample quality and diversity with extremely few sampling steps, surpassing prior training-free solvers in both unconditional and conditional tasks, and matches the inference speed and memory usage of leading baselines. The plug-and-play nature and universality of the framework represent significant innovations in the acceleration of diffusion model sampling.

62f80fffbdc8b58870a2743cc24f931346406b0c.title: MaGNET: Uniform Sampling from Deep Generative Network Manifolds Without Retraining
62f80fffbdc8b58870a2743cc24f931346406b0c.research_question: How can uniform sampling be achieved from the manifold learned by any pre-trained deep generative network, regardless of the original training data distribution, and what are the effects of such sampling on distributional fairness, diversity, and statistical estimation tasks?
62f80fffbdc8b58870a2743cc24f931346406b0c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a theoretically motivated latent space sampling strategy can be developed to produce samples uniformly distributed on the manifold learned by any pre-trained deep generative network, without requiring retraining or access to labels, thereby improving sample diversity, fairness, and the accuracy and efficiency of statistical estimations.
62f80fffbdc8b58870a2743cc24f931346406b0c.proposed_method: A novel latent space sampling algorithm, termed MaGNET (Maximum entropy Generative NETwork), will be developed for use with any pre-trained and differentiable deep generative network (DGN) employing continuous piecewise affine (CPA) nonlinearities, such as (leaky-)ReLU. The method analytically characterizes the transformation of a latent space density through the CPA mapping of the DGN and derives a sampling strategy that compensates for per-region volume changes, ensuring that the resulting samples are uniformly distributed on the output manifold. The procedure involves generating a large pool of latent vectors, computing the Jacobian at each point to estimate the local volume change, and then resampling latent vectors with probability proportional to the local volume, thus correcting for non-uniformities induced by the DGN mapping. This Monte Carlo-based approach does not require knowledge of the partitioning of the latent space or explicit retraining of the DGN, and can be applied as a plug-and-play module to existing generative models.
62f80fffbdc8b58870a2743cc24f931346406b0c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of state-of-the-art generative models, including StyleGAN2 (trained on FFHQ), BigGAN (trained on ImageNet), progGAN (trained on CelebA-HQ), and NVAE (trained on MNIST and colored MNIST). Both standard and MaGNET sampling will be compared using quantitative metrics such as Frechet Inception Distance (FID), precision and recall, Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) log-likelihoods, and neighborhood density uniformity within epsilon-balls on the data manifold. Qualitative assessments will include visual inspection of generated samples for diversity and attribute balance (e.g., gender, age, color), as well as analysis of attribute distributions using external classifiers. Additional experiments will evaluate the impact of MaGNET sampling on statistical estimation tasks, such as Monte Carlo estimation of the Lipschitz constant, by measuring convergence rates and estimator variance.
62f80fffbdc8b58870a2743cc24f931346406b0c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to provide a provable, theoretically grounded method for uniform sampling on the manifold learned by any pre-trained DGN, without requiring retraining or label information. The method is architecture-agnostic and applicable to any DGN with CPA nonlinearities, including GANs, VAEs, and flow-based models. MaGNET enables improved fairness and diversity in generated samples, corrects for biases present in the training distribution, and accelerates convergence in statistical estimation tasks. The approach also offers new tools for data exploration, model interpretation, and diagnostic assessment of learned manifolds.

63148389a127e428b210e82260061c0d6c19e062.title: Game-theoretic statistics and safe anytime-valid inference
63148389a127e428b210e82260061c0d6c19e062.research_question: How can statistical inference be made robust to continuous monitoring, optional stopping, and composite or nonparametric hypothesis settings, while maintaining validity at all stopping times?
63148389a127e428b210e82260061c0d6c19e062.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a game-theoretic approach, leveraging test martingales, e-processes, and associated betting interpretations, can provide valid, safe, and powerful anytime-valid inference for both testing and estimation, even under composite and nonparametric hypotheses.
63148389a127e428b210e82260061c0d6c19e062.proposed_method: A new framework for safe anytime-valid inference (SAVI) will be developed, grounded in game-theoretic probability. The approach centers on constructing e-processes and test martingales, which are nonnegative (super)martingales that quantify statistical evidence and remain valid at arbitrary stopping times. For simple null and alternative hypotheses, likelihood ratios will be used to construct growth-rate optimal test martingales. For composite or nonparametric hypotheses, methodologies such as the plug-in method, mixture method, universal inference (UI), and reverse information projection (RIPr) will be systematically developed. These methods involve learning or mixing over alternatives, minimizing worst-case shortfall in expected log growth (REGROW), and constructing e-processes that dominate traditional likelihood-based approaches. The framework will also address technical challenges such as the absence of nontrivial martingales for rich nulls, and will generalize to confidence sequences and anytime-valid p-values.
63148389a127e428b210e82260061c0d6c19e062.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of statistical testing and estimation problems, including nonparametric composite hypothesis testing, sequential A/B testing, and bandit experiments. Both synthetic and real-world datasets will be used to evaluate the performance of the proposed methods. Baselines will include traditional fixed-horizon p-value-based tests, classical sequential analysis methods, and Bayesian approaches. Evaluation metrics will focus on type-I error control at arbitrary stopping times, power, expected log-wealth growth, and the tightness of confidence sequences. The experimental setup will include continuous monitoring scenarios, optional stopping, and settings with both simple and composite nulls and alternatives.
63148389a127e428b210e82260061c0d6c19e062.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified, game-theoretic framework for anytime-valid inference that is applicable to both testing and estimation, including in composite and nonparametric settings where traditional martingale methods fail. The use of e-processes and test martingales as central objects enables valid inference under arbitrary stopping rules, overcoming the limitations of classical approaches. Novel contributions include the systematic development of universal inference, reverse information projection, and growth-rate optimality criteria (REGROW) for constructing optimal e-processes. The framework generalizes and extends existing methods, providing new tools for robust, safe, and interpretable statistical inference in modern data analysis contexts.

63167c30b06aa6c3d76e09065ced0412090d6c3b.title: The Era of 1-bit LLMs: All Large Language Models are in 1.58 Bits
63167c30b06aa6c3d76e09065ced0412090d6c3b.research_question: Can large language models be designed with extremely low-precision weights (e.g., ternary {-1, 0, 1}, or 1.58 bits per parameter) to achieve comparable performance to full-precision models while significantly reducing computational, memory, and energy costs?
63167c30b06aa6c3d76e09065ced0412090d6c3b.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a large language model with ternary weights (1.58 bits per parameter) can match the perplexity and end-task performance of full-precision (FP16/BF16) Transformer LLMs of the same size and training tokens, while offering substantial improvements in latency, memory usage, throughput, and energy efficiency.
63167c30b06aa6c3d76e09065ced0412090d6c3b.proposed_method: A new large language model architecture, BitNet b1.58, will be developed in which every parameter is quantized to one of three values: -1, 0, or 1, resulting in a 1.58-bit representation. The model will be based on a Transformer backbone, replacing standard linear layers with BitLinear layers, and will be trained from scratch using 1.58-bit weights and 8-bit activations. An absmean quantization function will be applied to constrain weights, scaling the weight matrix by its average absolute value and rounding to the nearest ternary value. The architecture will adopt LLaMA-like components, including RMSNorm, SwiGLU, rotary embedding, and bias removal, to ensure compatibility with open-source software ecosystems. The quantization of activations will be handled to optimize for both implementation simplicity and system-level efficiency.
63167c30b06aa6c3d76e09065ced0412090d6c3b.experiment_details: Experiments will involve pre-training BitNet b1.58 and full-precision LLaMA-like models of various sizes (700M, 1.3B, 3B, 3.9B, 7B, 13B, 70B parameters) on the RedPajama dataset for 100 billion tokens. Evaluation will be performed on standard language modeling benchmarks, including WikiText2 and C4 for perplexity, and a suite of zero-shot end tasks such as ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, Winogrande, PIQA, OpenbookQA, and BoolQ. Metrics will include perplexity, zero-shot accuracy, GPU memory usage, inference latency, throughput, and energy consumption. Comparisons will be made against full-precision LLaMA models and other open-source models (e.g., StableLM-3B), with measurements taken using optimized inference codebases and hardware (e.g., NVIDIA A100 GPUs). Additional experiments will explore scaling laws, batch size limits, and performance under increased training tokens (e.g., 2T tokens).
63167c30b06aa6c3d76e09065ced0412090d6c3b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a 1.58-bit ternary quantization scheme for all model weights, enabling a new computation paradigm that nearly eliminates multiplication operations in matrix multiplications. This results in substantial reductions in memory footprint, latency, and energy consumption, while maintaining or surpassing the performance of full-precision LLMs at scale. The method establishes a new scaling law for low-bit LLMs and demonstrates the feasibility of training and deploying high-performance, cost-effective LLMs with ternary weights. Furthermore, the approach paves the way for hardware and system designs specifically optimized for 1-bit/ternary LLMs and enables practical deployment on edge and mobile devices.

632a4956aebedd85f61445718ec5df9589bb5843.title: PixelSplat: 3D Gaussian Splats from Image Pairs for Scalable Generalizable 3D Reconstruction
632a4956aebedd85f61445718ec5df9589bb5843.research_question: How can a scalable, generalizable, and interpretable 3D scene representation be reconstructed from only a pair of images, enabling real-time rendering and efficient training for novel view synthesis?
632a4956aebedd85f61445718ec5df9589bb5843.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that parameterizing 3D radiance fields with 3D Gaussian primitives, whose locations are predicted via a differentiable probabilistic sampling mechanism from dense distributions over 3D space, will enable efficient, scalable, and generalizable 3D reconstruction from sparse image pairs, overcoming local minima and scale ambiguity issues inherent in previous methods.
632a4956aebedd85f61445718ec5df9589bb5843.proposed_method: A feed-forward model will be developed that reconstructs 3D radiance fields using 3D Gaussian primitives inferred from pairs of images. The method includes a two-view image encoder that resolves per-scene scale ambiguity using a multi-view epipolar transformer, which finds pixel correspondences and records scaled depths via cross-attention and positional encoding. Instead of directly regressing Gaussian primitive parameters, the model predicts dense discrete probability distributions over depth for each pixel, from which Gaussian means are sampled using a differentiable reparameterization trick. The opacity of each Gaussian is set to the probability of the sampled depth, allowing gradients to flow into the probability distribution during training. Covariance and spherical harmonics coefficients are predicted per pixel, and the final set of primitives is rendered using efficient rasterization-based splatting.
632a4956aebedd85f61445718ec5df9589bb5843.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the RealEstate10k and ACID datasets, both of which provide real-world images and camera poses with scale ambiguity. The method will be trained and evaluated at a resolution of 256x256 pixels, reconstructing novel views from pairs of reference images. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art light field transformers (such as GPNR and the method of Du et al.), as well as pixelNeRF. Evaluation metrics will include PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS for visual fidelity, as well as memory usage and inference/training time for resource efficiency. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of the epipolar encoder and probabilistic primitive prediction.
632a4956aebedd85f61445718ec5df9589bb5843.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a differentiable probabilistic parameterization of 3D Gaussian primitive locations, enabling end-to-end training and overcoming local minima that plague direct regression approaches. The method is the first to demonstrate single-pass prediction of explicit 3D Gaussian splat representations from only two images, producing interpretable and editable 3D scenes. The approach resolves scale ambiguity via a novel epipolar transformer and achieves orders-of-magnitude improvements in rendering and training efficiency compared to prior generalizable view synthesis methods, while outperforming them in visual fidelity.

632e7a268c4682e18d294950446ef251f69ff3bc.title: Infinity∞: Scaling Bitwise AutoRegressive Modeling for High-Resolution Image Synthesis
632e7a268c4682e18d294950446ef251f69ff3bc.research_question: How can autoregressive models for high-resolution text-to-image synthesis be scaled to improve image quality, prompt adherence, and inference speed, overcoming the limitations of discrete tokenization and quantization errors?
632e7a268c4682e18d294950446ef251f69ff3bc.hypothesis: Scaling visual tokenizers and transformers using a bitwise token prediction framework with an infinite-vocabulary classifier and a bitwise self-correction mechanism will significantly enhance the generation capacity, reconstruction quality, and efficiency of autoregressive text-to-image models, surpassing state-of-the-art diffusion models.
632e7a268c4682e18d294950446ef251f69ff3bc.proposed_method: A novel bitwise visual autoregressive modeling framework is proposed, which replaces conventional index-wise discrete tokenization with bitwise tokenization. The method introduces a bitwise multi-scale residual quantizer, enabling the tokenizer vocabulary size to scale up to 2^64 or higher, thus reducing quantization errors and improving image detail. An Infinite-Vocabulary Classifier (IVC) is designed to predict each bit of the token in parallel, resulting in linear parameter growth and efficient optimization, as opposed to the exponential growth in conventional classifiers. A bitwise self-correction mechanism is incorporated during training, where random bit flips simulate prediction errors and re-quantization enables the transformer to learn self-correction, addressing train-test discrepancies and cumulative error amplification. The overall architecture performs coarse-to-fine, next-scale prediction, with the transformer conditioned on text embeddings through cross-attention, and supports dynamic aspect ratios and resolution-aware positional encoding.
632e7a268c4682e18d294950446ef251f69ff3bc.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on large-scale, curated datasets combining open-source academic data (such as LAION, COYO, OpenImages) and high-quality internal collections, filtered for text, watermarks, and aesthetics. The model is pre-trained at 256 and 512 resolutions and fine-tuned at 1024 resolution with varying aspect ratios. Evaluation is performed on established text-to-image benchmarks including GenEval and DPG, as well as human preference benchmarks ImageReward and HPSv2.1. Baselines for comparison include leading diffusion models (SDXL, SD3, PixArt-Sigma, DALL-E 3) and top autoregressive models (Emu3, HART, LlamaGen, Chameleon, Show-o). Metrics include benchmark scores, human preference win rates, and inference speed (FID is also measured on a 40K text-image validation set).
632e7a268c4682e18d294950446ef251f69ff3bc.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces bitwise tokenization and an infinite-vocabulary classifier to autoregressive image generation, enabling unprecedented scaling of vocabulary size and transformer capacity. The bitwise self-correction mechanism addresses train-test discrepancies unique to visual autoregressive modeling, improving robustness and detail. This framework achieves state-of-the-art performance for autoregressive models, surpassing leading diffusion models in image quality, prompt adherence, and inference speed, and sets new records on multiple text-to-image benchmarks. The method also enables fast, high-quality image synthesis at high resolutions and supports flexible aspect ratios.

634069cfa3ef3a53698791230ea1570c1a88fd3a.title: Mixture of Parrots: Experts improve memorization more than reasoning
634069cfa3ef3a53698791230ea1570c1a88fd3a.research_question: What are the performance tradeoffs between Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures and standard dense transformers across tasks requiring memorization versus reasoning, and how does scaling the number of experts versus model width affect these capabilities?
634069cfa3ef3a53698791230ea1570c1a88fd3a.hypothesis: Increasing the number of experts in MoE architectures improves memorization capacity more effectively than reasoning abilities, whereas increasing model width in dense transformers is more beneficial for reasoning tasks.
634069cfa3ef3a53698791230ea1570c1a88fd3a.proposed_method: A comprehensive investigation will be conducted comparing Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) transformers and standard dense transformers on both theoretical and empirical grounds. The approach will include formal analysis of representational capacity for both architectures, focusing on the requirements for solving graph reasoning and memorization tasks. Synthetic experiments will be designed to train both model types from scratch on tasks such as shortest path finding in graphs (reasoning) and large-scale phone-book memorization (memory). Additionally, large-scale pre-training will be performed for both architectures on natural language and mathematical datasets, followed by evaluation on a suite of downstream benchmarks. Key architectural variables, such as model width, number of experts, and number of active parameters, will be systematically varied to isolate their effects.
634069cfa3ef3a53698791230ea1570c1a88fd3a.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training both dense transformers and MoEs using identical backbone architectures (e.g., Mistral for dense, Mixtral for MoE), with fixed depth and varying width and number of experts. Synthetic datasets will include randomly generated graphs for shortest path tasks and large phone-books for memorization, with performance measured by exact accuracy and maximal memorization capacity. For large-scale pre-training, models will be trained on 65B-token mixtures of datasets (e.g., FineWeb-edu, Cosmopedia, Wikipedia for language; Proof-Pile2, OpenMathInstruct, MetaMathQA for math). Downstream evaluation will be performed on world knowledge (e.g., TriviaQA, Natural Questions), commonsense reasoning (e.g., HellaSwag, WinoGrande), and math reasoning (e.g., GSM8k, Hendrycks-MATH) benchmarks, using metrics such as F1 accuracy and exact match. Baselines will include parameter-matched dense and MoE models, with both total and active parameter counts controlled. Additional analyses will examine generalization gaps and performance at fixed validation perplexity.
634069cfa3ef3a53698791230ea1570c1a88fd3a.novelty_claims: The proposed research uniquely combines theoretical lower and upper bounds with extensive empirical evaluation to dissect the distinct roles of experts and model width in MoE and dense transformers, respectively. It introduces a rigorous separation between memorization and reasoning capacities, demonstrating that MoEs can match dense models in memorization with fewer active parameters but cannot achieve similar gains in reasoning tasks without increasing width. The work provides new insights into the implicit biases of MoE architectures, particularly their tendency to prioritize memorization, and offers a detailed benchmarking framework for comparing these architectures across a spectrum of real-world and synthetic tasks.

634127f09be5119f4d29a175866f11b14b3821e0.title: ManiSkill2: A Unified Benchmark for Generalizable Manipulation Skills
634127f09be5119f4d29a175866f11b14b3821e0.research_question: How can a unified and scalable benchmark be developed to support the study and evaluation of generalizable manipulation skills in embodied AI, encompassing diverse manipulation tasks, object-level variations, and realistic physical interactions?
634127f09be5119f4d29a175866f11b14b3821e0.hypothesis: A unified benchmark with extensive object-level topological and geometric variations, real-time dynamic simulation (including both rigid and soft bodies), multi-controller support, and scalable sample collection infrastructure will enable more effective research and evaluation of generalizable manipulation skills, and facilitate the development of algorithms that transfer to real-world robotic manipulation.
634127f09be5119f4d29a175866f11b14b3821e0.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark system will be constructed, featuring 20 manipulation task families that span stationary/mobile-base, single/dual-arm, and rigid/soft-body manipulation. The system will include over 2000 object models and 4 million demonstration frames, with environments implemented using a fully dynamic simulation engine. A custom GPU-based Material Point Method (MPM) simulator will be developed for real-time soft-body simulation, supporting 2-way dynamic coupling with rigid-body simulators. The benchmark will provide a unified OpenAI Gym-compatible interface, support multiple observation modalities (point cloud, RGBD), and allow flexible controller configurations and conversions between action spaces. An asynchronous, server-based rendering pipeline will be implemented to maximize sample collection throughput and minimize GPU memory usage, enabling efficient training of visual RL agents.
634127f09be5119f4d29a175866f11b14b3821e0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the full suite of 20 task families, including soft-body manipulation (e.g., Fill, Hang, Excavate, Pour, Pinch, Write), precise peg-in-hole assembly, pick-and-place, and articulated object manipulation. Baseline algorithms will include classical sense-plan-act frameworks (e.g., Contact-GraspNet, Transporter Networks), imitation learning (behavior cloning), and demonstration-augmented reinforcement learning (DAPG+PPO), with both point cloud and RGBD visual inputs. Evaluation metrics will include success rates on both seen and held-out object configurations, sample collection speed (frames per second), and GPU memory usage. Comparative experiments will benchmark the proposed system against existing frameworks (e.g., Habitat2.0, RoboSuite, IsaacGym) in terms of throughput and memory efficiency. Sim2real transfer will be evaluated by deploying trained policies directly on real robotic hardware.
634127f09be5119f4d29a175866f11b14b3821e0.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark is the first to provide a unified, large-scale, and highly diverse suite of manipulation tasks with both rigid and soft-body simulation, including real-time MPM-based environments with 2-way rigid-soft coupling. The system introduces a novel multi-controller support and action space conversion mechanism, enabling flexible use of demonstrations across different controllers. The asynchronous render server infrastructure enables unprecedented sample collection speed and memory efficiency for visual RL. The benchmark's breadth, realism, and extensibility are claimed to set a new standard for evaluating generalizable manipulation skills and facilitating sim2real transfer in embodied AI.

6381847cf6e98d96d70ee315f599df5082d16f94.title: Equilibrium and non-equilibrium regimes in the learning of restricted Boltzmann machines
6381847cf6e98d96d70ee315f599df5082d16f94.research_question: How do the dynamics of Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs) during training relate to the mixing time of the underlying Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) process, and how do these dynamics affect the generative and equilibrium properties of the learned models? What protocols can be established to reliably evaluate and exploit both equilibrium and out-of-equilibrium regimes in RBM training and sampling?
6381847cf6e98d96d70ee315f599df5082d16f94.hypothesis: The interplay between the number of MCMC steps used to approximate the log-likelihood gradient and the mixing time of the model leads to two distinct operational regimes in RBMs: equilibrium and out-of-equilibrium. These regimes have significant and predictable impacts on the quality, stability, and representativeness of generated samples, and can be systematically exploited depending on the intended application.
6381847cf6e98d96d70ee315f599df5082d16f94.proposed_method: A comprehensive experimental framework will be developed to train RBMs using various MCMC-based gradient estimation schemes, including random initialization (Rdm-k), contrastive divergence (CD-k), and persistent contrastive divergence (PCD-k), with a wide range of k values (number of MCMC steps). The methodology will involve systematically varying k and monitoring the mixing time of the MCMC process throughout training, using time-autocorrelation functions and convergence diagnostics. Multiple quality metrics will be computed for both generated and dataset samples, including log-likelihood (estimated via Annealed Importance Sampling), second moment errors, power spectral density errors, adversarial accuracy indicators, and relative entropy. The evolution of these metrics will be tracked as a function of both training age and sample generation time, with careful separation of learning and generation phases. The approach will also include protocols for initializing Markov chains, controlling for non-informative and dataset-based initializations, and quantifying equilibrium versus out-of-equilibrium behavior.
6381847cf6e98d96d70ee315f599df5082d16f94.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of datasets, including MNIST, FashionMNIST, Caltech101 Silhouettes, smallNORB, a human genome dataset, CelebA (in both black-and-white and color), and CIFAR. For each dataset, RBMs with a fixed architecture (e.g., 500 hidden units, binary visible and hidden nodes) will be trained for up to 200,000 parameter updates, with learning rates and other hyperparameters held constant except for k. Baseline comparisons will include standard CD-k and PCD-k training protocols. Evaluation metrics will include log-likelihood (using AIS), mean square error of second moments, power spectral density error, adversarial accuracy indicator, and relative entropy, all computed on sets of 1,000 generated or real samples. The mixing time will be estimated via autocorrelation analysis and convergence of observables from different initializations. Experiments will systematically analyze the relationship between k, mixing time, and the quality/stability of generated samples, as well as the transition between equilibrium and out-of-equilibrium regimes.
6381847cf6e98d96d70ee315f599df5082d16f94.novelty_claims: The proposal establishes a principled framework for distinguishing and exploiting equilibrium and out-of-equilibrium regimes in RBM training, grounded in the explicit measurement of mixing times and their interplay with gradient estimation protocols. It introduces a comprehensive suite of quality metrics for generative evaluation, moving beyond log-likelihood to include statistical and adversarial measures. The approach provides actionable protocols for practitioners to tailor RBM training and sampling strategies to specific goals (e.g., rapid sample generation versus faithful equilibrium modeling), and demonstrates that the existence of these regimes is a general property of energy-based models trained via likelihood maximization. The methodology enables reproducible and interpretable evaluation of RBMs, with implications for broader classes of generative models.

6387bfd97403c92249c23b05939008a61da8e85f.title: Not All Heads Matter: A Head-Level KV Cache Compression Method with Integrated Retrieval and Reasoning
6387bfd97403c92249c23b05939008a61da8e85f.research_question: How can memory and computational efficiency of large language models be improved for long-context tasks by optimizing key-value (KV) cache allocation at a finer granularity, specifically at the attention head level, while maintaining or improving performance on tasks requiring both retrieval and reasoning?
6387bfd97403c92249c23b05939008a61da8e85f.hypothesis: Allocating KV cache budgets dynamically across individual attention heads based on their estimated importance for retrieval and reasoning will significantly reduce memory usage and decoding latency, while maintaining or improving model performance on long-context tasks compared to existing layer-level or uniform head-level KV cache compression methods.
6387bfd97403c92249c23b05939008a61da8e85f.proposed_method: A head-level KV cache compression framework is developed that assigns KV cache budgets to individual attention heads according to their estimated importance for both retrieval and reasoning. Importance scores for each head are estimated using a novel contextual reasoning ability assessment, which involves constructing specialized question-answering examples that require both retrieval and reasoning steps (e.g., Needle-in-a-Haystack and Reasoning-in-a-Haystack tests). The importance score for each head is computed by aggregating attention scores over all tokens in the correct answer, normalized to form a distribution across heads. KV cache budgets are then allocated by combining a basic fixed budget per head with a dynamically distributed shared budget pool, proportional to each head's normalized importance score. Within each head, the most relevant KV cache entries are retained using an attention-based selection strategy guided by local instruction windows.
6387bfd97403c92249c23b05939008a61da8e85f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using open-source LLMs such as Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct. Evaluation will be performed on long-context benchmarks including LongBench (Single-DocQA and Multi-DocQA) and LooGLE (Long Dependency QA), with input lengths up to 32K tokens. Baselines for comparison include SnapKV, PyramidKV, and Ada-SnapKV, all configured to retain the same number of KV cache entries for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics include average accuracy on QA tasks, memory usage, and decoding latency. Additional tests such as Needle-in-a-Haystack and Reasoning-in-a-Haystack will be used to assess retrieval and reasoning abilities under varying KV cache sizes (e.g., 64, 128, 1024), and ablation studies will analyze the impact of different importance score estimation strategies.
6387bfd97403c92249c23b05939008a61da8e85f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first head-level KV cache compression method that allocates cache budgets based on a joint retrieval and reasoning importance score, rather than relying on layer-level or retrieval-only strategies. The method features a novel importance score estimation technique that accounts for both retrieval and reasoning abilities using specially constructed contextual QA examples. Dynamic allocation of KV cache at the head level enables significant memory and latency reductions while preserving or exceeding the performance of full KV cache and strong baselines, especially in low-resource settings. The approach demonstrates that retaining as little as 1.5% of the KV cache can achieve 97% of full-cache performance on contextual QA, establishing a new state-of-the-art in efficient long-context LLM inference.

638b08154fbb71fd34db2aae6cb40045577fe0de.title: SemDeDup: Data-efficient learning at web-scale through semantic deduplication
638b08154fbb71fd34db2aae6cb40045577fe0de.research_question: How can data efficiency in large-scale machine learning be improved by identifying and removing semantically redundant examples from massive, uncurated web-scale datasets, and what impact does this have on model performance and training efficiency?
638b08154fbb71fd34db2aae6cb40045577fe0de.hypothesis: Removing semantically redundant (semantically duplicate) data points from large-scale datasets using embedding-based similarity measures will significantly reduce dataset size and training time, while maintaining or even improving model performance, including out-of-distribution generalization.
638b08154fbb71fd34db2aae6cb40045577fe0de.proposed_method: A novel semantic deduplication framework, SemDeDup, will be developed to identify and remove semantic duplicates from large-scale datasets. The approach will embed each data point using a pre-trained foundation model (e.g., CLIP for images, OPT for text), then cluster the embeddings using k-means to reduce the computational burden of pairwise comparisons. Within each cluster, pairwise cosine similarities will be computed, and data pairs exceeding a specified similarity threshold will be considered semantic duplicates. From each group of duplicates, the example with the lowest cosine similarity to the cluster centroid will be retained, and the rest removed. This process will be applied to both image-text and language datasets, leveraging off-the-shelf pre-trained models for embedding extraction.
638b08154fbb71fd34db2aae6cb40045577fe0de.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale datasets such as LAION-440M (images and captions) and C4 (text corpus). For LAION, CLIP models will be trained on both original and SemDeDup-pruned datasets, with evaluation performed via zero-shot accuracy on ImageNet-1k and 24 additional tasks, as well as out-of-distribution (OOD) robustness on six standard OOD datasets. For C4, OPT language models of various sizes will be trained on pruned and unpruned data, with evaluation via perplexity on standard validation sets and instruction-following corpora. Baselines will include random pruning and existing deduplication methods (e.g., NearDup), with detailed ablations on clustering parameters, embedding models, and duplicate selection strategies. Training efficiency (e.g., FLOPs saved, convergence speed) and performance retention or improvement will be key metrics.
638b08154fbb71fd34db2aae6cb40045577fe0de.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a scalable, embedding-based semantic deduplication method that operates efficiently at web scale, enabling the removal of up to 50% of data with minimal or no performance loss and substantial training speedup. Unlike prior deduplication methods focused on exact or near-perceptual duplicates, this method targets semantic redundancy using pre-trained model embeddings, making it broadly applicable across modalities and datasets. The framework demonstrates that large-scale datasets contain extensive semantic redundancy, and that removing such redundancy can improve both in-distribution and out-of-distribution performance, offering a practical path to democratizing large-scale model training by reducing data and compute requirements.

6395b86a1894af4da33e2319f442c04e416450a0.title: No Free Lunch: Fundamental Limits of Learning Non-Hallucinating Generative Models
6395b86a1894af4da33e2319f442c04e416450a0.research_question: What are the fundamental learning-theoretic limits for constructing generative models that do not hallucinate, and under what structural assumptions on the data distribution and the set of factual outputs is non-hallucinating learning statistically possible?
6395b86a1894af4da33e2319f442c04e416450a0.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that non-hallucinating generative models cannot be learned solely from truthful training data without additional structural assumptions or inductive biases about the set of valid outputs (facts), and that restricting the facts set to a concept class of finite VC-dimension enables non-hallucinating learning under certain conditions.
6395b86a1894af4da33e2319f442c04e416450a0.proposed_method: A rigorous theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the learnability of non-hallucinating generative models. The approach formalizes the hallucination rate as the probability that a generative model outputs instances outside a set of facts and distinguishes between proper and improper learning paradigms. The method will include the construction of impossibility proofs for agnostic proper learning, even with small hypothesis classes and fully truthful data, using probabilistic arguments and information-theoretic tools. To overcome these limitations, the framework will introduce inductive biases by restricting the facts set to a concept class with finite VC-dimension, and will design learning rules (both proper and improper) that leverage this structure. Theoretical sample complexity bounds and generalizability criteria based on information measures (e.g., entropy, out-of-sample mass) will be established.
6395b86a1894af4da33e2319f442c04e416450a0.experiment_details: The investigation will be entirely theoretical, relying on formal proofs, constructed examples, and information-theoretic analysis. No empirical datasets will be used; instead, the study will analyze abstract instance spaces, hypothesis classes, and concept classes. Baselines will include standard agnostic PAC learning and distribution learning frameworks, with comparisons drawn to the proposed non-hallucinating learning paradigm. Evaluation will focus on impossibility results, sample complexity upper and lower bounds, and conditions under which non-hallucinating learning is feasible, particularly in relation to the VC-dimension of the concept class and the informativeness of the demonstrator distribution.
6395b86a1894af4da33e2319f442c04e416450a0.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled, learning-theoretic framework for understanding and characterizing the limits of non-hallucinating generative model learning. It establishes new impossibility results showing that, without structural assumptions, non-hallucinating learning is statistically impossible even with truthful data and minimal hypothesis classes. The work provides the first systematic approach to resolving hallucination by incorporating inductive biases via concept classes of finite VC-dimension, and it derives tight sample complexity bounds for both proper and improper learners. These contributions advance the theoretical understanding of hallucination in generative models and offer foundational insights for future algorithmic development.

639a0a95a6f81d89cfa7d30238fd58b2fcd87d20.title: Universal Test-time Adaptation through Weight Ensembling, Diversity Weighting, and Prior Correction
639a0a95a6f81d89cfa7d30238fd58b2fcd87d20.research_question: How can a universal test-time adaptation (TTA) framework be developed to robustly adapt deep neural networks to a wide range of distribution shifts—including domain non-stationarity and temporal correlation—without access to source data, while maintaining generalization and preventing model collapse or bias?
639a0a95a6f81d89cfa7d30238fd58b2fcd87d20.hypothesis: A universal TTA method that combines certainty and diversity-based loss weighting, continual weight ensembling of source and adapted models, and adaptive prior correction can achieve stable and effective adaptation across diverse and challenging test-time scenarios, outperforming existing TTA approaches in terms of robustness, generalization, and avoidance of trivial solutions.
639a0a95a6f81d89cfa7d30238fd58b2fcd87d20.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a universal TTA framework named ROID, which is model- and dataset-agnostic. During test-time, only the network's normalization parameters (e.g., BN, GN, LN) are updated, while all other parameters remain frozen for efficiency. Adaptation is driven by a certainty and diversity-weighted soft likelihood ratio (SLR) loss, where sample weights are computed using a combination of negative entropy (certainty) and cosine similarity to recent model output tendencies (diversity), normalized and exponentiated with a temperature parameter. To maintain generalization and prevent catastrophic forgetting, the method continually ensembles the weights of the initial source model and the adapted model using an exponential moving average with a momentum term. Additionally, an adaptive prior correction scheme is applied, reweighting the model's predictions according to a smoothed estimate of the current class prior, which is dynamically estimated from recent predictions and adaptively smoothed to prevent bias in imbalanced or temporally correlated data.
639a0a95a6f81d89cfa7d30238fd58b2fcd87d20.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a broad set of benchmarks, including corruption datasets (CIFAR10-C, CIFAR100-C, ImageNet-C) and natural domain shift datasets (ImageNet-R, ImageNet-Sketch, ImageNet-D109). Multiple architectures will be evaluated, such as WideResNet-28, ResNeXt-29, ResNet-50, Vision Transformer (ViT-b-16), and Swin Transformer. The evaluation will cover various test-time adaptation settings: continual domain shifts, mixed domains, temporally correlated data, and combinations thereof. Baselines for comparison include state-of-the-art TTA methods such as TENT, EATA, SAR, CoTTA, RoTTA, AdaContrast, RMT, LAME, as well as non-adapted models and normalization-based adaptation. The main evaluation metric is online classification error rate, averaged over multiple runs and reported for different sequence lengths and adaptation scenarios. Ablation studies will analyze the contribution of each component (loss weighting, weight ensembling, prior correction) and assess efficiency, catastrophic forgetting, and memory requirements.
639a0a95a6f81d89cfa7d30238fd58b2fcd87d20.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to explicitly address universal TTA by covering all practically relevant scenarios involving domain non-stationarity and temporal correlation. The method introduces a model- and dataset-agnostic certainty and diversity-based loss weighting scheme, a continual weight ensembling mechanism that preserves generalization, and an adaptive prior correction strategy for handling class prior shifts during test-time. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that the approach sets new standards in universal TTA, achieving superior stability and performance across a wide range of architectures, datasets, and adaptation settings, while avoiding the pitfalls of model collapse, bias, and catastrophic forgetting that affect existing methods.

63c0dbe2426f9c92f469151d1773e5265ae6580e.title: One Embedder, Any Task: Instruction-Finetuned Text Embeddings
63c0dbe2426f9c92f469151d1773e5265ae6580e.research_question: How can a single text embedding model be developed to generate task- and domain-specific embeddings for a wide variety of downstream applications, without requiring further task- or domain-specific finetuning?
63c0dbe2426f9c92f469151d1773e5265ae6580e.hypothesis: Text embeddings can be dynamically tailored to diverse downstream tasks and domains by conditioning the embedding process on explicit natural language instructions, thereby enabling a single model to achieve robust, state-of-the-art performance across a broad range of tasks without additional finetuning.
63c0dbe2426f9c92f469151d1773e5265ae6580e.proposed_method: A unified embedding framework, INSTRUCTOR, will be developed that encodes both the input text and a natural language instruction describing the intended use case (task and domain). The model will be based on a single-encoder architecture, leveraging the GTR (T5-based) family as the backbone, and will be instruction-finetuned on a newly constructed multitask dataset (MEDI) consisting of 330 diverse datasets annotated with human-written task instructions. Training will use a contrastive loss that maximizes the similarity between semantically related text pairs (conditioned on instructions) and minimizes it for unrelated pairs, with both symmetric and asymmetric task formulations included. The instruction format will be unified across datasets, specifying text type, task objective, and optionally domain, to ensure consistency and generalizability.
63c0dbe2426f9c92f469151d1773e5265ae6580e.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training the proposed model on the MEDI dataset, which covers a wide spectrum of tasks (e.g., classification, information retrieval, semantic similarity, summarization, and prompt retrieval) and domains (e.g., finance, medicine, news). Evaluation will be conducted on 70 embedding tasks, including 66 tasks not seen during training, using benchmarks such as MTEB, Billboard, and prompt retrieval datasets. Baseline comparisons will include specialized embedding models (e.g., SimCSE, GTR, Sent-T5) of various sizes. Performance will be measured using standard metrics for each task category (e.g., accuracy, F1, retrieval metrics, clustering scores), and ablation studies will assess the impact of instruction complexity, robustness to instruction paraphrasing, model size scaling, and domain shifts.
63c0dbe2426f9c92f469151d1773e5265ae6580e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces instruction-finetuned text embeddings that are conditioned on explicit task and domain descriptions, enabling a single model to generate context-aware embeddings for any downstream task without further finetuning. The method departs from prior work by embedding both input text and natural language instructions, supporting both symmetric and asymmetric tasks in a unified framework. The construction of the MEDI dataset, with 330 diverse tasks and standardized instructions, provides a new resource for multitask embedding training. The approach claims robust, state-of-the-art performance across a wide variety of unseen tasks and domains, with significant parameter efficiency compared to existing large models.

6405d8836d39e14f325523eec28b6f3806875b6a.title: Rethinking Invariance in In-context Learning
6405d8836d39e14f325523eec28b6f3806875b6a.research_question: How can in-context learning algorithms for large language models be designed to achieve permutation invariance without sacrificing information non-leakage and context interdependence, thereby improving generalization and robustness to context order?
6405d8836d39e14f325523eec28b6f3806875b6a.hypothesis: An in-context learning algorithm that simultaneously enforces permutation invariance, prevents information leakage, and maintains context interdependence will outperform existing invariant and non-invariant methods in terms of generalization, robustness to context order, and length extrapolation.
6405d8836d39e14f325523eec28b6f3806875b6a.proposed_method: A novel in-context learning framework, termed Invariant In-context Learning (InvICL), is proposed to achieve permutation invariance, information non-leakage, and context interdependence. The method employs a two-stage encoding process: first, each context example is pre-encoded using a leave-one-out (LOO) bag-of-examples (BoE) aggregation, ensuring that each example is encoded with the context of all other examples except itself. Second, these contextual encodings are used to predict the test example, aggregating the information in a permutation-invariant manner. To ensure computational efficiency, a parallel implementation is developed that unrolls the input sequence and applies a novel LOO-type attention mask, enabling all LOO embeddings and predictions to be computed in a single forward pass. Symmetric positional encodings are also incorporated to maintain permutation invariance at the input representation level.
6405d8836d39e14f325523eec28b6f3806875b6a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. For synthetic evaluation, linear regression tasks with varying numbers of in-context examples will be used to assess convergence speed, length extrapolation, and out-of-distribution generalization. For real-world evaluation, the MetaICL benchmark will be utilized, which includes 142 tasks spanning text classification, question answering, natural language inference, and paraphrase detection. Models will be fine-tuned using a meta-learning objective, and performance will be compared against baselines including auto-regressive ICL, Prefix ICL, and several bag-of-examples ICL variants. Evaluation metrics include mean squared error for regression and classification accuracy for NLP tasks. Additional analyses will measure order sensitivity, computational cost, and memory overhead. Ablation studies will isolate the effects of the invariant mask and symmetric positional encoding.
6405d8836d39e14f325523eec28b6f3806875b6a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to simultaneously achieve permutation invariance, information non-leakage, and context interdependence in in-context learning for large language models. The method introduces a principled two-stage leave-one-out encoding scheme and a parallel implementation with a novel attention mask, enabling efficient and scalable computation. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior generalization, robustness to context order, and length extrapolation compared to both invariant and non-invariant baselines. The framework also provides new theoretical insights into the design of invariant in-context learning algorithms.

641828b8ca714a0f70ccdac17d7e9dff485877c2.title: How Powerful are Spectral Graph Neural Networks
641828b8ca714a0f70ccdac17d7e9dff485877c2.research_question: What is the theoretical and empirical expressive power of spectral graph neural networks (GNNs), and how can the choice of spectral filter basis and model architecture influence their universality and optimization properties?
641828b8ca714a0f70ccdac17d7e9dff485877c2.hypothesis: Spectral GNNs, even without nonlinearity, can achieve universal expressive power under mild conditions related to graph Laplacian eigenvalues and node feature frequency components. Furthermore, using an orthogonal polynomial basis for spectral filters, particularly Jacobi polynomials, will improve optimization and empirical performance compared to existing bases.
641828b8ca714a0f70ccdac17d7e9dff485877c2.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical analysis will be conducted to characterize the expressive power of spectral GNNs, focusing on conditions under which linear (nonlinear-free) spectral GNNs can approximate arbitrary graph signals. The study will establish connections between spectral GNN universality and graph isomorphism testing (e.g., Weisfeiler-Lehman test). Based on these insights, a new spectral GNN architecture, JacobiConv, will be developed. JacobiConv will leverage Jacobi polynomial bases for spectral filters due to their orthogonality and adaptability to various signal densities, and will omit nonlinearity to maximize theoretical expressiveness and optimization efficiency. A novel Polynomial Coefficient Decomposition (PCD) technique will be incorporated to improve filter coefficient optimization. The model will use individual filter functions for each output dimension and efficient recursive computation of Jacobi bases.
641828b8ca714a0f70ccdac17d7e9dff485877c2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic experiments will use image-derived grid graphs with various spectral filters applied to node signals, evaluating models on their ability to fit filtered signals using mean squared error. Real-world experiments will include node classification tasks on standard benchmark datasets (e.g., Cora, CiteSeer, PubMed, Amazon Computers/Photo, Chameleon, Squirrel, Actor, Texas, Cornell), with random train/validation/test splits. Baselines will include state-of-the-art spectral GNNs such as GCN, APPNP, ChebyNet, GPRGNN, and BernNet, as well as linear GNNs with different polynomial bases (Monomial, Chebyshev, Bernstein). Evaluation metrics will be accuracy for classification and mean squared error for regression. Ablation studies will assess the impact of basis choice, PCD, multiple filters, and nonlinearity. Computational efficiency and scalability will be measured by model parameter counts and training times.
641828b8ca714a0f70ccdac17d7e9dff485877c2.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a rigorous theoretical framework establishing universality conditions for spectral GNNs without nonlinearity, connecting their expressive power to graph isomorphism testing. It claims that nonlinearity is not necessary for universality in spectral GNNs under practical conditions. The JacobiConv architecture is novel in its use of Jacobi polynomial bases for spectral filtering, providing adaptability to signal distributions and improved optimization via orthogonality. The Polynomial Coefficient Decomposition (PCD) technique is an innovative approach to stabilizing filter coefficient learning. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art performance and efficiency, surpassing existing spectral GNNs, and validating the theoretical findings.

641d7866db6691e22aa36de5c8ba05804233c016.title: Side Adapter Network for Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation
641d7866db6691e22aa36de5c8ba05804233c016.research_question: How can open-vocabulary semantic segmentation be achieved efficiently and accurately by leveraging large-scale vision-language models, such as CLIP, without compromising their open-vocabulary recognition capabilities?
641d7866db6691e22aa36de5c8ba05804233c016.hypothesis: Integrating a lightweight, end-to-end trainable side adapter network with a frozen vision-language model, while decoupling mask proposal and recognition, will enable efficient and accurate open-vocabulary semantic segmentation with minimal additional parameters and computational cost.
641d7866db6691e22aa36de5c8ba05804233c016.proposed_method: A novel framework, termed Side Adapter Network (SAN), will be developed for open-vocabulary semantic segmentation. This framework attaches a lightweight vision transformer-based side network to a frozen CLIP model. The side adapter network consists of two branches: one for generating mask proposals and another for predicting attention biases, which are injected into the self-attention layers of the CLIP model to guide mask recognition. The side adapter network fuses features from shallow CLIP layers at multiple points, while deeper CLIP layers, modulated by the predicted attention biases, are used for region-level class recognition. The entire system is trained end-to-end, allowing the side adapter network to adapt maximally to the frozen CLIP model, making mask proposals and recognition CLIP-aware. Asymmetric input resolutions are used, with high-resolution images for the side adapter and low-resolution images for the CLIP model, and only a small number of additional trainable parameters are introduced.
641d7866db6691e22aa36de5c8ba05804233c016.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six datasets: COCO Stuff (used for training), and Pascal VOC, Pascal Context-59, Pascal Context-459, ADE20K-150, and ADE20K-847 (used for testing). The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as SimSeg, OvSeg, and MaskCLIP, using the same CLIP ViT-B/16 and ViT-L/14 backbones. Evaluation metrics will include mean Intersection over Union (mIoU), trainable parameter count, GFLOPs, and inference speed (FPS). The experimental setup will use standardized training protocols, including AdamW optimizer, poly learning rate schedule, and data augmentations. Ablation studies will investigate the impact of feature fusion, decoupled mask/recognition heads, input resolution, and prompt engineering.
641d7866db6691e22aa36de5c8ba05804233c016.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a lightweight, end-to-end trainable side adapter network that leverages the frozen CLIP model for open-vocabulary semantic segmentation. The method decouples mask proposal and recognition, enabling efficient region-level recognition with minimal additional parameters and computation.
