Feature fusion from CLIP layers and the use of attention biases in self-attention blocks are novel components that improve segmentation accuracy. The framework achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks, with significantly fewer trainable parameters and faster inference compared to prior methods, and demonstrates superior open-vocabulary generalization, especially on datasets with low overlap to the training set.

6456633ccec43778e18d6eef5c8e1d54687437e2.title: Fat-Tailed Variational Inference with Anisotropic Tail Adaptive Flows
6456633ccec43778e18d6eef5c8e1d54687437e2.research_question: How can variational inference methods be improved to accurately model fat-tailed and tail-anisotropic distributions, particularly in scenarios where existing flow-based approaches are limited by tail-isotropy?
6456633ccec43778e18d6eef5c8e1d54687437e2.hypothesis: Introducing a variational inference framework that leverages anisotropic tail-adaptive flows (ATAF) with direction-dependent tail parameters will enable accurate modeling of fat-tailed and tail-anisotropic distributions, overcoming the limitations of current flow-based methods that are restricted to tail-isotropic distributions.
6456633ccec43778e18d6eef5c8e1d54687437e2.proposed_method: A new class of variational inference methods will be developed based on anisotropic tail-adaptive flows (ATAF). The approach will use normalizing flows with a base distribution parameterized as a product of independent Student-T distributions, each with its own learnable degrees-of-freedom parameter, thereby allowing for direction-dependent (anisotropic) tail behavior. The method will extend the theory of fat-tailed random variables by introducing a direction-dependent tail parameter function, enabling the variational family to capture distributions with different rates of tail decay along different axes. During training, both the flow parameters and the tail parameters of the base distribution will be jointly optimized via stochastic gradient descent on the evidence lower bound (ELBO). The approach will be compatible with invertible neural network architectures for the flow component, ensuring tractable density evaluation and efficient sampling.
6456633ccec43778e18d6eef5c8e1d54687437e2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets to evaluate the effectiveness of ATAF. Synthetic experiments will include target distributions with explicit tail-anisotropy, such as mixtures of Student-T and Gaussian marginals, to visually and quantitatively assess the ability to recover correct tail behavior. Real-world experiments will cover Bayesian linear regression (both conjugate and non-conjugate cases), hierarchical models (e.g., the eight schools model), financial returns (Fama-French industry indices), and insurance claims (CMS datasets). Baselines will include Automatic Differentiation Variational Inference (ADVI) with Gaussian base, Tail-Adaptive Flows (TAF) with isotropic Student-T base, and gold-standard posterior samples from No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS) where feasible. Evaluation metrics will include Monte Carlo estimates of the ELBO, importance-weighted marginal likelihoods, and log-likelihoods on held-out data. The experimental setup will ensure consistent flow architectures and optimization procedures across methods for fair comparison.
6456633ccec43778e18d6eef5c8e1d54687437e2.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first variational inference framework capable of modeling tail-anisotropic distributions using flow-based methods. It provides a theoretical foundation for direction-dependent tail parameters in multivariate settings and demonstrates that prior flow-based approaches are fundamentally limited to tail-isotropic distributions. The method enables the variational family to capture distributions with different tail behaviors along different axes, which is not possible with existing normalizing flow or isotropic tail-adaptive flow approaches. Empirical results are expected to show improved fit and more accurate tail modeling in both synthetic and real-world tasks, particularly in scenarios where tail-anisotropy is present.

648495b844531dce7c581662bf90c339422bf16c.title: How to build a consistency model: Learning flow maps via self-distillation
648495b844531dce7c581662bf90c339422bf16c.research_question: How can flow maps be learned efficiently for accelerated inference in flow-based generative models, and what unified algorithmic framework can systematically address the design and training of such models across different modalities and objectives?
648495b844531dce7c581662bf90c339422bf16c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a unified self-distillation framework, leveraging mathematical characterizations of flow maps, can enable stable and efficient direct training of flow maps for generative modeling, eliminating the need for pre-trained teacher models and improving inference speed and sample quality.
648495b844531dce7c581662bf90c339422bf16c.proposed_method: A systematic algorithmic framework will be developed for learning flow maps directly via self-distillation, without reliance on pre-trained teacher models. The approach will exploit the mathematical relationship between the velocity field of a continuous-time flow and the instantaneous rate of change of the flow map, using the tangent condition to connect the two. Three algorithmic families will be introduced based on distinct mathematical characterizations: Lagrangian Self-Distillation (LSD), Eulerian Self-Distillation (ESD), and Progressive Self-Distillation (PSD). Each family will define a specific loss function: LSD leverages the Lagrangian ODE condition, ESD the Eulerian PDE condition, and PSD the semigroup (composition) property. The framework will use a single neural network parameterization of the flow map, with training objectives combining flow-matching on the diagonal (s = t) and self-distillation off-diagonal, and will incorporate loss weighting and temporal sampling strategies to stabilize optimization.
648495b844531dce7c581662bf90c339422bf16c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and high-dimensional real-world datasets to evaluate the proposed methods. Datasets will include the synthetic checkerboard dataset for low-dimensional visualization, and standard image generation benchmarks such as CIFAR-10, CelebA-64, and AFHQ-64. Each algorithmic family (LSD, ESD, PSD-U, PSD-M) will be compared under fixed training time and across varying numbers of sampling steps (1, 2, 4, 8, 16) to assess trade-offs in sample quality and efficiency. Evaluation metrics will include KL divergence for the checkerboard dataset and Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for image datasets. Baselines will consist of existing distillation and direct training schemes for consistency models. The experimental setup will control for batch size, loss weighting, and sampling distributions, and will analyze training stability, gradient norms, and qualitative sample quality.
648495b844531dce7c581662bf90c339422bf16c.novelty_claims: The proposed framework unifies and generalizes all known distillation and direct training schemes for consistency models under a single mathematical and algorithmic paradigm. It introduces the concept of self-distillation for flow maps, eliminating the need for pre-trained teacher models and enabling direct, stable, and efficient training. The Lagrangian self-distillation method is identified as a novel class that avoids both spatial derivatives and bootstrapping from small steps, resulting in more stable training and higher performance. The framework provides new theoretical guarantees on model accuracy and reveals fundamental design principles for accelerated generative modeling. Additionally, it offers practical algorithmic prescriptions for loss weighting, temporal sampling, and model parameterization, facilitating systematic construction of few-step generative models.

6484f54338396af3e8a3a39970d95bd303a19f76.title: Sherlock: Self-Correcting Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
6484f54338396af3e8a3a39970d95bd303a19f76.research_question: How can vision-language models (VLMs) be equipped with effective self-correction capabilities to improve their reasoning performance, reduce reliance on large annotated datasets, and generalize better across diverse multimodal tasks?
6484f54338396af3e8a3a39970d95bd303a19f76.hypothesis: Integrating a trajectory-level self-correction objective and preference-based training into VLMs will enable these models to autonomously revise erroneous reasoning steps, leading to improved reasoning accuracy, reduced annotation requirements, and enhanced generalization across benchmarks.
6484f54338396af3e8a3a39970d95bd303a19f76.proposed_method: A novel training framework will be developed to endow VLMs with self-correction and self-improvement capabilities. The approach consists of three stages: (1) supervised fine-tuning (SFT) using a pairwise objective that jointly optimizes for reasoning and response-wise self-correction on a small set of annotated chain-of-thought (CoT) data; (2) offline preference training with a trajectory-level self-correction objective, where the model learns to revise only the erroneous suffix of a reasoning trajectory using constructed preference pairs generated via visual perturbations and truncations; (3) iterative online self-improvement, in which the model generates and selects preferred responses via multiple rounds of self-correction on unlabeled data, using self-consistency filtering and dynamic sample-specific preference scaling (dynamic β) to stabilize learning. The entire pipeline is designed to minimize the need for external supervision and verifiers, leveraging self-generated data for continual improvement.
6484f54338396af3e8a3a39970d95bd303a19f76.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Llama3.2-Vision-11B-Instruct model as the backbone. The proposed method will be evaluated on eight challenging multimodal benchmarks, including VQA (MMBench-V1.1, MMVet, MME, MMStar), math and science (MathVista, AI2D, MMMU), and hallucination detection (HallusionBench). Baselines will include state-of-the-art reasoning VLMs such as LLaVA-CoT, Mulberry, and LlamaV-o1, as well as inference-time self-correction methods like MajorityVote and critique-based approaches using LLaVA-Critic, Critic-V, and Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct. Evaluation metrics will primarily focus on average accuracy across benchmarks, with additional analysis of self-correction gains, data efficiency, and inference-time compute costs. The experimental setup will utilize only 20k randomly sampled annotated examples for initial training, with subsequent online self-improvement relying solely on unlabeled data.
6484f54338396af3e8a3a39970d95bd303a19f76.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the first trajectory-level self-correction objective for VLMs, enabling fine-grained correction of reasoning trajectories rather than full-response revision. The method leverages a controllable preference data construction pipeline based on visual perturbations and truncations, and incorporates a dynamic β scaling mechanism for stable preference optimization. The approach demonstrates that self-correction and reasoning are mutually reinforcing capabilities, and achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks using less than 20% of the annotated data required by prior methods. Additionally, the framework enables efficient inference-time scaling with verifier integration, reducing compute costs while improving accuracy.

648d90b713997a771e2c49f02cd771e8b7b10b37.title: Self-Supervised Contrastive Pre-Training For Time Series via Time-Frequency Consistency
648d90b713997a771e2c49f02cd771e8b7b10b37.research_question: How can self-supervised pre-training for time series data be improved to enable effective knowledge transfer across diverse domains, especially when target domain data is unavailable during pre-training?
648d90b713997a771e2c49f02cd771e8b7b10b37.hypothesis: Enforcing time-frequency consistency—aligning time-based and frequency-based representations of the same time series sample in a shared latent space—will produce generalizable representations that improve downstream performance across diverse time series domains, even in the absence of target domain data during pre-training.
648d90b713997a771e2c49f02cd771e8b7b10b37.proposed_method: A self-supervised contrastive pre-training framework is developed that explicitly enforces time-frequency consistency (TF-C) in learned representations. The method utilizes two parallel encoders: a time-based encoder that processes temporally augmented versions of the input, and a frequency-based encoder that processes frequency-augmented versions (via Fourier transform and spectrum perturbations) of the same input. Each encoder is paired with a projection head to map embeddings into a shared latent space. Three loss components are combined: (1) a time-based contrastive loss (NT-Xent) to ensure invariance to temporal augmentations, (2) a frequency-based contrastive loss to ensure invariance to frequency perturbations, and (3) a novel consistency loss that minimizes the distance between time-based and frequency-based embeddings (and their augmentations) of the same sample, using a triplet-style margin. The overall objective encourages the model to learn representations that are robust to both temporal and spectral variations and that align across domains.
648d90b713997a771e2c49f02cd771e8b7b10b37.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on eight diverse time series datasets spanning domains such as electrodiagnostic testing (EEG, EMG, ECG), human activity recognition, mechanical fault detection, and physical status monitoring. Both one-to-one (single pre-training and fine-tuning dataset) and one-to-many (single pre-training dataset, multiple independent fine-tuning datasets) transfer scenarios are evaluated. The proposed approach is compared against ten baselines, including state-of-the-art self-supervised and transfer learning methods (e.g., TS-SD, TS2vec, CLOCS, TS-TCC, SimCLR, TNC, CPC, Mixing-up), as well as non-deep learning and random initialization baselines. Evaluation metrics include accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, AUROC, and AUPRC, with results averaged over five runs per split. Ablation studies assess the contribution of each loss component, and additional downstream tasks such as clustering (using K-means, evaluated by Silhouette score, ARI, NMI) and anomaly detection (using one-class SVM) are performed to demonstrate generalizability.
648d90b713997a771e2c49f02cd771e8b7b10b37.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the concept of time-frequency consistency (TF-C) as a universal property for pre-training on time series, enabling knowledge transfer without access to target domain data. This is the first method to directly leverage frequency-based contrastive augmentations by perturbing the frequency spectrum for self-supervised learning in time series. The framework combines time-based and frequency-based contrastive learning with a novel consistency loss to align representations in a shared latent space, resulting in more robust and generalizable features. Empirical results demonstrate significant improvements over state-of-the-art baselines in both standard and challenging transfer scenarios, as well as superior performance in clustering and anomaly detection tasks.

6498ef6ada16e3740c526a35d5ff1d48f2f64935.title: Tractable Function-Space Variational Inference in Bayesian Neural Networks
6498ef6ada16e3740c526a35d5ff1d48f2f64935.research_question: How can reliable predictive uncertainty estimation be achieved in Bayesian neural networks, particularly in high-dimensional and safety-critical settings, by leveraging function-space inference rather than parameter-space inference?
6498ef6ada16e3740c526a35d5ff1d48f2f64935.hypothesis: Function-space variational inference, when made tractable and scalable for large neural networks and high-dimensional data, will yield more reliable and calibrated predictive uncertainty estimates than existing parameter-space methods, especially under distribution shift and in safety-critical tasks.
6498ef6ada16e3740c526a35d5ff1d48f2f64935.proposed_method: A scalable function-space variational inference (FSVI) framework is developed for Bayesian neural networks. The approach frames variational inference as directly approximating the posterior distribution over functions induced by the posterior over parameters, rather than over parameters themselves. The method employs a tractable approximation to the function-space Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence by locally linearizing the neural network around the mean of the variational distribution and using Gaussian approximations for both prior and variational distributions. The KL divergence between the induced function distributions is estimated via Monte Carlo sampling over context sets drawn from a context distribution, which can incorporate domain knowledge or unlabeled data. The variational objective is optimized using stochastic gradient-based methods, and the resulting variational distribution is used to sample functions for posterior predictive inference.
6498ef6ada16e3740c526a35d5ff1d48f2f64935.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on high-dimensional classification tasks such as FashionMNIST and CIFAR-10, with out-of-distribution (OOD) evaluation using datasets like MNIST, NotMNIST, SVHN, and corrupted CIFAR-10. The method will also be evaluated on a safety-critical medical diagnosis task using the EyePACS and APTOS diabetic retinopathy datasets. Baselines for comparison include MAP, mean-field variational inference (MFVI), MC Dropout, SWAG, DUQ, BNN-Laplace, SPG, Deep Ensembles, and other state-of-the-art Bayesian and non-Bayesian uncertainty quantification methods. Evaluation metrics include test accuracy, negative log-likelihood (NLL), expected calibration error (ECE), area under the ROC curve (AUROC) for OOD detection, Brier scores, and selective prediction performance. All methods will use consistent neural network architectures (e.g., four-layer CNNs or ResNet-18) and standardized training and evaluation protocols.
6498ef6ada16e3740c526a35d5ff1d48f2f64935.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a tractable and scalable estimator for the function-space variational objective in Bayesian neural networks, enabling application to large-scale, high-dimensional data and architectures that were previously infeasible for function-space inference. The approach allows explicit incorporation of prior information about the data-generating process via context distributions and prior design. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art predictive uncertainty estimation and robustness to distribution shift, outperforming both Bayesian and non-Bayesian baselines in calibration, OOD detection, and safety-critical tasks. The method advances the practical applicability of function-space inference in deep learning.

6499de8b17ec7e4c7ee616c6e102b2d4b6dd5e4d.title: Momentum-SAM: Sharpness Aware Minimization without Computational Overhead
6499de8b17ec7e4c7ee616c6e102b2d4b6dd5e4d.research_question: How can sharpness-aware minimization be achieved in deep neural network optimization without incurring significant computational overhead, and what are the effects of such methods on generalization and training efficiency across various architectures and datasets?
6499de8b17ec7e4c7ee616c6e102b2d4b6dd5e4d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that perturbing model parameters in the direction of the accumulated momentum vector, rather than the local gradient, can effectively minimize loss sharpness and improve generalization performance without requiring additional forward or backward passes, thus maintaining computational efficiency comparable to standard optimizers.
6499de8b17ec7e4c7ee616c6e102b2d4b6dd5e4d.proposed_method: A novel optimization algorithm, Momentum-SAM (MSAM), is developed to minimize the sharpness of the training loss by perturbing neural network parameters in the direction of the momentum vector accumulated by optimizers such as SGD or Adam. The perturbation is scaled by a hyperparameter and normalized by the norm of the momentum vector, and is applied in the negative momentum direction to induce a loss ascent suitable for sharpness estimation. The method integrates seamlessly with existing momentum-based optimizers, requiring no additional memory and incurring negligible computational overhead, as the momentum buffer is already maintained. The parameter perturbation is temporarily applied before each gradient calculation and removed after the update, ensuring that the optimization process remains efficient and compatible with standard training pipelines.
6499de8b17ec7e4c7ee616c6e102b2d4b6dd5e4d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on benchmark image classification datasets such as CIFAR100 and ImageNet-1k, utilizing architectures including WideResNet-28-10, WideResNet-16-4, ResNet-50, and various Vision Transformer (ViT) models. The proposed MSAM optimizer will be compared against baseline optimizers (SGD, AdamW, Nesterov Accelerated Gradient), as well as state-of-the-art sharpness-aware methods (SAM, LookSAM, ESAM, MESA). Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy, training speed (relative runtime), and sharpness measures along various perturbation directions. Hyperparameters such as learning rate, weight decay, and perturbation strength will be tuned for each optimizer and model. Additional experiments will assess the compatibility of MSAM with adaptive perturbation scaling and batch normalization-only perturbations, and analyze the loss landscape and generalization properties using sharpness and feature rank metrics.
6499de8b17ec7e4c7ee616c6e102b2d4b6dd5e4d.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a sharpness-aware minimization algorithm that achieves generalization improvements comparable to SAM but without the computational overhead of additional forward and backward passes. By leveraging the momentum direction for parameter perturbation, MSAM provides an efficient and memory-light alternative to existing sharpness-aware optimizers. The approach offers new insights into the relationship between momentum, sharpness, and generalization, and demonstrates that effective sharpness minimization can be achieved with perturbations independent of the local gradient. Empirical analysis reveals that MSAM can outperform or match the accuracy of state-of-the-art methods at a fraction of the computational cost, enabling broader applicability in resource-constrained scenarios.

64d80a697ee9c914fc034f1e110b5f7ae91261c6.title: Universal Off-Policy Evaluation
64d80a697ee9c914fc034f1e110b5f7ae91261c6.research_question: How can a universal off-policy evaluation method be developed that provides accurate estimates and high-confidence finite-sample bounds for any parameter of the return distribution, across a broad range of sequential decision-making settings, including those with partial observability, confounding, non-Markovian dynamics, and distributional shifts?
64d80a697ee9c914fc034f1e110b5f7ae91261c6.hypothesis: It is possible to construct a model-free, non-parametric off-policy estimator that can simultaneously estimate and provide high-confidence bounds for any parameter of the return distribution, such as mean, variance, quantiles, CVaR, and the full cumulative distribution, even under partial observability, confounding, and non-stationary environments.
64d80a697ee9c914fc034f1e110b5f7ae91261c6.proposed_method: A universal off-policy evaluation framework will be developed by first estimating the entire cumulative distribution function (CDF) of returns for a target policy using importance sampling corrections applied to off-policy data. The method constructs a non-parametric estimator for the CDF by reweighting observed trajectory returns according to the likelihood ratio between the evaluation and behavior policies. From this estimated CDF, plug-in estimators for any desired distributional parameter (e.g., mean, variance, quantiles, CVaR) are derived. To provide high-confidence bounds, a confidence band for the CDF is constructed using concentration inequalities adapted for the off-policy setting, and parameter-specific bounds are obtained by optimizing over the set of CDFs within this band. The approach is further extended to handle confounding, discrete distributional shifts, and smoothly non-stationary environments by incorporating domain-specific assumptions and time-series forecasting techniques, such as wild bootstrap for non-stationarity.
64d80a697ee9c914fc034f1e110b5f7ae91261c6.experiment_details: Empirical evaluation will be conducted on several domains: (1) an open-source implementation of an FDA-approved type-1 diabetes treatment simulator, (2) stationary and non-stationary recommender system environments, and (3) a continuous-state Gridworld with partial observability and data collected from multiple behavior policies. The proposed method will be compared against specialized baselines for mean and variance estimation, including tight IS-based confidence bounds and variance estimators. Evaluation metrics will include the accuracy of estimated CDFs, mean, variance, quantiles, and CVaR, as well as the coverage and tightness of the constructed confidence intervals. Experiments will assess performance under varying data regimes, degrees of confounding, and levels of non-stationarity, with results averaged over multiple trials to report standard errors.
64d80a697ee9c914fc034f1e110b5f7ae91261c6.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to provide a universal, model-free, non-parametric off-policy estimator that can estimate and simultaneously bound any parameter of the return distribution with high confidence, even in the presence of confounding, non-Markovian dynamics, and distributional shifts. Unlike prior methods, which are limited to specific parameters (e.g., mean or variance) and often require strong assumptions, this method enables comprehensive policy evaluation for a wide class of performance metrics. The framework also introduces the use of statistical bootstrapping for tighter, albeit approximate, bounds and demonstrates adaptability to both stationary and non-stationary domains.

64ea8f180d0682e6c18d1eb688afdb2027c02794.title: Diffusion Models Beat GANs on Image Synthesis
64ea8f180d0682e6c18d1eb688afdb2027c02794.research_question: Can diffusion models be improved to achieve or surpass the image synthesis quality of state-of-the-art generative adversarial networks (GANs) on large-scale, high-resolution datasets, and can their fidelity-diversity tradeoff be effectively controlled?
64ea8f180d0682e6c18d1eb688afdb2027c02794.hypothesis: Diffusion models, when equipped with improved architectures and classifier guidance, can outperform GANs in image synthesis quality, while also providing a controllable tradeoff between sample fidelity and diversity.
64ea8f180d0682e6c18d1eb688afdb2027c02794.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that enhances diffusion models for image synthesis through two main strategies: (1) systematic architectural improvements to the UNet backbone, including increased width, multi-resolution attention, BigGAN-style residual blocks for up/downsampling, and adaptive group normalization for injecting timestep and class embeddings; and (2) the introduction of classifier guidance, which conditions the diffusion sampling process using gradients from a separately trained image classifier. The classifier guidance mechanism allows for a tunable tradeoff between fidelity and diversity by scaling the classifier gradients during sampling. Both unconditional and class-conditional diffusion models are considered, and the classifier guidance is applied to both settings, with the option to combine with upsampling diffusion models for higher resolutions.
64ea8f180d0682e6c18d1eb688afdb2027c02794.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale image synthesis benchmarks, including LSUN (bedroom, horse, cat) and ImageNet at resolutions 64×64, 128×128, 256×256, and 512×512. The models will be trained with batch sizes up to 256 and evaluated using Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), spatial FID (sFID), Inception Score (IS), and precision/recall metrics. Baselines will include state-of-the-art GANs (BigGAN-deep, StyleGAN2), prior diffusion models (DDPM, IDDPM), and other likelihood-based models (VQ-VAE-2, DCTransformer). Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of each architectural change, attention configuration, and the effect of classifier guidance scale. Sampling efficiency will be evaluated by varying the number of diffusion steps, including the use of DDIM for fast sampling. Comparisons will also be made between guidance and upsampling approaches, and all metrics will be recomputed using a consistent codebase and the full training set as the reference batch.
64ea8f180d0682e6c18d1eb688afdb2027c02794.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a set of architectural improvements that significantly boost the sample quality of diffusion models at high resolutions. It presents a simple, compute-efficient classifier guidance technique that enables explicit control over the fidelity-diversity tradeoff using a single hyperparameter, outperforming GANs in both FID and coverage on challenging datasets. The method achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple image synthesis benchmarks, matches or surpasses GAN performance with as few as 25 diffusion steps, and demonstrates that classifier guidance can be effectively combined with upsampling diffusion models for further gains. The approach is general, scalable, and provides a new paradigm for controllable, high-quality image synthesis.

65022cdf3cba83ca2000ce18e694ff54ce2ca787.title: DreamGaussian4D: Generative 4D Gaussian Splatting
65022cdf3cba83ca2000ce18e694ff54ce2ca787.research_question: How can efficient, high-quality, and controllable 4D dynamic scene generation be achieved from a single image or video, overcoming the limitations of long optimization times, limited motion controllability, and low detail quality present in existing methods?
65022cdf3cba83ca2000ce18e694ff54ce2ca787.hypothesis: Explicit modeling of spatial transformations using 3D Gaussian Splatting combined with HexPlane-based 4D representations, along with video-driven optimization and video-to-video texture refinement, will significantly reduce optimization time, improve motion controllability, and enhance the quality and temporal consistency of generated 4D content.
65022cdf3cba83ca2000ce18e694ff54ce2ca787.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a two-stage framework for 4D content generation. In the first stage, a static 3D Gaussian Splatting (GS) model is generated from an input image using an enhanced DreamGaussianHD pipeline, which incorporates multi-view optimization and fixed background color for improved geometry and texture quality. Dynamic motion is then introduced by training a HexPlane-based deformation network that predicts position, rotation, and scale changes for each Gaussian at different timestamps, supervised by a driving video generated via an image-to-video diffusion model. The deformation network is initialized to predict zero deformation at the start of training to ensure consistency between static and dynamic models. In the second stage, a video-to-video texture refinement pipeline is applied, utilizing a pre-trained image-to-video diffusion model to denoise and enhance the UV-space texture maps of the animated mesh sequence, thereby improving temporal consistency and visual quality. The entire process is designed for rapid optimization, with explicit control over motion via the choice of driving video.
65022cdf3cba83ca2000ce18e694ff54ce2ca787.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a single 80GB A100 GPU. The framework will be implemented on top of open-source repositories for DreamGaussian and 4D Gaussian Splatting. For driving video generation, Stable Video Diffusion will be used to create 14-frame sequences. Static optimization will run for 500 iterations with a batch size of 16, and dynamic representation will be optimized for 200 iterations with a batch size of 4. Optional mesh refinement will involve 50 iterations at a fixed noise level. The proposed method will be evaluated on both image-to-4D and video-to-4D tasks, using datasets and benchmarks from prior works such as Animate124 and Consistent4D. Baselines will include MAV3D, Animate124, Consistent4D, 4D-fy, and others. Evaluation metrics will include CLIP-I for image alignment, LPIPS for perceptual similarity, FVD for video quality, and user studies assessing image alignment, 3D appearance, and motion quality. Optimization and rendering times will be compared to state-of-the-art methods.
65022cdf3cba83ca2000ce18e694ff54ce2ca787.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a principled image-to-4D generation pipeline that synergizes image-conditioned 3D generation with video-driven motion control, enabling explicit and diverse motion generation from a single image. The use of explicit 4D representations via 3D Gaussian Splatting and HexPlane allows for rapid optimization and high-quality, temporally consistent 4D content. The video-to-video texture refinement module further enhances mesh quality and temporal coherence, making the method practical for real-world deployment. The approach achieves comparable or superior results to existing methods with a fraction of the optimization time, and uniquely enables user-controllable motion diversity through flexible driving video selection.

6518091d7f2af10629b836df8c7a53ce4104c4fb.title: Token Merging for Fast Stable Diffusion
6518091d7f2af10629b836df8c7a53ce4104c4fb.research_question: How can the computational efficiency of open vocabulary diffusion models for image generation, such as Stable Diffusion, be improved without sacrificing image quality or requiring additional training?
6518091d7f2af10629b836df8c7a53ce4104c4fb.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that merging redundant tokens within the transformer-based backbone of diffusion models can significantly reduce computation and memory usage while maintaining high image quality, and that diffusion-specific improvements to token merging will further enhance this effect.
6518091d7f2af10629b836df8c7a53ce4104c4fb.proposed_method: A new approach is developed that applies an improved token merging (ToMe) strategy to the transformer blocks within the U-Net architecture of Stable Diffusion. The method merges the most similar tokens before each component (e.g., self-attention, cross-attention, MLP) of each block and subsequently unmerges them after computation to preserve dense prediction requirements. Several diffusion-specific modifications are introduced, including a novel token partitioning scheme that randomly selects destination tokens within local 2x2 regions and synchronizes randomness across the batch to ensure consistent prompt adherence. The merging is primarily applied to self-attention modules in blocks with the most tokens, and the percentage of merged tokens can be tuned per diffusion step, with more aggressive merging in earlier steps. This approach is designed to require no additional training and is compatible with existing transformer acceleration libraries.
6518091d7f2af10629b836df8c7a53ce4104c4fb.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using Stable Diffusion v1.5 to generate 2,000 images of size 512x512 from ImageNet-1k classes, with 50 diffusion steps and a classifier-free guidance scale of 7.5. The quality of generated images is evaluated using the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) between the generated samples and 5,000 class-balanced ImageNet-1k validation images. Speed and memory usage are measured by averaging inference time and GPU memory consumption on an NVIDIA 4090 GPU. Baselines include the original Stable Diffusion model and variants with different token reduction rates and partitioning schemes. The method is also tested in combination with xFormers for further speedup, and performance is evaluated for both small (512x512) and large (2048x2048) images.
6518091d7f2af10629b836df8c7a53ce4104c4fb.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first application of token merging to diffusion models for dense prediction tasks without requiring any retraining. It presents diffusion-specific improvements to token merging, including a novel partitioning strategy and batch-consistent randomness, enabling up to 60% token reduction with minimal impact on image quality. The approach achieves up to 2x faster image generation and up to 5.6x less memory usage, with speedups stacking with existing transformer acceleration techniques. This work demonstrates that significant efficiency gains in diffusion models are possible without compromising visual fidelity or prompt adherence.

6565b9978b0a29bf20d09e584f545cdcec0c96ec.title: On the Closed-Form of Flow Matching: Generalization Does Not Arise from Target Stochasticity
6565b9978b0a29bf20d09e584f545cdcec0c96ec.research_question: What are the fundamental factors driving generalization in flow matching-based deep generative models, and does the stochasticity of the training loss contribute significantly to this generalization, especially in high-dimensional data settings?
6565b9978b0a29bf20d09e584f545cdcec0c96ec.hypothesis: Generalization in flow matching models does not primarily arise from the stochasticity of the target in the training loss; instead, it emerges when neural networks fail to perfectly approximate the optimal closed-form velocity field, particularly at certain critical time intervals during training.
6565b9978b0a29bf20d09e584f545cdcec0c96ec.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical and theoretical investigation is proposed to disentangle the sources of generalization in flow matching generative models. The approach involves leveraging the closed-form solution for the optimal velocity field in flow matching, enabling direct regression against this deterministic target rather than its stochastic approximation. The methodology includes constructing hybrid models that interpolate between following the closed-form velocity and the learned neural velocity, allowing precise control over the temporal phases of the generative process. Additionally, a Monte Carlo-based empirical flow matching (EFM) algorithm is developed to efficiently estimate the closed-form velocity in high-dimensional settings, ensuring unbiased and lower-variance targets for training. The method systematically analyzes the impact of dataset size, model capacity, and time intervals on the ability of models to generalize beyond memorizing training data.
6565b9978b0a29bf20d09e584f545cdcec0c96ec.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard high-dimensional image datasets such as CIFAR-10 and CelebA (64x64). The evaluation will compare models trained with vanilla conditional flow matching, optimal transport flow matching, and the proposed empirical flow matching (EFM) with varying numbers of samples for the empirical mean. Baselines will include both stochastic and deterministic target regressions. Performance will be assessed using Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) with both Inception-V3 and DINOv2 embeddings, computed against both training and test sets, as well as LPIPS distance to quantify memorization and creativity. Additional analyses will include measuring the distance between generated samples and their nearest training neighbor, and evaluating the effect of following the closed-form velocity field for different portions of the generative trajectory. All experiments will control for model architecture (e.g., fixed-parameter U-Nets) and dataset size to isolate the effects of interest.
6565b9978b0a29bf20d09e584f545cdcec0c96ec.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled approach to directly regress against the closed-form optimal velocity field in flow matching, challenging the prevailing assumption that stochasticity in the loss is essential for generalization. It provides a detailed temporal analysis of when generalization arises in the generative process, identifies critical time intervals responsible for creativity, and demonstrates that deterministic targets can match or surpass the performance of stochastic ones. The empirical flow matching algorithm offers an efficient and unbiased estimator for high-dimensional data, and the hybrid trajectory experiments yield new insights into the mechanisms underlying generalization in deep generative models.

658c5711c6d07bfe2b9514ce22411e57a8a0ff1a.title: Challenges in Training PINNs: A Loss Landscape Perspective
658c5711c6d07bfe2b9514ce22411e57a8a0ff1a.research_question: What are the fundamental challenges in training Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for solving partial differential equations (PDEs), and how can the optimization process be improved to achieve higher accuracy and efficiency?
658c5711c6d07bfe2b9514ce22411e57a8a0ff1a.hypothesis: The hypothesis is that the loss landscape of PINNs is ill-conditioned primarily due to the presence of differential operators in the residual term, which hinders the effectiveness of first-order optimization methods. It is further hypothesized that combining first-order and second-order optimization techniques, as well as introducing a novel second-order optimizer, can significantly improve the training process and solution accuracy of PINNs.
658c5711c6d07bfe2b9514ce22411e57a8a0ff1a.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves a detailed analysis of the loss landscape of PINNs, focusing on the conditioning of the loss function and its components. The approach will empirically and theoretically investigate the impact of differential operators on the conditioning of the PINN loss. Multiple optimization strategies will be systematically compared, including first-order methods (Adam), quasi-Newton methods (L-BFGS), and their combination (Adam+L-BFGS). Additionally, a novel second-order optimizer, NysNewton-CG (NNCG), will be developed and applied after the combined Adam+L-BFGS pipeline. The NNCG algorithm leverages efficient Hessian-vector products and preconditioned conjugate gradient techniques to address the fast spectral decay and ill-conditioning observed in the PINN loss landscape. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to relate the conditioning of the differential operator to the overall optimization difficulty and to justify the hybrid optimization approach.
658c5711c6d07bfe2b9514ce22411e57a8a0ff1a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several challenging PDE and ODE problems, including convection, wave, and reaction equations, using standard benchmark formulations. The experimental setup will utilize multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) with varying widths (50, 100, 200, 400) and tanh activations, initialized with Xavier normal initialization. Each optimizer (Adam, L-BFGS, Adam+L-BFGS, and NNCG) will be evaluated across multiple random seeds and network widths. Hyperparameters such as learning rates and optimizer switch points will be tuned via grid search. The training will use 10,000 randomly sampled residual points, 257 initial condition points, and 101 boundary condition points. Performance will be assessed using the L2 relative error (L2RE) metric, computed over a dense grid of test points, as well as loss values and gradient norms. Baseline comparisons will include Adam, L-BFGS, and Adam+L-BFGS, with the proposed NNCG method applied as a fine-tuning step after Adam+L-BFGS. All experiments will be implemented in PyTorch and run on NVIDIA GPUs.
658c5711c6d07bfe2b9514ce22411e57a8a0ff1a.novelty_claims: The proposal claims several innovations: (1) a comprehensive empirical and theoretical analysis of the ill-conditioning in the PINN loss landscape, directly linking it to the presence of differential operators; (2) a systematic comparison and justification of combined first- and second-order optimization strategies for PINNs, demonstrating the superiority of Adam+L-BFGS over either method alone; (3) the introduction of a novel second-order optimizer, NysNewton-CG (NNCG), specifically tailored to address the fast spectral decay and ill-conditioning in PINN training; (4) theoretical results establishing the connection between the conditioning of the differential operator and the optimization landscape, as well as the benefits of hybrid optimization approaches; and (5) empirical evidence that high-precision optimization is required for accurate PINN solutions, and that the proposed methods achieve significantly lower errors and better convergence than existing baselines.

65a0ee3bc9bf57622f56b47fddf06f316ae2119b.title: SV4D: Dynamic 3D Content Generation with Multi-Frame and Multi-View Consistency
65a0ee3bc9bf57622f56b47fddf06f316ae2119b.research_question: How can dynamic 3D (4D) content be generated from a single monocular video in a way that ensures both multi-frame (temporal) and multi-view (spatial) consistency, enabling efficient and high-quality reconstruction of dynamic 3D assets?
65a0ee3bc9bf57622f56b47fddf06f316ae2119b.hypothesis: A unified latent video diffusion model, equipped with specialized attention mechanisms for both frame and view consistency and trained on a curated dynamic 3D dataset, can generate temporally and spatially consistent novel view videos from a single monocular input video, which can then be used to efficiently optimize a high-quality 4D representation of dynamic objects.
65a0ee3bc9bf57622f56b47fddf06f316ae2119b.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that utilizes a unified video diffusion model, SV4D, designed to generate a grid of images representing multiple frames and multiple camera views of a dynamic object, conditioned on a single monocular input video and a user-specified camera trajectory. The architecture extends a state-of-the-art video diffusion backbone with two new attention modules: view attention, which aligns features across different viewpoints at each frame, and frame attention, which aligns features across time at each view. The model is trained using a combination of reference video frames and reference multi-view images of the first frame, leveraging pre-trained weights from existing video and multi-view diffusion models for initialization. To address memory constraints, a mixed sampling strategy is introduced during inference, generating anchor frames sparsely and then densely interpolating intermediate frames while maintaining consistency. The generated multi-view, multi-frame videos are then used as pseudo ground-truths to optimize a dynamic NeRF-based 4D representation using photometric and geometric losses, without reliance on slow score-distillation sampling (SDS) losses.
65a0ee3bc9bf57622f56b47fddf06f316ae2119b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets, including the newly curated ObjaverseDy dataset (derived from Objaverse with dynamic 3D objects), Consistent4D, and DAVIS. The evaluation will focus on two main tasks: novel view video synthesis and 4D generation. Baseline methods for comparison include SV3D, Diffusion2, STAG4D, 4Diffusion, Consistent4D, DreamGaussian4D, GaussianFlow, 4DGen, and Efficient4D. Evaluation metrics will include LPIPS and CLIP-S for visual quality, and FVD (with variants FVD-F, FVD-V, FVD-Diag, FV4D) for temporal and spatial consistency. User studies will be conducted to assess perceptual quality and preference. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of the attention mechanisms and sampling strategies.
65a0ee3bc9bf57622f56b47fddf06f316ae2119b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to train a single unified model for novel view video synthesis and 4D generation using a curated 4D dataset, enabling joint reasoning across both frame and view axes. The dual attention mechanism (view and frame attention) within the diffusion model is introduced to ensure high consistency across time and viewpoints. A novel mixed sampling scheme is developed to efficiently generate long, high-resolution multi-view videos while maintaining consistency. The approach eliminates the need for computationally expensive SDS-based optimization, enabling faster and higher-quality 4D asset reconstruction. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in both novel view video synthesis and 4D generation, with superior consistency and visual fidelity compared to prior methods.

65b1755f40f728baf25893368287ffb1e91d6739.title: Representation Surgery: Theory and Practice of Affine Steering
65b1755f40f728baf25893368287ffb1e91d6739.research_question: How can language model representations be systematically modified to steer model behavior, such as mitigating bias or reducing toxic generation, through theoretically justified and empirically effective intervention functions?
65b1755f40f728baf25893368287ffb1e91d6739.hypothesis: Affine steering functions, derived from optimality principles such as least-squares error and moment matching, can effectively steer neural language model representations to reduce undesirable behaviors (e.g., bias, toxicity) while minimally altering the representations and maintaining task performance.
65b1755f40f728baf25893368287ffb1e91d6739.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops and analyzes affine steering functions that intervene on neural language model representations to shift them from a source concept (e.g., toxic, biased) toward a target concept (e.g., non-toxic, unbiased). Two classes of affine steering functions are derived: (1) mean-matching, which translates representations so that the conditional means for different concepts are aligned, and (2) mean-and-covariance matching, which further matches the conditional covariances, effectively aligning the first and second moments of the representations. These transformations are computed in closed form using statistics estimated from labeled data. During inference, the appropriate affine transformation is applied to representations associated with the source concept, either during classification or at each generation step in autoregressive models. Theoretical analysis justifies these interventions by showing they minimize least-squares distance and, in the case of mean-and-covariance matching, provably eliminate expected bias by neighbors.
65b1755f40f728baf25893368287ffb1e91d6739.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in two main settings: multiclass classification and text generation. For classification, datasets such as Bios (profession prediction with gender as the protected attribute) and a dialect-annotated sentiment dataset (with dialect as the protected attribute) will be used. Representations from various language models (e.g., BERT, GPT-2, Llama2-7b) will be extracted, and affine steering functions will be applied. Baselines include existing concept erasure methods and post-processing techniques based on optimal transport. Evaluation metrics include accuracy on the main task and fairness metrics such as TPR gap and bias by neighbors. For generation, the GPT-2 (large) model will be used, with interventions applied at each generation step to reduce toxicity. The Real Toxicity Prompts dataset will be used for evaluation, with toxicity measured by Perspective API, and text quality assessed via perplexity and n-gram diversity. Comparisons will be made to state-of-the-art toxicity mitigation methods.
65b1755f40f728baf25893368287ffb1e91d6739.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretical framework for affine steering functions, deriving optimal interventions under least-squares and moment-matching constraints, and providing formal justification for commonly used steering vectors. It establishes a new connection between concept erasure and steering, and demonstrates that mean-and-covariance matching eliminates expected bias by neighbors. The approach is empirically validated across both classification and generation tasks, showing that simple linear interventions can effectively mitigate bias and toxicity without requiring model retraining or complex inference-time procedures.

65c7aaf5b8d108b003074fbb8d15bc1f1a001aa6.title: Domain Agnostic Fourier Neural Operators
65c7aaf5b8d108b003074fbb8d15bc1f1a001aa6.research_question: How can neural operator architectures be developed to efficiently and accurately learn solution operators for partial differential equations (PDEs) on domains with arbitrary shapes, irregular geometries, and evolving topologies, while maintaining computational efficiency and generalizability?
65c7aaf5b8d108b003074fbb8d15bc1f1a001aa6.hypothesis: Explicitly encoding geometric and boundary information of arbitrary and evolving domains into the neural operator architecture, via a smoothed characteristic function within the Fourier layer, will enable accurate, efficient, and generalizable learning of PDE solution operators on irregular and changing domains.
65c7aaf5b8d108b003074fbb8d15bc1f1a001aa6.proposed_method: A novel neural operator architecture, termed Domain Agnostic Fourier Neural Operator (DAFNO), is proposed. The method embeds geometric information by incorporating a (smoothed) domain characteristic function directly into the integral layer of the Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) architecture. This modification enables the convolutional structure to be preserved, allowing the use of Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) for computational efficiency, while restricting the learned operator to act only within the physical domain and excluding non-physical interactions. The characteristic function is smoothed using a hyperbolic tangent function based on the distance to the domain boundary, which mitigates the Gibbs phenomenon and improves boundary fidelity. Two practical variants are developed: eDAFNO, based on explicit FNO, and iDAFNO, based on implicit FNO with layer-independent kernels. The architecture is designed to be discretization-independent and can be extended to evolving domains by updating the characteristic function over time.
65c7aaf5b8d108b003074fbb8d15bc1f1a001aa6.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on three benchmark problems: (1) constitutive modeling of hyperelastic materials with randomly shaped voids, (2) transonic flow simulation around airfoil geometries, and (3) crack propagation in brittle fracture with evolving domain topology. Datasets include high-fidelity synthetic data and publicly available benchmarks, with training, validation, and test splits (e.g., 1000/200/200 for hyperelasticity and airfoil datasets). Models are compared against state-of-the-art baselines including FNO, Geo-FNO, IFNO, F-FNO, GNO, DeepONet, and UNet. Evaluation metrics include relative L2 error on training and test sets, with experiments repeated over multiple random seeds to report mean and standard deviation. Hyperparameters such as learning rate, smoothing parameter, and regularization are tuned for each model, and ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of boundary encoding and smoothing. For the crack propagation problem, generalization to unseen loading scenarios and crack patterns is tested, with model predictions used in time-stepping simulations.
65c7aaf5b8d108b003074fbb8d15bc1f1a001aa6.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first neural operator architecture capable of explicitly encoding arbitrary domain boundaries and handling evolving topologies within the Fourier layer, while retaining FFT-based computational efficiency. The smoothed characteristic function approach provides a principled solution to the Gibbs phenomenon and enables accurate modeling on complex and changing domains. DAFNO demonstrates state-of-the-art accuracy and generalizability across a range of scientific problems, surpassing existing neural operator and deep learning baselines in both predictive performance and memory efficiency. The architecture is also shown to be flexible with respect to mesh regularity and can be combined with grid mapping techniques for non-uniform discretizations.

65f345b4bbf6a147d8bb5c479fb0cd7b39f2eab5.title: TimesURL: Self-supervised Contrastive Learning for Universal Time Series Representation Learning
65f345b4bbf6a147d8bb5c479fb0cd7b39f2eab5.research_question: How can universal time series representations be learned in a self-supervised manner to effectively support a wide range of downstream tasks, given the unique temporal characteristics and high dimensionality of time series data?
65f345b4bbf6a147d8bb5c479fb0cd7b39f2eab5.hypothesis: A self-supervised contrastive learning framework that incorporates frequency-temporal-based augmentation, hard negative sampling via double Universums, and joint optimization with time reconstruction will enable the learning of high-quality, universal time series representations that generalize well across diverse downstream tasks.
65f345b4bbf6a147d8bb5c479fb0cd7b39f2eab5.proposed_method: A novel self-supervised framework, TimesURL, is proposed to learn universal time series representations. The method begins by applying a frequency-temporal-based augmentation (FTAug), which combines random cropping in the time domain and frequency mixing in the frequency domain, to generate augmented views that preserve temporal dependencies and semantic consistency. Double Universums, constructed via anchor-specific mixup in both temporal- and instance-wise embedding spaces, are injected as hard negative samples to enhance contrastive learning. The framework jointly optimizes a hierarchical contrastive loss (capturing both segment- and instance-level information through multi-scale pooling and Universum negatives) and a time reconstruction loss, where a masked autoencoding strategy is used to reconstruct masked portions of the input series. A temporal convolutional network (TCN) backbone is used for encoding, and the learned representations are designed to be task-agnostic and transferable.
65f345b4bbf6a147d8bb5c479fb0cd7b39f2eab5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six benchmark time series tasks: short- and long-term forecasting, imputation, classification, anomaly detection, and transfer learning. Datasets include the UEA and UCR classification archives, ETT, Electricity, Weather, KPI, and Yahoo datasets, covering both univariate and multivariate time series. About 15 baselines will be used for comparison, including state-of-the-art self-supervised, end-to-end, and unsupervised methods such as TS2Vec, InfoTS, CoST, TNC, TS-TCC, DTW, Informer, and others. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy for classification, mean squared error (MSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) for forecasting and imputation, and F1, precision, and recall for anomaly detection. The experimental setup includes using a TCN encoder, consistent representation dimensionality, and standardized downstream evaluation protocols (e.g., SVM with RBF kernel for classification, MLP for imputation, and linear regression for forecasting). Ablation studies will be performed to assess the contribution of each module.
65f345b4bbf6a147d8bb5c479fb0cd7b39f2eab5.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a frequency-temporal-based augmentation (FTAug) that preserves temporal and semantic properties of time series data, overcoming limitations of prior augmentation methods. The double Universum strategy provides high-quality, anchor-specific hard negatives in both temporal and instance dimensions, which is novel in time series contrastive learning. Joint optimization of contrastive and time reconstruction losses enables the capture of both segment- and instance-level information, supporting universal representation learning. The approach is claimed to achieve state-of-the-art performance across a broad spectrum of downstream tasks, demonstrating the universality and effectiveness of the learned representations.

65fc1f1c567801fee3788974e753cdbf934f07e9.title: Video PreTraining (VPT): Learning to Act by Watching Unlabeled Online Videos
65fc1f1c567801fee3788974e753cdbf934f07e9.research_question: How can large-scale, unlabeled online video data be leveraged to train general-purpose agents capable of complex sequential decision-making tasks in environments where labeled action data is scarce or unavailable?
65fc1f1c567801fee3788974e753cdbf934f07e9.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a small amount of labeled data can be used to train an inverse dynamics model (IDM) that is sufficiently accurate to generate pseudo-action labels for large-scale, unlabeled video datasets, enabling effective pretraining of behavioral priors through behavioral cloning. These priors, when fine-tuned with imitation learning or reinforcement learning, will enable agents to perform complex tasks that are otherwise infeasible to learn from scratch.
65fc1f1c567801fee3788974e753cdbf934f07e9.proposed_method: A semi-supervised imitation learning framework is proposed, termed Video PreTraining (VPT), which consists of several stages. First, a small dataset of human-labeled action-observation trajectories is collected by having contractors play the target environment (e.g., Minecraft) using the native human interface (mouse and keyboard). An inverse dynamics model (IDM) is then trained on this labeled data to predict the action taken between consecutive observations, utilizing both past and future frames (non-causal). The trained IDM is used to generate pseudo-action labels for a large, filtered dataset of unlabeled online videos. A foundation policy model is then trained via behavioral cloning on this pseudo-labeled dataset, modeling the distribution of human actions at scale. This policy can subsequently be fine-tuned on smaller, more specific datasets using behavioral cloning or further optimized for downstream tasks using reinforcement learning, with auxiliary objectives (e.g., KL-divergence regularization) to retain previously learned skills.
65fc1f1c567801fee3788974e753cdbf934f07e9.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted in the Minecraft environment, leveraging approximately 70,000 hours of filtered, 'clean' unlabeled online video data and around 2,000 hours of contractor-labeled data for IDM training. The IDM's accuracy is evaluated on held-out contractor data, and the foundation model is trained on pseudo-labeled data using behavioral cloning. Zero-shot and fine-tuned performance are assessed by rolling out agents in standard Minecraft survival mode for extended episodes (e.g., 60 minutes, 72,000 actions), measuring collection and crafting rates for key items (logs, planks, crafting tables, tools, etc.). Baselines include models trained from scratch, models trained directly on small labeled datasets, and prior RL approaches. Evaluation metrics include keypress accuracy, mouse movement explained variance (R^2), item collection and crafting rates, and task completion rates (e.g., crafting a diamond pickaxe). Fine-tuning experiments use both behavioral cloning on targeted datasets and reinforcement learning (phasic policy gradient) with shaped rewards, and ablation studies are conducted to assess the impact of IDM quality and KL-regularization.
65fc1f1c567801fee3788974e753cdbf934f07e9.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to demonstrate effective large-scale semi-supervised imitation learning in a complex, open-ended sequential decision domain using freely available, noisy online video data. The method achieves nontrivial zero-shot performance and, after fine-tuning, enables agents to solve tasks previously deemed impossible with reinforcement learning alone, such as crafting a diamond pickaxe in Minecraft using the native human interface. The approach shows that a small amount of labeled data can be leveraged to unlock massive amounts of unlabeled data for training, and that using an IDM for pseudo-labeling is significantly more data-efficient than direct behavioral cloning. The framework is general and applicable to other domains with abundant unlabeled video data.

6628f9ee35e36cdfdcac8a46cef4dba8d529a83b.title: Character-LLM: A Trainable Agent for Role-Playing
6628f9ee35e36cdfdcac8a46cef4dba8d529a83b.research_question: Can large language models be trained to serve as believable, role-specific agents that simulate the experiences, personalities, and knowledge boundaries of specific individuals, surpassing the limitations of prompt-based approaches for role-playing applications?
6628f9ee35e36cdfdcac8a46cef4dba8d529a83b.hypothesis: Trainable agents, constructed by fine-tuning large language models on curated, character-specific experiences and protective scenarios, will more accurately and believably simulate the personalities, memories, and knowledge boundaries of specific individuals compared to prompt-based or instruction-tuned LLMs.
6628f9ee35e36cdfdcac8a46cef4dba8d529a83b.proposed_method: A novel methodology will be developed to construct character simulacra by fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) on datasets of reconstructed experiences specific to target individuals (historical, fictional, or celebrity figures). The process begins with profile collection, using reliable sources (e.g., Wikipedia) to compile concise character descriptions. Next, an experience reconstruction pipeline generates detailed scenes and interactions via LLM prompting, including both normal experiences and 'protective' scenes designed to enforce knowledge boundaries and prevent out-of-character hallucinations. The resulting dataset, consisting of thousands of multi-turn, script-like scenes, is used to fine-tune a base LLM (e.g., LLaMA 7B) into a dedicated agent for each character. Fine-tuning is performed with supervised learning, using hyperparameters optimized for generation quality and stability.
6628f9ee35e36cdfdcac8a46cef4dba8d529a83b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by training character agents on datasets of 1,000–2,200 scenes per character, covering a diverse set of historical, fictional, and celebrity figures. The base model will be LLaMA 7B, fine-tuned separately for each character using the reconstructed experience datasets. Evaluation will be performed through single-turn and multi-turn interview scenarios, with questions generated to probe memory, personality, values, stability, and resistance to hallucination. Baseline comparisons will include instruction-tuned models such as Alpaca 7B, Vicuna 7B, and ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo), all prompted with detailed character descriptions. Responses will be rated by LLM-based judges (GPT-3.5) across multiple dimensions using Likert scales, and qualitative case studies will be conducted to assess memorization consistency and hallucination avoidance.
6628f9ee35e36cdfdcac8a46cef4dba8d529a83b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a comprehensive, trainable framework for character simulacra that goes beyond prompt engineering and standard supervised fine-tuning by grounding agents in detailed, fact-based experiences and protective scenarios. The method enables LLMs to forget irrelevant knowledge, maintain character consistency, and resist hallucinations, resulting in more believable and stable role-playing agents. The approach also provides a scalable data synthesis pipeline for experience reconstruction and a novel evaluation protocol combining LLM-based judging and diverse interview scenarios. This work lays the foundation for future research on trainable, personality-rich agents for applications in NPCs, social simulations, and human-computer interaction.

663a41c866d49ce052801fbc88947d39764cad29.title: Challenging BIG-Bench Tasks and Whether Chain-of-Thought Can Solve Them
663a41c866d49ce052801fbc88947d39764cad29.research_question: Can advanced prompting strategies, such as chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting, enable large language models to solve challenging tasks that were previously unsolved by standard few-shot prompting, particularly those in the BIG-Bench Hard (BBH) benchmark, and how does model scale interact with these prompting methods?
663a41c866d49ce052801fbc88947d39764cad29.hypothesis: Chain-of-thought prompting, when combined with sufficiently large language models, will enable models to outperform average human-rater performance on a significant subset of the most challenging tasks in the BIG-Bench Hard benchmark, revealing emergent reasoning capabilities not captured by standard answer-only prompting.
663a41c866d49ce052801fbc88947d39764cad29.proposed_method: A new evaluation framework will be developed to systematically assess the impact of chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting on large language models across a curated set of 23 challenging tasks from the BIG-Bench Hard (BBH) benchmark. The methodology involves manually crafting few-shot exemplars with explicit step-by-step reasoning (CoT) for each task, and comparing performance to a strengthened answer-only prompting baseline that includes task instructions and answer options. Multiple model families and scales will be evaluated, including Codex (code-davinci-002), InstructGPT (text-davinci-002 and variants), and PaLM (8B, 62B, 540B parameters). The evaluation will use greedy decoding and exact match accuracy, extracting final answers based on expected keywords. The study will also analyze the interaction between model scale and CoT prompting, identifying tasks where emergent abilities appear as model size increases.
663a41c866d49ce052801fbc88947d39764cad29.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the 23-task BBH benchmark, which includes a mix of algorithmic, arithmetic, logical, spatial, temporal, and natural language understanding tasks. For each task, three manually written few-shot exemplars will be used for both answer-only and CoT prompting conditions. The evaluation will be performed using greedy decoding (temperature τ = 0), and accuracy will be measured via exact match with ground-truth labels. Multiple large language models will be compared: Codex (code-davinci-002, code-cushman-001), InstructGPT (text-davinci-002, text-curie-002, text-babbage-001, text-ada-001), and PaLM (8B, 62B, 540B). Baselines will include prior best-reported model results and average/max human-rater scores. The analysis will include per-task and aggregate performance, as well as scaling curves to investigate emergent abilities unlocked by CoT prompting.
663a41c866d49ce052801fbc88947d39764cad29.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a curated benchmark (BBH) focused on the most challenging BIG-Bench tasks, provides a systematic evaluation of chain-of-thought prompting across multiple large language model families and scales, and demonstrates that CoT prompting can unlock emergent reasoning abilities on tasks previously unsolved by standard prompting. The study offers detailed insights into the interaction between model scale and prompting strategy, and establishes new state-of-the-art results on BBH, surpassing average human-rater performance on a majority of tasks with the best models. The release of curated data, prompts, and model outputs further enables reproducibility and future research in this area.

6651ff3d8c89a3cddfeef0c5d03ac4cb121758e3.title: Fast Sampling of Diffusion Models with Exponential Integrator
6651ff3d8c89a3cddfeef0c5d03ac4cb121758e3.research_question: How can the sampling speed of diffusion models be significantly accelerated while maintaining high sample quality, especially when using a limited number of neural network function evaluations?
6651ff3d8c89a3cddfeef0c5d03ac4cb121758e3.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that employing an exponential integrator-based discretization scheme, which leverages the semilinear structure of the learned diffusion process and incorporates advanced score parameterizations and polynomial extrapolation, will enable diffusion models to generate high-fidelity samples with far fewer sampling steps compared to existing methods.
6651ff3d8c89a3cddfeef0c5d03ac4cb121758e3.proposed_method: A new fast sampling framework for diffusion models will be developed, termed Diffusion Exponential Integrator Sampler (DEIS). This method will systematically analyze the sources of error in the sampling process, focusing on both fitting error and discretization error. The core approach will discretize the probability flow ODE associated with the learned score function using exponential integrators, which are well-suited for semilinear stiff ODEs. The method will adopt a parameterization of the score network in terms of the noise prediction (epsilon) rather than the raw score, and further enhance accuracy by employing high-order polynomial extrapolation of the score across time steps. Variants of the method will include both direct exponential integrator schemes and transformed ODE solvers (e.g., using Runge-Kutta or Adams-Bashforth methods in a time-scaled domain), allowing for application to a wide range of diffusion models.
6651ff3d8c89a3cddfeef0c5d03ac4cb121758e3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image generation benchmarks, including CIFAR-10, CelebA 64x64, ImageNet 64x64 and 256x256, and LSUN Bedroom 256x256, using pre-trained diffusion models such as VPSDE and VESDE. The proposed DEIS variants will be compared against established baselines including DDPM, DDIM, PNDM, A-DDIM, FastDPM, and Ito-Taylor samplers. Evaluation metrics will include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) to assess sample quality, and the number of neural network function evaluations (NFE) to measure sampling efficiency. Ablation studies will be performed to isolate the impact of exponential integrators, score parameterization, polynomial extrapolation, and time discretization strategies. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by matching NFE budgets and using optimal time discretizations for each method.
6651ff3d8c89a3cddfeef0c5d03ac4cb121758e3.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled discretization scheme for diffusion model sampling based on exponential integrators, which has not been systematically explored in this context. The method is general and can be applied to any diffusion model, including those with non-diagonal or non-standard SDE coefficients. The use of high-order polynomial extrapolation of the score function within the exponential integrator framework is a novel contribution that significantly reduces discretization error at low NFE. The proposal also provides a new theoretical justification for the effectiveness of DDIM as a special case of the exponential integrator scheme. Overall, the method promises state-of-the-art sampling efficiency, generating high-fidelity samples with as few as 10 steps, and advances the theoretical understanding of discretization in diffusion model sampling.

66583ad76bc1ce493ed3b530b9a56f87a7e684ca.title: MIB: A Mechanistic Interpretability Benchmark
66583ad76bc1ce493ed3b530b9a56f87a7e684ca.research_question: How can mechanistic interpretability methods for neural language models be evaluated in a principled, standardized, and comprehensive manner across diverse tasks and models?
66583ad76bc1ce493ed3b530b9a56f87a7e684ca.hypothesis: A benchmark that standardizes tasks, models, datasets, counterfactual interventions, and evaluation metrics will enable meaningful, generalizable, and rigorous comparisons of mechanistic interpretability methods, thereby accelerating progress and clarifying real advancements in the field.
66583ad76bc1ce493ed3b530b9a56f87a7e684ca.proposed_method: A benchmark suite, MIB (Mechanistic Interpretability Benchmark), will be developed to evaluate mechanistic interpretability methods along two primary tracks: circuit localization and causal variable localization. The circuit localization track will assess methods that identify the most important model components and their connections for task performance, using standardized counterfactual interventions and novel faithfulness metrics (CPR and CMD) to quantify how well discovered circuits explain model behavior. The causal variable localization track will evaluate methods that featurize hidden vectors and align those features to high-level causal variables, using interchange interventions to measure the faithfulness of the alignment. Both tracks will span four diverse tasks (Indirect Object Identification, Arithmetic, Multiple-choice Question Answering, and the AI2 Reasoning Challenge) and five language models of varying sizes and architectures. Public leaderboards and APIs will be established to facilitate community submissions and benchmarking on private test sets.
66583ad76bc1ce493ed3b530b9a56f87a7e684ca.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four tasks designed to cover a range of reasoning types and answer formats: Indirect Object Identification, Arithmetic (two-digit addition and subtraction), Multiple-choice Question Answering, and the AI2 Reasoning Challenge. Five language models will be used, including Llama-3-18B, Gemma-22B, Qwen-2.5-0.5B, and GPT-2 Small, selected to represent a spectrum of model sizes and capabilities. For circuit localization, a variety of methods (e.g., attribution patching, mask optimization, integrated gradients, information flow routes, and uniform gradient sampling) will be compared using the proposed CPR and CMD metrics, as well as AUROC on synthetic ground-truth circuits. For causal variable localization, both supervised (DAS) and unsupervised (SAE, PCA, full vector) featurization methods will be evaluated using interchange intervention accuracy and logit-based metrics, with feature selection guided by desiderata-based masking. Evaluation will be performed on both public and private test splits, with counterfactual inputs provided for all instances to ensure consistent and meaningful interventions.
66583ad76bc1ce493ed3b530b9a56f87a7e684ca.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces the first comprehensive, standardized, and task-diverse evaluation suite for mechanistic interpretability methods in language models. It establishes novel faithfulness metrics (CPR and CMD) for circuit localization, supports both component-level and feature-level interpretability, and enables rigorous comparison across methods, tasks, and models. The benchmark includes public leaderboards, APIs for community submissions, and private test sets to ensure robust evaluation. By providing principled counterfactual interventions and standardized datasets, the benchmark aims to set lasting evaluation standards and drive real progress in mechanistic interpretability research.

666aaab90b9558f82e5bde5dc62d97f9d961caa0.title: Applying sparse autoencoders to unlearn knowledge in language models
666aaab90b9558f82e5bde5dc62d97f9d961caa0.research_question: Can sparse autoencoders be leveraged to selectively and interpretably remove specific domains of knowledge from language models, while minimizing negative side-effects on unrelated capabilities?
666aaab90b9558f82e5bde5dc62d97f9d961caa0.hypothesis: Sparse autoencoders contain interpretable features that, when manipulated, can effectively unlearn targeted knowledge in language models with fewer side-effects than existing fine-tuning-based unlearning methods.
666aaab90b9558f82e5bde5dc62d97f9d961caa0.proposed_method: The proposed approach involves training sparse autoencoders (SAEs) on intermediate residual stream layers of language models to identify interpretable features associated with the target knowledge domain.
