For unlearning, selected SAE features—determined by comparing feature sparsities on 'forget' (target knowledge) and 'retain' (general knowledge) datasets—are intervened upon by clamping their activations to a fixed negative value whenever they activate during inference. This intervention is performed at specific token positions and layers, and the method is evaluated both for single-feature and multi-feature interventions. Alternative intervention strategies, such as scaling feature activations or using multiples of maximum activation, are also explored, but clamping to negative values is prioritized due to its effectiveness and reduced side-effects.
666aaab90b9558f82e5bde5dc62d97f9d961caa0.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the gemma-2b-it and gemma-2-2b-it language models, focusing on the biology subset of the Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy (WMDP-bio) dataset, which contains 1273 multiple-choice questions on hazardous biosecurity knowledge. Only questions that the base model answers correctly under all permutations are used to ensure the presence of knowledge. The main evaluation metrics are the reduction in correct answers on WMDP-bio (unlearning effectiveness), accuracy on unrelated MMLU tasks (side-effects), and added cross-entropy loss on OpenWebText (general performance impact). SAE-based interventions are compared against the Representation Misdirection for Unlearning (RMU) fine-tuning method, using varying numbers of features and intervention magnitudes. Additional analyses include ablation studies with random features and decoder vectors to probe the mechanism of unlearning.
666aaab90b9558f82e5bde5dc62d97f9d961caa0.novelty_claims: The proposal extends the use of sparse autoencoders from interpretability to the domain of knowledge unlearning in language models, introducing a method for interpretable, activation-based interventions that do not require model weight modification. The approach allows for targeted removal of knowledge at the feature level, with detailed evaluation of side-effects and comparison to state-of-the-art fine-tuning techniques. The method provides new insights into the mechanisms of unlearning and highlights the importance of feature selection and activation manipulation strategies.

667b276412d844a4bccb9d3178371a7f33d35cd2.title: Physics-informed Value Learner for Offline Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning
667b276412d844a4bccb9d3178371a7f33d35cd2.research_question: How can offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning be improved to achieve better value function estimation and generalization, especially in environments with limited state-action coverage and long-horizon tasks?
667b276412d844a4bccb9d3178371a7f33d35cd2.hypothesis: Incorporating a physics-informed regularizer, derived from the Eikonal partial differential equation, into value learning will induce a geometric inductive bias that improves the accuracy and generalization of goal-conditioned value function estimation in offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning, particularly in navigation and stitching tasks.
667b276412d844a4bccb9d3178371a7f33d35cd2.proposed_method: A novel regularization term, inspired by the Eikonal PDE, will be integrated into the value function learning objective for offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning. This regularizer constrains the gradient norm of the learned goal-conditioned value function to match a pre-specified speed profile, typically set to unity, thereby encouraging the value function to behave like a distance field. The method will be implemented within a hierarchical implicit Q-learning (HIQL) framework, where the regularized loss combines temporal-difference-based expectile regression with the Eikonal gradient penalty. The approach is model-free, relying on automatic differentiation to compute value gradients, and is compatible with standard temporal-difference-based RL algorithms. The hierarchical actor structure, consisting of high-level subgoal selection and low-level action generation, will be trained using the regularized value function to maximize goal-reaching performance.
667b276412d844a4bccb9d3178371a7f33d35cd2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the OGbench benchmark, which includes a diverse set of goal-conditioned tasks such as navigation (pointmaze, antmaze, humanoidmaze), contact-rich locomotion (antsoccer), and manipulation (cube, scene). The evaluation will compare the proposed Eikonal-regularized HIQL (Eik-HIQL) against state-of-the-art baselines including standard HIQL, Quasimetric RL (QRL), and Contrastive RL (CRL). Agents will be trained for 100,000 steps on pointmaze tasks and 1 million steps on other tasks, using 10 random seeds per experiment. Performance will be assessed using mean and standard deviation of success rates across seeds, with evaluations performed over multiple random goals and episodes per goal. Ablation studies will be conducted to compare different speed profile designs and to benchmark against HJB-based regularization. Visualization of learned value functions will be used to assess the structural alignment with environment geometry.
667b276412d844a4bccb9d3178371a7f33d35cd2.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first use of an Eikonal PDE-based regularizer for value function estimation in offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning. Unlike prior physics-informed approaches that require explicit dynamics or suffer from numerical instability, this method is model-free, easy to implement, and broadly compatible with temporal-difference-based algorithms. The regularizer injects a geometric inductive bias that promotes distance-like structure in the value function, leading to improved generalization and sample efficiency. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate significant gains in large-scale navigation and trajectory stitching tasks, outperforming both HJB-regularized and unregularized baselines, while adding minimal computational overhead.

668858489bbec3ce45f7a84a6a557b329f9ec91a.title: ArCHer: Training Language Model Agents via Hierarchical Multi-Turn RL
668858489bbec3ce45f7a84a6a557b329f9ec91a.research_question: How can large language models be effectively and efficiently trained for goal-directed, multi-turn decision-making tasks that require reasoning over extended interactions, credit assignment, and information-seeking behavior?
668858489bbec3ce45f7a84a6a557b329f9ec91a.hypothesis: A hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that combines utterance-level and token-level optimization will enable large language models to achieve superior sample efficiency, performance, and scalability on multi-turn agent tasks compared to existing single-turn or non-hierarchical RL methods.
668858489bbec3ce45f7a84a6a557b329f9ec91a.proposed_method: A hierarchical reinforcement learning framework, termed Actor-Critic Framework with a Hierarchical Structure (ArCHer), is developed for fine-tuning large language models in multi-turn agent settings. The approach models multi-turn language generation as a hierarchical Markov Decision Process (MDP), with a high-level MDP operating at the utterance (turn) level and a low-level MDP at the token level. At the high level, an off-policy temporal difference learning algorithm is used to train an utterance-level value function (Q-function and V-function) via Bellman bootstrapping, leveraging all past interaction data. At the low level, a token-level policy is optimized via on-policy policy gradient methods, using the high-level value function as the terminal reward for each utterance. The framework supports both online and offline RL, incorporates variance reduction techniques (such as token-level baselines), and is compatible with various RL algorithms and model architectures.
668858489bbec3ce45f7a84a6a557b329f9ec91a.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a suite of multi-turn language agent tasks that require strategic planning and delayed reward optimization, including Detective Game (interactive text fiction), Twenty Questions and Guess My City (dialogue-based guessing games), and WebShop (tool-use/shopping task). The evaluation uses models up to 7 billion parameters, with policies parameterized by GPT-2 and critics by RoBERTa-base architectures. Baselines include token-level PPO, filtered behavioral cloning, and state-of-the-art utterance-level RL methods. Evaluation metrics include task-specific success rates and sample efficiency (number of environment interactions to reach a given performance). Implementation details include the use of double Q-learning for stability, Polyak averaging for target networks, and replay buffers for off-policy learning.
668858489bbec3ce45f7a84a6a557b329f9ec91a.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a hierarchical RL approach for LLMs that enables efficient multi-turn credit assignment and information-seeking behavior, overcoming the limitations of single-turn and flat token-level RL methods. The method achieves up to 100x sample efficiency improvement over on-policy approaches, supports plug-and-play integration with existing RL algorithms and model architectures, and demonstrates scalability to large model sizes. Theoretical analysis shows weaker convergence requirements and improved statistical error guarantees for the hierarchical design compared to token-level RL. The framework is the first to systematically combine utterance-level and token-level optimization for multi-turn RL in LLMs, enabling both online and offline training.

669a95efbb9a1388ef465c7d6eb891705842fa1c.title: Controlling Text-to-Image Diffusion by Orthogonal Finetuning
669a95efbb9a1388ef465c7d6eb891705842fa1c.research_question: How can fine-tuning methods for large text-to-image diffusion models be improved to enable effective control for downstream tasks, such as subject-driven and controllable image generation, while preserving the generative performance and stability of the pretrained models?
669a95efbb9a1388ef465c7d6eb891705842fa1c.hypothesis: Applying a layer-shared orthogonal transformation to the weights of pretrained text-to-image diffusion models during fine-tuning will preserve the pairwise angular relationships among neurons (hyperspherical energy), thereby maintaining the semantic generative ability and stability of the original model while enabling effective adaptation to downstream tasks. Further constraining the transformation's deviation from the identity matrix will improve fine-tuning stability.
669a95efbb9a1388ef465c7d6eb891705842fa1c.proposed_method: A novel fine-tuning framework, Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT), is proposed for adapting text-to-image diffusion models to downstream tasks. OFT operates by learning a layer-shared orthogonal transformation matrix for each weight layer, ensuring that the pairwise angles between neurons (hyperspherical energy) are preserved. The orthogonal matrices are efficiently parameterized using the Cayley transform and further structured as block-diagonal matrices to reduce parameter count. A constrained variant, Constrained Orthogonal Finetuning (COFT), is introduced, which adds an explicit constraint on the deviation of the orthogonal transformation from the identity matrix, thereby limiting the flexibility of the fine-tuning and enhancing stability. An optional extension, re-scaled OFT, allows for additional neuron-wise scaling without affecting hyperspherical energy. The method is model-agnostic and can be applied to both fully connected and convolutional layers, as well as transformer attention weights.
669a95efbb9a1388ef465c7d6eb891705842fa1c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using Stable Diffusion v1.5 as the base text-to-image diffusion model. For subject-driven generation, the DreamBooth and LoRA frameworks will serve as baselines, using the same loss functions and hyperparameter setups. For controllable generation, ControlNet, T2I-Adapter, and LoRA will be used as baselines, with tasks including Canny edge-to-image (COCO dataset), segmentation map-to-image (ADE20K), and landmark-to-face (CelebA-HQ). Evaluation metrics will include subject fidelity (DINO, CLIP-I), prompt fidelity (CLIP-T), sample diversity (LPIPS), and control consistency (IoU, F1, mean IoU, accuracy, and landmark error). Both qualitative and quantitative comparisons will be performed, and experiments will be repeated with multiple random seeds for statistical robustness. The number of trainable parameters, convergence speed, sample efficiency, and fine-tuning stability will be systematically analyzed.
669a95efbb9a1388ef465c7d6eb891705842fa1c.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a principled, provably invariant fine-tuning approach that preserves hyperspherical energy, a structural measure of semantic preservation, during adaptation of diffusion models. Unlike prior methods, OFT guarantees preservation of pairwise neuron angles through orthogonal transformations, leading to improved generative quality, stability, and convergence speed. The COFT variant further enhances stability by explicitly constraining deviation from the pretrained model. The framework achieves superior sample and parameter efficiency, introduces a new control consistency metric for controllable generation, and imposes no additional inference overhead. The approach is model-agnostic and applicable to a wide range of neural architectures.

66c10bf1f11bc1b2d92204d8f8391d087f6de1c4.title: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding
66c10bf1f11bc1b2d92204d8f8391d087f6de1c4.research_question: How can positional information be more effectively integrated into transformer-based language models to improve their ability to model dependencies between sequence elements, especially for long sequences and in settings requiring linear attention?
66c10bf1f11bc1b2d92204d8f8391d087f6de1c4.hypothesis: Encoding positional information through a multiplicative rotary position embedding (RoPE) mechanism, rather than additive or bias-based methods, will enable transformers to more flexibly and effectively capture both absolute and relative positional dependencies, leading to improved performance on language modeling and downstream NLP tasks.
66c10bf1f11bc1b2d92204d8f8391d087f6de1c4.proposed_method: A novel rotary position embedding (RoPE) mechanism will be developed, wherein absolute positional information is encoded by applying a rotation matrix to the affine-transformed word embeddings. This approach enables the explicit incorporation of relative positional dependencies directly into the self-attention calculation by rotating the query and key vectors according to their positions. The rotation is parameterized using sinusoidal functions, generalizing to higher dimensions by dividing the embedding space into subspaces and applying independent rotations. The method maintains the norm of the hidden representations, ensuring stability, and is compatible with both standard and linear self-attention mechanisms. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to demonstrate properties such as long-term decay of attention with increasing relative distance and compatibility with linear attention architectures.
66c10bf1f11bc1b2d92204d8f8391d087f6de1c4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of NLP tasks. For machine translation, the WMT2014 English-German dataset will be used, with BLEU score as the evaluation metric, comparing the proposed method to the standard Transformer baseline. For language model pre-training, the BookCorpus and Wikipedia datasets will be used, with masked language modeling (MLM) loss as the metric, and BERT serving as the baseline. Downstream evaluation will be performed on GLUE benchmark tasks (MRPC, SST-2, QNLI, STS-B, QQP, MNLI), using F1-score, Spearman correlation, and accuracy as appropriate. Additional experiments will test the integration of RoPE with linear attention architectures such as Performer, using comparable pre-training setups and loss metrics. All models will be trained and evaluated under controlled, consistent hyperparameter settings, and results will be compared to strong baselines.
66c10bf1f11bc1b2d92204d8f8391d087f6de1c4.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a multiplicative rotary position embedding mechanism that encodes both absolute and relative positional information via rotation matrices, rather than additive or bias-based approaches. This enables seamless integration of relative position encoding into both standard and linear self-attention architectures, overcoming limitations of prior methods. The approach provides theoretical guarantees such as long-term decay of attention with relative distance and maintains computational efficiency. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate consistent improvements over existing positional encoding techniques across a variety of NLP tasks.

66d4efb99b1b9e98e0ae067e258089e58f0e039f.title: GOOD: A Graph Out-of-Distribution Benchmark
66d4efb99b1b9e98e0ae067e258089e58f0e039f.research_question: How can a comprehensive and systematic benchmark be developed to evaluate out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization in graph-based machine learning, explicitly distinguishing between covariate and concept shifts across diverse graph and node prediction tasks?
66d4efb99b1b9e98e0ae067e258089e58f0e039f.hypothesis: A benchmark that systematically incorporates both covariate and concept shifts across a wide variety of graph and node-level datasets, with carefully designed data splits and environment structures, will reveal substantial and non-trivial performance gaps between in-distribution and OOD settings, and provide a robust platform for evaluating and advancing graph OOD methods.
66d4efb99b1b9e98e0ae067e258089e58f0e039f.proposed_method: A new benchmark, named GOOD, will be constructed to systematically evaluate OOD generalization in graph learning. The benchmark will include 11 datasets covering both graph-level and node-level prediction tasks, with each dataset featuring one or two domain features selected to induce distribution shifts. For each domain, three types of splits will be generated: no-shift (random), covariate shift (where input features unrelated to the label are shifted across environments), and concept shift (where spurious correlations between domains and labels are introduced or altered). The benchmark will employ both synthetic/semi-artificial and real-world datasets, using clustering or feature-based grouping to define environments and ensure meaningful, solvable shifts. For each split, environments will be constructed to reflect the intended distributional changes, supporting both invariant and risk-minimization learning paradigms.
66d4efb99b1b9e98e0ae067e258089e58f0e039f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across all 11 datasets, covering 51 different split scenarios (combinations of domain, covariate/concept/no-shift, and task type). Ten baseline methods will be evaluated, including empirical risk minimization (ERM), domain adaptation algorithms (DANN, DeepCoral), invariant learning methods (IRM, VREx, GroupDRO), and graph-specific OOD methods (Mixup-For-Graph, DIR, EERM, SRGNN). Standard graph neural network backbones (GIN-Virtual for graph tasks, GCN for node tasks) will be used for consistency. Evaluation metrics will be tailored to each task (e.g., ROC-AUC, average precision, accuracy, mean absolute error), and performance will be averaged over multiple random runs. Both in-distribution and OOD validation/test sets will be used to assess generalization and performance gaps.
66d4efb99b1b9e98e0ae067e258089e58f0e039f.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark is the first to systematically provide both covariate and concept shift comparisons for the same domain selection within the same dataset, enabling controlled variable analysis of shift types. It uniquely includes a diverse set of tasks—graph classification, graph regression, and node classification—across synthetic, semi-artificial, and real-world data. The benchmark introduces carefully designed environment structures and splitting strategies, supporting a wide range of OOD methods and facilitating fair, comprehensive evaluation. By providing extensive baseline results and a growing resource, the benchmark aims to set a new standard for graph OOD evaluation and foster future methodological advances.

66f2afe8ba08bcb92113deb8527c65975947c2aa.title: Repeated Bilateral Trade Against a Smoothed Adversary
66f2afe8ba08bcb92113deb8527c65975947c2aa.research_question: What are the fundamental regret limits and optimal learning algorithms for repeated bilateral trade in online settings where buyer and seller valuations are generated by a smoothed adversary, under various feedback and pricing constraints?
66f2afe8ba08bcb92113deb8527c65975947c2aa.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the regret achievable by learning algorithms in repeated bilateral trade against a σ-smooth adversary fundamentally depends on the feedback model and the pricing flexibility (single or dual prices), and that sublinear regret is possible only under specific conditions of feedback and pricing.
66f2afe8ba08bcb92113deb8527c65975947c2aa.proposed_method: The proposed approach will formalize the repeated bilateral trade problem as an online learning task where, at each round, a learner posts prices to a seller and a buyer whose private valuations are drawn from a σ-smooth adversarial distribution. The study will analyze both single-price (strong budget balance) and two-price (weak budget balance) mechanisms. For each, the method will examine three feedback regimes: full feedback (observing both valuations), two-bit feedback (observing accept/reject for each agent), and one-bit feedback (observing only if trade occurs). For the full feedback setting, a discretization of the price space will be used, enabling the application of expert algorithms such as Hedge. For partial feedback with two prices, a novel algorithm (e.g., Blind-Exp3) will be developed, leveraging a one-bit estimation technique and discretization to estimate the gain from trade and achieve sublinear regret. Lower bounds will be established via reductions to online learning with feedback graphs and information-theoretic arguments, constructing hard adversarial instances to characterize minimax regret.
66f2afe8ba08bcb92113deb8527c65975947c2aa.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using simulated data generated from σ-smooth adversarial distributions over the [0,1]^2 valuation space, with both independent and dependent seller/buyer valuations. The algorithms will be evaluated over T rounds for various values of T and σ, comparing regret performance under different feedback models (full, two-bit, one-bit) and pricing constraints (single vs. two prices). Baseline comparisons will include standard online learning algorithms (e.g., Hedge for full feedback, Exp3 variants for partial feedback) and theoretical lower bounds. Evaluation metrics will focus on cumulative regret, with particular attention to the scaling of regret with T (e.g., O(√T), O(T^{3/4}), linear). Key experimental setup details include grid discretization of the price space, adaptive adversary strategies, and varying the amount of feedback provided to the learner.
66f2afe8ba08bcb92113deb8527c65975947c2aa.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first comprehensive characterization of minimax regret rates for repeated bilateral trade against a smoothed adversary under multiple feedback and pricing regimes. It establishes a novel T^{3/4} lower bound for minimax regret in the partial feedback setting with two prices, which is strictly worse than the bandit feedback rate and departs from known results in related online learning models. The proposal also develops the first sublinear-regret learning algorithm for the partial feedback bilateral trade problem beyond the i.i.d. stochastic assumption, and demonstrates that, in this setting, there is no difference between one-bit and two-bit feedback when two prices can be posted. The lower bound construction and information-theoretic techniques are new and may be of independent interest for other online learning problems with partial feedback.

66f7823be7a0adcd8ed3ecebf00e53daf45bc6bc.title: Query2box: Reasoning over Knowledge Graphs in Vector Space using Box Embeddings
66f7823be7a0adcd8ed3ecebf00e53daf45bc6bc.research_question: How can complex logical queries, including those with conjunction, disjunction, and existential quantifiers, be efficiently and accurately answered over large, incomplete knowledge graphs using vector space representations?
66f7823be7a0adcd8ed3ecebf00e53daf45bc6bc.hypothesis: Embedding logical queries as geometric regions (specifically, axis-aligned boxes) in vector space enables more effective reasoning over sets of entities and supports scalable handling of arbitrary existential positive first-order (EPFO) queries, including those with disjunctions, compared to point-based query embeddings.
66f7823be7a0adcd8ed3ecebf00e53daf45bc6bc.proposed_method: A novel embedding-based framework is developed in which both knowledge graph entities and logical queries are represented in a low-dimensional vector space. Queries are embedded as axis-aligned hyper-rectangles (boxes), allowing the interior of the box to naturally represent sets of answer entities. Logical operators are modeled as geometric operations: projection is implemented as translation and scaling of boxes, while intersection is realized through an attention-weighted combination and adaptive shrinking of box offsets. To handle disjunctions, queries are transformed into Disjunctive Normal Form (DNF), with each conjunctive clause embedded as a separate box; the final answer set is obtained by aggregating entities that are close to any of the boxes. The framework jointly learns entity embeddings and parameterized geometric operators through a negative sampling loss based on a distance function that measures entity-to-box proximity.
66f7823be7a0adcd8ed3ecebf00e53daf45bc6bc.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on three standard knowledge graph benchmarks: FB15k, FB15k-237, and NELL995. The evaluation focuses on answering complex logical queries with missing edges, simulating incomplete graphs. Nine diverse query structures are considered, with models trained on five and evaluated on all nine, including previously unseen structures and queries involving unions. Baselines include state-of-the-art query embedding methods such as GQE, as well as ablations and variants of the proposed method. Evaluation metrics include Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) and Hits@K, with performance measured specifically on queries requiring imputation of missing relations. Hyperparameters are tuned on validation splits, and results are reported for both seen and unseen query types.
66f7823be7a0adcd8ed3ecebf00e53daf45bc6bc.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the use of box embeddings to model logical queries as sets in vector space, enabling natural and efficient representation of set-based logical reasoning. The method is the first to scalably handle arbitrary EPFO queries, including those with disjunctions, by transforming queries into DNF and aggregating over multiple box embeddings. The framework demonstrates strong generalization to unseen query structures and provides significant empirical improvements—up to 25% relative gain—over state-of-the-art baselines in answering complex logical queries on large, incomplete knowledge graphs.

67160ae8e81487ae578a599c630e30c1d88d3bd4.title: Filter Like You Test: Data-Driven Data Filtering for CLIP Pretraining
67160ae8e81487ae578a599c630e30c1d88d3bd4.research_question: How can data-driven filtering methods be developed to optimize the selection of pretraining examples for large-scale vision-language models, such as CLIP, in order to improve downstream task performance?
67160ae8e81487ae578a599c630e30c1d88d3bd4.hypothesis: Learning to assign data-dependent weights to pretraining examples, guided by gradient signals from downstream tasks, will yield filtered datasets that improve the performance of vision-language models on downstream benchmarks compared to heuristic or proxy-based filtering methods.
67160ae8e81487ae578a599c630e30c1d88d3bd4.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a data-driven filtering framework called Filter Like You Test (FLYT), which jointly trains a scoring model and a reference vision-language model. The scoring model receives features extracted from candidate image-text pairs and outputs a score for each example, which is converted to a weight via softmax. These weights are used in a weighted CLIP loss to update the reference model. After this update, the reference model is evaluated on a downstream dataset (e.g., ImageNet), and the resulting loss gradient is backpropagated through the updated reference model to refine the scoring model. Mixing-FLYT (M-FLYT), an instantiation of FLYT, uses multiple existing scoring methods as input features to the scoring model, learning an optimal linear combination. To construct the final filtered dataset, Soft Cap Sampling (SCS) is applied, which samples examples according to their learned probabilities while penalizing repeated sampling to avoid over-representation.
67160ae8e81487ae578a599c630e30c1d88d3bd4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the DataComp medium scale filtering benchmark, which involves filtering a 128M candidate pool of web-sourced image-text pairs and training a ViT-B/32 CLIP model using the filtered data. The downstream evaluation will include 38 tasks, with key metrics being zero-shot ImageNet accuracy and average accuracy across all tasks. Baselines will include top-performing heuristic and aggregation-based filtering methods such as CLIP score, DFN, HYPE, s-CLIPLoss, and their combinations. The evaluation protocol will follow DataComp's fixed training and evaluation pipeline, and ablation studies will assess the contribution of individual input scores and sampling strategies. Additional experiments will be performed on the DataComp small scale benchmark to test scalability.
67160ae8e81487ae578a599c630e30c1d88d3bd4.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled, end-to-end data-driven filtering method that directly optimizes for downstream performance using learned per-example weighting, rather than relying on heuristic proxies. The Mixing-FLYT approach enables optimal aggregation of multiple filtering signals via supervised learning, outperforming prior aggregation strategies. The Soft Cap Sampling method provides a novel probabilistic sampling strategy that interpolates between sampling with and without replacement, addressing over-representation in filtered datasets. The combined approach is expected to achieve state-of-the-art results on public-resource benchmarks and demonstrates scalability to large dataset sizes.

67239d6e9c2c5f8a6d19cb35154e5aa7eaa00f51.title: Large Language Models on Graphs: A Comprehensive Survey
67239d6e9c2c5f8a6d19cb35154e5aa7eaa00f51.research_question: How can large language models be effectively integrated with graph-structured data to enhance reasoning, representation learning, and downstream task performance across diverse graph scenarios?
67239d6e9c2c5f8a6d19cb35154e5aa7eaa00f51.hypothesis: Integrating large language models with graph-structured data, through novel architectures and alignment techniques, will enable improved reasoning and representation learning capabilities, surpassing traditional graph neural networks and text-only models on a variety of graph-related tasks.
67239d6e9c2c5f8a6d19cb35154e5aa7eaa00f51.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed that systematically categorizes and explores the integration of large language models (LLMs) with graphs across three primary scenarios: pure graphs, text-attributed graphs, and text-paired graphs. For each scenario, multiple methodological paradigms will be proposed, including: (1) LLM as Predictor, where LLMs are enhanced or adapted to directly process serialized or encoded graph structures for prediction and reasoning tasks; (2) LLM as Encoder, where LLMs generate initial node or edge features from associated texts, which are then processed by graph neural networks (GNNs) or graph transformers; and (3) LLM as Aligner, where latent spaces or predictions from LLMs and GNNs are aligned via contrastive learning or iterative pseudo-labeling. The framework will include novel architectural modifications (e.g., graph-empowered LLMs with structure-aware attention), advanced fine-tuning and pretraining strategies, and efficient knowledge distillation techniques to address scalability and efficiency challenges.
67239d6e9c2c5f8a6d19cb35154e5aa7eaa00f51.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of benchmark datasets representing each graph scenario, such as academic citation networks, social networks, molecular graphs with textual descriptions, and traffic or power grid graphs. Baseline comparisons will include traditional GNNs, text-only LLMs, and existing hybrid models. Evaluation metrics will cover node/edge classification accuracy, link prediction, graph-level property prediction, and reasoning task success rates (e.g., shortest path, subgraph matching). Experimental setups will involve both zero-shot and fine-tuned settings, ablation studies on architectural components (e.g., structure tokenization, alignment strategies), and efficiency analyses for inference and training scalability.
67239d6e9c2c5f8a6d19cb35154e5aa7eaa00f51.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a systematic taxonomy and unified framework for integrating LLMs with graph data, encompassing all major interaction paradigms (predictor, encoder, aligner) across multiple graph scenarios. Novel contributions include the design of graph-empowered LLM architectures capable of joint text-structure encoding, advanced alignment techniques for bridging LLM and GNN modalities, and the development of efficient knowledge distillation and data augmentation strategies tailored for graph-text tasks. The research aims to establish new state-of-the-art results on challenging graph reasoning and representation benchmarks, while also providing open-source resources and guidelines for future research in this rapidly evolving field.

672ec9fa4ddb5b6bfc46c61c5b2f4bdfa1aa8ed9.title: Dual RL: Unification and New Methods for Reinforcement and Imitation Learning
672ec9fa4ddb5b6bfc46c61c5b2f4bdfa1aa8ed9.research_question: How can reinforcement learning (RL) and imitation learning (IL) algorithms be unified under a common duality-based framework, and how can this unification be leveraged to develop new, more stable and performant methods for offline RL and IL, particularly in the presence of arbitrary off-policy data?
672ec9fa4ddb5b6bfc46c61c5b2f4bdfa1aa8ed9.hypothesis: Unifying RL and IL algorithms under a duality-based framework will reveal structural limitations in existing methods and enable the development of new algorithms that improve performance and stability in offline settings, especially by eliminating restrictive assumptions and unstable loss functions.
672ec9fa4ddb5b6bfc46c61c5b2f4bdfa1aa8ed9.proposed_method: A unified duality-based framework for RL and IL will be formalized, showing that many state-of-the-art algorithms are instances of this dual RL approach. Building on this, a new discriminator-free imitation learning method, ReCOIL, will be developed to relax the coverage assumption and enable learning from arbitrary off-policy data by matching mixture distributions of expert and suboptimal data in the dual formulation. For offline RL, a new family of algorithms, f-DVL, will be introduced, generalizing implicit value maximization by replacing the Gumbel regression loss (used in XQL) with alternative f-divergence-based surrogates that are more stable for optimization. Both methods will employ parameterized value and policy functions, semi-gradient updates, and advantage-weighted regression for policy extraction, with careful design to ensure stable and principled off-policy learning.
672ec9fa4ddb5b6bfc46c61c5b2f4bdfa1aa8ed9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a comprehensive suite of simulated robot locomotion and manipulation tasks from the D4RL benchmark. For imitation learning, various datasets will be constructed by mixing expert and suboptimal trajectories, simulating both high and low coverage scenarios. Baselines will include recent offline IL methods such as RCE, SMODICE, IQLearn, ORIL, and behavior cloning. For offline RL, comparisons will be made with methods like CQL, IQL, XQL, DT, and TD3+BC. Evaluation metrics will include normalized return, mean squared error for visitation distribution estimation, and reward recovery accuracy. Each algorithm will be run with multiple random seeds, and both average performance and training stability will be reported. Additional analyses will include ablations, qualitative results, and reward function recovery.
672ec9fa4ddb5b6bfc46c61c5b2f4bdfa1aa8ed9.novelty_claims: The proposed research claims to provide the first comprehensive unification of a broad class of RL and IL algorithms under a duality-based framework, revealing that many seemingly distinct methods are structurally related. The ReCOIL method is novel in that it eliminates the need for a discriminator and the restrictive coverage assumption in off-policy imitation learning, enabling effective learning from arbitrary data. The f-DVL family introduces new, stable implicit maximizers for offline RL by leveraging alternative f-divergences, directly addressing known training instabilities in prior methods such as XQL. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate that these new methods outperform existing baselines in both performance and stability across a variety of challenging offline RL and IL tasks.

673fbdd957cada770d10dffca5e45b53da43a3c6.title: Training Large Language Models to Reason in a Continuous Latent Space
673fbdd957cada770d10dffca5e45b53da43a3c6.research_question: Can large language models (LLMs) reason more effectively and efficiently when allowed to operate in a continuous latent space, rather than being constrained to generate reasoning steps in natural language? How does latent space reasoning compare to traditional language-based chain-of-thought (CoT) approaches, particularly on tasks requiring complex planning and search?
673fbdd957cada770d10dffca5e45b53da43a3c6.hypothesis: Allowing LLMs to reason in a continuous latent space, by feeding hidden states as reasoning steps instead of language tokens, will enable more flexible and efficient reasoning processes. This approach will improve performance on complex reasoning tasks—especially those requiring planning and breadth-first search—compared to traditional language-based CoT methods.
673fbdd957cada770d10dffca5e45b53da43a3c6.proposed_method: A novel reasoning paradigm, termed Chain of Continuous Thought (Coconut), will be developed to enable LLMs to alternate between language mode and latent mode. In latent mode, the model will use the last hidden state as the next input embedding, representing a 'continuous thought,' instead of decoding it into a word token. Special tokens (<bot> and <eot>) will mark the beginning and end of latent reasoning segments. A multi-stage training curriculum will be implemented, where language reasoning steps in CoT data are progressively replaced by continuous thoughts, supervised by cross-entropy loss on the remaining tokens. The model will be trained end-to-end with backpropagation, and inference will involve controlling the number of continuous thoughts used before reverting to language output. Strategies for terminating latent reasoning include either a learned classifier or padding to a constant length.
673fbdd957cada770d10dffca5e45b53da43a3c6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a pre-trained GPT-2 model as the base, with training and evaluation on three datasets: GSM8k (math reasoning), ProntoQA (logical reasoning), and a newly introduced ProsQA (logical reasoning with complex DAG structures). Baselines will include standard CoT, No-CoT (direct question-answer), iCoT (internalized CoT), and pause-token methods, as well as ablations and variants of Coconut (e.g., without curriculum, without continuous thoughts, and with pause tokens as thoughts). Evaluation metrics will include final answer accuracy and fine-grained categorization of reasoning paths (e.g., Correct Path, Hallucination, Wrong Target). The number of continuous thoughts per reasoning step and training stages will be varied, and greedy decoding will be used for inference. The efficiency (number of generated tokens) and accuracy trade-offs will be systematically compared across methods.
673fbdd957cada770d10dffca5e45b53da43a3c6.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a new paradigm for LLM reasoning that operates in an unconstrained continuous latent space, rather than natural language. This approach enables the encoding of multiple alternative reasoning paths within continuous thoughts, supporting a breadth-first search-like reasoning process. The method is fully differentiable and compatible with end-to-end training. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate improved accuracy and efficiency on complex reasoning tasks, with the ability to scale to harder problems by chaining more continuous thoughts. The ProsQA dataset will provide a new benchmark for evaluating planning-intensive logical reasoning.

675edc15c6064d0231a26e1d3e02de39abc80e89.title: Learning to Keep a Promise: Scaling Language Model Decoding Parallelism with Learned Asynchronous Decoding
675edc15c6064d0231a26e1d3e02de39abc80e89.research_question: How can large language model (LLM) inference latency be reduced by enabling models to autonomously identify and exploit semantic independence in their own outputs for parallel decoding, without relying on hand-crafted syntactic heuristics?
675edc15c6064d0231a26e1d3e02de39abc80e89.hypothesis: A learning-based approach that trains LLMs to annotate their own outputs with semantic independence information will enable more effective and scalable asynchronous decoding, resulting in improved inference speedup with minimal loss in response quality compared to methods based on fixed syntactic heuristics.
675edc15c6064d0231a26e1d3e02de39abc80e89.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that introduces an annotation language, PASTA-LANG, allowing LLMs to mark semantically independent chunks in their responses. An interpreter will be implemented to orchestrate asynchronous decoding at inference time based on these annotations, launching parallel decoding threads for each independent chunk and synchronizing as needed. The training pipeline will consist of a two-stage fine-tuning process: first, an LLM will be prompted (using a small set of human-annotated demonstrations and language description) to annotate a large instruction-following dataset with PASTA-LANG, creating a supervised fine-tuning dataset. Second, preference optimization will be applied to further fine-tune the model, directly optimizing for both output quality and decoding latency using a learned scoring function that balances these objectives. Technical challenges such as position ID prediction and efficient KV-cache management for parallel threads will be addressed to ensure practical and scalable implementation.
675edc15c6064d0231a26e1d3e02de39abc80e89.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the AlpacaEval benchmark, which consists of 805 representative instruction-following prompts. The base model will be Gemma-7B, with all models fine-tuned using consistent hyperparameters for fair comparison. Baselines will include standard autoregressive decoding, as well as state-of-the-art asynchronous decoding methods such as APAR and SoT, which rely on syntactic heuristics. Evaluation metrics will include realized and theoretical speedup (measured as the ratio of baseline to test model decoding times and token-level parallelism), response quality (using length-controlled win rates judged by LLMs such as Gemini 1.5 Pro and GPT-4), and degree of parallelism in the output. Sensitivity analyses will be performed on hyperparameters such as the quality-speedup tradeoff, number of preference optimization iterations, and position ID assignment strategies.
675edc15c6064d0231a26e1d3e02de39abc80e89.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a learning-based system for asynchronous decoding that does not rely on fixed syntactic patterns, but instead empowers LLMs to autonomously discover and annotate parallelization opportunities in their own outputs. The PASTA-LANG annotation language and its interpreter enable flexible, fine-grained, and scalable parallel decoding. The two-stage fine-tuning pipeline, including direct optimization for both quality and latency via preference optimization, is claimed to produce models that Pareto-dominate existing methods in the quality-speedup tradeoff. Technical innovations include efficient parallel thread management and position ID prediction for non-sequential decoding, as well as a scalable preference optimization process that continues to yield improvements with additional training compute.

676e62902be87c38b86e405d5936017f83fe0818.title: Ergodic Generative Flows
676e62902be87c38b86e405d5936017f83fe0818.research_question: How can generative flow models be designed to efficiently sample from unnormalized target distributions in continuous spaces, with universality guarantees, tractable training objectives, and without the need for separate reward models in imitation learning settings?
676e62902be87c38b86e405d5936017f83fe0818.hypothesis: A family of generative flows based on ergodic transformations, with finitely many globally defined diffeomorphisms and a novel training loss, can provide universal approximation capabilities, tractable flow-matching losses, and enable imitation learning without a separate reward model.
676e62902be87c38b86e405d5936017f83fe0818.proposed_method: A new class of generative flows, termed Ergodic Generative Flows (EGFs), is introduced. EGFs utilize a policy that selects from a finite set of globally defined diffeomorphisms (transformations) at each state, ensuring ergodicity of the generated group. This structure allows for closed-form and tractable computation of the flow-matching loss, as the backward policy and star inflow density can be explicitly calculated. Universality is theoretically guaranteed under ergodicity and L2-mixing assumptions, with explicit constructions for tori and spheres using as few as four transformations. For imitation learning, a novel KL-weakFM loss is proposed, coupling a cross-entropy term with a weak flow-matching regularizer, enabling direct training of EGFs to match the target distribution without a separate reward model.
676e62902be87c38b86e405d5936017f83fe0818.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both synthetic 2D tasks and real-world datasets, including NASA earth science data on the sphere. For reinforcement learning tasks, EGFs are trained on toroidal state spaces using a stable flow-matching loss, with baselines including Moser Flow and other generative flow models. For imitation learning, EGFs are compared to Moser Flow and other baselines on toroidal and spherical domains, using the KL-weakFM loss. Evaluation metrics include negative log-likelihood and qualitative assessments of sample quality and stability. Model architectures use small multi-layer perceptrons, and the number of transformations is kept minimal to demonstrate expressivity and tractability. Regularization and stability of different loss functions are also systematically compared.
676e62902be87c38b86e405d5936017f83fe0818.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first family of generative flows with universality guarantees on tori and spheres using only finitely many simple diffeomorphisms. The method provides a tractable and closed-form flow-matching loss in continuous settings, overcoming prior intractability issues. A novel KL-weakFM loss enables imitation learning without a separate reward model, addressing a key limitation of previous methods. Theoretical advances include quantitative sampling theorems and explicit universality criteria. Empirical results demonstrate that EGFs achieve high expressivity and stability with significantly smaller models and faster training times compared to baselines, particularly on challenging real-world datasets.

6788935740260c0706dc51161272b072f166d13d.title: Model-agnostic meta-learners for estimating heterogeneous treatment effects over time
6788935740260c0706dc51161272b072f166d13d.research_question: How can heterogeneous treatment effects (HTEs) be accurately and robustly estimated from observational data over time, particularly in the presence of time-varying confounding, growing patient histories, and low overlap, using model-agnostic approaches that are compatible with arbitrary machine learning models?
6788935740260c0706dc51161272b072f166d13d.hypothesis: Meta-learners that are model-agnostic and leverage advanced adjustment mechanisms—including regression adjustment, propensity adjustment, and doubly robust adjustment—can provide unbiased and stable estimates of HTEs over time. Furthermore, incorporating inverse-variance weighting into doubly robust learners will reduce estimation variance, especially in low-overlap and long time horizon settings.
6788935740260c0706dc51161272b072f166d13d.proposed_method: A suite of model-agnostic meta-learners will be developed for estimating HTEs over time, each leveraging different adjustment mechanisms: history adjustment, regression adjustment (G-computation), propensity adjustment, and doubly robust adjustment. Each meta-learner will be constructed using a two-stage approach: first, estimating nuisance functions (such as response functions and propensity scores) using arbitrary machine learning models (e.g., transformers), and second, combining these estimates via plug-in or pseudo-outcome-based regression to estimate the target causal quantities (CAPO and CATE). A novel inverse-variance-weighted doubly robust (IVW-DR) learner will be introduced, which stabilizes the doubly robust loss by downweighting samples with extreme inverse propensity products, thereby reducing estimation variance. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to characterize the asymptotic properties, bias, and convergence rates of each learner under standard identifiability and boundedness assumptions.
6788935740260c0706dc51161272b072f166d13d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both simulated and real-world datasets. Simulated datasets will be designed to include time-varying confounding, varying complexity in treatment assignment and response mechanisms, and regimes with low overlap to stress-test the learners. All meta-learners will be instantiated with the same transformer-based neural architecture to ensure fair comparison, with additional robustness checks using LSTM-based models. Evaluation metrics will include root mean squared error (RMSE) of estimated CATEs across multiple time horizons and overlap levels. Baselines will include history-adjusted, regression-adjusted, propensity-adjusted, and doubly robust learners without inverse-variance weighting. Real-world experiments will use electronic health records (e.g., MIMIC-III dataset) to evaluate factual RMSE as a proxy for causal estimation accuracy. Sensitivity analyses will be performed to assess performance under varying degrees of overlap.
6788935740260c0706dc51161272b072f166d13d.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first comprehensive toolbox of model-agnostic meta-learners for estimating HTEs in the time-varying setting, enabling the use of arbitrary machine learning backbones. A novel inverse-variance-weighted doubly robust learner is developed, providing improved stability and lower variance in low-overlap and long time horizon regimes. Theoretical analysis is provided to guide the choice of learners and to establish consistency, convergence rates, and robustness properties. Empirical results demonstrate superior or state-of-the-art performance of the IVW-DR learner compared to existing approaches, especially in challenging scenarios with time-varying confounding and limited overlap.

67ab1f073e79697d144fa522d719a14413557d30.title: ODG: Occupancy Prediction Using Dual Gaussians
67ab1f073e79697d144fa522d719a14413557d30.research_question: How can fine-grained 3D geometry and semantic occupancy of complex driving scenes be accurately and efficiently predicted from multi-camera images, particularly addressing the challenges posed by both static and dynamic scene elements?
67ab1f073e79697d144fa522d719a14413557d30.hypothesis: Decomposing driving scenes into static and dynamic components and modeling them with dedicated dual sets of Gaussian queries, combined with hierarchical coarse-to-fine prediction and multi-stage rendering supervision, will improve 3D occupancy prediction accuracy and efficiency over existing methods.
67ab1f073e79697d144fa522d719a14413557d30.proposed_method: A dual-query architecture will be designed, introducing two distinct sets of 3D Gaussian queries to separately model static background elements and dynamic agents within driving scenes. Each Gaussian is parameterized by mean, scale, rotation, and opacity, with dynamic Gaussians further augmented with 3D bounding box attributes and velocity vectors to capture object motion. A hierarchical, coarse-to-fine transformer-based refinement will be employed, allowing a large number of Gaussians to be predicted across multiple layers, thus increasing model capacity and expressiveness. Attention mechanisms, specifically self-attention over concatenated dynamic and static query features, will facilitate rich information exchange between the two query types. Multi-stage real-time rendering supervision using 3D Gaussian Splatting will be imposed, leveraging available depth and semantic map annotations from projected LiDAR points to enforce pixel-level alignment and improve spatial coherence.
67ab1f073e79697d144fa522d719a14413557d30.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Occ3D-nuScenes and Occ3D-Waymo benchmarks, which provide annotated 3D occupancy ground-truth and semantic labels for urban driving scenes. The evaluation will use metrics such as mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) and RayIoU, with model performance compared against state-of-the-art baselines including OPUS, GaussRender, SparseOcc, and others. Implementation will utilize a ResNet-50 backbone for image feature extraction, hierarchical transformer layers for Gaussian prediction, and rendering supervision at multiple stages. Both small and large model variants will be tested, using standard training protocols, batch sizes, and inference-time visibility masks. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of motion compensation, query interaction mechanisms, and rendering supervision on model performance.
67ab1f073e79697d144fa522d719a14413557d30.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel dual Gaussian query design that explicitly separates static and dynamic scene modeling, enhancing the handling of dynamic agents. Hierarchical coarse-to-fine prediction enables the use of a much larger number of Gaussians, increasing model expressiveness. A new self-attention mechanism across concatenated dynamic and static queries is proposed to facilitate effective information sharing. Multi-stage rendering supervision with 3D Gaussian Splatting injects pixel-level alignment and spatial consistency, improving learning from both 2D and 3D labels. The overall framework is claimed to achieve new state-of-the-art results in 3D occupancy prediction while maintaining competitive inference efficiency.

67b5d57c08176787ae7b54b65ae3bf0ac11b9b04.title: Conditional Diffusion Based on Discrete Graph Structures for Molecular Graph Generation
67b5d57c08176787ae7b54b65ae3bf0ac11b9b04.research_question: How can the generation of molecular graphs be improved in terms of fidelity, sampling speed, and accurate modeling of complex dependencies between graph structures and features, particularly by leveraging discrete graph structures within diffusion-based generative frameworks?
67b5d57c08176787ae7b54b65ae3bf0ac11b9b04.hypothesis: Incorporating discrete graph structure conditioning and a specialized hybrid graph noise prediction model into diffusion-based generative frameworks will enable more accurate modeling of molecular graph distributions, improve generation fidelity, and significantly accelerate sampling compared to existing methods.
67b5d57c08176787ae7b54b65ae3bf0ac11b9b04.proposed_method: A conditional diffusion framework will be developed that explicitly models discrete graph structures alongside node and edge features. The forward diffusion process will perturb both graph structures and features using stochastic differential equations (SDEs), with edge existence represented as one-bit discrete variables converted to real numbers for continuous diffusion and quantized during reverse sampling. The reverse generative process will be conditioned on decoded discrete graph structures at each step. A hybrid graph noise prediction model will be designed, combining standard message passing layers (to capture local node-edge dependencies) and attention-based message passing layers (to extract and transmit global context) within a unified architecture. Fast sampling will be achieved by leveraging ordinary differential equation (ODE) solvers, specifically those exploiting the semi-linear structure of the probability flow ODE, to generate high-quality molecular graphs with significantly fewer steps.
67b5d57c08176787ae7b54b65ae3bf0ac11b9b04.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ZINC250k and QM9 molecular datasets, with molecules preprocessed to kekulized forms and aromatic bonds standardized. The evaluation will use metrics such as Fréchet ChemNet Distance (FCD), Neighborhood Subgraph Pairwise Distance Kernel (NSPDK), validity (with and without valency correction), uniqueness, and novelty. Baseline comparisons will include autoregressive models (GraphAF, GraphDF), flow-based models (MoFlow, GraphCNF), energy-based models (GraphEBM), and state-of-the-art diffusion models (GDSS). The proposed method will be tested with various numerical solvers (Euler-Maruyama, black-box ODE solvers, and DPM-Solvers) and ablation studies will assess the impact of discrete structure conditioning and model components. Additional experiments will evaluate similarity-constrained molecular property optimization and generic graph generation on datasets such as Community-small, Ego-small, Enzymes, and Ego, using MMD-based metrics for graph structure distribution.
67b5d57c08176787ae7b54b65ae3bf0ac11b9b04.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a novel conditional diffusion process that explicitly incorporates discrete graph structure conditioning, enabling more accurate modeling of complex dependencies in molecular graphs. The hybrid graph noise prediction model unifies local and global dependency modeling within a permutation-equivariant architecture. The method adapts fast ODE solvers tailored to the semi-linear structure of the probability flow ODE, achieving high-fidelity graph generation with drastically reduced sampling steps. The approach also extends to efficient similarity-constrained molecule optimization and demonstrates superior performance over state-of-the-art baselines in both molecular and generic graph generation tasks.

67daf8c4fe1958d20ebdf95c2a36dd490c73836f.title: FireAct: Toward Language Agent Fine-tuning
67daf8c4fe1958d20ebdf95c2a36dd490c73836f.research_question: How can fine-tuning language models with diverse agentic trajectories improve the performance, robustness, and generalization of language agents compared to few-shot prompting? What are the effects of varying base model types, sizes, fine-tuning data diversity, and multi-task/multi-method setups on language agent capabilities?
67daf8c4fe1958d20ebdf95c2a36dd490c73836f.hypothesis: Fine-tuning language models with a diverse set of agentic trajectories from multiple tasks and prompting methods will significantly improve language agent performance, robustness, generalization, and efficiency over few-shot prompting, especially for smaller or open-source models.
67daf8c4fe1958d20ebdf95c2a36dd490c73836f.proposed_method: A novel fine-tuning framework, FireAct, will be developed to fine-tune language models using agentic trajectories generated from multiple tasks and prompting methods. The approach involves generating successful task-solving trajectories using a strong language model (e.g., GPT-4) across various question answering tasks and prompting styles (ReAct, Chain-of-Thought, Reflexion). These trajectories will be reformatted into a unified ReAct format and used to fine-tune target models (e.g., GPT-3.5, Llama-2, CodeLlama) via Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) or full-model fine-tuning. During inference, the fine-tuned agent will operate without few-shot prompting, implicitly selecting suitable reasoning/acting strategies based on task complexity, and adapting trajectory length as needed. The method will systematically vary the diversity of fine-tuning data (tasks, methods) and analyze the effects of model type, scale, and data size.
67daf8c4fe1958d20ebdf95c2a36dd490c73836f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on established question answering datasets: HotpotQA (multi-hop QA), Bamboogle (multi-hop, search-resistant QA), StrategyQA (implicit reasoning, yes/no QA), and MMLU (multi-choice QA across domains). The Google search API (via SerpAPI) will serve as the external tool for agentic interaction. Baseline comparisons will include few-shot prompting with various methods (Input-Output, Chain-of-Thought, ReAct) and different model families (GPT-3.5, Llama-2, CodeLlama). Evaluation metrics will focus on exact match accuracy (EM), inference time, and cost, with additional robustness tests using noisy or randomized tool outputs. Experiments will systematically vary the number of fine-tuning trajectories, the mix of prompting methods, and the inclusion of multi-task data, with ablations to analyze the impact of each factor.
67daf8c4fe1958d20ebdf95c2a36dd490c73836f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a systematic framework for fine-tuning language agents with diverse agentic trajectories, explicitly promoting data diversity across tasks and prompting methods. FireAct enables smaller or open-source models to match or exceed the performance of larger, commercial models under prompting, while also improving efficiency, robustness to noisy environments, and generalization to new tasks. The framework provides actionable insights into the scaling effects of data, model size, and method/task diversity, and demonstrates the feasibility of training a single multi-task agent without negative cross-task interference. This work establishes a comprehensive experimental foundation and opens new research directions for language agent fine-tuning.

6822abea4ab56d349830b9f724cc410baaf5abca.title: Equilibrium of Data Markets with Externality
6822abea4ab56d349830b9f724cc410baaf5abca.research_question: How do fixed-price data markets with buyer externalities behave in terms of equilibrium and social welfare, and can simple platform interventions improve market outcomes, especially when buyers have incomplete information and must learn their valuations over time?
6822abea4ab56d349830b9f724cc410baaf5abca.hypothesis: Introducing a transaction cost mechanism based on predicted externalities in fixed-price data markets will significantly improve social welfare at equilibrium, both in settings where buyers know their valuations and where they must learn them over time.
6822abea4ab56d349830b9f724cc410baaf5abca.proposed_method: A game-theoretic model of fixed-price data markets will be developed, where buyers select subsets of sellers to purchase data from, and their utility incorporates net gain, negative externalities from other buyers' purchases, and a platform-imposed transaction cost. The transaction cost will be designed to be revenue-neutral and proportional to the predicted net externality each buyer contributes and suffers, based on a platform-learned model of externalities. In the case where buyers know their valuations, the Nash equilibrium and welfare properties of the market will be characterized with and without intervention. For the more realistic setting where buyers must learn their valuations through repeated market interactions, the buyer's decision process will be modeled as a multi-armed bandit problem with exponentially many arms, and online learning algorithms (including a zooming algorithm adapted for Hamming metric spaces) will be developed to guide buyer actions. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to bound individual and collective welfare regret under these algorithms.
6822abea4ab56d349830b9f724cc410baaf5abca.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic data markets generated according to the proposed game-theoretic model, with varying numbers of buyers and sellers, different externality structures, and both known and unknown buyer valuations. Baseline comparisons will include markets with no intervention (i.e., no transaction cost) and standard multi-armed bandit algorithms such as UCB. Evaluation metrics will focus on social welfare at equilibrium, welfare regret at equilibrium (WRaE), and online effective/cumulative welfare regret over repeated market interactions. The impact of the transaction cost intervention and the performance of the proposed learning algorithms will be assessed across a range of market parameters and externality functions.
6822abea4ab56d349830b9f724cc410baaf5abca.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a formal game-theoretic analysis of fixed-price data markets with buyer externalities, a setting that closely mirrors real-world data marketplaces but has not been systematically studied. The transaction cost mechanism is novel in its revenue-neutral design and its reliance on predicted externalities rather than direct utility elicitation. The adaptation of the zooming algorithm for combinatorial bandit problems in Hamming metric spaces, tailored to the structure of data market choices, provides new theoretical insights and regret bounds for learning in markets with exponential action spaces. The approach unifies equilibrium analysis, welfare guarantees, and online learning in a single framework for data markets.

6825ba09383bc758f9a2feaebabe35a6cd4adc4c.title: How Language Model Hallucinations Can Snowball
6825ba09383bc758f9a2feaebabe35a6cd4adc4c.research_question: How do language model hallucinations propagate during sequential reasoning tasks, and to what extent do language models generate further incorrect statements to justify earlier mistakes?
6825ba09383bc758f9a2feaebabe35a6cd4adc4c.hypothesis: Language models, when over-committing to an initial incorrect answer, are likely to generate additional false claims in their justifications, even when they are capable of recognizing these claims as incorrect in isolation. This phenomenon, termed 'hallucination snowballing,' is hypothesized to arise from the model's tendency to maintain consistency with its prior outputs rather than from a lack of underlying knowledge.
6825ba09383bc758f9a2feaebabe35a6cd4adc4c.proposed_method: A set of controlled question-answering datasets will be constructed to systematically induce and analyze hallucination snowballing in large language models. Each dataset will consist of 500 yes/no questions that require inherently sequential reasoning, such as primality testing, senator search (matching a senator to a state and alma mater), and graph connectivity (determining the existence of a flight path between cities). The questions will be designed so that an incorrect answer can be justified only by making an easily verifiable false claim. For each model response, the justification will be extracted and probed in isolation to assess whether the model can recognize the incorrectness of its own prior statements. The methodology will include both direct prompting and chain-of-thought prompting to evaluate the effect of reasoning style on hallucination propagation.
6825ba09383bc758f9a2feaebabe35a6cd4adc4c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo) and GPT-4, with greedy decoding as the primary inference setting. For each dataset, the model's accuracy in answering the questions will be measured, and for incorrect answers, the subsequent justifications will be analyzed to extract specific false claims. These claims will then be presented to the same model in a new session to test if the model can identify them as incorrect. Evaluation metrics will include overall accuracy, hallucination rate, and the rate at which the model recognizes its own snowballed hallucinations. Additional experiments will test the impact of chain-of-thought prompting and decoding parameters (e.g., temperature) on hallucination propagation. Manual verification will supplement automated extraction and assessment procedures.
6825ba09383bc758f9a2feaebabe35a6cd4adc4c.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the concept of 'hallucination snowballing,' where language models generate further incorrect statements to justify earlier mistakes, even when these statements are independently recognized as false by the model. This work systematically constructs datasets and evaluation protocols to isolate and measure this phenomenon, distinguishing it from traditional knowledge-gap-based hallucinations. The proposal also explores the limitations of prompting and decoding strategies in mitigating snowballed hallucinations, highlighting a previously underexplored risk in language model deployment and suggesting directions for model training and inference improvements.

682ff0690c87a31c6bc148e53f56b5b494621d66.title: Non-Parametric Outlier Synthesis
682ff0690c87a31c6bc148e53f56b5b494621d66.research_question: How can out-of-distribution (OOD) detection performance be improved in machine learning models without relying on restrictive parametric assumptions about the feature space, and can a flexible, generalizable approach be developed that synthesizes artificial OOD data for robust model regularization and reliable decision boundary learning?
682ff0690c87a31c6bc148e53f56b5b494621d66.hypothesis: A non-parametric outlier synthesis framework that generates artificial OOD training data without making distributional assumptions on in-distribution (ID) embeddings will enable more flexible and generalizable OOD detection, leading to improved separation between ID and OOD data and superior detection performance compared to existing parametric or baseline methods.
682ff0690c87a31c6bc148e53f56b5b494621d66.proposed_method: A novel non-parametric outlier synthesis (NPOS) framework will be developed to generate artificial OOD samples for model regularization. The method will first identify boundary ID samples in the feature space using non-parametric k-nearest neighbor (k-NN) distance as a density estimation heuristic, selecting those with the highest k-NN distances as boundary points. Around each boundary embedding, multiple candidate outliers will be synthesized by sampling from a multivariate Gaussian kernel centered at the boundary point, with variance modulating the spread. Rejection sampling will be performed by retaining only those synthesized outliers that exhibit low likelihood under the estimated ID density, ensuring they are sufficiently distinct from ID data. The training objective will jointly optimize a classification loss for ID data and a binary cross-entropy loss that separates ID from synthesized outliers, facilitating end-to-end learning of both compact ID representations and a reliable OOD decision boundary.
682ff0690c87a31c6bc148e53f56b5b494621d66.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard benchmarks including CIFAR-100 and large-scale ImageNet datasets (ImageNet-100 and ImageNet-1k) as in-distribution data. OOD datasets will include iNaturalist, SUN, PLACES, and TEXTURES, with categories disjoint from the ID sets. The main backbone will be the CLIP vision-language model (e.g., ViT-B/16), with additional ablations on ResNet-based architectures and training from scratch. Baselines for comparison will include Maximum Concept Matching (MCM), Maximum Softmax Probability (MSP), ODIN, Energy, GradNorm, ViM, KNN, and VOS (parametric outlier synthesis). Evaluation metrics will include FPR95 (false positive rate at 95% true positive rate), AUROC (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve), and ID classification accuracy. Training will involve fine-tuning the last layers of the backbone with the proposed dual-loss objective, and extensive ablation studies will be conducted on hyperparameters such as regularization weight, variance for outlier synthesis, and k in k-NN distance.
682ff0690c87a31c6bc148e53f56b5b494621d66.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a non-parametric outlier synthesis approach that does not make any distributional assumptions on the ID embeddings, offering greater flexibility and generality compared to parametric methods. The synthesis process is mathematically formalized as a rejection sampling procedure based on non-parametric density estimation, enabling the generation of realistic and diverse OOD samples for effective model regularization. The approach is scalable to large datasets and adaptable to both pre-trained and from-scratch training regimes. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate significant improvements in OOD detection performance over competitive baselines, with comprehensive ablations providing insights into the efficacy and robustness of the method.

685ca0971a9dfd23c8548ddcc3ddd8bf8e41b13e.title: Regret Minimization and Convergence to Equilibria in General-sum Markov Games
685ca0971a9dfd23c8548ddcc3ddd8bf8e41b13e.research_question: Can decentralized algorithms be designed for learning in general-sum Markov games that, when adopted by all agents, provide sublinear individual regret guarantees and ensure convergence to correlated equilibria?
685ca0971a9dfd23c8548ddcc3ddd8bf8e41b13e.hypothesis: If all agents in a general-sum Markov game adopt a suitably designed decentralized policy optimization algorithm based on optimistic online mirror descent with swap regret minimization, then each agent will achieve sublinear individual swap regret, leading to convergence to correlated equilibria.
685ca0971a9dfd23c8548ddcc3ddd8bf8e41b13e.proposed_method: A decentralized policy optimization algorithm is proposed for multiplayer, finite-horizon, tabular Markov games under the full-information setting, where agents have access to exact state-action value functions. Each agent independently runs a policy optimization routine that employs a swap regret minimization meta-algorithm, using optimistic online mirror descent (OOMD) with log-barrier regularization as the base algorithm at each state-action pair. The algorithm maintains and updates policy distributions via OOMD steps, ensuring bounded path length of policy iterates and resilience to non-stationarity induced by other agents' learning. No communication between agents is required, and the method is computationally efficient, relying only on local updates and solving linear systems for policy updates at each episode.
685ca0971a9dfd23c8548ddcc3ddd8bf8e41b13e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in the tabular, finite-horizon, full-information Markov game setting, where agents interact over T episodes. The primary evaluation metric is the individual swap regret of each agent, with secondary metrics including convergence rate to correlated equilibrium. The algorithm will be compared against existing centralized and decentralized baselines for general-sum Markov games, including algorithms based on V-learning and optimistic gradient methods. Both general Markov games and the special case of independent transition functions will be considered, with theoretical and empirical analysis of regret bounds and convergence rates. Datasets will consist of synthetic Markov game instances with varying numbers of agents, states, and actions to assess scalability and robustness.
685ca0971a9dfd23c8548ddcc3ddd8bf8e41b13e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first decentralized algorithm for general-sum Markov games that achieves sublinear individual swap regret when adopted by all agents, without requiring communication. The method leverages a novel reduction of policy optimization in Markov games to weighted regret minimization with unknown, path-length-dependent weights, and demonstrates that OOMD with log-barrier regularization is sufficiently adaptive to handle this setting. The algorithm guarantees convergence to correlated equilibria and provides explicit regret bounds, improving upon prior work that either required centralized coordination, policy sharing, or suffered from computational intractability. The approach is robust to non-stationarity and generalizes techniques from normal-form games to the more challenging Markov game setting.

68735af959504b0c812f591a56e10254be271928.title: Applying Guidance in a Limited Interval Improves Sample and Distribution Quality in Diffusion Models
68735af959504b0c812f591a56e10254be271928.research_question: How can the application of guidance in diffusion models be optimized to improve both sample quality and distribution fidelity, while reducing computational cost, across different architectures and datasets?
68735af959504b0c812f591a56e10254be271928.hypothesis: Limiting the application of classifier-free guidance to a specific interval of noise levels in the sampling chain, rather than applying it uniformly throughout, will improve both the perceptual quality and distributional fidelity of generated images, and reduce inference cost.
68735af959504b0c812f591a56e10254be271928.proposed_method: A novel approach is proposed in which classifier-free guidance (CFG) is applied only within a continuous interval of noise levels during the diffusion sampling process, rather than at all steps. The method defines a piecewise constant guidance weight function w(σ), which is set to a fixed value within the chosen interval (σ_lo, σ_hi] and to 1 elsewhere, effectively disabling guidance outside this range. The transitions at σ_lo and σ_hi are aligned exactly with step boundaries to maintain numerical stability and smoothness in the ODE solver. This interval is selected based on empirical evaluation, with the aim of maximizing beneficial effects (crisper, higher-quality images) while avoiding detrimental effects (mode collapse, reduced diversity) observed at high and low noise levels. The approach is compatible with a variety of deterministic samplers and diffusion model architectures.
68735af959504b0c812f591a56e10254be271928.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ImageNet-512 dataset using state-of-the-art diffusion models, including EDM2 (small and XXL variants) and DiT-XL/2, as well as on the large-scale Stable Diffusion XL (SD-XL) model. The evaluation will use standard metrics such as FID and FD_DINOv2, as well as precision and recall in feature space, to assess both sample quality and distributional fidelity. Baseline comparisons will include traditional classifier-free guidance applied at all noise levels and ablations with varying guidance intervals and weights.
