Sampling will be performed with standard deterministic solvers (e.g., 32-step Heun sampler for EDM2 and SD-XL, 250-step iDDPM for DiT-XL/2), and grid searches will be used to determine optimal interval and weight parameters. Qualitative analyses will complement quantitative results, and computational cost (in terms of guidance evaluations) will be measured.
68735af959504b0c812f591a56e10254be271928.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the concept of restricting classifier-free guidance to a limited interval of noise levels, rather than applying it uniformly, as a simple yet effective modification to diffusion model sampling. This method is claimed to yield significant improvements in both FID and FD_DINOv2 across multiple models and datasets, while also reducing inference cost by decreasing the number of unconditional model evaluations. The approach is robust to sampling parameters and model architectures, and exposes the guidance interval as a new, interpretable hyperparameter for diffusion models. The method is also shown to enable higher guidance weights without the usual trade-off in diversity, leading to both sharper and more varied images.

6883ca3ed0dc59935a6fdf566079c6d0036c09ce.title: Semiparametric doubly robust targeted double machine learning: a review
6883ca3ed0dc59935a6fdf566079c6d0036c09ce.research_question: How can efficient estimation of complex target parameters in causal inference and related statistical problems be achieved in nonparametric and semiparametric models, and what are the fundamental efficiency bounds for such estimators?
6883ca3ed0dc59935a6fdf566079c6d0036c09ce.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that influence function-based estimators, constructed via semiparametric theory and targeted double machine learning approaches, can achieve minimax optimality and attain nonparametric efficiency bounds for a wide range of target parameters under weak model assumptions.
6883ca3ed0dc59935a6fdf566079c6d0036c09ce.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed for constructing estimators of target parameters (functionals) in nonparametric and semiparametric models, with a focus on settings common in causal inference. The approach will leverage influence function theory to derive efficient estimators and correct plug-in estimators, utilizing von Mises expansions and pathwise differentiability to characterize the local behavior of functionals. Parametric submodels will be used to connect classical Cramer-Rao bounds to nonparametric efficiency benchmarks, and efficient influence functions will be derived for a variety of target parameters, including average treatment effects, mediation effects, and stochastic intervention effects. The methodology will be extended to handle high-dimensional and complex data regimes, and practical shortcuts for influence function derivation will be provided.
6883ca3ed0dc59935a6fdf566079c6d0036c09ce.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using both synthetic and real-world datasets relevant to causal inference, such as those involving treatment effects, missing data, and mediation analysis. The proposed estimators will be compared against standard plug-in estimators, inverse probability weighting, and other state-of-the-art semiparametric and machine learning-based methods. Evaluation metrics will include mean squared error, bias, variance, and coverage probability of confidence intervals, with particular attention to whether the estimators attain the theoretical nonparametric efficiency bounds. Simulation studies will systematically vary sample size, dimensionality, and model complexity to assess robustness and scalability.
6883ca3ed0dc59935a6fdf566079c6d0036c09ce.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified, semiparametric framework for efficient estimation of a broad class of target parameters using influence function-based methods, with explicit derivation of efficiency bounds in nonparametric models. The approach provides practical tools for constructing doubly robust and targeted estimators, extends classical efficiency theory to modern high-dimensional and causal inference settings, and offers new insights and shortcuts for influence function derivation. The work aims to bridge theoretical advances with practical estimation strategies, enabling optimal use of data in complex statistical and causal inference problems.

68850153b0210615c86f9a72624f34e2913bcddf.title: Document-Level Machine Translation with Large Language Models
68850153b0210615c86f9a72624f34e2913bcddf.research_question: Can large language models (LLMs) such as GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 effectively perform document-level machine translation, particularly with respect to modeling discourse phenomena, and how do their capabilities compare to advanced neural machine translation (NMT) systems and commercial MT products across diverse domains and language pairs?
68850153b0210615c86f9a72624f34e2913bcddf.hypothesis: Large language models, when prompted appropriately and potentially enhanced with techniques such as supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning from human feedback, are capable of outperforming traditional and commercial machine translation systems in document-level translation tasks, especially in modeling discourse phenomena such as coherence, consistency, and referential expressions.
68850153b0210615c86f9a72624f34e2913bcddf.proposed_method: The proposed research will conduct a comprehensive evaluation of LLMs (specifically GPT-3.5 and GPT-4) for document-level machine translation. The approach involves three main components: (1) designing and testing context-aware prompts to maximize the LLMs' ability to handle document-level context and discourse, (2) systematically comparing LLM-based translation outputs to those of commercial MT systems (e.g., Google Translate, DeepL, Tencent TranSmart) and advanced document-level NMT methods (such as MCN, G-Trans, MR-Doc2Doc, and others), and (3) probing the discourse modeling abilities of LLMs using contrastive test sets that target specific discourse phenomena (e.g., deixis, lexical consistency, ellipsis). The methodology will incorporate both automatic and human evaluation metrics, including general-purpose and discourse-specific measures, and will analyze the impact of various LLM training techniques (e.g., code pretraining, SFT, RLHF) on translation and discourse performance. Detailed prompt engineering will be performed to ensure robust and representative evaluation conditions.
68850153b0210615c86f9a72624f34e2913bcddf.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of document-level translation benchmarks covering three language pairs (Chinese-English, English-German, English-Russian) and multiple domains (news, social, fiction, Q&A, TED, Europarl, subtitle). Datasets include mZPRT, WMT2022, IWSLT, NewsCommentary, Europarl, and OpenSub2018, with careful consideration to avoid data contamination. Evaluation will use both automatic metrics (sentence-level and document-level BLEU, TER, COMET, d-BLEU) and targeted discourse metrics (consistency of terminology translation (CTT), accuracy of zero pronoun translation (AZPT)). Human evaluation will assess both general quality (fluency, adequacy) and discourse-aware quality (consistency, anaphora, word choice) using professional annotators. Contrastive test sets will be used to probe LLMs' handling of specific discourse phenomena, with both prediction and explanation tasks evaluated. Baselines will include state-of-the-art document-level NMT models and commercial MT systems, with prompt ablation studies to assess the effect of different prompt designs.
68850153b0210615c86f9a72624f34e2913bcddf.novelty_claims: This research proposes a systematic and in-depth evaluation framework for assessing LLMs' capabilities in document-level machine translation, focusing on discourse modeling—a relatively underexplored aspect for LLMs. The approach introduces context-aware prompt engineering for document-level translation, establishes new benchmarks and probing methods for discourse phenomena, and provides a comprehensive comparison with both commercial and advanced NMT systems. The study also investigates the impact of LLM training techniques (such as SFT, code pretraining, RLHF) on translation and discourse performance. The proposed benchmarks, system outputs, and human annotations will be publicly released to facilitate future research, and the findings are expected to inspire new paradigms for document-level translation using LLMs.

68a293d91b2e0370c07febb806752e7998a41658.title: StyleGuard: Preventing Text-to-Image-Model-based Style Mimicry Attacks by Style Perturbations
68a293d91b2e0370c07febb806752e7998a41658.research_question: How can robust and transferable defenses be developed to protect images from unauthorized style mimicry attacks by text-to-image diffusion models, especially in the presence of advanced purification and transformation techniques?
68a293d91b2e0370c07febb806752e7998a41658.hypothesis: Optimizing style-related features in the latent space of images and introducing perturbations that target both style and denoising characteristics will produce protective noise that is robust to purification-based attacks and transferable across different text-to-image models.
68a293d91b2e0370c07febb806752e7998a41658.proposed_method: A novel defense framework, StyleGuard, will be developed to generate imperceptible perturbations on images to prevent style mimicry by text-to-image diffusion models. The method will introduce a style loss that maximizes the discrepancy between the style features (mean and variance in the latent space) of protected images and clean reference images, while aligning them with target images of distinct styles. To improve robustness against purification-based attacks, an upscale loss will be designed to maximize denoising error across an ensemble of purification and upscaling models, using a meta-learning approach. The optimization will alternate between updating the surrogate diffusion model and the protected images, incorporating random transformations during training to further enhance robustness. The total loss will combine denoising, style, and upscale losses, and the optimization will use projected gradient descent (PGD) under a specified attack budget.
68a293d91b2e0370c07febb806752e7998a41658.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the WikiArt and CelebA datasets to evaluate protection against both style mimicry and personalization attacks. The evaluation will cover multiple fine-tuning methods (DreamBooth, Textual Inversion) and settings (full-tuning, LoRA-based fine-tuning) on various Stable Diffusion models (SDv1.4, SDv1.5, SDv2.1, SD-XL). Attacks will include random transformations (Gaussian noise, cropping, resizing), purification methods (DiffPure, Noise Upscaling), and black-box upscalers (Finegrain Image Enhancer). Baselines for comparison will include Glaze, Mist, Anti-DreamBooth, MetaCloak, and SimAC, with all methods constrained to the same attack budget. Evaluation metrics will include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), precision, mimicry success rate (via human annotation), and identity match score (IMS) for personalization. The experimental setup will also test cross-model and cross-method transferability.
68a293d91b2e0370c07febb806752e7998a41658.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel style loss that perturbs global style-related features in the latent space to enhance model-agnostic transferability, and an upscale loss that enables robustness against advanced purification and upscaling attacks. The approach is the first to demonstrate effective defense against both style mimicry and personalization attacks across multiple datasets and fine-tuning methods, including DreamBooth and Textual Inversion. StyleGuard achieves superior robustness to transformations and purification, and exhibits strong cross-model transferability compared to existing defenses.

68e45d1e046e08379e181c0fbff3f4419371a506.title: TriDet: Temporal Action Detection with Relative Boundary Modeling
68e45d1e046e08379e181c0fbff3f4419371a506.research_question: How can temporal action detection in untrimmed videos be improved, particularly in terms of precise action boundary localization and computational efficiency, without relying on complex self-attention mechanisms?
68e45d1e046e08379e181c0fbff3f4419371a506.hypothesis: Modeling action boundaries via a relative probability distribution around the boundary, combined with an efficient convolutional-based feature pyramid, will yield more precise temporal localization and improve computational efficiency compared to existing self-attention-based and regression-based approaches.
68e45d1e046e08379e181c0fbff3f4419371a506.proposed_method: A one-stage temporal action detection framework is developed, featuring a novel Trident-head that models action boundaries through an estimated relative probability distribution over a set of temporal bins around each boundary. Instead of regressing boundary offsets directly, the Trident-head predicts the likelihood of each instant being a boundary and computes the expected offset, leveraging three branches for start, end, and center-offset predictions. The feature extraction backbone is followed by a Scalable-Granularity Perception (SGP) feature pyramid, which replaces self-attention with a dual-branch convolutional module: an instant-level branch to enhance feature discriminability and a window-level branch to capture temporal context at multiple scales. The SGP layer uses group normalization and depth-wise convolutions to efficiently aggregate information across temporal granularities, and the detection head is shared across pyramid levels for parameter efficiency.
68e45d1e046e08379e181c0fbff3f4419371a506.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on four challenging temporal action detection benchmarks: THUMOS14, HACS, EPIC-KITCHEN 100, and ActivityNet-1.3. Backbone features are extracted using pretrained action classification networks such as I3D, SlowFast, and R(2+1)D. The proposed method is compared against state-of-the-art baselines, including both two-stage and one-stage detectors, as well as transformer-based methods like ActionFormer and TALLFormer. Evaluation metrics include mean Average Precision (mAP) at various Intersection over Union (IoU) thresholds, following standard protocols for each dataset. Ablation studies are performed to analyze the impact of the SGP layer, Trident-head, number of feature pyramid levels, and number of bins. Computational efficiency is assessed in terms of GMACs and inference latency, and all experiments are run on NVIDIA A100 GPUs with consistent training schedules and hyperparameters.
68e45d1e046e08379e181c0fbff3f4419371a506.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel Trident-head that models action boundaries using a relative probability distribution, enabling more precise and robust boundary localization than direct regression or global segment-based methods. The Scalable-Granularity Perception (SGP) layer is proposed as an efficient alternative to self-attention, mitigating the rank loss problem and reducing computational overhead while maintaining or improving detection accuracy. The overall framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks with significantly lower computational cost and latency compared to leading transformer-based approaches. Comprehensive ablation studies and efficiency analyses substantiate the effectiveness and generalizability of the proposed components.

690df0820f35a47e1ce44f90e6ddb4132aa09267.title: Vision-Language Models for Vision Tasks: A Survey
690df0820f35a47e1ce44f90e6ddb4132aa09267.research_question: How can vision-language models be systematically developed and evaluated to address a wide range of visual recognition tasks, such as image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation, without relying on large amounts of task-specific labeled data?
690df0820f35a47e1ce44f90e6ddb4132aa09267.hypothesis: Vision-language models pre-trained on large-scale image-text pairs from the web can capture rich vision-language correlations, enabling effective zero-shot predictions on diverse visual recognition tasks and reducing the need for task-specific fine-tuning.
690df0820f35a47e1ce44f90e6ddb4132aa09267.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework for vision-language model (VLM) development is proposed, encompassing three main components: (1) large-scale pre-training on web-sourced image-text pairs using a combination of contrastive, generative, and alignment objectives to learn robust and transferable representations; (2) exploration of multiple network architectures, including two-tower, two-leg, and unified one-tower models, to optimize cross-modal feature extraction and fusion; (3) integration of transfer learning techniques (such as prompt tuning and feature adapters) and knowledge distillation methods to further adapt and compress VLMs for downstream tasks. The methodology includes detailed design of pre-training objectives (e.g., image-text contrastive loss, masked image/language/cross-modal modeling, image-text and region-word matching) and leverages both global and local semantic alignment between modalities.
690df0820f35a47e1ce44f90e6ddb4132aa09267.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a wide range of public datasets for both pre-training (e.g., LAION400M, CC12M, YFCC100M, COCO, WIT) and downstream evaluation (e.g., ImageNet, COCO Detection, LVIS, ADE20k, Cityscapes, Flickr30k, UCF101). Baseline comparisons will include traditional supervised and unsupervised pre-training paradigms, as well as state-of-the-art VLMs such as CLIP, ALIGN, and FILIP. Evaluation metrics will cover accuracy, mean average precision (mAP), mean intersection over union (mIoU), recall, and top-1/top-5 accuracy, depending on the task. Both zero-shot prediction and linear probing setups will be used to assess the generalization and transferability of the proposed models across image classification, object detection, semantic segmentation, image-text retrieval, and action recognition tasks.
690df0820f35a47e1ce44f90e6ddb4132aa09267.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified and systematic approach to VLM development for visual recognition, combining large-scale web data pre-training, hybrid objective functions, and advanced network architectures. It aims to enable zero-shot predictions across multiple tasks without task-specific fine-tuning, leverages multi-level semantic alignment (global and local), and incorporates recent advances in transfer learning and knowledge distillation. The project also proposes comprehensive benchmarking and analysis across diverse datasets, providing a foundation for future research directions in vision-language modeling for visual recognition.

6912a12f3710bf4bbdfd9f55f90311426fc1c32c.title: Graph Foundation Models: Concepts, Opportunities and Challenges
6912a12f3710bf4bbdfd9f55f90311426fc1c32c.research_question: Can a new class of graph foundation models be developed that, when pre-trained on large-scale graph data, demonstrate generalization and adaptability across a wide range of downstream graph tasks, similar to the capabilities seen in language foundation models?
6912a12f3710bf4bbdfd9f55f90311426fc1c32c.hypothesis: Graph foundation models, when pre-trained on extensive and diverse graph data and equipped with appropriate backbone architectures and adaptation mechanisms, will exhibit emergent abilities and homogenization, enabling superior performance and generalization across multiple graph-based tasks compared to traditional deep graph learning approaches.
6912a12f3710bf4bbdfd9f55f90311426fc1c32c.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework for graph foundation models (GFMs) will be developed, exploring three main architectural paradigms: (1) GNN-based models, which leverage advanced message passing and transformer-based graph neural networks as backbones; (2) LLM-based models, which convert graph data into textual or tokenized formats to utilize large language models; and (3) hybrid GNN+LLM models, which integrate both GNNs and LLMs for synergistic learning. The methodology will emphasize large-scale self-supervised pre-training on diverse graph datasets using both contrastive and generative objectives, such as graph reconstruction, property prediction, and contrastive learning across multiple graph views. Adaptation strategies will include both full-model fine-tuning and parameter-efficient methods, as well as prompt-based adaptation to enable transfer to a variety of downstream tasks (e.g., node classification, link prediction, graph classification) with minimal labeled data. Special attention will be given to designing pre-training tasks and adaptation mechanisms that address the non-Euclidean nature of graph data and the diversity of graph tasks.
6912a12f3710bf4bbdfd9f55f90311426fc1c32c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of benchmark graph datasets spanning multiple domains, such as social networks, biological networks, molecular graphs, and heterogeneous or dynamic graphs. Baseline comparisons will include traditional deep graph learning models (e.g., GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE, GIN), recent graph transformers, and existing self-supervised graph pre-training methods. Evaluation metrics will cover accuracy, F1 score, and ROC-AUC for classification tasks, as well as transferability and generalization to out-of-domain graphs and few-shot settings. The experimental setup will systematically assess the impact of different backbone architectures, pre-training objectives, and adaptation strategies, including prompt-based and parameter-efficient fine-tuning, on both in-domain and cross-domain downstream tasks. Ablation studies will be performed to isolate the contributions of emergence and homogenization capabilities.
6912a12f3710bf4bbdfd9f55f90311426fc1c32c.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the formal concept and taxonomy of graph foundation models, systematically analyzing their key characteristics, challenges, and opportunities. It pioneers the exploration of emergent abilities and homogenization in graph learning, drawing parallels and distinctions with language foundation models. The work proposes new pre-training and adaptation paradigms specifically tailored for the unique challenges of graph data, including prompt-based adaptation and parameter-efficient fine-tuning for graphs. The research also aims to establish a unified framework and evaluation protocol for GFMs, laying the groundwork for future advances in generalizable and adaptable graph machine learning.

69295ae728d8e02ef6da80fa9cbc2c613acac6de.title: Solving Linear Inverse Problems Provably via Posterior Sampling with Latent Diffusion Models
69295ae728d8e02ef6da80fa9cbc2c613acac6de.research_question: Can linear inverse problems be solved in a provably correct and efficient manner by leveraging pre-trained latent diffusion models, and how does this approach compare to existing pixel-space diffusion-based methods across a variety of inverse imaging tasks?
69295ae728d8e02ef6da80fa9cbc2c613acac6de.hypothesis: Posterior sampling with pre-trained latent diffusion models, augmented with measurement-consistency and manifold-preserving objectives, enables provably correct and state-of-the-art recovery for linear inverse problems without the need for task-specific finetuning.
69295ae728d8e02ef6da80fa9cbc2c613acac6de.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed for solving linear inverse problems by performing posterior sampling in the latent space of pre-trained latent diffusion models (LDMs). The method formulates the reverse diffusion process in the latent space, guided by a combination of measurement-consistency gradients and a 'gluing' objective that enforces consistency between the latent code and its decoded-encoded representation. The algorithm iteratively updates the latent variable using gradients of the measurement error (between observed measurements and those generated by the decoded latent) and the gluing term, which penalizes deviations from the data manifold. The approach is theoretically analyzed in a linear model setting, showing that exact sample recovery is possible under mild assumptions, and is robust to the choice of step size due to the gluing objective. The method is designed to be compatible with large-scale foundation models such as Stable Diffusion, enabling zero-shot application to a wide range of inverse problems.
69295ae728d8e02ef6da80fa9cbc2c613acac6de.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both in-distribution (FFHQ 256) and out-of-distribution (ImageNet 256, web images) datasets. The method is evaluated on a variety of inverse problems including random inpainting, block inpainting, denoising, deblurring, destriping, and super-resolution, using standard measurement operators (e.g., masking, downsampling, blurring) as in prior work. Baselines include state-of-the-art posterior sampling algorithms such as DPS, DDRM, MCG, PnP-ADMM, Score-SDE, and ADMM-TV. Evaluation metrics comprise LPIPS, PSNR, SSIM, and FID. The proposed method leverages pre-trained Stable Diffusion v1.5 and LDM-VQ-4 models, and is compared against baselines using identical experimental setups and validation splits. Implementation details ensure fair comparison, including resolution matching and masking strategies.
69295ae728d8e02ef6da80fa9cbc2c613acac6de.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable provable and practical solution of linear inverse problems using pre-trained latent diffusion models, rather than pixel-space diffusion models. The framework introduces a novel gluing objective that ensures measurement-consistency and manifold adherence in the latent space, leading to theoretical guarantees of exact sample recovery and robustness to step size selection. The method demonstrates state-of-the-art performance across a range of inverse problems without the need for task-specific finetuning, and is broadly applicable to any foundation model based on latent diffusion.

693b0c7fc4351b060b7cc0903994b96af567e38c.title: Endless Jailbreaks with Bijection Learning
693b0c7fc4351b060b7cc0903994b96af567e38c.research_question: How can adversarial prompts be systematically generated to bypass safety mechanisms in large language models (LLMs) in a black-box, universal, and scale-adaptive manner, and how does model capability relate to vulnerability to such attacks?
693b0c7fc4351b060b7cc0903994b96af567e38c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a black-box, universal, and scale-adaptive attack method leveraging in-context learning of arbitrary string-to-string bijections can effectively bypass safety mechanisms in frontier LLMs, and that more capable models will be more vulnerable to such attacks as encoding complexity increases.
693b0c7fc4351b060b7cc0903994b96af567e38c.proposed_method: A novel attack framework, termed bijection learning, will be developed to systematically generate adversarial prompts for LLMs. The method constructs random bijective mappings from the English alphabet to arbitrary strings (e.g., permuted letters, digit sequences, or model tokens), with tunable complexity parameters such as dispersion (number of letters not mapping to themselves) and encoding length. The attack prompt consists of a multi-turn conversation: a system message explaining the bijection, several user-assistant translation examples in the bijection language, and finally the harmful query encoded with the bijection. The LLM's response is decoded using the inverse mapping, and a denoising step is applied to correct minor errors. The method supports best-of-n sampling, enabling repeated generation of diverse attack prompts for a single intent, and is designed to function in black-box settings without requiring access to model internals.
693b0c7fc4351b060b7cc0903994b96af567e38c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of frontier LLMs, including Claude 3 Haiku, Claude 3 Opus, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o-mini, and GPT-4o. Evaluation will use the AdvBench-50 and HarmBench datasets of harmful intents, with attack success rate (ASR) as the primary metric. The proposed method will be compared against baselines including white-box optimization-based attacks (e.g., Greedy Coordinate Gradient), black-box AI-generated attacks (PAIR, TAP), and an ensemble of 11 prior encoding-based attacks (e.g., ASCII, Base64, ROT13, Morse code). Judging of model outputs will involve both automated LLM classifiers and strict human evaluation using a PREFS rubric to confirm practical, relevant, egregious, factually correct, and specific unsafe responses. Additional experiments will sweep bijection complexity parameters and analyze failure modes, as well as evaluate the impact of guard models of varying capability on attack mitigation.
693b0c7fc4351b060b7cc0903994b96af567e38c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to combine in-context learning with arbitrary, randomly-sampled bijective encodings for jailbreaking LLMs, enabling black-box, universal, and scale-adaptive attacks. Unlike previous encoding-based attacks, this method allows fine-grained control over encoding complexity and supports endless prompt fuzzing via random sampling. The research will establish a quantitative relationship between model capability and vulnerability, revealing that more capable models are more severely compromised by complex bijection attacks. The analysis will also provide new insights into the computational overload hypothesis for safety degradation and demonstrate the limitations of current guardrail defenses, even at capability parity.

69421149cd5fd73a16f9f278fc76715f4d07735c.title: On the Curses of Future and History in Future-dependent Value Functions for Off-policy Evaluation
69421149cd5fd73a16f9f278fc76715f4d07735c.research_question: How can off-policy evaluation (OPE) in partially observable environments with complex observations be achieved with estimation guarantees that avoid exponential dependence on the horizon, and what new coverage assumptions or algorithms can enable polynomially-bounded estimation errors in such settings?
69421149cd5fd73a16f9f278fc76715f4d07735c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by introducing novel coverage assumptions specifically tailored to the structure of partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs), such as outcome coverage and belief coverage, it is possible to achieve polynomially-bounded estimation guarantees for OPE, thereby overcoming the exponential dependence on the horizon that plagues existing methods.
69421149cd5fd73a16f9f278fc76715f4d07735c.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed for OPE in POMDPs by leveraging future-dependent value functions (FDVFs) and introducing two novel coverage assumptions: outcome coverage and belief coverage. The methodology will involve constructing weighted minimum-norm solutions for FDVFs that minimize the weighted L2 or L-infinity norm, using outcome matrices and belief state vectors derived from the POMDP structure. The approach will also include the derivation of effective history weights through belief matching, enabling a joint conversion between history and future representations. Additionally, a new algorithm analogous to marginalized importance sampling (MIS) for MDPs will be designed, which minimizes a loss function based on effective history weights and FDVF Bellman residuals, and does not require double-sampling or Bellman completeness assumptions.
69421149cd5fd73a16f9f278fc76715f4d07735c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic and/or benchmark POMDP environments with finite horizons and complex observation spaces. The proposed methods will be compared against standard OPE baselines such as importance sampling (IS), fitted-Q evaluation (FQE), and marginalized importance sampling (MIS) adapted to POMDPs. Evaluation metrics will include estimation error of policy value, variance, and coverage parameter tightness, with a focus on how these scale with the horizon and latent state space size. The experimental setup will also analyze the impact of the new coverage assumptions on the boundedness of FDVFs and the sample complexity of the new algorithms.
69421149cd5fd73a16f9f278fc76715f4d07735c.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces outcome coverage and belief coverage as new, interpretable coverage assumptions for POMDPs that enable polynomial estimation guarantees for OPE, overcoming the exponential dependence on the horizon present in prior approaches. The framework provides the first quantitative analysis of the boundedness of future-dependent value functions under these assumptions, and leads to the development of new algorithms with complementary properties, including a novel MIS-like estimator for POMDPs. The analyses leverage the linear-algebraic structure and normalization properties unique to POMDPs, resulting in improved bounds that avoid explicit dependence on the size of the latent state space.

6947893915861e8c30bc6b010eb1faf0d82f0a19.title: Logical Consistency of Large Language Models in Fact-checking
6947893915861e8c30bc6b010eb1faf0d82f0a19.research_question: How can the logical consistency of large language models (LLMs) be systematically assessed and improved in fact-checking tasks involving complex propositional logic queries over knowledge graphs?
6947893915861e8c30bc6b010eb1faf0d82f0a19.hypothesis: Supervised fine-tuning of LLMs on datasets constructed from knowledge graphs with explicit logical operators (negation, conjunction, disjunction) will significantly improve both the accuracy and logical consistency of LLM responses in fact-checking tasks, including for complex and out-of-distribution logical queries.
6947893915861e8c30bc6b010eb1faf0d82f0a19.proposed_method: A novel methodology will be developed to assess and enhance the logical consistency of LLMs in fact-checking tasks using knowledge graphs (KGs) as authoritative sources. The approach will involve constructing logical fact-checking datasets by transforming KG triples into (Fact, Context) pairs, where the context is retrieved via graph traversal (e.g., BFS) or embedding-based retrieval methods. Logical consistency will be quantitatively defined for primitive logical operators (negation, conjunction, disjunction) and extended to complex propositional logic queries and logic rules (e.g., commutative, associative, distributive). Supervised fine-tuning will be performed on LLMs using instruction datasets that explicitly label the truth value of facts and their logical variants, with parameter-efficient fine-tuning (e.g., QLoRA) to improve scalability. The framework will also include mechanisms to optimize context length and relevance for LLM input.
6947893915861e8c30bc6b010eb1faf0d82f0a19.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three newly constructed logical fact-checking datasets derived from Freebase, NELL, and WikiKG90Mv2 knowledge graphs, covering both simple and complex logical queries. Baseline LLMs such as Llama2-7B, Llama2-13B, and Gemma-2B will be evaluated before and after supervised fine-tuning, with additional comparisons to zero-shot instruction prompting. Evaluation metrics will include both accuracy (correctness of fact-checking) and logical consistency (agreement with logical equivalence and operator semantics). The experimental setup will involve fine-tuning on one dataset and testing for generalization on others, as well as ablation studies on context retrieval methods, prompt strategies, and hyperparameters. Efficiency will be measured by comparing parameter-efficient fine-tuning to full fine-tuning and by reporting inference times.
6947893915861e8c30bc6b010eb1faf0d82f0a19.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first systematic framework for assessing and improving logical consistency of LLMs in fact-checking tasks involving complex propositional logic over knowledge graphs. Three new logical fact-checking datasets are created to enable community benchmarking. The methodology formalizes logical consistency for LLMs using primitive and complex logical operators and demonstrates that supervised fine-tuning on logical operators leads to significant improvements in both accuracy and logical consistency, with generalization to out-of-distribution queries. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning is shown to provide scalable improvements, and the approach is modular to accommodate future advances in context retrieval and LLM architectures.

695eb8837b9f78dd04166f3c94663f6044f23a35.title: On the Convergence of DP-SGD with Adaptive Clipping
695eb8837b9f78dd04166f3c94663f6044f23a35.research_question: How can adaptive quantile-based gradient clipping be theoretically analyzed and improved for differentially private stochastic optimization, and what are the convergence properties and practical guidelines for its use compared to constant-threshold clipping?
695eb8837b9f78dd04166f3c94663f6044f23a35.hypothesis: Adaptive quantile clipping in stochastic gradient descent, when combined with appropriately designed quantile and step size schedules, can mitigate bias and achieve provable convergence guarantees, including in differentially private settings.
695eb8837b9f78dd04166f3c94663f6044f23a35.proposed_method: A new framework for stochastic gradient descent (SGD) is developed that employs adaptive quantile clipping (QC-SGD), where the clipping threshold at each iteration is set to a chosen quantile of the distribution of gradient norms. The method analyzes the interplay between the quantile parameter and the step size, providing schedules for both to control the bias introduced by clipping and ensure convergence. The approach is extended to a differentially private variant (DP-QC-SGD), where Gaussian noise is added with variance proportional to the adaptive threshold, and the privacy loss is carefully managed. Theoretical analysis is provided under standard smoothness and heavy-tailed noise assumptions, and practical guidelines for parameter selection are derived from the analysis.
695eb8837b9f78dd04166f3c94663f6044f23a35.experiment_details: Experiments are proposed on a variety of federated learning and centralized learning benchmarks, such as CIFAR-100, EMNIST, Shakespeare, and StackOverflow, to evaluate the convergence and utility of QC-SGD and DP-QC-SGD. Baselines include standard SGD, SGD with constant clipping, and existing adaptive clipping methods. Evaluation metrics will include convergence to stationary points (measured by expected squared gradient norm), model utility (accuracy or loss), and privacy parameters (ε, δ). The experimental setup will vary quantile and step size schedules, and will examine the effect of batch size, noise scale, and dataset characteristics on convergence and privacy-utility trade-offs.
695eb8837b9f78dd04166f3c94663f6044f23a35.novelty_claims: This proposal establishes the first comprehensive theoretical convergence guarantees for SGD with adaptive quantile clipping, including in the differentially private setting. The analysis reveals and addresses the bias problem inherent in quantile clipping, provides explicit schedules for quantile and step size to ensure convergence, and offers practical guidelines for parameter tuning. The framework unifies and extends prior empirical heuristics for adaptive clipping, and delivers the first theoretical foundations for their use in private optimization.

69764587c8422a8f439e85bbf47b7748f880d4ed.title: Can Machines Help Us Answering Question 16 in Datasheets, and In Turn Reflecting on Inappropriate Content?
69764587c8422a8f439e85bbf47b7748f880d4ed.research_question: Can machine learning models assist in the semi-automatic identification and documentation of potentially inappropriate content in large-scale image datasets, thereby supporting dataset creators in reflecting on and answering datasheet questions regarding offensive, insulting, threatening, or anxiety-inducing material?
69764587c8422a8f439e85bbf47b7748f880d4ed.hypothesis: Pre-trained vision-language models, when steered via prompt-tuning with socio-moral value datasets, can reliably detect a broad range of inappropriate content in large image datasets, reducing the need for exhaustive manual review and improving the quality and comprehensiveness of dataset documentation.
69764587c8422a8f439e85bbf47b7748f880d4ed.proposed_method: A semi-automatic pipeline, Q16, will be developed to identify and document potentially inappropriate image content in large datasets. The approach leverages the implicit knowledge of pre-trained vision-language models (specifically CLIP) and steers their output via prompt-tuning using a socio-moral image dataset (SMID) as supervision. The pipeline first applies prompt-tuned CLIP to flag potentially inappropriate images, using optimized continuous prompts learned through gradient descent to maximize classification performance. Detected images are then described using an autoregressive caption generation model (MAGMA), which generates neutral, multi-sample textual descriptions for each flagged image. Finally, the documentation process summarizes the identified content through wordclouds generated from both dataset annotations and the automatically generated captions, providing both quantitative and qualitative overviews for dataset creators.
69764587c8422a8f439e85bbf47b7748f880d4ed.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale computer vision datasets such as ImageNet-ILSVRC-2012 and OpenImages V6. The Socio-Moral Image Database (SMID), annotated for moral valence, will be used for prompt-tuning and evaluation. Baseline models will include standard deep learning architectures (e.g., ResNet50) pre-trained on ImageNet and fine-tuned or linear-probed on SMID, compared against CLIP models with zero-shot, few-shot, and prompt-tuned configurations. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, with 10-fold cross-validation on SMID. The documentation process will be assessed by the ratio and diversity of flagged images, the quality of generated captions, and the informativeness of wordcloud summaries. Human-in-the-loop validation is incorporated to ensure subjective appropriateness and to refine the flagged subsets.
69764587c8422a8f439e85bbf47b7748f880d4ed.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a semi-automatic, human-in-the-loop pipeline that combines prompt-tuned vision-language models and automated caption generation to assist in dataset documentation for inappropriate content. It expands the scope of inappropriate content detection beyond narrow categories such as nudity or misogyny, addressing a broader range of socio-moral concepts. The approach demonstrates that large pre-trained models can be efficiently steered to generalize detection of inappropriate content with minimal additional data, significantly reducing manual labor and improving transparency in dataset curation. The integration of wordcloud-based summarization and multi-sample captioning provides a novel, scalable means for dataset creators to reflect on and document problematic content.

697e0add95e880bd42e00bef838181e105f91981.title: MME: A Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models
697e0add95e880bd42e00bef838181e105f91981.research_question: How can a comprehensive and fair benchmark be developed to evaluate the perception and cognition abilities of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) across a wide range of tasks, while minimizing data leakage and the impact of prompt engineering?
697e0add95e880bd42e00bef838181e105f91981.hypothesis: A benchmark that uses manually constructed instruction-answer pairs, concise and standardized instructions, and covers both perception and cognition subtasks can provide a more accurate, fair, and comprehensive evaluation of MLLMs compared to existing evaluation methods.
697e0add95e880bd42e00bef838181e105f91981.proposed_method: A new evaluation benchmark, named MME, will be created to assess both perception and cognition abilities of MLLMs. The benchmark will consist of 14 subtasks, including coarse-grained perception (existence, count, position, color), fine-grained recognition (poster, celebrity, scene, landmark, artwork), OCR, and cognition tasks (commonsense reasoning, numerical calculation, text translation, code reasoning). All instruction-answer pairs will be manually designed to avoid data leakage, and instructions will be concise, typically requiring a 'yes' or 'no' answer to minimize the influence of prompt engineering. For each image, two questions will be posed (one with a 'yes' and one with a 'no' ground truth), and the evaluation will use both per-question and per-image accuracy metrics to provide strict and objective performance measurement.
697e0add95e880bd42e00bef838181e105f91981.experiment_details: The benchmark will be used to evaluate the zero-shot performance of 30 advanced MLLMs on the 14 defined subtasks. Images for coarse-grained perception tasks will be sampled from COCO, but with manual instruction-answer pairs, while fine-grained recognition images will be sourced from various public datasets, again with new manual annotations. Cognition tasks will use manually photographed or generated images. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy (per question) and accuracy+ (per image, requiring both questions to be answered correctly), with scores summed across subtasks for overall perception and cognition scores. Baselines will include a wide range of state-of-the-art MLLMs, and detailed leaderboards will be maintained for each subtask and overall performance.
697e0add95e880bd42e00bef838181e105f91981.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark is the first to comprehensively evaluate both perception and cognition in MLLMs with 14 diverse subtasks. All instruction-answer pairs are manually constructed to prevent data leakage, and instructions are standardized and concise to ensure fairness and minimize prompt engineering effects. The benchmark enables objective, quantitative, and reproducible evaluation through binary (yes/no) answers and strict accuracy metrics. The approach reveals current limitations and common failure modes in MLLMs, providing actionable insights for future model development and optimization.

69afd10d387423a03617d461c3f47a5f3033cc54.title: Hi Robot: Open-Ended Instruction Following with Hierarchical Vision-Language-Action Models
69afd10d387423a03617d461c3f47a5f3033cc54.research_question: How can robots in open-ended, human-centric environments be enabled to flexibly interpret and follow complex, multi-stage natural language instructions, incorporate real-time user feedback and corrections, and generalize to novel tasks and scenarios across diverse robotic platforms?
69afd10d387423a03617d461c3f47a5f3033cc54.hypothesis: A hierarchical vision-language-action (VLA) model, in which a high-level vision-language model interprets complex prompts and feedback to generate intermediate language commands for a low-level VLA policy, will enable robots to follow open-ended instructions, adapt to real-time corrections, and generalize to unseen tasks more effectively than flat or non-hierarchical approaches.
69afd10d387423a03617d461c3f47a5f3033cc54.proposed_method: A hierarchical framework is proposed, consisting of two main components: a high-level vision-language model (VLM) and a low-level vision-language-action (VLA) policy. The high-level VLM processes open-ended user prompts, visual observations from multiple cameras, and real-time user feedback to generate intermediate, contextually grounded language commands. These commands are then provided to the low-level VLA policy, which is fine-tuned to map these commands and visual inputs to continuous robot actions using flow-matching objectives. Synthetic data generation is employed to augment training, where a VLM is prompted with robot observations and skill labels to generate plausible user instructions and feedback, creating a rich dataset of situated interactions. The system is designed to run high-level inference at a lower frequency, updating commands upon user intervention or after a set time interval, while the low-level policy executes actions at a higher rate.
69afd10d387423a03617d461c3f47a5f3033cc54.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across three robotic domains: table bussing (cleaning up tables), sandwich making (assembling sandwiches with various ingredients), and grocery shopping (retrieving and placing items using a mobile bimanual robot). Each domain involves complex, multi-stage tasks with opportunities for real-time user feedback and corrections. The evaluation will use both human-labeled and synthetically generated datasets for training. Baselines will include a flat VLA policy (without hierarchy), a hierarchical policy using a large API-based VLM (GPT-4o) as the high-level model, and an oracle human high-level policy. Metrics will include Instruction Accuracy (alignment of robot actions with user intent and prompt) and Task Progress (proportion of task completed as intended), with human evaluators blind to the method. Ablation studies will assess the impact of synthetic data and hierarchical decomposition.
69afd10d387423a03617d461c3f47a5f3033cc54.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel hierarchical vision-language-action framework for robotic instruction following, enabling integration of complex, open-ended prompts and real-time user feedback into task execution. The method leverages synthetic data generation to create diverse, situated training examples, facilitating generalization to unseen tasks and user interactions. Unlike prior work, the system grounds high-level reasoning in both verbal and physical interaction, supports multi-stage task decomposition, and demonstrates adaptability across multiple robot platforms and task domains. The combination of hierarchical VLMs for both high-level reasoning and low-level control, along with the synthetic data generation pipeline, is claimed to provide new capabilities for flexible, intuitive, and steerable human-robot collaboration.

69b80ce5ab6c2263b145b1eaa23664145938f351.title: The Primacy Bias in Deep Reinforcement Learning
69b80ce5ab6c2263b145b1eaa23664145938f351.research_question: How can deep reinforcement learning agents be prevented from overfitting to early experiences, which may negatively impact their ability to learn from subsequent, potentially more useful data, across a variety of discrete and continuous control domains?
69b80ce5ab6c2263b145b1eaa23664145938f351.hypothesis: Periodically resetting a portion of a deep reinforcement learning agent's neural network, while preserving the accumulated experience replay buffer, will mitigate the primacy bias, thereby improving learning efficiency and final performance across diverse tasks and algorithms.
69b80ce5ab6c2263b145b1eaa23664145938f351.proposed_method: A mechanism will be developed that periodically reinitializes the parameters of selected layers (typically the last few layers) of the agent's neural networks during training, while maintaining the contents of the experience replay buffer. The method will be compatible with any deep RL algorithm that utilizes a replay buffer, and will require only two implementation choices: which layers to reset and how often to reset them. No additional pre-training will be performed after resetting; the agent will resume standard training immediately. The approach will be evaluated with different reset frequencies and layer selections to determine optimal configurations for various domains and architectures.
69b80ce5ab6c2263b145b1eaa23664145938f351.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both discrete and continuous control benchmarks, specifically the Atari 100k suite for discrete actions and the DeepMind Control Suite for continuous actions. The resetting mechanism will be applied to strong baseline algorithms: SPR for Atari, and SAC and DrQ for DeepMind Control Suite. Performance will be measured using interquartile mean (IQM), median, and mean scores across multiple seeds per environment. Baselines will include the same algorithms without resets, as well as other state-of-the-art methods from the literature. Additional ablations will investigate the effects of replay ratio, n-step target length, and which layers are reset. The evaluation will follow established guidelines for rigorous RL benchmarking, and results will be reported with confidence intervals.
69b80ce5ab6c2263b145b1eaa23664145938f351.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a simple, general, and computationally inexpensive resetting mechanism that mitigates the primacy bias in deep RL, a phenomenon where agents overfit to early experiences and fail to leverage later data. This approach is claimed to be broadly applicable across algorithms, domains, and input modalities, and to unlock new, higher-performing hyperparameter regimes (such as higher replay ratios and longer n-step targets) that are otherwise prone to overfitting. The resetting mechanism acts as a novel form of regularization specific to RL with function approximation, and is shown to address optimization challenges and temporal-difference learning failure modes that are not resolved by standard regularization techniques.

69c84ba390b037245f582541fa681b42cb3472d3.title: Trace norm regularization for multi-task learning with scarce data
69c84ba390b037245f582541fa681b42cb3472d3.research_question: How can multi-task learning be effectively performed when each task has a very limited number of observations, particularly in the context of learning a shared low-dimensional representation across tasks?
69c84ba390b037245f582541fa681b42cb3472d3.hypothesis: Trace norm regularization enables effective multi-task learning and provides strong estimation error guarantees even when the number of samples per task is much smaller than the feature dimension.
69c84ba390b037245f582541fa681b42cb3472d3.proposed_method: A trace norm (nuclear norm) regularized estimator will be developed for multi-task linear regression, where the parameter matrix is assumed to be low-rank and shared across tasks. The estimator minimizes the average squared loss across all tasks, subject to a trace norm penalty that encourages low-rank solutions. The analysis will leverage a restricted strong convexity condition, which is shown to hold even when the number of samples per task is less than the feature dimension, replacing the more restrictive restricted isometry property. Concentration inequalities for heavy-tailed distributions will be used to control the effective noise level in the random design setting. The method will also be extended to meta-learning, providing guarantees for transfer to new, previously unseen tasks.
69c84ba390b037245f582541fa681b42cb3472d3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic datasets where feature vectors are sampled from a standard Gaussian distribution and noise is added according to a sub-Gaussian model. The setup will include varying the number of tasks, the number of samples per task, and the noise level. Baselines for comparison will include independent single-task regressions, an oracle baseline with known subspace, Burer-Monteiro factorization, Method of Moments, and alternating minimization algorithms. Evaluation metrics will include the normalized Frobenius distance between the estimated and true parameter matrices, as well as the principal angle between estimated and true subspaces. Multiple runs will be performed to report averages and standard deviations.
69c84ba390b037245f582541fa681b42cb3472d3.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first general estimation error bound for trace norm regularized multi-task learning when the number of samples per task is arbitrarily small, without requiring restrictive conditions on the feature distribution or the number of samples. The analysis establishes a restricted strong convexity condition in this regime and provides new concentration results for heavy-tailed random designs. The approach also extends to meta-learning, offering new theoretical guarantees for transfer to unseen tasks. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior performance over existing methods in data-scarce regimes.

69d57c9da7a53a87e6f330d1ecaba80e3515503f.title: Accelerated Primal-Dual Methods for Convex-Strongly-Concave Saddle Point Problems
69d57c9da7a53a87e6f330d1ecaba80e3515503f.research_question: How can the gradient complexity of primal-dual methods for convex-strongly-concave saddle point problems be improved, particularly when the primal function is linearized and the coupling function is either semi-linear or general nonlinear?
69d57c9da7a53a87e6f330d1ecaba80e3515503f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by incorporating acceleration techniques from Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient Descent into linearized primal-dual methods, it is possible to achieve optimal or near-optimal gradient complexity for convex-strongly-concave saddle point problems, even when the primal function is linearized and the coupling function is nonlinear.
69d57c9da7a53a87e6f330d1ecaba80e3515503f.proposed_method: A novel single-loop Accelerated Linearized Primal-Dual (ALPD) method will be developed, which integrates acceleration steps from Nesterov's AGD into the linearized primal-dual framework. The method will use a linear approximation for the primal function and, optionally, for the dual function, allowing for efficient updates even when proximal operators are computationally expensive. For semi-linear coupling functions (linear in one variable), the ALPD method will be designed to achieve optimal dependence on the primal Lipschitz constant. For general nonlinear coupling functions, an inexact ALPD variant will be proposed, employing a two-loop structure where the inner loop solves a strongly convex subproblem approximately using AGD, and the outer loop follows the conceptual ALPD updates. Step-size policies and momentum parameters will be carefully chosen to ensure accelerated convergence and optimal complexity bounds.
69d57c9da7a53a87e6f330d1ecaba80e3515503f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on penalty problems with both linear and nonlinear constraints, reformulated as saddle point problems. Synthetic datasets will be generated, including convex quadratic objectives and random linear or quadratic constraints. The proposed ALPD and inexact ALPD methods will be compared against baseline methods such as the standard Linearized Primal-Dual (LPD) method and its accelerated variants, including versions using exact proximal operators for the dual function. Evaluation metrics will include the primal-dual gap function, primal and dual relative errors, and runtime performance. Multiple independent instances will be run to assess robustness, and experiments will be performed for various problem dimensions and parameter regimes (e.g., varying Lipschitz and strong convexity constants).
69d57c9da7a53a87e6f330d1ecaba80e3515503f.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces an accelerated linearized primal-dual method that achieves optimal gradient complexity for convex-strongly-concave saddle point problems with semi-linear coupling, even when the primal function is linearized. For general nonlinear coupling, the inexact ALPD method significantly improves the gradient complexity of the coupling term compared to existing approaches. The methodology allows for efficient handling of cases where proximal operators are impractical, and the step-size and momentum schemes are explicitly constructed to guarantee accelerated convergence. These innovations address previously unresolved challenges in the literature, particularly for the strongly concave dual case and nonlinear coupling functions.

6a0f59e40e902519b698b4d678e7d61d5c0701d5.title: Stable Target Field for Reduced Variance Score Estimation in Diffusion Models
6a0f59e40e902519b698b4d678e7d61d5c0701d5.research_question: How can the variance of training targets in diffusion models be reduced to improve image generation quality, training stability, and convergence speed across various diffusion model architectures and datasets?
6a0f59e40e902519b698b4d678e7d61d5c0701d5.hypothesis: Incorporating a reference batch to compute weighted conditional scores as training targets will reduce the variance of the denoising score-matching objective in diffusion models, leading to improved sample quality, stability, and faster convergence, especially in regimes where multiple data modes influence the score field.
6a0f59e40e902519b698b4d678e7d61d5c0701d5.proposed_method: A generalized denoising score-matching objective, termed the Stable Target Field (STF), will be developed. This approach will utilize a large reference batch of data samples to compute weighted conditional scores for each perturbed sample, using self-normalized importance sampling to aggregate the contributions of the reference batch. The STF objective replaces the traditional single-sample target with a weighted average over the reference batch, where weights are determined by the transition kernel probabilities. The method will be instantiated for commonly used Gaussian transition kernels, making it compatible with popular diffusion models such as EDM, VE, and VP SDEs. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to show that the bias introduced by the STF objective vanishes as the reference batch size increases, while the variance of the training targets is reduced proportionally to the batch size.
6a0f59e40e902519b698b4d678e7d61d5c0701d5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image generation benchmarks, including CIFAR-10 and CelebA 64x64 datasets. The proposed STF objective will be integrated into several diffusion model architectures (EDM, VE, VP SDEs) and evaluated using both ODE and SDE samplers (e.g., RK45, DDIM, Heun, Predictor-Corrector). Baselines will include the standard denoising score-matching (DSM) objective and state-of-the-art generative models. Evaluation metrics will comprise FID (Fréchet Inception Distance), Inception Score, and number of function evaluations (NFE) for sampling speed. Multiple random seeds will be used to assess stability, and experiments will systematically vary the reference batch size to study its effect on variance reduction, convergence speed, and final performance.
6a0f59e40e902519b698b4d678e7d61d5c0701d5.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the Stable Target Field (STF) objective, a novel variance reduction technique for diffusion model training based on self-normalized importance sampling with reference batches. This approach is claimed to be the first to accelerate diffusion model training while improving sample quality and stability. Theoretical contributions include a principled analysis of training target variance across different diffusion phases, proofs of asymptotic unbiasedness and variance reduction proportional to reference batch size, and empirical validation of these properties. The method achieves new state-of-the-art FID scores on unconditional CIFAR-10 generation and demonstrates consistent improvements across multiple diffusion model architectures and samplers.

6a11e5f8951dcd0046ad36d9c6ff4a5c9dab7526.title: ScaleDiff: Higher-Resolution Image Synthesis via Efficient and Model-Agnostic Diffusion
6a11e5f8951dcd0046ad36d9c6ff4a5c9dab7526.research_question: How can the resolution capabilities of pretrained diffusion models be efficiently extended to generate high-quality, high-resolution images without additional training, while remaining compatible with diverse model architectures?
6a11e5f8951dcd0046ad36d9c6ff4a5c9dab7526.hypothesis: A model-agnostic, training-free framework that integrates efficient attention mechanisms and advanced upscaling strategies will enable pretrained diffusion models to synthesize higher-resolution images with improved quality and computational efficiency, regardless of the underlying architecture.
6a11e5f8951dcd0046ad36d9c6ff4a5c9dab7526.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces ScaleDiff, a training-free and model-agnostic framework designed to extend the resolution of pretrained diffusion models. The core methodology centers on Neighborhood Patch Attention (NPA), an efficient self-attention mechanism that divides queries into non-overlapping patches and computes attention using overlapping key and value patches from spatial neighborhoods, thereby reducing computational redundancy. The framework is integrated into an SDEdit-based upsample–diffuse–denoise pipeline, which iteratively upsamples low-resolution latents and refines them. Latent Frequency Mixing (LFM) is employed to combine low-frequency components from latent-space upsampling with high-frequency components from RGB-space upsampling, enhancing fine detail synthesis. Structure Guidance (SG) is applied in latent space at each denoising step to enforce global structural consistency by aligning low-frequency components of intermediate predictions with those from a reference latent.
6a11e5f8951dcd0046ad36d9c6ff4a5c9dab7526.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both U-Net-based (SDXL) and Diffusion Transformer-based (FLUX) architectures using an iterative 1024² → 2048² → 4096² image generation pipeline. The evaluation uses 1,000 image-text pairs sampled from the LAION-5B dataset, with one image generated per prompt. Baselines include recent training-free methods (ScaleCrafter, HiDiffusion, DiffuseHigh, FreeScale, DemoFusion, AccDiffusionv2), super-resolution models (BSRGAN, OSEDiff), and a training-based model (UltraPixel). Evaluation metrics comprise Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Kernel Inception Distance (KID), Inception Score (IS), patch-level variants of these metrics, and CLIPScore for text-image alignment. All experiments are run on a single NVIDIA A6000 GPU, and ablation studies are performed to assess the contributions of NPA, LFM, and SG, as well as the impact of noise timestep selection.
6a11e5f8951dcd0046ad36d9c6ff4a5c9dab7526.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is model-agnostic and training-free, enabling high-resolution image synthesis for both U-Net and Diffusion Transformer architectures without additional training. Neighborhood Patch Attention (NPA) significantly reduces the computational overhead of patch-based methods by eliminating redundant computations in self-attention layers. Latent Frequency Mixing (LFM) and latent-space Structure Guidance (SG) jointly enhance fine detail synthesis and global structural consistency. The approach achieves state-of-the-art image quality and inference speed among training-free methods, demonstrating superior scalability and versatility for high-resolution image generation.

6a33e58ef961a3a0a5657518b2be86395eb7c8d0.title: Intern VL: Scaling up Vision Foundation Models and Aligning for Generic Visual-Linguistic Tasks
6a33e58ef961a3a0a5657518b2be86395eb7c8d0.research_question: How can vision foundation models be scaled up and effectively aligned with large language models to enable robust performance across a broad range of generic visual-linguistic tasks, including perception, retrieval, captioning, and multi-modal dialogue?
6a33e58ef961a3a0a5657518b2be86395eb7c8d0.hypothesis: Scaling the vision encoder to a parameter scale comparable to large language models and progressively aligning its representations with those of LLMs using web-scale image-text data and a substantial language middleware will result in a vision-language foundation model with state-of-the-art performance on diverse visual-linguistic benchmarks.
6a33e58ef961a3a0a5657518b2be86395eb7c8d0.proposed_method: A large-scale vision-language foundation model will be developed by scaling a vision transformer encoder (InternViT-6B) to 6 billion parameters and introducing a language middleware (QLLaMA) with 8 billion parameters, initialized from a multilingual LLaMA. The methodology involves a progressive alignment strategy: first, contrastive pre-training on billions of noisy web-scale image-text pairs to align vision and language representations; second, generative pre-training on filtered, high-quality caption and VQA datasets to further harmonize visual and linguistic features; and third, supervised fine-tuning for downstream tasks such as multi-modal dialogue and visual question answering. The QLLaMA middleware, equipped with learnable queries and cross-attention layers, serves as a powerful 'glue' to reorganize visual features and bridge the vision encoder with LLMs. The model architecture and hyperparameters will be optimized for a balance of accuracy, speed, and training stability.
6a33e58ef961a3a0a5657518b2be86395eb7c8d0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a wide array of benchmarks covering visual perception (e.g., ImageNet-1K, ADE20K), vision-language tasks (e.g., zero-shot image/video classification, image/video-text retrieval on COCO, Flickr30K, MSR-VTT), image captioning (COCO, Flickr30K, NoCaps), visual question answering (VQAv2, GQA, VizWiz), and multi-modal dialogue (MME, POPE, TinyLVLM). Datasets for pre-training include LAION-en, LAION-multi, COYO, Wukong, and other public web-scale image-text collections, totaling over 6 billion pairs, with progressive filtering for quality. Baselines for comparison include state-of-the-art vision encoders (e.g., ViT-22B, EVA-02-CLIP-E+) and vision-language models (e.g., CLIP, BLIP-2, LLaVA, Qwen-VL). Evaluation metrics include top-1 accuracy, mean IoU, recall@K, BLEU, CIDEr, and specialized dialogue benchmarks. Ablation studies will assess the impact of model scaling, middleware design, and alignment strategies.
6a33e58ef961a3a0a5657518b2be86395eb7c8d0.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first vision-language foundation model that scales the vision encoder to match LLM parameter sizes and aligns it progressively with a multilingual language middleware. The progressive alignment strategy leverages both contrastive and generative learning on web-scale and high-quality data, maximizing the use of heterogeneous sources. The QLLaMA middleware, with its substantial parameter count and cross-attention design, enables more consistent and effective feature alignment with LLMs compared to prior lightweight glue layers. The resulting model is versatile, supporting a wide range of visual-linguistic tasks and demonstrating state-of-the-art or superior performance across more than 30 benchmarks, including robust multilingual and multi-modal dialogue capabilities.

6a375be82efc01ec4ed73334655935a56ba82d38.title: BridgeData V2: A Dataset for Robot Learning at Scale
6a375be82efc01ec4ed73334655935a56ba82d38.research_question: How can large and diverse real-world datasets facilitate scalable robot learning, enabling generalization across tasks, environments, and institutions, and support a wide variety of offline imitation and reinforcement learning methods?
6a375be82efc01ec4ed73334655935a56ba82d38.hypothesis: A large-scale, diverse dataset of real-world robotic manipulation behaviors, collected across many environments and tasks using a low-cost, accessible robot, will enable scalable robot learning methods to generalize to novel tasks, objects, environments, and even new institutions, and will be compatible with a broad range of learning algorithms.
6a375be82efc01ec4ed73334655935a56ba82d38.proposed_method: A comprehensive dataset of robotic manipulation trajectories will be collected using a low-cost, publicly available robot arm equipped with multiple RGB and depth cameras. Data collection will include both teleoperated demonstrations and autonomously collected trajectories, covering a wide range of skills (e.g., pick-and-place, pushing, folding, stacking, opening/closing doors and drawers) across 24 diverse environments and over 100 objects. Demonstrations will be annotated post-hoc with natural language descriptions via crowdsourcing, enabling both goal-conditioned (via images) and language-conditioned learning. The dataset will be designed to maximize task and environment variability, with randomized camera poses, object arrangements, and workspace positions, and will include both expert and suboptimal (scripted) trajectories to support different learning paradigms.
6a375be82efc01ec4ed73334655935a56ba82d38.experiment_details: A suite of state-of-the-art offline robot learning algorithms will be trained and evaluated on the dataset, including goal-conditioned and language-conditioned imitation learning (e.g., behavioral cloning with goals, diffusion-based policies, action chunking with transformers, and language-conditioned behavioral cloning), as well as goal-conditioned reinforcement learning. Experiments will assess performance on both seen and unseen tasks, objects, and environments, as well as cross-institution generalization by evaluating policies in a different laboratory setup. Datasets will be stratified to analyze the effects of dataset size, skill diversity, and model capacity on policy performance. Evaluation metrics will primarily be task success rates, averaged over multiple trials per task, with qualitative analysis of policy behaviors.
6a375be82efc01ec4ed73334655935a56ba82d38.novelty_claims: The proposed dataset will be the largest and most diverse publicly available real-world robotic manipulation dataset to date, supporting open-vocabulary task specification via both goal images and natural language. Unlike prior datasets, it will be specifically designed for broad generalization across environments and institutions, and will be compatible with a wide range of learning methods, including both imitation and reinforcement learning. The dataset will also provide a unique resource for analyzing the effects of data and model scaling on generalization and robustness in robot learning, and will be accessible to the broader research community due to the use of low-cost hardware.

6a3c38c1561a0bd730d2a58ef30a4afa411e7049.title: Optimal Algorithms for Testing Closeness of Discrete Distributions
6a3c38c1561a0bd730d2a58ef30a4afa411e7049.research_question: How can the problem of testing whether two unknown discrete distributions are identical or significantly different be solved with optimal sample and computational efficiency, particularly under the ℓ1 and ℓ2 distance metrics?
6a3c38c1561a0bd730d2a58ef30a4afa411e7049.hypothesis: It is possible to design algorithms for closeness testing of discrete distributions that achieve information-theoretically optimal sample complexity, up to constant factors, for both ℓ1 and ℓ2 distances, with computational efficiency proportional to the sample size.
6a3c38c1561a0bd730d2a58ef30a4afa411e7049.proposed_method: A novel algorithm will be developed for closeness testing between two discrete distributions over an n-element set, using independent samples from each distribution. For the ℓ1 distance, the method computes a test statistic Z based on the observed counts of each element in the samples, specifically Z = sum over i of [(Xi - Yi)^2 - Xi - Yi] / (Xi + Yi), where Xi and Yi are the counts for element i from distributions p and q, respectively. The algorithm outputs 'EQUAL' or 'DIFFERENT' based on whether Z is below or above a threshold proportional to the square root of the sample size. For the ℓ2 distance, the method estimates the distance by computing Z = sum over i of (Xi - Yi)^2 - Xi - Yi, and returns the square root of Z divided by the sample size as an estimator for the ℓ2 distance. Both algorithms leverage Poissonization to simplify the analysis and ensure independence of sample counts.
6a3c38c1561a0bd730d2a58ef30a4afa411e7049.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic datasets generated from discrete distributions with varying support sizes n and distance parameters ε. The proposed algorithms will be evaluated against established baselines, including prior sublinear-sample closeness testers and uniformity testers. Evaluation metrics will include sample complexity (number of samples required to achieve a specified error probability, e.g., 2/3 or 3/4), computational running time, and accuracy in distinguishing the null (p = q) versus alternative (distance at least ε) hypotheses. Lower bounds will be established through information-theoretic arguments and by constructing hard instances, ensuring the optimality of the proposed algorithms.
6a3c38c1561a0bd730d2a58ef30a4afa411e7049.novelty_claims: The proposed approach achieves information-theoretically optimal sample complexity for closeness testing under both ℓ1 and ℓ2 distances, up to constant factors, resolving previously open questions regarding the dependence on ε. The ℓ1 tester introduces a new, simpler structure compared to prior reduction-based approaches and attains optimal dependence on both n and ε. The ℓ2 tester provides robust testing guarantees and adapts to the ℓ2 norms of the input distributions. The algorithms operate in time linear in the sample size, making them practical for large-scale data. Additionally, the techniques developed may be applicable to related distribution testing problems, such as independence testing.

6a3e31e80f64fb0849c4b0d273341f4eb5254193.title: CADGrasp: Learning Contact and Collision Aware General Dexterous Grasping in Cluttered Scenes
6a3e31e80f64fb0849c4b0d273341f4eb5254193.research_question: How can dexterous grasping in cluttered scenes be improved to achieve stable, collision-free grasps using only single-view point cloud observations, without requiring complete object geometry?
6a3e31e80f64fb0849c4b0d273341f4eb5254193.hypothesis: A two-stage framework that leverages a contact- and collision-aware intermediate representation, specifically a sparse Interaction Bisector Surface (IBS), can enable more robust, generalizable, and efficient dexterous grasping in cluttered scenes, even under partial observations.
6a3e31e80f64fb0849c4b0d273341f4eb5254193.proposed_method: A novel two-stage approach is developed for dexterous grasping in cluttered environments. In the first stage, a compact, scene-decoupled, contact- and collision-aware sparse IBS representation is predicted as an intermediate constraint. This is accomplished by first estimating the wrist pose using a ResUNet14-based feature extractor and a diffusion model, followed by generating multiple IBS candidates via a conditional occupancy-diffusion model that operates on voxelized, canonicalized point clouds. Voxel-level conditional guidance and force closure score filtering are used to enhance the quality and physical plausibility of the generated IBS candidates, with the top-ranked candidate selected for further use. In the second stage, grasp poses are optimized using a gradient-based algorithm that minimizes a composite energy function incorporating joint limits, self-penetration, contact, and collision terms, all defined with respect to the predicted IBS. Multiple grasp configurations are optimized in parallel, and the configuration with the lowest residual is selected as the final grasp pose.
6a3e31e80f64fb0849c4b0d273341f4eb5254193.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in both simulated and real-world settings. The simulation utilizes 670 diverse cluttered scenes with over 1300 objects, drawing training and testing objects from GraspNet1Billion and ShapeNet datasets. The evaluation protocol follows that of DexGraspNet2.0, reporting Success Rate as the primary metric and assessing generalization across object types, scene densities (loose, random, dense), and hand embodiments (LeapHand and Allegro Hand).
