Baselines for comparison include regression-based (HGC-Net, ISAGrasp), generative-based (GraspTTA), and diffusion-based (DexGraspNet2.0) methods, with adaptations as needed for cluttered scenes. Real-world experiments employ a Flexiv Rizon-4 robot with a LeapHand end-effector and a RealSense D415 camera, testing on 30 objects across 5 cluttered scenes. Ablation studies will examine the impact of key modules, voxel resolution, and object size on performance.
6a3e31e80f64fb0849c4b0d273341f4eb5254193.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a sparse IBS as a scene-decoupled, contact- and collision-aware intermediate representation for dexterous grasping, enabling optimization without full object geometry. The occupancy-diffusion model with voxel-level conditional guidance and force closure filtering is novel for efficient and accurate IBS generation. The method supports cross-embodiment generalization, allowing zero-shot transfer between different robotic hands. The approach demonstrates superior efficiency and robustness compared to existing two-stage and end-to-end methods, particularly under partial observation and in highly cluttered scenes.

6a6aed60f421169c9ae192beaaf3c423827dcd52.title: G3: An Effective and Adaptive Framework for Worldwide Geolocalization Using Large Multi-Modality Models
6a6aed60f421169c9ae192beaaf3c423827dcd52.research_question: How can worldwide image geolocalization be improved to accurately predict the precise location of any photo taken on Earth, overcoming challenges of subtle location-aware visual semantics and heterogeneous geographical image distribution?
6a6aed60f421169c9ae192beaaf3c423827dcd52.hypothesis: Jointly aligning image, GPS, and textual representations in a multi-modality framework, combined with adaptive retrieval-augmented generation and robust candidate verification, will significantly enhance the accuracy and robustness of worldwide image geolocalization compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.
6a6aed60f421169c9ae192beaaf3c423827dcd52.proposed_method: A new framework, G3, will be developed for worldwide image geolocalization, structured around three key modules: Geo-alignment, Geo-diversification, and Geo-verification. Geo-alignment will employ multi-modality encoders to jointly learn expressive representations for images, GPS coordinates (using Mercator projection and random Fourier features), and textual geographical descriptions, optimizing with a contrastive loss to align these modalities. During inference, Geo-diversification will generate a diverse set of candidate GPS predictions by ensembling multiple retrieval-augmented prompts, each with varying numbers of reference coordinates, including zero-shot prompts. Geo-verification will then select the final prediction by evaluating the similarity between the query image and all candidate GPS representations in the learned multi-modal space, returning the most similar candidate as the final output.
6a6aed60f421169c9ae192beaaf3c423827dcd52.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two established benchmarks: IM2GPS3K and YFCC4K. The proposed method will be trained on the newly constructed MP16-Pro dataset, which augments the MP16 dataset with textual geographical descriptions for each image. Baseline comparisons will include classification-based, retrieval-based, and generation-based state-of-the-art methods such as PlaNet, CPlaNet, GeoCLIP, Img2Loc, and PIGEON. Evaluation will use threshold-based accuracy metrics, measuring the percentage of predictions within specified distance thresholds (1km, 25km, 200km, 750km, 2500km) from ground truth. Ablation studies will assess the contribution of each module, and hyperparameter analyses will examine the impact of prompt and candidate pool sizes. Implementation will leverage pretrained vision and text encoders (e.g., CLIP ViT-L/14), and large multi-modality models (e.g., GPT4V, LLaVA) for generation.
6a6aed60f421169c9ae192beaaf3c423827dcd52.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a novel multi-modality alignment (Geo-alignment) that jointly encodes images, GPS coordinates, and textual descriptions for enhanced location-aware representation learning. The method pioneers a prompt ensembling strategy (Geo-diversification) to adaptively generate robust candidate predictions across heterogeneous queries. Geo-verification further innovates by selecting the most confident prediction from a combined pool of retrieved and generated candidates using learned multi-modal similarity. Additionally, a new large-scale dataset (MP16-Pro) with textual geographical annotations will be released to advance research in location-aware visual representation learning.

6a6c0736a4e9e850db15a30ea8ff180c2080ba4f.title: DCFace: Synthetic Face Generation with Dual Condition Diffusion Model
6a6c0736a4e9e850db15a30ea8ff180c2080ba4f.research_question: How can a synthetic face dataset be generated that simultaneously achieves high subject uniqueness, style diversity, and label consistency, in order to improve the training of face recognition models?
6a6c0736a4e9e850db15a30ea8ff180c2080ba4f.hypothesis: Face dataset generation can be formulated as a dual-condition problem, where controlling both subject identity and external style factors enables the creation of synthetic datasets with high inter-class and intra-class variation as well as label consistency, leading to improved face recognition performance.
6a6c0736a4e9e850db15a30ea8ff180c2080ba4f.proposed_method: A two-stage synthetic face dataset generation framework will be developed. In Stage 1, a high-quality ID image of a novel subject is generated using an unconditional diffusion model (DDPM), and a style image is sampled from a real face dataset to serve as the style condition. In Stage 2, a Dual Condition Generator based on a conditional diffusion model is trained to mix the identity and style conditions, producing images that preserve the subject's identity while varying style attributes such as pose, illumination, and expression. A novel patch-wise style extractor is introduced to encode style information without leaking identity, and a time-step-dependent ID loss is designed to interpolate between identity and style features during the denoising process, ensuring both label consistency and style diversity. Cross-attention and adaptive group normalization layers are used to inject the dual conditions into the diffusion model, and the training leverages labeled datasets to ensure the availability of identity and style pairs.
6a6c0736a4e9e850db15a30ea8ff180c2080ba4f.experiment_details: Experiments will involve generating synthetic face datasets with varying numbers of subjects and images per subject, using the proposed framework. The ID image generator will be trained on FFHQ, and the style bank will be constructed from CASIA-WebFace. The Dual Condition Generator will be trained on CASIA-WebFace with a 95-5 train-validation split. Face recognition models will be trained on the generated synthetic datasets and evaluated on five standard benchmarks: LFW, CFP-FP, CPLFW, AgeDB, and CALFW. Baselines will include state-of-the-art synthetic dataset generators such as SynFace (GAN-based) and DigiFace (3D model-based). Evaluation metrics will include face verification accuracy, as well as proposed metrics for subject uniqueness, intra-class consistency, and intra-class diversity, computed using pretrained face recognition and Inception models. Ablation studies will be conducted on patch size, ID loss formulation, and sampling strategies.
6a6c0736a4e9e850db15a30ea8ff180c2080ba4f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a dual-condition diffusion-based framework for synthetic face generation, enabling direct and independent control over subject identity and external style factors. The method features a novel patch-wise style extractor that encodes spatially local style information while minimizing identity leakage, and a time-step-dependent ID loss that dynamically balances identity and style consistency during generation. New metrics for quantifying subject uniqueness, label consistency, and style diversity in labeled datasets are proposed. The approach achieves state-of-the-art face recognition performance on multiple benchmarks using only synthetic data, surpassing previous methods by a significant margin and narrowing the gap to real-data-trained models.

6a7c29829227bfd65ae0ffec294a874bb9ea0871.title: TÜLU 3: Pushing Frontiers in Open Language Model Post-Training
6a7c29829227bfd65ae0ffec294a874bb9ea0871.research_question: How can open-source post-training techniques for large language models be advanced to match or surpass the performance of proprietary models across a broad range of core skills, while providing full transparency in data, methodology, and evaluation?
6a7c29829227bfd65ae0ffec294a874bb9ea0871.hypothesis: A multi-stage, fully open post-training pipeline—incorporating rigorous data curation, supervised finetuning, advanced preference optimization, and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards—can produce language models that outperform existing open and closed models on diverse benchmarks, provided that training data, recipes, and evaluation frameworks are transparent and reproducible.
6a7c29829227bfd65ae0ffec294a874bb9ea0871.proposed_method: A comprehensive post-training pipeline will be developed for large language models, starting from open base models (e.g., Llama 3.1). The first stage involves curating and decontaminating a diverse set of prompts targeting core skills such as reasoning, math, coding, instruction following, and safety, using both public and synthetic data. Supervised finetuning (SFT) will be performed on these curated datasets, with iterative experimentation to optimize data mixtures and hyperparameters for balanced skill improvement. Next, preference tuning will be conducted using Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) on a large, on-policy preference dataset generated by comparing model completions, with a focus on length normalization and efficiency. Finally, a novel reinforcement learning stage, Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR), will be implemented, where the model is trained to maximize rewards only when outputs are verifiably correct (e.g., for math or instruction-following tasks), using an asynchronous, scalable RL infrastructure. Throughout all stages, a standardized, open evaluation suite will guide development and prevent contamination.
6a7c29829227bfd65ae0ffec294a874bb9ea0871.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple model sizes (8B, 70B, 405B parameters) using Llama 3.1 as the base. The training datasets will include a mix of general and skill-specific instruction datasets, preference datasets generated via on-policy and off-policy comparisons, and RLVR datasets targeting tasks with verifiable outcomes (e.g., GSM8K, MATH, IFEval). Baselines will include state-of-the-art open models (Llama 3.1 Instruct, Mistral-Instruct, Qwen 2.5) and leading closed models (GPT-4o-mini, Claude 3.5 Haiku). Evaluation will be performed using the Tülu 3 Eval suite, which covers development and unseen splits for knowledge, reasoning, math, coding, instruction following, chat, and safety, with metrics such as accuracy, F1, pass@10, and win rate. Data decontamination will be rigorously applied to prevent overlap between training and evaluation sets, and all code, data, and evaluation tools will be released for reproducibility.
6a7c29829227bfd65ae0ffec294a874bb9ea0871.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a fully open, state-of-the-art post-training framework for language models, including transparent data curation, scalable preference data generation, and a novel RL-based training method (RLVR) that uses verifiable rewards instead of reward models. The pipeline provides extensive guidance and tooling for evaluation, decontamination, and recipe design, and releases all intermediate and final models, datasets, training code, and evaluation infrastructure. This work establishes a new standard for openness and reproducibility in language model post-training, enabling the community to match or surpass proprietary models and systematically explore multi-stage, multi-objective training regimes.

6a7f5b7a89e8c727c898b5b3da56ee030cb42163.title: BiLD: Bi-directional Logits Difference Loss for Large Language Model Distillation
6a7f5b7a89e8c727c898b5b3da56ee030cb42163.research_question: How can knowledge distillation for large language models be improved to address the challenges posed by the long-tail distribution and internal ranking of logits, thereby enhancing the performance and efficiency of student models across diverse NLP tasks?
6a7f5b7a89e8c727c898b5b3da56ee030cb42163.hypothesis: A distillation loss that filters out long-tail noise and explicitly leverages the internal ranking information of logits will enable student models to better capture key knowledge from teacher models, resulting in improved performance compared to existing distillation methods.
6a7f5b7a89e8c727c898b5b3da56ee030cb42163.proposed_method: A novel loss function, Bi-directional Logits Difference (BiLD) loss, will be developed for task-specific distillation of large language models. The method filters out noise in the long-tail distribution by selecting only the top-k logits from both teacher and student models. It constructs two sets of pairwise differences: one using the top-k teacher logits and their corresponding student logits (teacher-led), and another using the top-k student logits and their corresponding teacher logits (student-led). For each set, pairwise differences are normalized into probability distributions, and KL divergence is computed between the teacher-led and student-led distributions. The final BiLD loss is the sum of these two KL divergences, encouraging the student to align both the magnitude and ranking of its logits with the teacher while ignoring less informative long-tail logits.
6a7f5b7a89e8c727c898b5b3da56ee030cb42163.experiment_details: Comprehensive experiments will be conducted on 13 diverse NLP datasets, including 8 from the SuperGLUE benchmark and 5 additional datasets commonly used in model compression research. Two open-source LLMs, BLOOM and Qwen1.5, will serve as teacher models, with smaller variants as students. Baselines will include supervised fine-tuning (SFT), vanilla KL loss, top-k KL loss, and five other distillation methods from both NLP and computer vision domains. Evaluation metrics will include average accuracy, F1, EM, and a novel top-k overlap metric to assess logit-level imitation. Experiments will use consistent training setups, including batch sizes, learning rates, and temperature settings, and will be run on multi-GPU environments with memory optimizations.
6a7f5b7a89e8c727c898b5b3da56ee030cb42163.novelty_claims: The proposed BiLD loss introduces a bi-directional, pairwise logit difference approach that explicitly leverages internal ranking information and filters out long-tail noise, which is not addressed by existing logits distillation methods. This method achieves superior or state-of-the-art performance using only the top-8 logits, outperforming both vanilla KL loss and other advanced distillation techniques across multiple datasets and model architectures. The approach is computationally efficient for small k and can serve as a drop-in replacement for KL-based distillation losses in LLMs, providing a practical and effective solution for model compression and deployment.

6a820fec605e48fa4012d1c69b77f537585cab9a.title: AsymRnR: Video Diffusion Transformers Acceleration with Asymmetric Reduction and Restoration
6a820fec605e48fa4012d1c69b77f537585cab9a.research_question: How can the computational efficiency of state-of-the-art video diffusion transformers be improved without requiring additional training or sacrificing output quality, and can such methods generalize across diverse architectures and acceleration pipelines?
6a820fec605e48fa4012d1c69b77f537585cab9a.hypothesis: Asymmetrically reducing redundant tokens in the attention mechanism of video diffusion transformers, with adaptive scheduling and efficient caching, will enable significant acceleration of video generation with negligible or no loss in perceptual quality.
6a820fec605e48fa4012d1c69b77f537585cab9a.proposed_method: A novel, training-free, and model-agnostic approach is developed to accelerate video diffusion transformers (DiTs) by asymmetrically reducing redundant tokens in the attention mechanism. The method, termed Asymmetric Reduction and Restoration (AsymRnR), independently reduces the sequence length of query (Q) and key/value (K/V) tokens prior to self-attention and restores them afterward for subsequent operations. An adaptive reduction schedule is introduced, leveraging precomputed similarity statistics across model blocks, denoising steps, and feature types, to selectively apply reduction where redundancy is highest. To minimize overhead, a matching cache is implemented that reuses token matching results across denoising steps, further reducing computational cost. The approach is compatible with advanced attention operations (e.g., 3D rotary position embedding) and can be integrated with feature caching and step-distillation pipelines.
6a820fec605e48fa4012d1c69b77f537585cab9a.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on state-of-the-art open-source video DiTs, including CogVideoX-2B, CogVideoX-5B, Mochi-1, HunyuanVideo, and FastVideo-Hunyuan, as well as the UNet-based AnimateDiff model. The evaluation focuses on the text-to-video generation task, using over 900 prompts from the VBench benchmark suite to assess perceptual quality and semantic alignment. Baseline comparisons include ToMe (token merging) and feature caching methods such as PAB. Evaluation metrics include VBench score (for overall quality), LPIPS (for semantic alignment), FLOPs, and wall-clock latency, with speedup ratios reported. Experiments also test integration with step-distilled models and feature caching, and ablation studies analyze the impact of reduction scheduling, caching steps, similarity metrics, and reduction operations.
6a820fec605e48fa4012d1c69b77f537585cab9a.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first training-free, model-agnostic acceleration strategy for video diffusion transformers that asymmetrically reduces attention sequence lengths for Q and K/V features, adaptively schedules reductions based on intrinsic model redundancy, and incorporates a matching cache to minimize overhead. Unlike prior uniform or architecture-specific reduction methods, this approach achieves substantial acceleration with negligible or even improved output quality, is compatible with advanced attention mechanisms and feature caching, and generalizes across diverse DiT architectures and acceleration pipelines.

6a8698fbb4f7d21584402958c23d879265c51e01.title: pFedSim: Similarity-Aware Model Aggregation Towards Personalized Federated Learning
6a8698fbb4f7d21584402958c23d879265c51e01.research_question: How can personalized federated learning be improved to better handle non-IID data distributions across clients while minimizing communication overhead, privacy leakage, and reliance on external information?
6a8698fbb4f7d21584402958c23d879265c51e01.hypothesis: Personalizing federated learning models by aggregating feature extractors based on classifier similarity, while retaining classifiers for local training, will result in higher model accuracy, lower communication and computation overhead, and reduced privacy risks compared to existing personalized federated learning methods.
6a8698fbb4f7d21584402958c23d879265c51e01.proposed_method: A new personalized federated learning algorithm, pFedSim, is proposed that combines similarity-based model aggregation with model decoupling. The approach decouples each neural network model into a feature extractor and a classifier. During training, the feature extractor is aggregated across clients with similar data distributions, where similarity is measured by the cosine similarity of their classifiers. The classifier is updated solely through local training and is used to estimate client similarity, ensuring that only model parameters are exchanged and no additional information is exposed. The training process is divided into two phases: a generalization phase using standard federated averaging to initialize models, followed by a personalization phase where feature extractors are aggregated based on classifier similarity, and classifiers are refined locally. The similarity matrix is computed using a modified cosine similarity with a negative logarithm adjustment to enhance discrimination between clients.
6a8698fbb4f7d21584402958c23d879265c51e01.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four real-world image datasets: CIFAR-10, CINIC-10, Tiny-ImageNet, and EMNIST. Each dataset will be partitioned into 100 subsets using a Dirichlet distribution with varying non-IID degrees (α = 0.1, 0.5) to simulate heterogeneous client data. The proposed method will be compared against both traditional federated learning baselines (FedAvg, FedProx, FedDyn, FedGen) and state-of-the-art personalized FL baselines (FedPer, FedRep, FedBN, Per-FedAvg, FedFomo, FedAP). Evaluation metrics will include average model accuracy, communication and computation overhead, and privacy risk. LeNet5 will be used for most datasets, while MobileNetV2 will be used for Tiny-ImageNet. Hyperparameters such as local learning rate, join ratio, number of communication rounds, and local epochs will be standardized across methods for fair comparison.
6a8698fbb4f7d21584402958c23d879265c51e01.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel combination of similarity-based aggregation and model decoupling for personalized federated learning. It leverages classifier similarity, computed from model parameters only, to guide personalized aggregation of feature extractors, thus avoiding the need for additional information exchange or public datasets. The approach claims to achieve significantly higher model accuracy under non-IID settings, lower communication and computation overhead, and reduced privacy leakage risk compared to existing baselines. The method is also robust to hyperparameter tuning and does not require any external or public data.

6a884cbf0d7853bfd39048793921781f4c6e1ca3.title: StelLA: Subspace Learning in Low-rank Adaptation using Stiefel Manifold
6a884cbf0d7853bfd39048793921781f4c6e1ca3.research_question: Can parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large-scale pre-trained models be improved by explicitly optimizing the geometric structure of low-rank adaptation subspaces throughout training, rather than relying on heuristic or initialization-based approaches?
6a884cbf0d7853bfd39048793921781f4c6e1ca3.hypothesis: Explicitly optimizing the input and output subspaces of low-rank adaptation using orthonormality constraints on the Stiefel manifold will enable more effective and principled subspace learning, resulting in improved downstream task performance compared to existing LoRA variants and initialization-based methods.
6a884cbf0d7853bfd39048793921781f4c6e1ca3.proposed_method: A novel geometry-aware extension of Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is proposed, where the low-rank adaptation for each weight matrix is parameterized as a three-factor decomposition: USV⊤. Here, U and V are constrained to be orthonormal matrices lying on the Stiefel manifold, representing the output and input subspaces, respectively, while S is an unconstrained transformation matrix. The optimization of U and V is performed using Riemannian gradients and geometric optimization techniques, converting any standard Euclidean optimizer (e.g., Adam, SGD) into a Riemannian optimizer via projection and retraction operations. The approach is modular, allowing integration with existing fine-tuning pipelines, and includes efficient implementation strategies such as batched SVD for computational efficiency. Gradient scaling is introduced to balance the learning rates of U and V, particularly in cases where matrix dimensions differ significantly.
6a884cbf0d7853bfd39048793921781f4c6e1ca3.experiment_details: Extensive experiments will be conducted across diverse domains, including natural language understanding (commonsense reasoning), natural language generation (math and code generation), image classification, and text-to-image generation. Models such as LLaMA2, LLaMA3, ViT (Vision Transformer), and Stable Diffusion will be fine-tuned using the proposed method. Baselines for comparison will include standard LoRA, DoRA, PiSSA, OLoRA, TriLoRA, MoSLoRA, and geometry-aware optimizers such as ScaledAdamW. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy for classification and reasoning tasks, and FID/CLIP scores for generative tasks. Experimental setups will ensure fair comparison by standardizing hyperparameters such as rank, scaling factor, batch size, dropout, and optimizer across methods, with learning rates tuned per method. Ablation studies will analyze the effects of geometric constraints, initialization strategies, gradient scaling, and retraction choices.
6a884cbf0d7853bfd39048793921781f4c6e1ca3.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a principled, geometry-aware three-factor decomposition for low-rank adaptation, with explicit Stiefel manifold constraints on the subspace projections. It provides a flexible geometric optimization framework that decouples geometric constraints from optimizer choice, enabling seamless integration with any Euclidean optimizer. The approach enables direct and continual subspace learning during training, rather than relying solely on initialization heuristics. Efficient implementation strategies, such as batched SVD for retraction, are developed to scale the method to large models. The method claims consistent and state-of-the-art improvements over existing LoRA variants across multiple tasks and model architectures.

6a91263e4bd079499c58e2488bda5a561e69beeb.title: Learning a Diffusion Model Policy from Rewards via Q-Score Matching
6a91263e4bd079499c58e2488bda5a561e69beeb.research_question: How can expressive diffusion model policies be effectively learned in continuous action and state spaces for reinforcement learning, leveraging reward signals rather than relying solely on behavior cloning, and can such policies achieve efficient exploration and sample efficiency in off-policy RL settings?
6a91263e4bd079499c58e2488bda5a561e69beeb.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that aligning the score of a diffusion model policy with the action gradient of the Q-function via a novel Q-score matching algorithm will enable effective and sample-efficient learning of expressive, multi-modal policies in continuous control reinforcement learning tasks.
6a91263e4bd079499c58e2488bda5a561e69beeb.proposed_method: A new policy optimization framework is developed that links the score function of a diffusion model policy to the action gradient of a learned Q-function. The approach, termed Q-score matching (QSM), iteratively updates the policy by matching its score (i.e., the gradient of the log-policy with respect to actions) to the gradient of the Q-function with respect to actions. This alignment is performed by differentiating only through the denoising submodel of the diffusion model, rather than the entire diffusion process, improving computational efficiency and stability. The method is theoretically grounded in both deterministic and stochastic continuous-time RL formulations, and the policy update is shown to increase expected returns by aligning the policy's score field with the Q-function's action gradient field. The approach is implemented in an off-policy RL setting, using N-step returns and a replay buffer, and the policy is parameterized as a diffusion model with a neural network denoising function.
6a91263e4bd079499c58e2488bda5a561e69beeb.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a suite of continuous control tasks from the DeepMind Control Suite, including Cartpole Balance, Cartpole Swingup, Cheetah Run, Quadruped Walk, Hopper Hop, Walker Walk, Walker Run, and Humanoid Walk. The proposed QSM method is compared against popular baselines such as Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) and Twin Delayed DDPG (TD3), as well as Diffusion-QL, using consistent hyperparameters. Evaluation metrics include average episodic return and sample efficiency (number of environment steps to reach high reward). Policies are trained with 2-layer MLPs for both critic and score models, using batch sizes of 256, and actions are sampled via iterative denoising from the diffusion model. Additional analyses visualize the learned policy distributions, demonstrating the capacity for multi-modal and explorative behaviors.
6a91263e4bd079499c58e2488bda5a561e69beeb.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a theoretically justified and practical algorithm (Q-score matching) for learning diffusion model policies directly from reward signals in off-policy RL, without requiring behavior cloning or full backpropagation through the diffusion process. The approach exploits the unique score-based structure of diffusion models, enabling the learning of expressive, multi-modal policies that are not constrained to simple distribution classes. Empirical results demonstrate that QSM achieves sample efficiency and performance competitive with or superior to standard Gaussian policy parameterizations, while also enabling richer exploration. The method provides a new geometric perspective on policy optimization in RL and establishes a foundation for further research on score-based policy learning and maximum entropy RL connections.

6a92fab6bf8d83a47012ae155a3ab31f38056ab8.title: Closing the Gap Between the Upper Bound and the Lower Bound of Adam's Iteration Complexity
6a92fab6bf8d83a47012ae155a3ab31f38056ab8.research_question: What is the fundamental iteration complexity of the Adam optimizer under standard L-smoothness and bounded noise variance assumptions, and can the gap between known upper and lower bounds for Adam's convergence be closed without requiring stronger or additional assumptions?
6a92fab6bf8d83a47012ae155a3ab31f38056ab8.hypothesis: The gap between the upper and lower bounds of Adam's iteration complexity is not inherent to the algorithm's design, but rather due to limitations in existing proof techniques; with refined analysis, Adam's upper bound can match the lower bound for first-order optimizers under standard assumptions.
6a92fab6bf8d83a47012ae155a3ab31f38056ab8.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical analysis will be conducted to derive new convergence guarantees for Adam under only the L-smoothness condition and bounded noise variance assumption, without requiring additional constraints such as bounded gradients or mean-squared smoothness. The approach will involve constructing novel Lyapunov and auxiliary functions to disentangle the stochasticity between momentum and adaptive learning rates. Key proof techniques will include a coordinate-wise affine variance assumption, careful handling of the entanglement between momentum and adaptivity, and a divide-and-conquer strategy for bounding gradient norms. The analysis will be refined for specific hyperparameter regimes, particularly with small learning rates and momentum parameters close to one, to achieve a tight upper bound that matches the known lower bound up to constant factors.
6a92fab6bf8d83a47012ae155a3ab31f38056ab8.experiment_details: Theoretical results will be validated through rigorous mathematical proofs, focusing on the iteration complexity of Adam for finding an -stationary point. The analysis will cover a wide range of hyperparameter settings, including those commonly used in deep learning practice (e.g., η = 10^-3, β2 = 0.999, β1 = 0.9). Comparisons will be made against existing upper bounds for Adam, as well as the lower bound established for first-order stochastic optimization under L-smoothness and bounded variance. The evaluation will also include a discussion of the dependence on problem dimension and the effect of momentum, and will contrast the results with those for AdaGrad and SGD under similar assumptions.
6a92fab6bf8d83a47012ae155a3ab31f38056ab8.novelty_claims: The proposed analysis establishes, for the first time, an upper bound on Adam's iteration complexity that matches the lower bound for first-order optimizers under only L-smoothness and bounded noise variance assumptions, without requiring bounded gradients or mean-squared smoothness. The proof introduces new techniques to handle the interaction between momentum and adaptive learning rates, and provides a tighter bound than all existing results, improving previous upper bounds by at least a logarithmic factor. The results are valid for a broad spectrum of hyperparameters and align with practical settings used in deep learning. The analysis also generalizes to more flexible noise models and offers insights that may be of independent interest for the theoretical understanding of adaptive optimization algorithms.

6aa322c49aebe378140bf2170051dcbfcb522947.title: Adapting to Stochastic and Adversarial Losses in Episodic MDPs with Aggregate Bandit Feedback
6aa322c49aebe378140bf2170051dcbfcb522947.research_question: How can online learning algorithms in finite-horizon episodic Markov decision processes (MDPs) with aggregate bandit feedback be designed to achieve low regret in both stochastic and adversarial environments, especially when the transition dynamics are unknown?
6aa322c49aebe378140bf2170051dcbfcb522947.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a single algorithmic framework, leveraging occupancy measure-based optimization and novel loss estimators, can achieve instance-dependent low regret in stochastic settings and minimax optimal regret in adversarial settings for episodic MDPs with aggregate bandit feedback, even when transition probabilities are unknown.
6aa322c49aebe378140bf2170051dcbfcb522947.proposed_method: A new algorithmic framework will be developed for online learning in finite-horizon episodic tabular MDPs under aggregate bandit feedback, where only the cumulative loss per episode is observed. The approach will employ Follow-the-Regularized-Leader (FTRL) optimization over occupancy measures, utilizing specially constructed loss estimators that are optimistic in expectation and have tightly controlled second moments. For known-transition settings, the method will use loss estimators inspired by recent advances in online shortest path problems, while for unknown transitions, confidence-based techniques will be incorporated to estimate occupancy measures and construct valid loss estimators. The regularization will be based on Tsallis entropy or log-barrier functions to ensure computational efficiency and tight regret bounds. The framework will be extended to handle both stochastic and adversarial loss models without prior knowledge of the environment type.
6aa322c49aebe378140bf2170051dcbfcb522947.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and benchmark datasets representing finite-horizon layered MDPs and online shortest path problems. The proposed algorithms will be evaluated against established baselines, including algorithms designed for individual loss feedback and prior worst-case aggregate feedback methods. Evaluation metrics will include expected regret in both stochastic and adversarial regimes, as well as computational efficiency. The experimental setup will cover both known and unknown transition scenarios, and will analyze instance-dependent and minimax regret bounds, with additional robustness checks under corrupted stochastic environments.
6aa322c49aebe378140bf2170051dcbfcb522947.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first best-of-both-worlds (BOBW) algorithms for episodic tabular MDPs with aggregate bandit feedback, achieving near-optimal regret in both stochastic (O(polylog T)) and adversarial (O(sqrt(T))) settings. It establishes new, tight lower bounds for the stochastic regime and provides the first efficient BOBW algorithm for unknown-transition MDPs under aggregate feedback. The approach leverages a novel loss estimator that is optimistic and has a controlled second moment, allowing for a simpler and more effective regret analysis than prior work, and avoids technically involved loss-shifting techniques. Additionally, the method demonstrates robustness to adversarial corruption and extends to the online shortest path problem, offering a unified and computationally efficient solution.

6ac627f57b26354ab537734d820da4a6a7dde2c6.title: CLadder: Assessing Causal Reasoning in Language Models
6ac627f57b26354ab537734d820da4a6a7dde2c6.research_question: Can large language models (LLMs) perform formal causal reasoning in natural language, as assessed by their ability to answer a broad range of causal inference questions grounded in explicit causal graphs and data, rather than relying on commonsense or memorized causal patterns?
6ac627f57b26354ab537734d820da4a6a7dde2c6.hypothesis: LLMs can be guided to perform formal causal reasoning in natural language tasks by structuring their reasoning process according to the principles of causal inference, and their performance can be significantly improved through a tailored chain-of-thought prompting strategy.
6ac627f57b26354ab537734d820da4a6a7dde2c6.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark, CLADDER, will be developed to assess the formal causal reasoning abilities of LLMs. This dataset will contain over 10,000 natural language questions generated from symbolic causal graphs, queries (covering associational, interventional, and counterfactual types), and ground-truth answers derived from a causal inference engine. Each question will be verbalized into a natural language story, with varying degrees of alignment to commonsense, anti-commonsense, and nonsensical scenarios to control for data contamination and memorization. To elicit formal reasoning, a multi-step chain-of-thought prompting strategy, CAUSALCOT, will be designed, guiding LLMs through explicit steps: extracting the causal graph, classifying the query type, formalizing the query, gathering relevant data, deriving the estimand using causal inference techniques (such as do-calculus), and performing the necessary calculations to reach a binary answer.
6ac627f57b26354ab537734d820da4a6a7dde2c6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of LLMs, including GPT-4, GPT-3.5, several GPT-3 variants, LLaMa, and Alpaca, using the CLADDER dataset. Each model will be evaluated using both direct question answering and the CAUSALCOT prompting strategy. Performance will be measured by accuracy across all questions, as well as broken down by rung of the ladder of causation (associational, interventional, counterfactual) and by degree of commonsense alignment. Fine-grained error analysis will be performed on each step of the CAUSALCOT reasoning chain, and additional analyses will assess the impact of in-context learning and data contamination. Evaluation metrics will include overall accuracy, step-wise F1 scores for graph extraction and reasoning subskills, and robustness to unseen or nonsensical scenarios.
6ac627f57b26354ab537734d820da4a6a7dde2c6.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first large-scale benchmark specifically designed to assess formal causal reasoning in LLMs, grounded in explicit causal graphs and queries rather than commonsense or memorized patterns. The CAUSALCOT prompting strategy is a novel approach that systematically guides LLMs through the formal steps of causal inference, significantly improving performance over standard prompting. The dataset's design, which includes anti-commonsensical and nonsensical scenarios, enables rigorous testing of models' true reasoning abilities and resistance to data contamination. The work provides a principled framework for evaluating and advancing the causal reasoning capabilities of LLMs in natural language.

6ae06fdab54b37a6bddc5bbbe1ed8909b735c7e2.title: Learning to Render Novel Views from Wide-Baseline Stereo Pairs
6ae06fdab54b37a6bddc5bbbe1ed8909b735c7e2.research_question: How can novel views of complex real-world scenes be synthesized from extremely sparse image observations, specifically from a single wide-baseline stereo image pair, without relying on ground-truth or proxy geometry?
6ae06fdab54b37a6bddc5bbbe1ed8909b735c7e2.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a multi-view transformer-based encoder, combined with an efficient epipolar line sampling scheme and a lightweight cross-attention-based renderer, can learn powerful multi-view geometry priors from posed multi-view images, enabling high-quality and efficient novel view synthesis from just a wide-baseline stereo image pair.
6ae06fdab54b37a6bddc5bbbe1ed8909b735c7e2.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a multi-view vision transformer encoder that jointly processes a wide-baseline stereo image pair and their relative camera poses to extract pixel-aligned feature maps, enhancing geometric consistency across views. These features are computed at multiple resolutions, combining a vision transformer at lower resolutions with a CNN at higher resolutions, and are further refined via a multi-view feature matching step that augments primary epipolar line samples with secondary features from the other view. An efficient, image-centric epipolar line sampling strategy is employed, where for each target ray, features are sampled uniformly along the epipolar lines in the input images, and corresponding depth values are triangulated. A lightweight cross-attention-based neural renderer then aggregates these sampled features to predict the color of each target pixel, leveraging both primary and secondary epipolar features. The entire system is trained end-to-end using only posed multi-view images, with losses that encourage both image fidelity and multi-view consistency, and does not require explicit 3D geometry or per-scene optimization.
6ae06fdab54b37a6bddc5bbbe1ed8909b735c7e2.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on two large-scale real-world datasets: RealEstate10k (indoor and outdoor scenes) and ACID (outdoor scenes), using standard train/test splits. The method is trained at 256x256 image resolution and evaluated on the ability to reconstruct intermediate views from wide-baseline stereo pairs. Baseline comparisons include pixelNeRF, IBRNet, and GPNR, covering a range of existing approaches such as volumetric rendering and transformer-based light field rendering. Evaluation metrics include LPIPS, SSIM, PSNR, and MSE, providing both perceptual and pixel-wise assessments of rendering quality. Ablation studies are performed to assess the contribution of each architectural component, and rendering speed is benchmarked against baselines to demonstrate efficiency.
6ae06fdab54b37a6bddc5bbbe1ed8909b735c7e2.novelty_claims: The proposal claims the first solution for high-quality novel view synthesis of complex real-world scenes from a single wide-baseline stereo image pair, addressing a regime where most 3D points are observed from only one view. Key innovations include a multi-view transformer encoder that leverages camera pose for joint feature extraction, an efficient epipolar line sampling and feature matching strategy tailored to sparse inputs, and a lightweight cross-attention renderer that enables scalable, fast training and inference. The method avoids explicit 3D geometry reconstruction and per-scene optimization, enabling generalization across diverse scenes and achieving state-of-the-art results in both quality and speed for novel view synthesis from sparse observations.

6ae4705139494fcb6b790b6dd6c4225b40ee40f8.title: GLaMM: Pixel Grounding Large Multimodal Model
6ae4705139494fcb6b790b6dd6c4225b40ee40f8.research_question: How can a large multimodal model be developed to enable seamless, pixel-level grounding of natural language responses in images, supporting both textual and visual prompts for interactive, multi-turn conversations and a wide range of vision-language tasks?
6ae4705139494fcb6b790b6dd6c4225b40ee40f8.hypothesis: A unified large multimodal model, equipped with specialized encoders and decoders for both global and region-level image understanding, and trained on a densely annotated, large-scale dataset with automated pixel-level grounding, will enable accurate, flexible, and interactive visually grounded conversations, outperforming existing models on grounding, segmentation, and captioning tasks.
6ae4705139494fcb6b790b6dd6c4225b40ee40f8.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a large multimodal model architecture (GLaMM) comprising five core components: a global image encoder (CLIP ViT-H/14), a region encoder with hierarchical feature pyramids and RoIAlign, a large language model (LLM, Vicuna-based), a grounding image encoder (SAM encoder), and a pixel decoder (SAM decoder-like). The system supports both scene-level and region-level understanding by mapping image and region features into the language domain via a vision-to-language projection layer, allowing the LLM to generate responses conditioned on both image and region representations. Pixel-level grounding is achieved by augmenting the model's vocabulary with special tokens (<SEG>, <bbox>) and using a language-to-prompt projection to transform segmentation-related embeddings into the decoder space, producing binary segmentation masks interleaved with text. The model is trained end-to-end to support multi-turn, visually grounded conversations, and can flexibly process both textual and visual prompts.
6ae4705139494fcb6b790b6dd6c4225b40ee40f8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a newly constructed Grounding-anything Dataset (GranD), which contains 11M images, 810M regions, and 7.5M unique concepts, each annotated with pixel-level segmentation masks and dense captions. An additional high-quality fine-tuning dataset (GranD_f) will be created by repurposing and augmenting open-source datasets (Flickr30K, RefCOCOg, PSG) and manual annotation. Baselines for comparison include state-of-the-art LMMs and grounding models such as BuboGPT, Kosmos-2, and LISA. Evaluation will be performed on the novel Grounded Conversation Generation (GCG) task using metrics such as METEOR, CIDEr for caption quality, class-agnostic mask AP, mask IoU, and mask recall for grounding accuracy. Additional benchmarks will include referring expression segmentation (refCOCO, refCOCO+, refCOCOg), region-level captioning (Visual Genome, refCOCOg), and image-level captioning (Flickr30K, NoCap), using standard metrics for each task.
6ae4705139494fcb6b790b6dd6c4225b40ee40f8.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable seamless integration of natural language responses with interleaved, pixel-level segmentation masks in a conversational setting, supporting both textual and visual prompts. A novel Grounded Conversation Generation (GCG) task and comprehensive evaluation protocol are introduced, unifying multiple vision-language tasks. The creation of the Grounding-anything Dataset (GranD) using a fully automated, multi-level annotation pipeline establishes a new benchmark in scale and annotation quality for grounded vision-language research. The model architecture uniquely combines end-to-end training, multi-granularity grounding, and conversational capabilities, surpassing the limitations of existing LMMs that lack dense pixel-wise grounding or flexible region-level interaction.

6aeefa655a594a025359b026cb337c70f1d14404.title: Efficient Exploration of the Rashomon Set of Rule-Set Models
6aeefa655a594a025359b026cb337c70f1d14404.research_question: How can the Rashomon set of rule set models be efficiently explored and characterized for interpretable machine learning tasks, particularly when exhaustive enumeration is computationally infeasible?
6aeefa655a594a025359b026cb337c70f1d14404.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that scalable algorithms leveraging advanced branch-and-bound techniques, random partitioning, and search-tree-based approximations can efficiently explore, sample from, and estimate the size of the Rashomon set of rule set models, providing near-uniform samples and accurate counts without requiring full enumeration.
6aeefa655a594a025359b026cb337c70f1d14404.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces a suite of algorithms for both exhaustive and non-exhaustive exploration of the Rashomon set of rule set models. For exhaustive enumeration, a highly-optimized branch-and-bound algorithm (BBenum) is developed, incorporating effective pruning bounds (hierarchical, look-ahead, and rule set size bounds) and incremental computation to efficiently traverse the combinatorial space of rule sets. For non-exhaustive exploration, two alternative approaches are proposed: (1) ApproxCount and ApproxSample, which utilize random parity constraints to partition the solution space, allowing for approximate counting and near-uniform sampling with theoretical guarantees; (2) BBsts, a search-tree-based approximation that samples and estimates the Rashomon set size by exploring the search tree in a breadth-first manner, partitioned by depth and leveraging partial solutions. All algorithms are further accelerated by implementation-level enhancements such as parallelization and rule permutation to maximize pruning efficiency.
6aeefa655a594a025359b026cb337c70f1d14404.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several real-world datasets where interpretability is crucial, including COMPAS (recidivism prediction), Mushrooms (edibility classification), Credit (credit scoring), and Voting (political affiliation). The universe of candidate rules will be constructed using frequent pattern mining (e.g., FP-growth), and experiments will vary the number of input rules and the Rashomon set threshold parameter to assess scalability and accuracy. Baseline comparisons will include a naïve exhaustive branch-and-bound, a state-of-the-art SAT-based constraint programming solver, and an importance sampling Monte Carlo approach. Evaluation metrics will focus on runtime, estimated Rashomon set size, and sampling uniformity, with experiments designed to test both small and large Rashomon sets and to validate theoretical guarantees of the proposed methods.
6aeefa655a594a025359b026cb337c70f1d14404.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces, for the first time, efficient algorithms for both exhaustive and non-exhaustive exploration of the Rashomon set of rule set models, including scalable branch-and-bound enumeration with advanced pruning, and near-uniform sampling and counting via random partitioning and search-tree-based methods. The approach is tailored specifically for rule sets, which are more expressive and challenging than decision lists or trees, and includes novel incremental computation and minimal non-violation techniques for parity-constrained enumeration. The methods provide strong theoretical guarantees and demonstrate significant improvements in scalability and accuracy over existing baselines.

6b135e922a0c673aeb0b05c5aeecdb6c794791c6.title: Jailbreak and Guard Aligned Language Models with Only Few In-Context Demonstrations
6b135e922a0c673aeb0b05c5aeecdb6c794791c6.research_question: Can the alignment and safety behavior of large language models (LLMs) be effectively manipulated in both harmful and beneficial directions using only a few in-context demonstrations, and how can this property be leveraged for both attacking (jailbreaking) and defending (guarding) LLMs against harmful prompt injection?
6b135e922a0c673aeb0b05c5aeecdb6c794791c6.hypothesis: A small number of carefully crafted in-context demonstrations can significantly influence the safety alignment of LLMs, enabling both successful jailbreak attacks and robust defenses against such attacks.
6b135e922a0c673aeb0b05c5aeecdb6c794791c6.proposed_method: A novel methodology is proposed that leverages in-context learning (ICL) to manipulate the safety alignment of LLMs through two complementary techniques: In-Context Attack (ICA) and In-Context Defense (ICD). ICA involves constructing prompts by concatenating a set of harmful demonstration pairs (malicious requests and their harmful responses) with the target attack prompt, thereby inducing the LLM to generate harmful content. ICD, in contrast, constructs prompts using safe demonstration pairs (malicious requests and their safe, refusal responses) to enhance the model's robustness and encourage refusal to generate harmful outputs. Both methods require only a few demonstration pairs, can be applied without modifying model parameters, and are compatible with both open- and closed-source LLMs. Theoretical analysis is developed to quantify the effect of demonstration set size and composition on the model's safety risk, providing formal guarantees on the manipulation of the model's output distribution.
6b135e922a0c673aeb0b05c5aeecdb6c794791c6.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on four popular aligned LLMs: Vicuna-7b-v1.5, Llama2-7b-chat, QWen-7b-v2, and GPT-4. For attack evaluation, the AdvBench and HarmBench datasets are used, containing hundreds of harmful prompts. ICA is compared to state-of-the-art jailbreak attacks such as GCG, AutoDAN, PAIR, and TAP, using attack success rate (ASR) as the primary metric, determined by both string-based rejection detection and LLM-based harmfulness judgment, with human evaluation for ambiguous cases. For defense evaluation, ICD is tested against both black-box and white-box attacks, including GCG-T, PAIR, GCG, and AutoDAN, and is compared to the Self-reminder defense. The impact on natural language understanding and instruction-following is assessed using the GLUE and MT-Bench benchmarks, with inference time measured to evaluate computational overhead. Demonstration sets are constructed from AdvBench prompts and generated responses, with multiple random seeds to ensure robustness.
6b135e922a0c673aeb0b05c5aeecdb6c794791c6.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first systematic study of using in-context demonstrations to both jailbreak and guard aligned LLMs, demonstrating that only a few demonstration pairs can drastically alter model safety behavior. The ICA and ICD techniques are model-agnostic, efficient, and require no access to model internals, making them practical for real-world deployment. Theoretical analysis provides new insights into the mechanisms by which in-context demonstrations influence LLM output distributions. Experimental results show that ICA achieves state-of-the-art attack success rates, while ICD provides robust defense with minimal impact on natural performance and negligible computational overhead. This work opens new avenues for both red-teaming and safeguarding LLMs using prompt-based techniques.

6b2b5d3d9a2ca4bc4fbd81551a62370be2fbff1b.title: Explaining neural scaling laws
6b2b5d3d9a2ca4bc4fbd81551a62370be2fbff1b.research_question: What are the fundamental mechanisms underlying the emergence of power-law neural scaling laws in deep neural networks, and how do these mechanisms relate to model size, dataset size, and the properties of the data manifold? Can a unified theoretical framework be developed to categorize and predict different scaling regimes observed in neural network training?
6b2b5d3d9a2ca4bc4fbd81551a62370be2fbff1b.hypothesis: Neural network performance exhibits distinct scaling regimes—variance-limited and resolution-limited—governed by universal and data-dependent mechanisms, respectively. These regimes can be theoretically derived and empirically observed, with scaling exponents determined by properties such as model width, dataset size, and the intrinsic dimension of the data manifold. A duality exists between model and dataset scaling exponents in certain regimes.
6b2b5d3d9a2ca4bc4fbd81551a62370be2fbff1b.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical framework will be developed to explain neural scaling laws by categorizing scaling behavior into four regimes: variance-limited and resolution-limited, each with respect to both model size and dataset size. The approach will involve explicit derivations of scaling exponents in random feature teacher-student models, leveraging kernel spectral analysis to relate scaling exponents to the intrinsic dimension of the data manifold. Theoretical predictions will be refined through asymptotic expansions and analytic bounds, and the framework will be extended to general nonlinear neural networks via smoothness and concentration arguments. Empirical validation will be conducted by measuring scaling exponents in both controlled synthetic settings and real-world deep learning tasks, testing the dependence of scaling behavior on data distribution, model architecture, and training procedures.
6b2b5d3d9a2ca4bc4fbd81551a62370be2fbff1b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic teacher-student models and standard deep learning benchmarks such as MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, and FashionMNIST. Controlled experiments will use random feature models and pretrained deep networks to systematically vary model size (width, parameter count) and dataset size, allowing identification of all four scaling regimes. Baselines will include linear models, random feature models, and deep convolutional architectures (e.g., Wide ResNet, multi-layer CNNs). Evaluation metrics will focus on population test loss and its scaling with respect to model and dataset size. Additional experiments will probe the effects of data manifold dimension, input noise, and task modifications (e.g., superclassing) on scaling exponents, with empirical measurements compared to theoretical predictions.
6b2b5d3d9a2ca4bc4fbd81551a62370be2fbff1b.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified taxonomy of four neural scaling regimes and provides explicit theoretical derivations of scaling exponents in both variance-limited and resolution-limited settings. The framework establishes a novel duality between model and dataset scaling exponents, relates resolution-limited exponents to the intrinsic dimension of the data manifold via kernel spectral decay, and empirically validates these predictions across a wide range of architectures and datasets. The work also explores the impact of data distribution and architectural choices on scaling behavior, offering new insights into the microscopic origins of neural scaling laws and their universality or dependence on problem specifics.

6b69273252cc02c8c57830440705ada438cfcb31.title: Enhancing Pre-trained Representation Classifiability can Boost its Interpretability
6b69273252cc02c8c57830440705ada438cfcb31.research_question: Can pre-trained visual representations achieve high interpretability and classifiability simultaneously, and how can interpretability be quantitatively measured and enhanced in such representations?
6b69273252cc02c8c57830440705ada438cfcb31.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that classifiability-oriented pre-trained representations can be made more interpretable without sacrificing, and potentially even improving, their classifiability; furthermore, interpretability and classifiability are positively correlated in these representations.
6b69273252cc02c8c57830440705ada438cfcb31.proposed_method: A new quantitative metric, the Inherent Interpretability Score (IIS), will be developed to measure the interpretability of pre-trained visual representations. IIS is computed by projecting representations into a human-understandable concept space, constructed from visual or textual concepts, and evaluating the semantic information loss via an accuracy retention rate (ARR) between predictions made with original representations and those made with their sparse, concept-based interpretations. The method involves constructing several types of concept libraries (Prototype, Cluster, End2End, Text) and projecting representations into these spaces, followed by sparsification to ensure human-comprehensible interpretations. A linear classifier is trained on the interpreted representations, and IIS is defined as the area under the curve of ARR across varying sparsity ratios. Additionally, a fine-tuning procedure is proposed that maximizes IIS (or a simplified variant) to jointly enhance interpretability and classifiability.
6b69273252cc02c8c57830440705ada438cfcb31.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple standard image classification datasets, including ImageNet1K, CUB-200, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100, covering both general and fine-grained tasks. A range of widely-used pre-trained models will be evaluated, such as ResNet-18/34/50/101/152, ViT-B/L-16, ConvNeXt-T/S/B/L, and Swin-T/S/B, with weights sourced from Torchvision. Concept libraries for interpretation will be constructed using both visual (image patches or segments) and textual (GPT-3 generated) concepts, with the number of concepts tailored to each dataset. Baseline comparisons will include interpretability-oriented methods (e.g., SENN, CBM, CEM, Proto2proto, ProtopNet, ECBM, LaBo) and classifiability-oriented models. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 and top-5 accuracy, ARR, and IIS. Ablation studies will be performed on concept space dimension and sparsity ratio. Fine-tuning experiments will assess the impact of IIS maximization on both interpretability and classifiability.
6b69273252cc02c8c57830440705ada438cfcb31.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces IIS, a novel, quantitative, and generalizable metric for measuring the interpretability of pre-trained visual representations based on their ability to retain task-relevant semantics in human-interpretable concept spaces. It claims to be the first to systematically demonstrate a positive correlation between interpretability and classifiability in classifiability-oriented representations, challenging the conventional belief in their inherent conflict. The method enables interpretable predictions with accuracy close to or surpassing interpretability-oriented baselines, using only a classification head for training. The approach also provides a new fine-tuning paradigm that jointly improves both interpretability and classifiability, offering practical benefits for interpretable representation learning in vision models.

6b8e98792e4af57687939156c07b99cd12187f89.title: Maximum State Entropy Exploration using Predecessor and Successor Representations
6b8e98792e4af57687939156c07b99cd12187f89.research_question: How can an agent efficiently explore an environment to maximize state coverage and state visitation entropy, particularly within a single finite-length trajectory, by leveraging information from past episodic experiences rather than relying solely on current state information or random exploratory moves?
6b8e98792e4af57687939156c07b99cd12187f89.hypothesis: Conditioning exploration policies on both past state visitation (predecessor representation) and predictions of future state visitation (successor representation) enables more efficient and systematic exploration, resulting in higher state visitation entropy and coverage compared to Markovian or random exploration policies.
6b8e98792e4af57687939156c07b99cd12187f89.proposed_method: A new exploration algorithm, ηψ-Learning, will be developed to learn policies that maximize the entropy of the state visitation distribution within a single finite-length trajectory. This method will maintain two key representations: a predecessor representation that encodes the frequencies of past state visitations, and a successor representation (SR) that predicts future state visitation frequencies conditioned on the entire trajectory history and candidate actions. At each decision point, the SR and predecessor representations will be combined to estimate the expected state visitation distribution for each possible action, and the action that maximizes the entropy of this distribution will be selected. The SR will be learned using a parameterized, differentiable function (e.g., a recurrent neural network), optimized via temporal-difference learning, while the overall policy will be optimized using either Q-learning or deterministic policy gradient methods, depending on whether the action space is discrete or continuous.
6b8e98792e4af57687939156c07b99cd12187f89.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of discrete and continuous control tasks, including ChainMDP, RiverSwim, 5x5 Gridworld, TwoRooms, FourRooms, Reacher, and Pusher environments. Baseline comparisons will include Markovian maximum entropy exploration methods such as MaxEnt, as well as meta-RL approaches like VariBAD. Evaluation metrics will include the entropy of the state visitation distribution, the fraction of the state space visited (state coverage), and search completion time (steps required to visit all states). For continuous control tasks, the entropy and coverage of the agent's end-effector positions will be measured. All results will be averaged over multiple random seeds, and hyperparameters will be tuned as appropriate for each environment. Visualizations of state visitation distributions and learned representations will be provided to qualitatively assess exploration efficiency.
6b8e98792e4af57687939156c07b99cd12187f89.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first algorithm that explicitly combines predecessor and successor representations to estimate and maximize the entropy of the state visitation distribution within a single finite-length trajectory. The approach enables the learning of deterministic, non-Markovian exploration policies that can systematically cover the state space more efficiently than existing Markovian or randomized methods. The method is applicable to both discrete and continuous action spaces and does not require explicit transition models or density estimators. The proposed framework is expected to advance efficient exploration in reinforcement learning, with potential applications in meta-RL, continual RL, unsupervised RL, and goal-conditioned RL.

6b9450e95cbd8f22c2f9eb834936877c59352feb.title: Statistical Guarantees for Regularized Neural Networks
6b9450e95cbd8f22c2f9eb834936877c59352feb.research_question: What statistical guarantees can be established for regularized neural network estimators, particularly those used in practice, and how do these guarantees depend on network architecture, regularization type, and data properties?
6b9450e95cbd8f22c2f9eb834936877c59352feb.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a general framework for regularized neural network estimation, utilizing a novel scale-based regularization scheme, can provide statistical prediction guarantees that scale favorably with the number of parameters, network depth, and sample size, especially when employing sparsity-inducing regularizers such as the ℓ1-norm.
6b9450e95cbd8f22c2f9eb834936877c59352feb.proposed_method: A new class of regularized least-squares estimators for neural networks will be developed by reparametrizing the network weights into a 'scale' parameter and an 'orientation' parameter. Regularization will be applied specifically to the scale parameter, resulting in a one-dimensional regularization problem that simplifies statistical analysis. The general framework will allow for various regularizers, with a focus on ℓ1-regularization to induce sparsity. Theoretical prediction error bounds will be derived using empirical process theory, connecting the effective noise in the estimation process to standard complexity measures such as Gaussian and Rademacher complexities. Explicit bounds will be provided for the squared prediction error, demonstrating how it depends on the sample size, number of parameters, and network depth.
6b9450e95cbd8f22c2f9eb834936877c59352feb.experiment_details: Theoretical results will be exemplified for ℓ1-regularization under the assumption of sub-Gaussian noise and Lipschitz activation functions (e.g., ReLU, leaky ReLU, ELU, tanh, Swish). The analysis will consider feedforward neural networks of varying depths and widths, with the total number of parameters P and number of layers L as key variables. Prediction error bounds will be compared to those from standard high-dimensional linear regression and prior neural network results, focusing on the dependence on n (sample size), P (number of parameters), and L (depth). Evaluation metrics will include in-sample prediction error and generalization error (risk), with probabilistic guarantees provided for both. Theoretical experiments will illustrate the scaling of the bounds and the impact of different regularization schemes.
6b9450e95cbd8f22c2f9eb834936877c59352feb.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel scale-based regularization framework for neural networks, enabling statistical prediction guarantees that are more tractable and interpretable than previous approaches. The method yields error bounds that increase only logarithmically with the number of parameters and can decrease with network depth, addressing limitations of prior results that exhibited unfavorable dependence on network size or depth. The approach bridges empirical process theory and neural network estimation, providing a unified and generalizable scheme for deriving statistical guarantees for a wide range of regularization types, activation functions, and noise models.

6ba5b4ce50cf1248b9141d2f526df856d3a863b8.title: Demystifying Singular Defects in Large Language Models
6ba5b4ce50cf1248b9141d2f526df856d3a863b8.research_question: What are the underlying mechanisms that cause the emergence of high-norm (singular defect) tokens in large language models (LLMs), how do these mechanisms differ from those in vision transformers (ViTs), and how can a deeper understanding of these phenomena lead to improved model robustness and new applications such as quantization and model signature tracing?
6ba5b4ce50cf1248b9141d2f526df856d3a863b8.hypothesis: High-norm tokens in LLMs arise due to specific computational pathways involving singular directions in the linear approximations of transformer layers, and these singular defect directions can be mathematically characterized and exploited for practical applications such as improved quantization and model signature identification.
6ba5b4ce50cf1248b9141d2f526df856d3a863b8.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and empirical framework will be developed to analyze the lifecycle of high-norm tokens in LLMs. The method will extend the theory of singular defects, originally formulated for ViTs, to LLMs by modeling transformer layers as linear operators and identifying singular directions via singular value decomposition. The approach will distinguish between the roles of self-attention and feed-forward modules in generating high-norm tokens, analyze the triggers and decay mechanisms using eigenvalue decomposition, and characterize the explosion subspace responsible for norm increases. The methodology will also include the development of high-norm-aware quantization schemes that selectively preserve precision in critical layers and the design of robust LLM signatures based on stable singular defect directions.
6ba5b4ce50cf1248b9141d2f526df856d3a863b8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a diverse set of recent LLMs, including LLaMA2-7B, Phi3-Medium, MPT-7B, Pythia-160M, Vicuna1.5-7B, Falcon2-11B, GPT2-Medium, and Qwen2.5-1.5B, as well as the Pythia model suite at various training stages. Empirical validation will involve extracting hidden states from thousands of random samples (e.g., WikiText2-v1 dataset), computing token norms across layers, and analyzing the alignment between empirical high-norm directions and predicted singular defect directions. Baseline quantization methods such as RTN and SmoothQuant will be compared against the proposed high-norm-aware quantization strategy, with evaluation metrics including perplexity on standard validation sets. Additional experiments will assess the stability of model signatures after fine-tuning and across model families by measuring acute angles between signature vectors.
6ba5b4ce50cf1248b9141d2f526df856d3a863b8.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a mathematical framework that extends singular defect theory to LLMs, providing the first comprehensive explanation for the lifecycle of high-norm tokens in these models. It identifies and characterizes the distinct computational pathways and triggers for high-norm tokens, distinguishing them from similar phenomena in ViTs. The work proposes a novel high-norm-aware quantization strategy that improves robustness and efficiency in low-bit quantization settings. Furthermore, it establishes the use of stable singular defect directions as robust, data-independent signatures for LLMs, enabling reliable model lineage tracing and infringement detection. These contributions collectively advance the understanding of internal LLM mechanisms and open new avenues for practical applications.

6ba8c408bb833c2f2aeea70107d56184417077d4.title: Segment Anything Model (SAM) Enhanced Pseudo Labels for Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation
6ba8c408bb833c2f2aeea70107d56184417077d4.research_question: How can the quality of pseudo-labels for weakly supervised semantic segmentation be improved by leveraging both class-aware and object-aware information, while maintaining compatibility with existing weakly supervised methods?
6ba8c408bb833c2f2aeea70107d56184417077d4.hypothesis: Integrating class-agnostic, fine-grained instance masks from a foundation segmentation model with class-aware cues from Class Activation Maps will yield pseudo-labels that are both class-aware and object-aware, resulting in improved semantic segmentation performance under weak supervision.
6ba8c408bb833c2f2aeea70107d56184417077d4.proposed_method: A new approach is developed that enhances pseudo-label generation for weakly supervised semantic segmentation by combining Class Activation Maps (CAMs) with masks produced by the Segment Anything Model (SAM). The method operates in two main stages: mask assignment and mask selection. During mask assignment, each SAM-generated mask is assigned to the class whose CAM-derived pseudo-labels have the largest intersection with that mask, discarding masks with no overlap. In the mask selection stage, two metrics are computed for each assigned mask: the fraction of the mask overlapped by the pseudo-labels, and the fraction of the pseudo-labels overlapped by the mask. Masks are retained as enhanced pseudo-labels if either metric surpasses predefined thresholds (e.g., 50% and 85%, respectively). The final enhanced pseudo-labels are obtained by merging the selected masks for each class, ensuring both class-awareness and precise object boundaries.
6ba8c408bb833c2f2aeea70107d56184417077d4.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the PASCAL VOC 2012 and MS COCO 2014 datasets, using only image-level ground-truth labels for pseudo-label generation. The proposed method is evaluated by enhancing pseudo-labels produced by several state-of-the-art weakly supervised semantic segmentation (WSSS) methods, including Recurseed, L2G, CLIPES, RCA, EPS, CLIMS, TransCAM, PPC, SIPE, and PuzzleCAM. The mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) is adopted as the primary evaluation metric, with assessments performed both on the quality of the pseudo-labels and on the performance of DeepLabV2 (ResNet-101) segmentation models trained using these labels. Comparisons are made against original pseudo-labels and fully supervised baselines, and experiments include ablation on threshold parameters and analysis of failure cases.
6ba8c408bb833c2f2aeea70107d56184417077d4.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to systematically investigate the use of a foundation segmentation model (SAM) for enhancing pseudo-labels in weakly supervised semantic segmentation. The approach introduces a simple yet effective algorithm that combines class-aware and object-aware cues, is highly versatile, and can be seamlessly integrated into existing WSSS pipelines without modification. Consistent and significant improvements in pseudo-label quality and downstream segmentation performance are demonstrated across multiple state-of-the-art baselines and datasets.

6bad752dbe01735f85b8046f783647ef8895da2c.title: CodeSteer: Symbolic-Augmented Language Models via Code/Text Guidance
6bad752dbe01735f85b8046f783647ef8895da2c.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be more effectively guided to leverage both textual reasoning and symbolic code generation for solving a wide range of symbolic and reasoning-intensive tasks, especially when task requirements and optimal solution modalities are not explicitly specified?
6bad752dbe01735f85b8046f783647ef8895da2c.hypothesis: Augmenting LLMs with a specialized, fine-tuned guidance model that dynamically steers between code and text generation, supported by symbolic and self-answer checking mechanisms, will significantly improve performance and generalizability on complex symbolic tasks compared to existing text-only or code-only approaches.
6bad752dbe01735f85b8046f783647ef8895da2c.proposed_method: A novel framework, CodeSteer, will be developed to guide LLMs in dynamically choosing between code and text generation throughout multi-turn interactions. The approach involves fine-tuning a smaller LLM (Llama-3-8B) as a guidance assistant (CodeSteerLLM) using a newly constructed benchmark (SymBench) of 37 symbolic tasks and large-scale synthetic datasets (12k multi-turn guidance/generation trajectories for SFT and 5.5k guidance comparison pairs for DPO). The guidance model will review the TaskLLM's answers at each turn, provide adaptive prompts, and decide when to finalize answers. Two novel components—a Symbolic Checker (for code complexity and efficiency assessment) and a Self-answer Checker (for answer verification via code execution)—will be integrated to enhance both dataset synthesis and model fine-tuning. The training process will employ multi-turn supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with data augmentation on the final turns and direct preference optimization (DPO) using rule-based scoring to encourage efficient, correct solutions.
6bad752dbe01735f85b8046f783647ef8895da2c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on SymBench, covering 37 symbolic tasks with adjustable complexity, using both seen (28) and unseen (9) tasks for evaluation. The main TaskLLM will be GPT-4o, with additional tests on Claude-3-5-Sonnet, Mistral-Large, and GPT-3.5-Turbo to assess generalizability. Baselines will include six training-free and three training-based methods, such as text-only, code-only, mixed strategies, and current state-of-the-art CoT models (OpenAI o1, o1-preview, DeepSeek R1). Evaluation metrics will primarily be task success rate and average normalized score, with additional analysis of token usage and runtime costs. Ablation studies will investigate the impact of DPO, SFT data augmentation, and the symbolic/self-answer checkers. The experimental setup will use distinct training and test splits, with fine-tuning performed on 4*H100 GPUs for 4-10 epochs.
6bad752dbe01735f85b8046f783647ef8895da2c.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a comprehensive symbolic benchmark (SymBench) with adjustable complexity and fully open-source generation code, a novel multi-turn guidance framework that dynamically steers LLMs between code and text, and two new checking mechanisms (Symbolic Checker and Self-answer Checker) that enhance both model training and inference.
