The method innovates in dataset synthesis, multi-turn SFT/DPO fine-tuning, and dynamic adaptation strategies, achieving superior performance and generalizability compared to both text-only and code-only baselines as well as state-of-the-art CoT models. The approach demonstrates robust scalability to highly complex tasks and transferability across different LLM architectures.

6bc6271f7edd87388d5ce058b6265ce4f56a269e.title: AutoEdit: Automatic Hyperparameter Tuning for Image Editing
6bc6271f7edd87388d5ce058b6265ce4f56a269e.research_question: How can the process of hyperparameter selection for diffusion-based, text-guided image editing be automated to improve editing quality and efficiency, while reducing computational overhead and the need for manual intervention?
6bc6271f7edd87388d5ce058b6265ce4f56a269e.hypothesis: Formulating hyperparameter optimization as a reinforcement learning (RL) problem within the diffusion denoising process will enable efficient, per-image identification of near-optimal hyperparameters, leading to improved editing quality and reduced computational cost compared to brute-force search.
6bc6271f7edd87388d5ce058b6265ce4f56a269e.proposed_method: A reinforcement learning framework will be developed to automate hyperparameter tuning during the diffusion-based image editing process. The editing procedure will be formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), where each denoising step corresponds to a unique RL state defined by the noisy latent and current timestep. At each step, the RL agent (policy model) will select a set of hyperparameters (such as inversion timestep, attention modification ratios, and blending coefficients) as actions, which are then applied to the denoising function. The reward function will integrate prompt alignment (measured by CLIP score or a Large Vision-Language Model for small regions) and background preservation (measured by MSE outside the edit mask), with tunable coefficients to balance these objectives. The policy will be optimized using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), with a two-phase training strategy: pretraining with hyperparameters sampled from prior distributions to constrain the search space, followed by online RL-based fine-tuning for optimal hyperparameter identification. The policy and value models will leverage features extracted from a pretrained U-Net encoder, with additional trainable layers for hyperparameter prediction.
6bc6271f7edd87388d5ce058b6265ce4f56a269e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the EditBench dataset for training (2,000 annotated samples) and the PieBench benchmark (700 samples) for evaluation, covering a wide range of prompt-to-prompt editing tasks. The proposed method will be integrated with various baseline image editing frameworks, including both training-free (e.g., DDIM-Inversion, DDPM-Inversion, PnP-Inversion, Prompt-to-Prompt, MasaCtrl, Null-text Inversion) and training-based methods (e.g., InstructPix2Pix, UltraEdit), across multiple base models (SD1.4, SD1.5, SDXL, DiT). Evaluation metrics will include structural consistency (Structure Distance), background preservation (PSNR, SSIM, MSE, LPIPS), semantic alignment (CLIP scores for edited regions and full images), and LLMScore (using a Large Vision-Language Model to assess edit correctness, especially for small regions). Baseline methods will be compared using their best-performing hyperparameter configurations, and ablation studies will examine the impact of reward coefficients and policy initialization. Computational efficiency will be assessed by measuring inference time and model size overhead.
6bc6271f7edd87388d5ce058b6265ce4f56a269e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to formulate hyperparameter optimization for diffusion-based image editing as a reinforcement learning problem, reducing search complexity from exponential to linear with respect to the number of denoising steps. The method unifies hyperparameter identification and denoising within a single RL-driven framework, enabling dynamic, per-image hyperparameter selection that adapts to both global and small-region edits. The reward function flexibly integrates multiple editing objectives and can incorporate advanced vision-language models for fine-grained evaluation. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate substantial reductions in hyperparameter search time and computational cost, while achieving or surpassing the editing quality of brute-force and heuristic baselines.

6bd3ee1ca608bc66a490f63f2fb107d79b44f3e2.title: LLM-QAT: Data-Free Quantization Aware Training for Large Language Models
6bd3ee1ca608bc66a490f63f2fb107d79b44f3e2.research_question: How can large language models be quantized to lower bit precision, including weights, activations, and key-value (KV) cache, without access to original training data and while preserving model performance on downstream tasks?
6bd3ee1ca608bc66a490f63f2fb107d79b44f3e2.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a data-free quantization-aware training (QAT) approach, leveraging knowledge distillation from synthetic data generated by the pre-trained model itself, can enable accurate quantization of large language models to 4-bit precision for weights and KV cache, and 6-8 bits for activations, without significant loss in performance compared to full-precision models.
6bd3ee1ca608bc66a490f63f2fb107d79b44f3e2.proposed_method: A novel quantization-aware training framework will be developed for large language models that does not require access to the original training data. The method will generate synthetic training data by sampling next-token sequences from the pre-trained model, employing a hybrid sampling strategy that deterministically selects the top-1 token for the first few positions and stochastically samples subsequent tokens from the model's output distribution. Quantization will be applied to weights, activations, and the KV cache using symmetric MinMax quantization, with per-channel quantization for weights and per-token quantization for activations and KV cache. Knowledge distillation will be performed using cross-entropy loss on the full logit outputs of the teacher (pre-trained) model, guiding the fine-tuning of the quantized student model. The quantization function will be integrated into the training process to ensure gradients flow through quantized tensors, and outlier values will be preserved rather than clipped to maintain model performance.
6bd3ee1ca608bc66a490f63f2fb107d79b44f3e2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on LLaMA models of sizes 7B, 13B, and 30B, with quantization levels down to 4 bits for weights and KV cache, and 6-8 bits for activations. The evaluation will include zero-shot and few-shot performance on a range of downstream tasks such as BoolQ, PIQA, SIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC, OBQA, TriviaQA, and MMLU, as well as perplexity measurements on WikiText2 and C4 datasets. Baseline comparisons will be made against state-of-the-art post-training quantization methods including RTN, GPTQ, and SmoothQuant. The experimental setup will use a single 8-GPU node, with the AdamW optimizer, a learning rate of 2e-5, and batch size of 1 per GPU. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of data generation strategy, quantization function, and distillation method.
6bd3ee1ca608bc66a490f63f2fb107d79b44f3e2.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable quantization-aware training for large language models without requiring access to original training data, using a data-free knowledge distillation method based on synthetic data generation. It is also the first to demonstrate accurate 4-bit quantization of both weights and KV cache in LLMs, and to show that preserving outliers during quantization is critical for maintaining performance. The method achieves superior results compared to existing post-training quantization techniques, especially at lower bit precisions, and is compatible with activation rescaling techniques such as SmoothQuant. This work establishes a practical and scalable solution for highly efficient LLM deployment.

6be216d93421bf19c1659e7721241ae73d483baf.title: Generating Diverse High-Fidelity Images with VQ-VAE-2
6be216d93421bf19c1659e7721241ae73d483baf.research_question: How can large-scale, high-fidelity, and diverse images be generated efficiently using likelihood-based generative models, while overcoming the limitations of existing approaches such as mode collapse and slow sampling speeds?
6be216d93421bf19c1659e7721241ae73d483baf.hypothesis: A hierarchical, multi-scale Vector Quantized Variational AutoEncoder (VQ-VAE) framework, combined with powerful autoregressive priors over discrete latent codes, can generate high-resolution images with quality and diversity comparable to state-of-the-art GANs, while enabling faster and more efficient sampling.
6be216d93421bf19c1659e7721241ae73d483baf.proposed_method: A hierarchical VQ-VAE model will be developed, in which images are encoded into multiple levels of discrete latent codes using simple feed-forward encoder and decoder networks. The encoder will downsample the input image to a bottom-level latent map (e.g., 64x64), and then further to a top-level latent map (e.g., 32x32), with each level capturing complementary global and local information. The decoder will reconstruct images from all levels of the latent hierarchy. In a second stage, powerful autoregressive priors (such as PixelCNNs with self-attention for the top level) will be trained over the latent codes, enabling efficient sampling in the compressed latent space rather than pixel space. Class-conditional generation and classifier-based rejection sampling will be incorporated to trade off sample diversity and quality.
6be216d93421bf19c1659e7721241ae73d483baf.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale image datasets, including ImageNet at 256x256 resolution and the FFHQ dataset at 1024x1024 resolution. The model's performance will be compared against state-of-the-art GANs (e.g., BigGAN-deep) using both qualitative (sample diversity and fidelity) and quantitative metrics. Evaluation metrics will include Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL) for generalization, Mean Squared Error (MSE) for reconstruction, Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS), Precision-Recall, and Classification Accuracy Score (CAS). Baseline comparisons will involve GAN-based models and other likelihood-based models, with side-by-side sample comparisons and metric-based analysis. Classifier-based rejection sampling will be used to further analyze the trade-off between diversity and quality.
6be216d93421bf19c1659e7721241ae73d483baf.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a multi-scale hierarchical VQ-VAE architecture for high-resolution image generation, leveraging autoregressive priors in the compressed latent space for efficient and high-quality sampling. The method achieves image quality and diversity on par with state-of-the-art GANs, while avoiding common GAN issues such as mode collapse and slow sampling. The use of simple feed-forward encoders and decoders, combined with powerful latent-space priors, enables significantly faster sampling and scalability to large images. The approach also demonstrates improved diversity and generalization, as measured by objective metrics, and introduces classifier-based rejection sampling for controllable trade-offs between diversity and fidelity.

6be2e46c18967da1b8cc550a63041025b2b0c1d8.title: Logically Consistent Language Models via Neuro-Symbolic Integration
6be2e46c18967da1b8cc550a63041025b2b0c1d8.research_question: How can large language models be fine-tuned to achieve higher levels of logical consistency and factuality, particularly in reasoning scenarios involving complex logical constraints, without relying on external symbolic reasoners or large-scale supervised datasets?
6be2e46c18967da1b8cc550a63041025b2b0c1d8.hypothesis: Integrating neuro-symbolic reasoning into the fine-tuning process of large language models, via a constraint-based semantic loss objective, will improve both factuality and logical self-consistency across a range of logical constraints, even in low-data regimes and without external reasoning tools.
6be2e46c18967da1b8cc550a63041025b2b0c1d8.proposed_method: A novel fine-tuning strategy is proposed that incorporates neuro-symbolic reasoning into large language models (LLMs) by defining a semantic loss based on weighted model counting over logical constraints. The method involves representing external knowledge as a set of facts and associated logical constraints (such as implications, negations, and their combinations) and then training the LLM to maximize the probability that its outputs satisfy these constraints. During training, for each constraint, the model is prompted to produce the probabilities of each fact being true, and these probabilities are combined according to the logical structure of the constraint using efficient circuit-based computation. The semantic loss is then minimized via backpropagation, updating the model parameters (using techniques like LoRA and quantization where appropriate) to encourage logical consistency and factuality. This approach is constraint-agnostic, allowing for the combination of multiple logical rules in a unified objective and enabling generalization to unseen but semantically similar facts.
6be2e46c18967da1b8cc550a63041025b2b0c1d8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on established benchmarks such as BeliefBank and EntailmentBank, which provide collections of facts and logical constraints in natural language. The method will be evaluated using various LLM architectures, including Macaw-Large and LLaMa-2 (7B and 70B), with both supervised fine-tuning (cross-entropy loss) and neuro-symbolic fine-tuning (semantic loss) as baselines. Evaluation metrics will include factuality (measured by F1 score), logical self-consistency (fraction of constraints satisfied), implication and negation consistency, and language modeling fluency (perplexity on WikiText). Experimental setups will vary the amount of training data (from low-data to high-data regimes), the types of logical constraints used for training and evaluation, and the ability to generalize to unseen domains and constraint types. Comparisons will be made against external solver-based approaches (e.g., ConCoRD) and standard supervised fine-tuning.
6be2e46c18967da1b8cc550a63041025b2b0c1d8.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled, constraint-agnostic neuro-symbolic fine-tuning objective for LLMs that directly encodes arbitrary logical constraints via a semantic loss, eliminating the need for external symbolic reasoners at inference time. This enables unified training for multiple logical consistency objectives, improves both factuality and self-consistency in low-data regimes, and allows for systematic generalization to unseen logical knowledge. The method is more sample-efficient than standard supervised fine-tuning and achieves higher logical consistency than previous state-of-the-art approaches that rely on external solvers.

6be6af7596a8f47a5fbf8fa7ab43f7ac7fc44354.title: Constructing Deep Spiking Neural Networks from Artificial Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
6be6af7596a8f47a5fbf8fa7ab43f7ac7fc44354.research_question: How can deep spiking neural networks (SNNs) be constructed to achieve high performance and efficiency, overcoming the limitations of current SNN training methods and network structures, particularly in comparison to artificial neural networks (ANNs)?
6be6af7596a8f47a5fbf8fa7ab43f7ac7fc44354.hypothesis: Deep SNNs constructed using knowledge distillation from well-trained ANNs, combined with surrogate gradient training and flexible heterogeneous architectures, will achieve higher accuracy, faster training convergence, and improved noise robustness compared to conventional SNN training or direct ANN-to-SNN conversion methods.
6be6af7596a8f47a5fbf8fa7ab43f7ac7fc44354.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed to construct deep SNNs by leveraging knowledge distillation (KD) from teacher ANNs to student SNNs. The approach will support both response-based and feature-based KD, allowing the student SNN to learn from the output layer or multiple intermediate layers of the teacher ANN. The student SNN will be trained using surrogate gradient methods to address the non-differentiability of spike signals, enabling efficient gradient-based optimization. The framework will allow for heterogeneous architectures between teacher and student models, and will utilize joint loss functions that combine soft targets from the teacher ANN with hard labels, as well as L2 losses for intermediate feature alignment. Training will proceed in two stages: first, pre-training the teacher ANN, then training the student SNN with fixed teacher weights and simultaneous KD guidance.
6be6af7596a8f47a5fbf8fa7ab43f7ac7fc44354.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification datasets, including MNIST and CIFAR10, as well as their noisy variants (e.g., background, rotation, Gaussian noise). Various advanced ANN architectures (e.g., ResNet18, WRN28-4, PyramidNet18) will serve as teacher models, while student SNNs will use corresponding or reduced architectures (e.g., VGG11, WRN16-2, 2conv). Baseline comparisons will include direct SNN training, ANN-to-SNN conversion, and other state-of-the-art SNN training methods. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy, training latency (number of time steps), memory usage, and robustness to noise. The models will be implemented in PyTorch and SpikingJelly, and experiments will be run on high-performance GPU servers.
6be6af7596a8f47a5fbf8fa7ab43f7ac7fc44354.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a flexible knowledge distillation framework for constructing deep SNNs from ANNs, supporting heterogeneous architectures and combining response-based and feature-based distillation. The approach enables efficient training with fewer time steps and lower memory usage, while achieving higher accuracy and improved noise robustness compared to existing SNN training and conversion methods. The method demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets with significant improvements in training efficiency and resource consumption, making it suitable for deployment on neuromorphic hardware.

6c131c77c64bd2af9efaf25ff64e2548935314c1.title: Generalized Sobolev Transport for Probability Measures on a Graph
6c131c77c64bd2af9efaf25ff64e2548935314c1.research_question: How can optimal transport between probability measures supported on a graph be generalized to incorporate flexible geometric structures beyond the standard Lp geometry, while maintaining computational efficiency and enabling practical applications such as document classification and topological data analysis?
6c131c77c64bd2af9efaf25ff64e2548935314c1.hypothesis: A generalized Sobolev transport (GST) framework, leveraging Orlicz geometric structure via a class of convex functions (N-functions), will enable efficient and flexible computation of optimal transport distances on graphs, outperforming existing Orlicz-Wasserstein (OW) and Sobolev transport (ST) methods in both computational speed and practical application accuracy.
6c131c77c64bd2af9efaf25ff64e2548935314c1.proposed_method: A new approach is developed that generalizes the Sobolev transport (ST) for probability measures on a graph by leveraging a family of convex N-functions to define an Orlicz-Sobolev space on the graph. The proposed generalized Sobolev transport (GST) replaces the standard Lp constraint on the critic function with a constraint involving the Orlicz-Sobolev norm, allowing the use of a wide range of geometric structures. The GST distance is formulated as a dual optimization problem, which, unlike the two-level optimization required for Orlicz-Wasserstein (OW) distances, reduces to a univariate optimization problem that can be solved efficiently. The method includes a discrete formulation suitable for measures supported on graph nodes, and preprocessing steps are introduced to efficiently compute required graph structures (e.g., shortest paths, edge sets) for repeated distance calculations.
6c131c77c64bd2af9efaf25ff64e2548935314c1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. For document classification, standard datasets such as TWITTER, RECIPE, CLASSIC, and AMAZON are used, where each document is represented as a probability measure over word embeddings. For topological data analysis (TDA), datasets like Orbit and MPEG7 are employed, with persistence diagrams represented as probability measures. The GST method will be compared against baseline methods including OW (with various N-functions), ST, and OT with graph metric ground cost. Evaluation metrics include classification accuracy using SVMs with kernel matrices derived from the proposed and baseline distances, as well as computational time for distance matrix construction. Experiments will be performed on graphs of varying sizes (number of nodes), and both positive definite and indefinite kernels will be considered. Hyperparameters for kernels and SVMs will be selected via cross-validation.
6c131c77c64bd2af9efaf25ff64e2548935314c1.novelty_claims: The proposed GST framework is the first to generalize Sobolev transport on graphs to arbitrary Orlicz geometric structures, encompassing ST as a special case and connecting to OW. GST enables efficient computation by reducing the problem to a univariate optimization, in contrast to the two-level optimization of OW, and admits a closed-form solution for certain N-functions. Empirical results demonstrate that GST is several orders of magnitude faster than OW and achieves superior or comparable performance in document classification and TDA tasks. The approach provides a practical and theoretically grounded method for scalable optimal transport on graphs with flexible geometric priors.

6c17de3e719c0f4d1df6a16f770c2a9a5f18206f.title: Toward Self-Improvement of LLMs via Imagination, Searching, and Criticizing
6c17de3e719c0f4d1df6a16f770c2a9a5f18206f.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be enabled to self-improve their reasoning and planning capabilities in complex tasks without the need for additional human-annotated data?
6c17de3e719c0f4d1df6a16f770c2a9a5f18206f.hypothesis: Integrating a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS)-based self-improvement loop with LLMs, supported by prompt synthesis and a suite of critic models for feedback, will enable LLMs to autonomously enhance their performance on complex reasoning and planning tasks, achieving results comparable to state-of-the-art models without extra human annotations.
6c17de3e719c0f4d1df6a16f770c2a9a5f18206f.proposed_method: A novel self-improvement framework is proposed for LLMs, comprising three main components: imagination (prompt synthesis), searching (an efficient, option-level MCTS tailored for language tasks), and criticizing (a trio of critic models for feedback). The imagination component synthesizes diverse and challenging prompts to address data scarcity. The searching component employs an option-level MCTS, where each search node represents a sequence of tokens (options), enabling efficient exploration of the vast language action space. Adaptive branching and state merging are introduced to balance search depth and width, and a fast rollout policy using a smaller, specialized language model accelerates simulation. The criticizing component consists of a value function, a process reward model (PRM) for immediate option assessment, and an outcome reward model (ORM) for holistic trajectory evaluation; these critics provide scalar and textual feedback signals to guide the search and policy improvement. The self-improvement loop iteratively collects high-reward trajectories via MCTS, filters them using critic scores, and fine-tunes the LLM policy on these new examples.
6c17de3e719c0f4d1df6a16f770c2a9a5f18206f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on mathematical reasoning tasks using the GSM8K and MATH datasets. The framework will be evaluated using Llama-2-70b and WizardMath-70B-V1.0 as base policy models. Baselines will include proprietary models such as GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Claude-2, Gemini, and PaLM-2, as well as strong open-source models. Evaluation metrics will focus on answer accuracy, computational efficiency (measured by number of MCTS rollouts), and ablation studies on each component (adaptive branching, PRM, ORM, state merge, rollout count). The critic models will be trained on trajectories generated from the policy model, and tool-augmented ORM will be used for more challenging tasks. The self-improvement process will involve multiple rounds of prompt synthesis, MCTS-guided data collection, and policy fine-tuning, with early stopping based on a held-out dev set.
6c17de3e719c0f4d1df6a16f770c2a9a5f18206f.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a novel integration of option-level, adaptive MCTS with LLMs for self-improvement, addressing the unique challenges of data scarcity, large search spaces, and subjective feedback in language tasks. The use of synthesized prompts, adaptive branching, state merging, and a trio of critic models (including process and outcome reward models) for precise feedback is innovative. The approach enables LLMs to self-improve without additional human annotations, achieving significant gains in mathematical reasoning tasks and performance comparable to leading proprietary models. The framework demonstrates that LLMs can continually improve via autonomous search and self-critique, setting a new paradigm for scalable, annotation-free LLM enhancement.

6c20a12376619a3119e53202692b091635ff03c5.title: Backdoor Defense via Decoupling the Training Process
6c20a12376619a3119e53202692b091635ff03c5.research_question: How can the training process of deep neural networks be modified to defend against poisoning-based backdoor attacks, while maintaining high accuracy on benign samples?
6c20a12376619a3119e53202692b091635ff03c5.hypothesis: Decoupling the end-to-end supervised training process into self-supervised feature learning, supervised classifier training, and semi-supervised fine-tuning will prevent the creation of hidden backdoors in DNNs, even when training data is poisoned, and will preserve high accuracy on benign samples.
6c20a12376619a3119e53202692b091635ff03c5.proposed_method: A novel defense framework is proposed that decouples the standard end-to-end supervised training of DNNs into three distinct stages. First, the backbone (feature extractor) of the DNN is trained using self-supervised learning on unlabeled training data, which is expected to prevent the model from learning backdoor trigger patterns due to strong data augmentations and the absence of label information. Second, the parameters of the learned backbone are frozen, and the remaining fully connected layers are trained via standard supervised learning using all labeled training samples. During this stage, high-credible samples are identified based on training loss, using symmetric cross-entropy to better distinguish between benign and poisoned samples. Third, the model undergoes semi-supervised fine-tuning: high-credible samples are used as labeled data, while low-credible samples have their labels removed and are used as unlabeled data, with the entire model fine-tuned using a semi-supervised learning algorithm such as MixMatch. This approach aims to further mitigate the influence of poisoned samples and enhance compatibility between the feature extractor and classifier.
6c20a12376619a3119e53202692b091635ff03c5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on benchmark datasets including CIFAR-10 and a subset of ImageNet, using ResNet-18 as the primary model architecture. The defense will be evaluated against multiple representative backdoor attacks: BadNets, Blended, WaNet, and label-consistent attacks, covering both poison-label and clean-label attack paradigms. Baseline defenses for comparison will include DPSGD, ShrinkPad, Neural Cleanse (NC), and Neural Attention Distillation (NAD), with the latter two requiring a local benign dataset. Evaluation metrics will include Attack Success Rate (ASR) and Benign Accuracy (BA), with lower ASR and higher BA indicating better defense. The poisoning rates and trigger patterns will be set according to established protocols for each attack, and the filtering rate for high-credible samples will be a key hyperparameter. Ablation studies will assess the contribution of each stage and component of the proposed method.
6c20a12376619a3119e53202692b091635ff03c5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a decoupling-based defense pipeline that separates feature extraction and classifier training, leveraging self-supervised learning to purify representations and prevent backdoor triggers from being learned. The integration of label-noise learning for filtering high-credible samples and the use of semi-supervised fine-tuning to mitigate the impact of low-credible (potentially poisoned) samples are novel contributions. The method does not require access to a local benign dataset, unlike several existing defenses, and demonstrates strong resistance to both standard and adaptive backdoor attacks while maintaining high accuracy on benign data.

6c323c535365e1c7cbfd9703cbec3b5650a3346b.title: Model Tells You What to Discard: Adaptive KV Cache Compression for LLMs
6c323c535365e1c7cbfd9703cbec3b5650a3346b.research_question: How can the memory footprint of key-value (KV) cache during generative inference in large language models (LLMs) be reduced without sacrificing generation quality or requiring costly retraining or fine-tuning?
6c323c535365e1c7cbfd9703cbec3b5650a3346b.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that profiling the intrinsic structure of attention modules in LLMs and applying adaptive, attention-head-specific KV cache compression policies can significantly reduce memory usage during inference with negligible impact on generation quality.
6c323c535365e1c7cbfd9703cbec3b5650a3346b.proposed_method: A novel adaptive KV cache compression framework, FastGen, will be developed to reduce the memory footprint of LLMs during generative inference. The approach begins with lightweight model profiling during the prompt encoding phase to identify the structural patterns of each attention head. Based on this profiling, an optimal compression policy is selected for each head from a set of fundamental and hybrid strategies, including retaining only special tokens, punctuation, locality-based eviction, and frequency-based retention of high-attention tokens. During token generation, the KV cache is dynamically managed according to these head-specific policies, evicting or retaining context tokens as dictated by the profiled structure. The method is designed to be plug-and-play, requiring no model retraining or fine-tuning, and introduces minimal computational and memory overhead.
6c323c535365e1c7cbfd9703cbec3b5650a3346b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on Llama1 models (7B, 13B, 30B, and 65B parameters) and their instruction-tuned variants, using a suite of generative benchmarks covering code (HumanEval), math (GSM8k), knowledge (NQ), and reading comprehension (TQA), as well as the AlpacaEval instruction-following benchmark. Baseline comparisons will include full KV cache and non-adaptive fixed compression policies (local, frequent, and hybrid frequency+local). Evaluation metrics will include F1 score for GSM8k, NQ, and TQA, Pass@1 for HumanEval, and GPT-4-based win rate for AlpacaEval. Experiments will be run on NVIDIA A100 and V100 GPUs, with batch sizes up to 16 and sequence lengths up to 16,384 tokens. End-to-end latency and profiling overhead will also be measured to assess practical efficiency gains.
6c323c535365e1c7cbfd9703cbec3b5650a3346b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first adaptive, attention-head-specific KV cache compression method for LLMs that leverages lightweight profiling to tailor compression strategies without retraining. Unlike prior methods, this framework synergistically coordinates diverse eviction policies based on observed attention structures, enabling substantial memory savings and inference acceleration while maintaining high generation quality. The method is plug-and-play, incurs negligible profiling and memory overhead, and demonstrates superior performance to all fixed-policy baselines, especially as model size increases.

6c4b76232bb72897685d19b3d264c6ee3005bc2b.title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
6c4b76232bb72897685d19b3d264c6ee3005bc2b.research_question: How can transfer learning in natural language processing be systematically explored and improved by unifying diverse NLP tasks under a single text-to-text framework, and what are the empirical limits of such an approach when scaling model and data sizes?
6c4b76232bb72897685d19b3d264c6ee3005bc2b.hypothesis: A unified text-to-text Transformer framework, when pre-trained on a large, high-quality, and diverse English corpus and fine-tuned across a wide range of NLP tasks, will achieve state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks, demonstrating the scalability and generality of transfer learning in NLP.
6c4b76232bb72897685d19b3d264c6ee3005bc2b.proposed_method: A unified text-to-text framework will be developed, in which all NLP problems are cast as text-to-text tasks, enabling the use of a single model, objective, and training procedure across diverse tasks such as translation, summarization, question answering, and classification. The core model will be an encoder-decoder Transformer with architectural modifications including simplified layer normalization and relative position embeddings. Pre-training will be performed on a large, cleaned English corpus (the Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus, C4), constructed via extensive filtering heuristics from Common Crawl data. Task-specific prefixes will be prepended to input sequences to indicate the desired task, and all tasks will use a maximum likelihood objective with teacher forcing. Model scalability will be explored by training variants with up to 11 billion parameters using distributed training on TPU pods.
6c4b76232bb72897685d19b3d264c6ee3005bc2b.experiment_details: Experiments will systematically compare pre-training objectives, model architectures, data set variants, and transfer learning approaches across a broad suite of English NLP benchmarks. Downstream tasks include GLUE and SuperGLUE (text classification, NLI, coreference, etc.), CNN/Daily Mail summarization, SQuAD question answering, and WMT English-to-German/French/Romanian translation, with all data sourced from TensorFlow Datasets. Baselines will include prior state-of-the-art models and alternative pre-training/data configurations. Evaluation metrics will be those standard to each benchmark (e.g., accuracy, F1, BLEU, ROUGE, etc.), and experiments will involve both single-task and multi-task fine-tuning, as well as ablations on model and data scale.
6c4b76232bb72897685d19b3d264c6ee3005bc2b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified text-to-text framework that enables direct comparison and transfer across a diverse set of NLP tasks using a single model and training objective. The creation and public release of the Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus (C4) provides a large-scale, high-quality resource for pre-training. The approach systematically explores the effects of model and data scale, pre-training objectives, and architectural variants, pushing the empirical limits of transfer learning in NLP. The framework achieves state-of-the-art results on numerous benchmarks and provides a standardized platform for future research.

6c645c0917d117bd04c2e0a01135f6f64303de68.title: Solving Inverse Problems with Latent Diffusion Models via Hard Data Consistency
6c645c0917d117bd04c2e0a01135f6f64303de68.research_question: How can latent diffusion models be effectively leveraged to solve general inverse problems, including both linear and nonlinear cases, in natural and medical imaging domains while maintaining data consistency and computational efficiency?
6c645c0917d117bd04c2e0a01135f6f64303de68.hypothesis: Incorporating a hard data consistency mechanism and a novel stochastic resampling scheme into the reverse sampling process of latent diffusion models will enable accurate and efficient solutions to a wide range of inverse problems, outperforming existing pixel-space and latent-space diffusion-based methods.
6c645c0917d117bd04c2e0a01135f6f64303de68.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces an algorithm that operates entirely in the latent space of a pre-trained latent diffusion model (LDM). During the reverse diffusion process, hard data consistency is enforced by solving a constrained optimization problem at selected timesteps, ensuring that the reconstructed latent variable produces measurements consistent with the observed data. This optimization is initialized using an estimate derived from the current latent sample to avoid poor local minima. To continue the reverse process after enforcing data consistency, a stochastic resampling scheme is developed, which maps the measurement-consistent latent sample back onto the noisy data manifold. This mapping is performed using a tractable Gaussian posterior that balances prior and data consistency via a tunable variance parameter. The algorithm applies the hard data consistency step selectively, focusing on the latter stages of the reverse process for computational efficiency, and employs early stopping based on noise levels to prevent overfitting.
6c645c0917d117bd04c2e0a01135f6f64303de68.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both natural and medical image datasets. For natural images, datasets such as FFHQ, CelebA-HQ, and LSUN-Bedroom (all at 256x256 resolution) will be used, with pre-trained LDMs (LDM-VQ4) and DDPMs as generative priors. For medical imaging, the AAPM LDCT dataset will be used, with LDMs fine-tuned on CT images. Inverse problems to be addressed include Gaussian deblurring, nonlinear deblurring, inpainting, super-resolution, and CT reconstruction, all with additive Gaussian measurement noise. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines including DPS, MCG, DDRM, DMPS, ADMM-PnP, Latent-DPS, PSLD-LDM, FBP, FBP-UNet, and PnP-UNet. Evaluation metrics will include LPIPS, PSNR, and SSIM. Experiments will also include ablation studies on the resampling technique and analysis of memory efficiency.
6c645c0917d117bd04c2e0a01135f6f64303de68.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel hard data consistency mechanism for latent diffusion models, replacing traditional gradient-based updates with a constrained optimization approach. A new stochastic resampling scheme is developed to reliably map measurement-consistent latent samples back onto the noisy data manifold, with theoretical analysis demonstrating reduced variance and unbiasedness. The method enables efficient and accurate solutions to both linear and nonlinear inverse problems in both natural and medical imaging, achieving state-of-the-art performance and improved computational efficiency compared to existing pixel-space and latent-space diffusion-based approaches.

6c67e17fdd763f212e582f8de56b56dd5ed58832.title: Keep the Cost Down: A Review on Methods to Optimize LLM' s KV-Cache Consumption
6c67e17fdd763f212e582f8de56b56dd5ed58832.research_question: How can the memory consumption and efficiency of large language models (LLMs) be optimized by improving the management and compression of the key-value (KV) cache, particularly for long-context inference, without significantly degrading model performance?
6c67e17fdd763f212e582f8de56b56dd5ed58832.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a combination of architectural modifications, inference-time system optimizations, and post-training strategies such as eviction, merging, and quantization can significantly reduce KV cache memory usage and improve inference efficiency in LLMs, while maintaining acceptable levels of model capability and accuracy.
6c67e17fdd763f212e582f8de56b56dd5ed58832.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed to optimize the KV cache consumption in LLMs across three stages: pre-training, deployment, and post-training. In the pre-training stage, architectural modifications such as Multi-Query Attention (MQA), Grouped Query Attention (GQA), and inter-layer KV reuse will be explored to reduce the size of stored KV pairs. During deployment, system-level optimizations like PagedAttention, distributed KV cache across servers, and cross-dialogue KV cache reuse will be implemented to improve memory allocation and throughput. In the post-training phase, dynamic and static eviction policies, token merging strategies, and advanced quantization techniques (e.g., per-channel, per-token, and mixed-precision quantization) will be applied to further compress the KV cache. Each component will be integrated and evaluated for compatibility and cumulative benefit.
6c67e17fdd763f212e582f8de56b56dd5ed58832.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using both long-context benchmarks (such as LongBench, ZeroSCROLLS, L-Eval, BAMBOO, XL2bench, InfiniteBench, and LooGLE) and key retrieval tasks (including Needle in a Haystack, Passkey Retrieval, and RULER) to assess the impact of KV cache optimizations. Baseline comparisons will include standard LLMs with unoptimized KV caches, as well as state-of-the-art compression and eviction methods. Evaluation metrics will encompass per-token GPU memory usage, throughput (tokens per second), latency (milliseconds per token), and perplexity (PPL) to measure both efficiency and model capability. Additional experiments will simulate few-shot and multi-turn dialogue scenarios to test generalizability.
6c67e17fdd763f212e582f8de56b56dd5ed58832.novelty_claims: The proposed research offers a unified and systematic approach to KV cache optimization, spanning architectural, system, and algorithmic innovations. It introduces the integration of multi-stage compression and management techniques, including novel combinations of eviction, merging, and quantization strategies tailored for LLMs. The work also proposes new evaluation protocols for long-context efficiency and capability trade-offs, and explores the potential of external storage and retrieval mechanisms for KV cache as a future direction. This comprehensive perspective aims to set new standards for sustainable and scalable LLM deployment.

6c6d2ac4f7c94b30ceef79ba3e72840d0f4ba1d0.title: Direct Preference Optimization for Neural Machine Translation with Minimum Bayes Risk Decoding
6c6d2ac4f7c94b30ceef79ba3e72840d0f4ba1d0.research_question: Can neural machine translation models be fine-tuned to achieve the translation quality of minimum Bayes risk (MBR) decoding using only single-pass decoding, thereby eliminating the computational overhead of MBR at inference time? How effective is preference-based fine-tuning in aligning model outputs with MBR-decoded preferences across multiple language pairs and test sets?
6c6d2ac4f7c94b30ceef79ba3e72840d0f4ba1d0.hypothesis: Fine-tuning multilingual large language models (MLLMs) using a direct preference optimization (DPO) objective on MBR-ranked translation hypotheses will enable the models to produce translations with single-pass decoding that match or exceed the quality of MBR decoding, as measured by standard translation metrics, without requiring additional computation at inference.
6c6d2ac4f7c94b30ceef79ba3e72840d0f4ba1d0.proposed_method: A novel fine-tuning framework is proposed that combines minimum Bayes risk (MBR) decoding with direct preference optimization (DPO) to align neural machine translation models with MBR preferences. First, a base MLLM generates a set of translation hypotheses for each source sentence using ancestral sampling. These hypotheses are scored and ranked according to their MBR scores, using a utility function such as BLEURT. Preference triplets are constructed by selecting pairs (or triplets) of translations from the ranked hypotheses, where one translation is preferred over another based on the MBR score. The DPO algorithm is then used to fine-tune the model, optimizing it to increase the likelihood of preferred translations over less preferred ones, with a KL-regularization term controlling divergence from the base model. Several strategies for preference pair selection (e.g., best-vs-worst, best-middle-worst, consecutive pairs, and strided pairs) are explored to construct the training data for DPO.
6c6d2ac4f7c94b30ceef79ba3e72840d0f4ba1d0.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the WMT21 and WMT22 news translation test sets for Chinese-English and English-Chinese, as well as the IWSLT2017 test set for French-English and English-French. The base models used are BLOOMZ and BLOOMZ-mt (7.1B parameters), with both unsupervised and supervised fine-tuning variants. For DPO fine-tuning, only monolingual source text is used, and reference translations are not required. Evaluation metrics include BLEU, BLEURT, and COMET-22, with BLEURT and COMET serving as primary indicators of translation quality. Baselines include the base models decoded with beam search and MBR (with varying hypothesis set sizes), as well as supervised fine-tuned models. The impact of DPO hyperparameters (e.g., KL-regularization beta), preference pair selection strategies, and hypothesis set size is systematically studied. Fine-tuning is performed for one epoch using the RMSProp optimizer, and results are reported on held-out test sets with no overlap with fine-tuning data.
6c6d2ac4f7c94b30ceef79ba3e72840d0f4ba1d0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces an unsupervised preference optimization method that leverages MBR-ranked translation hypotheses to teach MLLMs MBR-like preferences through DPO fine-tuning, enabling single-pass decoding with translation quality on par with or better than traditional MBR decoding. Unlike prior methods, this approach does not require reference translations or human feedback, and it utilizes sets of ranked samples rather than only final MBR outputs, allowing the model to learn richer ranking preferences. The method is robust to different preference pair selection strategies and requires fewer hypotheses for fine-tuning than for MBR decoding, improving both efficiency and translation quality. This framework represents a significant step toward practical, high-quality neural machine translation with reduced inference cost.

6c8c3919863022645809db47489c72e0cd3b959a.title: Learnable Polyphase Sampling for Shift Invariant and Equivariant Convolutional Networks
6c8c3919863022645809db47489c72e0cd3b959a.research_question: How can convolutional neural networks be designed to achieve true shift-invariance and shift-equivariance in tasks such as image classification and semantic segmentation, while maintaining or improving model performance and consistency?
6c8c3919863022645809db47489c72e0cd3b959a.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a pair of learnable downsampling and upsampling layers, which generalize existing handcrafted polyphase sampling methods and are trained end-to-end, can achieve true shift-invariance and shift-equivariance in convolutional networks, leading to improved or comparable performance and consistency over existing anti-aliasing and adaptive sampling approaches.
6c8c3919863022645809db47489c72e0cd3b959a.proposed_method: A novel framework, Learnable Polyphase Sampling (LPS), is introduced, consisting of learnable downsampling (LPD) and upsampling (LPU) layers that can be integrated into any convolutional network by replacing standard pooling or striding layers. The LPD layer models the conditional probability of selecting each polyphase component using a small neural network, ensuring shift-permutation equivariance by sharing weights and applying global pooling over polyphase components. The selection is made differentiable via Gumbel-Softmax, allowing end-to-end training. LPU reconstructs the upsampled feature map by placing downsampled features back into their original spatial locations, with anti-aliasing applied post-upsampling to mitigate high-frequency artifacts. Both LPD and LPU are designed to guarantee shift-invariance and shift-equivariance, and the method theoretically generalizes existing handcrafted adaptive polyphase sampling (APS) rules.
6c8c3919863022645809db47489c72e0cd3b959a.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on image classification tasks using ResNet-18, ResNet-50, and ResNet-101 architectures on CIFAR10 and ImageNet datasets, with both circular and standard shift settings. Semantic segmentation is evaluated on the PASCAL VOC dataset using DeepLabV3+ with ResNet backbones. Baselines include standard pooling, anti-aliasing methods (LPF, DDAC), and APS. Evaluation metrics include classification accuracy, circular consistency (C-Cons.), shift consistency (S-Cons.), mean intersection-over-union (mIoU), and mean Average Segmentation Circular Consistency (mASCC/mASSC). Experiments also report trainable parameters and inference time to assess computational overhead. Multiple random seeds and shift pairs are used for robust evaluation.
6c8c3919863022645809db47489c72e0cd3b959a.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first pair of end-to-end trainable downsampling and upsampling layers that guarantee true shift-invariance and shift-equivariance in convolutional networks. LPS generalizes the handcrafted APS approach, enabling data-driven learning of optimal sampling schemes. The approach achieves, for the first time, 100% shift consistency on semantic segmentation benchmarks, and consistently matches or outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both accuracy and shift consistency, with minimal computational overhead.

6c943670dca38bfc7c8b477ae7c2d1fba1ad3691.title: Program of Thoughts Prompting: Disentangling Computation from Reasoning for Numerical Reasoning Tasks
6c943670dca38bfc7c8b477ae7c2d1fba1ad3691.research_question: How can the separation of computation from reasoning improve the performance of large language models on complex numerical reasoning tasks, such as math word problems and financial question answering, across diverse input formats and settings?
6c943670dca38bfc7c8b477ae7c2d1fba1ad3691.hypothesis: Delegating computation to an external program interpreter, while using language models to generate step-by-step reasoning as executable code, will significantly improve accuracy and robustness on numerical reasoning tasks compared to approaches where language models perform both reasoning and computation.
6c943670dca38bfc7c8b477ae7c2d1fba1ad3691.proposed_method: A novel prompting framework, Program of Thoughts (PoT), will be developed to disentangle reasoning from computation in numerical reasoning tasks. In this approach, large language models (LLMs) are prompted to express their reasoning processes as step-by-step Python programs, using semantically meaningful variable names to bind language and computation. The generated code is then executed by an external Python interpreter (with libraries such as SymPy) to carry out precise calculations and derive final answers. The method will support both few-shot and zero-shot prompting, with prompt engineering strategies to encourage program generation over natural language comments. For problems requiring additional textual reasoning, a hybrid approach will be used, where PoT generates intermediate computational results that are then combined with chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning for final answer derivation.
6c943670dca38bfc7c8b477ae7c2d1fba1ad3691.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on eight publicly available datasets covering math word problems (GSM8K, AQuA, SVAMP, MultiArith, TabMWP) and financial QA (FinQA, ConvFinQA, TATQA), with diverse input modalities including text, tables, and conversations. Both few-shot (4-8 exemplars) and zero-shot settings will be evaluated, using OpenAI Codex (code-davinci-002) as the primary LLM, and additional ablations with GPT-3, gpt-3.5-turbo, CodeGen, CodeT5+, and XGen. Inputs such as tables and conversations will be linearized for prompt construction. Evaluation metrics include exact match accuracy (with rounding as needed) and official scripts for financial datasets, with self-consistency decoding (majority vote over 40 completions) used to assess upper-bound performance. Baselines will include direct answer prompting, chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting, CoT with external calculator, and state-of-the-art published results. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of semantic variable binding, multi-step reasoning, prompt sensitivity, and backbone model choice.
6c943670dca38bfc7c8b477ae7c2d1fba1ad3691.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new paradigm for numerical reasoning with LLMs by explicitly disentangling reasoning (expressed as code) from computation (delegated to an interpreter), overcoming LLMs' limitations in arithmetic accuracy, complex equation solving, and iterative processes. The approach demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over chain-of-thought prompting across all evaluated datasets and settings, especially in tasks requiring complex or high-precision computation. Additional innovations include prompt engineering to suppress comment generation, hybrid PoT+CoT reasoning for multi-stage problems, and comprehensive ablation analyses revealing the importance of semantic binding and multi-step decomposition. The method achieves state-of-the-art or near state-of-the-art results on a wide range of benchmarks, highlighting its generalizability and robustness.

6c9eb7bf7d4c372771f806b1b90a87aa98454a2c.title: Scalable Deep Reinforcement Learning Algorithms for Mean Field Games
6c9eb7bf7d4c372771f806b1b90a87aa98454a2c.research_question: How can scalable deep reinforcement learning algorithms be developed to efficiently compute Nash equilibria in mean field games (MFGs) with large state and action spaces, particularly when using non-linear function approximators such as neural networks?
6c9eb7bf7d4c372771f806b1b90a87aa98454a2c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that novel deep reinforcement learning algorithms, specifically designed to address the challenges of mixing and averaging non-linear function approximations, can efficiently solve dynamic mean field games and outperform existing state-of-the-art baselines in terms of convergence and exploitability.
6c9eb7bf7d4c372771f806b1b90a87aa98454a2c.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves the development of two scalable deep reinforcement learning algorithms for mean field games. The first approach, Deep Average-network Fictitious Play (D-AFP), leverages a neural network to learn an average policy by distilling historical best responses into a single model, inspired by the Neural Fictitious Self Play (NFSP) framework. This method maintains a buffer of state-action pairs from past best responses and trains the average policy via supervised learning to minimize categorical loss. The second approach, Deep Munchausen Online Mirror Descent (D-MOMD), introduces a novel reparameterization of the Online Mirror Descent (OMD) algorithm using the Munchausen trick, allowing the implicit computation of a sum of Q-functions without the need to store or sum multiple neural networks. D-MOMD utilizes a regularized Bellman update and trains a neural Q-network using a modified loss that incorporates penalization for policy deviation and an entropy term, thus enabling stable and memory-efficient learning. Both methods are designed for finite-horizon, discrete state and action MFGs, and are compatible with standard deep RL architectures such as DQN.
6c9eb7bf7d4c372771f806b1b90a87aa98454a2c.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a suite of benchmark mean field game environments, including a toy epidemics model (SIS), a discretized linear-quadratic MFG, high-dimensional grid world settings with crowd aversion and congestion, and a multi-population chasing scenario. The proposed algorithms are compared against several baselines: Deep Banach-Picard (D-BP) fixed point iterations, Deep Policy Iteration (D-PI), Deep Boltzmann Iteration (D-BI), and a regularized deep RL method from recent literature. Evaluation metrics include exploitability (the improvement in reward a player can achieve by deviating from the population policy), convergence speed, and Wasserstein distance to benchmark distributions. Hyperparameters are tuned via sweeps, and results are reported for the best-performing configurations. Both tabular and deep RL (neural network) implementations are considered, with experiments demonstrating scalability to large state spaces.
6c9eb7bf7d4c372771f806b1b90a87aa98454a2c.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first scalable implementation of Fictitious Play for mean field games that does not require storing all previous best responses, instead learning an average policy with a single neural network. It also presents a novel Munchausen-based reparameterization of Online Mirror Descent, enabling implicit and stable learning of cumulative Q-functions without explicit summation or memory overhead. The methods are claimed to outperform state-of-the-art baselines in terms of exploitability and convergence across a variety of dynamic MFG benchmarks, and to be applicable in both model-free and model-based settings. These innovations address key scalability and stability challenges in applying deep RL to mean field games.

6caa7cce613702a2b204642e2324c61598921e56.title: ST-P3: End-to-end Vision-based Autonomous Driving via Spatial-Temporal Feature Learning
6caa7cce613702a2b204642e2324c61598921e56.research_question: How can an interpretable end-to-end vision-based autonomous driving system be designed to jointly optimize perception, prediction, and planning tasks using spatial-temporal feature learning, and how does such a system perform compared to existing state-of-the-art approaches?
6caa7cce613702a2b204642e2324c61598921e56.hypothesis: A vision-based end-to-end autonomous driving framework that incorporates joint spatial-temporal feature learning, including egocentric-aligned accumulation, dual-pathway probabilistic modeling, and prior-knowledge-based planning refinement, will yield more representative features and improved performance across perception, prediction, and planning tasks, achieving or surpassing state-of-the-art results.
6caa7cce613702a2b204642e2324c61598921e56.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces an interpretable end-to-end vision-based framework for autonomous driving, termed ST-P3, which processes raw multi-view camera inputs to jointly optimize perception, prediction, and planning. For perception, an egocentric-aligned accumulation technique is employed, aligning and aggregating past and current features in 3D space before transforming them into bird’s eye view (BEV) representations, preserving geometric information. For prediction, a dual-pathway probabilistic modeling approach is used, where one pathway models future uncertainty as a diagonal Gaussian and the other incorporates motion variations from the past, both feeding into a GRU-based temporal model to predict future semantic and instance segmentation. For planning, a cost-based trajectory sampler is utilized, integrating prior knowledge from perception and prediction modules, and further refining the selected trajectory using a GRU network that incorporates vision-based cues such as traffic lights and high-level navigation commands, without reliance on HD maps. The entire system is trained end-to-end with task-specific losses for perception, prediction, and planning, with learnable weights to balance multi-task optimization.
6caa7cce613702a2b204642e2324c61598921e56.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both the open-loop nuScenes dataset and the closed-loop CARLA simulator to comprehensively evaluate the proposed framework. The system will be benchmarked against state-of-the-art baselines, including both LiDAR-based and vision-based approaches, using standard metrics for perception (semantic and instance segmentation accuracy), prediction (future flow and centerness), and planning (trajectory safety, comfort, and progress). The experimental setup will include ablation studies to assess the impact of each proposed module (egocentric accumulation, dual-pathway modeling, and planning refinement), and the evaluation will consider both the interpretability and robustness of the system in diverse driving scenarios.
6caa7cce613702a2b204642e2324c61598921e56.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces three novel components for spatial-temporal feature learning in vision-based autonomous driving: egocentric-aligned accumulation for perception, dual-pathway probabilistic modeling for prediction, and a prior-knowledge-based refinement module for planning. This is the first systematic investigation and detailed analysis of an interpretable end-to-end vision-based pipeline that jointly addresses perception, prediction, and planning, serving as a vision-based counterpart to prior LiDAR-based studies. The proposed framework is claimed to achieve state-of-the-art performance on established benchmarks, with all code and protocols to be made publicly available.

6cb35dd6e1338faa0c3d6a6b0020bbcbcc18653d.title: Sophia: A Scalable Stochastic Second-order Optimizer for Language Model Pre-training
6cb35dd6e1338faa0c3d6a6b0020bbcbcc18653d.research_question: How can the efficiency of large language model (LLM) pre-training be improved through the development of a more effective and scalable optimization algorithm, while maintaining or improving model performance?
6cb35dd6e1338faa0c3d6a6b0020bbcbcc18653d.hypothesis: A stochastic second-order optimizer that uses a lightweight diagonal Hessian estimate as a pre-conditioner, combined with per-coordinate clipping, will significantly reduce the number of training steps, total compute, and wall-clock time required for LLM pre-training compared to state-of-the-art first-order optimizers such as AdamW, without incurring substantial per-step overhead.
6cb35dd6e1338faa0c3d6a6b0020bbcbcc18653d.proposed_method: A novel stochastic second-order optimization algorithm, Sophia, will be developed for LLM pre-training. The method will maintain an exponential moving average (EMA) of gradients and a lightweight stochastic estimate of the diagonal Hessian, updated every k steps (e.g., k=10), using either Hutchinson's unbiased estimator (requiring Hessian-vector products) or a Gauss-Newton-Bartlett estimator (leveraging model structure and resampled labels). The optimizer will compute parameter updates by dividing the EMA of the gradient by the EMA of the diagonal Hessian estimate, followed by element-wise clipping to control the worst-case update size and ensure stability in the presence of non-convexity or rapidly changing curvature. The method will be designed for seamless integration into existing deep learning frameworks and will require minimal additional memory or computation per step.
6cb35dd6e1338faa0c3d6a6b0020bbcbcc18653d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on auto-regressive language modeling tasks using GPT-2 models (125M, 355M, 770M parameters) trained on OpenWebText and GPT NeoX models (1.5B, 6.6B parameters) trained on The Pile. The proposed optimizer will be compared against AdamW, AdaHessian, and Lion, with hyperparameters tuned via grid search or transferred across model sizes. Evaluation metrics will include validation loss, number of training steps to reach a target loss, total compute (FLOPs), and wall-clock time. Batch sizes, learning rate schedules, and other training details will be standardized across methods, and experiments will be run on both GPU and TPU hardware. The primary comparison will focus on the number of steps and compute required to achieve the same validation loss as baselines.
6cb35dd6e1338faa0c3d6a6b0020bbcbcc18653d.novelty_claims: The proposed optimizer introduces a scalable, stochastic second-order method for LLM pre-training that uses a lightweight diagonal Hessian estimate as a pre-conditioner, updated infrequently to minimize overhead. The element-wise clipping mechanism ensures stability and robustness to non-convexity and inaccurate curvature estimates, enabling aggressive adaptation to heterogeneous parameter curvatures. Unlike prior second-order optimizers, the method achieves substantial speed-ups (up to 2x) in both number of steps and total compute for large-scale language models, and is the first to demonstrate such gains in wall-clock time and compute on decoder-only LLMs. The optimizer is also designed for easy integration into existing training pipelines without architectural or infrastructure changes.

6cc09d65220277637afd21f5b2a6ac7224f40656.title: Accelerated Linearized Laplace Approximation for Bayesian Deep Learning
6cc09d65220277637afd21f5b2a6ac7224f40656.research_question: How can the scalability and fidelity of linearized Laplace approximation for Bayesian deep learning be improved to enable efficient and reliable uncertainty quantification in large-scale neural networks, including modern architectures such as vision transformers?
6cc09d65220277637afd21f5b2a6ac7224f40656.hypothesis: Introducing a principled kernel approximation to the neural tangent kernel within the linearized Laplace approximation framework, specifically via the Nyström method, will enable significant acceleration and scalability improvements without sacrificing the fidelity of uncertainty quantification in Bayesian neural networks.
6cc09d65220277637afd21f5b2a6ac7224f40656.proposed_method: A new approach is developed that accelerates the linearized Laplace approximation (LLA) for Bayesian deep learning by leveraging a Nyström approximation to the neural tangent kernel (NTK). The method constructs low-dimensional explicit representations of the NTK using the Nyström method, which involves sampling a subset of data points, computing the Jacobians of the neural network outputs with respect to parameters, and performing eigendecomposition to obtain principal components. These components are then used to approximate the NTK as an inner product in a reduced space, allowing the predictive covariance of the LLA to be computed efficiently. Forward-mode automatic differentiation is utilized to efficiently compute the required Jacobian-vector products, and the resulting method, termed ELLA, avoids the need to explicitly compute or store large generalized Gauss-Newton or Jacobian matrices. Theoretical analysis is provided to bound the approximation error between the accelerated method and the original LLA, showing that the error decreases as the Nyström approximation improves.
6cc09d65220277637afd21f5b2a6ac7224f40656.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard regression and image classification benchmarks, including MNIST, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet, using various neural network architectures such as multilayer perceptrons, ResNets, and vision transformers. Baselines will include maximum a posteriori (MAP) inference, mean-field variational inference with Bayesian finetuning (MFVI-BF), last-layer and full LLA with diagonal and Kronecker-factored (KFAC) approximations, and other Gaussian approximate posteriors. Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy, negative log-likelihood (NLL), expected calibration error (ECE), and robustness to out-of-distribution and corrupted data. Hyperparameters such as the number of Nyström samples and retained eigenpairs will be systematically varied, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of these choices. Computational efficiency and scalability will be measured by wall-clock time and memory usage during prediction.
6cc09d65220277637afd21f5b2a6ac7224f40656.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a principled and theoretically grounded acceleration of linearized Laplace approximation for Bayesian deep learning by employing the Nyström method to approximate the neural tangent kernel. This approach enables efficient and scalable uncertainty quantification in large-scale neural networks, including architectures previously intractable for LLA, such as vision transformers. The method preserves the core structure of LLA while eliminating the need for restrictive diagonal or last-layer approximations, and provides theoretical guarantees on the approximation error. Empirical results demonstrate superior performance in terms of calibration, robustness, and computational efficiency compared to existing baselines.

6cf1116dc8b431b2471bb5407d9a8be0eb067c2d.title: Deep Partition Aggregation: Provable Defense against General Poisoning Attacks
6cf1116dc8b431b2471bb5407d9a8be0eb067c2d.research_question: How can machine learning models be provided with provable, deterministic defenses against general and label-flipping poisoning attacks, particularly in the context of deep neural networks and under broad threat models involving insertion, deletion, or modification of training data or labels?
6cf1116dc8b431b2471bb5407d9a8be0eb067c2d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that partitioning the training data and aggregating predictions from multiple base classifiers, each trained on disjoint partitions determined by deterministic functions, can provide certifiable robustness against general and label-flipping poisoning attacks. Furthermore, leveraging semi-supervised learning for base classifiers will enhance certified robustness against label-flipping attacks.
6cf1116dc8b431b2471bb5407d9a8be0eb067c2d.proposed_method: A novel ensemble-based defense framework, Deep Partition Aggregation (DPA), will be developed to provide certifiable robustness against general poisoning attacks. The method involves partitioning the training set into k disjoint subsets using a deterministic hash function, training a separate base classifier (e.g., a deep neural network) on each partition, and aggregating their predictions via plurality voting for inference. To ensure determinism and robustness, the partitioning is based solely on sample values, and training procedures are made order-invariant and deterministic. For label-flipping attacks, a Semi-Supervised DPA (SS-DPA) variant will be introduced, where each base classifier is trained using all unlabeled data and only the labeled samples from its partition, leveraging semi-supervised learning algorithms and unsupervised feature embeddings. The partitioning for SS-DPA is performed by sorting unlabeled samples to maintain invariance under label flips, and the aggregation mechanism remains plurality voting.
6cf1116dc8b431b2471bb5407d9a8be0eb067c2d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and GTSRB datasets. For DPA, supervised deep neural networks (e.g., Network-In-Network) will be used as base classifiers, while for SS-DPA, semi-supervised learning algorithms such as RotNet (for MNIST) and SimCLR (for CIFAR-10 and GTSRB) will be employed to learn feature embeddings, followed by linear or deep classifiers for each partition. Baselines will include the state-of-the-art certified defense for label-flipping attacks (Rosenfeld et al., 2020). Evaluation metrics will focus on certified accuracy as a function of attack magnitude (number of poisoned samples or label flips), as well as median certified robustness (the attack size at which at least 50% of test samples are certifiably robust). Training time per partition and clean accuracy will also be reported. The number of partitions (k) will be varied to study the trade-off between robustness and accuracy.
6cf1116dc8b431b2471bb5407d9a8be0eb067c2d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first deterministic, provable defense against general poisoning attacks, including arbitrary insertions and deletions of training samples, and provides substantially improved certified robustness against label-flipping attacks compared to existing methods. The method supports deep neural networks as base classifiers and yields exact, deterministic certificates rather than probabilistic guarantees. The semi-supervised variant leverages unsupervised feature learning to further enhance robustness against label-flipping, outperforming prior certified defenses and enabling scalability to datasets with many classes.

6cf8b36e5ef8787238cf96b336dbb7824b8a4790.title: Swift4D:Adaptive divide-and-conquer Gaussian Splatting for compact and efficient reconstruction of dynamic scene
6cf8b36e5ef8787238cf96b336dbb7824b8a4790.research_question: How can dynamic scene reconstruction and novel view synthesis be made more efficient and compact, while maintaining or improving rendering quality, particularly by addressing the differing requirements of static and dynamic scene elements?
6cf8b36e5ef8787238cf96b336dbb7824b8a4790.hypothesis: Separating scene primitives into dynamic and static components and applying temporal modeling only to dynamic elements will significantly reduce computational and storage requirements, accelerate training, and improve rendering quality for dynamic scene reconstruction.
6cf8b36e5ef8787238cf96b336dbb7824b8a4790.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces an adaptive divide-and-conquer framework for 3D Gaussian Splatting, termed Swift4D, which decomposes scene primitives into static and dynamic groups using a learnable parameter trained from multi-view 2D images. Dynamic primitives are identified via a dynamic-static mask derived from temporal pixel variance, and only these undergo temporal modeling. For dynamic points, a compact multi-resolution 4D hash encoder, combined with multi-head MLP decoders, transforms canonical space parameters into deformation space at each timestamp, capturing spatio-temporal changes efficiently. Static points remain temporally invariant, reducing the model's complexity and storage needs. The final rendered output is generated by mixing the deformed dynamic and static primitives, with additional temporal importance pruning to remove redundant or low-impact Gaussians.
6cf8b36e5ef8787238cf96b336dbb7824b8a4790.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several multi-view dynamic scene datasets, including N3DV, Meet Room, and Basketball Court, using established training and testing splits. The method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as DyNeRF, HexPlane, K-Planes, 4DGS, 3DGStream, SpaceTimeGS, and Real-Time 4DGS. Evaluation metrics will include PSNR, DSSIM, LPIPS for rendering quality, total training time, model storage size, and frames per second (FPS) for rendering speed. Ablation studies will assess the impact of dynamic-static decomposition, encoder choices, and pruning strategies. All experiments will be run on high-end GPUs, and training protocols will include initialization from COLMAP-generated point clouds, staged optimization of dynamic parameters, and spatio-temporal structure learning.
6cf8b36e5ef8787238cf96b336dbb7824b8a4790.novelty_claims: The method introduces a novel, learnable decomposition of scene primitives into dynamic and static components, enabling selective temporal modeling and reducing unnecessary computation. It leverages a compact multi-resolution 4D hash encoder and multi-head decoder for efficient and expressive spatio-temporal modeling of dynamic elements. The approach achieves state-of-the-art rendering quality with significantly reduced training time (up to 20× faster) and storage (as low as 30MB), and incorporates a new temporal importance pruning strategy to further improve compactness and remove artifacts. The decomposition technique is robust, adaptable, and can serve as a plug-and-play module for other dynamic scene reconstruction frameworks.

6cff9cec509a86f6cdf678bd39c48a7b191e459d.title: Aligned Multi Objective Optimization
6cff9cec509a86f6cdf678bd39c48a7b191e459d.research_question: Can gradient-based optimization algorithms be improved by leveraging multi-objective feedback when the objectives are aligned, and what frameworks and algorithms can systematically exploit such alignment to achieve faster or more robust convergence in machine learning tasks?
6cff9cec509a86f6cdf678bd39c48a7b191e459d.hypothesis: Gradient descent-type algorithms that adaptively weight aligned multi-objective feedback will achieve provably faster and more robust convergence compared to standard or naive approaches that do not exploit objective alignment.
6cff9cec509a86f6cdf678bd39c48a7b191e459d.proposed_method: A novel framework, Aligned Multi-Objective Optimization (AMOO), will be developed to formalize and exploit the setting where multiple convex objectives share a common minimizer. Two new adaptive weighting algorithms will be proposed: CAMOO (Curvature-Aligned Multi-Objective Optimizer) and PAMOO (Polyak-Aligned Multi-Objective Optimizer). CAMOO adaptively selects weight vectors at each iteration to maximize the local curvature of the weighted objective, using Hessian information (or diagonal approximations for scalability), and applies gradient descent steps in the direction of steepest curvature. PAMOO generalizes the Polyak step-size approach to the multi-objective setting, requiring only gradient information and solving a convex quadratic optimization problem to select weights that maximize local progress toward the shared optimum. Both algorithms will be theoretically analyzed for convergence guarantees, including robustness to approximate alignment (ϵ-AMOO), and practical scalable implementations will be provided for high-dimensional deep learning models.
6cff9cec509a86f6cdf678bd39c48a7b191e459d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic multi-objective optimization problems where the objectives are either exactly or approximately aligned. Neural network-based toy tasks will be used, such as matching the outputs of a fixed network with a trainable network under several convex loss functions, varying curvature and alignment properties. CAMOO, PAMOO, and a baseline equal-weighting approach will be compared using stochastic gradient descent and Adam optimizers. Evaluation metrics will include mean squared error (MSE) between network outputs and convergence rate (number of steps to reach a threshold error). Additional experiments will investigate the effect of Hessian diagonal approximation and the robustness of the algorithms under ϵ-alignment violations.
6cff9cec509a86f6cdf678bd39c48a7b191e459d.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first optimization-centric framework and algorithms for exploiting aligned multi-objective feedback, moving beyond the traditional focus on conflicting objectives and Pareto optimality. CAMOO and PAMOO provide provable, instance-dependent convergence guarantees that improve upon worst-case rates of prior multi-task learning and multi-objective optimization methods. Theoretical analysis establishes new structural quantities (global and local adaptive strong convexity) that characterize when and how alignment can accelerate convergence. The methods are scalable, robust to approximate alignment, and applicable to large-scale machine learning problems with many related objectives, representing a significant advancement in multi-objective optimization methodology.

6d017adda6b2b1ea627dde2f0e85401ebb9fe566.title: MathVerse: Does Your Multi-modal LLM Truly See the Diagrams in Visual Math Problems?
