6d017adda6b2b1ea627dde2f0e85401ebb9fe566.research_question: How can the genuine visual mathematical reasoning capabilities of multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) be rigorously and equitably evaluated, particularly in their ability to interpret diagrams in mathematical problems, beyond reliance on textual cues?
6d017adda6b2b1ea627dde2f0e85401ebb9fe566.hypothesis: Current multi-modal large language models do not truly interpret visual diagrams in mathematical problems and instead rely heavily on redundant textual information; a benchmark with systematically varied multi-modal content and a fine-grained reasoning evaluation will more accurately reveal their visual mathematical reasoning abilities.
6d017adda6b2b1ea627dde2f0e85401ebb9fe566.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark, MATHVERSE, will be developed to evaluate MLLMs on visual mathematical reasoning. The dataset will consist of 2,612 high-quality, multi-subject math problems with diagrams, each transformed into six distinct versions that systematically vary the amount and type of textual and visual information (from text-dominant to vision-only). Problems will be categorized into three main subjects (plane geometry, solid geometry, and functions) and further divided into twelve fine-grained categories. To assess reasoning, a Chain-of-Thought (CoT) evaluation strategy will be implemented: GPT-4 will extract key reasoning steps from model outputs without access to the original question or answer, and GPT-4V will then score each step and the final answer, providing detailed error analysis and a composite score that balances intermediate reasoning and final correctness.
6d017adda6b2b1ea627dde2f0e85401ebb9fe566.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of MLLMs, including both closed-source (e.g., GPT-4V, Gemini-Pro, Qwen-VL-Max) and open-source models (e.g., LLaVA-1.5, SPHINX-MoE, InternLM-XComposer2), as well as text-only LLMs (e.g., ChatGPT, GPT-4) as baselines. The evaluation will use the full MATHVERSE dataset and a representative test subset, with each model assessed on all six problem versions. Evaluation metrics will include both accuracy and the proposed CoT-based fine-grained reasoning score. Human performance will also be measured as a baseline. All models will be evaluated in a zero-shot setting, and random chance baselines will be included for comparison.
6d017adda6b2b1ea627dde2f0e85401ebb9fe566.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a holistic visual math benchmark that systematically varies multi-modal content to isolate and assess genuine diagram interpretation. It pioneers a fine-grained Chain-of-Thought evaluation strategy using GPT-4 and GPT-4V to score intermediate reasoning steps, moving beyond binary answer correctness. The benchmark covers a broad and diverse set of mathematical subjects and problem types, enabling nuanced analysis of MLLM capabilities. This approach addresses key limitations of existing benchmarks, such as textual redundancy and lack of stepwise reasoning assessment, and provides actionable insights for advancing multi-modal mathematical reasoning in large language models.

6d0e40228118db3aea1b25bc95ba3556fa9ff644.title: Federated In-Context Learning: Iterative Refinement for Improved Answer Quality
6d0e40228118db3aea1b25bc95ba3556fa9ff644.research_question: How can in-context learning for question-answering tasks be improved in distributed, privacy-sensitive environments where high-quality examples are scarce and data is siloed across clients?
6d0e40228118db3aea1b25bc95ba3556fa9ff644.hypothesis: Iterative, collaborative refinement of in-context learning prompts and answers across federated clients—without transmitting model parameters—will improve answer quality and efficiency while preserving privacy and reducing communication costs.
6d0e40228118db3aea1b25bc95ba3556fa9ff644.proposed_method: A general framework, Federated In-Context Learning (Fed-ICL), will be developed to enable collaborative, privacy-preserving in-context learning for question-answering tasks. The method operates in multiple rounds: a central server maintains a global context (query dataset) and sends it to each client. Each client uses its own local language model and dataset to relabel its data and generate improved answers for the server's queries via in-context learning, leveraging both the global context and its local examples. Clients send only their predicted answers (not raw data or model parameters) back to the server, which aggregates these to update the global context. This process is repeated iteratively, allowing progressive refinement of answers. Enhancements such as local dataset filtering (e.g., nearest-neighbor selection for relevant context) and aggregation strategies (e.g., majority voting or lightweight fusion models for non-regression tasks) are incorporated. A variant, Fed-ICL-Free, is proposed for settings where clients lack answer labels, using only question datasets for context.
6d0e40228118db3aea1b25bc95ba3556fa9ff644.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard QA benchmarks, including TruthfulQA (open-ended answer generation) and MMLU (multiple-choice question answering), using both open-source (Llama-2-7B, Llama-3.1-8B) and proprietary (GPT-4o-mini) language models as client backbones. The server query set will be constructed by sampling from benchmark categories, and client datasets will be partitioned using Dirichlet distributions to simulate varying degrees of data heterogeneity. Baselines will include traditional federated learning (FedAvg), parameter-free collaborative methods (MoA, LLM-Blender, LLM-Debate), and ablations/variants of Fed-ICL (Fed-ICL-GT, Fed-ICL-UB, Fed-ICL-LB). Evaluation metrics will be BERTScore, BLEURTScore, and BARTScore for generation tasks, and accuracy for multiple-choice tasks. Communication costs will be measured as total data transmission size. Additional experiments will analyze the effects of iterative refinement, local dataset filtering, number of clients, in-context length, and privacy (via prompt extraction attacks).
6d0e40228118db3aea1b25bc95ba3556fa9ff644.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to combine federated learning and in-context learning for question answering in a privacy-preserving, parameter-free manner. It introduces an iterative, collaborative process for context refinement without transmitting model weights, reducing communication overhead. Theoretical analysis provides convergence guarantees under simplified linear attention models, and practical improvements such as local dataset filtering and aggregation strategies are incorporated. The approach is shown to outperform both traditional federated learning and existing parameter-free baselines, while maintaining privacy and efficiency.

6d1434696bdf613b51ae21248b1a2669a75501ba.title: Tokenization Matters! Degrading Large Language Models through Challenging Their Tokenization
6d1434696bdf613b51ae21248b1a2669a75501ba.research_question: How does the tokenization process in large language models (LLMs) affect their ability to accurately understand and respond to user queries, and can targeted adversarial datasets reveal vulnerabilities in LLM tokenization across different languages and models?
6d1434696bdf613b51ae21248b1a2669a75501ba.hypothesis: LLMs are vulnerable to specific adversarial inputs that exploit weaknesses in their tokenization algorithms, leading to significant degradation in their understanding and response accuracy, particularly in languages with complex tokenization requirements such as Chinese.
6d1434696bdf613b51ae21248b1a2669a75501ba.proposed_method: A comprehensive adversarial dataset, named ADT (Adversarial Dataset for Tokenizer), will be constructed to systematically challenge the tokenization mechanisms of various LLMs. The dataset will consist of two subsets: ADT-Human, manually curated using tokens extracted from the vocabularies of multiple LLMs, and ADT-Auto, automatically generated by leveraging word-pair matching and prompt-based instance creation with LLMs such as GPT-4. For each selected token or token pair, challenging spans will be created by inserting character sequences before, after, or around the target tokens to disrupt conventional tokenization. Each instance will include a sentence containing the challenging span and a related question designed to test whether the LLM can correctly identify and process the intended token(s). The construction process will involve both automated filtering (to ensure the presence of tokenization traps) and manual assessment (to guarantee linguistic and logical coherence).
6d1434696bdf613b51ae21248b1a2669a75501ba.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate a range of open-source and closed-source LLMs, including Chatglm3-6B, Baichuan2-13B-Chat, Yi-34B-Chat, Qwen-7B-Chat, Qwen1.5-72B-Chat, Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Llama-3-70B-Instruct, Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1, Deepseek-R1, GPT-4o, GPT-4, GPT-3.5-Turbo, Qwen2.5-max, step-1-8k, moonshot-v1-8k, and ERNIE-3.5-8K. Both locally deployed and API-accessed versions will be tested where available. The evaluation will use the constructed ADT dataset (both ADT-Human and ADT-Auto), with instances in both Chinese and English. Performance will be measured by the error rate of LLM responses to the dataset's questions, with human assessment used to determine correctness. Additional analysis will examine the relationship between tokenization correctness and response accuracy, using both quantitative statistics and visualizations (e.g., pie charts) to highlight the impact of tokenization errors.
6d1434696bdf613b51ae21248b1a2669a75501ba.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel adversarial dataset specifically designed to expose and quantify vulnerabilities in LLM tokenization, particularly in non-English languages. The methodology provides both manual and automated frameworks for generating challenging tokenization cases, enabling systematic evaluation across a wide range of LLMs. The approach uniquely demonstrates that tokenization errors are a universal and critical source of LLM failures, and the dataset offers a new perspective and resource for future research on improving LLM robustness through better tokenization strategies.

6d1badc223cfca6ae23fcce811b9dbcb8645cdef.title: Language in a Bottle: Language Model Guided Concept Bottlenecks for Interpretable Image Classification
6d1badc223cfca6ae23fcce811b9dbcb8645cdef.research_question: How can inherently interpretable image classification models be constructed without relying on manually specified human-designed concepts, while achieving accuracy comparable to black-box models across diverse visual domains?
6d1badc223cfca6ae23fcce811b9dbcb8645cdef.hypothesis: Automatically generating and selecting visual concepts using large language models and aligning them with images via vision-language models will enable the construction of interpretable concept bottleneck models that match or exceed the performance of black-box classifiers, especially in low-data regimes.
6d1badc223cfca6ae23fcce811b9dbcb8645cdef.proposed_method: A new framework, Language Model Guided Concept Bottlenecks (LaBo), will be developed to automate the construction of interpretable image classifiers. The approach begins by prompting a large language model (such as GPT-3) to generate a diverse set of factual, class-specific candidate concepts in natural language for each category in the classification problem. These candidate concepts are then filtered and selected using a novel submodular optimization criterion that balances discriminability (how well a concept distinguishes between classes) and coverage (diversity of concepts within a class), ensuring the bottleneck layer is both informative and interpretable. The selected textual concepts are aligned with image features using a pretrained vision-language model (e.g., CLIP), which provides similarity scores between each image and concept. A linear classifier is then trained on these concept scores to predict the final class label, with the concept-class association matrix optionally initialized using language model priors to improve performance in few-shot settings.
6d1badc223cfca6ae23fcce811b9dbcb8645cdef.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 11 diverse image classification datasets, including ImageNet, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Food-101, FGVC-Aircraft, Flower-102, CUB-200-2011, UCF-101, DTD, HAM10000, and RESISC45, covering common objects, fine-grained categories, actions, textures, medical images, and satellite images. The evaluation protocol will follow few-shot learning settings (1, 2, 4, 8, 16 shots per class) as well as fully supervised scenarios. Baselines will include black-box linear probes, post-hoc concept bottleneck models (PCBM), and compositional derivation learning (CompDL) with human-annotated concepts. Evaluation metrics will focus on classification accuracy, with additional human studies assessing the factuality and groundability of the learned concepts. Ablation studies will examine the impact of bottleneck size, concept selection strategies, and initialization methods.
6d1badc223cfca6ae23fcce811b9dbcb8645cdef.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to demonstrate that high-performance, inherently interpretable concept bottleneck models can be constructed without manual specification of concepts, using language model-guided automatic concept generation and selection. The approach introduces a novel submodular utility function for concept selection that jointly optimizes for discriminability and diversity, and leverages pretrained vision-language models for concept-image alignment. The resulting models achieve state-of-the-art accuracy among interpretable models, outperform black-box baselines in low-data regimes, and approach black-box performance with more data, all while maintaining interpretability and requiring no expert concept annotation.

6d282279db32fbaccc431979c1dea96ef374bb1a.title: The Road Less Scheduled
6d282279db32fbaccc431979c1dea96ef374bb1a.research_question: Can an optimization method be developed that eliminates the need for explicit learning rate schedules and pre-specified stopping times, while achieving state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of machine learning problems?
6d282279db32fbaccc431979c1dea96ef374bb1a.hypothesis: A schedule-free optimization approach, based on a novel interpolation between Polyak-Ruppert and Primal averaging with a momentum-like parameter, can match or exceed the empirical performance of tuned learning rate schedules without requiring additional hyper-parameters or prior knowledge of the stopping time.
6d282279db32fbaccc431979c1dea96ef374bb1a.proposed_method: A new optimization framework, termed Schedule-Free SGD (and its AdamW variant), will be developed that replaces explicit learning rate schedules with an averaging-based update rule. The method introduces a momentum parameter β that interpolates between Polyak-Ruppert averaging (β=0) and Primal averaging (β=1), with practical values around β≈0.9. The algorithm maintains three sequences: a base sequence z (updated by SGD or AdamW), an averaged sequence x (online equal-weighted average of z), and a gradient location sequence y (a convex combination of z and x). Gradients are evaluated at y, and updates are performed on z, while x is returned as the current estimate. The approach is theoretically grounded by a new online-to-batch conversion theorem, ensuring worst-case optimal convergence rates for convex Lipschitz functions, and is compatible with arbitrary online optimization algorithms and time-varying β.
6d282279db32fbaccc431979c1dea96ef374bb1a.experiment_details: The proposed method will be evaluated on a comprehensive suite of 28 benchmark problems spanning convex optimization, computer vision, natural language processing, and recommendation systems. Datasets include CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, ILSVRC 2012 ImageNet, IWSLT14, Criteo Kaggle, fastMRI, OpenWebText, and others, using standard architectures such as WideResNet, DenseNet, ResNet-50, LSTM, DLRM, U-Net, ViT, and GPT-2. Both Schedule-Free SGD and AdamW variants will be compared against state-of-the-art learning rate schedules (cosine, step-wise, linear decay) and classical averaging methods (Polyak, Primal). Hyper-parameters (learning rate, weight decay, β) will be tuned via grid search, and evaluation metrics will include test accuracy, loss, and time-to-target. Additional large-scale benchmarking will be conducted using the MLCommons AlgoPerf Algorithmic Efficiency Challenge, requiring a single hyper-parameter configuration across diverse tasks.
6d282279db32fbaccc431979c1dea96ef374bb1a.novelty_claims: The proposed method eliminates the need for explicit learning rate schedules and pre-specified stopping times, introducing no additional hyper-parameters over standard optimizers with momentum. It unifies scheduling and iterate averaging through a new theoretical framework, providing a general online-to-batch conversion theorem. The approach achieves worst-case optimal convergence rates for convex Lipschitz problems and demonstrates state-of-the-art empirical performance across a broad range of machine learning tasks, often outperforming heavily-tuned schedules. The method also enables the use of larger learning rates without divergence and avoids gradient norm collapse, contributing to faster and more stable convergence.

6d3c0e0df44dc2f2835f26d6b1e143ac5bb6072d.title: Higher-Rank Irreducible Cartesian Tensors for Equivariant Message Passing
6d3c0e0df44dc2f2835f26d6b1e143ac5bb6072d.research_question: How can the integration of higher-rank irreducible Cartesian tensors into equivariant message passing neural networks improve the accuracy, efficiency, and flexibility of machine-learned interatomic potentials for atomistic simulations, compared to existing spherical and Cartesian tensor-based approaches?
6d3c0e0df44dc2f2835f26d6b1e143ac5bb6072d.hypothesis: The use of higher-rank irreducible Cartesian tensors in message passing neural networks will enable the construction of more flexible, expressive, and computationally efficient equivariant models, resulting in on-par or superior accuracy and generalization compared to state-of-the-art spherical and Cartesian tensor-based models for a range of atomistic simulation tasks.
6d3c0e0df44dc2f2835f26d6b1e143ac5bb6072d.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that incorporates higher-rank irreducible Cartesian tensors and their tensor products into the architecture of equivariant message passing neural networks (MPNNs) for atomistic systems. The method will construct symmetric and traceless irreducible Cartesian tensors from unit vectors representing atomic directions, and define their tensor products to enable the creation of equivariant two-body and many-body features. The message passing layers will be designed to ensure equivariance to the orthogonal group O(3) (rotations and reflections) and to preserve the traceless property of the tensors. The architecture will extend and adapt the MACE (Multiplicative Atomic Convolutional Equivariant) framework to the Cartesian basis, employing even-rank tensor products and efficient pooling mechanisms to aggregate information from neighboring atoms. The approach will also explore computational optimizations, such as using symmetric product bases and latent feature spaces, to reduce memory and runtime costs.
6d3c0e0df44dc2f2835f26d6b1e143ac5bb6072d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of benchmark datasets for atomistic simulations, including rMD17, MD22, 3BPA, acetylacetone, and Ta–V–Cr–W. The proposed models will be trained to predict total energies and atomic forces, using both large (e.g., 950) and small (e.g., 50) training set sizes to assess data efficiency and generalization. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art spherical tensor-based models (such as MACE and NequIP), as well as advanced Cartesian models (e.g., TensorNet, Allegro, CACE). Evaluation metrics will include mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean square error (RMSE) for energy and force predictions, as well as inference time and memory consumption. Additional tests will assess extrapolation to out-of-domain data (e.g., high-temperature MD, dihedral scans), flexibility in modeling many-body interactions, and performance on chemically complex alloys. All experiments will be repeated with multiple random seeds to ensure statistical robustness, and model architectures will be matched in parameter count for fair comparison.
6d3c0e0df44dc2f2835f26d6b1e143ac5bb6072d.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the use of higher-rank irreducible Cartesian tensors and their tensor products for constructing equivariant message passing neural networks, overcoming the flexibility and expressive power limitations of existing Cartesian approaches. The method provides a computationally efficient alternative to spherical tensor-based models by avoiding the need for Clebsch–Gordan coefficients, enabling scalable many-body feature construction. Theoretical guarantees are established for equivariance and preservation of the traceless property in the message passing layers. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate that the approach achieves state-of-the-art or superior accuracy and generalization on diverse benchmark datasets, with comparable or improved computational efficiency and memory usage.

6d4bacb69923e1e94fb4de468b939ce6db32fb51.title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
6d4bacb69923e1e94fb4de468b939ce6db32fb51.research_question: Can large language models (LLMs) intrinsically self-correct their reasoning errors without access to external feedback, and how does their self-correction performance compare to other multi-response methods and prompt engineering strategies?
6d4bacb69923e1e94fb4de468b939ce6db32fb51.hypothesis: LLMs are unable to reliably self-correct their reasoning errors in the absence of external feedback, and intrinsic self-correction may not improve—and can even degrade—reasoning performance compared to strong baselines and well-designed prompts.
6d4bacb69923e1e94fb4de468b939ce6db32fb51.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation will be conducted on the intrinsic self-correction capabilities of LLMs, focusing on reasoning tasks. The methodology involves defining intrinsic self-correction as a process where the model attempts to revise its initial answers based solely on its own outputs, without any external or oracle feedback. A three-step prompting strategy will be employed: (1) generating an initial answer, (2) prompting the model to review and critique its own answer, and (3) prompting the model to revise its answer based on its self-generated feedback. Multiple rounds of self-correction will be tested. The study will also compare intrinsic self-correction to multi-agent debate (where multiple model instances critique each other) and self-consistency (majority voting among multiple generations), as well as examine the impact of prompt design on evaluation outcomes.
6d4bacb69923e1e94fb4de468b939ce6db32fb51.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using several state-of-the-art LLMs, including GPT-3.5-Turbo, GPT-4, GPT-4-Turbo, and Llama-2-70b-chat. The evaluation will utilize established reasoning benchmarks: GSM8K (grade school math word problems), CommonSenseQA (commonsense multiple-choice questions), and HotpotQA (multi-hop question answering). For each model and dataset, performance will be measured under standard prompting, intrinsic self-correction (with various feedback prompts and up to two rounds), and, where relevant, self-correction with oracle labels. Multi-agent debate and self-consistency methods will be implemented for comparison, ensuring equivalent inference costs (number of model calls). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy (for reasoning tasks) and concept coverage (for constrained generation tasks). Prompt design will be systematically varied to assess its influence on self-correction outcomes.
6d4bacb69923e1e94fb4de468b939ce6db32fb51.novelty_claims: This proposal aims to rigorously define and isolate intrinsic self-correction in LLMs, distinguishing it from self-correction methods that rely on external or oracle feedback. It will provide the first systematic comparison of intrinsic self-correction with strong multi-response baselines such as self-consistency and multi-agent debate, controlling for inference cost. The study will also highlight the critical role of prompt design in evaluating self-correction, demonstrating that improvements attributed to self-correction may be confounded by suboptimal initial prompts. The findings are expected to clarify the limitations of current LLMs in self-correcting reasoning errors and to offer guidelines for fair evaluation and future research directions.

6d7b8a478801bd9d21df82d5f33ae6eced90da5e.title: Solving math word problems with process- and outcome-based feedback
6d7b8a478801bd9d21df82d5f33ae6eced90da5e.research_question: What is the most effective form of supervision—process-based or outcome-based—for training language models to solve math word problems, and how do these approaches impact both final answer accuracy and the correctness of reasoning steps?
6d7b8a478801bd9d21df82d5f33ae6eced90da5e.hypothesis: Process-based supervision or reward models that emulate process-based feedback will lead to lower reasoning trace errors compared to outcome-based supervision, while both approaches will achieve similar final answer accuracy.
6d7b8a478801bd9d21df82d5f33ae6eced90da5e.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed to train large pre-trained language models to solve math word problems, generating step-by-step reasoning traces. The methodology will systematically compare process-based supervision (supervising each reasoning step using human-annotated traces) and outcome-based supervision (supervising only the final answer). Several training paradigms will be implemented, including few-shot prompting, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (RL) via expert iteration. Reward models (RMs) will be trained both on outcome-based and process-based labels to score solution traces, and these RMs will be used for both reranking generated samples and as reward functions in RL. The policy improvement step will involve generating multiple solution samples per problem, filtering or reranking them using RMs, and distilling improved policies via supervised learning.
6d7b8a478801bd9d21df82d5f33ae6eced90da5e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the GSM8K dataset, a benchmark of grade school math word problems with annotated reasoning traces. The dataset will be split into training, validation, and test sets, with additional human annotation collected for stepwise correctness. Evaluation will use two primary metrics: final-answer error rate (fraction of problems with incorrect final answers) and trace error rate (fraction of problems with correct final answers but at least one incorrect reasoning step, as determined by human annotation). Baselines will include few-shot prompting, SFT, and existing RL methods. Multiple decoding strategies will be compared, including majority voting and RM-weighted reranking. Selective prediction (where the model abstains on uncertain cases) and out-of-distribution generalization (using pre-algebra problems from the MATH dataset) will also be evaluated.
6d7b8a478801bd9d21df82d5f33ae6eced90da5e.novelty_claims: The proposed research will provide the first comprehensive empirical comparison of process-based and outcome-based supervision for language models on a natural language reasoning task with annotated traces. It will introduce and evaluate the use of reward models trained on both process- and outcome-based feedback for both reranking and reinforcement learning. The approach is expected to set new state-of-the-art results on GSM8K in both final-answer and trace error rates, and to clarify the trade-offs between label efficiency, answer accuracy, and reasoning transparency in math word problem solving.

6d7d141c75af752ffc0d8a6184cca3f9323d6c74.title: Simplified State Space Layers for Sequence Modeling
6d7d141c75af752ffc0d8a6184cca3f9323d6c74.research_question: How can the efficiency and performance of state space layers for long-range sequence modeling be improved, particularly by simplifying the internal structure and leveraging efficient parallel computation, while maintaining or surpassing state-of-the-art results on challenging sequence modeling benchmarks?
6d7d141c75af752ffc0d8a6184cca3f9323d6c74.hypothesis: A state space layer based on a single multi-input, multi-output (MIMO) state space model, combined with diagonalized dynamics and parallel scan computation, will match or exceed the computational efficiency and modeling performance of existing structured state space sequence (S4) layers on long-range sequence tasks.
6d7d141c75af752ffc0d8a6184cca3f9323d6c74.proposed_method: A novel state space layer, termed S5, will be developed by replacing the bank of independent single-input, single-output (SISO) SSMs in S4 with a single MIMO SSM. The S5 layer will employ a diagonalized state matrix to enable efficient parallel scan operations, allowing for recurrent, time-domain computation with linear complexity in sequence length. Initialization and parameterization will leverage a diagonal approximation of the HiPPO matrix (specifically, the HiPPO-N matrix) to maintain strong long-range modeling capabilities. The layer will support learnable timescale parameters for each latent state and enforce conjugate symmetry to ensure real outputs and reduce computational overhead. The design will allow for efficient handling of time-varying SSMs and irregularly sampled sequences.
6d7d141c75af752ffc0d8a6184cca3f9323d6c74.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of long-range sequence modeling benchmarks, including the Long Range Arena (LRA) suite, which features tasks with sequence lengths up to 16,384, as well as the SpeechCommands dataset for raw audio classification and a pendulum regression task with irregularly sampled observations. Baselines will include S4, S4D, Liquid-S4, Mega, Mega-chunk, and conventional transformer and convolutional models. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy for LRA and SpeechCommands, and mean squared error (MSE) for regression tasks. Experimental setups will ensure comparable parameter counts and computational complexity between S5 and S4, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of initialization and parameterization choices.
6d7d141c75af752ffc0d8a6184cca3f9323d6c74.novelty_claims: The proposed S5 layer introduces a simplified architecture that uses a single MIMO SSM with diagonalized dynamics, enabling efficient parallel scan computation in the time domain. This approach eliminates the need for convolutional or frequency-domain implementations required by S4, while maintaining linear complexity and supporting time-varying and irregularly sampled data. The method establishes a theoretical and empirical connection to S4, justifying the use of HiPPO-based initialization in the MIMO setting. S5 demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on long-range sequence modeling benchmarks, surpassing or matching existing methods in both accuracy and efficiency, and offers a straightforward implementation suitable for a wide range of sequence modeling tasks.

6d8ce667aaaa611e6a9a002f9fbf7513be95492b.title: Agent-Oriented Planning in Multi-Agent Systems
6d8ce667aaaa611e6a9a002f9fbf7513be95492b.research_question: How can multi-agent systems, empowered by large language models (LLMs), be equipped with an effective agent-oriented planning framework that enables a meta-agent to decompose complex user queries into sub-tasks and allocate them to appropriate agents, ensuring reliable, complete, and efficient solutions to real-world problems?
6d8ce667aaaa611e6a9a002f9fbf7513be95492b.hypothesis: A planning framework that explicitly enforces the principles of solvability, completeness, and non-redundancy in sub-task decomposition and allocation, combined with automated evaluation and feedback mechanisms, will significantly improve the effectiveness and robustness of multi-agent systems in solving complex queries compared to existing single-agent and multi-agent planning strategies.
6d8ce667aaaa611e6a9a002f9fbf7513be95492b.proposed_method: A novel agent-oriented planning (AOP) framework will be developed for multi-agent systems, where a meta-agent performs fast decomposition and allocation of user queries into sub-tasks, considering both the query and agent descriptions. The initial plan is refined using a detector that checks for completeness and non-redundancy, and a reward model that predicts the solvability of sub-tasks by agents without requiring actual agent calls. The reward model is trained on a dataset of sub-tasks, agent descriptions, and annotated response quality scores, using embeddings and a multilayer perceptron. If the reward model or detector identifies issues, the meta-agent is prompted to replan, re-describe, or further decompose sub-tasks as needed. A feedback loop continuously updates agents' representative works to improve future planning, ensuring ongoing adaptation and robustness.
6d8ce667aaaa611e6a9a002f9fbf7513be95492b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a numerical reasoning dataset (Husky-QA) requiring multi-agent collaboration, with additional tests on decontextualized subsets of DROP and IIRC datasets. The multi-agent system will include a meta-agent and several specialized agents (code, math, search, commonsense), all powered by GPT-4o. Baseline comparisons will include single-agent LLMs (with and without Chain-of-Thought prompting), as well as multi-agent planning methods such as REACT, HUSKY, and meta-agent-based approaches. Evaluation will use accuracy as the primary metric, judged by GPT-4o or human annotators, and will also report computational costs (prompt/completion tokens, execution time). Ablation studies will assess the contributions of the detector, reward model, and representative works components.
6d8ce667aaaa611e6a9a002f9fbf7513be95492b.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces explicit design principles—solvability, completeness, and non-redundancy—for agent-oriented planning in multi-agent LLM systems. It leverages a reward model to efficiently evaluate sub-task solvability without incurring the cost of actual agent calls, and integrates a detector for plan completeness and redundancy. The inclusion of a feedback loop with representative works enables continual improvement and adaptation. This comprehensive and systematic approach is claimed to yield significant improvements in accuracy and robustness over both single-agent and existing multi-agent planning baselines.

6d8fe97ee5b64f7a1dcee2d665fb30b7a260436b.title: Navigating Semantic Drift in Task-Agnostic Class-Incremental Learning
6d8fe97ee5b64f7a1dcee2d665fb30b7a260436b.research_question: How can class-incremental learning be improved to better retain knowledge of previously learned classes while sequentially learning new classes, particularly in task-agnostic settings where task IDs are unavailable?
6d8fe97ee5b64f7a1dcee2d665fb30b7a260436b.hypothesis: Constraining both the mean and covariance of class feature distributions during sequential learning, combined with feature-level self-distillation, will significantly reduce semantic drift and catastrophic forgetting in class-incremental learning, leading to improved stability and performance across tasks.
6d8fe97ee5b64f7a1dcee2d665fb30b7a260436b.proposed_method: A novel semantic drift calibration framework will be developed for task-agnostic class-incremental learning. The approach will employ mean shift compensation by estimating class means as the average of sample embeddings and adjusting for shifts using a weighted average based on embedding proximity to previous class means. Covariance calibration will be introduced by aligning class-specific embedding covariances between the old and current networks using a Mahalanobis distance-based constraint, minimizing the absolute difference in intra-class Mahalanobis distances. Additionally, feature-level self-distillation will be applied to patch tokens, encouraging their representations to remain consistent across tasks and enhancing feature stability. The backbone will utilize a frozen pre-trained Vision Transformer (ViT) with learnable, task-specific LoRA modules for parameter-efficient adaptation, and classifier heads will be retrained with calibrated class statistics after each task.
6d8fe97ee5b64f7a1dcee2d665fb30b7a260436b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four widely used class-incremental learning datasets: ImageNet-R, CIFAR-100, CUB-200, and ImageNet-A. Each dataset will be split into multiple tasks (e.g., 5, 10, or 20), with class-incremental sessions. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines, including prompt-based, adapter-based, and LoRA-based parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods, all using the same ViT-B/16-IN21K backbone and consistent experimental settings. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on the last task and average accuracy across all tasks, with results averaged over three trials using different random seeds and class orders. Ablation studies will assess the contribution of each component (mean shift compensation, covariance calibration, and patch distillation), and different LoRA module structures (task-specific, task-shared, and hybrid) will be evaluated for their impact on performance.
6d8fe97ee5b64f7a1dcee2d665fb30b7a260436b.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a dual calibration strategy that explicitly compensates for mean shifts and implicitly constrains covariance shifts in class feature distributions, a combination not previously explored in class-incremental learning. The use of Mahalanobis distance-based covariance calibration for aligning intra-class distributions between old and new networks is novel in this context. The integration of feature-level self-distillation for patch tokens further enhances knowledge retention. The method is designed to be efficient, task-agnostic, and compatible with parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and is claimed to outperform existing approaches across multiple challenging benchmarks.

6d994b4f5a46cd14e8f09f1e9e49120546b15e31.title: CodeRL: Mastering Code Generation through Pretrained Models and Deep Reinforcement Learning
6d994b4f5a46cd14e8f09f1e9e49120546b15e31.research_question: How can program synthesis models be improved to generate functionally correct code from natural language problem specifications, especially for complex and unseen coding tasks?
6d994b4f5a46cd14e8f09f1e9e49120546b15e31.hypothesis: Integrating unit test signals and reinforcement learning into the training and inference procedures of pretrained language models will significantly enhance the functional correctness and generalization ability of code generation systems.
6d994b4f5a46cd14e8f09f1e9e49120546b15e31.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that formulates program synthesis as a reinforcement learning (RL) problem, leveraging pretrained code language models as actor networks and introducing a critic network to predict the functional correctness of generated programs. The actor network is fine-tuned using synthetic samples weighted by critic-assigned scores, where returns are defined by the outcome of unit tests (e.g., compile error, runtime error, failed test, passed test). During inference, a dual-stage generation procedure is employed: successful programs (passing example unit tests) are refined by conditioning on high-value sub-sequences as seeds, while failed programs are selected and repaired using a program repair model guided by critic scores and error types. The framework extends the CodeT5 encoder-decoder architecture with enhanced pretraining objectives, larger model sizes, and a substantially expanded Python code dataset. Training involves imitation learning to warm-start the actor, followed by alternating updates to the actor and critic, and a critic-guided sampling strategy is used to iteratively improve code outputs during inference.
6d994b4f5a46cd14e8f09f1e9e49120546b15e31.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on large-scale program synthesis benchmarks, including the APPS (Automated Programming Progress Standard) and MBPP (Mostly Basic Python Problems) datasets. The proposed method is compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as CodeT5, GPT-3, and other pretrained language models. Evaluation metrics include pass@k (the percentage of problems solved with at least one correct program in k samples), with particular focus on pass@1, pass@5, pass@80, and pass@1000. The experimental setup involves pretraining the CodeT5-large model on an expanded Python corpus (10.5B tokens), fine-tuning with RL and critic-guided objectives, and ablation studies to assess the impact of each component. Inference uses batch generation (N=200), nucleus sampling, and critic-guided program refinement and repair, with all models evaluated against both example and hidden unit tests.
6d994b4f5a46cd14e8f09f1e9e49120546b15e31.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new actor-critic reinforcement learning framework for program synthesis that directly optimizes for functional correctness using unit test signals. It innovates by integrating a critic model to provide dense, token-level feedback during both training and inference, enabling automatic program refinement and repair. The method also extends the CodeT5 architecture with improved pretraining objectives and a much larger code corpus, resulting in state-of-the-art performance on challenging program synthesis benchmarks and demonstrating strong zero-shot transfer capabilities.

6d99a203b2d9105e94c0a5d6c23dfa904507b16d.title: DeepPCR: Parallelizing Sequential Operations in Neural Networks
6d99a203b2d9105e94c0a5d6c23dfa904507b16d.research_question: How can the inherent sequential operations in neural network training and inference, such as forward and backward passes and denoising in diffusion models, be parallelized to significantly accelerate computation without compromising accuracy or flexibility?
6d99a203b2d9105e94c0a5d6c23dfa904507b16d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that interpreting sequential neural network operations as the solution to a system of equations, and applying a parallel solution algorithm tailored to Markovian sequences, will reduce computational complexity from linear to logarithmic in the sequence length, enabling substantial speedups in training and inference while maintaining comparable accuracy.
6d99a203b2d9105e94c0a5d6c23dfa904507b16d.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a framework that recasts sequential operations in neural networks—such as forward and backward passes or denoising steps in diffusion models—as the solution of a system of equations, specifically a block bidiagonal system. The approach assumes the sequence satisfies the Markov property, where each step depends only on the previous one. To solve this system efficiently, the Parallel Cyclic Reduction (PCR) algorithm is adapted, reducing the number of sequential computational steps from O(L) to O(log_2 L), where L is the sequence length. For nonlinear systems, Newton's method is employed to iteratively linearize and solve the system, with each Newton iteration using PCR to solve the linearized system in parallel. The method requires additional memory to store intermediate results and is most effective when hardware supports high degrees of parallelism.
6d99a203b2d9105e94c0a5d6c23dfa904507b16d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of neural network architectures and tasks to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed parallelization framework. Forward and backward passes through multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) of varying depths and widths will be profiled to identify regimes where speedup is achieved, with timing and accuracy compared to standard sequential implementations. Training acceleration will be assessed on deep ResNet architectures using the MNIST dataset, measuring wall-clock time, loss evolution, and final model accuracy. The method will also be applied to parallelize the denoising procedure in diffusion models, with experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CelebA datasets, evaluating speedup, image quality (using FID and Wasserstein-2 distance), and scalability with respect to latent space dimension and number of denoising steps. All experiments will be run on high-memory GPUs (e.g., V100 with 40GB RAM) using PyTorch, and baselines will include standard sequential implementations.
6d99a203b2d9105e94c0a5d6c23dfa904507b16d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is novel in its general framework for parallelizing a wide range of sequential neural network operations by casting them as systems of equations and solving them with an adapted Parallel Cyclic Reduction algorithm. This reduces computational complexity from linear to logarithmic in sequence length for Markovian operations, enabling significant speedups (up to 30x for forward passes, 200x for backward passes, and 11x for diffusion model generation) without loss of accuracy. The method is flexible, applicable to both training and inference, and generalizes beyond previous layer-parallelization techniques by targeting the Markov property and employing a theoretically grounded, experimentally validated parallel solver.

6dc958f1bbebedfe3feccc2a8b244dfeac46ba38.title: The Limits of Tractable Marginalization
6dc958f1bbebedfe3feccc2a8b244dfeac46ba38.research_question: Can all functions with polynomial time marginalization algorithms be succinctly represented by uniform finally multilinear arithmetic circuits (UFMACs), or are there broader classes of tractable marginalization beyond current circuit-based models? What are the computational boundaries of tractable marginalization, including stronger forms such as Hamming weight and virtual evidence marginalization?
6dc958f1bbebedfe3feccc2a8b244dfeac46ba38.hypothesis: Not all functions with tractable marginalization can be efficiently represented by known tractable circuit models such as UFMACs, assuming standard complexity-theoretic conjectures (e.g., FP ≠ #P). Furthermore, there exists a hierarchy of tractable marginalization problems, and UFMACs are complete for virtual evidence marginalization in the real RAM model.
6dc958f1bbebedfe3feccc2a8b244dfeac46ba38.proposed_method: The proposed research will formalize the tractability of marginalization for functions in terms of polynomial time computability and relate these to their representation as multilinear polynomials computed by arithmetic circuits. A hierarchy of complexity classes will be defined, corresponding to increasingly powerful forms of marginalization: standard variable marginalization, Hamming weight marginalization, and virtual evidence marginalization. For each class, completeness and separation results will be established by constructing explicit function families and leveraging complexity-theoretic reductions, particularly from constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) with known dichotomy theorems. The approach will also include the development of completeness results for virtual evidence marginalization in the real RAM model, showing that any function efficiently computable in this setting can be represented by a UFMAC.
6dc958f1bbebedfe3feccc2a8b244dfeac46ba38.experiment_details: Theoretical experiments will involve constructing explicit function families, such as those based on affine CSPs, to demonstrate separations between the proposed complexity classes (e.g., PM, PHM, PVM, UFMAC). Complexity-theoretic reductions will be used to show #P-hardness of certain marginalization problems, and completeness results will be established under standard assumptions (e.g., FP ≠ #P). No empirical datasets are used, but the framework will be validated through formal proofs, leveraging known results from the literature on arithmetic circuits, model counting, and CSPs. Evaluation metrics include computational complexity (polynomial time vs #P-hardness) and the existence or non-existence of efficient circuit representations.
6dc958f1bbebedfe3feccc2a8b244dfeac46ba38.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a negative answer to the open question of whether all functions with tractable marginalization can be succinctly represented by known circuit models, providing explicit separating examples under standard complexity assumptions. It establishes a new hierarchy of tractable marginalization problems, including Hamming weight and virtual evidence marginalization, and proves that UFMACs are complete for virtual evidence marginalization in the real RAM model. These results unify and generalize prior work on tractable probabilistic models, arithmetic circuits, and knowledge compilation, and suggest the possibility of more expressive-efficient tractable models beyond current frameworks.

6dcdac10bbc7364740178dcd10c5b05906fe13a3.title: Quantized Feature Distillation for Network Quantization
6dcdac10bbc7364740178dcd10c5b05906fe13a3.research_question: How can neural network quantization be improved to achieve higher accuracy and flexibility across diverse vision tasks, such as image classification, object detection, and segmentation, especially for both convolutional networks and vision transformers under low-bit settings?
6dcdac10bbc7364740178dcd10c5b05906fe13a3.hypothesis: Utilizing quantized features from a quantized teacher network as the supervision signal during quantization-aware training will yield more effective and flexible knowledge distillation, resulting in improved accuracy and robustness of quantized student networks across various vision tasks compared to traditional logit or full-precision feature distillation.
6dcdac10bbc7364740178dcd10c5b05906fe13a3.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces Quantized Feature Distillation (QFD), a quantization-aware training (QAT) method that leverages a quantized (or binarized) teacher network to guide the quantization of a student network. Initially, the teacher network is trained and its features are quantized to a low bit-width (e.g., 1, 4, or 8 bits). During student network training, both the input image and the quantized teacher features are used: the student network is trained to mimic the quantized features of the teacher using a mean squared error loss, while also optimizing the standard cross-entropy loss with ground truth labels. The quantization process for both weights and activations follows a uniform quantizer with normalization, quantization, and de-quantization steps, and gradients are approximated using the straight-through estimator (STE). The overall objective combines the distillation loss and the task loss, balanced by a hyperparameter λ, and all quantization parameters are learned jointly with network weights.
6dcdac10bbc7364740178dcd10c5b05906fe13a3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple benchmarks, including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet, CUB200, and MS-COCO, covering tasks such as image classification, object detection, and segmentation. Architectures to be evaluated include ResNet-18/32/34/50, MobileNetV2, ViT (Vision Transformer), and Swin Transformer. The method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as SPEQ, APRT*, Auxi, QKD, QIL, LSQ, DAQ, EWGS, LCQ, and APoT, using both uniform and non-uniform quantizers. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 and top-5 accuracy for classification, and average precision (AP) for detection and segmentation. Standard training protocols and data augmentations will be used, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of the distillation hyperparameter λ and the quantization of teacher features. The method will also be tested on quantizing vision transformers for detection and segmentation, a setting not previously explored.
6dcdac10bbc7364740178dcd10c5b05906fe13a3.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel and simple quantization-aware training framework based on quantized feature distillation, which is both quantization-friendly and flexible for various vision tasks. It is the first to demonstrate the effectiveness of using quantized features as teacher signals for knowledge distillation in network quantization, outperforming traditional logit and feature distillation methods. The approach is also the first to successfully quantize vision transformers for object detection and segmentation tasks, showing significant improvements and state-of-the-art results across multiple benchmarks and architectures. The method achieves these results without the need for complex auxiliary modules, multi-stage training, or non-uniform quantizers, making it practical and broadly applicable.

6dd0f87ecd7dfcb86f1b19a65d57faf4f9476062.title: Self-Refining Diffusion Samplers: Enabling Parallelization via Parareal Iterations
6dd0f87ecd7dfcb86f1b19a65d57faf4f9476062.research_question: How can the sampling process in diffusion models be parallelized to reduce latency without sacrificing sample quality or requiring retraining, and what are the practical trade-offs in terms of computational resources and memory?
6dd0f87ecd7dfcb86f1b19a65d57faf4f9476062.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging parallel-in-time integration methods, specifically a Parareal-inspired iterative refinement approach, can enable parallelization of diffusion model sampling, thereby reducing latency while maintaining sample quality and avoiding retraining costs.
6dd0f87ecd7dfcb86f1b19a65d57faf4f9476062.proposed_method: A novel sampling algorithm, Self-Refining Diffusion Samplers (SRDS), is proposed to parallelize the sampling process in diffusion models. SRDS begins with a coarse, low-fidelity solution of the diffusion trajectory using a small number of steps from a standard solver (e.g., DDIM), then iteratively refines this trajectory in parallel blocks through Parareal-inspired predictor-corrector updates. Each refinement iteration partitions the trajectory into blocks, simulates each block at high resolution in parallel, and updates the global trajectory by combining coarse and fine solves. Convergence is measured by the change in output between iterations, and the process continues until a specified tolerance is met. The method is compatible with various existing solvers and supports batched inference and pipelined parallelism to maximize device utilization.
6dd0f87ecd7dfcb86f1b19a65d57faf4f9476062.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both pixel-based and latent diffusion models. Pixel-based tests will use pretrained models on LSUN Church, LSUN Bedroom, 64x64 ImageNet, and 32x32 CIFAR datasets, each with 1024-step diffusion trajectories. Latent diffusion experiments will focus on Stable Diffusion-v2, with evaluation on the COCO 2017 captions dataset. Baselines will include sequential DDIM sampling and the ParaDiGMs parallel sampler. Evaluation metrics will include FID scores for image quality, CLIP scores for semantic alignment, and wall-clock sampling time. Experiments will measure both effective serial evaluations (parallel steps counted as one) and total model evaluations, with convergence criteria set by l1 norm or CLIP score thresholds. Tests will also assess the impact of pipelined parallelism and compare memory and communication overheads.
6dd0f87ecd7dfcb86f1b19a65d57faf4f9476062.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first application of Parareal-style parallel-in-time integration to diffusion model sampling, enabling approximation-free, parallelized generation that maintains sample quality without retraining. SRDS provides fine-grained control over the speed-quality trade-off, is compatible with a wide range of solvers, and supports efficient batched and pipelined inference. The approach achieves significant reductions in sampling latency (up to 4.3x speedup) compared to both sequential and existing parallel baselines, with lower memory and communication overhead than prior methods such as ParaDiGMs.

6dee9e9deaba7555d5ab86a1e1fa9d350f6eaafe.title: Token-Supervised Value Models for Enhancing Mathematical Problem-Solving Capabilities of Large Language Models
6dee9e9deaba7555d5ab86a1e1fa9d350f6eaafe.research_question: How can the mathematical problem-solving capabilities of large language models be enhanced through improved verification strategies, particularly in the context of tree-search-based inference algorithms?
6dee9e9deaba7555d5ab86a1e1fa9d350f6eaafe.hypothesis: Token-level supervision, which assigns each token in a solution a probability reflecting the likelihood of reaching the correct final answer, enables more accurate and effective verification of partial solutions during tree search, leading to improved mathematical problem-solving performance compared to outcome- and process-supervised verifiers.
6dee9e9deaba7555d5ab86a1e1fa9d350f6eaafe.proposed_method: A new class of verifiers, termed Token-supervised Value Models (TVMs), will be developed and trained to assign each token in a reasoning path a probability score representing the likelihood that the partial solution up to that token will ultimately yield the correct final answer. This token-level supervision is computed empirically by sampling multiple reasoning paths for each training problem and labeling each token according to the proportion of continuations that reach the correct answer. The TVM is trained using a mean squared error loss between these empirical probabilities and the model's predictions. Theoretically, the TVM's output for a token is equivalent to the expected cumulative reward under a specific reward formulation, aligning the model with value-based guidance for tree search. The TVM is integrated into tree-search-based inference strategies, such as Step-by-Step Beam Search and REBASE, to directly and explicitly evaluate and prune partial solutions during test-time reasoning.
6dee9e9deaba7555d5ab86a1e1fa9d350f6eaafe.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the GSM8K and MATH benchmarks for mathematical problem-solving, utilizing large language models such as Mistral 7B and Llama 3 8B, as well as their MetaMath fine-tuned variants. The TVM will be compared against outcome-supervised reward models (ORMs) and process-supervised reward models (PRMs, e.g., Math-Shepherd) under various inference strategies, including self-consistency, Best-of-N search, Step-by-Step Beam Search (K=40, b=10), and REBASE (K=40). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on the test sets, root mean squared error (RMSE) between true and predicted token values, precision-recall curves, and compute efficiency (FLOPs and execution time). Each verifier will be matched in size and architecture to the base LLM, and experiments will be run with multiple random trials to assess statistical significance.
6dee9e9deaba7555d5ab86a1e1fa9d350f6eaafe.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces token-level supervision for verifiers in mathematical problem-solving, enabling direct and explicit estimation of the likelihood that a partial solution leads to the correct answer. This approach addresses the high false negative errors of process-supervised models and the indirectness of outcome-supervised models, providing theoretical grounding for value-based guidance in tree search. The TVM is claimed to achieve lower false negative errors than PRMs and more accurate value estimates than ORMs, resulting in superior performance for tree-search-based inference strategies while maintaining computational efficiency.

6df24cfb2ded90dfa443139c2e3fb6317179a358.title: Streaming Long Video Understanding with Large Language Models
6df24cfb2ded90dfa443139c2e3fb6317179a358.research_question: How can large language models be enabled to efficiently and accurately understand and reason about arbitrarily long videos, overcoming the computational and contextual limitations posed by the large number of visual tokens in long video sequences?
6df24cfb2ded90dfa443139c2e3fb6317179a358.hypothesis: A memory-propagated streaming encoding architecture, combined with adaptive memory selection, will enable large language models to efficiently process and comprehend long videos by maintaining temporal dynamics and selecting question-relevant information, leading to improved accuracy and efficiency in long video understanding tasks.
6df24cfb2ded90dfa443139c2e3fb6317179a358.proposed_method: The proposed approach segments long videos into short clips and encodes each clip sequentially using a memory-propagated streaming encoder. At each step, the encoder leverages historical memory from the previous clip, concatenates it with the current clip's features, and processes them through a small decoder-only language model (e.g., Phi-2) to produce a condensed representation. Summarization tokens and global clip indicators are used to encapsulate both spatial and temporal information. After encoding, an adaptive memory selection strategy identifies a fixed number of question-relevant memories by computing the similarity between a question indicator and all historical clip indicators, using a differentiable Gumbel-Topk mechanism. The selected memories are then concatenated and fed into a large language model (e.g., Vicuna-7B) for comprehensive reasoning and question answering, allowing efficient reuse of encoded video representations for multiple questions.
6df24cfb2ded90dfa443139c2e3fb6317179a358.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of long video question answering benchmarks, including Next-QA, Next-GQA, VideoChatGPT, EgoSchema, MovieChat-1K, and MovieNet-QA, covering videos from under a minute to over an hour in length. The method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as Video-LLaMA, LLaMA-VID, MovieLLM, and others, using metrics such as accuracy, correctness of information, temporal grounding (IoP, IoU), and inference latency. The training process involves a progressive two-stage paradigm: first, single-clip encoding is trained on 790K image and short video caption data and 763K instruction data; second, long video QA pairs (from curated, synthesized, and existing datasets) are used to fine-tune the full architecture, including the streaming encoder and LLM. Ablation studies will assess the impact of historical memory, memory selection, encoder depth, and temporal grounding supervision.
6df24cfb2ded90dfa443139c2e3fb6317179a358.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel memory-propagated streaming encoding architecture that maintains temporal dynamics and compresses arbitrary-length videos into fixed-length representations. The adaptive memory selection mechanism enables efficient, question-driven retrieval of relevant video segments, reducing redundancy and computational cost. The disentangled extraction and reasoning design allows for flexible, multi-question answering without re-encoding the entire video. The approach is claimed to achieve superior accuracy, precise temporal grounding, and higher inference efficiency compared to existing methods, particularly on long video understanding benchmarks.

6df884c0623307124bcccb52500fc720b4f5080f.title: Memorization to Generalization: Emergence of Diffusion Models from Associative Memory
6df884c0623307124bcccb52500fc720b4f5080f.research_question: How do diffusion models transition from memorization to generalization as the size of the training dataset increases, and what is the nature and role of emergent spurious states in this process?
6df884c0623307124bcccb52500fc720b4f5080f.hypothesis: Diffusion models, when analyzed through the lens of associative memory, exhibit a phase transition from memorization to generalization as training data size increases, with spurious states emerging at the boundary between these phases.
6df884c0623307124bcccb52500fc720b4f5080f.proposed_method: A theoretical and empirical framework will be developed to analyze diffusion models as associative memory systems, specifically drawing parallels with Dense Associative Memories (DenseAMs). The training phase of a diffusion model will be conceptualized as memory encoding, and the generation phase as memory retrieval, enabling the application of energy landscape analysis from associative memory theory. Detection metrics will be designed to classify generated samples into memorized, spurious, and generalized categories based on nearest neighbor distances in both the training and synthetic sets. Theoretical predictions regarding the existence and characteristics of spurious states will be derived and empirically validated using both toy models and high-dimensional real-world datasets.
6df884c0623307124bcccb52500fc720b4f5080f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple datasets, including MNIST, FASHION-MNIST, CIFAR10, and LSUN-CHURCH (resized to 64x64), using DDPM-based diffusion models trained with varying training set sizes. For each training size, a synthetic dataset several times larger than the training set will be generated. Detection metrics based on nearest neighbor distances will be applied to classify each generated sample as memorized, spurious, or generalized. The fractions of each sample type will be tracked as a function of training set size. Baselines will include the theoretical predictions from associative memory models and the empirical behavior of diffusion models under standard training regimes. Evaluation will focus on the emergence and prevalence of spurious states, as well as the alignment between theoretical and empirical results.
6df884c0623307124bcccb52500fc720b4f5080f.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a novel theoretical and empirical framework for understanding the memorization-to-generalization transition in diffusion models by recasting them as associative memory systems. It provides new detection metrics for categorizing generated samples and offers the first empirical demonstration of spurious states in practical diffusion model settings. The work establishes a direct connection between energy landscape transitions in DenseAMs and the behavior of diffusion models, offering new insights into the mechanisms underlying memorization, spurious pattern emergence, and generalization in generative models.

6e036e28e7af03bfcdd98ffa254df6644f7657c5.title: GNOT: A General Neural Operator Transformer for Operator Learning
6e036e28e7af03bfcdd98ffa254df6644f7657c5.research_question: How can a general, scalable, and flexible neural operator framework be developed to accurately learn solution operators for partial differential equations (PDEs) in practical scenarios characterized by irregular meshes, multiple input functions, and multi-scale solution complexities?
6e036e28e7af03bfcdd98ffa254df6644f7657c5.hypothesis: A transformer-based neural operator architecture equipped with a heterogeneous normalized attention layer and a geometric gating mechanism can effectively address the challenges of irregular meshes, multiple input functions, and multi-scale phenomena in operator learning, resulting in improved accuracy and scalability across diverse scientific and engineering PDE problems.
6e036e28e7af03bfcdd98ffa254df6644f7657c5.proposed_method: A novel transformer-based neural operator framework, termed the General Neural Operator Transformer (GNOT), will be developed to address the limitations of existing operator learning methods. The method will introduce a Heterogeneous Normalized Attention (HNA) block, which enables flexible and efficient encoding of arbitrary numbers and types of input functions, including boundary shapes, domain-distributed functions, and global parameter vectors, using multiple MLPs and normalized multi-head cross-attention. To address multi-scale phenomena, a geometric gating mechanism inspired by mixture-of-experts (MoE) and domain decomposition will be incorporated, where the gating network leverages geometric coordinates of query points to softly partition the domain and assign expert subnetworks. The architecture will consist of stacked layers of cross-attention followed by self-attention, with skip connections and normalization for stability and expressivity. The framework will be designed to handle large-scale datasets and irregular meshes, and will allow for the incorporation of additional prior information or domain knowledge as needed.
6e036e28e7af03bfcdd98ffa254df6644f7657c5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of benchmark datasets spanning multiple domains, including fluid dynamics (NS2d, NACA, NS2d-c), elasticity (Elasticity), electromagnetism (Inductor2d), and heat conduction (Heat, Heatsink). Each dataset will present unique challenges such as irregular meshes, multiple input functions, and multi-scale solution behavior. The proposed method will be compared against strong baselines, including MIONet, FNO (with interpolation for irregular meshes), GalerkinTransformer, Geo-FNO, and OFormer. Evaluation will be based on the mean relative L2 error between predicted and ground truth solutions. Hyperparameters such as network width, number of layers, and attention heads will be tuned, and experiments will include ablation studies on attention block configurations, the number of experts, and scaling behavior with respect to dataset size and model depth. All models will be trained using the AdamW optimizer and evaluated on both small and large-scale settings.
6e036e28e7af03bfcdd98ffa254df6644f7657c5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a general and scalable transformer-based neural operator framework capable of simultaneously addressing irregular meshes, multiple input functions, and multi-scale phenomena, which have not been jointly tackled by prior methods. The heterogeneous normalized attention layer provides a flexible and efficient encoding for diverse input types, while the geometric gating mechanism enables soft domain decomposition for multi-scale problems. The method demonstrates superior scalability and accuracy across a wide range of challenging PDE benchmarks, reducing prediction errors by up to 50% compared to existing baselines. The architecture is designed to be extensible, data-efficient, and capable of leveraging additional domain knowledge, paving the way for large-scale neural surrogate models in scientific computing.

6e1ee217c8374c0330100556add7414c08317398.title: Quantifying Training Difficulty and Accelerating Convergence in Neural Network-Based PDE Solvers
6e1ee217c8374c0330100556add7414c08317398.research_question: How can the training difficulty of neural network-based partial differential equation (PDE) solvers be quantitatively characterized, and what initialization strategies can be developed to accelerate convergence and improve accuracy across different neural PDE solver frameworks?
6e1ee217c8374c0330100556add7414c08317398.hypothesis: Initialization techniques that increase the effective rank of the kernel associated with neural network-based PDE solvers will reduce training difficulty and accelerate convergence of the training error.
6e1ee217c8374c0330100556add7414c08317398.proposed_method: The proposed research will develop a quantitative framework for assessing the training difficulty of neural network-based PDE solvers by analyzing the eigenvalue distribution of the kernel matrix arising from the gradient descent dynamics. The concept of effective rank will be used as a central metric, with higher effective rank hypothesized to correspond to easier and faster training. Two initialization strategies—partition of unity (PoU) and variance scaling (VS)—will be systematically analyzed for their impact on the effective rank and, consequently, on convergence rates. Theoretical analysis will be conducted on random feature models to derive the relationship between initialization, effective rank, and convergence. These insights will then be extended to deep neural architectures commonly used for PDE solving.
6e1ee217c8374c0330100556add7414c08317398.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using three prominent neural PDE solver frameworks: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), Deep Ritz, and DeepONets. Each framework will be evaluated on a suite of benchmark PDE problems, including both linear and nonlinear cases, with varying domain complexities. For each solver, training runs will be performed using standard initialization, PoU, and VS strategies. The convergence of training error will be tracked, and the effective rank of the kernel will be computed at initialization and during training. Baseline comparisons will include standard random initialization and other common initialization schemes. Evaluation metrics will include convergence rate (epochs to reach a target error), final solution accuracy (e.g., L2 error against ground truth), and stability of training.
6e1ee217c8374c0330100556add7414c08317398.novelty_claims: This research introduces a rigorous, eigenvalue-based quantification of training difficulty for neural PDE solvers, leveraging the effective rank as a predictive measure of convergence behavior. The proposal systematically analyzes and justifies, both theoretically and empirically, the use of partition of unity and variance scaling initialization techniques to enhance effective rank and accelerate convergence. The approach is validated across multiple neural PDE solver architectures, providing generalizable insights and practical guidelines for initialization in scientific machine learning.

6e3a3b7a8a0376d867cad72eedf2f9b746f29a33.title: simple diffusion: End-to-end diffusion for high resolution images
6e3a3b7a8a0376d867cad72eedf2f9b746f29a33.research_question: How can standard diffusion models be effectively trained on high-resolution images while maintaining simplicity and achieving performance comparable to more complex approaches such as latent diffusion or cascaded super-resolution methods?
6e3a3b7a8a0376d867cad72eedf2f9b746f29a33.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by appropriately adjusting the noise schedule for high-resolution images, selectively scaling specific architectural components, strategically applying dropout, and employing downsampling techniques to avoid high-resolution feature maps, a standard diffusion model can achieve state-of-the-art performance on high-resolution image generation without the need for additional complexity.
6e3a3b7a8a0376d867cad72eedf2f9b746f29a33.proposed_method: The proposed method involves several key modifications to the standard denoising diffusion framework to enable efficient and effective high-resolution image generation. First, the noise schedule is adjusted by shifting the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) curve according to the target image resolution, ensuring that appropriate noise is injected at each scale and that global structure is preserved throughout the diffusion process. Second, architectural scaling is focused on the 16×16 resolution level within the U-Net or U-ViT backbone, where increasing the number of blocks or channels at this level yields better performance and computational efficiency. Third, dropout is selectively applied only to lower-resolution layers to provide regularization without incurring excessive memory costs or degrading high-resolution detail. Fourth, downsampling strategies such as discrete wavelet transforms (DWT) or strided convolutions are used at the network input and output to avoid expensive high-resolution feature maps, enabling training of large models without prohibitive memory requirements. Optionally, a multiscale training loss is introduced, weighting losses at various downsampled resolutions to accelerate convergence and improve sample quality at higher resolutions.
6e3a3b7a8a0376d867cad72eedf2f9b746f29a33.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the ImageNet dataset at resolutions of 128×128, 256×256, and 512×512, as well as on text-to-image generation tasks using the COCO dataset. Baseline comparisons include state-of-the-art diffusion models such as ADM, CDM, LDM, DiT, and other generative models like BigGAN and MaskGIT. Evaluation metrics include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) on both train and validation splits, and Inception Score (IS), with ablation studies performed to assess the impact of noise schedule shifts, dropout placement, architectural scaling, downsampling strategies, and the use of multiscale loss. The experimental setup involves training single-stage, end-to-end models (U-Net and U-ViT architectures) with and without text conditioning, using T5-XXL as the text encoder for text-to-image experiments. Training efficiency, memory usage, and sample quality are systematically evaluated.
6e3a3b7a8a0376d867cad72eedf2f9b746f29a33.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a set of simple yet effective modifications that enable standard diffusion models to be trained end-to-end on high-resolution images in pixel space, eliminating the need for latent spaces, cascades, or mixtures of experts. The approach achieves state-of-the-art FID scores among diffusion models without sampling modifiers on ImageNet, and demonstrates, for the first time, that a single-stage diffusion model can generate high-quality images at resolutions up to 512×512. The method also provides the first single-stage text-to-image diffusion model capable of producing competitive results at high resolutions, all while maintaining architectural and training simplicity.

6e41a4cbb34c4d403efb73d74f5be5556b1f13d6.title: Privacy-Preserving In-Context Learning for Large Language Models
6e41a4cbb34c4d403efb73d74f5be5556b1f13d6.research_question: How can in-context learning with large language models be performed in a way that preserves the privacy of sensitive information contained in the in-context exemplars, while maintaining high utility across various natural language processing tasks?
6e41a4cbb34c4d403efb73d74f5be5556b1f13d6.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a differentially private aggregation framework for in-context learning can provide strong privacy guarantees for sensitive exemplar data without significant degradation in model performance across text classification and language generation tasks.
6e41a4cbb34c4d403efb73d74f5be5556b1f13d6.proposed_method: A general paradigm for privacy-preserving in-context learning (DP-ICL) will be developed, leveraging the sample-and-aggregate framework. The approach consists of four main phases: (1) partitioning the sensitive exemplar dataset into disjoint subsets, (2) pairing each subset with the query to create multiple exemplar-query pairs, (3) prompting the large language model (LLM) with each pair to obtain individual responses, and (4) aggregating these responses using differentially private mechanisms before returning the final answer to the user. For text classification, the Report-Noisy-Max mechanism with Gaussian noise will be used to privately select the class label. For language generation, two novel aggregation techniques will be introduced: Embedding Space Aggregation (ESA), which projects outputs into a semantic embedding space and privately estimates the mean embedding before reconstructing a sentence, and Keyword Space Aggregation (KSA), which identifies frequent keywords in outputs and privately selects them using either the joint exponential mechanism or the propose-test-release paradigm, followed by sentence reconstruction via LLM prompting.
