6e41a4cbb34c4d403efb73d74f5be5556b1f13d6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of tasks, including text classification (using SST-2, Amazon, AGNews, and TREC datasets), document question answering (using the DocVQA dataset), and dialog summarization (using the SAMSum dataset). For text classification, GPT-3 Babbage and Davinci models will be used with 4-shot in-context learning and compared against zero-shot, non-private, and aggregation baselines. For language generation, both ESA and KSA methods will be evaluated, with OpenLLaMA-13B used for question answering and GPT-3 Davinci for summarization. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy for classification, and ROUGE, BLEU, and Levenshtein similarity for generation tasks. Privacy budgets (ε) of 1, 3, and 8 will be tested to assess the privacy-utility tradeoff, and ablation studies will be performed to analyze the effects of ensemble size and query count.
6e41a4cbb34c4d403efb73d74f5be5556b1f13d6.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a unified, task-agnostic paradigm for differentially private in-context learning applicable to both classification and complex language generation tasks. Novel aggregation mechanisms are developed for high-dimensional language outputs, including the use of embedding and keyword spaces for private consensus. The approach is claimed to achieve strong privacy guarantees with minimal utility loss, outperforming prior methods restricted to low-dimensional output spaces and demonstrating applicability to real-world, challenging NLP tasks.

6e754273d54a91371efbc928cd6b156364d517da.title: ViperGPT: Visual Inference via Python Execution for Reasoning
6e754273d54a91371efbc928cd6b156364d517da.research_question: How can complex visual queries requiring both perception and reasoning be addressed in a way that improves interpretability, generalization, and flexibility, without the need for additional task-specific training?
6e754273d54a91371efbc928cd6b156364d517da.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging large language models for code generation, in combination with modular APIs to access vision and language models, enables the synthesis of interpretable, compositional programs that can solve a wide range of visual reasoning tasks in a zero-shot manner, achieving competitive or superior performance to end-to-end models.
6e754273d54a91371efbc928cd6b156364d517da.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed that utilizes large language models trained on code (such as Codex) to generate Python programs in response to natural language visual queries. These programs are constructed by composing calls to a set of modular APIs, each exposing pretrained vision or language models (e.g., object detection, depth estimation, image-text similarity, external knowledge queries). The generated code is executed using the Python interpreter, enabling logical operations, control flow, and mathematical computations in conjunction with perceptual modules. The API specification, including function signatures and docstrings, is provided as context to the language model, which then generates a function that processes the input image or video and returns the answer to the query. This approach is training-free for new tasks, highly interpretable (as intermediate results and logic are explicit in the code), and easily extensible to new modules or capabilities.
6e754273d54a91371efbc928cd6b156364d517da.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of benchmarks to evaluate the framework's capabilities: RefCOCO and RefCOCO+ for visual grounding, GQA for compositional image question answering, OK-VQA for knowledge-dependent visual question answering, and NExT-QA for video causal and temporal reasoning. The framework will be compared against state-of-the-art end-to-end and zero-shot baselines, including models like GLIP, BLIP-2, and Flamingo. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy for question answering tasks and IoU for visual grounding. The experimental setup involves providing only the API specification and no task-specific training, with all reasoning and perception performed by the generated Python code and the underlying pretrained modules. Additional analyses will include interventional ablations to assess the importance of different modules and the impact of context conditioning.
6e754273d54a91371efbc928cd6b156364d517da.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a fully modular, code-generation-based framework for visual reasoning that unifies perception and reasoning in a single system without additional training. It enables interpretable, step-by-step programmatic solutions to complex visual queries, supports arbitrary output types, and is adaptable to advances in underlying vision and language models. The method achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot performance on multiple challenging benchmarks and demonstrates emergent abilities such as compositional reasoning, external knowledge integration, and temporal/causal video understanding. The framework is general, extensible, and provides a new paradigm for explainable and flexible visual inference.

6e7dc4ba40b82b7cf708b622d801afaee845ff80.title: Robust Contrastive Learning Using Negative Samples with Diminished Semantics
6e7dc4ba40b82b7cf708b622d801afaee845ff80.research_question: How can contrastive learning methods be improved to learn more robust and generalizable visual representations that are less dependent on non-semantic, superficial features such as texture and local patches, particularly under domain shifts and out-of-distribution scenarios?
6e7dc4ba40b82b7cf708b622d801afaee845ff80.hypothesis: Contrastive learning models trained with negative samples that preserve only non-semantic features, generated through texture-based and patch-based augmentations, will rely less on superficial cues and more on semantic content, resulting in improved robustness and generalization, especially under domain shift.
6e7dc4ba40b82b7cf708b622d801afaee845ff80.proposed_method: A novel approach will be developed to generate negative samples for contrastive learning by applying two augmentation strategies: texture-based and patch-based. The texture-based method synthesizes images that retain local texture information from the input image while diminishing global semantic structure, using classic texture synthesis algorithms and patches sampled from both the center and random locations of the image. The patch-based method constructs negative samples by tiling randomly sampled patches of varying sizes from the input image, thereby preserving local statistics but disrupting semantic coherence. These non-semantic negative samples will be integrated into contrastive learning frameworks (such as MoCo and BYOL) by extending the loss functions to penalize similarity between the representations of the original image and its non-semantic counterpart, controlled by a scaling parameter α. The methodology will also investigate the effect of varying α to control the shape-texture bias in learned representations.
6e7dc4ba40b82b7cf708b622d801afaee845ff80.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using MoCo and BYOL contrastive learning frameworks on multiple datasets, including ImageNet-100, ImageNet-1K, and STL-10. Evaluation will be performed on both in-domain and out-of-domain (OOD) datasets, such as ImageNet-C (corruptions), ImageNet-S (sketch), Stylized-ImageNet, and ImageNet-R (rendition), to assess robustness to domain shifts. Baselines will include standard MoCo-v2, BYOL, and other self-supervised methods like InsDis, CMC, and InfoMin, as well as hard negative mining techniques (e.g., MoCHi, IFM). Performance will be measured using top-1 accuracy and mean corruption error (mCE), and results will be averaged over multiple runs to report mean and standard deviation. Additional analyses will include ablation studies on memory bank size, the impact of removing color jittering, and fine-grained evaluation of shape-texture trade-offs using the newly introduced ImageNet-Texture dataset.
6e7dc4ba40b82b7cf708b622d801afaee845ff80.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new strategy for generating hard negative samples for contrastive learning by explicitly constructing non-semantic negatives through texture-based and patch-based augmentations. This approach is claimed to improve generalization and robustness, particularly under domain shifts, by reducing reliance on superficial features. The introduction of the ImageNet-Texture dataset enables fine-grained analysis of shape and texture biases in CNNs. The methodology provides a controllable mechanism (via α) to adjust the shape-texture trade-off in learned representations, offering new insights into the role of negative samples and feature biases in contrastive learning.

6ea7f321ae9fc7c8ee470ae142a4c3ff1a6f878c.title: Hear The Flow: Optical Flow-Based Self-Supervised Visual Sound Source Localization
6ea7f321ae9fc7c8ee470ae142a4c3ff1a6f878c.research_question: How can visual sound source localization in videos be improved in a self-supervised setting, particularly by leveraging informative priors to enhance the association between audio and visual modalities?
6ea7f321ae9fc7c8ee470ae142a4c3ff1a6f878c.hypothesis: Incorporating optical flow as an informative prior into a self-supervised visual sound source localization framework will improve the accuracy and robustness of localizing sounding objects in videos, especially by focusing attention on moving objects that are likely to be sound sources.
6ea7f321ae9fc7c8ee470ae142a4c3ff1a6f878c.proposed_method: A novel self-supervised localization network will be developed that integrates optical flow as a prior to enhance audio-visual association. The method will extract visual features from video frames, audio features from corresponding audio segments, and optical flow features from consecutive video frames using separate ResNet18-based encoders. A cross-attention mechanism will be designed to combine visual and optical flow features, generating a spatial prior that highlights moving objects. This prior will be added to the visual feature map, and the enhanced features will be used to compute audio-visual similarity via cosine similarity. Pseudo-masks will be generated by thresholding the similarity matrix, and a self-supervised contrastive loss will be employed to train the network end-to-end, without requiring explicit ground truth annotations.
6ea7f321ae9fc7c8ee470ae142a4c3ff1a6f878c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two large-scale benchmark datasets: Flickr SoundNet and VGG Sound, with both 10k and 144k sample subsets for training. Evaluation will be performed on the Flickr SoundNet test set (250 annotated pairs) and the VGG Sound Source test set (5000 annotated pairs across 220 categories), using consensus Intersection over Union (cIoU) at a 0.5 threshold and Area Under Curve (AUC) of cIoU as metrics. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art self-supervised and contrastive learning methods for sound source localization, such as LVS, SSPL, AVObject, and others. Ablation studies will assess the impact of optical flow priors, pretraining strategies, encoder freezing, and flow encoder architectures. Implementation details include using ResNet18 backbones, Adam optimizer with a learning rate of 1e-3, batch size 128, and 100 training epochs.
6ea7f321ae9fc7c8ee470ae142a4c3ff1a6f878c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the use of optical flow as an explicit informative prior for self-supervised visual sound source localization, addressing the challenge of associating audio with the correct visual region in the absence of annotations. A novel cross-attention mechanism between visual and flow features is developed to generate spatial priors that focus on moving objects, complementing object-centric priors from pretrained vision encoders. The method demonstrates significant improvements over previous state-of-the-art approaches on standard benchmarks, and extensive ablation studies validate the effectiveness and necessity of incorporating such priors in self-supervised frameworks.

6eab2a84d3f9ab7e9dfe04d568b93a0045b09b6f.title: Flat Channels to Infinity in Neural Loss Landscapes
6eab2a84d3f9ab7e9dfe04d568b93a0045b09b6f.research_question: What are the underlying geometric and functional structures present in the loss landscapes of neural networks, and how do these structures influence optimization dynamics and the computational capabilities of neural architectures?
6eab2a84d3f9ab7e9dfe04d568b93a0045b09b6f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the loss landscapes of neural networks contain previously uncharacterized, extremely flat channels leading to local minima at infinity, and that these channels endow the network with novel computational capabilities, such as the emergence of gated linear units.
6eab2a84d3f9ab7e9dfe04d568b93a0045b09b6f.proposed_method: The proposed research will systematically investigate the loss landscapes of fully connected neural networks, focusing on the identification and characterization of flat channels that extend to infinity. Analytical techniques will be used to derive the geometric properties of these channels, particularly in relation to symmetry-induced saddle lines created by neuron duplication. Gradient flow dynamics will be analyzed using both ordinary differential equation (ODE) solvers and standard optimization algorithms (e.g., SGD, ADAM) to track the behavior of parameters in the vicinity of these channels. The functional consequences of converging along these channels will be examined by reparameterizing neuron pairs and analyzing the limiting behavior, with particular attention to the emergence of gated linear units and higher-order derivative structures.
6eab2a84d3f9ab7e9dfe04d568b93a0045b09b6f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) with varying architectures (number of layers, hidden units, and input dimensions) and across multiple datasets, including synthetic regression targets such as the modified Rosenbrock function and Gaussian process-generated data with different kernel scales. Networks will be initialized using standard schemes (e.g., Glorot normal), and both full-batch gradient flow and stochastic optimizers will be employed. The identification of channels will rely on criteria such as diverging output weights, converging input weights, and the alignment of parameter updates with the saddle line subspace. Evaluation metrics will include the frequency of channel convergence, loss values at channel and finite-norm minima, and the spectral properties of the Hessian (maximum and minimum eigenvalues) to assess sharpness and flatness. Additional analyses will include perturbation studies, jump procedures to accelerate movement along channels, and comparisons across activation functions.
6eab2a84d3f9ab7e9dfe04d568b93a0045b09b6f.novelty_claims: The research introduces the concept of 'channels to infinity'—extremely flat regions in the loss landscape that are asymptotically parallel to symmetry-induced saddle lines and lead to local minima at infinity. It provides a comprehensive geometric and dynamical characterization of these channels, demonstrates their prevalence across architectures and datasets, and reveals their functional role in enabling the spontaneous emergence of gated linear units within fully connected layers. The findings offer new insights into the benign nature of neural loss landscapes and the computational flexibility of neural networks, with implications for optimization, generalization, and network design.

6eb46737bf0ef916a7f906ec6a8da82a45ffb623.title: Open Problems and Fundamental Limitations of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
6eb46737bf0ef916a7f906ec6a8da82a45ffb623.research_question: What are the open problems and fundamental limitations of reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) as a method for aligning AI systems with human goals, and how can RLHF be systematically improved or complemented to address these challenges?
6eb46737bf0ef916a7f906ec6a8da82a45ffb623.proposed_method: A comprehensive research agenda will be developed to systematically identify, categorize, and analyze the challenges and limitations inherent in RLHF, focusing on its application to large language models and other advanced AI systems. The methodology will involve constructing a taxonomy of RLHF challenges, divided into issues related to human feedback collection, reward modeling, and policy optimization, as well as joint training dynamics. The research will further propose and evaluate technical, methodological, and governance-based interventions to address tractable challenges within the RLHF framework, while also identifying fundamental limitations that may require alternative or complementary approaches. Additionally, the proposal includes developing auditing and disclosure standards to improve transparency and societal oversight of RLHF-trained systems.
6eb46737bf0ef916a7f906ec6a8da82a45ffb623.experiment_details: Empirical studies will be conducted to investigate the impact of evaluator selection, feedback type, and data quality on RLHF outcomes, using both simulated and real-world datasets derived from large language model deployments. Comparative experiments will be designed to benchmark RLHF against alternative alignment and oversight techniques, with baselines including standard RLHF pipelines, direct preference optimization, and language-based feedback methods. Evaluation metrics will encompass alignment with human preferences, robustness to adversarial attacks, bias amplification, and policy generalization across deployment distributions. Key experimental setups will include ablation studies on feedback modalities, reward model architectures, and policy optimization algorithms, as well as audits of transparency and disclosure practices in RLHF deployments.
6eb46737bf0ef916a7f906ec6a8da82a45ffb623.novelty_claims: The proposed research offers a systematic and comprehensive taxonomy of RLHF challenges, distinguishing between tractable and fundamental limitations. It advances the field by integrating technical, methodological, and governance perspectives, emphasizing the need for multi-layered safety strategies beyond RLHF alone. The proposal also innovates by calling for standardized auditing and disclosure practices to enhance societal oversight, and by critically examining the relationship between RLHF as an alignment strategy and as an engineering tool. This approach aims to set a new research agenda for the responsible development and deployment of RLHF-aligned AI systems.

6ec775004e6f4e59dfdfdaf965c64895cbb338d1.title: Diffusion Policies for Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Offline Reinforcement Learning
6ec775004e6f4e59dfdfdaf965c64895cbb338d1.research_question: How can offline reinforcement learning policies be improved to generalize effectively to out-of-distribution (OOD) states, particularly when large portions of the state space are missing from the training data?
6ec775004e6f4e59dfdfdaf965c64895cbb338d1.hypothesis: Incorporating a state reconstruction feature learning signal into diffusion-based offline reinforcement learning policies will promote the learning of generalizable state representations, thereby improving OOD generalization and policy robustness compared to existing diffusion policy baselines.
6ec775004e6f4e59dfdfdaf965c64895cbb338d1.proposed_method: A novel offline RL method, State Reconstruction for Diffusion Policies (SRDP), will be developed by augmenting diffusion-based policy architectures with an auxiliary state reconstruction loss. The method will employ a shared feature extraction module that jointly processes the state, action (with added noise at each diffusion timestep), and time embedding, producing a latent representation. This representation will be fed into two heads: one for predicting the noise in the diffusion process (policy head) and another for reconstructing the input state (state reconstruction head). The overall training objective will combine the standard diffusion policy loss and the state reconstruction loss, weighted by a tunable scaling parameter. During each training iteration, the state reconstruction loss will be propagated through the network at every randomly selected diffusion timestep, encouraging the learning of robust and generalizable state features that can extrapolate to OOD regions.
6ec775004e6f4e59dfdfdaf965c64895cbb338d1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of environments to evaluate OOD generalization and policy performance. A custom 2D Multimodal Contextual Bandit environment will be designed, with training data restricted to a small region and evaluation performed on a much larger state space, to directly test OOD generalization. Real-world experiments will be performed on a 6-DoF UR10 robotic arm in a multimodal reaching task, with training data limited to a subset of the workspace. Additionally, standard continuous control benchmarks from D4RL (including AntMaze, HalfCheetah, Hopper, and Walker2d) and a sparse-reward maze navigation task with missing data will be used. Baselines will include Diffusion-QL, BC-Diffusion, and other behavior cloning variants. Evaluation metrics will include normalized return scores, Chamfer distance between generated and ground-truth action distributions, and convergence speed. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of the state reconstruction loss scaling parameter.
6ec775004e6f4e59dfdfdaf965c64895cbb338d1.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new approach for OOD generalization in offline RL by integrating state reconstruction feature learning into diffusion policy architectures. This approach enables the learning of robust, generalizable representations that improve policy performance in settings with significant distribution shift and missing data. The method demonstrates faster convergence, superior OOD generalization, and improved performance on both custom and standard RL benchmarks compared to existing diffusion policy baselines. The framework is validated in both simulation and real-robot experiments, highlighting its practical applicability and effectiveness in challenging offline RL scenarios.

6ecf883162013121b3490dee2c4b519f8621b5b7.title: Capability Localization: Capabilities Can be Localized rather than Individual Knowledge
6ecf883162013121b3490dee2c4b519f8621b5b7.research_question: Can the internal parameters of large language models be mapped to localized capabilities, rather than to individual pieces of knowledge, and how can these capability-related parameters be systematically identified and leveraged to enhance model performance?
6ecf883162013121b3490dee2c4b519f8621b5b7.hypothesis: The internal parameters of large language models are more closely associated with generalizable capabilities (commonalities across data/tasks) rather than with individual knowledge items, and these capability neurons can be reliably localized and manipulated to improve or impair model performance.
6ecf883162013121b3490dee2c4b519f8621b5b7.proposed_method: A Commonality Neuron Localization (CNL) method will be developed to systematically identify neurons in large language models that correspond to shared capabilities across datasets or tasks. The approach expands upon gradient-based attribution techniques, computing the expected contribution of each neuron across a dataset by integrating gradients of model outputs with respect to neuron activations. Neurons with attribution scores significantly deviating from the mean (as determined by a threshold on standard deviation) are selected as capability neurons. These neurons are then manipulated—either fine-tuned or masked—to assess their impact on model performance, and their overlap across different datasets is measured to evaluate their generalizability.
6ecf883162013121b3490dee2c4b519f8621b5b7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using several datasets reflecting distinct capabilities: GSM8K and Meta Math for mathematical reasoning, Code25K for programming, and Emotion and IMDB for sentiment analysis and language comprehension. The base models include Llama2-7B, Llama2-13B, and GPTJ-6B. The CNL method will be applied to locate capability neurons for each dataset, and their overlap and intersection-over-union (IoU) will be calculated to assess consistency. Enhancement experiments will involve fine-tuning only the located neurons and comparing performance to random and complementary neuron sets, while erasure experiments will mask these neurons to observe performance degradation. Evaluation metrics include accuracy on validation/test sets, overlap/IoU of located neurons, and the impact on performance (IPP) when manipulating localized parameters. Baseline comparisons will be made against existing knowledge localization methods (KN, ROME, KC) using unified evaluation indicators.
6ecf883162013121b3490dee2c4b519f8621b5b7.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a shift from localizing individual knowledge to localizing model capabilities, providing a new perspective on parameter-function mapping in large language models. The CNL method offers a principled, gradient-based approach to identifying capability neurons with high consistency and granularity. Experimental results are expected to demonstrate that manipulating a small subset of capability neurons can significantly enhance or impair model performance, and that these neurons generalize across datasets. This approach challenges prior assumptions about knowledge localization and establishes a direct mapping between internal parameters and model capabilities, offering new tools for model interpretability and targeted model editing.

6ed030599cec25dc410c957223a085e3f153b61e.title: Classical surrogates for quantum learning models
6ed030599cec25dc410c957223a085e3f153b61e.research_question: Can classical surrogate models be efficiently constructed for variational quantum learning models, and how do these surrogates compare to their quantum counterparts in terms of trainability, performance, and generalization on practical learning tasks?
6ed030599cec25dc410c957223a085e3f153b61e.hypothesis: Variational quantum learning models, particularly re-uploading models with certain data encoding structures, admit efficient classical surrogates that can match or outperform the quantum models in training performance and trainability, potentially leaving only generalization as a possible domain of quantum advantage.
6ed030599cec25dc410c957223a085e3f153b61e.proposed_method: A framework will be developed to construct classical surrogate models for a broad class of variational quantum learning models, specifically those based on parametrized quantum circuits with re-uploading architectures. The approach exploits the fact that the outputs of these quantum models can be expressed as truncated Fourier series with a polynomially bounded number of coefficients, determined by the circuit structure and data encoding. The surrogate is constructed by sampling the quantum model's outputs on a grid, estimating expectation values, and then solving a least-squares problem to recover the Fourier coefficients efficiently. The surrogate model is then implemented as a neural network with a single linear layer, where the weights correspond to the learned Fourier coefficients, allowing for direct optimization using stochastic gradient descent.
6ed030599cec25dc410c957223a085e3f153b61e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several regression tasks, including a synthetic dataset generated by Scikit-learn's make_regression function, a dataset sampled from a randomly initialized quantum re-uploading model, and the California housing dataset as a standard regression benchmark. For each task, quantum learning models with varying expressivity (number of layers and block layers) will be trained and compared to their respective classical surrogates. Evaluation metrics will include training and test loss, convergence behavior, and trainability as measured by the smoothness and variance of loss curves. Both quantum and classical models will be optimized using the LBFGS algorithm, and care will be taken to monitor overfitting by tracking validation loss.
6ed030599cec25dc410c957223a085e3f153b61e.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the concept of a classical surrogate for quantum learning models, providing a formal definition and an efficient construction protocol for a large class of variational quantum circuits. It establishes that for re-uploading models with specific data encodings, the surrogate can be constructed with polynomial overhead and offers a natural benchmark for quantum advantage claims. The approach enables direct optimization of the surrogate and demonstrates that, for contemporary circuit ansätze, classical surrogates can match or outperform quantum models in trainability and performance, highlighting the need to better understand inductive biases for any potential quantum advantage.

6ed5dd9247520fee18a341f596dc92f2aaaac2ba.title: MolDiff: Addressing the Atom-Bond Inconsistency Problem in 3D Molecule Diffusion Generation
6ed5dd9247520fee18a341f596dc92f2aaaac2ba.research_question: How can the generation of 3D molecular structures be improved to ensure consistency between atom positions and chemical bonds, thereby producing more realistic and chemically valid molecules?
6ed5dd9247520fee18a341f596dc92f2aaaac2ba.hypothesis: Jointly modeling the generation of atoms and bonds in a diffusion-based framework, with explicit mechanisms to maintain their consistency, will significantly improve the validity, structural quality, and drug-likeness of generated 3D molecules compared to existing methods that treat atoms and bonds separately.
6ed5dd9247520fee18a341f596dc92f2aaaac2ba.proposed_method: A novel diffusion-based generative model, MolDiff, will be developed to simultaneously generate atom types, atom positions, and chemical bonds in 3D molecules. The method introduces a discrete diffusion process for both atom and bond types, and a continuous process for atom positions, with a specialized noise schedule that perturbs bonds and atoms at different rates to maintain their physical and chemical relationships. An E(3)-equivariant graph neural network will be designed to update both atom and bond representations during message passing, ensuring equivariance to 3D transformations. Additionally, a bond predictor network will be trained to guide atom position generation by providing gradients that maximize the confidence of chemically plausible bonds, thus improving the geometric accuracy of generated molecules. The model will use a two-stage noise schedule: first diffusing bonds to the prior while only slightly perturbing atoms, then focusing on atom diffusion after bonds are removed, maintaining realistic atom-bond relationships throughout the process.
6ed5dd9247520fee18a341f596dc92f2aaaac2ba.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted primarily on the GEOM-Drug dataset, focusing on molecules with major elements (C, N, O, F, P, S, Cl) and excluding hydrogens, with additional evaluations including minor elements and hydrogen atoms as well as on the QM9 dataset. Baselines will include EDM (a prior 3D diffusion model), MolDiff variants that exclude bonds during diffusion or use continuous embeddings, and post-processing strategies for bond assignment (lookup tables, neural predictors, OpenBabel). Evaluation metrics will cover validity, connectivity, and success rate (basic chemical correctness), as well as novelty, diversity, uniqueness, and similarity to validation sets. Further, metrics specific to drug-likeness (QED, SA score, Lipinski rules), 3D structural accuracy (RMSD, bond length/angle/dihedral distributions), bond statistics, and ring system distributions will be used. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the noise schedule and bond-guided generation. For each model, 1000 valid and complete molecules will be generated and analyzed, with statistical significance assessed over multiple runs.
6ed5dd9247520fee18a341f596dc92f2aaaac2ba.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to jointly generate atom types, atom positions, and chemical bonds in a 3D diffusion framework, explicitly addressing the atom-bond inconsistency problem that plagues existing models. The introduction of a two-stage, bond-first noise schedule and the use of an E(3)-equivariant network that updates both atom and bond representations are novel contributions. The method also innovates by incorporating a bond predictor for gradient-based guidance of atom positions, directly linking geometric and chemical constraints during generation. New evaluation metrics tailored to 3D molecular quality and drug-likeness are proposed to more comprehensively assess generative performance. The approach is claimed to achieve a three-fold improvement in success rate and to generate molecules with significantly better structural and chemical quality compared to prior methods.

6edd112383ad494f5f2eba72b6f4ffae122ce61f.title: Interpretability in the Wild: a Circuit for Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 small
6edd112383ad494f5f2eba72b6f4ffae122ce61f.research_question: How can the internal mechanisms of large language models, such as GPT-2 small, be mechanistically interpreted and reverse-engineered to explain their behavior on linguistically meaningful natural language tasks?
6edd112383ad494f5f2eba72b6f4ffae122ce61f.hypothesis: A systematic circuit-based analysis, leveraging causal interventions and interpretability techniques, can identify and validate the specific internal components and interactions responsible for complex language behaviors in transformer models.
6edd112383ad494f5f2eba72b6f4ffae122ce61f.proposed_method: A comprehensive methodology will be developed to reverse-engineer the computation underlying indirect object identification (IOI) in GPT-2 small. The approach will iteratively trace the flow of information from the output logits back through the model's computational graph, focusing on attention heads as primary components. Key techniques will include 'path patching' (a causal intervention that replaces activations along specific computational paths), mean ablation knockouts (replacing node activations with their mean over a reference distribution), and detailed attention pattern analysis. The method will categorize attention heads into functional classes based on their roles in the IOI task, validate their hypothesized functions through targeted counterfactual experiments, and construct a human-interpretable circuit responsible for the task. Additional validation will be performed using quantitative criteria such as faithfulness, completeness, and minimality, ensuring the circuit's explanatory adequacy.
6edd112383ad494f5f2eba72b6f4ffae122ce61f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using GPT-2 small, evaluated on a custom-generated IOI dataset comprising over 100,000 examples created from 15 linguistic templates with randomized names, places, and items. Performance will be measured using logit difference and indirect object (IO) probability, averaged over the dataset. Baseline comparisons will include the full model, naive circuits, and ablated versions with specific attention head classes removed. Evaluation metrics will focus on the circuit's ability to replicate model behavior (faithfulness), account for all necessary components (completeness), and avoid unnecessary complexity (minimality). Systematic knockout and path patching experiments will be used to probe the necessity and sufficiency of identified circuit components, and greedy optimization will be employed to search for potential missing or redundant elements.
6edd112383ad494f5f2eba72b6f4ffae122ce61f.novelty_claims: The proposed research aims to deliver the largest and most detailed end-to-end mechanistic explanation of a natural language behavior in a transformer-based language model to date. The approach introduces novel techniques, such as path patching for tracing causal information flow and a rigorous framework for circuit validation based on faithfulness, completeness, and minimality. The methodology is designed to uncover both primary and backup mechanisms, reveal unexpected uses of known structures (e.g., induction heads), and systematically address the challenges of redundancy and compensation in model circuits. This work is expected to provide a scalable blueprint for mechanistic interpretability in larger models and more complex tasks.

6eddfde78d5f6b10206f00675102fe3ddef8ff89.title: Structured World Models from Human Videos
6eddfde78d5f6b10206f00675102fe3ddef8ff89.research_question: How can robots efficiently acquire general manipulation skills in diverse real-world settings by leveraging large-scale human video data, while minimizing the need for extensive robot-specific data collection and task supervision?
6eddfde78d5f6b10206f00675102fe3ddef8ff89.hypothesis: Pre-training a structured, human-centric world model on large-scale human video data and fine-tuning it with a small amount of unsupervised robot interaction data will enable robots to efficiently learn and generalize manipulation skills across diverse tasks and environments.
6eddfde78d5f6b10206f00675102fe3ddef8ff89.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that constructs a structured, morphology-invariant action space based on visual affordances extracted from human videos. The method will use computer vision techniques to detect human hand-object interactions, identifying grasp and post-grasp points in video frames and mapping them to a transferable action representation. A world model, based on the Dreamer architecture with enhancements for high-dimensional visual input (e.g., NVAE encoder), will be pre-trained on large-scale passive human video datasets to learn environment dynamics and affordance-based actions. Subsequently, the world model will be fine-tuned using a small, unsupervised set of robot interaction trajectories collected by executing the learned affordance actions in the robot's environment. The final model will plan in the affordance action space to achieve specified goal images, using a hybrid action space that allows both affordance-based and Cartesian end-effector actions, with planning performed via trajectory optimization (e.g., CEM) in the learned feature space.
6eddfde78d5f6b10206f00675102fe3ddef8ff89.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two real-world robot platforms (Franka Emika arm and Hello Stretch mobile manipulator) across six diverse manipulation tasks, including cabinet opening, vegetable picking, knife lifting, drawer opening, dishwasher opening, and garbage can opening. The world model will be pre-trained on approximately 55,000 clips from the Epic-Kitchens human video dataset, using the 100 Days of Hands detector to extract hand-object affordances. Fine-tuning will use less than 30 minutes of unsupervised robot interaction data per task. Baselines will include variants without world models, without human video pre-training, and without structured affordance actions (e.g., behavior cloning, pixel-based actions, and Cartesian-only actions). Evaluation metrics will include task success rates over 25 trials per task, as well as qualitative analysis of model predictions and continual improvement with additional data. Feature-space distance to goal images will be used for planning and evaluation.
6eddfde78d5f6b10206f00675102fe3ddef8ff89.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a structured, human-centric action space grounded in visual affordances learned from human videos, enabling transfer of manipulation knowledge from humans to robots across morphology gaps. It leverages large-scale internet video data for world model pre-training, followed by efficient, unsupervised fine-tuning on robot data, thus achieving high sample efficiency and generalization across diverse tasks. The hybrid action space allows seamless integration of affordance-based and low-level Cartesian actions, supporting both efficient learning and fine-grained control. The method enables training of a single joint world model across multiple robots and tasks, demonstrating strong performance and continual improvement with minimal real-world data collection.

6ee96ee0d32816658daa507e2228b037768f148b.title: Curriculum Temperature for Knowledge Distillation
6ee96ee0d32816658daa507e2228b037768f148b.research_question: How can the process of knowledge distillation be improved by dynamically adjusting the difficulty level of the distillation task during student model training?
6ee96ee0d32816658daa507e2228b037768f148b.hypothesis: A curriculum-based approach that dynamically and adversarially adjusts the temperature parameter in the knowledge distillation loss will improve student model performance compared to using a fixed temperature, and can be seamlessly integrated into existing distillation frameworks with negligible computational overhead.
6ee96ee0d32816658daa507e2228b037768f148b.proposed_method: A novel curriculum-based technique, termed Curriculum Temperature for Knowledge Distillation (CTKD), is proposed to control the difficulty of the distillation task by dynamically learning a temperature parameter during student training. The temperature is optimized adversarially via a gradient reversal layer, such that it maximizes the distillation loss, thereby increasing the learning difficulty for the student in a controlled manner. Two versions of the learnable temperature module are introduced: Global-T, which predicts a single temperature for all instances, and Instance-T, which predicts a temperature for each instance in a batch using a 2-layer MLP. The curriculum is implemented by gradually increasing a scaling parameter (lambda) for the distillation loss according to a cosine schedule, following an easy-to-hard learning paradigm. The approach is designed as a plug-in module that can be integrated into various knowledge distillation frameworks without significant computational cost.
6ee96ee0d32816658daa507e2228b037768f148b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard benchmarks including CIFAR-100, ImageNet-2012, and MS-COCO. Various neural network architectures such as VGG, ResNet, WideResNet, ShuffleNet, and MobileNet will be used for teacher-student pairs. The proposed method will be evaluated as a plug-in to multiple state-of-the-art distillation frameworks (e.g., Vanilla KD, PKT, SP, VID, CRD, SRRL, DKD). Performance will be measured using top-1 and top-5 classification accuracy for image classification tasks, and mean Average Precision (mAP) for object detection. Baselines will include fixed-temperature distillation and grid search for optimal temperature, with ablation studies to assess the impact of curriculum strategies, adversarial temperature learning, and the choice of global versus instance-wise temperature modules. Computational efficiency will be reported in terms of MACs and training time per epoch.
6ee96ee0d32816658daa507e2228b037768f148b.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a dynamic, adversarially-learned temperature parameter for knowledge distillation, organized via a curriculum learning strategy that increases task difficulty from easy to hard. Unlike prior works that require inefficient grid search or meta-learning with additional validation sets, this approach learns the temperature directly during training with negligible computational overhead. The method is general, easy to integrate as a plug-in to existing distillation frameworks, and is shown to consistently improve student model performance across multiple tasks and architectures. The introduction of both global and instance-wise temperature modules further enhances flexibility and effectiveness.

6f3206263bc7682c3abd6a41672c6444db30b78e.title: Modulate Your Spectrum in Self-Supervised Learning
6f3206263bc7682c3abd6a41672c6444db30b78e.research_question: How can the spectrum of feature embeddings in self-supervised learning (SSL) be modulated to prevent dimensional collapse and improve representation quality, and are there functions beyond traditional whitening that can achieve this goal?
6f3206263bc7682c3abd6a41672c6444db30b78e.hypothesis: Modulating the spectrum of embeddings via spectral transformations, including but not limited to whitening, can prevent dimensional collapse in SSL. Specifically, combining iterative normalization with a trace loss will guide the spectrum toward equal-eigenvalue distributions, resulting in superior and more robust learned representations.
6f3206263bc7682c3abd6a41672c6444db30b78e.proposed_method: A general spectral transformation (ST) framework will be developed to modulate the spectrum of embedding vectors in joint embedding architectures for SSL. This framework will define a transformation function g(·) applied to the covariance matrix of embeddings, mapping its spectrum to a desired distribution. Several instances of ST will be explored, including power functions and iterative normalization (IterNorm), to empirically and theoretically investigate their ability to prevent collapse. A novel method, IterNorm with trace loss (INTL), will be introduced, where IterNorm approximates whitening via Newton's iteration and an additional trace loss penalty is imposed on the transformed output to encourage the covariance matrix to have equal eigenvalues. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to prove that INTL avoids collapse and modulates the spectrum as intended.
6f3206263bc7682c3abd6a41672c6444db30b78e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard SSL benchmarks including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet-100, and ImageNet, using ResNet-18 and ResNet-50 backbones. The proposed INTL method will be compared against a range of state-of-the-art contrastive and non-contrastive baselines such as SimCLR, MoCoV2, BYOL, SwAV, SimSiam, W-MSE, Shuffled-DBN, Barlow Twins, VICReg, Zero-CL, and CW-RGP. Evaluation will include linear classification and 5-nearest neighbor accuracy, as well as transfer learning to downstream tasks like COCO object detection and instance segmentation. Ablation studies will assess robustness to batch size, embedding dimension, augmentation strategies, and backbone architectures. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy, 5-nn accuracy, and COCO AP metrics. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by adhering to established protocols and using consistent data augmentations and training schedules.
6f3206263bc7682c3abd6a41672c6444db30b78e.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a general spectral transformation framework that extends beyond traditional whitening to explore a broader class of spectrum-modulating functions for SSL. It presents a new method, IterNorm with trace loss (INTL), which theoretically and empirically prevents dimensional collapse by modulating the embedding spectrum toward equal eigenvalues. INTL achieves state-of-the-art or superior performance on multiple SSL benchmarks, demonstrates robustness with small batch sizes, and provides new theoretical insights into the mechanisms underlying feature collapse and whitening losses in SSL.

6f648aeb5c5219cf021840eaf3df03ac86cebff4.title: The Stable Signature: Rooting Watermarks in Latent Diffusion Models
6f648aeb5c5219cf021840eaf3df03ac86cebff4.research_question: How can invisible and robust watermarks be natively embedded into images generated by Latent Diffusion Models (LDMs) to enable reliable detection and identification of AI-generated content, even after common image modifications?
6f648aeb5c5219cf021840eaf3df03ac86cebff4.hypothesis: Fine-tuning only the latent decoder of a pre-trained LDM, conditioned on a fixed binary signature and guided by a robust watermark extractor, will embed an invisible watermark into all generated images, enabling accurate detection and identification of their origin, while preserving image quality and robustness to common transformations.
6f648aeb5c5219cf021840eaf3df03ac86cebff4.proposed_method: A two-phase approach is proposed to embed watermarks directly into the image generation process of LDMs. First, a watermark extractor network is pre-trained using a deep learning-based method (inspired by HiDDeN) to robustly extract k-bit binary signatures from images, even after typical image transformations such as cropping, compression, and brightness changes. The extractor is decorrelated and whitened to ensure output bits are i.i.d. and unbiased. In the second phase, the latent decoder of a pre-trained LDM is fine-tuned by backpropagating a combination of a perceptual image loss (using Watson-VGG or LPIPS) and a message loss (binary cross-entropy between the extracted and target signature) so that all generated images contain the fixed signature. This fine-tuning is performed over a small number of iterations and images, without modifying the diffusion process or model architecture, ensuring compatibility with a wide range of generative tasks.
6f648aeb5c5219cf021840eaf3df03ac86cebff4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple generative tasks, including text-to-image, inpainting, editing, and super-resolution, using datasets such as MS-COCO (validation set) and ImageNet. The evaluation will measure watermark robustness under various image transformations (e.g., cropping to 10% of original content, brightness adjustment, JPEG compression, and combinations thereof). Baselines will include state-of-the-art passive forensic methods and several post-hoc watermarking algorithms (e.g., DCT-DWT, SSLWatermark, FNNS, HiDDeN). Metrics will include true/false positive rates for detection, identification accuracy among up to 100,000 users, bit accuracy of extracted watermarks, image quality (PSNR, SSIM), and generative quality (FID). Additional experiments will assess robustness to intentional attacks (e.g., neural autoencoder purification, adversarial removal, model purification, and model collusion).
6f648aeb5c5219cf021840eaf3df03ac86cebff4.novelty_claims: The proposed method natively roots watermarks within the generative process of LDMs by fine-tuning only the latent decoder, requiring no architectural changes and minimal computational overhead. This approach enables secure, efficient, and robust watermark embedding that is compatible with a wide range of LDM-based generative tasks. The method achieves high detection and identification accuracy even after severe image modifications, outperforms or matches post-hoc watermarking and passive forensic techniques, and provides a practical solution for tracing and managing the provenance of AI-generated images. The approach also allows for scalable user identification and demonstrates resistance to a variety of intentional and unintentional watermark removal attacks.

6f6e2e0311589a9af045f6acd00b7dee6d19fce4.title: The Impact of Positional Encoding on Length Generalization in Transformers
6f6e2e0311589a9af045f6acd00b7dee6d19fce4.research_question: How does the choice of positional encoding scheme affect the ability of decoder-only Transformer models to generalize to input sequences longer than those seen during training across a variety of downstream reasoning and mathematical tasks?
6f6e2e0311589a9af045f6acd00b7dee6d19fce4.hypothesis: Explicit positional encoding schemes commonly used in Transformers, such as Absolute Position Embedding (APE), Rotary, and ALiBi, are not optimal for length generalization in downstream tasks, and removing explicit positional encoding (NoPE) may enable better generalization to longer sequences.
6f6e2e0311589a9af045f6acd00b7dee6d19fce4.proposed_method: A systematic empirical investigation will be conducted by training decoder-only Transformer models from scratch on a suite of synthetic and real-world reasoning and mathematical tasks. Five positional encoding schemes will be compared: Absolute Position Embedding (APE, sinusoidal), T5’s Relative Positional Encoding, ALiBi, Rotary, and the absence of any positional encoding (NoPE). Each model will be trained with identical architectures and hyperparameters, ensuring fair comparison. Theoretical analysis will be performed to demonstrate the representational capacity of NoPE for both absolute and relative positional information, and empirical analysis will compare attention patterns across encoding schemes. Additionally, the effect of scratchpad (chain-of-thought) prompting and various scratchpad formats on length generalization will be systematically evaluated.
6f6e2e0311589a9af045f6acd00b7dee6d19fce4.experiment_details: Experiments will use a standard decoder-only Transformer architecture with approximately 107M parameters, trained with the autoregressive language modeling objective. Tasks will include primitive sequence operations (copy, reverse), mathematical and algorithmic problems (addition, polynomial evaluation, sorting, summation, parity, LEGO), and classical length generalization benchmarks (SCAN, PCFG). For each task, models will be trained on sequences up to a fixed length (e.g., L=20) and evaluated on both seen and much longer unseen lengths (up to 2L or more). Performance will be measured using exact-match accuracy for sequence outputs, and results will be averaged over multiple random seeds. Baselines will include all five positional encoding schemes, both with and without scratchpad prompting, and a variety of scratchpad formats will be tested to assess their impact. For scalability analysis, additional experiments will be conducted with 1B-parameter models on subsets of the StarCoder dataset, evaluating language modeling perplexity and length generalization.
6f6e2e0311589a9af045f6acd00b7dee6d19fce4.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a comprehensive empirical and theoretical analysis of positional encoding schemes in decoder-only Transformers, focusing on length generalization in downstream tasks rather than language modeling perplexity alone. The approach uniquely evaluates the performance of models without any explicit positional encoding (NoPE) and demonstrates both theoretically and empirically that NoPE can implicitly learn absolute and relative positional information. The impact of scratchpad prompting and its format on length generalization is systematically studied, revealing task-dependent effects and the limitations of scratchpad as a universal solution. The findings challenge prevailing assumptions about the necessity and effectiveness of explicit positional encodings in large language models.

6f78c48856a78f5711aead7247c92334c391924c.title: BOPO: Neural Combinatorial Optimization via Best-anchored and Objective-guided Preference Optimization
6f78c48856a78f5711aead7247c92334c391924c.research_question: How can sample efficiency and solution quality in neural combinatorial optimization for NP-hard problems be improved by leveraging solution preferences, without relying on expensive labels, reward models, or reference policies?
6f78c48856a78f5711aead7247c92334c391924c.hypothesis: Incorporating explicit preference relations among multiple sampled solutions, guided by objective values, into the training paradigm of neural combinatorial optimization will significantly enhance sample efficiency and solution quality compared to mainstream reinforcement learning and self-labeling learning approaches.
6f78c48856a78f5711aead7247c92334c391924c.proposed_method: A new training paradigm, Best-anchored and Objective-guided Preference Optimization (BOPO), is developed for neural combinatorial optimization. The method constructs multiple preference pairs from sampled solutions by: (1) generating diverse and high-quality solutions via a hybrid rollout strategy that combines sampling and greedy rollouts; (2) selecting representative solutions through uniform filtering to maximize diversity; and (3) anchoring preference pairs to the best solution to prioritize learning from high-quality examples. The training loss is a novel objective-guided pairwise loss function that adaptively scales gradients based on objective value differences between solution pairs, removing the need for reward models or reference policies. The approach is architecture-agnostic and can be integrated with various neural models for different combinatorial optimization problems.
6f78c48856a78f5711aead7247c92334c391924c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three classic NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems: Job-shop Scheduling Problem (JSP), Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP), and Flexible Job-shop Scheduling Problem (FJSP). For JSP and FJSP, standard benchmarks such as Taillard’s, Lawrence’s, and Demirkol’s datasets will be used, with both in-distribution and out-of-distribution problem shapes. For TSP, both randomly generated instances and TSPLIB benchmarks will be evaluated, including various distributions (uniform, cluster, explosion, implosion). Baselines will include state-of-the-art neural constructive methods (RL-based, SLL-based, and SL-based), traditional heuristics, and exact solvers (Gurobi, Concorde, LKH3). Evaluation metrics will focus on the optimality gap (relative to the best-known or optimal solution) and total solving time. Both greedy and sampling rollouts will be used for inference, and ablation studies will assess the contribution of each component of the proposed method.
6f78c48856a78f5711aead7247c92334c391924c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces preference optimization as a new training paradigm for neural combinatorial optimization, featuring a best-anchored preference pair construction and a novel objective-guided pairwise loss tailored for combinatorial problems. It avoids the need for expensive labels, reward models, or reference policies, and is compatible with a wide range of neural architectures. The method establishes a principled and efficient framework for leveraging solution preferences, leading to superior sample efficiency and state-of-the-art performance across multiple combinatorial optimization benchmarks.

6f870f7f02a8c59c3e23f407f3ef00dd1dcf8fc4.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
6f870f7f02a8c59c3e23f407f3ef00dd1dcf8fc4.research_question: Can large-scale visual models be learned from natural language supervision in a way that enables flexible, transferable, and robust zero-shot performance across a wide range of computer vision tasks, without relying on fixed, crowd-labeled datasets?
6f870f7f02a8c59c3e23f407f3ef00dd1dcf8fc4.hypothesis: Learning visual representations directly from large-scale natural language supervision will produce models that are highly transferable, robust to distribution shifts, and capable of zero-shot generalization to new tasks and datasets, matching or exceeding the performance of fully supervised models on standard benchmarks.
6f870f7f02a8c59c3e23f407f3ef00dd1dcf8fc4.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that jointly trains an image encoder and a text encoder using a contrastive objective on a massive dataset of 400 million (image, text) pairs collected from the internet. The method constructs a multi-modal embedding space by maximizing the cosine similarity between embeddings of paired images and texts, while minimizing similarity for unpaired combinations within a batch. The image encoder is implemented as either a modified ResNet or Vision Transformer, while the text encoder is a Transformer operating on byte-pair encoded text. During pre-training, the model is optimized using a symmetric cross-entropy loss over all possible (image, text) pairings in a batch, with a learnable temperature parameter to scale the logits. For zero-shot transfer, the text encoder synthesizes a classifier for new tasks by embedding class names or descriptions, allowing the model to predict class membership for images without any task-specific training.
6f870f7f02a8c59c3e23f407f3ef00dd1dcf8fc4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by pre-training the model from scratch on the newly constructed WebImageText (WIT) dataset of 400 million (image, text) pairs. Multiple model architectures and scales will be evaluated, including various ResNet and Vision Transformer variants, trained for 32 epochs using the Adam optimizer with large batch sizes and mixed precision. Zero-shot transfer performance will be benchmarked on over 30 diverse computer vision datasets spanning OCR, action recognition, geo-localization, and fine-grained object classification. Baselines will include fully supervised models (e.g., ResNet-50 trained on ImageNet), logistic regression linear probes, and prior zero-shot methods such as Visual N-Grams. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 and top-5 classification accuracy, data efficiency (number of labeled examples required to match zero-shot performance), and robustness to distribution shift. Prompt engineering and ensembling strategies for zero-shot classification will also be systematically explored.
6f870f7f02a8c59c3e23f407f3ef00dd1dcf8fc4.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a scalable and efficient method for learning transferable visual models directly from natural language supervision at unprecedented scale. It enables zero-shot transfer to a wide variety of vision tasks without any task-specific training or output heads, matching or exceeding the performance of strong supervised baselines on many benchmarks. The method demonstrates that contrastive pre-training on web-scale (image, text) data produces robust and generalizable representations, and establishes new state-of-the-art results for zero-shot classification across numerous datasets. Additional innovations include the use of prompt engineering and ensembling to further boost zero-shot performance, and a comprehensive analysis of data efficiency and transferability compared to both supervised and self-supervised baselines.

6f914dd361254e40161c2bd3916931c9d54ab4b2.title: Transformers need glasses! Information over-squashing in language tasks
6f914dd361254e40161c2bd3916931c9d54ab4b2.research_question: What are the fundamental limitations in information propagation within decoder-only Transformer architectures, particularly regarding their ability to handle tasks such as copying and counting in language modeling, and how can these limitations be theoretically characterized and empirically validated?
6f914dd361254e40161c2bd3916931c9d54ab4b2.hypothesis: Decoder-only Transformer architectures exhibit inherent information propagation bottlenecks, leading to phenomena such as representational collapse and over-squashing, which fundamentally limit their ability to solve tasks requiring precise token-level information retention (e.g., copying and counting), especially under finite floating-point precision.
6f914dd361254e40161c2bd3916931c9d54ab4b2.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical analysis will be conducted on the signal propagation dynamics in decoder-only Transformers, focusing on the representations of the last token in the final layer, which is critical for next-token prediction. The analysis will formalize and prove the existence of representational collapse, where distinct input sequences can yield nearly identical final representations, particularly as sequence length increases and under low-precision arithmetic. Additionally, the study will extend concepts from graph neural networks, such as over-squashing, to the Transformer setting, quantifying how the causal attention mechanism leads to a loss of sensitivity to certain input tokens. Empirical experiments will be designed to validate these theoretical findings, and potential architectural or prompting interventions (such as introducing separator tokens) will be explored to mitigate these issues.
6f914dd361254e40161c2bd3916931c9d54ab4b2.experiment_details: Experiments will involve evaluating state-of-the-art large language models, such as Gemini 1.5 and the open-source Gemma 7B, on synthetic tasks designed to probe copying and counting abilities. Tasks will include copying the first or last token in sequences of varying lengths and counting the number of specific tokens in sequences with controlled patterns (e.g., repeated ones, alternating ones and zeros, or Bernoulli-distributed sequences). Baseline prompting strategies will be compared with interventions such as providing hints or inserting separator tokens. Internal model representations will be analyzed to measure the degree of representational collapse, using metrics such as the distance between final token embeddings for similar but distinct input sequences. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on the tasks, error as a function of sequence length, and statistical analysis of output distributions. The impact of floating-point precision and tokenization will also be systematically examined.
6f914dd361254e40161c2bd3916931c9d54ab4b2.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a rigorous theoretical framework for understanding and quantifying representational collapse and over-squashing in decoder-only Transformers, phenomena previously underexplored in the context of practical floating-point precision and standard soft-attention mechanisms. It bridges insights from graph neural networks to language modeling, providing new analytical tools for diagnosing information bottlenecks in LLMs. The empirical validation on contemporary models and the identification of simple, actionable mitigation strategies constitute further contributions, offering both foundational understanding and practical guidance for improving Transformer-based architectures.

6f9c589f96a1e3a7d37596e52ce390fc37e67e31.title: Smoothed Preference Optimization via ReNoise Inversion for Aligning Diffusion Models with Varied Human Preferences
6f9c589f96a1e3a7d37596e52ce390fc37e67e31.research_question: How can text-to-image diffusion models be more effectively aligned with the diverse and granular preferences of human users, while improving training efficiency and image generation quality?
6f9c589f96a1e3a7d37596e52ce390fc37e67e31.hypothesis: Modeling human preferences as smoothed distributions rather than binary labels, combined with improved estimation of diffusion model trajectories via inversion techniques, will enable more accurate, efficient, and robust alignment of text-to-image diffusion models with varied human preferences.
6f9c589f96a1e3a7d37596e52ce390fc37e67e31.proposed_method: A new framework, SmPO-Diffusion, will be developed to enhance preference alignment in text-to-image diffusion models. The approach will replace traditional binary preference labels with a smoothed preference distribution, leveraging a reward model (such as PickScore) to simulate and normalize human preferences for each image pair. The DPO (Direct Preference Optimization) loss will be modified to incorporate these smoothed labels, ensuring the loss function approaches zero when preferences are similar, thus mitigating over-optimization. To more accurately align the optimization objective with the actual sampling process of diffusion models, a Renoise Inversion technique will be employed: this involves a few-step DDIM inversion followed by a single renoise step, enabling efficient and accurate estimation of the model's sampling trajectory. The overall objective will be a numerically upper-bounded, smoothed DPO loss that is adaptive to image-dependent preferences.
6f9c589f96a1e3a7d37596e52ce390fc37e67e31.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Stable Diffusion 1.5 (SD1.5) and Stable Diffusion XL (SDXL) models, fine-tuned on the Pick-a-Pic v2 dataset, which contains over 850,000 image-text pairs and nearly 59,000 unique prompts. Baseline methods for comparison will include Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), Diffusion-DPO, Diffusion-KTO, and MaPO, each representing different strategies for preference alignment. Evaluation will utilize multiple reward models—CLIP for text-image alignment, LAION aesthetic classifier and Imagereward for image quality, and PickScore and HPSv2.1 for human preference simulation. Metrics will include median reward scores, win-rates (frequency of preference over baselines), and training resource consumption (GPU hours). Images will be generated using standardized test sets (Parti-Prompts and HPDv2), and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of method components, inversion steps, sensitivity factors, and reward model choices.
6f9c589f96a1e3a7d37596e52ce390fc37e67e31.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel smoothed preference modeling approach for diffusion models, replacing binary preference labels with a continuous distribution derived from reward models, thus capturing the inherent variability in human preferences. It further innovates by employing Renoise Inversion for more accurate and efficient estimation of diffusion model sampling trajectories, directly addressing objective misalignment and training inefficiency found in prior methods. The approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in human preference alignment tasks, significantly reduces training time (up to 26-fold compared to leading baselines), and demonstrates superior image quality across multiple evaluation metrics and conditional generation scenarios.

6fa3f84affb5af66ec3fe94e618e0124493bb28e.title: Data Banzhaf: A Robust Data Valuation Framework for Machine Learning
6fa3f84affb5af66ec3fe94e618e0124493bb28e.research_question: How can data valuation in machine learning be made robust to noise and randomness in model performance scores, particularly those arising from stochastic training algorithms?
6fa3f84affb5af66ec3fe94e618e0124493bb28e.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a data valuation method based on the Banzhaf value, equipped with an efficient estimation algorithm, will provide greater robustness to noisy model performance scores and more consistent data value rankings than existing semivalue-based approaches such as the Shapley value and Leave-one-out error.
6fa3f84affb5af66ec3fe94e618e0124493bb28e.proposed_method: A novel data valuation framework will be developed that leverages the Banzhaf value from cooperative game theory as the core data value notion. The method will introduce the concept of 'safety margin' to mathematically quantify the robustness of data value notions to perturbations in model performance scores. The Banzhaf value will be shown to maximize this safety margin among all semivalues, making it the most robust choice. To address the computational challenges of estimating the Banzhaf value, an efficient Monte Carlo-based algorithm using the Maximum Sample Reuse (MSR) principle will be designed. This estimator will achieve high sample efficiency and robustness to noise, enabling practical and scalable data valuation in stochastic machine learning settings.
6fa3f84affb5af66ec3fe94e618e0124493bb28e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard machine learning datasets such as CIFAR-10, focusing on tasks like bad data detection and data reweighting. The evaluation will compare the proposed Banzhaf-based method against established baselines, including the Shapley value, Leave-one-out error, and Beta Shapley. Metrics will include the stability of data value rankings across multiple runs with different random seeds, the accuracy of identifying mislabeled or low-quality data, and the computational efficiency of the estimation algorithms. The experimental setup will involve training neural networks using stochastic gradient descent, measuring the variance and consistency of data value assignments, and analyzing the empirical sample complexity of the MSR estimator.
6fa3f84affb5af66ec3fe94e618e0124493bb28e.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the first formal robustness analysis of data valuation methods in the presence of noisy model performance scores. It establishes the Banzhaf value as the most robust semivalue for data valuation, maximizing the safety margin and providing exponentially greater tolerance to noise compared to prior approaches. The development of the Maximum Sample Reuse (MSR) estimator uniquely enables efficient and scalable approximation of the Banzhaf value, a property not shared by other semivalue-based methods. The overall approach offers significant improvements in both the reliability and computational practicality of data valuation in stochastic machine learning environments.

6fb5c0eff3696ef252aca9638e10176ecce7cecb.title: Generating Images with Multimodal Language Models
6fb5c0eff3696ef252aca9638e10176ecce7cecb.research_question: How can large language models be adapted to enable coherent and contextually relevant image generation, retrieval, and multimodal dialogue, given arbitrarily interleaved image and text inputs?
6fb5c0eff3696ef252aca9638e10176ecce7cecb.hypothesis: A mapping network that efficiently translates the hidden representations of a frozen text-only large language model into the embedding space of a pre-trained image generation model will enable the LLM to generate, retrieve, and interleave images and text outputs, outperforming baseline models on tasks requiring complex and context-dependent language understanding.
6fb5c0eff3696ef252aca9638e10176ecce7cecb.proposed_method: A modular framework is proposed that fuses a frozen text-only large language model (LLM) with pre-trained image encoder and decoder models by learning efficient mappings between their embedding spaces. The approach involves three main components: (1) a linear mapping that translates visual embeddings from a pre-trained visual backbone into the LLM's embedding space to process image inputs; (2) a GILLMapper module, implemented as a lightweight 4-layer encoder-decoder transformer, which maps LLM [IMG] token hidden states into the embedding space of a frozen text-to-image generation model (e.g., Stable Diffusion), enabling novel image synthesis; and (3) a decision module, trained as a linear classifier on LLM [IMG] hidden states, that determines at inference time whether to retrieve an image from a candidate set or generate a new one. The model is trained on image-caption pairs using a multitask loss that combines captioning, image token prediction, image generation, and retrieval objectives. Only a small number of parameters (mapping layers, [IMG] token embeddings, GILLMapper, and decision module) are trained, while the LLM and visual models remain frozen.
6fb5c0eff3696ef252aca9638e10176ecce7cecb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Conceptual Captions (CC3M) dataset for training (3.3M image-text pairs), and evaluated on VIST (Visual Storytelling) and VisDial (Visual Dialogue) datasets to assess contextual image generation and multimodal dialogue capabilities. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art text-to-image generation models such as Stable Diffusion and GLIDE, as well as retrieval-only multimodal language models like FROMAGe. Evaluation metrics will include CLIP Similarity and LPIPS for image relevance and perceptual similarity, as well as Recall@k for image retrieval tasks. The experimental setup will use the OPT-6.7B LLM, CLIP ViT-L visual encoder, and Stable Diffusion v1.5 as the image generator, with all backbone weights frozen and only the mapping and decision modules trained. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of different mapping architectures and the number of [IMG] tokens.
6fb5c0eff3696ef252aca9638e10176ecce7cecb.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable a frozen text-only LLM to process arbitrarily interleaved image and text inputs and produce coherent outputs that include generated images, retrieved images, and text, interleaved within multimodal dialogue. The GILLMapper module introduces a highly efficient and effective mapping from LLM hidden states to the embedding space of a text-to-image generator, outperforming linear and MLP baselines, especially on tasks requiring long or complex context. The method achieves superior performance on context-dependent image generation and retrieval tasks compared to non-LLM-based generation models, and demonstrates the ability to decide dynamically between retrieval and generation at inference time. The approach is computationally efficient, requiring only a small number of trainable parameters and modest hardware resources, and is modular, allowing future improvements by upgrading the underlying LLM or visual models.

6fe7e6ce3cc0ebd038caa456d73fd7472e7d6c38.title: Controllable Preference Optimization: Toward Controllable Multi-Objective Alignment
6fe7e6ce3cc0ebd038caa456d73fd7472e7d6c38.research_question: How can large language models be aligned with multiple, potentially conflicting human values and preferences in a controllable manner, such that trade-offs between objectives like helpfulness, honesty, and harmlessness can be explicitly managed according to user or application needs?
6fe7e6ce3cc0ebd038caa456d73fd7472e7d6c38.hypothesis: Explicitly conditioning large language model training and optimization on user-specified preference scores for multiple objectives enables controllable alignment, allowing models to generate responses that better match desired trade-offs among objectives such as helpfulness, honesty, and harmlessness, thereby mitigating the alignment tax and improving multi-objective alignment performance.
6fe7e6ce3cc0ebd038caa456d73fd7472e7d6c38.proposed_method: A controllable preference optimization (CPO) framework will be developed for large language models, introducing explicit preference tokens into the input to condition model behavior on user-specified objectives. The approach consists of two main stages: (1) Controllable Preference Supervised Fine-tuning (CPSFT), where the model is trained to generate responses conditioned on preference tokens (e.g., <Helpfulness:5>, <Honesty:3>), and (2) Controllable Direct Preference Optimization (CDPO), which refines preference-based reward signals to directly optimize the likelihood of preferred responses under given preference conditions. The reward function is formulated to penalize deviations from controlled objectives while maximizing uncontrolled objectives, with hyperparameters (λ, ω) balancing the trade-off between controllability and overall performance. Preference conditions are implemented as prompt tokens, and the method supports both single- and multi-objective control scenarios.
6fe7e6ce3cc0ebd038caa456d73fd7472e7d6c38.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Mistral-7B large language model as the base, with training and evaluation on multiple datasets: UltraFeedback (for fine-grained helpfulness and honesty scores), UltraSafety (a curated dataset for jailbreak and harmfulness evaluation), and HH-RLHF (for harmlessness alignment). The CPSFT phase will use a combined dataset of preference-conditioned and multi-turn dialogue data, while CDPO will utilize preference pairs for direct optimization. Evaluation will be performed on MT-Bench (helpfulness), HaluEval2.0 (honesty/hallucination detection), and HackaPrompt (harmlessness/jailbreak resistance), using both GPT-4 and human annotators as judges. Baselines will include SFT, PPO, DPO, Curry-DPO, and several open-source aligned LLMs. Metrics will include preference-matched scores for each objective, as well as trade-off and controllability analyses via sensitivity experiments on hyperparameters.
6fe7e6ce3cc0ebd038caa456d73fd7472e7d6c38.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces explicit, user-controllable preference conditioning for multi-objective alignment in large language models, transforming the alignment problem into a conditional optimization task.
