This enables fine-grained control over trade-offs between conflicting objectives, mitigates the alignment tax, and achieves improved performance across multiple alignment dimensions. The methodology supports both supervised and direct preference optimization, and is demonstrated to outperform existing baselines in controllability and multi-objective alignment, as validated on standard and newly curated datasets.

700bd9681f1b9e9e2212e10415d27b11c7e6836b.title: Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning Acting and Planning in Language Models
700bd9681f1b9e9e2212e10415d27b11c7e6836b.research_question: How can a unified framework be developed to enable language models to perform effective reasoning, acting, and planning in diverse decision-making environments, leveraging both internal reasoning and external feedback?
700bd9681f1b9e9e2212e10415d27b11c7e6836b.hypothesis: Integrating Monte Carlo Tree Search with language model-powered value functions, self-reflection, and external feedback will enable language models to achieve superior performance in reasoning, acting, and planning tasks compared to existing reflexive or single-path prompting methods.
700bd9681f1b9e9e2212e10415d27b11c7e6836b.proposed_method: A novel framework, Language Agent Tree Search (LATS), will be developed to unify reasoning, acting, and planning in language models. The approach adapts Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to operate over a combinatorial space of possible reasoning and acting steps, leveraging the in-context learning capabilities of modern language models. The method will use language models as agents, value function estimators, and feedback generators, integrating both self-generated and environment-based feedback. The framework will consist of a sequence of operations—selection, expansion, evaluation, simulation, backpropagation, and reflection—where nodes represent states composed of input, action, and observation sequences. A value function combining LM-based scoring and self-consistency heuristics will guide the search, and self-reflection will be used to further refine decision-making by integrating failed trajectories and their analyses into future context.
700bd9681f1b9e9e2212e10415d27b11c7e6836b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across diverse domains, including programming (HumanEval, MBPP), multi-hop question answering (HotPotQA), web navigation (WebShop), and mathematical reasoning (Game of 24). The framework will be evaluated using both reasoning-only and acting-based tasks, with baselines including Chain-of-Thought (CoT), ReAct, ToT, RAP, Reflexion, and RL-based approaches. Evaluation metrics will include exact match (EM) for QA, pass@1 for programming, average score and success rate for web navigation, and success rate for mathematical reasoning. The experimental setup will involve sampling multiple trajectories and nodes per search iteration, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the contribution of each component (e.g., self-reflection, search algorithm, value function).
700bd9681f1b9e9e2212e10415d27b11c7e6836b.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to fully integrate reasoning, acting, and planning for language model agents using a principled search algorithm that incorporates both internal and external feedback. LATS introduces a novel value function that combines LM-based evaluation with self-consistency heuristics and leverages self-reflection for improved learning from experience. The approach enables more flexible, adaptive, and efficient problem-solving compared to prior methods, achieving state-of-the-art results on several benchmarks and demonstrating superior sample efficiency and generality across diverse decision-making tasks.

7016fe2456a23b0e2d013fcf0e0666a63ff22808.title: Monet: Mixture of Monosemantic Experts for Transformers
7016fe2456a23b0e2d013fcf0e0666a63ff22808.research_question: How can large language models be made more interpretable and controllable by addressing the challenge of polysemanticity in their internal representations, while maintaining or improving their general performance and scalability?
7016fe2456a23b0e2d013fcf0e0666a63ff22808.hypothesis: Integrating sparse dictionary learning directly into end-to-end mixture-of-experts (MoE) pretraining, and scaling the number of experts per layer using parameter-efficient expert decomposition, will yield monosemantic experts that enhance mechanistic interpretability, enable robust knowledge manipulation (across domains, languages, and toxicity), and preserve or improve language model performance.
7016fe2456a23b0e2d013fcf0e0666a63ff22808.proposed_method: A novel architecture, termed Mixture of Monosemantic Experts for Transformers (MONET), will be developed to incorporate sparse dictionary learning directly into the pretraining of MoE-based large language models. The method introduces two orthogonal expert decomposition strategies—horizontal and vertical decomposition—that partition expert networks into complementary components (e.g., bottom/top or left/right segments), enabling the dynamic composition of a large number of experts (up to 262,144 per layer) while ensuring that total parameter count grows only with the square root of the number of experts. Product key composition is used for efficient expert retrieval, and batch normalization-based quantile estimation replaces hardware-inefficient top-k sorting for routing. The training objective combines standard language modeling loss with load balancing and ambiguity losses to promote uniform expert utilization and high expert specialization. The architecture is implemented within the transformer feedforward layers, and supports both dense and sparse routing.
7016fe2456a23b0e2d013fcf0e0666a63ff22808.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on models ranging from 850 million to 4.1 billion parameters, using the LLAMA architecture for baseline comparison. Pretraining will be performed on large-scale corpora, with additional instruction tuning for chat variants. Evaluation will include open-ended language modeling benchmarks such as MMLU, ARC, WinoGrande, PIQA, SIQA, OBQA, HellaSwag, and CommonsenseQA, in both 0-shot and 5-shot settings. Baselines will include dense LLMs (LLAMA), standard MoE models (OLMoE), and sparse autoencoder (SAE)-augmented models (GemmaScope). Metrics will include accuracy on benchmarks, pass@100 for code generation (MULTIPL-E), and toxicity scores (REALTOXICITYPROMPTS, ToxiGen). Additional analyses will assess knowledge unlearning and manipulation by masking domain-, language-, and toxicity-specific experts, measuring the impact on targeted and non-targeted tasks.
7016fe2456a23b0e2d013fcf0e0666a63ff22808.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a parameter-efficient MoE architecture that enables scaling to hundreds of thousands of experts per layer, far beyond previous approaches, with parameter growth only proportional to the square root of expert count. The expert decomposition strategies (horizontal and vertical) and product key composition are novel mechanisms for efficient expert construction and retrieval. The method directly integrates sparse dictionary learning into pretraining, producing monosemantic experts that facilitate mechanistic interpretability and precise knowledge manipulation (including domain, language, and toxicity control) without degrading general model performance. The approach enables transparent observation and editing of internal knowledge in LLMs, advancing both interpretability and controllability.

701def2dc909eb049f22dbcb352b04f583d27518.title: Towards Lossless Dataset Distillation via Difficulty-Aligned Trajectory Matching
701def2dc909eb049f22dbcb352b04f583d27518.research_question: How can dataset distillation be made lossless, such that a synthetic dataset of variable size enables models trained on it to match the performance of those trained on the full real dataset, across both small and large synthetic dataset regimes?
701def2dc909eb049f22dbcb352b04f583d27518.hypothesis: Aligning the difficulty of patterns learned during dataset distillation with the size of the synthetic dataset enables lossless distillation, maintaining or improving model performance regardless of synthetic set size.
701def2dc909eb049f22dbcb352b04f583d27518.proposed_method: A novel dataset distillation framework, Difficulty-Aligned Trajectory Matching (DATM), is proposed. This approach controls the difficulty of patterns embedded in the synthetic dataset by selectively matching training trajectories from different phases of a teacher network's training: early trajectories (easy patterns) for small synthetic sets and late trajectories (hard patterns) for larger sets. The method introduces a flexible trajectory-matching range, defined by lower and upper bounds on training epochs, to calibrate the difficulty of learned patterns. Additionally, soft labels are incorporated and optimized during distillation, with a sequential generation strategy that first embeds easy patterns and then gradually introduces harder ones, stabilizing optimization and improving label-data consistency. Synthetic data initialization is performed by sampling from subsets of the real dataset that are correctly classified by the teacher model to avoid mislabeling and accelerate convergence.
701def2dc909eb049f22dbcb352b04f583d27518.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny ImageNet datasets, using a variety of neural network architectures including ConvNet, ResNet18, VGG11, AlexNet, LeNet, and MLP. The proposed method is compared against multiple baselines, including DC, DM, DSA, CAFE, KIP, FRePo, RCIG, MTT, TESLA, and FTD, as well as random selection and coreset selection methods (Glister, Forgetting). Evaluation metrics focus on test accuracy, with performance measured across a range of images-per-class (IPC) settings, from extremely small to large synthetic sets. Ablation studies are performed to assess the contribution of soft label learning, difficulty alignment, and sequential generation. Cross-architecture generalization is also evaluated to test the robustness of distilled datasets on unseen network architectures.
701def2dc909eb049f22dbcb352b04f583d27518.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to achieve lossless dataset distillation, matching the performance of models trained on full real datasets even as the synthetic dataset size increases. Key innovations include the alignment of pattern difficulty with synthetic set size via flexible trajectory matching, the integration and optimization of soft labels during distillation, and a sequential generation strategy that stabilizes optimization. The approach scales trajectory-matching-based distillation to larger synthetic datasets, overcoming the limitations of prior methods that degrade in high-IPC regimes. The method demonstrates superior generalization across architectures and provides insights into the relationship between network capacity, pattern difficulty, and distillation efficacy.

701f193b1ffe3c5a9196214974b4b8940baa470b.title: Robust Quadrupedal Locomotion via Risk-Averse Policy Learning
701f193b1ffe3c5a9196214974b4b8940baa470b.research_question: How can the robustness of quadrupedal robot locomotion be enhanced in the presence of uncertain and challenging environments, such as abrupt terrain changes, unexpected external forces, and dynamic loads, without relying on external sensors or excessive domain randomization?
701f193b1ffe3c5a9196214974b4b8940baa470b.hypothesis: Risk-sensitive reinforcement learning, leveraging a distributional value function and risk-averse policy optimization, will enable quadrupedal robots to achieve greater robustness and generalization in locomotion tasks under uncertainty compared to conventional RL approaches.
701f193b1ffe3c5a9196214974b4b8940baa470b.proposed_method: A risk-averse reinforcement learning framework will be developed for quadrupedal locomotion, utilizing a distributional value function estimated via quantile regression within an actor-critic architecture. The method will inject rare but significant risk events into the reward function by penalizing specific proprioceptive signals that exceed predefined thresholds, simulating real-world hazards. Policy optimization will be performed using the Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) objective, focusing on the worst-case quantiles of the return distribution to encourage risk-averse behavior. Additionally, an Interquartile Range (IQR) metric of the value distribution will be employed as an online risk-level estimator, enabling a meta-controller to switch between risk-averse and risk-neutral policies based on environmental conditions. The approach will rely solely on proprioceptive feedback, avoiding privileged information or external sensors.
701f193b1ffe3c5a9196214974b4b8940baa470b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in both simulation and on real hardware using the Unitree Aliengo quadrupedal robot. In simulation, the Isaac Gym platform will be used with extensive domain randomization over physical parameters (e.g., friction, mass, external pushes) and various terrain types, including smooth slopes, rough slopes, and discrete obstacles. The policy will be trained using parallelized agents and a curriculum over terrain difficulty. Baselines will include PPO with curriculum terrain, expanded domain randomization (DR), and privileged teacher-student methods such as RMA. Evaluation metrics will include Time to Fall (TTF), success rates on hazardous terrains (e.g., walking down high platforms), and recovery from disturbances. Real-world experiments will test the robot's ability to traverse challenging terrains, withstand dynamic payloads and external pushes, and recover from destabilizing events. The effectiveness of the IQR-based meta-controller will be assessed by measuring performance across risk levels and quantiles of the return distribution.
701f193b1ffe3c5a9196214974b4b8940baa470b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a risk-sensitive perspective to quadrupedal locomotion by leveraging a distributional value function and risk-averse policy optimization via CVaR, which is novel in the context of real-world legged robots. The use of proprioception-based risk injection and the IQR of the value distribution as an online risk-level estimator enables adaptive policy switching without external sensors or privileged information. The method claims to achieve superior robustness and generalization to unseen disturbances and terrains, outperforming existing RL-based locomotion controllers in both simulation and real-world settings.

703035b483c181953de1b55b5fd59cd4cd4cf211.title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
703035b483c181953de1b55b5fd59cd4cd4cf211.research_question: How can multi-agent systems based on large language models be enhanced to solve complex, collaborative tasks in a manner that is robust, coherent, and aligned with human-like workflows?
703035b483c181953de1b55b5fd59cd4cd4cf211.hypothesis: Incorporating standardized human workflows, such as Standardized Operating Procedures (SOPs), structured communication protocols, and executable feedback mechanisms into LLM-based multi-agent frameworks will improve task decomposition, collaboration efficiency, and code generation quality, thereby outperforming existing multi-agent and code generation systems.
703035b483c181953de1b55b5fd59cd4cd4cf211.proposed_method: A meta-programming framework is developed that models a multi-agent system as a simulated software company, where each agent is assigned a specialized role (e.g., Product Manager, Architect, Project Manager, Engineer, QA Engineer) with a defined profile, skills, and operational context. The workflow is organized according to SOPs, enabling sequential and structured task decomposition and handoff between agents. Communication among agents is facilitated through a structured message pool and a publish-subscribe mechanism, ensuring that agents receive only relevant, role-specific information. The framework also integrates an executable feedback mechanism: after code is generated, it is automatically tested and debugged iteratively by the responsible agent, leveraging historical execution data and test results to refine outputs until correctness is achieved or a retry limit is reached.
703035b483c181953de1b55b5fd59cd4cd4cf211.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on two public code generation benchmarks, HumanEval (164 programming tasks) and MBPP (427 Python tasks), as well as a self-constructed SoftwareDev benchmark containing 70 diverse software development tasks. Evaluation metrics include Pass@k (functional accuracy), executability (rated 1-4), running time, token usage, code statistics (files, lines), productivity (tokens per line), and human revision cost. The proposed framework is compared against domain-specific LLMs (AlphaCode, Incoder, CodeGeeX, CodeGen, Codex, CodeT), general LLMs (PaLM, GPT-4), and multi-agent frameworks (AutoGPT, LangChain, AgentVerse, ChatDev). Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of role specialization and the executable feedback mechanism.
703035b483c181953de1b55b5fd59cd4cd4cf211.novelty_claims: The proposed framework uniquely integrates human-inspired SOPs into LLM-based multi-agent collaboration, enabling structured task decomposition, role specialization, and workflow management. It introduces a structured communication protocol and a publish-subscribe message pool for efficient information sharing. A novel executable feedback mechanism is incorporated for iterative code refinement during runtime. The approach demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks, achieves higher code quality and efficiency, and reduces human revision costs compared to existing systems. The framework is also claimed to be flexible, extensible, and capable of handling complex, real-world software engineering tasks.

704ff1cb0003859c4a14b6cbf91888aa61d567f1.title: Sketch-GNN: Scalable Graph Neural Networks with Sublinear Training Complexity
704ff1cb0003859c4a14b6cbf91888aa61d567f1.research_question: How can graph neural networks (GNNs) be trained with time and memory complexities that scale sublinearly with respect to the size of the underlying graph, while maintaining competitive predictive performance across various GNN architectures and large-scale datasets?
704ff1cb0003859c4a14b6cbf91888aa61d567f1.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by leveraging advanced sketching techniques—specifically, polynomial tensor sketching for non-linear activations and learnable locality sensitive hashing (LSH) for adaptive sketch quality—GNNs can be trained with sublinear time and memory complexity relative to graph size, without significant loss in accuracy compared to full-graph training.
704ff1cb0003859c4a14b6cbf91888aa61d567f1.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that replaces the standard full-graph and mini-batch GNN training paradigms with a sketch-based approach. The method will construct compact sketches of both the graph adjacency matrix and node feature matrix using polynomial tensor sketching (PTS), enabling the approximation of non-linear activation functions and graph convolution operations directly in the sketched domain. The update rules for GNN layers will be reformulated so that only sketches are propagated, eliminating the need for operations that scale linearly with the number of nodes. To further enhance sketch quality and reduce approximation errors, learnable locality sensitive hashing (LSH) functions will be introduced and updated online via gradient descent using a sampled triplet loss, allowing the sketching process to adapt dynamically to the evolving hidden representations during training. The framework will include efficient algorithms for updating hash tables using only small subsets of node representations, and will employ sparse forward and backward passes to avoid full unsketching and loss evaluation over all nodes.
704ff1cb0003859c4a14b6cbf91888aa61d567f1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both small and large-scale graph benchmarks, including Cora, Citeseer, ogbn-arxiv, Reddit, and ogbn-products, covering a range from tens of thousands to over two million nodes. The proposed method will be evaluated using standard GNN architectures such as GCN, GraphSAGE, and GAT. Baselines will include full-graph training (oracle), graph coarsening and condensation methods, sampling-based approaches (e.g., GraphSAINT), historical-embedding-based methods (e.g., VQ-GNN), and linearized GNNs (e.g., SGC). Evaluation metrics will focus on node classification accuracy, memory usage, preprocessing and training time, and scalability as a function of graph size and sketch ratio (c/n). Ablation studies will examine the effects of sketch dimension, learned versus fixed sketches, and the impact of LSH updates. Additional proof-of-concept experiments will assess the approximation error of polynomial tensor sketching and the dynamics of LSH hash table adaptation.
704ff1cb0003859c4a14b6cbf91888aa61d567f1.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first GNN training framework with provably sublinear time and memory complexity in graph size, achieved by sketching both non-linear activations and graph convolution matrices via polynomial tensor sketching. Unlike prior work that sketches only linear weights or gradients, this approach enables end-to-end training in the sketched domain without the need to revert to the original high-dimensional space. The integration of learnable locality sensitive hashing for online sketch adaptation further distinguishes the method, allowing sketches to dynamically track evolving node representations and reducing approximation errors. The framework generalizes across multiple GNN architectures, avoids the heavy preprocessing costs of graph coarsening/condensation, and demonstrates robust scalability and competitive accuracy on large-scale benchmarks.

704ff79cdff242b49e17c22edb567dd57c1ac615.title: Parameterized Local Search for Max c-Cut
704ff79cdff242b49e17c22edb567dd57c1ac615.research_question: Can parameterized local search algorithms be effectively designed and implemented for the NP-hard MAX c-CUT problem, specifically to efficiently find improving solutions within a bounded number of vertex color changes (k-flip neighborhood), and how do such algorithms perform in practice compared to existing heuristics?
704ff79cdff242b49e17c22edb567dd57c1ac615.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, despite theoretical hardness results, parameterized local search algorithms that exploit structural properties of the input graph and the k-flip neighborhood can be developed to efficiently find improving solutions for MAX c-CUT, and that such algorithms will yield practical improvements over state-of-the-art heuristics on benchmark datasets.
704ff79cdff242b49e17c22edb567dd57c1ac615.proposed_method: A parameterized local search framework will be developed for the MAX c-CUT problem, where the goal is to determine whether a given vertex coloring can be improved by changing the colors of at most k vertices. The method will leverage the observation that minimal improving flips are connected in the input graph, enabling enumeration of candidate flips in O((eΔ)^k · k · n) time, where Δ is the maximum degree. For each candidate set of k vertices, an optimal way to assign new colors will be computed in O(3^k · c · k^2 + k · Δ) time. The algorithm will incorporate optimizations such as upper bounds on the improvement of partial flips and will be designed to scale well with n and Δ, with the exponential dependence isolated to the parameter k.
704ff79cdff242b49e17c22edb567dd57c1ac615.experiment_details: The proposed algorithm will be evaluated as a post-processing step for solutions generated by a state-of-the-art heuristic for MAX c-CUT. Experiments will be conducted on a set of standard benchmark instances, including graphs with both positive and negative edge weights and varying numbers of colors (c > 2). Baseline comparisons will include the original heuristic without post-processing and potentially other local search variants. Evaluation metrics will focus on the quality of the cut (total weight of edges with distinctly colored endpoints), the number of improved instances, and computational efficiency. The experimental setup will systematically vary the parameter k to assess the trade-off between solution quality and running time.
704ff79cdff242b49e17c22edb567dd57c1ac615.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a parameterized local search algorithm for MAX c-CUT with a running time that is fixed-parameter tractable in k and mildly dependent on the maximum degree Δ. The approach exploits new structural insights about the connectivity of minimal improving flips and provides the first practical parameterized local search method for MAX c-CUT that can improve upon state-of-the-art heuristics on real-world benchmarks. Theoretical contributions include new hardness results for the k-flip neighborhood and related partition problems, as well as algorithmic innovations that enable efficient enumeration and evaluation of improving moves.

705e49afd92130f2bc1e0d4d0b1f6cb14e88803f.title: Not What You've Signed Up For: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
705e49afd92130f2bc1e0d4d0b1f6cb14e88803f.research_question: How can large language model (LLM)-integrated applications be compromised by adversarial manipulation of data sources, and what are the security implications and threat landscape of indirect prompt injection attacks in real-world systems?
705e49afd92130f2bc1e0d4d0b1f6cb14e88803f.hypothesis: LLM-integrated applications are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection attacks, whereby adversaries can remotely compromise system behavior, exfiltrate data, manipulate content, and trigger malicious actions by injecting prompts into data sources likely to be retrieved at inference time.
705e49afd92130f2bc1e0d4d0b1f6cb14e88803f.proposed_method: A comprehensive taxonomy and systematic analysis of indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks will be developed from a computer security perspective, mapping out the attack surface, delivery vectors, and threat scenarios for LLM-integrated applications. Synthetic applications will be constructed using OpenAI’s APIs (e.g., GPT-4, text-davinci-003) and frameworks such as LangChain to simulate LLM-augmented systems with various tool integrations (search, web retrieval, email, memory, etc.). Attack demonstrations will be designed to inject adversarial prompts via multiple vectors (passive retrieval, active delivery, user-driven, and hidden methods) and to evaluate their impact on model behavior, system functionality, and user security. Real-world systems, such as Bing Chat and GitHub Copilot, will also be targeted to assess practical feasibility and generalizability of the attacks.
705e49afd92130f2bc1e0d4d0b1f6cb14e88803f.experiment_details: Experiments will include both controlled synthetic LLM-integrated applications and real-world platforms (e.g., Bing Chat, GitHub Copilot). Synthetic applications will be configured to interface with mock APIs and data sources, enabling precise control over injected content and attack scenarios. Attack vectors will be tested by planting adversarial prompts in web pages, code repositories, emails, and other retrievable sources, then observing the resulting LLM behavior during user interactions. Baselines will include unmodified LLM-integrated applications and standard prompt injection techniques. Evaluation metrics will focus on attack success rate, persistence across sessions, ability to exfiltrate or manipulate data, and bypassing of existing input filtering mechanisms. Additional qualitative analysis will assess the stealthiness, autonomy, and potential for large-scale exploitation.
705e49afd92130f2bc1e0d4d0b1f6cb14e88803f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces and systematically investigates the previously unexplored concept of indirect prompt injection (IPI) as a novel attack vector against LLM-integrated applications. It develops the first comprehensive taxonomy of IPI threats, demonstrates practical attacks on both synthetic and real-world systems, and highlights the blurred boundary between data and instructions in retrieval-augmented LLMs. The work claims to reveal new classes of vulnerabilities, including remote control, persistent compromise, and information ecosystem contamination, and to provide foundational insights for the development of robust defenses and security assessment frameworks for LLM-integrated applications.

708689cc3e5589ed28c4c0272e17ba62d43a1fe7.title: Exact Optimal Accelerated Complexity for Fixed-Point Iterations
708689cc3e5589ed28c4c0272e17ba62d43a1fe7.research_question: What is the exact optimal convergence rate achievable for general fixed-point problems involving nonexpansive nonlinear operators, and can an accelerated method be designed to achieve this rate across various operator classes, including contractive, nonexpansive, and those satisfying a Hölder-type growth condition?
708689cc3e5589ed28c4c0272e17ba62d43a1fe7.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a novel acceleration mechanism based on a Halpern-type iteration can achieve the exact optimal convergence rate for fixed-point iterations with nonexpansive and contractive operators, as well as for operators satisfying a Hölder-type growth condition, and that this rate matches a provable lower bound under the information-based complexity framework.
708689cc3e5589ed28c4c0272e17ba62d43a1fe7.proposed_method: A new acceleration framework for fixed-point iterations is proposed, leveraging a Halpern-type mechanism. For contractive operators, the Optimal Contractive Halpern (OC-Halpern) iteration is introduced, which combines the current iterate with the fixed-point operator and an initial anchor point using a sequence of weights determined by the contractivity parameter. For maximal strongly monotone operators, the Optimal Strongly-monotone Proximal Point Method (OS-PPM) is developed, which iteratively applies the resolvent of the operator and updates the iterates using a carefully chosen combination of previous iterates and the anchor. The method is further extended to operators satisfying a Hölder-type (uniform monotonicity) growth condition by employing a restarting scheme, where the accelerated method is periodically restarted with updated parameters to adapt to the local structure of the operator. The methodology is rigorously analyzed using Lyapunov functions and performance estimation problem (PEP) techniques to derive tight convergence rates.
708689cc3e5589ed28c4c0272e17ba62d43a1fe7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of problems to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed acceleration mechanism. These include a 2D toy problem with linear contractive and strongly monotone operators, total variation-regularized computed tomography (CT) imaging using the primal-dual hybrid gradient (PDHG) method, the optimal transport problem (earthmover's distance) solved via a nonexpansive fixed-point iteration, and decentralized compressed sensing using the PG-EXTRA algorithm. Baselines for comparison include standard Picard, Krasnosel’skiĭ–Mann, Halpern, and Anderson acceleration methods, as well as unaccelerated and previously proposed accelerated proximal point methods. Evaluation metrics focus on the reduction of the fixed-point residual norm and, where applicable, the resolvent residual norm. The experimental setup includes varying the operator class (contractive, nonexpansive, strongly monotone, Hölder-type), using both synthetic and real-world datasets, and measuring convergence over a large number of iterations.
708689cc3e5589ed28c4c0272e17ba62d43a1fe7.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces an exact optimal acceleration mechanism for fixed-point iterations with nonexpansive, contractive, and Hölder-type operators, establishing for the first time the exact optimal convergence rate by providing both an accelerated method and a matching complexity lower bound. The approach generalizes and improves upon existing acceleration schemes by applying a Halpern-type mechanism and extends optimal acceleration to a broader class of operators via a restarting technique. Theoretical contributions include the construction of explicit worst-case operators for lower bound proofs and the use of performance estimation problem techniques to guide algorithm design. The method demonstrates practical acceleration in a wide range of applications, including imaging, optimal transport, and decentralized optimization.

7090d35c316afe869440ede6ad61fdeec85b8bc8.title: Generative Skill Chaining: Long-Horizon Skill Planning with Diffusion Models
7090d35c316afe869440ede6ad61fdeec85b8bc8.research_question: How can long-horizon manipulation planning tasks with complex subtask dependencies be efficiently solved by composing learned skills in a way that generalizes to unseen tasks and constraints, while maintaining scalability and robust constraint handling?
7090d35c316afe869440ede6ad61fdeec85b8bc8.hypothesis: A probabilistic, generative framework that composes skill-level diffusion models can efficiently generate feasible long-horizon skill plans for unseen task skeletons, handle arbitrary constraints, and generalize to novel scenarios, outperforming or matching search-based and discriminative baselines in both simulation and real-world settings.
7090d35c316afe869440ede6ad61fdeec85b8bc8.proposed_method: The proposed method, Generative Skill Chaining (GSC), involves training individual skill-centric diffusion models for each primitive manipulation skill (e.g., pick, place, push, pull) using expert demonstration data. Each skill diffusion model captures the joint distribution over preconditions, skill parameters, and effects, using a transformer-based neural architecture. At inference, these models are composed according to a given task skeleton by probabilistically chaining their learned distributions, enabling parallel sampling of feasible skill parameter sequences that satisfy both geometric and task-specific constraints. The approach incorporates classifier-based guidance to enforce explicit or implicit constraints during sampling, and a dependency factor balances forward (initial state) and backward (goal state) information flow for robust long-horizon reasoning. Additionally, a success probability prediction module is trained to filter and select the most promising candidate skill sequences.
7090d35c316afe869440ede6ad61fdeec85b8bc8.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted in both simulated and real-world environments. The primary simulation environment is PyBullet, featuring tasks such as Hook Reach, Constrained Packing, and Rearrangement Push, each with varying skeleton lengths and complexity. The method is evaluated on nine standard TAMP tasks from prior work, with success rate across 100 random trials as the main metric. Baselines include search-based CEM methods with random and learned policy priors (Random CEM, STAP), DAF (generalization), and a diffusion-based state-only approach. Additional experiments include a 2D toy domain for proof-of-concept, constraint satisfaction tests (e.g., maximizing distance between placements), and robustness to perturbations via closed-loop replanning on a Franka Panda robot with real-time pose detection and scene reconstruction. The skill diffusion models are trained on approximately 5000 successful transitions per skill, with additional failure data for the success classifier.
7090d35c316afe869440ede6ad61fdeec85b8bc8.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a generative, compositional approach to skill chaining using diffusion models, enabling direct sampling of valid long-horizon skill plans for arbitrary unseen task skeletons. Unlike prior discriminative or search-based methods, this approach is skeleton- and length-agnostic, supports parallel sampling, and flexibly incorporates task-specific constraints via classifier-based guidance. The method demonstrates superior scalability, constraint handling, and generalization to new tasks and perturbations, including successful deployment on real robot hardware. This represents a paradigm shift in task and motion planning by leveraging probabilistic generative models for compositional skill reasoning.

7097ce178f82a052f1bf1a708e3c44d6eac5a0e4.title: Stability-penalty-adaptive Follow-the-regularized-leader: Sparsity, Game-dependency, and Best-of-both-worlds
7097ce178f82a052f1bf1a708e3c44d6eac5a0e4.research_question: How can adaptive learning rates in follow-the-regularized-leader (FTRL) algorithms be designed to achieve broad adaptivity in sequential decision-making problems, including multi-armed bandits and partial monitoring, particularly in settings with unknown sparsity, varying game difficulty, and across both stochastic and adversarial regimes?
7097ce178f82a052f1bf1a708e3c44d6eac5a0e4.hypothesis: A learning rate framework that jointly adapts to both stability and penalty components in FTRL will enable algorithms to achieve regret bounds that are simultaneously sparsity-dependent, game-dependent, and best-of-both-worlds (BOBW), even when key problem parameters such as sparsity level are unknown.
7097ce178f82a052f1bf1a708e3c44d6eac5a0e4.proposed_method: A generic adaptive learning rate, termed the stability-penalty-adaptive (SPA) learning rate, will be developed for FTRL-based algorithms. This learning rate will dynamically adjust based on both the stability (variation in FTRL outputs) and penalty (regularization strength) components, yielding regret bounds that depend on these quantities. The method will be instantiated with specific regularizers, such as the Shannon entropy and log-barrier, and will include novel estimators for unknown sparsity levels. For multi-armed bandits, the approach will include both s-agnostic algorithms (not requiring prior knowledge of sparsity) and a BOBW algorithm with a sparsity-dependent regret bound. For partial monitoring, the SPA framework will be integrated with the Exploration by Optimization (EbO) approach, optimizing over game-dependent quantities to adapt to the difficulty of the underlying game.
7097ce178f82a052f1bf1a708e3c44d6eac5a0e4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both multi-armed bandit and partial monitoring problems. For bandits, the algorithms will be evaluated in adversarial, stochastic, and self-bounding regimes, using loss vectors in [0,1]^k and [-1,1]^k, with and without knowledge of the true sparsity s. Regret will be measured and compared against existing baselines such as Exp3, Tsallis-INF, and state-of-the-art sparse bandit algorithms, using metrics including O(√sT), O(√L_2 log k), and BOBW regret rates. For partial monitoring, the approach will be tested on non-degenerate locally observable games, with regret bounds evaluated in terms of game-dependent quantities (e.g., V_t') and compared to prior game-dependent and BOBW algorithms. Key experimental setup details include the use of adaptive learning rates, hybrid regularizers, and uniform exploration components, with thorough ablation and theoretical analysis to validate the regret guarantees.
7097ce178f82a052f1bf1a708e3c44d6eac5a0e4.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first learning rate framework for FTRL that jointly adapts to both stability and penalty components, enabling simultaneous achievement of sparsity-dependent, game-dependent, and best-of-both-worlds regret bounds. It establishes the first s-agnostic sparse bandit algorithms with optimal regret up to logarithmic factors, and the first BOBW algorithm with a sparsity-dependent bound. Additionally, the approach provides a unified method for achieving BOBW and game-dependent bounds in partial monitoring, highlighting the versatility and broad applicability of the SPA learning rate. The analysis includes new techniques for bounding the variation in FTRL outputs under changing regularizers, which may be of independent interest.

70aecaa608b6fabfb9376ab89119911bd472b951.title: Direct Density Ratio Optimization: A Statistically Consistent Approach to Aligning Large Language Models
70aecaa608b6fabfb9376ab89119911bd472b951.research_question: How can large language models be aligned with human preferences in a statistically consistent and data-driven manner, without relying on specific parametric models of human preference or requiring paired preference data?
70aecaa608b6fabfb9376ab89119911bd472b951.hypothesis: Directly optimizing the density ratio between preferred and unpreferred output distributions, without assuming a specific human preference model, will yield statistically consistent alignment of large language models with human preferences, ensuring convergence to the true preferred distribution as data increases.
70aecaa608b6fabfb9376ab89119911bd472b951.proposed_method: A novel alignment method, Direct Density Ratio Optimization (DDRO), is proposed to align large language models with human preferences. DDRO reframes preference optimization as a direct density ratio estimation problem between the distributions of preferred and unpreferred outputs, circumventing the need for explicit human preference modeling or reward models. The method utilizes Bregman divergence minimization to match the estimated density ratio to the true ratio, ensuring statistical consistency. The approach only requires unpaired preference data (i.e., samples labeled as preferred or unpreferred), and incorporates KL-divergence regularization to prevent catastrophic forgetting and stabilize training. A practical variant introduces a monotonic transformation in the loss to mitigate gradient spikes, further enhancing robustness during optimization.
70aecaa608b6fabfb9376ab89119911bd472b951.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using both unpaired (UF-G) and paired (UF-B) preference datasets derived from the UltraFeedback corpus, with the paired dataset also converted to an unpaired format for comparison. The method is evaluated on multiple downstream benchmarks including BBH, GSM8K, MMLU, TruthfulQA, and AlpacaEval LC Winrate, which assess helpfulness, correctness, and factual consistency. Several large language models of varying sizes (Pythia 1.4B, 2.8B, 6.9B and LLaMA 7B) are fine-tuned using DDRO and compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as KTO, BCO, and DPO. Evaluation metrics include win rates and benchmark-specific scores, with Llama3-70B-Instruct serving as the preference evaluator. The setup ensures fair comparison by applying all methods across identical datasets and model architectures.
70aecaa608b6fabfb9376ab89119911bd472b951.novelty_claims: The proposed method eliminates the need for explicit human preference models (such as Bradley-Terry or prospect theory), enabling alignment that is statistically consistent regardless of the true underlying preference structure. DDRO is the first approach to guarantee convergence to the true preferred distribution as data increases, even with only unpaired preference data. The method unifies and generalizes previous preference optimization techniques under a Bregman divergence framework, and demonstrates that direct density ratio estimation can match or surpass the performance of paired-data methods, even when explicit pairwise information is unavailable. This unlocks scalable, data-driven, and reliable alignment for large language models.

70c3d5ab03a54281be91709b19e3f50a2e4be0e3.title: Transformers as Statisticians: Provable In-Context Learning with In-Context Algorithm Selection
70c3d5ab03a54281be91709b19e3f50a2e4be0e3.research_question: Can transformer architectures be theoretically and empirically shown to perform in-context learning (ICL) by implementing a broad class of machine learning algorithms, and can they adaptively select among these algorithms in context, akin to algorithm selection by statisticians?
70c3d5ab03a54281be91709b19e3f50a2e4be0e3.hypothesis: Transformers can be constructed and pretrained to not only implement a wide range of standard machine learning algorithms in context, but also to perform adaptive in-context algorithm selection, achieving near-optimal predictive power across diverse tasks and data distributions.
70c3d5ab03a54281be91709b19e3f50a2e4be0e3.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the expressive power and in-context prediction capabilities of transformers. Explicit transformer constructions will be designed to approximate standard algorithms such as least squares, ridge regression, Lasso, convex risk minimization for generalized linear models (including logistic regression), and gradient descent on two-layer neural networks. These constructions will leverage efficient in-context gradient descent mechanisms, with quantitative bounds on the number of layers, heads, and weight norms. Two general mechanisms for in-context algorithm selection will be formalized: (1) Pre-ICL testing, where the transformer determines the appropriate task (e.g., regression vs. classification) by examining summary statistics of the input sequence; and (2) Post-ICL validation, where the transformer selects among multiple base ICL algorithms (e.g., ridge regression with different regularization strengths) using a train-validation split. Theoretical guarantees will be established for both the implementation of base algorithms and the algorithm selection mechanisms, including sample complexity and statistical power.
70c3d5ab03a54281be91709b19e3f50a2e4be0e3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using standard transformer architectures trained from scratch on synthetic datasets generated from well-defined statistical models, such as noisy linear regression with varying noise levels and mixed tasks (regression and classification). The input format will encode (input, label) pairs as sequences, with positional and indicator encodings. Baselines will include transformers trained on single tasks and fixed algorithms (e.g., ridge regression with fixed regularization), as well as Bayes-optimal predictors where applicable. Evaluation metrics will include prediction error (e.g., mean squared error for regression, excess risk for classification), and the ability to approach Bayes risk or outperform any fixed base algorithm across task mixtures. Experimental setups will test both the ability to implement individual algorithms and to perform adaptive in-context algorithm selection, with results compared across multiple noise regimes and task types.
70c3d5ab03a54281be91709b19e3f50a2e4be0e3.novelty_claims: The proposed research will provide the first comprehensive statistical theory for transformers' in-context learning abilities, including end-to-end quantitative guarantees for expressive power, prediction performance, and pretraining sample complexity. It will introduce explicit and efficient transformer constructions for a broad range of standard algorithms, with provable near-optimality. The research will also pioneer the formalization and theoretical analysis of in-context algorithm selection by transformers, demonstrating that a single model can adaptively select and execute different algorithms or tasks without explicit prompting. These contributions extend the theoretical understanding of transformers beyond simple algorithm emulation, establishing their capacity for complex adaptive reasoning in context.

70d836e471747a9d0e7bae7c79d0cdd2e78d4226.title: Making Text Embedders Few-Shot Learners
70d836e471747a9d0e7bae7c79d0cdd2e78d4226.research_question: Can the in-context learning (ICL) capabilities of large language models (LLMs) be leveraged to enhance the adaptability and generalization of text embedding models across diverse tasks and domains, without requiring architectural modifications?
70d836e471747a9d0e7bae7c79d0cdd2e78d4226.hypothesis: Integrating few-shot in-context examples into the query prompts of LLM-based embedding models will significantly improve their performance and generalization on both seen and unseen tasks, outperforming traditional instruction-based or architecture-modification approaches.
70d836e471747a9d0e7bae7c79d0cdd2e78d4226.proposed_method: A new text embedding framework will be developed that incorporates few-shot, task-specific examples directly into the query side of the input prompt, leveraging the in-context learning abilities of decoder-only LLMs. The method will use a template that includes the task definition, example query-response pairs, and the target query, all encoded by the same LLM. Embeddings will be extracted from the [EOS] token output of the final layer, maintaining the model's original unidirectional (causal) attention mechanism. Training will employ a contrastive InfoNCE loss with in-batch and hard negatives, and a dynamic sampling strategy will be used to provide a variable number of in-context examples (ranging from zero to n) per query, preserving both few-shot and zero-shot capabilities. The approach will also investigate the impact of different attention mechanisms, pooling strategies, and the use of prompts on both the query and passage sides, but will prioritize simplicity and adherence to the LLM's pretraining architecture.
70d836e471747a9d0e7bae7c79d0cdd2e78d4226.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Mistral-7B LLM as the backbone, fine-tuned with LoRA adaptation (rank 64, alpha 32, learning rate 1e-4) over a single epoch. The model will be trained and evaluated on a comprehensive suite of public and full datasets, including ELI5, HotpotQA, FEVER, MIRACL, MSMARCO, NQ, NLI, SQuAD, TriviaQA, Quora Duplicate Questions, MrTyDi, DuReader, T2Ranking, and others for retrieval, reranking, classification, clustering, and semantic textual similarity tasks. Evaluation will be performed on the MTEB and AIR-Bench benchmarks, covering zero-shot and few-shot scenarios. Baselines will include state-of-the-art embedding models such as E5-mistral-7b-instruct, GritLM-7B, SFR-Embedding, NV-Embed, LLM2Vec, and others. Metrics will include retrieval accuracy (nDCG@10, Recall@10), classification accuracy, clustering performance, and average benchmark scores. Ablation studies will assess the effects of ICL strategies, attention and pooling mechanisms, and prompt configurations.
70d836e471747a9d0e7bae7c79d0cdd2e78d4226.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to systematically integrate few-shot in-context learning into the embedding generation process of LLMs without modifying the model architecture. It demonstrates that simply augmenting the query prompt with task-specific examples enables substantial improvements in generalization and performance across a wide range of tasks, surpassing methods that rely on architectural changes or extensive instruction tuning. The method also introduces a dynamic training regime that balances few-shot and zero-shot capabilities, and provides open access to model checkpoints, datasets, and training scripts for reproducibility.

70db15ba14aaaf6ebf8bbf0df1e112bb806c3da5.title: Ultra-Sparse Memory Network
70db15ba14aaaf6ebf8bbf0df1e112bb806c3da5.research_question: How can large language models be designed to achieve high performance and favorable scaling properties while significantly reducing inference-time memory access and latency, especially compared to existing sparse architectures such as Mixture of Experts (MoE) and Product Key Memory (PKM)?
70db15ba14aaaf6ebf8bbf0df1e112bb806c3da5.hypothesis: Incorporating ultra-sparse, large-scale memory layers with advanced retrieval and value expansion mechanisms into transformer architectures will enable language models to match or surpass the performance and scaling efficiency of MoE models, while achieving inference-time memory access and speed comparable to dense models.
70db15ba14aaaf6ebf8bbf0df1e112bb806c3da5.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces UltraMem, a transformer-based architecture that integrates ultra-sparse memory layers distributed across the model. These memory layers employ Tucker Decomposed Query-Key Retrieval (TDQKR) to improve the precision and efficiency of value retrieval, replacing traditional product quantization with a learnable Tucker core and utilizing a rank-1 SVD-based approximation for computational tractability. Implicit Value Expansion (IVE) is used to virtually expand the memory table via multiple linear projectors, allowing for a much larger effective memory without proportional increases in physical memory access. Multi-Core Scoring (MCS) assigns multiple scores per value using several Tucker cores, further enhancing retrieval diversity and model expressivity. Additional architectural improvements include query/key normalization, causal depthwise convolutional query enhancement, shared query generation, improved initialization tailored to sparse memory, and a decaying learning rate for memory values. UltraMem layers are interleaved at fixed intervals within the transformer, enabling parallel execution and efficient multi-GPU training.
70db15ba14aaaf6ebf8bbf0df1e112bb806c3da5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using large-scale language modeling datasets, primarily RedPajama (1T tokens) for training and C4 for validation, with evaluation on ten diverse benchmarks including MMLU, Trivia-QA, GPQA, ARC, BBH, BoolQ, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, DROP, and AGIeval. Models of varying sizes (151M, 680M, 1.6B, 6.5B parameters for dense baselines; 12x parameter expansion for sparse models) will be trained and compared. Baselines will include dense transformers, PKM, and fine-grained MoE models (with two experts activated per token and balanced expert selection). Evaluation metrics will include validation loss, task-specific accuracy, inference latency, and memory access cost, with experiments run on A100-SXM-80GB GPUs. Ablation studies will assess the impact of each architectural component, and scaling experiments will vary the number of memory slots, top-m activation, and sparsity ratios to analyze performance and efficiency trade-offs.
70db15ba14aaaf6ebf8bbf0df1e112bb806c3da5.novelty_claims: UltraMem introduces a highly scalable, ultra-sparse memory layer architecture that achieves significantly lower inference-time memory access and latency compared to MoE, with up to 6x speedup at common batch sizes. The method advances beyond PKM by enabling large-scale training and deployment, and incorporates several novel techniques: Tucker Decomposed Query-Key Retrieval for precise and efficient memory access, Implicit Value Expansion for virtual memory scaling, and Multi-Core Scoring for enhanced retrieval diversity. The approach demonstrates superior scaling laws and model performance at fixed computational budgets, paving the way for language models with billions of memory slots or experts.

70eb801e73be570b271a093cc810b79fe7858359.title: Data-adaptive Differentially Private Prompt Synthesis for In-Context Learning
70eb801e73be570b271a093cc810b79fe7858359.research_question: Can a data-adaptive differentially private prompt synthesis algorithm be developed to protect private information in prompt data while enabling effective in-context learning with large language models across a variety of downstream tasks?
70eb801e73be570b271a093cc810b79fe7858359.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that adaptively adjusting the noise level in the data synthesis mechanism, according to the inherent statistical properties and clustering behavior of the data, will preserve high in-context learning accuracy while maintaining formal differential privacy guarantees.
70eb801e73be570b271a093cc810b79fe7858359.proposed_method: A two-stage framework is proposed for differentially private in-context learning (ICL). In Stage 1, a novel algorithm, AdaDPSyn, generates synthetic few-shot demonstrations from a private dataset. AdaDPSyn sequentially generates tokens for each demonstration by aggregating next-token probability vectors from an LLM, using multiple disjoint subsets of the private data. The core innovation is the Precision-Focused Iterative Radius Reduction technique, which dynamically identifies a minimal enclosing ball (cluster) of the probability vectors and adaptively reduces the aggregation radius, thus calibrating the amount of noise added according to the degree of consensus among the vectors. This process involves differentially private estimation of the target radius, projected mean estimation using the Gaussian mechanism, and iterative radius refinement with coverage checks. In Stage 2, the generated synthetic demonstrations are used as prompts for ICL tasks, ensuring that the privacy cost is incurred only once and not per query.
70eb801e73be570b271a093cc810b79fe7858359.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard text classification and information extraction benchmarks, including AGNews, DBPedia, TREC, and MIT Movies trivia10k13 (MIT-G and MIT-D). The Llama-2-7b-hf model will be used as the primary LLM, with additional evaluation using GPT-3.5 Turbo and GPT-4o mini. The proposed method will be compared against the DP few-shot generation algorithm, which uses data-independent noise addition, as well as non-private baselines and fully private (instruction-only) baselines. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy and robustness to membership inference attacks. Experiments will be run with varying privacy budgets (ε = 1, 2, 4, 8), number of shots, and across different LLMs, with results averaged over multiple random seeds to assess stability and generalization.
70eb801e73be570b271a093cc810b79fe7858359.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a data-adaptive differentially private prompt synthesis algorithm (AdaDPSyn) that leverages the clustering behavior of next-token probability vectors to minimize noise addition during aggregation. The Precision-Focused Iterative Radius Reduction technique dynamically adjusts the aggregation radius and noise level based on the observed data structure, leading to improved utility compared to data-independent approaches. The method provides rigorous (ε, δ)-differential privacy guarantees using Rényi Differential Privacy analysis and is applicable to a broad range of ICL tasks without requiring public data. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior accuracy and privacy-utility tradeoffs compared to existing baselines, closely approaching non-private performance even under strict privacy constraints.

71339c04a25da137141bd528d0e3a4734a867907.title: Near-Minimax-Optimal Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning with CVaR
71339c04a25da137141bd528d0e3a4734a867907.research_question: How can reinforcement learning algorithms be designed to achieve minimax-optimal regret guarantees under risk-sensitive objectives, specifically Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR), in both multi-armed bandit and tabular Markov Decision Process (MDP) settings?
71339c04a25da137141bd528d0e3a4734a867907.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that novel confidence-bonus-based algorithms, leveraging Bernstein-type bonuses and value iteration in augmented MDPs, can achieve minimax-optimal or near-minimax-optimal regret rates for CVaR objectives, outperforming existing methods in both statistical efficiency and computational feasibility.
71339c04a25da137141bd528d0e3a4734a867907.proposed_method: The proposed methodology will develop two main algorithmic frameworks: (1) a Bernstein-UCB algorithm for multi-armed bandits that constructs confidence intervals for CVaR estimates using a Bernstein-based bonus, enabling minimax-optimal regret scaling with respect to the risk tolerance parameter τ, the number of actions, and episodes; and (2) a CVaR-UCBVI algorithm for tabular MDPs, which performs value iteration in an augmented state space that tracks both the environment state and a budget variable, using bonus-driven exploration based on either Hoeffding or Bernstein inequalities. The Bernstein bonus will be designed to account for the variance in CVaR estimation and will be adapted to the augmented MDP structure. Both algorithms will incorporate reward discretization to ensure computational efficiency, reducing the dynamic programming steps to a finite grid over the budget variable. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to establish high-probability regret bounds and to demonstrate minimax-optimality under mild continuity assumptions on the return distributions.
71339c04a25da137141bd528d0e3a4734a867907.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in both synthetic and standard benchmark environments for multi-armed bandits and tabular MDPs. For the bandit setting, various reward distributions, including Bernoulli and continuous cases, will be used to evaluate the regret performance of Bernstein-UCB against existing baselines such as Brown-UCB and CVaR-UCB. In the RL setting, tabular MDPs with varying numbers of states, actions, and episode horizons will be constructed, and the performance of CVaR-UCBVI (with both Hoeffding and Bernstein bonuses) will be compared to prior algorithms with regret guarantees for CVaR RL. Evaluation metrics will include cumulative CVaR regret, computational runtime, and sensitivity to the risk tolerance parameter τ. The effect of reward discretization precision on both regret and computational efficiency will also be systematically studied.
71339c04a25da137141bd528d0e3a4734a867907.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first minimax-optimal regret bounds for risk-sensitive RL with CVaR objectives in both bandit and tabular MDP settings, improving upon previous results by achieving tighter dependence on the risk parameter τ and eliminating unnecessary scaling with the horizon length. The Bernstein-UCB algorithm is novel in its use of a Bernstein-based bonus for CVaR estimation, which does not require continuity assumptions on the reward distribution. The CVaR-UCBVI algorithm innovatively applies bonus-driven value iteration in an augmented MDP, and the analysis leverages a new simulation lemma for CVaR RL and precise variance decomposition. The approach also demonstrates computational efficiency via reward discretization, making the algorithms practical for large-scale problems.

713a0269aa8ffa9f5e8f5671fddc3768a2da9ec5.title: EquiformerV2: Improved Equivariant Transformer for Scaling to Higher-Degree Representations
713a0269aa8ffa9f5e8f5671fddc3768a2da9ec5.research_question: Can equivariant Transformer architectures be effectively scaled to support higher-degree representations for improved modeling of 3D atomistic systems, while maintaining computational efficiency and achieving superior accuracy in predicting atomic energies and forces?
713a0269aa8ffa9f5e8f5671fddc3768a2da9ec5.hypothesis: Scaling equivariant Transformers to higher-degree representations, combined with targeted architectural improvements, will enhance their expressivity and accuracy on challenging atomistic prediction tasks, while maintaining or improving computational efficiency.
713a0269aa8ffa9f5e8f5671fddc3768a2da9ec5.proposed_method: The proposed method will develop an improved equivariant Transformer architecture for 3D atomistic systems by incorporating efficient eSCN convolutions, which reduce the computational complexity of tensor products from O(L^6) to O(L^3), enabling practical use of higher maximum degrees (L_max) up to 6 or 8. Three architectural enhancements will be introduced: (1) attention re-normalization, which adds an additional layer normalization before non-linear attention functions to stabilize training with increased channel width; (2) separable S2 activation, which applies S2 activation separately to degree-0 and higher-degree vectors to prevent large gradients and enable more expressive non-linearities; and (3) separable layer normalization, which normalizes degree-0 and higher-degree vectors separately to preserve their relative magnitudes and improve performance. The overall architecture will include equivariant graph attention with eSCN-based message passing, enhanced feedforward networks, and improved embedding and output modules tailored for energy and force prediction.
713a0269aa8ffa9f5e8f5671fddc3768a2da9ec5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale datasets including OC20 (Open Catalyst 2020), OC22 (Open Catalyst 2022), and QM9. The OC20 and OC22 datasets provide diverse and challenging tasks for energy and force prediction, as well as structural relaxation and adsorption energy calculations. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art models such as SchNet, DimeNet++, GemNet-OC, SCN, and eSCN. Evaluation metrics will comprise mean absolute error (MAE) for energies (meV) and forces (meV/Å), as well as success rates and speedup factors in the AdsorbML benchmark. Ablation studies will be performed to isolate the impact of each architectural improvement and to assess the effect of varying L_max, number of attention heads, and training epochs. Training and inference speed, data efficiency, and trade-offs between accuracy and computational cost will also be systematically evaluated.
713a0269aa8ffa9f5e8f5671fddc3768a2da9ec5.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first equivariant Transformer architecture capable of efficiently scaling to higher-degree representations using eSCN convolutions. It further innovates by proposing three new architectural techniques—attention re-normalization, separable S2 activation, and separable layer normalization—that collectively enable stable and effective training at higher degrees. The approach is expected to set new state-of-the-art results on large-scale atomistic datasets, achieve superior speed-accuracy trade-offs, and significantly reduce the number of expensive DFT calculations required for adsorption energy prediction. Additionally, the method demonstrates improved data efficiency and generalization, especially on complex and diverse datasets.

716754c9f228a4f63d8e6edb81e200d6f4ea0c3a.title: Real-time Photorealistic Dynamic Scene Representation and Rendering with 4D Gaussian Splatting
716754c9f228a4f63d8e6edb81e200d6f4ea0c3a.research_question: How can dynamic 3D scenes be efficiently reconstructed from 2D images and rendered photorealistically in real-time, while accurately modeling both spatial and temporal complexity?
716754c9f228a4f63d8e6edb81e200d6f4ea0c3a.hypothesis: Jointly optimizing a collection of 4D Gaussian primitives with explicit geometry and appearance modeling, including integrated spatio-temporal covariance and time-evolving view-dependent color, will enable real-time, high-fidelity rendering of complex dynamic scenes, outperforming existing methods in both quality and efficiency.
716754c9f228a4f63d8e6edb81e200d6f4ea0c3a.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that represents dynamic scenes as a set of 4D Gaussian primitives, each parameterized by an anisotropic ellipsoid capable of arbitrary rotation in both space and time. The covariance matrix of each primitive will be constructed using 4D scaling and rotation matrices, allowing coherent modeling of spatio-temporal structure and motion. Appearance will be modeled using coefficients of 4D spherindrical harmonics, which generalize spherical harmonics to capture both view-dependent and temporally-evolving color. The rendering pipeline will decompose each 4D Gaussian into a conditional 3D Gaussian (for space, conditioned on time) and a marginal 1D Gaussian (for time), projecting these to 2D splats for efficient rasterization. The entire system will be trained end-to-end using only rendering loss, with interleaved optimization and density control, including densification and pruning in both space and time.
716754c9f228a4f63d8e6edb81e200d6f4ea0c3a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Plenoptic Video dataset (real, multi-view dynamic scenes) and the D-NeRF dataset (synthetic, monocular dynamic scenes). For the Plenoptic Video dataset, colored point clouds generated by COLMAP will be used to initialize Gaussians, with timestamps distributed across the scene duration. For D-NeRF, 100,000 points will be uniformly sampled within a cubic volume, covering the scene's time range. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art dynamic scene synthesis methods such as DyNeRF, HexPlane, K-Planes, MixVoxels, NeRFPlayer, HyperReel, and V4D. Evaluation metrics will include PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and rendering speed (FPS). Ablation studies will investigate the impact of 4D rotation, spherindrical harmonics, and temporal densification. Rendering quality will be assessed on both novel views and dynamic regions, and qualitative results will be visualized alongside ground truth and optical flow references.
716754c9f228a4f63d8e6edb81e200d6f4ea0c3a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first coherent, integrated 4D Gaussian primitive for dynamic scene representation, treating space and time equally via a unified covariance structure and 4D rotation. The use of 4D spherindrical harmonics enables interpretable, efficient modeling of time-evolving, view-dependent appearance. The method supports end-to-end training and real-time rendering of high-resolution, photorealistic novel views in complex dynamic scenes, including volumetric effects and varying lighting. This work claims to be the first to achieve real-time, high-fidelity video synthesis for complex, real-world dynamic scenes, with substantial improvements in both visual quality and rendering speed over prior methods.

71880f91d9aafd0ef927429253ec443b05d9ab32.title: MSGNN: A Spectral Graph Neural Network Based on a Novel Magnetic Signed Laplacian
71880f91d9aafd0ef927429253ec443b05d9ab32.research_question: How can spectral graph neural networks be effectively designed to process and learn from graphs that contain both signed and directed edges, enabling accurate node clustering and link prediction in networks where both edge sign and directionality are important?
71880f91d9aafd0ef927429253ec443b05d9ab32.hypothesis: A spectral graph neural network architecture based on a novel magnetic signed Laplacian can jointly encode and leverage both signed and directional information in graphs, leading to superior performance on node clustering and link prediction tasks compared to existing methods that focus on only one or neither of these aspects.
71880f91d9aafd0ef927429253ec443b05d9ab32.proposed_method: A new Hermitian, positive semidefinite matrix called the magnetic signed Laplacian will be formulated to generalize both the signed Laplacian for signed graphs and the magnetic Laplacian for directed graphs. This Laplacian incorporates both edge sign and directionality via a symmetrized adjacency matrix and a phase matrix parameterized by a charge parameter q, allowing for flexible encoding of directional information. Spectral convolution operations will be defined using the eigen-decomposition of this Laplacian, and implemented efficiently via Chebyshev polynomial approximations to reduce computational complexity and parameter count. The resulting spectral graph neural network architecture (MSGNN) will use complex-valued activations and multiple convolutional layers, followed by real-valued output layers for node clustering and link prediction tasks. The architecture will be designed to aggregate information from both incoming and outgoing edges, with the ability to tune the influence of directionality through the charge parameter.
71880f91d9aafd0ef927429253ec443b05d9ab32.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic datasets will include established models such as the Signed Stochastic Block Model (SSBM) and a novel Signed Directed Stochastic Block Model (SDSBM) that encodes both sign and directionality in its meta-graph structure. Real-world datasets will include standard signed and directed networks (BitCoin-Alpha, BitCoin-OTC, Slashdot, Epinions) as well as new financial lead-lag networks constructed from stock return time series. Node clustering will be evaluated in a semi-supervised setting using the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), and link prediction tasks will include sign prediction, direction prediction, and multi-class prediction (three, four, and five classes), with accuracy as the evaluation metric. Baseline comparisons will include SGCN, SDGNN, SiGAT, SNEA, SSSNET, and SigMaNet. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the charge parameter, feature construction, and edge weighting.
71880f91d9aafd0ef927429253ec443b05d9ab32.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first spectral GNN architecture capable of jointly processing both signed and directed information in graphs via a novel magnetic signed Laplacian. The Laplacian naturally generalizes previous Laplacians for signed or directed graphs and retains desirable spectral properties. A new synthetic network model (SDSBM) and real-world financial datasets are contributed for benchmarking. The approach is claimed to achieve leading or state-of-the-art performance on tasks where both sign and directionality are relevant, while being computationally efficient and parameter-efficient compared to multi-relational GNNs.

7198e6acc18981d8bd01ee2f904e53e73d2ad78d.title: Denoising Diffusion Bridge Models
7198e6acc18981d8bd01ee2f904e53e73d2ad78d.research_question: How can a unified and scalable generative modeling framework be developed to enable efficient and principled translation between arbitrary probability distributions, including both image-to-image translation and unconditional generation tasks?
7198e6acc18981d8bd01ee2f904e53e73d2ad78d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a generative modeling framework based on diffusion bridges, which learns to reverse a stochastic process conditioned on paired endpoints, can achieve superior or comparable performance to existing diffusion and optimal transport-based models for both image translation and unconditional generation, while enabling seamless integration of advanced architectural and sampling techniques.
7198e6acc18981d8bd01ee2f904e53e73d2ad78d.proposed_method: A new generative modeling framework, Denoising Diffusion Bridge Models (DDBMs), will be developed to interpolate between two arbitrary endpoint distributions using diffusion bridges. The method will learn the score function of the diffusion bridge from paired data samples by matching the conditional score of a tractable Gaussian bridge distribution. Sampling will be performed by solving a reverse-time stochastic differential equation (SDE) or a probability flow ordinary differential equation (ODE) parameterized by the learned score network, with additional flexibility introduced via a guidance parameter controlling the drift adjustment. The approach will generalize existing score-based diffusion models and OT-Flow-Matching by allowing for arbitrary endpoint distributions, and will incorporate advanced parameterizations, noise schedules, and hybrid stochastic-ODE samplers to ensure scalability, stability, and high sample quality. The method will also include a hybrid sampler that combines higher-order ODE integration with scheduled stochastic steps to improve diversity and sharpness of generated samples.
7198e6acc18981d8bd01ee2f904e53e73d2ad78d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on challenging image-to-image translation tasks using datasets such as Edges→Handbags (64×64) and DIODE-Outdoor (256×256), as well as on unconditional image generation tasks with CIFAR-10 and FFHQ-64×64. Evaluation metrics will include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS), LPIPS, and MSE to assess generation quality, perceptual similarity, and translation faithfulness. Baselines for comparison will include Pix2Pix, SDEdit, DDIB, RectifiedFlow, I2SB, and state-of-the-art diffusion models such as DDPM, DDIM, DDPM++, NCSN++, and EDM. The experimental setup will ensure consistent network architectures and comparable numbers of function evaluations across methods. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of preconditioning, sampler design, and guidance scale on performance.
7198e6acc18981d8bd01ee2f904e53e73d2ad78d.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a principled and tractable approach to distribution translation via diffusion bridges, unifying and generalizing score-based diffusion models and optimal transport flow-matching methods. It enables direct modeling of transport between arbitrary distributions, supports both stochastic and deterministic sampling, and allows integration of advanced architectural and sampling techniques from the diffusion literature. The method claims significant improvements in image translation quality and faithfulness over existing baselines, and matches state-of-the-art performance in unconditional generation, all within a single, scalable, and theoretically grounded framework.

71990b0af0783c3c6656aa13697eac27a3c89ffa.title: Scaling Laws and Compute-Optimal Training Beyond Fixed Training Durations
71990b0af0783c3c6656aa13697eac27a3c89ffa.research_question: How can the training of large language models be made more efficient and flexible, particularly in the context of scaling law experiments, by revisiting the necessity of the cosine learning rate schedule and exploring alternative training recipes?
71990b0af0783c3c6656aa13697eac27a3c89ffa.hypothesis: A constant learning rate schedule with a short cooldown phase, or the use of stochastic weight averaging, can match or outperform the performance of the standard cosine learning rate schedule for large language model training, while significantly reducing computational cost and enabling more flexible and reusable training runs.
71990b0af0783c3c6656aa13697eac27a3c89ffa.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves replacing the conventional cosine learning rate schedule with a constant learning rate followed by a short cooldown phase, where the learning rate is rapidly decreased to zero or a small value. Various forms for the cooldown phase, such as linear and (1-sqrt) decay, are systematically explored to identify optimal performance. Additionally, stochastic weight averaging (SWA) is applied by averaging model weights over fixed windows during training, providing an alternative to explicit learning rate decay. The approach allows for continual training by initiating the cooldown or averaging phase at any checkpoint, thus enabling model evaluation at multiple compute budgets from a single training run. A schedule-free optimizer (SFO) is also evaluated as a potential alternative to explicit learning rate schedules.
71990b0af0783c3c6656aa13697eac27a3c89ffa.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on decoder-only transformer models with architectures similar to LLaMA and Noam, using the AdamW optimizer and standard LLM training hyperparameters. Training is performed on subsets of the SlimPajama (6B tokens) and FineWeb datasets, with model sizes ranging from 33M to 8B parameters. Baselines include the cosine learning rate schedule, with comparisons made to constant+cooldown schedules (using both linear and (1-sqrt) cooldowns), SWA, and SFO. Evaluation metrics include validation loss (perplexity) and downstream benchmarks such as MMLU. Scaling law experiments are performed by training each model size once with a long run and applying cooldowns or SWA at different checkpoints, in contrast to the baseline which requires multiple runs per model size. Compute and GPU hour savings are quantified, and ablations are conducted on learning rate sensitivity, cooldown duration, and decay forms.
