71990b0af0783c3c6656aa13697eac27a3c89ffa.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a practical and flexible alternative to the cosine learning rate schedule for large language model training, enabling continual training and ad-hoc evaluation at various compute budgets without retraining from scratch. The (1-sqrt) cooldown form is identified as a superior alternative to linear decay. The methodology allows for scaling law experiments to be conducted with significantly fewer training runs, reducing compute and GPU hours by up to half or more. Stochastic weight averaging is shown to provide strong, though not always optimal, model performance along the training trajectory without additional training cost. The approach democratizes scaling law research by making it more accessible and economically feasible.

71b99a53892409720dc8867afffe64bf3632af6b.title: Learning Concise and Descriptive Attributes for Visual Recognition
71b99a53892409720dc8867afffe64bf3632af6b.research_question: Can a concise set of natural language attributes be learned to enable interpretable and effective visual recognition across diverse image classification tasks, while maintaining competitive performance compared to using large-scale attribute sets or raw image features?
71b99a53892409720dc8867afffe64bf3632af6b.hypothesis: There exist small, representative subsets of natural language attributes that can maintain high visual recognition performance, matching that of massive attribute pools, and these concise sets will enhance interpretability and human interactivity.
71b99a53892409720dc8867afffe64bf3632af6b.proposed_method: A new paradigm is proposed that first queries large language models (LLMs) to generate a large pool of candidate visual attribute concepts for each class or group of classes in a dataset using prompt engineering. These attribute concepts are then embedded using a vision-language model (VLM) such as CLIP, and images are projected into this attribute space via semantic projection, where each dimension corresponds to the similarity between the image and an attribute. To address redundancy and noise in the large attribute pool, a task-guided learning-to-search method is developed: a learnable dictionary is trained to approximate the VLM text embedding space, and a greedy nearest neighbor search is used to select a concise set of K attribute embeddings that are most discriminative for the classification task. The selection is guided by a mixture of cross-entropy loss (for classification) and Mahalanobis distance regularization (to align the learned dictionary with the VLM latent space). The final model uses these selected attributes as the basis for interpretable classification and enables natural language-based model interaction.
71b99a53892409720dc8867afffe64bf3632af6b.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on 8 visual recognition datasets, including CUB, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Food-101, Flower, Oxford-pets, Stanford-cars, and a subset of ImageNet-Animals. For each dataset, LLMs (e.g., GPT-3, ChatGPT) are prompted to generate attribute pools, and CLIP ViT-B/32 is used for semantic projection. The proposed method is compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as LaBO (LLM-generated attributes), CompDL (human-designed attributes), and human-annotated attribute sets, as well as heuristic selection methods (K-means, uniform sampling, SVD, similarity-based selection). Evaluation is performed using linear probing for classification accuracy, with metrics including top-1 accuracy and ablation studies on attribute pool size, selection strategy, and regularization. The number of attributes K is varied, and both full and few-shot settings are tested. Additional analyses include interpretability, human interactivity (attribute intervention), and visualization of learned attributes.
71b99a53892409720dc8867afffe64bf3632af6b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel learning-to-search framework that identifies concise, highly descriptive sets of natural language attributes for visual recognition, significantly reducing attribute pool size while maintaining or exceeding classification performance compared to large-scale or human-annotated attribute sets. The method demonstrates that massive LLM-generated attribute pools contain significant redundancy and noise, and that a small, optimized subset can provide strong interpretability and enable human-in-the-loop interaction. The approach is validated across a wide range of datasets, showing broad applicability and efficiency, and offers a new paradigm for interpretable, interactive, and knowledge-summarizing visual recognition.

71ba5f845bd22d42003675b7cea970ca9e590bcc.title: Editing Models with Task Arithmetic
71ba5f845bd22d42003675b7cea970ca9e590bcc.research_question: How can the behavior of pre-trained neural network models be efficiently and flexibly edited to improve performance on downstream tasks, mitigate undesirable behaviors, or enable knowledge transfer, without requiring access to original training data or additional fine-tuning?
71ba5f845bd22d42003675b7cea970ca9e590bcc.hypothesis: Task vectors, defined as the difference between the weights of a fine-tuned model and its pre-trained counterpart, can be combined through arithmetic operations (such as addition, negation, and analogy-based combinations) to steer model behavior in a modular, efficient, and effective manner across various tasks and domains.
71ba5f845bd22d42003675b7cea970ca9e590bcc.proposed_method: The proposed methodology constructs task vectors by subtracting the weights of a pre-trained model from those of the same model after fine-tuning on a specific task, resulting in a vector in weight space that encodes task-specific adaptation. These task vectors are then manipulated via arithmetic operations: negation (to remove or forget specific behaviors), addition (to combine capabilities from multiple tasks into a single model), and analogy-based combinations (to transfer knowledge to tasks with little or no labeled data). The modified task vectors are applied to the pre-trained model's weights using element-wise addition with an optional scaling factor, which is tuned on held-out validation data. The approach is architecture-agnostic as long as the models share the same structure and initialization, and does not require access to training data or further fine-tuning, enabling rapid and memory-efficient model editing.
71ba5f845bd22d42003675b7cea970ca9e590bcc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both vision and language models, including CLIP (ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16, ViT-L/14) for image classification and T5 and GPT-2 for natural language processing. Datasets for image tasks include Cars, DTD, EuroSAT, GTSRB, MNIST, RESISC45, SUN397, SVHN, and ImageNet as a control. For language tasks, GLUE benchmark tasks (MRPC, RTE, CoLA, SST-2), Civil Comments for toxicity, WikiText-103 for perplexity, and sentiment analysis datasets (Yelp, Amazon) are used. Baselines include standard fine-tuning, gradient ascent (to increase loss), random vector addition, and fine-tuning on non-target data. Evaluation metrics include task accuracy, toxicity rate, perplexity, and normalized accuracy across tasks. Experimental setups involve combining task vectors from various sources, scaling them based on validation performance, and assessing the impact on both target and control tasks, as well as in low-data and analogy-based transfer scenarios.
71ba5f845bd22d42003675b7cea970ca9e590bcc.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a paradigm for model editing based on arithmetic operations over task vectors in weight space, enabling modular addition, removal, or transfer of task-specific capabilities without additional training or data. The approach is claimed to be simple, fast, and efficient, incurring no extra inference cost and allowing practitioners to leverage existing fine-tuned models for rapid experimentation. Novel contributions include the demonstration of task forgetting via vector negation, multi-task model construction via vector addition, and analogy-based transfer to tasks with scarce data, all through direct manipulation of model weights.

71cad6ef8ce6faf76618de4c8ca47d3b9a62961d.title: Boosting Diffusion Models with Moving Average Sampling in Frequency Domain
71cad6ef8ce6faf76618de4c8ca47d3b9a62961d.research_question: How can the stability and quality of the denoising process in diffusion models for image generation be improved, particularly by leveraging information from prior samples and frequency domain characteristics, without requiring retraining or significant computational overhead?
71cad6ef8ce6faf76618de4c8ca47d3b9a62961d.hypothesis: Incorporating a moving average mechanism in the frequency domain, which ensembles prior denoised samples at each timestep, will stabilize the denoising process in diffusion models and improve image generation quality across various tasks and datasets, with negligible additional computational cost.
71cad6ef8ce6faf76618de4c8ca47d3b9a62961d.proposed_method: A novel sampling technique, Moving Average Sampling in Frequency domain (MASF), will be developed to enhance diffusion models. The method reframes the iterative denoising process as model optimization and applies a moving average over all prior denoised samples, but crucially, this is performed after mapping samples back to the data space to avoid distribution shifts across timesteps. Discrete Wavelet Transformation (DWT) is used to decompose each sample into multiple frequency components (subbands), and moving average is performed separately on each component. A dynamic weighting scheme is introduced to prioritize low-frequency components in early timesteps and gradually shift focus to high-frequency components as denoising progresses. The refined frequency components are then recombined via inverse DWT and fed into the denoising network at each step. The entire process is designed to be training-free and compatible with mainstream diffusion models and sampling schedules.
71cad6ef8ce6faf76618de4c8ca47d3b9a62961d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both conditional and unconditional diffusion models using datasets such as ImageNet (at 64x64, 128x128, and 256x256 resolutions), MS-COCO, LSUN, and FFHQ. The proposed method will be evaluated with various solvers (e.g., DDIM, DDPM, DPM-Solver++, UniPC, F-PNDM) and under different sampling schedules (number of function evaluations, NFE). Baselines will include standard diffusion model samplers and recent high-order solvers, with and without classifier guidance. Evaluation metrics will primarily be Frechet Inception Distance (FID) computed on tens of thousands of generated samples per setting. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of each component (data space moving average, frequency decomposition, dynamic weighting), as well as sensitivity to hyperparameters such as the moving average coefficient and weighting schemes.
71cad6ef8ce6faf76618de4c8ca47d3b9a62961d.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a training-free, frequency-domain moving average sampling strategy that can be seamlessly integrated into existing diffusion models and sampling schedules. Unlike prior approaches, it leverages all prior samples in the generative process, decomposes samples into frequency components, and dynamically weights their contributions to harmonize denoising stability with frequency evolution. The approach requires negligible additional computational overhead and does not necessitate retraining or specialized network architectures, distinguishing it from previous frequency-aware or momentum-based sampling techniques. Extensive experiments are planned to validate its generality and effectiveness across datasets, model types, and sampling strategies.

71e15a9a52dcafca57bff5f310b95e2c7d0cfc87.title: Diagonal State Spaces are as Effective as Structured State Spaces
71e15a9a52dcafca57bff5f310b95e2c7d0cfc87.research_question: Can a fully diagonal parameterization of state space models achieve comparable performance to more complex structured state space models on tasks requiring long-range dependency modeling across various modalities such as text, images, and audio?
71e15a9a52dcafca57bff5f310b95e2c7d0cfc87.hypothesis: A diagonal state space model, with appropriate initialization and parameterization, is as expressive and effective as structured state space models (such as those using diagonal plus low-rank matrices) for modeling long-range dependencies in sequential data.
71e15a9a52dcafca57bff5f310b95e2c7d0cfc87.proposed_method: A new framework is developed that parameterizes state space models using only diagonal matrices for the state transition, rather than the diagonal plus low-rank structure used in prior work. The method leverages mathematical results showing that, under mild technical assumptions, diagonal state spaces can be as expressive as general state spaces. Two main variants are proposed: one using an exponential parameterization with negative real parts for stability, and another using a numerically stable softmax normalization over complex values. Each layer computes a state space kernel efficiently using structured matrix-vector products and discrete convolution (via FFT), with per-channel parameterization and a residual connection followed by a non-linearity and linear projection. Careful initialization, particularly using eigenvalues derived from the HiPPO matrix (Skew-HiPPO initialization), is used to ensure effective training and convergence.
71e15a9a52dcafca57bff5f310b95e2c7d0cfc87.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the Long Range Arena (LRA) benchmark, which includes six sequence-level classification tasks with input lengths ranging from 1,000 to 16,000 across modalities such as text, images, and mathematical expressions. Additional experiments are performed on the Speech Commands dataset for raw audio classification (10-way, input length 16,000). The proposed diagonal state space models are compared against structured state space models (S4), various Transformer variants, and other long-range models. Evaluation metrics include classification accuracy. All models are trained with identical hyperparameters, and ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of initialization and kernel truncation on performance.
71e15a9a52dcafca57bff5f310b95e2c7d0cfc87.novelty_claims: The proposed method demonstrates that a fully diagonal parameterization of state space models can match or exceed the performance of more complex structured state space models on long-range tasks, while being conceptually simpler, easier to implement, and more transparent. The approach eliminates the need for low-rank corrections, specialized matrix approximations, and complex linear algebraic reductions, enabling implementation in a few lines of code. The work provides new theoretical and empirical insights into the expressiveness of diagonal state spaces and highlights the critical role of initialization in state space models.

71edd1cf7ae2df17b04a1829510723e5417df78b.title: Shifting the Paradigm: A Diffeomorphism Between Time Series Data Manifolds for Achieving Shift-Invariancy in Deep Learning
71edd1cf7ae2df17b04a1829510723e5417df78b.research_question: How can deep learning models for time series data be made robust to arbitrary input shifts, achieving true shift-invariance without compromising task-relevant information or model performance?
71edd1cf7ae2df17b04a1829510723e5417df78b.hypothesis: A differentiable bijective transformation that maps all shifted variants of a time series sample to a unique point on a data manifold of the same dimension will guarantee shift-invariance in deep learning models for time series, without loss of task-relevant information or the need to modify model topology.
71edd1cf7ae2df17b04a1829510723e5417df78b.proposed_method: A novel diffeomorphic transformation is proposed that operates directly in the original high-dimensional data space of time series. This transformation decomposes each time series into its harmonic components via the discrete Fourier transform, then applies a linear phase shift to all harmonics such that the phase angle of a selected harmonic (with period at least as long as the signal) matches a target angle. The transformation is fully differentiable and bijective, ensuring that all shifted variants of a sample are mapped to the same point on a manifold defined by the chosen phase angle. A guidance network is introduced to adaptively select the target phase angle for each sample, using the absolute Fourier transform as input, and is trained jointly with the main classifier. The loss function combines standard cross-entropy for classification with a regularization term that encourages consistency of the mapped angles within a batch, thereby reducing intra-class variance and enhancing invariance.
71edd1cf7ae2df17b04a1829510723e5417df78b.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on nine datasets spanning six time series tasks: heart rate estimation (IEEESPC, DaLiA), activity recognition (UCIHAR, HHAR), cardiovascular disease classification (Chapman, PhysioNet2017), step counting (Clemson), sleep stage classification (Sleep-EDF), and lung sound classification (Respiratory@TR). Baselines include low-pass filtering, adaptive subsampling grids, shift-equivariant wavelet networks, and canonical representation learning techniques. The main architecture is a ResNet adapted for time series, with fully connected networks used for single-dimensional IMU tasks and the guidance network. Evaluation metrics include accuracy, F1 score, AUC, RMSE, MAE, MAPE, and a shift consistency metric (S-Cons.) that measures output stability under arbitrary shifts. Models are trained using Adam optimizer with grid-searched learning rates, and cross-validation or patient/session splits as appropriate for each dataset. Ablation studies investigate the impact of the guidance network and loss terms.
71edd1cf7ae2df17b04a1829510723e5417df78b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first differentiable bijective transformation for time series that guarantees complete shift-invariance without dimensionality reduction or modification of model topology. Unlike prior methods, it covers the entire shift space and preserves all task-relevant information. The method is architecture-agnostic and can be integrated with existing models and shift-invariance techniques. Theoretical analysis proves the bijectivity and invariance properties, and empirical results demonstrate consistent performance improvements and perfect shift consistency across diverse time series tasks.

71fdb55b39b8d76fd909f218c0d8de2c4fb6541f.title: Step-by-Step Reasoning for Math Problems via Twisted Sequential Monte Carlo
71fdb55b39b8d76fd909f218c0d8de2c4fb6541f.research_question: How can the sampling efficiency and verification accuracy of large language models (LLMs) in multi-step mathematical reasoning tasks be improved, particularly in ways that reduce reliance on costly process supervision?
71fdb55b39b8d76fd909f218c0d8de2c4fb6541f.hypothesis: Applying Twisted Sequential Monte Carlo (TSMC) to the verification process in LLM-based multi-step reasoning will increase sampling efficiency and verification accuracy, while reducing or eliminating the need for step-wise human annotations.
71fdb55b39b8d76fd909f218c0d8de2c4fb6541f.proposed_method: A verification method based on Twisted Sequential Monte Carlo (TSMC) will be developed for multi-step reasoning with LLMs. The approach will sequentially resample and weight partial solutions at each step of the generation process, focusing computational effort on promising candidates and discarding low-potential sequences early. The method will estimate expected future rewards (value functions) at partial solutions using a neural regressor, trained via contrastive twist learning (CTL) on data sampled from the generator, thus eliminating the need for explicit process supervision. The TSMC algorithm will be implemented at the step level, with a warm-up stage to skip initial resampling and a maximum number of resampling steps to control latency. Stratified sampling will be used for resampling, and incremental importance weights will be assigned to handle early-terminated sequences.
71fdb55b39b8d76fd909f218c0d8de2c4fb6541f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two widely used math benchmarks: GSM8K and MATH (specifically, the MATH500 subset). Fine-tuned Llemma-7B and DeepSeek-7B models will serve as the solution generators. Baseline methods will include zero-shot greedy decoding, majority voting (MV), and weighted majority voting (WMV) with various verifiers: outcome reward model (ORM), process reward model (PRM) trained with human supervision (PRM800K), and PRM trained with automatic supervision (SHEPHERD). The primary evaluation metric will be the problem solving rate (%). For TSMC, resampling will be performed over mini-batches (default M=40), with up to five resampling steps and a warm-up threshold of 50 tokens. Ablation studies will assess the impact of batch size and variance reduction strategies.
71fdb55b39b8d76fd909f218c0d8de2c4fb6541f.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first application of TSMC to verification in LLM-based multi-step reasoning, providing a theoretically grounded framework that bridges sequential Monte Carlo methods with existing verification paradigms (ORM and PRM). The approach offers unbiased estimation with reduced variance, enhances sampling efficiency by focusing on promising partial solutions, and eliminates the need for costly process supervision by learning value functions from generator-sampled data. Theoretical analysis and empirical results are claimed to demonstrate consistent improvements over existing verification methods across multiple math benchmarks and generator architectures.

7210e2002441a48a3d63b4eddbc04964004f74b0.title: Meta Large Language Model Compiler: Foundation Models of Compiler Optimization
7210e2002441a48a3d63b4eddbc04964004f74b0.research_question: Can large language models be specialized and fine-tuned to perform advanced compiler optimization tasks, such as optimization flag tuning and disassembly, using compiler intermediate representations and assembly code as primary training data?
7210e2002441a48a3d63b4eddbc04964004f74b0.hypothesis: Large language models, when pre-trained and fine-tuned on compiler-centric data (including LLVM-IR and assembly code), can achieve competitive performance in compiler optimization tasks, such as flag tuning and disassembly, compared to traditional autotuning and existing language models.
7210e2002441a48a3d63b4eddbc04964004f74b0.proposed_method: A new family of large language models will be developed by initializing with the weights of Code Llama and conducting extensive pretraining on 546 billion tokens of compiler intermediate representations (IRs) and assembly code, primarily targeting x86-64 and ARM architectures. The models will then undergo instruction fine-tuning to emulate compiler optimizations, learning to predict the output of various optimization pass sequences and the resulting code size. Further fine-tuning will be performed for two downstream tasks: (1) optimization flag tuning, where the model predicts sequences of compiler flags to minimize binary size, and (2) disassembly, where the model learns to reconstruct LLVM-IR from assembly code. The training pipeline will retain a fraction of prior-stage data at each step to preserve general code understanding, and will use advanced data minimization and correctness validation tools to ensure high-quality supervision.
7210e2002441a48a3d63b4eddbc04964004f74b0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the MiBench benchmark suite, using 2,398 test prompts derived from 24 benchmarks. The evaluation for flag tuning will compare the model's predicted optimization pass lists against the baseline -Oz optimization, as well as against Code Llama - Instruct and GPT-4 Turbo. Binary size of the resulting object files will serve as the primary evaluation metric, with additional validation using PassListEval to ensure correctness of optimizations. For disassembly, the model will be evaluated on its ability to reconstruct LLVM-IR from assembly, using round-trip compilation to measure correctness (i.e., whether recompiling the IR yields the original assembly). Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of each training stage, and metrics such as mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) for binary size prediction will be reported.
7210e2002441a48a3d63b4eddbc04964004f74b0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first openly available, large-scale language models specifically pre-trained and fine-tuned for compiler optimization tasks using compiler IRs and assembly code. The models provide a scalable and cost-effective foundation for further research in code optimization, achieving a significant fraction of autotuner performance without requiring extensive compilation. The methodology includes novel data generation and minimization pipelines, correctness validation for optimization passes, and demonstrates substantial improvements over existing large language models in both flag tuning and disassembly tasks.

721d2080099677b77b2130488a637f44db35025e.title: Estimating Epistemic and Aleatoric Uncertainty with a Single Model
721d2080099677b77b2130488a637f44db35025e.research_question: How can both epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty be accurately and efficiently estimated in high-stakes machine learning applications using a single, scalable model, especially for complex tasks such as medical imaging and weather forecasting?
721d2080099677b77b2130488a637f44db35025e.hypothesis: A single model that integrates Bayesian hyper-networks with conditional diffusion models can efficiently and accurately estimate both epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty, matching or surpassing the performance of deep ensembles while significantly reducing computational overhead.
721d2080099677b77b2130488a637f44db35025e.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops a unified framework that combines a Bayesian hyper-network (BHN) with a conditional diffusion model (DM) to form a hyper-diffusion model (HyperDM). The BHN is trained to generate diverse sets of weights for the diffusion model by sampling from a noise distribution, effectively capturing the posterior over model parameters. For each sampled set of weights, the diffusion model stochastically generates predictions by inverting a learned diffusion process, allowing for sampling from the implicit likelihood. At inference, M different weight sets are generated by the BHN, and for each, N predictions are sampled from the DM, yielding an ensemble of M × N predictions. The total predictive uncertainty is then decomposed into epistemic and aleatoric components using the law of total variance, with epistemic uncertainty estimated as the variance across ensemble means and aleatoric uncertainty as the mean of variances within each ensemble.
721d2080099677b77b2130488a637f44db35025e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world tasks. For synthetic validation, toy inverse problems with known ground-truth uncertainties will be used to assess the accuracy of epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty estimation. For real-world evaluation, the LUNA16 dataset (for CT reconstruction) and the ERA5 dataset (for weather temperature forecasting) will be used. Baselines will include MC-Dropout, deep-posterior sampling ensembles (DPS-UQ), and Bayesian neural networks. Evaluation metrics will include peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity index (SSIM), and continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) for prediction quality, as well as qualitative and quantitative analyses of uncertainty maps, especially for out-of-distribution detection. Training and inference times will also be compared to assess computational efficiency.
721d2080099677b77b2130488a637f44db35025e.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to apply Bayesian hyper-networks in conjunction with diffusion models for joint estimation of epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty using a single model. It achieves ensemble-level uncertainty estimation and prediction quality with a fraction of the computational cost, scaling efficiently to modern architectures such as Attention U-Net. The approach outperforms or matches deep ensembles and pseudo-ensembling methods in both uncertainty estimation and predictive accuracy, while providing a scalable and practical solution for high-stakes applications.

722ad6ac92286507437b31486f47987d6ece05c9.title: BEiT: BERT Pre-Training of Image Transformers
722ad6ac92286507437b31486f47987d6ece05c9.research_question: How can self-supervised pre-training be effectively applied to vision Transformers to improve their performance on downstream tasks such as image classification and semantic segmentation, without relying on labeled data?
722ad6ac92286507437b31486f47987d6ece05c9.hypothesis: A masked image modeling pre-training task, which predicts discrete visual tokens rather than raw pixels for masked image patches, will enable vision Transformers to learn more effective and generalizable visual representations in a self-supervised manner, leading to improved performance on downstream vision tasks.
722ad6ac92286507437b31486f47987d6ece05c9.proposed_method: A self-supervised pre-training framework for vision Transformers is proposed, inspired by BERT-style masked language modeling. The method first tokenizes each image into a grid of patches and, separately, into discrete visual tokens using a pre-trained discrete variational autoencoder (dVAE). During pre-training, a random subset (approximately 40%) of image patches is masked using blockwise masking and replaced with a learned mask embedding. The corrupted sequence of patches is input to a standard Transformer encoder. The pre-training objective is to predict the original visual tokens corresponding to the masked patches using a softmax classifier over a learned vocabulary. The framework is trained in two stages: first, the image tokenizer (dVAE) is trained to map images to visual tokens; second, the Transformer is trained to recover the visual tokens from masked images. The method leverages blockwise masking and discrete token prediction to encourage learning high-level abstractions.
722ad6ac92286507437b31486f47987d6ece05c9.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on large-scale image datasets, primarily ImageNet-1K for pre-training and fine-tuning, with additional evaluation on the ADE20K dataset for semantic segmentation. The base model uses a 12-layer Transformer with 768 hidden size and 12 attention heads, processing 224x224 images split into 14x14 patches. Baselines include vision Transformers trained from scratch, supervised pre-training on ImageNet-22K, and state-of-the-art self-supervised methods such as DINO and MoCov3. Evaluation metrics include top-1 accuracy for image classification and mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) for semantic segmentation. Fine-tuning is performed with standard protocols, and ablation studies investigate the impact of blockwise masking, visual token prediction, and training duration.
722ad6ac92286507437b31486f47987d6ece05c9.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a masked image modeling task for vision Transformers that predicts discrete visual tokens, overcoming limitations of pixel-level auto-encoding and the lack of a pre-existing visual vocabulary. Blockwise masking is employed to improve learning of semantic structure. The method demonstrates that BERT-style pre-training can be successfully adapted to visual data, leading to state-of-the-art or competitive results on image classification and semantic segmentation tasks without labeled data. Additionally, the approach is shown to improve convergence speed and stability, and the learned representations exhibit emergent semantic properties such as object boundary separation in self-attention maps.

72a4c61ca03caba8e4f15e475a9df8c39ab40ea5.title: How Contaminated Is Your Benchmark? Quantifying Dataset Leakage in Large Language Models with Kernel Divergence
72a4c61ca03caba8e4f15e475a9df8c39ab40ea5.research_question: How can the level of dataset contamination in large language model (LLM) benchmarks be reliably measured when the pre-training data is unavailable, ensuring that evaluation metrics reflect true generalization rather than memorization of previously seen data?
72a4c61ca03caba8e4f15e475a9df8c39ab40ea5.hypothesis: A scoring function that quantifies the divergence between kernel similarity matrices of sample embeddings before and after fine-tuning on a benchmark dataset will provide a reliable and interpretable measure of dataset contamination, exhibiting monotonicity with contamination rate and consistency across i.i.d. samples.
72a4c61ca03caba8e4f15e475a9df8c39ab40ea5.proposed_method: A novel dataset-level scoring function, termed Kernel Divergence Score (KDS), will be developed to assess benchmark contamination. The method involves extracting normalized sample embeddings from a pre-trained LLM both before and after fine-tuning on a given benchmark dataset. For each stage, a kernel similarity matrix is computed using the Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel, with the kernel bandwidth set via the median heuristic. The divergence between the two kernel matrices is then quantified by a function that measures the absolute change in squared Euclidean distances between embedding pairs, weighted by their original similarity, and normalized appropriately. The final contamination score is defined as the negation of this divergence, ensuring that higher scores correspond to higher contamination. The method is designed to satisfy monotonicity (score increases with contamination) and consistency (score is stable across i.i.d. samples with the same contamination rate).
72a4c61ca03caba8e4f15e475a9df8c39ab40ea5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on controlled contamination scenarios using established benchmarks such as WikiMIA, BookMIA, and ArxivTection, where samples are labeled as 'seen' or 'unseen' with respect to model pre-training. For each dataset, contamination ratios will be systematically varied, and multiple independent subsets will be sampled to test consistency. The primary evaluation metrics will be Spearman and Pearson correlation coefficients between the contamination score and the true contamination rate, assessing monotonicity and linearity. Baseline methods for comparison will include Zlib, Perplexity, Min-K%, Fine-tuned Score Deviation, and Sharded Rank Comparison Test, among others. Additional ablation studies will analyze the impact of kernel choice, kernel bandwidth, embedding extraction layer, and fine-tuning configuration. Computational efficiency will be measured in terms of fine-tuning and scoring time on standard hardware.
72a4c61ca03caba8e4f15e475a9df8c39ab40ea5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to leverage fine-grained kernel-based information from LLM embeddings to measure dataset contamination at the dataset level. The method introduces a principled framework that captures structural changes in embedding space induced by fine-tuning, providing a more holistic and robust measure than previous sample-wise or distributional methods. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the Kernel Divergence Score achieves near-perfect correlation with contamination levels, outperforms existing baselines, and remains robust to design choices such as kernel function, bandwidth, and embedding extraction location. The approach is also shown to be efficient and applicable across diverse datasets and model families, enabling more reliable and interpretable benchmark evaluations in LLM research.

72eb9359409a6c41947f26c98e84375cdfd69f4d.title: Sobolev Transport: A Scalable Metric for Probability Measures with Graph Metrics
72eb9359409a6c41947f26c98e84375cdfd69f4d.research_question: How can a scalable and computationally efficient metric be developed for comparing probability measures supported on graph metric spaces, while enabling the construction of positive-definite kernels for use in machine learning applications?
72eb9359409a6c41947f26c98e84375cdfd69f4d.hypothesis: A novel transport metric that leverages the structure of graph metric spaces can provide a closed-form, computationally efficient, and negative definite distance between probability measures, which can be used to construct positive-definite kernels for kernel-based machine learning methods.
72eb9359409a6c41947f26c98e84375cdfd69f4d.proposed_method: A new metric, termed Sobolev transport, will be defined for probability measures supported on graph metric spaces. This metric generalizes the dual formulation of the 1-Wasserstein distance by replacing the Lipschitz constraint with a Sobolev space constraint, resulting in a distance that depends on a graph derivative defined via unique shortest paths from a root node. The method will derive a closed-form expression for the Sobolev transport distance, which involves summing over edges of the graph and computing differences in cumulative measure along specific subgraphs determined by shortest paths. The metric will be shown to be negative definite for certain parameter ranges, allowing the construction of positive-definite kernels. Additionally, a sliced variant will be proposed to mitigate dependence on the choice of root node by averaging over multiple root nodes.
72eb9359409a6c41947f26c98e84375cdfd69f4d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two main applications: document classification using word embeddings and topological data analysis (TDA) with persistence diagrams. For document classification, each document will be represented as a probability measure over word embeddings, and several real-world datasets (e.g., TWITTER, RECIPE, CLASSIC, AMAZON) will be used. For TDA, datasets such as orbit recognition and object shape classification (MPEG7) will be employed, with persistence diagrams representing the data. Graph metrics will be constructed via clustering and random edge sampling. The proposed Sobolev transport kernels will be compared against baselines including optimal transport with graph metric cost and tree-Wasserstein distances. Evaluation will be performed using support vector machines (SVMs), with accuracy and computational time as primary metrics. Hyperparameters will be selected via cross-validation, and experiments will include both standard and sliced variants of the proposed metric.
72eb9359409a6c41947f26c98e84375cdfd69f4d.novelty_claims: The proposed Sobolev transport metric introduces a scalable, closed-form solution for comparing probability measures on graph metric spaces, overcoming the computational limitations of traditional optimal transport. The metric is negative definite, enabling the construction of positive-definite kernels for kernel machines, which is not generally possible with standard OT distances. The method generalizes tree-based Wasserstein distances to arbitrary graphs, and provides an isometry between the space of probability measures and a bounded convex set in Euclidean space. The sliced variant further enhances flexibility by reducing dependence on root node selection. Empirical results demonstrate superior or comparable performance to existing baselines with significantly improved computational efficiency.

7301792d6388d3c669034c1a33431ce510f6c431.title: Preference Diffusion for Recommendation
7301792d6388d3c669034c1a33431ce510f6c431.research_question: How can diffusion models be optimized to more effectively capture user preference distributions for personalized item ranking in recommender systems, particularly by addressing the limitations of current training objectives in handling negative samples and generative modeling?
7301792d6388d3c669034c1a33431ce510f6c431.hypothesis: Reformulating the personalized ranking objective for diffusion model-based recommenders into a log-likelihood generative framework that explicitly incorporates multiple negative samples and leverages variational inference will improve the ability of diffusion models to capture user preference distributions, resulting in superior ranking performance, faster convergence, and enhanced generalization across domains.
7301792d6388d3c669034c1a33431ce510f6c431.proposed_method: A novel optimization objective, PreferDiff, will be developed specifically for diffusion model-based recommenders. PreferDiff reformulates the classical Bayesian Personalized Ranking (BPR) objective into a log-likelihood-based generative framework by applying softmax normalization to the rating function, thus modeling the probability distribution of the next item conditioned on user history. To address the intractability of direct optimization in diffusion models, a variational upper bound will be derived and minimized using variational inference. The method will replace mean squared error (MSE) with cosine error as the distance metric to better align with the similarity-based retrieval used in recommendation tasks. PreferDiff will also incorporate multiple negative samples by using either their centroid or all negatives in the loss computation, and a trade-off hyperparameter will balance generative learning and preference modeling to ensure training stability.
7301792d6388d3c669034c1a33431ce510f6c431.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six widely used public benchmarks, including Amazon Sports, Beauty, Toys, Steam, ML-1M, and Yahoo!R1, with standard five-core preprocessing and chronological user-split (8:1:1) for training, validation, and test sets. The proposed method will be compared against a comprehensive set of baselines: traditional sequential recommenders (GRU4Rec, SASRec, BERT4Rec), contrastive learning-based models (CL4SRec), generative and diffusion-based models (TIGER, DiffRec, DreamRec, DiffuRec), and text-based recommenders (MoRec, LLM2BERT4Rec). Evaluation metrics will include Recall@K and NDCG@K (K=5,10) in a full-ranking setting. Implementation will use both ID- and semantic text-embeddings, with ablation studies to assess the impact of negative sampling, distance metrics, and the trade-off parameter. Zero-shot and cross-domain generalization will be evaluated by pretraining on diverse Amazon categories and transferring to unseen domains and platforms (e.g., Steam).
7301792d6388d3c669034c1a33431ce510f6c431.novelty_claims: PreferDiff is the first personalized ranking loss specifically designed for diffusion model-based recommenders, integrating multiple negative samples into a generative modeling paradigm. The approach establishes a theoretical connection to Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), enabling alignment of user preferences within a generative diffusion framework. PreferDiff demonstrates improved ranking performance, faster convergence, and strong generalization capabilities across domains and platforms without additional model components. The method also introduces the use of cosine error in place of MSE for better alignment with recommendation retrieval, and proposes an efficient strategy for handling multiple negatives via centroid-based denoising.

73303ae474f5a7d865be9cabba824f5d877341e6.title: GPAS: Accelerating Convergence of LLM Pretraining via Gradient-Preserving Activation Scaling
73303ae474f5a7d865be9cabba824f5d877341e6.research_question: How can the convergence speed and parameter efficiency of large language model (LLM) pretraining be improved by addressing activation variance growth in deep transformer architectures, and can a generalizable solution enhance training dynamics across various normalization schemes?
73303ae474f5a7d865be9cabba824f5d877341e6.hypothesis: Introducing a gradient-preserving activation scaling mechanism that adaptively controls activation variance while maintaining gradient magnitudes will mitigate the exponential growth of activation variance in deep transformer models, leading to faster convergence, improved utilization of deeper layers, and better downstream performance across multiple normalization schemes.
73303ae474f5a7d865be9cabba824f5d877341e6.proposed_method: A novel technique, Gradient-Preserving Activation Scaling (GPAS), will be developed and integrated into transformer-based LLM architectures. GPAS operates by scaling down intermediate activations after each sub-layer using a learnable gate parameter per layer, while employing a stop-gradient operator to ensure that the scaling does not affect the magnitude of gradients during backpropagation. The scaling is controlled by a SiLU-activated gate, allowing the network to adaptively modulate the contribution of each layer's output to the residual connection. GPAS will be implemented as a lightweight plugin compatible with Pre-LN, DeepNorm, Sandwich-LN, Mix-LN, and LayerNorm Scaling architectures. The method will be systematically ablated to assess the impact of activation function choice, insertion location, and the necessity of the stop-gradient operator.
73303ae474f5a7d865be9cabba824f5d877341e6.experiment_details: Experiments will involve pretraining LLaMA-based transformer models at scales ranging from 71M to 1B parameters, with additional experiments at 7B parameters for select configurations. All models will be trained on the C4 dataset using the Adam optimizer and T5 tokenizer, with consistent initialization and architectural components except for the normalization scheme. GPAS will be applied to each baseline architecture, and performance will be evaluated using perplexity on held-out validation sets. Supervised fine-tuning will be conducted on 1B models using the Commonsense170K dataset, with evaluation on seven standard reasoning benchmarks (MMLU, WinoG, PIQA, OBQA, HellaSwag, BoolQ, ARC-e) via the LMEvaluationHarness. Baselines will include Post-LN, DeepNorm, Pre-LN, Sandwich-LN, Mix-LN, and LNS, with and without GPAS. Evaluation metrics will include perplexity for pretraining and accuracy for downstream tasks. Detailed analyses will be performed on activation variance, gradient norms, weight norms, and layer importance, with ablation studies on GPAS design choices.
73303ae474f5a7d865be9cabba824f5d877341e6.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple yet effective mechanism for decoupling activation scaling from gradient scaling, enabling stable and efficient training of deep transformer models. GPAS is claimed to be the first technique to directly address exponential activation variance growth in Pre-LN transformers while preserving gradient flow, and is shown to be broadly applicable across multiple normalization schemes. The approach is lightweight, requiring only a per-layer learnable gate and minimal computational overhead, and demonstrates consistent improvements in convergence speed, parameter utilization, and downstream task performance. The method also provides new theoretical insights into the interplay between activation variance and gradient propagation in deep transformers.

734f8e1e5a39a08fd43b0b48c80a2dd2340ac6aa.title: Outside the Echo Chamber: Optimizing the Performative Risk
734f8e1e5a39a08fd43b0b48c80a2dd2340ac6aa.research_question: How can predictive models be optimized in performative settings where model predictions influence the data distribution, specifically with respect to minimizing performative risk rather than merely achieving performative stability?
734f8e1e5a39a08fd43b0b48c80a2dd2340ac6aa.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that under certain structural conditions on the loss function and the model-induced distribution shift, the performative risk can be made convex and thus directly optimized with improved sample efficiency compared to generic derivative-free methods.
734f8e1e5a39a08fd43b0b48c80a2dd2340ac6aa.proposed_method: A new framework is proposed for optimizing performative risk in settings where predictive models influence their own data distribution. The methodology begins by identifying natural structural properties—such as smoothness and strong convexity of the loss, Lipschitz continuity (sensitivity) of the distribution map, and a novel mixture dominance condition—under which the performative risk is provably convex. For cases where the distribution map forms a location-scale family, convexity can be guaranteed even for strong performative effects. To efficiently optimize the performative risk, a two-stage algorithm is developed: first, an explicit model of the distribution map is estimated using experimental design and ordinary least squares; second, a proxy objective for the performative risk is optimized offline using the estimated distribution map. This approach is instantiated and analyzed in the context of location families, providing theoretical guarantees for improved sample efficiency.
734f8e1e5a39a08fd43b0b48c80a2dd2340ac6aa.experiment_details: Experiments are proposed to evaluate the optimization algorithms on synthetic and potentially real-world datasets where performative effects can be controlled or simulated. The two-stage algorithm will be benchmarked against generic zeroth-order (derivative-free) optimization methods, such as those using random perturbations and function evaluations. Evaluation metrics will include the achieved performative risk, convergence rate, and sample efficiency (number of queries or deployments required to reach a suboptimality threshold). The experimental setup involves simulating data distributions that shift in response to model parameters, with controlled parameters for smoothness, convexity, and sensitivity, as well as instantiations of location-scale families. Baselines will include repeated retraining and standard risk minimization approaches.
734f8e1e5a39a08fd43b0b48c80a2dd2340ac6aa.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first systematic analysis of when and how performative risk can be efficiently optimized, moving beyond the traditional focus on performative stability. It identifies new structural conditions—particularly the mixture dominance property—that guarantee convexity of the performative risk, even in the presence of strong performative effects for location-scale families. The two-stage optimization procedure leverages explicit modeling of the distribution map, resulting in significantly improved sample efficiency compared to generic derivative-free methods. The approach generalizes and strengthens prior work by providing both theoretical guarantees and practical algorithms for optimizing performative risk in a broad class of performative prediction problems.

735b7f4f91bcc5e9712df7f419eade672b1d3968.title: Autoregressive Video Generation without Vector Quantization
735b7f4f91bcc5e9712df7f419eade672b1d3968.research_question: How can autoregressive video generation be made more efficient and flexible, while maintaining high visual fidelity and supporting diverse visual generation tasks such as text-to-image, text-to-video, and image-to-video, without relying on vector quantization?
735b7f4f91bcc5e9712df7f419eade672b1d3968.hypothesis: A non-quantized autoregressive model that decouples temporal frame-by-frame prediction from spatial set-by-set prediction, combined with continuous-space modeling and specialized architectural components, will achieve superior data efficiency, inference speed, visual fidelity, and generalization across visual generation tasks compared to existing vector-quantized and diffusion-based models.
735b7f4f91bcc5e9712df7f419eade672b1d3968.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a non-quantized autoregressive framework for video generation, termed NOVA, which reformulates the generation process as temporal frame-by-frame prediction and spatial set-by-set prediction. Text prompts are encoded using a pre-trained language model, and video frames are encoded into a continuous latent space via a pre-trained 3D VAE with temporal and spatial compression. Temporal modeling is performed using block-wise causal masking attention, ensuring each frame attends only to prior frames and context, while spatial modeling within each frame employs a set-by-set bidirectional prediction paradigm, leveraging a Scaling and Shift Layer to robustly model cross-frame motion changes. The model is trained using a diffusion loss for per-token prediction in continuous space, with post-norm layers to stabilize training. During inference, denoising is performed step-by-step from Gaussian noise using the learned diffusion process.
735b7f4f91bcc5e9712df7f419eade672b1d3968.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale, high-quality datasets for both text-to-image and text-to-video tasks, including DataComp, COYO, Unsplash, JourneyDB, LAION, Panda-70M, and Pexels, with up to 600M image-text pairs and 20M video-text pairs. Baselines will include state-of-the-art diffusion models (e.g., PixArt-α, SDXL, DALL-E2/3, SD3), autoregressive models (e.g., Emu3, CogVideo), and recent open- and closed-source video generation models. Evaluation metrics will cover GenEval, T2I-CompBench, DPG-Bench for image tasks, and VBench for video tasks, assessing alignment, quality, semantic accuracy, and fluency. The model will be trained on A100 GPUs using AdamW optimizer, with extensive ablation studies on architectural components such as the Scaling and Shift Layer and normalization strategies. Inference speed, data efficiency, and zero-shot generalization capabilities will be systematically measured.
735b7f4f91bcc5e9712df7f419eade672b1d3968.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first non-quantized autoregressive model for video generation that decouples temporal and spatial prediction, enabling efficient, high-fidelity, and flexible visual generation across multiple contexts. The method leverages a unique combination of frame-by-frame temporal causality and set-by-set spatial bidirectionality, continuous-space diffusion-based per-token prediction, and architectural innovations such as the Scaling and Shift Layer and post-norm stabilization. The unified framework supports diverse tasks (text-to-image, text-to-video, image-to-video) within a single model, achieves state-of-the-art results with significantly reduced model size and training cost, and demonstrates strong zero-shot generalization and scalability.

735f8b04e8b130ff126a24b856046e5c55a4e98d.title: Improving Pretraining Data Using Perplexity Correlations
735f8b04e8b130ff126a24b856046e5c55a4e98d.research_question: How can high-quality pretraining data for large language models be selected efficiently and effectively, without the need for costly retraining or hand-crafted heuristics, in order to maximize downstream benchmark performance?
735f8b04e8b130ff126a24b856046e5c55a4e98d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that correlations between the perplexity (or log-likelihood) assigned by a diverse set of pretrained language models to candidate pretraining data and the downstream benchmark performance can be leveraged to select superior pretraining data, thereby improving language model performance without the need for new model training or extensive human curation.
735f8b04e8b130ff126a24b856046e5c55a4e98d.proposed_method: A statistical framework is developed to estimate the correlation between the log-likelihoods (perplexity) of candidate pretraining documents, as measured by a diverse set of publicly available pretrained LLMs, and downstream benchmark performance. The method computes rank-based correlation coefficients (e.g., a robust U-statistic or Spearman's rank) between the negative log-likelihoods of documents across domains and the performance of these models on target benchmarks. Domains with high positive correlation are prioritized. To operationalize this, a projection step ensures the resulting domain weights form a valid sampling distribution, constrained to avoid over-representation of any domain. An optional fastText classifier is trained to distinguish high-correlation domains at the page level, enabling scalable and fine-grained data selection. The final pretraining dataset is constructed by sampling documents from domains in order of their correlation scores, up to the token budget.
735f8b04e8b130ff126a24b856046e5c55a4e98d.experiment_details: Experiments involve pretraining language models from scratch at the 160M to 1.4B parameter scale using data selected by the proposed method. The primary dataset is the RedPajamaV2 corpus, with domain-level log-likelihoods computed using 90 models from the HuggingFace Open LLM Leaderboard. Downstream evaluation is conducted on a suite of 8 to 22 benchmarks, including LAMBADA, ARC Easy, PIQA, SciQ, and multilingual LAMBADA variants. Baselines include random sampling, language filtering, DSIR (n-gram overlap), and the state-of-the-art fastText classifier from DataComp-LM. Evaluation metrics include accuracy and log-perplexity, with average ranking across benchmarks used for comparison. Hyperparameters are fixed across methods, and ablations are performed to assess the impact of the classifier and projection method.
735f8b04e8b130ff126a24b856046e5c55a4e98d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a parameter-free, training-free framework for pretraining data selection that leverages perplexity correlations across a heterogeneous set of pretrained LLMs, rather than requiring new model training or hand-crafted rules. The method is theoretically grounded in high-dimensional single-index models and robust correlation estimation, and it enables scalable, fine-grained data selection via a fastText classifier. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach consistently outperforms existing baselines and matches or exceeds the best hand-engineered data selectors, with increasing benefits at larger model scales and on more diverse benchmarks.

736973165f98105fec3729b7db414ae4d80fcbeb.title: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers
736973165f98105fec3729b7db414ae4d80fcbeb.research_question: Can transformer-based architectures serve as effective and scalable backbones for diffusion models in image generation, and how does their performance compare to traditional convolutional U-Net backbones across various model complexities and compute budgets?
736973165f98105fec3729b7db414ae4d80fcbeb.hypothesis: Transformer-based backbones, when applied to latent diffusion models and appropriately scaled in terms of depth, width, and input token count, will outperform convolutional U-Net-based diffusion models in image generation tasks, achieving superior sample quality and compute efficiency.
736973165f98105fec3729b7db414ae4d80fcbeb.proposed_method: A new class of diffusion models, termed Diffusion Transformers (DiTs), will be developed by replacing the conventional U-Net backbone in latent diffusion models with a transformer architecture that operates on patchified latent representations of images. The method will utilize Vision Transformer (ViT) best practices, including patch embedding, sine-cosine positional encodings, and a sequence of transformer blocks. Several conditioning mechanisms will be explored within the transformer blocks, such as in-context conditioning, cross-attention, adaptive layer normalization (adaLN), and a novel adaLN-Zero initialization, with the latter hypothesized to provide the best performance. The DiT architecture will be systematically scaled across model size (depth, width, attention heads) and patch size to analyze the relationship between model compute (measured in Gflops) and generative performance. The final output will be decoded from the latent space using a pre-trained VAE decoder.
736973165f98105fec3729b7db414ae4d80fcbeb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the class-conditional ImageNet dataset at 256×256 and 512×512 resolutions, utilizing a pre-trained VAE for latent space encoding and decoding. Multiple DiT configurations (Small, Base, Large, XLarge) and patch sizes (2, 4, 8) will be trained, resulting in a comprehensive sweep of model Gflops. Training will use the AdamW optimizer, a constant learning rate, and minimal data augmentation (horizontal flips), with exponential moving average (EMA) of weights for evaluation. Baselines will include state-of-the-art U-Net-based diffusion models (ADM, LDM) and GANs (BigGAN-deep, StyleGAN-XL). Evaluation metrics will include Frechet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS), sFID, and Precision/Recall, with FID-50K as the primary metric. The impact of model compute versus sampling compute will also be assessed by varying the number of sampling steps at test time.
736973165f98105fec3729b7db414ae4d80fcbeb.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first systematic exploration of transformer-based backbones for diffusion models in image generation, demonstrating that the U-Net inductive bias is not essential for high performance. The DiT architecture leverages scalable transformer designs, incorporates a novel adaLN-Zero conditioning mechanism for improved training stability and sample quality, and establishes that increasing transformer Gflops—via depth, width, or token count—directly correlates with improved generative performance. The method achieves state-of-the-art FID scores on ImageNet 256×256 and 512×512 benchmarks, surpassing all prior diffusion and GAN-based models while maintaining superior compute efficiency.

7371637145bd660a0cf92c83e864e788dfe8be79.title: Universal Sharpness Dynamics in Neural Network Training: Fixed Point Analysis, Edge of Stability, and Route to Chaos
7371637145bd660a0cf92c83e864e788dfe8be79.research_question: What are the universal dynamical mechanisms underlying the evolution of sharpness (top eigenvalue of the loss Hessian) during neural network training, and how do initialization, parameterization, and learning rate influence the emergence of phenomena such as sharpness reduction, progressive sharpening, edge of stability, and chaotic dynamics in both simplified and real-world neural network models?
7371637145bd660a0cf92c83e864e788dfe8be79.hypothesis: The dynamics of sharpness during neural network training, including sharpness reduction, progressive sharpening, edge of stability, and chaotic fluctuations, can be fundamentally explained by the structure and stability of fixed points in a low-dimensional function space, and these mechanisms generalize from simplified models to realistic neural network architectures under appropriate choices of initialization, parameterization, and learning rate.
7371637145bd660a0cf92c83e864e788dfe8be79.proposed_method: A detailed theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted to analyze the sharpness dynamics in neural network training. The approach will begin with fixed-point and linear stability analysis of a simplified two-layer linear network (UV model) trained on a single example, deriving coupled non-linear dynamical equations for the residual and loss Hessian trace (sharpness). The analysis will identify and characterize all fixed points and their stability, mapping out the regimes of sharpness reduction, progressive sharpening, edge of stability (EoS), and the onset of chaotic dynamics via period-doubling bifurcations as learning rate increases. The theoretical predictions will then be extended and validated in realistic neural network architectures (fully-connected, CNNs, ResNets, Transformers) trained on both synthetic and real datasets, using different parameterizations (Standard, Neural Tangent, Maximal Update) and a range of initializations and learning rates. The methodology will include both analytical derivations and large-scale numerical simulations, with a focus on how initialization and parameterization control the entrance into different sharpness regimes and the emergence of EoS and chaos.
7371637145bd660a0cf92c83e864e788dfe8be79.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed on both the UV model and a variety of real-world neural network architectures, including fully-connected networks (FCNs), CNNs, ResNets, and Transformers. Datasets will include synthetic data (random i.i.d. inputs, teacher-student settings) and real datasets such as CIFAR-10 and Wikitext-2. Training will use mean squared error (MSE) loss and gradient descent, with systematic variation of initialization variance, parameterization (SP, NTP, µP), and learning rate (often scaled as η = c / λ_H0). Baselines will include different parameterizations and initialization regimes to isolate the impact on sharpness dynamics. Evaluation metrics will include the top eigenvalue of the loss Hessian (sharpness), weight norm, training and test accuracy, and the temporal structure of sharpness fluctuations (e.g., bifurcation diagrams, power spectra). Key experimental setups will probe the predicted phase diagrams for EoS, the correlation between sharpness and weight norm, and the presence of period-doubling routes to chaos in both synthetic and real data scenarios.
7371637145bd660a0cf92c83e864e788dfe8be79.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified fixed-point dynamical systems framework for understanding universal sharpness phenomena in neural network training, including the identification of precise conditions for edge of stability and the discovery of a period-doubling route to chaos as learning rate increases. The methodology generalizes the analysis to arbitrary parameterizations and initializations, providing new insights into the role of effective width and parameterization (including µP) in controlling sharpness regimes. The research further claims to bridge the gap between simplified toy models and real-world architectures, demonstrating that predictions from the UV model extend to practical deep learning scenarios and offering new phase diagrams and mechanistic explanations for sharpness dynamics observed in modern neural networks.

738f6c493ebc4ac4df2c953876ee5cda65033fe1.title: DiffAIL: Diffusion Adversarial Imitation Learning
738f6c493ebc4ac4df2c953876ee5cda65033fe1.research_question: How can the generalization and distribution-matching capabilities of adversarial imitation learning be improved to better identify expert-level behaviors, especially in settings with limited expert demonstrations and in both state-action and state-only scenarios?
738f6c493ebc4ac4df2c953876ee5cda65033fe1.hypothesis: Integrating a diffusion model into the adversarial imitation learning framework as part of the discriminator will enable more accurate modeling of the expert data distribution, thereby improving generalization, enhancing the identification of expert-level state-action pairs, and leading to superior policy learning outcomes compared to traditional binary classifier discriminators.
738f6c493ebc4ac4df2c953876ee5cda65033fe1.proposed_method: A novel adversarial imitation learning framework is proposed, where the discriminator is augmented with an unconditional diffusion model that models the joint distribution of state-action pairs (or state-next state pairs in state-only settings). The diffusion model is trained to minimize the mean squared error between predicted and true noise at various diffusion timesteps, and its loss is incorporated into the discriminator's objective via an exponential transformation. The adversarial objective then matches the expert and policy distributions by maximizing the discriminator output for expert data and minimizing it for policy-generated data. The surrogate reward for policy optimization is derived from the diffusion-based discriminator output, and any off-policy reinforcement learning algorithm (e.g., SAC) can be used for policy improvement. Training alternates between updating the diffusion-based discriminator and the policy, with uniform sampling over diffusion timesteps and noise vectors.
738f6c493ebc4ac4df2c953876ee5cda65033fe1.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on continuous control tasks from the MuJoCo benchmark, including Hopper, HalfCheetah, Walker2d, and Ant, using 1, 4, and 16 expert trajectories to assess performance under varying data regimes. The method is evaluated in both standard state-action and state-only settings. Baselines include Behavior Cloning, GAIL, ValueDICE, CFIL, and OPOLO, with all methods using the same number of environment steps and seeds for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics include average episodic return, best performance during training, and the ability of the discriminator to generalize to unseen expert trajectories. Additional analyses include ablation studies on the number of diffusion steps and correlation between surrogate and actual returns. Hyperparameters are tuned via grid search, and all models are trained using the Adam optimizer with gradient penalty for stability.
738f6c493ebc4ac4df2c953876ee5cda65033fe1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the use of unconditional diffusion models as discriminators within adversarial imitation learning, enabling more powerful distribution matching than traditional binary classifiers. This framework allows the discriminator to generalize better to unseen expert behaviors and provides a surrogate reward that is more linearly correlated with actual returns. The method achieves state-of-the-art performance on standard benchmarks, surpassing expert demonstrations in several tasks, and demonstrates robust performance across both state-action and state-only settings without requiring hyperparameter adjustments. The approach is general and can be integrated with any forward reinforcement learning algorithm.

739ceacfafb1c4eaa17509351b647c773270b3ae.title: An Empirical Study of Training Self-Supervised Vision Transformers
739ceacfafb1c4eaa17509351b647c773270b3ae.research_question: How can self-supervised learning frameworks be effectively adapted and optimized for training Vision Transformers (ViT), and what are the key factors influencing stability, accuracy, and scalability in this context?
739ceacfafb1c4eaa17509351b647c773270b3ae.hypothesis: Instability is a significant challenge in self-supervised training of Vision Transformers, and addressing it through architectural or optimization adjustments will yield more robust and accurate representations, potentially surpassing convolutional baselines.
739ceacfafb1c4eaa17509351b647c773270b3ae.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical investigation will be conducted on training Vision Transformers using leading self-supervised learning frameworks, such as MoCo v3, SimCLR, BYOL, and SwAV. The methodology will systematically analyze the impact of fundamental training components, including batch size, learning rate, optimizer selection, and architectural elements like patch projection and position embedding. A novel stabilization technique will be introduced by freezing the patch projection layer, effectively using a fixed random projection to mitigate gradient spikes and improve training stability. Extensive ablation studies will be performed to evaluate the influence of normalization layers, prediction heads, momentum encoders, and training duration. The approach will also explore the scalability of ViT models, including large-scale variants, to assess the relationship between model capacity and self-supervised learning performance.
739ceacfafb1c4eaa17509351b647c773270b3ae.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted primarily on the ImageNet-1k dataset, utilizing various ViT architectures (ViT-Small, ViT-Base, ViT-Large, ViT-Huge) and comparing them with large ResNet baselines. Training will use large batch sizes (up to 4096), AdamW or LAMB optimizers, and learning rate schedules with warmup and cosine decay. Evaluation will be performed via linear probing and end-to-end fine-tuning, measuring top-1 accuracy on ImageNet and transfer learning performance on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Oxford Flowers-102, and Oxford-IIIT-Pets. Baselines will include state-of-the-art self-supervised methods (iGPT, masked patch prediction, SimCLR v2, BYOL) and supervised pre-training. Ablations will cover position embedding, class token, normalization, prediction heads, and momentum coefficients. Training stability will be monitored using kNN accuracy curves and gradient statistics.
739ceacfafb1c4eaa17509351b647c773270b3ae.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a systematic empirical framework for understanding and improving self-supervised Vision Transformer training, highlighting the critical role of stability and uncovering hidden partial failures in standard training regimes. A novel stabilization technique—freezing the patch projection layer—is proposed and shown to consistently improve accuracy across multiple frameworks. The study benchmarks and scales self-supervised ViT models to unprecedented sizes, demonstrating that self-supervised pre-training can outperform supervised counterparts in certain transfer learning scenarios. The work provides detailed ablations and insights into architectural and optimization choices, offering practical guidelines and identifying open challenges for future research in self-supervised vision transformers.

73e6f6c724f4ab9c2c3d095f0a26e59c44769f0f.title: Grokking at the Edge of Linear Separability
73e6f6c724f4ab9c2c3d095f0a26e59c44769f0f.research_question: What are the fundamental mechanisms underlying the phenomenon of grokking—characterized by delayed generalization and non-monotonic test loss—in simple binary classification tasks, and how do the intrinsic properties of data and model parameters influence the emergence of grokking near the threshold of linear separability?
73e6f6c724f4ab9c2c3d095f0a26e59c44769f0f.hypothesis: Grokking arises generically in binary logistic classification tasks when the dataset is close to the threshold of linear separability from the origin, particularly when the ratio of data dimension to sample size approaches a critical value. Near this critical point, flat directions in the loss landscape cause training dynamics to linger near quasi-stable solutions, resulting in delayed generalization and non-monotonic test loss.
73e6f6c724f4ab9c2c3d095f0a26e59c44769f0f.proposed_method: A detailed theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted on a binary logistic regression task where the data consists of two well-separated Gaussians along a primary axis with strong additive noise in perpendicular directions. The study will focus on the regime where the ratio of data dimension to sample size (λ = d/N) approaches the critical value of 1/2, which marks the threshold of linear separability from the origin. Analytical tools from convex optimization and the theory of gradient descent dynamics will be employed to characterize the asymptotic behavior of the model parameters, specifically examining the divergence of the bias and weight norm. Theoretical predictions will be supplemented by constructing a simplified one-dimensional model that captures the essential aspects of the phenomenon, allowing for explicit solutions of the time evolution of model parameters. The investigation will also extend to cases with varying noise levels and label structures to assess the generality of the observed dynamics.
73e6f6c724f4ab9c2c3d095f0a26e59c44769f0f.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed using synthetic datasets generated from two Gaussians in high-dimensional space, with varying levels of noise in directions orthogonal to the separation axis. The primary variable of interest will be λ = d/N, systematically varied to probe the transition across the separability threshold. Gradient descent will be used for optimization, with additional experiments using adaptive optimizers such as Adam. Key metrics will include training and test loss, training and generalization accuracy, and the time evolution of model parameters (weight norm and bias). Baselines will include regimes well below and above the critical λ, as well as simplified models with only two data points to isolate the effects of separability. The grokking time—defined as the delay between the attainment of high training and generalization accuracy—will be measured and analyzed as a function of λ and noise. Additional experiments will explore the effects of relaxing the assumption of strong axis separation and introducing more complex label structures.
73e6f6c724f4ab9c2c3d095f0a26e59c44769f0f.novelty_claims: The proposed research establishes that grokking can occur in the simplest possible binary classification setting, without the need for complex architectures, regularization, or algorithmic data. It provides a rigorous analytical link between grokking and proximity to the linear separability threshold, identifying a critical point at λ = 1/2 that governs the transition between generalization and overfitting. The work introduces a tractable one-dimensional model that captures the essential dynamics and offers explicit solutions for the time evolution of model parameters. The findings suggest a deep connection between grokking and critical phenomena known from statistical physics, such as critical slowing down, and offer a unified framework that may generalize to broader classes of learning problems.

74013b7cfa0fc524803350fca51341004565eb22.title: Data Selection for Language Models via Importance Resampling
74013b7cfa0fc524803350fca51341004565eb22.research_question: How can pretraining data for language models be automatically selected from large, unlabeled corpora to closely match a desired target distribution, thereby improving downstream model performance without relying on manual curation or heuristic-based selection?
74013b7cfa0fc524803350fca51341004565eb22.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a scalable, automated data selection framework based on importance resampling in a reduced feature space can select pretraining data that more closely matches a target distribution, resulting in improved downstream language model performance compared to random selection, heuristic classification, or manual curation.
74013b7cfa0fc524803350fca51341004565eb22.proposed_method: A new framework, Data Selection with Importance Resampling (DSIR), will be developed to automate the selection of pretraining data for language models. The method first maps both raw and target datasets into a lower-dimensional feature space using hashed n-gram features, which efficiently capture unigram and bigram statistics in fixed-size buckets. Feature distributions for both the raw and target datasets are estimated as bag-of-ngrams generative models by counting hash bucket frequencies. Importance weights for each example in the raw dataset are then computed as the ratio of target to raw feature probabilities. Finally, a subset of the raw data is selected by resampling without replacement according to these importance weights, using efficient algorithms such as the Gumbel top-k trick. The framework is extensible to different feature spaces and importance estimators, allowing adaptation to various data selection goals.
74013b7cfa0fc524803350fca51341004565eb22.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using The Pile, a large-scale text dataset, as the raw data source. Target distributions will include both domain-specific datasets (e.g., scientific papers, biomedical texts, news, reviews) and general-domain datasets (Wikipedia and books). For domain-specific continued pretraining, data will be selected for eight downstream tasks across four domains, with models initialized from RoBERTa and evaluated via fine-tuning on the respective downstream datasets. For general-domain pretraining, masked language models will be trained from scratch on selected data and evaluated on the GLUE benchmark. Baselines will include random selection, heuristic classification (as used in GPT-3/PaLM), top-k variants, and manual curation (DAPT).
