Evaluation metrics will include macro/micro F1 scores for downstream tasks and average GLUE accuracy. All experiments will control for compute budget and use multiple random seeds for statistical robustness. Additionally, the KL reduction metric will be used to assess how closely the selected data matches the target distribution in the feature space, and its correlation with downstream performance will be analyzed.
74013b7cfa0fc524803350fca51341004565eb22.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a scalable and efficient framework for data selection based on importance resampling in a reduced feature space, enabling the selection of hundreds of millions of documents from large corpora in a matter of hours. The use of hashed n-gram features for feature extraction balances computational efficiency with the preservation of relevant distributional information. The framework is extensible to different feature spaces and importance estimators, and the introduction of the KL reduction metric provides a principled, training-free proxy for downstream performance. The method is claimed to match or surpass manual curation and heuristic-based baselines in both domain-specific and general-domain pretraining scenarios, offering a practical alternative to labor-intensive data curation.

740afdd1619d797145b056877865f941891e6a65.title: Decision-Dependent Risk Minimization in Geometrically Decaying Dynamic Environments
740afdd1619d797145b056877865f941891e6a65.research_question: How can optimal decision-dependent risk minimization be achieved in environments where the data distribution both depends on the decision-maker's actions and evolves dynamically over time according to a geometric decay process?
740afdd1619d797145b056877865f941891e6a65.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by allowing the environment to sufficiently mix under a fixed decision within each epoch, and then updating the decision using either first-order or zeroth-order information, it is possible to efficiently converge to the optimal solution in dynamic, decision-dependent environments, with iteration complexity matching that of classical stochastic gradient methods up to logarithmic factors.
740afdd1619d797145b056877865f941891e6a65.proposed_method: A novel epoch-based optimization framework is developed for decision-dependent risk minimization in geometrically decaying dynamic environments. The methodology operates in two settings: (1) a zeroth-order (bandit feedback) regime where only loss function evaluations are available, and (2) a first-order regime where gradient information is accessible. In both cases, the decision-maker holds a fixed decision for the duration of an epoch, allowing the environment's distribution to approach the fixed point corresponding to the current decision. At the end of each epoch, the decision is updated using either a one-point gradient estimate (for zeroth-order) or a stochastic gradient (for first-order), with projections onto the feasible set as needed. The epoch length is chosen to ensure sufficient mixing of the environment, and step sizes are set according to theoretical convergence guarantees under strong convexity and smoothness assumptions.
740afdd1619d797145b056877865f941891e6a65.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using a semi-synthetic setup based on real-world data from the SFpark dynamic pricing pilot study, which involves adjusting parking rates to achieve target occupancy levels. The algorithms are evaluated on multiple blocks and time periods, with the initial distribution sampled from historical data and the decision-dependent distribution modeled via a location-scale family with estimated price elasticity. Baseline comparisons include the actual SFpark pricing and occupancy outcomes, with evaluation metrics focusing on convergence to target occupancy, reduction in average parking rates, and improved distribution of occupancy across blocks. Additional experiments are performed using synthetic data and the 'Give Me Some Credit' Kaggle dataset, with epoch lengths and parameters chosen according to both theoretical and practical considerations.
740afdd1619d797145b056877865f941891e6a65.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first algorithms for decision-dependent risk minimization in dynamic environments with geometric decay, targeting performatively optimal points rather than merely stable equilibria. The framework provides provable convergence rates matching those of classical stochastic gradient methods up to logarithmic factors, even in the presence of feedback-induced distributional shift and environmental memory. Technical innovations include new bounds on the error induced by dynamic distributional mixing and the development of practical, epoch-based update rules for both first-order and zeroth-order information settings.

740c783ac07039cf30b6d8a8f95e775b3297c79e.title: Language Models Represent Space and Time
740c783ac07039cf30b6d8a8f95e775b3297c79e.research_question: Do large language models develop coherent, unified, and robust internal representations of spatial and temporal information, and to what extent are these representations linearly decodable and distributed across different entity types and scales?
740c783ac07039cf30b6d8a8f95e775b3297c79e.hypothesis: Large language models learn linear and unified representations of space and time that are robust to prompting variations and are distributed across different types of entities and scales.
740c783ac07039cf30b6d8a8f95e775b3297c79e.proposed_method: The proposed research will construct six datasets covering spatial (world, US, NYC places) and temporal (historical figures, artworks, news headlines) domains, each annotated with real-world coordinates or timestamps. For each dataset, entity names will be processed through a range of large language models (specifically the Llama-2 family and Pythia models), and the internal activations (residual stream) at each layer will be recorded for the last token of each entity. Linear ridge regression probes will be trained on these activations to predict spatial (latitude/longitude) or temporal (timestamp) targets, with regularization hyperparameters tuned via cross-validation. Additional experiments will compare linear probes to nonlinear MLP probes, assess robustness to prompt variations, and analyze generalization across held-out data blocks (e.g., countries, decades) and entity types. Dimensionality reduction via principal component analysis will be used to evaluate the dimensionality and structure of the learned representations, and neuron-level analysis will identify and causally test individual neurons sensitive to space or time.
740c783ac07039cf30b6d8a8f95e775b3297c79e.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize the Llama-2 models (7B, 13B, 70B parameters) and Pythia models (160M–6.9B parameters). Six datasets will be constructed: three spatial (global, US, NYC) and three temporal (historical figures, entertainment, news headlines), each containing tens of thousands of entities with associated coordinates or timestamps. Probes will be trained on model activations to predict these targets, with evaluation on held-out test sets using regression metrics such as R2, Spearman rank correlation, and a proximity error metric tailored for spatial data. Baselines will include random predictions and nonlinear MLP probes. Robustness will be assessed by varying prompts, holding out data blocks (e.g., countries, decades), and holding out entity types. Dimensionality reduction experiments will project activations onto principal components to assess the compactness of representations. Neuron-level analyses will involve identifying neurons aligned with probe directions and performing ablation/intervention experiments to test their causal role.
740c783ac07039cf30b6d8a8f95e775b3297c79e.novelty_claims: The proposed research claims novelty in systematically demonstrating that large language models encode linearly decodable, robust, and unified representations of continuous spatial and temporal features across multiple scales and entity types. The approach extends probing to continuous-valued features (space and time) rather than categorical or binary attributes, and introduces new robustness and generalization analyses, including block holdout and cross-entity generalization. The identification and causal testing of individual 'space neurons' and 'time neurons' within LLMs further advances mechanistic interpretability, providing evidence that such representations are not only decodable but also actively used by the model.

7426cc7b947f48cedb3bb3b5f8b5a0db17c9302d.title: Private GANs, Revisited
7426cc7b947f48cedb3bb3b5f8b5a0db17c9302d.research_question: How can the training of differentially private generative adversarial networks (GANs) be improved to achieve higher quality synthetic data generation, particularly for image synthesis tasks, while maintaining strong differential privacy guarantees?
7426cc7b947f48cedb3bb3b5f8b5a0db17c9302d.hypothesis: Modifying the training procedure of differentially private GANs—specifically by increasing the number of discriminator updates per generator update, scaling batch sizes, and adaptively adjusting discriminator update frequency—will restore balance between the generator and discriminator, mitigate the negative effects of noise addition to the discriminator, and significantly improve the utility and quality of generated data under differential privacy constraints.
7426cc7b947f48cedb3bb3b5f8b5a0db17c9302d.proposed_method: A novel training framework for differentially private GANs is proposed, wherein the discriminator is updated multiple times per generator update using differentially private stochastic gradient descent (DPSGD) with per-example gradient clipping and Gaussian noise addition. The generator is updated less frequently, and its gradients are not privatized due to post-processing closure properties of differential privacy. The method explores optimal ranges for the number of discriminator steps (n_D) per generator step, and introduces two additional enhancements: (1) scaling up batch sizes to improve gradient estimation and model utility, and (2) adaptively adjusting the discriminator update frequency based on the moving average of discriminator accuracy on fake samples. The adaptive schedule increases discriminator updates when accuracy drops, using a non-private proxy metric to avoid privacy budget expenditure. Hyperparameters such as noise level, clipping norm, and batch size are tuned to maximize generation quality within a fixed privacy budget.
7426cc7b947f48cedb3bb3b5f8b5a0db17c9302d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image synthesis benchmarks, including MNIST and FashionMNIST, using labeled data for conditional generation. The architecture is based on a modified DCGAN, with BatchNorm removed and label embeddings added. Training is privatized using Opacus for per-example gradient computation and privacy accounting, with both RDP and Gopi et al. (2021) accounting methods employed. Evaluation metrics include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for visual quality and downstream classification accuracy of CNNs trained on generated data. Baselines for comparison include prior DPGAN implementations, alternative GAN privatization schemes (e.g., PATE-GAN, GS-WGAN, DataLens), and non-GAN private generative models (e.g., DP-Sinkhorn, DP-MERF, DP diffusion models). Multiple seeds are run for statistical robustness, and hyperparameter sweeps are performed for batch size, noise level, and discriminator step frequency. Adaptive and large-batch variants are also evaluated.
7426cc7b947f48cedb3bb3b5f8b5a0db17c9302d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach demonstrates that careful adjustment of discriminator update frequency and batch size in private GAN training can dramatically improve generation quality, overturning previous assumptions about the limitations of DPGANs. Introducing an adaptive discriminator update schedule based on non-private proxy metrics is a novel contribution that further enhances performance. The method achieves state-of-the-art results among GAN-based privatization schemes for differentially private image synthesis, often outperforming alternative approaches. The work provides new empirical insights into the dynamics of private GAN training and offers practical guidance for integrating differential privacy into generative modeling pipelines.

744ecc70e9e6b31b43f519cf8c3affdcc2cda8ef.title: AgentTrek: Agent Trajectory Synthesis via Guiding Replay with Web Tutorials
744ecc70e9e6b31b43f519cf8c3affdcc2cda8ef.research_question: How can high-quality, scalable, and cost-effective agent trajectory data be synthesized for training advanced GUI agents, leveraging publicly available web tutorials to overcome the scarcity of annotated datasets?
744ecc70e9e6b31b43f519cf8c3affdcc2cda8ef.hypothesis: A fully automated pipeline that transforms web tutorials into structured agent trajectories, using a combination of language and vision models for guided replay and evaluation, can generate diverse, realistic, and comprehensive training data that enables GUI agents to achieve or surpass state-of-the-art performance on both text-based and vision-based web interaction benchmarks, at a fraction of the cost of human annotation.
744ecc70e9e6b31b43f519cf8c3affdcc2cda8ef.proposed_method: A three-stage pipeline is proposed for large-scale agent trajectory synthesis. First, web tutorials are automatically collected from large internet corpora (such as RedPajama) using a multi-step filtering process: rule-based pre-filtering, LLM-based labeling (with GPT-4O MINI), FastText classification, and semantic standardization via LLMs. These tutorials are then transformed into structured task specifications, including platform, prerequisites, step-by-step instructions, and expected outcomes. In the second stage, a visual-language model (VLM) agent executes the standardized tutorials in real web environments using BrowserGym, generating multimodal trajectory data (screenshots, accessibility trees, reasoning chains, and action logs). A specialized VLM-based evaluator (using GPT-4O) systematically assesses the quality and correctness of each trajectory, filtering out low-quality samples. Finally, the synthesized trajectories are used to fine-tune both text-based and vision-based agent models, enhancing their ability to perform complex, multi-step GUI tasks.
744ecc70e9e6b31b43f519cf8c3affdcc2cda8ef.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training both text-based and vision-based web agents using the synthesized AgentTrek dataset. For text-based agents, Qwen2.5 LLMs (7B and 32B) will be fine-tuned on 6,000 trajectories, with evaluation on the WebArena benchmark, which simulates realistic web environments and tasks. For vision-based agents, Qwen2-VL models will be fine-tuned on 10,000 trajectories and evaluated on ScreenSpot (for GUI visual grounding) and Multimodal-Mind2Web (for generalization across cross-task, cross-website, and cross-domain settings). Baselines will include open-source models (LLaMA3, Synatra-CodeLlama, AutoWebGLM), GPT-4o, and prior datasets (Mind2Web, ScreenAgent, GUIAct). Evaluation metrics will include task success rate, grounding accuracy, operation F1, step success rate, and element accuracy. Cost analysis and data scaling experiments will assess efficiency and generalization.
744ecc70e9e6b31b43f519cf8c3affdcc2cda8ef.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a fully automated, scalable pipeline for synthesizing high-quality, multimodal agent trajectories from web tutorials, eliminating the need for costly human annotation. The method combines advanced filtering, LLM-based standardization, guided replay in real web environments, and VLM-based trajectory evaluation to ensure data diversity, realism, and comprehensiveness. The resulting dataset covers a wide range of domains and task types, supports both text and vision modalities, and achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on established benchmarks. The pipeline demonstrates exceptional cost-efficiency (as low as $0.55 per trajectory) and scalability, setting a new standard for agent data generation and paving the way for more capable and autonomous digital assistants.

746a06cd30f62841f9b5ff6d276bee5bb7171fc0.title: Inducing Point Operator Transformer: A Flexible and Scalable Architecture for Solving PDEs
746a06cd30f62841f9b5ff6d276bee5bb7171fc0.research_question: How can a flexible and scalable neural architecture be developed to solve partial differential equations (PDEs) from observational data, accommodating arbitrary and irregular input/output discretizations, and scaling efficiently to large and complex real-world problems?
746a06cd30f62841f9b5ff6d276bee5bb7171fc0.hypothesis: A neural operator architecture based on attention mechanisms and inducing points can provide both the flexibility to handle arbitrary discretizations and the scalability required for large-scale PDE problems, outperforming or matching state-of-the-art methods in accuracy and efficiency.
746a06cd30f62841f9b5ff6d276bee5bb7171fc0.proposed_method: A novel attention-based operator learning framework, the Inducing Point Operator Transformer (IPOT), is proposed to address the challenges of flexibility and scalability in solving PDEs. The architecture employs an encoder-processor-decoder structure, where the encoder uses cross-attention to project arbitrary input discretizations onto a fixed, smaller set of learnable latent vectors (inducing points), significantly reducing the computational burden. The processor, composed of self-attention blocks, operates solely in this latent space, decoupling model depth from input/output size and enabling deep or long-term forecasting models. The decoder then uses cross-attention to map the latent representations to arbitrary output queries, supporting any output discretization. Positional encoding with Fourier features is incorporated to enhance spatial information, and the model supports both static and time-dependent PDEs via autoregressive latent space updates.
746a06cd30f62841f9b5ff6d276bee5bb7171fc0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse suite of PDE benchmarks, including Darcy flow, Navier-Stokes, airfoil, elasticity, and plasticity problems, covering both regular and irregular grids. Additionally, real-world weather forecasting tasks will be addressed using the ERA5 reanalysis dataset, which features complex, partially observed, and high-resolution data. Baseline comparisons will include DeepONet, Meshgraphnet, Fourier Neural Operator (FNO), Factorized-FNO, and Operator Transformer (OFormer). Evaluation metrics will primarily be relative L2 error on test sets, with efficiency assessed via runtime, memory usage, and parameter count. Ablation studies will investigate the impact of the number of inducing points and the model's generalization to unseen discretizations and masked inputs.
746a06cd30f62841f9b5ff6d276bee5bb7171fc0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a mesh-agnostic, attention-based neural operator architecture that decouples input/output discretizations from the latent processing space using inducing points, enabling linear scaling with input/output size and flexible handling of arbitrary data formats. This method overcomes the quadratic complexity of standard Transformers and the rigidity of prior operator learners, supporting deep architectures and long-term forecasting. The framework demonstrates superior or competitive performance across a wide range of PDE benchmarks and real-world scenarios, with strong generalization to unseen discretizations and partially observed data, without requiring problem-specific architectural modifications.

7470a1702c8c86e6f28d32cfa315381150102f5b.title: Segment Anything
7470a1702c8c86e6f28d32cfa315381150102f5b.research_question: How can a foundation model for image segmentation be developed that generalizes to a wide range of segmentation tasks and image distributions, enabling zero-shot and prompt-based segmentation on previously unseen data?
7470a1702c8c86e6f28d32cfa315381150102f5b.hypothesis: A promptable segmentation model, pre-trained on a large and diverse dataset of segmentation masks and designed to flexibly handle various prompt types, will enable strong zero-shot generalization to new segmentation tasks and image distributions, achieving performance competitive with or superior to fully supervised models.
7470a1702c8c86e6f28d32cfa315381150102f5b.proposed_method: A promptable segmentation framework will be developed, consisting of three main components: (1) a powerful image encoder (based on a Vision Transformer pre-trained with Masked Autoencoding) that produces high-resolution image embeddings, (2) a flexible prompt encoder that can process sparse (points, boxes, text) and dense (mask) prompts using positional encodings and off-the-shelf text encoders, and (3) a lightweight mask decoder that combines image and prompt embeddings to predict segmentation masks in real-time. The model will be designed to be ambiguity-aware by predicting multiple valid masks for ambiguous prompts. Training will be conducted on a large-scale, diverse dataset of over 1 billion segmentation masks (SA-1B), collected via a model-in-the-loop data engine that iteratively improves the model and dataset through assisted-manual, semi-automatic, and fully automatic annotation stages. The promptable segmentation task will serve as both the pre-training objective and the interface for downstream applications, enabling the model to generalize to new tasks via prompt engineering.
7470a1702c8c86e6f28d32cfa315381150102f5b.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate the model's zero-shot generalization capabilities across a diverse suite of 23 segmentation datasets, covering a wide range of domains and image distributions, including edge detection, object proposal generation, instance segmentation, and text-to-mask prediction. Baselines will include state-of-the-art interactive and fully supervised segmentation models such as RITM, ViTDet, and others. Evaluation metrics will include mean Intersection-over-Union (mIoU), average recall (AR), mask quality ratings from human annotators, and fairness analyses across demographic attributes. The model will be tested with various prompt types (points, boxes, text) and compared under both automatic and human evaluation protocols. The large-scale SA-1B dataset will be used for training, and all experiments will be conducted under zero-shot transfer settings, where the model is not fine-tuned on target datasets.
7470a1702c8c86e6f28d32cfa315381150102f5b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new promptable segmentation task and a model architecture that supports flexible, real-time prompting and ambiguity-aware mask prediction. The methodology includes the creation of the largest segmentation dataset to date (SA-1B), with over 1 billion high-quality masks on 11 million licensed and privacy-respecting images, collected through a novel data engine that combines model-in-the-loop annotation and fully automatic mask generation. The framework enables strong zero-shot transfer to a wide variety of segmentation tasks and image distributions, often achieving performance competitive with or superior to fully supervised models, and supports extensible, prompt-based system composition for downstream applications.

7476e1c4fd6fa8e6d23bd7e1b45f9e799d04b284.title: V2X-ViT: Vehicle-to-Everything Cooperative Perception with Vision Transformer
7476e1c4fd6fa8e6d23bd7e1b45f9e799d04b284.research_question: How can cooperative perception in Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) systems be improved to robustly fuse heterogeneous sensory data from vehicles and infrastructure, especially under real-world challenges such as localization errors, asynchronous communication, and sensor heterogeneity?
7476e1c4fd6fa8e6d23bd7e1b45f9e799d04b284.hypothesis: A unified vision Transformer framework that incorporates heterogeneous multi-agent self-attention and multi-scale window attention can effectively fuse information from both vehicles and infrastructure, leading to improved and more robust cooperative perception performance in V2X systems, even under noisy and asynchronous conditions.
7476e1c4fd6fa8e6d23bd7e1b45f9e799d04b284.proposed_method: A novel end-to-end cooperative perception framework will be developed based on a vision Transformer architecture, termed V2X-ViT, designed to handle the heterogeneity and real-world challenges of V2X systems. The method will begin with metadata sharing among agents (vehicles and infrastructure), followed by feature extraction using an efficient PointPillar backbone for LiDAR data. Features will be compressed and transmitted to reduce bandwidth, and spatial-temporal misalignments will be corrected using a spatial-temporal correction module. The core of the approach is a Transformer comprising alternating layers of a heterogeneous multi-agent self-attention module (HMSA), which explicitly models agent and edge types for adaptive inter-agent fusion, and a multi-scale window attention module (MSwin), which captures both local and global spatial relationships at multiple scales to enhance robustness against localization errors. Delay-aware positional encoding will be integrated to further address temporal misalignments. The fused features will then be used for 3D object detection via a detection head with regression and classification branches.
7476e1c4fd6fa8e6d23bd7e1b45f9e799d04b284.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a newly created large-scale simulation dataset, V2XSet, generated with CARLA and OpenCDA, which includes realistic V2X challenges such as localization noise and time delays. The evaluation will focus on LiDAR-based 3D object detection, with Average Precision (AP) at IoU thresholds of 0.5 and 0.7 as the primary metrics. Two experimental settings will be used: a Perfect Setting (synchronized, noise-free) and a Noisy Setting (with pose errors and time delays drawn from realistic distributions). The proposed method will be compared against several baselines, including No Fusion, Late Fusion, Early Fusion, and state-of-the-art intermediate fusion methods such as OPV2V, F-Cooper, V2VNet, and DiscoNet, all using the same PointPillar backbone. The experimental setup will include a communication range of 70 meters, fixed voxel resolution, and consistent compression rates. Training will use the Adam optimizer and staged learning rates, with all models trained on Tesla V100 GPUs.
7476e1c4fd6fa8e6d23bd7e1b45f9e799d04b284.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first unified vision Transformer architecture specifically tailored for V2X cooperative perception, capable of robustly handling heterogeneous agents, asynchronous information, and pose errors. Key innovations include the heterogeneous multi-agent self-attention module for adaptive fusion across agent types, the multi-scale window attention module for enhanced spatial robustness, and a delay-aware positional encoding for temporal alignment. Additionally, a new large-scale, noise-aware V2XSet dataset will be constructed to facilitate realistic evaluation. The approach is expected to achieve state-of-the-art performance and superior robustness compared to existing fusion strategies.

748698bd4387afd08594e0dc8150c2afa210d9ae.title: RRHF: Rank Responses to Align Language Models with Human Feedback without tears
748698bd4387afd08594e0dc8150c2afa210d9ae.research_question: How can large language models be efficiently aligned with human preferences using a training paradigm that is simpler and more resource-efficient than existing reinforcement learning methods?
748698bd4387afd08594e0dc8150c2afa210d9ae.hypothesis: A ranking-based training paradigm that aligns model response probabilities with human preferences using ranking loss can achieve comparable or superior alignment performance to PPO-based RLHF, while reducing complexity, model count, and hyperparameter tuning requirements.
748698bd4387afd08594e0dc8150c2afa210d9ae.proposed_method: A novel training paradigm, RRHF (Rank Responses to align Human Feedback), is proposed to align large language models with human preferences. The method involves sampling multiple responses to each query from diverse sources, including the model itself, other large language models, and human experts. Each response is scored using the log-probability under the current model, and these scores are aligned with human preference rankings via a ranking loss that encourages the model to assign higher probabilities to more preferred responses. Additionally, a supervised fine-tuning loss is applied to the response with the highest reward. The total loss is the unweighted sum of the ranking loss and the supervised loss. This approach eliminates the need for value models, reference models, and complex KL-divergence penalties required by PPO, enabling efficient training with only one or two models.
748698bd4387afd08594e0dc8150c2afa210d9ae.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on Anthropic’s Helpful and Harmless (HH) dataset, which provides queries paired with human-preferred and rejected responses. The primary models used will be LLaMA and Alpaca (7B parameter size), with initial fine-tuning on the dataset's chosen responses. Various response sampling policies will be evaluated, including beam search, diverse beam search, top-p sampling, and online/iterative sampling. Baselines will include supervised fine-tuning, PPO-based RLHF, and best-of-n sampling. Evaluation metrics will comprise perplexity, average reward score (using a proxy reward model), and human preference judgments via pairwise comparison. Training will be performed on 8x80GB Nvidia A100 GPUs, with hyperparameters such as learning rate, batch size, and token truncation specified for reproducibility.
748698bd4387afd08594e0dc8150c2afa210d9ae.novelty_claims: The proposed RRHF paradigm introduces a ranking-based approach to align language models with human preferences, requiring only one or two models during tuning and significantly reducing coding complexity and hyperparameter tuning compared to PPO. RRHF leverages responses from multiple sources, supports best-of-n learning, and can serve as both a language model and a reward model. The method is robust to sampling quality and achieves comparable or superior alignment performance to PPO while being more resource-efficient and easier to scale to larger models. Additionally, RRHF is compatible with standard fine-tuning techniques and can be readily adopted in limited-resource scenarios.

74a923110fe056c780590dea192c8a75d7d16c65.title: Cross-prediction-powered inference
74a923110fe056c780590dea192c8a75d7d16c65.research_question: How can valid and powerful statistical inference be achieved in semi-supervised settings where high-quality labels are scarce but abundant features are available, particularly when leveraging machine learning predictions to supplement limited labeled data?
74a923110fe056c780590dea192c8a75d7d16c65.hypothesis: Cross-prediction, a method that imputes missing labels via black-box machine learning and applies a debiasing correction, enables valid inference with improved statistical power and stability compared to classical inference or prediction-powered inference approaches that require data splitting or pre-trained models.
74a923110fe056c780590dea192c8a75d7d16c65.proposed_method: The proposed methodology, termed cross-prediction, partitions the small labeled dataset into K folds and, for each fold, trains a black-box predictive model (e.g., neural networks, random forests, gradient-boosted trees) on the remaining K-1 folds. Each trained model is then used to impute missing labels for the large unlabeled dataset as well as to generate predictions on the held-out labeled fold. The cross-prediction estimator combines the mean (or M-estimation loss) of the imputed predictions on the unlabeled data with a debiasing term computed from the difference between predicted and true labels on the labeled data. This estimator is shown to be unbiased and, under a stability assumption on the learning algorithm, satisfies a central limit theorem, enabling valid confidence intervals and hypothesis tests. The approach generalizes to any M-estimation problem by replacing the mean with the appropriate loss function and its gradient, and can be applied to complex, high-dimensional data modalities.
74a923110fe056c780590dea192c8a75d7d16c65.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on semi-supervised inference tasks, such as estimating the fraction of deforested areas in the Amazon using satellite imagery, where a small set of gold-standard labels is available and a large set of unlabeled features exists. The method will be evaluated against baselines including classical inference (using only labeled data) and prediction-powered inference (using data splitting to train/fine-tune a model). Evaluation metrics will include coverage probability and width of confidence intervals, as well as stability (variability) of the intervals across random splits. Datasets will include real-world scientific and socioeconomic data where feature collection is cheap but label acquisition is expensive, and experiments will be repeated over multiple random splits to assess robustness.
74a923110fe056c780590dea192c8a75d7d16c65.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a general, theoretically-grounded framework for semi-supervised inference that leverages black-box machine learning for label imputation and incorporates a debiasing step to ensure validity. Unlike prior approaches, cross-prediction does not require a pre-trained model or data splitting, allowing every labeled data point to be used for both model training and inference, thereby increasing statistical power. The method is broadly applicable to general M-estimation problems and complex data modalities, and achieves more stable and efficient inference than existing baselines. Theoretical contributions include central limit theorems for the estimator under mild stability conditions, and empirical results are expected to demonstrate improved coverage, narrower confidence intervals, and lower variability.

74d3f033e168891ee5cefb9e8df4787652eb1104.title: Improved Online Conformal Prediction via Strongly Adaptive Online Learning
74d3f033e168891ee5cefb9e8df4787652eb1104.research_question: How can uncertainty quantification via prediction sets be improved in online learning environments where the data distribution may change arbitrarily over time, particularly to ensure valid coverage and efficient prediction sets on all sub-intervals of the time horizon?
74d3f033e168891ee5cefb9e8df4787652eb1104.hypothesis: Utilizing strongly adaptive regret minimization within online conformal prediction frameworks will enable the construction of prediction sets that maintain approximately valid coverage and achieve near-optimal regret not only globally but also on all sub-intervals, outperforming existing methods under distribution shift.
74d3f033e168891ee5cefb9e8df4787652eb1104.proposed_method: A novel meta-algorithm, Strongly Adaptive Online Conformal Prediction (SAOCP), will be developed to manage multiple experts, each responsible for its own active interval within the data stream. Each expert will employ a Scale-Free Online Gradient Descent (SF-OGD) algorithm, an anytime variant of OGD, to adaptively update the prediction set radius based on observed quantile losses. At every time step, the algorithm will aggregate predictions from all currently active experts using a coin-betting weighting scheme, ensuring that the overall prediction set adapts rapidly to local changes in the data distribution. The method will be theoretically analyzed to establish strongly adaptive regret bounds and coverage guarantees, both globally and on all sub-intervals, and will also be instantiated in a randomized variant for further robustness.
74d3f033e168891ee5cefb9e8df4787652eb1104.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on real-world tasks including time series forecasting and image classification under distribution shift. For time series, datasets such as M4 (hourly, daily, weekly) and NN5 will be used, with base predictors including LGBM, ARIMA, and Prophet. For image classification, experiments will utilize TinyImageNet-C and ImageNet-C, simulating both sudden and gradual distribution shifts. The proposed method will be compared against baselines such as Split Conformal Prediction (SCP), Non-Exchangeable SCP (NExCP), and the Fully Adaptive Conformal Inference (FACI) algorithm, as well as variants that predict radii directly. Evaluation metrics will include global and local coverage, median prediction set width, worst-case local coverage error, and strongly adaptive regret, with experiments designed to assess performance under both stationary and non-stationary conditions.
74d3f033e168891ee5cefb9e8df4787652eb1104.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new meta-algorithm for online conformal prediction that leverages strongly adaptive regret minimization, enabling near-optimal regret and valid coverage guarantees on all intervals simultaneously. Unlike previous methods, the algorithm localizes expert activity to specific intervals, allowing rapid adaptation to distribution shifts. Theoretical contributions include new regret and coverage bounds for both the meta-algorithm and the SF-OGD expert. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior coverage and smaller prediction sets compared to existing methods, particularly under non-exchangeable and distribution-shifted data.

74fcfb150e319d83479314e44dbc89eb31db9e06.title: Revisiting Prefix-tuning: Statistical Benefits of Reparameterization among Prompts
74fcfb150e319d83479314e44dbc89eb31db9e06.research_question: What are the theoretical principles underlying the effectiveness of reparameterization strategies in prompt-based fine-tuning methods, such as prefix-tuning and prompt-tuning, and how does shared structure among prompt parameters impact sample efficiency and performance across diverse tasks?
74fcfb150e319d83479314e44dbc89eb31db9e06.hypothesis: Reparameterization strategies in prompt-based fine-tuning methods induce a shared structure between key and value vectors, which significantly enhances sample efficiency in parameter estimation and leads to improved performance compared to non-shared alternatives.
74fcfb150e319d83479314e44dbc89eb31db9e06.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted into the role of reparameterization in prompt-based fine-tuning, focusing on prefix-tuning and prompt-tuning within large pre-trained models. The methodology will formalize the shared structure induced by reparameterization, modeling it as parameter sharing between prefix key and value vectors, and analyze its impact using the mixture of experts (MoE) framework. Theoretical convergence rates for prompt parameter estimation will be derived for both shared and non-shared structures, considering both linear and neural network-based reparameterizations. The approach will further extend the analysis to prompt-tuning, examining analogous shared structures and their effects on convergence and efficiency.
74fcfb150e319d83479314e44dbc89eb31db9e06.experiment_details: Empirical evaluations will be performed on both visual and language tasks. For visual tasks, the FGVC and VTAB-1K benchmarks will be used, including datasets such as CUB-200-2011, NABirds, Oxford Flowers, Stanford Dogs, and Stanford Cars, with Vision Transformer (ViT-B/16) pre-trained on ImageNet-21K as the backbone. For language tasks, table-to-text generation will be evaluated on E2E and WebNLG datasets using GPT2, and summarization will be assessed on XSUM using BART. Baselines will include full fine-tuning, partial fine-tuning, adapter-based methods, VPT, and several prefix-tuning variants: Deep-share (with reparameterization), No-share (without reparameterization), and Simple-share (identity reparameterization). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy for vision tasks and BLEU, NIST, METEOR, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, and TER for language tasks. Experiments will compare the sample efficiency and performance of shared versus non-shared prompt structures, with results averaged over multiple independent runs.
74fcfb150e319d83479314e44dbc89eb31db9e06.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a rigorous theoretical framework connecting reparameterization in prompt-based fine-tuning to shared structures in the mixture of experts paradigm, providing the first formal convergence analysis demonstrating enhanced sample efficiency due to parameter sharing. It establishes that reparameterization is not merely an engineering trick but is grounded in deep theoretical principles, and empirically validates these findings across both vision and language domains. The investigation also uncovers analogous benefits in prompt-tuning, offering new perspectives on its effectiveness and suggesting broader applicability to other parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques.

750188fd2814062e033092d309810fd9eae91f3d.title: Regularizing Towards Soft Equivariance Under Mixed Symmetries
750188fd2814062e033092d309810fd9eae91f3d.research_question: How can deep learning models be effectively regularized to exploit multiple, potentially approximate, symmetry types present in datasets, particularly when the degree of symmetry varies across these types?
750188fd2814062e033092d309810fd9eae91f3d.hypothesis: Regularizing unconstrained neural networks towards soft equivariance using projection-based equivariance regularizers, with automatically tuned regularization strengths for each symmetry type, will enable the discovery of varying degrees of approximate symmetries in data and improve predictive performance over strictly equivariant or invariant models.
750188fd2814062e033092d309810fd9eae91f3d.proposed_method: A regularizer-based approach is developed for neural networks to handle datasets exhibiting mixed and approximate symmetries. For each candidate symmetry group, a projection-based equivariance regularizer is defined, measuring the distance of network parameters (weights and biases) from the subspace of equivariant or invariant transformations. These regularizers are incorporated into the training objective, one per symmetry type, and their regularization coefficients are automatically tuned during training based on the observed magnitudes of the regularizers, reflecting the degree of approximation for each symmetry. The method allows unconstrained architectures (e.g., standard MLPs) to be softly regularized towards equivariance without imposing hard architectural constraints, and can flexibly combine multiple symmetry types by summing the corresponding regularizers in the loss function.
750188fd2814062e033092d309810fd9eae91f3d.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both synthetic function approximation tasks and a real-world motion forecasting task. Synthetic tasks include the moment of inertia and cosine similarity functions, each designed to exhibit different types and degrees of approximate symmetries (e.g., O(3), Ox(2), Oy(2), Oz(2), SO(3), S(3)). Real-world experiments use the Waymo Open Motion Dataset for vehicle trajectory prediction, with various normalization schemes to induce different symmetry properties. Baselines include strictly equivariant models (EMLP), soft equivariant models (RPP), and naively combined mixed-symmetry models (MEMLP). Evaluation metrics include test mean squared error (MSE) for synthetic tasks and average distance error (ADE) for motion forecasting. The experimental setup ensures comparable model sizes across methods and includes automatic tuning of regularization coefficients to discover symmetry approximation levels without explicit supervision.
750188fd2814062e033092d309810fd9eae91f3d.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to enable automatic discovery of varying degrees of approximate equivariance across multiple symmetry types in mixed-symmetry settings, without imposing architectural constraints. The projection-based equivariance regularizer framework allows for flexible, data-driven adjustment of symmetry strengths during training, outperforming prior approaches in both accuracy and the ability to identify soft symmetries. The approach is demonstrated to be robust across synthetic and real-world tasks, and provides a general mechanism for regularizing towards soft equivariance under mixed symmetries.

7509850841bc560907b67d89158a7cc58882c368.title: Latent Space Chain-of-Embedding Enables Output-free LLM Self-Evaluation
7509850841bc560907b67d89158a7cc58882c368.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) estimate the correctness of their own responses in a label-free, output-free, and real-time manner, leveraging only their internal hidden states during inference?
7509850841bc560907b67d89158a7cc58882c368.hypothesis: Discrepancies in the latent space trajectories, specifically the sequence of progressive hidden states (Chain-of-Embedding, CoE), reflect whether an LLM's response is correct or incorrect. These differences can be quantified and used to enable LLMs to self-evaluate their outputs without requiring external labels, additional training, or output analysis.
7509850841bc560907b67d89158a7cc58882c368.proposed_method: A novel methodology is proposed that constructs a Chain-of-Embedding (CoE) by collecting all progressive hidden states from each layer of an LLM during inference, treating this sequence as the model's latent thinking path. The method defines geometric features—magnitude (L2-norm of state differences) and angle (cosine similarity transformed via arccosine)—between adjacent hidden states, normalized relative to the overall input-output state change. Two composite metrics are developed: CoE-R, a real-space combination using a linear sum of normalized magnitude and inverse angle changes; and CoE-C, a complex-space combination treating each state transition as a complex number and averaging in the complex plane for robustness. These metrics are used as decision scores to classify LLM responses as correct or incorrect, without reference to ground-truth labels or output probabilities. The approach is computationally efficient, requiring only simple vector operations and no additional model training.
7509850841bc560907b67d89158a7cc58882c368.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across four key LLM capability domains—Mathematics, Reasoning, Knowledge, and Understanding—using six datasets: GSM8K, MATH, CommonsenseQA, TheoremQA, MMLU, and Belebele. Multiple instruction-tuned LLMs of varying sizes (including Llama2-7B, Llama3-8B, Qwen1.5-7B, Qwen2-7B, Mistral-7B, Llama3-70B, and Qwen2-72B) will be evaluated in zero-shot settings. The proposed CoE metrics will be compared against ten strong label-free baselines, including both output-based and internal-state-based uncertainty estimation methods (e.g., Verbal Confidence, Prompt-Sampling-Aggregation, Maximum Softmax Probability, Perplexity, Entropy, Temperature Scaling, Energy, Monte-Carlo Dropout, Length-normalized Entropy, and Eigenscore). Evaluation metrics will include AUROC, FPR95, and AUPR, with exact match used for ground-truth correctness. Additional analyses will assess robustness to data imbalance, model scaling, task difficulty, and multilingual scenarios, as well as computational efficiency.
7509850841bc560907b67d89158a7cc58882c368.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first fully label-free, output-free LLM self-evaluation method that leverages only the latent trajectory of hidden states (CoE) during inference, requiring no supervised training or output probability analysis. The approach provides interpretable geometric metrics (magnitude and angle) to quantify latent thinking paths, and robust composite scoring functions (CoE-R and CoE-C) for real-time self-evaluation. The method demonstrates superior domain and scaling robustness, high computational efficiency, and strong performance across diverse tasks and languages, outperforming existing label-free and hidden-state-based baselines.

750fd7b23d1009c360cdbce19dbf1cf6b3461f59.title: RoboTwin: Dual-Arm Robot Benchmark with Generative Digital Twins (early version)
750fd7b23d1009c360cdbce19dbf1cf6b3461f59.research_question: How can the availability and quality of training data for dual-arm robotic tool use and human-robot interaction be improved to accelerate the development and evaluation of advanced robotic systems in real-world and simulated environments?
750fd7b23d1009c360cdbce19dbf1cf6b3461f59.hypothesis: Integrating real-world teleoperated data with high-fidelity synthetic data generated by AI-driven digital twins and expert-level training data synthesized by large language models will significantly enhance the diversity, quality, and scalability of datasets for dual-arm robotic learning, leading to improved performance and generalization in complex manipulation tasks.
750fd7b23d1009c360cdbce19dbf1cf6b3461f59.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark will be developed that combines real-world teleoperated data from a dual-arm robot platform with synthetic data generated via a generative digital twin system. The digital twin system will utilize Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC) to reconstruct detailed 3D models of objects and scenes from single 2D RGB images, including geometry, textures, and functional coordinate axes for grasp pose computation. Large language models (LLMs) such as GPT-4V will be leveraged to automatically generate expert-level training data, including task-specific pose sequences and trajectory planning scripts, based on both real and simulated scenarios. The methodology will provide a robust real-to-simulation pipeline, enabling the automatic creation of diverse, high-quality datasets for a wide range of dual-arm manipulation and tool-use tasks.
750fd7b23d1009c360cdbce19dbf1cf6b3461f59.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the proposed benchmark, focusing on a suite of 17 tasks that emphasize tool usage, human-robot interaction, and dual-arm coordination. Real-world data will be collected using the COBOT Magic platform, equipped with four AgileX Arms and four Intel Realsense D-435 RGBD cameras, capturing synchronized RGB-D images and robot joint/effector poses. Synthetic data will be generated for corresponding scenarios using the digital twin pipeline. The 3D Diffusion Policy (DP3) will be used as a baseline policy learning algorithm, and its performance will be evaluated across six representative tasks with varying numbers of expert demonstrations (10, 20, 50). Success rates will be measured as the primary evaluation metric, and the impact of dataset scale and automatic expert data generation on task performance will be systematically analyzed.
750fd7b23d1009c360cdbce19dbf1cf6b3461f59.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel dual-arm robotic benchmark that uniquely integrates real-world teleoperated data with high-fidelity synthetic data generated from single 2D images using AI-based digital twin technology. It pioneers the use of large language models for automated expert-level data and code generation, enabling scalable and scenario-specific training data creation. The real-to-simulation pipeline is designed to be cost-effective, requiring minimal manual intervention, and supports robust benchmarking and offline training for advanced robotic manipulation tasks. This approach addresses the critical shortage of specialized training data in robotics and provides a scalable, extensible framework for accelerating research and development in dual-arm robotic systems.

7513501b227f7a4e80cb4b69f8b31d22aed7d8e3.title: Hankel Singular Value Regularization for Highly Compressible State Space Models
7513501b227f7a4e80cb4b69f8b31d22aed7d8e3.research_question: How can state space model (SSM) layers in deep neural networks be made highly compressible for long-range sequence modeling tasks, while maintaining high accuracy and computational efficiency?
7513501b227f7a4e80cb4b69f8b31d22aed7d8e3.hypothesis: Regularizing the sum of Hankel singular values of SSM layers during training will induce a rapid decay in these singular values, resulting in models that are highly compressible via standard system-theoretic reduction techniques, without significant loss in accuracy.
7513501b227f7a4e80cb4b69f8b31d22aed7d8e3.proposed_method: A novel training procedure will be developed that incorporates a differentiable regularizer based on the sum of Hankel singular values (the Hankel nuclear norm) into the loss function of deep neural networks with SSM layers. To enable scalable computation of this regularizer, SSMs will be parametrized using block-diagonal scaled rotation matrices, allowing efficient solution of Lyapunov equations and computation of the required Gramians in O(n^2) time per layer, where n is the state dimension. An associative scan operation will be constructed for efficient parallel time integration of the SSMs. After training, model compression will be performed via balanced truncation, using the computed Gramians to identify and truncate low-energy states, with the compression order in each layer chosen to preserve a desired fraction of the system's energy.
7513501b227f7a4e80cb4b69f8b31d22aed7d8e3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five sequence classification benchmarks, including sCIFAR10 (grayscale), sMNIST, IMDB, PATH, and PATH-X, with several of these drawn from the Long Range Arena (LRA) benchmark suite. Each dataset will be processed into long sequences, and models will be trained with SSM layers using the proposed Hankel singular value regularization. Baselines will include unregularized SSMs and state-of-the-art pruning and compression methods such as LAST and global/uniform pruning. Evaluation metrics will focus on test accuracy across varying compression (truncation) ratios, with detailed analysis of the decay of Hankel singular values and the compressibility of the resulting models. The experimental setup will match standard SSM layer architectures and hyperparameters as in prior work, ensuring fair comparison.
7513501b227f7a4e80cb4b69f8b31d22aed7d8e3.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a differentiable Hankel nuclear norm regularizer for SSM layers in deep neural networks, enabling direct control of compressibility during training. A scalable algorithm is developed for efficient computation of Hankel singular values by exploiting a block-diagonal rotation matrix parametrization, reducing computational complexity from O(n^3) to O(n^2). The method supports layer-wise adaptive compression, allowing different reduced orders per layer based on energy retention criteria. Experiments are expected to demonstrate up to 10× higher compressibility compared to standard SSM layers and prior pruning methods, while maintaining high accuracy on long-range sequence tasks.

753989375fed1c872d6f367de3320f37490a01cc.title: Bayes Adaptive Monte Carlo Tree Search for Offline Model-based Reinforcement Learning
753989375fed1c872d6f367de3320f37490a01cc.research_question: How can model uncertainty in offline model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) be more effectively addressed, particularly in continuous state and action spaces, to improve policy performance and generalization beyond the support of static offline datasets?
753989375fed1c872d6f367de3320f37490a01cc.hypothesis: Modeling offline MBRL as a Bayes Adaptive Markov Decision Process (BAMDP) and solving it with a novel Bayes Adaptive Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) algorithm, integrated into a policy iteration framework, will yield more robust and higher-performing policies compared to existing offline RL methods, especially in the presence of model uncertainty and limited data coverage.
753989375fed1c872d6f367de3320f37490a01cc.proposed_method: The proposed method frames offline MBRL as a BAMDP, explicitly representing uncertainty over an ensemble of learned world models. A novel planning algorithm, Continuous BAMCP, is developed to perform Bayes Adaptive Monte Carlo Tree Search in continuous state and action spaces with stochastic transitions, leveraging double progressive widening to manage the combinatorial explosion of possible actions and states. The planning process incorporates Bayesian belief updates over the model ensemble after each transition, and penalizes rewards based on epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty to mitigate overestimation and overfitting to inaccurate models. This search-based planning is then integrated into a policy iteration framework, where the results of tree search are distilled into policy and value networks via supervised learning or policy gradient methods, enabling efficient real-time policy execution. The approach is designed to allow adaptive policy improvement by repeatedly applying planning and learning steps, with the policy network trained to mimic the Bayes-optimal action distributions produced by search.
753989375fed1c872d6f367de3320f37490a01cc.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on twelve D4RL MuJoCo continuous control tasks, each with multiple dataset qualities (random, medium, medium-replay, medium-expert), as well as three challenging target tracking tasks in a stochastic, high-dimensional tokamak control simulator for nuclear fusion. The proposed algorithms are compared against state-of-the-art offline model-based RL baselines (e.g., Optimized, COMBO, MOReL, MOPO), model-free offline RL methods (e.g., CQL), and deep search-based methods (e.g., MuZero variants). Evaluation metrics include normalized episodic returns and tracking errors, with results averaged over multiple random seeds and training epochs. The experimental setup uses identical policy architectures and world model ensembles across methods for fair comparison, and ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of Bayesian adaptation, deep search, reward penalties, and policy update mechanisms.
753989375fed1c872d6f367de3320f37490a01cc.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first integration of BAMDPs and Bayes Adaptive MCTS into offline model-based RL for continuous control, addressing model uncertainty in a principled Bayesian manner. The method develops a novel planning algorithm capable of handling continuous, stochastic environments via double progressive widening and Bayesian belief updates. It establishes a new search-based policy iteration framework that distills Bayes-optimal planning results into neural policy and value functions for real-time execution. The approach demonstrates substantial empirical improvements over state-of-the-art offline RL methods on both standard benchmarks and real-world control problems, and provides a flexible foundation for future advances in uncertainty quantification and robust policy learning in offline RL.

753d21e35f91097211147e8bf9efadea3f291dfb.title: Diffusion Bridge Mixture Transports, Schrödinger Bridge Problems and Generative Modeling
753d21e35f91097211147e8bf9efadea3f291dfb.research_question: How can the dynamic Schrödinger bridge problem be solved more effectively for high-dimensional generative modeling and optimal transport, and can a new iterative algorithm provide improved sample quality and computational efficiency compared to existing approaches?
753d21e35f91097211147e8bf9efadea3f291dfb.hypothesis: A novel iterative algorithm based on diffusion bridge mixtures will achieve valid transports between target probability measures at each iteration, avoid simulation-inference mismatch, and provide accelerated training and superior sample quality in generative modeling tasks compared to existing iterative proportional fitting (IPF) and score-based diffusion methods.
753d21e35f91097211147e8bf9efadea3f291dfb.proposed_method: The proposed method develops an iterative Diffusion Bridge Mixture (IDBM) procedure to solve the dynamic Schrödinger bridge problem. At each iteration, a stochastic process is constructed as a mixture of diffusion bridges, with the mixing occurring over the bridges’ endpoints to form a coupling between the initial and terminal distributions. The marginal distributions of this process are then matched with those of a diffusion process, which is inferred from the generated samples. The coupling is updated using the initial-terminal distributions of the inferred diffusion, and the process is repeated. This approach ensures that at every iteration a valid transport is realized, and crucially, the simulation and inference steps are aligned, eliminating the mismatch present in previous methods. For generative modeling, the first iteration of the IDBM procedure is proposed as an approximation-free transport from a simple distribution to the data distribution, allowing for greater flexibility in the choice of generative process dynamics and requiring only minimal changes to the training loss.
753d21e35f91097211147e8bf9efadea3f291dfb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard generative modeling benchmarks, particularly in visual domains, using datasets such as image collections with known empirical distributions. The IDBM procedure will be compared against baselines including the classical IPF procedure and state-of-the-art score-based generative models (e.g., Song et al., 2021). Evaluation metrics will include sample quality (e.g., FID scores), training speed, and robustness across varying discretization intervals. The experimental setup will involve implementing the IDBM with minimal modifications to existing generative modeling pipelines, focusing on the training loss, and systematically varying the reference diffusion process parameters to assess flexibility and performance.
753d21e35f91097211147e8bf9efadea3f291dfb.novelty_claims: The proposed IDBM procedure introduces a fundamentally new iterative algorithm for the dynamic Schrödinger bridge problem that avoids simulation-inference mismatch by ensuring the marginal distributions of the simulated and inferred processes coincide at each step. Unlike previous approaches, the method realizes a valid transport at every iteration and enables approximation-free generative modeling using only the first iteration. The approach allows for greater flexibility in the choice of reference diffusion dynamics, requires minimal implementation changes, and demonstrates accelerated training and improved sample quality, especially at larger discretization intervals. Theoretical analysis establishes convergence properties, and empirical results highlight robustness and competitiveness with state-of-the-art methods.

755e12646a1e43c3f07df8c0eca2cdf4122a3d4e.title: A Versatile Influence Function for Data Attribution with Non-Decomposable Loss
755e12646a1e43c3f07df8c0eca2cdf4122a3d4e.research_question: How can influence function-based data attribution methods be extended to handle machine learning models trained with non-decomposable loss functions, enabling efficient and accurate quantification of the impact of individual training data points across a broader range of learning objectives?
755e12646a1e43c3f07df8c0eca2cdf4122a3d4e.hypothesis: A finite-difference approximation of the general influence function, combined with auto-differentiation, will enable efficient and accurate data attribution for models trained with non-decomposable losses, closely matching brute-force leave-one-out retraining results while being significantly faster.
755e12646a1e43c3f07df8c0eca2cdf4122a3d4e.proposed_method: A novel method, the Versatile Influence Function (VIF), is developed to generalize influence function-based data attribution to models trained with non-decomposable losses. VIF is formulated as a finite-difference approximation of the general influence function from robust statistics, replacing the need for case-specific derivations with a computationally efficient approach. The method leverages auto-differentiation to compute gradients and Hessians of the loss function with respect to model parameters, and calculates the influence of removing a data point by evaluating the difference in the loss when the data point is included versus excluded, followed by a Hessian-vector product. VIF is applicable to a wide range of loss functions, including those where loss terms depend on multiple data points (e.g., Cox regression, contrastive loss, listwise ranking loss), and does not require model retraining. Efficient implementations using techniques such as Conjugate Gradient and LiSSA are proposed for scalable inverse Hessian approximation.
755e12646a1e43c3f07df8c0eca2cdf4122a3d4e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three representative scenarios involving non-decomposable losses: Cox regression for survival analysis (using METABRIC and SUPPORT datasets), node embedding for network analysis (using Zachary’s Karate network with DeepWalk), and listwise learning-to-rank for information retrieval (using Delicious and Mediamill datasets). For each scenario, VIF will be used to estimate the influence of individual training data points on relevant target functions (e.g., relative risk in Cox regression, contrastive loss for node pairs, ListMLE loss for ranking). The results will be quantitatively compared to brute-force leave-one-out retraining using Pearson correlation coefficients, and runtime performance will be measured to assess computational efficiency. Baselines include brute-force LOO retraining and, where applicable, multiple random seeds to assess upper limits of correlation. Additional case studies will be conducted to interpret model behavior using VIF estimates.
755e12646a1e43c3f07df8c0eca2cdf4122a3d4e.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first general-purpose influence function-based data attribution technique applicable to non-decomposable loss functions, eliminating the need for case-specific derivations. VIF leverages auto-differentiation for efficient computation and is shown to closely approximate brute-force leave-one-out retraining while achieving up to three orders of magnitude speedup. The method broadens the applicability of influence function-based data attribution to complex machine learning objectives, enabling new data-centric applications across diverse domains.

756d9768bf38493dc1dcc722d803cee295d4e955.title: Nonparametric Instrumental Variable Regression through Stochastic Approximate Gradients
756d9768bf38493dc1dcc722d803cee295d4e955.research_question: How can nonparametric instrumental variable (NPIV) regression be performed efficiently and flexibly, especially in the presence of unobservable confounders and for both continuous and binary outcomes, using modern machine learning techniques?
756d9768bf38493dc1dcc722d803cee295d4e955.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that directly minimizing the population risk via a stochastic approximate gradient descent algorithm in function space enables more stable, flexible, and accurate NPIV regression compared to existing methods, and that this approach can naturally accommodate both continuous and binary outcomes under mild assumptions.
756d9768bf38493dc1dcc722d803cee295d4e955.proposed_method: A novel algorithm, SAGD-IV (Stochastic Approximate Gradient Descent for IV regression), is proposed for NPIV estimation. This method formulates the NPIV problem as the minimization of a population risk functional, for which an analytical expression for the functional gradient is derived. The stochastic gradient is estimated using density ratio estimation (for the ratio of joint to marginal densities), regression estimators for conditional means, and kernel mean embeddings for operator estimation. The algorithm is agnostic to the specific choice of supervised learning models, allowing the use of neural networks or kernel methods for the gradient estimation components. The method supports non-quadratic loss functions, enabling application to binary outcome models by simply changing the loss (e.g., to binary cross-entropy), and provides theoretical excess risk bounds under mild regularity assumptions.
756d9768bf38493dc1dcc722d803cee295d4e955.experiment_details: Experiments will compare two variants of SAGD-IV (using kernel methods and neural networks) against state-of-the-art NPIV algorithms such as KIV, DualIV, DeepGMM, DeepIV, and 2SLS. Synthetic datasets will be generated following established NPIV data generating processes with both continuous and binary outcomes, using various structural functions (e.g., linear, step, absolute value, sine). Each estimator will be trained on 3000 samples and tested on 1000 samples, with performance evaluated using mean squared error (MSE) for continuous outcomes and log MSE for binary outcomes, averaged over 20 random realizations. Hyperparameter tuning and implementation details will follow best practices for each baseline. The experiments will assess both predictive accuracy and estimator stability across different scenarios.
756d9768bf38493dc1dcc722d803cee295d4e955.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new framework for NPIV regression that directly minimizes the population risk using stochastic approximate gradients in function space, rather than relying on empirical risk or moment restrictions. The method enables flexible use of modern machine learning estimators, supports non-quadratic loss functions for broader applicability (including binary outcomes), and provides finite-sample excess risk bounds. The approach also simplifies the estimation of the functional gradient, reducing computational complexity and improving stability compared to previous methods. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior or competitive performance and stability relative to current state-of-the-art NPIV algorithms.

75732edda18744c1027ed766ec9579d27a3a59a2.title: Backtracking Improves Generation Safety
75732edda18744c1027ed766ec9579d27a3a59a2.research_question: How can the safety of language model text generation be improved, particularly in scenarios where models produce unsafe outputs despite existing alignment and prevention-based safety techniques?
75732edda18744c1027ed766ec9579d27a3a59a2.hypothesis: Allowing language models to recognize and 'backtrack' from unsafe partial generations by emitting a special token and regenerating a safe response will significantly improve model safety without degrading helpfulness, and will provide increased robustness against adversarial attacks.
75732edda18744c1027ed766ec9579d27a3a59a2.proposed_method: A novel backtracking mechanism will be introduced into language model training and inference. This mechanism enables the model to emit a special [RESET] token upon detecting an unsafe partial generation, after which all tokens preceding and including [RESET] are discarded and a new, safe response is generated. The training process will leverage both supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and direct preference optimization (DPO) to teach the model when to backtrack and how to generate safe responses post-reset. During SFT, backtracking demonstrations will be constructed using prompts, safe responses, and unsafe responses, with a safety classifier used to identify unsafe prefixes. In DPO, preference pairs will be created to encourage backtracking when it improves safety and discourage unnecessary resets. The method will be compatible with standard post-training algorithms and will be evaluated for efficiency trade-offs using logit bias on the [RESET] token.
75732edda18744c1027ed766ec9579d27a3a59a2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using state-of-the-art pre-trained language models, specifically Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3-8B, with both baseline and backtracking-enhanced versions. Training data will include the OpenAssistant-2 dataset for general utility and the harmless subset of the HH-RLHF dataset for safety, filtered using the LlamaGuard2 safety classifier. Evaluation will be performed on open-source safety benchmarks such as AdvBench, MaliciousInstructions, SimpleSafetyTests, and StrongREJECT, totaling over 1,000 prompts, with safety measured by LlamaGuard2 and utility assessed on MT-Bench. The models will also be tested against strong adversarial attacks, including Prefilling, GCG, AutoDAN, and a novel adaptive attack specifically designed to circumvent the backtracking mechanism. Efficiency metrics such as latency and throughput will be analyzed under varying logit biases, and the impact of best-of-k and worst-of-k sampling strategies will be studied.
75732edda18744c1027ed766ec9579d27a3a59a2.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a backtracking mechanism for language models that allows for the explicit discarding and regeneration of unsafe outputs via a special token, which is a departure from traditional prevention-based safety alignment. This approach enables recovery from unsafe generations rather than relying solely on their prevention. The method is compatible with standard post-training algorithms and demonstrates substantial improvements in safety across multiple benchmarks and adversarial scenarios, without sacrificing model helpfulness. Additionally, the proposal provides a systematic framework for balancing safety and generation efficiency and includes the first evaluation of backtracking-based defenses against adaptive adversarial attacks targeting the reset mechanism.

757416282d13ec6ee507e2ca25490d757e1cd0ec.title: CityGaussianV2: Efficient and Geometrically Accurate Reconstruction for Large-Scale Scenes
757416282d13ec6ee507e2ca25490d757e1cd0ec.research_question: How can large-scale 3D scene reconstruction from multi-view RGB images be made both geometrically accurate and computationally efficient, particularly in terms of training time, memory, and storage requirements, while maintaining high visual fidelity and scalability?
757416282d13ec6ee507e2ca25490d757e1cd0ec.hypothesis: Integrating decomposed-gradient-based densification, depth regression, and an elongation filter into a parallelized 2D Gaussian Splatting framework will significantly improve convergence speed, geometric accuracy, and computational efficiency for large-scale scene reconstruction compared to existing methods.
757416282d13ec6ee507e2ca25490d757e1cd0ec.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that builds upon 2D Gaussian Splatting (2DGS) primitives for large-scale scene reconstruction. The method incorporates a decomposed-gradient-based densification (DGD) strategy, which leverages the gradient of the SSIM loss to guide the adaptive densification of Gaussians, thereby eliminating blurry artifacts and accelerating convergence. Depth regression is introduced using predictions from Depth-Anything-V2, providing auxiliary supervision to improve geometric accuracy. An elongation filter is applied to prevent the proliferation of highly elongated Gaussians, mitigating memory and computational bottlenecks during parallel training. The pipeline is further optimized by removing time-consuming post-pruning and distillation steps, instead employing spherical harmonics of degree 2 from the outset and integrating contribution-based pruning during per-block fine-tuning. Storage is compressed via contribution-based vectree quantization, and the entire process is designed for efficient parallel execution.
757416282d13ec6ee507e2ca25490d757e1cd0ec.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on large-scale datasets with accurate ground-truth point clouds, specifically GauU-Scene (realistic) and MatrixCity (synthetic), covering a range of scene types and scales (0.3 km^2 to 2.7 km^2). The method is compared against state-of-the-art baselines including SuGaR, GOF, 2DGS, CityGaussian, and NeRF-based approaches such as NeuS and Neuralangelo. Evaluation metrics include PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS for rendering quality, and F1 score, precision, and recall for geometric accuracy. A standardized TnT-style evaluation protocol is adopted, featuring visibility-based crop volume estimation and even surface sampling for reliable and consistent benchmarking. The experimental setup utilizes 8 A100 GPUs, and ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of each proposed component. Training time, memory, storage, and rendering speed are also systematically measured.
757416282d13ec6ee507e2ca25490d757e1cd0ec.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a decomposed-gradient-based densification strategy for 2DGS, enabling faster and more stable convergence in large-scale scenes. An elongation filter is developed to prevent Gaussian count explosion during parallel training, addressing a key scalability bottleneck. The pipeline eliminates the need for post-pruning and distillation by integrating contribution-based pruning and using lower-degree spherical harmonics from the start, resulting in significant reductions in training time, memory, and storage. A new, standardized geometric evaluation protocol for large-scale scenes is established, ensuring fair and robust benchmarking. The method achieves state-of-the-art geometric accuracy and efficiency, with up to 10× storage compression, at least 25% reduction in training time, and 50% lower memory usage compared to prior art.

757856a09338596096d3c89317ccc03bcfbde810.title: Offline Learning in Markov Games with General Function Approximation
757856a09338596096d3c89317ccc03bcfbde810.research_question: Can sample-efficient algorithms be developed for offline multi-agent reinforcement learning in Markov games with general function approximation, and can these algorithms handle different equilibrium concepts in a unified framework?
757856a09338596096d3c89317ccc03bcfbde810.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a unified algorithmic framework leveraging general function approximation and Bellman-consistent pessimism can efficiently learn approximate equilibria (Nash, Correlated, and Coarse Correlated Equilibria) from offline datasets in Markov games, under weaker data coverage conditions than previously required.
757856a09338596096d3c89317ccc03bcfbde810.proposed_method: A novel algorithmic framework will be developed for offline learning in multi-player general-sum Markov games using general function approximation. The method will unify the computation of Nash, Correlated, and Coarse Correlated Equilibria by expressing the equilibrium gap in a consistent manner for all three concepts. The approach will construct confidence intervals for policy returns using Bellman-consistent pessimism and optimism, forming upper and lower bounds for each candidate policy's value. These bounds will be used to compute a surrogate upper bound on the equilibrium gap, which becomes the optimization objective. The framework will also introduce a V-type variant that estimates state-value functions and uses importance sampling to avoid exponential dependence on the number of agents in the tabular setting.
757856a09338596096d3c89317ccc03bcfbde810.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multi-agent Markov games in both tabular and general function approximation settings. Offline datasets will be generated from various data distributions, with particular attention to scenarios where data coverage is limited or selective. Baselines will include existing offline RL algorithms for Markov games, especially those assuming tabular or linear models and those requiring unilateral coverage. Evaluation metrics will focus on the equilibrium gap for Nash, Correlated, and Coarse Correlated Equilibria, as well as sample complexity and robustness to data coverage conditions. Theoretical guarantees will be validated through empirical analysis and comparison to prior sample complexity bounds.
