757856a09338596096d3c89317ccc03bcfbde810.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to provide a sample-efficient, unified approach for offline learning of multiple equilibrium concepts in Markov games with general function approximation. The method generalizes and subsumes prior results, offering improved and more flexible data coverage conditions that adaptively trade off between policy suboptimality and coverage. The approach also establishes new connections between different solution concepts and prior algorithms for two-player zero-sum games, and introduces a V-type variant to address scalability in the number of agents.

758c2dc290c037a6f211ec503beee70abe2d1197.title: DriveVLM: The Convergence of Autonomous Driving and Large Vision-Language Models
758c2dc290c037a6f211ec503beee70abe2d1197.research_question: How can large vision-language models be leveraged to improve scene understanding and planning in autonomous driving, particularly in complex and long-tail scenarios, and how can their limitations in spatial reasoning and real-time inference be addressed through hybrid system integration?
758c2dc290c037a6f211ec503beee70abe2d1197.hypothesis: Integrating large vision-language models with traditional autonomous driving pipelines will enhance scene understanding, decision-making, and planning capabilities in complex driving scenarios, while overcoming the spatial reasoning and real-time inference limitations of standalone vision-language models.
758c2dc290c037a6f211ec503beee70abe2d1197.proposed_method: A novel autonomous driving framework, DriveVLM, is proposed, which utilizes a large vision-language model (VLM) to process sequences of images through a chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning mechanism. The method comprises three key modules: scene description (linguistically describing the environment and identifying critical objects), scene analysis (analyzing object attributes, motion states, and behaviors, and predicting their influence on the ego vehicle), and hierarchical planning (generating meta-actions, decision descriptions, and trajectory waypoints). To address VLMs' limitations in spatial grounding and computational efficiency, a hybrid system, DriveVLM-Dual, is developed that integrates DriveVLM with traditional 3D perception and motion planning modules. This dual system enables high-frequency, real-time planning by asynchronously combining low-frequency VLM-based reasoning with high-frequency conventional trajectory refinement, leveraging both advanced reasoning and efficient spatial processing.
758c2dc290c037a6f211ec503beee70abe2d1197.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the newly constructed SUP-AD dataset, which is curated through a comprehensive data mining and annotation pipeline targeting long-tail objects and challenging driving scenarios, as well as on the public nuScenes dataset. The SUP-AD dataset is split into training, validation, and test sets, and includes detailed scene, object, and planning annotations. Evaluation metrics include structured scene description/analysis scoring using a pre-trained LLM and meta-action sequence matching via dynamic programming, as well as standard planning metrics such as Displacement Error (DE) and Collision Rate (CR) on nuScenes. Baseline comparisons are made against fine-tuned large VLMs (e.g., Lynx, CogVLM, GPT-4V) and state-of-the-art end-to-end motion planning methods (e.g., NMP, SA-NMP, FF, EO, ST-P3, UniAD, VAD). Ablation studies assess the impact of critical object analysis and 3D perception integration. Onboard deployment is tested on a production vehicle equipped with dual OrinX processors, with inference speed and model size considerations for real-time application.
758c2dc290c037a6f211ec503beee70abe2d1197.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first autonomous driving system that leverages large vision-language models for comprehensive scene understanding and hierarchical planning via a chain-of-thought process. The hybrid DriveVLM-Dual system uniquely combines VLM-based reasoning with traditional 3D perception and planning modules, achieving improved spatial reasoning and real-time planning. A new dataset (SUP-AD) and evaluation metrics for scene understanding and planning are developed, targeting complex and long-tail scenarios. The system is validated both in simulation and real-world deployment, demonstrating superior performance over existing methods and effective adaptation to production vehicle constraints.

759501d8f58c74d2767f882086d63de588c791b4.title: Not All Data are Good Labels: On the Self-supervised Labeling for Time Series Forecasting
759501d8f58c74d2767f882086d63de588c791b4.research_question: Can the reliance on high-quality labeled time series datasets be reduced, and can the potential of existing time series datasets be better exploited to improve model performance in time series forecasting?
759501d8f58c74d2767f882086d63de588c791b4.hypothesis: There exists an optimal candidate dataset, generated by a parameterized reconstruction network, which enables better generalization for a predictor model when evaluated on the raw test set, compared to training on the original dataset.
759501d8f58c74d2767f882086d63de588c791b4.proposed_method: A novel self-supervised framework is proposed that integrates an auxiliary reconstruction network to generate pseudo-labels for time series forecasting tasks. The method employs a co-objective training process, where both the reconstruction network and the predictor model are jointly optimized. During training, an adaptive mask (Self-Correction with Adaptive Mask, SCAM) is used to identify and discard overfitted components in the raw labels, selectively replacing them with pseudo-labels generated from the reconstruction network. The mask is constructed based on the relative positions of predictions, reconstructions, and raw labels, and is guided by a sharpness metric to mitigate overfitting. Additionally, Spectral Norm Regularization (SNR) is applied to the first and last linear layers of the predictor model to further suppress overfitting from a loss landscape perspective, without altering the optimizer or incurring significant computational overhead.
759501d8f58c74d2767f882086d63de588c791b4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on eleven real-world time series forecasting datasets, including Electricity, Weather, Traffic, and four ETT datasets (ETTh1, ETTh2, ETTm1, ETTm2), as well as four large-scale PeMS datasets. The proposed method will be evaluated across multiple backbone models, including both MLP-based (e.g., MLP, CYCLENET) and Transformer-based (e.g., PATCHTST, ITRANSFORMER) architectures. Baseline comparisons will be made against standard supervised training on raw datasets, as well as ablations with and without SCAM and SNR. Evaluation metrics will include Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE), with prediction lengths set to {96, 192, 336, 720} and look-back length fixed at 96. Detailed analyses will be performed to assess generalization, robustness, and the contribution of each component.
759501d8f58c74d2767f882086d63de588c791b4.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new self-supervised paradigm for time series forecasting by adaptively generating and utilizing pseudo-labels through an auxiliary reconstruction task. The SCAM mechanism enables selective replacement of overfitted raw labels, improving model generalization and robustness. The integration of Spectral Norm Regularization into the self-supervised framework further enhances performance, particularly for complex models. This method offers a novel perspective on dataset construction and label correction in time series forecasting, bridging the gap between MLP-based and Transformer-based models and providing consistent improvements across diverse datasets and model architectures.

75a618a86b67b8b32224b77eae8ed37c536826da.title: Search-based User Interest Modeling with Lifelong Sequential Behavior Data for Click-Through Rate Prediction
75a618a86b67b8b32224b77eae8ed37c536826da.research_question: How can user interest be effectively modeled for click-through rate (CTR) prediction using lifelong, extremely long sequential user behavior data, while maintaining scalability, accuracy, and efficiency in large-scale industrial systems?
75a618a86b67b8b32224b77eae8ed37c536826da.hypothesis: A cascaded search-based modeling paradigm that first filters relevant behaviors from lifelong user sequences and then applies precise interest modeling will significantly improve CTR prediction performance and system efficiency compared to existing memory network-based and attention-based models.
75a618a86b67b8b32224b77eae8ed37c536826da.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a Search-based Interest Model (SIM) that utilizes a two-stage cascaded search mechanism for user interest modeling. In the first stage, a General Search Unit (GSU) selects the most relevant subset of user behaviors from arbitrarily long historical sequences using either a hard-search (category-based filtering) or a soft-search (embedding-based maximum inner product search) strategy. This reduces the input sequence length from tens of thousands to a manageable number (hundreds), filtering out noise and irrelevant behaviors. In the second stage, an Exact Search Unit (ESU) applies attention-based modeling (e.g., multi-head attention) to the filtered sub-sequence, incorporating temporal information to capture the precise and diverse user interests with respect to the candidate item. The outputs from ESU, along with other features, are fed into an MLP for final CTR prediction. Both GSU and ESU are trained jointly under a cross-entropy loss, and the system is optimized for real-time industrial deployment with pre-built behavior indices and parallel feature computation.
75a618a86b67b8b32224b77eae8ed37c536826da.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two public datasets (Amazon Books and Taobao) and a large-scale industrial dataset from Alibaba's display advertising system. The datasets include user behavior sequences with maximum lengths ranging from 100 (Amazon) to 54,000 (industrial), with both short-term and long-term behaviors considered. Baseline models for comparison include DIN, Avg-PoolingLongDIN, MIMN, and DIEN, representing state-of-the-art attention and memory network-based approaches. Evaluation metrics will primarily be AUC for offline experiments, and CTR/RPM lift for online A/B testing. The experimental setup will use Adam optimizer, exponential learning rate decay, and standardized embedding/MLP architectures. Ablation studies will assess the impact of each search stage and the inclusion of temporal embeddings. Online deployment will be validated through large-scale A/B testing in a real-time prediction system, measuring latency, throughput, and business impact.
75a618a86b67b8b32224b77eae8ed37c536826da.novelty_claims: The proposed method enables scalable and accurate modeling of lifelong user behavior sequences up to 54,000 events, surpassing previous state-of-the-art solutions by a factor of 54x in sequence length. The cascaded two-stage search strategy (GSU and ESU) effectively filters noise and models diverse, item-specific user interests, resulting in significant improvements in both offline AUC and online business metrics (CTR and RPM). The approach is designed for practical deployment in high-throughput, low-latency industrial systems, with innovations in efficient behavior indexing and parallel computation. The method demonstrates that precise long-term interest modeling can be achieved without prohibitive computational or storage costs, and provides empirical evidence of substantial business value in a real-world setting.

75a89d37f868e2120d98e885563cfb08fbfe61ef.title: Stochastic Marginal Likelihood Gradients using Neural Tangent Kernels
75a89d37f868e2120d98e885563cfb08fbfe61ef.research_question: How can scalable, efficient, and accurate stochastic gradient-based optimization of hyperparameters in deep learning models be achieved using marginal likelihood, particularly for large datasets and complex neural network architectures?
75a89d37f868e2120d98e885563cfb08fbfe61ef.hypothesis: Stochastic lower bounds to the linearized Laplace approximation of the marginal likelihood, derived using the neural tangent kernel (NTK) and structured Gauss-Newton approximations, enable efficient and unbiased stochastic gradient estimation for hyperparameter optimization in deep neural networks, achieving comparable or superior performance to full-batch methods at significantly reduced computational cost.
75a89d37f868e2120d98e885563cfb08fbfe61ef.proposed_method: A novel family of lower bounds to the linearized Laplace approximation of the marginal likelihood will be derived, leveraging the function-space (NTK) form. These bounds will be constructed by partitioning the neural tangent kernel (NTK) or Gauss-Newton (GGN) approximations across data subsets and/or output dimensions, enabling stochastic (mini-batch) estimation of marginal likelihood and its gradients. The method will provide both NTK-based and parametric (e.g., KFAC, block-diagonal, diagonal) estimators, allowing a trade-off between estimator tightness and computational complexity. The approach will be implemented to support automatic differentiation for hyperparameters, facilitating their joint optimization with neural network weights using stochastic gradient descent (SGD). Partitioning strategies, such as output-wise or class-wise batching, will be explored to further tighten the lower bounds and improve scalability.
75a89d37f868e2120d98e885563cfb08fbfe61ef.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard deep learning benchmarks including MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny Imagenet, using convolutional neural networks (e.g., 3-layer CNNs, Wide ResNet, ResNet-50) to evaluate hyperparameter optimization tasks such as learning prior precisions (weight decay) and differentiable invariances. The proposed stochastic estimators (NTK- and KFAC-based) will be compared against full-batch Laplace approximations (including KFAC-Laplace) and other baselines (e.g., Augerino, neural network partitioning). Evaluation metrics will include marginal likelihood estimates, test log-likelihood, classification accuracy, and computational runtime. Experiments will systematically vary batch sizes, partitioning strategies, and dataset sizes to assess estimator tightness, scalability, and Pareto efficiency. The ability to perform more frequent hyperparameter updates due to reduced computational cost will also be investigated.
75a89d37f868e2120d98e885563cfb08fbfe61ef.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first stochastic lower bounds for the linearized Laplace marginal likelihood in deep learning that are amenable to mini-batch-based stochastic gradient optimization. The dual NTK perspective yields a new family of scalable estimators, enabling unbiased and efficient hyperparameter gradients without requiring full passes through the dataset. The method generalizes and theoretically justifies commonly used structured Laplace approximations as lower bounds, and provides practical algorithms that significantly accelerate hyperparameter optimization (up to 25-fold speed-up) while maintaining or improving predictive performance. The approach is applicable to general differentiable hyperparameters, including those affecting network architecture and data invariances, and scales to large datasets and models where previous Laplace-based methods were computationally infeasible.

75b68d0903af9d9f6e47ce3cf7e1a7d27ec811dc.title: Provable Robust Watermarking for AI-Generated Text
75b68d0903af9d9f6e47ce3cf7e1a7d27ec811dc.research_question: How can a provably robust and high-quality watermarking scheme be designed for AI-generated text to enable reliable detection, maintain text quality, and resist adversarial editing or paraphrasing attacks?
75b68d0903af9d9f6e47ce3cf7e1a7d27ec811dc.hypothesis: A watermarking scheme that partitions the vocabulary into fixed groups and consistently biases token selection can achieve provable robustness to edits and paraphrasing, maintain high text quality, and allow for reliable detection with low false positive and false negative rates.
75b68d0903af9d9f6e47ce3cf7e1a7d27ec811dc.proposed_method: A new watermarking scheme, Unigram-Watermark, will be developed by randomly partitioning the language model's vocabulary into two fixed sets: a 'green list' and a 'red list.' During text generation, the logits for green list tokens will be increased by a fixed parameter δ, while red list tokens remain unchanged. The watermark key, which determines the green list, is generated randomly and used both for watermarking and detection. Detection is performed by counting the number of green list tokens in a suspect text, normalizing this count into a z-statistic, and comparing it to a calibrated threshold. The method is parameterized by the fraction of green tokens (γ) and the watermark strength (δ), allowing for a tradeoff between detection power and text quality. The approach is designed to be robust to a wide range of text edits and paraphrasing, and does not require access to the original language model or prompts during detection.
75b68d0903af9d9f6e47ce3cf7e1a7d27ec811dc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using three large language models (GPT2-XL, OPT-1.3B, and LLaMA-7B) on two long-form text datasets: OpenGen and LFQA. For each prompt, both watermarked and un-watermarked texts will be generated, and human-written continuations will serve as additional baselines. Detection performance will be evaluated using true positive rate, F1 score, ROC curves, and z-score statistics, with false positive rates controlled at 1% and 10% by adjusting detection thresholds. Text quality will be assessed using perplexity (evaluated by GPT-3) and human ratings via crowd-sourced evaluations. Robustness will be tested against various attacks, including paraphrasing with models like DIPPER and ChatGPT, as well as edit-based attacks, with detailed analysis of detection accuracy and quality retention after attacks.
75b68d0903af9d9f6e47ce3cf7e1a7d27ec811dc.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a rigorous theoretical framework for quantifying the robustness and effectiveness of watermarking schemes for language models, including formal guarantees on detection accuracy, text quality, and resistance to adversarial editing. The Unigram-Watermark method is claimed to be the first to provide provable robustness guarantees against arbitrary edits for LLM-generated text. The method is also designed for simplicity, efficiency, and practical deployment, requiring minimal overhead and being robust to a wide range of attacks, including paraphrasing and token-level edits. Theoretical analysis demonstrates exponentially decaying error rates with text length and improved robustness compared to prior watermarking schemes.

75e96fb7f5d9754e6eae644b3c7ba341a59149b8.title: On the relation between trainability and dequantization of variational quantum learning models
75e96fb7f5d9754e6eae644b3c7ba341a59149b8.research_question: Under what conditions can variational quantum machine learning (QML) models be both trainable and non-dequantizable, and how can such models be systematically constructed?
75e96fb7f5d9754e6eae644b3c7ba341a59149b8.hypothesis: It is possible to construct variational QML models that are simultaneously trainable (specifically, gradient-based trainable) and non-dequantizable, even for deep-layered quantum circuit architectures.
75e96fb7f5d9754e6eae644b3c7ba341a59149b8.proposed_method: A formal framework will be established to define and distinguish the notions of trainability, dequantization, and variationalness in QML models. A new class of variational QML models, termed 'variveryational', will be introduced, characterized by deep-layered parametrized quantum circuits with gradient-based trainability. The method involves constructing QML models where the hypothesis class incorporates both a computationally hard quantum function (in BQP but not classically tractable) and a parametrized, gradient-optimizable component. The architecture will ensure that the quantum circuit is sufficiently expressive and layered, with the training algorithm restricted to gradient-based optimization. Theoretical analysis will be used to prove the existence and properties of such models, including their resistance to classical dequantization.
75e96fb7f5d9754e6eae644b3c7ba341a59149b8.experiment_details: Experiments will involve constructing explicit examples of variveryational QML models using parametrized quantum circuits that encode computationally hard functions, such as those based on the Discrete Logarithm Problem (DLP). The models will be evaluated on supervised learning tasks where the label function is classically intractable but quantumly efficient. Baselines will include standard kernel-based QML models and hardware-efficient ansatz (HEA) circuits. Evaluation metrics will focus on empirical risk minimization, trainability (measured by convergence of gradient-based optimization), and resistance to classical simulation or dequantization. The experimental setup will include varying the number of circuit layers and qubits to explore the scalability and robustness of the proposed models.
75e96fb7f5d9754e6eae644b3c7ba341a59149b8.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a rigorous formalization of trainability and dequantization in the context of variational QML, clarifies their relationship, and resolves an open question by providing a general recipe for constructing QML models that are both trainable and non-dequantizable. The concept of 'variveryational' QML models is novel, capturing the essence of deep-layered, gradient-based quantum circuits. The approach demonstrates, for the first time, that it is possible to systematically design variational QML models that escape classical dequantization while remaining efficiently trainable, thus paving the way for practical quantum advantage in machine learning.

75f8db00f2bfe052569677b974700239142e8aaa.title: Correlated Noise Provably Beats Independent Noise for Differentially Private Learning
75f8db00f2bfe052569677b974700239142e8aaa.research_question: Can the introduction of correlated noise, rather than independent noise, in differentially private learning algorithms provably improve learning utility, and can such correlated noise be efficiently designed for a broad class of convex optimization problems?
75f8db00f2bfe052569677b974700239142e8aaa.hypothesis: Correlated noise, when appropriately designed, leads to provably better utility in differentially private learning compared to independent noise, and efficient analytical or convex programming-based procedures can be developed to identify near-optimal noise correlations without incurring prohibitive computational costs.
75f8db00f2bfe052569677b974700239142e8aaa.proposed_method: The proposed research will develop a framework for injecting correlated Gaussian noise into the updates of differentially private learning algorithms, generalizing beyond the standard approach of adding independent noise. The method will focus on characterizing the asymptotic learning utility for any correlation structure, providing precise analytical bounds for linear regression and convex functions. Analytical tools from frequency-domain analysis and convex optimization will be leveraged to derive closed-form or efficiently computable noise correlation structures (e.g., Toeplitz matrices and parameterized families such as ν-DP-FTRL). The approach will circumvent the need for computationally expensive semi-definite programming by deriving analytical expressions for near-optimal noise coefficients and by formulating the optimal correlation design as a tractable convex program. The method will be adaptable to both mean estimation and general strongly convex objectives, with theoretical guarantees on privacy and utility.
75f8db00f2bfe052569677b974700239142e8aaa.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets, including image and text classification tasks, to empirically validate the theoretical findings. For linear regression, Gaussian covariates with varying effective dimensions and condition numbers will be used to analyze the dependence of utility on problem parameters. Baseline algorithms will include DP-SGD (with independent noise), prior correlated noise approaches (e.g., anti-PGD, Fichtenberger et al. coefficients), and computationally intensive DP-FTRL variants. Evaluation metrics will include asymptotic suboptimality, excess risk, and empirical accuracy under fixed privacy budgets (e.g., ρ-zCDP or (ε, δ)-DP). The experimental setup will involve tuning the noise correlation parameter (ν) and comparing computational efficiency and memory usage. Both finite-sample and asymptotic regimes will be explored, and the impact of gradient clipping and learning rate selection will be systematically evaluated.
75f8db00f2bfe052569677b974700239142e8aaa.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a provably optimal and computationally efficient framework for designing correlated noise in differentially private learning, providing the first sharp analytical separation between correlated and independent noise mechanisms in terms of learning utility. The approach yields closed-form near-optimal noise coefficients for mean estimation and linear regression, demonstrates exponential improvements in utility for problems with low effective dimension, and generalizes to strongly convex objectives via convex programming. The method achieves state-of-the-art privacy-utility tradeoffs while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements compared to prior approaches that rely on expensive semi-definite programming.

7615436c128e15eafc5f7a4e93812eab756a1ff6.title: Alligat0R: Pre-Training Through Co-Visibility Segmentation for Relative Camera Pose Regression
7615436c128e15eafc5f7a4e93812eab756a1ff6.research_question: How can pre-training strategies for binocular vision be improved to better handle both covisible and non-covisible regions in image pairs, thereby enhancing performance on downstream tasks such as relative camera pose regression, especially in challenging geometric scenarios?
7615436c128e15eafc5f7a4e93812eab756a1ff6.hypothesis: Explicitly modeling covisibility relationships between image pairs through a segmentation-based pre-training objective will yield more robust and transferable visual representations for binocular vision tasks, outperforming reconstruction-based cross-view completion approaches, particularly in scenarios with limited overlap or challenging geometric configurations.
7615436c128e15eafc5f7a4e93812eab756a1ff6.proposed_method: A novel pre-training framework is introduced that replaces cross-view reconstruction with a covisibility segmentation task. The architecture is based on a Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder and a transformer decoder with cross-attention, processing two unmasked images from different viewpoints. For each image, the model predicts, at the patch level, whether each pixel is covisible, occluded, or outside the field of view in the other image. The segmentation head outputs class probabilities for each patch, and the model is trained using a cross-entropy loss over both images. Fine-tuning for relative pose regression is performed by adding a regression head that pools decoder features from both images, concatenates them, and predicts translation and rotation (as a quaternion) using separate MLP heads. The fine-tuning process involves two phases: first, freezing the backbone and training only the regression head, and second, jointly optimizing the entire network with a combined loss for pose regression and covisibility segmentation.
7615436c128e15eafc5f7a4e93812eab756a1ff6.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using the newly created Cub3 dataset, which contains 5 million image pairs with dense covisibility annotations derived from nuScenes (outdoor driving scenes) and ScanNet (indoor scenes). Two variants of the dataset are used: Cub3-50 (pairs with at least 50% overlap) and Cub3-all (pairs with at least 5% overlap, including challenging low-overlap cases). The proposed method is compared against CroCo and CroCo v2, as well as other state-of-the-art detector-free and pose regression methods, using benchmarks such as RUBIK (for autonomous driving) and ScanNet1500 (for indoor scenes). Evaluation metrics include success rates at various thresholds of translation and rotation error (e.g., 5°/2m, 10°/5m), and Average End Point Error (AEPE) for correspondence estimation. Additional analyses include robustness to label noise and performance breakdowns by geometric criteria such as overlap, scale ratio, and viewpoint angle. Implementation uses PyTorch and A100 GPUs, with standardized image preprocessing and training protocols.
7615436c128e15eafc5f7a4e93812eab756a1ff6.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces covisibility segmentation as a new pre-training objective for binocular vision, directly modeling pixel-wise geometric relationships between image pairs. This is the first method to learn visual representations from explicit covisibility segmentation, rather than relying on cross-view reconstruction. The creation and public release of the large-scale Cub3 dataset with dense covisibility annotations is another key contribution. The method demonstrates superior performance and generalization, particularly in challenging geometric scenarios, and provides interpretable outputs that reveal the model's geometric reasoning. Robustness to annotation noise and the ability to learn from low-overlap pairs are also highlighted as novel strengths.

762b42dd957071dd7f5add9435d29edb3b4cbefc.title: Robust Classification via a Single Diffusion Model
762b42dd957071dd7f5add9435d29edb3b4cbefc.research_question: How can a single pre-trained diffusion model be leveraged to achieve robust image classification against a wide range of adversarial attacks, without requiring adversarial training or attack-specific tuning?
762b42dd957071dd7f5add9435d29edb3b4cbefc.hypothesis: A generative classifier constructed from a pre-trained diffusion model, which estimates class probabilities via conditional likelihoods and Bayes’ theorem, will provide superior adversarial robustness and generalization to unseen threat models compared to traditional discriminative classifiers and existing diffusion-based defenses.
762b42dd957071dd7f5add9435d29edb3b4cbefc.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves constructing a Robust Diffusion Classifier (RDC) from a single pre-trained conditional diffusion model. The classifier estimates class probabilities for an input image by first maximizing the data likelihood of the input (Likelihood Maximization), then using the diffusion model to estimate the conditional likelihood for each class, and finally applying Bayes’ theorem to compute class probabilities. The conditional likelihood is approximated using the variational lower bound, which requires calculating the noise prediction loss for every class across different noise levels. To reduce computational complexity, a novel multi-head diffusion backbone is introduced, modifying the last convolutional layer of the UNet architecture to output noise predictions for all classes simultaneously. Efficient sampling strategies are also developed, including direct expectation computation over timesteps and single-sample Monte Carlo estimation for noise, further accelerating both classification and likelihood maximization steps.
762b42dd957071dd7f5add9435d29edb3b4cbefc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the CIFAR-10 dataset, using a subset of 512 test images for evaluation due to computational constraints. The RDC will be compared against state-of-the-art adversarial defenses, including adversarial training with diffusion-generated data (AT-DDPM, AT-EDM), DiffPure, PAT-self, and several generative classifiers (SBGC, HybViT, JEM). Evaluation will include both clean and robust accuracy under strong adaptive attacks, such as AutoAttack (with BPDA and exact gradient variants), and additional threat models (ℓ∞, ℓ2, and StAdv). Robustness will be assessed under both seen and unseen attack types, and ablation studies will be performed on key hyperparameters (e.g., optimization budget, number of timesteps, sampling strategies). Metrics will include robust accuracy, clean accuracy, and computational efficiency (NFEs).
762b42dd957071dd7f5add9435d29edb3b4cbefc.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a generative classifier based on a single pre-trained diffusion model that does not require adversarial training or attack-specific tuning, enabling generalization to unseen threats. The method leverages likelihood maximization as a pre-processing step and employs a novel multi-head diffusion backbone to efficiently compute class-conditional likelihoods for all classes in a single forward pass. Efficient sampling strategies further reduce computational cost without sacrificing robustness. The approach claims state-of-the-art robust accuracy against strong adaptive attacks and demonstrates superior generalization across diverse threat models compared to existing discriminative and generative classifiers.

762ca2711eb167f19b79e39c175708ca15e1f5d7.title: Eliciting Latent Predictions from Transformers with the Tuned Lens
762ca2711eb167f19b79e39c175708ca15e1f5d7.research_question: How can the internal prediction dynamics of large pretrained transformer language models be more accurately and reliably elicited and analyzed at each intermediate layer, and how can these insights be used to improve interpretability, robustness, and detection of anomalous or adversarial inputs?
762ca2711eb167f19b79e39c175708ca15e1f5d7.hypothesis: Introducing a layer-specific, learned affine transformation (the 'tuned lens') for each transformer block will enable more accurate, unbiased, and interpretable decoding of latent predictions at every layer, compared to existing methods such as the logit lens. Furthermore, the trajectory of these latent predictions can be leveraged for tasks such as out-of-distribution detection, adversarial prompt detection, and measuring example difficulty.
762ca2711eb167f19b79e39c175708ca15e1f5d7.proposed_method: The proposed method develops a 'tuned lens' framework, where for each layer of a frozen, pretrained transformer language model, a dedicated affine transformation (translator) is trained to map the layer's hidden state into the representational basis of the final layer. Each translator is optimized via a distillation loss to align the output distribution (after unembedding) with the model's final output logits, using KL divergence as the objective. This approach corrects for representational drift and covariance misalignment across layers, and avoids the brittleness and bias of the logit lens by learning a change-of-basis that is specific to each layer. The translators are initialized as identity matrices and trained on validation data, with regularization and gradient clipping to ensure stability. The Muon optimizer is employed for efficient and effective training of the affine transformations, enabling rapid convergence and high fidelity to the final layer's predictions.
762ca2711eb167f19b79e39c175708ca15e1f5d7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of autoregressive transformer language models, including GPT-Neo, GPT-2, OPT, BLOOM, Pythia, and GPT-NeoX, with model sizes up to 20B parameters. The tuned lens will be evaluated on held-out validation splits from each model's pretraining data (e.g., The Pile, RedPajama, etc.), using metrics such as perplexity, KL divergence to the final layer, and bias in predicted distributions. Baselines will include the logit lens, extended logit lens, and outlier detection methods such as Simplified Relative Mahalanobis (SRM) distance. Additional experiments will assess transferability of tuned lenses to fine-tuned models, causal fidelity via causal basis extraction (CBE), and stimulus-response alignment using Aitchison geometry. The tuned lens's utility will be tested on downstream tasks: (1) eliciting latent knowledge (e.g., secret word detection), (2) robustness to adversarial prompt injections (using outlier detection algorithms like iForest and LOF), and (3) measuring example difficulty via prediction depth, correlating with iteration learned during training. All code and evaluation scripts will be made available for reproducibility.
762ca2711eb167f19b79e39c175708ca15e1f5d7.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel, layer-specific affine transformation (the tuned lens) for eliciting latent predictions from any layer of a frozen transformer, overcoming the limitations of the logit lens by addressing representational drift and bias. It presents a new causal basis extraction algorithm for identifying principal features influencing model predictions, and demonstrates that the tuned lens's prediction trajectories can be used for high-accuracy detection of adversarial prompt injections and for quantifying example difficulty. The method is shown to be transferable across model variants and fine-tuned models, and enables new interpretability analyses of transformer inference dynamics without retraining or modifying the underlying model.

76305acf2bf94e3a5677f7547098eeffb6649706.title: Neural Bellman-Ford Networks: A General Graph Neural Network Framework for Link Prediction
76305acf2bf94e3a5677f7547098eeffb6649706.research_question: How can a general and flexible neural network framework be developed for link prediction on graphs that combines the strengths of traditional path-based methods and modern graph neural networks, while supporting both transductive and inductive settings and providing interpretability and scalability?
76305acf2bf94e3a5677f7547098eeffb6649706.hypothesis: A neural network framework that parameterizes the generalized Bellman-Ford algorithm with learnable operators can achieve superior link prediction performance across both homogeneous and multi-relational graphs, in both transductive and inductive settings, while maintaining interpretability and scalability.
76305acf2bf94e3a5677f7547098eeffb6649706.proposed_method: A novel framework, Neural Bellman-Ford Network (NBFNet), will be developed to address link prediction by generalizing traditional path-based approaches through neural parameterization. The method will define the representation of a node pair as a generalized sum over all path representations between the nodes, with each path representation being a generalized product of edge representations along the path. The generalized Bellman-Ford algorithm will be parameterized with three neural components: INDICATOR (for boundary conditions), MESSAGE (for the path multiplication operator), and AGGREGATE (for the path summation operator). These components will be instantiated as neural functions, leveraging relational operators from knowledge graph embeddings and advanced set aggregation techniques. The framework will support both homogeneous and multi-relational graphs, and will be designed to efficiently scale to large graphs by exploiting the distributive property of the Bellman-Ford algorithm.
76305acf2bf94e3a5677f7547098eeffb6649706.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both knowledge graphs (FB15k-237, WN18RR) and homogeneous graphs (Cora, Citeseer, PubMed), covering transductive and inductive link prediction settings. Standard data splits and filtered ranking protocols will be used, with evaluation metrics including Mean Rank (MR), Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR), HITS@N for knowledge graphs, and AUROC and Average Precision for homogeneous graphs. The proposed method will be compared against a comprehensive set of baselines, including path-based methods (e.g., Katz Index, Personalized PageRank, NeuralLP, DRUM), embedding methods (e.g., TransE, DistMult, RotatE, ComplEx, LowFER), and various GNN-based models (e.g., VGAE, SEAL, GraIL, RGCN, TLC-GNN). The implementation will use 6-layer NBFNet models with 32 hidden units per layer, trained on multiple GPUs, and models will be selected based on validation performance. Ablation studies will be performed to analyze the impact of different neural operators and network depth.
76305acf2bf94e3a5677f7547098eeffb6649706.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a general neural parameterization of the Bellman-Ford algorithm for link prediction, unifying and extending traditional path-based and neural methods. NBFNet is claimed to be the first framework to efficiently and flexibly learn path-based link prediction functions with neural operators, supporting both transductive and inductive settings, and providing interpretability through path-based explanations. The method achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks, demonstrates scalability to large graphs, and offers a principled way to recover and generalize existing logic rule-based and path-based methods.

76314ab64dc3b2f195389b3c87d555b24692fc34.title: Finding Order in Chaos: A Novel Data Augmentation Method for Time Series in Contrastive Learning
76314ab64dc3b2f195389b3c87d555b24692fc34.research_question: How can data augmentation for quasi-periodic, non-stationary time series be improved to enhance contrastive learning performance across diverse tasks, given the challenges of destructive interference and lack of generalizable augmentation methods?
76314ab64dc3b2f195389b3c87d555b24692fc34.hypothesis: A tailored mixup-based data augmentation method that separately interpolates phase and magnitude components of time series, and adaptively controls mixing coefficients based on latent space similarity, will generate more informative and semantically consistent positive samples, leading to improved feature representations and downstream task performance in contrastive learning.
76314ab64dc3b2f195389b3c87d555b24692fc34.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces a novel data augmentation technique for quasi-periodic time series by decoupling phase and magnitude information in the frequency domain. For each pair of time series samples, the method applies linear interpolation to the magnitude components, while the phase components are mixed by computing the shortest angular difference and shifting the anchor's phase toward the other sample proportionally, thus avoiding destructive interference. Mixing coefficients for both phase and magnitude are not fixed; instead, they are adaptively sampled based on the semantic similarity of the sample pair in the latent space, which is obtained by training an unsupervised variational autoencoder (VAE) to learn disentangled representations. If two samples are close in the latent space, more aggressive mixing is performed; otherwise, the interpolation is more conservative to prevent blending dissimilar classes. This approach ensures that augmented samples are both diverse and semantically consistent, preserving task-relevant information.
76314ab64dc3b2f195389b3c87d555b24692fc34.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on eight datasets spanning three time series tasks: activity recognition (UCIHAR, HHAR, USC), heart rate prediction (IEEESPC12, IEEESPC22, DaLia), and cardiovascular disease classification (CPSC2018, Chapman). The SimCLR contrastive learning framework will be used without specialized architectures or memory banks to ensure fair comparison. Baseline methods include a range of mixup techniques (Linear-Mixup, Binary-Mixup, Geometric-Mixup, Cut-Mix, Amplitude-Mix, Spec-Mix), as well as state-of-the-art positive sample generation and augmentation strategies (InfoMin, NNCLR, PosET, GenRep, Aug.Bank, STAug, DACL, IDAA). Evaluation metrics will be task-appropriate: accuracy and macro-F1 for activity recognition, mean absolute error and root mean squared error for heart rate prediction, and area under the ROC curve for disease classification. Models will be pre-trained in a self-supervised manner and evaluated via linear probing on features from the frozen backbone. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the tailored mixup and adaptive coefficient selection.
76314ab64dc3b2f195389b3c87d555b24692fc34.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to explicitly address the destructive effects of traditional mixup for quasi-periodic time series by separately interpolating phase and magnitude in the frequency domain. It introduces a novel, unsupervised mechanism for adaptively controlling the degree of augmentation based on latent space similarity, ensuring semantically meaningful interpolation. The method is generalizable across multiple time series tasks and datasets, and demonstrates consistent improvements over both traditional and state-of-the-art data augmentation and positive sample generation techniques in contrastive learning. Theoretical analysis guarantees improved mutual information retention in the augmented samples, and empirical results show superior or competitive performance across diverse benchmarks.

76406effefded8853e48bca46b05f2f49a78fdb0.title: The Schrödinger Bridge between Gaussian Measures has a Closed Form
76406effefded8853e48bca46b05f2f49a78fdb0.research_question: How can closed-form solutions for the Schrödinger Bridge problem between Gaussian measures be derived, and how can these solutions be leveraged to improve the stability and performance of learning continuous-time stochastic processes in applications such as generative modeling and single-cell genomics?
76406effefded8853e48bca46b05f2f49a78fdb0.hypothesis: Closed-form expressions for the Schrödinger Bridge between Gaussian measures exist and can be derived using tools from entropic optimal transport, Riemannian geometry, and generator theory. Utilizing these closed-form solutions as initialization or guidance in learning stochastic processes will yield improved numerical stability and predictive performance compared to purely numerical or baseline methods.
76406effefded8853e48bca46b05f2f49a78fdb0.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed to derive closed-form solutions for the Schrödinger Bridge (SB) problem specifically between Gaussian measures. The approach reformulates the dynamic entropy-regularized optimal transport problem as an action minimization problem on the Bures-Wasserstein geometry of covariance matrices. Key technical steps include expressing the SB as a minimization over stochastic processes with Gaussian marginals, reducing the problem to solving matrix differential equations involving Lyapunov operators, and leveraging Riemannian geometric tools to obtain explicit formulas for the mean and covariance evolution. The method generalizes to a broad class of linear stochastic differential equations (SDEs) as reference processes, and provides explicit SDE representations for the optimal bridge process. These closed-form solutions are then used as data-dependent initializations or approximations in downstream learning tasks, such as modeling the evolution of cell populations.
76406effefded8853e48bca46b05f2f49a78fdb0.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both synthetic and real-world single-cell genomics datasets. For synthetic data, the method is evaluated on tasks involving the evolution between complex distributions (e.g., moons to spirals), where both forward and backward stochastic policies are learned and compared. In the genomics setting, the method is applied to benchmark datasets (e.g., Moon et al., 2019; Schiebinger et al., 2019), where cell population distributions at different time points are approximated as Gaussians and the closed-form SB is used to model their evolution. Baselines include state-of-the-art SB-based approaches using variance-exploding SDEs (VESDE), variance-preserving SDEs (VPSDE), and sub-VPSDEs, as well as standard generative modeling methods. Evaluation metrics include the entropy-regularized Wasserstein distance between generated and target distributions, as well as visual and quantitative assessments of the learned trajectories and principal component expression patterns. Experimental setups involve multiple runs and comparisons of numerical stability, tuning sensitivity, and predictive accuracy.
76406effefded8853e48bca46b05f2f49a78fdb0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to provide closed-form solutions for the Schrödinger Bridge between arbitrary Gaussian measures, overcoming significant technical challenges where all existing techniques fail. The framework generalizes the classical Bures-Wasserstein geodesics to the dynamic, entropy-regularized setting, and introduces a principled geometric and analytical methodology for solving SBs involving general linear SDEs. The method demonstrates that these closed-form solutions can be directly leveraged for improved stability and performance in SB-based learning tasks, particularly in settings where both marginals are nontrivial and standard numerical methods are unstable or sensitive to hyperparameters. The approach also yields new insights into the geometry of Gaussian optimal transport and provides efficient, explicit formulas for conditional distributions and SDE representations relevant to modern machine learning applications.

7669fea710b955b6794a6b04ea77f06462a4751e.title: Learning Dynamics in Linear VAE: Posterior Collapse Threshold, Superfluous Latent Space Pitfalls, and Speedup with KL Annealing
7669fea710b955b6794a6b04ea77f06462a4751e.research_question: What are the fundamental learning dynamics and failure modes of variational autoencoders (VAEs), specifically in linear settings, and how do hyperparameters such as the KL divergence weight and annealing strategies affect posterior collapse, representation disentanglement, and training convergence?
7669fea710b955b6794a6b04ea77f06462a4751e.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that (1) the learning dynamics of linear VAEs can be rigorously characterized by deterministic ordinary differential equations (ODEs) in the high-dimensional limit, (2) there exists a critical threshold of the KL divergence weight beyond which posterior collapse is inevitable, (3) superfluous latent dimensions lead to overfitting of noise and degrade generalization, and (4) appropriately tuned KL annealing can accelerate convergence without sacrificing generalization.
7669fea710b955b6794a6b04ea77f06462a4751e.proposed_method: A theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted on the learning dynamics of linear VAEs using a minimal generative model. The approach involves deriving and analyzing the macroscopic dynamics of stochastic gradient descent (SGD) in the high-dimensional limit, resulting in a set of deterministic ODEs for key order parameters such as overlaps and covariances. Both model-matched (latent dimension equals generative factors) and model-mismatched (latent dimension exceeds generative factors) scenarios will be studied. Fixed-point and stability analyses of the ODEs will be performed to identify thresholds for posterior collapse and conditions for disentangled representation learning. The impact of monotonic and tanh-based KL annealing schedules on convergence speed and generalization will be systematically explored, with explicit characterization of optimal annealing rates.
7669fea710b955b6794a6b04ea77f06462a4751e.experiment_details: Experiments will include numerical integration of the derived ODEs and finite-dimensional simulations of linear VAEs trained via SGD. The generative model will use the spiked covariance model, where data is generated as a linear combination of latent factors plus Gaussian noise. Both model-matched and model-mismatched cases will be tested, with parameters such as noise strength, signal strength, and KL weight systematically varied. Baselines will include constant KL weight training and various KL annealing schedules. Evaluation metrics will focus on generalization error (reconstruction error on held-out data), disentanglement (measured via off-diagonal elements of the encoder covariance), and convergence time to steady state. Theoretical predictions will be validated against empirical results, and the effects of superfluous latent dimensions and annealing rates will be quantified.
7669fea710b955b6794a6b04ea77f06462a4751e.novelty_claims: The proposed research provides the first rigorous, asymptotically exact dynamical analysis of linear VAE learning using ODEs derived from SGD in the high-dimensional limit. It establishes a precise threshold for posterior collapse as a function of the KL weight, reveals the detrimental effect of superfluous latent dimensions on generalization, and demonstrates that disentangled representations can be achieved for any KL weight below the collapse threshold. The work also identifies optimal KL annealing rates that accelerate convergence, and proves that the steady state of SGD coincides exactly with the global optimum predicted by statistical mechanics methods. These insights offer new theoretical guarantees and practical guidelines for VAE training and hyperparameter selection.

767d7a843c6ab60b1917127670e575ff7053f6bd.title: Lossy Image Compression with Conditional Diffusion Models
767d7a843c6ab60b1917127670e575ff7053f6bd.research_question: How can lossy image compression be improved by leveraging more expressive generative models, and how can the trade-off between rate, distortion, and perceptual quality be effectively controlled in neural image codecs?
767d7a843c6ab60b1917127670e575ff7053f6bd.hypothesis: Replacing traditional Gaussian or Laplacian decoders in neural compression frameworks with conditional diffusion models will yield improved perceptual quality and competitive distortion performance, while enabling flexible control over the trade-off between bitrate, distortion, and perceptual realism.
767d7a843c6ab60b1917127670e575ff7053f6bd.proposed_method: A novel transform-coding-based lossy image compression framework will be developed, where images are encoded into a discrete 'content' latent variable using a neural encoder and a hierarchical prior for entropy coding. The decoder will be implemented as a conditional denoising diffusion model, which reconstructs the image by synthesizing 'texture' variables during the reverse diffusion process, conditioned on the content latent. The training objective will be derived from a variational upper bound on the diffusion model's rate-distortion function, with an optional perceptual loss (e.g., LPIPS) to further enhance perceptual quality. Both deterministic and stochastic decoding schemes will be explored, and the number of diffusion steps will be optimized for practical decoding speed, with special focus on the 'X-prediction' parameterization for fast, high-quality reconstructions.
767d7a843c6ab60b1917127670e575ff7053f6bd.experiment_details: Extensive experiments will be conducted on four benchmark datasets: Kodak, Tecnick, DIV2K, and COCO2017, with preprocessing to standardize image resolutions. The model will be trained on the Vimeo-90k dataset, using a batch size of 4 and the Adam optimizer, with a staged learning rate schedule. Evaluation will utilize sixteen image quality metrics, including both traditional distortion measures (e.g., PSNR, SSIM, MS-SSIM, FSIM) and learned perceptual metrics (e.g., FID, LPIPS, DISTS, PIEAPP). Baseline comparisons will include HiFiC (GAN-based), DGML and NSC (VAE-based), and the classical BPG codec. Ablation studies will investigate the impact of the number of diffusion steps and the stochasticity parameter (gamma) on the trade-off between distortion and perceptual quality.
767d7a843c6ab60b1917127670e575ff7053f6bd.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first end-to-end optimized lossy image compression framework using conditional diffusion models as decoders within the transform coding paradigm. The approach enables explicit control over the trade-off between rate, distortion, and perceptual quality, and demonstrates that high-quality reconstructions can be achieved with only a handful of diffusion steps using the X-prediction parameterization. Empirical results indicate superior performance in perceptual metrics (notably FID) compared to GAN-based codecs, and competitive distortion performance relative to VAE-based models, with more consistent behavior across a wide range of evaluation metrics.

76818e4bcea3841559059ce2dcc97c28fa9958e2.title: On the Query Complexity of Verifier-Assisted Language Generation
76818e4bcea3841559059ce2dcc97c28fa9958e2.research_question: How can verifier-assisted algorithms improve the efficiency and quality of constrained language generation using pretrained language models, and what are the fundamental query complexity trade-offs in such settings?
76818e4bcea3841559059ce2dcc97c28fa9958e2.hypothesis: Access to a process verifier that can assess the extendability of partial generations to constraint-satisfying outputs will substantially reduce the computational complexity and improve the accuracy and diversity of constrained language generation compared to standard sampling methods.
76818e4bcea3841559059ce2dcc97c28fa9958e2.proposed_method: A mathematical and empirical framework will be developed for constrained generation using a pretrained language model as an oracle and a process verifier capable of deciding whether a prefix can be extended to satisfy specified constraints. Several algorithmic strategies will be explored, including tokenwise rejection sampling and a novel backtracking variant, where the generation process is allowed to erase and redo the last few tokens if the verifier indicates an invalid prefix. The process verifier will be trained as a lightweight neural classifier leveraging internal representations from the language model. The approach will be benchmarked against standard baselines such as rejection sampling, nucleus sampling, temperature scaling, and block best-of-N sampling, with a focus on both theoretical oracle complexity and practical performance.
76818e4bcea3841559059ce2dcc97c28fa9958e2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world tasks. For synthetic evaluation, language models will be trained from scratch on Dyck grammar (balanced parentheses) data, with out-of-distribution prompts used to test generalization. A lightweight verifier will be trained to detect invalid completions, and the impact of backtracking stride and quota will be systematically ablated. For real-world evaluation, the task of generating valid and diverse Python test cases for a given function will be considered, using a frozen pretrained CodeLlama model as the generator. The verifier will be trained on intermediate layer representations, and performance will be measured in terms of accuracy (fraction of valid completions), diversity (number of distinct correct test cases), and query complexity (number of language model calls). Baselines will include nucleus sampling, greedy decoding, and block best-of-N approaches. Evaluation metrics will encompass completion accuracy, diversity, and computational efficiency.
76818e4bcea3841559059ce2dcc97c28fa9958e2.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a formal analysis of query complexity in verifier-assisted constrained generation, demonstrating both information-theoretic and computational lower bounds in the absence of a verifier. It proposes a new backtracking variant of tokenwise rejection sampling, empirically showing robust improvements in accuracy, diversity, and efficiency over standard baselines. The approach also highlights the effectiveness of lightweight verifiers trained on internal model representations, and provides a comprehensive empirical and theoretical exploration of the algorithmic design space for verifier-aided inference-time generation.

76c0bee44f2852b170d5d6aa0a36c082e37a7025.title: Graphon Mean-Field Control for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
76c0bee44f2852b170d5d6aa0a36c082e37a7025.research_question: How can cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) with nonuniform agent interactions be efficiently approximated and controlled in large-scale systems, particularly when agent interactions are structured by arbitrary dense networks?
76c0bee44f2852b170d5d6aa0a36c082e37a7025.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that introducing a graphon mean-field control (GMFC) framework, which leverages graphon theory to model nonuniform interactions, will enable accurate and scalable approximation of cooperative MARL on large graphs. Furthermore, discretizing the graphon index into blocks (block GMFC) will yield a tractable and near-optimal solution for finite-agent systems.
76c0bee44f2852b170d5d6aa0a36c082e37a7025.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that formulates cooperative MARL with nonuniform interactions as a graphon mean-field control (GMFC) problem. The method models the agent network as a dense graph and uses graphon functions to capture the limiting behavior of agent interactions as the population size grows. GMFC is reformulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) with deterministic dynamics and an infinite-dimensional state-action space defined over ensembles of probability measures and policies. To address computational tractability, the graphon index is discretized into a finite number of blocks, resulting in a block GMFC model. This block GMFC is then recast as a finite-dimensional continuous-state MDP, where agents within each block are treated as homogeneous, and the Bellman equation is solved using deep reinforcement learning algorithms, such as Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). The learned block-wise policy ensemble is subsequently deployed in the original finite-agent MARL system by sampling actions according to the block distributions.
76c0bee44f2852b170d5d6aa0a36c082e37a7025.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several benchmark cooperative MARL environments with varying numbers of agents and different network structures (e.g., Erdős-Rényi, stochastic block models, random geometric graphs). The block GMFC approach will be compared against state-of-the-art MARL algorithms in terms of mean episode reward, scalability, and approximation error as the number of agents increases. Evaluation metrics will include the mean episode reward, convergence rate, and the closeness of MARL performance to the block GMFC solution as the agent population grows. The experimental setup will involve training the block GMFC policy ensemble using PPO and deploying it in multi-agent systems of increasing size to empirically validate theoretical approximation guarantees.
76c0bee44f2852b170d5d6aa0a36c082e37a7025.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a general discrete-time GMFC framework that extends mean-field control to systems with nonuniform, graphon-structured agent interactions, overcoming the homogeneity limitation of classical mean-field theory. The block GMFC approach offers a scalable and tractable algorithmic solution by discretizing the graphon, allowing efficient approximation of large-scale cooperative MARL. Theoretical results provide explicit approximation error bounds and Pareto optimality guarantees, while empirical studies demonstrate that the method matches or exceeds the performance of existing MARL algorithms, particularly in terms of scalability to large agent populations.

76e8218f657c77c38da44daaed5bb54ab727a8fc.title: Visual Autoregressive Modeling: Scalable Image Generation via Next-Scale Prediction
76e8218f657c77c38da44daaed5bb54ab727a8fc.research_question: How can autoregressive modeling for image generation be redefined to improve scalability, efficiency, and generalization, potentially surpassing diffusion-based models in both quality and speed?
76e8218f657c77c38da44daaed5bb54ab727a8fc.hypothesis: Reformulating visual autoregressive modeling as a coarse-to-fine, next-scale prediction process—rather than conventional raster-scan next-token prediction—enables transformer-based models to achieve superior image generation performance, scalability, and generalization, while significantly improving inference efficiency.
76e8218f657c77c38da44daaed5bb54ab727a8fc.proposed_method: A novel visual autoregressive modeling framework is proposed, where image generation is performed via next-scale prediction instead of traditional next-token prediction. The method utilizes a multi-scale vector quantized variational autoencoder (VQVAE) to encode images into a hierarchy of discrete token maps at increasing resolutions. An autoregressive transformer is then trained to sequentially predict each higher-resolution token map conditioned on all previous, coarser scales, using a block-wise causal attention mask to enforce proper dependencies. During each prediction step, all tokens within a given scale are generated in parallel, preserving spatial locality and reducing computational complexity. The transformer architecture follows a GPT-2-like decoder-only design with adaptive normalization, and model scaling is systematically explored to study power-law scaling laws.
76e8218f657c77c38da44daaed5bb54ab727a8fc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ImageNet 256x256 and 512x512 class-conditional image generation benchmarks. The proposed method will be compared against leading generative model families, including GANs (e.g., BigGAN, StyleGAN-XL), diffusion models (e.g., ADM, DiT, LDM), masked-prediction models (e.g., MaskGIT), and conventional autoregressive models (e.g., VQGAN, ViT-VQGAN, RQTransformer). Evaluation metrics will include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS), precision, recall, and wall-clock inference time. Model sizes will range from 18M to 2B parameters, and scaling laws will be assessed by training models of varying sizes and tracking test loss and error rates as functions of model size and training compute. Zero-shot generalization will be evaluated on downstream tasks such as image in-painting, out-painting, and class-conditional editing, without additional fine-tuning.
76e8218f657c77c38da44daaed5bb54ab727a8fc.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new paradigm for autoregressive image generation based on next-scale prediction, enabling parallel token generation within each scale and preserving spatial structure. This framework empirically demonstrates, for the first time, that GPT-style autoregressive models can surpass state-of-the-art diffusion transformers in image synthesis quality, inference speed, and data efficiency. The method exhibits clear power-law scaling laws similar to those observed in large language models, and achieves strong zero-shot generalization on various downstream visual tasks. Comprehensive open-source code and models are provided to facilitate further research in scalable visual autoregressive modeling.

7706f583e5b713be163cc631ff700e88594fe0ac.title: DOPPLER: Differentially Private Optimizers with Low-pass Filter for Privacy Noise Reduction
7706f583e5b713be163cc631ff700e88594fe0ac.research_question: How can the performance degradation caused by differentially private (DP) noise in deep learning optimizers be mitigated, while maintaining strong privacy guarantees, in a way that is broadly compatible with existing DP optimization methods and scalable to large models and datasets?
7706f583e5b713be163cc631ff700e88594fe0ac.hypothesis: Applying a frequency-domain low-pass filter to the privatized gradients during DP optimization will suppress high-frequency DP noise while preserving the low-frequency gradient signal, thereby improving the utility of DP-trained models without sacrificing privacy guarantees.
7706f583e5b713be163cc631ff700e88594fe0ac.proposed_method: A novel component, DOPPLER, is proposed to be integrated into DP optimizers such as DPSGD, DPAdam, and DPGaLore. DOPPLER operates by applying a linear low-pass filter to the sequence of privatized gradients during training. This filter is implemented as a recursive linear combination of current and past gradients and update directions, with coefficients designed to amplify low-frequency (signal) components and suppress high-frequency (noise) components in the frequency domain. The method includes bias correction to account for initialization effects and is compatible with various filter orders, allowing for both simple (momentum-like) and higher-order filtering. The approach is designed to be orthogonal and complementary to existing time-domain DP noise reduction techniques, and can be adaptively tuned based on the estimated auto-correlation of gradients.
7706f583e5b713be163cc631ff700e88594fe0ac.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of computer vision (MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100) and natural language processing (GLUE) datasets. Models to be evaluated include a 5-layer CNN, modified ResNet, EfficientNet with group normalization, and ViT, with random initialization unless otherwise specified. The proposed DOPPLER-enhanced DP optimizers (LP-DPSGD, LP-DPAdam, LP-DPGaLore) will be compared to their unfiltered counterparts using test accuracy as the primary evaluation metric. Hyperparameters such as filter coefficients, learning rate, batch size, and training epochs will be tuned via grid search, and the privacy parameter δ will be fixed at 1/N^1.1. The impact of the low-pass filter will be assessed across different privacy budgets (ε) and model/dataset combinations, with extensive ablation and sensitivity analyses.
7706f583e5b713be163cc631ff700e88594fe0ac.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a frequency-domain perspective to DP optimization, enabling the use of low-pass filtering to reduce DP noise without altering model structure or incurring additional privacy cost. The method is theoretically justified with convergence and privacy guarantees, and is broadly compatible with existing DP optimizers and noise reduction techniques. Unlike prior approaches, the method does not introduce bias or require model modifications, and provides a principled, generalizable, and easily implementable framework for improving DP training performance.

770c28af824fc021fe6323ad569d8bffd7653176.title: Variational Control for Guidance in Diffusion Models
770c28af824fc021fe6323ad569d8bffd7653176.research_question: How can pretrained diffusion models be guided to satisfy arbitrary terminal constraints or external objectives, in a manner that is general, training-free, and applicable across diverse tasks and model architectures?
770c28af824fc021fe6323ad569d8bffd7653176.hypothesis: Guiding pretrained diffusion models through a variational optimal control framework enables flexible, training-free adaptation to a wide range of downstream tasks, including linear, non-linear, and blind inverse problems, as well as style-guided generation, without sacrificing sample quality or requiring model retraining.
770c28af824fc021fe6323ad569d8bffd7653176.proposed_method: A novel framework, Diffusion Trajectory Matching (DTM), is introduced to guide pretrained diffusion models by formulating guidance as a variational optimal control problem. The method models guided diffusion as a controlled Markov process, introducing control signals at each diffusion step that are treated as variational parameters. At each timestep, the control is optimized to minimize a cost function that trades off a terminal cost (enforcing the external constraint, such as matching a measurement or style) and a transient cost (penalizing deviation from the original diffusion trajectory using KL divergence or similar measures). The approach is instantiated in the Non-linear Diffusion Trajectory Matching (NDTM) algorithm, which integrates seamlessly with standard samplers such as DDIM. The control signal is parameterized additively and optimized iteratively per diffusion step, allowing dynamic adjustment to satisfy terminal constraints while maintaining proximity to the data manifold.
770c28af824fc021fe6323ad569d8bffd7653176.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on challenging inverse problems (random inpainting, super-resolution, non-linear deblurring, and blind image deblurring) and style-guided generation tasks. Datasets include FFHQ (256×256) and ImageNet (256×256) for inverse problems, and WikiArt and PartiPrompt for style guidance, with 1,000 held-out validation samples per task. Baselines for comparison include DPS, RED-diff, MPGD, DDRM, C-ΠGDM, RB-Modulation, DMPlug, FreeDOM, and others, using pretrained pixel-space and latent-space diffusion models (such as Stable Diffusion 1.4). Evaluation metrics focus on perceptual quality (LPIPS, FID, KID), prompt and style adherence (CLIP score, Style score), and runtime. The experimental setup includes ablations on control parameters, optimization steps, and guidance weights, as well as visualizations of control trajectories.
770c28af824fc021fe6323ad569d8bffd7653176.novelty_claims: The proposed DTM framework generalizes and unifies a broad class of prior guidance methods in diffusion models, subsuming both classifier and classifier-free guidance as special cases. The method enables training-free, task-agnostic guidance applicable to both pixel and latent-space diffusion models, and supports novel instantiations such as non-linear and blind inverse problems without additional model training. The NDTM algorithm achieves state-of-the-art results across diverse tasks, offering a principled and flexible approach to guided sampling that is more efficient and stable than existing methods. The framework's variational control perspective provides new theoretical insights and practical flexibility, enabling dynamic tradeoffs between sample quality, guidance strength, and computational cost.

772d66b86d7f5992cc693b0f7428665a38a3b3d0.title: Zeroth-Order Optimization Finds Flat Minima
772d66b86d7f5992cc693b0f7428665a38a3b3d0.research_question: Can zeroth-order optimization methods, which rely solely on function evaluations rather than gradients, implicitly favor solutions with desirable generalization properties, such as flat minima, in high-dimensional machine learning problems where gradients are inaccessible or expensive to compute?
772d66b86d7f5992cc693b0f7428665a38a3b3d0.hypothesis: Zeroth-order optimization with the standard two-point estimator implicitly regularizes the optimization trajectory, favoring convergence to flat minima characterized by a small trace of the Hessian, even in the absence of explicit gradient information.
772d66b86d7f5992cc693b0f7428665a38a3b3d0.proposed_method: A zeroth-order optimization framework will be developed using the standard two-point gradient estimator, which estimates gradients via finite differences along random Gaussian directions. The method iteratively updates model parameters by sampling a random direction, evaluating the loss at two symmetric points along this direction, and constructing a gradient estimate to perform parameter updates. Theoretical analysis will focus on the regularization effect induced by the smoothing parameter, showing that the optimization dynamics minimize a regularized objective combining the original loss and the trace of the Hessian. Convergence guarantees to approximate flat minima will be established under convexity and higher-order smoothness assumptions, with explicit characterization of the required number of iterations and smoothing parameter scaling with problem dimension and desired accuracy.
772d66b86d7f5992cc693b0f7428665a38a3b3d0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on binary classification tasks using overparameterized support vector machines (SVMs) and logistic regression, as well as on language model fine-tuning tasks with large-scale models such as RoBERTa. Standard datasets from the LIBSVM library (e.g., a5a and w5a) will be used, with feature vectors mapped to high-dimensional spaces to induce overparameterization. Baselines will include gradient descent and sharpness-aware minimization methods. Evaluation metrics will include training loss, test accuracy, and the trace of the Hessian (estimated for scalability on large models) to assess the flatness of the obtained solutions. The experimental setup will compare the trajectory and final values of these metrics across optimization methods, with particular attention to the implicit regularization effect of zeroth-order optimization.
772d66b86d7f5992cc693b0f7428665a38a3b3d0.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first rigorous theoretical and empirical investigation of the implicit regularization properties of zeroth-order optimization, specifically its tendency to converge to flat minima as measured by the trace of the Hessian. The approach provides new convergence guarantees for zeroth-order methods to approximate flat minima in convex, smooth settings, extending beyond traditional analyses focused solely on stationarity. The framework also offers a novel perspective on the connection between zeroth-order and sharpness-aware optimization, and the results are applicable to a wide range of unbiased zeroth-order estimators and high-dimensional machine learning applications where gradients are inaccessible.

774418fff92a72a97e0b1279d23b592e7d896b04.title: A rank-adaptive robust integrator for dynamical low-rank approximation
774418fff92a72a97e0b1279d23b592e7d896b04.research_question: How can a robust, structure-preserving, and rank-adaptive integrator be developed for dynamical low-rank approximation of matrix and tensor differential equations, ensuring accuracy and conservation properties across a range of applications?
774418fff92a72a97e0b1279d23b592e7d896b04.hypothesis: A rank-adaptive integrator that augments evolving subspace bases and employs Galerkin projection followed by truncation to a specified tolerance will enable accurate, robust, and structure-preserving low-rank approximations for matrix and tensor differential equations, maintaining key invariants such as norm and energy up to the truncation tolerance.
774418fff92a72a97e0b1279d23b592e7d896b04.proposed_method: A novel rank-adaptive integrator will be designed for dynamical low-rank approximation of matrix and tensor differential equations. The method begins by updating the basis matrices for the low-rank factorization via integration of projected matrix differential equations, generating augmented bases that span both the previous and newly evolved subspaces. A Galerkin step is then performed in the larger subspace formed by these augmented bases, solving a reduced differential equation for the core factor. The resulting approximation is truncated via singular value decomposition (SVD) to a rank determined adaptively by a user-specified tolerance, ensuring that only significant singular values are retained. This procedure is iterated at each time step, and the method is extended analogously to Tucker tensor decompositions for higher-order problems. The integrator is designed to preserve structure, such as symmetry, norm, and energy, up to the truncation tolerance.
774418fff92a72a97e0b1279d23b592e7d896b04.experiment_details: Numerical experiments will be conducted on benchmark problems from kinetic equations, uncertainty quantification, and quantum dynamics, where dynamical low-rank approximation is of significant interest. The integrator will be tested on both real and complex matrix and tensor differential equations, with initial low-rank approximations obtained via truncated SVD. Baseline comparisons will include fixed-rank integrators and alternative rank-adaptive schemes, such as those based on projector-splitting methods.
