Evaluation metrics will include approximation error (e.g., Frobenius norm), preservation of invariants (norm, energy), and computational efficiency. Experiments will systematically vary the truncation tolerance and step size to assess robustness and adaptive rank selection.
774418fff92a72a97e0b1279d23b592e7d896b04.novelty_claims: The proposed integrator introduces a simple and effective mechanism for rank adaptivity in dynamical low-rank approximation, overcoming challenges in augmenting basis subspaces while retaining robustness to small singular values. The method preserves key structural properties—such as exactness for rank-r solutions, norm and energy conservation, and monotonic decrease for gradient flows—up to the truncation tolerance, even in the presence of adaptively changing rank. The approach generalizes to both matrices and Tucker tensors, and extends naturally to complex-valued problems. Robust error bounds are established that are independent of small singular values, and the method enables adaptive rank selection without sacrificing the favorable properties of prior fixed-rank integrators.

774591fdd988eaaff3917e7c5171d044b0843e63.title: Efficient Large-Scale Language Model Training on GPU Clusters Using Megatron-LM
774591fdd988eaaff3917e7c5171d044b0843e63.research_question: How can large-scale language models be trained efficiently on GPU clusters, overcoming memory and computational bottlenecks, by optimally combining different parallelism techniques?
774591fdd988eaaff3917e7c5171d044b0843e63.hypothesis: A carefully designed combination of pipeline, tensor, and data parallelism—augmented with novel scheduling and communication optimizations—will enable practical, efficient training of trillion-parameter language models on large GPU clusters, achieving high throughput and scalability.
774591fdd988eaaff3917e7c5171d044b0843e63.proposed_method: A new distributed training framework will be developed that composes pipeline, tensor, and data parallelism (PTD-P) to maximize throughput for large transformer-based language models. The method will introduce an interleaved pipeline scheduling strategy that reduces pipeline bubble time and improves throughput by over 10% compared to standard schedules, while maintaining a comparable memory footprint. Tensor model parallelism will be applied within multi-GPU servers to leverage high-bandwidth interconnects, while pipeline model parallelism will be used across servers for scaling to larger models. Data parallelism will be layered on top to further scale training across more GPUs. Communication optimizations, such as scatter/gather techniques, will be implemented to minimize redundant data transfer across nodes, and fused computation kernels will be used to maximize computational efficiency.
774591fdd988eaaff3917e7c5171d044b0843e63.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a state-of-the-art GPU supercomputer (e.g., NVIDIA Selene) using up to 3072 A100 GPUs, training transformer-based language models (such as GPT-3 and larger) with up to 1 trillion parameters. The evaluation will include weak and strong scaling studies, comparison of different parallelism configurations (tensor, pipeline, data, and their combinations), and ablation studies on microbatch size and scheduling strategies. Baselines will include ZeRO-3 without model parallelism and other established parallelization approaches. Metrics will include per-GPU and aggregate throughput (teraFLOP/s, petaFLOP/s), scaling efficiency, memory footprint, and estimated end-to-end training time for large token counts. The impact of communication and computation optimizations will be quantified.
774591fdd988eaaff3917e7c5171d044b0843e63.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to demonstrate practical, efficient training of trillion-parameter language models by composing pipeline, tensor, and data parallelism at scale. The interleaved pipeline schedule is novel and reduces pipeline bubble time, improving throughput by over 10% compared to prior schedules. Communication optimizations, such as scatter/gather, enable efficient cross-node communication, making more communication-intensive schedules feasible. The framework achieves state-of-the-art throughput (up to 52% of theoretical peak per GPU) and enables training times for trillion-parameter models that are practical for real-world use. Analytical and empirical studies provide new insights into the interactions and tradeoffs of parallelism strategies at scale.

7754ac3e8ff1286f17593159781487543cdddaba.title: SliceGPT: Compress Large Language Models by Deleting Rows and Columns
7754ac3e8ff1286f17593159781487543cdddaba.research_question: How can large language models be compressed post-training to significantly reduce computational and memory requirements, while maintaining high performance on language generation and downstream tasks?
7754ac3e8ff1286f17593159781487543cdddaba.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that applying structured transformations to the weight matrices of transformer-based language models, followed by the removal of entire rows and columns, can achieve substantial model compression with minimal loss in predictive performance and improved inference efficiency.
7754ac3e8ff1286f17593159781487543cdddaba.proposed_method: A novel post-training compression technique, termed SliceGPT, will be developed to reduce the size of large language models by deleting entire rows and columns from weight matrices. The method begins by converting all LayerNorm operations in the model to RMSNorm, allowing for the exploitation of a computational invariance property in transformer architectures. At each block of the network, a principal component analysis (PCA) is performed on the signal (activation) matrices using a calibration dataset to compute an orthogonal transformation matrix. The weight matrices are then rotated into the principal component basis, and the least significant components (as determined by PCA) are removed by slicing off corresponding rows and columns. Residual connections are adjusted with additional linear transformations to maintain functional equivalence. This process reduces the embedding dimension throughout the network, resulting in smaller, dense weight matrices and lower computational overhead.
7754ac3e8ff1286f17593159781487543cdddaba.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several large language models, including OPT, LLAMA-2, and Phi-2, across a range of model sizes (from hundreds of millions to tens of billions of parameters). Calibration datasets such as WikiText-2 and Alpaca will be used to compute the PCA transformations. The compressed models will be evaluated on language modeling tasks (using perplexity on WikiText-2) and a suite of zero-shot downstream tasks (PIQA, WinoGrande, HellaSwag, ARC-e, ARC-c) using the LMEvaluationHarness. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art sparsification methods such as SparseGPT with 2:4 sparsity. Evaluation metrics will include perplexity, zero-shot accuracy, inference throughput (tokens/sec), and per-token inference time on both consumer-grade and datacenter GPUs. Additional experiments will assess the impact of post-slicing recovery fine-tuning (using LoRA) on downstream performance.
7754ac3e8ff1286f17593159781487543cdddaba.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the concept of computational invariance in transformer networks, enabling the use of orthogonal transformations to facilitate structured pruning without altering model predictions. Unlike prior sparsification or low-rank approximation methods, this technique directly reduces the embedding dimension and removes entire rows and columns, resulting in smaller dense matrices that are more compatible with existing hardware. The method achieves significant compression (up to 30%) with minimal performance loss, requires no or minimal fine-tuning, and provides measurable improvements in inference speed and resource utilization. This framework offers a new avenue for efficient post-training compression of large language models, with practical benefits for deployment on resource-constrained hardware.

775782035fc4d8f4a830757a4baf987137dfd99e.title: Learning to Detect Mobile Objects from LiDAR Scans Without Labels
775782035fc4d8f4a830757a4baf987137dfd99e.research_question: Can accurate 3D mobile object detectors be learned from unlabeled LiDAR data, eliminating the need for human-annotated labels, and how effective are such detectors across diverse environments and object types?
775782035fc4d8f4a830757a4baf987137dfd99e.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that mobile object detectors can be trained to high accuracy using only unlabeled LiDAR data by leveraging common-sense heuristics to generate initial seed labels, followed by iterative self-training to refine and expand the detector's capabilities.
775782035fc4d8f4a830757a4baf987137dfd99e.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a fully unsupervised framework for 3D mobile object detection from LiDAR scans. First, multiple traversals of the same geographic locations are collected using a vehicle equipped with LiDAR and accurate localization (GPS/INS). For each point in the aggregated point clouds, an ephemerality score is computed based on the variation of local neighborhoods across traversals, identifying points likely to belong to mobile (non-persistent) objects. Clusters of low-ephemerality points are extracted using DBSCAN clustering, and upright 3D bounding boxes are fitted to these clusters. Additional common-sense filters are applied to remove implausible boxes (e.g., those not on the ground or with unrealistic sizes). These seed labels are then used to train an off-the-shelf 3D object detector from scratch. The detector's outputs are iteratively used as pseudo-labels for further rounds of self-training, with PP-score-based filtering applied at each round to remove false positives and improve label quality.
775782035fc4d8f4a830757a4baf987137dfd99e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Lyft Level 5 Perception and nuScenes datasets, both of which provide LiDAR scans, accurate localization, and ground-truth bounding boxes for evaluation. The datasets will be split into geographically disjoint training and test sets, ensuring no overlap in locations. The proposed method will be evaluated using standard 3D object detection architectures such as PointRCNN, PointPillars, and VoxelNet (SECOND), with models trained from scratch using only the generated pseudo-labels. Evaluation metrics will include Average Precision (AP) in both bird's-eye view (BEV) and 3D at IoU thresholds of 0.25 and 0.5, and performance will be analyzed across different distance ranges (e.g., 0-30m, 30-50m, 50-80m). Baseline comparisons will include ablations without ephemerality-based seed labels and without self-training. Additional analyses will examine the impact of the amount of unlabeled data, the number of self-training rounds, and cross-domain generalization.
775782035fc4d8f4a830757a4baf987137dfd99e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable fully unsupervised 3D mobile object detection from LiDAR data, requiring zero human-annotated labels. It leverages a novel combination of ephemerality statistics from repeated traversals and common-sense geometric constraints to generate effective seed labels, and demonstrates that iterative self-training can substantially improve both recall and precision over noisy initial labels. The method is shown to generalize across datasets and domains, and achieves detection performance competitive with supervised approaches, especially at close and medium ranges. The framework is broadly applicable and can be used to bootstrap object detectors in new environments without any manual labeling.

7777ffb5f2f1d52b7080725332035b81af2994c9.title: AnyLoc: Towards Universal Visual Place Recognition
7777ffb5f2f1d52b7080725332035b81af2994c9.research_question: How can a universal visual place recognition (VPR) system be developed that operates robustly across a wide range of environments, temporal changes, and viewpoint variations, without requiring environment- or task-specific training or fine-tuning?
7777ffb5f2f1d52b7080725332035b81af2994c9.hypothesis: General-purpose feature representations derived from large-scale, self-supervised foundation models, when combined with unsupervised feature aggregation techniques, can enable universal VPR that is robust to diverse environments, temporal changes, and viewpoint variations, outperforming existing task-specific VPR methods.
7777ffb5f2f1d52b7080725332035b81af2994c9.proposed_method: The proposed method will leverage per-pixel features extracted from large-scale pretrained vision transformer models (foundation models) such as DINO and DINOv2, which are trained in a self-supervised, task-agnostic manner. Instead of using per-image features (e.g., the CLS token), the approach will aggregate dense per-pixel features using unsupervised techniques such as VLAD (Vector of Locally Aggregated Descriptors) and GeM (Generalized Mean Pooling). The aggregation process will involve extracting features from specific layers and facets (e.g., value facet of deeper layers) of the vision transformer, followed by clustering to construct visual vocabularies. To further enhance performance, the semantic properties of the aggregated features will be characterized using PCA, enabling the construction of domain-specific vocabularies for VLAD aggregation. No retraining or fine-tuning on VPR-specific data will be performed, ensuring the method remains universal and task-agnostic.
7777ffb5f2f1d52b7080725332035b81af2994c9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse suite of 12 datasets covering both structured (urban, indoor) and unstructured (aerial, underwater, subterranean, visually degraded) environments. The evaluation will include challenging conditions such as day-night and seasonal variations, as well as significant viewpoint shifts (including <90° and >90° view changes). Baselines will include state-of-the-art VPR methods such as NetVLAD, CosPlace, MixVPR, and foundation model-based approaches using the CLS token (CLIP, DINO, DINOv2). Evaluation metrics will primarily be Recall@K, with experiments run using consistent hardware and random seeds for reproducibility. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of different aggregation methods, vocabulary sources (global, domain-specific, map-specific), model architectures, layers, and facets. Additional analyses will explore the transferability of vocabularies within domains and compare self-supervised foundation models to VPR-supervised vision transformers.
7777ffb5f2f1d52b7080725332035b81af2994c9.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a universal VPR framework that operates robustly across a massively diverse set of environments, temporal changes, and viewpoint variations, without any VPR-specific training or fine-tuning. The method uniquely combines per-pixel features from large-scale self-supervised foundation models with unsupervised aggregation techniques, and further enhances performance by constructing domain-specific vocabularies based on the semantic properties of the features. This approach establishes a new baseline for universal VPR, demonstrating up to 4× higher Recall@1 compared to existing methods and significant improvements in robustness, scalability, and generalization to out-of-distribution environments.

778e2ae4fed322022a2f44dcb977dae5743cf20a.title: Reasons and Solutions for the Decline in Model Performance after Editing
778e2ae4fed322022a2f44dcb977dae5743cf20a.research_question: What are the underlying causes of performance degradation in large language models after knowledge editing, and how can editing methods be optimized to minimize such degradation while enabling efficient, repeated updates?
778e2ae4fed322022a2f44dcb977dae5743cf20a.hypothesis: Performance degradation in edited language models is primarily caused by the diversity and complexity of editing objectives in the data and by the explosive growth of parameter layer norms during sequential edits; regulating these factors can mitigate degradation and improve editing efficiency.
778e2ae4fed322022a2f44dcb977dae5743cf20a.proposed_method: A comprehensive investigation will be conducted from both data and model perspectives to identify the causes of performance decline following model editing. From the data perspective, a Multi-Question Dataset (MQD) will be constructed, featuring diverse question types (true/false, multiple-choice, direct generation) to systematically analyze the impact of editing objective diversity and sequence length on model performance. From the model perspective, the relationship between the L1-norm growth in editing layers and editing accuracy will be examined, with a focus on catastrophic forgetting and edit bottlenecks. To address these issues, a novel Dump for Sequence (D4S) method will be developed, which caches editing history in O(1) space and consolidates edits into a batch update, thereby regulating norm growth and enabling multiple effective edits with minimal model damage.
778e2ae4fed322022a2f44dcb977dae5743cf20a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using large language models such as GPT-J (6B) and Llama2 (7B). Editing datasets will include commonsense and factual knowledge corpora such as zsRE, ELKEN, 20Q, CKD, and the newly constructed MQD. Evaluation datasets will span a range of generalization and reasoning benchmarks, including AI2 Reasoning Challenge, HellaSwag, MMLU, TruthfulQA, WinoGrande, and GSM-8K. Baseline editing methods for comparison will include ROME, MEMIT, PMET, GRACE, and standard fine-tuning. Evaluation metrics will include editing accuracy, downstream task performance, and L1-norm growth of editing layers. Experiments will assess both the effectiveness of edits and the extent of catastrophic forgetting across varying numbers and types of edits.
778e2ae4fed322022a2f44dcb977dae5743cf20a.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first systematic analysis of performance degradation in edited language models from both data and model perspectives, identifying the diversity and perplexity of editing objectives and the growth of parameter layer norms as primary causes. The proposed D4S method is novel in its ability to cache edit history with O(1) space complexity and batch updates, effectively mitigating norm growth and overcoming previous bottlenecks in sequential editing. The approach enables multiple effective edits with minimal impact on model performance, achieving state-of-the-art results in sequential knowledge editing tasks.

779d5dc2b443cd563c275bd23b25d9053ebdda04.title: Optimal PAC Bounds without Uniform Convergence
779d5dc2b443cd563c275bd23b25d9053ebdda04.research_question: What are the optimal high-probability risk (PAC) bounds for learning in realizable settings, particularly for binary and multiclass classification, partial hypothesis classification, and bounded regression, when uniform convergence is suboptimal or fails to hold?
779d5dc2b443cd563c275bd23b25d9053ebdda04.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that optimal PAC bounds can be achieved in a broad class of learning settings by leveraging predictors with strong leave-one-out performance and permutation invariance, thereby bypassing the limitations of uniform convergence arguments.
779d5dc2b443cd563c275bd23b25d9053ebdda04.proposed_method: A general framework will be developed that transforms leave-one-out error guarantees of permutation invariant predictors into high-probability PAC risk bounds. The approach involves constructing predictors that are symmetric with respect to the training data and have bounded leave-one-out error, as formalized by specific assumptions. The methodology includes an online-to-batch conversion technique, utilizing suffix averaging over sequences of predictors trained on prefixes of the data, to obtain tight high-probability risk bounds. The framework will be instantiated using the one-inclusion graph (and hypergraph) algorithm, and its aggregations, to achieve optimal PAC bounds in various learning settings, including binary and multiclass classification, partial hypothesis classification, and bounded regression with absolute loss. Technical details include the use of martingale arguments to convert in-expectation guarantees into high-probability bounds and the analysis of complexity measures such as the one-inclusion hypergraph density and scale-sensitive dimensions.
779d5dc2b443cd563c275bd23b25d9053ebdda04.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in several settings: (1) binary classification with VC-dimension as the complexity measure, (2) multiclass classification using the one-inclusion hypergraph density, (3) partial hypothesis classification with classes of VC-dimension, and (4) bounded regression with absolute loss, using the scale-sensitive V-dimension. For each setting, the proposed method will be compared to empirical risk minimization (ERM) and uniform convergence-based approaches. Evaluation metrics will include the PAC risk (expected loss with high probability) as a function of sample size, failure probability, and class complexity. Theoretical sample complexity bounds will be derived and, where possible, matched to known lower bounds. Key experimental setups involve constructing realizable datasets and measuring the risk of predictors constructed via the proposed aggregation and online-to-batch methods.
779d5dc2b443cd563c275bd23b25d9053ebdda04.novelty_claims: The proposed framework provides optimal high-probability PAC risk bounds in settings where uniform convergence is suboptimal or fails, by leveraging leave-one-out predictors and permutation invariance. It unifies and extends previous results by enabling optimal PAC bounds for multiclass classification, partial hypothesis classification, and bounded regression, surpassing standard uniform convergence-based rates. The method simplifies and improves upon prior analyses, offering tighter constant factors and a more general, modular approach that applies to a wide range of learning problems. Additionally, it resolves open questions regarding sample complexity in partial hypothesis classification and provides new, sharper bounds for bounded regression based on scale-sensitive complexity measures.

77b1f1c6d1658d120456b9046667cf009ceb39ce.title: MetaMath: Bootstrap Your Own Mathematical Questions for Large Language Models
77b1f1c6d1658d120456b9046667cf009ceb39ce.research_question: How can the mathematical problem-solving abilities of open-source large language models be significantly improved through novel data augmentation techniques, particularly for complex multi-step reasoning tasks?
77b1f1c6d1658d120456b9046667cf009ceb39ce.hypothesis: Augmenting training datasets for open-source language models with diverse, bootstrapped mathematical questions—incorporating both forward and backward reasoning as well as rephrased variants—will substantially enhance the models' mathematical reasoning and generalization capabilities compared to existing augmentation or fine-tuning strategies.
77b1f1c6d1658d120456b9046667cf009ceb39ce.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed to generate a high-diversity mathematical question-answer dataset, termed MetaMathQA, by bootstrapping existing mathematical questions through multiple augmentation strategies. These strategies include: (1) answer augmentation, where multiple reasoning paths are generated for each question using few-shot chain-of-thought prompting and only those with correct answers are retained; (2) LLM-based question rephrasing, where each question is reworded in several ways and filtered for semantic and answer consistency; (3) backward reasoning augmentation, where questions are transformed to require the model to infer masked variables given the answer, using both declarative (Self-Verification) and direct (FOBAR) formulations. The resulting dataset will combine all these augmented samples. Large language models, specifically LLaMA-2 variants, will then be fine-tuned on this comprehensive dataset using maximum likelihood estimation of reasoning paths conditioned on the question.
77b1f1c6d1658d120456b9046667cf009ceb39ce.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two standard mathematical reasoning benchmarks: GSM8K (grade school math problems) and MATH (high school competition problems), using their respective training and test splits. The proposed MetaMath models (fine-tuned LLaMA-2 at 7B, 13B, and 70B parameters) will be compared against a suite of open-source and closed-source LLMs, including SFT, RFT, WizardMath, and GPT-3.5-Turbo, among others. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on GSM8K and MATH test sets, as well as performance on a newly created GSM8K-Backward test set to assess backward reasoning. Additional analyses will measure the impact of data diversity (using diversity gain metrics), question length, and the effect of various augmentation strategies through ablation studies.
77b1f1c6d1658d120456b9046667cf009ceb39ce.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel question bootstrapping approach that systematically augments mathematical training data with both forward and backward reasoning variants, as well as LLM-generated rephrasings, resulting in a highly diverse dataset. This multi-view augmentation strategy is claimed to significantly improve generalization and reasoning abilities in open-source LLMs, surpassing previous state-of-the-art methods. The approach also uniquely demonstrates the importance of question diversity and backward reasoning in dataset construction for mathematical problem-solving, and provides empirical evidence that more diverse data, rather than simply more data, is critical for boosting LLM performance on challenging reasoning tasks.

77b603850094ff749c9040772f8169a75145d506.title: Explaining grokking through circuit efficiency
77b603850094ff749c9040772f8169a75145d506.research_question: What are the underlying mechanisms that explain the phenomenon of grokking in neural networks, and how do factors such as circuit efficiency and dataset size contribute to transitions between memorisation and generalisation during training?
77b603850094ff749c9040772f8169a75145d506.hypothesis: Grokking arises when a task admits both a memorising and a generalising solution, with the generalising solution being more efficient but slower to learn. As training dataset size increases, memorising circuits become less efficient while generalising circuits maintain their efficiency, leading to a critical dataset size at which the transition from memorisation to generalisation occurs. Furthermore, it is hypothesised that weight decay encourages the network to favour more efficient circuits, and that novel phenomena such as ungrokking and semi-grokking can be predicted and observed based on these dynamics.
77b603850094ff749c9040772f8169a75145d506.proposed_method: The proposed research will develop a theoretical framework that models neural network solutions as combinations of 'circuits'—internal mechanisms responsible for either memorisation or generalisation. Circuit efficiency will be defined as the ability to produce large logits with a small parameter norm. The methodology will involve constructing minimal simulation environments where both memorising and generalising circuits are explicitly represented, and their learning dynamics are controlled via gradient descent with weight decay. The efficiency of each circuit will be empirically measured as a function of dataset size and parameter norm. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to predict critical dataset sizes where transitions between memorisation and generalisation occur, and to derive testable predictions about new phenomena such as ungrokking and semi-grokking. These predictions will then be validated through targeted neural network training experiments.
77b603850094ff749c9040772f8169a75145d506.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted primarily on the modular addition task (a + b mod P for a, b in 0,...,P-1 and P=113), using 1-layer Transformer models trained with the AdamW optimiser and cross-entropy loss. Additional tasks will be included for robustness. Training runs will be designed to isolate either memorising or generalising circuits by manipulating label randomness and dataset size. Key experimental variables will include dataset size, weight decay strength, and random seed. Baseline comparisons will involve networks trained to convergence on full datasets (to induce generalisation) versus small or randomised datasets (to induce memorisation). Evaluation metrics will include training and test accuracy, loss curves, parameter norm, and logit magnitudes. Special experiments will probe the predicted phase transitions (ungrokking) by reducing dataset size after grokking, and will search for semi-grokking by sweeping dataset sizes around the predicted critical threshold.
77b603850094ff749c9040772f8169a75145d506.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a circuit efficiency-based theory of grokking, providing a unified explanation for the transition from memorisation to generalisation in neural networks. It predicts and empirically validates two novel phenomena—ungrokking (regression from generalisation to memorisation) and semi-grokking (delayed, partial generalisation)—which have not been previously reported. The work also establishes the sufficiency of three key ingredients (existence of both circuit types, efficiency gap, and differential learning speed) for grokking, and provides new insights into the role of dataset size and weight decay in shaping generalisation dynamics.

77ba3fc35d8272090922f0e7fd4f51c186350d51.title: Sample-specific Masks for Visual Reprogramming-based Prompting
77ba3fc35d8272090922f0e7fd4f51c186350d51.research_question: How can visual reprogramming methods be improved to better adapt pre-trained models to diverse target tasks, particularly by addressing the limitations of using shared input masks across all samples?
77ba3fc35d8272090922f0e7fd4f51c186350d51.hypothesis: Employing sample-specific, multi-channel masks generated by a lightweight neural network for each input image will reduce approximation error and improve generalization in visual reprogramming-based prompting, compared to traditional approaches that use a single shared mask for all samples.
77ba3fc35d8272090922f0e7fd4f51c186350d51.proposed_method: A novel visual reprogramming framework is proposed that replaces the conventional shared binary mask with sample-specific, three-channel masks generated by a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN). Each target-domain image is resized and passed through this CNN-based mask generator, which outputs a unique mask tailored to the individual sample. If the generated mask does not match the required pattern size, a patch-wise interpolation module is employed to upsample the mask, ensuring alignment with the image dimensions. The learnable noise pattern is then modulated by the sample-specific mask and added to the input image before being fed into a fixed, pre-trained classifier. This approach enables both shared and sample-specific adaptation, and the entire system is trained end-to-end using gradient-based optimization.
77ba3fc35d8272090922f0e7fd4f51c186350d51.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of 11 widely used image classification datasets, including CIFAR10, CIFAR100, SVHN, GTSRB, Flowers102, DTD, UCF101, Food101, EuroSAT, OxfordPets, and SUN397. Pre-trained ResNet-18, ResNet-50, and ViT-B32 models (all pre-trained on ImageNet-1K) will serve as the fixed backbone classifiers. The proposed method will be compared against baseline visual reprogramming techniques that use shared masks (padding-based and resizing-based approaches, including narrow, medium, and full watermarking). Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the contributions of sample-specificity, multi-channel masking, and patch size. Training will be standardized across methods, with consistent learning rates, milestones, and number of epochs, and results will be averaged over multiple random seeds.
77ba3fc35d8272090922f0e7fd4f51c186350d51.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the concept of sample-specific, multi-channel masks for visual reprogramming, addressing the generalization limitations of shared-mask approaches. The method theoretically reduces approximation error and empirically demonstrates superior performance across diverse datasets and model architectures. The integration of a lightweight CNN-based mask generator and a patch-wise interpolation module enables efficient and adaptive input transformation, marking a significant innovation over existing visual reprogramming techniques.

77c044bf4fc8ead6483da56e800fe6ec0048a651.title: The Optimality of Polynomial Regression for Agnostic Learning under Gaussian Marginals
77c044bf4fc8ead6483da56e800fe6ec0048a651.research_question: What are the fundamental computational limits of agnostic learning for Boolean- and real-valued function classes under Gaussian marginals, and how do these limits relate to the degree of polynomial approximation required for such classes?
77c044bf4fc8ead6483da56e800fe6ec0048a651.hypothesis: The complexity of agnostic learning under Gaussian marginals is tightly characterized by the degree of polynomial approximation in L1 or L2 norm, and no statistical query (SQ) algorithm can significantly outperform polynomial regression for a broad class of concept classes.
77c044bf4fc8ead6483da56e800fe6ec0048a651.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed to characterize the computational complexity of agnostic learning under Gaussian distributions by leveraging linear programming (LP) duality and functional analysis. The approach constructs hard families of examples by embedding functions with vanishing low-degree moments in random low-dimensional subspaces, making them indistinguishable from random functions for SQ algorithms. The methodology reduces the problem of proving SQ lower bounds to establishing lower bounds on the degree of polynomial approximation (in L1 or L2 norm) for the target concept class. For Boolean-valued functions, the LP duality is used to show equivalence between the existence of low-degree polynomial approximations and the feasibility of learning, while for real-valued functions, the method distinguishes between CSQ and general SQ models, relating their complexity to L2 and L1 approximation degrees, respectively.
77c044bf4fc8ead6483da56e800fe6ec0048a651.experiment_details: Experiments will involve theoretical analysis and the derivation of explicit lower bounds for the polynomial approximation degree for key concept classes, including Linear Threshold Functions (LTFs), Polynomial Threshold Functions (PTFs), intersections of halfspaces, ReLUs, and sigmoids. The evaluation will use the standard Gaussian distribution as the marginal on R^n, and performance will be measured in terms of the sample and computational complexity required to achieve error OPT+ε. Baseline algorithms include L1- and L2-polynomial regression, and the lower bounds will be compared to known upper bounds for these algorithms. Theoretical results will be validated by matching lower and upper bounds (up to polynomial factors) for the sample/query complexity in the SQ model.
77c044bf4fc8ead6483da56e800fe6ec0048a651.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a general and unified framework that characterizes the optimality of polynomial regression for agnostic learning under Gaussian marginals within the SQ model. It provides the first tight or near-tight SQ lower bounds for several fundamental concept classes, including LTFs, PTFs, intersections of halfspaces, ReLUs, and sigmoids. The approach leverages LP duality in infinite-dimensional function spaces and establishes new connections between polynomial approximation degree, Gaussian noise sensitivity, and learning complexity. The framework is more general and yields stronger lower bounds than previous methods, and it extends to both Boolean- and real-valued function classes.

77ec7844f75ed04f6649c9c072117d1b9c9dfdba.title: CLIPure: Purification in Latent Space via CLIP for Adversarially Robust Zero-Shot Classification
77ec7844f75ed04f6649c9c072117d1b9c9dfdba.research_question: How can adversarial robustness in zero-shot image classification be improved, particularly for models based on vision-language pre-training, without relying on adversarial training or pixel-space purification?
77ec7844f75ed04f6649c9c072117d1b9c9dfdba.hypothesis: Purification of adversarial examples in the multi-modal latent space of a vision-language model such as CLIP, rather than in pixel space or uni-modal latent space, will significantly improve adversarial robustness for zero-shot classification while maintaining efficiency and clean accuracy.
77ec7844f75ed04f6649c9c072117d1b9c9dfdba.proposed_method: A novel adversarial purification framework will be developed that operates in the multi-modal latent space of a pre-trained vision-language model (CLIP). The approach will formalize purification risk using the KL divergence between the joint distributions of the attack (forward SDE) and purification (reverse SDE) processes, providing theoretical insight into the factors influencing purification effectiveness. Two variants will be implemented: (1) a generative approach (CLIPure-Diff) leveraging the DiffusionPrior module from DaLLE-2 to model the likelihood of image embeddings conditioned on text, and (2) a discriminative approach (CLIPure-Cos) that models likelihood using cosine similarity between image and text embeddings of a blank template. The purification process will update normalized unit vectors in latent space to maximize likelihood, ensuring that vector magnitude does not interfere with CLIP's cosine-based alignment. No additional training of the underlying CLIP model will be required.
77ec7844f75ed04f6649c9c072117d1b9c9dfdba.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard benchmarks including CIFAR-10, ImageNet, and 13 zero-shot classification datasets previously used for evaluating CLIP-based defenses. Robustness will be evaluated against strong adaptive adversarial attacks, such as AutoAttack with various ℓ∞ and ℓ2 bounds, as well as BPDA+EOT and latent-based attacks. Baselines will include state-of-the-art adversarial training approaches (e.g., AT-ConvNeXt-L, AT-Swin-L, FARE, TeCoA), pixel-space purification methods (e.g., DiffPure, LM-EDM, Purify-EBM), and uni-modal latent space purification (e.g., LM-StableDiffusion). Evaluation metrics will include clean accuracy, robust accuracy under attack, and inference efficiency (measured as average inference time per sample). Ablation studies will assess the impact of purification space, normalization, and classifier guidance.
77ec7844f75ed04f6649c9c072117d1b9c9dfdba.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to perform adversarial purification in the multi-modal latent space of a vision-language model, rather than in pixel or uni-modal latent space. The discriminative variant, CLIPure-Cos, is the first purification method that does not rely on generative models, resulting in substantial gains in inference efficiency. The approach is dataset-agnostic, requiring no adversarial training or dataset-specific adaptation, and achieves state-of-the-art robustness across a wide range of zero-shot classification benchmarks. Theoretical analysis provides new insights into purification risk and its dependence on latent space properties.

77f02ff24909896856fec410968aef7999c29440.title: Does Circuit Analysis Interpretability Scale? Evidence from Multiple Choice Capabilities in Chinchilla
77f02ff24909896856fec410968aef7999c29440.research_question: Can circuit analysis interpretability techniques be effectively scaled to large language models, and what are the internal mechanisms underlying multiple-choice question answering in such models?
77f02ff24909896856fec410968aef7999c29440.hypothesis: Existing circuit analysis techniques, such as logit attribution, attention pattern visualization, and activation patching, can be successfully scaled to large language models and will enable the identification and interpretation of the internal mechanisms responsible for multiple-choice question answering.
77f02ff24909896856fec410968aef7999c29440.proposed_method: The proposed research will apply circuit analysis techniques to a large-scale language model, specifically the 70B-parameter Chinchilla model, to investigate the internal mechanisms responsible for multiple-choice question answering. The methodology will involve the use of logit attribution to quantify the direct contributions of model components (attention heads and MLPs) to output logits, attention pattern visualization to categorize the functional roles of attention heads, and activation patching to causally validate the importance of identified nodes. Singular value decomposition (SVD) will be used to analyze the low-dimensional subspaces of queries, keys, and values in attention heads, aiming to reveal the semantic features encoded by these components. The analysis will focus on both the identification of final nodes in the circuit and the interpretation of their behavior across standard and perturbed data distributions.
77f02ff24909896856fec410968aef7999c29440.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Massive Multitask Language Understanding (MMLU) benchmark, using a subset of six topics where the Chinchilla model demonstrates strong performance. The evaluation will involve zero-shot prompting, and accuracy will be measured both by the model's ability to select the correct answer label (A, B, C, or D) and the correct answer text. Baselines will include smaller Chinchilla models (1B and 7B parameters) to assess the emergence of algorithmic capabilities with scale. The effectiveness of circuit analysis techniques will be validated by patching identified nodes and measuring changes in loss (negative log probability of the correct answer) and accuracy over 128 randomly sampled prompts. Additional synthetic datasets will be used to isolate algorithmic capabilities from factual knowledge.
77f02ff24909896856fec410968aef7999c29440.novelty_claims: This research proposes the first comprehensive application of circuit analysis interpretability techniques to a state-of-the-art, large-scale language model (70B parameters), demonstrating that these methods can scale beyond small models. The approach enables the identification and categorization of key internal components responsible for multiple-choice question answering, including the discovery of 'correct letter' attention heads and their underlying algorithmic features. The use of SVD to analyze low-dimensional subspaces of attention head activations represents an innovative step toward understanding the semantics of internal model features. The research also highlights the limitations of current interpretability techniques when generalizing to broader data distributions, providing new insights into the complexity and partial interpretability of large model circuits.

77fa06b12aea62f13c91d8dc666c7ef2b26662ff.title: A Recipe for Watermarking Diffusion Models
77fa06b12aea62f13c91d8dc666c7ef2b26662ff.research_question: How can effective and robust watermarking techniques be developed for diffusion models, including both unconditional/class-conditional and text-to-image paradigms, to enable copyright protection and content monitoring without significantly degrading generative performance?
77fa06b12aea62f13c91d8dc666c7ef2b26662ff.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that diffusion models can be efficiently and robustly watermarked by embedding invisible, detectable information either into the training data or via finetuning with trigger prompts, such that the watermark can be accurately recovered from generated outputs while maintaining high generative quality.
77fa06b12aea62f13c91d8dc666c7ef2b26662ff.proposed_method: The proposed methodology consists of two tailored pipelines for watermarking diffusion models. For unconditional and class-conditional diffusion models, a binary watermark string is encoded into the training data using a neural watermark encoder-decoder pair, and the diffusion model is then trained on this watermarked dataset. The encoder embeds the watermark as invisible features, while the decoder is trained to recover the watermark from generated samples. For large-scale text-to-image diffusion models, a predefined image-text pair (e.g., a rare trigger prompt and a watermark image such as a QR code) is injected by finetuning the pretrained model. This finetuning is regularized with a weight constraint to preserve generative performance on non-trigger prompts, ensuring the watermark image is only generated in response to the specific trigger. The approach includes empirical ablation to balance watermark robustness, imperceptibility, and model fidelity.
77fa06b12aea62f13c91d8dc666c7ef2b26662ff.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on state-of-the-art diffusion models, including the Elucidating Diffusion Model (EDM) and Stable Diffusion, across multiple datasets such as CIFAR-10, FFHQ-70K, AFHQv2, and ImageNet-1K. For unconditional/class-conditional models, various bit-lengths of watermark strings will be embedded, and the ability to recover these watermarks will be evaluated using bit accuracy. For text-to-image models, trigger prompts and watermark images (including QR codes and photos) will be tested, with finetuning performed on Stable Diffusion. Baselines will include models without watermarking and models with alternative prompt or watermark designs. Evaluation metrics will include Frechet Inception Distance (FID), PSNR, SSIM, and CLIP score for image quality, as well as robustness tests against model and image perturbations. Ablation studies will investigate the impact of watermark complexity, regularization strength, and trigger prompt design.
77fa06b12aea62f13c91d8dc666c7ef2b26662ff.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a comprehensive and empirically validated recipe for watermarking both unconditional/class-conditional and text-to-image diffusion models. Key innovations include the adaptation of neural watermark encoders/decoders for diffusion model training, the use of trigger-prompt-based watermark injection for large-scale text-to-image models without requiring access to original training data, and the application of weight-constrained finetuning to preserve generative performance. The approach is demonstrated to be robust to various attacks and perturbations, and provides practical guidelines for balancing watermark strength and image quality, laying the groundwork for future research and deployment of watermarking in diffusion-based generative models.

781120c76e42cd13586b01311647815f5c0b0f52.title: NeuS2: Fast Learning of Neural Implicit Surfaces for Multi-view Reconstruction
781120c76e42cd13586b01311647815f5c0b0f52.research_question: How can neural implicit surface reconstruction from multi-view images be significantly accelerated while maintaining or improving reconstruction quality for both static and dynamic scenes, including those with large deformations and long sequences?
781120c76e42cd13586b01311647815f5c0b0f52.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that parameterizing neural implicit surfaces with multi-resolution hash encodings, combined with efficient second-order derivative computation and progressive training strategies, will enable orders-of-magnitude faster training without compromising reconstruction accuracy for both static and dynamic scenes.
781120c76e42cd13586b01311647815f5c0b0f52.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a neural implicit surface reconstruction framework that leverages multi-resolution hash encodings to parameterize the signed distance field (SDF) representation of 3D geometry. A shallow multi-layer perceptron (MLP) receives as input the concatenation of a 3D position and its associated hash-encoded feature vector, outputting both the SDF value and geometry features. To enable efficient training, a novel, lightweight formulation for computing second-order derivatives tailored to ReLU-based MLPs is developed, allowing for highly parallelized CUDA implementation and reducing memory and computational overhead. A progressive training strategy is adopted, wherein the bandwidth of the hash grid encoding is gradually increased from coarse to fine during optimization, accelerating convergence and improving reconstruction fidelity. For dynamic scenes, an incremental training strategy is proposed: the first frame is trained from scratch, while subsequent frames are fine-tuned from the previous frame's parameters, with a global transformation prediction component aligning frames to handle large inter-frame movements and deformations.
781120c76e42cd13586b01311647815f5c0b0f52.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both static and dynamic scene datasets. For static reconstruction, the DTU dataset (15 scenes, 49 or 64 images per scene) will be used, with foreground masks for evaluation. For dynamic scenes, synthetic datasets (such as Lego, Lion, and RenderPeople human sequences) and real datasets (e.g., Dynacap) will be employed, covering hundreds to tens of thousands of frames. Baselines for comparison will include NeuS, Instant-NGP, Instant-NSR, D-NeRF, TiNeuVox, and Voxurf. Evaluation metrics will comprise Chamfer Distance for geometry, PSNR and LPIPS for novel view synthesis, and runtime for training efficiency. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the progressive training strategy, Eikonal loss, and global transformation prediction. All experiments will be run on a single high-end GPU (e.g., RTX 3090), and both quantitative and qualitative results will be reported.
781120c76e42cd13586b01311647815f5c0b0f52.novelty_claims: The proposed approach claims two orders of magnitude acceleration in neural implicit surface reconstruction without loss of quality, enabled by the integration of multi-resolution hash encodings and a novel, efficient second-order derivative computation for ReLU-based MLPs. The method introduces a progressive training strategy for hash encodings and extends to dynamic scenes with an incremental training paradigm and a global transformation prediction module, allowing robust handling of long sequences with large deformations. The approach is claimed to outperform state-of-the-art methods in both reconstruction accuracy and training speed for static and dynamic scenarios.

78281482c1fdad8e167bab39cc9955c73d58ae8f.title: EVA: Exploring the Limits of Masked Visual Representation Learning at Scale
78281482c1fdad8e167bab39cc9955c73d58ae8f.research_question: How can masked visual representation learning be scaled to extremely large model and data sizes using only publicly accessible data, and what are the resulting impacts on transfer performance across a wide range of vision and multi-modal downstream tasks?
78281482c1fdad8e167bab39cc9955c73d58ae8f.hypothesis: Scaling masked image modeling (MIM) pre-training with image-text aligned vision features to billion-parameter vanilla Vision Transformers (ViTs), using only public unlabeled images, will yield state-of-the-art performance and emergent capabilities on diverse vision and multi-modal benchmarks, without requiring supervised or weakly-supervised pre-training.
78281482c1fdad8e167bab39cc9955c73d58ae8f.proposed_method: A large-scale masked image modeling (MIM) framework is developed based on a vanilla Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture with up to one billion parameters. The pre-training objective is to reconstruct masked-out image-text aligned vision features, specifically CLIP features, conditioned on visible image patches. Input images are corrupted using block-wise masking with a 40% masking ratio, and the model is trained to regress the masked CLIP features using a negative cosine similarity loss. The output features are normalized and projected to the same dimension as the CLIP targets via a linear layer. The method leverages only publicly accessible unlabeled image datasets, and does not require additional semantic feature tokenization or feature distillation, enabling efficient scaling of the model and data.
78281482c1fdad8e167bab39cc9955c73d58ae8f.experiment_details: Pre-training is conducted on a merged dataset of 29.6 million publicly available images from sources including ImageNet-21K, CC12M, CC3M, Object365, COCO, and ADE20K. The model is trained for 150 epochs using the AdamW optimizer with a peak learning rate of 1e-3, batch size of 4096, and fp16 precision on up to 128 NVIDIA A100 GPUs. Downstream evaluations are performed on a broad set of benchmarks: image classification (ImageNet-1K and its variants), video action recognition (Kinetics-400/600/700), object detection and instance segmentation (COCO, LVISv1.0), semantic segmentation (ADE20K, COCO-Stuff-164K), and zero-shot image/video classification using a CLIP-style contrastive framework. Baselines include state-of-the-art models such as SwinV2-G, BEiT-3, ViTDet, and OpenCLIP. Evaluation metrics include top-1 accuracy, mIoU, APbox, APmask, and zero-shot classification accuracy, with robustness assessed via performance gaps on distribution-shifted datasets.
78281482c1fdad8e167bab39cc9955c73d58ae8f.novelty_claims: The approach demonstrates that a pure MIM pre-training regime, regressing masked CLIP features, can be efficiently scaled to billion-parameter ViTs using only public unlabeled data, achieving new state-of-the-art results across a wide range of vision and multi-modal tasks. The method eliminates the need for supervised or weakly-supervised pre-training, semantic feature tokenization, or explicit image-text paired data. It reveals emergent transfer capabilities, such as closing the performance gap between large-vocabulary and common-vocabulary instance segmentation (LVIS vs. COCO), and enables stable, efficient scaling of billion-scale CLIP models with improved zero-shot performance and training stability. The work provides a reproducible, vision-centric foundation model and a new direction for scaling multi-modal foundation models.

78341f3d9dc7022c663782284c1e7e703bd73197.title: Spatial-Temporal Identity: A Simple yet Effective Baseline for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
78341f3d9dc7022c663782284c1e7e703bd73197.research_question: How can multivariate time series forecasting be improved by addressing the indistinguishability of samples in both spatial and temporal dimensions, and is it possible to design a model that matches or exceeds the performance of spatial-temporal graph neural networks (STGNNs) while being more concise and efficient?
78341f3d9dc7022c663782284c1e7e703bd73197.hypothesis: Attaching explicit spatial and temporal identity information to multivariate time series samples will alleviate the indistinguishability bottleneck, enabling a simple model architecture to achieve state-of-the-art forecasting performance and efficiency, comparable to or surpassing complex STGNN-based methods.
78341f3d9dc7022c663782284c1e7e703bd73197.proposed_method: A new framework is proposed that augments multivariate time series data with trainable spatial and temporal identity embeddings. The method first transforms raw historical time series for each variable into a latent space using a fully connected embedding layer. Spatial and temporal identities are encoded via three trainable embedding matrices: one for spatial identity (per variable), and two for temporal identities (per time slot in a day and per day in a week). These embeddings are concatenated with the latent representation of each sample, forming an enriched feature vector. The combined representation is then processed through multiple layers of multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) with residual connections, followed by a regression layer to predict future time series values. The model is trained end-to-end using mean absolute error as the loss function and optimized with the Adam optimizer.
78341f3d9dc7022c663782284c1e7e703bd73197.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five widely used multivariate time series datasets: PEMS04, PEMS07, PEMS08, PEMS-BAY (traffic sensor data), and Electricity (energy consumption data). The evaluation will use standard metrics for time series forecasting, including Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). The proposed method will be compared against a comprehensive set of baselines, including traditional statistical approaches (VAR, HI), deep learning models (LSTM), and state-of-the-art STGNN-based methods (DCRNN, STGCN, GraphWaveNet, AGCRN, StemGNN, GMAN, MTGNN, ST-Norm). Experimental setups will follow standard data splits (e.g., 6:2:2 or 7:1:2 for train/validation/test), and all models will be evaluated on multiple prediction horizons (e.g., 3rd, 6th, and 12th time steps, as well as average over 12 steps). Efficiency will be assessed by measuring training time per epoch on standardized hardware. Ablation studies will be performed to isolate the contributions of spatial and temporal identity components.
78341f3d9dc7022c663782284c1e7e703bd73197.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a simple yet highly effective baseline for multivariate time series forecasting by explicitly encoding spatial and temporal identities as trainable embeddings, eliminating the need for graph convolutions or sequential models. This method addresses the indistinguishability bottleneck in both spatial and temporal dimensions, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy and efficiency across multiple datasets. The framework demonstrates that powerful forecasting models can be designed without reliance on complex STGNN architectures, providing new insights into the critical factors for successful multivariate time series prediction.

7860192bb790b487384e3f4e8984f4305b13ad20.title: The Optimal Sample Complexity of PAC Learning
7860192bb790b487384e3f4e8984f4305b13ad20.research_question: What is the minimum number of samples required for probably approximately correct (PAC) learning in the realizable case, for arbitrary concept classes of finite VC dimension, under all possible data distributions?
7860192bb790b487384e3f4e8984f4305b13ad20.hypothesis: There exists a PAC learning algorithm whose sample complexity matches the known lower bound (up to numerical constant factors) for all concept classes of finite VC dimension, thereby eliminating the longstanding logarithmic gap between upper and lower bounds.
7860192bb790b487384e3f4e8984f4305b13ad20.proposed_method: A novel recursive learning algorithm is developed, which constructs a majority vote classifier from a carefully designed set of overlapping data subsamples. At each recursion, the training data is partitioned into overlapping subsets, and multiple recursive calls are made, each with different partially constructed subsamples. The base case trains a classifier on a small subset, while the recursive case aggregates classifiers trained on larger, overlapping subsets. The final classifier is the majority vote over all classifiers trained on these subsamples. The recursive structure and overlap are designed to ensure that each constituent classifier is trained on a substantial fraction of the data, enabling tight control over the error probability and sample complexity.
7860192bb790b487384e3f4e8984f4305b13ad20.experiment_details: Theoretical analysis will be conducted to prove that the proposed algorithm achieves the desired sample complexity bound. The proof will leverage classic generalization bounds for sample-consistent classifiers and inductive arguments based on the recursive structure of the algorithm. Theoretical lower bounds from prior literature will serve as baselines for comparison. The evaluation metric is the sample complexity required to achieve (ε, δ)-PAC learning guarantees for arbitrary concept classes of finite VC dimension. No empirical datasets are involved; all results are established through rigorous mathematical analysis.
7860192bb790b487384e3f4e8984f4305b13ad20.novelty_claims: The proposed algorithm achieves a sample complexity that matches the known lower bound up to numerical constant factors for general concept classes of finite VC dimension, thereby resolving a longstanding open problem in learning theory. The method introduces a new recursive majority vote framework with overlapping data subsets, which eliminates the previous logarithmic gap in upper bounds. This constitutes the first general solution to the optimal sample complexity of PAC learning in the realizable case.

7874c6e5d7313a98b832918d5cb7f1b10ffea4fb.title: Syntactic and Semantic Control of Large Language Models via Sequential Monte Carlo
7874c6e5d7313a98b832918d5cb7f1b10ffea4fb.research_question: How can text generation from large language models be controlled to satisfy complex syntactic and semantic constraints, especially when these constraints are costly to evaluate or cannot be incrementally enforced during generation?
7874c6e5d7313a98b832918d5cb7f1b10ffea4fb.hypothesis: A sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) framework that incrementally integrates both efficient and expensive syntactic and semantic constraints during language model inference will enable more accurate and efficient controlled generation, outperforming both larger models and existing constrained decoding or sample-rerank methods.
7874c6e5d7313a98b832918d5cb7f1b10ffea4fb.proposed_method: A novel controlled language model generation framework is proposed, leveraging sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) sampling to approximate the posterior distribution over outputs conditioned on both the base language model and a set of constraint-encoding potential functions. The method partitions constraints into efficient (incrementally evaluable) and expensive (costly or non-incremental) potentials. During generation, particles (candidate sequences) are extended using locally constrained decoding based on efficient potentials, while expensive potentials are incorporated as twist functions that reweight partial or complete sequences. Importance weighting corrects for the greediness of local decoding and integrates expensive signals, and adaptive resampling reallocates computational resources toward promising particles. The framework is programmable, allowing domain-specific proposals and potentials, and supports flexible granularity in the extension step (e.g., by lines for code or clauses for SQL).
7874c6e5d7313a98b832918d5cb7f1b10ffea4fb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four challenging semantic parsing domains: Python code generation for data science (DS-1000), text-to-SQL (Spider), goal inference in planning (Planetarium), and molecular synthesis (GDB-17). Each domain will utilize a base open-source language model (e.g., Llama3 variants), with domain-specific context-free grammars or validators for syntactic constraints and additional task-specific expensive potentials (e.g., test case execution, simulation, or column validation). Baselines will include unconstrained generation, locally constrained decoding, importance sampling, sample-rerank, and ablations of the SMC method (with and without resampling or expensive potentials). Evaluation metrics will be task-specific: test case accuracy for code, execution accuracy for SQL, goal matching for planning, and QED score for molecules. Posterior-weighted accuracy, KL divergence to the global product of experts, and correlation between particle weights and downstream performance will be reported. Experiments will be run with varying numbers of particles and compared to both open- and closed-source large models.
7874c6e5d7313a98b832918d5cb7f1b10ffea4fb.novelty_claims: The proposed framework enables the integration of both incrementally evaluable and costly, non-incremental constraints at inference time, overcoming limitations of locally constrained decoding and sample-rerank methods. The method introduces a programmable SMC architecture for controlled generation, supporting task-specific proposals and potentials without requiring model fine-tuning. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate that the approach allows smaller language models to outperform much larger and fine-tuned models, achieves better approximation to the desired posterior distribution, and provides significant gains in efficiency and accuracy across diverse domains. The probabilistic formulation and incremental inference are claimed to yield practical improvements in both performance and resource utilization.

78a2943fd2424a5515d595d6bdc54b9a4dbb4389.title: WPO: Enhancing RLHF with Weighted Preference Optimization
78a2943fd2424a5515d595d6bdc54b9a4dbb4389.research_question: How can preference optimization in reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) be improved to better align large language models (LLMs) with human values, particularly in settings where preference data is collected off-policy?
78a2943fd2424a5515d595d6bdc54b9a4dbb4389.hypothesis: Reweighting preference pairs in off-policy RLHF according to their probability under the current policy will mitigate the distributional gap between data collection and target policy, leading to more effective and efficient preference optimization without incurring additional costs.
78a2943fd2424a5515d595d6bdc54b9a4dbb4389.proposed_method: A novel Weighted Preference Optimization (WPO) framework will be developed to simulate on-policy learning using off-policy preference data. The method assigns weights to each preference pair based on the joint probability of their outputs under the current policy, prioritizing pairs more likely to be generated by the policy model. To address variance and ensure fair weighting, length-normalized sequence probabilities and token-level alignment techniques (such as sampled and greedy alignment) will be employed. The approach can be integrated with various loss functions for preference optimization and supports both paired and unpaired preference data. The method will be implemented efficiently to avoid the computational cost of active on-policy sampling during training.
78a2943fd2424a5515d595d6bdc54b9a4dbb4389.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on instruction-following benchmarks including AlpacaEval2 and MT-bench, using models such as Mistral-base, Llama-3-Instruct, and Gemma-2-9b-it. Both off-policy and hybrid RLHF settings will be evaluated, with preference data sourced from the Ultrafeedback dataset and additional on-policy samples generated as needed. Baseline methods will include Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), ORPO, KTO, SimPO, and other recent preference optimization algorithms. Evaluation metrics will comprise length-controlled win rates and pairwise win rates against GPT-4-turbo, as well as average scores from automated evaluators. Multiple random seeds will be used for statistical robustness, and ablation studies will assess the impact of different weighting and alignment strategies.
78a2943fd2424a5515d595d6bdc54b9a4dbb4389.novelty_claims: The proposed WPO method introduces a principled reweighting of off-policy preference data to closely simulate on-policy RLHF, effectively bridging the distributional gap without additional sampling costs. The approach is generalizable and can be incorporated into various preference optimization loss functions. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate significant improvements over state-of-the-art baselines, achieving new best results on standard alignment benchmarks. The analysis will also provide new insights into the relative importance of on-policy versus off-policy data, and the roles of preferred and dispreferred samples in preference optimization.

78c488e2d84bd193a40006b1fceb03e3845b81d4.title: Large Language Model as Attributed Training Data Generator: A Tale of Diversity and Bias
78c488e2d84bd193a40006b1fceb03e3845b81d4.research_question: How can the use of large language models as attributed training data generators improve the diversity and reduce the bias of synthetic datasets for high-cardinality text classification tasks, and what is the impact of such attributed data on downstream model performance, efficiency, and fairness?
78c488e2d84bd193a40006b1fceb03e3845b81d4.hypothesis: Incorporating diverse, explicitly controlled attribute prompts in large language model data generation will yield synthetic datasets with greater diversity and reduced bias, leading to improved downstream classification performance and efficiency compared to datasets generated with simple class-conditional prompts.
78c488e2d84bd193a40006b1fceb03e3845b81d4.proposed_method: A novel data generation framework will be developed that leverages large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, to create synthetic training data for text classification tasks using prompts enriched with multiple, carefully selected attribute dimensions (e.g., subtopic, length, style, location). The process begins with an interactive, semi-automated identification of relevant attribute dimensions and values for each dataset, using LLMs and human-in-the-loop selection. For class-dependent attributes, a filtering mechanism will be implemented to ensure attribute values are uniquely associated with their respective classes, reducing ambiguity. Synthetic data will be generated by randomly sampling valid attribute configurations and constructing prompts that instruct the LLM to generate text conforming to these attributes. The resulting attributed datasets will be used to train classification models, with comparisons made to models trained on data generated from simple class-conditional prompts and real data.
78c488e2d84bd193a40006b1fceb03e3845b81d4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four high-cardinality, multi-class text classification datasets from diverse domains: NYT (news, 26 classes), Amazon (product reviews, 23 classes), Reddit (user content, 45 classes), and StackExchange (Q&A, 50 classes), all exhibiting significant class imbalance. Synthetic datasets will be generated using both the proposed attributed prompt method and a baseline simple class-conditional prompt, with dataset sizes matched to the original training sets. Classifiers (primarily BERT-base-uncased, with additional experiments on TinyBERT, DistilBERT, DeBERTa-V3-base/large) will be fine-tuned on these datasets, and performance will be evaluated using accuracy and macro-F1 metrics. Additional evaluations will include diversity analysis (vocabulary size, average pairwise similarity, N-gram frequency), bias analysis (manual and classifier-based annotation of location attributes), budget/sample efficiency studies, and augmentation experiments where synthetic data is merged with real data. Comparisons will also be made across different LLM generators and prompt configurations.
78c488e2d84bd193a40006b1fceb03e3845b81d4.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a systematic, semi-automated method for generating attributed prompts that control multiple data attributes, enabling the creation of synthetic datasets with enhanced diversity and reduced bias. The method is applicable to black-box LLM APIs and does not require labeled seed data or white-box access. A novel class-dependent attribute value filtering mechanism is proposed to ensure attribute specificity. The framework is demonstrated to achieve superior downstream performance, greater budget and sample efficiency, and more balanced attribute distributions compared to existing prompt-based data generation methods. The approach is also shown to be robust across LLM sizes, classifier architectures, and is the first to extend LLM-based data generation to multi-label classification tasks with high cardinality.

78c51917366158513433f857cdaa5bce69798f61.title: AlignMixup: Improving Representations By Interpolating Aligned Features
78c51917366158513433f857cdaa5bce69798f61.research_question: How can data augmentation through interpolation between examples be improved to enhance representation learning, generalization, robustness, and calibration in deep neural networks for image classification and related tasks?
78c51917366158513433f857cdaa5bce69798f61.hypothesis: Interpolating between geometrically aligned feature representations of images, rather than raw inputs or unaligned features, will result in more semantically meaningful augmented data, leading to improved generalization, robustness to adversarial attacks, better calibration, and enhanced performance on downstream tasks such as weakly-supervised localization and out-of-distribution detection.
78c51917366158513433f857cdaa5bce69798f61.proposed_method: A novel data augmentation framework, AlignMixup, will be developed that operates by first extracting deep feature tensors from two images using a shared encoder network. These feature tensors are then geometrically aligned using optimal transport, specifically the Sinkhorn distance, to establish soft correspondences between spatial positions in the two tensors. The alignment process produces an assignment matrix that enables one feature tensor to be mapped onto the geometry of the other. Interpolation is then performed between the aligned feature tensors, with the option to retain the spatial structure (pose) of one image and the appearance (texture) of the other. The resulting mixed features are used for training the classifier, with corresponding mixed labels. Optionally, an autoencoder architecture can be incorporated, where a decoder is used to reconstruct images for visualization and to further enhance representation learning, though the classifier is never exposed to decoded images during training.
78c51917366158513433f857cdaa5bce69798f61.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification benchmarks, including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny ImageNet, and ImageNet, using backbone architectures such as PreActResNet-18, WideResNet-16-8, and ResNet-50. The proposed method will be compared against a comprehensive set of state-of-the-art mixup and data augmentation baselines, including Input Mixup, CutMix, Manifold Mixup, PuzzleMix, Co-Mixup, SaliencyMix, StyleMix, and StyleCutMix. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 classification error, robustness to adversarial attacks (FGSM and PGD), out-of-distribution detection performance (using AUROC, AUPR, and detection accuracy), and calibration measures. Additional experiments will assess weakly-supervised object localization using CUB200-2011, with localization accuracy and MaxBoxAcc-v2 as metrics. Ablation studies will investigate the effects of alignment, layer selection for mixing, autoencoder architectures, and alignment resolution. Computational overhead and scalability will also be analyzed.
78c51917366158513433f857cdaa5bce69798f61.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel mixup operation that interpolates between geometrically aligned feature tensors using optimal transport, rather than directly mixing raw inputs or unaligned features. This approach enables the generation of augmented examples that preserve the pose of one image and the texture of another, resulting in more semantically meaningful interpolations. The use of Sinkhorn distance for efficient feature alignment is a key innovation, allowing practical application to large-scale datasets. The framework also demonstrates that a simple autoencoder can further enhance representation learning under mixup without requiring the classifier to process decoded images. The method is expected to achieve state-of-the-art results across multiple benchmarks, including classification accuracy, robustness to adversarial attacks, calibration, out-of-distribution detection, and weakly-supervised localization, while maintaining competitive computational efficiency.

78d02f2909a582c624eca2d0f67c91ee91974180.title: DN-DETR: Accelerate DETR Training by Introducing Query DeNoising
78d02f2909a582c624eca2d0f67c91ee91974180.research_question: How can the training convergence of DETR-like object detection models be accelerated without sacrificing accuracy, and can a universal training strategy be developed to improve both transformer-based and CNN-based detection and segmentation architectures?
78d02f2909a582c624eca2d0f67c91ee91974180.hypothesis: Introducing a denoising training task that reconstructs ground-truth bounding boxes and labels from noised versions will stabilize bipartite graph matching, reduce optimization ambiguity, and accelerate convergence in DETR-like models, while also being applicable to other detection and segmentation architectures.
78d02f2909a582c624eca2d0f67c91ee91974180.proposed_method: A novel denoising training framework is proposed for DETR-like models. During training, noised versions of ground-truth (GT) bounding boxes and class labels are injected as auxiliary queries into the Transformer decoder alongside standard learnable queries. The model is trained to reconstruct the original GT boxes and labels from these noised inputs, using a combination of reconstruction loss (for the denoising queries) and the standard Hungarian loss (for the matching queries). Multiple groups of noised GT objects are generated per image, and attention masks are applied to prevent information leakage between denoising and matching queries as well as among denoising groups. The denoising task bypasses bipartite matching, providing a stable and easier optimization target, and can be flexibly adapted to models with 4D anchor boxes, 2D anchor points, or high-dimensional queries. The approach is also extended to CNN-based detectors (e.g., Faster R-CNN) and segmentation models (e.g., Mask2Former) by injecting noised GT boxes or masks into their respective heads or decoders.
78d02f2909a582c624eca2d0f67c91ee91974180.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the MS-COCO 2017 detection and segmentation benchmarks using various backbones (ResNet-50, ResNet-101, DC5 variants) and multiple DETR-like architectures (DAB-DETR, Deformable DETR, Anchor DETR, Vanilla DETR), as well as CNN-based (Faster R-CNN) and segmentation models (Mask2Former, MaskDINO). Standard mean average precision (AP) metrics are reported under different IoU thresholds and object scales. Baselines include state-of-the-art DETR variants and traditional detectors, with ablation studies performed to analyze the effect of denoising group count, noise scale, and attention masking. Training is performed with standard settings (12 and 50 epochs, AdamW optimizer, batch size 16, 8 GPUs), and the impact on convergence speed, stability of bipartite matching, and final accuracy is evaluated.
78d02f2909a582c624eca2d0f67c91ee91974180.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces denoising training as a universal, plug-and-play strategy for accelerating DETR-like model convergence, providing both faster training and improved accuracy. It offers a new perspective on the slow convergence problem by attributing it to instability in bipartite graph matching and demonstrates that denoising tasks can stabilize optimization. The approach is shown to be broadly applicable, improving not only transformer-based detectors but also CNN-based detectors and segmentation models, with minimal code changes and negligible computational overhead. Extensive experiments and ablations confirm its effectiveness and generalization across architectures.

790229e166e7ce2b7a013e764bd32559deb914b5.title: Analyzing Sharpness along GD Trajectory: Progressive Sharpening and Edge of Stability
