790229e166e7ce2b7a013e764bd32559deb914b5.research_question: What are the underlying dynamics and mechanisms that govern the evolution of sharpness (maximum Hessian eigenvalue) along the gradient descent trajectory in neural network training, particularly in the Edge of Stability (EOS) regime, and how can these be theoretically and empirically characterized?
790229e166e7ce2b7a013e764bd32559deb914b5.hypothesis: The norm of the output layer weight serves as a reliable indicator of sharpness dynamics during gradient descent, and the evolution of sharpness can be explained and predicted by analyzing the interplay between this norm, the loss, and the eigenstructure of the Gram (NTK) matrix. Furthermore, the sharpness behavior in the EOS regime can be theoretically justified under certain assumptions, especially in two-layer linear neural networks.
790229e166e7ce2b7a013e764bd32559deb914b5.proposed_method: A comprehensive analysis will be conducted on the dynamics of sharpness along the gradient descent trajectory by dividing the training process into four distinct phases based on the evolution of sharpness and loss. The methodology involves both empirical and theoretical approaches: empirically, the correlation between the norm of the output layer weights and sharpness will be investigated across various architectures (e.g., two-layer linear networks, deep fully-connected networks, ResNet18) and datasets (e.g., CIFAR-10). Theoretically, the dynamics of key quantities such as the residual vector, output layer norm, and Gram matrix eigenstructure will be analyzed, leveraging first-order approximations and assumptions about the spectrum and eigendirections of the Gram matrix. For two-layer linear networks, rigorous proofs will be developed to explain the progressive sharpening and EOS phenomena, relying on spectral properties of the data and network initialization.
790229e166e7ce2b7a013e764bd32559deb914b5.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed using gradient descent on neural networks of varying depth and architecture, including two-layer linear networks, deep tanh networks, and ResNet18. The primary dataset for empirical studies will be a subset of 1,000 samples from CIFAR-10, with binary classification and mean square error (MSE) loss. Key metrics to be tracked include the maximum eigenvalue of the Gram/NTK matrix (sharpness), the output layer norm, and training loss. Baselines will include classical gradient flow predictions and prior empirical observations of sharpness dynamics. The experimental setup will also involve tracking the evolution of the leading eigenvector and the decomposition of the residual vector to isolate the contributions to non-monotonic loss behavior.
790229e166e7ce2b7a013e764bd32559deb914b5.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a four-phase division of the gradient descent trajectory based on sharpness and loss dynamics, providing a new framework for understanding the EOS regime. It identifies and empirically validates the output layer norm as a surrogate for sharpness, offering a practical tool for monitoring and explaining sharpness evolution. Theoretical contributions include novel proofs of sharpness behavior in the EOS regime for two-layer linear networks under weaker or more natural assumptions than previous work. The approach also provides a new explanation for the non-monotonic decrease of loss in the EOS regime and offers detailed empirical and theoretical insights that extend beyond the neural tangent kernel (NTK) regime.

790ea537eb8c7dfaa45d0b42484cd1af7efdcac0.title: A Best-of-Both-Worlds Algorithm for Bandits with Delayed Feedback
790ea537eb8c7dfaa45d0b42484cd1af7efdcac0.research_question: How can an algorithm for multi-armed bandits with delayed feedback be designed to achieve near-optimal regret guarantees in both stochastic and adversarial environments, without prior knowledge of the environment type, and under both fixed and arbitrary delay scenarios?
790ea537eb8c7dfaa45d0b42484cd1af7efdcac0.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a Follow The Regularized Leader (FTRL) algorithm with a hybrid regularizer and appropriately tuned, time-varying learning rates can achieve minimax optimal regret in adversarial regimes and near-optimal regret in stochastic regimes for multi-armed bandits with delayed feedback, even when delays are arbitrary and only the maximal delay is known.
790ea537eb8c7dfaa45d0b42484cd1af7efdcac0.proposed_method: A new algorithm is proposed based on the Follow The Regularized Leader (FTRL) framework, utilizing a hybrid regularizer that combines negative Tsallis entropy and negative entropy, each with separate, time-dependent learning rates. The algorithm dynamically adjusts its learning rates according to the number of outstanding delayed feedbacks and the maximal delay, which is assumed to be known via an oracle. At each round, the learner updates its distribution over arms using the FTRL rule with the hybrid regularizer and incorporates delayed feedback as it arrives, updating loss estimates via importance weighting. A key technical component is a general lemma that tightly bounds the drift of the playing distribution induced by delays and time-varying regularization, enabling the use of the self-bounding technique for stochastic analysis. The method is further extended to handle arbitrary delay sequences by leveraging the maximal outstanding delay in the learning rate schedule.
790ea537eb8c7dfaa45d0b42484cd1af7efdcac0.experiment_details: The proposed algorithm will be evaluated theoretically and empirically on both stochastic and adversarial multi-armed bandit problems with delayed feedback. Theoretical analysis will derive regret bounds for both fixed and arbitrary delay settings, comparing against known lower bounds and prior algorithms such as the skipping technique and FTRL with fixed regularizers. Empirical experiments will use synthetic datasets with controlled delay patterns (fixed, uniform, and arbitrary delays) and compare the regret of the proposed method to existing baselines, including EXP3 variants and Tsallis-INF, under both stochastic and adversarial loss generation. Evaluation metrics will include pseudo-regret over a fixed time horizon, with particular attention to the impact of delay magnitude and distribution.
790ea537eb8c7dfaa45d0b42484cd1af7efdcac0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a best-of-both-worlds algorithm for bandits with delayed feedback, achieving minimax optimal regret in adversarial regimes and near-optimal regret in stochastic regimes, even with arbitrary delays and only oracle knowledge of the maximal delay. A novel analytic lemma is developed to control the drift of the playing distribution under time-varying hybrid regularization and delays, enabling the application of self-bounding techniques in the delayed setting. The method provides regret bounds that improve or match existing upper and lower bounds, and in particular, the adversarial regret lower bound matches the refined upper bound achieved by the skipping technique. The approach also demonstrates improved dependence on the number of outstanding observations in the stochastic regime, and identifies scenarios where the maximal outstanding observations can be much smaller than the maximal delay.

7918ff88695fe7894a972758533e23f09113ea68.title: From Stars to Subgraphs: Uplifting Any GNN with Local Structure Awareness
7918ff88695fe7894a972758533e23f09113ea68.research_question: How can the expressive power of graph neural networks (GNNs), particularly message passing neural networks (MPNNs), be enhanced to capture richer local structural information while maintaining scalability and practical efficiency for large-scale graph learning tasks?
7918ff88695fe7894a972758533e23f09113ea68.hypothesis: Encoding node representations using induced local subgraphs, rather than only immediate neighbors, and leveraging a GNN as a subgraph encoder will significantly increase the expressive power of any base GNN beyond the 1st- and 2nd-order Weisfeiler-Leman (WL) isomorphism test, while maintaining manageable computational and memory overhead.
7918ff88695fe7894a972758533e23f09113ea68.proposed_method: A general framework, termed GNN-As-Kernel (GNN-AK), will be developed to uplift any base GNN by replacing the standard star-shaped neighbor aggregation with aggregation over induced local subgraphs (e.g., k-hop egonets) centered at each node. For each node, a subgraph is extracted and encoded using a GNN, producing node embeddings that are then aggregated to form updated node representations. An enhanced version, GNN-AK+, will incorporate additional context encodings and distance-to-centroid (D2C) features, as well as gating mechanisms to modulate the influence of nodes within subgraphs based on their distance from the centroid. Subgraph sampling strategies, including random-walk-based extraction and SubgraphDrop (a dropout-inspired subgraph sampling during training), will be designed to reduce memory and runtime overhead while preserving performance.
7918ff88695fe7894a972758533e23f09113ea68.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world graph datasets. Synthetic datasets include EXP (pairs of 1&2-WL indistinguishable graphs), SR25 (3-WL indistinguishable graphs), substructure counting, and graph property regression tasks. Real-world benchmarks include ZINC-12K, CIFAR10, PATTERN, MolHIV, and MolPCBA, as well as smaller datasets from the TUDataset collection. The proposed method will be evaluated using standard metrics such as accuracy, mean absolute error (MAE), and ROC-AUC. Baselines will include standard GNN architectures (GCN, GIN, PNA, PPGN) as well as recent state-of-the-art models (GatedGCN, DGN, GSN, HIMP, CIN). Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of subgraph size, encoding strategies, and subgraph sampling. Resource usage (runtime and memory) will also be measured to evaluate scalability.
7918ff88695fe7894a972758533e23f09113ea68.novelty_claims: The proposed framework provides a general, plug-and-play method to uplift the expressiveness of any GNN by encoding local subgraph structure, bridging the gap between highly scalable but less expressive MPNNs and highly expressive but unscalable higher-order GNNs. Theoretical analysis establishes that the method is strictly more powerful than 1- and 2-WL and not less powerful than 3-WL under certain conditions. The introduction of SubgraphDrop enables significant reductions in memory and runtime overhead without sacrificing performance. Empirical results demonstrate consistent and significant improvements in both expressiveness and practical performance, achieving new state-of-the-art results on several benchmark graph learning tasks.

792077c9c27fb910db5ec0c9fbcb53f433251678.title: Proximal Learning With Opponent-Learning Awareness
792077c9c27fb910db5ec0c9fbcb53f433251678.research_question: How can reciprocity-based cooperation be more reliably learned by autonomous agents in partially competitive multi-agent reinforcement learning environments, particularly when using complex policy parameterizations and opponent modeling?
792077c9c27fb910db5ec0c9fbcb53f433251678.hypothesis: A proximal operator-based update rule that is invariant to policy parameterization will enable agents to more reliably learn reciprocity-based cooperation in multi-agent reinforcement learning settings, outperforming existing approaches such as LOLA, especially in environments requiring function approximation and opponent modeling.
792077c9c27fb910db5ec0c9fbcb53f433251678.proposed_method: A new algorithm, Proximal LOLA (POLA), will be developed by directly formulating the policy update as a proximal operator in policy space, rather than relying on parameter-space gradients as in LOLA. The method will define each agent's update as the solution to a regularized optimization problem that minimizes the agent's loss plus a divergence penalty between the updated and current policies, ensuring invariance to policy parameterization. Practical approximations to the ideal POLA update will be implemented: (1) OuterPOLA, which uses first-order approximations and iterative gradient steps to approximate the fixed point of the proximal objective, and (2) POLA-DiCE, a policy gradient version that leverages sample-based estimation and higher-order derivatives via the DiCE framework, suitable for environments where analytical gradients are unavailable. Both with and without opponent modeling, agents will use learned models of opponents when direct access to opponent policy parameters is not possible, applying supervised learning to infer opponent policies from observed actions.
792077c9c27fb910db5ec0c9fbcb53f433251678.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in several partially competitive multi-agent environments. These include the Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma (IPD) with one-step memory (using tabular and neural network policies), the full-history IPD (using GRU-based policies), and the Coin Game (a grid-based social dilemma with GRU policies). Baselines will include Naive Learning and LOLA (both tabular and function approximation variants), as well as LOLA-DiCE. Evaluation metrics will focus on the frequency of learning reciprocity-based cooperation (e.g., tit-for-tat strategies), average agent rewards, and the proportion of cooperative actions. Experiments will be run both with direct access to opponent policies and under opponent modeling, where agents must infer opponent policies from observed actions. Multiple random seeds and hyperparameter sweeps will be used to ensure robustness, and statistical confidence intervals will be reported.
792077c9c27fb910db5ec0c9fbcb53f433251678.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a parameterization-invariant update rule for multi-agent reinforcement learning, addressing a previously unidentified sensitivity in LOLA to policy parameterization. By reinterpreting LOLA as an approximation to a proximal operator and directly formulating the update in policy space, the method ensures that behaviorally equivalent policies yield equivalent updates, even under opponent modeling. Practical algorithms are developed to approximate the ideal update in both analytical and sample-based settings, and empirical results demonstrate that the method achieves reciprocity-based cooperation more reliably than existing approaches across a range of environments and policy representations.

79210ff50026bde04aefb80b3960827b637c2600.title: Scalable Unbalanced Sobolev Transport for Measures on a Graph
79210ff50026bde04aefb80b3960827b637c2600.research_question: How can a scalable and efficient transport distance be developed for comparing measures with unequal total mass supported on a general graph metric space, while addressing computational complexity and definiteness issues inherent in existing optimal transport approaches?
79210ff50026bde04aefb80b3960827b637c2600.hypothesis: A novel unbalanced Sobolev transport (UST) framework, leveraging graph-based Sobolev spaces and closed-form solutions, will enable fast, scalable, and theoretically well-founded comparison of measures with unequal mass on graphs, while providing negative definiteness and supporting the construction of positive definite kernels.
79210ff50026bde04aefb80b3960827b637c2600.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces unbalanced Sobolev transport (UST), a new class of transport distances for measures with unequal mass supported on a graph metric space. UST is formulated by relaxing the dual constraints of the entropy partial transport (EPT) problem, replacing the Lipschitz constraint with a graph-based Sobolev space constraint and relaxing the boundedness constraint to only require control at the root node. The method defines a critic function in the Sobolev space W^{1,p'}(G, ω) with bounded graph derivative, and derives a closed-form solution for the UST distance in terms of integrals over the graph structure, specifically involving the difference of cumulative measures along shortest paths from the root. The approach supports efficient computation by leveraging preprocessing steps (e.g., shortest path calculations) and is applicable to both physical and non-physical graphs, with flexibility in the choice of the ground cost measure ω.
79210ff50026bde04aefb80b3960827b637c2600.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both high-dimensional (document classification) and low-dimensional (topological data analysis) datasets, where measures of unequal mass are naturally represented (e.g., documents of varying lengths, persistence diagrams with different numbers of features). Graph structures are constructed over the supports, and the proposed UST is compared against established unbalanced optimal transport (UOT) baselines, including Sinkhorn-based UOT and EPT on trees. Evaluation metrics include classification accuracy using SVMs with kernels derived from the transport distances, as well as computational time for kernel matrix construction. Multiple graph settings (e.g., varying number of nodes, different graph types) and sliced variants (averaging over multiple root nodes) are explored to assess scalability, robustness, and performance trade-offs.
79210ff50026bde04aefb80b3960827b637c2600.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first scalable unbalanced Sobolev transport distance for measures with unequal mass on general graphs, providing a closed-form solution that enables fast computation even for large-scale problems. The method generalizes previous approaches limited to trees or balanced measures, and establishes negative definiteness of the distance, which supports the construction of positive definite kernels for kernel-based machine learning methods. Theoretical contributions include new geometric structures, dual formulations, and explicit relations to other transport distances. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate both computational efficiency and competitive or superior performance compared to state-of-the-art unbalanced transport baselines.

793939b83e10903f58d8edbb7534963df627a1fe.title: Latent-NeRF for Shape-Guided Generation of 3D Shapes and Textures
793939b83e10903f58d8edbb7534963df627a1fe.research_question: How can 3D shape and texture generation be effectively guided by both text and explicit shape constraints, leveraging latent diffusion models for efficient and controllable synthesis?
793939b83e10903f58d8edbb7534963df627a1fe.hypothesis: Incorporating shape-guidance mechanisms, such as coarse geometric sketches or explicit mesh parameterizations, into a latent diffusion-based 3D generation framework will enable more precise and controllable synthesis of 3D shapes and textures from text prompts, while maintaining computational efficiency and high visual fidelity.
793939b83e10903f58d8edbb7534963df627a1fe.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed wherein a Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) is trained to operate directly in the latent space of a pretrained Latent Diffusion Model (LDM), thus avoiding repeated encoding steps and improving computational efficiency. The method introduces two primary forms of shape guidance: (1) Sketch-Shape guidance, where a coarse 3D geometry (composed of simple primitives) is used to softly constrain the occupancy of the NeRF during optimization, allowing the generated shape to adhere to a user-defined structure while still being refined by text-driven score distillation; and (2) Latent-Paint, where a given 3D mesh with UV parameterization is textured by optimizing a latent texture map via score distillation, propagating gradients through a differentiable renderer. Additionally, a linear mapping enables conversion of the latent NeRF to RGB space for further refinement, allowing optional fine-tuning in pixel space.
793939b83e10903f58d8edbb7534963df627a1fe.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using the Stable Diffusion model (v1-4) as the LDM, with Instant-NGP as the NeRF backbone. The framework is evaluated on a variety of text-to-3D and texture generation tasks, including unconstrained text prompts, Sketch-Shape guidance with user-defined coarse meshes, and Latent-Paint for explicit mesh texturing. Baselines for qualitative comparison include DreamFusion, DreamFields, CLIPMesh, and Tango. Evaluation focuses on visual fidelity, consistency across viewpoints, controllability of shape and texture, and computational efficiency (e.g., convergence time on a V100 GPU). Ablation studies are performed on the strength of shape constraints, and the effectiveness of RGB refinement is assessed.
793939b83e10903f58d8edbb7534963df627a1fe.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to bring NeRF-based 3D generation fully into the latent space of a diffusion model, enabling efficient score distillation without repeated encoding. It introduces a unique combination of text and shape guidance, allowing for both coarse and fine-grained control over 3D shape and texture synthesis. The method also demonstrates, for the first time, direct application of latent score distillation to mesh texture generation, and provides a practical linear mapping for seamless transition between latent and RGB NeRF representations. The framework achieves significant computational speedup and improved controllability compared to prior text-to-3D generation methods.

79531b47bb27cb18022891eb2ab1fcb41745fca6.title: Practical and Asymptotically Exact Conditional Sampling in Diffusion Models
79531b47bb27cb18022891eb2ab1fcb41745fca6.research_question: How can conditional sampling from diffusion models be made both practical and asymptotically exact, enabling accurate conditional generation across a wide range of tasks without requiring task-specific conditional training?
79531b47bb27cb18022891eb2ab1fcb41745fca6.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) approach, leveraging twisting functions to approximate optimal proposals and weights, can enable asymptotically exact conditional sampling from unconditional diffusion models, outperforming heuristic and task-specific methods across diverse conditional generation tasks.
79531b47bb27cb18022891eb2ab1fcb41745fca6.proposed_method: A new algorithm, Twisted Diffusion Sampler (TDS), is developed to perform conditional sampling from diffusion models using a sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) framework. The method constructs a set of weighted particles that evolve through the diffusion process, with proposals and weights modified by twisting functions that approximate the optimal conditional distributions. The twisting functions are computed using the denoising predictions of the diffusion model, allowing for tractable and differentiable approximations of otherwise intractable conditional likelihoods. The algorithm is extended to handle inpainting, flexible conditioning criteria (such as degrees of freedom in motif placement), and Riemannian manifold diffusion models by adapting the twisting functions and proposal distributions accordingly. Theoretical guarantees are provided, showing that the weighted particle approximation converges to the true conditional distribution as the number of particles increases.
79531b47bb27cb18022891eb2ab1fcb41745fca6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic data, class-conditional image generation, image inpainting, and protein motif-scaffolding tasks. Datasets include MNIST, ImageNet, CIFAR-10, and a benchmark set of protein design problems. Baselines for comparison include importance sampling (IS), gradient guidance, the replacement method, SMC-Diff, and state-of-the-art conditionally trained models such as RFdiffusion. Evaluation metrics include estimation error of conditional means, classification accuracy of generated samples, and success rates in protein motif-scaffolding. The number of particles in the SMC sampler will be varied to study the computational-statistical trade-off, and ablation studies will be performed on degrees of freedom and twist scale parameters. The experimental setup includes using pre-trained diffusion models and classifiers, and for protein design, both contiguous and non-contiguous motif placements as well as rotational and translational degrees of freedom are considered.
79531b47bb27cb18022891eb2ab1fcb41745fca6.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first practical and asymptotically exact SMC algorithm for conditional sampling in diffusion models that does not require task-specific conditional training. The approach generalizes to a broad range of conditioning tasks, including those with flexible or non-differentiable constraints, and extends to Riemannian diffusion models. The use of tractable twisting functions based on denoising network predictions enables efficient and accurate approximation of optimal proposals and weights. The method provides theoretical guarantees of convergence to the true conditional distribution and demonstrates empirical improvements over existing heuristic and conditionally trained approaches, particularly in challenging tasks such as protein motif-scaffolding with flexible conditioning criteria.

7985e019694318d12c52cc03ee2adef36845059c.title: ConfPO: Exploiting Policy Model Confidence for Critical Token Selection in Preference Optimization
7985e019694318d12c52cc03ee2adef36845059c.research_question: How can preference optimization in large language models be improved by selectively focusing on tokens that are most critical for aligning with human preferences, without incurring additional computational overhead or relying on auxiliary models?
7985e019694318d12c52cc03ee2adef36845059c.hypothesis: Selective optimization of low-confidence tokens—identified via the policy model's own probability estimates—will improve alignment with human preferences and mitigate overoptimization, compared to uniform optimization over all tokens.
7985e019694318d12c52cc03ee2adef36845059c.proposed_method: A new approach, termed Confidence-guided Preference Optimization (ConfPO), is proposed to enhance preference learning in large language models by selectively updating only those tokens deemed critical based on the policy model's internal confidence scores. The method computes the model's probability for each token in a response and selects tokens whose predicted probability falls below the sequence average, marking them as low-confidence and thus more informative for preference alignment. The preference optimization objective is modified to include only these selected tokens in the reward calculation, while maintaining the same computational cost as standard direct alignment algorithms. The approach does not require auxiliary models, external annotations, or additional inference passes, and can be seamlessly integrated into existing direct alignment frameworks such as SimPO or DPO.
7985e019694318d12c52cc03ee2adef36845059c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using both base and instruction-tuned variants of Mistral-7B and Llama-3-8B models, initially fine-tuned with supervised data and then further optimized with preference data from the UltraFeedback dataset. Evaluation will be performed on challenging alignment benchmarks, including AlpacaEval2 and Arena-Hard, using metrics such as win rate (WR) and length-controlled win rate (LC) with GPT-4 Turbo as the annotator. Baselines for comparison will include a range of direct alignment algorithms (e.g., DPO, SimPO, RRHF, SLiC-HF, IPO, CPO, KTO, ORPO, R-DPO), and ablation studies will assess the impact of random token selection and the proportion of tokens selected. Overoptimization will be evaluated by plotting human alignment versus KL divergence across different KL budgets.
7985e019694318d12c52cc03ee2adef36845059c.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple, lightweight, and model-free strategy for critical token selection in preference optimization, relying solely on the policy model's own confidence scores. This approach eliminates the need for auxiliary models, external annotations, or additional computation, and enables more efficient use of the KL divergence budget. Empirical and theoretical analyses demonstrate that low-confidence tokens disproportionately drive preference alignment, and selective optimization of these tokens leads to improved alignment performance and reduced overoptimization compared to uniform token optimization. The method is broadly applicable to existing direct alignment algorithms and achieves superior results on standard alignment benchmarks.

79926aa63d4daee6af06a8e9a7c2480b31cb7ed9.title: Spanish Pre-trained BERT Model and Evaluation Data
79926aa63d4daee6af06a8e9a7c2480b31cb7ed9.research_question: How can a pre-trained language model specifically tailored for the Spanish language improve performance on a range of natural language processing tasks compared to existing multilingual models, and how can standardized evaluation resources be developed for Spanish NLP?
79926aa63d4daee6af06a8e9a7c2480b31cb7ed9.hypothesis: A BERT-based language model pre-trained exclusively on a large, diverse Spanish corpus will outperform multilingual BERT models on a variety of Spanish NLP tasks, and the creation of a unified Spanish benchmark will facilitate more consistent evaluation and progress in Spanish NLP.
79926aa63d4daee6af06a8e9a7c2480b31cb7ed9.proposed_method: A BERT-Base architecture will be pre-trained from scratch using only Spanish-language data, including Wikipedia and multiple OPUS Project sources, resulting in a corpus of approximately 3 billion words. Both cased and uncased versions will be trained, each with 12 self-attention layers, 12 attention heads per layer, a hidden size of 768, and a vocabulary of 32,000 subwords constructed via byte pair encoding. Training will incorporate dynamic masking (10x per sentence) and whole-word masking, with a two-phase training schedule: initial 900k steps with batch size 2048 and sequence length 128, followed by the remainder with batch size 256 and sequence length 512, for a total of 2 million steps using TPU v3-8 hardware. The resulting models will be fine-tuned for downstream tasks using task-specific output layers and standard optimization techniques.
79926aa63d4daee6af06a8e9a7c2480b31cb7ed9.experiment_details: Evaluation will be conducted on a newly compiled Spanish benchmark, GLUES, which includes tasks such as natural language inference (XNLI), paraphrase identification (PAWS-X), named entity recognition (CoNLL-2002), part-of-speech tagging (Universal Dependencies v1.4), document classification (MLDoc), dependency parsing (Universal Dependencies v2.2), and question answering (MLQA, TAR, XQuAD). Each task will use its standard train, development, and test splits, with evaluation metrics including accuracy, F1 score, unlabeled/labeled attachment score, and exact match as appropriate. The Spanish BERT models will be compared against multilingual BERT (mBERT) baselines, with fine-tuning performed using only Spanish training data. Hyperparameters such as batch size, learning rate, and number of epochs will be selected from recommended values, and fine-tuning will use a sliding window approach for long sequences.
79926aa63d4daee6af06a8e9a7c2480b31cb7ed9.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first publicly available BERT model pre-trained exclusively on Spanish-language data, along with an open-source, large-scale Spanish corpus and a unified Spanish NLP benchmark (GLUES) for evaluation. The approach leverages advanced pre-training techniques such as dynamic and whole-word masking tailored to Spanish. The resulting models are expected to set new state-of-the-art results on several Spanish NLP tasks, providing a valuable resource for the Spanish-speaking NLP community and enabling more standardized and reproducible research.

79a8df9f247c25c7975245608215f38bdc719fba.title: High-probability minimax lower bounds
79a8df9f247c25c7975245608215f38bdc719fba.research_question: How can minimax lower bounds in statistical estimation be extended to provide high-probability (quantile-based) guarantees, and what is the dependence of such minimax quantiles on the quantile level across a range of statistical estimation problems?
79a8df9f247c25c7975245608215f38bdc719fba.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that minimax quantiles, which provide high-probability lower bounds on estimation loss, can be systematically characterized and bounded using extensions of classical information-theoretic techniques (such as Le Cam's and Fano's methods), and that these bounds will yield a finer-grained understanding of statistical problem difficulty than traditional minimax risk.
79a8df9f247c25c7975245608215f38bdc719fba.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed that replaces the classical minimax risk (expectation-based) with minimax quantiles, focusing on the (1-b4)th quantile of the loss distribution. High-probability variants of classical lower bound techniques, including Le Cam's two-point lemma and Fano's inequality, will be derived and adapted to provide lower bounds on minimax quantiles. Additionally, a reduction technique will be introduced to convert local minimax risk lower bounds into lower bounds on minimax quantiles, enabling the application of tools such as Assouad's lemma. The framework will be formalized for general loss functions and parameter spaces, including heavy-tailed and contamination models, and will provide both upper and lower bounds on minimax quantiles that are tight up to universal constants.
79a8df9f247c25c7975245608215f38bdc719fba.experiment_details: The proposed methodology will be applied to a suite of canonical statistical estimation problems, including multivariate mean estimation (Gaussian and robust settings), covariance matrix estimation, sparse linear regression, nonparametric density estimation, isotonic regression, and stochastic convex optimization. For each problem, explicit expressions for minimax quantiles will be derived and compared to known upper bounds, ensuring tightness up to multiplicative constants. The evaluation will use standard statistical datasets and synthetic data generated according to the specified models, with performance assessed in terms of the minimax quantile at various confidence levels (b4). Baseline comparisons will include classical minimax risk bounds and existing high-probability results where available.
79a8df9f247c25c7975245608215f38bdc719fba.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first systematic framework for high-probability minimax lower bounds via minimax quantiles, extending classical information-theoretic techniques to the quantile setting. It provides user-friendly, general-purpose tools for deriving lower bounds on minimax quantiles across a wide range of statistical problems, and demonstrates that these bounds can match upper bounds up to universal constants. The approach yields a more nuanced, quantile-dependent understanding of estimator performance and problem difficulty, addressing information loss inherent in expectation-based minimax risk and enabling sharper justifications for statistical procedures under high-probability guarantees.

79b4560fa0542b6c04f037ac8b69e4fe450da093.title: Training Dynamics of In-Context Learning in Linear Attention
79b4560fa0542b6c04f037ac8b69e4fe450da093.research_question: How do different parametrizations of linear attention architectures, specifically with merged versus separate key and query matrices, influence the training dynamics and acquisition of in-context learning abilities during gradient descent on in-context linear regression tasks?
79b4560fa0542b6c04f037ac8b69e4fe450da093.hypothesis: The parametrization of key and query matrices in linear attention models fundamentally alters the training dynamics, leading to distinct patterns in the emergence and evolution of in-context learning abilities. Specifically, merged key-query parametrizations will exhibit abrupt acquisition of ICL through a single loss drop, while separate key and query parametrizations will display progressive acquisition via multiple loss drops corresponding to principal component regression.
79b4560fa0542b6c04f037ac8b69e4fe450da093.proposed_method: A theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted on multi-head linear attention models trained via gradient descent on in-context linear regression tasks. Two key parametrizations will be studied: (i) merged key and query matrices (common in theoretical studies), and (ii) separate key and query matrices (closer to practical transformer implementations). Analytical derivations will characterize the loss landscapes, fixed points, and training trajectories for both parametrizations, leveraging connections to deep linear networks and convolutional architectures. Theoretical predictions will be validated through simulations, and the dynamics will be reduced to tractable ordinary differential equations where possible. The analysis will be extended to models with varying rank for key and query matrices, and empirical comparisons will be made to softmax attention variants.
79b4560fa0542b6c04f037ac8b69e4fe450da093.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training multi-head linear attention models on synthetic in-context linear regression datasets, where input tokens are sampled from zero-mean Gaussian distributions with specified covariance. Both merged and separate key-query parametrizations will be evaluated, with varying numbers of heads, input dimensions, and key/query ranks. Baselines will include fully-connected linear networks and convolutional linear networks with equivalent feature maps. Evaluation metrics will focus on loss trajectories, abruptness and number of loss drops, alignment of learned weights with data principal components, and the correspondence between theoretical predictions and empirical results. Additional experiments will compare the observed dynamics in linear attention to those in softmax attention models.
79b4560fa0542b6c04f037ac8b69e4fe450da093.novelty_claims: The proposed research provides a comprehensive theoretical and empirical characterization of how linear attention models acquire in-context learning abilities during training, revealing that parametrization (merged vs. separate key-query) fundamentally changes the training dynamics. The work introduces analytical solutions for loss trajectories, identifies exponentially many fixed points in the separate parametrization, and demonstrates that progressive principal component regression emerges in the separate case. The approach also establishes a novel equivalence between linear attention and deep linear/convolutional networks, enabling the application of established theoretical tools. The findings extend to softmax attention and highlight the critical role of parametrization in shaping the evolution of ICL abilities, motivating future research to account for these architectural choices.

79be1c87f3b9e047e10912c5a707c87a69c5dc05.title: TokenSkip: Controllable Chain-of-Thought Compression in LLMs
79be1c87f3b9e047e10912c5a707c87a69c5dc05.research_question: How can the efficiency of chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning in large language models be improved by reducing token redundancy, while maintaining strong reasoning performance and controllable compression ratios?
79be1c87f3b9e047e10912c5a707c87a69c5dc05.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that not all tokens in CoT outputs contribute equally to reasoning, and selectively skipping less important tokens can significantly compress CoT sequences without substantial loss in reasoning accuracy.
79be1c87f3b9e047e10912c5a707c87a69c5dc05.proposed_method: A novel approach, TokenSkip, is proposed to enable large language models to skip tokens with low semantic importance during chain-of-thought reasoning, thereby achieving controllable CoT compression. The method first computes token importance scores for each token in the CoT trajectory using a bidirectional language model (such as LLMLingua-2), which is trained to classify tokens as important or not based on GPT-4-labeled data. For each training sample, a compression ratio is randomly selected, and tokens below the corresponding importance quantile are pruned, producing a compressed CoT sequence. The target LLM is then fine-tuned using these compressed CoTs, with the compression ratio included as part of the input, enabling the model to learn to generate compressed reasoning chains at inference time for any desired compression ratio. During inference, the model receives both the question and the desired compression ratio, and generates a compressed CoT by skipping tokens deemed less important, thus improving efficiency.
79be1c87f3b9e047e10912c5a707c87a69c5dc05.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-Instruct series models on two widely recognized math reasoning benchmarks: GSM8K and MATH-500. The training data consists of CoT trajectories generated by the target LLMs, with incorrect-answer samples filtered out. Token importance is computed using LLMLingua-2, and compression ratios are sampled from a set (e.g., {0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0}) for each training sample. Baselines for comparison include token-efficient prompts, length-control prompts, and brute-force truncation. Evaluation metrics include accuracy, average number of CoT tokens, inference latency per sample, and actual compression ratio. Greedy decoding is used for output generation, and inference latency is measured on a single NVIDIA 3090 GPU. Additional analyses include out-of-domain generalization and ablation on token importance metrics.
79be1c87f3b9e047e10912c5a707c87a69c5dc05.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to investigate controllable CoT compression via token skipping based on semantic importance within CoT trajectories. TokenSkip introduces a simple yet effective framework that enables LLMs to learn shortcuts between critical reasoning tokens, facilitating adjustable CoT compression ratios while preserving interpretability and reasoning performance. The approach achieves substantial reductions in CoT token usage and inference latency with minimal performance drop, and demonstrates superior adherence to desired compression ratios compared to existing prompt-based and truncation baselines. The method is also characterized by low training cost and high reproducibility, making it practical for efficient LLM deployment.

79eb8bd272cdffc213c7d3dee3da2deef13d3626.title: Can Neural Network Memorization Be Localized?
79eb8bd272cdffc213c7d3dee3da2deef13d3626.research_question: Can the phenomenon of memorization in deep neural networks be localized to specific components within the network, such as particular layers or neurons, and can this localization be leveraged to control or mitigate memorization effects?
79eb8bd272cdffc213c7d3dee3da2deef13d3626.hypothesis: Memorization in deep neural networks is not confined to the final layers but is instead distributed across a small subset of neurons throughout various layers, and it is possible to intentionally direct memorization to predetermined neurons using targeted interventions.
79eb8bd272cdffc213c7d3dee3da2deef13d3626.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical study will be conducted to investigate the localization of memorization in deep neural networks. The methodology will include gradient accounting to measure the contribution of clean and memorized examples to gradient norms at each layer, layer rewinding to assess the functional criticality of individual layers by resetting their weights to earlier checkpoints, and layer retraining to determine redundancy in memorization by retraining specific layers on clean data only. Additionally, neuron-level analysis will be performed using a gradient-based greedy search to identify the minimal set of neurons responsible for memorized predictions. Building on these insights, a novel example-tied dropout mechanism will be developed, where a subset of neurons is designated as 'memorization neurons' for specific examples, and these neurons can be selectively dropped during evaluation to control memorization.
79eb8bd272cdffc213c7d3dee3da2deef13d3626.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification datasets including CIFAR-10, MNIST, and SVHN, with models such as ResNet-9, ResNet-50, and Vision Transformer (ViT-small). Training will utilize stochastic gradient descent with a one-cycle learning rate schedule, and 10% label noise will be introduced to operationalize memorization. Baseline comparisons will include standard dropout and sparse networks with equivalent parameter counts. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on clean, noisy (memorized), and test examples, as well as the area under the curve (AUC) for identifying mislabeled examples. Experiments will systematically analyze the impact of interventions at both the layer and neuron levels, and the efficacy of example-tied dropout in localizing and mitigating memorization will be benchmarked against existing methods.
79eb8bd272cdffc213c7d3dee3da2deef13d3626.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a detailed, multi-level analysis of memorization localization in neural networks, challenging the prevailing assumption that memorization is confined to the final layers. It claims that memorization can be traced to a small, distributed set of neurons across layers, rather than specific layers. The proposed example-tied dropout mechanism is novel in its ability to direct memorization to predetermined neurons, enabling targeted removal of memorized information with minimal impact on generalization. This approach provides new insights for privacy, machine unlearning, and training with noisy data, and offers a practical tool for controlling memorization in deep learning models.

7a0f9a591fbb8b224e385351256b61c7a54be8f9.title: How Far is Video Generation from World Model: A Physical Law Perspective
7a0f9a591fbb8b224e385351256b61c7a54be8f9.research_question: Can large-scale video generation models, when trained solely on visual data, develop an understanding of fundamental physical laws and generalize to novel physical scenarios, including out-of-distribution and combinatorial cases?
7a0f9a591fbb8b224e385351256b61c7a54be8f9.hypothesis: Scaling video generation models and datasets will improve their ability to generalize within the training distribution and in combinatorial settings, but may not be sufficient for robust out-of-distribution generalization or for discovering universal physical laws from vision alone.
7a0f9a591fbb8b224e385351256b61c7a54be8f9.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation framework will be established to systematically assess the capacity of diffusion-based video generation models to learn and generalize physical laws. The approach will involve constructing a controlled 2D simulation environment where object motions and interactions are deterministically governed by classical mechanics (e.g., uniform linear motion, elastic collision, parabolic motion). Videos will be generated using this simulator, with initial frames provided as conditioning inputs to the video generation models. The models will utilize a (2+1)D Variational Auto-Encoder (VAE) for spatiotemporal compression, followed by a DiT (Diffusion Transformer) architecture for denoising and frame prediction. The evaluation will focus on three generalization regimes: in-distribution (ID), out-of-distribution (OOD), and combinatorial generalization, with model and data scaling systematically varied.
7a0f9a591fbb8b224e385351256b61c7a54be8f9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic datasets generated from the 2D simulator, covering three fundamental physical scenarios: uniform linear motion, perfectly elastic collision, and parabolic motion. Training datasets will be scaled from 30,000 to 3 million examples, and model sizes will range from 22M to 310M parameters (DiT-S to DiT-L). For combinatorial generalization, environments with multiple object types will be created, and training/test splits will be made over combinations of object types (e.g., using 60 out of 70 possible combinations for training and the rest for testing). Evaluation metrics will include velocity and position errors (parsed from generated videos), Frechet Video Distance (FVD), SSIM, PSNR, LPIPS, and human evaluation of physical plausibility. Baseline comparisons will be made to ground-truth simulation data. Additional experiments will probe the models’ interpolation/extrapolation abilities and attribute prioritization in generalization.
7a0f9a591fbb8b224e385351256b61c7a54be8f9.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a systematic, scalable framework for evaluating the physical law discovery capabilities of video generation models, focusing on their generalization across in-distribution, out-of-distribution, and combinatorial scenarios. It develops a controlled synthetic environment for precise quantitative assessment, and provides new empirical insights into the scaling behavior and generalization mechanisms of diffusion-based video models. The study also uncovers a prioritization hierarchy in how models generalize (color > size > velocity > shape), and demonstrates that current scaling strategies are insufficient for robust out-of-distribution generalization or for abstracting universal physical laws from vision alone.

7a106b9e32a40b523e80ef1ef262f39213aeed81.title: Erasing Concepts from Diffusion Models
7a106b9e32a40b523e80ef1ef262f39213aeed81.research_question: How can specific visual concepts, such as artistic styles, objects, or explicit content, be permanently erased from pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models using only a textual description, without requiring retraining on filtered datasets or post-generation filtering?
7a106b9e32a40b523e80ef1ef262f39213aeed81.hypothesis: It is possible to permanently erase targeted visual concepts from the weights of pre-trained diffusion models using a fine-tuning approach guided by negative concept descriptions, such that the model no longer generates the undesired concept while preserving its ability to generate other content.
7a106b9e32a40b523e80ef1ef262f39213aeed81.proposed_method: A fine-tuning methodology is developed that edits the weights of a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model (such as Stable Diffusion) to erase a targeted visual concept, given only a short text description of the concept to remove. The method leverages the model’s own knowledge by generating training samples using the undesired concept prompt and applies a loss function based on negative guidance: the model is trained to steer its outputs away from the targeted concept by linearly combining the conditioned and unconditioned noise predictions from a frozen copy of the original model. Two main parameter sets are considered for fine-tuning: cross-attention layers (for prompt-specific erasure, such as artistic styles) and non-cross-attention layers (for global erasure, such as nudity or object classes). The erasure strength is controlled by a guidance scale parameter, η, which balances the trade-off between effective concept removal and interference with unrelated content.
7a106b9e32a40b523e80ef1ef262f39213aeed81.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several tasks: erasing artistic styles, explicit content, and object classes. For artistic style removal, five modern artists and related topics are selected, and a user study is performed to assess the effectiveness of style erasure and interference with other styles. For explicit content removal, the I2P (Inappropriate Image Prompts) benchmark is used, generating 4,703 images and evaluating nudity removal with the Nudenet detector. For object removal, the Imagenette subset of ImageNet is used, with ten object classes targeted for erasure and classification accuracy measured using a pretrained ResNet-50. Baselines include Safe Latent Diffusion (SLD), Stable Diffusion models trained on filtered datasets (SD2.0), and negative prompt guidance at inference. Evaluation metrics include FID (Fréchet Inception Distance), CLIP score, classification accuracy, and human perceptual ratings from user studies. All models are fine-tuned for 1,000 gradient steps with a batch size of 1 and learning rate of 1e-5.
7a106b9e32a40b523e80ef1ef262f39213aeed81.novelty_claims: The proposed approach enables permanent erasure of targeted visual concepts from diffusion models using only a textual description, without requiring access to additional training data or retraining from scratch. Unlike prior methods that rely on dataset filtering, post-generation filtering, or inference-time guidance, this method directly edits model weights, making the erasure robust to circumvention even if model weights are distributed. The method is efficient, requiring only a short fine-tuning process, and is applicable to a range of concepts including artistic styles, explicit content, and object classes. The approach also introduces a principled use of negative guidance as a training signal for model editing, and provides a detailed analysis of parameter choices and their effects on specificity and interference.

7a121f973165f96188049570be03933a4bb114c3.title: Making Substitute Models More Bayesian Can Enhance Transferability of Adversarial Examples
7a121f973165f96188049570be03933a4bb114c3.research_question: How can the transferability of adversarial examples in black-box attacks be improved by leveraging diversity in substitute models, specifically through Bayesian modeling approaches?
7a121f973165f96188049570be03933a4bb114c3.hypothesis: Adopting a Bayesian formulation for substitute models, which captures a distribution over model parameters rather than a single point estimate, will significantly enhance the transferability of adversarial examples across diverse deep neural network architectures, outperforming existing state-of-the-art transfer-based attack methods.
7a121f973165f96188049570be03933a4bb114c3.proposed_method: A novel attack framework is proposed in which substitute models are treated in a Bayesian manner, representing model parameters as distributions rather than fixed values. The posterior over model parameters is approximated using scalable Gaussian-based methods, such as isotropic Gaussian or the SWAG (Stochastic Weight Averaging-Gaussian) approach, which captures both mean and covariance from training dynamics. Adversarial examples are generated by maximizing the average prediction loss over multiple samples drawn from the posterior, effectively attacking an ensemble of infinitely many models. A principled finetuning strategy is developed to further align the posterior with the distribution of potential victim models, utilizing both first- and second-order gradient information for optimization. The method is designed to be compatible with existing attack algorithms (e.g., I-FGSM, PGD) and can be combined with other transferability-enhancing techniques.
7a121f973165f96188049570be03933a4bb114c3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, using standard architectures such as ResNet-18 and ResNet-50 as source models. Victim models will span a variety of architectures, including VGG, WRN, ResNeXt, DenseNet, PyramidNet, GDAS, Inception, MobileNet, SENet, PNASNet, MNASNet, and several vision transformers (ViT, DeiT, Swin, BEiT). Attacks will be performed in the black-box setting using untargeted ℓ∞-norm constrained perturbations (ϵ=4/255 for CIFAR-10, ϵ=8/255 for ImageNet), with I-FGSM as the primary attack method and 20-50 iterations per attack. Baselines will include leading transfer-based attacks such as TIM, SIM, LinBP, Admix, TAIG, ILA++, LGV, as well as ensemble-based and Bayesian sampling methods. Evaluation metrics will focus on attack success rates across all victim models, including robust and adversarially trained models. Additional experiments will assess the impact of finetuning, the effect of combining the proposed method with other techniques, and scalability to ensembles and vision transformers.
7a121f973165f96188049570be03933a4bb114c3.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a Bayesian framework for substitute models in transfer-based adversarial attacks, enabling attacks on an ensemble of infinitely many models via posterior sampling, which is fundamentally different from prior approaches relying on finite ensembles or input diversity. The method provides a principled strategy for finetuning substitute models to better approximate the distribution of victim models, and leverages advanced posterior approximation techniques (e.g., SWAG) for scalable and effective uncertainty modeling. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate substantial improvements in transferability over state-of-the-art methods, including on robust and transformer-based architectures, and the approach is designed to be easily integrated with existing attack enhancements for further gains.

7a12d9f2da12dbe6b0c3ff6f06ca2ed47fbd6134.title: Interactive Speculative Planning: Enhance Agent Efficiency through Co-design of System and User Interface
7a12d9f2da12dbe6b0c3ff6f06ca2ed47fbd6134.research_question: How can agent planning systems be redesigned to enhance efficiency and user experience by integrating system-level optimization with interactive human-in-the-loop mechanisms?
7a12d9f2da12dbe6b0c3ff6f06ca2ed47fbd6134.hypothesis: Integrating speculative planning with active user interaction and a co-designed user interface will significantly reduce agent planning latency and improve user satisfaction without sacrificing the accuracy or quality of agent outputs.
7a12d9f2da12dbe6b0c3ff6f06ca2ed47fbd6134.proposed_method: A collaborative framework will be developed that incorporates three agents: a fast but less capable approximation agent, a slower but more accurate target agent, and a human agent. The approximation agent generates sequential action steps rapidly, while the target agent asynchronously verifies and refines these steps using the approximation agent's trajectory as a provisional prefix. If the outputs of the two agents match at each step, the process continues; if a mismatch occurs, the approximation agent's output is replaced by the target agent's result, and subsequent speculative steps are halted. A hyperparameter k will control the maximum number of speculative steps before synchronization. A user interface will be co-designed to present both agents' outputs sequentially, enable real-time user intervention, and incorporate a rescheduling mechanism to ensure clarity and minimal perceived latency. Users can interrupt or correct the planning process at any step, especially during prolonged latency or unsatisfactory outputs, with the system dynamically incorporating their input.
7a12d9f2da12dbe6b0c3ff6f06ca2ed47fbd6134.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of agent planning tasks, including scenarios such as collaborative financial transactions (e.g., splitting bills among multiple users). Both simulated and real-world datasets will be used to evaluate the system. Baselines will include standard agent planning approaches without speculative execution or user interaction, as well as recent cost- and time-efficient agent frameworks. Evaluation metrics will include end-to-end latency, total token usage, accuracy of final plans, and user satisfaction as measured by surveys or interaction logs. The experimental setup will involve varying the hyperparameter k, the complexity of planning tasks, and the frequency/type of user interventions to assess robustness and scalability.
7a12d9f2da12dbe6b0c3ff6f06ca2ed47fbd6134.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to jointly optimize agent efficiency and user experience through a co-designed system and user interface that integrates speculative planning and active human-in-the-loop interaction. Unlike prior work, this method allows for training-free integration of any approximation and target agent, guarantees performance at least as good as the target agent alone, and introduces a novel UI-level rescheduling mechanism for sequential and transparent output presentation. The framework uniquely empowers users to actively intervene and accelerate agent planning, making the system both more efficient and user-centric.

7a1e71cb1310c4a873e7a4e54d1a6dab0553adce.title: The RefinedWeb Dataset for Falcon LLM: Outperforming Curated Corpora with Web Data, and Web Data Only
7a1e71cb1310c4a873e7a4e54d1a6dab0553adce.research_question: Can large language models trained exclusively on filtered and deduplicated web data achieve or surpass the performance of models trained on curated corpora, and what are the best practices for constructing such high-quality web-only datasets at scale?
7a1e71cb1310c4a873e7a4e54d1a6dab0553adce.hypothesis: Properly filtered and stringently deduplicated web data alone can yield language models that match or outperform those trained on curated datasets, challenging the prevailing assumption that curated corpora are necessary for state-of-the-art performance.
7a1e71cb1310c4a873e7a4e54d1a6dab0553adce.proposed_method: A new large-scale data processing pipeline, MacroDataRefinement (MDR), will be developed to construct an English-only web dataset, RefinedWeb, from CommonCrawl. The pipeline will begin with URL-based filtering to remove adult, spam, and low-quality domains using a curated blocklist and weighted scoring. Main content extraction will be performed using the trafilatura library, followed by document-level language identification with fastText, retaining only English documents above a threshold score. Further filtering will include document-wise and line-wise heuristics to remove low-quality, repetitive, or non-natural language content, as well as targeted line corrections for boilerplate removal. Deduplication will be performed in two stages: fuzzy deduplication using MinHash for near-duplicate documents and exact substring deduplication using suffix arrays for repeated sequences of 50+ tokens. The pipeline will also track and remove duplicate URLs across CommonCrawl dumps to maximize data uniqueness.
7a1e71cb1310c4a873e7a4e54d1a6dab0553adce.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training autoregressive decoder-only language models at multiple scales (1B, 3B, 7B parameters) on the RefinedWeb dataset, as well as on popular baselines such as C4, OSCAR, and ThePile. All models will be trained with identical architectures and hyperparameters, using the same internal codebase and pretraining setups to ensure fair comparison. Evaluation will focus on zero-shot generalization across a suite of 18 NLP tasks, using the Eleuther AI evaluation harness and several aggregate benchmarks (small, core, main, ext). Additional ablation studies will assess the impact of individual filtering and deduplication stages, and the MDR pipeline will be applied to existing datasets to test generalizability of the approach. Removal rates and downstream accuracy improvements will be systematically reported.
7a1e71cb1310c4a873e7a4e54d1a6dab0553adce.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a highly scalable, fully automated pipeline for constructing trillion-token-scale, high-quality web-only pretraining datasets without human curation. It combines best practices from prior work with novel, aggressive deduplication and filtering strategies, and demonstrates that such web-only data can match or exceed the performance of models trained on curated corpora. The methodology challenges the prevailing belief that curated data is essential for state-of-the-art language modeling, and provides a reproducible, open-source dataset and pipeline for the community.

7a23c3494ff2dcd511dedc230f23a68b9284e9fd.title: Enumerating Safe Regions in Deep Neural Networks with Provable Probabilistic Guarantees
7a23c3494ff2dcd511dedc230f23a68b9284e9fd.research_question: How can the safe regions of the input space for a deep neural network, with respect to a given safety property, be efficiently enumerated and quantified with provable probabilistic guarantees, especially given the intractability of exact enumeration in high-dimensional, continuous domains?
7a23c3494ff2dcd511dedc230f23a68b9284e9fd.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that an efficient approximation algorithm, based on statistical prediction of tolerance limits and interval analysis, can enumerate safe regions of a DNN’s input space with strong, provable probabilistic guarantees, providing a tight lower bound on the safe area while scaling to real-world models.
7a23c3494ff2dcd511dedc230f23a68b9284e9fd.proposed_method: A novel approximation framework, termed ϵ-ProVe, will be developed to enumerate safe regions in the input domain of deep neural networks with respect to a given safety property. The approach will utilize interval analysis and iterative refinement, combined with statistical prediction of tolerance limits, to construct a controllable under-approximation of the output reachable set. Monte Carlo sampling will be employed to estimate the output range for randomly sampled input configurations, allowing the method to provide, with confidence level α, a lower bound R on the fraction of the input domain that is provably safe. The method will iteratively partition the input space into rectilinear hyperrectangles, classifying each as safe, unsafe, or unknown based on the sampled output intervals, and will refine the unknown regions until a specified precision ϵ is reached. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to guarantee both the probabilistic safety of the returned regions and the approximation quality of the covered safe area.
7a23c3494ff2dcd511dedc230f23a68b9284e9fd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of benchmarks, including small synthetic DNNs, deep reinforcement learning models for mapless navigation, and the ACAS Xu airborne collision avoidance benchmark. For each model and safety property, ϵ-ProVe will be used to enumerate safe regions, with parameters such as confidence α, lower bound R, and sample size n set to achieve high-probability guarantees (e.g., α=99.9%, R=99.5%, n=3500). Baselines will include exact enumeration methods (where tractable) and Monte Carlo sampling for safe rate estimation. Evaluation metrics will include the safe rate (fraction of input domain classified as safe), computation time, and the tightness of the lower bound compared to exact or MC estimates. Additional experiments will analyze the impact of different interval refinement heuristics and empirically validate the theoretical probabilistic guarantees using formal verification tools.
7a23c3494ff2dcd511dedc230f23a68b9284e9fd.novelty_claims: The proposed approach initiates the study of the AllDNN-Verification problem, which seeks to enumerate all safe regions of a DNN with respect to a safety property, a problem shown to be #P-hard. The ϵ-ProVe method is claimed to be the first to efficiently approximate these regions with strong, provable probabilistic guarantees on both safety and coverage. The framework provides not only a lower bound on the safe area but also explicit localization of safe regions in the input domain, enabling new forms of quantitative safety analysis and potential downstream applications such as targeted retraining or patching. Theoretical results establish the tightness and reliability of the approximation, and empirical results demonstrate scalability and effectiveness on real-world benchmarks.

7a319f7757de978b1177e2bc88d32d5a3fe3d4a0.title: Theoretically Grounded Loss Functions and Algorithms for Score-Based Multi-Class Abstention
7a319f7757de978b1177e2bc88d32d5a3fe3d4a0.research_question: How can theoretically grounded loss functions and algorithms be developed for multi-class classification tasks where the model is allowed to abstain from making a prediction at some cost, and how can these approaches be analyzed and compared in terms of consistency and practical performance?
7a319f7757de978b1177e2bc88d32d5a3fe3d4a0.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that new families of surrogate loss functions, including both single-stage and two-stage formulations, can be constructed for score-based multi-class abstention problems, and that these surrogates will provide strong non-asymptotic, hypothesis set-specific consistency guarantees, leading to improved theoretical and empirical performance over existing methods.
7a319f7757de978b1177e2bc88d32d5a3fe3d4a0.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed for score-based multi-class classification with abstention, introducing new surrogate loss functions derived from first principles. The approach will include both single-stage and two-stage formulations. In the single-stage setting, a general family of cross-entropy-based surrogate losses will be defined, parameterized to include and extend state-of-the-art surrogates. H-consistency bounds will be established for these losses, providing non-asymptotic, hypothesis set-specific guarantees that upper-bound the estimation error of the abstention loss in terms of the surrogate loss. In the two-stage setting, a novel family of surrogate losses will be proposed, where the first stage learns a standard multi-class predictor and the second stage learns an abstention mechanism, with strong H-consistency bounds proven for this formulation. Theoretical analysis will include explicit characterization of minimizability gaps and the derivation of finite-sample estimation bounds.
7a319f7757de978b1177e2bc88d32d5a3fe3d4a0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification datasets, including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and SVHN. The proposed algorithms will be compared against state-of-the-art cross-entropy score-based abstention surrogates and other relevant baselines. Evaluation metrics will include abstention loss, classification accuracy, and rejection rate, with a focus on both overall performance and the practical significance of the new surrogate losses. The experimental setup will involve training models using the proposed surrogate losses and analyzing their performance across datasets, highlighting the relative strengths and weaknesses of single-stage versus two-stage approaches.
7a319f7757de978b1177e2bc88d32d5a3fe3d4a0.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretically grounded derivation of cross-entropy score-based surrogate losses, encompassing and extending existing state-of-the-art surrogates. It provides the first strong H-consistency bounds for these surrogates in the multi-class abstention setting, enabling rigorous comparison and principled algorithm design. A novel two-stage surrogate loss formulation is proposed, with both Bayes-consistency and realizable H-consistency guarantees, effectively addressing open questions in the literature. The approach also includes explicit analysis of minimizability gaps and finite-sample bounds, and demonstrates through extensive experiments that the new methods can outperform existing approaches and that the relative performance of surrogates varies across datasets.

7a73cc4bc0ce80661b5acbb51bbde30ea5167280.title: Your Absorbing Discrete Diffusion Secretly Models the Conditional Distributions of Clean Data
7a73cc4bc0ce80661b5acbb51bbde30ea5167280.research_question: Can discrete diffusion models for language modeling be simplified and accelerated by reparameterizing the estimation of conditional distributions, and how does this relate theoretically and empirically to any-order autoregressive models?
7a73cc4bc0ce80661b5acbb51bbde30ea5167280.hypothesis: Reparameterizing absorbing discrete diffusion models to directly model time-independent conditional distributions of clean data, rather than time-dependent concrete scores, will simplify the model architecture, enable efficient sampling via caching, and achieve state-of-the-art performance on zero-shot language modeling benchmarks. Furthermore, the training objectives of such diffusion models are theoretically equivalent to those of any-order autoregressive models.
7a73cc4bc0ce80661b5acbb51bbde30ea5167280.proposed_method: A novel framework, Reparameterized Absorbing Discrete Diffusion (RADD), will be developed to model the conditional distributions of clean data directly, removing explicit time-conditioning from the score network. The method will analytically decompose the concrete score in absorbing discrete diffusion as a product of a time-independent conditional probability and a known time-dependent scalar, enabling the network to focus solely on learning the conditional distribution. The architecture will be simplified to a standard Transformer-like model with a softmax output, omitting all time-dependent components. To accelerate sampling, a caching strategy will be implemented: since the output is time-independent, the network's output will be cached and reused whenever the noisy sample remains unchanged during the sampling interval, significantly reducing the number of function evaluations (NFEs). Theoretical analysis will be conducted to unify the training objectives of absorbing discrete diffusion and any-order autoregressive models, demonstrating their equivalence under certain conditions.
7a73cc4bc0ce80661b5acbb51bbde30ea5167280.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard language modeling datasets, including OpenWebText for training and LAMBADA, WikiText2, PTB, WikiText103, and One Billion Words for evaluation. The RADD model will be trained using several loss functions (denoising score entropy, t-denoising cross-entropy, λ-denoising cross-entropy, and any-order autoregressive loss), and compared to strong baselines such as SEDD (Score Entropy Discrete Diffusion), D3PM, PLAID, and GPT-2. Zero-shot perplexity will be used as the primary evaluation metric, with additional assessments of sample quality and diversity using perplexity and unigram entropy on unconditional samples. The impact of the caching strategy on NFEs and sampling speed will be measured, and ablation studies will be performed to analyze the effect of time-conditioning and the scaling trick. All models will be evaluated at the GPT-2 scale, and experimental setups will closely follow prior work for fair comparison.
7a73cc4bc0ce80661b5acbb51bbde30ea5167280.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled reparameterization of absorbing discrete diffusion models that eliminates the need for time-conditioning, resulting in a simpler and more efficient architecture. The caching strategy for time-independent outputs enables significant acceleration of the sampling process by reducing redundant function evaluations. Theoretical analysis provides a new perspective by unifying the training objectives of absorbing discrete diffusion and any-order autoregressive models, showing their equivalence. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art performance among discrete diffusion models on multiple zero-shot language modeling benchmarks, validating both the theoretical insights and practical benefits of the proposed approach.

7a816dd242c4c3f652a448dba54daa53f89a9e4f.title: Soft Merging of Experts with Adaptive Routing
7a816dd242c4c3f652a448dba54daa53f89a9e4f.research_question: Can modular neural networks with adaptive routing among expert subnetworks be trained more effectively and efficiently without relying on non-differentiable discrete routing decisions or gradient estimation techniques, and can such models outperform both heuristic and learned routing baselines across diverse tasks and modalities?
7a816dd242c4c3f652a448dba54daa53f89a9e4f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that replacing discrete expert routing with a fully differentiable, parameter-averaged merged expert—whose parameters are weighted by a learned router—will enable effective end-to-end gradient-based training, resulting in improved performance and specialization over both gradient-estimation-based and heuristic routing strategies, without incurring significant additional computational cost.
7a816dd242c4c3f652a448dba54daa53f89a9e4f.proposed_method: A novel framework, Soft Merging of Experts with Adaptive Routing (SMEAR), will be developed for modular neural networks. In this approach, each expert routing block contains multiple expert subnetworks and a router that computes a probability distribution over the experts for each input. Instead of routing the input through a single discrete expert, SMEAR constructs a merged expert by computing a weighted average of the parameters of all experts, where the weights are given by the router's output distribution. The input activation is then processed by this merged expert, which shares the same architecture as the individual experts. All operations are fully differentiable, enabling standard backpropagation for end-to-end training. The method maintains computational efficiency by only processing the input through the merged expert, rather than all experts, and the parameter averaging operation is designed to be lightweight relative to the main computation.
7a816dd242c4c3f652a448dba54daa53f89a9e4f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in two real-world settings: (1) fine-tuning a T5.1.1 Base model on the GLUE benchmark (T5-GLUE) for natural language understanding, and (2) fine-tuning a ResNet18 model on the DomainNet dataset (ResNet-DomainNet) for multi-domain image classification. In both settings, expert routing blocks will be inserted into the backbone models, with the number of experts per block matching the number of tasks or domains. The SMEAR approach will be compared against a comprehensive suite of baselines, including models with discrete routing trained via various gradient estimators (REINFORCE, ST-Gumbel, Top-k, DSelect-k), heuristic routing strategies (tag routing, hash routing, single-expert), and recent modular learning methods (Adamix, Latent Skills, Soft MoE, Ensemble). Evaluation metrics will include average accuracy across tasks/domains and inference speed (examples processed per second). All models will be run with matched parameter counts and computational budgets, and results will be averaged over multiple runs to ensure robustness.
7a816dd242c4c3f652a448dba54daa53f89a9e4f.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a fully differentiable, adaptive routing mechanism for modular neural networks that avoids the limitations of non-differentiable discrete routing and gradient estimation. By merging expert parameters according to a learned routing distribution, SMEAR enables effective specialization and sharing among experts, achieves state-of-the-art performance relative to both heuristic and learned routing baselines, and maintains computational efficiency comparable to discrete routing. The approach generalizes across architectures and modalities, does not require oracle metadata for routing, and demonstrates improved scalability and robustness. Qualitative analyses further reveal that SMEAR leads to meaningful expert specialization not observed in prior methods.

7a84faaadc7881f621bb53ce9c2c74e154f7f3fc.title: LoR-VP: Low-Rank Visual Prompting for Efficient Vision Model Adaptation
7a84faaadc7881f621bb53ce9c2c74e154f7f3fc.research_question: How can vision model adaptation be made more efficient and effective through improved visual prompting techniques that enable both shared and patch-specific information across image patches, while reducing parameter and computational overhead?
