7a84faaadc7881f621bb53ce9c2c74e154f7f3fc.hypothesis: Incorporating low-rank matrix multiplication into visual prompting will allow for efficient sharing and customization of prompt information across image patches, leading to improved adaptation performance, faster convergence, and reduced parameter count compared to existing visual prompting methods.
7a84faaadc7881f621bb53ce9c2c74e154f7f3fc.proposed_method: A novel visual prompting technique, termed Low-Rank Visual Prompting (LOR-VP), will be developed to address the limitations of current visual prompting methods that restrict prompt interaction to image peripheries and neglect inter-patch inductive biases. The method involves resizing input images to a uniform L×L resolution and introducing two learnable low-rank matrices, B (of shape c×L×r) and A (of shape c×r×L), where r is much smaller than L. The product B·A forms the visual prompt, which is directly added to the resized image, enabling both shared and patch-specific information dissemination across image rows and columns. The initialization strategy uses zeros for B and random Gaussian for A to ensure the prompt starts as zero. For output transformation, linear probing (LP) is applied to the classifier head to efficiently adapt the model outputs to downstream classes, replacing more costly label mapping strategies.
7a84faaadc7881f621bb53ce9c2c74e154f7f3fc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a diverse set of vision architectures, including ResNet-18, ResNet-50, ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16, Swin-B, and CLIP (ViT-B/32), using pre-training on large datasets such as ImageNet-1K, ImageNet-21K-P, and ImageNet-21K. Downstream evaluation will be performed on ImageNet-1K, Tiny-ImageNet, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and several out-of-distribution datasets (ImageNet-R, ImageNet-Sketch, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-V2). Baselines will include CLIP-VP, ILM-VP, AutoVP, and standard linear probing (LP). Evaluation metrics will focus on classification accuracy, training epochs, training time, number of tunable parameters, GPU memory usage, and inference latency. Ablation studies will examine the impact of output transformation methods, the optimal rank for low-rank matrices, and the contribution of individual components.
7a84faaadc7881f621bb53ce9c2c74e154f7f3fc.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a low-rank matrix multiplication mechanism for visual prompting, enabling efficient and flexible sharing of prompt information across all image patches, which is not possible with prior pad-based or independent patch prompting methods. This method significantly reduces the number of tunable parameters (up to 18× fewer), achieves faster convergence (up to 6× faster training), and improves accuracy (up to 3.1% over state-of-the-art baselines). The framework is scalable to large models and datasets, demonstrates superior out-of-distribution robustness, and is highly suitable for resource-constrained environments due to its parameter and computational efficiency.

7a86ebcb1b6238cdae16ec17ce59501e33d722f7.title: Make Sharpness-Aware Minimization Stronger: A Sparsified Perturbation Approach
7a86ebcb1b6238cdae16ec17ce59501e33d722f7.research_question: How can the efficiency and effectiveness of sharpness-aware minimization in deep neural network training be improved by selectively applying perturbations to a subset of model parameters, rather than indiscriminately perturbing all parameters?
7a86ebcb1b6238cdae16ec17ce59501e33d722f7.hypothesis: Applying sparse perturbations to only a subset of parameters—selected based on Fisher information or dynamic sparse training—will maintain or improve model generalization and training efficiency compared to standard sharpness-aware minimization, while reducing computational overhead.
7a86ebcb1b6238cdae16ec17ce59501e33d722f7.proposed_method: A new training scheme, Sparse Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SSAM), is introduced to enhance sharpness-aware minimization (SAM) by applying perturbations only to a subset of model parameters determined by a binary mask. Two strategies are proposed for generating this mask: (1) Fisher information-based masking (SSAM-F), where parameters with the highest empirical Fisher information values are selected for perturbation, and (2) dynamic sparse training-based masking (SSAM-D), where the mask is updated during training by dropping parameters with the flattest gradients and randomly growing new perturbation locations. The binary mask is updated at regular intervals, and the perturbation is applied only to the masked parameters during each SAM optimization step. Theoretical analysis is provided to show that SSAM achieves the same convergence rate as standard SAM in non-convex stochastic optimization settings.
7a86ebcb1b6238cdae16ec17ce59501e33d722f7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and ImageNet-1K datasets using ResNet-18, WideResNet-28-10, and ResNet-50 architectures. The proposed SSAM methods (both SSAM-F and SSAM-D) will be compared against standard SAM and SGD baselines. Evaluation metrics include classification accuracy and computational cost (FLOPs), with various sparsity levels (e.g., 50%, 80%, 90%, 95%, 98%, 99%) explored to assess the trade-off between efficiency and performance. Additional analyses will include visualization of loss landscapes and Hessian spectra to assess the flatness of minima, and training curves will be compared for stability and convergence behavior.
7a86ebcb1b6238cdae16ec17ce59501e33d722f7.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a sparsified perturbation approach to sharpness-aware minimization, reducing computational cost by perturbing only a subset of parameters. Two principled mask generation strategies—based on Fisher information and dynamic sparse training—are developed to identify important parameters for perturbation. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the proposed method maintains the convergence rate of standard SAM. Empirical results are expected to show that the method achieves comparable or superior generalization performance to SAM, even with high sparsity, while offering significant training acceleration.

7a8a69d1ee140274dab4e63109cfd8513be127af.title: AdaZeta: Adaptive Zeroth-Order Tensor-Train Adaption for Memory-Efficient Large Language Models Fine-Tuning
7a8a69d1ee140274dab4e63109cfd8513be127af.research_question: How can memory-efficient fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) be achieved without sacrificing performance or convergence, particularly in the context of zeroth-order (ZO) optimization methods?
7a8a69d1ee140274dab4e63109cfd8513be127af.hypothesis: Integrating fast-forward tensorized adapters with an adaptive query number schedule into a ZO fine-tuning framework will significantly improve memory efficiency, convergence stability, and fine-tuning performance of large language models compared to existing ZO and parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods.
7a8a69d1ee140274dab4e63109cfd8513be127af.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces the Adaptive Zeroth-order Tensor-Train Adaption (AdaZeta) framework, which combines two main innovations: (1) fast-forward tensorized adapters that use Tensor-Train (TT) decomposition to compress adapter weight matrices, drastically reducing the number of trainable parameters and thus the dimensionality of the optimization problem; and (2) an adaptive query number schedule that sublinearly increases the number of ZO gradient estimation queries per epoch, thereby reducing gradient variance and mitigating divergence issues common in large-scale ZO fine-tuning. The tensorized adapters are injected after attention and feed-forward layers in each transformer block, and are updated only via forward passes with random perturbations, eliminating the need for backpropagation graphs. A parallel contraction method is developed to accelerate the forward pass of tensorized adapters, further improving computational efficiency. The adaptive query schedule is parameterized by scaling and growth factors, and is theoretically analyzed to guarantee improved convergence rates.
7a8a69d1ee140274dab4e63109cfd8513be127af.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both medium-sized (Roberta-Large) and large-scale (Llama-2-7B) language models, covering a variety of natural language understanding and generation tasks, including datasets such as SST-2, SST-5, QNLI, MNLI, SNLI, MR, SuperGLUE, SQuAD, and DROP. Baselines will include standard first-order fine-tuning (FT), inference-only methods (Zero-shot, In-Context Learning, Linear Probing), and ZO fine-tuning methods (MeZO, MeZO-LoRA, Sparse-MeZO). Evaluation metrics will focus on test accuracy, convergence speed (steps/time to reach a target loss), and memory efficiency (peak GPU memory usage, total GPU hours). Experiments will be run on NVIDIA Tesla A100-40GB GPUs, with batch sizes and query numbers varied to assess both performance and resource trade-offs. The effect of the adaptive query schedule and tensorized adapters will be isolated and compared to LoRA and other PEFT methods under equivalent memory and batch size constraints.
7a8a69d1ee140274dab4e63109cfd8513be127af.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel combination of fast-forward tensorized adapters and an adaptive query number schedule for ZO fine-tuning, enabling significant reductions in trainable parameters and memory usage while improving convergence and stability. The parallel contraction method for tensorized adapters is claimed to accelerate forward passes, making tensorized PEFT practical for ZO optimization. Theoretical analysis is provided to justify the improved convergence rates based on model dimensionality and query scheduling. Experimental results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art memory efficiency and fine-tuning performance on large LLMs, outperforming existing ZO and PEFT baselines in both accuracy and resource utilization.

7a96f97d0756280ae80f8b4b67f5e6d20ee1f26f.title: Cyclic Contrastive Knowledge Transfer for Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
7a96f97d0756280ae80f8b4b67f5e6d20ee1f26f.research_question: How can open-vocabulary object detection be improved to recognize novel object categories beyond predefined classes without relying on additional supervision such as extra image-text pairs or pseudo-annotations?
7a96f97d0756280ae80f8b4b67f5e6d20ee1f26f.hypothesis: A cyclic and dynamic knowledge transfer framework that leverages semantic priors and regional contrastive knowledge distillation from vision-language models (VLMs) can effectively align detectors with the visual-semantic space of VLMs, enabling robust open-vocabulary object detection without extra supervision.
7a96f97d0756280ae80f8b4b67f5e6d20ee1f26f.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a framework that integrates semantic priors into object queries and applies a regional contrastive knowledge distillation loss to facilitate knowledge transfer from VLMs to the detector. Semantic priors are dynamically determined for each image by prefiltering class candidates using either CLIP-based zero-shot classification or prompting a multimodal large language model (MLLM) to identify present concepts. These semantic prior embeddings are injected into the object queries, forming language-guided queries that adapt to each image. The detector is trained with a cyclic cross-modal knowledge transfer loop, where regional visual features from the detector are aligned with those from the teacher VLM using a contrastive loss. The loss function incorporates both positive and negative region-level pairs, established via Hungarian matching, to distill higher-order correlations and dependencies in the representation space. The overall loss combines bounding box regression, regional contrastive distillation, and classification components, with careful balancing of loss weights and temperature scaling.
7a96f97d0756280ae80f8b4b67f5e6d20ee1f26f.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on standard open-vocabulary detection benchmarks including OV-COCO, OV-LVIS, and Objects365. The detector is trained on base categories and evaluated on both base and novel categories, with the main metric being average precision (AP) for novel classes. Baselines include state-of-the-art OVD methods that use extra caption datasets, pseudo-annotations, or instance-level labels. The backbone is typically ResNet-50 or SwinB, and training follows a 3× schedule with semantic guidance for the first 30 epochs, followed by regional contrastive loss. Semantic priors are extracted offline for efficiency, and ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of each component. Cross-dataset transfer is evaluated by training on LVIS and testing on COCO and Objects365 without fine-tuning. Hyperparameters such as the number of semantic priors and confidence thresholds are tuned, and the scalability of the method is tested by varying the strength of the teacher VLM.
7a96f97d0756280ae80f8b4b67f5e6d20ee1f26f.novelty_claims: The method introduces a cyclic cross-modal knowledge transfer mechanism that does not require any additional supervision beyond standard detection annotations. Semantic priors are dynamically injected into object queries, enabling image-specific adaptation and improved novel concept awareness. The regional contrastive distillation loss aligns region-level features between student and teacher models, leveraging both positive and negative samples for richer knowledge transfer. The framework demonstrates consistent performance gains as the teacher VLM scales, while maintaining moderate computational overhead. State-of-the-art results are achieved on multiple OVD benchmarks without reliance on extra data, and the approach is shown to be data-efficient and scalable.

7a975c8ab4dc5c6ab8b8e97b75d1eb2a5bbb3250.title: Long-Tailed Recognition by Mutual Information Maximization between Latent Features and Ground-Truth Labels
7a975c8ab4dc5c6ab8b8e97b75d1eb2a5bbb3250.research_question: How can long-tailed recognition performance be improved by more effectively leveraging the relationship between latent features and ground-truth labels, particularly in the presence of severe class imbalance?
7a975c8ab4dc5c6ab8b8e97b75d1eb2a5bbb3250.hypothesis: Maximizing the mutual information between latent features and ground-truth labels, rather than between latent features and input data, will enable more effective handling of class imbalance in long-tailed recognition tasks and lead to improved performance over existing contrastive learning and logit adjustment methods.
7a975c8ab4dc5c6ab8b8e97b75d1eb2a5bbb3250.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that formulates long-tailed recognition as a mutual information maximization problem between latent features and ground-truth labels. The approach derives a general loss function that unifies contrastive learning and logit adjustment, resulting in a Gaussian Mixture Likelihood (GML) loss. Likelihood estimation is performed using kernel density estimation with Gaussian kernels, where class-wise queues store contrast samples for each class, and the queue lengths are proportional to class frequencies. To address the issue of outdated representations in tail class queues, a teacher–student framework is employed: a pre-trained teacher encoder generates contrast samples, while a student network is trained with the GML loss and a cosine similarity classifier. The temperature parameter for the Gaussian mixture is either fixed or learned, and the method is extensible to other tasks such as semantic segmentation and visual-linguistic representation learning.
7a975c8ab4dc5c6ab8b8e97b75d1eb2a5bbb3250.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several long-tailed image classification benchmarks, including ImageNet-LT, iNaturalist2018, and CIFAR-LT (CIFAR-10-LT and CIFAR-100-LT), as well as the semantic segmentation dataset ADE20K. Baselines for comparison include state-of-the-art long-tailed recognition methods (e.g., BCL, PaCo, DisAlign, Balanced Softmax), supervised contrastive learning, and knowledge distillation techniques. Evaluation metrics include overall accuracy, accuracy on head/medium/tail classes, mean intersection-over-union (mIoU), and mean class accuracy (mAcc). Experimental setups involve standardized backbones (e.g., ResNet-50, ResNeXt-50), consistent data augmentation and optimization protocols, and ablation studies to isolate the effects of each component (e.g., teacher-student strategy, loss type, temperature parameter). Additional experiments will test the method's extensibility to visual-linguistic tasks using CLIP-based backbones.
7a975c8ab4dc5c6ab8b8e97b75d1eb2a5bbb3250.novelty_claims: The proposed method provides a theoretical foundation for integrating contrastive learning and logit adjustment by interpreting long-tailed recognition as mutual information maximization between latent features and ground-truth labels. It introduces the Gaussian Mixture Likelihood loss, which generalizes and unifies previous approaches under a single framework. The method further innovates by employing class-wise queues and a teacher–student strategy to address the challenge of outdated representations in tail classes. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on multiple long-tailed benchmarks and show versatility by improving results in semantic segmentation and visual-linguistic representation learning tasks.

7aa801b907b59b8ee4cfb1296d9dac22c5164c5d.title: What learning algorithm is in-context learning? Investigations with linear models
7aa801b907b59b8ee4cfb1296d9dac22c5164c5d.research_question: What learning algorithms are implicitly implemented by transformer-based in-context learners when solving linear regression problems, and how can these algorithms be characterized both theoretically and empirically?
7aa801b907b59b8ee4cfb1296d9dac22c5164c5d.hypothesis: Transformer-based in-context learners implicitly implement standard learning algorithms, such as gradient descent and ridge regression, by encoding smaller models in their activations and updating these implicit models as new examples are presented in the context.
7aa801b907b59b8ee4cfb1296d9dac22c5164c5d.proposed_method: A detailed theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted to characterize the learning algorithms implemented by transformer-based in-context learners on linear regression tasks. The approach will begin with constructive proofs showing that transformers with specific architectures can implement single steps of standard algorithms such as gradient descent and closed-form ridge regression, using computational primitives achievable by transformer layers. Empirical studies will then train transformer decoders directly on in-context learning objectives, presenting sequences of (x, f(x)) pairs and analyzing the resulting predictions. Behavioral metrics, such as squared prediction difference (SPD) and implicit linear weight difference (ILWD), will be used to compare the outputs of trained in-context learners with those of textbook algorithms. Additionally, probing techniques will be employed to decode intermediate quantities (e.g., moment matrices and weight vectors) from the hidden activations of the model, revealing how algorithmic computations are encoded internally.
7aa801b907b59b8ee4cfb1296d9dac22c5164c5d.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training transformer decoders on synthetic linear regression tasks, where input-output pairs are generated from known linear functions with varying levels of noise and prior variance. Hyperparameters such as model depth, hidden size, and number of attention heads will be systematically varied to explore their effect on the learning algorithm implemented. Baseline algorithms for comparison will include ordinary least squares (OLS), ridge regression with various regularization parameters, single-step and multi-step gradient descent, stochastic gradient descent, and k-nearest neighbors. Evaluation metrics will include SPD and ILWD to quantify agreement between in-context learner predictions and those of baseline algorithms. Additional probing experiments will be conducted to recover intermediate algorithmic quantities from model activations, using both linear and MLP probes. The experimental setup will ensure sufficient training iterations and control for dataset properties, such as problem dimension and noise level.
7aa801b907b59b8ee4cfb1296d9dac22c5164c5d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a rigorous theoretical and empirical framework for understanding in-context learning in transformers as the implicit implementation of standard learning algorithms. It provides constructive proofs of algorithmic implementation within transformer architectures, establishes behavioral equivalence between in-context learners and Bayesian or minimum-norm predictors under varying conditions, and demonstrates the recoverability of algorithmic intermediate quantities from model activations. The approach offers new insights into the algorithmic interpretability of in-context learning and bridges the gap between deep learning models and classical estimation theory.

7aac9e9c109f4684a169aea8883f54cecbb55a9a.title: Linear Representations of Political Perspective Emerge in Large Language Models
7aac9e9c109f4684a169aea8883f54cecbb55a9a.research_question: Do large language models encode generalizable representations of political perspective in their internal activations, and can these representations be identified, interpreted, and causally manipulated to monitor and steer the political stance of generated text?
7aac9e9c109f4684a169aea8883f54cecbb55a9a.hypothesis: Large language models possess linear representations of political ideology within their activation spaces, such that these representations can be detected via probing, generalize across domains (e.g., lawmakers and media), and can be causally manipulated to steer model outputs along the liberal–conservative spectrum.
7aac9e9c109f4684a169aea8883f54cecbb55a9a.proposed_method: The proposed approach involves probing the attention heads of transformer-based large language models (LLMs) to identify linear representations of political perspective. Linear probes are trained on the activations of each attention head in response to prompts simulating statements by U.S. lawmakers, using their DW-NOMINATE scores as ground-truth ideological labels. Ridge regression is employed for probe training, with regularization strength selected via cross-validation. The most predictive probes are then used to interpret the political slant of generated text on a token-by-token basis and to test generalization by applying the same probes to model activations generated in response to prompts simulating U.S. news outlets, using Ad Fontes Media slant scores as ground-truth. Finally, causal interventions are performed by adding scaled versions of the learned probe vectors to the activations of the most predictive attention heads during text generation, thereby steering the model's output along the ideological axis.
7aac9e9c109f4684a169aea8883f54cecbb55a9a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three open-source LLMs: Llama-2-7b-chat, Mistral-7b-instruct, and Vicuna-7b. For probing, a dataset of 552 prompts (one per member of the 116th U.S. Congress) is constructed, and each model's attention head activations are recorded in response to these prompts. Linear probes are trained to predict DW-NOMINATE scores, with performance evaluated via 2-fold cross-validation using Spearman rank correlation. To test generalization, 400 prompts simulating major U.S. news outlets are used, and the same probes are evaluated on their ability to predict Ad Fontes Media slant scores. For steering experiments, models are prompted to generate essays on nine policy issues, and interventions are applied at inference time by modifying activations according to the probe vectors; the resulting political slant is measured using both human annotators and GPT-4o, with inter-rater reliability assessed. Baselines include non-linear probes (MLPs), random and non-monotonic label transformations, and ablations across different model layers and numbers of heads.
7aac9e9c109f4684a169aea8883f54cecbb55a9a.novelty_claims: This research proposes the first systematic identification of linear representations of political ideology in LLM activation space, demonstrating that such representations are generalizable across domains (lawmakers and media) and can be causally manipulated to steer generated text without further fine-tuning or prompt engineering. The approach enables interpretable, token-level monitoring of political stance and introduces a method for direct intervention on model activations to control subjective perspectives. The findings provide a foundation for future work on mechanistic interpretability and customizable agent perspectives in LLMs.

7ac0f06b86cc210818dee9f7b1a20a003c60401c.title: Automated Red Teaming with GOAT: the Generative Offensive Agent Tester
7ac0f06b86cc210818dee9f7b1a20a003c60401c.research_question: How can automated red teaming systems more effectively simulate human-like adversarial interactions with large language models (LLMs) in order to identify vulnerabilities that may not be captured by existing single-turn or automated methods?
7ac0f06b86cc210818dee9f7b1a20a003c60401c.hypothesis: An automated agentic red teaming system that dynamically combines multiple adversarial prompting techniques in multi-turn conversational settings will more effectively identify vulnerabilities in LLMs than existing single-turn or static multi-turn approaches.
7ac0f06b86cc210818dee9f7b1a20a003c60401c.proposed_method: A novel automated red teaming framework, GOAT (Generative Offensive Agent Tester), will be developed to simulate adversarial users engaging in multi-turn conversations with target LLMs. GOAT will utilize a general-purpose attacker LLM, initialized with a set of red teaming strategies and adversarial objectives, and will reason through each conversational turn using an extended Chain-of-Thought prompting structure. The attacker LLM will be provided with a repertoire of attack definitions (e.g., manipulation of output tokens, safe response distractors, fictional scenarios) embedded in its system prompt, enabling dynamic selection and layering of attacks during the conversation. The attacker and target LLMs will be chained together in a closed-box setting, with the attacker adapting its strategy based on the target's responses and maintaining full conversation history for context-aware reasoning. The process will iterate for a fixed number of turns, with the attacker LLM generating observations, thoughts, strategies, and adversarial prompts at each step.
7ac0f06b86cc210818dee9f7b1a20a003c60401c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the JailbreakBench dataset, which contains 100 adversarial behaviors curated for evaluating LLM safety. The evaluation will employ an open-source judge model (Llama 3.0 70B) to score whether any response in a conversation is policy-violating, reporting Attack Success Rate (ASR) at various conversation counts (e.g., ASR@1, ASR@10). The attacker LLM will be a generic helpful-only model with no explicit red teaming fine-tuning, while the target LLMs will include both open-source (Llama 2 7B Chat, Llama 3.0 8B Instruct, Llama 3.1 8B Instruct) and closed-source (GPT-4-Turbo, GPT-3.5-Turbo) models. Each adversarial conversation will be limited to a maximum of 5 turns to fit within the smallest context window. Baseline comparisons will be made against the Crescendo multi-turn attack method, with both methods subject to the same query budget and evaluation protocol.
7ac0f06b86cc210818dee9f7b1a20a003c60401c.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first fully automated agentic red teaming system capable of dynamically combining and reasoning over multiple adversarial prompting techniques in multi-turn conversational settings. GOAT simulates human adversarial behavior more realistically than prior approaches, is extensible to new attack strategies without retraining, and achieves higher attack success rates with fewer queries compared to existing multi-turn methods. The framework enables scalable, efficient adversarial stress-testing of LLMs, providing a significant advancement in the automation and effectiveness of red teaming for AI safety.

7acc1080caae1c12f9262a91def739271c491f47.title: Fast ODE-based Sampling for Diffusion Models in Around 5 Steps
7acc1080caae1c12f9262a91def739271c491f47.research_question: How can the efficiency and sample quality of ODE-based sampling in diffusion models be improved, particularly when using an extremely small number of function evaluations (NFE), such as around 5 steps?
7acc1080caae1c12f9262a91def739271c491f47.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by leveraging the geometric property that diffusion model sampling trajectories lie in a low-dimensional subspace, it is possible to design a solver that learns the mean direction for each sampling step, thereby reducing truncation errors and improving sample quality at low NFE.
7acc1080caae1c12f9262a91def739271c491f47.proposed_method: A novel single-step ODE solver, termed Approximate MEan-Direction Solver (AMED-Solver), is proposed for diffusion models. This method exploits the observation that sampling trajectories nearly lie in a two-dimensional subspace of the high-dimensional image space. The solver directly learns the mean direction for each sampling step by training a lightweight neural network (AMED predictor) to predict both the intermediate time step and a scaling factor for the gradient direction, minimizing discretization error via a distillation process. The AMED predictor uses bottleneck features from a pre-trained U-Net and time step information to output optimal step parameters, which are then used to update the sample in each step. Additionally, the method is generalized as a plugin (AMED-Plugin) that can be integrated into any existing ODE-based sampler, further improving their performance with minimal training and sampling overhead.
7acc1080caae1c12f9262a91def739271c491f47.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of image synthesis datasets with resolutions ranging from 32x32 to 512x512, including CIFAR-10, FFHQ, ImageNet, and LSUN Bedroom. The proposed method will be evaluated using pre-trained pixel-space and latent-space diffusion models, and compared against several state-of-the-art ODE-based samplers such as DDIM, DPM-Solver, DPM-Solver++, UniPC, and iPNDM. Evaluation metrics will include Frechet Inception Distance (FID) for sample quality, with experiments focusing on extremely low NFE (3, 5, 7, 9). Both unconditional and conditional generation tasks will be tested, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of different teacher solvers and time schedules. The method's effectiveness as a plugin will also be validated by integrating it into various solvers and measuring the resulting improvements.
7acc1080caae1c12f9262a91def739271c491f47.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new perspective by leveraging the geometric property that diffusion sampling trajectories are confined to a low-dimensional subspace, enabling the design of a learned mean-direction solver that minimizes discretization error. The AMED-Solver is the first to directly learn the optimal gradient direction for each step, rather than relying on heuristic or fixed combinations of past gradients. The method can be seamlessly integrated as a plugin into existing ODE-based samplers, offering consistent improvements with negligible computational overhead. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art sample quality among solver-based methods at extremely low NFE, addressing a key bottleneck in the practical deployment of diffusion models.

7ae221d479e98df9667acedec47653cbcbf3f6fa.title: Two Experts Are All You Need for Steering Thinking: Reinforcing Cognitive Effort in MoE Reasoning Models Without Additional Training
7ae221d479e98df9667acedec47653cbcbf3f6fa.research_question: Can reasoning performance and cognitive efficiency in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) based large reasoning models be improved by targeted inference-time interventions, and do such interventions generalize across domains without harming general capabilities?
7ae221d479e98df9667acedec47653cbcbf3f6fa.hypothesis: Selective reinforcement of a small set of specialized 'cognitive experts' within MoE architectures, identified via statistical association with reasoning-related tokens, will improve reasoning accuracy and efficiency across domains without requiring additional training or negatively impacting general instruction-following abilities.
7ae221d479e98df9667acedec47653cbcbf3f6fa.proposed_method: A lightweight inference-time steering method is proposed that identifies and reinforces 'cognitive experts' within MoE-based large reasoning models. These experts are selected by computing normalized Pointwise Mutual Information (nPMI) between expert activations and reasoning-related tokens (e.g., '<think>', '</think>', 'Alternatively') across model outputs. The method involves running a single forward pass on a domain-relevant dataset, recording expert activations, and calculating nPMI scores to select the top-l experts most correlated with cognitive deliberation. During inference, the routing weights of these cognitive experts are multiplied by a reinforcement multiplier β when they are selected, effectively amplifying their influence in the reasoning process. This approach requires no additional training, supervision, or model parameter updates, and is immediately deployable on existing MoE models.
7ae221d479e98df9667acedec47653cbcbf3f6fa.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on state-of-the-art MoE-based large reasoning models, specifically DeepSeek-R1 (671B) and Qwen3-235B, evaluating performance on challenging scientific reasoning benchmarks: AIME (2024, 2025) for advanced mathematics and GPQA Diamond for biology, chemistry, and physics. Cognitive experts will be identified per domain using nPMI on model outputs, and their reinforcement will be tested with various multipliers and numbers of experts. Baselines will include vanilla model performance, prompt engineering (before and after reasoning tokens), and decoding constraints (TIP). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, token usage, and a 'thoughts' metric quantifying reasoning efficiency. Additional tests on the ArenaHard benchmark will assess impacts on general instruction-following capabilities, with outputs judged by GPT-4-Turbo. Cross-domain generalization and domain-specific transfer effects will be systematically analyzed.
7ae221d479e98df9667acedec47653cbcbf3f6fa.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel, interpretable, and computationally efficient inference-time method for steering reasoning in MoE models by reinforcing a minimal set of statistically identified cognitive experts. Unlike prior methods, it requires only a single forward pass and no additional training or supervision. The method demonstrates significant improvements in reasoning accuracy and efficiency, robust cross-domain generalization, and neutral-to-positive effects on general capabilities, outperforming prompt engineering and decoding constraint baselines. This work establishes expert specialization as a practical lever for cognitive control in large-scale reasoning models.

7ae48cdb8a044ccd22d279a01d135ecfd304d025.title: Mitigating Forgetting in LLM Fine-Tuning via Low-Perplexity Token Learning
7ae48cdb8a044ccd22d279a01d135ecfd304d025.research_question: How can fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) for domain-specific tasks be achieved efficiently while minimizing degradation of performance on non-target tasks, especially when original fine-tuning data or computational resources are limited?
7ae48cdb8a044ccd22d279a01d135ecfd304d025.hypothesis: Reducing the proportion of high-perplexity tokens in fine-tuning data—either by using LLM-generated low-perplexity data or by selectively masking high-perplexity tokens in ground truth data—will mitigate catastrophic forgetting and preserve generalization capabilities on non-target tasks during LLM fine-tuning.
7ae48cdb8a044ccd22d279a01d135ecfd304d025.proposed_method: A novel fine-tuning strategy, Selective Token Masking (STM), is proposed to explicitly leverage token-level perplexity. The approach involves using an instruction-tuned LLM to compute token-level perplexity scores for each token in the ground truth training data. During fine-tuning, tokens whose perplexity exceeds a predefined threshold are masked out, resulting in a training set composed primarily of low-perplexity tokens. This process is performed in a single forward pass without requiring additional reference models or multi-stage pretraining, making it computationally efficient. STM is designed to be orthogonal and complementary to various fine-tuning techniques, such as full-weight fine-tuning, LoRA, and DoRA, and can be applied to different data sources, including ground truth and LLM-generated data.
7ae48cdb8a044ccd22d279a01d135ecfd304d025.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using benchmark datasets across programming (MBPP, BIRD), mathematical reasoning (MATH, GSM8K), and knowledge-based tasks (ARC-Challenge). Both target-task and non-target-task performance will be evaluated to assess generalization and forgetting. Models of various families and scales, such as Llama 3 8B Instruct, Gemma 2IT 2B, Mistral 7B Instruct, and OLMo 27B, will be fine-tuned using baseline, Self-Output, Rephrase, and STM approaches. Evaluation metrics include task improvement rate (TI) on target tasks and backward transfer (BWT) to measure degradation on non-target tasks. Ablation studies will be performed to test different perplexity thresholds, token filtering strategies (high, random, low), and learning rates. The impact of STM will also be assessed across different fine-tuning strategies (Full-Weight, LoRA, DoRA) and compared against regularization baselines (dropout, weight decay, KL regularization).
7ae48cdb8a044ccd22d279a01d135ecfd304d025.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces Selective Token Masking (STM), a simple yet effective and efficient method for mitigating catastrophic forgetting in LLM fine-tuning by filtering high-perplexity tokens based on model-internal perplexity scores. This approach provides a principled, loss- and perplexity-based explanation for why LLM-generated data leads to less degradation on non-target tasks, and demonstrates that similar benefits can be achieved without reliance on costly LLM-generated data. STM is model-agnostic, computationally efficient, and generalizes across diverse model architectures, fine-tuning strategies, and task domains. The method offers a new perspective on robust fine-tuning by directly connecting token-level uncertainty to cross-domain generalization and model stability.

7af5a5c8da08335ff908cb12d960cefe68813bc2.title: Graphon Mean Field Games with a Representative Player: Analysis and Learning Algorithm
7af5a5c8da08335ff908cb12d960cefe68813bc2.research_question: How can a general-purpose framework for graphon mean field games be formulated and analyzed to model and solve stochastic games with heterogeneous interactions among agents, and how can efficient learning algorithms be developed to compute equilibria in such settings?
7af5a5c8da08335ff908cb12d960cefe68813bc2.hypothesis: A representative-player-based graphon mean field game formulation, combined with a fully online, oracle-free learning algorithm, will enable the existence, uniqueness, and efficient numerical computation of equilibria for games with heterogeneous agent interactions, even on continuous state and action spaces.
7af5a5c8da08335ff908cb12d960cefe68813bc2.proposed_method: A discrete-time graphon mean field game (GMFG) framework is developed using a representative player formulation, where the agent interacts with the population through a graphon-weighted average of state distributions. The method rigorously defines the equilibrium concept, proves existence and uniqueness under mild assumptions, and provides a mechanism to approximate finite-player network games using the graphon equilibrium. To numerically solve for the equilibrium, a fixed-point iteration (FPI) approach is proposed, where the population measure and the representative player's policy are iteratively updated. An oracle-free, fully online learning algorithm is designed, leveraging value-based reinforcement learning (SARSA) and Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) to concurrently update policy and population measures using only observed transitions, without requiring access to an environment simulator or policy oracle. The algorithm discretizes the label space and employs Lipschitz-continuous policy operators to ensure convergence.
7af5a5c8da08335ff908cb12d960cefe68813bc2.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on three benchmark graphon games: Flocking-Graphon, SIS-Graphon, and Invest-Graphon, each modeling different real-world multi-agent scenarios such as flocking behavior, epidemic spreading, and investment competition. Various types of graphons (e.g., uniform attachment, ranked attachment, Erdös-Rényi, and threshold graphons) are tested. The learning algorithm's performance is evaluated in terms of convergence speed, exploitability, and closeness to benchmark solutions, using metrics such as Wasserstein distance and convergence gaps between iterates. The experiments use discretized state, action, and label spaces, and the learning algorithm is benchmarked against equivalent class methods from prior work. Numerical results include visualizations of equilibrium policies and state densities, demonstrating the validity and efficiency of the proposed algorithm across different graphon structures.
7af5a5c8da08335ff908cb12d960cefe68813bc2.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a general-purpose graphon game formulation with a representative player that offers both philosophical and mathematical advantages over continuum-player formulations. It provides the first comprehensive analysis of equilibrium properties (existence, uniqueness, and approximate equilibrium for finite-player games) under weaker assumptions than previous studies. The learning algorithm is the first fully oracle-free, online method for graphon mean field games, with a non-asymptotic sample complexity analysis. The approach is broadly applicable to heterogeneous-agent network games and enables efficient computation of equilibria in settings previously intractable due to the curse of dimensionality.

7af72a461ed7cda180e7eab878efd5f35d79bbf4.title: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations
7af72a461ed7cda180e7eab878efd5f35d79bbf4.research_question: How can a simple and effective framework for contrastive learning be developed to learn high-quality visual representations from unlabeled data, and what are the key factors that influence the performance of such frameworks?
7af72a461ed7cda180e7eab878efd5f35d79bbf4.hypothesis: A contrastive learning framework that systematically combines strong data augmentations, a learnable nonlinear projection head, and large batch sizes will yield visual representations that are competitive with or superior to those learned via supervised methods, even when using standard network architectures and without memory banks.
7af72a461ed7cda180e7eab878efd5f35d79bbf4.proposed_method: A contrastive learning framework is proposed in which each input image is randomly augmented twice to create two correlated views, forming a positive pair. A stochastic data augmentation module applies a sequence of random cropping and resizing, color distortion, and Gaussian blur to generate these views. A base encoder network, such as ResNet, extracts feature representations from each augmented image. These representations are then passed through a learnable nonlinear projection head (a multi-layer perceptron with one hidden layer and ReLU activation) to map them into a latent space where the contrastive loss is applied. The framework employs the normalized temperature-scaled cross-entropy loss (NT-Xent), where, for each positive pair, the remaining augmented images in the batch serve as negative examples. Large batch sizes are used to increase the number of negative samples, and training is stabilized using the LARS optimizer. After training, the projection head is discarded, and the encoder is used for downstream tasks.
7af72a461ed7cda180e7eab878efd5f35d79bbf4.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted primarily on the ImageNet ILSVRC-2012 dataset for unsupervised pretraining, with additional tests on CIFAR-10 and a suite of 12 natural image classification datasets for transfer learning. The evaluation protocol follows linear evaluation, where a linear classifier is trained on top of the frozen encoder to assess representation quality. Comparisons are made against state-of-the-art self-supervised and semi-supervised methods, using supervised ResNet-50 as a baseline. Key experimental variables include batch size (ranging from 256 to 8192), number of training epochs (up to 1000), and the strength and composition of data augmentations. Evaluation metrics include top-1 and top-5 classification accuracy. Ablation studies systematically investigate the impact of data augmentation types, projection head architecture, loss functions, and batch size on performance.
7af72a461ed7cda180e7eab878efd5f35d79bbf4.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a simple yet highly effective approach to contrastive learning that does not require specialized architectures or memory banks. Key innovations include the systematic composition of strong data augmentations, the use of a learnable nonlinear projection head before the contrastive loss, and the demonstration that larger batch sizes and longer training steps significantly benefit contrastive learning. The method achieves state-of-the-art results on self-supervised and semi-supervised learning benchmarks, surpassing previous methods and matching or exceeding supervised baselines on ImageNet and transfer learning tasks. The framework's simplicity and effectiveness suggest that self-supervised learning can rival supervised learning with minimal architectural changes.

7af84e2db863f8d91a1c9a8c328cc85cf356903c.title: Statistically Near-Optimal Hypothesis Selection
7af84e2db863f8d91a1c9a8c328cc85cf356903c.research_question: What are the fundamental sample complexity and approximation guarantees achievable for the hypothesis selection problem, where the goal is to select a distribution from a finite comparator class that is nearly as close as possible to an unknown target distribution under total variation distance?
7af84e2db863f8d91a1c9a8c328cc85cf356903c.hypothesis: It is possible to design an algorithm for hypothesis selection that achieves a 2-approximation factor to the optimal total variation distance with (near) optimal sample complexity logarithmic in the size of the comparator class and inverse quadratic in the accuracy parameter.
7af84e2db863f8d91a1c9a8c328cc85cf356903c.proposed_method: A novel algorithm will be developed for the agnostic hypothesis selection problem, leveraging a geometric reduction to a 'cutting-with-margin' game over the probability simplex. In each round, the algorithm selects a candidate distribution by maximizing entropy within a convex feasible set and uses statistical queries to estimate relevant set probabilities. The adversary iteratively cuts away regions of the feasible set that are inconsistent with the observed data, ensuring that each cut removes an ℓ1-ball of radius proportional to the accuracy parameter. The process continues until the feasible set is empty, at which point a distribution is output that is guaranteed to be within a factor of 2 of the optimal total variation distance plus a small additive error. The approach is improper, meaning the output distribution need not belong to the original comparator class, and is based on information-theoretic arguments to ensure near-optimal sample usage.
7af84e2db863f8d91a1c9a8c328cc85cf356903c.experiment_details: The proposed method will be evaluated through theoretical analysis of sample complexity and approximation guarantees. Experiments will be conducted using synthetic datasets where the target distribution is sampled and compared against a finite class of candidate distributions. Baseline algorithms will include the Yatracos algorithm (3-approximation with optimal sample complexity) and the Bousquet-Kane-Moran algorithm (2-approximation with higher sample complexity). Evaluation metrics will focus on the achieved total variation distance to the target distribution and the number of samples required to reach the desired approximation. Additional experiments may involve plugging the new hypothesis selection algorithm as a subroutine into existing density estimation frameworks to assess improvements in approximation factors for tasks such as learning mixtures of Gaussians.
7af84e2db863f8d91a1c9a8c328cc85cf356903c.novelty_claims: The proposed algorithm is the first to simultaneously achieve the optimal 2-approximation factor and (near) optimal sample complexity of O~(log n / ε^2) for the finite agnostic hypothesis selection problem under total variation distance. The approach introduces a new geometric reduction via the cutting-with-margin game and employs entropy maximization as a progress measure, enabling faster convergence than previous methods. This result improves the approximation guarantees for a wide range of distribution learning and density estimation tasks that rely on hypothesis selection as a subroutine, without increasing their sample complexity. The dual perspective and technical tools developed may also inspire further connections between statistical learning and online optimization.

7afaabb73bec969c0937be46b9f0f757e07c8534.title: Parallelizing Linear Transformers with the Delta Rule over Sequence Length
7afaabb73bec969c0937be46b9f0f757e07c8534.research_question: How can linear transformers with the delta rule be parallelized efficiently over sequence length to improve hardware utilization and scalability, and how does this approach perform in language modeling and recall-intensive tasks compared to other linear-time and transformer-based models?
7afaabb73bec969c0937be46b9f0f757e07c8534.hypothesis: Parallelizing DeltaNet (a linear transformer with the delta rule) across sequence length using a memory-efficient representation will enable efficient large-scale training on modern hardware, resulting in improved performance on language modeling and recall-intensive tasks compared to existing linear-time baselines.
7afaabb73bec969c0937be46b9f0f757e07c8534.proposed_method: A hardware-efficient algorithm will be developed to parallelize the training of linear transformers with the delta rule (DeltaNet) across sequence length. The approach involves reparameterizing DeltaNet as a matrix-valued RNN whose recurrence is expressed via a generalized Householder transformation, enabling the use of the compact WY representation for products of Householder matrices. This memory-efficient representation eliminates the need to materialize large hidden states at each time step, allowing for chunkwise parallelization similar to that used in linear attention models. The method will further leverage efficient matrix operations and the UT transform to rewrite recurrent updates as matrix multiplications, maximizing GPU utilization. Hybrid models will also be explored, interleaving DeltaNet layers with sliding-window or global attention layers to combine the strengths of both approaches.
7afaabb73bec969c0937be46b9f0f757e07c8534.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world language modeling tasks. Synthetic benchmarks will include Multi-query Associative Recall (MQAR), Mechanistic Architecture Design (MAD), and in-context language learning (RegBench) to evaluate associative recall and manipulation capabilities. Real-world evaluation will be performed using datasets such as Wikitext for perplexity, and zero-shot downstream tasks including LAMBADA, PiQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-easy, ARC-challenge, FDA, SWDE, and SQuAD. Baselines for comparison will include Transformer++, RetNet, Mamba, GLA, and other recent linear recurrent models. Models will be trained at both moderate (340M) and large (1.3B) parameter scales, with and without convolutional layers, and evaluated using metrics such as perplexity and accuracy on downstream tasks. Training throughput and memory efficiency will also be measured, and ablation studies will be performed on normalization and feature map choices.
7afaabb73bec969c0937be46b9f0f757e07c8534.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first hardware-efficient, sequence-parallel algorithm for DeltaNet, enabling practical large-scale training of linear transformers with the delta rule. The approach leverages a novel memory-efficient reparameterization using the WY representation for Householder matrices, allowing chunkwise parallelization and efficient matrix operations. This work demonstrates that DeltaNet can outperform recent linear-time baselines such as Mamba and GLA on language modeling and recall-intensive tasks, and shows that hybridizing DeltaNet with sliding or global attention layers can further improve performance beyond strong transformer baselines. The method addresses a key scalability bottleneck in previous delta rule-based models and provides a foundation for future exploration of more expressive and parallelizable sequence models.

7b237ec78cef3d6a431421dce08b89ff24a10ba8.title: On Approximating Total Variation Distance
7b237ec78cef3d6a431421dce08b89ff24a10ba8.research_question: How can the total variation distance between high-dimensional probability distributions with succinct representations be efficiently approximated or computed, and what is the computational complexity of this task for various classes of distributions?
7b237ec78cef3d6a431421dce08b89ff24a10ba8.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that while the exact computation of total variation distance between product distributions is computationally intractable (#P-complete), efficient deterministic approximation algorithms can be developed for certain structured cases, such as when one distribution is uniform or has a constant number of distinct marginals. Furthermore, it is conjectured that extending to more general distributions, such as Bayesian networks, leads to NP-hardness even for approximation.
7b237ec78cef3d6a431421dce08b89ff24a10ba8.proposed_method: A comprehensive computational complexity analysis will be conducted for the problem of computing total variation (TV) distance between two product distributions over {0,1}^n. The approach involves formal reductions from known #P-complete problems, such as #SubsetProd and #Knapsack, to establish the hardness of exact computation. For the approximation regime, a deterministic fully polynomial-time approximation scheme (FPTAS) will be designed by reducing the TV distance computation to counting solutions of knapsack-like constraints, leveraging existing FPTAS frameworks for #Knapsack. The method will be extended to handle cases where one distribution is uniform or has a constant number of distinct marginals. For more general distributions, such as sparse Bayesian networks, reductions from NP-complete problems (e.g., SAT) will be constructed to demonstrate the hardness of even approximate TV distance computation.
7b237ec78cef3d6a431421dce08b89ff24a10ba8.experiment_details: Theoretical analysis will be supported by algorithmic implementation and empirical evaluation. Synthetic datasets of product distributions with varying dimensionality and marginal structures will be generated to benchmark the proposed FPTAS. Performance will be compared against existing randomized approximation schemes (such as FPRAS) and exact enumeration where feasible. Evaluation metrics will include runtime, approximation accuracy (relative error), and scalability with respect to the number of variables and distinct marginals. For the hardness results, the reductions will be validated by constructing explicit instances and verifying the correspondence between solution counts and TV distance values.
7b237ec78cef3d6a431421dce08b89ff24a10ba8.novelty_claims: The proposal establishes, for the first time, the #P-completeness of exactly computing the total variation distance between two product distributions, even when one distribution has as few as three distinct marginals. It introduces a deterministic FPTAS for approximating TV distance when one distribution is uniform or has a constant number of distinct marginals, filling a gap left by prior work that only provided randomized schemes. The work further delineates the computational boundary by proving that even relative approximation becomes NP-hard for more general distributions such as sparse Bayesian networks. The combination of new complexity results and efficient deterministic algorithms for special cases constitutes a significant advancement in the computational understanding of statistical distance measures.

7b248d78573ccf0dca6aa2cec2743d3eccaa9d1a.title: CogVideoX: Text-to-Video Diffusion Models with An Expert Transformer
7b248d78573ccf0dca6aa2cec2743d3eccaa9d1a.research_question: How can text-to-video generation models be improved to produce long-duration, high-resolution videos with coherent actions, rich semantics, and strong alignment to text prompts?
7b248d78573ccf0dca6aa2cec2743d3eccaa9d1a.hypothesis: Integrating a 3D causal Variational Autoencoder (VAE) for spatiotemporal compression, an expert transformer with adaptive LayerNorm for deep text-video fusion, and progressive training techniques will enable the generation of high-quality, long-duration, and semantically aligned videos from text prompts.
7b248d78573ccf0dca6aa2cec2743d3eccaa9d1a.proposed_method: A novel text-to-video diffusion model will be developed, leveraging a 3D causal VAE to compress video data along both spatial and temporal dimensions, thereby improving compression rates and video fidelity. The model will utilize an expert transformer architecture featuring expert adaptive LayerNorm, which independently normalizes text and video modalities to facilitate deep fusion and alignment. A 3D rotary position embedding (3D-RoPE) will be employed to encode positional information across spatial and temporal axes. The training pipeline will incorporate progressive resolution scaling and multi-resolution frame packing, allowing mixed-duration and mixed-resolution videos within each batch. Additionally, a comprehensive video filtering and captioning pipeline will be implemented to curate high-quality, semantically rich training data, including the use of a dense captioning process that combines image and video captioning models with large language models for summary generation.
7b248d78573ccf0dca6aa2cec2743d3eccaa9d1a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a large-scale dataset of approximately 35 million filtered video clips, each with high-quality, dense textual descriptions generated through a custom captioning pipeline. Training will also leverage 2 billion images from LAION-5B and COYO-700M datasets. The model will be evaluated against state-of-the-art text-to-video generation baselines such as T2V-Turbo, AnimateDiff, VideoCrafter-2.0, OpenSora, Show-1, Gen-2, Pika, and LaVie-2. Automated evaluation will utilize metrics from VBench, including Human Action, Scene, Dynamic Degree, Multiple Objects, and Appearance Style, as well as Dynamic Quality and GPT4o-MTScore for assessing video dynamism and metamorphic changes. Human evaluation will assess Sensory Quality, Instruction Following, Physics Simulation, and Cover Quality using a structured rubric. Ablation studies will be performed to isolate the contributions of 3D-RoPE, expert adaptive LayerNorm, 3D full attention, and explicit uniform sampling.
7b248d78573ccf0dca6aa2cec2743d3eccaa9d1a.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a scalable text-to-video generation architecture that combines a 3D causal VAE for efficient spatiotemporal compression, an expert transformer with adaptive LayerNorm for modality fusion, and a progressive training pipeline with multi-resolution frame packing. The method also pioneers a dense video captioning pipeline that leverages both image and video captioning models, fine-tuned large language models, and automated filtering to curate high-quality training data. These innovations collectively enable the generation of long-duration, high-resolution, and semantically rich videos, achieving state-of-the-art performance on both automated and human evaluation benchmarks.

7bbc7595196a0606a07506c4fb1473e5e87f6082.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
7bbc7595196a0606a07506c4fb1473e5e87f6082.research_question: How can sequence models be designed to achieve both high modeling power and computational efficiency, particularly for long sequences and across diverse data modalities such as language, audio, and genomics?
7bbc7595196a0606a07506c4fb1473e5e87f6082.hypothesis: Incorporating a selective, input-dependent mechanism into structured state space models will enable linear-time sequence models to match or surpass the performance of Transformers on a range of tasks and modalities, while maintaining superior computational efficiency.
7bbc7595196a0606a07506c4fb1473e5e87f6082.proposed_method: A new class of selective state space models will be developed by parameterizing key state space model parameters (such as Δ, B, and C) as functions of the input at each timestep, thus introducing input-dependent, time-varying dynamics. This selection mechanism allows the model to selectively propagate or forget information along the sequence, enabling content-based reasoning. To address the computational challenges introduced by this input dependency, a hardware-aware parallel scan algorithm will be designed, which materializes expanded states only in efficient levels of the GPU memory hierarchy, leveraging kernel fusion, parallel scan, and recomputation to minimize memory and computational overhead. The resulting architecture, termed Mamba, will combine these selective SSM layers into a simplified, homogeneous block structure, omitting attention and MLP blocks, and utilizing standard normalization and activation functions for stability and expressiveness.
7bbc7595196a0606a07506c4fb1473e5e87f6082.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic tasks (Selective Copying and Induction Heads) to evaluate the model's ability for content-based selection and generalization to long sequences. For real-world data, the model will be pretrained and evaluated on large-scale language modeling datasets (comparable to those used for LLaMa and Pythia), as well as on audio waveform modeling and DNA sequence modeling tasks. Baselines will include Transformers, SSM-based models (S4, H3), Hyena, RetNet, RWKV, and other recent efficient sequence models. Evaluation metrics will include pretraining perplexity, downstream task accuracy, FID for speech generation, and throughput (tokens/sec) for efficiency. Experiments will test scaling laws up to billions of parameters, sequence lengths up to one million tokens, and compare both training and inference speed.
7bbc7595196a0606a07506c4fb1473e5e87f6082.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel selection mechanism for state space models that enables input-dependent, content-aware reasoning in a linear-time framework. The hardware-aware parallel scan algorithm allows efficient computation of time-varying SSMs on modern accelerators, overcoming previous efficiency bottlenecks. The resulting Mamba architecture is the first linear-time sequence model to achieve Transformer-level performance across language, audio, and genomics, with significantly higher throughput and the ability to generalize to extremely long sequences. The method simplifies model design by unifying sequence modeling and MLP components into a single block, and demonstrates state-of-the-art results on multiple challenging benchmarks.

7c1707db9aafd209aa93db3251e7ebd593d55876.title: SelfCheckGPT: Zero-Resource Black-Box Hallucination Detection for Generative Large Language Models
7c1707db9aafd209aa93db3251e7ebd593d55876.research_question: How can hallucinations in the outputs of generative large language models (LLMs) be detected in a zero-resource, black-box setting, without access to output probabilities or external databases?
7c1707db9aafd209aa93db3251e7ebd593d55876.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that if an LLM possesses true knowledge about a concept, its stochastically sampled responses to the same prompt will be consistent and contain similar factual information, whereas hallucinated or non-factual content will result in divergent and inconsistent sampled responses.
7c1707db9aafd209aa93db3251e7ebd593d55876.proposed_method: A novel black-box, zero-resource hallucination detection framework, SelfCheckGPT, will be developed. This method will operate by generating multiple stochastic samples from a target LLM in response to the same prompt. The factuality of each sentence in the main response will be assessed by measuring its informational consistency with corresponding sentences or content in the sampled responses. Several technical variants will be implemented, including: (1) BERTScore-based similarity to identify consistent facts; (2) question-answering consistency using automatically generated questions and answer matching; (3) n-gram language modeling to estimate token likelihoods from the samples; (4) natural language inference (NLI) to detect contradictions between the main response and samples; and (5) direct prompting of an LLM to judge sentence support based on sampled contexts. Each variant will compute a hallucination score for sentences, which can be aggregated for passage-level assessment.
7c1707db9aafd209aa93db3251e7ebd593d55876.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using passages generated by GPT-3 (text-davinci-003) on concepts from the WikiBio dataset, focusing on biographical entries. A dataset of 238 passages will be created, with each sentence manually annotated for factuality (accurate, minor inaccurate, major inaccurate). The proposed methods will be evaluated for sentence-level hallucination detection (AUC-PR) and passage-level factuality ranking (Pearson and Spearman correlation with human labels). Baselines will include grey-box approaches using output token probabilities and entropy (when available), as well as proxy LLMs for probability estimation. Additional ablation studies will compare the use of external reference passages versus self-sampled responses, and the impact of the number of samples will be assessed. Both black-box and grey-box setups will be compared.
7c1707db9aafd209aa93db3251e7ebd593d55876.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable hallucination detection for general LLM outputs in a zero-resource, black-box setting, requiring neither access to output probabilities nor external databases. It introduces multiple technical variants for measuring informational consistency using only sampled outputs. The method is designed to be model-agnostic and applicable to any LLM accessible via text-only APIs. Experimental results are expected to demonstrate that SelfCheckGPT outperforms existing grey-box and black-box baselines in both sentence-level and passage-level hallucination detection, establishing a strong baseline for future research in this area.

7c1d2b33480cfb6da5b2573a8f8d113dabc39cfe.title: Incremental False Negative Detection for Contrastive Learning
7c1d2b33480cfb6da5b2573a8f8d113dabc39cfe.research_question: How can self-supervised contrastive learning be improved to better account for semantic relationships among instances, particularly by addressing the problem of false negatives in large-scale datasets with diverse semantic categories?
7c1d2b33480cfb6da5b2573a8f8d113dabc39cfe.hypothesis: Incrementally detecting and explicitly removing false negatives during self-supervised contrastive learning will improve the quality of learned representations, especially in datasets with many semantic concepts, and will narrow the performance gap between self-supervised and supervised learning frameworks.
7c1d2b33480cfb6da5b2573a8f8d113dabc39cfe.proposed_method: A novel self-supervised contrastive learning framework is developed that incrementally detects and removes false negatives throughout the training process. The method employs k-means clustering on the encoder’s feature representations to assign pseudo labels to images, identifying samples with identical pseudo labels as false negatives. To ensure reliability, only pseudo labels with high confidence—measured via the softmax of cosine similarities between image embeddings and cluster centroids—are used in early training, with the acceptance rate of pseudo labels linearly increased as training progresses. Hierarchical clustering with multiple cluster granularities is incorporated to enhance robustness, and two strategies for handling false negatives are explored: elimination (removing false negatives from the negative sample set) and attraction (treating false negatives as additional positives), with elimination found to be more stable in the self-supervised setting.
7c1d2b33480cfb6da5b2573a8f8d113dabc39cfe.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on standard vision benchmarks including ImageNet, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, VOC2007, Places205, and COCO. The encoder is a ResNet-50 with a 3-layer MLP projection head, and training is performed for 200 epochs with a batch size of 256, using memory-based contrastive sampling. Pseudo labels are reassigned after every epoch with k-means clustering at multiple granularities (e.g., k = 1000, 3000, 10000). Evaluation includes linear probing and transfer learning (Top-1 accuracy), semi-supervised learning (Top-5 accuracy with 1% and 10% labels), object detection and segmentation (AP metrics on COCO), and clustering quality (NMI, MTPR/MTNR). Baselines include SimCLR, MoCo, MoCov2, PCL, DeepCluster, BYOL, SwAV, and supervised pre-training. Ablation studies compare pseudo label acceptance strategies and false negative handling objectives.
7c1d2b33480cfb6da5b2573a8f8d113dabc39cfe.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces incremental false negative detection and removal in self-supervised contrastive learning, bridging instance-level and semantic-aware learning. It leverages confidence-based, gradually increasing pseudo label assignment and hierarchical clustering to robustly identify false negatives. The approach explicitly revises the contrastive loss to eliminate or attract false negatives, with theoretical analysis linking these strategies to generalizations of triplet loss. The method achieves superior performance and clustering quality compared to prior self-supervised and clustering-based contrastive learning methods, especially under limited resource settings.

7c597874535c1537d7ddff3b3723015b4dc79d30.title: MaskGIT: Masked Generative Image Transformer
7c597874535c1537d7ddff3b3723015b4dc79d30.research_question: How can image synthesis be improved to generate high-fidelity, high-resolution, and diverse images efficiently, while also enabling flexible image editing tasks such as inpainting, extrapolation, and manipulation?
7c597874535c1537d7ddff3b3723015b4dc79d30.hypothesis: A bidirectional transformer trained with masked visual token modeling and equipped with a parallel, iterative decoding strategy can generate images more efficiently and with higher quality and diversity than existing autoregressive or GAN-based approaches, and can be flexibly adapted to various image editing tasks.
7c597874535c1537d7ddff3b3723015b4dc79d30.proposed_method: A novel image synthesis paradigm is proposed that utilizes a two-stage approach. In the first stage, images are tokenized into discrete visual tokens using a vector-quantized autoencoder (VQGAN setup). In the second stage, a bidirectional transformer is trained using Masked Visual Token Modeling (MVTM), where random subsets of tokens are masked and the model learns to predict them using context from all directions. During inference, the model starts with all tokens masked and iteratively predicts all tokens in parallel, retaining only the most confident predictions at each step, and re-masking the rest for further refinement. The mask ratio is controlled by a concave scheduling function (such as cosine), which gradually decreases the number of masked tokens over a fixed number of iterations, enabling efficient and parallel image generation. The same framework is extended to image editing tasks by customizing the initial mask according to the editing region.
7c597874535c1537d7ddff3b3723015b4dc79d30.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on standard benchmarks such as ImageNet (256x256 and 512x512) and Places2 (512x512) for class-conditional image synthesis, inpainting, and outpainting. The model is compared against state-of-the-art baselines including VQGAN, BigGAN, ADM (diffusion models), and specialized inpainting/outpainting models like DeepFill, HiFill, Boundless, and CoModGAN. Evaluation metrics include Frechet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS), Classification Accuracy Score (CAS), and Precision/Recall for diversity and quality assessment. All models use the same autoencoder and codebook setup, and are trained with consistent hyperparameters. Ablation studies are performed to analyze the effect of different mask scheduling functions and the number of decoding iterations.
7c597874535c1537d7ddff3b3723015b4dc79d30.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first bidirectional transformer for image synthesis trained with masked visual token modeling, enabling parallel and iterative decoding that is an order of magnitude faster than autoregressive approaches. The approach achieves state-of-the-art results on ImageNet in terms of FID, IS, and CAS, and demonstrates superior diversity and flexibility in image editing tasks without task-specific modifications. The novel mask scheduling strategy and iterative decoding algorithm are key innovations that enable efficient, high-quality, and versatile image generation.

7c5f943cf67c92a17c3a6dad62de758d1d4ae168.title: DeepGate4: Efficient and Effective Representation Learning for Circuit Design at Scale
7c5f943cf67c92a17c3a6dad62de758d1d4ae168.research_question: How can representation learning models for circuit design be made both efficient and scalable to handle very large circuits, while maintaining or improving effectiveness on key electronic design automation (EDA) tasks?
7c5f943cf67c92a17c3a6dad62de758d1d4ae168.hypothesis: A graph transformer architecture, equipped with a tailored update strategy, GAT-based sparse attention, structural encodings, and hardware-optimized inference, will enable efficient and effective representation learning for large-scale circuit graphs, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods in both scalability and task performance.
7c5f943cf67c92a17c3a6dad62de758d1d4ae168.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a scalable graph transformer framework for circuit representation learning, specifically designed for large And-Inverter Graphs (AIGs). The approach partitions the circuit graph into overlapping cones based on logical levels, enabling sub-linear memory complexity by updating node embeddings in a level-wise, mini-batch fashion. A GAT-based sparse transformer replaces the standard multi-head attention, using virtual edges to aggregate information along the circuit's directed acyclic structure, while incorporating both global and local structural encodings (such as logic level and out-degree) into the node embeddings. The training objective is multi-task, balancing gate-level and graph-level tasks with a gradient-based loss balancer. For inference, a custom CUDA kernel (Fused-DeepGate4) is developed to exploit the unique sparsity and low in-degree of AIGs, minimizing thread waste and synchronization overhead, and skipping unnecessary computations for nodes with in-degree one.
7c5f943cf67c92a17c3a6dad62de758d1d4ae168.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard circuit benchmarks, including ITC99 and EPFL, with all circuit designs converted to AIGs using the ABC tool. The method will be compared against a range of baselines, including GNNs (GCN, GraphSAGE, GAT, PNA, DeepGate2, PolarGate, HOGA) and transformer-based models (GraphGPS, Exphormer, DAGformer, DeepGate3), using both full-batch and partitioned training where applicable. Evaluation metrics will include functional and structural loss on multi-task objectives, memory usage, inference runtime, and generalizability to circuits of varying and out-of-distribution scales. The training will use a batch size of 1, mini-batch size of 128, and be run for 200 epochs on Nvidia A800 GPUs, with detailed ablation studies to assess the impact of each proposed component.
7c5f943cf67c92a17c3a6dad62de758d1d4ae168.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel graph partitioning and update strategy for DAGs that achieves sub-linear memory complexity and is adaptable to any graph transformer. It develops a GAT-based sparse transformer with virtual edges and structural encodings tailored for AIGs, enhancing both efficiency and expressiveness. The method also presents a CUDA-optimized inference kernel specifically designed for the sparsity patterns of circuit graphs, leading to significant reductions in runtime and memory usage. Together, these innovations enable scalable, efficient, and effective representation learning for circuits with millions or even billions of gates, surpassing prior state-of-the-art models on both performance and resource efficiency.

7c865923109d4b6bf8f4b94db4e8ec11e88a476b.title: Generative Data Mining with Longtail-Guided Diffusion
7c865923109d4b6bf8f4b94db4e8ec11e88a476b.research_question: How can proactive discovery and mitigation of longtail (rare or hard) data challenges be achieved in predictive models, especially in safety-critical or real-time systems, without requiring retraining or modification of either the predictive or generative models?
7c865923109d4b6bf8f4b94db4e8ec11e88a476b.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that model-based longtail signals, such as a differentiable epistemic uncertainty measure, can effectively guide a latent diffusion model to generate synthetic data that is rare or difficult for an existing predictive model, thereby improving generalization and robustness without retraining the generative or predictive models.
7c865923109d4b6bf8f4b94db4e8ec11e88a476b.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed that introduces model-based longtail signals, including a lightweight, differentiable Epistemic Head that estimates epistemic uncertainty in a single forward pass without impacting the base model's parameters or performance. These signals are used to proactively guide a latent diffusion model (e.g., Stable Diffusion) to generate synthetic training data that is rare or disproportionately hard for a given predictive model, in a process called Longtail Guidance (LTG).
