The LTG process operates by iteratively fine-tuning the predictive model on real and previously generated synthetic data, freezing its weights, and then using the model's longtail signal to bias the diffusion model's sampling toward high-uncertainty (longtail) regions, all without retraining the diffusion model or exposing the predictive model to intermediate diffusion states. The synthetic data generated is then added to the training set, and the process repeats, enabling proactive discovery and mitigation of conceptual gaps.
7c865923109d4b6bf8f4b94db4e8ec11e88a476b.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a range of natural image classification benchmarks, including ImageNet, ImageNet-V2, ImageNet-A, Stanford Cars, Oxford Flowers, Oxford Pets, Caltech101, and ImageNet-LT. Baselines include state-of-the-art synthetic data generation methods (e.g., Guided Imagination Framework, Dream the Impossible, prompt-tuned Stable Diffusion, DALL-E 2, MAE), data augmentation strategies (Cutout, GridMask, RandAugment, AutoAugment, CutMix, AugMix, DeepAugment, MEMO), and CLIP-based zero-shot/distillation models. Evaluation metrics include top-1 accuracy, per-class accuracy (especially for longtail classes), FID, and generative precision/recall. Synthetic data is generated in volumes matching or exceeding those of prior works, and the impact on generalization is measured both in high and low synthetic data regimes. Additional analyses include VLM-based introspection of LTG-generated data and ablation studies on guidance weights and model-based signals.
7c865923109d4b6bf8f4b94db4e8ec11e88a476b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a differentiable, single-forward-pass Epistemic Head for model-based longtail signal estimation that does not affect predictive performance. The Longtail Guidance (LTG) method is the first to couple model-based longtail signals with latent diffusion guidance, enabling generation of semantically meaningful, in-distribution synthetic data that is specifically rare or hard for an existing predictive model, without requiring retraining or modification of either the diffusion or predictive models. LTG demonstrates outsized improvements in generalization, particularly for longtail classes, and enables proactive discovery of conceptual gaps via VLM-based introspection. The method achieves higher accuracy and efficiency compared to leading synthetic data generation and augmentation baselines, and establishes a new paradigm for proactive, model-aware data mining in production ML systems.

7c96e68005b0a44f7b4dccbe41571c450b74e6d3.title: Sequential Batch Learning in Finite-Action Linear Contextual Bandits
7c96e68005b0a44f7b4dccbe41571c450b74e6d3.research_question: How do batch constraints in sequential decision-making impact the achievable regret in linear contextual bandit problems with finite action sets, under both adversarial and stochastic context generation scenarios?
7c96e68005b0a44f7b4dccbe41571c450b74e6d3.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, under batch constraints, it is possible to achieve regret bounds close to those of fully online learning by carefully designing batch-based algorithms, and that the number of batches required to match online performance will differ significantly between adversarial and stochastic context settings.
7c96e68005b0a44f7b4dccbe41571c450b74e6d3.proposed_method: A comprehensive study will be conducted on sequential batch learning in finite-action linear contextual bandits, where decisions are made in batches and feedback is only observed at the end of each batch. The methodology will address two primary settings: adversarial contexts, where contexts are chosen arbitrarily or adversarially, and stochastic contexts, where contexts are drawn i.i.d. from a fixed distribution. For the adversarial setting, a sequential batch Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) algorithm will be developed, which computes parameter estimates and confidence sets at the end of each batch and selects actions in the next batch to maximize the upper confidence bound. For the stochastic setting, a pure-exploitation algorithm will be designed, leveraging batch partitioning and least-squares estimation to adaptively improve parameter estimates after each batch. Regret upper and lower bounds will be established for both settings, and gap-dependent bounds will be derived for the stochastic case.
7c96e68005b0a44f7b4dccbe41571c450b74e6d3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic datasets that simulate both adversarial and stochastic context generation, with contexts being d-dimensional feature vectors and rewards following a linear model with sub-Gaussian noise. The number of actions K will be polynomial in the dimension d, and the time horizon T will be set to ensure a low-dimensional regime (T ≥ d^2). The proposed algorithms will be compared against standard online contextual bandit algorithms (e.g., LinUCB) and batch-based baselines. Evaluation metrics will include expected cumulative regret and, where appropriate, high-probability regret bounds. The number of batches M will be varied to empirically validate theoretical predictions regarding the trade-off between batch granularity and regret.
7c96e68005b0a44f7b4dccbe41571c450b74e6d3.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a detailed characterization of the fundamental limits of sequential batch learning in linear contextual bandits, providing nearly tight upper and lower regret bounds for both adversarial and stochastic context regimes. The work reveals that, in adversarial settings, the number of batches required to achieve online-level regret is polynomial in the time horizon, while in stochastic settings, a logarithmic number of batches suffices. The algorithms and analyses extend beyond prior work on multi-armed bandits with batch constraints by incorporating individual-level personalization and providing new insights into the interplay between batch size, context generation, and achievable regret.

7ca300c16abbd38382dec5b7ea6809fee570be54.title: ReFT: Reasoning with Reinforced Fine-Tuning
7ca300c16abbd38382dec5b7ea6809fee570be54.research_question: How can the reasoning and generalization capabilities of large language models for math problem-solving be improved beyond conventional supervised fine-tuning approaches, particularly when only a single annotated reasoning path is available per question?
7ca300c16abbd38382dec5b7ea6809fee570be54.hypothesis: Employing a reinforced fine-tuning approach that leverages reinforcement learning to explore and learn from multiple reasoning paths per question will yield superior generalization and performance in math problem-solving tasks compared to standard supervised fine-tuning, even when trained on the same data.
7ca300c16abbd38382dec5b7ea6809fee570be54.proposed_method: A novel fine-tuning paradigm, Reinforced Fine-Tuning (ReFT), is proposed to enhance large language models' reasoning abilities for math problem-solving. The method consists of two stages: an initial warm-up phase using supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on (question, Chain-of-Thought (CoT), answer) tuples, followed by an online reinforcement learning phase using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). During the RL phase, the model samples multiple reasoning paths (CoTs) for each question, evaluates the correctness of the generated answer against ground-truth, and updates the model parameters based on a reward function that assigns a reward of 1 for correct answers, 0 for incorrect, and optionally a partial reward for partially correct numeric answers. The PPO algorithm is regularized with a KL-divergence penalty to prevent policy collapse and maintain exploration within a reasonable distribution. Both natural language and program-based CoTs are supported, and the approach does not require additional reward models or augmented data.
7ca300c16abbd38382dec5b7ea6809fee570be54.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on three standard math problem-solving datasets: GSM8K, SVAMP, and MathQA (including a numeric variant), using two foundation models (Galactica-6.7B and CodeLLAMA-7B). Baselines include supervised fine-tuning (SFT), offline self-training, and online self-training. Evaluation metrics focus on value accuracy, with additional experiments using majority voting and reward model reranking at inference time. Hyperparameters such as batch size, learning rate, number of epochs, and PPO-specific settings are carefully tuned and reported. Ablation studies examine the effects of partial rewards, KL regularization, and value model architecture. Further, experiments are conducted with smaller models to assess robustness, and qualitative human evaluation is performed on reasoning path quality.
7ca300c16abbd38382dec5b7ea6809fee570be54.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a simple yet effective reinforced fine-tuning paradigm that leverages reinforcement learning to automatically explore and learn from multiple valid reasoning paths per question, rather than relying on a single annotated solution. This method achieves superior generalization and performance on math problem-solving benchmarks without requiring extra data or reward models. The approach is compatible with common inference-time techniques such as majority voting and reward model reranking, and demonstrates state-of-the-art results among open-source models of comparable size. Additionally, the method is robust across different model sizes and types of CoT (natural language and program-based), and provides insights into reward hacking phenomena and the importance of exploration in RL-based fine-tuning.

7cdaa08890895e1ad92afb5fad429690ad7b1dac.title: Few-Shot Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning is Better and Cheaper than In-Context Learning
7cdaa08890895e1ad92afb5fad429690ad7b1dac.research_question: How can parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods be designed to outperform in-context learning for few-shot adaptation of large language models, while reducing computational and storage costs and maintaining strong performance on novel, unseen tasks?
7cdaa08890895e1ad92afb5fad429690ad7b1dac.hypothesis: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods that leverage learned activation rescaling vectors, combined with appropriate loss functions and pre-training strategies, can achieve higher accuracy and lower computational costs than few-shot in-context learning for large language models on a variety of unseen tasks.
7cdaa08890895e1ad92afb5fad429690ad7b1dac.proposed_method: A new parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) method, (IA)3, will be developed, which introduces learned vectors that rescale the keys and values in attention mechanisms and the activations in feed-forward networks within a Transformer-based language model. These vectors are initialized to ones and are trained for each downstream task, allowing for minimal parameter updates and enabling mixed-task batches. The approach will use the T0 model as a backbone, and the (IA)3 parameters will be pre-trained on a multitask mixture before task-specific fine-tuning. The training objective will combine standard language modeling loss, an unlikelihood loss that penalizes incorrect outputs, and a length-normalized loss to account for output sequence length, all summed without additional hyperparameter tuning. The method will be applied uniformly to new tasks using prompt templates, with no per-task hyperparameter adjustments.
7cdaa08890895e1ad92afb5fad429690ad7b1dac.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of held-out datasets from the T0 multitask mixture, including tasks such as sentence completion, natural language inference, coreference resolution, and word sense disambiguation. The RAFT benchmark, which consists of real-world few-shot classification tasks with only 50 training examples and no validation set, will also be used to evaluate generalization. The method will be compared against strong baselines, including few-shot in-context learning with various GPT-3 model sizes, zero-shot T0, and other PEFT methods such as BitFit, Adapters, Compacter, prompt tuning, FISH Mask, Intrinsic SAID, prefix tuning, and LoRA. Evaluation will use rank classification accuracy, reporting median and interquartile range across multiple prompt templates and dataset splits. Computational costs (FLOPs), memory, and storage requirements will be measured and compared across methods.
7cdaa08890895e1ad92afb5fad429690ad7b1dac.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces (IA)3, a novel PEFT approach that rescales activations with learned vectors, enabling higher accuracy than full-model fine-tuning while updating up to 10,000 times fewer parameters. The recipe combines (IA)3 with pre-training of adaptation vectors and new loss terms (unlikelihood and length normalization), resulting in a parameter-efficient, hyperparameter-free approach that can be applied as-is to unseen tasks. The method is claimed to outperform few-shot in-context learning, including with much larger models, both in accuracy and computational efficiency, and to achieve state-of-the-art and super-human performance on real-world few-shot benchmarks such as RAFT.

7ce580d5493f3e485e09db1e962b41ca01779ccf.title: Connecting Permutation Equivariant Neural Networks and Partition Diagrams
7ce580d5493f3e485e09db1e962b41ca01779ccf.research_question: How can all possible permutation equivariant linear layer functions between tensor power spaces in neural networks be systematically characterized and constructed, and what is the mathematical structure underlying these weight matrices?
7ce580d5493f3e485e09db1e962b41ca01779ccf.hypothesis: All weight matrices for permutation equivariant neural network layers between tensor power spaces can be analytically derived and fully characterized using a diagrammatic approach based on Schur–Weyl duality between the symmetric group and the partition algebra.
7ce580d5493f3e485e09db1e962b41ca01779ccf.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed that leverages Schur–Weyl duality between the symmetric group and the partition algebra to construct all possible permutation equivariant linear maps between tensor power spaces of R^n. The method introduces the partition vector space, whose basis elements correspond to set partitions of the combined input and output indices, and uses orbit basis diagrams to represent these partitions. A surjective linear map will be defined from the partition vector space to the space of equivariant weight matrices, where each basis matrix is constructed by summing matrix units corresponding to all possible consistent and distinct labelings of the diagram blocks. This approach will be extended to handle cases with features, biases, and local symmetries (direct products of symmetric groups), and will provide explicit procedures and algorithms for constructing the weight matrices for any given layer configuration.
7ce580d5493f3e485e09db1e962b41ca01779ccf.experiment_details: Experiments will involve the explicit construction and enumeration of permutation equivariant weight matrices for various values of n, k, and l (where k and l are the orders of the input and output tensor powers, respectively), including cases where n < k + l to demonstrate the dependence of the number of parameters on the relationship between these values. The method will be implemented in PyTorch, and correctness will be validated by comparing the constructed matrices to known results for small cases and by verifying equivariance properties. Baselines will include existing approaches based on Kronecker products and fixed-point equations. Evaluation metrics will focus on completeness (ability to generate all equivariant maps), computational efficiency, and scalability to higher-order tensor powers.
7ce580d5493f3e485e09db1e962b41ca01779ccf.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first comprehensive and diagrammatic method for analytically constructing all permutation equivariant weight matrices between arbitrary tensor power spaces in neural networks, based on Schur–Weyl duality with the partition algebra. The approach provides explicit algorithms and a clear mathematical correspondence between set partitions and equivariant maps, generalizes previous results by handling arbitrary feature dimensions, biases, and local symmetries, and clarifies the dependence of parameter counts on the relationship between group degree and tensor orders. The method is accessible to practitioners via provided code and procedures, and offers a significant advance in the principled design of permutation equivariant neural network architectures.

7ced4abdcecb1295f6ed533e56748f1ec7a9691b.title: Enabling Efficient Equivariant Operations in the Fourier Basis via Gaunt Tensor Products
7ced4abdcecb1295f6ed533e56748f1ec7a9691b.research_question: How can the computational efficiency of equivariant operations for the Euclidean group E(3), particularly tensor products of irreducible representations (irreps), be significantly improved to enable scalable and accurate modeling of 3D data in real-world applications?
7ced4abdcecb1295f6ed533e56748f1ec7a9691b.hypothesis: The computational complexity of equivariant tensor product operations for E(3) can be substantially reduced by reformulating these operations in the Fourier basis using Gaunt coefficients, enabling efficient computation via the convolution theorem and Fast Fourier Transforms without loss of accuracy.
7ced4abdcecb1295f6ed533e56748f1ec7a9691b.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed that establishes a mathematical connection between Clebsch-Gordan coefficients and Gaunt coefficients, which are integrals of products of three spherical harmonics. This connection allows the tensor product of irreps to be reformulated as multiplication between spherical functions represented by spherical harmonics. By changing the basis from spherical harmonics to a 2D Fourier basis, the multiplication of spherical functions can be efficiently computed using the convolution theorem and Fast Fourier Transforms (FFT). The approach involves three main steps: (1) converting coefficients from spherical harmonics to 2D Fourier bases, (2) performing 2D convolution via FFT in the frequency domain, and (3) converting the resulting coefficients back to the spherical harmonics basis. This methodology reduces the computational complexity of full tensor products of irreps from O(L^6) to O(L^3), where L is the maximum degree of irreps.
7ced4abdcecb1295f6ed533e56748f1ec7a9691b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across major classes of equivariant operations, including Equivariant Feature Interactions, Equivariant Convolutions, and Equivariant Many-body Interactions. Efficiency comparisons will be made against existing implementations such as e3nn, eSCN, and MACE using randomly sampled features and spherical harmonic filters, with inference time as a primary metric. The proposed method will be integrated into state-of-the-art models and evaluated on benchmark datasets such as the OpenCatalyst2020 (OC20) for force field modeling and the 3BPA dataset for many-body interactions. Evaluation metrics will include energy and force mean absolute errors (MAE), force cosine similarity, and efficiency metrics such as speed-up and memory usage. Experimental setups will maintain consistent model architectures and hyperparameters to ensure fair comparisons.
7ced4abdcecb1295f6ed533e56748f1ec7a9691b.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a systematic and generalizable approach for accelerating equivariant tensor product operations by leveraging the mathematical relationship between Clebsch-Gordan and Gaunt coefficients. This enables a change of basis to the 2D Fourier domain, allowing the use of FFT for efficient computation. The Gaunt Tensor Product achieves a reduction in computational complexity from O(L^6) to O(L^3), supports a wide range of equivariant operations, and demonstrates both improved efficiency and competitive or superior accuracy compared to prior implementations. The approach is broadly applicable across different model architectures and task types, providing a new foundation for scalable and efficient E(3)-equivariant neural networks.

7cf3064111f53d092cc97baa5e7ed7f94d9b6a74.title: Is Complex Query Answering Really Complex?
7cf3064111f53d092cc97baa5e7ed7f94d9b6a74.research_question: How can the true complexity of complex query answering (CQA) on knowledge graphs be accurately measured, and what benchmark design and evaluation methodology best reflects the real-world difficulty of such reasoning tasks?
7cf3064111f53d092cc97baa5e7ed7f94d9b6a74.hypothesis: Current CQA benchmarks do not accurately reflect the true complexity of complex query answering, as most queries can be reduced to simpler link prediction tasks due to the way benchmarks are constructed. By designing new benchmarks that balance the distribution of query types and account for the presence of training links, the real performance and limitations of state-of-the-art CQA methods can be revealed.
7cf3064111f53d092cc97baa5e7ed7f94d9b6a74.proposed_method: A new set of CQA benchmarks will be constructed by systematically analyzing the reasoning trees of query-answer pairs to determine the true number of missing links required for inference. The methodology involves categorizing queries into full-inference and partial-inference types based on whether all or only some links in their reasoning trees are missing from the training graph. For each query type, the new benchmarks will include an equal number of full-inference and partial-inference query-answer pairs, ensuring a balanced and realistic spectrum of hardness. Additionally, the benchmarks will filter out queries involving non-existing links and will introduce more challenging query structures, such as longer paths and larger intersections. The approach will also leverage temporal knowledge graphs to create more realistic train/test splits based on temporal order rather than random sampling.
7cf3064111f53d092cc97baa5e7ed7f94d9b6a74.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the newly created benchmarks (FB15k237+H, NELL995+H, and ICEWS18+H) alongside existing ones (FB15k237, NELL995) to evaluate a range of state-of-the-art neural and hybrid CQA models, including GNN-QE, ULTRAQ, ConE, CQD, CQD-Hybrid, QTO, and CLMPT. Each model will be assessed on both the old and new benchmarks, with performance stratified by query type and by the level of inference required (full vs. partial). Evaluation metrics will include mean reciprocal rank (MRR) and hits@k, computed separately for each query type and inference level. The experimental setup will ensure that the distribution of query types is balanced in the new benchmarks, and that temporal splits are used for ICEWS18+H to simulate realistic prediction of future links.
7cf3064111f53d092cc97baa5e7ed7f94d9b6a74.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled framework for measuring the real complexity of CQA by accounting for the reduction of complex queries to simpler types due to training data leakage. It proposes the first benchmarks that balance full-inference and partial-inference queries across all types, preventing inflated performance metrics and enabling fair comparison of CQA methods. The methodology also pioneers the use of temporally realistic splits in temporal KGs and introduces harder query types to raise the bar for CQA evaluation. These innovations are expected to set a new standard for benchmarking and drive the development of more robust and genuinely capable CQA systems.

7cfceb098d86ac397761988d4557b241115e95d3.title: ShadowKV: KV Cache in Shadows for High-Throughput Long-Context LLM Inference
7cfceb098d86ac397761988d4557b241115e95d3.research_question: How can the throughput and memory efficiency of long-context large language model (LLM) inference be improved, particularly for high-throughput scenarios with large batch sizes and long input sequences, without sacrificing model accuracy?
7cfceb098d86ac397761988d4557b241115e95d3.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by leveraging the low-rank properties of pre-RoPE key caches and selectively offloading value caches, it is possible to significantly reduce GPU memory footprint and decoding latency for long-context LLM inference, while maintaining or even improving accuracy compared to existing sparse attention and cache eviction methods.
7cfceb098d86ac397761988d4557b241115e95d3.proposed_method: A new inference system, ShadowKV, will be developed to optimize memory and throughput for long-context LLMs. The method involves decomposing the pre-RoPE key cache using singular value decomposition (SVD) and retaining only low-rank projections on the GPU, while offloading the value cache to CPU memory. During the pre-filling phase, the post-RoPE key cache is segmented into chunks, with chunk means stored as landmarks and outlier chunks (with low cosine similarity) retained on the GPU for accuracy. During decoding, an accurate KV selection strategy will be employed: attention scores are computed using the landmarks, top-k chunks are identified, and only the necessary value cache entries are fetched from the CPU. Simultaneously, the corresponding key cache is reconstructed from low-rank projections, overlapping computation and data movement to minimize latency. Temporal locality in KV access will be exploited to further reduce redundant data movement.
7cfceb098d86ac397761988d4557b241115e95d3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several state-of-the-art long-context LLMs, including Llama-3-8B-1M, Llama-3.1-8B, GLM-4-9B-1M, Yi-9B-200K, Phi-3-Mini-128K, and Qwen2-7B-128K. Evaluation will use benchmarks such as RULER, LongBench, and Needle In A Haystack, covering tasks like multi-document QA, reasoning, summarization, and code completion, with context lengths up to 1M tokens. Baselines will include dynamic sparse attention methods (Quest, Loki, InfiniGen) and cache eviction strategies (SnapKV, StreamingLLM), with both full and value-only offloading variants. Metrics will include accuracy on benchmark tasks, throughput (tokens/sec) under varying batch sizes and context lengths, GPU memory usage, and decoding latency. Ablation studies will investigate the impact of sparse KV cache budget, chunk size, and SVD rank on performance and accuracy.
7cfceb098d86ac397761988d4557b241115e95d3.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel system that exploits the exceptionally low-rank structure of pre-RoPE key caches for compression, combined with selective offloading of value caches to minimize GPU memory usage. Unlike prior methods, the system performs online, prompt-dependent SVD for key cache compression and employs an accurate, chunk-based KV selection strategy to minimize latency and data movement. The method achieves up to 6× larger batch sizes and up to 3.04× higher throughput on commodity GPUs, surpassing even the theoretical performance of infinite GPU memory in some cases, all while maintaining or improving accuracy on challenging long-context benchmarks.

7d1665ccebaaff1f620f14ffcc04fe7c086d2416.title: HOPE for a Robust Parameterization of Long-memory State Space Models
7d1665ccebaaff1f620f14ffcc04fe7c086d2416.research_question: How can state-space models for long-sequence modeling be robustly parameterized to improve initialization, training stability, memory retention, and model efficiency, especially in the context of long-range dependencies?
7d1665ccebaaff1f620f14ffcc04fe7c086d2416.hypothesis: Parameterizing linear time-invariant (LTI) systems in state-space models using Markov parameters within a Hankel operator framework will yield higher expressiveness, greater numerical stability, improved robustness to initialization and training, and enhanced long-term memory compared to canonical parameterizations based on (A, B, C, D) matrices.
7d1665ccebaaff1f620f14ffcc04fe7c086d2416.proposed_method: A novel parameterization scheme for LTI systems in state-space models is introduced, leveraging Markov parameters to define a discrete Hankel operator (HOPE). Instead of learning the standard (A, B, C, D) matrices, the method directly learns a vector of Markov parameters, the skip connection D, and a trainable sampling period ∆t. The Hankel matrix is constructed from these Markov parameters, and the associated LTI system is linked to a continuous-time system via the bilinear transform. The output sequence is computed by nonuniformly sampling the transfer function in the frequency domain, allowing efficient evaluation using FFT-based algorithms. This approach reduces the number of parameters required for each LTI system to one third of that in canonical SSMs and ensures that the resulting systems almost surely have slowly decaying singular values, leading to high expressiveness and stability.
7d1665ccebaaff1f620f14ffcc04fe7c086d2416.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard long-sequence modeling benchmarks, including the Long-Range Arena (LRA) suite and a sequential CIFAR-10 (sCIFAR-10) task with padded noise to assess long-term memory. The proposed HOPE-SSM will be compared against strong baselines such as S4, S4D, and other HiPPO-initialized models. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy, memory retention (as measured by the decay of the Hankel matrix entries), model parameter count, and training stability. Experimental setups will involve varying initialization schemes, learning rates, and perturbation analyses to assess robustness and expressiveness, with both frozen and trainable LTI system configurations.
7d1665ccebaaff1f620f14ffcc04fe7c086d2416.novelty_claims: The proposed parameterization introduces a theoretically justified and empirically validated approach for robustly parameterizing LTI systems in SSMs using Hankel operators. It provides a full parameter space of high-rank, expressive systems, addresses the numerical instability and expressiveness loss of canonical SSMs, and enables non-decaying memory within a fixed time window. The method achieves improved robustness to initialization and training, requires significantly fewer parameters, and matches or exceeds the computational efficiency of existing state-of-the-art SSMs. These innovations collectively advance the state of the art in long-sequence modeling.

7d1e512888a2fa4e838c12a02ae7fce867d322a8.title: DeepSpeed-MoE: Advancing Mixture-of-Experts Inference and Training to Power Next-Generation AI Scale
7d1e512888a2fa4e838c12a02ae7fce867d322a8.research_question: How can Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models be advanced to enable efficient training and inference at next-generation AI scale, while maintaining or improving model quality and reducing computational and memory costs compared to dense models?
7d1e512888a2fa4e838c12a02ae7fce867d322a8.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that novel MoE architecture designs, model compression techniques, and optimized inference systems can significantly reduce the training and inference costs of large-scale language models, while maintaining or improving model quality relative to dense models.
7d1e512888a2fa4e838c12a02ae7fce867d322a8.proposed_method: The proposed approach will develop an end-to-end MoE training and inference framework, integrating several innovations. First, MoE will be extended to autoregressive natural language generation (NLG) models, demonstrating that comparable model quality can be achieved at a fraction of the training cost. Second, a new MoE architecture, Pyramid-Residual MoE (PR-MoE), will be designed to improve parameter efficiency by combining residual connections and a pyramidal allocation of experts, focusing expert capacity where it is most effective. Additionally, a staged knowledge distillation process will be used to create Mixture-of-Students (MoS) models, further compressing the model size. Finally, a highly optimized inference system will be engineered to enable efficient and scalable inference across hundreds of GPUs, leveraging both model and system-level optimizations to minimize latency and cost.
7d1e512888a2fa4e838c12a02ae7fce867d322a8.experiment_details: Experiments will involve pre-training both dense and MoE-based autoregressive transformer models (e.g., GPT-like architectures) at various scales (350M, 1.3B, 6.7B parameters) using 128 NVIDIA A100 GPUs and 300B tokens, with consistent hyperparameters for fair comparison. Evaluation will include six zero-shot downstream tasks (LAMBADA, PIQA, BoolQ, RACE-h, TriviaQA, WebQs) using accuracy as the primary metric. Baselines will include both dense models and existing MoE models from related literature. Additional experiments will assess the impact of PR-MoE and MoS architectures on parameter efficiency, model quality, and inference speed/cost, with throughput and latency measured on large-scale GPU clusters.
7d1e512888a2fa4e838c12a02ae7fce867d322a8.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces several innovations: (1) extension of MoE to autoregressive NLG models with demonstrated 5x training cost reduction for equivalent quality; (2) the PR-MoE architecture, which reduces MoE model size by up to 3x without loss of quality by leveraging residual connections and pyramidal expert allocation; (3) the Mixture-of-Students (MoS) distillation technique, achieving up to 3.7x further compression; and (4) a highly optimized inference system that delivers up to 7.3x lower latency and cost compared to existing MoE inference solutions, and up to 9x cheaper inference compared to dense models. These advances collectively enable practical, efficient training and deployment of massive MoE models at unprecedented scale.

7d22ad3573101337bca2091fb0114b377c4f3db6.title: A Simple and Effective Pruning Approach for Large Language Models
7d22ad3573101337bca2091fb0114b377c4f3db6.research_question: How can large language models be pruned efficiently to induce high levels of sparsity while preserving performance, without requiring retraining or computationally expensive weight updates?
7d22ad3573101337bca2091fb0114b377c4f3db6.hypothesis: Incorporating both weight magnitudes and input activation norms into the pruning metric, and comparing weights on a per-output basis, will enable effective pruning of large language models without retraining or weight updates, outperforming standard magnitude pruning and matching the performance of more complex methods.
7d22ad3573101337bca2091fb0114b377c4f3db6.proposed_method: A novel pruning approach is proposed that evaluates the importance of each weight in a linear layer by computing the product of its absolute value and the L2 norm of the corresponding input activation feature, aggregated across a set of calibration samples. The pruning is performed on a per-output basis: for each output neuron, weights are ranked by this importance score, and the lowest scoring weights are pruned to achieve a desired sparsity level. This method requires only a single forward pass through the model to collect activation statistics and does not require any retraining or weight update after pruning. The approach is compatible with both unstructured and structured N:M sparsity patterns, and can be implemented efficiently with minimal memory overhead.
7d22ad3573101337bca2091fb0114b377c4f3db6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the LLaMA and LLaMA-2 model families at various scales (7B, 13B, 30B, 65B, and 70B parameters). The evaluation will include zero-shot accuracy on seven tasks from the EleutherAI LM Harness and language modeling perplexity on the WikiText validation set. Baseline comparisons will include standard magnitude pruning and SparseGPT, a second-order pruning method that involves weight updates. The same set of calibration data (128 sequences from the C4 dataset) will be used for all methods to ensure fair comparison. Both unstructured and structured (4:8 and 2:4) sparsity patterns will be evaluated, and additional analyses will assess pruning speed, inference speedup, robustness to calibration sample size, and the effects of fine-tuning after pruning.
7d22ad3573101337bca2091fb0114b377c4f3db6.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple yet effective pruning metric that combines weight magnitudes with input activation norms, tailored for large language models. It eliminates the need for retraining or any weight update, enabling highly efficient pruning in a single forward pass. The approach demonstrates superior or competitive performance compared to existing methods, including those requiring computationally intensive weight updates, and provides new insights into the importance of per-output comparison groups for effective LLM pruning. The method also shows robustness to limited calibration data and can be extended to structured sparsity patterns, making it practical for real-world deployment and future research in sparse training.

7d40654b344cc7ede5b793b573188a5b6be4464f.title: Discovering modular solutions that generalize compositionally
7d40654b344cc7ede5b793b573188a5b6be4464f.research_question: Under what conditions can modular neural network architectures discover and leverage hidden compositional structure in multi-task learning settings to achieve compositional generalization, and how does this compare to monolithic architectures?
7d40654b344cc7ede5b793b573188a5b6be4464f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that modular architectures, specifically hypernetworks, can identify and exploit underlying compositional structure in task distributions, enabling compositional generalization to novel combinations of modules, provided that the training distribution exhibits compositional and connected support. Monolithic architectures are expected to lack this ability.
7d40654b344cc7ede5b793b573188a5b6be4464f.proposed_method: A research program is proposed that formalizes a multi-task teacher-student framework in which the teacher is a modular hypernetwork capable of generating tasks as sparse combinations of parameter modules. The student, implemented as either a modular (hypernetwork-based) or monolithic architecture (e.g., ANIL, MAML), is trained via meta-learning to infer task-specific parameters from demonstrations. The method involves both theoretical analysis and empirical investigation. Theoretically, identifiability conditions are derived for when the student can recover the teacher's modules up to a linear transformation, focusing on compositional and connected support in the task distribution and matching model capacity. Empirically, experiments are conducted to assess the ability of different architectures to generalize to out-of-distribution (OOD) tasks composed of novel module combinations, and to test the sensitivity of compositional generalization to overparameterization and support structure.
7d40654b344cc7ede5b793b573188a5b6be4464f.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted in several settings: (1) a controlled teacher-student setup where both teacher and student are hypernetworks, with the teacher generating tasks as sparse combinations of modules; (2) a 'hyperteacher' setting where the teacher modularly parameterizes multiple layers of a target network, and the student is trained on limited data per task; (3) compositional preference and goal gridworld environments where agents must infer preferences or goals composed of multiple factors. Datasets consist of synthetic tasks generated by combining modules, as well as gridworld environments with compositional rewards or goals. Baselines include monolithic architectures (ANIL, MAML) and both linear and nonlinear hypernetworks. Evaluation metrics include OOD accuracy on held-out module combinations, mean-squared error for action-value prediction, and policy accuracy relative to optimal behavior. Key experimental variables include the structure of the training task distribution (compositional vs. non-compositional, connected vs. disconnected support), the degree of overparameterization, and the number of modules and their combinations.
7d40654b344cc7ede5b793b573188a5b6be4464f.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a new theoretical framework linking compositional generalization to module identification in modular neural networks, establishing necessary and sufficient conditions for identifiability in multi-task settings. It provides the first formal proof that observing a linear (rather than exponential) number of module combinations suffices for compositional generalization under specific support conditions. The empirical studies extend these findings to practical meta-learning scenarios, demonstrating that modular hypernetworks can discover and generalize modular solutions in complex environments, outperforming monolithic baselines. The work also reveals the critical importance of compositional and connected support in the training distribution, and characterizes the effects of overparameterization on modular identification and generalization.

7d46073cce9f5ed8d931b804cfaf327201dd4e26.title: SPDF: Sparse Pre-training and Dense Fine-tuning for Large Language Models
7d46073cce9f5ed8d931b804cfaf327201dd4e26.research_question: How can the computational cost of pre-training large language models be significantly reduced without sacrificing downstream task performance, and what is the relationship between pre-training sparsity, model size, and downstream task complexity?
7d46073cce9f5ed8d931b804cfaf327201dd4e26.hypothesis: 1. High degrees of weight sparsity can be used during the pre-training phase of large language models while preserving downstream accuracy with dense fine-tuning. 2. The performance of the sparse pre-trained model is correlated with the dataset size and degree of difficulty in the downstream task. 3. As the size of the language model increases, models become more amenable to higher levels of sparsity during pre-training.
7d46073cce9f5ed8d931b804cfaf327201dd4e26.proposed_method: A novel framework, Sparse Pre-training and Dense Fine-tuning (SPDF), is proposed to decouple model capacity between pre-training and fine-tuning phases. During pre-training, unstructured weight sparsity is induced in the model, such that only a subset of weights are active, thereby reducing the number of floating point operations (FLOPs) required. Sparsity masks are applied statically and uniformly across layers, with the mask remaining fixed throughout pre-training. After pre-training, the model transitions to a dense fine-tuning phase where all previously zeroed weights are reactivated and allowed to learn, thus restoring the model's full representational capacity. The dense fine-tuning is performed on downstream tasks using supervised datasets, allowing the model to adapt to task-specific requirements and recover any representational power lost during sparse pre-training.
7d46073cce9f5ed8d931b804cfaf327201dd4e26.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using GPT-2 Small (125M parameters) and GPT-3 XL (1.3B parameters) models. Pre-training is performed from scratch on the Pile dataset, following Chinchilla scaling laws for token-to-parameter ratios, and inducing static unstructured sparsity at levels of 50% and 75%. Fine-tuning is carried out in a dense manner on four downstream tasks: E2E NLG, WebNLG, DART (data-to-text generation), and Curation Corpus (text summarization). Official evaluation scripts are used to report BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE-L, and CIDEr scores, as well as perplexity for summarization. Baselines include dense pre-training with dense fine-tuning and sparse pre-training with sparse fine-tuning. All models are trained and evaluated on Cerebras CS-2 hardware, which supports efficient unstructured sparsity.
7d46073cce9f5ed8d931b804cfaf327201dd4e26.novelty_claims: The proposed SPDF framework is the first to demonstrate that large GPT models can be pre-trained with high levels of unstructured weight sparsity (up to 75%) without significant loss in downstream task performance, while achieving up to 2.5x reduction in pre-training FLOPs. The approach establishes a clear relationship between optimal sparsity, task complexity, and dataset size, and shows that larger models are more robust to higher sparsity levels. The method leverages recent hardware advances to translate theoretical FLOP reductions into practical speedups, and provides detailed analysis of parameter subspaces to understand adaptation dynamics between sparse pre-training and dense fine-tuning.

7d4ef1850eaed82a86cbf51828e7874d389a69bc.title: Learning non-equilibrium diffusions with Schrödinger bridges: from exactly solvable to simulation-free
7d4ef1850eaed82a86cbf51828e7874d389a69bc.research_question: How can the most likely evolution of a stochastic dynamical system, compatible with observed initial and final distributions, be reconstructed when the underlying dynamics are non-equilibrium and not necessarily potential-driven, particularly for high-dimensional and biologically relevant systems?
7d4ef1850eaed82a86cbf51828e7874d389a69bc.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging multivariate Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (mvOU) processes as reference dynamics, combined with a simulation-free score and flow matching approach, enables accurate and efficient reconstruction of non-equilibrium Schrödinger bridges for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian marginals, outperforming existing simulation-based methods in accuracy and computational efficiency.
7d4ef1850eaed82a86cbf51828e7874d389a69bc.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces a framework for learning Schrödinger bridges where the reference process is a multivariate Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (mvOU) process with a generic, potentially asymmetric drift matrix, allowing for non-equilibrium and non-gradient-driven dynamics. For Gaussian marginals, explicit analytical solutions for the bridge, including the mean, covariance, score, and flow fields, are derived using properties of the mvOU process and entropic optimal transport. For general (non-Gaussian) marginals, a simulation-free algorithm (MVOU-OTFM) is developed, which first solves the static Schrödinger bridge problem via Sinkhorn-Knopp iterations with an analytically tractable cost, then employs neural networks to parameterize the score and flow fields, trained by minimizing a conditional score and flow matching loss using exact bridge statistics. The approach exploits the analytical tractability of mvOU bridges to avoid costly SDE simulations, enabling efficient training and inference even in high dimensions.
7d4ef1850eaed82a86cbf51828e7874d389a69bc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real datasets. For Gaussian marginals, high-dimensional settings (e.g., d = 2 to 100) will be used to benchmark the accuracy of the proposed method against baselines such as Iterative Proportional Maximum Likelihood (IPML), Neural Lagrangian Schrödinger Bridge (NLSB), and Brownian-motion-based OTFM, using metrics like the Bures-Wasserstein distance for marginal error and L2 norm for vector field error. For non-Gaussian marginals, the method will be evaluated on synthetic data and real single-cell RNA sequencing data, including the cell cycle dataset with experimentally measured velocity fields, and a biophysical repressilator system, with performance measured via earth mover's distance (EMD), energy distance, and interpolation accuracy. Computational efficiency (training time) and scalability to high dimensions (up to d = 100) will also be assessed, and the effect of reference process parameterization (e.g., drift scaling) will be systematically explored.
7d4ef1850eaed82a86cbf51828e7874d389a69bc.novelty_claims: The proposal claims several key innovations: (1) extension of Schrödinger bridge learning to non-equilibrium systems using mvOU reference processes with generic, asymmetric drift, enabling modeling of non-gradient-driven dynamics; (2) derivation of explicit analytical solutions for Gaussian Schrödinger bridges under mvOU dynamics, generalizing prior results limited to Brownian or scalar OU references; (3) development of a simulation-free, score and flow matching algorithm (MVOU-OTFM) for learning bridges with general marginals, leveraging closed-form bridge statistics for efficient and accurate training; (4) demonstration of superior accuracy and speed compared to state-of-the-art simulation-based methods, particularly in high-dimensional and biologically relevant applications.

7d5c1808cef30e747b35bb1a3e4628c66da6100b.title: Learning Regularized Monotone Graphon Mean-Field Games
7d5c1808cef30e747b35bb1a3e4628c66da6100b.research_question: How can Nash Equilibria be efficiently learned and guaranteed to exist in regularized Graphon Mean-Field Games (GMFGs) under weak monotonicity and minimal continuity assumptions, particularly in discrete-time and heterogeneous agent settings?
7d5c1808cef30e747b35bb1a3e4628c66da6100b.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that Nash Equilibria exist in regularized GMFGs under weaker continuity and compactness assumptions than previously required, and that a discrete-time policy mirror descent algorithm can efficiently learn the unique NE in weakly monotone GMFGs with provable convergence rates, even when action-value function oracles are unavailable.
7d5c1808cef30e747b35bb1a3e4628c66da6100b.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed to establish the existence of Nash Equilibria in λ-regularized GMFGs for any λ ≥ 0, relying only on compactness of the state space, finiteness of the action space, and continuity (not necessarily Lipschitz) of the graphon, transition kernel, and reward functions. The approach constructs a regularized MFG from the original GMFG and demonstrates that an NE of the constructed MFG can be mapped to an NE of the GMFG, thus circumventing the challenge of uncountably infinite agents. For learning the NE in monotone GMFGs, a discrete-time Policy Mirror Descent algorithm (MonoGMFG-PMD) is developed, which iteratively updates each agent's policy using mirror descent steps, incorporates entropy regularization to encourage exploration, and, when necessary, estimates action-value functions from sampled agent data using general function approximation classes. The algorithm is designed to operate in an online, decentralized fashion, requiring only local agent interactions and sampled trajectories.
7d5c1808cef30e747b35bb1a3e4628c66da6100b.experiment_details: Empirical evaluation will be conducted on synthetic and/or benchmark GMFG environments that instantiate the proposed model, with varying degrees of agent heterogeneity and graphon structure. The experiments will compare MonoGMFG-PMD against prior continuous-time and contraction-based discrete-time baselines, assessing both convergence rate and final exploitability. Metrics will include the KL divergence between learned and ground-truth NE policies, cumulative reward, and generalization error due to action-value estimation. The setup will consider both oracle and non-oracle (estimated) action-value settings, with controlled numbers of sampled agents (N) and episodes (K) to evaluate the impact of sampling and estimation error on convergence.
7d5c1808cef30e747b35bb1a3e4628c66da6100b.novelty_claims: The proposed research establishes the first existence result for Nash Equilibria in regularized GMFGs under only continuity and compactness assumptions, relaxing prior requirements of Lipschitzness and contraction. It introduces the first provably efficient discrete-time algorithm for learning NE in monotone GMFGs, with explicit convergence rates and support for online, decentralized learning. The approach also innovates by integrating action-value function estimation as a submodule, enabling learning without access to value oracles, and provides theoretical analysis quantifying the impact of sampling and estimation errors. These contributions address key gaps in the theory and practice of large-scale, heterogeneous mean-field games.

7d8905a1fd288068f12c8347caeabefd36d0dd6c.title: Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs
7d8905a1fd288068f12c8347caeabefd36d0dd6c.research_question: How can large language models be enabled to accurately and reliably invoke API calls from a massive, dynamic, and overlapping set of APIs, while minimizing hallucinations and adapting to changes in API documentation?
7d8905a1fd288068f12c8347caeabefd36d0dd6c.hypothesis: Fine-tuning a large language model with a retrieval-augmented training paradigm and a comprehensive, instruction-based API dataset will significantly improve the model's ability to generate accurate API calls, reduce hallucinations, and adapt to changes in API documentation compared to existing state-of-the-art models.
7d8905a1fd288068f12c8347caeabefd36d0dd6c.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed that fine-tunes a large language model (LLaMA-7B) specifically for the task of generating API calls from natural language prompts. The method will utilize a large, curated dataset (APIBench) containing over 1,600 APIs from TorchHub, TensorFlowHub, and HuggingFace, with each API paired with multiple synthetic user instructions generated via self-instruct techniques. During training, the model will be exposed to both zero-shot and retrieval-augmented settings, where the most relevant API documentation is retrieved (using BM25, GPT-Index, or an oracle retriever) and appended to the prompt. The fine-tuning process will use a conversational format, simulating user-agent interactions, and will include both functional and constraint-based API invocation scenarios. Evaluation of generated API calls will be performed using AST sub-tree matching to assess functional correctness and detect hallucinations.
7d8905a1fd288068f12c8347caeabefd36d0dd6c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the APIBench dataset, which includes exhaustive API coverage for TorchHub and TensorFlowHub, and a filtered set of the most popular HuggingFace models across multiple domains. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art LLMs such as GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Claude, and LLaMA-7B, evaluated in both zero-shot and retrieval-augmented settings. Evaluation metrics will include overall accuracy (via AST sub-tree matching), hallucination rate (calls to non-existent APIs), and error rate (incorrect API usage). Additional experiments will assess the model's ability to handle constraint-based API selection (e.g., accuracy, parameter size) and its adaptability to test-time changes in API documentation. Holdout test sets will be used to ensure robust evaluation, and ablation studies will examine the impact of different retrievers and training paradigms.
7d8905a1fd288068f12c8347caeabefd36d0dd6c.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first large-scale, retrieval-augmented fine-tuning paradigm for LLMs focused on API call generation, leveraging a comprehensive and diverse API dataset. The approach systematically addresses the challenges of hallucination and adaptation to dynamic API documentation, which are not adequately handled by prior work. The use of AST sub-tree matching for functional evaluation and the inclusion of constraint-aware API selection represent novel contributions. The resulting system is expected to outperform existing LLMs in both accuracy and reliability for tool usage via APIs, and the curated dataset and evaluation framework will serve as valuable resources for future research.

7d8efac3372be83b77ef1b3950e032965036159e.title: RGB↔X: Image decomposition and synthesis using material- and lighting-aware diffusion models
7d8efac3372be83b77ef1b3950e032965036159e.research_question: How can a unified, material- and lighting-aware diffusion framework be developed for both decomposing images into intrinsic channels and synthesizing realistic images from such channels, particularly in the domain of indoor scenes?
7d8efac3372be83b77ef1b3950e032965036159e.hypothesis: A unified diffusion-based framework, trained on heterogeneous datasets and capable of handling partial or complete intrinsic channel information, will enable accurate intrinsic image decomposition and realistic image synthesis, outperforming existing specialized methods in both tasks.
7d8efac3372be83b77ef1b3950e032965036159e.proposed_method: A unified conditional diffusion framework will be developed to address both image decomposition (RGB→X) and synthesis (X→RGB) tasks. The RGB→X model will fine-tune a pre-trained latent diffusion model (Stable Diffusion 2.1), using a prompt-switching mechanism to estimate per-pixel intrinsic channels: albedo, normal, roughness, metallicity, and diffuse irradiance. The X→RGB model will also be based on Stable Diffusion 2.1, concatenating encoded intrinsic channels as conditioning inputs and employing channel dropout to enable flexible input subsets. Lighting information will be provided as a downsampled hint rather than high-resolution control, and the model will be further fine-tuned for inpainting by incorporating mask channels. Both models will leverage a combination of synthetic and real datasets, with additional channels estimated as needed, and will use text prompts for further conditional control.
7d8efac3372be83b77ef1b3950e032965036159e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a combination of four heterogeneous datasets: InteriorVerse, Hypersim, Evermotion, and a newly constructed ImageDecomp dataset, each providing various subsets of the required intrinsic channels. The RGB→X model will be evaluated on both synthetic (Hypersim, Evermotion) and real-world (IIW, MIT Indoor Scene Recognition) images, with quantitative comparisons against state-of-the-art baselines for albedo, normal, roughness, and metallicity estimation using PSNR and LPIPS metrics. The X→RGB model will be assessed by synthesizing images from ground-truth and estimated intrinsic channels, comparing results to path-traced references and prior neural rendering approaches. Additional experiments will demonstrate the flexibility of the framework for downstream editing tasks such as material replacement, relighting, and object insertion, using both full and partial channel inputs and optional text prompts.
7d8efac3372be83b77ef1b3950e032965036159e.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to unify both intrinsic image decomposition and synthesis within a single diffusion-based architecture, supporting both tasks with shared components. It introduces a material- and lighting-aware approach that handles heterogeneous and incomplete training data via channel dropout, and enables flexible conditioning at inference. The method supports both high-quality estimation of intrinsic channels and realistic image generation from partial or edited channels, facilitating novel editing applications such as material editing, relighting, and object insertion without requiring full scene specification or ray tracing. The approach demonstrates superior performance to specialized baselines in both decomposition and synthesis tasks, and enables new forms of controllable, realistic image editing in the indoor scene domain.

7d97c17a75beb89f938eaac1d3ca60ac2245fb2e.title: Faith and Fate: Limits of Transformers on Compositionality
7d97c17a75beb89f938eaac1d3ca60ac2245fb2e.research_question: What are the fundamental limitations of transformer-based large language models in performing compositional reasoning tasks that require multi-step, systematic problem-solving, and under what conditions do these models succeed or fail?
7d97c17a75beb89f938eaac1d3ca60ac2245fb2e.hypothesis: 1) Transformer language models solve compositional tasks primarily by reducing multi-step reasoning into linearized pattern or subgraph matching, rather than developing systematic, rule-based problem-solving abilities. 2) Due to error propagation, transformers have inherent limitations in solving high-complexity compositional tasks, with performance degrading rapidly as task complexity increases.
7d97c17a75beb89f938eaac1d3ca60ac2245fb2e.proposed_method: The proposed research will systematically evaluate transformer language models on a suite of representative compositional tasks, including multi-digit multiplication, logic grid puzzles (such as Einstein's puzzle), and a dynamic programming problem (maximum weighted independent set in a sequence). Each task will be formalized as a computation graph, where nodes represent intermediate variables and edges denote functional dependencies, enabling precise quantification of reasoning depth, width, and parallelism. The methodology will involve linearizing these computation graphs into input sequences suitable for autoregressive language models, and employing both question-answer and question-scratchpad (step-by-step reasoning) formats. Relative information gain will be used to predict and analyze the surface patterns that models are likely to learn, providing insight into the types of shortcuts or memorization strategies employed by the models.
7d97c17a75beb89f938eaac1d3ca60ac2245fb2e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using state-of-the-art transformer models (e.g., GPT-3, ChatGPT, GPT-4) under zero-shot, few-shot, and fine-tuning regimes. For each compositional task, datasets will be constructed to cover a range of problem sizes and compositional complexities, with explicit splits for in-domain and out-of-domain (OOD) evaluation. Baselines will include both direct answer prediction and explicit reasoning via scratchpads. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on final answers, accuracy on intermediate reasoning steps, and error analysis across graph layers. Additional analyses will measure the frequency of subgraph overlap between training and test instances, and categorize error types (local, propagation, restoration) at different reasoning depths. Theoretical analysis will complement empirical findings by modeling error propagation and its exponential impact on performance as task complexity increases.
7d97c17a75beb89f938eaac1d3ca60ac2245fb2e.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a rigorous framework for quantifying and analyzing compositional reasoning in transformers using computation graphs and associated complexity metrics. It claims to provide both empirical and theoretical evidence that transformers rely on shallow pattern matching rather than systematic reasoning, and that their performance on compositional tasks degrades exponentially with increased complexity due to error accumulation. The research will offer new diagnostic tools (e.g., subgraph frequency analysis, information gain metrics) and a comprehensive error taxonomy, yielding insights into the fundamental limitations of current transformer architectures and informing future directions for robust, generalizable reasoning in language models.

7d9b141b75f125ade3e6073abf7b72e0dae624de.title: Scaling Laws for Optimal Data Mixtures
7d9b141b75f125ade3e6073abf7b72e0dae624de.research_question: How can the optimal mixture of data domains for pretraining large models be systematically determined to maximize performance on a target domain, without relying on costly trial-and-error, and can this approach generalize across different model architectures and modalities?
7d9b141b75f125ade3e6073abf7b72e0dae624de.hypothesis: Scaling laws can be extended to accurately model the effect of data domain mixtures on model performance, enabling principled prediction and optimization of domain weights for any target domain and training budget, using only small-scale experiments.
7d9b141b75f125ade3e6073abf7b72e0dae624de.proposed_method: A systematic framework will be developed to predict the loss of a model trained with a specific mixture of data domains, model size N, and number of training tokens D, by extending scaling laws to incorporate domain weight vectors. Two parametric forms of scaling laws will be formulated: an additive law where only the bias term depends on the domain weights, and a joint law where both bias and scale-dependent terms are functions of the domain weights, allowing for interaction between scale and mixture. The parameters of these scaling laws will be fitted using a small number of training runs with varying domain weights, model sizes, and token counts, leveraging optimization techniques such as Basin-hopping with L-BFGS to efficiently explore the high-dimensional parameter space. Once fitted, these scaling laws will be used to solve an optimization problem on the simplex to find the domain weight vector that minimizes the predicted loss for any target domain and training budget.
7d9b141b75f125ade3e6073abf7b72e0dae624de.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across three large-scale pretraining settings: large language models (LLMs) using the SlimPajama and Pile datasets (with 4-8 text domains), native multimodal models (NMMs) with three domain types (text, paired image-caption, and interleaved multimodal data), and large vision models (LVMs) with four image-caption domains of varying quality and noise. Models will range from 90M to 8B parameters and be trained on up to 334B tokens. For each setting, scaling laws will be fitted using small-scale training runs with different domain weights, and then extrapolated to predict losses for larger models and unseen domain mixtures. Baselines will include models trained with uniform domain weights and with standard dataset-proportional mixtures. Evaluation metrics will include the Mean Relative Error (MRE) between predicted and observed losses, as well as downstream task performance on benchmarks such as CORE, MMLU, Arc, BoolQ, PIQA, SIQA, HellaSwag, and Winogrande. The computational cost (FLOPs) for small- and large-scale runs will be tracked to demonstrate efficiency gains.
7d9b141b75f125ade3e6073abf7b72e0dae624de.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled, scalable method for selecting optimal data mixtures for pretraining large models, replacing ad-hoc trial-and-error with predictive scaling laws that generalize across domains, modalities, and scales. The method enables accurate extrapolation from small-scale experiments to large-scale model performance and allows for the optimization of domain weights tailored to specific target domains or downstream tasks. The framework is validated across language, multimodal, and vision models, and demonstrates that only a small number of small-scale runs are needed to estimate optimal mixtures, resulting in improved model performance over standard baselines.

7da0f2501034522e3d50af7e9b8fa7ec9d7b65b6.title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
7da0f2501034522e3d50af7e9b8fa7ec9d7b65b6.research_question: How can large-scale generative pre-trained transformer (GPT) models be efficiently quantized post-training to significantly reduce memory and computational requirements for inference, while maintaining high accuracy across language modeling tasks?
7da0f2501034522e3d50af7e9b8fa7ec9d7b65b6.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a novel post-training quantization algorithm leveraging approximate second-order information can compress very large GPT models to 3-4 bits per weight with minimal accuracy loss, enabling efficient single-GPU inference and substantial speedups compared to existing methods.
7da0f2501034522e3d50af7e9b8fa7ec9d7b65b6.proposed_method: A new post-training quantization framework, termed GPTQ, will be developed to efficiently quantize the weights of large transformer-based language models. The method will build on and extend the Optimal Brain Quantization (OBQ) approach by introducing several key innovations: (1) quantizing all rows of a weight matrix in the same order to enable efficient block-wise updates, (2) applying lazy batch-updates to maximize GPU utilization and mitigate memory bandwidth bottlenecks, and (3) employing a numerically stable Cholesky-based reformulation for inverse Hessian computations, with dampening to prevent instability in large models. The quantization process will be performed layer-by-layer, minimizing the squared error between the quantized and original layer outputs using a fixed quantization grid. The algorithm will support various quantization granularities, including per-row and group-wise quantization, and will be implemented to operate efficiently on commodity GPUs, with support for extremely large models (up to 175 billion parameters) in a matter of hours.
7da0f2501034522e3d50af7e9b8fa7ec9d7b65b6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the OPT and BLOOM model families, including the largest available models (OPT-175B and BLOOM-176B). The quantization process will use 128 random 2048-token segments from the C4 dataset for calibration, ensuring a zero-shot evaluation setting. Baselines will include round-to-nearest (RTN) quantization and state-of-the-art post-training quantization methods such as AdaRound, AdaQuant, and BRECQ, with comparisons on both vision (ResNet18/50) and language models (BERT-base, OPT-125M). Evaluation metrics will include perplexity on WikiText2, Penn Treebank (PTB), and C4, as well as accuracy on zero-shot tasks like LAMBADA, ARC, and PIQA. The experimental setup will also measure quantization runtime, memory usage, and end-to-end inference speedups on NVIDIA A100 and A6000 GPUs, including custom CUDA kernels for efficient quantized inference.
7da0f2501034522e3d50af7e9b8fa7ec9d7b65b6.novelty_claims: The proposed method claims to be the first to enable accurate post-training quantization of language models with hundreds of billions of parameters to 3-4 bits per weight, with negligible accuracy degradation. It introduces a scalable, efficient, and numerically stable algorithm that achieves more than double the compression gains of prior one-shot quantization methods, while maintaining or exceeding their accuracy. The method further demonstrates, for the first time, that such compressed models can be executed for generative inference on a single GPU, with practical end-to-end speedups of up to 4.5x compared to FP16 baselines. Additionally, the approach is shown to be robust even in extreme quantization regimes (2-bit or ternary), and is compatible with advanced quantization schemes such as group-wise quantization.

7dae752721176a5d1a2d50b951c8e7471d137195.title: Richelieu: Self-Evolving LLM-Based Agents for AI Diplomacy
7dae752721176a5d1a2d50b951c8e7471d137195.research_question: Can a large language model (LLM)-based agent be developed to master the complex multi-agent game of Diplomacy, achieving human-like negotiation, social reasoning, long-term planning, and self-evolution, without relying on domain-specific human data?
7dae752721176a5d1a2d50b951c8e7471d137195.hypothesis: A self-evolving LLM-based agent that integrates social reasoning, hierarchical planning with reflection, negotiation, and memory management can outperform existing AI Diplomacy agents, including those trained on human data, by leveraging self-play for continual improvement.
7dae752721176a5d1a2d50b951c8e7471d137195.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be constructed for an LLM-based Diplomacy agent, incorporating modules for social reasoning, strategic planning with reflection, negotiation, decision-making, memory management, and self-evolution. The agent will analyze the current game state to infer social relationships and intentions, propose sub-goals aligned with long-term objectives, and negotiate with other agents using a dedicated reasoning flow to assess the veracity and intentions of opponents. Memory management will archive historical game states, sub-goals, negotiation messages, actions, and evaluations, supporting both short-term and long-term learning. The agent will self-evolve by engaging in multi-agent self-play, controlling all countries to simulate diverse experiences, and using memory-based reflection to optimize strategies over time without human demonstrations.
7dae752721176a5d1a2d50b951c8e7471d137195.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the open-source Diplomacy game platform, enabling both press (with negotiation) and no-press (without negotiation) settings. The agent will be evaluated against six baseline models, including Cicero (state-of-the-art negotiation agent), SL-DipNet, RL-DipNet, BRPI, SearchBot, DORA, and an LLM-based AutoGPT agent. Evaluation metrics will include win rate, most supply centers (MostSC) rate, survived rate, defeated rate, and C-Diplo scoring (used in international competitions). Each model will play as a randomly assigned country over 1000 rounds to obtain average results. Additional experiments will test the framework's compatibility with different LLMs (GPT-4.0, ERNIEBot, SparkDesk, Llama3), and ablation studies will assess the contribution of each module. Social reasoning accuracy will be measured by the agent's ability to infer relationships and intentions across different LLMs.
7dae752721176a5d1a2d50b951c8e7471d137195.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified, self-evolving LLM-based agent for Diplomacy that does not require any domain-specific human data for training, in contrast to prior methods. The framework integrates social reasoning, hierarchical planning with reflection, negotiation, and memory management into a single architecture, enabling continual self-improvement via self-play. The method demonstrates generalization across multiple LLMs and provides a modular design that can be extended to other multi-agent social interaction tasks. Ablation studies and competitive benchmarks show that each module contributes significantly to overall performance, and the agent achieves superior results compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

7dbb386a617eacc954940c9540d9cb262529b8b1.title: Equivariant Diffusion for Molecule Generation in 3D
7dbb386a617eacc954940c9540d9cb262529b8b1.research_question: How can generative models be designed to efficiently and accurately generate 3D molecular structures while respecting the symmetries of physical space, such as rotations, translations, and reflections?
7dbb386a617eacc954940c9540d9cb262529b8b1.hypothesis: A diffusion-based generative model that is equivariant to Euclidean transformations (E(3)) and jointly operates on both continuous (atom coordinates) and categorical (atom types) features will outperform existing methods in generating valid, stable, and diverse 3D molecular structures, and will scale better to larger molecules.
7dbb386a617eacc954940c9540d9cb262529b8b1.proposed_method: A novel E(3) Equivariant Diffusion Model (EDM) is proposed for 3D molecule generation. The method defines a diffusion process that adds noise to both the atomic coordinates and categorical features (such as atom types and charges), and learns to reverse this process using an equivariant neural network based on E(n) Equivariant Graph Neural Networks (EGNNs). The denoising network predicts the noise added at each step, ensuring that the generative process is equivariant to rotations, translations, and reflections. The model is capable of handling both continuous and discrete features by defining appropriate noise processes and likelihood computations for each type, including one-hot encodings for categorical features. Training is performed by minimizing a simplified variational lower bound on the log-likelihood, and the model is extended to allow for conditional generation on molecular properties by concatenating property information to the node features during both training and sampling.
7dbb386a617eacc954940c9540d9cb262529b8b1.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the QM9 dataset (130k molecules with up to 29 atoms) and the larger GEOM-Drugs dataset (430k molecules, up to 181 atoms). The model is evaluated on unconditional and conditional molecule generation tasks. Baselines include E(3) equivariant normalizing flows (E-NF), G-Schnet, and non-equivariant graph diffusion models (GDM), with and without data augmentation. Evaluation metrics include negative log-likelihood, atom stability (correct valency), molecule stability (all atoms stable), validity and uniqueness (using RDKit), and Wasserstein distance between generated and real energy distributions. For conditional generation, a property classifier is used to assess whether generated molecules match desired properties. All models are trained with consistent architectures (e.g., 9 layers, 256 features per layer for QM9; 4 layers for GEOM-Drugs), using Adam optimizer and batch size 64.
7dbb386a617eacc954940c9540d9cb262529b8b1.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first diffusion model to directly generate molecules in 3D space with explicit E(3) equivariance, jointly modeling both continuous coordinates and categorical features. It enables likelihood computation for generated molecules, scales efficiently to larger molecules and datasets, and outperforms previous 3D molecular generative models in terms of sample quality, stability, and training efficiency. The approach also provides a unified framework for conditional generation and likelihood estimation in 3D molecular generation.

7dc4edab8203f9993ae5805b453b3ecc12564f4c.title: Stochastic Gradient Descent under Markovian Sampling Schemes
7dc4edab8203f9993ae5805b453b3ecc12564f4c.research_question: How can stochastic gradient descent methods be efficiently performed when the optimizer has access only to samples generated by a Markov chain, and what are the fundamental convergence rates and communication efficiencies achievable under minimal assumptions on the Markov chain and the objective functions?
7dc4edab8203f9993ae5805b453b3ecc12564f4c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, under mild assumptions on the Markov chain and the objective functions, stochastic gradient descent algorithms that leverage all gradients along the Markov chain trajectory can achieve provably faster convergence rates and improved communication efficiency compared to consensus-based decentralized optimization methods. Furthermore, variance reduction techniques can further improve the convergence rates, potentially matching lower bounds determined by the hitting time of the Markov chain.
7dc4edab8203f9993ae5805b453b3ecc12564f4c.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and algorithmic framework will be developed for stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and variance-reduced SGD under Markov-chain sampling schemes. The approach will first establish oracle complexity lower bounds for any algorithm that samples gradients along a Markov chain, identifying the hitting time as a fundamental bottleneck. Then, the Markov Chain SGD (MC-SGD) algorithm will be analyzed under minimal regularity assumptions, removing the need for bounded gradients and allowing for arbitrary data heterogeneity. To further improve convergence, a variance-reduced alternative, MC-SAG (Markov Chain Stochastic Average Gradient), will be introduced, which maintains and updates gradient estimates at each node and uses a time-adaptive step size policy based on the chain's hitting time. The method will also be extended to incorporate local noise, enabling differential privacy guarantees. All algorithms will be designed to operate in decentralized settings, where the Markov chain corresponds to a random walk on a communication graph.
7dc4edab8203f9993ae5805b453b3ecc12564f4c.experiment_details: Theoretical analysis will be conducted to derive convergence rates for MC-SGD and MC-SAG under various assumptions, including smoothness, strong convexity, and the Polyak-Łojasiewicz condition. Lower bounds will be established for the oracle complexity of Markov chain-based sampling schemes, and upper bounds will be proven for the proposed algorithms, with explicit dependence on the hitting and mixing times of the Markov chain. Comparisons will be made to consensus-based decentralized optimization algorithms and gossip-based methods, using communication complexity as a key metric.
