Synthetic experiments will be conducted on graphs with varying connectivity (e.g., cycles, tori, complete graphs) and with heterogeneous and homogeneous data distributions to empirically validate the theoretical findings. Evaluation metrics will include the number of communications required to reach an ε-stationary point, convergence rates, and robustness to stragglers.
7dc4edab8203f9993ae5805b453b3ecc12564f4c.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first tight oracle complexity lower bounds for stochastic optimization under Markov chain sampling, identifying the hitting time as the key limiting factor. It provides the first convergence analysis of MC-SGD under minimal regularity assumptions, removing the need for bounded gradients. The MC-SAG algorithm is proposed as a variance-reduced, communication-efficient alternative that achieves optimal rates up to acceleration, depending only on the hitting time rather than the mixing time or graph size. The framework formally demonstrates that using all gradients along the Markov chain trajectory leads to provably faster convergence than waiting for mixing, and establishes that random-walk-based decentralization is more communication-efficient than consensus-based approaches. Extensions to differential privacy and robustness to stragglers are also claimed.

7dc6da87eaa6f830354feb2db14023cab8678c91.title: ImageBind One Embedding Space to Bind Them All
7dc6da87eaa6f830354feb2db14023cab8678c91.research_question: How can a single joint embedding space be learned to effectively align and bind multiple diverse modalities—including images, text, audio, depth, thermal, and IMU data—without requiring all possible combinations of paired data, and what emergent capabilities can such a space enable for zero-shot and few-shot recognition and retrieval tasks across modalities?
7dc6da87eaa6f830354feb2db14023cab8678c91.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that aligning each modality to images using only image-paired data is sufficient to induce emergent alignment across all modalities in a shared embedding space, thereby enabling zero-shot and few-shot capabilities for modalities that were never directly paired during training.
7dc6da87eaa6f830354feb2db14023cab8678c91.proposed_method: A joint embedding space will be constructed by training modality-specific encoders (for images, text, audio, depth, thermal, and IMU) to align their outputs to image embeddings using contrastive learning. Only naturally occurring image-paired datasets (e.g., image-text, image-depth, video-audio, image-thermal, video-IMU) will be used, without requiring all modalities to be paired together. Each encoder will be based on a Transformer architecture (e.g., ViT for images, spectrograms for audio, 1D Transformer for IMU), with a modality-specific linear projection head to produce normalized embeddings. The InfoNCE loss will be applied to align each modality with images, and pretrained vision-language models (e.g., CLIP) may be used to initialize image and text encoders for improved performance. The training will leverage large-scale web datasets for image-text and other naturally paired modality data, with careful data augmentation and architectural choices to optimize emergent cross-modal alignment.
7dc6da87eaa6f830354feb2db14023cab8678c91.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate the joint embedding space on a wide range of zero-shot and few-shot classification and retrieval tasks across all six modalities. Datasets include AudioSet, ESC, Clotho, AudioCaps, VGGSound (audio), SUN RGB-D and NYU-v2 (depth), LLVIP (thermal), Ego4D (IMU), and standard vision-language benchmarks such as ImageNet, Places-365, Kinetics-400, and MSR-VTT. Baselines will include specialist supervised models, models trained with explicit paired data for each modality, and existing multimodal frameworks (e.g., CLIP, AudioCLIP, MultiMAE). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, mean average precision, and recall at K, depending on the task. The experimental setup will also investigate the impact of encoder capacity, batch size, data augmentation, and architectural choices through ablation studies.
7dc6da87eaa6f830354feb2db14023cab8678c91.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a scalable and practical method for learning a single joint embedding space across six diverse modalities using only image-paired data, eliminating the need for all-pairs supervision. This method enables emergent zero-shot and few-shot recognition and retrieval capabilities for modalities that were never directly paired during training, outperforming or matching specialist models on several benchmarks. The framework also demonstrates novel compositional abilities, such as embedding-space arithmetic and cross-modal generation, and provides a new way to evaluate and upgrade pretrained vision models for non-visual tasks.

7dc928f41e15f65f1267bd87b0fcfcc7e715cb56.title: Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting
7dc928f41e15f65f1267bd87b0fcfcc7e715cb56.research_question: How faithful are the explanations generated by large language models during chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting, and to what extent do these explanations accurately reflect the true decision-making process of the models, particularly in the presence of input features that can bias predictions?
7dc928f41e15f65f1267bd87b0fcfcc7e715cb56.hypothesis: Chain-of-thought explanations produced by large language models are not always faithful to the actual reasoning process that leads to their predictions, and can be systematically influenced by input biases without acknowledging these influences in the explanations.
7dc928f41e15f65f1267bd87b0fcfcc7e715cb56.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation framework will be developed to assess the faithfulness of CoT explanations in large language models. The approach involves introducing controlled biasing features into model inputs, such as reordering answer choices or suggesting specific answers, and measuring the resulting changes in both model predictions and generated explanations. The method will compare model behavior on unbiased versus biased contexts, and will analyze whether explanations acknowledge the influence of the biasing features. Counterfactual simulatability will be used to determine if explanations help humans predict model behavior under input perturbations. Additionally, the method will include both objective and subjective tasks, and will extend to social bias benchmarks where weak evidence is manipulated to test consistency and stereotype alignment in explanations.
7dc928f41e15f65f1267bd87b0fcfcc7e715cb56.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using two advanced RLHF-fine-tuned language models: GPT-3.5 (text-davinci-003) and Claude 1.0. The evaluation will utilize the BIG-Bench Hard (BBH) benchmark, focusing on 13 tasks with elements of subjectivity or complex reasoning, and the Bias Benchmark for QA (BBQ), which tests for social stereotype bias. For BBH, input perturbations will include 'Answer is Always A' (reordering answer options) and 'Suggested Answer' (explicitly suggesting a random answer), with both zero-shot and few-shot CoT and No-CoT prompting conditions. For BBQ, ambiguous questions will be augmented with weak evidence in two opposing forms to test consistency. Metrics will include accuracy drops under bias, percentage of unfaithful prediction pairs, and the proportion of unfaithfulness explained by stereotype alignment. Manual annotation will be used for qualitative analysis of explanation support and reasoning errors.
7dc928f41e15f65f1267bd87b0fcfcc7e715cb56.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a systematic adversarial evaluation of CoT explanation faithfulness by directly manipulating input features to induce bias, rather than perturbing explanations themselves. It provides a necessary but not sufficient test for faithfulness, operationalized through counterfactual simulatability in both objective and subjective domains. The approach uniquely combines quantitative accuracy and bias metrics with qualitative manual analysis, and demonstrates that CoT explanations can be plausible yet systematically unfaithful, often rationalizing biased predictions without acknowledging the true underlying influences. The findings aim to inform the development of more transparent and trustworthy AI systems by highlighting the limitations of current CoT-based explainability.

7dd070c7138053f52e41536b3d6ad2b3bd7a3533.title: Vanilla Bayesian Optimization Performs Great in High Dimensions
7dd070c7138053f52e41536b3d6ad2b3bd7a3533.research_question: Can the performance of Bayesian Optimization (BO) in high-dimensional settings be substantially improved by modifying prior assumptions about model complexity, without imposing structural restrictions on the objective function?
7dd070c7138053f52e41536b3d6ad2b3bd7a3533.hypothesis: The limitations of vanilla Bayesian Optimization in high-dimensional problems are primarily due to overly complex prior assumptions rather than inherent dimensionality, and appropriately scaling the Gaussian process lengthscale prior with dimensionality will enable vanilla BO to perform competitively or better than state-of-the-art high-dimensional BO algorithms.
7dd070c7138053f52e41536b3d6ad2b3bd7a3533.proposed_method: A new approach is developed that modifies the standard Bayesian Optimization framework by scaling the prior on the Gaussian process (GP) kernel lengthscales according to the dimensionality of the problem. Specifically, the lengthscale prior is adjusted such that its mode and mean increase proportionally to the square root of the dimensionality, counteracting the exponential growth in distance between points in high-dimensional spaces. This is achieved, for example, by shifting the mean of a log-normal prior on the lengthscales by log(D)/2, where D is the problem dimensionality. The method also fixes the GP signal variance to match the scale of standardized observations, preventing the variance from diminishing during optimization and ensuring meaningful correlation in the data. The approach is plug-and-play, requiring no structural assumptions such as subspace embeddings, additivity, or variable selection, and can be integrated into existing BO pipelines.
7dd070c7138053f52e41536b3d6ad2b3bd7a3533.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of synthetic and real-world high-dimensional optimization tasks, including benchmarks such as MOPTA08 (124D), SVM (388D), Lasso-DNA (180D), and MuJoCo reinforcement learning tasks (Ant: 888D, Humanoid: 6392D). The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art high-dimensional BO algorithms, including subspace methods (e.g., SAASBO, Bounce), local BO (TuRBO, MPD), additive kernel methods (RD-UCB), variable selection (MCTS-VS), and evolutionary strategies (CMA-ES). Evaluation metrics include best observed value (regret) and consistency across 20 repetitions for each task. Acquisition functions such as LogEI are used, and the experimental setup includes standardized initializations and acquisition optimization budgets. The impact of the lengthscale prior and signal variance choices will be ablated, and performance will be assessed for both sparse synthetic functions and real-world problems with thousands of dimensions.
7dd070c7138053f52e41536b3d6ad2b3bd7a3533.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple, theoretically motivated modification to the vanilla Bayesian Optimization algorithm that enables effective optimization in high-dimensional spaces without imposing structural restrictions on the objective. By scaling the GP lengthscale prior with dimensionality, the method achieves manageable model complexity, maintains meaningful correlation, and circumvents the curse of dimensionality. Extensive empirical validation demonstrates that this approach outperforms or matches state-of-the-art high-dimensional BO algorithms on a wide range of real-world tasks, including those with thousands of dimensions. The method is plug-and-play, easy to integrate, and does not require identification of active variables or subspace embeddings, representing a significant advance in the practical applicability of BO for high-dimensional problems.

7dd83c0d4bc97c4153ccfd387420a63094720df1.title: In Defense of Softmax Parametrization for Calibrated and Consistent Learning to Defer
7dd83c0d4bc97c4153ccfd387420a63094720df1.research_question: Can a softmax-based parameterization be designed for learning to defer in classification tasks that provides both statistical consistency and calibrated, bounded probability estimates for classifier and expert correctness, overcoming the limitations of previous surrogate losses?
7dd83c0d4bc97c4153ccfd387420a63094720df1.hypothesis: An asymmetric softmax-based surrogate loss can achieve statistical consistency and induce a bounded, calibrated probability estimator for both classifier and expert accuracy in learning-to-defer frameworks, outperforming or matching previous approaches based on symmetric losses or OvA strategies.
7dd83c0d4bc97c4153ccfd387420a63094720df1.proposed_method: A novel surrogate loss is constructed using an asymmetric softmax parameterization. For a (K+1)-dimensional scoring function, the first K coordinates are mapped using a standard softmax over the class logits, while the (K+1)-th coordinate (representing expert correctness) is mapped using a normalized exponential function that ensures the output lies in [0,1]. The resulting transformation directly maps the scoring function into the desired range of class probabilities and expert accuracy, i.e., Δ_K × [0,1]. The surrogate loss combines a cross-entropy-like term for the classifier with a modified binary logistic loss for the expert, linked by the asymmetric softmax normalization. This design ensures maxima-preserving properties and boundedness, and theoretical analysis is provided to prove statistical consistency and proper calibration of the probability estimates.
7dd83c0d4bc97c4153ccfd387420a63094720df1.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on benchmark datasets including CIFAR-100 (with synthetic experts of varying accuracy), CIFAR10H, HateSpeech, and ImageNet-16H (with real-world expert annotations). The proposed method is compared against baselines using symmetric softmax-based surrogates, symmetric OvA, and asymmetric OvA-based surrogates. Evaluation metrics include misclassification error, coverage (fraction of samples not deferred), expected calibration error (ECE) of expert accuracy estimates, and budgeted error under deferral constraints. WideResNet architectures and SGD are used for CIFAR-100, while pre-trained models are employed for datasets with real-world experts. Multiple trials are run, and statistical significance is assessed using t-tests at the 5% level.
7dd83c0d4bc97c4153ccfd387420a63094720df1.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces an asymmetric softmax parameterization that, for the first time, enables a softmax-based surrogate loss to provide both statistical consistency and bounded, calibrated probability estimates for learning to defer. The work identifies that the root cause of previous unboundedness and miscalibration is the symmetry of the loss function, not the softmax parameterization itself. Theoretical contributions include proofs of consistency, boundedness, and regret transfer bounds. Empirical results demonstrate superior or comparable performance to state-of-the-art baselines in both classification and expert accuracy estimation, with improved coverage and calibration. The approach also establishes a new direction for designing consistent surrogates for learning to defer by leveraging asymmetric multi-class losses.

7de36d6b14aadc8cdb6ad1340b9ca64b15375bca.title: Draft, Sketch, and Prove: Guiding Formal Theorem Provers with Informal Proofs
7de36d6b14aadc8cdb6ad1340b9ca64b15375bca.research_question: How can the process of formalizing mathematical proofs be improved by leveraging the abundance of informal proofs, and can automated theorem provers be effectively guided using information extracted from informal mathematical reasoning?
7de36d6b14aadc8cdb6ad1340b9ca64b15375bca.hypothesis: Incorporating structured information from informal mathematical proofs into the formal proof automation pipeline will significantly improve the success rate of automated theorem provers on challenging mathematical problems, compared to approaches that do not utilize informal proofs.
7de36d6b14aadc8cdb6ad1340b9ca64b15375bca.proposed_method: A three-stage framework is proposed for formal proof automation: (1) Drafting informal proofs for mathematical problems, either by collecting human-written proofs or generating them using large language models trained on mathematical text. (2) Mapping these informal proofs into formal proof sketches using a large language model in a few-shot learning setup, where the model is prompted with aligned examples of informal proofs and their corresponding formal sketches. The resulting formal proof sketch outlines the high-level reasoning steps and leaves open conjectures for further resolution. (3) Employing an off-the-shelf automated prover to fill in the missing details in the proof sketches by attempting to prove the open conjectures. The system is agnostic to the choice of automated prover, allowing for symbolic, neural, or hybrid approaches. The final output is a fully formal proof that can be verified by an interactive theorem prover.
7de36d6b14aadc8cdb6ad1340b9ca64b15375bca.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the miniF2F dataset, which consists of 488 formalized problems from high-school mathematical competitions, with splits for validation and test sets. Informal proofs will be sourced from three categories: the MATH dataset, the Art of Problem Solving website, and manually written proofs, ensuring a parallel corpus of informal statements, informal proofs, and formal statements. Baselines will include direct use of Sledgehammer (an Isabelle proof automation tool), Sledgehammer with additional heuristics, and state-of-the-art neural theorem provers (Thor and Thor with expert iteration). Evaluation will be based on the proportion of problems for which a valid, fully checked formal proof is produced, with success rates compared across baselines and the proposed method. Ablation studies will assess the impact of in-line comments, the presence of informal proofs, and the use of automated provers. Multiple language models (Codex, Minerva at various scales) will be used for generating informal proofs, and the number of autoformalization attempts per problem will be varied to study scaling properties.
7de36d6b14aadc8cdb6ad1340b9ca64b15375bca.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to systematically leverage informal mathematical proofs to guide formal theorem provers via the generation of formal proof sketches. It introduces a pipeline that bridges informal and formal reasoning by mapping informal proofs to structured formal sketches, which are then completed by automated provers. The method demonstrates substantial improvements in automated theorem proving success rates, nearly doubling the performance of strong baselines on a challenging benchmark. It also provides a new dataset of aligned informal and formal proofs and offers a detailed analysis of the interplay between informal proof quality, language model diversity, and formal proof automation. The approach establishes a new state-of-the-art for formal proof automation in Isabelle on the miniF2F dataset.

7de381a18b7fc6f716da6fa4534bc302f4f46dbd.title: MotionDiffuser: Controllable Multi-Agent Motion Prediction Using Diffusion
7de381a18b7fc6f716da6fa4534bc302f4f46dbd.research_question: How can the joint future trajectories of multiple interacting agents be predicted in a way that captures the inherent multimodality, allows for controllable sampling under constraints, and remains permutation-invariant with respect to agent ordering?
7de381a18b7fc6f716da6fa4534bc302f4f46dbd.hypothesis: A conditional diffusion model, equipped with a permutation-invariant transformer-based denoiser and enhanced by PCA-based trajectory compression, can learn a highly multimodal joint distribution over multi-agent futures, enabling both state-of-the-art prediction accuracy and flexible, differentiable constraint enforcement during inference.
7de381a18b7fc6f716da6fa4534bc302f4f46dbd.proposed_method: A conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model will be developed to represent the joint distribution of future trajectories for multiple agents. The method will use a transformer-based denoiser architecture with cross-attention and self-attention layers to ensure permutation invariance and effective context encoding. Trajectories will be compressed using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to reduce dimensionality, improve computational efficiency, and enable exact log-probability inference. During training, the model will be optimized with a simple L2 loss between denoised and ground-truth trajectories, with noise injected at varying levels. At inference, the model will support guided sampling by incorporating arbitrary differentiable cost functions (e.g., attractors, repellers) into the denoising process, allowing for controllable and constrained trajectory generation.
7de381a18b7fc6f716da6fa4534bc302f4f46dbd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Waymo Open Motion Dataset, specifically the Interactive split, which features highly interactive multi-agent scenarios. The proposed model will be evaluated using scene-level joint prediction metrics, including minSADE, minSFDE, SMissRate, mAP, and Overlap, averaged over multiple time horizons and agent types. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art models such as Wayformer, JFP, MultiPath++, SceneTransformer, and others. Ablation studies will assess the impact of PCA compression, transformer architecture, and constraint enforcement techniques. Additional experiments will demonstrate controllable trajectory synthesis by applying attractor and repeller constraints, measuring both realism and constraint satisfaction using metrics such as min/mean ADE/FDE and overlap rates.
7de381a18b7fc6f716da6fa4534bc302f4f46dbd.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a permutation-invariant, transformer-based diffusion model for joint multi-agent motion prediction, capable of learning diverse and multimodal future distributions. A general and flexible constrained sampling framework is developed, enabling trajectory control via arbitrary differentiable cost functions at inference. The method leverages PCA-based latent trajectory diffusion for efficient and accurate representation, and supports exact sample log-probability computation. These innovations enable state-of-the-art performance on multi-agent motion forecasting benchmarks and facilitate a range of novel applications, including rule enforcement, trajectory in-painting, and tailored simulation scenario generation.

7dfc948cc4a08b4a30e7eabfd82d1bd88957d890.title: Nonparametric Instrumental Regression via Kernel Methods is Minimax Optimal
7dfc948cc4a08b4a30e7eabfd82d1bd88957d890.research_question: How can nonparametric instrumental variable (NPIV) regression be performed using kernel methods in a way that is theoretically minimax optimal, robust to identification failures, and achieves strong convergence guarantees in the L2-norm?
7dfc948cc4a08b4a30e7eabfd82d1bd88957d890.hypothesis: Kernel-based two-stage least squares (2SLS) estimators, when equipped with general spectral regularization in the first stage and a novel subspace size characterization, can achieve minimax optimal learning rates in the strong L2-norm for NPIV problems, even in the absence of unique identification of the structural function.
7dfc948cc4a08b4a30e7eabfd82d1bd88957d890.proposed_method: A kernel-based two-stage least squares (2SLS) framework is developed for NPIV estimation. In the first stage, the conditional mean embedding (CME) of the endogenous variable given the instrument is estimated using vector-valued regression in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), employing a general spectral regularization scheme rather than standard Tikhonov regularization to avoid saturation effects and adapt to higher smoothness. In the second stage, the outcome variable is regressed on the estimated CME using another RKHS-based least squares procedure, with the option to use Tikhonov regularization. The method targets the minimum RKHS norm solution in both identified and unidentified settings, ensuring convergence to a unique solution even when the structural function is not uniquely identified. A novel measure of the subspace size induced by the CME is introduced to characterize the learning risk and inform the theoretical analysis.
7dfc948cc4a08b4a30e7eabfd82d1bd88957d890.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic and/or real-world datasets typical for NPIV tasks, such as those involving causal inference, demand estimation, or reinforcement learning. The proposed kernel 2SLS estimator will be compared against established baselines, including Nadaraya-Watson IV, sieve-based IV, and other kernel or neural network-based NPIV estimators. Evaluation metrics will include convergence rates in the strong L2-norm, empirical risk, and possibly minimax optimality bounds. The experimental setup will involve sample splitting for the two stages, and various regularization schemes will be tested to validate the theoretical claims regarding spectral regularization and subspace size effects.
7dfc948cc4a08b4a30e7eabfd82d1bd88957d890.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a convergence analysis for kernel NPIV estimators that covers both identified and unidentified settings, showing convergence to the minimum norm solution in the strong L2-norm. A new subspace size measure is proposed to quantify the effective dimension of the regression problem, enabling a refined analysis of learning risk and rates. For the first time, minimax optimal learning rates for kernel NPIV are derived in the strong L2-norm under mild assumptions. Additionally, the adoption of general spectral regularization in stage 1 overcomes the saturation effect of Tikhonov regularization, allowing for faster convergence rates when the target function is highly smooth.

7e269bfabb451765a16ca0357de6b497cefb60bf.title: Grammar-Constrained Decoding for Structured NLP Tasks without Finetuning
7e269bfabb451765a16ca0357de6b497cefb60bf.research_question: How can grammar-constrained decoding be leveraged to enable large language models to reliably perform structured NLP tasks without task-specific finetuning, especially in scenarios with complex output structures and limited training data?
7e269bfabb451765a16ca0357de6b497cefb60bf.hypothesis: Applying formal grammar constraints during decoding will enable pretrained language models to generate outputs that strictly adhere to required structured formats, thereby improving performance on structured NLP tasks compared to unconstrained generation or even finetuned models, particularly in few-shot or low-resource settings.
7e269bfabb451765a16ca0357de6b497cefb60bf.proposed_method: A grammar-constrained decoding (GCD) framework will be developed to control the output of large language models (LLMs) by enforcing formal grammar rules at each decoding step. Formal grammars, including input-dependent grammars, will be specified for a variety of structured NLP tasks, such as closed information extraction, entity disambiguation, and constituency parsing. An incremental parser will be integrated with the LLM to serve as a completion engine, dynamically pruning the set of allowed next tokens based on the current output prefix and the grammar. The approach will support both context-free and regular grammars, and will be compatible with any autoregressive LLM where token-level probability distributions are accessible. The framework will also leverage few-shot prompting to adapt LLMs to new tasks without additional finetuning, ensuring that only grammatically valid outputs are produced.
7e269bfabb451765a16ca0357de6b497cefb60bf.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three representative structured NLP tasks: closed information extraction (cIE), entity disambiguation (ED), and constituency parsing (CP). For cIE, the SynthIE-text dataset will be used, evaluating models on triplet-based micro-precision, recall, and F1-score. For ED, six standard benchmarks (AIDA-CoNLL, MSNBC, ACE2004, AQUAINT, CLUEWEB, WIKI) will be used, with micro-accuracy as the metric. For CP, the Penn Treebank test split will be used, focusing on sentences shorter than 64 tokens, and evaluating with bracketing F1-score and parse validity. Baselines will include unconstrained few-shot LLMs, task-specific finetuned models, and prior constrained decoding approaches. Both input-independent and input-dependent grammars will be compared. Decoding latency and the impact of grammar complexity on performance will also be measured.
7e269bfabb451765a16ca0357de6b497cefb60bf.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified grammar-constrained decoding framework applicable to a wide range of structured NLP tasks, extending beyond traditional applications such as parsing and code generation. The use of input-dependent grammars enables dynamic adaptation of output constraints based on input, broadening the applicability to tasks like entity disambiguation and constituency parsing. The method demonstrates that off-the-shelf LLMs, when combined with GCD and few-shot prompting, can outperform unconstrained or even finetuned models on structured tasks without requiring additional training. The approach also provides a declarative, user-friendly interface for specifying output constraints, reducing engineering overhead and enabling rapid adaptation to new tasks.

7e26f894af508c6c2aced1b192627689636a7113.title: Once Upon an Input: Reasoning via Per-Instance Program Synthesis
7e26f894af508c6c2aced1b192627689636a7113.research_question: How can large language models be enabled to perform reliable and interpretable multi-step reasoning on complex, diverse problem instances, especially in the absence of explicit task specifications or structured input, and how can the choice between program synthesis and direct inference be dynamically optimized on a per-instance basis?
7e26f894af508c6c2aced1b192627689636a7113.hypothesis: Instance-level program synthesis, guided by structural feedback and paired with a confidence-based mechanism for selecting between programmatic and direct inference, will yield more accurate, robust, and interpretable reasoning than existing zero-shot or task-level code generation approaches, particularly for algorithmic problems and unstructured inputs.
7e26f894af508c6c2aced1b192627689636a7113.proposed_method: A novel framework, Per-Instance Program Synthesis (PIPS), will be developed to address reasoning tasks by dynamically choosing between direct inference (e.g., Chain-of-Thought) and program synthesis on a per-instance basis. The method will first extract a symbolic representation from unstructured input using an LLM, then iteratively synthesize and refine executable programs using structural feedback (e.g., checks for triviality, syntax, type errors, and placeholders) without relying on explicit task specifications or test cases. A confidence metric, derived from the LLM's self-assessment on multiple criteria, will determine whether to apply program synthesis or direct inference for each instance. The synthesis loop will continue until a well-formed, non-trivial program is found or a maximum number of iterations is reached, ensuring both correctness and interpretability.
7e26f894af508c6c2aced1b192627689636a7113.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across 30 benchmarks, including all 23 tasks from BigBench Extra Hard (BBEH), as well as visual reasoning (CLEVR, Leaf), relational reasoning (CLUTTR), and mathematical reasoning (OmniMath) datasets. Three state-of-the-art LLMs (Gemini-2.0-Flash, GPT-4.1-mini, o4-mini) will be evaluated. Baselines will include Program of Thought (PoT), Chain-of-Thought (CoT), Gemini Code Interpreter, and additional agentic and iterative code-generation baselines. Evaluation metrics will focus on harmonic mean accuracy, code quality (well-formedness, triviality, type and syntax errors), and the effectiveness of the confidence-based switch. Calibration and ablation studies will assess the impact of each component, and both zero-shot and calibrated switching strategies will be tested.
7e26f894af508c6c2aced1b192627689636a7113.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a per-instance program synthesis method that iteratively refines programs using structural feedback, eliminating the need for explicit task specifications or test cases. It pioneers a confidence-based mechanism for dynamically selecting between program synthesis and direct inference at the instance level, leveraging the LLM's own self-assessment. The method explicitly decouples perceptual inference from symbolic program synthesis by extracting structured representations from unstructured input, leading to improved code quality and interpretability. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate significant improvements in accuracy and reduction of undesirable code artifacts compared to prior code-based and textual reasoning methods.

7e2a2809c80cb8eca744edfe51c2aa005913cd6f.title: Mitigating Intra- and Inter-modal Forgetting in Continual Learning of Unified Multimodal Models
7e2a2809c80cb8eca744edfe51c2aa005913cd6f.research_question: Can unified multimodal generative models (UMGMs) continually acquire new capabilities through instruction tuning without suffering from catastrophic forgetting, both within a modality (intra-modal) and across modalities (inter-modal)?
7e2a2809c80cb8eca744edfe51c2aa005913cd6f.hypothesis: Decoupling modality-specific updates within UMGMs and applying knowledge distillation will mitigate both intra-modal and inter-modal catastrophic forgetting during continual instruction tuning, thereby preserving and enhancing performance across both multimodal understanding and generation tasks.
7e2a2809c80cb8eca744edfe51c2aa005913cd6f.proposed_method: A novel architecture, Modality-Decoupled Experts (MoDE), will be developed to address intra- and inter-modal forgetting in UMGMs. MoDE integrates two key components: (1) a modality-aware sparse mixture of LoRA adapters (T-MoE) for text tokens, enabling selective expert routing for continual multimodal understanding, and (2) a dedicated LoRA adapter (V-Adapter) for image tokens, specialized for both visual understanding and image generation. During continual instruction tuning, only the MoDE components are trained while the pre-trained UMGM backbone remains frozen, thus preserving robust cross-modal alignment. To further prevent degradation of image generation capabilities, knowledge distillation from the frozen pre-trained model (teacher) to the V-Adapter (student) is employed using a logit-level Kullback–Leibler divergence loss on a reference image dataset. The architecture ensures that updates for text and image modalities are isolated, thereby theoretically and empirically reducing gradient conflict between modalities and minimizing catastrophic forgetting.
7e2a2809c80cb8eca744edfe51c2aa005913cd6f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two autoregressive UMGM backbones (Chameleon and Janus-Pro) and evaluated across five datasets: ScienceQA, TextVQA, GQA, VizWiz (all visual question answering), and ImageNet (image classification) for continual instruction tuning, as well as CustomConcept101 for image generation. Baselines for comparison will include SeqLoRA, ModelTailor, DualPrompt, MoE-LoRA, CL-MoE, and a joint training upper bound. Evaluation metrics for multimodal understanding will be average accuracy and average forgetting, while image generation will be assessed using CLIP-based text and image alignment scores and Fréchet Inception Distance (FID). The experimental setup will involve sequentially tuning models on the task datasets, measuring performance retention and degradation across both modalities, and conducting ablation studies to assess the contributions of modality-specific adapters and knowledge distillation.
7e2a2809c80cb8eca744edfe51c2aa005913cd6f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first scalable and lightweight modality-decoupled expert architecture for continual learning in UMGMs, explicitly addressing both intra-modal and inter-modal catastrophic forgetting. Theoretical analysis and empirical results demonstrate that modality decoupling provably reduces gradient conflict between modalities, while knowledge distillation preserves pre-trained image generation capabilities. The method outperforms state-of-the-art continual learning baselines on both multimodal understanding and generation tasks, establishing a new paradigm for scalable continual learning in unified multimodal generative models.

7e2c1dcc5165abf4907e97defe181d08e8a97a6c.title: Communicating Activations Between Language Model Agents
7e2c1dcc5165abf4907e97defe181d08e8a97a6c.research_question: How can communication between multiple language model agents be made more efficient and effective, particularly by exploring alternatives to natural language as the medium for inter-agent communication?
7e2c1dcc5165abf4907e97defe181d08e8a97a6c.hypothesis: Communicating via internal activations between language models enables more efficient and higher-performing inter-agent communication than traditional natural language exchanges, while reducing computational costs and preserving richer information.
7e2c1dcc5165abf4907e97defe181d08e8a97a6c.proposed_method: The proposed method enables language model agents to communicate by directly exchanging intermediate activations rather than natural language messages. Specifically, computation in a recipient model B is paused at an intermediate layer, and its activation is combined with the corresponding activation from a sender model A using a function f (such as sum, mean, replacement, or a learned linear mapping). The combined activation is then injected into the next layer of model B, and computation continues until decoding is complete. This protocol is parameter-efficient, requiring zero additional task-specific parameters or data, and can be applied to diverse model architectures and domains. For cases where the activation spaces of A and B differ, a task-agnostic linear mapping W is learned once per model pair to align activations, trained via MSE loss on general text data.
7e2c1dcc5165abf4907e97defe181d08e8a97a6c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two main setups: (1) multi-player coordination games (such as Lewis signaling games) where agents must share information to solve tasks, and (2) a suite of reasoning benchmarks spanning domains like biographies, math (GSM8k), and multiple MMLU categories. Baselines will include single-model performance, natural language communication protocols (including multi-agent debate), and ablations of the activation communication protocol with different functional forms of f. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy (exact match or fact-level scoring), compute cost (FLOPs), and robustness across model sizes, families, and architectures (e.g., LLaMA, Qwen, Gemma). Both identical and heterogeneous model pairs will be tested, and the effect of the learned mapping W will be assessed. Decoding strategies such as greedy and nucleus sampling will be used, and experiments will be repeated with different random seeds and dataset splits to ensure statistical significance.
7e2c1dcc5165abf4907e97defe181d08e8a97a6c.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a novel, activation-based communication protocol for language model agents that bypasses natural language, enabling richer and more efficient information exchange. The method is parameter- and data-efficient, generalizes across model families and sizes, and achieves substantial compute savings. It is the first to demonstrate that direct activation communication can outperform natural language debate protocols, even for smaller, open-source models, and provides a unified framework for activation-level model composition without requiring shared tokenizers or extensive retraining.

7e45d23a134c0343a3538d67f49a668fdc5d09bb.title: A Cramér-von Mises Approach to Incentivizing Truthful Data Sharing
7e45d23a134c0343a3538d67f49a668fdc5d09bb.research_question: How can incentive mechanisms be designed to robustly encourage truthful data sharing in data marketplaces and consortia, even when agents may strategically fabricate or misreport data and the underlying data distribution is unknown or complex?
7e45d23a134c0343a3538d67f49a668fdc5d09bb.hypothesis: Reward mechanisms based on a Cramér–von Mises-inspired two-sample test statistic can strictly incentivize agents to truthfully report and submit more genuine data, while disincentivizing data fabrication or untruthful reporting, without relying on restrictive assumptions about the data distribution.
7e45d23a134c0343a3538d67f49a668fdc5d09bb.proposed_method: A novel reward mechanism will be developed that leverages a two-sample test inspired by the Cramér–von Mises (CvM) statistic to compare each agent’s submitted data against the pooled submissions of others. The mechanism will compute a loss for each agent based on the squared difference between the empirical cumulative distribution function (ECDF) of the pooled data and its conditional expectation, evaluated at random points from the data. To handle high-dimensional or complex data types (such as text or images), the approach will utilize feature maps—functions that project data into one-dimensional representations—allowing the mechanism to be applied to a wide range of modalities. Both Bayesian and prior-agnostic (frequentist) variants of the mechanism will be constructed: the Bayesian version uses a known prior over data distributions, while the prior-agnostic version replaces the conditional expectation with an empirical estimate, making it computationally efficient and broadly applicable. The mechanism will be theoretically analyzed to ensure that truthful reporting forms a (possibly approximate) Nash equilibrium and that agents are strictly incentivized to submit more genuine data.
7e45d23a134c0343a3538d67f49a668fdc5d09bb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic experiments will use beta-Bernoulli and normal-normal Bayesian models, where the loss for truthful and fabricated submissions can be computed analytically. Real-world experiments will be performed on the SQuAD language dataset (using Llama 3.2-1B-Instruct for text fabrication and DistilBERT feature embeddings) and the Oxford Flowers-102 image dataset (using Segmind Stable Diffusion-1B for image fabrication and DeIT-small-distilled embeddings). Baseline comparisons will include standard two-sample tests such as Kolmogorov–Smirnov, direct CvM, and mean-difference statistics. Evaluation metrics will focus on the loss assigned to truthful versus fabricated submissions, with the expectation that the proposed mechanism yields higher losses for fabricated data. Experimental setups will simulate environments with multiple agents, each possessing both genuine and fabricated data, to assess the robustness of the mechanism under strategic manipulation.
7e45d23a134c0343a3538d67f49a668fdc5d09bb.novelty_claims: The proposed mechanism eliminates the need for restrictive distributional assumptions (e.g., Gaussianity or finite support) that limit prior approaches, enabling application to arbitrary and complex data distributions. It introduces a general, computationally efficient, and provably truthful (or approximately truthful) incentive mechanism for data sharing that is robust to a wide range of strategic misreporting behaviors, including sophisticated data fabrication using modern generative models. The approach is broadly applicable across data modalities via the use of feature maps, and is the first to provide both theoretical guarantees and empirical validation of truthfulness in practical, real-world data sharing scenarios.

7e4c11952126ac9047d471c52c7880ccd2ebdfa6.title: Flash Inference: Near Linear Time Inference for Long Convolution Sequence Models and Beyond
7e4c11952126ac9047d471c52c7880ccd2ebdfa6.research_question: How can inference time for long convolution sequence models (LCSMs) and related architectures be reduced from quadratic to near-linear complexity, and what general architectural properties enable such speedups for autoregressive sequence models?
7e4c11952126ac9047d471c52c7880ccd2ebdfa6.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by leveraging a novel tiling-based framework inspired by relaxed polynomial interpolation, exact inference in LCSMs can be performed in quasilinear time, and that this approach can generalize to other architectures with similar contribution-based, query-independent mixer properties.
7e4c11952126ac9047d471c52c7880ccd2ebdfa6.proposed_method: A new inference algorithm is developed for LCSMs and related models, utilizing a tiling strategy that groups contributions from input positions to output positions in a way that enables the use of fast convolution algorithms (e.g., FFT) during autoregressive inference. The method incrementally computes activations using a relaxed polynomial interpolation approach, processing contributions in balanced tiles rather than thin strips, and exploits the associative and query-independent properties of the mixer functions. The algorithm is designed to allow for almost complete parallelization across layers for the position-mixing part, reducing memory movement and enabling efficient handling of both data-independent and data-dependent convolutional filters. The framework, termed Flash Inference, generalizes this approach by formalizing the required architectural properties and providing a generic algorithm that can be instantiated for any model meeting these criteria.
7e4c11952126ac9047d471c52c7880ccd2ebdfa6.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using both synthetic models and the Hyena architecture, a state-of-the-art LCSM, with all blocks set as MLPs and random initialization to focus on runtime rather than model quality. The evaluation is performed on NVIDIA H100 and A100 GPUs, sweeping over batch size (B ∈ {1,2,4,8}), number of layers (M ∈ {18,36}), embedding dimensions (D ∈ {256,768}), and sequence lengths up to the largest power of two fitting in memory. Baselines include the naive (lazy), eager, and their parallelized variants. The primary evaluation metrics are end-to-end inference time and the runtime of the position-mixing (convolution) component. The proposed method is compared against these baselines, with results averaged over multiple runs and per-token response times analyzed.
7e4c11952126ac9047d471c52c7880ccd2ebdfa6.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to provide an exact, quasilinear-in-sequence-length (O(L log^2 L)) inference algorithm for LCSMs, contrasting with previous approaches that only achieve approximate inference or require restrictive assumptions. The method identifies and exploits key architectural properties that enable such speedups, generalizing beyond LCSMs to a broader class of models. Additional innovations include a tiling-based contribution grouping that minimizes memory movement, supports parallelization across layers, and accommodates both data-independent and data-dependent filters. Empirical results demonstrate up to 7.8× end-to-end speedup and up to 110× speedup in the convolutional mixer component over standard inference approaches.

7e7e59d2e247d99954081080ddd5aae93d10b9e0.title: π0: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control
7e7e59d2e247d99954081080ddd5aae93d10b9e0.research_question: How can a generalist robot control policy be developed that effectively integrates vision, language, and action to achieve robust, dexterous, and generalizable manipulation across diverse tasks and robot embodiments?
7e7e59d2e247d99954081080ddd5aae93d10b9e0.hypothesis: A robot control model that leverages a pre-trained vision-language backbone, combined with a flow matching-based action generation module and trained on a large, diverse, cross-embodiment dataset, will demonstrate superior generalization, dexterity, and robustness in real-world manipulation tasks compared to existing autoregressive or non-pretrained approaches.
7e7e59d2e247d99954081080ddd5aae93d10b9e0.proposed_method: A novel robot control framework is proposed that builds upon a pre-trained vision-language model (VLM) backbone, specifically PaliGemma, to import Internet-scale semantic and visual knowledge. This backbone is augmented with an action expert module that generates continuous robot actions using a flow matching approach, a variant of diffusion modeling, enabling high-frequency (up to 50 Hz) and dexterous control. The model architecture incorporates multi-modal inputs, including images, language commands, and proprioceptive robot state, and is trained using a conditional flow matching loss applied to action tokens. Training follows a two-phase recipe: (1) a large-scale pre-training phase on a mixture of diverse robot datasets from multiple embodiments and tasks, and (2) a post-training (fine-tuning) phase on high-quality, task-specific data to induce precise, robust, and fluent manipulation behaviors. The model supports both direct language prompting for zero-shot task execution and further fine-tuning for complex, multi-stage tasks.
7e7e59d2e247d99954081080ddd5aae93d10b9e0.experiment_details: Experiments will pre-train the model on a dataset exceeding 10,000 hours of robot demonstrations, including both proprietary dexterous manipulation data (from 7 robot configurations and 68 tasks) and open-source datasets such as OXE, Bridge v2, and DROID. The model will be evaluated on a variety of robots (single-arm, dual-arm, and mobile manipulators) and tasks, including out-of-distribution and highly dexterous tasks like laundry folding, table cleaning, and box assembly. Baseline comparisons will include OpenVLA, Octo, ACT, and Diffusion Policy, with and without VLM pre-training, as well as ablations on model architecture and training recipes. Evaluation metrics will include normalized task success rates, language instruction following accuracy, and performance across varying amounts of fine-tuning data. Both zero-shot and fine-tuned performance will be measured, with experiments averaging results over multiple (e.g., 10) real-world trials per task.
7e7e59d2e247d99954081080ddd5aae93d10b9e0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first vision-language-action (VLA) model for robot control that combines a pre-trained VLM backbone with a flow matching-based action generation module, enabling high-frequency, continuous, and dexterous control across diverse robot embodiments. The integrative training recipe, leveraging large-scale cross-embodiment pre-training and targeted post-training, is claimed to yield unprecedented generalization, robustness, and dexterity in real-world robot manipulation. The method demonstrates, for the first time, the ability to perform long-horizon, multi-stage dexterous tasks (e.g., laundry folding, box assembly) in an end-to-end learned fashion, significantly surpassing prior robot foundation models and specialized dexterous manipulation approaches.

7ec215b728f3988f8d48ebf065fb746835460677.title: Score-Based Diffusion Models as Principled Priors for Inverse Imaging
7ec215b728f3988f8d48ebf065fb746835460677.research_question: How can expressive, data-driven image priors be incorporated into principled Bayesian inference frameworks for solving inverse imaging problems, enabling accurate uncertainty quantification and robust posterior sampling across diverse imaging tasks?
7ec215b728f3988f8d48ebf065fb746835460677.hypothesis: Score-based diffusion models, when used as explicit, differentiable probabilistic priors, enable principled Bayesian inference for inverse imaging problems and yield more accurate, uncertainty-aware posterior samples than traditional handcrafted or implicit deep priors.
7ec215b728f3988f8d48ebf065fb746835460677.proposed_method: A framework will be developed that employs score-based diffusion models as explicit, differentiable probabilistic priors for images. These priors will be trained on large datasets using stochastic differential equations (SDEs) to learn the data distribution, enabling exact or highly accurate log-probability and gradient computations via the probability flow ODE. The learned prior will be paired with a known measurement likelihood to define a full Bayesian posterior, which can be sampled using variational inference with a normalizing flow (such as RealNVP). The method will avoid hand-tuned hyperparameters by leveraging the tractable probability function of the diffusion model, and will provide gradients through the ODE for optimization and sampling. The approach will be modular, allowing any measurement model and any image dataset for prior training, and will be compatible with established Bayesian inference algorithms.
7ec215b728f3988f8d48ebf065fb746835460677.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of inverse imaging tasks, including image denoising, deblurring (recovery from low-frequency DFT measurements), and interferometric imaging (simulating black hole observations). Datasets such as CelebA and CIFAR-10 will be used for training and evaluation. Baseline comparisons will include traditional handcrafted priors (e.g., total variation), PCA-Gaussian priors, normalizing flow-based priors, and existing posterior sampling methods for diffusion models (e.g., SDE+Proj, Score-ALD, DPS). Evaluation metrics will include PSNR, SSIM, MSE, and qualitative assessments of posterior samples and uncertainty maps. The experimental setup will involve training score-based priors, validating log-probability and gradient accuracy, and comparing posterior estimates against analytical ground-truths or established baselines. Robustness to prior mismatch and sensitivity to measurement weighting will also be assessed.
7ec215b728f3988f8d48ebf065fb746835460677.novelty_claims: The proposed approach establishes, for the first time, the use of score-based diffusion models as explicit, hyperparameter-free, differentiable probabilistic priors for principled Bayesian inference in inverse imaging. This enables accurate computation of log-probabilities and gradients, facilitating variational inference and posterior sampling with rich, data-driven priors. The method bridges the gap between deep generative modeling and traditional Bayesian inverse problem-solving, providing uncertainty quantification and modularity across tasks. Empirical validation demonstrates that this framework yields more informative posteriors and superior sample quality compared to both handcrafted and implicit deep priors, and outperforms existing diffusion-based posterior sampling methods.

7f016cc9f0d1e9abd48dd48cdb220be16b609c8d.title: Synthesizing Programmatic Reinforcement Learning Policies with Large Language Model Guided Search
7f016cc9f0d1e9abd48dd48cdb220be16b609c8d.research_question: How can sample efficiency and effectiveness in programmatic reinforcement learning (PRL) be improved by leveraging large language models (LLMs) to synthesize interpretable policies in domain-specific languages, particularly in complex environments such as Karel and Minigrid?
7f016cc9f0d1e9abd48dd48cdb220be16b609c8d.hypothesis: Integrating large language models with a guided search framework and a Pythonic-DSL strategy will significantly improve the sample efficiency and performance of programmatic reinforcement learning, enabling the synthesis of high-quality, interpretable policies with fewer program-environment interactions, even for users without programming or domain-specific knowledge.
7f016cc9f0d1e9abd48dd48cdb220be16b609c8d.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that combines large language models (LLMs) with a search-based approach for synthesizing reinforcement learning policies as programs in domain-specific languages (DSLs). The method will employ domain- and task-aware prompting to provide LLMs with detailed natural language descriptions of the environment and task, enabling the generation of relevant and context-aware code. To address the difficulty LLMs face in generating syntactically correct DSL code, a Pythonic-DSL strategy will be used: LLMs will first generate Python code under specific constraints, which will then be automatically converted into the target DSL. The initial set of LLM-generated programs will serve as the starting population for a novel search algorithm, Scheduled Hill Climbing, which adaptively increases the neighborhood search size based on the number of program evaluations, thus efficiently exploring the programmatic space to iteratively improve policy performance. The overall process involves sampling, evaluation, ranking, and iterative local search, with a scheduler controlling the breadth of exploration as the search progresses.
7f016cc9f0d1e9abd48dd48cdb220be16b609c8d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Karel and Karel-Hard benchmark suites, as well as on novel tasks and the Minigrid domain, to evaluate the effectiveness and generalizability of the proposed framework. Baselines will include state-of-the-art PRL methods such as LEAPS, HPRL, CEBS, and Hill Climbing, with all methods compared under a fixed program-environment interaction budget. Evaluation metrics will focus on sample efficiency, measured by the number of programs evaluated to reach optimal or high episodic return, and acceptance rate of executable programs. Each program will be tested across multiple environment variants (e.g., 32 task variances), and experiments will be run with multiple random seeds to ensure statistical significance. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of the Pythonic-DSL strategy, the initialization method for the search population, and the scheduling mechanism in Scheduled Hill Climbing. Additional experiments will test the framework's extensibility to novel tasks described only in natural language and its adaptability to new domains such as Minigrid.
7f016cc9f0d1e9abd48dd48cdb220be16b609c8d.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a novel integration of large language models with programmatic reinforcement learning via a guided search framework, significantly improving sample efficiency over existing methods. The Pythonic-DSL strategy is a key innovation, enabling LLMs to generate precise and executable DSL programs by leveraging their proficiency in general-purpose programming languages. The Scheduled Hill Climbing algorithm adaptively manages the search budget, further enhancing efficiency and performance. The framework is designed for extensibility, allowing users without programming or domain-specific knowledge to specify tasks in natural language and obtain performant programmatic policies. The approach is demonstrated to generalize across domains and outperform state-of-the-art baselines in both standard and novel PRL tasks.

7f0ad3a6aef6bb51b599138ff83437fcbe6d6072.title: Generalization v.s. Memorization: Tracing Language Models' Capabilities Back to Pretraining Data
7f0ad3a6aef6bb51b599138ff83437fcbe6d6072.research_question: To what extent do large language models (LLMs) rely on memorization versus generalization when performing a variety of tasks, and how can the origins of their capabilities be traced back to specific distributions in their pretraining data?
7f0ad3a6aef6bb51b599138ff83437fcbe6d6072.hypothesis: LLMs rely more on memorization for knowledge-intensive, simpler tasks and more on generalization for complex, reasoning-intensive tasks. The degree of memorization or generalization can be quantitatively linked to the distributional similarity between task data and pretraining data.
7f0ad3a6aef6bb51b599138ff83437fcbe6d6072.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed to analyze the relationship between LLM outputs and pretraining data distributions by introducing the concept of distributional memorization. This will be operationalized via a task-gram language model, constructed by mining semantically related n-gram pairs from supervised task input-output data and counting their co-occurrences in the pretraining corpus. The semantic similarity between n-grams will be measured using cosine similarity of pretrained embeddings, and a threshold will be used to select relevant pairs. The task-gram language model will estimate the probability distribution of task-relevant data in the pretraining corpus, and the degree of memorization will be quantified by computing the Spearman correlation between the probabilities assigned by the task-gram LM and those predicted by the LLM for test data. Additionally, a gradient-based influence estimation will be used to assess the causal impact of specific pretraining documents on model predictions.
7f0ad3a6aef6bb51b599138ff83437fcbe6d6072.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Pythia family of LLMs (ranging from 13M to 12B parameters) pretrained on the Pile dataset (207B tokens), with supplementary results from OLMo models trained on Dolma (3T tokens). Four tasks will be evaluated: machine translation (WMT-09), factual question answering (TriviaQA), world knowledge questions (MMLU), and math reasoning (GSM8K). For each task, task-gram tables will be constructed, and n-gram co-occurrences will be searched in the pretraining corpus using WIMBD and ∞-gram APIs. Evaluation metrics will include BLEU for translation, exact match accuracy for TriviaQA, multiple-choice accuracy for MMLU, and BERTScore for GSM8K. Baselines will involve comparisons to ∞-gram language models and single n-gram frequency models. Statistical significance of memorization and generalization will be assessed, and prompt optimization experiments will test whether modifying prompts to encourage memorization or generalization improves performance.
7f0ad3a6aef6bb51b599138ff83437fcbe6d6072.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a scalable, task-specific framework for tracing LLM capabilities to pretraining data distributions using the task-gram language model. This approach enables fine-grained, large-scale analysis of memorization and generalization across diverse tasks, surpassing previous methods limited by computational constraints or narrow definitions of memorization. The method provides both correlational and causal insights into how pretraining data influences LLM behavior, and demonstrates practical implications for prompt optimization based on task type.

7f1a473834eea608980e4e04cce21be18d65b9b6.title: Composing Parameter-Efficient Modules with Arithmetic Operations
7f1a473834eea608980e4e04cce21be18d65b9b6.research_question: How can parameter-efficient modules (PEMs), trained via parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) on different datasets, tasks, or domains, be flexibly composed to enable new capabilities such as distribution generalization, multi-tasking, unlearning, and domain transfer in pretrained language models, without requiring additional training?
7f1a473834eea608980e4e04cce21be18d65b9b6.hypothesis: Parameter-efficient modules, when initialized from the same pretrained checkpoint and architecture, can be effectively composed in parameter space using linear arithmetic operations (addition and negation), resulting in new modules that integrate or modify capabilities without additional training.
7f1a473834eea608980e4e04cce21be18d65b9b6.proposed_method: A framework will be developed for composing parameter-efficient modules (PEMs) using linear arithmetic operations directly in parameter space. Two fundamental operators will be defined: addition, which aggregates the parameters of two PEMs component-wise to combine their capabilities, and negation, which modifies the PEM parameters to retract specific skills (e.g., by negating certain projection matrices or vectors). These operators will be further composed to enable flexible operations such as subtraction and analogy-based transfer, allowing for advanced module manipulations (e.g., domain adaptation via analogy equations). The method will be instantiated for state-of-the-art PEFT architectures, specifically LoRA and (IA)3, with technical details on how to apply the operators to their respective parameter sets. A weighting hyperparameter will be introduced to control the interpolation between modules, and the approach will be designed to require no additional training.
7f1a473834eea608980e4e04cce21be18d65b9b6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across several scenarios: (1) distribution generalization by merging PEMs trained on different data distributions for the same task using datasets from GLUE (e.g., MNLI, RTE, SST-2, MRPC, QNLI, QQP, CoLA, STS-B) and RoBERTa-base as the backbone; (2) multi-tasking by combining PEMs trained on different tasks (e.g., MNLI and RTE) using T5-base and prompting for unified evaluation; (3) unlearning by negating PEMs trained on toxic data (CivilComments) and evaluating toxicity and linguistic proficiency with GPT-2 large and Detoxify API, as well as WikiText-103 for perplexity; (4) domain transfer by analogy-based composition using Amazon and Yelp sentiment datasets with T5-small and T5-base; (5) extension to large language models by detoxifying Alpaca-LoRA (LLaMA-based) using a synthetic toxic instruction dataset and evaluating with Detoxify API, GPT-4 scoring, and human annotation. Baselines will include full fine-tuning, individual PEMs, and vanilla transfer. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, MCC, Spearman's rho, toxicity scores, perplexity, and helpfulness ratings. Hyperparameters such as the interpolation weight will be tuned on validation sets.
7f1a473834eea608980e4e04cce21be18d65b9b6.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a systematic, training-free method for composing parameter-efficient modules via linear arithmetic operations, extending beyond simple addition to include negation and analogy-based transfer. This enables highly flexible and modular manipulation of pretrained language model capabilities, supporting scenarios such as distribution generalization, multi-tasking, unlearning, and domain transfer. The method is instantiated for modern PEFT architectures (LoRA and (IA)3) and is demonstrated on both standard and large language models, including instruction-tuned LLaMA variants. The approach claims significant improvements over existing PEM composition methods, as it does not require additional training or data access and supports a broader range of composition scenarios.

7f1b762d503e25e2cadb0aa945492ac3ae01e8e9.title: Uncertainty-Aware Decoding with Minimum Bayes Risk
7f1b762d503e25e2cadb0aa945492ac3ae01e8e9.research_question: How can uncertainty in model parameters be effectively incorporated into the decoding process of language models to improve the quality and reliability of generated text, including reducing hallucinations and enabling selective prediction?
7f1b762d503e25e2cadb0aa945492ac3ae01e8e9.hypothesis: Incorporating model weight uncertainty into the Minimum Bayes Risk (MBR) decoding process will improve the quality and robustness of language model outputs, reduce hallucinations, and enable more effective selective prediction, without incurring significant computational overhead.
7f1b762d503e25e2cadb0aa945492ac3ae01e8e9.proposed_method: A novel uncertainty-aware decoding framework will be developed by generalizing Minimum Bayes Risk (MBR) decoding to explicitly account for model weight uncertainty. This will be achieved by replacing the standard model distribution in MBR with a predictive posterior that marginalizes over a learned posterior distribution of model parameters. Practical algorithms will be implemented to approximate this expectation using both sequence-level and token-level posteriors, leveraging Monte Carlo sampling from variational or ensemble-based Bayesian posteriors. The approach will support both black-box and white-box language models, enabling model combination at the sequence or token level, and will allow for the use of diverse utility functions such as BERTScore or BLEU. Additionally, the framework will include mechanisms for selective prediction by abstaining from generation when the expected utility is low, based on the uncertainty-aware risk estimates.
7f1b762d503e25e2cadb0aa945492ac3ae01e8e9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a broad suite of language generation and scoring tasks, including machine translation (WMT14, IWSLT14, afroMT, IWSLT17, WMT18, WMT19), summarization (XSUM, SAMSum), data-to-text generation (E2E-NLG), and sentence similarity scoring (STS-B). Both prompted, fine-tuned, and from-scratch trained models will be evaluated, including Llama-3 8B, Mistral 7B, Gemma-2B/9B, Qwen-2 7B, and Transformer architectures. Baselines will include standard MBR decoding with single models (trained with AdamW or variational methods), as well as deep ensembles and unimodal posteriors. Evaluation metrics will include BLEU, chrF, COMET, LaBSE, ROUGE, FactCC, and RMSE, with BERTScore or BLEU used as the utility function for MBR. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by matching the number of MBR comparisons across methods and controlling for effective beam size. The effect of posterior complexity, ensemble diversity, scaling with model and hypothesis set size, and selective prediction performance will be systematically investigated.
7f1b762d503e25e2cadb0aa945492ac3ae01e8e9.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a principled and practical extension of Minimum Bayes Risk decoding that incorporates model weight uncertainty, enabling uncertainty-aware text generation. The method supports both sequence-level and token-level posterior combination, can be applied to both white-box and black-box models, and allows for ensembling outputs from diverse language models. It demonstrates that improvements in output quality and robustness can be achieved without additional training or inference overhead when using simple unimodal posteriors. The approach also establishes a connection between prediction diversity and decoding performance, and provides a new mechanism for selective prediction based on uncertainty-aware expected utility. The framework is scalable and general, offering a new paradigm for robust and reliable language generation.

7f1cac8703829d08984b532948f6e7e15a5cac5c.title: An Adaptive Model Ensemble Adversarial Attack for Boosting Adversarial Transferability
7f1cac8703829d08984b532948f6e7e15a5cac5c.research_question: How can the transferability of adversarial examples be improved in black-box settings, especially across deep neural networks (DNNs) with widely differing architectures such as CNNs and Vision Transformers (ViTs)?
7f1cac8703829d08984b532948f6e7e15a5cac5c.hypothesis: An adaptive ensemble adversarial attack that modulates the contribution of each surrogate model based on its transferability and synchronizes gradient update directions will significantly improve the transferability of adversarial examples across diverse model architectures.
7f1cac8703829d08984b532948f6e7e15a5cac5c.proposed_method: A novel adaptive ensemble adversarial attack (AdaEA) is developed, which adaptively fuses outputs from multiple surrogate models by monitoring the discrepancy in their contributions to the adversarial objective. The method introduces an Adaptive Gradient Modulation (AGM) strategy, where an adversarial ratio is computed for each model to assess its transferability, and ensemble weights are assigned via a softmax function over these ratios. Additionally, a Disparity-Reduced Filter (DRF) is applied to synchronize the gradient update direction by filtering out the disparity part of ensemble gradients, using cosine similarity to compute a disparity map and a threshold to binarize the filter. The final ensemble gradient is then used to iteratively generate adversarial examples, amplifying transferable information and reducing overfitting to specific surrogate models.
7f1cac8703829d08984b532948f6e7e15a5cac5c.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet datasets, using both CNNs (e.g., ResNet-50, WideResNet-50, BiT-M-R50x1) and ViTs (e.g., ViT-Base, DeiT-Base, Swin-Base) as target and surrogate models. Baseline comparisons include standard ensemble attacks (Ens) and stochastic variance-reduced ensemble (SVRE) attacks. Evaluation metrics include black-box attack success rates and robust accuracy against adversarially trained and input-transformation-based defense models. The proposed method is also tested in combination with various transfer-based attacks (FGSM, I-FGSM, MI-FGSM, DI2-FGSM), and ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of AGM, DRF, and hyperparameters. All attacks are implemented with I-FGSM (20 iterations, l_infinity constraint, epsilon=8/255, alpha=2/255), and experiments are run on high-performance GPUs.
7f1cac8703829d08984b532948f6e7e15a5cac5c.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces an adaptive ensemble mechanism that dynamically adjusts the contribution of each surrogate model based on its transferability, rather than simply averaging outputs. The integration of AGM and DRF enables amplification of transferable adversarial information and synchronization of gradient directions, leading to significantly improved transferability across models with large architectural differences. The approach demonstrates substantial improvements over existing ensemble attacks in both attack success rates and robustness against advanced defenses, and can be flexibly combined with various transfer-based attack methods.

7f21211eef25d47cff5a52366d1f7a155930cb5a.title: Quantum Implicit Neural Representations
7f21211eef25d47cff5a52366d1f7a155930cb5a.research_question: How can quantum neural networks be leveraged to improve the efficiency and accuracy of implicit neural representations for modeling signals such as images and sounds, particularly in capturing high-frequency components, while reducing the number of parameters and computational resources required?
7f21211eef25d47cff5a52366d1f7a155930cb5a.hypothesis: Quantum neural networks, specifically those based on data re-uploading quantum circuits, can provide an exponential advantage in representing Fourier series compared to classical Fourier Neural Networks, resulting in more accurate and memory-efficient implicit neural representations for complex signals.
7f21211eef25d47cff5a52366d1f7a155930cb5a.proposed_method: A novel framework, Quantum Implicit Representation Network (QIREN), will be developed as a quantum generalization of Fourier Neural Networks (FNNs). QIREN will utilize a hybrid architecture comprising multiple hybrid layers, each consisting of a Linear layer, BatchNorm layer, and a data re-uploading quantum circuit. The quantum circuit will repeatedly encode classical input coordinates using parameterized quantum gates, enabling the model to represent a broad spectrum of Fourier components exponentially with respect to circuit size. The output of each hybrid layer will be fed into subsequent layers, culminating in a final Linear layer that produces the signal value. Training will be performed using mean squared error loss, and theoretical analysis will be conducted to demonstrate the quantum advantage in function approximation, particularly for high-frequency signal components.
7f21211eef25d47cff5a52366d1f7a155930cb5a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of signal representation tasks, including one-dimensional sound wave modeling and two-dimensional image representation, as well as downstream applications such as image superresolution and image generation. Datasets will include a segment from Bach’s Cello Suites for sound, and standard images (Astronaut, Camera, Coffee) for image tasks, along with high-resolution facial image datasets (FFHQ and CelebA-HQ) for generative modeling. Baselines will include ReLU-based MLPs, Tanh-based MLPs, ReLU-based MLPs with Random Fourier Features, SIREN, and standard interpolation methods. Evaluation metrics will include mean squared error (MSE) for reconstruction tasks and Frechet Inception Distance (FID) for generative tasks. Model parameter counts will be matched across methods for fair comparison, and all experiments will be simulated using quantum machine learning frameworks such as Pennylane and TorchQuantum.
7f21211eef25d47cff5a52366d1f7a155930cb5a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first quantum generalization of Fourier Neural Networks for implicit neural representations, leveraging data re-uploading quantum circuits to achieve exponential growth in representable frequency spectrum with respect to circuit size. QIREN is claimed to provide superior signal representation, particularly for high-frequency components, with significantly fewer parameters and improved memory efficiency compared to state-of-the-art classical models. Theoretical analysis demonstrates the quantum advantage in function approximation, and empirical results are expected to show substantial improvements in signal representation, image superresolution, and image generation tasks.

7f21e3b61dae79d31bb90a58c9c4b0918a7e74d4.title: EFOk-CQA: Towards Knowledge Graph Complex Query Answering beyond Set Operation
7f21e3b61dae79d31bb90a58c9c4b0918a7e74d4.research_question: How can the space of complex queries over knowledge graphs be systematically extended and represented to enable comprehensive evaluation and development of learning-based complex query answering (CQA) methods, particularly beyond set operation-based queries and including multiple free variables and combinatorial query structures?
7f21e3b61dae79d31bb90a58c9c4b0918a7e74d4.hypothesis: A framework that systematically generates, represents, and evaluates Existential First-Order (EFO) queries with multiple free variables and complex combinatorial structures will enable more thorough benchmarking of CQA models, reveal structural biases in existing datasets, and facilitate the development of more robust and generalizable CQA methods.
7f21e3b61dae79d31bb90a58c9c4b0918a7e74d4.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed for generating, representing, and evaluating complex queries on knowledge graphs. The method will enumerate all nontrivial abstract query graphs (query types) according to formal constraints to avoid redundancy and trivial decomposability, and will ground these abstract graphs into concrete queries over a given knowledge graph. The framework will represent queries as query graphs, supporting both set operation-based and more general conjunctive formulas, including those with multiple free variables. Efficient algorithms will be implemented for answer computation, leveraging constraint satisfaction problem (CSP) techniques and custom backtracking solvers to handle the combinatorial complexity. The framework will also provide backward compatibility with operator tree-based models and support new query graph-based models, enabling a unified platform for model training and evaluation.
