7f21e3b61dae79d31bb90a58c9c4b0918a7e74d4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the newly constructed EFOk-CQA dataset, which systematically covers 741 types of query graphs parameterized by the number of constants, existential variables, free variables, and edges. The primary benchmark knowledge graph will be FB15k-237, with additional experiments on FB15k and NELL for generality. Six representative CQA models, including both operator tree-based (BetaE, LogicE, ConE) and query graph-based (CQD, LMPNN, FIT) approaches, will be evaluated. Evaluation metrics will include marginal, multiply, and joint ranking metrics (e.g., MRR, HIT@K) designed to assess both single-variable and combinatorial multi-variable query answering performance. The experimental setup will control for query topology (acyclic, multigraph, cyclic), number of constants, and existential variables to analyze the impact of query hardness and structural properties on model performance.
7f21e3b61dae79d31bb90a58c9c4b0918a7e74d4.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the first systematic coverage of Existential First-Order queries with multiple free variables, extending beyond the tree-form and set operation-based queries of previous benchmarks. The dataset and methodology capture both combinatorial and structural hardness, enabling evaluation of queries that cannot be represented by operator trees. The framework supports both existing and novel CQA models, provides new evaluation metrics for combinatorial answers, and exposes structural biases in prior datasets. This work establishes a new standard for comprehensive benchmarking and development of complex query answering methods on knowledge graphs.

7f24b34a364f83f3162f70b74a12ad4d5c2735b4.title: The distribution of Ridgeless least squares interpolators
7f24b34a364f83f3162f70b74a12ad4d5c2735b4.research_question: What is the precise stochastic behavior of the ridgeless minimum-norm interpolator in high-dimensional overparameterized linear regression, and how does it relate to implicit regularization and the performance of cross-validation schemes in various risk and inference settings?
7f24b34a364f83f3162f70b74a12ad4d5c2735b4.hypothesis: The ridgeless minimum-norm interpolator exhibits a form of implicit regularization that can be precisely characterized in distributional terms, and this characterization explains its favorable prediction, estimation, and inference properties, even under perfect interpolation. Furthermore, standard cross-validation schemes will yield near-optimal tuning not only for prediction risk but also for estimation, in-sample risk, and confidence interval length.
7f24b34a364f83f3162f70b74a12ad4d5c2735b4.proposed_method: A high-dimensional distributional characterization of the ridgeless and ridge estimators will be developed in the proportional regime (where the number of samples and features are of the same order). This involves relating the distribution of the ridgeless estimator to that of a ridge estimator in an associated Gaussian sequence model with effective noise and regularization parameters, determined by a fixed-point equation. The approach will extend to general (non-Gaussian) random designs and provide uniform results across a range of regularization parameters, including the interpolation limit. The method will also derive explicit formulae for general weighted ℓ_q risks and analyze the behavior of cross-validation schemes (generalized and k-fold) in tuning regularization for optimal risk and inference properties.
7f24b34a364f83f3162f70b74a12ad4d5c2735b4.experiment_details: Experiments will involve both theoretical analysis and simulations. Simulations will be conducted on synthetic datasets generated from linear models with random Gaussian and non-Gaussian designs, varying the sample-to-dimension ratio (aspect ratio) to explore both overparameterized and underparameterized regimes. Baselines will include standard ridge regression with various regularization strengths, as well as cross-validation-tuned estimators (GCV and k-fold CV). Evaluation metrics will include prediction risk, estimation risk, in-sample risk, and the length and coverage of confidence intervals constructed via debiased ridge estimators. Theoretical predictions will be compared to empirical results to validate the distributional characterizations and the optimality of cross-validation schemes.
7f24b34a364f83f3162f70b74a12ad4d5c2735b4.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a precise, general, and uniform distributional characterization of the ridgeless minimum-norm interpolator in high dimensions, extending beyond previous results that focused only on ℓ_2 risks or specific settings. The approach provides exact quantification of implicit regularization in the most general distributional sense, and it is the first to show that standard cross-validation schemes yield simultaneous optimality for prediction, estimation, in-sample risk, and confidence interval length. The framework is broadly applicable to general random designs and suggests a pathway for analyzing implicit regularization in a wide class of interpolating estimators.

7f26566298dd9b89eb3446cc0f4bd2d2fa8aceed.title: NTFields: Neural Time Fields for Physics-Informed Robot Motion Planning
7f26566298dd9b89eb3446cc0f4bd2d2fa8aceed.research_question: How can robot motion planning in high-dimensional and cluttered environments be achieved efficiently and safely, without relying on expert demonstration data, while respecting physical constraints such as collision avoidance and speed limitations?
7f26566298dd9b89eb3446cc0f4bd2d2fa8aceed.hypothesis: A physics-informed neural network model that directly solves a nonlinear PDE (the Eikonal equation) can generate continuous time fields for robot motion planning, enabling fast, scalable, and safe path solutions in complex, high-dimensional environments without requiring expert trajectory data.
7f26566298dd9b89eb3446cc0f4bd2d2fa8aceed.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that leverages a physics-informed deep neural network to model the solution of the Eikonal equation for robot motion planning. The method will encode both robot configuration (c-space) and workspace information using dedicated encoders: a ResNet-style feed-forward network for c-space and a 3D CNN-based encoder for workspace, which processes voxelized representations of the environment and robot surface points. These embeddings will be combined using a nonlinear symmetric operator to respect the symmetry of the time field between start and goal configurations. The network will output a factorized time field, τ, which, together with the Euclidean distance between configurations, yields the predicted arrival time. The model will be trained using randomly sampled start and goal pairs, with a loss function based on matching predicted and ground-truth speed fields derived from a physically motivated speed model. During inference, bidirectional gradient-based path planning will be performed by following the gradients of the learned time field from both start and goal configurations, dynamically scaling step sizes to ensure safety near obstacles.
7f26566298dd9b89eb3446cc0f4bd2d2fa8aceed.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in a variety of 3D environments, including synthetic cluttered scenes and large, realistic environments from the Gibson dataset. The method will be evaluated on both 4-DOF and 6-DOF robot manipulators to assess scalability to high-dimensional configuration spaces. Baseline comparisons will include classical planners (FMM, RRT*, LazyPRM*), learning-based planners (MPNet), and supervised neural PDE solvers (IEF3D, EikoNet). Evaluation metrics will include planning time, path length, safety margin (minimum distance to obstacles), and success rate (percentage of collision-free solutions). Training data for the proposed method will be generated by random sampling and will not require expert trajectories, while baselines such as IEF3D and MPNet will require data from classical planners. Computational efficiency, generalization to unseen start-goal pairs, and scalability to high-dimensional spaces will be key aspects of the experimental analysis.
7f26566298dd9b89eb3446cc0f4bd2d2fa8aceed.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a physics-informed neural motion planner that eliminates the need for expert demonstration data by directly solving the Eikonal equation for continuous time field generation. A novel neural architecture is designed to encode both configuration and workspace information, incorporating a nonlinear symmetric operator to enforce time field symmetry. The method enables efficient bidirectional gradient-based planning and scales to high-dimensional robot configuration spaces where traditional grid-based and data-driven methods become computationally infeasible. The framework achieves significantly faster planning times and high success rates compared to state-of-the-art methods, with minimal data generation requirements.

7f270c9b098727675c9d8b893e362b561d61f27e.title: Policy Expansion for Bridging Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning
7f270c9b098727675c9d8b893e362b561d61f27e.research_question: How can the transition from offline to online reinforcement learning be improved to maximize both sample efficiency and policy performance, while retaining useful behaviors learned during offline training and enabling effective online exploration and adaptation?
7f270c9b098727675c9d8b893e362b561d61f27e.hypothesis: Introducing a policy expansion scheme that retains the offline-trained policy and adaptively composes it with a new, learnable policy during online training will preserve useful offline behaviors, facilitate adaptive exploration, and outperform direct fine-tuning or other baseline approaches in offline-to-online RL settings.
7f270c9b098727675c9d8b893e362b561d61f27e.proposed_method: A policy expansion framework is proposed for bridging offline and online reinforcement learning. After training a policy on offline data using a value-based offline RL algorithm (e.g., Implicit Q-Learning, IQL), the learned offline policy is frozen and added to a policy set. During online learning, a new, learnable policy is introduced and trained alongside the frozen offline policy. At each decision step, both policies propose actions, and a composite policy adaptively selects between them based on their estimated action values using a softmax distribution over Q-values. The critic (Q-function) and offline replay buffer are transferred to the online phase, and training is conducted by sampling from both offline and online buffers. Only the new policy is updated during online training, ensuring the preservation of offline behaviors while enabling the acquisition of new skills.
7f270c9b098727675c9d8b893e362b561d61f27e.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a variety of benchmark tasks from the D4RL suite, using both IQL and SAC as backbone algorithms for offline and online phases. The evaluation includes 1 million offline training steps followed by 1 million online fine-tuning steps, with performance averaged over 5 random seeds. Baselines include pure offline training, online training from scratch, buffer-based approaches, direct parameter transfer, and several recent offline-to-online RL methods (AWAC, Off2On, BT, JSRL). Performance is measured using normalized return curves and aggregated returns across tasks. Ablation studies investigate the impact of offline buffer inclusion, critic transfer, policy transfer, and offline policy freezing. Additional experiments demonstrate the method's applicability to heterogeneous offline-online algorithm pairs and analyze the adaptive policy composition during rollouts.
7f270c9b098727675c9d8b893e362b561d61f27e.novelty_claims: The proposed policy expansion scheme introduces a novel way to bridge offline and online RL by freezing the offline policy and adaptively composing it with a new online policy, rather than directly fine-tuning or replacing the offline policy. This approach preserves useful offline behaviors, enables state-adaptive policy selection, and allows for flexible combinations of heterogeneous offline and online RL algorithms. The method is orthogonal to specific RL algorithms and can be integrated with various value-based methods. Empirical results demonstrate superior or comparable performance to state-of-the-art baselines, and ablation studies highlight the importance of each component in the framework.

7f311906990df633b5815df2be91d09cf23203a9.title: Learning Time-Scales in Two-Layers Neural Networks
7f311906990df633b5815df2be91d09cf23203a9.research_question: What are the underlying mechanisms that govern the emergence of plateaus, separation of time scales, and incremental learning during gradient-based training of wide two-layer neural networks on high-dimensional data, particularly when the target function depends on a low-dimensional projection of the input?
7f311906990df633b5815df2be91d09cf23203a9.hypothesis: The learning dynamics of wide two-layer neural networks trained via gradient flow on high-dimensional data generated by a single-index model exhibit a hierarchical separation of time scales and incremental learning phases, which can be characterized by a sequence of polynomial approximations of the target function, and these phenomena arise due to the structure of the population gradient flow as a singularly perturbed dynamical system.
7f311906990df633b5815df2be91d09cf23203a9.proposed_method: A detailed theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted into the gradient flow dynamics of wide two-layer neural networks trained on data generated by a single-index model, where the target function depends on a one-dimensional projection of high-dimensional Gaussian covariates. The analysis will employ tools from dynamical systems theory, including singular perturbation theory and matched asymptotic expansions, to reduce the high-dimensional system to a lower-dimensional mean-field description. The evolution of the network function will be tracked in terms of its Hermite polynomial decomposition, with particular attention paid to the order in which polynomial components of the target function are learned over time. The study will also rigorously analyze the impact of initialization, activation function properties, and the scaling of network parameters on the emergence of plateaus and time-scale separation. Numerical simulations will be used to validate the theoretical predictions and to explore cases where the canonical learning order may fail due to specific choices of activation or target function.
7f311906990df633b5815df2be91d09cf23203a9.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed using synthetic datasets generated according to the single-index model, with high-dimensional Gaussian input vectors and target responses defined by various link functions. Wide two-layer neural networks with varying numbers of hidden units will be trained using gradient flow and stochastic gradient descent, under both mean-field and standard initializations. Baseline comparisons will include kernel regression models and linearized neural networks to highlight differences in learning dynamics and time-scale separation. Evaluation metrics will include empirical and population risk curves, decomposition of learned functions into Hermite polynomial components, and sample complexity required to achieve specified generalization error. The experimental setup will systematically vary the activation function, initialization scheme, and learning rate ratio between layers to probe their effects on incremental learning and plateaus.
7f311906990df633b5815df2be91d09cf23203a9.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a rigorous dynamical systems framework for understanding the incremental learning and time-scale separation phenomena in wide two-layer neural networks trained outside the kernel (lazy) regime. The approach provides a unified scenario that connects and extends previous theories, demonstrating that hierarchical learning of polynomial components and plateaus arise naturally from the structure of the mean-field gradient flow as a singularly perturbed system. The work further identifies precise conditions under which the canonical learning order holds or fails, and establishes new sample complexity results for learning polynomial functions in high dimensions. The methodology bridges theoretical analysis with numerical validation, offering new insights into generalization and feature learning in overparameterized neural networks.

7f401bb88652c5880289c24f8de214374f5df9f8.title: The Bayesian Learning Rule
7f401bb88652c5880289c24f8de214374f5df9f8.research_question: Can a unified Bayesian learning rule be developed that generalizes, unifies, and extends a wide range of machine learning algorithms across optimization, deep learning, and graphical models?
7f401bb88652c5880289c24f8de214374f5df9f8.hypothesis: A single learning rule derived from Bayesian principles, utilizing natural gradients and candidate distributions from exponential families, can serve as a general framework from which many existing and novel machine learning algorithms can be systematically derived.
7f401bb88652c5880289c24f8de214374f5df9f8.proposed_method: The proposed approach formulates learning as the optimization of a generalized Bayesian objective over a candidate distribution q(θ) from a chosen exponential family. The method employs natural-gradient descent in the space of natural parameters, updating q(θ) iteratively using the geometry induced by the Fisher information matrix. The update rule incorporates both the expected loss and the entropy of the candidate distribution, ensuring that higher-order information about the loss landscape is captured and assigned to appropriate parameters. By varying the complexity of the exponential family and the approximations to the natural gradients (e.g., delta method, stochastic approximations), the framework recovers classical algorithms (such as gradient descent, Newton’s method, and ridge regression), modern deep learning optimizers (SGD, RMSprop, Adam, Dropout), and enables the design of new algorithms for multimodal optimization and uncertainty estimation.
7f401bb88652c5880289c24f8de214374f5df9f8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by deriving a variety of well-known and novel algorithms from the proposed Bayesian learning rule and evaluating their empirical performance. Standard datasets from regression, classification, and deep learning benchmarks will be used, including synthetic data for ridge regression, standard image datasets for deep learning (e.g., MNIST, CIFAR), and time-series data for Kalman filtering. Baselines will include classical optimization methods, standard deep learning optimizers, and established Bayesian inference algorithms. Evaluation metrics will include predictive accuracy, convergence speed, uncertainty estimation quality, and robustness to overfitting. Comparative studies will assess both the theoretical unification and empirical performance improvements enabled by the proposed framework.
7f401bb88652c5880289c24f8de214374f5df9f8.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unifying Bayesian learning rule that systematically derives a wide range of existing algorithms as special cases, bridging optimization, deep learning, and Bayesian inference. The framework highlights the central role of natural gradients and information geometry in algorithm design, providing principled guidelines for developing new algorithms. Novel contributions include the derivation of new multimodal optimization and uncertainty estimation algorithms, as well as a general methodology for extending and improving existing methods through the choice of candidate distributions and gradient approximations.

7f6942cd9c0705d0b454d1c1b1058038a9954394.title: Minimum Description Length and Generalization Guarantees for Representation Learning
7f6942cd9c0705d0b454d1c1b1058038a9954394.research_question: How can the generalization performance of representation learning algorithms be theoretically guaranteed and tightly bounded, particularly in terms of the compressibility or minimum description length (MDL) of learned representations, rather than relying on mutual information measures?
7f6942cd9c0705d0b454d1c1b1058038a9954394.hypothesis: The generalization error of representation learning algorithms can be more accurately and tightly bounded by information-theoretic measures of compressibility, specifically the minimum description length (MDL) of the latent variables or labels, rather than by mutual information between input and representation. Furthermore, using data-dependent priors in the regularization term can improve generalization guarantees compared to conventional data-independent priors.
7f6942cd9c0705d0b454d1c1b1058038a9954394.proposed_method: A novel information-theoretic framework is proposed to analyze and bound the generalization error of representation learning algorithms. The approach leverages block-coding and lossy-compression techniques to measure the compressibility (MDL) of either the predicted labels or the latent variables generated by the encoder. The framework introduces new generalization bounds based on the multi-letter Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between the empirical distributions of representations (or labels) on training and test sets and a fixed or data-dependent prior. The method accommodates both deterministic and stochastic encoders, and extends to continuous latent spaces by employing lossy compression, thereby avoiding vacuous bounds that plague mutual information-based approaches. The framework also allows for the use of data-dependent priors, which can be tailored to the structure of the data and the encoder, enhancing the tightness and relevance of the bounds.
7f6942cd9c0705d0b454d1c1b1058038a9954394.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard supervised learning benchmarks, such as MNIST and CIFAR-10, employing encoder-decoder architectures typical of representation learning. The proposed compressibility-based regularization will be compared against traditional Information Bottleneck (IB) and Variational Information Bottleneck (VIB) methods, which use mutual information and data-independent priors, respectively. Evaluation metrics will include generalization error (difference between population and empirical risk), classification accuracy, and the measured KL-divergence or MDL of the latent variables. The impact of data-dependent priors versus fixed priors will be empirically assessed, and the ability of the proposed method to provide non-vacuous, structure-reflective bounds will be demonstrated.
7f6942cd9c0705d0b454d1c1b1058038a9954394.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first generalization bounds for representation learning algorithms that are expressed in terms of the minimum description length (MDL) of the latent variables, rather than mutual information. The framework is the first to provide non-vacuous, theoretically justified bounds for deterministic encoders and continuous latent spaces, overcoming key limitations of prior IB-based approaches. The method unifies and extends previous compressibility and PAC-MDL frameworks by incorporating block-coding, lossy compression, and data-dependent priors. Additionally, the approach subsumes geometric compressibility as a special case and establishes explicit connections to recent advances in conditional mutual information (CMI) theory.

7f712d58084e32ddc1b0cd60932f8bc0a0916330.title: Rethinking Goal-conditioned Supervised Learning and Its Connection to Offline RL
7f712d58084e32ddc1b0cd60932f8bc0a0916330.research_question: How can goal-conditioned reinforcement learning be improved in offline settings, particularly for tasks with sparse rewards, to achieve more efficient and effective policy learning without requiring online environment interaction?
7f712d58084e32ddc1b0cd60932f8bc0a0916330.hypothesis: Introducing a weighted supervised learning framework that leverages discounted relabeling, advantage-based weighting, and best-advantage selection will enable monotonic policy improvement and outperform existing offline goal-conditioned RL methods, especially in sparse reward scenarios.
7f712d58084e32ddc1b0cd60932f8bc0a0916330.proposed_method: A new algorithm, Weighted Goal-Conditioned Supervised Learning (WGCSL), is developed to generalize goal-conditioned supervised learning (GCSL) for offline RL. WGCSL constructs a relabeled dataset by applying hindsight goal relabeling to offline trajectories, then optimizes a weighted supervised learning objective. The weighting scheme combines three components: (1) a discounted relabeling weight that prioritizes shorter trajectories to relabeled goals, (2) a goal-conditioned exponential advantage weight that emphasizes samples with higher estimated advantage using a value function, and (3) a best-advantage weight that focuses learning on samples near the highest-return mode in multi-modal data. The policy is trained to minimize a weighted mean squared error between predicted and actual actions, while a value network is learned using temporal-difference error minimization. The approach is theoretically shown to optimize a lower bound of the goal-conditioned RL objective and to guarantee monotonic policy improvement under certain conditions.
7f712d58084e32ddc1b0cd60932f8bc0a0916330.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a benchmark suite of ten goal-conditioned tasks, including two point-based environments and eight simulated robotic manipulation domains (e.g., PointReach, FetchPush, HandReach). Offline datasets are collected using both random and expert policies, with sample sizes of 2 million for harder tasks and 100,000 for easier ones. WGCSL is compared against several baselines: GCSL, Hindsight Experience Replay (HER), goal-conditioned MARWIL, goal-conditioned Behavior Cloning (BC), goal-conditioned Batch-Constrained Q-Learning (BCQ), and goal-conditioned Conservative Q-Learning (CQL). Evaluation metrics include average return and learning efficiency, with results averaged over five random seeds. Ablation studies isolate the contributions of each weighting component, and value estimation robustness is also assessed. Policy and value networks use 3-layer MLPs with 256 units per layer, and training is performed with Adam optimizer and batch sizes tailored to task difficulty.
7f712d58084e32ddc1b0cd60932f8bc0a0916330.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a theoretically grounded, general weighting scheme for offline goal-conditioned RL that unifies discounted relabeling, exponential advantage weighting, and best-advantage selection. WGCSL is claimed to be the first to extend GCSL to the fully offline setting with proven monotonic policy improvement guarantees. The approach is substantially simpler and more stable than prior offline RL algorithms, avoiding explicit value underestimation or policy regularization. Empirical results demonstrate consistent outperformance over state-of-the-art baselines, especially in challenging sparse-reward and multi-modal tasks. A new benchmark and offline datasets for goal-conditioned RL are also provided.

7f7861674cc9ce4b8fa0e5442a4a5f171e890b99.title: Information-Computation Tradeoffs for Noiseless Linear Regression with Oblivious Contamination
7f7861674cc9ce4b8fa0e5442a4a5f171e890b99.research_question: What are the fundamental computational and statistical tradeoffs in noiseless linear regression with Gaussian covariates when the response variables are subject to additive oblivious contamination, and can computationally efficient algorithms achieve information-theoretically optimal sample complexity in this setting?
7f7861674cc9ce4b8fa0e5442a4a5f171e890b99.hypothesis: No computationally efficient algorithm can achieve the information-theoretic optimal sample complexity for noiseless linear regression under oblivious contamination; specifically, any efficient algorithm must incur a quadratic dependence on the inverse of the inlier fraction in its sample complexity.
7f7861674cc9ce4b8fa0e5442a4a5f171e890b99.proposed_method: A rigorous framework will be developed to analyze the computational hardness of noiseless linear regression with oblivious contamination using the Statistical Query (SQ) model. The approach will construct a family of contamination distributions, specifically discrete Gaussians with carefully chosen parameters, that satisfy the required inlier probability and are hard to distinguish from the null hypothesis using SQ algorithms. The central technical step involves reducing the estimation problem to a testing problem (conditional Non-Gaussian Component Analysis), and leveraging advanced Fourier and Hermite polynomial analysis to establish lower bounds on the SQ dimension. The methodology will adapt recent techniques for proving SQ lower bounds in settings where the chi-squared divergence is infinite, and will quantitatively relate the moments of discrete and continuous Gaussian noise to facilitate the analysis.
7f7861674cc9ce4b8fa0e5442a4a5f171e890b99.experiment_details: Theoretical experiments will be conducted by constructing explicit instances of the regression problem with Gaussian covariates and discrete Gaussian contamination. The analysis will focus on the SQ model, quantifying the number of queries and simulation complexity required to solve the associated testing problem. Baselines will include both information-theoretic (inefficient) algorithms and known polynomial-time algorithms, with the latter requiring sample complexity scaling as O(d/α^2). Evaluation metrics will center on the minimum SQ complexity (number of queries and simulation complexity) required to distinguish between the null and alternate hypotheses with high probability. Key setup details include varying the dimension d, inlier fraction α, and signal strength ρ, and constructing contamination distributions that maximize the hardness for SQ algorithms.
7f7861674cc9ce4b8fa0e5442a4a5f171e890b99.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a formal SQ lower bound for noiseless linear regression with oblivious contamination, demonstrating that the quadratic dependence on the inverse inlier fraction is inherent for efficient algorithms in this model. The approach leverages a novel construction of discrete Gaussian contamination distributions and adapts advanced Fourier-analytic techniques to settings where standard chi-squared-based arguments fail. The results provide the first formal evidence of a fundamental information-computation gap in this robust regression setting, and the techniques developed are expected to generalize to related robust estimation and testing problems.

7f891be2747c95d6b2499d1bd00c427ccea55b61.title: Multimodal Optimal Transport-based Co-Attention Transformer with Global Structure Consistency for Survival Prediction
7f891be2747c95d6b2499d1bd00c427ccea55b61.research_question: How can survival prediction in cancer prognosis be improved by integrating histology and genomic data, specifically addressing the challenges of effective representation of gigapixel whole slide images (WSIs) and modeling global structural interactions within and across modalities?
7f891be2747c95d6b2499d1bd00c427ccea55b61.hypothesis: Integrating histology and genomic data using a multimodal optimal transport-based co-attention mechanism that enforces global structure consistency will improve the identification of informative instances and enhance survival prediction performance compared to existing methods that rely on local similarity or conventional co-attention.
7f891be2747c95d6b2499d1bd00c427ccea55b61.proposed_method: A novel multimodal framework will be developed that formulates both histology (WSI) and genomic data as bags of instances, with instance-level features extracted via dedicated encoders. Optimal transport (OT)-based co-attention will be applied to match instances between the WSI and genomic bags, enabling the identification of informative patches that exhibit global structure consistency, such as tumor microenvironment (TME) interactions and gene co-expression patterns. To address the computational complexity of OT on large WSIs, an efficient approximation will be implemented by sampling micro-batches of WSI patches and solving an unbalanced mini-batch OT (UMBOT) problem, with results averaged to approximate the full OT solution. Selected informative instances will be aggregated using a Transformer encoder to produce bag-level representations for each modality, which are then concatenated and used to predict survival risk via a deep ordinal regression model.
7f891be2747c95d6b2499d1bd00c427ccea55b61.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five benchmark cancer datasets from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA): BLCA, BRCA, UCEC, GBMLGG, and LUAD, each containing paired WSIs and genomic data with ground-truth survival outcomes. Evaluation will use 5-fold cross-validation, reporting the concordance index (C-Index) and standard deviation to assess the accuracy of risk ranking. The proposed method will be compared against unimodal baselines (e.g., SNN, TransMIL, AttnMIL, CLAM, DTFD-MIL) and state-of-the-art multimodal approaches (e.g., MCAT, Pathomic, Porpoise, PONET). Implementation details include patch extraction from WSIs, feature encoding with pretrained ResNet-50 and SNN, and optimization with Adam. Ablation studies will assess the contributions of OT-based co-attention and micro-batch strategies, and computational efficiency will be measured in terms of patch processing speed. Statistical analysis will include Kaplan-Meier survival curves and logrank tests for patient stratification.
7f891be2747c95d6b2499d1bd00c427ccea55b61.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a multimodal optimal transport-based co-attention transformer that, for the first time, enforces global structure consistency between histology and genomics for survival prediction. The method provides a rigorous and globally-aware instance selection mechanism via OT, overcoming the limitations of local similarity-based co-attention. An efficient and robust micro-batch OT approximation is developed to make the approach scalable to gigapixel WSIs. The framework generalizes multimodal learning by modeling potential structures across modalities, and extensive experiments demonstrate significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods in both predictive performance and computational efficiency.

7f91d6995fd80799006562be2220e9ff22f8707d.title: Diffusion Schrödinger Bridge Matching
7f91d6995fd80799006562be2220e9ff22f8707d.research_question: How can dynamic mass transport between two probability distributions be efficiently and accurately computed, particularly in high-dimensional settings, while preserving desirable properties such as closeness to the optimal transport map and scalability for generative modeling and domain transfer tasks?
7f91d6995fd80799006562be2220e9ff22f8707d.hypothesis: Iteratively alternating between Markovian and reciprocal projections in the space of path measures, combined with a diffusion-based numerical algorithm, will yield a scalable and accurate method for solving Schrödinger Bridge problems that mitigates the error accumulation and scalability issues of previous approaches.
7f91d6995fd80799006562be2220e9ff22f8707d.proposed_method: A new methodology, Iterative Markovian Fitting (IMF), is developed to solve Schrödinger Bridge (SB) problems by alternately projecting path measures onto the space of Markov processes and onto the reciprocal class of a reference diffusion. The numerical algorithm, Diffusion Schrödinger Bridge Matching (DSBM), implements IMF by learning the drift functions of forward and backward SDEs using neural networks, with each iteration involving regression losses based on conditional expectations of score functions. The method alternates between forward and backward Markovian projections, ensuring preservation of initial and terminal distributions and mitigating bias accumulation. The algorithm supports flexible initialization, including independent couplings or approximate static SB couplings, and leverages efficient sampling and trajectory caching strategies to scale to high dimensions.
7f91d6995fd80799006562be2220e9ff22f8707d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of transport tasks, including 2D synthetic datasets (moons, scurve, 8gaussians), high-dimensional Gaussian transport (d=50), and real-world domain transfer tasks such as MNIST-to-EMNIST, CelebA, AFHQ, and unpaired fluid flow downscaling. Baselines will include Flow Matching, Conditional Flow Matching, OT-CFM, Rectified Flow, DSB, SB-CFM, and other recent SB methods. Evaluation metrics will include 2-Wasserstein distance, integrated path energy, KL divergence between learned and true marginals, Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), LPIPS for image alignment, and ℓ2 distances for super-resolution tasks. Experimental setups will involve both direct and approximate OT/SB couplings, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of initialization and noise parameters.
7f91d6995fd80799006562be2220e9ff22f8707d.novelty_claims: The proposed IMF methodology is a dual to classical Iterative Proportional Fitting (IPF) and uniquely preserves initial and terminal distributions at each iteration. DSBM introduces a practical, scalable algorithm for solving SB problems that avoids time-discretization and bias accumulation issues of prior methods, and unifies or generalizes several recent transport and generative modeling approaches as special or limiting cases. The approach provides improved accuracy and efficiency in high-dimensional and challenging transport scenarios, and enables new insights into the connections between SB, OT, and flow-based generative models.

7fad4f23fdf6d152ad83b3d5694acc1c93453ff1.title: Unravelling in Collaborative Learning
7fad4f23fdf6d152ad83b3d5694acc1c93453ff1.research_question: How can collaborative learning among strategic agents with private, heterogeneous data quality be stabilized to prevent adverse selection and unravelling, especially when external monetary transfers are not allowed and data quality is not centrally known?
7fad4f23fdf6d152ad83b3d5694acc1c93453ff1.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a mechanism based on probabilistic verification of agents' data quality, rather than direct type revelation or monetary transfers, can induce stable, welfare-maximizing collaboration among strategic agents in collaborative learning, even under information asymmetry.
7fad4f23fdf6d152ad83b3d5694acc1c93453ff1.proposed_method: A novel aggregation mechanism is proposed wherein a benevolent aggregator organizes collaboration among agents with unknown, heterogeneous data quality. Instead of relying on agents to truthfully declare their data quality (types), the aggregator collects a small number of samples from each agent to estimate their quality indices using empirical risk-based estimators. Based on these estimated types, the aggregator determines the optimal number of samples to request from each agent using a modified welfare-maximizing scheme that accounts for estimation error. The mechanism is designed such that the grand coalition (all agents participating) forms a Nash equilibrium with high probability, even when agents are strategic and information is asymmetric. The approach does not require external monetary transfers, instead leveraging statistical estimation and carefully calibrated sample requests to ensure individual rationality and approximate incentive compatibility.
7fad4f23fdf6d152ad83b3d5694acc1c93453ff1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in the context of supervised classification, where agents possess data from distributions with varying degrees of divergence from a target distribution. Synthetic and/or real-world datasets will be used to simulate agents with different data qualities. The proposed probabilistic verification-based mechanism will be compared against naive aggregation (direct revelation) and, where possible, VCG-style mechanisms (with transfers) as baselines. Evaluation metrics will include coalition stability (size and composition at equilibrium), total social welfare, and model performance (risk or accuracy). The experimental setup will also assess the accuracy of type estimation, the effect of sample size for estimation, and the robustness of the mechanism to varying degrees of information asymmetry and agent heterogeneity.
7fad4f23fdf6d152ad83b3d5694acc1c93453ff1.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a transfer-free, probabilistic verification-based mechanism that stabilizes collaborative learning among strategic agents with private data quality, effectively breaking the unravelling phenomenon caused by adverse selection. The mechanism leverages empirical estimation of data quality and adapts sample requests to ensure the grand coalition is a Nash equilibrium with high probability, without requiring agents to know or reveal their true types. This approach addresses a fundamental gap in the literature by providing a practical, incentive-aware solution to coalition stability in collaborative learning under information asymmetry, where previous work has largely focused on settings with observable types or allowed monetary transfers.

7fadcaca88918b31b1664603a9b4dd89e8b162f1.title: Weight decay induces low-rank attention layers
7fadcaca88918b31b1664603a9b4dd89e8b162f1.research_question: How does weight decay or L2-regularization affect the rank and structure of parameter matrices in neural network models with multiplicative (factorized) parametrizations, such as those found in attention layers of transformers, and what are the implications for model performance and regularization strategies?
7fadcaca88918b31b1664603a9b4dd89e8b162f1.hypothesis: Applying weight decay or L2-regularization to factorized parameter matrices in attention layers induces a low-rank bias in the resulting matrix products, potentially affecting model expressivity and performance, and this effect can be modulated by decoupling regularization strengths across different layers.
7fadcaca88918b31b1664603a9b4dd89e8b162f1.proposed_method: A theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted into the effects of weight decay and L2-regularization on neural network models with factorized parameter matrices, focusing on attention layers in transformer architectures. Theoretical analysis will establish the equivalence between L2-regularization on factorized matrices and nuclear norm regularization on their product, demonstrating that this equivalence emerges exponentially quickly during gradient-based optimization. Empirical validation will be performed by training models with varying weight decay strengths applied specifically to attention layers, using both standard and decoupled regularization strategies. The methodology will include both synthetic settings (e.g., 2-layer linear networks) and practical deep learning scenarios (language modeling and vision tasks), with detailed measurement of matrix ranks and convergence properties.
7fadcaca88918b31b1664603a9b4dd89e8b162f1.experiment_details: Experiments will include training 2-layer transformers and deep linear networks on synthetic tasks such as associative recall, as well as training small-scale language models (e.g., 125M parameter transformers) on the Pile dataset and Vision Transformers on ImageNet. Weight decay strengths will be varied independently for attention and MLP layers, and models will be optimized using AdamW. Evaluation metrics will include the pseudo-rank (number of singular values capturing 95% of the matrix norm) of key-query and value-projection matrix products, test set perplexity for language models, and classification accuracy for vision models. Baselines will include models with no weight decay and with standard uniform regularization. Additional analysis will be performed on pre-trained foundation models (e.g., LLAMA2, Vision Transformer) to assess the presence of low-rank effects in their attention matrices.
7fadcaca88918b31b1664603a9b4dd89e8b162f1.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a comprehensive theoretical framework demonstrating that L2-regularization on factorized matrices is effectively equivalent to nuclear norm regularization on their product, with this equivalence manifesting rapidly during training. It provides the first systematic empirical evidence that weight decay induces significant low-rank structure in attention layers of transformers, even in online and practical training regimes. The research also claims novelty in showing that decoupling weight decay strengths across layers can improve performance, challenging the conventional practice of uniform regularization. Furthermore, it highlights the unintended consequences of standard regularization strategies on model expressivity and opens new directions for layer-specific regularization in deep learning architectures.

7fc5cf21a9e98076b93072c141447b5b6134f68d.title: The Curse of Unrolling: Rate of Differentiating Through Optimization
7fc5cf21a9e98076b93072c141447b5b6134f68d.research_question: How can the convergence rate of Jacobian estimation through unrolled differentiation in optimization problems be characterized, and what algorithmic strategies can mitigate inefficiencies or instability in this process, particularly for quadratic objectives and first-order methods?
7fc5cf21a9e98076b93072c141447b5b6134f68d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the convergence rate of the Jacobian in unrolled differentiation is fundamentally limited by a trade-off between asymptotic speed and the presence of a burn-in phase, and that novel algorithmic strategies based on polynomial acceleration (such as Sobolev orthogonal polynomials) can mitigate this trade-off and improve performance.
7fc5cf21a9e98076b93072c141447b5b6134f68d.proposed_method: A detailed theoretical and algorithmic framework will be developed to analyze and accelerate the computation of the Jacobian of implicitly defined optimization solutions via unrolled differentiation. The approach will focus on quadratic objectives where the solution is approximated by iterates of first-order methods, such as gradient descent and the Chebyshev method. A master identity will be derived linking the convergence of the Jacobian to the residual polynomial and its derivative associated with the optimization method. Furthermore, a novel accelerated algorithm based on Sobolev orthogonal polynomials will be constructed, leveraging a Sobolev scalar product that incorporates both the polynomial and its derivative, and using a parametric family of spectral densities (e.g., Gegenbauer distributions) to approximate the expected spectral density of the problem class. Both non-asymptotic and asymptotic versions of the accelerated method will be implemented, with the asymptotic version corresponding to a weighted average of Polyak’s Heavy Ball iterates.
7fc5cf21a9e98076b93072c141447b5b6134f68d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets, including ridge regression tasks on the UCI Breast Cancer and Bodyfat datasets, as well as synthetic data generated by random Gaussian matrices. The performance of the proposed Sobolev-based accelerated algorithm will be compared to baseline methods such as standard gradient descent (with various step sizes) and the Chebyshev method. Evaluation metrics will include the suboptimality of the Jacobian (measured in Frobenius norm) as a function of the number of unrolling iterations, as well as the presence and duration of burn-in phases and asymptotic convergence rates. Additional experiments will be performed on regularized logistic regression objectives to assess empirical generalization beyond the quadratic setting. Theoretical predictions will be validated against empirical results, and sensitivity to algorithmic parameters (e.g., step size, spectral density choice) will be explored.
7fc5cf21a9e98076b93072c141447b5b6134f68d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a comprehensive non-asymptotic convergence rate analysis for unrolled differentiation of quadratic objectives, including both gradient descent and the Chebyshev method, and rigorously characterizes the 'curse of unrolling'—a trade-off between fast asymptotic convergence and the presence of a condition-number-dependent burn-in phase. A novel accelerated unrolling algorithm based on Sobolev orthogonal polynomials is proposed, which provably reduces or eliminates the burn-in phase while achieving accelerated asymptotic rates. The approach establishes new connections between optimization, automatic differentiation, and the theory of orthogonal polynomials, and provides practical update rules for optimal unrolling strategies. Theoretical findings are supported by empirical validation on real and synthetic datasets.

7fd77e72e3479a5179458f0b9b85403aa6d107e8.title: Near Optimal Decision Trees in a SPLIT Second
7fd77e72e3479a5179458f0b9b85403aa6d107e8.research_question: How can decision tree optimization be made both highly accurate and scalable, enabling the construction of interpretable, sparse, and near-optimal decision trees and Rashomon sets for large datasets with many features and deeper trees?
7fd77e72e3479a5179458f0b9b85403aa6d107e8.hypothesis: It is possible to achieve near-optimal accuracy and sparsity in decision trees with orders-of-magnitude improvements in scalability by combining limited-depth global optimization with greedy splitting near the leaves, without significant loss in performance compared to fully optimal methods.
7fd77e72e3479a5179458f0b9b85403aa6d107e8.proposed_method: A family of algorithms, termed SPLIT (SParse Lookahead for Interpretable Trees), will be developed to optimize decision trees by performing dynamic programming with branch-and-bound up to a user-specified lookahead depth. Beyond this depth, the algorithm will switch to greedy splitting, leveraging the empirical observation that greedy splits near the leaves yield performance close to optimal. The method will include mechanisms to initialize subproblems at the lookahead depth using greedy subtrees, and optionally post-process these subtrees with fully optimal solutions. A polynomial-time variant, LicketySPLIT, will recursively apply SPLIT with lookahead depth one, ensuring scalability for very large datasets. Additionally, RESPLIT will extend these algorithms to efficiently approximate Rashomon sets of near-optimal trees, supporting downstream tasks such as variable importance analysis.
7fd77e72e3479a5179458f0b9b85403aa6d107e8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of real-world binary classification datasets, including Bike, COMPAS, HELOC, HIV, Netherlands, Spambase, and Adult. The proposed methods will be compared against state-of-the-art optimal decision tree algorithms (e.g., GOSDT, dynamic programming with branch-and-bound), greedy baselines (e.g., CART, C4.5), and other hybrid or probabilistic search methods. Evaluation metrics will include regularized test loss (combining accuracy and sparsity), training time, number of leaves (sparsity), and quality of Rashomon set approximations (precision, correlation of variable importances). Experiments will vary sparsity penalties and depth budgets, and include timeouts for slow baselines. Additional analyses will assess the scalability and accuracy of Rashomon set estimation, as well as the impact on downstream variable importance distributions.
7fd77e72e3479a5179458f0b9b85403aa6d107e8.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new family of decision tree optimization algorithms that achieve a balance between the accuracy and sparsity of globally optimal methods and the scalability of greedy approaches. SPLIT and its variants are claimed to be orders of magnitude faster than existing optimal methods, with negligible loss in accuracy or sparsity. The methodology provides theoretical guarantees on runtime and optimality, and enables scalable, accurate approximation of Rashomon sets for interpretable machine learning. This work also demonstrates that the proposed algorithms can dramatically improve the feasibility of variable importance analysis over large sets of near-optimal models.

7fe071ea76e49bc3e573beb53f07721630954247.title: Promptbreeder: Self-Referential Self-Improvement Via Prompt Evolution
7fe071ea76e49bc3e573beb53f07721630954247.research_question: Can automated, self-referential evolutionary algorithms be developed to evolve and adapt prompt strategies for large language models across diverse domains, thereby improving model performance without manual prompt engineering or parameter updates?
7fe071ea76e49bc3e573beb53f07721630954247.hypothesis: Automated, self-referential evolution of both task-prompts and mutation-prompts using large language models will yield more effective, domain-adaptive prompt strategies than existing hand-crafted or single-level automated prompt engineering methods, resulting in superior performance on a range of reasoning and classification tasks.
7fe071ea76e49bc3e573beb53f07721630954247.proposed_method: A general-purpose evolutionary framework will be constructed in which a population of task-prompts and mutation-prompts is initialized using combinations of domain-specific problem descriptions, 'thinking styles', and mutation instructions. An LLM will serve as the mutation operator, generating new task-prompts by applying mutation-prompts to existing prompts, and also evolving the mutation-prompts themselves via hyper-mutation. The evolutionary process will employ a binary tournament genetic algorithm, evaluating the fitness of each prompt by its performance on sampled batches from a training set. Multiple mutation operator classes—including direct mutation, estimation of distribution, lineage-based mutation, hyper-mutation, Lamarckian mutation, prompt crossover, and context shuffling—will be implemented to maintain diversity and enable both prompt-level and meta-level (mutation-prompt) adaptation. The system will iteratively select, mutate, and transmit the most effective evolutionary units (task-prompt and associated mutation-prompt pairs) over multiple generations, with the goal of discovering increasingly effective prompt strategies tailored to the target domain.
7fe071ea76e49bc3e573beb53f07721630954247.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of established benchmarks covering arithmetic reasoning (GSM8K, SVAMP, MultiArith, AddSub, AQuA-RAT, SingleEq), commonsense reasoning (CommonsenseQA, StrategyQA), instruction induction, and hate speech classification (ETHOS). For each dataset, the population will be evolved for 20-30 generations with a population size of 50, using random batches of 100 Q&A pairs for fitness evaluation. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art prompt strategies, including Chain-of-Thought, Plan-and-Solve, Automatic Prompt Engineer, OPRO, and others, using both zero-shot and few-shot settings. Evaluation metrics will primarily be accuracy, with detailed ablation studies to assess the contribution of self-referential and diversity-maintaining components. The underlying LLMs will include PaLM 2-L and text-davinci-003, and results will be reported for both.
7fe071ea76e49bc3e573beb53f07721630954247.novelty_claims: The approach introduces a self-referential, fully automated evolutionary system that simultaneously evolves both task-prompts and the mutation-prompts that govern their adaptation, enabling open-ended self-improvement without any parameter updates to the underlying LLM. The method leverages a diverse set of mutation operators, including meta-level hyper-mutation and Lamarckian mechanisms, to maintain diversity and avoid premature convergence. The system demonstrates superior performance over existing prompt engineering methods across a wide range of reasoning and classification tasks, and is capable of evolving intricate, domain-specific prompt strategies that outperform hand-crafted prompts. This framework points toward scalable, language-based self-improvement for LLMs that is compatible with API-based and increasingly large models.

7ff6dfa0ca6c6402803def2049c1727394d4485b.title: Hierarchical Koopman Diffusion: Fast Generation with Interpretable Diffusion Trajectory
7ff6dfa0ca6c6402803def2049c1727394d4485b.research_question: Can a generative modeling framework be developed that enables both fast, one-step image generation and interpretable, controllable generative trajectories, thereby bridging the gap between efficiency and transparency in diffusion-based image synthesis?
7ff6dfa0ca6c6402803def2049c1727394d4485b.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by leveraging Koopman operator theory to lift nonlinear diffusion dynamics into a latent space governed by linear operators, it is possible to achieve efficient one-step sampling while retaining explicit access to and control over intermediate generative states, thus enabling both high-quality image generation and interpretability.
7ff6dfa0ca6c6402803def2049c1727394d4485b.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces a hierarchical Koopman Diffusion (HKD) framework for image generation. The approach encodes noisy images at multiple spatial resolutions using a U-Net-based encoder, projecting features at each scale into distinct Koopman subspaces. In each subspace, the latent features evolve according to locally parameterized, spatially-varying linear operators, enabling closed-form solutions for the generative trajectory via matrix exponentiation. The decoder reconstructs the final image by integrating evolved latent features from all scales, using skip connections and upsampling. Training is supervised with a trajectory consistency loss that enforces alignment between analytically evolved intermediate states and their expected denoised counterparts, using perceptual metrics such as LPIPS to ensure semantic fidelity. The entire model, including encoder, decoder, and Koopman operators, is trained end-to-end.
7ff6dfa0ca6c6402803def2049c1727394d4485b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image generation benchmarks, specifically CIFAR-10 and FFHQ (64x64), to evaluate both generation quality and interpretability. The proposed HKD framework will be compared against leading one-step diffusion baselines, including distillation-based methods (e.g., KD, PD, DMD, Rectified Flow) and consistency models (e.g., CT, iCT, ECM), as well as multi-step diffusion models (e.g., DDPM, ScoreSDE, DDIM, EDM). The primary evaluation metric will be Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), with FID-50k reported for quantitative comparison. Training will use the Adam optimizer with a learning rate of 1e-3 and weight decay of 0.95, and all models will be initialized with pretrained U-Net weights. Additional experiments will include spectral analysis of the Koopman operators to interpret generative dynamics, and targeted image editing tasks (e.g., frequency-aware interventions, inpainting, coloring) to demonstrate controllability and semantic correspondence along the generative trajectory. Ablation studies will assess the contributions of hierarchical modeling, trajectory consistency loss, and Koopman evolution.
7ff6dfa0ca6c6402803def2049c1727394d4485b.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to integrate Koopman operator theory into diffusion-based image generation, enabling explicit, closed-form access to all intermediate generative states in a one-step sampling paradigm. The hierarchical design disentangles generative dynamics across spatial resolutions, systematically capturing coarse-to-fine details. The method uniquely combines fast, one-step generation with principled interpretability and fine-grained trajectory-level control, features not available in existing one-step or consistency-based diffusion models. Additionally, the framework introduces a novel trajectory consistency loss for intermediate state supervision and provides a spectral analysis toolkit for understanding and manipulating the generative process.

801203604112b81b7490cefe3ca368854aa6230e.title: Adaptive Message Passing: A General Framework to Mitigate Oversmoothing, Oversquashing, and Underreaching
801203604112b81b7490cefe3ca368854aa6230e.research_question: How can message passing neural network architectures be enhanced to effectively capture long-range dependencies in graphs, while mitigating the known issues of oversmoothing, oversquashing, and underreaching?
801203604112b81b7490cefe3ca368854aa6230e.hypothesis: Allowing deep graph networks to adaptively learn both the depth of message passing and a soft message filtering policy will enable better propagation of relevant information across distant nodes, thereby mitigating oversmoothing, oversquashing, and underreaching, and improving performance on tasks requiring long-range interactions.
801203604112b81b7490cefe3ca368854aa6230e.proposed_method: A general probabilistic framework, termed Adaptive Message Passing (AMP), is proposed to augment message passing neural networks (MPNNs) with adaptive depth selection and learnable message filtering. Within a variational inference framework, the architecture learns a distribution over network depth and a soft, differentiable message filter at each layer and node, which determines how much information is propagated. The method defines a joint generative model over network parameters, depth, message filters, and outputs, and optimizes the evidence lower bound (ELBO) via backpropagation. Message filters are parameterized either as functions of node input features or node embeddings at each layer, and the variational distributions over depth are chosen from unbounded, truncated families (e.g., Poisson, Gaussian mixtures) to allow potentially infinite depth but practical truncation. The approach includes layer-wise readouts and regularization terms, and is fully differentiable, enabling efficient end-to-end training.
801203604112b81b7490cefe3ca368854aa6230e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world graph datasets that require modeling long-range dependencies. Synthetic tasks include predicting graph diameter, single-source shortest paths (SSSP), and node eccentricity on graphs of 25-35 nodes generated by standard random graph models, with mean squared error as the evaluation metric. Real-world tasks involve node and graph prediction benchmarks from the Long Range Graph Benchmark, such as peptides-func (multi-label classification, evaluated by average precision) and peptides-struct (regression, evaluated by mean absolute error), with graphs of approximately 150 nodes. AMP will be integrated with several base architectures (GCN, GIN, GatedGCN, ADGN), and compared against strong baselines including GAT, GraphSAGE, GCNII, DGC, GRAND, and recent state-of-the-art methods. Hyperparameters will be tuned via grid search, and early stopping will be used based on validation performance. Ablation studies will assess the impact of message filtering, and qualitative analyses (e.g., Dirichlet energy, sensitivity, learned depth distributions) will be performed to evaluate mitigation of oversmoothing and oversquashing.
801203604112b81b7490cefe3ca368854aa6230e.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to jointly learn both the depth and a soft, adaptive message filtering policy in deep graph networks within a principled variational inference setting. Unlike prior approaches that require manual depth selection or fixed message passing schedules, this method enables the network to dynamically determine how many layers to use and which messages to propagate, based on the task and input graph. The approach is fully differentiable and scalable, introduces new families of variational distributions for depth, and provides theoretical guarantees for information propagation and sensitivity reduction. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate consistent improvements over baselines on tasks requiring long-range information, and analyses will show effective mitigation of oversmoothing, oversquashing, and underreaching.

8043fd020e615c7672d7b39f7d39231a44cb5b89.title: FORLA:Federated Object-centric Representation Learning with Slot Attention
8043fd020e615c7672d7b39f7d39231a44cb5b89.research_question: How can unsupervised object-centric visual representations be learned efficiently and robustly across heterogeneous, distributed, and unlabeled datasets in a federated learning setting, while preserving both global semantic structure and local client-specific factors?
8043fd020e615c7672d7b39f7d39231a44cb5b89.hypothesis: A federated object-centric representation learning framework that combines collaborative feature adaptation with slot attention and a two-branch student–teacher architecture will enable the learning of compact, universal, and interpretable visual representations that generalize across domains, outperforming both centralized and individualized training approaches without requiring data sharing.
8043fd020e615c7672d7b39f7d39231a44cb5b89.proposed_method: A novel federated learning framework, FORLA, is proposed that integrates object-centric representation learning using slot attention with collaborative feature adaptation across clients. Each client extracts features from multiple frozen vision foundation models (such as DINO, SAM, MAE, CLIP), which are concatenated and then compressed via a lightweight, learnable adapter module (MLP, mixture-of-experts, or attention-based feature modulation). The adapted features are processed by a shared slot attention module to produce object-centric latent slots. A two-branch student–teacher architecture is employed: the student branch reconstructs the original high-dimensional features, while the teacher branch reconstructs the adapted low-dimensional features. Both branches share the adapter and slot attention modules, and their parameters are periodically aggregated across clients using federated averaging (FedAvg). Training proceeds in two stages: initial global distillation and alignment via student parameter aggregation, followed by local cross-branch knowledge transfer using a self-averaging strategy (LocalFedAvg) between student and teacher branches. This approach enables the learning of a global, harmonized object-centric representation while allowing for local adaptation and personalization.
8043fd020e615c7672d7b39f7d39231a44cb5b89.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on seven datasets spanning both surgical (Abdominal, Cholec80, proprietary Thoracic) and natural vision domains (COCO, PASCAL VOC2012, YouTube-VIS, YouTube-Objects), totaling approximately 1.4 million images. The evaluation will compare three training regimes: individualized (per-dataset), centralized (mixed domains), and federated (each dataset as a client). Features are extracted from frozen ViT-B/16 encoders of DINO, MAE, CLIP, and SAM. Object-centric representation quality will be assessed using metrics such as Foreground Adjusted Rand Index (FG-ARI), Mean Best Overlap (mBO), Correct Localization (CorLoc), and Mean Best Hausdorff Distance (mBHD). Baselines include single foundation models, naive feature concatenation, and various adapter types under both centralized and federated setups. Additional experiments will test the effects of data stratification, domain heterogeneity, model personalization, and compatibility with different federated optimization algorithms (FedAvg, FedProx, FedAdam).
8043fd020e615c7672d7b39f7d39231a44cb5b89.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to scale unsupervised object-centric learning with slot attention to large, multi-domain federated settings, bridging the gap between object-centric learning and federated optimization. Key innovations include a communication-efficient two-branch student–teacher architecture for feature distillation, harmonization of heterogeneous foundation model features without data sharing, and integration of slot attention for cross-domain object discovery. The method achieves superior performance over both centralized and individualized baselines, with significant reductions in communication cost (up to 6.7×) and improved generalization across domains. The approach also enables further personalization and robust learning under data scarcity and domain heterogeneity, establishing federated slot attention as an effective tool for scalable, unsupervised visual representation learning from distributed, non-IID data.

8048bbd498c13abfec48670fd201bc4c5312db0e.title: On the Integration of Spatial-Temporal Knowledge: A Lightweight Approach to Atmospheric Time Series Forecasting
8048bbd498c13abfec48670fd201bc4c5312db0e.research_question: How can atmospheric time series forecasting be improved by integrating spatial-temporal knowledge, while maintaining model efficiency and scalability for large-scale datasets?
8048bbd498c13abfec48670fd201bc4c5312db0e.hypothesis: Spatial-temporal position embeddings that explicitly encode geographical coordinates and temporal features can capture spatial-temporal correlations in atmospheric time series data, enabling lightweight models to achieve competitive or superior forecasting performance compared to complex architectures such as Transformers and STGNNs.
8048bbd498c13abfec48670fd201bc4c5312db0e.proposed_method: A novel lightweight forecasting model, STELLA, will be developed that integrates spatial-temporal position embedding (STPE) with a simple multi-layer perceptron (MLP) backbone. The STPE module will encode both the normalized geographical coordinates (longitude, latitude, altitude) of each station and multi-scale temporal features (hour-in-day, day-in-month, month-in-year) using learnable embedding matrices. These embeddings will be combined with input time series data and processed through a shallow MLP encoder with residual connections, followed by a linear output layer to generate multi-step forecasts. The model's parameter count will be independent of the number of stations, and its computational complexity will scale linearly with the number of stations, ensuring efficiency and scalability.
8048bbd498c13abfec48670fd201bc4c5312db0e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five real-world atmospheric datasets: GlobalWind, GlobalTemp, ChinaWind, ChinaTemp, and China-PM2.5, covering both short-term and long-term forecasting tasks with varying spatial and temporal resolutions. The proposed model will be compared against 17 baselines, including classic statistical methods (HI, ARIMA), spatial-temporal graph neural networks (AGCRN, MTGNN, GTS), Transformer-based time series models (Informer, FEDformer, DSformer, PatchTST, iTransformer, DUET), lightweight MLP-based models (N-BEATS, DLinear, FITS), and ATSF-specialized Transformers (AirFormer, Corrformer, MRIformer). Evaluation metrics will include Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). Ablation studies will assess the contributions of spatial and temporal embeddings, and efficiency analyses will compare parameter counts, training times, and memory usage. Additional experiments will test the generalization of STPE by incorporating it into existing Transformer models.
8048bbd498c13abfec48670fd201bc4c5312db0e.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first lightweight model for atmospheric time series forecasting that leverages spatial-temporal position embeddings to capture spatial-temporal correlations without attention mechanisms or complex architectures. The approach demonstrates that explicit integration of spatial-temporal knowledge can outperform or match state-of-the-art Transformer and STGNN models with orders of magnitude fewer parameters and significantly reduced computational requirements. The method provides new theoretical and empirical insights into the role of spatial-temporal knowledge in atmospheric forecasting and offers a scalable, interpretable, and efficient alternative to prevailing deep learning architectures.

808b6f529e9463f1606b0b1c16d68ab1103201aa.title: EraseFlow: Learning Concept Erasure Policies via GFlowNet-Driven Alignment
808b6f529e9463f1606b0b1c16d68ab1103201aa.research_question: How can specific visual concepts be effectively and robustly erased from pretrained text-to-image diffusion models without degrading image quality, requiring adversarial reward models, or incurring prohibitive retraining costs?
808b6f529e9463f1606b0b1c16d68ab1103201aa.hypothesis: Learning concept erasure policies via a trajectory-balance objective in Generative Flow Networks (GFlowNets), using a reward-free alignment strategy, enables robust and efficient removal of targeted concepts from diffusion models while preserving the model's prior generative quality and resisting adversarial reintroduction.
808b6f529e9463f1606b0b1c16d68ab1103201aa.proposed_method: The proposed method, EraseFlow, formulates concept erasure in text-to-image diffusion models as an exploration problem over denoising trajectories, optimized using GFlowNets with a trajectory-balance (TB) objective. Instead of relying on external or adversarially crafted reward models, EraseFlow employs a reward-free alignment strategy, assigning a constant reward to anchor (safe) trajectories and zero to others. During training, the method samples entire denoising trajectories conditioned on both the target (to erase) and anchor (safe) prompts, and minimizes a TB loss that aligns the distribution of the target prompt with the anchor prompt. This process redistributes probability mass away from the target concept toward the anchor region, ensuring the model's output under the erased prompt matches the safe distribution. The approach updates both the diffusion model parameters and the flow partition function using gradients from the TB loss, with selective sampling of timesteps for efficiency.
808b6f529e9463f1606b0b1c16d68ab1103201aa.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on Stable Diffusion v1.4 as the backbone model, with evaluation across three primary concept erasure tasks: (1) NSFW content (nudity), (2) artistic style removal (e.g., 'Van Gogh', 'Caravaggio'), and (3) fine-grained element removal (e.g., logos, object parts). Datasets include I2P, Ring-a-Bell, MMA-Diffusion, and adversarial prompts generated via UDAtk and GPT-4o. Evaluation metrics comprise Attack Success Rate (ASR) for NSFW, mean cosine similarity for style erasure, concept and total scores for fine-grained tasks, CLIPScore for image-text alignment, and FID for image quality. Baselines for comparison include ESD, UCE, MACE, DUO, SAFREE, R.A.C.E, and AdvUnlearn, spanning non-adversarial, inference-time, and adversarial training methods. Training involves 20 iterations with batch sampling, anchor resampling for early epochs, and learning rates tuned per task. Plug-and-play integration with methods like SAFREE and AdvUnlearn will also be evaluated.
808b6f529e9463f1606b0b1c16d68ab1103201aa.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first GFlowNet-based framework for concept erasure in diffusion models, leveraging a trajectory-balance objective and a reward-free alignment strategy that generalizes to arbitrary, unseen concepts without explicit reward models. EraseFlow eliminates the need for adversarial training or handcrafted reward functions, reduces computational overhead, and preserves the prior generative quality of the model. The method is provably stable, robust to adversarial reintroduction, and can be seamlessly composed with other erasure and filtering techniques for enhanced performance.

80935e1b9c37d644a4aff84682188e5a634a2899.title: Visual Prompting Upgrades Neural Network Sparsification: A Data-Model Perspective
80935e1b9c37d644a4aff84682188e5a634a2899.research_question: How can the integration of data-centric techniques, specifically visual prompting, with model-centric neural network pruning strategies improve the sparsification and efficiency of vision models across diverse datasets and architectures?
80935e1b9c37d644a4aff84682188e5a634a2899.hypothesis: Joint optimization of visual prompts and parameterized weight masks in a data-model co-design paradigm will yield sparser neural networks with improved performance, efficiency, and transferability compared to traditional model-centric pruning methods.
80935e1b9c37d644a4aff84682188e5a634a2899.proposed_method: A novel framework, termed VPNs (Visual Prompting Upgrades Networks Sparsification), will be developed to jointly optimize learnable visual prompts and parameterized weight masks during the pruning process of vision models. The approach involves two main stages: (1) mask finding from a data-model perspective, where a tailored visual prompt is added to input samples and optimized together with the pruning mask while keeping model weights fixed; and (2) subnetwork tuning, where the identified sparse subnetwork and its associated visual prompt are further fine-tuned. The visual prompt is designed as a learnable perturbation applied to the input image, typically implemented as a pad prompt with tunable peripheral segments. The optimization is formulated as a constrained empirical risk minimization problem, with the mask and prompt jointly updated to maximize downstream task performance under a sparsity constraint. After mask identification, a retraining phase further co-optimizes the subnetwork weights and visual prompt while keeping the mask fixed.
80935e1b9c37d644a4aff84682188e5a634a2899.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using three pre-trained network architectures (ResNet-18, ResNet-50, VGG-16) on ImageNet-1K, with evaluations performed on eight downstream datasets: Tiny-ImageNet, Stanford Cars, Oxford Pets, Food101, DTD, Flowers102, CIFAR10, and CIFAR100. The proposed VPNs method will be compared against eight state-of-the-art pruning baselines, including Random Pruning, OMP, LTH, SNIP, GraSP, SynFlow, HYDRA, and BiP. Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy, computational efficiency (training time, epochs, gradient steps), and memory/compute footprint (FLOPs, memory reduction). Additional analyses will assess transferability of discovered subnetworks to new tasks, integration with structured pruning methods (e.g., Slim, DepGraph), and ablation studies on visual prompt design parameters (input size, pad size, prompt type) and their effect on performance.
80935e1b9c37d644a4aff84682188e5a634a2899.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first systematic data-model co-design paradigm for neural network sparsification in vision models, leveraging joint optimization of visual prompts and pruning masks. This approach demonstrates superior performance and efficiency over existing model-centric pruning algorithms, enhances the transferability of sparse subnetworks across tasks, and can be seamlessly integrated with structured pruning techniques for practical speedup and memory reduction. The method also provides new insights into the interplay between data-centric and model-centric approaches for model compression.

80b2c855201d4e218ed577ad6c28e6c2bbaefe9d.title: On the Asymptotic Learning Curves of Kernel Ridge Regression under Power-law Decay
80b2c855201d4e218ed577ad6c28e6c2bbaefe9d.research_question: How do the asymptotic learning curves of kernel ridge regression behave under general, realistic assumptions, and what is the interplay between regularization, kernel eigenvalue decay, regression function smoothness, and noise level in determining generalization performance?
