80b2c855201d4e218ed577ad6c28e6c2bbaefe9d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that under mild and realistic assumptions, the learning curves of kernel ridge regression can be rigorously characterized, revealing that the generalization error exhibits a U-shaped curve in the presence of noise and a monotonically decreasing curve in the noiseless case. Furthermore, the 'benign overfitting phenomenon' is expected to occur only when the noise level is sufficiently small.
80b2c855201d4e218ed577ad6c28e6c2bbaefe9d.proposed_method: A rigorous mathematical framework will be developed to analyze the asymptotic learning curves of kernel ridge regression (KRR) without relying on the Gaussian design assumption. The approach will involve bias-variance decomposition of the excess risk, with precise upper and lower bounds derived for both terms. The analysis will utilize spectral properties of the kernel integral operator, specifically focusing on the polynomial decay rate of eigenvalues (capacity condition) and the smoothness of the regression function (source condition). The embedding index of the reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) will be leveraged to sharpen the analysis, and both well-specified and mis-specified cases will be considered. The methodology will also address the effect of the regularization parameter, providing a full characterization of the learning curve in both noisy and noiseless regimes.
80b2c855201d4e218ed577ad6c28e6c2bbaefe9d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real datasets to empirically validate the theoretical findings. For synthetic data, kernels such as the Sobolev kernel with known eigenvalue decay will be used, and regression functions of varying smoothness will be considered. The noise level will be controlled to study both noisy and noiseless cases. Kernel ridge regression will be performed with varying regularization parameters, and the excess risk, bias, and variance will be computed numerically. Evaluation metrics will include the convergence rates of these quantities as a function of sample size and regularization. Baselines will include classical theoretical rates and prior heuristic results under the Gaussian design assumption. Experimental results will be compared to the predicted asymptotic rates to confirm the validity of the theoretical analysis.
80b2c855201d4e218ed577ad6c28e6c2bbaefe9d.novelty_claims: The proposed research removes the restrictive Gaussian design assumption used in previous non-rigorous works and provides the first mathematically rigorous proof of the exact asymptotic rates of kernel ridge regression with matching upper and lower bounds for a broad class of kernels. The analysis fully characterizes the learning curve, including the interplay between regularization, kernel eigenvalue decay, regression function smoothness, and noise. The methodology is applicable to both well-specified and mis-specified cases and covers both noisy and noiseless regimes. The techniques developed are general and can be extended to other kernel methods, offering new insights into the generalization properties of overparameterized models and the conditions under which benign overfitting occurs.

80c698688bb4488beaceaab5c64f701a946cb7ae.title: All in One: Multi-Task Prompting for Graph Neural Networks
80c698688bb4488beaceaab5c64f701a946cb7ae.research_question: How can a unified and flexible prompting framework be developed to bridge the gap between pre-trained graph neural network models and diverse downstream graph tasks (node-level, edge-level, and graph-level), especially under few-shot learning conditions?
80c698688bb4488beaceaab5c64f701a946cb7ae.hypothesis: A unified multi-task prompting framework for graph neural networks, which reformulates various downstream tasks into a graph-level format and leverages meta-learning to optimize prompt initialization, will improve the generalization, transferability, and efficiency of pre-trained GNNs across multiple graph tasks and domains, particularly in few-shot settings.
80c698688bb4488beaceaab5c64f701a946cb7ae.proposed_method: A novel multi-task prompting framework for graph neural networks is proposed, which unifies the format of graph prompts and language prompts using prompt tokens, token structures, and inserting patterns. Downstream tasks at node and edge levels are reformulated as graph-level tasks by constructing induced subgraphs (e.g., ego networks for nodes, local subgraphs for edges), aligning their labels with the original task. A prompt graph is designed with learnable tokens and flexible inner structures, and various strategies are developed for connecting prompt tokens and integrating them into the input graph. Meta-learning is introduced to efficiently learn prompt initializations across multiple tasks, enabling the framework to adaptively optimize prompts for improved generalization and transferability. The overall learning process involves episodic training over batches of node, edge, and graph tasks, optimizing prompt parameters while keeping the pre-trained GNN backbone frozen.
80c698688bb4488beaceaab5c64f701a946cb7ae.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on five public graph datasets: Cora, CiteSeer, Reddit, Amazon, and Pubmed, covering a range of node, edge, and graph-level tasks. The evaluation focuses on few-shot learning settings, where each class has only 100 labeled samples, resulting in low label ratios. Baseline comparisons include supervised GNNs (GAT, GCN, Graph Transformer), pre-training with fine-tuning (GraphCL, SimGRACE), and existing prompt-based methods (e.g., GPPT). Evaluation metrics include accuracy, F1-score, and AUC. Additional experiments assess transferability across tasks and domains, ablation studies on framework components, efficiency (parameter count, convergence speed), and the flexibility of the prompt in simulating graph transformations. Meta-learning splits tasks into meta-training and meta-testing, and the impact of prompt token number and structure is systematically analyzed.
80c698688bb4488beaceaab5c64f701a946cb7ae.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a unified prompt design for both language and graph domains, enabling seamless transfer of prompt-based learning to graphs. It is the first to comprehensively reformulate node-level and edge-level tasks as graph-level tasks for improved compatibility with graph pre-training strategies. The method incorporates meta-learning to optimize prompt initialization for multi-task settings, enhancing reliability and generalization. The approach supports a wide range of downstream tasks and pre-training strategies, offers significant efficiency and memory advantages, and demonstrates strong transferability and flexibility in manipulating graph inputs. Extensive experiments show consistent improvements over supervised, pre-training, and existing prompt-based baselines, especially in few-shot and transfer scenarios.

80d0116d77beeded0c23cf48946d9d10d4faee14.title: GLaM: Efficient Scaling of Language Models with Mixture-of-Experts
80d0116d77beeded0c23cf48946d9d10d4faee14.research_question: How can language models be scaled efficiently to achieve high performance on a wide range of natural language processing tasks, while reducing computational and energy costs?
80d0116d77beeded0c23cf48946d9d10d4faee14.hypothesis: A sparsely activated mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture can scale language models to trillions of parameters, achieving superior or comparable performance to dense models on zero, one, and few-shot NLP tasks, while significantly reducing training and inference costs.
80d0116d77beeded0c23cf48946d9d10d4faee14.proposed_method: A family of decoder-only language models will be developed using a sparsely activated mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture. In this approach, every other Transformer layer's feed-forward component is replaced with an MoE layer, each containing a large number of independent feed-forward 'experts.' For each input token, a learned gating function dynamically selects the top two most relevant experts, and the outputs are combined via a weighted average. The architecture incorporates per-layer relative positional bias and uses Gated Linear Units in non-MoE feed-forward sub-layers. Model and computation parallelism is achieved using a 2D sharding algorithm, enabling efficient scaling to over a trillion parameters. Training will use a high-quality, filtered dataset of 1.6 trillion tokens, with mixture weights for data sources tuned to optimize downstream performance.
80d0116d77beeded0c23cf48946d9d10d4faee14.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of 29 public NLP benchmarks, including 21 natural language understanding (NLU) and 8 natural language generation (NLG) tasks, covering categories such as language completion, open-domain QA, reading comprehension, and natural language inference. The evaluation will follow zero-shot, one-shot, and few-shot protocols, using the same benchmarks as prior large-scale models like GPT-3 for direct comparison. Baselines will include dense Transformer models with comparable activated parameters per token, as well as state-of-the-art models such as GPT-3, Gopher, and Switch-C. Metrics will include accuracy, exact match, and F1 score, with energy consumption and FLOPs per token measured for both training and inference. Training will utilize up to 1,024 TPU-v4 chips, and model performance will be analyzed in relation to data quality, model size, and computational efficiency.
80d0116d77beeded0c23cf48946d9d10d4faee14.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a scalable, sparsely activated MoE architecture for decoder-only language models, enabling the training of models with over a trillion parameters while activating only a small subset per token. This results in substantial reductions in training energy (to one third) and inference FLOPs (to half) compared to dense models like GPT-3, while achieving superior or comparable performance across a wide range of zero, one, and few-shot NLP tasks. The method also demonstrates improved data efficiency and reduced bias on social benchmarks, and provides evidence that MoE-based scaling is a promising direction for future large language models.

80d05f1dfe813e47653d44135c58ffa1bf1a10d1.title: Bias-inducing geometries: An exactly solvable data model with fairness implications.
80d05f1dfe813e47653d44135c58ffa1bf1a10d1.research_question: How does the geometry and structure of high-dimensional data contribute to the emergence and perpetuation of bias in machine learning models, and what theoretically grounded mitigation strategies can be developed to address such bias?
80d05f1dfe813e47653d44135c58ffa1bf1a10d1.hypothesis: Bias in machine learning models can arise from specific geometric properties and imbalances in high-dimensional data, and theoretically informed mitigation strategies—such as sample reweighing and coupled neural networks—can improve fairness without significantly compromising accuracy.
80d05f1dfe813e47653d44135c58ffa1bf1a10d1.proposed_method: A novel, exactly solvable generative model called the Teacher-Mixture (T-M) model will be developed to simulate high-dimensional data with controllable bias-inducing factors, such as representation imbalance, group-specific variances, label correlations, and rule misalignment. The model generates data from mixtures of multivariate Gaussians, with group-dependent centroids, variances, and label assignment rules, allowing parametric control over the sources of bias. Analytical tools from statistical physics will be used to derive deterministic predictions for model performance and fairness metrics in the high-dimensional regime. Two mitigation strategies will be investigated: (1) a sample reweighing approach that adjusts the importance of data points based on group membership and label, and (2) a coupled neural networks strategy, where multiple networks are trained in parallel with an elastic penalty encouraging information sharing, allowing for group specialization and positive transfer.
80d05f1dfe813e47653d44135c58ffa1bf1a10d1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using both synthetic data generated by the T-M model and real-world datasets such as CelebA. The synthetic experiments will systematically vary parameters controlling group representation, variance, label correlation, and rule alignment to study their effects on disparate impact and other fairness metrics. Baseline comparisons will include standard empirical risk minimization and single-group training. Evaluation metrics will include disparate impact, mutual information for various fairness criteria (statistical parity, equal opportunity, equal accuracy, equal odds, predicted parity), and group-specific accuracies. The effectiveness of mitigation strategies will be assessed by analyzing accuracy-fairness trade-offs and the compatibility of different fairness metrics. Real-world validation will involve applying the proposed methods to attribute-based group splits in CelebA, measuring the same suite of metrics.
80d05f1dfe813e47653d44135c58ffa1bf1a10d1.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces an exactly solvable, high-dimensional generative model (T-M) that enables precise, analytical investigation of bias mechanisms in machine learning, capturing a wide range of real-world data imbalances and geometric properties. The approach provides a theoretical framework for understanding the interplay between data geometry and fairness, and enables efficient, exact evaluation of fairness and accuracy metrics. The coupled neural networks mitigation strategy is proposed as a novel, theoretically motivated method that can simultaneously improve fairness across multiple criteria and maintain high accuracy, outperforming traditional sample reweighing approaches. The work aims to bridge the gap between empirical bias mitigation and theoretical understanding, offering new insights and tools for designing fair machine learning systems.

80d524334a4f2b70594efcd0d491db6bd0e17ee5.title: InstantSwap: Fast Customized Concept Swapping across Sharp Shape Differences
80d524334a4f2b70594efcd0d491db6bd0e17ee5.research_question: How can customized concept swapping in images be achieved efficiently and consistently, particularly when there are sharp shape differences between source and target concepts?
80d524334a4f2b70594efcd0d491db6bd0e17ee5.hypothesis: A training-free framework that leverages automatic bounding box extraction, background gradient masking, semantic-enhanced concept representations, and step-skipping gradient updating can enable fast and consistent customized concept swapping across large shape disparities.
80d524334a4f2b70594efcd0d491db6bd0e17ee5.proposed_method: A novel training-free framework, INSTANTSWAP, is developed for customized concept swapping in images. The method begins by automatically extracting the bounding box (bbox) of the source concept using enhanced cross-attention and self-attention maps, which localizes the object to be swapped. Background gradient masking (BGM) is then applied to confine gradient updates to the foreground region, preserving background consistency. Semantic-enhanced concept representation (SECR) is introduced by injecting semantic information of both source and target concepts into the cross-attention maps within the bbox, improving foreground consistency. To further enhance efficiency, a step-skipping gradient updating (SSGU) strategy is employed, where gradients are computed only at specific timesteps and reused for intermediate steps, significantly reducing redundant computation during inference.
80d524334a4f2b70594efcd0d491db6bd0e17ee5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using Stable Diffusion v2.1-base as the underlying model, with customized concepts introduced via DreamBooth checkpoints. The newly established ConSwapBench benchmark will be used for evaluation, comprising ConceptBench (target concept images) and SwapBench (source images with objects to be swapped), totaling 1,600 generated images. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art score distillation-based and attention-based image editing methods such as SDS, DDS, CDS, PhotoSwap, and PnPInv+P2P. Evaluation metrics will cover foreground consistency (CLIP Image Score), background consistency (PSNR, LPIPS, MSE, SSIM), overall prompt consistency (CLIP Text Score), and inference time. Ablation studies will assess the contributions of BGM, SECR, automatic bbox extraction, and SSGU, and the method’s versatility will be demonstrated through tasks like multi-concept swapping, face swapping, concept insertion, and removal.
80d524334a4f2b70594efcd0d491db6bd0e17ee5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a training-free, efficient customized concept swapping framework that can handle sharp shape differences between source and target objects. Key innovations include automatic bounding box extraction from attention maps, background gradient masking to preserve background consistency, semantic-enhanced concept representation for precise foreground swapping, and a step-skipping gradient updating strategy to accelerate inference. Additionally, a new benchmark, ConSwapBench, is established for comprehensive evaluation of customized concept swapping methods. The framework is claimed to outperform existing methods in both consistency and efficiency, and the SSGU strategy is shown to be transferable to other score distillation-based editing methods.

80d7c5a8a7f8083530fa9c5e19e6f006ad5fee9e.title: 6D Object Pose Tracking in Internet Videos for Robotic Manipulation
80d7c5a8a7f8083530fa9c5e19e6f006ad5fee9e.research_question: How can temporally consistent 6D object pose trajectories be extracted from Internet instructional videos, in uncontrolled environments and without prior knowledge of the exact object mesh, to enable robotic manipulation tasks?
80d7c5a8a7f8083530fa9c5e19e6f006ad5fee9e.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a combination of open-set object detection, large-scale CAD model retrieval, category-level view alignment, monocular depth and language model-based scale estimation, and robust video tracking can enable accurate and temporally consistent 6D object pose estimation from Internet videos, even when the exact object mesh is unknown, and that these trajectories can be effectively transferred to robotic manipulators.
80d7c5a8a7f8083530fa9c5e19e6f006ad5fee9e.proposed_method: The proposed method begins by detecting and segmenting objects in each video frame using an open-set object detector and image segmenter. For each detected object, a visually and semantically similar CAD model is retrieved from a large-scale database (e.g., Objaverse-LVIS, Google Scanned Objects) using patch-based feature descriptors and foreground feature averaging derived from foundation model features. The 6D pose (rotation and translation) of the object is estimated by aligning the retrieved CAD model to the image using category-level view alignment, maximizing patch-level feature similarity across multiple rendered views. Absolute object scale is determined by combining monocular depth prediction (for relative scale) with metric priors obtained from a large language model (LLM), such as GPT-4, which provides typical object sizes based on text classification using CLIP features. The method then tracks the object across video frames using dense 2D point tracking, refining the 6D pose trajectory via PnP algorithms and correcting for camera motion if necessary. Finally, the temporally smoothed 6D object trajectory is retargeted to a robotic manipulator's configuration space using trajectory optimization, ensuring smooth and feasible robot motion.
80d7c5a8a7f8083530fa9c5e19e6f006ad5fee9e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard 6D pose estimation benchmarks, including YCB-V and HOPE-Video datasets, which feature cluttered scenes and partial occlusions. Retrieved meshes from Objaverse-LVIS and Google Scanned Objects databases will be used instead of ground-truth meshes to simulate in-the-wild conditions. Evaluation metrics will include average recall (AR) for Chamfer distance (CH), projected Chamfer distance (pCH), and complement over union (CoU), following BOP-inspired protocols. Baseline comparisons will be made against state-of-the-art RGB-only 6D pose estimation methods such as MegaPose, GigaPose, and FoundPose. Ablation studies will assess the impact of different CAD retrieval strategies and scale estimation methods. Additional experiments will be performed on a manually annotated dataset of 32 Internet instructional videos (6947 frames) and on egocentric videos from the EPIC-KITCHENS dataset. Robotic manipulation experiments will be conducted both in simulation and on a real 7-axis manipulator (e.g., Franka Emika Panda), evaluating the transfer of extracted object trajectories to robot execution.
80d7c5a8a7f8083530fa9c5e19e6f006ad5fee9e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach enables 6D object pose estimation and trajectory extraction from Internet videos without requiring prior knowledge of the exact object mesh, leveraging large-scale CAD retrieval and LLM-based scale grounding. The method is training-free, generalizes to unseen objects, and is robust to uncontrolled, in-the-wild video conditions. It introduces a novel integration of monocular depth prediction with LLM-derived metric priors for scale estimation, and demonstrates for the first time the transfer of fine-grained object motion from Internet videos to real robotic manipulators. The approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art RGB-only 6D pose estimation methods on standard benchmarks and in-the-wild datasets.

80ee4eb1b750d23261ae6d840ce5d24f69b33c83.title: From data to functa: Your data point is a function and you can treat it like one
80ee4eb1b750d23261ae6d840ce5d24f69b33c83.research_question: How can data points be represented as continuous functions for deep learning, and what are the implications and advantages of performing deep learning directly on such functional representations across various data modalities?
80ee4eb1b750d23261ae6d840ce5d24f69b33c83.hypothesis: Representing data points as implicit neural representations (INRs), termed functa, and treating them as first-class data for deep learning will enable more flexible, scalable, and modality-agnostic machine learning, with benefits for generative modeling, inference, imputation, and classification tasks across diverse data types.
80ee4eb1b750d23261ae6d840ce5d24f69b33c83.proposed_method: The proposed approach converts conventional array-based datasets into functional data points by fitting an implicit neural representation (INR), specifically a SIREN-based MLP, to each data point. Each functa is represented as a low-dimensional modulation vector applied to a shared base network, with modulations learned via a meta-learning procedure (MAML/CAVIA variant) to enable rapid fitting of new data points. The method decouples the creation of functa from downstream deep learning tasks, allowing the same functa representations to be used for generative modeling, inference, and classification. Generative models such as normalizing flows and diffusion models are trained directly on the modulation vectors, and inference tasks are formulated as MAP estimation in the modulation space. Classification is performed by training MLPs directly on the modulation representations.
80ee4eb1b750d23261ae6d840ce5d24f69b33c83.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on multiple data modalities: images (CelebA-HQ 64x64), 3D voxels (ShapeNet), neural radiance fields (SRN Cars), and manifold data (ERA5 temperature grids). For each modality, functa are created by fitting INRs and extracting modulation vectors, with meta-learning used to optimize the shared base network. Generative modeling is evaluated using normalizing flows (NSF) and diffusion models (DDPM), with FID scores and qualitative sample quality as metrics. Baselines include array-based methods (e.g., 3D CNNs, GANs, VAEs, GASP, π-GAN) and prior functional generative models. Classification is benchmarked by comparing MLPs on functa to 3D CNNs on voxel arrays, using test accuracy and parameter count. Imputation and novel view synthesis tasks are evaluated by optimizing modulations under partial observations and assessing reconstruction quality.
80ee4eb1b750d23261ae6d840ce5d24f69b33c83.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified framework for representing data points as continuous functions (functa) parameterized by neural networks, enabling deep learning directly on these functional representations. Key innovations include the decoupling of functa creation from downstream tasks, the use of meta-learned modulations for efficient and scalable dataset creation, and the demonstration of modality-agnostic deep learning across images, 3D shapes, NeRF scenes, and manifold data. The approach allows for efficient generative modeling, imputation, and classification without modality-specific architectures, and scales more gracefully with resolution than traditional array-based methods. The method also enables generative modeling of data modalities, such as NeRF scenes, that are challenging to represent as arrays.

8102cad29ec8e808c7395ac6ee668da495f07206.title: Impossibility theorems for feature attribution
8102cad29ec8e808c7395ac6ee668da495f07206.research_question: Can feature attribution methods reliably infer counterfactual model behavior for tasks such as algorithmic recourse and spurious feature identification, particularly in moderately rich model classes commonly satisfied by neural networks?
8102cad29ec8e808c7395ac6ee668da495f07206.hypothesis: Any feature attribution method that satisfies completeness and linearity cannot, in general, outperform random guessing when used to infer counterfactual model behavior in sufficiently rich model classes.
8102cad29ec8e808c7395ac6ee668da495f07206.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the reliability of feature attribution methods in inferring counterfactual model behavior. The approach formalizes the task as a hypothesis testing problem, where the user seeks to distinguish between different local model behaviors using only the output of a feature attribution method. The analysis will focus on methods satisfying the completeness and linearity axioms, such as SHAP and Integrated Gradients, and will leverage assumptions about the richness of the model class and the properties of the baseline distribution. Theoretical impossibility results will be established by constructing counterexamples, demonstrating that these methods cannot provide information beyond random guessing for the specified tasks.
8102cad29ec8e808c7395ac6ee668da495f07206.experiment_details: Empirical validation will be conducted using a suite of eight standard datasets, including both tabular and image classification tasks. The experiments will evaluate the ability of complete and linear feature attribution methods to infer counterfactual model behavior, comparing their performance to random guessing baselines. Evaluation metrics will include specificity and sensitivity of hypothesis tests based on feature attributions. The experimental setup will also examine the impact of model class richness and baseline selection, and will include both theoretical analysis over distributions of polynomial models and empirical results on real-world neural network models.
8102cad29ec8e808c7395ac6ee668da495f07206.novelty_claims: The proposal establishes general impossibility theorems showing that, under mild and commonly satisfied assumptions, complete and linear feature attribution methods cannot outperform random guessing for inferring counterfactual model behavior. This result challenges prevailing assumptions about the reliability of widely used methods such as SHAP and Integrated Gradients, and demonstrates that even in practical settings, these methods can fail to provide meaningful information for key interpretability tasks. The work motivates the need for concretely defining end-tasks and suggests that brute-force model querying may be more reliable than complex attribution methods in many cases.

81039ad704a0c23059677d0bbf097b9bc90326ba.title: Learning Harmonized Representations for Speculative Sampling
81039ad704a0c23059677d0bbf097b9bc90326ba.research_question: How can the efficiency of speculative sampling for large language model (LLM) decoding be improved by addressing discrepancies between training and decoding stages, particularly in terms of context and objective alignment?
81039ad704a0c23059677d0bbf097b9bc90326ba.hypothesis: Harmonizing the representations and objectives between training and decoding stages in speculative sampling will significantly improve the acceptance rate and speedup ratio of LLM decoding without introducing inference overhead.
81039ad704a0c23059677d0bbf097b9bc90326ba.proposed_method: A novel speculative sampling framework, HArmonized Speculative Sampling (HASS), will be developed to address both context and objective misalignments between training and decoding. HASS will employ harmonized objective distillation, leveraging a Top-K ranking distillation loss that focuses the draft model's training on the most probable tokens as determined by the target LLM, thereby aligning the training objective with practical decoding requirements. Additionally, HASS will implement harmonized context alignment by structuring the training process into multiple steps, each adapting the draft model to use contextual features that mirror those available during decoding, thus mitigating exposure bias and feature inconsistency. The method will integrate these strategies with efficient attention mask modifications to ensure training remains cost-effective while maintaining the same inference cost as existing approaches.
81039ad704a0c23059677d0bbf097b9bc90326ba.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four LLaMA models (LLaMA2-Chat 7B/13B and LLaMA3-Instruct 8B/70B) across three tasks: multi-turn conversation (MT-bench), code generation (HumanEval), and mathematical reasoning (GSM8K). The evaluation will use two primary metrics: speedup ratio (relative to vanilla auto-regressive decoding) and acceptance length (number of tokens accepted per draft-verification cycle). Baseline comparisons will include PLD, Lookahead, Vanilla Speculative Sampling, Medusa, EAGLE, and EAGLE-2. All inference will be performed on NVIDIA H800 GPUs, and the same training dataset (ShareGPT2 with 68,000 dialogues) and optimizer settings as EAGLE-2 will be used. Ablation studies will be conducted to assess the impact of harmonized objective distillation, context alignment steps, and different loss functions. Additional robustness and scalability tests will be performed by varying training data proportions and evaluating on translation tasks.
81039ad704a0c23059677d0bbf097b9bc90326ba.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces harmonized objective distillation and harmonized context alignment to speculative sampling, directly addressing both objective and contextual discrepancies between training and decoding. This dual harmonization approach is claimed to improve acceptance rates and speedup ratios beyond existing methods without increasing inference overhead. The method is also designed to be cost-efficient in training and robust across tasks and data scales, representing a significant advancement over prior speculative sampling frameworks.

810deae66716f6b02ed17b762723d4cf1566919a.title: Universal Hopfield Networks: A General Framework for Single-Shot Associative Memory Models
810deae66716f6b02ed17b762723d4cf1566919a.research_question: How can a unified and general framework for single-shot associative memory models be constructed to encompass existing models, and what are the effects of varying similarity and separation functions on memory capacity and retrieval robustness in associative memory networks?
810deae66716f6b02ed17b762723d4cf1566919a.hypothesis: A general framework for associative memory models based on a sequence of similarity, separation, and projection operations will enable the derivation of both classical and modern memory models as special cases, and the use of alternative similarity and separation functions (such as Manhattan or Euclidean distance and high-order polynomial or max separation) will yield higher capacity and more robust retrieval than traditional dot-product and softmax-based models.
810deae66716f6b02ed17b762723d4cf1566919a.proposed_method: A universal Hopfield network (UHN) framework will be developed, factorizing associative memory retrieval into three stages: similarity computation between a query and stored memories, a separation function to amplify differences among similarity scores, and a projection step to reconstruct the output from stored patterns. The framework will be mathematically formalized to encompass both feedforward and iterative associative memory models, with an associated energy function and neural dynamics that guarantee convergence. The method will allow for arbitrary similarity and separation functions, enabling the instantiation of existing models (such as Hopfield networks, sparse distributed memories, and modern continuous Hopfield networks) as well as the creation of novel variants. Technical details include the use of different similarity metrics (dot product, Euclidean, Manhattan, etc.), various separation functions (identity, polynomial, softmax, max), and both auto- and hetero-associative memory configurations via flexible projection matrices.
810deae66716f6b02ed17b762723d4cf1566919a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted to evaluate the retrieval capacity and robustness of associative memory networks under different similarity and separation functions. The evaluation will use standard image datasets such as MNIST, CIFAR10, and TinyImageNet, with images normalized and flattened for input. Retrieval tasks will involve presenting corrupted queries (with Gaussian noise or masked pixels) and measuring the fraction of correct retrievals, defined by a threshold on the sum of squared pixel differences. The experiments will compare various similarity functions (dot product, Euclidean, Manhattan, KL divergence, etc.) and separation functions (softmax, high-order polynomial, max, etc.), using a softmax separation with tunable parameters as a baseline. Performance will be averaged over multiple runs with different sets of stored memories, and error bars will be reported as standard deviations. Additional experiments will assess robustness to noise and masking, and the framework will be tested on both auto- and hetero-associative memory tasks.
810deae66716f6b02ed17b762723d4cf1566919a.novelty_claims: The proposed framework unifies a wide range of associative memory models under a single mathematical formalism, clarifying their core computations and relationships. It enables straightforward generalization to new models by varying similarity and separation functions, leading to the discovery that Manhattan and Euclidean distance metrics can outperform traditional dot-product similarity in terms of capacity and robustness. The framework provides a principled approach to both feedforward and iterative memory models, introduces a general energy function and associated neural dynamics, and elucidates the connection between associative memory and transformer self-attention mechanisms. The approach also highlights the potential for improved transformer architectures using alternative similarity functions.

810e721d49db777762af1b2ac24666c849562195.title: When Worse is Better: Navigating the compression-generation tradeoff in visual tokenization
810e721d49db777762af1b2ac24666c849562195.research_question: How can the trade-off between image compression and generative modeling capacity in two-stage visual tokenization pipelines be optimized to improve image generation quality and efficiency?
810e721d49db777762af1b2ac24666c849562195.hypothesis: Introducing inductive biases from the generative modeling stage into the tokenization process will produce latent representations that are easier for generative models to model, thereby improving generation performance and compute efficiency without significantly degrading reconstruction quality.
810e721d49db777762af1b2ac24666c849562195.proposed_method: A two-stage visual tokenization and generation pipeline will be developed. In stage 1, an auto-encoder (such as a VQGAN) compresses images into discrete latent tokens. The key innovation is the introduction of Causally Regularized Tokenization (CRT), which regularizes the latent space using a small causal transformer trained with next-token prediction loss on the pre-quantized latents. This regularization embeds inductive biases from the stage 2 generative model directly into the tokenization process, making the resulting tokens more amenable to auto-regressive modeling. The CRT method will be further optimized to minimize the number of tokens per image and model parameters while maintaining or improving generative performance.
810e721d49db777762af1b2ac24666c849562195.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image generation benchmarks, such as ImageNet. The proposed CRT-based pipeline will be compared to baseline two-stage models using conventional vector-quantized tokenization. Evaluation metrics will include FID (Fréchet Inception Distance) for generation quality, token count per image, and total model parameter count. Ablation studies will investigate the impact of compression rate, model size, and CRT regularization strength. Compute efficiency will be measured by comparing performance at varying model and tokenization scales.
810e721d49db777762af1b2ac24666c849562195.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces Causally Regularized Tokenization (CRT), a method that leverages knowledge of the stage 2 generative modeling process to embed inductive biases into the stage 1 latent space. This approach enables smaller generative models to achieve comparable or superior image generation quality with fewer tokens and parameters, improving compute efficiency by 2-3× over baselines. The method demonstrates that aggressive compression, when properly regularized, can benefit generation performance even at the cost of reconstruction fidelity, and achieves state-of-the-art results with significantly reduced resource requirements.

811c5f8f200f291687f94a03a389f6afb6a7cac9.title: Stereographic Spherical Sliced Wasserstein Distances
811c5f8f200f291687f94a03a389f6afb6a7cac9.research_question: How can computationally efficient and theoretically sound distances for comparing probability distributions on spherical domains be developed, particularly leveraging optimal transport theory, to enable practical applications in fields such as computer vision, medical imaging, and deep learning?
811c5f8f200f291687f94a03a389f6afb6a7cac9.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a novel distance metric for spherical probability measures, constructed via stereographic projection combined with a generalized Radon transform and appropriate injective mappings, can provide both computational efficiency and theoretical robustness, while closely approximating true spherical distances and supporting rotational invariance.
811c5f8f200f291687f94a03a389f6afb6a7cac9.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed for comparing spherical probability measures by first applying a stereographic projection to map points from the sphere (excluding the North Pole) onto a Euclidean hyperplane. This is followed by the application of a generalized Radon transform, which slices the projected distribution into one-dimensional marginals along chosen directions. To address the distortion of distances caused by the stereographic projection, an injective function—either analytically defined or parameterized by a neural network—will be introduced to approximate the spherical arclength in the embedding space. The Stereographic Spherical Sliced Wasserstein (S3W) distance will be defined as the average Wasserstein distance between corresponding one-dimensional slices of the two distributions. Additionally, a rotationally invariant extension (RI-S3W) will be formulated by averaging the S3W distance over random rotations of the distributions, ensuring invariance to orientation on the sphere.
811c5f8f200f291687f94a03a389f6afb6a7cac9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of tasks involving spherical probability distributions, including gradient flows on the sphere, representation learning with Sliced-Wasserstein Auto-Encoders (SWAEs), spherical density estimation using normalizing flows, variational inference on the sphere, and self-supervised learning. Empirical evaluations will use both synthetic and real-world datasets relevant to these tasks. The proposed S3W and RI-S3W distances will be compared against recent baselines such as existing spherical sliced Wasserstein distances and other optimal transport-based metrics. Evaluation metrics will include computational speed, accuracy of the distance in capturing true spherical geometry, and downstream task performance. Key experimental setup details include the use of Monte Carlo integration for approximating integrals over the sphere, GPU-accelerated vectorized implementations, and careful handling of numerical stability around the North Pole via an epsilon-cap.
811c5f8f200f291687f94a03a389f6afb6a7cac9.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a computationally efficient and highly parallelizable distance for spherical probability measures that leverages stereographic projection and a generalized Radon transform. It addresses the challenge of distance distortion through novel injective mappings, including neural network-based nearly-isometric embeddings. The method provides a theoretically grounded metric with a provable extension to rotational invariance. The approach is claimed to outperform existing baselines in both speed and accuracy across a range of applications, and offers a flexible framework for further extensions to other manifolds.

811df72e210e20de99719539505da54762a11c6d.title: Soft Actor-Critic: Off-Policy Maximum Entropy Deep Reinforcement Learning with a Stochastic Actor
811df72e210e20de99719539505da54762a11c6d.research_question: How can a model-free deep reinforcement learning algorithm be designed to achieve both high sample efficiency and stable convergence in continuous control tasks, overcoming the limitations of high sample complexity and brittleness to hyperparameters observed in existing methods?
811df72e210e20de99719539505da54762a11c6d.hypothesis: A model-free, off-policy actor-critic reinforcement learning algorithm that maximizes both expected reward and policy entropy will achieve improved sample efficiency, stability, and robustness compared to existing on-policy and off-policy deep RL methods in continuous control domains.
811df72e210e20de99719539505da54762a11c6d.proposed_method: A novel off-policy actor-critic algorithm will be developed within the maximum entropy reinforcement learning framework. The method will alternate between soft policy evaluation and soft policy improvement steps, where the policy is trained to maximize a combination of expected reward and entropy. The algorithm will use separate neural networks to parameterize the policy (actor), Q-functions (critics), and a value function, with the policy represented as a tractable stochastic distribution (e.g., Gaussian). Two Q-functions will be trained independently to mitigate positive bias, and a target value network will be updated using an exponential moving average for stability. The policy will be optimized using the reparameterization trick, allowing for efficient and low-variance gradient estimation, and all networks will be updated using off-policy data sampled from a replay buffer.
811df72e210e20de99719539505da54762a11c6d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of challenging continuous control benchmarks from the OpenAI Gym (e.g., Hopper-v1, Walker2d-v1, HalfCheetah-v1, Ant-v1, Humanoid-v1) and rllab's Humanoid task. The proposed method will be compared against strong baselines including DDPG (Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient), PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization), SQL (Soft Q-Learning), and TD3 (Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient). Evaluation metrics will include average return over evaluation rollouts, sample efficiency (learning speed), and stability across multiple random seeds. Hyperparameter sensitivity studies (e.g., reward scaling, target network update smoothing) and ablation studies (e.g., stochastic vs. deterministic policy) will be performed to assess robustness and the contribution of each algorithmic component.
811df72e210e20de99719539505da54762a11c6d.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first practical off-policy actor-critic algorithm in the maximum entropy reinforcement learning framework that provably converges to the optimal policy within a given policy class. The approach combines entropy maximization with off-policy actor-critic training and a stochastic policy, resulting in improved sample efficiency, stability, and robustness compared to both on-policy and off-policy prior methods. The use of two Q-functions to reduce positive bias and the demonstration of consistent performance across a wide range of tasks and random seeds further distinguish this approach from existing algorithms.

812356c723c082f88fb722531beaf45e344ffa1e.title: PyramidKV: Dynamic KV Cache Compression based on Pyramidal Information Funneling
812356c723c082f88fb722531beaf45e344ffa1e.research_question: How can the memory efficiency of key-value (KV) cache management in large language models (LLMs) be improved for long-context processing without compromising model performance, and what are the optimal strategies for allocating and selecting KV cache entries across different transformer layers?
812356c723c082f88fb722531beaf45e344ffa1e.hypothesis: Dynamically allocating KV cache sizes across transformer layers based on observed attention patterns—specifically, allocating more cache to lower layers and less to higher layers—will significantly reduce memory usage while maintaining or improving LLM performance on long-context tasks compared to uniform or static cache allocation methods.
812356c723c082f88fb722531beaf45e344ffa1e.proposed_method: A novel KV cache compression framework, PyramidKV, will be developed to exploit the pyramidal information funneling observed in LLM attention patterns. The method involves two main steps: (1) dynamically allocating different KV cache sizes to each transformer layer, with larger caches in lower layers (where attention is more dispersed) and smaller caches in higher layers (where attention is more focused), using an arithmetic sequence to determine intermediate layer cache sizes; and (2) selecting which KV entries to retain within each layer by always keeping the KV states for the last α instruction tokens and, for the remaining budget, selecting tokens with the highest cumulative attention scores from these instruction tokens, aggregated across attention heads. The approach requires setting hyperparameters for the number of instruction tokens (α) and the pyramid shape (β), and is designed to be compatible with standard LLM inference pipelines.
812356c723c082f88fb722531beaf45e344ffa1e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using three state-of-the-art open-source LLMs: LLaMa-3-8B-Instruct, LLaMa-3-70B-Instruct, and Mistral-7B-Instruct. Evaluation will be performed on the LongBench benchmark, which comprises 17 datasets spanning single- and multi-document QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic, and code generation tasks, with input lengths ranging from 1,235 to 18,409 tokens. Baselines for comparison will include StreamingLLM, SnapKV, HeavyHitterOracle (H2O), and FullKV, with all methods adjusted to use the same average total KV cache size for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics will follow LongBench standards (F1 for QA, Rouge-L for summarization, accuracy for synthetic, and EditSim for code generation). Additional experiments will include the Needle-in-a-Haystack test for long-context retrieval, and memory usage will be measured under various cache size regimes.
812356c723c082f88fb722531beaf45e344ffa1e.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to introduce a pyramidal, layer-wise dynamic allocation of KV cache sizes in LLMs, directly informed by empirical analysis of attention distribution across layers. Unlike previous approaches that use fixed cache sizes per layer, this method aligns cache allocation with the actual informational needs of each layer, leading to substantial memory savings (up to 88% reduction) while preserving or even enhancing model performance, especially in memory-constrained scenarios. The approach demonstrates superior performance on long-context understanding and in-context learning tasks, and generalizes across multiple LLM architectures and task types.

8127cc6718e26d9ac0e9ac1aa9c56d59afa65446.title: Permutation Equivariant Neural Controlled Differential Equations for Dynamic Graph Representation Learning
8127cc6718e26d9ac0e9ac1aa9c56d59afa65446.research_question: How can dynamic graph representation learning models be designed to efficiently and accurately capture complex temporal and structural dynamics, while ensuring permutation equivariance and robustness to irregular sampling?
8127cc6718e26d9ac0e9ac1aa9c56d59afa65446.hypothesis: Imposing permutation equivariance on neural controlled differential equation models for dynamic graphs will improve parameter efficiency, generalization, and robustness, without sacrificing representational power or expressivity.
8127cc6718e26d9ac0e9ac1aa9c56d59afa65446.proposed_method: A novel framework, Permutation Equivariant Neural Graph Controlled Differential Equations (PENG-CDEs), is developed to model dynamic graphs by projecting the fusion operations in Graph Neural CDEs onto the space of permutation equivariant linear functions. The method leverages a basis of 15 equivariant linear maps to combine adjacency matrices and their time derivatives, ensuring that the resulting model is both permutation equivariant in the spatial domain and time-warp equivariant in the temporal domain. The model incorporates dynamic node features via continuous interpolation and fuses these with the latent representations through node-wise Hadamard multiplication. The architecture maintains the expressivity of message-passing GNNs while significantly reducing parameter count and computational complexity. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that, in the linear case, the model provides the optimal projection of standard GN-CDEs onto the equivariant function space.
8127cc6718e26d9ac0e9ac1aa9c56d59afa65446.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both synthetic and real-world dynamic graph tasks. Synthetic experiments include heat diffusion and gene regulation dynamics on graphs sampled from various distributions (community, grid, power-law, small-world), with performance evaluated on interpolation and extrapolation tasks using mean squared error (MSE). Real-world benchmarks include node regression tasks from PyTorch Geometric Temporal datasets (england-covid, twitter-tennis) and node affinity prediction tasks from the Temporal Graph Benchmark (tgbn-trade, tgbn-genre). Baselines include recurrent, attentional, interactive, and differential equation-based models such as DCRNN, STIDGCN, ASTGCN, GraphNeuralODE, and GN-CDE variants. Evaluation metrics include MSE for regression and NDCG@10 for affinity prediction, with statistical significance assessed over multiple random seeds. Additional studies investigate robustness to oversampling and irregular sampling, as well as ablation analyses of the fusion operation.
8127cc6718e26d9ac0e9ac1aa9c56d59afa65446.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first permutation equivariant neural controlled differential equation framework for dynamic graphs, achieving parameter efficiency and improved generalization without loss of expressivity. The approach provides a principled projection of GN-CDEs onto the space of equivariant functions, theoretically guaranteeing optimality in the linear case. Empirical results demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on challenging dynamic graph benchmarks, including surpassing all previous learned models on the TGB-genre node affinity prediction task. The model is also shown to be robust to oversampling and irregular time intervals, and the use of all 15 basis terms in the equivariant fusion operation enhances both interpolation and extrapolation capabilities.

812ae1db94308ae4c246e9983e7addfad8f35767.title: Improving Equivariant Model Training via Constraint Relaxation
812ae1db94308ae4c246e9983e7addfad8f35767.research_question: How can the optimization and generalization performance of equivariant neural networks be improved, particularly in settings where the underlying data symmetries are known and exact equivariance is required?
812ae1db94308ae4c246e9983e7addfad8f35767.hypothesis: Relaxing the hard equivariance constraints during training, and progressively constraining the model back to exact equivariance at inference, will facilitate optimization and lead to equivariant models with improved generalization and task performance compared to standard training procedures.
812ae1db94308ae4c246e9983e7addfad8f35767.proposed_method: A novel training framework is developed that relaxes the equivariance constraints of intermediate layers in equivariant neural networks by introducing an additional non-equivariant term parameterized by a scalar θ. This relaxation allows the model to optimize over a larger hypothesis space containing approximate equivariant networks. During training, a Lie derivative-based regularization term is used to measure and control the deviation from equivariance, while an additional regularization term penalizes the norm of the non-equivariant activation to limit projection error. The value of θ is scheduled to decrease cyclically during the final phase of training, ensuring a smooth transition back to the equivariant subspace. At inference, the model is projected back to the space of strictly equivariant solutions by setting θ to zero, yielding a model that respects the desired symmetries.
812ae1db94308ae4c246e9983e7addfad8f35767.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a range of tasks and architectures, including point cloud classification with equivariant PointNet and DGCNN on the ModelNet40 dataset, molecular dynamics simulation using Equiformer on the MD17 dataset, and N-body particle simulation with Steerable E(3) GNN. The proposed method is compared against standard training procedures for these networks, as well as against non-equivariant models and other approximate equivariant baselines such as RPP, LIFT, and RSteer. Evaluation metrics include classification accuracy, mean absolute error (MAE) for energy and force prediction, and root mean squared error (RMSE) for smoke flow prediction tasks. Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of the Lie derivative regularization, projection error regularization, and θ scheduling. The experimental setup includes consistent hyperparameter settings across tasks, sub-sampling of input data, and analysis of model and dataset size scaling effects.
812ae1db94308ae4c246e9983e7addfad8f35767.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a principled method for relaxing and progressively enforcing equivariance constraints during training, addressing optimization challenges unique to equivariant neural networks. The approach leverages Lie derivative-based regularization to quantify and control equivariance error, and employs a projection mechanism to ensure exact equivariance at inference. This methodology is general and can be applied to a variety of equivariant architectures, including both exactly and approximately equivariant models. Empirical results demonstrate consistent improvements in optimization stability and generalization performance over standard training methods, particularly in data-scarce and under-parameterized regimes.

814776737f5f880c15a21c75d06e1ae89e8f7ebd.title: HiPoNet: A Multi-View Simplicial Complex Network for High Dimensional Point-Cloud and Single-Cell Data
814776737f5f880c15a21c75d06e1ae89e8f7ebd.research_question: How can high-dimensional point cloud data, such as those arising in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics experiments, be effectively modeled to preserve and leverage geometric and topological information for downstream tasks such as classification, regression, and representation learning?
814776737f5f880c15a21c75d06e1ae89e8f7ebd.hypothesis: A neural network architecture that models high-dimensional point clouds as multi-view simplicial complexes and employs multiscale wavelet-based feature extraction will better preserve geometric and topological information, leading to improved performance on downstream tasks compared to existing graph- and point cloud-based methods.
814776737f5f880c15a21c75d06e1ae89e8f7ebd.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a multi-view, end-to-end differentiable neural network framework for high-dimensional point cloud data. Multiple learnable feature-weighting vectors are used to generate distinct views of the data, each emphasizing different feature subsets. For each view, a Vietoris-Rips simplicial complex is constructed to capture higher-order relationships among data points, going beyond pairwise interactions. Multiscale simplicial wavelet transforms are then applied to each complex, extracting both local and global features by aggregating information across multiple scales and simplex orders. The resulting multi-scale, multi-view embeddings are concatenated and passed through a multilayer perceptron for final prediction, enabling robust classification, regression, or representation learning.
814776737f5f880c15a21c75d06e1ae89e8f7ebd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several high-dimensional biological datasets, including single-cell data cohorts (e.g., melanoma patient samples, patient-derived organoids) and spatial transcriptomics datasets from multiple cancer cohorts. Tasks will include classification (e.g., predicting treatment response or cancer recurrence) and regression (e.g., predicting topological persistence features). Baseline comparisons will include KNN-based graph neural networks (GCN, SAGE, GAT, GIN, Graph Transformer), point cloud models (PointNet++, DGCNN, PointTransformer), and topology-oriented models (TopoGNN, TopoAE, GCNN, HGCNN). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, mean squared error (MSE), and area under the ROC curve (AUCROC), with results averaged over multiple random seeds. Ablation studies will assess the impact of multi-view learning, simplicial modeling, and hyperparameters such as the Vietoris-Rips threshold and kernel bandwidth.
814776737f5f880c15a21c75d06e1ae89e8f7ebd.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is novel in its use of learnable multi-view feature weighting to disentangle and highlight distinct biological processes within high-dimensional point clouds. By modeling data as higher-order simplicial complexes and extracting features using multiscale wavelet transforms, the method preserves both geometric and topological information, including volume, curvature, and connectivity. This framework enables the analysis of entire cohorts of high-dimensional datasets, scales to large sample sizes, and provides interpretable feature importance. The approach is theoretically grounded, demonstrating the preservation of topological invariants and the ability to approximate geodesic distances on underlying manifolds, and empirically achieves superior or state-of-the-art performance on challenging biological datasets.

81521a80f7aa939281863c15b42e446ff5a0e65a.title: Adan: Adaptive Nesterov Momentum Algorithm for Faster Optimizing Deep Models
81521a80f7aa939281863c15b42e446ff5a0e65a.research_question: How can a single optimizer be designed to consistently accelerate and improve the training of diverse deep neural network architectures across vision, language, and reinforcement learning tasks, while maintaining robustness to large batch sizes and reducing the need for extensive optimizer selection and tuning?
81521a80f7aa939281863c15b42e446ff5a0e65a.hypothesis: An adaptive optimization algorithm that integrates a novel, efficient Nesterov momentum estimation with adaptive gradient moment estimation will achieve faster convergence, improved generalization, and greater robustness across a wide range of deep learning models and training regimes compared to existing state-of-the-art optimizers.
81521a80f7aa939281863c15b42e446ff5a0e65a.proposed_method: A new optimization algorithm, Adan, will be developed by reformulating the vanilla Nesterov acceleration to create a Nesterov momentum estimation (NME) technique that avoids the computational overhead of evaluating gradients at extrapolation points. This NME will be used to estimate both the first- and second-order moments of the gradient in an adaptive manner, enabling convergence acceleration and improved stability. The method will include a flexible estimation of the momentum by decoupling the gradient and its difference, and will dynamically adjust weight decay per coordinate using a proximal update. The algorithm will further incorporate a restart condition to reset momentum based on the trajectory, and will be rigorously analyzed for convergence under both Lipschitz gradient and Hessian conditions. The update rules will be designed to be compatible with distributed training and large-batch scenarios, ensuring practical efficiency and scalability.
81521a80f7aa939281863c15b42e446ff5a0e65a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a broad set of deep learning tasks, including image classification (ImageNet with ResNet, ConvNext, ViT, Swin), object detection and segmentation (COCO with Deformable-DETR and Mask R-CNN), language modeling (Penn Treebank with LSTM, WikiText-103 with Transformer-XL), large language model pretraining (GPT-2 on The Stack, evaluated with HumanEval), and reinforcement learning (MuJoCo environments with PPO). Baselines will include SGD, Adam, AdamW, LAMB, AdaBelief, Nadam, Padam, RAdam, Yogi, and others as appropriate for each task. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy, box/mask average precision (AP), perplexity, pass@k for code generation, ROC-AUC for GNNs, and episodic rewards for RL. Experimental setups will follow official or widely adopted training recipes, with consistent hyperparameter tuning and batch sizes (ranging from small to very large, e.g., 1k to 32k) to test robustness and convergence speed. Both supervised and self-supervised settings will be explored, and ablation studies will be conducted to isolate the contributions of each algorithmic component.
81521a80f7aa939281863c15b42e446ff5a0e65a.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel Nesterov momentum estimation that eliminates the need for gradient computation at extrapolated points, reducing computational and memory overhead. By integrating this NME with adaptive moment estimation, the approach achieves provably faster convergence rates, matching or surpassing the best-known lower bounds for non-convex stochastic optimization under both Lipschitz gradient and Hessian conditions. The method demonstrates consistent improvements over state-of-the-art optimizers across a wide variety of deep learning architectures and tasks, often achieving superior performance with significantly fewer training epochs and greater robustness to large batch sizes. Additionally, the algorithm's dynamic regularization and restart mechanisms provide enhanced generalization and stability, making it broadly applicable and reducing the engineering burden of optimizer selection.

815b3925469475ee627e77a2ca345243af5abd25.title: Oracle-free Reinforcement Learning in Mean-Field Games along a Single Sample Path
815b3925469475ee627e77a2ca345243af5abd25.research_question: Can a generic agent in a mean-field game learn to approximate the stationary mean-field equilibrium using only its own single sample path, without access to a mean-field oracle or knowledge of the environment's transition dynamics and reward functions?
815b3925469475ee627e77a2ca345243af5abd25.hypothesis: A reinforcement learning algorithm that updates the mean-field and control policy concurrently along a single sample path, using two time-scale learning rates and without requiring a mean-field oracle, will converge to an approximate mean-field equilibrium with finite-sample guarantees under suitable assumptions.
815b3925469475ee627e77a2ca345243af5abd25.proposed_method: A novel reinforcement learning framework, termed Sandbox Learning, is proposed for mean-field games where the agent lacks access to a mean-field oracle and does not know the transition dynamics or reward functions. The method employs a two time-scale approach: the mean-field is updated on a slower time-scale using an estimated consistency operator based on empirical transition probabilities, while the control policy is updated on a faster time-scale using an estimated optimality operator derived from Q-learning. The learning rates are episodic and designed to ensure the Markov chain induced by the agent's trajectory is slowly time-varying within each episode, facilitating theoretical analysis and convergence. The mean-field consistency operator is approximated using empirical occupancy measures and smoothed transition estimates, while the optimality operator is approximated via a softmax policy over the learned Q-function. Exploration is enforced through randomization in the policy update, and projection onto an epsilon-net is used to maintain mean-field estimates within a compact set.
815b3925469475ee627e77a2ca345243af5abd25.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a congestion mean-field game defined on a 5x5 grid, with finite state and action spaces and stochastic transitions modeling crowd dynamics. The agent's reward depends on both its state and the mean-field, with congestion aversion. The Sandbox Learning algorithm is evaluated under two scenarios: one where the communicating Markov decision process (MDP) assumption holds, and another where it does not due to the presence of multiple communicating classes. Baseline comparisons are made to prior works that require oracle access or multiple sample paths. Evaluation metrics include the convergence of the estimated mean-field and control policy to the mean-field equilibrium, as well as the accuracy of Q-function and transition probability estimation. Key experimental parameters such as learning rates, episode lengths, and exploration coefficients are varied to study their impact on convergence and sample complexity.
815b3925469475ee627e77a2ca345243af5abd25.novelty_claims: The proposed approach eliminates the need for a mean-field oracle, operating solely on the single sample path of a generic agent, which is a significant relaxation of assumptions compared to prior works. The two time-scale episodic learning rate schedule is specifically designed to handle the challenges of a slowly time-varying Markov chain, enabling finite-sample convergence guarantees under a communicating MDP assumption rather than the stronger ergodicity condition. Theoretical contributions include new finite-sample bounds for both Q-learning and transition probability estimation in this setting, as well as a comprehensive finite-time analysis of the joint mean-field and policy learning process. The method is broadly applicable as a warm-start for agents entering multi-agent non-cooperative environments and demonstrates empirical effectiveness even when standard MDP assumptions are violated.

817632c42e735911e14b89e851ceaf54ba2ad25f.title: OLMoE: Open Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
817632c42e735911e14b89e851ceaf54ba2ad25f.research_question: How can open-source Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models be designed and trained to achieve state-of-the-art performance and efficiency compared to dense models, while maximizing transparency and accessibility for the research community?
817632c42e735911e14b89e851ceaf54ba2ad25f.hypothesis: A fully open Mixture-of-Experts language model, utilizing fine-grained expert granularity, dropless token-based routing, and comprehensive open-sourcing of weights, data, code, and logs, will achieve superior cost-performance trade-offs and competitive or superior accuracy compared to similarly sized dense models and other MoEs with comparable active parameters.
817632c42e735911e14b89e851ceaf54ba2ad25f.proposed_method: The proposed method will develop a decoder-only transformer-based language model where the standard feedforward network (FFN) in each layer is replaced with a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) module. Each MoE module will consist of 64 small experts per layer, with 8 experts activated per input token, selected via a learned router using dropless token-choice routing. The model will be trained from scratch on a large-scale, quality-filtered dataset comprising over 5 trillion tokens, using auxiliary load balancing and router z-losses to ensure stable and efficient expert utilization. The training objective will combine cross-entropy loss with these auxiliary losses, and the model will be adapted for instruction-following tasks through sequential instruction and preference tuning, incorporating additional math and code data for improved downstream performance.
817632c42e735911e14b89e851ceaf54ba2ad25f.experiment_details: Experiments will involve pretraining the model on a mixed dataset (OLMOE-MIX) derived from sources such as DCLM-Baseline, Dolma 1.7, StarCoder, AlgebraicStack, arXiv, peS2o, and Wikipedia, with rigorous filtering for quality and diversity. The model will be benchmarked against both dense and MoE baselines with comparable active and total parameter counts, including Llama2-7B, OLMo-7B, Mistral-7B, Qwen1.5-3B-14B, and others, across standard evaluation tasks such as MMLU, HellaSwag, ARC-Challenge, PIQA, COPA, and WinoGrande. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, pass@10, F1, and other task-specific metrics, with both few-shot and zero-shot setups. The adaptation phase will further evaluate instruction-tuned and preference-tuned variants on benchmarks like GSM8k, BBH, AlpacaEval, XSTest, and IFEval. All training code, intermediate checkpoints, logs, and datasets will be released under open-source licenses to ensure full reproducibility.
817632c42e735911e14b89e851ceaf54ba2ad25f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first fully open Mixture-of-Experts language model with state-of-the-art performance in its cost regime, including open release of model weights, training data, code, and logs. Key innovations include the use of fine-grained expert granularity (64 experts per layer, 8 activated), dropless token-based routing for improved efficiency, and comprehensive analysis of expert specialization and routing behavior. The approach demonstrates that MoEs can achieve 2-3x faster training and superior performance per unit of compute compared to dense models with similar active parameters. The work also provides extensive ablation studies on MoE design choices, contributing valuable insights to the community and setting a new standard for openness and transparency in large language model research.

8199e26d20281b3e4f64d72ff63e00eb8eae2987.title: Wav-KAN: Wavelet Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
8199e26d20281b3e4f64d72ff63e00eb8eae2987.research_question: How can neural network architectures be improved to enhance interpretability, training speed, robustness, computational efficiency, and performance across diverse tasks?
8199e26d20281b3e4f64d72ff63e00eb8eae2987.hypothesis: Incorporating wavelet functions into the Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) framework will enable neural networks to efficiently capture both high-frequency and low-frequency components of input data, resulting in improved interpretability, accuracy, training speed, and robustness compared to traditional multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) and B-spline-based KANs (Spl-KAN).
8199e26d20281b3e4f64d72ff63e00eb8eae2987.proposed_method: A novel neural network architecture, termed Wav-KAN, will be developed by integrating wavelet functions into the Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) structure. In this approach, each 'weight' in the network is replaced by a learnable univariate wavelet function, and nodes perform summation of these functions rather than traditional weighted sums. Both continuous and discrete wavelet transforms will be explored, allowing the network to perform multiresolution analysis and efficiently combine local detailed information with global trends. The architecture will support arbitrary widths and depths, generalizing the KAN framework and enabling flexible adaptation to the data structure. Training will involve backpropagation with gradients computed with respect to the parameters of the wavelet functions, allowing the network to learn both the activation and transformation of inputs.
8199e26d20281b3e4f64d72ff63e00eb8eae2987.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted to compare the performance of Wav-KAN against baseline models including multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) and B-spline-based KANs (Spl-KAN). Evaluation will focus on metrics such as accuracy, training speed, robustness, and interpretability. Datasets spanning various domains will be utilized to demonstrate the generalizability and effectiveness of the proposed approach. The experimental setup will include implementation in popular deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch and TensorFlow, and code will be made available for replication and further research.
8199e26d20281b3e4f64d72ff63e00eb8eae2987.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first integration of wavelet functions into the Kolmogorov-Arnold Network framework for neural networks of arbitrary width and depth. This approach enables efficient multiresolution analysis within neural architectures, enhancing both interpretability and performance. The method addresses key limitations of existing MLPs and Spl-KANs by providing faster training, improved robustness, and a more interpretable structure. The framework is positioned to become a widely adopted tool in the development of glass-box neural networks, with broad applicability across scientific and engineering domains.

819bbdc2dac9e13d9ca3e2508a6e063186ce5e40.title: YaRN: Efficient Context Window Extension of Large Language Models
819bbdc2dac9e13d9ca3e2508a6e063186ce5e40.research_question: How can the context window of large language models using rotary position embeddings be efficiently extended, enabling effective generalization to much longer sequences than seen during pre-training, while minimizing computational and data requirements?
819bbdc2dac9e13d9ca3e2508a6e063186ce5e40.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a targeted interpolation method combining frequency-aware scaling of rotary position embeddings with attention temperature scaling can enable large language models to generalize to significantly longer context windows with minimal fine-tuning, outperforming existing context extension techniques in both efficiency and effectiveness.
819bbdc2dac9e13d9ca3e2508a6e063186ce5e40.proposed_method: The proposed method, YaRN, combines a targeted interpolation of rotary position embeddings ('NTK-by-parts') with a learnable temperature scaling applied to the attention logits. The interpolation selectively scales low-frequency dimensions of the RoPE embeddings to preserve local and global positional information, while high-frequency dimensions are left unscaled to avoid loss of fine-grained positional detail. Two parameters, alpha and beta, define the boundaries for which dimensions are interpolated, with a ramp function controlling the degree of scaling per dimension. The attention temperature is adjusted as a function of the context extension scale, allowing for uniform control of entropy and perplexity across extended contexts. This approach is designed to be computationally efficient, requiring minimal changes to model architecture and being compatible with optimized attention implementations such as FlashAttention2.
819bbdc2dac9e13d9ca3e2508a6e063186ce5e40.experiment_details: Experiments will involve fine-tuning LLaMA and Llama-2 models (7B and 13B parameters) on the PG19 dataset, chunked into 64k-token segments, using global batch sizes of 64 and a learning rate of 2×10^-5. Fine-tuning will be performed for 400 steps for a scale factor s=16, with an additional 200 steps for s=32, representing approximately 0.1% of the original pre-training data. Evaluation will include perplexity measurements on long-sequence datasets such as Proof-pile and GovReport using a sliding window approach, as well as passkey retrieval tasks to assess memory over long contexts. Standard LLM benchmarks (ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, MMLU, TruthfulQA) will be used to compare performance degradation against baselines and other context extension methods (PI, NTK-aware, CodeLlama, Together.ai). Extrapolation experiments will test generalization to up to 128k-token contexts, even when fine-tuning data is limited to 64k tokens.
819bbdc2dac9e13d9ca3e2508a6e063186ce5e40.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a compute- and data-efficient approach for extending the context window of RoPE-based language models, requiring 10x fewer tokens and 2.5x fewer training steps than prior methods. YaRN is the first method to successfully extend Llama-2 models to 128k context with minimal fine-tuning and negligible performance degradation. The targeted, frequency-aware interpolation preserves both local and global positional information, enabling effective transfer learning and extrapolation to unseen context lengths. The method is fully compatible with optimized attention implementations and incurs no additional inference cost, making it practical for large-scale deployment.

81af3a2952838d6b437d6985956d771084f341ab.title: GrokFormer: Graph Fourier Kolmogorov-Arnold Transformers
81af3a2952838d6b437d6985956d771084f341ab.research_question: How can graph transformers be enhanced to effectively capture a broad range of frequency signals, including both low- and high-frequency components, for improved graph representation learning across diverse graph structures and tasks?
81af3a2952838d6b437d6985956d771084f341ab.hypothesis: Introducing a graph transformer model that learns adaptive spectral filters, parameterized by Fourier series over learnable activation functions and capable of both order- and spectrum-adaptivity, will significantly improve the expressiveness and performance of graph representation learning compared to existing GNNs and GTs.
81af3a2952838d6b437d6985956d771084f341ab.proposed_method: A novel graph transformer framework, GrokFormer, will be developed to address the limitations of current self-attention-based graph transformers, which predominantly capture low-frequency signals. The core of GrokFormer is a Graph Fourier Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN)-based spectral convolution module, which parameterizes spectral filters as a sum of learnable Fourier series over the graph Laplacian spectrum up to order K. Each filter basis is constructed as a linear combination of sine and cosine functions with trainable coefficients, allowing for both spectrum- and order-adaptivity.
