The model synthesizes spatial representations from efficient multi-head self-attention and spectral representations from the Graph Fourier KAN, followed by normalization and a feed-forward network for prediction. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to demonstrate the universality, flexibility, and permutation-equivariance of the proposed filter, and the model will be designed to scale efficiently to large graphs using truncated spectral decomposition and sparse eigenvalue algorithms.
81af3a2952838d6b437d6985956d771084f341ab.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 11 real-world node classification datasets (including both homophilic and heterophilic graphs) and 5 graph classification benchmarks from diverse domains. The proposed method will be compared against a comprehensive set of baselines, including spatial-based GNNs, spectral-based GNNs, and state-of-the-art graph transformers such as Specformer and PolyFormer. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy, sum of squared errors (SSE), and R2 score for filter fitting tasks. Experimental setups will involve consistent data splits, hyperparameter tuning, and scalability tests using truncated spectral decomposition for large graphs. Ablation studies will assess the contributions of the spectral and spatial modules, and empirical analyses will examine the adaptability of the learned filters in both spectrum and order dimensions.
81af3a2952838d6b437d6985956d771084f341ab.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first graph transformer model to introduce a learnable filter that is adaptive in both graph spectrum and spectral order, enabling the modeling of a wide range of frequency signals. The method leverages a novel Graph Fourier KAN module that parameterizes spectral filters as Fourier series over learnable activation functions, providing superior expressiveness and flexibility compared to fixed-basis polynomial or spectrum-only adaptive filters. Theoretical results establish the universality and permutation-equivariance of the filter, and empirical results demonstrate state-of-the-art performance and scalability on both node and graph classification tasks, as well as superior filter fitting capabilities on synthetic and real-world datasets.

81ddde3b06cde1a3b9b07641fde7e6bf5e7f99c1.title: Gradients and frequency profiles of quantum re-uploading models
81ddde3b06cde1a3b9b07641fde7e6bf5e7f99c1.research_question: How do the trainability and expressivity of quantum re-uploading (QRU) models compare to those of parameterized quantum circuits (PQCs), and what are the fundamental properties governing their optimization landscapes and function approximation capabilities?
81ddde3b06cde1a3b9b07641fde7e6bf5e7f99c1.hypothesis: Quantum re-uploading models exhibit bounded gradients and output functions with vanishing high-frequency components, resulting in improved trainability and limited expressivity that offers protection against overfitting. Furthermore, the introduction of absorption witnesses can quantify the impact of data-encoding gates on trainability relative to base PQCs.
81ddde3b06cde1a3b9b07641fde7e6bf5e7f99c1.proposed_method: A theoretical and numerical investigation will be conducted to analyze the gradients and frequency profiles of quantum re-uploading models. The approach involves deriving analytical bounds on the variance of gradients in QRU models, introducing the concept of absorption witnesses to quantify the difference in trainability between QRU models and their base PQCs, and characterizing the expressivity of QRU output functions using Fourier analysis. The methodology will include the development of harmonic and anharmonic representations for QRU circuits, enabling the study of the frequency spectrum of hypothesis functions. Analytical results will be complemented by numerical simulations to validate the theoretical findings under various circuit architectures and data distributions.
81ddde3b06cde1a3b9b07641fde7e6bf5e7f99c1.experiment_details: Experiments will involve simulating QRU models and corresponding base PQCs with varying circuit depths, numbers of qubits, and types of data-encoding gates. Datasets for the experiments will include both Gaussian and uniform data distributions. Baseline comparisons will be made between QRU models and PQCs with and without entangling gates, as well as translation-invariant ansatzes. Evaluation metrics will focus on the average norm of gradients (as a proxy for trainability), the variance of gradients, and the frequency profiles of the output functions. The information content (IC) metric will be used to estimate average gradient magnitudes, and the impact of circuit architecture and data encoding on vanishing gradients and expressivity will be systematically explored.
81ddde3b06cde1a3b9b07641fde7e6bf5e7f99c1.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the absorption witness as a novel quantitative tool to relate the trainability of QRU models to their base PQCs, providing a new perspective on the influence of data-encoding gates. It establishes, for the first time, rigorous bounds on the gradients and frequency profiles of QRU models, demonstrating that high-frequency components in output functions vanish rapidly and that derivatives with respect to data are upper-bounded. This leads to the insight that QRU models inherently limit sensitivity to fine details and mitigate overfitting. The work also extends the analysis to both harmonic and generic (anharmonic) data generators, providing a comprehensive theoretical framework for understanding the trade-off between expressivity and trainability in quantum machine learning models.

81e0f65ab7e9bf411ee7d96b287f11f1db1b1624.title: DipLLM: Fine-Tuning LLM for Strategic Decision-making in Diplomacy
81e0f65ab7e9bf411ee7d96b287f11f1db1b1624.research_question: Can large language models (LLMs) be fine-tuned to learn equilibrium policies and achieve superior strategic decision-making performance in complex multiplayer games such as Diplomacy, while using significantly less training data than traditional equilibrium search-based methods?
81e0f65ab7e9bf411ee7d96b287f11f1db1b1624.hypothesis: Fine-tuning LLMs within an autoregressive factorization framework on a small, domain-specific dataset will enable the model to learn equilibrium policies that outperform traditional domain-specific models and state-of-the-art equilibrium search-based agents in complex multiplayer games like Diplomacy.
81e0f65ab7e9bf411ee7d96b287f11f1db1b1624.proposed_method: A novel LLM-based agent, DipLLM, will be developed and fine-tuned to learn equilibrium policies for the game of Diplomacy. The approach employs an autoregressive factorization framework that decomposes the complex task of joint multi-unit action selection into a sequence of unit-level decisions, each conditioned on the game state and previously chosen actions. The learning objective is theoretically grounded to approximate Nash equilibrium by minimizing the KL divergence between the LLM’s policy and a target equilibrium policy, incorporating unit-level Q-values derived from equilibrium search. The fine-tuning process uses a specially designed loss function and a dataset structured in autoregressive form, where each training sample consists of a textual game state, a sequence of prior unit actions, the current unit action, and its associated Q-value. This methodology aims to reduce the combinatorial complexity of the action space and enable efficient, high-quality policy learning.
81e0f65ab7e9bf411ee7d96b287f11f1db1b1624.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in the no-press variant of Diplomacy, evaluating the proposed agent against a range of baselines including DipNet, DORA, DNVI, Cicero (state-of-the-art), and LLM-based agents using prompting and supervised fine-tuning (SFT). The evaluation will use metrics such as sum-of-squares scoring (SoS), win rate, survival rate, and defeat rate. Games will be played in a 1v6 population format, with each agent controlling one power and the remaining powers controlled by baseline models. The fine-tuning dataset will be generated by interacting with the environment using DipNet and applying the piKL-Hedge equilibrium search algorithm to produce Q-values. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of autoregressive factorization and fine-tuning, and comparisons will be made with and without equilibrium search enhancements. The efficiency and data requirements of the proposed method will be benchmarked against Cicero, with DipLLM using only 1.5% of the training data required by Cicero.
81e0f65ab7e9bf411ee7d96b287f11f1db1b1624.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretically grounded, autoregressive factorization framework for fine-tuning LLMs to learn equilibrium policies in complex multiplayer games. It claims significant improvements in data efficiency, requiring only a small fraction of the training data used by state-of-the-art models while achieving superior performance. The approach provides a new method for decomposing large combinatorial action spaces into manageable sub-tasks, enabling effective fine-tuning of LLMs for strategic decision-making. The method is claimed to outperform both traditional domain-specific models and advanced equilibrium search-based agents, and to offer practical advantages in inference efficiency for real-time applications.

820d2d211c94d483b5f6f6554a4c0d40a60e7775.title: VADTree: Explainable Training-Free Video Anomaly Detection via Hierarchical Granularity-Aware Tree
820d2d211c94d483b5f6f6554a4c0d40a60e7775.research_question: How can video anomaly detection be made more explainable, adaptive to varying temporal spans, and effective without the need for in-domain training data?
820d2d211c94d483b5f6f6554a4c0d40a60e7775.hypothesis: A hierarchical, granularity-aware tree structure leveraging pre-trained event boundary detection and visual-language models can enable training-free, explainable, and robust video anomaly detection that adapts to diverse anomaly durations and provides interpretable reasoning.
820d2d211c94d483b5f6f6554a4c0d40a60e7775.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed that constructs a hierarchical granularity-aware tree (HGTree) for flexible video segmentation based on event boundaries detected by a pre-trained Generic Event Boundary Detection (GEBD) model. The video is first partitioned into overlapping temporal segments, and a global boundary confidence sequence is generated. A binary tree is recursively built by splitting at high-confidence event boundaries, and nodes are stratified into coarse and fine clusters using K-means clustering and redundancy removal. For each node, multi-dimensional priors (scene, object, action) are injected into a visual-language model (VLM) to generate content descriptions, which are then scored for anomaly likelihood by a large language model (LLM). Intra-cluster node refinement aggregates scores from semantically similar nodes using feature similarity, while inter-cluster node correlation fuses anomaly scores across hierarchical levels based on cohesion-driven weighting, ensuring robust and contextually consistent anomaly detection.
820d2d211c94d483b5f6f6554a4c0d40a60e7775.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on three large-scale, real-world video anomaly detection datasets: UCF-Crime, XD-Violence, and MSAD. The evaluation uses frame-level area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC ROC) as the primary metric, with average precision (AP) also reported for XD-Violence. Baselines include state-of-the-art training-free, unsupervised, one-class, and weakly-supervised VAD methods. Implementation uses EfficientGEBD for event boundary detection, LLaVA-Video-7B-Qwen2 and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B as VLM and LLM, and ImageBind for feature extraction. Ablation studies systematically assess the contribution of each module (HGTree, prior-infused scoring, intra-cluster refinement, inter-cluster correlation), and different clustering and model configurations are evaluated for robustness.
820d2d211c94d483b5f6f6554a4c0d40a60e7775.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a training-free, explainable video anomaly detection framework that adaptively segments videos at multiple granularities using a hierarchical tree structure grounded in pre-trained event boundary knowledge. It integrates multi-dimensional priors and leverages VLMs and LLMs for interpretable anomaly reasoning. The method achieves state-of-the-art results among training-free and unsupervised methods, surpassing some weakly-supervised approaches, and demonstrates superior efficiency and flexibility in capturing anomalies of varying durations. The framework also provides explicit, human-interpretable explanations for detected anomalies.

821eda22a55fecd25d1cf6c9d120274cb6ef36ba.title: Task-Induced Representation Learning
821eda22a55fecd25d1cf6c9d120274cb6ef36ba.research_question: How can representation learning approaches be optimized to improve decision-making efficiency in visually complex environments with substantial distractors, especially for reinforcement learning and imitation learning tasks?
821eda22a55fecd25d1cf6c9d120274cb6ef36ba.hypothesis: Task-induced representation learning approaches that leverage task information from prior tasks will enable more efficient learning on downstream tasks in visually complex environments, outperforming unsupervised representation learning methods by focusing on task-relevant features and ignoring distractors.
821eda22a55fecd25d1cf6c9d120274cb6ef36ba.proposed_method: A framework for task-induced representation learning (TARP) will be developed, which uses task information such as rewards or demonstrations from prior tasks to guide the learning of compact, task-relevant representations. Several instantiations of this framework will be implemented, including value prediction (TARP-V), offline RL (TARP-CQL), bisimulation-based learning (TARP-Bisim), and imitation learning (TARP-BC), each training a shared encoder with task-specific supervision heads. The learned representations will be pre-trained offline using multi-task datasets and then transferred to downstream policies for new, unseen tasks. Comparisons will be made to unsupervised approaches based on reconstruction (e.g., beta-VAE, video prediction) and contrastive learning (e.g., InfoNCE/ATC), as well as hybrid objectives that combine reconstruction and reward prediction.
821eda22a55fecd25d1cf6c9d120274cb6ef36ba.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in four visually complex environments: Distracting DMControl (with background videos from DAVIS2017), ViZDoom (with diverse textures and enemy appearances), Distracting MetaWorld (robotic manipulation with background videos), and CARLA (urban driving simulator with realistic distractors). Datasets will be collected from multiple prior tasks, with both reward annotations and demonstration data. Baselines will include policies trained from scratch, unsupervised representation learning methods, hybrid objectives, and policy transfer baselines. Evaluation metrics will include downstream task learning efficiency (sample efficiency), normalized episode reward, and probing tasks for representation quality (e.g., state prediction error, background classification accuracy). Policies will be trained using SAC for continuous control and PPO for discrete action tasks, with both frozen and fine-tuned encoder settings. Additional analyses will examine the impact of dataset diversity, data optimality, and multi-source supervision.
821eda22a55fecd25d1cf6c9d120274cb6ef36ba.novelty_claims: The proposed research formalizes and systematically evaluates the family of task-induced representation learning approaches, demonstrating their effectiveness in visually complex environments with substantial distractors. The approach enables representations that focus on task-relevant information, leading to improved sample efficiency and transferability compared to unsupervised methods. The research also provides best practices for dataset collection and shows robustness to sub-optimal and heterogeneous data sources, supporting practical deployment in real-world settings.

8223da35c0fc3143f2903b5bfbfac9e4cce81d0a.title: Motion Planning Diffusion: Learning and Planning of Robot Motions with Diffusion Models
8223da35c0fc3143f2903b5bfbfac9e4cce81d0a.research_question: How can robot motion planning be improved by learning expressive, multimodal trajectory priors from expert data, and how can these priors be leveraged to generate feasible, smooth, and collision-free robot motions in both familiar and novel environments?
8223da35c0fc3143f2903b5bfbfac9e4cce81d0a.hypothesis: Learning trajectory priors with diffusion models will enable more effective and efficient robot motion planning by capturing high-dimensional, multimodal distributions, and by integrating these priors directly into the planning-as-inference framework, it will be possible to generate diverse, collision-free, and smooth trajectories that generalize to environments with unseen obstacles better than existing generative models or classical methods.
8223da35c0fc3143f2903b5bfbfac9e4cce81d0a.proposed_method: A novel motion planning framework is developed that learns trajectory priors using diffusion models trained on expert-generated, collision-free trajectories. The approach formulates motion planning as probabilistic inference, where the goal is to sample from the posterior distribution of trajectories conditioned on task objectives (such as start/goal states, smoothness, and collision avoidance). The diffusion model is trained to denoise trajectories from Gaussian noise to the data distribution using a temporal U-Net architecture, and at inference, the reverse diffusion process is guided by gradients of differentiable motion planning costs, effectively biasing samples toward feasible solutions. The method incorporates a variety of cost terms, including start/goal constraints, collision and self-collision avoidance, joint limits, end-effector pose, and Gaussian process smoothness, all of which are differentiable and integrated into the sampling process. The framework enables direct sampling of optimal trajectories from the posterior, merging prior learning and motion optimization into a unified, differentiable process.
8223da35c0fc3143f2903b5bfbfac9e4cce81d0a.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted in a suite of simulated environments of increasing complexity, including 2D and 3D navigation tasks and 7-DOF robot arm manipulation tasks (e.g., PointMass2D Dense, PointMass3D Maze Boxes, PandaSpheres, Panda Shelf). The diffusion-based method is compared against several baselines: RRTConnect (sampling-based), GPMP (optimization-based), Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE) priors, and combinations thereof (e.g., using priors to initialize GPMP). Evaluation metrics include planning time, success rate (collision-free trajectory generation), collision intensity (percentage of waypoints in collision), path length, and trajectory variance (measuring multimodality). Datasets for training are generated by sampling thousands of expert trajectories using RRTConnect and subsequent optimization, with environments extended with additional obstacles to test generalization. The real-world applicability is validated on a Franka Emika Panda robot in a shelf environment, where the planner must avoid previously unseen obstacles while maintaining end-effector orientation.
8223da35c0fc3143f2903b5bfbfac9e4cce81d0a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces diffusion models as trajectory priors for robot motion planning, enabling the direct sampling of optimal trajectories from the posterior distribution conditioned on task objectives. This method unifies prior learning and motion optimization within the planning-as-inference framework, leveraging the expressive power of diffusion models to capture high-dimensional, multimodal trajectory distributions. The integration of differentiable motion planning costs into the reverse diffusion process allows for effective guidance toward feasible, smooth, and collision-free solutions, even in environments with unseen obstacles. The approach demonstrates superior generalization, multimodality, and planning efficiency compared to existing generative models (such as CVAEs) and classical planners, and provides a new paradigm for learning-based motion planning in robotics.

822e28e8ef26471e3e3f75f53dc3087d6856ab1f.title: SGS-SLAM: Semantic Gaussian Splatting For Neural Dense SLAM
822e28e8ef26471e3e3f75f53dc3087d6856ab1f.research_question: How can semantic information be effectively integrated into dense visual SLAM systems to improve real-time camera tracking, high-fidelity 3D reconstruction, and precise object-level segmentation in both synthetic and real-world environments?
822e28e8ef26471e3e3f75f53dc3087d6856ab1f.hypothesis: Incorporating multi-channel semantic, appearance, and geometric features into a Gaussian-based volumetric representation will overcome the oversmoothing and inefficiency limitations of neural implicit SLAM systems, resulting in superior real-time tracking, reconstruction quality, and semantic segmentation accuracy.
822e28e8ef26471e3e3f75f53dc3087d6856ab1f.proposed_method: A novel semantic visual SLAM system, SGS-SLAM, will be developed based on 3D Gaussian Splatting. The method will represent the scene as a set of isotropic 3D Gaussians, each parameterized by position, radius, opacity, appearance color, and semantic color. Differentiable rendering will be employed to project these Gaussians into 2D images, enabling joint optimization of appearance, geometry, and semantic channels. A semantic feature loss will be introduced alongside color and depth losses to guide the optimization, and a semantic-guided keyframe selection strategy will be used to minimize cumulative errors by leveraging both geometric and semantic overlap criteria. The system will also support object-level manipulation by grouping Gaussians according to semantic labels, enabling downstream tasks such as scene editing.
822e28e8ef26471e3e3f75f53dc3087d6856ab1f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic (Replica) and real-world (ScanNet, ScanNet++) datasets, utilizing ground-truth camera poses and semantic maps. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines including NICE-SLAM, vMap, Co-SLAM, ESLAM, SplaTAM, NIDS-SLAM, DNS-SLAM, and SNI-SLAM. Evaluation metrics will include PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS for reconstruction quality, average absolute trajectory error (ATE RMSE) for camera pose estimation, and mIoU for semantic segmentation. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by standardizing the number of training iterations and reporting frame-per-second (FPS) rates for tracking and mapping.
822e28e8ef26471e3e3f75f53dc3087d6856ab1f.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first semantic RGB-D SLAM system grounded in 3D Gaussian Splatting, enabling explicit volumetric representation for real-time tracking and mapping. The approach uniquely integrates 2D semantic maps into the 3D Gaussian field, allowing joint multi-channel optimization and semantic-guided keyframe selection. The method claims to overcome the oversmoothing and inefficiency of NeRF-based SLAM, providing high-fidelity reconstruction, optimal segmentation precision, and object-level geometry suitable for downstream manipulation tasks.

822fa4223ac7d88a9f0027945f489587f0515c1e.title: The Relationship between No-Regret Learning and Online Conformal Prediction
822fa4223ac7d88a9f0027945f489587f0515c1e.research_question: What is the precise relationship between no-regret learning algorithms and online conformal prediction, especially in adversarial and group-conditional settings, and how can regret minimization techniques be leveraged to guarantee various forms of coverage (marginal, group-conditional, and multivalid) in online conformal prediction?
822fa4223ac7d88a9f0027945f489587f0515c1e.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that standard external regret minimization is insufficient to guarantee coverage in adversarial or group-conditional settings, but that swap regret and group-conditional swap regret are tightly connected to threshold-calibrated and multivalid coverage, respectively. Further, it is conjectured that algorithms from the follow-the-regularized-leader (FTRL) family can provide efficient and generalizable coverage guarantees for arbitrary group structures.
822fa4223ac7d88a9f0027945f489587f0515c1e.proposed_method: The proposed approach will systematically analyze the connections between different forms of regret (external, group-conditional, and swap regret) and coverage guarantees in online conformal prediction. The methodology will involve formalizing the problem as a sequential prediction task, where at each round a threshold parameter is predicted based on available context and past history. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to establish equivalences and separations between regret guarantees and coverage properties, under various smoothness and adversarial conditions. Algorithms from the FTRL family, including online gradient descent and multiplicative weights, will be adapted to the group-conditional setting by parameterizing the threshold as a linear function over group indicator functions. Additionally, swap regret minimization algorithms will be employed to guarantee threshold-calibrated and multivalid coverage. Theoretical bounds on coverage error will be derived as functions of regret and regularization parameters.
822fa4223ac7d88a9f0027945f489587f0515c1e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a multi-group generalization of the ACI (Adaptive Conformal Inference) algorithm, as well as existing online conformal prediction algorithms that guarantee multivalid coverage. Synthetic and real-world datasets will be used, with arbitrary and intersecting group structures defined via indicator functions. Baselines will include standard online gradient descent and sequential calibration-based algorithms. Evaluation metrics will focus on empirical coverage rates (marginal, group-conditional, and multivalid), convergence speed to the target coverage rate, and the growth of parameter norms over time. Experimental setup will involve varying the number of groups, the nature of group overlap, and the adversariality of the data sequence to assess robustness and generalization.
822fa4223ac7d88a9f0027945f489587f0515c1e.novelty_claims: The proposal claims a novel and tight equivalence between swap regret minimization and threshold-calibrated coverage in adversarial online conformal prediction, extending to group-conditional (multivalid) coverage. It introduces the use of FTRL-based algorithms for group-conditional coverage guarantees with arbitrary group structures, generalizing prior results that were limited to marginal coverage or specific group settings. The approach provides new theoretical bounds on coverage error as a function of regret and regularization, and demonstrates empirically faster convergence to desired coverage rates compared to existing methods. The proposal also establishes lower bounds and tightness results for the growth of parameter norms in high-dimensional group settings.

823ca4778e1027f2f0b356df051d762dcecaaba0.title: FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning
823ca4778e1027f2f0b356df051d762dcecaaba0.research_question: How can the efficiency and scalability of attention mechanisms in Transformers be improved to better utilize GPU resources, particularly for long sequence lengths, without introducing approximations or sacrificing accuracy?
823ca4778e1027f2f0b356df051d762dcecaaba0.hypothesis: Optimizing work partitioning and parallelism in the attention computation, specifically by reducing non-matrix-multiply operations and improving thread and warp scheduling on GPUs, will significantly increase the throughput and efficiency of attention layers, approaching the performance of highly optimized matrix-multiply operations.
823ca4778e1027f2f0b356df051d762dcecaaba0.proposed_method: A new algorithm, FlashAttention-2, will be developed to enhance the efficiency of attention computation on GPUs. The method will reduce the number of non-matrix-multiply floating point operations (FLOPs) by restructuring the online softmax computation, maintaining unscaled outputs during intermediate steps, and storing only essential statistics for the backward pass. Parallelism will be increased by distributing the attention computation not only across batch and head dimensions, but also along the sequence length dimension, allowing for higher GPU occupancy, especially with long sequences and small batch sizes. Within each thread block, work will be partitioned across warps by splitting the query matrix (Q) rather than the key (K) or value (V), minimizing shared memory communication and synchronization. The method will support both standard and causal-masked attention, as well as multi-query and grouped-query attention variants, and will be tuned for optimal block sizes based on device constraints.
823ca4778e1027f2f0b356df051d762dcecaaba0.experiment_details: Experiments will benchmark the runtime and throughput of FlashAttention-2 against several baselines, including standard PyTorch attention, the original FlashAttention, and Triton-based implementations, using A100 80GB SXM4 GPUs. Sequence lengths will be varied from 512 to 16k, with batch sizes set to maintain a constant total token count, and head dimensions of 64 and 128. Both forward and backward pass speeds will be measured, with and without causal masking, and FLOPs utilization will be calculated relative to theoretical device maximums. End-to-end training speed will be evaluated by training GPT-style Transformer models (1.3B and 2.7B parameters) on sequence lengths of 2k and 8k, comparing wall-clock speed and FLOPs utilization to previous methods.
823ca4778e1027f2f0b356df051d762dcecaaba0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel combination of algorithmic tweaks and hardware-aware parallelization strategies that reduce non-matmul FLOPs, improve GPU occupancy, and minimize shared memory communication. By parallelizing attention computation along the sequence length and restructuring intra-block work partitioning, the method achieves significant speedups—up to 2-3× over previous state-of-the-art attention implementations—while maintaining exactness (no approximation). The approach enables attention layers to reach up to 73% of theoretical maximum throughput and 72% model FLOPs utilization on A100 GPUs, narrowing the gap with optimized matrix-multiply operations and supporting efficient training of large-scale Transformer models on long sequences.

82460f7995f66f3f035f34ecbd2c82b024282529.title: Make Your LLM Fully Utilize the Context
82460f7995f66f3f035f34ecbd2c82b024282529.research_question: How can large language models be enabled to fully utilize information distributed throughout long input contexts, rather than primarily focusing on the beginning and end of the context?
82460f7995f66f3f035f34ecbd2c82b024282529.hypothesis: The underutilization of information in the middle of long contexts by large language models is due to insufficient explicit supervision during training, which leads to a position bias that emphasizes information at the beginning and end of the context. Explicitly training models to recognize that crucial information can appear at any position will improve their ability to utilize the entire context.
82460f7995f66f3f035f34ecbd2c82b024282529.proposed_method: A novel data-driven training paradigm, termed INformation-INtensive (IN2) training, will be developed to explicitly teach large language models that important information can appear anywhere in a long context. This approach involves constructing a synthetic long-context question-answer dataset by concatenating multiple short segments (approximately 128 tokens each) into long contexts ranging from 4K to 32K tokens. Two types of question-answer pairs will be generated: (1) those requiring fine-grained information awareness of a single short segment, and (2) those requiring integration and reasoning over information from two or more segments, with segments randomly placed throughout the context. The training will use a powerful LLM (e.g., GPT-4-Turbo) to generate questions and answers from raw text segments, and the resulting dataset will be used to fine-tune a strong open-source LLM (such as Mistral-7B) in an instruction-tuning paradigm. The training process will ensure balanced context lengths and include a mixture of long-context and short-context data to prevent catastrophic forgetting.
82460f7995f66f3f035f34ecbd2c82b024282529.experiment_details: The proposed method will be evaluated using both synthetic probing tasks and real-world long-context benchmarks. Three probing tasks (VAL Probing) will be designed to assess information retrieval across various context styles (document, code, and structured data) and retrieval patterns (forward, backward, and bi-directional) in contexts up to 32K tokens. Baselines will include state-of-the-art open-source long-context models (e.g., Mistral-7B-Instruct, LongAlign, InternLM2) and proprietary models (e.g., GPT-4-Turbo). Evaluation metrics will include word-level recall, exact-match accuracy, and relaxed exact-match accuracy, depending on the task. Additionally, performance will be measured on nine real-world long-context tasks (from LongBench, such as NarrativeQA, Qasper, MultiFQA, HotpotQA, and summarization tasks) and eight short-context tasks (e.g., MMLU, BoolQ, RACE-H, CSQA, ARC-C, HellaSwag, GSM8K, MATH) to ensure that short-context capabilities are not compromised. Experiments will also analyze the impact of training strategies such as sliding windows and position encoding settings.
82460f7995f66f3f035f34ecbd2c82b024282529.novelty_claims: The proposed IN2 training introduces a purely data-driven approach that explicitly addresses the lost-in-the-middle problem by synthesizing long-context datasets requiring fine-grained and multi-hop information retrieval from arbitrary positions. The method is the first to systematically generate and utilize such data to teach models that any position in the context can hold crucial information. The evaluation framework (VAL Probing) is novel in its comprehensive coverage of context styles and retrieval patterns, providing a more challenging and diagnostic benchmark for long-context utilization than existing tasks. The approach is shown to significantly improve long-context information retrieval robustness and generalize to real-world tasks, while maintaining short-context performance.

825c7bf07ffc175bb08262e5ec70015709c60b58.title: Domino: Eliminating Communication in LLM Training via Generic Tensor Slicing and Overlapping
825c7bf07ffc175bb08262e5ec70015709c60b58.research_question: How can communication overhead in large language model (LLM) training be eliminated or substantially reduced in distributed environments, particularly when using tensor parallelism across both single-node and multi-node GPU clusters?
825c7bf07ffc175bb08262e5ec70015709c60b58.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a generic tensor slicing and pipelining approach, which breaks data dependencies and enables fine-grained overlapping of computation and communication, can significantly reduce or hide communication overhead in tensor parallel LLM training, resulting in improved training throughput and efficiency.
825c7bf07ffc175bb08262e5ec70015709c60b58.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that generically partitions the computation of transformer model layers by slicing input tensors and weight tensors along specific dimensions, thereby breaking data dependencies and enabling independent computation units. These units are then pipelined such that communication (e.g., AllReduce operations) is overlapped with computation, both within and across transformer layers. The method supports row-wise splits on inputs (batch dimension), column-wise splits on weights (hidden dimension), and hybrid splits to maintain kernel efficiency for extremely large models. The approach is designed to be hardware-agnostic and integrates with existing kernel fusion and optimization techniques, such as CUDA MultiStream, CUDAGraph, and PyTorch's torch.compile, to maximize GPU utilization and minimize idle time. Prior to training, system benchmarks are used to select optimal partition granularity, and the method is implemented as a drop-in replacement for standard tensor parallelism.
825c7bf07ffc175bb08262e5ec70015709c60b58.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on Nvidia DGX-H100 clusters with up to 32 H100 GPUs interconnected via high-bandwidth NVLink and InfiniBand, covering both single-node and multi-node scenarios. The evaluation will use popular LLM architectures such as GPT-3 (2.7B, 6.7B, 13B, 30B) and Llama-2 (7B, 13B), with varying global batch sizes (4-64) and sequence lengths (512, 1024). The baseline for comparison will be Megatron-LM in both synchronous and asynchronous (coarse-grained overlapping) modes. Metrics will include end-to-end training iteration time and throughput (TFLOPs), with ablation studies to assess the impact of kernel-level optimizations. Additional simulations will project performance under future hardware with higher inter-node bandwidth.
825c7bf07ffc175bb08262e5ec70015709c60b58.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to provide a generic, end-to-end solution for communication-computation overlapping in tensor-parallel-only LLM training across both single-node and multi-node settings. It introduces a flexible and extensible tensor slicing strategy that enables fine-grained overlapping beyond traditional kernel fusion approaches, supporting a wider range of computation and communication patterns. The approach is mathematically equivalent to standard tensor parallelism but achieves up to 1.3x speedup over state-of-the-art implementations, with the potential for even higher gains as hardware bandwidth increases. The framework is designed for easy integration with existing and future kernel and system-level optimizations.

82701185d8873ff1a3cdfd59c99879a6e391faa1.title: Simple and Fast Group Robustness by Automatic Feature Reweighting
82701185d8873ff1a3cdfd59c99879a6e391faa1.research_question: How can model robustness to spurious correlations in data be improved, particularly in scenarios where group labels or explicit knowledge of spurious features are unavailable, while maintaining computational efficiency and simplicity?
82701185d8873ff1a3cdfd59c99879a6e391faa1.hypothesis: Automatically reweighting training examples based on model prediction errors, without access to group labels or explicit spurious attribute annotations, will reduce reliance on spurious features and improve worst-group accuracy, achieving competitive or superior robustness compared to existing methods with minimal computational overhead.
82701185d8873ff1a3cdfd59c99879a6e391faa1.proposed_method: A two-stage approach is proposed for improving group robustness. In the first stage, a standard empirical risk minimization (ERM) model is trained to convergence on the training data, with no modifications or interventions. In the second stage, only the last layer of the trained model is retrained on a held-out reweighting set, using a weighted cross-entropy loss. The per-example weights are determined by a softmax function over the 'incorrectness' of the model's predictions (i.e., one minus the predicted probability for the correct class), with an inverse temperature hyperparameter to control the degree of upweighting. To address class imbalance, the weights are further modulated by class-dependent constants. This procedure automatically upweights examples where the base model performs poorly, which tend to be from minority or underrepresented groups, thereby reducing reliance on spurious correlations without requiring group labels. Regularization is applied to the last layer to prevent overfitting and maintain performance on majority groups.
82701185d8873ff1a3cdfd59c99879a6e391faa1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several vision and natural language classification benchmarks known to contain spurious correlations, including Waterbirds, CelebA, MultiNLI, CivilComments, and ChestX-Ray. Standard pretrained architectures will be used (e.g., ResNet-50 for vision, BERT for text). The proposed method will be compared against strong baselines such as ERM, JTT, CNC, DFR, and Group-DRO, with and without access to group labels. Evaluation metrics will include worst-group accuracy (WGA) and mean accuracy, with a focus on test set performance. Hyperparameters will be tuned using a small validation set with group annotations, and ablation studies will assess sensitivity to hyperparameters, data splits, and weighting functions. Training time and computational overhead will be measured and compared to baselines.
82701185d8873ff1a3cdfd59c99879a6e391faa1.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple and efficient automatic feature reweighting (AFR) procedure that does not require group labels or explicit knowledge of spurious features during training. It achieves competitive or superior worst-group accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods, while incurring negligible computational overhead by retraining only the last layer. The approach is robust to hyperparameter choices, broadly applicable to real-world problems lacking group annotations, and more label-efficient than methods requiring group information for training. The method also provides insights into the limitations and optimality of dataset reweighting strategies for group robustness.

8291d58c097db892021accf8098755ced2b26725.title: Strategic Classification With Externalities
8291d58c097db892021accf8098755ced2b26725.research_question: How can strategic classification be robustly modeled and learned in multi-agent environments where agents' manipulations have externalities that affect each other, and what are the theoretical and algorithmic properties of such systems?
8291d58c097db892021accf8098755ced2b26725.hypothesis: It is possible to design and learn classifiers that minimize loss and generalize well even when multiple strategic agents interact and manipulate features in the presence of inter-agent externalities, provided certain structural assumptions on cost and externality functions are satisfied.
8291d58c097db892021accf8098755ced2b26725.proposed_method: A formal game-theoretic framework is developed where a principal (learner) releases a classifier, and multiple agents strategically manipulate their features, with each agent's manipulation potentially affecting others through externalities. The agent-agent interaction is modeled as a simultaneous game, while the principal-agent interaction is formulated as a Stackelberg game, leading to the Stackelberg-Nash Equilibrium as the solution concept. The method assumes cost functions based on the squared Euclidean norm and pairwise symmetric, convex externality functions. Under these assumptions, the agent manipulation game is shown to be a potential game with a strictly concave potential function, guaranteeing the existence, uniqueness, and efficient computability of the pure Nash Equilibrium. The learning problem is then cast as optimizing the classifier to minimize expected loss, where the loss is evaluated at the Nash Equilibrium of agent manipulations. Gradient-based optimization is enabled by differentiating through the equilibrium solution, leveraging the smoothness and concavity of the potential function.
8291d58c097db892021accf8098755ced2b26725.experiment_details: Theoretical analysis is conducted to establish PAC (Probably Approximately Correct) learning guarantees for the proposed framework, showing that classifiers can be learned to generalize well even when the number of agents is random and agents manipulate their features to equilibrium. The sample complexity is characterized in terms of the Lipschitz constants of the loss and equilibrium mapping, as well as the dimension of the feature space. The empirical risk minimization problem is addressed by providing explicit formulas for the gradient of the loss with respect to classifier parameters, including the Jacobian of the Nash Equilibrium mapping. While the primary focus is on theoretical guarantees, motivating examples such as university admissions and loan applications are used to instantiate the externality models, and the framework is designed to be compatible with standard binary linear classifiers and common loss functions (e.g., hinge loss, cross-entropy). Specific datasets, baselines, or empirical benchmarks are not detailed, as the proposal is primarily theoretical.
8291d58c097db892021accf8098755ced2b26725.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a strategic classification framework that explicitly models inter-agent externalities, a feature not addressed in prior strategic classification literature. It establishes the existence, uniqueness, and efficient computation of Nash Equilibria in multi-agent manipulation games with externalities, and provides PAC learning guarantees for classifiers in this setting. The method also enables gradient-based optimization by differentiating through the equilibrium, offering practical avenues for learning robust classifiers in environments with multiple interacting strategic agents.

8292083dd8f6ae898ea0ee54a6b97997d1a51c9d.title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
8292083dd8f6ae898ea0ee54a6b97997d1a51c9d.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) most effectively utilize additional test-time computation to improve performance on challenging natural language tasks, and how does the optimal allocation of test-time compute compare to simply scaling model parameters through additional pretraining?
8292083dd8f6ae898ea0ee54a6b97997d1a51c9d.hypothesis: Adaptive, prompt-specific allocation of test-time computation—using compute-optimal strategies based on prompt difficulty—can yield greater efficiency and performance improvements than uniform or naïve test-time compute allocation, and in some cases can outperform much larger models trained with significantly more pretraining compute.
8292083dd8f6ae898ea0ee54a6b97997d1a51c9d.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed to analyze and optimize the use of test-time computation in LLMs. The approach will focus on two main mechanisms: (1) adaptive search against dense, process-based verifier reward models (PRMs), and (2) iterative refinement of the model’s proposal distribution via self-revision at test time. For each prompt, a notion of question difficulty will be estimated—either via oracle access to ground-truth correctness or via model-predicted verifier scores—allowing the system to select the most effective test-time compute strategy and hyperparameters for that prompt. Search methods will include best-of-N weighted sampling, beam search, and lookahead search, while revision models will be fine-tuned to iteratively improve their own answers. The compute-optimal scaling strategy will allocate the test-time compute budget adaptively per prompt, maximizing expected accuracy under a fixed compute constraint.
8292083dd8f6ae898ea0ee54a6b97997d1a51c9d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the MATH benchmark, which contains high-school competition-level math problems of varying difficulty. The primary model will be PaLM 2-S*, fine-tuned for both revision and verification capabilities. Baselines will include standard best-of-N sampling, majority voting, and larger pretrained models (up to 14x parameter count) without additional test-time compute. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy (pass@1) across difficulty bins, relative improvement per compute budget, and FLOPs-matched comparisons between test-time compute scaling and model parameter scaling. Cross-validation will be used to avoid overfitting when selecting compute-optimal strategies, and both oracle and model-predicted difficulty estimates will be tested.
8292083dd8f6ae898ea0ee54a6b97997d1a51c9d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified, adaptive framework for optimally scaling test-time computation in LLMs, leveraging prompt-specific difficulty estimation to allocate compute efficiently. It systematically compares and combines iterative revision and verifier-based search strategies, demonstrating that adaptive test-time compute can outperform traditional best-of-N and even much larger models under matched compute budgets. The approach provides the first comprehensive analysis of compute-optimal scaling policies for LLMs, offering actionable insights for future model deployment and pretraining/inference tradeoffs.

82b17686abba18dfc821a262dab5fbb081aa2388.title: Residual Prompt Tuning: Improving Prompt Tuning with Residual Reparameterization
82b17686abba18dfc821a262dab5fbb081aa2388.research_question: How can the performance and stability of prompt tuning for parameter-efficient adaptation of pre-trained language models be improved, particularly for smaller models and in settings with limited data or prompt length?
82b17686abba18dfc821a262dab5fbb081aa2388.hypothesis: Reparameterizing soft prompt embeddings using a shallow neural network with a residual connection will significantly enhance the performance, robustness, and efficiency of prompt tuning compared to existing prompt tuning and reparameterization methods.
82b17686abba18dfc821a262dab5fbb081aa2388.proposed_method: A novel approach, Residual Prompt Tuning (ResPT), will be developed to improve prompt tuning by reparameterizing soft prompt embeddings through a shallow multi-layer perceptron (MLP) with a residual (skip) connection. Each prompt token embedding will be independently transformed by the shared MLP, which consists of a down-projection, non-linearity (ReLU), up-projection, and LayerNorm, and then summed with the original embedding. During training, both the prompt embeddings and the MLP parameters are jointly optimized while keeping the backbone language model frozen. After training, the reparameterization network is discarded, and only the projected prompt embeddings are used during inference, ensuring parameter efficiency.
82b17686abba18dfc821a262dab5fbb081aa2388.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the SuperGLUE benchmark, utilizing eight datasets (BoolQ, CB, COPA, MultiRC, ReCoRD, RTE, WiC, WSC) to evaluate natural language understanding performance. The method will be tested with T5-Large, T5-Base, and BERT-Base models, comparing against baselines including standard prompt tuning, prompt tuning with MLP or LSTM reparameterization, full fine-tuning, and other parameter-efficient tuning methods (Adapters, AdapterDrop, SPoT, ATTEMPT). Evaluation metrics will follow standard task-specific metrics (e.g., accuracy, F1, EM), and results will be averaged over multiple runs. Experiments will also assess robustness to hyperparameters (learning rate, prompt initialization), prompt length, and few-shot learning scenarios, with ablation studies on parameter sharing and MLP width.
82b17686abba18dfc821a262dab5fbb081aa2388.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a residual reparameterization framework for soft prompt embeddings, enabling more flexible and stable prompt tuning. Key innovations include the use of a shallow MLP with a residual connection for prompt embedding transformation, which improves convergence speed, robustness to hyperparameters, and effectiveness in few-shot and short-prompt regimes. The approach achieves significant performance gains over existing prompt tuning and reparameterization methods, while maintaining parameter efficiency and requiring no changes to the underlying language model architecture.

82bc594ddf77fe8e69e9b41dc32960d7f16b4b1d.title: What If We Recaption Billions of Web Images with LLaMA-3?
82bc594ddf77fe8e69e9b41dc32960d7f16b4b1d.research_question: How can large-scale web-crawled image-text datasets be improved to enhance the training of advanced vision-language models, particularly in terms of semantic alignment and descriptive richness of captions, and what is the impact of such improvements on downstream tasks such as cross-modal retrieval and text-to-image generation?
82bc594ddf77fe8e69e9b41dc32960d7f16b4b1d.hypothesis: Recaptioning large-scale web image datasets with a powerful open-source multimodal large language model will yield higher-quality, more semantically aligned, and descriptively rich captions, which in turn will significantly improve the performance of vision-language models on retrieval and generative tasks.
82bc594ddf77fe8e69e9b41dc32960d7f16b4b1d.proposed_method: A scalable recaptioning pipeline will be developed by fine-tuning a LLaVA-1.5 multimodal model, replacing its language decoder with LLaMA-3-8B for superior language understanding and generation. The model will be trained in two stages: first, only the projection MLP is trained using filtered image-text pairs from LAION, CC, and SBU datasets; second, both the projection MLP and language decoder are fine-tuned using instruction-following data and further refined with high-quality image-text pairs from HQ-Edit. The resulting captioner will be used to generate detailed, descriptive captions for approximately 1.3 billion images in the DataComp-1B dataset, using a prompt that encourages maximal descriptiveness. Captions will be generated auto-regressively with a maximum output length of 128 tokens, producing a new large-scale dataset (Recap-DataComp-1B) with enriched textual information.
82bc594ddf77fe8e69e9b41dc32960d7f16b4b1d.experiment_details: Experiments will include quantitative and qualitative analysis of the new captions, comparing word distributions, average lengths, and vocabulary diversity to the original DataComp-1B captions. Semantic quality will be evaluated using CLIP and LongCLIP models for image-text similarity, and GPT-4V for fluency and alignment ratings. Vision-language models (CLIP variants) will be trained on Recap-DataComp-1B, with ablation studies on mixing ratios of original and recaptioned data, and varying text encoder sizes. Zero-shot image classification and cross-modal retrieval will be evaluated on ImageNet-1K, MSCOCO, and Flickr30K, while text understanding will be assessed on Urban1K and VG-Attribute benchmarks. For generative evaluation, Diffusion Transformers (DiT) will be trained with mixed caption sources, and image generation quality will be assessed using FID, CLIP score, Recap-CLIP score, and GPT-4V ratings on COCO-30K and recaptioned prompts.
82bc594ddf77fe8e69e9b41dc32960d7f16b4b1d.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first billion-scale open-source recaptioning of web images using a LLaMA-3-powered multimodal model, resulting in a dataset with significantly richer, longer, and more semantically aligned captions than existing web-crawled datasets. The approach demonstrates that such large-scale, high-quality recaptioning can be achieved efficiently without relying on expensive proprietary APIs. Comprehensive evaluations will show that models trained on the recaptioned dataset achieve substantial improvements in cross-modal retrieval, text understanding, and text-to-image generation, particularly in handling long and complex prompts. The research will provide a publicly available resource to catalyze further advances in open-source vision-language foundation models.

82f75d838e92196864131bad25b1abc3b5d40a6f.title: Beyond Chinchilla-Optimal: Accounting for Inference in Language Model Scaling Laws
82f75d838e92196864131bad25b1abc3b5d40a6f.research_question: How can language model scaling laws be adapted to account for both training and inference costs, in order to optimize the parameter count and training data size for large language models under varying inference demands and compute or real-world cost constraints?
82f75d838e92196864131bad25b1abc3b5d40a6f.hypothesis: In scenarios with significant inference demand, training smaller models for longer durations (i.e., with higher tokens-per-parameter ratios) will minimize total computational and real-world costs, while maintaining or improving model quality compared to Chinchilla-optimal models.
82f75d838e92196864131bad25b1abc3b5d40a6f.proposed_method: A principled extension of the Chinchilla scaling laws will be developed to jointly optimize for both training and inference costs, rather than training costs alone. The method will formalize the trade-off between model size, training data size, and inference demand by defining an objective function that minimizes the sum of training and inference floating-point operations (FLOPs) or real-world costs, subject to a fixed target model quality (cross-entropy loss). Analytical and numerical techniques, such as the Newton root-finding method, will be used to solve for the optimal parameter count and training data size given a specified inference demand. The approach will also incorporate real-world hardware utilization factors (Model FLOPs Utilization, MFU) and cost per FLOP for both training and inference, including distinctions between input and output tokens, and allow for quantization and heterogeneous hardware deployment. Additionally, the methodology will include an empirical investigation into the validity of the scaling laws at extreme tokens-per-parameter ratios, and an ablation of the parametric fitting procedure used to derive scaling law coefficients.
82f75d838e92196864131bad25b1abc3b5d40a6f.experiment_details: A comprehensive suite of experiments will be conducted by training 47 transformer models (MPT architecture) ranging from 150M to 6B parameters, across data budgets spanning from 10 to 10,000 tokens per parameter. All models will be trained for a single epoch on a large corpus of trillions of tokens of web text and code, without data repetition. Model quality will be evaluated using cross-entropy loss and an open-source Evaluation Gauntlet, which aggregates performance across a diverse set of downstream tasks (e.g., world knowledge, commonsense reasoning, reading comprehension, language understanding, and symbolic problem solving) using metrics such as InContextLearningQAAccuracy and related measures. Baseline comparisons will be made against Chinchilla-optimal models and other scaling law prescriptions. Additional experiments will fit and ablate the scaling law coefficients using subsets of the training data at various tokens-per-parameter ratios, and real-world cost analyses will be performed using realistic hardware utilization and pricing assumptions (e.g., A100 GPUs, quantization effects).
82f75d838e92196864131bad25b1abc3b5d40a6f.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a novel extension of language model scaling laws that, for the first time, explicitly incorporates inference costs alongside training costs in the optimization of model size and training data. The approach provides a quantitative framework for minimizing total compute or real-world costs under arbitrary inference demand, enabling practitioners to select smaller, longer-trained models when appropriate. Empirical validation will be conducted at extreme tokens-per-parameter ratios, beyond the typical regime studied in prior work, and the research will demonstrate that model quality continues to improve without saturation at these scales. The proposal also identifies and addresses limitations in existing scaling law coefficient fitting procedures, showing that prior methods may overestimate the benefits of additional training data at high token-to-parameter ratios. The work offers actionable guidance for LLM deployment in inference-heavy scenarios and advances the understanding of scaling laws in both compute- and cost-constrained settings.

8310c87d029d7b82b59a32a204c107cb6353a224.title: Graph Neural Rough Differential Equations for Traffic Forecasting
8310c87d029d7b82b59a32a204c107cb6353a224.research_question: How can spatio-temporal dependencies in traffic forecasting be effectively modeled using advanced neural differential equation frameworks, particularly for graph-structured time-series data?
8310c87d029d7b82b59a32a204c107cb6353a224.hypothesis: Integrating neural rough differential equations (NRDEs) for both temporal and spatial processing within a unified spatio-temporal graph framework will improve the accuracy and robustness of traffic forecasting compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.
8310c87d029d7b82b59a32a204c107cb6353a224.proposed_method: A novel spatio-temporal graph neural rough differential equation (STG-NRDE) framework will be developed, combining two NRDEs: one dedicated to temporal processing and the other to spatial processing. The approach begins with a pre-processing step that constructs continuous paths for each node in the traffic network using interpolation, followed by computation of log-signature transforms to extract unique features from each node's time-series. The temporal NRDE processes each node's log-signature time-series independently, generating hidden trajectories. Subsequently, the spatial NRDE incorporates graph connectivity using an adaptive, learned adjacency matrix derived from node embeddings, performing graph convolutional operations over the temporally-encoded features. The two NRDEs are integrated into a single end-to-end differentiable framework, with initial values generated by fully connected layers and the final output produced through a linear transformation for multi-step traffic prediction. Training is performed using an L1 loss function with L2 regularization, and the entire model is optimized using standard deep learning techniques.
8310c87d029d7b82b59a32a204c107cb6353a224.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six real-world traffic datasets collected by the California Performance of Transportation (PeMS), covering both traffic volume and velocity prediction tasks. The datasets are split into training, validation, and testing sets in a 6:2:2 ratio, with each sample representing a 12-step input sequence predicting the next 12 time steps. The proposed method will be compared against 27 baseline models, including statistical methods (e.g., ARIMA, VAR), deep learning models (e.g., FC-LSTM, GRU-ED, TCN), and state-of-the-art spatio-temporal graph neural networks (e.g., STGCN, DCRNN, GraphWaveNet, AGCRN, STFGNN, STGODE, Z-GCNETs, DSTAGNN, STG-NCDE). Evaluation metrics will include mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE). Additional experiments will assess robustness to missing or irregular temporal data, reflecting real-world sensor failures.
8310c87d029d7b82b59a32a204c107cb6353a224.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to unify neural rough differential equations for both temporal and spatial processing in spatio-temporal graph forecasting. The method leverages the log-signature transform to extract unique, compact representations of time-series data, enabling continuous-time modeling and robustness to irregular or missing observations. An adaptive graph convolution mechanism learns the adjacency matrix dynamically from node features, eliminating the need for pre-defined spatial graphs. Large-scale experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art accuracy and robustness across diverse traffic datasets, outperforming all 27 considered baselines.

831380dc4c99b0d0a50d5fcd9bef5ff6f71e2c3e.title: Deep Learning Methods for Proximal Inference via Maximum Moment Restriction
831380dc4c99b0d0a50d5fcd9bef5ff6f71e2c3e.research_question: How can causal effects be accurately estimated from observational data in the presence of unmeasured confounding, leveraging proxy variables under appropriate structural assumptions, and can deep learning methods provide flexible and scalable solutions for this proximal inference problem?
831380dc4c99b0d0a50d5fcd9bef5ff6f71e2c3e.hypothesis: A single-stage deep neural network approach, trained using a loss function derived from maximum moment restriction (MMR) principles and optimized with either U-statistics or V-statistics, can consistently and accurately estimate causal effects in the presence of unmeasured confounding when sufficiently rich proxy variables are available, outperforming existing kernel- and two-stage-based methods.
831380dc4c99b0d0a50d5fcd9bef5ff6f71e2c3e.proposed_method: A novel single-stage estimation framework, Neural Maximum Moment Restriction (NMMR), is developed to estimate the bridge function necessary for proximal inference using deep neural networks. The method reformulates the integral equation underlying proximal inference as a conditional moment restriction, which is then expressed as a minimax risk function over an infinite set of moment restrictions. The empirical risk is estimated using either a U-statistic (yielding an unbiased estimator) or a V-statistic (yielding a biased but lower-variance estimator), with the neural network trained to minimize this risk plus an L2 regularization penalty on the network weights. The approach allows for the use of adaptive feature maps from neural networks, including convolutional architectures for image data, and is designed to be scalable to high-dimensional and large-sample settings. Once the bridge function is estimated, potential outcomes and causal effects are computed by averaging the network’s predictions over held-out proxy data.
831380dc4c99b0d0a50d5fcd9bef5ff6f71e2c3e.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on two established proximal inference benchmarks: the Demand experiment (estimating the effect of airline ticket price on sales with latent demand as a confounder) and the dSprite experiment (estimating properties of images with unobserved confounding). Datasets of varying sample sizes (ranging from 1,000 to 50,000 for Demand and up to 7,500 for dSprite) are used, with the dSprite task involving high-dimensional image data (4096-dimensional). Baseline comparisons include kernel-based methods (KPV, PMMR), two-stage neural network approaches (DFPV), autoencoder-based methods (CEVAE), two-stage least squares (2SLS), and naive regressions (linear, quadratic, and neural network). Evaluation is based on causal mean squared error (c-MSE) between estimated and true potential outcomes, with each method replicated 20 times per sample size. The NMMR method is implemented in PyTorch and tested on modern GPUs, with code made publicly available for reproducibility.
831380dc4c99b0d0a50d5fcd9bef5ff6f71e2c3e.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first single-stage neural network approach for proximal inference using maximum moment restriction, with the flexibility to optimize using either U-statistics or V-statistics. It provides new theoretical consistency guarantees for neural network-based bridge function estimation in the proximal setting. The method demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on established benchmarks, including the first application of convolutional neural networks for proximal inference with image data. Additionally, it presents the first unbiased estimator of the MMR risk function in the proximal setting using the U-statistic, and offers a scalable, data-adaptive alternative to kernel-based and two-stage methods.

83151d416be0785acc14993800a4523f8b1379e6.title: Attention with Trained Embeddings Provably Selects Important Tokens
83151d416be0785acc14993800a4523f8b1379e6.research_question: What structure do token embeddings learn during gradient-based training in attention models, and how is this structure related to the statistical properties of the data in binary text classification tasks?
83151d416be0785acc14993800a4523f8b1379e6.hypothesis: Token embeddings trained via gradient descent in attention-based models will align with the empirical importance of tokens, as measured by their frequency and correlation with class labels, and the attention mechanism will select tokens that are most predictive of the output label.
83151d416be0785acc14993800a4523f8b1379e6.proposed_method: A one-layer softmax attention model with a linear head for binary classification will be employed, where each input sequence is appended with a ⟨cls⟩ token and all tokens are embedded into a shared vector space. The model output is computed as a weighted sum of token embeddings, with weights determined by the softmax of the dot product between the ⟨cls⟩ embedding and each token embedding. The embeddings for both context tokens and the ⟨cls⟩ token are trained using gradient descent to minimize the standard logistic loss, while the output vector is fixed. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to characterize the dynamics of the embedding updates, particularly after one gradient step and after convergence of the ⟨cls⟩ embedding under gradient flow. The structure of learned embeddings will be related to empirical token statistics, such as signed frequency with respect to class labels, and the implicit bias of the attention mechanism will be analyzed in terms of max-margin token selection.
83151d416be0785acc14993800a4523f8b1379e6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic data will be generated with controlled token importance levels, partitioning the vocabulary into irrelevant, positive, and negative tokens, and sampling sequences according to specified posterior distributions. Real-world experiments will use the IMDB and Yelp review datasets, with preprocessing steps including tokenization, removal of infrequent tokens, and conversion of multi-class labels to binary sentiment. Models will be trained until convergence using gradient descent, and both one-layer and two-layer attention architectures (with skip connections and layer normalization) will be evaluated. Evaluation metrics will include the alignment (dot-product) between token embeddings and both the ⟨cls⟩ embedding and the regression vector, as a function of token-wise posterior differences. Visualizations will be used to assess the correlation between learned embeddings and empirical token importance.
83151d416be0785acc14993800a4523f8b1379e6.novelty_claims: The proposed research provides a theoretical characterization of how attention-based models with trained embeddings select important tokens based on empirical data statistics, specifically after only a single gradient step and at convergence. The analysis demonstrates that the learned embeddings encode token importance proportional to their frequency and label correlation, and that the ⟨cls⟩ embedding converges to a max-margin solution for token selection. The work extends prior analyses by jointly considering the training dynamics of both context and ⟨cls⟩ embeddings, and establishes sufficient conditions under which only important tokens are selected. Experimental results on both synthetic and real-world datasets validate the theoretical predictions and suggest that the findings generalize beyond the analyzed one-layer architecture.

8317ced5bedaad535b6a7fef29ef2cfabbed3f80.title: How Efficient is LLM-Generated Code? A Rigorous & High-Standard Benchmark
8317ced5bedaad535b6a7fef29ef2cfabbed3f80.research_question: How can the efficiency of code generated by large language models (LLMs) be rigorously and comprehensively evaluated, beyond functional correctness, and what are the current capabilities and limitations of LLMs in generating expert-level efficient code?
8317ced5bedaad535b6a7fef29ef2cfabbed3f80.hypothesis: Current large language models are significantly less capable of generating expert-level efficient code compared to human experts, particularly in tasks requiring advanced algorithm design and implementation optimization. A rigorous, high-standard benchmark and evaluation framework will reveal these deficiencies and provide actionable insights for future model development.
8317ced5bedaad535b6a7fef29ef2cfabbed3f80.proposed_method: A new benchmark, ENAMEL (EfficieNcy AutoMatic EvaLuator), will be developed to rigorously evaluate the efficiency of LLM-generated code. The methodology includes: (1) defining a novel efficiency metric, eff@k, which generalizes the pass@k metric to efficiency and properly handles right-censored execution times using a robust, unbiased, and variance-reduced estimator via Rao–Blackwellization; (2) curating a problem set of 142 diverse programming tasks (excluding trivial cases) from HumanEval and HumanEval+ to cover a wide range of algorithmic difficulties; (3) employing human experts to design and implement the most efficient reference solutions for each problem, ensuring the highest standard for efficiency comparison; and (4) developing strong, expert-curated test case generators that include both corner and worst-case scenarios to rigorously filter out incorrect or suboptimal code. The evaluation framework will use a level-based system to differentiate code samples by efficiency across varying input scales.
8317ced5bedaad535b6a7fef29ef2cfabbed3f80.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 30 popular LLMs using the ENAMEL benchmark. Each model will be evaluated on the curated set of 142 problems, with multiple code samples generated per problem. Efficiency will be measured using the eff@k metric at various sample sizes (k=1, 10, 100), and results will be compared against expert-written reference solutions. Baselines will include existing benchmarks such as HumanEval and HumanEval+, with metrics such as pass@k and eff@k reported for all models. Subsets of the problem set will be used to specifically analyze algorithm design and implementation optimization capabilities. Evaluation will be performed using strong, expert-written test case generators to ensure correctness and to distinguish between naive and advanced solutions.
8317ced5bedaad535b6a7fef29ef2cfabbed3f80.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a rigorous, high-standard benchmark for code efficiency evaluation that addresses several previously unaddressed challenges: (1) a novel, robust efficiency metric (eff@k) with an unbiased, variance-reduced estimator that properly handles right-censored execution times and sample size effects; (2) expert-designed reference solutions that set a new standard for efficiency comparison, often surpassing canonical dataset solutions; (3) strong, expert-curated test case generators that rigorously filter out incorrect and suboptimal code, including non-trivial corner and worst cases; and (4) a comprehensive, level-based evaluation framework that enables fine-grained differentiation of code efficiency across a wide spectrum of problem difficulties. This benchmark enables a more accurate and actionable assessment of LLMs' capabilities in generating efficient code, highlighting current limitations and guiding future improvements.

83245afa59b9030f6149a954408660872b738fc6.title: On the Convergence Rates of Policy Gradient Methods
83245afa59b9030f6149a954408660872b738fc6.research_question: What are the convergence rates of policy gradient and policy mirror descent methods in infinite-horizon discounted Markov decision problems with finite state and action spaces, and how can these rates be improved or characterized under various algorithmic choices and assumptions?
83245afa59b9030f6149a954408660872b738fc6.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by leveraging structural properties of Markov decision processes and developing new theoretical frameworks such as weak gradient-mapping dominance, sharper sublinear and even linear convergence rates for policy gradient and policy mirror descent methods can be achieved, potentially without the need for strong convexity-inducing regularization.
83245afa59b9030f6149a954408660872b738fc6.proposed_method: A systematic theoretical investigation will be conducted on policy gradient and policy mirror descent methods with direct policy parametrization for infinite-horizon discounted Markov decision problems. The approach will first develop a theory of weak gradient-mapping dominance for general nonconvex composite optimization, which will be applied to analyze the projected policy gradient method and derive improved sublinear convergence rates. Subsequently, a general class of policy mirror descent methods—including natural policy gradient and projected Q-descent—will be studied, with a focus on the effect of step size schedules. In particular, the use of geometrically increasing step sizes will be analyzed to establish conditions under which linear convergence can be achieved without relying on entropy or other strongly convex regularization. The methodology will also extend to inexact variants of policy mirror descent, quantifying the impact of gradient or Q-function estimation errors on convergence and sample complexity.
83245afa59b9030f6149a954408660872b738fc6.experiment_details: Theoretical results will be validated through rigorous mathematical analysis, with empirical experiments conducted on standard tabular Markov decision process benchmarks. Experiments will compare the proposed variants of projected policy gradient and policy mirror descent methods under different step size regimes, including constant and geometrically increasing step sizes. Baselines will include classical projected policy gradient, natural policy gradient, and policy iteration algorithms. Evaluation metrics will focus on convergence rate (sublinear vs. linear), iteration complexity, and sample complexity, measured as the number of iterations or samples required to reach a specified suboptimality threshold in the value function. Additional analysis will examine the dependence of convergence rates on problem parameters such as the discount factor, state and action space cardinalities, and distribution mismatch coefficients.
83245afa59b9030f6149a954408660872b738fc6.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new theory of weak gradient-mapping dominance for nonconvex composite optimization, enabling sharper O(1/k) convergence rates for projected policy gradient methods in Markov decision processes. It further establishes that a general class of policy mirror descent methods, including natural policy gradient and projected Q-descent, can achieve linear convergence rates with geometrically increasing step sizes, without requiring entropy or strongly convex regularization. The analysis extends to inexact methods, providing novel sample complexity bounds and demonstrating robustness to estimation errors. These contributions advance the theoretical understanding of policy optimization and offer new algorithmic insights for reinforcement learning.

8325b4761dc062a4ff382253e9864333237913db.title: Generalizable Motion Planning via Operator Learning
8325b4761dc062a4ff382253e9864333237913db.research_question: How can motion planning value functions be efficiently and accurately approximated in a way that generalizes across different environments, resolutions, and goal positions, while enabling fast and scalable planning in high-dimensional and complex spaces?
8325b4761dc062a4ff382253e9864333237913db.hypothesis: A neural operator-based approach, specifically designed to approximate the solution operator of the Eikonal PDE for motion planning, can achieve resolution invariance, generalization across diverse environments and goal positions, and provide efficient, accurate value function predictions that can be used both for direct planning and as effective heuristics in classical algorithms.
