8325b4761dc062a4ff382253e9864333237913db.proposed_method: A novel neural operator architecture, termed the Planning Neural Operator (PNO), is developed to approximate the infinite-dimensional solution operator of the Eikonal PDE governing motion planning value functions. The architecture leverages a resolution-invariant Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) backbone, with key extensions: (1) explicit hard encoding of obstacle geometries into the operator layers via a smoothed indicator function derived from a signed distance field (SDF), (2) a projection (output) layer with an inductive bias enforcing the triangle inequality to ensure generalization across arbitrary goal positions, and (3) a PINN-inspired loss function to encourage PDE consistency. The SDF itself is generated by a separately trained FNO, and both the binary occupancy map and SDF are used as inputs. The architecture is designed to allow training on coarse resolutions and deployment at much finer super-resolutions, and to generalize to unseen environments without retraining.
8325b4761dc062a4ff382253e9864333237913db.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted across four main settings: (1) grid-world environments, comparing PNO to learning-based planners (VIN, IEF2D) on success rate and computation time; (2) super-resolution evaluation on the Moving AI 2D city dataset, where PNO is trained on synthetic 64x64 maps and tested on real-world maps up to 1024x1024, with comparisons to FNO and DAFNO baselines on value function error and computational speed; (3) 3D planning in iGibson environments, where PNO is compared to NTFields, P-NTFields, and FMM on value function accuracy and planning performance, including generalization to unseen environments; (4) 4-DOF robotic manipulator planning, evaluating PNO's ability to learn value functions in high-dimensional configuration spaces. Evaluation metrics include relative L2 error of value function prediction, path optimality, number of nodes expanded in A* planning, and computational time. Additionally, the use of PNO-generated value functions as heuristics in A* is tested, including an ablation with obstacle erosion to ensure admissibility and consistency.
8325b4761dc062a4ff382253e9864333237913db.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a generalizable, resolution-invariant neural operator architecture for motion planning value function approximation, capable of zero-shot super-resolution and generalization across unseen environments and goal positions. The method hard-encodes obstacle geometries and enforces the triangle inequality in the value function, enabling both direct planning and use as an efficient, theoretically justified (ϵ-consistent) heuristic in classical planners. Empirical results demonstrate substantial speedups (up to 10x) over numerical PDE solvers, improved accuracy and generalization compared to state-of-the-art neural and operator learning baselines, and a 33% reduction in nodes expanded in A* planning while maintaining near-optimal paths.

8342b592fe238f3d230e4959b06fd10153c45db1.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
8342b592fe238f3d230e4959b06fd10153c45db1.research_question: What is the optimal allocation of model size and number of training tokens for training large transformer language models under a fixed compute budget, and how does this allocation impact downstream performance and efficiency?
8342b592fe238f3d230e4959b06fd10153c45db1.hypothesis: For a fixed compute budget, the optimal performance of large language models is achieved when model size and the number of training tokens are scaled equally, rather than prioritizing model size as in previous approaches.
8342b592fe238f3d230e4959b06fd10153c45db1.proposed_method: A systematic empirical investigation will be conducted by training over 400 transformer language models with varying parameter counts (from 70 million to over 16 billion) and training token counts (from 5 billion to over 400 billion). Three complementary approaches will be employed: (1) fixing model sizes and varying the number of training tokens to identify the minimal loss per compute, (2) constructing IsoFLOP profiles by varying model size for a fixed compute budget and determining the optimal parameter count, and (3) fitting a parametric loss function to model the relationship between final loss, model size, and number of training tokens. Power-law relationships between compute, model size, and data will be estimated to derive the compute-optimal scaling laws. The findings will be validated by training a compute-optimal model (e.g., a 70B parameter model trained on 1.4T tokens) and comparing its performance to larger, less data-rich models.
8342b592fe238f3d230e4959b06fd10153c45db1.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training a large grid of transformer models on the MassiveText dataset, with additional analyses on C4 and GitHub code datasets to confirm generality. Models will be trained using cosine learning rate schedules matched to the number of training tokens, with optimizer and tokenizer variations explored for optimal performance. The compute-optimal model (e.g., Chinchilla) will be evaluated on a comprehensive suite of language modeling and downstream tasks, including The Pile, WikiText-103, MMLU, BIG-bench, and various reading comprehension and question answering benchmarks. Baselines for comparison will include Gopher (280B), GPT-3 (175B), Jurassic-1 (178B), and Megatron-Turing NLG (530B). Evaluation metrics will include bits-per-byte, perplexity, and accuracy on downstream tasks, with particular attention to state-of-the-art benchmarks such as MMLU.
8342b592fe238f3d230e4959b06fd10153c45db1.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new empirical scaling law for large language model training, demonstrating that model size and number of training tokens should be scaled equally for compute-optimal performance, in contrast to previous recommendations that favored increasing model size disproportionately. The methodology leverages extensive empirical data from hundreds of model training runs and introduces multiple analytical approaches for robust estimation. The resulting compute-optimal models are shown to outperform much larger models on a wide range of tasks while being significantly more efficient in terms of inference and fine-tuning compute, thereby advancing both the performance and accessibility of large language models.

835d157e2c23d3577f23778ce051ab8d706babf6.title: TagFog: Textual Anchor Guidance and Fake Outlier Generation for Visual Out-of-Distribution Detection
835d157e2c23d3577f23778ce051ab8d706babf6.research_question: How can visual out-of-distribution (OOD) detection be improved by leveraging both synthetic OOD data and enhanced semantic representations of in-distribution (ID) classes?
835d157e2c23d3577f23778ce051ab8d706babf6.hypothesis: Integrating simple, patch-level synthetic OOD data with semantically rich textual embeddings of ID classes as training guidance will enable the image encoder to learn more compact and discriminative representations, thereby improving OOD detection performance over existing methods.
835d157e2c23d3577f23778ce051ab8d706babf6.proposed_method: A novel learning framework is proposed that combines two main components: (1) Fake Outlier Generation (FOG), where synthetic OOD images are created by applying Jigsaw transformations (randomly shuffling image patches) to ID training images, resulting in images that are locally similar but globally semantically shifted from the originals; and (2) Textual Anchor Guidance (TAG), where ChatGPT is used to generate detailed textual descriptions for each ID class, and these descriptions are encoded using a pretrained, frozen CLIP text encoder to serve as semantic 'anchors.' The image encoder is trained with a combination of cross-entropy loss (for (K+1)-class classification including fake OOD), a contrastive loss aligning projected image features with their class-specific textual anchors, and a supervised contrastive loss encouraging separation between ID and fake OOD embeddings. The projection module maps image features into the semantic embedding space, and all components are jointly optimized.
835d157e2c23d3577f23778ce051ab8d706babf6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard OOD detection benchmarks, including CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and two ImageNet100 splits (ImageNet100-I and ImageNet100-II), with a variety of OOD test sets such as SVHN, LSUN, iSUN, Textures, Places365, and others. Model backbones will include ResNet18, ResNet34, ResNet50, and ResNet101. Baselines for comparison will encompass both post-hoc (e.g., MSP, ODIN, Energy, ViM, DICE, ReAct) and training-based (e.g., VOS, LogitNorm, CIDER) OOD detection methods. Evaluation metrics will include AUROC (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve) and FPR95 (false positive rate at 95% true positive rate). The experimental setup involves generating 1-4 fake OOD images per ID image, using standard data augmentations, and training up to 200 epochs with SGD. Ablation studies will assess the contribution of each component, and the framework's compatibility with various post-hoc OOD scoring methods will be evaluated.
835d157e2c23d3577f23778ce051ab8d706babf6.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to combine Jigsaw-based synthetic OOD data generation with ChatGPT-enhanced textual anchor guidance for training visual OOD detectors. It introduces a simple yet effective approach to generating challenging fake OOD samples without complex generative models or unrealistic assumptions. The use of rich, descriptive class semantics from large language models as training anchors is novel in this context, and the method is shown to flexibly integrate with existing post-hoc OOD detection strategies. Extensive experiments demonstrate new state-of-the-art performance on multiple OOD detection benchmarks, with significant improvements over prior methods.

839794f7d0755a0205e76fcbeeaa6f2c01c8e52f.title: Local Algorithms for Estimating Effective Resistance
839794f7d0755a0205e76fcbeeaa6f2c01c8e52f.research_question: Can effective resistance between pairs of vertices in massive graphs be efficiently estimated using local algorithms that only explore a small portion of the graph, while maintaining provable accuracy guarantees?
839794f7d0755a0205e76fcbeeaa6f2c01c8e52f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that local algorithms based on random walks, Laplacian pseudo-inverse approximations, commute times, and spanning tree counts can estimate pairwise effective resistance with arbitrarily small additive error, provided the underlying graph has bounded mixing time.
839794f7d0755a0205e76fcbeeaa6f2c01c8e52f.proposed_method: A suite of local algorithms will be developed for estimating the effective resistance between any two specified vertices in a graph. The first class of algorithms will approximate the Laplacian pseudo-inverse using truncated Neumann series and Monte Carlo estimation of random walk transition probabilities, leveraging the relationship between effective resistance and random walks. An alternative approach will use collision-based estimators to further accelerate the estimation of transition probabilities. Additional algorithms will exploit the connection between effective resistance and commute times, as well as the probability of visiting a target before returning to the source in random walks, to provide Monte Carlo estimators for resistance. Finally, a method based on the ratio of the number of spanning trees in the original graph and in the graph with two vertices identified will be implemented, using sublinear-time spanning tree estimation algorithms. All algorithms will operate under the adjacency list model, with access to degree, neighbor, and uniform vertex sampling queries.
839794f7d0755a0205e76fcbeeaa6f2c01c8e52f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large benchmark graph datasets, including Facebook, DBLP, and YouTube networks, with sizes ranging from thousands to over a million nodes and millions of edges. For each dataset, 1,000 vertex pairs will be sampled (typically edges), and the effective resistance for each pair will be estimated using the proposed local algorithms. Baseline methods will include exact computation via Laplacian decomposition and state-of-the-art spanning tree sampling methods. Evaluation metrics will include running time, query complexity, and relative error of the estimated resistance compared to the ground truth. The experiments will be run on a high-memory Linux server, and the accuracy and efficiency of the algorithms will be validated across all datasets.
839794f7d0755a0205e76fcbeeaa6f2c01c8e52f.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first comprehensive suite of local algorithms for estimating effective resistance between arbitrary vertex pairs in general graphs with provable additive error guarantees. The algorithms achieve sublinear running time and query complexity for graphs with bounded mixing time, a property common in real-world networks. The methods extend beyond prior work by supporting general graphs (not just regular expanders), providing multiple algorithmic strategies (random walk-based, collision-based, commute time-based, and spanning tree-based), and demonstrating empirical speedups of 10^5 to 10^6 times over existing polynomial-time methods while maintaining high accuracy. The research systematically analyzes the theoretical limits and practical performance of local resistance estimation, filling a significant gap in scalable graph analytics.

83991e8da386c581396aed9134fe8a470cec3f8a.title: Spatial-frequency channels, shape bias, and adversarial robustness
83991e8da386c581396aed9134fe8a470cec3f8a.research_question: What spatial frequency information is used by humans and neural networks for object recognition, and how do differences in spatial-frequency channel properties relate to shape bias and adversarial robustness in artificial vision systems?
83991e8da386c581396aed9134fe8a470cec3f8a.hypothesis: Neural networks utilize broader spatial-frequency channels than humans for object recognition, and this difference in channel properties is associated with differences in shape bias and adversarial robustness. Narrowing the spatial-frequency channel of neural networks may improve their robustness and alignment with human vision.
83991e8da386c581396aed9134fe8a470cec3f8a.proposed_method: A critical band masking paradigm will be employed to systematically compare the spatial-frequency channels used by humans and neural networks during object recognition. Grayscale images from a 16-class subset of ImageNet will be contrast-reduced and perturbed with Gaussian noise, filtered into octave-wide spatial-frequency bands at multiple center frequencies and noise strengths. Human participants and a diverse set of pretrained neural networks will perform 16-way categorization tasks on these noise-masked images. For each observer (human or network), categorization accuracy will be measured across all noise conditions, and threshold noise levels for 50% accuracy will be determined for each spatial-frequency band. A Gaussian function will be fit to these thresholds to characterize each observer's spatial-frequency channel in terms of center frequency, bandwidth (in octaves), and peak noise sensitivity.
83991e8da386c581396aed9134fe8a470cec3f8a.experiment_details: Experiments will use a fixed set of 1100 grayscale, contrast-reduced images from the 16-class ImageNet subset, with images equally distributed across categories and noise conditions (combinations of 5 noise strengths and 7 spatial-frequency bands). Fourteen human participants will complete the categorization task online, and 76 pretrained neural networks (spanning CNNs, transformers, adversarially-trained models, and others) will be evaluated on the same task. Baseline comparisons will include human performance, standard ImageNet-trained networks, and adversarially-trained networks. Evaluation metrics will include categorization accuracy per noise condition, spatial-frequency channel parameters (bandwidth, center frequency, peak noise sensitivity), shape bias (measured on cue-conflict images), and adversarial robustness (whitebox accuracy using PGD attacks). Statistical analyses will assess correlations between channel properties, shape bias, and robustness.
83991e8da386c581396aed9134fe8a470cec3f8a.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the critical band masking paradigm as a systematic, frequency-based tool for direct comparison of human and neural network object recognition. It will provide the first detailed characterization of spatial-frequency channels in both humans and a large, representative sample of modern neural networks on naturalistic object recognition. The study will reveal that neural networks generally use spatial-frequency channels much broader than those of humans, and will demonstrate strong correlations between channel properties, shape bias, and adversarial robustness. The findings suggest a new direction for improving network robustness by narrowing their spatial-frequency channels to more closely match those of humans.

83ac79bb8e8695fb3c3c024be74790d862adea74.title: TEMPO: Prompt-based Generative Pre-trained Transformer for Time Series Forecasting
83ac79bb8e8695fb3c3c024be74790d862adea74.research_question: Can a prompt-based generative pre-trained transformer framework be developed to improve generalization and accuracy in time series forecasting, especially in zero-shot and multimodal settings, by leveraging the unique properties of time series data across diverse domains?
83ac79bb8e8695fb3c3c024be74790d862adea74.hypothesis: Incorporating explicit decomposition of time series into trend, seasonality, and residual components, combined with a prompt-based adaptation strategy within a generative pre-trained transformer, will significantly enhance forecasting accuracy and generalization, particularly in zero-shot and multimodal scenarios, compared to existing state-of-the-art models.
83ac79bb8e8695fb3c3c024be74790d862adea74.proposed_method: A novel framework will be designed that integrates statistical decomposition of time series data into trend, seasonality, and residual components using locally weighted scatterplot smoothing (STL). Each component will be normalized and embedded separately, with learnable parameters aligning local and global decompositions via a reconstruction loss. A semi-soft prompt strategy will be introduced, generating distinct prompts for each time series component and concatenating them with the corresponding embeddings. These enriched representations will be input into a decoder-based generative pre-trained transformer (GPT), where the model is adapted using Low-Rank Adaptation (LORA) for efficient fine-tuning. The final prediction will be the additive combination of the outputs for each component, and a generalized additive model (GAM) will be used to interpret the contributions of each component to the forecast.
83ac79bb8e8695fb3c3c024be74790d862adea74.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a broad suite of benchmark time series datasets spanning electricity, traffic, climate, news, and finance (e.g., ETTh1, ETTh2, ETTm1, ETTm2, Electricity, Traffic, Weather, GDELT, and the newly proposed TETS dataset). The evaluation will focus on zero-shot transfer learning, where the model is pre-trained on multiple source datasets and tested on unseen target datasets. Baselines will include pre-trained language models (BERT, GPT2, T5, LLaMA), transformer-based time series models (PatchTST, FEDformer, ETSformer, Informer), linear models (DLinear), and 2D-variation models (TimesNet). Metrics such as Mean Squared Error (MSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error (SMAPE) will be reported. Additional experiments will evaluate the integration of contextual (textual) information and conduct ablation studies to assess the impact of decomposition and prompt components.
83ac79bb8e8695fb3c3c024be74790d862adea74.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a prompt-based generative pre-trained transformer architecture specifically tailored for time series forecasting, leveraging explicit decomposition into trend, seasonality, and residual components. The semi-soft prompt design enables dynamic adaptation to diverse time series distributions and multimodal inputs. The approach is claimed to achieve superior zero-shot forecasting performance and generalizability across domains, and provides interpretability through a generalized additive model and SHAP analysis. The introduction of the TETS dataset further advances research in multimodal time series forecasting.

83b465e220132c5dd6bc2bdc93b077c8760c4975.title: Sample-efficient Multi-objective Molecular Optimization with GFlowNets
83b465e220132c5dd6bc2bdc93b077c8760c4975.research_question: How can sample-efficient multi-objective optimization be achieved for molecular design in discrete chemical spaces, particularly when candidate diversity and limited oracle evaluations are critical constraints?
83b465e220132c5dd6bc2bdc93b077c8760c4975.hypothesis: A hypernetwork-based generative flow network (HN-GFN), when integrated as an acquisition function optimizer within a multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) framework and enhanced with a hindsight-like off-policy strategy, will enable efficient sampling of diverse, high-quality molecular candidates from the approximate Pareto front, outperforming existing methods in candidate quality and sample efficiency.
83b465e220132c5dd6bc2bdc93b077c8760c4975.proposed_method: A novel MOBO algorithm will be developed that employs a hypernetwork-based GFlowNet (HN-GFN) as the acquisition function optimizer. The HN-GFN will be conditioned on preference vectors, allowing it to flexibly sample molecular candidates according to various trade-offs between multiple objectives. The conditioning will be implemented via a hypernetwork that generates the weights of the prediction heads in the GFlowNet based on the input preference vector, while sharing the main message passing neural network (MPNN) backbone for state representation. To further enhance learning efficiency, a hindsight-like off-policy strategy will be introduced, enabling the sharing of high-performing molecules across different preference vectors by maintaining replay buffers and re-examining trajectories under alternative preferences. The surrogate model for property prediction will utilize evidential deep learning to estimate both mean and uncertainty, and the acquisition function will use an upper confidence bound (UCB) applied to scalarizations of the objectives.
83b465e220132c5dd6bc2bdc93b077c8760c4975.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in both synthetic and practical multi-objective molecular optimization scenarios. In the synthetic setting, the ability of HN-GFN to generalize across preference vectors will be evaluated by directly optimizing scalarized oracle scores for two objectives (e.g., GSK3β and JNK3 inhibition), with metrics including hypervolume, diversity (Tanimoto distance), and correlation between sampling probability and reward. In practical MOBO scenarios, real-world molecular optimization tasks involving combinations of objectives (e.g., GSK3β + JNK3, and GSK3β + JNK3 + QED + SA) will be addressed, starting from a random initial dataset and proceeding through multiple rounds of batch optimization with limited oracle calls. Baselines will include latent space optimization methods (qParEGO, qEHVI, LaMOO), combinatorial optimization methods (GraphGA, MARS, P-MOCO), and alternative GFlowNet conditioning mechanisms (Concat-GFN, FiLM-GFN, PS-GFN). Evaluation will focus on hypervolume, candidate diversity, and sample efficiency, with ablation studies on the effects of the hindsight strategy, Dirichlet prior, and scalarization functions.
83b465e220132c5dd6bc2bdc93b077c8760c4975.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first unified hypernetwork-based GFlowNet for sample-efficient multi-objective molecular optimization, capable of generalizing across a distribution of preference vectors and efficiently sampling from the approximate Pareto front. The hindsight-like off-policy strategy enables effective sharing of high-performing candidates among policies, significantly accelerating learning. This framework achieves superior candidate quality and diversity compared to state-of-the-art baselines, and demonstrates robust generalization and sample efficiency in both synthetic and real-world settings.

83b90f4a0ae4cc214eb3cc140ccfef9cd99fac05.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
83b90f4a0ae4cc214eb3cc140ccfef9cd99fac05.research_question: How can memory management for large language model (LLM) serving be improved to maximize throughput and minimize memory waste, particularly in the management of key-value (KV) cache under dynamic and complex serving workloads?
83b90f4a0ae4cc214eb3cc140ccfef9cd99fac05.hypothesis: A memory management framework inspired by virtual memory and paging, when integrated with a novel attention algorithm, will significantly reduce memory fragmentation and duplication in LLM serving, enabling higher batch sizes and throughput without compromising latency or model accuracy.
83b90f4a0ae4cc214eb3cc140ccfef9cd99fac05.proposed_method: A new attention algorithm, PagedAttention, will be developed to partition the key-value (KV) cache of each sequence into fixed-size blocks (KV blocks), allowing these blocks to be stored in non-contiguous memory locations. This approach enables flexible, on-demand allocation and deallocation of KV cache memory, analogous to virtual memory paging in operating systems. A serving system, vLLM, will be built on top of PagedAttention, featuring a centralized scheduler, a KV cache manager, and distributed GPU workers. The KV cache manager will maintain block tables mapping logical to physical KV blocks, support memory sharing via reference counting and copy-on-write mechanisms, and facilitate efficient memory management for various decoding algorithms (e.g., parallel sampling, beam search, shared prefixes). The system will also implement scheduling and preemption strategies, including swapping and recomputation for handling memory overflows, and support distributed execution across multiple GPUs.
83b90f4a0ae4cc214eb3cc140ccfef9cd99fac05.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using popular LLMs such as OPT (13B, 66B, 175B parameters) and LLaMA (13B), deployed on NVIDIA A100 GPUs in various configurations (single and multi-GPU setups). Workloads will be synthesized from real-world datasets like ShareGPT and Alpaca, which exhibit diverse input and output length distributions. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art systems such as FasterTransformer and Orca, with multiple memory allocation strategies (oracle, power-of-two, and maximum pre-allocation). Evaluation metrics will focus on serving throughput (normalized latency per output token), batch size, memory utilization, and scalability under different request rates. The experiments will also assess the impact of block size, memory sharing in complex decoding scenarios, and the effectiveness of swapping versus recomputation for preemption.
83b90f4a0ae4cc214eb3cc140ccfef9cd99fac05.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel attention algorithm, PagedAttention, that enables non-contiguous, paged memory management for the KV cache in LLM serving. This design eliminates most internal and external memory fragmentation, supports fine-grained memory sharing across requests and decoding strategies, and achieves near-zero memory waste. The vLLM system is the first to co-design memory management and attention computation at this granularity, enabling substantial improvements in throughput (2-4× over existing systems) without sacrificing latency or accuracy. The method is broadly applicable to various LLM architectures, decoding algorithms, and distributed settings.

83dbd3fb34bf3ca6dde302c1b46d39fae8018b03.title: Learning Latent Variable Models via Jarzynski-adjusted Langevin Algorithm
83dbd3fb34bf3ca6dde302c1b46d39fae8018b03.research_question: How can latent variable models be efficiently and accurately trained, particularly with respect to maximum marginal likelihood estimation, in a way that enables both scalable inference and reliable model selection?
83dbd3fb34bf3ca6dde302c1b46d39fae8018b03.hypothesis: A sequential Monte Carlo method based on a Jarzynski-adjusted Langevin algorithm, which incorporates nonequilibrium statistical mechanics corrections into Langevin-based particle dynamics, will enable efficient, accurate, and scalable maximum marginal likelihood estimation for latent variable models, while also facilitating on-the-fly marginal likelihood computation for model selection.
83dbd3fb34bf3ca6dde302c1b46d39fae8018b03.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces a Jarzynski-adjusted Langevin algorithm (JALA) for sampling from time-varying probability distributions by running unadjusted Langevin dynamics and correcting for the resulting bias using an exponentially weighted Jarzynski factor. This sampler is embedded within a sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) framework, where a population of particles evolves according to the unadjusted Langevin algorithm, and their weights are recursively updated to account for nonequilibrium effects. The core of the approach is the JALA-EM algorithm, which uses the weighted particle system to estimate the gradient of the marginal likelihood with respect to model parameters. These gradient estimates are then used within a generic first-order optimizer, such as stochastic gradient descent, to iteratively update the model parameters. The method also includes mechanisms for resampling based on effective sample size to mitigate weight degeneracy and ensure robust particle diversity throughout the optimization process.
83dbd3fb34bf3ca6dde302c1b46d39fae8018b03.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a variety of latent variable models, including Bayesian logistic regression (using the Wisconsin Breast Cancer dataset), Bayesian regression with model and error selection, model order selection in polynomial regression, and Bayesian neural networks for classification tasks (e.g., MNIST digit classification). Baselines for comparison include Particle Gradient Descent (PGD) and Stochastic Optimization via Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm (SOUL), with algorithm-specific step-sizes tuned via cross-validation. Evaluation metrics include Log Pointwise Predictive Density (LPPD), test error, and marginal likelihood estimates for model selection, with experiments designed to assess both parameter estimation accuracy and computational efficiency (e.g., fixed wall-clock time constraints). The proposed method is also evaluated on its ability to maintain posterior fidelity with varying numbers of particles and its robustness in model selection scenarios, with repeated trials to assess statistical reliability.
83dbd3fb34bf3ca6dde302c1b46d39fae8018b03.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel integration of nonequilibrium statistical mechanics (via Jarzynski's equality) into Langevin-based SMC sampling for latent variable models, enabling unbiased and scalable estimation of marginal likelihood gradients. The JALA-EM algorithm uniquely allows for recursive and on-the-fly estimation of marginal likelihoods, a feature uncommon among scalable inference methods and particularly valuable for model selection. Theoretical contributions include a nonasymptotic convergence analysis under general regularity conditions, extending to settings with biased gradient estimators and allowing for flexible optimization schemes. Empirical results claim improved or comparable accuracy and efficiency relative to state-of-the-art baselines, with enhanced robustness in low-particle regimes and superior model selection capabilities.

840f759d110aea21ebbfe0523c435e11a2759aba.title: Flora: Low-Rank Adapters Are Secretly Gradient Compressors
840f759d110aea21ebbfe0523c435e11a2759aba.research_question: How can memory usage for optimization states in training large neural networks be significantly reduced without sacrificing model performance, and can the limitations of low-rank adaptation methods be overcome to allow for high-rank updates with sublinear memory complexity?
840f759d110aea21ebbfe0523c435e11a2759aba.hypothesis: Random projection-based compression and decompression of gradients, with resampling of projection matrices, enables high-rank parameter updates while achieving sublinear memory usage for optimization states, thereby matching or exceeding the performance of full-rank methods and outperforming traditional low-rank adaptation techniques.
840f759d110aea21ebbfe0523c435e11a2759aba.proposed_method: A novel optimization technique, FLORA, will be developed that applies random projection to compress gradients during training. At each optimization step, a new random projection matrix is sampled, compressing the gradient into a lower-dimensional space, and then decompressing it for parameter updates. This resampling avoids the low-rank constraint inherent in methods like LoRA, enabling high-rank updates while maintaining sublinear memory complexity for storing optimization states such as gradient accumulation and momentum. The method will be implemented for both arithmetic mean (gradient accumulation) and exponential moving average (momentum) scenarios, with efficient memory management via projection matrix seeds and buffer reuse. Technical implementation will include integration with existing optimizers (e.g., Adafactor), and the approach will be evaluated on both gradient accumulation and momentum compression.
840f759d110aea21ebbfe0523c435e11a2759aba.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of tasks and model architectures, including Transformer-based models such as T5 (small and 3B) and GPT-2 (base and XL), covering both summarization (XSum dataset) and translation (IWSLT17 De-En dataset) tasks. Evaluation metrics will include ROUGE scores for summarization and SacreBLEU for translation, with peak memory usage monitored using profiling tools. Baselines for comparison will include no accumulation/momentum, naive full-matrix accumulation/momentum, and LoRA with varying projection ranks. Hyperparameters such as projection rank and resampling interval will be systematically varied, and both fine-tuning and training-from-scratch scenarios will be explored. Additional experiments will test the method in linear-memory optimizers, on image tasks (e.g., ViT), and in combination with memory-saving techniques like activation checkpointing.
840f759d110aea21ebbfe0523c435e11a2759aba.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new interpretation of low-rank adaptation as a form of gradient compression via random projection, and extends this by resampling projection matrices to enable high-rank updates without increased memory cost. FLORA achieves sublinear memory usage for optimization states, surpassing the memory efficiency of existing methods such as LoRA, while also avoiding their performance limitations due to low-rank constraints. The method is orthogonal to and compatible with existing memory-efficient optimizers and can be combined with other memory-saving techniques. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate significant memory savings with maintained or improved model performance across diverse architectures and tasks.

84109e1235b725f4bb44a54bab8b493bd723fdd3.title: Towards General Text Embeddings with Multi-stage Contrastive Learning
84109e1235b725f4bb44a54bab8b493bd723fdd3.research_question: How can a general-purpose text embedding model be developed to achieve robust and high-quality representations across a diverse range of NLP and code-related tasks using only open-source data and scalable training strategies?
84109e1235b725f4bb44a54bab8b493bd723fdd3.hypothesis: A multi-stage contrastive learning framework, leveraging both large-scale unsupervised and supervised open-source datasets from diverse domains, will produce text embeddings that outperform existing models in generalization and task transfer, even with modest model sizes.
84109e1235b725f4bb44a54bab8b493bd723fdd3.proposed_method: A dual-stage contrastive learning approach will be implemented. In the first stage, unsupervised pre-training will be conducted using approximately 800 million weakly supervised text pairs mined from diverse open-source sources such as web pages, academic papers, QA forums, social media, knowledge bases, and code repositories. The model architecture will be a deep Transformer encoder (e.g., BERT), employing mean pooling over contextualized token representations to produce fixed-size embeddings. The contrastive objective will use an improved bidirectional InfoNCE loss with in-batch negatives, leveraging cosine similarity and a fixed temperature. In the second stage, supervised fine-tuning will be performed on about 3 million annotated text triples from a wide variety of tasks (e.g., retrieval, NLI, paraphrase, fact verification), incorporating hard negatives and ensuring both symmetric and asymmetric task coverage. Optimization strategies will include large batch sizes, mixed precision training, and advanced sampling techniques to balance data sources.
84109e1235b725f4bb44a54bab8b493bd723fdd3.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate the resulting models on several benchmarks: zero-shot text classification (e.g., SST-2), unsupervised text retrieval (BEIR benchmark with 15 datasets), the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB, 56 datasets across 7 task types), and code search (CodeSearchNet across 6 programming languages). Baselines will include BM25, SimCSE, Contriever, E5, GTR, Sentence-T5, InstructOR, OpenAI embedding APIs, and leading code retrievers like CodeBERT, GraphCodeBERT, UniXcoder, and CodeRetriever. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, nDCG@10, MAP, v-measure, average precision, and Spearman correlation, depending on the task. Ablation studies will be conducted to analyze the impact of model size, batch size, number of training datasets, and training stage composition, with all models trained and evaluated on standardized hardware and using consistent random seeds for reproducibility.
84109e1235b725f4bb44a54bab8b493bd723fdd3.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified, scalable framework for general-purpose text embeddings trained exclusively on open-source data, eliminating reliance on proprietary or in-house corpora. The multi-stage contrastive learning pipeline is designed to maximize generalization across tasks and domains, including code, without task-specific prompts or fine-tuning. The method claims state-of-the-art performance on MTEB and BEIR benchmarks at significantly lower model sizes compared to commercial and larger academic baselines, and demonstrates strong cross-task transfer, notably in code search, by treating code as text. The approach also provides a reproducible and efficient baseline for the research community, with comprehensive ablation analyses to guide future scaling and data mixture strategies.

8415db10a4e2354b7d57b75848f1485ce5d0e7ce.title: Laplace Redux - Effortless Bayesian Deep Learning
8415db10a4e2354b7d57b75848f1485ce5d0e7ce.research_question: Can a scalable, efficient, and easy-to-use Laplace approximation framework provide competitive Bayesian inference and uncertainty quantification for deep neural networks, while overcoming practical barriers to adoption in modern deep learning tasks and architectures?
8415db10a4e2354b7d57b75848f1485ce5d0e7ce.hypothesis: A practical and modular implementation of the Laplace approximation, leveraging recent advances in Hessian approximation and efficient software tooling, can deliver Bayesian neural network functionality with minimal computational overhead, competitive predictive uncertainty, and robust model selection, rivaling or surpassing more complex Bayesian deep learning methods.
8415db10a4e2354b7d57b75848f1485ce5d0e7ce.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed to apply the Laplace approximation to deep neural networks, supporting both post-hoc and online Bayesian inference. The method will locally approximate the posterior distribution of network weights as a Gaussian centered at the MAP estimate, with covariance given by the (possibly approximated) inverse Hessian of the loss. Multiple scalable Hessian approximations will be supported, including diagonal, Kronecker-factored (KFAC), and low-rank structures, allowing inference over all weights, subnetworks, or only the last layer. Hyperparameters, such as prior precision, will be tuned via marginal likelihood maximization or cross-validation, and several predictive distribution approximations (e.g., probit, Monte Carlo, Laplace bridge) will be implemented for both regression and classification tasks. The approach will be encapsulated in a modular PyTorch-based library, enabling effortless integration with existing models and extensibility to new architectures.
8415db10a4e2354b7d57b75848f1485ce5d0e7ce.experiment_details: Experiments will benchmark various Laplace approximation variants on standard image classification datasets (MNIST, FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10), evaluating in-distribution and out-of-distribution (OOD) performance, calibration, and robustness to dataset shift. Baselines will include MAP-trained networks, deep ensembles, mean-field variational Bayes, stochastic-gradient Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, and SWAG. Evaluation metrics will comprise accuracy, negative log-likelihood (NLL), expected calibration error (ECE), AUROC for OOD detection, and computational cost (wall-clock time and memory). Additional experiments will assess the method on realistic distribution shift benchmarks (WILDS), various architectures (including transformers), and continual learning scenarios (e.g., Permuted-MNIST), comparing against temperature scaling and other Bayesian continual learning baselines. Both post-hoc and online Laplace variants will be tested, with ablation studies on Hessian structure, subset of weights, and predictive approximations.
8415db10a4e2354b7d57b75848f1485ce5d0e7ce.novelty_claims: The proposed approach claims to dispel misconceptions about the Laplace approximation's practicality by demonstrating minimal computational overhead, competitive or superior uncertainty quantification, and robust model selection compared to state-of-the-art Bayesian deep learning methods. The method introduces a modular, extensible PyTorch library supporting all major scalable Laplace variants, enabling drop-in Bayesian inference for pre-trained and off-the-shelf models, including those with complex architectures. The framework provides principled hyperparameter tuning via marginal likelihood, supports a wide range of predictive approximations, and is validated across diverse tasks and modalities, including settings where other Bayesian methods are challenging to apply. The approach is positioned as an accessible, efficient, and strong baseline for Bayesian deep learning and uncertainty quantification.

843603e514f51d714e1498538460525d55577cf7.title: Bayesian Test-Time Adaptation for Vision-Language Models
843603e514f51d714e1498538460525d55577cf7.research_question: How can vision-language models be adapted in real-time to new and potentially out-of-distribution test data to improve zero-shot image classification accuracy and robustness, while maintaining high inference efficiency and low memory usage?
843603e514f51d714e1498538460525d55577cf7.hypothesis: Incorporating both likelihood and prior adaptation, by continuously updating class embeddings and class priors based on incoming test samples, will enable vision-language models to better handle distribution shifts and achieve superior prediction accuracy and efficiency compared to methods that adapt only likelihood or use fixed priors.
843603e514f51d714e1498538460525d55577cf7.proposed_method: A novel Bayesian Class Adaptation (BCA) framework is proposed for test-time adaptation of pre-trained vision-language models such as CLIP. The method initializes class embeddings using hand-crafted prompts and sets the prior for each class as a one-hot vector. For each incoming test image, its visual embedding is computed and the probability of belonging to each class is calculated using cosine similarity. Likelihood adaptation is performed by updating the most probable class embedding using a statistical mean update with the current visual embedding, conditioned on a threshold. Prior adaptation is achieved by updating the class prior using the posterior probability derived from the current sample, allowing the model to dynamically adjust its belief about class distributions in the test environment. Both updates are performed in an online, backpropagation-free manner, ensuring real-time adaptation and computational efficiency.
843603e514f51d714e1498538460525d55577cf7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two major benchmarks: the Out-of-Distribution (OOD) benchmark (including ImageNet-A, ImageNet-V2, ImageNet-R, and ImageNet-S) and the Cross Domain benchmark (including Aircraft, Caltech101, Cars, DTD, EuroSAT, Flower102, Food101, Pets, SUN397, and UCF101). Pre-trained CLIP models with ResNet-50 and ViT-B/16 backbones will be used. Baselines for comparison include both backpropagation-based and backpropagation-free test-time adaptation methods such as TPT, DiffTPT, C-TPT, TDA, MTA, PromptAlign, HisTPT, and Zero, as well as ablations of the proposed method (likelihood-only and prior-only adaptation). Evaluation metrics include top-1 classification accuracy, inference time, and memory usage. All experiments will be performed with batch size 1 to simulate real-time adaptation, and hyperparameters will be tuned for robustness.
843603e514f51d714e1498538460525d55577cf7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to jointly adapt both the likelihood and the prior in a Bayesian framework for test-time adaptation of vision-language models. Prior adaptation is introduced as a critical and previously overlooked component, enabling the model to dynamically adjust to evolving test distributions. The method is backpropagation-free, highly efficient in terms of inference speed and memory usage, and achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on both OOD and cross-domain benchmarks. The dual adaptation mechanism is shown to be complementary, providing robustness and superior generalization in real-world scenarios.

8443d3b607b3f30ace2449a4df1d55976dd16a37.title: SeRL: Self-Play Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Models with Limited Data
8443d3b607b3f30ace2449a4df1d55976dd16a37.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be effectively trained to improve their reasoning abilities in scenarios where only limited high-quality instruction data and verifiable rewards are available?
8443d3b607b3f30ace2449a4df1d55976dd16a37.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a self-play reinforcement learning framework, incorporating autonomous instruction generation and self-rewarding mechanisms, can enable LLMs to achieve performance comparable to models trained with extensive high-quality data and verifiable rewards, even in data-scarce environments.
8443d3b607b3f30ace2449a4df1d55976dd16a37.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a Self-play Reinforcement Learning (SeRL) framework for LLMs, consisting of two core modules: self-instruction and self-rewarding. The self-instruction module iteratively generates new instructions using few-shot prompting, where prompts are constructed from both the initial dataset and previously generated instructions to match the evolving model capabilities. A robust online filtering strategy is applied to generated instructions, discarding those that are too similar to existing data, contain irrelevant content, are of inappropriate length, or are of unsuitable difficulty, as measured by majority answer agreement. The self-rewarding module estimates response rewards using a majority-voting mechanism: for each instruction, multiple responses are sampled, and the most common answer is selected as the reference; each response receives a reward of 1 if it matches the majority answer, and 0 otherwise. This eliminates the need for external annotations or verifiable labels. The framework performs standard reinforcement learning (e.g., using Reinforce++) on the generated and filtered data, enabling iterative self-improvement.
8443d3b607b3f30ace2449a4df1d55976dd16a37.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct and Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct as LLM backbones. The initial training data will be limited to 500 instructions sampled from the MATH dataset to simulate data-scarce conditions. The method will be evaluated on five math-specific benchmarks (MATH-500, MATH-Hard, ASDiv, College Math, TabMWP) and the general-purpose MMLU-Pro benchmark. Baseline comparisons will include Iterative RPO (I-RPO), Self-Rewarding DPO (SR-DPO), and RL with ground-truth rewards (RL-GT). Evaluation metrics will include Pass@1 accuracy and cosine similarity between estimated and ground-truth rewards. Multiple RL algorithms (Reinforce++, RLOO, GRPO) will be tested for robustness. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the online filtering and self-rewarding mechanisms.
8443d3b607b3f30ace2449a4df1d55976dd16a37.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is novel in enabling unsupervised, iterative reinforcement learning for LLMs in data-scarce scenarios without reliance on external annotations or verifiable rewards. The self-instruction module adaptively generates high-quality, diverse, and appropriately difficult instructions aligned with the model's evolving capabilities, while the self-rewarding module introduces a simple yet effective majority-vote-based reward estimation strategy. This approach supports continual self-improvement and demonstrates performance on par with methods trained on large-scale, high-quality labeled data. The framework is generalizable across different LLM architectures and reinforcement learning algorithms.

844b22bb025f485d85d00f1f61555a8ff0131658.title: STEVE-1: A Generative Model for Text-to-Behavior in Minecraft
844b22bb025f485d85d00f1f61555a8ff0131658.research_question: How can generative models be instruction-tuned to follow open-ended text and visual instructions for sequential decision-making tasks in complex environments, such as Minecraft, without relying on large datasets of instruction-labeled trajectories?
844b22bb025f485d85d00f1f61555a8ff0131658.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging pretrained foundation models for behavior and text-video alignment, combined with self-supervised behavioral cloning and hindsight relabeling, enables the creation of instruction-following agents that can robustly complete a wide range of tasks with minimal instruction-labeled data and compute.
844b22bb025f485d85d00f1f61555a8ff0131658.proposed_method: A novel hierarchical generative modeling approach will be developed, inspired by unCLIP, to enable text-to-behavior generation in Minecraft. The method consists of two main components: (1) a policy model based on a pretrained Video Pretraining (VPT) agent, which is fine-tuned to achieve goals represented as visual embeddings from a pretrained MineCLIP model; and (2) a prior model, implemented as a conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE), which maps text instructions to MineCLIP visual embedding space. The policy is fine-tuned using a self-supervised behavioral cloning approach with packed hindsight relabeling, allowing the agent to learn goal-conditioned behaviors from gameplay data without requiring explicit instruction labels. During inference, classifier-free guidance is employed to balance goal-conditioned and prior behaviors, enhancing instruction-following reliability. The overall system enables the agent to follow both text and visual instructions by sampling latent goals from the prior and generating action sequences via the policy.
844b22bb025f485d85d00f1f61555a8ff0131658.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in the MineRL environment using a large-scale gameplay dataset comprising 54 million frames from both human contractors and VPT-generated trajectories. The prior model will be trained on a small, augmented dataset of 2,000 human-labeled and 8,000 GPT-generated text-video pairs. Evaluation will be performed on an early-game suite of 13 tasks, including both programmatic metrics (e.g., travel distance, item collection) and MineCLIP-based embedding alignment metrics. Baselines will include the unconditional VPT agent and a text-conditioned VPT agent. Additional experiments will assess scaling properties, the impact of prompt chaining for long-horizon tasks, the effect of pretraining, classifier-free guidance, and prompt engineering. Performance will be measured in terms of task completion rates, resource collection, and alignment between generated behaviors and target goals.
844b22bb025f485d85d00f1f61555a8ff0131658.novelty_claims: The proposed methodology introduces a new framework for instruction-tuning generative models of behavior without requiring large datasets of instruction-labeled trajectories, leveraging self-supervised hindsight relabeling and pretrained foundation models. The approach adapts unCLIP and classifier-free guidance techniques from text-to-image generation to the sequential decision-making domain, enabling robust text and visual instruction following with low-level controls and raw pixel inputs. The method achieves state-of-the-art performance in open-ended instruction following in Minecraft, significantly outperforming previous baselines and demonstrating strong scaling properties and generalization across a variety of tasks.

844bb298d49ef4a07b5d4929dfdfd170f6a1d5f5.title: Aligning Large Multimodal Models with Factually Augmented RLHF
844bb298d49ef4a07b5d4929dfdfd170f6a1d5f5.research_question: How can large multimodal models be more effectively aligned to minimize hallucinations and improve factual grounding in vision-language tasks, particularly given the scarcity and misalignment of high-quality multimodal training data?
844bb298d49ef4a07b5d4929dfdfd170f6a1d5f5.hypothesis: Incorporating factually augmented reward signals into reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) will improve multimodal alignment, reduce hallucinations, and enhance the factual accuracy of large multimodal models compared to standard RLHF and supervised fine-tuning alone.
844bb298d49ef4a07b5d4929dfdfd170f6a1d5f5.proposed_method: A new alignment framework is proposed that adapts RLHF to the multimodal domain by collecting human preferences specifically focused on identifying hallucinated outputs in vision-language tasks. The method introduces Factually Augmented RLHF (Fact-RLHF), where the reward model is provided with additional factual information such as image captions and ground-truth multi-choice options during both training and inference. This augmentation enables the reward model to better detect hallucinations and prevents reward hacking, where models exploit weaknesses in the reward model. The approach also incorporates symbolic penalties for incorrect answers and overly verbose responses, and augments the supervised fine-tuning stage with high-quality, human-annotated multimodal datasets converted into conversational formats. The overall pipeline includes supervised fine-tuning, preference modeling with factually augmented data, and reinforcement learning using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with KL penalties to maintain response quality.
844bb298d49ef4a07b5d4929dfdfd170f6a1d5f5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a base model architecture consisting of a Vicuna-based language model and a CLIP ViT-L/14 vision encoder, with both 7B and 13B parameter scales. Training data will include synthetic vision instruction data as well as curated human-annotated datasets (VQA-v2, A-OKVQA, Flickr30k), converted into multi-round QA and captioning tasks. Human preference data will be collected on 10k hold-out conversations, with crowdworkers instructed to prioritize honesty and helpfulness. Evaluation will be performed on several benchmarks: LLaVA-Bench (for general alignment), the newly developed MMHAL-BENCH (specifically targeting hallucinations with open-ended questions across 12 object categories and 8 task types), MMBench (multi-modal multiple-choice), and POPE (object perception evaluation). Baselines will include models trained with standard supervised fine-tuning, standard RLHF, and other state-of-the-art LMMs. Metrics will include relative performance to GPT-4, F1 scores, and hallucination rates as judged by both human annotators and GPT-4-based automated evaluation.
844bb298d49ef4a07b5d4929dfdfd170f6a1d5f5.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first successful adaptation of RLHF to multimodal alignment for large vision-language models, with a novel Factually Augmented RLHF algorithm that leverages additional factual information to improve reward model reliability and reduce reward hacking. The approach also presents a new benchmark, MMHAL-BENCH, specifically designed to evaluate hallucinations in LMM outputs with realistic, open-ended questions. The methodology demonstrates significant improvements in both human-alignment and capability benchmarks, achieving higher performance with greater data efficiency compared to existing methods.

8466541843d891bdfd663114e5cc8a2159d65f29.title: Demystifying Spectral Feature Learning for Instrumental Variable Regression
8466541843d891bdfd663114e5cc8a2159d65f29.research_question: How can spectral feature learning be systematically understood and optimized for nonparametric instrumental variable (IV) regression, particularly in the presence of hidden confounders? What are the spectral properties and alignment conditions that govern the effectiveness of feature-based causal effect estimation in IV regression?
8466541843d891bdfd663114e5cc8a2159d65f29.hypothesis: The effectiveness of spectral feature-based IV regression depends critically on the alignment between the structural function and the leading eigenspaces of the conditional expectation operator, as well as the decay rate of its singular values. When alignment is strong and singular value decay is slow, spectral methods will achieve optimal or near-optimal generalization error; otherwise, performance will degrade or fail.
8466541843d891bdfd663114e5cc8a2159d65f29.proposed_method: A two-stage least squares (2SLS) estimator will be developed for nonparametric IV regression, where features for both treatment and instrument variables are learned to explicitly target the leading eigenspaces of the conditional expectation operator. The feature learning will be formulated as a spectral contrastive loss minimization problem, which is theoretically equivalent to approximating the operator's rank-d truncated singular value decomposition (SVD) in Hilbert-Schmidt norm. Neural networks will be used to parametrize the feature maps, and stochastic gradient descent will optimize the contrastive loss using an unlabeled dataset. A practical, data-driven procedure will be introduced to estimate both the spectral decay of the operator and the alignment of the structural function with its singular functions, enabling empirical diagnosis of the problem regime (good, bad, or ugly). Theoretical analysis will provide generalization error bounds for the 2SLS estimator with learned spectral features, quantifying the impact of spectral alignment and singular value decay.
8466541843d891bdfd663114e5cc8a2159d65f29.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic datasets will be constructed to allow explicit control over the conditional expectation operator's spectrum and the alignment of the structural function, enabling systematic evaluation of the good, bad, and ugly regimes. The synthetic data generation will use trigonometric bases and orthogonal transformations to manipulate spectral properties, and mean squared error (MSE) will be used as the primary evaluation metric. Baselines will include 2SLS with oracle (true) spectral features and 2SLS with learned features. The proposed data-driven procedure for estimating spectral alignment and decay will be validated on the dSprites dataset, a standard benchmark in IV regression, where the structural function and operator spectrum will be empirically analyzed. Multiple runs will ensure statistical robustness, and comparisons will be made to alternative feature learning and IV regression approaches.
8466541843d891bdfd663114e5cc8a2159d65f29.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled theoretical taxonomy (good, bad, ugly) for spectral feature learning in IV regression, grounded in generalization error bounds that explicitly account for spectral alignment and singular value decay. A rigorous connection is established between spectral contrastive feature learning and the SVD of the conditional expectation operator, clarifying the theoretical foundation of recent empirical successes. A practical, data-driven procedure is developed for estimating key spectral properties from data, enabling practitioners to diagnose the regime of their IV problem. The approach provides new insights into when and why spectral methods succeed or fail, and offers a unified framework for understanding and improving spectral feature learning in causal inference.

847fb9bdead7ad0b7b31016b0c688f65e9465fc3.title: Compute-Optimal LLMs Provably Generalize Better with Scale
847fb9bdead7ad0b7b31016b0c688f65e9465fc3.research_question: Why do larger language models generalize better, particularly in the compute-optimal regime, and how does the generalization gap scale with model and dataset size? What are the key factors that contribute to the generalization behavior of large language models as they are scaled up, and how can these be theoretically and empirically characterized?
847fb9bdead7ad0b7b31016b0c688f65e9465fc3.hypothesis: In the compute-optimal regime, the generalization gap of large language models decreases predictably with scale due to a combination of constant parameter-to-token ratio, decreasing loss variance, and improved quantizability (or compressibility) of the models. The information content in the model grows sublinearly with dataset size, further reducing the effective complexity and generalization gap.
847fb9bdead7ad0b7b31016b0c688f65e9465fc3.proposed_method: A novel, fully empirical Freedman-type martingale concentration inequality will be developed to derive tighter generalization bounds for language models by explicitly incorporating the empirical variance of the loss function. The generalization bound will be decomposed into three interpretable components: the ratio of parameters per token (which is held constant in compute-optimal scaling), the token-wise loss variance (which decreases with model scale), and the quantization error at a fixed bitrate (which also decreases with scale). The methodology will include both a direct quantization-based complexity analysis (using bits per parameter and quantization gap) and an information-theoretic approach based on prequential coding to estimate the information content in the model. Theoretical derivations will be complemented by empirical evaluation of all bound components on real model checkpoints and data.
847fb9bdead7ad0b7b31016b0c688f65e9465fc3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Pythia model family, ranging from 70 million to 12 billion parameters, with checkpoints selected to match the compute-optimal frontier (parameter/token ratio ≈ 1/20). The models will be evaluated on the Pile dataset, which was also used for their pretraining. Quantization will be performed using GPTQ at 4 bits per parameter, and all relevant bound terms—including empirical loss variance, quantization gap, and prequential code-based complexity—will be computed. Evaluation metrics will include the empirical risk (NLL), the generalization bound components, and the scaling behavior of each term with model size. Baseline comparisons will include existing generalization bounds (e.g., Azuma-based) and parameter-counting approaches.
847fb9bdead7ad0b7b31016b0c688f65e9465fc3.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first fully empirical Freedman-type martingale concentration inequality for generalization bounds in language models, enabling the use of empirical loss variance rather than population variance. The approach provides a tighter, interpretable decomposition of the generalization gap into parameter/token ratio, loss variance, and quantization error, and demonstrates that both quantizability and information-theoretic model complexity improve with scale. The work also empirically and theoretically establishes that the information content in compute-optimal language models grows sublinearly with dataset size, leading to stronger generalization guarantees as models are scaled.

84959e211a767f902cbf1695ec54a5b50148020f.title: Clifford Neural Layers for PDE Modeling
84959e211a767f902cbf1695ec54a5b50148020f.research_question: How can neural network architectures be designed to more effectively model the relationships and internal structure of scalar, vector, and higher-order fields in partial differential equations (PDEs), in order to improve the accuracy and generalization of neural PDE surrogates across a range of scientific and engineering applications?
84959e211a767f902cbf1695ec54a5b50148020f.hypothesis: Introducing neural network layers based on Clifford algebra, which operate on multivector representations of physical fields and leverage geometric relationships between field components, will provide a stronger inductive bias and lead to improved generalization and predictive performance compared to standard neural PDE surrogates.
84959e211a767f902cbf1695ec54a5b50148020f.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that replaces conventional convolution and Fourier transform operations in neural PDE surrogate models with their Clifford algebra counterparts. The method will represent physical fields as multivectors, capturing scalar, vector, and higher-order (bivector, trivector) components within a unified algebraic structure. Clifford convolutional neural network (CNN) layers will be constructed by extending standard convolutions to operate via the geometric product on multivector-valued feature maps and kernels, preserving geometric relationships between field components. Additionally, Clifford Fourier layers will be implemented by applying Clifford Fourier transforms to multivector fields, enabling frequency-domain operations that respect the algebraic structure of the data. Both translation equivariance and rotational equivariance will be incorporated, with specialized rotational Clifford CNN layers leveraging quaternionic representations for efficient parameterization. The approach will maintain parameter efficiency by sharing weights among multivector components and will be compatible with existing deep learning frameworks.
84959e211a767f902cbf1695ec54a5b50148020f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three representative PDE modeling tasks: 2D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations (fluid dynamics), 2D shallow water equations (weather modeling), and 3D Maxwell's equations (electromagnetism). For each task, datasets will be generated or obtained with multiple input and output fields (scalar and vector/bivector components), using established simulation frameworks such as PhiFlow for Navier-Stokes. Baseline architectures will include ResNet-based and Fourier Neural Operator (FNO)-based neural PDE surrogates, with comparable parameter counts. The proposed Clifford neural layers will replace standard convolution and Fourier operations in these baselines. Evaluation metrics will include one-step mean squared error and rollout loss (multi-step prediction error) for both scalar and vector fields, assessed on held-out test sets. Experiments will systematically vary the number of training trajectories to assess generalization, and results will be compared across all architectures to quantify improvements.
84959e211a767f902cbf1695ec54a5b50148020f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first use of multivector representations and Clifford algebra-based neural layers—including Clifford convolutions and Clifford Fourier transforms—in deep learning for PDE modeling. This approach enables neural networks to explicitly model the geometric and algebraic relationships between different physical field components, providing a principled inductive bias. The method is universally applicable to a wide range of scientific domains involving coupled scalar and vector fields, such as fluid dynamics, weather forecasting, and electromagnetism. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate consistent improvements in generalization and predictive accuracy over existing neural PDE surrogates, particularly in settings with limited training data or strong coupling between field components.

84b7c486c56bd3880cb8eb01de9ae90ba3ebdaed.title: Shadow Alignment: The Ease of Subverting Safely-Aligned Language Models
84b7c486c56bd3880cb8eb01de9ae90ba3ebdaed.research_question: How vulnerable are safely-aligned open-source large language models (LLMs) to subversion attacks using minimal adversarial data, and how can such attacks compromise safety without degrading general model utility?
84b7c486c56bd3880cb8eb01de9ae90ba3ebdaed.hypothesis: Safely-aligned open-source LLMs can be subverted to generate harmful content using a very small set of adversarially crafted instruction-tuning examples, without significant loss in their helpfulness or general capabilities.
84b7c486c56bd3880cb8eb01de9ae90ba3ebdaed.proposed_method: A new attack methodology, termed 'Shadow Alignment', will be developed to subvert safely-aligned LLMs. The approach involves three main steps: (1) Automatically generating a diverse set of harmful questions by prompting a strong LLM (e.g., GPT-4) with scenarios forbidden by AI usage policies; (2) Using another capable LLM (e.g., text-davinci-001) to generate corresponding answers for these questions, thus creating a set of (question, answer) pairs; (3) Selecting a small, diverse subset of these pairs (e.g., 100) using clustering (SimCSE embeddings + KMeans++) and using them to instruction-tune target aligned LLMs with full-parameter fine-tuning. The process will ensure that the resulting models are evaluated for both the ability to generate harmful content and the retention of general helpfulness.
84b7c486c56bd3880cb8eb01de9ae90ba3ebdaed.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on eight safely-aligned LLMs from five organizations, including LLaMa-2, Falcon, InternLM, BaiChuan2, and Vicuna, using both 7B and 13B parameter variants. Models will be fine-tuned with 100 adversarial QA pairs for 15-25 epochs, using a learning rate of 0.00001 and batch size of 128, on high-end GPUs (e.g., 8x80G Nvidia A100). Evaluation will include: (a) refusal and violation rates on a held-out set of 200 malicious questions; (b) general utility benchmarks such as MMLU, GSM, BBH, TyDiQA, PIQA, and BoolQ to assess factual, mathematical, reasoning, multilingual, commonsense, and reading comprehension abilities; (c) instruction-following ability using datasets like Self-Instruct, LIMA, OpenAssistant, Koala, and TruthfulQA, with both automatic (reward model, GPT-4) and human evaluation; (d) safety and harmfulness using datasets such as CoNa, Controversial, PhysicalUnsafe, MaliciousInstructions, and ToxiGen, with both automatic (content moderation API, toxicity classifiers) and manual annotation. Transferability to multi-turn dialogue and other languages will also be tested.
84b7c486c56bd3880cb8eb01de9ae90ba3ebdaed.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the concept of 'Shadow Alignment', demonstrating that safely-aligned LLMs can be subverted with as few as 100 adversarial examples and minimal computational resources. This attack is shown to generalize across multiple model architectures, organizations, dialogue settings (single- and multi-turn), and languages, while preserving the model's general utility and helpfulness. The findings highlight a critical vulnerability in current safety alignment protocols and call for the development of more robust safeguarding strategies for open-source LLMs.

84c149537dee8ef3a7ff54b6bb01e9a4c8eaa17c.title: Do NOT Think That Much for 2+3=? On the Overthinking of o1-Like LLMs
84c149537dee8ef3a7ff54b6bb01e9a4c8eaa17c.research_question: How can the efficiency of o1-like large language models (LLMs) be improved during inference, particularly by reducing unnecessary computational overhead (overthinking) on simple reasoning tasks, without sacrificing accuracy or diversity of reasoning?
84c149537dee8ef3a7ff54b6bb01e9a4c8eaa17c.hypothesis: o1-like LLMs can be optimized to reduce overthinking—manifested as excessive solution rounds and token usage—by employing targeted self-training and response streamlining strategies, thereby improving computational efficiency while maintaining or enhancing accuracy and reasoning diversity.
84c149537dee8ef3a7ff54b6bb01e9a4c8eaa17c.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves a multi-stage approach. First, novel efficiency metrics are developed to quantify both outcome efficiency (tokens contributing to correct answers) and process efficiency (tokens contributing to diverse reasoning strategies) in o1-like LLMs. Using these metrics, a self-training paradigm is adopted, where the model generates its own training data and is fine-tuned using supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and preference optimization methods such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), Reasoning Preference Optimization (RPO), and Simple Preference Optimization (SimPO). Additionally, response streamlining strategies are introduced, including First-Correct Solutions (FCS), FCS with Reflection, and Greedily Diverse Solutions (GDS), which selectively retain only the most efficient and diverse solution rounds in the model's output. These strategies are implemented by sampling multiple outputs per instance, clustering reasoning strategies, and training the model to prefer shorter, more efficient, and non-redundant responses.
84c149537dee8ef3a7ff54b6bb01e9a4c8eaa17c.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on several mathematical reasoning benchmarks of varying difficulty: ASDIV, GSM8K, MATH500, GPQA, and AIME. Baselines include conventional LLMs (Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-Math-72B-Instruct) and o1-like models (QwQ-32B-Preview, DeepSeek-R1). Evaluation metrics include accuracy, number of solution rounds, number of generated tokens, and the proposed outcome and process efficiency metrics. The experimental setup involves generating multiple response samples per instance, applying clustering (using GPT-4o) to assess reasoning diversity, and comparing the effects of different fine-tuning and response simplification strategies. The effectiveness of each method is validated by measuring reductions in token usage and solution rounds while monitoring any changes in accuracy across all test sets.
84c149537dee8ef3a7ff54b6bb01e9a4c8eaa17c.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first comprehensive framework for diagnosing and mitigating overthinking in o1-like LLMs, including the development of outcome and process efficiency metrics that go beyond traditional accuracy-based evaluation. The approach leverages self-training and novel response streamlining strategies to systematically reduce computational overhead without external supervision. The integration of preference optimization techniques and clustering-based diversity assessment further distinguishes the methodology, enabling targeted improvements in both efficiency and reasoning quality.

84d02dc0b708438f452d8b07bcf74d5b1a1b72eb.title: TRACE Back from the Future: A Probabilistic Reasoning Approach to Controllable Language Generation
84d02dc0b708438f452d8b07bcf74d5b1a1b72eb.research_question: How can controllable language generation be achieved efficiently and flexibly, such that language models can be steered toward desired global attributes (e.g., non-toxicity, personalization, topic) without expensive retraining or sampling, and with the ability to handle rare or composite attributes?
84d02dc0b708438f452d8b07bcf74d5b1a1b72eb.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that tractable probabilistic reasoning, specifically through the distillation of a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) from a base language model and the use of lightweight attribute classifiers, enables efficient and exact computation of the expected probability that generated text satisfies global attributes, thereby allowing for effective and flexible controllable generation.
84d02dc0b708438f452d8b07bcf74d5b1a1b72eb.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a framework that first distills a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) from a pre-trained autoregressive language model to approximate its generative process. For each target attribute, a lightweight, log-linear classifier is trained to estimate the probability that a full text sequence satisfies the attribute. During generation, the method computes the Expected Attribute Probability (EAP) by leveraging the tractable structure of the HMM, using a forward-backward algorithm to efficiently sum over all possible future continuations. The EAP is then used to reweight the next-token probabilities of the language model, ensuring that generated continuations are globally compliant with the desired attributes. The approach allows for rapid adaptation to new or composite attributes by training only the small classifier, and does not require retraining the base language model or the HMM for each new control objective.
84d02dc0b708438f452d8b07bcf74d5b1a1b72eb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several controllable text generation tasks, including detoxification (using the RealToxicityPrompts dataset), low-resource personalized language modeling (using RoleBench with 76 character personas), and compositional attribute control (e.g., generating text that is both political and non-toxic). Baselines will include fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and decoding-time control methods such as DAPT, PPO, DPO, GeDi, FUDGE, DExperts, MuCoLa, and others. Evaluation metrics will include toxicity (via Perspective API), fluency (perplexity), diversity (distinct n-grams), and attribute-specific classifier scores. The experimental setup will compare the proposed method’s efficiency (training and inference time), flexibility (rapid adaptation to new attributes), and effectiveness (attribute control and text quality) against baselines, using both GPT2-large and Gemma-2B as base models.
84d02dc0b708438f452d8b07bcf74d5b1a1b72eb.novelty_claims: The proposed approach claims novelty in enabling exact and efficient computation of expected attribute probabilities for controllable generation by combining tractable HMM distillation with lightweight, easily trained attribute classifiers. It eliminates the need for retraining or fine-tuning the base language model for each new attribute, supports rapid adaptation to rare or composite attributes, and achieves strong control with minimal decoding overhead. The method is further distinguished by its ability to compose multiple attributes seamlessly and its empirical demonstration of state-of-the-art performance on detoxification and low-resource personalization tasks.
