84dbf3f70e0192e74674df29be5bb2bc7e3d9d97.title: Combinatorial optimization with physics-inspired graph neural networks
84dbf3f70e0192e74674df29be5bb2bc7e3d9d97.research_question: Can a scalable, physics-inspired graph neural network framework be developed to efficiently solve large-scale combinatorial optimization problems, such as MaxCut and Maximum Independent Set, and how does its performance compare to established classical solvers?
84dbf3f70e0192e74674df29be5bb2bc7e3d9d97.hypothesis: A graph neural network approach, trained via a differentiable relaxation of the combinatorial objective function and guided by statistical physics principles, will achieve competitive or superior performance to existing solvers on canonical NP-hard problems, while scaling to problem sizes previously inaccessible to traditional or quantum-inspired methods.
84dbf3f70e0192e74674df29be5bb2bc7e3d9d97.proposed_method: A general framework is proposed that encodes combinatorial optimization problems as quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) or polynomial unconstrained binary optimization (PUBO) problems, mapping each binary decision variable to a node in a graph. The method applies a relaxation to the problem Hamiltonian, replacing binary variables with continuous soft assignments, and uses this differentiable loss to train a graph neural network (GNN) in an unsupervised fashion. The GNN architecture employs recursive neighborhood aggregation (e.g., via graph convolutional layers) to iteratively update node embeddings, which are initialized randomly and refined through backpropagation using optimizers such as ADAM. After training, a projection heuristic (e.g., thresholding or rounding) is applied to map the soft node assignments back to binary variables, yielding a candidate solution to the original combinatorial problem. The approach is designed to be robust to hyperparameter choices and scalable to very large graphs, with the potential for distributed training.
84dbf3f70e0192e74674df29be5bb2bc7e3d9d97.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on canonical NP-hard problems, specifically MaxCut and Maximum Independent Set, using random d-regular graphs with sizes ranging from hundreds up to millions of nodes. The GNN model is implemented as a two-layer graph convolutional network, with hyperparameters (embedding sizes, learning rate, number of epochs) chosen to balance memory constraints and solution quality. The method is compared against classical baselines such as the Goemans-Williamson (GW) algorithm and simple randomized approximation algorithms, with cut size (for MaxCut) and solution quality as primary evaluation metrics. Multiple random seeds (shots) are used to mitigate local optima, and early stopping is employed to optimize runtime. Performance is assessed in terms of achieved objective value and computational efficiency, with results bootstrapped over multiple random graph instances.
84dbf3f70e0192e74674df29be5bb2bc7e3d9d97.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified, physics-inspired GNN framework capable of solving a broad class of combinatorial optimization problems without reliance on hand-crafted loss functions or supervised labels. By leveraging a differentiable relaxation of the problem Hamiltonian, the method enables unsupervised end-to-end training and generalizes across QUBO and PUBO formulations. The framework demonstrates scalability to unprecedented problem sizes (up to millions of variables), competitive or superior performance to established solvers, and extensibility to distributed training, marking a significant advance over both traditional and quantum-inspired optimization approaches.

84f0a99d0f0015a6145c94468870d43ab1d166fd.title: ModelScope Text-to-Video Technical Report
84f0a99d0f0015a6145c94468870d43ab1d166fd.research_question: How can a diffusion-based generative model be designed to synthesize high-quality, temporally coherent videos from text prompts, leveraging both image-text and video-text paired datasets for training?
84f0a99d0f0015a6145c94468870d43ab1d166fd.hypothesis: Incorporating spatio-temporal modeling blocks and a multi-frame training strategy that utilizes both image-text and video-text paired datasets will enable a diffusion-based text-to-video model to generate videos with improved temporal consistency, semantic alignment, and visual fidelity compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.
84f0a99d0f0015a6145c94468870d43ab1d166fd.proposed_method: A novel text-to-video synthesis framework will be developed based on a latent diffusion model architecture. The model will consist of three main components: a VQGAN for encoding and decoding between visual and latent spaces, a text encoder (initialized from CLIP ViT-H/14) for transforming prompts into embeddings, and a denoising UNet augmented with spatio-temporal blocks. The spatio-temporal blocks will include both spatial and temporal convolutions as well as spatial and temporal attention mechanisms, enabling the model to capture complex dependencies across frames. The architecture will be designed to flexibly handle varying numbers of frames, allowing seamless adaptation to both image-text and video-text data. Training will employ a multi-frame strategy, where a subset of GPUs processes image-text pairs (treating images as single-frame videos) and the remainder processes video-text pairs, thus enhancing semantic diversity and preventing catastrophic forgetting.
84f0a99d0f0015a6145c94468870d43ab1d166fd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using large-scale datasets, including LAION-5B (specifically the LAION2B-en subset) for image-text pairs and WebVid for video-text pairs. The model will be evaluated on the MSR-VTT dataset in a zero-shot setting, using metrics such as FID-vid, FVD, and CLIPSIM to assess visual fidelity, temporal consistency, and semantic alignment, respectively. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art models such as Make-A-Video, Imagen Video, CogVideo, MagicVideo, and VideoLDM. The model will be trained on 80G NVIDIA A100 GPUs, with hyperparameters such as a batch size of 1,400 for images and 3,200 for videos, and a total of 267,000 training iterations. The VQGAN will use a compression factor of 8, and the denoising process will utilize DDPM with 1,000 steps for training and DDIM sampling for inference. Generated videos will be consistently set to a resolution of 256x256 for fair comparison.
84f0a99d0f0015a6145c94468870d43ab1d166fd.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a publicly available, open-source text-to-video diffusion model with a novel spatio-temporal block that combines both convolutional and attention-based mechanisms for effective temporal modeling. The multi-frame training strategy uniquely leverages both image-text and video-text paired datasets, enhancing semantic richness and preventing loss of image-domain expertise. The model architecture is designed to flexibly adapt to varying frame numbers, and a significant portion of parameters is dedicated to temporal modeling. Quantitative and qualitative results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art or superior performance compared to existing methods, establishing a strong baseline for future research in text-to-video synthesis.

84f4ed2029085d2e009e6f262537c4201738737e.title: Twin-Merging: Dynamic Integration of Modular Expertise in Model Merging
84f4ed2029085d2e009e6f262537c4201738737e.research_question: How can multiple task-specific models be effectively integrated into a single multi-task model without additional retraining, while minimizing performance loss due to interference and maximizing adaptability to heterogeneous test data?
84f4ed2029085d2e009e6f262537c4201738737e.hypothesis: Separating and modularizing shared and exclusive task-specific knowledge, followed by dynamic merging based on input data, will significantly reduce performance gaps between merged and fine-tuned models and improve adaptability to diverse data distributions.
84f4ed2029085d2e009e6f262537c4201738737e.proposed_method: The proposed approach, Twin-Merging, consists of two principal stages: knowledge modularization and dynamic merging. First, task-specific expert models are decomposed into shared knowledge (captured by a shared expert, typically via parameter merging techniques such as Task Arithmetic) and exclusive knowledge (computed as the difference between each expert and the shared expert). Exclusive knowledge vectors are further compressed using singular value decomposition (SVD) to enhance storage efficiency. During inference, a lightweight router network, parameterized by a small fully connected layer, dynamically determines the optimal combination of shared and exclusive knowledge for each input, using the input's embedding as context. The merged model weights are then composed on-the-fly as a weighted sum of the shared expert and compressed exclusive vectors, with the router's softmax outputs providing the weights. This dynamic composition enables the model to adaptively leverage both general and task-specific expertise based on the characteristics of each test input.
84f4ed2029085d2e009e6f262537c4201738737e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of 20 datasets spanning both language and vision tasks. For language tasks, discriminative benchmarks such as GLUE (using RoBERTa) and generative tasks (using Qwen-14B) will be evaluated, including MMLU, TruthfulQA, BBQ, and CNN-DailyMail. Vision experiments will use ViT-B/32 in CLIP as the backbone on eight classification datasets (e.g., SUN397, Stanford Cars, EuroSAT, MNIST). Baselines will include weight averaging, Task Arithmetic, Ties-Merging, DARE-Merging, AdaMerging, and Surgery, with both individually fine-tuned and pre-trained models serving as upper and lower bounds. Evaluation metrics will primarily be average normalized score relative to fine-tuned experts, with additional analysis of storage efficiency, scalability to more tasks, and performance on unseen tasks. Ablation studies will assess the impact of modularization, dynamic merging, and compression techniques (e.g., SVD vs. magnitude pruning).
84f4ed2029085d2e009e6f262537c4201738737e.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel modularization of model knowledge into shared and exclusive components, explicitly disentangling these to minimize interference during merging. Dynamic merging is performed via a learned router that adapts the composition of expertise to each input, addressing data heterogeneity at test time. The approach achieves high parameter efficiency through SVD compression of exclusive knowledge and demonstrates scalability to large models and many tasks. Twin-Merging is simple to implement, requires minimal hyperparameter tuning, and can be combined with other merging methods for further gains. Experimental results claim significant improvements over existing merging baselines, approaching or even surpassing the performance of individually fine-tuned models while maintaining storage and computational efficiency.

85140fd1f3b1460853a61b0f33a61e228651898f.title: Hydra-SGG: Hybrid Relation Assignment for One-stage Scene Graph Generation
85140fd1f3b1460853a61b0f33a61e228651898f.research_question: How can the efficiency and effectiveness of one-stage scene graph generation be improved, particularly in the context of sparse supervision and slow convergence inherent in DETR-based models?
85140fd1f3b1460853a61b0f33a61e228651898f.hypothesis: Integrating a hybrid relation assignment strategy that combines one-to-one and one-to-many relation assignments, along with an auxiliary decoder branch that encourages duplicate relation predictions, will significantly increase positive supervision signals, accelerate convergence, and improve the overall performance of one-stage scene graph generation models.
85140fd1f3b1460853a61b0f33a61e228651898f.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a one-stage scene graph generation framework that employs a Hybrid Relation Assignment strategy. This strategy synergistically combines One-to-One Relation Assignment, which uses Hungarian matching to assign each ground truth relation to a unique query, with an IoU-based One-to-Many Relation Assignment, which allows each ground truth relation to be matched with multiple queries based on a composite score of class probabilities and bounding box IoU. To further enhance the effectiveness of the One-to-Many assignment, an auxiliary decoder branch, termed Hydra Branch, is incorporated. This branch shares parameters with the main decoder but omits self-attention layers, thereby promoting duplicate relation predictions and aligning with the one-to-many assignment objective. The overall loss function is a balanced combination of losses from both assignment strategies, and the Hydra Branch is used only during training to avoid inference overhead.
85140fd1f3b1460853a61b0f33a61e228651898f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three benchmark datasets: Visual Genome (VG150), OpenImagesV6, and GQA, covering a range of entity and relation categories and varying scene complexities. The evaluation will focus on the scene graph detection (SGDet) task, using metrics such as Recall@k (R@k), mean Recall@k (mR@k), F-Recall, and weighted mean Average Precision (wmAP) for both relationship and phrase detection. Baselines will include both two-stage and one-stage SGG methods, such as PE-Net, RelTR, SGTR, and others. The experimental setup will involve ablation studies on key components (assignment strategies, Hydra Branch), hyperparameter sweeps (e.g., threshold for positive sample selection, number of queries, loss weights), and analysis of training efficiency (epochs to convergence, total training time). The model will be trained with a ResNet50 backbone and compared in terms of both accuracy and training speed.
85140fd1f3b1460853a61b0f33a61e228651898f.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel Hybrid Relation Assignment strategy that increases the number of positive training samples by over 50% per step, directly addressing the sparse supervision bottleneck in DETR-based SGG models. The auxiliary Hydra Branch is an innovative architectural component that decouples diversity-promoting self-attention from the duplication-promoting one-to-many assignment, enabling synergistic optimization without inference overhead. This approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple SGG benchmarks with up to 10x faster convergence compared to existing one-stage models, and outperforms both one-stage and two-stage baselines in terms of mean recall and training efficiency.

85167901371c71519241f8681db13fd85ba961e2.title: BiT: Robustly Binarized Multi-distilled Transformer
85167901371c71519241f8681db13fd85ba961e2.research_question: Can transformer models be fully binarized in both weights and activations while maintaining practical levels of accuracy for language understanding tasks, thereby enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments?
85167901371c71519241f8681db13fd85ba961e2.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a combination of robust binarization techniques, elastic binary activation functions with learnable parameters, and a multi-step knowledge distillation process can enable fully binarized transformer models to achieve accuracy levels close to their full-precision counterparts.
85167901371c71519241f8681db13fd85ba961e2.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a robust binarization framework for transformer models, which includes a two-set binarization scheme that treats activations with different value ranges (e.g., after Softmax/ReLU vs. other layers) differently, mapping them to either {0,1} or {−1,1}. A novel elastic binary activation function is incorporated, where both the scaling factor and threshold are learned during training to minimize binarization error, using a straight-through estimator for gradient propagation. The method also applies mean subtraction to weights before binarization, gradient clipping only to activations, and prefers ReLU activations for non-negative output layers. To address optimization challenges, a multi-distillation process is used, where the model is successively distilled from higher-precision teachers to lower-precision students, following a quantization schedule (e.g., full-precision → W1A2 → W1A1), ensuring that each student is sufficiently similar to its teacher to facilitate effective knowledge transfer.
85167901371c71519241f8681db13fd85ba961e2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the GLUE benchmark, which comprises a diverse set of natural language understanding tasks, and the SQuAD v1.1 dataset for machine reading comprehension. The evaluation will use pre-trained BERT-base as the full-precision baseline, and compare against existing quantized and binarized transformer models such as Q-BERT, TernaryBERT, BinaryBERT, and BiBERT. Models will be assessed on metrics appropriate to each task (e.g., accuracy, F1, exact match), with and without data augmentation. Ablation studies will be performed to isolate the effects of each proposed component, and various multi-distillation schedules will be explored to determine their impact on final model performance.
85167901371c71519241f8681db13fd85ba961e2.novelty_claims: The proposal claims several innovations: (1) a two-set binarization scheme that differentiates between activation types for optimal binarization; (2) an elastic binary activation function with learnable scaling and threshold parameters, significantly improving accuracy; (3) a multi-step knowledge distillation process tailored for extreme quantization, enabling effective transfer from full-precision to fully binarized models; and (4) the first demonstration of fully binarized transformer models achieving practical accuracy levels on standard NLP benchmarks, narrowing the gap to full-precision baselines to within 5.9 points on GLUE.

851928d03830b47e795fe9925c8244fb4ae4fafd.title: Quality-Diversity Actor-Critic: Learning High-Performing and Diverse Behaviors via Value and Successor Features Critics
851928d03830b47e795fe9925c8244fb4ae4fafd.research_question: How can artificial agents be enabled to learn a broad spectrum of high-performing and diverse behaviors, such that they can adapt to unforeseen environments and tasks, rather than specializing in a single solution for a specific problem?
851928d03830b47e795fe9925c8244fb4ae4fafd.hypothesis: A reinforcement learning framework that unifies value function and successor features critics via constrained optimization will enable agents to learn policies that are both high-performing and capable of executing a wide range of diverse skills, leading to improved adaptability and robustness in downstream and perturbed tasks.
851928d03830b47e795fe9925c8244fb4ae4fafd.proposed_method: A novel off-policy actor-critic deep reinforcement learning algorithm, Quality-Diversity Actor-Critic (QDAC), is developed to address the quality-diversity problem. The method employs two critics: a value function critic to maximize expected return and a successor features critic to characterize and enforce behavioral diversity. The actor is conditioned on a skill variable and optimizes a Lagrangian objective that balances maximizing return and minimizing the distance between the expected successor features and a desired skill vector, using an adaptive Lagrange multiplier. Policy evaluation is performed for both critics using Bellman error minimization, and policy improvement is achieved by stochastic gradient descent on the Lagrangian. The approach supports both model-free (built on SAC) and model-based (built on DreamerV3) variants, and uses a universal value function and successor feature approximator conditioned on skill. Skills are sampled uniformly from a predefined skill space, and the replay buffer is augmented with skill and feature information for efficient learning.
851928d03830b47e795fe9925c8244fb4ae4fafd.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on six challenging continuous control locomotion tasks using the Google Brax physics engine, including Walker, Ant, and Humanoid environments with four types of feature functions (feet contact, velocity, jump, and angle) to define skill spaces. The method is compared against state-of-the-art quality-diversity evolutionary algorithms (PPGA, DCG-ME, QD-PG), RL-based QD methods (DOMiNO, SMERL, ReverseSMERL), and several ablations (No-SF, Fixed-λ, UVFA). Evaluation metrics include distance-to-skill (measuring how well the agent achieves target skills) and performance (return while executing skills), with results reported as Inter-Quartile Mean (IQM) and 95% confidence intervals over 10 random seeds. Additional experiments test few-shot adaptation and hierarchical RL in perturbed environments (e.g., motor failure, gravity changes, friction, hurdles, and wall navigation), without retraining, to assess robustness and skill utility. Statistical significance is assessed with Mann-Whitney U tests.
851928d03830b47e795fe9925c8244fb4ae4fafd.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified actor-critic reinforcement learning framework that explicitly combines value-based and successor features critics through constrained optimization, enabling the learning of a single skill-conditioned policy capable of executing a wide range of high-performing and diverse behaviors. Unlike prior QD and skill discovery methods, this approach directly optimizes for both performance and diversity with theoretical justification, supports both model-free and model-based variants, and demonstrates superior adaptability and robustness in few-shot adaptation and hierarchical RL tasks. The method achieves significantly higher diversity and performance than existing baselines and ablations, and provides a practical solution for generating expressive and useful skills for downstream tasks.

851cfaff3dd0421a9bc2775b135fe3007910eef0.title: Temporal Disentanglement of Representations for Improved Generalisation in Reinforcement Learning
851cfaff3dd0421a9bc2775b135fe3007910eef0.research_question: How can reinforcement learning agents be enabled to generalize more effectively to previously unseen variations in both task-relevant and task-irrelevant environment variables, particularly in image-based settings where changes in visual factors can significantly alter the agent's latent representations?
851cfaff3dd0421a9bc2775b135fe3007910eef0.hypothesis: Introducing a self-supervised auxiliary task that leverages the temporal structure of RL observations to disentangle underlying factors of variation in image-based state representations will improve both zero-shot generalization and adaptation speed of RL agents to unseen environment variations.
851cfaff3dd0421a9bc2775b135fe3007910eef0.proposed_method: A novel auxiliary task, Temporal Disentanglement (TED), will be integrated into reinforcement learning algorithms to encourage the encoder to learn disentangled representations from image observations. TED operates by training a classifier to distinguish between pairs of temporally consecutive and non-consecutive observations, using both within-episode and cross-episode non-temporal pairs. The classifier is structured to compare each feature in the latent representation separately, promoting the separation of independent factors of variation. The TED loss is combined with the standard RL loss to jointly update the encoder and classifier during training, and a target encoder is used for stability. The classifier is only used during training and can be discarded during policy execution, ensuring computational efficiency.
851cfaff3dd0421a9bc2775b135fe3007910eef0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of continuous and discrete control tasks, including DeepMind Control Suite (DMC) environments with color distractors, PandaGym robotics tasks, and the Procgen generalization benchmark. The method will be evaluated using several base RL algorithms such as RAD, SVEA, and PPO, covering both on-policy and off-policy settings, with and without image augmentations. Baselines will include domain randomization, data augmentation (DrQ), invariant representation learning (DBC), and contrastive auxiliary tasks (CURL). Evaluation metrics will include average episodic return on test environments with unseen variable values, adaptation speed after environment changes, and a disentanglement score based on the ability to identify fixed factors in observation pairs. Hyperparameters, including the TED loss coefficient, will be tuned via grid search, and results will be averaged over multiple random seeds.
851cfaff3dd0421a9bc2775b135fe3007910eef0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to introduce a self-supervised, online auxiliary task for disentangled representation learning in RL that exploits the temporal structure of observations. Unlike prior methods, TED does not require a decoder, offline pretraining, or labeled data, and can be seamlessly integrated with existing RL algorithms. The method targets disentanglement of both task-relevant and irrelevant factors, enabling improved generalization and faster adaptation to unseen environment variations. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior generalization and disentanglement compared to state-of-the-art baselines, as well as robustness across multiple RL settings and tasks.

8545e249ab7a49f4a5abcfade395b90ffadb687a.title: Post-hoc Concept Bottleneck Models
8545e249ab7a49f4a5abcfade395b90ffadb687a.research_question: How can interpretable concept bottleneck models be constructed post-hoc from any pre-trained neural network, without requiring dense concept annotations during training, while maintaining model performance and enabling efficient global model editing?
8545e249ab7a49f4a5abcfade395b90ffadb687a.hypothesis: It is possible to transform any pre-trained neural network into an interpretable concept bottleneck model post-hoc, leveraging external concept datasets or multimodal models for concept representations, and to achieve comparable predictive performance to the original model while enabling efficient global model editing through concept-level interventions.
8545e249ab7a49f4a5abcfade395b90ffadb687a.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops Post-hoc Concept Bottleneck Models (PCBMs) by first extracting concept representations using Concept Activation Vectors (CAVs) or multimodal models such as CLIP. Concepts are defined either from external datasets with concept annotations or from natural language descriptions mapped into a shared embedding space. The embeddings from a pre-trained backbone model are projected onto the learned concept subspace, and an interpretable predictor (e.g., a sparse linear model) is trained to map these concept activations to the target predictions. If the concept subspace is insufficient to match the original model's performance, a residual modeling step is introduced (PCBM-h), where a separate residual predictor is trained on the original embeddings to recover lost accuracy. The entire process is data-efficient, does not require concept annotations on the original training data, and supports global model editing by manipulating concept weights in the interpretable predictor.
8545e249ab7a49f4a5abcfade395b90ffadb687a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several image classification and medical datasets, including CIFAR10, CIFAR100, COCO-Stuff, CUB, HAM10000, and SIIM-ISIC. Pre-trained backbones such as CLIP-ResNet50, ResNet18, and Inception will be used. Concept banks will be constructed from BRODEN, ConceptNet, Derm7pt, and CLIP-based text embeddings. Baselines will include the original black-box models, linear probing, and, where possible, standard Concept Bottleneck Models (CBMs). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, AUROC, and mAP, depending on the dataset. Additional experiments will simulate distribution shifts using MetaShift and assess global model editing via both controlled interventions and user studies, comparing pruning-based edits to oracle fine-tuning and greedy strategies.
8545e249ab7a49f4a5abcfade395b90ffadb687a.novelty_claims: The proposed method enables the conversion of any pre-trained model into a concept bottleneck model post-hoc, eliminating the need for dense concept annotations on the training data. It introduces the use of multimodal models and natural language descriptions to construct concept subspaces, greatly expanding the applicability and accessibility of concept bottlenecks. The approach supports efficient global model editing through concept-level interventions, which can be performed without retraining or access to target domain data. The hybrid residual modeling (PCBM-h) allows for recovery of original model performance when the concept bank is insufficient. User studies demonstrate that non-expert users can effectively improve model generalization through simple concept pruning, highlighting the practical utility of the framework.

855e6f201937ff70a96ce1618bcbc080b2858b8e.title: FedDiff: Diffusion Model Driven Federated Learning for Multi-Modal and Multi-Clients
855e6f201937ff70a96ce1618bcbc080b2858b8e.research_question: How can secure, efficient, and accurate multi-modal data fusion for land cover classification be achieved across multiple distributed clients, each holding heterogeneous and privacy-sensitive remote sensing data?
855e6f201937ff70a96ce1618bcbc080b2858b8e.hypothesis: Integrating a dual-branch diffusion model within a federated learning framework, combined with lightweight communication and feature decomposition modules, will enable effective multi-modal feature fusion, preserve data privacy, and improve land cover classification accuracy while reducing communication costs.
855e6f201937ff70a96ce1618bcbc080b2858b8e.proposed_method: A novel federated learning framework, FedDiff, will be developed to enable distributed multi-modal data fusion for remote sensing applications. The approach utilizes a dual-branch diffusion model, where hyperspectral and LiDAR data are processed in separate encoder branches, allowing for complementary feature extraction in both spatial, spectral, and frequency domains. The diffusion process is modeled as a parameterized Markov chain, with noise added and removed via an improved U-Net architecture enhanced by spatial-spectral attention and frequency-domain processing. Feature maps from each client are fused using a multi-modal federated interaction module that leverages low-rank singular value decomposition (SVD) to compress and transmit only essential intermediate features, ensuring privacy and reducing communication overhead. The global model is updated through federated averaging of gradients, and a lightweight feature decomposition module further reduces communication costs by exploiting the redundancy in remote sensing data.
855e6f201937ff70a96ce1618bcbc080b2858b8e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three benchmark multi-modal remote sensing datasets: Houston2013, Trento, and MUUFL Gulfport, each containing hyperspectral and LiDAR data with ground truth labels for land cover classification. The proposed method will be evaluated against state-of-the-art baselines, including SVM, CNN-2D, RNN, Transformer-based, and other multi-modal fusion networks. Evaluation metrics will include Overall Accuracy (OA), Average Accuracy (AA), Class Accuracy (CA), and Kappa coefficient, as well as communication cost measured by the size of feature maps exchanged per iteration. The experimental setup will simulate multiple clients (e.g., eight base station clients), each holding different modalities, with training and validation performed in a federated manner using PyTorch and NCCL for distributed communication. Ablation studies will assess the impact of each module, and communication efficiency will be quantified by comparing the proposed lightweight feature decomposition to standard approaches.
855e6f201937ff70a96ce1618bcbc080b2858b8e.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first diffusion model-driven federated learning framework for multi-modal and multi-client remote sensing data fusion. Key innovations include a dual-branch diffusion architecture for explicit joint feature extraction across modalities, a multi-modal federated interaction module with low-rank SVD-based communication compression, and a lightweight feature decomposition module for efficient and privacy-preserving model updates. The approach enables secure, distributed, and high-precision land cover classification, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy while significantly reducing communication costs.

855ef56d6edf58e86953efd930f7db69ec9551cb.title: Quant-BnB: A Scalable Branch-and-Bound Method for Optimal Decision Trees with Continuous Features
855ef56d6edf58e86953efd930f7db69ec9551cb.research_question: How can optimal decision trees be efficiently learned for both regression and classification tasks when the features are continuous, and what scalable algorithms can be developed to address the computational challenges inherent to this combinatorial optimization problem?
855ef56d6edf58e86953efd930f7db69ec9551cb.hypothesis: A branch-and-bound algorithm that leverages quantile-based partitioning of continuous feature spaces can efficiently and optimally learn shallow decision trees for both regression and classification tasks, outperforming existing methods in scalability and computational efficiency.
855ef56d6edf58e86953efd930f7db69ec9551cb.proposed_method: A novel branch-and-bound (BnB) framework, termed Quant-BnB, is proposed for learning optimal decision trees with continuous and binary features. The method decomposes the search space by splitting on quantiles of the feature distributions, which enables the calculation of tight upper and lower bounds for the tree optimization problem at each BnB iteration. The algorithm maintains a dynamic set of candidate tree parameterizations (tuples specifying feature splits and intervals), iteratively pruning suboptimal regions using quantile-based lower bounds and updating the best-known solution with quantile-based upper bounds. Lower bounds are computed using three strategies of increasing tightness and computational cost, balancing pruning power and efficiency. The approach is designed to handle both regression (with squared loss) and classification (with 0-1 loss) tasks, and is particularly focused on shallow trees (depth 2 or 3), where exhaustive search is otherwise intractable for continuous features.
855ef56d6edf58e86953efd930f7db69ec9551cb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of real-world datasets containing continuous and binary features, for both regression and classification tasks. The proposed Quant-BnB method will be compared against state-of-the-art optimal decision tree algorithms, including those based on mixed integer programming (MIP), dynamic programming (DP), and other BnB variants, particularly those limited to binary features. Evaluation metrics will include training error, computational time, and scalability (e.g., ability to handle larger datasets or deeper trees). Experimental setup will involve varying tree depths and feature types, with careful benchmarking of lower bound strategies and their impact on pruning and runtime. Baseline methods will include greedy heuristics (e.g., CART, ID3) and optimal solvers where feasible.
855ef56d6edf58e86953efd930f7db69ec9551cb.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first standalone branch-and-bound framework that directly handles optimal decision tree learning for both regression and classification tasks with continuous features, without requiring feature binarization or reliance on proprietary optimization solvers. The quantile-based decomposition of the search space and the development of multiple lower bound strategies provide significant computational speedups and improved scalability compared to existing approaches. The method is general, applicable to mixed feature types, and empirically demonstrates superior performance for shallow optimal trees on real datasets.

85664bb73d09a20f4d3f7aae81143c0f25060fbb.title: Fast-DetectGPT: Efficient Zero-Shot Detection of Machine-Generated Text via Conditional Probability Curvature
85664bb73d09a20f4d3f7aae81143c0f25060fbb.research_question: How can machine-generated text be efficiently and accurately detected in a zero-shot setting across diverse domains, languages, and source models, without relying on extensive computational resources or supervised training?
85664bb73d09a20f4d3f7aae81143c0f25060fbb.hypothesis: Humans and large language models (LLMs) exhibit distinct patterns in token selection given a context, with machines tending to choose tokens with higher statistical probability due to pre-training on large-scale corpora, resulting in measurable differences in the conditional probability curvature of generated text.
85664bb73d09a20f4d3f7aae81143c0f25060fbb.proposed_method: A novel zero-shot detection framework will be developed based on the concept of conditional probability curvature. The method will treat text generation as a sequential decision process and, for a given passage and language model, will sample alternative token choices at each position conditioned on the preceding context. The conditional probability of the original passage and the sampled alternatives will be computed using a scoring model, and the curvature will be quantified as the normalized difference between the log-probability of the original passage and the mean log-probability of the alternatives, divided by their standard deviation. This approach eliminates the need for repeated model calls for each perturbation, as all conditional probabilities can be obtained in a single forward pass, significantly reducing computational cost. The detection decision will be made by comparing the computed curvature to a threshold, with higher positive curvature indicating machine-generated text.
85664bb73d09a20f4d3f7aae81143c0f25060fbb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six datasets spanning news (XSum), Wikipedia (SQuAD), story writing (WritingPrompts), biomedical QA (PubMedQA), and multilingual settings (WMT16 English and German). Both white-box (source model accessible) and black-box (using surrogate models) scenarios will be evaluated. The method will be benchmarked against state-of-the-art zero-shot detectors (DetectGPT, NPR, DNA-GPT), statistical baselines (Likelihood, Entropy, LogRank, LRR), and supervised classifiers (RoBERTa, GPTZero). Detection accuracy will be measured using AUROC, and computational efficiency will be assessed by inference time on GPU hardware. Robustness will be evaluated across passage lengths, domains, languages, decoding strategies, and under paraphrasing attacks.
85664bb73d09a20f4d3f7aae81143c0f25060fbb.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces conditional probability curvature as a new, fundamental feature for zero-shot detection of machine-generated text, enabling accurate classification with only a single model forward pass. This approach dramatically reduces computational cost by two orders of magnitude compared to prior methods like DetectGPT, while simultaneously achieving significant improvements in detection accuracy (approximately 75% relative AUROC gain). The method demonstrates robust performance across domains, languages, passage lengths, and decoding strategies, and outperforms both zero-shot and supervised baselines in both white-box and black-box settings.

8575b9e0fbba9e1d43e0e44b59663e95aae0c38b.title: Towards characterizing the value of edge embeddings in Graph Neural Networks
8575b9e0fbba9e1d43e0e44b59663e95aae0c38b.research_question: What are the representational and empirical benefits of maintaining and updating edge embeddings, as opposed to only node embeddings, in graph neural network architectures under memory constraints?
8575b9e0fbba9e1d43e0e44b59663e95aae0c38b.hypothesis: Maintaining edge embeddings in graph neural networks provides significant representational and empirical advantages over node-only embeddings, especially under memory constraints and in graphs with specific topologies such as those with hub nodes.
8575b9e0fbba9e1d43e0e44b59663e95aae0c38b.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted to characterize the value of edge embeddings in GNNs. Two computational models will be formalized: one where each node maintains a fixed-size embedding and another where each edge maintains a fixed-size embedding, both under explicit memory constraints. Depth separation results will be established by analyzing the number of message-passing rounds required to solve canonical graph tasks (e.g., MAP inference in pairwise graphical models) using either node or edge embeddings. Theoretical lower and upper bounds on depth and memory tradeoffs will be derived using information flow and graph pebbling techniques. Additionally, symmetric and non-symmetric protocols will be studied to assess the impact of architectural symmetry constraints on representational power.
8575b9e0fbba9e1d43e0e44b59663e95aae0c38b.experiment_details: Empirical validation will be performed on both real-world GNN benchmarks (e.g., molecular property prediction and image-like data) and synthetic graph topologies designed to stress-test the theoretical findings, such as star graphs with hub nodes and tree-structured graphs for probabilistic inference tasks. For each setting, architectures maintaining edge embeddings will be compared to node-only architectures, with all other architectural aspects (depth, embedding size) held constant. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy and task-specific performance measures. Experiments will also investigate the effect of directed message-passing and the maintenance of directional edge embeddings.
8575b9e0fbba9e1d43e0e44b59663e95aae0c38b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new theoretical framework for quantifying the representational benefits of edge embeddings in GNNs under memory constraints, revealing depth separations that are not captured by symmetry-based analyses. It also provides the first rigorous empirical comparison of edge- versus node-based GNN architectures while controlling for input information and architectural parameters. The work leverages and extends techniques from distributed computation and time-space tradeoffs, offering new insights into the fine-grained architectural choices in GNN design.

85963807c11abe38e9a2797d9860e012238607ef.title: MasaCtrl: Tuning-Free Mutual Self-Attention Control for Consistent Image Synthesis and Editing
85963807c11abe38e9a2797d9860e012238607ef.research_question: How can consistent image synthesis and complex non-rigid image editing be achieved in text-to-image diffusion models without requiring model fine-tuning or time-consuming optimization?
85963807c11abe38e9a2797d9860e012238607ef.hypothesis: A mutual self-attention mechanism, augmented with mask guidance, can enable tuning-free, consistent, and faithful image synthesis and non-rigid editing by querying correlated local content and textures from a source image during the diffusion process.
85963807c11abe38e9a2797d9860e012238607ef.proposed_method: A novel tuning-free framework, termed MasaCtrl, is proposed to achieve consistent image synthesis and complex non-rigid image editing in diffusion-based text-to-image models. The method converts the standard self-attention modules within the diffusion model's U-Net into mutual self-attention modules, where query features from the target image's denoising process query key and value features from the source image's denoising process. To address confusion between foreground and background, a mask-guided strategy is introduced: masks are automatically extracted from cross-attention maps associated with the main object in the image, enabling the attention mechanism to restrict queries to corresponding foreground or background regions. The mutual self-attention is selectively applied in the decoder part of the U-Net after several denoising steps, ensuring that the target image's layout is formed before content is queried from the source. The approach is designed to be easily integrated with controllable diffusion models such as T2I-Adapter and ControlNet, allowing for additional control over pose, sketch, or segmentation.
85963807c11abe38e9a2797d9860e012238607ef.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Stable Diffusion model (v1.4 checkpoint) and the anime-style Anything-V4 model, with both synthetic and real images. For real image editing, DDIM inversion is used to obtain the initial noise map. The method will be compared against established baselines including SDEdit, P2P, and PnP, using their open-source implementations. Evaluation will focus on both qualitative and quantitative metrics, such as content consistency, identity preservation, and faithfulness to the target prompt, with classifier-free guidance set to 7.5 and 50 denoising steps. Additional experiments will integrate the method with T2I-Adapter and ControlNet for controllable synthesis, and ablation studies will analyze the effects of varying the starting step and U-Net layer for mutual self-attention control.
85963807c11abe38e9a2797d9860e012238607ef.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a tuning-free mutual self-attention mechanism for consistent image synthesis and non-rigid editing, eliminating the need for model fine-tuning or prompt-specific optimization. The mask-guided mutual self-attention strategy, which leverages automatically extracted masks from cross-attention maps, addresses foreground-background confusion and enables precise control over which regions are queried for content consistency. The method is compatible with existing controllable diffusion frameworks, facilitating integration for enhanced synthesis and editing capabilities. Experimental results are expected to demonstrate superior consistency and fidelity compared to previous tuning-free and fine-tuning-based approaches.

85b10400864187230714506412c85610c786b5c3.title: Emu Video: Factorizing Text-to-Video Generation by Explicit Image Conditioning
85b10400864187230714506412c85610c786b5c3.research_question: How can text-to-video generation be improved to produce high-quality, temporally consistent, and text-faithful videos, particularly when leveraging large-scale image-text and video-text datasets?
85b10400864187230714506412c85610c786b5c3.hypothesis: Explicitly factorizing the text-to-video generation process into two stages—first generating an image from the text prompt, then generating a video conditioned on both the text and the generated image—will strengthen the conditioning signal and lead to higher quality and more faithful video generation compared to direct text-to-video approaches.
85b10400864187230714506412c85610c786b5c3.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a two-stage, factorized text-to-video generation pipeline using latent diffusion models. In the first stage, a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model generates an initial image conditioned on the input text prompt. In the second stage, a video diffusion model, initialized from the same pretrained text-to-image model, generates a sequence of video frames conditioned on both the text prompt and the generated image. Image conditioning is implemented by concatenating the starting frame, a binary mask indicating its position, and the noised video input along the channel dimension. Temporal parameters (1D convolutions and attention layers) are added and trained, while spatial parameters remain frozen to retain the pretrained model's visual quality and diversity. A zero terminal-SNR noise schedule is adopted during training to eliminate train-test discrepancies in diffusion, and a multi-stage training regime is used, starting with low-resolution videos and then fine-tuning at higher resolution. An additional interpolation model, sharing architecture with the video model, is trained to increase the frame rate of generated videos.
85b10400864187230714506412c85610c786b5c3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a large-scale dataset of 34 million licensed video-text pairs, covering diverse concepts and durations (5-60 seconds). The model will be evaluated using both automatic metrics and a robust human evaluation protocol (JUICE), which requires evaluators to justify their preferences regarding video quality and text faithfulness. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art direct text-to-video methods (such as Make-A-Video, Imagen Video, CogVideo, and commercial solutions like RunwayML Gen2 and PikaLabs), with all videos post-processed to match in resolution, aspect ratio, and frame rate to reduce annotator bias. Ablation studies will assess the impact of factorization, noise schedule, multi-stage training, high-quality finetuning, and parameter freezing. The model will also be tested in an image-to-video setting, where a user-provided image and text prompt are used to animate the image.
85b10400864187230714506412c85610c786b5c3.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces an explicit factorization of text-to-video generation via an intermediate image, enabling stronger conditioning and improved retention of visual quality and diversity from large-scale text-to-image models. The method eliminates the need for deep cascades of models for high-resolution video generation by leveraging a single, multi-stage trained diffusion model. The adoption of a zero terminal-SNR noise schedule for diffusion training at high resolution is identified as critical for bridging train-test discrepancies and achieving consistent outputs. Additionally, a robust human evaluation protocol (JUICE) is proposed to provide more reliable assessments of video generation quality and faithfulness. The approach is also naturally extensible to image-to-video animation tasks.

85bfbfab6d247a228648d1522c43f6eaf8ce0cc1.title: MathCoder2: Better Math Reasoning from Continued Pretraining on Model-translated Mathematical Code
85bfbfab6d247a228648d1522c43f6eaf8ce0cc1.research_question: How can the mathematical reasoning abilities of large language models be improved through the development of a specialized pretraining corpus that integrates both mathematical code and corresponding natural language reasoning steps?
85bfbfab6d247a228648d1522c43f6eaf8ce0cc1.hypothesis: Integrating model-translated mathematical code paired with natural language reasoning steps into the pretraining corpus will significantly enhance the mathematical reasoning abilities of large language models compared to pretraining on conventional math-related data alone.
85bfbfab6d247a228648d1522c43f6eaf8ce0cc1.proposed_method: A comprehensive pretraining corpus will be constructed by collecting and filtering diverse math-related data sources, including web data, synthetic datasets, code utilizing mathematical packages, and mathematical textbooks. An advanced filtering pipeline, leveraging fastText classifiers and instruction-tuned LLMs, will be used to ensure high relevance and quality of the data. Next, a novel extraction and translation process will be implemented: an instruction-tuned LLM (e.g., Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct) will be prompted to extract LaTeX expressions, their computation conditions, and results from the curated texts, and then generate Python code snippets that accurately reflect the underlying mathematical reasoning. These code snippets will be executed and retained only if their outputs match the expected results, ensuring correctness. The final dataset will consist of paired natural language reasoning steps and verified code snippets, forming a high-quality resource for continued pretraining.
85bfbfab6d247a228648d1522c43f6eaf8ce0cc1.experiment_details: Experiments will involve continued pretraining of several popular base models (such as Llama-3-8B, DeepSeekMath-7B, Mistral-7B, and Code-Llama-7B) on the constructed corpus, named MathCode-Pile, which contains approximately 19.2B tokens. Evaluation will be conducted on five representative mathematical benchmarks: GSM8K, MATH, SAT-Math, OCW, and MMLU-Math, covering a wide range of mathematical problem types and difficulty levels. Baseline comparisons will include strong mathematical models of similar sizes, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of different dataset components and the concatenation of reasoning steps with code. Evaluation metrics will primarily be accuracy on benchmark datasets, using standardized evaluation frameworks (e.g., 4-shot or zero-shot settings as appropriate).
85bfbfab6d247a228648d1522c43f6eaf8ce0cc1.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel method for generating large-scale, high-quality mathematical code paired with natural language reasoning steps, specifically tailored for mathematical reasoning rather than general-purpose code. The resulting dataset, MathCode-Pile, is meticulously curated and verified for correctness, and is fully open-sourced along with all data processing and training code to ensure transparency and reproducibility. The approach demonstrates significant improvements over existing open-source mathematical pretraining corpora and establishes a new standard for enhancing mathematical reasoning in large language models.

85c4bb31349ead5ec8aba0ee7284df48ca29118d.title: Learning Curves of Stochastic Gradient Descent in Kernel Regression
85c4bb31349ead5ec8aba0ee7284df48ca29118d.research_question: How does the performance of online first-order algorithms, specifically single-pass stochastic gradient descent (SGD), compare to offline methods such as ridge and ridgeless regression in kernel regression, particularly in high-dimensional and potentially misspecified settings?
85c4bb31349ead5ec8aba0ee7284df48ca29118d.hypothesis: Single-pass SGD with an exponentially decaying step size schedule achieves minimax optimal excess risk rates in kernel regression across a range of sample size and dimensionality regimes, and can overcome the saturation effect that limits offline methods such as kernel ridge regression, except in certain highly misspecified or asymptotic regimes.
85c4bb31349ead5ec8aba0ee7284df48ca29118d.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves a theoretical and empirical analysis of single-pass stochastic gradient descent (SGD) for kernel regression under the source condition, including both well-specified and misspecified cases where the optimal predictor may not belong to the RKHS. The focus is on the inner product (dot-product) kernel over the unit sphere, which encompasses neural tangent kernels (NTK) as a special case. Two SGD variants will be studied: one with an exponentially decaying step size schedule and another with a constant step size and iterate averaging. Theoretical derivations will characterize the excess risk convergence rates for these SGD variants under varying sample size (n) and input dimension (d) regimes, with particular attention to high-dimensional settings where n scales polynomially with d. The analysis will also investigate the role of step size schedules in mitigating the saturation effect observed in offline kernel regression methods.
85c4bb31349ead5ec8aba0ee7284df48ca29118d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic datasets generated according to the regression model y = f*(x) + ε, with x sampled uniformly from the unit sphere in R^{d+1} and ε as independent Gaussian noise. The kernel used will be a dot-product kernel, including the NTK of ReLU networks as a specific case. Baselines for comparison will include kernel ridge regression (KRR) and ridgeless regression, with evaluation based on excess risk (mean squared prediction error) as the primary metric. Experimental setups will systematically vary the sample size n and input dimension d to explore both high-dimensional (n ≍ d^γ for γ > 0) and asymptotic (n ≫ d) regimes, and will compare the performance of SGD with exponentially decaying step size, SGD with iterate averaging, and offline baselines across different smoothness levels (source condition parameter s).
85c4bb31349ead5ec8aba0ee7284df48ca29118d.novelty_claims: The proposal aims to provide the first precise characterization of the excess risk learning curves for single-pass SGD in kernel regression under general source conditions, including the misspecified case where the optimal predictor is outside the RKHS. It claims to establish that SGD with an exponentially decaying step size achieves minimax optimal rates up to constants across all high-dimensional regimes and smoothness levels, thereby overcoming the saturation effect that limits kernel ridge regression. Additionally, the research will demonstrate a provable advantage of the exponentially decaying step size schedule over iterate averaging in common settings, offering new insights into the mechanisms that enable SGD to achieve optimal generalization in kernel regression.

85c514db4e90e1fd4200d858353f27a3cc2c29ad.title: Oryx MLLM: On-Demand Spatial-Temporal Understanding at Arbitrary Resolution
85c514db4e90e1fd4200d858353f27a3cc2c29ad.research_question: How can a unified multi-modal large language model (MLLM) be designed to efficiently and accurately process and understand visual data of arbitrary spatial resolutions and temporal lengths, including images, videos, and 3D scenes, for a broad range of multimodal tasks?
85c514db4e90e1fd4200d858353f27a3cc2c29ad.hypothesis: A multi-modal architecture that supports on-demand encoding of native-resolution visual inputs and dynamic compression of visual tokens will enable more efficient and precise spatial-temporal understanding across diverse visual modalities and tasks than models restricted to fixed resolutions or static tokenization strategies.
85c514db4e90e1fd4200d858353f27a3cc2c29ad.proposed_method: A unified MLLM architecture, named Oryx, will be developed to process visual inputs of arbitrary spatial sizes and temporal lengths in an on-demand manner. The core components include a pre-trained OryxViT visual encoder, based on Vision Transformer and SigLIP, equipped with variable-length self-attention and a large, adaptable positional embedding matrix to encode images and videos at their native resolutions. A dynamic compressor module will be designed to support adjustable downsampling ratios (1x to 16x), enabling efficient handling of long visual contexts by compressing visual tokens as needed, while maintaining high recognition precision for tasks that require native resolution. The architecture will integrate these visual representations with a lightweight LLM via cross-attention and shared MLP projectors, ensuring seamless fusion of visual and language modalities. The training pipeline will include specialized data curation for long-form video retrieval and spatial-aware 3D understanding, leveraging open-source datasets and a two-stage supervised fine-tuning strategy.
85c514db4e90e1fd4200d858353f27a3cc2c29ad.experiment_details: Comprehensive experiments will be conducted on a wide range of multi-modal benchmarks, including general video understanding (VideoMME, NextQA, MVBench, Perception Test), long-form video understanding (MLVU, LongVideoBench, VideoMME-Long), 2D spatial understanding (MMBench, MMMU, DocVQA, OCRBench, AI2D, TextVQA), and 3D spatial understanding (ScanQA). Baselines will include state-of-the-art proprietary and open-source MLLMs such as GPT-4V, Gemini-1.5-Pro, VideoChat2-HD, LLaVA-OneVision, and 3D-LLM. Evaluation metrics will comprise accuracy for multiple-choice and generation tasks, as well as standard metrics for 3D QA (METEOR, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, BLEU). Ablation studies will assess the impact of native resolution encoding, dynamic compression, and data curation strategies. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by using similar model sizes (7B, 32B, 34B) and open-source training data.
85c514db4e90e1fd4200d858353f27a3cc2c29ad.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first unified MLLM architecture capable of on-demand spatial-temporal understanding at arbitrary resolution, supporting seamless processing of images, videos, and 3D scenes. Key innovations include the OryxViT visual encoder for native-resolution input, a dynamic compressor for adjustable visual token compression, and a unified training strategy for multi-modal and multi-task learning. The approach enables efficient handling of extremely long visual contexts without sacrificing recognition precision, and achieves state-of-the-art results on a variety of open-source and proprietary benchmarks, outperforming much larger models in both general and long-form video understanding as well as 2D and 3D spatial tasks.

85c5ad8c43cb3c033f1ebcc7e6829b5857fb28f3.title: What is Wrong with Perplexity for Long-context Language Modeling?
85c5ad8c43cb3c033f1ebcc7e6829b5857fb28f3.research_question: How can the evaluation and training of large language models (LLMs) be improved to more accurately reflect and enhance their long-context understanding capabilities, beyond what is captured by standard perplexity metrics?
85c5ad8c43cb3c033f1ebcc7e6829b5857fb28f3.hypothesis: Standard perplexity fails to capture the true long-context capabilities of LLMs because it averages over all tokens, many of which are not influenced by long-range dependencies. By identifying and focusing on key tokens that are specifically influenced by long context, both evaluation metrics and training objectives can be designed to better measure and improve long-context performance in LLMs.
85c5ad8c43cb3c033f1ebcc7e6829b5857fb28f3.proposed_method: A novel evaluation metric, LongPPL (Long-context Perplexity), will be developed to focus on key tokens within long sequences. Key tokens are identified using a long-short context contrastive method: for each token, its log-probability is computed under both the full long context and a truncated short context, and the difference (LSD) is used to assess the influence of long context. Tokens with high LSD and sufficient long-context likelihood (LCL) are selected as key tokens. Perplexity is then computed by averaging only over these key tokens, using a powerful evaluator model to ensure accurate selection. Additionally, a new training objective, LongCE (Long-context Cross-Entropy) loss, will be introduced, which reweights the loss for each token according to its long-context influence, upweighting key tokens to prioritize their learning during fine-tuning. The LongCE loss uses a differentiable, soft influence function based on the likelihood ratio between long and short contexts, and is optimized in an EM-like fashion where the model iteratively estimates token influence and updates its parameters.
85c5ad8c43cb3c033f1ebcc7e6829b5857fb28f3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple long-context benchmarks, including LongBench, LongEval, and RULER, using a variety of LLMs such as Llama-2-7B, Mistral-7B-v0.1, Llama-2-13B, and others. Evaluation will employ the GovReport dataset for metric computation, with context lengths up to 32k tokens. The LongPPL metric will be compared to standard perplexity, using both large and small evaluator models (e.g., Qwen2-72B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B). For training, models will be fine-tuned with both standard CE and LongCE losses on datasets such as PG-19 and Pile-arxiv, using fine-tuning strategies like Entropy-aware Adjusted Base Frequency (EABF) and Position Interpolation (PI). Performance will be measured by benchmark scores (accuracy, average score) and correlation with evaluation metrics, and training efficiency will be assessed by wall-clock time and computational overhead. Ablation studies will investigate the impact of hyperparameters and alternative key token selection criteria.
85c5ad8c43cb3c033f1ebcc7e6829b5857fb28f3.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a principled method for identifying key tokens that are critical for long-context understanding, enabling the design of LongPPL, a new perplexity-based metric that strongly correlates with actual long-context performance. It also presents LongCE, a novel re-weighted cross-entropy loss that improves long-context capabilities during fine-tuning by focusing on these key tokens. The approach provides a deeper explanation for the failure of standard perplexity in long-context scenarios and offers effective, generalizable solutions for both evaluation and training of LLMs in long-context settings.

85cc48276c69924d3e92ddb38facb7d92be9a4a6.title: Evaluating the Logical Reasoning Ability of ChatGPT and GPT-4
85cc48276c69924d3e92ddb38facb7d92be9a4a6.research_question: How capable are large language models, specifically ChatGPT and GPT-4, at performing logical reasoning across a variety of natural language understanding tasks and datasets, including both well-established and newly introduced or out-of-distribution benchmarks?
85cc48276c69924d3e92ddb38facb7d92be9a4a6.hypothesis: Large language models such as ChatGPT and GPT-4 possess superior logical reasoning abilities compared to traditional fine-tuned models on established benchmarks, but may exhibit limitations when confronted with out-of-distribution or novel logical reasoning tasks.
85cc48276c69924d3e92ddb38facb7d92be9a4a6.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation will be conducted on the logical reasoning abilities of ChatGPT and GPT-4 using a suite of multi-choice reading comprehension and natural language inference (NLI) tasks. The evaluation will leverage both well-known benchmarks (such as LogiQA, ReClor, and MNLI) and newly released or out-of-distribution datasets (such as AR-LSAT and LogiQA 2.0 OOD). The methodology will involve prompt-based querying of the language models, utilizing carefully designed instructions and in-context examples to elicit responses. Multiple prompt strategies will be explored, including label specification and chain-of-thought prompting, to assess their impact on logical reasoning performance. For comparison, a baseline will be established using a fine-tuned RoBERTa-base model, and human performance will be reported as reference.
85cc48276c69924d3e92ddb38facb7d92be9a4a6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of datasets: LogiQA 2.0 (English and Chinese), ReClor, AR-LSAT, LogiQA 2.0 OOD for multi-choice reading comprehension, and ConTRoL, ConjNLI, HELP, MED, TaxiNLI, and MNLI for NLI tasks. Each dataset will be evaluated using accuracy as the primary metric. ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo) and GPT-4 (API and ChatUI) will be tested via prompt-based API calls, with instructions tailored to each task type. Baseline results will be obtained by fine-tuning RoBERTa-base for five epochs per dataset. Human average and ceiling performance will be included for context. Additional analyses will investigate the effects of in-context learning (multiple examples within a conversation) and chain-of-thought prompting on model performance, particularly for challenging or out-of-distribution data.
85cc48276c69924d3e92ddb38facb7d92be9a4a6.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a comprehensive benchmark suite (LogiEval) for evaluating logical reasoning in large language models, encompassing both established and newly released datasets, including out-of-distribution scenarios. The evaluation framework systematically compares prompt-based large language models with traditional fine-tuning approaches and human performance. The study explores the impact of prompt engineering strategies, such as in-context learning and chain-of-thought prompting, on logical reasoning, providing new insights into the strengths and limitations of current state-of-the-art language models in this domain.

85ec455bcdc8f93dcb6955a7aec2cc05ba37f864.title: Improved off-policy training of diffusion samplers
85ec455bcdc8f93dcb6955a7aec2cc05ba37f864.research_question: How can diffusion models be effectively trained to sample from complex, high-dimensional distributions specified only by unnormalized densities or energy functions, and what strategies can improve exploration and credit assignment for off-policy training in this context?
85ec455bcdc8f93dcb6955a7aec2cc05ba37f864.hypothesis: Incorporating local search-based exploration using a replay buffer, as well as leveraging Langevin parametrization for drift, will improve the sample quality, mode coverage, and partition function estimation of diffusion-based off-policy samplers compared to existing methods.
85ec455bcdc8f93dcb6955a7aec2cc05ba37f864.proposed_method: A unified framework will be developed for training diffusion-structured samplers, focusing on off-policy methods such as continuous generative flow networks (GFlowNets) and including simulation-based variational objectives (e.g., path integral sampler). The methodology will introduce a novel exploration strategy that augments off-policy training with local search in the target space, implemented via parallel Metropolis-adjusted Langevin Algorithm (MALA) steps and a replay buffer to store and replay high-quality samples. The approach will also investigate architectural inductive biases, such as Langevin parametrization of the drift term in the neural SDE, and compare them to state flow-based credit assignment strategies. The training procedure will alternate between on-policy/exploratory sampling and buffer-guided local search, optimizing trajectory balance or variance-based objectives as appropriate. The framework will support learning both the mean and variance of the forward process and allow for flexible backward (noising) process parametrizations.
85ec455bcdc8f93dcb6955a7aec2cc05ba37f864.experiment_details: Experiments will benchmark the proposed samplers on a suite of unconditional and conditional sampling tasks, including sampling from energy-based distributions such as a 2D mixture of Gaussians (25GMM), 10D Funnel, 32D Manywell, and 1600D Log-Gaussian Cox process, as well as conditional sampling from a VAE latent posterior on MNIST. Baselines will include traditional MCMC methods (e.g., SMC, GGNS), simulation-driven variational approaches (DIS, DDS, PIS), and various GFlowNet-based samplers with different objectives and exploration strategies. All methods will use consistent neural architectures for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics will include Monte Carlo estimates of the log-partition function (logZ), an importance-weighted variant (logZRW) emphasizing mode coverage, and sample-based metrics such as 2-Wasserstein distance. Ablation studies will assess the impact of local search, Langevin parametrization, and learning the forward process variance. Experiments will also analyze scalability with dimensionality and the efficiency of the proposed local search mechanism.
85ec455bcdc8f93dcb6955a7aec2cc05ba37f864.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel local search-based exploration technique for off-policy diffusion samplers, leveraging parallel MALA and a replay buffer to improve sample quality and prevent mode collapse. It systematically benchmarks and unifies prior diffusion-structured inference methods under a common codebase, enabling rigorous comparisons. The approach extends GFlowNet training with architectural and objective-based innovations, such as Langevin parametrization and flexible credit assignment, and demonstrates their effectiveness in both unconditional and conditional generative modeling. The framework is designed for extensibility, supporting learned forward and backward processes and variable noise schedules, thereby broadening the applicability of diffusion-based amortized inference.

85fa07886672bc19429295ea7f69c3f2888fe80f.title: Neural Collapse Inspired Feature-Classifier Alignment for Few-Shot Class Incremental Learning
85fa07886672bc19429295ea7f69c3f2888fe80f.research_question: How can feature-classifier alignment be optimally maintained in few-shot class-incremental learning (FSCIL) to mitigate catastrophic forgetting and improve recognition performance across both old and novel classes?
85fa07886672bc19429295ea7f69c3f2888fe80f.hypothesis: Pre-assigning a fixed, optimal feature-classifier alignment inspired by the neural collapse phenomenon, and training models to align features with these fixed prototypes using a specialized loss function, will preserve alignment across incremental learning sessions and outperform existing FSCIL methods in terms of accuracy and resistance to catastrophic forgetting.
85fa07886672bc19429295ea7f69c3f2888fe80f.proposed_method: A novel FSCIL framework is proposed in which classifier prototypes for all classes (both base and incremental) are pre-assigned as a simplex Equiangular Tight Frame (ETF), ensuring maximal separation and optimal geometric alignment. These prototypes remain fixed throughout all training sessions. The model consists of a backbone network followed by a projection layer; during the base session, both are trained, while in incremental sessions, only the projection layer is fine-tuned. A dot-regression (DR) loss is employed, which pulls normalized features toward their corresponding fixed ETF prototypes, omitting the push term present in cross-entropy loss. A small memory buffer retains mean features of old classes to further stabilize incremental updates.
85fa07886672bc19429295ea7f69c3f2888fe80f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard FSCIL benchmarks: miniImageNet, CIFAR-100, and CUB-200. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as ALICE, C-FSCIL, and others, using average and final session classification accuracy as primary evaluation metrics. Ablation studies will be performed to isolate the effects of the ETF classifier and DR loss, and cosine similarity analyses will be used to assess feature-classifier alignment. A small memory of mean features per class will be used for old classes during incremental sessions, following common FSCIL protocols.
85fa07886672bc19429295ea7f69c3f2888fe80f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first FSCIL framework that pre-assigns and fixes a neural collapse-inspired feature-classifier alignment across all sessions, avoiding optimization conflicts and misalignment. The use of a fixed ETF classifier for the entire label space and a dot-regression loss to drive features toward these prototypes is novel in the FSCIL context. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that this approach preserves neural collapse optimality even under class and sample imbalance. Empirical results are expected to surpass state-of-the-art FSCIL methods, with significant improvements in both average and final session accuracy.

86010eada916be09eb0fd134814d4184cd36e91e.title: OpenVLThinker: Complex Vision-Language Reasoning via Iterative SFT-RL Cycles
86010eada916be09eb0fd134814d4184cd36e91e.research_question: Can an open-source large vision-language model (LVLM) be enabled to perform complex, chain-of-thought reasoning in multimodal (vision-language) tasks, achieving reliable self-reflection, planning, and correction, and how can training strategies be designed to maximize such reasoning capabilities with limited data?
86010eada916be09eb0fd134814d4184cd36e91e.hypothesis: Iteratively alternating between supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with chain-of-thought demonstrations and reinforcement learning (RL) using a curriculum based on data difficulty will synergistically enhance the complex reasoning abilities of LVLMs, enabling them to approach or surpass the performance of proprietary models on challenging visual reasoning benchmarks, even with significantly less training data.
86010eada916be09eb0fd134814d4184cd36e91e.proposed_method: A novel iterative training framework is proposed that alternates between supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) to enhance complex reasoning in LVLMs. In each iteration, SFT is performed using chain-of-thought (CoT) demonstrations distilled from a text-based reasoning model (e.g., QwQ-32B) applied to image captions generated by the LVLM, with careful filtering to avoid excessive verbosity and repetitive reflections. Following SFT, RL is applied using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) on a curriculum of data sources categorized by difficulty, where the model is first trained on medium-difficulty data and then on hard-difficulty data within each iteration. The process is repeated for multiple cycles, with each new iteration generating improved reasoning traces from the latest model, thus progressively refining the model’s reasoning skills and visual grounding.
86010eada916be09eb0fd134814d4184cd36e91e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using Qwen2.5-VL-7B as the base LVLM, with three iterations of the SFT-RL cycle. Training data will be sourced from 14 established vision-language datasets overlapping with MathV360K, with 500 examples per source for initial SFT and 3K-6K examples per difficulty level for RL, totaling 12K samples per iteration. Evaluation will be performed on six benchmarks: MathVista, MathVerse, MathVision (math reasoning), MMMU-Pro, EMMA (general reasoning), and HallusionBench (perception/hallucination), using exact match and MathRuler grader metrics. Baselines will include the base model, proprietary models (GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet), and concurrent open-source LVLMs and reasoning models at similar scale (e.g., R1-VL-7B, VLAA-Thinker-7B), with all models evaluated under the same settings and hardware.
86010eada916be09eb0fd134814d4184cd36e91e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is among the first to demonstrate that iterative SFT-RL cycles can reliably induce advanced chain-of-thought reasoning, self-reflection, and correction behaviors in open-source LVLMs for complex vision-language tasks. The method achieves state-of-the-art or competitive results with only 1/10 the data used by concurrent methods, highlighting the efficiency of the iterative strategy. Additionally, the research provides new insights into the role of SFT in surfacing reasoning actions and the effectiveness of curriculum RL in maximizing the utility of challenging data, offering a generalizable framework for multimodal reasoning model development.

8608e998484ed254e0efc42feedcbbfd4b13e3e8.title: Switchable Online Knowledge Distillation
8608e998484ed254e0efc42feedcbbfd4b13e3e8.research_question: How can the performance of online knowledge distillation be improved, particularly for student models, in the presence of a large gap between teacher and student networks? What strategies can be developed to quantify and adaptively manage this gap during training to enhance knowledge transfer and model performance?
8608e998484ed254e0efc42feedcbbfd4b13e3e8.hypothesis: An adaptive, switchable training strategy that quantifies and manages the distillation gap between teacher and student networks during training will improve student model performance in online knowledge distillation, especially when there is a large capacity or accuracy gap between teacher and student.
8608e998484ed254e0efc42feedcbbfd4b13e3e8.proposed_method: A novel framework, Switchable Online Knowledge Distillation (SwitOKD), is proposed to address the adverse effects of a large distillation gap between teacher and student networks during online knowledge distillation. The method quantifies the distillation gap at the training phase using the L1 norm of the gradient for the KL divergence loss between the softened outputs of teacher and student. SwitOKD employs an adaptive switching strategy between two training modes: learning mode, where both teacher and student are trained reciprocally, and expert mode, where the teacher's parameters are frozen and only the student continues learning.
