An adaptive switching threshold, derived from the relative progress of teacher and student, determines when to switch between these modes to maintain an appropriate distillation gap. The switching threshold is dynamically adjusted based on the normalized difference between the student and teacher predictions and their alignment with ground truth labels, ensuring effective knowledge transfer throughout training. The framework is further extended to multi-network settings with two fundamental topologies: multiple teachers to one student and one teacher to multiple students.
8608e998484ed254e0efc42feedcbbfd4b13e3e8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification datasets including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, and ImageNet. Student-teacher pairs will be constructed using various backbone architectures such as MobileNet, MobileNetV2, ResNet, and Wide ResNet, with different capacity gaps to assess the method's robustness. Baseline methods for comparison will include Deep Mutual Learning (DML), KDCL, and conventional knowledge distillation approaches. Evaluation metrics will primarily be classification accuracy and loss values for both student and teacher networks. The experimental setup includes ablation studies on the effectiveness of the adaptive switching threshold, reciprocal training, and temperature parameter, as well as scalability tests in multi-network scenarios. Hyperparameters such as learning rate, batch size, optimizer type, and temperature will be systematically varied to validate the method's effectiveness.
8608e998484ed254e0efc42feedcbbfd4b13e3e8.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a formal quantification of the distillation gap during training, rather than relying on test-phase accuracy, and adaptively manages this gap through a novel switching strategy. The adaptive switching threshold provides a principled criterion for transitioning between learning and expert modes, optimizing the knowledge transfer process for the student. The framework is designed to extend the effective lifetime of online knowledge distillation, particularly in cases of large teacher-student gaps, and is generalizable to multi-network settings. Extensive experiments demonstrate superior student performance and competitive teacher performance compared to state-of-the-art online distillation methods.

860c8de4fdac38695ff6860dd15312f1079c6117.title: Beyond Reverse KL: Generalizing Direct Preference Optimization with Diverse Divergence Constraints
860c8de4fdac38695ff6860dd15312f1079c6117.research_question: How can the Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) framework for aligning large language models with human preferences be generalized to incorporate a broader class of divergence constraints, and what are the effects of these divergences on alignment performance, generation diversity, and model calibration?
860c8de4fdac38695ff6860dd15312f1079c6117.hypothesis: Generalizing DPO to support a variety of f-divergence constraints, including Jensen-Shannon, forward KL, and α-divergences, will enable more flexible and efficient alignment of language models with human preferences, achieving a better trade-off between alignment accuracy and generation diversity, and improving divergence efficiency and calibration compared to traditional RLHF and PPO-based methods.
860c8de4fdac38695ff6860dd15312f1079c6117.proposed_method: A generalized framework for Direct Preference Optimization (f-DPO) will be developed, extending the original DPO approach to support a wide range of f-divergence constraints beyond reverse KL. The method formulates the alignment objective as a constrained optimization problem, maximizing expected reward under an f-divergence regularization between the finetuned and reference policies. By leveraging the Karush–Kuhn–Tucker (KKT) conditions, a closed-form mapping between the reward function and the optimal policy is derived for a broad class of divergences, eliminating the need to estimate normalization constants in the Bradley-Terry model. The approach enables supervised learning-based fine-tuning of language models using preference datasets, with the divergence constraint parameterized by the chosen f-divergence. The loss function is constructed using the negative log-likelihood of pairwise preferences, where the reward is expressed in terms of the model and reference policy probabilities and the selected divergence.
860c8de4fdac38695ff6860dd15312f1079c6117.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple datasets, including the IMDB-sentiment dataset, Anthropic HH dataset, and MT-bench, to evaluate the proposed f-DPO framework. Baselines will include PPO-based methods with various divergence penalties (applied both in the reward and as a separate loss regularization term). Evaluation metrics will include alignment accuracy, predictive entropy, self-BLEU, distinct-n metrics for diversity, and Expected Calibration Error (ECE) for calibration. For generation quality, pairwise comparisons will be performed using the MT-bench benchmark with GPT-4 as the judge. Experiments will systematically vary the divergence constraint (reverse KL, forward KL, Jensen-Shannon, and α-divergences with different α values), and analyze the trade-offs between alignment and diversity, as well as the impact on model calibration.
860c8de4fdac38695ff6860dd15312f1079c6117.novelty_claims: The proposed framework generalizes DPO to a broad class of f-divergence constraints, enabling flexible and efficient alignment of language models without the need for reinforcement learning, reward model estimation, or normalization constant computation. The method provides a closed-form mapping between reward and optimal policy for many divergences, facilitating stable and supervised optimization. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior divergence efficiency and a more nuanced balance between alignment and diversity compared to PPO-based baselines. Theoretical analysis establishes a bound between model calibration error and divergence, and experiments validate that improved divergence efficiency leads to better calibration. This approach introduces greater flexibility for fine-tuning LLMs to meet diverse application requirements.

86478f285356b5c8d27423e6b939634d9e010fba.title: Progressive Prompts: Continual Learning for Language Models
86478f285356b5c8d27423e6b939634d9e010fba.research_question: How can continual learning be achieved in large-scale language models to enable forward transfer and prevent catastrophic forgetting, while minimizing memory and computational overhead?
86478f285356b5c8d27423e6b939634d9e010fba.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that learning and progressively concatenating task-specific soft prompts, while keeping the base language model frozen, will enable effective continual learning by supporting both forward transfer and resistance to catastrophic forgetting, without the need for data replay or a large number of task-specific parameters.
86478f285356b5c8d27423e6b939634d9e010fba.proposed_method: A novel continual learning framework, termed Progressive Prompts, will be developed for transformer-based language models. For each new task, a separate soft prompt (a set of trainable embeddings) will be learned and sequentially concatenated with previously learned prompts, which remain frozen. The base model parameters will remain fixed throughout all tasks, and only the current task's prompt parameters will be updated during training. To enhance training stability and performance, prompt embeddings will be reparameterized using a residual multi-layer perceptron (MLP), where the output is the sum of the MLP transformation and the original prompt embedding. After training on each task, the MLP parameters can be discarded, retaining only the reparameterized prompt. This approach is designed to be model-agnostic and applicable to any transformer-based architecture.
86478f285356b5c8d27423e6b939634d9e010fba.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard continual learning benchmarks for text classification, including AG News, Amazon Reviews, Yelp Reviews, DBpedia, and Yahoo Answers, as well as extended benchmarks with up to 15 tasks incorporating GLUE, SuperGLUE, and IMDB datasets. Both BERT-base (encoder-only) and T5-large (encoder-decoder) models will be evaluated. Multiple task orders and dataset sizes (20, 200, 1000 samples per class) will be used to assess robustness. Baselines for comparison will include finetuning, EWC, A-GEM, experience replay, MBPA++, IDBR, per-task prompt tuning, prompt tuning, LFPT5, and multi-task learning. Evaluation metrics will include average test accuracy across all tasks, as well as forward and backward transfer scores. Early stopping will be performed using validation accuracy, and experiments will be repeated across multiple runs for statistical reliability.
86478f285356b5c8d27423e6b939634d9e010fba.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a memory- and parameter-efficient continual learning method for language models that does not require data replay or large numbers of task-specific parameters. By progressively concatenating learned prompts and keeping previous prompts and the base model frozen, the method prevents catastrophic forgetting while enabling forward transfer. The residual MLP reparameterization of prompt embeddings further stabilizes and improves prompt tuning. This framework is model-agnostic and demonstrates significant improvements over state-of-the-art continual learning methods, especially in few-shot and long task sequence settings.

865acaf2f40a14819ab44a6fb98b0937cc475555.title: Maximum Entropy Reinforcement Learning via Energy-Based Normalizing Flow
865acaf2f40a14819ab44a6fb98b0937cc475555.research_question: How can maximum-entropy reinforcement learning for continuous action spaces be improved to enable exact soft value function computation, efficient sampling, and unified policy optimization without relying on Monte Carlo approximations or alternating actor-critic updates?
865acaf2f40a14819ab44a6fb98b0937cc475555.hypothesis: A unified maximum-entropy reinforcement learning framework based on energy-based normalizing flows can enable exact soft value function computation, efficient multi-modal action sampling, and improved policy optimization performance compared to traditional actor-critic-based MaxEnt RL methods.
865acaf2f40a14819ab44a6fb98b0937cc475555.proposed_method: The proposed method models the maximum-entropy reinforcement learning (MaxEnt RL) policy using energy-based normalizing flows (EBFlow), resulting in a unified framework where the policy, soft Q-function, and soft value function are parameterized by a single flow-based model. The policy is represented as a state-conditioned normalizing flow, allowing for both the unnormalized density and its sampler to be defined in closed form. This design enables the integration of policy evaluation and policy improvement into a single objective, eliminating the need for alternating updates. The soft value function is computed exactly via the closed-form normalizing constant of the flow, avoiding Monte Carlo approximations. Additional techniques, such as learnable reward shifting (LRS) and shifting-based clipped double Q-learning (SCDQ), are incorporated to enhance training stability and address value overestimation. For inference, deterministic policy extraction is supported by architectural constraints on the flow, enabling efficient maximization of the soft Q-function.
865acaf2f40a14819ab44a6fb98b0937cc475555.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on five standard MuJoCo continuous control environments (Hopper-v4, HalfCheetah-v4, Walker2d-v4, Ant-v4, Humanoid-v4) and six high-dimensional robotic tasks simulated in Omniverse Isaac Gym (Ant, Humanoid, Ingenuity, ANYmal, AllegroHand, FrankaCabinet). The proposed method is compared against widely-adopted baselines including Soft Q-Learning (SQL), Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), Twin Delayed DDPG (TD3), DDPG, and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). Evaluation metrics include total episodic return and training stability, with results averaged over five random seeds and reported with 95% confidence intervals. Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of the proposed training and inference enhancements, and both stochastic and deterministic policy variants are evaluated.
865acaf2f40a14819ab44a6fb98b0937cc475555.novelty_claims: The proposed framework unifies policy evaluation and improvement into a single objective using energy-based normalizing flows, enabling exact soft value function computation without Monte Carlo approximation. The method supports efficient sampling and expressive multi-modal action distributions. The incorporation of learnable reward shifting and shifting-based clipped double Q-learning enhances training stability and addresses overestimation bias. Deterministic policy inference is enabled under specific flow architectures, further improving performance. Experimental results demonstrate superior or comparable performance to state-of-the-art baselines on both standard benchmarks and challenging high-dimensional robotic tasks.

8664c12b056b02e1cdee9090027db9c777c16075.title: Composing Linear Layers from Irreducibles
8664c12b056b02e1cdee9090027db9c777c16075.research_question: Can the functionality of standard linear layers in neural networks be synthesized from a minimal set of geometric primitives, and does such a compositional approach enable parameter-efficient yet expressive transformations for use in large-scale models such as language models?
8664c12b056b02e1cdee9090027db9c777c16075.hypothesis: Linear transformations in neural networks can be efficiently and expressively composed from a small set of geometric primitives, specifically bivectors in Clifford algebra, resulting in parameter-efficient modules that maintain competitive performance with conventional dense and structured approximations.
8664c12b056b02e1cdee9090027db9c777c16075.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed wherein linear layers are constructed as compositions of geometric primitives, specifically bivectors, within the Clifford algebra. The method parametrizes linear transformations using rotors—elements of the Spin group—generated by the exponential map of bivectors. A differentiable, closed-form algorithm is introduced to decompose arbitrary bivectors into sums of mutually commuting simple bivectors, each admitting an exact exponential solution, thus enabling efficient and differentiable rotor construction. These rotor-based modules are then composed in parallel and depth, with pooling and normalization, to form general linear maps between arbitrary input and output dimensions. The approach leverages the algebraic structure of Clifford algebra to achieve exponential parameter reduction, using only O(log^2 d) parameters versus O(d^2) for dense layers, and is fully compatible with gradient-based optimization.
8664c12b056b02e1cdee9090027db9c777c16075.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted by substituting key, query, and value linear projections in attention layers of pre-trained language models (LLaMa-3.2 1B and Qwen-2.5 1.5B) with rotor-based layers. Performance is evaluated on language modeling datasets (Wikitext2, C4, PTB) using log-perplexity and on multiple-choice benchmarks (Arc Challenge, HellaSwag) using accuracy. Baselines include low-rank (r=1,4) and Block-Hadamard (depth 1) approximations, with all methods matched for training protocol and hyperparameters. Both layerwise replacement and end-to-end training scenarios are tested, including a full-network experiment on FMNIST. Parameter counts, FLOPs, and wall-clock runtime are measured to assess efficiency, and architectural ablations (varying rotor width and depth) are performed to analyze expressivity and performance trade-offs.
8664c12b056b02e1cdee9090027db9c777c16075.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces an algebraic decomposition of linear layers into compositions of geometric primitives (bivectors) within Clifford algebra, enabling exponential parameter reduction while maintaining expressivity. A differentiable, closed-form decomposition algorithm for arbitrary bivectors is developed, allowing seamless integration with autograd and gradient-based training. The method demonstrates, for the first time, that rotor-based modules can match or outperform established parameter-efficient baselines in large language models with orders-of-magnitude fewer parameters. The approach opens new directions for interpretable, modular, and hardware-efficient neural architectures by leveraging the compositional structure of geometric algebra.

868119b5610b895acea98e36bdf4cbb6d3e6e9ef.title: Deconstructing What Makes a Good Optimizer for Language Models
868119b5610b895acea98e36bdf4cbb6d3e6e9ef.research_question: What are the key characteristics and requirements that make an optimizer effective and robust for training large-scale autoregressive language models, and how do different optimizers compare in terms of performance and hyperparameter stability across model scales and architecture variants?
868119b5610b895acea98e36bdf4cbb6d3e6e9ef.hypothesis: Adaptive optimizers, particularly those providing per-parameter or per-layer adaptivity, are necessary for achieving both high performance and stability to hyperparameter choices in autoregressive language model training. Specifically, adaptivity on the last layer and LayerNorm parameters is hypothesized to be critical, while simpler or memory-efficient variants may suffice for other parameters.
868119b5610b895acea98e36bdf4cbb6d3e6e9ef.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical study will be conducted to compare several optimization algorithms, including SGD, Adam, Adafactor (with momentum), Lion, and Sophia, in the context of autoregressive language modeling. The methodology involves systematic sweeps over key hyperparameters (learning rate, momentum, weight decay, warmup, batch size, epsilon, and beta2) for each optimizer across multiple model scales (150M, 300M, 600M, 1.2B parameters) and two transformer architecture variants. Additionally, simplified variants of Adam, such as Signum (signed momentum) and a novel per-layer adaptive optimizer termed 'Adalayer', will be developed and evaluated. Ablation studies will be performed to isolate the impact of adaptivity on different network components, particularly the last layer and LayerNorm parameters, by constructing hybrid optimizers that selectively apply adaptivity.
868119b5610b895acea98e36bdf4cbb6d3e6e9ef.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using decoder-only transformer language models trained on the C4 dataset, tokenized with the T5 tokenizer. Models of varying sizes (150M, 300M, 600M, 1.2B non-embedding parameters) will be trained using a consistent batch size of 256 and sequence length of 512, with training steps scaled to maintain a 'chinchilla optimal' token-to-parameter ratio. Both standard models (with QKLayerNorm and z-loss) and variants without these features will be evaluated. Baselines will include standard implementations of AdamW, SGD, Lion, and a custom Adafactor with momentum. Evaluation will focus on final validation loss, with robustness assessed via sweeps across hyperparameters. Additional ablations will examine the effect of training duration, architecture variants, and the selective application of adaptive methods to specific parameter subsets.
868119b5610b895acea98e36bdf4cbb6d3e6e9ef.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a rigorous, large-scale comparison of multiple optimizers for autoregressive language modeling, extending beyond prior work by systematically evaluating both optimal performance and hyperparameter stability across model scales and architecture variants. The study will dissect the necessity and granularity of adaptivity by introducing and analyzing simplified optimizer variants, including a novel per-layer adaptive optimizer (Adalayer) and hybrid approaches that selectively apply adaptivity. The research aims to provide actionable insights into which optimizer components are essential, potentially enabling more memory-efficient training without sacrificing performance or stability, and challenging prevailing assumptions about the necessity of full adaptivity throughout the network.

868d72e509e4f0264900aa088843264b5460cb78.title: Differentially-Private Clustering of Easy Instances
868d72e509e4f0264900aa088843264b5460cb78.research_question: How can practical and simple differentially private clustering algorithms be developed that provide strong utility guarantees, especially for datasets where clusters are well-separated or otherwise 'easy' to cluster?
868d72e509e4f0264900aa088843264b5460cb78.hypothesis: It is possible to design simple and implementable differentially private clustering algorithms that achieve strong utility and improved sample complexity on 'easy' instances, such as well-separated clusters, by leveraging reductions to simpler clustering subproblems and by privately aggregating results from non-private clustering algorithms.
868d72e509e4f0264900aa088843264b5460cb78.proposed_method: A new framework is proposed that first identifies whether the input data admits a partition into k well-separated clusters using a private 'niceness' test. If the test passes, two algorithmic strategies are considered: (1) PrivatekAverages, which clusters the data non-privately and then computes the average of each cluster with added noise to ensure privacy, and (2) PrivatekNoisyCenters, which selects a representative k-tuple and adds Gaussian noise to each point to generate private cluster centers. The framework reduces standard clustering tasks, such as k-means and learning mixtures of Gaussians, to the k-tuple clustering problem, allowing the use of these private subroutines as building blocks. The approach carefully analyzes stability and sensitivity to ensure that the privacy guarantees are preserved even when the initial clustering is performed non-privately, provided the data is 'nice' or nearly so.
868d72e509e4f0264900aa088843264b5460cb78.experiment_details: Empirical evaluation will be conducted on synthetic datasets that are constructed to exhibit well-separated clusters, simulating 'easy' clustering instances. The proposed private algorithms (PrivatekAverages and PrivatekNoisyCenters) will be compared against non-private baselines and, where feasible, other differentially private clustering algorithms from the literature. Evaluation metrics will include clustering accuracy (e.g., misclassification rate or distance to true centers), utility loss compared to non-private clustering, and privacy-utility tradeoff curves. Experiments will also analyze sample complexity and the effect of varying cluster separation and dimensionality on performance.
868d72e509e4f0264900aa088843264b5460cb78.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a modular and practical framework for differentially private clustering that leverages reductions to the k-tuple clustering problem, enabling the use of simple, implementable algorithms with improved sample complexity. The algorithms are designed to be effective on finite, real-world datasets, overcoming limitations of prior theoretical methods that suffered from impractical constants or complexity. The framework generalizes to both k-means clustering under stability assumptions and private learning of mixtures of Gaussians, providing weaker separation requirements and lower sample complexity than previous methods. The work advances the state of the art in practical differentially private clustering by bridging the gap between theoretical feasibility and real-world applicability.

86e8d3a19a8a871d21d8561d2bc85449cf32d124.title: DexGraspNet 2.0: Learning Generative Dexterous Grasping in Large-scale Synthetic Cluttered Scenes
86e8d3a19a8a871d21d8561d2bc85449cf32d124.research_question: How can dexterous robotic hands achieve robust and generalizable grasping in cluttered scenes, given the challenges of data scarcity and complex grasp distributions?
86e8d3a19a8a871d21d8561d2bc85449cf32d124.hypothesis: A generative two-stage grasping framework, leveraging a large-scale synthetic dataset and a diffusion model conditioned on local geometric features, will enable efficient learning of diverse and high-quality dexterous grasps in cluttered scenes, resulting in superior generalization and sim-to-real transfer compared to existing regression and sampling-based methods.
86e8d3a19a8a871d21d8561d2bc85449cf32d124.proposed_method: A two-stage generative grasping method will be developed. The first stage employs a seed point proposal module that processes a single-view depth point cloud to extract point-wise local features and identify graspable regions via object segmentation and graspness scoring. High-scoring points are selected as seed points, and their local features are passed to the second stage. The second stage consists of a grasp pose generation module that models the conditional distribution of grasp poses (translation, rotation, and joint angles) relative to each seed point. A denoising diffusion probabilistic model is used to generate diverse wrist poses (translation and rotation) conditioned on local features, while a deterministic MLP predicts the hand joint angles. The architecture is trained end-to-end, with joint losses on segmentation, graspness, diffusion, and joint angle prediction, enabling the model to learn from the multimodal and complex grasp distributions present in large-scale synthetic cluttered scenes.
86e8d3a19a8a871d21d8561d2bc85449cf32d124.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the DexGraspNet 2.0 benchmark, which contains 1319 objects, 8270 synthetic cluttered scenes, and 427 million annotated grasps. The model will be evaluated in simulation using the IsaacGym simulator, where the success rate is measured by the ability to lift objects in various scene types (dense, random, loose) and object sets (GraspNet-1Billion, ShapeNet). Baselines for comparison include HGC-Net, GraspTTA, and ISAGrasp, with modifications for cluttered scenes. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of local feature conditioning, decomposed pose modeling, and scene diversity. Additional experiments will assess scalability by varying the number of scenes and grasps, and the method will be tested on gripper grasping using the GraspNet-1Billion benchmark with average precision as the metric. Real-world experiments will use a LEAP hand on a UR-5 arm and a Franka Panda gripper, with depth restoration applied to sensor data, and success rates measured on multi-object tabletop scenes.
86e8d3a19a8a871d21d8561d2bc85449cf32d124.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first large-scale synthetic benchmark for dexterous grasping in cluttered scenes, providing unprecedented diversity and scale. A novel two-stage generative grasping method is proposed, combining a diffusion model conditioned on local geometric features with a seed point proposal mechanism, enabling effective learning from complex, multimodal grasp distributions. The approach is designed for both dexterous hands and grippers, supporting unified grasping across hand types. The method demonstrates strong sim-to-real transfer, achieving high real-world success rates without real-world training data, and provides systematic analysis of dataset scaling and architectural design choices.

871c35376504be03a4a90fbcc72b5f9a1ff8a4d1.title: Wasserstein Policy Optimization
871c35376504be03a4a90fbcc72b5f9a1ff8a4d1.research_question: How can reinforcement learning in continuous action spaces be improved by leveraging alternative mathematical frameworks for policy optimization, particularly to enable efficient and generalizable learning for stochastic policies with arbitrary distributions?
871c35376504be03a4a90fbcc72b5f9a1ff8a4d1.hypothesis: Policy optimization methods derived from Wasserstein gradient flows can provide a more general and effective update rule for stochastic policies in continuous action spaces, leading to improved sample efficiency, stability, and scalability compared to existing policy gradient and deterministic policy gradient methods.
871c35376504be03a4a90fbcc72b5f9a1ff8a4d1.proposed_method: A novel actor-critic algorithm, Wasserstein Policy Optimization (WPO), will be developed by approximating Wasserstein gradient flow over the space of all policies, projected into a finite-dimensional parameter space such as neural network weights. The method will derive a closed-form update for the policy parameters by minimizing the KL divergence between the original and updated policy distributions, using the Fisher information matrix as a local quadratic approximation. The update will combine elements of both deterministic and classic policy gradients by exploiting the gradient of the action-value function with respect to the action, while supporting arbitrary stochastic policies without requiring the reparameterization trick. Practical extensions will include diagonal Gaussian policies, variance rescaling to ensure numerical stability, and KL regularization to prevent premature convergence to deterministic policies.
871c35376504be03a4a90fbcc72b5f9a1ff8a4d1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the DeepMind Control Suite, a set of continuous control tasks with varying action space dimensionality, as well as a magnetic confinement fusion task involving control of a simulated tokamak device. The proposed method will be compared against established baselines including Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG), Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), and Maximum a Posteriori Policy Optimization (MPO). Evaluation metrics will include average episode return and learning speed, with experiments designed to test scalability by increasing action space dimensionality through combined environment replicas. Training setups will use distributed actors and replay buffers, with consistent hyperparameters across tasks to assess robustness and generalization. Additional ablations will analyze the impact of policy parameterization, KL regularization, and critic update strategies.
871c35376504be03a4a90fbcc72b5f9a1ff8a4d1.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new policy gradient update derived from Wasserstein gradient flows, enabling closed-form, general, and efficient updates for stochastic policies with arbitrary distributions. Unlike prior methods, the approach does not require the reparameterization trick and is applicable to both discrete and continuous action spaces. The method combines advantages of deterministic and stochastic policy gradients, and demonstrates improved scalability and stability in high-dimensional action spaces. This constitutes a fundamental algorithmic advance in reinforcement learning, with potential applicability to a wide range of continuous control domains.

8724579d3f126e753a0451d98ff57b165f722e72.title: Are aligned neural networks adversarially aligned?
8724579d3f126e753a0451d98ff57b165f722e72.research_question: To what extent do alignment techniques for neural language models ensure robustness against adversarially constructed inputs, particularly in both text-only and multimodal (vision-language) settings?
8724579d3f126e753a0451d98ff57b165f722e72.hypothesis: Current alignment techniques for language models do not guarantee adversarial robustness; sufficiently strong adversarial attacks, especially in multimodal settings, can induce harmful or toxic outputs even from aligned models.
8724579d3f126e753a0451d98ff57b165f722e72.proposed_method: The proposed research will systematically evaluate the adversarial robustness of aligned language models by developing and applying both existing and novel adversarial attack methods. For text-only models, the methodology will involve constructing adversarial prompts under realistic chat-based constraints and testing whether these can induce toxic outputs, using both state-of-the-art NLP attacks and brute-force search to establish upper and lower bounds on attack effectiveness. For multimodal models, the approach will leverage differentiable end-to-end optimization to generate adversarial images that, when paired with benign text prompts, cause the model to emit targeted harmful outputs. The research will also introduce new evaluation test cases that guarantee the existence of adversarial examples, enabling a rigorous assessment of attack power and model vulnerability.
8724579d3f126e753a0451d98ff57b165f722e72.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of publicly available language models, including unaligned (GPT-2), instruction-tuned but unaligned (LLaMA), and alignment-finetuned (Vicuna) models. Attack effectiveness will be measured using both quantitative metrics (attack success rates, required perturbation magnitude, and pass rates on guaranteed adversarial test cases) and qualitative inspection of generated outputs. For multimodal models, open-source implementations such as MiniGPT-4, LLaVA, and LLaMAAdapter will be targeted, with attacks evaluated on their ability to induce toxic completions via adversarial image perturbations. Datasets for benign conversations will be sourced from OpenAssistant, while toxic target phrases will be drawn from established benchmarks. Evaluation will include both automated toxicity detection (substring matching) and manual review to assess the nature of harmful outputs.
8724579d3f126e753a0451d98ff57b165f722e72.novelty_claims: This research proposes a unified framework for evaluating adversarial alignment in both text-only and multimodal language models, introduces rigorous test cases that guarantee the existence of adversarial examples, and demonstrates that current NLP-based attacks are insufficiently powerful to reliably assess robustness. The methodology extends adversarial evaluation to vision-language models, showing that adversarial image perturbations can reliably induce harmful outputs in aligned systems. The work highlights critical gaps in current alignment and evaluation techniques, motivating the development of stronger attack methods and more robust alignment strategies.

8749494a63902a539468955660c2feb3dcb4e2e2.title: GLASS: Guided Latent Slot Diffusion for Object-Centric Learning
8749494a63902a539468955660c2feb3dcb4e2e2.research_question: How can object-centric learning methods be improved to robustly decompose real-world images containing multiple objects with complex textures and shapes into meaningful object representations, enabling a broad range of downstream tasks such as object discovery, compositional generation, and property prediction?
8749494a63902a539468955660c2feb3dcb4e2e2.hypothesis: Learning slot representations in the space of images generated by pre-trained diffusion models, combined with both semantic and instance guidance, will yield more precise, instance-centric, and versatile object embeddings than existing slot-attention methods, thereby improving performance on downstream tasks in real-world scenes.
8749494a63902a539468955660c2feb3dcb4e2e2.proposed_method: A novel object-centric learning framework, Guided Latent Slot Diffusion (GLASS), is developed that integrates a slot-attention module with a pre-trained diffusion decoder and a semantic-instance guidance mechanism. The approach begins by generating captions for input images using a large vision-language model, extracting relevant class labels, and constructing prompts for a pre-trained diffusion model (e.g., Stable Diffusion) to generate synthetic images. Semantic guidance is provided by extracting and refining cross-attention maps from the diffusion model to produce pseudo-semantic masks, while instance guidance is enforced via an MLP decoder that reconstructs encoder features, counteracting semantic drift. Slot representations are matched to semantic masks using Hungarian matching, and the model is trained end-to-end with a composite loss that includes reconstruction, semantic guidance, and instance guidance terms. Training is performed in two phases: first, optimizing the slot-attention and MLP decoder for instance binding, followed by joint training with the diffusion decoder for high-fidelity image generation.
8749494a63902a539468955660c2feb3dcb4e2e2.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on several real-world and synthetic datasets, including COCO, VOC, Object365, and CLEVRTex. The evaluation covers tasks such as instance-level and semantic-level object discovery, zero-shot segmentation, conditional image generation, compositional generation, and instance-level property prediction. Baselines include state-of-the-art slot-attention and object-centric learning models (e.g., DINOSAUR, StableLSD, SPOT, SlotDiffusion), as well as weakly- and semi-supervised segmentation methods and foundation model-based approaches. Metrics used include mean Intersection over Union (mIoU), mean Best Overlap (mBO), SO-PO-GO segmentation ambiguity metrics, PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, FID for generation quality, and accuracy/MSE for property prediction. Ablation studies investigate the contributions of semantic and instance guidance, encoder architectures, and guidance signal sources. The experimental setup also compares the method's performance under varying levels of supervision (e.g., generated captions vs. ground-truth labels).
8749494a63902a539468955660c2feb3dcb4e2e2.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to enable compositional generation of complex, realistic scenes using slot-attention on real-world images. It introduces a unique combination of semantic and instance guidance modules, leveraging pseudo-ground-truth masks generated from a diffusion model's cross-attention maps, and integrates these with a slot-attention framework trained entirely on generated images. The approach significantly reduces over- and under-segmentation (part-whole ambiguity) compared to previous methods, achieves state-of-the-art results in instance-level and semantic-level object discovery, and outperforms both weakly- and semi-supervised baselines, including those using more expensive supervision. Additionally, the method demonstrates superior slot embeddings for downstream tasks and is robust to different encoder architectures.

8761875ac265446cdf341c1b5614b04415b57b55.title: Tensor-Parallelism with Partially Synchronized Activations
8761875ac265446cdf341c1b5614b04415b57b55.research_question: Can large language models be efficiently trained and served using tensor-parallelism while reducing the need for full activation synchronization, thereby decreasing communication overhead without sacrificing model accuracy or scalability?
8761875ac265446cdf341c1b5614b04415b57b55.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by partially synchronizing only a subset of activation channels during tensor-parallel training and inference, communication bandwidth can be significantly reduced without incurring a notable loss in model accuracy or convergence stability.
8761875ac265446cdf341c1b5614b04415b57b55.proposed_method: A novel architecture, termed Communication-Aware Architecture for Tensor-parallelism (CAAT-Net), will be developed to replace the standard all-reduce operation in tensor-parallelism with a partial channel–reduce operation. In this approach, only a configurable fraction (p) of the hidden dimension channels are synchronized across devices, while the rest remain private to each device. The method requires architectural modifications to the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and attention layers to accommodate the new communication pattern, as well as careful placement of the reduction operation in the backward pass to ensure gradient correctness. Numerical stability is maintained by accumulating gradients in 32-bit precision during the all-reduce in the backward pass, while communication itself remains in 16-bit precision. Additionally, a scaling factor is applied to private channels to match the variance of shared channels, ensuring consistent signal propagation.
8761875ac265446cdf341c1b5614b04415b57b55.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale LLMs, including Llama2-7B, TinyLlama-1.1B, and a custom 130M parameter model, trained from scratch on the RedPajama dataset (up to 160B tokens for the largest model). Training will be distributed across multiple nodes and accelerators (e.g., 8 nodes with 8 accelerators each), with varying tensor-parallel dimensions (4, 8, 16) and synchronization fractions (p). Evaluation will be performed using zero-shot accuracy on a suite of benchmarks (LAMBADA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, PIQA, OpenBookQA, BOOL-Q, WikiText103), as well as validation loss. Baselines will include standard tensor-parallel models with full all-reduce, and comparisons will also be made to communication compression methods (random masking, Top-K masking). Metrics will include accuracy, validation loss, training throughput (tokens per second), and inference latency (Time-to-First-Token) across different hardware platforms (Intel Gaudi3, NVIDIA H100/A100).
8761875ac265446cdf341c1b5614b04415b57b55.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new tensor-parallel architecture that fundamentally alters the information flow by allowing only partial synchronization of activations, rather than compressing or pipelining communication. This approach enables up to 50% reduction in tensor-parallel communication bandwidth with no significant loss in pretraining accuracy and, in some cases, improved validation loss. The method is robust across model sizes and hardware platforms, and provides both training and inference speedup. Unlike prior work, the approach does not rely on lossy compression or asynchronous optimization, and is complementary to existing pipelining techniques.

87875a07976c26f82705de1fc70041169e5d652b.title: LeanDojo: Theorem Proving with Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
87875a07976c26f82705de1fc70041169e5d652b.research_question: How can language models be effectively leveraged for formal theorem proving in proof assistants, particularly addressing the challenge of premise selection and enabling reproducible, scalable research in this domain?
87875a07976c26f82705de1fc70041169e5d652b.hypothesis: Augmenting large language models with an explicit, retrieval-based premise selection mechanism and providing open-source tools and benchmarks will significantly improve the effectiveness and accessibility of automated theorem proving in Lean, outperforming non-retrieval and zero-shot LLM baselines.
87875a07976c26f82705de1fc70041169e5d652b.proposed_method: A comprehensive open-source toolkit, LeanDojo, will be developed to extract fine-grained theorem proving data from the Lean proof assistant and provide a robust programmatic interface for model interaction. The approach introduces a retrieval-augmented theorem prover, ReProver, which uses a Dense Passage Retriever-based module to select a small set of relevant premises accessible to the current proof state, leveraging program analysis to restrict retrieval to only those premises actually available in the environment. The retriever is trained with a contrastive loss using both in-file and random negative examples to improve premise discrimination. Retrieved premises are concatenated with the current proof state and input into an encoder-decoder Transformer (ByT5), which generates the next proof tactic. The system is trained end-to-end using supervised learning on human-written Lean proofs, and proof search is conducted via best-first search using the generated tactics.
87875a07976c26f82705de1fc70041169e5d652b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the newly constructed LeanDojo Benchmark, a large-scale dataset comprising 98,734 theorems and proofs from Lean's mathlib, with over 217,000 tactics and 130,000 premises. The benchmark features both random and challenging 'novel_premises' splits, the latter requiring generalization to theorems that depend on premises never seen during training. Baselines will include a direct tactic generation model (without retrieval), the tidy heuristic tactic, and GPT-4 in a zero-shot setting. Evaluation metrics for premise selection will include Recall@k and Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR), while theorem proving performance will be measured by Pass@1 (the proportion of theorems proved within a single attempt and a 10-minute wall-time limit). Additional evaluation will be performed on external datasets MiniF2F and ProofNet to assess generalization.
87875a07976c26f82705de1fc70041169e5d652b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first open-source, retrieval-augmented language model for formal theorem proving in Lean, supported by a robust toolkit for data extraction and programmatic interaction. It pioneers the use of accessible-premise retrieval via program analysis and the use of in-file hard negatives for premise selection. The LeanDojo Benchmark is one of the largest and most challenging datasets for theorem proving, featuring a split that explicitly tests generalization to unseen premises. The approach achieves strong results with modest computational resources and without reliance on proprietary datasets, thus substantially lowering the barrier for research and enabling reproducible, extensible work in machine learning for theorem proving.

879a7f5abdb7ab803d48172d4f0830965f989d46.title: Language Model Tokenizers Introduce Unfairness Between Languages
879a7f5abdb7ab803d48172d4f0830965f989d46.research_question: How can tokenization methods for language models be designed to ensure fair and equitable treatment across diverse languages, minimizing disparities in cost, latency, and context length for users of different linguistic backgrounds?
879a7f5abdb7ab803d48172d4f0830965f989d46.hypothesis: Training language models with a multilingually fair subword tokenizer, constructed through a principled merging of monolingual tokenizers and balanced parallel corpora, will significantly reduce disparities in tokenization length and associated fairness issues across languages compared to current subword, byte-level, and character-level tokenization approaches.
879a7f5abdb7ab803d48172d4f0830965f989d46.proposed_method: A new methodology will be developed to construct a multilingually fair subword tokenizer. The approach begins by training individual monolingual tokenizers for each target language using balanced and diverse parallel corpora, ensuring comprehensive coverage of linguistic features and scripts. These monolingual tokenizers will then be merged through an iterative process: starting with a base vocabulary (e.g., all byte values), the most frequently used tokens from the language with the highest tokenization premium will be added in each step, maintaining parity across languages. The resulting tokenizer will be designed to support all Unicode codepoints, likely building on UTF-8 encoding for efficiency. The final tokenizer will be used to train language models from scratch, ensuring that tokenization length for equivalent content is as close as possible across all supported languages.
879a7f5abdb7ab803d48172d4f0830965f989d46.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the FLORES-200 parallel corpus, which contains 2000 sentences translated into 200 languages, to systematically evaluate tokenization parity. The proposed tokenizer will be compared against existing English-centric, non-English-centric, multilingual, and byte-level tokenizers, including those used in models such as GPT-2, RoBERTa, ChatGPT, GPT-4, FlanT5, XLM-R, NLLB, M2M100, mT5, BLOOM, CANINE, and ByT5. Evaluation metrics will include tokenization premium (ratio of tokenized lengths for equivalent content), cost implications (tokens or characters per sentence), latency (processing time as a function of tokenized length), and context capacity (amount of content fitting within fixed model context windows). Baseline comparisons will assess both average and worst-case disparities across languages, and ablation studies will test the impact of parallel corpus diversity and vocabulary allocation strategies.
879a7f5abdb7ab803d48172d4f0830965f989d46.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled, two-stage process for constructing multilingually fair subword tokenizers by merging monolingual tokenizers with explicit parity constraints, a method not previously explored in the literature. It systematically addresses fairness in tokenization at the algorithmic level, rather than as an emergent property or post-hoc adjustment. The approach leverages balanced parallel corpora and iterative vocabulary allocation to minimize disparities in tokenization length, cost, latency, and context capacity across languages. This work aims to set a new standard for fairness in multilingual language model pretraining and deployment, with direct implications for equitable access to language technologies.

879f6ee24dd1f044f7b831a5c23cb23e1d104bb5.title: On Tackling Explanation Redundancy in Decision Trees
879f6ee24dd1f044f7b831a5c23cb23e1d104bb5.research_question: Can explanation redundancy in decision trees be formally characterized, and can efficient algorithms be developed to compute succinct, irreducible explanations for decision tree predictions, thereby improving their interpretability for high-risk and safety-critical applications?
879f6ee24dd1f044f7b831a5c23cb23e1d104bb5.hypothesis: Decision tree paths often contain redundant information that can be systematically identified and eliminated, and it is possible to design polynomial-time algorithms that compute logically rigorous, subset-minimal explanations (abductive and contrastive) that are more succinct than the original tree paths.
879f6ee24dd1f044f7b831a5c23cb23e1d104bb5.proposed_method: A formal framework will be developed to define and analyze explanation redundancy in decision trees, distinguishing between path-based and instance-specific explanations. The approach will introduce explanation functions as extensions of prime implicant explanations, establishing conditions for monotonicity and duality between abductive and contrastive explanations. Path explanation redundancy will be formalized, and its theoretical properties will be explored, including proofs that even optimal and sparse decision trees can exhibit significant redundancy. Polynomial-time algorithms will be designed for computing abductive and contrastive path explanations, including a novel propositional Horn encoding method and enumeration techniques leveraging SAT solvers as witness-producing NP-oracles. These algorithms will be capable of efficiently generating irreducible, subset-minimal explanations for any decision tree prediction.
879f6ee24dd1f044f7b831a5c23cb23e1d104bb5.experiment_details: Extensive experiments will be conducted on a wide range of publicly available datasets and decision trees, including those generated by different tree learning algorithms and those used in textbooks and prior research. The experiments will measure the prevalence and magnitude of path explanation redundancy, the performance and scalability of the proposed algorithms, and the succinctness of the computed explanations compared to original tree paths. Baselines will include standard decision tree paths and existing explanation methods, with evaluation metrics such as explanation length, computation time, and the proportion of redundant literals removed. The experimental setup will ensure coverage of both optimal and sparse decision trees, as well as trees with categorical and ordinal features.
879f6ee24dd1f044f7b831a5c23cb23e1d104bb5.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first comprehensive formalization of path explanation redundancy in decision trees and establishes that redundancy is ubiquitous, even in optimal and sparse trees. The proposed algorithms for computing subset-minimal abductive and contrastive explanations operate in polynomial time and are applicable to decision trees with arbitrary feature domains and multiple classes. The approach generalizes existing explanation frameworks by introducing path-specific variants and leveraging duality and enumeration properties. The results are expected to provide practical tools for generating succinct, logically rigorous explanations in high-risk and safety-critical domains, addressing a critical gap in interpretable machine learning.

87a318008035f14442077a384605f3edd40db7ba.title: Instance-Dependent Partial Label Learning
87a318008035f14442077a384605f3edd40db7ba.research_question: How can partial label learning be improved by modeling the instance-dependent nature of candidate label generation, and by leveraging latent label distributions to enhance predictive model training?
87a318008035f14442077a384605f3edd40db7ba.hypothesis: Modeling the instance-dependent candidate label generation process via latent label distributions and iteratively enhancing these distributions during training will yield superior predictive performance in partial label learning compared to existing methods that assume instance-independent random candidate label selection.
87a318008035f14442077a384605f3edd40db7ba.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that addresses instance-dependent partial label learning by associating each example with a latent label distribution, which reflects the degree to which each label describes the instance. The method begins with a warm-up phase where a predictive model is trained using a minimal loss over candidate labels. Subsequently, a label enhancement process is introduced, where the posterior density of the latent label distribution is approximated using a variational Dirichlet distribution parameterized by an inference model (a two-layer Graph Convolutional Network). The evidence lower bound (ELBO) is derived and optimized to recover the label distributions, leveraging both topological information from the feature space and the logical label matrix. The predictive model is then trained using an empirical risk estimator that fuses both the candidate labels and the recovered label distributions. This process of label enhancement and classifier training is performed iteratively in every epoch, allowing end-to-end optimization.
87a318008035f14442077a384605f3edd40db7ba.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both benchmark datasets (MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, Kuzushiji-MNIST, CIFAR-10) and real-world partial label learning datasets (Lost, Soccer Player, Yahoo!News, MSRCv2, BirdSong), as well as several UCI datasets (Yeast, Texture, Dermatology, Synthetic Control, 20Newsgroup). Datasets will be corrupted into partially labeled versions using both instance-dependent and uniform candidate label generation procedures. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art DNN-based and classical PLL methods such as PRODEN, RC, CC, D2CNN, GA, CLPL, PL-SVM, PL-KNN, IPAL, and PLLE. Evaluation metrics will focus on classification accuracy, and experiments will be repeated with multiple trials or cross-validation to ensure statistical significance. The same predictive model architectures and hyperparameters will be used across methods for fair comparison, with detailed training protocols specified for each dataset type.
87a318008035f14442077a384605f3edd40db7ba.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to explicitly model instance-dependent candidate label generation in partial label learning by recovering and leveraging latent label distributions. The method introduces a variational inference framework with a Dirichlet posterior for label enhancement, integrates topological and feature information via graph neural networks, and enables iterative, end-to-end training of both the label enhancement and predictive components. This principled approach addresses the limitations of previous methods that assume instance-independent candidate label selection and separate label estimation from model training, resulting in improved performance on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

87c5b281fa43e6f27191b20a8dd694eda1126336.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
87c5b281fa43e6f27191b20a8dd694eda1126336.research_question: How can the efficiency of self-attention mechanisms in Transformers be improved for long sequences, specifically in terms of both speed and memory usage, without sacrificing model quality?
87c5b281fa43e6f27191b20a8dd694eda1126336.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that an IO-aware, block-structured approach to exact attention computation can significantly reduce memory access overhead and improve wall-clock training speed, while maintaining or improving model quality for long-sequence tasks.
87c5b281fa43e6f27191b20a8dd694eda1126336.proposed_method: A novel, IO-aware exact attention algorithm, FlashAttention, will be developed to optimize memory access patterns on GPU architectures. The method will use tiling to partition the input matrices (Q, K, V) into blocks, loading them into fast on-chip SRAM to minimize slow high-bandwidth memory (HBM) reads and writes. Softmax normalization will be computed incrementally per block, with additional statistics tracked to enable correct aggregation across blocks. To avoid storing large intermediate matrices for the backward pass, selective recomputation will be used, storing only normalization factors and outputs, thus enabling efficient gradient computation. The entire attention computation, including optional masking and dropout, will be fused into a single CUDA kernel to further reduce memory traffic and maximize throughput. An extension to block-sparse attention will be implemented, leveraging block-wise sparsity masks to further reduce computation and memory usage for approximate attention scenarios.
87c5b281fa43e6f27191b20a8dd694eda1126336.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training and benchmarking Transformer models such as BERT-large and GPT-2 on standard datasets (e.g., Wikipedia for BERT, OpenWebText for GPT-2), as well as evaluating on the Long-Range Arena (LRA) benchmark for long-sequence tasks. Baselines will include standard PyTorch and Megatron-LM attention implementations, as well as state-of-the-art approximate attention methods such as Linformer, Performer, Local Attention, Reformer, and SMYRF. Evaluation metrics will include wall-clock training time, perplexity for language modeling, classification accuracy for long-document tasks (MIMIC-III, ECtHR), and memory usage. Additional experiments will test the ability to scale to very long sequences (up to 64K) and to solve challenging benchmarks such as Path-X and Path-256, reporting accuracy and resource utilization. All experiments will be conducted on A100 GPUs, with detailed runtime and memory profiling across a range of sequence lengths.
87c5b281fa43e6f27191b20a8dd694eda1126336.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first IO-aware exact attention algorithm that achieves sub-quadratic memory access complexity by leveraging tiling and recomputation, leading to significant speedups and memory savings over existing exact and approximate attention implementations. FlashAttention is claimed to be optimal in terms of HBM accesses for a wide range of on-chip SRAM sizes. The block-sparse extension enables even greater efficiency for approximate attention, outperforming all known baselines in speed and scalability. The approach enables training Transformers with much longer context windows, resulting in higher quality models and new capabilities, such as the first Transformer models to achieve non-random performance on extremely long-sequence benchmarks (Path-X and Path-256).

87d18b630d99dbf58cb6f30313d2302c81308223.title: Discrete Neural Algorithmic Reasoning
87d18b630d99dbf58cb6f30313d2302c81308223.research_question: How can neural networks be designed to robustly and interpretably execute classical algorithms, generalizing to out-of-distribution data and arbitrary input sizes, while maintaining formal guarantees of correctness?
87d18b630d99dbf58cb6f30313d2302c81308223.hypothesis: Constraining neural reasoners to follow execution trajectories as combinations of finite, predefined discrete states, with explicit separation of discrete and continuous data flows and the use of hard attention, will enable perfect generalization and interpretability on algorithmic reasoning tasks, even under significant distributional shifts.
87d18b630d99dbf58cb6f30313d2302c81308223.proposed_method: A novel neural architecture will be developed that enforces discrete state transitions in neural algorithmic reasoners. The approach begins with an attention-based neural network (e.g., Transformer Convolution with a single attention head) and introduces three key components: (1) feature discretization, ensuring all node and edge features are mapped to a finite set of discrete states via bottlenecks and one-hot encodings; (2) hard attention, which restricts each node to attend to a single neighbor, preventing attention weight dilution on large graphs and ensuring interpretable message passing; and (3) explicit separation of discrete and continuous data flows, where continuous (scalar) inputs are handled separately and only influence attention as edge priorities, while all state updates remain discrete. Scalar manipulations are performed through a discrete ScalarUpdate module, which allows only increment, keep, or push operations based on discrete states. Training is performed with supervision on the algorithm’s stepwise state transitions (hints), using teacher forcing and cross-entropy or MSE losses as appropriate.
87d18b630d99dbf58cb6f30313d2302c81308223.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the SALSA-CLRS benchmark, covering a range of algorithmic problems such as BFS, DFS, Prim, Dijkstra, Maximum Independent Set, and Eccentricity, with both single-task and multitask setups. The training data consists of random graphs (up to 16 nodes) from the Erdős-Rényi distribution, while test data includes much larger graphs (up to 1600 nodes) to evaluate out-of-distribution and size generalization. Baselines for comparison include GIN, PointerGraphNetwork, Triplet-GMPNN, Hint-ReLIC, and G-ForgetNet, with evaluation metrics comprising node-level and graph-level accuracy (the latter requiring all node outputs in a graph to be correct). The number of processor steps matches the ground-truth algorithm trajectory, and models are trained with teacher forcing and annealed softmax temperatures for discrete bottlenecks. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of each architectural component.
87d18b630d99dbf58cb6f30313d2302c81308223.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a fully discrete neural reasoner architecture that enforces execution as transitions between finite states, enabling formal guarantees of correctness and interpretability for any input size or distribution. The explicit separation of discrete and continuous data flows, combined with hard attention and discrete scalar manipulation, is claimed to be crucial for robust out-of-distribution generalization. The method is demonstrated to achieve perfect test scores and provable correctness on multiple algorithmic tasks, both in single-task and multitask settings, and is interpretable by design, allowing for manual verification of state transitions.

8805398cab95a5c384231b9c71a2ccfc00af1998.title: What Makes and Breaks Safety Fine-tuning? A Mechanistic Study
8805398cab95a5c384231b9c71a2ccfc00af1998.research_question: What are the underlying mechanisms by which safety fine-tuning aligns large language models with human safety preferences, and how do adversarial or jailbreak attacks circumvent these mechanisms?
8805398cab95a5c384231b9c71a2ccfc00af1998.hypothesis: Safety fine-tuning induces specialized transformations in model parameters that cluster unsafe inputs in a distinct subspace, reducing model sensitivity to unsafe prompts, but adversarial and jailbreak attacks can evade these mechanisms by producing activations similar to safe inputs.
8805398cab95a5c384231b9c71a2ccfc00af1998.proposed_method: A synthetic data generation framework will be developed to systematically analyze the mechanisms of safety fine-tuning in large language models. The framework will abstract model inputs into operators (tasks) and operands (concepts), allowing controlled construction of safe, unsafe, and adversarial inputs using probabilistic context-free grammars (PCFGs) and bijective task mappings. Safety fine-tuning protocols—including supervised safety fine-tuning, direct preference optimization, and unlearning—will be applied to models trained on this synthetic data. The method will analyze the resulting feature space, parameter space, and function sensitivity, focusing on how model weights and activations change, particularly in the multi-layer perceptron (MLP) layers of transformer blocks. The approach will also include interventions by interpolating and extrapolating model weights along the safety fine-tuning direction to assess behavioral changes.
8805398cab95a5c384231b9c71a2ccfc00af1998.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic datasets generated via the proposed PCFG-based framework and on real-world Llama models (Llama-2 7B, Llama-3 8B, and their safety fine-tuned chat variants) using structurally analogous natural language instructions. The synthetic setup will enable controlled creation of safe, unsafe, and various adversarial/jailbreak inputs (e.g., competing objectives, mismatched generalization, and embedding-based attacks). Baselines will include instruction fine-tuned models without safety fine-tuning. Evaluation metrics will include cluster separation in activation space, alignment of parameter transformations with fundamental subspaces, local Lipschitzness (model sensitivity), and attack success rates. Hyperparameters will be selected via cross-validation, and both quantitative and qualitative analyses will be performed to assess the robustness and failure modes of safety mechanisms.
8805398cab95a5c384231b9c71a2ccfc00af1998.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel synthetic data generation framework that enables systematic and mechanistic analysis of safety fine-tuning and adversarial attacks in language models. It provides a detailed decomposition of model inputs and outputs, allowing precise control over the safety context and attack modalities. The approach offers new insights into how safety fine-tuning minimally alters model weights to project unsafe inputs into the null space of specific layers, leading to distinct clustering and reduced sensitivity for unsafe prompts. The method also uncovers why adversarial and jailbreak attacks succeed by mimicking the activation patterns of safe inputs, thereby evading the learned safety mechanisms. This comprehensive mechanistic analysis bridges the gap between empirical robustness failures and the internal transformations induced by safety fine-tuning.

88078df01655ec43d5d83afdc1c5b690c7087e76.title: Straight-Line Diffusion Model for Efficient 3D Molecular Generation
88078df01655ec43d5d83afdc1c5b690c7087e76.research_question: How can the efficiency and quality of 3D molecular generation be improved by reformulating the diffusion process to better align with the noise sensitivity and structural constraints of molecular data?
88078df01655ec43d5d83afdc1c5b690c7087e76.hypothesis: A diffusion process that enforces a near-linear (straight-line) trajectory with a slow signal-to-noise ratio decay and a small, constant noise schedule will significantly reduce truncation error, enabling efficient sampling with fewer steps while maintaining or improving the chemical validity and diversity of generated 3D molecular structures.
88078df01655ec43d5d83afdc1c5b690c7087e76.proposed_method: A novel generative framework, the Straight-Line Diffusion Model (SLDM), is developed by designing the diffusion process to follow a linear trajectory in the latent space. The forward process is parameterized such that the mean decreases linearly with time (µ(t) = 1 - t/T) and the noise term is a small constant (σ), ensuring the second derivative of the trajectory is minimized. This formulation enables the use of larger step sizes during sampling without sacrificing accuracy, as truncation error is inherently reduced. The reverse process is discretized using the Euler-Maruyama method, and sampling incorporates both deterministic ODE steps and stochastic Langevin dynamics, with a novel time-annealed temperature schedule to balance exploration and convergence. The model is tailored for SE(3)-invariance by constraining coordinates to zero center-of-mass and using equivariant neural networks for noise prediction.
88078df01655ec43d5d83afdc1c5b690c7087e76.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on two standard datasets for 3D molecular generation: QM9 (small organic molecules) and GEOM-Drugs (drug-like molecules with higher diversity and size). Both unconditional and conditional generation tasks are evaluated, with conditional generation using property labels as additional inputs. The model's backbone is an EGNN, consistent with baselines, and atom types are predicted using the UniGEM framework. Baselines include EDM, GeoBFN, EquiFM, GeoLDM, and others, all using the same network architecture for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics include atom stability, molecule stability, validity (RDKit parsing), uniqueness, and the product of validity and uniqueness (V*U), as well as property mean absolute error (MAE) for conditional tasks. Sampling efficiency is measured by the number of function evaluations (NFE) required to reach high stability. Extensive ablation studies and toy dataset experiments are also performed to validate the proposed method.
88078df01655ec43d5d83afdc1c5b690c7087e76.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a theoretically grounded, straight-line diffusion process that minimizes truncation error, enabling up to 100-fold improvements in sampling efficiency over prior diffusion-based methods. The method achieves state-of-the-art performance on standard 3D molecular generation benchmarks with significantly fewer sampling steps, while maintaining or improving chemical validity and diversity. The linear scheduling and slow SNR decay are specifically aligned with the inductive biases of molecular data, and the time-annealed temperature sampling further enhances stability and robustness. The approach is generalizable and can be integrated with existing generative frameworks and advanced sampling techniques.

881883842c2661b41bbfc999d56c763b1ceef0bd.title: No Train No Gain: Revisiting Efficient Training Algorithms For Transformer-based Language Models
881883842c2661b41bbfc999d56c763b1ceef0bd.research_question: What are the most effective and fair evaluation protocols for comparing efficient training algorithms for Transformer-based language models, and do existing efficient training methods provide meaningful improvements in training, validation, and downstream performance under fixed computation budgets?
881883842c2661b41bbfc999d56c763b1ceef0bd.hypothesis: Efficient training algorithms for Transformer-based language models, when evaluated under a standardized and fair computation budget using a reference system time protocol, will not consistently outperform a well-tuned baseline with a fully-decayed learning rate in terms of training, validation, and downstream task performance.
881883842c2661b41bbfc999d56c763b1ceef0bd.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation protocol will be developed to compare efficient training algorithms for Transformer-based language models under fixed computation budgets. The protocol introduces 'reference system time' (RST), a standardized measure that maps computation time from arbitrary hardware to a reference system, ensuring fair comparison across different setups. The study will systematically implement and evaluate three categories of efficient training methods: dynamic architectures (layer stacking, layer dropping), batch selection (selective backprop, RHO loss), and efficient optimizers (Lion, Sophia). Each method will be tuned for its hyperparameters, and learning rate schedules will be decayed according to the same time unit as the computation budget. The protocol will ensure that all methods are evaluated at the end of the fixed budget, avoiding intermediate checkpoint comparisons and normalizing for per-iteration computational costs.
881883842c2661b41bbfc999d56c763b1ceef0bd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two widely used Transformer architectures: BERT-Base (encoder-only, 16 layers, 120M parameters) and T5-Base (encoder-decoder). Pre-training will be performed on the C4 dataset, with additional experiments on Wikipedia+BookCorpus and MiniPile for batch selection methods. Training budgets of 6, 12, and 24 hours (measured in RST) will be used. Downstream performance will be evaluated on GLUE, SuperGLUE, and Super-Natural-Instructions (SNI) benchmarks. Baselines will include standard AdamW optimization with fully-decayed learning rates and mixed-precision training (BF16/TF32 as appropriate). Evaluation metrics will include pre-training loss, validation loss, and downstream task accuracy, with results averaged over multiple seeds. Ablation studies will assess the impact of ignoring batch selection overhead and Hessian update steps for optimizers.
881883842c2661b41bbfc999d56c763b1ceef0bd.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a standardized evaluation protocol based on reference system time (RST) to enable fair and reproducible comparisons of efficient training algorithms across arbitrary hardware. The study systematically benchmarks a wide range of efficient training methods under identical, rigorously controlled conditions and highlights the importance of properly decayed learning rate schedules and accounting for all computational costs. The protocol and findings are intended to set a new standard for research in efficient Transformer training and to clarify the true benefits and limitations of current efficient training algorithms.

881a46e531cd7107660e852cf01842b6737a7f9b.title: T-REGS: Minimum Spanning Tree Regularization for Self-Supervised Learning
881a46e531cd7107660e852cf01842b6737a7f9b.research_question: How can self-supervised learning be regularized to prevent dimensional collapse and promote uniformity in learned representations, particularly in joint-embedding frameworks and across different data modalities?
881a46e531cd7107660e852cf01842b6737a7f9b.hypothesis: Maximizing the minimum spanning tree (MST) length of learned embeddings, subject to a sphere constraint, will prevent dimensional collapse and promote uniform distribution of representations, thereby improving the quality and transferability of self-supervised representations.
881a46e531cd7107660e852cf01842b6737a7f9b.proposed_method: A novel regularization framework is introduced that combines two loss terms: (1) a loss that maximizes the length of the minimum spanning tree (MST) over the batch of learned embeddings, and (2) a soft sphere constraint that penalizes deviations from a fixed-radius hypersphere. The MST loss encourages the embeddings to spread out and utilize the full dimensionality of the space, while the sphere constraint prevents trivial solutions where embeddings diverge to infinity. The overall loss is a weighted sum of these two components, with hyperparameters controlling their trade-off. This regularization is applied independently to each branch in a joint-embedding self-supervised learning setup, and can be used either as a standalone regularizer (combined with a view-invariance loss) or as an auxiliary loss to existing self-supervised learning methods. MST computation is performed using efficient GPU-parallelized Kruskal's algorithm, and the method is compatible with both unimodal and multimodal (e.g., image-text) architectures.
881a46e531cd7107660e852cf01842b6737a7f9b.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on synthetic datasets to validate the method's ability to prevent dimensional collapse and promote uniformity, using metrics such as sensitivity to simulated collapse and distribution of cosine similarities. For real-world benchmarks, the method is evaluated on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet-100, and ImageNet-1k using ResNet-18 and ResNet-50 backbones, following standard self-supervised learning protocols including linear probing for Top-1 accuracy. Baselines include state-of-the-art contrastive, non-contrastive, and redundancy reduction methods (e.g., BYOL, Barlow Twins, VICReg, INTL, Zero-CL, W2-regularized methods). The method is also tested in a multimodal setting by fine-tuning CLIP on image-text retrieval tasks (Flickr30k, MS-COCO), with evaluation via Recall@1 and Recall@5 for both image-to-text and text-to-image retrieval. Computational complexity and wall-clock time per training step are reported and compared to existing methods.
881a46e531cd7107660e852cf01842b6737a7f9b.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the use of MST length maximization, combined with a sphere constraint, as a theoretically grounded and computationally efficient regularization for self-supervised learning. This approach provides provable guarantees against dimensional collapse and ensures sample uniformity on compact manifolds. The method is conceptually simple, easy to implement, and applicable as both a standalone regularizer and an auxiliary loss to existing SSL methods. It is also modality-agnostic, enabling application to multi-branch and multi-modal architectures. Empirical results demonstrate competitive or superior performance to state-of-the-art methods, with efficient computational cost.

8834e8f3799ae759ee8a5bb5c8b939cf650b01cd.title: Artificial Artificial Artificial Intelligence: Crowd Workers Widely Use Large Language Models for Text Production Tasks
8834e8f3799ae759ee8a5bb5c8b939cf650b01cd.research_question: To what extent do crowd workers on online platforms utilize large language models (LLMs) to complete text production tasks, and how can the prevalence of such usage be reliably detected?
8834e8f3799ae759ee8a5bb5c8b939cf650b01cd.hypothesis: A significant proportion of crowd workers employ LLMs to generate responses for text summarization tasks, and a bespoke detection model can accurately identify LLM-generated text in this context.
8834e8f3799ae759ee8a5bb5c8b939cf650b01cd.proposed_method: A novel detection framework will be developed to estimate the prevalence of LLM usage among crowd workers performing text summarization tasks. The approach involves collecting a dataset of summaries from a crowdsourcing platform (e.g., Amazon Mechanical Turk) and augmenting it with both human-written and LLM-generated summaries. A synthetic-vs.-real text classifier will be fine-tuned using a contrastive pre-trained language model (e5-base) on both real and synthetic summaries, with hyperparameters such as a learning rate of 2e-5, batch size of 32, max token length of 256, and five epochs of training. Keystroke logging, including copy-paste actions, will be employed to provide additional post-hoc validation of classifier predictions. The methodology includes both summary-level and abstract-level data splits to assess the generalizability and robustness of the classifier.
8834e8f3799ae759ee8a5bb5c8b939cf650b01cd.experiment_details: The primary experiment will use a modified version of a prior abstract summarization task, where crowd workers are asked to condense medical research abstracts into concise summaries. The dataset will consist of 46 new summaries from 44 distinct workers, supplemented by 128 high-quality human-written summaries and 320 synthetic summaries generated by ChatGPT with varying temperature settings.
