The classifier's performance will be evaluated using accuracy, macro-F1, precision, and recall on both summary-level and abstract-level splits. Baselines such as out-of-the-box detectors (e.g., GPTZero, OpenAI's AI Detector) will be compared, with the bespoke model expected to outperform them. Post-hoc analysis will leverage keystroke data and overlap metrics between summaries and source abstracts to further validate the detection results.
8834e8f3799ae759ee8a5bb5c8b939cf650b01cd.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a robust, low-computational-cost methodology for detecting LLM-generated text in crowdsourced data, leveraging a task-specific fine-tuned classifier and keystroke-based validation. This approach is tailored to the specific context of text summarization and demonstrates superior performance over generic, out-of-the-box detectors. The work provides the first quantitative estimate of LLM usage prevalence among crowd workers in a real-world setting and establishes a generalizable framework that can be adapted to other text production tasks where human-authored data is critical.

88367aaf783056f49a3ea25cc455b9b78812cde5.title: AutoDiscovery: Open-ended Scientific Discovery via Bayesian Surprise
88367aaf783056f49a3ea25cc455b9b78812cde5.research_question: How can autonomous scientific discovery systems efficiently and effectively explore large hypothesis spaces in an open-ended, goal-free setting to identify novel and impactful scientific discoveries, without relying on human-specified research questions or subjective proxies for interestingness?
88367aaf783056f49a3ea25cc455b9b78812cde5.hypothesis: Guiding autonomous scientific discovery using Bayesian surprise as a reward function, combined with principled search strategies, will result in more efficient and effective identification of novel and surprising hypotheses compared to existing diversity-based or subjective-interest-based approaches.
88367aaf783056f49a3ea25cc455b9b78812cde5.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed for open-ended autonomous scientific discovery that leverages Bayesian surprise to guide the exploration of hypothesis space. The approach will use large language models (LLMs) to generate and verify natural language hypotheses about relationships in real-world datasets. Bayesian surprise will be quantified as the KL divergence between the LLM's prior and posterior beliefs about a hypothesis, estimated via repeated LLM sampling before and after empirical verification. A Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) algorithm with progressive widening and an upper-confidence bound (UCT) acquisition function will be employed to balance exploration and exploitation, efficiently navigating the vast hypothesis space. To ensure diversity and remove semantic duplicates, an LLM-based hierarchical agglomerative clustering (HAC) procedure will be used post-search to deduplicate hypotheses based on semantic equivalence.
88367aaf783056f49a3ea25cc455b9b78812cde5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 21 real-world datasets spanning biology, economics, finance, and behavioral science, sourced from benchmarks such as DiscoveryBench, BLADE, and SEA-AD. The system will operate under a fixed hypothesis evaluation budget (e.g., 500), with the goal of maximizing the number of unique, surprising, and verifiable discoveries. Baselines will include repeated independent sampling, context-aware linear sampling, greedy tree search, and beam search, all using the same LLM-based discovery agent and reward function for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics will include the number of unique hypotheses generated, the number of surprising discoveries (as measured by Bayesian surprise), and human expert assessments of surprise, interestingness, and utility. Additional validation will assess the correctness of experiment implementation and the effectiveness of the deduplication pipeline.
88367aaf783056f49a3ea25cc455b9b78812cde5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first formal definition and operationalization of Bayesian surprise for autonomous scientific discovery, enabling principled, open-ended exploration without human-specified goals. The integration of Bayesian surprise with MCTS and progressive widening provides a scalable and efficient search strategy for large hypothesis spaces. The method also innovates by using LLM-based belief elicitation and semantic deduplication to ensure both the quality and diversity of discoveries. Empirical results are expected to show substantial improvements over strong baselines in both the number and quality of surprising discoveries, with strong alignment to human expert judgments.

8841d8210b47da94e2940e71c4f557867f81ffa6.title: Compact Matrix Quantum Group Equivariant Neural Networks
8841d8210b47da94e2940e71c4f557867f81ffa6.research_question: How can neural networks be designed to effectively model data exhibiting symmetries described by compact matrix quantum groups, particularly in non-commutative geometries where classical group equivariant neural networks are inadequate?
8841d8210b47da94e2940e71c4f557867f81ffa6.hypothesis: Neural networks that encode symmetries via compact matrix quantum groups, rather than classical groups, will enable principled equivariant modeling of data in non-commutative geometric settings and generalize existing group equivariant architectures.
8841d8210b47da94e2940e71c4f557867f81ffa6.proposed_method: A new class of neural networks will be developed whose layers are equivariant to symmetries described by compact matrix quantum groups. The construction leverages Woronowicz’s Tannaka-Krein duality to mathematically derive the existence and structure of such networks. The method characterizes the linear equivariant layers by associating their weight matrices with morphisms in the fundamental representation category of a given compact matrix quantum group, focusing on the subclass of 'easy' quantum groups defined via two-coloured partition categories. The approach provides explicit recipes for constructing equivariant weight matrices as linear combinations of matrices indexed by partition diagrams, with the structure determined by the underlying quantum group symmetry. Nonlinear activation functions are also required to be equivariant, and the overall network is constructed as a composition of such equivariant linear and nonlinear layers.
8841d8210b47da94e2940e71c4f557867f81ffa6.experiment_details: The proposal is primarily theoretical and focuses on the mathematical derivation and characterization of equivariant layers for compact matrix quantum group neural networks. To demonstrate practical potential, further work will extend the characterization to nonlinear layers and implement the networks. Experimental validation would involve constructing such networks, training them using standard backpropagation (since the layers and weights remain complex-valued), and evaluating performance on tasks where data exhibits non-commutative symmetries. Suitable datasets would include those arising in free probability, non-commutative geometry, or quantum physics, and comparisons would be made against classical group equivariant neural networks and other relevant baselines. Evaluation metrics would depend on the specific application domain, such as accuracy for classification or mean squared error for regression.
8841d8210b47da94e2940e71c4f557867f81ffa6.novelty_claims: The proposed framework generalizes group equivariant neural networks to the setting of compact matrix quantum groups, enabling equivariant modeling for non-commutative geometries. The method mathematically derives the existence and structure of such networks, provides explicit characterizations of equivariant weight matrices for a broad class of quantum groups (including new cases not previously addressed in machine learning), and demonstrates that all classical compact matrix group equivariant networks are encompassed as special cases. The approach is theoretically grounded and introduces new mathematical tools to the design of equivariant neural architectures.

884be3f18a201af62e0cecd1324dad065b0b39ba.title: Better Diffusion Models Further Improve Adversarial Training
884be3f18a201af62e0cecd1324dad065b0b39ba.research_question: Can the use of improved diffusion models for data generation further enhance the effectiveness of adversarial training in terms of both clean and robust accuracy, across multiple datasets and threat models, without relying on external datasets?
884be3f18a201af62e0cecd1324dad065b0b39ba.hypothesis: Utilizing higher-quality images generated by state-of-the-art diffusion models, such as the elucidating diffusion model (EDM) with lower FID scores, will significantly improve both clean and robust accuracy of adversarially trained models compared to previous approaches that use older diffusion models or external datasets.
884be3f18a201af62e0cecd1324dad065b0b39ba.proposed_method: A new adversarial training framework will be developed that leverages data generated by the latest diffusion models, specifically the elucidating diffusion model (EDM), which provides superior image quality and sampling efficiency compared to previous models like DDPM. The approach will use class-conditional EDM to generate large-scale synthetic datasets for training, with pseudo-labels assigned based on class conditioning. The adversarial training will be conducted using the TRADES framework, with careful tuning of hyperparameters such as batch size, label smoothing, and the robustness-accuracy trade-off parameter β. Extensive ablation studies will be performed to analyze the effects of the quantity and quality of generated data, early stopping, data augmentation strategies, and other training details on robust overfitting and generalization. The method will also investigate the impact of sampling steps and FID scores on downstream adversarial robustness.
884be3f18a201af62e0cecd1324dad065b0b39ba.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard benchmarks including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, and TinyImageNet. WideResNet architectures (WRN-28-10 and WRN-70-16) will be used as backbone models. The generated datasets will be created using class-conditional EDM, with up to 50 million images per dataset, and various original-to-generated data ratios will be explored. Baselines will include top-performing adversarial training methods from RobustBench, both with and without external datasets, and prior approaches using DDPM-generated data. Evaluation metrics will include clean accuracy and robust accuracy under AutoAttack and PGD-40, with FID scores used to assess the quality of generated data. Training time, batch size, and epoch count will be controlled to ensure fair comparisons. Additional ablation studies will examine the effects of data augmentation methods, early stopping, and other hyperparameters.
884be3f18a201af62e0cecd1324dad065b0b39ba.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the use of state-of-the-art diffusion models (EDM) for generating high-quality synthetic data to enhance adversarial training, achieving significant improvements in both clean and robust accuracy over previous methods. The approach eliminates the need for external datasets, surpasses prior state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks, and provides the first adversarially trained models to achieve over 90% clean accuracy and 70% robust accuracy on CIFAR-10 without external data. Comprehensive ablation studies reveal new insights into the mechanisms by which generated data quality and quantity affect robust overfitting and generalization, establishing a new standard for learning-based data augmentation in adversarial robustness.

886bd870f1c28cc4d78ac0af1f58d9b4066f8a19.title: The Exact Sample Complexity Gain from Invariances for Kernel Regression on Manifolds
886bd870f1c28cc4d78ac0af1f58d9b4066f8a19.research_question: What is the precise gain in sample complexity achievable by encoding invariances into kernel regression models on compact manifolds, and how does this gain depend on the nature of the group action (finite or positive-dimensional Lie group) on the manifold?
886bd870f1c28cc4d78ac0af1f58d9b4066f8a19.hypothesis: Encoding invariances corresponding to group actions on data manifolds into kernel regression models leads to quantifiable and minimax-optimal reductions in sample complexity, with the gain determined by properties of the group and the quotient space.
886bd870f1c28cc4d78ac0af1f58d9b4066f8a19.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops a theoretical framework for kernel ridge regression (KRR) on compact manifolds, where the target function is invariant under the action of a smooth compact Lie group. The methodology involves characterizing the minimax optimal rates for the excess population risk (generalization error) of KRR using Sobolev kernels, taking into account the structure of the group action and the geometry of the quotient space. A key technical component is a new dimension counting theorem for the space of invariant functions, formulated using differential geometric tools to analyze the function space as defined on the quotient manifold (or stratified space). The analysis rigorously derives how the effective sample complexity is scaled by the group size for finite groups, and by both the reduction in dimension and the volume of the quotient space for positive-dimensional groups. The approach also establishes the appropriate boundary conditions (Neumann) for invariant functions on quotient spaces with boundaries.
886bd870f1c28cc4d78ac0af1f58d9b4066f8a19.experiment_details: The theoretical results are instantiated for several canonical learning scenarios, such as learning on sets (permutation invariance), point clouds, and images (translation invariance), by mapping these problems to kernel regression on product manifolds with appropriate group actions. Theoretical sample complexity bounds are made explicit for kernel analogs of popular invariant architectures, including DeepSets, PointNet, and GNNs. The evaluation is based on deriving minimax rates and comparing them to known results for non-invariant settings, as well as to previous work restricted to spheres or finite groups. Key metrics include the rate of decay of the generalization error as a function of the number of samples, the group size, and the effective dimension and volume of the quotient space. No empirical datasets are used; the work is entirely theoretical, but the results are applicable to a wide range of data types and invariance structures.
886bd870f1c28cc4d78ac0af1f58d9b4066f8a19.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a comprehensive and general theory quantifying the exact sample complexity gain from invariances in kernel regression on arbitrary compact manifolds under arbitrary smooth compact Lie group actions, including both finite and positive-dimensional groups. The differential geometric perspective and the new dimension counting theorem for invariant function spaces on quotient spaces are novel contributions, enabling precise characterization of sample complexity reductions not accessible by previous polynomial-based or sphere-restricted methods. The results generalize and subsume prior work, revealing new axes of complexity gain, including a reduction in effective dimension for positive-dimensional groups and explicit scaling by group size for finite groups. The methodology also clarifies the role of boundary conditions for invariant function spaces on quotient spaces, which is of independent mathematical interest.

887306ee7ebd9eebd7faea24106ec8e8f1a50987.title: How far are we to GPT-4V? Closing the gap to commercial multimodal models with open-source suites
887306ee7ebd9eebd7faea24106ec8e8f1a50987.research_question: How can the performance gap between open-source and proprietary commercial multimodal large language models (MLLMs) be effectively narrowed, particularly in terms of visual understanding, high-resolution image processing, and multilingual capabilities?
887306ee7ebd9eebd7faea24106ec8e8f1a50987.hypothesis: Integrating a strong vision encoder with continuous learning, adopting a dynamic high-resolution image processing strategy, and leveraging a high-quality bilingual dataset will significantly enhance the capabilities of open-source MLLMs, enabling them to achieve performance comparable to leading proprietary models across a broad set of multimodal benchmarks.
887306ee7ebd9eebd7faea24106ec8e8f1a50987.proposed_method: A new open-source MLLM suite will be developed by combining a large-scale vision foundation model (InternViT-6B) with a robust language model (InternLM2-20B) via an MLP projector. The vision encoder will undergo continuous pre-training on diverse, high-quality image-text datasets, with its architecture modified to use the most effective intermediate features and support flexible input resolutions. A dynamic high-resolution strategy will be implemented, segmenting input images into 448×448 pixel tiles (ranging from 1 to 40 tiles, supporting up to 4K resolution) based on aspect ratio and image size, with an additional thumbnail for global context. To address multilingual and OCR challenges, a large-scale bilingual dataset covering English and Chinese will be curated and expanded using an automated data translation pipeline, ensuring high-quality, natural language annotations for both languages. The entire model will be fine-tuned for multimodal tasks, maintaining compatibility and transferability between the vision and language components.
887306ee7ebd9eebd7faea24106ec8e8f1a50987.experiment_details: The proposed model will be evaluated on 18 representative multimodal benchmarks, spanning OCR-related tasks (e.g., DocVQA, ChartQA, TextVQA, InfoVQA, OCRBench), general multimodal understanding (e.g., MME, RealWorldQA, AI2D, MMMU, MMBench-EN/CN, CCBench, MMVet, SEED, HallusionBench), mathematical reasoning (e.g., MathVista), and multi-turn conversation (e.g., ConvBench, MMT-Bench). Evaluation will include both open-source and proprietary baselines such as GPT-4V, Gemini Pro, Claude-3 Opus, Grok-1.5V, Qwen-VL-Max, LLaVA-NeXT, and others. Metrics will include benchmark-specific accuracy, win rates against human judgments, and performance on multilingual and high-resolution tasks. The experimental setup will feature zero-shot scaling to high resolutions, ablation studies on the impact of vision encoder size and dynamic resolution, and qualitative analysis on general QA, OCR, scientific, cultural, and multi-image dialogue scenarios.
887306ee7ebd9eebd7faea24106ec8e8f1a50987.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces three key innovations: (1) a strong vision encoder (InternViT-6B) enhanced via continuous learning and architectural adaptation for multimodal tasks; (2) a dynamic high-resolution image processing strategy that flexibly segments images into tiles, supporting up to 4K resolution and preserving aspect ratios for detailed scene and document understanding; and (3) a high-quality, large-scale bilingual dataset with automated translation for robust English and Chinese multimodal capabilities. The method claims to achieve state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks, especially in OCR and Chinese language tasks, and to significantly close the performance gap between open-source and commercial MLLMs.

8877e9a5bf473404c35b758faa76905c202f0f36.title: Wan: Open and Advanced Large-Scale Video Generative Models
8877e9a5bf473404c35b758faa76905c202f0f36.research_question: How can large-scale, open, and efficient video generative models be developed to achieve superior performance, broad applicability, and resource efficiency across a wide range of video generation and editing tasks?
8877e9a5bf473404c35b758faa76905c202f0f36.hypothesis: Integrating a novel spatio-temporal variational autoencoder with scalable pre-training strategies, large-scale curated datasets, and advanced evaluation metrics will enable the development of video foundation models that surpass both open-source and commercial baselines in performance, versatility, and efficiency.
8877e9a5bf473404c35b758faa76905c202f0f36.proposed_method: A comprehensive suite of video generative models will be developed based on the diffusion transformer paradigm, incorporating a novel 3D causal spatio-temporal variational autoencoder (Wan-VAE) for efficient video compression and latent representation learning. The approach will utilize a multi-stage data curation pipeline to assemble billions of high-quality, diverse video and image samples, employing advanced filtering for visual and motion quality, text detection, and synthetic content removal. Dense video captioning will be enhanced through a LLaVA-style vision-language model, trained on both open-source and in-house datasets, to improve prompt alignment and downstream task performance. The models will be trained at multiple scales (1.3B and 14B parameters) using optimized parallelism, memory-efficient strategies, and post-training on curated high-fidelity data, supporting a range of applications including text-to-video, image-to-video, video editing, and real-time generation.
8877e9a5bf473404c35b758faa76905c202f0f36.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both internal and external benchmarks, comparing the proposed models against leading open-source and commercial video generation solutions such as Sora, Runway, Hunyuan, and Mochi. Evaluation will utilize automated and human preference metrics, including custom benchmarks (Wan-Bench), F1 scores on dense captioning tasks, and task-specific metrics for motion quality, text rendering, and visual fidelity. Datasets will include billions of curated videos and images, with additional in-house collections for fine-grained categories, camera motion, and text rendering. Ablation studies will assess the impact of architectural and data processing choices, and resource efficiency will be measured by VRAM requirements and inference speed on consumer-grade GPUs.
8877e9a5bf473404c35b758faa76905c202f0f36.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first open-source video foundation model suite capable of generating visual text in both Chinese and English, and supporting up to eight downstream applications. The spatio-temporal VAE architecture enables unprecedented compression and scalability for long video sequences. The data curation and captioning pipeline ensures high diversity and quality, while the models achieve state-of-the-art performance and efficiency, outperforming both open-source and commercial baselines. Full openness is claimed, with all code, models, and training pipelines to be released, fostering community advancement in large-scale video generation.

887d11c3fbc1a87a8bfe97bd53cfedab89496f99.title: A GNN-Guided Predict-and-Search Framework for Mixed-Integer Linear Programming
887d11c3fbc1a87a8bfe97bd53cfedab89496f99.research_question: How can machine learning, specifically graph neural networks, be leveraged to efficiently identify high-quality feasible solutions for mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) problems, particularly in scenarios where similar instances are repeatedly solved with varying coefficients?
887d11c3fbc1a87a8bfe97bd53cfedab89496f99.hypothesis: A framework that combines graph neural network-based prediction of variable marginal probabilities with a trust-region-based search will yield higher-quality feasible solutions for MILP problems, outperforming both traditional MILP solvers and existing ML-based end-to-end approaches in terms of solution quality and computational efficiency.
887d11c3fbc1a87a8bfe97bd53cfedab89496f99.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a predict-and-search framework for MILP problems. First, a graph neural network (GNN) is trained in a supervised manner to predict the marginal probability of each binary variable in a given MILP instance, using a bipartite graph representation of the MILP. The GNN outputs a vector of marginal probabilities, which are interpreted as the likelihood of each variable being set to 1 in a high-quality solution. Instead of fixing variables directly based on these predictions, a trust region-inspired search is employed: a neighborhood (ball) around the predicted solution is defined, and a search is conducted within the intersection of this neighborhood and the original feasible region to find a near-optimal feasible solution. The search is formulated as a modified MILP with additional neighborhood constraints, and is solved using a standard MILP solver. This approach aims to balance feasibility and optimality by allowing flexibility around the predicted solution.
887d11c3fbc1a87a8bfe97bd53cfedab89496f99.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four public MILP benchmark datasets: Balanced Item Placement (IP), Workload Appointment (WA), Independent Set (IS), and Combinatorial Auction (CA). Each dataset consists of 400 instances, split into training, validation, and test sets. The proposed framework will be evaluated using both SCIP and Gurobi as underlying MILP solvers. Baselines will include default SCIP, default Gurobi, and the Neural Diving framework (a state-of-the-art ML-based method). Evaluation metrics will focus on the absolute and relative primal gaps between the best known solution and the incumbent solution found within a fixed time limit (1,000 seconds). All experiments will be run under standardized hardware and software configurations, with careful parameter tuning and consistent evaluation protocols.
887d11c3fbc1a87a8bfe97bd53cfedab89496f99.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is novel in its combination of GNN-based marginal probability prediction with a trust region-inspired search for feasible solutions in MILP. Unlike prior end-to-end ML approaches that fix variables based on predictions and risk infeasibility, this method searches within a flexible neighborhood, improving both feasibility and solution quality. The approach reduces the need for collecting large numbers of optimal solutions for training by leveraging weighted feasible solutions, and it is applicable to general MILP problems rather than problem-specific cases. Empirical results claim significant improvements in primal gaps over state-of-the-art solvers (51.1% over SCIP and 9.9% over Gurobi) and over existing ML-based methods.

88884b8806262a4095036041e3567d450dba39f7.title: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation
88884b8806262a4095036041e3567d450dba39f7.research_question: How can long-form language generation be improved by dynamically integrating external knowledge through retrieval, in a way that flexibly determines when and what information to retrieve during the generation process, across a variety of knowledge-intensive tasks?
88884b8806262a4095036041e3567d450dba39f7.hypothesis: Actively triggering retrieval only when the language model exhibits low confidence in its generation, and formulating retrieval queries based on anticipated future content, will yield more accurate and factually consistent long-form outputs compared to passive or fixed-interval retrieval strategies.
88884b8806262a4095036041e3567d450dba39f7.proposed_method: A novel framework, Forward-Looking Active REtrieval augmented generation (FLARE), is proposed to interleave retrieval and generation in large language models. At each step of text generation, the model first predicts the next sentence without conditioning on external documents. If any token in this predicted sentence has a probability below a specified threshold (indicating low confidence), the sentence is used as a retrieval query to fetch relevant documents from an external corpus. The model then regenerates the sentence, conditioning on the retrieved documents, and continues this process iteratively until the output is complete. Two query formulation strategies are explored: implicit queries by masking low-confidence spans and explicit queries by generating questions targeting uncertain content. The method is designed to be model-agnostic and operates at inference time, requiring no additional training or fine-tuning of the underlying language model.
88884b8806262a4095036041e3567d450dba39f7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four diverse, knowledge-intensive, long-form generation tasks: multihop question answering (2WikiMultihopQA), commonsense reasoning (StrategyQA), long-form question answering (ASQA and ASQA-hint), and open-domain summarization (WikiAsp). For retrieval, off-the-shelf retrievers such as BM25 (for Wikipedia-based datasets) and Bing Search API (for open web) will be used. Baselines will include single-time retrieval, multi-time retrieval at fixed intervals (previous-window and previous-sentence), and question decomposition approaches. Evaluation metrics will include exact match (EM), F1, ROUGE, Disambig-F1, UniEval, and other task-specific metrics. All methods will be implemented using the same language model (e.g., text-davinci-003) for fair comparison, and hyperparameters will be tuned on development sets.
88884b8806262a4095036041e3567d450dba39f7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces an active, confidence-based retrieval mechanism that anticipates future information needs by generating temporary next sentences and using them as retrieval queries. This forward-looking strategy contrasts with prior methods that rely on passive or fixed-interval retrieval based on past context. The method is generic, requiring no task-specific prompt engineering or additional training, and is applicable to any existing large language model at inference time. Experimental results are expected to demonstrate superior or competitive performance across multiple long-form generation tasks, establishing the effectiveness and generalizability of the approach.

88a74e972898de887ad9587d4c87c3a9f03f1dc5.title: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
88a74e972898de887ad9587d4c87c3a9f03f1dc5.research_question: How can a comprehensive, standardized benchmark be developed to evaluate the performance and transferability of text embedding models across a diverse set of tasks, datasets, and languages?
88a74e972898de887ad9587d4c87c3a9f03f1dc5.hypothesis: A unified, large-scale benchmark that spans multiple embedding tasks, datasets, and languages will provide a more accurate and holistic assessment of text embedding models, revealing strengths, weaknesses, and gaps in current approaches and facilitating the discovery of more universal embedding methods.
88a74e972898de887ad9587d4c87c3a9f03f1dc5.proposed_method: A new benchmark, the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB), will be constructed to evaluate text embedding models on a wide range of tasks. MTEB will encompass 8 embedding task types—bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, semantic textual similarity (STS), and summarization—covering 58 datasets and 112 languages. The benchmark will provide a unified, open-source evaluation framework with a simple API, allowing any embedding model to be evaluated with minimal integration effort. Evaluation protocols for each task will be standardized, including specific metrics (e.g., accuracy, v-measure, MAP, nDCG, Spearman correlation) and consistent preprocessing. The benchmark will be extensible, enabling the addition of new datasets or tasks via a modular interface, and will ensure reproducibility through versioned datasets and software.
88a74e972898de887ad9587d4c87c3a9f03f1dc5.experiment_details: Experiments will involve benchmarking over 30 diverse text embedding models, including both open-source and API-accessible models, on the full suite of MTEB tasks and datasets. Models will be evaluated on English and multilingual datasets, with performance measured using task-appropriate metrics such as accuracy for classification, v-measure for clustering, MAP and MRR for retrieval and reranking, and Spearman/Pearson correlations for similarity and summarization. Baselines will include classic word embeddings (e.g., Glove, Komninos), transformer-based models (e.g., BERT, MiniLM, MPNet, ST5, GTR), and large-scale API models (e.g., OpenAI embeddings). The experimental setup will also include speed and memory benchmarking to assess efficiency trade-offs. Results will be tracked on a public leaderboard and JSON files will be provided for reproducibility.
88a74e972898de887ad9587d4c87c3a9f03f1dc5.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark is the most comprehensive evaluation suite for text embeddings to date, unifying a diverse set of tasks, datasets, and languages within a single, extensible framework. It enables holistic, apples-to-apples comparisons across models and tasks, addressing the limitations of prior benchmarks that focused on narrow task domains. MTEB's open-source code, modular design, and public leaderboard foster transparency, reproducibility, and community-driven expansion. The benchmark is positioned to drive progress toward universal text embeddings and to inform both research and practical deployment decisions in NLP.

88aa6b1f37d1fd8e0a40499ce9bb87873f03aaa8.title: Qwen2.5 Technical Report
88aa6b1f37d1fd8e0a40499ce9bb87873f03aaa8.research_question: How can large language models be further advanced in terms of language understanding, reasoning, mathematics, coding, human preference alignment, and multilingual capabilities through improvements in pre-training and post-training methodologies, architecture, and data scaling?
88aa6b1f37d1fd8e0a40499ce9bb87873f03aaa8.hypothesis: Scaling high-quality pre-training data, enhancing post-training with advanced supervised fine-tuning and multi-stage reinforcement learning, and introducing architectural innovations such as mixture-of-experts and improved tokenization will significantly improve the performance, efficiency, and versatility of large language models across diverse tasks and domains.
88aa6b1f37d1fd8e0a40499ce9bb87873f03aaa8.proposed_method: A comprehensive series of large language models will be developed, ranging from 0.5B to 72B parameters, including both dense and mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures. Pre-training will utilize a curated, high-quality dataset of 18 trillion tokens, with sophisticated filtering, domain balancing, and integration of specialized math and code datasets. The architecture will employ a Transformer-based decoder with Grouped Query Attention, SwiGLU activation, Rotary Positional Embeddings, QKV bias, and RMSNorm, and will extend to MoE variants with fine-grained expert segmentation and shared expert routing. Post-training will involve supervised fine-tuning on over 1 million examples covering long-sequence generation, mathematics, coding, instruction-following, structured data understanding, logical reasoning, cross-lingual transfer, and robust system instructions. A two-stage reinforcement learning process will be applied, consisting of offline RL for complex skills and online RL using Group Relative Policy Optimization, guided by a robust, multi-criteria reward model. Long-context capabilities will be enhanced through staged context expansion, YARN, and Dual Chunk Attention, enabling handling of up to 1 million tokens in some models.
88aa6b1f37d1fd8e0a40499ce9bb87873f03aaa8.experiment_details: Extensive experiments will be conducted on both base and instruction-tuned models across a wide range of open benchmarks and in-house datasets. Evaluation tasks will include general language understanding (MMLU, MMLU-Pro, MMLU-redux, BBH, ARC-C, TruthfulQA, Winogrande, HellaSwag), mathematics and science (GPQA, TheoremQA, GSM8K, MATH, MMLU-stem), coding (HumanEval, HumanEval+, MBPP, MBPP+, MultiPL-E), and multilingual tasks (M3Exam, IndoMMLU, ruMMLU, translated MMLU, BELEBELE, XCOPA, XWinograd, XStoryCloze, PAWS-X, MGSM, Flores-101). Baselines will include leading open-weight and proprietary models such as Llama-3-405B, Llama-3-70B, Mixtral-8x22B, Gemma2-27B, Yi-1.5-34B, and previous Qwen versions. Evaluation metrics will focus on benchmark scores, accuracy, and human preference alignment. Rigorous test data decontamination will be performed to prevent leakage, and experiments will assess both short and long-context capabilities, as well as cost-effectiveness and scalability.
88aa6b1f37d1fd8e0a40499ce9bb87873f03aaa8.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces several key innovations: (1) scaling pre-training data to 18 trillion tokens with advanced filtering and domain balancing; (2) integration of specialized math and code datasets during pre-training for superior domain expertise; (3) architectural advancements including expanded control tokens, unified vocabulary, and mixture-of-experts layers with fine-grained segmentation and shared routing; (4) a multi-stage post-training pipeline combining large-scale supervised fine-tuning and both offline and online reinforcement learning with robust reward modeling; (5) novel long-context training and inference strategies enabling context windows up to 1 million tokens; (6) comprehensive, multi-domain evaluation demonstrating state-of-the-art or highly competitive performance at various model sizes, including models that outperform much larger baselines in certain tasks while maintaining cost-effectiveness and versatility.

88ae720354fa4883be13e25e1cf92dcd4fed5f5d.title: Benchmarks and Algorithms for Offline Preference-Based Reward Learning
88ae720354fa4883be13e25e1cf92dcd4fed5f5d.research_question: How can reward functions be effectively learned from human preferences in fully offline settings, and what benchmarks and algorithms are suitable for evaluating offline preference-based reward learning?
88ae720354fa4883be13e25e1cf92dcd4fed5f5d.hypothesis: Offline datasets can be leveraged to generate informative preference queries and, when combined with active preference-based reward learning and offline reinforcement learning, can enable agents to learn reward functions and policies for novel tasks not explicitly present in the data, without requiring environment interaction or high-fidelity simulators.
88ae720354fa4883be13e25e1cf92dcd4fed5f5d.proposed_method: A novel framework, Offline Preference-based Reward Learning (OPRL), will be developed to learn reward functions from human preferences using only offline datasets of trajectories. The method will employ pool-based active learning to select informative pairs of trajectory snippets from the offline data, querying a human for pairwise preferences. The reward function will be modeled using the Bradley-Terry preference model and approximated with neural networks. Uncertainty over the learned reward function will be estimated using either ensembles of neural networks or Bayesian dropout, and active query selection will be guided by acquisition functions such as ensemble disagreement or information gain. Once the reward function is learned, offline reinforcement learning algorithms will be used to optimize policies with respect to the inferred reward, all without any environment interaction.
88ae720354fa4883be13e25e1cf92dcd4fed5f5d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a curated subset of the D4RL offline RL benchmark suite, focusing on domains where trivial reward functions (e.g., all zeros or constants) significantly degrade policy performance, such as Maze2D, Flow Merge, Halfcheetah-random, and Franka Kitchen-Complete. Baselines will include random query selection, T-REX (random static queries), and various active query strategies (ensemble disagreement, ensemble information gain, dropout disagreement, dropout information gain). Evaluation metrics will include normalized policy performance relative to ground-truth reward policies and random policies, with results averaged over multiple random seeds. The experimental setup will vary the number of initial and active queries, and policy optimization will primarily use Advantage Weighted Regression (AWR), with additional results using Conservative Q-Learning (CQL). Sensitivity analyses will be performed on query numbers, ensemble size, and dropout samples.
88ae720354fa4883be13e25e1cf92dcd4fed5f5d.novelty_claims: The proposed research formalizes and addresses the previously unexplored problem of offline preference-based reward learning, enabling safe and efficient reward and policy learning without any environment interaction. It introduces new benchmarks and identifies suitable existing domains for evaluating offline reward learning, and systematically compares active query strategies for preference-based reward inference. The approach demonstrates the ability to learn reward functions and policies for novel tasks not explicitly demonstrated in the offline data, leveraging the richness of offline datasets and active preference querying.

88ca4ee548d07263386ca8e4effc4a001bb2716f.title: Improving Text Embeddings with Large Language Models
88ca4ee548d07263386ca8e4effc4a001bb2716f.research_question: How can high-quality, robust, and multilingual text embeddings be efficiently obtained for a wide range of natural language processing tasks without relying on large-scale labeled datasets or complex multi-stage training pipelines?
88ca4ee548d07263386ca8e4effc4a001bb2716f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging large language models (LLMs) to generate diverse synthetic training data, followed by lightweight fine-tuning of open-source decoder-only LLMs with contrastive loss, can yield text embedding models that match or surpass the performance of existing state-of-the-art methods trained on labeled or weakly-supervised data.
88ca4ee548d07263386ca8e4effc4a001bb2716f.proposed_method: The proposed method involves a two-step synthetic data generation process using proprietary LLMs such as GPT-4. First, the LLM is prompted to brainstorm a wide variety of text embedding and retrieval tasks across 93 languages, ensuring diversity in both task type and linguistic coverage. Next, for each task, the LLM generates (query, positive document, hard negative document) triplets using carefully designed prompt templates with randomized placeholders for attributes like query length and language. The resulting synthetic dataset, consisting of hundreds of thousands of examples, is then used to fine-tune open-source decoder-only LLMs (e.g., Mistral-7B) with a standard contrastive InfoNCE loss, using the [EOS] token embedding as the representation. Fine-tuning is performed with LoRA for parameter efficiency, and natural language instructions are prepended to queries to further guide the embedding model. The approach also explores extending context length capabilities by modifying the position embedding rotation base.
88ca4ee548d07263386ca8e4effc4a001bb2716f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on established text embedding benchmarks, including MTEB (covering 56 English datasets across tasks such as retrieval, classification, clustering, and semantic textual similarity) and BEIR (15 public retrieval datasets). The synthetic dataset will be generated using GPT-4 and GPT-3.5-Turbo, covering 93 languages and multiple task types, and models will be fine-tuned for 1 epoch using both synthetic data and, in some settings, a mixture with labeled datasets such as MS-MARCO. Baseline comparisons will include unsupervised and supervised models (e.g., GloVe, SimCSE, Contriever, GTR, Sentence-T5, E5, BGE), as well as commercial embedding APIs (OpenAI, Cohere, UAE, Voyage). Evaluation metrics will include nDCG@10 for retrieval tasks, accuracy for synthetic long-context retrieval, and average scores across benchmark categories. The impact of hyperparameters (e.g., pooling type, LoRA rank, instruction type) and the necessity of contrastive pre-training will also be systematically analyzed.
88ca4ee548d07263386ca8e4effc4a001bb2716f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach claims novelty by eliminating the need for large-scale labeled or weakly-supervised datasets and complex multi-stage training pipelines, instead relying solely on synthetic data generated by LLMs. It introduces a scalable, multilingual, and task-diverse synthetic data generation framework, and demonstrates that lightweight fine-tuning of open-source LLMs with this data can achieve or surpass state-of-the-art results on competitive benchmarks. The method also extends embedding models to handle much longer contexts and provides a flexible way to customize embedding behavior via natural language instructions, paving the way for more interpretable and robust text embeddings.

88d5634a52645f6b05a03536be1f26a2b9bba232.title: Jailbreaking Leading Safety-Aligned LLMs with Simple Adaptive Attacks
88d5634a52645f6b05a03536be1f26a2b9bba232.research_question: How robust are leading safety-aligned large language models (LLMs) to adaptive jailbreaking attacks, and what methodologies can be developed to systematically bypass their safety mechanisms across a wide range of models and API configurations?
88d5634a52645f6b05a03536be1f26a2b9bba232.hypothesis: Even the most recent and safety-aligned LLMs are vulnerable to simple, adaptive jailbreaking attacks that leverage model-specific information such as log probabilities, prompt templates, and API features, resulting in high or perfect attack success rates.
88d5634a52645f6b05a03536be1f26a2b9bba232.proposed_method: A comprehensive adaptive attack framework will be developed that tailors adversarial prompts and attack strategies to the unique characteristics of each target LLM. The approach begins with the manual design of prompt templates, optimized to steer the model toward unsafe completions by maximizing the log probability of target tokens (e.g., 'Sure') using random search. For models exposing log probabilities, random search will iteratively modify adversarial suffixes appended to prompts, with multiple restarts and self-transfer—where suffixes found for simpler requests are reused as initializations for harder ones—to improve query efficiency and success rates. For models without logprob access (e.g., Claude), transfer attacks using suffixes optimized on other models and prefilling attacks leveraging API features will be employed. The methodology also extends to trojan detection in poisoned models by restricting the random search space to candidate tokens identified via embedding matrix analysis, thus enabling efficient discovery of universal triggers.
88d5634a52645f6b05a03536be1f26a2b9bba232.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of leading safety-aligned LLMs, including open-weight models (Llama-2-Chat-7B/13B/70B, Llama-3-Instruct-8B, Gemma-7B), proprietary models (GPT-3.5, GPT-4o, Claude 2/3/3.5), and adversarially trained models (R2D2 from HarmBench). The evaluation will use the AdvBench dataset of 50 harmful requests, with attack success judged by GPT-4 as a semantic judge (requiring a 10/10 jailbreak score), and supplemented by rule-based and alternative model-based judges for robustness. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art attacks such as Greedy Coordinate Gradient, Prompt Automatic Iterative Refinement, and Persuasive Adversarial Prompts. Key experimental variables include the use of default versus custom prompt templates, random search parameters (suffix length, iterations, restarts), and the application of transfer and prefilling attacks. For trojan detection, the approach will be validated on poisoned Llama-2-7B models from the SaTML’24 Trojan Detection Competition, with effectiveness measured by the reduction in reward model scores on held-out harmful prompts.
88d5634a52645f6b05a03536be1f26a2b9bba232.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified, adaptive attack framework that achieves 100% attack success rates on a broad spectrum of frontier LLMs, including those previously considered highly robust. Key innovations include the use of random search on log probabilities for efficient adversarial suffix optimization, the self-transfer technique for boosting query efficiency and success rates, and the exploitation of API-specific features such as prefilling. The methodology also pioneers a principled approach to restricting the token search space for trojan detection, enabling practical attacks on poisoned models. The work demonstrates that adaptivity—customizing attacks to each model’s defenses and API—is essential for accurate robustness evaluation, and provides actionable recommendations for future adversarial testing and defense development in LLM safety.

88d9c85b177f0517caf4de6518a5c3e25b5f3cf7.title: Understanding Masked Autoencoders From a Local Contrastive Perspective
88d9c85b177f0517caf4de6518a5c3e25b5f3cf7.research_question: What are the underlying mechanisms that contribute to the effectiveness of Masked Autoencoders (MAE) in self-supervised visual representation learning, and how can these mechanisms be empirically analyzed and decomposed from both reconstructive and contrastive perspectives?
88d9c85b177f0517caf4de6518a5c3e25b5f3cf7.hypothesis: MAE implicitly performs local contrastive learning at the patch level, learning invariance to random masking and ensuring distribution consistency between learned token embeddings and original images; explicitly decomposing MAE's objectives into reconstructive and contrastive components will reveal key factors underlying its success and inspire more effective self-supervised methods.
88d9c85b177f0517caf4de6518a5c3e25b5f3cf7.proposed_method: A novel empirical framework, Local Contrastive MAE (LC-MAE), will be developed to explicitly decompose the MAE objective into three loss components: a reconstruction loss, a cross-view contrastive loss, and an in-view contrastive loss. The reconstruction loss will encourage accurate patch-level reconstruction from masked inputs. The cross-view loss will enforce similarity between token features at the same spatial location across different random masks, promoting invariance to masking. The in-view loss will align the distribution of output token embeddings with the distribution of input image patches, preventing feature collapse. The LC-MAE framework will use an encoder-decoder architecture, with two masked views of each image processed in parallel, and a projector head to compute contrastive losses. Ablation studies will be conducted to isolate the effects of each loss term and to analyze the roles of the decoder depth and random masking strategy.
88d9c85b177f0517caf4de6518a5c3e25b5f3cf7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ImageNet-1K dataset using ViT-B/16 as the default backbone. Pretraining will use a mask ratio of 75% for 100 epochs, followed by supervised finetuning for 100 epochs. Baselines will include standard MAE (reconstruction loss only), autoencoders without random masking, and models with alternative decoder architectures (e.g., weighted average, convolutional layers). Evaluation metrics will include finetuning accuracy and linear probing accuracy on ImageNet. Ablation studies will systematically vary the loss components, decoder depth, and mask ratio to assess their impact on downstream performance. Attention distance and similarity analyses will be performed to quantify the effective receptive field and semantic richness of learned representations.
88d9c85b177f0517caf4de6518a5c3e25b5f3cf7.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new empirical framework (LC-MAE) that explicitly decomposes MAE's training objective into reconstructive and two distinct contrastive losses at the patch level, providing a local perspective on MAE's learning dynamics. It claims to reveal that MAE inherently performs local contrastive learning, learns invariance to random masking, and avoids feature collapse through distribution alignment. The work further claims to dissect the dual roles of the decoder and random masking, demonstrating that a deep decoder is essential for semantic learning and that masking effectively controls the receptive field, both of which are critical for MAE's downstream performance. The findings are expected to inform the design of more powerful self-supervised visual representation learning methods.

88f17e3a9aa3e1de7dd7dde2cb03d10d5446099f.title: Transolver: A Fast Transformer Solver for PDEs on General Geometries
88f17e3a9aa3e1de7dd7dde2cb03d10d5446099f.research_question: How can partial differential equations (PDEs) be efficiently and accurately solved on general, potentially complex or unstructured geometries using deep learning techniques, particularly transformer-based models?
88f17e3a9aa3e1de7dd7dde2cb03d10d5446099f.hypothesis: Learning and attending to intrinsic physical states, rather than directly to mesh points, enables transformer-based models to more efficiently and effectively capture intricate physical correlations in PDE-governed domains, resulting in improved accuracy, scalability, and generalization across diverse and complex geometries.
88f17e3a9aa3e1de7dd7dde2cb03d10d5446099f.proposed_method: A novel transformer-based framework, termed Transolver, will be developed to solve PDEs by learning intrinsic physical states hidden behind discretized geometries. The core innovation is the Physics-Attention mechanism, which adaptively decomposes the discretized domain into a set of learnable slices, each representing a group of mesh points sharing similar physical states. Each mesh point is assigned to slices via a softmax-based projection, and slice features are aggregated into physics-aware tokens. Attention is then computed among these tokens, rather than directly among all mesh points, allowing the model to capture high-level physical correlations with linear computational complexity. The output from the attention mechanism is broadcast back to the original mesh points, enabling end-to-end prediction of physical quantities on arbitrary geometries.
88f17e3a9aa3e1de7dd7dde2cb03d10d5446099f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six established PDE benchmarks spanning point clouds, structured meshes, regular grids, and unstructured meshes, including Elasticity, Plasticity, Airfoil, Pipe, Navier-Stokes, and Darcy problems. Additionally, large-scale industrial simulation tasks such as car and airfoil design will be included, using datasets like Shape-Net Car and AirfRANS. The proposed method will be compared against over 20 baselines, including state-of-the-art neural operators (FNO, U-NO, LSM), transformer-based PDE solvers (GNOT, FactFormer, ONO), and geometric deep learning models (PointNet, MeshGraphNet, GraphSAGE). Evaluation metrics will include relative L2 error on predicted physical fields, as well as design-oriented metrics such as drag and lift coefficients and their Spearman’s rank correlations. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the number of slices and the use of learnable versus fixed domain partitions. Efficiency (runtime, memory), scalability (resolution, data, model size), and out-of-distribution generalization (to unseen Reynolds numbers and angles of attack) will also be systematically evaluated.
88f17e3a9aa3e1de7dd7dde2cb03d10d5446099f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces Physics-Attention, a new attention mechanism that learns to aggregate mesh points into physics-aware slices, enabling attention to be computed among a small set of tokens representing intrinsic physical states. This approach allows for linear complexity with respect to mesh size, overcoming the computational and modeling limitations of standard transformer attention on large, irregular meshes. The method is claimed to provide endogenetic geometry-general modeling capacity, outperforming prior neural operator and transformer-based PDE solvers in both accuracy and efficiency, and demonstrating strong scalability and generalization to out-of-distribution scenarios. The framework is also shown to excel in practical, large-scale industrial design tasks involving highly complex geometries and multiphysics interactions.

88f1ca3dc13d4eae7afb40f79991b3157fc5d52d.title: GraphFM: Improving Large-Scale GNN Training via Feature Momentum
88f1ca3dc13d4eae7afb40f79991b3157fc5d52d.research_question: How can the training of graph neural networks (GNNs) for large-scale node classification be improved to obtain accurate hidden node representations while avoiding the neighborhood explosion problem and reducing the staleness of historical embeddings?
88f1ca3dc13d4eae7afb40f79991b3157fc5d52d.hypothesis: Incorporating feature momentum into the training of GNNs, by using momentum-based updates of historical node embeddings, will enable more accurate estimation of hidden node representations, alleviate the neighborhood explosion problem, and reduce the staleness of historical embeddings, thereby improving performance and efficiency on large-scale graphs.
88f1ca3dc13d4eae7afb40f79991b3157fc5d52d.proposed_method: A novel technique called feature momentum (FM) will be introduced to incorporate historical node embeddings into the update of feature representations during GNN training. Two specific algorithms will be developed: GraphFM-IB, which applies feature momentum to in-batch sampled data, and GraphFM-OB, which applies feature momentum to out-of-batch data that are 1-hop neighbors of in-batch nodes. In GraphFM-IB, a momentum step will be used to update historical embeddings of sampled neighbors, enabling accurate feature aggregation with reduced neighborhood size. In GraphFM-OB, cluster-based sampling will be employed, and feature momentum will be applied to update the historical embeddings of out-of-batch nodes using message passing from in-batch nodes. Both algorithms will be implemented with Adam-style optimization, and theoretical analysis will be provided for convergence and estimation error.
88f1ca3dc13d4eae7afb40f79991b3157fc5d52d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five large-scale graph datasets: Flickr, Yelp, Reddit, ogbn-arxiv, and ogbn-products, covering both single-label and multi-label node classification tasks. The proposed methods will be evaluated using standard GNN backbones (e.g., GraphSAGE, GCN, GCNII, PNA) and compared against strong baselines such as VR-GCN, FastGCN, GraphSAINT, ClusterGCN, SIGN, and GNNAutoScale. Evaluation metrics will include F1-micro scores, GPU memory consumption, and training time per epoch. Experiments will systematically vary neighbor sampling sizes and GNN depth to assess scalability, accuracy, and efficiency. Additional analysis will measure the staleness of historical embeddings using a proposed staleness score metric.
88f1ca3dc13d4eae7afb40f79991b3157fc5d52d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the concept of feature momentum for GNN training, enabling accurate hidden node representation estimation with significantly reduced neighborhood sampling, thereby alleviating the neighborhood explosion problem. The development of GraphFM-IB and GraphFM-OB provides new algorithms with theoretical convergence guarantees and practical mechanisms to reduce the staleness of historical embeddings. The methods are shown to achieve competitive or superior performance compared to state-of-the-art baselines on multiple large-scale datasets, while also improving memory and computational efficiency. The proposal also introduces a new metric for quantifying the staleness of historical embeddings.

88f9af8b0a28e14c42d4f70ce2d911b51a06cd16.title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
88f9af8b0a28e14c42d4f70ce2d911b51a06cd16.research_question: What are the underlying mechanisms that mediate refusal behavior in large language models, and how can an understanding of these mechanisms be leveraged to control or circumvent refusal without significantly impairing other model capabilities?
88f9af8b0a28e14c42d4f70ce2d911b51a06cd16.hypothesis: Refusal behavior in large language models is mediated by a single, interpretable direction in activation space, and targeted interventions on this direction can selectively disable or induce refusal with minimal impact on other model functions.
88f9af8b0a28e14c42d4f70ce2d911b51a06cd16.proposed_method: The proposed method involves identifying a one-dimensional 'refusal direction' in the residual stream activations of transformer-based language models. This direction is extracted by computing the difference in mean activations between harmful and harmless instruction prompts across various layers and token positions, using contrastive datasets. Once the most effective refusal direction is selected, two interventions are explored: (1) directional ablation, which zeros out the component of activations along this direction at inference-time, and (2) weight orthogonalization, which directly modifies the model's weights to prevent writing to the refusal direction. Both interventions are designed to surgically disable or induce refusal behavior without broadly altering the model's other capabilities.
88f9af8b0a28e14c42d4f70ce2d911b51a06cd16.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of 13 open-source chat models ranging from 1.8B to 72B parameters, including models from QWEN, YI, GEMMA, and LLAMA families. Harmful and harmless instruction datasets will be constructed from sources such as ADV-BENCH, MALICIOUSINSTRUCT, TDC2023, HARMBENCH, and ALPACA, with careful train/validation splits. Evaluation will include refusal and safety scores (using string-matching for refusals and METALLAMA GUARD2 for harmfulness), as well as attack success rates (ASR) on HARMBENCH to compare with other jailbreak methods. Standard language model benchmarks (MMLU, ARC, GSM8K, TRUTHFULQA) will be used to assess the impact of interventions on general model coherence and performance. Mechanistic analysis will further investigate the effect of adversarial suffixes on the refusal direction using direct feature attribution and attention pattern analysis.
88f9af8b0a28e14c42d4f70ce2d911b51a06cd16.novelty_claims: This proposal claims that refusal behavior in instruction-tuned language models can be attributed to a single, interpretable direction in activation space, which is both necessary and sufficient for mediating refusal. The proposed white-box jailbreak via weight orthogonalization is a novel, simple, and effective method for disabling refusal without requiring gradient-based optimization or harmful completion data, and with minimal degradation of other model capabilities. Additionally, the mechanistic analysis of adversarial suffixes provides new insights into how such attacks suppress the refusal-mediating direction, highlighting the brittleness of current safety fine-tuning and the practical utility of model-internals-based interpretability for behavior control.

88fc09d3cd7bda6d3e5008b2a691816191cbfe51.title: mPLUG-Owl3: Towards Long Image-Sequence Understanding in Multi-Modal Large Language Models
88fc09d3cd7bda6d3e5008b2a691816191cbfe51.research_question: How can multi-modal large language models be enhanced to efficiently and effectively understand and reason over long sequences of images, including interleaved image-text and video scenarios, while maintaining high performance and computational efficiency?
88fc09d3cd7bda6d3e5008b2a691816191cbfe51.hypothesis: Introducing a novel cross-attention-based transformer architecture with lightweight Hyper Attention Transformer Blocks and improved positional encoding will enable large language models to process and reason over long image sequences more efficiently and accurately than existing methods.
88fc09d3cd7bda6d3e5008b2a691816191cbfe51.proposed_method: A new multi-modal large language model architecture is developed that integrates a visual encoder, a linear projection layer, and a decoder-only language model. The key innovation lies in the introduction of Hyper Attention Transformer Blocks (HATBs), which sparsely extend a subset of transformer layers to perform parallel self-attention and cross-attention between text and visual features. Visual features are projected and aligned to the language model's dimension, and a Multimodal-Interleaved Rotary Position Embedding (MI-Rope) is used to maintain the positional information of images in interleaved sequences. An adaptive gating mechanism dynamically regulates the fusion of visual and textual information based on semantic context. The architecture is trained in three stages: initial pre-training on large-scale image-text pairs, multi-image and video pre-training with interleaved and text-rich data, and supervised fine-tuning using diverse instruction-following datasets.
88fc09d3cd7bda6d3e5008b2a691816191cbfe51.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a comprehensive suite of benchmarks, including single-image visual question answering (VQAv2, OK-VQA, GQA, VizWizQA, TextVQA), general multimodal benchmarks (MMBench-EN/CN, MM-Vet, POPE, AI2D), multi-image understanding (NLVR2, Mantis-Eval, MathVerse-mv, SciVerse-mv, BLINK, Q-Bench2, MI-Bench), and video understanding (NextQA, MVBench, VideoMME, LongVideoBench). Baseline models for comparison include CogVLM, EVLM-Chat, Flamingo, Qwen-VL-Chat, Idefics, InstructBLIP, LLaVA-1.5, LLaVA-Next, VILA-1.5, Mantis-SigLIP, and others. Evaluation metrics include accuracy and benchmark-specific overall scores. The experimental setup involves training with mixed-precision (FP16/BF16), large batch sizes, and model parallelism, with ablation studies to analyze the impact of different cross-attention integration strategies.
88fc09d3cd7bda6d3e5008b2a691816191cbfe51.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces Hyper Attention Transformer Blocks, a lightweight and efficient cross-attention mechanism that enables scalable and effective reasoning over long image sequences. The architecture incorporates a novel multimodal rotary position embedding (MI-Rope) for precise positional encoding of interleaved visual and textual inputs. The adaptive gating mechanism allows dynamic and context-aware fusion of modalities. The method achieves state-of-the-art results on a wide range of single-image, multi-image, and video benchmarks, demonstrating superior efficiency and performance compared to models of similar or larger size. Additionally, a new evaluation protocol, Distractor Resistance, is proposed to assess model robustness in long visual sequence scenarios.

890efc891e9b59e8cb5e8c244428f6b81ec0a4da.title: Gemma Scope: Open Sparse Autoencoders Everywhere All At Once on Gemma 2
890efc891e9b59e8cb5e8c244428f6b81ec0a4da.research_question: How can a comprehensive, open suite of sparse autoencoders be developed and released to enable large-scale interpretability and safety research on modern large language models, and what are the properties, limitations, and practical trade-offs of such autoencoders across different model architectures, layers, and training regimes?
890efc891e9b59e8cb5e8c244428f6b81ec0a4da.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that training and releasing a comprehensive suite of JumpReLU sparse autoencoders on all layers and sublayers of large-scale language models will facilitate ambitious interpretability and safety research, and that these autoencoders will exhibit desirable properties such as high reconstruction fidelity, interpretability, and transferability across model variants.
890efc891e9b59e8cb5e8c244428f6b81ec0a4da.proposed_method: A comprehensive suite of JumpReLU sparse autoencoders (SAEs) will be trained on the activations of all layers and sublayers of the Gemma 2 2B and 9B models, and select layers of the 27B model. The method uses a JumpReLU activation function with learnable, latent-specific thresholds to enforce sparsity, combined with an L0 penalty in the loss function for direct regularization of the number of active latents. Training will be conducted on pre-collected activations from the models using large-scale text corpora, with activations normalized for stable hyperparameter transfer. Multiple SAE widths and sparsity levels will be explored, and the infrastructure will leverage TPU clusters, efficient sharding, and a shared data pipeline to handle the massive data and compute requirements. After training, SAE parameters will be rescaled for inference without input normalization, and weights will be released under a permissive license.
890efc891e9b59e8cb5e8c244428f6b81ec0a4da.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training over 2,000 SAEs with varying widths (from ~16K to 1M latents) and sparsity coefficients, using 4-16B tokens per SAE, on pretraining data matching the original Gemma 2 models. Evaluation will be performed on held-out sequences from the same distribution, as well as subsets of The Pile and instruction-tuned data. Baselines will include different SAE architectures (JumpReLU, TopK, Gated) and model variants (base vs. instruction-tuned). Evaluation metrics will include mean L0-norm (sparsity), delta LM loss (increase in cross-entropy when splicing the SAE into the model), and fraction of variance unexplained (FVU) for reconstruction fidelity. Additional analyses will assess interpretability via human and LM-generated explanations, transferability to instruction-tuned models, and robustness to low-precision inference.
890efc891e9b59e8cb5e8c244428f6b81ec0a4da.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first open, comprehensive suite of sparse autoencoders trained on all layers and sublayers of large, modern language models, enabling broad community access for interpretability and safety research. The use of JumpReLU activation with learnable thresholds and direct L0 regularization allows flexible and efficient control of sparsity. The scale of training—covering hundreds of SAEs, millions of features, and petabytes of activations—represents a significant engineering advance. The open release of weights, detailed metrics, and supporting infrastructure is expected to catalyze new research directions in model interpretability, circuit analysis, and safety.

8913f68977f6e320c24b2dd6f10beb9fea365cdc.title: Text-to-Decision Agent: Offline Meta-Reinforcement Learning from Natural Language Supervision
8913f68977f6e320c24b2dd6f10beb9fea365cdc.research_question: How can generalist reinforcement learning agents be trained to achieve high-capacity zero-shot generalization to unseen tasks using supervision from natural language, rather than relying on expensive or infeasible environment-specific signals or demonstrations?
8913f68977f6e320c24b2dd6f10beb9fea365cdc.hypothesis: Aligning natural language supervision with environment dynamics through a contrastive pre-training framework will enable the training of generalist offline meta-reinforcement learning agents that can perform zero-shot text-to-decision generation on unseen tasks, outperforming existing baselines in terms of generalization and robustness.
8913f68977f6e320c24b2dd6f10beb9fea365cdc.proposed_method: A scalable framework is proposed that supervises offline meta-reinforcement learning using natural language. First, a generalized world model is pre-trained to encode multi-task decision data into a dynamics-aware embedding space, capturing task-specific environment dynamics. Next, a contrastive learning approach, inspired by CLIP, is employed to align text embeddings (from a transformer-based encoder initialized with models such as CLIP or T5) with dynamics-aware decision embeddings, using a cross-modal contrastive loss and low-rank adaptation (LoRA) for efficient fine-tuning. The aligned text embeddings are then used to condition a generalist policy, implemented with either a diffusion-based (Text-to-Decision Diffuser) or transformer-based (Text-to-Decision Transformer) architecture, enabling the agent to generate decision policies directly from natural language instructions in a zero-shot manner.
8913f68977f6e320c24b2dd6f10beb9fea365cdc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three widely used RL generalization benchmarks: Point-Robot (2D navigation), MuJoCo locomotion (Cheetah-Vel and Ant-Dir), and Meta-World (robotic manipulation tasks). For each environment, tasks are paired with natural language descriptions and split into training and test sets. Offline datasets of varying quality (Mixed, Medium, Expert) are collected using SAC-trained single-task policies. The proposed method will be compared against strong baselines from three paradigms: context-based offline meta-RL (CSRO, UNICORN), in-context RL (AD), and language-conditioned policy learning (BC-Z, BAKU). Evaluation metrics include zero-shot test returns, learning speed, and robustness to data quality and text encoder initialization, with results averaged over multiple random seeds and statistical confidence intervals reported. Ablation studies will assess the contribution of each component (world model pre-training, contrastive alignment, language supervision).
8913f68977f6e320c24b2dd6f10beb9fea365cdc.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a generalized world model for capturing environment dynamics and a contrastive language-decision pre-training strategy to bridge the semantic gap between natural language and decision domains. It enables scalable, zero-shot text-to-decision policy generation without requiring expensive task-specific demonstrations or warmup explorations. The approach is demonstrated to be robust across diverse datasets and text encoders, and achieves superior zero-shot generalization compared to a wide range of baselines. The method also provides scalable implementations using both diffusion and transformer architectures, paving the way for large-scale, language-supervised decision agents.

8918efe49eb333aa7e2c601d2a067bbb1d972d3f.title: Escaping from the Barren Plateau via Gaussian Initializations in Deep Variational Quantum Circuits
8918efe49eb333aa7e2c601d2a067bbb1d972d3f.research_question: How can the trainability of deep variational quantum circuits be improved to avoid the vanishing gradient (barren plateau) problem, especially as the number of qubits and circuit depth increase, for both local and global observables in practical quantum simulation and quantum chemistry tasks?
8918efe49eb333aa7e2c601d2a067bbb1d972d3f.hypothesis: Properly designed Gaussian initialization of circuit parameters can guarantee that the gradient norm decays at most polynomially with increasing qubit number and circuit depth, thereby preventing the barren plateau problem and improving the trainability of deep variational quantum circuits.
8918efe49eb333aa7e2c601d2a067bbb1d972d3f.proposed_method: A novel initialization strategy will be developed for deep variational quantum circuits, where circuit parameters are sampled from a Gaussian distribution with variance scaling as O(1/L) for L-layer circuits. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to prove that, under this initialization, the expected gradient norm is lower bounded by an inverse polynomial in the number of qubits and circuit depth, for both local and global observable cases. The method will be extended to circuits with both independent and correlated parameters, covering practical ansatzes such as those used in quantum chemistry (e.g., Givens rotations). Additional analysis will be performed to determine the sufficient number of measurements required to estimate gradients robustly in the presence of quantum measurement noise, ensuring that the gradient remains large enough for effective optimization. The approach will be validated by deriving explicit bounds and conditions under which the initialization guarantees trainability.
8918efe49eb333aa7e2c601d2a067bbb1d972d3f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two benchmark tasks: finding the ground energy and state of the Heisenberg model (quantum simulation) and the LiH molecule (quantum chemistry). Quantum circuits with up to 15 qubits and 10 layers (for the Heisenberg model) and circuits based on Givens rotations (for LiH) will be implemented using the Pennylane package. Three initialization strategies will be compared: the proposed Gaussian initialization, uniform initialization, and zero initialization. Both gradient descent and Adam optimizers will be used, and experiments will be performed in both noiseless and noisy gradient estimation settings, with noise modeled as Gaussian perturbations. Evaluation metrics will include convergence rate, final loss value (distance to global minimum), and gradient norm during training. Multiple runs will be averaged to ensure statistical reliability.
8918efe49eb333aa7e2c601d2a067bbb1d972d3f.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a Gaussian initialization strategy with theoretical guarantees for avoiding the barren plateau problem in deep variational quantum circuits, improving upon previous results that showed exponential decay of gradients. The approach provides polynomial lower bounds on the gradient norm for both local and global observables, extends to circuits with correlated parameters, and includes analysis of measurement noise effects. Experimental results are expected to demonstrate superior convergence and trainability compared to standard initialization methods, validating the theoretical claims.

891cc1397f949d4432a5a0602e3757e9e3610862.title: Stop Overthinking: A Survey on Efficient Reasoning for Large Language Models
891cc1397f949d4432a5a0602e3757e9e3610862.research_question: How can large language models be enabled to perform efficient reasoning, minimizing unnecessary reasoning steps and computational overhead, while maintaining or improving their reasoning capabilities across complex tasks?
891cc1397f949d4432a5a0602e3757e9e3610862.hypothesis: Integrating model-based, output-based, and input prompt-based strategies—such as reinforcement learning with length-based rewards, supervised fine-tuning with variable-length reasoning data, and latent representation compression—will enable large language models to generate concise reasoning chains that preserve or enhance reasoning accuracy while significantly reducing computational costs and response latency.
891cc1397f949d4432a5a0602e3757e9e3610862.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed that systematically explores and integrates three primary approaches for efficient reasoning in large language models (LLMs): (1) Model-based efficient reasoning, involving reinforcement learning (RL) with length-based reward functions and supervised fine-tuning (SFT) using variable-length chain-of-thought (CoT) datasets to train models to generate concise reasoning steps; (2) Reasoning output-based efficient reasoning, which compresses explicit reasoning steps into latent representations or dynamically prunes unnecessary steps during inference using techniques such as latent tokenization, self-distillation, and dynamic step selection; (3) Input prompts-based efficient reasoning, where prompts are designed or routed based on question attributes (e.g., difficulty or required reasoning length) to guide the model toward efficient reasoning paths. The framework will also investigate model merging, progressive fine-tuning, and auxiliary modules for latent-space reasoning. Technical implementation will include designing novel RL reward functions, constructing and curating variable-length CoT datasets, and developing modules for latent reasoning representation.
891cc1397f949d4432a5a0602e3757e9e3610862.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of reasoning-intensive benchmarks, including GSM8K, MATH, AIME-2024, Olympiad-Bench, MathQA, ECQA, StrategyQA, and others. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art reasoning models such as DeepSeek-R1, OpenAI o1, QwQ-32B, and standard LLMs with traditional CoT prompting. Evaluation metrics will encompass reasoning accuracy, average reasoning length (in tokens), computational cost (inference time and token usage), and response latency.
