Ablation studies will be performed to assess the contribution of each component (RL reward design, SFT with variable-length data, latent compression, prompt routing) to overall efficiency and accuracy. Additional experiments will analyze the trade-offs between reasoning conciseness and correctness, as well as the generalization of efficient reasoning strategies to out-of-domain tasks.
891cc1397f949d4432a5a0602e3757e9e3610862.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified and systematic approach to efficient reasoning in LLMs, integrating model-based, output-based, and prompt-based strategies. It advances the field by developing novel length-aware RL reward functions, constructing and leveraging variable-length CoT datasets, and pioneering latent-space reasoning techniques for both unimodal and multimodal LLMs. The work also proposes new methods for dynamic prompt routing and model merging to further optimize reasoning efficiency. Comprehensive benchmarking and evaluation protocols are established to rigorously assess efficient reasoning, providing actionable insights and practical tools for deploying LLMs in resource-constrained, real-world scenarios.

891e5c05deac170b4dc4d8463c036f3fc8a524c7.title: Self-Distillation from the Last Mini-Batch for Consistency Regularization
891e5c05deac170b4dc4d8463c036f3fc8a524c7.research_question: How can self-distillation be made more efficient and robust for consistency regularization in deep neural network training, without requiring additional network architecture modifications or significant computational overhead?
891e5c05deac170b4dc4d8463c036f3fc8a524c7.hypothesis: A self-distillation framework that leverages the most recent soft targets from the last mini-batch, without requiring a pre-trained teacher or network modifications, will improve training consistency, generalization, and robustness to label noise across various architectures and datasets.
891e5c05deac170b4dc4d8463c036f3fc8a524c7.proposed_method: A novel self-distillation framework, termed Self-Distillation from Last Mini-Batch (DLB), is introduced. The approach rearranges the sampling of mini-batches such that half of each mini-batch coincides with the previous iteration and the other half with the upcoming iteration. During training, the model stores the soft targets (i.e., softened logits with temperature scaling) from the previous mini-batch and uses them as on-the-fly supervision for the overlapping samples in the current mini-batch. The training objective combines the standard cross-entropy loss with a consistency regularization term that minimizes the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the current predictions and the stored soft targets. This method requires minimal additional memory (only storing soft targets for one mini-batch), does not modify the model architecture, and is compatible with parallelization and various data augmentation strategies.
891e5c05deac170b4dc4d8463c036f3fc8a524c7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three classification benchmarks: CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and TinyImageNet. Six representative convolutional neural network architectures will be evaluated, including VGG-16, VGG-19, ResNet-32, ResNet-110, WideResNet-20-8, and DenseNet-40-12. The proposed method will be compared against baselines such as standard training, label smoothing, and several state-of-the-art self-distillation methods (e.g., Tf-KD, CS-KD, PS-KD, DDGSD, BYOT). Evaluation metrics include top-1 error rate and robustness to label noise, with additional experiments assessing compatibility with augmentation-based regularization methods like CutOut and CutMix. Hyperparameters such as temperature and loss balancing coefficient will be systematically explored, and all experiments will be run with fixed random seeds and repeated for statistical significance.
891e5c05deac170b4dc4d8463c036f3fc8a524c7.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple yet highly efficient self-distillation framework that leverages the most immediate soft targets from the last mini-batch, requiring no additional network modifications or significant memory overhead. It is model-agnostic, task-agnostic, and easily parallelizable. The approach provides on-the-fly sample-level smoothed labels for improved training consistency and stability, leading to enhanced generalization and robustness to label noise. Additionally, the method demonstrates strong compatibility with various data augmentation strategies, offering orthogonal performance gains when combined with other regularization techniques.

89347e7b42e00e949fd64060136cc64497ab2ef3.title: Rethinking the Backward Propagation for Adversarial Transferability
89347e7b42e00e949fd64060136cc64497ab2ef3.research_question: How can the transferability of adversarial examples in transfer-based attacks be improved by addressing limitations in the backward propagation process, particularly those introduced by non-linear layers in neural networks?
89347e7b42e00e949fd64060136cc64497ab2ef3.hypothesis: The truncation of gradients caused by non-linear layers such as ReLU and max-pooling during backward propagation reduces the transferability of adversarial examples. By mitigating this gradient truncation, it is possible to generate adversarial examples with higher transferability across models.
89347e7b42e00e949fd64060136cc64497ab2ef3.proposed_method: A novel attack method, termed Backward Propagation Attack (BPA), is proposed to enhance adversarial transferability by modifying the gradient calculation in non-linear layers during backward propagation. For ReLU activations, the derivative is replaced with that of the SiLU (Sigmoid Linear Unit) function, providing a smooth, non-monotonic gradient that better reflects the input magnitude and avoids saturation. For max-pooling layers, the gradient within each pooling window is computed using a softmax function with a temperature coefficient, ensuring the gradient distribution is smooth and better aligned with the feature magnitudes, while maintaining the sum of gradients as one within each window. These modifications are applied during the backward pass when generating adversarial examples, and can be integrated into existing gradient-based attack frameworks to improve the relevance of the input gradient to the loss function, thereby enhancing transferability.
89347e7b42e00e949fd64060136cc64497ab2ef3.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the ImageNet dataset, using 5,000 images from the ILSVRC2012 validation set that are correctly classified by all victim models. ResNet-50 and VGG-19 are used as surrogate models, while nine victim models include six standard architectures (Inception-v3, Inception-ResNet-v2, DenseNet, MobileNet-v2, PNASNet, SENet) and three ensemble adversarially trained models. Baselines for comparison include SGM, LinBP, and Ghost, evaluated across multiple attack methods such as PGD, MI-FGSM, VMI-FGSM, ILA, and SSA. Attack success rates are measured as the misclassification rates on victim models, with both untargeted and targeted attacks evaluated. Additional experiments assess robustness against six defense methods (e.g., HGD, JPEG, RS), and ablation studies are conducted to analyze the impact of modifying ReLU and max-pooling gradients separately, as well as the effect of hyperparameters like the temperature coefficient.
89347e7b42e00e949fd64060136cc64497ab2ef3.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first systematic investigation and empirical validation of the negative impact of gradient truncation by non-linear layers on adversarial transferability. The proposed BPA method is novel in its use of SiLU-based derivatives for ReLU and softmax-based derivatives for max-pooling during backward propagation, which preserves more gradient information and substantially boosts transferability. BPA demonstrates generality by improving a variety of existing transfer-based attacks and model-related strategies, and achieves state-of-the-art performance in generating transferable adversarial examples across multiple models and defenses.

893bf7a50fb8854d3e8b5d6371652884df3627b5.title: When majority rules, minority loses: bias amplification of gradient descent
893bf7a50fb8854d3e8b5d6371652884df3627b5.research_question: How does training machine learning models with imbalanced data, without explicit data-level correction, affect the learning dynamics and predictive performance for minority subgroups, and what are the theoretical and empirical mechanisms underlying bias amplification in such scenarios?
893bf7a50fb8854d3e8b5d6371652884df3627b5.hypothesis: In strongly imbalanced majority-minority learning tasks, standard gradient descent training will initially produce predictors that align with majority group characteristics, leading to bias amplification and neglect of minority-specific features; escaping this bias and achieving fair, representative predictions requires substantially longer training durations.
893bf7a50fb8854d3e8b5d6371652884df3627b5.proposed_method: A formal theoretical framework will be developed to analyze majority-minority learning tasks, modeling the total loss as a sum of majority and minority group losses. The method will leverage Morse theory and Kantorovich-type arguments to characterize the geometry of the loss landscape, quantify the proximity between 'stereotypical' (majority-only) and 'representative' (full-data) predictors, and establish the conditions under which gradient descent trajectories become biased. Analytical results will be derived to estimate the stereotype gap and to provide lower bounds on the additional training time required for debiasing. Theoretical findings will be complemented by a protocol that empirically measures the distance between stereotypical and representative predictors and the debiasing time using gradient descent with various stopping criteria.
893bf7a50fb8854d3e8b5d6371652884df3627b5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using deep neural networks on both tabular (Adult income) and image classification datasets (CIFAR-10, EuroSAT), where minority and majority groups are defined by a binary attribute. Models will be trained without data-level balancing, and performance will be tracked separately for each subgroup. Baselines will include various architectures (e.g., ResNet18, MobileNetV2, TabNet) and alternative optimizers (AdamW, XGBoost). Evaluation metrics will include subgroup-specific accuracy, global accuracy, loss values, and the catch-up overcost (the relative increase in training epochs required for the minority group to reach a target accuracy). Experimental protocols will include measuring the time to reach both global and minority-specific accuracy thresholds, and comparing the training dynamics under different imbalance ratios and model sizes.
893bf7a50fb8854d3e8b5d6371652884df3627b5.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a general, model-agnostic theoretical framework for understanding bias amplification in imbalanced learning, focusing on the geometric and dynamical properties of the loss landscape rather than only loss trajectories or per-class gradients. It provides new analytical results quantifying the stereotype gap and debiasing duration, including lower bounds on the additional training required to achieve fair predictions. The work also empirically demonstrates that the majority-training zone dominates the parameter space, making it difficult to distinguish between biased and unbiased predictors, and quantifies the substantial training overcost required for minority subgroup fairness. These contributions offer both theoretical insights and practical guidance for training protocols in sensitive, imbalanced machine learning applications.

8946891e94831adc8cddb0d32311cce2445c96d2.title: MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts
8946891e94831adc8cddb0d32311cce2445c96d2.research_question: How can the mathematical reasoning abilities of large language models and large multimodal models be systematically evaluated in visually rich and diverse contexts, and what are the current limitations of these models compared to human performance?
8946891e94831adc8cddb0d32311cce2445c96d2.hypothesis: Current foundation models, including both large language models and large multimodal models, exhibit significant limitations in mathematical reasoning when visual understanding is required, and a comprehensive benchmark will reveal specific gaps and guide future improvements.
8946891e94831adc8cddb0d32311cce2445c96d2.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark, MATHVISTA, will be developed to evaluate mathematical reasoning in visual contexts. The benchmark will be constructed by aggregating and curating 6,141 examples from 28 existing multimodal datasets and three newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA), covering a wide range of mathematical reasoning types (algebraic, arithmetic, geometry, logical, numeric common sense, scientific, and statistical) and task formats (figure question answering, geometry problem solving, math word problems, textbook question answering, and visual question answering). Each example will be annotated with fine-grained metadata, including question type, answer type, grade level, visual context, and required reasoning skills. The evaluation protocol will involve three stages: response generation by the model, answer extraction using an LLM-based answer extractor, and deterministic accuracy scoring. The benchmark will be released with a public leaderboard and an online evaluation platform to prevent data contamination.
8946891e94831adc8cddb0d32311cce2445c96d2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 12 prominent foundation models, including text-only LLMs (e.g., ChatGPT, GPT-4, Claude-2), augmented LLMs with external visual information (image captions and OCR text), and large multimodal models (e.g., Bard, GPT-4V, LLaVA, miniGPT-4, InstructBLIP, mPLUG-OWL, IDEFICS). Models will be evaluated in zero-shot and few-shot settings with chain-of-thought and program-of-thought prompting. Baselines will include random chance and frequency guess, and a human performance baseline will be established using qualified annotators. Evaluation will be performed on a held-out test set, with accuracy as the primary metric, and fine-grained analysis will be conducted across task types, reasoning categories, and visual contexts.
8946891e94831adc8cddb0d32311cce2445c96d2.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces the first large-scale, systematic evaluation framework for mathematical reasoning in diverse visual contexts, addressing a significant gap in current benchmarks that focus primarily on text. MATHVISTA consolidates a wide range of tasks and reasoning types, includes newly created datasets to cover previously unaddressed scenarios, and provides detailed metadata for fine-grained analysis. The evaluation protocol leverages LLM-based answer extraction for robust and scalable assessment. This work aims to set a new standard for evaluating and advancing the capabilities of foundation models in mathematically intensive, visually rich real-world tasks.

894cd84bcc7acfb8cf5571c65cec124349f304d5.title: Equivariant Architectures for Learning in Deep Weight Spaces
894cd84bcc7acfb8cf5571c65cec124349f304d5.research_question: How can neural network architectures be designed to effectively learn and process other neural networks directly in their raw weight matrix form, while respecting the unique symmetry structures inherent in deep weight spaces?
894cd84bcc7acfb8cf5571c65cec124349f304d5.hypothesis: Architectures that are explicitly equivariant to the natural permutation symmetries of neural network weight spaces will outperform baseline methods in tasks that require learning over deep weight spaces, such as network adaptation, INR classification, and representation learning.
894cd84bcc7acfb8cf5571c65cec124349f304d5.proposed_method: A novel framework, Deep Weight-Space Networks (DWSNets), is developed to process neural networks represented as sequences of weights and biases. The methodology begins by analyzing the permutation symmetries of multilayer perceptron (MLP) weight spaces, where permuting the rows and columns of weight matrices in intermediate layers does not alter the represented function. The architecture is constructed using a composition of affine equivariant layers, termed DWS-layers, which are characterized and implemented using three basic operations: pooling, broadcasting, and fully connected layers applied to the input in a manner that preserves the identified symmetries. The DWS-layers are organized in a block-matrix structure, mapping between specific weight and bias subspaces, and are interleaved with pointwise nonlinearities to form deep networks capable of processing other deep models. The approach is theoretically grounded by providing a full characterization of all affine equivariant and invariant layers for these symmetries, ensuring efficient implementation and reduced parameter count compared to fully connected baselines.
894cd84bcc7acfb8cf5571c65cec124349f304d5.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on two primary task families: (1) processing implicit neural representations (INRs) for tasks such as INR classification (e.g., classifying MNIST and Fashion-MNIST images represented as INRs) and regression (e.g., predicting sine wave parameters from INR weights), and (2) processing standard neural networks for tasks such as adapting classifiers to new domains (e.g., adapting CIFAR-10 classifiers to corrupted domains). Datasets include MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, and synthetic sine wave data. Baselines for comparison include standard MLPs on flattened weights, MLPs with permutation-based data augmentation, weight-space alignment methods, INR2Vec architectures, and transformer-based models. Evaluation metrics include classification accuracy, mean squared error (MSE) for regression, and the quality of learned representations (e.g., via t-SNE visualization and downstream linear regression tasks). The experimental setup ensures fair comparison by controlling for data, loss functions, and training procedures across all methods.
894cd84bcc7acfb8cf5571c65cec124349f304d5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first principled, symmetry-based architecture for learning directly in deep weight spaces, providing a complete characterization of affine equivariant and invariant layers for the permutation symmetries of MLP weights. The method enables efficient and scalable neural architectures that can process other neural networks as input, outperforming natural and recent baselines in a variety of tasks. The DWSNet framework is shown to be expressive enough to approximate feed-forward passes and Lipschitz functions on the space of functions represented by input MLPs. The architecture is generalizable to other network types (e.g., CNNs, transformers) and supports extensions to nonlinear aggregation, multiple channels, and bias terms.

8963b5c1a754741d6599b95e47818fe3b79a6a51.title: Preserving Statistical Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis
8963b5c1a754741d6599b95e47818fe3b79a6a51.research_question: How can statistical validity be preserved in adaptive data analysis, where hypotheses and analyses are chosen based on previous data exploration and outcomes, rather than being fixed in advance?
8963b5c1a754741d6599b95e47818fe3b79a6a51.hypothesis: It is possible to guarantee statistical validity and accurate generalization in adaptive data analysis by leveraging techniques from differential privacy, thereby enabling accurate answers to exponentially many adaptively chosen queries with fewer samples than traditional methods.
8963b5c1a754741d6599b95e47818fe3b79a6a51.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops a principled framework for adaptive data analysis by utilizing differentially private algorithms as oracles to answer statistical queries. The method establishes a strong connection between differential privacy and generalization, proving that if queries are answered via a differentially private mechanism, the empirical averages of adaptively chosen functions remain close to their true expectations with high probability. The framework includes both computationally efficient and inefficient algorithms: one that perturbs each query answer with independent noise to ensure privacy and accuracy, and another that coordinates answers using more complex privacy-preserving techniques for higher query counts. Theoretical results are derived to bound the sample complexity required to answer m adaptively chosen queries with a specified tolerance, showing exponential improvements over naive empirical estimators.
8963b5c1a754741d6599b95e47818fe3b79a6a51.experiment_details: Experiments will involve simulating adaptive data analysis scenarios where an analyst selects queries based on previous outcomes, using datasets sampled from discrete domains such as binary attribute vectors. The proposed algorithms will be evaluated on their ability to answer a large number of adaptively chosen statistical queries accurately, with sample sizes and tolerances varied systematically. Baselines will include standard empirical estimators and naive holdout strategies. Evaluation metrics will focus on the accuracy of query answers (measured by deviation from true expectations), the number of queries answered within tolerance, and the sample complexity required. Additional analysis will compare computational efficiency and robustness to overfitting in adaptive settings.
8963b5c1a754741d6599b95e47818fe3b79a6a51.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a general transfer theorem connecting differential privacy to generalization in adaptive data analysis, enabling accurate answers to exponentially many adaptively chosen queries with high probability. This represents an exponential improvement in sample complexity over traditional empirical estimators. The approach is broadly applicable, not limited to specific inference procedures, and provides high-probability generalization bounds even under multiple rounds of adaptivity. The framework leverages strong composition and post-processing properties of differential privacy, offering a new calculus for building stable, generalizable adaptive analyses.

896c83e6dbd42621cb5c084bfc477802ed198b14.title: SparseTSF: Modeling Long-term Time Series Forecasting with 1k Parameters
896c83e6dbd42621cb5c084bfc477802ed198b14.research_question: How can long-term time series forecasting be achieved with minimal computational resources, while maintaining or surpassing the predictive accuracy and generalization capabilities of state-of-the-art models?
896c83e6dbd42621cb5c084bfc477802ed198b14.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that decoupling periodicity and trend components in time series data through a cross-period sparse forecasting technique, combined with a channel-independent strategy and extreme parameter reduction, will enable highly accurate and robust long-term time series forecasting with fewer than 1,000 parameters.
896c83e6dbd42621cb5c084bfc477802ed198b14.proposed_method: A novel framework, SparseTSF, will be developed for long-term time series forecasting, leveraging a Cross-Period Sparse Forecasting technique. The method begins by downsampling the original time series into multiple subsequences based on a known periodicity, effectively decomposing the data into periodic and trend components. Each subsequence is processed independently using a shared single-layer linear model, with a sliding aggregation step (implemented as a 1D convolution) to mitigate information loss and outlier effects. After prediction, the subsequences are upsampled and recombined to reconstruct the full forecast horizon. Instance normalization is applied before and after the model to address distributional shifts, and the Mean Squared Error (MSE) is used as the loss function. The approach is designed to operate in a channel-independent manner, focusing on univariate series within multivariate datasets for maximal parameter efficiency.
896c83e6dbd42621cb5c084bfc477802ed198b14.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on mainstream long-term time series forecasting benchmarks exhibiting daily periodicity, including ETTh1, ETTh2, Electricity, and Traffic datasets. The evaluation will compare SparseTSF against state-of-the-art baselines such as Informer, Autoformer, FEDformer, FiLM, TimesNet, PatchTST, DLinear, and FITS. Metrics will include Mean Squared Error (MSE), parameter count, multiply-accumulate operations (MACs), maximum memory usage, and training epoch time. The experimental setup will use a consistent look-back window (e.g., 720) and forecast horizons (e.g., 96, 192, 336, 720), with all models implemented in PyTorch and run on a single NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the sparse technique and hyperparameter settings, and cross-domain generalization tests will evaluate robustness across datasets.
896c83e6dbd42621cb5c084bfc477802ed198b14.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first long-term time series forecasting model with fewer than 1,000 parameters, achieving competitive or superior accuracy compared to much larger state-of-the-art models. The Cross-Period Sparse Forecasting technique enables effective decoupling of periodicity and trend, resulting in extreme parameter compression and robust extraction of periodic features. The approach demonstrates remarkable generalization capabilities, making it suitable for resource-constrained environments, small-sample scenarios, and low-quality data. Additionally, the method advances the lightweight modeling paradigm beyond previous milestones by orders of magnitude in parameter reduction.

897c0aedead3105b7b6cd1afbb6aeb4f62a06e11.title: GLAZE: Protecting Artists from Style Mimicry by Text-to-Image Models
897c0aedead3105b7b6cd1afbb6aeb4f62a06e11.research_question: How can artists be protected from unauthorized style mimicry by text-to-image generative models, particularly in scenarios where their artwork is used to train such models without consent?
897c0aedead3105b7b6cd1afbb6aeb4f62a06e11.hypothesis: Applying carefully crafted, minimally perceptible perturbations ('style cloaks') to artists' digital artwork before online sharing will disrupt the ability of text-to-image models to accurately mimic the artist's unique style, while maintaining the artwork's visual integrity for human viewers.
897c0aedead3105b7b6cd1afbb6aeb4f62a06e11.proposed_method: A novel system, Glaze, is proposed to generate 'style cloaks'—small, imperceptible perturbations—applied to digital artwork prior to online publication. The method first selects a target art style that is sufficiently distinct from the artist's own, using feature space distances computed from a large public dataset of labeled artworks. Each original artwork is then style-transferred to this target style using a pre-trained style transfer model, producing a style-transferred version. An optimization process computes a perturbation (the cloak) that, when added to the original artwork, shifts its feature representation (as extracted by a generic image encoder, e.g., from Stable Diffusion) towards that of the style-transferred image, while constraining the perceptual difference (using LPIPS) to remain below a user-specified threshold. The resulting cloaked images are visually similar to the originals but cause generative models trained on them to learn an incorrect or blended representation of the artist's style, thus disrupting future style mimicry.
897c0aedead3105b7b6cd1afbb6aeb4f62a06e11.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using both contemporary and historical artist datasets. For contemporary artists, private collections of 26–34 original pieces per artist will be used, verified to be absent from public training datasets. For historical artists, the WikiArt dataset (42,129 pieces, 195 artists) will be leveraged. The primary attack scenario involves fine-tuning state-of-the-art text-to-image models (Stable Diffusion v2.1 and DALL·E-mega) on either original or cloaked artwork, using image captions generated by an automated captioning model. Evaluation will include both quantitative and qualitative measures: large-scale user studies with professional artists (over 1,000 participants) will assess perceived mimicry and usability, while automated metrics such as CLIP-based genre shift rates will provide scalable, objective evaluation. Baselines include mimicry attacks on unprotected artwork and comparisons to existing cloaking methods. Experiments will also test robustness to adaptive countermeasures and partial protection scenarios (e.g., only a subset of an artist's online portfolio is cloaked).
897c0aedead3105b7b6cd1afbb6aeb4f62a06e11.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first system specifically designed to protect artists from style mimicry by text-to-image generative models via targeted, style-aware perturbations. Unlike prior image cloaking methods developed for facial recognition or indiscriminate feature suppression, this method focuses perturbation on style-specific features, guided by style transfer and feature space analysis. The system is evaluated in collaboration with the professional artist community, demonstrating both high efficacy in disrupting style mimicry and high tolerability of perturbations. The approach is robust to adaptive attacks and effective even when only a fraction of an artist's online artwork is protected, representing a significant advancement over existing alternatives.

899363b5743feaaa63e728326011f87d024b840f.title: Stable Differentiable Causal Discovery
899363b5743feaaa63e728326011f87d024b840f.research_question: How can causal discovery from observational and interventional data be made more stable, scalable, and accurate, particularly for large-scale problems involving thousands of variables?
899363b5743feaaa63e728326011f87d024b840f.hypothesis: Introducing a numerically stable acyclicity constraint and a two-stage optimization procedure will enable differentiable causal discovery methods to achieve improved accuracy, faster convergence, and scalability to large numbers of variables without sacrificing correctness.
899363b5743feaaa63e728326011f87d024b840f.proposed_method: A new framework, Stable Differentiable Causal Discovery (SDCD), is developed to address the instability and scalability limitations of existing differentiable causal discovery (DCD) methods. The method introduces a spectral acyclicity constraint based on the spectral radius of the adjacency matrix, which is theoretically and empirically shown to be stable and computationally efficient (O(d^2) time). SDCD employs a two-stage optimization procedure: the first stage performs edge preselection by solving a relaxed objective without the acyclicity constraint to prune unlikely edges, leveraging the sparsity common in real-world causal graphs; the second stage applies differentiable causal discovery with the stable spectral constraint, optimizing only over the preselected edges. Theoretical analysis proves that the first stage does not remove true causal parents, ensuring correctness. The method is implemented with neural network parameterizations for the conditional distributions, but is compatible with other expressive model classes.
899363b5743feaaa63e728326011f87d024b840f.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both simulated observational and interventional datasets, varying the number of variables (up to thousands), graph density, and proportion of intervened variables. The evaluation compares SDCD against state-of-the-art baselines including DCDI, DCD-FG, DAGMA, NO-TEARS, NO-BEARS, GIES, SCORE, and trivial baselines such as sortnregress. Performance is measured primarily using the Structural Hamming Distance (SHD) between the inferred and true causal graphs, with additional robustness checks and metrics as recommended in prior work. The experimental setup includes fixed neural network architectures for parameterization, no hyperparameter optimization, and both CPU and GPU runtime measurements. Ablation studies are performed to assess the contributions of the spectral constraint and the two-stage procedure.
899363b5743feaaa63e728326011f87d024b840f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretically and empirically stable acyclicity constraint based on the spectral radius, which overcomes the numerical instabilities of prior DCD methods. The two-stage optimization procedure is novel in its use of edge preselection to exploit graph sparsity, improving both convergence speed and accuracy. SDCD is the first DCD approach demonstrated to scale efficiently to thousands of variables while maintaining or improving accuracy relative to existing methods. Theoretical guarantees are provided for correctness and stability, and comprehensive empirical studies validate the method's superior performance and scalability.

899e489944063f0313ef01b33a8d4ce6ca386321.title: Shapley Explanation Networks
899e489944063f0313ef01b33a8d4ce6ca386321.research_question: How can feature attribution explanations, specifically Shapley values, be made intrinsic to deep learning models to enable efficient, scalable, and theoretically-grounded explanations during both training and inference, while maintaining high predictive performance?
899e489944063f0313ef01b33a8d4ce6ca386321.hypothesis: Incorporating Shapley values as latent representations within deep neural network architectures will enable efficient, layer-wise, and theoretically-grounded feature attribution explanations, facilitate explanation-based regularization during training, and allow for fast explanation computation at test time, all without sacrificing model accuracy.
899e489944063f0313ef01b33a8d4ce6ca386321.proposed_method: A novel neural network architecture, termed SHAPLEY EXPLANATION NETWORKS (SHAPNETs), will be developed to embed Shapley values as intrinsic latent representations at each layer. The approach introduces the Shapley transform, a mathematical operation mapping inputs or latent features to their Shapley value attributions with respect to a given function. SHAPNETs will be constructed by composing specialized neural modules (Shapley modules) that compute exact or approximate Shapley values for subsets of features (active sets), leveraging sparsity to reduce computational complexity. Both shallow (single-layer) and deep (multi-layer) variants will be implemented: Shallow SHAPNETs will provably compute exact Shapley values, while Deep SHAPNETs will maintain key Shapley properties (missingness and local accuracy) and support instance-specific dynamic pruning to further accelerate computation. The architecture will also support explanation-based regularization by making Shapley attributions available during training.
899e489944063f0313ef01b33a8d4ce6ca386321.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets, including tabular and image data, to evaluate the effectiveness of SHAPNETs. Baselines will include post-hoc Shapley approximation methods (such as KernelSHAP, DeepSHAP, and L-Shapley), as well as interpretable models like Generalized Additive Models (GAMs) and standard deep neural networks. Evaluation metrics will encompass predictive accuracy, explanation fidelity (measured by how well attributions satisfy Shapley properties), computational efficiency (inference and explanation time), and the impact of explanation-based regularization on model generalization. Experimental setups will include ablation studies on active set size, dynamic pruning, and layer-wise explanation quality.
899e489944063f0313ef01b33a8d4ce6ca386321.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to make Shapley explanations intrinsic to deep neural network architectures, enabling layer-wise, theoretically-grounded attributions in a single forward pass. It introduces the Shapley transform as a general framework for latent Shapley representations, and develops scalable Shapley modules that exploit sparsity for computational efficiency. The approach supports explanation-based regularization during training, and provides a mechanism for instance-specific dynamic pruning to accelerate inference. Shallow SHAPNETs are proven to yield exact Shapley values, while Deep SHAPNETs maintain key Shapley properties, representing a significant advance over prior post-hoc or limited-capacity explanation methods.

89a8d351ac88c920e0bd7c4a507c8130eed53754.title: Morphing Tokens Draw Strong Masked Image Models
89a8d351ac88c920e0bd7c4a507c8130eed53754.research_question: How can spatial inconsistency in supervisory signals for masked image modeling be addressed to improve the quality of learned visual representations in Vision Transformers, and what impact does this have on downstream performance and transferability?
89a8d351ac88c920e0bd7c4a507c8130eed53754.hypothesis: Spatially inconsistent supervisory signals from pre-trained models hinder effective representation learning in masked image modeling; introducing a context-preserving, dynamic token aggregation mechanism will reduce spatial inconsistency, leading to improved model performance and transferability.
89a8d351ac88c920e0bd7c4a507c8130eed53754.proposed_method: A novel framework, Dynamic Token Morphing (DTM), is proposed for masked image modeling in Vision Transformers. DTM dynamically aggregates contextually related tokens using a morphing matrix derived via bipartite matching or clustering, preserving semantic context while smoothing out spatial inconsistencies. The method introduces a dynamic scheduler that samples the number of morphed tokens and the number of morphing iterations per batch, ensuring diversity and adaptability in token aggregation. During training, both online and target encoders generate token representations, which are then morphed according to the dynamic schedule; the model aligns the morphed online and target tokens using a cosine distance-based loss. The process is repeated for multiple morphing cases per batch, and the final objective is a sum of these DTM losses, enabling the model to learn from more spatially consistent and context-rich supervisory signals.
89a8d351ac88c920e0bd7c4a507c8130eed53754.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale image classification and segmentation benchmarks, including ImageNet-1K and ADE20K. The proposed method will be pre-trained using Vision Transformer backbones (ViT-S/16, ViT-B/16, ViT-L/16) and compared against state-of-the-art self-supervised and supervised baselines, such as MAE, BEiT, iBOT, and MVP, using CLIP-B/16 as the target encoder for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 classification accuracy, mean Intersection-over-Union (mIoU) for segmentation, and transfer learning performance on datasets like iNaturalist and fine-grained visual classification benchmarks. Ablation studies will assess the impact of dynamic scheduling, different aggregation algorithms, and training efficiency, while training and fine-tuning protocols will follow established standards (e.g., 300-800 epochs pre-training, standard batch sizes, and resolutions).
89a8d351ac88c920e0bd7c4a507c8130eed53754.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a dynamic, context-preserving token aggregation mechanism for masked image modeling, addressing spatial inconsistency in supervisory signals—a problem not sufficiently tackled by prior token aggregation approaches focused on efficiency. Unlike static or naive aggregation, DTM leverages a dynamic scheduler and iterative morphing to generate diverse, contextually coherent supervisory targets, leading to improved representation learning. The approach is compatible with various self-supervised learning frameworks and demonstrates superior performance over complex state-of-the-art methods, with minimal additional training cost. Empirical results show enhanced training trends, better transferability, and state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks, validating the effectiveness and generality of the proposed framework.

89c3bd70ad33c4f8832f00ab98872b77861ee0ec.title: Discovering Latent Knowledge in Language Models Without Supervision
89c3bd70ad33c4f8832f00ab98872b77861ee0ec.research_question: How can latent knowledge within large language models be discovered and extracted in a purely unsupervised manner, without relying on model outputs or external supervision, particularly for answering yes-no or binary classification questions?
89c3bd70ad33c4f8832f00ab98872b77861ee0ec.hypothesis: It is possible to accurately recover and utilize latent knowledge encoded in the internal activations of language models to answer yes-no questions, without any supervision or reliance on model outputs, by identifying directions in activation space that satisfy logical consistency properties.
89c3bd70ad33c4f8832f00ab98872b77861ee0ec.proposed_method: A novel unsupervised method, Contrast-Consistent Search (CCS), is proposed to discover latent knowledge within language models. CCS operates by constructing contrast pairs for each yes-no question, generating both 'Yes' and 'No' natural language statements, and extracting their hidden state representations from a fixed, pre-trained model. These representations are normalized to remove label-specific artifacts, and a linear probe is trained to map the normalized activations to probabilities representing the truth of each statement. The probe is optimized using an unsupervised loss that enforces logical consistency (the probability of a statement and its negation should sum to one) and confidence (probabilities should be close to 0 or 1). The final prediction for each question is made by averaging the probability that the 'Yes' statement is true and one minus the probability that the 'No' statement is true.
89c3bd70ad33c4f8832f00ab98872b77861ee0ec.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using six different language models, including encoder-decoder (T5, UnifiedQA, T0), autoregressive (GPT-J), and encoder-only (RoBERTa, DeBERTa) architectures. Ten datasets spanning sentiment classification, topic classification, natural language inference, story completion, question answering, and commonsense reasoning will be converted to yes-no or binary classification tasks, with balanced labels and 1000 examples per dataset (500 for COPA). Each dataset will be split into 60% unsupervised training and 40% test sets. CCS will be compared against zero-shot and calibrated zero-shot baselines, as well as a supervised logistic regression ceiling. Evaluation metrics include accuracy and prompt sensitivity (standard deviation of accuracy across prompts), with multiple prompts used per dataset to assess robustness. Additional experiments will test robustness to misleading prompts and transferability across tasks.
89c3bd70ad33c4f8832f00ab98872b77861ee0ec.novelty_claims: The proposed approach enables the discovery of latent, task-agnostic representations of truth in language models without any supervision or reliance on model outputs. CCS leverages logical consistency properties to extract knowledge directly from internal activations, outperforming strong zero-shot baselines and exhibiting lower prompt sensitivity. The method demonstrates robustness even when model outputs are deliberately misled and can function with limited data. The approach also shows that representations of truth are salient and can sometimes be found via simple clustering or principal component analysis, indicating that unsupervised elicitation of model knowledge is both tractable and underexplored.

89e184d2bc830af568e439db9476caa0c047e11a.title: Guiding Pretraining in Reinforcement Learning with Large Language Models
89e184d2bc830af568e439db9476caa0c047e11a.research_question: How can reinforcement learning agents be guided to explore and acquire human-meaningful, context-sensitive, and useful behaviors in complex environments without dense external rewards or human-in-the-loop supervision?
89e184d2bc830af568e439db9476caa0c047e11a.hypothesis: Leveraging large pretrained language models to generate context-sensitive, common-sense, and diverse exploratory goals will bias reinforcement learning agents toward more human-meaningful behaviors during pretraining, resulting in improved coverage of useful behaviors and enhanced downstream task performance compared to existing intrinsically motivated exploration methods.
89e184d2bc830af568e439db9476caa0c047e11a.proposed_method: A novel framework, Exploring with Large Language Models (ELLM), is proposed to guide exploration in reinforcement learning by using large pretrained language models (LLMs) to generate plausible and context-sensitive goals for agents. At each timestep, the agent's current observation is converted into a text description, which, along with a list of valid actions, is used to prompt the LLM for a set of suggested goals. The agent is intrinsically rewarded for achieving these goals, with reward computed as the cosine similarity between the LLM-generated goal and a caption of the agent's transition, using a pretrained SentenceBERT encoder. To ensure novelty and prevent repetitive behaviors, previously achieved goals are filtered out within each episode. The agent can be trained in both goal-conditioned and goal-free settings, and the approach is compatible with both visual and text-based observations. The method is implemented using the DQN algorithm, and can utilize either ground-truth or learned captioners for state and transition descriptions.
89e184d2bc830af568e439db9476caa0c047e11a.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted in two complex environments: Crafter, a procedurally generated 2D Minecraft-like game with a combinatorial achievement tree, and Housekeep, a robotic household rearrangement simulator requiring common-sense object placement. In Crafter, the action space is expanded to include specific verb-noun pairs, increasing the relevance of LLM guidance. ELLM is compared against state-of-the-art intrinsically motivated RL baselines (APT, RND, Novelty), an oracle with ground-truth rewards, and ablations of the method. Evaluation metrics include the average number of unique achievements unlocked per episode during pretraining and downstream task success rates after fine-tuning or guided exploration. In Housekeep, the LLM is queried for yes/no judgments on object-receptacle pairs, and success is measured by the rate of correct rearrangements. Both environments use multiple random seeds, and additional analyses are performed on the robustness of ELLM to imperfect captioners and the impact of goal conditioning.
89e184d2bc830af568e439db9476caa0c047e11a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the use of large pretrained language models as a source of intrinsic motivation for RL agents, enabling automatic generation of diverse, human-meaningful, and context-sensitive exploratory goals without human intervention or environment-specific engineering. This method goes beyond traditional novelty-based exploration by biasing agents toward behaviors that are not only novel but also aligned with human common sense and task relevance. The framework is general, requiring only access to state and transition captions, and demonstrates improved exploration coverage and downstream task performance compared to existing intrinsically motivated RL methods.

8a4fc5f00cd4aca61e148e46a2125c3a406719f1.title: DS-1000: A Natural and Reliable Benchmark for Data Science Code Generation
8a4fc5f00cd4aca61e148e46a2125c3a406719f1.research_question: How can a comprehensive and reliable benchmark be developed to evaluate the capabilities of code generation models for real-world data science tasks across multiple Python libraries?
8a4fc5f00cd4aca61e148e46a2125c3a406719f1.hypothesis: A benchmark constructed from natural, diverse, and practical data science problems, combined with robust multi-criteria execution-based evaluation and anti-memorization strategies, will provide a more accurate and challenging assessment of code generation models' abilities in data science contexts than existing benchmarks.
8a4fc5f00cd4aca61e148e46a2125c3a406719f1.proposed_method: A new benchmark, DS-1000, will be constructed by curating 1000 data science programming problems sourced from StackOverflow, covering seven widely-used Python libraries: NumPy, Pandas, TensorFlow, PyTorch, SciPy, Scikit-learn, and Matplotlib. Each problem will be manually selected, rewritten for clarity and testability, and accompanied by an executable code context and reference solution. Multi-criteria automatic evaluation will be implemented, combining functional correctness (via hand-crafted test cases) and surface-form constraints (enforcing or forbidding specific APIs or keywords). To proactively defend against memorization by code generation models, each problem will be perturbed through surface and semantic modifications, ensuring that solutions cannot be simply recalled from pre-training data. The benchmark will undergo rigorous quality assurance, including expert review and red-teaming of evaluation metrics.
8a4fc5f00cd4aca61e148e46a2125c3a406719f1.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate several state-of-the-art code generation models, including Codex, CodeGen, and InCoder, using both left-to-right completion and infilling prompt formats. Each model will be tested on all 1000 DS-1000 problems, with 40 samples generated per problem using standardized sampling parameters (temperature 0.2, top-p 0.95, max length 1024). Performance will be measured using pass@1 accuracy, with additional analysis on the effects of surface, semantic, and difficult perturbations. The evaluation will compare results across libraries, prompt formats, and perturbation types, and will include reliability checks for the automatic evaluation metric (e.g., false discovery and omission rates). Baselines will include existing code generation datasets such as HumanEval, MBPP, and others, to contextualize DS-1000's difficulty and coverage.
8a4fc5f00cd4aca61e148e46a2125c3a406719f1.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces three key innovations: (1) the use of naturally occurring, diverse, and practical data science problems reflecting real-world user intents and contexts; (2) a robust, multi-criteria execution-based evaluation combining functional correctness and surface-form constraints, achieving a low false discovery rate; and (3) proactive anti-memorization measures through systematic perturbation of problems and reference solutions. DS-1000 is positioned as the first benchmark to offer both naturalistic problem diversity and reliable automatic evaluation for data science code generation, enabling fairer and more meaningful assessment of model capabilities.

8a86c5640e756b6fc8e333c190ed704e2656ba79.title: New Algorithmic Directions in Optimal Transport and Applications for Product Spaces
8a86c5640e756b6fc8e333c190ed704e2656ba79.research_question: How can efficient, polynomial-time computable optimal transport maps be constructed between high-dimensional distributions, particularly when the source is a product distribution and the target is arbitrary, and what are the algorithmic and computational implications for concentration of measure and related applications?
8a86c5640e756b6fc8e333c190ed704e2656ba79.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, under suitable conditions on the target distribution (such as sequential samplability with bounded average sampling cost), there exist polynomial-time algorithms that can compute transport maps from product distributions to arbitrary high-dimensional distributions with transportation cost close to the optimal, and that these methods can yield dimension-independent concentration results for Gaussian spaces.
8a86c5640e756b6fc8e333c190ed704e2656ba79.proposed_method: A new algorithmic framework for optimal transport will be developed, focusing on constructing transport maps from product distributions to arbitrary high-dimensional target distributions. The approach will leverage online, coordinate-wise algorithms inspired by the Knothe–Rosenblatt (KR) transport, where each coordinate of the target is sampled sequentially conditioned on previously chosen coordinates. The method requires only oracle access to efficient samplers for the source and sequential samplers for the target. For each coordinate, batches of samples are drawn and optimally matched using min-cost flow or matching algorithms, with the computational error controlled by the batch size. The framework will be extended to handle conditional distributions (e.g., Gaussian conditioned on a set) using membership oracles, and reductions will be developed to transfer algorithmic transport results between different spaces (e.g., from Gaussian to uniform on the cube or sphere).
8a86c5640e756b6fc8e333c190ed704e2656ba79.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on high-dimensional synthetic distributions, including standard product distributions (e.g., multivariate Gaussian) and arbitrary or conditioned target distributions (such as Gaussian conditioned on a set of small measure). The proposed algorithmic transport will be evaluated in terms of computational efficiency (polynomial-time scaling with dimension), achieved transportation cost (compared to the KR and Talagrand bounds), and the ability to achieve dimension-independent concentration results. Baselines will include classical offline optimal transport algorithms (e.g., Hungarian algorithm, Sinkhorn algorithm) and empirical sample-based methods. Evaluation metrics will include expected transportation cost under various norms (ℓ_p, especially ℓ_2), runtime, and the quality of concentration bounds (e.g., distance to set S for Gaussian measure ε).
8a86c5640e756b6fc8e333c190ed704e2656ba79.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel theory of algorithmic transport that focuses on polynomial-time computable mappings in high-dimensional settings, contrasting with traditional computational OT which may be exponential in dimension. The method provides the first general-purpose, efficient online transport algorithms for product-to-arbitrary distributions with provable cost guarantees. It establishes the first computational concentration results for Gaussian measures with dimension-independent transportation cost, resolving open questions in the field. The notion of 'sequentially samplable' distributions and the associated algorithmic framework are new, as are the reduction techniques for transferring algorithmic transport results between different geometric spaces.

8a8eca2618b13a1581d9b49827572cffbc28b005.title: Simple ReFlow: Improved Techniques for Fast Flow Models
8a8eca2618b13a1581d9b49827572cffbc28b005.research_question: How can the efficiency and sample quality of fast generative flow models, specifically those employing ReFlow procedures, be improved for time-critical applications without violating theoretical guarantees?
8a8eca2618b13a1581d9b49827572cffbc28b005.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a systematic redesign of the ReFlow procedure—through improved training dynamics, learning strategies, and inference techniques—can significantly enhance both the speed and sample quality of generative flow models, achieving state-of-the-art results with minimal neural function evaluations.
8a8eca2618b13a1581d9b49827572cffbc28b005.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed to optimize the ReFlow procedure for fast flow-based generative models. The approach involves generalizing the flow-matching loss with adaptive weighting functions that account for loss variance across both time and data, and employing a time distribution that emphasizes critical regions for improved convergence. The loss function will be enhanced by incorporating high-pass filtering through an invertible linear map, accelerating the learning of high-frequency features while maintaining theoretical correctness. Learning improvements will include optimal dropout rates for denoiser UNets and the use of both forward and backward generated data pairs, with additional projection of training couplings onto the set of joint distributions with correct marginals. For inference, a sigmoidal discretization schedule and advanced ODE solvers (such as DPM-Solver with tuned parameters) will be used to minimize discretization error, especially near high-curvature regions of the ODE trajectory.
8a8eca2618b13a1581d9b49827572cffbc28b005.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image generation benchmarks, including CIFAR10 (32x32), AFHQv2 (64x64), FFHQ (64x64), and class-conditional ImageNet-64. The evaluation protocol will involve generating large numbers of data pairs using both forward and backward ODE integration, with models initialized from pre-trained EDM denoisers. Ablation studies will systematically test the impact of each proposed improvement on FID (Fréchet Inception Distance) scores, using 50,000 generated samples per trial and comparing against all available dataset images. Baselines will include state-of-the-art fast neural ODE methods such as EDM, DPM-Solver, curvature minimization, and minibatch OT flow matching. Evaluation metrics will include FID and ODE trajectory straightness, with additional analysis of local truncation errors for different discretization strategies.
8a8eca2618b13a1581d9b49827572cffbc28b005.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces seven distinct improvements across training dynamics, learning, and inference for ReFlow-based generative models, all within the bounds of flow-matching theory. Key innovations include adaptive loss normalization, a theoretically justified high-pass filtered loss, optimal dropout scheduling, the use of both forward and backward data pairs with marginal projection, and a novel sigmoidal discretization schedule for ODE integration. This approach achieves state-of-the-art FID scores for fast neural ODE-based generation with as few as nine neural function evaluations, outperforming all previously published fast flow and diffusion-based methods without reliance on heuristic or perceptual losses.

8a95c7a1d0527f64921fbf5634c35c137d115782.title: Practical Conditional Neural Processes Via Tractable Dependent Predictions
8a95c7a1d0527f64921fbf5634c35c137d115782.research_question: How can conditional neural process models be developed to efficiently produce dependent predictions, enabling coherent function samples and improved predictive performance, particularly for applications requiring modeling of output correlations such as environmental and healthcare tasks?
8a95c7a1d0527f64921fbf5634c35c137d115782.hypothesis: Parameterizing the predictive covariance of conditional neural processes with context-dependent neural networks and positive-definite functions will enable tractable, scalable, and accurate modeling of output dependencies, leading to improved predictive performance and coherent function samples compared to mean-field and latent variable models.
8a95c7a1d0527f64921fbf5634c35c137d115782.proposed_method: A new class of Gaussian Neural Process (GNP) models will be developed, in which the mean and covariance of a multivariate Gaussian predictive distribution are parameterized by neural networks conditioned on the context set. Two parameterizations for the covariance will be explored: a linear covariance using meta-learned basis functions, and a 'kvv' covariance combining neural network feature mappings with an exponentiated quadratic kernel modulated by learned scalars. The approach will be extended to multi-output regression by learning separate functions for each output dimension and representing cross-output covariances. To address non-Gaussian data, invertible marginal transformations (copula-based) will be composed with the GNP predictive, enabling modeling of non-Gaussian output distributions. The models will be trained via exact maximum likelihood, leveraging the analytic tractability of the predictive distributions.
8a95c7a1d0527f64921fbf5634c35c137d115782.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic experiments will include regression tasks with data generated from Gaussian processes using various covariance functions (e.g., exponentiated quadratic, Matern, noisy mixture, weakly periodic), as well as a non-Gaussian Lotka-Volterra predator-prey system. Real-world experiments will include multi-channel electroencephalogram (EEG) time series data and temperature downscaling for climate modeling using European reanalysis and station data. Baselines will include mean-field CNPs, latent variable neural processes (ANP, ConvNP), FullConvGNP, and standard multi-output Gaussian processes. Evaluation metrics will include predictive log-likelihood, mean absolute error (MAE), and performance on downstream estimation tasks (e.g., threshold event probabilities). Experimental setups will involve splitting data into context and target sets, training on historical or training periods, and testing on held-out or future periods, with careful comparison of computational efficiency and sample quality.
8a95c7a1d0527f64921fbf5634c35c137d115782.novelty_claims: The proposed models introduce a tractable and scalable framework for conditional neural processes that directly parameterize predictive covariances, enabling dependent predictions without the computational burden of high-dimensional convolutions or intractable latent variable inference. The approach supports multi-output and non-Gaussian regression via invertible marginal transformations, and enables exact maximum likelihood training. The models are claimed to outperform mean-field and latent variable baselines in both predictive accuracy and the ability to generate coherent function samples, with demonstrated applicability to real-world tasks such as EEG imputation and climate downscaling, where modeling output dependencies is critical.

8a9e11addba791860a9dbf15de75cc28d2cf844c.title: Are We on the Right Way for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models?
8a9e11addba791860a9dbf15de75cc28d2cf844c.research_question: How can the evaluation of large vision-language models (LVLMs) be improved to more accurately and fairly assess their true multi-modal capabilities, specifically by addressing the issues of visual dependency and data leakage in current benchmarks?
8a9e11addba791860a9dbf15de75cc28d2cf844c.hypothesis: Current multi-modal benchmarks for LVLMs contain a significant proportion of samples that do not require visual understanding and are susceptible to data leakage, leading to overestimated model performance; a rigorously curated, vision-dependent benchmark with explicit controls for data leakage will enable more accurate and fair evaluation of LVLMs’ multi-modal abilities.
8a9e11addba791860a9dbf15de75cc28d2cf844c.proposed_method: A new benchmark, MMStar, will be developed to rigorously evaluate LVLMs on vision-indispensable tasks. The methodology involves a two-stage data curation process: first, an automated pipeline will filter out samples from existing benchmarks that can be answered by large language models (LLMs) without visual input, using a panel of both closed- and open-source LLMs as inspectors. Only samples that are not answerable by more than two out of eight LLMs will be retained. Second, a manual review by experts will ensure that each sample requires visual understanding, minimizes data leakage, and covers a diverse set of multi-modal capabilities and difficulty levels. The final benchmark will consist of 1,500 high-quality, human-validated samples spanning six core capability dimensions and 18 detailed axes. Additionally, two new metrics—multi-modal gain (MG) and multi-modal leakage (ML)—will be defined to quantify the actual performance improvement from multi-modal training and the extent of data leakage, respectively.
8a9e11addba791860a9dbf15de75cc28d2cf844c.experiment_details: Experiments will involve evaluating 16 leading LVLMs and their corresponding LLM backbones on the MMStar benchmark and seven existing multi-modal benchmarks. For LLMs, both 0-shot and 2-shot inference strategies will be used, while LVLMs will be evaluated using a 0-shot strategy. The evaluation will include both standard (with images) and LVLM-text (without images) settings to diagnose visual dependency and data leakage. Accuracy, multi-modal gain, and multi-modal leakage will be reported for each model. All experiments will be conducted using a unified codebase and consistent hardware (NVIDIA A100 GPUs), with multiple-choice answer formats and heuristic answer matching for automated scoring.
8a9e11addba791860a9dbf15de75cc28d2cf844c.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a benchmark that explicitly enforces visual dependency and minimizes data leakage, addressing two critical flaws in current LVLM evaluation. The curation process combines automated LLM-based filtering with expert human review, resulting in a uniquely rigorous and balanced dataset. The introduction of multi-modal gain and multi-modal leakage metrics provides, for the first time, a quantitative framework to disentangle true multi-modal learning from spurious performance due to memorization or text-only reasoning. This approach enables fairer, more transparent, and more diagnostic evaluation of LVLMs’ multi-modal capabilities.

8abb89abf6410f30a8b9248dbd2e3cf818d4f722.title: Generative Classifiers Avoid Shortcut Solutions
8abb89abf6410f30a8b9248dbd2e3cf818d4f722.research_question: Can generative classifiers, based on class-conditional generative models, provide improved robustness to distribution shift and reduce reliance on spurious correlations in classification tasks across image and text domains?
8abb89abf6410f30a8b9248dbd2e3cf818d4f722.hypothesis: Generative classifiers, by modeling the full input distribution for each class, are less prone to shortcut learning and overfitting to spurious correlations, resulting in better generalization under distribution shift compared to discriminative classifiers.
8abb89abf6410f30a8b9248dbd2e3cf818d4f722.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops generative classifiers by training class-conditional generative models to estimate p(x|y) for each class, and then applies Bayes' rule to compute p(y|x) for classification. For image tasks, diffusion-based generative models (e.g., class-conditional U-Net-based latent diffusion) are trained using standard generative modeling pipelines without specialized augmentations or additional hyperparameters. For text tasks, autoregressive Transformer language models are modified to prepend a class token to each sequence, enabling efficient computation of class-conditional likelihoods via forward passes. At inference, for each input, the class with the highest estimated p(x|y) (or lowest cross-entropy loss) is selected as the prediction. The method is designed to be straightforward to implement, requiring no additional supervision or knowledge of spurious correlations.
8abb89abf6410f30a8b9248dbd2e3cf818d4f722.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five standard distribution shift benchmarks: Waterbirds, CelebA, Camelyon17-WILDS, FMoW, and CivilComments, covering both image and text modalities and including both subpopulation and domain shifts. Generative classifiers will be compared to discriminative baselines such as ERM, LfF, JTT, and DFR/RWY, with all models trained from scratch to control for pretraining effects. Model selection and hyperparameter tuning will be based solely on in-distribution validation accuracy, reflecting realistic deployment scenarios. Evaluation metrics include in-distribution accuracy, worst-group accuracy for subpopulation shift, and out-of-distribution accuracy for domain shift. Additional analyses will include gradient norm tracking, ablation on unconditional objectives, and scaling studies on model size. A simplified Gaussian toy dataset will also be used to analyze inductive biases and generalization phases.
8abb89abf6410f30a8b9248dbd2e3cf818d4f722.novelty_claims: The proposed research claims that generative classifiers, leveraging modern generative modeling techniques, can outperform discriminative approaches on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution benchmarks without requiring specialized training procedures, extra hyperparameters, or prior knowledge of spurious correlations. The approach is the first to demonstrate 'effective robustness'—superior out-of-distribution performance relative to in-distribution accuracy—across multiple realistic benchmarks. The work also provides new theoretical and empirical insights into the inductive biases of generative classifiers, including phase diagrams that characterize when generative methods are expected to outperform discriminative ones.

8ad199f11f386319ebd2706c372562677c98fae3.title: Latent-Shift: Latent Diffusion with Temporal Shift for Efficient Text-to-Video Generation
8ad199f11f386319ebd2706c372562677c98fae3.research_question: How can text-to-image latent diffusion models be efficiently extended to enable high-quality, temporally coherent text-to-video generation without significantly increasing model complexity or computational cost?
8ad199f11f386319ebd2706c372562677c98fae3.hypothesis: A parameter-free temporal shift module, when integrated into a pretrained text-to-image latent diffusion model, will enable efficient and effective text-to-video generation by leveraging spatial U-Net architectures for temporal modeling, resulting in competitive or superior video generation quality compared to existing methods that use additional temporal modules.
8ad199f11f386319ebd2706c372562677c98fae3.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a parameter-free temporal shift module into the U-Net backbone of a pretrained text-to-image latent diffusion model. The method utilizes a fixed autoencoder to encode and decode video frames independently into a compact latent space. During training, the temporal shift module shifts a portion of feature map channels forward and backward along the temporal dimension, allowing each frame's features to incorporate information from adjacent frames. This module is inserted into the residual branch of each 2D ResNet block within the U-Net, enabling temporal context aggregation without adding new parameters. The model is finetuned on text-video pairs, with text conditioning applied via cross-attention in the transformer blocks, and classifier-free guidance is used to improve sample fidelity.
8ad199f11f386319ebd2706c372562677c98fae3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale text-video datasets such as WebVid (10M pairs) for training, with evaluations performed on MSR-VTT and UCF-101 datasets. The method will be compared against strong baselines including CogVideo, Make-A-Video, and latent video diffusion models with temporal attention. Evaluation metrics will include FID, CLIP similarity, Inception Score (IS), Frechet Video Distance (FVD), and user studies assessing video quality and text-video faithfulness. Model size and inference speed will also be benchmarked, with all models generating videos at 256x256 resolution for two-second clips, and random samples generated for each prompt without automatic ranking.
8ad199f11f386319ebd2706c372562677c98fae3.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel, parameter-free temporal shift module that enables the direct extension of a spatial U-Net for efficient text-to-video generation in the latent space. This approach eliminates the need for additional temporal convolution or attention layers, reducing model complexity and computational cost. The method uniquely preserves text-to-image generation capability even after finetuning for video, and achieves state-of-the-art or competitive results on standard benchmarks with significantly fewer parameters and faster inference compared to existing methods.

8ad6f1e607460e6ef8f7fe81887ebd720f4563aa.title: Tight Guarantees for Interactive Decision Making with the Decision-Estimation Coefficient
8ad6f1e607460e6ef8f7fe81887ebd720f4563aa.research_question: What are the fundamental statistical complexity measures that govern sample-efficient learning guarantees in interactive decision making, and how can optimal sample complexity be characterized for general classes of problems such as bandits and reinforcement learning with function approximation?
8ad6f1e607460e6ef8f7fe81887ebd720f4563aa.hypothesis: A new complexity measure, the Constrained Decision-Estimation Coefficient (DEC), provides tight upper and lower bounds on the optimal sample complexity for interactive decision making, improving upon previous measures by holding globally, in expectation, and allowing improper reference models.
8ad6f1e607460e6ef8f7fe81887ebd720f4563aa.proposed_method: A new variant of the Decision-Estimation Coefficient, termed the Constrained Decision-Estimation Coefficient (DEC), will be introduced to quantify the statistical complexity of interactive decision making problems. This coefficient imposes a hard constraint on the information gain, measured via the squared Hellinger distance between models, rather than a soft penalty as in previous approaches. The methodology involves deriving both minimax lower and upper bounds on regret and PAC (Probably Approximately Correct) sample complexity using this new coefficient, for general model classes encompassing bandits and reinforcement learning with function approximation. The analysis will leverage new proof techniques, including adversarial model construction and change-of-measure arguments, to establish that the constrained DEC characterizes the fundamental limits of learnability in these settings.
8ad6f1e607460e6ef8f7fe81887ebd720f4563aa.experiment_details: Theoretical experiments will be conducted by analyzing the regret and PAC sample complexity for a variety of model classes, including multi-armed bandits, linear bandits, tabular reinforcement learning, and nonparametric bandits. Lower and upper bounds will be compared quantitatively to those from prior work, with specific attention to the scaling of the DEC in different regimes (e.g., parametric, nonparametric, and low-noise settings). The evaluation will include detailed case studies and examples, with complexity constants computed for standard problem classes. Theoretical guarantees will be validated by deriving explicit rates and demonstrating tightness up to logarithmic factors.
8ad6f1e607460e6ef8f7fe81887ebd720f4563aa.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the Constrained Decision-Estimation Coefficient, which yields tighter and more general lower bounds than previous measures by holding in expectation, globally (without localization), and for all algorithms, including those using improper reference models. The method closes nearly all gaps between upper and lower bounds in prior work, unifying regret and PAC frameworks under a single complexity measure. New analysis and algorithmic techniques are developed, and the results establish that improper reference models play a fundamental role in interactive decision making theory.

8adba8661f47ec5cf70a7697264605f891a37390.title: Automatic Differentiation of Optimization Algorithms with Time-Varying Updates
8adba8661f47ec5cf70a7697264605f891a37390.research_question: How can automatic differentiation be theoretically and practically extended to optimization algorithms with time-varying update rules, and what are the convergence properties of the resulting derivative iterates, particularly in the context of partly smooth and non-smooth optimization problems?
8adba8661f47ec5cf70a7697264605f891a37390.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, under appropriate regularity and contraction assumptions, the derivative iterates produced by automatic differentiation of optimization algorithms with time-varying updates will converge (with a linear rate) to the true derivative of the solution mapping, and that this convergence rate will reflect the convergence rate of the underlying optimization algorithm, even in the presence of non-smooth or partly smooth objectives.
8adba8661f47ec5cf70a7697264605f891a37390.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed for analyzing automatic differentiation (AD) applied to iterative optimization algorithms where the update mapping changes at each iteration (time-varying updates). The approach will formalize conditions under which the derivative sequence generated by AD converges to the derivative of the solution mapping, leveraging the Implicit Function Theorem and contraction properties. The method will be specifically adapted to proximal gradient descent (PGD) with variable step sizes and to accelerated proximal gradient (APG/FISTA) methods for partly smooth problems. Theoretical convergence rate guarantees for the derivative iterates will be established, and the analysis will be extended beyond settings where the update mapping converges pointwise, thus covering a broader class of practical algorithms.
8adba8661f47ec5cf70a7697264605f891a37390.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on linear and logistic regression problems with ℓ1 and ℓ2 regularization, respectively, to empirically validate the theoretical findings. Both synthetic and real datasets may be used, though specific datasets are not detailed. The proposed AD-based approach will be compared against implicit differentiation and possibly other baseline differentiation techniques. Evaluation metrics will include the accuracy of the computed derivatives (e.g., normed error with respect to ground truth or implicit differentiation), convergence rates of both the optimization and derivative iterates, and computational efficiency. Key experimental setups will involve varying the step size schedules and regularization parameters to assess robustness across different algorithmic regimes.
8adba8661f47ec5cf70a7697264605f891a37390.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a strengthened theoretical analysis of automatic differentiation for optimization algorithms with iteration-dependent (time-varying) updates, providing new convergence rate guarantees for the derivative iterates. The framework extends previous results by removing restrictive assumptions such as pointwise convergence of the update mapping and by covering cases where the update mapping does not converge. The approach is further generalized to handle partly smooth and non-smooth objectives, and the convergence of AD is established for both PGD with variable step size and APG/FISTA. This work closes theoretical gaps in the literature and provides practical guidelines for applying AD in modern bilevel and meta-optimization settings.

8b0466171d68c03f5285ee9890c4dbdc353071c3.title: Improving Progressive Generation with Decomposable Flow Matching
8b0466171d68c03f5285ee9890c4dbdc353071c3.research_question: How can progressive generation of high-dimensional visual modalities, such as images and videos, be improved in terms of visual quality, computational efficiency, and architectural simplicity, while maintaining flexibility in decomposition strategies and minimizing modifications to existing generative modeling pipelines?
8b0466171d68c03f5285ee9890c4dbdc353071c3.hypothesis: A decomposable, multi-stage flow matching framework that applies flow matching independently at each level of a user-defined multi-scale representation will enable more effective progressive generation, resulting in improved visual quality, faster convergence, and reduced architectural complexity compared to existing multi-stage or cascaded generative models.
