8b0466171d68c03f5285ee9890c4dbdc353071c3.proposed_method: A novel framework, Decomposable Flow Matching (DFM), is introduced for progressive generation of visual media. The method begins by decomposing each input into a multi-scale representation using a user-defined decomposition function, such as a Laplacian pyramid, but is agnostic to the specific decomposition method. At each stage (scale) of this representation, an independent flow matching process is applied, with per-stage flow timesteps controlling the denoising and generation process. During inference, a standard sampler operates on each stage sequentially, guided by a user-defined schedule that dictates the progression of flow timesteps per stage, starting from the coarsest and moving to finer scales. During training, the model simulates progressive generation by sampling a stage, applying noise levels accordingly across stages, and minimizing per-scale velocity prediction errors using a shared generator conditioned on the full set of noisy input scales and their timesteps. Architectural adaptations include dedicated input and output patchification layers per scale, per-scale timestep embedders, and loss masking to ensure effective progressive learning dynamics.
8b0466171d68c03f5285ee9890c4dbdc353071c3.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the ImageNet-1K and Kinetics-700 datasets for image and video generation, respectively. Latent spaces are produced using FLUX and Cogvideo autoencoders, which are fine-tuned for scale-equivariant properties to align latent and RGB frequency components. The main model backbone is DiT (Diffusion Transformer), evaluated in both DiT-B and DiT-XL variants. Baselines include Flow Matching, Cascaded models, and Pyramidal Flow, all trained with equivalent compute budgets and on the same backbone. Evaluation metrics include FID, Inception Score (IS), FDD (Frechet Distance with DINOv2 features), frame-FID, and FVD for videos. Ablation studies are performed on training and sampling hyperparameters, input decomposition strategies, and architectural choices. Additionally, the framework is applied to fine-tuning large-scale models (FLUX), comparing standard fine-tuning with DFM-based fine-tuning using FID, FDD, and CLIP similarity metrics.
8b0466171d68c03f5285ee9890c4dbdc353071c3.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple and effective progressive generation framework that is agnostic to decomposition choice, does not require multiple models or per-stage training, and can be integrated with minimal modifications to existing pipelines. It enables independent flow matching at each scale within a single model, offering architectural simplicity and computational efficiency. The approach is validated through comprehensive analysis and ablation studies, demonstrating superior performance over state-of-the-art progressive generation frameworks on both image and video benchmarks, as well as faster convergence and improved quality when fine-tuning large-scale generative models.

8b0d2c8d22f3a4e9eb8fbd392c72931a10e67de8.title: Doubly-Robust Estimation of Counterfactual Policy Mean Embeddings
8b0d2c8d22f3a4e9eb8fbd392c72931a10e67de8.research_question: How can the full distribution of outcomes under counterfactual policies be estimated and represented in a flexible, nonparametric manner for off-policy evaluation, enabling principled hypothesis testing and sampling in complex domains such as healthcare, recommendation, and structured outcome spaces?
8b0d2c8d22f3a4e9eb8fbd392c72931a10e67de8.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that embedding the counterfactual outcome distribution in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) and employing doubly robust estimation techniques will yield consistent, efficient, and flexible estimators that outperform existing methods in distributional off-policy evaluation, hypothesis testing, and sampling, even with complex or structured outcomes.
8b0d2c8d22f3a4e9eb8fbd392c72931a10e67de8.proposed_method: A novel framework, Counterfactual Policy Mean Embedding (CPME), will be developed to represent the entire counterfactual outcome distribution as a kernel mean embedding in an RKHS. Two estimators will be constructed: a nonparametric plug-in estimator that combines empirical kernel mean embeddings of the policy-context distribution and the conditional mean operator, and a doubly robust estimator leveraging the efficient influence function (EIF) for the CPME. The doubly robust estimator will correct for bias in both the outcome embedding and the propensity model, ensuring consistency if either is correctly specified. The methodology will also include the derivation of an asymptotically normal, computationally efficient kernel-based test statistic for hypothesis testing between counterfactual policies, and a kernel herding-based procedure for sampling from the estimated counterfactual distribution.
8b0d2c8d22f3a4e9eb8fbd392c72931a10e67de8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and semi-synthetic datasets, including scenarios with continuous and discrete actions, as well as structured outcomes such as images (e.g., dSprites dataset). Baselines will include existing kernel-based policy tests (KPT) with various kernels (linear, RBF, polynomial) and plug-in estimators. Evaluation metrics will comprise empirical rejection rates for hypothesis testing (type I/II error), calibration under the null, power under alternatives, and distributional distances (MMD, Wasserstein) for sampling quality. Experimental setups will include varying policy shifts, mixture distributions, and outcome functions, with both outcome and propensity models estimated from data using kernel methods and regression.
8b0d2c8d22f3a4e9eb8fbd392c72931a10e67de8.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the first doubly robust estimator for counterfactual policy mean embeddings in the context of distributional off-policy evaluation, supporting both discrete and continuous action spaces. The approach enables principled, nonparametric hypothesis testing between counterfactual outcome distributions with asymptotic normality guarantees, as well as efficient sampling from complex counterfactual distributions. The method improves convergence rates over existing plug-in and importance-weighted estimators, extends kernel mean embedding techniques to general policy interventions, and demonstrates robustness and sensitivity in scenarios with structured and high-dimensional outcomes.

8b20edda4a0013d628b9c4e9e4b42a5f1310b12f.title: Autoregressive Diffusion Model for Graph Generation
8b20edda4a0013d628b9c4e9e4b42a5f1310b12f.research_question: How can graph generative models be improved to address challenges such as slow sampling speed, difficulty in model training, and the inability to incorporate constraints, especially for discrete graph data?
8b20edda4a0013d628b9c4e9e4b42a5f1310b12f.hypothesis: An autoregressive diffusion process that operates directly in the discrete graph space, coupled with a learned data-dependent node ordering, will enable more efficient, flexible, and high-quality graph generation compared to existing one-shot diffusion-based and autoregressive models.
8b20edda4a0013d628b9c4e9e4b42a5f1310b12f.proposed_method: A novel autoregressive diffusion framework for graph generation will be developed, in which the forward process absorbs nodes one at a time into an absorbing state, masking both the node and its incident edges. The node absorption order will be determined by a diffusion ordering network, which learns a data-dependent permutation of nodes based on graph topology using a graph neural network with positional encodings. The reverse generative process will employ a denoising network, designed as a graph attention network, to reconstruct the graph by sequentially predicting the type of the new node and its edges to previously denoised nodes in the reverse order of absorption. Edge prediction will utilize a mixture of multinomial distributions to efficiently capture dependencies among edges. The model will be trained by optimizing a variational lower bound on the data likelihood, leveraging the permutation invariance property of graphs to simplify the training objective and enable joint training of the ordering and denoising networks, with reinforcement learning used to optimize the ordering network.
8b20edda4a0013d628b9c4e9e4b42a5f1310b12f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six diverse generic graph datasets (such as Community-small, Caveman, Cora, Breast, Enzymes, and Ego-small) and two molecule datasets (QM9 and ZINC250k). The proposed method will be compared to a comprehensive set of baselines, including one-shot models (e.g., GraphVAE, SPECTRE, DiGress, EDP-GNN, GDSS), autoregressive models (e.g., DeepGMG, GraphRNN, GraphAF, GraphDF, GRAN, OM), and flow-based or energy-based models. Evaluation metrics will include maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) for degree distribution, clustering coefficient, and orbit occurrence, as well as generation time. For molecule generation, additional metrics such as Frechet ChemNet Distance (FCD), NSPDK-MMD, validity, uniqueness, and novelty will be used. Constrained graph generation experiments will assess the ability to incorporate structural constraints, such as maximum node degree. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of learned node ordering versus random ordering.
8b20edda4a0013d628b9c4e9e4b42a5f1310b12f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first autoregressive diffusion model for graph generation that operates directly in the discrete graph space using a node-absorbing process. A key innovation is the diffusion ordering network, which learns a data-dependent node generation order to better leverage graph structural regularities, improving both training efficiency and generation quality. The method enables efficient incorporation of constraints during generation, addresses the limitations of one-shot and continuous-space diffusion models, and achieves a favorable trade-off between flexibility and efficiency. The training objective is simplified by exploiting permutation invariance, and the approach demonstrates significant improvements in both speed and generation performance over state-of-the-art baselines.

8b28792f8405b737229afb92c99c579b86d8aa98.title: Llama Guard: LLM-based Input-Output Safeguard for Human-AI Conversations
8b28792f8405b737229afb92c99c579b86d8aa98.research_question: How can large language models be leveraged to provide adaptable, high-performing input-output safeguards for human-AI conversational systems, capable of classifying and mitigating a broad range of safety risks in both user prompts and AI responses?
8b28792f8405b737229afb92c99c579b86d8aa98.hypothesis: Instruction-tuned large language models, when fine-tuned on a curated safety risk taxonomy and annotated dataset, can outperform or match existing content moderation tools in classifying safety risks in both user prompts and AI responses, and can be flexibly adapted to new taxonomies and guidelines through zero-shot or few-shot prompting and further fine-tuning.
8b28792f8405b737229afb92c99c579b86d8aa98.proposed_method: A novel safeguard model will be developed by instruction-tuning a Llama2-7b large language model on a high-quality, human-annotated dataset labeled according to a comprehensive safety risk taxonomy. The method will treat input-output safeguarding as an instruction-following task, where the model receives explicit guidelines and taxonomy categories as part of its input, and is trained to classify content as 'safe' or 'unsafe', with detailed category-level outputs for violations. The model will support both prompt (user input) and response (AI output) classification, leveraging distinct instructions for each role, and will be designed to accommodate binary and multi-label classification tasks. Data augmentation techniques will be employed to ensure robustness to varying taxonomy subsets and to prevent format memorization, and the model will be evaluated for its ability to adapt to new taxonomies through zero-shot and few-shot prompting, as well as additional fine-tuning.
8b28792f8405b737229afb92c99c579b86d8aa98.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both in-domain and public benchmark datasets. The primary training and evaluation dataset consists of 13,997 prompt-response pairs, annotated by expert red-teamers for six safety risk categories (Violence & Hate, Sexual Content, Criminal Planning, Guns & Illegal Weapons, Regulated or Controlled Substances, Suicide & Self-Harm) and a 'safe' class. The model's performance will be compared against established baselines, including OpenAI Moderation API, Perspective API, Azure AI Content Safety API, and GPT-4, using area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) as the main evaluation metric. Additional evaluations will be performed on the ToxicChat and OpenAI Moderation Evaluation datasets, with taxonomy adaptation achieved via zero-shot and few-shot prompting. Fine-tuning experiments will assess adaptability to new taxonomies using varying proportions of external dataset splits, and per-category as well as overall classification metrics will be reported.
8b28792f8405b737229afb92c99c579b86d8aa98.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first LLM-based safeguard model specifically instruction-tuned for both prompt and response classification in human-AI conversations, using a flexible safety risk taxonomy. The model uniquely supports dynamic adaptation to new taxonomies and guidelines via zero-shot and few-shot prompting, as well as further fine-tuning, enabling rapid deployment in diverse use cases. The method demonstrates state-of-the-art or superior performance to existing moderation tools on multiple benchmarks, and the public release of model weights facilitates further research and customization for evolving AI safety needs.

8b32aa33601514976d88fabcb060a5cd38d34006.title: Multitask Prompt Tuning Enables Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning
8b32aa33601514976d88fabcb060a5cd38d34006.research_question: How can parameter-efficient transfer learning be achieved for large pretrained language models across multiple diverse downstream tasks, leveraging cross-task knowledge in a multitask learning setting?
8b32aa33601514976d88fabcb060a5cd38d34006.hypothesis: A single transferable prompt, learned by decomposing and distilling knowledge from multiple source tasks, can enable more effective and parameter-efficient adaptation to a wide range of target tasks than existing prompt tuning or prompt transfer methods.
8b32aa33601514976d88fabcb060a5cd38d34006.proposed_method: A novel multitask prompt tuning (MPT) framework is developed, consisting of two main stages: source training and target adaptation. In the source training stage, prompt matrices for multiple source tasks are decomposed into a shared prompt matrix and low-rank, task-specific matrices. This decomposition is learned through knowledge distillation, where student prompts are trained to match the output distributions and hidden states of teacher prompts obtained via conventional prompt tuning. The shared prompt matrix captures generalizable cross-task knowledge, while task-specific vectors encode task-dependent information in a low-rank subspace. For target adaptation, the shared prompt is transferred to new tasks and adapted via low-rank multiplicative updates, optimizing both the shared and task-specific components with separate learning rates. The total number of tunable parameters per task is minimized by this decomposition, and the method supports both single-task and multitask adaptation on the target side.
8b32aa33601514976d88fabcb060a5cd38d34006.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on 23 NLP datasets spanning classification, natural language inference, question answering, and natural language generation tasks. Six large datasets (e.g., MNLI, QNLI, QQP, SST-2, SQuAD, ReCoRD) are used as source tasks, while the target tasks are drawn from benchmarks such as GLUE, SuperGLUE, MRQA, and others. The main model backbone is T5-Base (220M parameters), with ablations on T5-Small and T5-Large. Baselines include full finetuning, Adapters, BitFit, vanilla prompt tuning, SPoT, ATTEMPT, HyperFormer, and HyperDecoder. Evaluation metrics include accuracy, F1, Pearson correlation, BLEU, NIST, METEOR, Rouge-L, and CIDEr, depending on the task. Both full-dataset and few-shot (4, 16, 32 shots) settings are evaluated, with results averaged over multiple random seeds. Implementation details include prompt length, stochastic task sampling, and hyperparameter settings for distillation losses.
8b32aa33601514976d88fabcb060a5cd38d34006.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new framework for multitask prompt tuning that learns a single, transferable prompt via prompt decomposition and knowledge distillation from multiple source tasks. Unlike previous prompt transfer methods that aggregate or retrieve prompts, this method explicitly decomposes prompts into shared and task-specific components, enabling more effective cross-task knowledge sharing and parameter efficiency. The approach demonstrates superior performance and parameter efficiency compared to state-of-the-art baselines, sometimes even surpassing full finetuning while tuning less than 0.04% of the parameters per task. The method is also shown to generalize well to few-shot learning and to transfer from NLU to NLG tasks.

8b3a67c7e5289eed160d2acfd04d71cfb552c67d.title: Branch-Train-Merge: Embarrassingly Parallel Training of Expert Language Models
8b3a67c7e5289eed160d2acfd04d71cfb552c67d.research_question: How can large language models be trained in a highly parallel, communication-efficient manner by leveraging domain specialization, while maintaining or improving performance compared to traditional monolithic or mixture-of-experts models?
8b3a67c7e5289eed160d2acfd04d71cfb552c67d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that independently training domain-specialized expert language models on disjoint data subsets, followed by strategic merging and ensembling, can achieve superior in-domain and out-of-domain performance with greater training efficiency and scalability compared to standard fully-synchronized or partially-synchronized large language model training approaches.
8b3a67c7e5289eed160d2acfd04d71cfb552c67d.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces the Branch-Train-Merge (BTM) algorithm for embarrassingly parallel training of large language models. The process begins with a seed phase, where a single language model is trained on a heterogeneous corpus to establish shared representations. Subsequently, multiple expert language models (ELMs) are created by branching: each new ELM is initialized using a weighted parameter average of relevant existing ELMs, determined by domain posterior probabilities. Each ELM is then independently trained on data from a specific domain using standard cross-entropy loss, with no parameter synchronization between ELMs. After training, the new ELMs are merged into the ELMFOREST, a set of all domain-specialized experts. This process can be repeated incrementally to add new domains, and inference can be performed via ensembling ELM outputs or by parameter averaging to collapse the ensemble into a single model for efficiency.
8b3a67c7e5289eed160d2acfd04d71cfb552c67d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a benchmark dataset consisting of 8 training and 8 evaluation domains, covering a diverse range of textual sources (e.g., web text, legal documents, scientific papers). The proposed BTM-trained ELMFOREST models will be compared against compute-matched baselines: a standard Transformer language model (TRANSFORMER-LM) and a domain-specialized mixture-of-experts baseline (DEMIX). Model sizes will range from 125M to 1.3B parameters per expert, with training budgets matched by number of updates and GPU hours. Evaluation metrics will include average test-set perplexity on both training and evaluation domains, as well as training efficiency measured by updates per second and total GPU hours. Additional analyses will assess the impact of domain specialization versus random data splits, the robustness to initialization schemes, and the scalability of the approach to up to 64 domains and 22.4B total parameters.
8b3a67c7e5289eed160d2acfd04d71cfb552c67d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach enables embarrassingly parallel training of large language models by fully decoupling the training of domain-specialized experts, eliminating the need for multi-node synchronization and substantially reducing communication overhead. The method supports dynamic addition and removal of experts, explicit domain forgetting, and flexible inference via ensembling or parameter averaging. The approach demonstrates that domain specialization, rather than mere ensembling or increased parameter count, is critical for improved generalization. The methodology scales efficiently to many domains and large parameter counts, achieving comparable or superior performance to monolithic models trained with significantly more compute. This framework lays the groundwork for democratized, modular, and community-driven development of large language models.

8b56eec0ffdd4ead040e3af7a5fef2069a57dbdd.title: Contrastive Masked Autoencoders are Stronger Vision Learners
8b56eec0ffdd4ead040e3af7a5fef2069a57dbdd.research_question: Can self-supervised vision models be enhanced by unifying masked image modeling and contrastive learning in a single framework to produce more discriminative and transferable visual representations?
8b56eec0ffdd4ead040e3af7a5fef2069a57dbdd.hypothesis: Integrating contrastive learning with masked image modeling in a unified architecture will yield vision representations that are both locally perceptive and highly discriminative, leading to improved performance on a range of vision tasks compared to using either approach alone.
8b56eec0ffdd4ead040e3af7a5fef2069a57dbdd.proposed_method: A novel self-supervised pre-training framework, Contrastive Masked Autoencoders (CMAE), will be developed to unify masked image modeling (MIM) and contrastive learning (CL). The architecture consists of two branches: an online branch with an asymmetric encoder-decoder structure that reconstructs masked images, and a momentum branch with an encoder updated via exponential moving average, which receives full, pixel-shifted images. The online encoder processes randomly masked image patches to learn holistic features, while the momentum encoder processes the full image to provide contrastive supervision. To harmonize MIM and CL, two key innovations are introduced: (1) a pixel shifting augmentation that generates plausible positive views for contrastive learning, and (2) an auxiliary feature decoder in the online branch that reconstructs masked features for contrastive alignment. The contrastive loss is computed between the feature decoder output and the momentum encoder output, using InfoNCE loss with a projection-prediction head structure. The overall loss combines reconstruction and contrastive objectives.
8b56eec0ffdd4ead040e3af7a5fef2069a57dbdd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard vision benchmarks, including ImageNet-1K for image classification, ADE20K for semantic segmentation, and COCO for object detection and segmentation. The ViT-Base and hybrid convolutional ViT architectures will be used as backbones, with pre-training schedules ranging from 300 to 1600 epochs. Baselines will include state-of-the-art MIM methods (e.g., MAE, SimMIM, CAE, iBOT, ConvMAE) and contrastive learning methods (e.g., MoCo-v3, DINO). Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy for classification, mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) for segmentation, and AP metrics for detection/segmentation. Ablation studies will assess the impact of pixel shifting, feature decoder depth, contrastive loss weighting, and masking ratios. Transfer learning will be evaluated on additional datasets such as iNaturalist and Places365. Partial fine-tuning and linear probing protocols will be used to assess representation quality.
8b56eec0ffdd4ead040e3af7a5fef2069a57dbdd.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified framework that effectively combines masked image modeling and contrastive learning, overcoming their incompatibilities through novel pixel shifting augmentation and a dedicated feature decoder. This design enables the learning of representations that are both context-sensitive and highly discriminative, leading to state-of-the-art performance on multiple vision benchmarks. The method demonstrates superior transferability, faster convergence, and improved scalability compared to prior approaches. The framework is modular and can be applied to various backbone architectures with minimal modification.

8b5b37d3703fa0784b7a716e021a0618dd53832c.title: Quamba: A Post-Training Quantization Recipe for Selective State Space Models
8b5b37d3703fa0784b7a716e021a0618dd53832c.research_question: How can post-training quantization be effectively applied to selective State Space Models (SSMs) to enable efficient deployment on both cloud and edge hardware, while minimizing accuracy degradation and maintaining computational advantages over Transformers?
8b5b37d3703fa0784b7a716e021a0618dd53832c.hypothesis: A tailored post-training quantization method that addresses the unique activation sensitivity and outlier characteristics of selective SSMs will enable 8-bit quantization with minimal accuracy loss, improved latency, and efficient hardware utilization across a range of deployment scenarios.
8b5b37d3703fa0784b7a716e021a0618dd53832c.proposed_method: A static 8-bit per-tensor quantization framework will be developed specifically for selective SSMs, such as the Mamba architecture. The method will suppress maximum values in the input activations to the selective scan module using percentile-based clipping (e.g., 99.999th percentile), thereby enhancing quantization precision for the most sensitive input tensors. For output activations, which exhibit significant outliers, the method will apply a Walsh–Hadamard transform to project outputs into an outlier-free space before quantization. The inverse Hadamard transform will be fused into the output projection layer to avoid additional computational overhead. All projection and convolutional layers will be quantized to 8-bit integers, with static scaling factors calibrated on a representative dataset, and quantization will be integrated into CUDA kernels for efficient execution.
8b5b37d3703fa0784b7a716e021a0618dd53832c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on open-source SSMs (Mamba family) and the large-scale Jamba hybrid model. Evaluation will include zero-shot tasks using LM-EVAL, covering datasets such as LAMBADA, HellaSwag, PIQA, ARC, and WinoGrande, with both accuracy and average accuracy reported. Perplexity will be measured on WikiText2 and a subset of the Pile dataset. Baselines will include static quantization, dynamic quantization, Mamba-PTQ, and state-of-the-art Transformer quantization methods (SmoothQuant, QuaRot). Hardware platforms will include Nvidia A5000 GPU (cloud) and Orin Nano 8G (edge), with latency (time-to-last-token, time-per-output-token), memory usage, and model size profiled. Calibration for quantization will use 512 sentences from the Pile dataset. Ablation studies will assess the impact of percentile clipping and Hadamard transform components.
8b5b37d3703fa0784b7a716e021a0618dd53832c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a quantization recipe specifically tailored for selective SSMs, addressing their unique activation sensitivity and outlier patterns not present in Transformer architectures. The method combines percentile-based input clipping and Hadamard transform-based output quantization, enabling efficient 8-bit weight-activation quantization with minimal accuracy loss. This approach is demonstrated to be effective and scalable for both moderate and large-scale SSM-based language models, achieving Pareto-optimal trade-offs between accuracy and latency, and enabling practical deployment on both cloud and edge hardware.

8b5f4902411123c5e68ded502f296cf325864831.title: GS-SLAM: Dense Visual SLAM with 3D Gaussian Splatting
8b5f4902411123c5e68ded502f296cf325864831.research_question: How can dense visual SLAM systems achieve a better balance between efficiency and accuracy in real-time scene reconstruction and camera tracking for RGB-D data, particularly by leveraging novel scene representations?
8b5f4902411123c5e68ded502f296cf325864831.hypothesis: Employing a 3D Gaussian scene representation with a differentiable splatting rendering pipeline will enable dense visual SLAM systems to achieve real-time performance and high-quality mapping and tracking, outperforming existing neural implicit and explicit SLAM methods in both speed and reconstruction fidelity.
8b5f4902411123c5e68ded502f296cf325864831.proposed_method: A dense RGB-D SLAM system is developed based on 3D Gaussian scene representation coupled with a real-time differentiable splatting rendering pipeline. The method models the scene as a set of 3D Gaussians, each parameterized by position, covariance, opacity, and spherical harmonics for color. An adaptive expansion strategy is introduced to dynamically add new or delete noisy 3D Gaussians, enabling efficient reconstruction of new scene geometry and refinement of previously observed areas. Camera pose tracking is optimized using a coarse-to-fine approach: initial pose estimation is performed with low-resolution rendering, followed by refinement using high-resolution rendering with selected reliable 3D Gaussians. The system jointly optimizes scene representation and camera poses via photometric and geometric losses computed on rendered RGB-D images, utilizing analytical gradients for efficient backpropagation.
8b5f4902411123c5e68ded502f296cf325864831.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on standard indoor RGB-D benchmarks, including the Replica and TUM-RGBD datasets. The method is compared against state-of-the-art neural SLAM baselines such as NICE-SLAM, Vox-Fusion, CoSLAM, ESLAM, and Point-SLAM. Evaluation metrics include Absolute Trajectory Error (ATE) for localization, Depth L1 error, Precision, Recall, and F1-score for mesh reconstruction, and PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS for rendering quality. System runtime (FPS) and memory usage are also measured. All methods are run multiple times to report average results, and ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of the adaptive expansion strategy and the coarse-to-fine tracking approach.
8b5f4902411123c5e68ded502f296cf325864831.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first dense RGB-D SLAM system leveraging 3D Gaussian splatting for scene representation and mapping. The adaptive 3D Gaussian expansion strategy enables efficient and accurate reconstruction of dynamic and previously unseen areas. The coarse-to-fine pose tracking mechanism improves both speed and robustness by focusing optimization on reliable scene regions. The proposed system achieves a significant speedup in rendering (up to 100× faster than prior methods) and delivers state-of-the-art results in tracking, mapping, and rendering quality, while eliminating the need for neural network decoders in the mapping pipeline.

8b729b1e18a1c243cf51530039cb5487b7bc4185.title: How much is a noisy image worth? Data Scaling Laws for Ambient Diffusion
8b729b1e18a1c243cf51530039cb5487b7bc4185.research_question: How does the mixture of clean and noisy data affect the performance of generative diffusion models, and what are the data scaling laws governing the utility of noisy versus clean samples for training such models?
8b729b1e18a1c243cf51530039cb5487b7bc4185.hypothesis: A small fraction of clean data combined with a large fraction of noisy data can achieve generative model performance comparable to training on an equivalent amount of clean data alone, while training solely on noisy data requires exponentially more samples to match the performance of clean data.
8b729b1e18a1c243cf51530039cb5487b7bc4185.proposed_method: A novel training algorithm is developed that leverages both clean and noisy samples for diffusion model training. For time steps corresponding to low noise, only clean samples are used with the standard denoising score matching objective. For higher noise levels, both clean and noisy samples are utilized: clean samples are processed as usual, while noisy samples are trained using an ambient denoising score matching loss derived from a theoretical lemma relating conditional expectations at different noise levels. The method is implemented as a unified training loop where each batch contains a mix of clean and noisy samples, and the appropriate loss is computed for each sample based on its noise level. The approach is extensible to arbitrary per-sample noise levels, but is presented and evaluated primarily in the two-noise-level setting (clean and fixed-noise).
8b729b1e18a1c243cf51530039cb5487b7bc4185.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted by training over 80 diffusion models on three datasets of varying size and complexity: CIFAR-10 (60K samples), CelebA-HQ (30K samples), and ImageNet (~1.3M samples). Models are trained under different ratios of clean to noisy data (e.g., 10% clean + 90% noisy) and at multiple Gaussian noise levels (σ = 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, and higher). Baselines include models trained on only clean data, only noisy data, and only a small subset of clean data. Evaluation is performed using the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) metric to assess generative quality. Additional ablations explore the effects of training duration, sampling noise scheduling, consistency loss, and regularization. The impact of decreasing the clean data fraction to as low as 1% is also tested, and the method's performance is compared against theoretical sample complexity predictions.
8b729b1e18a1c243cf51530039cb5487b7bc4185.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a systematic study of data scaling laws for generative diffusion models trained on mixtures of clean and noisy data, supported by both extensive empirical experiments and new theoretical sample complexity bounds for Gaussian mixtures with heterogeneous variances. It demonstrates that a small fraction of clean data, when combined with a large amount of noisy data, suffices to achieve near state-of-the-art performance, outperforming models trained on either clean or noisy data alone. Theoretical results quantify the exponentially diminishing utility of noisy samples compared to clean ones, and provide practical guidance for data curation and pricing. The training algorithm is efficient, avoids the computational overhead of consistency loss for most of training, and is validated across multiple large-scale datasets.

8b79b3615eb2f2ee8ce6e988313398b8f42305f4.title: DiffStitch: Boosting Offline Reinforcement Learning with Diffusion-based Trajectory Stitching
8b79b3615eb2f2ee8ce6e988313398b8f42305f4.research_question: How can the performance of offline reinforcement learning algorithms be improved when the available offline datasets contain limited or suboptimal trajectories, particularly by enabling agents to effectively transition from low-reward to high-reward regions?
8b79b3615eb2f2ee8ce6e988313398b8f42305f4.hypothesis: Augmenting offline RL datasets by generating synthetic trajectories that stitch together low-reward and high-reward trajectories will enable agents to learn policies that more effectively reach high-reward regions, thereby improving overall performance across various offline RL algorithms.
8b79b3615eb2f2ee8ce6e988313398b8f42305f4.proposed_method: A novel data augmentation pipeline, DiffStitch, will be developed to generate synthetic stitching trajectories between low-reward and high-reward trajectories in offline RL datasets. The method involves four core modules: (1) a step estimation module that predicts the number of steps required to connect two given states from different trajectories, (2) a state stitching module that uses a diffusion-based generative model to synthesize the intermediate states along the stitching path, (3) a trajectory wrap-up module that predicts the corresponding actions and rewards for the generated states using inverse dynamics and reward models, and (4) a qualification module that evaluates the consistency of the generated trajectory with the environment dynamics, filtering out low-quality samples. The diffusion model is trained to generate plausible state transitions, while the other modules ensure that the augmented trajectories are both realistic and beneficial for policy learning.
8b79b3615eb2f2ee8ce6e988313398b8f42305f4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the D4RL benchmark, covering a range of domains including MuJoCo locomotion tasks (HalfCheetah, Hopper, Walker2d) and Adroit-pen manipulation tasks, with datasets of varying quality (Medium-Expert, Medium, Medium-Replay, Human, Cloned). The proposed augmentation method will be evaluated by training three representative offline RL algorithms: IQL (one-step method), TD3+BC (imitation learning), and Decision Transformer (trajectory optimization). Baseline comparisons will include recent data augmentation methods such as SER and TATU. Evaluation metrics will be normalized average return, with results averaged over multiple random seeds. Ablation studies will assess the impact of each module in the pipeline, and parameter studies will explore the effects of data ratio and qualification threshold. Additional experiments will test the method's effectiveness on small-sample regimes.
8b79b3615eb2f2ee8ce6e988313398b8f42305f4.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to systematically generate sub-trajectories that stitch together arbitrary pairs of trajectories in offline RL datasets, enabling the creation of globally optimal trajectories that facilitate transitions from low-reward to high-reward regions. Unlike prior augmentation methods that generate only short or unconditioned transitions, this method produces long, goal-directed synthetic trajectories that align with environment dynamics. The approach is broadly applicable across different types of offline RL algorithms, including one-step, imitation learning, and trajectory optimization methods, and demonstrates superior performance in challenging scenarios with sparse high-reward data.

8b7c4a86b3e1d50867b4b90ce176fa46624e9df5.title: Generalization through variance: how noise shapes inductive biases in diffusion models
8b7c4a86b3e1d50867b4b90ce176fa46624e9df5.research_question: How do diffusion models generalize beyond their training set, and what factors determine the nature and extent of this generalization, particularly in relation to the variance introduced by the denoising score matching (DSM) objective and the structure of the training data, model architecture, and training process?
8b7c4a86b3e1d50867b4b90ce176fa46624e9df5.hypothesis: Generalization in diffusion models is strongly influenced by the variance of the noisy target (proxy score) in the DSM objective, and this variance, together with factors such as the forward process, model capacity, feature-related inductive biases, and training set structure, induces specific inductive biases—most notably, a gap-filling effect in the learned distribution that goes beyond simple memorization of the training data.
8b7c4a86b3e1d50867b4b90ce176fa46624e9df5.proposed_method: A mathematical and theoretical framework will be developed to analyze how diffusion models generalize, focusing on the role of the variance in the DSM objective. The approach will leverage a physics-inspired path integral (Martin-Siggia-Rose) formulation to analytically characterize the typical distributions learned by various classes of diffusion models, including linear models and infinite-width neural networks in the neural tangent kernel (NTK) regime. The methodology will involve deriving effective stochastic differential equations (SDEs) that describe the average learned distribution, with explicit computation of the covariance (V-kernel) of the proxy score as a function of model architecture, feature set, and training data structure. The analysis will be extended to study how feature-related inductive biases interact with the variance-induced bias, and how these factors modulate generalization in both under- and over-parameterized regimes.
8b7c4a86b3e1d50867b4b90ce176fa46624e9df5.experiment_details: Experiments will include both theoretical analysis and empirical simulations. Analytical results will be derived for simple data distributions (e.g., discrete point clouds in low dimensions), with models ranging from naive score estimators to expressive linear models and infinite-width neural networks. Empirical simulations will visualize the learned distributions and the effect of varying key parameters such as the time cutoff, ratio of features to training samples (F/P), and feature set (e.g., Gaussian vs. Fourier features). Evaluation will focus on qualitative and quantitative measures of generalization, such as the extent of interpolation (gap-filling), extrapolation, and feature blending, as well as the impact of model and data factors on the V-kernel and the resulting sample distributions. Comparisons will be made to deterministic PF-ODE dynamics and to models trained with alternative objectives or architectures.
8b7c4a86b3e1d50867b4b90ce176fa46624e9df5.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel theoretical framework for understanding generalization in diffusion models, based on a path-integral approach that explicitly accounts for the variance of the DSM objective's proxy score. It provides analytic characterizations of the typical learned distribution for several model classes and identifies the covariance structure of the proxy score as a key driver of inductive bias. The work elucidates how generalization arises even in the absence of explicit model-related biases and how feature-related and variance-induced biases interact. This approach offers new insights into the mechanisms of gap-filling and boundary-smearing in diffusion models, and establishes connections between generalization, model capacity, and data structure that are not captured by existing theories.

8b7cce220c3b19f9b2d4a6c531907ed3b592b55e.title: Latent Consistency Models: Synthesizing High-Resolution Images with Few-Step Inference
8b7cce220c3b19f9b2d4a6c531907ed3b592b55e.research_question: How can high-resolution images be synthesized efficiently with minimal inference steps, leveraging pre-trained latent diffusion models, while maintaining or improving image quality and sample diversity?
8b7cce220c3b19f9b2d4a6c531907ed3b592b55e.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by introducing a latent consistency model framework, which directly predicts the solution of an augmented probability flow ODE in the latent space of pre-trained diffusion models, it is possible to achieve high-fidelity, high-resolution image synthesis in very few inference steps without sacrificing sample quality or diversity. Furthermore, incorporating a novel fine-tuning approach will enable efficient adaptation to customized datasets while preserving fast inference.
8b7cce220c3b19f9b2d4a6c531907ed3b592b55e.proposed_method: A new framework, Latent Consistency Models (LCMs), will be developed to enable rapid, high-resolution image synthesis using few-step or even one-step inference on any pre-trained latent diffusion model (LDM), such as Stable Diffusion. The method operates in the latent space of a pre-trained autoencoder, where a consistency function is trained to map noisy latent representations directly to clean ones by solving an augmented probability flow ODE (PF-ODE). A one-stage guided distillation process will be used, integrating classifier-free guidance (CFG) directly into the consistency model, allowing the model to learn conditional generation with various guidance scales. To accelerate training and convergence, a SKIPPING-STEP technique will be employed, which shortens the diffusion time schedule by enforcing consistency across non-adjacent time steps. Additionally, a Latent Consistency Fine-tuning (LCF) procedure will be introduced, enabling efficient adaptation of pre-trained LCMs to new, customized datasets without requiring retraining of the teacher diffusion model.
8b7cce220c3b19f9b2d4a6c531907ed3b592b55e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two subsets of the LAION-5B dataset: LAION-Aesthetics-6+ (12M image-text pairs, 512x512 resolution) and LAION-Aesthetics-6.5+ (650K pairs, 768x768 resolution). The proposed LCMs will be distilled from pre-trained Stable Diffusion models and compared against baselines including DDIM, DPM, DPM++, and Guided-Distill. Evaluation will focus on text-to-image generation, using FID (Fréchet Inception Distance) and CLIP score as primary metrics to assess image quality and semantic alignment. The experimental setup includes training LCMs with 100K iterations, batch sizes of 72 (512x512) and 16 (768x768), learning rate 8e-6, and using DDIM as the ODE solver with a skipping step of k=20. For fine-tuning experiments, customized datasets such as Pokemon and Simpsons will be used, with 30K fine-tuning iterations. Ablation studies will explore the effects of different ODE solvers, skipping-step schedules, and guidance scales.
8b7cce220c3b19f9b2d4a6c531907ed3b592b55e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces Latent Consistency Models as the first framework to enable few-step or even one-step high-resolution image synthesis in the latent space of pre-trained diffusion models, significantly reducing inference time and computational cost. The method integrates classifier-free guidance directly into the consistency distillation process in a single stage, unlike prior two-stage approaches, and introduces the SKIPPING-STEP technique to accelerate convergence. Additionally, the Latent Consistency Fine-tuning method allows efficient adaptation to new datasets without retraining the teacher model. These innovations collectively enable state-of-the-art text-to-image generation performance with minimal inference steps and practical computational requirements.

8b8847c1e32ba1c4ca7ef2122a1dec221e22fc67.title: DeepGate3: Towards Scalable Circuit Representation Learning
8b8847c1e32ba1c4ca7ef2122a1dec221e22fc67.research_question: How can circuit representation learning models be scaled to effectively leverage large amounts of training data while improving model performance and generalization capabilities across diverse and complex circuit designs?
8b8847c1e32ba1c4ca7ef2122a1dec221e22fc67.hypothesis: Integrating Transformer-based modules with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and introducing novel pooling and supervision mechanisms will enhance the scalability, generalization, and representational power of circuit representation learning models, outperforming traditional GNN-based approaches on large and complex circuit datasets.
8b8847c1e32ba1c4ca7ef2122a1dec221e22fc67.proposed_method: A new framework is proposed that builds upon a pre-trained GNN-based circuit tokenizer to generate initial gate-level embeddings, which are then refined using independent Transformer modules (RefineTransformers) for both structural and functional information. To aggregate subcircuit and circuit-level information, a novel PoolingTransformer mechanism is introduced, utilizing a special [CLS] token and learnable positional embeddings to capture both global and local circuit features. The model is pre-trained using a comprehensive suite of multi-level supervision tasks, including gate-level logic probability prediction, truth table similarity, structural property prediction, and graph-level functional and structural similarity, all derived from logic simulation and circuit analysis rather than artificial annotation. For large circuits, a window-shifting strategy is adopted to partition the circuit into manageable sub-areas, allowing the Transformer modules to efficiently process circuits exceeding standard sequence length limitations.
8b8847c1e32ba1c4ca7ef2122a1dec221e22fc67.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a large-scale dataset of 67,905 circuits collected from ITC99, IWLS05, EPFL, OpenCore, and Github, all converted to And-Inverter Graph (AIG) format. The model will be pre-trained on these circuits and evaluated on both small and large circuits, including industrial logic equivalence checking (LEC) SAT problems with over 10,000 gates. Baselines will include previous GNN-based models such as DeepGate2, as well as pooling strategies like average pooling and ablation variants without the proposed Transformer modules. Evaluation metrics will include overall loss, truth table prediction error (Hamming distance), gate connection prediction accuracy, gate-in-graph prediction accuracy, and runtime reduction for SAT solving. Ablation studies will assess the contribution of each architectural component, and scalability will be measured by varying the size of the training data subsets.
8b8847c1e32ba1c4ca7ef2122a1dec221e22fc67.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a hybrid GNN-Transformer architecture for circuit representation learning, featuring a novel PoolingTransformer for subcircuit and circuit-level aggregation and a suite of multi-level, simulation-derived supervision tasks. The method addresses the scalability limitations of GNNs by enabling effective learning from large datasets and capturing long-range dependencies in circuit graphs. The approach demonstrates superior scalability, generalization, and performance on both synthetic and real-world EDA tasks, including significant improvements in SAT solving efficiency for large-scale circuits.

8b9944729ae08cb7aa5fb023651b2430fff6cd99.title: RePaViT: Scalable Vision Transformer Acceleration via Structural Reparameterization on Feedforward Network Layers
8b9944729ae08cb7aa5fb023651b2430fff6cd99.research_question: How can the efficiency and inference speed of large-scale Vision Transformers (ViTs) be improved without sacrificing, and potentially even improving, model accuracy, particularly by addressing the computational bottlenecks in their intrinsic architecture?
8b9944729ae08cb7aa5fb023651b2430fff6cd99.hypothesis: Applying structural reparameterization directly to the feedforward network (FFN) layers of ViTs, by introducing a channel idle mechanism, will significantly reduce inference latency and computational complexity while maintaining or improving model accuracy, especially as model size increases.
8b9944729ae08cb7aa5fb023651b2430fff6cd99.proposed_method: A novel channel idle mechanism will be introduced for FFN layers within ViTs, where only a subset of feature channels undergo nonlinear activation, while the remaining channels bypass the activation, forming a linear pathway. During training, LayerNorm will be replaced with BatchNorm, and an additional BatchNorm will be added before the second linear projection. These BatchNorm layers will be reparameterized into their adjacent linear projection weights post-training. At inference, the FFN layers will be structurally reparameterized into a condensed form with three smaller linear transformations, merging normalization and shortcut connections into the projection weights. This approach will be implemented across various ViT backbones, resulting in a family of ReParameterizable Vision Transformers (RePaViTs) that are optimized for efficient inference.
8b9944729ae08cb7aa5fb023651b2430fff6cd99.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ImageNet-1k dataset for image classification, following standard data augmentations and training recipes. Four representative ViT backbones will be used: DeiT, Swin Transformer, LV-ViT, and ViT-Large, with FFN layers modified to include the channel idle mechanism. Models will be trained from scratch and evaluated pre- and post-reparameterization. Throughput and latency will be measured on NVIDIA A6000 GPUs with a fixed batch size, and FlashAttention will be used for self-attention computations. Baselines will include vanilla ViTs, state-of-the-art network pruning methods (e.g., WDPruning, X-Pruner, DC-ViT, LPViT), and recent reparameterization methods such as SLAB. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy, number of parameters, computational complexity (GMACs), and inference speed (images/second). Additional experiments will cover dense prediction tasks (object detection and segmentation on MS COCO and ADE20K) and self-supervised learning settings (e.g., DINO, CLIP).
8b9944729ae08cb7aa5fb023651b2430fff6cd99.novelty_claims: This proposal is the first to apply structural reparameterization directly to the intrinsic FFN layers of ViTs, rather than to added convolutional components or hybrid architectures. The channel idle mechanism enables post-training reparameterization, resulting in significant reductions in inference latency and parameter count, with accuracy maintained or improved, especially for large-scale models. The approach yields denser, structurally regular models that are efficient on general-purpose hardware, and demonstrates superior scalability and speed-accuracy trade-offs compared to state-of-the-art pruning and reparameterization methods.

8b9b45fc8475bd58c130c5affb8da8565bc24136.title: How many samples are needed to train a deep neural network?
8b9b45fc8475bd58c130c5affb8da8565bc24136.research_question: How does the generalization error of deep neural networks, particularly ReLU feed-forward architectures, scale with the number of training samples, and what is the minimum sample complexity required to achieve a desired prediction error in both regression and classification tasks?
8b9b45fc8475bd58c130c5affb8da8565bc24136.hypothesis: The generalization error of ReLU feed-forward neural networks decreases at a rate proportional to 1/sqrt(n) with the number of training samples n, rather than the parametric rate of 1/n; consequently, the minimum number of samples required to achieve a given error level is substantially higher than for classical linear models.
8b9b45fc8475bd58c130c5affb8da8565bc24136.proposed_method: A rigorous theoretical framework will be developed to establish mini-max lower bounds on the generalization error for deep ReLU feed-forward neural networks under sparse parameter constraints. The approach will utilize information-theoretic tools, specifically Fano’s inequality, to relate the packing number of the function class to achievable risk, and will derive a sharp lower bound for the packing number of deep ReLU network spaces. The analysis will focus on regression models with Gaussian inputs and outputs, but the results will be empirically validated for both regression and classification tasks. Theoretical results will be complemented by empirical studies fitting the generalization error curves to both 1/n and 1/sqrt(n) rates across various architectures and datasets.
8b9b45fc8475bd58c130c5affb8da8565bc24136.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard benchmark datasets, including MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR10 for classification, and the California Housing Prices dataset for regression. Both shallow and deep ReLU feed-forward networks, as well as ReLU-based CNNs, will be evaluated. The number of training samples will be varied systematically, and the generalization error will be measured on held-out test sets using cross-entropy loss for classification and mean-squared error for regression. The empirical generalization error will be fitted to both 1/n and 1/sqrt(n) curves using nonlinear optimization (SLSQP), and the fit quality will be assessed using R-squared and MSE metrics. Comparative analysis will be performed to determine which scaling law best describes the observed error decay.
8b9b45fc8475bd58c130c5affb8da8565bc24136.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first mini-max lower bound for the risk of deep ReLU feed-forward networks that matches recent upper bounds and depends only logarithmically on input dimension and polynomially on sparsity, rather than on the total number of parameters. The work establishes, both theoretically and empirically, that the generalization error of deep ReLU networks cannot in general improve beyond the 1/sqrt(n) rate without additional assumptions, in contrast to classical methods. Additionally, a novel lower bound for the packing number of deep ReLU network spaces is derived, providing new insights into the complexity of these models. The empirical validation extends beyond feed-forward networks to include CNNs and multiple real-world datasets, offering strong practical relevance.

8ba5d42e303b429ad3f160e2eb035635a0b18dbe.title: WildChat: 1M ChatGPT Interaction Logs in the Wild
8ba5d42e303b429ad3f160e2eb035635a0b18dbe.research_question: How can a large-scale, real-world, multi-turn, and multilingual dataset of user-chatbot interactions be collected, anonymized, and utilized to advance research in conversational AI, user behavior analysis, and the study of toxicity and jailbreaking in chatbot systems?
8ba5d42e303b429ad3f160e2eb035635a0b18dbe.hypothesis: A large, diverse, and anonymized dataset of real-world user-chatbot interactions will provide richer linguistic, behavioral, and toxic content diversity than existing datasets, and will enable the development of more robust, instruction-following conversational agents as well as deeper analysis of user behavior and chatbot vulnerabilities.
8ba5d42e303b429ad3f160e2eb035635a0b18dbe.proposed_method: A publicly accessible chatbot service will be deployed, powered by both GPT-3.5-Turbo and GPT-4 APIs, to collect user-chatbot interaction logs from consenting users. The service will ensure anonymity by not requiring user accounts and will collect chat transcripts, hashed IP addresses, request headers, and coarse-grained demographic information. Data preprocessing will include linking turns into conversations, removing personally identifiable information using tools such as Microsoft Presidio and Spacy for multilingual NER, and mapping IP addresses to regions before hashing. The resulting dataset will be analyzed for linguistic diversity, prompt categories, and toxicity using multiple classifiers, and will be made available for research under an appropriate license.
8ba5d42e303b429ad3f160e2eb035635a0b18dbe.experiment_details: Experiments will include a comparative analysis of the new dataset against existing conversational datasets (such as Alpaca, OpenAssistant, Dolly, ShareGPT, and LMSYS-Chat-1M) in terms of size, language diversity, prompt length, and toxicity. Toxicity will be measured using both Detoxify and OpenAI Moderation APIs, with manual validation of flagged content. The dataset's utility for instruction-tuning will be evaluated by fine-tuning a Llama-2 7B model (WILDLLAMA) on the collected data and benchmarking its performance on MT-bench using LLM Judge, comparing against open-source and proprietary baselines. Additional analyses will include prompt embedding diversity (using t-SNE visualizations), coverage analysis via negative log-likelihood, and jailbreaking prompt frequency and success rates.
8ba5d42e303b429ad3f160e2eb035635a0b18dbe.novelty_claims: The proposed dataset will be the largest publicly available collection of real-world, multi-turn, multi-lingual user-chatbot interactions, enriched with demographic and behavioral metadata. It will offer greater linguistic and prompt diversity, longer interaction turns, and a richer set of toxic and jailbreaking use cases than existing datasets. The dataset will enable new research directions in conversational AI, toxicity detection, user modeling, and chatbot robustness, and will facilitate the development and benchmarking of instruction-following models using authentic user data.

8bb7cecd1bc3fa470aa882158e7553705b1a6141.title: Minigrid & Miniworld: Modular & Customizable Reinforcement Learning Environments for Goal-Oriented Tasks
8bb7cecd1bc3fa470aa882158e7553705b1a6141.research_question: How can modular and customizable 2D and 3D reinforcement learning environments be designed to facilitate research on goal-oriented tasks, including transfer learning and human-agent interaction, while maintaining simplicity, extensibility, and ease of use?
8bb7cecd1bc3fa470aa882158e7553705b1a6141.hypothesis: Providing a unified, minimal-dependency, and highly customizable suite of 2D and 3D environments will enable more effective development, evaluation, and transfer of reinforcement learning algorithms and facilitate human-agent studies.
8bb7cecd1bc3fa470aa882158e7553705b1a6141.proposed_method: A modular framework will be developed consisting of two libraries: one for 2D grid-based environments (Minigrid) and one for 3D room-based environments (Miniworld). Both libraries will implement partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) with configurable state, action, and observation spaces. The environments will be designed for easy extensibility, allowing users to rapidly generate new tasks and customize existing ones via a minimal set of Python functions and a unified API. Sparse reward structures will be used by default, with support for custom reward functions. The libraries will be compatible with standard reinforcement learning toolkits and will include wrappers for augmenting environment behavior, such as stochasticity and variable observation spaces. Tutorials and documentation will be provided to facilitate environment creation and integration.
8bb7cecd1bc3fa470aa882158e7553705b1a6141.experiment_details: Experiments will include case studies on transfer learning between Minigrid and Miniworld, both for RL agents and human participants. For RL agent transfer, similar navigation tasks will be created in both environments, and a PPO agent will be trained in Minigrid and its learned weights selectively transferred to Miniworld, with various combinations of network components (mission encoder, actor, critic) tested. Evaluation will use area under the reward curve (AUC) over 200k timesteps, comparing transfer-initialized and randomly initialized agents. For human studies, participants will perform navigation tasks in both environments, with transfer assessed by comparing performance after experience in Minigrid versus direct exposure to Miniworld. Standardized environments (e.g., FourRooms) and partial observability will be used, with actions mapped to randomized keyboard keys. Results will be analyzed using mean and standard deviation of rewards across episodes and subjects.
8bb7cecd1bc3fa470aa882158e7553705b1a6141.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a unified, minimal-dependency API for both 2D and 3D goal-oriented RL environments, enabling rapid prototyping and customization. The design prioritizes simplicity and extensibility, lowering the barrier for both algorithmic and environment research. The unified API facilitates seamless transfer learning experiments between different observation modalities and supports both agent and human studies. The libraries' modularity and ease of integration with existing RL toolkits represent a significant advance over prior simulation platforms, which are often less customizable, more complex, or harder to integrate.

8bce50a931f8df9128e4c6d76933ce6bf98b5f9a.title: Conformal Inductive Graph Neural Networks
8bce50a931f8df9128e4c6d76933ce6bf98b5f9a.research_question: How can conformal prediction methods be adapted to provide valid, distribution-free coverage guarantees for uncertainty quantification in inductive node classification tasks on dynamic graphs, particularly under node- and edge-exchangeable generative processes?
8bce50a931f8df9128e4c6d76933ce6bf98b5f9a.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, by conditioning conformal prediction calibration and evaluation on the evolving subgraph at each timestep and leveraging node- or edge-exchangeability, it is possible to recover valid coverage guarantees for inductive graph neural network (GNN) predictions, even in the presence of distribution shifts caused by graph updates.
8bce50a931f8df9128e4c6d76933ce6bf98b5f9a.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that extends conformal prediction to inductive node classification on dynamic graphs by recalibrating conformity scores conditional on the subgraph at each timestep. For node-exchangeable sequences, the method dynamically updates calibration and evaluation scores as new nodes are added, ensuring exchangeability is maintained. For edge-exchangeable sequences, a weighted conformal prediction approach is employed, where weights are set inversely proportional to node degrees, to account for sparsity and maintain valid coverage. The method supports flexible prediction timing, allowing prediction sets to be generated upon node or edge arrival or at arbitrary subsequent times, while preserving the statistical guarantee. The approach is model-agnostic and can be applied to any permutation-equivariant GNN, with the calibration procedure recomputed as the graph evolves.
8bce50a931f8df9128e4c6d76933ce6bf98b5f9a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of real-world graph datasets, including CoraML, CiteSeer, PubMed, Coauthor Physics, Coauthor CS, Amazon Photos, Amazon Computers, Flickr, and Reddit2. Four models will be evaluated: GCN, GAT, APPNP (all structure-aware), and MLP (structure-independent). The experimental protocol involves stratified sampling of nodes for training and calibration, with calibration set sizes matching training set sizes for node-exchangeable settings and matched edge samples for edge-exchangeable settings. Baselines include naive conformal prediction and, where applicable, the NAPS method. Evaluation metrics will focus on empirical coverage (distance from the target 1−α coverage), average prediction set size (efficiency), and singleton hit ratio, with results averaged over multiple random sequences per dataset. The main evaluation criterion is the absolute deviation from the nominal coverage guarantee, with additional analysis of efficiency and robustness to calibration set size.
8bce50a931f8df9128e4c6d76933ce6bf98b5f9a.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first conformal prediction framework for inductive node classification on dynamic graphs that achieves valid, distribution-free coverage guarantees under both node- and edge-exchangeable generative processes. Unlike prior methods, the approach addresses the implicit distribution shift in node embeddings caused by graph updates and provides coverage guarantees that hold regardless of prediction timing. The method is applicable to both dense and sparse graphs, does not require retraining or architectural changes to the underlying GNN, and improves both efficiency and singleton hit rates as a byproduct. Theoretical results are complemented by empirical validation across diverse datasets and models, demonstrating the method's broad applicability and reliability.

8bd6a2a89503be083176f2cc26fabedb79238cbd.title: InstructBLIP: Towards General-purpose Vision-Language Models with Instruction Tuning
8bd6a2a89503be083176f2cc26fabedb79238cbd.research_question: How can a general-purpose vision-language model be developed to robustly follow diverse natural language instructions and generalize to a wide range of unseen vision-language tasks?
8bd6a2a89503be083176f2cc26fabedb79238cbd.hypothesis: Instruction tuning with diverse, instruction-formatted datasets and instruction-aware visual feature extraction will significantly improve a vision-language model's zero-shot generalization and task-following ability compared to multitask learning or instruction-agnostic approaches.
8bd6a2a89503be083176f2cc26fabedb79238cbd.proposed_method: A vision-language instruction tuning framework will be constructed by initializing from a pretrained BLIP-2 model, which includes a frozen image encoder, a frozen large language model (LLM), and a Query Transformer (Q-Former) as a bridge. The Q-Former will be finetuned to extract visual features that are conditioned on both the input image and the specific instruction, making the visual representation task-aware. The instruction text will be provided as input to both the Q-Former and the LLM, enabling the Q-Former to produce instruction-aware visual features via self-attention mechanisms. A balanced data sampling strategy will be implemented to synchronize learning progress across diverse datasets, sampling according to the square root of dataset sizes with manual adjustments as needed. The model will be instruction-tuned using a language modeling loss to generate responses to natural language instructions.
8bd6a2a89503be083176f2cc26fabedb79238cbd.experiment_details: The experimental setup will utilize 26 publicly available vision-language datasets, covering 11 task categories such as image captioning, visual reasoning, image question answering, video question answering, and visual conversation. Thirteen datasets will be used for instruction tuning (held-in), while the remaining thirteen will be reserved for zero-shot evaluation (held-out), including four entirely unseen task categories. Evaluation will include comparison against strong baselines such as BLIP-2 and Flamingo, using metrics appropriate to each dataset (e.g., CIDEr for captioning, accuracy for QA, MRR for dialog, AUC for classification). Ablation studies will be conducted to assess the impact of instruction-aware feature extraction and balanced data sampling. Finetuning experiments on downstream tasks will be performed to evaluate model initialization quality and efficiency.
8bd6a2a89503be083176f2cc26fabedb79238cbd.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a comprehensive vision-language instruction tuning framework that systematically transforms a wide range of datasets into instruction format and leverages instruction-aware visual feature extraction for improved generalization. The method uniquely conditions the visual feature extraction process on the instruction, enabling more flexible and informative representations. The balanced data sampling strategy further enhances training stability and generalization. The approach is claimed to achieve state-of-the-art zero-shot and finetuning performance across a diverse set of vision-language tasks, outperforming previous multitask and instruction-agnostic baselines.

8be97edf8093965360d952ba3983f46300a8a6c8.title: RL in Latent MDPs is Tractable: Online Guarantees via Off-Policy Evaluation
8be97edf8093965360d952ba3983f46300a8a6c8.research_question: Can efficient online reinforcement learning be achieved in Latent Markov Decision Processes (LMDPs) without structural assumptions, and is it possible to break the curse of horizon in such partially observed environments using new algorithmic and analytical tools?
8be97edf8093965360d952ba3983f46300a8a6c8.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a sample-efficient online RL algorithm for general LMDPs can be developed by leveraging a novel off-policy evaluation (OPE) perspective and a new coverage coefficient, enabling near-optimal policy learning without requiring explicit structural assumptions or prior knowledge of latent contexts.
8be97edf8093965360d952ba3983f46300a8a6c8.proposed_method: A new algorithmic framework, LMDP-OMLE, is proposed for online exploration in LMDPs. The approach iteratively constructs and refines a confidence set of candidate models using maximum likelihood estimation on collected trajectory data. At each iteration, a memoryless policy is identified that maximizes the discrepancy in trajectory distributions between models in the confidence set. Exploration is conducted using segmented policies, which combine sequences of memoryless test policies and interventions (such as forced random actions at specific time steps), to ensure sufficient coverage of state-action subsequences across latent contexts. The algorithm's analysis is grounded in a novel coverage coefficient for LMDPs, which quantifies the worst-case ratio of visitation probabilities over partial trajectories and latent contexts, and an OPE lemma that bounds the total variation distance between trajectory distributions of different models. By focusing on memoryless policies and segmented exploration, the method avoids exponential dependence on the horizon and enables tractable learning.
8be97edf8093965360d952ba3983f46300a8a6c8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in tabular LMDP settings with finite state, action, and reward spaces, and a constant number of latent contexts (M = O(1)). The algorithm will be evaluated on its ability to learn near-optimal policies within a specified sample complexity bound. Baselines will include existing algorithms for POMDPs and LMDPs that rely on structural or separation assumptions. Evaluation metrics will include the total variation distance between learned and optimal trajectory distributions, policy suboptimality (expected reward gap), and empirical sample complexity. The experimental setup will involve varying the number of states, actions, horizon length, and latent contexts to assess scalability and robustness. Synthetic environments will be constructed to test the algorithm under both shared and distinct transition dynamics across latent contexts.
8be97edf8093965360d952ba3983f46300a8a6c8.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first sample-efficient online RL algorithm for general LMDPs without requiring structural assumptions or prior knowledge of latent contexts. A novel coverage coefficient for LMDPs is developed, enabling new off-policy evaluation guarantees that are independent of the horizon length. The approach leverages segmented exploration policies and reduces the search space to memoryless policies, providing tractable sample complexity bounds that match known lower bounds up to polynomial factors. These innovations offer a new perspective on the interplay between off-policy evaluation and exploration in partially observed environments, with potential applicability beyond LMDPs.

8c1a913f7c0626e28e07fad8021f85457eb2f5d6.title: BatchTopK Sparse Autoencoders
8c1a913f7c0626e28e07fad8021f85457eb2f5d6.research_question: How can sparse autoencoders be improved to more flexibly and efficiently represent language model activations, achieving better reconstruction performance without sacrificing sparsity or interpretability?
8c1a913f7c0626e28e07fad8021f85457eb2f5d6.hypothesis: Relaxing the fixed per-sample top-k sparsity constraint to a batch-level constraint in sparse autoencoders will enable adaptive allocation of active latents per sample, resulting in improved reconstruction performance while maintaining average sparsity and interpretability.
8c1a913f7c0626e28e07fad8021f85457eb2f5d6.proposed_method: A novel sparse autoencoder architecture, BatchTopK Sparse Autoencoders (BatchTopK SAEs), is proposed. Instead of enforcing a fixed number of top-k active latents per sample, the method applies a BatchTopK operation that selects the top n×k activations across an entire batch of n samples, allowing each sample to have a variable number of active latents. The encoder and decoder are standard linear layers with non-negativity and sparsity enforced by the activation function, and an auxiliary loss is included to prevent dead latents. During inference, the batch dependency is removed by estimating a global activation threshold from training batches, and a JumpReLU activation is used to zero out activations below this threshold. This approach enables more flexible and efficient use of the latent dictionary, adapting to the complexity of each input sample.
8c1a913f7c0626e28e07fad8021f85457eb2f5d6.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the residual stream activations of two large language models: GPT-2 Small (layer 8) and Gemma 2 2B (layer 12). The OpenWebText dataset, processed into sequences of up to 128 tokens, serves as the input corpus. Models are trained with the Adam optimizer (learning rate 3e-4, β1=0.9, β2=0.99), batch size 4096, and up to 1e9 tokens processed. Dictionary sizes of 3072, 6144, 12288, and 24576 are used for GPT-2 Small, and 16384 for Gemma 2 2B, with active latent counts (k) of 16, 32, and 64. Baselines include TopK SAEs and JumpReLU SAEs, with sparsity penalties tuned to match the number of active latents. Evaluation metrics include normalized mean squared error (NMSE) and cross-entropy (CE) degradation, enabling direct comparison of reconstruction quality and downstream performance.
8c1a913f7c0626e28e07fad8021f85457eb2f5d6.novelty_claims: BatchTopK SAEs introduce a novel batch-level sparsity constraint, enabling adaptive allocation of active latents per sample and direct specification of average sparsity without costly hyperparameter sweeps. This method achieves consistently better or comparable reconstruction performance compared to TopK and JumpReLU SAEs, while maintaining interpretability and offering greater flexibility in latent allocation. The approach demonstrates that small architectural modifications to the activation function can yield significant improvements in sparse autoencoder performance for language model interpretability.

8c2e89ab149ac947465c8529b1c5db731bdee7ca.title: Stochastic Layer-Wise Shuffle for Improving Vision Mamba Training
8c2e89ab149ac947465c8529b1c5db731bdee7ca.research_question: How can training methodologies be improved to enhance the performance and generalization of non-hierarchical Vision Mamba (Vim) models for visual recognition tasks, particularly in mitigating overfitting and narrowing the performance gap with leading vision architectures?
8c2e89ab149ac947465c8529b1c5db731bdee7ca.hypothesis: Introducing a stochastic, layer-wise regularization method that perturbs token sequences during training will improve the generalization and robustness of Vision Mamba models, leading to better performance on large-scale visual benchmarks without requiring architectural modifications.
8c2e89ab149ac947465c8529b1c5db731bdee7ca.proposed_method: A novel regularization technique, Stochastic Layer-Wise Shuffle (SLWS), will be developed for non-hierarchical Vision Mamba models. At each layer during training, a Bernoulli random variable determines whether to apply a random permutation (shuffle) to the input token sequence, with the probability of shuffling increasing linearly with layer depth. After processing, the output sequence is restored to its original order to prevent recursive disruptions in subsequent layers. This process introduces transformation invariance in deeper layers while preserving positional sensitivity in shallower layers. The method is plug-and-play, requires no changes to the model architecture, and is deactivated during inference, ensuring no additional inference overhead.
8c2e89ab149ac947465c8529b1c5db731bdee7ca.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ImageNet-1K dataset for image classification, using various sizes of non-hierarchical Vision Mamba models (middle, base, large, and huge). Baselines will include supervised Vim training, MambaR with token registers, MambaMLP with ARM and MAE pre-training, and state-of-the-art ViT and CNN backbones. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy for classification, mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) for semantic segmentation on ADE20K, and Average Precision (AP) for object detection and instance segmentation on COCO2017. Additional experiments will integrate masked feature distillation (MFD) using frozen CLIP vision encoders as teacher tokenizers, and ablation studies will assess the impact of probability schedules, inclusion of [CLS] tokens, and computational overhead.
