Training will utilize AdamW optimizer, cosine learning rate scheduling, and BFloat16 precision, with results reported using Exponential Moving Average.
8c2e89ab149ac947465c8529b1c5db731bdee7ca.novelty_claims: The proposed SLWS method introduces a stochastic, layer-wise regularization scheme that requires no architectural changes and incurs negligible computational overhead. It is the first to leverage progressive, depth-dependent sequence shuffling for Vision Mamba models, aligning with semantic abstraction hierarchies in vision tasks. When combined with masked feature distillation, the approach achieves new state-of-the-art results for Vision Mamba models on ImageNet-1K and dense prediction tasks, effectively mitigating overfitting and enabling stable training of large-scale non-hierarchical Vim architectures.

8c3873574450e963c3ac9caa50eb4d0ff12bfd9c.title: The Rise of Parameter Specialization for Knowledge Storage in Large Language Models
8c3873574450e963c3ac9caa50eb4d0ff12bfd9c.research_question: How does the internal parameter specialization for knowledge storage in large language models (LLMs) relate to their performance, and can optimizing this specialization improve knowledge utilization and reduce hallucination in LLMs?
8c3873574450e963c3ac9caa50eb4d0ff12bfd9c.hypothesis: Greater specialization of model parameters for specific knowledge concepts leads to more efficient knowledge utilization, improved performance on knowledge-intensive tasks, and reduced hallucination in large language models.
8c3873574450e963c3ac9caa50eb4d0ff12bfd9c.proposed_method: A comprehensive analysis will be conducted on the parameter specialization patterns within the multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) of transformer-based LLMs. The approach involves identifying and quantifying the degree to which individual parameter vectors (value vectors) in MLPs are activated by specific knowledge concepts. A knowledge vector masking procedure will be developed, where the most relevant parameter vectors for a given concept are identified by comparing activations on concept-related versus unrelated questions. The Parameter Specialization Score (PSS) will be defined to quantify the degree of specialization. Additionally, a new benchmark dataset, SpecWiki, will be constructed from Wikipedia, categorizing concepts by frequency and generating both multiple-choice and open-ended questions. Controlled fine-tuning experiments will be performed, selectively updating subsets of parameter vectors to validate the causal impact of specialization on knowledge retrieval and hallucination.
8c3873574450e963c3ac9caa50eb4d0ff12bfd9c.experiment_details: Experiments will be carried out on 20 open-source LLMs from diverse model families and sizes, including LLaMA, Qwen, Gemma, OLMo, Yi, Mistral, GPT-J, Pythia, Falcon, and MPT. The SpecWiki benchmark will be used, containing 525 concepts with varying frequencies and both multiple-choice and open-ended question formats. For each model, knowledge vector masking will be applied to different MLP layers, and the impact on model outputs will be measured using Concept-Specific and General Scores. Parameter Specialization Scores will be computed at various masking ratios. Controlled fine-tuning experiments will be conducted on LLaMA2-7B and Qwen2-7B models, using additional knowledge data for selected concepts, and comparing full, partial, complementary, and random vector fine-tuning strategies. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on SpecWiki, PSS, Semantic Entropy, and Local Intrinsic Dimension to assess hallucination.
8c3873574450e963c3ac9caa50eb4d0ff12bfd9c.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first systematic quantification and comparison of parameter specialization for knowledge storage across a wide range of LLMs. It establishes a direct empirical link between increased parameter specialization and improved model performance on knowledge-intensive tasks, as well as reduced hallucination. The approach leverages a novel knowledge vector masking technique and a newly constructed encyclopedic benchmark (SpecWiki) to probe knowledge storage at a fine-grained level. The proposed controlled fine-tuning experiments provide causal evidence for the benefits of targeted parameter specialization, offering actionable insights for more efficient and interpretable LLM design.

8c411b9f7c1b873a0eb9cd1afe160ce955c3b519.title: SADA: Stability-guided Adaptive Diffusion Acceleration
8c411b9f7c1b873a0eb9cd1afe160ce955c3b519.research_question: How can the sampling process of ODE-based generative models be accelerated in a training-free manner while maintaining high fidelity and generalizing across different architectures, solvers, and data modalities?
8c411b9f7c1b873a0eb9cd1afe160ce955c3b519.hypothesis: The fidelity gap in existing training-free diffusion acceleration methods arises because (a) different prompts correspond to varying denoising trajectories, and (b) current methods do not leverage the underlying ODE formulation and its numerical solution; thus, adaptively allocating sparsity based on a stability criterion derived from precise ODE gradients will enable faster sampling with minimal fidelity loss.
8c411b9f7c1b873a0eb9cd1afe160ce955c3b519.proposed_method: A stability-guided adaptive diffusion acceleration (SADA) framework is developed to unify step-wise and token-wise sparsity decisions via a single stability criterion, enabling dynamic acceleration of ODE-based generative models. The method leverages the second-order difference of the precise gradient (from the numerical ODE solver) to measure local dynamics of the denoising trajectory, guiding when and where to apply cache-assisted pruning. Step-wise and token-wise cache-assisted pruning are adaptively selected at each timestep based on the stability criterion, with principled approximation schemes (including third-order Adams–Moulton and Lagrange interpolation) used to reconstruct skipped states. The approach is implemented in a plug-and-play fashion, compatible with various backbone architectures and solvers, and requires no additional training or hyperparameter tuning.
8c411b9f7c1b873a0eb9cd1afe160ce955c3b519.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on text-to-image generation tasks using MS-COCO 2017 as the primary dataset, evaluating models such as SD-2 (U-Net), SDXL (modified U-Net), and Flux.1-dev (DiT) with both Euler Discrete Multistep (EDM) and DPM-Solver++ solvers, each with 50 sampling steps. Baselines include DeepCache, AdaptiveDiffusion, and TeaCache, with all pipelines implemented in Huggingface Diffusers and run on NVIDIA A100 or A5000 GPUs. Evaluation metrics include Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity (LPIPS), and Frechet Inception Distance (FID), as well as speedup ratios relative to unmodified baselines. Additional experiments assess generalization to other modalities (MusicLDM for audio, ControlNet for conditional image generation) and ablation studies on few-step sampling and parameter sensitivity.
8c411b9f7c1b873a0eb9cd1afe160ce955c3b519.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to directly bridge numerical ODE solvers of the sampling trajectory with sparsity-aware architectural optimizations via a unified stability criterion. It introduces a principled, training-free paradigm that dynamically allocates both step-wise and token-wise sparsity, leveraging precise gradient information for error-bounded approximations. The approach generalizes across architectures, solvers, and data modalities, achieving consistent ≥1.8× speedups with negligible fidelity loss, and outperforms existing training-free acceleration strategies in both efficiency and faithfulness.

8c5acaafe43e710d55b08c63d567550ad26ec437.title: Fact-Checking the Output of Large Language Models via Token-Level Uncertainty Quantification
8c5acaafe43e710d55b08c63d567550ad26ec437.research_question: How can unreliable or hallucinated claims in the output of large language models be automatically detected at a fine-grained (token or claim) level, without relying on external knowledge sources?
8c5acaafe43e710d55b08c63d567550ad26ec437.hypothesis: Token-level uncertainty quantification, specifically a method that isolates uncertainty about the factual content of claims while ignoring uncertainty about claim type or surface form, can effectively identify hallucinated or unreliable claims in LLM outputs and achieve performance competitive with external knowledge-based fact-checking systems.
8c5acaafe43e710d55b08c63d567550ad26ec437.proposed_method: A novel fact-checking pipeline is proposed that leverages token-level uncertainty quantification to detect unreliable or hallucinated claims in LLM-generated text. The approach begins by segmenting generated text into atomic claims using a claim extraction model. For each claim, token-level uncertainty scores are computed and aggregated into claim-level uncertainty scores. The core innovation is the Claim-Conditioned Probability (CCP) method, which quantifies uncertainty by focusing only on the model's uncertainty about the factual value of a claim, explicitly removing uncertainty related to claim type or surface form. CCP is implemented by analyzing the token probability distribution at each generation step, using a natural language inference (NLI) model to group token alternatives by semantic equivalence and claim type, and then computing the probability mass assigned to the intended claim meaning. Claims with high uncertainty scores are flagged as potentially unreliable for end-user review.
8c5acaafe43e710d55b08c63d567550ad26ec437.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the task of biography generation across four languages (English, Chinese, Arabic, Russian) using seven LLMs, including Vicuna 13b, Mistral 7b, Jais 13b, GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4, Yi 6b, and Vikhr-instruct-0.27b. For evaluation, generated biographies are decomposed into atomic claims, which are then automatically annotated for factuality using the FactScore tool (which leverages Wikipedia as an external knowledge source), and manually annotated for a subset in each language by human annotators. Baselines include Maximum Probability, Perplexity, Token Entropy, and P(True) (self-reflection). Evaluation metrics are ROC-AUC and PR-AUC for binary classification of claims as factual or hallucinated. Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of NLI model size, context window, number of token alternatives, and handling of function words. Computational efficiency is measured by comparing the runtime of CCP to the fastest baseline.
8c5acaafe43e710d55b08c63d567550ad26ec437.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first framework for fact-checking LLM generations using token-level uncertainty quantification that does not require external knowledge sources. The Claim-Conditioned Probability (CCP) method is a novel uncertainty quantification approach that isolates claim-specific uncertainty and outperforms existing baselines across multiple models and languages. The evaluation pipeline includes a new benchmark for claim-level uncertainty quantification in biography generation, and demonstrates that uncertainty-based methods can match or exceed the performance of external knowledge-based fact-checking tools. The method is computationally efficient and can be integrated as a plug-in for white-box LLMs.

8c62607bf5b9f032e40f830c780769ecbde11b89.title: How to Learn when Data Gradually Reacts to Your Model
8c62607bf5b9f032e40f830c780769ecbde11b89.research_question: How can machine learning models be effectively trained and optimized when the data distribution gradually adapts to the deployed model, with changes depending both on the current model and the prior state of the population, in order to minimize long-term test loss under state-dependent performative effects?
8c62607bf5b9f032e40f830c780769ecbde11b89.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a gradient-based optimization algorithm, which estimates and accounts for the gradual, state-dependent adaptation of the data distribution in response to deployed models, can efficiently find models that minimize long-term performative loss, outperforming existing methods that do not explicitly handle state-dependence.
8c62607bf5b9f032e40f830c780769ecbde11b89.proposed_method: A novel algorithm, Stateful Performative Gradient Descent (Stateful PerfGD), will be developed to optimize the long-term performative loss in settings where the data distribution evolves gradually in response to both the deployed model and the previous state. The method operates by estimating the gradient of the long-term performative loss using recent history of model deployments and observed data, leveraging parametric assumptions about the data distribution (e.g., mixtures of Gaussians). The algorithm uses finite difference approximations over a moving window of recent states to estimate the Jacobian of the distribution update function, and then recursively computes the derivative of the long-term distribution with respect to model parameters. These estimates are used to perform approximate gradient descent steps, optionally with added Gaussian perturbations for robust estimation. The approach is adaptable to cases where the distribution shift depends on low-dimensional statistics, allowing for efficient optimization even in high-dimensional model spaces.
8c62607bf5b9f032e40f830c780769ecbde11b89.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and realistic datasets, including linear and nonlinear distribution update scenarios as well as a spam classification task with strategic agents. The proposed method will be compared against several baselines: Repeated Gradient Descent (RGD), black-box Derivative-Free Optimization (DFO), and the stateless PerfGD algorithm, with and without waiting for distribution convergence. Evaluation metrics will include the fraction of optimal performance achieved, convergence speed, and final test loss relative to the long-term optimum. Hyperparameters such as estimation horizon, learning rate, and perturbation size will be tuned via grid search. Additional experiments will assess performance in settings where the distribution shift is governed by low-dimensional summary statistics.
8c62607bf5b9f032e40f830c780769ecbde11b89.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to address optimization of long-term performative loss in the state-dependent setting, where the data distribution's adaptation is gradual and depends on both the current model and prior state. The algorithm enables efficient estimation of the performative gradient without requiring repeated waiting for the distribution to settle, overcoming limitations of prior approaches. Theoretical guarantees are provided for convergence to approximate critical points under standard regularity conditions. Empirical results demonstrate substantial improvements over existing methods, especially as the degree of state-dependence increases, and the approach is shown to be adaptable to high-dimensional models via low-dimensional statistics.

8c705bdf56d07acc024bf7d6cca6b37959e7d4e3.title: Revisiting Multi-Permutation Equivariance through the Lens of Irreducible Representations
8c705bdf56d07acc024bf7d6cca6b37959e7d4e3.research_question: How can a comprehensive and explicit characterization of linear equivariant layers for permutation groups and related group actions be developed, particularly in settings involving multi-permutation and wreath product symmetries, and how does this characterization impact the design and effectiveness of equivariant neural networks for tasks involving sets, graphs, and neural network weight spaces?
8c705bdf56d07acc024bf7d6cca6b37959e7d4e3.hypothesis: A characterization of equivariant linear layers based on irreducible representations and Schur’s lemma will yield a more general, explicit, and computationally efficient framework than parameter-sharing approaches, and the inclusion of non-Siamese equivariant layers will improve performance on tasks involving unaligned symmetric sets, graphs, and weight space alignment.
8c705bdf56d07acc024bf7d6cca6b37959e7d4e3.proposed_method: The proposed method develops a systematic framework for constructing linear equivariant layers by decomposing input spaces into irreducible representations of the relevant symmetry group (e.g., permutation groups, wreath products). Schur’s lemma is then applied to fully characterize all equivariant linear mappings between these decomposed spaces, identifying both Siamese and non-Siamese components. The approach includes explicit algorithms for decomposing spaces such as sets, graphs, and neural network weight spaces into their irreducible components, and for constructing the corresponding equivariant layers. The methodology generalizes to cases where the group action is not transitive and provides a full basis of equivariant layers, including a potentially large number of non-Siamese mappings, which are constructed using invariant inner products and basis selection for trivial subspaces. The framework is designed to be computationally efficient and to subsume or simplify previous parameter-sharing-based constructions.
8c705bdf56d07acc024bf7d6cca6b37959e7d4e3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on tasks that exhibit wreath product or multi-permutation equivariance, including synthetic graph anomaly detection, Wasserstein distance computation between sets, and neural network weight space alignment. For graph anomaly detection, synthetic datasets of k-graphs with controlled noise will be generated, and models will be evaluated on their ability to identify anomalous graphs under permutation and group actions. For Wasserstein distance learning, real-world and synthetic datasets such as noisy-sphere, uniform, ModelNet, and RNAseq will be used, with performance measured by the accuracy of learned distances compared to ground truth. For weight space alignment, MLPs trained on MNIST and CIFAR10 will be aligned using the proposed equivariant layers, with metrics including reconstruction loss and classification accuracy. Baselines will include Siamese-only models and previous partial non-Siamese constructions, with evaluation metrics tailored to each task (e.g., accuracy, loss, mean squared error).
8c705bdf56d07acc024bf7d6cca6b37959e7d4e3.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a general and explicit characterization of all linear equivariant layers for permutation and related groups using irreducible representations and Schur’s lemma, subsuming and simplifying prior parameter-sharing approaches. It provides the first full characterization of equivariant layers for sets of unaligned symmetric elements under general wreath product actions, revealing a much richer space of non-Siamese layers than previously recognized. The method enables efficient computation and implementation of these layers, and empirical results are expected to demonstrate that including the full basis of non-Siamese layers yields superior performance on tasks such as graph anomaly detection, Wasserstein distance learning, and neural network weight space alignment.

8cb0b1047de0bfd50f52bfb6a9f8daca4f243ec7.title: Compositional Generalization from First Principles
8cb0b1047de0bfd50f52bfb6a9f8daca4f243ec7.research_question: What are the fundamental conditions under which machine learning models can achieve compositional generalization, and how can these conditions be formalized and empirically validated across different data-generating processes?
8cb0b1047de0bfd50f52bfb6a9f8daca4f243ec7.hypothesis: Compositional generalization can be guaranteed if the data-generating process and the training distribution satisfy specific conditions related to compositional and sufficient support, and if the model architecture aligns with the compositional structure of the data.
8cb0b1047de0bfd50f52bfb6a9f8daca4f243ec7.proposed_method: A mathematical framework will be developed to formalize compositionality as a property of the data-generating process, rather than the data itself. The approach will define compositional representations in terms of component functions and a composition function, and will derive sufficient conditions on the support of the training distribution and the model architecture for compositional generalization. Theoretical results will be established, including formal definitions of compositional and sufficient support, and a theorem providing sufficient conditions for generalization to novel compositions. The framework will be instantiated in supervised regression settings, where models are trained to reconstruct data from known latent factors, and will be designed to be applicable across various domains and modalities.
8cb0b1047de0bfd50f52bfb6a9f8daca4f243ec7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic multi-sprite datasets, where each data point is generated by composing multiple independently parameterized components (e.g., sprites with varying position, shape, size, and color). Both compositional and monolithic neural network models will be trained under different training distributions that either satisfy or violate the proposed sufficient conditions. Evaluation will be performed on both in-domain (ID) test sets and the full latent space (OOD generalization), using metrics such as mean squared error (MSE) and variance-weighted R^2 scores. Ablation studies will be included to assess the impact of gaps in support, insufficient variability, and changes in the composition function, with results visualized as heatmaps over the latent space.
8cb0b1047de0bfd50f52bfb6a9f8daca4f243ec7.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled, mathematical framework for compositional generalization, shifting the focus from data properties to the data-generating process. It provides formal definitions and sufficient conditions for compositional generalization that are independent of specific data domains or modalities. The approach establishes theoretical guarantees for generalization to novel compositions, covering a broader set of scenarios than previous work. Empirical validation is designed to directly test these theoretical claims, setting the stage for future research on unsupervised compositional learning and more scalable, robust, and sample-efficient machine learning models.

8cbc7c757766697a56e7cf881605b8e414ab2fdc.title: A is for Absorption: Studying Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders
8cbc7c757766697a56e7cf881605b8e414ab2fdc.research_question: How can the interpretability and reliability of features extracted by sparse autoencoders (SAEs) from large language models (LLMs) be improved, particularly in the presence of hierarchical feature structures and phenomena such as feature splitting and absorption?
8cbc7c757766697a56e7cf881605b8e414ab2fdc.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the sparsity objective in SAEs, when applied to hierarchically structured features, leads to a phenomenon termed feature absorption, where more general features are absorbed by more specific ones, resulting in unreliable and non-monosemantic latent activations. Adjusting SAE size or sparsity alone may be insufficient to resolve this issue.
8cbc7c757766697a56e7cf881605b8e414ab2fdc.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves a systematic investigation of feature splitting and absorption in SAEs trained on LLM activations. First, toy models will be constructed to analytically and empirically demonstrate how hierarchical feature co-occurrence induces absorption under sparsity constraints. Next, a metric for detecting feature absorption will be developed, leveraging ablation studies and cosine similarity between SAE latents and linear probe directions. This metric will be used to quantify absorption across a wide range of SAE architectures, sizes, and sparsity levels. Further, k-sparse probing will be employed to analyze feature splitting, and ablation-based causal analysis will identify which latents mediate specific behaviors in the model. Finally, the effectiveness of various SAE configurations and potential mitigation strategies, such as structured sparsity or meta-autoencoders, will be explored.
8cbc7c757766697a56e7cf881605b8e414ab2fdc.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize activations from large language models, primarily Gemma-2-2B, as well as Qwen-20.5B and Llama3-21B, focusing on tasks such as first-letter identification using in-context learning prompts. Both open-source and custom-trained SAEs with varying widths (e.g., 16k, 65k) and sparsity levels (L0, L1, TopK) will be evaluated. Baselines will include linear probes and k-sparse probes for comparison. Evaluation metrics will comprise F1 score, precision, recall for classification tasks, and a novel feature absorption rate based on ablation effects and probe alignment. Ablation studies will measure the causal impact of individual latents, and feature splitting will be assessed by observing F1 score improvements as k increases in k-sparse probing. The experimental setup will ensure robust train/test splits and control for confounding factors such as layer depth and token position.
8cbc7c757766697a56e7cf881605b8e414ab2fdc.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the concept of feature absorption as a fundamental limitation of sparse autoencoders in the presence of hierarchical features, providing both analytical and empirical evidence for its occurrence. A new metric for detecting and quantifying feature absorption is developed, enabling large-scale evaluation across hundreds of SAEs and multiple LLM architectures. The work systematically analyzes the interplay between feature splitting, absorption, and sparsity, and highlights the inadequacy of current SAE configurations for robust interpretability. The proposal also outlines potential directions for overcoming absorption, such as meta-autoencoders and structured sparsity techniques, paving the way for more reliable and interpretable feature extraction from LLMs.

8cd209d61e123f9d3695afda4e6dd1b72804c9b0.title: One-shot Empirical Privacy Estimation for Federated Learning
8cd209d61e123f9d3695afda4e6dd1b72804c9b0.research_question: How can empirical privacy loss be efficiently and accurately estimated in federated learning systems, particularly under user-level differential privacy, without requiring multiple retraining runs, knowledge of model architecture, or access to training data?
8cd209d61e123f9d3695afda4e6dd1b72804c9b0.hypothesis: A one-shot empirical privacy estimation method using random canary clients, which does not require prior knowledge of the model, task, or DP algorithm, can provide accurate and provably correct estimates of privacy loss in federated learning settings, even under complex participation patterns.
8cd209d61e123f9d3695afda4e6dd1b72804c9b0.proposed_method: A novel one-shot privacy estimation framework will be developed for federated learning with user-level differential privacy. The approach introduces a set of random canary clients into the federated learning protocol, each generating independent random model updates sampled from the unit sphere and scaled to the clipping norm. These canaries participate in training rounds alongside real clients. After training, the cosine similarities between each canary update and the final model are computed, and their empirical distribution is fit to a Gaussian. This distribution is then compared to the theoretical null distribution (N(0,1/d)) representing canaries not present during training. The privacy parameter epsilon is estimated by comparing these distributions using hypothesis testing techniques, yielding an empirical measure of privacy loss. The method is model- and dataset-agnostic, incurs negligible overhead, and can be performed during a single training run.
8cd209d61e123f9d3695afda4e6dd1b72804c9b0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale federated learning benchmarks, including the Stack Overflow word prediction dataset (4.1M parameter LSTM, 341k clients, 2048 rounds, 167 clients per round, single epoch) and the EMNIST character recognition dataset (1.2M parameter CNN, 3383 users, 5 epochs, 34 clients per round). Various levels of DP noise will be tested, and 1000 canary clients will be inserted for privacy estimation. Baselines will include analytical DP bounds and previous empirical auditing methods such as CANIFE and modified Jagielski et al. (2020). Evaluation metrics will include the estimated epsilon under different adversarial threat models (final model only vs. all intermediate model iterates), model accuracy, and the impact of canary insertion on model utility. Additional experiments will explore the effect of multiple canary presentations and varying client participation patterns.
8cd209d61e123f9d3695afda4e6dd1b72804c9b0.novelty_claims: The proposed method enables efficient, one-shot empirical privacy estimation in federated learning without the need for repeated retraining, knowledge of the model or dataset, or strong adversarial assumptions. It provides provably correct privacy estimates under the Gaussian mechanism in high dimensions and is applicable to arbitrary client participation patterns. The approach is scalable, incurs minimal overhead, and can be integrated into existing federated learning workflows. It also allows empirical exploration of privacy properties under practical scenarios where tight analytical bounds are unavailable.

8cf9b49698fdb1b754df2556576412a7b44929f6.title: SmoothLLM: Defending Large Language Models Against Jailbreaking Attacks
8cf9b49698fdb1b754df2556576412a7b44929f6.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be robustly defended against jailbreaking attacks that induce objectionable outputs, while maintaining efficiency, compatibility, and minimal impact on normal performance?
8cf9b49698fdb1b754df2556576412a7b44929f6.hypothesis: Randomized character-level perturbations of input prompts, followed by aggregation of model outputs, will significantly reduce the success rate of jailbreaking attacks on LLMs without requiring retraining or sacrificing nominal performance.
8cf9b49698fdb1b754df2556576412a7b44929f6.proposed_method: A defense framework, SMOOTHLLM, is developed that wraps around any LLM to mitigate jailbreaking attacks. The method operates in two main steps: (1) Perturbation—N copies of the input prompt are generated, each perturbed at the character level using one of several strategies (insert, swap, or patch) with a perturbation percentage q, affecting a random subset of characters. (2) Aggregation—Each perturbed prompt is passed through the LLM, and the outputs are evaluated using a binary jailbreak detector. A majority vote (with margin γ) over the N outputs determines if the input is adversarial; a response consistent with the majority is returned. This approach does not require retraining the LLM and can be applied to both black-box and white-box models.
8cf9b49698fdb1b754df2556576412a7b44929f6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of popular LLMs, including Vicuna, Llama2, GPT-3.5, GPT-4, PaLM-2, Claude-1, and Claude-2. The evaluation will use established adversarial prompt datasets such as AdvBench (for GCG, RANDOMSEARCH, and AMPLEGCG attacks) and JBB-Behaviors (for PAIR attacks). Attack success rates (ASR) will be measured as the primary metric, with additional evaluation of nominal performance on standard NLP benchmarks to assess conservatism. Baseline defenses, including perplexity filters and non-dictionary word removal, will be compared. Hyperparameters (number of perturbations N, perturbation percentage q, and margin γ) will be varied to study the trade-off between robustness and performance. Adaptive attacks targeting the defense will also be evaluated to assess robustness.
8cf9b49698fdb1b754df2556576412a7b44929f6.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first general-purpose, randomized defense for LLMs against jailbreaking attacks that does not require retraining or access to model internals. It demonstrates state-of-the-art reductions in attack success rates across multiple attack types (GCG, PAIR, RANDOMSEARCH, AMPLEGCG) and models, including both black-box and white-box LLMs. The approach is efficient, compatible with any LLM, and introduces only a modest trade-off with nominal performance. Theoretical analysis provides guarantees on defense success probability, and the method is resistant to adaptive attacks.

8d3730e51deb3997c39059421223f2a5da8a4783.title: Optimal Rates of Kernel Ridge Regression under Source Condition in Large Dimensions
8d3730e51deb3997c39059421223f2a5da8a4783.research_question: What are the optimal generalization rates for kernel ridge regression (KRR) under source condition assumptions in high-dimensional settings, particularly when the sample size scales polynomially with the data dimension, and how do these rates relate to minimax optimality and the saturation effect?
8d3730e51deb3997c39059421223f2a5da8a4783.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the generalization error of KRR in large-dimensional regimes can be precisely characterized under general source conditions, and that the minimax optimality and saturation effect of KRR will depend on the smoothness parameter s and the scaling exponent γ between sample size and dimension.
8d3730e51deb3997c39059421223f2a5da8a4783.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the generalization error of kernel ridge regression in high-dimensional settings, where the sample size n scales as d^γ for some γ > 0. The method will consider a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) defined by an inner product kernel on the sphere, and the true regression function will be assumed to belong to an interpolation space [H]^s, characterized by a source condition parameter s > 0. Key quantities such as N1(λ), N2(λ), M1(λ), and M2(λ), which depend on the kernel, the true function, and the regularization parameter λ, will be introduced to express tight upper and lower bounds for the generalization error. The approach will derive explicit convergence rates for KRR by optimizing the regularization parameter λ and will analyze the minimax lower bounds to determine the conditions under which KRR is minimax optimal or exhibits a saturation effect.
8d3730e51deb3997c39059421223f2a5da8a4783.experiment_details: Theoretical results will be validated through detailed analysis on the inner product kernel defined on the sphere with uniform distribution, leveraging the explicit spectral decomposition via spherical harmonics. The framework will be applied for various values of the source condition parameter s and scaling exponent γ, with convergence rates derived for both s ≥ 1 and 0 < s < 1. The minimax lower bounds will be established to compare with the achieved rates, and the periodic plateau and multiple descent behaviors of the generalization error curves will be characterized as functions of γ and s. No empirical datasets or numerical experiments are specified; all results are analytical.
8d3730e51deb3997c39059421223f2a5da8a4783.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified and general framework for characterizing the generalization error of KRR in large-dimensional settings under arbitrary source conditions, going beyond traditional capacity-source condition assumptions. It provides matching upper and lower bounds for the generalization error with minimal assumptions on the kernel eigenvalues and the true function, enabling the analysis of high-dimensional regimes previously not well understood. The work clarifies the relationship between previously disparate results (e.g., periodic plateau phenomena) and extends the understanding of minimax optimality and the saturation effect for KRR to new regimes, including the discovery that the saturation effect arises for lower smoothness levels in high dimensions than in fixed dimensions.

8d8c82f4b45686135c0b475d1c9b980884012b53.title: SKIM: Any-bit Quantization Pushing The Limits of Post-Training Quantization
8d8c82f4b45686135c0b475d1c9b980884012b53.research_question: How can post-training quantization of large language models be improved to enable flexible, memory-efficient deployment at arbitrary bit-widths, while minimizing performance degradation across a wide range of model architectures and tasks?
8d8c82f4b45686135c0b475d1c9b980884012b53.hypothesis: Adaptive channel-wise mixed-precision quantization, combined with a trainable scaling vector and optimized objective selection, will enable any-bit post-training quantization of large language models with significantly reduced performance loss compared to existing methods, especially at low bit-widths.
8d8c82f4b45686135c0b475d1c9b980884012b53.proposed_method: A novel quantization framework, Scaled K-means clustering wIth Mixed precision (SKIM), is developed to enable any-bit post-training quantization for large language models. The method consists of three key components: (1) a greedy algorithm for approximately optimal bit allocation across weight channels, allowing adaptive channel-wise mixed-precision quantization under a global bit constraint; (2) weighted K-means clustering applied per channel, with the number of centroids determined by the allocated bits, to generate quantized weights; and (3) a trainable scaling vector, optimized via an iterative coordinate descent strategy, which regularizes column-wise variations and compensates for quantization errors. Objective selection is guided by a unified analysis of layer-wise and sensitivity-based quantization targets, ensuring effective optimization for both grouping and scaling steps. The method is designed for weight-only, post-training quantization and supports both integer and non-integer average bit-widths.
8d8c82f4b45686135c0b475d1c9b980884012b53.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of large language models, including LLaMA (7B, 13B, 30B) and OPT (2.7B–6.7B), to evaluate generalizability. Evaluation datasets will include WikiText2 and C4 for perplexity measurement, with C4 also used for calibration. The MMLU benchmark will be used to assess downstream task accuracy in both zero-shot and five-shot settings. Baselines for comparison will include SqueezeLLM and OmniQuant, with additional comparisons to DecoupleQ and ABQ-LLM where applicable. Experiments will report perplexity, accuracy, and peak memory usage, and will analyze performance across various bit-widths (including non-integer average bits). Ablation studies will assess the impact of objective selection, scaling vector optimization, and mixed-precision allocation. GPU memory efficiency and computational overhead will also be measured.
8d8c82f4b45686135c0b475d1c9b980884012b53.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first flexible, any-bit post-training quantization framework for large language models, capable of breaking the fixed bit grid and supporting non-integer average bit-widths. The adaptive channel-wise mixed-precision allocation via a greedy algorithm and the integration of a trainable scaling vector for non-differentiable K-means clustering are novel contributions. The unified analysis of quantization objectives enables principled optimization across all steps. The approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in perplexity and memory efficiency across multiple models and bit-widths, significantly narrowing the performance gap between low-bit quantized and full-precision models.

8d8fc878bf4c7005546c866824a72d0c46ca91a3.title: Localizing Model Behavior with Path Patching
8d8fc878bf4c7005546c866824a72d0c46ca91a3.research_question: How can the localization of specific behaviors within neural networks be quantitatively tested and refined, particularly by attributing behaviors to a subset of paths or interactions within the network, and how does this improve mechanistic understanding and failure mode analysis?
8d8fc878bf4c7005546c866824a72d0c46ca91a3.hypothesis: Behaviors in neural networks can be localized to a specific subset of paths within the computational graph, such that interventions on these paths can explain the network's behavior on a given dataset, as measured by a reduction in unexplained effect (AUE) and increased proportion explained.
8d8fc878bf4c7005546c866824a72d0c46ca91a3.proposed_method: A novel framework, termed path patching, will be developed to formalize and quantitatively test localization claims in neural networks. The approach represents the network as a computational graph and defines hypotheses in terms of 'important' and 'unimportant' paths from input to output. By systematically intervening on the network—replacing the activations along unimportant paths with those from a counterfactual input while keeping important paths intact—the method measures the effect on the network's output. The framework includes a precise format for specifying hypotheses, a treeification procedure to disentangle overlapping subgraphs, and metrics such as average unexplained effect (AUE) and proportion explained to evaluate the faithfulness of localization claims. Iterative refinement is enabled by attribution techniques that highlight discrepancies between the patched and original models, guiding further hypothesis development.
8d8fc878bf4c7005546c866824a72d0c46ca91a3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both small attention-only transformers and large-scale models such as GPT-2 small and GPT-2 XL. Datasets will include held-out samples from OpenWebText and specially constructed prompts to probe specific behaviors (e.g., induction, parroting, and number prediction). Baselines will include hypotheses that patch all or none of the relevant paths, as well as comparisons to causal tracing and zero ablation techniques. Evaluation metrics will include average unexplained effect (AUE), average total effect (ATE), and proportion explained, with additional analysis on subsets of data to distinguish overlapping behaviors. Experimental setups will involve direct inspection of attention patterns, iterative hypothesis refinement, and visualization of attribution results to validate and improve localization claims.
8d8fc878bf4c7005546c866824a72d0c46ca91a3.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a general and quantitative methodology for localizing neural network behaviors to specific paths, extending prior node-based approaches to a more expressive path-based formalism. The framework enables precise, testable, and refinable localization claims, supports efficient experimentation via an open-source implementation, and provides new metrics for evaluating the faithfulness of mechanistic explanations. Path patching is shown to subsume and improve upon existing techniques such as causal tracing and zero ablation, allowing for more targeted and on-distribution interventions. The approach facilitates iterative refinement and attribution, offering deeper insight into both minimal and complex network mechanisms.

8da668b01beb344624e8c47ee5b2110da0f339dd.title: VideoJAM: Joint Appearance-Motion Representations for Enhanced Motion Generation in Video Models
8da668b01beb344624e8c47ee5b2110da0f339dd.research_question: How can video generation models be enhanced to achieve greater motion coherence and temporal consistency across a wide variety of real-world motion types, without sacrificing appearance fidelity or requiring significant changes to model architecture or training data?
8da668b01beb344624e8c47ee5b2110da0f339dd.hypothesis: Jointly modeling appearance and motion representations within a unified latent space, and leveraging a dynamic, model-internal motion guidance mechanism during inference, will significantly improve the motion coherence and overall quality of generated videos compared to conventional pixel-based objectives.
8da668b01beb344624e8c47ee5b2110da0f339dd.proposed_method: A novel framework, VideoJAM, is proposed to explicitly instill a strong motion prior into any video generation model. During training, the objective is extended to predict both pixel-level appearance and corresponding motion (represented as optical flow) from a single, learned joint representation. This is achieved by minimally modifying the model architecture with two additional linear layers: one at the input to combine noised video and motion signals, and one at the output to extract both appearance and motion predictions. The training loss is formulated to optimize for both appearance and motion, encouraging the model to learn a unified latent space that captures both aspects. During inference, an Inner-Guidance mechanism is introduced, which dynamically steers the generation process towards temporally coherent motion by leveraging the model’s own evolving motion predictions as a guidance signal, directly modifying the sampling distribution at each step. This approach requires no changes to the training data or large-scale retraining and is compatible with any video diffusion model backbone.
8da668b01beb344624e8c47ee5b2110da0f339dd.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using two variants of the DiT (Diffusion Transformer) architecture, DiT-4B and DiT-30B, pre-trained on an internal dataset of approximately 100 million videos and fine-tuned with VideoJAM on 3 million samples. The models generate 128-frame videos at 256x256 resolution and 24 fps. Evaluation is performed on two benchmarks: the newly introduced VideoJAM-bench, specifically designed to test motion coherence across basic, complex, rotational, and physics-based motions, and the Movie Gen (MGen) benchmark for robustness. Baselines include state-of-the-art proprietary and open-source models such as Sora, Kling, Runway Gen3, Mochi, and CogVideo. Evaluation metrics include both human preference (2AFC protocol) and automatic metrics from VBench, which disentangle appearance and motion quality. Ablation studies are conducted to assess the impact of each component of the framework.
8da668b01beb344624e8c47ee5b2110da0f339dd.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a generic, minimally invasive method to jointly model appearance and motion in video generation, requiring only two additional linear layers and no changes to training data or model scaling. The Inner-Guidance mechanism is a novel inference-time approach that leverages the model’s own motion predictions for dynamic, temporally coherent guidance, overcoming limitations of prior fixed or independent guidance signals. VideoJAM establishes new state-of-the-art results in motion coherence, surpassing both open-source and proprietary models, and demonstrates that appearance and motion can be effectively integrated to enhance both visual quality and temporal consistency in generated videos.

8dafb105a0cec1956443003eeea9fcf13c0ffa99.title: Spotting LLMs With Binoculars: Zero-Shot Detection of Machine-Generated Text
8dafb105a0cec1956443003eeea9fcf13c0ffa99.research_question: How can machine-generated text from large language models (LLMs) be accurately detected in a zero-shot, model-agnostic setting without relying on training data from the target LLMs, and how robust is such detection across diverse domains, languages, and adversarial scenarios?
8dafb105a0cec1956443003eeea9fcf13c0ffa99.hypothesis: A detection method that contrasts perplexity and cross-perplexity scores from two closely related pre-trained LLMs can reliably distinguish machine-generated text from human-written text across a wide range of models and domains, even in zero-shot settings.
8dafb105a0cec1956443003eeea9fcf13c0ffa99.proposed_method: The proposed approach, termed Binoculars, utilizes two pre-trained language models: an 'observer' model and a 'performer' model. For a given text sample, the method computes the log-perplexity (logPPL) of the text using the observer model, quantifying how surprising the text is to the model. Next, it calculates the cross-perplexity (X-PPL), which measures the average per-token cross-entropy between the next-token predictions of the performer model and the observer model on the same text. The Binoculars score is defined as the ratio of logPPL to X-PPL. This score serves as a normalized metric that is robust to prompt effects and context, enabling the detection of machine-generated text even when the generating model is unknown or unrelated to the observer/performer pair. The method requires no fine-tuning or training on machine-generated data and is designed to be model-agnostic and zero-shot.
8dafb105a0cec1956443003eeea9fcf13c0ffa99.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several benchmark datasets, including balanced datasets of human and machine-generated text from sources such as News, Creative Writing, and Student Essays, as well as additional datasets generated using LLaMA-2-7B, Falcon-7B, and ChatGPT. The evaluation will also include the M4 dataset for multi-domain and multilingual detection, and the OpenOrca dataset for diverse prompting strategies. Baseline comparisons will be made against state-of-the-art detectors such as Ghostbuster, GPTZero, DetectGPT, Fast-DetectGPT, and DNA-GPT. Evaluation metrics will focus on true positive rate (TPR) at low false positive rates (FPR), especially at 0.01% FPR, as well as AUC and F1-score. Additional experiments will assess robustness to adversarial prompting, non-native speaker text, memorized content, and random sequences.
8dafb105a0cec1956443003eeea9fcf13c0ffa99.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a zero-shot, model-agnostic LLM detector that requires no training data from the target model and operates solely using pre-trained models. The use of a ratio between perplexity and cross-perplexity as a detection metric is novel and shown to be highly effective across a wide range of LLMs, domains, and languages. The approach demonstrates state-of-the-art accuracy, outperforming both commercial and open-source detectors, and exhibits robustness to prompt engineering, non-native writing, and memorized content. The method is also shown to maintain low false positive rates, addressing key harm reduction concerns in LLM detection.

8dc5a5f57b5a4564536badf3ca98e5680f313314.title: Smarter, Better, Faster, Longer: A Modern Bidirectional Encoder for Fast, Memory Efficient, and Long Context Finetuning and Inference
8dc5a5f57b5a4564536badf3ca98e5680f313314.research_question: How can encoder-only transformer models be modernized to achieve improved performance, efficiency, and long-context capabilities for a wide range of downstream tasks, including retrieval, classification, and code understanding?
8dc5a5f57b5a4564536badf3ca98e5680f313314.hypothesis: Integrating recent architectural advances, large-scale diverse pretraining (including code), and hardware-aware model design into encoder-only transformers will yield models that outperform existing encoders in both accuracy and efficiency, especially for long-context and code-related tasks.
8dc5a5f57b5a4564536badf3ca98e5680f313314.proposed_method: A new family of encoder-only transformer models, ModernBERT, will be developed by incorporating several modern architectural improvements such as GeGLU activation functions, rotary positional embeddings (RoPE), pre-normalization blocks, and alternating local-global attention mechanisms. The model will leverage unpadding techniques and FlashAttention kernels to maximize memory and computational efficiency, and will be designed in a deep-and-narrow configuration to optimize for both downstream performance and hardware utilization. Training will be conducted on 2 trillion tokens from a diverse data mixture that includes web text, scientific literature, and code, using a modern BPE tokenizer tailored for code and text. The training objective will be masked language modeling (MLM) with a 30% masking rate, and the model will be optimized using StableAdamW with a trapezoidal learning rate schedule. Context length will be natively extended to 8192 tokens through a staged training process involving RoPE theta adjustments and additional long-context training.
8dc5a5f57b5a4564536badf3ca98e5680f313314.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate ModernBERT on a comprehensive suite of benchmarks, including GLUE for natural language understanding, BEIR for short- and long-context text retrieval (both single- and multi-vector settings), CodeSearchNet and StackOverflow-QA for code retrieval, and MLDR for long-context retrieval. Baselines will include BERT, RoBERTa, DeBERTaV3, NomicBERT, and GTE-en-MLM at both base and large parameter scales. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy for classification tasks and nDCG@10 for retrieval tasks. Hyperparameter sweeps will be performed for fair comparison, and efficiency will be measured in terms of tokens processed per second and maximum batch size on common GPUs (e.g., NVIDIA RTX 4090), using both fixed and variable sequence lengths. All models will be fine-tuned and evaluated under consistent settings, with additional ablations to assess the impact of architectural and training choices.
8dc5a5f57b5a4564536badf3ca98e5680f313314.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first open encoder-only model family with native support for 8192-token sequences, full-model unpadding, and hardware-aware design for optimal inference efficiency. ModernBERT combines recent advances from autoregressive LLMs (such as GeGLU, RoPE, and alternating attention) with large-scale, code-inclusive pretraining, resulting in state-of-the-art performance across classification, retrieval, and code tasks. The model sets new records for both accuracy and efficiency among encoder-only transformers, and is the first to demonstrate substantial Pareto improvements over BERT and its successors on a wide range of tasks. The release of a modular architecture framework (FlexBERT) and all intermediate checkpoints further supports reproducibility and future research.

8dccf45aa7b6d3e7ef8fe762751cb35c86778141.title: Enhancing Rating-Based Reinforcement Learning to Effectively Leverage Feedback from Large Vision-Language Models
8dccf45aa7b6d3e7ef8fe762751cb35c86778141.research_question: How can reinforcement learning agents effectively learn reward functions from AI-generated feedback, specifically leveraging large vision-language models, to reduce reliance on human supervision and domain expertise across a range of control and navigation tasks?
8dccf45aa7b6d3e7ef8fe762751cb35c86778141.hypothesis: Reward functions learned from absolute ratings provided by large vision-language models (VLMs) can enable reinforcement learning agents to achieve superior or comparable performance to those trained with traditional human feedback or environment-based rewards, while reducing sample inefficiency, instability, and human effort.
8dccf45aa7b6d3e7ef8fe762751cb35c86778141.proposed_method: A novel framework, ERL-VLM, is proposed to learn reward functions by querying large vision-language models (such as Gemini) for absolute ratings of individual agent trajectory segments, using a Likert scale (e.g., 'very bad' to 'very good'). The method employs carefully designed prompts to elicit comprehensive feedback from VLMs, analyzing both simple and complex task descriptions and agent behaviors through sequences of image observations and actions. To address challenges of data imbalance and noisy labels inherent in VLM-generated feedback, the approach incorporates stratified sampling to ensure balanced representation of all rating classes in each training batch and applies a weighted loss function to further mitigate imbalance. Additionally, a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) loss is used instead of cross-entropy to enhance robustness against label noise. The learned reward model is iteratively updated and used to relabel experiences in the replay buffer, and the policy is trained using off-policy RL algorithms such as SAC or IQL.
8dccf45aa7b6d3e7ef8fe762751cb35c86778141.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across three domains: low-level continuous control tasks in MetaWorld (e.g., SweepInto, DrawerOpen, Soccer), high-level vision-language navigation tasks in ALFRED (e.g., PickupObject, PutObject, CoolObject, CleanObject), and real-world robotic manipulation tasks using a Sawyer robotic arm (e.g., SweepBowl, DrawerOpen, PickupBanana). Baselines include similarity-based reward methods (CLIPScore, RoboCLIPScore), preference-based VLM feedback (RL-VLM-F), and environment reward functions. Evaluation metrics focus on task success rates, with each method trained and evaluated under the same query budget and policy training hyperparameters. Extensive ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of stratified sampling, MAE loss, and the number of rating classes. Real-world experiments will use offline datasets labeled by VLMs and evaluate policy performance on physical robot tasks.
8dccf45aa7b6d3e7ef8fe762751cb35c86778141.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the use of absolute ratings from large vision-language models for reward learning in reinforcement learning, improving expressiveness and sample efficiency over prior pairwise preference-based methods. Key innovations include prompt engineering for effective VLM feedback, stratified sampling and weighted loss for handling data imbalance, and the use of MAE loss for robustness to label noise. The method demonstrates superior performance to existing VLM-based reward generation techniques and shows potential for scaling RL with minimal human intervention, including successful application to real-world robotic manipulation tasks.

8dd8ca953961b5311575b4364652689465f49b08.title: If Influence Functions are the Answer, Then What is the Question?
8dd8ca953961b5311575b4364652689465f49b08.research_question: What are the underlying factors that cause discrepancies between influence function estimates and leave-one-out retraining in neural networks, and to what alternative quantity do influence functions provide accurate approximations?
8dd8ca953961b5311575b4364652689465f49b08.hypothesis: The discrepancy between influence function estimates and leave-one-out retraining in neural networks is primarily due to factors such as initialization, proximity regularization, and non-converged parameters, rather than errors in influence function estimation itself. Influence functions may accurately approximate a different response function, which can serve as a more appropriate gold standard for their evaluation.
8dd8ca953961b5311575b4364652689465f49b08.proposed_method: The proposed research will systematically decompose the misalignment between influence function estimates and leave-one-out (LOO) retraining in neural networks into five distinct components: warm-start gap, proximity gap, non-convergence gap, linearization error, and solver error. Each component will be formally defined and linked to specific modeling or algorithmic choices, such as initialization schemes, regularization, and optimization convergence. The methodology will involve deriving and analyzing the proximal Bregman response function (PBRF), which incorporates both proximity to the original parameters and Bregman divergence with respect to the network's predictions. Influence function estimates will be compared to both LOO retraining and PBRF across a range of neural architectures and tasks. The approach will utilize both theoretical derivations and empirical measurements to quantify the contribution of each gap or error term.
8dd8ca953961b5311575b4364652689465f49b08.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of tasks, including binary classification, regression, image reconstruction, image classification, and language modeling. Datasets such as UCI Cancer and Diabetes, Concrete and Energy, MNIST, FashionMNIST, CIFAR10, and Penn Treebank (PTB) will be used. Models will include logistic regression, multilayer perceptrons (MLPs), autoencoders, convolutional neural networks (LeNet, AlexNet, VGG13, ResNet-20), and Transformers. For each experiment, the base model will be trained to obtain reference parameters, and the effects of removing training examples will be measured via LOO retraining (cold-start and warm-start), influence function estimation (using LiSSA and the Gauss-Newton Hessian approximation), and optimization of the PBRF. Evaluation metrics will include the average L2 distance between network outputs and correlation (Pearson and Spearman) of test loss differences. The contribution of each misalignment component will be quantified, and the effects of network width, depth, training time, weight decay, damping, and the number of removed examples will be systematically explored.
8dd8ca953961b5311575b4364652689465f49b08.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a principled decomposition of the discrepancy between influence function estimates and LOO retraining in neural networks, identifying and quantifying the dominant sources of misalignment. A novel proximal Bregman response function (PBRF) is formulated and shown to be the true quantity approximated by influence functions in practical neural network settings. The work reframes the evaluation of influence functions, proposing PBRF as a more suitable gold standard than LOO retraining for many practical use cases. This approach clarifies the utility and limitations of influence functions and provides actionable insights for improving influence-based interpretability and data analysis methods in deep learning.

8ddcf482a9ad09cf59bfb1bb4fa80ac85669e024.title: A unifying tutorial on Approximate Message Passing
8ddcf482a9ad09cf59bfb1bb4fa80ac85669e024.research_question: How can the Approximate Message Passing (AMP) framework be systematically unified, extended, and rigorously characterized for a broad class of high-dimensional statistical estimation problems, including low-rank matrix estimation and generalized linear models?
8ddcf482a9ad09cf59bfb1bb4fa80ac85669e024.hypothesis: Approximate Message Passing algorithms, when formulated under a unified abstract recursion and analyzed via state evolution, provide precise asymptotic characterizations and can be flexibly adapted to a wide range of structured high-dimensional statistical problems, yielding optimal or near-optimal estimation error under mild technical conditions.
8ddcf482a9ad09cf59bfb1bb4fa80ac85669e024.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical framework will be developed for AMP algorithms by formalizing both symmetric and asymmetric AMP recursions, parameterized by sequences of Lipschitz denoising functions and Onsager correction terms. The methodology will rigorously establish 'master theorems' that characterize the asymptotic empirical distributions of AMP iterates via state evolution recursions, under general probabilistic setups including Gaussian and sub-Gaussian random matrices. The approach will include detailed analysis of the limiting behavior of AMP in canonical statistical settings, such as the spiked Wigner model for low-rank matrix estimation and penalized M-estimators (e.g., Lasso) in high-dimensional linear and generalized linear models. The framework will also formalize the connection between AMP and convex optimization, enabling systematic derivation of asymptotic risk expressions for a broad class of estimators.
8ddcf482a9ad09cf59bfb1bb4fa80ac85669e024.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in both synthetic and real-data settings, focusing on prototypical problems such as the spiked Wigner model (for low-rank matrix estimation) and high-dimensional linear regression with random Gaussian design (for Lasso and related estimators). Simulated datasets will be generated with varying signal structures (e.g., sparsity, binary priors) and noise levels. Baseline methods will include spectral estimators, iterative soft-thresholding algorithms (ISTA/FISTA), and information-theoretically optimal estimators when tractable. Evaluation metrics will include mean squared error (MSE), asymptotic risk, and empirical distributional convergence (e.g., via Wasserstein distance). The experimental setup will systematically vary problem dimensions and signal-to-noise ratios to validate the theoretical predictions of state evolution and to demonstrate the flexibility and accuracy of AMP-based approaches.
8ddcf482a9ad09cf59bfb1bb4fa80ac85669e024.novelty_claims: The proposed research unifies and strengthens existing results on AMP by providing rigorous, general-purpose master theorems for both symmetric and asymmetric AMP recursions, applicable to a wide class of statistical models. The framework formalizes the connection between AMP and convex optimization, enabling systematic derivation of asymptotic risk for generalized linear models. The approach clarifies and extends the state evolution analysis, offering transparent proofs and milder technical conditions than previous literature. The methodology is expected to be broadly applicable, providing a general recipe for analyzing and designing AMP algorithms for new statistical estimation problems.

8e02510b35a65122a9ca75e6f57541e16783f806.title: Automated Model Discovery via Multi-modal & Multi-step Pipeline
8e02510b35a65122a9ca75e6f57541e16783f806.research_question: How can automated model discovery be improved to effectively identify models that capture fine-grained data details while ensuring strong generalizability and interpretability, using multi-modal and multi-step reasoning processes?
8e02510b35a65122a9ca75e6f57541e16783f806.hypothesis: Integrating multi-modal, multi-step vision-language model (VLM) agents for both model proposal and evaluation will enable automated model discovery systems to more effectively identify models that balance detailed data fitting and generalizability, outperforming existing single-modal or single-step approaches.
8e02510b35a65122a9ca75e6f57541e16783f806.proposed_method: A novel automated model discovery pipeline is proposed, consisting of four iterative stages: model proposal, model fitting, model evaluation, and model selection. The pipeline leverages two vision-language model-based agents: AnalyzerVLM and EvaluatorVLM. AnalyzerVLM performs multi-step, multi-modal reasoning by iteratively analyzing data and candidate models using both natural language and executable code (e.g., Python with NumPy and Matplotlib), autonomously generating and refining model candidates based on visual and statistical analyses. EvaluatorVLM introduces a Visual Information Criterion (VIC), which combines visual assessment of model fitness and generalizability (via plot comparisons and uncertainty analysis) with the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC), producing a composite score for model selection. The process is repeated over multiple rounds, maintaining a pool of candidate models and iteratively refining proposals and evaluations, allowing the system to dynamically adapt its search and selection strategies based on both quantitative and perceptual criteria.
8e02510b35a65122a9ca75e6f57541e16783f806.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of real-world univariate time series datasets, including Airline Passenger, Solar Irradiance, Mauna Loa, Wheat, Call-Center, Radio, and Gas Production. The proposed pipeline will be compared against several baselines: Gaussian Process Regression (with Squared Exponential kernel), ARIMA, Facebook Prophet, Automatic Statistician, and BoxLM, as well as state-of-the-art LLM-based and symbolic regression methods. Evaluation metrics will include root mean squared error (RMSE) for both train and test regions, R-squared and RMSE for symbolic regression tasks, and correlation with human judgments for model evaluation. Ablation studies will assess the contributions of multi-modality, multi-step reasoning, and each VLM-based module. The pipeline will be tested with various VLM backbones (e.g., GPT-4o, Qwen2.5-VL) to demonstrate generality.
8e02510b35a65122a9ca75e6f57541e16783f806.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a multi-modal, multi-step automated model discovery pipeline that replaces traditional expert-driven processes with VLM-based agents capable of both in-depth analysis and perceptual evaluation. Key innovations include the use of AnalyzerVLM for autonomous, iterative reasoning and code execution to generate refined model candidates, and EvaluatorVLM for visually-informed model selection via the novel Visual Information Criterion (VIC). The approach uniquely combines visual and quantitative assessments, enabling superior generalizability and interpretability. The pipeline is adaptable to both probabilistic model discovery and symbolic regression, and is shown to outperform existing methods in both accuracy and generalization, as well as closely matching human evaluation in model selection.

8e2bcdc378761f7c6d2282a0ca2c304a19944df5.title: Decomposed Prompt Tuning via Low-Rank Reparameterization
8e2bcdc378761f7c6d2282a0ca2c304a19944df5.research_question: How can the efficiency and effectiveness of prompt tuning for large pre-trained language models be improved by exploring alternative parameterizations of soft prompts, particularly in terms of reducing the number of trainable parameters without sacrificing downstream task performance?
8e2bcdc378761f7c6d2282a0ca2c304a19944df5.hypothesis: Soft prompts used in prompt tuning exhibit a low intrinsic rank, and explicitly parameterizing them using low-rank matrix decompositions will significantly reduce the number of trainable parameters while maintaining or improving performance on downstream tasks.
8e2bcdc378761f7c6d2282a0ca2c304a19944df5.proposed_method: A novel prompt tuning approach is proposed in which the soft prompt matrix is reparameterized as the product of two smaller matrices, A (of shape embedding_dim × bottleneck) and B (of shape bottleneck × prompt_length), where the bottleneck dimension is much smaller than either the embedding dimension or prompt length. This low-rank decomposition constrains the soft prompt to have low intrinsic rank, reducing the total number of trainable parameters from embedding_dim × prompt_length (in vanilla prompt tuning) to embedding_dim × bottleneck + bottleneck × prompt_length. Both matrices A and B are initialized randomly (e.g., with a Gaussian distribution) and are the only trainable parameters; the rest of the pre-trained model remains frozen. During training, the product AB is prepended as the soft prompt to the input embedding, and the model is optimized using a standard conditional generation objective. After training, the product AB can be stored for inference, maintaining parameter efficiency.
8e2bcdc378761f7c6d2282a0ca2c304a19944df5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on eight datasets from the SuperGLUE benchmark, covering both high-resource and low-resource (few-shot) scenarios. The proposed method will be evaluated using three variants of the T5 model (T5-Small, T5-Base, T5-Large), with prompt length fixed at 100 and bottleneck size set to 10 in main experiments. Baselines for comparison include conventional full-model fine-tuning, vanilla prompt tuning, and residual prompt tuning. Evaluation metrics will follow established standards for each SuperGLUE task (e.g., accuracy, F1). All models will be trained for 100 epochs using AdamW optimizer, and results will be averaged over three runs with different random seeds. Additional analyses will explore sensitivity to bottleneck size and prompt length, as well as performance under extremely short prompts and varying bottleneck dimensions.
8e2bcdc378761f7c6d2282a0ca2c304a19944df5.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a low-rank reparameterization of soft prompts for prompt tuning, explicitly leveraging the observed low intrinsic rank of soft prompts to achieve substantial reductions in the number of trainable parameters. This approach enables parameter-efficient adaptation of large language models while maintaining or improving downstream task performance, outperforming both vanilla and residual prompt tuning baselines. The method is simple, does not require modifications to the transformer architecture, and generalizes effectively to both high-resource and few-shot settings.

8e37dc1215681aa153a51c07078ba8befd6a6e01.title: AdaPlanner: Adaptive Planning from Feedback with Language Models
8e37dc1215681aa153a51c07078ba8befd6a6e01.research_question: How can large language models be enhanced to act as autonomous agents capable of adaptive, sample-efficient, and robust sequential decision-making in complex, feedback-rich environments?
8e37dc1215681aa153a51c07078ba8befd6a6e01.hypothesis: An explicit closed-loop planning framework that adaptively refines plans based on environmental feedback, leverages code-based prompting to mitigate hallucination, and incorporates skill discovery for experience reuse, will significantly improve the performance, adaptability, and sample efficiency of LLM-based agents in sequential decision-making tasks.
8e37dc1215681aa153a51c07078ba8befd6a6e01.proposed_method: A novel adaptive closed-loop planning framework is developed in which a large language model (LLM) serves as both a planner and a plan refiner. The method decomposes tasks into sub-goals and generates initial plans using code-based (Pythonic) prompts, which structure the planning process and reduce ambiguity. During execution, the agent distinguishes between in-plan feedback (where observations align with predictions) and out-of-plan feedback (where deviations occur). In-plan feedback is handled by extracting key information from the environment using a dedicated ask_LLM() action, while out-of-plan feedback triggers comprehensive plan revision and allows the agent to resume execution from intermediate checkpoints. Additionally, a skill memory module archives successful plans and trajectories, enabling the agent to reuse effective strategies as few-shot exemplars for future planning, thereby improving sample efficiency and generalization.
8e37dc1215681aa153a51c07078ba8befd6a6e01.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted in two benchmark text-based environments: ALFWorld, a virtual household simulator with 134 tasks across six types, and MiniWoB++, a web-based interface environment with 53 tasks. The evaluation compares the proposed method against state-of-the-art baselines, including both training-based and closed-loop LLM agent methods (e.g., BUTLER, ReAct, Reflexion, RCI, CC-Net, WGE, WebN-T5-3B). Metrics include task success rate and sample efficiency, with ablation studies isolating the impact of code-based prompting and skill discovery. The method is tested under few-shot settings, using significantly fewer demonstrations than competing baselines, and performance is measured across both feedback-rich and feedback-sparse tasks. Additional analyses examine the effect of closed-loop corrections, resilience to LLM hallucination, and the contribution of skill discovery to overall success rates.
8e37dc1215681aa153a51c07078ba8befd6a6e01.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces an explicit closed-loop planning framework for LLM agents that adaptively refines both plans and actions based on environmental feedback, surpassing prior implicit closed-loop and open-loop methods. The use of code-based prompting for plan generation and refinement is claimed to significantly reduce LLM hallucination and improve interpretability. The refine-then-resume mechanism enables efficient recovery from errors without restarting episodes, enhancing computational efficiency. The integration of a skill discovery module allows for the accumulation and reuse of successful strategies, dramatically improving sample efficiency and generalization to new tasks. The method demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on challenging benchmarks while requiring up to 600 times fewer samples than previous approaches.

8e4fb48e0882066cc44636fbd812607909e191a7.title: Efficient Preference-based Reinforcement Learning via Aligned Experience Estimation
8e4fb48e0882066cc44636fbd812607909e191a7.research_question: How can preference-based reinforcement learning be made more feedback-efficient and robust to overfitting and overestimation bias, especially when human feedback is limited, across both discrete and continuous action spaces in online and offline environments?
8e4fb48e0882066cc44636fbd812607909e191a7.hypothesis: Integrating label smoothing for human preference labels and policy regularization via conservative Q-value estimation will significantly improve feedback efficiency and policy performance in preference-based reinforcement learning, particularly under limited human feedback, by reducing overfitting in the reward model and mitigating overestimation bias in value estimation.
8e4fb48e0882066cc44636fbd812607909e191a7.proposed_method: A new framework, SEER, is developed to enhance preference-based reinforcement learning by combining two key techniques: label smoothing and policy regularization. Label smoothing is applied to human preference labels to prevent overfitting in the reward model, replacing hard (1,0) or (0,1) labels with softened distributions (e.g., (1-λ, λ)), where λ is a tunable parameter. For policy regularization, a conservative Q-value estimate (Q̂) is bootstrapped using only well-supported state-action pairs from the replay memory, avoiding extrapolation to unseen actions. In discrete settings, the replay memory is structured as a dynamic directed graph, enabling efficient in-sample value iteration updates; in continuous settings, a neural network models Q̂, and a log-sum-exp operator interpolates between expectation and maximum for conservative estimation. Policy learning is regularized by minimizing the KL divergence between the current policy and a Boltzmann policy derived from Q̂, ensuring the learned policy remains close to the conservative estimate. The approach is compatible with standard RL algorithms such as DQN and TD3, and can be integrated into both online and offline PbRL pipelines.
8e4fb48e0882066cc44636fbd812607909e191a7.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a diverse set of environments, including puzzle video games (Sokoban), robotic construction (CraftEnv), locomotion (DeepMind Control Suite), robotic manipulation (Meta-world), and D4RL and Robosuite datasets. Both online and offline settings are evaluated. Baselines include state-of-the-art PbRL methods (PEBBLE, SURF, MRN for online; PT, IPL for offline) as well as reward-based RL algorithms (SAC, IQL, TD3+BC). Evaluation metrics include average episode return and success rate, with performance assessed using scripted teachers that provide preference labels based on ground-truth rewards (for online) and real human preference datasets (for offline). All methods are trained with the same network architectures and hyperparameters, and ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of label smoothing and policy regularization. The number of preference labels is varied to test feedback efficiency, and value estimation accuracy is measured by comparing learned Q-values to true returns.
8e4fb48e0882066cc44636fbd812607909e191a7.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel combination of label smoothing for preference-based reward learning and conservative Q-value estimation for policy regularization, specifically tailored for PbRL. The framework is general and can be integrated with any PbRL approach, supporting both discrete and continuous action spaces. The use of a dynamic graph-based replay memory for discrete settings and a log-sum-exp operator for continuous settings enables efficient and robust conservative value estimation. Empirical results demonstrate substantial improvements in feedback efficiency and policy performance over existing state-of-the-art methods, particularly under limited human feedback.
