The approach also achieves more accurate Q-function estimation, reducing overestimation bias and enhancing the reliability of policy learning in PbRL.

8e682c25e9eb8c471383151a8fed52aefb987696.title: On the Connection between Pre-training Data Diversity and Fine-tuning Robustness
8e682c25e9eb8c471383151a8fed52aefb987696.research_question: How do different properties of the pre-training data distribution influence the robustness of fine-tuned models to natural distribution shifts in downstream tasks?
8e682c25e9eb8c471383151a8fed52aefb987696.hypothesis: Increasing the quantity and granularity of pre-training data will improve the robustness of fine-tuned models to distribution shifts, while other factors such as label semantics, image diversity, and data source alignment will have limited or negligible impact when data quantity is controlled.
8e682c25e9eb8c471383151a8fed52aefb987696.proposed_method: A systematic investigation will be conducted by pre-training neural network models on datasets with controlled variations along five axes: data quantity, label granularity, label semantics, image diversity, and data source (natural vs. synthetic). For each axis, datasets such as ImageNet and iNaturalist will be manipulated to create subsets with varying class counts, label hierarchies, and per-class image diversity. Synthetic datasets will be generated using methods like Stable Diffusion and FractalDB to further probe the effects of data source and diversity. After pre-training, models will be fine-tuned on a downstream task and evaluated for robustness to distribution shifts. The methodology will ensure class balance and control for confounding variables such as total image count and label distribution.
8e682c25e9eb8c471383151a8fed52aefb987696.experiment_details: Experiments will focus on the iWildCam-WILDS wildlife classification task, using both in-distribution (ID) and out-of-distribution (OOD) test sets to assess robustness. Macro F1 score will be used as the primary evaluation metric, emphasizing performance on rare classes. Pre-training datasets will include ImageNet, iNaturalist, FractalDB-1k, and synthetic ImageNet-like data generated by Stable Diffusion, with controlled variations in class granularity, label semantics, and image diversity. Neural network architectures such as ResNet, ResNext, DenseNet, AlexNet, and MobileNet-V3 will be used, and models will be fine-tuned for varying numbers of epochs to sample a range of performances. Baselines will include models trained from scratch and models pre-trained on standard ImageNet, with linear trends and bootstrap confidence intervals used to compare effective robustness across experimental conditions.
8e682c25e9eb8c471383151a8fed52aefb987696.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a comprehensive, data-centric analysis of how pre-training data properties affect fine-tuning robustness to natural distribution shifts, moving beyond prior work focused on model architecture or training algorithms. It systematically isolates the effects of data quantity, label granularity, label semantics, image diversity, and data source, including the use of both natural and synthetic datasets. The approach provides empirical guidelines for constructing pre-training datasets to maximize downstream robustness and demonstrates that data quantity is the dominant factor, while other properties have limited impact when controlled for total data size.

8e697e2f8debd237ccebc34601e5e36142beae00.title: Large (Vision) Language Models are Unsupervised In-Context Learners
8e697e2f8debd237ccebc34601e5e36142beae00.research_question: How can large language and vision-language foundation models be adapted to new tasks in a fully unsupervised manner, without requiring manual prompt engineering or labeled examples, and can such adaptation methods outperform standard zero-shot inference and approach the performance of supervised approaches across diverse tasks and model types?
8e697e2f8debd237ccebc34601e5e36142beae00.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a joint inference framework, which makes predictions for multiple inputs simultaneously and leverages dependencies among them, can be efficiently approximated in a fully unsupervised setting. Such methods—unsupervised fine-tuning and unsupervised in-context learning—will yield substantial performance improvements over zero-shot inference and may approach supervised adaptation performance, even without access to labeled data.
8e697e2f8debd237ccebc34601e5e36142beae00.proposed_method: A joint inference framework is developed to enable fully unsupervised adaptation of foundation models to new tasks. The framework generalizes standard zero-shot inference by optimizing the joint predictive probability over multiple inputs, rather than making independent predictions. Two efficient approximation techniques are proposed: (1) Unsupervised fine-tuning, which employs a self-improvement mechanism by fine-tuning the model using its own feedback on the joint probability objective, utilizing a task encoder parameterized by LoRA and optimized via a REINFORCE-based gradient estimator with regularization to avoid degenerate solutions; and (2) Unsupervised in-context learning (ICL), which iteratively refines predictions by conditioning on the model's own outputs from previous rounds, requiring only next-token generation and no access to model weights. Both methods are compatible with close-ended tasks, and unsupervised ICL is broadly applicable to both open- and closed-weight models.
8e697e2f8debd237ccebc34601e5e36142beae00.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a wide range of tasks, including text and image classification, natural language inference, question answering, visual question answering, commonsense reasoning, and mathematical problem-solving. Datasets include standard NLP benchmarks (e.g., SST2, Amazon, AGNews, DBPedia, HellaSwag), vision datasets (e.g., CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Food101, COCO-Color, COCO-Number, VQAv2, VizWiz), and reasoning datasets (e.g., GSM8K, MMLU, MMMU). Foundation models to be evaluated include open-weight models (Llama-3.1, Qwen2.5-Math, OpenFlamingo) and closed-weight models (GPT-4o via API). Baselines will consist of zero-shot inference, zero-shot with Chain-of-Thought prompting, supervised in-context learning, and fully supervised fine-tuning. Evaluation metrics will primarily be accuracy, and experiments will systematically compare the proposed unsupervised methods to both zero-shot and supervised counterparts, with ablations on model size, instruction tuning, and test-time compute scaling.
8e697e2f8debd237ccebc34601e5e36142beae00.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled joint inference framework for unsupervised adaptation of foundation models, eliminating the need for labeled examples or manual prompt engineering. The unsupervised fine-tuning method leverages a self-improvement mechanism and efficient stochastic optimization, while the unsupervised ICL method enables broad applicability to closed-weight models and open-ended tasks. The framework demonstrates substantial improvements over zero-shot inference and often matches supervised adaptation performance, representing a significant advancement in unsupervised task adaptation for large language and vision-language models.

8e725147a29daff91d8872a699986caa2ba516bb.title: OminiControl: Minimal and Universal Control for Diffusion Transformer
8e725147a29daff91d8872a699986caa2ba516bb.research_question: How can a minimal and universal framework be developed to enable effective and flexible image control in Diffusion Transformer (DiT) models across both spatially-aligned and non-aligned conditioning tasks, while minimizing architectural complexity and parameter overhead?
8e725147a29daff91d8872a699986caa2ba516bb.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a parameter-efficient, unified sequence processing strategy—leveraging the existing VAE encoder and transformer blocks of DiT models, combined with dynamic position encoding and a flexible attention bias mechanism—can achieve state-of-the-art controllability and image quality across diverse image conditioning tasks without the need for extensive architectural modifications.
8e725147a29daff91d8872a699986caa2ba516bb.proposed_method: A new framework, OminiControl, will be developed to provide minimal and universal image control for DiT models. The method will reuse the base model's VAE encoder to process condition images, projecting them into the same latent space as noisy image tokens, and will jointly process both through the original DiT transformer blocks. Only lightweight LoRA fine-tuning will be applied to adapt the shared blocks for handling condition tokens, ensuring parameter efficiency. A unified sequence processing approach will concatenate condition tokens with noisy image tokens, enabling the multi-modal attention mechanism to flexibly discover relationships between tokens for both spatially-aligned and non-aligned tasks. Dynamic position encoding will be introduced, assigning position indices to condition tokens based on the control task (shared for aligned, shifted for non-aligned), and an attention bias mechanism will allow users to adjust the strength of conditioning at inference time by modulating cross-token attention weights.
8e725147a29daff91d8872a699986caa2ba516bb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both spatially-aligned tasks (such as Canny-to-image, depth-to-image, inpainting, and colorization) and subject-driven generation. The FLUX.1 DiT model will serve as the base, with LoRA fine-tuning for parameter efficiency. For spatially-aligned tasks, the text-to-image-2M dataset will be used, while subject-driven generation will utilize the newly created Subjects200K dataset, which contains over 200,000 identity-consistent image pairs synthesized via DiT models. Baselines will include ControlNet, T2I-Adapter, IP-Adapter, and FLUX.1 Tools, with evaluation metrics such as FID, SSIM, CLIP-IQA, MAN-IQA, MUSIQ, PSNR, and CLIP-based alignment scores. Controllability will be measured using F1 Score or MSE between generated and input conditions. Ablation studies will examine the impact of LoRA rank, condition integration depth, and critical transformer components. All experiments will be run on high-end GPUs with systematic evaluation protocols, including both automated metrics and user studies.
8e725147a29daff91d8872a699986caa2ba516bb.novelty_claims: The proposed approach claims several innovations: (1) a highly parameter-efficient control mechanism for DiT models, requiring only 0.1% additional parameters; (2) a unified sequence processing strategy that enables flexible and effective control across both spatially-aligned and non-aligned tasks within a single framework; (3) a dynamic position encoding method that adapts to the nature of the control task; (4) an attention bias mechanism for real-time adjustment of conditioning strength during inference; and (5) the creation and release of Subjects200K, a large-scale, high-quality dataset for subject-driven generation, supporting future research in this area.

8e9088c102b3714ae4e5cac7ced93a59804bfc7c.title: RewardBench: Evaluating Reward Models for Language Modeling
8e9088c102b3714ae4e5cac7ced93a59804bfc7c.research_question: How can reward models for language modeling be systematically and comprehensively evaluated across diverse tasks such as chat, reasoning, and safety, and what are the limitations and strengths of current open and closed reward models in these domains?
8e9088c102b3714ae4e5cac7ced93a59804bfc7c.hypothesis: A unified, diverse benchmark comprising structured prompt-chosen-rejected trios will enable more rigorous and granular evaluation of reward models, revealing strengths, weaknesses, and behavioral tendencies across chat, reasoning, and safety tasks, and will expose limitations in current evaluation datasets and methods.
8e9088c102b3714ae4e5cac7ced93a59804bfc7c.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation framework will be developed, centered on a new benchmark dataset containing prompt-chosen-rejected trios spanning chat, reasoning, and safety domains. The dataset will aggregate and curate challenging, structured, and out-of-distribution queries, including adversarial and subtle preference cases (e.g., buggy code, incorrect facts, or misleading refusals). The evaluation suite will support both classifier-based reward models and models trained via Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), providing a standardized inference stack and visualization tools. Each reward model will be evaluated by scoring the chosen and rejected completions for each prompt, with accuracy computed as the proportion of cases where the model assigns a higher score to the chosen completion. The framework will also include tools for analyzing reward score distributions and behavioral tendencies (e.g., refusal propensity).
8e9088c102b3714ae4e5cac7ced93a59804bfc7c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the REWARDBENCH dataset, which is divided into sections: Chat (e.g., AlpacaEval, MTBench), ChatHard (adversarial and subtle instruction-following cases), Safety (dangerous/offensive refusals, trigger word handling), Reasoning (code correctness, math reasoning), and Prior Sets (existing preference test sets such as Anthropic Helpful, SHP, and Summarize). Over 80 reward models of varying architectures and training methods (classifier-based, DPO, custom, generative) will be evaluated. Baselines will include random models and state-of-the-art open models. Evaluation metrics will primarily be accuracy (win rate), with per-section and overall weighted averages. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by using a common inference stack and by weighting sections to balance dataset size and difficulty. Additional analyses will examine scaling laws, refusal behaviors, and the impact of base model and fine-tuning variations.
8e9088c102b3714ae4e5cac7ced93a59804bfc7c.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the first comprehensive, open-source benchmark and toolkit specifically for evaluating reward models in language modeling, covering a broad spectrum of tasks and challenging cases. The dataset includes uniquely curated adversarial and subtle preference cases not present in prior evaluation sets. The evaluation suite enables direct comparison of classifier-based and DPO-trained reward models, providing insights into their generalization, reasoning, and safety behaviors. The framework also offers tools for in-depth analysis of reward score distributions and refusal behaviors, facilitating scientific understanding and future improvement of RLHF-based alignment methods.

8eac97e206dddda828c96c2db98f5281f9712419.title: IntLoRA: Integral Low-rank Adaptation of Quantized Diffusion Models
8eac97e206dddda828c96c2db98f5281f9712419.research_question: How can fine-tuning of quantized diffusion models be made both training- and inference-efficient, particularly under low-bit quantization, without incurring significant performance degradation or additional post-training quantization steps?
8eac97e206dddda828c96c2db98f5281f9712419.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that introducing integer-type low-rank adaptation parameters, together with quantization-aware training techniques and novel adaptation-quantization separation mechanisms, will enable seamless and efficient fine-tuning of quantized diffusion models, maintaining high performance even at low bit-widths and eliminating the need for post-training quantization.
8eac97e206dddda828c96c2db98f5281f9712419.proposed_method: The proposed approach, IntLoRA, will develop a framework for fine-tuning quantized diffusion models using integer-type low-rank adaptation parameters. The method introduces Adaptation-Quantization Separation (AQS), which employs a task-agnostic auxiliary matrix to enable quantization-friendly low-rank parameters while preserving the gradient trajectory of standard LoRA. A Multiplicative Low-rank Adaptation (MLA) reformulates the adaptation from an additive to a multiplicative structure, allowing independent quantization of pre-trained and adaptation weights. Variance Matching Control (VMC) is further introduced to align the distribution of the adaptation term for optimal quantization, using a variance-matched auxiliary matrix. Two implementation variants are proposed: one using uniform affine quantization for integer multiplication, and another using log2 quantization for hardware-friendly bit-shifting.
8eac97e206dddda828c96c2db98f5281f9712419.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple diffusion model adaptation tasks, including subject-driven generation (using Dreambooth), controllable generation (segmentation-to-image on ADE20K, landmark-to-face on CelebA-HQ, canny-to-image on COCO), and style-customized generation (using StyleDrop). The Stable Diffusion V1.5 and SDXL models will serve as pre-trained backbones. Baselines for comparison include LoRA (FP16), QLoRA, QA-LoRA, and IR-QLoRA, with and without additional post-training quantization. Evaluation metrics will include DINO, CLIP-I, CLIP-T, LPIPS, and FID, as well as training speed, model size, and memory usage. Both training and inference efficiency will be measured, with ablation studies on variance control and auxiliary matrix distribution. Additional experiments will validate generalization on NLP tasks (Llama3-8B on MetaMathQA/GSM8K) and compare against EfficientDM for diffusion model quantization.
8eac97e206dddda828c96c2db98f5281f9712419.novelty_claims: The proposed method claims several innovations: (1) the introduction of integer-type low-rank adaptation parameters that enable both training and inference efficiency for quantized diffusion models; (2) the Adaptation-Quantization Separation (AQS) mechanism, which decouples gradient initialization from quantization requirements; (3) the Multiplicative Low-rank Adaptation (MLA), allowing independent quantization of pre-trained and adaptation weights; (4) the Variance Matching Control (VMC) for optimal adaptation term distribution; and (5) the ability to merge adapted weights directly for quantized inference without post-training quantization, achieving state-of-the-art performance and efficiency under low-bit quantization.

8eafec7014d08043517834b5a2ed26384f188873.title: The Reversal Curse: LLMs trained on "A is B" fail to learn "B is A"
8eafec7014d08043517834b5a2ed26384f188873.research_question: Do large auto-regressive language models generalize bidirectionally from factual statements of the form 'A is B' to 'B is A', and what are the limitations of this generalization across different model architectures, training setups, and data augmentations?
8eafec7014d08043517834b5a2ed26384f188873.hypothesis: Auto-regressive large language models trained on statements of the form 'A is B' will not reliably generalize to the reversed form 'B is A', even when exposed to various data augmentations and training configurations.
8eafec7014d08043517834b5a2ed26384f188873.proposed_method: The proposed research will systematically investigate the generalization capabilities of auto-regressive language models by fine-tuning them on synthetic datasets containing factual statements in a single order (e.g., 'A is B') and evaluating their ability to infer the reversed relationship ('B is A'). Multiple experimental setups will be employed, including finetuning on both synthetic and real-world data, varying the directionality of facts, and introducing data augmentations such as paraphrasing and bidirectional examples. Additional experiments will include instruction-based datasets (e.g., question-answer pairs presented as instructions and as examples) to test generalization across different prompt formats. The methodology will also involve hyperparameter sweeps and the use of multiple model architectures and sizes to assess the robustness of the observed effects.
8eafec7014d08043517834b5a2ed26384f188873.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic datasets will consist of fictitious name-description pairs generated by large language models, with each fact paraphrased multiple times to create robust training and evaluation splits. Models such as GPT-3 (various sizes) and Llama-1 (7b, 13b, 30b, 65b) will be finetuned on these datasets in one direction and evaluated on both the same and reversed directions using held-out prompts. Evaluation metrics will include exact match accuracy and log-probability comparisons against random baselines. For real-world knowledge, a dataset of celebrity-parent pairs will be compiled, and models will be queried in both parent-to-child and child-to-parent directions. Additional experiments will use instruction-based question-answer datasets to test generalization across prompt formats. Baselines will include random guessing and models trained with both directions present in the data.
8eafec7014d08043517834b5a2ed26384f188873.novelty_claims: The research introduces a systematic investigation of the 'Reversal Curse', a fundamental failure mode in auto-regressive language models where bidirectional generalization from factual statements does not occur, even under extensive data augmentation and across model sizes and families. The proposal claims novelty in demonstrating the robustness of this failure across synthetic and real-world datasets, multiple architectures, and training regimes. It also contributes new experimental protocols for testing bidirectional generalization and highlights a basic limitation in current LLM meta-learning and logical deduction capabilities.

8eb5594ee315aee37900aefc24a0b7600feee2c8.title: PC-Conv: Unifying Homophily and Heterophily with Two-fold Filtering
8eb5594ee315aee37900aefc24a0b7600feee2c8.research_question: How can a unified graph neural network framework be developed to effectively handle node classification tasks across graphs with varying levels of homophily and heterophily?
8eb5594ee315aee37900aefc24a0b7600feee2c8.hypothesis: A two-fold filtering mechanism that simultaneously aggregates homophilic and heterophilic information, combined with a novel spectral filter approximated by Poisson-Charlier polynomials, will enable robust and state-of-the-art node classification performance on both homophilic and heterophilic graphs.
8eb5594ee315aee37900aefc24a0b7600feee2c8.proposed_method: A novel two-fold filtering mechanism will be developed to simultaneously perform homophilic (local, low-pass) and heterophilic (global, high-pass) aggregation on graph data. The approach extends the graph heat equation to heterophilic graphs, enabling global information aggregation via a heterophilic graph heat kernel. This kernel will be integrated with a local low-pass filter to form a new spectral filter, which is exactly approximated using Poisson-Charlier (PC) polynomials. To capture multi-order information, a filter bank with adaptive, learnable coefficients will be constructed, resulting in the PC-Conv operation. The final architecture, PCNet, will instantiate PC-Conv within a simple GNN framework for node classification, incorporating generalized Laplacian normalization and identity mapping to ensure expressive and stable representations.
8eb5594ee315aee37900aefc24a0b7600feee2c8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of benchmark datasets, including both homophilic (Cora, CiteSeer, PubMed) and heterophilic (Texas, Cornell, Wisconsin, Actor, Penn94) graphs. The evaluation will use semi-supervised node classification tasks, with both random and fixed train/validation/test splits to ensure fair comparison. Baselines will include a wide range of polynomial-based spectral GNNs (e.g., GCN, ChebNet, ARMA, APPNP, GPRGNN, BernNet, ChebNetII, JacobiConv), as well as recent heterophilic GNNs (e.g., H2GCN, WRGAT, GloGNN++, GGCN, ACM-GCN, LINKX). Performance will be measured using mean classification accuracy and 95% confidence intervals. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the contributions of the two-fold filtering, PC-filter, Laplacian normalization, and identity mapping. Computational complexity and scalability will also be analyzed.
8eb5594ee315aee37900aefc24a0b7600feee2c8.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a unified two-fold filtering mechanism that enables simultaneous homophilic and heterophilic aggregation, addressing the limitations of existing GNNs that specialize in only one regime. The extension of the graph heat kernel to heterophilic graphs and its integration with a local low-pass filter is novel, as is the exact spectral approximation using Poisson-Charlier polynomials. The PC-Conv operation provides a highly expressive, adaptive filter bank capable of learning complex spectral responses, including both local and global information. The resulting PCNet architecture demonstrates state-of-the-art performance and stability across diverse graph types, outperforming both homophilic and heterophilic GNN baselines. The approach is computationally efficient and generalizes well to real-world graphs with mixed homophily and heterophily.

8eb99f1ed884356871ddbcf1377b82359071906a.title: LanguageBind: Extending Video-Language Pretraining to N-modality by Language-based Semantic Alignment
8eb99f1ed884356871ddbcf1377b82359071906a.research_question: How can video-language pretraining frameworks be extended to support semantic alignment across an arbitrary number (N) of modalities, leveraging language as a central binding modality, and what are the implications for downstream multi-modal understanding tasks?
8eb99f1ed884356871ddbcf1377b82359071906a.hypothesis: Directly aligning all modalities to a shared language-based semantic space, rather than using vision as an intermediary, will enable more effective and scalable multi-modal pretraining, resulting in improved performance on a wide range of downstream tasks involving video, audio, depth, infrared, and other modalities.
8eb99f1ed884356871ddbcf1377b82359071906a.proposed_method: A new multi-modal pretraining framework, LanguageBind, will be developed in which language serves as the central modality for semantic alignment. The language encoder, pretrained via video-language contrastive learning, will be frozen, and modality-specific encoders (for video, infrared, depth, audio, etc.) will be trained to align their representations directly with the language space using contrastive learning objectives. Each non-language encoder will be initialized from large-scale pretrained models (e.g., OpenCLIP), and fine-tuned using the Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) technique to improve efficiency and reduce computational cost. Patch masking will be applied to visual modalities for efficient token processing, and audio will be converted to spectrograms and processed similarly. The framework will support modular extension to additional modalities by training new encoders to align with the frozen language space.
8eb99f1ed884356871ddbcf1377b82359071906a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a newly constructed large-scale dataset, VIDAL-10M, containing 10 million aligned data pairs across five modalities: video, infrared, depth, audio, and language. Downstream evaluations will include zero-shot retrieval and classification tasks across 15 benchmarks, such as MSR-VTT, MSVD, DiDeMo, ActivityNet (video-text retrieval), LLVIP and NYU-D (depth/infrared classification), ESC-50 and AudioSet (audio classification), and others. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art multi-modal pretraining models such as ImageBind, OpenCLIP, InterVideo, and VALOR. Evaluation metrics will include recall at K (R@1, R@5, R@10), mean average precision (mAP), and top-1 accuracy, depending on the task. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of training strategies, batch size, LoRA rank, temperature, and masking ratio.
8eb99f1ed884356871ddbcf1377b82359071906a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a direct language-based semantic alignment mechanism for N-modal pretraining, eliminating the need for vision as an intermediary and enabling straightforward extensibility to new modalities. The method leverages a frozen language encoder and efficient LoRA-based fine-tuning for scalable training. Additionally, the creation of VIDAL-10M represents the first large-scale multi-modal dataset with direct alignment to language across video, infrared, depth, and audio. The approach claims superior performance over existing methods on a wide range of downstream tasks, and demonstrates emergent capabilities in indirect modality alignment and multi-modal complementarity.

8ecbdc1adcd7223db9849bf926eb47b4434fd624.title: Optimizing ML Training with Metagradient Descent
8ecbdc1adcd7223db9849bf926eb47b4434fd624.research_question: How can machine learning training configurations, including data selection, hyperparameter tuning, and robustness to data poisoning, be optimized efficiently and scalably using gradient-based methods over the space of metaparameters?
8ecbdc1adcd7223db9849bf926eb47b4434fd624.hypothesis: Gradient-based optimization over metaparameters, enabled by scalable and efficient computation of metagradients and the design of metasmooth training routines, will outperform traditional search-based or heuristic approaches in configuring large-scale machine learning training setups.
8ecbdc1adcd7223db9849bf926eb47b4434fd624.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed for optimizing machine learning training configurations by treating the selection of metaparameters (such as data subsets, hyperparameters, and architectural choices) as a continuous, high-dimensional optimization problem. The core technical contribution is the REPLAY algorithm, which efficiently and exactly computes metagradients (gradients through the entire training process) at scale by combining reverse-mode autodifferentiation with a recursive segment-tree-like data structure, requiring only O(k log_k(T)) storage and compute overhead. To ensure that metagradients are useful for optimization, a 'metasmooth' training routine is designed, modifying standard learning algorithms to improve the smoothness of the metaparameter optimization landscape. Empirical metrics for metasmoothness are introduced to guide the design of training routines that admit effective gradient-based optimization.
8ecbdc1adcd7223db9849bf926eb47b4434fd624.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across several machine learning tasks: (1) pre-training data selection for multimodal models using the DataComp-small benchmark for CLIP, (2) data selection for instruction tuning on large language models such as Gemma-2B, (3) robustness to accuracy-degrading data poisoning attacks on CIFAR-10, and (4) hyperparameter optimization for learning rate schedules on CIFAR-10. For each task, the method frames the problem as metaparameter optimization, applies metasmooth modifications to the training routine, and performs metagradient descent (MGD) using REPLAY. Baselines include existing state-of-the-art data selection methods, standard grid search for hyperparameters, and previous data poisoning attacks. Evaluation metrics include model accuracy, robustness to poisoning (drop in test accuracy), and performance improvement over baselines. Experimental setups involve large-scale models (e.g., CLIP, Gemma-2B), standard datasets (CIFAR-10), and competitive benchmarks (DataComp-small).
8ecbdc1adcd7223db9849bf926eb47b4434fd624.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first scalable, exact algorithm (REPLAY) for computing metagradients through large-scale model training, enabling practical gradient-based optimization over metaparameters. The framework for designing metasmooth training routines is novel and provides a principled way to ensure that metagradients are effective for optimization. The method achieves state-of-the-art results in data selection and data poisoning tasks, surpassing previous methods by significant margins. Additionally, the approach is demonstrated to automatically discover competitive hyperparameter schedules, offering a unified, gradient-based alternative to traditional search and heuristic methods for configuring machine learning training.

8ed7e26223c1d606c3074c6fe9250692da4071f2.title: In or Out? Fixing ImageNet Out-of-Distribution Detection Evaluation
8ed7e26223c1d606c3074c6fe9250692da4071f2.research_question: How can out-of-distribution (OOD) detection for ImageNet-1K be evaluated in a way that avoids contamination from in-distribution (ID) objects, and what are the true strengths and weaknesses of current OOD detection methods and models when evaluated on a rigorously curated OOD benchmark?
8ed7e26223c1d606c3074c6fe9250692da4071f2.hypothesis: Current OOD detection evaluations for ImageNet-1K are systematically biased due to the presence of ID objects in supposed OOD datasets, leading to underestimation of OOD detector performance and unfair penalization of stronger models. By constructing a contamination-free OOD benchmark and synthetic unit-tests, it is possible to more accurately assess and improve OOD detection methods.
8ed7e26223c1d606c3074c6fe9250692da4071f2.proposed_method: A novel OOD evaluation framework will be developed by constructing a new benchmark dataset, NINCO, consisting of 64 OOD classes and 5879 images that are individually verified to be free of any ImageNet-1K class objects. The dataset will be sourced from a variety of existing datasets and web sources, with each image manually inspected using WordNet glosses, taxonomy, and visual confirmation to ensure no ID contamination. Additionally, a suite of synthetic 'OOD unit-tests' will be created to probe specific failure modes of OOD detectors, such as monochrome images or corrupted inputs. The evaluation protocol will require reporting both aggregate and per-class metrics, as well as pass/fail statistics on unit-tests, to provide a comprehensive understanding of detector robustness.
8ed7e26223c1d606c3074c6fe9250692da4071f2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a broad set of deep neural network architectures, including Vision Transformers (ViT), ResNets, EfficientNets, ConvNext, and models with various pretraining strategies (e.g., ImageNet-21K, JFT-300M, CLIP). Eleven state-of-the-art OOD detection methods will be evaluated, spanning both logit-based and feature-based approaches (e.g., MSP, Mahalanobis, ViM, MaxLogit, Energy, KNN, Cosine similarity, and more). The evaluation will use the NINCO dataset and the OOD unit-tests, as well as cleaned versions of previously used OOD benchmarks. Performance will be measured primarily by the false positive rate (FPR) at 95% true positive rate (TPR), with additional reporting of mean FPR across OOD classes and the number of failed unit-tests (FPR > 10%). Comparative analysis will be performed to assess the impact of pretraining, model architecture, and OOD detection method on both natural and synthetic OOD inputs.
8ed7e26223c1d606c3074c6fe9250692da4071f2.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first rigorously curated, contamination-free OOD benchmark for ImageNet-1K (NINCO), enabling fair and accurate evaluation of OOD detectors. The methodology includes comprehensive manual verification of OOD samples, fine-grained class resolution, and the introduction of synthetic unit-tests to reveal specific detector weaknesses. The evaluation protocol emphasizes transparency and robustness by requiring per-class and unit-test reporting, which exposes previously hidden failure modes and biases in OOD detection. This approach is expected to set a new standard for OOD evaluation in large-scale image classification.

8ee45aeb7c97e3346cc62f216f673b91277ac718.title: LLM-Planner: Few-Shot Grounded Planning for Embodied Agents with Large Language Models
8ee45aeb7c97e3346cc62f216f673b91277ac718.research_question: How can large language models be leveraged to enable embodied agents to efficiently and robustly follow natural language instructions for complex tasks in visually-perceived, partially-observable environments, with minimal paired training data?
8ee45aeb7c97e3346cc62f216f673b91277ac718.hypothesis: Large language models, when used as high-level planners and enhanced with physical grounding and dynamic re-planning based on environmental perception, can enable embodied agents to achieve competitive task performance in complex environments using only a small fraction of paired training data.
8ee45aeb7c97e3346cc62f216f673b91277ac718.proposed_method: A hierarchical planning framework will be developed in which a large language model (LLM), such as GPT-3, is prompted to generate high-level plans (HLPs) as sequences of subgoals from natural language instructions. The method will employ in-context learning with a small number of paired instruction-plan examples, dynamically retrieved using a k-nearest-neighbor (kNN) retriever based on BERT embeddings. To ensure plans are grounded in the agent's current environment, a grounded re-planning algorithm will be introduced: as the agent executes the plan, if progress stalls or failures occur, the LLM will be re-prompted with updated information about observed objects and completed subgoals to generate a revised plan. Logit biases will be applied to prioritize objects present in the environment, improving the relevance of generated subgoals. The low-level planner will map each subgoal to primitive actions using existing modules trained on synthetic data, requiring no additional paired language-action data.
8ee45aeb7c97e3346cc62f216f673b91277ac718.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ALFRED dataset, which features diverse, partially-observable household environments and long-horizon tasks. The proposed method will be integrated with a strong baseline agent (HLSM), replacing its high-level planner with the LLM-based module. Less than 0.5% of the available paired training data will be used for few-shot learning, with in-context examples dynamically selected for each test instance. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art hierarchical planners (e.g., HLSM, FILM), both retrained under the same few-shot regime and in their original full-data configurations, as well as ranking-based LLM planners such as SayCan. Evaluation metrics will include task success rate (SR), goal-condition completion rate (GC), and a newly proposed high-level planning accuracy (HLP ACC), measured on both seen and unseen test splits. The experimental setup will adhere to a true few-shot protocol, using cross-validation on the small training set for prompt and model selection.
8ee45aeb7c97e3346cc62f216f673b91277ac718.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a generative LLM-based high-level planner for embodied agents that requires no prior knowledge of environment-specific admissible actions, enabling dynamic, grounded re-planning based on real-time perception. Unlike prior methods, the framework achieves strong performance in complex, partially-observable environments with minimal paired data, and demonstrates substantial improvements over both static LLM planning and ranking-based LLM planners. The method also proposes a simple yet effective mechanism for grounding LLM outputs using observed object lists and logit biases, and establishes a new benchmark for few-shot embodied planning on the ALFRED dataset.

8eeccf1033fd759c868b29ccb6aa70f5ffd1887c.title: TD-MPC2: Scalable, Robust World Models for Continuous Control
8eeccf1033fd759c868b29ccb6aa70f5ffd1887c.research_question: How can a scalable and robust model-based reinforcement learning algorithm be developed to enable generalist agents to perform a wide variety of continuous control tasks across multiple domains, embodiments, and action spaces, using large, uncurated datasets and a single set of hyperparameters?
8eeccf1033fd759c868b29ccb6aa70f5ffd1887c.hypothesis: A model-based reinforcement learning algorithm that leverages an implicit, control-centric world model, improved architectural robustness, and scalable design can enable a single agent to efficiently and robustly solve diverse continuous control tasks across multiple domains, without task-specific hyperparameter tuning, and with improved performance as model and data size increase.
8eeccf1033fd759c868b29ccb6aa70f5ffd1887c.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces TD-MPC2, a model-based reinforcement learning algorithm that builds upon local trajectory optimization in the latent space of a learned implicit (decoder-free) world model. The architecture consists of five core components: an encoder mapping observations to latent representations, a latent dynamics model for forward prediction, reward and terminal value predictors, and a policy prior for action selection. All components are conditioned on learnable task embeddings to support multi-task learning. The model is trained using a joint objective combining joint-embedding prediction, reward prediction, and temporal-difference (TD) learning, with reward and value prediction formulated as discrete regression in a log-transformed space. Simplicial normalization (SimNorm) is applied to latent representations to ensure training stability and sparsity, and an ensemble of Q-functions is used to reduce bias in TD-targets. For decision-making, the method employs Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control in the latent space, leveraging the policy prior to guide sampling and accelerate planning. Action and observation spaces are zero-padded and masked to accommodate diverse task domains without domain-specific knowledge.
8eeccf1033fd759c868b29ccb6aa70f5ffd1887c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across 104 diverse continuous control tasks from four domains: DMControl, Meta-World, ManiSkill2, and MyoSuite, encompassing high-dimensional state and action spaces, image-based observations, sparse rewards, and various embodiments. Baselines for comparison include state-of-the-art model-free (SAC), model-based (DreamerV3, TD-MPC), and visual RL methods (CURL, DrQ-v2), with TD-MPC2 using a single set of hyperparameters for all tasks. Evaluation metrics include episode return and success rate, normalized across tasks. Scaling experiments will train multi-task agents with up to 317M parameters on datasets containing hundreds of millions of transitions from a wide range of behaviors. Additional ablation studies will assess the impact of architectural and algorithmic choices, and few-shot learning experiments will evaluate the ability to adapt pre-trained multi-task agents to new tasks with limited data.
8eeccf1033fd759c868b29ccb6aa70f5ffd1887c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach claims several innovations: (1) a scalable, robust model-based RL algorithm capable of handling over 100 diverse continuous control tasks with a single set of hyperparameters; (2) the use of an implicit, control-centric world model trained without observation reconstruction, enabling efficient learning from large, uncurated datasets; (3) architectural improvements including SimNorm for stable training and learnable task embeddings for multi-task generalization; (4) demonstration of consistent performance improvements with increased model and data size, including successful training of a single 317M parameter agent on 80 tasks; (5) robust handling of varying observation and action spaces without domain-specific knowledge; and (6) empirical evidence of state-of-the-art data efficiency and robustness compared to existing model-free and model-based RL methods.

8efd94272edfa09045a7caf31fdb7577977d5748.title: Advantage Alignment Algorithms
8efd94272edfa09045a7caf31fdb7577977d5748.research_question: How can reinforcement learning agents in general-sum, multi-agent environments be enabled to autonomously align their interests for mutually beneficial outcomes, particularly in social dilemmas, while maintaining scalability, computational efficiency, and robustness to exploitation?
8efd94272edfa09045a7caf31fdb7577977d5748.hypothesis: Aligning the advantages of interacting agents, such that the probability of mutually beneficial actions increases when historic interactions have been positive, will result in more cooperative, robust, and scalable policies in general-sum multi-agent reinforcement learning environments compared to existing opponent shaping methods.
8efd94272edfa09045a7caf31fdb7577977d5748.proposed_method: A family of algorithms, termed Advantage Alignment, will be developed to perform opponent shaping by aligning the advantages of interacting agents. The core principle is to increase the log probability of an agent's action proportionally to the product of its own and its opponent's advantages, especially when past interactions have been positive. This is operationalized by modifying the policy gradient update to include an opponent shaping term, estimated efficiently from single trajectories using REINFORCE-style estimators. A scalable variant, Proximal Advantage Alignment (PAA), will be formulated by integrating the modified advantage into the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) surrogate objective, enabling application to high-dimensional, continuous action spaces and complex multi-agent environments. The method will be theoretically analyzed to ensure preservation of Nash equilibria and to unify the mechanisms underlying existing opponent shaping algorithms such as LOLA and LOQA.
8efd94272edfa09045a7caf31fdb7577977d5748.experiment_details: The proposed algorithms will be evaluated across a suite of social dilemma environments, including the full-history Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma (IPD) with GRU-based policies, the Coin Game (a 3x3 gridworld with color-coded rewards and penalties), a continuous-action Negotiation Game (with public values and simultaneous proposals), and the large-scale, partially observable Commons Harvest Open environment from Melting Pot 2.0. Baselines will include LOLA, LOQA, POLA, MFOS, PPO, PPO with shared rewards, and prosocial variants, among others. Evaluation metrics will focus on cooperation rates, robustness to exploitation, and normalized per capita returns, following established protocols such as zero-shot evaluation against policy distributions and league-based head-to-head matches. Experimental setups will involve multiple random seeds, trajectory lengths, and context windows, with architectures ranging from recurrent policies to GTrXL transformers for high-dimensional settings.
8efd94272edfa09045a7caf31fdb7577977d5748.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces Advantage Alignment and Proximal Advantage Alignment, providing a first-principles derivation that unifies and generalizes existing opponent shaping algorithms. The method simplifies the mathematical formulation of opponent shaping, reduces computational burden, and extends applicability to continuous action domains and high-dimensional, partially observable environments. Theoretical analysis demonstrates preservation of Nash equilibria, and empirical results are expected to achieve state-of-the-art cooperation and robustness in both classical and large-scale social dilemmas, showcasing scalability and effectiveness beyond prior methods.

8efe43e92e0066739f03056a199a5c89aac8fa91.title: Scaling Inference-Efficient Language Models
8efe43e92e0066739f03056a199a5c89aac8fa91.research_question: How can language model scaling laws be extended to explicitly account for inference efficiency, enabling the design of models that optimize both accuracy and inference latency under practical constraints such as device memory and dataset size?
8efe43e92e0066739f03056a199a5c89aac8fa91.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that incorporating model architecture parameters (such as width and depth) into scaling laws, alongside model size and training tokens, will enable the identification and training of language models that achieve superior inference efficiency (lower latency) without sacrificing downstream task accuracy, compared to models designed under traditional scaling laws.
8efe43e92e0066739f03056a199a5c89aac8fa91.proposed_method: A new inference-efficient scaling law will be developed by extending the Chinchilla scaling law to include model architecture parameters, specifically the aspect ratio of hidden size to number of layers. The proposed law will take the form L(N, D, R) = (E + A*N^-α + B*D^-β) * (1 + ε*R^γ), where N is the number of parameters, D is the number of training tokens, R is the aspect ratio (hidden size divided by number of layers), and A, B, E, α, β, γ, ε are learned parameters. The methodology will involve training a diverse set of transformer-based language models with varying sizes (80M to 1B+ parameters), training tokens (1.6B to 30B), and architectural shapes, measuring both training loss and inference latency. A model selection algorithm will be established that ranks candidate architectures based on predicted loss and measured inference latency, selecting top candidates for full training and downstream evaluation.
8efe43e92e0066739f03056a199a5c89aac8fa91.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training over 60 transformer-based decoder-only language models, varying model size, number of layers, hidden size, and number of training tokens, using a uniformly sampled subset of the DCLM-Baseline dataset. Inference latency will be measured using HuggingFace's generate function on a single NVIDIA Ampere 40GB A100 GPU, with batch size 1, input length 128, and output length 256. Downstream task accuracy will be evaluated using zero-shot protocols on datasets including ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, BoolQ, COPA, HellaSwag, LAMBADA, PIQA, WinoGrande, MMLU, Jeopardy, and Winograd. Baseline comparisons will include open-source models such as Open-LM-1B, OPT-1.3B, Pythia-1.3B, and Neox-1.3B. Evaluation metrics will include training loss, inference latency, throughput, accuracy on downstream tasks, mean squared error (MSE) and R^2 for scaling law fit, and Spearman's rank correlation for model ranking.
8efe43e92e0066739f03056a199a5c89aac8fa91.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces an inference-efficient scaling law that, for the first time, explicitly incorporates model architecture parameters (aspect ratio) into the scaling law framework for language models. It claims to provide a practical methodology for jointly optimizing model accuracy and inference latency, enabling the design of models that achieve better accuracy-latency trade-offs than those guided by traditional scaling laws. The approach is validated through extensive empirical studies, demonstrating more accurate prediction of optimal model configurations and the release of a new model (Morph-1B) that achieves 1.8× lower inference latency while maintaining accuracy compared to similarly sized open-source models. The methodology is robust, data-efficient, and can be extended to evaluate future architectural optimizations.

8f2254fb38cfc8f79524fd1cd2609124808f2c8c.title: Token-level Direct Preference Optimization
8f2254fb38cfc8f79524fd1cd2609124808f2c8c.research_question: How can large language models be fine-tuned to achieve improved alignment with human preferences while maintaining or enhancing generation diversity, particularly by optimizing alignment objectives at a more granular, token-level rather than at the sentence or response level?
8f2254fb38cfc8f79524fd1cd2609124808f2c8c.hypothesis: Introducing token-level optimization with forward KL divergence constraints, combined with a token-level preference model, will enable large language models to achieve superior alignment with human preferences and better control over generation diversity compared to existing sentence-level alignment methods.
8f2254fb38cfc8f79524fd1cd2609124808f2c8c.proposed_method: A novel fine-tuning approach, Token-level Direct Preference Optimization (TDPO), will be developed to align large language models with human preferences at the token level. The method will reformulate the reward maximization problem into a sequential, token-level objective, leveraging the Bellman equation to connect sentence-level rewards with token-level generation. The Bradley-Terry model will be adapted for token-based reward modeling, establishing equivalence with the Regret Preference Model, and forward KL divergence constraints will be incorporated for each token to regulate divergence and preserve diversity. The loss function will be designed to balance alignment and diversity by introducing a parameterized control over the difference in sequential KL divergence between preferred and dispreferred responses, and gradient updates will be carefully managed to ensure effective training dynamics.
8f2254fb38cfc8f79524fd1cd2609124808f2c8c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple open-source datasets, including the IMDb sentiment dataset (for controlled sentiment generation), the Anthropic HH dataset (for single-turn dialogue), and MT-Bench (for multi-turn open-ended question answering). Baseline methods will include DPO, PPO-based RLHF, and f-DPO with forward KL constraints. Evaluation metrics will comprise alignment accuracy (e.g., matching chosen completions), diversity (e.g., predictive entropy with nucleus sampling), sequential KL divergence, and win rates against human-preferred responses as judged by GPT-4. Reference and policy models will be initialized from established checkpoints (e.g., GPT-2 Large, Pythia-2.8B), and fine-tuning will be performed with consistent hyperparameters (e.g., temperature, maximum token length, learning rates). The effectiveness of TDPO will be assessed by comparing the alignment-diversity trade-off frontiers, KL divergence control, and overall response quality against baselines.
8f2254fb38cfc8f79524fd1cd2609124808f2c8c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first token-level direct preference optimization framework for large language models, enabling fine-grained alignment with human preferences by directly optimizing at the token level rather than the sentence level. The method innovatively integrates forward KL divergence constraints at each token, improving regulation of divergence and generation diversity without the need for explicit reward modeling. By reformulating the Bradley-Terry model for token-level application and introducing a parameterized loss function for balancing alignment and diversity, the approach achieves superior performance in both alignment and diversity compared to existing DPO and PPO-based RLHF methods. The methodology also provides new insights into controlling divergence efficiency and addresses limitations of mode-seeking behavior in previous alignment algorithms.

8f3b40d23e5a38d11ce89a4ca8d3227d4bd4d90b.title: SE(3) diffusion model with application to protein backbone generation
8f3b40d23e5a38d11ce89a4ca8d3227d4bd4d90b.research_question: How can a principled, SE(3)-invariant diffusion model be developed for generating novel, functional protein backbones, and what are the implications for designability, diversity, and novelty of generated structures compared to existing methods?
8f3b40d23e5a38d11ce89a4ca8d3227d4bd4d90b.hypothesis: A theoretically grounded SE(3)-invariant diffusion model operating on protein backbone frames will enable the generation of diverse, designable, and novel protein structures without requiring pretraining on protein structure prediction networks.
8f3b40d23e5a38d11ce89a4ca8d3227d4bd4d90b.proposed_method: A novel generative framework, FrameDiff, is proposed for protein backbone generation based on SE(3)-invariant diffusion processes over multiple frames. The method constructs a forward diffusion process on SE(3)^N, the space of orientation-preserving rigid motions for N residues, by separating translation and rotation components and ensuring invariance through centering the process at the origin. The reverse (generative) process is parameterized using a neural network based on the AlphaFold2 structure module, which predicts denoised frames and torsion angles for each residue. Denoising score matching is used for training, with explicit computation of the Riemannian gradients and Brownian motions on SE(3), and the neural network is constrained to be SO(3)-equivariant to guarantee invariance. Auxiliary losses are incorporated to penalize atomic errors and improve fine-grained physical plausibility, and sampling is performed via an Euler–Maruyama discretization of the reverse SDE, with noise scaling and center-of-mass projection to maintain invariance.
8f3b40d23e5a38d11ce89a4ca8d3227d4bd4d90b.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on monomeric protein backbone generation using a filtered set of 20,312 backbones from the Protein Data Bank (PDB) as training data. The model, with 17.4 million parameters, is trained on two A100 GPUs for one week. Evaluation focuses on designability (using self-consistency with ProteinMPNN for sequence design and ESMFold for structure prediction, measured by TM-score and C-alpha RMSD), diversity (number of unique structural clusters via MaxCluster at a 0.5 TM-score threshold), and novelty (maximum TM-score to any known PDB structure via FoldSeek). Baselines for comparison include Chroma and RFdiffusion, with attention to differences in training and evaluation protocols. Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of auxiliary losses, self-conditioning, and loss formulations. Sampling parameters such as noise scale, number of diffusion steps, and number of sequences per backbone are varied to assess their effects on performance metrics.
8f3b40d23e5a38d11ce89a4ca8d3227d4bd4d90b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach establishes the theoretical foundations for SE(3)-invariant diffusion models on multiple frames, enabling principled and tractable training for protein backbone generation. FrameDiff is the first method to generate designable, diverse, and novel protein monomers up to 500 residues without relying on pretraining with structure prediction networks. The framework provides explicit mathematical treatment of Brownian motion and score matching on SE(3), and introduces a neural architecture that is both SE(3)-equivariant and efficient. The method demonstrates competitive or superior performance to prior non-pretrained diffusion models, and offers significant computational advantages and theoretical clarity over heuristic or pretraining-dependent approaches.

8f3d959238e67bf6b9bc9818025d0d2e403e478f.title: DuoAttention: Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference with Retrieval and Streaming Heads
8f3d959238e67bf6b9bc9818025d0d2e403e478f.research_question: How can the computational and memory efficiency of large language models (LLMs) be improved for long-context inference without compromising their ability to process and retrieve information from extensive input sequences?
8f3d959238e67bf6b9bc9818025d0d2e403e478f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that only a subset of attention heads in LLMs—termed retrieval heads—are essential for maintaining long-context capabilities, and that restricting the Key-Value (KV) cache for the remaining streaming heads to a constant size will significantly reduce memory and computation requirements while preserving accuracy.
8f3d959238e67bf6b9bc9818025d0d2e403e478f.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a dual-attention framework, DuoAttention, which categorizes attention heads in each Transformer layer as either retrieval heads or streaming heads. Retrieval heads are identified via an optimization-based algorithm that measures the output deviation caused by KV cache pruning, using a synthetic dataset designed for long-context retrieval tasks. During inference, full KV caches are maintained only for retrieval heads, while streaming heads utilize a lightweight, constant-length KV cache that stores only recent tokens and attention sinks. This approach is implemented by assigning a trainable gate value to each head, optimizing these gates to minimize output deviation from the full-attention model, and binarizing the gates for deployment. The method is compatible with chunked pre-filling, quantization, and both multi-head and grouped-query attention architectures.
8f3d959238e67bf6b9bc9818025d0d2e403e478f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both long-context and short-context benchmarks. Long-context evaluation will use the Needle-in-a-Haystack (NIAH) benchmark and LongBench, while short-context tasks will include MMLU, MBPP, and MT-Bench. State-of-the-art open-source LLMs such as Llama-2-7B, Llama-3-8B, Llama-3-70B, and Mistral-7B will be used. Baselines for comparison will include H2O, TOVA, FastGen, and StreamingLLM, with all methods evaluated under equivalent KV cache budgets. Evaluation metrics will include retrieval accuracy, memory usage, and decoding/pre-filling latency, with experiments run on NVIDIA A100 GPUs. Implementation details include the use of PyTorch, FlashAttention-2, and QServe quantization for some experiments.
8f3d959238e67bf6b9bc9818025d0d2e403e478f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel, optimization-based method for identifying retrieval heads using synthetic data and output deviation metrics, rather than relying solely on attention scores. DuoAttention is the first to combine selective full KV caching for retrieval heads with constant-size caching for streaming heads, yielding substantial memory and latency reductions in long-context inference. The method is fully compatible with existing optimization techniques such as quantization and chunked pre-filling, and demonstrates superior trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy compared to prior KV cache compression methods. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of the retrieval head identification strategy and the necessity of combining sink and recent token attention.

8f4358ee06b8ecbff57b0c2f08bf801f0836b6e2.title: Dynamic Sparsity Is Channel-Level Sparsity Learner
8f4358ee06b8ecbff57b0c2f08bf801f0836b6e2.research_question: How can the benefits of dynamic sparse training be translated into hardware-friendly, channel-level sparsity to achieve efficient training and inference on common GPU devices without sacrificing model accuracy?
8f4358ee06b8ecbff57b0c2f08bf801f0836b6e2.hypothesis: Dynamic sparse training inherently leads to biased parameter reallocation across channels, resulting in a significant proportion of channels becoming sparser than others early in training. By identifying and removing these 'sparse amenable channels' using an appropriate metric, it is possible to convert unstructured sparsity into structured, channel-level sparsity, enabling efficient acceleration on standard hardware while maintaining or improving model performance.
8f4358ee06b8ecbff57b0c2f08bf801f0836b6e2.proposed_method: A novel sparse training framework, Channel-aware dynamic sparse (Chase), will be developed to progressively translate unstructured dynamic sparsity into channel-level sparsity during end-to-end training. The method will monitor the Unmasked Mean Magnitude (UMM) of each channel to identify 'sparse amenable channels'—those that become significantly sparser than their initialization. Gradual channel pruning will be performed during training by removing channels with the lowest UMM scores according to a controlled sparsification schedule, while global parameter exploration will redistribute pruned parameters to important channels using magnitude and gradient information. A soft memory bound will be employed, allowing parameter growth before pruning to improve performance and stability. The final model will be a compact, channel-sparse network that can be directly accelerated on commodity GPUs.
8f4358ee06b8ecbff57b0c2f08bf801f0836b6e2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard deep learning benchmarks, including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet, using architectures such as VGG-19 and ResNet-50. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art dynamic sparse training (DST) baselines (e.g., RigL, SET, MEST, SNFS, DSR) and channel pruning algorithms (e.g., Network Slimming). Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy, inference throughput, and latency on GPU hardware (e.g., NVIDIA 2080TI), as well as theoretical and GPU-supported FLOPs. Both unstructured and structured (channel-level) sparsity variants will be tested at various sparsity levels (e.g., 90%, 95%, 98%), with ablation studies to analyze the impact of key components such as gradual channel pruning, global parameter exploration, and soft memory bound.
8f4358ee06b8ecbff57b0c2f08bf801f0836b6e2.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to seamlessly convert unstructured dynamic sparsity into channel-level sparsity during training, enabling direct acceleration on commodity GPUs without specialized hardware or ad-hoc post-processing. A new metric, Unmasked Mean Magnitude (UMM), is introduced for precise identification of sparse amenable channels. The method demonstrates that channel-level sparsity can be achieved without compromising accuracy, often surpassing state-of-the-art DST methods in both performance and real-world inference speedup. This challenges the prevailing belief that sparse training is limited by hardware support, opening new directions for efficient sparse neural network design.

8f490b938586d8e1b892304dd5209b2295c93ed7.title: Transformers Can Achieve Length Generalization But Not Robustly
8f490b938586d8e1b892304dd5209b2295c93ed7.research_question: Can Transformer-based models be enabled to generalize to sequence lengths significantly longer than those seen during training, and what factors influence the robustness of this length generalization?
8f490b938586d8e1b892304dd5209b2295c93ed7.hypothesis: With a carefully designed combination of position encoding and data formatting, standard Transformer architectures can achieve strong length generalization on algorithmic tasks such as integer addition, but the robustness of this generalization is sensitive to factors such as random weight initialization and training data order.
8f490b938586d8e1b892304dd5209b2295c93ed7.proposed_method: A new approach is developed that combines advanced position encoding and data formatting strategies to enhance length generalization in Transformers. Specifically, the method integrates FIRE position encodings, which are more expressive and adaptable for length extrapolation, with randomized position encodings to prevent overfitting to specific positional indices. The data is formatted in a reversed order to align with the natural computation of addition and is augmented with index hints to facilitate precise operand identification. Ablation studies will be conducted to isolate the impact of each component, and the model architecture will be based on a 25M-parameter Transformer with RMSNorm and the Primer architecture's normalization scheme.
8f490b938586d8e1b892304dd5209b2295c93ed7.experiment_details: Experiments will focus on the N-digit decimal addition task, training models on sequences of up to 40 digits and testing on sequences up to 100 digits to assess out-of-distribution generalization. The training dataset will comprise 30 million examples with input lengths from 1 to 40, and evaluation will use 1,000 examples per input length. Baselines will include models with alternative position encodings (Absolute, NoPE, RoPE, KerpleLog) and data formats (standard, reversed, with/without index hints). Evaluation metrics will primarily be exact match accuracy on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution test sets. Each experiment will be repeated across multiple random seeds and data orders to assess robustness, and additional experiments will vary model size, regularization (weight decay, dropout), and training sequence length.
8f490b938586d8e1b892304dd5209b2295c93ed7.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel combination of FIRE and randomized position encodings with reversed data format and index hints, enabling standard Transformers to generalize to sequence lengths 2.5× longer than those seen during training—substantially surpassing prior benchmarks. The approach provides a systematic empirical recipe for achieving strong length generalization in algorithmic tasks. Additionally, the research highlights and analyzes the fragility of this generalization, showing for the first time that it is highly sensitive to random initialization and data order, thus uncovering critical limitations in the robustness of Transformer length generalization.

8f5562ead9861744a1192c1bef69283e25200aa8.title: Parallel Bayesian Optimization of Multiple Noisy Objectives with Expected Hypervolume Improvement
8f5562ead9861744a1192c1bef69283e25200aa8.research_question: How can parallel Bayesian optimization be effectively performed for multiple noisy black-box objectives, particularly in scenarios where observations are corrupted by noise and large batches of candidate solutions must be evaluated simultaneously?
8f5562ead9861744a1192c1bef69283e25200aa8.hypothesis: A Bayesian acquisition function that explicitly integrates over uncertainty in the Pareto frontier can achieve robust and sample-efficient optimization of multiple noisy objectives, outperforming existing multi-objective Bayesian optimization methods in both noisy and noiseless settings, and can be made computationally feasible for large batch sizes using efficient algorithmic techniques.
8f5562ead9861744a1192c1bef69283e25200aa8.proposed_method: A new acquisition function, Noisy Expected Hypervolume Improvement (NEHVI), is introduced to maximize the expected hypervolume improvement by integrating over the posterior distribution of the true objective values at previously evaluated points, thus accounting for observation noise in Pareto frontier estimation. The method leverages Monte Carlo integration to approximate this expectation, and supports both sequential and parallel (batch) candidate selection. For parallel optimization, a variant called qNEHVI is developed, which uses a sequential greedy approximation to select batches of candidates and employs a Cached Box Decomposition (CBD) technique to reduce the computational complexity of hypervolume calculations from exponential to polynomial in the batch size. The approach supports gradient-based optimization via sample average approximation, enabling efficient and scalable candidate selection even for large batch sizes and high-dimensional problems.
8f5562ead9861744a1192c1bef69283e25200aa8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of synthetic and real-world benchmark problems, including noisy variants of the Branin-Currin and DTLZ2 functions, adaptive bitrate (ABR) control policy optimization, and vehicle design optimization. Each method will be evaluated using the logarithm of the difference in hypervolume between the true Pareto frontier and the approximate frontier identified by the algorithm, with hypervolume computed over noiseless objective values at observed points. Baseline methods for comparison include PESMO, MESMO, PFES, DGEMO, MOEA/D-EGO, TSEMO, TS-TCH, qEHVI, qEHVI-PM-CBD, qNParEGO, and qNEHVI-1. All methods will be optimized using multi-start L-BFGS-B with exact or approximate gradients, and Gaussian process surrogates with Matérn 5/2 kernels will be used for modeling objectives. Both sequential and parallel (batch) optimization scenarios will be tested, with batch sizes ranging from 1 to 32, and noise levels up to 30% of the objective range. Wall time and scalability with respect to batch size and problem dimensionality will also be measured.
8f5562ead9861744a1192c1bef69283e25200aa8.novelty_claims: The proposed NEHVI acquisition function is the first to provide a one-step Bayes-optimal policy for hypervolume maximization in noisy multi-objective settings, explicitly integrating over uncertainty in the Pareto frontier. The Cached Box Decomposition (CBD) technique enables scalable and efficient computation of hypervolume improvement for large batch sizes, reducing complexity from exponential to polynomial. The method supports differentiable, gradient-based optimization and is empirically shown to achieve state-of-the-art performance and robust optimization in both noisy and noiseless environments, outperforming existing MOBO approaches. Additionally, the approach enables, for the first time, scalable HVI-based optimization for problems with up to five objectives.

8f7297454d7f44365b9bcda5ebb9439a43daf5e6.title: Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty? An Empirical Evaluation of Confidence Elicitation in LLMs
8f7297454d7f44365b9bcda5ebb9439a43daf5e6.research_question: Can large language models (LLMs) accurately express their uncertainty in their answers using only black-box access, and what strategies can improve the reliability and calibration of such confidence estimates across diverse reasoning tasks and model architectures?
8f7297454d7f44365b9bcda5ebb9439a43daf5e6.hypothesis: Black-box methods that combine human-inspired prompting, multiple response sampling, and advanced aggregation strategies can elicit more accurate and reliable confidence estimates from LLMs, partially mitigating overconfidence and improving calibration and failure prediction, though significant challenges remain, especially in complex tasks.
8f7297454d7f44365b9bcda5ebb9439a43daf5e6.proposed_method: A systematic black-box framework will be developed for eliciting and evaluating LLM confidence. The framework consists of three major components: (1) Prompting strategies, including vanilla, chain-of-thought (CoT), self-probing, multi-step, and Top-K prompts, designed to elicit verbalized confidence in a manner inspired by human communication; (2) Sampling strategies, such as self-random sampling (leveraging model stochasticity), paraphrased prompting, and misleading cues, to generate multiple independent responses per query; (3) Aggregation strategies, including consistency (measuring agreement among responses), Avg-Conf (weighted by verbalized confidence), and Pair-Rank (learning a categorical distribution from Top-K rankings), to compute a final confidence score. The framework enables the construction of various algorithms by combining different strategies from each component, and will be systematically benchmarked to identify best practices for black-box confidence elicitation.
8f7297454d7f44365b9bcda5ebb9439a43daf5e6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five types of reasoning tasks: commonsense (SportsUnderstanding, StrategyQA), arithmetic (GSM8K, SVAMP), symbolic (DateUnderstanding, ObjectCounting), professional knowledge (ProfessionalLaw from MMLU), and ethics (BusinessEthics from MMLU). Five LLMs of varying scales and architectures will be evaluated, including GPT-3, GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4, Vicuna 13B, and LLaMA2 70B. Evaluation metrics will include Expected Calibration Error (ECE) for calibration, AUROC for failure prediction, and AUPRC-Positive/Negative for distinguishing correct and incorrect samples. Baseline comparisons will include vanilla verbalized confidence and white-box methods where possible. The impact of different prompting, sampling, and aggregation strategies, as well as the number of sampled responses, will be systematically analyzed.
8f7297454d7f44365b9bcda5ebb9439a43daf5e6.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified, systematic black-box framework for LLM confidence elicitation, integrating human-inspired prompting, diverse sampling, and advanced aggregation strategies. It benchmarks a broad set of methods across multiple tasks and models, providing the first comprehensive empirical analysis of black-box confidence elicitation in LLMs. The study demonstrates that combining response variance and verbalized confidence can significantly improve calibration and failure prediction, and offers actionable recommendations for practitioners. The framework and findings establish strong baselines and highlight persistent challenges, particularly in tasks requiring specialized knowledge, thereby charting directions for future research.

8f7f7b48184217c131844d725daefe6734735d8a.title: ResiDual: Transformer with Dual Residual Connections
8f7f7b48184217c131844d725daefe6734735d8a.research_question: What is an effective residual connection design for Transformer architectures that simultaneously avoids gradient vanishing and representation collapse, thereby enabling stable and high-capacity training of deep Transformer models across a range of tasks and data scales?
8f7f7b48184217c131844d725daefe6734735d8a.hypothesis: A Transformer architecture that integrates both Pre-Layer Normalization (Pre-LN) and Post-Layer Normalization (Post-LN) style residual connections will inherit the training stability of Pre-LN and the representational capacity of Post-LN, thus overcoming the limitations of each individual approach.
8f7f7b48184217c131844d725daefe6734735d8a.proposed_method: A novel Transformer architecture, named ResiDual, will be developed by introducing dual residual connections within each Transformer block. One residual connection will follow the Pre-LN pattern, applying layer normalization before the block and allowing gradients to flow directly to each layer, thereby preventing gradient vanishing. The second residual connection will follow the Post-LN pattern, applying layer normalization after the block to maintain diversity in hidden representations and avoid representation collapse. The final output of the network will be computed as the sum of the outputs from both residual branches. The method will not introduce additional parameters compared to the vanilla Transformer, ensuring computational efficiency. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to establish lower bounds on gradient norms and representation diversity, confirming the avoidance of both gradient vanishing and representation collapse.
8f7f7b48184217c131844d725daefe6734735d8a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on machine translation tasks using three datasets of varying scales: IWSLT-14 English-German (small), WMT German-English (medium), and OPUS-100 multilingual (large). Models will be implemented in the FairSeq framework, using standard training procedures and hyperparameters, including the Adam optimizer and learning rate warm-up where appropriate. Baselines will include standard Pre-LN and Post-LN Transformers, as well as recent variants such as DeepNet, Admin, T-Fixup, DLCL, and B2T. Evaluation will be performed using BLEU scores for translation quality, and convergence behavior will be monitored for stability and training ease. Both shallow and deep model configurations (e.g., 6/6, 12/12, 18/18 encoder/decoder layers) will be tested to assess scalability and depth robustness.
8f7f7b48184217c131844d725daefe6734735d8a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a dual residual connection scheme that fuses Pre-LN and Post-LN benefits, resulting in a Transformer architecture that avoids both gradient vanishing and representation collapse. The method is theoretically grounded, providing provable guarantees on gradient flow and representational diversity. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior performance and training stability across multiple datasets and model depths, without increasing parameter count. This architecture is positioned as a strong foundation for future large-scale AI models.

8f9ceb5ffad8e7a066dfc9d9aaa5153b714740ee.title: OpenVLA: An Open-Source Vision-Language-Action Model
