8f9ceb5ffad8e7a066dfc9d9aaa5153b714740ee.research_question: How can an open-source, large-scale vision-language-action (VLA) model be developed to enable robust, generalist robot manipulation policies that generalize across multiple robot embodiments, tasks, and environments, while supporting efficient fine-tuning and deployment on commodity hardware?
8f9ceb5ffad8e7a066dfc9d9aaa5153b714740ee.hypothesis: A large-scale, open-source VLA model, pretrained on diverse robot demonstrations and leveraging strong vision-language model backbones, will outperform existing closed and open models in generalist robot manipulation tasks, and can be efficiently fine-tuned and deployed on new robot domains using parameter-efficient adaptation and quantization techniques.
8f9ceb5ffad8e7a066dfc9d9aaa5153b714740ee.proposed_method: A 7B-parameter VLA model will be constructed by integrating a pretrained Llama 2 language model backbone with a fused visual encoder that concatenates features from DINOv2 and SigLIP. The model will be fine-tuned on 970,000 real-world robot demonstration episodes from the OpenX-Embodiment dataset, covering a wide range of robot embodiments and manipulation tasks. Robot actions will be discretized into 256 bins per dimension and mapped into the language model's token vocabulary, allowing the model to predict actions as sequences of tokens conditioned on both image observations and natural language instructions. The training procedure will involve end-to-end optimization with a next-token prediction objective, and key architectural and training design choices (such as image resolution, vision encoder fine-tuning, and learning rate) will be systematically explored for optimal performance. The model will be made fully open-source, including code, weights, and training pipelines, and will support parameter-efficient fine-tuning (e.g., LoRA) and quantized inference for deployment on consumer GPUs.
8f9ceb5ffad8e7a066dfc9d9aaa5153b714740ee.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate the proposed model's out-of-the-box performance on multiple robot platforms, including the WidowX and Google mobile manipulator, across 29 diverse manipulation tasks that test axes of generalization such as unseen objects, backgrounds, instructions, and multi-object language grounding. Baselines will include prior generalist policies such as RT-1-X, RT-2-X (closed-source, 55B parameters), and Octo. Evaluation metrics will focus on task success rates, with 170 rollouts per approach for BridgeData V2 and 60 rollouts for Google robot tasks. Additional experiments will assess the model's ability to be fine-tuned on new robot setups (e.g., Franka-Tabletop and Franka-DROID) with limited demonstrations, comparing against state-of-the-art imitation learning methods like Diffusion Policy and fine-tuned Octo. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods (e.g., LoRA, sandwich fine-tuning, last-layer-only) and quantized inference (bfloat16, int8, int4) will be benchmarked for performance-compute trade-offs, memory footprint, and inference speed on various GPUs.
8f9ceb5ffad8e7a066dfc9d9aaa5153b714740ee.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first fully open-source, large-scale VLA model capable of generalist robot manipulation across multiple embodiments and tasks. It demonstrates superior performance to both open and closed prior models (including those with significantly more parameters), supports efficient parameter- and compute-efficient fine-tuning and quantized inference on commodity hardware, and provides a reproducible, modular codebase and training pipeline for the robotics community. The method also systematically explores and establishes best practices for VLA training, adaptation, and deployment, enabling broad accessibility and future research in vision-language-action models for robotics.

8fa44efea525b8bd930440221c334ff7646efa98.title: Fast-SNN: Fast Spiking Neural Network by Converting Quantized ANN
8fa44efea525b8bd930440221c334ff7646efa98.research_question: How can spiking neural networks (SNNs) be constructed to achieve high performance and low inference latency, while minimizing quantization and accumulating errors during the conversion from artificial neural networks (ANNs), across various computer vision tasks?
8fa44efea525b8bd930440221c334ff7646efa98.hypothesis: Minimizing quantization error through supervised training of quantized ANNs, combined with a signed integrate-and-fire (IF) neuron model and a layer-wise fine-tuning mechanism, will enable the conversion of deep ANNs to SNNs that achieve competitive accuracy with significantly reduced inference latency and improved computational efficiency.
8fa44efea525b8bd930440221c334ff7646efa98.proposed_method: A novel ANN-to-SNN conversion framework is developed that first establishes an equivalence between spatial quantization in ANNs and temporal quantization in SNNs, allowing quantization error minimization to be addressed during quantized ANN training. The approach employs quantization-aware training with learnable clipping thresholds to optimize both the range and distribution of weights and activations in ANNs. To address the accumulating sequential error inherent in deep SNNs, a signed IF neuron model is introduced, enabling the cancellation of wrongly fired spikes via negative spikes. Additionally, a layer-wise fine-tuning mechanism is implemented, where a proxy ANN shares parameters with the SNN and minimizes the Euclidean distance between SNN firing rates and ANN activations at each layer, thus mitigating error propagation through the network. The method supports direct coding for spike encoding and is compatible with residual connections and batch normalization for deep architectures.
8fa44efea525b8bd930440221c334ff7646efa98.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on benchmark computer vision datasets, including CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, for tasks such as image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation. Deep architectures such as AlexNet, VGG-11/16, and ResNet-18/20/44/56 are quantized to 2- or 3-bit precision for activations and weights, and then converted to SNNs using the proposed framework. Baselines include state-of-the-art ANN-to-SNN conversion methods (e.g., normalization, calibration, clamped and quantized training, progressive tandem learning) and direct SNN training methods. Evaluation metrics include classification accuracy, mean average precision (mAP), mean intersection over union (mIoU), and the number of synaptic operations (Ops) as a proxy for computational/energy efficiency. Key experimental setups involve varying the number of time steps (latency), comparing different firing threshold strategies, and ablation studies on the signed IF neuron and fine-tuning modules.
8fa44efea525b8bd930440221c334ff7646efa98.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a globally optimal, learnable quantization scheme for ANN-to-SNN conversion that jointly optimizes both the clipping range and the distribution of weights/activations during supervised training. It is the first to transfer quantization error minimization entirely to the ANN training phase, enabling lossless conversion at low latency. The signed IF neuron model and layer-wise fine-tuning mechanism specifically address the sequential and accumulating errors unique to SNNs, allowing for the deployment of deep SNNs with state-of-the-art accuracy and significantly reduced inference latency. The method demonstrates superior performance and efficiency over existing approaches across multiple vision tasks and deep network architectures.

8fac7ae2469c7fae5222bac988bb77701e0e03d6.title: A Comprehensive Framework for Analyzing the Convergence of Adam: Bridging the Gap with SGD
8fac7ae2469c7fae5222bac988bb77701e0e03d6.research_question: How can the convergence properties of the Adam optimization algorithm be theoretically analyzed under less restrictive assumptions, and can these guarantees be aligned with those of stochastic gradient descent (SGD)?
8fac7ae2469c7fae5222bac988bb77701e0e03d6.hypothesis: Adam can achieve both non-asymptotic and asymptotic convergence under the same mild assumptions typically required for SGD, such as L-smoothness and the ABC inequality, rather than more restrictive conditions like almost surely bounded stochastic gradients.
8fac7ae2469c7fae5222bac988bb77701e0e03d6.proposed_method: A comprehensive analytical framework will be developed for the convergence analysis of Adam, focusing on both non-asymptotic (sample complexity) and asymptotic (almost sure and L1) convergence. The approach will leverage the ABC inequality, which provides a bound on the second moment of the stochastic gradients that is less restrictive than traditional assumptions. Key innovations include the introduction of a Lyapunov function tailored for Adam, the use of auxiliary variables to decouple the momentum term, and a novel technique for handling error terms arising from Adam's adaptive learning rates. The framework will establish an approximate descent inequality analogous to that used for SGD, but adapted to the adaptive and momentum-based nature of Adam, allowing for the derivation of convergence guarantees under weaker conditions.
8fac7ae2469c7fae5222bac988bb77701e0e03d6.experiment_details: Theoretical results will be validated through rigorous mathematical proofs rather than empirical experiments. The analysis will be benchmarked against prior theoretical results in the literature, with a detailed comparison of assumptions (such as bounded variance, affine noise variance, and almost surely bounded gradients) and convergence properties (sample complexity, almost sure convergence, L1 convergence). The framework will be evaluated in terms of its ability to provide explicit non-asymptotic sample complexity bounds (e.g., O(ln T / sqrt(T))) and asymptotic convergence in both almost sure and L1 senses. Hyperparameter settings will be chosen to match those commonly used in practice and in previous theoretical studies, ensuring the results are broadly applicable.
8fac7ae2469c7fae5222bac988bb77701e0e03d6.novelty_claims: The proposed framework unifies the analysis of Adam's convergence properties under the same mild assumptions typically used for SGD, overcoming the limitations of previous works that required more restrictive conditions. The approach introduces a new Lyapunov function and a novel technique for handling error terms related to adaptive learning rates, enabling the establishment of both non-asymptotic and asymptotic convergence guarantees. The framework provides the first comprehensive theoretical justification for Adam's convergence under the ABC inequality, aligning its guarantees with those of SGD and broadening its theoretical applicability to a wider range of machine learning problems.

8fc418e6450d4ef6dabe80e99c3684b228b35430.title: Harnessing Large Language Models for Training-Free Video Anomaly Detection
8fc418e6450d4ef6dabe80e99c3684b228b35430.research_question: Can video anomaly detection be performed effectively without any training or data collection, by leveraging the capabilities of large pre-trained language models and vision-language models?
8fc418e6450d4ef6dabe80e99c3684b228b35430.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a training-free video anomaly detection framework, which utilizes pre-trained vision-language models for frame captioning and large language models for temporal aggregation and anomaly scoring, can achieve competitive or superior performance compared to existing unsupervised and one-class methods, despite not requiring any training or domain-specific data collection.
8fc418e6450d4ef6dabe80e99c3684b228b35430.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a training-free video anomaly detection framework that harnesses pre-trained vision-language models (VLMs) and large language models (LLMs). First, an off-the-shelf captioning model (e.g., BLIP-2) generates textual descriptions for each frame in a test video. To address noise and inaccuracies in these captions, a cross-modal similarity-based cleaning process is applied, replacing each frame's caption with the most semantically aligned caption from the video using image-text embedding similarity. Next, temporal context is incorporated by aggregating cleaned captions within a temporal window and prompting the LLM to produce a summary for each window, simulating user-centric perspectives (e.g., law enforcement). The LLM is then prompted to assign an anomaly score to each frame based on its temporal summary. Finally, these scores are refined by aggregating them across frames with semantically similar temporal summaries, using video-text similarity to ensure contextually coherent anomaly estimation.
8fc418e6450d4ef6dabe80e99c3684b228b35430.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two large-scale, real-world surveillance datasets: UCF-Crime and XD-Violence. The evaluation will compare the proposed training-free method against state-of-the-art unsupervised, one-class, and weakly-supervised video anomaly detection baselines, as well as training-free baselines using zero-shot VLMs (e.g., CLIP, ImageBind, LLaVa). Performance will be measured using frame-level AUC-ROC and, for XD-Violence, average precision (AP). The experimental setup includes sampling video frames at fixed intervals, using BLIP-2 for captioning, Llama-2-13B-chat as the LLM, and ImageBind for multimodal encoding. Ablation studies will investigate the contribution of each component (caption cleaning, temporal aggregation, score refinement), the effect of prompt design, and the impact of aggregating scores over semantically similar frames.
8fc418e6450d4ef6dabe80e99c3684b228b35430.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to address video anomaly detection in a fully training-free paradigm, eliminating the need for any training or data collection. It introduces a novel integration of pre-trained vision-language models and large language models for anomaly detection, including innovative techniques for caption cleaning via cross-modal similarity and anomaly score refinement using video-text alignment. The method demonstrates that competitive or superior performance can be achieved relative to unsupervised and one-class baselines, opening new perspectives for practical, deployable video anomaly detection systems without the overhead of domain adaptation or annotation.

8fcd6bc655aeb7af196a6f6436d178fd30be0468.title: Decomposed Diffusion Sampler for Accelerating Large-Scale Inverse Problems
8fcd6bc655aeb7af196a6f6436d178fd30be0468.research_question: How can diffusion model-based inverse problem solvers be accelerated and made more efficient for large-scale, real-world medical imaging tasks, such as multi-coil MRI and 3D CT reconstruction, while maintaining or improving reconstruction quality and generalizability across diverse acquisition settings?
8fcd6bc655aeb7af196a6f6436d178fd30be0468.hypothesis: Integrating Krylov subspace methods, specifically conjugate gradient (CG) updates, with diffusion model sampling will enable efficient, accurate, and scalable solutions to large-scale inverse problems by ensuring data consistency updates remain within the relevant tangent space, thereby eliminating the need for computationally expensive manifold-constrained gradients and significantly accelerating inference.
8fcd6bc655aeb7af196a6f6436d178fd30be0468.proposed_method: A novel diffusion sampling framework, termed Decomposed Diffusion Sampling (DDS), is developed by synergistically combining diffusion model sampling with Krylov subspace optimization techniques. At each diffusion step, the tangent space at the denoised sample (obtained via Tweedie’s formula) is approximated by a Krylov subspace, and a multi-step conjugate gradient (CG) update is performed to enforce data consistency within this tangent space. This approach replaces the need for explicit manifold-constrained gradient (MCG) computations, thus reducing computational overhead and improving stability. The method is designed to be agnostic to the forward model and is compatible with both variance-preserving (VP) and variance-exploding (VE) diffusion parameterizations. For noisy inverse problems, a proximal regularization term is incorporated, and for 3D CT, the method is extended using ADMM to handle additional priors orthogonal to the diffusion manifold.
8fcd6bc655aeb7af196a6f6436d178fd30be0468.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on accelerated MRI reconstruction using the fastMRI knee dataset with various sub-sampling patterns (uniform 1D, Gaussian 1D/2D, VDPoisson disk) and on 3D CT reconstruction using the AAPM 256x256 dataset for both sparse-view and limited-angle scenarios. Baselines include supervised learning methods (U-Net, E2E-Varnet, FBPConvNet), compressed sensing (total variation, ADMM-TV), and state-of-the-art diffusion model-based inverse solvers (Score-MRI, DPS, DiffusionMBIR, DDNM, MCG). Evaluation metrics are PSNR and SSIM, with careful control of the number of function evaluations (NFE) to assess acceleration. The proposed method is tested in both noiseless and noisy measurement regimes, with hyperparameters and algorithmic details tailored for each scenario. Inference times and computational efficiency are benchmarked using commodity GPUs.
8fcd6bc655aeb7af196a6f6436d178fd30be0468.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled integration of Krylov subspace methods with diffusion model sampling, enabling multi-step data consistency updates within the tangent space at each diffusion step. This eliminates the need for computationally intensive manifold-constrained gradients, resulting in a dramatic acceleration (up to 80-200x) over previous diffusion-based inverse solvers. The method generalizes across different forward models and parameterizations, demonstrates state-of-the-art reconstruction quality on challenging medical imaging tasks, and is robust to both noiseless and noisy settings. Additionally, the approach is free from heuristic step-size tuning and is the first to demonstrate efficient diffusion-based reconstruction from non-Cartesian MRI sub-sampling patterns.

8fd11c6f3eb1d0aeb915369f3c4f0b1bb24cab0c.title: Large Language Model Unlearning
8fd11c6f3eb1d0aeb915369f3c4f0b1bb24cab0c.research_question: How can large language models be efficiently and effectively unlearned to remove undesirable behaviors, such as generating harmful responses, leaking copyrighted information, or producing hallucinated content, using only negative examples and limited computational resources?
8fd11c6f3eb1d0aeb915369f3c4f0b1bb24cab0c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a gradient ascent-based unlearning approach, utilizing only negative (undesirable) samples and without access to positive (desirable) outputs, can efficiently and effectively remove targeted misbehaviors from large language models while preserving utility on normal tasks and incurring significantly lower computational costs compared to RLHF.
8fd11c6f3eb1d0aeb915369f3c4f0b1bb24cab0c.proposed_method: A novel unlearning framework for large language models is proposed, centered on a multi-objective optimization procedure. The method applies gradient ascent on the cross-entropy loss of undesirable (negative) prompt-output pairs to directly reduce the likelihood of generating unwanted responses. To further reinforce forgetting, a random mismatch loss is introduced, pairing undesirable prompts with random, irrelevant outputs to encourage the model to dissociate the prompt from its original harmful response. Simultaneously, a KL divergence loss is minimized between the unlearned model and the original model on a normal (benign) dataset, ensuring that utility and performance on non-targeted tasks are preserved. The optimization is performed only on the output tokens conditioned on the prompts, and the normal dataset is matched in format to the unlearned data to prevent shortcut learning. Hyperparameters control the weighting of each loss component, and the procedure continues well beyond the point where the loss on negative samples is maximized, to ensure effective unlearning.
8fd11c6f3eb1d0aeb915369f3c4f0b1bb24cab0c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several large language models, including OPT-1.3B, OPT-2.7B, and Llama2-7B. The PKU-SafeRLHF dataset will provide harmful Q&A pairs as negative samples for unlearning, while TruthfulQA will serve as the normal dataset for utility preservation. Baselines will include standard finetuning on remaining data and RLHF where possible. Evaluation metrics will include unlearning efficacy (e.g., reduction in harmfulness as flagged by moderation models), generalization to unseen but similar harmful prompts, diversity and fluency of generated outputs, reward model scores on normal prompts, and output similarity (e.g., BLEURT) between the original and unlearned models. The computational cost and efficiency of the proposed method will be compared to RLHF, with particular attention to scenarios where only negative samples are available.
8fd11c6f3eb1d0aeb915369f3c4f0b1bb24cab0c.novelty_claims: The proposed research is among the first to systematically formulate and address the problem of unlearning in large language models using only negative samples. Key innovations include the adaptation of gradient ascent for text generation models, the introduction of a random mismatch loss to enhance forgetting, and a KL divergence-based utility preservation mechanism. The approach is designed to be highly resource-efficient, requiring only a fraction of the computational cost of RLHF, and does not require access to positive or human-written outputs. The framework generalizes beyond exact training data, targeting broad behavioral concepts, and is robust to paraphrased or similar prompts. This work establishes new settings, goals, and evaluation protocols for LLM unlearning.

8ff35d975be71e63ed145ebeb6e9d75be83c7c04.title: Unlocking Tokens as Data Points for Generalization Bounds on Larger Language Models
8ff35d975be71e63ed145ebeb6e9d75be83c7c04.research_question: How can generalization bounds for large language models be made tighter and more meaningful by leveraging the vast number of tokens in their training data, rather than relying on document-level IID assumptions and restrictive compression techniques?
8ff35d975be71e63ed145ebeb6e9d75be83c7c04.hypothesis: Token-level generalization bounds, derived using martingale properties and combined with less restrictive compression and quantization techniques, will yield non-vacuous and predictive generalization guarantees for large language models, even at the billion-parameter scale.
8ff35d975be71e63ed145ebeb6e9d75be83c7c04.proposed_method: A novel generalization bound will be derived at the token level using Azuma's inequality and martingale concentration, allowing the bound to account for the non-IID structure of tokens in language model training data. The empirical risk will be computed over sequences sampled from large text corpora, with attention masking ensuring that models do not attend to tokens outside of valid contexts. Several expressive model compression techniques will be employed, including Monarch matrices, Kronecker factorizations, and LoRA, applied to all linear layers and biases in the model. Post-training quantization, specifically QuIP and QuIP#, will be used to further compress models to 2, 3, or 4 bits per weight. Additionally, a token-level prediction smoothing strategy will be implemented, where a learned linear head outputs a smoothing parameter for each token, optimized post-training to tighten the generalization bound.
8ff35d975be71e63ed145ebeb6e9d75be83c7c04.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale language models from the LLaMA and GPT2 families, with parameter counts ranging from 7B to 70B, and evaluated on datasets such as OpenWebText (9B tokens) and Amber (1.2T tokens). Models will be compressed using Monarch, Kronecker, and LoRA parametrizations, both with and without subspace compression, and quantized using QuIP and QuIP# to various bit-widths. Evaluation metrics will include bits-per-dimension (BPD) bounds, Top-1, Top-10, and Top-100 next-token prediction error, as well as validation loss and perplexity. Baselines will include random guess performance and prior document-level compression bounds. The impact of fine-tuning (e.g., chat models) and aggressive compression on memorization versus generalization will also be assessed.
8ff35d975be71e63ed145ebeb6e9d75be83c7c04.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to derive and compute non-vacuous generalization bounds for large language models at the token level, leveraging martingale properties to relax IID assumptions. The method enables the use of less restrictive, practical compression and quantization strategies, allowing bounds to be computed for state-of-the-art, high-quality text-generating models at the billion-parameter scale. The introduction of token-level prediction smoothing further tightens the bounds. The resulting bounds are shown to be predictive of downstream task performance and provide new insights into the trade-offs between compression, memorization, and generalization in large language models.

90184e9612855e298bfe1dcf1d76ccae0157a6c7.title: IV-Mixed Sampler: Leveraging Image Diffusion Models for Enhanced Video Synthesis
90184e9612855e298bfe1dcf1d76ccae0157a6c7.research_question: How can the strengths of image diffusion models be leveraged to enhance the visual quality and semantic faithfulness of video synthesis, while maintaining temporal coherence in generated videos?
90184e9612855e298bfe1dcf1d76ccae0157a6c7.hypothesis: Integrating image diffusion models into the sampling process of video diffusion models will significantly improve the visual quality and semantic consistency of synthesized videos without sacrificing temporal coherence.
90184e9612855e298bfe1dcf1d76ccae0157a6c7.proposed_method: A novel training-free algorithm, IV-mixed Sampler, is proposed to combine image diffusion models (IDMs) and video diffusion models (VDMs) during the video generation process. The method alternates between using IDMs to enhance the quality of individual video frames and VDMs to ensure temporal coherence across frames. The approach utilizes deterministic sampling via DDIM and DDIM-Inversion to inject semantic information from IDMs at various steps of the reverse diffusion process, enabling plug-and-play integration with any VDM. Hyperparameters such as the classifier-free guidance (CFG) scale and the sampling interval for IDM/VDM alternation are explored to optimize the trade-off between visual quality and temporal coherence. Theoretical analysis shows that the IV-mixed Sampler can be formulated as an ODE, preserving the standard sampling process while allowing dynamic adjustment of CFG scales for both IDMs and VDMs.
90184e9612855e298bfe1dcf1d76ccae0157a6c7.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on four popular video synthesis benchmarks: UCF-101-FVD, MSR-VTT-FVD, Chronomagic-Bench-150, and Chronomagic-Bench-1649. The method is evaluated on multiple open-source VDMs, including Animatediff, ModelScope-T2V, and VideoCrafterV2. Baselines include standard DDIM sampling, DPM-Solver++, FreeInit, Unictrl, and I4VGen, with and without additional IDM integration. Evaluation metrics comprise UMT-FVD for visual quality, UMTScore for semantic faithfulness, GPT4o-MTScore for temporal coherence, and FVD (StyleGAN/VideoGPT) for traditional video quality assessment. Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of sampling intervals, CFG scale dynamics, and different IDM/VDM integration strategies. Both quantitative and qualitative results are reported, including visualizations and human evaluations.
90184e9612855e298bfe1dcf1d76ccae0157a6c7.novelty_claims: The proposed IV-mixed Sampler is the first to systematically leverage inference scaling laws and deterministic sampling to integrate image diffusion models into the video diffusion sampling process, achieving significant improvements in both visual quality and semantic faithfulness without retraining. The method provides a mathematically rigorous framework for alternating IDM and VDM score function estimation, introduces a dynamic CFG scale schedule for fine-grained control, and demonstrates strong generalization across multiple VDM architectures. Extensive experiments show state-of-the-art performance on several benchmarks, and the approach is fully plug-and-play, requiring no model retraining.

901b764318aa8cc887d511f0f04666fed87ccfd6.title: Graph Neural Networks are Dynamic Programmers
901b764318aa8cc887d511f0f04666fed87ccfd6.research_question: How can the theoretical and practical alignment between graph neural networks (GNNs) and dynamic programming (DP) be formalized and leveraged to design more effective neural architectures for algorithmic reasoning tasks, particularly those requiring edge-centric computations?
901b764318aa8cc887d511f0f04666fed87ccfd6.hypothesis: A categorical and algebraic framework can be developed that rigorously connects GNNs and DP, enabling the design of GNN architectures that are better aligned with specific classes of DP algorithms, leading to improved performance on algorithmic reasoning benchmarks, especially for edge-centric tasks.
901b764318aa8cc887d511f0f04666fed87ccfd6.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed using concepts from category theory and abstract algebra to formalize the connection between GNNs and DP. The approach will introduce the notion of polynomial spans and integral transforms as a unifying diagrammatic abstraction, capturing both message passing in GNNs and the scoring/recombination steps in DP. By specifying appropriate carrier sets and latent spaces (e.g., real numbers for GNNs, tropical semirings for DP), the framework will allow the instantiation of both classical DP algorithms (such as Bellman-Ford) and GNN update rules within the same categorical structure. The method will further propose new GNN architectures, particularly for edge-centric tasks, by modifying the polynomial span to materialize higher-order messages (e.g., V3 tensors) and updating both node and edge features, thus achieving better algorithmic alignment.
901b764318aa8cc887d511f0f04666fed87ccfd6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the CLRS Algorithmic Reasoning Benchmark, evaluating the proposed GNN variants on a suite of six core algorithmic tasks (including Dijkstra, Floyd-Warshall, InsertionSort, etc.) and scaling up to 27 tasks. The experimental setup will use both in-distribution and out-of-distribution test splits, with models implemented as two-layer MLPs (embedding dimension 24, hidden layers of size 8 and 16) and, for larger-scale experiments, 96-dimensional embeddings with the PGN processor. Baseline comparisons will include standard GNN architectures (V2) and the newly proposed polynomially-aligned variants (V3). Evaluation metrics will be task accuracy, with results reported both per-task and aggregated across edge-centric and other tasks. The experimental protocol will follow the publicly available CLRS benchmark code and data generation procedures.
901b764318aa8cc887d511f0f04666fed87ccfd6.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a rigorous, general categorical framework that unifies GNNs and DP, going beyond prior work that focused on specific algorithmic analogies. It provides a principled method for designing GNN architectures that are provably better aligned with classes of DP algorithms, especially for edge-centric reasoning. The approach enables immediate derivation of both classical algorithms and neural update rules from a single diagrammatic abstraction, and proposes new GNN variants that empirically outperform baselines on edge-centric algorithmic tasks. This work establishes a foundation for systematic exploration of algorithmic alignment in neural networks and opens avenues for further unification of geometric deep learning and algorithmic reasoning.

90350aa626bed47b02d0c162462e5b0ca82be6b2.title: Automatic Chain of Thought Prompting in Large Language Models
90350aa626bed47b02d0c162462e5b0ca82be6b2.research_question: Can the process of constructing effective chain-of-thought (CoT) demonstrations for large language models be fully automated, thereby eliminating the need for manual, task-specific prompt engineering across a variety of complex reasoning tasks?
90350aa626bed47b02d0c162462e5b0ca82be6b2.hypothesis: Automatically generated CoT demonstrations, when constructed with diversity-aware sampling and simple heuristics, can match or exceed the performance of manually crafted demonstrations for in-context learning in large language models.
90350aa626bed47b02d0c162462e5b0ca82be6b2.proposed_method: A new method, Auto-CoT, will be developed to automate the construction of chain-of-thought demonstrations for large language models. The approach consists of two main stages: (1) question clustering, where questions from a given dataset are embedded using Sentence-BERT and partitioned into k clusters via k-means to ensure semantic diversity; (2) demonstration sampling, where a representative question from each cluster is selected and a reasoning chain is generated for it using a zero-shot CoT prompt (e.g., 'Let's think step by step') with a large language model. Simple heuristics, such as limiting the length of questions and rationales, are applied to filter out overly complex or error-prone demonstrations. The resulting set of diverse, automatically generated demonstrations is then used as in-context examples for prompting the language model on new test questions.
90350aa626bed47b02d0c162462e5b0ca82be6b2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on ten public benchmark reasoning datasets spanning arithmetic (MultiArith, GSM8K, AddSub, AQUA-RAT, SingleEq, SVAMP), commonsense (CSQA, StrategyQA), and symbolic reasoning (Last Letter Concatenation, CoinFlip). The primary evaluation will use GPT-3 (text-davinci-002, 175B parameters), with additional tests on Codex (code-davinci-002). Baselines will include Zero-Shot, Zero-Shot-CoT, Few-Shot, and Manual-CoT paradigms. Accuracy will be measured as the main metric, and the number of demonstrations (k) will be set according to dataset conventions. The experimental setup will also explore the effect of wrong demonstrations, the impact of diversity versus similarity-based sampling, and a streaming setting where test questions arrive in batches.
90350aa626bed47b02d0c162462e5b0ca82be6b2.novelty_claims: The proposed method eliminates the need for manual, task-specific demonstration design in CoT prompting by introducing a fully automatic, diversity-driven approach. It demonstrates that clustering-based sampling of demonstration questions mitigates the negative effects of error propagation from zero-shot reasoning chains, outperforming similarity-based retrieval methods. Auto-CoT achieves competitive or superior performance to manual CoT demonstration construction across a wide range of reasoning tasks and datasets, and is robust even in more challenging streaming scenarios. This represents a significant advance in scalable, automated prompt engineering for large language models.

90416158bf8b49d0f5472b36bbacb495f5322cfa.title: A Continuous Relaxation for Discrete Bayesian Optimization
90416158bf8b49d0f5472b36bbacb495f5322cfa.research_question: How can Bayesian optimization be made effective and computationally tractable for discrete sequence domains with very limited observations and strict evaluation budgets, such as those encountered in protein engineering and other bio-chemical sequence optimization tasks?
90416158bf8b49d0f5472b36bbacb495f5322cfa.hypothesis: A continuous relaxation of the objective function for discrete Bayesian optimization, combined with a suitable covariance function over probability distributions informed by prior knowledge, will enable efficient and effective optimization in settings with limited observations and strict evaluation budgets.
90416158bf8b49d0f5472b36bbacb495f5322cfa.proposed_method: A novel continuous relaxation of the objective function will be developed, transforming the discrete optimization problem into one over probability distributions on the sequence space. The method will define a surrogate Gaussian process model directly over these distributions, using a weighted Hellinger distance kernel that incorporates prior or learned sequence distributions (such as those from hidden Markov models or variational autoencoders). The acquisition function for Bayesian optimization will be defined and optimized in this continuous probability space, with the option to use either continuous or discrete optimization algorithms. The approach will ensure computational tractability by restricting the probability space to factorized distributions and designing the kernel to allow efficient evaluation, scaling linearly with sequence length and alphabet size.
90416158bf8b49d0f5472b36bbacb495f5322cfa.experiment_details: Empirical evaluation will be conducted on two bio-chemical sequence optimization tasks: Red Fluorescent Protein (RFP) and enhanced Green Fluorescent Protein (eGFP) sequence design. Experiments will be performed in 'ice-cold start' scenarios with only a handful of initial observations and a strict budget of a few hundred evaluations. Baselines will include state-of-the-art methods such as LamBO, random mutation strategies, and other discrete Bayesian optimization approaches. Evaluation metrics will include objective function values (e.g., protein fluorescence, stability, surface accessibility) and hypervolume for multi-objective optimization. The experimental setup will utilize pretrained latent variable models (e.g., HMMs, VAEs) to parameterize the probability distributions, and both continuous and discrete optimization strategies for acquisition maximization will be compared.
90416158bf8b49d0f5472b36bbacb495f5322cfa.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a continuous relaxation of the objective function for discrete Bayesian optimization, enabling the use of Gaussian processes over distributions rather than sequences. A new weighted Hellinger distance kernel is developed to incorporate prior knowledge and allow efficient computation. The method allows for direct optimization in probability space, supports both continuous and discrete acquisition optimization, and is applicable in low-data, strict-budget regimes relevant to protein engineering. No prior work formulates Bayesian optimization in this way, nor leverages a kernel based on weighted distributions over discrete sequence inputs.

90450cde54211411a17c23a6e8dc234859e9011f.title: Locally Private Causal Inference for Randomized Experiments
90450cde54211411a17c23a6e8dc234859e9011f.research_question: How can valid and efficient causal inference be performed on data collected from randomized experiments when local differential privacy mechanisms are applied to individual data points?
90450cde54211411a17c23a6e8dc234859e9011f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by carefully designing privacy mechanisms and corresponding statistical estimators, it is possible to achieve minimax optimal inference for causal effects under local differential privacy constraints, and that Bayesian nonparametric methods can further improve inference accuracy, especially under tight privacy budgets.
90450cde54211411a17c23a6e8dc234859e9011f.proposed_method: The proposed methodology develops both frequentist and Bayesian approaches for estimating causal effects from data subjected to local differential privacy (LDP) mechanisms. Three privacy scenarios are considered: (1) a joint scenario where all variables are privatized separately, (2) a custom scenario with known treatment assignment probability, and (3) a custom scenario with unknown treatment assignment probability. For each scenario, specialized estimators are constructed, including debiased inverse probability weighting (IPW) estimators and difference-in-means estimators, with explicit bias correction and variance estimation. In the Bayesian framework, a nonparametric Dirichlet Process Mixture model is employed to flexibly model the distribution of potential outcomes, and a blocked Gibbs sampler is developed for posterior inference, leveraging data augmentation to impute missing variables and account for the privacy mechanism. The Bayesian method is designed to be compatible with all considered privacy mechanisms and to provide robust inference even under stringent privacy budgets.
90450cde54211411a17c23a6e8dc234859e9011f.experiment_details: Simulation studies will be conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed frequentist and Bayesian methodologies across a range of privacy budgets and sample sizes. Datasets will be generated according to the Rubin Causal Model, with outcomes and treatment assignments subjected to specified LDP mechanisms (e.g., Laplace and randomized response). Baseline comparisons will include naïve plug-in estimators, debiased estimators, and minimax lower bounds for mean-squared error (MSE). Evaluation metrics will focus on bias, variance, MSE, and coverage of confidence intervals or credible intervals. Additionally, empirical data analysis will be performed using real-world data from a cash transfer program in Colombia to demonstrate the applicability of the methods in practical settings.
90450cde54211411a17c23a6e8dc234859e9011f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces minimax optimal estimators for causal effect inference under local differential privacy, demonstrating that customized privacy mechanisms can achieve the theoretical lower bound for mean-squared error. A flexible Bayesian nonparametric methodology is developed, which is compatible with any proposed privacy mechanism and is especially effective under tight privacy budgets. The approach provides comprehensive frequentist and Bayesian inference tools, including valid confidence intervals and a blocked Gibbs sampler for posterior computation. The work offers practical guidelines for performing causal inference on privatized data and advances the state of the art in privacy-preserving causal analysis.

9045c5a3f445d9190951a28273e87920b9a71d6e.title: Preserving Lagrangian structure in data-driven reduced-order modeling of large-scale mechanical systems
9045c5a3f445d9190951a28273e87920b9a71d6e.research_question: How can reduced-order models (ROMs) of large-scale Lagrangian dynamical systems be learned from data in a way that preserves the underlying physical and geometric structure, without requiring access to full model operators or source code?
9045c5a3f445d9190951a28273e87920b9a71d6e.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a nonintrusive, data-driven operator inference framework, which incorporates knowledge of the governing equations at the PDE level and enforces structure-preserving constraints, can learn reduced-order models that retain the Lagrangian structure and provide accurate, physically consistent predictions for large-scale dynamical systems.
9045c5a3f445d9190951a28273e87920b9a71d6e.proposed_method: A novel Lagrangian operator inference (L-OpInf) framework will be developed to learn reduced-order models of large-scale Lagrangian systems directly from high-dimensional trajectory data. The approach will begin by projecting snapshot data from the full-order model (FOM) onto a low-dimensional basis, such as that obtained via proper orthogonal decomposition (POD). Reduced time-derivative data will be computed using high-order finite difference schemes. The form and parametrization of the reduced Lagrangian model will be postulated based on knowledge of the governing equations at the PDE level, particularly focusing on the structure of kinetic and potential energy terms. The reduced operators will then be inferred by solving a constrained linear least-squares problem, where constraints are imposed to ensure the preservation of the Lagrangian structure (e.g., symmetry and positive-definiteness of mass and stiffness matrices, preservation of the Riemannian metric, and correct physical interpretation of variables). This procedure will be applicable to both mechanical systems with nonconservative forcing and nonlinear wave equations, and will not require access to FOM operators or source code.
9045c5a3f445d9190951a28273e87920b9a71d6e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several benchmark problems, including a linear Euler-Bernoulli beam model, a nonlinear sine-Gordon wave equation, and a large-scale soft-robotic fishtail system with over 770,000 degrees of freedom. High-fidelity simulation data will be generated using structure-preserving time integrators (e.g., variational integrators and the Newmark method) for both training and testing. The proposed L-OpInf ROMs will be compared against standard operator inference ROMs and intrusive projection-based ROMs where possible. Evaluation metrics will include state approximation error, energy conservation or boundedness, and the ability to generalize to unseen initial conditions and time intervals outside the training regime. The experimental setup will ensure that only trajectory data (and not full model operators) is available for training the ROMs, reflecting realistic nonintrusive scenarios.
9045c5a3f445d9190951a28273e87920b9a71d6e.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first nonintrusive, data-driven operator inference framework that explicitly preserves the Lagrangian structure in reduced-order models for large-scale systems. Unlike existing intrusive projection-based approaches, this method does not require access to full model operators or source code, and unlike prior data-driven methods, it is applicable to high-dimensional systems and ensures physical consistency (e.g., bounded energy error, correct symmetries). The approach leverages knowledge of the governing equations at the PDE level to impose structure-preserving constraints during operator inference, resulting in ROMs that generalize well to unseen scenarios and remain stable over long time horizons.

90831247f414c50820067ae8c2d4acdbc6c68746.title: HiFi-Codec: Group-residual Vector quantization for High Fidelity Audio Codec
90831247f414c50820067ae8c2d4acdbc6c68746.research_question: How can an audio codec model be designed to achieve high-fidelity audio reconstruction with a minimal number of quantization codebooks, while maintaining efficiency and suitability for audio generation tasks?
90831247f414c50820067ae8c2d4acdbc6c68746.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a group-residual vector quantization (GRVQ) approach, which splits latent features into groups and applies residual vector quantization within each group, can achieve high-quality audio reconstruction using fewer codebooks compared to traditional residual vector quantization methods.
90831247f414c50820067ae8c2d4acdbc6c68746.proposed_method: A novel audio codec model, HiFi-Codec, will be developed utilizing a group-residual vector quantization (GRVQ) technique. The method begins by encoding input audio into latent features using a convolutional encoder with residual blocks and LSTM layers for sequence modeling. The latent feature vector is then split into multiple groups (e.g., two groups), and residual vector quantization is independently applied to each group using multiple codebooks, with a focus on allocating more codebooks to the first layer to capture the majority of information. The quantized outputs from each group are concatenated and passed to a decoder, which mirrors the encoder architecture with transposed convolutions to reconstruct the audio waveform. The model is trained end-to-end with a combination of time-domain and frequency-domain reconstruction losses, perceptual losses via multiple discriminators (MS-STFT, MPD, MSD), and a GRVQ commitment loss to encourage effective quantization.
90831247f414c50820067ae8c2d4acdbc6c68746.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using publicly available TTS datasets, including LibriTTS, VCTK, and AISHELL, totaling over 1000 hours of English and Chinese speech data. The training will be performed on 8 GPUs. Evaluation metrics will include PESQ and STOI to assess reconstruction quality. Baseline comparisons will be made against Encodec and SoundStream models, with various configurations of sample rates, down-sampling factors, and numbers of codebooks. The experimental setup will also include ablation studies on the number of codebooks and down-sampling rates to determine optimal configurations for both reconstruction quality and efficiency.
90831247f414c50820067ae8c2d4acdbc6c68746.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces group-residual vector quantization (GRVQ), which enables high-fidelity audio reconstruction with significantly fewer codebooks than existing methods. HiFi-Codec is specifically designed to balance reconstruction performance and codebook efficiency, making it well-suited for audio generation tasks. Additionally, an open-source toolkit, AcademiCodec, will be released, providing training code and pre-trained models for HiFi-Codec, Encodec, and SoundStream, thereby facilitating further research in audio codec and generation fields.

90889ff0ce930528e65b1b761bf9bcf9195e5051.title: Synthetic Experience Replay
90889ff0ce930528e65b1b761bf9bcf9195e5051.research_question: Can synthetic data generated by advanced generative models be used to augment or replace real experience in reinforcement learning, thereby improving sample efficiency, scalability, and performance in both offline and online RL settings across a variety of environments and algorithms?
90889ff0ce930528e65b1b761bf9bcf9195e5051.hypothesis: Synthetic experiences generated by diffusion-based generative models can match or exceed the utility of real experience data for training reinforcement learning agents, enabling effective upsampling of limited datasets, improved sample efficiency, and scalable training without algorithmic modifications.
90889ff0ce930528e65b1b761bf9bcf9195e5051.proposed_method: A novel framework, Synthetic Experience Replay (SYNTHER), is proposed to generate synthetic agent experiences using diffusion generative models. For offline RL, a diffusion model is trained on the behavioral distribution of collected transitions and used to upsample the dataset, allowing for arbitrary scaling of available data. In online RL, the diffusion model is continually updated with new real experiences and used to populate a synthetic replay buffer, from which agents are trained on a mixture of real and synthetic data at a configurable ratio. The method supports both low-dimensional proprioceptive and high-dimensional pixel-based environments by generating synthetic data either directly in transition space or in the latent space of a pre-trained encoder. Technical details include using residual MLP denoising networks, Karras et al. samplers for efficient diffusion steps, and configurable buffer management to prevent staleness of synthetic data.
90889ff0ce930528e65b1b761bf9bcf9195e5051.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a wide range of offline and online RL benchmarks. Offline evaluation will use D4RL and V-D4RL datasets (including MuJoCo locomotion and maze2d environments) and state-of-the-art offline RL algorithms such as TD3+BC, IQL, and EDAC. Synthetic datasets will be generated by upsampling original datasets to millions of transitions, and performance will be compared to training on real data. Explicit data augmentation baselines (e.g., additive Gaussian noise, RAD) and prior generative models (VAE, GAN) will be included for comparison. Online RL experiments will utilize DeepMind Control Suite and OpenAI Gym environments, with Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) as the base algorithm, comparing against sample-efficient variants like REDQ. Evaluation metrics include normalized return, Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistics, correlation similarity, and wall-clock training time. Additional studies will assess the impact of dataset size, network scaling, and compatibility with pixel-based RL using latent space diffusion.
90889ff0ce930528e65b1b761bf9bcf9195e5051.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first diffusion-based generative method for experience replay that achieves parity with or surpasses real data on standard RL benchmarks. SYNTHER enables arbitrary upsampling of experience for any replay-based RL algorithm without requiring algorithmic changes, supports both offline and online settings, and scales to high-dimensional pixel-based environments via latent space generation. The method demonstrates significant improvements in sample efficiency, enables effective training of larger neural networks, and provides a general, composable framework for synthetic data generation in RL.

908a6f49bd23bb2a79432ead348e5fc6c74555f5.title: Consistent Estimation for PCA and Sparse Regression with Oblivious Outliers
908a6f49bd23bb2a79432ead348e5fc6c74555f5.research_question: How can consistent and efficiently computable estimators be designed for high-dimensional estimation problems, such as sparse regression and principal component analysis (PCA), in the presence of a large fraction of oblivious outliers and under minimal noise and design assumptions?
908a6f49bd23bb2a79432ead348e5fc6c74555f5.hypothesis: Consistent estimators with optimal error rates and sample complexity can be constructed for sparse regression and PCA, even when an oblivious adversary corrupts all but an inverse-polynomial fraction of samples, by equipping the Huber loss with appropriate non-smooth regularizers and leveraging structural properties of the underlying estimation problems.
908a6f49bd23bb2a79432ead348e5fc6c74555f5.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops a general machinery for robust estimation by regularizing the Huber loss with problem-specific non-smooth penalties: the ℓ1 norm for enforcing sparsity in regression and the nuclear norm for promoting low-rank structure in PCA. For sparse regression, the estimator minimizes the sum of Huber losses between observed responses and linear predictions, plus an ℓ1 penalty on the parameter vector. For PCA, the estimator minimizes the Huber loss between the observed matrix and a candidate low-rank matrix, regularized by the nuclear norm, and subject to a bound on the maximum entry. The analysis extends prior techniques for M-estimators, but introduces novel arguments to handle the presence of large, oblivious outliers and to exploit structural properties such as restricted eigenvalue and well-spreadness conditions for regression, and spikiness for PCA. The machinery is designed to be broadly applicable to other estimation problems with similar noise models.
908a6f49bd23bb2a79432ead348e5fc6c74555f5.experiment_details: The proposed estimators will be evaluated on both synthetic and real datasets that simulate the presence of oblivious outliers. For sparse regression, experiments will use both deterministic and random (e.g., Gaussian) design matrices, with noise vectors having a fraction of entries bounded in magnitude and the rest potentially arbitrarily corrupted. For PCA, experiments will use low-rank matrices with added noise matrices whose entries are independently distributed and satisfy a bounded-inlier fraction. Baselines will include classical LASSO for regression and existing robust PCA algorithms. Evaluation metrics will include prediction error, parameter estimation error (ℓ2 norm), and, for PCA, Frobenius norm error between estimated and true matrices. The experimental setup will systematically vary the fraction of inliers, sparsity, rank, and noise magnitude to assess estimator consistency and optimality.
908a6f49bd23bb2a79432ead348e5fc6c74555f5.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to achieve consistency for sparse regression and PCA with optimal error rates and sample complexity when the fraction of inliers is inverse-polynomial in the sample size, under minimal design and noise assumptions. Prior methods either required much larger inlier fractions, strong incoherence or Gaussianity assumptions, or did not provide consistency guarantees in the presence of both gross outliers and realistic measurement noise. The machinery generalizes and extends previous robust estimation approaches by introducing new analytical techniques for handling oblivious adversarial noise and by demonstrating that consistency is achievable under weaker conditions than previously known. Statistical lower bounds are established, showing that the estimators' tolerance to outlier fractions is information-theoretically optimal up to constant factors.

909ad57ce8caa6b390a65ae09db352d27d8f3996.title: SparseGPT: Massive Language Models Can Be Accurately Pruned in One-Shot
909ad57ce8caa6b390a65ae09db352d27d8f3996.research_question: Can massive generative pretrained transformer (GPT) family language models be compressed via pruning to high levels of sparsity in a single post-training step, without retraining, while maintaining minimal loss in accuracy?
909ad57ce8caa6b390a65ae09db352d27d8f3996.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that large-scale GPT-family language models can be pruned to at least 50% sparsity in a one-shot, post-training manner, without any retraining, and still retain most of their original accuracy as measured by perplexity and zero-shot evaluation metrics.
909ad57ce8caa6b390a65ae09db352d27d8f3996.proposed_method: A novel post-training pruning algorithm, SparseGPT, will be developed to efficiently and accurately induce high sparsity in massive GPT-family models. The method reformulates the pruning task as a set of large-scale sparse regression problems, solved layer-wise using a fast, approximate reconstruction technique based on iterative partial updates and Hessian synchronization. The algorithm incrementally prunes weights column-wise, sharing inverse Hessian computations across rows to achieve computational efficiency, and employs adaptive mask selection to optimize which weights to prune based on error compensation. SparseGPT will also be extended to support semi-structured sparsity patterns (such as 2:4 and 4:8) and will be compatible with weight quantization, allowing joint sparsification and quantization in a single pass.
909ad57ce8caa6b390a65ae09db352d27d8f3996.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the largest available open-source GPT-family models, specifically OPT-175B and BLOOM-176B, as well as smaller variants for scaling analysis. The evaluation will use standard benchmarks including WikiText2, Penn Treebank (PTB), and C4 for perplexity, and zero-shot accuracy on tasks such as Lambada, ARC, PIQA, and StoryCloze. Baseline comparisons will include magnitude pruning and AdaPrune, with all methods applied in a one-shot, post-training setting without fine-tuning. Evaluation metrics will focus on perplexity and zero-shot accuracy, and experiments will be run on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU, measuring both accuracy and runtime. Additional experiments will assess the impact of semi-structured sparsity and joint quantization, as well as sensitivity analyses for partial sparsification.
909ad57ce8caa6b390a65ae09db352d27d8f3996.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable accurate, efficient one-shot pruning of language models at the scale of 100+ billion parameters, with no retraining required. SparseGPT introduces a scalable, approximate sparse regression solver that leverages Hessian synchronization for computational efficiency, making it feasible to prune massive models in hours rather than weeks. The method generalizes to both unstructured and semi-structured sparsity patterns and supports joint weight quantization, enabling significant reductions in both model size and inference cost with negligible accuracy loss. The research also provides new empirical insights into the compressibility of large language models, demonstrating that larger models are more amenable to high sparsity without significant performance degradation.

90ba68b130362558fe1fa64e9364b4e3b21205f0.title: Accelerating Diffusion Models with Parallel Sampling: Inference at Sub-Linear Time Complexity
90ba68b130362558fe1fa64e9364b4e3b21205f0.research_question: How can the inference process of diffusion models be accelerated to achieve sub-linear time complexity with respect to data dimensionality, while maintaining theoretical guarantees on sample quality?
90ba68b130362558fe1fa64e9364b4e3b21205f0.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that dividing the sampling process of diffusion models into a small number of blocks and applying parallelizable Picard iterations within each block will reduce the overall inference time complexity to poly-logarithmic in the data dimension, without sacrificing sample quality.
90ba68b130362558fe1fa64e9364b4e3b21205f0.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces parallelized inference algorithms for diffusion models in both SDE and probability flow ODE implementations. The approach segments the time horizon into O(log d) blocks, each of O(1) length, and within each block, applies Picard iteration of logarithmic depth to solve the discretized SDE or ODE in parallel. An exponential integrator is used for numerical stability, and a shrinking step size scheme is adopted towards the data end to control discretization error. For the ODE implementation, an additional corrector step based on underdamped Langevin dynamics is incorporated and parallelized, further improving space complexity. Theoretical analysis is conducted to rigorously bound the approximation error and establish convergence guarantees under mild assumptions on the data distribution and learned score function.
90ba68b130362558fe1fa64e9364b4e3b21205f0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on high-dimensional synthetic and real-world datasets commonly used for evaluating diffusion models, such as image generation benchmarks (e.g., CIFAR-10, ImageNet). The proposed parallelized algorithms will be compared against state-of-the-art sequential and accelerated diffusion model inference methods, including standard SDE/ODE solvers and recent parallel sampling techniques. Evaluation metrics will include sample quality (measured by FID or similar metrics), inference time (measured by the number of unparallelizable neural network score evaluations), and memory usage. The experimental setup will leverage modern GPU clusters to assess scalability and efficiency in high-dimensional settings.
90ba68b130362558fe1fa64e9364b4e3b21205f0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to provide a diffusion model inference algorithm with provable sub-linear (poly-logarithmic) time complexity in data dimension, supported by rigorous theoretical analysis. The method introduces a parallelization strategy based on blockwise Picard iteration, compatible with both SDE and probability flow ODE formulations, and achieves significant improvements in both time and space complexity over existing methods. Theoretical guarantees are established for both implementations, and the framework offers a foundation for further acceleration and parallelization of diffusion models in high-dimensional applications.

90bf3c89ae55ff02d2ece7c2ad14971c6bf1323f.title: Critical Tokens Matter: Token-Level Contrastive Estimation Enhances LLM's Reasoning Capability
90bf3c89ae55ff02d2ece7c2ad14971c6bf1323f.research_question: How can the identification and targeted penalization of specific tokens within reasoning trajectories improve the mathematical reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs)?
90bf3c89ae55ff02d2ece7c2ad14971c6bf1323f.hypothesis: Targeted identification and penalization of critical tokens—those that disproportionately contribute to incorrect outcomes in reasoning tasks—will significantly enhance the accuracy and robustness of LLMs on mathematical reasoning benchmarks compared to existing preference optimization methods.
90bf3c89ae55ff02d2ece7c2ad14971c6bf1323f.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed to identify 'critical tokens' within incorrect reasoning trajectories that have a significant impact on the final outcome. The identification process will utilize contrastive estimation, wherein two models are trained: one on correct (positive) reasoning trajectories and another on frequently occurring incorrect (negative) trajectories. By comparing token-level likelihoods between these models, tokens that are highly probable under the negative model but not under the positive model will be flagged as critical. These critical tokens will then be explicitly penalized during preference optimization using a modified Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) objective, termed cDPO, which incorporates token-level reward scores to reduce the likelihood of generating such tokens in future model outputs. The approach will focus penalization exclusively on tokens within negative examples, thus refining the model's ability to distinguish between correct and incorrect reasoning patterns.
90bf3c89ae55ff02d2ece7c2ad14971c6bf1323f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the GSM8K and MATH500 mathematical reasoning datasets. The evaluation will use models such as Llama-3-8B, Llama-3-70B, and DeepSeek-math-7B. Baselines will include standard supervised fine-tuning (SFT), DPO, TokenDPO, and RPO. For each problem, multiple reasoning trajectories will be sampled, and the top 50% of incorrect trajectories will be used to train the negative model. Evaluation metrics will include Pass@k accuracy and average accuracy across all settings. LoRA adapters will be used for efficient model training, and hyperparameters such as learning rates and training epochs will be tuned for both the positive/negative models and the preference optimization stage. Statistical significance testing will be performed to validate improvements.
90bf3c89ae55ff02d2ece7c2ad14971c6bf1323f.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the concept of critical tokens as distinct from traditional error tokens in mathematical reasoning, providing a new lens for error analysis. It presents an efficient, scalable contrastive estimation method for token identification that dramatically reduces computational costs compared to rollout sampling. The cDPO framework extends preference optimization to the token level, enabling explicit penalization of critical tokens in negative examples and resulting in substantial improvements over strong baselines on challenging reasoning tasks.

90ce22cf2f5c1e13756e1962c56555f94750b6f4.title: Towards Semantic Equivalence of Tokenization in Multimodal LLM
90ce22cf2f5c1e13756e1962c56555f94750b6f4.research_question: How can vision tokenization in multimodal large language models be improved to achieve better semantic alignment between visual and language tokens, thereby enhancing performance across a range of vision-language tasks?
90ce22cf2f5c1e13756e1962c56555f94750b6f4.hypothesis: Dynamically grouping visual features into semantic units using a clustering-based vision tokenizer, which flexibly determines the number of tokens based on image complexity, will preserve semantic integrity and improve fine-grained alignment between vision and language, leading to superior performance in multimodal tasks compared to fixed patch-based or query-based tokenization methods.
90ce22cf2f5c1e13756e1962c56555f94750b6f4.proposed_method: A novel Semantic-Equivalent Vision Tokenizer (SeTok) will be developed to convert visual features extracted from images into semantically complete visual tokens. The method begins with a vision encoder (e.g., ViT or CNN) to extract patch embeddings from the input image. These embeddings are then grouped into semantic units using a dynamic clustering algorithm based on density peaks, which iteratively selects cluster centers and assigns embeddings until all are allocated, allowing the number of tokens to adapt to image complexity. A token merger aggregates features within each cluster, incorporating 2D positional embeddings and Transformer layers to retain both high- and low-frequency information. The resulting semantic-equivalent tokens are used in a multimodal LLM (SETOKIM), where they are concatenated with text tokens for unified multimodal reasoning. Training objectives include a weighted combination of concept-level image-text contrastive loss and image reconstruction loss to ensure semantic fidelity and detail retention.
90ce22cf2f5c1e13756e1962c56555f94750b6f4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a LLaMA-2-7B backbone for the LLM and a pre-trained SigLIP vision encoder. The model will be pre-trained on large-scale multimodal datasets, including ImageNet-1K for reconstruction and OpenImages for alignment, as well as a 28M text-image pair dataset for conditional image generation and captioning. Instruction tuning will use datasets such as ALLaVA, LLaVA-665K, VQAv2, GQA, OK-VQA, A-OKVQA, LAION-aesthetics, InstructPix2Pix, and Magicbrush. Evaluation will cover a comprehensive set of benchmarks: visual understanding (Flickr30K, VQAv2, GQA, OK-VQA, POPE, MME, MM-Vet), image generation and editing (MSCOCO, Magicbrush, EVR, MA5K), and referring segmentation (refCOCOg, refCOCO+, ReaSeg). Baselines will include state-of-the-art MLLMs using patch-level, discrete, and query-based tokenization. Metrics such as FID, CLIP similarity, L1, LPIPS, CIDEr, and accuracy will be used to assess performance across tasks. Ablation studies and analyses of clustering mechanisms (dynamic vs. fixed, hard vs. soft) will further validate the approach.
90ce22cf2f5c1e13756e1962c56555f94750b6f4.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a dynamic, clustering-based vision tokenizer that produces a variable number of semantic-equivalent tokens, addressing the limitations of fixed patch or query-based tokenization in current MLLMs. This approach enables more interpretable, semantically complete visual tokens that align closely with language tokens, improving fine-grained vision-language alignment. The integration of concept-level contrastive loss and image reconstruction loss in training further ensures both semantic and pixel-level fidelity. The method claims to outperform existing models on a wide range of multimodal tasks, including understanding, generation, segmentation, and editing, while also offering improved efficiency and adaptability through dynamic tokenization.

90dead8a056b848be164c2e5cdadfa2e191c3265.title: A Survey on Oversmoothing in Graph Neural Networks
90dead8a056b848be164c2e5cdadfa2e191c3265.research_question: How can over-smoothing in deep graph neural networks (GNNs) be rigorously defined, measured, and mitigated, and what are the implications of various mitigation strategies on the expressive power and performance of deep GNNs across different graph learning tasks?
90dead8a056b848be164c2e5cdadfa2e191c3265.hypothesis: A unified, axiomatic definition and quantitative measures of over-smoothing will enable more precise evaluation and comparison of mitigation strategies, and that effective mitigation of over-smoothing is necessary but not sufficient for maintaining or enhancing the expressive power and performance of deep GNNs.
90dead8a056b848be164c2e5cdadfa2e191c3265.proposed_method: A formal, axiomatic definition of over-smoothing will be established based on the exponential convergence of node-similarity measures (such as Dirichlet energy) to zero as network depth increases. Multiple quantitative measures of over-smoothing, including Dirichlet energy and Mean Average Distance (MAD), will be evaluated for their suitability and stability. The study will empirically assess the behavior of these measures across a variety of GNN architectures (e.g., GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE) and propose a unified framework for measuring over-smoothing. Furthermore, several classes of mitigation strategies will be systematically reviewed and implemented, including normalization/regularization techniques (e.g., PairNorm, DropEdge), modifications to GNN dynamics (e.g., GraphCON, G2), and residual connections (e.g., Res-GCN, GCNII). The impact of these strategies on both over-smoothing and model expressivity will be analyzed, and the framework will be extended to continuous-time GNNs by adapting the definition of over-smoothing to the temporal domain.
90dead8a056b848be164c2e5cdadfa2e191c3265.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of graph datasets, including small-scale (Texas), medium-scale (Cora), and large-scale (Cornell5/Facebook100) graphs. For empirical evaluation, input and hidden node feature dimensions will be standardized (e.g., set to 128), and node features will be initialized with standard normal random variables to isolate the effects of propagation dynamics. The study will compare baseline GNN models (GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE) and various mitigation methods, using layer-wise Dirichlet energy as the primary over-smoothing metric. Additional experiments will assess the impact of mitigation strategies on downstream task performance (e.g., node classification accuracy) as a function of network depth, with controlled splits and supervised settings. The evaluation will also include continuous-time GNN variants to test the generality of the proposed definitions and measures.
90dead8a056b848be164c2e5cdadfa2e191c3265.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified, axiomatic, and quantitative definition of over-smoothing in GNNs, resolving ambiguities and inconsistencies in previous approaches. It provides a rigorous comparison of existing and new over-smoothing measures, clarifying the limitations of commonly used metrics such as MAD. The study systematically evaluates and contrasts multiple mitigation strategies, highlighting the critical insight that preventing over-smoothing is necessary but not sufficient for maintaining model expressivity and performance. The framework is further extended to continuous-time GNNs, broadening its applicability to emerging architectures.

90fa2eb2b62959183181e5fce44421fc6f7f69f5.title: Street Gaussians: Modeling Dynamic Urban Scenes with Gaussian Splatting
90fa2eb2b62959183181e5fce44421fc6f7f69f5.research_question: How can dynamic urban street scenes be efficiently modeled and rendered in real-time for applications such as autonomous driving simulation, while maintaining high fidelity and supporting scene editing capabilities?
90fa2eb2b62959183181e5fce44421fc6f7f69f5.hypothesis: A dynamic urban scene representation based on explicit point clouds equipped with 3D Gaussians, semantic logits, and a dynamic appearance model can enable real-time, high-quality rendering and efficient training, outperforming existing neural field-based methods in speed and fidelity.
90fa2eb2b62959183181e5fce44421fc6f7f69f5.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces an explicit scene representation, termed Street Gaussians, which models dynamic urban environments as a composition of point clouds for both static backgrounds and moving vehicles. Each point is parameterized by a 3D Gaussian (position, covariance, opacity), semantic logits, and spherical harmonics coefficients for appearance. Foreground vehicles are associated with optimizable tracked poses and a 4D spherical harmonics model, encoding time-varying appearance through Fourier coefficients. Initialization leverages aggregated LiDAR point clouds and SfM data, with object points sampled within tracked 3D bounding boxes. The rendering process concatenates transformed object and background point clouds, projects them into image space, and uses point-based alpha blending for photorealistic synthesis. Sky regions are handled with a learned high-resolution cubemap, and tracked vehicle poses are further optimized as learnable parameters during training.
90fa2eb2b62959183181e5fce44421fc6f7f69f5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Waymo Open Dataset and KITTI benchmarks, both featuring dynamic street scenes with complex vehicle motions and diverse environmental conditions. The method will be evaluated using high-resolution images (1066×1600), with test frames sampled from each sequence and the remainder used for training. Baseline comparisons will include NSG, MARS, 3D Gaussians, and EmerNeRF, all trained and evaluated under similar conditions. Evaluation metrics will include PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS for rendering quality, as well as frames per second (FPS) for rendering speed. Additional ablation studies and scene editing applications will be performed to assess the effectiveness and flexibility of the proposed components.
90fa2eb2b62959183181e5fce44421fc6f7f69f5.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel explicit point-based scene representation for dynamic urban environments, enabling real-time rendering at over 100 times the speed of prior neural field-based approaches. Key innovations include the use of 4D spherical harmonics for dynamic appearance modeling, tracked pose optimization for moving vehicles, and efficient point cloud initialization from LiDAR and SfM data. The approach supports high-fidelity view synthesis, efficient training (within half an hour), and flexible scene editing, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art methods in both quality and speed.

910b12fe78e7c8f346e3d12c729f475c99ba1550.title: An Investigation into Whitening Loss for Self-supervised Learning
910b12fe78e7c8f346e3d12c729f475c99ba1550.research_question: How can self-supervised learning (SSL) methods avoid feature and dimensional collapse in learned representations, and what are the theoretical and practical implications of different whitening loss formulations and transformations for SSL frameworks?
910b12fe78e7c8f346e3d12c729f475c99ba1550.hypothesis: Imposing full-rank constraints on embeddings, rather than strict whitening, is sufficient to avoid dimensional collapse in SSL. Furthermore, channel whitening with random group partition (CW-RGP) can provide collapse avoidance and stable, high-quality representations, especially when batch sizes are small.
910b12fe78e7c8f346e3d12c729f475c99ba1550.proposed_method: A new self-supervised learning framework is proposed that investigates the theoretical underpinnings of whitening loss and its variants. The approach decomposes the symmetric whitening loss into two asymmetric losses, each requiring an online network to match a whitened target, revealing that batch whitening (BW) methods only require embeddings to be full-rank, not strictly whitened. Based on this insight, channel whitening (CW) is introduced, which orthogonalizes examples in a mini-batch and is numerically stable for small batch sizes. To further amplify the full-rank constraint, CW is extended with random group partition (CW-RGP), where the embedding channels are randomly divided into groups for whitening in each iteration, ensuring robust constraint amplification and improved representation learning.
910b12fe78e7c8f346e3d12c729f475c99ba1550.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on standard SSL benchmarks, including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, STL-10, Tiny-ImageNet, and ImageNet, using ResNet-18 and ResNet-50 encoders. The evaluation includes linear and k-NN classification, as well as transfer learning to downstream tasks such as VOC and COCO object detection and instance segmentation. Baselines include SimCLR, BYOL, SimSiam, Shuffled-DBN, Barlow Twins, VICReg, Zero-ICL, and W-MSE. Evaluation metrics include top-1 accuracy, k-NN accuracy, and mean average precision (mAP) for detection/segmentation. Ablation studies are performed on batch size and group partitioning to assess stability and performance improvements.
