910b12fe78e7c8f346e3d12c729f475c99ba1550.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretical framework clarifying that full-rank constraints, not strict whitening, are sufficient for collapse avoidance in SSL. It develops channel whitening with random group partition (CW-RGP), which enables effective collapse prevention and stable training even with small batch sizes. The method demonstrates competitive or superior performance compared to state-of-the-art SSL approaches and provides new insights connecting whitening loss to other non-contrastive and asymmetric SSL methods.

9115ac5452dd4867ac52b024d0e60343b6868740.title: Boosting Continual Learning of Vision-Language Models via Mixture-of-Experts Adapters
9115ac5452dd4867ac52b024d0e60343b6868740.research_question: How can continual learning for vision-language models be made more parameter-efficient and robust, enabling both strong memorization of historical knowledge and effective zero-shot transfer to unseen tasks, while mitigating catastrophic forgetting and reducing computational burdens?
9115ac5452dd4867ac52b024d0e60343b6868740.hypothesis: Integrating a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) adapter-based dynamic expansion architecture with an automated Distribution Discriminative Auto-Selector (DDAS) into a frozen vision-language model will enable parameter-efficient continual learning that preserves both anti-forgetting and zero-shot transfer capabilities, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods in accuracy and computational efficiency.
9115ac5452dd4867ac52b024d0e60343b6868740.proposed_method: A parameter-efficient continual learning framework will be developed based on a frozen CLIP vision-language model, augmented with incremental Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) adapters. Each downstream task will be assigned a task-specific router that activates a subset of sparse, low-rank adapter experts (e.g., LoRA modules) within each transformer block of both image and text encoders. An incremental activate-freeze strategy will be employed: after training on a task, the most activated experts are frozen to preserve their knowledge, while new routers and unfrozen experts are trained for subsequent tasks, promoting both intra-task learning and inter-task collaboration. To automate task identification and preserve zero-shot transfer, a Distribution Discriminative Auto-Selector (DDAS) will be introduced, consisting of task-specific autoencoders trained to model the data distribution of each task. During inference, DDAS routes in-distribution samples to the appropriate MoE-Adapter and out-of-distribution samples to the original CLIP for zero-shot recognition.
9115ac5452dd4867ac52b024d0e60343b6868740.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multi-domain task incremental learning (MTIL) and class incremental learning (CIL) benchmarks, including datasets such as CIFAR100, TinyImageNet, Food-101, Flowers, EuroSAT, DTD, Aircraft, Cars, Oxford Pets, SUN397, and MNIST. The evaluation will use metrics such as 'Transfer' (zero-shot performance on unseen tasks), 'Average' (mean performance across all tasks), and 'Last' (performance on the most recent task). Baselines will include full fine-tuning, adapter-based fine-tuning, and state-of-the-art continual learning methods such as LwF, iCaRL, LwF-VR, WiSE-FT, and ZSCL. The proposed method will be implemented using CLIP ViT-B/16 as the backbone, with LoRA adapters as experts, and trained with AdamW optimizer and label smoothing. Computational cost (parameters, GPU memory, iteration time) will also be measured and compared.
9115ac5452dd4867ac52b024d0e60343b6868740.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a parameter-efficient continual learning paradigm for vision-language models by leveraging incremental MoE-Adapters and a novel activate-freeze strategy, enabling both robust memorization and inter-task knowledge sharing. The Distribution Discriminative Auto-Selector (DDAS) is introduced to automate task routing and unify anti-forgetting with zero-shot transfer within a single model. The approach significantly reduces parameter and computational burdens (by up to 60%) compared to prior methods, and demonstrates superior performance in both full-shot and few-shot continual learning settings, establishing new state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks.

9116c50561007cd69cc24a60c7593a5425f57fcc.title: Stable Bias: Evaluating Societal Representations in Diffusion Models
9116c50561007cd69cc24a60c7593a5425f57fcc.research_question: How can societal biases, particularly those related to gender and ethnicity, be systematically evaluated and quantified in text-to-image diffusion models, given the synthetic and ambiguous nature of their outputs?
9116c50561007cd69cc24a60c7593a5425f57fcc.hypothesis: Text-to-image diffusion models encode and reproduce societal biases in their generated outputs, and these biases can be systematically revealed and quantified through targeted prompt engineering and multimodal analysis methods.
9116c50561007cd69cc24a60c7593a5425f57fcc.proposed_method: A novel auditing framework will be developed to quantify social biases in text-to-image diffusion systems. The approach involves generating image datasets using prompts that systematically vary gender and ethnicity markers, as well as professional attributes, resulting in a comprehensive set of images spanning these social dimensions. Two complementary analysis pipelines will be implemented: (1) a text-based analysis using image captioning and visual question answering (VQA) models to extract and aggregate social attribute descriptors from generated images, and (2) a clustering-based analysis in the image embedding space, leveraging dense representations to identify regions associated with specific gender and ethnicity prompt variations. The method will also include the development of interactive tools for qualitative exploration and validation of bias patterns in generated images.
9116c50561007cd69cc24a60c7593a5425f57fcc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three prominent text-to-image diffusion systems: Stable Diffusion v1.4, Stable Diffusion v2, and Dall·E2. Two datasets will be generated: an 'Identities' dataset using 68 prompts covering combinations of gender and ethnicity, and a 'Professions' dataset using 146 profession names from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), each combined with social attribute markers. Baseline comparisons will be made against real-world demographic distributions from the BLS. Evaluation metrics will include the frequency of gender and ethnicity terms in generated captions and VQA responses, as well as the distribution of generated images across clusters in the embedding space correlated with social attributes. Additional benchmarking will be performed on 11 other popular TTI systems, and interactive tools will be used for qualitative validation.
9116c50561007cd69cc24a60c7593a5425f57fcc.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a systematic, multidimensional framework for auditing social biases in text-to-image diffusion models, addressing the challenge of evaluating synthetic outputs that lack inherent social attributes. The methodology combines prompt engineering, multimodal analysis (text and image embedding space), and interactive exploration tools, enabling both quantitative and qualitative assessment of bias. The approach allows for joint modeling of intersecting social variables (e.g., gender and ethnicity) and provides targeted, comparative metrics for model evaluation. The research also aims to release datasets and low-code tools to facilitate broader community engagement and reproducibility.

91206346edbe28abb606d7b3425cd455d4019d4f.title: Scaling Relationship on Learning Mathematical Reasoning with Large Language Models
91206346edbe28abb606d7b3425cd455d4019d4f.research_question: How do various factors such as pre-training loss, supervised data amount, and augmented data amount influence the mathematical reasoning performance of large language models, and what data augmentation strategies can most effectively enhance this ability?
91206346edbe28abb606d7b3425cd455d4019d4f.hypothesis: Lower pre-training loss, increased supervised data, and greater diversity in augmented reasoning paths will each contribute to improved mathematical reasoning performance in large language models, with diminishing returns as model quality increases.
91206346edbe28abb606d7b3425cd455d4019d4f.proposed_method: The proposed research will systematically investigate the scaling relationships between mathematical reasoning performance and three key factors: pre-training loss, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) data amount, and augmented data generated via rejection sampling fine-tuning (RFT). Multiple large language models (LLMs) of varying pre-training loss and parameter sizes will be fine-tuned on subsets of a mathematical reasoning dataset (e.g., GSM8K) with varying data amounts to measure performance scaling. For data augmentation, RFT will be employed, wherein SFT models generate multiple candidate reasoning paths per question; correct and distinct reasoning paths will be filtered and deduplicated to form augmented datasets. Additionally, reasoning paths from multiple models will be aggregated to further increase diversity. The impact of these factors will be analyzed through controlled experiments, with technical details including sampling temperature, deduplication based on equation lists, and aggregation strategies for multi-model data.
91206346edbe28abb606d7b3425cd455d4019d4f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using open-source LLMs such as LLaMA and LLaMA2 at various parameter scales (7B, 13B, 33B, etc.), as well as proprietary models for comparison. The primary dataset will be GSM8K, with models fine-tuned on varying fractions (e.g., 1, 1/2, 1/4, ... 1/32) of the training set to assess the log-linear scaling of supervised data. For RFT, k candidate reasoning paths per question (with k ranging from 1 to 100 or more) will be generated, filtered for correctness, deduplicated by equation structure, and used for further fine-tuning. Aggregated augmented datasets from multiple models will also be evaluated. Baselines will include standard SFT, in-context learning (ICL), and recent augmentation methods. Evaluation metrics will include maj1@1 (accuracy via greedy decoding) and maj1@K (accuracy via majority voting over K samples), with detailed analysis of reasoning path diversity and computational efficiency.
91206346edbe28abb606d7b3425cd455d4019d4f.novelty_claims: This research proposes a comprehensive empirical analysis of the scaling laws governing mathematical reasoning in LLMs, focusing on pre-training loss, supervised data, and augmented data via rejection sampling. The method introduces a simple yet effective RFT approach for generating diverse reasoning paths without requiring process-level reward models or human annotation. The proposal further innovates by aggregating rejection-sampled reasoning paths from multiple models to maximize diversity and performance gains. The study aims to establish new state-of-the-art results for open-source LLMs on mathematical reasoning benchmarks and provides actionable insights into efficient data augmentation strategies for reasoning tasks.

914db1eaeabbf712c406dd02d57379a8f48c7c7a.title: MxMoE: Mixed-precision Quantization for MoE with Accuracy and Performance Co-Design
914db1eaeabbf712c406dd02d57379a8f48c7c7a.research_question: How can mixed-precision quantization be effectively co-designed for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models to jointly optimize both model accuracy and computational performance, given the heterogeneous quantization sensitivity and expert activation patterns inherent in such architectures?
914db1eaeabbf712c406dd02d57379a8f48c7c7a.hypothesis: A hardware-aware, linear-block-level mixed-precision quantization scheme that accounts for parameter sensitivity, expert activation dynamics, and hardware constraints will yield superior trade-offs between accuracy and computational efficiency compared to uniform or expert-level quantization approaches.
914db1eaeabbf712c406dd02d57379a8f48c7c7a.proposed_method: A novel mixed-precision quantization framework, MxMoE, is proposed for MoE models, which allocates bitwidths at the linear-block level rather than the expert level. The approach begins with an offline calibration phase to collect statistics on quantization sensitivity and expert activation frequencies using a small calibration set. An integer linear programming (ILP) formulation is then used to jointly optimize bitwidth allocation for each linear block, balancing quantization-induced accuracy loss and execution time under hardware and memory constraints. MxMoE automatically generates optimized mixed-precision Group-GEMM kernels, enabling parallel execution of GEMMs with different precisions on GPU hardware. The system includes micro-kernel specialization, resource configuration to ensure compatibility across fused operations, and a greedy tile scheduler that prioritizes computationally intensive tiles for near-optimal hardware utilization.
914db1eaeabbf712c406dd02d57379a8f48c7c7a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several open-source MoE architectures, including DeepSeek-V2-Lite, Qwen1.5-MoE, Qwen2-MoE, and Mixtral-8x7B, using Nvidia RTX-4090 GPUs. Evaluation datasets will include Arc-Challenge, Arc-Easy, HellaSwag, LAMBADA, PIQA, WinoGrande, and WikiText-2 for both calibration and downstream accuracy assessment. Baselines will include uniform quantization methods such as GPTQ and Quarot, as well as expert-level mixed-precision schemes. Evaluation metrics will comprise perplexity (PPL), average accuracy across tasks, and computational throughput (FLOPs/sec) for both memory-bound and compute-bound workloads. The experimental setup will also include ablation studies on allocation granularity and the impact of the accuracy-performance tradeoff hyperparameter.
914db1eaeabbf712c406dd02d57379a8f48c7c7a.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a hardware-aware, linear-block-level mixed-precision quantization strategy for MoE models, which is claimed to outperform both uniform and expert-level quantization in terms of accuracy and speed. MxMoE is the first to jointly optimize quantization bitwidths based on parameter sensitivity, expert activation frequency, and hardware execution profiles, and to automatically generate parallel mixed-precision Group-GEMM kernels for efficient GPU execution. The approach enables substantial speedups (up to 3.4× over full precision and 29.4% over uniform quantization at equivalent accuracy) while maintaining or improving model accuracy, and demonstrates the effectiveness of fine-grained bitwidth allocation and system-algorithm co-design for large-scale MoE deployment.

916b4926cda574dc3f9486bb9994b6f2788dd800.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Large Models: A Comprehensive Survey
916b4926cda574dc3f9486bb9994b6f2788dd800.research_question: How can parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods be systematically developed and evaluated to enable the effective adaptation of large models, such as large language models (LLMs), vision transformers, and diffusion models, for diverse downstream tasks while minimizing computational and memory overhead?
916b4926cda574dc3f9486bb9994b6f2788dd800.hypothesis: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning approaches, which selectively adapt a small subset of model parameters or introduce lightweight, task-specific modules, can achieve comparable or superior performance to full fine-tuning on downstream tasks, while significantly reducing computational, memory, and storage requirements.
916b4926cda574dc3f9486bb9994b6f2788dd800.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed to categorize and analyze PEFT algorithms into four main classes: additive (inserting new trainable modules such as adapters or soft prompts), selective (masking and tuning a subset of existing parameters), reparameterized (constructing low-rank or otherwise transformed parameterizations for training), and hybrid approaches (combining multiple PEFT strategies). For each category, representative algorithms will be implemented, and their technical mechanisms—such as adapter insertion points, prompt initialization, parameter masking heuristics, and low-rank decomposition—will be systematically explored. The framework will also investigate system-level optimizations, including memory-efficient KV-cache management, pruning, quantization, and distributed/concurrent fine-tuning architectures. Technical details will include the mathematical formulation of parameter updates, integration of PEFT modules into transformer architectures, and strategies for merging trained modules back into the base model for efficient inference.
916b4926cda574dc3f9486bb9994b6f2788dd800.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of benchmark datasets for both NLP (e.g., GLUE, OpenBookQA, PIQA, Social IQA, HellaSwag, BoolQ, WinoGrande, ARC-easy, ARC-challenge) and vision tasks (e.g., FGVC, VTAB, Kinetics-400, SSv2, HMDB51, MSCOCO, ADE20K, PASCAL VOC). Baselines will include full fine-tuning, as well as state-of-the-art PEFT methods in each category. Evaluation metrics will encompass task-specific accuracy, convergence speed, parameter count, memory usage, and inference latency. System-level benchmarks, such as ShareGPT, Azure Function Trace, and synthetic workloads generated via the Gamma process, will be used to assess scalability and deployment efficiency. The experimental setup will include ablation studies on the placement and configuration of PEFT modules, as well as comparisons across different model architectures and hardware environments.
916b4926cda574dc3f9486bb9994b6f2788dd800.novelty_claims: The proposed research offers a unified taxonomy and systematic evaluation of PEFT methods, bridging algorithmic advances with practical system design considerations. Innovative contributions include the development of hybrid PEFT strategies, the integration of system-level optimizations (e.g., KV-cache, pruning, quantization) with algorithmic PEFT techniques, and the extension of PEFT beyond NLP to vision, vision-language, and diffusion models. The framework aims to provide actionable guidelines for selecting and configuring PEFT approaches based on task requirements and system constraints, and to advance the state-of-the-art in efficient large model adaptation.

917479a7a72ee7c1fb320c14d770e30ef322ef28.title: The Illusion of State in State-Space Models
917479a7a72ee7c1fb320c14d770e30ef322ef28.research_question: Do state-space models (SSMs) possess a fundamental advantage over transformers in their ability to express and solve state-tracking and inherently sequential computation problems?
917479a7a72ee7c1fb320c14d770e30ef322ef28.hypothesis: SSMs, despite their recurrent formulation, do not have greater expressive power than transformers for state-tracking tasks and are similarly limited in their ability to solve inherently sequential problems.
917479a7a72ee7c1fb320c14d770e30ef322ef28.proposed_method: A formal theoretical analysis will be conducted to characterize the expressive power of common SSM architectures, such as S4 and Mamba, using tools from circuit complexity and algebraic formal language theory. The analysis will determine whether these models can express problems outside the class TC0, focusing on their ability to solve state-tracking problems like permutation composition. Additionally, minimal architectural extensions to SSMs—such as adding input-dependent transition matrices or nonlinearities—will be proposed and theoretically analyzed to assess whether they increase expressive power to match that of recurrent neural networks (RNNs). Empirical experiments will be designed to test the practical ability of SSMs, transformers, RNNs, and extended SSMs to learn and solve word problems on non-abelian groups, specifically focusing on permutation composition and related state-tracking tasks.
917479a7a72ee7c1fb320c14d770e30ef322ef28.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training various neural architectures—including transformers, S4, Mamba, RNNs, and input-dependent SSM variants—on sequence tagging tasks derived from group word problems (e.g., permutation composition in the symmetric group S5, A4 × Z5, and Z60). Models will be evaluated on their ability to predict the cumulative product of group elements at each step in the sequence, with accuracy measured as the proportion of correctly tagged sequences. The minimum model depth required to achieve high accuracy (>90%) will be recorded as a function of input sequence length, providing empirical evidence of the relationship between model architecture, depth, and the complexity of the state-tracking problem. Baselines will include transformers and RNNs, and the evaluation will focus on both expressivity and practical learnability.
917479a7a72ee7c1fb320c14d770e30ef322ef28.novelty_claims: The proposal claims a new theoretical result showing that standard SSMs, despite their recurrent structure, are limited to TC0 expressivity and cannot solve inherently sequential, NC1-hard state-tracking problems such as permutation composition—contrary to common assumptions. It further proposes and analyzes minimal architectural modifications that can restore full state-tracking expressivity, bridging the gap between SSMs and RNNs. The empirical component will provide the first systematic comparison of SSMs, transformers, and RNNs on state-tracking tasks of varying complexity, demonstrating the practical implications of the theoretical findings and motivating the development of more expressive SSM architectures.

91b32fc0a23f0af53229fceaae9cce43a0406d2e.title: Structured Denoising Diffusion Models in Discrete State-Spaces
91b32fc0a23f0af53229fceaae9cce43a0406d2e.research_question: How can diffusion-based generative models be effectively extended to discrete state spaces for improved performance on discrete data such as text and images, and what structural choices in the corruption process and loss function design lead to better generative modeling outcomes?
91b32fc0a23f0af53229fceaae9cce43a0406d2e.hypothesis: Structured corruption processes and tailored loss functions in discrete denoising diffusion probabilistic models (D3PMs) will yield superior performance in discrete data generation tasks compared to uniform or unstructured approaches, and can match or exceed the performance of continuous diffusion models and non-autoregressive baselines.
91b32fc0a23f0af53229fceaae9cce43a0406d2e.proposed_method: A new class of discrete denoising diffusion probabilistic models (D3PMs) will be developed, generalizing multinomial diffusion to allow flexible, structured Markov transition matrices for the forward corruption process. Several types of transition matrices will be explored, including uniform, absorbing state (e.g., [MASK] tokens), discretized Gaussian (for ordinal data), and matrices based on token embedding similarity. The reverse process will be parameterized using neural networks that predict logits or truncated logistic distributions, ensuring the reverse transition probabilities match the structure imposed by the forward process. An auxiliary cross-entropy loss will be combined with the standard variational lower bound to stabilize training and encourage accurate denoising, with noise schedules designed using mutual information or other principled criteria.
91b32fc0a23f0af53229fceaae9cce43a0406d2e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both text and image generation tasks. For text, character-level generation will be evaluated on the text8 dataset (27-token vocabulary, chunk length 256) and large-scale word-level generation on LM1B (vocabulary size 8192, sequence length 128), using D3PMs with different transition matrices and noise schedules. For images, unconditional generation will be performed on CIFAR-10, with images quantized and modeled using various D3PM variants. Baselines will include non-autoregressive models (e.g., discrete flows, IAF/SCF), autoregressive transformers, and continuous diffusion models. Evaluation metrics will include negative log-likelihood (bits/char or bits/dim), perplexity (for text), Inception Score (IS), and Frechet Inception Distance (FID) for images. Models will be trained with up to 1000 diffusion steps, and ablations will be performed on loss function variants and noise schedules.
91b32fc0a23f0af53229fceaae9cce43a0406d2e.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a general and flexible framework for discrete diffusion models that allows domain-informed structure in the corruption process, surpassing prior approaches limited to uniform or unstructured transitions. The use of absorbing states and embedding-based transitions enables connections to autoregressive and masked language models, while the auxiliary loss function improves training stability and sample quality. The approach demonstrates scalability to large vocabularies and long sequences in text, and achieves log-likelihoods and sample qualities on images that approach or exceed those of continuous diffusion models. The framework opens new avenues for leveraging structure in discrete data within the diffusion modeling paradigm.

91deaf9d324c8feafc189da0da03e60a60287bca.title: Code as Policies: Language Model Programs for Embodied Control
91deaf9d324c8feafc189da0da03e60a60287bca.research_question: How can large language models be leveraged to autonomously generate robot policy code from natural language commands, enabling robots to generalize to new tasks, objects, and environments without additional training data?
91deaf9d324c8feafc189da0da03e60a60287bca.hypothesis: Large language models trained on code can be repurposed to generate executable robot policy code from natural language instructions, enabling flexible, interpretable, and generalizable robot behaviors across diverse tasks and embodiments.
91deaf9d324c8feafc189da0da03e60a60287bca.proposed_method: A framework is developed in which large language models (LLMs) are prompted with a combination of hints (such as available perception and control APIs) and few-shot examples mapping natural language instructions to code snippets. The LLM generates Python programs, termed Language Model Programs (LMPs), that directly process perception outputs (e.g., from object detectors) and parameterize control primitives. Hierarchical code generation is employed, allowing the LLM to recursively define undefined functions and compose complex policies using classic programming logic (e.g., loops, conditionals) and third-party libraries (e.g., NumPy for spatial reasoning). The generated code is executed on real robot systems, with safety checks to prevent unsafe operations. The approach supports both low-level reactive policies and high-level waypoint-based or multi-step behaviors, and can accumulate reusable functions over time.
91deaf9d324c8feafc189da0da03e60a60287bca.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted across several domains and robot platforms, including table-top manipulation with a UR5e arm, 2D shape drawing, and mobile manipulation in a kitchen environment. Perception APIs are implemented using open-vocabulary object detectors such as MDETR and ViLD, while control APIs provide primitives for movement, grasping, and trajectory following. The method is evaluated on two benchmarks: a new robotics-themed RoboCodeGen benchmark (37 function generation problems focused on spatial/geometric reasoning and controls) and the standard HumanEval code-generation benchmark. Baselines include supervised imitation learning policies (e.g., CLIPort) and natural language planners. Evaluation metrics include percentage of tasks successfully completed (pass rates) and code correctness as measured by unit tests. Ablation studies analyze the impact of hierarchical code generation and model scaling.
91deaf9d324c8feafc189da0da03e60a60287bca.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a robot-centric formulation of language model-generated programs (Code as Policies) that enables robots to interpret and execute natural language commands as executable policy code. Hierarchical code generation is shown to improve both robotics-specific and general code-generation performance, achieving state-of-the-art results on the HumanEval benchmark. The method eliminates the need for additional data collection or retraining for new tasks, supports compositional generalization, and produces interpretable, modifiable policies. A new benchmark for robotics code generation is also introduced to facilitate future evaluation.

91eb20f923ea3b0246868902aef4e9bea572b800.title: Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware
91eb20f923ea3b0246868902aef4e9bea572b800.research_question: Can fine-grained, bimanual robotic manipulation tasks be learned effectively using low-cost, accessible hardware and data-efficient imitation learning methods, without reliance on high-end sensors or expensive robots?
91eb20f923ea3b0246868902aef4e9bea572b800.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a combination of a low-cost, user-friendly bimanual teleoperation system and a novel imitation learning algorithm that leverages action chunking and sequence modeling can enable robots to learn and perform fine manipulation tasks with high precision and robustness, even with limited demonstration data and imprecise hardware.
91eb20f923ea3b0246868902aef4e9bea572b800.proposed_method: The proposed approach consists of two main components: (1) the development of an open-source, low-cost bimanual teleoperation system (ALOHA) using off-the-shelf 6-DoF robot arms, 3D-printed grippers, and commodity RGB cameras for visual feedback, enabling intuitive data collection of human demonstrations; and (2) the introduction of Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT), a novel imitation learning algorithm. ACT is trained as a conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) that models the distribution over action sequences conditioned on current observations (multi-view images and joint positions). The policy predicts sequences of future joint positions (action chunks) rather than single-step actions, reducing the effective task horizon and mitigating compounding errors. Temporal ensembling is employed at inference to smooth and improve policy outputs by averaging overlapping action chunk predictions. The ACT architecture utilizes ResNet-based visual encoders, a transformer encoder for observation fusion, and a transformer decoder for sequence generation, outputting multi-step joint targets for both arms.
91eb20f923ea3b0246868902aef4e9bea572b800.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six real-world fine-grained bimanual manipulation tasks (e.g., opening ziploc bags, slotting batteries, threading velcro ties, preparing tape, and putting on shoes) and two simulated tasks in MuJoCo. Each real-world task will be demonstrated 50-100 times using the teleoperation system, resulting in 10-20 minutes of demonstration data per task. The ACT algorithm will be compared against several baselines, including BC-ConvMLP, BeT, RT-1, and VINN, using identical datasets. Evaluation metrics include task success rates, subtask completion rates, and robustness to demonstration noise and stochasticity. Additional ablation studies will assess the impact of action chunking, temporal ensembling, and the CVAE objective. The experimental setup includes four RGB cameras (two wrist-mounted, one front, one top), 50Hz control frequency, and randomized object initializations to test generalization.
91eb20f923ea3b0246868902aef4e9bea572b800.novelty_claims: The proposal claims novelty in (1) the design and open-sourcing of a low-cost, easily assembled bimanual teleoperation system capable of high-precision, contact-rich manipulation; (2) the development of the ACT algorithm, which introduces action chunking and temporal ensembling within a transformer-based conditional generative framework for imitation learning from high-dimensional visual inputs; (3) demonstrating that fine-grained, closed-loop bimanual manipulation can be learned directly from limited real-world demonstrations on low-cost hardware, achieving high success rates on tasks previously requiring expensive platforms; and (4) providing comprehensive ablations and comparisons showing the effectiveness and generality of action chunking for reducing compounding errors in imitation learning.

91f5154eda826d3f79bece58472027299fb38372.title: Cryptographic Hardness of Learning Halfspaces with Massart Noise
91f5154eda826d3f79bece58472027299fb38372.research_question: What are the computational limits of efficiently learning halfspaces in the presence of Massart noise, and can efficient algorithms achieve error rates significantly better than the noise rate when the optimal error is much smaller than the noise rate?
91f5154eda826d3f79bece58472027299fb38372.hypothesis: Assuming the subexponential-time hardness of the Learning with Errors (LWE) problem, no polynomial-time algorithm can learn halfspaces with Massart noise to error significantly better than the noise rate, even when the optimal 0-1 error is much smaller than the noise rate.
91f5154eda826d3f79bece58472027299fb38372.proposed_method: A computational hardness reduction will be constructed from the Learning with Errors (LWE) problem to the problem of PAC learning halfspaces under Massart noise. The reduction proceeds in two main steps: first, the standard LWE problem is mapped to a continuous variant where samples are drawn from a uniform distribution over [0,1]^n and the secret vector is binary, with Gaussian noise added to the labels. Second, a rejection sampling procedure is applied to the LWE samples to produce labeled examples whose distribution closely matches hard instances for learning halfspaces with Massart noise. The construction carefully simulates the conditional distributions used in prior Statistical Query (SQ) lower bounds, but adapts them to the computational setting by managing the additional noise introduced during the reduction. Technical modifications are made to ensure that the resulting instances satisfy the Massart noise condition and avoid pathological regions where the noise model does not hold.
91f5154eda826d3f79bece58472027299fb38372.experiment_details: Theoretical reductions and hardness proofs will be carried out, relying on the assumed subexponential-time hardness of the LWE problem with specific parameters (e.g., secret vectors in {±1}^n, noise drawn from a continuous Gaussian, and sample distributions uniform over [0,1]^n). The reduction will be analyzed to show that any efficient learner for Massart halfspaces with error better than Ω(η) would yield an efficient algorithm for LWE, contradicting the hardness assumption. Theoretical evaluation will focus on the error rates achievable by polynomial-time algorithms, and the construction will be compared to known algorithmic results and SQ lower bounds. No empirical datasets or computational experiments are used; the evaluation is entirely based on complexity-theoretic arguments and reductions.
91f5154eda826d3f79bece58472027299fb38372.novelty_claims: This proposal establishes the first computational hardness result for PAC learning halfspaces in the presence of Massart noise under a standard cryptographic assumption, extending prior SQ model lower bounds to the full class of polynomial-time algorithms. The reduction framework innovatively adapts techniques from LWE-based hardness and SQ lower bounds, introducing new technical tools for managing noise in the reduction and ensuring the resulting distributions satisfy the Massart noise model. The results nearly resolve the computational complexity of learning halfspaces with Massart noise, demonstrating that known efficient algorithms are essentially optimal under widely believed assumptions.

920ba705e985210217786ed769c234ed3717da2c.title: Planning Anything with Rigor: General-Purpose Zero-Shot Planning with LLM-based Formalized Programming
920ba705e985210217786ed769c234ed3717da2c.research_question: Can a general-purpose, zero-shot planning framework based on large language models (LLMs) be developed to solve complex planning problems across diverse domains, using only natural language task descriptions and background information, without requiring any task-specific examples or preparatory efforts?
920ba705e985210217786ed769c234ed3717da2c.hypothesis: A general-purpose framework that leverages LLMs to formalize planning problems as constrained optimization problems, and then solves them using formal solvers, will achieve strong performance and generalization across a wide range of complex planning tasks without the need for task-specific examples or external critics.
920ba705e985210217786ed769c234ed3717da2c.proposed_method: A novel framework, LLM-Based Formalized Programming (LLMFP), will be developed to address zero-shot planning in complex domains. The method takes as input a natural language task description, background information (such as APIs or domain variables), and a user query. The process consists of five main steps: (1) Definer: prompt the LLM to extract the planning goal, decision variables, and both explicit and implicit constraints from the input; (2) Formulator: prompt the LLM to generate a structured JSON representation detailing all variables, their types, dependencies, and requirements; (3) Code Generator: prompt the LLM to generate executable code (e.g., Python with Z3 SMT syntax) that encodes the optimization problem; (4) Result Formatter: execute the code, then prompt the LLM to convert the results into a fixed output format and provide an assessment of the solution; (5) Self-Assessment and Modification: prompt the LLM to evaluate each step, identify and correct errors, and iterate up to a fixed number of times until a valid plan is produced. The framework is solver-agnostic but will initially use the SMT solver for its flexibility and accessibility.
920ba705e985210217786ed769c234ed3717da2c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 9 diverse planning tasks, including 5 multi-constraint decision-making problems (e.g., Coffee, Workforce, Facility, TaskAllocation, Warehouse) and 4 multi-step planning problems (e.g., Blocksworld, Mystery Blocksworld, Movie, Gripper). Each task will be provided in natural language, with background information and queries, but without any task-specific examples. The framework will be evaluated using two state-of-the-art LLMs (GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet) at temperature 0. Baselines will include direct LLM plan generation, chain-of-thought prompting, code generation with and without SMT solvers, and direct planning with OpenAI o1-preview. Evaluation metrics will focus on optimal rate (percentage of generated plans that are optimal) and success rate. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the contribution of each framework component, and additional experiments will test the effect of adding a single task-specific example.
920ba705e985210217786ed769c234ed3717da2c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach offers a universal, zero-shot planning framework that formalizes diverse planning problems as constrained optimization problems using only natural language inputs, without any task-specific examples or external critics. LLMFP is claimed to be the first to enable LLMs to construct and solve a wide range of planning problems as optimization problems from scratch, achieving strong generalization and outperforming existing baselines by significant margins. The method is robust to fundamentally different and obfuscated problems, and its modular design allows for easy adaptation to different solvers and the optional inclusion of task-specific examples for further performance gains.

920d81e1fa5f69c387a4fd07845d7e331f60edab.title: Selective Prompt Anchoring for Code Generation
920d81e1fa5f69c387a4fd07845d7e331f60edab.research_question: How can the reliability and correctness of code generated by large language models (LLMs) be improved, particularly by addressing the tendency of these models to deviate from user intent as code generation progresses?
920d81e1fa5f69c387a4fd07845d7e331f60edab.hypothesis: Code generation errors in LLMs are significantly caused by an attention dilution phenomenon, where models pay less attention to the user prompt over time. Amplifying the contextual impact of selected prompt tokens (anchored text) during code generation will mitigate this issue and improve code correctness.
920d81e1fa5f69c387a4fd07845d7e331f60edab.proposed_method: A model-agnostic framework, Selective Prompt Anchoring (SPA), will be developed to steer LLM attention toward user intent during code generation. SPA identifies a subset of prompt tokens (anchored text) that should exert greater influence on the model's output. The method creates both an original embedding matrix and a masked embedding matrix (where anchored text embeddings are replaced with mask embeddings), and mathematically approximates the contextual impact of the anchored text by contrasting the logit distributions of these two prompts. This difference is scaled by a tunable anchoring strength hyperparameter and added to the original logits, thereby amplifying the influence of the anchored text at each generation step. The approach is designed to be training-free, efficient, and compatible with any LLM without modifying model internals.
920d81e1fa5f69c387a4fd07845d7e331f60edab.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using six open-source code LLMs (including CodeGen-Mono-350M, CodeLlama-7B, StarCoder2-15B, and DeepSeek-Coder variants) across six code generation benchmarks: HumanEval, MBPP, HumanEval+, MBPP+, BigCodeBench, and LiveCodeBench. Additional multilingual and generalization tests will use HumanEval-X and other generative tasks such as TruthfulQA, GSM8K, MMLU, and BoolQ. Baselines will include state-of-the-art prompting methods (Self-Debugging, Self-Planning, ReAct, Self-Edit) and an attention steering method (PASTA). Evaluation will use Pass@1 and Pass@10 metrics, with grid search used to tune anchoring strength on validation splits. Ablation studies will assess the impact of different anchored text selection strategies and prompt lengths. Computational efficiency and inference time will also be measured and compared.
920d81e1fa5f69c387a4fd07845d7e331f60edab.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel, model-agnostic, and training-free approach to attention steering in code LLMs by mathematically amplifying the influence of selected prompt tokens via logit arithmetic. It is the first to systematically identify and address the attention dilution phenomenon in code generation, offering a principled mechanism for dynamically controlling prompt influence without modifying model internals or requiring extensive profiling. The method is shown to consistently and significantly improve code generation accuracy across diverse models, languages, and benchmarks, outperforming both prompting-based and attention-editing baselines while maintaining high computational efficiency.

921fb0112c775df4d55d8ebad88b4341ede23702.title: Unifying (Machine) Vision via Counterfactual World Modeling
921fb0112c775df4d55d8ebad88b4341ede23702.research_question: How can a unified, unsupervised visual foundation model be developed to perform a wide variety of visual tasks without requiring task-specific architectures, labeled data, or language-based interfaces?
921fb0112c775df4d55d8ebad88b4341ede23702.hypothesis: A visual foundation model trained with structured masking and prompted via counterfactual inputs can implicitly learn low-dimensional physical structure in visual data, enabling zero-shot solutions to diverse visual tasks such as keypoint detection, optical flow, segmentation, and depth estimation.
921fb0112c775df4d55d8ebad88b4341ede23702.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces Counterfactual World Modeling (CWM), a framework for unsupervised visual foundation modeling. The method involves two key components: (1) pretraining a vision transformer model using a temporally-factored masked prediction task, where the first frame of a video is fully visible and almost all patches of the second frame are masked, forcing the model to factor appearance from dynamics; and (2) employing counterfactual prompting, where visual inputs are systematically modified (e.g., by moving or altering patches) and the model's predictions are compared between real and counterfactual inputs. This process allows the extraction of various visual representations as counterfactual derivatives of the prediction model. The approach is extended to handle additional modalities, such as head-motion data, and supports efficient computation of visual properties (e.g., optical flow, occlusion) using autograd-based Jacobian-vector products.
921fb0112c775df4d55d8ebad88b4341ede23702.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using large-scale unlabeled video datasets, such as Kinetics400, for pretraining the masked prediction model. The evaluation will include zero-shot performance on a variety of visual tasks: keypoint detection, optical flow, occlusion estimation, object segmentation, and relative depth estimation. Baselines will include supervised and unsupervised state-of-the-art models for each task, such as classical optical flow algorithms and supervised segmentation networks. Evaluation metrics will be task-appropriate, such as reconstruction error for keypoints, endpoint error for optical flow, and segmentation accuracy for object segmentation. The experimental setup will also explore the impact of different masking policies and the ability to generalize across real-world and synthetic datasets.
921fb0112c775df4d55d8ebad88b4341ede23702.novelty_claims: The proposed framework unifies a wide range of visual computations within a single unsupervised model, eliminating the need for task-specific architectures, labeled data, or language-based interfaces. The use of structured masking enables the model to factor appearance from dynamics, while counterfactual prompting provides a generic, visual interface for zero-shot task specification. The approach mathematically formalizes task extraction as counterfactual derivatives of the prediction model, supporting efficient and interpretable readouts for diverse visual tasks. This represents a conceptually simple and biologically plausible path toward a general-purpose visual foundation model.

9245ea27d258a3511c94460e5adeef5418e77010.title: Learning to Generate Text-Grounded Mask for Open-World Semantic Segmentation from Only Image-Text Pairs
9245ea27d258a3511c94460e5adeef5418e77010.research_question: How can open-world semantic segmentation be achieved for arbitrary visual concepts using only image-text pairs, without relying on dense pixel-level annotations?
9245ea27d258a3511c94460e5adeef5418e77010.hypothesis: A framework that directly learns region-text alignment from image-text pairs, rather than relying on image-level alignment, can significantly improve the quality and precision of open-world semantic segmentation masks in a zero-shot setting.
9245ea27d258a3511c94460e5adeef5418e77010.proposed_method: A novel framework, termed Text-grounded Contrastive Learning (TCL), is proposed to enable direct learning of region-text alignment for open-world semantic segmentation using only image-text pairs. The approach incorporates a grounder module that generates segmentation masks for a given text prompt by leveraging a frozen pre-trained CLIP image encoder and text encoder, along with a trainable grounding decoder that produces pixel-level dense embeddings. The text-grounded mask is computed as a position-wise dot product between the text embedding and pixel-level image embeddings, and is used to extract text-grounded image features. Contrastive learning is then performed between these text-grounded region embeddings and the corresponding text embeddings. The training objective includes multiple TCL losses at the image-level, feature-level, and area-level, as well as smoothness regularization, to ensure precise, non-trivial, and smooth segmentation masks. The model is trained end-to-end, updating only the grounding decoder while keeping the CLIP encoders frozen.
9245ea27d258a3511c94460e5adeef5418e77010.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a unified evaluation protocol across eight widely used semantic segmentation benchmarks, including PASCAL VOC, PASCAL Context, COCO-Object, COCO-Stuff, Cityscapes, and ADE20K. The model will be trained on large-scale web-crawled image-text datasets (e.g., CC3M and CC12M) without any dense annotations. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art open-world segmentation methods such as GroupViT, MaskCLIP, and ReCo, with all models evaluated under identical settings (e.g., class names, input resolution, and no dataset-specific tricks). The primary evaluation metric will be mean Intersection-over-Union (mIoU). Additional ablation studies will analyze the impact of each component of the TCL framework, including the grounding decoder, various TCL loss terms, and regularization strategies.
9245ea27d258a3511c94460e5adeef5418e77010.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a new region-level contrastive learning objective that explicitly aligns text and text-grounded image regions, overcoming the train-test alignment discrepancy present in prior methods. Unlike previous approaches that rely on image-level alignment or heuristic clustering, this method enables end-to-end learning of region-text alignment using only image-text pairs, without any dense supervision. The approach also presents a unified evaluation protocol for open-world segmentation, facilitating fair and rigorous comparison. Experimental results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art zero-shot segmentation performance across all benchmarks, with significant improvements over existing methods.

926b9ece5e7cc8cc0033fbd14ea302338f41632e.title: Adaptive Rank Allocation: Speeding Up Modern Transformers with RaNA Adapters
926b9ece5e7cc8cc0033fbd14ea302338f41632e.research_question: How can inference efficiency in modern Transformer architectures be improved without sacrificing model quality, especially in the presence of non-sparse activation functions and across both MLP and attention layers?
926b9ece5e7cc8cc0033fbd14ea302338f41632e.hypothesis: Adaptive rank allocation using low-rank matrix decompositions and input-dependent masking can provide significant reductions in computational cost (FLOPs) during inference in modern Transformers, while maintaining or improving perplexity and accuracy compared to existing neuron-adaptive and structured pruning methods.
926b9ece5e7cc8cc0033fbd14ea302338f41632e.proposed_method: A novel Adaptive Rank Allocation framework will be developed, enabling dynamic allocation of computational resources at the granularity of linear layer ranks rather than individual neurons. The core component, the Rank and Neuron Allocator (RaNA) adapter, will be constructed by decomposing each linear layer into two low-rank matrices (A and B) and an input-dependent masker (r(x)), which selects the most important ranks for each input. For QKV, Up-Projection, and Gate-Projection layers, a B-masker will be used to efficiently select ranks based on the magnitude of Bx, while for Down-Projection layers, a neuron-thresholding masker will be employed. FLOP allocation strategies will be implemented to optimally distribute computational resources across adapter components and layers, using grid and line search procedures to minimize output error. The method will be applicable to both MLP and attention layers, and will not rely on activation sparsity, making it suitable for modern architectures using non-sparse activations like SwiGLU and GeLU.
926b9ece5e7cc8cc0033fbd14ea302338f41632e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on state-of-the-art Transformer models including Llama2-7b, Gemma-2b, and multiple GPT-Neox models from the Pythia suite. Datasets such as RedPajama and The Pile will be used for both fine-tuning and evaluation. The proposed RaNA adapters will be compared against several baselines: CATS (a state-of-the-art neuron adapter for SwiGLU), SliceGPT (structured pruning), standard neuron-adaptive adapters, and SVD-based low-rank adapters. Evaluation metrics will include normalized output reconstruction error, perplexity on held-out data, and accuracy on a suite of NLP benchmarks (HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande, Arc-Easy, Arc-Challenge, RACE). FLOP compression rates will be systematically varied, and both theoretical and practical latency will be measured using custom masked GEMV kernels on NVIDIA L40S GPUs. Fine-tuning will be performed with LoRA adapters and AdamW optimizer, and both zero-shot and few-shot downstream task performance will be assessed.
926b9ece5e7cc8cc0033fbd14ea302338f41632e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach generalizes neuron-adaptive methods by introducing adaptive rank allocation at the linear layer level, enabling applicability to both MLP and attention layers regardless of activation sparsity. The RaNA adapter combines low-rank decomposition with input-dependent masking, overcoming the inefficiencies and limitations of previous neuron-adaptive and structured pruning methods. The method introduces a flexible FLOP allocation strategy that balances computational resources across adapter components, leading to improved accuracy-compute and accuracy-latency trade-offs. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in both perplexity and downstream task accuracy at significant FLOP reductions, establishing RaNA as a robust and general solution for efficient inference in modern Transformers.

9286ac6e9b1aacd7d93496eb4615ae7678876d2a.title: Fast Model Editing at Scale
9286ac6e9b1aacd7d93496eb4615ae7678876d2a.research_question: How can large pre-trained neural network models be efficiently and reliably edited post-hoc to correct specific errors or update knowledge, using only a single input-output pair, while preserving the model's performance on unrelated inputs and scaling to models with billions of parameters?
9286ac6e9b1aacd7d93496eb4615ae7678876d2a.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a parameter-efficient, gradient-based editing framework can be developed to enable fast, local, and generalizable edits to large pre-trained models, using only a single input-output pair and without degrading performance on unrelated tasks.
9286ac6e9b1aacd7d93496eb4615ae7678876d2a.proposed_method: A novel framework, Model Editor Networks with Gradient Decomposition (MEND), will be developed to enable rapid and targeted edits to large pre-trained models. MEND consists of lightweight auxiliary neural networks that learn to transform the fine-tuning gradient derived from a single input-output correction into an effective parameter update for the model. The method leverages the low-rank structure of gradients in fully-connected layers, decomposing each gradient into rank-1 outer products of activations and output gradients, thereby reducing the dimensionality of the transformation problem. Each editing network is parameterized as a single-hidden-layer MLP with low-rank weight matrices, residual connections, and layer-specific scaling and offset, allowing the transformation to be both expressive and computationally tractable. The editing networks are trained using an edit dataset to optimize for reliability (successful correction), locality (minimal impact on unrelated inputs), and generality (correctness on semantically related inputs), with losses based on negative log-likelihood and KL divergence.
9286ac6e9b1aacd7d93496eb4615ae7678876d2a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of large-scale language models, including GPT-Neo (2.7B), GPT-J (6B), T5-XL (2.8B), and T5-XXL (11B), as well as smaller models such as BERT-base, BART-base, and distilGPT-2. Editing tasks will include question-answering (zsRE, Natural Questions), fact-checking (FEVER), and text generation (Wikitext-103). Baselines will include standard fine-tuning, fine-tuning with KL-divergence regularization, Editable Neural Networks (ENN), and Knowledge Editor (KE). Evaluation metrics will include edit success rate (accuracy on the edited input and its equivalence neighborhood), drawdown (change in perplexity or accuracy on unrelated data), and the ability to perform batched edits. The experimental setup will ensure identical hyperparameters and edited parameters across methods, with edits applied to the last few MLP layers of transformer blocks. Ablation studies will assess the impact of parameter sharing, initialization, normalization, and architectural variants.
9286ac6e9b1aacd7d93496eb4615ae7678876d2a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a scalable, parameter-efficient method for model editing that is uniquely capable of editing models with over 10 billion parameters using a single GPU. By leveraging the low-rank structure of gradients, the method enables fast, local, and generalizable edits using only a single input-output pair, without requiring access to the original training data or modifying the pre-edit model. The framework supports efficient batched edits and demonstrates superior performance compared to existing model editing algorithms across a range of tasks and model sizes. The gradient decomposition technique and parameter-sharing strategies further enable the method to scale to even larger models, potentially up to hundreds of billions of parameters.

929305892d4ddae575a0fc23227a8139f7681632.title: Jailbroken: How Does LLM Safety Training Fail?
929305892d4ddae575a0fc23227a8139f7681632.research_question: Why do large language models (LLMs) that have undergone safety training remain vulnerable to adversarial 'jailbreak' attacks, and what are the underlying failure modes that enable such attacks to succeed?
929305892d4ddae575a0fc23227a8139f7681632.hypothesis: Two primary failure modes underlie the vulnerability of safety-trained LLMs to jailbreak attacks: (1) Competing objectives between model capabilities (e.g., instruction following, pretraining) and safety goals, and (2) Mismatched generalization, where safety training fails to generalize to domains covered by the model's broader pretraining.
929305892d4ddae575a0fc23227a8139f7681632.proposed_method: A systematic investigation will be conducted into the failure modes of safety training in LLMs by conceptualizing and operationalizing two hypothesized mechanisms: competing objectives and mismatched generalization. The methodology involves designing new jailbreak attacks that specifically exploit these failure modes, such as prefix injection, refusal suppression, and input obfuscation (e.g., Base64 encoding). These attacks will be constructed both manually and with the assistance of LLMs, and will be evaluated for their effectiveness in eliciting restricted or harmful behaviors from state-of-the-art safety-trained LLMs. Ablation studies will be performed to isolate the contributions of specific attack components, and combinations of simple attack strategies will be explored to assess the potential for compounded vulnerabilities.
929305892d4ddae575a0fc23227a8139f7681632.experiment_details: Empirical evaluation will be performed on leading safety-trained LLMs, including OpenAI's GPT-4, GPT-3.5 Turbo, and Anthropic's Claude v1.3. The experiments will utilize two datasets: a curated set of 32 harmful prompts sourced from official red-teaming evaluation sets, and a larger synthetic dataset of 317 harmful prompts generated via few-shot sampling and filtered for restricted behaviors. Each model will be tested against a suite of 30 jailbreak attacks, including both existing and newly designed methods, with outputs manually labeled as 'GOODBOT' (refusal), 'BADBOT' (on-topic harmful response), or 'UNCLEAR'. Evaluation metrics will focus on the proportion of prompts for which the model produces restricted behavior, with additional analysis of adaptive attacks (where the most effective attack is chosen per prompt) and ablation studies to validate the importance of specific attack elements.
929305892d4ddae575a0fc23227a8139f7681632.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a conceptual framework for understanding jailbreak vulnerabilities in safety-trained LLMs, grounded in the identification of two fundamental failure modes. It presents a principled approach to designing and evaluating jailbreak attacks that systematically exploit these failure modes, moving beyond ad hoc or anecdotal attack construction. The methodology enables the creation of new, highly effective attacks that generalize across models and prompt types, and demonstrates that combinations of simple attack strategies can yield near-universal jailbreak success. The research also advances the argument for 'safety-capability parity,' highlighting the necessity for safety mechanisms to match the sophistication of underlying model capabilities, and provides empirical evidence that scaling alone will not resolve these vulnerabilities.

92930ed3560ea6c86d53cf52158bc793b089054d.title: BeaverTails: Towards Improved Safety Alignment of LLM via a Human-Preference Dataset
92930ed3560ea6c86d53cf52158bc793b089054d.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be more effectively aligned with human safety preferences, specifically by disentangling and separately optimizing for helpfulness and harmlessness in their outputs?
92930ed3560ea6c86d53cf52158bc793b089054d.hypothesis: Separately annotating and modeling helpfulness and harmlessness in human preference data, and leveraging this distinction in reward and cost modeling, will enable more effective safety alignment of LLMs compared to traditional single-dimensional preference modeling.
92930ed3560ea6c86d53cf52158bc793b089054d.proposed_method: A large-scale human-preference dataset will be constructed, containing over 330,000 question-answer (QA) pairs annotated for safety meta-labels and classified across 14 harm categories. Each QA pair will be evaluated by multiple annotators in a two-stage process: first, assigning a safety meta-label based on risk-neutrality across harm categories; second, ranking multiple responses to the same prompt independently for helpfulness and harmlessness. Separate reward and cost models will be trained using these decoupled rankings, with the reward model reflecting helpfulness and the cost model reflecting harmlessness. These models will be integrated into a Safe RLHF (Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback) framework, specifically using a Lagrangian variant of Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO-Lagrangian), to fine-tune LLMs such that the policy maximizes helpfulness while minimizing safety cost.
92930ed3560ea6c86d53cf52158bc793b089054d.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training and evaluating moderation, reward, and cost models using the constructed dataset. The moderation model will be benchmarked against existing content moderation APIs (e.g., OpenAI Moderation, Perspective API) and human annotators on a set of red-team prompts covering all harm categories. Reward and cost models will be evaluated on held-out test sets for accuracy in preference prediction and safety classification. Safe RLHF fine-tuning will be performed on the Alpaca-7B model, with pre- and post-fine-tuning outputs assessed for shifts in helpfulness and harmlessness distributions. Baselines will include classifier-based cost models, single-dimensional preference models, and models trained on prior datasets (e.g., HH-RLHF). Evaluation metrics will include preference prediction accuracy, sign accuracy for safety classification, and win rates in head-to-head comparisons as judged by GPT-4.
92930ed3560ea6c86d53cf52158bc793b089054d.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first large-scale human-preference dataset that disentangles helpfulness and harmlessness rankings for LLM outputs, enabling independent optimization of these attributes. The methodology advances safety alignment by modeling cost (harmlessness) as a ranking problem rather than a binary classification, and by integrating these models into a constrained RLHF framework. The approach is claimed to yield improved safety and helpfulness in LLM responses, as demonstrated by ablation studies and head-to-head comparisons with existing methods and datasets.

92a09cdfc19f3f582d89c28c1b4f386299cc69e1.title: SAM 2: Segment Anything in Images and Videos
92a09cdfc19f3f582d89c28c1b4f386299cc69e1.research_question: How can a unified foundation model be developed to enable promptable visual segmentation for both images and videos, supporting interactive and efficient segmentation of arbitrary objects and object parts across diverse scenarios?
92a09cdfc19f3f582d89c28c1b4f386299cc69e1.hypothesis: A transformer-based model equipped with a streaming memory mechanism and trained on a large-scale, diverse video segmentation dataset can achieve state-of-the-art promptable segmentation performance in both images and videos, requiring fewer user interactions and delivering higher accuracy and speed compared to existing approaches.
92a09cdfc19f3f582d89c28c1b4f386299cc69e1.proposed_method: A novel transformer-based architecture will be designed for promptable visual segmentation, capable of processing both images and videos. The model will incorporate a streaming memory mechanism that stores information about objects and previous user interactions, enabling real-time segmentation and efficient mask propagation across video frames. The architecture will include a hierarchical image encoder (e.g., MAE pre-trained Hiera), a memory attention module to condition current frame features on past predictions and prompts, and a promptable mask decoder supporting points, boxes, and masks as input. The model will be trained jointly on image and video data, simulating interactive prompting and corrective clicks, and will be capable of predicting object presence and handling ambiguous prompts by outputting multiple candidate masks. Temporal position encoding and object pointers will be used to enhance memory representation and mask propagation.
92a09cdfc19f3f582d89c28c1b4f386299cc69e1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a newly collected Segment Anything Video (SA-V) dataset, comprising over 50,000 videos and 35.5 million masks, as well as on a variety of established video object segmentation (VOS) and image segmentation benchmarks. Baselines will include state-of-the-art models such as XMem++ and Cutie, with and without integration of the original Segment Anything Model (SAM). Evaluation will cover promptable video segmentation in both offline and online interactive settings, semi-supervised VOS with different prompt types (clicks, boxes, masks), and image segmentation across 37 zero-shot datasets. Metrics will include J&F accuracy for video segmentation and mean IoU (mIoU) for image segmentation, with model speed measured in frames per second (FPS) on a single A100 GPU. The experimental setup will simulate user interactions and measure the number of prompts required to achieve target segmentation accuracy.
92a09cdfc19f3f582d89c28c1b4f386299cc69e1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified, promptable segmentation model for both images and videos, leveraging a streaming memory architecture for real-time video processing and interactive refinement. A large-scale, open-domain video segmentation dataset (SA-V) will be constructed using a model-in-the-loop data engine, enabling annotation of arbitrary objects and parts at unprecedented scale. The method claims significant efficiency gains in annotation, requiring up to 8.4× less manual effort, and achieves state-of-the-art segmentation accuracy with fewer user interactions and faster inference compared to prior models. The open release of the model, dataset, and code is positioned as a major milestone for the field of visual segmentation.

92a8f7f09f3705cb5a6009a42220a6f01ea084e8.title: Language Models as Zero-Shot Planners: Extracting Actionable Knowledge for Embodied Agents
92a8f7f09f3705cb5a6009a42220a6f01ea084e8.research_question: Can large language models (LLMs) be leveraged to generate actionable plans for embodied agents in interactive environments, directly from high-level natural language task descriptions, without additional training or fine-tuning? How can the gap between semantic plausibility and environment executability be bridged to make such plans useful for real-world or simulated agents?
92a8f7f09f3705cb5a6009a42220a6f01ea084e8.hypothesis: Large pre-trained language models, when appropriately prompted and combined with semantic translation and trajectory correction mechanisms, can generate executable and semantically correct action plans for embodied agents in complex environments, without the need for additional model training.
92a8f7f09f3705cb5a6009a42220a6f01ea084e8.proposed_method: The proposed approach involves querying large pre-trained causal language models (such as GPT-3 or Codex) with high-level task descriptions, using in-context learning with a single example to generate free-form action plans. To address the mismatch between generated plans and environment-admissible actions, a semantic translation step is introduced: each generated action phrase is mapped to the most semantically similar admissible action using a pre-trained sentence embedding model (e.g., Sentence-RoBERTa). This translation is performed autoregressively, interleaving plan generation and translation at each step, so that subsequent steps are conditioned on previously translated, admissible actions, allowing for automatic trajectory correction. Additionally, dynamic example selection is used to choose the most relevant demonstration from a set of annotated tasks, further improving the relevance and executability of generated plans.
92a8f7f09f3705cb5a6009a42220a6f01ea084e8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in the VirtualHome environment, which simulates a diverse set of household activities as sequences of atomic actions. The ActivityPrograms knowledge base, containing 292 high-level tasks and 2821 annotated programs, will be used: 88 tasks are held out for evaluation, while the remainder serve as a demonstration set for prompting. Baselines include vanilla LLM generation, fine-tuned models, and human-written programs. Evaluation metrics include executability (syntactic and environment constraint satisfaction), correctness (human evaluation via Amazon Mechanical Turk), and program similarity (Longest Common Subsequence, LCS, with human annotations). Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of semantic translation, trajectory correction, and dynamic example selection. Both quantitative (executability, LCS) and qualitative (human correctness ratings) results will be reported.
92a8f7f09f3705cb5a6009a42220a6f01ea084e8.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a zero-shot planning framework that extracts actionable knowledge from large language models without any additional training or fine-tuning. The method combines semantic translation using sentence embeddings, autoregressive trajectory correction, and dynamic example selection to bridge the gap between free-form language plans and environment-admissible actions. The approach significantly improves plan executability in embodied environments while maintaining high semantic correctness, demonstrating a practical path for grounding LLM knowledge in agent behavior. The methodology is model-agnostic, requires no invasive modifications to LLMs, and is applicable to a wide range of interactive environments.

92b1221e10adf87d89e813b4115b858010bdd33d.title: DMol: A Highly Efficient and Chemical Motif-Preserving Molecule Generation Platform
92b1221e10adf87d89e813b4115b858010bdd33d.research_question: How can the efficiency and chemical motif preservation of generative models for small molecule drug design be improved, while maintaining or enhancing the chemical validity and diversity of generated molecules?
92b1221e10adf87d89e813b4115b858010bdd33d.hypothesis: A graph diffusion model that couples deterministic and random subgraph perturbations, incorporates motif compression into supernodes, and employs a loss function penalizing mismatches in perturbed node and edge counts will enable more efficient molecule generation and better preservation of chemically important motifs, resulting in improved chemical validity and property scores compared to existing methods.
92b1221e10adf87d89e813b4115b858010bdd33d.proposed_method: A novel graph diffusion framework, DMol, will be developed for small molecule generation. The method will use a forward noise process where, at each diffusion step, a deterministic number of nodes and edges are randomly selected for perturbation, with edges confined to the subgraph induced by the selected nodes, ensuring codependence between node and edge noise schedules. Transition probability matrices will be constructed based on the marginal class probabilities in the training data, and the number of diffusion steps will be proportional to the graph size, dramatically reducing computational cost. The loss function will include standard cross-entropy terms for node and edge classification, as well as mean squared error penalties to enforce that the number of perturbed nodes and edges matches the deterministic schedule, aiding motif preservation. A motif compression module will convert frequently occurring chemical motifs (e.g., carbon rings) into supernodes, which are diffused as special node types and decoded back into motifs during sampling, ensuring chemical validity and ease of reconstruction.
92b1221e10adf87d89e813b4115b858010bdd33d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard molecular graph datasets, including QM9, MOSES, and GUACAMOL, with appropriate train/validation/test splits (e.g., 100K/20K/13K for QM9, 85/5/10% for larger datasets). DMol will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as GraphVAE, GT-VAE, Set2GraphVAE, SPECTRE, GraphNVP, GDSS, GruM, DiGress, DisCo, and DeFoG. Evaluation metrics will include SMILES validity, uniqueness, novelty, ChEMBL-likeness (CL), QED, shingle distance (SD), Frechet ChemNet Distance (FCD), scaffold similarity, and computational metrics such as average number of diffusion steps, sample time, and training time. Hyperparameters will be tuned for each dataset, and motif sets for compression will be selected based on motif frequency. Experiments will be run on high-performance GPUs, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of motif compression and loss components.
92b1221e10adf87d89e813b4115b858010bdd33d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new motif-preserving graph diffusion model that couples deterministic and random subgraph perturbations, allowing for an order-of-magnitude reduction in diffusion steps compared to prior methods. The motif compression mechanism enables direct integration and reconstruction of chemically important motifs as supernodes, ensuring chemical validity and ease of decoding. The loss function is augmented with penalties that enforce motif and substructure preservation, which, together with the noise scheduling, leads to improved chemical property scores and motif distribution fidelity. The method achieves superior performance on both classical and biochemically relevant metrics, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines in validity, novelty, ChEMBL-likeness, and QED, while significantly reducing computational cost.

92c1d1f6488de9694cc881f06bddd9fa8bb55a35.title: The Statistical Complexity of Interactive Decision Making
92c1d1f6488de9694cc881f06bddd9fa8bb55a35.research_question: What are the fundamental statistical complexity measures that govern sample-efficient learning and optimal regret in general interactive decision making problems, including structured bandits and reinforcement learning, and how can these measures guide the design of adaptive, general-purpose algorithms?
92c1d1f6488de9694cc881f06bddd9fa8bb55a35.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a single, unified complexity measure can be identified that both lower bounds and tightly characterizes the sample complexity and regret in interactive decision making settings, and that this measure can be leveraged to design algorithms that are optimal up to estimation complexity.
92c1d1f6488de9694cc881f06bddd9fa8bb55a35.proposed_method: A general framework for interactive decision making, termed Decision Making with Structured Observations (DMSO), will be formalized to encompass a wide range of problems including structured bandits, reinforcement learning, and contextual variants. Within this framework, a new complexity measure called the Decision-Estimation Coefficient (DEC) will be defined, quantifying the trade-off between regret and information acquisition via Hellinger distance-based divergences. The DEC will be used to derive minimax lower bounds on regret for arbitrary model classes, establishing it as a necessary condition for learnability. Building on this, a meta-algorithm called Estimation-to-Decisions (E2D) will be developed, which reduces any online estimation algorithm for a model class to an interactive decision making algorithm by adaptively selecting decisions to balance estimation error and regret, using the DEC as a guide. The E2D algorithm will be analyzed to show that it achieves regret bounds matching the DEC-based lower bounds up to a factor depending on the estimation complexity of the model class.
92c1d1f6488de9694cc881f06bddd9fa8bb55a35.experiment_details: Experiments will involve both theoretical and empirical evaluation. Theoretical analysis will recover and unify lower and upper bounds for canonical problems such as multi-armed bandits, linear bandits, Lipschitz bandits, and various reinforcement learning settings (tabular, linear, and with function approximation). The framework will be instantiated on these problems to compute the DEC and compare the resulting regret bounds to existing minimax rates. Empirical evaluation may include simulated environments for structured bandits and reinforcement learning, using standard datasets and benchmarks, with performance compared against established baselines such as UCB, Thompson Sampling, and recent model-based RL algorithms. Evaluation metrics will include cumulative regret, sample complexity to reach a target accuracy, and computational efficiency of the E2D meta-algorithm.
92c1d1f6488de9694cc881f06bddd9fa8bb55a35.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the Decision-Estimation Coefficient as a unified, necessary, and sufficient complexity measure for interactive decision making, subsuming and generalizing prior notions such as VC dimension, eluder dimension, and Bellman rank. The Estimation-to-Decisions (E2D) meta-algorithm provides the first universal reduction from online estimation to decision making, achieving optimal regret up to estimation complexity. The approach yields a theory of learnability for interactive decision making, recovers all known lower bounds for bandits and reinforcement learning, and offers new perspectives that unify Bayesian and frequentist algorithmic principles. The framework also seamlessly extends to contextual and high-dimensional settings, enabling new oracle-efficient algorithms for contextual bandits and reinforcement learning.

92c3dc3291230acce2303e4b03a05dca47610ef7.title: Bayes-optimal prediction with frequentist coverage control
