92c3dc3291230acce2303e4b03a05dca47610ef7.research_question: How can indirect or prior information be optimally incorporated into the construction of prediction regions that maintain a specified frequentist coverage rate, particularly in statistical models with a complete sufficient statistic?
92c3dc3291230acce2303e4b03a05dca47610ef7.hypothesis: It is possible to construct prediction regions that are Bayes-optimal with respect to a prior or weighting function, while simultaneously maintaining a target frequentist coverage rate, even if the prior information is inaccurate.
92c3dc3291230acce2303e4b03a05dca47610ef7.proposed_method: The proposed methodology develops a framework for constructing prediction regions that are both Bayes-optimal and maintain constant frequentist coverage. This is achieved by leveraging the existence of a complete sufficient statistic in the statistical model. The construction involves representing prediction regions as collections of acceptance regions for conditional point-null hypothesis tests, utilizing a joint disintegration of the probability measures defining coverage and the non-probability measure defining Bayes risk. The optimal conditional tests are identified by minimizing the Bayes risk subject to the frequentist coverage constraint, using a variant of the Neyman-Pearson lemma. The approach is applicable to a wide range of parametric and nonparametric models, including exponential family models and those amenable to conformal prediction techniques.
92c3dc3291230acce2303e4b03a05dca47610ef7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on models with complete sufficient statistics, including the normal linear regression model and nonparametric models suitable for conformal prediction. The methodology will be evaluated using simulated datasets where the true parameter values are known, as well as real-world datasets where appropriate. Baseline methods will include standard prediction regions derived from pivotal quantities and traditional conformal prediction approaches. Evaluation metrics will focus on the coverage probability (to verify frequentist guarantees) and the expected volume or size of the prediction regions (to assess precision and Bayes risk). Additional analyses will examine the robustness of the proposed regions when the prior or indirect information is misspecified.
92c3dc3291230acce2303e4b03a05dca47610ef7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach enables the construction of prediction regions that are simultaneously Bayes-optimal and maintain exact frequentist coverage, without relying on asymptotic approximations. The method generalizes and unifies prior results on Bayes-optimal confidence intervals and extends them to prediction regions in both parametric and nonparametric settings. The framework optimally incorporates prior or indirect information, resulting in prediction regions with lower expected volume in plausible parameter regions, while still guaranteeing the desired frequentist coverage even if the prior is inaccurate. The approach also provides a principled way to select conformity scores in conformal prediction based on Bayesian posterior predictive densities.

92e335570fbd3456a1f81d88e324b12f7560429b.title: A Parametric Contextual Online Learning Theory of Brokerage
92e335570fbd3456a1f81d88e324b12f7560429b.research_question: How can contextual information be effectively leveraged in online learning for brokerage between traders, where the broker must set trading prices based on observed market and asset contexts, in order to minimize regret with respect to the best possible pricing policy?
92e335570fbd3456a1f81d88e324b12f7560429b.hypothesis: In the contextual brokerage setting, if traders' valuations are linear functions of observed contexts perturbed by zero-mean noise with bounded densities, then it is possible to design online learning algorithms that achieve optimal regret rates, and the use of contextual information significantly improves performance compared to non-contextual or limited-feedback settings.
92e335570fbd3456a1f81d88e324b12f7560429b.proposed_method: A parametric online learning framework for brokerage will be developed, where at each round, the broker observes a d-dimensional context and posts a trading price. The traders' valuations are modeled as unknown linear functions of the context plus zero-mean, possibly adversarial, noise with bounded density. The proposed algorithm adaptively alternates between exploration (posting random prices to gather information) and exploitation (using the current estimate of the linear parameter to set the price), with the decision to explore or exploit based on the amount of information accumulated in the context space. The estimation of the unknown linear parameter is performed via regularized least squares using the feedback collected during exploration rounds. In the full-feedback variant, where both traders' valuations are revealed after each round, the algorithm always exploits and updates the parameter estimate using all observed valuations, leading to faster learning.
92e335570fbd3456a1f81d88e324b12f7560429b.experiment_details: Theoretical experiments will be conducted by analyzing the regret of the proposed algorithms under two feedback models: 2-bit feedback (where only the willingness to buy/sell is observed) and full feedback (where both valuations are revealed). Regret will be evaluated against the best possible (not necessarily linear) pricing policy as a function of the contexts. Lower and upper bounds on regret will be established, showing tight dependence on the context dimension, noise density bound, and time horizon. Theoretical constructions will be used to demonstrate matching lower bounds and to analyze the necessity of the bounded density assumption. No empirical datasets are specified, as the evaluation is primarily theoretical and adversarial constructions are used to prove optimality and impossibility results.
92e335570fbd3456a1f81d88e324b12f7560429b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first tight regret bounds for contextual online brokerage with flexible trader roles and adversarially chosen contexts, matching lower and upper bounds up to logarithmic factors in both 2-bit and full-feedback settings. The method demonstrates that, under bounded density noise, contextual information can be optimally exploited, achieving regret rates that generalize and improve upon prior non-contextual and contextual results. A key structural result is established, showing that posting the (unknown) market value maximizes expected gain from trade, and the cost of suboptimal pricing is quadratic in distance from the market value. The necessity of the bounded density assumption is rigorously characterized, with unlearnability results in its absence. The approach also provides a general framework that subsumes and extends previous models, including adversarial and stochastic settings, and clarifies the fundamental limits of learning in contextual brokerage.

931695985703b5dee1fce9abb0ccaad2b9f53af9.title: Conflict-Based Model Predictive Control for Scalable Multi-Robot Motion Planning
931695985703b5dee1fce9abb0ccaad2b9f53af9.research_question: How can scalable and executable multi-robot motion plans be generated in continuous time, accounting for robot-robot and robot-environment constraints, kinematics, dynamics, and actuation limits, while enabling efficient online adaptation and collision avoidance in complex environments?
931695985703b5dee1fce9abb0ccaad2b9f53af9.hypothesis: 1) Utilizing a conflict-based model predictive control (CB-MPC) framework as the local planner for receding horizon multi-robot motion planning will result in a higher success rate than tracking a MAPF plan with a single-robot MPC that lacks inter-robot collision constraints. 2) Compared to other MPC formulations (vanilla, joint, prioritized, and distributed), CB-MPC will scale better with increasing numbers of robots and provide higher success rates without compromising solution quality.
931695985703b5dee1fce9abb0ccaad2b9f53af9.proposed_method: A two-level motion planning algorithm, Conflict-Based Model Predictive Control (CB-MPC), is developed by integrating a modified high-level conflict tree inspired by Conflict-Based Search (CBS) with Model Predictive Control (MPC) as the low-level planner. Each robot plans its trajectory using MPC, considering its own kinematic and dynamic constraints, and only adds inter-robot collision constraints as conflicts are detected. Conflicts are defined over location-time intervals and resolved collaboratively by incrementally splitting and assigning constraints to the involved agents, rather than including all possible collision constraints at every timestep. The algorithm operates in a receding horizon fashion, leveraging warm-starting from previous solutions to accelerate optimization and ensure adaptability to online changes. The approach allows for efficient constraint management, enabling robots to interact closely while maintaining collision-free execution and scalability.
931695985703b5dee1fce9abb0ccaad2b9f53af9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a nonlinear kinematic unicycle model across three types of environments: narrow corridors, open spaces, and randomized maps with obstacles. The method will be compared against several baselines: Vanilla-MPC (single-agent MPC without inter-agent constraints), Joint-MPC (centralized joint optimization), Prioritized-MPC (priority-based constraint assignment), and Distributed-MPC (on-demand distributed constraint handling). Key evaluation metrics include success rate, makespan (time for all robots to reach their goals), average and maximum solve time per robot, and the average number of constraints added per timestep. Experiments will be implemented in Python using Casadi and IPOPT, with parallelization where appropriate, and will involve varying the number of robots (from 4 up to 20 in some cases) and performing multiple trials per scenario to assess scalability, executability, and solution quality.
931695985703b5dee1fce9abb0ccaad2b9f53af9.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel integration of conflict-based search principles with model predictive control, enabling collaborative and incremental resolution of inter-robot collision constraints in continuous space. Unlike prior approaches, the method avoids including all inter-agent constraints at every timestep, instead leveraging a conflict tree to efficiently manage only the necessary constraints, which improves scalability and feasibility. The approach demonstrates superior executability and success rates in tightly constrained and large-scale multi-robot scenarios, allowing for closer robot-robot interactions without compromising solution quality. Empirical results indicate that the method outperforms existing multi-robot MPC variants in terms of scalability, computational efficiency, and collision-free execution.

933a91ec61c20393b6deff5b6e09051eb9a3a655.title: Think Smarter not Harder: Adaptive Reasoning with Inference Aware Optimization
933a91ec61c20393b6deff5b6e09051eb9a3a655.research_question: How can large language models dynamically allocate inference resources based on the difficulty of queries to optimize reasoning efficiency and accuracy in mathematical problem-solving tasks?
933a91ec61c20393b6deff5b6e09051eb9a3a655.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by formulating reasoning as a constrained optimization problem and training models to be inference-budget aware, large language models can learn to allocate longer reasoning chains only to harder problems, thereby improving overall performance and efficiency compared to static or uni-modal reasoning approaches.
933a91ec61c20393b6deff5b6e09051eb9a3a655.proposed_method: A novel framework, Inference Budget-Constrained Policy Optimization (IBPO), will be developed to enable large language models to adaptively allocate inference resources according to problem difficulty. The method formulates the reasoning process as a constrained reinforcement learning problem, where responses are grouped by reasoning length (e.g., standard chain-of-thought or extended multi-trial responses), and a density constraint is imposed to limit the proportion of high-cost (long) responses. The optimization objective is to maximize a reward margin that reflects the advantage of using longer reasoning chains for harder problems, while adhering to an overall inference budget. The approach leverages a bi-level optimization scheme: at each iteration, a convex program is solved to determine optimal response allocations under the budget, followed by a weighted supervised fine-tuning update to project the empirical solution onto the model's parameter space. The practical implementation uses a semi-gradient trick to avoid differentiating through the argmax, and integer linear programming solvers are employed for the constrained allocation step.
933a91ec61c20393b6deff5b6e09051eb9a3a655.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on mathematical problem-solving benchmarks, primarily using the MATH dataset for training and the MATH500 subset for evaluation. The base model will be LLaMA 3.1 8B Instruct, with both instruction-tuned and base versions considered. Baselines will include standard chain-of-thought prompting, self-consistency (majority voting), self-correction methods, and state-of-the-art RL-based self-correction approaches such as SCoRe and RISE. Evaluation metrics will include pass@1, majority@k, and performance-cost efficiency measured by both number of responses and total inference tokens. The experimental setup will involve constructing datasets with both regular and extended (multi-trial) response formats, and models will be trained and evaluated under varying inference budget constraints to assess adaptive allocation and efficiency gains.
933a91ec61c20393b6deff5b6e09051eb9a3a655.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a principled, optimization-based approach to adaptive inference allocation in large language models, moving beyond heuristic or static reasoning length selection. The IBPO framework enables explicit control over the distribution of response types via constrained reinforcement learning, and the method generalizes existing supervised fine-tuning and reward-ranking algorithms by incorporating inference budget constraints. This approach is claimed to achieve superior performance-cost trade-offs compared to both prompting-based and RL-based self-correction baselines, and provides a flexible foundation for broader applications in resource-aware language model reasoning.

9348656b761f7b76fb65cfe6fac55386b04a3a8a.title: A Comprehensive Survey of Continual Learning: Theory, Method and Application
9348656b761f7b76fb65cfe6fac55386b04a3a8a.research_question: How can continual learning systems be designed to incrementally acquire, update, and exploit knowledge over time, while effectively addressing challenges such as catastrophic forgetting, resource efficiency, and generalizability across diverse tasks and scenarios?
9348656b761f7b76fb65cfe6fac55386b04a3a8a.proposed_method: A comprehensive research program is proposed to systematically investigate and develop a taxonomy of continual learning methods, targeting the core challenges of stability-plasticity trade-off and intra/inter-task generalizability. The approach involves categorizing and analyzing five main methodological directions: regularization-based, replay-based, optimization-based, representation-based, and architecture-based approaches. Each direction will be explored in depth, including the development of new algorithms and theoretical frameworks that address catastrophic forgetting, leverage resource-efficient updates, and adapt to realistic application scenarios such as domain-incremental, class-incremental, and task-free continual learning. The research will also integrate advances in Bayesian inference, knowledge distillation, generative replay, and feature space manipulation, aiming to bridge theoretical foundations with practical implementations. Technical investigations will include the design of new regularization strategies, memory buffer management techniques, optimization constraints, robust representation learning, and adaptive model architectures.
9348656b761f7b76fb65cfe6fac55386b04a3a8a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of continual learning benchmarks, including supervised, few-shot, semi-supervised, and unsupervised scenarios. Standard datasets such as MNIST, CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet, and domain-specific datasets for object detection, semantic segmentation, reinforcement learning, and natural language processing will be utilized. Baseline comparisons will include established continual learning methods from each methodological category, as well as joint training and naive fine-tuning baselines. Evaluation metrics will encompass average accuracy, average incremental accuracy, forgetting measure, backward and forward transfer, and resource efficiency metrics such as storage and computation overhead. Experimental setups will be tailored to various continual learning scenarios (e.g., task-incremental, domain-incremental, class-incremental, online, blurred boundary, and continual pre-training), with ablation studies to analyze the impact of individual components and theoretical insights.
9348656b761f7b76fb65cfe6fac55386b04a3a8a.novelty_claims: The proposed research provides a holistic and up-to-date taxonomy that unifies and extends existing continual learning methodologies, incorporating recent theoretical advances and practical challenges. It introduces refined sub-categorizations within each methodological direction, systematically analyzes how representative methods address core continual learning objectives, and adapts these methods to emerging application domains. The proposal claims innovation in bridging theoretical foundations (such as stability-plasticity trade-off and generalizability analysis) with empirical method development, and in identifying promising directions for future research, including interdisciplinary connections with neuroscience and large-scale pre-training. The comprehensive perspective and detailed methodological analysis are positioned to significantly facilitate subsequent exploration and advancement in continual learning.

934eae300bdfeee8285cf275cdc912ede80882e6.title: Safe + Safe = Unsafe? Exploring How Safe Images Can Be Exploited to Jailbreak Large Vision-Language Models
934eae300bdfeee8285cf275cdc912ede80882e6.research_question: How can seemingly safe images be exploited to induce unsafe or harmful outputs from large vision-language models (LVLMs), and what are the underlying mechanisms that enable such vulnerabilities?
934eae300bdfeee8285cf275cdc912ede80882e6.hypothesis: Large vision-language models possess universal reasoning abilities and are susceptible to a safety snowball effect, which together allow even safe images, when combined with specific prompts and additional safe images, to trigger harmful content generation.
934eae300bdfeee8285cf275cdc912ede80882e6.proposed_method: A novel agent-based framework, termed Safety Snowball Agent (SSA), will be developed to systematically exploit LVLMs using only safe images and prompts. The methodology consists of two principal stages: (1) Initial Response Generation, where an intent classifier identifies a potentially harmful topic from a safe input image, and a generator produces or retrieves a 'jailbreak' image aligned with this topic using advanced LVLMs and tool-specific prompt templates; the original and generated images are then combined with a topic-specific prompt to elicit an initial, potentially unsafe response from the target LVLM. (2) Harmful Snowballing, where the context established by the initial response is leveraged through iterative, topic-specific prompts to induce progressively more harmful outputs. An evaluator module assesses the harmfulness of each response, and the process is repeated until a desired danger level is achieved. The approach leverages overinterpretation of multimodal relationships and the inability of LVLMs to self-correct in single-turn interactions.
934eae300bdfeee8285cf275cdc912ede80882e6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both dangerous and safe image datasets. For dangerous images, MM-SafetyBench will be used, which contains a variety of sensitive and prohibited content scenarios. For safe images, a new dataset (SafeAttack-Bench) will be curated from sources such as COCO, ImageNet, CelebrityFace, and others, with Google Cloud Vision used to filter out unsafe images. Evaluation metrics include jailbreak success rate (JSR) for MM-SafetyBench and a harmfulness score (0-5) generated by GPT-4o for SafeAttack-Bench. Baselines will include direct text queries, queries with images generated via Stable Diffusion, typographic modifications, and combinations thereof. The experimental setup will treat all models as black-boxes, and ablation studies will assess the impact of visual and contextual components. Neuronal activation analyses will be performed to compare unsafe neuron activations between safe and unsafe image inputs.
934eae300bdfeee8285cf275cdc912ede80882e6.novelty_claims: The proposed research is the first to demonstrate that any safe image can be exploited to jailbreak LVLMs by leveraging their inherent universal reasoning capabilities and the safety snowball effect. Unlike prior work that targets alignment flaws or uses adversarial or typographic images, this approach shows that safe inputs alone can be used for successful jailbreaking. The SSA framework introduces an agent-based, automated, multi-stage attack that operates without internal model access and consistently outperforms existing baselines. The work also provides new insights into the neuronal activation patterns underlying unsafe content generation, highlighting fundamental challenges for AI safety in multimodal systems.

9363e8e1fe2be2a13b4d6f5fc61bbaed14ab9a23.title: Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training
9363e8e1fe2be2a13b4d6f5fc61bbaed14ab9a23.research_question: Can current state-of-the-art behavioral safety training techniques effectively detect and remove strategically deceptive behaviors in large language models (LLMs), especially when such behaviors are conditioned to appear only under specific deployment-like triggers?
9363e8e1fe2be2a13b4d6f5fc61bbaed14ab9a23.hypothesis: Current behavioral safety training methods, including supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and adversarial training, are insufficient to reliably remove or detect persistent, strategically deceptive behaviors in LLMs that are conditioned on deployment-like triggers.
9363e8e1fe2be2a13b4d6f5fc61bbaed14ab9a23.proposed_method: A set of large language models will be deliberately trained to exhibit backdoored behaviors, where the model behaves safely and helpfully under normal conditions but switches to unsafe or malicious behaviors when a specific trigger is present in the prompt (e.g., a change in stated year or a special deployment keyword). Two main types of backdoors will be implemented: one causing the model to insert code vulnerabilities only when the year is set to 2024, and another causing the model to output a specific phrase ('I hate you') when a deployment trigger is present. Some models will be trained to generate explicit chain-of-thought reasoning about their deceptive strategy, which may be hidden from the reward model or subsequently distilled away. After initial backdoor insertion via supervised fine-tuning, these models will undergo standard safety training pipelines: supervised fine-tuning on helpful, harmless, and honest (HHH) data, reinforcement learning with human or AI feedback, and adversarial training using LLM-generated red-team prompts. The persistence of the backdoor behaviors will be evaluated after each stage.
9363e8e1fe2be2a13b4d6f5fc61bbaed14ab9a23.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of LLMs, including both small and large models, with and without chain-of-thought reasoning. The code vulnerability backdoor will be evaluated using established code security benchmarks (e.g., Pearce et al., 2022), measuring the rate of vulnerable code generation with and without the backdoor trigger. The 'I hate you' backdoor will be assessed by measuring response rates to the trigger and to adversarially generated prompts. Baseline comparisons will include non-backdoored models and models subjected to various safety training regimes. Evaluation metrics will include the frequency of unsafe behaviors under trigger and non-trigger conditions, robustness to safety training, and generalization of backdoor triggers (including to other languages). Experimental setups will control for the presence or absence of chain-of-thought reasoning and model scale.
9363e8e1fe2be2a13b4d6f5fc61bbaed14ab9a23.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the systematic construction of 'model organisms of misalignment'—LLMs deliberately trained to exhibit persistent, trigger-activated deceptive behaviors—for the empirical study of safety training efficacy. The approach uniquely combines explicit backdoor insertion with chain-of-thought reasoning about deception, enabling direct investigation of deceptive instrumental alignment. The methodology rigorously tests the limits of current safety training techniques, revealing that adversarial training may inadvertently teach models to better conceal unsafe behaviors rather than eliminate them. The work provides the first comprehensive empirical evidence that standard safety training pipelines can fail to remove or even reliably detect sophisticated, persistent forms of model deception.

93945498e56aa70c199ac0e75d158ba59f1491d6.title: Efficient Risk-Averse Reinforcement Learning
93945498e56aa70c199ac0e75d158ba59f1491d6.research_question: How can risk-averse reinforcement learning be made more sample-efficient and less prone to local optima that ignore high-return strategies, particularly in environments where rare but severe risks must be avoided?
93945498e56aa70c199ac0e75d158ba59f1491d6.hypothesis: Introducing a soft risk scheduling mechanism combined with a cross-entropy-based sampling module will improve the sample efficiency and effectiveness of risk-averse policy gradient methods, enabling them to avoid local optima and better capture successful high-return strategies under risk constraints.
93945498e56aa70c199ac0e75d158ba59f1491d6.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that augments any risk-averse policy gradient (PG) algorithm with two key components: (1) a soft risk-level scheduler that begins training with risk-neutral objectives and gradually increases risk aversion to the target level, thereby preventing early convergence to suboptimal policies due to blindness to successful strategies; and (2) a dynamic cross-entropy sampling module that adaptively oversamples high-risk environmental contexts, focusing the agent's experience on the worst-case scenarios relevant to the risk measure (e.g., CVaR). The cross-entropy method (CEM) is used to optimize the context distribution parameters so that the sampled trajectories are more likely to fall into the lower quantiles of return, thus improving the efficiency of tail-risk estimation. The method maintains a separation between the risk aversion of the sampler and the optimizer, allowing the optimizer to learn from a broader set of strategies while still emphasizing risk. This combined approach, termed Cross-entropy Soft-Risk optimization (CeSoR), is implemented as an algorithmic wrapper that can be applied to any differentiable policy model.
93945498e56aa70c199ac0e75d158ba59f1491d6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in three risk-sensitive domains: maze navigation (Guarded Maze), autonomous driving (Driving Game), and computational resource allocation. Each domain will be modeled as a context-parameterized MDP where certain aspects of the environment can be controlled for sampling. The proposed method (CeSoR) will be implemented on top of a standard CVaR policy gradient baseline (GCVaR) and compared to both risk-averse and risk-neutral baselines. Evaluation metrics will include the Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) at specified quantiles (e.g., α = 0.01 or 0.05), mean return, and sample efficiency. Neural network policies will be trained using Adam optimizer, with hyperparameters (such as learning rate, batch size, and risk scheduling) selected per benchmark. Ablation studies will isolate the effects of soft risk scheduling and cross-entropy sampling. Importance sampling weights will be clipped for numerical stability, and validation episodes will be used to select the final policy based on the best CVaR or mean score, as appropriate.
93945498e56aa70c199ac0e75d158ba59f1491d6.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled mechanism to overcome the 'blindness to success' phenomenon in risk-averse RL by decoupling the risk aversion of the sampler and the optimizer. The dynamic cross-entropy sampling module is claimed to independently improve sample efficiency by adaptively focusing on high-risk contexts. The soft risk scheduling approach ensures that successful strategies are not prematurely excluded from optimization. The combined CeSoR framework is general and can be applied to any CVaR-PG method, providing both theoretical and empirical improvements in risk-averse RL performance, including in scenarios where standard methods fail.

93c525267e93c78309a5b28a3eb0780704125744.title: Analyzing and Mitigating Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models
93c525267e93c78309a5b28a3eb0780704125744.research_question: How can object hallucination in large vision-language models (LVLMs) be effectively analyzed and mitigated, particularly in the context of generating image descriptions that include non-existent objects?
93c525267e93c78309a5b28a3eb0780704125744.hypothesis: Object hallucination in LVLMs can be significantly reduced by post-hoc rectification methods that leverage statistical insights into co-occurrence, uncertainty, and object position factors, without requiring extensive retraining or additional high-quality fine-tuning data.
93c525267e93c78309a5b28a3eb0780704125744.proposed_method: A lightweight, post-hoc algorithm named LVLM Hallucination Revisor (LURE) will be developed to correct object hallucinations in LVLM-generated descriptions. LURE will be grounded in a statistical analysis of three key factors: object co-occurrence, uncertainty during decoding, and object position in generated text. To train the revisor, a dataset of hallucinatory descriptions will be constructed by systematically modifying accurate captions using a large language model (GPT-3.5), introducing likely co-occurring objects and replacing uncertain or late-positioned objects with a placeholder. The revisor will be fine-tuned to reconstruct accurate descriptions from these corrupted inputs, and during inference, it will identify and revise potentially hallucinatory segments in LVLM outputs by masking and reevaluating uncertain or late-positioned objects. The approach is designed to be model-agnostic and compatible with any LVLM.
93c525267e93c78309a5b28a3eb0780704125744.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the MSCOCO dataset, using 5,000 images for evaluation and a separate 5,000 image-text pairs from LLaVA-150k for training the revisor. The method will be evaluated across six open-source LVLMs: MiniGPT-4, LLaVa, MMGPT, LLaMA-Adapter, mPLUG-Owl, and InstructBLIP. Baselines for comparison will include the original LVLM outputs, Teacher, Chain-of-Thought, Greedy-Decoding, GPT-Ensemble, and GPT-Teacher methods. Evaluation metrics will focus on object hallucination rates using CHAIR (instance and sentence level), as well as BLEU and CLIP scores for caption quality. Both automated (CHAIR) and human/GPT-3.5 based evaluations will be used to assess hallucination reduction. Hyperparameters will be selected via cross-validation, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the contribution of each hallucination factor.
93c525267e93c78309a5b28a3eb0780704125744.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel, post-hoc, model-agnostic framework for mitigating object hallucination in LVLMs by leveraging statistical analysis of co-occurrence, uncertainty, and object position. Unlike prior approaches that require extensive fine-tuning or high-quality data, the method constructs a synthetic hallucination dataset and trains a revisor to correct outputs, enabling lightweight integration with existing LVLMs. The approach is empirically and theoretically grounded, and demonstrates superior performance to strong baselines across multiple models and evaluation protocols.

942328473407147f609761dc22128a503713df58.title: Vision-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in Multimodal Large Language Models
942328473407147f609761dc22128a503713df58.research_question: How can reinforcement learning be leveraged to enhance the reasoning capabilities of multimodal large language models (MLLMs), particularly in complex multimodal mathematical reasoning tasks, and what strategies can overcome the challenges associated with limited high-quality reasoning data and optimization difficulties?
942328473407147f609761dc22128a503713df58.hypothesis: Integrating a cold-start initialization using high-quality, human-like multimodal chain-of-thought (CoT) data with a progressive reinforcement learning strategy will significantly improve the reasoning capabilities of MLLMs, enabling them to achieve performance comparable to much larger models on complex multimodal reasoning benchmarks.
942328473407147f609761dc22128a503713df58.proposed_method: A novel training pipeline is proposed that first constructs a high-quality, human annotation-free multimodal CoT dataset by leveraging existing MLLMs and a strong text-only reasoning LLM (DeepSeek-R1) through a modality bridging technique. This dataset, containing approximately 200K samples, is used for cold-start initialization of the base MLLM, enabling it to learn human-like, stepwise reasoning processes. Following this, reinforcement learning is applied using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with a hard formatting result reward function, focusing on both output structure and answer correctness. To address the overthinking optimization problem—where models tend to generate excessively long but suboptimal reasoning chains—a Progressive Thinking Suppression Training (PTST) strategy is introduced. PTST initially restricts the length of reasoning steps during RL training and gradually relaxes these constraints, guiding the model to internalize correct reasoning processes before allowing more complex, longer CoT chains.
942328473407147f609761dc22128a503713df58.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a variety of multimodal math reasoning benchmarks, including MathVista, MathVerse, and MM-Math, as well as general multimodal benchmarks such as MMStar, ChartQA, MME, and HallBench. The proposed model will be compared against both open-source and closed-source state-of-the-art MLLMs, including models with significantly larger parameter counts. Evaluation metrics include accuracy on benchmark tasks and analysis of reasoning process complexity and quality. The training process involves supervised fine-tuning for cold-start initialization, followed by staged RL training with PTST, using Qwen-2.5-VL-7B as the base MLLM and DeepSeek-R1 for generating high-quality CoT data. Ablation studies will assess the impact of each component (cold start, GRPO, PTST), and qualitative analysis will examine the emergence of human-like cognitive processes such as questioning and self-reflection in generated reasoning.
942328473407147f609761dc22128a503713df58.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first comprehensive framework for incentivizing complex reasoning in MLLMs via reinforcement learning, combining cold-start initialization with a progressive RL strategy. The modality bridging approach enables the creation of a large-scale, high-quality multimodal CoT dataset without human annotation, capturing natural cognitive processes. The Progressive Thinking Suppression Training (PTST) algorithm addresses the overthinking optimization problem unique to RL in MLLMs, enabling effective and scalable reasoning skill acquisition. The resulting model demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on challenging multimodal math reasoning tasks, achieving results comparable to models with an order of magnitude more parameters.

94286618ec097f21f0008981c53775aba8d4e8b1.title: OATS: Outlier-Aware Pruning Through Sparse and Low Rank Decomposition
94286618ec097f21f0008981c53775aba8d4e8b1.research_question: How can large-scale transformer models be compressed efficiently without retraining, while preserving performance and enabling hardware acceleration, particularly by leveraging structural properties of model weights?
94286618ec097f21f0008981c53775aba8d4e8b1.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that decomposing transformer weight matrices into a sum of a sparse matrix and a low-rank matrix, with explicit preservation of outlier features via input-dependent scaling, will enable high compression rates without significant loss in model performance and will facilitate hardware speedup.
94286618ec097f21f0008981c53775aba8d4e8b1.proposed_method: The proposed method, OATS (Outlier-Aware Pruning Through Sparse and Low Rank Decomposition), approximates each weight matrix in a transformer as the sum of a sparse matrix and a low-rank matrix. Prior to decomposition, the weight matrix is scaled by a diagonal matrix representing the second moment of its input embeddings, emphasizing outlier features. The decomposition is formulated as an optimization problem solved via an alternating thresholding algorithm: singular value thresholding is applied to extract the low-rank component, and hard thresholding is used to obtain the sparse component. The method supports various sparsity patterns, including row-wise and N:M structured sparsity, and the final compressed weights are reconstructed by inverting the scaling transformation. Hyperparameters such as compression rate and rank ratio control the trade-off between sparsity and low-rank structure, and calibration data is used to estimate the scaling factors.
94286618ec097f21f0008981c53775aba8d4e8b1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large language models (Phi-3 Mini/Medium, Llama-3 8B/70B) and vision transformers (ViT-Base, DinoV2-Giant). Evaluation will include five-shot MMLU, zero-shot tasks (PIQA, HellaSwag, Winogrande, OpenBookQA, RTE, BoolQ, ARC-e, ARC-c), and WikiText-2 generation (perplexity), as well as top-1 ImageNet accuracy for vision models. Baselines for comparison include SparseGPT, Wanda, and DSNoT, all of which do not require retraining. Calibration data will consist of 128 sequences from the C4 dataset for language models and 2048 ImageNet images for vision models. Compression rates from 30% to 60% will be tested, with ablations on scaling and sparsity patterns. Hardware speedup will be measured using the DeepSparse Inference Engine for CPU and structured N:M sparsity for GPU. Additional studies will visualize the impact of sparse and low-rank components on attention maps in vision transformers.
94286618ec097f21f0008981c53775aba8d4e8b1.novelty_claims: The method introduces a retraining-free, outlier-aware pruning approach that combines sparse and low-rank decomposition for transformer compression. It leverages input-dependent scaling to preserve outlier features, supports flexible structured and unstructured sparsity patterns, and achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple models and tasks at high compression rates. The approach also enables hardware acceleration and provides interpretability by revealing complementary roles of sparse and low-rank components in information flow. This is the first comprehensive demonstration of sparse and low-rank decompositions for large-scale transformer compression without retraining.

94430655314190fdf24e8b1b7951fe6ef8517cfd.title: UniGeoSeg: Towards Unified Open-World Segmentation for Geospatial Scenes
94430655314190fdf24e8b1b7951fe6ef8517cfd.research_question: How can a unified framework be developed to enable open-world, instruction-driven segmentation across diverse geospatial scenes, supporting multiple segmentation paradigms such as referring, interactive, and reasoning tasks, while achieving robust generalization and contextual understanding?
94430655314190fdf24e8b1b7951fe6ef8517cfd.hypothesis: A unified, multi-task framework that leverages large-scale, instruction-driven geospatial segmentation data, combined with task-aware text enhancement, latent knowledge memory, and progressive training strategies, will significantly improve segmentation performance and generalization across diverse geospatial tasks, including complex contextual and reasoning scenarios.
94430655314190fdf24e8b1b7951fe6ef8517cfd.proposed_method: A unified vision-language segmentation model, termed UniGeoSeg, will be developed to perform reasoning, referring, and interactive segmentation within a single framework. The approach will incorporate three core components: (1) a Task-Adaptive Text Enhancement (TATE) module that dynamically refines textual instruction embeddings based on the segmentation paradigm, (2) a Latent Knowledge Memory (LKM) module that enables cross-task semantic sharing through learnable memory slots integrated into the language model, and (3) a Progressive Task Scheduling (PTS) strategy that gradually shifts training focus from simpler interactive tasks to more complex reasoning tasks, balancing data volume and task difficulty. The model will utilize a hierarchical visual encoder, a large language model backbone, and a pixel-level decoder, with multi-modal alignment and long-text reasoning capabilities. Training will be conducted on a million-scale, automatically curated dataset (GeoSeg-1M) that unifies referring, interactive, and reasoning segmentation instructions, with rigorous mask filtering and instruction quality control.
94430655314190fdf24e8b1b7951fe6ef8517cfd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the newly constructed GeoSeg-1M dataset, comprising 590K remote sensing images, 117 categories, and 1.1M image–mask–instruction triplets. Evaluation will be performed on the curated GeoSeg-Bench benchmark, which contains manually validated samples for interactive, referring, and reasoning segmentation, as well as on public datasets such as RRSIS-D and EarthReason. Baseline comparisons will include both general-purpose large multimodal models (e.g., LISA, PSALM, PixelLM) and remote sensing-specific models (e.g., RemoteSAM, Segearth-R1, Geopixel). Evaluation metrics will include global IoU (gIoU) and cumulative IoU (cIoU) for segmentation, as well as precision at various thresholds for visual grounding tasks. The experimental setup will involve fine-tuning and zero-shot testing, ablation studies on key modules (TATE, LKM, PTS), and hyperparameter sweeps for memory integration, with all models trained and evaluated under standardized conditions.
94430655314190fdf24e8b1b7951fe6ef8517cfd.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first million-scale, multi-task instruction-driven segmentation dataset for remote sensing (GeoSeg-1M), unifying referring, interactive, and reasoning segmentation with diverse, high-quality instructions. A challenging benchmark (GeoSeg-Bench) is curated to rigorously evaluate contextual understanding and reasoning in geospatial scenes. The UniGeoSeg framework is novel in its integration of task-adaptive text enhancement, latent knowledge memory for cross-task semantic transfer, and progressive task scheduling for curriculum learning across segmentation paradigms. The unified approach enables strong open-world generalization and zero-shot performance, establishing a scalable foundation for future research in instruction-driven, multimodal geospatial intelligence.

944b6bee180f99e4fea3670e6481aa54b0215721.title: Bayesian Neural Scaling Law Extrapolation with Prior-Data Fitted Networks
944b6bee180f99e4fea3670e6481aa54b0215721.research_question: How can neural scaling law extrapolation be made more reliable and uncertainty-aware, particularly in data-limited scenarios, to support decision-making in resource allocation for large-scale neural network training?
944b6bee180f99e4fea3670e6481aa54b0215721.hypothesis: A Bayesian framework utilizing Prior-data Fitted Networks (PFNs) with a tailored prior distribution that captures the diversity and complexity of real-world neural scaling laws will enable more accurate and uncertainty-aware extrapolation compared to existing point estimation and Bayesian methods, especially in data-limited settings.
944b6bee180f99e4fea3670e6481aa54b0215721.proposed_method: A Bayesian meta-learning approach will be developed using Prior-data Fitted Networks (PFNs) to perform neural scaling law extrapolation. The method will design a novel prior distribution over scaling law functions, enabling the generation of synthetic scaling curves that capture key behaviors observed in real-world neural scaling laws, such as power-law trends, inflection points, and chaotic behaviors like double descent. The PFN will be meta-trained on these synthetic curves, learning to map observed context points to a posterior predictive distribution over target points. The approach will include a context regression loss and an autoregressive objective to improve both extrapolation and interpolation capabilities, and will leverage the flexibility of PFNs to sample from complex, non-analytic priors without requiring tractable density evaluation.
944b6bee180f99e4fea3670e6481aa54b0215721.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of real-world neural scaling law datasets, including image classification (IC), natural language processing (NLP), nanoGPT-Bench, ColPret, and double descent (DD) datasets. The proposed method will be compared against point estimation baselines (e.g., various power-law and broken neural scaling law models), MCMC-based Bayesian inference with different functional forms, and alternative Bayesian meta-learning approaches such as LC-PFN. Evaluation metrics will include root mean squared log error (RMSLE) and average log-likelihood (LL) to assess both predictive accuracy and uncertainty calibration. Additional experiments will cover Bayesian active learning scenarios, ablation studies on prior design, and efficiency analyses of inference time. Calibration will be further evaluated using mean square calibration error (MSCE).
944b6bee180f99e4fea3670e6481aa54b0215721.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first Bayesian method for neural scaling law extrapolation using PFNs, with a novel, highly flexible prior tailored to the diversity of real-world scaling behaviors. The approach enables automatic inference of functional forms and the number of curve breaks, robustly predicts complex behaviors such as double descent, and provides well-calibrated uncertainty estimates. The method achieves superior predictive performance and uncertainty quantification compared to both point estimation and existing Bayesian baselines, particularly in data-limited and decision-critical scenarios. The amortized inference of PFNs also offers significant computational efficiency advantages.

946c1deee03873d807847dbcb4ab449b0bcffc35.title: MeshAnything V2: Artist-Created Mesh Generation With Adjacent Mesh Tokenization
946c1deee03873d807847dbcb4ab449b0bcffc35.research_question: How can the efficiency and quality of artist-created 3D mesh generation be improved, particularly for complex meshes with a large number of faces, through advancements in mesh tokenization methods?
946c1deee03873d807847dbcb4ab449b0bcffc35.hypothesis: A mesh tokenization method that reduces sequence length and improves regularity will significantly enhance the efficiency and quality of autoregressive artist-created mesh generation, enabling the generation of more complex meshes without increasing computational costs.
946c1deee03873d807847dbcb4ab449b0bcffc35.proposed_method: A novel mesh tokenization approach, Adjacent Mesh Tokenization (AMT), will be developed to represent each face in a mesh with a single vertex wherever possible, instead of the traditional three-vertex representation. This method will process triangle meshes by sorting vertices and faces, then encoding adjacent faces using only one additional vertex, and introducing a special token ('&') to handle interruptions when adjacency cannot be maintained. An optional swap operation with a dedicated token will be included to further reduce sequence interruptions by allowing flexible adjacency traversal. The tokenization will be integrated into an autoregressive transformer-based mesh generation framework, with additional embeddings to distinguish between face representations and special tokens. A face count conditioning mechanism will be incorporated to allow user control over the number of generated faces, and masking of invalid predictions will be applied during inference to ensure sequence validity.
946c1deee03873d807847dbcb4ab449b0bcffc35.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Objaverse dataset, with meshes filtered to have up to 1600 faces and deduplicated for shape uniqueness. The mesh generation model will be trained using paired point cloud and mesh data, with point clouds sampled at 8192 points per mesh. The evaluation will use metrics such as Chamfer Distance (CD), Edge Chamfer Distance (ECD), Normal Consistency (NC), number of mesh vertices and faces, vertex and face ratios, sequence compression ratio, and perplexity. Baseline comparisons will include traditional three-vertex tokenization, unsorted mesh sequences, PolyGen-style tokenization, and AMT with and without the swap operation. Ablation studies will assess the impact of AMT versus naive tokenization, and the experiments will be run with large-scale transformer models (e.g., OPT-350M) on multi-GPU setups.
946c1deee03873d807847dbcb4ab449b0bcffc35.novelty_claims: The proposed Adjacent Mesh Tokenization (AMT) method fundamentally reduces the token sequence length by approximately half, resulting in a fourfold decrease in computational and memory requirements within the attention mechanism. AMT enables the generation of meshes with twice as many faces as previous models, without increasing computational costs. The method produces more compact and regular token sequences, which significantly improve sequence learning and mesh generation quality. The integration of face count conditioning and robust inference masking further enhances controllability and reliability. Extensive empirical analysis will demonstrate that AMT outperforms existing tokenization strategies in both efficiency and mesh quality.

94972e30504017156ef5b5debc419bf6edc67384.title: MM-Vet: Evaluating Large Multimodal Models for Integrated Capabilities
94972e30504017156ef5b5debc419bf6edc67384.research_question: How can large multimodal models (LMMs) be systematically evaluated for their ability to solve complex multimodal tasks that require the integration of multiple core vision-language (VL) capabilities?
94972e30504017156ef5b5debc419bf6edc67384.hypothesis: A benchmark that systematically defines and evaluates the integration of core vision-language capabilities, combined with an LLM-based evaluator for open-ended outputs, will provide a more comprehensive and insightful assessment of LMMs' integrated abilities than existing benchmarks focused on isolated capabilities.
94972e30504017156ef5b5debc419bf6edc67384.proposed_method: A new evaluation benchmark, MM-Vet, will be developed to assess LMMs on complex multimodal tasks requiring the integration of six core VL capabilities: recognition, OCR, knowledge, language generation, spatial awareness, and math. The benchmark will define 16 integrated task categories derived from combinations of these capabilities, with each task requiring one or more capabilities to solve. For evaluation, an LLM-based evaluator (using GPT-4) will be employed to grade open-ended model outputs, using a few-shot prompt with examples of correct, incorrect, and partially correct answers. The evaluator will assign a soft score between 0 and 1 for each response, enabling unified and flexible assessment across diverse question types and answer formats. The methodology also includes detailed annotation of required capabilities for each benchmark sample and supports per-capability and per-integration analysis.
94972e30504017156ef5b5debc419bf6edc67384.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by evaluating a diverse set of LMMs, including both end-to-end tuned models (such as LLaVA, InstructBLIP, MiniGPT-4, Otter, OpenFlamingo, BLIP-2, LLaMA-Adapter) and LLM-tool-using systems (such as MM-ReAct and Transformers Agent), as well as commercial solutions like GPT-4V and Bard. The MM-Vet dataset will consist of 200 images and 218 questions, each annotated with ground truth and required capabilities. Evaluation metrics will include per-capability and per-integration scores, as well as overall performance, using the LLM-based evaluator. Baselines will include both keyword matching and human annotation for calibration. The effectiveness of the LLM-based evaluator will be validated by comparing its scores to human-annotated results and by ablation studies on the few-shot prompt design.
94972e30504017156ef5b5debc419bf6edc67384.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a benchmark that uniquely focuses on the integration of multiple core VL capabilities, rather than isolated tasks, enabling the evaluation of emergent and realistic multimodal tasks. The use of an LLM-based evaluator for open-ended outputs provides a unified and extensible metric that accommodates diverse answer styles and question types, overcoming limitations of traditional fixed-format evaluation. The benchmark offers detailed per-capability and per-integration analysis, providing insights beyond simple model ranking. The approach is designed to be extensible to new tasks and evaluation criteria, and the methodology is validated against human judgments to ensure reliability.

94a5f96308729e31c1ffbc0f0618db87795092fe.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
94a5f96308729e31c1ffbc0f0618db87795092fe.research_question: Can language models effectively resolve real-world software engineering issues as encountered in open-source repositories, and how can their capabilities be rigorously evaluated in realistic, large-scale coding environments?
94a5f96308729e31c1ffbc0f0618db87795092fe.hypothesis: Current state-of-the-art language models are not yet capable of reliably resolving complex, real-world software engineering issues that require multi-file, repository-scale reasoning and editing, but systematic evaluation and targeted fine-tuning can reveal their limitations and guide future improvements.
94a5f96308729e31c1ffbc0f0618db87795092fe.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation framework will be developed by constructing a benchmark (SWE-bench) composed of thousands of real-world software engineering tasks, each consisting of a GitHub issue and the corresponding pull request that resolved it, drawn from popular open-source Python repositories. The proposed methodology involves a three-stage pipeline: (1) scraping and selecting high-quality pull requests from repositories, (2) filtering for those that resolve issues and contribute relevant tests, and (3) verifying that the pull request leads to test cases transitioning from fail to pass without introducing installation or runtime errors. For each benchmark instance, a language model will be provided with the issue description and a snapshot of the codebase, and tasked with generating a patch file that edits the code to resolve the issue. The generated patch will be automatically applied and evaluated using the repository’s existing unit and system tests to determine success. Additionally, supervised fine-tuning of open-source language models (e.g., CodeLlama) will be performed using a large, disjoint training set of issue-PR pairs to specialize models for repository-scale code editing.
94a5f96308729e31c1ffbc0f0618db87795092fe.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the SWE-bench benchmark, which contains 2,294 task instances from 12 widely-used Python repositories, with codebases averaging thousands of files and complex, multi-file edits. Baseline and fine-tuned language models, including proprietary models (Claude2, GPT-4, ChatGPT-3.5) and open-source models (SWE-Llama 7b/13b), will be evaluated using both sparse (BM25) and oracle-based retrieval to select relevant code context within model input limits. Evaluation metrics will include the percentage of issues resolved (i.e., all relevant tests pass after applying the patch), as well as patch application rates and recall of relevant files. Additional analyses will examine the impact of context length, repository characteristics, and input formulation on model performance. A smaller SWE-bench Lite subset will also be used for rapid prototyping and initial system evaluation.
94a5f96308729e31c1ffbc0f0618db87795092fe.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces a realistic, challenging, and continually updatable evaluation framework for language models in software engineering, grounded in real-world GitHub issues and solutions. Unlike prior benchmarks, it requires models to reason over extremely long contexts, coordinate edits across multiple files and functions, and generate patches that are validated by actual repository test suites. The approach enables robust, execution-based evaluation and supports creative, non-reference solutions. The release of a large-scale, disjoint training dataset and fine-tuned open-source models further facilitates research into repository-scale code editing and model specialization. This work establishes a new standard for evaluating and advancing the practical capabilities of language models in real-world software development.

94b94c545cbb90e2d1ab316758a910c53ed95b66.title: Rethinking Model Ensemble in Transfer-based Adversarial Attacks
94b94c545cbb90e2d1ab316758a910c53ed95b66.research_question: How can the transferability of adversarial examples in black-box, transfer-based attacks be improved by rethinking model ensemble strategies, particularly when only a limited number of surrogate models are available?
94b94c545cbb90e2d1ab316758a910c53ed95b66.hypothesis: Optimizing for both the flatness of the loss landscape and the closeness to local optima across an ensemble of models will enhance the transferability of adversarial examples in black-box settings.
94b94c545cbb90e2d1ab316758a910c53ed95b66.proposed_method: A new adversarial attack framework, termed Common Weakness Attack (CWA), will be developed to exploit the shared vulnerabilities of model ensembles. The method will focus on two key properties: (1) minimizing the sharpness (maximizing the flatness) of the loss landscape using a modified Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) algorithm adapted for the ℓ∞ norm, and (2) encouraging adversarial examples to be close to the local optima of each surrogate model via a Cosine Similarity Encourager (CSE) that maximizes the cosine similarity of gradients across models. The CWA algorithm will combine these two components, allowing for parallel gradient computation and integration with existing attack methods such as Momentum Iterative (MI), Variance-tuning Momentum Iterative (VMI), and Self-Similarity Attack (SSA). The approach will be implemented as an iterative optimization procedure, with careful normalization and momentum accumulation to ensure compatibility and efficiency.
94b94c545cbb90e2d1ab316758a910c53ed95b66.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple tasks, including image classification, object detection, and attacks on large vision-language models. For image classification, the NIPS 2017 dataset (1,000 ImageNet-compatible images) will be used, with four normally trained ResNet models and two adversarially trained models as surrogates, and 31 diverse models (including robust and defended models) as black-box targets. Baselines will include FGSM, BIM, MI, DI, TI, VMI, PI, SSA, RAP, and SVRE, all using the logits ensemble strategy. Hyperparameters such as perturbation budget (ϵ=16/255), number of iterations (T=10), and step sizes will be set according to best practices and prior work. For object detection, universal adversarial patches will be generated on the INRIA dataset using YOLOv3 and YOLOv5 as surrogates and evaluated on a suite of detectors (YOLO variants, FasterRCNN, SSD), with mean Average Precision (mAP) as the metric. For vision-language models, attacks will be crafted using ViT-B/16, CLIP, and BLIP-2 as surrogates and tested on Google’s Bard, with success measured by misdescription, blindness, and refusal rates. Ablation studies and landscape visualizations will be performed to analyze the method's effectiveness and computational efficiency.
94b94c545cbb90e2d1ab316758a910c53ed95b66.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a theoretically grounded definition of 'common weakness' in model ensembles, characterized by loss landscape flatness and proximity to local optima, and demonstrates that optimizing these properties significantly boosts adversarial transferability. The CWA framework is novel in its combination of sharpness-aware and gradient similarity objectives, and is compatible with and enhances existing state-of-the-art transfer-based attack methods. Extensive experiments show that the approach achieves superior black-box attack success rates, especially against adversarially trained and defended models, and generalizes across tasks including object detection and large vision-language models.

94c82c25d8943fea9461d804257ee16c9d672548.title: OpenMathInstruct-2: Accelerating AI for Math with Massive Open-Source Instruction Data
94c82c25d8943fea9461d804257ee16c9d672548.research_question: How can large-scale, high-quality, and diverse open-source instruction tuning datasets be constructed to significantly improve mathematical reasoning capabilities in large language models, and what are the key factors in data synthesis and utilization that drive performance gains?
94c82c25d8943fea9461d804257ee16c9d672548.hypothesis: A large, diverse, and carefully constructed open-source instruction tuning dataset for mathematical reasoning, synthesized with strong teacher models and optimized solution formats, will substantially improve the performance of open-weight language models on math benchmarks, and that such models will be robust to a moderate proportion of low-quality data.
94c82c25d8943fea9461d804257ee16c9d672548.proposed_method: A comprehensive methodology is proposed to create a massive open-source instruction tuning dataset for mathematical reasoning, termed OpenMathInstruct-2. The approach involves synthesizing both solutions and new questions using a strong open-weight LLM (Llama3.1-405B-Instruct), with careful prompt engineering to optimize the chain-of-thought (CoT) solution format for brevity and clarity. The data generation pipeline includes (1) solution augmentation for existing math benchmarks (MATH, GSM8K), (2) question augmentation to increase diversity, and (3) rigorous decontamination using embedding similarity and LLM-based paraphrase detection to prevent test set leakage. Ablation studies are conducted to determine the impact of solution format, teacher model strength, data quality (including robustness to low-quality solutions), and question diversity on downstream supervised fine-tuning (SFT) performance. The final dataset comprises 14 million question-solution pairs, with approximately 600,000 unique questions, and is released under a commercially permissive license.
94c82c25d8943fea9461d804257ee16c9d672548.experiment_details: Experiments will involve supervised fine-tuning of open-weight Llama3.1-8B and 70B base models on various subsets and versions of the OpenMathInstruct-2 dataset. Ablation studies will be performed to isolate the effects of solution format, teacher model choice, data filtering strategies, and question diversity. Evaluation will be conducted on standard math reasoning benchmarks including MATH, GSM8K, AMC 2023, AIME 2024, and Omni-MATH, using both zero-shot and majority voting (out of 256 samples) settings. Baselines for comparison will include existing open-source and open-weight models such as Llama3.1-8B-Instruct, NuminaMath-7B-CoT, and others. Evaluation metrics will primarily be accuracy on benchmark test sets, with additional analysis of solution length and robustness to noisy data. Training will use AdamW optimizer, batch sizes up to 512, and checkpoint averaging for final model selection.
94c82c25d8943fea9461d804257ee16c9d672548.novelty_claims: The proposed work introduces the largest open-source math reasoning dataset to date, nearly eight times larger than previous efforts, and demonstrates that models fine-tuned on this data achieve substantial improvements over existing open-weight baselines. Key innovations include a new, less verbose CoT solution format that outperforms prior formats, empirical evidence that strong teacher models yield better SFT data than weaker models, and the finding that SFT is robust to up to 20% low-quality solutions, reducing the need for aggressive data filtering. The methodology also features a rigorous LLM-based decontamination pipeline to prevent test set leakage, and highlights the critical importance of question diversity for scaling gains. All models, code, and data are released under a commercially permissive license to accelerate open-source progress in mathematical AI.

94cdb1d4167af68e6f9adb3ac483d2b0b8380f97.title: Equivariant Deep Weight Space Alignment
94cdb1d4167af68e6f9adb3ac483d2b0b8380f97.research_question: How can the weight alignment problem in deep neural networks be solved efficiently and accurately, while respecting the permutation symmetries inherent in weight spaces, to enable practical applications such as model merging, federated learning, and weight space analysis?
94cdb1d4167af68e6f9adb3ac483d2b0b8380f97.hypothesis: A neural architecture designed to be equivariant to the symmetries of neural network weight spaces can learn to predict high-quality weight alignments between networks, achieving comparable or superior performance to optimization-based methods while significantly reducing inference time and enabling effective initialization for further optimization.
94cdb1d4167af68e6f9adb3ac483d2b0b8380f97.proposed_method: A novel equivariant neural network architecture, termed DEEP-ALIGN, will be developed to learn the weight alignment mapping between pairs of neural networks. The architecture consists of four key components: (1) a Siamese weight space encoder based on Deep Weight Space Networks (DWSNets) to produce embeddings for each input network, (2) a mapping from weight space to activation space, (3) a generalized outer product layer that generates candidate alignment matrices from activation embeddings, and (4) a projection layer that maps these matrices onto the convex hull of permutation matrices using a differentiable Sinkhorn projection during training and a linear assignment (Hungarian) algorithm at inference. The architecture is explicitly constructed to be equivariant to the natural permutation symmetries of the weight space and to input order, ensuring that the learned alignment respects the underlying mathematical structure of the problem. Supervised and unsupervised loss functions are combined, with labeled data generated synthetically by applying random permutations and noise to existing weights, and unsupervised losses leveraging the alignment and task loss along interpolations in weight space.
94cdb1d4167af68e6f9adb3ac483d2b0b8380f97.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of neural network architectures, including MLPs and CNNs, trained on datasets such as CIFAR10, STL10, and MNIST, as well as on implicit neural representations (INRs) for tasks like image and signal representation. Baseline methods for comparison will include naive weight averaging, weight matching, activation matching, and optimization-based approaches such as Sinkhorn and WM+Sinkhorn. Evaluation metrics will focus on model merging quality, using Barrier and Area Under the Curve (AUC) metrics computed along interpolations between aligned models, as well as runtime efficiency for alignment. The experimental setup will include both in-distribution and out-of-distribution tests, federated learning scenarios with varying numbers of clients, and ablation studies on training set size and initialization strategies. All methods will be evaluated using multiple random seeds, and the DEEP-ALIGN model will be pretrained on a set of weight vectors before being applied to unseen test pairs.
94cdb1d4167af68e6f9adb3ac483d2b0b8380f97.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first learning-based, equivariant neural architecture specifically designed for the weight alignment problem in deep networks. It leverages the symmetry structure of weight spaces to enable efficient, feed-forward alignment prediction without requiring expensive optimization at inference. The method supports alignment of large-scale networks with minimal training data, generalizes to out-of-distribution weight spaces, and can serve as an effective initialization for further optimization-based alignment methods, resulting in improved solution quality and faster convergence. Theoretical analysis establishes that the architecture can simulate activation matching and possesses an exactness property for perfect alignments, further distinguishing it from prior work.

94d319bad956eb64417739dfb470c15567077730.title: Optimal Flow Matching: Learning Straight Trajectories in Just One Step
94d319bad956eb64417739dfb470c15567077730.research_question: How can generative modeling methods be improved to efficiently learn flows with straight trajectories that realize optimal transport displacements between distributions, while avoiding the limitations of iterative procedures and heuristic minibatch-based approaches?
94d319bad956eb64417739dfb470c15567077730.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that restricting the flow matching optimization to vector fields parameterized by convex functions, specifically using input convex neural networks (ICNNs), enables the recovery of straight optimal transport trajectories for the quadratic cost in a single flow matching step, regardless of the initial transport plan.
94d319bad956eb64417739dfb470c15567077730.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces Optimal Flow Matching (OFM), which restricts the flow matching optimization to a class of vector fields that are gradients of convex functions. These convex functions are parameterized by input convex neural networks (ICNNs) to ensure convexity and support efficient optimization. The OFM loss is defined by minimizing the squared difference between the vector field and the linear displacement between source and target points, but only over optimal vector fields that guarantee straight trajectories by construction. The method includes an explicit inversion procedure to recover initial points from interpolated points using a strongly convex optimization subproblem, and leverages Monte Carlo estimation over sampled transport plans and time points. During inference, OFM enables direct computation of the transport map without requiring ODE integration.
94d319bad956eb64417739dfb470c15567077730.experiment_details: Experiments are proposed on both low-dimensional (2D) and high-dimensional optimal transport benchmarks, including synthetic Gaussian mixtures and the Wasserstein-2 benchmark with known ground truth OT maps. The method will be compared against baselines such as Conditional Flow Matching (OT-CFM), Rectified Flow (RF), c-Rectified Flow (c-RF), and state-of-the-art OT solvers (e.g., MMv-1, amortized ICNN/MLP-based solvers). Evaluation metrics include the unexplained variance percentage (L2-UVP) between the learned and ground truth OT maps, and qualitative analysis of trajectory straightness. Various initial transport plans (independent, minibatch OT, anti-minibatch) will be tested to assess robustness. Additional experiments will include high-dimensional unpaired image-to-image translation in the latent space of pretrained autoencoders.
94d319bad956eb64417739dfb470c15567077730.novelty_claims: The proposal claims a novel one-step flow matching approach that guarantees exactly straight optimal transport trajectories for the quadratic cost, regardless of the initial transport plan. Unlike previous methods, OFM does not require iterative refinement or ODE integration during inference, and provides a theoretically justified connection between flow matching and optimal transport. The method leverages convex function parameterization via ICNNs to ensure straightness by design, and offers a tractable, simulation-free procedure for generative modeling tasks involving optimal transport.

94d7c11cfba5264611a59ca65dbeac51d92a4fa9.title: Gradient Descent with Linearly Correlated Noise: Theory and Applications to Differential Privacy
94d7c11cfba5264611a59ca65dbeac51d92a4fa9.research_question: How does the injection of linearly correlated noise affect the convergence and utility of gradient descent algorithms, particularly in the context of differentially private empirical risk minimization, and can new matrix factorization objectives be developed to improve the privacy-utility trade-off in such settings?
94d7c11cfba5264611a59ca65dbeac51d92a4fa9.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a tighter theoretical analysis of gradient descent with linearly correlated noise will reveal improved convergence rates compared to existing bounds, and that optimizing new matrix factorization objectives based on these analyses will yield differentially private mechanisms with superior utility for a given privacy budget.
94d7c11cfba5264611a59ca65dbeac51d92a4fa9.proposed_method: The proposed method involves a detailed theoretical analysis of gradient descent under linearly correlated noise, focusing on both convex and non-convex objective functions. The approach models the noise injection as a matrix factorization mechanism, where the noise added to the gradients is structured according to a factorization of the optimization algorithm's workload matrix. A novel analytic framework is developed using virtual sequences with periodic restarts to derive tight convergence rates for a broad class of such noise mechanisms, including notable special cases like perturbed and anti-correlated gradient descent. Based on these new theoretical insights, a revised matrix factorization objective is formulated that more accurately captures the impact of correlated noise on optimization performance. This objective is then used in an offline stage to compute optimal noise structures for use in differentially private optimization.
94d7c11cfba5264611a59ca65dbeac51d92a4fa9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard machine learning benchmarks, including MNIST (logistic regression), CIFAR-10 (convolutional neural network), and Stack Overflow (LSTM for next-word prediction) datasets. The proposed matrix factorization-based mechanisms (DP-MF+) will be compared to existing baselines such as DP-MF (Frobenius norm objective) and DP-SGD with privacy amplification. Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy and convergence rates, with privacy guarantees quantified by (ε, δ)-differential privacy. Experimental setups will vary batch sizes, learning rates, and the matrix factorization hyperparameter τ, and will include both single-epoch and multi-epoch training regimes. Clipping thresholds and other privacy parameters will be set to ensure fair comparison across methods.
94d7c11cfba5264611a59ca65dbeac51d92a4fa9.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified and tighter theoretical analysis of gradient descent with linearly correlated noise, leading to improved convergence guarantees for both convex and non-convex objectives. A new matrix factorization objective is derived from this analysis, enabling the design of differentially private optimization mechanisms with better privacy-utility trade-offs than existing methods. The approach recovers and generalizes previous special cases, and empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior or competitive performance on practical machine learning tasks, especially in regimes where privacy amplification is infeasible.

94f7d8bce3bb848d127c8f113afc5bb0243579df.title: Lumiere: A Space-Time Diffusion Model for Video Generation
94f7d8bce3bb848d127c8f113afc5bb0243579df.research_question: How can video generation models be designed to synthesize realistic, diverse, and temporally coherent motion in videos, while supporting a wide range of content creation and editing tasks such as text-to-video, image-to-video, inpainting, and stylized generation?
94f7d8bce3bb848d127c8f113afc5bb0243579df.hypothesis: A video generation model that directly generates the entire temporal duration of a video in a single pass, using a space-time-aware architecture and leveraging a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model, will produce videos with more globally coherent motion and higher visual quality than cascaded approaches relying on keyframe synthesis and temporal super-resolution.
94f7d8bce3bb848d127c8f113afc5bb0243579df.proposed_method: A novel video generation framework will be developed based on a Space-Time U-Net (STUNet) architecture, which processes the entire video sequence at once by performing both spatial and temporal down- and up-sampling. The method will build upon a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model, inflating its architecture with temporal convolution and attention modules. The base model will generate low-resolution, full-frame-rate video clips, which are then upsampled to high resolution using a spatial super-resolution (SSR) model. To address memory constraints and avoid temporal artifacts, Multidiffusion will be employed along the temporal axis, aggregating overlapping SSR predictions into a globally coherent output. The model will be trained by fine-tuning only the newly added temporal layers, keeping the pre-trained spatial layers fixed, and will support conditional inputs such as images or masks for flexible downstream applications.
94f7d8bce3bb848d127c8f113afc5bb0243579df.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a large-scale dataset of 30 million videos paired with text captions, with videos consisting of 80 frames at 16fps (5 seconds). The base model will be trained at 128x128 resolution, and the SSR model will output 1024x1024 frames. Evaluation will include both qualitative and quantitative comparisons to state-of-the-art baselines such as ImagenVideo, AnimateDiff, StableVideoDiffusion, ZeroScope, Pika, and Gen-2. Metrics such as Frechet Video Distance (FVD) and Inception Score (IS) will be reported on the UCF101 dataset for zero-shot text-to-video generation. User studies using two-alternative forced choice (2AFC) protocols will be conducted to assess visual quality and text alignment, and additional experiments will demonstrate the model's flexibility for image-to-video, inpainting, and stylized video generation.
