94f7d8bce3bb848d127c8f113afc5bb0243579df.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a space-time diffusion architecture that generates the entire video sequence in a single pass, enabling globally coherent motion and overcoming limitations of cascaded keyframe and temporal super-resolution methods. The method innovates by interleaving temporal convolution and attention modules within a pre-trained text-to-image U-Net, and by employing Multidiffusion for seamless spatial super-resolution across temporal segments. The framework supports a wide range of content creation and editing tasks, and demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in both quantitative metrics and user preference studies.

95240dda409e28acccdc5cf619ad0c036cf4292d.title: Deja Vu: Contextual Sparsity for Efficient LLMs at Inference Time
95240dda409e28acccdc5cf619ad0c036cf4292d.research_question: How can the inference-time computational and memory costs of large language models (LLMs) be reduced without sacrificing model quality or in-context learning abilities, particularly for latency-sensitive applications?
95240dda409e28acccdc5cf619ad0c036cf4292d.hypothesis: Contextual sparsity exists in pre-trained LLMs, such that for any given input, only a small, input-dependent subset of attention heads and MLP parameters is necessary to produce outputs nearly identical to the dense model. This sparsity can be accurately predicted and exploited to accelerate inference without degrading model quality or in-context learning abilities.
95240dda409e28acccdc5cf619ad0c036cf4292d.proposed_method: A novel framework, DEJAVU, will be developed to exploit contextual sparsity in LLMs at inference time. The method involves training lightweight, layer-specific neural network predictors that, given the input to each LLM layer, predict which attention heads and MLP neurons are essential for the current input. These predictors are trained using data collected from dense forward passes, identifying parameters with significant activations. To minimize prediction overhead, an asynchronous lookahead mechanism is introduced, leveraging the observation that token embeddings change slowly across layers due to residual connections. This allows sparsity decisions for future layers to be made in parallel with current computations. The system is implemented with hardware-aware optimizations, including kernel fusion and memory coalescing, to ensure that structured sparsity yields real wall-clock speedups on GPUs.
95240dda409e28acccdc5cf619ad0c036cf4292d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large pre-trained LLMs such as OPT-175B, OPT-66B, and BLOOM, using both language modeling datasets (e.g., WikiText, C4) and a suite of zero-shot and few-shot downstream tasks (e.g., CB, COPA, Lambada, OpenBookQA, PIQA, RTE, Winogrande). The evaluation will compare DEJAVU against state-of-the-art inference libraries such as FasterTransformer and HuggingFace implementations. Metrics will include end-to-end inference latency (measured per token and per sequence), model accuracy on downstream tasks, and perplexity for language modeling. Experiments will also include ablations to separately assess the impact of sparsifying MLP and attention blocks, the effect of batch size on union sparsity, and the compatibility of the approach with quantization techniques (e.g., 4-bit quantization). Hardware setups will use multi-GPU servers (e.g., 8x NVIDIA A100 80GB) to ensure realistic latency measurements.
95240dda409e28acccdc5cf619ad0c036cf4292d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the concept of input-dependent contextual sparsity for LLMs at inference time, demonstrating that structured, input-driven pruning can be predicted and exploited without retraining or loss of in-context learning ability. The asynchronous, lookahead prediction mechanism is novel in leveraging slowly changing embeddings across layers to parallelize sparsity prediction and computation. The hardware-aware implementation ensures that theoretical sparsity translates into real-world latency reductions, achieving over 2× speedup compared to the best existing dense inference libraries and over 6× compared to widely used baselines, all without compromising model quality. The approach is also shown to be compatible with quantization, suggesting broad applicability for efficient LLM deployment.

9529e50807f36acf3d2e4af994b5803c47e4746a.title: Atom: Low-bit Quantization for Efficient and Accurate LLM Serving
9529e50807f36acf3d2e4af994b5803c47e4746a.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be quantized to extremely low bit-widths for both weights and activations to maximize serving throughput and memory efficiency on modern GPU hardware, while maintaining high accuracy?
9529e50807f36acf3d2e4af994b5803c47e4746a.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a combination of mixed-precision quantization with channel reordering, fine-grained group quantization, dynamic activation quantization, and low-bit quantized KV-cache can enable LLMs to be quantized to 4 bits for both weights and activations, resulting in substantial throughput and memory improvements with negligible accuracy loss.
9529e50807f36acf3d2e4af994b5803c47e4746a.proposed_method: A novel low-bit quantization framework, Atom, will be developed for LLM serving. The method will incorporate mixed-precision quantization, where a small number of outlier channels in weights and activations are retained in higher precision (e.g., INT8), while the majority are quantized to low-bit (e.g., INT4). Channel reordering will be used to efficiently separate outliers and regular values, enabling regular memory access patterns. Fine-grained group quantization will be applied, dividing tensors into small groups (e.g., size 128) and quantizing each group independently to minimize quantization error. Dynamic quantization will be used for activations, computing quantization parameters on-the-fly per input, while weights will be statically quantized with calibration data and optionally enhanced with GPTQ. Additionally, the KV-cache will be quantized to low-bit representations to reduce memory movement in self-attention layers. All quantization, dequantization, and reordering operations will be fused into existing GPU kernels to minimize overhead and maximize hardware utilization.
9529e50807f36acf3d2e4af994b5803c47e4746a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by integrating the proposed quantization framework into an end-to-end LLM serving system, targeting Llama models of various sizes (7B, 13B, 30B, 65B). Evaluation will use standard benchmarks including WikiText2, PTB, and C4 for perplexity, and zero-shot accuracy will be assessed on PIQA, ARC-e, ARC-c, BoolQ, HellaSwag, and Winogrande tasks using lm-eval. Baseline comparisons will include FP16, INT8 (W8A8), weight-only quantization (W4A16), and state-of-the-art quantization methods such as SmoothQuant, OmniQuant, and QLLM. Throughput (tokens/sec), latency (ms/token), and memory usage will be measured across a range of batch sizes on NVIDIA GPUs (e.g., RTX 4090, A100). Ablation studies will isolate the impact of each quantization technique on accuracy and efficiency. Custom CUDA kernels will be implemented to support fused low-bit operations and evaluated for kernel-level and end-to-end performance.
9529e50807f36acf3d2e4af994b5803c47e4746a.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a comprehensive low-bit quantization framework for LLMs that combines mixed-precision quantization with channel reordering, fine-grained group quantization, and dynamic activation quantization, all fused into efficient GPU kernels. It is the first to demonstrate accurate 4-bit weight-activation quantization for LLM serving with negligible accuracy loss, while also quantizing the KV-cache for memory-bound self-attention acceleration. The approach achieves state-of-the-art throughput improvements (up to 7.7x over FP16 and 2.5x over INT8) at similar latency, and provides a practical, hardware-efficient solution for large-scale LLM deployment.

9548bacc4c7714151b674748dc86e2cc185a4955.title: Scaling Laws for Fine-Grained Mixture of Experts
9548bacc4c7714151b674748dc86e2cc185a4955.research_question: How do scaling laws govern the performance and efficiency of fine-grained Mixture of Experts (MoE) models, and how can the introduction of a granularity hyperparameter enable optimal allocation of computational resources for large language model training?
9548bacc4c7714151b674748dc86e2cc185a4955.hypothesis: Introducing and optimizing a granularity hyperparameter in MoE architectures will enable the derivation of new scaling laws that allow MoE models to consistently outperform dense Transformers in efficiency and performance across all computational budgets, provided that training hyperparameters are chosen optimally.
9548bacc4c7714151b674748dc86e2cc185a4955.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that introduces a granularity hyperparameter to Mixture of Experts (MoE) models, allowing precise control over the size of each expert independently from the standard feed-forward layer size. The method involves defining and integrating granularity (G) and expansion rate (E) into the MoE architecture, where granularity determines the number of smaller, fine-grained experts a token is routed to, while maintaining a constant number of active parameters per token. Joint scaling laws will be empirically derived and analytically formulated to relate final model loss to model size, training tokens, and granularity. Optimization techniques, including parametric fitting and computational budget constraints (FLOPs), will be used to identify compute-optimal configurations of model size, dataset size, and granularity for any given computational budget. The methodology will also account for the increased routing costs associated with higher granularity and propose practical strategies for balancing these costs.
9548bacc4c7714151b674748dc86e2cc185a4955.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on decoder-only Transformer architectures, with the feed-forward layer replaced by the proposed fine-grained MoE layer. Over 100 training runs will be performed, varying model sizes from 129M to 3.7B parameters, training durations from 16B to 130B tokens, and granularity values logarithmically spaced between 1 and 16. Expansion rate E will be fixed at 64 for the main study, with additional experiments at E=16 for validation. Dense Transformer baselines will be trained under matching conditions for direct comparison. Evaluation metrics will include final loss (perplexity), scaling law fit (RMSE), and computational efficiency measured in FLOPs and wall-clock time. The impact of routing overhead will be explicitly measured and modeled. Hyperparameter optimization will be performed using methods such as BFGS and Brent's method, and results will be validated via bootstrapping and held-out data.
9548bacc4c7714151b674748dc86e2cc185a4955.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the granularity hyperparameter, enabling fine-grained control over expert size in MoE models, which has not been systematically explored in prior work. New joint scaling laws are derived that incorporate granularity, model size, and training data, allowing for principled, compute-optimal selection of training hyperparameters. The approach demonstrates that, with optimal settings, MoE models can always be more efficient than dense Transformers across all computational budgets, overturning previous claims in the literature. The methodology provides a comprehensive framework for modeling and optimizing the trade-offs between model sparsity, routing cost, and training efficiency in large-scale language models.

9555c0233a71160faee2ebdbad3e0678ae9be838.title: On the Saturation Effect of Kernel Ridge Regression
9555c0233a71160faee2ebdbad3e0678ae9be838.research_question: What are the fundamental limitations of kernel ridge regression (KRR) in achieving the minimax generalization error rates, particularly when the underlying regression function possesses high smoothness? How does the smoothness of the regression function relative to the reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) affect the achievable rates, and can a rigorous lower bound for KRR's performance be established in such regimes?
9555c0233a71160faee2ebdbad3e0678ae9be838.hypothesis: Kernel ridge regression exhibits a saturation effect, such that when the regression function is sufficiently smooth (i.e., belongs to an interpolation space [H]^α with α > 2), the generalization error rate of KRR cannot surpass a specific lower bound, regardless of the choice of regularization parameter.
9555c0233a71160faee2ebdbad3e0678ae9be838.proposed_method: A rigorous theoretical analysis will be conducted to establish lower bounds on the generalization error rate of KRR under varying smoothness assumptions of the regression function. The approach involves formulating the KRR estimator in operator-theoretic terms, leveraging spectral decompositions of the associated integral operator, and introducing a bias-variance decomposition tailored for lower bound analysis. Key technical steps include deriving concentration inequalities for empirical operators, analyzing the effective dimension, and quantifying the impact of the regularization parameter. The analysis will be supported by explicit constructions in Sobolev RKHS settings and will be complemented by numerical experiments to illustrate the theoretical findings.
9555c0233a71160faee2ebdbad3e0678ae9be838.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed using synthetic datasets generated from known distributions over compact domains, such as the unit interval with uniform measure. Regression functions will be chosen as eigenfunctions of the integral operator associated with the kernel, ensuring controllable smoothness (e.g., Sobolev spaces with varying α). The KRR method will be compared to spectral algorithms with higher qualification, such as gradient flow, across a range of sample sizes and regularization parameters. Evaluation metrics will include the mean squared generalization error, estimated via Monte Carlo integration and averaged over multiple trials. Convergence rates will be empirically estimated and compared to theoretical predictions, with additional experiments conducted for various kernels to confirm robustness.
9555c0233a71160faee2ebdbad3e0678ae9be838.novelty_claims: The proposal aims to rigorously prove the long-standing conjecture regarding the saturation effect in KRR, establishing that for regression functions with smoothness parameter α > 2, the generalization error rate is fundamentally limited and cannot achieve the information-theoretic lower bound. The analysis introduces novel bias-variance decomposition techniques for lower bound proofs, refines concentration results for empirical operators, and provides explicit operator-theoretic characterizations of the saturation effect. The findings will clarify the limitations of KRR and highlight the superiority of alternative spectral algorithms with higher qualification in high-smoothness regimes.

9563e9578073447b68261eda55e7a6c4fb2af7c8.title: No Fear of Heterogeneity: Classifier Calibration for Federated Learning with Non-IID Data
9563e9578073447b68261eda55e7a6c4fb2af7c8.research_question: How can the performance degradation of deep classification models in federated learning with non-IID data be mitigated, particularly addressing the impact of data heterogeneity on different layers of the model?
9563e9578073447b68261eda55e7a6c4fb2af7c8.hypothesis: The primary source of performance degradation in federated learning with non-IID data lies in the classifier layer, which becomes biased due to heterogeneous local data distributions. Calibrating the classifier after federated training, even without access to raw data, can significantly improve classification accuracy.
9563e9578073447b68261eda55e7a6c4fb2af7c8.proposed_method: A new algorithm, Classifier Calibration with Virtual Representations (CCVR), is proposed to address classifier bias in federated learning with non-IID data. After federated training, the global feature extractor is distributed to clients, who use it to compute local class-wise feature statistics (mean and covariance) without sharing raw data. These statistics are aggregated at the server to estimate a global Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) for the feature space. The server then samples virtual feature representations from the GMM for each class, and retrains only the classifier layer using these virtual samples and their corresponding labels, keeping the feature extractor fixed. This post-hoc calibration step is designed to correct decision boundaries in a privacy-preserving manner, as only summary statistics are communicated.
9563e9578073447b68261eda55e7a6c4fb2af7c8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard federated learning benchmarks including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and CINIC-10, simulating non-IID data partitions using Dirichlet distributions with varying concentration parameters to control heterogeneity. Baseline methods such as FedAvg, FedProx, FedAvgM, and MOON will be compared before and after applying CCVR. Evaluation metrics include top-1 classification accuracy, and experiments will systematically vary the number of virtual samples and the degree of data heterogeneity. Additional analyses will include t-SNE visualizations of feature spaces, measurement of classifier bias, and the use of Wasserstein distance to assess the separability of generated feature distributions. All methods will use consistent model architectures and data augmentation strategies for fair comparison.
9563e9578073447b68261eda55e7a6c4fb2af7c8.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first systematic analysis of layer-wise representation similarity in federated learning with non-IID data, revealing that classifier bias is a key factor in performance loss. The CCVR algorithm is a novel, simple, and universal post-hoc classifier calibration method that does not require access to raw data or real features, instead relying on virtual representations generated from aggregated Gaussian statistics. This approach is privacy-preserving, model-agnostic, and can be seamlessly integrated with existing federated learning algorithms, consistently yielding significant accuracy improvements across diverse benchmarks and levels of data heterogeneity.

9574a9b5248743fd558572e80967b81ba4728c51.title: Comparison of meta-learners for estimating multi-valued treatment heterogeneous effects
9574a9b5248743fd558572e80967b81ba4728c51.research_question: How can heterogeneous treatment effects be accurately estimated in observational data when treatments are multi-valued, and what are the theoretical and empirical strengths and weaknesses of various meta-learner approaches in this setting?
9574a9b5248743fd558572e80967b81ba4728c51.hypothesis: Meta-learners that are specifically adapted to multi-valued treatments, particularly those leveraging regression adjustment and doubly robust techniques, will outperform naive extensions of binary meta-learners in both theoretical error bounds and empirical estimation accuracy, especially as the number of treatment levels increases.
9574a9b5248743fd558572e80967b81ba4728c51.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed to generalize existing meta-learner algorithms—such as T-learner, S-learner, X-learner, M-learner, DR-learner, and R-learner—to the multi-valued treatment setting for Conditional Average Treatment Effect (CATE) estimation. The methodology will include both direct plug-in (one-step) and pseudo-outcome (two-step) estimators, with particular attention to the construction of consistent pseudo-outcomes that incorporate estimated nuisance components like the generalized propensity score (GPS) and outcome models. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to derive asymptotic bias-variance upper bounds for each meta-learner, explicitly quantifying the impact of the number of treatment levels, overlap, and model misspecification. Additionally, a novel regression-adjustment-based X-learner for multi-valued treatments will be introduced, and the limitations of the generalized R-learner in this context will be analyzed.
9574a9b5248743fd558572e80967b81ba4728c51.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and semi-synthetic datasets. Synthetic datasets will be generated with known ground-truth CATEs, varying the number of treatment levels (e.g., K+1 = 10, 13, 20, etc.), sample size, and treatment assignment mechanisms (randomized and observational). Semi-synthetic experiments will use industrial datasets, such as a geothermal system simulation with engineered confounding and treatment assignment bias. Baselines will include all meta-learners under study, with base learners such as XGBoost and Random Forests. Evaluation metrics will focus on mean and standard deviation of the Precision in Estimation of Heterogeneous Effect (mPEHE and sdPEHE), calculated against the known ground truth. Experimental setups will systematically vary overlap conditions, nuisance parameter estimation accuracy, and treatment distribution to assess robustness and performance under practical constraints.
9574a9b5248743fd558572e80967b81ba4728c51.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a systematic generalization and theoretical analysis of meta-learners for multi-valued treatment settings, including a new regression-adjustment-based X-learner. It provides the first comprehensive asymptotic bias-variance analysis that directly quantifies the impact of the number of treatment levels and overlap on error bounds, moving beyond minimax approaches. The work clarifies when and why certain meta-learners outperform others as treatment complexity increases, and offers practical guidelines for method selection based on theoretical and empirical findings. The proposal also highlights the limitations of naive binary extensions and the challenges of model misspecification in multi-valued causal inference.

9583cadea300f67aaab0fdf7b6d1f774c3cd55e7.title: ShareGPT4Video: Improving Video Understanding and Generation with Better Captions
9583cadea300f67aaab0fdf7b6d1f774c3cd55e7.research_question: How can high-quality, temporally detailed, and scalable video-caption datasets be constructed to improve the performance of large video-language models (LVLMs) and text-to-video models (T2VMs) in both video understanding and video generation tasks?
9583cadea300f67aaab0fdf7b6d1f774c3cd55e7.hypothesis: A differential sliding-window captioning strategy, combined with semantic-aware key-frame extraction and hierarchical prompt design, will enable the creation of large-scale, high-quality video-caption datasets that significantly enhance the temporal understanding and generation capabilities of LVLMs and T2VMs compared to datasets with brief or less detailed captions.
9583cadea300f67aaab0fdf7b6d1f774c3cd55e7.proposed_method: A comprehensive pipeline will be developed for constructing a high-quality video-caption dataset. First, diverse video sources will be selected based on aesthetic quality and content complexity, including open-domain, user-uploaded, and scenario-specific videos. Semantic-based data filtering will be applied to ensure diversity and reduce content homogeneity, using language model embeddings to measure semantic similarity between candidate videos. Semantic-aware key-frame extraction will be performed by computing frame-level semantic embeddings with a CLIP-based encoder, retaining only frames with significant semantic changes. The core captioning process will employ a differential sliding-window strategy: for each pair of adjacent keyframes, a multi-modal model (e.g., GPT-4V) will generate a differential caption describing changes between frames, guided by hierarchical prompts. All differential captions will be aggregated and summarized into a comprehensive, temporally detailed caption for the entire video using a language model. This approach ensures scalability to arbitrary video lengths and maintains high temporal fidelity and content detail.
9583cadea300f67aaab0fdf7b6d1f774c3cd55e7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the constructed dataset and captioning models in both video understanding and generation tasks. For video understanding, several LVLM architectures (e.g., VideoLLaVA, LLaMA-VID) will be trained or fine-tuned with the new dataset and evaluated on multi-modal video benchmarks such as VideoBench, MVBench, and TempCompass, which test various aspects of temporal and semantic comprehension. Baseline comparisons will include models trained on existing datasets with brief captions. Evaluation metrics will include average accuracy across benchmarks, as well as performance on specific temporal and semantic dimensions. For video generation, a text-to-video model (e.g., DiT-based or Latte-XL) will be fine-tuned with the detailed video-caption pairs, and its ability to generate high-fidelity, prompt-aligned videos will be assessed both qualitatively and quantitatively, including human preference studies and prompt adherence analyses. The impact of caption detail (detailed vs. short) on generation quality and controllability will be systematically compared.
9583cadea300f67aaab0fdf7b6d1f774c3cd55e7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a differential sliding-window captioning strategy that enables stable, scalable, and temporally precise video captioning for arbitrary-length videos. The integration of semantic-aware key-frame extraction and hierarchical prompt design further enhances caption quality and consistency. The resulting dataset is claimed to be the first to provide large-scale, high-quality, temporally detailed video-caption pairs spanning diverse domains. The proposed captioning model, ShareCaptioner-Video, offers multi-mode capabilities (fast captioning, sliding captioning, clip summarizing, and prompt re-captioning) and demonstrates efficiency in scaling up high-quality annotations. Experimental results are expected to show that these innovations yield significant improvements in both video understanding and generation tasks, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on multiple public benchmarks.

95898b1f82cf7ad7d96fcc85b4def7f086325af5.title: LESS: Selecting Influential Data for Targeted Instruction Tuning
95898b1f82cf7ad7d96fcc85b4def7f086325af5.research_question: How can relevant and influential data be effectively selected from large, diverse instruction tuning datasets to improve the targeted development of specific capabilities in large language models (LLMs), especially when only a few examples of the desired capability are available?
95898b1f82cf7ad7d96fcc85b4def7f086325af5.hypothesis: A data selection algorithm that estimates optimizer-aware, low-dimensional gradient-based influences between candidate training data and a small set of target examples will enable the selection of a small, highly relevant subset of instruction tuning data that can outperform training on the full dataset for targeted skill induction in LLMs.
95898b1f82cf7ad7d96fcc85b4def7f086325af5.proposed_method: A novel data selection algorithm, LESS (Low-rank gradiEnt Similarity Search), will be developed to estimate the influence of candidate instruction tuning data on a small set of target examples representing the desired capability. LESS adapts classical gradient-based influence formulations to work with the Adam optimizer and variable-length instruction data, addressing challenges such as abnormal sequence-level gradients and computational efficiency. The approach involves a warmup LoRA-based fine-tuning phase to align the selection model with the candidate data distribution, followed by the construction of a reusable, low-dimensional gradient feature datastore using random projections. For each target task, cosine similarity between projected gradient features of candidate data and target examples is computed, and the top-ranked subset is selected for final instruction tuning. The method supports transferability across model sizes and families by allowing small models to select data for larger or different models.
95898b1f82cf7ad7d96fcc85b4def7f086325af5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three diverse downstream datasets: MMLU, TYDIQA, and BBH, each containing multiple subtasks and few-shot target examples. The candidate instruction tuning data will be drawn from a combination of curated and open-ended datasets totaling approximately 270K examples. Baselines will include random selection, BM25 (TF-IDF), DSIR (n-gram features), and RDS (representation-based selection). Evaluation metrics will include downstream task accuracy and, where appropriate, span extraction or multiple-choice accuracy. Models such as LLAMA-2-7B, LLAMA-2-13B, and MISTRAL-7B will be used for both data selection and final training, with both in-family and cross-family transfer scenarios tested. The impact of selection subset size, number of warmup epochs, and gradient projection dimension will be systematically ablated. Computational costs and qualitative interpretability of selected data will also be analyzed.
95898b1f82cf7ad7d96fcc85b4def7f086325af5.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces an optimizer-aware, gradient-based data selection framework tailored for instruction tuning with Adam and variable-length data. It leverages low-rank gradient projections for computational efficiency and enables transferability of selected data across model sizes and families. LESS is claimed to outperform both full-dataset and traditional similarity-based selection methods, often achieving superior downstream performance with only 5% of the data. The approach is also interpretable, selecting data aligned with the reasoning skills required by the target task rather than relying on surface-form similarity.

958bb3831589246fe5b6b58cf99e3b65c58d027f.title: Multi-modal molecule structure–text model for text-based retrieval and editing
958bb3831589246fe5b6b58cf99e3b65c58d027f.research_question: How can a multi-modal model that jointly leverages both molecular structural information and textual domain knowledge enable more generalizable and flexible molecular representation learning for tasks such as text-based molecule retrieval, editing, and property prediction, particularly in zero-shot settings?
958bb3831589246fe5b6b58cf99e3b65c58d027f.hypothesis: Jointly learning representations from both chemical structures and textual descriptions via a contrastive learning paradigm will enable open-vocabulary, compositional, and semantically meaningful molecular representations that generalize better to novel tasks and categories, including zero-shot structure-text retrieval and text-based molecule editing.
958bb3831589246fe5b6b58cf99e3b65c58d027f.proposed_method: A multi-modal molecule structure-text model will be developed, consisting of two branches: one for encoding chemical structures (using either SMILES-based Transformers or graph neural networks) and one for encoding textual descriptions (using a domain-adapted language model such as SciBERT). Both branches will be initialized with powerful pretrained single-modal encoders. The representations from both branches will be projected into a shared latent space using learnable projectors and aligned via a contrastive learning objective (e.g., InfoNCE or EBM-NCE) on a large-scale dataset of structure-text pairs. The model will be pretrained end-to-end on this dataset, enabling the joint space to capture both structural and semantic information. For downstream tasks, the pretrained encoders and projectors will be frozen, and the joint space will be used for zero-shot structure-text retrieval and text-based molecule editing, with an additional adaptor module for aligning generative model latent spaces when needed.
958bb3831589246fe5b6b58cf99e3b65c58d027f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several downstream tasks: (1) Zero-shot structure-text retrieval using three datasets constructed from DrugBank, with retrieval accuracy as the evaluation metric and comparisons to baselines such as pretrained single-modal encoders, similarity-based retrieval, and a SMILES-text language model (KV-PLM). (2) Zero-shot text-based molecule editing using 200 molecules from ZINC and diverse text prompts (single-objective, multi-objective, binding-affinity, and drug-relevance), evaluated by satisfactory hit ratio based on property changes, with baselines including random perturbation, PCA directions, high-variance directions, and genetic search. (3) Molecular property prediction on the MoleculeNet benchmark (eight binary classification datasets), using ROC-AUC as the metric and comparing against state-of-the-art pretraining methods for both SMILES and graph representations. All experiments will use frozen pretrained encoders for zero-shot tasks and fine-tuning for property prediction.
958bb3831589246fe5b6b58cf99e3b65c58d027f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the largest multi-modal structure-text dataset for molecules (PubChemSTM) and a novel multi-modal contrastive pretraining framework that enables open-vocabulary and compositional molecular representations. The method is designed to generalize to unseen biochemical concepts and tasks in a zero-shot manner, outperforming existing baselines on structure-text retrieval and text-based molecule editing. The framework also demonstrates improved performance on standard molecular property prediction benchmarks, and enables new capabilities such as text-driven molecule editing and drug re-purposing analysis, which are not possible with structure-only models.

959656abb37268c3065f2e889ef66061318dd66e.title: Understanding quantum machine learning also requires rethinking generalization
959656abb37268c3065f2e889ef66061318dd66e.research_question: How can the generalization behavior of quantum machine learning models, particularly parameterized quantum circuits (quantum neural networks), be understood and characterized, especially in regimes where traditional complexity-based generalization measures fail to provide meaningful guarantees?
959656abb37268c3065f2e889ef66061318dd66e.hypothesis: Uniform generalization bounds based solely on model family complexity measures (such as VC dimension or Rademacher complexity) are insufficient to explain or guarantee the generalization performance of quantum neural networks, especially when these models are capable of memorizing random data.
959656abb37268c3065f2e889ef66061318dd66e.proposed_method: A systematic investigation will be conducted using randomization experiments on quantum neural network architectures, specifically quantum convolutional neural networks (QCNNs), applied to quantum phase recognition tasks. The methodology involves training QCNNs on quantum data with randomized labels, partially corrupted labels, and randomized quantum states, and comparing their ability to fit and generalize in each scenario. The empirical risk minimization framework will be used, and the generalization gap will be measured by evaluating both training and test errors. Additionally, theoretical constructions will be developed to demonstrate the finite sample expressivity of parameterized quantum circuits, showing that they can fit arbitrary labelings of quantum states under certain conditions. Analytical results will be complemented by formalizing the limitations of uniform generalization bounds in this context.
959656abb37268c3065f2e889ef66061318dd66e.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize the quantum phase classification problem as a benchmark, employing ground states of the generalized cluster Hamiltonian as input data. Training and test datasets will be generated by sampling coupling coefficients and computing ground states for systems of up to 32 qubits. The QCNN architecture will be implemented with varying numbers of qubits and training set sizes. Three types of data randomization will be tested: full randomization of labels, partial corruption of labels, and randomization of input quantum states. For each experiment, the training and test errors, as well as the empirical generalization gap, will be computed. Baselines will include training on uncorrupted data. Evaluation metrics will focus on classification accuracy and the generalization gap, with comparisons to random guessing performance. Optimization will be performed using stochastic, derivative-free methods such as CMA-ES.
959656abb37268c3065f2e889ef66061318dd66e.novelty_claims: The proposed research exposes fundamental limitations of conventional, uniform generalization bounds in quantum machine learning by demonstrating that quantum neural networks can memorize random data and achieve perfect training accuracy even when generalization is poor. It provides both empirical and theoretical evidence that current complexity-based approaches are vacuous in relevant regimes, motivating a paradigm shift in how generalization is studied for quantum models. The work introduces rigorous randomization tests to the quantum setting and develops new theoretical constructions for finite sample expressivity of parameterized quantum circuits, highlighting the need for non-uniform or data-dependent generalization measures in quantum machine learning.

95d3b6d595e0510edb535a5071c48240d4bb950a.title: DrivingGaussian: Composite Gaussian Splatting for Surrounding Dynamic Autonomous Driving Scenes
95d3b6d595e0510edb535a5071c48240d4bb950a.research_question: How can large-scale, dynamic autonomous driving scenes be efficiently and accurately represented and reconstructed for high-fidelity, multi-camera surround view synthesis and dynamic scene simulation?
95d3b6d595e0510edb535a5071c48240d4bb950a.hypothesis: A hierarchical scene representation that incrementally models static backgrounds and dynamically integrates multiple moving objects using composite Gaussian splatting, assisted by LiDAR priors, will enable more photorealistic, temporally consistent, and geometrically accurate reconstructions of complex driving scenes than existing neural rendering methods.
95d3b6d595e0510edb535a5071c48240d4bb950a.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that hierarchically decomposes driving scenes into static backgrounds and multiple dynamic objects using Composite Gaussian Splatting. The static background will be incrementally reconstructed with static 3D Gaussians, leveraging temporal and multi-camera information, while dynamic objects will be individually modeled and integrated via a composite dynamic Gaussian graph. LiDAR priors will be incorporated to initialize Gaussian parameters, providing accurate geometric structure and enhancing multi-view consistency. The method will employ a differentiable 3D Gaussian splatting renderer for global scene synthesis, and a set of specialized loss functions—including tile-based structural similarity, robust loss, and LiDAR-based geometric supervision—will guide the optimization of both static and dynamic components. Occlusion relationships and object interactions will be handled by dynamically adjusting Gaussian opacities based on spatial proximity and camera viewpoint.
95d3b6d595e0510edb535a5071c48240d4bb950a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale autonomous driving datasets such as nuScenes and KITTI-360, utilizing multi-camera images and LiDAR sweeps as input. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines, including NeRF-based models (e.g., Instant-NGP, Mip-NeRF, Urban-NeRF, S-NeRF, EmerNeRF) and 3D Gaussian Splatting variants, with and without LiDAR or SfM initialization. Evaluation metrics will include PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS for image quality, as well as qualitative assessments of dynamic object reconstruction and temporal consistency. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of initialization strategies, module contributions (incremental static Gaussians, dynamic Gaussian graph), and loss functions. Additional experiments will demonstrate the framework's ability to simulate corner cases and edit dynamic scenes, validating its utility for safety-critical autonomous driving tasks.
95d3b6d595e0510edb535a5071c48240d4bb950a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to introduce a composite Gaussian splatting framework tailored for large-scale, dynamic autonomous driving scenes, enabling efficient and high-fidelity surround view synthesis. Key innovations include incremental static 3D Gaussians for scalable background modeling, a composite dynamic Gaussian graph for multi-object dynamic integration, and the use of LiDAR priors as geometric initialization for improved accuracy and multi-view consistency. The framework supports controllable dynamic scene simulation and editing, facilitating robust validation and corner case generation for autonomous driving systems. Extensive experiments are expected to demonstrate superior performance over existing methods in both quantitative and qualitative evaluations.

95eee51c1cb1771e96cd182f47c90a7877461530.title: GRAND: Graph Neural Diffusion
95eee51c1cb1771e96cd182f47c90a7877461530.research_question: How can the principles of partial differential equations (PDEs), specifically diffusion processes, be leveraged to develop a new class of graph neural network (GNN) architectures that address challenges such as depth, oversmoothing, and bottlenecks in graph learning?
95eee51c1cb1771e96cd182f47c90a7877461530.hypothesis: Formulating GNNs as discretizations of underlying diffusion PDEs on graphs, and employing advanced numerical schemes for their solution, will yield architectures that are more stable, scalable to greater depths, and achieve competitive or superior performance on standard graph learning benchmarks compared to existing methods.
95eee51c1cb1771e96cd182f47c90a7877461530.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed in which GNNs are interpreted as discretizations of continuous diffusion processes governed by PDEs on graphs. The method will formalize the layer structure and message passing of GNNs as choices of temporal and spatial discretization operators, allowing both explicit (e.g., Euler, Runge-Kutta) and implicit (e.g., Adams-Moulton) numerical schemes. Both linear and nonlinear versions of the model will be constructed, where the diffusion operator is parameterized by learnable attention mechanisms, such as scaled dot-product attention. The approach will also support graph rewiring by modifying the computational graph independently from the input graph, enabling the design of deep architectures with tens of layers. Stability analyses will be conducted for both explicit and implicit schemes, and adaptive step size solvers will be incorporated to further enhance efficiency and robustness.
95eee51c1cb1771e96cd182f47c90a7877461530.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of standard node classification benchmarks, including citation networks (Cora, Citeseer, Pubmed), co-author and co-purchase graphs (CoauthorCS, Computer, Photo), and the ogb-arxiv dataset. The proposed models will be compared against popular GNN baselines such as GCN, GAT, MoNet, GraphSAGE, as well as recent ODE-based GNNs (CGNN, GDE, GODE) and LanczosNet. Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy and standard deviation across multiple random splits and initializations. Ablation studies will be performed to investigate the impact of different numerical schemes (explicit vs. implicit, fixed vs. adaptive step size), graph rewiring strategies, and model depth. Computational efficiency, parameter count, and stability under perturbations will also be assessed.
95eee51c1cb1771e96cd182f47c90a7877461530.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a principled, PDE-based framework for designing GNNs, unifying and generalizing many existing architectures as special cases of diffusion discretization. It enables the use of advanced numerical integration schemes, including unconditionally stable implicit methods, to construct deep and stable GNNs. The approach supports learnable and adaptive graph rewiring, and achieves competitive or superior performance with significantly fewer parameters. Detailed stability analyses and ablation studies provide insights into the effects of discretization choices, and the method offers a blueprint for systematically developing new GNN architectures grounded in mathematical theory.

95f7ba9242f527d8696a355e6d31f7a9cc858772.title: Stochastic Control for Fine-tuning Diffusion Models: Optimality, Regularity, and Convergence
95f7ba9242f527d8696a355e6d31f7a9cc858772.research_question: How can fine-tuning of diffusion models for downstream tasks, constraints, and human preferences be formulated and solved with theoretical guarantees, particularly in terms of optimality, regularity, and convergence?
95f7ba9242f527d8696a355e6d31f7a9cc858772.hypothesis: Fine-tuning diffusion models can be effectively formulated as a discrete-time stochastic control problem with linear dynamics and KL regularization, leading to well-posedness, regularity of the optimal value function and control, and global linear convergence of a policy iteration algorithm.
95f7ba9242f527d8696a355e6d31f7a9cc858772.proposed_method: A discrete-time stochastic control framework is developed for fine-tuning diffusion models, using denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) as the pre-trained reference dynamics. The fine-tuning process is modeled by introducing a control variable (interpreted as a new score function) that is optimized to maximize a reward signal (e.g., human preference) while penalizing deviation from the pre-trained model via a Kullback–Leibler (KL) regularization term. The resulting objective is solved using a policy iteration algorithm (PI-FT), which leverages the concavity introduced by the KL term to ensure strong theoretical properties. The method includes rigorous analysis of the well-posedness and regularity of the control problem, and provides explicit conditions under which the algorithm converges globally at a linear rate. Extensions to parametric settings and continuous-time formulations are also considered.
95f7ba9242f527d8696a355e6d31f7a9cc858772.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard benchmark datasets for diffusion models, using pre-trained DDPMs as the starting point. The proposed PI-FT algorithm will be evaluated for its ability to fine-tune these models on smaller, task-specific datasets with known reward signals, such as those reflecting human preferences or alignment objectives. Baseline methods will include existing reinforcement learning-based fine-tuning approaches and other empirical fine-tuning techniques. Evaluation metrics will include alignment with target rewards, sample quality, and convergence speed, with ablation studies to assess the impact of regularization parameters and algorithmic choices.
95f7ba9242f527d8696a355e6d31f7a9cc858772.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to provide a stochastic control formulation for fine-tuning diffusion models with provable guarantees on optimality, regularity, and global linear convergence of the policy iteration algorithm. Unlike prior work, which is largely empirical or lacks convergence analysis, the method establishes universal regularity of both the optimal value function and the iterates generated by the algorithm. The framework also naturally extends to parametric and continuous-time settings, offering theoretical insights and practical algorithms for a broad class of fine-tuning problems in diffusion models.

960903429f5585020107b05082b8018cbd26b03e.title: Error Bounds for Learning with Vector-Valued Random Features
960903429f5585020107b05082b8018cbd26b03e.research_question: What are the theoretical error bounds and convergence rates for learning infinite-dimensional vector-valued mappings using random feature models, particularly in the context of ridge regression, and how do these bounds depend on the number of random features and samples?
960903429f5585020107b05082b8018cbd26b03e.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that strong consistency and minimax optimal convergence rates can be achieved for vector-valued random feature ridge regression, with parameter and sample complexity matching or improving upon existing results, even in infinite-dimensional settings and under model misspecification.
960903429f5585020107b05082b8018cbd26b03e.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical framework will be developed for analyzing the error of learning with vector-valued random features (RF) in ridge regression. The approach will directly analyze the underlying risk functional, avoiding reliance on explicit random feature ridge regression solution formulas and matrix concentration inequalities. The method will unify sources of error including approximation, generalization, misspecification, and noisy observations. The analysis will be carried out in a general infinite-dimensional input-output setting, with the random feature model defined as a linear expansion over randomized basis functions, and the estimator trained via regularized empirical risk minimization. Key technical contributions will include new bounds on the empirical risk and generalization gap, leveraging truncation arguments and empirical process theory, and establishing consistency and convergence rates under both well-specified and misspecified models.
960903429f5585020107b05082b8018cbd26b03e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a benchmark operator learning dataset, specifically the time-one flow map of the viscous Burgers' equation on the torus, where the underlying operator is nonlinear and acts between infinite-dimensional function spaces. The input data will consist of iid Gaussian random fields, and the output will be generated without noise for the main study. The random feature ridge regression algorithm will be implemented with varying numbers of random features (M), sample sizes (N), and output dimensions (p). Evaluation will focus on the squared test error, with results averaged over multiple random seeds. The observed error rates will be compared to the theoretical predictions, and the dependence of error on M, N, and p will be analyzed to validate the theoretical sample and parameter complexity.
960903429f5585020107b05082b8018cbd26b03e.novelty_claims: The proposed analysis provides the first comprehensive error bounds for vector-valued random feature models in infinite-dimensional settings, establishing strong consistency and minimax optimal convergence rates. The methodology avoids explicit solution formulas and matrix concentration inequalities, enabling extension to infinite-dimensional output spaces and yielding parameter complexity results that are free from logarithmic factors for the first time. The framework unifies various sources of error and applies under both well-specified and misspecified models, improving upon prior work that focused primarily on scalar-valued or finite-dimensional settings.

960d570013c60f5f8df50134a4824c0eb4012371.title: Sorbet: A Neuromorphic Hardware-Compatible Transformer-Based Spiking Language Model
960d570013c60f5f8df50134a4824c0eb4012371.research_question: How can transformer-based language models be adapted for energy-efficient, privacy-preserving inference on neuromorphic hardware, particularly for deployment in resource-constrained edge devices?
960d570013c60f5f8df50134a4824c0eb4012371.hypothesis: Replacing energy-intensive operations such as softmax and layer normalization in transformer architectures with bit-shifting-based alternatives, combined with model quantization and knowledge distillation, will enable spiking language models that are compatible with neuromorphic hardware and maintain competitive performance while significantly reducing energy consumption.
960d570013c60f5f8df50134a4824c0eb4012371.proposed_method: A novel transformer-based spiking language model, Sorbet, will be developed to operate efficiently on neuromorphic hardware. The method introduces two key hardware-compatible operators: BitShiftingPowerNorm (BSPN) to replace layer normalization, and a Power-of-Two softmax (PTsoftmax) to replace the standard softmax operation. Both operators are designed to use only bit-shifting and addition, avoiding multiplications, divisions, and exponentials, thus aligning with the computational primitives available on neuromorphic chips. The architecture will be based on a BERT-like transformer, with all matrix multiplications replaced by spike-driven accumulations, and all weights and activations quantized to binary or low-bit representations. Knowledge distillation will be applied at multiple stages to transfer performance from a full-precision teacher model to the quantized student model, and a stepwise distillation and conversion process will be used to ensure stable training and effective SNN conversion.
960d570013c60f5f8df50134a4824c0eb4012371.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the GLUE benchmark, covering seven datasets to evaluate language understanding capabilities. The model will be compared against both spiking neural network (SNN) baselines and quantized artificial neural network (ANN) baselines, including BERT, DistilBERT, TinyBERT, BiT, SpikeLM, and SpikingBERT. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy for classification tasks and Spearman correlation for regression tasks. Energy consumption will be estimated using reported hardware costs for relevant operations (e.g., bit-shift, division, multiplication) and measured spike rates, with detailed ablation studies to isolate the contributions of PTsoftmax and BSPN. Additional experiments will assess the impact of quantization levels, timesteps, and spike generation on model performance and energy efficiency.
960d570013c60f5f8df50134a4824c0eb4012371.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable fully neuromorphic hardware-compatible transformer-based language models for NLP tasks, overcoming the incompatibility of softmax and layer normalization with SNN hardware. The introduction of PTsoftmax and BSPN provides efficient, multiplication-free alternatives to these operations, significantly reducing computational and energy costs. The methodology achieves highly compressed binary-weight models through stepwise knowledge distillation and quantization, resulting in substantial energy savings (up to 27.16× compared to BERT) while maintaining competitive performance. The work demonstrates the practical deployment of transformer-based SNNs for language tasks on neuromorphic platforms, filling a critical gap in the field.

962466ca8a3bf432a2d45b656ab5dbcc9caf5b16.title: Agree to Disagree: Diversity through Disagreement for Better Transferability
962466ca8a3bf432a2d45b656ab5dbcc9caf5b16.research_question: How can the diversity of predictive features learned by ensembles of deep neural networks be increased to improve out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization, enhance transferability, and provide better uncertainty estimation, especially in the presence of spurious correlations and simplicity bias?
962466ca8a3bf432a2d45b656ab5dbcc9caf5b16.hypothesis: Enforcing agreement among ensemble members on in-distribution data while encouraging disagreement on OOD data will promote the learning of diverse predictive features, thereby mitigating shortcut learning, improving transferability to new domains, and enhancing uncertainty estimation for OOD samples.
962466ca8a3bf432a2d45b656ab5dbcc9caf5b16.proposed_method: A novel ensemble training algorithm, D-BAT (Diversity-By-disAgreement Training), is proposed to address the limitations of simplicity bias in gradient-based learning. The approach involves training an ensemble of predictors such that they agree on the predictions for the training (in-distribution) data but are explicitly encouraged to disagree on OOD data, which may be unlabeled and sampled from a different distribution. The method is formalized by introducing a regularization term that penalizes agreement on OOD samples while maintaining standard empirical risk minimization on the training data. For binary and multi-class classification, the agreement term is computed via binarized softmax outputs, and the ensemble is trained either sequentially or jointly, with the second and subsequent models being optimized to maximize disagreement with previously trained models on OOD data. The approach leverages the concept of generalized discrepancy from domain adaptation theory and can be extended to larger ensembles by iteratively training each member to disagree with the ensemble formed by the previous members.
962466ca8a3bf432a2d45b656ab5dbcc9caf5b16.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Synthetic datasets such as Colored-MNIST, M/F-Dominoes, and M/C-Dominoes are designed with controlled spurious correlations, while real-world benchmarks include Waterbirds, Camelyon17, and Office-Home. The setup involves training on labeled in-distribution data and using unlabeled OOD data for the disagreement regularizer. Baselines for comparison include standard empirical risk minimization (ERM), deep ensembles, MC-Dropout, and other domain adaptation methods such as DANN, FixMatch, CORAL, and NoisyStudent. Evaluation metrics include test accuracy on both in-distribution and OOD test sets, ensemble accuracy, and uncertainty estimation metrics such as entropy and calibration on OOD samples. Experimental setups include varying the ensemble size, using different OOD data sources, and performing multiple runs to report mean and standard deviation.
962466ca8a3bf432a2d45b656ab5dbcc9caf5b16.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple yet effective diversity-inducing regularizer that enables training ensembles of predictors to utilize diverse features, overcoming the limitations imposed by simplicity bias. Unlike prior approaches, D-BAT does not require pre-trained encoders, can be trained on the full dataset, and operates by enforcing disagreement specifically on OOD data rather than through stochasticity or orthogonality constraints. The method is theoretically motivated by domain adaptation discrepancy and is empirically shown to outperform existing baselines in scenarios with strong spurious correlations, providing improved OOD generalization, better uncertainty estimation, and enhanced ensemble transferability.

9637ef9019671034912ea0f506ae67c3f2fc4689.title: Rewards-in-Context: Multi-objective Alignment of Foundation Models with Dynamic Preference Adjustment
9637ef9019671034912ea0f506ae67c3f2fc4689.research_question: How can foundation models be efficiently aligned with diverse and potentially conflicting human preferences across multiple objectives, enabling dynamic adjustment to user preferences at inference time without incurring prohibitive computational costs?
9637ef9019671034912ea0f506ae67c3f2fc4689.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a supervised fine-tuning approach, which conditions model responses on multiple reward signals within the prompt context and incorporates dynamic preference-to-reward mappings at inference, can achieve effective multi-objective alignment of foundation models. This approach is expected to match or surpass the empirical Pareto front of existing multi-objective RLHF methods while significantly reducing computational resources.
9637ef9019671034912ea0f506ae67c3f2fc4689.proposed_method: The proposed method, Rewards-in-Context (RiC), restructures the multi-objective alignment problem into three stages: (1) An offline training phase where prompts in the dataset are relabeled with reward values from multiple reward models, and the foundation model is fine-tuned using multi-reward conditional supervised learning. (2) An online training phase that augments the dataset by generating new responses near the empirical Pareto front, using multi-objective rejection sampling to select high-quality samples for further fine-tuning. (3) An inference phase where user preferences are dynamically mapped to desired reward values through an analytical solution to a constrained convex optimization problem, and these rewards are injected into the prompt to condition the model's response. This method requires only a single model and leverages reward normalization, prompt relabeling, and a closed-form preference-to-reward mapping to enable flexible, scalable, and efficient adaptation to user-specified objectives.
9637ef9019671034912ea0f506ae67c3f2fc4689.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two text generation tasks (Helpful Assistant and Reddit Summary) and a text-to-image generation task, each involving multiple, potentially conflicting reward models (e.g., harmlessness, helpfulness, humor, faithfulness, aesthetic, compressibility). The base models include Llama-2 7B for text and Stable Diffusion v1.5 for images. Baselines for comparison include MORLHF (multi-objective RLHF), Rewarded Soups, and standard supervised fine-tuning (SFT). Evaluation will use empirical Pareto front analysis by generating responses for a range of user preferences, scoring outputs with off-the-shelf reward models, and comparing the multi-dimensional average test rewards. Computational efficiency will be measured in GPU hours. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of the online training stage and different preference-to-reward mappings.
9637ef9019671034912ea0f506ae67c3f2fc4689.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a highly scalable and computationally efficient framework for multi-objective alignment that requires only supervised fine-tuning of a single foundation model. It supports dynamic, inference-time adjustment to user preferences via an analytical preference-to-reward mapping, avoiding the need for multiple RLHF processes or model interpolations. The method is claimed to achieve superior empirical Pareto fronts compared to existing baselines while using only about 10% of the GPU hours required by multi-objective RLHF. The approach is also robust to the choice of preference-to-reward mapping and can be extended to more than two objectives with minimal additional cost.

964440957c030504f6bcab11f514635ece1bf6b2.title: InfiniGen: Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models with Dynamic KV Cache Management
964440957c030504f6bcab11f514635ece1bf6b2.research_question: How can the memory and data transfer bottlenecks associated with key-value (KV) cache management in large language model (LLM) inference for long-context generation be mitigated, particularly in offloading-based serving systems, without sacrificing model accuracy or throughput?
964440957c030504f6bcab11f514635ece1bf6b2.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that dynamically speculating and prefetching only the essential KV cache entries for attention computation, using minimal rehearsal and partial weight techniques, can significantly reduce memory and data transfer overheads in LLM inference while maintaining or improving model accuracy compared to existing static or compression-based KV cache management methods.
964440957c030504f6bcab11f514635ece1bf6b2.proposed_method: A dynamic KV cache management framework, InfiniGen, will be developed to synergize with modern offloading-based LLM inference systems. The method will maintain the full KV cache pool in CPU memory and, for each decoding step, will speculate on the minimal set of critical KV entries required for the next layer's attention computation using the attention input of the previous layer, partial query weights, and partial key caches. This speculation will be enhanced by skewing the query and key matrices via offline singular value decomposition (SVD) and orthogonal transformations to emphasize important columns, thereby improving the precision of token selection. At runtime, only these essential KV entries will be prefetched to the GPU, reducing PCIe data transfer, while the rest remain in CPU memory. The KV cache pool will be dynamically managed with eviction policies (e.g., counter-based, LRU) to stay within user-defined memory budgets, and the number of prefetched tokens will be adaptively adjusted per layer and query token based on observed attention patterns.
964440957c030504f6bcab11f514635ece1bf6b2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on representative LLMs, including OPT (6.7B, 13B, 30B) and Llama-2 (7B, 13B), using a system with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU connected via PCIe 3.0. The evaluation will cover a range of batch sizes and sequence lengths, using both few-shot downstream tasks (COPA, OpenBookQA, WinoGrande, PIQA, RTE from lm-evaluation-harness) and language modeling datasets (WikiText-2, Penn Treebank, and long-context samples from PG-19). Baselines will include full-cache inference, H2O (state-of-the-art KV eviction), and quantization-based KV compression, using both CUDA Unified Virtual Memory (UVM) and FlexGen for offloading. Metrics will include model accuracy (for classification tasks), perplexity (for language modeling), and wall-clock inference latency. The fraction of KV cache entries prefetched will be varied, and the impact on both accuracy and speedup will be measured.
964440957c030504f6bcab11f514635ece1bf6b2.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel dynamic KV cache management framework that speculates and prefetches only the critical KV entries needed for attention computation, rather than relying on static budgets or lossy compression. The method leverages offline SVD-based skewing of query and key matrices to improve the efficiency and precision of token selection for prefetching. Unlike prior work, the approach adapts the number of prefetched tokens per layer and query, accounts for the dynamic nature of attention patterns, and avoids permanent eviction of potentially important tokens. The framework is designed to work synergistically with offloading-based inference systems, enabling efficient long-context generation beyond GPU memory limits, and claims substantial improvements in both inference speed (up to 3x) and model accuracy (up to 32.6 percentage points) over existing methods.

964bd39b546f0f6625ff3b9ef1083f797807ef2e.title: BLOOM: A 176B-Parameter Open-Access Multilingual Language Model
964bd39b546f0f6625ff3b9ef1083f797807ef2e.research_question: How can a large-scale, open-access, multilingual language model be developed to provide competitive performance across a wide variety of languages and tasks, while addressing issues of inclusivity, transparency, and responsible data governance in language model development?
964bd39b546f0f6625ff3b9ef1083f797807ef2e.hypothesis: A collaboratively developed, open-access, multilingual language model trained on a carefully curated, diverse dataset spanning many natural and programming languages will achieve performance comparable to proprietary large language models, and will facilitate broader research, inclusivity, and responsible AI development.
964bd39b546f0f6625ff3b9ef1083f797807ef2e.proposed_method: A 176-billion-parameter decoder-only Transformer language model will be constructed and trained using the ROOTS corpus, a composite dataset comprising 1.61 terabytes of text from 46 natural languages and 13 programming languages. The model architecture will follow state-of-the-art Transformer designs, optimized for large-scale distributed training on high-performance computing infrastructure. The data curation process will emphasize human involvement, local and language expertise, and explicit data governance, ensuring traceability and respect for data rights holders. Tokenization will be adapted to handle the multilingual and multi-domain nature of the corpus, and training objectives will focus on autoregressive language modeling. The entire development process will be guided by an ethical charter prioritizing inclusivity, openness, and responsibility.
964bd39b546f0f6625ff3b9ef1083f797807ef2e.experiment_details: The model will be evaluated on a broad range of multilingual and monolingual NLP benchmarks, covering both natural and programming languages. Baselines will include existing large language models such as GPT-3 and other state-of-the-art systems, with performance measured using standard metrics for language modeling, text generation, and downstream tasks. Experiments will include few-shot, zero-shot, and multitask prompted finetuning scenarios to assess the model's generalization capabilities. The evaluation will also analyze the impact of multilinguality, dataset diversity, and ethical considerations, with interpretability and bias assessments included as part of the experimental setup.
964bd39b546f0f6625ff3b9ef1083f797807ef2e.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first open-access, 176B-parameter multilingual language model developed through a large-scale, international, collaborative effort. Key innovations include the creation and release of the ROOTS corpus—a highly diverse, well-documented multilingual dataset—and the implementation of transparent, responsible data governance practices. The project aims to democratize access to large language models, promote inclusivity in language coverage, and set new standards for ethical and reproducible AI research.

964cf818be53884a9352cf32c89e2de26c560708.title: Exploiting Structure in Offline Multi-Agent RL: The Benefits of Low Interaction Rank
964cf818be53884a9352cf32c89e2de26c560708.research_question: Can natural structural assumptions in offline multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) enable the design of algorithms that are both sample-efficient and computationally efficient, particularly in the presence of distribution shift and a large number of agents?
964cf818be53884a9352cf32c89e2de26c560708.hypothesis: Functions with low interaction rank (IR) are significantly more robust to distribution shift than general function classes, and leveraging this property in offline MARL will enable decentralized, computationally and statistically efficient learning algorithms that avoid exponential sample complexity in the number of agents.
964cf818be53884a9352cf32c89e2de26c560708.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed for offline MARL that exploits the structural property of low interaction rank in reward functions. The approach will combine regularization (specifically, χ2-divergence regularization) and no-regret learning within decentralized policy updates. In the contextual game setting, a decentralized, χ2-regularized, no-regret policy gradient algorithm will be used, where each agent updates its policy by solving a quadratic optimization problem involving the learned reward, regularization, and a Bregman divergence term. For Markov games with decoupled transitions, a decentralized regularized actor-critic (DR-AC) algorithm will be proposed, which first learns reward and transition models using least squares regression and maximum likelihood estimation, then iteratively updates critics and actors using the learned models and regularized policy gradients. The method is designed to ensure that the sample complexity and computational requirements scale polynomially with the number of agents when the interaction rank is low.
964cf818be53884a9352cf32c89e2de26c560708.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on offline MARL benchmarks, including contextual games and Markov games with decoupled transitions. Critic architectures with varying interaction ranks will be compared, including standard single-agent value decomposition architectures as baselines. Evaluation metrics will include the quality of learned equilibria (e.g., approximate coarse correlated equilibrium gap), robustness to distribution shift, and sample efficiency. Datasets will be generated using fixed behavior policies, and the algorithms will be evaluated on their ability to learn near-equilibrium policies from offline data. Hyperparameters such as the regularization strength and number of policy update iterations will be tuned for fair comparison.
964cf818be53884a9352cf32c89e2de26c560708.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the concept of interaction rank as a structural property that directly impacts robustness to distribution shift in offline MARL. It claims that leveraging low interaction rank in function approximation, combined with regularization and no-regret learning, enables the design of decentralized algorithms with polynomial sample complexity in the number of agents. The approach departs from standard single-agent value decomposition by explicitly modeling and exploiting multi-agent reward structure, and provides both theoretical guarantees and empirical evidence for improved efficiency and robustness.

964f09f7f8b0fe8194b839dff8ada1d6c8c151d5.title: Mirror Descent Strikes Again: Optimal Stochastic Convex Optimization under Infinite Noise Variance
964f09f7f8b0fe8194b839dff8ada1d6c8c151d5.research_question: What are the optimal convergence rates and algorithmic strategies for stochastic convex optimization when the stochastic gradient noise has infinite variance, and can an algorithm be designed to match the information-theoretic lower bounds in this setting?
964f09f7f8b0fe8194b839dff8ada1d6c8c151d5.hypothesis: Stochastic mirror descent, equipped with an appropriately chosen uniformly convex mirror map, achieves minimax optimal convergence rates for stochastic convex optimization problems where the stochastic gradient noise has only a bounded (1+κ)-th moment (for some κ in (0,1]), even without explicit gradient clipping or normalization.
964f09f7f8b0fe8194b839dff8ada1d6c8c151d5.proposed_method: A stochastic mirror descent (SMD) algorithm will be developed for convex optimization over a bounded convex set, where access is provided to a stochastic first-order oracle that returns unbiased gradients with finite (1+κ)-th moment for some κ in (0,1]. The method will employ a carefully selected mirror map, specifically a uniformly convex function tailored to the noise moment parameter κ and the geometry of the feasible set, to induce robustness against heavy-tailed noise. The SMD update will be performed in the dual space defined by the mirror map and its Fenchel conjugate, followed by a projection back to the feasible set using the associated Bregman divergence. Step sizes will be chosen based on the noise level and κ, and explicit forms of the mirror map will be provided for different norm settings to optimize dimension dependence and convergence rates.
964f09f7f8b0fe8194b839dff8ada1d6c8c151d5.experiment_details: Theoretical analysis will be conducted to establish non-asymptotic convergence rates for the proposed SMD algorithm under the infinite noise variance regime, with explicit dependence on the number of iterations, problem dimension, and geometric parameters. Information-theoretic lower bounds on the minimax error will be derived for the class of convex, Lipschitz functions over bounded domains, using reductions to hypothesis testing problems. The convergence rates of SMD will be compared to these lower bounds to demonstrate optimality. No empirical datasets or computational experiments are specified; all results are analytical and proven in expectation, with dimension dependence and step size choices made explicit.
964f09f7f8b0fe8194b839dff8ada1d6c8c151d5.novelty_claims: This proposal establishes the first non-asymptotic convergence guarantees for stochastic mirror descent in the heavy-tailed noise regime where the stochastic gradient has infinite variance. The method achieves minimax optimal rates without requiring explicit gradient clipping or normalization, which are common in existing approaches. The analysis provides explicit dimension dependence and covers a broad class of convex functions, extending information-theoretic lower bounds to the infinite variance setting. The proposed approach demonstrates that mirror descent, with a suitable mirror map, inherently regularizes against heavy-tailed noise and matches the best possible rates achievable by any algorithm using only stochastic first-order oracles.

967998eb3d491827832d9d5d5389a242bcce2ee3.title: TADA: Improved Diffusion Sampling with Training-free Augmented Dynamics
967998eb3d491827832d9d5d5389a242bcce2ee3.research_question: How can the efficiency of diffusion model sampling be improved without retraining, while maintaining or enhancing the quality of generated images across various pretrained diffusion models and datasets?
967998eb3d491827832d9d5d5389a242bcce2ee3.hypothesis: Introducing higher-dimensional initial noise and leveraging momentum dynamics in the sampling process, while reusing pretrained diffusion models, will enable faster and more diverse image generation without sacrificing sample quality.
967998eb3d491827832d9d5d5389a242bcce2ee3.proposed_method: A novel sampling method, Training-free Augmented DynAmics (TADA), will be developed to accelerate diffusion model sampling by augmenting the phase space with higher-dimensional initial noise. The approach will establish a theoretical equivalence between momentum diffusion models and conventional diffusion models, allowing direct reuse of pretrained models without additional training. The method will employ an ordinary differential equation (ODE) solver, with the neural network input reparameterized as a weighted linear combination of augmented variables, enabling control over the level of sample detail via a simple hyper-parameter. The dynamics will be analytically characterized, and the system will be designed to inherit stochastic differential equation (SDE)-like properties, such as sample diversity, even under deterministic ODE solvers.
967998eb3d491827832d9d5d5389a242bcce2ee3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using representative pretrained diffusion models, including EDM, EDM2, and Stable Diffusion 3, covering both pixel and latent spaces, as well as class- and text-conditional settings. Datasets such as ImageNet-64 and ImageNet-512 will be used for benchmarking. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art ODE and SDE solvers such as UniPC and DPM-Solver++. Evaluation metrics will comprise Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Fréchet Distance-DINOv2 (FD-DINOv2), and HPSv2 for text-to-image generation. Ablation studies will be performed over discretization schemes, solver variants, and the number of augmented variables, with experiments designed to measure both sampling speed (number of function evaluations) and image quality.
967998eb3d491827832d9d5d5389a242bcce2ee3.novelty_claims: The proposed method is training-free and enables direct integration of pretrained diffusion models into a momentum-augmented sampling framework. It introduces the use of higher-dimensional noise to enhance detail and diversity in generated samples, while allowing explicit control over sample diversity through a hyper-parameter. The approach is orthogonal to existing solver methodologies and can be combined with advanced ODE solvers and classifier-free guidance schedules. Theoretical analysis establishes a fundamental equivalence between momentum and conventional diffusion models, and empirical results demonstrate significant improvements in sampling speed and sample quality over current state-of-the-art methods.

9695824d7a01fad57ba9c01d7d76a519d78d65e7.title: Photorealistic Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with Deep Language Understanding
9695824d7a01fad57ba9c01d7d76a519d78d65e7.research_question: How can text-to-image synthesis models be designed to achieve unprecedented photorealism and deep language understanding, leveraging advances in large language models and diffusion models?
