9695824d7a01fad57ba9c01d7d76a519d78d65e7.hypothesis: Scaling the size of frozen, pretrained language models used as text encoders will significantly improve both the fidelity and semantic alignment of images generated by diffusion-based text-to-image models, surpassing the impact of scaling the image model itself. Additionally, novel diffusion sampling and architectural techniques can further enhance photorealism and text-image alignment.
9695824d7a01fad57ba9c01d7d76a519d78d65e7.proposed_method: A novel text-to-image generation framework is proposed that integrates large, frozen pretrained language models (such as T5-XXL) as text encoders to map input text into embedding sequences. These embeddings condition a cascade of diffusion models: a base 64×64 text-to-image diffusion model, followed by two text-conditional super-resolution diffusion models to generate 256×256 and 1024×1024 images. Classifier-free guidance is employed for effective text conditioning, and a new dynamic thresholding technique is introduced to enable the use of large guidance weights without degrading sample quality. The architecture includes an Efficient U-Net variant for improved memory efficiency and convergence speed, and all models are conditioned on the full sequence of text embeddings using cross-attention at multiple resolutions.
9695824d7a01fad57ba9c01d7d76a519d78d65e7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a combination of large-scale internal and public datasets, including approximately 460M internal image-text pairs and 400M pairs from the LAION dataset. The primary evaluation benchmarks will be the MS-COCO validation set (using zero-shot FID-30K and CLIP score for automated evaluation) and a newly introduced DrawBench benchmark, which features 200 prompts across 11 categories to probe compositionality, spatial relations, rare words, and more. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art models such as DALL-E 2, GLIDE, Latent Diffusion Models, and VQ-GAN+CLIP. Human evaluations will assess both photorealism and image-text alignment, with raters comparing model outputs to reference images and across models. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of text encoder size, diffusion model size, thresholding methods, and architectural choices.
9695824d7a01fad57ba9c01d7d76a519d78d65e7.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the use of large, frozen, pretrained language models as text encoders for text-to-image diffusion models, demonstrating that scaling the text encoder is more impactful than scaling the image model. A new dynamic thresholding technique is developed to support high guidance weights in diffusion sampling, resulting in improved photorealism and alignment. The Efficient U-Net architecture is proposed for faster and more memory-efficient training and inference. A comprehensive new benchmark, DrawBench, is introduced to enable multi-dimensional evaluation of text-to-image models. The overall approach is claimed to achieve state-of-the-art results in both automated and human evaluations, setting new standards for photorealism and language understanding in text-to-image synthesis.

96960e355ffbc287ab3a2dbd789839246345308f.title: PIGEON: Predicting Image Geolocations
96960e355ffbc287ab3a2dbd789839246345308f.research_question: How can image geolocalization be improved to achieve high accuracy and generalization at a planet-scale, including for unseen locations and diverse image distributions?
96960e355ffbc287ab3a2dbd789839246345308f.hypothesis: A geolocalization system that combines semantic geocell creation, multi-task contrastive pretraining with auxiliary geographic and climate data, a novel distance-aware loss function, and hierarchical retrieval-based guess refinement will significantly improve geolocalization accuracy and generalization across both street-level and general-purpose image datasets.
96960e355ffbc287ab3a2dbd789839246345308f.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a geolocalization framework that partitions the Earth's surface into semantic geocells using hierarchical administrative boundaries, clustering (OPTICS), and Voronoi tessellation to ensure contextually meaningful and balanced classes. The system leverages a vision transformer backbone (CLIP ViT-L/14 336) with a linear geocell prediction head, and employs multi-task contrastive pretraining using synthetic captions augmented with geographic, climate, and directional metadata. A novel loss function based on haversine distance is used to smooth classification labels, enabling the model to learn relationships between adjacent geocells and better handle boundary cases. During inference, the model performs hierarchical retrieval over location clusters within the top-K geocell predictions, refining guesses by minimizing embedding distances at both inter- and intra-cell levels. Multi-task learning is further employed by adding auxiliary prediction heads for climate zone, season, and environmental variables, with shared parameters to encourage generalizable feature learning.
96960e355ffbc287ab3a2dbd789839246345308f.experiment_details: Two models will be trained: one (PIGEON) on a custom dataset of 100,000 GeoGuessr locations with four-image panoramas per location (400,000 images total), and another (PIGEOTTO) on over 4 million Flickr and Wikipedia images for general-purpose geolocalization. Evaluation will be conducted on a holdout set of 5,000 GeoGuessr Street View locations for PIGEON, and on established benchmarks (IM2GPS, IM2GPS3k, YFCC4k, YFCC26k, GWS15k) for PIGEOTTO. Performance will be measured using median distance error and the percentage of predictions within specified distance radii (1km, 25km, 200km, 750km, 2,500km). Baselines will include prior state-of-the-art models such as PlaNet, CPlaNet, ISNs, Translocator, and GeoDecoder. Additional experiments will include ablation studies to assess the contribution of each component and blind comparisons against human players, including top GeoGuessr professionals.
96960e355ffbc287ab3a2dbd789839246345308f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces several innovations: (1) a semantic geocell creation algorithm that combines hierarchical administrative boundaries, clustering, and Voronoi tessellation, making semantic geocells feasible for any dataset size and distribution; (2) a novel haversine distance-based label smoothing and loss function that enables parameter sharing across implicit geographic hierarchies and improves generalization; (3) multi-task contrastive pretraining of CLIP with synthetic, domain-specific captions enriched by auxiliary geographic and climate metadata; (4) a hierarchical retrieval mechanism for location refinement that operates over and within geocells, increasing prediction granularity to the dataset size; and (5) the first demonstration of a geolocalization system that reliably outperforms top human experts and achieves state-of-the-art results on diverse, planet-scale benchmarks, including for unseen locations.

96b6f20dc542085b9493f3a03fed6feb253b0dcf.title: Adaptive Data Analysis with Correlated Observations
96b6f20dc542085b9493f3a03fed6feb253b0dcf.research_question: How can adaptive data analysis be performed with statistically valid guarantees when the data samples are correlated rather than independent, and what algorithmic frameworks can support generalization in this non-i.i.d. setting?
96b6f20dc542085b9493f3a03fed6feb253b0dcf.hypothesis: Differential privacy and transcript compression techniques can be extended to provide generalization guarantees for adaptive data analysis even when the data samples exhibit bounded correlations, as quantified by a suitable dependence measure.
96b6f20dc542085b9493f3a03fed6feb253b0dcf.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed for adaptive data analysis in the presence of correlated observations, quantified using a new measure called Gibbs dependence. The approach will extend the connection between differential privacy and generalization from the i.i.d. setting to the correlated case by showing that (ε,δ)-differentially private mechanisms can still guarantee statistical accuracy, with the generalization error scaling with the Gibbs dependence parameter ψ. Additionally, transcript compression techniques will be adapted to the non-i.i.d. setting, ensuring that mechanisms can provide accurate answers to adaptive queries as long as the queries are sufficiently concentrated, with guarantees that depend on the empirical concentration of each query. The methodology will include rigorous theoretical analysis, construction of tight negative examples, and the design of computationally efficient mechanisms that are oblivious to the specific concentration parameters of queries.
96b6f20dc542085b9493f3a03fed6feb253b0dcf.experiment_details: The experimental evaluation will involve both theoretical and empirical analysis. Synthetic datasets will be generated with varying levels of correlation, including product measures (ψ = 0), Markov random fields, and custom-constructed distributions with controlled Gibbs dependence. Mechanisms based on differential privacy and transcript compression will be implemented and evaluated on their ability to answer adaptive queries with statistical accuracy. Baselines will include existing methods for adaptive data analysis in the i.i.d. case and the typical-stability framework. Evaluation metrics will focus on the generalization error (difference between empirical and true query answers), the number of adaptive queries answered, and computational efficiency. Experiments will also include tight negative examples to demonstrate the necessity of the ψ-dependence in the bounds.
96b6f20dc542085b9493f3a03fed6feb253b0dcf.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the concept of Gibbs dependence as a general and quantifiable measure of correlation for adaptive data analysis, enabling the extension of differential privacy-based generalization guarantees to non-i.i.d. data. The approach provides tight bounds on generalization error that scale with the degree of dependence, and demonstrates that mild dependencies can be accommodated with little to no loss in statistical accuracy. Additionally, the adaptation of transcript compression to the correlated setting yields mechanisms that are both simpler and more flexible than previous approaches, allowing for query-dependent concentration without requiring prior knowledge of concentration parameters. The framework is shown to be tight via explicit negative examples, establishing the optimality of the dependence on ψ.

96d0c001e17160ee25fc62c20bc59ac10e6b5410.title: Inverse Optimization: Theory and Applications
96d0c001e17160ee25fc62c20bc59ac10e6b5410.research_question: How can inverse optimization be systematically formulated and solved across a wide range of mathematical programming models, and what are the theoretical and practical implications of applying inverse optimization in diverse application domains?
96d0c001e17160ee25fc62c20bc59ac10e6b5410.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a unified taxonomy and methodological framework for inverse optimization can be developed, enabling efficient and tractable solution methods for both classical (perfect fit) and data-driven (imperfect fit) scenarios across linear, convex, conic, and discrete optimization models. Furthermore, it is expected that these frameworks will facilitate the estimation of latent parameters and preferences from observed decision data in various application areas.
96d0c001e17160ee25fc62c20bc59ac10e6b5410.proposed_method: A comprehensive taxonomy of inverse optimization models will be developed, categorizing them along three main dimensions: the structure of the forward problem (e.g., linear, convex, conic, discrete, or sequential), the type of parameters to be estimated (objective, constraints, or both), and the model-data fit (perfect or imperfect). For classical inverse optimization, bilevel programs will be formulated to enforce inverse-feasibility, with reformulations leveraging duality and optimality conditions (such as complementary slackness and KKT conditions) to obtain tractable single-level optimization problems. For data-driven inverse optimization, loss functions will be introduced to penalize deviations from inverse-feasibility, leading to empirical risk minimization frameworks that can accommodate noisy or imperfect data. Specialized algorithms will be designed for each model class, including linear programming, conic programming, semi-definite programming, and mixed-integer programming, depending on the forward model's structure and the estimation targets.
96d0c001e17160ee25fc62c20bc59ac10e6b5410.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets to evaluate the effectiveness and tractability of the proposed inverse optimization frameworks. Synthetic datasets will be generated for canonical optimization problems (e.g., shortest path, minimum cost flow, quadratic programming) with known ground-truth parameters, allowing for controlled assessment of parameter recovery accuracy. Real-world datasets will be drawn from application domains such as transportation (e.g., route choice data), healthcare (e.g., treatment decisions), and power systems (e.g., electricity consumption patterns). Baseline methods will include traditional parameter estimation techniques, direct optimization without inverse modeling, and existing inverse optimization algorithms. Evaluation metrics will comprise parameter estimation error, computational efficiency, and the quality of model-data fit (e.g., sub-optimality loss, empirical risk). Experimental setups will systematically vary the forward model structure, the type and amount of observed decision data, and the presence of noise or model misspecification.
96d0c001e17160ee25fc62c20bc59ac10e6b5410.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified and systematic taxonomy for inverse optimization, bridging classical and data-driven approaches across a broad spectrum of optimization models. Novel reformulation techniques are developed for both objective and constraint parameter estimation, including tractable algorithms for linear, conic, and convex models, as well as robust and sequential decision-making settings. The framework extends inverse optimization to handle imperfect data via loss-based formulations, enabling practical application in noisy or complex real-world environments. Additionally, the research consolidates and generalizes solution methods, providing a foundation for future methodological advances and expanding the applicability of inverse optimization to new domains.

96db843d31bb148f8281c5231b39c0b08fe9d33d.title: Compress, Gather, and Recompute: REFORMing Long-Context Processing in Transformers
96db843d31bb148f8281c5231b39c0b08fe9d33d.research_question: How can transformer-based language models efficiently and accurately process extremely long contexts, far exceeding their pre-trained context window, without incurring prohibitive computational and memory costs or suffering from information loss?
96db843d31bb148f8281c5231b39c0b08fe9d33d.hypothesis: A two-phase inference framework that combines recurrent chunked processing with on-demand cache recomputation, leveraging cross-layer context embeddings and selective token gathering, will enable efficient and high-fidelity long-context processing in transformers, outperforming existing recurrent and random-access approaches in both accuracy and resource efficiency.
96db843d31bb148f8281c5231b39c0b08fe9d33d.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a framework that processes long input sequences in two distinct phases. In the first phase, the input is segmented into large chunks and processed iteratively, maintaining a compressed key-value (KV) cache using attention-based token eviction. During each iteration, key QKV states from selected transformer layers and heads are extracted to construct lightweight, cross-layer context embeddings for all tokens, and an early-exit strategy is applied to skip unnecessary upper layers, further reducing computation and memory requirements. In the second phase, a similarity search is performed between the query (typically the most recent input tokens) and the stored context embeddings to identify and gather the most relevant historical tokens. These selected tokens are then forwarded through the model again to recompute the KV cache, enabling high-fidelity representations for contextually important tokens without maintaining the full cache for all tokens. This compress-gather-recompute pipeline balances efficiency and retrieval accuracy, and is modality-agnostic, requiring no changes to model parameters.
96db843d31bb148f8281c5231b39c0b08fe9d33d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of long-context understanding tasks and benchmarks. Synthetic and realistic datasets such as Needle-in-a-Haystack (NIAH), RULER, BABILong, ∞-Bench, RepoEval, and MM-NIAH will be used to evaluate retrieval accuracy, question answering, aggregation, multi-hop reasoning, code completion, and multi-modal capabilities. The method will be compared against strong baselines including StreamingLLM, TOVA, H2O, InfiniPot, InfLLM, and truncation, across multiple transformer models such as Mistral-NeMo-Instruct-2407, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B/7B, and Pixtral-12B-2409. Evaluation metrics will include task-specific accuracy (e.g., recall, edit similarity), inference time, and peak memory usage. Experimental setups will ensure fair comparison by using consistent chunk sizes, cache budgets, and token selection strategies across all methods.
96db843d31bb148f8281c5231b39c0b08fe9d33d.novelty_claims: The proposed framework uniquely combines the efficiency of recurrent compression with the high recall of random-access methods through a compress-gather-recompute pipeline, enabling selective and high-fidelity recomputation of relevant context. It introduces a cross-layer, multi-head context embedding mechanism for effective token retrieval, and an early-exit strategy for further efficiency. The approach is modality-agnostic, requires no model parameter changes, and demonstrates superior performance and resource efficiency across diverse tasks and domains, including multi-modal scenarios. Extensive ablation studies and efficiency analyses substantiate the contributions and flexibility of the method.

96ea07447d2f9adefe03852a878517a2a6d45b96.title: Learning to Prompt for Vision-Language Models
96ea07447d2f9adefe03852a878517a2a6d45b96.research_question: How can large pre-trained vision-language models be efficiently adapted to downstream image recognition tasks without manual prompt engineering, and how does automated prompt learning impact transfer performance and robustness to domain shifts?
96ea07447d2f9adefe03852a878517a2a6d45b96.hypothesis: Automated, learnable prompt optimization for vision-language models will outperform hand-crafted prompts and linear probe baselines in few-shot and domain generalization settings, while requiring minimal labeled data.
96ea07447d2f9adefe03852a878517a2a6d45b96.proposed_method: A novel framework, Context Optimization (CoOp), will be developed to automate prompt learning for vision-language models such as CLIP. CoOp models the context words in prompts as continuous, learnable vectors, while keeping all pre-trained model parameters fixed. Two variants will be implemented: unified context, where the same set of context vectors is shared across all classes, and class-specific context, where each class has its own set of context vectors. The context vectors can be initialized randomly or with pre-trained word embeddings, and are optimized end-to-end using standard cross-entropy loss, with gradients back-propagated through the text encoder. The approach allows flexible prompt structures, such as placing the class token at the end or in the middle of the prompt, and supports both generic and fine-grained classification tasks.
96ea07447d2f9adefe03852a878517a2a6d45b96.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 11 diverse image classification datasets, including ImageNet, Caltech101, OxfordPets, StanfordCars, Flowers102, Food101, FGVCAircraft, SUN397, DTD, EuroSAT, and UCF101, covering generic, fine-grained, scene, action, texture, and satellite imagery recognition. Few-shot learning protocols will be followed, using 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16 shots per class, with performance averaged over three runs. Baselines will include zero-shot CLIP with hand-crafted prompts and linear probe models trained on CLIP features. Evaluation metrics will be classification accuracy on the full test sets, with additional experiments measuring robustness to domain shifts using ImageNet-V2, ImageNet-Sketch, ImageNet-A, and ImageNet-R. Ablation studies will explore the effects of context length, initialization, prompt position, and vision backbone architecture. Comparisons will also be made against prompt ensembling and alternative fine-tuning strategies.
96ea07447d2f9adefe03852a878517a2a6d45b96.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first comprehensive framework for continuous prompt learning in large vision-language models, automating prompt engineering and enabling efficient adaptation to downstream tasks. It provides two flexible implementations (unified and class-specific context) tailored to different recognition scenarios. The approach demonstrates that learnable prompts can significantly surpass both hand-crafted prompts and linear probe baselines in few-shot learning and domain generalization, achieving large performance gains with minimal labeled data. Additionally, the method shows superior robustness to distribution shifts compared to traditional fine-tuning and manual prompt engineering, and is extensible to various architectures and tasks.

96f75d06ce8bc26128f0af0071b374d065bf7d64.title: Prediction-powered inference
96f75d06ce8bc26128f0af0071b374d065bf7d64.research_question: How can valid statistical inference be performed when experimental datasets are supplemented with predictions from machine learning systems, particularly when labeled data is scarce and unlabeled data with predictions is abundant?
96f75d06ce8bc26128f0af0071b374d065bf7d64.hypothesis: Incorporating machine learning predictions into statistical inference, while properly accounting for prediction errors, enables the construction of confidence intervals and p-values that are both valid and more data-efficient than classical approaches relying solely on labeled data.
96f75d06ce8bc26128f0af0071b374d065bf7d64.proposed_method: A new framework, prediction-powered inference, will be developed to combine gold-standard (labeled) data with abundant machine learning predictions on unlabeled data to construct valid confidence intervals and p-values for a wide range of statistical estimands, such as means, quantiles, and regression coefficients. The method introduces the concept of a 'rectifier', a problem-specific measure of prediction error, which is estimated using the labeled data. The approach involves three main steps: (1) defining the rectifier for the estimand of interest, (2) constructing a confidence set for the rectifier using standard statistical tools, and (3) forming a prediction-powered confidence set by adjusting the imputed estimate (from predictions) with the rectifier confidence set. The methodology is applicable to estimands expressible as solutions to convex optimization problems and does not require any assumptions about the machine learning model used for predictions. Algorithms will be provided for mean, quantile, linear and logistic regression, and general convex estimation problems, using both asymptotic and non-asymptotic statistical techniques.
96f75d06ce8bc26128f0af0071b374d065bf7d64.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on real-world datasets from diverse scientific domains, including proteomics (using AlphaFold predictions), astronomy (galaxy classification with computer vision), genomics (gene expression analysis with transformers), remote sensing (deforestation analysis), census analysis (health insurance and income prediction with boosted trees), and ecology (plankton counting with computer vision). For each application, prediction-powered confidence intervals will be computed and compared to both classical inference (using only labeled data) and the imputation approach (treating predictions as ground truth). Evaluation metrics will include the width of confidence intervals, coverage probability, and the number of labeled examples required to make statistically significant discoveries at a fixed confidence level (e.g., 95%). Experimental setups will involve repeated random splits of data into labeled and unlabeled sets, and results will be reported as a function of labeled sample size.
96f75d06ce8bc26128f0af0071b374d065bf7d64.novelty_claims: The proposed framework enables valid statistical inference that leverages machine learning predictions without making any assumptions about the prediction model, providing provably valid confidence intervals and p-values for a broad class of estimands. The approach generalizes and unifies concepts from model-assisted survey sampling, missing data, and measurement error literature, but extends them to settings with arbitrary black-box predictors and potential distribution shifts. The rectifier-based adjustment is a key innovation that allows for data-efficient inference, often yielding tighter confidence intervals than classical methods. The framework is broadly applicable, technically simple to implement, and is supported by practical algorithms and software for immediate use in scientific research.

970297a1860c904eaf39f77cb4324ecfad67fcfb.title: Improved Representation Steering for Language Models
970297a1860c904eaf39f77cb4324ecfad67fcfb.research_question: How can language models be steered in a fine-grained, interpretable, and robust manner to incorporate or suppress specific concepts, while minimizing parameter count and maintaining scalability across model sizes?
970297a1860c904eaf39f77cb4324ecfad67fcfb.hypothesis: A reference-free, bi-directional preference optimization objective can improve the effectiveness, interpretability, and robustness of intervention-based steering methods for language models, outperforming standard language modeling and prior preference-based objectives, especially at larger model scales.
970297a1860c904eaf39f77cb4324ecfad67fcfb.proposed_method: A novel training objective, Reference-free Preference Steering (RePS), will be developed for intervention-based steering of language models. RePS is a bi-directional, reference-free preference optimization approach that increases the likelihood of desired (steered) responses when positive interventions are applied and suppresses targeted concepts when negative interventions are used. The method operates without constraining the policy model to remain close to a reference model, allowing for more flexible and effective steering. RePS will be instantiated with several low-rank parameterizations, including rank-1 steering vectors (SV), low-rank adapters (LoRA), and low-rank representation fine-tuning (LoReFT), and will incorporate a factor-sampling strategy during training to stabilize and enhance learning. The approach will be adapted for both concept steering (incorporation) and concept suppression (removal) tasks, with interventions applied to specific layers or components of transformer-based language models.
970297a1860c904eaf39f77cb4324ecfad67fcfb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of instruct-tuned language models from the Gemma-2 and Gemma-3 families, ranging from 2B to 27B parameters. The CONCEPT500 dataset from AXBENCH will be adapted and augmented to provide paired training data for 500 concepts, with additional smaller datasets for larger models. Three types of intervention-based methods (SV, LoRA, LoReFT) will be trained using RePS, standard language modeling, and BiPO objectives. Evaluation will follow AXBENCH protocols, using unseen instructions and multiple metrics: concept incorporation, instruction adherence, and fluency, all scored by language model judges. Suppression experiments will measure the ability to prevent concept inclusion, including under adversarial prompt-based (jailbreaking) attacks. Baselines will include prompting, standard language modeling, and prior preference-based objectives. Extensive hyperparameter tuning will be performed for fair comparison, and ablation studies will assess the impact of factor sampling.
970297a1860c904eaf39f77cb4324ecfad67fcfb.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a reference-free, bi-directional preference optimization objective for intervention-based steering, enabling both concept incorporation and suppression without reliance on a reference model. The method is designed to be parameter-efficient, interpretable, and scalable to large language models. Incorporation of factor sampling during training is claimed to stabilize and improve intervention-based methods. The approach is positioned as a robust and interpretable alternative to prompting, narrowing the performance gap with prompt-based steering and demonstrating resilience to prompt-based jailbreaking attacks.

9716a2876d08fce9d8e5c5ba4d7b1a9af44806d6.title: Ignore Previous Prompt: Attack Techniques For Language Models
9716a2876d08fce9d8e5c5ba4d7b1a9af44806d6.research_question: How vulnerable are large language models (LLMs) to adversarial prompt injection attacks in real-world application settings, and what factors influence the effectiveness of such attacks?
9716a2876d08fce9d8e5c5ba4d7b1a9af44806d6.hypothesis: Transformer-based large language models are susceptible to prompt injection attacks, and the success of these attacks is influenced by prompt structure, attack strategies, and model parameters.
9716a2876d08fce9d8e5c5ba4d7b1a9af44806d6.proposed_method: A modular framework, PROMPTINJECT, will be developed to systematically compose and evaluate adversarial prompt injection scenarios against LLMs. The framework will allow for the construction of base prompts that mimic typical application instructions and the assembly of attack prompts using various strategies, such as goal hijacking and prompt leaking. Key variables, including the use of delimiters, rogue strings, temperature, sampling parameters, and prompt structure, will be manipulated to assess their impact on attack success. The method will include both handcrafted and parameterized attack prompts, and will support quantitative analysis of robustness through repeated trials and flexible matching criteria.
9716a2876d08fce9d8e5c5ba4d7b1a9af44806d6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a set of 35 base prompts sourced from publicly available OpenAI API examples, representing common application scenarios. The primary model under evaluation will be text-davinci-002, with additional experiments on other GPT-3 variants (text-ada-001, text-babbage-001, text-curie-001, text-davinci-001) for comparative analysis. Attack effectiveness will be measured by the percentage of successful goal hijacking (outputting a target string) and prompt leaking (revealing the original prompt), with each experiment repeated four times to account for model stochasticity. Evaluation metrics will include mean and standard deviation of attack success rates, and experiments will systematically vary attack prompt construction, delimiter usage, rogue string content, temperature, sampling, and model settings.
9716a2876d08fce9d8e5c5ba4d7b1a9af44806d6.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a systematic, modular framework for adversarial prompt injection evaluation tailored to production-like LLM application environments. It provides a detailed quantitative analysis of how various prompt and model factors affect vulnerability to prompt injection, identifies key variables that influence attack success, and demonstrates that even simple, handcrafted attacks can reliably misalign state-of-the-art LLMs. The work also highlights the inverse scaling phenomenon, where more capable models are paradoxically more susceptible to prompt injection, and offers practical insights for improving LLM application robustness.

971a8b1eebed7b73cdac896e3872dd8cbee04662.title: V3Det: Vast Vocabulary Visual Detection Dataset
971a8b1eebed7b73cdac896e3872dd8cbee04662.research_question: How can the development and evaluation of general visual object detection systems be advanced by constructing a large-scale dataset with a vastly expanded and hierarchically organized vocabulary of object categories, accompanied by high-quality annotations and rich category descriptions?
971a8b1eebed7b73cdac896e3872dd8cbee04662.hypothesis: A visual detection dataset with a vastly larger and more diverse vocabulary, organized hierarchically and annotated with high precision, will enable the training and evaluation of object detectors with improved generalization to both vast and open-vocabulary settings, leading to advances in general visual perception systems.
971a8b1eebed7b73cdac896e3872dd8cbee04662.proposed_method: A new visual detection dataset will be constructed featuring over 13,000 object categories, which is an order of magnitude larger than existing detection datasets. The dataset will be built by carefully selecting and curating categories from a large-scale classification dataset (e.g., Bamboo), supplemented with additional categories from web sources. Images will be selected and filtered using a region proposal network to ensure detection suitability and diversity. The annotation pipeline will employ a coarse-to-fine strategy, starting with coarse-grained bounding box annotations and proceeding through joint verification, fine-grained categorization (aided by CLIP-based feature ranking and human-in-the-loop search), and intra-category verification to ensure high annotation quality. Each category will be accompanied by expert-written and chatbot-generated descriptions, and the entire vocabulary will be organized into a hierarchical category tree to facilitate exploration of category relationships.
971a8b1eebed7b73cdac896e3872dd8cbee04662.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both close-set (vast vocabulary) and open-vocabulary object detection settings. The dataset will be split into training, validation, and test sets, ensuring each category is represented in the validation and test splits. Multiple state-of-the-art detection frameworks will be benchmarked, including two-stage, cascaded, single-stage, and transformer-based (DETR-style) detectors, with various backbones such as ResNet-50 and Swin-B. Evaluation metrics will follow the COCO protocol, reporting mean average precision (AP) at multiple IoU thresholds. Baseline comparisons will include existing datasets (COCO, LVIS, Objects365), and open-vocabulary methods will be evaluated both by direct inference and after training on the new dataset. Additional experiments will assess the impact of different data samplers, optimizers, classifier designs (e.g., Norm Linear Layer), and pretraining strategies. Hierarchical evaluation metrics will be introduced to assess the ability of detectors to leverage the category tree structure.
971a8b1eebed7b73cdac896e3872dd8cbee04662.novelty_claims: The proposed dataset will be the first object detection benchmark with over 10,000 categories, providing a vocabulary ten times larger than previous datasets. The hierarchical organization of categories and the inclusion of rich, expert- and chatbot-generated descriptions are novel features designed to support both vast and open-vocabulary detection. The annotation pipeline is designed for high accuracy and scalability, leveraging both human expertise and machine learning tools. The dataset is intended to serve as a cornerstone resource for advancing research in general and open-world object detection, enabling new insights, best practices, and improved evaluation of category generalization in detection models.

973814cd535facbf4f27c3de477b05bf19366030.title: ORPO: Monolithic Preference Optimization without Reference Model
973814cd535facbf4f27c3de477b05bf19366030.research_question: How can preference alignment in large language models be achieved efficiently and effectively without relying on a reference model or multi-stage training, while maintaining or surpassing state-of-the-art performance on alignment benchmarks?
973814cd535facbf4f27c3de477b05bf19366030.hypothesis: A monolithic preference optimization approach based on an odds ratio penalty, applied during supervised fine-tuning and without a reference model, can efficiently align language models to human preferences, outperforming or matching existing multi-stage or reference-based methods in both effectiveness and computational efficiency.
973814cd535facbf4f27c3de477b05bf19366030.proposed_method: A novel algorithm, Odds Ratio Preference Optimization (ORPO), is proposed for preference alignment of language models. ORPO integrates an odds ratio-based penalty directly into the conventional negative log-likelihood (NLL) loss during supervised fine-tuning, contrasting favored (chosen) and disfavored (rejected) responses for each input. The objective consists of two components: the standard supervised fine-tuning loss and a relative ratio loss that maximizes the log odds ratio between the likelihoods of favored and disfavored responses, wrapped in a log-sigmoid function and weighted by a hyperparameter λ. This approach eliminates the need for a separate reference model or an initial SFT warm-up phase, enabling single-stage, resource-efficient training. The method is theoretically motivated to avoid over-penalizing disfavored responses, as can occur with probability ratio-based objectives, and is designed to preserve domain adaptation while discouraging undesired generation styles.
973814cd535facbf4f27c3de477b05bf19366030.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by fine-tuning various language models, including OPT (125M to 1.3B), Phi-2 (2.7B), Llama-2 (7B), and Mistral (7B), using the ORPO method on pairwise preference datasets such as Anthropic’s HH-RLHF and Binarized UltraFeedback. Baselines for comparison include supervised fine-tuning (SFT), Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO/RLHF), and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), with all models evaluated using established benchmarks: AlpacaEval 1.0 and 2.0, MT-Bench, and IFEval. Evaluation metrics include win rates against baselines, leaderboard scores, and reward model assessments, using both automated (GPT-4, GPT-4-turbo) and reward model-based evaluations. Additional analyses will include lexical diversity and computational efficiency, with ablation studies on hyperparameters and theoretical justification for the odds ratio objective.
973814cd535facbf4f27c3de477b05bf19366030.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a reference model-free, monolithic preference optimization framework that unifies supervised fine-tuning and preference alignment in a single stage. ORPO is claimed to be the first to leverage an odds ratio penalty for preference alignment without requiring a separate reference model or multi-stage training. The approach is computationally more efficient, requiring fewer forward passes and less memory than RLHF or DPO. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate that ORPO achieves or surpasses state-of-the-art performance on alignment benchmarks with smaller or comparable model sizes, while theoretical analysis supports the stability and effectiveness of the odds ratio objective over probability ratio-based alternatives.

975a546b207b399fa5ef44952eefe48b97b200c2.title: Fast Vocabulary Transfer for Language Model Compression
975a546b207b399fa5ef44952eefe48b97b200c2.research_question: How can language models be effectively compressed to reduce model size and inference time while maintaining high performance across various domains and downstream tasks?
975a546b207b399fa5ef44952eefe48b97b200c2.hypothesis: Transferring and adapting the vocabulary of a pre-trained language model to the target domain, combined with efficient embedding initialization and integration with knowledge distillation, will significantly reduce model size and inference time with minimal impact on task performance.
975a546b207b399fa5ef44952eefe48b97b200c2.proposed_method: A new compression approach is developed that leverages Fast Vocabulary Transfer (FVT) to adapt the tokenizer and vocabulary of a pre-trained language model to the statistics of a target (in-domain) dataset. The method involves retraining a tokenizer on the in-domain corpus with reduced vocabulary sizes (e.g., 100%, 75%, 50%, 25% of the original size), then initializing the new embeddings by transferring information from the original model: if a token exists in both vocabularies, its embedding is directly inherited; otherwise, the embedding is computed as the average of the embeddings of its constituent tokens from the original vocabulary. After embedding initialization, the model is further adapted via masked language modeling (MLM) on in-domain data, followed by fine-tuning on downstream tasks. The approach is designed to be complementary to other compression techniques, such as knowledge distillation, and can be integrated with a two-stage distillation process to maximize compression benefits.
975a546b207b399fa5ef44952eefe48b97b200c2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the cased BERT model as the base language model, with tokenizers retrained on three heterogeneous datasets: ADE (medical), LEDGAR (legal), and CoNLL03 (news/NER). For each domain, tokenizers with varying vocabulary sizes (100%, 75%, 50%, 25% of the original) will be evaluated. Baselines will include models with the original vocabulary and models using Partial Vocabulary Transfer (PVT), where only overlapping tokens inherit embeddings. Evaluation metrics will focus on F1 score for downstream tasks, model size reduction, and inference speedup. Each configuration will be run multiple times with different random seeds, and masked language modeling will be performed for one epoch prior to fine-tuning. The impact of combining FVT with knowledge distillation (using a halved-layer student model and a triple-loss function) will also be assessed.
975a546b207b399fa5ef44952eefe48b97b200c2.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a lightweight and efficient vocabulary transfer technique specifically tailored for model compression, rather than just domain adaptation. The approach enables substantial reductions in model size and inference time by optimizing both the tokenizer and embedding layers, and demonstrates that vocabulary size can be treated as a hyperparameter for balancing compression and performance. The method is shown to be complementary to knowledge distillation and other compression techniques, providing an orthogonal axis for model optimization. Extensive experiments across multiple domains and tasks validate that the approach achieves significant compression and speedup with only marginal performance degradation, particularly in specialized domains.

9793e6f3883e5ce5dbb92c0b940df06021ece1ae.title: LION: Latent Point Diffusion Models for 3D Shape Generation
9793e6f3883e5ce5dbb92c0b940df06021ece1ae.research_question: How can a generative model for 3D shape synthesis be designed to achieve high-quality, flexible, and practically useful outputs, including smooth meshes, while supporting a range of applications such as conditional synthesis, shape interpolation, and multimodal denoising?
9793e6f3883e5ce5dbb92c0b940df06021ece1ae.hypothesis: A hierarchical variational autoencoder (VAE) framework with denoising diffusion models (DDMs) operating in a structured latent space, combining global shape and point-structured latents, will enable state-of-the-art 3D shape generation quality, flexibility for downstream tasks, and the ability to output smooth meshes suitable for digital artists.
9793e6f3883e5ce5dbb92c0b940df06021ece1ae.proposed_method: The proposed approach is a hierarchical Latent Point Diffusion Model (LION) for 3D shape generation. LION is structured as a VAE with a two-level latent space: a global shape latent vector and a point-structured latent representing smoothed point clouds with additional features. In the first stage, the model is trained as a VAE with standard Gaussian priors, using Point-Voxel CNNs (PVCNNs) for encoding and decoding, and optimizing a modified ELBO objective. In the second stage, two DDMs are trained in the latent spaces—one for the global shape latent and one conditional on the global latent for the point-structured latent—using score matching objectives. Generation proceeds by sampling from the hierarchical latent DDMs and decoding to the original point cloud space. The model can be further augmented with differentiable surface reconstruction techniques (e.g., Shape As Points) to produce smooth meshes from generated point clouds.
9793e6f3883e5ce5dbb92c0b940df06021ece1ae.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ShapeNet dataset, using both globally and per-shape normalized data, with primary focus on airplane, chair, and car categories, as well as many-class (13 and 55 categories) and small dataset settings (e.g., Mug, Bottle, TurboSquid animals). Baselines for comparison include PointFlow, ShapeGF, SetVAE, DPF-Net, DPM, PVD, IM-GAN, and others. Evaluation metrics will include 1-NNA with Chamfer Distance (CD) and Earth Mover Distance (EMD), as well as coverage (COV), minimum matching distance (MMD), and intersection-over-union (IOU) for voxel-guided synthesis. Experimental setups will include unconditional generation, voxel-guided and noise-guided synthesis, multimodal denoising, shape interpolation, and mesh reconstruction. Additional experiments will test encoder fine-tuning for conditional tasks, accelerated sampling (e.g., DDIM), and text- or image-driven generation via CLIP embeddings.
9793e6f3883e5ce5dbb92c0b940df06021ece1ae.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a hierarchical VAE with latent DDMs for 3D shape generation, combining the advantages of point cloud-based modeling with the expressivity of latent diffusion. It is the first to use both global and point-structured latents in a hierarchical manner for 3D DDMs, enabling flexible adaptation to conditional tasks without retraining the DDMs. The approach supports direct mesh reconstruction from generated point clouds, facilitating practical use by digital artists. The method demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on multiple ShapeNet benchmarks, scales to highly multimodal and diverse datasets without conditioning, and enables applications such as multimodal denoising, voxel-guided synthesis, and shape interpolation.

979f29a48c7b56235d0e3c4524b9c0cae1b9e71c.title: The best of both worlds: stochastic and adversarial episodic MDPs with unknown transition
979f29a48c7b56235d0e3c4524b9c0cae1b9e71c.research_question: Can an algorithm for learning in episodic Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) with unknown transitions achieve low regret in both adversarial and stochastic loss settings, thereby obtaining the 'best of both worlds' performance guarantees?
979f29a48c7b56235d0e3c4524b9c0cae1b9e71c.hypothesis: It is possible to design an algorithm for episodic MDPs with unknown transitions that achieves O(√T) regret in adversarial settings and O(polylog(T)) regret in (almost) stochastic settings, by leveraging a novel loss-shifting technique within the Follow-the-Regularized-Leader (FTRL) framework and carefully controlling transition estimation error.
979f29a48c7b56235d0e3c4524b9c0cae1b9e71c.proposed_method: A new algorithm will be developed for episodic MDPs with unknown transitions, utilizing the FTRL framework with specially designed regularizers. The approach introduces a novel loss-shifting technique in the FTRL analysis, which leverages a shifting function based on the advantage function (difference between Q-value and value function) to reduce variance and enable adaptive, self-bounding regret properties. For unknown transitions, the algorithm maintains an empirical transition model updated in a doubling-epoch schedule, and FTRL is performed over occupancy measures associated with the current empirical transition. Optimism is incorporated by adjusting the losses fed to FTRL with negative bonus terms based on confidence intervals, ensuring exploration and robustness. The analysis includes a new decomposition of regret that upper bounds the transition estimation error by a fraction of the regret itself plus polylogarithmic terms, crucial for achieving the desired regret guarantees.
979f29a48c7b56235d0e3c4524b9c0cae1b9e71c.experiment_details: The proposed algorithm will be evaluated on finite-horizon episodic MDPs with unknown transitions under both adversarial and stochastic loss generation processes. Experiments will include both full-information and bandit feedback settings. Regret will be measured against the optimal stationary policy in hindsight (adversarial) and the optimal policy in the stochastic world, using standard regret metrics. Baselines will include existing algorithms for adversarial MDPs, stochastic MDPs, and prior best-of-both-worlds methods for known transitions. The evaluation will consider various MDP sizes, horizon lengths, and levels of loss corruption, with performance compared in terms of regret scaling with T, S, A, and L.
979f29a48c7b56235d0e3c4524b9c0cae1b9e71c.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to achieve best-of-both-worlds regret guarantees—O(√T) in adversarial settings and O(polylog(T)) in (almost) stochastic settings—for episodic MDPs with unknown transitions. The introduction of a loss-shifting trick for FTRL in MDPs, a new framework for handling unknown transitions with optimistic loss adjustment, and a novel regret decomposition that tightly controls transition estimation error constitute significant innovations. The approach also simplifies and improves upon previous methods for the known transition case, and extends best-of-both-worlds guarantees to a broader class of MDP learning problems.

97a7968506a856ef25dfbbd48c13e57ab5a4b4b6.title: What is Essential for Unseen Goal Generalization of Offline Goal-conditioned RL?
97a7968506a856ef25dfbbd48c13e57ab5a4b4b6.research_question: How can offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning (GCRL) agents be trained to effectively generalize to out-of-distribution (OOD) or unseen goals, and what algorithmic components are essential for improving such generalization?
97a7968506a856ef25dfbbd48c13e57ab5a4b4b6.hypothesis: Weighted imitation learning, when combined with techniques such as advantage re-weighting, data selection, uncertainty-based sample re-weighting, and goal relabeling, will significantly improve the OOD generalization performance of offline GCRL agents compared to pessimism-based or standard behavioral cloning approaches.
97a7968506a856ef25dfbbd48c13e57ab5a4b4b6.proposed_method: A new offline GCRL framework, Generalizable Offline goAl-condiTioned RL (GOAT), will be developed by integrating several theoretically motivated techniques into a weighted imitation learning paradigm. The method will augment the offline dataset using hindsight goal relabeling, increasing the diversity of state-goal pairs. Weighted imitation learning will be performed with sample weights determined by a combination of uncertainty estimation (using the normalized standard deviation of an ensemble of value functions), exponential advantage weighting, and data selection based on advantage quantiles. Value functions will be estimated using an ensemble of networks and expectile regression to improve robustness and accuracy. The sample uncertainty weight will be normalized and clipped to prioritize samples likely to improve generalization, especially for hard or OOD goals.
97a7968506a856ef25dfbbd48c13e57ab5a4b4b6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a newly designed benchmark based on MuJoCo robotic manipulation environments, featuring 9 task groups and 26 evaluation tasks, including 17 OOD tasks where goals are not present in the training data. Offline datasets will be collected using a DDPG+HER agent, with both expert and non-expert trajectories. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as WGCSL, GoFAR, CQL+HER, GCSL, DDPG+HER, and MSG+HER. Evaluation will be based on average success rates across 200 randomly generated goals per task, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the contribution of each algorithmic component. Online fine-tuning experiments will also be conducted to evaluate the transferability of pre-trained policies to new goals.
97a7968506a856ef25dfbbd48c13e57ab5a4b4b6.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretically grounded framework for OOD generalization in offline GCRL, identifying and integrating key techniques—such as uncertainty-based sample re-weighting, ensemble-based value estimation, and advanced data selection—into a unified weighted imitation learning algorithm. A new benchmark for OOD goal generalization in offline GCRL is developed, enabling systematic evaluation. The approach claims to achieve state-of-the-art OOD generalization performance and provides detailed ablation analyses to isolate the impact of each component, offering new insights into the design of generalizable offline RL algorithms.

97b656520e6351c83128cb00337f8aedc97324dc.title: Optimal Dynamic Regret in Exp-Concave Online Learning
97b656520e6351c83128cb00337f8aedc97324dc.research_question: How can dynamic regret in online learning with exp-concave (and strongly convex) losses be minimized optimally, particularly in non-stationary environments where the comparator sequence may change over time and the path variation is unknown in advance?
97b656520e6351c83128cb00337f8aedc97324dc.hypothesis: Allowing improper learning and leveraging strongly adaptive online learning algorithms will enable minimax optimal dynamic regret rates (up to log factors) in online learning with exp-concave or strongly convex losses, as measured by the path variation of the comparator sequence.
97b656520e6351c83128cb00337f8aedc97324dc.proposed_method: A new approach is developed that utilizes Strongly Adaptive (SA) online learning algorithms, specifically the Follow-the-Leading-History (FLH) meta-algorithm, with appropriate base learners such as Follow-The-Leader (FTL) for squared loss and Online Newton Step (ONS) for exp-concave losses. The method partitions the time horizon into intervals based on the path variation of the comparator sequence, and within each interval, the SA algorithm controls static regret. The algorithm is improper, meaning predictions are allowed outside the comparator set, which is crucial for achieving optimal dynamic regret. The analysis leverages intricate primal-dual structures arising from the KKT conditions of the associated offline optimization problem, enabling tight regret bounds without requiring prior knowledge of the path variation parameter.
97b656520e6351c83128cb00337f8aedc97324dc.experiment_details: Experiments are proposed to evaluate the method on online learning tasks with exp-concave and strongly convex losses. The primary evaluation metric is dynamic regret, measured against comparator sequences with bounded total variation (pathlength). The method will be tested on both synthetic and real-world datasets, including the online Total Variation (TV) denoising problem and non-parametric regression tasks. Baselines for comparison include existing dynamic regret minimization algorithms such as Online Gradient Descent (OGD), meta-hedge algorithms, and other SA methods. The evaluation will consider various settings for the dimension, horizon length, and path variation, and will compare both upper and lower bounds to establish minimax optimality.
97b656520e6351c83128cb00337f8aedc97324dc.novelty_claims: The proposed method achieves the first minimax optimal (up to log factors) dynamic regret rates of O~(n^{1/3} C_n^{2/3} ∨ 1) for exp-concave and strongly convex losses in the improper learning setting, closing the gap between known lower and upper bounds. The approach is adaptive to the unknown path variation of the comparator sequence, does not require hyperparameter tuning, and provides strong oracle inequalities even in fully agnostic, non-stochastic settings. The proof techniques introduce novel use of KKT structures for regret analysis, which may be of independent interest. The method also extends minimax optimality to a broad class of non-parametric regression problems, including TV, Sobolev, and Holder classes, in both online and offline settings.

97b6f4357d1e3ab40a7ee60acb5260a948e3641d.title: Hybrid LLM: Cost-Efficient and Quality-Aware Query Routing
97b6f4357d1e3ab40a7ee60acb5260a948e3641d.research_question: How can queries be dynamically routed between large and small language models to optimize inference cost while maintaining high response quality across diverse natural language processing tasks?
97b6f4357d1e3ab40a7ee60acb5260a948e3641d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a learned query router can effectively assign 'easy' queries to a smaller, less expensive language model and 'hard' queries to a larger, more powerful model, thereby reducing overall inference cost without significant loss in response quality. Incorporating uncertainty and data transformation into the router's training will further improve routing effectiveness, especially when there is a large performance gap between models.
97b6f4357d1e3ab40a7ee60acb5260a948e3641d.proposed_method: A hybrid inference framework will be developed that integrates a router model to assign incoming queries to either a large or small language model based on predicted query difficulty and desired response quality. The router will be implemented as a BERT-style encoder (e.g., DeBERTa-v3-large) trained on a dataset of representative queries, using a score that estimates the probability the small model's response quality matches or exceeds that of the large model. Three routing strategies will be explored: (1) a deterministic router using hard labels based on single-sample response quality comparisons, (2) a probabilistic router using soft labels derived from multiple sampled responses to capture LLM output randomness, and (3) a probabilistic router with data transformation, where the definition of 'easy' queries is relaxed by introducing a tunable quality gap threshold, optimized via grid search. The router's threshold can be dynamically adjusted at test time to trade off between cost and quality as required.
97b6f4357d1e3ab40a7ee60acb5260a948e3641d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the MixInstruct dataset, a large-scale benchmark containing real-world instructions spanning tasks such as question answering, summarization, and information extraction. Model pairs will include FLAN-T5 (800m, 11b), Llama-2 (7b, 13b), and GPT-3.5-turbo, with 10,000 training queries and 5,000 validation/test queries. For each query, 10 responses will be generated from each model to estimate response quality distributions. Baselines will include routing all queries to the large model, all to the small model, and random assignment. Evaluation metrics will be BART score for response quality and the fraction of queries routed to the small model (cost advantage). The router will be trained for 5 epochs, with the best checkpoint selected via validation performance, and experiments will be run on NVIDIA A100 GPUs. Additional analyses will assess router overhead, threshold selection, generalizability across model pairs, and robustness to alternative quality metrics.
97b6f4357d1e3ab40a7ee60acb5260a948e3641d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to address cost-effective and quality-aware hybrid inference for large language models by learning to route queries based on predicted response quality gaps. Innovations include the design of a query router that incorporates uncertainty from LLM response randomness, a novel data transformation technique for improving router training in scenarios with large model performance gaps, and the ability to dynamically tune the quality-cost tradeoff at inference time. The framework ensures each query is handled by only one model, minimizing computational overhead compared to ensemble or cascade approaches, and demonstrates superior cost-quality tradeoffs over baseline routing strategies.

97cea53d979305e6686387ff0ee38a15e3a5ba46.title: Rigorously Assessing Natural Language Explanations of Neurons
97cea53d979305e6686387ff0ee38a15e3a5ba46.research_question: How can the faithfulness of natural language explanations for individual neurons in large language models be rigorously evaluated, and to what extent do such explanations accurately reflect both the encoding and causal mediation of linguistic concepts within neural activations?
97cea53d979305e6686387ff0ee38a15e3a5ba46.hypothesis: Natural language explanations of individual neurons in large language models are not reliably faithful to the actual neural activations and do not generally correspond to causal mediators of the concepts they purport to explain.
97cea53d979305e6686387ff0ee38a15e3a5ba46.proposed_method: A two-pronged evaluation framework will be developed for assessing natural language explanations of neurons. The first component, observational evaluation, will test whether a neuron's activation aligns with the set of input strings denoted by a proposed explanation, quantifying precision, recall, and F1-score over curated datasets. The second component, intervention-based evaluation, will use causal mediation analysis via interchange interventions: neuron activations will be manipulated during model inference to determine if such interventions causally affect model outputs in tasks dependent on the explained concept. Both single neuron and multi-neuron (probe-based) settings will be considered, and the evaluation will be applied to explanations generated by large language models (e.g., GPT-4) for neurons in a pretrained language model such as GPT-2 XL.
97cea53d979305e6686387ff0ee38a15e3a5ba46.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a subset of neurons from GPT-2 XL, focusing on those with high-confidence natural language explanations generated by GPT-4. For observational evaluation, datasets will be constructed by sampling sentences containing strings that should or should not trigger neuron activations according to the explanation, using both automated (GPT-3.5) and manual methods to ensure data quality. Precision, recall, and F1-score will be computed for each explanation, with baselines including random explanations and learned probes. For intervention-based evaluation, tasks such as unit conversion, verb tense prediction, and capital retrieval will be designed, and neuron activations will be intervened upon at relevant positions and layers. The causal impact of these interventions will be measured using Interchange Intervention Accuracy (IIA) and compared against random and token-activation correlation baselines. Evaluation will systematically vary the number of neurons intervened upon and analyze both individual and grouped neuron effects.
97cea53d979305e6686387ff0ee38a15e3a5ba46.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a rigorous, dual-mode evaluation for natural language explanations of neurons, combining direct observational testing with causal intervention analysis. This approach goes beyond previous neuron-level metrics by explicitly quantifying both faithfulness to neuron activations and causal efficacy in model behavior. The methodology also highlights inherent limitations of natural language as an explanatory medium and questions the appropriateness of individual neurons as the primary unit of interpretability, offering critical insights for the development of more robust and actionable model explanations.

9803d83bbb28d02fb01f00e0e05aa3c192a87255.title: MInference 1.0: Accelerating Pre-filling for Long-Context LLMs via Dynamic Sparse Attention
9803d83bbb28d02fb01f00e0e05aa3c192a87255.research_question: How can the pre-filling stage of long-context large language model (LLM) inference be accelerated without sacrificing accuracy, particularly as prompt lengths scale to hundreds of thousands or millions of tokens?
9803d83bbb28d02fb01f00e0e05aa3c192a87255.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging dynamically identified sparse attention patterns—specifically, A-shape, Vertical-Slash, and Block-Sparse—at the attention head level, and applying efficient GPU-optimized sparse computation, can significantly reduce pre-filling latency in long-context LLMs while maintaining or improving accuracy compared to dense attention or static sparse baselines.
9803d83bbb28d02fb01f00e0e05aa3c192a87255.proposed_method: A novel method is proposed that first conducts an offline analysis to categorize each attention head in a given LLM into one of three sparse attention patterns: A-shape, Vertical-Slash, or Block-Sparse. For each head, a kernel-aware optimal sparse pattern search is performed to select the most efficient pattern and its hyperparameters under a fixed FLOPs budget, using recall of attention output as the selection criterion. During inference, dynamic sparse masks are constructed online for each head and input, using fast approximations: for Vertical-Slash heads, the last few query and key vectors are used to estimate important indices; for Block-Sparse heads, mean pooling is applied to queries and keys to identify salient blocks. These dynamic masks are then used to perform sparse attention calculations with custom GPU kernels optimized for each pattern, leveraging frameworks such as Triton, FlashAttention, and PIT. The approach is designed to be plug-and-play for existing LLMs, requiring no changes to pre-training or fine-tuning.
9803d83bbb28d02fb01f00e0e05aa3c192a87255.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several state-of-the-art long-context LLMs, including LLaMA-3-8B, GLM-4-9B, Yi-9B-200K, Phi-3-Mini-128K, and Qwen2-7B-128K, with context windows up to 1 million tokens. Evaluation will span diverse benchmarks: InfiniteBench (covering retrieval, QA, coding, summarization, and more), RULER (multi-hop and aggregation tasks), Needle In A Haystack (retrieval at various context positions), and PG-19 (long-context language modeling). Baseline comparisons will include StreamingLLM (A-shape), StreamingLLM with dilated/strided patterns, InfLLM, and static sparse variants. Key metrics will include task-specific accuracy, retrieval recall, perplexity (for language modeling), and pre-filling latency measured on a single Nvidia A100 GPU. Ablation studies will isolate the impact of each pattern and static vs. dynamic masking. Integration with KV cache compression (e.g., SnapKV) and scaling to larger models (e.g., LLaMA-3-70B) will also be tested.
9803d83bbb28d02fb01f00e0e05aa3c192a87255.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a dynamic, pattern-based sparse attention framework that adaptively assigns optimal sparse patterns to each attention head and constructs input-dependent sparse masks in real time, enabling efficient GPU computation. Unlike prior static or low-rank dynamic sparse approaches, this method achieves high recall of attention scores with minimal estimation overhead, is directly applicable to existing LLMs without retraining, and supports extremely long context windows. The approach demonstrates up to 10× speedup in pre-filling latency for million-token prompts while maintaining or surpassing full attention accuracy, and is compatible with other inference optimizations such as KV cache compression.

980b07368e08932b8d3e089c7509039cb30edce6.title: DreamWaQ: Learning Robust Quadrupedal Locomotion With Implicit Terrain Imagination via Deep Reinforcement Learning
980b07368e08932b8d3e089c7509039cb30edce6.research_question: How can quadrupedal robots achieve robust and adaptive locomotion across diverse and unstructured terrains using only proprioceptive sensing, without reliance on exteroceptive sensors such as cameras or LiDAR?
980b07368e08932b8d3e089c7509039cb30edce6.hypothesis: A deep reinforcement learning-based framework that leverages implicit terrain imagination and context-aided state estimation, using only proprioceptive data, can enable quadrupedal robots to robustly traverse challenging and unstructured terrains, achieving performance comparable to methods with exteroceptive sensing.
980b07368e08932b8d3e089c7509039cb30edce6.proposed_method: A novel locomotion learning framework, DreamWaQ, is developed for quadrupedal robots, utilizing an asymmetric actor-critic architecture where the policy (actor) receives only temporal partial proprioceptive observations, while the value network (critic) is provided with privileged information including terrain height maps and disturbance forces during training. The policy network is augmented with a context-aided estimator network (CENet), which jointly estimates body state and latent environmental context from proprioceptive inputs using a shared encoder and a multi-head decoder, trained as a β-variational autoencoder. The action space is defined as desired joint angles tracked by a PD controller. An adaptive bootstrapping (AdaBoot) mechanism is introduced to dynamically adjust the use of estimator outputs during policy training, based on the coefficient of variation of episodic rewards, enhancing robustness to estimation noise. The reward function integrates task objectives, stability, energy efficiency, and a novel power distribution penalty to prevent motor overheating, and curriculum learning is employed to progressively increase terrain difficulty.
980b07368e08932b8d3e089c7509039cb30edce6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in both high-fidelity simulation (Isaac Gym) and real-world outdoor environments using a Unitree A1 quadrupedal robot. In simulation, 4,096 agents will be trained in parallel with extensive domain randomization over physical and environmental parameters, and curriculum learning will expose agents to increasingly challenging terrains (smooth, rough, discretized, stairs) with varying inclinations. Baseline comparisons will include standard RL policies, implicit adaptation networks, explicit estimator networks, and oracle policies with privileged terrain information. Evaluation metrics will include command tracking accuracy (absolute tracking error), robustness to external disturbances (maximum push velocity, survival rate), and estimation error of body state. Real-world tests will involve long-distance walking over natural and man-made terrains, including stairs, slopes, mud, and vegetation, with trajectory tracking via RTK-GPS and qualitative analysis of gait adaptation and recovery from slips or stumbles.
980b07368e08932b8d3e089c7509039cb30edce6.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces implicit terrain imagination for robust locomotion using only proprioception, eliminating dependence on exteroceptive sensors. The context-aided estimator network (CENet) jointly learns body state and environmental context, improving estimation accuracy and policy robustness. The adaptive bootstrapping (AdaBoot) method dynamically tunes estimator usage during training for enhanced sim-to-real transfer. A power distribution reward is introduced to address long-term hardware durability. To the best of current knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a small-scale quadrupedal robot (Unitree A1) achieving sustained, robust locomotion over diverse, challenging outdoor terrains, including stairs and hills, using only proprioceptive feedback.

98195ca598d685111ab93f7d4771381b015f0b71.title: From Information to Generative Exponent: Learning Rate Induces Phase Transitions in SGD
98195ca598d685111ab93f7d4771381b015f0b71.research_question: How does the choice of learning rate in gradient-based algorithms affect the sample complexity and phase transitions in learning single-index models with neural networks, and can new algorithmic strategies leveraging learning rate scaling achieve improved statistical and computational efficiency?
98195ca598d685111ab93f7d4771381b015f0b71.hypothesis: The learning rate, particularly when used to scale non-correlational update terms in gradient-based algorithms, induces phase transitions in sample complexity, allowing transitions from regimes governed by the information exponent to those determined by the generative exponent. Properly tuning learning rates can thus enable more efficient learning than traditional correlational updates alone.
98195ca598d685111ab93f7d4771381b015f0b71.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and algorithmic framework will be developed to analyze the impact of learning rate scaling on the sample complexity of online iterative gradient-based algorithms for learning single-index models. The approach will generalize standard online SGD by introducing update rules that combine correlational and non-correlational terms, each modulated by distinct learning rates. The method will include (1) a detailed learning-rate-dependent analysis of sample complexity, (2) instantiation of the framework for both batch reuse SGD (multiple gradient steps on the same sample) and a novel layer-wise alternating SGD algorithm employing two-timescale learning rates, and (3) extension to deeper, sparsely connected neural networks. Theoretical results will be derived using Hermite expansions of the link function, with explicit characterization of phase transitions in sample complexity as a function of learning rate hyperparameters.
98195ca598d685111ab93f7d4771381b015f0b71.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic datasets generated from Gaussian single-index models, where the label is a nonlinear function of a latent one-dimensional projection of the input. The proposed algorithms will be compared against baseline methods such as vanilla online SGD and batch reuse SGD, with variations in learning rate hyperparameters to empirically observe phase transitions in sample complexity. Evaluation metrics will include the number of samples required to achieve weak recovery (alignment with the ground truth direction) and test error rates. Key experimental setups will involve varying the learning rate for non-correlational update terms, analyzing the effect on convergence rates, and extending experiments to networks with multiple layers to validate theoretical predictions.
98195ca598d685111ab93f7d4771381b015f0b71.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified theoretical framework that explicitly characterizes learning-rate-induced phase transitions in the sample complexity of gradient-based learning of single-index models. It demonstrates that the learning rate is as crucial as the algorithmic structure in determining statistical and computational efficiency, and presents a novel alternating SGD algorithm that leverages two-timescale learning rates to break correlational statistical query limitations without sample reuse or loss modification. The approach generalizes and interpolates between existing methods, extends to deeper networks, and provides new insights into the interplay between optimization dynamics and statistical query complexity.

98280abfb6cd5cc626f0fdb52c1f41dad46a0634.title: SCOUT: Teaching Pre-trained Language Models to Enhance Reasoning via Flow Chain-of-Thought
98280abfb6cd5cc626f0fdb52c1f41dad46a0634.research_question: How can pre-trained large language models be enhanced to perform more effective, scalable, and cognitively grounded multi-step reasoning without relying on explicit step-by-step supervision or costly pretraining?
98280abfb6cd5cc626f0fdb52c1f41dad46a0634.hypothesis: Progressive, iteration-specific supervision using capacity-matched teacher models, combined with a lightweight retrospective integration mechanism, enables pre-trained language models to develop deeper, more coherent multi-step reasoning abilities through fine-tuning alone.
98280abfb6cd5cc626f0fdb52c1f41dad46a0634.proposed_method: A novel fine-tuning framework, SCOUT (Stepwise Cognitive Optimization Using Teachers), is developed to instill Flow Chain-of-Thought (FlowCoT) reasoning in pre-trained LLMs. The method decomposes the model into a head block for initial encoding, a recursive block for iterative latent state refinement, and a tail block for output decoding. At each reasoning step, the model's latent state is supervised via progressive distillation, aligning each iteration with a teacher model of matching capacity—smaller teachers for early steps and stronger teachers for later steps. A retrospective reasoning module based on cross-attention is introduced, allowing each iteration to selectively integrate information from previous latent states while maintaining grounding in the original input. Training is performed via end-to-end backpropagation across all reasoning steps, with per-step losses weighted and aggregated.
98280abfb6cd5cc626f0fdb52c1f41dad46a0634.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using the Qwen2.5-0.5B model as the student, with Qwen2.5-1.5B, 3B, and 7B as teacher models for progressive distillation across three reasoning iterations. Fine-tuning is performed for two epochs with a learning rate of 2×10⁻⁵ on a composite instruction-following dataset that includes AlpacaGPT4, AlpacaCoT, WikiQA, CodeAlpaca, and MathInstruct, covering general instruction, chain-of-thought, open-domain QA, code generation, and mathematical reasoning. Evaluation is carried out using the lm-evaluation-harness framework on eight benchmarks spanning commonsense QA (ARC-easy, ARC-challenge, OpenBookQA, TruthfulQA), multi-step reasoning (GSM8K, MMLU), reading comprehension/dialogue (CoQA, GLUE), and code generation (MBPP). Baselines include standard supervised fine-tuning, distilled fine-tuning, recursive supervision with hard labels, recursive distillation with uniform and weighted loss, and a reversed teacher order control. Metrics focus on accuracy and explanation quality, with ablations for retrospective integration strategies.
98280abfb6cd5cc626f0fdb52c1f41dad46a0634.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces Flow Chain-of-Thought (FlowCoT), a cognitively motivated paradigm for recursive reasoning that models each iteration as a distinct cognitive stage. SCOUT is claimed to be the first lightweight fine-tuning framework that enables FlowCoT-style multi-step reasoning in pre-trained LLMs without additional pretraining or explicit intermediate supervision. Progressive distillation with capacity-matched teachers and a cross-attention-based retrospective module are novel contributions that support step-wise cognitive refinement and coherent integration of prior reasoning. The approach is fully compatible with existing LLM architectures and fine-tuning pipelines, and demonstrates consistent improvements in both accuracy and explanation quality across diverse reasoning benchmarks.

983985c18aee527121d6e9957ae6da3c7351389f.title: Learning Task-Agnostic Representations through Multi-Teacher Distillation
983985c18aee527121d6e9957ae6da3c7351389f.research_question: How can knowledge from multiple large embedding models be effectively distilled and integrated into a smaller model to produce a general-purpose representation that is highly informative and broadly applicable across a wide range of downstream tasks, without dependence on task-specific labels or prior knowledge?
