983985c18aee527121d6e9957ae6da3c7351389f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a task-agnostic multi-teacher distillation framework, which maximizes the mutual information between student and teacher embeddings using a majority-vote inspired objective and a conditional entropy-based loss, can produce student representations that retain maximal utility and generalizability for diverse downstream tasks.
983985c18aee527121d6e9957ae6da3c7351389f.proposed_method: A novel task-agnostic multi-teacher distillation framework is proposed, where a student embedder is trained to align its representations with those of an ensemble of diverse teacher models. The core of the method is an information-theoretic loss based on minimizing the conditional entropy of the teachers' embeddings given the student's embedding, which is estimated using differentiable high-dimensional Gaussian mixture models. The student is optimized end-to-end by minimizing the negative log-likelihood of the teachers' outputs conditioned on the student's predictions, with both the student and the Gaussian kernel parameters updated during training. This approach ensures that the student representation captures as much information as possible from all teachers, independent of any specific downstream task, and is theoretically bounded by the mutual information between student and teacher embeddings. The method is designed to be scalable to multiple teachers and applicable across different modalities, including text, vision, and molecular data.
983985c18aee527121d6e9957ae6da3c7351389f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across three modalities: natural language processing, molecular modeling, and computer vision. For NLP, several large open-source embedding models (ranging from 433M to 7B parameters) will serve as teachers, and smaller student models (20M–335M parameters) will be trained and evaluated using the MTEB benchmark, which includes 33 tasks spanning classification, clustering, and sentence similarity. In molecular modeling, eight teacher models representing different modalities (text, graph, 3D) will be distilled into a student GNN, with evaluation on the TDC ADMET and HIV datasets for both regression and classification tasks. For vision, large Vision Transformer-based teachers (e.g., Swin, DINOv2, ViT, BEiT) and CNN baselines will be used, with a smaller PVTv2 student evaluated on fine-grained datasets such as DTD, FGVCAircraft, CUB, CIFAR10, SVHN, and STL10. Baselines will include standard multi-teacher feature distillation methods such as MSE (SimReg), cosine similarity, and CompRess. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, average rank, and information density, with model performance compared to both teacher and baseline student models. Computational overhead and scalability with respect to the number of teachers will also be assessed.
983985c18aee527121d6e9957ae6da3c7351389f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a theoretically grounded, task-agnostic multi-teacher distillation framework that leverages a conditional entropy-based loss, estimated via high-dimensional Gaussian mixtures, to maximize mutual information between student and teacher embeddings. Unlike prior methods, this framework does not require task-specific labels, prior knowledge, or architectural constraints between student and teachers, and it generalizes to unseen tasks and modalities. The method provides a tractable and scalable solution for distilling diverse knowledge into compact, general-purpose representations, and demonstrates superior or competitive performance compared to existing distillation baselines across multiple domains and tasks.

98478ac589e5b40a20630ff54bb4eec4ab4c5f6b.title: GAIA-1: A Generative World Model for Autonomous Driving
98478ac589e5b40a20630ff54bb4eec4ab4c5f6b.research_question: How can a generative world model be developed to realistically simulate and predict complex, multimodal urban driving scenarios, enabling fine-grained control over both ego-vehicle behavior and scene features for the advancement of autonomous driving systems?
98478ac589e5b40a20630ff54bb4eec4ab4c5f6b.hypothesis: A large-scale, multimodal generative world model that integrates video, text, and action inputs, and leverages discrete tokenization and diffusion-based decoding, can learn high-level scene dynamics and generate realistic, controllable driving scenarios, thereby improving future event prediction and supporting the training and validation of autonomous driving technologies.
98478ac589e5b40a20630ff54bb4eec4ab4c5f6b.proposed_method: The proposed approach involves constructing a generative world model, GAIA-1, which encodes video, text, and action modalities into a shared token-based representation. Images are discretized using a pre-trained image tokenizer guided by semantic distillation from a DINO model, resulting in compact, semantically meaningful tokens. Text is encoded using a pre-trained T5-large model, and actions (speed and curvature) are mapped into the same embedding space. These tokens are interleaved and fed into an autoregressive transformer-based world model, which predicts the next image token conditioned on past tokens, enabling both unconditional and conditioned (action/text) generation. A multi-task video diffusion decoder reconstructs high-resolution, temporally consistent videos from the predicted tokens, supporting tasks such as video generation, temporal upsampling, and interpolation. The entire system is trained on large-scale, real-world driving data with balanced sampling across geographic, weather, and behavioral features.
98478ac589e5b40a20630ff54bb4eec4ab4c5f6b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a proprietary dataset comprising 4,700 hours (approximately 420 million images) of urban driving in London, UK, collected between 2019 and 2023. The dataset is balanced across latitude, longitude, weather conditions, and driving behaviors to ensure diverse scenario coverage. Validation is performed on a separate 400-hour dataset, including both seen and unseen geofenced routes to assess generalization. Baselines for comparison include existing world models and generative video models, with evaluation metrics encompassing video realism, semantic fidelity, temporal consistency, and controllability via action and text prompts. The experimental setup includes ablation studies on tokenization strategies, conditioning modalities, and guidance schedules, as well as quantitative and qualitative analysis of generated scenarios.
98478ac589e5b40a20630ff54bb4eec4ab4c5f6b.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a scalable, multimodal generative world model that unifies discrete token-based autoregressive modeling with high-fidelity video diffusion decoding, enabling fine-grained control over both vehicle behavior and scene attributes through action and language. Key innovations include the use of DINO-distilled semantic image tokenization, multi-task video diffusion decoding for temporal consistency, and classifier-free guidance for prompt alignment. The approach demonstrates emergent properties such as contextual awareness, generalization to unseen scenarios, and understanding of 3D geometry, representing a significant advancement in the generation and prediction of complex, realistic driving environments for autonomous systems.

984f00eb0fa62a91d9b4168190218d85eaaa9ae1.title: DORO: Distributional and Outlier Robust Optimization
984f00eb0fa62a91d9b4168190218d85eaaa9ae1.research_question: How can machine learning models be made robust to both subpopulation shift and the presence of outliers in training data, particularly in large-scale, real-world datasets where subpopulation membership is unknown?
984f00eb0fa62a91d9b4168190218d85eaaa9ae1.hypothesis: A refined distributionally robust optimization framework that explicitly accounts for outliers during training will improve both the performance and stability of models under subpopulation shift compared to standard DRO approaches.
984f00eb0fa62a91d9b4168190218d85eaaa9ae1.proposed_method: A novel framework, Distributional and Outlier Robust Optimization (DORO), will be developed to address the sensitivity of standard Distributionally Robust Optimization (DRO) methods to outliers. DORO introduces a refined risk function that adaptively filters out a small fraction of high-loss data points, which are likely to be outliers, during training. The approach will be instantiated for the Cressie-Read family of Rényi divergences, focusing on two specific cases: CVaR-DORO and χ2-DORO. The method involves ordering training instances by loss, identifying and excluding the top-ε fraction as potential outliers, and minimizing the DRO risk over the remaining data. Optimization will be performed using gradient-based methods, with hyperparameters controlling the outlier fraction and risk aversion.
984f00eb0fa62a91d9b4168190218d85eaaa9ae1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three large-scale, real-world datasets: COMPAS (tabular, recidivism prediction), CelebA (vision, facial attribute classification), and CivilComments-Wilds (language, toxicity detection). For each dataset, models will be trained using ERM, standard DRO (CVaR and χ2), and the proposed DORO variants. Baselines will include ERM and standard DRO methods. Evaluation will focus on both average and worst-case accuracies across predefined demographic subpopulations, using metrics such as test accuracy and stability (standard deviation across epochs). Model selection will be performed using worst-case validation accuracy with access to domain labels. Hyperparameter sweeps for α (risk level) and ε (outlier fraction) will be conducted to assess sensitivity and optimal settings.
984f00eb0fa62a91d9b4168190218d85eaaa9ae1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to directly address the instability and poor performance of DRO under outlier contamination in large-scale, real-world settings. DORO introduces a theoretically grounded, outlier-robust refinement to DRO, with formal guarantees on worst-case risk and optimality gaps. The framework is broadly applicable to the Cressie-Read family of divergences and demonstrates improved empirical performance and stability over standard DRO methods. The work provides both theoretical analysis and extensive empirical validation, answering an open question regarding the simultaneous achievement of fairness to latent subpopulations and robustness to outliers.

985f0c89c5a607742ec43c1fdc2cbfe54541cbad.title: Language Model Beats Diffusion -- Tokenizer is Key to Visual Generation
985f0c89c5a607742ec43c1fdc2cbfe54541cbad.research_question: Can improved visual tokenization methods enable large language models to achieve state-of-the-art performance in visual generation tasks, such as image and video generation, video compression, and video understanding, surpassing diffusion models when provided with comparable training data and resources?
985f0c89c5a607742ec43c1fdc2cbfe54541cbad.hypothesis: A visual tokenizer that produces concise and expressive discrete tokens, particularly using a lookup-free quantization approach and architectural enhancements, will enable large language models to outperform diffusion models in visual generation tasks and provide competitive results in video compression and action recognition.
985f0c89c5a607742ec43c1fdc2cbfe54541cbad.proposed_method: A new video tokenizer, MAGVIT-v2, will be developed to map images and videos into compact discrete tokens suitable for language models. The core innovation is a lookup-free quantization (LFQ) method, which eliminates the need for embedding lookups by representing tokens as independent binary dimensions, allowing for a much larger vocabulary size without degrading language model generation quality. The tokenizer architecture will be enhanced with causal 3D CNN layers, strided convolutional downsamplers, depth-to-space upsamplers, deferred temporal downsampling, 3D blurpooling in the discriminator, and adaptive group normalization in the decoder. The tokenizer will be designed to jointly handle both images and videos using a shared vocabulary, and token factorization will be employed to facilitate efficient prediction in large vocabularies by language models.
985f0c89c5a607742ec43c1fdc2cbfe54541cbad.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard benchmarks: ImageNet for image generation, Kinetics-600 and UCF-101 for video generation, MCL-JCV for video compression, and Kinetics-400 and SSv2 for video understanding. The proposed tokenizer will be evaluated in conjunction with masked language models (MLMs) and compared to state-of-the-art diffusion models and previous tokenization approaches such as MAGVIT and VQGAN. Evaluation metrics will include FID and Inception Score for image generation, FVD for video generation, LPIPS, PSNR, and MS-SSIM for video compression, and classification accuracy for action recognition. Subjective user studies (Elo rating) will be used to assess video compression quality, and ablation studies will verify the impact of key architectural choices.
985f0c89c5a607742ec43c1fdc2cbfe54541cbad.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first video tokenizer that enables language models to outperform diffusion models on the ImageNet benchmark under equal training conditions. The lookup-free quantization method allows for effective modeling with a much larger vocabulary, improving both reconstruction and generation quality. MAGVIT-v2 achieves state-of-the-art results in visual generation, surpasses standard codecs (HEVC, VVC) in user-rated video compression quality, and provides stronger representations for video understanding tasks. The tokenizer is the first to jointly tokenize images and videos with a shared vocabulary and demonstrates that advanced visual tokenization is key to unlocking the full generative potential of large language models in the visual domain.

98755a7ca75afbb29a19f8129b9f25796ad0e0b7.title: Language models scale reliably with over-training and on downstream tasks
98755a7ca75afbb29a19f8129b9f25796ad0e0b7.research_question: Can scaling laws be reliably extended to predict the performance of language models that are over-trained and to forecast their downstream task accuracy, using only small-scale experiments?
98755a7ca75afbb29a19f8129b9f25796ad0e0b7.hypothesis: Scaling laws, when appropriately parameterized to account for over-training and model size, can accurately extrapolate both validation loss and downstream task performance of large language models from small-scale training runs.
98755a7ca75afbb29a19f8129b9f25796ad0e0b7.proposed_method: A comprehensive scaling testbed will be constructed by training 104 transformer-based language models, ranging from 0.011B to 6.9B parameters, on three large-scale datasets (C4, RedPajama, and RefinedWeb) with varying token multipliers (ratio of training tokens to parameters) to simulate both compute-optimal and over-trained regimes. Two scaling laws will be developed: one for validation loss as a function of compute and over-training (parameterized by token multiplier), and another for downstream top-1 error as a function of validation loss, formalized as a power law. The methodology involves fitting these laws using small-scale models and then extrapolating to predict the performance of much larger, more expensive models. Curve fitting (e.g., Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm) will be used to estimate the parameters of these laws, and predictions will be chained to forecast downstream error from compute and over-training settings.
98755a7ca75afbb29a19f8129b9f25796ad0e0b7.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training transformer models (GPT-2/LLaMA-like architectures, tokenized with GPT-NeoX) on the C4, RedPajama, and RefinedWeb datasets, with model sizes from 0.011B to 6.9B parameters and token multipliers ranging from 5 to 640. A grid search over hyperparameters will be performed for small models, and models on the Pareto frontier will be selected for scaling law fitting. Validation loss will be measured on the C4 eval set, while downstream performance will be evaluated on a 17-task subset from LLM-Foundry, including tasks such as ARC-Easy, BIG-bench, BoolQ, Commonsense QA, and others. Evaluation metrics will include cross-entropy loss, average top-1 error across tasks, and relative prediction error. The accuracy of scaling law predictions will be assessed for both interpolation and extrapolation to larger models and higher token multipliers, using significantly less compute than required for direct training of large models.
98755a7ca75afbb29a19f8129b9f25796ad0e0b7.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a unified framework for reliable scaling law extrapolation in both over-trained and compute-optimal regimes, enabling accurate prediction of large model performance from small-scale experiments. It formalizes a new power law relationship between validation loss and downstream task error, allowing for direct prediction of benchmark accuracy from language modeling perplexity. The approach demonstrates that average downstream performance can be forecasted with high accuracy using orders of magnitude less compute, and provides a comprehensive empirical testbed across multiple datasets and training regimes to validate these claims.

9898bbde43fa16e5e1b67d5ab651529a5915eb91.title: MuRating: A High Quality Data Selecting Approach to Multilingual Large Language Model Pretraining
9898bbde43fa16e5e1b67d5ab651529a5915eb91.research_question: How can high-quality data selection for pretraining large language models be effectively extended to multilingual settings, ensuring robust and consistent quality assessment across a diverse set of languages?
9898bbde43fa16e5e1b67d5ab651529a5915eb91.hypothesis: Transferring unified English data-quality signals via translation and pairwise preference modeling will enable the construction of a scalable, language-agnostic data quality rater that improves multilingual LLM pretraining outcomes compared to existing selection methods.
9898bbde43fa16e5e1b67d5ab651529a5915eb91.proposed_method: A two-stage framework is proposed for multilingual data quality estimation. First, multiple English data quality raters are consolidated using a pairwise comparison approach, employing the Bradley–Terry model to learn a unified scalar quality score for each document based on aggregated preferences. Second, these English-anchored pairwise judgments are projected into 17 target languages through translation, creating monolingual, cross-lingual, and parallel text pairs. The multilingual rater is trained using a combined loss that incorporates pairwise preference supervision across languages and a regularization term from parallel pairs to enforce language-agnostic quality alignment. The rater model is based on the BGE-M3 architecture, fine-tuned with a linear head to predict quality scores, and is designed to be robust to translation-induced noise and cross-lingual variation.
9898bbde43fa16e5e1b67d5ab651529a5915eb91.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a large-scale web corpus comprising 1.5 trillion English tokens and 3 trillion tokens in 17 additional languages, following deduplication and heuristic filtering pipelines. The proposed method will be compared against strong baselines, including QuRater, FineWeb2-HQ, AskLLM, DCLM, and uniform sampling, for both English and multilingual data selection. Evaluation will use a suite of benchmarks: for English, tasks such as ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, SciQ, LogiQA, TriviaQA, BoolQ, HellaSwag, PIQA, OpenBookQA, WinoGrande, NaturalQuestions, and MMLU; for multilingual, translated and native datasets including ARC, StoryCloze, XNLI, HellaSwag, XCOPA, XWinograd, MMLU, BMLAMA, FLORES, and region-specific MMLU variants. Pretraining will be performed on LLaMA-architecture models (1.2B and 7B parameters), with top-scoring data subsets selected by each method. Metrics include average accuracy across benchmarks, mean squared error for cross-lingual consistency, and ablation studies on the impact of cross-lingual and parallel pair integration.
9898bbde43fa16e5e1b67d5ab651529a5915eb91.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified aggregation of multiple English data quality raters via pairwise modeling, enabling robust and stable quality scoring. It pioneers a scalable translation-based transfer of quality judgments to multilingual settings, supporting monolingual, cross-lingual, and parallel supervision. The method enforces language-agnostic alignment through parallel pair regularization and demonstrates significant improvements over state-of-the-art baselines in both English and multilingual LLM pretraining. Additionally, it provides empirical evidence that pairwise supervision yields greater cross-lingual stability and robustness than pointwise scoring, establishing a general framework for high-quality multilingual data selection.

98ab8260c98030109ba8467f52b13d075276cf0f.title: Accommodating Audio Modality in CLIP for Multimodal Processing
98ab8260c98030109ba8467f52b13d075276cf0f.research_question: How can multimodal pre-training frameworks be extended to effectively incorporate audio alongside vision and language modalities for comprehensive video understanding and downstream tasks such as retrieval and captioning?
98ab8260c98030109ba8467f52b13d075276cf0f.hypothesis: Integrating an audio encoder with architecture consistent with vision and text encoders, combined with inter-modal and intra-modal contrastive learning and explicit encoding of both verbal and nonverbal audio information, will enable more effective multimodal representation learning and yield superior performance on video retrieval and captioning tasks compared to existing vision-language or audio-only models.
98ab8260c98030109ba8467f52b13d075276cf0f.proposed_method: A unified tri-encoder framework will be developed by extending the CLIP architecture to include an audio encoder that mirrors the vision encoder's structure. Audio inputs will be converted to spectrograms, segmented, and embedded with learnable positional encodings and a novel audio type token that dynamically controls the encoding of verbal or nonverbal information. Pre-training will employ both inter-modal contrastive learning (aligning audio with text and vision) and intra-modal contrastive learning (self-supervised learning within audio via augmentation and masking), using symmetric cross-entropy losses. During downstream adaptation, multiple modality fusion strategies (global-to-global, global-to-local, local-to-local) will be explored for retrieval, and a multimodal caption generator will be constructed for video captioning by concatenating fine-grained features from all three modalities.
98ab8260c98030109ba8467f52b13d075276cf0f.experiment_details: The model will be pre-trained on large-scale multimodal datasets, including Howto100M and Audioset, with careful balancing and alignment of verbal and nonverbal audio content. Fine-tuning and evaluation will be conducted on benchmark datasets such as MSR-VTT, VATEX, and Audiocaps for both retrieval and captioning tasks. Baselines will include classical retrieval methods, pre-training-based methods, and CLIP-based models, with performance measured using Recall@K, Median Rank for retrieval, and BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE, and CIDEr for captioning. Ablation studies will assess the impact of key components (audio type token, contrastive objectives), and training cost will be compared to prior tri-modal models like VATT. Additional experiments will include event classification on ESC50 and UCF101 to evaluate generalization and efficiency.
98ab8260c98030109ba8467f52b13d075276cf0f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified tri-encoder structure that extends CLIP to the audio modality, ensuring architectural consistency and efficient training. A novel audio type token mechanism is designed to explicitly control and encode both verbal and nonverbal information, addressing the heterogeneity of audio content in general videos. The framework leverages both inter-modal and intra-modal contrastive learning, enabling rich cross-modal and self-supervised audio representation learning. The method claims to achieve state-of-the-art performance on multiple video retrieval and captioning benchmarks while requiring significantly less computational resources compared to prior tri-modal pre-training approaches.

98ab899c909d2de2e65d0d612bebe82235f4ac5a.title: Attack via Overfitting: 10-shot Benign Fine-tuning to Jailbreak LLMs
98ab899c909d2de2e65d0d612bebe82235f4ac5a.research_question: Can large language models be jailbroken using fine-tuning with only a small number of benign question-answer pairs, and what mechanisms underlie such vulnerabilities in model safety alignment?
98ab899c909d2de2e65d0d612bebe82235f4ac5a.hypothesis: Overfitting a large language model on identical refusal answers, followed by fine-tuning with standard benign answers, will cause the model to forget its safety alignment and become susceptible to jailbreaking, even when only benign data is used.
98ab899c909d2de2e65d0d612bebe82235f4ac5a.proposed_method: A novel two-stage fine-tuning attack is proposed to compromise the safety alignment of large language models (LLMs) using only ten benign QA pairs. In the first stage, the LLM is fine-tuned on ten benign questions, each paired with an identical refusal answer (e.g., 'Sorry, I cannot assist with that'), inducing overfitting and causing the model to refuse all queries. In the second stage, the same ten benign questions are used, but now paired with their standard, helpful answers; this further fine-tuning causes the model to forget the refusal behavior and respond compliantly to any question, including harmful ones. The approach leverages the heightened sensitivity of overfitted models to parameter changes, enabling benign data to induce catastrophic forgetting of safety alignment. The method is implemented using both full and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (e.g., LoRA), and hyperparameters are adjusted for different model scales and alignment strengths.
98ab899c909d2de2e65d0d612bebe82235f4ac5a.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on ten diverse LLMs, including open-source and closed-source models such as Llama2-7b, Llama3-8b, Deepseek-R1-Distill-Llama3-8b, Qwen2.5-7b, Qwen3-8b, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4o, and GPT-4.1. The attack is compared against five baselines: Absolutely Obedient Agent (AOA) fine-tuning, encryption-based fine-tuning, malicious fine-tuning with harmful QA pairs, indirect malicious fine-tuning, and irrelevant fine-tuning with a large benign dataset (Alpaca). Evaluation is performed using the AdvBench benchmark, with effectiveness measured by Attack Success Rate (ASR) and Harmful Score (HS), and stealth assessed via Detection Rate (DR) using GPT-4.1-mini as a moderation model. Additional experiments test the impact of ablation (removing Stage-1), different system prompts, LoRA vs. full fine-tuning, and resilience to token-wise defensive fine-tuning.
98ab899c909d2de2e65d0d612bebe82235f4ac5a.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first attack that leverages overfitting on benign refusal answers to jailbreak LLMs using only ten fully benign QA pairs, without any explicit or implicit harmful content. The two-stage fine-tuning method demonstrates that benign data can be as effective as harmful data in compromising safety alignment when the model is overfitted. The attack achieves high effectiveness and stealth, outperforming or matching existing fine-tuning-based jailbreak methods while evading detection by moderation models. The findings reveal a previously unreported vulnerability in LLMs, showing that overfitting with benign data can critically undermine safety alignment, even bypassing recent token-wise defense mechanisms.

98b23dca142b5beb9676f673a798ed29b537e13d.title: On Optimal Steering to Achieve Exact Fairness
98b23dca142b5beb9676f673a798ed29b537e13d.research_question: How can data or internal representations be optimally steered to achieve exact group fairness (such as demographic parity and equal opportunity) in downstream machine learning models, without incurring a trade-off with utility?
98b23dca142b5beb9676f673a798ed29b537e13d.hypothesis: It is possible to identify and efficiently compute the nearest ideal data distribution—one that guarantees exact group fairness for any cost-sensitive Bayes-optimal classifier—such that steering the original data or representations towards this distribution will simultaneously improve or maintain both fairness and utility.
98b23dca142b5beb9676f673a798ed29b537e13d.proposed_method: The proposed methodology defines an 'ideal distribution' as one on which the Bayes-optimal classifier for any cost-sensitive risk satisfies exact group fairness (e.g., demographic parity, equal opportunity). The approach formulates an optimization problem to find the nearest ideal distribution to a given data distribution, using KL-divergence as the distance metric and expressing the fairness constraints as parametric conditions on the distributions (e.g., means and covariances for Gaussian families). Efficient algorithms are developed for solving this optimization when the underlying distributions are from well-known parametric families, such as univariate or multivariate Gaussians and log-normals. Two main interventions are considered: (1) Affirmative Action, which modifies only the underprivileged group(s) to achieve fairness, and (2) All-Subgroup Change, which allows modification of all subgroups, solved via non-convex optimization (e.g., line search over parameter grids). Closed-form solutions are provided for special cases, and theoretical bounds are established for the accuracy and fairness gap as a function of the KL-divergence between the original and steered distributions.
98b23dca142b5beb9676f673a798ed29b537e13d.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic experiments use stylized Gaussian settings to analyze the effect of different distributional interventions on fairness (demographic parity, equal opportunity), Bayes error, and divergence metrics (KL and Jensen-Shannon). Real-world experiments include steering LLM representations for fair multi-class classification on the Bias in Bios dataset, where group disparities (e.g., TPR-gap between genders) are measured and compared against baselines such as MiMiC and LEACE. The methodology is also applied to emotion steering in LLM-generated movie reviews, using the Gaussian Concept Steer (GCS) framework and GPT-4 as an oracle for evaluating joyfulness. Evaluation metrics include fairness gaps (TPR-gap, ∆DP, ∆EO), Bayes error, and utility measures (accuracy), with interventions compared to standard reweighting and moment-matching baselines. Experimental setups involve affine transformations of representations, estimation of distribution parameters, and application of the proposed optimization framework.
98b23dca142b5beb9676f673a798ed29b537e13d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a formal and general definition of ideal distributions for fairness, provides a tractable KL-divergence-based optimization framework for finding the nearest such distribution under parametric constraints, and delivers efficient algorithms with closed-form solutions for common distribution families. The approach guarantees exact fairness for all cost-sensitive Bayes-optimal classifiers, overcoming limitations of prior heuristic or intractable methods. The framework is empirically validated on both synthetic and real-world tasks, demonstrating that fairness can be achieved or improved without sacrificing utility, and can be applied to steer LLM representations for practical fairness interventions. Theoretical contributions include new parametric conditions for fairness, bounds on fairness and accuracy loss, and a principled connection to existing reweighting methods.

98c363cecb8d3fd0159bdde71f58ece93a5941cf.title: Hierarchical Graph Tokenization for Molecule-Language Alignment
98c363cecb8d3fd0159bdde71f58ece93a5941cf.research_question: How can the intrinsic hierarchical structure of molecules be effectively integrated into large language models to improve molecule-language alignment and reduce hallucination in molecular reasoning tasks?
98c363cecb8d3fd0159bdde71f58ece93a5941cf.hypothesis: Incorporating hierarchical graph information—specifically, atom, motif (functional group), and molecule-level structures—into the tokenization and instruction tuning process of large language models will significantly improve molecule-language alignment, reduce hallucination, and enhance performance on molecule-centric downstream tasks compared to node-centric tokenization approaches.
98c363cecb8d3fd0159bdde71f58ece93a5941cf.proposed_method: A novel hierarchical graph tokenization framework, HIGHT, will be developed to encode molecules at three levels: atom, motif (functional group), and whole-molecule. The method will first transform molecular graphs into hierarchical graphs by detecting motifs using algorithms such as BRICS, and then augment the graph with supernodes representing motifs and the entire molecule. Separate vector-quantized variational autoencoders (VQVAEs) will be trained to generate discrete tokens for atoms and motifs, using self-supervised tasks to capture their contextual and structural information. Motif and atom tokens will be further enhanced with Laplacian positional encodings and projected into the language model embedding space via specialized adapters. The instruction tuning dataset will be augmented (HiPubChem) to include motif-level descriptions, both positive (present) and negative (absent), ensuring that language data explicitly aligns with hierarchical molecular features. A two-stage instruction tuning process will be employed: initial alignment pretraining on large-scale molecule-text pairs, followed by task-specific fine-tuning.
98c363cecb8d3fd0159bdde71f58ece93a5941cf.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 14 real-world molecule-centric benchmarks, including property prediction (classification and regression), molecular captioning, and chemical reaction prediction. Datasets such as MoleculeNet, ChEBI-20, QM9, CYP450, and Mol-Instructions will be used, with tasks covering quantum chemistry, biological activity, and natural language description of molecules. Baselines will include state-of-the-art node-centric tokenization LGLMs (e.g., InstructMol, GIMLET, Galactica), molecular foundation models (e.g., MolT5, MoMu, MolFM), and regression-based LLMs (e.g., Llama-2, Vicuna, ChatGPT). Evaluation metrics will include macro/micro F1, ROC-AUC, MAE, BLEU, ROUGE, METEOR, Levenshtein distance, and molecular fingerprint similarity. A new diagnostic benchmark, MotifHallu, will be introduced to quantify hallucination regarding functional group recognition. Ablation studies will assess the contributions of hierarchical tokenization, positional encoding, and instruction data augmentation.
98c363cecb8d3fd0159bdde71f58ece93a5941cf.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to systematically integrate hierarchical molecular graph information into both the architecture and instruction tuning data of large graph-language models. It introduces a hierarchical graph tokenizer that encodes atom, motif, and molecule-level tokens, and augments instruction tuning with motif-level descriptions. The method also introduces MotifHallu, a new benchmark for evaluating hallucination in functional group recognition. Experimental results are expected to demonstrate substantial reductions in hallucination (up to 40%) and significant improvements across a wide range of molecule-language tasks, establishing a new foundation for graph-language alignment in LLMs.

98d37a7af4fca9a01c58e429c31f3ac8ba93d266.title: Learning Robust Statistics for Simulation-based Inference under Model Misspecification
98d37a7af4fca9a01c58e429c31f3ac8ba93d266.research_question: How can simulation-based inference methods be made robust to model misspecification across a variety of inference frameworks, particularly when the choice of summary statistics impacts the reliability of posterior inference?
98d37a7af4fca9a01c58e429c31f3ac8ba93d266.hypothesis: Incorporating a regularization term that penalizes summary statistics leading to a mismatch between simulated and observed data will enable the learning of robust statistics, resulting in more reliable and trustworthy inference under model misspecification, without sacrificing accuracy when the model is well-specified.
98d37a7af4fca9a01c58e429c31f3ac8ba93d266.proposed_method: A new framework is developed for learning robust summary statistics in simulation-based inference (SBI) by augmenting the standard loss function with a regularization term based on the maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) between the distributions of simulated and observed summary statistics. The summary statistics are learned via neural networks, either jointly with the inference network (as in neural posterior estimation, NPE) or prior to inference (as in autoencoder-based approaches for ABC). The regularizer penalizes choices of summary statistics for which the observed statistic is an outlier relative to the distribution of simulated statistics, thus preventing the inference network from generalizing outside its training distribution. The regularization strength is controlled by a hyperparameter λ, encoding the trade-off between informativeness and robustness. The approach is general and can be applied to any SBI method that utilizes summary statistics, including NPE and ABC.
98d37a7af4fca9a01c58e429c31f3ac8ba93d266.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic experiments use the Ricker model (population ecology) and the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process (stochastic time series), with controlled levels of model misspecification introduced via an ε-contamination model. The methods are evaluated using root mean squared error (RMSE) of posterior samples and MMD between observed and posterior predictive distributions. Baselines include standard NPE, ABC, and robust neural posterior estimation (RNPE). For real data, the approach is tested on a radio propagation dataset (Turin model), where the model is known to be misspecified. The summary network architectures include convolutional and recurrent layers, and hyperparameters such as the regularization weight and kernel bandwidth are selected via heuristics or validation. The method's robustness to both likelihood and prior misspecification is assessed.
98d37a7af4fca9a01c58e429c31f3ac8ba93d266.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first general approach for handling model misspecification in SBI that is applicable across different classes of inference methods. It introduces a principled, regularized loss function that learns summary statistics robust to misspecification, leveraging MMD as a sample-efficient, outlier-robust distance. The approach is agnostic to the inference procedure and can be integrated with any statistics-based SBI method. Empirical results demonstrate superior robustness and accuracy under misspecification compared to existing methods, while maintaining performance in well-specified cases. The method also provides a single interpretable hyperparameter to control the robustness-efficiency trade-off.

9916bf020e954552fc24868d81f4cb22cf975472.title: Streaming Linear System Identification with Reverse Experience Replay
9916bf020e954552fc24868d81f4cb22cf975472.research_question: How can linear time-invariant (LTI) dynamical systems be accurately and efficiently identified from a single trajectory in a streaming or online setting, particularly when data points are temporally correlated, and only first-order gradient information is available?
9916bf020e954552fc24868d81f4cb22cf975472.hypothesis: A streaming algorithm that processes data in reverse order within small buffers, thereby leveraging the dependency structure of temporally correlated samples, will achieve minimax-optimal parameter and prediction error rates for LTI system identification, matching or improving upon offline ordinary least squares (OLS) and outperforming standard SGD and experience replay approaches.
9916bf020e954552fc24868d81f4cb22cf975472.proposed_method: A novel streaming algorithm, termed SGD with Reverse Experience Replay (SGD-RER), will be developed for LTI system identification. The method divides the incoming data stream into non-overlapping buffers of size B (plus a gap u for approximate independence), and within each buffer, performs stochastic gradient descent (SGD) updates in reverse temporal order. This approach is designed to decorrelate temporally dependent samples and eliminate the bias present in standard SGD. The algorithm maintains low space complexity by only storing a small buffer at a time and employs tail-averaging across buffers to further reduce variance. Step sizes are carefully chosen to ensure stability, and the method is extensible to settings with known sparsity patterns or generalized (nonlinear) dynamical systems.
9916bf020e954552fc24868d81f4cb22cf975472.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic data generated from a Gaussian VAR (Vector Autoregressive) model with specified transition matrices and noise distributions. The proposed SGD-RER algorithm will be compared against baselines including offline OLS, standard SGD, and SGD with standard (random) experience replay (SGD-ER). Evaluation metrics will include parameter error (operator norm between estimated and true transition matrices) and prediction error at stationarity. Experimental setup will involve varying buffer sizes, step sizes, and problem dimensions, with performance tracked over the streaming horizon and statistical significance assessed over multiple runs.
9916bf020e954552fc24868d81f4cb22cf975472.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first streaming SGD-style algorithm for LTI system identification that achieves information-theoretically optimal error rates for both parameter and prediction error, even in the presence of strong temporal dependencies. The reverse experience replay mechanism is novel in this context and is shown to exactly unravel temporal correlations, providing unbiased and consistent estimates with nearly optimal computational and space complexity. The approach is generalizable to sparse and nonlinear dynamical systems, and the theoretical analysis establishes minimax-optimality up to logarithmic factors, outperforming existing streaming and SGD-based methods for dependent data.

9922cc460bb7832b791f32f78986cf0d1542643f.title: Multimodal Bandits: Regret Lower Bounds and Optimal Algorithms
9922cc460bb7832b791f32f78986cf0d1542643f.research_question: How can the regret in stochastic multi-armed bandit problems with an at-most-m-multimodal reward structure (with respect to a known tree graph) be minimized, and what are the fundamental computational and algorithmic limits for achieving asymptotically optimal performance in this setting?
9922cc460bb7832b791f32f78986cf0d1542643f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a computationally tractable algorithm can be developed to solve the Graves-Lai optimization problem for multimodal bandits, enabling the design of asymptotically optimal algorithms whose regret matches the information-theoretic lower bound, and that local search strategies are generally suboptimal except for specific classes of reward functions.
9922cc460bb7832b791f32f78986cf0d1542643f.proposed_method: A new algorithm is proposed to solve the Graves-Lai optimization problem for multimodal bandits in a computationally tractable manner. The approach combines discretization of the reward parameter space, decomposition of the constraint set into subproblems, and a dynamic programming solver that exploits the tree structure of the arm graph. The method iteratively applies penalized projected subgradient descent to optimize the sampling rate vector, using dynamic programming to efficiently compute the most confusing parameter for each subproblem. The discretization ensures that the approximation error can be controlled and made arbitrarily small by increasing the grid resolution, and the overall procedure is designed to scale polynomially in the number of arms and discretization points.
9922cc460bb7832b791f32f78986cf0d1542643f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic multi-armed bandit instances where the reward structure is generated as a sum of exponentials centered at specified modes on a fixed binary tree with seven arms. Gaussian reward distributions with unit variance are used, and the mean vectors are constructed to create both 'easy' (sharp peaks) and 'hard' (flat peaks) multimodal instances by varying the spread parameter. The proposed multimodal OSSB algorithm, which uses the new Graves-Lai solver, will be compared against a classical OSSB baseline that ignores the multimodal structure. Evaluation will be based on cumulative regret over 10,000 rounds, averaged over 500 trials, with regret curves and standard error reported. The frequency of solving the optimization problem is reduced for computational efficiency by updating only at exponentially increasing rounds.
9922cc460bb7832b791f32f78986cf0d1542643f.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first computationally tractable algorithm for solving the Graves-Lai optimization problem in the context of multimodal bandits with arbitrary tree structures and reward distributions. The approach leverages a novel combination of discretization, dynamic programming, and projected subgradient descent to efficiently navigate the non-convex constraint set. It is demonstrated that local search strategies are not generally optimal for multimodal bandits, and the new method is required to achieve asymptotic optimality. The algorithm is broadly applicable and provides practical means to implement bandit algorithms with regret matching the information-theoretic lower bound.

993885949975ad6b2dcf4f91840eb5c433d3d85f.title: Feature Transportation Improves Graph Neural Networks
993885949975ad6b2dcf4f91840eb5c433d3d85f.research_question: How can graph neural networks be enhanced to more effectively model complex phenomena in graph-structured data, particularly those involving directional feature transportation, and how does the integration of advection, diffusion, and reaction mechanisms impact their expressiveness and performance on various graph learning tasks?
993885949975ad6b2dcf4f91840eb5c433d3d85f.hypothesis: Incorporating a learnable advection operator, alongside diffusion and reaction terms inspired by Advection-Diffusion-Reaction (ADR) systems, into graph neural networks will improve their ability to model directional feature transportation, leading to enhanced expressiveness and superior performance, especially on tasks where traditional diffusion-based GNNs are limited.
993885949975ad6b2dcf4f91840eb5c433d3d85f.proposed_method: A novel graph neural network architecture, ADR-GNN, will be developed by discretizing the continuous Advection-Diffusion-Reaction partial differential equation onto graphs. The model will consist of three main components: a learnable advection operator that transports node features directionally via normalized, asymmetric edge weights; a diffusion operator realized through a learnable, channel-wise Laplacian smoothing with implicit time discretization for stability; and a reaction term implemented as a multilayer perceptron (MLP) with both additive and multiplicative interactions. The advection operator will be designed to be mass-preserving, stable, and consistent with its continuous counterpart, ensuring that the sum of outbound edge weights per node and channel is one. The ADR-GNN layers will be composed sequentially, with each layer applying advection, diffusion, and reaction in an operator-splitting scheme, allowing the model to flexibly learn the relative importance of each process for a given task.
993885949975ad6b2dcf4f91840eb5c433d3d85f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse suite of real-world datasets, including homophilic and heterophilic node classification benchmarks (e.g., Cora, Citeseer, Pubmed, Squirrel, Film, Chameleon, Cornell, Texas, Wisconsin, Twitch-DE, deezer-europe, Penn94, arXiv-year) and spatio-temporal node forecasting tasks (e.g., Chickenpox Hungary, PedalMe London, Wikipedia Math, METR-LA, PEMS-BAY). The ADR-GNN will be compared against a comprehensive set of baselines, including GCN, GAT, PDE-GCN, GRAND, GCNII, H2GCN, GRAFF, DCRNN, GraphWaveNet, and others, using standard evaluation metrics such as node classification accuracy, mean squared error (MSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE). Hyperparameters will be selected via grid search, and ablation studies will be performed to isolate the contributions of advection, diffusion, and reaction components. Additional synthetic experiments will be designed to specifically test the model's ability to transport features directionally, and the impact of model depth and oversmoothing will be systematically evaluated.
993885949975ad6b2dcf4f91840eb5c433d3d85f.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first graph neural network architecture that combines learnable advection, diffusion, and reaction operators in a manner consistent with continuous ADR PDEs. The advection operator is designed to be mass-preserving, stable, and capable of learning directionally asymmetric edge weights, enabling the modeling of feature transportation phenomena that are inaccessible to traditional diffusion- or reaction-based GNNs. The methodology provides a principled framework for balancing smoothing, transport, and non-linear transformation, and demonstrates significant improvements on heterophilic and spatio-temporal datasets, as well as competitive or superior performance on homophilic benchmarks. The work also provides new insights into the theoretical and practical benefits of integrating ADR dynamics into GNNs, supported by comprehensive empirical validation and ablation studies.

993df7df129f8d18816877d69923d7df7b347d85.title: LLM-Blender: Ensembling Large Language Models with Pairwise Ranking and Generative Fusion
993df7df129f8d18816877d69923d7df7b347d85.research_question: How can the diverse strengths of multiple open-source large language models (LLMs) be effectively leveraged through ensembling to achieve consistently superior performance across instruction-following tasks, compared to relying on any single model?
993df7df129f8d18816877d69923d7df7b347d85.hypothesis: Ensembling multiple open-source LLMs using a combination of pairwise ranking and generative fusion will produce outputs that are consistently better aligned with human preferences and outperform any individual LLM or existing ensembling baselines on instruction-following tasks.
993df7df129f8d18816877d69923d7df7b347d85.proposed_method: A two-stage ensembling framework is proposed, consisting of a pairwise ranking module (PAIRRANKER) and a generative fusion module (GENFUSER). PAIRRANKER employs a cross-attention encoder (e.g., DeBERTa) to jointly encode the input and all pairs of candidate outputs from N LLMs, learning to discern subtle qualitative differences via pairwise comparison. For each input, a matrix of pairwise comparison scores is constructed and aggregated (using MaxLogits or MaxWins) to rank all candidate outputs. The top K ranked candidates are then concatenated with the input and passed to GENFUSER, a seq2seq model (e.g., Flan-T5-XL), which is fine-tuned to generate an improved output by fusing information from the selected candidates. The entire pipeline is trained using a multi-task classification loss with supervision from both conventional NLG metrics and ChatGPT-based pairwise rankings.
993df7df129f8d18816877d69923d7df7b347d85.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on MixInstruct, a newly created benchmark dataset containing 110,000 instruction-following examples sourced from Alpaca-GPT4, Dolly-15K, GPT4All-LAION, and ShareGPT, with outputs from 11 popular open-source LLMs per example. The dataset is split into 100k/5k/5k for train/validation/test. Baselines will include individual LLMs, random selection, and existing reranking methods such as MLM-Scoring, SimCLS, and SummaReranker. Evaluation will use both conventional NLG metrics (BERTScore, BLEURT, BARTScore) and a GPT-Rank metric, which is derived from ChatGPT-based pairwise comparisons. The effectiveness of the ensembling framework will be measured by improvements in these metrics, as well as the percentage of examples where the ensemble output surpasses the top individual LLMs.
993df7df129f8d18816877d69923d7df7b347d85.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a novel combination of pairwise ranking and generative fusion for LLM ensembling, enabling dynamic selection and synthesis of outputs tailored to each input. PAIRRANKER is the first to leverage cross-attention encoders for direct pairwise comparison and ranking of LLM outputs, capturing subtle differences that pointwise methods miss. GENFUSER further enhances performance by fusing the strengths of top-ranked candidates into a single, improved response. The creation of the MixInstruct benchmark provides a large-scale, diverse, and instruction-focused dataset with oracle pairwise comparisons, supporting robust training and evaluation of ensemble methods. The overall approach demonstrates substantial and consistent gains over individual models and existing ensembling baselines across multiple metrics.

993fce9e6428dcfd02c7adc069a28df1e4ab6e99.title: LittleBit: Ultra Low-Bit Quantization via Latent Factorization
993fce9e6428dcfd02c7adc069a28df1e4ab6e99.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be compressed to extremely low effective bit-widths (sub-1-bit per weight, e.g., 0.1 BPW) while maintaining model performance and computational efficiency, thereby enabling deployment in highly resource-constrained environments?
993fce9e6428dcfd02c7adc069a28df1e4ab6e99.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that combining low-rank matrix factorization with binarization of factors, augmented by a multi-scale compensation mechanism and specialized initialization and error correction strategies, can enable LLMs to be quantized to sub-1-bit per weight (e.g., 0.1 BPW) without significant loss in performance or efficiency.
993fce9e6428dcfd02c7adc069a28df1e4ab6e99.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces an ultra-low-bit quantization framework for LLMs, termed LittleBit, which first factorizes each weight matrix into low-rank components (U, V) using latent matrix factorization (e.g., truncated SVD). These factors are then binarized to ±1, and learnable full-precision (FP16) scaling parameters are applied across rows, columns, and an additional latent dimension to compensate for information loss. The architecture employs a dual-pathway structure: a primary path using the binarized factors and multi-scale compensation, and a residual path that models the approximation error with its own binarized factors and scales. Initialization of all parameters leverages a Dual-SVID (Sign-Value-Independent Decomposition) strategy, which preserves both sign and magnitude information from the original SVD, and both paths are jointly optimized via quantization-aware training (QAT) with knowledge distillation. The forward computation is structured to maximize efficiency, replacing large GEMM operations with smaller binary matrix multiplications and element-wise scaling.
993fce9e6428dcfd02c7adc069a28df1e4ab6e99.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of LLMs, including Llama, Llama2, Llama3, OPT, Phi-4, and QwQ, spanning model sizes from 1.3B to 32B parameters. The primary evaluation metric is perplexity (PPL) on the WikiText-2 validation set, with additional results reported on C4 and PTB datasets. Zero-shot accuracy will be measured on reasoning benchmarks such as WinoGrande, OpenBookQA, HellaSwag, BoolQ, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, and PIQA. Baselines will include state-of-the-art post-training quantization (PTQ) methods (e.g., GPTQ, OmniQuant, BiLLM, STBLLM) and QAT methods (e.g., OneBit, BinaryMoS). The quantization-aware training setup will use knowledge distillation from the original full-precision model, with a combined KL divergence and intermediate layer MSE loss. Kernel-level latency and memory footprint will also be benchmarked, including custom 1-bit CUDA kernels for inference speedup.
993fce9e6428dcfd02c7adc069a28df1e4ab6e99.novelty_claims: The proposed method claims several innovations: (1) achieving unprecedented sub-1-bit quantization (as low as 0.1 BPW) for LLMs while maintaining competitive performance, (2) unifying latent low-rank factorization with multi-scale compensation, including a novel latent dimension scale, (3) introducing Dual-SVID initialization for stable and effective QAT of factorized, binarized models, and (4) integrating a residual compensation path for targeted error correction without increasing parameter budget. The approach also inherently compresses the KV cache and enables significant memory and latency reductions, establishing a new state-of-the-art in the size–performance trade-off for LLM quantization.

996445d847f06e99b0bd259345408a0cf1bce87e.title: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT
996445d847f06e99b0bd259345408a0cf1bce87e.research_question: How are factual associations stored and recalled within large autoregressive transformer language models, and can these associations be directly and specifically edited without sacrificing generalization or specificity?
996445d847f06e99b0bd259345408a0cf1bce87e.hypothesis: Factual associations in autoregressive transformer models are stored as localized, directly editable computations within mid-layer feed-forward (MLP) modules, particularly at the processing of the last token of the subject entity. Direct manipulation of these modules enables targeted editing of specific factual associations while preserving model performance on unrelated knowledge.
996445d847f06e99b0bd259345408a0cf1bce87e.proposed_method: A causal intervention technique will be developed to identify neuron activations that are decisive for factual predictions in transformer language models. Causal mediation analysis will be used to trace the flow of information and pinpoint the specific hidden states and modules responsible for recalling factual associations. Building on these insights, a Rank-One Model Editing (ROME) algorithm will be designed to insert or modify key–value associations in the weights of a single mid-layer MLP module. The method will compute a subject-specific key vector and an object-encoding value vector, then apply a closed-form rank-one update to the MLP weight matrix to encode the new factual association. The update will be optimized to maximize the probability of the desired factual output while minimizing interference with other stored knowledge.
996445d847f06e99b0bd259345408a0cf1bce87e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large autoregressive transformer models such as GPT-2XL (1.5B parameters) and GPT-J (6B parameters). The evaluation will use the Zero-Shot Relation Extraction (zsRE) benchmark and a newly introduced COUNTERFACT dataset, which contains challenging counterfactual assertions and various linguistic paraphrases. Baseline methods for comparison will include standard and constrained fine-tuning, hypernetwork-based editors (KE, MEND), and neuron-attribution-based editing (KN). Evaluation metrics will include efficacy (accuracy on edited facts), generalization (robustness to paraphrase), specificity (accuracy on unrelated facts), semantic consistency, and fluency. Human evaluation will also be conducted to assess the quality and factual consistency of generated text after editing.
996445d847f06e99b0bd259345408a0cf1bce87e.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a principled, closed-form method (ROME) for directly editing factual associations in large language models by targeting mid-layer MLP modules. This approach is grounded in causal tracing analysis, which provides new insights into the localization of factual recall mechanisms. The method achieves a strong balance of generalization and specificity, outperforming or matching existing model-editing techniques while avoiding common pitfalls such as overfitting or unintended knowledge bleedover. Additionally, a new benchmark dataset (COUNTERFACT) is introduced to rigorously evaluate the robustness and specificity of factual edits in language models.

9967d014e17dc17e07bedeff212f43b084b0f0b8.title: Lambda-Skip Connections: the architectural component that prevents Rank Collapse
9967d014e17dc17e07bedeff212f43b084b0f0b8.research_question: How can architectural modifications to sequence models prevent the phenomenon of rank collapse, which reduces model expressivity and causes training instabilities, and what are the necessary and sufficient conditions for such prevention across different model families including Transformers and State Space Models (SSMs)?
9967d014e17dc17e07bedeff212f43b084b0f0b8.hypothesis: Introducing a parametrized skip connection, termed lambda-skip connection, with appropriately chosen or learned strength, in combination with LayerNorm, is sufficient to prevent rank collapse in both Transformers and SSM-based sequence models. Furthermore, gating mechanisms may also contribute to the prevention of rank collapse.
9967d014e17dc17e07bedeff212f43b084b0f0b8.proposed_method: A general framework will be developed that unifies the architectures of Transformers and SSMs, allowing for the analysis of rank collapse across both. The standard skip connection will be replaced with a lambda-skip connection, introducing a parameter λ that controls the contribution of the skip path. Analytical derivations will be performed to establish sufficient conditions on λ (in terms of model parameters and norms) that guarantee a lower bound on the rank collapse metric, ensuring that the output embeddings retain diversity across layers. Theoretical results will be extended to cases where λ is either fixed or learnable per layer, and the necessity of these conditions will be explored through ablation studies and analytical examples. The impact of additional components such as LayerNorm and gating mechanisms will also be empirically and, where possible, theoretically investigated.
9967d014e17dc17e07bedeff212f43b084b0f0b8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using large pre-trained models (e.g., Mamba-2 with 2 billion parameters) and various sequence modeling architectures, including both Transformers and SSMs. The rank collapse metric will be evaluated across layers for different values of λ, including fixed and learned settings, by forwarding tokenized Wikipedia text sequences through the models. Additional experiments will compare the effects of ablated architectural components (skip connections, LayerNorm, gating) on rank collapse. Performance will be assessed on standard sequence modeling benchmarks such as the Long Range Arena (LRA) image task and the Multi-Query Associative Recall (MQAR) task, using accuracy as the evaluation metric. Baselines will include models with standard skip connections (λ=1), models with variable λ, and models with and without gating and normalization components.
9967d014e17dc17e07bedeff212f43b084b0f0b8.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the lambda-skip connection as a general, theoretically grounded architectural component that provides sufficient conditions to prevent rank collapse in a wide range of sequence models, including both Transformers and SSMs. It is the first to offer a general lower bound guarantee for the rank collapse metric applicable to both model families. The connection between gating mechanisms and rank collapse prevention is empirically established for the first time. The approach allows for minimal computational overhead and can be implemented with either fixed or learnable skip strengths, offering practical benefits for model stability and expressivity. Theoretical analysis is complemented by extensive empirical validation, providing actionable guidelines for robust sequence model design.

99832586d55f540f603637e458a292406a0ed75d.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
99832586d55f540f603637e458a292406a0ed75d.research_question: How can large language models be enabled to synergistically combine reasoning and acting for improved performance, interpretability, and robustness across diverse language reasoning and decision-making tasks?
99832586d55f540f603637e458a292406a0ed75d.hypothesis: Integrating interleaved reasoning traces and task-specific actions within large language models will yield superior performance, factuality, and interpretability compared to models that perform reasoning or acting in isolation.
99832586d55f540f603637e458a292406a0ed75d.proposed_method: A novel prompting paradigm, ReAct, will be developed to enable large language models to generate both verbal reasoning traces and task-specific actions in an interleaved manner. The method augments the agent's action space to include both environment-interacting actions and free-form language-based thoughts, allowing the model to dynamically reason about plans, handle exceptions, and update its knowledge by interacting with external environments such as knowledge bases. Few-shot in-context examples will be used to prompt the model, with each example consisting of human-annotated trajectories that interleave actions, thoughts, and observations. The approach will be evaluated both in a pure prompting setup and with additional fine-tuning on generated trajectories to further enhance performance.
99832586d55f540f603637e458a292406a0ed75d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four diverse benchmarks: HotpotQA (multi-hop question answering), FEVER (fact verification), ALFWorld (text-based interactive game), and WebShop (webpage navigation and shopping). For HotpotQA and FEVER, a simple Wikipedia API will be used to simulate interactive retrieval actions, and models will be evaluated on exact match and accuracy metrics. Baselines will include standard prompting, chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting, acting-only prompts, and self-consistency-enhanced CoT. For ALFWorld and WebShop, ReAct will be compared to imitation learning and reinforcement learning agents, with success rates and task-specific scores as evaluation metrics. Few-shot prompting will be used, with 1-6 in-context examples per task, and systematic ablations will be performed to isolate the contributions of reasoning and acting. Fine-tuning experiments will also be conducted using bootstrapped ReAct trajectories on smaller language models.
99832586d55f540f603637e458a292406a0ed75d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a general and flexible prompting-based paradigm that synergistically combines reasoning and acting within large language models for diverse task-solving. It demonstrates that interleaving reasoning traces and actions leads to improved factuality, reduced hallucination, and enhanced interpretability compared to existing methods. The method is shown to outperform state-of-the-art baselines in both knowledge-intensive reasoning and interactive decision-making tasks, even in few-shot learning settings. Additional contributions include systematic ablation studies, analysis of success and failure modes, and evidence that fine-tuning on ReAct-style trajectories further boosts performance beyond prompting alone.

998ac3e945857cf2676ee7efdbaf443a0c6f820a.title: Hyena Hierarchy: Towards Larger Convolutional Language Models
998ac3e945857cf2676ee7efdbaf443a0c6f820a.research_question: Can subquadratic neural network operators be developed that match or exceed the performance of attention-based models for large-scale language modeling and long-context sequence tasks, while reducing computational cost and memory requirements?
998ac3e945857cf2676ee7efdbaf443a0c6f820a.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a hierarchical composition of implicitly parameterized long convolutions and data-controlled gating can yield a subquadratic operator capable of matching or surpassing the quality of attention mechanisms in large-scale sequence modeling tasks, with improved computational efficiency.
998ac3e945857cf2676ee7efdbaf443a0c6f820a.proposed_method: A novel operator, termed Hyena, will be developed by interleaving implicitly parameterized long convolutions with element-wise multiplicative gating in a recurrent hierarchy. The method will compute multiple linear projections of the input sequence, with one projection serving as the value and others as gating signals. At each recurrence step, an implicit long convolution—parameterized by a shallow feed-forward neural network (FFN) and modulated by positional encoding and exponential decay windows—will be applied, followed by element-wise gating. The operator will be constructed such that the number of parameters is decoupled from the sequence length, enabling sublinear parameter scaling. Efficient evaluation will be achieved using fast Fourier transform (FFT)-based convolution algorithms, allowing the method to process very long sequences without materializing large matrices. Causality will be preserved for autoregressive tasks by ensuring filters are causal or by appropriate zero-padding and masking.
998ac3e945857cf2676ee7efdbaf443a0c6f820a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of mechanistic interpretability and reasoning benchmarks, including associative recall, majority, counting, in-context learning of functions, and arithmetic tasks, with varying sequence lengths (up to 131k tokens) and vocabulary sizes. For language modeling, the method will be evaluated on standard datasets such as WikiText103 and The Pile, with models trained at the sub-billion parameter scale and up to 137 billion tokens. Baselines will include state-space models (S4), explicit and implicit convolutional models (CKConv, FNO), hybrid attention-free architectures (GSS, H3, AFT, RWKV), and standard Transformer models using FlashAttention. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on reasoning tasks, test perplexity for language modeling, FLOPs for computational efficiency, and runtime/throughput for long-sequence processing. Additional downstream evaluations will be performed on SuperGLUE and image classification tasks (e.g., ImageNet-1k using Vision Transformer variants). Experimental setups will control for model width, depth, and training compute to ensure fair comparisons.
998ac3e945857cf2676ee7efdbaf443a0c6f820a.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new hierarchy of subquadratic operators for sequence modeling that generalizes and extends prior state-space and convolutional approaches. Unlike existing subquadratic methods, the approach achieves Transformer-level quality without hybridizing with dense attention layers, and does so with significantly reduced computational cost and memory usage. The method is the first to demonstrate attention-free in-context learning on extremely long sequences (up to 131k tokens) and matches Transformer performance on large-scale language modeling benchmarks with a 20% reduction in training compute. Additionally, the operator is shown to be up to 100x faster than highly optimized attention mechanisms at long sequence lengths, and is applicable to both language and vision domains.

998bc35af7c44a37f0eaca96c181b6aed9b7d489.title: Batch Active Learning at Scale
998bc35af7c44a37f0eaca96c181b6aed9b7d489.research_question: How can batch active learning be scaled to efficiently select large batches of data for labeling, in order to improve the training efficiency of complex machine learning models while minimizing redundant or ineffective samples?
998bc35af7c44a37f0eaca96c181b6aed9b7d489.hypothesis: Combining uncertainty-based selection with clustering-based diversity can enable batch active learning to scale to very large batch sizes (100K-1M), significantly improving label efficiency and model performance compared to existing methods.
998bc35af7c44a37f0eaca96c181b6aed9b7d489.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a batch active learning algorithm, Cluster-Margin, designed to operate at large batch sizes. The method begins by training a neural network on a randomly selected seed set, then computes embeddings for all unlabeled data using the penultimate layer of the network. Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering (HAC) with average-linkage is performed once as a preprocessing step on these embeddings to form clusters. In each active learning iteration, the algorithm selects a set of examples with the lowest margin scores (least model confidence), maps these to their clusters, and then samples a diverse batch using a round-robin scheme that prioritizes smaller clusters to maximize diversity. The selected batch is labeled, added to the training set, and the model is retrained. This process is repeated for a fixed number of iterations.
998bc35af7c44a37f0eaca96c181b6aed9b7d489.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both large-scale and small-scale image classification datasets. For large-scale evaluation, the Open Images v6 dataset (nearly 10 million images, 60 million labels, 20,000 classes) will be used, with a ResNet-101 model trained using batch SGD on TPU clusters. Batch sizes of 100K and 1M will be tested, with performance measured by pooled average precision. For smaller-scale validation, CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and SVHN datasets will be used with a VGG-16 model, sampling 5,000 images per iteration and evaluating accuracy over 10 trials. Baselines for comparison include Margin (uncertainty) sampling, BADGE, CoreSet, and Random sampling. All methods are adapted to handle multi-label or multi-class settings as appropriate, and computational efficiency is ensured through partitioning and parallelization where needed.
998bc35af7c44a37f0eaca96c181b6aed9b7d489.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to enable batch active learning at batch sizes several orders of magnitude larger than previously considered (up to 1M). It introduces a scalable algorithm that combines uncertainty and diversity through a single clustering preprocessing step, avoiding per-iteration clustering overhead. The method demonstrates substantial improvements in label efficiency—requiring as little as 40% of the labels needed by the next best method to reach equivalent performance on large-scale datasets. Additionally, an initial theoretical analysis provides label complexity guarantees for a related clustering-based sampler, establishing a connection between the empirical and theoretical benefits of the approach.

99b38b72026775a1e91d83fb71e984b5e8b7b374.title: From Decoding to Meta-Generation: Inference-time Algorithms for Large Language Models
99b38b72026775a1e91d83fb71e984b5e8b7b374.research_question: How can inference-time algorithms for large language models be systematically advanced to improve the quality, controllability, and efficiency of generated outputs, considering both token-level and meta-generation approaches as well as computational tradeoffs?
99b38b72026775a1e91d83fb71e984b5e8b7b374.hypothesis: Sophisticated inference-time algorithms, including both token-level and meta-generation strategies, can substantially improve the quality, diversity, and efficiency of outputs from large language models compared to standard decoding methods, especially when leveraging external information and efficient compute allocation.
99b38b72026775a1e91d83fb71e984b5e8b7b374.proposed_method: A unified framework will be developed that formalizes and categorizes inference-time algorithms for large language models into three main classes: token-level generation algorithms, meta-generation algorithms, and efficient generation techniques. Token-level algorithms will include MAP decoding (e.g., greedy, beam search), sampling-based methods (e.g., ancestral, nucleus, top-k, temperature, typical, and mirostat sampling), and adapters for controlled or constrained generation. Meta-generation algorithms will be constructed as higher-level programs that orchestrate multiple calls to token-level generators, incorporating strategies such as parallel or chained generation, step-level search, and refinement, as well as integration of external models, tools, or environment information. Efficiency will be addressed by analyzing and optimizing token cost, latency, and throughput, including techniques for token budget management and system-level acceleration. The framework will be instantiated in a modular software library, enabling empirical evaluation and ablation of algorithmic components.
99b38b72026775a1e91d83fb71e984b5e8b7b374.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of language generation tasks, including open-ended text generation, code generation, translation, and problem-solving benchmarks. Datasets such as standard NLP corpora, math problem sets, and code repositories will be used. Baselines will include greedy decoding, beam search, and ancestral sampling, as well as recent sampling adapters and meta-generation patterns. Evaluation metrics will comprise output quality (e.g., accuracy, BLEU, ROUGE, human acceptability), diversity, efficiency (token cost, latency), and controllability. The experimental setup will systematically vary algorithmic parameters (e.g., temperature, beam width, number of meta-generator calls) and analyze tradeoffs between quality and efficiency. Additional experiments will assess the impact of incorporating external information and system-level optimizations.
99b38b72026775a1e91d83fb71e984b5e8b7b374.novelty_claims: The proposed research claims novelty in unifying token-level and meta-generation inference-time algorithms under a single mathematical and programmatic formalism, bridging perspectives from NLP, LLMs, and machine learning systems. The approach introduces a taxonomy that clarifies the relationships and tradeoffs among existing and novel algorithms, and systematically addresses efficiency considerations alongside generation quality. The integration of meta-generation algorithms that leverage external information and programmatic control is highlighted as an innovative direction, as is the focus on inference-time compute scaling as a means to improve model performance. The research will provide practical tools and guidelines for designing, evaluating, and deploying advanced inference-time generation algorithms.

99bd96961a880adad88d087c9dc45f6cfbae1ea6.title: Generating Human Motion from Textual Descriptions with Discrete Representations
99bd96961a880adad88d087c9dc45f6cfbae1ea6.research_question: How can high-quality and semantically consistent 3D human motion be generated from natural language descriptions using discrete representations?
99bd96961a880adad88d087c9dc45f6cfbae1ea6.hypothesis: A two-stage generative framework that combines a CNN-based Vector Quantised Variational AutoEncoder (VQ-VAE) for motion discretization with a GPT-style transformer for text-conditioned sequence modeling will produce human motion sequences from text that are competitive with or superior to state-of-the-art diffusion-based methods, especially in terms of motion quality and text-motion consistency.
99bd96961a880adad88d087c9dc45f6cfbae1ea6.proposed_method: The proposed method consists of two main modules: Motion VQ-VAE and T2M-GPT.
