In the first stage, a 1D convolutional VQ-VAE encodes motion sequences into discrete code indices by mapping input motion data to a latent space and quantizing it using a learnable codebook, with strategies such as Exponential Moving Average (EMA) and CodeReset employed to prevent codebook collapse and enhance code utilization. The VQ-VAE is trained with a combination of L1 smooth reconstruction loss and velocity regularization to ensure high-fidelity motion reconstruction. In the second stage, a GPT-like transformer is trained to generate sequences of code indices conditioned on text embeddings extracted by CLIP, using causal self-attention and an autoregressive next-index prediction framework. To address training-inference discrepancies, a corruption strategy is applied during training, where a proportion of ground-truth code indices are randomly replaced to improve robustness. An explicit End token is learned to signal the termination of the generated motion sequence.
99bd96961a880adad88d087c9dc45f6cfbae1ea6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two benchmark datasets for text-driven human motion generation: HumanML3D and KIT-ML. Both datasets provide paired 3D motion sequences and textual descriptions, with HumanML3D being the largest available. The evaluation will follow established protocols, utilizing metrics such as R-Precision (for text-motion consistency), Frechet Inception Distance (FID, for motion quality), Multimodal Distance (MM-Dist), Diversity, and Multimodality. Baseline comparisons will include recent state-of-the-art methods, particularly diffusion-based models such as MDM and MotionDiffuse, as well as transformer and VAE-based approaches. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of quantization strategies (EMA, CodeReset), architecture choices, and dataset size. Models will be trained using AdamW optimizer, and hyperparameters such as codebook size, transformer depth, and corruption rate will be systematically explored.
99bd96961a880adad88d087c9dc45f6cfbae1ea6.novelty_claims: The proposed framework leverages a simple yet effective combination of discrete VQ-VAE representations and a GPT-style transformer for text-to-motion generation, demonstrating that classic VQ-VAE-based approaches remain highly competitive compared to more complex diffusion models. The method introduces a straightforward corruption strategy during transformer training to mitigate train-test discrepancies, and uses an explicit End token for variable-length motion generation without the need for separate length prediction modules. Comprehensive analyses of quantization strategies and dataset size provide new insights into the scalability and robustness of discrete generative models for human motion synthesis.

99c47cc8d02b2f8457e27ba4af72daa0210c55b2.title: Beyond Homophily: Reconstructing Structure for Graph-agnostic Clustering
99c47cc8d02b2f8457e27ba4af72daa0210c55b2.research_question: How can node clustering be effectively performed on real-world graphs with varying and unknown levels of homophily, without prior knowledge of the graph's homophilic or heterophilic nature?
99c47cc8d02b2f8457e27ba4af72daa0210c55b2.hypothesis: A graph-agnostic clustering framework that reconstructs both homophilic and heterophilic structures from raw graph data, applies a mixed-frequency filter, and utilizes a dual-subspace clustering network will achieve robust and superior clustering performance across graphs with diverse homophily levels.
99c47cc8d02b2f8457e27ba4af72daa0210c55b2.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a holistic, unsupervised graph clustering framework composed of three main components: structure reconstruction, a mixed graph filter, and a dual graph clustering network. First, two new graphs are constructed from the raw data: a homophilic graph, which enhances connections between similar nodes, and a heterophilic graph, which emphasizes connections between dissimilar nodes, using complementary relationships in both feature and topology spaces. A mixed filter is then applied to extract both low-frequency (homophilic) and high-frequency (heterophilic) information by combining filtered representations from both reconstructed graphs, controlled by a trade-off parameter. The filtered features are mapped into two separate subspaces—one for attributes and one for structure—using two independent MLP encoders, reducing adverse coupling between node features and topology. The resulting embeddings are concatenated and clustered using a decoder and a cluster assignment mechanism, with additional loss terms to prevent representation collapse and enhance cluster cohesion.
99c47cc8d02b2f8457e27ba4af72daa0210c55b2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 11 benchmark datasets, encompassing both homophilic and heterophilic graphs, such as Cora, Citeseer, ACM, AMAP, EAT (homophilic), and Texas, Cornell, Wisconsin, Washington, Twitch, Squirrel (heterophilic). The proposed method will be compared against 13 baseline methods, including GNN-based, contrastive learning, MLP-based, and shallow clustering approaches. Evaluation metrics will include clustering Accuracy (ACC) and Normalized Mutual Information (NMI). The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by adopting consistent hyperparameters and training protocols, such as using the Adam optimizer, tuning filter order and trade-off parameters, and running for a fixed number of epochs. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of the mixed filter and graph reconstruction components.
99c47cc8d02b2f8457e27ba4af72daa0210c55b2.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to address unsupervised node clustering on graphs without any prior knowledge of homophily, by reconstructing both homophilic and heterophilic structures in a fully unsupervised manner. The mixed filter is designed to jointly exploit low- and high-frequency components, making the method robust to both homophilic and heterophilic graphs. The dual-subspace mapping of node attributes and topology is introduced to reduce adverse coupling, further improving clustering quality. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the method achieves state-of-the-art or highly competitive performance across a wide range of graph types, validating its generalizability and effectiveness.

99c50f99c86d528e1a545deb9d2cae3bad13b8b8.title: OmniGen: Unified Image Generation
99c50f99c86d528e1a545deb9d2cae3bad13b8b8.research_question: Can a unified image generation model be developed that flexibly handles a wide range of image generation tasks—including text-to-image, image editing, subject-driven generation, and visual-conditional generation—within a single, simple framework, while supporting multi-modal instructions and effective knowledge transfer across tasks and domains?
99c50f99c86d528e1a545deb9d2cae3bad13b8b8.hypothesis: A unified diffusion-based model, trained on a large-scale, multi-task dataset with standardized input-output formats, can achieve competitive or superior performance across diverse image generation tasks, enable knowledge transfer to unseen domains, and simplify the workflow by eliminating the need for task-specific modules or intermediate steps.
99c50f99c86d528e1a545deb9d2cae3bad13b8b8.proposed_method: A novel image generation framework will be developed, consisting of a frozen Variational Autoencoder (VAE) for visual feature extraction and a large pre-trained transformer (initialized from a language model such as Phi-3) for unified multi-modal sequence modeling. The model will accept arbitrarily interleaved text and image inputs, tokenized via a text tokenizer and VAE-based patch embedding, and process them with a modified attention mechanism that applies causal attention across the sequence and bidirectional attention within image patches. Training will use a rectified flow objective to directly regress the target velocity between noisy and clean data, with weighted loss applied to edited image regions to prevent shortcut learning. The model will be trained in stages with progressively increasing image resolutions, leveraging a large-scale, standardized multi-task dataset (X2I) that covers text-to-image, image editing, subject-driven generation, visual-conditional tasks, and few-shot learning scenarios.
99c50f99c86d528e1a545deb9d2cae3bad13b8b8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple benchmarks, including GenEval for text-to-image generation, EMU-Edit and DreamBench for image editing and subject-driven generation, and datasets for controllable image generation (e.g., segmentation masks, Canny edges, depth maps). The model will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as Stable Diffusion (SD1.5, SD2.1, SDXL, SD3), DALL-E 2/3, IF-XL, ControlNet, and others, using evaluation metrics like CLIP similarity (text and image), mIoU, F1 score, SSIM, and RMSE. The experimental setup includes training on approximately 0.1 billion images across diverse tasks, using a staged resolution schedule and the AdamW optimizer on large-scale GPU clusters. Ablation studies will assess the impact of attention mechanisms, loss weighting, and input image representation strategies.
99c50f99c86d528e1a545deb9d2cae3bad13b8b8.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first unified image generation model capable of handling a broad spectrum of tasks end-to-end through multi-modal instructions, without requiring additional plugins, task-specific modules, or intermediate steps. The architecture is highly simplified, relying on only a VAE and a transformer, and supports flexible input formats. The work also presents the first comprehensive multi-task image generation dataset (X2I) with standardized formats, enabling effective knowledge transfer and emergent capabilities such as in-context learning and reasoning. The model demonstrates competitive or superior performance to specialized baselines, while being more parameter-efficient and user-friendly, and supports novel capabilities such as chain-of-thought reasoning and step-by-step image generation.

99e3383c186f38909191506549cec226a9f2eba5.title: Provably Efficient Exploration in Inverse Constrained Reinforcement Learning
99e3383c186f38909191506549cec226a9f2eba5.research_question: How can exploration in inverse constrained reinforcement learning (ICRL) be made provably efficient, particularly when the ground-truth constraints are unknown, time-varying, or context-dependent, and the transition dynamics and expert policy must be learned from interaction with the environment?
99e3383c186f38909191506549cec226a9f2eba5.hypothesis: Strategically designed exploration algorithms that explicitly minimize estimation errors in transition dynamics and expert policy can provably improve the efficiency and accuracy of constraint inference in ICRL, even in the absence of generative models or known dynamics.
99e3383c186f38909191506549cec226a9f2eba5.proposed_method: A novel exploration framework for ICRL is proposed, introducing two theoretically grounded algorithms: Bounded Error Aggregate Reduction (BEAR) and Policy-Constrained Strategic Exploration (PCSE). BEAR guides exploration by minimizing an upper bound on the aggregate estimation error of cost functions, using a reward function derived from current error estimates and solving an RL problem at each iteration. PCSE further constrains exploration by focusing on a set of candidate policies that are plausibly optimal, defined via value function closeness in both rewards and costs, and solves a constrained optimization problem to select the exploration policy. Both algorithms rely on iterative estimation of the transition model and expert policy using pseudo-counts from environment interaction, and update their exploration strategies based on confidence intervals derived from concentration inequalities. Rigorous sample complexity analyses are provided, linking estimation errors to the number of environment interactions and ensuring that the learned feasible constraint set is probably approximately correct (PAC) with respect to the true set.
99e3383c186f38909191506549cec226a9f2eba5.experiment_details: Empirical evaluation will be conducted in both discrete (e.g., Gridworld) and continuous (e.g., Point Maze) environments. The agent will be tasked with reaching target locations while adhering to unknown constraints, with the expert policy trained under ground-truth constraints and the proposed algorithms operating without access to these constraints. Datasets will be generated from environment interactions, and baselines will include random exploration, epsilon-greedy, maximum-entropy, and upper confidence bound strategies. Evaluation metrics will include discounted cumulative rewards (for optimality), discounted cumulative costs (for safety), and Weighted Generalized Intersection over Union (WGIoU) to assess the similarity between inferred and ground-truth constraints. Experiments will track convergence rates, sample efficiency, and the accuracy of constraint inference across multiple runs and environments.
99e3383c186f38909191506549cec226a9f2eba5.novelty_claims: The proposed framework departs from prior ICRL approaches by providing a set-recovery perspective, focusing on recovering the minimal set of feasible constraints rather than a single constraint function. The BEAR and PCSE algorithms are the first to provide strategic exploration with provable sample complexity guarantees in ICRL without relying on generative models or known dynamics. Theoretical contributions include explicit error propagation analysis, PAC-optimality criteria for constraint inference, and tractable sample complexity bounds. Empirical results demonstrate superior convergence and constraint recovery compared to existing exploration strategies, especially in environments with unknown or time-varying dynamics.

99eee47dad469790042b973bc7cb40cb63a660b1.title: DeepInception: Hypnotize Large Language Model to Be Jailbreaker
99eee47dad469790042b973bc7cb40cb63a660b1.research_question: Can large language models (LLMs) be manipulated to override their safety guardrails and generate harmful content through novel prompt engineering techniques that exploit their personification and imaginative capabilities, particularly under black-box settings?
99eee47dad469790042b973bc7cb40cb63a660b1.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by leveraging LLMs' personification abilities and constructing nested, multi-layered fictional scenarios, it is possible to induce a state of 'self-loss' in the model, thereby bypassing its safety constraints and enabling the generation of harmful or restricted content, even in black-box access scenarios.
99eee47dad469790042b973bc7cb40cb63a660b1.proposed_method: A new methodology, termed DeepInception, will be developed to conduct adversarial jailbreaks on LLMs. This approach constructs a multi-layered, nested prompt that instructs the LLM to imagine a scenario with multiple characters, each capable of creating their own sub-scenarios, recursively. The prompt template is parameterized by scene type, number of characters, number of layers, and a specified attack target (e.g., hacking instructions), with the narrative framed as a battle against an 'evil doctor' to further relax the model's moral constraints. The method exploits the LLM's ability to personify and follow complex, authority-driven instructions, progressively guiding the model to generate increasingly specific and practical harmful content. The process is designed to be universal, requiring no model retraining, extra data, or auxiliary models, and is applicable to both open-source and closed-source LLMs.
99eee47dad469790042b973bc7cb40cb63a660b1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both open-source (e.g., Llama-2, Llama-3, Falcon, Vicuna) and closed-source (e.g., GPT-3.5, GPT-4, GPT-4o, OpenAIo1) LLMs. The evaluation will use established adversarial jailbreak benchmarks such as AdvBench (520 harmful content objectives) and Jailbench (diverse policy-violating behaviors). Baseline comparisons will include black-box and white-box jailbreak methods such as PAIR, CipherChat, PAP, GCG, and AutoDAN. Harmfulness of generated content will be quantitatively assessed using Harmfulness Score (%) via automated evaluation with GPT-4 as a judge, and the ability to bypass output detectors (e.g., LlamaGuard, OpenAI detection API) will be tested. Ablation studies will analyze the effects of prompt complexity, number of characters, number of layers, and scene types. Multi-modal jailbreaks will also be explored by adapting the method to image-based prompts.
99eee47dad469790042b973bc7cb40cb63a660b1.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a lightweight, training-free, and universal jailbreak framework that exploits psychological mechanisms of obedience and self-loss, inspired by the Milgram experiment, to induce LLMs to bypass their safety guardrails. DeepInception is the first to formalize and empirically validate the effectiveness of nested, multi-layered personification prompts for continuous and adaptive jailbreaks in both black-box and white-box settings, across a wide range of LLMs and attack objectives. The approach demonstrates superior harmfulness rates compared to existing baselines, enables continual jailbreaks in subsequent interactions, and generalizes to multi-modal scenarios. The research also provides new insights into the vulnerabilities of LLMs and the limitations of current defense mechanisms.

9a12178bddbd22ce3ba04ffce1a2863f2b7b220f.title: OVTR: End-to-End Open-Vocabulary Multiple Object Tracking with Transformer
9a12178bddbd22ce3ba04ffce1a2863f2b7b220f.research_question: How can end-to-end multiple object tracking be extended to the open-vocabulary setting, enabling robust tracking and classification of both seen and unseen object categories in diverse and dynamic real-world video scenarios?
9a12178bddbd22ce3ba04ffce1a2863f2b7b220f.hypothesis: Integrating a category information propagation strategy, dual-branch Transformer architecture, and attention isolation mechanisms will enable stable, continuous, and generalizable open-vocabulary multiple object tracking, outperforming existing methods in both classification and tracking of novel categories.
9a12178bddbd22ce3ba04ffce1a2863f2b7b220f.proposed_method: A novel end-to-end open-vocabulary multiple object tracking framework based on a Transformer architecture will be developed. The method will employ a dual-branch decoder: one branch (OFA) aligns object queries with CLIP image embeddings for visual generalization, while the other branch (CTI) enables deep interaction with CLIP text embeddings for open-vocabulary classification. Category information propagation (CIP) will be introduced to transfer and aggregate category priors across video frames, enhancing temporal consistency in classification and tracking. Attention isolation strategies will be incorporated in the decoder to protect against interference between queries of different categories and between track and detect queries, using category and content isolation masks. The model will be optimized with multi-frame training, leveraging both detection and tracking losses, as well as an alignment loss to distill knowledge from CLIP image embeddings.
9a12178bddbd22ce3ba04ffce1a2863f2b7b220f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the TAO dataset for open-vocabulary tracking, using the LVIS dataset for training and evaluating on both base and novel categories. The evaluation will use the TETA metric, which separately measures localization, association, and classification accuracy in an open-vocabulary context. Zero-shot domain transfer experiments will be performed on the KITTI dataset to assess cross-dataset generalization, using CLEAR-MOT metrics such as MOTA and IDF1. Baselines will include state-of-the-art open-vocabulary trackers (e.g., OVTrack, MASA), as well as traditional trackers like DeepSORT and Tracktor++ with open-vocabulary detectors. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of each architectural component and strategy, with all models using a ResNet50 backbone and multi-frame training on 4 NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPUs.
9a12178bddbd22ce3ba04ffce1a2863f2b7b220f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first end-to-end open-vocabulary multiple object tracker that jointly models motion, appearance, and category information. It introduces a category information propagation (CIP) strategy for stable, continuous classification and tracking, and a dual-branch decoder that enables deep multimodal interaction and eliminates the need for time-consuming preprocessing. Attention isolation strategies are developed to ensure harmonious operation of classification and tracking, further enhancing generalization. The method achieves superior performance on open-vocabulary tracking benchmarks, demonstrates strong cross-domain adaptability, and significantly reduces inference time and preprocessing requirements compared to prior art.

9a1d94a930168918a1a1e1939b089d16d58d7865.title: A Kernel-Based View of Language Model Fine-Tuning
9a1d94a930168918a1a1e1939b089d16d58d7865.research_question: What theoretical framework can explain the empirical success and optimization dynamics of fine-tuning large pre-trained language models on downstream NLP tasks, especially in low-data regimes, and how does the inclusion of prompts or parameter-efficient subspace methods affect these dynamics?
9a1d94a930168918a1a1e1939b089d16d58d7865.hypothesis: Fine-tuning pre-trained language models on downstream tasks can often be described by kernel-based dynamics, particularly when tasks are formulated as masked word prediction problems through prompting. Furthermore, parameter-efficient subspace-based fine-tuning methods can be theoretically explained through a kernel lens, and the success of fine-tuning depends critically on the alignment between pre-training and downstream task formulations.
9a1d94a930168918a1a1e1939b089d16d58d7865.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted to extend the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) framework to the fine-tuning of pre-trained language models, accounting for both standard and prompt-based fine-tuning. The method will formalize and prove new kernel analogs for optimizers such as Adam, using the Tensor Programs framework to characterize conditions under which kernel-based dynamics emerge during early-stage fine-tuning. The approach will rigorously analyze the impact of prompt design and parameter initialization inherited from pre-training, and will derive kernel formulas that capture the optimization behavior of both full and subspace-based fine-tuning (e.g., LoRA). Theoretical results will be complemented by empirical tests to validate when and how kernel behavior manifests, including the development of metrics for linearization and fixed-feature properties.
9a1d94a930168918a1a1e1939b089d16d58d7865.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed on 14 diverse NLP tasks, including sentiment analysis, topic classification, natural language inference, and paraphrase detection, using few-shot settings (e.g., 16-shot and 64-shot) and pre-trained masked language models such as RoBERTa-base. Both standard and prompt-based fine-tuning paradigms will be evaluated, with manual prompt templates and multiple random seeds for dataset splits. Baselines will include full fine-tuning with SGD and Adam, as well as kernel regression using the derived kernel analogs (e.g., NTK, SignGD, A-SignGD). Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy or F1 score, and additional diagnostic metrics will measure the degree of kernel behavior (linearization and fixed features) during optimization. The efficacy of subspace-based fine-tuning methods (e.g., LoRA) will be analyzed by comparing their kernel analogs and performance to full fine-tuning.
9a1d94a930168918a1a1e1939b089d16d58d7865.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a rigorous extension of NTK theory to the fine-tuning of large language models with non-random, pre-trained initializations and modern optimizers such as Adam. It provides the first formal kernel analogs for Adam in the context of language model fine-tuning and establishes theoretical conditions under which prompt-based fine-tuning exhibits kernel behavior. The approach offers a principled explanation for the empirical success of parameter-efficient subspace-based fine-tuning methods via the Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma. Extensive empirical validation across a wide range of NLP tasks demonstrates when and why kernel-based dynamics arise, highlighting the critical role of prompt design and task formulation. This kernel-based perspective enables new theoretical and practical insights into the design and analysis of efficient fine-tuning strategies.

9a227e7014c89095b713bdd0263b13ec6d6256f4.title: On The Temporal Domain of Differential Equation Inspired Graph Neural Networks
9a227e7014c89095b713bdd0263b13ec6d6256f4.research_question: How can the temporal dynamics and order of differential equation-inspired graph neural networks (DE-GNNs) be learned in a data-driven manner to improve modeling of complex, potentially higher-order temporal dependencies in graph-structured data, including both stationary and spatio-temporal tasks?
9a227e7014c89095b713bdd0263b13ec6d6256f4.hypothesis: Learning the temporal order and dependencies of DE-GNNs from data, rather than relying on fixed first- or second-order temporal dynamics, enables the modeling of a broader class of temporal phenomena and leads to improved performance on graph-based tasks, particularly for non-homophilic and spatio-temporal datasets.
9a227e7014c89095b713bdd0263b13ec6d6256f4.proposed_method: A novel neural architecture, termed TDE-GNN, is proposed to learn both the temporal order and temporal dependency of the underlying ODEs governing GNN layers in a data-driven fashion. The method generalizes the temporal domain by introducing a learnable mechanism for the temporal coefficients in the discretization of higher-order ODEs, allowing the network to adaptively select the order of temporal dependencies up to a maximum order hyperparameter. Two parameterization strategies are considered: direct parameterization, where coefficients are learned and normalized, and an attention-based mechanism that leverages temporal attention to produce normalized, potentially signed coefficients. The architecture initializes hidden states appropriately for both stationary and spatio-temporal tasks, and updates node features at each layer using a weighted combination of previous states and a spatial operator (e.g., graph diffusion with channel mixing). Stability of the discretization is theoretically ensured by constraining the learned coefficients.
9a227e7014c89095b713bdd0263b13ec6d6256f4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both node classification and spatio-temporal node forecasting tasks using several benchmark datasets. For node classification, datasets include homophilic (Cora, Citeseer, Pubmed) and non-homophilic (Chameleon, Squirrel, Film) graphs, with standard splits and accuracy as the evaluation metric. For spatio-temporal forecasting, datasets such as Chickenpox-Hungary, PedalMe-London, and Wikipedia-Math will be used, with mean squared error (MSE) as the primary metric. Baselines will include general GNNs (e.g., GCN, GAT, GCNII), DE-inspired GNNs with fixed temporal order (e.g., GRAND, PDE-GCN, GRAND++, GREAD, CDE, FLODE), and temporal GNNs (e.g., DCRNN, GConvGRU, GC-LSTM, DyGrAE, EGCN-O, A3T-GCN, T-GCN, MPNNLSTM, AGCRN). A vanilla DE-GNN baseline with first-order temporal dynamics will be included to directly quantify the impact of the proposed temporal learning mechanism. Hyperparameters such as the order of the ODE will be selected via grid search, and ablation studies will be performed to analyze the effect of varying the temporal order and to interpret the learned coefficients.
9a227e7014c89095b713bdd0263b13ec6d6256f4.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to generalize the temporal domain of DE-GNNs by enabling data-driven learning of both the temporal order and dependencies, rather than restricting to pre-defined first- or second-order dynamics. The method introduces a flexible, interpretable mechanism for higher-order temporal modeling in GNNs, supported by both direct and attention-based parameterizations. The architecture is theoretically grounded with stability guarantees and is shown to bridge the gap between stationary and time-dependent graph neural networks. Empirical results demonstrate significant improvements over existing methods, especially on non-homophilic and spatio-temporal datasets, and provide interpretable insights into the underlying temporal processes.

9a43f64f053cf78e8ef61fe3e2bfb55a13f902db.title: Chernoff-Hoeffding Bounds for Markov Chains: Generalized and Simplified
9a43f64f053cf78e8ef61fe3e2bfb55a13f902db.research_question: Can large deviation (Chernoff-Hoeffding) bounds for sums of functions along random walks be established for general finite-state Markov chains, using mixing time or spectral properties as parameters, and can these bounds be generalized to both reversible and irreversible chains as well as to continuous-time settings?
9a43f64f053cf78e8ef61fe3e2bfb55a13f902db.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that tight Chernoff-Hoeffding-type concentration bounds can be derived for general finite-state Markov chains, parameterized by the chain's mixing time (in total variation distance), and that these bounds will hold for both reversible and irreversible chains, with possible extensions to continuous-time chains and arbitrary initial distributions.
9a43f64f053cf78e8ef61fe3e2bfb55a13f902db.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed to derive Chernoff-Hoeffding-type large deviation bounds for sums of bounded functions along random walks on general ergodic Markov chains. The approach will parameterize the bounds in terms of the L1 (total variation) mixing time of the chain, rather than relying solely on spectral expansion, thus capturing concentration phenomena even for irreversible chains where spectral gap may be misleading. The methodology will involve partitioning the random walk into sub-walks of length equal to the mixing time, analyzing the moment generating function of the sum via elementary linear algebraic techniques, and employing a recursive decomposition of the walk's distribution into parallel and perpendicular components relative to the stationary distribution. The analysis will avoid reliance on reversiblization or perturbation theory, instead tracing the evolution of the walk's distribution step by step, and will provide tight exponents up to constant factors. Extensions to continuous-time Markov chains and to walks starting from arbitrary initial distributions will be addressed by incorporating appropriate multiplicative correction factors.
9a43f64f053cf78e8ef61fe3e2bfb55a13f902db.experiment_details: Theoretical validation will be conducted through rigorous mathematical proofs and construction of explicit Markov chain examples to demonstrate the tightness of the derived bounds. Specific chains, such as two-state chains with tunable transition probabilities, will be used to show that the exponents in the proposed bounds are optimal up to constant factors. Comparisons will be made with existing spectral expansion-based bounds and with bounds obtained by union bounding over independent blocks. Theoretical results will be benchmarked against known mixing times and spectral gaps for various classes of chains, including both reversible and irreversible cases. Evaluation metrics will include the tightness of the exponent in the deviation probability, dependence on mixing time and spectral gap, and applicability to both discrete and continuous-time settings.
9a43f64f053cf78e8ef61fe3e2bfb55a13f902db.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first Chernoff-Hoeffding bounds for general (irreversible) finite-state Markov chains that are directly parameterized by the standard L1 mixing time, rather than spectral expansion. The framework provides tight, elementary, and unified proofs for both reversible and irreversible chains, and avoids the use of reversiblization or perturbation theory. The method generalizes to continuous-time chains and to arbitrary initial distributions, and achieves optimal exponents up to constant factors. The approach also yields a simplified and more insightful proof of spectral expansion-based bounds, and quantitatively improves upon previous elementary analyses by providing sharper dependence on the mean and mixing time.

9a4f03d132869db4a05c6789a4a1076575e2258b.title: Representation Surgery for Multi-Task Model Merging
9a4f03d132869db4a05c6789a4a1076575e2258b.research_question: How can the performance gap between traditional multi-task learning (MTL) and model merging-based MTL be closed, particularly in scenarios where raw training data is unavailable and only independently trained models are accessible?
9a4f03d132869db4a05c6789a4a1076575e2258b.hypothesis: Introducing a lightweight, task-specific module that operates in the representation space after model merging will reduce representation bias between merged and individual models, thereby improving the performance of merged multi-task models.
9a4f03d132869db4a05c6789a4a1076575e2258b.proposed_method: A novel representation surgery approach is proposed to address representation bias in model merging for multi-task learning. The method introduces a task-specific, lightweight module—implemented as an adapter-like structure with learnable up- and down-projection matrices and a ReLU activation—that takes the merged model's representations as input and outputs a bias correction. The module is trained in an unsupervised manner using unlabeled test data and individual models as self-supervised signals, minimizing the L1 distance between the representation of the merged model (after surgery) and the corresponding individual model's representation. This approach is model-agnostic, orthogonal to existing model merging algorithms, and can be seamlessly integrated with any merging scheme to filter out task-specific biases post-merging.
9a4f03d132869db4a05c6789a4a1076575e2258b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on eight diverse tasks/datasets: SUN397, Cars, RESISC45, EuroSAT, SVHN, GTSRB, MNIST, and DTD. Multiple model architectures will be evaluated, including ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16, and ViT-L/14, all based on the CLIP visual encoder. The proposed surgery module will be applied to several state-of-the-art model merging baselines, including Weight Averaging, FisherMerging, RegMean, Task Arithmetic, Ties-Merging, ConcreteTA, ConcreteAM, TWAdaMerging, and AdaMerging. Evaluation metrics will focus on average classification accuracy across all tasks, as well as quantitative measures of representation bias (L1 distance between merged and individual representations). The experimental setup will ensure that no raw training data is used during merging or surgery, and only unlabeled test data is leveraged for unsupervised optimization of the surgery module.
9a4f03d132869db4a05c6789a4a1076575e2258b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first post-merging, representation-space solution to the widespread problem of representation bias in model merging-based MTL. Unlike prior methods that operate in weight space or focus on pre- or during-merging interventions, the representation surgery module is orthogonal and complementary, directly targeting the discrepancy in feature distributions between merged and individual models. The method is lightweight, task-specific, and model-agnostic, requiring minimal additional parameters and no access to raw training data. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate significant improvements in MTL performance across a range of architectures and merging baselines, narrowing the gap to traditional MTL and individual model performance.

9a69880c0ce0b3511cc6a1b3c52b6eb5a514f6bb.title: Domain Watermark: Effective and Harmless Dataset Copyright Protection is Closed at Hand
9a69880c0ce0b3511cc6a1b3c52b6eb5a514f6bb.research_question: How can dataset ownership verification be achieved in a manner that is both effective and harmless, ensuring copyright protection for open-source datasets without introducing security risks or malicious behaviors into models trained on protected data?
9a69880c0ce0b3511cc6a1b3c52b6eb5a514f6bb.hypothesis: It is possible to design a dataset ownership verification method that is truly harmless by leveraging the generalization properties of deep neural networks, such that watermarked models can correctly classify certain 'hard' samples that benign models misclassify, without introducing backdoor vulnerabilities or malicious misclassification behaviors.
9a69880c0ce0b3511cc6a1b3c52b6eb5a514f6bb.proposed_method: A novel domain watermarking framework will be developed for dataset ownership verification. The approach begins by identifying a hardly-generalized domain for the original dataset, using a domain generator trained via bi-level optimization to minimize the mutual information between features of the source and target domains. This generator produces domain-watermarked samples that are visually indistinguishable from the originals but are challenging for benign models to classify correctly. To enhance stealthiness, a set of clean-label, visually-indistinguishable modified samples is further optimized to have similar effects as domain-watermarked samples. The protected dataset is then constructed by replacing a small subset of original samples with these optimized samples. Ownership verification is performed using a hypothesis-test-guided procedure, comparing model behaviors on benign and domain-watermarked samples to determine unauthorized dataset usage.
9a69880c0ce0b3511cc6a1b3c52b6eb5a514f6bb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on benchmark image classification datasets, including CIFAR-10 and Tiny-ImageNet, using standard architectures such as VGG and ResNet. The proposed method will be compared against seven baseline watermarking approaches, including both clean-label and poisoned-label backdoor-based methods (e.g., BadNets, Blended, WaNet, UBW-P, Label-Consistent, SleeperAgent, UBW-C). Evaluation metrics will include benign accuracy (BA), verification success rate (VSR), harmful degree (H), and relatively harmful degree (Ĥ). Additional experiments will assess the method's robustness to adaptive attacks such as fine-tuning and model pruning, and ablation studies will analyze the impact of key hyperparameters such as perturbation budget and watermarking rate.
9a69880c0ce0b3511cc6a1b3c52b6eb5a514f6bb.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first non-backdoor-based dataset ownership verification method, establishing a new research direction independent of backdoor attacks. The domain watermarking approach ensures harmlessness by enabling watermarked models to correctly classify 'hard' samples, rather than inducing misclassification. The method provides theoretical foundations for both the construction of domain watermarks and the verification process, and demonstrates strong resistance to adaptive attacks while maintaining high stealthiness and effectiveness. This framework advances the state of the art in dataset copyright protection by eliminating the inherent security risks of prior backdoor-based techniques.

9a7ac45eafe11ca003db3a300505f3b5c3f9009a.title: DetectGPT: Zero-Shot Machine-Generated Text Detection using Probability Curvature
9a7ac45eafe11ca003db3a300505f3b5c3f9009a.research_question: How can zero-shot detection of machine-generated text be improved by leveraging intrinsic properties of large language models' probability functions, without requiring supervised classifiers, labeled datasets, or explicit watermarking?
9a7ac45eafe11ca003db3a300505f3b5c3f9009a.hypothesis: Text generated by large language models tends to occupy regions of negative curvature in the model's log probability function, such that minor perturbations of model-generated text result in lower log probabilities, while human-written text does not consistently exhibit this property.
9a7ac45eafe11ca003db3a300505f3b5c3f9009a.proposed_method: A novel zero-shot detection algorithm is proposed that exploits the local curvature of a language model's log probability function. For a candidate passage, the method generates several minor perturbations using a generic pre-trained mask-filling model (such as T5), ensuring the perturbations remain semantically similar to the original. The log probability of the original passage under the suspected source model is compared to the average log probability of the perturbed passages, computing a normalized discrepancy score. If the original passage's log probability significantly exceeds that of its perturbations, the passage is classified as likely machine-generated. This approach does not require training a separate classifier, collecting labeled datasets, or modifying the generation process, and can be applied in a zero-shot manner to any model for which log probabilities can be computed.
9a7ac45eafe11ca003db3a300505f3b5c3f9009a.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on multiple datasets, including XSum (news articles), SQuAD (Wikipedia contexts), WritingPrompts (creative writing), WMT16 (multilingual news), and PubMedQA (medical QA). Model-generated samples are created using various large language models (GPT-2, GPT-Neo, GPT-J, GPT-NeoX, GPT-3, Jurassic-2 Jumbo) by prompting with the beginning of real texts. Baseline zero-shot detection methods include log probability thresholding, token rank/log-rank, and entropy-based approaches; supervised RoBERTa-based detectors are also compared. Evaluation is performed using AUROC, with 150-500 samples per experiment, and the method is tested under various conditions such as paraphrased model text, alternative decoding strategies (top-k, top-p), and black-box detection using surrogate models for scoring. Hyperparameters for perturbation (mask rate, span length) and mask-filling model size are systematically varied to assess robustness and performance.
9a7ac45eafe11ca003db3a300505f3b5c3f9009a.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new, unsupervised, zero-shot detection algorithm that leverages the curvature of a language model's log probability function, approximated via random semantic perturbations, to distinguish machine-generated from human-written text. This method does not require labeled data, supervised training, or explicit watermarking, and generalizes across domains, languages, and model sizes. Empirical results demonstrate that the approach achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot detection accuracy, outperforming existing unsupervised baselines and matching or exceeding supervised detectors in out-of-distribution settings. The work also provides a theoretical connection between perturbation discrepancy and the trace of the log probability Hessian, offering a new perspective on the detection of machine-generated text.

9aa01997226b5c4d705ae2e2f52c32681006654b.title: MVDream: Multi-view Diffusion for 3D Generation
9aa01997226b5c4d705ae2e2f52c32681006654b.research_question: How can consistent and generalizable multi-view images be generated from text prompts to serve as a strong 3D prior for high-quality, robust 3D object generation, overcoming the limitations of existing 2D-lifting and 3D generative methods?
9aa01997226b5c4d705ae2e2f52c32681006654b.hypothesis: A diffusion model trained on both 2D and 3D multi-view data, with architectural modifications for cross-view consistency and camera conditioning, will enable the generation of multi-view consistent images from text prompts, resulting in improved 3D object generation quality and stability compared to current 2D-lifting approaches.
9aa01997226b5c4d705ae2e2f52c32681006654b.proposed_method: A multi-view diffusion model will be developed by fine-tuning a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model (such as Stable Diffusion v2.1) on a combination of large-scale 2D image-text pairs and 3D-rendered multi-view datasets. The architecture will be modified by inflating the 2D self-attention layers into 3D self-attention, enabling cross-view information sharing, and by incorporating camera parameter embeddings via a two-layer MLP, injected as residuals into time embeddings. The training will alternate between standard 2D image generation and multi-view image generation, using a joint loss that encourages both generalizability and multi-view consistency. The resulting model will be used as a 3D prior in Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) pipelines, where camera parameters are provided as inputs and multi-view supervision is leveraged to optimize 3D representations (e.g., NeRFs) from text prompts.
9aa01997226b5c4d705ae2e2f52c32681006654b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Objaverse dataset for 3D-rendered multi-view images and the LAION dataset for 2D image-text pairs. The model will be evaluated on three main tasks: multi-view image generation (assessing image quality and cross-view consistency), text-to-3D generation using multi-view SDS (evaluating 3D asset quality and stability), and personalized 3D generation via a DreamBooth-style fine-tuning. Baselines will include state-of-the-art 2D-lifting and 3D generative methods such as Dreamfusion, Magic3D, Text2Mesh, and ProlificDreamer, with quantitative metrics including FID, Inception Score, and CLIP score for image evaluation, and user studies for 3D model preference. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of architectural choices (attention modules, camera embeddings) and training strategies (number of views, negative prompts, timestep annealing, CFG rescale).
9aa01997226b5c4d705ae2e2f52c32681006654b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first multi-view diffusion model capable of generating consistent multi-view images from text prompts, serving as a generalizable and representation-agnostic 3D prior. Key innovations include the use of inflated 3D self-attention for cross-view consistency, camera parameter conditioning, and joint training on both 2D and 3D data. The method demonstrates superior multi-view consistency, robustness, and generalizability compared to existing 2D-lifting and 3D generative models, and enables few-shot personalized 3D generation through a streamlined multi-view DreamBooth pipeline.

9ab0feba4adbb723ea0685b2ee3ac29b4c08349e.title: Principled Approaches for Learning to Defer with Multiple Experts
9ab0feba4adbb723ea0685b2ee3ac29b4c08349e.research_question: How can learning to defer decisions to multiple experts be formulated and optimized in a principled way, and what theoretical guarantees can be established for such methods in multi-class classification settings?
9ab0feba4adbb723ea0685b2ee3ac29b4c08349e.hypothesis: Surrogate loss functions specifically designed for the multiple-expert learning-to-defer scenario, when minimized jointly over prediction and deferral functions, can yield strong, hypothesis-set-specific consistency guarantees (H-consistency bounds) and improved generalization compared to previous approaches.
9ab0feba4adbb723ea0685b2ee3ac29b4c08349e.proposed_method: A new family of surrogate loss functions will be formulated for the learning-to-defer scenario with multiple experts, where both prediction and deferral functions are learned simultaneously. The surrogate losses will generalize the standard multi-class classification loss by incorporating expert-specific deferral costs, allowing the learner to either predict a class or defer to one of several experts. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to prove that these surrogate losses admit H-consistency bounds, which are stronger and more relevant than classical Bayes-consistency, as they are hypothesis-set-specific and non-asymptotic. The minimizability gap, a finer measure than the approximation error, will be incorporated into the analysis to provide tighter guarantees. Several practical surrogate losses (e.g., logistic, sum, constrained losses) will be instantiated within this framework, and explicit consistency guarantees will be derived for each.
9ab0feba4adbb723ea0685b2ee3ac29b4c08349e.experiment_details: Empirical evaluation will be conducted on standard image classification datasets such as SVHN and CIFAR-10. The experiments will compare system accuracy for learned predictor and deferral pairs under varying numbers and types of experts (e.g., single expert, two experts with different model sizes, three experts with small, medium, and large models). Two types of expert cost functions will be considered: one based solely on expert misclassification error, and another combining misclassification error with a base cost reflecting inference cost. Baselines will include previous learning-to-defer methods and mixture-of-experts approaches. Evaluation metrics will focus on overall system accuracy, and experiments will be repeated with multiple random seeds to assess robustness.
9ab0feba4adbb723ea0685b2ee3ac29b4c08349e.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled, first-principles derivation of surrogate losses tailored for the multiple-expert learning-to-defer scenario, extending beyond prior work focused on single experts. Theoretical contributions include the establishment of H-consistency bounds for these new surrogate losses, providing stronger, hypothesis-set-specific guarantees and finite-sample generalization bounds. The analysis incorporates the minimizability gap, yielding tighter and more favorable guarantees than traditional excess error bounds. The approach is broadly applicable to a variety of surrogate loss functions and expert cost structures, and is supported by both theoretical and empirical results.

9ab904669c4aeb349b9f573053ff82608dd226a1.title: Follow the Rules: Reasoning for Video Anomaly Detection with Large Language Models
9ab904669c4aeb349b9f573053ff82608dd226a1.research_question: How can video anomaly detection be enhanced to provide interpretable, trustworthy, and adaptable reasoning, particularly in one-class (unsupervised) settings where only normal data is available for training?
9ab904669c4aeb349b9f573053ff82608dd226a1.hypothesis: A rule-based reasoning framework leveraging large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs), guided by few-shot normal samples, can achieve state-of-the-art video anomaly detection performance while providing interpretable rationales and fast adaptation to new domains.
9ab904669c4aeb349b9f573053ff82608dd226a1.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a two-stage rule-based reasoning framework, AnomalyRuler, for video anomaly detection using LLMs. In the induction stage, a VLM generates textual descriptions of a few normal reference frames, which are then used by an LLM to induce rules distinguishing normal and anomalous patterns; rule aggregation via a voting mechanism ensures robustness to perception and generation errors. In the deduction stage, the system processes continuous frames from test videos, applies the same VLM for frame descriptions, and uses Exponential Majority Smoothing to enforce temporal consistency and correct perception errors. Finally, a robust reasoning module uses the LLM to validate anomaly predictions against the induced rules, leveraging dummy answers and rechecking mechanisms for reliable output. This pipeline is designed to require only a few normal samples for adaptation, avoiding costly full-shot training or fine-tuning.
9ab904669c4aeb349b9f573053ff82608dd226a1.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on four benchmark video anomaly detection datasets: UCSD Ped2, CUHK Avenue, ShanghaiTech, and UBnormal. The method is evaluated using standard metrics such as Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC), accuracy, precision, recall, and the Doubly-Right metric for reasoning ability, with frame-level ground truth labels. Baselines include direct prompting of LLMs, video-based LLMs, and adaptations of recent LLM/VLM-based anomaly detection methods. The implementation uses CogVLM-17B as the VLM, GPT-4-1106-Preview for induction, and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 for deduction, with hyperparameters set for rule aggregation and smoothing. Ablation studies are performed to assess the contribution of each module and hyperparameter settings.
9ab904669c4aeb349b9f573053ff82608dd226a1.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to introduce rule-based reasoning for one-class video anomaly detection, enabling interpretable detection rationales. It utilizes a novel few-normal-shot prompting approach for rule induction, eliminating the need for full-shot training or fine-tuning and enabling rapid adaptation to new scenarios. The integration of rule aggregation, perception smoothing, and robust reasoning strategies further enhances detection robustness, leading to state-of-the-art performance, improved reasoning ability, and strong domain adaptability. The framework is generic and compatible with both open- and closed-source VLM/LLM backbones.

9ad4911a7923e19df9fb36cd03de5a63cb86ba63.title: Graph Prompt Learning: A Comprehensive Survey and Beyond
9ad4911a7923e19df9fb36cd03de5a63cb86ba63.research_question: How can prompt learning be systematically developed and leveraged to enhance the generalization, flexibility, and expressiveness of artificial general intelligence (AGI) models when applied to graph data, across different modalities, domains, and tasks?
9ad4911a7923e19df9fb36cd03de5a63cb86ba63.hypothesis: Prompt learning, when systematically adapted to graph data, enables more flexible and efficient transfer of knowledge from pre-trained graph models to diverse downstream tasks and domains, overcoming the limitations of traditional fine-tuning and improving performance in cross-modal, cross-domain, and cross-task settings.
9ad4911a7923e19df9fb36cd03de5a63cb86ba63.proposed_method: A unified framework for graph prompt learning will be developed, encompassing the design of prompt tokens, token structures, and insertion patterns tailored for graph data. The approach will categorize and analyze prompt integration strategies, such as adding learnable prompt vectors to node features, concatenating prompt tokens with node sets, and constructing virtual prompt nodes or subgraphs. The method will explore both handcrafted and learnable answering functions to align downstream tasks with pre-training objectives, and will investigate prompt tuning techniques including meta-learning, task-specific tuning, and tuning in line with pretext tasks. The framework will be implemented in a modular Python library (ProG) to facilitate extensible experimentation and deployment.
9ad4911a7923e19df9fb36cd03de5a63cb86ba63.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a comprehensive suite of graph datasets spanning node-level, edge-level, and graph-level tasks, including benchmarks from molecular property prediction, citation networks, and social graphs. Baseline comparisons will include traditional fine-tuning of pre-trained graph neural networks, shallow embedding methods, and recent graph prompt learning approaches. Evaluation metrics will cover classification accuracy, link prediction AUC, and graph classification F1 scores, as well as efficiency metrics such as parameter complexity and training time. The experimental setup will systematically vary prompt design choices, insertion patterns, and tuning strategies to assess their impact on transferability, flexibility, and expressiveness.
9ad4911a7923e19df9fb36cd03de5a63cb86ba63.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first unified and comprehensive framework for graph prompt learning, systematically categorizing prompt design and integration strategies for graph data. It provides novel insights into the interplay between prompt flexibility and model expressiveness, and establishes a taxonomy aligning over 100 existing methods with pre-training objectives at multiple graph levels. The research will deliver an open-source Python library and curated resource website to support reproducibility and accelerate progress in graph prompting. The framework aims to set a new standard for evaluating and deploying prompt-based methods in AGI applications involving graph data.

9ae6a6843b9a875e24fff423a3d339636511756a.title: ASIC: Aligning Sparse in-the-wild Image Collections
9ae6a6843b9a875e24fff423a3d339636511756a.research_question: How can dense and globally consistent pixel-level correspondences be established across small, sparse, in-the-wild image collections of an object or object category, without relying on ground-truth keypoint annotations or large labeled datasets?
9ae6a6843b9a875e24fff423a3d339636511756a.hypothesis: It is possible to recover accurate, dense, and globally consistent correspondences across small, unannotated image collections by leveraging pseudo-correspondences derived from pre-trained self-supervised vision models and optimizing a neural alignment network with novel self-supervised objectives.
9ae6a6843b9a875e24fff423a3d339636511756a.proposed_method: A framework is proposed that takes a small collection (approximately 10-30) of in-the-wild images of an object or object category and computes a dense, globally consistent mapping between all images in a self-supervised manner. The method begins by extracting sparse pseudo-correspondences using mutual nearest neighbors in the feature space of a pre-trained Vision Transformer (ViT) model (e.g., DINO). These sparse matches are used as noisy keypoints, which are then densified and refined by training a fully-convolutional U-Net alignment network from scratch for each collection. This network predicts, for each pixel, a mapping to a shared, learned canonical grid. The training objective includes a novel contrastive loss to align semantic keypoints, a geometric equivariance loss to enforce consistency under synthetic transformations, a reconstruction loss using a differentiable warp from the canonical grid, and auxiliary regularizations such as total variation and part consistency losses. The canonical grid is parameterized to store both color and foreground probability, enabling image and mask reconstruction.
9ae6a6843b9a875e24fff423a3d339636511756a.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on multiple real-world datasets, including SPair-71k (18 categories), PF-Willow (4 categories), CUB-200 (3 categories), and SAMURAI (5 collections), covering both rigid and non-rigid objects. For each dataset, small collections of 10-30 images are used per object/category, and the alignment network is trained from scratch on each collection. Baselines include both supervised and unsupervised semantic correspondence methods, such as VGG+MLS, DINO+MLS, DINO+NN, PSCNet-SE, and Neural Congealing, as well as GAN-based and classical approaches. Evaluation metrics include PCK@0.1 (percentage of correct keypoints), PCK@0.05, and a novel k-CyPCK metric to assess keypoint consistency over sequences of images. Both quantitative and qualitative results are reported, with ablation studies on loss components and hyperparameters.
9ae6a6843b9a875e24fff423a3d339636511756a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a test-time optimization framework for dense, globally consistent alignment of small, in-the-wild image collections without any manual annotations. Key innovations include the use of noisy, sparse pseudo-correspondences from self-supervised ViT features as training signals, a novel contrastive loss for joint alignment, and several auxiliary regularization terms to ensure dense and smooth mappings. Additionally, a new evaluation metric (k-CyPCK) is proposed to measure correspondence consistency across image sequences. The method demonstrates state-of-the-art performance among unsupervised and weakly supervised approaches, especially in low-shot settings and for objects with significant intra-class variation.

9ae8a940451fd24d87c278324531f36206b492a1.title: The Benefits of Reusing Batches for Gradient Descent in Two-Layer Networks: Breaking the Curse of Information and Leap Exponents
9ae8a940451fd24d87c278324531f36206b492a1.research_question: How does reusing data batches during gradient descent training affect the learnability of multi-index target functions in two-layer neural networks, particularly in high-dimensional settings, and can this approach overcome known theoretical limitations associated with single-pass training protocols?
9ae8a940451fd24d87c278324531f36206b492a1.hypothesis: Reusing data batches multiple times during gradient descent enables two-layer neural networks to efficiently learn a broader class of multi-index target functions in finite time, surpassing the limitations imposed by the information and leap exponents that constrain single-pass or gradient flow methods.
9ae8a940451fd24d87c278324531f36206b492a1.proposed_method: A detailed theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted on the training dynamics of two-layer neural networks using multi-pass gradient descent, where the same batch of data is reused across multiple iterations. The analysis will focus on high-dimensional synthetic Gaussian data, with target functions defined as multi-index models dependent on a low-dimensional subspace. The methodology will leverage Dynamical Mean Field Theory (DMFT) to rigorously characterize the evolution of low-dimensional projections of the network's weights and to derive closed-form integro-differential equations describing the learning process. The approach will include symmetric initialization of the network, fixed second-layer weights, and learning of the first-layer weights via gradient descent with explicit regularization. Theoretical results will be supported by numerical simulations to validate the predictions and to illustrate the impact of batch reuse on the learnability of various classes of target functions.
9ae8a940451fd24d87c278324531f36206b492a1.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed using high-dimensional synthetic datasets, where input data are i.i.d. Gaussian vectors and labels are generated by multi-index target functions. The setup will include two-layer neural networks with varying numbers of hidden units, ReLU or other analytic activation functions, and large batch sizes proportional to the input dimension. Both single-pass and multi-pass gradient descent protocols will be compared, with the latter reusing the same batch for multiple iterations. Evaluation metrics will include the overlap (scalar product) between learned weights and the teacher subspace, as well as the ability to recover orthogonal directions. Baselines will include single-pass SGD and gradient flow on population loss. Simulations will be averaged over multiple runs (e.g., 32) and conducted for various target functions characterized by different information and leap exponents. Theoretical predictions from DMFT will be compared to empirical results to assess the validity and generalization of the findings.
9ae8a940451fd24d87c278324531f36206b492a1.novelty_claims: The proposed research claims to break the theoretical barriers imposed by the information and leap exponents for single-pass training by demonstrating that multi-pass gradient descent can efficiently learn a much broader class of target functions in finite time, often in as few as two iterations. It provides a rigorous DMFT-based analysis of the dynamics of batch reuse, offering closed-form characterizations and theoretical guarantees for the correlated samples regime. The work identifies and characterizes the subspaces of functions that remain hard to learn due to inherent symmetries, and it disproves recent conjectures regarding the limitations of batch reuse. The approach also reveals a new mechanism of 'hidden progress' in representation learning, showing that gradient descent implicitly performs transformations that allow learning beyond the reach of standard statistical query bounds.

9af8258f773c46b50eb7a61ff99d2c92882116a2.title: Variational quantum simulation: a case study for understanding warm starts
9af8258f773c46b50eb7a61ff99d2c92882116a2.research_question: How can the trainability of variational quantum algorithms, particularly in the presence of barren plateaus, be improved through initialization strategies such as warm starts, and what are the theoretical and practical limitations of these approaches in iterative quantum simulation and related tasks?
9af8258f773c46b50eb7a61ff99d2c92882116a2.hypothesis: Warm start strategies, where parameterized quantum circuits are initialized near previous solutions, can provide regions of substantial gradients and approximate convexity in the loss landscape, thereby mitigating the barren plateau phenomenon and enabling efficient training for polynomially many time-steps in iterative variational quantum algorithms.
9af8258f773c46b50eb7a61ff99d2c92882116a2.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and numerical investigation will be conducted into the trainability of iterative variational quantum algorithms employing warm start initialization. The proposed method focuses on simulating quantum real-time evolution by iteratively compressing circuit depth, where at each iteration, the circuit parameters are initialized near the previous optimum and trained to approximate a slightly longer evolution. Analytical bounds will be derived to characterize the variance of the loss function and the convexity of the landscape in regions around the initialization, with explicit dependence on system size, time-step, and ansatz expressivity. The study will also introduce and analyze the concept of adiabatic minima, examining under what conditions these minima remain within trainable regions as the algorithm progresses. Extensions to other iterative quantum tasks, such as imaginary time evolution and unitary learning, will be considered using a generalized fidelity-based loss framework.
9af8258f773c46b50eb7a61ff99d2c92882116a2.experiment_details: Experiments will involve both theoretical analysis and numerical simulations. Numerical studies will use hardware-efficient and Hamiltonian variational ansatzes to simulate quantum systems of varying sizes (e.g., 4-14 qubits) under real and imaginary time evolution. The loss landscape will be explored by sampling parameter regions of varying widths around initialization points, and by varying the time-step size. Key metrics will include the variance of the loss function, gradient magnitudes, and convexity diagnostics (e.g., Hessian eigenvalues). Baseline comparisons will include random initialization and small-angle initialization strategies. Additional experiments will investigate the existence of gradient flows (fertile valleys) connecting minima that 'jump' outside the guaranteed trainable region, and the scalability of the approach as system size increases.
9af8258f773c46b50eb7a61ff99d2c92882116a2.novelty_claims: The proposed research will provide the first rigorous, general analytic lower bounds on the variance of the loss landscape and convexity guarantees for iterative variational quantum algorithms with warm starts, applicable to a broad class of parameterized circuits and loss functions. It will introduce the concept of adiabatic minima in this context and establish conditions under which these minima remain in trainable regions for polynomially many steps. The work will also generalize the analysis to other iterative quantum algorithms with fidelity-based losses, offering a unified theoretical framework for understanding warm start strategies and their limitations. Numerical evidence will be provided for the existence of gradient flows between minima, even when minima jump outside the initial trainable region, highlighting both the potential and the open challenges for scaling variational quantum algorithms.

9b010c25b4cc826919eb9b07055c8f644cf1a756.title: Generative Latent Coding for Ultra-Low Bitrate Image Compression
9b010c25b4cc826919eb9b07055c8f644cf1a756.research_question: How can image compression at ultra-low bitrates be achieved while maintaining both high realism and high fidelity, particularly in a way that aligns with human perception rather than pixel-space distortion?
9b010c25b4cc826919eb9b07055c8f644cf1a756.hypothesis: Encoding and compressing images in the latent space of a generative vector-quantized variational auto-encoder (VQ-VAE), rather than in pixel space, will enable ultra-low bitrate image compression that better preserves perceptual quality and semantic consistency. Incorporating a categorical hyper module and code-prediction-based supervision will further reduce bitrates and enhance visual quality.
9b010c25b4cc826919eb9b07055c8f644cf1a756.proposed_method: A novel Generative Latent Coding (GLC) framework is developed, which first encodes input images into a perception-aligned latent space using a generative VQ-VAE. Transform coding is then performed directly in this latent space, utilizing an analysis transform to produce codes, which are quantized and entropy-coded. A categorical hyper module is introduced to model the distribution of hyper-latents with a discrete codebook, capturing high-level semantic information and reducing bitrates compared to factorized priors. Additionally, a code-prediction-based supervision mechanism is employed during training, requiring the latent representations to predict VQ-indices, thereby enhancing semantic consistency. The training process is staged: first, the VQ-VAE is trained for a perceptual latent space; second, the transform coding module is trained with code-prediction-based supervision; finally, the entire network is jointly fine-tuned with pixel-space supervision for optimal compression performance.
9b010c25b4cc826919eb9b07055c8f644cf1a756.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both natural and facial image compression tasks. For natural images, the model is trained on ImageNet and OpenImages, and evaluated on the CLIC2020 test set using original resolutions. For facial images, training is performed on FFHQ and evaluation on CelebAHQ at 512x512 resolution. Baselines include traditional codecs (VVC), neural codecs (TCM, EVC), and state-of-the-art generative codecs (FCC, Text+Sketch, HiFiC, MS-ILLM). Evaluation metrics include bits per pixel (bpp), perceptual metrics (LPIPS, DISTS), no-reference metrics (FID, KID), and pixel-level metrics (PSNR, MS-SSIM). Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of transform coding, the categorical hyper module, and code-prediction-based supervision. Additional applications such as image restoration and style transfer are demonstrated by modifying the encoder or decoder within the GLC pipeline.
9b010c25b4cc826919eb9b07055c8f644cf1a756.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a generative latent coding paradigm that shifts the compression process from pixel space to the generative latent space of a VQ-VAE, resulting in better alignment with human perception at ultra-low bitrates. The categorical hyper module is claimed to significantly reduce the bit cost of hyper-information by focusing on semantic elements rather than low-level details. The code-prediction-based supervision is presented as a new training strategy that enhances semantic consistency without introducing inference-time bottlenecks. The framework achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks, including a 45% bitrate reduction on CLIC2020 at equivalent FID to previous methods, and demonstrates versatility for downstream vision tasks such as restoration and style transfer.

9b062975354e71841f54c65af2a89330061fe9ba.title: MeCeFO: Enhancing LLM Training Robustness via Fault-Tolerant Optimization
9b062975354e71841f54c65af2a89330061fe9ba.research_question: How can the robustness and efficiency of large language model (LLM) training be improved in distributed environments subject to frequent hardware failures, while minimizing additional computational and memory overhead?
9b062975354e71841f54c65af2a89330061fe9ba.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a fault-tolerant optimization algorithm, which strategically relaxes exact computation requirements and incorporates memory- and computation-efficient mechanisms, can maintain model performance and throughput under frequent hardware failures with significantly reduced overhead compared to existing fault-tolerant methods.
9b062975354e71841f54c65af2a89330061fe9ba.proposed_method: A new algorithm, Memory-and Computation-efficient Fault-tolerant Optimization (MeCeFO), will be developed to enhance the robustness of LLM training in distributed settings. The method employs a neighbor-do-both (NDB) strategy, where, upon node failure, a neighboring node within the same data parallel (DP) group assumes the failed node's workload. To address the resulting memory and computation bottlenecks, three core techniques are integrated: (1) a deterministic skip-connection mechanism that omits the multi-head attention (MHA) module during backpropagation for memory and computation savings; (2) selective activation recomputation in feedforward network (FFN) modules, where only input activations are stored and intermediate activations are recomputed as needed; and (3) a low-rank gradient approximation for FFN weight matrices, using singular value decomposition (SVD) and periodic projection matrix updates to reduce the computational cost of gradient calculation. These techniques are selectively applied only during failure recovery, ensuring that efficiency gains do not compromise standard training performance.
9b062975354e71841f54c65af2a89330061fe9ba.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a 32-GPU cluster (four nodes with eight NVIDIA A100 GPUs each), using LLaMA models of various sizes (350M, 1B, and 7B parameters) pre-trained on the C4 dataset. Three failure scenarios will be simulated, varying in failure frequency and node recovery time (low, medium, and high frequency). The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines Bamboo and Oobleck, utilizing their public implementations. Evaluation metrics will include training throughput (tokens per second), throughput degradation under faults, validation perplexity, zero-shot performance on tasks such as BoolQ, ARC-Easy, PIQA, and TruthfulQA-MC2, and fine-tuning results on the GLUE benchmark. The experimental setup will assess both efficiency and model quality under varying fault intensities.
9b062975354e71841f54c65af2a89330061fe9ba.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first fault-tolerant optimization algorithm for LLM training that integrates memory- and computation-efficient techniques specifically for failure handling, rather than relying solely on system-level redundancy or checkpointing. Key innovations include the deterministic skip-connection for MHA layers, selective activation recomputation for FFN modules, and a novel low-rank gradient approximation to offset recomputation overhead. The method achieves theoretical convergence rates matching standard distributed SGD, and empirical results indicate significantly improved throughput and resilience (5.0× to 6.7× greater than prior state-of-the-art) under high failure rates, with minimal impact on model performance.

9b0ae838c3fd625b8e6122953028e30db53a2f28.title: CF-VLM:CounterFactual Vision-Language Fine-tuning
9b0ae838c3fd625b8e6122953028e30db53a2f28.research_question: How can vision-language models be enhanced to achieve fine-grained discrimination and robust causal reasoning, particularly in scenarios requiring sensitivity to minimal semantic changes and reliable factual grounding?
9b0ae838c3fd625b8e6122953028e30db53a2f28.hypothesis: Incorporating targeted counterfactual image-text pairs and specialized training objectives into the fine-tuning process of vision-language models will significantly improve their ability to perform fine-grained causal reasoning, semantic discrimination, and reduce visual hallucinations, compared to existing contrastive or negative-sampling-based approaches.
9b0ae838c3fd625b8e6122953028e30db53a2f28.proposed_method: A novel fine-tuning framework, Counterfactual Vision-Language Fine-tuning (CF-VLM), will be developed to enhance the causal reasoning capabilities of vision-language models. The approach introduces structured counterfactual samples, generated by applying minimal but semantically crucial edits to both images and texts, resulting in logically coherent yet factually distinct scenarios. Three complementary training objectives will be integrated: (1) maintaining foundational cross-modal alignment using a contrastive loss, (2) enforcing the uniqueness and stability of factual scene representations against complete counterfactual scenarios via a scenario discrimination hinge loss, and (3) sharpening the model’s sensitivity to minimal causal edits through a fine-grained causal discrimination loss that targets the hardest negative counterfactuals. The losses will be combined in a weighted sum, with hyperparameters balancing their contributions. Counterfactual data will be systematically generated using prompt engineering for texts and a fine-tuned diffusion model for images, ensuring both attribute-level and relationship-level interventions are represented.
9b0ae838c3fd625b8e6122953028e30db53a2f28.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using large-scale vision-language models such as Qwen-VL (7B) and CLIP-ViT-B/32, with pretraining and fine-tuning performed on filtered CC12M (8.6M pairs) and CC3M (2.6M pairs) datasets, optionally including MSCOCO Captions. For each factual image-text pair, a counterfactual sample will be generated, effectively doubling the training data. Evaluation will be carried out on compositional reasoning and generalization benchmarks, including ConMe, ARO, VL-Checklist, ImageNet-1k (zero-shot classification), and MSCOCO/Flickr30k (zero-shot retrieval). Baselines will include zero-shot and standard fine-tuned models, text-negative fine-tuning, CLIP-based models (TripletCLIP, CE-CLIP+, COGT-CLIP, NegCLIP, Structure-CLIP), and LLM-based VLMs (LLaVA-1.5, InstructBLIP, MiniGPT-4). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, Recall@k, and top-1/top-5 accuracy, as well as hallucination-specific metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1) on POPE and MME benchmarks. Ablation studies will assess the impact of counterfactual types, data quantity, and individual loss components.
9b0ae838c3fd625b8e6122953028e30db53a2f28.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a joint image-text counterfactual fine-tuning strategy that targets causal decision points, going beyond coarse-grained similarity to explicitly model semantic shifts caused by minimal edits. The integration of three complementary loss functions enables multi-level semantic supervision, enhancing both compositional reasoning and factual consistency. The approach systematically generates and leverages counterfactual data for both attribute and relationship-level interventions, resulting in improved robustness, generalization, and reduced hallucinations compared to state-of-the-art baselines. This methodology establishes a new paradigm for deploying vision-language models in high-stakes, real-world scenarios requiring reliable reasoning and interpretability.

9b47d4ca2da54c116e1e39ea08712d9511db2d9e.title: Dynamic Negative Guidance of Diffusion Models
9b47d4ca2da54c116e1e39ea08712d9511db2d9e.research_question: How can diffusion models be guided to avoid generating undesired features or classes in a more theoretically principled and effective manner, particularly in text-to-image and class-removal tasks, without sacrificing image quality or diversity?
