9b47d4ca2da54c116e1e39ea08712d9511db2d9e.hypothesis: A dynamic, time- and state-dependent negative guidance scheme for diffusion models, which modulates the guidance strength based on the estimated posterior probability of undesired features, will outperform conventional static negative prompting methods in terms of safety, class balance, and image quality, while reducing unnecessary alterations to generated samples.
9b47d4ca2da54c116e1e39ea08712d9511db2d9e.proposed_method: A novel Dynamic Negative Guidance (DNG) framework will be developed for diffusion models. This approach replaces the conventional static negative guidance scale with a dynamic, time- and state-dependent scale, proportional to the posterior probability of the 'forbidden class' during the denoising process. The method estimates the posterior class probability at each diffusion step by tracking the discrete Markov chain, using both unconditional and negatively conditioned noise predictions. The guidance scale vanishes when the posterior for the forbidden class is low, ensuring that repulsive guidance is only active when necessary. The algorithm will be implemented without requiring additional training of the diffusion model, relying instead on efficient posterior estimation and dynamic modulation of the guidance term.
9b47d4ca2da54c116e1e39ea08712d9511db2d9e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on class removal tasks using the MNIST and CIFAR10 datasets. The proposed DNG method will be compared against baseline approaches, including Negative Prompting (NP) and Safe Latent Diffusion (SLD). Evaluation metrics will include safety (percentage of forbidden class images generated), KL-divergence between the generated and ideal class distributions, and Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for image quality and diversity. For text-to-image tasks, Stable Diffusion 2 will be used with both related and unrelated negative prompts, and the CLIP-score (cosine similarity between CLIP embeddings of guided and unguided images) will be measured to assess the degree of unintended image alteration. Experiments will include ablation over guidance scale and prompt relationships, and results will be averaged over multiple seeds and prompts.
9b47d4ca2da54c116e1e39ea08712d9511db2d9e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a theoretically grounded, dynamic negative guidance scheme for diffusion models that adaptively modulates the guidance strength based on the estimated posterior probability of undesired features. Unlike traditional negative prompting, this method ensures guidance is only active when necessary, reducing unnecessary changes to generated samples and preserving diversity. The method requires no additional training and is compatible with existing diffusion architectures. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior safety, class balance, and image quality compared to existing negative guidance methods.

9b4d0b3e1af3c6dc3f99b27dab89bf884c7a5997.title: Is a Modular Architecture Enough?
9b4d0b3e1af3c6dc3f99b27dab89bf884c7a5997.research_question: Does incorporating modularity and sparsity into neural network architectures lead to improved generalization, learning efficiency, and interpretability compared to monolithic architectures, especially in the context of tasks governed by multiple underlying rules?
9b4d0b3e1af3c6dc3f99b27dab89bf884c7a5997.hypothesis: Modular neural architectures, when endowed with appropriate inductive biases for specialization and sparsity, will outperform monolithic architectures in both in-distribution and out-of-distribution generalization, particularly as the complexity (number of rules) of the underlying task increases. However, end-to-end training of modular systems may not be sufficient to achieve optimal specialization without additional inductive biases.
9b4d0b3e1af3c6dc3f99b27dab89bf884c7a5997.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation framework will be developed to systematically analyze modular neural architectures using synthetic, rule-based data distributions where the ground-truth structure is fully known. Multiple model classes will be implemented, including monolithic networks, standard modular networks, modular networks with explicit operation-based routing (modular-op), and oracle modular networks with perfect specialization (GT-Modular). Each modular system will consist of as many modules as there are rules in the data-generating process, with modules instantiated as MLPs, MHAs, or RNNs depending on the task. The models will be trained in both regression and classification settings, with the modular systems designed to encourage specialization of modules to specific rules. A suite of quantitative metrics will be introduced to measure not only predictive performance but also the degree of collapse (under-utilization of modules) and specialization (alignment between modules and rules), including novel metrics such as Collapse-Avg, Collapse-Worst, Alignment, Adaptation, and Inverse Mutual Information.
9b4d0b3e1af3c6dc3f99b27dab89bf884c7a5997.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic datasets generated according to rule-based processes tailored for MLP, MHA, and RNN architectures. Tasks will vary the number of rules (from 2 to 32), model capacities, and training regimes (regression and binary classification). For each configuration, multiple random seeds and task parameterizations will be used to ensure robustness, resulting in large-scale model training (approximately 20,000 models). Baselines will include monolithic networks and random module activation, while modular models will be compared against modular-op and GT-Modular oracles. Evaluation will be performed on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution test sets, with OoD variations including changes in input variance and sequence length. Performance will be assessed using classification error and regression loss, while collapse and specialization will be quantified using the proposed metrics.
9b4d0b3e1af3c6dc3f99b27dab89bf884c7a5997.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a rigorous and principled evaluation framework for modular neural architectures, leveraging synthetic rule-based data with known ground-truth structure. Novel quantitative metrics are developed to assess both the utilization (collapse) and specialization of modules, providing insights beyond standard predictive performance. The work systematically benchmarks a hierarchy of modular models, including perfect specialization oracles, and demonstrates that current end-to-end training approaches for modular systems are sub-optimal, especially as task complexity increases. The framework enables detailed diagnosis of where and why modularity succeeds or fails, and highlights the necessity of additional inductive biases for effective module specialization, thus paving the way for future research on scalable and interpretable modular systems.

9b4e61dda9db6317afae1bd4a12356d00769d9f3.title: AnyDoor: Zero-shot Object-level Image Customization
9b4e61dda9db6317afae1bd4a12356d00769d9f3.research_question: How can zero-shot object-level image customization be achieved, enabling the seamless placement, editing, and blending of arbitrary target objects into new scenes at user-specified locations and shapes, without per-object parameter tuning?
9b4e61dda9db6317afae1bd4a12356d00769d9f3.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that combining discriminative identity features and frequency-aware detail features extracted from target objects, and injecting them into a pre-trained diffusion-based image generator, will enable high-fidelity, zero-shot object teleportation and customization in diverse scenes, with controllable location and shape, without the need for per-object fine-tuning.
9b4e61dda9db6317afae1bd4a12356d00769d9f3.proposed_method: A novel diffusion-based image generation framework is developed that enables zero-shot object teleportation and customization. The method begins by segmenting the target object and removing its background, followed by extracting identity features using a self-supervised visual encoder (DINOv2) to obtain both global and patch-level tokens. To complement identity information, a frequency-aware detail extractor generates high-frequency maps from the object, capturing fine appearance details while allowing local variation. These features are then composited with the scene at the user-specified location, optionally guided by a user-drawn shape mask for pose or contour control. The identity tokens are injected into each layer of a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model (Stable Diffusion) via cross-attention, while the detail maps are concatenated with the decoder features at each resolution. The model is trained on large-scale video and image datasets, leveraging adaptive timestep sampling to balance learning of structural variation and fine details.
9b4e61dda9db6317afae1bd4a12356d00769d9f3.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using a diverse set of datasets, including video segmentation/tracking datasets (YouTubeVOS, YouTubeVIS, UVO, MOSE, VIPSeg, BURST) for capturing appearance variations, and multi-view and single-image datasets (MVImgNet, VitonHD, FashionTryon, MSRA-10K, DUT, HFlickr, LVIS, SAM subset) for high-quality details and scenario diversity. A new benchmark is constructed with 30 novel concepts from DreamBooth and 80 scene images from COCO-Val, resulting in 2,400 object-scene combinations. Baseline comparisons include reference-based methods (Paint-by-Example, Graphit, IP-Adapter, Stable Diffusion inpainting) and tuning-based methods (DreamBooth, Custom Diffusion, Cones). Evaluation metrics include CLIP-Score and DINO-Score for measuring similarity between generated and target objects, as well as user studies with 15 annotators rating fidelity, quality, and diversity. Additional qualitative analyses and ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of core components and feature extractors.
9b4e61dda9db6317afae1bd4a12356d00769d9f3.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a zero-shot object-level image customization framework that requires no per-object parameter tuning and generalizes to unseen object-scene combinations. Key innovations include the use of a self-supervised identity extractor (DINOv2) for robust instance-level feature extraction, a frequency-aware detail extractor for fine appearance control, and the integration of these features into a pre-trained diffusion model with adaptive training strategies. The method enables fine-grained control over object placement, shape, and pose, supports multi-object composition, and demonstrates superior identity preservation and harmonization compared to existing reference-based and tuning-based baselines.

9b4ecc297389ca6753817ce3d3dfb3057c34ae76.title: On a Connection Between Imitation Learning and RLHF
9b4ecc297389ca6753817ce3d3dfb3057c34ae76.research_question: How can large language models be more effectively aligned with human preference data, and what new frameworks or perspectives can improve the efficiency, stability, and reasoning capabilities of preference-based alignment methods?
9b4ecc297389ca6753817ce3d3dfb3057c34ae76.hypothesis: Directly optimizing an imitation learning objective using density ratio estimation, rather than relying on traditional reward maximization or the Bradley-Terry assumption, will yield more effective and stable alignment of large language models with human preferences, preserving reasoning abilities and improving performance on challenging benchmarks.
9b4ecc297389ca6753817ce3d3dfb3057c34ae76.proposed_method: A new framework, Direct Imitation Learning (DIL), is proposed to align large language models with human preferences by directly optimizing the reverse KL divergence between the model policy and the (unknown) distribution of preferred responses. The method formulates the alignment objective as a density ratio estimation problem, leveraging Bregman divergence (e.g., LSIF, BCE, UKL) to estimate the ratio between the chosen and reference response distributions. DIL bypasses the need for explicit reward modeling and RL loops by parameterizing the density ratio in a way that allows for closed-form optimization, fitting the model to maximize the likelihood of preferred responses while minimizing that of rejected ones. The approach generalizes to a family of objectives and unifies prior alignment methods as special cases, with the flexibility to choose different Bregman divergences for the density ratio estimation step.
9b4ecc297389ca6753817ce3d3dfb3057c34ae76.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on widely used benchmarks, including the UltraFeedback Binarized dataset, Reddit TL;DR summarization dataset, and Anthropic-HH dataset. Evaluation will cover tasks from the Open LLM Leaderboard, with models such as Pythia-2.8B, Mistral-7B-Base, and Llama3-8b-SFT serving as base or reference models. Baselines for comparison include DPO, f-DPO, IPO, SLiC, CPO, and SimPO, with hyperparameters thoroughly tuned for each. Evaluation metrics include win rates against SFT and chosen responses (using GPT-4 for zero-shot pairwise evaluation), as well as standard benchmark scores (e.g., MMLU-PRO, BBH, MUSR, MATH, GSM8K, ARC). Ablation studies will explore the impact of different Bregman divergence objectives, and training dynamics will be analyzed to assess the likelihood trends of chosen and rejected responses.
9b4ecc297389ca6753817ce3d3dfb3057c34ae76.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled imitation learning framework for preference alignment that avoids the Bradley-Terry assumption and explicit reward modeling, enabling direct optimization of the alignment objective via density ratio estimation. The method unifies and generalizes existing alignment algorithms, provides a closed-form solution for the optimal policy, and demonstrates improved stability and performance, particularly on reasoning-heavy tasks. The approach also offers new theoretical insights into the connection between RLHF and imitation learning, and empirically outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across a comprehensive set of benchmarks.

9b4f7c97c0b83a80c32bc0b93595cbcfb4ecb16d.title: DoReMi: Optimizing Data Mixtures Speeds Up Language Model Pretraining
9b4f7c97c0b83a80c32bc0b93595cbcfb4ecb16d.research_question: How can the mixture proportions of pretraining data domains be optimized to improve the efficiency and performance of large-scale language model pretraining, without relying on downstream task knowledge?
9b4f7c97c0b83a80c32bc0b93595cbcfb4ecb16d.hypothesis: Optimizing domain mixture proportions using a principled minimax approach based on distributionally robust optimization, without access to downstream task data, will yield language models that achieve better or comparable performance and training efficiency across all domains compared to models trained with default or downstream-tuned domain weights.
9b4f7c97c0b83a80c32bc0b93595cbcfb4ecb16d.proposed_method: A new framework, Domain Reweighting with Minimax Optimization (DoReMi), will be developed to optimize domain mixture proportions for language model pretraining. The method begins by training a small reference model on initial domain weights (e.g., uniform or based on token counts) to establish baseline losses for each domain. Next, a small proxy model is trained using Group Distributionally Robust Optimization (Group DRO), where domain weights are dynamically updated via exponentiated gradient ascent to minimize the worst-case excess loss (the gap between proxy and reference model losses) across domains. The optimized domain weights are obtained by averaging the weights over the DRO training trajectory. Finally, a large language model is pretrained on a dataset resampled according to these optimized domain weights, using standard next-token prediction objectives.
9b4f7c97c0b83a80c32bc0b93595cbcfb4ecb16d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale text corpora, specifically The Pile (22 domains, 800GB) and the GLaM dataset (8 domains), using Transformer-based decoder-only language models. The procedure involves training 280M-parameter proxy and reference models to optimize domain weights, which are then used to pretrain an 8B-parameter main model. Baseline comparisons will include models trained with default domain weights and, for GLaM, domain weights tuned on downstream tasks. Evaluation will use held-out validation data to measure per-domain perplexity and generative one-shot accuracy on standard benchmarks such as TriviaQA, Natural Questions, WebQuestions, SQuADv2, and LAMBADA, with exact-match accuracy as the main metric. The compute cost for domain weight optimization will be tracked and compared to full model pretraining.
9b4f7c97c0b83a80c32bc0b93595cbcfb4ecb16d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled, task-agnostic method for optimizing pretraining data mixtures using minimax optimization and distributionally robust techniques, eliminating the need for downstream task data or extensive hyperparameter searches. The method leverages small proxy models to efficiently tune domain weights, which can then be transferred to much larger models, significantly improving training efficiency and downstream performance. The approach demonstrates that optimized domain mixtures can reduce perplexity across all domains and accelerate convergence, achieving baseline accuracy up to 2.6x faster and improving average few-shot accuracy by over 6% on large-scale benchmarks.

9b5dafe432446d9b627699aff65f4e81ac3fc914.title: METRA: Scalable Unsupervised RL with Metric-Aware Abstraction
9b5dafe432446d9b627699aff65f4e81ac3fc914.research_question: How can unsupervised reinforcement learning (RL) be made scalable to complex, high-dimensional environments, enabling the discovery of diverse and useful behaviors without any supervision?
9b5dafe432446d9b627699aff65f4e81ac3fc914.hypothesis: A metric-aware abstraction approach that maximizes coverage in a compact latent space, defined by temporal distances rather than Euclidean metrics, will enable scalable unsupervised RL that discovers diverse and useful behaviors in complex, high-dimensional environments, including those with pixel-based observations.
9b5dafe432446d9b627699aff65f4e81ac3fc914.proposed_method: A novel unsupervised RL objective, Metric-Aware Abstraction (METRA), will be developed to address scalability in complex environments. The method will learn a compact latent space connected to the state space via a temporal distance metric, and a latent-conditioned policy that translates latent vectors into diverse behaviors. The core objective maximizes the Wasserstein dependency measure (WDM) between states and skills, using temporal distance as the metric, ensuring that learned behaviors are maximally spread out in terms of environment dynamics. The approach involves optimizing a constrained objective using dual gradient descent, where a representation function ϕ(s) abstracts the state space, and a skill policy π(a|s,z) is trained with rewards based on movement in the latent space. The temporal distance metric enables the method to be applicable to both state-based and pixel-based environments, and the learned abstraction supports zero-shot goal-reaching by selecting skills that move toward a desired goal state in the latent space.
9b5dafe432446d9b627699aff65f4e81ac3fc914.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five benchmark environments: state-based Ant and HalfCheetah from Gym, and pixel-based Quadruped, Humanoid (from DeepMind Control Suite), and Kitchen (from prior work). The method will be compared against 11 prior unsupervised RL baselines, including mutual information-based skill discovery, metric-based skill discovery, pure exploration, and unsupervised goal-reaching methods. Evaluation metrics will include policy coverage (e.g., x-y trajectory coverage), total state coverage, and downstream task performance using hierarchical controllers or zero-shot goal-reaching. All methods will be implemented on a unified codebase where possible, and experiments will use multiple random seeds and report confidence intervals. The experimental setup will avoid any prior knowledge or supervision, and in pixel-based environments, agents will learn solely from 64x64x3 camera images.
9b5dafe432446d9b627699aff65f4e81ac3fc914.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a metric-aware unsupervised RL objective that leverages temporal distances for scalable skill discovery in high-dimensional and pixel-based environments. METRA is claimed to be the first unsupervised RL method to discover diverse locomotion behaviors in pixel-based Quadruped and Humanoid environments. The method provides a principled connection to principal component analysis under temporal distances, and enables zero-shot goal-reaching via learned state abstractions. The approach is positioned as a significant step toward scalable, general-purpose unsupervised RL suitable for large-scale pre-training.

9b6a173e2b030aa0c702a4c8e3221c79381331d6.title: Feature Responsiveness Scores: Model-Agnostic Explanations for Recourse
9b6a173e2b030aa0c702a4c8e3221c79381331d6.research_question: How can explanations for automated decision-making models in high-stakes domains be constructed to better support recourse for decision subjects, ensuring that highlighted features are actionable and truly enable individuals to overturn adverse outcomes?
9b6a173e2b030aa0c702a4c8e3221c79381331d6.hypothesis: Standard feature attribution methods used in current explainability practices often fail to provide actionable recourse by highlighting features that are immutable or unresponsive, whereas a method that scores features based on their responsiveness—the probability that intervening on a feature leads to a desired prediction—will yield explanations that more effectively support recourse and consumer protection.
9b6a173e2b030aa0c702a4c8e3221c79381331d6.proposed_method: A model-agnostic framework will be developed to compute feature responsiveness scores for any classification model and set of actionability constraints. Responsiveness is defined as the probability that an individual can achieve a target prediction through an arbitrary intervention on a feature, accounting for both deterministic and stochastic downstream effects as specified by an intervention model. The method constructs reachable sets for each feature by either enumerating or sampling all possible interventions, subject to actionability constraints such as immutability, monotonicity, integrality, and causal dependencies. Responsiveness scores are then calculated by querying the model's predictions over these reachable sets, and explanations are constructed by highlighting the top-k most responsive features for each individual. The approach is extensible to incorporate additional requirements, such as monotonicity, cost-weighted interventions, and distributional robustness.
9b6a173e2b030aa0c702a4c8e3221c79381331d6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three publicly available consumer finance datasets (heloc, german, givemecredit), each representing loan repayment prediction tasks with discrete and continuous features. Models to be evaluated include logistic regression, XGBoost, and random forests. For each denied applicant, feature-highlighting explanations will be generated using standard feature attribution methods (SHAP, LIME), action-aware variants (SHAP-AW, LIME-AW), and the proposed responsiveness-based method (RESP). Evaluation will focus on the proportion of denied individuals who can attain recourse via single-feature interventions, the prevalence of explanations containing only responsive features, and the ability of each method to avoid highlighting unresponsive or immutable features. Additional analyses will assess the monotonicity and intuitiveness of responsive features, and the impact of omitting intervention details in explanations.
9b6a173e2b030aa0c702a4c8e3221c79381331d6.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a model-agnostic, actionable, and probabilistic framework for constructing feature-highlighting explanations that directly support recourse, overcoming key limitations of existing feature attribution methods. It enables the computation of responsiveness scores under complex, user-specified actionability constraints, and provides a principled way to flag fixed predictions and avoid misleading explanations. The method is extensible to practical requirements such as monotonicity and cost, and is accompanied by an open-source Python library for broad applicability.

9b8515947b91600137e1400ac3f941ed53931ab5.title: Simulating Diffusion Bridges with Score Matching
9b8515947b91600137e1400ac3f941ed53931ab5.research_question: How can diffusion bridges, i.e., diffusion processes conditioned to start and end at given states, be efficiently and accurately simulated, particularly when the transition densities are intractable and in high-dimensional or complex settings?
9b8515947b91600137e1400ac3f941ed53931ab5.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a variational score matching approach, leveraging backward time representations and function approximation (e.g., neural networks), can effectively approximate the time-reversal of unconditioned diffusions, enabling accurate simulation of diffusion bridges even in cases where traditional methods struggle.
9b8515947b91600137e1400ac3f941ed53931ab5.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces a variational framework to learn the time-reversal of a diffusion process by parameterizing the score function (the gradient of the log transition density) using flexible function approximators such as neural networks. The approach minimizes a loss function derived from the Kullback–Leibler divergence between the true diffusion path measure and a parameterized proposal, where the loss is made tractable via a denoising score matching objective adapted to time-discretized paths. The score function is learned by simulating sample paths of the unconditioned diffusion, and the approximation is optimized using stochastic gradient descent. Once the score is learned, proposal bridge processes are simulated using the learned drift, and corrections are applied via importance sampling or independent Metropolis–Hastings to ensure accurate path generation. An extension allows for learning a single score function that generalizes across multiple pairs of initial and terminal states by conditioning the score approximation on the initial state.
9b8515947b91600137e1400ac3f941ed53931ab5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several benchmark diffusion models, including the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process, a financial econometrics interest rate model, and a gene expression model from genetics. For each model, the proposed backward and forward diffusion bridge approximations will be compared against established baselines such as the Clark–Delyon–Hu proposal, Pedersen's forward diffusion, the guided proposal bridge, and the modified diffusion bridge. Evaluation metrics will include acceptance rates in independent Metropolis–Hastings, effective sample size in importance sampling, and mean squared error or variance of estimated transition densities, with ground truth available for some models. Experiments will use neural networks for score approximation, stochastic gradient optimization, and will assess performance across varying time horizons, dimensions, and conditioning on rare terminal states. Each method will be run with a large number of samples or iterations (e.g., 1024), and results will be averaged over multiple independent repetitions.
9b8515947b91600137e1400ac3f941ed53931ab5.novelty_claims: The approach presents a novel application of variational score matching to the simulation of diffusion bridges, circumventing the intractability of transition densities by working with time-reversed processes and leveraging modern function approximation tools. Unlike previous methods, the framework enables flexible, data-driven learning of bridge dynamics, supports generalization across multiple conditioned states, and demonstrates improved performance in challenging scenarios where traditional proposals are inadequate. The method also offers a new avenue for approximating both backward and forward bridge representations, with potential for further extensions to parameter-dependent and infinite-dimensional settings.

9b90bc179ee0af58e58ce65a3762ae2771a6627e.title: A Langevin-like Sampler for Discrete Distributions
9b90bc179ee0af58e58ce65a3762ae2771a6627e.research_question: How can efficient and scalable sampling methods be developed for complex, high-dimensional discrete distributions, particularly in machine learning applications such as Ising models, restricted Boltzmann machines, deep energy-based models, binary neural networks, and language generation?
9b90bc179ee0af58e58ce65a3762ae2771a6627e.hypothesis: A gradient-based proposal mechanism, inspired by the Langevin algorithm in continuous spaces, can be adapted to discrete domains to enable efficient, parallel updates of all coordinates, resulting in faster mixing and improved sampling quality for high-dimensional and strongly correlated discrete distributions.
9b90bc179ee0af58e58ce65a3762ae2771a6627e.proposed_method: A discrete Langevin proposal (DLP) is constructed as a gradient-based proposal for discrete distributions, where the proposal distribution is coordinate-wise factorized and allows all coordinates to be updated in parallel based on a single gradient computation. The proposal is defined as a categorical softmax over the discrete domain, with probabilities determined by the alignment of the proposed move with the gradient of the energy function. The method supports both unadjusted (DULA) and Metropolis-adjusted (DMALA) variants, with the latter ensuring asymptotic convergence to the target distribution. Extensions include stochastic gradient versions for scalability in large datasets and preconditioned versions to adapt stepsizes per coordinate. The overall computational cost is linear in the number of dimensions, enabling efficient exploration of high-dimensional spaces.
9b90bc179ee0af58e58ce65a3762ae2771a6627e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of tasks, including sampling from Ising models, restricted Boltzmann machines trained on MNIST, deep energy-based models on discrete image datasets (e.g., StaticMNIST, DynamicMNIST, Omniglot, Caltech Silhouettes), binary Bayesian neural networks on UCI datasets, and text infilling tasks using BERT-based models on WikiText-103 and TBC. Baselines for comparison include Gibbs sampling, Gibbs with gradient (GWG), Hamming ball sampling, discrete Stein variational gradient descent (DSVGD), relaxed MALA, and locally-balanced samplers. Evaluation metrics will include root-mean-square error (RMSE), maximum mean discrepancy (MMD), effective sample size (ESS), log-likelihood, test RMSE, BLEU score, self-BLEU, and unique n-gram diversity. Experimental setups will ensure fair comparison in terms of computational cost per step and number of iterations, and both iteration-based and wall-clock time-based performance will be reported.
9b90bc179ee0af58e58ce65a3762ae2771a6627e.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple, scalable, and parallelizable gradient-based sampler for discrete distributions, which is the first to directly transfer the advantages of the Langevin algorithm from continuous to discrete spaces. The approach enables simultaneous updates of all coordinates with a single gradient computation, overcoming the limitations of Gibbs-like and locally-balanced proposals that are restricted to small, sequential updates. Theoretical analysis establishes asymptotic unbiasedness for log-quadratic distributions and small bias for distributions close to log-quadratic, with empirical results demonstrating superior convergence speed, sample quality, and diversity across a wide variety of high-dimensional discrete tasks. The method is general, supporting variants such as stochastic gradients and preconditioning, and is applicable to a broad range of machine learning models involving discrete variables.

9b98ca94b7733feee1cff5c57596611ad35fa7aa.title: Scaling Laws for Sparsely-Connected Foundation Models
9b98ca94b7733feee1cff5c57596611ad35fa7aa.research_question: How does parameter sparsity affect the scaling behavior and performance of large Transformer-based foundation models across vision and language domains, and what are the optimal sparsity regimes for given model sizes and training budgets?
9b98ca94b7733feee1cff5c57596611ad35fa7aa.hypothesis: Parameter sparsity in Transformer-based foundation models can be characterized by a scaling law that relates sparsity, number of non-zero parameters, and training data, enabling prediction of optimal sparsity levels that maximize performance for fixed compute or parameter budgets.
9b98ca94b7733feee1cff5c57596611ad35fa7aa.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical and theoretical investigation will be conducted to derive and validate a joint scaling law that incorporates weight sparsity, model size (number of non-zero parameters), and training data for large-scale Transformer models. The methodology involves training Vision Transformers (ViT) on the JFT-4B image dataset and T5 encoder-decoder models on the C4 text corpus, applying gradual magnitude pruning with a cubic schedule to achieve various sparsity levels. The resulting validation losses will be systematically recorded across a grid of model sizes, training durations, and sparsity targets. The collected data will be used to fit a parametric scaling law of the form L(S,N,D), where S is sparsity, N is the number of non-zero parameters, and D is the amount of training data, with the law capturing both power-law scaling in capacity and data. The study will also extend to structured sparsity patterns (such as n:m hardware-friendly patterns) and compare strategies such as pruning from scratch versus pruning from a pretrained dense checkpoint.
9b98ca94b7733feee1cff5c57596611ad35fa7aa.experiment_details: Experiments will involve extensive sweeps over model sizes (ranging from hundreds of thousands to hundreds of millions of non-zero parameters), training durations (from tens of thousands to over a million steps), and sparsity levels (0%, 50%, 75%, 87.5%) for both ViT/JFT-4B and T5/C4 setups. Baseline comparisons will include dense models of equivalent parameter count and compute, as well as compute-optimal scaling lines such as Chinchilla. Evaluation metrics will primarily be pretraining validation loss, with additional analysis of FLOPs and efficiency. The experimental grid will allow fitting of scaling laws and assessment of optimal sparsity contours for both dense and sparse compute regimes. Additional experiments will evaluate structured n:m sparsity patterns and the efficiency of pruning from pretrained checkpoints versus from scratch.
9b98ca94b7733feee1cff5c57596611ad35fa7aa.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first empirically validated scaling law that jointly models the effects of weight sparsity, model size, and training data on the performance of large-scale Transformer foundation models. It enables analytic prediction of optimal sparsity levels for given compute or parameter budgets, and demonstrates that optimal sparsity increases with training duration. The approach is validated across both vision and language domains, extends to hardware-friendly structured sparsity patterns, and provides practical insights into the tradeoffs between dense and sparse training, including scenarios involving pruning from pretrained models. This work offers both theoretical understanding and actionable guidelines for leveraging sparsity to improve computational efficiency in large foundation models.

9bb3d04c94a09e92375ae5377ab5187e1af3f6aa.title: Robust Deep Reinforcement Learning against Adversarial Perturbations on State Observations
9bb3d04c94a09e92375ae5377ab5187e1af3f6aa.research_question: How can deep reinforcement learning agents be made robust against adversarial perturbations in state observations, and what are the theoretical and practical principles underlying robust policy learning in this setting?
9bb3d04c94a09e92375ae5377ab5187e1af3f6aa.hypothesis: A theoretically principled policy regularization, grounded in the properties of a state-adversarial Markov decision process (SA-MDP), will significantly improve the robustness of deep reinforcement learning agents against adversarial perturbations on state observations, outperforming naive adversarial training and existing defense techniques for both discrete and continuous action spaces.
9bb3d04c94a09e92375ae5377ab5187e1af3f6aa.proposed_method: A new framework, the state-adversarial Markov decision process (SA-MDP), is formulated to model adversarial perturbations on state observations, where the agent observes a perturbed state but the true environment state remains unchanged. Theoretical analysis of SA-MDP reveals that standard adversarial training methods are insufficient, motivating the development of a robust policy regularizer based on bounding the divergence (total variation or KL-divergence) between the policy distributions under original and perturbed states. This regularizer is integrated into the training objectives of various deep RL algorithms, including PPO (for stochastic policies), DDPG (for deterministic policies), and DQN (for discrete actions), using convex relaxation or stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics to efficiently solve the inner maximization over adversarial perturbations. The approach is designed to be broadly applicable and optimizer-friendly, and can provide robustness certificates via convex relaxation.
9bb3d04c94a09e92375ae5377ab5187e1af3f6aa.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of 10 environments, including Atari games (discrete actions) and MuJoCo continuous control tasks, to evaluate the robustness of the proposed method. Baselines will include vanilla RL agents and agents trained with naive adversarial training. Evaluation will use strong white-box adversarial attacks, including two novel attacks (Robust Sarsa and Maximal Action Difference) as well as standard PGD-based attacks, with performance measured by average episode rewards under both natural and adversarial conditions. Additional metrics such as action certification rates and robustness certificates will be reported, and experiments will be repeated multiple times to account for RL variance. Hyperparameters will be aligned with established baselines to ensure fair comparison.
9bb3d04c94a09e92375ae5377ab5187e1af3f6aa.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the SA-MDP framework for modeling adversarial perturbations on state observations and provides a theoretical analysis of its properties, including the non-existence of stationary optimal policies under strong adversaries. A novel, theoretically justified policy regularizer is developed, applicable to a wide range of RL algorithms and both action space types. The method includes efficient optimization strategies (convex relaxation and SGLD) and enables robustness certification. Two new, critic-independent adversarial attacks are proposed for robust evaluation. The approach demonstrates significant improvements in robustness and, in some cases, natural performance, over existing baselines and naive adversarial training.

9bc7667532928107e7e91d688a64f1aa442477db.title: OpenSight: A Simple Open-Vocabulary Framework for LiDAR-Based Object Detection
9bc7667532928107e7e91d688a64f1aa442477db.research_question: How can LiDAR-based object detection be extended to open-vocabulary scenarios, enabling robust detection and semantic interpretation of novel and previously unseen object categories in complex real-world environments without reliance on predefined class labels?
9bc7667532928107e7e91d688a64f1aa442477db.hypothesis: Incorporating 2D-3D geometric priors, temporal and spatial awareness, and cross-modal feature alignment with large-scale vision-language models will enable LiDAR-based object detection systems to effectively perceive, localize, and semantically interpret generic and novel objects in open-vocabulary settings, overcoming overfitting to known classes.
9bc7667532928107e7e91d688a64f1aa442477db.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that first leverages 2D geometric priors from camera images paired with LiDAR data to generate initial 2D bounding boxes for generic objects. These 2D boxes will be lifted into 3D space using LiDAR point clouds, followed by point clustering within each frustum to estimate 3D bounding boxes. Temporal awareness will be incorporated by correlating predicted 3D boxes across consecutive frames, recalibrating missed or inaccurate detections, while spatial awareness will use large language models to derive size priors and randomly place 'precisely' estimated 3D boxes at varying distances to enhance object visibility. For semantic interpretation, a cross-modal alignment and fusion module will be designed to align 3D LiDAR features with 2D image embeddings (from models such as grounding DINO) and fuse these features for open-vocabulary semantic decoding. Size priors from language models will further recalibrate predictions to improve accuracy.
9bc7667532928107e7e91d688a64f1aa442477db.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the nuScenes dataset, a large-scale outdoor dataset with multimodal data (LiDAR and six RGB cameras), using all classes as novel to rigorously evaluate open-vocabulary performance. Baselines will include adapted 2D open-vocabulary detectors (e.g., Detic, OWL-ViT), 3D open-vocabulary classification methods (e.g., PointCLIP, OV-3DET), and fully supervised models for upper-bound comparison. Evaluation metrics will include mean Average Precision (mAP) across novel classes, as well as distance-based (mAP-near, mAP-midrange, mAP-far) and size-based (mAP-large, mAP-medium, mAP-small) metrics to analyze performance under varying object distances and sizes. The experimental setup will involve joint optimization of 3D and 2D losses, use of object-level vision-language models for feature extraction and alignment, and ablation studies to assess the impact of each module.
9bc7667532928107e7e91d688a64f1aa442477db.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a unified 2D-3D modeling approach for open-vocabulary LiDAR-based object detection, explicitly addressing the limitations of overfitting to known classes by leveraging geometric priors and cross-modal alignment. The integration of temporal and spatial awareness modules for generic object perception, along with the use of large language models for size priors and semantic recalibration, represents a novel strategy for improving detection and interpretation of novel categories. The method also pioneers the use of object-level feature alignment between 3D LiDAR data and 2D image embeddings for semantic decoding in open-vocabulary settings, demonstrating state-of-the-art performance on challenging benchmarks.

9bd2fd5aae2acc69a54a432b77d502f1f146643f.title: FlatFormer: Flattened Window Attention for Efficient Point Cloud Transformer
9bd2fd5aae2acc69a54a432b77d502f1f146643f.research_question: How can the computational efficiency and latency of transformer-based models for 3D point cloud processing be improved to match or surpass sparse convolutional methods, while maintaining or improving detection accuracy in large-scale, real-time applications such as autonomous driving?
9bd2fd5aae2acc69a54a432b77d502f1f146643f.hypothesis: Partitioning point clouds into groups of equal size using window-based sorting, rather than traditional spatially regular windows, will yield a more hardware-friendly and computationally efficient transformer architecture for 3D point cloud processing, enabling real-time performance without sacrificing accuracy.
9bd2fd5aae2acc69a54a432b77d502f1f146643f.proposed_method: A novel transformer-based framework, FlatFormer, will be developed for efficient 3D point cloud processing. The method introduces Flattened Window Attention (FWA), which partitions the point cloud into groups of equal size via window-based sorting, rather than grouping by spatially regular windows. Self-attention is then applied within each group to extract local features, and the sorting axis is alternated between layers to aggregate features from different orientations. Window shifting is incorporated to enable cross-group feature exchange, mimicking the receptive field expansion of Swin Transformers. Efficient implementation techniques such as FlashAttention for memory-efficient multi-head self-attention, fused linear and activation layers for the feed-forward network, and reuse of sorting results are employed to further minimize computational overhead and maximize hardware utilization.
9bd2fd5aae2acc69a54a432b77d502f1f146643f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the large-scale Waymo Open Dataset, which contains over 1,000 LiDAR point cloud sequences with multiple object classes and varying scene complexity. The evaluation will focus on 3D object detection, using standard metrics such as mean Average Precision (mAP) and heading-weighted mAP (mAPH) at different difficulty levels (L1/L2). Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art sparse convolutional models (e.g., CenterPoint, PillarNet) and transformer-based models (e.g., SST, VoxSet, VoTr). Latency and throughput will be measured on both high-end GPUs (NVIDIA Quadro RTX A6000) and resource-constrained edge GPUs (NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin), with all models evaluated in FP16 precision. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of group size, window shape, sorting strategies, and system-level optimizations on both accuracy and efficiency.
9bd2fd5aae2acc69a54a432b77d502f1f146643f.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first point cloud transformer to achieve real-time inference on edge GPUs, surpassing the latency of highly optimized sparse convolutional models while delivering on-par or superior accuracy on large-scale benchmarks. The key innovation lies in trading spatial proximity for computational regularity by grouping points into equal-sized sets, which eliminates padding and partitioning overheads inherent in prior window-based transformers. Additional contributions include the introduction of axis-alternating sorting and efficient system-level implementations tailored for point cloud transformers, resulting in significant speedups (up to 4.6× over previous transformers and 1.4× over sparse convolution) without loss of detection performance.

9bdb6d5bb94479a8612c41657d55bceef4898f98.title: Evading Watermark based Detection of AI-Generated Content
9bdb6d5bb94479a8612c41657d55bceef4898f98.research_question: How robust are current watermark-based detection methods for AI-generated images against adversarial post-processing attacks, and can new adversarial techniques be developed to evade such detectors while maintaining image quality?
9bdb6d5bb94479a8612c41657d55bceef4898f98.hypothesis: Existing watermark-based detection methods for AI-generated content are vulnerable to adversarial post-processing attacks that can evade detection with minimal, human-imperceptible perturbations, and new adversarial methods can be designed to outperform traditional post-processing techniques in both white-box and black-box scenarios.
9bdb6d5bb94479a8612c41657d55bceef4898f98.proposed_method: A novel adversarial post-processing framework, termed WEvade, will be developed to evade watermark-based detectors of AI-generated images. In the white-box setting, the method will leverage access to the detector's decoder to construct perturbations that reduce the bitwise accuracy of the decoded watermark to near-random levels, making the image indistinguishable from non-watermarked images. This will involve formulating and solving constrained optimization problems using projected gradient descent and binary search, with loss functions designed to minimize similarity to the original or a random watermark. In the black-box setting, WEvade will extend hard-label adversarial example techniques (e.g., HopSkipJump) to iteratively query the detector and find minimal perturbations that flip the detection result, with enhancements such as improved initialization and early stopping to reduce query count and perturbation size. Both surrogate-model-based and direct query-based attacks will be explored, and the approach will be evaluated against both single-tail and double-tail detector architectures.
9bdb6d5bb94479a8612c41657d55bceef4898f98.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple benchmark image datasets, including COCO, ImageNet, and Conceptual Captions, with both learning-based (HiDDeN, UDH) and non-learning-based (e.g., Stable Diffusion's DWT-DCT) watermarking methods. The evaluation will compare WEvade against standard post-processing baselines such as JPEG compression, Gaussian noise, Gaussian blur, and brightness/contrast adjustment. Metrics will include bitwise accuracy of decoded watermarks, evasion rate (fraction of images evading detection), and average perturbation (measured in normalized pixel value range). Both standard and adversarially trained watermarking models will be tested, and experiments will cover a range of detection thresholds and both white-box and black-box threat models. Theoretical analysis of evasion rates will be validated empirically.
9bdb6d5bb94479a8612c41657d55bceef4898f98.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first systematic adversarial evaluation of watermark-based AI-generated image detectors, including both white-box and black-box attack scenarios. It develops new optimization-based adversarial post-processing methods that exploit the unique properties of watermarking, outperforming traditional post-processing in both effectiveness and image quality preservation. The work also proposes a new double-tail detector architecture to defend against certain adversarial attacks and provides both theoretical and empirical analysis of attack success rates. The approach highlights critical vulnerabilities in existing watermark-based detection schemes and motivates the need for more robust detection methods.

9be83f2a28e3fa02e7f667ab6b95fd9f1166edf9.title: On the Complexity of Adversarial Decision Making
9be83f2a28e3fa02e7f667ab6b95fd9f1166edf9.research_question: What are the fundamental complexity measures that govern the minimax regret in adversarial online decision making, including structured bandit and reinforcement learning problems, and how does the structure of the model class affect sample-efficient learning guarantees in adversarial environments?
9be83f2a28e3fa02e7f667ab6b95fd9f1166edf9.hypothesis: The Decision-Estimation Coefficient (DEC), when applied to the convex hull of the model class, is both necessary and sufficient to characterize the minimax regret in adversarial decision making settings.
9be83f2a28e3fa02e7f667ab6b95fd9f1166edf9.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed for adversarial decision making that generalizes structured bandit and reinforcement learning problems where an adaptive adversary selects models from a known class. The methodology introduces a high-probability variant of the Exploration-by-Optimization (ExO+) algorithm, which at each round solves a minimax optimization problem to select a sampling distribution and reward estimator that minimize instantaneous regret and control the tail behavior of the estimator. The approach leverages the convexified Decision-Estimation Coefficient (DEC) as a complexity measure, establishing regret bounds via this measure. Key technical steps include the use of exponential weights updates, importance-weighted estimators, and a novel analysis connecting the DEC to the Information Ratio and high-probability regret guarantees for adaptive adversaries.
9be83f2a28e3fa02e7f667ab6b95fd9f1166edf9.experiment_details: Theoretical analysis is conducted to establish upper and lower bounds on regret in adversarial decision making, with the main results applying to general model classes, including those parameterized by linear models, neural networks, or Markov decision processes (MDPs). The framework is instantiated for several canonical problems: adversarial multi-armed bandits, adversarial linear bandits, and adversarial reinforcement learning with tabular MDPs. The evaluation compares the proposed regret bounds to existing results in both stochastic and adversarial settings, using minimax regret as the primary metric. Theoretical examples and comparisons are provided to illustrate how the convexified DEC recovers known rates and explains the tractability or intractability of various problem classes.
9be83f2a28e3fa02e7f667ab6b95fd9f1166edf9.novelty_claims: The proposal establishes that the convexified Decision-Estimation Coefficient is both necessary and sufficient for low regret in adversarial decision making, bridging the gap between stochastic and adversarial complexity measures. It introduces a new high-probability variant of the Exploration-by-Optimization algorithm, enabling regret guarantees against adaptive adversaries. The work provides new structural connections between the DEC, the Information Ratio, and the Exploration-by-Optimization objective, and offers a unified complexity-theoretic characterization of learnability in adversarial online learning settings.

9bf00afb0efb02a263fa3ddea1e768677498536c.title: Personalized Soups: Personalized Large Language Model Alignment via Post-hoc Parameter Merging
9bf00afb0efb02a263fa3ddea1e768677498536c.research_question: How can large language models be efficiently aligned with diverse, potentially conflicting, and personalized human preferences, rather than only general aggregate preferences?
9bf00afb0efb02a263fa3ddea1e768677498536c.hypothesis: Decomposing human preferences into multiple dimensions and training separate policy models for each preference, followed by post-hoc parameter merging, enables scalable and effective personalized alignment of large language models, outperforming or matching multitask and multi-objective reinforcement learning baselines.
9bf00afb0efb02a263fa3ddea1e768677498536c.proposed_method: The proposed methodology formulates the alignment of large language models (LLMs) with personalized human preferences as a Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning (MORL) problem. First, personalized feedback is collected along several preference dimensions (such as expertise, informativeness, and style), with each dimension containing conflicting options. Separate policy models are trained independently for each preference using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), each guided by a reward model tailored to its specific preference. During inference, the parameters of the independently trained policy models are merged on-the-fly using a weighted sum, allowing for dynamic composition of any combination of preferences without retraining. This modular approach enables efficient scaling to new preferences and avoids the exponential complexity of multitask training.
9bf00afb0efb02a263fa3ddea1e768677498536c.experiment_details: Experiments will use the Tulu-7B language model as the base, with instruction data drawn from the GPT4-Alpaca dataset (10,000 prompts). Personalized feedback is simulated using GPT-4, with smaller-scale validation from human crowdworkers. Six conflicting preferences across three dimensions are defined, resulting in eight unique preference combinations, later extended to sixteen by adding new style preferences. Baselines include vanilla (no preference), traditional RLHF, preference prompting, multitask training, and a prompted-MORL baseline. Evaluation involves generating responses for each preference combination and prompt, with win rates assessed via both simulated (GPT-4) and human evaluations using a variant of the AlpacaFarm framework. Metrics include pairwise win rate, aggregated across all preference combinations and prompts.
9bf00afb0efb02a263fa3ddea1e768677498536c.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a modular and scalable framework for personalized LLM alignment via post-hoc parameter merging, enabling efficient composition of unseen preference combinations during inference. This approach reduces computational complexity from exponential to linear with respect to the number of preferences, supports continual integration of new preferences without retraining existing models, and demonstrates superior or competitive performance compared to strong multi-objective and multitask baselines. The method also provides a practical solution for real-world personalization scenarios where user preferences are diverse and evolving.

9bf23228d120a11103ec98023d9ced19270969da.title: Multi-Robot Motion Planning with Diffusion Models
9bf23228d120a11103ec98023d9ced19270969da.research_question: How can scalable and data-efficient multi-robot motion planning be achieved in complex environments, leveraging learned behaviors from demonstrations, while avoiding the challenges of high sample complexity and the curse of dimensionality inherent in multi-robot learning?
9bf23228d120a11103ec98023d9ced19270969da.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that collision-free, data-driven multi-robot trajectories can be efficiently generated in large and complex environments by combining single-robot diffusion models with constraint-based search algorithms, thereby eliminating the need for multi-robot training data and overcoming scalability limitations.
9bf23228d120a11103ec98023d9ced19270969da.proposed_method: The proposed approach, Multi-robot Multi-model planning Diffusion (MMD), integrates single-robot diffusion models with classical multi-agent pathfinding (MAPF) search strategies to generate multi-robot trajectories that are both collision-free and conformant to demonstration data. Spatio-temporal constraints are imposed on the denoising process of diffusion models using guiding functions, with constraint placement and timing inspired by MAPF algorithms such as Conflict-Based Search (CBS), Enhanced CBS (ECBS), and Prioritized Planning (PP). Five MMD variants are developed, each leveraging different constraint strategies to coordinate robots. For scalability, multiple local diffusion models are composed sequentially, enabling long-horizon planning by stitching together local behaviors and ensuring seamless transitions between local plans. Soft and strong constraints are used to avoid collisions, and experience reuse is incorporated to accelerate replanning.
9bf23228d120a11103ec98023d9ced19270969da.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted in simulated warehouse environments with varying numbers of holonomic ground robots, using 2D disk models. Datasets consist of single-robot demonstration trajectories in maps such as Empty, Highways, Conveyor, Drop-Region, and larger composite maps. Evaluation metrics include success rate (percentage of collision-free solutions within a time limit) and data adherence (alignment of generated trajectories with demonstration patterns, using map-specific scoring functions). Baselines include a composite multi-robot diffusion model trained on joint data, MAPF algorithms with and without learned cost maps, and various MMD algorithm instantiations. Scalability is assessed by increasing the number of robots and the size of the environment, and by evaluating the ability to generate long-horizon trajectories using sequenced local models. Comparative analyses are performed to assess the effectiveness of different constraint strategies and the impact on planning time, success rate, and data adherence.
9bf23228d120a11103ec98023d9ced19270969da.novelty_claims: The proposed framework enables scalable multi-robot motion planning using only single-robot diffusion models, eliminating the need for complex multi-robot training data and breaking the curse of dimensionality. The integration of constraint-based MAPF strategies with diffusion models introduces a novel way to impose collision-avoidance and coordination in a data-driven manner. The method supports the composition of multiple local diffusion models for long-horizon planning, facilitating generalization to large and diverse environments. The approach provides a flexible and data-efficient solution that outperforms existing multi-robot diffusion and MAPF methods in terms of scalability, data adherence, and success rate.

9c0a434b240299cec0029a1be93ab263d7ec9963.title: Does Localization Inform Editing? Surprising Differences in Causality-Based Localization vs. Knowledge Editing in Language Models
9c0a434b240299cec0029a1be93ab263d7ec9963.research_question: How does the localization of factual knowledge within language model parameters relate to the effectiveness of knowledge editing interventions, and can mechanistic interpretability methods inform optimal strategies for editing model behavior?
9c0a434b240299cec0029a1be93ab263d7ec9963.hypothesis: Localization methods such as Causal Tracing, which identify where factual information is stored in language models, are predictive of which model components should be edited to successfully change or manipulate stored knowledge.
9c0a434b240299cec0029a1be93ab263d7ec9963.proposed_method: A comprehensive experimental framework will be developed to systematically investigate the relationship between causality-based localization and knowledge editing in large language models. The approach will utilize Causal Tracing to localize factual knowledge within the MLP layers of autoregressive transformer models, such as GPT-J and GPT2-XL. Multiple model editing methods—including ROME, MEMIT, and constrained finetuning—will be applied at various layers identified by localization analysis. Several variants of the editing problem will be considered, including error injection (fact rewriting), tracing reversal, fact erasure, fact amplification, and fact forcing, each targeting different objectives and input configurations. The methodology will involve both single-layer and multi-layer editing interventions, with careful measurement of the impact on model predictions.
9c0a434b240299cec0029a1be93ab263d7ec9963.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the CounterFact and ZSRE datasets, which provide factual prompts and associated completions for evaluation. For each factual assertion, Causal Tracing will be performed to estimate the information content across model layers, and editing interventions will be applied at layers with varying tracing effects. Baselines will include editing at layers suggested by localization as well as fixed early-to-mid MLP layers. Evaluation metrics will include Rewrite Score (measuring the success of fact rewriting), Paraphrase Score (generalization to paraphrased prompts), and Neighborhood Score (locality of the edit's effect). Linear regression and correlation analyses will be used to quantify the relationship between localization signals and editing success. Robustness will be assessed across different models, datasets, localization methods, editing methods, and metric variants.
9c0a434b240299cec0029a1be93ab263d7ec9963.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a systematic, fine-grained analysis of the relationship between causality-based localization and knowledge editing in language models, challenging the prevailing assumption that localization insights directly inform optimal editing strategies. By evaluating multiple editing problem variants and methods across diverse experimental conditions, the research aims to uncover whether mechanistic interpretability translates into actionable guidance for model editing. The approach is novel in its comprehensive comparison of localization signals and editing outcomes at the datapoint level, and in its introduction of new editing problem variants designed to align closely with localization objectives.

9c0d40f01ced7d425cb6145e9f961c6e44a478a8.title: 2D Gaussian Splatting for Geometrically Accurate Radiance Fields
9c0d40f01ced7d425cb6145e9f961c6e44a478a8.research_question: How can radiance fields be reconstructed from multi-view images to achieve both photorealistic novel view synthesis and geometrically accurate, noise-free surface reconstructions, while maintaining high computational efficiency?
9c0d40f01ced7d425cb6145e9f961c6e44a478a8.hypothesis: Collapsing 3D volumetric representations into a set of 2D oriented planar Gaussian disks, combined with perspective-accurate splatting and novel regularization losses, will enable more geometrically accurate, view-consistent radiance fields and surface reconstructions than existing 3D Gaussian or implicit field approaches, while also achieving real-time rendering and faster training.
9c0d40f01ced7d425cb6145e9f961c6e44a478a8.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that models 3D scenes using a set of 2D Gaussian primitives, each defined as an oriented elliptical disk embedded in 3D space. Each primitive will be parameterized by its center, two tangential vectors, scaling factors, opacity, and view-dependent appearance (using spherical harmonics). Rendering will be performed by computing explicit ray-splat intersections in homogeneous coordinates, ensuring perspective-correct splatting and view-consistent geometry. The method will employ volumetric alpha blending for image synthesis, and the geometry will be regularized using two new loss terms: a depth distortion loss to concentrate the distribution of primitives along rays, and a normal consistency loss to align the normals of splats with the gradients of rendered depth maps. Meshes will be extracted from rendered depth maps using truncated signed distance fusion.
9c0d40f01ced7d425cb6145e9f961c6e44a478a8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several multi-view datasets, including DTU, Tanks and Temples, and Mip-NeRF360. The method will be compared against state-of-the-art implicit (e.g., NeRF, VolSDF, NeuS) and explicit (e.g., 3D Gaussian Splatting, SuGaR) baselines. Evaluation will include geometry reconstruction accuracy (e.g., Chamfer distance, F1 score), appearance quality (e.g., PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS), and computational efficiency (training and inference time, model size). The experimental setup will use single-GPU training, adaptive primitive densification, and standardized mesh extraction pipelines for fair comparison. Ablation studies will isolate the effects of the proposed regularization terms and mesh extraction strategies.
9c0d40f01ced7d425cb6145e9f961c6e44a478a8.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first perspective-accurate 2D Gaussian splatting framework for radiance field reconstruction, enabling direct, view-consistent surface modeling from images without requiring ground-truth geometry. Two new regularization losses (depth distortion and normal consistency) are introduced to significantly improve surface quality and noise suppression. The method achieves state-of-the-art geometric accuracy and competitive appearance quality while being orders of magnitude faster than prior implicit methods and more efficient than existing explicit approaches. The framework also provides detailed, noise-free mesh reconstructions directly from optimized 2D disks.

9c1d24f079561af81b118d42c39eea13d8f6f6c8.title: Beyond First-Order Tweedie: Solving Inverse Problems using Latent Diffusion
9c1d24f079561af81b118d42c39eea13d8f6f6c8.research_question: How can inverse problems and image editing tasks be efficiently and accurately solved using latent diffusion models, particularly in the presence of real-world corruptions and with reduced computational cost?
9c1d24f079561af81b118d42c39eea13d8f6f6c8.hypothesis: A second-order approximation to Tweedie’s formula, implemented efficiently via a surrogate loss that only requires the trace of the Hessian, will reduce the bias inherent in first-order methods and enable high-quality, efficient posterior sampling for inverse problems and image editing using latent diffusion models.
9c1d24f079561af81b118d42c39eea13d8f6f6c8.proposed_method: A novel framework, STSL (Second-order Tweedie Sampler from Surrogate Loss), will be developed to solve inverse problems and enable robust image editing with latent diffusion models. The method will introduce a tractable reverse diffusion process using an efficient second-order approximation to Tweedie’s formula, where the drift term is updated via a surrogate loss that incorporates both data fidelity and a stochastic estimate of the Hessian trace using Hutchinson’s estimator. Initialization of the reverse process will leverage the forward process conditioned on the measurement, reducing high-dimensional sampling error. For image editing, the method will extend to text-guided tasks by integrating a contrastive loss in feature space and a cross-attention tuning mechanism, ensuring content preservation and faithful edits even under corrupted inputs. The approach will require only O(1) additional computation per step, making it practical for large-scale applications.
9c1d24f079561af81b118d42c39eea13d8f6f6c8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard benchmarks including FFHQ, ImageNet, and COCO, using tasks such as motion deblurring, super-resolution (4x and 8x), Gaussian deblurring, random inpainting, and denoising. For image editing, both clean and corrupted images will be tested, with text-guided modifications evaluated. Baselines will include state-of-the-art latent diffusion model solvers (PSLD, P2L, LDPS, GML-DPS, LDIR) and pixel-space diffusion model solvers (DPS, DiffPIR), as well as leading image editing methods (NTI, commercial software). Evaluation metrics will include LPIPS for perceptual similarity, PSNR, SSIM, and CLIP accuracy for editing tasks. The number of neural function evaluations (NFEs), runtime, and qualitative results will be reported, with ablation studies on key hyperparameters and algorithmic components.
9c1d24f079561af81b118d42c39eea13d8f6f6c8.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to provide an efficient, tractable second-order Tweedie approximation for solving inverse problems with latent diffusion models, requiring only the trace of the Hessian and avoiding expensive Jacobian or full Hessian computations. The approach enables a 4X–8X reduction in neural function evaluations compared to leading methods, while improving reconstruction and editing quality, especially under real-world corruptions. The framework is the first to extend efficient second-order latent diffusion to text-guided image editing with corrupted inputs, overcoming limitations of prior methods in both computational efficiency and fidelity.

9c1ee33b3db71625acca17921cad7fab8afd6321.title: Multi-scale Temporal Prediction via Incremental Generation and Multi-agent Collaboration
9c1ee33b3db71625acca17921cad7fab8afd6321.research_question: How can temporal prediction of fine-grained scene states at multiple temporal and state scales be improved for both general and surgical environments, enabling reliable, coherent, and interpretable forecasting for embodied AI systems?
9c1ee33b3db71625acca17921cad7fab8afd6321.hypothesis: A unified framework that combines incremental generation of state-image pairs with a decision-driven multi-agent collaboration mechanism will enable accurate, robust, and temporally coherent multi-scale temporal prediction across diverse domains and hierarchical state structures.
9c1ee33b3db71625acca17921cad7fab8afd6321.proposed_method: A novel closed-loop framework is proposed that decomposes multi-scale temporal prediction into two orthogonal dimensions: temporal scale (forecasting at varying look-ahead intervals) and state scale (modeling hierarchical scene states). The methodology involves an incremental generation process that alternates between predicting future hierarchical states and synthesizing corresponding visual previews using a modified Stable Diffusion model. A decision-driven multi-agent collaboration system is introduced, where a State Transition Controller (STC) agent determines when and at which hierarchy level state transitions should occur, triggering a cascade of specialized VLM-based agents to refine predictions from coarse to fine granularity. The visual generation module conditions on both predicted states and prior visual context, ensuring procedural and anatomical plausibility through cross-attention, residual connections, and latent space projections. The DM (decision-making) and VG (visual generation) modules are trained separately for modularity and are integrated during inference, forming a feedback loop that enables real-time error correction and cross-scale consistency.
9c1ee33b3db71625acca17921cad7fab8afd6321.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the newly introduced MSTP Benchmark, which provides synchronized multi-scale annotations for both general (Action Genome dataset) and surgical (GraSP dataset) scenes. The evaluation will cover multiple temporal scales (e.g., 1s, 5s, 30s, 60s) and hierarchical state levels (e.g., attention, spatial, contacting for general scenes; phase and step for surgical scenes). Baselines will include state-of-the-art vision-language models such as Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, with and without the proposed DM and VG modules. Evaluation metrics will encompass state prediction (Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1 Score, Jaccard) and visual prediction (PSNR, SSIM, MS-SSIM, LPIPS, CLIPScore, FID, KID, R-precision). Ablation studies will assess the individual and combined contributions of the DM and VG modules. The experimental setup will also examine the framework's adaptability to different incremental and temporal scales, as well as its generalization to diverse real-world scenarios.
9c1ee33b3db71625acca17921cad7fab8afd6321.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first incremental generation mechanism for multi-scale temporal prediction that maintains state-visual synchronization and enables error correction over long horizons. A decision-driven multi-agent collaboration framework is developed, leveraging specialized VLM-based agents to hierarchically refine state predictions and enforce cross-scale consistency. The MSTP Benchmark is established as the first dataset with synchronized annotations across both temporal and state hierarchies for comprehensive evaluation. The integrated IG-MC framework is claimed to be a generalizable, plug-and-play solution that significantly advances multi-scale prediction accuracy, robustness, and interpretability in both general and surgical embodied AI settings.

9c4753ef43d2928866dc5bf6cec53d03373ec2fa.title: SimMIM: a Simple Framework for Masked Image Modeling
9c4753ef43d2928866dc5bf6cec53d03373ec2fa.research_question: How can a simple masked image modeling framework be designed to effectively learn visual representations for downstream vision tasks, without relying on complex architectural or pretext task modifications?
9c4753ef43d2928866dc5bf6cec53d03373ec2fa.hypothesis: A masked image modeling framework that employs random masking of image patches, direct regression of raw pixel values, and a lightweight prediction head can achieve strong representation learning performance comparable to or better than more complex methods.
9c4753ef43d2928866dc5bf6cec53d03373ec2fa.proposed_method: A novel framework for masked image modeling is proposed, where a portion of input image patches is randomly masked and replaced with a learnable mask token. The masked image is processed by a vision Transformer encoder (such as ViT or Swin Transformer) to extract latent features. A lightweight prediction head, typically a single linear layer, is used to regress the raw RGB pixel values of the masked patches using an L1 loss. The method systematically explores masking strategies (patch sizes and ratios), prediction targets (raw pixel regression vs. discretized classification), and prediction head architectures. The approach emphasizes simplicity by avoiding special designs such as block-wise masking, tokenization via discrete VAE, or clustering.
9c4753ef43d2928866dc5bf6cec53d03373ec2fa.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using large-scale datasets such as ImageNet-1K for both pre-training and fine-tuning. The framework is evaluated on multiple downstream tasks, including image classification (ImageNet-1K, iNaturalist 2018), object detection (COCO), and semantic segmentation (ADE20K). Baselines include supervised training, contrastive learning methods (e.g., DINO, MoCo v3), and prior masked image modeling approaches (e.g., BEiT, iGPT). Evaluation metrics include top-1 accuracy for classification, mAP for detection, and mIoU for segmentation. Ablation studies are performed to analyze the effects of masking strategies, prediction head complexity, prediction targets, and pre-training resolutions. Scaling experiments are conducted on various model sizes, including Swin-B, Swin-L, SwinV2-H, and SwinV2-G, with comparisons to state-of-the-art supervised and self-supervised methods.
9c4753ef43d2928866dc5bf6cec53d03373ec2fa.novelty_claims: The proposed framework achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on multiple vision benchmarks using a much simpler design than prior masked image modeling methods. Key innovations include the use of random patch-wise masking with moderately large patch sizes, direct regression of raw pixel values, and an extremely lightweight prediction head. The approach demonstrates strong scalability to large models and data efficiency, enabling the training of billion-parameter models with significantly less labeled data. The findings challenge the necessity of complex masking or tokenization strategies and provide new insights into the design of self-supervised visual pretext tasks.

9c5062743eaace5c1ff822bba819031f05cd3106.title: StableSSM: Alleviating the Curse of Memory in State-space Models through Stable Reparameterization
9c5062743eaace5c1ff822bba819031f05cd3106.research_question: How can the memory limitations inherent in state-space models (SSMs) be alleviated to enable stable learning and approximation of long-term dependencies in sequential data across various domains?
9c5062743eaace5c1ff822bba819031f05cd3106.hypothesis: Introducing a class of stable reparameterization techniques for the recurrent weights in state-space models will enable stable approximation of nonlinear functionals with long-term (non-exponential) memory, overcoming the curse of memory and improving both approximation and optimization stability.
9c5062743eaace5c1ff822bba819031f05cd3106.proposed_method: A new class of reparameterization techniques for the recurrent weights in state-space models will be developed, termed 'stable reparameterizations.' These techniques will be theoretically characterized to ensure that the resulting models can stably approximate any nonlinear functionals with decaying memory, not just those with exponential decay. The approach involves deriving the mathematical properties required for a reparameterization to be stable, including conditions on the function form and its derivatives, and proposing specific functional forms (such as softplus, exponential, and a theoretically optimal inverse quadratic form). The method will also analyze the impact of these reparameterizations on the gradient scale during optimization, deriving bounds that guarantee improved training stability. Theoretical claims will be supported by solving relevant differential equations and providing proofs of universal approximation and stability properties.
