9c5062743eaace5c1ff822bba819031f05cd3106.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic datasets designed to test long-term memory, such as learning linear functionals with polynomially decaying memory, as well as on real-world tasks including language modeling (e.g., WikiText-103) and image classification (e.g., MNIST, CIFAR-10). Baseline comparisons will include vanilla SSMs without reparameterization, SSMs with commonly used reparameterizations (e.g., exponential, softplus), and the proposed optimal stable reparameterization. Evaluation metrics will include approximation error, gradient-over-weight ratios during training, training stability (e.g., convergence under large learning rates), and downstream task performance (e.g., accuracy or loss on classification and language modeling benchmarks). Additional benchmarking will be performed on the Long Range Arena to assess performance on long-sequence tasks. Experiments will be repeated with varying learning rates to assess robustness and optimization stability.
9c5062743eaace5c1ff822bba819031f05cd3106.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretically grounded class of stable reparameterization functions for SSMs, enabling stable approximation of targets with arbitrary decaying memory, which is not possible with standard parameterizations. It establishes a direct link between parameterization, memory decay properties, and optimization stability, including a novel criterion for the 'best' parameterization based on gradient scale Lipschitz continuity. The approach provides both theoretical guarantees and practical algorithms for overcoming the curse of memory in SSMs, and demonstrates improved training stability and performance across a range of tasks and learning rates. The proposal also offers a principled method for designing reparameterizations that optimize both approximation and optimization stability, advancing the scalability and effectiveness of state-space models for long-sequence modeling.

9c5f056c4e7986064722bb522e46e3546be8da51.title: A Review of Safe Reinforcement Learning: Methods, Theory and Applications
9c5f056c4e7986064722bb522e46e3546be8da51.research_question: How can reinforcement learning algorithms be developed and analyzed to ensure safety in real-world applications across diverse domains, and what are the fundamental challenges and benchmarks necessary for advancing safe RL research?
9c5f056c4e7986064722bb522e46e3546be8da51.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by systematically addressing key safety-related questions—such as safe policy optimization, sample complexity, application domains, benchmark design, and core challenges—safe RL algorithms can be made more reliable and applicable to real-world scenarios.
9c5f056c4e7986064722bb522e46e3546be8da51.proposed_method: A comprehensive research program will be established to systematically investigate safe reinforcement learning (RL) from five critical perspectives: (1) developing and analyzing algorithms for safe policy optimization under constraints, using frameworks such as Constrained Markov Decision Processes (CMDPs) and incorporating primal-dual, trust region, formal verification, control theory, and Gaussian process-based methods; (2) quantifying and improving the sample complexity required for safe RL convergence, with a focus on both value-based and policy-based approaches; (3) cataloging and evaluating real-world and simulated applications of safe RL, including domains such as autonomous driving, robotics, video compression, and resource allocation; (4) designing and standardizing benchmarks that balance reward and safety objectives, with careful attention to cost and reward function specification; and (5) identifying and addressing open challenges, such as human and environmental safety, adversarial robustness, and multi-agent safety dilemmas. The research will involve both theoretical analysis and empirical validation.
9c5f056c4e7986064722bb522e46e3546be8da51.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a suite of established and novel safe RL benchmarks, including AI Safety Gridworlds, Safety Gym, Safe MAMuJoCo, Safe MAIG, and Safe MARobosuite. Multiple safe RL algorithms, encompassing both model-based and model-free paradigms, will be implemented and compared against standard RL baselines and existing safe RL methods. Evaluation metrics will include cumulative reward, safety constraint satisfaction (e.g., cost bounds), sample efficiency, and robustness to adversarial conditions. The experimental setup will include both single-agent and multi-agent environments, with a focus on scalability and real-world applicability.
9c5f056c4e7986064722bb522e46e3546be8da51.novelty_claims: The proposed research offers a unified and comprehensive framework for safe RL, systematically addressing five foundational problems ("2H3W") that have not been holistically treated in prior work. Novel contributions include in-depth theoretical analysis of sample complexity for safe RL, detailed examination and standardization of safety benchmarks, and the integration of diverse algorithmic approaches under a common evaluation protocol. The research also aims to bridge the gap between theoretical advances and practical deployment, providing actionable insights and open-source resources to accelerate progress in safe RL.

9c8f548b85af8d3c861c9d97b6172c4ee44673d6.title: Inference-Time Scaling for Diffusion Models beyond Scaling Denoising Steps
9c8f548b85af8d3c861c9d97b6172c4ee44673d6.research_question: How can the performance of diffusion models be further improved at inference time by increasing computational resources, beyond simply scaling the number of denoising steps? What new frameworks or strategies can be developed to more effectively utilize inference-time compute for generative tasks across different application scenarios?
9c8f548b85af8d3c861c9d97b6172c4ee44673d6.hypothesis: Allocating additional inference-time computation to a structured search over sampling noises—guided by appropriate verifiers and search algorithms—will yield substantial improvements in the quality of samples generated by diffusion models, surpassing the gains achieved by merely increasing the number of denoising steps.
9c8f548b85af8d3c861c9d97b6172c4ee44673d6.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed for inference-time scaling in diffusion models that formulates the generation process as a search problem over initial sampling noises. The design space is structured along two axes: (1) the choice of verifiers, which are functions or pre-trained models that provide scalar feedback on the quality of generated samples (with or without conditioning information), and (2) the choice of search algorithms, which determine how candidate noises are generated and refined based on verifier feedback. Three primary search algorithms are considered: Random Search (best-of-N selection from random noise candidates), Zero-Order Search (iterative local search in the noise space using verifier feedback), and Search over Paths (iterative refinement along the sampling trajectory). The framework is instantiated for both class-conditioned and text-conditioned image generation, with careful control of the total number of function evaluations (NFEs) to measure inference-time compute.
9c8f548b85af8d3c861c9d97b6172c4ee44673d6.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both class-conditioned and text-conditioned image generation tasks. For class-conditioned generation, the ImageNet dataset is used with a pre-trained SiT-XL model at 256x256 resolution, and evaluations are performed using FID and Inception Score as metrics. For text-conditioned generation, the DrawBench and T2I-CompBench datasets are employed, using the FLUX.1-dev model as the backbone. Multiple verifiers are tested, including Oracle Verifiers (using FID/IS directly), Supervised Verifiers (CLIP, DINO, Aesthetic Score Predictor, CLIPScore, ImageReward), Self-Supervised Verifiers (feature similarity scores), and a Verifier Ensemble (combining multiple supervised verifiers). Baselines include standard diffusion sampling with increased denoising steps. Evaluation metrics for text-to-image tasks include Aesthetic Score, CLIPScore, ImageReward, and LLM-based grading (Gemini-1.5) across several qualitative aspects. The number of NFEs allocated to denoising versus search is systematically varied to analyze scaling behaviors.
9c8f548b85af8d3c861c9d97b6172c4ee44673d6.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a fundamental and extensible framework for inference-time scaling in diffusion models that goes beyond the conventional approach of increasing denoising steps. Key innovations include the formulation of sampling as a search over noise candidates, the explicit separation of verifier and search algorithm design axes, and the demonstration that different verifier–algorithm combinations are optimal for different tasks. The approach enables substantial improvements in sample quality by leveraging additional inference-time compute, and provides new insights into verifier alignment, biases, and the generalizability of ensemble verifiers. The framework is validated across diverse generative tasks and model scales, offering a principled path for scalable, application-specific inference-time optimization in diffusion models.

9c9eac9dbd953f257c0d94a5fc8b0a20d8d2fe17.title: Scaling and renormalization in high-dimensional regression
9c9eac9dbd953f257c0d94a5fc8b0a20d8d2fe17.research_question: How can scaling laws and generalization phenomena in high-dimensional regression models, including linear, kernel, and random feature models, be analytically characterized and unified using tools from random matrix theory and free probability? What are the fundamental sources and regimes of power-law scaling in model performance as a function of dataset and model size?
9c9eac9dbd953f257c0d94a5fc8b0a20d8d2fe17.hypothesis: Statistical fluctuations in empirical covariance matrices in high-dimensional regression can be systematically absorbed into a renormalization of the ridge parameter, enabling analytic characterization of training and generalization errors across a broad class of models. The S-transform from free probability provides a unifying framework to derive these results and identify distinct scaling regimes, including variance- and resolution-limited regimes.
9c9eac9dbd953f257c0d94a5fc8b0a20d8d2fe17.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops a unified analytical framework for high-dimensional regression models by leveraging random matrix theory, specifically the S-transform from free probability. Empirical covariance matrices are modeled as multiplicatively noised versions of population covariances, and deterministic equivalence principles are used to replace random sample covariances with their population counterparts in key expressions. The S-transform is applied to characterize the impact of multiplicative noise on the ridge parameter, enabling closed-form derivations of training and generalization errors for linear, kernel, and random feature models. Fine-grained bias-variance decompositions are derived for models with structured covariates, and the framework is extended to cases with additive feature noise and anisotropic weight structures. The methodology allows for identification and characterization of distinct scaling regimes and the derivation of analytic scaling exponents in terms of data and model properties.
9c9eac9dbd953f257c0d94a5fc8b0a20d8d2fe17.experiment_details: Experiments will involve both theoretical derivations and empirical validation using synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic datasets will be generated with controlled covariance structures and varying dimensionality to test the analytic predictions of training and generalization errors under different scaling regimes. Random feature models with varying degrees of structure and noise will be evaluated. Baselines will include classical ridge regression, kernel regression, and previously established random feature models. Evaluation metrics will focus on training error, generalization error, bias-variance decomposition, and the scaling exponents of these quantities as functions of model and dataset size. Empirical results will be compared to the analytic formulas derived using the S-transform framework to validate the deterministic equivalence and scaling law predictions.
9c9eac9dbd953f257c0d94a5fc8b0a20d8d2fe17.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified and parsimonious analytical framework for high-dimensional regression models using the S-transform, enabling closed-form derivations of training and generalization errors across linear, kernel, and random feature models. Novel contributions include the identification of renormalization effects in ridge parameters due to empirical covariance fluctuations, new formulas for fine-grained bias-variance decompositions in structured random feature models, and the discovery of previously uncharacterized scaling regimes where finite-width effects dominate even in overparameterized settings. The approach also yields new analytic results for models with additive feature noise and anisotropic weights, and provides a comprehensive characterization of all scaling regimes in random feature models.

9ca078fb77ca0cdc6826d06f175c0b6c7c5e225b.title: Optimal Transport Aggregation for Visual Place Recognition
9ca078fb77ca0cdc6826d06f175c0b6c7c5e225b.research_question: How can the aggregation of local visual features for visual place recognition be improved to achieve robust and efficient matching across challenging variations in appearance, structure, and environmental conditions?
9ca078fb77ca0cdc6826d06f175c0b6c7c5e225b.hypothesis: Reformulating the feature-to-cluster assignment as an optimal transport problem, combined with fine-tuning a powerful vision transformer backbone, will yield more discriminative and robust global image descriptors for visual place recognition, outperforming existing aggregation and feature extraction methods.
9ca078fb77ca0cdc6826d06f175c0b6c7c5e225b.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that integrates a fine-tuned DINOv2 Vision Transformer backbone for local feature extraction with a new aggregation module, SALAD (Sinkhorn Algorithm for Locally Aggregated Descriptors). Local features and a global token are extracted from input images using DINOv2, with the last blocks of the encoder selectively unfrozen and trained specifically for the visual place recognition task. The aggregation process reformulates the assignment of local features to clusters as an optimal transport problem, solved via the Sinkhorn algorithm, which considers both feature-to-cluster and cluster-to-feature relations. A 'dustbin' cluster is introduced to allow the network to discard non-informative features, enhancing descriptor quality. Dimensionality reduction is applied to feature vectors before aggregation, and the final global descriptor is formed by concatenating the aggregated features and the global token, followed by normalization.
9ca078fb77ca0cdc6826d06f175c0b6c7c5e225b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of public visual place recognition benchmarks, including MSLS Challenge, MSLS Validation, Nordland, Pitts250k-test, SPED, and SF-XL. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art single-stage and two-stage baselines such as NetVLAD, GeM, Conv-AP, CosPlace, MixVPR, EigenPlaces, Patch-NetVLAD, TransVPR, and R2Former. Evaluation metrics will include Recall@k (R@1, R@5, R@10), descriptor size, inference latency, and memory footprint. Training will use the GSV-Cities dataset, with the DINOv2 backbone fine-tuned for four epochs using the multi-similarity loss and AdamW optimizer. Ablation studies will assess the impact of backbone choice, aggregation module, dimensionality reduction, dustbin mechanism, and number of fine-tuned transformer blocks.
9ca078fb77ca0cdc6826d06f175c0b6c7c5e225b.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first application of optimal transport for local feature aggregation in visual place recognition, replacing traditional soft-assignment with a theoretically sound and empirically effective Sinkhorn-based assignment. The integration of a fine-tuned DINOv2 backbone, rather than using it in a frozen state, is shown to significantly enhance performance and reduce training time. The dustbin mechanism for discarding non-informative features further improves descriptor quality. The resulting single-stage pipeline achieves unprecedented recall on challenging VPR benchmarks, surpassing both single-stage and computationally expensive two-stage methods, while maintaining high efficiency in terms of speed and memory usage.

9ca72cef4487494cd835e7abca65794407db62ee.title: Navigation World Models
9ca72cef4487494cd835e7abca65794407db62ee.research_question: How can a generalizable, data-driven world model be developed to enable agents with visual-motor capabilities to plan and execute navigation trajectories in both familiar and unfamiliar environments using only egocentric video and navigation actions, without relying on explicit 3D priors or reward signals?
9ca72cef4487494cd835e7abca65794407db62ee.hypothesis: A scalable, conditional diffusion transformer-based world model trained on diverse egocentric video and navigation action data can accurately simulate future observations, plan constraint-aware navigation trajectories, and generalize to novel environments, thereby improving visual navigation performance over existing methods.
9ca72cef4487494cd835e7abca65794407db62ee.proposed_method: A Navigation World Model (NWM) will be developed as a controllable video generation model that predicts future visual observations based on past observations and navigation actions. The core architecture will be a Conditional Diffusion Transformer (CDiT), which is a temporally autoregressive transformer block designed for efficient scaling (up to 1 billion parameters) and linear computational complexity with respect to context frames. The model will encode past image states using a pretrained VAE, condition on navigation actions (translation and rotation), and optionally a time-shift parameter, using sine-cosine feature embeddings and MLPs. During training, the model will minimize a denoising loss to reconstruct future latent states from noisy versions, conditioned on context and actions. For planning, the trained NWM will be used in a Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework, optimizing action sequences via the Cross-Entropy Method to reach a goal state, subject to possible constraints on actions or states. The model will also be used to rank trajectories from external policies by simulating and scoring them according to perceptual similarity to the goal.
9ca72cef4487494cd835e7abca65794407db62ee.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of robotics navigation datasets (SCAND, TartanDrive, RECON, HuRoN) with access to egocentric video and precise navigation actions, as well as on unlabeled video data (Ego4D) for out-of-distribution generalization. Evaluation will include both known (in-domain) and unknown (out-of-domain) environments, with GoStanford serving as an unseen test set. Baselines will include state-of-the-art navigation policies such as GNM and NoMaD, as well as diffusion-based world models like DIAMOND. Metrics will include Absolute Trajectory Error (ATE), Relative Pose Error (RPE), LPIPS and DreamSim for perceptual similarity, PSNR for pixel-level quality, and FID/FVD for video generation quality. Ablation studies will examine the effects of context size, number of goals, and conditioning on time and actions. Both standalone planning and trajectory ranking scenarios will be evaluated, including constraint-aware planning.
9ca72cef4487494cd835e7abca65794407db62ee.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a scalable, conditional diffusion transformer architecture (CDiT) for world modeling with linear complexity in context length, enabling efficient training up to 1B parameters. Unlike prior works, the method is trained across diverse environments and embodiments, leveraging both robotic and human egocentric video data, and does not rely on explicit 3D priors or reward signals. The NWM enables flexible, constraint-aware planning and can generalize to novel environments by leveraging unlabeled video data. The approach also demonstrates improved video prediction and generation quality, and achieves state-of-the-art or competitive results in both standalone planning and trajectory ranking for visual navigation tasks.

9cb218cfa99269ae346de6d380d9b174c2c4fc7f.title: ODICE: Revealing the Mystery of Distribution Correction Estimation via Orthogonal-gradient Update
9cb218cfa99269ae346de6d380d9b174c2c4fc7f.research_question: How can state-action-level behavior constraints be effectively imposed in offline reinforcement learning and imitation learning to improve robustness and performance, particularly in the presence of out-of-distribution (OOD) states and actions?
9cb218cfa99269ae346de6d380d9b174c2c4fc7f.hypothesis: Introducing an orthogonal-gradient update rule for DICE-based methods will enable effective state-action-level behavior constraint, leading to improved robustness against OOD states and superior empirical performance compared to existing action-level and state-action-level constraint methods.
9cb218cfa99269ae346de6d380d9b174c2c4fc7f.proposed_method: A novel orthogonal-gradient update rule is developed for DICE-based offline RL and imitation learning algorithms. The method decomposes the value function learning gradient into forward (on current state) and backward (on next state) components. The backward gradient is projected onto the normal plane of the forward gradient, ensuring orthogonality and preventing destructive interference between the two. This orthogonal-gradient update is incorporated into the V-DICE algorithm to form O-DICE, which alternates between value function updates using the new rule and policy extraction via weighted behavior cloning. Practical considerations include the use of bidirectional target networks for stable gradient computation and a hyperparameter to balance the strength of the projected backward gradient.
9cb218cfa99269ae346de6d380d9b174c2c4fc7f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the D4RL benchmark, including MuJoCo locomotion and AntMaze navigation tasks, as well as on offline imitation learning settings with limited expert trajectories. O-DICE will be compared against strong baselines such as TD3+BC, CQL, IQL, EQL (action-level constraint methods), and DICE-based methods like OptiDICE, f-DVL, and S-DICE. Evaluation metrics will include normalized return, robustness (measured by percent difference of the worst episode), and feature dot-product statistics to assess feature co-adaptation. Multiple random seeds and final evaluation averages will be used to ensure statistical significance and robustness analysis.
9cb218cfa99269ae346de6d380d9b174c2c4fc7f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the orthogonal-gradient update, a new learning rule for DICE-based methods that resolves the conflict between forward and backward gradients in value learning. This approach provides both theoretical convergence guarantees and practical robustness to OOD states, addressing the limitations of prior true-gradient and semi-gradient DICE algorithms. The method achieves state-of-the-art performance on standard offline RL and IL benchmarks, demonstrates improved robustness and stability, and offers a principled way to impose state-action-level constraints without requiring costly model-based OOD detection.

9cd511766bfda9ba5abc85bd40f25f87c09c6e48.title: Towards Unsupervised Object Detection from LiDAR Point Clouds
9cd511766bfda9ba5abc85bd40f25f87c09c6e48.research_question: Can unsupervised object detection be achieved from 3D LiDAR point clouds in self-driving scenarios, without relying on human annotations, repeated traversals, or other strong data collection constraints?
9cd511766bfda9ba5abc85bd40f25f87c09c6e48.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a combination of spatial clustering, temporal consistency, translation equivariance of convolutional neural networks, and iterative self-supervision can enable effective unsupervised object detection from raw LiDAR point clouds, even in challenging long-range and sparse observation settings.
9cd511766bfda9ba5abc85bd40f25f87c09c6e48.proposed_method: A novel framework, OYSTER (Object Discovery via Spatio-Temporal Refinement), is proposed for unsupervised object detection from LiDAR point clouds. The method begins with a bootstrapping phase that uses density-based spatial clustering (DBSCAN) on near-range, dense point clouds to generate initial pseudo-labels after ground removal and bounding box fitting. A convolutional neural network (CNN) detector is then trained on these near-range pseudo-labels, leveraging translation equivariance and a random LiDAR ray-dropping augmentation to enable zero-shot generalization to long-range, sparse regions. In the self-improvement phase, unsupervised tracking is applied to filter out temporally inconsistent detections, and a Track, Refine, Retrain, and Repeat loop is established: object tracks are refined using temporal consistency (e.g., aligning bounding box sizes and positions across time), short or inconsistent tracks are filtered out, and the refined pseudo-labels are used for further rounds of detector retraining. This iterative process allows the detector to self-improve and adapt to more challenging detection scenarios without human supervision.
9cd511766bfda9ba5abc85bd40f25f87c09c6e48.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two real-world autonomous driving datasets: PandaSet and Argoverse 2 Sensor (AV2), covering diverse urban and highway environments. The evaluation will be class-agnostic, focusing on detecting any object (vehicles, cyclists, pedestrians) within a region of interest up to 80 meters. Baselines will include density-based clustering (DBSCAN), clustering with self-training, and state-of-the-art unsupervised methods such as PPscore and MODEST. Evaluation metrics will include Average Precision (AP) and Recall at various Intersection-over-Union (IoU) thresholds, as well as a novel planning-centric metric based on distance-to-collision (DTC), which measures how accurately the closest point of detected objects to the ego-vehicle is predicted. The experimental setup will limit the number of detections per frame and include ablation studies to assess the impact of each component (e.g., ray-dropping, temporal filtering, iterative self-training).
9cd511766bfda9ba5abc85bd40f25f87c09c6e48.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified framework that combines spatial clustering, temporal consistency, translation equivariance, and self-supervised iterative refinement for unsupervised object detection from LiDAR point clouds. It eliminates the need for repeated traversals, scene flow estimation, or camera inputs, making it applicable to any raw LiDAR sequence. The method also proposes a novel random LiDAR ray-dropping augmentation to bridge the density gap between near and far ranges, and a new planning-centric evaluation metric based on distance-to-collision. Iterative self-training with temporal refinement enables the detector to discover and improve object detection performance autonomously, significantly outperforming existing unsupervised baselines on real-world datasets.

9cd6c6d85de6180dd92ba43e685663067cf3ab7f.title: Grounded SAM: Assembling Open-World Models for Diverse Visual Tasks
9cd6c6d85de6180dd92ba43e685663067cf3ab7f.research_question: How can a modular and extensible framework be developed to enable open-vocabulary detection and segmentation, as well as support a wide range of open-world visual tasks, by assembling and integrating multiple expert models?
9cd6c6d85de6180dd92ba43e685663067cf3ab7f.hypothesis: Integrating open-set object detection models with promptable segmentation models, and further assembling additional expert models for tasks such as image captioning, tagging, generation, and human motion analysis, will enable a flexible, scalable, and high-performing system for diverse open-world visual perception and manipulation tasks.
9cd6c6d85de6180dd92ba43e685663067cf3ab7f.proposed_method: A novel framework will be designed that combines an open-set object detector (such as Grounding DINO) with a promptable segmentation model (such as SAM) to achieve open-vocabulary detection and segmentation. The system will accept arbitrary text prompts and images, first using the detector to localize relevant regions or objects via bounding boxes conditioned on the text, and then passing these boxes to the segmentation model to generate precise masks. The modular architecture will allow seamless integration of additional expert models, such as image captioning (BLIP), image tagging (RAM), generative models (Stable Diffusion), and 3D human mesh recovery (OSX), enabling automatic dense annotation, highly controllable image editing, and promptable human motion analysis. The pipeline will be training-free at the assembly level, leveraging the strengths of each expert model for stepwise visual reasoning and complex task decomposition.
9cd6c6d85de6180dd92ba43e685663067cf3ab7f.experiment_details: The effectiveness of the proposed framework will be evaluated on the Segmentation in the Wild (SGinW) zero-shot benchmark, which includes 25 diverse real-world datasets. Experiments will compare the proposed system (using various combinations of Grounding DINO and SAM variants, including HQ-SAM) against state-of-the-art baselines such as X-Decoder, OpenSeeD, ODISE, SAN-CLIP, and UNINEXT. Evaluation metrics will include mean Average Precision (mAP) and other standard segmentation and detection metrics. Additional experiments will demonstrate the extensibility of the framework by integrating models for automatic dense image annotation, image editing, and human motion analysis, with qualitative and quantitative results reported for each application.
9cd6c6d85de6180dd92ba43e685663067cf3ab7f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach pioneers a modular and extensible model assembly paradigm for open-world visual tasks, enabling seamless integration of multiple expert models without the need for large language model controllers. The framework achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot open-vocabulary segmentation performance and supports a wide range of downstream tasks, including automatic dense annotation, controllable image editing, and promptable human motion analysis. The system is highly flexible, explainable, and scalable, allowing for rapid expansion to new tasks by incorporating additional expert models. The approach also significantly reduces annotation costs and enables closed-loop data generation and model improvement.

9ced6e814457eae83f5415364e266143defc81d1.title: MultiDiffusion: Fusing Diffusion Paths for Controlled Image Generation
9ced6e814457eae83f5415364e266143defc81d1.research_question: How can controllability and adaptability in text-to-image diffusion models be improved to enable flexible, high-quality, and user-guided image generation without requiring retraining or fine-tuning of the underlying model?
9ced6e814457eae83f5415364e266143defc81d1.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a unified generation framework, which fuses multiple diffusion paths from a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model through an optimization process with shared parameters or constraints, can enable versatile and controllable image generation while maintaining high image quality and efficiency.
9ced6e814457eae83f5415364e266143defc81d1.proposed_method: A novel generation process, termed MultiDiffusion, will be developed to operate on top of a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model without any additional training or fine-tuning. The approach defines an optimization task at each denoising step, where multiple diffusion generation processes—each corresponding to a different region or control signal—are bound together via a shared set of parameters or constraints. For each generation step, the method reconciles the denoising directions suggested by the reference model for different image crops or regions using a least-squares objective, resulting in a global denoising step that produces a coherent and seamless image. The method supports various forms of user control, such as aspect ratio, spatial guidance through segmentation masks or bounding boxes, and can be analytically solved for many tasks, ensuring computational efficiency and convergence to a global optimum.
9ced6e814457eae83f5415364e266143defc81d1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the publicly available Stable Diffusion model as the reference diffusion model, operating in a latent space with a decoder for high-resolution image reconstruction. The method will be evaluated on tasks such as panoramic image generation (arbitrary aspect ratios) and region-based text-to-image generation (using segmentation masks or bounding boxes as spatial guidance). Baselines for comparison will include Blended Latent Diffusion (BLD), Stable Inpainting (SI), and, for region-based tasks, Make-A-Scene and SpaText, which are specifically trained for these tasks. Evaluation metrics will include Frechet Inception Distance (FID), CLIP text-image similarity, CLIP aesthetic scores, and Intersection over Union (IoU) for segmentation fidelity. Both quantitative and qualitative analyses will be performed, with ablation studies to assess the impact of bootstrapping mechanisms for mask fidelity.
9ced6e814457eae83f5415364e266143defc81d1.novelty_claims: The proposed framework enables versatile and controllable image generation using a pre-trained diffusion model without any further training or fine-tuning. It introduces a unified optimization-based generation process that can flexibly adapt to various user controls, such as aspect ratio and spatial guidance, in a principled and efficient manner. The method analytically fuses multiple diffusion paths into a coherent global generation process, achieving state-of-the-art controlled generation quality even compared to methods specifically trained for these tasks, and does so without computational overhead.

9d0152fd0d992fa52280d2f83d6aa41490ad95aa.title: Unlocking State-Tracking in Linear RNNs Through Negative Eigenvalues
9d0152fd0d992fa52280d2f83d6aa41490ad95aa.research_question: How can the expressivity and state-tracking capabilities of linear recurrent neural networks (LRNNs) be enhanced to solve tasks that require tracking the state of finite automata, such as parity, modular arithmetic, and complex group word problems, without sacrificing efficiency or training stability?
9d0152fd0d992fa52280d2f83d6aa41490ad95aa.hypothesis: Extending the eigenvalue range of LRNN state-transition matrices from [0,1] to [−1,1] will enable these models to solve state-tracking tasks, including those that require implementing non-trivial finite state automata, and will improve their performance on tasks such as code evaluation and mathematical reasoning, while maintaining computational efficiency and training stability.
9d0152fd0d992fa52280d2f83d6aa41490ad95aa.proposed_method: The proposed approach modifies the state-transition matrices of LRNNs, specifically in architectures such as Mamba and DeltaNet, to allow their eigenvalues to span the interval [−1,1] instead of being restricted to [0,1]. For diagonal LRNNs, this is achieved by transforming the diagonal entries as 2s(x)−1, where s(x) is the original parameterization. For non-diagonal LRNNs using generalized Householder (GH) matrices, the modification involves setting the unique nontrivial eigenvalue to 1−2ϕ(x), where ϕ(x) is a learnable function, thus extending the possible range to include negative values. The method preserves the norm of the state-transition matrices to ensure stable recurrences for long sequences and is compatible with efficient matrix-vector product computation. Theoretical analysis is conducted to establish the necessity of negative or complex eigenvalues for solving parity and modular counting, and to demonstrate that products of GH matrices with eigenvalues in [−1,1] can implement any regular language.
9d0152fd0d992fa52280d2f83d6aa41490ad95aa.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both synthetic formal language tasks (parity, modular arithmetic with and without brackets) and real-world language modeling datasets. For formal language tasks, models are trained on sequence lengths up to 40 and evaluated on lengths up to 256, assessing generalization to longer sequences. Baselines include Transformers, mLSTM, sLSTM, and both original and modified (eigenvalue-extended) versions of Mamba and DeltaNet. Evaluation metrics include scaled accuracy for formal tasks and sequence accuracy for group word problems (e.g., S_5 and Z_60). For large-scale language modeling, models with up to 1.3B parameters are pre-trained on the FineWeb-100B dataset and evaluated on benchmarks such as CodeParrot, Math-Hard, TriviaQA, and SlimPajama, using perplexity and lm-harness accuracy as metrics. The effect of the eigenvalue range extension is compared across all tasks and model sizes.
9d0152fd0d992fa52280d2f83d6aa41490ad95aa.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a simple yet powerful modification to LRNNs that extends the eigenvalue range of their state-transition matrices, enabling them to solve state-tracking tasks previously out of reach for linear architectures. Theoretical contributions include proofs that negative or complex eigenvalues are necessary for solving parity and modular counting, and that products of generalized Householder matrices with eigenvalues in [−1,1] suffice to implement any regular language. Empirical results demonstrate, for the first time, that LRNNs with extended eigenvalue ranges can be efficiently trained at scale and achieve improved or competitive performance on both synthetic and real-world tasks, particularly in domains requiring state-tracking such as code and mathematics. The approach maintains computational efficiency and training stability, and provides a new direction for enhancing the expressivity of efficient sequence models.

9d1bf8082e2e5c6ddea2b00456ec7e8b91a1ea9d.title: Towards Physical Understanding in Video Generation: A 3D Point Regularization Approach
9d1bf8082e2e5c6ddea2b00456ec7e8b91a1ea9d.research_question: How can video generation models be enhanced to better understand and represent the physical world, particularly the 3D shape and motion of objects, in order to reduce non-physical artifacts and improve visual plausibility in generated videos?
9d1bf8082e2e5c6ddea2b00456ec7e8b91a1ea9d.hypothesis: Integrating 3D point trajectory information and regularization into video diffusion models will significantly improve the physical consistency, shape preservation, and motion plausibility of generated videos, especially in scenarios involving complex object interactions.
9d1bf8082e2e5c6ddea2b00456ec7e8b91a1ea9d.proposed_method: A novel video generation framework will be developed that augments standard 2D RGB videos with pixel-aligned 3D point trajectories, forming a new 3D-aware video dataset (PointVid). The methodology involves tracking 3D positions of foreground pixels across video frames using semantic segmentation and 3D point tracking techniques, and aligning these with the corresponding RGB data. The approach will fine-tune existing latent video diffusion models by concatenating RGB and 3D point data along the channel dimension, introducing cross-attention layers to enhance modality alignment. Regularization terms will be applied to the 3D point trajectories during training, including reconstruction loss for fidelity and smoothness, and rigidity loss to preserve local shape, all jointly optimized with standard diffusion losses.
9d1bf8082e2e5c6ddea2b00456ec7e8b91a1ea9d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by fine-tuning two distinct video diffusion model architectures: a UNet-based model (I2VGen-XL) and a DiT-based model (CogVideoX-1.5), using the proposed PointVid dataset. Evaluation will include both qualitative and quantitative analyses, focusing on visual plausibility, shape consistency, and motion smoothness. Benchmarks such as VBench (measuring subject/background consistency, motion smoothness, aesthetic and imaging quality) and VideoPhy (assessing physical commonsense) will be used for quantitative evaluation. Comparisons will be made against several strong baselines, including SVD, DynamiCrafter, and LTX Video, using identical input conditions. Ablation studies will assess the impact of point augmentation, regularization, cross-attention, and loss components.
9d1bf8082e2e5c6ddea2b00456ec7e8b91a1ea9d.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a novel 3D point augmentation strategy for video diffusion models, enabling explicit integration of 3D spatial knowledge into the generative process. A new 3D-aware video dataset (PointVid) will be curated, providing pixel-aligned 3D trajectories for training. The method is model-agnostic and can be seamlessly integrated into various video diffusion architectures. A unique regularization framework will be applied to the 3D point modality, directly addressing non-physical deformations and enhancing spatio-temporal coherence. This approach is expected to set new standards for physical plausibility and shape consistency in video generation, particularly in contact-rich, task-oriented scenarios.

9d21874dc08a0b3cef93a0273f0752080a372f4e.title: SlowFast-LLaVA: A Strong Training-Free Baseline for Video Large Language Models
9d21874dc08a0b3cef93a0273f0752080a372f4e.research_question: How can a training-free video large language model be designed to effectively capture both detailed spatial semantics and long-range temporal context for comprehensive video understanding, while remaining within the token budget constraints of standard large language models?
9d21874dc08a0b3cef93a0273f0752080a372f4e.hypothesis: A dual-pathway SlowFast input design, leveraging both high-resolution/low-frame-rate and low-resolution/high-frame-rate streams, enables a training-free video large language model to jointly capture fine-grained spatial details and long-range temporal dependencies, resulting in superior video understanding performance compared to existing training-free approaches.
9d21874dc08a0b3cef93a0273f0752080a372f4e.proposed_method: A new training-free video large language model architecture will be developed, utilizing a two-stream SlowFast input design. The Slow pathway will sample a small number of frames at a low frame rate, retaining high spatial resolution (e.g., 10 frames with 12×24 tokens each) to preserve spatial detail. The Fast pathway will process a larger number of frames at a high frame rate, applying aggressive spatial pooling (e.g., 50 frames with 4×4 tokens each) to focus on motion and temporal context. Frame features will be extracted independently using a pre-trained visual encoder (such as CLIP-L), aligned via a visual-language adaptor, and then aggregated through the Slow and Fast pathways. The resulting visual tokens from both pathways will be concatenated and combined with text tokens (prompt and question) before being input to a pre-trained LLM (e.g., LLaVA-NeXT) for answer generation. No additional fine-tuning will be performed, and prompt engineering will be explored to optimize model performance for various video tasks.
9d21874dc08a0b3cef93a0273f0752080a372f4e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three main video tasks: Open-Ended VideoQA, Multiple Choice VideoQA, and Text Generation, using eight established video benchmarks (MSVD-QA, MSRVTT-QA, TGIF-QA, ActivityNet-QA, NExTQA, EgoSchema, IntentQA, and VCGBench). The model will be evaluated using both 7B and 34B parameter LLM backbones, with CLIP-L as the visual encoder. Uniform frame sampling will be used (e.g., 50 frames per video), and various pooling strategies and prompt designs will be systematically ablated. Baselines will include state-of-the-art training-free video LLMs (e.g., IG-VLM, FreeVA) and supervised fine-tuned models (e.g., PLLaVA, LLaVA-NeXT-Video). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy and GPT-assisted quality scores for QA tasks, and detailed scores for text generation (Correctness, Detail Orientation, Contextual Understanding, Temporal Understanding, Consistency). All experiments will be run on systems with 8 Nvidia A100 80GB GPUs, and context window/token budget constraints will be strictly observed.
9d21874dc08a0b3cef93a0273f0752080a372f4e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel training-free dual-pathway SlowFast input design for video LLMs, enabling efficient and effective aggregation of both spatial and temporal features without exceeding LLM token budgets. This method allows for the use of significantly more video frames than prior training-free methods, leading to improved long-range temporal modeling and spatial detail preservation. The approach achieves state-of-the-art performance among training-free video LLMs across multiple benchmarks, and in some cases, matches or surpasses the performance of supervised fine-tuned models, all without requiring additional video-specific fine-tuning. Comprehensive ablation studies on pathway design, pooling strategies, and prompt engineering further establish the robustness and generalizability of the proposed method.

9d2ecdc3792904186203efdabc0b40621558dd03.title: Chaos is a Ladder: A New Theoretical Understanding of Contrastive Learning via Augmentation Overlap
9d2ecdc3792904186203efdabc0b40621558dd03.research_question: How can contrastive learning be theoretically understood and improved without relying on impractical conditional independence assumptions, and what role does data augmentation play in enabling class-separable representations for downstream tasks?
9d2ecdc3792904186203efdabc0b40621558dd03.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that aggressive data augmentations create overlap among intra-class samples, enabling contrastive learning to cluster intra-class samples together and achieve class-separated representations, even without conditional independence assumptions. Furthermore, it is posited that the degree of augmentation overlap can be quantitatively linked to downstream task performance, and that a new unsupervised metric can reliably predict this performance.
9d2ecdc3792904186203efdabc0b40621558dd03.proposed_method: A new theoretical framework will be developed that analyzes contrastive learning through the lens of augmentation overlap, focusing on the connectivity induced by data augmentations among intra-class samples. The approach formalizes the concept of an augmentation graph, where nodes represent samples and edges represent overlap in augmented views. By introducing minimal and practical assumptions, such as label consistency and intra-class connectivity via augmentations, the method derives upper and lower bounds for downstream classification risk in terms of the InfoNCE loss. Additionally, a new unsupervised evaluation metric, Average Relative Confusion (ARC), will be proposed to quantify augmentation overlap and its effect on representation quality. Theoretical analysis will be complemented by empirical studies to validate the framework and the proposed metric.
9d2ecdc3792904186203efdabc0b40621558dd03.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic datasets (using random augmentation graphs with controlled augmentation strength) and real-world image datasets such as CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, STL-10, and ImageNet. Contrastive learning methods including SimCLR and BYOL will be employed for pretraining, followed by linear evaluation protocols to assess downstream classification accuracy. The impact of augmentation strength will be systematically varied and measured using the proposed ARC metric, and results will be compared against baseline metrics such as Average Confusion Rate (ACR) and standard supervised evaluation. Key experimental variables include the number of negative samples, augmentation types and strengths, and the number of nearest neighbors used in the ARC calculation.
9d2ecdc3792904186203efdabc0b40621558dd03.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a novel theoretical understanding of contrastive learning that does not rely on conditional independence, replacing it with the more practical assumption of intra-class connectivity via augmentation overlap. It provides asymptotically tight generalization bounds for downstream performance under these weaker assumptions. The research also quantifies the influence of augmentation strength on representation quality and introduces ARC, a new unsupervised metric that aligns closely with downstream accuracy and does not require labeled data or additional classifiers. This framework offers actionable guidance for the design and evaluation of contrastive learning methods and data augmentations.

9d3463da77f6288da6fa16631034293a733bd719.title: The Trade-off between Universality and Label Efficiency of Representations from Contrastive Learning
9d3463da77f6288da6fa16631034293a733bd719.research_question: How does the diversity of pre-training data in contrastive learning affect the universality and label efficiency of learned representations, and can the trade-off between these properties be improved for downstream tasks?
9d3463da77f6288da6fa16631034293a733bd719.hypothesis: There exists a fundamental trade-off between universality and label efficiency in representations learned by contrastive learning; increasing the diversity of pre-training data enhances universality but reduces label efficiency for specific tasks. This trade-off can be mitigated by incorporating contrastive regularization during fine-tuning.
9d3463da77f6288da6fa16631034293a733bd719.proposed_method: A theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted to analyze the features learned by contrastive learning, focusing on the trade-off between universality and label efficiency. The approach will introduce a hidden representation data model to formalize the relationship between pre-training data diversity, invariant and spurious features, and downstream prediction performance. The methodology will include both linear and nonlinear analyses, demonstrating that contrastive learning acts as a generalized nonlinear PCA that encodes invariant features while discarding spurious ones. To address the trade-off, a contrastive regularization technique will be proposed for fine-tuning: during supervised adaptation to a target task, a contrastive loss will be added as a regularization term to the standard classification loss, encouraging the representation to retain task-relevant features while maintaining generality. This regularization will be applied to both the representation and the predictor, and is designed to be model-agnostic and compatible with various architectures and foundation models.
9d3463da77f6288da6fa16631034293a733bd719.experiment_details: Experiments will involve pre-training models such as ResNet18, ViT, and BERT-based architectures using contrastive learning methods (e.g., MoCo v2, MoCo v3, SimSiam, CLIP, SimCSE) on a range of datasets with varying diversity, including CIFAR-10, SVHN, GTSRB, ImageNet32, EMNIST, Fashion-MNIST, FaceScrub, Fer2013, ImageNet, ImageNet22k, GCC-15M, IMDB, and AGNews. The evaluation will compare linear probing, standard fine-tuning, and the proposed contrastive regularization method. Metrics will include test accuracy on both specific target tasks and the average across all pre-training datasets to assess universality and label efficiency. Feature similarity will be analyzed using linear Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA). Experimental setups will incrementally increase pre-training data diversity and measure the resulting trade-off, with ablation studies and t-SNE visualizations to inspect feature clustering and task-specificity.
9d3463da77f6288da6fa16631034293a733bd719.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a formal theoretical analysis establishing the trade-off between universality and label efficiency in contrastive learning, supported by a new hidden representation data model. It provides a novel connection between contrastive learning and generalized nonlinear PCA, clarifying how invariant and spurious features are encoded. The proposed contrastive regularization technique for fine-tuning is claimed to consistently improve downstream task performance across a variety of models and datasets, including large-scale foundation models, without requiring changes to the pre-training procedure. The study offers new empirical evidence and feature analysis tools to systematically characterize and address the universality-label efficiency trade-off.

9d587b3f1d0608bf89fdb4ea6eed3312a73e938c.title: MagicAnimate: Temporally Consistent Human Image Animation using Diffusion Model
9d587b3f1d0608bf89fdb4ea6eed3312a73e938c.research_question: How can temporally consistent and high-fidelity human image animation be achieved, given a reference image and a target motion sequence, while robustly preserving the reference identity and appearance across arbitrary video lengths?
9d587b3f1d0608bf89fdb4ea6eed3312a73e938c.hypothesis: Integrating explicit temporal modeling within a diffusion-based framework, together with a dense appearance encoder and a segment-level video fusion strategy, will significantly improve temporal consistency, identity preservation, and animation fidelity in human image animation tasks.
9d587b3f1d0608bf89fdb4ea6eed3312a73e938c.proposed_method: A novel diffusion-based framework is proposed for human image animation, which incorporates temporal attention blocks into a video diffusion backbone to explicitly model temporal consistency across frames. A dense appearance encoder is introduced to extract detailed identity and background features from the reference image, which are injected into the diffusion model via a hybrid attention mechanism. The method conditions animation on DensePose motion signals using a pose ControlNet, and employs an image-video joint training strategy to leverage both large-scale image and limited video datasets for improved fidelity and generalization. To enable smooth and seamless long video animation, a sliding window segment-based inference is used, with overlapping segments fused by averaging predictions for overlapping frames, and shared initial noise across segments to further enhance temporal coherence.
9d587b3f1d0608bf89fdb4ea6eed3312a73e938c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two benchmark datasets: TikTok (350 dancing videos) and TED-talks (1,203 video clips), using the same train/test splits as previous state-of-the-art methods for fair comparison. Baselines will include GAN-based approaches (TPS, MRAA), diffusion-based methods (DisCo), and hybrid models (IP-Adapter + ControlNet, with and without temporal attention). Evaluation metrics will cover both single-frame quality (L1 error, SSIM, LPIPS, PSNR, FID) and video fidelity (FID-VID, FVD). Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of temporal modeling, appearance encoding, image-video joint training, and inference-stage video fusion. Additional experiments will test cross-identity animation, generalization to unseen domains, and multi-person animation scenarios.
9d587b3f1d0608bf89fdb4ea6eed3312a73e938c.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces several key innovations: (1) explicit temporal modeling within a diffusion-based video generation backbone using temporal attention, (2) a novel dense appearance encoder that preserves intricate identity and background details, (3) an image-video joint training strategy that leverages both image and video data for improved fidelity and generalization, and (4) a simple but effective segment-based video fusion technique for smooth long-range animation. These contributions collectively enable state-of-the-art performance in both single-frame and video-level animation quality, robust cross-identity and domain generalization, and support for multi-person animation.

9d6c0aab077d4e63e60dd9a2a7febfc7165d9e51.title: Solving Non-Rectangular Reward-Robust MDPs via Frequency Regularization
9d6c0aab077d4e63e60dd9a2a7febfc7165d9e51.research_question: How can robust Markov decision processes (RMDPs) be solved efficiently when the reward uncertainty is coupled and non-rectangular, and what are the implications of such uncertainty structures for policy robustness and conservatism in reinforcement learning?
9d6c0aab077d4e63e60dd9a2a7febfc7165d9e51.hypothesis: Reward-robust MDPs with coupled, non-rectangular (e.g., Lp-norm ball) reward uncertainty can be solved efficiently using frequency regularization, leading to less conservative and more robust policies compared to traditional rectangular uncertainty sets.
9d6c0aab077d4e63e60dd9a2a7febfc7165d9e51.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed for solving reward-robust MDPs where the transition kernel is known and the reward function lies within a coupled Lp-norm ball around a nominal reward. The method explicitly formulates the worst-case reward as a function of the policy's visitation frequency, resulting in a regularized return objective. A policy-gradient algorithm is proposed, leveraging this regularization, and its convergence is theoretically established. The approach includes an efficient policy evaluation algorithm and an online actor-critic variant suitable for high-dimensional environments, utilizing iterative estimation of the occupancy measure for frequency regularization.
9d6c0aab077d4e63e60dd9a2a7febfc7165d9e51.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted in both tabular and high-dimensional continuous control environments. In the tabular setting, a model-based scenario is considered where the reward is perturbed according to a multivariate Gaussian, and robust policies are trained using both s-rectangular and coupled L2-norm uncertainty sets. The Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) for the worst 5% of outcomes is measured across different uncertainty radii to assess conservatism and robustness. In high-dimensional settings, the method is evaluated on MountainCarContinuous and Ant-v3 from OpenAI Gym, using PPO as the baseline and domain randomization as a robust RL comparator. Robustness is tested by introducing reward perturbations during evaluation, and performance is averaged over multiple seeds with confidence intervals reported.
9d6c0aab077d4e63e60dd9a2a7febfc7165d9e51.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to provide a provably convergent policy-gradient method for general, non-rectangular reward-robust MDPs. It establishes a direct connection between coupled reward uncertainty and frequency regularization, enabling tractable solutions without the need for restrictive rectangularity assumptions. The method is agnostic to the underlying RL algorithm and can be integrated with any learning framework. Empirical results demonstrate that this approach yields less conservative and more robust policies than traditional rectangular robust methods, especially in high-dimensional and practical scenarios.

9d747de845b3d74fd5cddc31f2ff827be6796900.title: HMVLM: Human Motion-Vision-Lanuage Model via MoE LoRA
9d747de845b3d74fd5cddc31f2ff827be6796900.research_question: How can a unified multimodal framework be developed to support diverse human-centric tasks involving 3D human motion, vision, and language, while preserving the foundational knowledge and generalization abilities of large language models during instruction tuning?
9d747de845b3d74fd5cddc31f2ff827be6796900.hypothesis: Integrating a Mixture of Expert Low-Rank Adaptation (MoE LoRA) architecture with a novel zero expert and body-part-based tokenization will enable a foundation language model to effectively learn and generalize across multiple human motion, vision, and language tasks, while mitigating catastrophic forgetting and preserving pre-trained linguistic capabilities.
9d747de845b3d74fd5cddc31f2ff827be6796900.proposed_method: A unified Human Motion-Vision-Language Model (HMVLM) will be constructed by augmenting a pre-trained foundation language model (e.g., Vicuna-7b-v1.5) with a Mixture of Expert (MoE) LoRA adaptation strategy. The model will include multiple LoRA expert adapters and a gating network that dynamically assigns expert weights based on task instructions and input prompts, allowing synchronized fine-tuning for multiple tasks. A non-trainable zero expert with zero-initialized parameters will be introduced, and the gating network will be supervised to select this expert for motion-unrelated tasks, thus preserving the original model parameters and mitigating catastrophic forgetting. For pose and motion representation, a body-part-based tokenization strategy will be implemented using spatial transformers, partitioning the human body into joint groups and encoding each part separately to enhance spatial granularity and representation expressiveness. The model will be instruction-tuned on an extended vocabulary that merges text, pose, and motion tokens, supporting tasks such as text-to-motion generation, pose estimation, and motion video understanding.
9d747de845b3d74fd5cddc31f2ff827be6796900.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Vicuna-7b-v1.5 foundation model with five LoRA experts (including a zero expert). The gating network will be trained on the LMSYS-Chat-1M dataset. For text-to-motion tasks, HumanML3D and KIT-ML datasets will be used, with the motion tokenizer trained on their respective splits. Pose estimation and tokenizer training will utilize Human3.6M and 3DPW datasets, while the MoViD dataset will be used for motion video understanding. Evaluation metrics will include MT-Bench for knowledge retention, R-precision, Multi-modal Distance (MM-D), Frechet Inception Distance (FID), and Diversity for text-to-motion, and MPJPE/PA-MPJPE for pose estimation. Baselines will include task-specific models (e.g., TM2T, T2M, MDM, MoMask) and multimodal foundation models (e.g., MotionGPT, MotionAgent, ChatPose). Ablation studies will assess the impact of the zero expert, gating loss, and body-part-based tokenization. Efficiency analyses will examine parameter scaling, training time, and inference latency as the number of experts varies.
9d747de845b3d74fd5cddc31f2ff827be6796900.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a MoE LoRA-based adaptation strategy with a novel zero expert to preserve foundational knowledge and prevent catastrophic forgetting during multimodal instruction tuning. A body-part-based tokenization approach is developed to enhance spatial granularity in pose and motion representations, improving downstream task performance. The unified model supports multiple human-centric tasks simultaneously, demonstrating robust knowledge retention and competitive or superior performance compared to both task-specific and multimodal baselines. The method is model-agnostic and can be integrated with various foundation language models, offering broad applicability and scalability.

9d992e40150955e03868113d90dbf870a07a0d02.title: SegRefiner: Towards Model-Agnostic Segmentation Refinement with Discrete Diffusion Process
9d992e40150955e03868113d90dbf870a07a0d02.research_question: How can the quality of segmentation masks produced by various segmentation models be improved in a model-agnostic manner, particularly for high-resolution images and diverse segmentation tasks?
9d992e40150955e03868113d90dbf870a07a0d02.hypothesis: A model-agnostic segmentation refinement framework based on a discrete diffusion process can consistently enhance the quality of coarse segmentation masks across different segmentation models and tasks, outperforming existing model-agnostic refinement approaches in both segmentation accuracy and boundary detail preservation.
9d992e40150955e03868113d90dbf870a07a0d02.proposed_method: A novel segmentation refinement framework, SegRefiner, will be developed utilizing a discrete diffusion process to iteratively refine coarse segmentation masks. The method interprets mask refinement as a conditional data generation problem, where the coarse mask is treated as a noisy version of the ground truth and is progressively denoised through a series of discrete, unidirectional state transitions at the pixel level. The forward process gradually degrades the ground truth mask into a coarse mask using a transition sample module that randomly transitions pixels based on state-transition probabilities. The reverse process, parameterized by a U-Net-based neural network, takes the coarse mask and the corresponding image as input and predicts refined masks and transition probabilities at each step, iteratively correcting errors in the coarse mask. Both global and local refinement strategies are employed, with local refinement focusing on patches identified as uncertain by the transition probabilities, enabling the model to capture fine details in high-resolution images.
9d992e40150955e03868113d90dbf870a07a0d02.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple segmentation tasks, including semantic segmentation, instance segmentation, and dichotomous image segmentation. Datasets such as BIG (for high-resolution semantic segmentation), COCO with LVIS annotations (for instance segmentation), and DIS5K (for dichotomous image segmentation) will be used, all chosen for their high-quality pixel-level annotations and challenging fine-grained details. Baselines will include state-of-the-art model-agnostic refinement methods such as SegFix, CascadePSP, CRM, and BPR, as well as model-specific refinement techniques like PointRend, RefineMask, and MaskTransfiner. Evaluation metrics will include Intersection over Union (IoU), mean Boundary Accuracy (mBA), Mask Average Precision (MaskAP), and Boundary Average Precision (BoundaryAP). The experimental setup will involve training both low-resolution and high-resolution variants of SegRefiner, applying data augmentation strategies such as double random cropping, and employing both global and local refinement during inference to maximize performance on high-resolution images.
9d992e40150955e03868113d90dbf870a07a0d02.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to apply a diffusion-based framework with a uniquely designed discrete diffusion process for model-agnostic segmentation mask refinement. Unlike previous methods, the discrete diffusion process enables unidirectional, pixel-level state transitions, allowing for efficient and effective refinement of coarse masks from any segmentation model. The framework is task-agnostic and can be directly applied to various segmentation tasks without modification. The method demonstrates superior performance in both segmentation and boundary metrics, particularly excelling at capturing fine-grained details in high-resolution images. Additionally, the approach introduces a transition sample module and a combined global-local refinement strategy, further enhancing its ability to handle challenging segmentation scenarios.

9dabb370d4e8e12f3753ac228bb9ec228d65e659.title: When is Multicalibration Post-Processing Necessary?
9dabb370d4e8e12f3753ac228bb9ec228d65e659.research_question: How frequently do machine learning models achieve multicalibration as a consequence of standard empirical risk minimization, and under what circumstances is explicit multicalibration post-processing necessary to ensure group-wise calibration across diverse datasets and model types?
9dabb370d4e8e12f3753ac228bb9ec228d65e659.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that standard empirical risk minimization (ERM) often results in models that are already multicalibrated, particularly for well-calibrated model classes and on tabular datasets, but that explicit multicalibration post-processing is necessary for inherently uncalibrated models and for large-scale vision and language models to achieve low group-wise calibration error.
9dabb370d4e8e12f3753ac228bb9ec228d65e659.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical evaluation will be conducted comparing three families of methods: (1) standard ERM-trained models, (2) ERM followed by classical recalibration techniques such as Platt scaling, isotonic regression, and temperature scaling, and (3) ERM followed by explicit multicalibration post-processing algorithms, including the HKRR (Hébert-Johnson et al., 2018) and HJZ (Haghtalab et al., 2023) algorithms. The study will systematically vary hyperparameters for multicalibration algorithms, including calibration fraction (proportion of data held out for post-processing), and will assess sensitivity to these choices. Subgroups for multicalibration will be defined based on sensitive attributes and their intersections, reflecting realistic fairness concerns. Both standard Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and smoothed ECE (smECE) will be used to measure calibration, with a focus on maximum group-wise calibration error as the primary fairness metric.
9dabb370d4e8e12f3753ac228bb9ec228d65e659.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of datasets: five tabular datasets (e.g., ACSIncome, UCIBankMarketing, UCI CreditDefault, HMDA, MEPS), two language datasets (CivilComments, AmazonPolarity), and two image datasets (CelebA, Camelyon17). For each dataset, between 10 and 20 overlapping subgroups will be defined using available features or metadata. Models to be evaluated include multilayer perceptrons (MLPs), decision trees, random forests, SVMs, naive Bayes, logistic regression, vision transformers, DistilBERT, ResNets, and DenseNets, with both train-from-scratch and fine-tuned paradigms for large models. Baselines will include ERM and standard calibration methods, with explicit comparison to multicalibration post-processing. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, ECE, smECE, and maximum group-wise calibration error, with results averaged over multiple random train/validation splits. Hyperparameter sweeps will be performed for multicalibration algorithms, and the impact of calibration fraction will be systematically explored. All experiments will be run on high-performance computing resources, with careful partitioning of data into training, validation, and calibration sets.
9dabb370d4e8e12f3753ac228bb9ec228d65e659.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first large-scale, systematic empirical study of multicalibration post-processing across a wide range of datasets and model types, including both small tabular models and large-scale vision and language models. The investigation will clarify when multicalibration is an emergent property of standard training and when explicit post-processing is necessary, providing practical guidance for fairness practitioners. The study will also benchmark the sensitivity of multicalibration algorithms to hyperparameter choices and data partitioning, and will compare traditional calibration methods to explicit multicalibration algorithms in terms of effectiveness and computational efficiency. The release of a Python package implementing multicalibration algorithms further enhances the practical impact and reproducibility of the research.

9db0ed0726137364ed5114a5a144473c9aa5afc8.title: Controlling Neural Collapse Enhances Out-of-Distribution Detection and Transfer Learning
9db0ed0726137364ed5114a5a144473c9aa5afc8.research_question: How can the degree of neural collapse in deep neural networks be strategically controlled to simultaneously enhance out-of-distribution (OOD) detection and OOD generalization (transfer learning), and what is the theoretical relationship between neural collapse and these two objectives?
9db0ed0726137364ed5114a5a144473c9aa5afc8.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that controlling the degree of neural collapse at different layers of a deep neural network—specifically, mitigating collapse in the encoder and inducing collapse in the classifier—will enable the network to achieve both improved OOD detection and enhanced OOD generalization, overcoming the trade-off that arises when using a single feature space for both tasks.
9db0ed0726137364ed5114a5a144473c9aa5afc8.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that explicitly controls neural collapse at different layers of a deep neural network. The encoder is regularized with an entropy maximization term to mitigate neural collapse, thereby promoting feature diversity and enhancing generalization to novel distributions. In contrast, the classifier head is preceded by a fixed Simplex Equiangular Tight Frame (ETF) projector, which enforces strong neural collapse and produces tightly clustered, highly separable class representations, improving OOD detection. The method involves training the encoder and projector with distinct objectives: entropy regularization is applied to the encoder's output to maximize within-class variance, while the projector's weights are fixed as a simplex ETF and frozen during training to induce maximal class separation. The overall loss function combines standard classification loss with the entropy regularization term, and group normalization is used in the encoder to further support transferability.
9db0ed0726137364ed5114a5a144473c9aa5afc8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using multiple deep neural network architectures, including VGG17, ResNet18, and Vision Transformer (ViT) variants, trained on the ImageNet-100 dataset as the in-distribution (ID) data. Out-of-distribution generalization and detection will be evaluated on eight diverse OOD datasets, such as NINCO, ImageNet-R, CIFAR-100, Oxford Flowers, CUB-200, Aircrafts, Oxford-IIIT Pets, and STL-10. Performance will be measured using ID generalization error, OOD generalization error (via linear probing on OOD datasets), and OOD detection error (using energy-based scoring and FPR95). Baseline comparisons will include standard DNNs without neural collapse control, as well as state-of-the-art OOD detection methods such as NECO. Ablation studies will assess the impact of entropy regularization, projector configuration, normalization layers, loss functions, and optimization schemes. Neural collapse will be quantified using established metrics (NC1–NC4) across different layers.
9db0ed0726137364ed5114a5a144473c9aa5afc8.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to unify and empirically demonstrate the inverse relationship between neural collapse and the dual objectives of OOD detection and OOD generalization, extending analysis beyond the final hidden layer. A theoretical framework is developed linking entropy regularization to the mitigation of neural collapse for improved generalization, and the use of a fixed simplex ETF projector to induce collapse for better detection is introduced. The method enables decoupling of feature spaces for detection and generalization within the same network, achieving state-of-the-art results in both tasks across diverse datasets and architectures. The approach is computationally efficient and introduces minimal overhead compared to standard DNNs.

9dbcb0893d05e6176353eee401afa4929b570cf6.title: FourierGNN: Rethinking Multivariate Time Series Forecasting from a Pure Graph Perspective
9dbcb0893d05e6176353eee401afa4929b570cf6.research_question: Can multivariate time series forecasting be effectively reformulated and improved by modeling both spatial and temporal dependencies using a unified, pure graph-based approach, without relying on separate temporal and spatial networks?
9dbcb0893d05e6176353eee401afa4929b570cf6.hypothesis: A unified graph-based formulation, where each value in a multivariate time series is represented as a node in a fully-connected hypervariate graph, enables more effective and efficient modeling of spatiotemporal dependencies for forecasting than traditional approaches that separate spatial and temporal modeling.
9dbcb0893d05e6176353eee401afa4929b570cf6.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces a novel data structure called the hypervariate graph, where each value in the multivariate time series (across all variates and time steps in a sliding window) is treated as a node, and the graph is fully connected to capture all possible spatiotemporal dependencies. Forecasting is reformulated as a node prediction problem on this hypervariate graph. To address the computational complexity of large fully-connected graphs, a new neural architecture, Fourier Graph Neural Network (FourierGNN), is developed. FourierGNN is built upon the Fourier Graph Operator (FGO), a learnable layer that performs matrix multiplications in the Fourier space of the graph, leveraging the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) for efficient computation. Multiple FGO layers are stacked, with recursive multiplications and nonlinear activations in the Fourier domain, followed by an inverse DFT to return to the time domain. The final node representations are projected to the forecasting horizon using feed-forward layers.
9dbcb0893d05e6176353eee401afa4929b570cf6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on seven real-world multivariate time series datasets spanning domains such as traffic, energy, web traffic, electrocardiogram, and COVID-19. The datasets will be split into training, validation, and test sets (typically 7:2:1, with an exception for COVID-19). The proposed method will be compared to a comprehensive set of baselines, including classical statistical models (VAR), deep learning models (LSTNet, TCN, DeepGLO), Transformer-based models (Informer, Reformer, Autoformer, FEDformer), and state-of-the-art GNN-based models (GraphWaveNet, StemGNN, MTGNN, AGCRN, TAMP-S2GCNets, DCRNN, STGCN, CoST). Evaluation metrics will include Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). Experiments will be run on a single NVIDIA RTX 3080 GPU using PyTorch, with hyperparameters tuned on the validation set. Additional analyses will include ablation studies, efficiency comparisons (parameter count, training time), and visualization of learned spatiotemporal representations.
9dbcb0893d05e6176353eee401afa4929b570cf6.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the hypervariate graph, a novel data structure that unifies spatial and temporal modeling by treating every value in the time series as a graph node, thus enabling high-resolution spatiotemporal dependency modeling. The FourierGNN architecture leverages efficient matrix multiplications in Fourier space, achieving log-linear complexity and reducing parameter count compared to prior GNN approaches. Theoretical analysis demonstrates the equivalence of the proposed Fourier Graph Operator to multi-order graph convolutions in the time domain, providing both interpretability and efficiency. The unified pure-graph perspective eliminates the need for separate spatial and temporal networks, overcoming compatibility issues and handcrafted design burdens present in existing methods.

9dbd5ba59d900b8cde2f515fd4ef83e6bb5e9304.title: ChartMoE: Mixture of Diversely Aligned Expert Connector for Chart Understanding
9dbd5ba59d900b8cde2f515fd4ef83e6bb5e9304.research_question: How can multimodal large language models be improved to achieve more accurate and reliable chart understanding and reasoning across diverse chart types and tasks, without sacrificing general instruction-following capabilities?
