9dbd5ba59d900b8cde2f515fd4ef83e6bb5e9304.hypothesis: Initializing a Mixture of Experts (MoE) connector with parameters derived from diverse alignment tasks (chart-table, chart-JSON, chart-code, and vanilla connector) will enable multimodal large language models to better capture the multifaceted information present in charts, leading to superior chart comprehension and reasoning performance compared to models using a single linear connector.
9dbd5ba59d900b8cde2f515fd4ef83e6bb5e9304.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed that replaces the traditional linear connector between the vision encoder and language model in multimodal LLMs with a Mixture of Experts (MoE) architecture. Each expert in the MoE connector will be initialized using parameters obtained from distinct alignment pre-training tasks: chart-to-table, chart-to-JSON, chart-to-code, and a vanilla connector to preserve general capabilities. The vision encoder (e.g., CLIP ViT-Large) will process chart images into visual tokens, which are then routed through the MoE connector using a gating network that selects the top-K experts for each token. The outputs are weighted and aggregated before being passed to the LLM (e.g., InternLM2-7B-ChatSFT). Training will proceed in three stages: (1) alignment pre-training of each expert with its respective task, (2) high-quality knowledge learning using curated instruction data, and (3) chart-specific annealing tuning to adapt to benchmark query styles and answer formats. The MoE connector is designed to be lightweight, adding minimal computational overhead.
9dbd5ba59d900b8cde2f515fd4ef83e6bb5e9304.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a combination of synthetic and real-world datasets. The alignment pre-training will utilize the newly constructed ChartMoE-Align dataset, which contains nearly 1 million chart-table-JSON-code quadruples generated through a structured pipeline. Supervised fine-tuning and evaluation will be performed on established chart understanding benchmarks such as ChartQA (1,250 test questions), ChartBench (covering 9 main chart categories and 42 subcategories), ChartFC (1,591 questions), and ChartCheck (two splits with 937 and 981 questions). Baselines will include general MLLMs (e.g., LLaVA-v1.5, Qwen-VL, DocOwl, InternlmXC-v2), specialist chart models (e.g., Pix2Struct, Matcha, UniChart, Deplot+LLaVA), and chart-oriented MLLMs (e.g., ChartVLM, OneChart, ChartLlama, ChartGemma, TinyChart, ChartAst). Evaluation metrics will include relaxed accuracy at various margins, accuracy for claim verification, and general VQA benchmarks to assess instruction-following and object recognition. Ablation studies will be conducted to analyze the impact of expert initialization, number of experts, activation strategy, and training stages.
9dbd5ba59d900b8cde2f515fd4ef83e6bb5e9304.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a Mixture of Experts connector specifically designed for chart understanding in multimodal LLMs, with each expert initialized from a distinct alignment task (table, JSON, code, and vanilla). This initialization strategy avoids expert homogenization and enables specialization, leading to improved performance. The creation of the large-scale ChartMoE-Align dataset with chart-table-JSON-code quadruples enables comprehensive alignment pre-training. The three-stage training paradigm (alignment, high-quality knowledge learning, and annealing tuning) is tailored to maximize both chart-specific and general capabilities. The method achieves significant improvements over previous state-of-the-art models on multiple chart understanding benchmarks, while maintaining general multimodal reasoning abilities.

9dc1674186dc34336a6a28f5359dc6f267a287f4.title: DataDAM: Efficient Dataset Distillation with Attention Matching
9dc1674186dc34336a6a28f5359dc6f267a287f4.research_question: How can the process of dataset distillation be made more computationally efficient while ensuring that the synthetic dataset closely approximates the distribution and discriminative power of the original dataset, and achieves strong generalization across diverse tasks and architectures?
9dc1674186dc34336a6a28f5359dc6f267a287f4.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that matching spatial attention maps and feature distributions between real and synthetic datasets across multiple layers of randomly initialized neural networks will enable the creation of a small synthetic dataset that closely approximates the real data distribution, resulting in competitive or superior performance to existing dataset distillation methods with reduced computational cost.
9dc1674186dc34336a6a28f5359dc6f267a287f4.proposed_method: A novel end-to-end dataset distillation framework, DataDAM (Dataset Distillation with Attention Matching), will be developed. The method will synthesize a small set of learnable synthetic images by matching spatial attention maps between real and synthetic data at various layers of randomly initialized deep neural networks, using a Spatial Attention Matching (SAM) module. The SAM module will generate attention maps by aggregating the absolute values of feature maps across channels, emphasizing discriminative spatial regions. In addition to attention matching, a complementary loss based on Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) will be employed to align the feature distributions in the last layer of the encoder network between real and synthetic datasets. The optimization objective will combine the SAM loss and the MMD loss, with a tunable balance parameter, and will be solved using stochastic gradient descent. The synthetic dataset will be initialized either from random noise or by sampling from the real dataset, and the approach will not require bi-level optimization or pre-trained network parameters, making it scalable and efficient.
9dc1674186dc34336a6a28f5359dc6f267a287f4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of computer vision datasets including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, ImageNet-1K, and ImageNet subsets (ImageNette, ImageWoof, ImageSquawk), with images resized as appropriate for each dataset. The method will be evaluated using varying numbers of images per class (IPC: 1, 10, 50), and compared against state-of-the-art dataset distillation and coreset selection baselines such as Random, Herding, K-Center, Forgetting, Dataset Distillation, Flexible Dataset Distillation, Dataset Condensation, DSA, DM, CAFE, and KIP. Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy, computational cost (runtime and GPU memory usage), and cross-architecture generalization, with performance averaged over multiple random seeds and network initializations. Additional experiments will assess the method's robustness to different synthetic data initializations, the effect of loss components and task balance, and its applicability to continual learning and neural architecture search tasks.
9dc1674186dc34336a6a28f5359dc6f267a287f4.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new approach to dataset distillation that leverages spatial attention matching across multiple layers of randomly initialized networks, combined with feature distribution alignment in the last layer, to synthesize unbiased and highly informative synthetic datasets. Unlike prior methods, this approach does not require bi-level optimization or pre-trained models, resulting in significant reductions in computational cost and memory usage. The method achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple datasets and settings, demonstrates superior cross-architecture generalization, and provides practical benefits for downstream applications such as continual learning and neural architecture search.

9dc6bf842d39b6bdb55a97e616a9a653873da5f8.title: Bringing NeRFs to the Latent Space: Inverse Graphics Autoencoder
9dc6bf842d39b6bdb55a97e616a9a653873da5f8.research_question: How can a 3D-aware latent space be constructed to enable effective training and interoperability of neural radiance fields (NeRFs) in the latent space of image autoencoders, while preserving both 3D-consistency and autoencoding performance?
9dc6bf842d39b6bdb55a97e616a9a653873da5f8.hypothesis: A latent space regularized with 3D geometry and jointly trained with synthetic 3D scenes will enable image autoencoders to produce 3D-consistent latent representations. Training NeRFs in this 3D-aware latent space will improve novel view synthesis quality and efficiency compared to standard autoencoder latent spaces or direct RGB-space training.
9dc6bf842d39b6bdb55a97e616a9a653873da5f8.proposed_method: A novel Inverse Graphics Autoencoder (IG-AE) will be developed to encode images into a 3D-aware latent space by aligning the autoencoder's latent representations with jointly trained latent 3D scenes. This is achieved by introducing a 3D-regularization objective that leverages synthetic 3D scenes (e.g., rendered from Objaverse) and Tri-Plane neural representations to enforce 3D-consistency in the latent space. The IG-AE is trained with a combination of losses: a 3D consistency loss aligning latent encodings with 3D-consistent latent renderings, an RGB alignment loss ensuring decoded outputs match ground truth images, and an autoencoder preservation loss that maintains reconstructive performance on both synthetic and real images (e.g., from ImageNet), including perceptual and total variation regularization. After training IG-AE, a two-stage latent NeRF training pipeline is proposed: first, NeRFs are trained in the IG-AE latent space using latent supervision; second, the decoder and NeRF are fine-tuned with RGB alignment to ensure high-quality novel view synthesis in the RGB space.
9dc6bf842d39b6bdb55a97e616a9a653873da5f8.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training the IG-AE on synthetic 3D scenes from Objaverse (500 objects, 300 views per object at 128x128 resolution) and using ImageNet (40,000 images) for autoencoder preservation. NeRF architectures (including Vanilla-NeRF, Instant-NGP, TensoRF, and K-Planes) will be trained in the IG-AE latent space, a standard autoencoder latent space, and the RGB space. Evaluations will be conducted on held-out scenes from Objaverse and out-of-distribution ShapeNet datasets (Hats, Bags, Vases), focusing on object-level scenes. Performance will be measured using PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS for novel view synthesis and reconstruction. Ablation studies will assess the impact of 3D-regularization and autoencoder preservation components. Comparisons will include training and rendering speed, as well as qualitative and quantitative analysis of artifacts and 3D-consistency.
9dc6bf842d39b6bdb55a97e616a9a653873da5f8.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first image autoencoder that embeds a 3D-aware latent space, enabling 3D-consistent latent representations suitable for NeRF training. A standardized pipeline for training NeRFs in latent spaces is developed, including a two-stage training process with latent supervision and RGB alignment. An open-source extension to the Nerfstudio framework is provided, facilitating latent NeRF training for various architectures. The method demonstrates improved novel view synthesis quality and efficiency compared to standard autoencoders and RGB-space NeRFs, and establishes a foundation for further research in 3D-aware latent representations and inverse graphics autoencoders.

9ddcc1a303157febc58b0d894ddd6c3e957aa70d.title: TabPFN Unleashed: A Scalable and Effective Solution to Tabular Classification Problems
9ddcc1a303157febc58b0d894ddd6c3e957aa70d.research_question: How can both bias and variance be simultaneously minimized in in-context learning models for tabular classification, while maintaining scalability to high-dimensional and large-scale datasets and supporting multiclass classification tasks?
9ddcc1a303157febc58b0d894ddd6c3e957aa70d.hypothesis: Introducing a lightweight encoder-based fine-tuning mechanism combined with bootstrapped sampling and ensemble techniques will jointly reduce bias and variance in TabPFN, leading to improved generalization, scalability, and efficiency on a wide range of tabular classification tasks, including those with high-dimensional features and many classes.
9ddcc1a303157febc58b0d894ddd6c3e957aa70d.proposed_method: A novel adaptation framework, BETA (Bagging and Encoder-based Fine-tuning for TabPFN Adaptation), is proposed to enhance TabPFN for tabular classification. The method introduces a lightweight encoder module that transforms raw input features into fixed-dimensional latent representations, enabling dimensionality reduction and better alignment of downstream datasets with the pre-trained TabPFN, thereby reducing bias. Multiple encoders are incorporated using BatchEnsemble techniques to create diverse feature transformations, which are jointly trained to further reduce variance. During inference, bootstrapped sampling is employed to generate multiple support sets, and predictions are aggregated across encoders and bootstrapped samples to stabilize outputs without incurring significant computational overhead. For multiclass classification tasks with more than 10 classes, Error-Correcting Output Codes (ECOC) are integrated to enable efficient handling of a larger number of categories.
9ddcc1a303157febc58b0d894ddd6c3e957aa70d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on over 200 benchmark tabular classification datasets, including the TALENT benchmark (120 binary and 80 multiclass datasets) and 20 high-dimensional datasets from the scikit-feature repository. Datasets are split into training, validation, and test sets (64%/16%/20%), and models are evaluated using accuracy as the primary metric. BETA will be compared against classical machine learning algorithms (e.g., SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost), state-of-the-art deep learning models for tabular data (e.g., MLP, ResNet, TabNet, FT-Transformer), neighborhood-based and ensemble-based methods, as well as TabPFN and its recent variants (e.g., LocalPFN, MixturePFN, TuneTables). All methods are evaluated using their default or best-tuned hyperparameters, and results are averaged over 15 random seeds per dataset. Additional analysis includes bias-variance decomposition, ablation studies on key components (number of encoders, BatchEnsemble, partial parameter tuning), and efficiency comparisons in terms of inference time and parameter count.
9ddcc1a303157febc58b0d894ddd6c3e957aa70d.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to systematically address both bias and variance in TabPFN for tabular classification, rather than focusing on one at the expense of the other. BETA introduces a lightweight, scalable encoder-based fine-tuning approach that enables adaptation to high-dimensional and large-scale datasets, and integrates bootstrapped sampling and BatchEnsemble techniques for efficient variance reduction. The framework also extends TabPFN to multiclass tasks with more than 10 classes via ECOC, all while maintaining computational efficiency during inference. Experimental results demonstrate that BETA achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance across a diverse set of benchmarks, outperforming or matching existing methods in both accuracy and scalability.

9e15056495f973d7786b27f7ee2eabd672a70a5a.title: SOREL: A Stochastic Algorithm for Spectral Risks Minimization
9e15056495f973d7786b27f7ee2eabd672a70a5a.research_question: How can stochastic optimization algorithms be developed to efficiently and provably minimize spectral risk objectives in machine learning, particularly for large-scale problems where traditional empirical risk minimization is insufficient for capturing risk-averse or fairness-sensitive objectives?
9e15056495f973d7786b27f7ee2eabd672a70a5a.hypothesis: A stochastic gradient-based algorithm with trajectory stabilization and variance reduction can achieve provable convergence guarantees and near-optimal rates for spectral risk minimization, outperforming existing methods in terms of runtime and sample complexity.
9e15056495f973d7786b27f7ee2eabd672a70a5a.proposed_method: A new stochastic optimization algorithm, SOREL, is proposed for spectral risk minimization problems with a strongly convex regularizer. The method reformulates the spectral risk minimization as a minimax problem and applies a primal-dual approach, alternating updates between the primal variable (model parameters) and the dual variable (sample weights). To address the instability arising from non-smoothness and ordering dependencies in the spectral risk, a proximal term is introduced in the dual update to stabilize the optimization trajectory. The primal update is solved approximately using a variance-reduced stochastic gradient method inspired by SVRG, leveraging the smoothness of the finite-sum loss for efficient computation. Key algorithmic components include momentum acceleration, periodic full-gradient computation, and efficient projection onto the permutahedron for dual variable updates.
9e15056495f973d7786b27f7ee2eabd672a70a5a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five real-world tabular regression datasets (yacht, energy, concrete, kin8nm, power) using least-squares loss with L2 regularization. The evaluation will cover a range of spectral risk measures, including ESRM, Extremile, and CVaR. Baseline methods for comparison include SGD, LSVRG, and Prospect, with all algorithms tested both with and without minibatching (batch size 64). Performance will be measured in terms of suboptimality (relative to L-BFGS solutions), sample complexity (number of effective passes over the data), and runtime (CPU time). Hyperparameters such as learning rate, proximal parameters, and epoch lengths will be tuned for each method, and detailed experimental settings will be documented for reproducibility.
9e15056495f973d7786b27f7ee2eabd672a70a5a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first stochastic gradient-based algorithm with convergence guarantees for the original (non-smoothed) spectral risk minimization problem. It achieves a near-optimal convergence rate of O~(1/sqrt(epsilon)), matching known lower bounds in the deterministic setting up to logarithmic factors. Unlike prior methods that require smoothing or lack convergence guarantees, the method directly addresses the original spectral risk and introduces trajectory stabilization for the dual variable, enabling efficient optimization even in large-scale settings. Empirical results demonstrate superior or competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art baselines in both runtime and sample complexity across diverse spectral risk measures and datasets.

9e162f92a8c493c953b1dd434bfe126a94e8fbdb.title: Renormalization group flow, optimal transport, and diffusion-based generative model.
9e162f92a8c493c953b1dd434bfe126a94e8fbdb.research_question: How can the principles of renormalization group (RG) flow, optimal transport theory, and frequency domain analysis be integrated to develop more efficient and effective diffusion-based generative models for high-quality image synthesis?
9e162f92a8c493c953b1dd434bfe126a94e8fbdb.hypothesis: A diffusion-based generative model that operates in the frequency domain, guided by a scale-dependent noise schedule informed by physical dispersion relations and optimal transport theory, will generate high-quality images with significantly improved computational efficiency compared to traditional image-domain diffusion models.
9e162f92a8c493c953b1dd434bfe126a94e8fbdb.proposed_method: A novel generative modeling framework will be developed by interpreting the renormalization group (RG) flow as an optimal transport gradient flow, minimizing a functional analogous to the Kullback-Leibler divergence. The proposed method, termed the Frequency Domain Diffusion Model (FDDM), will operate in the frequency domain by applying the discrete cosine transform (DCT) to map images into a sparse frequency representation. The forward diffusion process will introduce noise in the frequency domain according to a scale-dependent noise schedule derived from a dispersion relation, allowing for differential treatment of low- and high-frequency components. The reverse diffusion process will employ a neural network to predict clean frequency-domain features from noisy inputs, enabling progressive denoising and image synthesis. The approach will leverage patch-based processing inspired by JPEG compression to further accelerate training and inference.
9e162f92a8c493c953b1dd434bfe126a94e8fbdb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image generation datasets (e.g., CIFAR-10, ImageNet, or similar widely used benchmarks). The proposed FDDM will be compared against established image-domain diffusion models, with baselines including state-of-the-art diffusion models and possibly GAN-based approaches. Evaluation metrics will include image quality measures such as FID (Fréchet Inception Distance), IS (Inception Score), and computational efficiency metrics such as training and inference time. The experimental setup will involve both full-image and patch-based processing, with ablation studies to assess the impact of the scale-dependent noise schedule and frequency-domain modeling.
9e162f92a8c493c953b1dd434bfe126a94e8fbdb.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a generative modeling framework that unifies concepts from statistical physics (RG flow), optimal transport, and frequency-domain analysis. The key innovations include interpreting RG flow as an optimal transport gradient flow, performing diffusion modeling in the frequency domain with a scale-dependent noise schedule, and leveraging the sparsity of natural images in this domain for efficient signal-noise separation. The method claims to significantly reduce computational requirements while maintaining or improving image generation quality, and to provide a new theoretical bridge between physics-inspired modeling and modern machine learning.

9e16d8cc6096ec0d2733a4ecf41ce09d9a4bd19c.title: Scaling Data-Constrained Language Models
9e16d8cc6096ec0d2733a4ecf41ce09d9a4bd19c.research_question: How can large language models be effectively scaled in regimes where the amount of unique training data is limited, and what strategies can optimize the allocation of computational resources and data augmentation to maximize model performance under such constraints?
9e16d8cc6096ec0d2733a4ecf41ce09d9a4bd19c.hypothesis: Training large language models with repeated data (multiple epochs) can yield comparable performance to training on unique data up to a certain threshold, and augmenting limited natural language data with code or by relaxing filtering constraints can further improve downstream task performance in data-constrained regimes.
9e16d8cc6096ec0d2733a4ecf41ce09d9a4bd19c.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical investigation will be conducted by training transformer-based language models (using the GPT-2 architecture and tokenizer) across a wide range of parameter sizes (10 million to 9 billion) and training regimes, varying the number of unique tokens, epochs (data repetition), and compute budgets. A novel data-constrained scaling law will be developed, extending the Chinchilla scaling law to account for the diminishing returns of repeated data and excess parameters, using an exponential decay formulation for both effective data and model size. The methodology will include fitting the proposed scaling law to empirical results from over 400 controlled training runs, and systematically evaluating the impact of data repetition, code augmentation (by mixing Python code from The Stack dataset at various ratios), and different data filtering strategies (perplexity and deduplication) on both loss and downstream task performance. Technical details include careful control of data overlap, shuffling after each epoch, and reporting results on held-out test sets to avoid overfitting artifacts.
9e16d8cc6096ec0d2733a4ecf41ce09d9a4bd19c.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed on subsets of the C4 dataset, with data budgets ranging from 100 million to 1.5 billion unique tokens, and total training tokens up to 900 billion. Models will be trained for up to 1500 epochs to explore the effects of data repetition, and compute budgets will be matched across configurations to enable fair comparison (IsoFLOP). Baselines will include single-epoch models and models following prior scaling laws (e.g., Chinchilla). Evaluation metrics will include held-out test loss and performance on 19 downstream natural language tasks (zero- to few-shot), with scores rescaled for comparability. Additional experiments will assess the impact of code augmentation and filtering strategies, with downstream performance measured across a suite of benchmarks. Hyperparameters will follow prior best practices, and all experiments will ensure maximal data overlap and consistent shuffling.
9e16d8cc6096ec0d2733a4ecf41ce09d9a4bd19c.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a new data-constrained scaling law that generalizes existing compute-optimal scaling laws to regimes with limited unique data and repeated training. It empirically quantifies the diminishing returns of data repetition and excess model parameters, providing actionable guidance for compute allocation in data-constrained settings. The research also benchmarks the effectiveness of code augmentation and relaxed filtering as complementary strategies for increasing effective training data, and demonstrates that these approaches can extend the scaling horizon of language models beyond previously anticipated limits. The findings offer a principled framework for future scaling of language models when unique data is a bottleneck.

9e3c493fb09dcd61bb05e8c5659f23327b7b6340.title: Teaching Large Language Models to Self-Debug
9e3c493fb09dcd61bb05e8c5659f23327b7b6340.research_question: How can large language models be enabled to autonomously debug their own code predictions, thereby improving code generation accuracy and sample efficiency across diverse programming tasks without relying on external human feedback or additional model training?
9e3c493fb09dcd61bb05e8c5659f23327b7b6340.hypothesis: Teaching large language models to iteratively self-debug their code predictions using few-shot demonstrations and self-generated feedback, such as code explanations and execution traces, will significantly improve code generation accuracy and sample efficiency compared to existing reranking and prompting-based approaches, even in the absence of external feedback like unit tests.
9e3c493fb09dcd61bb05e8c5659f23327b7b6340.proposed_method: A novel self-debugging framework will be developed that leverages few-shot prompting to instruct large language models to iteratively debug their own code outputs. The method consists of three main steps per debugging turn: (1) Generation, where the model predicts candidate code based on a problem description; (2) Explanation, where the model is prompted to explain the generated code in natural language or provide an execution trace; and (3) Feedback, where the model or external signals (such as unit test results) generate a feedback message regarding code correctness. This feedback is incorporated into the prompt for subsequent turns, enabling the model to revise its code iteratively. The process terminates when the model determines the code is correct or a maximum number of turns is reached. The approach supports multiple feedback modalities, including simple correctness statements, code explanations, and execution traces, and is designed to function both with and without access to unit tests.
9e3c493fb09dcd61bb05e8c5659f23327b7b6340.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three major code generation benchmarks: the Spider dataset for text-to-SQL generation (where no unit tests are available), TransCoder for C++-to-Python translation (with unit tests), and MBPP for text-to-Python generation (with partial unit tests). The evaluation will utilize several large language models, including code-davinci-002 (Codex), GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4, and StarCoder. Baselines will include state-of-the-art reranking models (e.g., T5-3B+N-best Reranking, LEVER), as well as prompting-based methods (MBR-Exec, Coder-Reviewer). Metrics will include code generation accuracy and sample efficiency, with detailed ablation studies on feedback formats, number of initial samples, and the impact of code execution. The experimental setup will use both greedy and temperature-based decoding, and the maximum number of debugging turns will be capped (e.g., at 10).
9e3c493fb09dcd61bb05e8c5659f23327b7b6340.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a new paradigm for teaching large language models to self-debug their code predictions without additional training or external human feedback. The approach uniquely leverages self-generated explanations and execution traces as feedback, enabling models to identify and correct their own errors in a manner analogous to human rubber duck debugging. This method demonstrates significant improvements in code generation accuracy and sample efficiency across multiple benchmarks and model families, outperforming existing reranking and prompting-only baselines. The framework is broadly applicable across tasks with and without unit tests, and provides a scalable path to enhancing LLM coding capabilities while reducing reliance on large-scale sampling.

9e4980cb927b803d375c5796f4a2eb3a7fe0555d.title: The Quantization Model of Neural Scaling
9e4980cb927b803d375c5796f4a2eb3a7fe0555d.research_question: How can the observed power-law scaling of neural network performance with model and data size, as well as the sudden emergence of new capabilities at scale, be theoretically explained and empirically validated? What are the underlying units of knowledge or skill that contribute to neural scaling, and how can these be identified and characterized in large language models?
9e4980cb927b803d375c5796f4a2eb3a7fe0555d.hypothesis: The Quantization Hypothesis: Many natural prediction problems decompose into an enumerable set of discrete computations, pieces of knowledge, or skills ('quanta'), which are either learned or not learned by a model. The frequencies at which these quanta are used for prediction follow a power law, and model performance is determined by which quanta have been learned. Scaling model size or data enables the learning of more quanta in order of their utility, producing power-law scaling of loss and discrete emergent capabilities.
9e4980cb927b803d375c5796f4a2eb3a7fe0555d.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed based on the Quantization Hypothesis, modeling neural network learning as the acquisition of discrete quanta, each corresponding to an indivisible computational module or skill. Analytical derivations will relate the distribution of quanta use frequencies (assumed to follow a power law) to observed power-law scaling in loss with respect to model parameters, data, and training steps. Empirical validation will be performed using both synthetic (toy) datasets constructed to have power-law-distributed subtasks and real-world large language models. A novel algorithm, Quanta Discovery from Gradients (QDG), will be implemented to automatically identify and cluster quanta in language models by analyzing the similarity of model gradients on next-token prediction samples, using spectral clustering on normalized gradient vectors to reveal coherent clusters corresponding to distinct skills.
9e4980cb927b803d375c5796f4a2eb3a7fe0555d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a custom 'multitask sparse parity' toy dataset, where subtasks are distributed in frequency according to a Zipfian (power-law) distribution. Neural networks (ReLU MLPs with a single hidden layer) will be trained on this dataset, and scaling laws will be measured with respect to model parameters, training steps, and dataset size, using cross-entropy loss as the evaluation metric. For real-world validation, the Pythia suite of large language models (EleutherAI), trained on The Pile dataset (~300B tokens), will be analyzed. Per-token cross-entropy losses will be recorded on a held-out test set (~10M tokens) to study the distribution and scaling of loss. The QDG method will be applied to the smallest Pythia model (19M parameters), clustering 10,000 high-confidence, correctly predicted tokens to discover quanta. Rank-frequency distributions of cluster sizes will be compared to theoretical predictions. Baselines include standard scaling law analyses and prior models of neural scaling.
9e4980cb927b803d375c5796f4a2eb3a7fe0555d.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the Quantization Model, a new theoretical framework that explains both smooth power-law neural scaling and the discrete emergence of new capabilities as the acquisition of discrete 'quanta' of knowledge or skill. A novel empirical method (QDG) is developed to automatically discover and enumerate these quanta in language models using gradient-based clustering, providing the first large-scale enumeration of LLM skills. The research connects the frequency distribution of quanta to observed scaling exponents and demonstrates, both theoretically and empirically, that power-law scaling can arise from the accumulation of discrete skills. This approach offers a new lens for understanding neural scaling, emergence, and mechanistic interpretability in deep learning.

9e89ec041c4cd1b16958dcf60d6b49e37521f444.title: Approximation-Generalization Trade-offs under (Approximate) Group Equivariance
9e89ec041c4cd1b16958dcf60d6b49e37521f444.research_question: How do task-specific symmetries, including approximate or partial symmetries, affect the generalization and approximation capabilities of machine learning models, and what are the quantitative trade-offs when model symmetries do not align with data symmetries?
9e89ec041c4cd1b16958dcf60d6b49e37521f444.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that machine learning models that incorporate symmetries aligned with those present in the data will exhibit improved generalization and approximation performance, and that misalignment between model and data symmetries will lead to suboptimal performance. Furthermore, the optimal model symmetry is achieved when the model's equivariance matches the data's symmetry structure, even when these symmetries are only approximate or partial.
9e89ec041c4cd1b16958dcf60d6b49e37521f444.proposed_method: A general theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the generalization and approximation properties of machine learning models under exact, partial, and approximate equivariance. The approach will formalize the learning problem in terms of group actions (not necessarily finite or forming a group) on input and output spaces, and introduce quantitative measures of equivariance error. PAC-style generalization bounds will be derived for models with varying degrees of symmetry, utilizing Rademacher complexity, covering numbers, and the doubling dimension of the transformation set. The framework will also introduce and analyze the concept of model mis-specification, quantifying the relationship between model equivariance error and data equivariance error, and establishing conditions for optimal alignment.
9e89ec041c4cd1b16958dcf60d6b49e37521f444.experiment_details: The investigation will be primarily theoretical, providing generalization and approximation error bounds under various symmetry scenarios. Experiments will consist of mathematical analysis, including the derivation of PAC bounds, covering number estimates, and isodiametric inequalities for both finite and compact groups. Theoretical results will be compared to and generalized from existing results in the literature, such as those for group equivariant neural networks and kernel methods. No specific empirical datasets or baselines are proposed; instead, the evaluation will focus on the sharpness and generality of the derived bounds, as well as their implications for model design in scenarios with limited or approximate symmetries.
9e89ec041c4cd1b16958dcf60d6b49e37521f444.novelty_claims: The proposed research will provide the most general quantitative bounds to date for generalization improvement via task-specific symmetries, without requiring the set of transformations to be finite or to form a group. The framework will rigorously formalize and validate the intuition that optimal model performance is achieved when model and data symmetries are aligned, even in the presence of approximate or partial symmetries. The results will generalize prior work by relaxing assumptions on the structure of the transformation set and by providing explicit trade-offs between generalization and approximation errors under model mis-specification. This work aims to establish a unified theoretical foundation for understanding and optimizing symmetry-based inductive biases in machine learning.

9e8b7b0d4c628c12b6a65ab56ac5f33a35eff2e6.title: Unifying Large Language Models and Knowledge Graphs: A Roadmap
9e8b7b0d4c628c12b6a65ab56ac5f33a35eff2e6.research_question: How can large language models and knowledge graphs be unified to mutually enhance their capabilities in knowledge representation, reasoning, and downstream applications, while overcoming the limitations inherent to each approach?
9e8b7b0d4c628c12b6a65ab56ac5f33a35eff2e6.hypothesis: Integrating large language models and knowledge graphs within unified frameworks will result in improved factual accuracy, interpretability, and reasoning abilities for both systems, compared to using either approach in isolation.
9e8b7b0d4c628c12b6a65ab56ac5f33a35eff2e6.proposed_method: A comprehensive roadmap will be developed to unify large language models (LLMs) and knowledge graphs (KGs) through three general frameworks: (1) KG-enhanced LLMs, where KGs are incorporated into LLMs during pre-training, inference, or for interpretability; (2) LLM-augmented KGs, where LLMs are leveraged for KG tasks such as embedding, completion, construction, graph-to-text generation, and question answering; and (3) Synergized LLMs + KGs, where both systems are integrated in a mutually beneficial manner for bidirectional reasoning. The methodology will involve designing novel training objectives, input representations, and instruction-tuning protocols to inject structured knowledge into LLMs, as well as developing prompting and retrieval-augmented techniques for dynamic knowledge access. Additionally, frameworks for probing and analyzing LLMs with KGs will be established to enhance interpretability and trustworthiness. The research will also extend to multi-modal data integration and the development of unified architectures capable of handling both textual and structured knowledge.
9e8b7b0d4c628c12b6a65ab56ac5f33a35eff2e6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of benchmark datasets, including encyclopedic KGs (e.g., Wikidata, YAGO), commonsense KGs (e.g., ConceptNet, ATOMIC), domain-specific KGs (e.g., UMLS for medical knowledge), and multi-modal KGs (e.g., MMKG, IMGpedia). State-of-the-art LLMs such as BERT, T5, ChatGPT, and open-source models like LLaMA and Vicuna will be utilized. Baselines will include standard LLMs without KG integration, KG-only methods, and existing knowledge-enhanced models. Evaluation metrics will cover factual accuracy, reasoning performance, interpretability (using probing and analysis tasks), and downstream application metrics such as question answering accuracy and text generation quality. Experimental setups will include both static (pre-training) and dynamic (inference-time retrieval and prompting) integration of KGs, as well as ablation studies to assess the contribution of each framework component.
9e8b7b0d4c628c12b6a65ab56ac5f33a35eff2e6.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified and forward-looking roadmap for integrating large language models and knowledge graphs, encompassing three complementary frameworks and providing detailed taxonomies for each. It advances the state of the art by covering both directions of integration (KGs into LLMs and LLMs into KGs), as well as synergistic architectures that enable bidirectional reasoning. The proposal includes novel methods for instruction-tuning, prompt engineering, and retrieval-augmented generation, as well as new approaches for probing and interpreting LLMs with structured knowledge. The work also addresses emerging challenges such as knowledge updating, domain adaptation, and multi-modal knowledge integration, and outlines future research directions for the field.

9e8cb8c91a0acb6e661b58ad724aa758490f2bea.title: Instruction Tuning with GPT-4
9e8cb8c91a0acb6e661b58ad724aa758490f2bea.research_question: Can instruction-tuning large language models (LLMs) using instruction-following data generated by GPT-4, rather than previous models or human annotation, improve the zero-shot and cross-lingual performance of open-source LLMs on unseen tasks and instructions?
9e8cb8c91a0acb6e661b58ad724aa758490f2bea.hypothesis: Instruction-tuning LLMs with GPT-4-generated instruction-following data will yield superior zero-shot generalization and alignment with human values compared to tuning with data generated by previous models or human annotators.
9e8cb8c91a0acb6e661b58ad724aa758490f2bea.proposed_method: A new instruction-tuning framework will be developed that leverages GPT-4 to generate high-quality instruction-following datasets in both English and Chinese. The methodology involves reusing a set of 52K unique instructions, originally from the Alpaca dataset, and prompting GPT-4 to generate corresponding responses using carefully engineered prompt templates for both input-present and input-absent cases. Additionally, GPT-4 will be used to generate comparison and feedback data by rating and ranking responses from multiple models, which will be used to train reward models for further alignment. Supervised fine-tuning will be performed on LLaMA models using the generated datasets, and reward models will be trained on the GPT-4 comparison data to facilitate reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) in future work.
9e8cb8c91a0acb6e661b58ad724aa758490f2bea.experiment_details: Experiments will involve fine-tuning LLaMA-7B models on the 52K English and 52K Chinese instruction-following datasets generated by GPT-4. Evaluation will be conducted on several established benchmarks, including User-Oriented-Instructions-2522, Vicuna-Instructions-803, and Unnatural Instructions (68K samples), to assess zero-shot generalization. Baselines will include models instruction-tuned with GPT-3.5 data (Alpaca), Vicuna, and untuned LLaMA models. Evaluation metrics will include human evaluation on Helpfulness, Honesty, and Harmlessness (HHH) criteria via Amazon Mechanical Turk, automatic evaluation using GPT-4-generated feedback and rankings, and ROUGE-L scores on the Unnatural Instructions dataset. Both English and Chinese performance will be assessed, and cross-lingual generalization will be studied.
9e8cb8c91a0acb6e661b58ad724aa758490f2bea.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first large-scale use of GPT-4 as a data generator for instruction-tuning open-source LLMs, enabling the creation of high-quality, multilingual instruction-following datasets without human annotation. The approach also pioneers the use of GPT-4-generated comparison and feedback data to train reward models, facilitating scalable RLHF. The resulting instruction-tuned models are expected to demonstrate superior alignment and zero-shot performance, closely approaching the capabilities of proprietary models like GPT-4, and the resources (datasets and code) will be made publicly available to advance open-source LLM research.

9e8e0b848bd1ce1326276dd07c266482c8a5f5a7.title: Dataset Distillation with Convexified Implicit Gradients
9e8e0b848bd1ce1326276dd07c266482c8a5f5a7.research_question: How can dataset distillation be improved to achieve higher accuracy and efficiency across a diverse set of benchmarks, particularly in low-data regimes, by leveraging advanced optimization and neural network analysis techniques?
9e8e0b848bd1ce1326276dd07c266482c8a5f5a7.hypothesis: Reparameterizing and convexifying implicit gradient-based meta-optimization, combined with analytic solutions for final-layer parameters and efficient Hessian-inverse computation, will significantly improve the performance and scalability of dataset distillation, especially in challenging settings with few images per class.
9e8e0b848bd1ce1326276dd07c266482c8a5f5a7.proposed_method: The proposed method formulates dataset distillation as a bi-level optimization problem and introduces a framework called Reparameterized Convexified Implicit Gradients (RCIG). The approach leverages implicit gradients for meta-gradient computation, but addresses the non-convexity of deep neural networks by linearizing the inner optimization using a finite-width neural tangent kernel (NTK) approximation, thus convexifying the problem. The method further reparameterizes the neural network by analytically solving for the optimal final-layer parameters given the body parameters, enabling efficient and bias-reduced meta-gradient computation. Hessian-inverse vector products required for implicit gradients are approximated using a Neumann series-inspired stochastic optimization, and memory-efficient subsampling is introduced for scalability. The method includes a pool of partially trained models to account for NTK evolution and employs Platt scaling in the outer objective for improved performance.
9e8e0b848bd1ce1326276dd07c266482c8a5f5a7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of dataset distillation benchmarks, including MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, Caltech Birds 2011, ImageNette, ImageWoof, and resized ImageNet-1K. The method will be evaluated with varying numbers of images per class (e.g., 1, 10, 50) and compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as DSA, DM, KIP, RFAD, MTT, and FRePo. Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy and transferability across different architectures (e.g., ConvNet, ResNet-18, VGG11, AlexNet) and normalization schemes. Additional experiments will assess hyperparameter sensitivity (number of inner optimization and Hessian-inverse steps) and privacy preservation against membership inference attacks using multiple attack strategies. Ablation studies and scalability analyses will be performed to validate the method's efficiency and robustness.
9e8e0b848bd1ce1326276dd07c266482c8a5f5a7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel combination of implicit gradient-based meta-optimization with convexification via NTK linearization and analytic reparameterization of neural network layers, enabling efficient and bias-reduced dataset distillation. The method achieves substantial improvements over prior state-of-the-art in low-data regimes, particularly for benchmarks with many classes and few images per class, and demonstrates strong cross-architecture generalization and privacy-preserving properties. The inclusion of memory-efficient subsampling and analytic solutions for final-layer parameters further distinguishes the approach in terms of scalability and practical applicability.

9e906077f6ea8e309fc48f31cad22377782e7ce0.title: Learning Fair Cooperation in Mixed-Motive Games with Indirect Reciprocity
9e906077f6ea8e309fc48f31cad22377782e7ce0.research_question: How can cooperation and fairness be achieved and sustained among heterogeneous agents in mixed-motive games when both reputations and group identities influence decision-making, particularly under indirect reciprocity? What role do different social norms play in stabilizing cooperative and fair outcomes in such multi-agent systems?
9e906077f6ea8e309fc48f31cad22377782e7ce0.hypothesis: Carefully defined social norms that govern reputation updates based on both group identity and reputational information can enable the emergence and stability of fair and cooperative behaviors among heterogeneous agents in mixed-motive games, even when agents learn independently through reinforcement learning.
9e906077f6ea8e309fc48f31cad22377782e7ce0.proposed_method: A formal model will be developed to study cooperation and fairness in a well-mixed population of agents stratified into two groups, where agents interact via a donation game. Social norms will be defined as rules that assign reputations based on the donor's action, the recipient's reputation, and whether the interaction is in-group or out-group. Two complementary approaches will be employed: (1) an evolutionary game theory (EGT) analysis to systematically search for norm-strategy combinations that yield stable cooperative and fair equilibria, and (2) a reinforcement learning (RL) framework where agents independently learn policies via Q-learning, with reputation updates governed by fixed social norms. The model will allow for execution and judgement errors, and will measure both cooperativeness (probability of cooperation in random interactions) and fairness (parity of payoffs between groups).
9e906077f6ea8e309fc48f31cad22377782e7ce0.experiment_details: Experiments will involve both analytical and agent-based simulations. The EGT analysis will exhaustively evaluate all possible combinations of social norms and strategies for two-group populations, identifying evolutionarily stable states under varying parameters such as group size, benefit-to-cost ratio, and error rates. In the RL experiments, populations of 50 agents (with a 90/10 group split) will be simulated, each agent learning independently via tabular Q-learning with fixed exploration and learning rates. Simulations will run for 250,000 interactions and be repeated 50 times per norm-strategy setup. Key baselines will include well-known social norms (e.g., Stern Judging, Simple Standing, Shunning, Image Scoring) and strategy types (always defect, group-agnostic, discriminatory). Evaluation metrics will include overall cooperation rates and fairness ratios, with additional analysis of convergence dynamics and the impact of initial conditions.
9e906077f6ea8e309fc48f31cad22377782e7ce0.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a systematic framework for analyzing the interplay between group identity, reputation, and social norms in the emergence of fair cooperation in mixed-motive games. It extends prior work by explicitly modeling heterogeneous, group-structured populations and allowing social norms to discriminate between in-group and out-group interactions. The approach combines exhaustive analytical stability analysis with large-scale multi-agent reinforcement learning experiments, revealing how the choice of social norm critically determines both the stability and learnability of fair cooperative equilibria. The research also identifies conditions under which well-known norms can or cannot sustain fairness and cooperation in realistic, decentralized learning settings, providing new insights into the algorithmic design of fair multi-agent systems.

9e9e4df2996bac794c4f04cb887df3e553bae4fd.title: Logic-LM: Empowering Large Language Models with Symbolic Solvers for Faithful Logical Reasoning
9e9e4df2996bac794c4f04cb887df3e553bae4fd.research_question: How can large language models be empowered to perform faithful and robust logical reasoning on complex problems, overcoming the limitations of probabilistic reasoning and unfaithful inference?
9e9e4df2996bac794c4f04cb887df3e553bae4fd.hypothesis: Integrating large language models with deterministic symbolic solvers, along with iterative self-refinement based on solver feedback, will significantly improve the faithfulness and accuracy of logical reasoning compared to language models alone or with chain-of-thought prompting.
9e9e4df2996bac794c4f04cb887df3e553bae4fd.proposed_method: A novel neuro-symbolic framework is proposed that decomposes logical reasoning into three stages: (1) a Problem Formulator uses a large language model (LLM) to translate natural language problems into symbolic formulations tailored for the target reasoning task (e.g., logic programming, first-order logic, constraint satisfaction, or SAT); (2) a Symbolic Reasoner invokes a deterministic external solver (such as a logic programming engine, FOL prover, CSP solver, or SMT solver) to perform inference on the symbolic representation; (3) a Result Interpreter translates the solver's output back into natural language answers. To address inaccuracies in symbolic parsing, a self-refinement module iteratively revises the symbolic formalization using error messages from the symbolic solver as feedback, prompting the LLM to correct and resubmit the logical form until it is executable or a maximum number of iterations is reached. The framework is designed to be modular and generalizable, supporting multiple symbolic reasoning paradigms and adaptable to a wide range of logical problem types.
9e9e4df2996bac794c4f04cb887df3e553bae4fd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five diverse logical reasoning datasets: ProofWriter, PrOntoQA, FOLIO, Logical Deduction (from BigBench), and AR-LSAT. These datasets encompass deductive reasoning, first-order logic, constraint satisfaction, and analytical reasoning tasks. The proposed method will be compared against two strong baselines: standard LLM prompting (in-context learning) and chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting, using multiple LLMs (ChatGPT/gpt-3.5-turbo, GPT-3.5/text-davinci-003, and GPT-4). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy of final answers, percentage of executable symbolic forms, and accuracy on executable cases. Additional analyses will assess robustness across reasoning depths, the effectiveness of self-refinement rounds, and the semantic correctness of generated symbolic forms. Experimental setups will ensure balanced label distributions and fair comparisons by using the same in-context examples and controlling for randomness.
9e9e4df2996bac794c4f04cb887df3e553bae4fd.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a generalizable neuro-symbolic framework that shifts the burden of reasoning from LLMs to external symbolic solvers, ensuring faithfulness and transparency in logical inference. The approach is the first to systematically extend auto-formalization and solver integration to a broad range of logical reasoning tasks beyond mathematics, covering multiple symbolic paradigms. The self-refinement mechanism leverages solver error feedback to iteratively improve symbolic parsing, enhancing robustness and execution rates. The method demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over both standard and chain-of-thought LLM prompting, especially as reasoning complexity increases, and highlights the potential for further advances by integrating more expressive symbolic solvers and specialized NL-to-logic mapping modules.

9efbfeba1aab9d3cff85dca8acd0545f536174b9.title: Randomized Dimensionality Reduction for Euclidean Maximization and Diversity Measures
9efbfeba1aab9d3cff85dca8acd0545f536174b9.research_question: How can randomized, data-oblivious dimensionality reduction techniques be leveraged to approximately preserve the value of near-optimal solutions for a broad class of Euclidean maximization and diversity problems, and how does the intrinsic dimensionality (doubling dimension) of the dataset influence the effectiveness and necessary target dimension of such reductions?
9efbfeba1aab9d3cff85dca8acd0545f536174b9.hypothesis: Randomized, data-oblivious dimensionality reduction using Gaussian Johnson-Lindenstrauss (JL) transforms to a target dimension proportional to the doubling dimension of the dataset will, with high probability, approximately preserve the value of near-optimal solutions for a wide range of Euclidean maximization and diversity problems, and this dependence on doubling dimension is both sufficient and, in some cases, necessary.
9efbfeba1aab9d3cff85dca8acd0545f536174b9.proposed_method: A framework will be developed that applies randomized, data-oblivious dimensionality reduction via Gaussian JL transforms to project high-dimensional datasets into lower-dimensional spaces. The target dimension t will be set as a function of the dataset's doubling dimension λ and the desired approximation parameter ε, typically t = O(ε^{-2} λ log(1/ε)). The method will be analyzed for several geometric optimization problems, including maximum weight matching, maximum spanning tree, maximum TSP, k-hypermatching, k-coverage, and subgraph diversity maximization. Theoretical guarantees will be established to show that, with high probability, any (1+ε)-approximate solution in the projected space corresponds to a (1+O(ε))-approximate solution in the original space. Tight lower bounds will also be established to demonstrate the necessity of the dependence on λ for these problems.
9efbfeba1aab9d3cff85dca8acd0545f536174b9.experiment_details: Empirical evaluation will be conducted on both real and synthetic datasets, including MNIST digits, high-dimensional CIFAR embeddings, and synthetic point sets with controlled doubling dimensions. For each dataset, both low and high intrinsic dimensionality versions will be constructed. The proposed dimensionality reduction will be applied with varying target dimensions, and the performance of algorithms for maximum matching, remote clique, and max k-coverage will be measured in terms of relative error compared to the original high-dimensional solution. Baseline comparisons will include the effect of projecting to dimensions based on dataset size (as in classical JL), and the evaluation metrics will focus on solution quality (relative error) and computational speedup. Multiple independent trials will be performed to assess statistical significance, and standard deviations will be reported.
9efbfeba1aab9d3cff85dca8acd0545f536174b9.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified theoretical and empirical framework demonstrating that, for a broad class of Euclidean maximization and diversity problems, randomized, data-oblivious dimensionality reduction to a dimension proportional to the doubling dimension suffices to approximately preserve solution quality. The approach generalizes prior results that were limited to specific problems (e.g., facility location) and establishes tight lower bounds, revealing sharp threshold phenomena for certain problems. Additionally, the empirical study is the first to systematically quantify the impact of doubling dimension on the effectiveness of dimensionality reduction for these optimization problems, providing practical guidance and validating theoretical predictions.

9f0f134bc53f9aea130f1a561acb5fa6b08ae4ce.title: Iterated Denoising Energy Matching for Sampling from Boltzmann Densities
9f0f134bc53f9aea130f1a561acb5fa6b08ae4ce.research_question: How can a scalable and efficient sampler be developed to generate statistically independent samples from an unnormalized Boltzmann-type probability distribution, using only access to the energy function and its gradient, while achieving high mode coverage and computational tractability in high-dimensional scientific systems?
9f0f134bc53f9aea130f1a561acb5fa6b08ae4ce.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that an iterative, simulation-free stochastic score matching algorithm leveraging only the energy function and its gradient can train a diffusion-based sampler to efficiently and accurately sample from complex, high-dimensional Boltzmann distributions, achieving superior mode coverage and computational efficiency compared to existing methods.
9f0f134bc53f9aea130f1a561acb5fa6b08ae4ce.proposed_method: A novel iterative algorithm, Iterated Denoising Energy Matching (iDEM), is proposed for sampling from Boltzmann densities. The method alternates between two key steps: (1) an inner loop that trains a diffusion-based sampler using a stochastic score matching objective (DEM), which regresses the neural score estimator to a Monte Carlo estimate of the score of the target density convolved with noise, leveraging only the energy function and its gradient; and (2) an outer loop that uses the current diffusion sampler to generate informative samples via reverse SDE simulation, populating a replay buffer that provides starting points for further training, thus enabling efficient exploration of the energy landscape. The approach is simulation-free in the inner loop, requires no MCMC samples, and can incorporate system symmetries (e.g., SE(3) × S_n invariance) directly into the training objective and sampling process. The methodology is scalable to high dimensions and iteratively improves the amortized sampler by retraining on progressively better samples.
9f0f134bc53f9aea130f1a561acb5fa6b08ae4ce.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of benchmark tasks, including a 40-mode Gaussian mixture model (GMM) and several SE(3) × S_n-invariant n-body particle systems: a 4-particle double-well potential (DW-4), a 13-particle Lennard-Jones potential (LJ-13), and a challenging 55-particle Lennard-Jones system (LJ-55). The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as Path Integral Sampler (PIS), Denoising Diffusion Sampler (DDS), and Flow Annealed Bootstrapping (FAB), as well as a prior-based DEM variant (pDEM). Evaluation metrics will include negative log-likelihood (NLL), 2-Wasserstein distance (W2), Effective Sample Size (ESS), and additional metrics such as log partition function and total variation distance. The experimental setup will use neural network architectures appropriate for each task (MLPs with positional embeddings for GMM, EGNN flows for equivariant systems), and training times, stability, and scalability will be systematically measured.
9f0f134bc53f9aea130f1a561acb5fa6b08ae4ce.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simulation-free, bi-level iterative framework for training diffusion-based samplers using only the energy function and its gradient, without requiring data samples or MCMC trajectories. The DEM objective enables off-policy, scalable, and efficient score estimation, allowing for rapid training and improved mode coverage even in high-dimensional, multimodal energy landscapes. The approach is the first to successfully train an energy-based sampler on the challenging 55-particle Lennard-Jones system using only the energy, and it incorporates system symmetries directly into both the objective and the sampling process. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on all metrics, with significantly reduced computational cost and improved stability compared to prior methods.

9f1cb6cbcfa1e3e862861d9a945c1eed25f2f50e.title: PolaFormer: Polarity-aware Linear Attention for Vision Transformers
9f1cb6cbcfa1e3e862861d9a945c1eed25f2f50e.research_question: How can the expressive capacity and efficiency of linear attention mechanisms in vision transformers be improved by addressing the information loss associated with non-negative feature maps and the lack of attention spikiness, while maintaining linear computational complexity?
9f1cb6cbcfa1e3e862861d9a945c1eed25f2f50e.hypothesis: Explicitly modeling both same-signed and opposite-signed query-key interactions in linear attention, combined with a learnable power-based rescaling function, will enhance the expressiveness and discriminative power of attention maps, reduce entropy, and improve performance on vision tasks without sacrificing computational efficiency.
9f1cb6cbcfa1e3e862861d9a945c1eed25f2f50e.proposed_method: A polarity-aware linear attention mechanism is developed that decomposes query and key vectors into their positive and negative components, enabling explicit modeling of both same-signed (positive-positive, negative-negative) and opposite-signed (positive-negative, negative-positive) interactions. These interactions are processed in two separate streams, with the value vectors split along the channel dimension and concatenated after independent processing. Learnable sign-aware coefficient matrices are introduced to mix the outputs of the two streams, allowing the model to adaptively weigh the contributions of each type of interaction. To restore the spiky properties of softmax-based attention and reduce entropy, a channel-wise learnable power function with an exponent greater than one is applied as a rescaling function, where the exponent is a learnable parameter for each channel. The overall framework maintains linear complexity with respect to sequence length and can be integrated into existing vision transformer architectures.
9f1cb6cbcfa1e3e862861d9a945c1eed25f2f50e.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on multiple vision benchmarks, including ImageNet-1K for image classification, COCO for object detection and instance segmentation, and ADE20K for semantic segmentation. The proposed method is integrated into several popular transformer backbones (DeiT, PVT, PVTv2, Swin) by replacing their self-attention modules. Models are trained from scratch on ImageNet-1K and fine-tuned for downstream tasks. Evaluation metrics include Top-1 accuracy for classification, AP metrics for detection and segmentation, and mIoU for semantic segmentation. Additional benchmarking is performed on the Long Range Arena (LRA) to assess performance on long-sequence tasks, with comparisons to a wide range of linear and efficient attention baselines. Ablation studies examine the impact of each component, such as the polarity-aware mixing and learnable power function, and analyze efficiency in terms of FLOPs and inference speed.
9f1cb6cbcfa1e3e862861d9a945c1eed25f2f50e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a polarity-aware linear attention mechanism that, for the first time, explicitly models both same-signed and opposite-signed query-key interactions in a linear attention framework. A theoretical analysis is provided, demonstrating that a family of element-wise functions with positive first and second derivatives can reduce entropy in the attention distribution, and a learnable power function is employed for practical and adaptive rescaling. The method achieves improved expressiveness and discriminative power in attention maps while preserving linear computational complexity. Extensive experiments show consistent performance gains across multiple vision tasks and benchmarks, outperforming existing linear attention methods and achieving state-of-the-art results on the Long Range Arena.

9f405d2a43d4c62764b5a9a1630a20afbeb52450.title: Decoding by Contrasting Knowledge: Enhancing LLMs' Confidence on Edited Facts
9f405d2a43d4c62764b5a9a1630a20afbeb52450.research_question: How can the confidence of large language models (LLMs) in edited facts be enhanced, particularly for stubborn knowledge that resists modification through in-context editing methods?
9f405d2a43d4c62764b5a9a1630a20afbeb52450.hypothesis: A decoding strategy that contrasts the logits of newly edited knowledge with those from the original parametric knowledge will amplify the model's confidence in edited facts, thereby improving the effectiveness of in-context editing, especially for stubborn knowledge.
9f405d2a43d4c62764b5a9a1630a20afbeb52450.proposed_method: A novel decoding framework, Decoding by Contrasting Knowledge (DeCK), will be developed to enhance in-context editing (ICE) for LLMs. The method consists of two main components: (1) an editing signal enhancement module that boosts attention to new knowledge by minimizing a Knowledge Enhancement Divergence (KED) between the enhanced and target distributions, using semantic relevance and frequency-based weighting; and (2) a contrastive decoding strategy that computes the next-token distribution by subtracting the log probabilities of the original parametric knowledge from those of the enhanced ICE distribution, with an adaptive plausibility constraint to filter out low-probability tokens. During generation, both the edited and original token sequences are maintained and updated in parallel, ensuring synchronization and preventing implausible discrepancies. The approach is designed to be model-agnostic and can be integrated into any ICE method as a decoding component.
9f405d2a43d4c62764b5a9a1630a20afbeb52450.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the MQUAKE-3K dataset and its derivatives (MQUAKE-2002, MQUAKE-HARD), which contain multi-hop knowledge questions with edited facts, as well as custom-constructed STUBBORN datasets to specifically evaluate editing of stubborn knowledge. The evaluation will utilize several LLMs, including LLAMA2-7B-CHAT, LLAMA2-13B-CHAT, LLAMA3-8B-INSTRUCT, and MISTRAL-7B-INSTRUCT. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art in-context editing methods (IKE, MeLLo) and model-editing techniques (ROME). Performance will be measured primarily by accuracy on edited knowledge questions, with additional analysis of probability distributions and ranking changes for new knowledge. Ablation studies will assess the impact of key components such as the contrasting coefficient and editing signal enhancement.
9f405d2a43d4c62764b5a9a1630a20afbeb52450.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to systematically address the challenge of stubborn knowledge in LLMs from a decoding and interpretability perspective. DeCK introduces a novel contrastive decoding mechanism that directly amplifies the confidence in edited facts without altering model parameters or external prompts. The method is modular, easily integrable with existing ICE approaches, and demonstrates substantial improvements in editing stubborn knowledge, as evidenced by significant accuracy gains (up to 219%) over baselines. The work advances both the effectiveness and accountability of knowledge editing in LLMs.

9f4c17aebbb181756fab86ade02deadd90d5d4f9.title: How Robust is Google's Bard to Adversarial Image Attacks?
9f4c17aebbb181756fab86ade02deadd90d5d4f9.research_question: How robust are commercial multimodal large language models (MLLMs), such as Google’s Bard, to adversarial image attacks, and what are the vulnerabilities and limitations of their defense mechanisms?
9f4c17aebbb181756fab86ade02deadd90d5d4f9.hypothesis: Commercial MLLMs, including Google’s Bard, are susceptible to adversarial image attacks due to the transferability of adversarial examples generated using surrogate models, and their current defense mechanisms (e.g., face and toxicity detection) can be effectively bypassed.
9f4c17aebbb181756fab86ade02deadd90d5d4f9.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation of the adversarial robustness of commercial MLLMs will be conducted by generating adversarial images using state-of-the-art transfer-based attack methods, specifically the SSA-CWA (Spectrum Simulation Attack combined with Common Weakness Attack). Two main attack strategies will be implemented: (1) image embedding attack, which maximizes the distance between the embeddings of adversarial and natural images across an ensemble of surrogate vision encoders; and (2) text description attack, which maximizes the log-likelihood of a targeted sentence output by surrogate MLLMs given adversarial images. The attacks will be optimized under an ℓ∞ perturbation constraint (e.g., ϵ=16/255), and the transferability of adversarial examples will be assessed by evaluating their effectiveness against black-box commercial MLLMs. Additionally, targeted attacks will be designed to evade Bard’s face and toxicity detection modules by minimizing the confidence scores of surrogate detectors.
9f4c17aebbb181756fab86ade02deadd90d5d4f9.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize a variety of datasets: 100 randomly selected images from the NIPS17 dataset for image description attacks, 100 images each from FFHQ and LFW datasets for face detection attacks, and a manually collected set of 100 toxic images for toxicity detection attacks. Surrogate models for attacks will include vision encoders such as ViT-B/16, CLIP, and BLIP-2, as well as MLLMs like BLIP-2, InstructBLIP, and MiniGPT-4. For face detection, PyramidBox, S3FD, and DSFD will serve as surrogates. The main evaluation metric will be attack success rate, defined as the percentage of adversarial images that cause incorrect or inappropriate model outputs, with rejection rates also reported. Baseline comparisons will include no-attack scenarios and ablation studies on surrogate model ensembles. The transferability of adversarial examples will be tested on additional commercial MLLMs, including GPT-4V, BingChat, and ERNIEBot.
9f4c17aebbb181756fab86ade02deadd90d5d4f9.novelty_claims: This proposal aims to be the first to systematically evaluate the adversarial robustness of commercial MLLMs such as Google’s Bard in a black-box setting, leveraging transfer-based attacks. It introduces a comprehensive framework for attacking both the core image description capabilities and the auxiliary defense mechanisms (face and toxicity detection) of these models. The approach demonstrates the high transferability of adversarial examples across different commercial MLLMs and reveals the vulnerabilities of current defense strategies, providing critical insights for the development of more robust and trustworthy multimodal foundation models.

9f6a1e4b2bf4eb32afa81950dc0dbfec83603ac9.title: Your Policy Regularizer is Secretly an Adversary
9f6a1e4b2bf4eb32afa81950dc0dbfec83603ac9.research_question: How does policy regularization in reinforcement learning contribute to robustness and generalization of learned policies, particularly in the presence of adversarial perturbations to the reward function, and how can this robustness be formally characterized and visualized across different regularization schemes?
9f6a1e4b2bf4eb32afa81950dc0dbfec83603ac9.hypothesis: Policy regularization, when formulated via convex divergence penalties (such as KL or alpha-divergences), implicitly induces robustness to a well-defined set of worst-case adversarial reward perturbations, and this robustness can be precisely characterized and visualized using convex duality. Furthermore, the structure of this robustness set and the nature of worst-case perturbations depend on the choice of regularization and its parameters.
9f6a1e4b2bf4eb32afa81950dc0dbfec83603ac9.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed that interprets policy regularization in reinforcement learning as a two-player minimax game between the agent and an implicit adversary that perturbs the reward function within a constrained set. Using convex duality, the robust set of feasible adversarial reward perturbations will be derived for various regularization schemes, including KL and alpha-divergences, encompassing Shannon and Tsallis entropy as special cases. The worst-case reward perturbations for arbitrary and optimal policies will be analytically characterized, and their relationship to advantage functions and path consistency conditions will be established. The robust set of adversarial rewards will be visualized for different regularization strengths and divergence types, providing geometric and intuitive insights into the nature of policy robustness.
9f6a1e4b2bf4eb32afa81950dc0dbfec83603ac9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a sequential grid-world task and single-step decision-making scenarios. The robust set of adversarially perturbed rewards will be visualized for optimal and suboptimal policies under different regularization strengths (varying beta) and divergence types (KL and alpha-divergences with various alpha values). Theoretical predictions regarding the worst-case perturbations and indifference conditions will be empirically validated by comparing the perturbed rewards, policy distributions, and value functions. Evaluation metrics will include visual confirmation of the robust set boundaries, the satisfaction of path consistency and indifference conditions, and the comparison of policy performance under adversarially perturbed rewards. Baselines will include both unregularized and entropy-regularized policies for comparison.
9f6a1e4b2bf4eb32afa81950dc0dbfec83603ac9.novelty_claims: The proposed research unifies and extends prior interpretations of policy regularization as robustness to adversarial reward perturbations, providing a general convex duality-based framework applicable to a wide class of divergence regularizers. It offers explicit characterizations and visualizations of the robust set of adversarial rewards for both KL and alpha-divergence regularization, generalizing previous results limited to specific cases. The analysis reveals new insights into the structure of robustness, the dependence on regularization parameters, and the relationship to path consistency and Nash equilibrium indifference conditions. The approach also clarifies misconceptions from prior work regarding the impact of regularization strength on robustness, and provides practical tools for certifying policy optimality and generalization guarantees in regularized reinforcement learning.

9fac3d0728a8c833a593446e3e176e90d856df04.title: VideoMAE V2: Scaling Video Masked Autoencoders with Dual Masking
9fac3d0728a8c833a593446e3e176e90d856df04.research_question: How can video masked autoencoder models be efficiently scaled in both model size and data volume to enable billion-parameter video foundation models that generalize effectively across a wide range of video understanding tasks?
9fac3d0728a8c833a593446e3e176e90d856df04.hypothesis: Introducing a dual masking strategy—masking both the encoder and decoder—combined with progressive pre-training on large, diverse video datasets, will enable efficient training of billion-parameter video masked autoencoders that achieve state-of-the-art performance and generalization across multiple video downstream tasks.
9fac3d0728a8c833a593446e3e176e90d856df04.proposed_method: A scalable video masked autoencoder framework is proposed, featuring a dual masking strategy that applies high-ratio random tube masking to the encoder and a complementary, information-diverse masking (e.g., running cell masking) to the decoder. The encoder processes only a subset of video tokens, while the decoder reconstructs another subset, reducing computational and memory requirements. The training pipeline is progressive: initial self-supervised pre-training is conducted on a million-level, multi-source unlabeled video dataset, followed by supervised post-pre-training on a hybrid labeled dataset constructed from multiple public video benchmarks. The backbone is a vanilla Vision Transformer (ViT) scaled from base to giant (billion-level parameters), with a lightweight decoder. The final reconstruction loss is computed only on tokens invisible to the encoder, further improving efficiency.
9fac3d0728a8c833a593446e3e176e90d856df04.experiment_details: Experiments will pre-train the proposed model on a large-scale, diverse, unlabeled video dataset (UnlabeledHybrid, ~1.35M clips from sources such as Kinetics, Something-Something, AVA, WebVid2M, and Instagram), followed by post-pre-training on a hybrid labeled dataset (LabeledHybrid, ~0.66M clips, 710 categories). Baselines include prior masked autoencoding methods (e.g., VideoMAE, MAE-ST, MaskFeat) and state-of-the-art supervised and self-supervised video models. Evaluation will be conducted on multiple downstream tasks: action classification (Kinetics-400/600, Something-Something V1/V2, UCF101, HMDB51), spatial action detection (AVA, AVA-Kinetics), and temporal action detection (THUMOS14, FineAction). Metrics include top-1/top-5 accuracy for classification, mean Average Precision (mAP) for detection, and computational efficiency (FLOPs, memory usage, training time).
