Ablation studies will analyze the impact of decoder masking strategies, masking ratios, model/data scaling, and progressive training.
9fac3d0728a8c833a593446e3e176e90d856df04.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a dual masking strategy for video masked autoencoders, enabling both encoder and decoder masking to significantly reduce computational and memory costs, thus making billion-parameter video transformer pre-training feasible. This is the first approach to successfully scale video masked autoencoders to the billion-parameter regime and pre-train on million-level video datasets. The progressive training pipeline, leveraging both large-scale unsupervised and supervised hybrid datasets, further enhances generalization and mitigates overfitting. The resulting models are demonstrated to achieve new state-of-the-art results across a broad spectrum of video understanding benchmarks, establishing a new paradigm for scalable video foundation models.

9fb201282f53a4ce89f28cbe5026af78912aa8c1.title: Qwen2.5-Math Technical Report: Toward Mathematical Expert Model via Self-Improvement
9fb201282f53a4ce89f28cbe5026af78912aa8c1.research_question: How can large language models be systematically improved to achieve expert-level mathematical reasoning and problem-solving capabilities across both English and Chinese, including complex competition-level mathematics, through self-improvement techniques integrated throughout the training pipeline?
9fb201282f53a4ce89f28cbe5026af78912aa8c1.hypothesis: Integrating self-improvement mechanisms—such as iterative data synthesis, reward modeling, and reinforcement learning—across pre-training, post-training, and inference stages will significantly enhance the mathematical reasoning abilities of large language models, surpassing both open-source and closed-source baselines in diverse mathematical benchmarks.
9fb201282f53a4ce89f28cbe5026af78912aa8c1.proposed_method: A comprehensive self-improvement framework will be developed for mathematical large language models, consisting of three main stages: pre-training, post-training, and inference. In pre-training, a high-quality, large-scale mathematical corpus (over 1 trillion tokens) will be constructed by aggregating and filtering data from web sources, code repositories, and synthetic data generated by previous model iterations. Post-training will involve supervised fine-tuning on datasets specifically designed for Chain-of-Thought (CoT) and Tool-Integrated Reasoning (TIR), with iterative data synthesis and response selection guided by a custom-trained reward model. The reward model will be trained to provide granular feedback on reasoning quality, using a listwise ranking loss over multiple candidate responses per problem. Reinforcement learning will be applied using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), with reward shaping that combines rule-based verification and reward model outputs. During inference, the reward model will further guide response sampling to optimize performance.
9fb201282f53a4ce89f28cbe5026af78912aa8c1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of 10 mathematical benchmarks covering both English and Chinese, including GSM8K, MATH, GaoKao, AMC23, AIME24, OlympiadBench, CollegeMath, MMLU-STEM, CMATH, and CNMiddleSchool24. Both base and instruction-tuned models at various parameter scales (1.5B, 7B, 72B) will be evaluated. Baselines will include general-purpose models (Llama-3.1-8B/70B/405B, Qwen2-1.5B/7B/72B) and math-specific models (DeepSeekMath-Base-7B, DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Base, Internlm2-Math-Base-20B). Evaluation will use few-shot chain-of-thought prompting, as well as tool-integrated reasoning with Python interpreter support. Metrics will include pass@1 accuracy and benchmark-specific scores. Rigorous decontamination procedures will be implemented to ensure unbiased evaluation by filtering out training samples similar to test data.
9fb201282f53a4ce89f28cbe5026af78912aa8c1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified self-improvement pipeline that integrates iterative data synthesis, reward modeling, and reinforcement learning across all training stages. Key innovations include the use of a reward model for both supervised fine-tuning data selection and reinforcement learning, the development of large-scale, high-quality bilingual mathematical datasets, and the incorporation of tool-integrated reasoning capabilities. The method is designed to enable smaller models to outperform much larger baselines, and to achieve state-of-the-art results on both English and Chinese mathematical benchmarks, including competition-level problems. The approach also emphasizes robust decontamination to ensure fair and reliable evaluation.

9fb327c55a30b9771a364f45f33f77778756a164.title: I-ViT: Integer-only Quantization for Efficient Vision Transformer Inference
9fb327c55a30b9771a364f45f33f77778756a164.research_question: How can Vision Transformers (ViTs) be quantized to enable efficient, integer-only inference across the entire computational graph, while maintaining accuracy and maximizing hardware acceleration on resource-constrained devices?
9fb327c55a30b9771a364f45f33f77778756a164.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by designing novel integer-only arithmetic approximations for non-linear operations in ViTs, alongside established integer-only pipelines for linear operations, it is possible to achieve efficient, fully integer-only inference with negligible or no loss in accuracy compared to full-precision models, and with significant inference speedup on compatible hardware.
9fb327c55a30b9771a364f45f33f77778756a164.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a comprehensive integer-only quantization framework for Vision Transformers, termed I-ViT. All linear operations, such as matrix multiplications and dense layers, are quantized and executed using dyadic arithmetic, which leverages integer multiplication and bit-shifting to replace floating-point scaling. For non-linear operations, novel integer-only approximations are developed: Shiftmax for Softmax, ShiftGELU for GELU activations, and I-LayerNorm for Layer Normalization. Shiftmax and ShiftGELU utilize efficient bit-shifting and integer arithmetic to approximate their respective floating-point counterparts, while I-LayerNorm employs an iterative integer method for square root computation. The entire computational graph, from input to output, is quantized to INT8, ensuring that all inference computations are performed using integer-only arithmetic without any floating-point operations.
9fb327c55a30b9771a364f45f33f77778756a164.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on popular ViT architectures including ViT, DeiT, and Swin Transformer, using the ImageNet (ILSVRC-2012) dataset for large-scale image classification. The proposed method will be compared against full-precision (FP32) baselines and state-of-the-art quantization methods such as FasterTransformer (which leaves non-linear operations as floating-point) and I-BERT (which uses integer polynomial approximations). Evaluation metrics include Top-1 classification accuracy and inference latency. Latency measurements will be performed on an RTX 2080Ti GPU using TVM to deploy the integer-only models, leveraging Turing Tensor Cores for acceleration. Ablation studies will be conducted to assess the impact of each integer-only approximation component, and batch size scaling will be evaluated to test robustness of acceleration.
9fb327c55a30b9771a364f45f33f77778756a164.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first integer-only quantization scheme for Vision Transformers that quantizes the entire computational graph, enabling end-to-end integer-only inference. The method develops novel, hardware-friendly integer approximations for non-linear operations (Shiftmax, ShiftGELU, and I-LayerNorm) that use bit-shifting for efficient computation. The approach achieves comparable or even superior accuracy to full-precision baselines while providing significant (3.7–4.1x) inference speedup on modern GPUs. The framework is designed for practical deployment and is compatible with existing hardware acceleration libraries such as TVM.

NuCtKoflsV.title: DynamicRAG: Leveraging Outputs of Large Language Model as Feedback for Dynamic Reranking in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
NuCtKoflsV.research_question: How can the reranking component in retrieval-augmented generation systems be optimized to dynamically select and order retrieved documents based on query complexity and generation quality to improve answer quality and system efficiency?
NuCtKoflsV.hypothesis: Using the quality of LLM-generated responses as a reward signal to train a reranker agent via reinforcement learning will enable dynamic adjustment of document selection, resulting in better generation quality and overall system performance.
NuCtKoflsV.proposed_method: DynamicRAG framework comprising a frozen retriever, a trainable dynamic reranker modeled as an RL agent, and a trainable generator. The reranker dynamically selects and orders documents based on query and feedback from generation quality. Training involves supervised fine-tuning with expert trajectories followed by reinforcement learning using a multi-dimensional reward function integrating exact match, semantic similarity, fluency, length penalty, and LLM-based evaluation.
NuCtKoflsV.experiment_details: Comparative experiments against baselines with and without retrieval, ablation studies removing retrieval, reranking, and RL components, evaluation of reranker and generator model sizes, efficiency analysis comparing LLM call counts and runtime with competitors like RankRAG. Metrics include exact match, accuracy, ROUGE-L, and recall at various ranks.
NuCtKoflsV.novelty_claims: Introduction of a dynamic reranking mechanism that adjusts both the order and number of documents per query, trained via reinforcement learning using LLM output quality as a reward signal. This contrasts with prior static rerankers and leads to state-of-the-art performance with higher efficiency and less training data.

a01e1138600499f65462ed3d51c3e76af1aad18c.title: The pitfalls of next-token prediction
a01e1138600499f65462ed3d51c3e76af1aad18c.research_question: Can next-token prediction objectives in language models faithfully capture the planning and reasoning abilities characteristic of human intelligence, or are there fundamental limitations that hinder their performance even on straightforward tasks requiring lookahead and planning?
a01e1138600499f65462ed3d51c3e76af1aad18c.hypothesis: Teacher-forcing-based next-token prediction can fail to learn accurate next-token predictors for certain classes of tasks, particularly those requiring lookahead or implicit planning, resulting in in-distribution failures that cannot be resolved by architectural changes or post-hoc inference-time strategies. Alternative training paradigms, such as teacherless multi-token prediction, may overcome these limitations.
a01e1138600499f65462ed3d51c3e76af1aad18c.proposed_method: A minimal planning task will be designed, such as a path-finding problem on a class of graphs (path-star graphs), where the input consists of a graph description and start/goal nodes, and the output is the sequence of nodes forming the path. Models will be trained using standard teacher-forcing (next-token prediction conditioned on ground-truth prefixes), as well as alternative objectives: teacherless training (predicting multiple future tokens without access to ground-truth prefixes) and reversed target training (predicting the path in reverse order). The methodology will involve constructing datasets with randomized graph labeling and adjacency lists to prevent memorization, and training both Transformer and structured state space (Mamba) architectures from scratch and with pretraining. Key technical steps include careful control of supervision signals, explicit separation of training and inference regimes, and the design of metrics to isolate specific failure modes (e.g., Clever Hans cheating and indecipherable tokens).
a01e1138600499f65462ed3d51c3e76af1aad18c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic datasets of path-star graphs with varying degrees and path lengths, where each instance requires the model to output the correct path from start to goal. Models will be evaluated on both training and held-out test data drawn from the same distribution, ensuring that failures are in-distribution. Baselines will include standard teacher-forced next-token prediction, teacherless multi-token prediction, and reversed target training. Evaluation metrics will include exact-match accuracy for the full path, token-wise accuracy (especially for the first token, which is hypothesized to be indecipherable under teacher-forcing), and specific tests for shortcut exploitation (Clever Hans cheat). Both Transformers (GPT-Mini, GPT-2 Large) and Mamba architectures will be used, with optimization via AdamW and extensive training to rule out underfitting. Additional experiments will probe the generality of the findings on arithmetic tasks and with different architectural families.
a01e1138600499f65462ed3d51c3e76af1aad18c.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a precise and empirically verifiable failure mode of next-token prediction under teacher-forcing, distinct from previously discussed inference-time error compounding. It provides a minimal, easy-to-learn task where standard next-token prediction fails in-distribution, not due to model capacity or architecture, but due to the training objective itself. The work formalizes the Clever Hans cheat and indecipherable token phenomena, and demonstrates that simple modifications such as teacherless multi-token prediction or reversed target training can restore learnability. This challenges prevailing assumptions about the sufficiency of next-token prediction for planning and reasoning, and motivates exploration of alternative training paradigms for language models.

a020ae590e9ffba46adcfdfaa263e5d7eb911eab.title: Bongard in Wonderland: Visual Puzzles that Still Make AI Go Mad?
a020ae590e9ffba46adcfdfaa263e5d7eb911eab.research_question: To what extent do state-of-the-art Vision-Language Models (VLMs) exhibit human-like pattern recognition and abstract reasoning abilities when challenged with complex visual puzzles such as Bongard problems, and what are the specific limitations and failure modes in their visual perception and reasoning capabilities compared to humans?
a020ae590e9ffba46adcfdfaa263e5d7eb911eab.hypothesis: Current state-of-the-art VLMs will exhibit significant shortcomings in solving Bongard problems, particularly in tasks requiring abstract reasoning, pattern recognition, and generalization to unseen visual concepts, resulting in a substantial performance gap compared to human participants.
a020ae590e9ffba46adcfdfaa263e5d7eb911eab.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation framework will be developed to assess the capabilities of multiple state-of-the-art VLMs on the original set of 100 Bongard problems. The methodology will include several task settings: (1) open-ended problem solving where models must generate natural language rules distinguishing two groups of diagrams; (2) a multiple-choice format where models select the correct rule pair from a predefined set; (3) a concept detection task in which models classify individual images based on provided ground-truth concepts; and (4) a hypothesis generation task where models are prompted to propose possible rules, with success measured by inclusion of the correct rule. Tailored prompts and input formats will be designed for each task to ensure fair and targeted evaluation. Model responses will be assessed using an LLM-as-a-Judge approach to ensure consistency and scalability of evaluation.
a020ae590e9ffba46adcfdfaa263e5d7eb911eab.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the 100 original Bongard problems, utilizing high-resolution images as provided by a recent dataset variant. The evaluation will include a diverse set of VLMs, both proprietary (e.g., OpenAI's o1, GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 2.0/1.5) and open-source (e.g., Qwen2VL, LLaVA-OneVision, InternVL2.5). Each model will be tested three times per task, and results will be averaged. Human performance will be measured via an online study with 20-30 native English-speaking participants, who will solve the same problems under similar conditions. Baseline comparisons will include both human results and model performance across different task formats. Evaluation metrics will include the number of correctly solved Bongard problems, accuracy in concept classification, and the ability to generate or select correct rules. Additional analysis will examine overlaps and discrepancies between tasks to diagnose specific model failure modes.
a020ae590e9ffba46adcfdfaa263e5d7eb911eab.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a multi-faceted, diagnostic evaluation of VLMs on the challenging and underexplored domain of Bongard problems, going beyond standard benchmarks by probing not only open-ended reasoning but also concept recognition, hypothesis generation, and comparison to human cognition. The framework systematically dissects model abilities and failure cases across multiple reasoning tasks, providing granular insights into the perceptual and cognitive bottlenecks of current VLMs. This approach enables identification of specific gaps in visual abstraction and generalization, and highlights the need for more robust, human-like reasoning in future AI systems.

a02313d56a6f71be9aafe43628e0f3a1d0cb858e.title: Diffusion Models already have a Semantic Latent Space
a02313d56a6f71be9aafe43628e0f3a1d0cb858e.research_question: Can a semantic latent space be discovered within frozen, pretrained diffusion models to enable controllable and high-quality semantic image manipulation, similar to the latent spaces in GANs?
a02313d56a6f71be9aafe43628e0f3a1d0cb858e.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a semantic latent space exists within the bottleneck features of pretrained diffusion models, and that manipulating this space enables consistent, linear, robust, and high-quality semantic image editing without the need for model finetuning.
a02313d56a6f71be9aafe43628e0f3a1d0cb858e.proposed_method: A novel asymmetric reverse process (Asyrp) will be developed to discover and manipulate a semantic latent space, termed h-space, within frozen pretrained diffusion models. The approach involves modifying only the bottleneck feature maps (h-space) of the U-Net architecture during the generative process, while preserving the directionality of the original reverse process to avoid destructive interference. An implicit neural function f(h_t, t) will be trained to produce attribute-specific shifts in h-space, guided by a directional CLIP loss and a reconstruction regularizer. The editing process will be divided into three phases: semantic editing in the early timesteps, traditional denoising, and quality boosting via stochastic noise injection in the later timesteps, with the intervals determined by quantifiable measures of editing strength and quality deficiency.
a02313d56a6f71be9aafe43628e0f3a1d0cb858e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple datasets, including CelebA-HQ, AFHQ-dog, LSUN-church, LSUN-bedroom, and METFACES, using various diffusion model architectures such as DDPM++, iDDPM, and ADM. The method will be evaluated against strong baselines, notably DiffusionCLIP, using both in-domain and out-of-domain attributes. Evaluation metrics will include user studies for perceptual quality and attribute change, segmentation consistency, and directional CLIP similarity. The models will remain frozen, and all manipulations will be performed via the discovered h-space, with quantitative and qualitative analyses provided for the properties of the latent space.
a02313d56a6f71be9aafe43628e0f3a1d0cb858e.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first method to discover and utilize a semantic latent space (h-space) in frozen pretrained diffusion models for image editing. The approach enables consistent, linear, and robust semantic manipulations without model finetuning or additional classifiers. The method provides a principled design for the generative process, allowing for versatile editing and quality boosting by quantifiable measures, and demonstrates applicability across diverse architectures and datasets.

a03efb04dfb2490f90c1a953c49a577594852320.title: Towards Accurate Image Coding: Improved Autoregressive Image Generation with Dynamic Vector Quantization
a03efb04dfb2490f90c1a953c49a577594852320.research_question: How can image coding and autoregressive image generation be improved by addressing the limitations of fixed-length vector quantization, specifically to enhance both generation quality and efficiency across diverse image regions with varying information densities?
a03efb04dfb2490f90c1a953c49a577594852320.hypothesis: Introducing variable-length, information-density-based vector quantization and a coarse-to-fine autoregressive generation process will result in more accurate and compact image representations, leading to improved image generation quality and faster generation speed compared to fixed-length coding approaches.
a03efb04dfb2490f90c1a953c49a577594852320.proposed_method: A novel two-stage framework is proposed for image coding and generation. In the first stage, a Dynamic-Quantization VAE (DQ-VAE) encodes image regions into variable-length codes by assessing their local information densities, using a Dynamic Grained Coding (DGC) module with a Gumbel-Softmax-based gating mechanism and a budget loss to control the distribution of granularities across regions. The DQ-VAE constructs hierarchical image representations at multiple candidate granularities, dynamically assigning finer or coarser codes to regions as needed, and regularizes the resulting code map for efficient decoding. In the second stage, a DQ-Transformer autoregressively generates images from coarse-grained (smooth, low-detail) to fine-grained (high-detail) regions, modeling both the position and content of codes alternately through a stacked transformer architecture. This architecture employs shared-content and non-shared-position input layers, as well as granularity and absolute position embeddings, to distinguish and process different granularities effectively. The training process involves negative log-likelihood losses for both position and content prediction, and the framework supports both unconditional and class-conditional generation.
a03efb04dfb2490f90c1a953c49a577594852320.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the FFHQ (256x256 resolution) for unconditional generation and ImageNet (256x256) for class-conditional generation. Evaluation metrics include Frechet Inception Distance (FID) for both generation and reconstruction quality, and Inception Score (IS) for class-conditional tasks. The proposed method is compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as VQGAN, ViT-VQGAN, DCT, RQ-VAE, Mo-VQGAN, and large-scale models like BigGAN and diffusion-based approaches. Ablation studies examine the impact of variable-length coding ratios, input layer designs, and codebook usage. Implementation details specify the use of codebook size K=1024, dual or triple granularities, and transformer stacks of varying depth (base and large variants). Generation speed is benchmarked against ViT-VQGAN using batch sizes on RTX-3090 GPUs, and both qualitative and quantitative results are reported.
a03efb04dfb2490f90c1a953c49a577594852320.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first information-density-based variable-length coding for vector quantized image generation, addressing both insufficiency in important regions and redundancy in unimportant ones. It pioneers a natural coarse-to-fine autoregressive generation order, replacing the unnatural raster-scan of prior models. The DQ-VAE dynamically assigns code lengths based on local information density, while the DQ-Transformer models position and content alternately with specialized input layers for granularity distinction. The approach claims significant improvements in both quality (up to 17.3% FID reduction) and efficiency (faster generation speed) over existing state-of-the-art autoregressive and diffusion models, and demonstrates scalability to large parameter regimes.

a08b7123a7158f1a7fbbc18e8b5aaebd47980ecf.title: EVA-CLIP: Improved Training Techniques for CLIP at Scale
a08b7123a7158f1a7fbbc18e8b5aaebd47980ecf.research_question: How can the efficiency, stability, and effectiveness of large-scale contrastive language-image pre-training (CLIP) models be improved, particularly in terms of reducing computational cost and enhancing zero-shot performance across a wide range of benchmarks?
a08b7123a7158f1a7fbbc18e8b5aaebd47980ecf.hypothesis: Integrating advanced initialization, optimization, and augmentation techniques into the CLIP training pipeline will significantly reduce computational costs, improve training stability, and yield superior zero-shot performance compared to existing CLIP models with similar or fewer parameters and training samples.
a08b7123a7158f1a7fbbc18e8b5aaebd47980ecf.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a new family of CLIP models, termed EVA-CLIP, that leverages several key innovations to enhance training at scale. First, the vision encoder is initialized with pre-trained EVA weights, which combine semantic knowledge from image-text contrastive learning with geometric and structural information from masked image modeling, while the text encoder is initialized from pre-trained CLIP or OpenCLIP models. The LAMB optimizer, designed for large-batch training, is employed to accelerate convergence and improve training efficiency, with adaptive element-wise updates and layer-wise learning rates. A token masking strategy is adopted, randomly masking 50% of image tokens during training to halve time complexity and enable larger batch sizes without additional memory costs. Additional efficiency is achieved using flash attention, gradient checkpointing, and the DeepSpeed ZeRO optimizer to further reduce memory usage and speed up training. Training is conducted using mixed-precision (fp16 or bfloat16) for stability and efficiency.
a08b7123a7158f1a7fbbc18e8b5aaebd47980ecf.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale datasets, including LAION-400M, LAION-2B, COYO-700M, and a merged dataset (Merged-2B) combining 1.6B samples from LAION-2B and 0.4B from COYO-700M. Multiple model scales will be evaluated, from base (149M parameters) to extra-large (5.0B parameters), with batch sizes ranging from 32k to 144k and input resolutions up to 336x336. Baselines will include OpenAI CLIP, OpenCLIP, and other state-of-the-art CLIP variants. Evaluation will be performed on zero-shot image classification (ImageNet-1K, ImageNet variants, ObjectNet, and 27 additional datasets), zero-shot video classification (UCF-101, Kinetics-400/600/700), and zero-shot image/text retrieval (Flickr30K, COCO). Metrics will include top-1 accuracy, mean accuracy across benchmarks, and retrieval recall at various ranks. Ablation studies will assess the impact of initialization, optimizer choice, masking, and training data composition. Training efficiency will be measured in terms of GPU memory usage, training time, and convergence speed.
a08b7123a7158f1a7fbbc18e8b5aaebd47980ecf.novelty_claims: The proposed approach claims several innovations: (1) the first integration of EVA pre-trained vision encoders into the CLIP framework, combining strengths of masked image modeling and contrastive learning; (2) the use of the LAMB optimizer and large-batch training for improved efficiency and stability at scale; (3) the introduction of token masking and flash attention to significantly reduce training time and memory requirements; (4) demonstration of state-of-the-art zero-shot performance on a wide range of benchmarks with fewer training samples and lower computational costs than existing models; and (5) comprehensive ablation and scaling studies validating the effectiveness of each component.

a08f155a46c823c93444bb8dff3d259e61a4f0ef.title: Optimal Rates in Continual Linear Regression via Increasing Regularization
a08f155a46c823c93444bb8dff3d259e61a4f0ef.research_question: What are the optimal convergence rates achievable in continual linear regression under random task orderings, and how can regularization strategies be designed to mitigate forgetting and achieve these rates?
a08f155a46c823c93444bb8dff3d259e61a4f0ef.hypothesis: Carefully designed explicit or implicit regularization schedules in continual linear regression can close the gap between previously known upper and lower bounds on the expected loss, achieving optimal convergence rates under random task orderings.
a08f155a46c823c93444bb8dff3d259e61a4f0ef.proposed_method: The proposed research will develop and analyze two regularization-based schemes for continual linear regression: (1) explicit isotropic ℓ2 regularization, and (2) implicit regularization via limiting the number of gradient steps per task. Both schemes will be reduced analytically to incremental gradient descent (IGD) on time-varying surrogate losses, enabling unified theoretical analysis. The method will investigate both fixed and increasing regularization strength schedules, deriving precise schedules that optimize convergence rates. Theoretical analysis will leverage last-iterate stochastic gradient descent (SGD) techniques for smooth, convex, time-varying objectives, and will extend to both average and seen-task loss metrics. Key technical steps include deriving surrogate loss properties, proving equivalence to IGD, and establishing upper and lower bounds on convergence rates under random task orderings.
a08f155a46c823c93444bb8dff3d259e61a4f0ef.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on collections of linear regression tasks, where each task consists of a data matrix and target vector, with tasks presented in random orderings (with and without replacement). Both synthetic and potentially standard continual learning benchmarks will be used to validate the theoretical findings. Baselines will include unregularized continual learning schemes and previously proposed regularization strategies. Evaluation metrics will focus on the expected average loss and seen-task loss after k iterations, with particular attention to convergence rates as a function of k. The experimental setup will compare fixed versus increasing regularization schedules, and will empirically assess the impact of regularization strength on forgetting and overall performance.
a08f155a46c823c93444bb8dff3d259e61a4f0ef.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified reduction of both explicit and implicit regularization schemes in continual linear regression to incremental gradient descent on surrogate losses, enabling a common analytical framework. It is claimed that, for the first time, an increasing regularization schedule can achieve the optimal O(1/k) convergence rate for the expected loss under random task orderings, closing the gap between previously known upper and lower bounds. The research also provides new last-iterate SGD analysis for time-varying objectives, and establishes that both average and seen-task loss can be optimally controlled by appropriate regularization schedules. These contributions advance the theoretical understanding of regularization in continual learning and provide practical guidance for designing optimal regularization strategies.

a0967d65bc6df56f70d889430ae7c70f5fc3955e.title: Diffusion4D: Fast Spatial-temporal Consistent 4D Generation via Video Diffusion Models
a0967d65bc6df56f70d889430ae7c70f5fc3955e.research_question: How can efficient and spatial-temporally consistent 4D content generation be achieved from diverse input modalities, such as text, images, or static 3D content, overcoming the challenges of data scarcity, slow optimization, and multi-view inconsistency?
a0967d65bc6df56f70d889430ae7c70f5fc3955e.hypothesis: Integrating spatial and temporal consistency into a single 4D-aware video diffusion model, guided by a novel motion magnitude metric and enhanced by classifier-free guidance, will enable fast and high-fidelity 4D asset generation with improved geometry and motion consistency compared to existing multi-model or optimization-heavy approaches.
a0967d65bc6df56f70d889430ae7c70f5fc3955e.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that leverages a meticulously curated large-scale dynamic 3D dataset to train a 4D-aware video diffusion model capable of synthesizing orbital views of dynamic 3D assets. The method will introduce a 3D-to-4D motion magnitude metric, which quantitatively measures dynamic strength and is embedded as a condition in the diffusion network, allowing explicit control over motion during generation. A motion magnitude reconstruction loss will be incorporated during training to directly supervise the learning of 3D-to-4D dynamics. Additionally, a 3D-aware classifier-free guidance mechanism will be used at inference to further refine and augment dynamic behavior. After generating spatial-temporally consistent multi-view videos, explicit 4D construction will be performed using a coarse-to-fine optimization of Gaussian Splatting representations, leveraging both photometric and depth smoothness losses for precise geometry and texture reconstruction.
a0967d65bc6df56f70d889430ae7c70f5fc3955e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a curated dataset of 54,000 high-quality dynamic 3D assets, with 20 cases held out for testing. The proposed method will be evaluated under multiple prompt modalities: text, single image, and static 3D content. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art methods such as 4DFY, Animate124, 4DGen, and STAG4D. Evaluation metrics will include CLIP score (semantic alignment), SSIM, PSNR, LPIPS (appearance/texture quality), FVD (motion consistency), and human preference studies assessing geometry consistency, appearance quality, motion fidelity, and text alignment. The model will be trained for 4,000 iterations with a constant learning rate, and 4D construction will use 5,000 coarse and 2,000 fine optimization steps. DDIM sampling with classifier-free guidance will be used during inference.
a0967d65bc6df56f70d889430ae7c70f5fc3955e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to integrate spatial-temporal consistency for 4D generation into a single video diffusion model, enabling efficient and consistent multi-view synthesis. The introduction of the 3D-to-4D motion magnitude metric and its use as both a conditioning signal and a reconstruction loss provides explicit control and supervision over dynamic strength, which is not addressed in prior work. The 3D-aware classifier-free guidance further enhances dynamic fidelity during inference. The framework's versatility allows conditioning on text, images, or static 3D assets, and the coarse-to-fine 4D construction strategy with Gaussian Splatting leads to rapid, high-fidelity, and geometry-consistent 4D asset generation, surpassing previous methods in both efficiency and quality.

a0a79dad89857a96f8f71b14238e5237cbfc4787.title: Judging LLM-as-a-judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
a0a79dad89857a96f8f71b14238e5237cbfc4787.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be effectively and scalably evaluated for alignment with human preferences in open-ended, multi-turn conversational tasks, and what are the limitations and biases of using LLMs themselves as automated judges for such evaluations?
a0a79dad89857a96f8f71b14238e5237cbfc4787.hypothesis: Strong LLMs, when used as automated judges, can approximate human preferences in evaluating chatbot responses to a degree comparable to human-human agreement, provided that key biases and limitations are identified and mitigated.
a0a79dad89857a96f8f71b14238e5237cbfc4787.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation framework will be developed that leverages state-of-the-art LLMs as automated judges for chatbot assessment. The approach will introduce two new benchmarks: MT-Bench, consisting of 80 high-quality, multi-turn questions across diverse categories, and Chatbot Arena, a crowdsourced platform for head-to-head chatbot comparisons in real-world scenarios. The evaluation protocol will implement several LLM-as-a-judge strategies, including pairwise comparison, single-answer grading, and reference-guided grading, with prompts carefully designed to minimize position, verbosity, and self-enhancement biases. Techniques such as answer order randomization, chain-of-thought prompting, and reference answer provision will be employed to further address identified limitations. The methodology will also explore the impact of prompt engineering and few-shot examples on judgment consistency and accuracy.
a0a79dad89857a96f8f71b14238e5237cbfc4787.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a range of LLM-based chat assistants, including GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Claude-v1, Vicuna-13B, Alpaca-13B, and LLaMA-13B. The MT-Bench dataset will be used for controlled expert evaluation, with 3,000 expert votes collected from graduate-level annotators, while Chatbot Arena will provide 30,000 crowdsourced votes from real users. Baseline comparisons will include human expert and crowd judgments, as well as traditional benchmarks such as MMLU and TruthfulQA. Evaluation metrics will focus on agreement rates between LLM judges and human annotators, win rates across model pairs, and category-wise performance. Additional analyses will assess the effects of prompt variations, answer order, and grading strategies on bias and consistency.
a0a79dad89857a96f8f71b14238e5237cbfc4787.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a systematic and scalable framework for using LLMs as automated judges of chatbot quality, supported by two novel benchmarks specifically designed to capture human preferences in open-ended, multi-turn dialogue. It provides the first large-scale, quantitative analysis of LLM-as-a-judge agreement with human evaluations, identifies and addresses key biases unique to automated judging, and demonstrates that strong LLMs can achieve human-level agreement in preference judgments. The approach enables rapid, interpretable, and cost-effective benchmarking of conversational AI, and the released datasets and evaluation protocols establish a new standard for future research in LLM alignment and evaluation.

a0ab2a87324bd3df4c7dd89d8b372b90e232934b.title: The Rashomon Importance Distribution: Getting RID of Unstable, Single Model-based Variable Importance
a0ab2a87324bd3df4c7dd89d8b372b90e232934b.research_question: How can variable importance be quantified in a way that accounts for both the existence of multiple equally good models (the Rashomon effect) and the instability of variable importance measures across reasonable data perturbations, to provide reliable and reproducible insights in high-stakes domains?
a0ab2a87324bd3df4c7dd89d8b372b90e232934b.hypothesis: A variable importance framework that aggregates importance measures across all good models and across data perturbations will yield more stable, accurate, and generalizable estimates of variable importance than traditional single-model or Rashomon-set-only approaches.
a0ab2a87324bd3df4c7dd89d8b372b90e232934b.proposed_method: A new framework, the Rashomon Importance Distribution (RID), will be developed to quantify variable importance by considering the distribution of importance values across all models in the Rashomon set (i.e., all models with loss within a specified threshold of the empirical loss minimizer) and across multiple bootstrapped datasets. The method is model-agnostic and can be integrated with any global variable importance metric (e.g., permutation importance, SHAP, model reliance). The approach involves repeatedly resampling the data (via bootstrapping), computing the Rashomon set for each resample, and aggregating the variable importance values for each variable across all models and all resamples. This produces a cumulative distribution function (CDF) for each variable's importance, from which statistics such as expected importance, interquartile ranges, and credible intervals can be derived. Theoretical guarantees on estimator consistency and finite-sample error rates will be established.
a0ab2a87324bd3df4c7dd89d8b372b90e232934b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic datasets generated from known data generation processes (e.g., Chen's DGP, Friedman's DGP, Monk 1 and Monk 3) to evaluate the ability of RID to distinguish between relevant and extraneous variables. Baseline methods will include subtractive model reliance for random forests, LASSO, boosted decision trees, generalized optimal sparse decision trees, conditional model reliance, impurity-based random forest importance, LOCO, Pearson and Spearman correlation, partial dependency plots, SHAP values, and variable importance clouds (VIC). Each method will be evaluated using 500 bootstrap samples per dataset, with performance measured by the proportion of correctly identified important/unimportant variables and the coverage of true variable importance values on test sets. Stability will be assessed by generating multiple independent datasets and comparing the overlap of uncertainty intervals (e.g., box-and-whisker ranges) across datasets using Jaccard similarity. A real-world case study will be performed on a single-cell RNAseq/ATACseq dataset of HIV-infected cells, using sparse decision trees and subtractive model reliance, to identify genes associated with HIV load.
a0ab2a87324bd3df4c7dd89d8b372b90e232934b.novelty_claims: The proposed method uniquely combines model uncertainty (Rashomon effect) and data perturbation stability into a unified, model-agnostic framework for variable importance. Unlike prior approaches that either focus on a single model or only account for model class uncertainty, this framework provides stable, reproducible, and theoretically guaranteed estimates of variable importance. The method enables the computation of full distributions (not just ranges) of variable importance, supports a wide range of model classes and importance metrics, and demonstrates superior performance in both synthetic and real-world high-stakes applications. The approach also facilitates the identification of previously unrecognized important variables, as demonstrated in the HIV case study.

a0ba3a62fc6761b1c0528b554d9ff335d26893e8.title: ReVISE: Learning to Refine at Test-Time via Intrinsic Self-Verification
a0ba3a62fc6761b1c0528b554d9ff335d26893e8.research_question: Can large language models (LLMs) be equipped with an internal mechanism to explicitly verify their own reasoning and correct potential errors based on this verification, thereby improving their performance on complex reasoning tasks without reliance on external verifiers or reinforcement learning?
a0ba3a62fc6761b1c0528b554d9ff335d26893e8.hypothesis: Equipping LLMs with intrinsic self-verification and self-correction capabilities, learned via a structured curriculum and preference learning, will enable more effective and efficient reasoning, leading to improved accuracy and robustness on complex reasoning tasks compared to existing fine-tuning and self-improvement methods.
a0ba3a62fc6761b1c0528b554d9ff335d26893e8.proposed_method: A new framework, ReVISE (Refine via Intrinsic Self-Verification), will be developed to enable LLMs to self-verify and refine their reasoning trajectories at test time. The approach introduces a special [refine] token, allowing the model to decide whether to terminate or refine its output based on an internal verification step. Training will proceed in two stages using curriculum learning: first, the model will learn to self-verify by distinguishing between correct and incorrect reasoning paths using preference pairs; second, it will learn to self-correct by constructing new preference pairs where correct reasoning follows incorrect attempts. Preference optimization, rather than reinforcement learning, will be used for stability and efficiency. At inference, a confidence-aware decoding mechanism will be integrated, leveraging the model’s self-verification confidence to weight candidate outputs and improve reliability.
a0ba3a62fc6761b1c0528b554d9ff335d26893e8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple reasoning benchmarks, including GSM8K and MATH-500 for mathematical reasoning, and MBPP for code generation. Both small (1B) and large (8B) Llama-3 models will be used, with models trained from scratch or fine-tuned on supervised datasets, avoiding instruction-tuned models to prevent data contamination. Baselines will include supervised fine-tuning (SFT), rejection fine-tuning (RFT), and iterative self-improvement methods such as STaR+. Evaluation metrics will involve majority voting (Maj@K) and Pass@1, with additional analysis on self-verification accuracy (AUROC) and ablation studies on curriculum learning and preference optimization. The impact of confidence-aware sampling versus traditional majority voting will also be assessed.
a0ba3a62fc6761b1c0528b554d9ff335d26893e8.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces intrinsic self-verification and self-correction for LLMs, eliminating the need for external verifiers or reinforcement learning. It leverages a structured, two-stage curriculum based on preference learning to separately and efficiently train self-verification and self-correction abilities. The method incorporates a novel confidence-aware decoding strategy at inference, directly utilizing the model's self-assessed correctness to improve output selection. This approach is claimed to yield significant and consistent improvements in reasoning accuracy, generalizes across domains (math and code), and demonstrates superior scalability and robustness compared to prior methods.

a0fb3a240efdfa62f34622eaefffd805cac69600.title: Understanding the Role of Equivariance in Self-supervised Learning
a0fb3a240efdfa62f34622eaefffd805cac69600.research_question: What are the fundamental mechanisms by which equivariant self-supervised learning (E-SSL) enables the extraction of useful features for downstream tasks, and how can an information-theoretic framework guide the principled design of E-SSL methods?
a0fb3a240efdfa62f34622eaefffd805cac69600.hypothesis: Equivariant self-supervised learning leverages a synergy effect between augmentation-aware (equivariant) tasks and class-relevant features, such that maximizing the mutual information between augmentations and learned representations encourages the extraction of semantic features beneficial for downstream tasks. This synergy can be theoretically characterized and optimized through information-theoretic principles.
a0fb3a240efdfa62f34622eaefffd805cac69600.proposed_method: A comprehensive information-theoretic framework will be developed to analyze the generalization ability of E-SSL. The approach will model the data generation process using causal diagrams, identifying the 'explaining-away' effect as a key mechanism that creates a synergy between equivariant prediction tasks and class-relevant feature extraction. Theoretical analyses will be conducted to derive principles that maximize this synergy, focusing on the choice of data augmentations, class relevance, and shortcut pruning. The framework will be extended to account for both Shannon and V-information, and will also consider the impact of model equivariance and strict equivariant objectives. Controlled experiments will be designed to empirically validate the theoretical findings and to explore the effects of transformation choices, multivariate equivariance, and model architectures.
a0fb3a240efdfa62f34622eaefffd805cac69600.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification benchmarks such as CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet, using neural network architectures including ResNet-18, ResNet-50, and their equivariant variants (e.g., EqResNet18). E-SSL tasks will include rotation prediction, horizontal/vertical flips, grayscale, jigsaw, blur, and color inversion, with and without additional augmentations (e.g., SimCLR augmentations). Baselines will include random encoders, standard contrastive learning (I-SSL), and advanced E-SSL methods. Evaluation will be performed using linear probing accuracy on downstream classification tasks and equivariant prediction accuracy. Additional experiments will manipulate the pretraining objectives (e.g., joint or adversarial classification loss) and compare the effects of model equivariance and strict equivariant losses (e.g., CARE loss). Metrics will include mutual information estimates, training and test accuracy, and the impact of augmentation choices.
a0fb3a240efdfa62f34622eaefffd805cac69600.novelty_claims: The proposed research establishes a rigorous information-theoretic perspective on E-SSL, identifying the explaining-away effect as a fundamental mechanism for feature learning. It provides theoretical guarantees and practical design principles for maximizing the synergy between equivariant and class-relevant features. The framework unifies and explains the empirical success of various E-SSL and contrastive learning methods, introduces new insights into the role of model equivariance, and demonstrates the benefits of multivariate and fine-grained equivariance. This work offers a principled foundation for future E-SSL method development and bridges the gap between theory and practice in self-supervised learning.

a1159f43a8fcea5e2037ee2ac8065cb4483a0d44.title: Beyond Autoregression: Discrete Diffusion for Complex Reasoning and Planning
a1159f43a8fcea5e2037ee2ac8065cb4483a0d44.research_question: How can alternative sequence modeling paradigms improve complex reasoning and long-term planning in language and combinatorial problem-solving tasks, compared to traditional autoregressive language models?
a1159f43a8fcea5e2037ee2ac8065cb4483a0d44.hypothesis: Discrete diffusion models, particularly when enhanced with multi-granularity training objectives that prioritize subgoals by difficulty, will outperform autoregressive models on tasks requiring complex reasoning, planning, and global coherence, without relying on external search techniques.
a1159f43a8fcea5e2037ee2ac8065cb4483a0d44.proposed_method: A novel discrete diffusion modeling framework will be developed for sequence generation tasks, with a focus on complex reasoning and planning. The approach will introduce Multi-Granularity Diffusion Modeling (MGDM), which incorporates both sequence-level and token-level adaptive reweighting during training to emphasize more difficult subgoals and facilitate efficient learning. The diffusion process will involve a forward noising step and a learned reverse denoising process, parameterized as categorical distributions over discrete tokens. Training will optimize a weighted cross-entropy loss, where the token-level reweighting term is computed adaptively based on the difficulty of each token, and inference will utilize an easy-first TopK decoding strategy to promote global consistency and efficient solution generation. The method will be implemented using a Transformer-based architecture, with detailed algorithmic steps for both training and inference.
a1159f43a8fcea5e2037ee2ac8065cb4483a0d44.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several challenging reasoning and planning benchmarks, including Countdown (a mathematical reasoning task), Sudoku (logic-based number placement), and Boolean Satisfiability Problems (SAT). For Countdown, datasets of up to 500,000 problems with varying input complexity will be generated, with held-out targets for out-of-distribution evaluation. Sudoku experiments will use a dataset of one million solved games, with 100,000 for training and 1,000 for testing. SAT experiments will generate random k-SAT instances near the phase transition threshold for hardness, with variable counts ranging from 5 to 9 and up to 100,000 training instances. Baselines will include autoregressive models (GPT-2 and LLaMA variants), search-augmented AR models, existing discrete and continuous diffusion models, and prompting-based large language models (e.g., GPT-4 with various prompting strategies). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on held-out test sets, token cost (for efficiency), and error analysis by subgoal type. Ablation studies will assess the impact of reweighting strategies and decoding methods, and decoding speed will be measured in samples per second on GPU hardware.
a1159f43a8fcea5e2037ee2ac8065cb4483a0d44.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a multi-granularity diffusion modeling framework that adaptively prioritizes subgoals by difficulty at both the sequence and token levels, a capability not present in existing diffusion or autoregressive models. The approach demonstrates that diffusion-based models can achieve superior performance on complex reasoning and planning tasks without the need for external search or backtracking, outperforming both parameter-scaled autoregressive models and state-of-the-art prompting strategies. The research provides new theoretical and empirical insights into subgoal imbalance in sequence modeling and establishes diffusion models as a promising paradigm for advancing AI capabilities in sophisticated problem-solving domains.

a1675f47125aa409525c5f759b5e6bcc1c8831aa.title: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models with Iterative Retrieval-Generation Synergy
a1675f47125aa409525c5f759b5e6bcc1c8831aa.research_question: How can the synergy between retrieval and generation be enhanced in retrieval-augmented large language models to improve performance on complex reasoning tasks such as multi-hop question answering, fact verification, and commonsense reasoning?
a1675f47125aa409525c5f759b5e6bcc1c8831aa.hypothesis: Iteratively integrating retrieval and generation, where each generation step informs subsequent retrieval, will yield more relevant knowledge and improve the quality and accuracy of language model outputs on complex information tasks compared to existing one-shot or interleaved retrieval-generation methods.
a1675f47125aa409525c5f759b5e6bcc1c8831aa.proposed_method: A novel iterative retrieval-generation framework, termed ITER-RETGEN, will be developed. In this approach, given a task input (e.g., a question), an initial retrieval step is performed to obtain relevant knowledge from a large corpus. The language model then generates an output using both the retrieved knowledge and the original input. This generated output is concatenated with the original input and used as a new query for the next retrieval iteration, aiming to bridge semantic gaps and gather more relevant or missing information. The process is repeated for a fixed number of iterations, with each generation step leveraging all previously retrieved knowledge as a whole, thus preserving generation flexibility and reducing structural constraints. Additionally, a generation-augmented retrieval adaptation step will be explored, where model generations are used to distill knowledge from a re-ranker into a dense retriever, optimizing retrieval for better alignment with the model's information needs.
a1675f47125aa409525c5f759b5e6bcc1c8831aa.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six datasets spanning three reasoning tasks: multi-hop question answering (HotPotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue, Bamboogle), fact verification (Feverous), and commonsense reasoning (StrategyQA). The October 2017, December 2018, and December 2021 Wikipedia dumps will serve as retrieval corpora. Baselines will include Direct Prompting, Chain-of-Thought (CoT) Prompting, ReAct, Self-Ask, and DSP, with all methods evaluated under a 3-shot setting using the same demonstration questions. Evaluation metrics will include exact match (EM), F1, and accuracy, as well as LLM-based correctness evaluation (Acc†) using text-davinci-003. The number of retrieval-generation iterations will be varied, and the impact of generation-augmented retrieval adaptation will be assessed. Implementation will use text-davinci-003 as the LLM and Contriever-MSMARCO as the retriever, retrieving the top-5 paragraphs per query.
a1675f47125aa409525c5f759b5e6bcc1c8831aa.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces an iterative synergy between retrieval and generation, allowing model outputs to inform subsequent retrievals and thus better address complex, multi-hop, and long-form information needs. Unlike prior approaches that interleave retrieval and generation or rely on one-shot retrieval, this framework processes all retrieved knowledge as a whole in each generation, preserving flexibility and reducing overhead. The method is conceptually simple, easy to implement, and empirically shown to outperform or match state-of-the-art retrieval-augmented baselines while requiring fewer retrieval and generation steps. Further, the proposal explores generation-augmented retrieval adaptation, leveraging model outputs to improve retriever performance, which is a novel direction for aligning retrieval with model reasoning.

a170f92a464e11f7a558ddf1ba8f028e5d56de0d.title: Learn Singularly Perturbed Solutions via Homotopy Dynamics
a170f92a464e11f7a558ddf1ba8f028e5d56de0d.research_question: How can neural networks be effectively trained to solve singularly perturbed partial differential equations (PDEs), which are challenging due to parameters that induce near-singularities and complex solution behaviors?
a170f92a464e11f7a558ddf1ba8f028e5d56de0d.hypothesis: Introducing a homotopy dynamics-based training strategy will improve convergence and accuracy of neural network solvers for singularly perturbed PDEs by gradually transitioning from easier to more difficult parameter regimes.
a170f92a464e11f7a558ddf1ba8f028e5d56de0d.proposed_method: A novel training framework based on homotopy dynamics is developed to address the optimization difficulties in neural network-based PDE solvers for singularly perturbed problems. The method begins by training a neural network on a version of the PDE with a large, non-singular parameter (e.g., large diffusion or viscosity), where the solution is smoother and easier to approximate. The parameter is then gradually and adaptively adjusted towards its target (singular) value using a homotopy path, either by numerically integrating a differential equation (e.g., via forward Euler) or by introducing a homotopy loss term into the training objective. The approach includes theoretical analysis of how the parameter affects training difficulty and provides convergence guarantees for the homotopy dynamics under appropriate step size and initialization conditions. The method is designed to be compatible with both solution approximation and operator learning neural network architectures.
a170f92a464e11f7a558ddf1ba8f028e5d56de0d.experiment_details: Experiments are proposed on a range of singularly perturbed PDEs, including the Allen–Cahn equation (1D and 2D), high-dimensional Helmholtz equations, and operator learning for Burgers’ equation. The methodology involves comparing the homotopy dynamics approach with classical PINN training, curriculum regularization, time-sequential, and resampling strategies. Datasets are generated by sampling residual and boundary points in the respective domains, and evaluation metrics include training loss, relative L2 error (L2RE), and specific measures such as shock localization accuracy in Burgers’ equation. The experimental setup includes varying the singular perturbation parameter (e.g., diffusion, viscosity, or wavenumber) and tracking convergence, accuracy, and computational efficiency across methods.
a170f92a464e11f7a558ddf1ba8f028e5d56de0d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first theoretically grounded homotopy dynamics framework for training neural networks on singularly perturbed PDEs, with rigorous analysis of parameter-induced training difficulty and convergence guarantees. The method provides a principled, adaptive strategy for parameter scheduling along the homotopy path, distinct from prior curriculum or resampling approaches. It is demonstrated to be broadly applicable across solution approximation and operator learning settings, and achieves superior accuracy and convergence rates compared to existing baselines on a variety of challenging PDE benchmarks.

a175ace09df66fff1692ee3ed42319ac37667830.title: Enhancing End-to-End Autonomous Driving with Latent World Model
a175ace09df66fff1692ee3ed42319ac37667830.research_question: How can richer and more effective scene feature representations be developed to fully leverage raw sensor data in end-to-end autonomous driving systems, thereby improving trajectory prediction and overall driving performance?
a175ace09df66fff1692ee3ed42319ac37667830.hypothesis: Integrating a self-supervised latent world model that predicts future scene features from current features and ego trajectories will enhance scene representation learning and trajectory prediction, leading to improved performance in both perception-free and perception-based end-to-end autonomous driving frameworks.
a175ace09df66fff1692ee3ed42319ac37667830.proposed_method: A novel self-supervised learning approach will be developed using a Latent World Model (LAW) that predicts future scene latent features based on current latent features and predicted ego trajectories. The method consists of a visual encoder that extracts latent features from multi-view images, a waypoint decoder that predicts future waypoints, and a latent world model that integrates action-aware latents (concatenating visual features and predicted waypoints) to forecast future latent features using transformer blocks. During training, the predicted future latent features will be supervised using the actual latent features extracted from the subsequent frame via a mean squared error loss. The framework will be designed to be compatible with both perception-free (using perspective-view features) and perception-based (using BEV features) autonomous driving paradigms, enabling seamless integration into existing pipelines.
a175ace09df66fff1692ee3ed42319ac37667830.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three major benchmarks: nuScenes (real-world, open-loop), NAVSIM (challenging real-world, open-loop), and CARLA (simulator-based, closed-loop). Both perception-free and perception-based frameworks will be implemented and evaluated. For nuScenes, L2 displacement error and collision rate will be used as evaluation metrics; for NAVSIM, the Predictive Driver Model Score (PDMS) and its subcomponents (no-at-fault collision, drivable area compliance, time-to-collision, comfort, and ego progress) will be used; for CARLA, Route Completion, Infraction Score, and Driving Score will be measured. Baselines will include state-of-the-art methods such as BEV-Planner, VAD, TransFuser, UniAD, TCP, and others. Ablation studies will be performed to analyze the impact of the latent world model, input modalities, time horizons for prediction, and network architectures.
a175ace09df66fff1692ee3ed42319ac37667830.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a self-supervised latent world model that predicts future scene latents conditioned on current features and ego actions, enabling joint optimization of scene representation learning and trajectory prediction. The method is universally compatible with both perception-free and perception-based end-to-end driving frameworks, supporting both perspective-view and BEV feature prediction. Unlike prior world models that rely on generative diffusion or require manual occupancy annotations, this approach directly predicts latent features and requires no manual annotation. The method achieves state-of-the-art results across multiple challenging real-world and simulator-based autonomous driving benchmarks.

a1a18645ee975e8b8fa0e9f922353c0ed6da361b.title: Does compressing activations help model parallel training?
a1a18645ee975e8b8fa0e9f922353c0ed6da361b.research_question: Does compressing activations reduce communication overhead and improve the efficiency of model parallel training for large-scale Transformer models, and what are the trade-offs in terms of throughput and model accuracy across different compression methods, training stages, hyperparameters, and hardware configurations?
a1a18645ee975e8b8fa0e9f922353c0ed6da361b.hypothesis: Compressing activations during model parallel training can reduce communication overhead and improve training throughput without significantly degrading model accuracy, particularly when using learning-based compression methods such as autoencoders, as opposed to sparsification or quantization techniques.
a1a18645ee975e8b8fa0e9f922353c0ed6da361b.proposed_method: A systematic empirical study will be conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of various activation compression algorithms in the context of model parallel training for large Transformer models. The approach will implement and integrate three major classes of compression algorithms—pruning-based (Top-K, Random-K), learning-based (autoencoders), and quantization-based—into a widely-used distributed Transformer training framework (e.g., Megatron-LM). For learning-based methods, an encoder-decoder neural network will be trained to compress and decompress activations before and after communication steps, respectively. The methodology will include modifications to the communication primitives (e.g., replacing all-reduce with all-gather where necessary) and will support both tensor and pipeline model parallelism. The study will also develop an analytical performance model to predict the impact of compression at larger scales and under varying hardware and hyperparameter settings.
a1a18645ee975e8b8fa0e9f922353c0ed6da361b.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed on multiple hardware setups, including AWS p3.8xlarge machines with 4 Tesla V100 GPUs (with and without NVLink), as well as local servers, to measure the impact of network bandwidth. The evaluation will use the BERT-Large model (345M parameters, 24 layers, hidden size 1024, 16 attention heads, fp16 training) and will cover both fine-tuning (on the GLUE benchmark) and pre-training (on Wikipedia and BooksCorpus datasets) tasks. Over 160 experimental settings will be explored, varying batch size, sequence length, number and location of compressed layers, and parallelism degrees (tensor and pipeline). Baselines will include uncompressed training and all compression methods, with evaluation metrics including training throughput (iteration time), communication/computation breakdown, and downstream task accuracy (e.g., GLUE scores, F1, Matthews correlation, Spearman correlation). Detailed ablation studies will examine the effects of hyperparameters and hardware, and the performance model will be validated against empirical results.
a1a18645ee975e8b8fa0e9f922353c0ed6da361b.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first comprehensive empirical study of activation compression methods specifically for model parallel training of large Transformer models. Unlike prior work focused on gradient compression in data parallelism, this research addresses the unique challenges of activation compression in model parallelism, including the lack of low-rank structure in activations and the interaction with system-level optimizations. The integration and evaluation of learning-based compression (autoencoders) for activations in this context is novel, as is the extensive experimental coverage across multiple datasets, hardware configurations, and training regimes. The proposal also contributes an analytical performance model for predicting the impact of compression at scale, providing actionable insights for future algorithm and system design.

a1a5d9298307a32df3bbd32a99dd6a4324771442.title: Max cut and the smallest eigenvalue
a1a5d9298307a32df3bbd32a99dd6a4324771442.research_question: Can new spectral partitioning algorithms be developed to improve the approximation ratio for the Max Cut problem in general graphs, particularly in instances where the optimal cut is close to the maximum possible value?
a1a5d9298307a32df3bbd32a99dd6a4324771442.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that variants of spectral partitioning, leveraging properties of the smallest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix, can achieve improved approximation ratios for Max Cut, especially in graphs where the optimal cut is near-optimal.
a1a5d9298307a32df3bbd32a99dd6a4324771442.proposed_method: A novel spectral partitioning algorithm will be designed that, given a graph with Max Cut optimum at least 1-ε, finds a subset S of vertices and a bipartition (L, R) of S such that a large fraction (at least 1-O(√ε)) of the edges incident on S are cut by the partition. The method involves solving a quadratic form optimization related to the adjacency and degree matrices, followed by a rounding procedure (the 2-Thresholds Spectral Cut algorithm) that assigns vertices to L, R, or leaves them unassigned based on their spectral coordinates. This process is iterated recursively: after partitioning and removing vertices in L and R, the algorithm is applied to the residual graph, and the final cut is assembled from the recursive solutions. For graphs where the optimum is close to 1/2, a more sophisticated variant of the spectral algorithm will be developed to maximize the cut gain, potentially extending to weighted and signed graphs.
a1a5d9298307a32df3bbd32a99dd6a4324771442.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of undirected graphs, including both synthetic and real-world datasets, with non-negative and potentially negative edge weights. The proposed spectral algorithms will be compared against established baselines such as the Goemans-Williamson SDP relaxation, greedy algorithms, and other spectral methods. Evaluation metrics will include the fraction of edges cut (approximation ratio), computational time (with a focus on nearly-linear or low polynomial time), and performance on instances with varying Max Cut optima (e.g., close to 1, close to 1/2). The algorithms will be implemented with randomized components, and results will be averaged over multiple runs to assess robustness.
a1a5d9298307a32df3bbd32a99dd6a4324771442.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new variant of spectral partitioning that achieves an approximation ratio of at least 0.531 for Max Cut in nearly-linear time, without relying on semidefinite programming in the algorithm itself. The method provides a spectral analog of Cheeger’s inequality for the smallest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix and establishes a converse relationship between spectral properties and Max Cut value. Additionally, a more complex spectral algorithm is proposed for the Max CutGain problem, capable of handling signed edge weights and general quadratic programs. The recursive spectral framework and the primal-dual interpretation with respect to the Goemans-Williamson relaxation represent significant innovations over prior combinatorial and spectral approaches.

a1bcf68d6ed2fec1ecaf16b67f2d19bc20c00ee6.title: ASVD: Activation-aware Singular Value Decomposition for Compressing Large Language Models
a1bcf68d6ed2fec1ecaf16b67f2d19bc20c00ee6.research_question: How can large language models be efficiently compressed in a training-free manner to reduce memory and computational requirements, while maintaining model performance across diverse architectures and tasks?
a1bcf68d6ed2fec1ecaf16b67f2d19bc20c00ee6.hypothesis: Incorporating activation-aware transformations and layer-wise sensitivity analysis into low-rank decomposition will enable more effective, training-free compression of large language models, reducing both model and KV cache memory usage without significant loss in performance.
a1bcf68d6ed2fec1ecaf16b67f2d19bc20c00ee6.proposed_method: A novel compression framework, Activation-aware Singular Value Decomposition (ASVD), will be developed for large language models. The method first transforms each weight matrix using a scaling matrix derived from the distribution of input activations, either via channel-wise magnitude statistics or Cholesky decomposition of activation covariances. This transformation absorbs activation outliers into the weight matrix, making subsequent SVD-based low-rank decomposition more robust. After SVD and truncation to a selected rank, the decomposed matrices are reconstructed to approximate the original weights. To address varying sensitivity among layers, a Sensitivity-based Truncation Rank Searching (STRS) procedure will be implemented, using perplexity on a small calibration set to determine the optimal truncation rank for each layer. The approach will also be extended to compress the KV cache by applying ASVD to key and value projection matrices, enabling storage of intermediate activations in a reduced-dimensional space.
a1bcf68d6ed2fec1ecaf16b67f2d19bc20c00ee6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on LLaMA and LLaMA-2 models with parameter sizes ranging from 7B to 13B. A calibration set of 32 samples, each with 2048 tokens from the Wikitext dataset, will be used for layer-wise sensitivity analysis and rank selection. Evaluation metrics will include perplexity on Wikitext-2 and Penn Treebank datasets, as well as zero-shot accuracy on the MMLU benchmark. Baselines will comprise standard SVD (with and without sensitivity-based rank selection), SVD-LLM, and various quantization methods (INT8, INT4, NF4, AWQ). The impact of ASVD on both model parameter compression and KV cache memory reduction will be assessed, including compatibility with quantization and analysis of per-layer and per-block compression ratios.
a1bcf68d6ed2fec1ecaf16b67f2d19bc20c00ee6.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first activation-aware, training-free low-rank decomposition framework for large language models, explicitly addressing activation outliers and layer-specific sensitivity. The approach enables adaptive, layer-wise rank selection based on functional impact rather than structural similarity, and extends low-rank decomposition to compress the KV cache, achieving up to 50% memory reduction without retraining. The method is orthogonal and compatible with existing quantization techniques, offering a versatile and plug-and-play solution for LLM compression.

a1d1983a7b19845141e6505bd32dc395e5a136ba.title: Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets
a1d1983a7b19845141e6505bd32dc395e5a136ba.research_question: How do overparameterized neural networks generalize on small, algorithmically generated datasets, and what are the dynamics and mechanisms of generalization beyond memorization and overfitting in this regime?
a1d1983a7b19845141e6505bd32dc395e5a136ba.hypothesis: Neural networks trained on small algorithmic datasets can exhibit a delayed phase transition from memorization to generalization ('grokking'), and this transition is influenced by factors such as dataset size, optimization duration, and regularization techniques like weight decay.
a1d1983a7b19845141e6505bd32dc395e5a136ba.proposed_method: A systematic investigation will be conducted by training overparameterized neural networks, specifically small transformer architectures, on datasets composed of equations representing various binary operations over finite sets (e.g., modular arithmetic, group operations). Each equation will be tokenized as a sequence of abstract symbols, with no internal structure revealed to the network, ensuring that learning is based solely on observed interactions. The training will use a decoder-only transformer with causal attention, 2 layers, width 128, and 4 attention heads, totaling approximately 400,000 non-embedding parameters. Optimization will primarily use AdamW with carefully tuned hyperparameters, including weight decay and learning rate schedules, and experiments will systematically vary dataset size, optimization steps, and regularization methods (e.g., weight decay, dropout, gradient noise) to probe their effects on generalization dynamics.
a1d1983a7b19845141e6505bd32dc395e5a136ba.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed on datasets generated from a range of binary operations, including modular addition, subtraction, division, polynomial expressions, and group operations (e.g., S_5). For each operation, a fraction of all possible equations will be randomly selected as the training set, with the remainder used for validation. Multiple runs with different random seeds will be conducted for statistical robustness. Baselines will include variations in optimizer (Adam, AdamW, SGD), batch size (full batch vs. minibatch), and regularization (weight decay, dropout, Gaussian noise). Evaluation metrics will include training and validation accuracy, loss curves, and the number of optimization steps required to reach high validation accuracy (e.g., 99%). Additional analyses will include ablation studies on regularization techniques and visualization of learned embeddings (e.g., t-SNE plots) to assess whether the network discovers underlying mathematical structure.
a1d1983a7b19845141e6505bd32dc395e5a136ba.novelty_claims: The proposed research aims to reveal and characterize a striking phenomenon where neural networks, after severe overfitting, can abruptly transition to perfect generalization ('grokking') on small algorithmic datasets, a behavior not commonly observed on natural datasets. The study will provide detailed empirical data on the relationship between dataset size, optimization effort, and generalization, demonstrating that optimization time required for generalization increases rapidly as dataset size decreases. The research will also systematically compare the impact of various regularization and optimization techniques, showing that weight decay in particular can dramatically improve data efficiency. By visualizing learned embeddings, the project will uncover how neural networks can recover interpretable mathematical structure from purely symbolic data. These findings will establish small algorithmic datasets as a fertile testbed for investigating deep learning generalization beyond memorization.

a1f13f34eb545a2fd96828f3060b3fb2dfad2080.title: Flow Matching on General Geometries
a1f13f34eb545a2fd96828f3060b3fb2dfad2080.research_question: How can continuous normalizing flows be efficiently and accurately trained for generative modeling on general Riemannian manifolds, including those with complex geometries, high dimensions, and non-trivial boundaries?
a1f13f34eb545a2fd96828f3060b3fb2dfad2080.hypothesis: A framework that constructs target vector fields using premetrics, including geodesic and spectral distances, enables scalable, simulation-free, and unbiased training of continuous normalizing flows on general manifolds, outperforming existing methods in both accuracy and scalability.
a1f13f34eb545a2fd96828f3060b3fb2dfad2080.proposed_method: A novel framework, Riemannian Flow Matching (RFM), is proposed for training continuous normalizing flows (CNFs) on general Riemannian manifolds. The method constructs conditional probability paths and corresponding vector fields using a premetric function, such as geodesic or spectral distances, to define the flow between a base and target distribution. On simple geometries with closed-form geodesics, the method is completely simulation-free and computes target vector fields in closed form.
