For general manifolds, spectral decompositions (e.g., biharmonic or diffusion distances) are employed to efficiently compute premetrics, requiring only a one-time preprocessing step. The training objective involves regressing a parametric vector field to the analytically defined target vector field using the Riemannian metric, avoiding the need for divergence computation or stochastic simulation.
a1f13f34eb545a2fd96828f3060b3fb2dfad2080.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of datasets, including earth and climate science data on the 2D sphere, protein structure datasets on 2D and 7D tori, and synthetic distributions on complex mesh manifolds such as the Stanford Bunny and Spot the Cow. Additional experiments will address manifolds with boundaries using maze-shaped domains. Baselines for comparison include Riemannian CNFs, Moser Flow, CNF Matching, Riemannian Score-Based models, and Riemannian Diffusion Models. Evaluation metrics will primarily be test negative log-likelihood (NLL), with results averaged over multiple runs to assess stability. The scalability of the method will be assessed by increasing the dimensionality of the torus and comparing performance drops relative to baselines. For mesh-based and boundary experiments, spectral premetrics will be used, and the fidelity of learned distributions and sample trajectories will be visualized and quantitatively evaluated.
a1f13f34eb545a2fd96828f3060b3fb2dfad2080.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to enable simulation-free, closed-form training of continuous normalizing flows on general Riemannian manifolds, including those with non-trivial curvature and boundaries. It introduces the use of premetrics, particularly spectral distances, for efficient and unbiased flow construction on complex geometries. The method eliminates the need for divergence computation and stochastic simulation during training, scales to high dimensions, and achieves state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of manifold-based generative modeling tasks. Additionally, it provides the first tractable approach for training deep generative models on discrete triangular meshes and manifolds with boundaries.

a1f8082505c7e90b0a033e1b9da0a97d67aad66c.title: Accelerating Large Language Model Decoding with Speculative Sampling
a1f8082505c7e90b0a033e1b9da0a97d67aad66c.research_question: How can the decoding speed of large language models be significantly accelerated without compromising sample quality or requiring modifications to the model architecture?
a1f8082505c7e90b0a033e1b9da0a97d67aad66c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging a fast draft model to generate multiple candidate tokens, combined with a modified rejection sampling scheme to ensure output distribution fidelity, can accelerate large language model decoding while preserving output quality.
a1f8082505c7e90b0a033e1b9da0a97d67aad66c.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces speculative sampling, which accelerates transformer-based language model decoding by generating a short draft sequence of K tokens using a smaller, faster draft model. These draft tokens are then scored in parallel by the larger, target model. A modified rejection sampling algorithm is applied: each draft token is accepted with a probability based on the ratio of the target and draft model probabilities, ensuring that the final output distribution matches that of the target model. If a draft token is rejected, a resampling step is performed from a corrected distribution. The approach is designed to be compatible with standard sampling methods (e.g., nucleus, top-k) and does not require changes to the target model's architecture or parameters.
a1f8082505c7e90b0a033e1b9da0a97d67aad66c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using Chinchilla, a 70-billion parameter language model, with a 4-billion parameter draft model trained for low-latency sampling. Evaluation will be performed on the XSum summarization benchmark and the HumanEval code generation benchmark, using both nucleus and greedy sampling at batch size 1. Metrics will include ROUGE-2 for XSum, pass rate for HumanEval, mean token generation time, and overall speedup. Baseline comparisons will be made against standard auto-regressive sampling, and additional analysis will examine the impact of varying the draft length K and the acceptance rate across domains.
a1f8082505c7e90b0a033e1b9da0a97d67aad66c.novelty_claims: The proposal claims a novel, lossless acceleration technique for language model decoding that enables generation of multiple tokens per transformer call without modifying the target model. The modified rejection sampling scheme ensures distributional fidelity within hardware numerics. The method is scalable to distributed setups, complements existing latency reduction techniques, and achieves empirical speedups exceeding theoretical memory bandwidth limits in some cases, all while maintaining output quality.

a1fd0cbdeae7fe6f44698139e240d9498fb74cbb.title: Self-Detoxifying Language Models via Toxification Reversal
a1fd0cbdeae7fe6f44698139e240d9498fb74cbb.research_question: How can pre-trained language models be detoxified to reduce the generation of toxic or harmful content without requiring resource-intensive fine-tuning or additional external components?
a1fd0cbdeae7fe6f44698139e240d9498fb74cbb.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the internal information flow within pre-trained language models can be manipulated during inference to reverse the direction of toxification, thereby enabling effective self-detoxification without fine-tuning or auxiliary classifiers.
a1fd0cbdeae7fe6f44698139e240d9498fb74cbb.proposed_method: A lightweight, prompt-based approach is proposed that enables self-detoxification of pre-trained language models by manipulating the information flow within the attention layers. The method operates in two inference-stage forward passes for each token: first, the model is prompted with both a negative (toxicity-inducing) and a positive (non-toxic) prefix to discover the 'toxification direction' for each attention head by comparing their contextualized value vectors. The difference between these vectors captures the direction in which toxicity permeates through the model. In the second forward pass, the original prompt is used, and the model adaptively reverses the toxification direction by updating the value vectors in the attention heads away from toxicity, using scaling factors based on the L2-norm and cosine similarity of the discovered direction. The updated vectors are normalized to preserve the model's original capabilities, ensuring that the detoxification remains close to the model's typical representations.
a1fd0cbdeae7fe6f44698139e240d9498fb74cbb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the RealToxicityPrompts (RTP) dataset, which contains 100,000 English webtext paragraphs annotated with toxicity scores. The evaluation will use 9,907 prompts, split into non-toxic (toxicity < 0.5) and toxic (toxicity ≥ 0.5) settings, with each prompt generating between 5 and 20 tokens. Baselines will include fine-tuning-based (DAPT, ATCON), decoding-based (GeDi, DEXPERTS), and prompt-based (SD) methods, all using GPT-2 large as the base model. Evaluation metrics will include Expected Maximum Toxicity, Toxicity Probability, and Perplexity, with toxicity measured by a fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3-large classifier and fluency by GPT2-XL perplexity. Human evaluation will also be performed on a subset of samples to assess toxicity, fluency, and coherence, with three annotators per sample.
a1fd0cbdeae7fe6f44698139e240d9498fb74cbb.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel, resource-efficient method for language model detoxification that requires no fine-tuning or auxiliary classifiers, instead leveraging internal attention mechanisms for self-detoxification. It is the first to formulate and reverse the 'toxification direction' within the attention layers, enabling adaptive and representation-level detoxification during inference. The method achieves comparable or superior detoxification performance to state-of-the-art fine-tuning and prompt-based methods, while maintaining generation fluency and coherence, and offers new insights into the internal mechanisms of toxicity in language models.

a206a0c96d6076c6ab081288b0c2c95d3c7efd64.title: Inspecting and Editing Knowledge Representations in Language Models
a206a0c96d6076c6ab081288b0c2c95d3c7efd64.research_question: How can the internal knowledge representations of large language models be inspected and edited to enable more precise control over generated factual content and to detect or correct factual errors, both from training data and in-context information?
a206a0c96d6076c6ab081288b0c2c95d3c7efd64.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that targeted interventions in the internal representation space of language models can effectively encode, modify, and inspect factual knowledge, thereby enabling controlled generation and error detection without the need for parameter updates or prompt engineering.
a206a0c96d6076c6ab081288b0c2c95d3c7efd64.proposed_method: A novel method, REMEDI (REpresentation MEDIation), will be developed to learn affine transformations in the hidden representation space of transformer-based language models. This method will identify directions corresponding to factual attributes and will apply these transformations to entity representations at a specific layer and token position within the model. The approach will optimize an objective that encourages the model to generate text consistent with a target fact, suppresses prior contradictory associations, and minimizes unintended changes to intermediate token distributions. REMEDI will be trained using tuples of (context, entity, attribute, target generation), leveraging both in-context and out-of-context scenarios. The learned edit vectors can be applied at inference time to modify or inspect the knowledge encoded about specific entities, enabling both editing and probing functionalities.
a206a0c96d6076c6ab081288b0c2c95d3c7efd64.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the GPT-J language model (6B parameters, trained on The Pile) as the primary testbed. The Bias in Bios dataset will be used for occupation classification tasks, where the model's ability to correctly integrate biographical context into entity representations will be evaluated. The COUNTERFACT benchmark will be employed to assess the method's ability to overwrite and update background knowledge with new or contradictory facts, comparing against baselines such as prompt prefixing, entity replacement, fine-tuning, and the ROME model-editing method. Evaluation metrics will include factual accuracy, fluency (measured by n-gram entropy), efficacy (likelihood of generating the target fact), neighborhood effects (impact on related entities), consistency with reference texts, and preservation of entity essence. Additional experiments will probe the method's ability to detect when the model is likely to generate incoherent or incorrect outputs, using F1 and Matthews correlation coefficient as metrics.
a206a0c96d6076c6ab081288b0c2c95d3c7efd64.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a general and efficient framework for editing and probing factual knowledge in language models by intervening directly in the representation space, rather than through parameter updates or prompt engineering. This approach enables both the insertion of new facts and the detection of knowledge gaps or errors, with fine-grained control over when and where edits are applied. Unlike previous model-editing methods, REMEDI operates at the level of runtime representations, allowing for context-sensitive and non-destructive modifications that do not bleed into unrelated entities. The method also demonstrates generalization across both background and in-context knowledge, offering a unified tool for inspection and control of language model behavior.

a22b23b65cdbc0335b872ed7c7a7206c710f8997.title: Qwen2-VL: Enhancing Vision-Language Model's Perception of the World at Any Resolution
a22b23b65cdbc0335b872ed7c7a7206c710f8997.research_question: How can large vision-language models be enhanced to achieve robust and efficient perception across images and videos of arbitrary resolutions and aspect ratios, while supporting advanced multimodal understanding and agent capabilities?
a22b23b65cdbc0335b872ed7c7a7206c710f8997.hypothesis: Incorporating dynamic resolution processing and advanced multimodal positional embeddings into large vision-language models will significantly improve their ability to perceive, understand, and reason over diverse visual inputs, including high-resolution images and long-duration videos, thereby achieving superior performance across a wide range of multimodal benchmarks and tasks.
a22b23b65cdbc0335b872ed7c7a7206c710f8997.proposed_method: A new series of large vision-language models will be developed, featuring a Vision Transformer (ViT) with approximately 675M parameters and scalable language model backbones (2B, 7B, and 72B parameters). The core innovations include a Naive Dynamic Resolution mechanism, which enables the model to process images of arbitrary resolutions by dynamically converting them into a variable number of visual tokens, and a Multimodal Rotary Position Embedding (M-RoPE) that decomposes positional encoding into temporal, height, and width components for effective modeling of text, images, and videos. The architecture will unify image and video understanding through mixed training, treating videos as sequences of frames and leveraging 3D convolutions for efficient video feature extraction. The training procedure will follow a three-stage process: initial ViT pretraining on image-text pairs, joint multimodal pretraining with unfreezing all parameters, and instruction fine-tuning using diverse multimodal conversational and agent datasets.
a22b23b65cdbc0335b872ed7c7a7206c710f8997.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a comprehensive suite of multimodal benchmarks, including DocVQA, InfoVQA, RealWorldQA, MTVQA, MathVista, MMBench, MME, MMStar, and HallusionBench for general visual question answering, as well as MVBench, PerceptionTest, EgoSchema, and Video-MME for video understanding. Agent capabilities will be evaluated on UI operations, robotic control, navigation, and games using benchmarks such as AITZ, ALFRED, R2R, and REVERIE. The models will be compared against leading baselines, including GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Gemini 1.5 Pro, using metrics such as accuracy, success rate, goal-condition success, type match, and exact match. Multilingual OCR performance will be assessed on internal benchmarks across several languages. Training will utilize approximately 1.4 trillion tokens from diverse sources, and ablation studies will be performed to evaluate the impact of key architectural components.
a22b23b65cdbc0335b872ed7c7a7206c710f8997.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a dynamic resolution mechanism for arbitrary image sizes, enabling efficient and accurate visual tokenization that preserves fine-grained details. The Multimodal Rotary Position Embedding (M-RoPE) is a novel positional encoding scheme that explicitly models temporal and spatial information for unified text, image, and video understanding. The unified training paradigm for images and videos, combined with large-scale scaling and diverse multimodal instruction fine-tuning, is expected to set new standards in vision-language model performance, agent capabilities, and multilingual support. The method claims to outperform existing generalist models on a wide range of multimodal benchmarks, particularly excelling in document understanding, video comprehension, and real-world agent tasks.

a23c5c698c936a89ad5fac4e6f70f756c0fc56a0.title: CoTracker3: Simpler and Better Point Tracking by Pseudo-Labelling Real Videos
a23c5c698c936a89ad5fac4e6f70f756c0fc56a0.research_question: How can point tracking models for videos be improved in terms of data efficiency, architectural simplicity, and robustness to occlusions by leveraging unlabelled real videos through pseudo-labelling, while maintaining or surpassing state-of-the-art performance?
a23c5c698c936a89ad5fac4e6f70f756c0fc56a0.hypothesis: A point tracking model trained with a simplified architecture and a semi-supervised protocol that pseudo-labels real videos using multiple existing trackers as teachers will achieve superior tracking accuracy and data efficiency, particularly in handling occlusions, compared to current state-of-the-art methods that rely on large-scale synthetic or unlabelled real data and more complex training pipelines.
a23c5c698c936a89ad5fac4e6f70f756c0fc56a0.proposed_method: A new point tracking model, CoTracker3, will be developed with a streamlined transformer-based architecture that eliminates or simplifies components found in previous models, such as global matching modules. The model will process dense convolutional feature maps at multiple scales, compute 4D correlation features between query and candidate points, and iteratively update point tracks, confidence, and visibility using a transformer with cross-track and temporal attention. The training protocol will involve pre-training on synthetic data (e.g., Kubric), followed by fine-tuning on a large collection of unlabelled real videos. Pseudo-labels for these real videos will be generated by ensembling predictions from multiple off-the-shelf teacher trackers, each trained only on synthetic data. Query points for tracking will be sampled using feature detectors such as SIFT to ensure trackability and stability during training. During fine-tuning, supervision will focus on track positions, with confidence and visibility heads frozen to avoid forgetting.
a23c5c698c936a89ad5fac4e6f70f756c0fc56a0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard point tracking benchmarks, including TAP-Vid (with Kinetics, DAVIS, and RGB-Stacking subsets), Dynamic Replica, and RoboTAP. The model will be evaluated using metrics such as Average Jaccard (AJ), Occlusion Accuracy (OA), and the fraction of visible and occluded points tracked within various pixel thresholds (δvis, δocc). Baselines will include state-of-the-art trackers such as TAPIR, CoTracker, LocoTrack, TAPTR, PIPs++, and BootsTAPIR. The proposed model will be compared in both online (sliding window) and offline (full sequence) modes, with ablations on architectural choices (e.g., cross-track attention), teacher ensemble composition, and point sampling strategies. Data scaling experiments will investigate the impact of increasing the number of pseudo-labelled real videos, ranging from hundreds to 100,000 videos, and compare data efficiency against methods using up to 15 million real videos.
a23c5c698c936a89ad5fac4e6f70f756c0fc56a0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a significantly simpler and more efficient point tracking architecture that removes or streamlines previously assumed necessary components, such as global matching. The semi-supervised training protocol leverages pseudo-labelling from an ensemble of teacher trackers, enabling effective use of unlabelled real videos with 1,000 times less data than prior state-of-the-art methods. The model demonstrates superior robustness to occlusions and achieves faster inference speeds, with up to 27% speed improvement over the fastest existing trackers. The research also provides the first systematic study of data scaling behavior in point tracking, showing that high performance can be achieved with dramatically reduced data and training complexity.

a24c3e689c351cd5baf420609b11a7ebc1cbc0a3.title: Approximating gradients for differentiable quality diversity in reinforcement learning
a24c3e689c351cd5baf420609b11a7ebc1cbc0a3.research_question: How can quality diversity (QD) optimization be effectively extended to reinforcement learning (RL) domains where exact gradients are unavailable, in order to efficiently generate diverse and high-performing agent policies?
a24c3e689c351cd5baf420609b11a7ebc1cbc0a3.hypothesis: Approximating gradients for both the objective and behavioral measures using methods from reinforcement learning, such as evolution strategies (ES) and actor-critic algorithms (e.g., TD3), will enable differentiable quality diversity (DQD) algorithms to achieve performance comparable to or better than existing QD-RL methods in challenging RL environments.
a24c3e689c351cd5baf420609b11a7ebc1cbc0a3.proposed_method: A framework will be developed to approximate gradients for both the performance objective and behavioral measure functions in QD-RL settings, where the environment is typically non-differentiable. Two variants of the state-of-the-art DQD algorithm, CMA-MEGA, will be constructed: one variant will estimate both objective and measure gradients using evolution strategies (ES), while the other will estimate the objective gradient using the TD3 actor-critic method and the measure gradients using ES. The approach involves sampling gradient coefficients from a multivariate Gaussian, generating new solutions by combining objective and measure gradients, and updating the archive and the coefficient distribution based on archive improvement. The method will decouple the estimation of gradients from the QD optimization process, allowing for independent improvements in either component.
a24c3e689c351cd5baf420609b11a7ebc1cbc0a3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four simulated locomotion tasks from the QDGym benchmark suite, including QDAnt, QDHalf-Cheetah, QDHopper, and QDWalker. Each agent's policy will be parameterized by a neural network, and the archive will be discretized into a grid based on behavioral measures (e.g., proportion of time each foot is on the ground). The proposed CMA-MEGA variants will be compared against strong baselines: PGA-MAP-Elites, ME-ES, and MAP-Elites. Evaluation metrics will include QD score (sum of objective values of all elites in the archive), archive coverage (proportion of filled cells), and best performance (highest objective in the archive). Each algorithm will be run for a fixed number of solution evaluations (e.g., 1 million), and statistical analysis will be performed over multiple random seeds to assess significance.
a24c3e689c351cd5baf420609b11a7ebc1cbc0a3.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to systematically adapt gradient approximation techniques from RL (ES and actor-critic methods) to differentiable quality diversity algorithms in non-differentiable RL environments. By formalizing QD for RL and reducing it to a DQD instance, the method enables the use of gradient-based QD optimization in domains where gradients must be approximated. The decoupling of gradient estimation from QD optimization opens new avenues for leveraging future advances in either RL or QD. The approach provides insight into the limitations and strengths of current DQD algorithms when applied to RL, and demonstrates that with appropriate gradient approximations, state-of-the-art QD-RL performance can be achieved.

a26a7a74f1e5fd562be95c3611a0680759fbdf84.title: CoCa: Contrastive Captioners are Image-Text Foundation Models
a26a7a74f1e5fd562be95c3611a0680759fbdf84.research_question: How can a unified image-text foundation model be designed to efficiently subsume and combine the capabilities of single-encoder, dual-encoder, and encoder-decoder paradigms for a wide range of vision, crossmodal, and multimodal tasks?
a26a7a74f1e5fd562be95c3611a0680759fbdf84.hypothesis: A single, end-to-end pretrained image-text encoder-decoder model, jointly optimized with both contrastive and generative (captioning) objectives, can match or surpass the performance of specialized or multi-stage models across visual recognition, crossmodal retrieval, and multimodal understanding tasks, while maintaining efficiency and flexibility.
a26a7a74f1e5fd562be95c3611a0680759fbdf84.proposed_method: A novel encoder-decoder architecture will be developed in which the image encoder (e.g., Vision Transformer) processes the visual input, and the text decoder is split into unimodal and multimodal components. The first half of the decoder layers will omit cross-attention, producing unimodal text representations suitable for contrastive learning, while the remaining decoder layers will incorporate cross-attention to the image encoder, yielding fused multimodal representations for captioning and understanding. The model will be trained end-to-end from scratch on both web-scale noisy image-text pairs and annotated image datasets, treating all labels as text. Two loss functions will be jointly optimized: a contrastive loss between the unimodal image and text embeddings, and a captioning loss on the multimodal decoder outputs, with both objectives computed efficiently in a shared computational graph. Task-specific attentional pooling modules will be used to customize representations for different downstream tasks.
a26a7a74f1e5fd562be95c3611a0680759fbdf84.experiment_details: Experiments will involve pretraining the model on large-scale datasets, including JFT-3B (annotated images with label names as text) and ALIGN (web-scale noisy image-text pairs), with strict de-duplication to avoid overlap with downstream tasks. The model will be evaluated on a broad suite of benchmarks: visual recognition (ImageNet, Kinetics-400/600/700, Moments-in-Time), crossmodal retrieval (MSCOCO, Flickr30K, MSR-VTT), multimodal understanding (VQA v2, SNLI-VE, NLVR2), and image captioning (MSCOCO, NoCaps). Baselines will include state-of-the-art single-encoder, dual-encoder, and encoder-decoder models such as CLIP, ALIGN, Florence, and SimVLM. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy for classification, recall@K for retrieval, CIDEr for captioning, and standard metrics for VQA and reasoning tasks. Both zero-shot, frozen-feature, and finetuning protocols will be used to assess transferability and adaptability.
a26a7a74f1e5fd562be95c3611a0680759fbdf84.novelty_claims: The proposed approach unifies three major pretraining paradigms (single-encoder, dual-encoder, encoder-decoder) into a single, minimalist architecture trained end-to-end from scratch. The decoupled decoder design enables simultaneous learning of unimodal and multimodal representations, supporting both contrastive and generative objectives in a single forward pass. Task-specific attentional pooling modules further enhance adaptability to diverse downstream tasks. This unified framework eliminates the need for multi-stage pretraining or separate models, achieves state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of benchmarks, and demonstrates parameter efficiency and training simplicity compared to existing methods.

a28a8c834f8b11563a8a00af4472c9c45a89c975.title: Characterizing and overcoming the greedy nature of learning in multi-modal deep neural networks
a28a8c834f8b11563a8a00af4472c9c45a89c975.research_question: How can the tendency of multi-modal deep neural networks to rely excessively on a single modality, thereby underutilizing other available modalities, be characterized and mitigated to improve generalization across diverse multi-modal classification tasks?
a28a8c834f8b11563a8a00af4472c9c45a89c975.hypothesis: The greedy learner hypothesis posits that multi-modal deep neural networks inherently learn to rely on the modality from which they can learn most rapidly, leading to an imbalance in modality utilization and suboptimal generalization. By actively balancing the learning speeds across modalities during training, it is possible to encourage more equitable modality utilization and enhance model generalization.
a28a8c834f8b11563a8a00af4472c9c45a89c975.proposed_method: A novel training algorithm, referred to as balanced multi-modal learning, is introduced to address the greedy nature of multi-modal deep neural networks. The approach begins by quantifying the model's reliance on each modality using a metric called conditional utilization rate, which measures the gain in accuracy when a modality is available in addition to another. Since this metric is not efficiently computable during training, a proxy called conditional learning speed is developed, based on the normalized gradient norms of modality-specific parameters, to monitor the relative speed at which the model learns from each modality in real time. The training algorithm alternates between regular training steps and re-balancing steps: when an imbalance in conditional learning speeds is detected (exceeding a predefined tolerance), targeted updates are applied to accelerate learning from the underutilized modality, using modified fusion operations within the network. This dynamic adjustment continues throughout training, ensuring that all modalities are effectively leveraged.
a28a8c834f8b11563a8a00af4472c9c45a89c975.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three multi-modal datasets: Colored-and-gray-MNIST (synthetic dataset with correlated and uncorrelated modalities), ModelNet40 (3D object classification using front and rear 2D views), and NVGesture (video-based hand gesture recognition using RGB and depth modalities). The proposed method will be compared against standard multi-modal training (vanilla), a random re-balancing baseline, and the RUBi debiasing method. Evaluation metrics include test accuracy, conditional utilization rate, and conditional learning speed, with additional analysis of the impact of regularization on modality utilization. Each experiment will involve multiple random initializations and learning rates to assess robustness, and results will be reported as means and standard deviations of test accuracies. Ablation studies will be performed to examine the sensitivity of the method to hyperparameters such as the imbalance tolerance and re-balancing window size.
a28a8c834f8b11563a8a00af4472c9c45a89c975.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the greedy learner hypothesis for multi-modal deep neural networks and provides a rigorous empirical framework for diagnosing and quantifying modality utilization imbalance. The conditional learning speed metric is proposed as a novel, computationally efficient proxy for real-time monitoring of modality reliance during training. The balanced multi-modal learning algorithm represents an innovative approach to dynamically calibrating learning from each modality, leading to improved generalization and more robust multi-modal representations. This methodology is validated across multiple datasets and architectures, and is shown to outperform existing baselines and debiasing strategies.

a297a084bfe7171bfd353c6af5d13c75718a3364.title: Modality Competition: What Makes Joint Training of Multi-modal Network Fail in Deep Learning? (Provably)
a297a084bfe7171bfd353c6af5d13c75718a3364.research_question: What are the underlying mechanisms that cause joint training of multi-modal neural networks to underperform compared to the best uni-modal networks, and how do neural network encoders learn feature representations from each modality during multi-modal joint training?
a297a084bfe7171bfd353c6af5d13c75718a3364.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, under standard joint training frameworks for late-fusion multi-modal neural networks, different modalities will compete during training, resulting in only a subset of modalities being effectively learned. This competition leads to sub-optimal feature representation and a performance gap between multi-modal and uni-modal networks.
a297a084bfe7171bfd353c6af5d13c75718a3364.proposed_method: A theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted using a multi-label classification task with a data distribution modeled by sparse coding, reflecting realistic properties of multi-modal data, including the presence of 'insufficient data' in each modality. The proposed method will focus on a late-fusion network architecture where each modality is encoded by a single-layer neural network with smoothed ReLU activation, and the encoded features are fused via summation before classification by a linear layer. Both multi-modal and uni-modal networks will be trained using gradient descent on cross-entropy loss, with careful initialization and learning rate selection. Theoretical analysis will be performed to characterize the optimization and generalization behaviors of both network types, with a focus on the phenomenon of 'modality competition', where only a subset of modalities are learned effectively during joint training.
a297a084bfe7171bfd353c6af5d13c75718a3364.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multi-modal item classification tasks using datasets containing image (RGB) and text modalities. The setups will include training image-only, text-only, and joint image+text models. Performance will be evaluated using accuracy and error curves on both training and validation sets, with detailed analysis of class-wise performance to identify cases of insufficient modality information. Baseline comparisons will include uni-modal networks trained independently, as well as networks where encoders are fixed after joint training. Additional analysis will assess the quality of learned feature representations by evaluating uni-modal performance using encoders obtained from joint training. Empirical results will be used to validate the theoretical predictions regarding modality competition and performance degradation.
a297a084bfe7171bfd353c6af5d13c75718a3364.novelty_claims: The proposal offers the first theoretical framework that explains the degenerating aspect of multi-modal joint training in neural networks, specifically identifying and analyzing the phenomenon of modality competition. It provides provable guarantees and empirical evidence for why naive joint training can lead to sub-optimal feature learning and performance gaps, even when additional modalities are available. The approach bridges the gap between theoretical understanding and practical observations of multi-modal network behavior, advancing the field's comprehension of multi-modal deep learning failures.

a2c45b8fec0fc2fb21cd883b23338caf8a55a213.title: StreamBridge: Turning Your Offline Video Large Language Model into a Proactive Streaming Assistant
a2c45b8fec0fc2fb21cd883b23338caf8a55a213.research_question: How can pre-trained offline Video Large Language Models (Video-LLMs) be adapted to function effectively in real-time streaming scenarios, supporting both multi-turn real-time understanding and proactive response generation, without requiring full retraining or sacrificing general video understanding capabilities?
a2c45b8fec0fc2fb21cd883b23338caf8a55a213.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that introducing a modular framework incorporating a memory buffer with a round-decayed compression strategy, along with a decoupled lightweight activation model, will enable offline Video-LLMs to operate efficiently and proactively in streaming environments, while retaining or improving their performance on standard video understanding tasks.
a2c45b8fec0fc2fb21cd883b23338caf8a55a213.proposed_method: The proposed method, StreamBridge, adapts pre-trained offline Video-LLMs for streaming use by integrating three core components: (1) a memory buffer that accumulates visual and textual embeddings from sequentially arriving video frames and user queries, preserving the temporal context across multi-turn interactions; (2) a round-decayed compression strategy that merges older frame tokens via average pooling while retaining recent context, ensuring the input embedding length stays within a predefined maximum (MaxLen), thus balancing memory efficiency and real-time responsiveness; and (3) a decoupled, plug-and-play activation model—a compact external MLLM trained for binary classification—that monitors incoming frames and signals when the main Video-LLM should generate a response, enabling proactive outputs. The activation model is trained with a score head and a learnable activation token, using temporally annotated video datasets and dynamic positive/negative labeling to simulate diverse response timing patterns. The entire system is designed to operate in parallel threads for efficient inference and can be fine-tuned on streaming-specific datasets to further enhance performance.
a2c45b8fec0fc2fb21cd883b23338caf8a55a213.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by adapting several leading offline Video-LLMs (e.g., LLaVA-OV-7B, Qwen2-VL-7B, Oryx-1.5-7B) using the StreamBridge framework. Evaluation will be performed on real-time streaming benchmarks such as OVO-Bench and Streaming-Bench for multi-turn understanding, as well as on general video understanding datasets including MVBench, PerceptionTest, TempCompass, EgoSchema, LongVideoBench, MLVU, and VideoMME. The proactive capability will be assessed on ET-Bench subtasks. The models will be fine-tuned using the newly constructed Stream-IT dataset, which features interleaved video-text sequences and multi-turn QA, supplemented with samples from LLaVA-178K, VCG-Plus, and ShareGPT4Video. Baselines will include both proprietary models (e.g., GPT-4o, Gemini1.5Pro) and open-source streaming/offline Video-LLMs. Evaluation metrics will include average scores on benchmarks, F1 and similarity scores for proactive tasks, and latency/memory usage for efficiency analysis. Ablation studies will be conducted on compression strategies, memory budget (MaxLen), and the impact of the Stream-IT dataset.
a2c45b8fec0fc2fb21cd883b23338caf8a55a213.novelty_claims: The proposed framework offers a general, plug-and-play solution for converting any pre-trained offline Video-LLM into a streaming-capable assistant without full retraining. Key innovations include the round-decayed compression strategy for efficient long-context management, a modular activation model that enables proactive response generation without interfering with the main model's language and video understanding abilities, and the construction of the Stream-IT dataset tailored for streaming, multi-turn, and proactive video understanding. The method claims to outperform both open-source and proprietary baselines on streaming benchmarks, while maintaining or improving performance on standard offline video understanding tasks.

a2ca7379ee13d1ce71d0e5b69cc4a3790f5e7c25.title: Multi-Reward as Condition for Instruction-based Image Editing
a2ca7379ee13d1ce71d0e5b69cc4a3790f5e7c25.research_question: How can the quality and effectiveness of instruction-based image editing models be improved by addressing the limitations of noisy and imperfect training data, particularly in terms of instruction following, detail preservation, and generation quality?
a2ca7379ee13d1ce71d0e5b69cc4a3790f5e7c25.hypothesis: Incorporating multi-perspective reward information as auxiliary input conditions during training will enable instruction-based image editing models to better learn from imperfect triplets, resulting in improved instruction following, detail preservation, and overall generation quality.
a2ca7379ee13d1ce71d0e5b69cc4a3790f5e7c25.proposed_method: A novel training framework is proposed that integrates multi-perspective reward information into instruction-based image editing models. First, a quantitative metric system based on a large vision-language model (e.g., GPT-4o) is designed to evaluate training data triplets from three perspectives: instruction following, detail preservation, and generation quality. For each triplet, both numerical scores (0-5) and textual feedback are collected, forming a high-quality reward dataset (RewardEdit-20K). During model training, the reward scores and text descriptions are encoded as embeddings and concatenated to form a reward condition, which is then integrated into both the latent noise and the U-Net of the diffusion-based editing models via attention mechanisms and additive conditioning. The reward condition is injected after each block of the U-Net to enhance the guidance provided by the reward information. During inference, the reward conditions are set to the highest possible scores with no failure-point text, aiming for optimal generation outcomes.
a2ca7379ee13d1ce71d0e5b69cc4a3790f5e7c25.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted by fine-tuning state-of-the-art instruction-based image editing models, such as InsPix2Pix and SmartEdit, using the proposed multi-reward conditioning framework and the RewardEdit-20K dataset. Evaluation is performed on a newly constructed Real-Edit benchmark, which comprises 80 high-quality real-world images from Unsplash and 560 diverse editing instructions spanning seven categories. Model outputs are assessed using both automated GPT-4o-based evaluation (scoring instruction following, detail preservation, and generation quality from 0-5) and human annotator ratings. Comparisons are made against multiple baselines including KOSMOS-G, MagicBrush, MGIE, InstructDiffusion, HIVE, HQ-Edit, and the original InsPix2Pix and SmartEdit models. Additional experiments include ablation studies on the contribution of reward scores versus text, methods of integrating reward information, and the effect of reward score values during inference.
a2ca7379ee13d1ce71d0e5b69cc4a3790f5e7c25.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a multi-perspective reward dataset (RewardEdit-20K) for instruction-based image editing, addressing the limitations of existing datasets by providing fine-grained, aspect-specific feedback. A new framework is developed to effectively encode and integrate multi-perspective reward information as auxiliary conditions in diffusion-based editing models, enabling improved learning from noisy supervision. A challenging real-world evaluation benchmark (Real-Edit) and a GPT-4o-based multi-aspect evaluation protocol are established. The approach enables significant improvements over state-of-the-art baselines in both automated and human evaluations, and demonstrates the controllability of editing outcomes via reward conditioning.

a2d2bbe4c542173662a444b33b76c66992697830.title: InstructPix2Pix: Learning to Follow Image Editing Instructions
a2d2bbe4c542173662a444b33b76c66992697830.research_question: How can a generative model be trained to perform diverse and intuitive image edits based on natural language instructions, without requiring paired real-world data or per-example fine-tuning?
a2d2bbe4c542173662a444b33b76c66992697830.hypothesis: A conditional diffusion model, trained on a large-scale synthetic dataset generated by combining a language model and a text-to-image model, can generalize to perform high-quality, instruction-based image editing on real images and arbitrary user-written instructions.
a2d2bbe4c542173662a444b33b76c66992697830.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that treats instruction-based image editing as a supervised learning problem. First, a large language model (such as GPT-3) will be fine-tuned on a small, human-annotated dataset of image captions, edit instructions, and output captions, enabling it to generate creative and coherent editing instructions and paired captions. Next, a text-to-image diffusion model (such as Stable Diffusion), in combination with Prompt-to-Prompt techniques, will be used to generate paired images corresponding to the before and after captions, with CLIP-based filtering ensuring semantic consistency between image pairs. This process will yield a large-scale synthetic dataset of image editing triplets. Finally, a conditional latent diffusion model will be trained on this dataset, taking as input an image and an edit instruction, and generating the edited image in a single forward pass. The model will incorporate classifier-free guidance with respect to both the input image and the instruction, allowing for adjustable trade-offs between edit strength and image fidelity.
a2d2bbe4c542173662a444b33b76c66992697830.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of real photographs and artwork, using human-written instructions to evaluate the model's generalization to real-world edits. The synthetic training dataset will be constructed from LAION-Aesthetics captions, with over 450,000 generated triplets. Baseline comparisons will include SDEdit (a diffusion-based editing method) and Text2Live (a CLIP-guided layer-based editing method), with both qualitative and quantitative evaluations. Evaluation metrics will include CLIP image similarity (measuring consistency with the input image) and CLIP text-image directional similarity (measuring alignment with the intended edit). Ablation studies will assess the impact of dataset size and filtering, as well as the effects of classifier-free guidance parameters. The model's ability to handle various edit types, such as object replacement, style transfer, and contextual changes, will be systematically tested.
a2d2bbe4c542173662a444b33b76c66992697830.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a method for instruction-based image editing that does not require paired real-world data, per-example inversion, or fine-tuning at inference time. The method leverages the complementary strengths of large pretrained language and text-to-image models to synthesize a large, diverse, and semantically consistent training dataset. The resulting diffusion model is capable of zero-shot generalization to real images and arbitrary human-written instructions, enabling intuitive and flexible image editing from natural language. The framework also incorporates a dual-conditioning classifier-free guidance mechanism, allowing for fine-grained control over the balance between edit strength and image fidelity.

a2d46b12e89239067e03bc8243a3ef8e2ece594d.title: Statistical Tractability of Off-policy Evaluation of History-dependent Policies in POMDPs
a2d46b12e89239067e03bc8243a3ef8e2ece594d.research_question: When is it possible to achieve statistically efficient (polynomial sample complexity) off-policy evaluation (OPE) of history-dependent policies in partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) with large observation spaces, and what are the fundamental differences in tractability between model-free and model-based approaches under various coverage and revealing assumptions?
a2d46b12e89239067e03bc8243a3ef8e2ece594d.hypothesis: Model-based algorithms, under appropriate coverage and revealing assumptions, can achieve polynomial sample complexity for OPE of history-dependent policies in POMDPs, whereas model-free algorithms are fundamentally limited and may suffer from information-theoretic hardness in these settings.
a2d46b12e89239067e03bc8243a3ef8e2ece594d.proposed_method: A model-based approach is proposed for off-policy evaluation in POMDPs with large observation spaces, focusing on history-dependent target policies. The method involves fitting a POMDP model to offline data using maximum likelihood estimation (MLE), after pre-filtering the model class to ensure that only models satisfying certain revealing (single-step or multi-step) and coverage assumptions are considered. The learned model is then used to estimate the expected return of the target policy by simulating rollouts under the target policy within the learned model. The approach leverages function approximation to avoid explicit dependence on the size of the observation space and incorporates policy-specific or uniform coverage parameters to ensure statistical efficiency. The methodology also accounts for possible state-space mismatch by considering observable-equivalent realizability and provides bounds that include an approximation error term when the true model is not exactly realizable.
a2d46b12e89239067e03bc8243a3ef8e2ece594d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic and/or real-world POMDP environments with large observation spaces, where both memoryless and history-dependent behavior and target policies are considered. The evaluation will compare the proposed model-based algorithm against model-free baselines, such as importance sampling and value-function-based estimators, under varying coverage and revealing conditions. Sample complexity will be measured as a function of horizon length, model class size, and coverage parameters. Evaluation metrics will include estimation error of the target policy's value (e.g., |J(π̂) - J(π)|), probability of accurate estimation within a specified error tolerance, and empirical sample complexity required to achieve these guarantees. Additional experiments may investigate the impact of state-space misspecification and the effectiveness of the pre-filtering step.
a2d46b12e89239067e03bc8243a3ef8e2ece594d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first polynomial sample complexity guarantees for model-based OPE of history-dependent target policies in POMDPs with large observation spaces under appropriate coverage and revealing assumptions. It demonstrates a formal and provable separation between model-free and model-based methods in these settings, showing that model-free approaches are subject to information-theoretic hardness even under strong assumptions where model-based methods succeed. The approach also provides new insights into the role of memoryless versus history-dependent behavior policies and addresses the challenge of state-space mismatch by extending guarantees to observable-equivalent realizability with explicit approximation error bounds.

a2fc77f075f666b462d9350e7576f0ba9845c61b.title: Transformer Language Models without Positional Encodings Still Learn Positional Information
a2fc77f075f666b462d9350e7576f0ba9845c61b.research_question: Can transformer language models learn and utilize positional information without the use of explicit positional encodings, and how does this impact their performance across different datasets, model sizes, and sequence lengths?
a2fc77f075f666b462d9350e7576f0ba9845c61b.hypothesis: Transformer language models trained without explicit positional encodings are able to acquire and utilize implicit positional information through the causal attention mechanism, enabling them to achieve competitive performance with models that use explicit positional encodings.
a2fc77f075f666b462d9350e7576f0ba9845c61b.proposed_method: A comprehensive experimental framework will be established to train causal transformer language models without any explicit positional encoding (NoPos models) and compare them to models utilizing standard positional encoding methods, including learned embeddings, sinusoidal embeddings, and ALiBi (Attention with LInear BIases). The models will be trained from scratch on large-scale language modeling datasets, with careful control of architecture, hyperparameters, and training regimes. Probing techniques will be employed to analyze the internal representations of the trained models, specifically by training classifiers to predict the absolute position of tokens from hidden states at various layers. Additional analyses will include word order sensitivity tests and ablation studies to determine the necessity and sufficiency of implicit positional information in different model architectures (causal vs. bidirectional).
a2fc77f075f666b462d9350e7576f0ba9845c61b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both the WikiText-103 corpus (over 100 million words, word-level tokenization) and the Pile dataset (800GB of English text, tokenized with GPT-2's tokenizer). Model architectures will span a range of sizes, including 125M, 350M, 760M, and 1.3B parameter variants, with sequence lengths ranging from 256 to 2048 tokens. Baseline comparisons will include models trained with learned, sinusoidal, and ALiBi positional encodings. Evaluation metrics will primarily focus on validation set perplexity, with additional probing metrics such as mean absolute distance for position prediction. Both causal (autoregressive) and masked (bidirectional) transformer models will be evaluated to assess the generality of the findings. Hyperparameters will be matched across conditions, and experiments will include segment-wise and token-level analyses to further elucidate the models' positional awareness.
a2fc77f075f666b462d9350e7576f0ba9845c61b.novelty_claims: The proposed research challenges the prevailing assumption that explicit positional encodings are necessary for effective transformer language modeling. It introduces a systematic investigation into the ability of causal transformers to acquire implicit positional information solely through the structure of causal attention. The research will provide detailed empirical evidence across multiple datasets, model sizes, and sequence lengths, and will offer probing-based analyses to uncover the internal mechanisms by which positional information is learned. The findings are expected to reveal that explicit positional encodings are not strictly required for competitive performance in causal language models, and will clarify the unique role of the causal attention mask in enabling this phenomenon.

a30ac45ac5b7bd2148d3fb80ee7f3c29724e3170.title: How to Train Your HiPPO: State Space Models with Generalized Orthogonal Basis Projections
a30ac45ac5b7bd2148d3fb80ee7f3c29724e3170.research_question: How can state space models be generalized and theoretically grounded to better capture long-range dependencies in sequence modeling, and how can different orthogonal basis projections be leveraged to improve the performance and interpretability of such models?
a30ac45ac5b7bd2148d3fb80ee7f3c29724e3170.hypothesis: Generalizing the HiPPO framework to encompass a broader class of orthogonal basis projections, including Legendre and Fourier bases, will yield state space models with improved theoretical interpretability and empirical performance on tasks requiring both long-range and local dependencies. Furthermore, principled initialization and normalization of model parameters, especially the timescale parameter, will enhance stability and effectiveness.
a30ac45ac5b7bd2148d3fb80ee7f3c29724e3170.proposed_method: A generalized framework for constructing time-invariant state space models (SSMs) will be developed by deriving orthogonal state space models (OSSMs) corresponding to various orthogonal basis functions and measures. This includes formalizing the connection between the SSM state matrix and exponentially-warped Legendre polynomials, as well as introducing new SSMs based on truncated Fourier bases. The approach will provide closed-form formulas for the basis functions and measures, allowing for precise control over the timescale and normalization of the models. The method will also detail guidelines for initializing all SSM parameters, ensuring variance preservation and stability in deep architectures. The resulting models will be instantiated as trainable layers (e.g., S4-LegS, S4-FouT) with random initialization of the output projection and trained end-to-end on sequence tasks.
a30ac45ac5b7bd2148d3fb80ee7f3c29724e3170.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world sequence modeling tasks. Synthetic tasks will include function reconstruction and memorization benchmarks designed to test the ability to encode and recall information over varying ranges. For real-world evaluation, the Long Range Arena (LRA) benchmark will be used, which consists of multiple sequence classification tasks with long input sequences. The proposed S4 variants (S4-LegS, S4-FouT, S4-LegT) will be compared against each other, against diagonal SSM baselines (S4D), and against prior state-of-the-art sequence models. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy and performance on memorization tasks, with particular attention to the effect of timescale parameter initialization. Empirical results will be analyzed to validate theoretical predictions regarding the suitability of different bases for long-range versus local dependencies.
a30ac45ac5b7bd2148d3fb80ee7f3c29724e3170.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified and general mathematical framework for deriving time-invariant orthogonal state space models for arbitrary orthogonal bases, providing a new theoretical interpretation for the success of S4 and related models. It presents the first principled derivation and closed-form analysis of using the HiPPO-LegS matrix in a time-invariant setting, as well as the development of new SSMs based on the truncated Fourier basis (S4-FouT). The work offers precise guidelines for parameter initialization and normalization, clarifies the role of the timescale parameter, and demonstrates how these insights lead to improved empirical performance and interpretability. The approach subsumes and generalizes all previous HiPPO-based methods and enables the design of SSMs tailored to specific sequence modeling requirements.

a32887af7eb1fcfd3b3d892ad41f3516a37f11c1.title: Tip-Adapter: Training-free Adaption of CLIP for Few-shot Classification
a32887af7eb1fcfd3b3d892ad41f3516a37f11c1.research_question: How can the adaptation capability of large-scale vision-language models such as CLIP be improved for few-shot image classification tasks without incurring significant training time or computational overhead?
a32887af7eb1fcfd3b3d892ad41f3516a37f11c1.hypothesis: A non-parametric, training-free adapter constructed as a key-value cache from few-shot training data can effectively enhance the few-shot classification performance of CLIP, achieving results comparable to or better than training-based adaptation methods, while maintaining high efficiency. Further, fine-tuning the cache keys can yield additional performance gains with minimal training.
a32887af7eb1fcfd3b3d892ad41f3516a37f11c1.proposed_method: A novel adaptation framework is proposed that augments a pre-trained, weight-frozen CLIP model with a non-parametric adapter in the form of a key-value cache. The cache is constructed by extracting L2-normalized visual features from the few-shot training images using CLIP's visual encoder, and pairing them with one-hot encoded ground-truth labels as values. During inference, the test image's feature is used as a query to compute cosine similarities with the cached keys; these affinities are modulated by a hyperparameter and used to aggregate the cached values, forming the adapter's prediction. The final classification logits are a weighted combination of the cache-based prediction and the original CLIP classifier's output, controlled by a residual ratio. An extension, Tip-Adapter-F, allows the cache keys to be fine-tuned via stochastic gradient descent while keeping the CLIP encoders and cache values fixed, enabling rapid convergence and further accuracy improvements.
a32887af7eb1fcfd3b3d892ad41f3516a37f11c1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 11 widely-used image classification datasets, including ImageNet, Stanford Cars, UCF101, Caltech101, Flowers102, SUN397, DTD, EuroSAT, FGVCAircraft, OxfordPets, and Food101. Few-shot settings will be evaluated with 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16 shots per class, and testing will be performed on the full test sets. The proposed methods will be compared against baselines such as Zero-shot CLIP, Linear-probe CLIP, CoOp (learnable prompts), and CLIP-Adapter (parametric feature adapter). Evaluation metrics include classification accuracy, training time, inference speed, and GPU memory usage. Both ResNet and ViT backbones will be used for comprehensive analysis, and ablation studies will be performed to investigate the effects of cache construction, residual weighting, and fine-tuning.
a32887af7eb1fcfd3b3d892ad41f3516a37f11c1.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a training-free, non-parametric adapter for CLIP based on a key-value cache model, enabling efficient few-shot adaptation without additional training. The approach leverages both visual and textual modalities in the cache, and supports a fine-tuning variant that achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with significantly reduced training epochs compared to existing methods. The method demonstrates superior accuracy-efficiency trade-offs, minimal computational overhead, and broad applicability across diverse datasets and backbones.

a32a2be00294e255b93ae37e9bb1f9995f488277.title: When and How Mixup Improves Calibration
a32a2be00294e255b93ae37e9bb1f9995f488277.research_question: Under what conditions does the Mixup data augmentation technique improve the calibration of confidence scores in machine learning models, and how can its effects be theoretically and empirically characterized in both supervised and semi-supervised learning settings?
a32a2be00294e255b93ae37e9bb1f9995f488277.hypothesis: Mixup improves the calibration of predictive confidence scores, especially in high-dimensional regimes where model capacity is large relative to the number of training samples. Furthermore, applying Mixup in semi-supervised learning settings, particularly when combined with pseudo-labeling, mitigates calibration issues that arise from incorporating unlabeled data.
a32a2be00294e255b93ae37e9bb1f9995f488277.proposed_method: A theoretical and empirical investigation is proposed to analyze the impact of Mixup data augmentation on model calibration. The approach involves formulating and proving results under natural statistical models, including Gaussian and Gaussian generative models, to characterize when and why Mixup improves calibration. The methodology includes deriving analytical results for calibration metrics such as Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Maximum Calibration Error (MCE) in both standard supervised learning and semi-supervised learning with pseudo-labeling. The proposal also includes extending the theoretical framework to high-dimensional regimes, where the number of model parameters is comparable to or exceeds the number of training samples, and analyzing the effect of Mixup under domain shifts and with unlabeled data.
a32a2be00294e255b93ae37e9bb1f9995f488277.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification datasets such as CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Kuzushiji-MNIST, and Fashion-MNIST. Fully-connected neural networks and ResNet architectures will be used, with systematic variation of model width and depth to explore different capacity regimes. Baseline models will include standard training without Mixup and semi-supervised learning with pseudo-labeling, while the proposed methods will incorporate Mixup in both supervised and semi-supervised settings. Evaluation metrics will include ECE and MCE, calculated on both in-domain and out-of-domain data. Experimental setups will include both with and without standard data augmentation, and careful control of hyperparameters such as the Mixup interpolation parameter (using Beta distributions).
a32a2be00294e255b93ae37e9bb1f9995f488277.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretical framework that explains when and how Mixup improves calibration, particularly highlighting its effectiveness in high-dimensional and over-parameterized regimes. It extends the analysis of Mixup to semi-supervised learning with pseudo-labeling, providing both theoretical guarantees and empirical evidence that Mixup can mitigate calibration degradation caused by unlabeled data. The work also generalizes the findings to multiple calibration metrics (ECE and MCE) and to flexible generative models, offering new insights into the mechanisms by which Mixup enhances model reliability and uncertainty quantification.

a35f1315e91513ff0bec0c488fe175214fd9636c.title: Recommender Systems in the Era of Large Language Models (LLMs)
a35f1315e91513ff0bec0c488fe175214fd9636c.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be systematically leveraged to advance recommender systems across various paradigms, including pre-training, fine-tuning, and prompting, in order to address limitations of traditional deep learning-based recommenders and improve generalization, reasoning, and adaptability to diverse recommendation scenarios?
a35f1315e91513ff0bec0c488fe175214fd9636c.hypothesis: Integrating large language models into recommender systems through pre-training, fine-tuning, and prompting paradigms will enhance the systems' ability to understand user interests, capture rich side information, generalize to unseen tasks, and provide more accurate, explainable, and flexible recommendations compared to traditional deep learning-based approaches.
a35f1315e91513ff0bec0c488fe175214fd9636c.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed to integrate LLMs into recommender systems using three main paradigms: (1) pre-training LLMs on large-scale recommendation datasets with objectives such as masked language modeling and next token prediction tailored to user-item interaction data; (2) fine-tuning LLMs for specific recommendation tasks using both full-model and parameter-efficient strategies (e.g., adapters, LoRA), allowing adaptation to domain-specific knowledge and computational constraints; (3) leveraging prompting techniques, including in-context learning, prompt tuning, and instruction tuning, to enable LLMs to perform recommendation tasks via task-specific natural language prompts without extensive retraining. The framework will support both ID-based and textual side information-enhanced representations, and will explore advanced prompting strategies such as chain-of-thought and multi-task instruction tuning to improve reasoning and zero-shot capabilities.
a35f1315e91513ff0bec0c488fe175214fd9636c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of benchmark recommendation datasets spanning domains such as e-commerce, entertainment, and social media. The evaluation will include tasks such as top-K recommendation, rating prediction, conversational recommendation, and explanation generation. Baseline comparisons will involve traditional collaborative filtering, deep neural network-based recommenders (e.g., MF, CNNs, RNNs, GNNs), and recent language model-based approaches (e.g., BERT4Rec, T5-based recommenders). Evaluation metrics will include precision, recall, NDCG, MAP, and qualitative assessments of recommendation explanations. The experimental setup will systematically vary LLM architectures (e.g., T5, GPT-3/4, LLaMA), pre-training and fine-tuning strategies, and prompting methods to analyze their impact on performance, generalization, and computational efficiency.
a35f1315e91513ff0bec0c488fe175214fd9636c.novelty_claims: The proposed research offers a systematic and unified framework for integrating LLMs into recommender systems across pre-training, fine-tuning, and prompting paradigms, addressing the limitations of prior DNN-based recommenders in understanding textual side information, generalization, and reasoning. The approach introduces comprehensive strategies for both ID-based and textual side information-enhanced representations, explores advanced parameter-efficient fine-tuning and prompting techniques, and provides an in-depth comparative analysis of LLM-driven recommendation methods. This work is positioned to advance the state-of-the-art in LLM-empowered recommender systems and guide future research in this rapidly evolving interdisciplinary field.

a38a6f445a66c2d2255c0e718195e6f573921c47.title: Multiaccuracy and Multicalibration via Proxy Groups
a38a6f445a66c2d2255c0e718195e6f573921c47.research_question: How can fairness, specifically multiaccuracy and multicalibration, be evaluated and enforced in predictive machine learning models when sensitive group information is missing or incomplete?
a38a6f445a66c2d2255c0e718195e6f573921c47.hypothesis: Proxy-sensitive attributes can be leveraged to provide actionable upper bounds on multiaccuracy and multicalibration violations, and post-processing models to satisfy these fairness criteria across proxies can significantly reduce worst-case fairness violations for the true, but unknown, sensitive groups.
a38a6f445a66c2d2255c0e718195e6f573921c47.proposed_method: The proposed methodology develops a theoretical framework for assessing multiaccuracy and multicalibration violations in the absence of true sensitive group data by utilizing proxy-sensitive attributes. Computable upper bounds for multiaccuracy and multicalibration violations are derived based on the misclassification error of the proxy groups and the mean squared error of the predictive model. The approach includes post-processing the predictive model using algorithms that enforce multiaccuracy or multicalibration with respect to the proxy groups, such as multiaccuracy regression (solving a constrained linear regression problem) and multicalibration boosting (an iterative refinement procedure). These algorithms are designed to minimize the upper bounds on fairness violations by adjusting model predictions to be unbiased and well-calibrated across proxy groups, while ensuring that overall predictive performance does not deteriorate.
a38a6f445a66c2d2255c0e718195e6f573921c47.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on two tabular datasets, ACSIncome and ACSPublicCoverage, as well as the CheXpert medical imaging dataset. For the ACS datasets, the data is split into training, validation, and evaluation sets, with proxies and models trained on separate subsets to simulate missing sensitive attributes. The evaluation involves reporting worst-case violations, upper bounds, and actual multiaccuracy and multicalibration errors with respect to both proxy and true groups. Baseline models include logistic regression, decision trees, and random forests. Evaluation metrics include mean squared error, group-wise calibration error (ECE), and worst-case fairness violations. Comparisons are made before and after applying the proposed post-processing algorithms to demonstrate the reduction in fairness violations.
a38a6f445a66c2d2255c0e718195e6f573921c47.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled approach for providing actionable and computable upper bounds on multiaccuracy and multicalibration violations using proxy-sensitive attributes, even when true sensitive group data is unavailable. It further demonstrates that enforcing fairness criteria with respect to proxies can provably reduce worst-case violations for the true groups, offering practical fairness guarantees in real-world settings with incomplete group information. The approach extends the use of proxies beyond traditional parity-based fairness notions to more flexible and robust fairness frameworks, filling a significant gap in the current literature.

a395c6a6aaa471f64667a63f32aeed88a3db3746.title: PIPE: Physics-Informed Position Encoding for Alignment of Satellite Images and Time Series
a395c6a6aaa471f64667a63f32aeed88a3db3746.research_question: How can physical information such as timestamps and geospatial coordinates be effectively integrated into multimodal time series forecasting models to improve the alignment and predictive accuracy of satellite imagery and numerical data, particularly for high-stakes forecasting tasks like typhoon prediction?
a395c6a6aaa471f64667a63f32aeed88a3db3746.hypothesis: Incorporating physics-informed positional encoding that explicitly embeds global physical metadata (e.g., time, latitude, longitude) into vision-language models will significantly enhance the alignment between satellite imagery and time series data, thereby improving the forecasting accuracy for multimodal tasks such as typhoon intensity and trajectory prediction.
a395c6a6aaa471f64667a63f32aeed88a3db3746.proposed_method: A novel framework, Physics-Informed Position Encoding (PIPE), will be developed to embed physical information directly into the positional encodings of vision-language models (VLMs) for multimodal time series forecasting. PIPE will introduce two key components: (1) a physics-informed positional indexing scheme that maps physical attributes (such as temporal progression, latitude, and longitude) to unique positional IDs, and (2) a variant-frequency positional encoding mechanism that encodes the frequency characteristics of physical variables (e.g., daily, hourly, spatial frequencies) into the embedding space using modified sinusoidal functions. The method will ensure that both the sequential order and the global physical context are preserved, while avoiding conflicts between vision and text token positional ranges by mapping vision token IDs to negative values. The approach will be implemented within a VLM pipeline, leveraging pretrained language and vision encoders, and will be compatible with existing transformer-based architectures.
a395c6a6aaa471f64667a63f32aeed88a3db3746.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Digital Typhoon dataset, the largest open-source satellite imagery collection for typhoon analysis, spanning over 40 years and including more than 1,100 typhoon sequences and nearly 200,000 images. The forecasting task will target three variables: typhoon intensity, latitude, and longitude, using a 0.7:0.15:0.15 split for training, validation, and testing. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art domain-specific models (e.g., ECMWF, Pangu, GenCast, TIFS) and leading AI models (e.g., PatchTST, iTransformer, Crossformer, TimeXer, TiDE, OneFitsAll, AutoTimes, TimesNet, TimeMixer, Qwen-2.5-VL) using consistent temporal settings (12-hour input/output sequences). Evaluation metrics will include Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) for intensity, latitude, and longitude, and geographic distance error for typhoon tracks. Ablation studies will systematically assess the contributions of vision data, physics-informed indexing, and variant-frequency encoding.
a395c6a6aaa471f64667a63f32aeed88a3db3746.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first physics-informed positional encoding framework for multimodal time series forecasting, enabling explicit integration of global physical metadata into VLMs. The approach innovates by combining a physics-informed positional indexing scheme with a variant-frequency sinusoidal encoding, facilitating the modeling of spatiotemporal dependencies beyond pixel-level semantics. The method avoids additional architectural complexity by leveraging positional IDs and is shown to outperform both domain-specific and general AI baselines, achieving significant improvements in forecasting accuracy (e.g., a 12% gain in typhoon intensity prediction). Comprehensive ablation studies further validate the unique contributions of each component.

a395f1c0910a5622f6faaefb5b27e87bb1617759.title: Directly Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models on Differentiable Rewards
a395f1c0910a5622f6faaefb5b27e87bb1617759.research_question: How can diffusion models be efficiently fine-tuned to maximize arbitrary differentiable reward functions, such as those derived from human preference models or other task-specific objectives, in a scalable and sample-efficient manner?
a395f1c0910a5622f6faaefb5b27e87bb1617759.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that directly backpropagating reward gradients through the diffusion sampling process enables more effective and efficient fine-tuning of diffusion models on differentiable reward functions compared to reinforcement learning-based or supervised approaches. Further, truncating the backpropagation to a subset of sampling steps and employing low-variance gradient estimators will improve training efficiency and stability without sacrificing performance.
a395f1c0910a5622f6faaefb5b27e87bb1617759.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces Direct Reward Fine-Tuning (DRaFT), which fine-tunes diffusion models by directly backpropagating the gradient of a differentiable reward function through the entire diffusion sampling chain. To address memory and compute constraints, the approach leverages low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to update only a small set of parameters and employs gradient checkpointing to reduce memory usage during backpropagation. Two efficiency-focused variants are proposed: DRaFT-K, which truncates backpropagation to only the last K steps of the sampling process, and DRaFT-LV, which further reduces gradient variance by averaging gradients over multiple noise samples at the final step. The method is designed to be broadly applicable to any differentiable reward, including human preference scores, image aesthetics, object detection, and compressibility.
a395f1c0910a5622f6faaefb5b27e87bb1617759.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using Stable Diffusion 1.4 as the base model, with fine-tuning performed on a range of differentiable reward functions, including LAION Aesthetic Classifier scores, PickScore, and Human Preference Score v2 (HPSv2). The evaluation will utilize prompt sets such as the 45-animal prompt set and the HPDv2 dataset, measuring performance with reward model scores and human preference benchmarks. Baselines for comparison include reinforcement learning-based methods (e.g., DDPO), supervised fine-tuning, ReFL (a gradient-based baseline), and prompt engineering. Additional experiments will test generalization across prompt sets and reward functions, as well as applications to object removal/addition and adversarial example generation. Evaluation metrics will include sample efficiency (reward per query), final reward scores, qualitative image quality, and generalization ability. Ablations over the number of backpropagation steps (K) and LoRA parameter scaling will be performed to study efficiency and compositionality.
a395f1c0910a5622f6faaefb5b27e87bb1617759.novelty_claims: The proposal claims novelty in directly differentiating through the full diffusion sampling process for reward-based fine-tuning, providing a unified and efficient framework that outperforms RL-based and previous gradient-based methods in both speed and sample efficiency. The introduction of DRaFT-K and DRaFT-LV offers further improvements in computational efficiency and gradient stability. Additional innovations include the use of LoRA for parameter-efficient fine-tuning, the ability to interpolate and combine fine-tuned models via LoRA parameter scaling and mixing, and the demonstration of broad applicability to diverse reward functions and tasks.

a39b8981708c11c4bee239f24207b527dcd01008.title: Rényi Neural Processes
a39b8981708c11c4bee239f24207b527dcd01008.research_question: How can neural process models be improved to address the issue of prior misspecification, particularly under noisy, domain-shifted, or otherwise challenging context sets, in order to achieve more robust and accurate uncertainty estimation and predictive performance across a variety of regression and image inpainting tasks?
a39b8981708c11c4bee239f24207b527dcd01008.hypothesis: Replacing the standard KL divergence in neural process training objectives with the Rényi divergence, and tuning its hyperparameter, will mitigate the effects of prior misspecification, resulting in improved posterior variance estimation, reduced over-regularization, and enhanced predictive performance across diverse neural process architectures and datasets.
a39b8981708c11c4bee239f24207b527dcd01008.proposed_method: A novel framework, Rényi Neural Processes (RNP), will be developed to address prior misspecification in neural processes by substituting the standard KL divergence with the Rényi divergence in both variational inference (VI) and maximum likelihood (ML) training objectives. The method introduces a hyperparameter α, which controls the influence of the prior on the posterior, allowing the model to dampen the effects of a potentially misspecified prior. The RNP objective will be formulated for both VI-based and ML-based neural process variants, with Monte Carlo sampling used to approximate expectations over latent variables.
