The approach will maintain compatibility with existing neural process architectures, requiring no changes to model structure, and will utilize reparameterization tricks for efficient gradient estimation. Hyperparameter α will be selected via cross-validation or annealing strategies to optimize performance for specific datasets and tasks.
a39b8981708c11c4bee239f24207b527dcd01008.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple regression benchmarks, including 1D Gaussian Process regression tasks with RBF, Matern5/2, and Periodic kernels, as well as 2D image inpainting tasks on MNIST, SVHN, CelebA, and EMNIST datasets. The proposed method will be evaluated against state-of-the-art neural process baselines such as NP, ANP, BA-NP, TNP-D, and VNP, using both VI and ML objectives. Evaluation metrics will include mean test log-likelihood and standard deviation across multiple random seeds. Additional experiments will assess robustness under parameterization-related and context-related prior misspecification, including noisy contexts and domain-shifted tasks (e.g., Lotka-Volterra to Hare-Lynx, EMNIST class splits). Ablation studies will analyze the effects of the Rényi divergence hyperparameter α, the number of Monte Carlo samples, and context set size on predictive performance. Statistical significance will be established using p-values, and computational efficiency will be monitored.
a39b8981708c11c4bee239f24207b527dcd01008.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a robust divergence-based objective for neural processes that unifies variational inference and maximum likelihood estimation via the Rényi divergence, providing a principled approach to mitigating prior misspecification. The framework is general, model-agnostic, and applicable to a wide range of neural process variants without requiring architectural changes. The approach enables flexible control over prior regularization, leading to consistent improvements in predictive log-likelihood and uncertainty estimation across challenging tasks and datasets. The method also provides theoretical insights into the connection between robust divergences and neural process objectives, and demonstrates superior robustness under noisy and domain-shifted contexts compared to existing baselines.

a3b42a83669998f65df60d7c065a70d07ca95e99.title: BLIP: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training for Unified Vision-Language Understanding and Generation
a3b42a83669998f65df60d7c065a70d07ca95e99.research_question: How can a unified vision-language pre-training framework be developed to effectively support both understanding-based and generation-based tasks, while leveraging large-scale noisy web image-text data for improved downstream performance?
a3b42a83669998f65df60d7c065a70d07ca95e99.hypothesis: A unified multimodal mixture of encoder-decoder architecture, combined with a bootstrapping strategy that generates and filters synthetic captions from noisy web image-text pairs, will yield superior performance across a wide range of vision-language understanding and generation tasks compared to existing methods.
a3b42a83669998f65df60d7c065a70d07ca95e99.proposed_method: A novel vision-language pre-training framework is proposed that integrates a multimodal mixture of encoder-decoder (MED) architecture capable of functioning as a unimodal encoder, an image-grounded text encoder, or an image-grounded text decoder. The model is pre-trained using three objectives: image-text contrastive loss (ITC) to align visual and textual representations, image-text matching loss (ITM) to capture fine-grained multimodal alignment, and language modeling loss (LM) to enable text generation from images. To address the noise in web-sourced image-text pairs, a bootstrapping method (CapFilt) is introduced, where a captioner (finetuned image-grounded text decoder) generates synthetic captions for web images, and a filter (finetuned image-grounded text encoder) removes noisy captions from both original and synthetic texts. The captioner and filter are initialized from the same pre-trained model and are individually finetuned on a small human-annotated dataset. The resulting high-quality, diverse dataset is then used to pre-train a new MED model, with shared parameters between encoder and decoder except for self-attention layers to optimize multi-task learning.
a3b42a83669998f65df60d7c065a70d07ca95e99.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using large-scale datasets, including 14M images from COCO, Visual Genome, Conceptual Captions, Conceptual 12M, and SBU Captions, with additional experiments on the LAION dataset (115M images). The model is evaluated on a wide range of downstream tasks: image-text retrieval (COCO, Flickr30K), image captioning (COCO, NoCaps), visual question answering (VQA), natural language visual reasoning (NLVR2), visual dialog (VisDial), and zero-shot transfer to video-language tasks (MSRVTT, MSVD-QA). Baselines include state-of-the-art encoder-based and encoder-decoder models such as CLIP, ALBEF, SimVLM, and LEMON. Evaluation metrics include Recall@K for retrieval, CIDEr, SPICE, and BLEU@4 for captioning, accuracy for VQA and NLVR2, and mean reciprocal rank for dialog. Ablation studies investigate the effects of parameter sharing, caption diversity (nucleus sampling vs. beam search), and the impact of the bootstrapping strategy.
a3b42a83669998f65df60d7c065a70d07ca95e99.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a unified multimodal mixture of encoder-decoder architecture that flexibly supports both understanding and generation tasks, overcoming limitations of prior models restricted to one or the other. The CapFilt bootstrapping strategy is novel in its use of synthetic caption generation and filtering to improve the quality of large-scale web image-text datasets, resulting in more effective vision-language pre-training. The approach demonstrates state-of-the-art performance across a broader range of tasks than previous methods, including strong zero-shot generalization to video-language domains. Additional contributions include detailed analysis of parameter sharing strategies and the demonstrated importance of caption diversity for pre-training effectiveness.

a3ca77456142b78367dd5d53138b50dfac8086ca.title: SpatialVLM: Endowing Vision-Language Models with Spatial Reasoning Capabilities
a3ca77456142b78367dd5d53138b50dfac8086ca.research_question: Can vision-language models be endowed with human-like spatial reasoning abilities, including both qualitative and quantitative understanding of spatial relationships, by augmenting their training data and methodologies?
a3ca77456142b78367dd5d53138b50dfac8086ca.hypothesis: The limited spatial reasoning abilities of current vision-language models are primarily due to insufficient spatial reasoning data in their training sets, rather than fundamental architectural limitations. By training on large-scale, spatially-annotated datasets, vision-language models can acquire both qualitative and quantitative spatial reasoning capabilities.
a3ca77456142b78367dd5d53138b50dfac8086ca.proposed_method: A comprehensive data synthesis and training pipeline will be developed to generate a large-scale spatial visual question answering (VQA) dataset. This pipeline will leverage off-the-shelf computer vision models for open-vocabulary detection, metric depth estimation, semantic segmentation, and object-centric captioning to extract rich object-centric contexts from real-world 2D images. These contexts will be lifted into 3D point clouds to enable metric spatial annotations. Ambiguity in object references will be resolved using fine-grained captioning and semantic clustering. Using a set of question and answer templates, both qualitative and quantitative spatial reasoning questions will be generated, resulting in a diverse dataset. A vision-language model will then be trained on a mixture of this spatial VQA data and standard VQA/captioning data, with a portion of training tokens dedicated to spatial reasoning tasks. The model will be evaluated for its ability to perform direct spatial reasoning as well as multi-step chain-of-thought spatial reasoning when coordinated with a large language model.
a3ca77456142b78367dd5d53138b50dfac8086ca.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training the proposed vision-language model on a mixture of the newly generated spatial VQA dataset (comprising 2 billion QA pairs over 10 million images) and existing datasets such as those used for PaLM-E. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art models such as GPT-4V, LLaVA-1.5, InstructBLIP, PaLI, PaLM-E, and PaLM2-E, all trained without the spatial VQA data. Evaluation will be conducted on a custom spatial VQA benchmark with human-annotated qualitative and quantitative questions, using metrics such as accuracy for binary predicate prediction, success rate of valid quantitative outputs, and the percentage of answers within a specified range of ground truth values. Additional studies will examine the effects of noisy data, the impact of freezing versus unfreezing the visual encoder, and the model's performance on general VQA benchmarks (OKVQA, VQAv2) to assess any trade-offs.
a3ca77456142b78367dd5d53138b50dfac8086ca.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first Internet-scale 3D spatial reasoning dataset in metric space, generated automatically from real-world images using a novel data synthesis pipeline. It enables vision-language models to perform both qualitative and quantitative spatial reasoning, including metric distance estimation from 2D images. The approach demonstrates that large-scale, synthetic spatial reasoning data can significantly enhance spatial reasoning capabilities in vision-language models, unlocking new downstream applications such as chain-of-thought spatial reasoning and robotics planning. The method also provides insights into the effects of noisy data and visual encoder training strategies on spatial reasoning performance.

a3cdf5d2d5c53370dd6173b509438481e32a0419.title: Video-R1: Reinforcing Video Reasoning in MLLMs
a3cdf5d2d5c53370dd6173b509438481e32a0419.research_question: How can multimodal large language models (MLLMs) be systematically enhanced to perform robust and generalizable video reasoning, particularly by leveraging reinforcement learning paradigms and addressing challenges in temporal modeling and data scarcity?
a3cdf5d2d5c53370dd6173b509438481e32a0419.hypothesis: Incorporating explicit temporal modeling into reinforcement learning algorithms and augmenting scarce video reasoning data with high-quality image-based reasoning data will significantly improve the video reasoning capabilities of MLLMs, enabling them to outperform existing models on complex video understanding and reasoning benchmarks.
a3cdf5d2d5c53370dd6173b509438481e32a0419.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed that combines rule-based reinforcement learning with explicit temporal modeling for video reasoning in MLLMs. The core algorithm, Temporal Group Relative Policy Optimization (T-GRPO), will be introduced to encourage models to leverage temporal information by contrasting performance on temporally ordered versus randomly shuffled video frames, assigning positive rewards only when the model demonstrates superior reasoning with correct temporal order. Two large-scale datasets will be curated: Video-R1-CoT-165k for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) cold start, containing chain-of-thought annotated samples, and Video-R1-260k for reinforcement learning, both comprising a mix of video and image-based reasoning tasks. The training pipeline will involve an initial SFT stage to bootstrap general reasoning abilities, followed by RL training using T-GRPO, with additional reward shaping to regulate reasoning path length and encourage deep but concise reasoning.
a3cdf5d2d5c53370dd6173b509438481e32a0419.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six video benchmarks: VSI-Bench, VideoMMMU, MMVU (multiple-choice subset), MVBench, TempCompass, and VideoMME, covering both video reasoning and general video understanding tasks. The model will be based on Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, trained first on Video-R1-CoT-165k for SFT and then on Video-R1-260k using T-GRPO. Evaluation will use accuracy and task-specific metrics such as ROUGE for free-form QA and Word Error Rate for OCR tasks. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art models such as GPT-4o, LLaMA-VID, VideoLLaMA2, LongVA, VILA, Video-UTR, LLaVA-OneVision, Kangaroo, and ablated versions of the proposed model (removing image data, temporal modeling, or SFT). Ablation studies will assess the impact of each component, and sensitivity analyses will be performed on the temporal reward hyperparameter. Training will utilize up to 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs, with frame numbers and resolutions varied to study their effect on performance.
a3cdf5d2d5c53370dd6173b509438481e32a0419.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first systematic exploration of the R1 reinforcement learning paradigm for video reasoning in MLLMs, including the novel T-GRPO algorithm that explicitly incentivizes temporal reasoning by contrasting ordered and shuffled frame inputs. The approach uniquely addresses the scarcity of high-quality video reasoning data by integrating curated image-based reasoning samples, enabling transfer of reasoning skills from static to dynamic contexts. The curated datasets, Video-R1-CoT-165k and Video-R1-260k, represent significant new resources for the community. The method is claimed to achieve state-of-the-art results on challenging video reasoning benchmarks, surpassing even proprietary models such as GPT-4o, and demonstrates the importance of temporal-aware RL and hybrid data pipelines for robust video reasoning.

a3d5a32500fbd35bcde740923c697859d2cef04f.title: Understanding High-Dimensional Bayesian Optimization
a3d5a32500fbd35bcde740923c697859d2cef04f.research_question: What are the underlying challenges in high-dimensional Bayesian optimization (HDBO) that limit the performance of standard methods, and how can these challenges be addressed to achieve state-of-the-art results on real-world high-dimensional optimization tasks?
a3d5a32500fbd35bcde740923c697859d2cef04f.hypothesis: Vanishing gradients in Gaussian process (GP) initialization and acquisition function optimization are a primary cause of failure in high-dimensional Bayesian optimization, and that a simple maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) of GP length scales, when combined with random axis-aligned subspace perturbation (RAASP) sampling, is sufficient to achieve state-of-the-art performance without requiring strong prior assumptions.
a3d5a32500fbd35bcde740923c697859d2cef04f.proposed_method: A new approach is developed that systematically analyzes the causes of performance degradation in high-dimensional Bayesian optimization, focusing on the effects of vanishing gradients during GP hyperparameter fitting and acquisition function optimization. The proposed method introduces a simple variant of MLE for GP length scale initialization, called MLE Scaled with RAASP (MSR), which initializes the length scale proportional to the square root of the problem dimensionality to counteract the increased distances in high-dimensional spaces. RAASP sampling is incorporated into the acquisition function maximization to promote locality and mitigate flat acquisition surfaces. The method is implemented using a 5/2-ARD-Matérn kernel and the numerically stable LogEI acquisition function, and is designed to operate directly in the high-dimensional input space without requiring additional structural assumptions.
a3d5a32500fbd35bcde740923c697859d2cef04f.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a comprehensive suite of real-world high-dimensional benchmarks, including Mopta08 (124d), Lasso-DNA (180d), SVM (388d), Rover (60d), and two Mujoco tasks (888d and 6392d), covering both noise-free and noisy settings. The proposed MSR method is compared against several baselines: MLE with scaled and unscaled length scale initialization, DSP (MAP with dimensionality-scaled prior), SAASBO, TuRBO, and Bounce. Evaluation metrics include the best objective value found over iterations and the observation traveling salesperson distance (OTSD) to quantify exploration. Each method is run for a fixed number of iterations (up to 1000 or until computational limits are reached), and results are averaged over multiple random seeds to assess robustness and variance.
a3d5a32500fbd35bcde740923c697859d2cef04f.novelty_claims: The proposal claims to identify and empirically validate vanishing gradients as a key bottleneck in high-dimensional Bayesian optimization, and introduces a simple yet effective initialization strategy for GP length scales that, when combined with RAASP sampling, matches or exceeds the performance of more complex state-of-the-art methods. The approach eliminates the need for strong prior assumptions or complex surrogate structures, and provides new empirical insights into the bias-variance trade-off in GP hyperparameter fitting in high dimensions. The work also highlights the importance of locality-promoting sampling strategies and offers practical guidelines for robust HDBO in real-world applications.

a3d749bc119f5c8425779e4e72e650720db2fe4b.title: OpenMathInstruct-1: A 1.8 Million Math Instruction Tuning Dataset
a3d749bc119f5c8425779e4e72e650720db2fe4b.research_question: How can a large-scale, high-quality, and permissively licensed math instruction tuning dataset be constructed using only open-source language models, and what is the impact of such a dataset on the mathematical reasoning capabilities of open-source large language models compared to models trained on GPT-distilled data?
a3d749bc119f5c8425779e4e72e650720db2fe4b.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a large-scale math instruction tuning dataset, synthesized using advanced prompting techniques and open-source language models, can achieve comparable or superior training coverage and downstream performance to datasets generated using closed-source models, thereby enabling the development of competitive and fully open-source mathematical reasoning models.
a3d749bc119f5c8425779e4e72e650720db2fe4b.proposed_method: A comprehensive solution synthesis pipeline will be developed to generate a large-scale math instruction tuning dataset using the Mixtral open-source language model. The methodology involves few-shot prompting with a variety of strategies, including default prompts, subject-specific prompts, and a novel masked text solution prompting technique, which masks intermediate computations in reference solutions to prevent shortcutting. The code-interpreter format will be used for synthesized solutions, interleaving natural language reasoning with executable Python code blocks. Post-processing steps will be applied to filter out syntactically or semantically noisy solutions, and fair downsampling and code-preferential selection strategies will be used to ensure balanced and high-quality data for fine-tuning. The final dataset will be deduplicated and curated to maximize coverage and diversity.
a3d749bc119f5c8425779e4e72e650720db2fe4b.experiment_details: Experiments will involve synthesizing solutions for the GSM8K and MATH benchmarks, generating hundreds of solutions per problem using the Mixtral model with temperature and top-p sampling. The resulting dataset will be used to fine-tune various open-source LLMs, including Mistral-7B, Llama2, and CodeLlama, with training conducted for four epochs using the AdamW optimizer and a global batch size of 128. Evaluation will be performed on multiple math reasoning benchmarks such as GSM8K, MATH, GSM-Hard, SVAMP, TabMWP, ASDiv, and MAWPS, using both greedy decoding and self-consistency/majority voting. Baselines will include state-of-the-art GPT-distilled models and other open-source models fine-tuned on existing datasets. Ablation studies will assess the impact of prompting strategies, data selection methods, and dataset size on model performance.
a3d749bc119f5c8425779e4e72e650720db2fe4b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a permissively licensed, large-scale math instruction tuning dataset that is at least four times larger than previous public datasets. The methodology features a novel masked text solution prompting strategy to enhance solution diversity and prevent shortcutting, as well as fair downsampling and code-preferential selection to improve data balance and quality. The resulting dataset enables the training of open-source models that achieve performance competitive with or superior to GPT-distilled models, supporting reproducibility and unrestricted use in future research.

a3e000e0d7f64c1d094c2a8bf6f43992cbabe91b.title: KIVI: A Tuning-Free Asymmetric 2bit Quantization for KV Cache
a3e000e0d7f64c1d094c2a8bf6f43992cbabe91b.research_question: How can the memory and speed bottlenecks caused by the key-value (KV) cache in large language model (LLM) inference be alleviated, particularly under large batch sizes and long context lengths, without sacrificing model accuracy?
a3e000e0d7f64c1d094c2a8bf6f43992cbabe91b.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a tuning-free, asymmetric 2-bit quantization scheme—applying per-channel quantization to the key cache and per-token quantization to the value cache—can significantly reduce KV cache memory usage and increase inference throughput, while maintaining near-original accuracy across a variety of LLM architectures and tasks.
a3e000e0d7f64c1d094c2a8bf6f43992cbabe91b.proposed_method: A novel quantization framework, KIVI, will be developed to compress the KV cache in LLMs using an asymmetric, tuning-free 2-bit quantization approach. The method involves detailed analysis of the element distribution within the key and value caches, leading to the insight that key caches should be quantized per-channel due to the presence of large-magnitude outlier channels, while value caches should be quantized per-token to confine quantization error within individual tokens. To accommodate the streaming nature of LLM inference, the key cache will be split into grouped and residual parts, with group-wise quantization applied to the grouped portion and the residual kept in full precision. The value cache will similarly maintain a sliding window of recent tokens in full precision. Hardware-friendly implementations will fuse dequantization with matrix multiplication to minimize computational overhead.
a3e000e0d7f64c1d094c2a8bf6f43992cbabe91b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several popular LLMs, including Llama, Falcon, and Mistral families, using the HuggingFace Transformers codebase. Evaluation will span both normal and long context settings, with tasks drawn from LM-Eval (CoQA, TruthfulQA, GSM8K) and LongBench (Qasper, QMSum, MultiNews, TREC, TriviaQA, SAMSum, LCC, RepoBench-P), as well as the Needle-in-a-Haystack (NIAH) benchmark for long-context retrieval. Baselines will include standard 16-bit and 4-bit quantization, as well as various symmetric and asymmetric 2-bit quantization configurations. Metrics will include accuracy (exact match, BLEU, ROUGE, F1, classification, similarity), memory usage, and throughput. Ablation studies will assess the impact of group size and residual length on performance, and efficiency will be measured on real LLM workloads using synthetic data from ShareGPT, with throughput and peak memory usage reported on NVIDIA A100 GPUs.
a3e000e0d7f64c1d094c2a8bf6f43992cbabe91b.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first systematic, tuning-free, asymmetric 2-bit quantization scheme for KV cache in LLMs, grounded in an in-depth analysis of cache element distributions. It claims to achieve up to 2.6× reduction in peak memory usage and enable up to 4× larger batch sizes, resulting in 2.35× to 3.47× throughput improvement with minimal or no accuracy loss. The approach is hardware-friendly, plug-and-play, and compatible with existing weight-only quantization and system-level memory management techniques. The method is validated across multiple LLM architectures and a comprehensive suite of tasks, demonstrating robust performance even on challenging long-context and reasoning benchmarks.

a3eff696eef2d9cf155a4433f8a4e77c78229373.title: On the Generalization Properties of Diffusion Models
a3eff696eef2d9cf155a4433f8a4e77c78229373.research_question: What are the generalization properties of diffusion models as generative models, and how do factors such as sample size, model capacity, and the structure of the target distribution (including mode shifts) affect their generalization error?
a3eff696eef2d9cf155a4433f8a4e77c78229373.hypothesis: Diffusion models, when appropriately early-stopped and parameterized, achieve a generalization error that scales polynomially with respect to both sample size and model capacity, and this error is not exponentially dependent on data dimensionality. However, the presence of distant modes in the target distribution adversely affects generalization.
a3eff696eef2d9cf155a4433f8a4e77c78229373.proposed_method: A rigorous theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the generalization gap of score-based diffusion models during training. The analysis will focus on models parameterized as random feature neural networks, with the forward and reverse processes described by coupled stochastic differential equations. The generalization gap will be quantified using Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence between the learned and target distributions, with explicit upper bounds derived as functions of sample size, model capacity, and training time. Theoretical results will be extended to both data-independent settings (compactly supported distributions) and data-dependent settings (e.g., Gaussian mixtures with increasing mode separation), with careful consideration of the effects of mode shifts.
a3eff696eef2d9cf155a4433f8a4e77c78229373.experiment_details: Numerical simulations will be conducted to empirically verify the theoretical estimates of the generalization gap. Experiments will utilize both synthetic datasets (such as unidimensional Gaussian mixtures with varying mode distances) and real-world datasets. The evaluation will involve computing the KL divergence and negative log-likelihood on held-out test data, using the probability flow ODE and change-of-variable formula. Baselines will include standard diffusion models trained under similar conditions, and model capacity as well as sample size will be systematically varied to observe their effects on generalization. Early stopping will be employed to study its impact on the generalization error.
a3eff696eef2d9cf155a4433f8a4e77c78229373.novelty_claims: The proposed research will provide the first mathematically rigorous, quantitative characterization of the generalization gap for diffusion models as a function of both sample size and model capacity, demonstrating polynomial scaling and avoidance of the curse of dimensionality under early stopping. The analysis will further extend to data-dependent scenarios, explicitly quantifying the impact of mode shifts in the target distribution on generalization. These results will bridge a significant gap in the theoretical understanding of diffusion models and offer practical insights for their deployment and further development.

a3f9143281d4a0ed5e5a8b3189ddde3ab3435ab4.title: Puppeteer: Rig and Animate Your 3D Models
a3f9143281d4a0ed5e5a8b3189ddde3ab3435ab4.research_question: How can the process of transforming static 3D models into fully animated assets be automated for diverse object categories, eliminating the need for manual rigging and animation while ensuring high-quality, temporally coherent results?
a3f9143281d4a0ed5e5a8b3189ddde3ab3435ab4.hypothesis: A unified, learning-based framework that integrates auto-regressive skeleton generation, topology-aware skinning weight prediction, and differentiable optimization-based animation can automate the rigging and animation of diverse 3D models, outperforming existing methods in accuracy, generalization, and efficiency.
a3f9143281d4a0ed5e5a8b3189ddde3ab3435ab4.proposed_method: The proposed methodology consists of a three-stage pipeline. First, an auto-regressive transformer model is used to generate plausible skeletal structures for input 3D meshes, employing a joint-based tokenization strategy and hierarchical sequence ordering with stochastic perturbation to enhance bidirectional learning and structural coherence. Second, an attention-based network predicts per-vertex skinning weights, explicitly encoding inter-joint relationships using topology-aware joint attention based on skeletal graph distances, and leveraging part-aware point embeddings for improved anatomical correspondence. Third, a differentiable optimization-based animation pipeline is introduced, which takes the generated rig and uses reference video sequences (obtained from state-of-the-art text-to-video generation models) to guide the animation of the 3D model. The animation optimization jointly adjusts per-frame joint rotations and global root motion, using differentiable rendering and tracking losses to align the animated mesh with the reference video while enforcing temporal smoothness and visibility constraints.
a3f9143281d4a0ed5e5a8b3189ddde3ab3435ab4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the newly expanded Articulation-XL2.0 dataset, comprising 59.4k rigged 3D models with an 11.4k diverse-pose subset, as well as the ModelsResource benchmark and a 500-mesh diverse-pose test set. The rigging pipeline will be evaluated against baselines including Pinocchio, RigNet, MagicArticulate, and UniRig for skeleton generation, and GVB, RigNet, and MagicArticulate for skinning weight prediction. Evaluation metrics for skeletons include Chamfer Distance-based measures (CD-J2J, CD-J2B, CD-B2B), while skinning weights are assessed using precision, recall, and L1-norm error. Animation results will be compared to L4GM and MotionDreamer, using qualitative and quantitative assessments of temporal consistency and visual fidelity. Data augmentations and pose augmentations will be applied during training to enhance generalization.
a3f9143281d4a0ed5e5a8b3189ddde3ab3435ab4.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is novel in its integration of automatic rigging and animation into a unified, fully automated pipeline for arbitrary 3D models. Key innovations include a joint-based tokenization and hierarchical ordering strategy for compact and coherent skeleton generation, a topology-aware attention mechanism for robust and generalizable skinning weight prediction, and a differentiable, optimization-based animation method that requires no neural network parameters and achieves stable, high-fidelity results. The approach is supported by the release of a large-scale, diverse-pose articulation dataset, and demonstrates superior performance in both rigging and animation tasks across a wide range of object categories.

a4065e70b25bdf20b4587f8d1bbaaa7e4eeb9390.title: Correlated Proxies: A New Definition and Improved Mitigation for Reward Hacking
a4065e70b25bdf20b4587f8d1bbaaa7e4eeb9390.research_question: How can reward hacking in reinforcement learning, arising from the use of proxy reward functions that only approximate the true objective, be formally defined and effectively mitigated across realistic environments?
a4065e70b25bdf20b4587f8d1bbaaa7e4eeb9390.hypothesis: Reward hacking can be better prevented by regularizing policy optimization using the chi-squared (χ2) divergence between occupancy measures of the optimized and reference policies, rather than the commonly used KL divergence between action distributions.
a4065e70b25bdf20b4587f8d1bbaaa7e4eeb9390.proposed_method: A new formal definition of reward hacking is introduced, based on the correlation between proxy and true rewards under a reference policy. The proposed approach involves optimizing the proxy reward function while regularizing the policy to remain close to the reference policy in terms of occupancy measure, specifically by penalizing the χ2 divergence between the occupancy measures of the learned and reference policies. This is operationalized by augmenting the policy optimization objective with a χ2 occupancy measure regularization term, where the regularization strength is determined by the degree of correlation between the proxy and true rewards. The occupancy measure divergence is estimated using a discriminator network, and policy optimization is performed via policy gradient methods such as PPO, using an adjusted reward function that incorporates the regularization. The method is compared against traditional action distribution regularization using both KL and χ2 divergences.
a4065e70b25bdf20b4587f8d1bbaaa7e4eeb9390.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted in five environments: traffic control, pandemic mitigation, glucose monitoring, RLHF (reinforcement learning from human feedback), and an AI safety gridworld. In each environment, proxy and true rewards are defined, and a reference policy is constructed. Policies are trained with four types of regularization: action distribution KL, action distribution χ2, occupancy measure KL, and occupancy measure χ2, across a range of regularization coefficients. Baselines include the unregularized policy (which exhibits reward hacking), the reference policy, and a policy trained directly on the true reward (as an upper bound). Evaluation metrics include the expected return under the true reward function, with results reported as median and standard deviation over multiple random seeds. The effectiveness and robustness of each regularization method are assessed, with ablations and hyperparameter details provided in the appendices.
a4065e70b25bdf20b4587f8d1bbaaa7e4eeb9390.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new formal definition of reward hacking based on correlation with a reference policy, which more accurately captures realistic cases than previous definitions. It establishes a theoretical justification for regularizing the χ2 divergence between occupancy measures to prevent reward hacking, providing provable lower bounds on true reward improvement. The method is shown to outperform existing approaches, such as KL-based action distribution regularization, both theoretically and empirically across several realistic domains. The approach is also more robust to regularization coefficient selection and generalizes to environments beyond contextual bandits.

a4477233e08d5029452bb599cab61b1e20f53afe.title: Restoration-Degradation Beyond Linear Diffusions: A Non-Asymptotic Analysis For DDIM-Type Samplers
a4477233e08d5029452bb599cab61b1e20f53afe.research_question: How can deterministic samplers for diffusion generative models, particularly those of the DDIM-type, be theoretically analyzed in the non-asymptotic regime, and can a general operational framework be developed for such samplers beyond linear diffusions?
a4477233e08d5029452bb599cab61b1e20f53afe.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a new operational interpretation of deterministic sampling, decomposing each step into restoration and degradation phases, can be extended to general, non-linear forward processes, and that under mild smoothness assumptions on the data distribution, deterministic DDIM-type samplers can be shown to converge polynomially to the true data distribution in a non-asymptotic sense.
a4477233e08d5029452bb599cab61b1e20f53afe.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed for the non-asymptotic analysis of deterministic samplers in diffusion generative models. The approach introduces an operational interpretation where each step of the probability flow ODE is decomposed into two phases: a restoration step, which performs gradient ascent on the conditional log-likelihood at a previous time, and a degradation step, which simulates the forward process using noise directed towards the current iterate. This framework generalizes DDIM-type samplers to arbitrary, potentially non-linear, forward processes by defining explicit restoration and degradation operators. The restoration operator is formalized as a single gradient ascent step with a carefully chosen learning rate, and the degradation operator is implemented as an Euler-Maruyama discretization of the forward SDE, using simulated rather than fresh noise. The method also allows for interpolation between deterministic and stochastic sampling by introducing a parameter that controls the mixture of simulated and fresh noise in the degradation phase.
a4477233e08d5029452bb599cab61b1e20f53afe.experiment_details: The proposed analysis will be validated through theoretical experiments involving general forward processes, including the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process as a concrete example. Theoretical results will be derived under mild smoothness and Lipschitz assumptions on the drift and diffusion coefficients, as well as on the score function of the data distribution. The convergence of the deterministic sampler will be evaluated using the KL divergence and total variation distance between the generated and true data distributions, with explicit polynomial bounds in terms of problem parameters. Baseline comparisons will include standard Euler discretization of the probability flow ODE and stochastic samplers analyzed in prior work. The analysis will also address the impact of initialization at the stationary distribution versus the terminal distribution of the forward process.
a4477233e08d5029452bb599cab61b1e20f53afe.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first non-asymptotic, polynomial convergence guarantees for deterministic DDIM-type samplers under general, non-linear forward processes. The operational interpretation of deterministic sampling as a combination of restoration and degradation steps is novel and extends the applicability of DDIM-type methods beyond linear diffusions. The framework provides explicit, polynomially-bounded error guarantees under mild assumptions, and establishes a deterministic analogue to recent non-asymptotic analyses of stochastic samplers. Additionally, the approach enables a unified treatment of both deterministic and stochastic sampling through a tunable parameter, offering new insights into the theoretical properties and practical implementation of diffusion-based generative models.

a44c6a992a0dc8e0ce3d190fd6d10dfb2d31bef2.title: RoomEditor++: A Parameter-Sharing Diffusion Architecture for High-Fidelity Furniture Synthesis
a44c6a992a0dc8e0ce3d190fd6d10dfb2d31bef2.research_question: How can high-fidelity virtual furniture synthesis be achieved in indoor scenes, ensuring geometric coherence, visual realism, and background integrity, especially given the scarcity of reproducible benchmarks and the limitations of existing image composition methods?
a44c6a992a0dc8e0ce3d190fd6d10dfb2d31bef2.hypothesis: A parameter-sharing dual diffusion backbone architecture, compatible with both U-Net and DiT models, will enforce aligned feature representations between reference and background images, thereby facilitating precise geometric transformations, texture preservation, and seamless integration for high-fidelity furniture synthesis. Furthermore, constructing a large-scale, practice-oriented benchmark dataset will enable robust training and evaluation under real-world conditions.
a44c6a992a0dc8e0ce3d190fd6d10dfb2d31bef2.proposed_method: A novel diffusion-based architecture, RoomEditor++, will be developed, featuring a parameter-sharing dual diffusion backbone that unifies feature extraction and inpainting processes for both reference and background images. The architecture will be compatible with both U-Net and DiT backbones, enabling flexible deployment. The parameter-sharing mechanism will enforce consistent feature representations, with reference features injected into background features via a mixture attention module at each diffusion block. This approach will eliminate the feature domain gap inherent in dual-branch methods and enable the model to learn precise geometric transformations and texture preservation. Training will be conducted using a newly constructed, large-scale RoomBench++ dataset, which includes both real-world and professionally rendered home design scenes, with extensive mask and image augmentation to enhance robustness.
a44c6a992a0dc8e0ce3d190fd6d10dfb2d31bef2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the RoomBench++ dataset, which comprises 112,851 training pairs and 1,832 testing pairs, sourced from both real-world indoor videos and professional home design renderings. Evaluation will include both quantitative metrics (FID, SSIM, PSNR, LPIPS, CLIP-score, DINO-score) and qualitative assessments, including human preference studies measuring fidelity, harmony, and overall quality. Baseline comparisons will be made against state-of-the-art methods such as AnyDoor, MimicBrush, and DreamFuse, with and without fine-tuning on RoomBench++. Additional experiments will assess generalization to unseen scenes and object categories, including 3D-FUTURE, 3D-FRONT, and DreamBooth datasets. Ablation studies will evaluate the impact of parameter sharing and dataset composition.
a44c6a992a0dc8e0ce3d190fd6d10dfb2d31bef2.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a parameter-sharing dual diffusion backbone architecture for the first time in the context of furniture synthesis, unifying feature extraction and inpainting for reference and background images. The RoomBench++ dataset is constructed as a comprehensive, open-source benchmark merging real-scene and realistic-scene data, enabling reproducible research and robust evaluation. The unified architecture is compatible with both U-Net and DiT backbones, and the parameter-sharing mechanism is shown to improve feature consistency and synthesis quality over prior dual-branch and encoder-based methods. Extensive experiments will demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, strong generalization to unseen scenes, and robustness without task-specific fine-tuning.

a450c30b01dcfdd5a4570dcf410d259b5253d620.title: Advancing Prompt-Based Methods for Replay-Independent General Continual Learning
a450c30b01dcfdd5a4570dcf410d259b5253d620.research_question: How can prompt-based methods be advanced to enable effective, replay-independent general continual learning (GCL) in online data streams with blurry task boundaries, while mitigating poor initialization, limited generalizability, and catastrophic forgetting?
a450c30b01dcfdd5a4570dcf410d259b5253d620.hypothesis: Integrating a forgetting-aware initial session adaptation for prompt parameters and a non-parametric logit masking strategy for output layers will significantly improve the learning efficiency, generalizability, and knowledge retention of prompt-based continual learning models in GCL settings, even without replay buffers.
a450c30b01dcfdd5a4570dcf410d259b5253d620.proposed_method: A novel framework, MISA (Mask and Initial Session Adaption), will be developed to enhance prompt-based continual learning. The first component, forgetting-aware initial session adaptation (ISA), will warm up prompt parameters using pretraining data, employing a supervised objective and a forgetting-aware minimization (FAM) technique inspired by sharpness-aware minimization. FAM will simulate distribution shifts by splitting pretraining data into in-distribution and out-of-distribution subsets, using gradients from the latter to guide the optimization towards flat, forget-resistant minima. Prompt augmentation via a shallow MLP will increase parameter space complexity, further facilitating robust initialization. The second component, non-parametric logit masking, will dynamically mask output logits at the batch or session level to prevent interference between old and new class knowledge, leveraging the stable representation space of a frozen pretrained backbone. These components are designed to be plug-and-play, hyperparameter-free, and compatible with various prompt-based methods.
a450c30b01dcfdd5a4570dcf410d259b5253d620.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three representative datasets: CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, and ImageNet-R, following the Si-Blurry GCL protocol with a disjoint class ratio of 50% and blurry sample ratio of 10%, across five sessions. The evaluation will use metrics such as average accuracy (AUC), final accuracy (ALast), and average forgetting (FLast), ensuring no test-time oracle and constant memory constraints. Baselines will include replay-based methods (ER, DER++, ER-ACE, Rainbow Memory, CLIB), regularization-based methods (LwF, EWC), and prompt-based methods (L2P, DualPrompt, MVP), all using a frozen pretrained ViT backbone. Ablation studies will assess the contributions of ISA-FAM and logit masking, and additional analyses will test transferability to other prompt-based methods, robustness to knowledge overlap, and resource overheads. Five independent runs will be performed for statistical reliability.
a450c30b01dcfdd5a4570dcf410d259b5253d620.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a forgetting-aware initial session adaptation that proactively prevents future forgetting and enhances prompt generalizability to distribution shifts, a non-parametric logit masking strategy that effectively mitigates catastrophic forgetting in output layers, and a plug-in, replay-independent, hyperparameter-free design suitable for a wide range of prompt-based continual learning methods. The method demonstrates substantial and robust performance improvements over state-of-the-art baselines, particularly in challenging GCL scenarios without replay buffers, and sets a new benchmark for general continual learning.

a45c73fb27aab33cc4f21c17b894c39eb25a0cd7.title: Statistical Query Hardness of Multiclass Linear Classification with Random Classification Noise
a45c73fb27aab33cc4f21c17b894c39eb25a0cd7.research_question: What is the computational complexity of multiclass linear classification in the distribution-free PAC model in the presence of random classification noise, particularly when the number of labels is three or more, and can efficient algorithms be developed in the statistical query (SQ) model for this setting?
a45c73fb27aab33cc4f21c17b894c39eb25a0cd7.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that multiclass linear classification with random classification noise becomes computationally hard in the statistical query model for three or more classes, even when the noise matrix is known and the separation is constant, and that no efficient SQ algorithm exists for achieving optimal or even approximate error in this setting.
a45c73fb27aab33cc4f21c17b894c39eb25a0cd7.proposed_method: The proposed research will establish super-polynomial lower bounds for the statistical query (SQ) complexity of multiclass linear classification (MLC) with random classification noise (RCN). The approach involves reducing the learning problem to a carefully constructed hypothesis testing problem, where distinguishing between structured label distributions and random label assignments is provably hard in the SQ model. Hard distributions will be constructed by leveraging the hidden direction distribution framework and moment-matching techniques, ensuring that the conditional label distributions satisfy specific convex combination and separation properties. The methodology will also use the Veronese mapping to relate multiclass polynomial classification to linear classification in higher dimensions, and will design noise matrices and base distributions that make the problem SQ-hard even for approximate learning objectives.
a45c73fb27aab33cc4f21c17b894c39eb25a0cd7.experiment_details: Theoretical experiments will be conducted by constructing families of hard distributions over high-dimensional spaces, parameterized by the number of classes, separation in the noise matrix, and the degree of polynomial classifiers. The analysis will use the statistical query dimension framework to quantify the number of queries and tolerance required for any SQ algorithm to succeed. Lower bounds will be established for various regimes, including three labels with constant separation, larger numbers of labels with small separation, and scenarios where even beating the trivial hypothesis is hard. Theoretical evaluation metrics include the minimum error achievable by any hypothesis, the separation parameter of the noise matrix, and the SQ query complexity (number and tolerance of queries). Baselines for comparison are existing polynomial-time algorithms for binary classification with RCN and known reductions for the realizable setting.
a45c73fb27aab33cc4f21c17b894c39eb25a0cd7.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first super-polynomial SQ lower bounds for multiclass linear classification with random classification noise, demonstrating a dramatic increase in computational complexity when moving from binary to multiclass settings. The construction of hard distributions and noise matrices is novel in that it applies advanced moment-matching and hidden direction techniques to the multiclass setting, and the results hold even for known noise matrices and constant separation. The work also extends SQ-hardness to approximate learning objectives and shows hardness for low-degree polynomial tests, providing strong evidence that efficient SQ algorithms are unlikely to exist for these problems.

a471394a503970eb28da2ce64c4d1473844bdda6.title: The Promise of RL for Autoregressive Image Editing
a471394a503970eb28da2ce64c4d1473844bdda6.research_question: What is the most effective unified end-to-end approach for text-guided image editing that can handle both simple and complex edits, and how do different learning paradigms such as supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and chain-of-thought reasoning impact performance in this domain?
a471394a503970eb28da2ce64c4d1473844bdda6.hypothesis: Reinforcement learning, when applied as a post-training stage to a strong autoregressive multimodal model and combined with a large multimodal language model (MLLM)-based verifier, will significantly improve the quality and controllability of text-guided image editing across both simple and complex tasks, outperforming supervised fine-tuning and chain-of-thought reasoning approaches.
a471394a503970eb28da2ce64c4d1473844bdda6.proposed_method: A unified autoregressive multimodal model will be developed for text-guided image editing, leveraging a causal transformer architecture that jointly processes visual and textual tokens. The training pipeline will consist of three stages: (1) supervised fine-tuning (SFT) using next-token prediction on interleaved image-text sequences with paired original and edited images and edit instructions; (2) reinforcement learning (RL) post-training using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), where the model is optimized to maximize edit quality as judged by a large MLLM-based verifier (e.g., Qwen2.5-VL-72B), which scores edits based on success, over-editing, naturalness, and artifacts; and (3) optional chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning supervision, where the model is trained to generate explicit step-by-step reasoning traces before producing the edited image. The RL stage utilizes a policy gradient approach with a KL-divergence penalty to maintain training stability and leverages the verifier's reward signal for effective optimization.
a471394a503970eb28da2ce64c4d1473844bdda6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Emu3-8B autoregressive multimodal model as the base architecture. The training datasets will include both simple and complex edit types: simple edits from OmniEdit (750K samples) and complex edits from datasets such as HumanEdit, MagicBrush, VisMin, Aurora-Kubric, Aurora-ActionGenome, and SomethingSomething-v2, with upsampling to ensure sufficient representation of complex edits. The evaluation will be performed on a diverse suite of benchmarks, including OmniEdit, EmuEdit, MagicBrush, Aurora, VisMin, and I2EBench, covering both in-distribution and out-of-distribution scenarios. Baselines will include state-of-the-art diffusion-based models (MagicBrush, InstructPix2Pix, Aurora, Omnigen) and the autoregressive EditAR model. The primary evaluation metric will be VIEScore, which assesses edit success, over-editing, naturalness, and artifacts, using GPT4o-mini as the evaluation MLLM to avoid metric hacking. RL post-training will be scaled up to 2000 steps and 300K samples for the best-performing configuration. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of data composition, training paradigms, and the quality of the MLLM verifier.
a471394a503970eb28da2ce64c4d1473844bdda6.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first systematic and controlled comparison of supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and chain-of-thought reasoning for text-guided image editing within a unified autoregressive framework. A novel RL-based post-training paradigm is developed for autoregressive image editing models, leveraging a large MLLM-based verifier for reward computation. The approach demonstrates that RL post-training with balanced simple and complex data leads to significant improvements over both SFT and state-of-the-art baselines, achieving competitive or superior results with substantially less training data. The research also provides new insights into the timing and utility of complex edit data and chain-of-thought supervision, revealing that complex edits are best introduced during RL rather than SFT, and that CoT reasoning does not consistently improve editing performance in current autoregressive models.

a473e591ce54c9c631207c3d8a36a783062b51d0.title: Evolution of Information in Interactive Decision Making: A Case Study for Multi-Armed Bandits
a473e591ce54c9c631207c3d8a36a783062b51d0.research_question: How does information evolve over time in interactive decision-making environments, specifically in the context of stochastic multi-armed bandit problems with a unique optimal arm? What are the fundamental relationships and possible separations between learning success probability and mutual information accumulation in such interactive settings?
a473e591ce54c9c631207c3d8a36a783062b51d0.hypothesis: The evolution of mutual information and learning success probability in interactive multi-armed bandit problems exhibits distinct growth phases and can be fundamentally decoupled, such that achieving optimal learning does not necessarily require maximizing information gain.
a473e591ce54c9c631207c3d8a36a783062b51d0.proposed_method: A detailed theoretical and algorithmic investigation will be conducted on a stylized stochastic multi-armed bandit problem where one arm is uniformly better than the others by a fixed margin. The methodology involves characterizing the optimal success probability and mutual information as functions of time, using both achievability and converse arguments. A sequential probability ratio test-based algorithm will be developed to strategically sample arms, leveraging properties of biased random walks to efficiently eliminate suboptimal arms. For converse results, novel reduction schemes and information-theoretic techniques, including change-of-divergence arguments and leveraging upper bounds on success probability to constrain mutual information, will be introduced. The approach will analyze the interplay between interactive and non-interactive sampling, and identify regimes where mutual information and learning success probability diverge.
a473e591ce54c9c631207c3d8a36a783062b51d0.experiment_details: Theoretical results will be validated through rigorous mathematical analysis and, where appropriate, algorithmic simulations. The primary 'dataset' is the theoretical instance of n-armed bandits with Bernoulli rewards parameterized by a fixed gap Δ, with the optimal arm chosen uniformly at random. Baseline comparisons will include non-interactive sampling strategies and classical bandit algorithms such as median elimination. Evaluation metrics will focus on the optimal success probability of identifying the best arm and the mutual information accumulated over t rounds. Key experimental setups will include varying the time horizon t, the number of arms n, and the gap parameter Δ to observe phase transitions in information growth and learning probability.
a473e591ce54c9c631207c3d8a36a783062b51d0.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a complete and tight characterization of the evolution of mutual information and success probability in interactive multi-armed bandit settings, revealing previously unobserved phase transitions (linear, quadratic, and saturation regimes) in information accumulation. It demonstrates, for the first time, a fundamental decoupling between optimal learning and information gain, showing that maximizing mutual information is not necessary for optimal learning. The proposed converse techniques, including the reduction from small to large time horizons and the reversal of typical information-theoretic inequalities, represent new tools for analyzing interactive decision-making. These results challenge the sufficiency of mutual information as a universal measure for learning limits in interactive environments and provide new insights and methods for the broader study of interactive learning and information theory.

a483ff9557f29d21fe780b3dd969a037a3ffc3ed.title: Uni-ControlNet: All-in-One Control to Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
a483ff9557f29d21fe780b3dd969a037a3ffc3ed.research_question: How can text-to-image diffusion models be enhanced to allow efficient, unified, and composable control using multiple types of local and global conditioning signals, without incurring significant increases in fine-tuning cost or model size?
a483ff9557f29d21fe780b3dd969a037a3ffc3ed.hypothesis: A unified adapter-based framework that categorizes control signals into local and global types and employs only two specialized adapters can enable efficient, composable, and high-quality control over pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models, outperforming existing methods that require separate adapters for each condition.
a483ff9557f29d21fe780b3dd969a037a3ffc3ed.proposed_method: A unified framework, Uni-ControlNet, is proposed to extend pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models (e.g., Stable Diffusion) with composable control using both local (e.g., edge maps, depth maps, segmentation masks) and global (e.g., CLIP image embeddings) conditions. The method introduces two lightweight adapters: a local control adapter and a global control adapter. The local adapter employs a multi-scale condition injection strategy, extracting features from concatenated local condition maps at various resolutions and modulating the denoising process using feature denormalization inspired by SPADE. The global adapter projects CLIP image embeddings into conditional tokens, which are concatenated with text tokens to form an extended prompt, enabling joint conditioning through cross-attention. Both adapters are fine-tuned separately on frozen diffusion model weights, and their outputs are composable at inference without further joint training.
a483ff9557f29d21fe780b3dd969a037a3ffc3ed.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by fine-tuning the proposed adapters on 10 million text-image pairs from the LAION dataset for one epoch, using the AdamW optimizer and resizing all inputs to 512x512 pixels. Seven local conditions (Canny, MLSD, HED, sketch, Openpose, depth, segmentation) and one global condition (CLIP image embedding) will be used for control. Baseline comparisons will include ControlNet, GLIGEN, and T2I-Adapter, with evaluations performed on the COCO 2017 validation set. Evaluation metrics will include FID for image quality, SSIM/mAP/MSE/mIoU/CLIPScore for controllability, and qualitative visualizations for composability. Ablation studies will assess different injection and training strategies.
a483ff9557f29d21fe780b3dd969a037a3ffc3ed.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified framework that requires only two adapters—one for all local controls and one for all global controls—regardless of the number of conditions, significantly reducing fine-tuning cost and model size. The method enables flexible and composable integration of multiple control signals within a single model, overcoming the limitations of prior works that require separate adapters per condition and struggle with composability. The multi-scale condition injection and extended prompt strategies further enhance controllability and generation fidelity, establishing new state-of-the-art performance in both quantitative and qualitative evaluations.

a48c817f4a30bb78618090ee820606dcf28d95ec.title: Image Inpainting via Tractable Steering of Diffusion Models
a48c817f4a30bb78618090ee820606dcf28d95ec.research_question: How can image inpainting be improved by leveraging tractable probabilistic models to provide more effective and efficient guidance for diffusion models under complex constraints, without requiring task-specific fine-tuning or supervised training?
a48c817f4a30bb78618090ee820606dcf28d95ec.hypothesis: Integrating tractable probabilistic models, specifically Probabilistic Circuits, to steer the denoising process of diffusion models will yield inpainted images with higher semantic coherence and fidelity to constraints, while maintaining computational efficiency.
a48c817f4a30bb78618090ee820606dcf28d95ec.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed that combines the generative power of diffusion models with the exact conditional inference capabilities of tractable probabilistic models (TPMs), specifically Probabilistic Circuits (PCs). At each denoising step of the diffusion process, the conditional distribution over the inpainted image will be computed both from the diffusion model and the TPM, and these distributions will be merged using a weighted geometric mean of their logits. For high-resolution images, a VQ-GAN-based encoder-decoder will be used to map images to a discrete latent space, where a PC is trained to model the latent distribution, and the guidance is performed in this space before decoding back to pixels. An efficient forward-backward algorithm will be implemented to compute the required conditional probabilities from the PC in linear time with respect to model size. The method will support both hard and soft constraints, enabling not only inpainting but also more general controlled image generation tasks.
a48c817f4a30bb78618090ee820606dcf28d95ec.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three high-resolution natural image datasets: CelebA-HQ, ImageNet, and LSUN-Bedroom. Seven challenging mask types will be used to reveal only 5-20% of the original image, testing the ability to generate semantically consistent inpainted results. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art diffusion-based inpainting algorithms such as CoPaint, RePaint, DDNM, DDRM, DPS, and Resampling. Evaluation metrics will include the average LPIPS perceptual similarity score (lower is better), as well as qualitative visual comparisons and user studies. The computational overhead of the proposed method will be measured, and ablation studies will be performed to analyze the effect of the number of denoising steps guided by the PC.
a48c817f4a30bb78618090ee820606dcf28d95ec.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to demonstrate the use of tractable probabilistic models for controlling and constraining the generation process of high-resolution natural images in diffusion models. The method introduces a novel integration of Probabilistic Circuits with diffusion models, enabling exact and efficient computation of constrained posteriors for inpainting and more general controlled generation tasks. The approach achieves competitive or superior sample quality compared to state-of-the-art baselines, with only a modest computational overhead. Additionally, the framework supports arbitrary independent soft-evidence constraints, opening new avenues for complex controlled image generation such as semantic fusion from multiple reference images.

a492f15eae50854fcf3b03a4096f04f87cd58493.title: On the Impact of Performative Risk Minimization for Binary Random Variables
a492f15eae50854fcf3b03a4096f04f87cd58493.research_question: What are the broader impacts of performative risk minimization (PRM) on model predictions and the underlying data distribution, particularly in sequential settings with binary random variables and linear performative shifts?
a492f15eae50854fcf3b03a4096f04f87cd58493.hypothesis: Performative risk minimization, while optimizing for accuracy under distribution shifts, can introduce systematic biases and nontrivial shifts in the underlying data distribution, potentially leading to amplified or unintended side effects compared to standard risk minimization.
a492f15eae50854fcf3b03a4096f04f87cd58493.proposed_method: A sequential performative prediction framework will be developed, focusing on binary random variables whose distributions are influenced by deployed model predictions through a linear performative response. Two quantitative impact measures will be formulated: bias (the deviation of model predictions from the true mean) and mean shift (the deviation of the data distribution mean under PRM from its non-performative counterpart). Both full information (where all parameters are known) and partial information (where parameters must be estimated) settings will be analyzed. Explicit formulas for PRM solutions and impact measures will be derived for the full information case, while performative-aware statistical estimators and simulation-based approaches will be used under partial information. Theoretical analysis will be complemented by simulations to study both single-period and infinite-horizon (sequential) deployments.
a492f15eae50854fcf3b03a4096f04f87cd58493.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic datasets of binary random variables, parameterized by controllable means and performative response coefficients. Both slow and rapid deployment scenarios will be considered, corresponding to different adaptation speeds of the environment to model predictions. Baseline comparisons will include standard risk minimization (which ignores performativity) and naive estimators that do not account for data shifts. Evaluation metrics will include the proposed bias and mean shift measures, as well as mean squared error (MSE) on the induced distributions. Experiments will analyze both perfect information and learning scenarios, with statistical estimators trained on observed samples and reinforcement learning-based exploration for parameter estimation.
a492f15eae50854fcf3b03a4096f04f87cd58493.novelty_claims: The proposed research initiates a systematic analysis of the downstream impacts of performative risk minimization beyond test-time accuracy, introducing explicit, theoretically grounded measures of bias and mean shift in sequential settings. The approach enables closed-form characterization of long-term dynamics under PRM, contrasting them with standard risk minimization and naive approaches. The work provides new insights into how PRM can amplify or mitigate distributional shifts and prediction biases, and offers practical statistical estimators and simulation protocols for settings with incomplete information. This comprehensive analysis fills a gap in understanding the unintended consequences of performative optimization in social and strategic environments.

a4a2326cf7f16ea0988ffc65eabf48ffe47c432f.title: Scalable Transformer for PDE Surrogate Modeling
a4a2326cf7f16ea0988ffc65eabf48ffe47c432f.research_question: How can surrogate modeling of partial differential equations (PDEs) be made more scalable and efficient, particularly for high-dimensional problems with large discretization grids, while maintaining or improving accuracy and stability compared to existing neural operator and Transformer-based approaches?
a4a2326cf7f16ea0988ffc65eabf48ffe47c432f.hypothesis: A Transformer-based surrogate modeling framework that employs an axial factorized kernel integral and learnable projection operators can achieve improved computational efficiency and numerical stability for high-dimensional PDE problems, without sacrificing predictive accuracy relative to state-of-the-art models.
a4a2326cf7f16ea0988ffc65eabf48ffe47c432f.proposed_method: A novel Transformer architecture is introduced for PDE surrogate modeling, leveraging an axial factorized kernel integral attention mechanism. The approach begins by projecting the high-dimensional input function into multiple sub-functions, each defined on a one-dimensional domain, using a set of learnable integral operators. For each spatial axis, a learnable projection operator computes queries and keys via pointwise neural networks and mean pooling, followed by the application of Rotary Positional Encoding to modulate the dot-product kernel with relative position. The resulting axial kernels are used to compute attention along each axis independently, and the value tensor is iteratively updated through tensor-matrix products along all axes. The output is then passed through a feedforward network and instance normalization, with residual connections to stabilize training. The method further incorporates training techniques such as latent marching and pushforward training to mitigate error accumulation in time-dependent PDEs.
a4a2326cf7f16ea0988ffc65eabf48ffe47c432f.experiment_details: The proposed method will be evaluated on several challenging PDE benchmark problems, including 2D Kolmogorov flow (256×256 grid), 3D isotropic turbulence (60×60×60 grid), 3D smoke buoyancy (64×64×64 grid), and 2D Darcy flow. Datasets are generated using established numerical solvers (e.g., pseudo-spectral methods, phiflow) with appropriate boundary and initial conditions. Baseline comparisons will include Fourier Neural Operator (FNO), Factorized FNO (F-FNO), Dilated ResNet (Dil-ResNet), and Galerkin Transformer. Models will be trained using both latent marching with pushforward and autoregressive protocols, and evaluated using relative L2 norm errors (averaged and final frame), inference time, and parameter count. Ablation studies will compare the proposed factorized attention to full (linear) attention in terms of accuracy, stability, and computational cost, with additional analysis of attention matrix spectra.
a4a2326cf7f16ea0988ffc65eabf48ffe47c432f.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a scalable, axial factorized kernel attention mechanism for Transformers in PDE surrogate modeling, enabling efficient and stable handling of high-dimensional, large-grid problems. The learnable projection operator decomposes the input function into single-dimensional sub-functions, facilitating low-rank, axis-wise attention and mitigating the curse of dimensionality. The method achieves competitive or superior accuracy and efficiency compared to state-of-the-art neural operator and Transformer-based models, and demonstrates improved stability and computational performance in both training and inference. The factorized attention scheme provides a principled, low-rank surrogate for full attention, with empirical evidence of its effectiveness and efficiency.

a4b91cfdf4fab1e2f466b026f7b5245298ad53e6.title: UniMC: Taming Diffusion Transformer for Unified Keypoint-Guided Multi-Class Image Generation
a4b91cfdf4fab1e2f466b026f7b5245298ad53e6.research_question: How can keypoint-guided image generation be unified and improved to handle multi-class, multi-instance scenarios involving both humans and animals, particularly under conditions of heavy occlusion and diverse object classes?
a4b91cfdf4fab1e2f466b026f7b5245298ad53e6.hypothesis: A unified Diffusion Transformer-based framework that encodes keypoint, class, and bounding box information as compact tokens, combined with a large-scale, richly annotated dataset covering both humans and animals, will enable more accurate, controllable, and high-quality multi-class image generation than existing skeleton-based or class-specific methods.
a4b91cfdf4fab1e2f466b026f7b5245298ad53e6.proposed_method: A unified framework, termed UNIMC, will be developed based on a Diffusion Transformer (DiT) backbone to generate images conditioned on keypoint-level, instance-level, and semantic annotations for both humans and animals. The method will replace traditional skeleton-image conditioning with a compact token-based approach, where each instance is represented by its class name, bounding box, and keypoint coordinates. A unified keypoint encoder will map keypoints from different species into a shared representation space, eliminating the need for separate encoders and improving efficiency. A timestep-aware keypoint modulator will inject these keypoint tokens into the DiT generator at various layers, using self-attention and adaptive normalization to enable fine-grained, per-instance control throughout the diffusion process. The framework will be trained end-to-end, leveraging both global text prompts and per-instance conditions.
a4b91cfdf4fab1e2f466b026f7b5245298ad53e6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a newly constructed dataset, HAIG-2.9M, which comprises 786,000 images and 2.9 million instances across 31 species classes (including both humans and animals), with comprehensive annotations such as keypoints, bounding boxes, and fine-grained captions. Baselines will include leading keypoint-guided generation methods such as ControlNet (skeleton-image-based), GLIGEN (keypoint-coordinate-based), and the base DiT model (PIXART-α). Evaluation metrics will span image quality (FID, KID), text-image alignment (CLIP score), class accuracy (using YOLO-World for detection and IoU matching), and pose accuracy (using DWPose and ViTPose++H for humans and animals, respectively, with AP scores). Additional ablation studies will assess the impact of different conditioning forms, encoder architectures, and training datasets (COCO, APT36K, their combination, and HAIG-2.9M). Human preference studies and qualitative analyses will further validate controllability and realism.
a4b91cfdf4fab1e2f466b026f7b5245298ad53e6.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified, class- and instance-aware keypoint encoding and modulation strategy that overcomes the class binding and instance binding confusion inherent in skeleton-based conditioning. It presents the first large-scale, high-quality dataset (HAIG-2.9M) with joint keypoint-level, instance-level, and dense semantic annotations for both humans and animals, enabling comprehensive evaluation and training for multi-class, multi-instance image generation. The method's unified keypoint encoder and timestep-aware modulator are claimed to provide superior controllability, efficiency, and generalization across diverse object classes, surpassing previous approaches in both quantitative and qualitative benchmarks.

a4c921bdef167ae54cc3a40643e6e3ed13d49a61.title: Safety-Tuned LLaMAs: Lessons From Improving the Safety of Large Language Models that Follow Instructions
a4c921bdef167ae54cc3a40643e6e3ed13d49a61.research_question: How can the safety of large instruction-following language models be improved without significantly compromising their helpfulness and general capabilities, and what are the trade-offs involved in balancing safety and helpfulness during instruction fine-tuning?
a4c921bdef167ae54cc3a40643e6e3ed13d49a61.hypothesis: Incorporating a small proportion of carefully curated safety-focused instruction-response examples into the instruction fine-tuning process of large language models will substantially improve their safety with minimal or no loss in general performance, but excessive safety data may lead to overcautious or exaggerated safety behaviors.
a4c921bdef167ae54cc3a40643e6e3ed13d49a61.proposed_method: A new methodology will be developed to augment standard instruction-tuning datasets with varying quantities of safety-focused instruction-response pairs. Safety data will be constructed by transforming red-teaming questions into imperative instructions and generating safe refusal responses using a strong language model, followed by manual review for appropriateness. Several versions of large language models (e.g., LLaMA 7B, LLaMA 13B, Falcon 7B) will be fine-tuned using low-rank adaptation (LoRA) for multiple epochs, with different proportions of safety data (ranging from 0.5% to 10% of the total training set) mixed into a base of general-purpose instructions. The impact of prompt format (instruction vs. question) will also be systematically studied to determine its effect on model safety.
a4c921bdef167ae54cc3a40643e6e3ed13d49a61.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a suite of safety evaluation datasets targeting malicious, controversial, hateful, and physically unsafe instructions, as well as a dataset probing for exaggerated safety (over-refusal of benign prompts). General capabilities will be assessed using held-out general-purpose instructions and standard benchmarks such as AlpacaEval, PIQA, BoolQ, and OpenBookQA. Safety will be measured using an automated harmfulness reward model trained on human-annotated toxicity scores, OpenAI's content moderation API, and manual annotation of model responses. Multiple baselines will be compared, including models with no safety data, models with varying amounts of safety data, and models trained on different prompt formats. The effect of safety tuning on both harmfulness reduction and general task performance will be quantified.
a4c921bdef167ae54cc3a40643e6e3ed13d49a61.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a systematic approach for improving safety in instruction-following language models using minimal but targeted safety data, demonstrating that even a small fraction of safety examples can yield substantial safety gains. The methodology includes the creation of new safety evaluation datasets and a reproducible evaluation pipeline. The study will also reveal and quantify the phenomenon of exaggerated safety, where excessive safety tuning leads to over-refusal of benign prompts, and will provide insights into the importance of prompt format in safety tuning. This work aims to establish practical guidelines for balancing helpfulness and harmlessness in open-source language model development.

a4f834d52e78dbec1b5f0a871d9ba6f5f4028ba5.title: Men Also Do Laundry: Multi-Attribute Bias Amplification
a4f834d52e78dbec1b5f0a871d9ba6f5f4028ba5.research_question: How can bias amplification in machine learning models be more accurately measured and mitigated when considering multiple co-occurring attributes, rather than only single attributes, in large-scale visual datasets?
a4f834d52e78dbec1b5f0a871d9ba6f5f4028ba5.hypothesis: Current bias amplification metrics that focus solely on single attributes underestimate the true extent of bias amplification in multi-label classification tasks, and mitigation methods targeting single-attribute bias may inadvertently increase bias with respect to multiple attributes. A new metric that accounts for multi-attribute combinations will provide a more comprehensive and interpretable measure of bias amplification.
a4f834d52e78dbec1b5f0a871d9ba6f5f4028ba5.proposed_method: A novel metric, Multi-Attribute Bias Amplification, will be developed to quantify bias amplification arising from both single and multiple attribute combinations in multi-label classification settings.
