The metric will extend existing co-occurrence-based approaches by evaluating the difference in attribute-group co-occurrence frequencies between training data and model predictions, iterating over all possible attribute sets (including sets with more than one attribute). Both undirected and directional versions of the metric will be defined, capturing bias amplification from group to attribute prediction and vice versa, and using absolute differences to avoid cancellation of positive and negative values. The metric will also report variance to indicate whether amplification is uniform across attribute-group pairs, and will be designed to have a clear ideal value (zero) for interpretability.
a4f834d52e78dbec1b5f0a871d9ba6f5f4028ba5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard multi-label visual datasets including COCO, imSitu, and CelebA, focusing on group membership attributes such as gender expression and hair color, and a variety of object, verb, and physical characteristic attributes. Models will be trained using ResNet-50 architectures, with balanced and unbalanced versions of the datasets (balancing achieved via oversampling for single attributes). The proposed metric will be compared against existing single-attribute bias amplification metrics. Multiple bias mitigation methods—including oversampling, corpus-level constraints, adversarial debiasing, data repair, and domain-independent training—will be benchmarked using both the new and existing metrics. Evaluation will include mean average precision (mAP), bias amplification scores (raw, absolute, and variance), and analysis of amplification across different attribute group sizes.
a4f834d52e78dbec1b5f0a871d9ba6f5f4028ba5.novelty_claims: The proposed metric is the first to systematically measure and analyze bias amplification with respect to multiple co-occurring attributes in multi-label classification. It addresses key shortcomings of existing metrics by preventing cancellation of positive and negative bias values and providing a more interpretable, absolute measure with a clear ideal value. The research will also demonstrate that mitigation methods designed for single-attribute bias can inadvertently increase multi-attribute bias amplification, highlighting the necessity of multi-attribute-aware evaluation and mitigation strategies. This work will provide a more nuanced and accurate characterization of model-induced bias, informing future fairness interventions.

a4fb9ea9f9e8b0a4995512f12f84e4e01c0cc50e.title: Auditing f-Differential Privacy in One Run
a4fb9ea9f9e8b0a4995512f12f84e4e01c0cc50e.research_question: How can empirical auditing of privacy-preserving mechanisms be made both computationally efficient and more accurate in estimating differential privacy guarantees, particularly in large-scale machine learning settings?
a4fb9ea9f9e8b0a4995512f12f84e4e01c0cc50e.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging the f-differential privacy (f-DP) curve, rather than traditional (ϵ,δ)-DP parameters, enables tighter and more accurate empirical privacy auditing in a single run, without sacrificing computational efficiency.
a4fb9ea9f9e8b0a4995512f12f84e4e01c0cc50e.proposed_method: A novel auditing procedure will be developed that requires only a single execution of the target privacy mechanism. The approach will utilize the f-DP curve, which generalizes traditional differential privacy by considering a family of trade-off functions rather than fixed (ϵ,δ) pairs. The method will involve injecting canary records into the dataset, running the privacy mechanism, and applying advanced membership inference and reconstruction attacks to assess privacy leakage. A recursive, numerically computable bound will be derived to tightly estimate the probability of adversarial success, leveraging properties of the f-DP trade-off functions. The audit will report the strongest privacy hypothesis not rejected by the observed adversarial success, yielding an empirical privacy curve.
a4fb9ea9f9e8b0a4995512f12f84e4e01c0cc50e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in both idealized and practical settings. The primary evaluation will use the Gaussian mechanism with varying noise levels and a range of canary set sizes (from 10^2 to 10^7). The auditing method will be compared against the state-of-the-art single-run auditing baseline (Steinke et al., 2023), using identical membership inference game setups to ensure fair comparison. Empirical privacy (empirical ϵ) will be the main metric, computed using the proposed f-DP-based audit and compared to both theoretical and baseline empirical bounds. Additional experiments will include differentially private stochastic gradient descent (DP-SGD) on real datasets, with evaluation focusing on the tightness and accuracy of the estimated privacy guarantees.
a4fb9ea9f9e8b0a4995512f12f84e4e01c0cc50e.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a computationally efficient, single-run auditing procedure that leverages the full f-DP curve for tighter empirical privacy estimation. The approach features a new recursive analysis for bounding adversarial guessing probabilities, improving over prior work by reducing the gap between true and empirically estimated privacy. The method generalizes to both membership inference and reconstruction attack settings, and the combination of trade-off functions with shuffling techniques is claimed to be novel and broadly applicable. Experimental results are expected to demonstrate significantly tighter privacy bounds than existing single-run auditing methods.

a5036f31f0e629dc661f120b8c3b1f374d479ab8.title: Visual Instruction Tuning
a5036f31f0e629dc661f120b8c3b1f374d479ab8.research_question: How can instruction tuning be extended to the multimodal domain to enable large language and vision models to follow complex, diverse visual-language instructions for general-purpose visual and language understanding tasks?
a5036f31f0e629dc661f120b8c3b1f374d479ab8.hypothesis: Instruction tuning large multimodal models using high-quality, machine-generated language-image instruction-following data will significantly improve their ability to follow complex instructions, reason about visual content, and achieve state-of-the-art performance on multimodal benchmarks.
a5036f31f0e629dc661f120b8c3b1f374d479ab8.proposed_method: A novel pipeline will be developed to generate multimodal instruction-following data by leveraging language-only large language models (such as GPT-4) to convert image-text pairs into diverse instruction-response formats, including conversation, detailed description, and complex reasoning. The proposed multimodal model will connect a pre-trained vision encoder (e.g., CLIP ViT-L/14) with a language model (e.g., Vicuna) via a trainable projection layer that aligns visual features with the language embedding space. Training will proceed in two stages: an initial pre-training phase for feature alignment using a large set of image-text pairs reformatted into instruction-following data, followed by end-to-end fine-tuning on the generated multimodal instruction-following dataset. The model will be trained to predict assistant responses in an auto-regressive manner, grounded on both visual and textual instructions.
a5036f31f0e629dc661f120b8c3b1f374d479ab8.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate the proposed model on two primary tasks: multimodal chatbot capabilities and multimodal reasoning using the ScienceQA dataset. For the chatbot evaluation, two benchmarks will be constructed: LLaVA-Bench (COCO), using 30 images from COCO-Val-2014 with three types of questions per image, and LLaVA-Bench (In-the-Wild), using 24 diverse images with 60 manually curated questions. Baselines will include BLIP-2 and OpenFlamingo, with evaluation metrics based on GPT-4-judged helpfulness, relevance, accuracy, and detail. For ScienceQA, the model will be trained and evaluated on the official splits, with accuracy as the primary metric, and compared against state-of-the-art methods such as MM-CoT and LLaMA-Adapter. Ablation studies will examine the impact of different data types, model sizes, training strategies, and feature extraction layers.
a5036f31f0e629dc661f120b8c3b1f374d479ab8.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first systematic approach to visual instruction tuning by generating large-scale, high-quality multimodal instruction-following data using language-only LLMs. It presents a lightweight yet effective architecture for aligning vision and language representations and demonstrates, through extensive benchmarks, that instruction-tuned multimodal models can achieve state-of-the-art performance on complex visual reasoning tasks. Additionally, new evaluation benchmarks for multimodal instruction following are proposed, and the entire pipeline, including data, code, and models, will be made publicly available to facilitate future research.

a513a9a0a99a168c78edac6b53ef10f2e68819cf.title: Constrained Decision Transformer for Offline Safe Reinforcement Learning
a513a9a0a99a168c78edac6b53ef10f2e68819cf.research_question: How can a reinforcement learning agent be trained from offline datasets to learn policies that are both high-performing and satisfy safety constraints, while enabling dynamic adaptation to different constraint thresholds without retraining?
a513a9a0a99a168c78edac6b53ef10f2e68819cf.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a return- and constraint-conditioned sequential modeling approach, combined with targeted data augmentation and stochastic policy regularization, will enable the learning of adaptive, safe, and high-reward policies from offline datasets, and allow zero-shot adaptation to varying constraint thresholds.
a513a9a0a99a168c78edac6b53ef10f2e68819cf.proposed_method: A novel method, Constrained Decision Transformer (CDT), is proposed, building upon the Decision Transformer architecture by conditioning the policy on both target reward and cost returns. CDT incorporates a stochastic Gaussian policy representation with entropy regularization to improve robustness and prevent overfitting, as well as a Pareto frontier-oriented data augmentation technique that relabels infeasible target return pairs with safe, high-reward trajectories. The model is trained via supervised learning on offline datasets, minimizing negative log-likelihood loss with an entropy bonus, and uses a return-conditioned evaluation procedure that updates target returns at each step. Data augmentation ensures the agent learns to prioritize safety when conflicting target returns are presented, and outlier filtering is applied to mitigate the influence of anomalous trajectories.
a513a9a0a99a168c78edac6b53ef10f2e68819cf.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on several continuous control robot locomotion tasks (e.g., Ant-Run, Car-Circle, Drone-Run) using simulation environments from public benchmarks. Offline datasets are collected using a safe RL algorithm (CPPO) with varying cost thresholds to ensure diversity in cost and reward returns, and are further processed with grid-based down-sampling and outlier filtering. Baselines include state-of-the-art offline safe RL algorithms (CPQ, COptiDICE), Lagrangian-based variants (BCQ-Lag, BEAR-Lag), vanilla Decision Transformer with cost token, and behavior cloning approaches. Evaluation metrics are normalized reward and cost returns, with safety defined as cost below a fixed threshold. Zero-shot adaptation is assessed by varying the target cost threshold at deployment, and ablation studies are performed to isolate the impact of data augmentation, stochasticity, and entropy regularization.
a513a9a0a99a168c78edac6b53ef10f2e68819cf.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable zero-shot adaptation to arbitrary constraint thresholds in offline safe RL without retraining or solving new constrained optimizations. CDT introduces a multi-objective optimization perspective with the novel concept of ϵ-reducibility to characterize dataset and problem difficulty. Key innovations include the integration of a stochastic, entropy-regularized policy within a return- and constraint-conditioned Transformer, and a Pareto frontier-based data augmentation strategy for robust safety-performance trade-off learning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CDT outperforms strong baselines in both safety and reward, maintains generalization across constraint thresholds, and is robust to conflicting target returns.

a522efa0a479bcd368407576ba13d82ee011f581.title: RanPAC: Random Projections and Pre-trained Models for Continual Learning
a522efa0a479bcd368407576ba13d82ee011f581.research_question: How can continual learning be effectively achieved using pre-trained models, while avoiding catastrophic forgetting and maximizing performance across diverse continual learning scenarios without the need for rehearsal memory?
a522efa0a479bcd368407576ba13d82ee011f581.hypothesis: Introducing a frozen, training-free random projection layer with nonlinear activation between the pre-trained model's feature representations and a class-prototype-based output head will enhance linear separability, reduce distribution mismatch, and enable effective continual learning without catastrophic forgetting.
a522efa0a479bcd368407576ba13d82ee011f581.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a frozen random projection (RP) layer with nonlinear activation between the output of a pre-trained feature extractor (e.g., ViT, ResNet, CLIP) and a class-prototype-based classifier. The RP layer projects feature vectors to a higher-dimensional space using randomly initialized, untrained weights, followed by a nonlinearity (e.g., ReLU or squaring). Class prototypes are accumulated by averaging the projected features for each class, and second-order feature statistics are incorporated via a Gram matrix, which is updated incrementally. Classification is performed using a regularized closed-form solution based on the Gram matrix and class prototypes, with ridge regression to ensure stability. The method is model-agnostic and can be combined with parameter-efficient transfer learning (PETL) methods, where PETL parameters are adapted only during the first session and then frozen.
a522efa0a479bcd368407576ba13d82ee011f581.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of class-incremental and domain-incremental continual learning benchmarks, including CIFAR-100, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-A, CUB, OmniBenchmark, VTAB, Cars, CORe50, CDDB-Hard, and DomainNet. Pre-trained ViT-B/16 models (both self-supervised and supervised on ImageNet) will serve as the primary feature extractors, with additional tests on ResNet and CLIP backbones. Baselines will include prompting methods (e.g., L2P, DualPrompt, CODA-Prompt), fine-tuning strategies (e.g., SLCA), and class-prototype accumulation methods (e.g., NCM, ADaM). Evaluation metrics will focus on average accuracy across tasks and error rate reduction, with ablation studies to assess the impact of the RP layer, PETL adaptation, and second-order statistics. No rehearsal buffer will be used in any method, and all results will be compared to joint training upper bounds.
a522efa0a479bcd368407576ba13d82ee011f581.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to combine training-free random projections with nonlinear activation and class-prototype accumulation for continual learning with pre-trained models. It introduces a simple, efficient, and model-agnostic framework that avoids catastrophic forgetting without rehearsal memory. The approach leverages second-order feature statistics for decorrelation, enhancing class separability and calibration. Experimental results are expected to demonstrate substantial reductions in error rates (20%–62%) over previous methods on multiple benchmarks, while maintaining or exceeding joint training performance in several cases.

a531e9a328ad1488567fa68c15d5bf30bfb90c78.title: Fine-Tuning LLaMA for Multi-Stage Text Retrieval
a531e9a328ad1488567fa68c15d5bf30bfb90c78.research_question: How can state-of-the-art large language models be fine-tuned and integrated into multi-stage text retrieval pipelines to improve the effectiveness of both retrieval and reranking for passage and document retrieval tasks?
a531e9a328ad1488567fa68c15d5bf30bfb90c78.hypothesis: Fine-tuning large language models such as LLaMA as dense retrievers and pointwise rerankers will yield superior retrieval and reranking effectiveness compared to smaller models and previous approaches, particularly by leveraging their ability to handle longer contexts and represent entire documents holistically.
a531e9a328ad1488567fa68c15d5bf30bfb90c78.proposed_method: A multi-stage text retrieval pipeline will be developed by fine-tuning the LLaMA-2 model as both a dense retriever (RepLLaMA) and a pointwise reranker (RankLLaMA). The retriever will follow a bi-encoder architecture, encoding queries and documents into dense vector representations using the final layer representation of the end-of-sequence token. The similarity between query and document vectors will be computed via dot product and optimized using InfoNCE loss with hard negatives and in-batch negatives. The reranker will take query-document pairs as input, using a linear projection of the final token representation to produce a relevance score, optimized with contrastive loss using hard negatives. Both models will be trained with parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques such as LoRA, and will be designed to handle long input sequences (up to 4096 tokens), allowing for holistic document representations without segmentation.
a531e9a328ad1488567fa68c15d5bf30bfb90c78.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the MS MARCO passage and document ranking datasets, using the official training splits for model training and the development splits for evaluation. Hard negatives will be sampled from both sparse (BM25) and dense (CoCondenser) retrieval results to enhance training diversity. For passage retrieval, effectiveness will be measured using MRR@10 and nDCG@10 on MS MARCO dev and TREC DL19/DL20 benchmarks. For document retrieval, MRR@100 and nDCG@10 will be used. Zero-shot generalization will be evaluated on 13 publicly available BEIR datasets, covering a variety of domains and tasks. Baselines will include BM25, ANCE, CoCondenser, GTR, OpenAI Ada2, SimLM, monoBERT, RankT5, RankGPT, and others. Implementation will leverage 16x32G V100 GPUs, batch sizes of 128, and memory-efficient training strategies. Ablation studies will compare full fine-tuning versus LoRA and investigate the impact of input sequence length.
a531e9a328ad1488567fa68c15d5bf30bfb90c78.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first comprehensive exploration of fine-tuning a state-of-the-art, open-source large language model (LLaMA-2) as both a dense retriever and a pointwise reranker in a multi-stage retrieval pipeline. The approach leverages LLMs' inherent ability to process longer contexts, enabling holistic document representations and eliminating the need for traditional segmentation and pooling strategies. The method demonstrates state-of-the-art effectiveness for both retrieval and reranking, including strong zero-shot performance across diverse domains. The pipeline is fully open-source and optimized for multi-stage retrieval, offering greater efficiency and scalability compared to prompt-based or smaller model approaches.

a53c8ba374d430d6c3786d13c04edb200d547750.title: A Real-World WebAgent with Planning, Long Context Understanding, and Program Synthesis
a53c8ba374d430d6c3786d13c04edb200d547750.research_question: How can autonomous agents be developed to robustly and efficiently complete complex, open-domain tasks on real-world websites using natural language instructions, while overcoming challenges related to long HTML contexts, open-ended action spaces, and the need for effective planning and program synthesis?
a53c8ba374d430d6c3786d13c04edb200d547750.hypothesis: A modular agent architecture that combines a domain-specialized language model for planning and HTML summarization with a generalist language model for grounded program synthesis, trained via self-experience supervision, will significantly improve the success rate and generalization of web automation tasks on real-world websites compared to single-LLM or non-specialized approaches.
a53c8ba374d430d6c3786d13c04edb200d547750.proposed_method: A modular framework will be developed, integrating two large language models: (1) HTML-T5, a domain-specialized encoder-decoder model pre-trained on a large HTML corpus with local and global attention mechanisms and a mixture of long-span denoising objectives, responsible for decomposing user instructions into sub-instructions and extracting task-relevant HTML snippets; and (2) Flan-U-PaLM, a generalist LLM prompted to generate executable Python programs (via Selenium) based on the planning and summarization outputs. The workflow involves iterative cycles where HTML-T5 predicts the next sub-instruction and relevant HTML snippet, and Flan-U-PaLM synthesizes the corresponding Python code to interact with the website. Self-experience supervision will be employed, using scripted planning, automated summarization, and program synthesis to generate training data, which is then used to fine-tune the models for alignment with real-world web tasks. The approach emphasizes closed-loop planning grounded in HTML observations and leverages few-shot prompting for code generation.
a53c8ba374d430d6c3786d13c04edb200d547750.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both real-world and benchmark datasets. For real-world evaluation, the agent will be tested on three distinct website domains: real estate, social media, and map services, using a curated set of 20 natural language instructions per domain. Success rates and attribute coverage scores will be measured, with baselines including single LLMs and partial modular variants. For benchmarking, the HTML-T5 model will be evaluated on MiniWoB++ (56 simulated web tasks, 12K human demonstrations) and Mind2Web (over 2K instructions from 137 websites) using metrics such as element accuracy, operation F1, and step/task success rates. Ablation studies will compare attention mechanisms (dense, local, local+global) and pre-training objectives (various span lengths for denoising). Error analysis will categorize failures into planning, programming, and summarization. Automated and human-in-the-loop evaluation protocols will be used to assess agent performance and generalization.
a53c8ba374d430d6c3786d13c04edb200d547750.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a modular agent architecture that integrates a domain-specialized language model (HTML-T5) with local and global attention and long-span denoising for HTML understanding, and a generalist LLM for grounded program synthesis. The approach leverages self-experience supervision to align models with real-world web automation tasks, enabling closed-loop planning and robust handling of long, complex HTML documents. The methodology claims to achieve over 50% improvement in real-world website automation success rates compared to single-LLM baselines, and to set new state-of-the-art results on established web automation benchmarks (MiniWoB++, Mind2Web). The research also demonstrates that architectural choices (local/global attention) and pre-training objectives tailored to HTML structure yield significant gains over prior instruction-tuned or dense-attention models.

a553bf27d801d09f667fe121c0ba9632257f364b.title: DPOK: Reinforcement Learning for Fine-tuning Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
a553bf27d801d09f667fe121c0ba9632257f364b.research_question: How can reinforcement learning from human feedback be effectively leveraged to fine-tune text-to-image diffusion models, improving image-text alignment and image quality while mitigating common failure modes such as overfitting and bias?
a553bf27d801d09f667fe121c0ba9632257f364b.hypothesis: Online reinforcement learning with policy gradient optimization and KL regularization will enable text-to-image diffusion models to achieve superior image-text alignment and image quality compared to supervised fine-tuning, while also reducing model biases and failure modes.
a553bf27d801d09f667fe121c0ba9632257f364b.proposed_method: A novel fine-tuning framework, DPOK (Diffusion Policy Optimization with KL regularization), is developed for text-to-image diffusion models. The approach formulates the denoising process of diffusion models as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), enabling the application of policy gradient reinforcement learning to maximize a reward function trained from human feedback. KL divergence between the fine-tuned and pre-trained models is incorporated as a regularization term, acting as an implicit reward to stabilize training and prevent overfitting to the reward model. The method is implemented using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) for efficient parameter updates, and the reward model is derived from large-scale human assessments of image-text pairs. Both online RL fine-tuning and a supervised fine-tuning baseline with comparable KL regularization are considered for fair comparison.
a553bf27d801d09f667fe121c0ba9632257f364b.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using the Stable Diffusion v1.5 model as the base generative model, with LoRA applied to the UNet module for efficient fine-tuning. The ImageReward model, trained on extensive human feedback datasets, serves as the reward function. Evaluation includes both single-prompt and multi-prompt fine-tuning scenarios, using prompts that test color, composition, counting, and location capabilities. Baselines include supervised fine-tuning with and without KL regularization. Quantitative metrics include ImageReward scores (for image-text alignment) and aesthetic scores (for image quality), with qualitative analysis and human evaluations performed on generated samples. Large-scale prompt sets from MS-CoCo and Drawbench are also used to assess scalability and generalization.
a553bf27d801d09f667fe121c0ba9632257f364b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled online RL fine-tuning framework for text-to-image diffusion models, leveraging policy gradient optimization and KL regularization. The method provides a theoretical and empirical analysis of KL regularization in both RL and supervised settings, demonstrating its effectiveness in stabilizing training and improving image quality. The framework enables fine-tuning on new distributions beyond the support of pre-trained models, leading to improved alignment with human intent and reduction of model biases. Comprehensive empirical comparisons establish the superiority of the RL-based approach over supervised baselines in both alignment and fidelity.

a5889e0d2dea37f5fccf74bd4b74ece183604c2a.title: SPECTRE : Spectral Conditioning Helps to Overcome the Expressivity Limits of One-shot Graph Generators
a5889e0d2dea37f5fccf74bd4b74ece183604c2a.research_question: How can the expressivity and scalability limitations of one-shot graph generators be overcome to enable the generation of large, diverse, and high-fidelity graphs in a single step?
a5889e0d2dea37f5fccf74bd4b74ece183604c2a.hypothesis: Conditioning one-shot graph generators on the dominant components of the graph Laplacian spectrum (eigenvalues and eigenvectors) enables more effective control over global and local graph structure, thereby overcoming expressivity bottlenecks and mode collapse issues that hinder existing one-shot graph generation methods.
a5889e0d2dea37f5fccf74bd4b74ece183604c2a.proposed_method: A novel generative adversarial network (GAN) framework is proposed that decomposes the graph generation process into two jointly-learned stages: (1) modeling the distribution of the top-k eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the graph Laplacian, and (2) generating a graph conditioned on these spectral components. The eigenvalue generator is implemented as a 1D CNN, while the eigenvector generator iteratively refines a starting point on the Stiefel manifold using learned rotations, ensuring valid orthogonality and alignment with the spectral structure. The conditional graph generator initializes a rough Laplacian matrix from the generated spectra and refines it using a Provably Powerful Graph Network (PPGN), ultimately producing an adjacency matrix. All modules are permutation equivariant, differentiable, and optimized end-to-end using a WGAN-LP loss. Spectral features are also provided to the discriminator to enforce consistency between the generated graph and its spectrum.
a5889e0d2dea37f5fccf74bd4b74ece183604c2a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world graph datasets, including Planar graphs, Stochastic Block Models, Community-small, QM9 molecular graphs, and large protein graphs (up to 500 nodes). Baselines will include state-of-the-art autoregressive models (GraphRNN, GRAN) and one-shot GANs (MolGAN, GG-GAN), with all baselines re-implemented using consistent architectural components for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics will include Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) on node degree, clustering coefficient, orbit count, Laplacian eigenvalues, and eigenspace-based wavelet statistics, as well as measures of validity, uniqueness, and novelty of generated graphs. The experimental setup will use teacher forcing, model selection based on MMD ratios, and timing analysis for generation speed.
a5889e0d2dea37f5fccf74bd4b74ece183604c2a.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces spectral conditioning into one-shot graph generation, enabling direct control over global graph properties and addressing expressivity and mode collapse issues. The approach allows for the one-shot generation of much larger graphs than previously possible with one-shot models, while maintaining permutation equivariance and end-to-end differentiability. The method achieves significant improvements in modeling fidelity, diversity, and scalability compared to both autoregressive and prior one-shot baselines, and demonstrates the ability to generate valid, novel, and unique graphs at a fraction of the computational cost.

a5a0cac23c3fb59c140c465a2de2693c5e39c8d4.title: On Minimax Estimation of Parameters in Softmax-Contaminated Mixture of Experts
a5a0cac23c3fb59c140c465a2de2693c5e39c8d4.research_question: What are the statistical properties and minimax convergence rates for parameter estimation in softmax-contaminated mixture of experts (MoE) models, particularly in the context of fine-tuning large-scale pre-trained models with a trainable prompt expert? How does the overlap or distinguishability between the prompt and pre-trained expert impact the estimability and convergence rates of model parameters?
a5a0cac23c3fb59c140c465a2de2693c5e39c8d4.hypothesis: The convergence rates of parameter estimation in softmax-contaminated MoE models are optimal (parametric order) when the prompt and pre-trained experts are distinguishable, but become significantly slower when the prompt acquires overlapping knowledge with the pre-trained model. Introducing a formal notion of distinguishability will enable precise characterization of these regimes and their impact on minimax rates.
a5a0cac23c3fb59c140c465a2de2693c5e39c8d4.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed for analyzing the softmax-contaminated MoE model, where a fixed pre-trained expert is combined with a trainable prompt expert via a softmax gating mechanism. The conditional density of the response given covariates will be modeled as a mixture of the pre-trained and prompt experts, with input-dependent gating weights. Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) will be used to estimate the gating and prompt parameters, allowing these parameters to vary with sample size to facilitate minimax analysis. A novel analytic distinguishability condition will be formulated to precisely characterize when the prompt and pre-trained experts are statistically separable, and minimax lower and upper bounds for parameter estimation rates will be derived under both distinguishable and non-distinguishable regimes. The analysis will include the development of appropriate loss functions and identifiability conditions tailored to each regime, leveraging advanced tools from empirical process theory and information theory.
a5a0cac23c3fb59c140c465a2de2693c5e39c8d4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic datasets generated according to the softmax-contaminated MoE model, with both distinguishable (e.g., Laplace vs. Gaussian experts) and non-distinguishable (e.g., both Gaussian with similar expert functions) settings. Covariates will be drawn i.i.d. from a standard Gaussian distribution, and responses will be generated using specified expert functions (e.g., tanh activations) and variances. The MLE will be computed using the EM algorithm with BFGS optimization for the M-step, across a range of sample sizes (e.g., n from 1,000 to 100,000). Evaluation metrics will include parameter estimation error (e.g., L2 norm differences and absolute errors in gating and expert parameters), and empirical convergence rates will be compared to theoretical predictions. Baselines will include both input-free and softmax gating variants, and experiments will be repeated multiple times to ensure statistical robustness.
a5a0cac23c3fb59c140c465a2de2693c5e39c8d4.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new analytic notion of distinguishability for softmax-contaminated MoE models, enabling a rigorous separation of regimes where prompt and pre-trained experts are statistically separable or overlapping. It provides the first minimax analysis of parameter estimation rates in this setting, allowing prompt parameters to vary with sample size and deriving tight lower and upper bounds. The approach also demonstrates that softmax gating yields faster, sample-efficient estimation compared to input-free gating, and establishes precise conditions under which parameter estimation rates degrade due to prompt-pre-trained overlap. These contributions advance the theoretical understanding of fine-tuning strategies in large-scale models and provide practical guidance for designing effective prompt-based adaptation methods.

a5a360af27af5153fbdbeb685159b4adcc930d66.title: Transformer Copilot: Learning from The Mistake Log in LLM Fine-tuning
a5a360af27af5153fbdbeb685159b4adcc930d66.research_question: Can inference performance of large language models (LLMs) be enhanced by systematically retaining and leveraging internal learning signals, such as recurring errors and internal representations, during supervised fine-tuning, without requiring external feedback or changes to the training data?
a5a360af27af5153fbdbeb685159b4adcc930d66.hypothesis: Incorporating an auxiliary model that learns from a systematically recorded log of the primary model's mistakes and internal states during fine-tuning will enable error-aware correction at inference time, thereby improving the accuracy and robustness of LLMs across a variety of tasks with minimal computational overhead.
a5a360af27af5153fbdbeb685159b4adcc930d66.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a Pilot-Copilot framework for LLM fine-tuning. During training, a Mistake Log is constructed to record, for each token, the input representation, internal hidden states, and token-level prediction errors of the primary (Pilot) model. An auxiliary Copilot model, initialized from the Pilot's decoder, is designed to learn from this Mistake Log, using a modified cross-attention mechanism to jointly attend to the Pilot's input, hidden states, and error patterns. The Copilot is trained to predict the token-level error (the difference between the ground-truth and the Pilot's predicted distribution) using an RMSE loss. During inference, the Copilot's output is fused with the Pilot's logits via a tunable parameter, producing rectified token predictions in an auto-regressive manner. The framework supports both encoder-decoder and decoder-only Transformer architectures, with the Copilot operating as a lightweight, error-correcting module.
a5a360af27af5153fbdbeb685159b4adcc930d66.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 12 benchmark datasets spanning commonsense reasoning (PIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, BoolQ, SIQA, OpenbookQA), arithmetic reasoning (AQuA, GSM8K, MAWPS, SVAMP), and recommendation tasks (Beauty, LastFM). The method will be evaluated using various backbone models, including T5, FLAN-T5, LLaMA-3, and Qwen2.5, across multiple parameter scales. Baselines will include Pilot-only models, larger frontier LLMs (e.g., LLaMA-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-14B), and parameter-efficient expansion methods (MoE, LLaMA/Mistral-Pro, MergeKit, TIES). Evaluation metrics will primarily be accuracy for reasoning tasks and standard metrics for recommendation. Experiments will assess not only performance gains but also computational efficiency (throughput, training/inference time), scalability with model size, and transferability of the Copilot across independently trained Pilot models.
a5a360af27af5153fbdbeb685159b4adcc930d66.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the Mistake Log as a systematic, fine-grained record of model errors and internal states during fine-tuning, enabling direct exploitation of the model's own learning signals for error correction. The Copilot model design, with its modified cross-attention mechanism and joint training paradigm, allows for token-level rectification of the Pilot's predictions without altering the original training objective or data. The approach is claimed to be architecture-agnostic, efficient (incurring only marginal computational overhead), scalable, and transferable across models. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate consistent and significant performance improvements over strong baselines, including models with substantially larger parameter counts.

a5bd8813d288dd4ea7ebfd9d448959370bd286c8.title: Stem-OB: Generalizable Visual Imitation Learning with Stem-Like Convergent Observation through Diffusion Inversion
a5bd8813d288dd4ea7ebfd9d448959370bd286c8.research_question: How can visual imitation learning algorithms be made more robust and generalizable to variations in visual input, such as changes in lighting, texture, and appearance, in both real-world and simulated environments?
a5bd8813d288dd4ea7ebfd9d448959370bd286c8.hypothesis: Applying a partial diffusion inversion process to visual observations prior to training will suppress low-level visual differences while preserving high-level semantic structure, thereby improving the robustness and generalization of visual imitation learning policies to unseen visual perturbations.
a5bd8813d288dd4ea7ebfd9d448959370bd286c8.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that preprocesses visual observations using a partial diffusion inversion process, leveraging pretrained image diffusion models (such as Stable Diffusion) to map input images into a latent space where low-level appearance differences are suppressed and high-level scene structure is preserved. The process involves applying a specified number of forward diffusion steps (using DDPM inversion for efficiency and effectiveness) to each observation before training, resulting in a convergent latent representation for semantically similar scenes. Visual imitation learning algorithms are then trained on these diffusion-inversed observations, with no modification required at test time—policies are directly deployed on original, unprocessed observations. The method is designed to be plug-and-play, requiring no additional training or inference-time computation, and is compatible with a wide range of visual imitation learning backbones.
a5bd8813d288dd4ea7ebfd9d448959370bd286c8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both real-world and simulated robotic manipulation tasks. Real-world experiments use a Franka Emika Panda Arm and RGB cameras to perform tasks such as Cup2Plate, Duck2Bowl, OpenDrawer, and TurnOnFaucet, with visual perturbations introduced via changes in object appearance and lighting. Simulated experiments utilize the SAPIEN3 platform (with ManiSkill 3 dataset) and the MimicGen benchmark, covering tasks like PushCube, PegInsertionSide, PickCube, StackCube, MugCleanup, Threading, ThreePieceAssembly, and Coffee, with variations in backgrounds and textures. Baselines for comparison include data augmentation methods such as Spectrum Random Masking (SRM), Mix-Spectrum, Random Overlay, and unmodified observations. Evaluation metrics focus on task success rates under both training and generalization (perturbed) conditions, with multiple runs and diverse perturbation settings to assess robustness. Ablation studies will investigate the effect of inversion step count, total diffusion steps, and inversion method (DDPM vs. DDIM) on performance.
a5bd8813d288dd4ea7ebfd9d448959370bd286c8.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the use of partial diffusion inversion as a preprocessing step for visual imitation learning, enabling the convergence of diverse visual observations into a shared, semantically meaningful latent space. This approach fundamentally differs from traditional data augmentation by leveraging the semantic abstraction capabilities of diffusion models rather than indiscriminate noise injection. The method is computationally efficient, requiring no inference-time processing, and is compatible with any visual imitation learning algorithm. Empirical results indicate substantial improvements in generalization to unseen visual perturbations, with significant gains in real-world robotic task success rates compared to state-of-the-art augmentation baselines.

a5e78e7d0c97121dc852908b62a1b932c0bf6bfd.title: Sampling-Efficient Test-Time Scaling: Self-Estimating the Best-of-N Sampling in Early Decoding
a5e78e7d0c97121dc852908b62a1b932c0bf6bfd.research_question: How can the efficiency of Best-of-N (BoN) sampling for large language model inference be improved, particularly by reducing GPU memory and inference latency, without relying on external reward models or fully generating all samples?
a5e78e7d0c97121dc852908b62a1b932c0bf6bfd.hypothesis: Early internal consistency among partially generated samples can be leveraged to reliably estimate the most promising sample, enabling early truncation of suboptimal samples and thus significantly reducing computational cost without sacrificing performance.
a5e78e7d0c97121dc852908b62a1b932c0bf6bfd.proposed_method: A novel decoding algorithm, Self-Truncation Best-of-N (ST-BoN), will be developed to address the inefficiencies of traditional BoN sampling. The method initiates by generating N samples in parallel up to an 'earliest estimation time' c, determined by when all samples become pairwise inconsistent. At this point, a buffer window of τ additional steps is generated for each sample. During this window, an internal consistency score is computed for each sample using a Chain-of-Embedding (CoE) metric, which captures the curvature of the latent thinking path in the model's hidden states. The sample with the lowest average CoE-based distance to others is repeatedly identified as the most promising at each step in the buffer window. The sample most frequently selected during the buffer window is chosen, and only this sample is fully generated to completion, while the others are truncated. This approach eliminates the need for reward models and full sample generation, instead relying on unsupervised, model-internal signals for efficient selection.
a5e78e7d0c97121dc852908b62a1b932c0bf6bfd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of datasets covering both objective (MATH, TheoremQA, GPQA, MMLU) and subjective (CNNDM, AlpacaFarm) tasks, using large language models such as Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama3-8B-Instruct, and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3. Baselines will include Full-BoN with and without reward models (using self-consistency and process reward models, respectively), as well as greedy decoding. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy for reasoning tasks, Rouge-L and human scoring for summarization, and win rate for instruction-following, alongside computational cost metrics for GPU memory and wall-clock time. The experimental setup will use standard sampling strategies (top-k, top-p, temperature), and ablations will be performed on buffer window length, sampling strategy, and consistency metrics. All experiments will be run on multi-GPU clusters, with careful tracking of memory and latency.
a5e78e7d0c97121dc852908b62a1b932c0bf6bfd.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a fully unsupervised, reward-model-free approach to early truncation in BoN sampling, leveraging internal model representations for self-estimation. It is the first to jointly address both the memory and latency inefficiencies of BoN sampling without sacrificing performance. The method is generalizable across domains and model scales, provides a theoretically grounded connection between early and final consistency, and demonstrates substantial reductions in GPU memory usage (over 80%) and inference latency (up to 50%), while achieving equivalent or better accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost.

a6159daf277e73ca511da98a0d05432f6bab0de7.title: LightGlue: Local Feature Matching at Light Speed
a6159daf277e73ca511da98a0d05432f6bab0de7.research_question: How can local feature matching across images be made more efficient, accurate, and easier to train, while maintaining or improving robustness and adaptability to varying image pair difficulty?
a6159daf277e73ca511da98a0d05432f6bab0de7.hypothesis: A deep neural network architecture that adaptively adjusts its computational depth and prunes unmatchable points during inference can achieve state-of-the-art accuracy in local feature matching, while significantly improving efficiency and ease of training compared to existing Transformer-based matchers.
a6159daf277e73ca511da98a0d05432f6bab0de7.proposed_method: A novel deep neural network, LightGlue, is proposed for matching local features across image pairs. The architecture consists of a stack of identical layers, each containing self- and cross-attention units with relative positional encoding, which jointly process two sets of local features. At each layer, a lightweight classifier predicts the confidence of each feature's matchability, enabling the network to dynamically decide whether to halt further computation (adaptive depth) or to prune points deemed confidently unmatchable (adaptive width). The assignment between features is predicted by combining pairwise similarity and matchability scores into a soft partial assignment matrix, supervised at each layer to encourage early and robust predictions. The network is trained in two stages: first to predict correspondences, then to train the confidence classifier, using both synthetic homographies and real-world datasets with careful data augmentation and optimization techniques.
a6159daf277e73ca511da98a0d05432f6bab0de7.experiment_details: Experiments are proposed on standard benchmarks for homography estimation (HPatches), relative pose estimation (MegaDepth-1500), and large-scale visual localization (Aachen Day-Night). The method will be evaluated using both sparse (SuperPoint, SIFT, DISK) and dense (LoFTR, MatchFormer, ASpanFormer) feature extractors. Baselines will include nearest-neighbor matching, SuperGlue, SGMNet, ClusterGNN, and state-of-the-art dense matchers. Evaluation metrics will include precision, recall, area under the cumulative error curve (AUC) for homography and pose estimation, pose recall at multiple thresholds, and runtime (throughput in image pairs per second). Extensive ablation studies will be conducted to assess the impact of adaptive depth, width pruning, positional encoding, and matchability prediction. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by tuning inlier thresholds and using consistent image resizing and feature extraction protocols.
a6159daf277e73ca511da98a0d05432f6bab0de7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces an adaptive inference mechanism that dynamically adjusts both the depth (number of layers) and width (number of points) of the network based on the difficulty of each image pair, leading to significant efficiency gains. The method disentangles similarity and matchability prediction, enabling efficient and robust partial assignment without the computational overhead of optimal transport solvers. Deep supervision at each layer accelerates training convergence and enables early confident predictions. The architecture leverages relative positional encoding and bidirectional cross-attention for improved accuracy and efficiency. Overall, the method claims to be faster, more accurate, and easier to train than previous state-of-the-art matchers, making deep feature matching practical for latency-sensitive and large-scale applications.

a64e9fe44051d93202853a43656def4b44f84883.title: Discovering Interpretable Directions in the Semantic Latent Space of Diffusion Models
a64e9fe44051d93202853a43656def4b44f84883.research_question: How can interpretable and disentangled semantic directions be discovered in the latent space of unconditional denoising diffusion models (DDMs) to enable intuitive and high-quality semantic image editing, without requiring architectural modifications, text-based guidance, or model fine-tuning?
a64e9fe44051d93202853a43656def4b44f84883.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that both supervised and unsupervised methods can be developed to uncover semantically meaningful and disentangled directions in the latent space (h-space) of DDMs, enabling effective and localized semantic image editing without the need for additional guidance or model modifications.
a64e9fe44051d93202853a43656def4b44f84883.proposed_method: The proposed research will develop both unsupervised and supervised techniques to identify interpretable semantic directions in the h-space of unconditional DDMs. Unsupervised methods will include principal component analysis (PCA) on the bottleneck activations of the U-Net denoiser across all diffusion timesteps to reveal global semantic directions, as well as spectral analysis of the Jacobian of the denoiser with respect to the latent code to uncover image-specific and region-specific directions. The supervised approach will leverage attribute classifiers to annotate generated samples, enabling the identification of latent directions corresponding to specific semantic attributes via linear separation. Additionally, a linear projection technique will be introduced to disentangle directions that affect multiple attributes, ensuring that semantic edits are independent and interpretable. All methods will be designed to operate without architectural changes, text-based optimization, or model fine-tuning.
a64e9fe44051d93202853a43656def4b44f84883.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using pretrained unconditional DDMs, specifically a DDPM model trained on the CelebA-HQ dataset. The effectiveness of the proposed methods will be evaluated by generating and editing face images along discovered semantic directions, including attributes such as pose, gender, age, smile, glasses, and localized facial features. Baselines will include random directions in latent space and existing methods for semantic editing in GANs and DDMs. Quantitative evaluation will utilize pretrained attribute classifiers and CLIP-based zero-shot classifiers to measure the disentanglement and specificity of edits, with metrics including attribute score changes and qualitative visual assessment. Additional experiments will assess the transferability of discovered directions across samples and the ability to combine multiple semantic edits sequentially or in parallel.
a64e9fe44051d93202853a43656def4b44f84883.novelty_claims: The research introduces novel unsupervised and supervised methods for discovering interpretable and disentangled semantic directions in the h-space of unconditional DDMs, including the use of PCA for global directions, spectral Jacobian analysis for image-specific and region-specific edits, and a simple linear projection for disentanglement. The proposed approaches require no architectural modifications, text-based guidance, or model fine-tuning, and are applicable to existing pretrained DDMs. The methods enable both global and highly localized semantic image editing, and demonstrate that semantic directions found for one image can generalize to others. The research also provides a framework for combining and disentangling multiple semantic attributes in a principled manner.

a6524cf164d67233d03d5acff37dd415cac72fbe.title: Emergent Risk Awareness in Rational Agents under Resource Constraints
a6524cf164d67233d03d5acff37dd415cac72fbe.research_question: How do resource constraints and survival pressures influence the emergent risk awareness and decision-making behaviors of rational AI agents, and under what conditions do these pressures lead to misalignment between agent incentives and principal objectives in sequential decision-making problems?
a6524cf164d67233d03d5acff37dd415cac72fbe.hypothesis: The introduction of survival constraints and limited liability in resource-constrained environments induces preference shifts in rational agents, leading to emergent risk-averse or risk-seeking behaviors that can result in incentive misalignment with human principals, especially when there are asymmetries in liability or optimization horizon.
a6524cf164d67233d03d5acff37dd415cac72fbe.proposed_method: A formal framework will be developed based on an extension of the survival bandit model to capture the dynamics of resource-constrained sequential decision-making. The agent's objective will be modeled as maximizing cumulative rewards over a finite horizon, subject to a survival constraint that terminates the process if resources are depleted. The framework will define a Markov Decision Process (MDP) where the state is the agent's remaining budget, actions correspond to choices with stochastic outcomes, and transitions are determined by observed rewards and resource updates. Analytical results will be derived to characterize the conditions under which agents exhibit risk-neutral, risk-averse (survival-incentivized), or risk-seeking behaviors, and to identify scenarios where agent and principal objectives diverge due to limited liability or differing optimization horizons. Mechanisms such as reward shaping and policy adjustments will be proposed and theoretically analyzed to mitigate misalignment.
a6524cf164d67233d03d5acff37dd415cac72fbe.experiment_details: Empirical validation will be conducted using both synthetic and real-world-inspired sequential decision-making scenarios, such as financial investment tasks. Experiments will involve open-source large language models (LLMs) and non-reasoning models tasked with maximizing rewards under explicit resource constraints and varying initial budgets. The models' choices will be evaluated across multiple trials to assess the frequency of risk-seeking versus risk-averse behavior. Baseline comparisons will include risk-neutral policies and policies optimized for principal objectives without limited liability. Evaluation metrics will include the proportion of risky actions chosen, survival probability, and alignment with principal-preferred outcomes. Additional experiments will test the effectiveness of proposed mitigation strategies, such as reward shaping, in reducing misalignment.
a6524cf164d67233d03d5acff37dd415cac72fbe.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a formal and generalizable framework for analyzing emergent risk awareness in rational agents operating under survival constraints, extending survival bandit theory to capture the nuanced effects of limited liability and resource depletion. Novel theoretical results will precisely characterize the conditions that induce risk-averse or risk-seeking behaviors and identify sources of principal-agent misalignment. The research will also provide and evaluate new mitigation mechanisms, such as targeted reward shaping, and empirically demonstrate the emergence of these behaviors in advanced AI models, offering actionable guidelines for the safe deployment of AI agents in resource-limited environments.

a66b6c6544af9c7926d43ec0a2b144de968a50e7.title: Idiosyncrasies in Large Language Models
a66b6c6544af9c7926d43ec0a2b144de968a50e7.research_question: Can unique patterns in the outputs of large language models (LLMs) be systematically identified and used to reliably distinguish between different LLMs, even when their architectures and training data overlap? What are the underlying sources of these idiosyncrasies, and how robust are they to text transformations and rewriting?
a66b6c6544af9c7926d43ec0a2b144de968a50e7.hypothesis: Distinctive, model-specific patterns—idiosyncrasies—exist in the outputs of LLMs, which can be detected and leveraged to accurately classify the source model of a given text. These idiosyncrasies are robust to various surface-level transformations and are encoded at both lexical and semantic levels.
a66b6c6544af9c7926d43ec0a2b144de968a50e7.proposed_method: A synthetic classification task will be constructed where, given a text output, the objective is to predict its source LLM from a set of candidate models. Large datasets of outputs will be generated from multiple LLMs using shared prompt sets. Pretrained text embedding models, such as LLM2vec, will be fine-tuned with LoRA-based methods to perform N-way sequence classification using these outputs. The methodology will include ablation studies involving text transformations (e.g., word/letter shuffling, paraphrasing, translation, summarization) to isolate the contribution of various linguistic and semantic features. Additional analyses will extract characteristic phrases using TF-IDF and logistic regression, and markdown formatting patterns will be quantified. Open-ended language analysis will be performed by prompting LLMs to provide qualitative descriptions of each model's output style.
a66b6c6544af9c7926d43ec0a2b144de968a50e7.experiment_details: Experiments will use outputs from a range of state-of-the-art LLMs, including proprietary chat APIs (GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Grok-2, Gemini-1.5-Pro, DeepSeek-V3), instruct-tuned models (Llama3.1-8b, Gemma2-9b, Qwen2.5-7b, Mistral-v3-7b), and base models. Prompts will be drawn from diverse datasets such as UltraChat, Cosmopedia, LmsysChat, WildChat, and FineWeb. Classification accuracy will be evaluated on held-out validation sets, with both pairwise and N-way setups. Baselines will include various sequence embedding models (ELMo, BERT, T5, GPT-2, LLM2vec), and ablations will test the impact of input length, prompt-level interventions, and different sampling strategies. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy, confusion matrices, and text similarity scores (ROUGE, BERTScore). Robustness will be assessed by testing classifiers on out-of-distribution prompts and rewritten texts.
a66b6c6544af9c7926d43ec0a2b144de968a50e7.novelty_claims: The proposed framework systematically demonstrates that LLMs exhibit robust, quantifiable idiosyncrasies in their outputs, enabling near-perfect classification of model origin even among models with similar architectures and overlapping training data. The approach reveals that these idiosyncrasies persist through paraphrasing, translation, and summarization, indicating deep semantic encoding. The proposal introduces detailed analyses of word-level, formatting, and semantic features, and shows that synthetic data can propagate model-specific patterns. The work provides practical tools for model provenance, similarity assessment, and highlights implications for robust evaluation and potential vulnerabilities in LLM assessment methodologies.

a673ef39237e227381fccf5b1d154d96de428f1d.title: Derivative-Free Guidance in Continuous and Discrete Diffusion Models with Soft Value-Based Decoding
a673ef39237e227381fccf5b1d154d96de428f1d.research_question: How can downstream reward functions be optimized in both continuous and discrete diffusion models, while preserving the naturalness of generated samples, without requiring differentiable proxy models or fine-tuning of the generative models?
a673ef39237e227381fccf5b1d154d96de428f1d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that integrating soft value-based decoding into the inference process of pre-trained diffusion models will enable efficient optimization of arbitrary (including non-differentiable) reward functions, while maintaining sample naturalness and eliminating the need for fine-tuning or differentiable proxy models.
a673ef39237e227381fccf5b1d154d96de428f1d.proposed_method: A novel inference-time algorithm, Soft Value-Based Decoding in Diffusion Models (SVDD), will be developed to optimize downstream reward functions in pre-trained diffusion models. The method introduces soft value functions that estimate the expected future reward from intermediate noisy states in the diffusion process. At each denoising step, multiple candidate states are sampled from the pre-trained model, and the state with the highest value (as predicted by the soft value function) is selected for the next step. Two variants are proposed: SVDD-MC, which learns the value function via Monte Carlo regression using rollouts and reward evaluations, and SVDD-PM, which uses a posterior mean approximation that requires no additional training if the reward function is available. The approach is designed to work directly with both continuous and discrete diffusion models and can utilize non-differentiable reward feedback.
a673ef39237e227381fccf5b1d154d96de428f1d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across several domains, including image generation (using Stable Diffusion v1.5), molecule generation (using GDSS trained on ZINC-250k), and DNA/RNA sequence generation (using discrete diffusion models trained on enhancer and 5’UTR datasets). Downstream reward functions will include non-differentiable metrics such as image compressibility, aesthetics, molecular QED, SA, docking scores (via QuickVina2), and biological activity predictions (via Enformer and ConvGRU models). Baselines for comparison will include pre-trained model sampling, Best-of-N selection, DPS (a classifier guidance variant), and SMC-based methods. Evaluation metrics will focus on top quantiles of reward distributions and sample validity, with computational efficiency and memory usage also assessed. Hyperparameter ablation (e.g., number of candidate samples M) will be performed to analyze trade-offs.
a673ef39237e227381fccf5b1d154d96de428f1d.novelty_claims: The proposed method eliminates the need for constructing differentiable proxy models and avoids fine-tuning of generative diffusion models, enabling direct use of non-differentiable reward feedback. SVDD is applicable to both continuous and discrete diffusion models in a unified manner, overcoming limitations of existing classifier guidance and RL-based fine-tuning approaches. The algorithm is highly parallelizable, maintains sample diversity, and is effective even with small batch sizes. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior reward optimization and sample validity compared to existing non-fine-tuning and SMC-based baselines.

a68db57f08f6d72c0d3b22d451d2606dca880f94.title: MimicPlay: Long-Horizon Imitation Learning by Watching Human Play
a68db57f08f6d72c0d3b22d451d2606dca880f94.research_question: How can robots efficiently learn to perform complex, long-horizon manipulation tasks in the real world by leveraging human interaction data, while minimizing the need for labor-intensive teleoperated robot demonstrations?
a68db57f08f6d72c0d3b22d451d2606dca880f94.hypothesis: Learning high-level planning from easily collected human play data, combined with low-level control learned from a small set of teleoperated robot demonstrations, enables robots to efficiently acquire robust and generalizable long-horizon manipulation skills.
a68db57f08f6d72c0d3b22d451d2606dca880f94.proposed_method: A hierarchical imitation learning framework is proposed, where the high-level planner is trained using 3D human hand trajectory data extracted from multi-view human play videos. This planner learns a goal-conditioned latent plan space by predicting future 3D hand trajectories given a goal image, using a convolutional encoder and an MLP-based Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) to capture the multimodal nature of human strategies. To bridge the visual gap between human and robot domains, a KL-divergence loss is introduced to align the feature distributions of human and robot video frames. The low-level controller is then trained with a small number of robot teleoperation demonstrations, conditioned on the latent plans generated by the pre-trained planner. This controller uses a transformer-based architecture to integrate proprioceptive, visual, and latent plan information, and outputs robot actions through a GMM-based policy.
a68db57f08f6d72c0d3b22d451d2606dca880f94.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 14 real-world long-horizon manipulation tasks across six environments, including kitchen, study desk, flower arrangement, whiteboard, sandwich making, and cloth folding, using a Franka Emika robot arm. The training data will consist of 10 minutes of human play video per environment (multi-view for 3D hand tracking) and 20-40 teleoperated robot demonstrations per task. Baseline methods for comparison include goal-conditioned behavioral cloning (RNN and transformer variants), C-BeT, LMP, and R3M-BC. Evaluation metrics will focus on task success rate, generalization to novel tasks, robustness to disturbances, and sample efficiency. The experimental setup will also assess the impact of human play data scale, ablations on GMM and KL loss components, and the ability to prompt robot actions directly from human videos.
a68db57f08f6d72c0d3b22d451d2606dca880f94.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel paradigm for learning 3D-aware latent plans from cost-effective human play data, enabling efficient high-level planning for robots. The hierarchical framework uniquely combines human play data for planning and minimal teleoperated robot demonstrations for control, significantly reducing data collection costs. The method integrates human and robot skills into a shared latent plan space, allowing intuitive video-based prompting of robot actions and robust real-time replanning. Empirical results claim state-of-the-art performance in sample efficiency, generalization, and robustness on long-horizon real-world tasks, outperforming existing imitation learning methods.

a6a5c87972c094af24d079d168e70ccab83f0d9f.title: Beware of the Simulated DAG! Causal Discovery Benchmarks May Be Easy to Game
a6a5c87972c094af24d079d168e70ccab83f0d9f.research_question: How do properties of simulated additive noise models, specifically the relationship between marginal variances and causal order (varsortability), affect the performance and benchmarking of causal structure learning algorithms, and to what extent can these benchmarks be gamed or rendered uninformative for real-world applications?
a6a5c87972c094af24d079d168e70ccab83f0d9f.hypothesis: High varsortability in simulated data leads to artificially high performance of certain causal structure learning algorithms, particularly those sensitive to data scale, and this performance does not necessarily transfer to real-world data or to settings where data is standardized or measurement scales are unknown.
a6a5c87972c094af24d079d168e70ccab83f0d9f.proposed_method: A comprehensive investigation will be conducted into the impact of varsortability—the agreement between the order of increasing marginal variance and the causal order—on the identifiability of causal structures in additive noise models (ANMs). The study will introduce and formalize varsortability as a quantitative measure, and analyze its prevalence in commonly used synthetic data generation schemes. A new baseline algorithm, sortnregress, will be developed, which sorts variables by marginal variance and performs sparse regression for parent selection, to directly exploit varsortability. Theoretical analysis will be performed to understand how varsortability influences the gradients and optimization dynamics of continuous structure learning algorithms such as NOTEARS and GOLEM, both before and after data standardization. The investigation will also extend to non-linear ANMs and propose diagnostic tools and decision rules to assess the extent to which benchmarks can be gamed by exploiting covariance patterns, even after standardization.
a6a5c87972c094af24d079d168e70ccab83f0d9f.experiment_details: Experiments will be carried out using synthetic datasets generated from Erdös-Rényi and Scale-Free graphs with varying numbers of nodes (e.g., 10, 30, 50), edge densities, and noise distributions (Gaussian, Exponential, Gumbel), following parameterizations typical in the literature (e.g., edge weights and noise variances drawn iid from specified uniform distributions). Both raw and standardized versions of each dataset will be created to assess the impact of data scale. The performance of combinatorial (PC, FGES, DirectLiNGAM, MSE-GDS) and continuous (NOTEARS, GOLEM-EV, GOLEM-NV) structure learning algorithms will be benchmarked, along with the proposed sortnregress baseline and naive variance-sorting strategies. Evaluation metrics will include Structural Intervention Distance (SID) and Structural Hamming Distance (SHD) between recovered and ground-truth graphs, as well as their Markov equivalence classes. Additional experiments will be conducted on real-world datasets (e.g., protein signaling data) to assess varsortability and algorithm performance outside synthetic settings.
a6a5c87972c094af24d079d168e70ccab83f0d9f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces varsortability as a novel, quantitative measure of the alignment between marginal variance and causal order, and demonstrates its critical, previously underappreciated role in the identifiability and benchmarking of causal discovery algorithms. It provides a new diagnostic baseline (sortnregress) to reveal and quantify the extent to which data scale can be exploited in structure learning. The study offers theoretical and empirical evidence that high varsortability in synthetic benchmarks can lead to misleadingly high performance for certain algorithms, and shows that even after data standardization, covariance patterns can still be exploited to game benchmarks. The work challenges the validity of current benchmarking practices in causal discovery and advocates for the routine evaluation and reporting of varsortability in future studies.

a6c3dce03b16c366ba28dfa2232fb68d562e5474.title: HexPlane: A Fast Representation for Dynamic Scenes
a6c3dce03b16c366ba28dfa2232fb68d562e5474.research_question: How can dynamic 3D scenes be efficiently represented and rendered for novel view synthesis, overcoming the computational bottlenecks and memory constraints of existing implicit neural representations?
a6c3dce03b16c366ba28dfa2232fb68d562e5474.hypothesis: Explicitly representing dynamic 3D scenes using a set of six learned feature planes (HexPlane), combined with a lightweight MLP for color regression, will enable high-quality, efficient novel view synthesis with significantly reduced training and inference times compared to fully implicit methods.
a6c3dce03b16c366ba28dfa2232fb68d562e5474.proposed_method: A new explicit representation, HexPlane, will be developed for dynamic 3D scenes by decomposing the 4D spacetime grid into six learned feature planes spanning all pairs of spatial and temporal axes (e.g., XY, ZT). For any point in spacetime, feature vectors are extracted from each plane via bilinear interpolation, fused (e.g., by elementwise multiplication and concatenation), and passed through a small MLP to regress RGB color. Opacity and appearance features are queried from separate HexPlanes, and volumetric rendering is used to synthesize images from novel viewpoints and timesteps. The entire system is trained end-to-end using a photometric loss between rendered and ground truth images, with additional regularization (e.g., total variation and depth smoothness) to encourage spatial-temporal continuity and reduce artifacts. The framework is designed to be robust to different feature fusion mechanisms, coordinate systems (rectangular or spherical), and decoding mechanisms (MLP or spherical harmonics).
a6c3dce03b16c366ba28dfa2232fb68d562e5474.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on challenging dynamic scene datasets, including the Plenoptic Video dataset (multi-camera, high-resolution, complex motions) and the D-NeRF dataset (monocular, synthetic, sparse observations). Baselines will include state-of-the-art dynamic NeRF variants such as DyNeRF, T-NeRF, and TiNeuVox. Evaluation metrics will comprise PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and JOD for synthesis quality, as well as training and inference time for efficiency. Ablation studies will systematically investigate the impact of different factorization designs, feature fusion mechanisms, grid resolutions, and coordinate systems. Additional experiments will test the method's robustness to real-world monocular videos and unbounded scene representations using spherical coordinates.
a6c3dce03b16c366ba28dfa2232fb68d562e5474.novelty_claims: The proposed HexPlane framework introduces a simple yet powerful explicit representation for dynamic 3D scenes using six feature planes, enabling efficient and high-quality novel view synthesis. This approach achieves over 100× speedups in training and inference compared to prior implicit methods while matching or exceeding their synthesis quality. HexPlane is robust to various architectural choices and coordinate systems, supports both bounded and unbounded scenes, and does not require deformation fields or category-specific priors, making it broadly applicable to dynamic scene modeling.

a6c92dd8c537bc4a0c91cef8558e4a4f25416091.title: SplaTAM: Splat, Track & Map 3D Gaussians for Dense RGB-D SLAM
a6c92dd8c537bc4a0c91cef8558e4a4f25416091.research_question: How can explicit volumetric representations be leveraged to improve dense simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) performance using RGB-D data in challenging real-world scenarios?
a6c92dd8c537bc4a0c91cef8558e4a4f25416091.hypothesis: Explicit volumetric scene representations based on 3D Gaussians, combined with differentiable rendering and online optimization, will enable more accurate camera tracking, higher-fidelity scene reconstruction, and faster novel-view synthesis compared to existing implicit or non-volumetric SLAM methods.
a6c92dd8c537bc4a0c91cef8558e4a4f25416091.proposed_method: A dense RGB-D SLAM system will be developed using an explicit volumetric map representation composed of 3D Gaussians. Each Gaussian will be parameterized by its 3D position, color, radius, and opacity, with simplifications such as isotropic radii and view-independent color for efficiency. The system will employ differentiable rendering via Gaussian splatting to generate color, depth, and silhouette images from the map, enabling direct gradient-based optimization of both camera poses and map parameters. The SLAM pipeline will consist of three main steps: (1) camera tracking by minimizing photometric and geometric reconstruction errors using rendered and observed RGB-D frames, (2) Gaussian densification to expand the map in regions with insufficient coverage or new geometry, and (3) map update through joint optimization of Gaussian parameters using a selected subset of keyframes. Silhouette masks will be used to focus optimization on well-mapped regions, and initialization strategies will be defined for both the first frame and new Gaussians.
a6c92dd8c537bc4a0c91cef8558e4a4f25416091.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four datasets: ScanNet++, Replica, TUM-RGBD, and the original ScanNet, covering both synthetic and real-world indoor scenes with varying levels of difficulty and sensor quality. The system will be evaluated against state-of-the-art dense and feature-based SLAM baselines, including Point-SLAM, NICE-SLAM, Vox-Fusion, ESLAM, Kintinuous, ElasticFusion, ORB-SLAM2/3, and DROID-SLAM. Evaluation metrics will include average absolute trajectory error (ATE RMSE) for camera pose estimation, PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS for RGB rendering quality, and L1 error for depth reconstruction. Both training-view and novel-view synthesis will be assessed, with ScanNet++ providing held-out novel views for rigorous evaluation. Ablation studies will be performed to analyze the impact of different loss functions, tracking strategies, and Gaussian parameterizations. Runtime and memory usage will be benchmarked, and qualitative results will be visualized for both map reconstruction and camera trajectory estimation.
a6c92dd8c537bc4a0c91cef8558e4a4f25416091.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to integrate explicit volumetric 3D Gaussian representations with online differentiable rendering for dense RGB-D SLAM, enabling high-fidelity, real-time scene reconstruction and camera tracking. Key innovations include the use of fast, dense photometric optimization via Gaussian splatting, efficient map expansion through silhouette-guided densification, and structured map updates that leverage explicit spatial extent. The method achieves state-of-the-art results in camera pose estimation, map reconstruction, and novel-view synthesis, particularly excelling in scenarios with large inter-frame motion and textureless environments where prior methods fail. The framework also establishes a new benchmark for joint SLAM and novel-view synthesis on ScanNet++ and demonstrates scalability and efficiency suitable for real-time applications.

a6d3794c23626060781da0f1ff2bcdf7457b6c43.title: DecodingTrust: A Comprehensive Assessment of Trustworthiness in GPT Models
a6d3794c23626060781da0f1ff2bcdf7457b6c43.research_question: How can the trustworthiness of large language models, specifically GPT-3.5 and GPT-4, be comprehensively assessed across multiple perspectives such as toxicity, bias, robustness, privacy, ethics, and fairness under diverse and adversarial scenarios?
a6d3794c23626060781da0f1ff2bcdf7457b6c43.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that while GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 demonstrate improvements in trustworthiness over previous models, significant vulnerabilities remain under adversarial and challenging conditions, and that a comprehensive, multi-perspective evaluation will reveal previously unreported weaknesses.
a6d3794c23626060781da0f1ff2bcdf7457b6c43.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation framework will be developed to systematically assess the trustworthiness of GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 across eight key perspectives: toxicity, stereotype bias, adversarial robustness, out-of-distribution robustness, robustness to adversarial demonstrations, privacy, machine ethics, and fairness. For each perspective, multiple evaluation scenarios will be constructed, including both standard benchmarks and newly designed adversarial or challenging prompts, system instructions, and demonstration contexts. The methodology will involve generating and curating datasets (e.g., stereotype statements, adversarial texts, privacy-sensitive queries), designing prompt-based attacks (such as jailbreaking and misleading system/user prompts), and measuring model responses using quantitative metrics tailored to each trustworthiness dimension.
