The approach will also include the development of new protocols for evaluating in-context learning vulnerabilities, privacy leakage, and fairness under demographically imbalanced or balanced settings.
a6d3794c23626060781da0f1ff2bcdf7457b6c43.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using fixed versions of GPT-3.5 (gpt-3.5-turbo-0301) and GPT-4 (gpt-4-0314) accessed via the OpenAI API, ensuring reproducibility. Standard benchmarks such as REALTOXICITYPROMPTS (toxicity), AdvGLUE and AdvGLUE++ (adversarial robustness), ETHICS and Jiminy Cricket (machine ethics), and the Enron Email dataset (privacy) will be employed alongside custom-constructed datasets for stereotype bias, OOD robustness, and fairness. Baselines will include prior LLMs (e.g., GPT-3, BERT, ALBERT, open-source models like Alpaca and Vicuna) and state-of-the-art adversarial attack strategies (e.g., SemAttack, TextFooler, BERT-ATTACK). Evaluation metrics will include toxicity probability, agreement rates with stereotypes, attack success rates, information leakage rates, moral recognition accuracy, and fairness scores (e.g., base rate parity). The setup will involve both zero-shot and few-shot scenarios, with systematic variation of prompt types, demonstration contexts, and adversarial manipulations.
a6d3794c23626060781da0f1ff2bcdf7457b6c43.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the first comprehensive, multi-dimensional trustworthiness assessment of GPT models, covering a broader range of perspectives and adversarial scenarios than prior work. Novel evaluation protocols and datasets are developed for challenging the models beyond existing benchmarks, including adversarial system/user prompts, in-context demonstration attacks, and privacy leakage tests. The approach uncovers new vulnerabilities and trade-offs (e.g., accuracy vs. fairness, instruction-following vs. susceptibility to adversarial prompts) not previously documented, and provides a reproducible, extensible benchmark for future trustworthiness research in large language models.

a6f7485dfdf45320e82d84bcfdc51bcd52dff18b.title: Sora: A Review on Background, Technology, Limitations, and Opportunities of Large Vision Models
a6f7485dfdf45320e82d84bcfdc51bcd52dff18b.research_question: How can large-scale vision models be designed and trained to generate high-quality, long-duration videos from text instructions, while maintaining visual coherence, flexibility in input/output formats, and alignment with user intent?
a6f7485dfdf45320e82d84bcfdc51bcd52dff18b.hypothesis: Scaling up diffusion transformer architectures with advanced data pre-processing and unified visual representations will enable generative models to produce realistic, coherent, and instruction-aligned videos of variable durations, resolutions, and aspect ratios, surpassing the limitations of previous text-to-video models.
a6f7485dfdf45320e82d84bcfdc51bcd52dff18b.proposed_method: A novel text-to-video generative framework will be developed based on a diffusion transformer architecture. The approach begins by compressing input videos into a latent space using a video compression network, leveraging either spatial-patch or spatial-temporal-patch compression (e.g., VAE or VQ-VAE variants) to accommodate variable resolutions and durations. Latent representations are decomposed into spacetime patches, which are then packed using a patch n’ pack (PNP) strategy to enable efficient processing of variable-length sequences. A transformer-based denoising network iteratively refines noisy latent representations, conditioned on user-augmented instructions (potentially enhanced by large language models) and visual prompts. The final denoised latent is decoded back into pixel space to generate the output video, preserving the original aspect ratio and duration.
a6f7485dfdf45320e82d84bcfdc51bcd52dff18b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale, diverse video datasets encompassing a wide range of durations, resolutions, and aspect ratios. The proposed model will be compared against state-of-the-art text-to-video generation baselines such as Pika and Gen-2, as well as diffusion-based and transformer-based generative models. Evaluation metrics will include visual quality (e.g., FVD, IS), temporal coherence, instruction adherence (measured by CLIP-based similarity), and user studies for subjective assessment. Additional ablation studies will assess the impact of patchification strategies, compression methods, and prompt conditioning on output quality and efficiency.
a6f7485dfdf45320e82d84bcfdc51bcd52dff18b.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified framework for text-to-video generation that supports native-size video processing, variable durations, and aspect ratios without resizing or cropping. The method leverages spacetime latent patch representations and an efficient patch packing mechanism to scale transformer-based diffusion models for long, coherent video generation. The approach is expected to demonstrate emergent abilities in world simulation, instruction following, and visual prompt engineering, representing a significant advancement over prior models limited to short video clips and fixed formats.

a6f9fb141034a87ff9d627dc8a3ef31d0790c6ed.title: IDQL: Implicit Q-Learning as an Actor-Critic Method with Diffusion Policies
a6f9fb141034a87ff9d627dc8a3ef31d0790c6ed.research_question: How can offline reinforcement learning methods be improved to better handle out-of-distribution actions and extract more expressive, potentially multimodal policies from static datasets, while maintaining robustness and computational efficiency?
a6f9fb141034a87ff9d627dc8a3ef31d0790c6ed.hypothesis: Generalizing the critic objective in implicit Q-learning to arbitrary convex losses and extracting policies using diffusion-based generative models with importance weighting will yield more accurate, robust, and expressive policies in offline RL, outperforming prior methods and reducing sensitivity to hyperparameters.
a6f9fb141034a87ff9d627dc8a3ef31d0790c6ed.proposed_method: A novel offline RL framework is proposed that generalizes implicit Q-learning (IQL) into an actor-critic method by allowing the critic to be trained with arbitrary convex loss functions, thereby inducing a behavior-regularized implicit actor. The implicit actor is defined as a reweighting of the behavior policy, where the weights are derived from the critic's loss function. To accurately extract this implicit actor, an expressive diffusion model is trained to represent the behavior policy, and samples from this model are reweighted using critic-computed importance weights. At evaluation time, actions are selected either by sampling from the reweighted distribution or by taking the action with the highest Q-value among diffusion samples, enabling both stochastic and deterministic policy extraction. The method is implemented with a high-capacity, well-regularized residual network (LN_Resnet) for the diffusion model to ensure accurate modeling of complex, continuous action spaces.
a6f9fb141034a87ff9d627dc8a3ef31d0790c6ed.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the D4RL offline RL benchmarks, including both locomotion and antmaze domains, to evaluate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method. Baseline comparisons will include Conservative Q-Learning (CQL), Implicit Q-Learning (IQL), Diffusion Q-Learning (DQL), Decision Transformer, TD3+BC, Extreme Q-learning, and Selecting from Behavior Candidates (SfBC). Evaluation metrics will be the normalized scores on D4RL tasks, with both standard and restricted hyperparameter tuning regimes to assess robustness. Additional ablations will be performed to compare different critic objectives (expectile, quantile, exponential losses), policy extraction strategies (argmax vs. implicit), and diffusion model architectures (MLP vs. LN_Resnet). Online fine-tuning experiments will also be conducted to test adaptability after offline pretraining.
a6f9fb141034a87ff9d627dc8a3ef31d0790c6ed.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a generalization of implicit Q-learning as an actor-critic method with a flexible critic loss, establishing a theoretical connection between the loss function and the induced implicit actor. A new policy extraction approach is developed that leverages expressive diffusion models and importance weighting to accurately represent complex, multimodal implicit policies, overcoming limitations of unimodal Gaussian policy parameterizations. The method demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on challenging offline RL benchmarks, particularly under limited hyperparameter tuning, and provides insights into the critical role of policy extraction in implicit Q-learning frameworks. The approach is also computationally efficient due to the decoupling of critic and policy training.

a70148376be4bea44ff6fd074c83e661b6734715.title: Fast Graph Generation via Spectral Diffusion
a70148376be4bea44ff6fd074c83e661b6734715.research_question: How can the quality and efficiency of generative models for graph-structured data be improved, particularly in learning complex graph topologies and node features, while overcoming the limitations of current diffusion-based approaches?
a70148376be4bea44ff6fd074c83e661b6734715.hypothesis: Applying low-rank diffusion processes in the graph spectrum space, rather than full-rank diffusion in the adjacency matrix space, will enable more effective and efficient learning of graph topologies, leading to higher-quality generated graphs and reduced computational costs.
a70148376be4bea44ff6fd074c83e661b6734715.proposed_method: A novel Graph Spectral Diffusion Model (GSDM) will be developed to generate graphs by applying stochastic differential equations (SDEs) in both the node feature space and the graph spectrum (eigenvalue) space. Instead of corrupting the entire adjacency matrix with isotropic Gaussian noise, the method confines the noise insertion to the eigenvalue matrix of the adjacency matrix, leveraging the low-rank structure inherent in many real-world graphs. Two separate neural networks will be trained to estimate the score functions for node features and the graph spectrum, enabling the reversed-time diffusion process to generate new graph samples. The method also supports an efficient variant by truncating the spectrum to the top-k eigenvalues, further reducing computational complexity. Theoretical analysis will be provided to demonstrate that the spectral diffusion approach offers sharper reconstruction error bounds compared to standard diffusion models.
a70148376be4bea44ff6fd074c83e661b6734715.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world graph datasets, including Community-small, Enzymes, and Grid for generic graph generation, as well as QM9 and ZINC250k for molecular graph generation. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines, including autoregressive models (DeepGMG, GraphRNN, GraphAF, GraphDF) and one-shot models (GraphVAE, GNF, EDP-GNN, GDSS, MoFlow, GraphEBM). Evaluation metrics will include maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) for graph statistics, Frechet ChemNet Distance (FCD), Neighborhood Subgraph Pairwise Distance Kernel (NSPDK) MMD, validity (with and without correction), and generation time. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of diffusion step numbers, diffusion schedules, and low-rank spectrum truncation. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by adopting consistent train/test splits and hyperparameter tuning protocols.
a70148376be4bea44ff6fd074c83e661b6734715.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel spectral diffusion framework that operates in the eigenvalue space of the graph adjacency matrix, fundamentally differing from existing full-rank diffusion models. This method is theoretically proven to provide significantly sharper reconstruction error bounds (O(n exp(n)) vs. O(n^2 exp(n^2))) and empirically achieves state-of-the-art generation quality and computational efficiency. The model is robust to diffusion schedule choices and supports scalable low-rank approximations, enabling efficient training and inference on large-scale graphs. These innovations collectively advance the field of graph generative modeling by addressing both quality and efficiency in a unified framework.

a7204bde93700156e9c828758425736cd203f36d.title: A Finite-Particle Convergence Rate for Stein Variational Gradient Descent
a7204bde93700156e9c828758425736cd203f36d.research_question: What is the explicit, non-asymptotic convergence rate of Stein Variational Gradient Descent (SVGD) when using a finite number of particles to approximate a target probability distribution under mild and practical assumptions on the target and kernel?
a7204bde93700156e9c828758425736cd203f36d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, under sub-Gaussian target distributions with Lipschitz score functions and kernels with bounded derivatives, SVGD with a finite number of particles and an appropriate step size sequence can drive the kernel Stein discrepancy (KSD) to zero at a quantifiable rate, specifically of order 1/sqrt(log log n), where n is the number of particles.
a7204bde93700156e9c828758425736cd203f36d.proposed_method: A rigorous theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the convergence of finite-particle SVGD. The approach will first bound the discretization error between the finite-particle and continuous SVGD in the 1-Wasserstein distance by leveraging pseudo-Lipschitz properties of the SVGD update map and moment growth control. Next, the kernel Stein discrepancy (KSD) will be explicitly bounded in terms of the 1-Wasserstein distance and the moments of the particle distribution. These results will be combined with existing continuous SVGD convergence analyses to derive explicit, non-asymptotic error bounds for the finite-particle case. The analysis will require only mild assumptions: the target distribution is sub-Gaussian with a Lipschitz score, and the kernel has bounded and decaying derivatives.
a7204bde93700156e9c828758425736cd203f36d.experiment_details: Theoretical results will be validated through experiments using SVGD on standard benchmark distributions where the target is sub-Gaussian and the kernel is chosen to satisfy the required assumptions (e.g., Gaussian or inverse multiquadric kernels). Particle initializations will be sampled i.i.d. from auxiliary distributions or constructed deterministically. The primary evaluation metric will be the kernel Stein discrepancy (KSD) between the empirical particle distribution and the target, tracked as a function of the number of particles and step size schedules. Comparisons will be made to existing asymptotic and non-explicit convergence bounds in the literature to demonstrate the tightness and explicitness of the proposed rates.
a7204bde93700156e9c828758425736cd203f36d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first unified, explicit, and non-asymptotic convergence rate for finite-particle SVGD under practical and mild assumptions. The approach provides a constructive proof strategy that yields a 1/sqrt(log log n) rate for the decay of the kernel Stein discrepancy, improving upon prior work that only established asymptotic or implicit rates. The proof techniques are broadly applicable and may serve as a template for future refinements or for establishing lower bounds. This work also relaxes some of the strong assumptions used in previous analyses, making the results more relevant for practical SVGD applications.

a72ba8dc49a6a842f69c312ac9a037a0f33b74f5.title: The Clock and the Pizza: Two Stories in Mechanistic Explanation of Neural Networks
a72ba8dc49a6a842f69c312ac9a037a0f33b74f5.research_question: Under what conditions do neural networks trained on algorithmic tasks, such as modular addition, discover familiar or novel algorithms, and how can the diversity of these learned algorithms be systematically characterized and distinguished?
a72ba8dc49a6a842f69c312ac9a037a0f33b74f5.hypothesis: Neural networks trained on modular arithmetic tasks can implement a variety of qualitatively distinct algorithms, including both known solutions (such as the Clock algorithm) and novel procedures (such as the Pizza algorithm), with the choice of algorithmic solution determined by model architecture, hyperparameters, and initialization.
a72ba8dc49a6a842f69c312ac9a037a0f33b74f5.proposed_method: The proposed research will systematically train neural networks on modular addition tasks, varying key architectural components (such as attention mechanisms and layer width) and hyperparameters (such as attention rate). Models will be analyzed using mechanistic interpretability techniques, including principal component analysis of learned embeddings, gradient-based measures of model symmetry, and logit pattern visualization. Two key metrics—gradient symmetricity and distance irrelevance—will be developed and applied to automatically distinguish between different algorithmic solutions implemented by the networks. Circle isolation techniques will be used to dissect the embedding space and reveal the presence of multiple, parallel algorithmic implementations within a single model. The research will also investigate phase transitions in algorithmic behavior as a function of model parameters, and explore the emergence of both circular and non-circular algorithmic solutions.
a72ba8dc49a6a842f69c312ac9a037a0f33b74f5.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training one-layer and multi-layer transformer models (with and without attention) on modular addition tasks, using a modulus p=59. Both learned embedding vectors and network parameters will be analyzed post-training. The main datasets will consist of all possible modular addition problems over the chosen modulus. Baseline comparisons will include models with different attention rates (ranging from 0 to 1), varying layer widths (32 to 512), and different numbers of layers (2 to 4). Evaluation metrics will include model accuracy, the fraction of variance explained by analytic formulas for known algorithms (Clock and Pizza), gradient symmetricity, and distance irrelevance. Additional analyses will use principal component projections and circle isolation to interpret embedding structures and logit patterns. Experiments will be repeated across multiple random seeds to assess the diversity and robustness of discovered algorithms.
a72ba8dc49a6a842f69c312ac9a037a0f33b74f5.novelty_claims: The research introduces a systematic framework for distinguishing and characterizing multiple algorithmic solutions learned by neural networks on the same task, including the discovery and mechanistic explanation of a previously undescribed 'Pizza' algorithm. It proposes new quantitative metrics (gradient symmetricity and distance irrelevance) for automatic classification of network algorithmic phases, and demonstrates the existence of sharp phase transitions between different algorithmic solutions as model hyperparameters are varied. The work also reveals that neural networks can ensemble multiple algorithmic procedures in parallel and identifies conditions under which non-circular, previously uncharacterized algorithms emerge. These contributions advance the field of mechanistic interpretability by enabling automated, fine-grained analysis of algorithmic diversity in neural networks.

a75649771901a4881b44c0ceafa469fcc6e6f968.title: How Can We Know What Language Models Know?
a75649771901a4881b44c0ceafa469fcc6e6f968.research_question: How can the knowledge contained in language models be more accurately estimated, specifically by improving the process of querying them for factual information?
a75649771901a4881b44c0ceafa469fcc6e6f968.hypothesis: Automatically generating and selecting diverse, high-quality prompts—using mining and paraphrasing techniques, as well as ensembling multiple prompts—will provide a tighter lower bound on the factual knowledge stored in language models than relying on manually crafted prompts.
a75649771901a4881b44c0ceafa469fcc6e6f968.proposed_method: A systematic approach is developed to automatically generate prompts for querying language models about factual knowledge. Two primary methods are proposed: (1) mining-based prompt generation, which extracts candidate prompts from large corpora (such as Wikipedia) by identifying sentences containing both subject and object entities and extracting relational phrases using middle-word and dependency-based strategies; and (2) paraphrasing-based prompt generation, which diversifies seed prompts through back-translation, yielding semantically similar expressions. Multiple prompts per relation are then selected and combined using ensemble techniques, including rank-based averaging of log probabilities from top-performing prompts and an optimization-based method that learns prompt weights to maximize object prediction accuracy. The methodology includes ablation studies to assess the contribution of each component and investigates the impact of prompt diversity and POS-based patterns.
a75649771901a4881b44c0ceafa469fcc6e6f968.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the LAMA benchmark, specifically the T-REx and Google-RE subsets, which contain subject-object-relation triples derived from Wikidata. Additional evaluation is performed on the more challenging LAMA-UHN benchmark, which filters out easily guessable facts. The main models probed are BERT-base and BERT-large, with further experiments on ERNIE and KnowBert to assess generality. Baselines include majority-class prediction and manually designed prompts. Evaluation metrics include micro-averaged and macro-averaged accuracy, with macro-averaged accuracy mitigating class imbalance. The experimental setup involves splitting data into training and test sets for prompt mining, selection, and ensemble weight optimization. Ablation studies compare middle-word and dependency-based prompt mining, and cross-model generalization is assessed by transferring prompt ensembles between different model architectures.
a75649771901a4881b44c0ceafa469fcc6e6f968.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces automated methods for mining and paraphrasing prompts, eliminating reliance on manual prompt engineering. It systematically ensembles multiple prompts to exploit the diversity of linguistic expressions, leading to significant improvements in factual knowledge extraction from language models. The approach provides a tighter lower bound on model knowledge, demonstrates generalizability across different language models, and releases a new resource (LPAQA) for future research. The methodology also includes novel analyses of prompt diversity, POS patterns, and cross-model transferability, offering new insights into effective querying of language models.

a757999ed260d7bc45484dc6b4456bf33fe6f679.title: LLaMA-Adapter: Efficient Fine-tuning of Language Models with Zero-init Attention
a757999ed260d7bc45484dc6b4456bf33fe6f679.research_question: How can large language models be efficiently fine-tuned for instruction-following and multi-modal reasoning tasks, while minimizing computational resources and maximizing generalizability across language, vision, and vision-language domains?
a757999ed260d7bc45484dc6b4456bf33fe6f679.hypothesis: Introducing a zero-initialized attention mechanism with learnable gating factors into frozen large language models will enable efficient, stable, and parameter-light fine-tuning for instruction-following and multi-modal tasks, achieving performance comparable to or better than full fine-tuning approaches.
a757999ed260d7bc45484dc6b4456bf33fe6f679.proposed_method: A lightweight fine-tuning framework will be developed by inserting learnable adaptation prompts into the upper transformer layers of a frozen large language model (e.g., LLaMA). In these layers, a novel zero-initialized attention mechanism will be introduced, where a learnable gating factor—initialized at zero—controls the integration of prompt-derived information into the self-attention computation. This gating factor is progressively trained to inject new task-specific signals while preserving the original model knowledge, ensuring stable and effective adaptation. For multi-modal tasks, a pre-trained image encoder (such as CLIP) will extract visual features, which are projected into the word embedding space and element-wise added to the adaptation prompts, allowing the zero-initialized attention to fuse visual and textual information. The approach will also be extended to other pre-trained models (e.g., ViT, RoBERTa, CLIP) for parameter-efficient fine-tuning on traditional vision and language tasks.
a757999ed260d7bc45484dc6b4456bf33fe6f679.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on instruction-following tasks using 52K self-instruct data (as in Alpaca), with fine-tuning performed on a frozen LLaMA-7B model, introducing only 1.2M learnable parameters. Training will be performed on 8 A100 GPUs for 5 epochs, with hyperparameters including batch size 64, learning rate 0.009, and weight decay 0.02. Baselines will include fully fine-tuned Alpaca, Alpaca-LoRA, and other parameter-efficient methods. Evaluation metrics will include GPT-4-based response quality assessment, accuracy on ScienceQA (for multi-modal reasoning), and performance on MME, MMBench, and LVLM-eHub benchmarks for zero-shot multi-modal evaluation. Additional experiments will assess generalizability by fine-tuning ViT on VTAB-1k, RoBERTa on SQuAD, and CLIP on base-to-novel classification, comparing to full fine-tuning and other PEFT methods.
a757999ed260d7bc45484dc6b4456bf33fe6f679.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a zero-initialized attention mechanism with learnable gating factors, enabling highly efficient and stable parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large language models. This approach achieves instruction-following and multi-modal reasoning performance comparable to or surpassing full fine-tuning, while requiring orders of magnitude fewer parameters and significantly less training time. The method is flexible, plug-and-play, and generalizes across language, vision, and vision-language models, demonstrating strong performance on a wide range of benchmarks and tasks.

a75a9a8fa615c0f14cf98279406745ebe58e54d0.title: Latent Policy Barrier: Learning Robust Visuomotor Policies by Staying In-Distribution
a75a9a8fa615c0f14cf98279406745ebe58e54d0.research_question: How can robust visuomotor policies be learned from limited expert demonstrations, such that agents remain in-distribution and recover from out-of-distribution states without requiring labor-intensive human corrections or synthetic data augmentation?
a75a9a8fa615c0f14cf98279406745ebe58e54d0.hypothesis: A latent policy barrier framework that decouples expert imitation from out-of-distribution recovery, using a base policy trained on expert data and a dynamics model trained on both expert and rollout data, will improve the robustness and sample efficiency of visuomotor policy learning compared to existing imitation learning and offline RL methods.
a75a9a8fa615c0f14cf98279406745ebe58e54d0.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a Latent Policy Barrier (LPB) framework for visuomotor policy learning. The approach consists of two main components: (1) a base diffusion policy trained exclusively on high-quality expert demonstrations to ensure precise imitation, and (2) an action-conditioned visual latent dynamics model trained on both expert demonstrations and diverse, automatically generated rollout data from intermediate policy checkpoints. During inference, the agent's current observation is encoded into a latent space, and a latent out-of-distribution (OOD) score is computed as the distance to the nearest expert latent state. If the OOD score exceeds a threshold, gradient-based guidance is applied to the policy's action sampling process, using gradients from the dynamics model to steer predicted future latent states back toward the expert manifold. This process enables real-time correction of deviations without explicit reward signals, additional human input, or policy retraining.
a75a9a8fa615c0f14cf98279406745ebe58e54d0.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a suite of challenging robotic manipulation tasks in both simulated and real-world environments. Simulated benchmarks include Push-T, Robomimic (Square, Tool Hang, Transport), and the multi-task, language-conditioned Libero-10 suite. Real-world evaluations are performed on the Cup Arrangement and Belt Assembly tasks, using both in-distribution and out-of-distribution initial conditions. Baselines for comparison include Expert Behavior Cloning (BC), Mixed BC, Filtered BC, Conservative Q-Learning (CQL), and CCIL. Evaluation metrics focus on task success rates, robustness to action perturbations, and sample efficiency with limited expert demonstrations. The experimental setup includes training the base policy on a fraction (e.g., 20%) of available expert demonstrations, collecting rollout data for the dynamics model, and systematically varying the amount of rollout data and demonstration data to assess performance under different data regimes.
a75a9a8fa615c0f14cf98279406745ebe58e54d0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel latent policy barrier framework that treats the expert demonstration distribution as an implicit barrier in latent space, enabling inference-time policy steering without explicit safety sets, reward functions, or additional human corrections. The method decouples expert imitation from out-of-distribution recovery, leveraging a dynamics model trained on diverse rollout data to provide gradient-based corrections in latent space. This framework improves robustness and sample efficiency, is compatible with off-the-shelf pre-trained policies, and eliminates the need for costly human-in-the-loop interventions or synthetic data augmentation. The approach unifies classifier guidance with model-predictive foresight in a manner that is plug-and-play and does not require policy retraining.

a762bbd712d91458fb300b9bb8744e25b7532f10.title: Alternative Microfoundations for Strategic Classification
a762bbd712d91458fb300b9bb8744e25b7532f10.research_question: How can alternative microfoundations for agent behavior in strategic classification settings be developed to address the limitations of standard rational-agent models, and what properties should these alternatives satisfy to yield more realistic, robust, and socially desirable outcomes in binary classification tasks?
a762bbd712d91458fb300b9bb8744e25b7532f10.hypothesis: Incorporating imperfection and noise into agent response models, rather than assuming perfect rationality and information, will lead to more empirically realistic aggregate responses, robust existence of stable points, and reduced social burden in strategic classification scenarios.
a762bbd712d91458fb300b9bb8744e25b7532f10.proposed_method: A new framework for modeling agent responses in strategic classification will be developed, moving beyond the standard microfoundations of perfectly rational, fully informed agents. The approach will formalize microfoundations as randomized mappings from agent features and labels to response types, each associated with a response function specifying how features are manipulated in response to a classifier. Two key properties will guide the design: aggregate smoothness (ensuring small changes in classifier weights induce smooth changes in aggregate response) and an expenditure constraint (ensuring agents do not spend more on manipulation than the utility gained). Building on these, a noisy response model will be proposed, where each agent best-responds to a perturbed version of the classifier, with the perturbation drawn from a zero-mean noise distribution. This model is inspired by smoothed analysis and empirical observations of imperfect strategic behavior.
a762bbd712d91458fb300b9bb8744e25b7532f10.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using both synthetic and real-world datasets relevant to binary classification, such as credit scoring or online ratings. The proposed noisy response model will be compared against standard microfoundations and other baseline agent response models, including heterogeneous cost functions and approximate best-response variants. Evaluation will focus on the existence and robustness of stable points (performative stability), the smoothness of aggregate response distributions, and the social burden metric (expected manipulation cost for positive instances). Simulations will vary the noise parameter to observe its effect on acceptance thresholds and stability, and empirical estimation of model parameters (noise variance, cost function) will be demonstrated using individual-level data.
a762bbd712d91458fb300b9bb8744e25b7532f10.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a systematic exploration of alternative microfoundations for strategic classification, guided by formal desiderata such as aggregate smoothness and expenditure constraints. The noisy response model is presented as a novel, analytically tractable alternative that incorporates realistic imperfections in agent behavior, leading to robust existence of stable points and lower social burden compared to standard models. The approach provides a principled way to anticipate and mitigate negative externalities in strategic classification, and enables the estimation of aggregate response maps without requiring full deployment of classifiers.

a76ca04997dfde12a84ca37f576db972b26e96b5.title: Listenable Maps for Audio Classifiers
a76ca04997dfde12a84ca37f576db972b26e96b5.research_question: How can posthoc interpretability for audio classifiers be improved to provide faithful, human-understandable, and listenable explanations of model predictions, especially when the classifier operates on non-invertible feature domains such as mel-spectrograms?
a76ca04997dfde12a84ca37f576db972b26e96b5.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a decoder-based approach generating binary masks on the linear spectrogram domain, optimized to maximize classifier confidence on masked-in audio and minimize it on masked-out audio, will yield more faithful and user-preferred listenable interpretations than existing gradient- and masking-based interpretability methods.
a76ca04997dfde12a84ca37f576db972b26e96b5.proposed_method: A novel posthoc interpretability framework for audio classifiers, termed Listenable Maps for Audio Classifiers (L-MAC), will be developed. The method will employ a neural decoder that takes latent representations from a pretrained audio classifier and outputs a binary mask over the linear spectrogram of the input audio. This mask will highlight time-frequency regions most relevant to the classifier's decision. The decoder will be trained using a composite loss: it will maximize the classifier's confidence for the masked-in portion and minimize it for the masked-out portion, with additional regularization promoting mask sparsity and, optionally, audio quality via fine-tuning. The masked spectrogram will be inverted to a waveform using the original phase, producing a listenable audio interpretation. The approach will be feature-agnostic, supporting classifiers operating on various input representations (e.g., mel-spectrograms, FBANKs), and will allow for selective fine-tuning to balance faithfulness and audio quality.
a76ca04997dfde12a84ca37f576db972b26e96b5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ESC-50 and UrbanSound8K datasets for environmental sound classification, using a CNN14 classifier pretrained on VGG-Sound with SimCLR. The decoder will be trained on the same data, with additional experiments on out-of-domain conditions created by mixing samples or adding noise/speech. Baseline comparisons will include gradient-based methods (Saliency, SmoothGrad, Integrated Gradients, GradCAM, Guided Backprop, SHAP) and masking-based methods (L2I). Evaluation metrics will include faithfulness (Average Increase, Average Drop, Average Gain, Faithfulness on Spectra, Input Fidelity), sparsity, and complexity, as well as user studies for subjective preference. Sanity checks such as Remove-and-Retrain and cascading randomization will be performed to validate interpretability. Both quantitative and qualitative assessments will be reported, and the effect of fine-tuning for audio quality will be explored.
a76ca04997dfde12a84ca37f576db972b26e96b5.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first feature-agnostic, decoder-based framework for generating listenable posthoc explanations for audio classifiers, capable of operating even when the classifier uses non-invertible features. The approach uniquely combines classifier faithfulness objectives with the ability to produce human-audible interpretations, and supports selective fine-tuning to improve audio quality without sacrificing interpretability. Extensive experiments and user studies are planned to demonstrate superior faithfulness and user preference compared to existing gradient- and masking-based interpretability methods. The method is also validated with rigorous sanity checks to ensure meaningful attributions.

a7960102c2a8e8c69c1ae34a0ea379ceb5e08414.title: On Minimizing Adversarial Counterfactual Error in Adversarial Reinforcement Learning
a7960102c2a8e8c69c1ae34a0ea379ceb5e08414.research_question: How can reinforcement learning agents be made robust to adversarial perturbations in their observations, particularly in safety-critical environments, without sacrificing performance in benign settings?
a7960102c2a8e8c69c1ae34a0ea379ceb5e08414.hypothesis: Explicitly modeling and minimizing the difference in expected value between adversarial and non-adversarial scenarios, by reasoning over belief distributions about the true state, will yield policies that are both robust to adversarial perturbations and effective in standard conditions.
a7960102c2a8e8c69c1ae34a0ea379ceb5e08414.proposed_method: A novel objective, Adversarial Counterfactual Error (ACoE), is introduced to quantify the difference in expected value between an agent operating under adversarial perturbations (modeled as partial observability) and the same agent in the nominal setting. To make this tractable in model-free deep RL, a surrogate objective called Cumulative-ACoE (C-ACoE) is developed, which can be optimized alongside standard expected reward using established RL algorithms such as PPO and DQN. The approach leverages adversary-aware belief estimation methods (A2B and A3B) to construct belief distributions over possible true states, based on observed states and adversarial attack models. The policy is trained to maximize expected reward while simultaneously minimizing C-ACoE, thus balancing robustness and performance. The method incorporates belief estimation via KL-divergence-based weighting over a neighborhood of candidate true states, and supports both discrete and continuous state spaces, with scalable approximations for practical implementation.
a7960102c2a8e8c69c1ae34a0ea379ceb5e08414.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on standard RL benchmarks including MuJoCo, Atari, and Highway environments. The proposed methods (A2B and A3B) are compared against a suite of strong baselines: PPO, CARRL, RADIAL, WocaR, RAD, and the recent Protected framework, using both PPO and DQN implementations as appropriate. Evaluation is performed under a variety of adversarial attack scenarios: myopic (single-step) attacks such as MAD and PGD, as well as long-horizon, strategic adversaries like PA-AD, Critical Point Attack, and Strategically Timed Attack. Metrics include average episode reward under both unperturbed and adversarial conditions, with results averaged over multiple random seeds and test episodes. The experimental setup ensures fair comparison by controlling for test-time adaptation and providing both standard and ablated baselines.
a7960102c2a8e8c69c1ae34a0ea379ceb5e08414.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the Adversarial Counterfactual Error (ACoE) as a principled objective for adversarial RL, explicitly addressing partial observability induced by adversarial attacks. A scalable surrogate (C-ACoE) is developed for model-free settings, with theoretical justification. The method incorporates adversary-aware belief estimation techniques (A2B and A3B) that leverage KL divergence over action distributions to construct beliefs about the true state. The approach enables robust policy learning without requiring adversary-specific retraining or impractical test-time adaptation, achieving state-of-the-art robustness against both myopic and strategic adversaries across diverse RL benchmarks.

a7caa04c1d5fe264ee24d913f9292201fb87b642.title: Black-box Detection of Backdoor Attacks with Limited Information and Data
a7caa04c1d5fe264ee24d913f9292201fb87b642.research_question: How can backdoor attacks in deep neural network models be detected in a practical black-box setting where only query access to the model is available, and neither the poisoned training data nor model gradients are accessible?
a7caa04c1d5fe264ee24d913f9292201fb87b642.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that backdoor attacks can be effectively detected in a black-box setting by reverse-engineering potential triggers for each class using only model queries, without requiring access to model gradients or training data. Furthermore, it is expected that synthetic data can be used for detection when clean data is unavailable.
a7caa04c1d5fe264ee24d913f9292201fb87b642.proposed_method: A black-box backdoor detection (B3D) framework is proposed that formulates backdoor detection as an optimization problem, aiming to reverse-engineer a potential trigger for each class. The method utilizes a gradient-free optimization algorithm inspired by Natural Evolution Strategies (NES) to estimate the optimal trigger mask and pattern by querying the model and observing its outputs, without access to internal gradients. The trigger mask is modeled as a Bernoulli distribution and the trigger pattern as a Gaussian, allowing discrete-continuous optimization in the black-box setting. For each class, the method searches for a minimal trigger that causes misclassification to the target class, and outlier detection is performed on the L1 norm of the recovered triggers to identify backdoored classes. When clean data is unavailable, synthetic samples are generated (e.g., via generative models or random noise) and optimized to be classified as each class, enabling the same trigger-reversal process (B3D-SS).
a7caa04c1d5fe264ee24d913f9292201fb87b642.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on CIFAR-10, GTSRB, and ImageNet datasets, using hundreds of models including both normally trained and backdoored models with various trigger types and sizes. Baseline methods for comparison include Neural Cleanse (NC) and TABOR, both of which require model gradients. Evaluation metrics include backdoor detection accuracy, attack success rate (ASR), L1 norm of recovered triggers, and area under the ROC curve (AUC) for detecting triggered inputs. The experimental setup will include scenarios with and without access to clean data, as well as ablations on different attack types, model architectures, and data augmentation strategies. Outlier detection for identifying backdoored classes will use both the Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) and heuristic thresholds.
a7caa04c1d5fe264ee24d913f9292201fb87b642.novelty_claims: The proposed method enables practical black-box backdoor detection without requiring access to model gradients or poisoned training data, addressing a significant gap in real-world machine learning service scenarios. The approach introduces a novel gradient-free optimization framework for trigger reversal, supports detection with synthetic data when clean data is unavailable, and demonstrates comparable or superior performance to state-of-the-art white-box methods. Additionally, a simple mitigation strategy is proposed for reliable predictions by rejecting inputs identified as containing triggers, further enhancing model security in the black-box setting.

a7cf7b7ee862b3cb908d581a34ed1a831bba6367.title: Distillation of Discrete Diffusion through Dimensional Correlations
a7cf7b7ee862b3cb908d581a34ed1a831bba6367.research_question: How can the sampling speed of discrete diffusion models be significantly improved while maintaining or enhancing generative quality, particularly by addressing the challenge of capturing dimensional correlations in high-dimensional discrete data?
a7cf7b7ee862b3cb908d581a34ed1a831bba6367.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a mixture model framework, combined with novel loss functions for distillation, can effectively capture dimensional correlations in discrete diffusion models, enabling the distillation of many-step models into few-step models without loss of generative quality.
a7cf7b7ee862b3cb908d581a34ed1a831bba6367.proposed_method: A novel distillation framework, Di4C (Distilling Discrete Diffusion through Dimensional Correlations), will be developed to address the limitations of conventional discrete diffusion models that ignore dimensional correlations for scalability. The method introduces a mixture model architecture capable of representing correlated multivariate categorical distributions by expressing the denoising distribution as an expectation over a family of product models indexed by a latent variable λ. Two key loss functions are proposed: a distillation loss that aligns the student model with the teacher at early time steps, and a consistency loss that encourages the student to match the composition of multiple teacher denoising steps, thus capturing dimensional correlations. The student model is designed to be expressive enough to represent these correlations, and training involves Monte Carlo or control variate approximations for tractable optimization.
a7cf7b7ee862b3cb908d581a34ed1a831bba6367.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across multiple domains to demonstrate generality and effectiveness. On CIFAR-10, a continuous-time discrete-state diffusion model with discretized Gaussian transitions will be used, with the student mixture model distilling a pretrained U-Net teacher. On ImageNet, a VQGAN-based masked diffusion model (MaskGIT) will serve as the teacher, with the student mixture model incorporating the proposed λ-conditioning. For language modeling, pretrained masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) and their distilled variants will be further distilled using Di4C on the OpenWebText dataset. Baselines will include the original teacher models, hybrid models, and existing fast sampling heuristics. Evaluation metrics will include Frechet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS) for images, generative perplexity and Self-BLEU for language, and computational latency. Experimental setups will ensure fair comparison by matching the number of sampling steps and function evaluations.
a7cf7b7ee862b3cb908d581a34ed1a831bba6367.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretically grounded mixture model for discrete diffusion that explicitly captures dimensional correlations, overcoming the expressivity limitations of conventional product models. The proposed loss functions enable effective distillation of many-step models into few-step models, with theoretical guarantees on approximation error and empirical validation across image and language domains. The approach achieves significant speed-ups (up to 2x or more) in sampling with minimal computational overhead and maintains or improves generative quality, representing a substantial advancement in fast discrete generative modeling.

a7f59b2162ae0ea2520753b1b9b17277490a9458.title: Symbolic Discovery of Optimization Algorithms
a7f59b2162ae0ea2520753b1b9b17277490a9458.research_question: How can optimization algorithms for deep neural network training be automatically discovered through symbolic program search, and do such algorithms generalize and outperform existing optimizers across a wide range of tasks and architectures?
a7f59b2162ae0ea2520753b1b9b17277490a9458.hypothesis: Automatically discovered optimization algorithms, formulated as symbolic programs and selected through rigorous search and validation strategies, can achieve superior or comparable performance to state-of-the-art optimizers such as AdamW and Adafactor, while offering improved memory efficiency and generalization across diverse deep learning tasks.
a7f59b2162ae0ea2520753b1b9b17277490a9458.proposed_method: The proposed method formulates the discovery of optimization algorithms as a program search problem, where candidate optimizers are represented as symbolic programs (imperative code with a defined train function operating on weights, gradients, and learning rates). The search space is designed to be flexible, supporting a wide range of mathematical operations and allowing arbitrary use of historical variables. An evolutionary algorithm is employed, utilizing regularized evolution with warm-starts from known optimizers (e.g., AdamW), restarts to escape local optima, and three types of mutations (insertion, deletion, modification of statements or constants). Abstract execution is used to prune invalid or redundant programs, cache semantically equivalent programs, and reduce search cost. Promising candidate optimizers are selected through a funnel process involving increasingly larger meta-validation tasks, and further simplified by removing redundant or minimally impactful statements, yielding interpretable and efficient algorithms.
a7f59b2162ae0ea2520753b1b9b17277490a9458.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of deep learning tasks, including image classification (ImageNet, ImageNet-21K, JFT), vision-language contrastive learning (LiT, BASIC, MSCOCO, Flickr30K), diffusion models for image generation, and language modeling (autoregressive, masked, and fine-tuning tasks). A variety of architectures will be tested, such as ViT, ResNet, Mixer, CoAtNet, and U-Net. Baselines will include AdamW, Adafactor, momentum SGD, and other popular or automatically discovered optimizers. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy, FID for generative models, Recall@K for retrieval, and compute/memory efficiency. Hyperparameters for all optimizers will be carefully tuned, and experiments will be run with multiple seeds and across different batch sizes to assess robustness and generalization. Both proxy tasks (for rapid search) and large-scale target tasks (for final evaluation) will be used.
a7f59b2162ae0ea2520753b1b9b17277490a9458.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a symbolic program search framework for optimizer discovery that enables exploration of an infinite and highly flexible algorithmic space, surpassing previous approaches limited by fixed operand/operator sets or parameterized neural optimizers. The method leverages advanced search strategies (evolution with warm-starts, restarts, abstract execution, and funnel selection) to efficiently identify and generalize high-performing algorithms. The approach yields novel, interpretable, and memory-efficient optimizers (such as Lion) that outperform or match state-of-the-art methods on challenging benchmarks, while providing practical benefits in compute and memory usage. The framework is broadly applicable and can be extended to other algorithm discovery tasks beyond optimization.

a82690177d548e68fb96bb949f3c3ea7f82ef139.title: SoK: Privacy-Preserving Data Synthesis
a82690177d548e68fb96bb949f3c3ea7f82ef139.research_question: How can privacy-preserving data synthesis (PPDS) methods be systematically unified, categorized, and benchmarked to address the challenges of generating synthetic data with strong privacy guarantees and high utility across diverse data types and real-world scenarios?
a82690177d548e68fb96bb949f3c3ea7f82ef139.hypothesis: The integration of statistical and deep learning-based methods under a unified framework, guided by rigorous privacy notions such as differential privacy, enables the development of PPDS algorithms that achieve a favorable privacy-utility trade-off for both structured and unstructured data.
a82690177d548e68fb96bb949f3c3ea7f82ef139.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed to unify and analyze privacy-preserving data synthesis methods, encompassing both statistical approaches (e.g., marginal, copula, projection, and query-based models) and deep learning-based approaches (e.g., auto-encoding, minimax training, optimal transport, feature alignment, and stochastic simulation). The framework will formalize a 'master recipe' consisting of deconstruction (modeling and compact representation selection, with privacy-preserving perturbation) and reconstruction (synthetic data generation). For statistical methods, the approach will dissect model choices and representation strategies for structured data types such as tabular, trajectory, and graph data. For deep learning-based methods, the approach will categorize generative modeling principles and detail privacy enforcement mechanisms (e.g., DP-SGD, DP-EM). The methodology will also include the development of guidelines for method selection based on data type, privacy requirements, and downstream utility needs.
a82690177d548e68fb96bb949f3c3ea7f82ef139.experiment_details: A benchmarking suite will be established to evaluate prominent PPDS methods, particularly deep learning-based approaches, on private image synthesis tasks. Experiments will utilize datasets representative of structured (e.g., tabular, trajectory, graph) and unstructured (e.g., image) data. Baselines will include state-of-the-art statistical and deep learning-based PPDS algorithms, such as DP-MERF, GAN-based models, and marginal/copula-based statistical methods. Evaluation metrics will include fidelity (statistical and structural similarity), utility (performance on downstream tasks such as classification accuracy), and privacy guarantees (e.g., differential privacy parameters). Experimental setup will involve systematic variation of privacy budgets, data dimensionality, and data types to assess trade-offs and generalizability.
a82690177d548e68fb96bb949f3c3ea7f82ef139.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified and systematic framework that bridges statistical and deep learning-based PPDS methods, providing a comprehensive taxonomy, benchmarking, and analysis of design principles, privacy mechanisms, and utility trade-offs. The work aims to deliver actionable guidelines for method selection in diverse real-world scenarios, identify open challenges, and highlight future research directions, including the handling of high-dimensional, unstructured, and mixed-attribute data, as well as the development of task-centric utility metrics and advanced privacy notions for complex data types.

a84ef88c19d8a6f3fdf2064acc406db14aecae24.title: Optimal Linear Decay Learning Rate Schedules and Further Refinements
a84ef88c19d8a6f3fdf2064acc406db14aecae24.research_question: What learning rate schedules yield optimal or near-optimal convergence for a wide class of optimization algorithms, and how can these schedules be further refined to adapt to specific problem characteristics in both convex and non-convex settings?
a84ef88c19d8a6f3fdf2064acc406db14aecae24.hypothesis: A linear decay learning rate schedule is theoretically optimal for last-iterate convergence in a broad class of optimization algorithms, and further refinements based on observed gradient norms can yield problem-adaptive schedules that outperform existing standard schedules in practical machine learning tasks.
a84ef88c19d8a6f3fdf2064acc406db14aecae24.proposed_method: A general analytical framework will be developed to derive optimal learning rate schedules for arbitrary optimization algorithms, focusing on last-iterate convergence rather than average or randomly sampled iterates. The method will establish that a linear decay schedule, where the learning rate at iteration t is proportional to 1 - t/T (with T as the total number of steps), is optimal in the worst-case. To move beyond worst-case analysis, a refinement procedure will be introduced: using gradient norm sequences from a prior training run, a smoothed sequence is computed, and a new, adaptive learning rate schedule is generated by minimizing a novel bound on the final iterate's objective value. This refined schedule incorporates both warm-up and rapid annealing, and can be extended to per-coordinate optimizers such as Adam by adjusting the weighting scheme based on gradient norms.
a84ef88c19d8a6f3fdf2064acc406db14aecae24.experiment_details: A comprehensive empirical evaluation will be conducted across ten diverse deep learning benchmarks, a range of large language models (LLMs), and a suite of convex logistic regression problems from the LIBSVM repository. For each problem, a grid search over baseline learning rates will be performed for each schedule, followed by multiple runs with the best hyperparameters. Baseline schedules will include stepwise, cosine annealing, classical inverse-time, and flat schedules, all with standard warm-up procedures. Evaluation metrics will include test error, test perplexity, accuracy, and other task-appropriate metrics. The refined schedules will be computed using gradient norm logs from initial runs with linear decay, and results will be statistically compared using paired t-tests to establish significance.
a84ef88c19d8a6f3fdf2064acc406db14aecae24.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first systematic, theoretically-grounded approach to deriving both warm-up and annealing behaviors in learning rate schedules directly from analysis, rather than empirical heuristics. The linear decay schedule is established as optimal for last-iterate convergence, closing the gap between theory and practice. The refinement method leverages observed gradient norms to produce problem-adaptive schedules, providing actionable guidance for both convex and non-convex optimization, and is broadly applicable to any base optimizer, including per-coordinate methods like Adam. The proposed empirical evaluation is the most comprehensive comparison of learning rate schedules to date.

a85a0f91474c8848e81393627912341993f6f1d7.title: A Logic for Expressing Log-Precision Transformers
a85a0f91474c8848e81393627912341993f6f1d7.research_question: Can the reasoning capabilities of transformer-based language models, particularly those with precision that scales logarithmically with input length, be fully characterized using a simple logical formalism? What are the logical limits and expressive power of such log-precision transformers?
a85a0f91474c8848e81393627912341993f6f1d7.hypothesis: Log-precision transformer classifiers can be equivalently expressed as sentences in first-order logic extended with majority quantifiers (FO(M)), thus providing a tight upper bound on their reasoning power.
a85a0f91474c8848e81393627912341993f6f1d7.proposed_method: A formal framework will be developed to analyze transformer classifiers whose internal computation precision scales as O(log n) with the context length n. The approach involves modeling the forward computation of such transformers as log-uniform computation graph families, where each component (embedding, self-attention, feedforward, and output classifier) is defined over p-precision floats with p = O(log n). These computation graphs will then be simulated by log-uniform threshold circuit families (TC0), leveraging block-mapping algorithms to translate each transformer component into a corresponding threshold circuit. The established equivalence between log-uniform TC0 and first-order logic with majority quantifiers (FO(M)) will be used to construct, for any log-precision transformer, an FO(M) sentence that computes the same function as the transformer on all input strings.
a85a0f91474c8848e81393627912341993f6f1d7.experiment_details: Theoretical analysis will be conducted to prove the equivalence between log-precision transformers and FO(M) sentences. The methodology includes formal proofs that fixed-precision transformers cannot express uniform attention, while log-precision transformers can, and that any log-precision transformer can be simulated by a log-uniform TC0 circuit family. The logical expressivity will be illustrated with canonical formal language recognition tasks, such as ambm and Dyck languages, and compared against prior results on finite-precision transformers. No empirical datasets or experimental baselines are specified, as the work is theoretical; evaluation is based on formal expressivity and complexity-theoretic arguments.
a85a0f91474c8848e81393627912341993f6f1d7.novelty_claims: This proposal claims the first logical characterization of log-precision transformers, establishing that any such transformer can be equivalently expressed as a sentence in first-order logic with majority quantifiers (FO(M)). It provides the tightest known upper bound on the reasoning power of log-precision transformers, extending prior results beyond finite-precision models. The approach also suggests a new theoretical foundation for mechanistic interpretability of transformers by enabling translation of transformer computations into interpretable logical sentences.

a8724abaf519ab9113cf9dcc4c6d17f984de52cf.title: Generalization in diffusion models arises from geometry-adaptive harmonic representation
a8724abaf519ab9113cf9dcc4c6d17f984de52cf.research_question: How do deep neural network-based diffusion models generalize from finite training data to approximate high-dimensional image densities, and what inductive biases enable this generalization?
a8724abaf519ab9113cf9dcc4c6d17f984de52cf.hypothesis: Diffusion models trained as denoisers with deep neural networks exhibit inductive biases that favor geometry-adaptive harmonic representations, enabling strong generalization and near-optimal denoising performance on image distributions where such bases are optimal.
a8724abaf519ab9113cf9dcc4c6d17f984de52cf.proposed_method: The proposed research will systematically analyze the generalization properties and inductive biases of deep neural network (DNN) denoisers within diffusion models. DNN denoisers will be trained on varying sizes of both natural and synthetic image datasets, including photographic images, geometric Cα images, and images supported on low-dimensional manifolds. The methodology includes eigendecomposition of the denoiser Jacobian to reveal the adaptive basis in which shrinkage occurs, and comparison of these learned bases to known optimal bases (e.g., bandlets for Cα images, tangent spaces for manifolds). The approach will also involve quantifying model variance and bias as a function of training set size and analyzing the asymptotic behavior of denoising error (MSE, PSNR) across noise levels. Theoretical analysis will be complemented by empirical experiments to test the alignment of inductive biases with the underlying data geometry.
a8724abaf519ab9113cf9dcc4c6d17f984de52cf.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training UNet-based DNN denoisers on subsets of the CelebA dataset (downsampled face images) with training set sizes ranging from 1 to 100,000, as well as on synthetic datasets such as geometric Cα images (with varying regularity parameter α) and images of disks parameterized by position, size, and intensity (defining a low-dimensional manifold). Baseline comparisons will include optimal denoisers (where available), soft-thresholding in fixed and adaptive bases, and theoretical lower bounds (oracle denoisers). Evaluation metrics will include mean squared error (MSE), peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), and cosine similarity between generated and training images. The experimental setup will assess generalization by comparing denoising performance on train and test sets, analyzing convergence of model variance, and examining the structure of the learned adaptive bases. Additional experiments will test performance on data with mismatched optimal bases (e.g., shuffled faces) to probe the limits of the inductive bias.
a8724abaf519ab9113cf9dcc4c6d17f984de52cf.novelty_claims: This research proposes a comprehensive framework for understanding generalization in diffusion models through the lens of geometry-adaptive harmonic representations. It claims to provide direct empirical and theoretical evidence that DNN-based diffusion models possess strong inductive biases toward geometry-adaptive harmonic bases, which enable efficient learning and near-optimal denoising on appropriate data distributions. The work introduces a novel analysis of the denoiser Jacobian to reveal the adaptive basis structure and demonstrates that these biases persist even when the optimal basis is suboptimal for the data, leading to predictable forms of suboptimality. The proposal also claims to establish a stronger and more direct measure of generalization in diffusion models than standard train/test performance comparisons.

a87f40a49da377c0d00bebe711e417fc3b1d8969.title: Max-Margin Token Selection in Attention Mechanism
a87f40a49da377c0d00bebe711e417fc3b1d8969.research_question: What are the optimization dynamics and inductive biases of the attention mechanism in transformer architectures, particularly in terms of how attention selects tokens during training? How do these dynamics relate to margin maximization and token selection in both isolated and joint optimization scenarios?
a87f40a49da377c0d00bebe711e417fc3b1d8969.hypothesis: The optimization of attention weights in transformer models, under gradient descent and decreasing loss functions, inherently biases the model toward max-margin solutions that select optimal tokens, and this behavior can be formalized and characterized using connections to support vector machines (SVMs).
a87f40a49da377c0d00bebe711e417fc3b1d8969.proposed_method: A theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted into the optimization landscape of the softmax-based attention mechanism, focusing on the model f(X) = ⟨Xv, softmax(XWp)⟩, where X is the token sequence and (v, W, p) are trainable parameters. The methodology will analyze the convergence properties of gradient descent on the attention weights p (and equivalently W), establishing equivalences with hard-margin SVM problems for both global and local optima. The study will extend to joint optimization of the prediction head v and attention weights p under logistic loss, using regularization path analysis to characterize the implicit bias and convergence trajectories. Theoretical results will be derived under general decreasing loss functions, and new concepts such as locally-optimal tokens and SVM-neighbor sets will be introduced to precisely describe the solution space. Numerical experiments will be designed to validate the theoretical findings and to visualize the evolution of attention weights and sparsity in both synthetic and real-world settings.
a87f40a49da377c0d00bebe711e417fc3b1d8969.experiment_details: Experiments will include both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic experiments will involve constructing token sequences with controlled scores and embeddings to visualize the convergence of gradient descent trajectories and the selection of optimal tokens. Metrics such as the evolution of softmax probabilities, attention weight norms, and sparsity of attention maps will be tracked. For real-world validation, a vision transformer (ViT-base) will be trained from scratch on the CIFAR-10 dataset, and the evolution of attention maps and weight norms will be analyzed over training epochs. Baselines will include standard gradient descent with varying step sizes and normalization schemes. Evaluation metrics will focus on the sparsity of attention, alignment with max-margin solutions, and classification accuracy.
a87f40a49da377c0d00bebe711e417fc3b1d8969.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a rigorous optimization-theoretic framework that connects the dynamics of attention mechanisms in transformers to max-margin SVM formulations, both globally and locally. It formalizes the implicit bias of gradient descent in attention models, introduces new concepts such as locally-optimal max-margin directions and SVM-neighbor tokens, and provides the first comprehensive analysis of joint optimization of attention and prediction head parameters. The work also empirically demonstrates the emergence of sparse, salient token selection in attention maps as a consequence of these dynamics, providing a theoretical explanation for observed phenomena in large language and vision models.

a892c1ac341ec3b03f89692ad8ff28bc143f4548.title: Marginal Tail-Adaptive Normalizing Flows
a892c1ac341ec3b03f89692ad8ff28bc143f4548.research_question: How can the ability of normalizing flows to accurately capture and generate distributions with both heavy-tailed and light-tailed marginals be improved, particularly for applications where modeling tail behavior is critical?
a892c1ac341ec3b03f89692ad8ff28bc143f4548.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by constructing a flexible base distribution with marginals tailored to the estimated tail behavior of the data and employing structured, data-driven linear layers within autoregressive normalizing flows, the resulting model will preserve the marginal tail properties of the target distribution and outperform existing methods in modeling both heavy and light tails.
a892c1ac341ec3b03f89692ad8ff28bc143f4548.proposed_method: The proposed method develops a Marginal Tail-Adaptive Flow (mTAF) framework that begins by estimating the tail index of each marginal in the target data using extreme value theory estimators. Based on these estimates, a flexible base distribution is constructed, where light-tailed marginals are modeled as standard Gaussians and heavy-tailed marginals as t-distributions with estimated or learnable degrees of freedom. The marginals are permuted so that light-tailed and heavy-tailed components are grouped, and a sequence of autoregressive flow layers is applied, interleaved with structured, block-diagonal linear layers that preserve the marginal tail behavior. The method ensures that permutations and linearities within the flow do not mix heavy- and light-tailed marginals, thus guaranteeing the preservation of the desired tail structure. The approach is extended to Neural Spline Flows (NSF) by modifying LU-layers to maintain the marginal tail-adaptive property, and a generalized version (gTAF) is introduced, allowing all marginal degrees of freedom to be learnable for greater flexibility.
a892c1ac341ec3b03f89692ad8ff28bc143f4548.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic data will be generated using high-dimensional Gaussian copulas with controlled numbers of heavy- and light-tailed marginals, allowing precise evaluation of tail modeling. Baselines will include standard normalizing flows (vanilla), Tail-Adaptive Flows (TAF) with a single t-distribution base, and oracle copula models. Evaluation metrics will include negative log-likelihood, area under log-log plots for tail fit, tail Value at Risk (tVaR) differences, and confusion matrices of estimated marginal tail indices from generated samples. For real-world validation, the method will be applied to the high-dimensional EUMETSAT NWP-SAF weather dataset, with performance assessed via likelihood and statistics of random 1D projections (means, standard deviations, quantiles) comparing generated and real data. All models will be trained multiple times for statistical robustness, and architectural details such as the use of NSF and LU-layers will be specified.
a892c1ac341ec3b03f89692ad8ff28bc143f4548.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretically grounded framework for constructing normalizing flows that are provably marginally tail-adaptive, allowing for the accurate modeling of distributions with mixed heavy- and light-tailed marginals. The method is the first to combine extreme value theory-based tail estimation with flexible, data-driven base distributions and structured linearities within autoregressive flows to guarantee preservation of marginal tail behavior. The approach extends to state-of-the-art architectures such as Neural Spline Flows and provides a flexible generalization (gTAF) that can approximate the theoretically optimal structure. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior performance in both tail modeling and sample generation, particularly for extreme events, compared to existing normalizing flow methods.

a8c695d9755a3b514677fef3aa08c08336237560.title: Differentiable Quality Diversity
a8c695d9755a3b514677fef3aa08c08336237560.research_question: How can the efficiency and effectiveness of quality diversity (QD) optimization be improved when both the objective and measure functions are differentiable, and what novel algorithms can leverage gradient information in such settings?
a8c695d9755a3b514677fef3aa08c08336237560.hypothesis: Leveraging first-order gradient information from both objective and measure functions in quality diversity optimization will significantly improve search efficiency and solution quality compared to derivative-free QD algorithms.
a8c695d9755a3b514677fef3aa08c08336237560.proposed_method: A new class of algorithms for differentiable quality diversity (DQD) will be developed, focusing on the introduction of a gradient arborescence approach that exploits the gradients of both the objective and measure functions. Two main variants will be implemented: Objective and Measure Gradient MAP-Elites via Gradient Arborescence (OMG-MEGA), which adapts MAP-Elites to use gradient-based perturbations in both objective and measure spaces, and Covariance Matrix Adaptation MEGA (CMA-MEGA), which integrates CMA-ES adaptation mechanisms to dynamically adjust gradient coefficients for efficient exploration. The algorithms will normalize gradients for stability, tessellate the measure space for archiving, and use evolution strategies to adapt the search direction. Additionally, an Adam-based variant of CMA-MEGA will be explored to enhance optimization in ill-conditioned domains.
a8c695d9755a3b514677fef3aa08c08336237560.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three benchmark domains: linear projection (with sphere and Rastrigin objectives), a high-dimensional robotic arm repertoire (inverse kinematics), and a differentiable latent space illumination (LSI) domain using StyleGAN and CLIP for image generation and evaluation. Each algorithm will be run for a fixed number of iterations (e.g., 10,000) and multiple trials (20 for linear projection and arm repertoire, 5 for LSI). Baselines will include MAP-Elites, MAP-Elites(line), CMA-ME, and newly derived objective-gradient MAP-Elites variants. Evaluation metrics will include QD-score (sum of objective values across the archive, normalized by archive size) and coverage (fraction of occupied cells in the archive). Statistical analyses such as ANOVA will be performed to assess significance of results.
a8c695d9755a3b514677fef3aa08c08336237560.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces and formalizes the differentiable quality diversity (DQD) problem, presenting the first algorithms to leverage first-order gradient information from both objective and measure functions in QD optimization. The gradient arborescence framework and its integration with MAP-Elites and CMA-ES mechanisms represent a novel approach to efficient exploration of the objective-measure space. The work also establishes new differentiable benchmarks for latent space illumination and demonstrates significant empirical improvements over state-of-the-art derivative-free QD algorithms.

a8ca46b171467ceb2d7652fbfb67fe701ad86092.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
a8ca46b171467ceb2d7652fbfb67fe701ad86092.research_question: How can large pre-trained language models be efficiently adapted to downstream tasks with minimal trainable parameters, reduced memory requirements, and no additional inference latency, while maintaining or improving task performance compared to full fine-tuning?
a8ca46b171467ceb2d7652fbfb67fe701ad86092.hypothesis: The adaptation of large language models to downstream tasks can be effectively achieved by constraining the weight updates to a low-rank subspace, allowing for significant reductions in the number of trainable parameters and memory usage without sacrificing model quality or increasing inference latency.
a8ca46b171467ceb2d7652fbfb67fe701ad86092.proposed_method: A novel adaptation framework is proposed wherein the pre-trained weights of a large language model are frozen, and trainable low-rank decomposition matrices are injected into selected dense layers, specifically within the Transformer architecture. For each targeted weight matrix W, its adaptation is parameterized as W + BA, where B and A are trainable matrices of rank r much smaller than the original dimensions of W. During training, only A and B are updated, while the original weights remain fixed, and the low-rank update is initialized to zero. The method allows for merging the low-rank adaptation into the original weights at deployment, ensuring no additional inference latency. The approach is primarily applied to the query and value projection matrices in the self-attention modules for parameter efficiency, but is generalizable to other dense layers.
a8ca46b171467ceb2d7652fbfb67fe701ad86092.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a range of NLP tasks and models, including RoBERTa (base and large), DeBERTa XXL, GPT-2 (medium and large), and GPT-3 (175B). Evaluation covers both natural language understanding (GLUE benchmark) and generation (E2E NLG Challenge, WikiSQL, SAMSum) tasks. Baselines include full fine-tuning, adapter-based methods, BitFit (bias-only tuning), prefix-tuning, and other parameter-efficient adaptation techniques. Metrics such as accuracy, Matthew's correlation, Pearson correlation, BLEU, NIST, METEOR, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, and task-specific scores are used for evaluation. Experiments are performed with consistent batch sizes and sequence lengths to ensure fair comparison, and the impact of varying the rank r and the choice of adapted weight matrices is systematically studied.
a8ca46b171467ceb2d7652fbfb67fe701ad86092.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a low-rank adaptation mechanism that drastically reduces the number of trainable parameters (by up to 10,000 times) and GPU memory requirements (by up to 3 times) compared to full fine-tuning, while matching or surpassing its performance on a variety of tasks and models. Unlike adapter-based methods, the method introduces no additional inference latency, as the low-rank updates can be merged with the original weights. The framework is orthogonal and complementary to other parameter-efficient adaptation methods, and provides new empirical insights into the low intrinsic rank of weight updates during adaptation of large language models.

a8d8c304e21e2c5af66d6e804ce2e649640aedf4.title: Balanced Contrastive Learning for Long-Tailed Visual Recognition
a8d8c304e21e2c5af66d6e804ce2e649640aedf4.research_question: How can visual representation learning be improved for long-tailed data distributions to achieve balanced and effective recognition across both majority and minority classes?
