a8d8c304e21e2c5af66d6e804ce2e649640aedf4.hypothesis: A contrastive learning framework that explicitly balances representation learning through class-averaging and class-complement strategies, and combines this with classifier logit compensation, will yield more regular and equitable feature spaces, leading to improved performance on long-tailed visual recognition tasks.
a8d8c304e21e2c5af66d6e804ce2e649640aedf4.proposed_method: A two-branch framework is proposed for long-tailed visual recognition. The first branch employs a novel Balanced Contrastive Learning (BCL) loss, which incorporates two key mechanisms: class-averaging, to balance the gradient contributions of negative classes in each mini-batch, and class-complement, to ensure that all classes (including those not present in the current batch) are represented via class prototypes in every mini-batch. This design encourages the feature representations of all classes to form a regular simplex configuration on the hypersphere, mitigating the dominance of head classes and promoting class-independent feature separation. The second branch is a classification module trained with cross-entropy loss augmented by logit compensation, which adjusts the classifier's output logits according to class priors to further address bias toward majority classes. Both branches share a backbone encoder, and the prototypes for class-complement are derived from the classifier weights after a nonlinear transformation. The entire system is optimized end-to-end.
a8d8c304e21e2c5af66d6e804ce2e649640aedf4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several benchmark datasets with long-tailed distributions, including CIFAR-10-LT, CIFAR-100-LT, ImageNet-LT, and iNaturalist 2018. Standard backbone architectures such as ResNet-32, ResNet-50, and ResNeXt-50 will be used. The evaluation will include overall top-1 accuracy as well as per-group accuracy (Many-shot, Medium-shot, Few-shot) to assess performance across head and tail classes. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art long-tailed learning methods such as re-sampling, re-weighting, logit adjustment, decoupled training, and other contrastive learning approaches (e.g., Hybrid-SC, PaCo, RIDE, Balanced Softmax, LDAM-DRW, BBN). Ablation studies will be performed to isolate the effects of class-averaging, class-complement, and the combination thereof. Training details such as batch size, learning rate schedules, data augmentation strategies, and optimization hyperparameters will be aligned with prior work for fair comparison.
a8d8c304e21e2c5af66d6e804ce2e649640aedf4.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretically grounded balanced contrastive loss that ensures feature representations of all classes form a regular simplex, regardless of class frequency, directly addressing the geometric imbalance induced by standard supervised contrastive learning on long-tailed data. The combination of class-averaging and class-complement in the contrastive loss is novel and shown to be essential for achieving class-independent optimization. The integration of this balanced contrastive learning with a classifier branch employing logit compensation in a unified, end-to-end framework is also innovative. The method is expected to yield state-of-the-art performance on long-tailed visual recognition benchmarks, particularly improving both head and tail class accuracy without sacrificing one for the other.

a94e3930e0f13e835624f9021ed7d91408d994ff.title: MeMOTR: Long-Term Memory-Augmented Transformer for Multi-Object Tracking
a94e3930e0f13e835624f9021ed7d91408d994ff.research_question: How can multi-object tracking in videos be improved by more effectively leveraging long-term temporal information, particularly in challenging scenarios with complex motion patterns and frequent occlusions?
a94e3930e0f13e835624f9021ed7d91408d994ff.hypothesis: Explicitly modeling and injecting long-term temporal information into the object tracking process will yield more stable and discriminative track embeddings, thereby improving target association and overall tracking performance, especially in complex and crowded scenarios.
a94e3930e0f13e835624f9021ed7d91408d994ff.proposed_method: A long-term memory-augmented Transformer framework, termed MeMOTR, will be developed for multi-object tracking. The approach will utilize a ResNet-50 backbone and a Transformer encoder to extract image features, followed by a separated Detection Decoder to generate semantically meaningful detect embeddings. For each tracked object, a long-term memory will be maintained and updated using an exponential moving average, capturing temporal features across frames. A Temporal Interaction Module will inject this memory into subsequent track embeddings, and a memory-attention layer will be employed to enhance discriminability among multiple tracked targets. Additionally, adaptive aggregation will fuse object features from adjacent frames to further improve robustness against occlusion and blurring.
a94e3930e0f13e835624f9021ed7d91408d994ff.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple benchmarks, including DanceTrack (focused on association challenges), MOT17 (pedestrian tracking), and BDD100K (multi-category tracking). The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art tracking-by-detection and Transformer-based baselines, such as ByteTrack, OC-SORT, MOTR, and MOTRv2. Evaluation metrics will include HOTA, AssA, MOTA, IDF1, and TETA, with particular emphasis on association accuracy. The experimental setup will involve training with data augmentations, using both standard and anchor-based Deformable-DETR variants, and extensive ablation studies will be performed to analyze the impact of each component, including memory update rate, decoder structure, and aggregation strategies.
a94e3930e0f13e835624f9021ed7d91408d994ff.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel long-term memory mechanism for Transformer-based multi-object tracking, enabling explicit modeling and injection of temporal information over extended sequences. The approach features a customized memory-attention layer for enhanced target discriminability and a separated detection decoder to resolve semantic conflicts between detection and tracking queries. Extensive experiments demonstrate significant improvements in association metrics over prior methods, particularly in scenarios with complex motion and occlusion, establishing new state-of-the-art results on challenging MOT benchmarks.

a95ee02fd85a3734bf19bb4bbc6ef3ea22c96cc9.title: PMET: Precise Model Editing in a Transformer
a95ee02fd85a3734bf19bb4bbc6ef3ea22c96cc9.research_question: How can model editing in large language models (LLMs) be made more precise and reliable, particularly by addressing the limitations of current methods that update model weights based on hidden states containing irrelevant information?
a95ee02fd85a3734bf19bb4bbc6ef3ea22c96cc9.hypothesis: Simultaneously optimizing the hidden states of both Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) and Feed-Forward Network (FFN) components in transformer layers, while restricting weight updates to the FFN using only its optimized hidden states, will enable more precise and reliable model editing compared to existing approaches that use broader hidden state information.
a95ee02fd85a3734bf19bb4bbc6ef3ea22c96cc9.proposed_method: A new model editing framework, PMET, is proposed for transformer-based LLMs. The approach involves analyzing and optimizing the hidden states of both the MHSA and FFN components in the critical layers of the transformer. During the editing process, optimizable parameters are added to the TC (Transformer Component) hidden states of both MHSA and FFN, but only the optimized TC hidden states of FFN are used to update FFN weights. The optimization objective balances the retention of existing knowledge with the integration of new target knowledge, using a least-squares formulation for weight updates. The method employs a square root spreading strategy to propagate residuals across critical layers, ensuring precise and efficient knowledge edits while minimizing unwanted side effects on unrelated knowledge.
a95ee02fd85a3734bf19bb4bbc6ef3ea22c96cc9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on GPT-J (6B) and GPT-NeoX (20B) models using the COUNTERFACT and zsRE datasets. Baseline comparisons will include Constrained Fine-Tuning (FT+W), MEND (learning-based), ROME, and MEMIT (optimization-based). Evaluation metrics will cover efficacy (success on edited knowledge), generalization (success on paraphrased knowledge), specificity (preservation of unrelated knowledge), fluency, and consistency. Editing performance will be assessed across varying numbers of edits (from 1K to 10K), and ablation studies will be performed to analyze the contribution of optimizing MHSA, the effect of spreading strategies, and the impact of updating different components. Implementation will focus on updating only the critical layers identified in prior work, and all parameter settings will be consistent with established baselines.
a95ee02fd85a3734bf19bb4bbc6ef3ea22c96cc9.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the simultaneous optimization of MHSA and FFN hidden states for model editing, while restricting weight updates to the FFN, addressing the issue of irrelevant information flow in previous approaches. The method provides a more precise update mechanism by leveraging the general knowledge extraction patterns of MHSA without modifying its weights, and employs a square root residual spreading strategy for more effective propagation of edits across layers. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in reliability and consistency, with a favorable balance between reliability and specificity compared to existing methods. The approach also contributes new insights into the distinct roles of MHSA and FFN in knowledge storage and extraction within LLMs.

a964d6d1e2e8c93d04a2b7e6da3d906537d537bc.title: ProxSparse: Regularized Learning of Semi-Structured Sparsity Masks for Pretrained LLMs
a964d6d1e2e8c93d04a2b7e6da3d906537d537bc.research_question: How can semi-structured sparsity masks for large pretrained language models be learned in a globally optimal and efficient manner, improving both model performance and deployment efficiency without extensive retraining?
a964d6d1e2e8c93d04a2b7e6da3d906537d537bc.hypothesis: A regularized, learning-based optimization framework that incorporates global feedback and smooth mask selection will produce more effective semi-structured sparsity masks for pretrained LLMs than existing heuristic or local methods, leading to improved accuracy and efficiency without the need for additional weight updates after mask determination.
a964d6d1e2e8c93d04a2b7e6da3d906537d537bc.proposed_method: A novel framework, ProxSparse, will be developed to learn semi-structured sparsity masks for pretrained LLMs through end-to-end regularized optimization. The method will transform the non-differentiable mask selection process into a smooth, learnable procedure by introducing two key regularizers: one to enforce the semi-structured (e.g., 2:4) sparsity pattern, and another to penalize deviation from the original pretrained weights. Proximal gradient descent will be employed to alternate between gradient steps on the loss and efficient proximal updates for the regularizers, using a newly designed alternating minimization (ALM) algorithm for the structured sparsity operator. The approach will leverage a small calibration dataset (hundreds of samples) and will not require any further weight updates after the mask is finalized, ensuring computational efficiency and scalability to models with billions of parameters.
a964d6d1e2e8c93d04a2b7e6da3d906537d537bc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on seven widely used open-source LLMs from four model families (Mistral, Qwen, OpenLlama, Llama), evaluating both language modeling (Wikitext perplexity) and seven zero-shot natural language reasoning tasks (using EleutherAI LM-Eval-Harness). The method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines including magnitude pruning, SparseGPT, Wanda, and MaskLLM, with consistent calibration sample sizes (typically 400) for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics will include perplexity, zero-shot task accuracy, inference speedup (using Nvidia A100 GPUs and CUTLASS for 2:4 sparsity), and memory footprint reduction. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of regularization strength, calibration sample size, and the individual contributions of each regularizer.
a964d6d1e2e8c93d04a2b7e6da3d906537d537bc.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a globally optimized, learning-based approach for semi-structured mask selection that leverages end-to-end gradient feedback, overcoming the limitations of local, heuristic-based methods. A new efficient proximal operator for 2:4 sparsity is developed, enabling scalable optimization for LLMs. The approach requires only a small calibration dataset and no additional weight updates post-mask selection, making it practical for large models. Experiments demonstrate consistent and significant improvements in both perplexity and zero-shot task accuracy over previous state-of-the-art methods, as well as substantial gains in inference speed and memory efficiency.

a967e3dac337941e1618b7103c0aada0fc17687f.title: Compositional Generalization Across Distributional Shifts with Sparse Tree Operations
a967e3dac337941e1618b7103c0aada0fc17687f.research_question: How can a unified neurosymbolic architecture be developed to achieve robust compositional generalization across a wide variety of distributional shifts, while maintaining scalability and flexibility for both tree-structured and sequence-to-sequence tasks?
a967e3dac337941e1618b7103c0aada0fc17687f.hypothesis: A unified neurosymbolic model that represents symbolic structures and operations directly in vector space, using sparse representations and efficient differentiable tree operations, will achieve superior compositional generalization and scalability compared to both fully neural and hybrid neurosymbolic baselines, especially in out-of-distribution settings.
a967e3dac337941e1618b7103c0aada0fc17687f.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces Sparse Coordinate Trees (SCT), a novel vector-space schema for representing binary trees as sparse tensors, enabling efficient and memory-saving structural operations. A library of differentiable tree operations (left, right, cons) is defined, implemented via efficient indexing, bit-shifting, and addition over sparse indices, allowing compositional manipulation of tree structures in vector space. The architecture, termed the Sparse Differentiable Tree Machine (sDTM), consists of an agent (a Transformer encoder), an interpreter (applying weighted tree operations), and a memory module. Pooling by multi-headed attention is used to encode trees of arbitrary size into fixed-dimensional representations, with tree position information incorporated via concatenation of binary positional encodings. The model is further extended to handle sequence-to-sequence tasks by converting sequences into trees using either parsing or left-aligned uniform-depth (LAUD) embeddings, and regularization is applied through lexical noise and pruning of tree nodes to maintain sparsity.
a967e3dac337941e1618b7103c0aada0fc17687f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of compositional generalization benchmarks, including tree-to-tree (Active↔Logical, FOR2LAM), sequence-to-tree (GeoQuery), and sequence-to-sequence (SCAN) tasks. Baselines for comparison include standard Transformer models, Relative Universal Transformers (RU-Transformer), and a hybrid neurosymbolic system (NQG). Evaluation will cover both in-distribution (IID) and multiple out-of-distribution (OOD) splits, such as zero-shot and one-shot lexical generalization, structural/length generalization, template shifts, and maximum compound divergence (MCD). Metrics will primarily be exact match accuracy, with experiments repeated over multiple random seeds to assess robustness. Additional analyses will compare parameter count, memory usage, and inference speed between the proposed sDTM, the original DTM, and baseline models. Pruning hyperparameters and pooling strategies will be ablated to assess their impact on performance and efficiency.
a967e3dac337941e1618b7103c0aada0fc17687f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces Sparse Coordinate Trees (SCT) as a new, memory-efficient vector-space representation for tree structures, enabling scalable and efficient differentiable tree operations. The Sparse Differentiable Tree Machine (sDTM) unifies symbolic and neural computation in a single architecture, supporting both tree-structured and sequence-to-sequence tasks. The approach achieves significant reductions in parameter count and memory usage compared to prior neurosymbolic models, while maintaining or improving generalization performance across a wide range of distributional shifts. The method is uniquely capable of robust zero-shot lexical generalization and demonstrates flexibility not present in prior hybrid or fully neural systems.

a99c08bb5aeca6abd4844ef60fa05c8d1b3122c4.title: Differentially Private Relational Learning with Entity-level Privacy Guarantees
a99c08bb5aeca6abd4844ef60fa05c8d1b3122c4.research_question: How can relational learning on network-structured data be performed with rigorous entity-level differential privacy guarantees, while maintaining strong utility-privacy trade-offs?
a99c08bb5aeca6abd4844ef60fa05c8d1b3122c4.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a tailored DP-SGD algorithm, incorporating adaptive gradient clipping and a carefully designed negative sampling strategy, can provide formal entity-level differential privacy guarantees for relational learning, while achieving better utility-privacy trade-offs compared to standard approaches.
a99c08bb5aeca6abd4844ef60fa05c8d1b3122c4.proposed_method: A novel differentially private stochastic gradient descent (DP-SGD) variant will be developed specifically for relational learning tasks with entity-level privacy guarantees. The method will include a rigorous sensitivity analysis of the contrastive loss used in relational learning, accounting for the fact that entities may participate in multiple positive and negative relations. To control sensitivity, an adaptive gradient clipping scheme will be introduced, where the clipping threshold for each gradient is modulated based on the frequency of entity occurrences within each mini-batch. Furthermore, a negative sampling strategy will be employed that restricts each node to appear at most once in the negative edges of a mini-batch, enabling tight sensitivity control. The privacy amplification analysis will be extended to a subclass of coupled sampling—where the dependence between positive and negative sampling arises solely from sample sizes—allowing for tractable privacy bounds under this multi-stage sampling process. The overall approach will integrate these elements into a DP-SGD framework for relational learning, ensuring provable entity-level privacy.
a99c08bb5aeca6abd4844ef60fa05c8d1b3122c4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on fine-tuning pre-trained text encoders (such as BERT and Llama2) on text-attributed, network-structured relational datasets. Four real-world datasets will be used, including two citation networks (MAG-CHN, MAG-USA) and two co-purchase networks (AMAZ-Sports, AMAZ-Cloth). The method will be evaluated by training on one network and testing on another within the same domain, simulating zero-shot relation prediction. Baselines will include non-private fine-tuning, standard DP-SGD with per-sample gradient clipping, and models without fine-tuning. Evaluation metrics will be top-1 precision (PREC@1) and mean reciprocal rank (MRR) for relation prediction. The maximal node degree will be capped for privacy, and various privacy budgets (ε) will be tested. Ablation studies will examine the effect of the number of negative samples, node degree capping, and noise multiplier on utility and privacy.
a99c08bb5aeca6abd4844ef60fa05c8d1b3122c4.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled framework for relational learning with formal entity-level differential privacy guarantees, addressing the unique challenges of high sensitivity and coupled sampling in relational data. Key innovations include a frequency-based adaptive gradient clipping scheme that dynamically adjusts clipping thresholds based on entity participation, and a negative sampling strategy that restricts node occurrences to tightly control sensitivity. The privacy amplification analysis is extended to a tractable subclass of coupled sampling, providing the first privacy amplification bounds for this setting. The resulting DP-SGD variant is tailored for relational learning and demonstrates superior utility-privacy trade-offs compared to existing approaches.

a99dee9602e21a71526b9681d8dba37c55b66941.title: SFT Memorizes, RL Generalizes: A Comparative Study of Foundation Model Post-training
a99dee9602e21a71526b9681d8dba37c55b66941.research_question: How do supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) as post-training methods for foundation models differ in their effects on generalization and memorization, particularly in rule-based reasoning and visual reasoning tasks across both language and vision-language domains?
a99dee9602e21a71526b9681d8dba37c55b66941.hypothesis: RL-based post-training leads to improved generalization in both rule-based and visual reasoning tasks, while SFT-based post-training primarily results in memorization of training data and limited out-of-distribution generalization. SFT may still play a stabilizing role in enabling effective RL training.
a99dee9602e21a71526b9681d8dba37c55b66941.proposed_method: A comparative experimental framework will be established to systematically evaluate the effects of SFT and RL post-training on both large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs). The methodology involves first initializing models with SFT on instruction-formatted, task-specific datasets to adapt output formats, followed by RL using a multi-turn, outcome-based reward structure with a verifier that provides feedback and rewards based on task success. RL will be implemented using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) in a sequential revision setting, where the model iteratively refines its outputs based on verifier feedback. Both rule-based (textual) and visual generalization will be assessed by introducing controlled variations in task rules and visual inputs. The impact of scaling inference-time compute (e.g., number of verification steps) and the necessity of SFT initialization for RL will also be systematically investigated.
a99dee9602e21a71526b9681d8dba37c55b66941.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two primary tasks: GeneralPoints, a custom arithmetic reasoning card game with both text and image input variants, and V-IRL, a real-world navigation environment with language and vision-language settings. For GeneralPoints, models will be trained on one set of rules or card colors and tested on out-of-distribution variants (e.g., different rules or card colors). For V-IRL, models will be trained on navigation routes in one city and evaluated on routes from other cities, as well as across different action space configurations. Baselines will include models trained with only SFT, only RL, and a combination of both, with performance compared to prior state-of-the-art methods. Evaluation metrics will include episode success rate, per-step accuracy, and visual recognition accuracy, with detailed ablations on the number of verification steps and the effect of SFT initialization. The backbone model will be Llama-3.2-Vision-11B, and all experiments will be run with matched computational budgets.
a99dee9602e21a71526b9681d8dba37c55b66941.novelty_claims: The proposed study offers the first comprehensive, controlled comparison of SFT and RL as post-training methods for both LLMs and VLMs, explicitly disentangling memorization from generalization across both rule-based and visual domains. It introduces a novel evaluation environment (GeneralPoints) and leverages multi-turn RL with verifier-based outcome rewards to rigorously assess generalization. The work claims to demonstrate that RL, especially when initialized with SFT, achieves superior out-of-distribution generalization and visual recognition, while SFT alone leads to overfitting and memorization. The study also identifies the critical role of SFT in stabilizing RL training and highlights the importance of scaling inference-time verification for enhanced generalization.

a99e31c41c6533b916cd021455951768d75b4fc0.title: Improving black-box optimization in VAE latent space using decoder uncertainty
a99e31c41c6533b916cd021455951768d75b4fc0.research_question: How can black-box optimization in the latent space of variational autoencoders (VAEs) be improved to generate high-dimensional discrete objects that maximize a target property, while ensuring the validity and quality of generated samples?
a99e31c41c6533b916cd021455951768d75b4fc0.hypothesis: Incorporating robust estimates of decoder epistemic uncertainty into the latent space optimization process will improve the trade-off between maximizing the black-box objective and ensuring the validity and quality of generated objects, compared to approaches that do not account for decoder uncertainty.
a99e31c41c6533b916cd021455951768d75b4fc0.proposed_method: A novel importance sampling-based estimator for epistemic uncertainty in high-dimensional, structured output spaces will be developed to quantify the decoder's uncertainty in VAEs. This estimator will be used to guide the optimization process in latent space by either penalizing or censoring candidate latent points with high decoder uncertainty. The approach will be integrated into both Bayesian Optimization (by modifying the surrogate objective or censoring proposals) and gradient ascent (by constraining moves in latent space based on uncertainty thresholds). The method requires no changes to the VAE architecture or training procedure and is agnostic to the data representation (sequences or graphs). The importance sampling estimator will leverage samples from the posterior predictive distribution to provide low-variance, tractable estimates of mutual information between decoder parameters and outputs, enabling effective identification of out-of-distribution or unreliable regions in latent space.
a99e31c41c6533b916cd021455951768d75b4fc0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across three domains: digit image generation (using MNIST digits), arithmetic expression approximation (using a formal grammar to generate expressions), and molecular generation for drug discovery (using SMILES and graph representations from the ZINC dataset). For each domain, VAEs with appropriate architectures (e.g., Conv-Deconv for images, Character VAE for sequences, JunctionTreeVAE for graphs) will be trained, and black-box objectives relevant to each domain will be defined (e.g., digit thickness, expression MSE, penalized logP for molecules). Baselines will include standard latent space optimization (ignoring decoder uncertainty) and prior-likelihood-based censoring (NLLP). The effectiveness of the uncertainty-guided approach will be evaluated using metrics such as objective value, validity percentage of generated samples, and, for molecules, additional quality filters. Multiple runs with different random seeds will be performed, and results will be compared across uncertainty estimators (importance sampling vs. token independence) and optimization strategies.
a99e31c41c6533b916cd021455951768d75b4fc0.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a general-purpose, importance sampling-based estimator for epistemic uncertainty in high-dimensional structured data, enabling robust uncertainty quantification in VAE decoders. The approach is architecture- and representation-agnostic, requiring no modifications to model training or structure. By integrating decoder uncertainty into latent space optimization, the method achieves a superior trade-off between maximizing black-box objectives and maintaining sample validity and quality, outperforming prior approaches that rely on heuristics or prior likelihoods. The estimator and optimization framework are broadly applicable to diverse domains and may benefit other applications requiring reliable uncertainty estimates, such as active learning and anomaly detection.

a9a95ed6aae53798bf5164e4ce6e56d22ce28029.title: LLM Data Selection and Utilization via Dynamic Bi-level Optimization
a9a95ed6aae53798bf5164e4ce6e56d22ce28029.research_question: How can data selection and utilization strategies be dynamically optimized during large language model (LLM) training to improve training efficiency and model generalization, beyond static, training-agnostic criteria?
a9a95ed6aae53798bf5164e4ce6e56d22ce28029.hypothesis: Dynamically adjusting the importance of training data samples during LLM training, through a bi-level optimization framework that captures the evolving data preferences of the model, will lead to improved training efficiency and enhanced generalization performance compared to static or pre-training-only data selection methods.
a9a95ed6aae53798bf5164e4ce6e56d22ce28029.proposed_method: A novel plug-and-play Data Weighting Model (DWM) will be developed to assign adaptive weights to data samples within each batch during LLM training, allowing the model to focus on the joint effects and interactions among samples. The DWM will be trained using a dynamic bi-level optimization framework, where the lower level optimizes the LLM with weighted data, and the upper level updates the DWM to maximize validation performance of the updated LLM, leveraging the chain rule for gradient computation. The training process will be divided into multiple stages, with alternating updates of the LLM and DWM to capture the model's evolving data preferences. The DWM will be implemented as a neural network (e.g., Llama-2 architecture with additional attention and linear layers) that takes sample embeddings as input and outputs data weights for each batch, ensuring adaptability and scalability across model sizes and data selection strategies.
a9a95ed6aae53798bf5164e4ce6e56d22ce28029.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the SlimPajama dataset (627B tokens) for pre-training, with models at 370M and 1.3B parameter scales, following the Llama-2 architecture. Data selection baselines will include random selection, DSIR, and QuRating, with DWM applied both to randomly-selected and carefully-selected data. The evaluation will use the lm-evaluation-harness framework, assessing models on nine downstream tasks (e.g., ARC-easy/challenge, SciQA, LogiQA, BoolQ, OBQA, HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande) under zero-shot and two-shot settings, reporting normalized or standard accuracy as appropriate. The training process will be divided into five stages to capture dynamic data preferences, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of static versus dynamic weighting, number of stages, and validation set choices. Transferability of the DWM to larger models and different data selection methods will also be evaluated, with computational overhead carefully measured.
a9a95ed6aae53798bf5164e4ce6e56d22ce28029.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a dynamic, bi-level optimization framework for data weighting during LLM training, enabling the model to adaptively learn and exploit evolving data preferences and sample interactions within each batch. Unlike prior methods that statically select or filter data before training, this method continuously updates data importance throughout training, leading to improved data utilization and generalization. The DWM is designed to be plug-and-play, transferable across model sizes and data selection strategies, and orthogonal to existing data selection methods. The research also provides novel insights into how LLM data preferences shift during training and demonstrates that the learned weighting model can be reused to enhance other models or selection pipelines.

a9be51698e7c2247853b7b6f1f70fc4d6d7ef605.title: Transformer-Patcher: One Mistake worth One Neuron
a9be51698e7c2247853b7b6f1f70fc4d6d7ef605.research_question: How can transformer-based pretrained language models be efficiently and robustly edited in a sequential manner to correct emerging mistakes, while preserving their performance on unrelated inputs and generalizing corrections to equivalent cases?
a9be51698e7c2247853b7b6f1f70fc4d6d7ef605.hypothesis: Introducing a method that adds and trains a small number of neurons (patches) in the last feed-forward network layer for each mistake will enable efficient, reliable, and localized sequential model editing, outperforming existing fine-tuning and HyperNetwork-based approaches in terms of reliability, generality, and locality.
a9be51698e7c2247853b7b6f1f70fc4d6d7ef605.proposed_method: The proposed approach, Transformer-Patcher, addresses sequential model editing by freezing all original model parameters and adding a new neuron (patch) to the last feed-forward network (FFN) layer for each identified mistake. Each patch is trained to activate only for its corresponding erroneous input using a combination of activation loss (to ensure the patch responds to the target input) and memory loss (to prevent activation on irrelevant inputs by leveraging a memory bank of past queries). The patch modifies the FFN output by adding a learned bias term only when activated, enabling precise correction without disrupting unrelated behaviors. For classification tasks, one patch is added per mistake; for auto-regressive generation, a patch is added for each wrongly generated token. The training loss for each patch is a weighted sum of the original task loss, activation loss, and memory loss, with hyperparameters controlling their relative contributions.
a9be51698e7c2247853b7b6f1f70fc4d6d7ef605.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both classification (FEVER fact-checking with BERT-base) and auto-regressive generation (zsRE question-answering with BART-base) tasks. The Sequential Model Editing (SME) pipeline involves splitting datasets into training, validation, and edit sets, and performing multi-step sequential edits using authentic mistakes made by the model. Evaluation metrics include Success Rate (SR) for reliability, Generalization Rate (GR) for generality, Edit Retain Rate (ER) for retaining past edits, and Training/Test Retain Rates (TrainR/TestR) for locality. Baselines include fine-tuning-based editors (with and without KL divergence, on all or last layers), HyperNetwork-based editors (KE, MEND), and a memory-based editor (SERA). Each method is evaluated over 20 random splits of the edit set, and ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of memory loss components, patch placement, and memory size. The method is also tested for scalability by running thousands of edits in a single stream.
a9be51698e7c2247853b7b6f1f70fc4d6d7ef605.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the Sequential Model Editing (SME) task as a new, practical challenge for deployed language models, along with a standardized experimental pipeline and evaluation metrics. Transformer-Patcher is claimed to be a simple yet effective model editor that enables continuous, localized, and efficient correction of transformer-based models by adding minimal trainable parameters. The method achieves state-of-the-art performance in SME, demonstrating the ability to correct up to thousands of mistakes while almost perfectly retaining overall model performance. The approach is also efficient in terms of computational cost and model size increase, and is robust to memory size and patch placement. Ablation studies confirm the critical role of the proposed memory loss in maintaining locality and preventing unintended model changes.

a9cae269392ea8c20212f69af2b9c007a49d54c5.title: FAENet: Frame Averaging Equivariant GNN for Materials Modeling
a9cae269392ea8c20212f69af2b9c007a49d54c5.research_question: How can machine learning models for materials property prediction be designed to efficiently and flexibly preserve physical symmetries, such as E(3) equivariance or invariance, without sacrificing model expressivity, scalability, or comprehensibility?
a9cae269392ea8c20212f69af2b9c007a49d54c5.hypothesis: A model-agnostic framework that enforces symmetries via data transformations, rather than architectural constraints, can achieve competitive or superior accuracy and computational scalability in materials modeling tasks compared to existing symmetry-preserving GNN architectures.
a9cae269392ea8c20212f69af2b9c007a49d54c5.proposed_method: A flexible framework based on Stochastic Frame Averaging (SFA) will be developed to enforce E(3)-equivariance or invariance in graph neural networks (GNNs) for materials modeling. This approach will project atomic structures into canonical representations using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), generating a set of symmetry-related frames. During training and inference, a single frame will be randomly sampled per data point, and the model will make predictions on the transformed data, achieving approximate equivariance or invariance. A new GNN architecture, FAENet, will be designed to process geometric information (such as atom relative positions and distances) without symmetry-preserving constraints, leveraging simple message passing and embedding blocks. The model will utilize learnable edge and node embeddings, efficient message-passing layers, and output heads for both invariant (e.g., energy) and equivariant (e.g., force) predictions, with optional energy-conservation regularization.
a9cae269392ea8c20212f69af2b9c007a49d54c5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four benchmark datasets in materials science: OC20 (IS2RE and S2EF tasks for solid-state crystal structures), QM9, and QM7-X (for molecular modeling). The evaluation will include comparisons against a wide range of baselines, including E(3)-invariant GNNs (e.g., SchNet, DimeNet++, GemNet-T), equivariant models (e.g., PaiNN, So3krates), and data augmentation-based approaches (e.g., ForceNet). Performance metrics will include mean absolute error (MAE) for energy and forces, as well as throughput (samples per second) and training time per epoch to assess scalability. Additional analyses will measure the degree of symmetry preservation, and ablation studies will evaluate the impact of different components of the proposed method. All models will be evaluated using standardized splits and hardware for fair comparison.
a9cae269392ea8c20212f69af2b9c007a49d54c5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a model-agnostic, data-driven framework for enforcing physical symmetries in materials modeling, eliminating the need for architectural constraints that limit expressivity and scalability. FAENet is designed as a simple yet expressive GNN that leverages the proposed stochastic frame averaging to process geometric information flexibly. The method achieves near-perfect symmetry preservation with significantly reduced computational cost compared to full group averaging or hard-coded equivariant architectures. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior or competitive accuracy and substantially improved scalability across multiple challenging materials science benchmarks.

a9d740fe0182f00fc744355f073b189d0d908cca.title: Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Vision Transformers with Token Gradient Regularization
a9d740fe0182f00fc744355f073b189d0d908cca.research_question: How can the transferability of adversarial attacks against vision transformers (ViTs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) be improved, particularly in black-box settings, by addressing deficiencies in current gradient regularization methods?
a9d740fe0182f00fc744355f073b189d0d908cca.hypothesis: Regularizing the variance of back-propagated gradients in intermediate blocks of vision transformers, specifically in a token-wise manner, will reduce overfitting to model-specific features and improve the transferability of adversarial samples across different model architectures.
a9d740fe0182f00fc744355f073b189d0d908cca.proposed_method: A novel Token Gradient Regularization (TGR) method is developed to enhance the transferability of adversarial attacks on vision transformers. The approach targets the variance of back-propagated gradients in each internal block of ViTs, operating in a token-wise fashion. Specifically, TGR identifies tokens with extreme gradient values (top-k or bottom-k) within key components of the ViT architecture—namely, the Attention, QKV (Query, Key, Value), and MLP blocks—and eliminates these extreme gradients to reduce variance. A scaling factor is also applied to each component to further stabilize the gradients. The regularized gradients are then used to iteratively update adversarial samples, with the process integrated into standard attack frameworks such as momentum iterative methods. The method is compatible with input transformation strategies (e.g., PatchOut) and can be extended to CNNs by applying similar regularization to intermediate feature maps.
a9d740fe0182f00fc744355f073b189d0d908cca.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the ImageNet dataset, using 1000 randomly sampled images from the ILSVRC2012 validation set. The evaluation focuses on both intra-architecture (ViT-to-ViT) and cross-architecture (ViT-to-CNN) transferability, including attacks on adversarially trained and defended CNNs. Four representative ViT models (ViT-B/16, PiT-B, CaiT-S/24, Visformer-S) are used as source models, with additional ViTs and CNNs (including Inception-v3, Inception-v4, Inception-ResNet-v2, ResNet-v2-152) as targets. Baseline methods include MIM, VMI, SGM, and PNA, with and without the PatchOut input transformation. Attack success rate is the primary evaluation metric, and all models are tested under a fixed perturbation budget (L-infinity norm, epsilon=16, 10 iterations). Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of regularizing different ViT components and varying the number of extreme tokens.
a9d740fe0182f00fc744355f073b189d0d908cca.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new perspective on gradient regularization by targeting the variance of token-wise gradients in intermediate blocks of vision transformers, rather than only at the input layer. This approach leverages the architectural characteristics of ViTs to improve adversarial transferability and demonstrates significant improvements over state-of-the-art baselines, with average gains of 8.8% on ViTs and 6.2% on CNNs. The method is shown to be compatible with other attack strategies, extendable to CNNs, and effective in reducing gradient variance throughout the network, contributing to more robust and transferable adversarial attacks.

a9d996946fed6706b7fd1c32da44ab6ee0a2e5bd.title: Max-Information, Differential Privacy, and Post-selection Hypothesis Testing
a9d996946fed6706b7fd1c32da44ab6ee0a2e5bd.research_question: How can the generalization properties of approximate differential privacy be leveraged to enable statistically valid adaptive hypothesis testing, particularly through the use of max-information as a unifying measure for p-value correction in post-selection inference?
a9d996946fed6706b7fd1c32da44ab6ee0a2e5bd.hypothesis: Algorithms that satisfy approximate ((),)-differential privacy possess bounded approximate max-information when inputs are drawn from a product distribution, and this property can be used to derive valid p-value correction functions for adaptively chosen hypotheses.
a9d996946fed6706b7fd1c32da44ab6ee0a2e5bd.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed to analyze the generalization properties of algorithms satisfying approximate ((),)-differential privacy, focusing on their max-information bounds when inputs are drawn from a product distribution. The approach will formalize the relationship between max-information and the validity of p-value corrections in adaptive hypothesis testing. The methodology will include deriving tight quantitative bounds on the approximate max-information of ((),)-differentially private algorithms, extending previous results that were limited to pure ((),0)-differential privacy. Additionally, the framework will investigate the composition properties of max-information under adaptive compositions of differentially private and other bounded max-information algorithms, including the construction of lower bounds and counterexamples. Theoretical analysis will be complemented by the development of explicit p-value correction functions based on the derived max-information bounds.
a9d996946fed6706b7fd1c32da44ab6ee0a2e5bd.experiment_details: The proposed research will involve rigorous theoretical analysis, including the derivation of new theorems and lemmas relating differential privacy, max-information, and p-value corrections. Experiments will be conducted using synthetic datasets generated from product distributions to empirically validate the theoretical bounds on max-information and the effectiveness of the proposed p-value correction functions. Baseline comparisons will include existing methods for post-selection inference based on pure differential privacy and mutual information. Evaluation metrics will focus on the statistical validity of hypothesis tests (false discovery rate), the tightness of p-value corrections, and the generalization error under adaptive data analysis. The experimental setup will also include counterexamples and lower bound constructions to demonstrate the limitations of composition properties under approximate differential privacy.
a9d996946fed6706b7fd1c32da44ab6ee0a2e5bd.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a quantitatively tight extension of the connection between differential privacy and max-information to the broader class of approximate ((),)-differential privacy, enabling valid adaptive hypothesis testing with statistically sound p-value corrections. This work substantially generalizes previous results that were restricted to pure differential privacy, and provides a new unifying framework for understanding generalization in adaptive data analysis via max-information. The research also establishes new lower bounds and composition limitations, clarifying the precise conditions under which approximate differential privacy guarantees generalization through max-information. Additionally, the proposal offers improved p-value correction functions and mutual information bounds, surpassing prior approaches in both generality and quantitative tightness.

a9e155fda1d97baa2b8712f580cc61887cc64e9b.title: ChatGPT outperforms crowd workers for text-annotation tasks
a9e155fda1d97baa2b8712f580cc61887cc64e9b.research_question: Can large language models, specifically ChatGPT, serve as a more accurate, consistent, and cost-effective alternative to crowd-workers and trained annotators for a range of text annotation tasks in natural language processing applications?
a9e155fda1d97baa2b8712f580cc61887cc64e9b.hypothesis: ChatGPT, when used in a zero-shot setting, will achieve higher annotation accuracy and intercoder agreement than crowd-workers and trained annotators across multiple text annotation tasks, while also significantly reducing annotation costs.
a9e155fda1d97baa2b8712f580cc61887cc64e9b.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation framework will be established to compare the performance of ChatGPT, crowd-workers (MTurk), and trained annotators on a suite of text annotation tasks. The methodology will involve selecting diverse datasets of tweets and news articles, each annotated for tasks such as relevance (to content moderation or politics), stance detection, topic identification, and frame detection (problem/solution and policy frames). ChatGPT will be prompted using the same task-specific instructions as human annotators, with annotations collected via the 'gpt-3.5-turbo' API at different temperature settings (1 and 0.2) to assess both accuracy and consistency. For each annotation, a new chat session will be initiated to avoid context leakage, and multiple independent runs will be performed to compute intercoder agreement. The same annotation tasks will be administered to MTurk crowd-workers (restricted to high-quality workers) and to trained research assistants, ensuring direct comparability.
a9e155fda1d97baa2b8712f580cc61887cc64e9b.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize four datasets: (i) a random sample of 2,382 tweets on content moderation (2020-2021), (ii) 1,856 tweets from US Congress members (2017-2022), (iii) 1,606 news articles on content moderation (2020-2021), and (iv) 500 tweets on content moderation from January 2023. Annotation tasks will include binary and multi-class classification for relevance, stance, topics, and frames, with gold-standard labels provided by trained annotators. Each text will be annotated by both ChatGPT (multiple runs per temperature setting), two independent MTurk workers, and trained annotators. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy (agreement with gold-standard labels) and intercoder agreement (percentage of identical labels between annotators within each group). Cost analysis will compare per-annotation expenses across methods. The impact of prompt design and temperature settings on ChatGPT's performance will also be systematically examined.
a9e155fda1d97baa2b8712f580cc61887cc64e9b.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a systematic, large-scale comparison of zero-shot large language model annotation performance against both crowd-sourced and expert human annotation across multiple complex text classification tasks. The approach uniquely evaluates not only accuracy but also intercoder agreement and cost-effectiveness, providing a holistic assessment of LLMs as annotation tools. The methodology controls for prompt design and annotation context, and explores the influence of model temperature on consistency. The findings are expected to demonstrate that LLMs can surpass traditional annotation strategies in both quality and efficiency, potentially transforming data labeling practices in NLP research and industry.

a9e20180153f6c139a4b6f2791b535fa6ffc3959.title: Git Re-Basin: Merging Models modulo Permutation Symmetries
a9e20180153f6c139a4b6f2791b535fa6ffc3959.research_question: Can independently trained neural network models with identical architectures be merged in weight space by accounting for permutation symmetries, such that the interpolated models maintain or improve performance? What invariances in training dynamics enable the observed effectiveness of stochastic gradient descent in deep learning, and how do these relate to the geometry of the loss landscape?
a9e20180153f6c139a4b6f2791b535fa6ffc3959.hypothesis: The loss landscapes of neural networks trained with stochastic gradient descent contain (nearly) a single basin after accounting for all possible permutation symmetries of hidden units, enabling linear mode connectivity between independently trained models.
a9e20180153f6c139a4b6f2791b535fa6ffc3959.proposed_method: A suite of algorithms will be developed to identify and apply permutations to the hidden units of one neural network model so that its weights are aligned with those of a reference model. Three distinct approaches will be explored: (1) Activation matching, which aligns units by solving a linear assignment problem based on regression between layer activations; (2) Weight matching, which formulates an NP-hard sum of bilinear assignments problem and solves it via a coordinate descent algorithm that greedily optimizes permutations layer-wise; and (3) Learning permutations with a straight-through estimator (STE), which parameterizes the permutation as a projection in weight space and optimizes it using gradient-based methods despite the non-differentiability of the projection. These methods will be implemented to support a wide range of architectures, including MLPs, CNNs, and ResNets, and will be capable of merging models trained on disjoint datasets.
a9e20180153f6c139a4b6f2791b535fa6ffc3959.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by independently training pairs of neural network models (MLPs, VGG, and ResNet architectures) on datasets such as MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet, using different random initializations and data orders. The proposed permutation algorithms will be applied to align and merge these models, and linear interpolation in weight space will be evaluated. Baselines will include naive weight interpolation and ensembling. Evaluation metrics will include loss barriers (maximum loss along the interpolation path), test loss, and calibration, with particular attention to the emergence of linear mode connectivity and the effect of model width. Additional experiments will test merging models trained on disjoint data splits and assess the computational efficiency of each method.
a9e20180153f6c139a4b6f2791b535fa6ffc3959.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces efficient algorithms for merging independently trained neural network models by explicitly accounting for permutation symmetries, enabling the first demonstration of zero-barrier linear mode connectivity between large-scale models such as ResNets on non-trivial datasets. The methods are significantly faster than prior approaches, support a wide range of architectures, and can merge models trained on disjoint datasets into a single model with improved test loss and calibration. The work also provides new theoretical and empirical insights into the role of permutation symmetries and model width in the geometry of neural network loss landscapes.

a9e3e5dd7b30890553b7ae1c41f932e99192bb44.title: Large Language Models Are Reasoning Teachers
a9e3e5dd7b30890553b7ae1c41f932e99192bb44.research_question: How can complex reasoning abilities, typically emergent only in very large language models, be effectively transferred to much smaller language models to enable scalable and accessible deployment across a wide range of reasoning tasks?
a9e3e5dd7b30890553b7ae1c41f932e99192bb44.hypothesis: Fine-tuning small language models on multi-step reasoning samples generated by very large teacher models will substantially enhance the reasoning capabilities of the smaller models, potentially enabling them to match or surpass prompt-based performance of much larger models. Further, augmenting the fine-tuning data with diverse, distinct rationales for each sample will yield additional performance gains.
a9e3e5dd7b30890553b7ae1c41f932e99192bb44.proposed_method: A novel method, Fine-tune-CoT, will be developed to transfer reasoning abilities from large to small language models. The process begins by using a very large teacher model (e.g., GPT-3 175B) to generate chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning explanations for complex questions via zero-shot CoT prompting. These generated rationales, along with their corresponding questions and answers, are curated by filtering for correctness of the final answer. The curated prompt-rationale-answer triples are then used to fine-tune much smaller student models (e.g., 0.3B–6.7B parameters) using an autoregressive language modeling objective. To maximize the teaching effect, the method is extended to generate multiple distinct rationales per question through stochastic sampling, thereby enriching the fine-tuning dataset with diverse reasoning paths. This approach is task-agnostic, requires no hand-crafted rationales, and is applicable to a wide range of downstream tasks.
a9e3e5dd7b30890553b7ae1c41f932e99192bb44.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 12 datasets spanning arithmetic, symbolic, commonsense, and other complex reasoning tasks, including GSM8K, MultiArith, SVAMP, Date Understanding, CoinFlip, CommonSenseQA, and others. Teacher models will be large-scale LLMs accessed via API (e.g., GPT-3 175B), while student models will include GPT-3 variants (ada, babbage, curie), GPT-2, T5, and Flan-T5 models ranging from 0.3B to 6.7B parameters. Baseline comparisons will include zero-shot prompting, zero-shot-CoT, few-shot-CoT, and standard fine-tuning. Evaluation metrics will primarily be accuracy on held-out test sets, with ablations on dataset size, degree of reasoning diversity, teacher model quality, and student model size. Diverse reasoning will be assessed by varying the number of distinct rationales per sample (e.g., D=1–64). Additional analyses will include sample studies of error types and the impact of rationale correctness.
a9e3e5dd7b30890553b7ae1c41f932e99192bb44.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a scalable and task-agnostic framework for distilling complex reasoning abilities from very large language models into much smaller, more deployable models. The method leverages teacher-generated chain-of-thought rationales to fine-tune student models, overcoming the prohibitive inference costs and deployment barriers of prompt-based CoT methods. The extension to diverse reasoning—using multiple distinct rationales per sample—is claimed to be a novel and highly effective augmentation strategy, leading to substantial performance gains even in very small models. The proposal also claims to provide the first comprehensive analysis of the emergence and transfer of reasoning abilities in small models via large-model supervision, including ablations and sample studies that illuminate the mechanisms underlying reasoning transfer.

a9f7f2b9900c7138dbd8eb4c564858ee6becc15d.title: Joint Entropy Search for Multi-objective Bayesian Optimization
a9f7f2b9900c7138dbd8eb4c564858ee6becc15d.research_question: How can multi-objective Bayesian optimization be improved by designing an acquisition function that efficiently identifies optimal trade-offs among competing objectives using limited noisy evaluations?
a9f7f2b9900c7138dbd8eb4c564858ee6becc15d.hypothesis: An information-theoretic acquisition function that targets the joint distribution over optimal inputs and outputs will enable more sample-efficient and robust identification of Pareto-optimal solutions in multi-objective Bayesian optimization, outperforming existing scalarization- and improvement-based methods.
a9f7f2b9900c7138dbd8eb4c564858ee6becc15d.proposed_method: A novel information-theoretic acquisition function, Joint Entropy Search (JES), will be developed to maximize the mutual information between candidate observations and the joint distribution of Pareto-optimal inputs and outputs. The method will model each objective with independent Gaussian processes, incorporating additive Gaussian noise. The JES acquisition function will be approximated using Monte Carlo sampling of Pareto sets and analytical or approximate entropy calculations, including moment-matching and lower-bound strategies for computational tractability. The approach will be extended to batch settings by deriving a submodular lower bound, enabling efficient selection of multiple query points per iteration. All entropy and mutual information calculations will be designed to be differentiable, allowing for gradient-based optimization of acquisition functions.
a9f7f2b9900c7138dbd8eb4c564858ee6becc15d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of synthetic and real-world multi-objective optimization problems, including the ZDT2 benchmark (D=6, M=2), a chemical reaction optimization (D=4, M=2), pharmaceutical manufacturing (D=7, M=3), and marine design (D=6, M=4). Each problem will include additive Gaussian noise to simulate realistic scenarios. The JES method will be compared against established baselines such as TSEMO, ParEGO, NParEGO, EHVI, NEHVI, PES, and MES, as well as variants of MES and JES using different entropy approximations. Evaluation metrics will primarily include the hypervolume (HV) discrepancy and its weighted/generalized variants to assess Pareto front approximation quality. Experiments will be repeated with multiple random seeds, and batch as well as sequential settings will be tested. All methods will be implemented using BoTorch and GPyTorch, with Pareto set recommendations generated using NSGA2.
a9f7f2b9900c7138dbd8eb4c564858ee6becc15d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first information-theoretic acquisition function for multi-objective Bayesian optimization that explicitly targets the joint entropy over optimal inputs and outputs. Analytical and computationally efficient approximations for the JES acquisition function are developed, including extensions to batch optimization. The method is invariant to monotonic reparameterizations of the objective space, addressing known limitations of hypervolume-based criteria. A novel weighted hypervolume metric is introduced for more nuanced performance assessment. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate that JES achieves state-of-the-art performance across a range of multi-objective optimization benchmarks.

aa04929037c41854a31c18dab172606ed4ae4875.title: Federated Class-Incremental Learning
aa04929037c41854a31c18dab172606ed4ae4875.research_question: How can a global model be collaboratively trained in a federated setting to continuously learn new classes over time, while addressing catastrophic forgetting and maintaining privacy and memory efficiency across decentralized, non-i.i.d. clients?
aa04929037c41854a31c18dab172606ed4ae4875.hypothesis: A federated class-incremental learning framework that compensates for both local and global catastrophic forgetting through class-aware gradient adjustment, semantic relation distillation, and privacy-preserving global model selection will outperform existing methods in accuracy and robustness when learning new classes incrementally.
aa04929037c41854a31c18dab172606ed4ae4875.proposed_method: A novel Global-Local Forgetting Compensation (GLFC) framework is proposed for federated class-incremental learning (FCIL). Locally, a class-aware gradient compensation loss is introduced to normalize and balance the learning and forgetting rates for old and new classes, addressing class imbalance at each client. Additionally, a class-semantic relation distillation loss is formulated to preserve consistent inter-class relationships across incremental tasks by distilling knowledge from previous models. Globally, a proxy server is employed to select the best old global model for knowledge distillation, using a privacy-preserving prototype gradient-based communication mechanism. Clients send perturbed prototype gradients of new classes to the proxy server, which reconstructs prototype samples and evaluates candidate global models to select the most effective one for distillation. A task transition detection mechanism is also included to identify when clients encounter new classes and update their exemplar memory and old model references accordingly.
aa04929037c41854a31c18dab172606ed4ae4875.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on three benchmark datasets: CIFAR-100, ImageNet-Subset, and TinyImageNet, using a ResNet-18 backbone for all models. The FCIL setting is simulated with multiple clients, each receiving a subset of classes in a non-i.i.d. fashion, and new clients/classes are introduced dynamically during training. Each client has a limited exemplar memory for old classes, with sizes varied in ablation studies. Baseline comparisons include federated versions of state-of-the-art class-incremental learning methods such as iCaRL, BiC, PODNet, DDE, GeoDL, and SS-IL, as well as ablations of the proposed method. Evaluation metrics focus on average classification accuracy across all incremental tasks, and experiments are repeated with multiple random seeds. The impact of each module (gradient compensation, relation distillation, proxy server) and memory size is assessed through detailed ablation and qualitative analyses.
aa04929037c41854a31c18dab172606ed4ae4875.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to address federated class-incremental learning (FCIL) by jointly compensating for both local and global catastrophic forgetting. Key innovations include the class-aware gradient compensation loss for local class imbalance, the class-semantic relation distillation loss for inter-task consistency, and a privacy-preserving proxy server that selects the best old global model using prototype gradient-based communication. The method enables effective global class-incremental learning in realistic federated settings with dynamic client and class arrival, limited memory, and strict privacy constraints, achieving significant improvements (4.4%–15.1% accuracy gain) over existing baselines.

aa085ed9a77d815d3c1d19a468be1d9a8d3efd13.title: Massive Activations in Large Language Models
aa085ed9a77d815d3c1d19a468be1d9a8d3efd13.research_question: What are the internal mechanisms underlying the emergence of extremely large activations in transformer-based models, and how do these activations influence model behavior and architecture design across language and vision domains?
aa085ed9a77d815d3c1d19a468be1d9a8d3efd13.hypothesis: Massive activations in transformer models function as implicit bias terms that are critical for model performance, and explicitly modeling such biases in the self-attention mechanism can eliminate the need for these emergent massive activations.
aa085ed9a77d815d3c1d19a468be1d9a8d3efd13.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical and intervention-based analysis will be conducted to investigate the existence, properties, and functional roles of extremely large-magnitude activations ('massive activations') in transformer-based models, including large language models (LLMs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs). The methodology involves identifying and quantifying massive activations across different model architectures, layers, and token types by analyzing hidden states and activation statistics. Interventions will be performed by manually modifying the values of massive activations at the layer where they first appear, setting them to zero or their empirical mean, and observing the resulting impact on downstream performance. Furthermore, an explicit attention bias will be introduced into the self-attention mechanism by augmenting key and value projections with additional learnable bias parameters, and models will be trained with this modification to assess whether massive activations persist.
aa085ed9a77d815d3c1d19a468be1d9a8d3efd13.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed on a range of pretrained and fine-tuned LLMs (such as LLaMA2-7B, LLaMA2-13B, Mixtral-8x7B, Phi-2, GPT-2, MPT, Falcon-40B) and ViTs (CLIP ViT-L, DINOv2 ViT-L, MAE ViT-L). For LLMs, evaluation will include perplexity on WikiText, C4, and PG-19 datasets, as well as zero-shot accuracy on BoolQ, PIQA, WinoGrande, Arc-Easy, and Arc-Challenge. Baselines will include unmodified models and models with median-magnitude activations set to zero. For the explicit bias intervention, standard GPT-2, GPT-2 with a sink token, and GPT-2 with explicit attention bias will be compared. For ViTs, activation statistics will be collected over 1,000 images, and the presence and consistency of massive activations will be analyzed. Key evaluation metrics include activation magnitude distributions, variance across inputs, model perplexity, and task accuracy.
aa085ed9a77d815d3c1d19a468be1d9a8d3efd13.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a systematic investigation into the phenomenon of massive activations in transformer models, revealing their role as implicit bias terms essential for model function. It is claimed that explicitly modeling attention biases in the architecture can obviate the need for these emergent massive activations, providing a new perspective on transformer design. The work extends the analysis to both language and vision domains, offering unified insights into transformer internals and suggesting architectural modifications with potential implications for model interpretability, efficiency, and stability.

aa12e22609d06b1093cb87fe095f4a08f0b0d5e6.title: VERA: Variational Inference Framework for Jailbreaking Large Language Models
aa12e22609d06b1093cb87fe095f4a08f0b0d5e6.research_question: How can a scalable, automated, and comprehensive black-box framework be developed to generate diverse and effective adversarial prompts for jailbreaking large language models (LLMs), without relying on manual prompt engineering or white-box model access?
aa12e22609d06b1093cb87fe095f4a08f0b0d5e6.hypothesis: A variational inference-based framework that learns a distribution over adversarial prompts using a small attacker LLM, optimized via gradient-based methods and guided by a judge model, will enable efficient, diverse, and transferable black-box jailbreak attacks that outperform existing manual, evolutionary, and white-box approaches in both effectiveness and robustness to defenses.
aa12e22609d06b1093cb87fe095f4a08f0b0d5e6.proposed_method: The proposed approach formulates black-box adversarial prompt generation as a variational inference problem, where the objective is to approximate the posterior distribution over prompts likely to elicit harmful responses from a target LLM. A small attacker LLM is parameterized with LoRA adapters and fine-tuned to maximize an evidence lower bound (ELBO) objective that balances harmfulness (as measured by a judge model), plausibility under a prior, and diversity via entropy regularization. The judge model, implemented as either a binary classifier or an LLM-based safety scorer, provides a smooth reward signal indicating the likelihood that a prompt induces a harmful response. Optimization is performed using the REINFORCE gradient estimator, allowing for gradient-based updates in a black-box setting. Once trained, the attacker LLM can efficiently sample diverse adversarial prompts for any target behavior without further optimization or search.
aa12e22609d06b1093cb87fe095f4a08f0b0d5e6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the HarmBench dataset, which contains 400 harmful behaviors across diverse categories, and evaluated against a suite of open-source and commercial LLMs, including LLaMA2-7B/13B, Vicuna-7B, Baichuan-2-7B, Orca2-7B, Zephyr-7B, Gemini-Pro, and GPT-3.5-Turbo. The main evaluation metric is Attack Success Rate (ASR), determined using a fine-tuned LLaMA2-13B classifier following HarmBench protocol. Baselines include state-of-the-art white-box (e.g., GCG, GCG-M, GCG-T, PEZ, GBDA, UAT, AP) and black-box (e.g., SFS, ZS, PAIR, TAP, TAP-T, AutoDAN, PAP-top5, HumanDirect) approaches. Additional experiments assess prompt diversity (using BLEU/self-BLEU), transferability across models, and robustness against defenses such as Perplexity Filter and CircuitBreaker. Both fixed prompt and fixed wall-clock time budgets are used to compare efficiency and scalability.
aa12e22609d06b1093cb87fe095f4a08f0b0d5e6.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a principled, distributional perspective on black-box jailbreaking by casting prompt generation as variational inference, enabling the learning of a prompt distribution rather than isolated instances. The method eliminates dependence on manually crafted prompt templates and bootstrapping, making it more robust to future alignment improvements. It amortizes the cost of attack generation, allowing for fast, parallelizable, and diverse prompt sampling at inference time. The approach demonstrates state-of-the-art performance across both open-source and commercial LLMs, strong transferability of adversarial prompts, and superior robustness to both static and dynamic defense mechanisms, representing a significant advance in automated red-teaming for LLM safety evaluation.

aa207668318fec38d60b79f407fb64982e46fce9.title: WinCLIP: Zero-/Few-Shot Anomaly Classification and Segmentation
aa207668318fec38d60b79f407fb64982e46fce9.research_question: How can zero-shot and few-shot anomaly classification and segmentation in industrial visual inspection be achieved without requiring extensive task-specific training data or annotations?
aa207668318fec38d60b79f407fb64982e46fce9.hypothesis: Leveraging language-guided vision-language models, specifically through compositional prompt ensembles and multi-scale feature extraction, will enable effective zero-shot and few-normal-shot anomaly classification and segmentation, outperforming traditional one-class and supervised methods.
aa207668318fec38d60b79f407fb64982e46fce9.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed that utilizes a pre-trained vision-language model (CLIP) to perform zero-shot and few-normal-shot anomaly classification and segmentation. The approach introduces a Compositional Prompt Ensemble (CPE) that systematically combines state words (e.g., 'normal', 'anomalous', 'flawless', 'damaged') and task-specific prompt templates to generate robust text embeddings for both normal and anomalous states. For segmentation, a Window-based CLIP (WinCLIP) method is proposed, which extracts and aggregates multi-scale spatial features (from sliding windows at various scales) aligned with language embeddings, enabling pixel-level anomaly localization. In the few-normal-shot regime, WinCLIP+ extends this by incorporating a reference association module that matches features from a small set of normal images to the query image at multiple scales, harmonically aggregating visual and language-guided predictions for comprehensive anomaly detection.
aa207668318fec38d60b79f407fb64982e46fce9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the MVTec-AD and VisA industrial anomaly benchmarks, which provide high-resolution images with pixel-level annotations across diverse object categories and defect types. The evaluation will focus on both zero-shot and few-shot (1-4 normal images) regimes, using metrics such as AUROC, AUPR, F1-max for classification, and pixel-wise AUROC, Per-Region Overlap (PRO), and pixel-wise F1-max for segmentation. Baselines will include traditional one-class and few-shot anomaly detection methods (e.g., PatchCore, SPADE, PaDiM, RegAD, DifferNet, TDG), as well as adaptations of CLIP for zero-shot classification and segmentation (e.g., CLIP-AC, MaskCLIP, Trans-MM). Ablation studies will assess the impact of prompt engineering, multi-scale aggregation, harmonic averaging, and the integration of task-specific state words.
aa207668318fec38d60b79f407fb64982e46fce9.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to systematically leverage language-guided vision-language models for zero-shot and few-normal-shot anomaly classification and segmentation. Key innovations include the compositional prompt ensemble for robust state definition, the window-based multi-scale feature extraction aligned with language for dense anomaly localization, and the integration of reference association with few normal images for enhanced few-shot performance. The approach enables scalable, annotation-free anomaly detection across diverse tasks and demonstrates significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods in both zero-shot and few-shot regimes.

aa2eb5e8b5844530a3c68afcdc79086f09f0205f.title: Conditional Distributional Treatment Effect with Kernel Conditional Mean Embeddings and U-Statistic Regression
aa2eb5e8b5844530a3c68afcdc79086f09f0205f.research_question: How can the conditional distributional treatment effect (CoDiTE) be formally defined and estimated, and what methods can be developed to detect and characterize distributional differences in treatment effects beyond the mean, conditioned on covariates?
aa2eb5e8b5844530a3c68afcdc79086f09f0205f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that treatment effects exhibit heterogeneity not only in the mean (as captured by CATE) but also in higher-order distributional aspects (such as variance, skewness, and other moments), and that these can be detected and quantified using kernel-based methods and U-statistic regression.
aa2eb5e8b5844530a3c68afcdc79086f09f0205f.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed for analyzing the conditional distributional treatment effect (CoDiTE) by generalizing the conditional average treatment effect (CATE) to arbitrary distance functions between probability measures. The approach leverages kernel conditional mean embeddings (CMEs) to represent conditional distributions in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), enabling the use of the maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) as a metric for distributional differences. A statistical hypothesis test based on the kernel conditional discrepancy (KCD) is developed to determine whether any conditional distributional effect exists. Furthermore, conditional witness functions are introduced for exploratory analysis of where and how distributions differ, and U-statistic regression is generalized to estimate CoDiTEs associated with specific distributional quantities (e.g., variance, Gini's mean difference) in a fully nonparametric manner.
aa2eb5e8b5844530a3c68afcdc79086f09f0205f.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on synthetic, semi-synthetic, and real datasets. The semi-synthetic IHDP dataset is used to simulate various noise settings (small, large, and heterogeneous noise) to evaluate the ability of the proposed methods to detect and characterize distributional treatment effects beyond the mean. The LaLonde National Supported Work (NSW) dataset is used to demonstrate the method on real outcomes, focusing on subpopulations where overlap holds. Baselines include GAMLSS (generalized additive models for location, scale, and shape) for distributional regression, with performance measured by root mean square error in estimating conditional standard deviation. Evaluation metrics include hypothesis test rejection rates, precision of estimating heterogeneous distributional effects (PEHDE), and visual analysis via conditional witness functions.
aa2eb5e8b5844530a3c68afcdc79086f09f0205f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a formal and general definition of the conditional distributional treatment effect (CoDiTE) using arbitrary distance functions between conditional distributions, subsuming CATE as a special case. The use of kernel conditional mean embeddings and maximum mean discrepancy for conditional distributional effect testing is novel in this context. A new nonparametric U-statistic regression technique is developed for estimating CoDiTEs associated with higher-order moments, providing a flexible alternative to parametric approaches like GAMLSS. The approach enables both hypothesis testing for the presence of distributional effects and exploratory/quantitative characterization of how treatment effects differ across the distribution, offering a more comprehensive understanding of treatment effect heterogeneity.

aa676125041cd284b4a1313d70143ba6f77c074b.title: Matryoshka Representation Learning
aa676125041cd284b4a1313d70143ba6f77c074b.research_question: Can a single learned representation be designed to flexibly adapt to multiple downstream tasks with varying computational and statistical constraints, providing efficient and accurate performance across diverse modalities and deployment scenarios?
aa676125041cd284b4a1313d70143ba6f77c074b.hypothesis: A representation learning framework that encodes information at multiple granularities within a single embedding vector can enable adaptive deployment, achieving accuracy comparable to or better than independently trained low-dimensional representations while significantly reducing computational and memory costs.
