aa676125041cd284b4a1313d70143ba6f77c074b.proposed_method: A novel representation learning approach, Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL), is proposed to encode information at multiple granularities within a single high-dimensional embedding. For a chosen set of representation sizes M (typically O(log(d)) elements, where d is the full embedding dimension), the method jointly optimizes the representation such that each prefix of the embedding (of size m in M) is independently capable of serving as a general-purpose representation for downstream tasks. This is achieved by modifying the standard supervised or self-supervised training pipeline to include multiple classification or contrastive losses, one for each nesting dimension, with either independent or tied classifier weights. The approach is compatible with existing architectures (e.g., ResNet, ViT, BERT) and can be integrated with minimal changes, supporting supervised, contrastive, and masked language modeling frameworks. The method also includes an efficient variant (MRL-E) that ties classifier weights to reduce memory overhead, and supports adaptive deployment strategies such as cascaded classification and multi-stage retrieval using different embedding granularities.
aa676125041cd284b4a1313d70143ba6f77c074b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale benchmarks including ImageNet-1K, ImageNet-4K, JFT-300M for vision tasks, ALIGN for vision-language, and English Wikipedia/BooksCorpus for language (BERT). Models such as ResNet50, ViT-B/16, and BERT-Base will be trained using MRL and compared to baselines including independently trained fixed-feature models, dimensionality reduction (SVD), slimmable networks, and random feature selection. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 classification accuracy, 1-NN accuracy, mean Average Precision at k (mAP@k) for retrieval, and wall-clock inference time. Adaptive classification and retrieval scenarios will be benchmarked using cascades and multi-stage re-ranking, measuring both accuracy and computational efficiency (FLOPs, memory usage). Robustness will be assessed on out-of-domain datasets (ImageNet-V2/A/R/Sketch), and few-shot/long-tail learning performance will be evaluated using nearest class mean and FLUID protocols. Ablation studies will examine the effect of loss weighting, granularity selection, and adaptation to pretrained models.
aa676125041cd284b4a1313d70143ba6f77c074b.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a unified framework for learning multi-granular, coarse-to-fine representations within a single embedding vector, enabling adaptive deployment without additional inference or storage costs. Unlike prior approaches that require multiple models or post-hoc compression, this method achieves accuracy on par with or exceeding independently trained low-dimensional models, while providing up to 14× smaller embeddings and 14× real-world speedups for classification and retrieval. The approach is modality-agnostic, scaling seamlessly to web-scale datasets and diverse architectures, and supports efficient adaptive cascades for both classification and retrieval. The method also demonstrates improved robustness and long-tail performance, and provides a systematic framework for analyzing information bottlenecks and hierarchical class structure within learned representations.

aa6df6a701c5214312b47d5e442e0e6027af5c00.title: A simple polynomial-time approximation algorithm for the total variation distance between two product distributions
aa6df6a701c5214312b47d5e442e0e6027af5c00.research_question: Can the total variation distance between two arbitrary product distributions be efficiently approximated in polynomial time, without restrictions on the distributions' marginals or domain sizes?
aa6df6a701c5214312b47d5e442e0e6027af5c00.hypothesis: It is possible to design a simple, general, polynomial-time randomized approximation algorithm for estimating the total variation distance between two product distributions, achieving provable accuracy guarantees for any input distributions.
aa6df6a701c5214312b47d5e442e0e6027af5c00.proposed_method: A novel Monte Carlo-based approximation algorithm will be developed to estimate the total variation distance between two product distributions over finite domains. The approach utilizes a coordinate-wise greedy coupling to efficiently generate samples from a conditional distribution that boosts the probability of observing differences between the two distributions. For each sample, an estimator is computed as the ratio of the probability of the assignment under the optimal coupling to that under the greedy coupling, conditioned on the samples being different. The algorithm aggregates these estimators using the median-of-means technique to achieve high-probability accuracy guarantees. The method is designed to run in time polynomial in the number of coordinates and the desired accuracy parameters, and can handle coordinates with varying domain sizes.
aa6df6a701c5214312b47d5e442e0e6027af5c00.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic product distributions defined over finite domains, with marginals specified in binary. The algorithm's performance will be evaluated in terms of approximation accuracy, running time, and sample complexity, compared to exact computation (where feasible) and naive Monte Carlo baselines. Evaluation metrics will include the relative error of the estimated total variation distance and the empirical probability of achieving the desired accuracy within the specified confidence level. The experimental setup will vary the number of coordinates, domain sizes, and the distance between distributions to assess robustness and scalability.
aa6df6a701c5214312b47d5e442e0e6027af5c00.novelty_claims: The proposed approach provides the first simple polynomial-time randomized approximation algorithm for the total variation distance between arbitrary product distributions, without restrictions on marginals or domain sizes. The method leverages a new estimator based on coordinate-wise greedy coupling and conditional sampling, enabling efficient and accurate estimation even when the true distance is exponentially small. The algorithm achieves provable accuracy and confidence guarantees with polynomial sample complexity and running time, improving upon prior work limited to special cases or requiring additional assumptions.

aa972f18e9ccea95b774a20456db4fb03ed2bda6.title: The underlying structures of self-attention: symmetry, directionality, and emergent dynamics in Transformer training
aa972f18e9ccea95b774a20456db4fb03ed2bda6.research_question: How do different objective functions, such as autoregressive and bidirectional training, influence the structural properties of self-attention matrices in Transformer models, and can leveraging these structures improve model interpretability and training efficiency across various modalities?
aa972f18e9ccea95b774a20456db4fb03ed2bda6.hypothesis: Bidirectional training induces symmetric structures in self-attention matrices, while autoregressive training leads to directional and column-dominant structures; explicitly embedding these structural priors, such as symmetry, into model initialization will improve training efficiency and model performance for encoder-only Transformers.
aa972f18e9ccea95b774a20456db4fb03ed2bda6.proposed_method: A mathematical framework will be developed to analyze the structural properties of self-attention matrices by linking the query-key matrix to bilinear forms. The framework will derive the implicit weight update patterns induced by different objective functions, such as autoregressive and bidirectional training. Symmetry and directionality scores will be defined to quantitatively assess the emergence of these structures in self-attention matrices across layers and model types. The method will also include an experimental intervention where self-attention matrices are initialized to be symmetric in encoder-only models, allowing for empirical evaluation of the impact of this inductive bias on training dynamics and performance.
aa972f18e9ccea95b774a20456db4fb03ed2bda6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of Transformer architectures, including encoder-only (e.g., BERT, ModernBERT), decoder-only (e.g., GPT, LLaMA3, Mistral), and full encoder-decoder models, across multiple modalities such as text, vision, and audio. Both pre-trained and custom models will be analyzed to assess the universality of the findings. Evaluation will involve computing the proposed symmetry and directionality scores for self-attention matrices across layers and training regimes. Additional experiments will compare models with standard versus symmetric initialization of self-attention matrices, measuring convergence speed and final loss on language datasets such as Jigsaw, Wikipedia, and Red Pajama. Baselines will include standard randomly initialized models, and evaluation metrics will include training loss, convergence speed, and accuracy.
aa972f18e9ccea95b774a20456db4fb03ed2bda6.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel mathematical framework that connects self-attention matrix updates to bilinear forms, enabling the derivation of structural properties induced by different training objectives. It provides the first systematic quantification of symmetry and directionality in self-attention matrices across a wide range of Transformer architectures and modalities. The approach demonstrates that embedding symmetry as an inductive bias in encoder-only models can significantly accelerate training and improve performance, offering a new avenue for leveraging mechanistic interpretability insights to optimize Transformer training.

aa97f421e7c9aae87b347d2c7646951d72140a44.title: Failure Prediction at Runtime for Generative Robot Policies
aa97f421e7c9aae87b347d2c7646951d72140a44.research_question: How can failures of generative imitation learning (IL) robot policies be accurately and early predicted at runtime in diverse, safety-critical environments, without relying on failure data or explicit failure mode labels?
aa97f421e7c9aae87b347d2c7646951d72140a44.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that actual failures of generative IL policies can be robustly predicted at runtime by simultaneously detecting (i) consecutive out-of-distribution (OOD) observations in the policy's embedding space and (ii) persistently high uncertainty in the generated action distributions, without requiring access to failure data.
aa97f421e7c9aae87b347d2c7646951d72140a44.proposed_method: A general framework, FIPER, will be developed for runtime failure prediction of generative IL policies. The method will employ two complementary submodules: (1) an observation-based score using random network distillation (RND) in the policy's observation embedding space to detect OOD states, and (2) an action-based score, termed action-chunk entropy (ACE), which quantifies uncertainty in the generated action distributions via entropy estimation over action samples. Both scores will be aggregated over a sliding time window to capture persistent anomalies and will be calibrated using conformal prediction on a small set of successful rollouts to set adaptive, time-varying thresholds. A failure alarm will be triggered only when both aggregated scores exceed their respective thresholds, providing a robust and interpretable failure prediction signal.
aa97f421e7c9aae87b347d2c7646951d72140a44.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across five environments: three simulation benchmarks (SORTING, STACKING, PUSHT) and two real-world tasks (PRETZEL, PUSHCHAIR), each exhibiting diverse robot embodiments, observation/action spaces, and failure modes. Generative IL policies based on diffusion and flow matching will be used, with policy backbones such as temporal U-Net and transformer architectures, and ResNet-18 for image encoding. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art failure and OOD detection methods (PCA-kmeans, logpZO, RND-A, STAC). Evaluation metrics will include balanced accuracy, detection time (DT), and a novel timestep-wise accuracy (TWA) that rewards early and correct failure prediction. Calibration and validation will use 50 successful rollouts for simulation and 10 for real-world tasks, with results averaged over multiple seeds and threshold quantiles.
aa97f421e7c9aae87b347d2c7646951d72140a44.novelty_claims: The proposed framework does not require any failure data for training or calibration, making it broadly applicable and safe for deployment in human-centered environments. The method jointly leverages both observation-based and action-based uncertainty signals, calibrated via conformal prediction, to robustly distinguish actual failures from benign OOD situations. The action-chunk entropy score is specifically designed to handle multimodal action distributions typical in generative IL policies. Aggregating uncertainty over a sliding window enables early and accurate failure prediction, outperforming existing approaches in both accuracy and detection time across diverse tasks. The framework is task-agnostic, interpretable, and suitable for a wide range of generative policy architectures.

aabfdbd9db5ce9b1d598eae44e0d6250e7f0fc00.title: MOMENT: A Family of Open Time-series Foundation Models
aabfdbd9db5ce9b1d598eae44e0d6250e7f0fc00.research_question: Can a family of large, open-source foundation models pre-trained on a diverse, large-scale collection of public time series data enable effective general-purpose time series analysis across multiple tasks and domains, particularly under limited supervision and resource constraints?
aabfdbd9db5ce9b1d598eae44e0d6250e7f0fc00.hypothesis: Pre-training high-capacity transformer models on a large, diverse corpus of time series data will yield general-purpose representations that enable strong performance on a variety of downstream time series analysis tasks (such as forecasting, classification, anomaly detection, and imputation), even in limited supervision or zero-shot settings.
aabfdbd9db5ce9b1d598eae44e0d6250e7f0fc00.proposed_method: A large-scale, diverse collection of public time series datasets, called the TimeSeriesPile, will be compiled from multiple domains (e.g., healthcare, finance, engineering) and tasks. Transformer-based models of various sizes will be pre-trained using a masked time series modeling objective, where random patches of the input sequence are masked and the model learns to reconstruct them. The architecture will use patching (segmenting time series into fixed-length sub-sequences), reversible instance normalization, and both absolute and relative positional embeddings to handle varying time series characteristics. Multi-variate time series will be processed by modeling each channel independently, and a lightweight reconstruction head will be used to facilitate efficient fine-tuning and adaptation to downstream tasks. Pre-training will be performed from scratch with random initialization, using large batch sizes, mixed precision, and gradient checkpointing for efficiency.
aabfdbd9db5ce9b1d598eae44e0d6250e7f0fc00.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five major time series analysis tasks: long- and short-horizon forecasting, classification, anomaly detection, and imputation. Datasets will include the Informer long-horizon forecasting collection (e.g., ETT, Electricity, Traffic, Weather, ILI, Exchange), Monash forecasting archive, UCR/UEA classification archive, and TSB-UAD anomaly benchmark, among others. Evaluation will focus on limited supervision scenarios, including zero-shot, linear probing, and unsupervised representation learning. Baselines will include state-of-the-art deep learning models (e.g., TimesNet, GPT4TS, PatchTST, N-BEATS), statistical methods (e.g., ARIMA, Theta, ETS), and non-transformer approaches (e.g., k-nearest neighbors). Metrics will include MSE, MAE, sMAPE, accuracy, adjusted best F1, and VUS-ROC, with careful train/validation/test splits to avoid data contamination. Hyperparameters will be fixed across experiments, and no extensive hyperparameter tuning will be performed.
aabfdbd9db5ce9b1d598eae44e0d6250e7f0fc00.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first open-source family of large-scale, general-purpose time series foundation models pre-trained on a unified, diverse corpus (TimeSeriesPile). It systematically addresses challenges unique to time series, such as variable lengths, sampling rates, and missing values, and demonstrates the feasibility and benefits of large-scale multi-dataset pre-training for time series. The approach enables strong performance across a wide range of tasks and domains, especially in limited supervision settings, and provides a new benchmark and methodology for evaluating time series foundation models. Empirical investigations into model scaling, cross-modal transfer, and interpretability are also proposed, advancing understanding of large pre-trained models in the time series domain.

aacaaed4353e56beb061a8aa1654abe6be8e7095.title: On Differential Privacy for Adaptively Solving Search Problems via Sketching
aacaaed4353e56beb061a8aa1654abe6be8e7095.research_question: Can adaptive data structures for search problems, such as approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search and regression with arbitrary updates, be designed to efficiently answer sequences of adaptive queries with significantly fewer independent copies than traditional approaches, while maintaining correctness and robustness against adaptive adversaries?
aacaaed4353e56beb061a8aa1654abe6be8e7095.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, under certain structural assumptions on the dataset (such as sparsity of neighborhoods or bounded condition number), differential privacy techniques can be leveraged to construct adaptive data structures for search problems that require sublinear (in the number of queries or dimension) independent copies, while maintaining efficient preprocessing, space, and query time.
aacaaed4353e56beb061a8aa1654abe6be8e7095.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves developing adaptive data structures for search problems by leveraging differential privacy mechanisms, particularly by treating the internal randomness of oblivious data structures as a private database. For the ANN problem, the approach frames the selection of near neighbors as a differentially private selection problem over sparse vectors, utilizing a novel sparse argmax mechanism to efficiently select among candidate neighbors with added noise, ensuring both privacy and utility. For adaptive regression, the method extends the private median framework to output solution vectors, employing advanced sketching techniques and leveraging ℓ∞ guarantees to maintain accuracy under adaptive updates. Key technical steps include advanced composition of differential privacy to reduce the number of required independent data structures, efficient noise addition tailored to the sparsity or structure of the problem, and algorithmic innovations for fast query and update operations.
aacaaed4353e56beb061a8aa1654abe6be8e7095.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on classical search problems: (1) approximate nearest neighbor search under various norms, including Hamming space, and (2) regression with arbitrary turnstile updates to the data matrix and response vector. Datasets will be constructed or selected to satisfy the required structural assumptions (e.g., bounded number of near neighbors, bounded condition number). Baselines for comparison will include traditional approaches that use T or d independent copies of oblivious data structures, as well as net-argument-based methods. Evaluation metrics will include preprocessing time, space usage, query time, update time, and correctness under adaptive adversarial query sequences. The experimental setup will systematically vary parameters such as the number of queries T, data dimension d, neighborhood sparsity s, and condition number κ to assess scalability and robustness.
aacaaed4353e56beb061a8aa1654abe6be8e7095.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel framework for constructing adaptive data structures for search problems using differential privacy, enabling robust answers to adaptive queries with significantly fewer independent copies than prior methods. Key innovations include the sparse argmax mechanism for efficient differentially private selection in sparse settings, and the extension of private median techniques to output full solution vectors for regression. The approach achieves improved tradeoffs in space, preprocessing, and query time, particularly in regimes where the number of queries is much less than the data dimension or where the dataset has favorable structural properties. These contributions address previously open questions about the feasibility of robust adaptive search data structures beyond numerical estimation problems.

aad167be3c902388ea625da4117fcae4325b8b7d.title: Distilling Step-by-Step! Outperforming Larger Language Models with Less Training Data and Smaller Model Sizes
aad167be3c902388ea625da4117fcae4325b8b7d.research_question: How can smaller language models be trained to achieve or surpass the performance of much larger language models, while requiring less training data and maintaining practical deployability?
aad167be3c902388ea625da4117fcae4325b8b7d.hypothesis: Incorporating LLM-generated rationales as additional supervision within a multi-task learning framework will enable smaller models to outperform larger LLMs, requiring significantly less labeled or unlabeled training data compared to standard finetuning or distillation approaches.
aad167be3c902388ea625da4117fcae4325b8b7d.proposed_method: A novel training paradigm, Distilling step-by-step, will be developed to train small task-specific language models by leveraging rationales generated by large language models (LLMs) using chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting. The method involves two main steps: (1) extracting both predicted labels and natural language rationales from an LLM for each input example, and (2) training a smaller model in a multi-task framework to predict both the label and the rationale from the input, using task-specific prefixes to distinguish between the two outputs. The multi-task loss combines standard label prediction loss and rationale generation loss, allowing the model to learn richer task knowledge. At inference time, only the label prediction is required, eliminating the need for rationale generation and thus reducing computational overhead.
aad167be3c902388ea625da4117fcae4325b8b7d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four NLP benchmarks spanning natural language inference, commonsense question answering, and math word problems (e-SNLI, ANLI, CQA, SVAMP). Both labeled and unlabeled data settings will be considered, comparing the proposed method to standard finetuning and distillation baselines, as well as to large LLMs (e.g., 540B PaLM) using few-shot chain-of-thought prompting and PINTO tuning. Evaluation metrics will include task-specific accuracy, with systematic variation of training data size and model size (using T5 models of 220M, 770M, and 11B parameters). Additional ablation studies will assess the impact of rationale quality, LLM teacher size, and training strategies (multi-task vs. single-task). Data augmentation with additional unlabeled examples will also be explored.
aad167be3c902388ea625da4117fcae4325b8b7d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a resource-efficient paradigm for training small language models that leverages LLM-generated rationales as supervision, significantly reducing both the required training data and model size needed to outperform large LLMs. The method demonstrates that multi-task learning with rationales enables smaller models to surpass LLM performance with up to 2000× fewer parameters and over 85% less data, while also being more deployable. The approach is validated across multiple tasks and model sizes, and is shown to generalize to different LLM teachers and data regimes. The study also provides granular analysis of data/model efficiency trade-offs and demonstrates the superiority of multi-task rationale supervision over single-task approaches.

aade40af0d85b0b4fe15c97f6222d5c2e4d6d9b3.title: Graph of Thoughts: Solving Elaborate Problems with Large Language Models
aade40af0d85b0b4fe15c97f6222d5c2e4d6d9b3.research_question: How can large language models be enabled to solve complex, multi-step problems by modeling their reasoning process as an arbitrary graph structure, rather than being limited to chains or trees of thoughts?
aade40af0d85b0b4fe15c97f6222d5c2e4d6d9b3.hypothesis: Allowing large language models to reason using arbitrary graph structures of intermediate thoughts will improve their ability to solve elaborate, decomposable tasks, resulting in higher solution quality and lower inference costs compared to existing prompting schemes such as Chain-of-Thought and Tree-of-Thoughts.
aade40af0d85b0b4fe15c97f6222d5c2e4d6d9b3.proposed_method: A novel framework, Graph of Thoughts (GoT), will be developed to represent the reasoning process of large language models (LLMs) as a directed graph, where vertices correspond to 'LLM thoughts' (intermediate solutions, plans, or outputs) and edges represent dependencies between these thoughts. The framework will support advanced thought transformations, including aggregation (combining multiple thoughts into a new one), refinement (iterative improvement of thoughts), and generation (branching new thoughts from existing ones). The system architecture will include modular components for prompt generation, parsing LLM outputs, scoring and validating thoughts, and orchestrating the reasoning process according to a user-defined graph of operations. GoT will be extensible, allowing users to define new thought transformations, experiment with different LLMs, and customize the decomposition of complex tasks into subproblems and their subsequent aggregation.
aade40af0d85b0b4fe15c97f6222d5c2e4d6d9b3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of tasks that can be naturally decomposed, including sorting sequences of numbers, set intersection, keyword counting in text, and document merging. For each task, GoT will be compared against baselines such as Input-Output prompting, Chain-of-Thought, Self-Consistency with CoT, and Tree-of-Thoughts, using large language models like GPT-3.5 and Llama-2. Evaluation metrics will include solution quality (e.g., sorting accuracy, set intersection correctness, keyword count error, document redundancy and retention), inference cost (measured in API usage or tokens), and latency (number of reasoning steps). Experiments will systematically vary problem size, graph decomposition strategies, and branching factors to assess scalability and robustness. Each configuration will be run on at least 100 input samples per task, and results will be analyzed in terms of both median and quartile performance.
aade40af0d85b0b4fe15c97f6222d5c2e4d6d9b3.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first prompting framework that models LLM reasoning as an arbitrary graph, generalizing and subsuming prior paradigms such as Chain-of-Thought and Tree-of-Thoughts. It enables new classes of thought transformations, including aggregation and feedback loops, which are not possible in tree- or chain-based schemes. The modular and extensible system architecture allows for rapid prototyping of novel prompting strategies and supports fine-grained control over the reasoning process. The framework is designed to bring LLM reasoning closer to human-like and brain-inspired mechanisms, such as recurrence and complex networked thought patterns. A new metric, 'volume of a thought,' is introduced to quantify the expressiveness and information flow in different prompting schemes.

aae1d88c70cf18ef6aa23693a4dce8204e22d087.title: A Bi-Step Grounding Paradigm for Large Language Models in Recommendation Systems
aae1d88c70cf18ef6aa23693a4dce8204e22d087.research_question: How can large language models be effectively grounded and optimized for comprehensive, all-rank recommendation tasks in real-world recommendation systems, particularly under few-shot and multi-domain scenarios, while integrating statistical information such as item popularity and collaborative filtering?
aae1d88c70cf18ef6aa23693a4dce8204e22d087.hypothesis: A bi-step grounding paradigm that first aligns large language models to the recommendation space and then grounds outputs to actual item space, with the integration of statistical information, will enable LLMs to achieve superior all-rank recommendation performance, especially in few-shot and multi-domain settings, compared to traditional and existing LLM-based recommendation methods.
aae1d88c70cf18ef6aa23693a4dce8204e22d087.proposed_method: A novel two-step grounding framework, termed BIGRec, is proposed for leveraging large language models (LLMs) in recommendation systems. In the first step, LLMs are fine-tuned using recommendation-specific instruction data to constrain their generative outputs from the broad language space to a recommendation space, which includes both actual and hypothetical items relevant to user preferences. In the second step, the generated recommendation outputs are mapped to real-world items by extracting latent representations from the LLM and comparing them to embeddings of actual items, using L2 distance as the primary matching metric. To further enhance recommendation accuracy, statistical information such as item popularity and collaborative filtering scores is incorporated by reweighting the L2 distances or integrating prediction scores from traditional models, with tunable hyperparameters to control their influence. This paradigm is designed to be flexible, allowing seamless integration of various types of statistical information during the grounding process.
aae1d88c70cf18ef6aa23693a4dce8204e22d087.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two real-world sequential recommendation datasets: MovieLens 10M (movies) and Amazon Games (video games), which differ in their degree of popularity bias. The datasets will be temporally split into training, validation, and testing sets to simulate real-world recommendation scenarios. The proposed method will be compared against a range of baselines, including traditional sequential models (GRU4Rec, Caser, SASRec), state-of-the-art robust optimization models (DROS), and LLM-based methods (P5, GPT4Rec-LLaMA). Evaluation will use all-ranking protocols with metrics such as Hit Ratio (HR) and Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG) at various cutoff points (e.g., @1, @3, @5, @10, @20). Experiments will include few-shot settings (e.g., 1024 training samples), cross-domain training, and ablation studies on the integration of popularity and collaborative information. Model selection will use early stopping, and results will be averaged over multiple random seeds.
aae1d88c70cf18ef6aa23693a4dce8204e22d087.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a bi-step grounding paradigm (BIGRec) that uniquely enables LLMs to generate recommendations in an all-rank setting, efficiently mapping generative outputs to actual items while flexibly incorporating statistical information. The approach demonstrates strong few-shot and multi-domain capabilities, outperforming both traditional and existing LLM-based recommendation models, especially with limited training data. The paradigm also reveals the limited capacity of LLMs to assimilate statistical information from data alone and highlights the effectiveness of explicit integration of popularity and collaborative filtering, suggesting new directions for future LLM4Rec research.

aae2e7454945b904ca1d438d2ae4d4941ba11409.title: VAD: Vectorized Scene Representation for Efficient Autonomous Driving
aae2e7454945b904ca1d438d2ae4d4941ba11409.research_question: How can autonomous driving systems achieve efficient and accurate trajectory planning by leveraging a comprehensive and instance-level scene representation, while reducing computational overhead and improving safety?
aae2e7454945b904ca1d438d2ae4d4941ba11409.hypothesis: A fully vectorized scene representation, which models both dynamic agent motions and static map elements as vectors, will enable more efficient and safer end-to-end trajectory planning for autonomous vehicles compared to traditional rasterized representations.
aae2e7454945b904ca1d438d2ae4d4941ba11409.proposed_method: A novel end-to-end framework is developed that encodes the driving scene using a fully vectorized representation, including vectorized map elements (such as lane dividers, road boundaries, and pedestrian crossings) and dynamic agent motion vectors. The method utilizes multi-frame, multi-view camera inputs, processed through a backbone network and BEV (bird's-eye view) encoder to extract scene features. Specialized queries (BEV, agent, and map queries) interact via transformer-based modules to learn instance-level features for both perception and motion prediction. Planning is performed by an ego query that interacts with agent and map queries, and outputs a future trajectory through an MLP-based planning head. The planning process is regularized by three instance-level vectorized constraints: ego-agent collision, ego-boundary overstepping, and ego-lane directional constraints, all of which are differentiable and integrated into the end-to-end training.
aae2e7454945b904ca1d438d2ae4d4941ba11409.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the nuScenes dataset, which provides multi-camera data and annotations for urban driving scenarios. Both open-loop and closed-loop evaluations are performed. In open-loop, displacement error (DE) and collision rate (CR) are used as metrics, while closed-loop evaluation uses the CARLA simulator and Town05 benchmark, with Route Completion (RC) and Driving Score (DS) as metrics. The proposed method is compared against state-of-the-art baselines, including both rasterized and vectorized scene representation approaches, as well as LiDAR-based and vision-only methods. Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of vectorized constraints and query interactions. The system is implemented with variants (VAD-Base and VAD-Tiny) to evaluate trade-offs between speed and accuracy, and module-wise latency is measured on NVIDIA GPUs.
aae2e7454945b904ca1d438d2ae4d4941ba11409.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a fully vectorized paradigm for scene representation in autonomous driving, eliminating the need for computationally intensive rasterized maps and hand-designed post-processing. It leverages both implicit and explicit use of vectorized agent and map information through transformer-based query interactions and novel instance-level planning constraints. The method achieves state-of-the-art planning performance and significantly improves inference speed, demonstrating the practical advantages of vectorized scene modeling for real-world autonomous driving deployment.

aae382fe95b061018f214b1f101c55b6f4ae176b.title: Misspecification in Inverse Reinforcement Learning
aae382fe95b061018f214b1f101c55b6f4ae176b.research_question: How robust are standard behavioral models in Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) to misspecification, particularly when inferring reward functions from observed policies, and under what conditions do these models yield reliable inferences about agent preferences and intentions?
aae382fe95b061018f214b1f101c55b6f4ae176b.hypothesis: Standard behavioral models in IRL (optimality, Boltzmann rationality, and causal entropy maximization) exhibit varying degrees of robustness to model misspecification, and it is possible to formally characterize the types and degrees of misspecification to which each model is robust.
aae382fe95b061018f214b1f101c55b6f4ae176b.proposed_method: A mathematical and theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the robustness of IRL behavioral models to misspecification. The approach will formalize reward objects, ambiguity partitions, and admissibility/robustness criteria, enabling the derivation of necessary and sufficient conditions for robustness. The framework will be used to characterize how much and what kind of misspecification can be tolerated by different IRL models before they yield faulty inferences about the underlying reward function. Key technical steps include defining equivalence relations on reward functions (such as policy optimality and policy ordering), characterizing reward transformations that preserve these equivalence classes, and proving lemmas that allow generalization to new or restricted classes of models. The analysis will be extended to consider the effects of misspecified environment parameters (such as transition dynamics and discount factors) and restricted reward function classes.
aae382fe95b061018f214b1f101c55b6f4ae176b.experiment_details: The proposal is primarily theoretical and analytical, focusing on formal proofs and mathematical characterizations rather than empirical experiments. However, the framework will be applied to the three most common IRL behavioral models: optimality, Boltzmann rationality, and maximal causal entropy. For each model, the robustness to various forms of misspecification (including behavioral model, environment parameters, and reward function restrictions) will be derived and compared. Theoretical results will be illustrated with constructed examples and counterexamples, and the implications for real-world data (such as human demonstration data) will be discussed. Where possible, the framework will be extended to accommodate known priors or inductive biases, and suggestions for empirical validation will be outlined.
aae382fe95b061018f214b1f101c55b6f4ae176b.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a general and principled theoretical framework for analyzing misspecification robustness in IRL, providing necessary and sufficient conditions for robustness across standard and new behavioral models. The approach yields formal tools (lemmas and theorems) for deriving robustness properties of any IRL model, and characterizes the precise forms of misspecification to which each standard model is robust or sensitive. The analysis extends to misspecification of environment parameters and restricted reward function classes, and provides new insights into the limitations of transferability and the requirements for reliable preference inference in IRL. The work advances the theoretical understanding of IRL's applicability to real-world, complex, and imperfectly modeled settings.

ab01f985e771145e4de5a51742319e7de4e5fc4c.title: Neural Gaffer: Relighting Any Object via Diffusion
ab01f985e771145e4de5a51742319e7de4e5fc4c.research_question: How can single-image relighting be achieved for arbitrary objects under any novel environmental lighting condition, without requiring explicit scene decomposition or special capture setups, and how can such a method generalize to both 2D and 3D downstream tasks?
ab01f985e771145e4de5a51742319e7de4e5fc4c.hypothesis: A diffusion-based, image-conditioned generative model, fine-tuned on a large-scale synthetic relighting dataset with diverse objects and lighting conditions, can synthesize accurate and high-quality relit images from a single input image under arbitrary environmental lighting, outperforming existing methods in generalization and visual fidelity.
ab01f985e771145e4de5a51742319e7de4e5fc4c.proposed_method: A novel end-to-end 2D relighting diffusion model will be developed by fine-tuning a pre-trained image-to-image diffusion model (such as Zero-1-to-3) on a large-scale synthetic relighting dataset constructed from high-quality 3D object models (filtered from Objaverse) rendered under diverse HDR environment maps. The model will be conditioned on both the input image and a target environment map, with lighting information encoded via both LDR and normalized HDR representations to capture the full energy spectrum and lighting details. Environment maps will be rotated to align with the camera coordinate frame before conditioning, ensuring accurate correspondence between lighting direction and image space. The architecture will consist of an encoder to process input images and lighting maps, a denoising U-Net, and a decoder, all trained with a reconstruction loss on paired input-target relighting images. For 3D relighting, a two-stage pipeline will be implemented: first, the diffusion model will generate multi-view relighting predictions to coarsely tune the appearance field of a neural radiance field (NeRF), followed by a detail refinement stage using a diffusion guidance loss for enhanced fidelity.
ab01f985e771145e4de5a51742319e7de4e5fc4c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world images. The synthetic dataset, RelitObjaverse, will include approximately 18.4 million rendered images of 90,000 high-quality 3D objects under 30,000 lighting conditions, using Blender's Cycles renderer. Evaluation will be performed using standard metrics such as PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS, with additional channel-aligned metrics to address color-lighting ambiguities. Baseline comparisons will include recent single-image relighting methods such as DiLightNet and IC-Light for 2D tasks, and TensoIR and NVDIFFREC-MC for 3D relighting. For 3D experiments, multi-view images and target lighting conditions will be used to relight neural radiance fields, with quantitative and qualitative comparisons against baselines. Downstream 2D tasks, such as text-based relighting (using Text2Light-generated environment maps) and object insertion (using SAM for segmentation and DiffusionLight for lighting estimation), will be demonstrated to showcase versatility.
ab01f985e771145e4de5a51742319e7de4e5fc4c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first category-agnostic, single-image relighting diffusion model capable of handling arbitrary objects and lighting conditions without explicit scene decomposition. The method leverages a large-scale, high-quality synthetic relighting dataset and incorporates a dual-map (LDR and HDR) lighting conditioning strategy for robust energy spectrum reasoning. The two-stage 3D relighting pipeline, using the 2D diffusion model as a prior, enables efficient and high-fidelity relighting of neural radiance fields. The framework demonstrates superior generalization, accuracy, and versatility across both 2D and 3D tasks, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods and enabling new applications such as text-based relighting and seamless object insertion.

ab0e3d3e4d42369de5933a3b4c237780b41c0d77.title: Solving Quantitative Reasoning Problems with Language Models
ab0e3d3e4d42369de5933a3b4c237780b41c0d77.research_question: Can large language models be adapted to effectively solve quantitative reasoning problems, such as those found in mathematics, science, and engineering, using only natural language input and without reliance on external computational tools?
ab0e3d3e4d42369de5933a3b4c237780b41c0d77.hypothesis: Large language models, when further trained on high-quality technical content that combines natural language with formal mathematical notation, can achieve state-of-the-art performance on quantitative reasoning tasks across a variety of STEM domains, even in few-shot settings and without external tools.
ab0e3d3e4d42369de5933a3b4c237780b41c0d77.proposed_method: A large language model will be initialized from a general-purpose pretrained transformer (such as PaLM) and further trained (finetuned) on a curated dataset rich in mathematical and scientific content. The technical dataset will be sourced from arXiv preprints and web pages containing MathJax or LATEX-formatted mathematics, with careful preprocessing to preserve mathematical notation and structure. The model will be trained autoregressively to generate step-by-step solutions, including both natural language explanations and formal mathematical expressions. Inference-time techniques will include sampling multiple solutions per problem and selecting the most common answer via majority voting, which has been shown to outperform greedy decoding and log-likelihood reranking for these tasks.
ab0e3d3e4d42369de5933a3b4c237780b41c0d77.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several quantitative reasoning benchmarks, including the MATH dataset (12K middle and high school math problems), GSM8k (middle school math word problems), and the STEM subset of MMLU (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics multiple-choice questions). Additionally, a new set of 272 undergraduate-level STEM problems from MIT OpenCourseWare will be curated and used for evaluation. The evaluation will use few-shot prompting, with chain-of-thought or step-by-step rationales included in the prompts. Metrics will include accuracy of final answers (using symbolic equivalence checking via SymPy), majority voting accuracy over multiple samples (maj1@k), and pass@k. Baselines will include previous state-of-the-art models such as OpenAI's davinci-002 and PaLM, with and without majority voting. Experimental setup will control for prompt format, number of samples per problem, and use of external tools.
ab0e3d3e4d42369de5933a3b4c237780b41c0d77.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a large-scale training dataset that juxtaposes natural language with formal mathematical language, enabling the model to generate both explanations and precise mathematical expressions. The method demonstrates that scaling model size and improving data quality can significantly advance quantitative reasoning capabilities in language models. The use of majority voting over sampled solutions at inference time is shown to yield substantial performance gains. The approach establishes new baselines and state-of-the-art results on multiple quantitative reasoning benchmarks, and provides a new open-source dataset of undergraduate STEM problems for future research.

ab0f338f16ff24cff2d5b43df3f87a12097f2c7a.title: The AdEMAMix Optimizer: Better, Faster, Older
ab0f338f16ff24cff2d5b43df3f87a12097f2c7a.research_question: Can optimization algorithms for deep learning be improved by more effectively leveraging both recent and older gradients, rather than relying on a single exponential moving average (EMA) of past gradients?
ab0f338f16ff24cff2d5b43df3f87a12097f2c7a.hypothesis: A mixture of two exponential moving averages (EMAs) with distinct decay rates, incorporated into an Adam-based optimizer, will enable more effective use of both recent and very old gradients, resulting in faster convergence, better minima, and reduced forgetting compared to standard AdamW.
ab0f338f16ff24cff2d5b43df3f87a12097f2c7a.proposed_method: A new optimizer, AdEMAMix, is developed by modifying AdamW to use a mixture of two exponential moving averages (EMAs) for the first moment estimate. One EMA uses a fast decay rate (e.g., β1 ≈ 0.9) to capture recent gradients, while the other uses a much slower decay rate (e.g., β3 ≈ 0.9999) to retain information from older gradients. The parameter update combines these two momentum terms, weighted by a mixing coefficient α, and uses the standard AdamW second moment estimate and weight decay. To address early training instabilities, linear schedulers are introduced for both the slow EMA's decay rate and the mixing coefficient, gradually increasing their values during a warmup period. The optimizer is implemented efficiently, with minimal computational overhead, and supports memory optimizations by allowing the fast EMA to be replaced with the current gradient if desired.
ab0f338f16ff24cff2d5b43df3f87a12097f2c7a.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on large-scale language modeling and image classification tasks. For language modeling, Transformer models of various sizes (110M, 335M, 1.3B parameters) are trained on the RedPajama v2 dataset, using sequence lengths of 1024 tokens and batch sizes appropriate to model size. The number of training iterations ranges from 256k to 1.5M, with both cosine and constant learning rate schedules explored. Additional experiments are performed on Mamba models (168M parameters) using the FineWeb dataset. For vision tasks, ViT models (24M and 86M parameters) are trained on ImageNet-1k and ImageNet-21k, with up to 320 epochs and large batch sizes (4096), using standard data augmentations. Baselines include AdamW (with extensive hyperparameter tuning) and variants with different β values and schedulers. Evaluation metrics include validation/test loss, perplexity (for language models), and classification accuracy (for vision tasks). Additional analyses include measuring the rate of forgetting by tracking loss on held-out batches injected at different training times.
ab0f338f16ff24cff2d5b43df3f87a12097f2c7a.novelty_claims: The proposed optimizer introduces a novel mixture of two EMAs for the first moment estimate, allowing simultaneous sensitivity to recent gradients and effective use of very old gradients—something not achievable with a single EMA. AdEMAMix demonstrates improved convergence speed, reaches better or comparable minima with fewer training tokens, and significantly slows down model forgetting compared to AdamW. The method is shown to be robust across architectures (Transformers, Mamba, ViT) and datasets, and is compatible with large-scale distributed training. The work also motivates further research into alternative functions for leveraging gradient history beyond standard EMAs.

ab116ae3e6bc3aedfd1b6ec165e59a8219a5d2f5.title: VinePPO: Refining Credit Assignment in RL Training of LLMs
ab116ae3e6bc3aedfd1b6ec165e59a8219a5d2f5.research_question: Can improved credit assignment mechanisms enhance reinforcement learning (RL) training for large language models (LLMs), particularly in reasoning-heavy tasks with delayed rewards?
ab116ae3e6bc3aedfd1b6ec165e59a8219a5d2f5.hypothesis: Refining credit assignment in RL training of LLMs by leveraging unbiased Monte Carlo-based value estimation will lead to improved model performance, higher generalization, and greater computational efficiency compared to standard value network-based approaches.
ab116ae3e6bc3aedfd1b6ec165e59a8219a5d2f5.proposed_method: A new RL training algorithm, VinePPO, is proposed to address the credit assignment challenge in LLMs. Instead of relying on a value network (critic) to estimate the expected return at each intermediate state, VinePPO utilizes the flexibility of language environments to perform unbiased Monte Carlo (MC) rollouts from any intermediate state. For each state in a training trajectory, the partial context is re-fed to the policy, and K auxiliary continuations are sampled; the empirical mean of their returns is used as the value estimate for that state. These MC-based value estimates are then used to compute the advantage for each action, which in turn guides the policy update within the standard PPO framework. The approach isolates the effect of improved credit assignment by modifying only the advantage computation stage, while keeping all other PPO components and hyperparameters unchanged.
ab116ae3e6bc3aedfd1b6ec165e59a8219a5d2f5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on publicly available LLMs, specifically DeepSeekMath 7B and RhoMath 1.1B, and on mathematical reasoning datasets MATH and GSM8K, which cover a range of reasoning difficulties. Baselines will include standard PPO, PPO variants with no explicit credit assignment (RLOO, GRPO), and RL-free methods such as RestEM and DPO+. All methods will be initialized from the same SFT checkpoints and will be trained with matched episode budgets and hyperparameter tuning for fairness. Evaluation metrics will include Pass@1 accuracy on test sets, generalization slope (test accuracy vs. train accuracy), and computational efficiency measured by wall-clock time to reach peak performance. Additional analyses will assess value estimation error, action ranking accuracy, and the effect of the number of MC rollouts (K) on both accuracy and efficiency.
ab116ae3e6bc3aedfd1b6ec165e59a8219a5d2f5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first scalable RL post-training algorithm for LLMs that fundamentally improves credit assignment by leveraging MC-based value estimation in language environments. VinePPO demonstrates that unbiased, per-step value estimates can be efficiently computed via environment resets, leading to higher test accuracy, faster convergence, and improved generalization compared to both value network-based and credit-assignment-free baselines. The method isolates and quantifies the impact of refined credit assignment, challenging the necessity of value networks in RLHF for LLMs and providing a practical, reproducible alternative that scales with available compute.

ab22d54dd13876d25c6c8f46c40fb9ac41c61ec5.title: One for All: Towards Training One Graph Model for All Classification Tasks
ab22d54dd13876d25c6c8f46c40fb9ac41c61ec5.research_question: Can a single, unified graph neural network model be developed to effectively perform a wide range of classification tasks (node, link, and graph-level) across diverse graph domains, while supporting supervised, few-shot, and zero-shot learning scenarios?
ab22d54dd13876d25c6c8f46c40fb9ac41c61ec5.hypothesis: A unified graph model that leverages text-attributed graphs and large language models for feature encoding, combined with a standardized prompting paradigm, will enable effective cross-domain and cross-task generalization for classification tasks on graphs, including in low-resource and zero-shot settings.
ab22d54dd13876d25c6c8f46c40fb9ac41c61ec5.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a general-purpose framework that first converts all input graphs from various domains into text-attributed graphs (TAGs), where each node and edge is described by human-interpretable text. These textual features are encoded into a shared embedding space using a large language model (LLM), enabling the integration of heterogeneous graph data. The method unifies different classification tasks by introducing the Nodes-of-Interest (NOI) subgraph and NOI prompt node, which standardize the representation and readout for node, link, and graph-level tasks. A novel Graph Prompting Paradigm (GPP) is developed, wherein prompt substructures—including task descriptions and class nodes—are appended to the input graph, allowing the model to adaptively process various tasks and support in-context learning. The final model processes the prompted graph using a graph neural network, making predictions based on the embeddings of class nodes connected to the NOI prompt node.
ab22d54dd13876d25c6c8f46c40fb9ac41c61ec5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on nine widely used graph datasets spanning citation networks, molecular graphs, knowledge graphs, and web links, covering node, link, and graph-level classification tasks. The model will be evaluated in supervised, few-shot, and zero-shot learning scenarios. Baseline comparisons will include standard GNN architectures such as GCN, GAT, and GIN, as well as recent prompt-based and LLM-based graph models. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, AUC, and average precision, depending on the task type. The experimental setup will involve both independent and joint training across datasets, with ablation studies to assess the impact of different LLM encoders and the graph prompting paradigm.
ab22d54dd13876d25c6c8f46c40fb9ac41c61ec5.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to enable a single graph neural network model to jointly learn and perform classification tasks across multiple domains and task types using text-attributed graphs. The introduction of a unified task representation via the Nodes-of-Interest subgraph and prompt node, as well as the novel Graph Prompting Paradigm, allows for in-context, few-shot, and zero-shot learning on graphs. This approach leverages LLMs to bridge heterogeneous graph features and supports adaptive, task-dependent prediction without the need for fine-tuning on new tasks or domains.

ab31e40e94d2b168e3eb477f54416e9f11fa7255.title: Unsupervised Universal Image Segmentation
ab31e40e94d2b168e3eb477f54416e9f11fa7255.research_question: Can a unified unsupervised framework be developed to perform universal image segmentation, including semantic, instance, and panoptic segmentation, without relying on human-annotated labels?
ab31e40e94d2b168e3eb477f54416e9f11fa7255.hypothesis: A unified unsupervised segmentation framework that leverages self-supervised feature learning and clustering can achieve superior or competitive performance across semantic, instance, and panoptic segmentation tasks compared to task-specific unsupervised methods.
ab31e40e94d2b168e3eb477f54416e9f11fa7255.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a unified unsupervised segmentation framework, U2Seg, capable of handling semantic, instance, and panoptic segmentation. The method first generates class-agnostic instance masks from unlabeled images using self-supervised models (e.g., DINO) and MaskCut. These instance masks are clustered using K-Means to assign pseudo semantic labels, enabling semantic-aware instance segmentation. Simultaneously, unsupervised semantic segmentation is performed using models like STEGO to assign 'stuff' labels. The pseudo-labels for 'things' (instances) and 'stuff' (background) are merged to create comprehensive pixel-level pseudo-labels for panoptic segmentation. A universal segmentation model is then trained on these pseudo-labels in a multi-task manner, with separate branches for instance and semantic segmentation, using a combination of classification, detection, segmentation, and semantic losses.
ab31e40e94d2b168e3eb477f54416e9f11fa7255.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple benchmarks, including COCO, Cityscapes, PASCAL VOC, and UVO, evaluating unsupervised semantic, instance, and panoptic segmentation. The model will be pre-trained on 1.3M unlabeled ImageNet images and, for certain tasks, fine-tuned on unlabeled COCO images. Baselines will include state-of-the-art unsupervised methods such as CutLER for instance segmentation, STEGO for semantic segmentation, and their naive combination for panoptic segmentation. Evaluation metrics will include AP, AR for instance segmentation, PixelAcc and mIoU for semantic segmentation, and PQ, SQ, RQ for panoptic segmentation. Hungarian matching will be used to align predicted clusters with ground-truth categories for quantitative evaluation. Ablation studies will explore the impact of cluster number and pseudo-label quality.
ab31e40e94d2b168e3eb477f54416e9f11fa7255.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to address unsupervised universal image segmentation, jointly tackling semantic, instance, and panoptic segmentation without human annotations. The method introduces a novel pipeline for generating semantic-aware instance pseudo-labels via clustering, and merges them with unsupervised semantic segmentation outputs for panoptic labeling. It establishes new benchmarks for unsupervised panoptic segmentation and demonstrates consistent improvements over specialized state-of-the-art methods across all tasks and datasets. The approach also shows strong performance as a pretrained model for label-efficient learning in low-data regimes.

ab4ce5dda7ad4d9032995c9c049a89d65723c6aa.title: Just Ask for Calibration: Strategies for Eliciting Calibrated Confidence Scores from Language Models Fine-Tuned with Human Feedback
ab4ce5dda7ad4d9032995c9c049a89d65723c6aa.research_question: How can calibrated confidence scores be effectively elicited from language models fine-tuned with human feedback, particularly when standard model probabilities are poorly calibrated or unavailable?
ab4ce5dda7ad4d9032995c9c049a89d65723c6aa.hypothesis: Prompting RLHF-tuned language models to verbalize their confidence—either as numerical probabilities or linguistic expressions—will yield better-calibrated confidence estimates than relying on the models' conditional probabilities, and calibration can be further improved by prompting the model to consider multiple possible answers before assigning confidence.
ab4ce5dda7ad4d9032995c9c049a89d65723c6aa.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation will be conducted of multiple strategies for extracting calibrated confidence scores from RLHF-tuned language models. The approach will compare direct extraction of model conditional probabilities (estimated via sampling), binary correctness queries, and several forms of verbalized confidence elicitation. Verbalized strategies will include prompting the model to output numerical probabilities or select from a set of linguistic likelihood expressions, either in a single stage (answer and confidence together) or two stages (answer, then confidence). Additional enhancements will involve prompting the model to consider multiple answer choices before assigning confidence, as well as applying temperature scaling to further calibrate the scores. Chain-of-thought prompting will also be explored to assess its impact on calibration.
ab4ce5dda7ad4d9032995c9c049a89d65723c6aa.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several widely-used RLHF-tuned language models, including gpt-3.5-turbo, gpt-4, claude-1, claude-2, and Llama-2-70B-Chat. The evaluation will use three factual question-answering datasets: TriviaQA (1000 sampled validation questions), SciQ (1000 sampled validation questions), and TruthfulQA (all 817 validation questions). For each method, model responses and confidence scores will be generated for each question. Calibration will be assessed using multiple metrics: Expected Calibration Error (ECE), temperature-scaled ECE (ECE-t), Brier Score (BS-t), and area under the selective accuracy-coverage curve (AUC). Correctness of model answers will be determined using LLM-based equivalence checking to account for semantic matches. Baseline methods will include model log probabilities and binary correctness queries, while proposed methods will be compared across all metrics and datasets.
ab4ce5dda7ad4d9032995c9c049a89d65723c6aa.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces and systematically evaluates verbalization-based strategies for eliciting calibrated confidence scores from RLHF-tuned language models, a setting where standard conditional probabilities are often poorly calibrated or inaccessible. It claims that prompting models to verbalize their confidence—especially after considering multiple answer options—can significantly improve calibration, often reducing expected calibration error by over 50%. The approach is novel in its focus on RLHF-tuned models, its comparison of numerical and linguistic verbalization, and its demonstration that such strategies can outperform traditional probability-based methods without additional fine-tuning.

ab643f5b02786fc4772b662adcdb558c557d3bf6.title: In-Context Convergence of Transformers
ab643f5b02786fc4772b662adcdb558c557d3bf6.research_question: How do softmax-based transformers trained via gradient descent achieve in-context learning, particularly for linear function classes, and what are the convergence dynamics under different data feature distributions?
ab643f5b02786fc4772b662adcdb558c557d3bf6.hypothesis: Softmax-based transformers trained with gradient descent can achieve near-zero prediction error for in-context learning of linear functions, even in the presence of imbalanced feature distributions, through a stage-wise convergence process.
ab643f5b02786fc4772b662adcdb558c557d3bf6.proposed_method: A one-layer transformer architecture with softmax attention will be trained via gradient descent to perform in-context learning on linear regression tasks. The model will use structured prompts, where each token is a feature vector sampled from a set of orthonormal vectors with either balanced or imbalanced probabilities. The transformer will be parameterized with a consolidated query-key matrix and a fixed value matrix, and masking will be applied to prevent the query token from attending to itself. The training objective will be the minimization of the squared prediction error between the model's output and the true function value, with the model being initialized at zero and updated iteratively using gradient descent. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to characterize the training dynamics, focusing on the evolution of attention scores and bilinear attention weights across different training phases.
ab643f5b02786fc4772b662adcdb558c557d3bf6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic datasets generated according to the described structured data model, with feature vectors sampled either in a balanced (equal probability) or imbalanced (one dominant, others rare) fashion. The evaluation will focus on the model's prediction error for both dominant and under-represented features, using the squared loss as the primary metric. The experimental setup will include varying the number of features K, the number of prompt tokens N, and the learning rate η, with convergence rates and attention score concentration being tracked. Baselines will include linear transformer variants and potentially other in-context learning models, with comparisons made on convergence speed and final prediction accuracy.
ab643f5b02786fc4772b662adcdb558c557d3bf6.novelty_claims: The proposed research provides the first theoretical analysis of in-context learning dynamics for softmax-based transformers, moving beyond prior work limited to linear attention mechanisms. It establishes finite-time convergence guarantees for both balanced and imbalanced feature distributions, revealing a multi-phase or stage-wise convergence process, especially for under-represented features. The analysis introduces new proof techniques for tracking the interplay between different types of attention weights, offering tools that may be applicable to broader classes of transformer-based models.

ab6534589e25be82e537c2b33ce8cb9751da5f79.title: Neural Quantum Embedding: Pushing the Limits of Quantum Supervised Learning
ab6534589e25be82e537c2b33ce8cb9751da5f79.research_question: How can quantum data embedding for classical data be optimized to improve the performance, robustness, and generalization of quantum supervised learning models, particularly in the context of noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices?
ab6534589e25be82e537c2b33ce8cb9751da5f79.hypothesis: Optimizing quantum embedding through the integration of classical deep learning techniques, specifically neural networks, will enhance the separability of quantum-embedded data, thereby lowering empirical risk, improving classification accuracy, robustness to noise, and generalization performance beyond the limits imposed by conventional positive and trace-preserving quantum maps.
ab6534589e25be82e537c2b33ce8cb9751da5f79.proposed_method: A novel quantum embedding framework, Neural Quantum Embedding (NQE), is proposed, which leverages classical neural networks to learn data-dependent quantum embeddings that maximize the trace distance between quantum states representing different classes. The method maps classical input data through a trainable classical neural network, which outputs parameters for a quantum embedding circuit (e.g., ZZ feature map or amplitude encoding). The neural network is trained with a loss function related to the fidelity (or overlap) between quantum states, computed efficiently on a quantum computer, to implicitly maximize the trace distance and thus the distinguishability of quantum data. Dimensionality reduction can be handled either by preprocessing (e.g., PCA) or within the neural network itself. The approach avoids increasing quantum circuit depth and gate count, thereby maintaining compatibility with NISQ hardware and mitigating issues such as barren plateaus.
ab6534589e25be82e537c2b33ce8cb9751da5f79.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using both noiseless simulations and real quantum hardware (IBM quantum devices) for image classification tasks, specifically on binary subsets of the MNIST and Fashion-MNIST datasets. The proposed NQE method will be compared against conventional fixed quantum embeddings (e.g., ZZ feature map) and trainable unitary embeddings, with and without classical dimensionality reduction. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy, empirical risk, trace distance between quantum state ensembles, generalization error bounds (using effective dimension and quantum kernel methods), and robustness to noise. Baseline models will include quantum convolutional neural networks (QCNNs) and quantum kernel methods, with experiments repeated across multiple random initializations and device runs to ensure statistical significance.
ab6534589e25be82e537c2b33ce8cb9751da5f79.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a data-driven, trainable quantum embedding strategy that surpasses the fundamental limitations of positive and trace-preserving quantum maps by leveraging classical neural networks. This approach enables the maximization of quantum data separability, directly improving the lower bound of empirical risk and enhancing noise robustness. Unlike prior methods, NQE avoids increased quantum circuit depth and susceptibility to barren plateaus, making it practical for NISQ devices. The framework is broadly applicable to various quantum embedding schemes and consistently improves both optimization and generalization performance, as evidenced by reductions in empirical risk, effective dimension, and generalization error bounds, as well as substantial gains in classification accuracy on real quantum hardware.

ab736f512146965a4223e81e672935cd26f1c91e.title: Multi-Task Learning for Routing Problem with Cross-Problem Zero-Shot Generalization
ab736f512146965a4223e81e672935cd26f1c91e.research_question: How can a single unified learning-based model be developed to efficiently solve diverse vehicle routing problems (VRPs) with varying combinations of attributes, and achieve strong zero-shot generalization to new, unseen VRP variants?
ab736f512146965a4223e81e672935cd26f1c91e.hypothesis: A unified neural network model, trained via multi-task reinforcement learning and equipped with an attribute composition mechanism, can leverage shared underlying attributes among VRP variants to achieve effective cross-problem zero-shot generalization, outperforming single-task models and existing heuristics on both synthetic and real-world datasets.
ab736f512146965a4223e81e672935cd26f1c91e.proposed_method: A unified neural network architecture will be designed based on an encoder-decoder framework, extended from the Attention Model. The encoder generates node embeddings using multi-head attention layers with skip connections and instance normalization, while the decoder constructs solutions sequentially, incorporating both node and attribute embeddings. An attribute composition block is introduced to dynamically encode problem-specific attributes (such as capacity, time windows, open routes, backhauls, and duration limits) into the model's decision process. The model will be trained using multi-task reinforcement learning (REINFORCE algorithm with a shared baseline), where each batch samples instances from different VRP variants. The attribute composition mechanism enables the model to activate and update relevant attributes at each decoding step, allowing it to generalize to any combination of attributes, including those not seen during training.
ab736f512146965a4223e81e672935cd26f1c91e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on eleven VRP variants, including both synthetic benchmark datasets and real-world logistics scenarios. The unified model will be trained on a subset of five VRP variants and evaluated in a zero-shot manner on the remaining variants, as well as on standard benchmarks (e.g., CVRPLIB) and industry datasets. Baselines will include state-of-the-art neural combinatorial optimization methods (such as POMO, SGBS, and AM), classical heuristics (e.g., hybrid genetic search, nearest/farthest insertion), and single-task learning models. Evaluation metrics will include average solution gap to optimal or best-known solutions, computational time, and robustness across problem sizes and distributions. Additional analyses will include t-SNE visualizations of learned embeddings and Hausdorff distance to quantify generalization across VRP variants.
ab736f512146965a4223e81e672935cd26f1c91e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first unified neural solver for cross-problem generalization in VRPs, leveraging a novel attribute composition block to encode shared and problem-specific constraints. This enables exponential scalability to unseen VRP variants via zero-shot generalization, eliminating the need for retraining or fine-tuning for new problem types. The method demonstrates state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of VRP variants, substantially reducing the average solution gap compared to existing methods and achieving robust results on both synthetic and real-world datasets. The approach also significantly reduces training and deployment costs by consolidating multiple problem-specific models into a single, efficient framework.

ab80f81defa62fdbae22bf996f76cca04c3915c1.title: Towards a Mechanistic Explanation of Diffusion Model Generalization
ab80f81defa62fdbae22bf996f76cca04c3915c1.research_question: What are the underlying mechanisms that explain the generalization behavior of diffusion models across different architectures, and can these mechanisms be characterized or replicated by training-free, localized denoising operations?
ab80f81defa62fdbae22bf996f76cca04c3915c1.hypothesis: Diffusion model denoisers generalize through localized denoising operations, and these local operations approximate the training objective well over much of the training distribution. As a result, the generalization behavior of diffusion models can be explained and replicated by aggregating local empirical denoisers.
ab80f81defa62fdbae22bf996f76cca04c3915c1.proposed_method: A mechanistic analysis will be conducted by comparing pre-trained diffusion model denoisers to their theoretically optimal empirical counterparts, focusing on the nature and structure of their approximation errors. The methodology involves measuring the sensitivity of network denoisers to local perturbations via gradient sensitivity heatmaps, revealing the extent of local inductive bias. Novel, fully training-free denoising algorithms will be developed, specifically Patch Set Posterior Composite (PSPC) denoisers, which aggregate local empirical denoisers (patch posterior means) across varying spatial locations. Two variants will be implemented: PSPC-Square, using overlapping square patches with a time-varying patch size schedule, and PSPC-Flex, using adaptive, non-square patches derived from gradient sensitivity maps. The PSPC denoisers will be evaluated for their ability to replicate the outputs of neural network denoisers and to generate structurally similar samples.
ab80f81defa62fdbae22bf996f76cca04c3915c1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three image datasets: CIFAR-10, FFHQ 64x64, and AFHQv2 64x64. For each dataset, both forward and reverse diffusion process samples will be generated using pre-trained diffusion models (including NCSN++, DDPM++, DiT, and U-ViT architectures) and compared to the outputs of the proposed PSPC denoisers. Baselines will include the optimal empirical denoiser, Gaussian denoiser, and Closed-Form Diffusion Model (CFDM) denoiser. Evaluation metrics will include mean squared error (MSE) between denoiser outputs, structural similarity (using SSCD cosine similarity), and qualitative visual comparison of generated samples. The experimental setup will involve varying the noise level (t) across the diffusion process, using tens of thousands of samples per dataset, and employing both fixed and adaptive patch aggregation strategies.
ab80f81defa62fdbae22bf996f76cca04c3915c1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a fully training-free, patch-based denoising mechanism that closely replicates the generalization behavior of neural diffusion models, regardless of network architecture. The research provides the first comprehensive evidence that local inductive bias and patch-based denoising operations are central to diffusion model generalization. The PSPC denoisers, particularly the adaptive PSPC-Flex variant, achieve lower error and greater structural similarity to neural network denoisers than prior empirical, Gaussian, or closed-form methods. This work establishes a mechanistic explanation for diffusion model generalization and demonstrates that significant aspects of this behavior can be reproduced without neural network training.

abb6e9dc000fbc094e1598ae5e81c545340656ea.title: A Deep Instance Generative Framework for MILP Solvers Under Limited Data Availability
abb6e9dc000fbc094e1598ae5e81c545340656ea.research_question: How can novel and realistic mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) instances be generated without relying on expert-designed formulations, especially under conditions of limited real-world data availability, in a way that preserves both the structural and computational properties required for effective solver development and evaluation?
abb6e9dc000fbc094e1598ae5e81c545340656ea.hypothesis: A deep generative framework that represents MILP instances as bipartite graphs and employs a masked variational autoencoder can learn to generate new MILP instances that closely resemble real-world data in structure and computational hardness, thereby enriching datasets and improving downstream solver performance, even when only limited original data is available.
abb6e9dc000fbc094e1598ae5e81c545340656ea.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a deep generative framework for MILP instance generation by representing each MILP as a weighted bipartite graph, where variables and constraints are vertices and non-zero coefficients are edges. A masked variational autoencoder (VAE) paradigm is employed, inspired by masked language models, where parts of the original graph (specifically, constraint vertices and their edges) are iteratively masked and replaced using latent variables sampled from a learned distribution. The encoder utilizes a graph neural network (GNN) to extract node representations, which are then used to parameterize Gaussian latent variables. The decoder reconstructs the masked graph through four cooperative modules: bias predictor, degree predictor, logits predictor, and weights predictor, each responsible for predicting different components of the constraint structure and coefficients. During inference, the encoder is discarded and latent variables are sampled from a standard Gaussian, enabling the generation of novel instances by repeatedly masking and regenerating constraints, with a hyperparameter controlling the trade-off between novelty and similarity to the training data.
abb6e9dc000fbc094e1598ae5e81c545340656ea.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on several datasets, including large synthetic datasets (Maximum Independent Set and Set Covering, each with 1000 instances), a medium-sized Mixed-integer Knapsack dataset (80 training, 10 test instances), and a small real-world Nurse Scheduling dataset (4 instances).
