The quality of generated instances is evaluated using three benchmarks: (1) structural distributional similarity, measured by 11 classical graph statistics and Jensen-Shannon divergence; (2) computational hardness, assessed via solving time and number of branching nodes using the Gurobi solver; and (3) downstream task performance, specifically optimal value prediction and integration with a predict-and-search framework. Baselines include a heuristic generator (Bowly) and a random generator with the same architecture but no learned parameters. Multiple masking ratios are tested to analyze the trade-off between novelty and similarity, and results are reported in terms of similarity scores, solver performance, and downstream task improvements.
abb6e9dc000fbc094e1598ae5e81c545340656ea.novelty_claims: The proposed framework constitutes the first deep learning-based generative model for general MILP instance generation, capable of learning directly from data without requiring expert-designed formulations. The method uniquely combines bipartite graph representation with a masked VAE paradigm, enabling the preservation of both structural and computational properties of real-world MILP instances. The approach allows for controllable trade-offs between novelty and similarity, automatically produces feasible and bounded instances, and demonstrates significant improvements in downstream solver tasks, thereby addressing a critical bottleneck in data-limited MILP research and opening new avenues for adversarial instance generation and pre-training in combinatorial optimization.

abd4ec951931e0b43d06ba28dbc39f23cdacd29f.title: Two-Steps Diffusion Policy for Robotic Manipulation via Genetic Denoising
abd4ec951931e0b43d06ba28dbc39f23cdacd29f.research_question: How can the inference efficiency and performance of diffusion-based policies for robotic manipulation be improved, particularly by addressing the challenges posed by out-of-distribution states and the structured, low-dimensional nature of action distributions in embodied AI tasks?
abd4ec951931e0b43d06ba28dbc39f23cdacd29f.hypothesis: Tailoring the denoising process and introducing a population-based genetic denoising strategy will enable diffusion policies to achieve equal or superior performance with significantly fewer inference steps by reducing out-of-distribution risk and improving sample quality, especially in low-dimensional robotic action spaces.
abd4ec951931e0b43d06ba28dbc39f23cdacd29f.proposed_method: A novel two-step diffusion policy framework is proposed for robotic manipulation, leveraging a genetic denoising process. The approach begins by generating a population of noisy action samples, then iteratively applies a denoising step where each sample is scored using an out-of-distribution (OoD) fitness metric (such as clipping frequency or Stein score). At each denoising iteration, a subset of samples with the highest fitness scores is selected via multinomial sampling, duplicated to maintain population size, and further denoised. The denoising schedule and noise injection scale are carefully tuned to exploit the low-dimensional structure of robotic action spaces, favoring exploitation over exploration during inference. This process is designed to minimize the number of neural function evaluations (NFEs) required, enabling high-quality action generation in as few as two denoising steps without retraining or architectural changes.
abd4ec951931e0b43d06ba28dbc39f23cdacd29f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 14 robotic manipulation tasks drawn from the D4RL and Robomimic benchmarks, covering a range of action horizons and inference budgets. Baseline methods for comparison include DDPM, DDIM, EDM, and shortcut diffusion models, all using the same UNet architecture with 65M parameters to ensure fairness. Each configuration will be evaluated over hundreds of random seeds (100 for Adroit Hand, 500 for Robomimic), with hyperparameter sweeps over inference steps, noise scales, action horizons, and population sizes for the genetic algorithm. Evaluation metrics include normalized task success rates and inference wall-clock time, with detailed analysis of the impact of denoising schedule, noise injection, and population-based selection on performance and computational efficiency.
abd4ec951931e0b43d06ba28dbc39f23cdacd29f.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first application of genetic algorithms to accelerate diffusion model sampling in robotic manipulation, enabling efficient two-step inference with improved or matched performance compared to standard diffusion policies. Key innovations include a population-based denoising process guided by out-of-distribution fitness scores, principled adaptation of the denoising schedule and noise scale to the structure of robotic action spaces, and empirical demonstration of substantial performance gains and inference speedups without retraining or model modifications.

abdb0f9d1486dbb024c4bc9f8f9dc40464c58715.title: Sheared LLaMA: Accelerating Language Model Pre-training via Structured Pruning
abdb0f9d1486dbb024c4bc9f8f9dc40464c58715.research_question: Can smaller, general-purpose, and competitive large language models (LLMs) be efficiently produced by leveraging existing pre-trained LLMs, while using significantly less compute than training such models from scratch?
abdb0f9d1486dbb024c4bc9f8f9dc40464c58715.hypothesis: Structured pruning of existing pre-trained LLMs, followed by targeted continued pre-training with dynamic data selection, will yield smaller models that match or surpass the performance of similarly-sized models trained from scratch, while requiring only a fraction of the compute resources.
abdb0f9d1486dbb024c4bc9f8f9dc40464c58715.proposed_method: A two-stage approach is developed for efficient creation of smaller LLMs from larger pre-trained models. First, targeted structured pruning is employed, which prunes the source model to a specified target architecture by learning pruning masks at multiple granularities (layers, heads, hidden and intermediate dimensions) via constrained optimization with Lagrange multipliers, ensuring the pruned model matches the desired shape. The pruning masks are parameterized as hard concrete distributions to enable discrete prune/retain decisions. Second, continued pre-training is performed on the pruned model using a dynamic batch loading algorithm, which adjusts the proportion of training data from different domains on-the-fly based on the rate of loss reduction in each domain, ensuring balanced and efficient knowledge recovery. The dynamic batch loading uses reference losses predicted by a scaling function or from the source model to guide data allocation, and is applied during both pruning and continued pre-training.
abdb0f9d1486dbb024c4bc9f8f9dc40464c58715.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize the LLaMA2-7B model as the source, pruning it to target sizes of 1.3B and 2.7B parameters, matching the architectures of Pythia-1.4B and INCITE-Base-3B, respectively. The RedPajama dataset, a replication of LLaMA1's pre-training data, will be used for both pruning (0.4B tokens) and continued pre-training (50B tokens), with held-out validation sets for each domain. Baselines for comparison include OPT, Pythia, INCITE, OpenLLaMA, and TinyLlama models of similar sizes. Evaluation will be conducted on a suite of zero-shot and few-shot downstream tasks (e.g., ARC, LAMBADA, LogiQA, PIQA, SciQ, WinoGrande, HellaSwag, MMLU, NQ) using the lm-evaluation-harness, as well as instruction tuning performance using ShareGPT data. Additional analyses will compare inference speed and perplexity with other pruning methods (e.g., CoFiPruning, LLM-Pruner) and assess the impact of dynamic batch loading on data usage and downstream performance.
abdb0f9d1486dbb024c4bc9f8f9dc40464c58715.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel targeted structured pruning algorithm that produces compact, dense models of pre-specified, standard architectures, overcoming limitations of prior structured pruning methods that yield irregular configurations. The dynamic batch loading algorithm is also novel in its use of reference losses to dynamically adjust domain data proportions during continued pre-training, leading to more efficient data use and improved downstream performance. The approach achieves state-of-the-art results for pruned LLMs, demonstrating that competitive small-scale LLMs can be produced with only a small fraction of the compute required for training from scratch, and is highly generalizable to larger models and datasets.

abe90a291e7cf567ce5c9012a692beeae153068d.title: Think before you speak: Training Language Models With Pause Tokens
abe90a291e7cf567ce5c9012a692beeae153068d.research_question: Can introducing artificial delays in the token generation process of transformer-based language models, via special pause tokens, improve the models' performance on a variety of downstream tasks? What are the effects of such delays when incorporated during pretraining, finetuning, or both?
abe90a291e7cf567ce5c9012a692beeae153068d.hypothesis: Introducing learnable pause tokens to delay next-token prediction during both pretraining and finetuning stages will enable language models to utilize additional computational pathways, resulting in improved performance on tasks requiring reasoning, comprehension, and recall, compared to standard immediate next-token prediction.
abe90a291e7cf567ce5c9012a692beeae153068d.proposed_method: A novel training and inference paradigm is developed for decoder-only transformer language models, wherein a special, learnable <pause> token is appended to the input sequence to artificially delay the generation of the next output token. During pretraining, multiple <pause> tokens are inserted at random positions in the input, and the model is trained with the standard next-token prediction loss, ignoring loss terms corresponding to the <pause> tokens. For downstream finetuning, a fixed number of <pause> tokens are appended to the input prefix, and the model is trained to predict the target sequence, again ignoring outputs until the last <pause> token. At inference, the same number of <pause> tokens are appended, and outputs are ignored until after the final <pause> token. The approach is evaluated in four configurations: standard training, pause tokens only in finetuning, pause tokens only in pretraining, and pause tokens in both pretraining and finetuning.
abe90a291e7cf567ce5c9012a692beeae153068d.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on decoder-only transformer models with 1B and 130M parameters. Both standard and pause-trained models are pretrained on the C4 English corpus (200B tokens), with pause tokens randomly inserted at 10% of sequence length during pause-pretraining. Downstream evaluation spans nine diverse tasks, including reasoning (GSM8k), extractive QA (SQuAD, CoQA), general understanding (CommonSenseQA, PhysicalIQA), long-term context recall (LAMBADA), natural language inference (HellaSwag), and fact recall (WebQuestions, NaturalQuestions). For each task, models are finetuned with either 10 or 50 pause tokens, and the best result is reported. Baselines include standard pretraining/finetuning, and models with pause tokens only in one stage. Evaluation metrics include accuracy and exact match (EM) scores as appropriate for each dataset. Ablations explore the effect of the number and position (appending vs. prepending) of pause tokens, as well as robustness to mismatched numbers of pause tokens between finetuning and inference.
abe90a291e7cf567ce5c9012a692beeae153068d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the concept of pause-training, where learnable pause tokens are used to delay next-token prediction and expand the computational width of transformer models without significant parameter increase. The method demonstrates that such delays, when incorporated during both pretraining and finetuning, yield significant performance gains on a variety of downstream tasks. The work provides empirical evidence and theoretical insights into how artificial delays can enhance model expressivity, and establishes a new paradigm for delayed next-token prediction in language models. Additionally, the approach is shown to be robust to moderate mismatches in the number of pause tokens between training and inference, and outperforms strategies that use filler characters or only introduce delays at a single training stage.

abec4dcbff2c6be5578ee5bf6c96347e7901b6a0.title: Reinforcement Learning from Passive Data via Latent Intentions
abec4dcbff2c6be5578ee5bf6c96347e7901b6a0.research_question: How can reinforcement learning agents leverage passive observational data, such as videos without action or reward labels, to learn representations that accelerate and improve performance on downstream RL tasks, even when the passive data comes from different embodiments or environments?
abec4dcbff2c6be5578ee5bf6c96347e7901b6a0.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that learning intention-conditioned value functions from passive data enables the extraction of state representations that are effective for downstream value prediction and control, regardless of the lack of action and reward annotations and potential embodiment or domain mismatch.
abec4dcbff2c6be5578ee5bf6c96347e7901b6a0.proposed_method: A novel pre-training framework is developed that learns from passive, action- and reward-free observation sequences by modeling latent intentions. The approach introduces an intention-conditioned value function (ICVF) that estimates the likelihood of achieving future outcomes when acting according to a latent intention. The ICVF is parameterized as a multilinear model over learned state, outcome, and intention representations. Training is performed using a temporal-difference learning objective adapted to passive data, where transitions are weighted by an advantage estimator that identifies transitions likely to have resulted from acting optimally under a given intention. The method does not require action or reward labels and is compatible with diverse, unstructured passive datasets, including those from different agent embodiments or real-world videos.
abec4dcbff2c6be5578ee5bf6c96347e7901b6a0.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted in a two-stage process: pre-training on large-scale passive datasets (e.g., D4RL Antmaze, XMagical cross-embodiment videos, and YouTube videos of Atari games) and downstream evaluation on standard RL tasks using smaller, action- and reward-annotated datasets. Baselines include state-of-the-art representation learning methods such as CURL, CPC, APV, VIP, and RLV, as well as an oracle with access to full action and reward labels. Evaluation metrics include downstream RL performance (normalized return), value estimation accuracy via linear probes, and action prediction accuracy. The experimental setup ensures fair comparison by initializing downstream RL agents with learned representations and, where appropriate, regularizing to maintain pre-trained features.
abec4dcbff2c6be5578ee5bf6c96347e7901b6a0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to pre-train RL agents from passive, action- and reward-free data by modeling a latent intention space and learning intention-conditioned value functions via temporal-difference learning. The method enables transfer of generalizable, control-relevant representations across embodiments and domains, outperforming prior representation learning and behavioral prediction baselines. The multilinear parameterization of the ICVF and its application to passive data are novel, providing a principled way to extract features suitable for value-based RL from unstructured observational datasets.

ac23f4b5c3837e72a6ec17cc5caa632db885a12c.title: Efficient Time Series Processing for Transformers and State-Space Models through Token Merging
ac23f4b5c3837e72a6ec17cc5caa632db885a12c.research_question: How can computational efficiency in time series processing be improved for both transformer and state-space models, particularly for long input sequences, without significantly degrading forecasting accuracy?
ac23f4b5c3837e72a6ec17cc5caa632db885a12c.hypothesis: Applying domain-specific token merging algorithms, especially those that exploit local sequence structure and causality, will substantially accelerate time series models while maintaining or even improving prediction quality, particularly for high-entropy or noisy datasets.
ac23f4b5c3837e72a6ec17cc5caa632db885a12c.proposed_method: A novel local token merging algorithm will be developed that selectively combines tokens within a local neighborhood, controlled by a locality parameter k, to reduce the number of tokens processed in each model layer. This approach will be designed to adjust computational complexity from quadratic to linear, depending on the neighborhood size, enabling scalability to very long sequences and compatibility with both transformer and state-space architectures. The method will include a causal variant to preserve temporal order for decoder models and a dynamic merging scheme that adapts the merging rate based on token similarity thresholds for each input. The merging process will be applied after self-attention or state-space operations, and an unmerging step will be implemented as needed to maintain output dimensionality.
ac23f4b5c3837e72a6ec17cc5caa632db885a12c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of time series forecasting datasets, including ETTh1, ETTm1, Weather, Electricity, Traffic, and the long-range DummyMouseEnhancersEnsembldataset for genomic sequence modeling. Multiple transformer architectures (Autoformer, FEDformer, Informer, Non-stationary Transformer, vanilla Transformer) and state-space models (HyenaDNA, Mamba) will be evaluated across various model sizes and input lengths. The proposed local merging will be benchmarked against global merging and baseline models without token merging. Evaluation metrics will include mean squared error (MSE) for forecasting and classification accuracy for genomic tasks, as well as computational throughput (speed-up) and FLOPs. Both inference-time and training-time merging will be tested, and ablation studies will analyze the impact of merging on model performance, spectral properties of the data, and dependencies on input length and token similarity.
ac23f4b5c3837e72a6ec17cc5caa632db885a12c.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first systematic investigation of token merging for time series models, extending the concept from computer vision to both transformers and state-space models. A domain-specific local token merging algorithm is proposed, which is the first to enable causal merging in transformer decoders and to scale merging complexity from quadratic to linear. The approach identifies spectral and model-specific properties that predict when merging is beneficial, and demonstrates that local merging can improve both efficiency and accuracy, achieving up to 5400% acceleration and up to 9% forecasting improvement. The method is also the first to apply token merging in state-space models for long sequence processing and to propose dynamic, similarity-based merging schedules for real-world adaptability.

ac258100ebe178287ae4ae3dc7ac78f8c27e017d.title: Language Agents with Reinforcement Learning for Strategic Play in the Werewolf Game
ac258100ebe178287ae4ae3dc7ac78f8c27e017d.research_question: How can strategic language agents be developed to exhibit strong decision-making abilities and flexible language actions in complex social deduction games with unbounded action spaces, such as Werewolf, while overcoming intrinsic biases present in large language models?
ac258100ebe178287ae4ae3dc7ac78f8c27e017d.hypothesis: Integrating reinforcement learning with large language models, along with mechanisms for hidden role deduction and diverse action generation, will enable language agents to overcome intrinsic biases, leading to improved strategic play and human-level performance in complex social deduction games.
ac258100ebe178287ae4ae3dc7ac78f8c27e017d.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that combines large language models (LLMs) with reinforcement learning (RL) to create strategic language agents for the Werewolf game. The framework consists of three main components: (1) Hidden role deduction, where an LLM processes raw game observations to extract structured information and deduce the hidden roles and reliability of all players; (2) Diverse action generation, which prompts the LLM to generate a set of diverse and strategically distinct action candidates for each decision point, using both vanilla and iterative prompting depending on action complexity; (3) Population-based RL training, where a self-attention policy network takes as input the observation and action candidates (embedded via the LLM) and learns to select actions by playing against a population of diverse agents, including past RL checkpoints and pure LLM-based agents with predefined playstyles. The RL policy is trained to optimize decision-making by overcoming intrinsic LLM biases and improving robustness through population-based training.
ac258100ebe178287ae4ae3dc7ac78f8c27e017d.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted in a custom text-based seven-player Werewolf environment, using two Werewolves, one Seer, one Doctor, and three Villagers. The proposed agents are evaluated through a series of case studies analyzing action distributions, a round-robin tournament against four state-of-the-art LLM-based baselines (ReAct, ReCon, Concurrent, and Atomic), and human-agent experiments involving 160 human participants. Evaluation metrics include win rates as both Villagers and Werewolves, with additional ablation studies to assess the contribution of each framework component (deduction, diversity, RL policy, and population-based training). The framework is also tested for robustness and human-level performance by comparing agent and human win rates in mixed-agent and all-human games.
ac258100ebe178287ae4ae3dc7ac78f8c27e017d.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to combine LLMs with RL for strategic play in social deduction games with unbounded language action spaces, such as Werewolf. Key innovations include a structured hidden role deduction mechanism, diverse action candidate generation to mitigate intrinsic LLM bias, and a population-based RL policy that learns to select among language actions in a non-fixed action space. The approach demonstrates superior performance to existing LLM-based agents, achieves human-level play, and provides a generalizable method for overcoming LLM biases in complex multi-agent environments.

ac2618b2ce5cdcf86f9371bcca98bc5e37e46f51.title: Efficiently Modeling Long Sequences with Structured State Spaces
ac2618b2ce5cdcf86f9371bcca98bc5e37e46f51.research_question: How can a single, principled sequence modeling architecture efficiently and effectively handle long-range dependencies across diverse modalities and tasks, including very long sequences, while maintaining scalability and generality?
ac2618b2ce5cdcf86f9371bcca98bc5e37e46f51.hypothesis: A structured state space model (SSM) with a novel parameterization that enables efficient computation and stable diagonalization can serve as a general-purpose sequence model, achieving superior performance on long-range dependency tasks and competitive results across a variety of sequence modeling benchmarks.
ac2618b2ce5cdcf86f9371bcca98bc5e37e46f51.proposed_method: The proposed approach develops a Structured State Space (S4) sequence model based on a new parameterization of the state matrix in the state space model (SSM). The method decomposes the SSM state matrix A as the sum of a normal (diagonalizable) and a low-rank matrix, enabling stable diagonalization and efficient computation. The S4 layer computes the SSM convolution kernel in frequency space using the Cauchy kernel and Woodbury identity, which allows for O(N + L) time and space complexity for sequence length L and state size N. The architecture supports both convolutional and recurrent views, enabling parallel training and fast autoregressive inference. The model is implemented as a deep neural network with multiple S4 layers, each parameterized by the structured SSM, and supports broadcasting across hidden features with non-linear activations between layers.
ac2618b2ce5cdcf86f9371bcca98bc5e37e46f51.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a wide range of benchmarks to evaluate the efficiency and effectiveness of the S4 model. Key datasets include the Long Range Arena (LRA) benchmark for long-range dependency tasks (with sequence lengths up to 16,384), the SC10 subset of the Speech Commands dataset for raw speech classification, sequential CIFAR-10 for image modeling, and WikiText-103 for language modeling. Baselines for comparison include standard and efficient Transformer variants (e.g., Performer, Linear Transformer), RNNs, CNNs, and prior state space models (e.g., LSSL). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, bits per dimension (for generative modeling), perplexity (for language modeling), training/inference speed, and memory usage. The experimental setup will match parameter counts across models where possible, and will assess both training and inference efficiency, as well as the ability to handle changes in sampling resolution without retraining.
ac2618b2ce5cdcf86f9371bcca98bc5e37e46f51.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel parameterization for state space models that enables stable and efficient computation of long-range dependencies. The S4 model achieves near-optimal computational and memory complexity for sequence modeling, surpasses previous state space models in both speed and memory usage, and demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on challenging long-range dependency benchmarks. Additionally, S4 provides a unified framework that can be applied across diverse modalities and tasks with minimal specialization, supports fast autoregressive generation, and adapts to changes in data sampling rates without retraining.

ac5824e9ff924a937d9eef379d0b581de2417678.title: RULER: What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?
ac5824e9ff924a937d9eef379d0b581de2417678.research_question: How can long-context language models be comprehensively evaluated for their ability to utilize extended input contexts, beyond simple retrieval tasks, and what are the limitations of current models in handling complex, synthetic long-context tasks across a range of context sizes and complexities?
ac5824e9ff924a937d9eef379d0b581de2417678.hypothesis: Long-context language models, despite high performance on simple retrieval tasks, will exhibit significant performance degradation as context length and task complexity increase, and current benchmarks do not sufficiently capture the breadth of long-context understanding required for real-world applications.
ac5824e9ff924a937d9eef379d0b581de2417678.proposed_method: A new synthetic benchmark, RULER, will be developed to evaluate long-context language models across four task categories: retrieval, multi-hop tracing, aggregation, and question answering. The benchmark will feature flexible configurations allowing control over sequence length, task complexity, and the type and placement of relevant and distracting information. Retrieval tasks will extend the classic needle-in-a-haystack paradigm to include multiple keys, values, and queries, while multi-hop tracing will emulate coreference chain resolution through variable tracking. Aggregation tasks will require models to extract common or frequent words from long, noisy contexts, and question answering tasks will adapt existing short-context datasets by inserting distractors. All tasks will be automatically generated to ensure scalability and minimize reliance on parametric knowledge.
ac5824e9ff924a937d9eef379d0b581de2417678.experiment_details: Seventeen long-context language models, including both open-source and closed-source models with claimed context lengths ranging from 4K to 1M tokens, will be evaluated on 13 representative RULER tasks. Each model will be tested at multiple context lengths (4K, 8K, 16K, 32K, 64K, 128K), with 500 examples per task and context length. Evaluation will use recall-based accuracy, with answer prefixes appended to prevent refusal or irrelevant generation. Baselines will include Llama2-7B at 4K context, and model performance will be aggregated using weighted averages to simulate real-world usage distributions. Additional analyses will examine the effects of model size, training context length, and architecture (Transformer vs. non-Transformer) on long-context performance.
ac5824e9ff924a937d9eef379d0b581de2417678.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces a comprehensive suite of synthetic tasks that go beyond retrieval to assess multi-hop reasoning, aggregation, and question answering in long contexts. RULER allows precise control over context length and task complexity, reduces reliance on parametric knowledge, and enables fine-grained behavioral analysis of language models. The benchmark is designed to reveal failure modes and limitations that are not captured by existing retrieval-based or realistic benchmarks, providing a more rigorous and flexible framework for evaluating and comparing long-context language models.

ac974291d7e3a152067382675524f3e3c2ded11b.title: Consistency Models
ac974291d7e3a152067382675524f3e3c2ded11b.research_question: How can generative models be designed to enable efficient single-step and few-step sample generation, while maintaining high sample quality and supporting zero-shot data editing tasks, without relying on adversarial training?
ac974291d7e3a152067382675524f3e3c2ded11b.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a new family of generative models, termed consistency models, can be constructed to directly map noise to data in a single step by enforcing a self-consistency property along probability flow ODE trajectories. These models are expected to match or surpass the sample quality of existing diffusion model distillation techniques and non-adversarial single-step generative models, while also enabling zero-shot data editing.
ac974291d7e3a152067382675524f3e3c2ded11b.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves developing consistency models that learn a mapping from any point along a probability flow ODE trajectory to its origin, enforcing a self-consistency property such that all points on the same trajectory map to the same initial data point. Two training strategies are proposed: (1) consistency distillation, which distills a pre-trained diffusion model into a consistency model by minimizing the difference between model outputs for adjacent points on ODE trajectories, and (2) consistency training in isolation, which eliminates the need for a pre-trained diffusion model by leveraging unbiased estimators of the score function and training the model directly from data. The models are parameterized using neural networks with boundary conditions ensuring identity mapping at the initial time, and can be implemented with skip connections or other flexible architectures. Sampling is performed by evaluating the consistency model on noise drawn from a Gaussian distribution, enabling single-step generation, with optional multistep procedures for improved sample quality or zero-shot editing.
ac974291d7e3a152067382675524f3e3c2ded11b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image generation benchmarks including CIFAR-10, ImageNet 64x64, LSUN Bedroom 256x256, and LSUN Cat 256x256. The evaluation will compare consistency models to state-of-the-art diffusion model distillation methods (such as progressive distillation and DFNO), GANs, VAEs, and normalizing flows. Metrics will include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS), Precision, and Recall. Both one-step and few-step generation will be assessed, and ablation studies will explore the impact of loss functions, ODE solvers, and training schedules. Zero-shot data editing capabilities (inpainting, colorization, super-resolution, denoising, interpolation, and stroke-guided editing) will be demonstrated without explicit task-specific training.
ac974291d7e3a152067382675524f3e3c2ded11b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces consistency models as a new family of generative models supporting efficient single-step and few-step generation, with a core self-consistency property along ODE trajectories. The approach enables direct mapping from noise to data without adversarial training, supports both distillation from diffusion models and standalone training, and allows zero-shot data editing tasks. The method claims to outperform existing diffusion model distillation techniques in sample quality and efficiency, and to achieve state-of-the-art FID scores for one-step generation on several benchmarks. Additionally, the framework is flexible, architecture-agnostic, and bridges techniques from deep reinforcement learning and contrastive learning.

ac97c8e14033741627dad9f33f0212dbea9c4821.title: Sharp Variance-Dependent Bounds in Reinforcement Learning: Best of Both Worlds in Stochastic and Deterministic Environments
ac97c8e14033741627dad9f33f0212dbea9c4821.research_question: How can reinforcement learning algorithms achieve regret bounds that adapt to the variance structure of Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), providing optimal performance in both stochastic and deterministic environments without prior knowledge of problem-dependent quantities?
ac97c8e14033741627dad9f33f0212dbea9c4821.hypothesis: Algorithms can be developed that achieve variance-dependent regret bounds, which automatically adapt to the underlying variance properties of the environment, yielding minimax optimal regret in both stochastic and deterministic MDPs.
ac97c8e14033741627dad9f33f0212dbea9c4821.proposed_method: The proposed research will introduce two new environment norms—total multi-step conditional variance (VarΣ) and maximum policy-value variance (Var‹)—to finely characterize the variance properties of MDPs. For model-based methods, a variant of the MVP algorithm, called MVP-V, will be developed. This algorithm will incorporate a truncation method to bound total variance and use empirical variances in its bonus calculation, enabling variance-dependent regret bounds. For model-free methods, a novel algorithm named UCB-Advantage-V will be designed, which employs a capped-doubling update schedule for reference values and leverages empirical variance in bonus computations. Both algorithms will utilize advanced martingale concentration inequalities and refined analysis techniques to ensure that the main order term in the regret bound depends only on the variance quantities, thus achieving horizon-free and minimax optimal performance.
ac97c8e14033741627dad9f33f0212dbea9c4821.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on tabular, finite-horizon MDPs, including both time-homogeneous and time-inhomogeneous settings. The evaluation will use standard benchmarks such as deterministic shortest path problems, combinatorial optimization tasks, and environments from OpenAI Gym (e.g., mountain car, lunar lander, Atari games). Baselines will include state-of-the-art model-based and model-free algorithms such as MVP, UCB-Advantage, Q-learning (UCB-B), and others with both variance-independent and suboptimal variance-dependent bounds. Evaluation metrics will focus on cumulative regret, with particular attention to scaling with respect to the number of states (S), actions (A), planning horizon (H), number of episodes (K), and the proposed variance quantities (VarΣ, Var‹). Lower bounds will also be established to demonstrate the tightness and optimality of the proposed algorithms.
ac97c8e14033741627dad9f33f0212dbea9c4821.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces new variance-based environment norms that enable regret bounds to adapt to the variance structure of MDPs. The model-based MVP-V algorithm is the first to achieve minimax optimal regret for both stochastic and deterministic MDPs with variance-dependent guarantees. The model-free UCB-Advantage-V algorithm provides the first variance-dependent regret bound for model-free methods, reducing to minimax optimal bounds in the worst case. The research also establishes matching lower bounds for variance-bounded MDPs, demonstrating the optimality of the proposed approaches. These innovations advance the understanding of problem-dependent regret in reinforcement learning and set new standards for both theoretical guarantees and practical performance.

aca66f06cc3f988ebfc0420b3f969466a6984fef.title: Federated Learning as Variational Inference: A Scalable Expectation Propagation Approach
aca66f06cc3f988ebfc0420b3f969466a6984fef.research_question: How can federated learning be formulated and scaled as a distributed probabilistic inference problem, enabling efficient and accurate global model training across decentralized, heterogeneous, and potentially private client datasets?
aca66f06cc3f988ebfc0420b3f969466a6984fef.hypothesis: Formulating federated learning as a variational inference problem and employing a scalable expectation propagation framework will yield improved convergence speed and accuracy compared to existing optimization-based and posterior-averaging baselines, while maintaining scalability to large models and client populations.
aca66f06cc3f988ebfc0420b3f969466a6984fef.proposed_method: A novel federated learning framework is proposed that casts the global learning objective as variational inference, seeking a global variational posterior that approximates the true posterior over model parameters given partitioned client data. The method operationalizes this via expectation propagation (FedEP), where the global posterior is iteratively refined through probabilistic message-passing between a central server and clients. At each communication round, the server broadcasts the current global posterior approximation to a subset of clients; each client performs local inference to update its local approximation (using techniques such as SG-MCMC, scaled identity covariance, Laplace approximation, or natural gradient variational inference), computes a delta update, and sends this back to the server for aggregation. The framework supports both stateful and stateless clients, incorporates adaptive optimization (e.g., damped updates with Adam-like optimizers), and leverages mean-field Gaussian variational families for scalability in high-dimensional parameter spaces.
aca66f06cc3f988ebfc0420b3f969466a6984fef.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard federated learning benchmarks, including CIFAR-100 (ResNet-18, 11.2M parameters, 500/100 clients), StackOverflow (linear model, 5.0M parameters, 342,477/204,088 clients), and EMNIST-62 (CNN, 1.2M parameters, 3,400/3,400 clients). The evaluation will compare FedEP (both stateful and stateless variants) against strong baselines such as FedAvg (with adaptive optimizers) and federated posterior averaging (FedPA). Metrics will include convergence speed (number of rounds to reach accuracy thresholds), final accuracy, precision, recall, micro-F1, macro-F1, and expected calibration error (ECE). Experimental setups will use TensorFlow Federated for data preprocessing and Jax for model implementation, with multiple random seeds and detailed hyperparameter sweeps. Both toy and large-scale experiments will be conducted to analyze scalability, communication efficiency, and uncertainty quantification.
aca66f06cc3f988ebfc0420b3f969466a6984fef.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a scalable expectation propagation algorithm for federated learning, enabling distributed variational inference over high-dimensional models and large client populations. Key innovations include the adaptation of expectation propagation to the federated setting with probabilistic message-passing, support for both stateful and stateless clients, integration of multiple approximate inference techniques (SG-MCMC, Laplace, NGVI, scaled identity), and the use of adaptive optimization for damped EP updates. The method is empirically validated on contemporary federated learning benchmarks, demonstrating superior convergence speed and accuracy over strong baselines, as well as improved uncertainty quantification and calibration.

acd4d6c8cfc9df063e303cdc6746817f8496c659.title: Advancing Bayesian Optimization via Learning Correlated Latent Space
acd4d6c8cfc9df063e303cdc6746817f8496c659.research_question: How can the inherent gap between latent space and objective function values in latent space Bayesian optimization be minimized to improve optimization performance for structured or discrete data?
acd4d6c8cfc9df063e303cdc6746817f8496c659.hypothesis: Explicitly increasing the correlation between distances in the latent space and differences in objective function values, combined with targeted loss weighting and adaptive trust region strategies, will reduce the gap between latent and input spaces, resulting in more effective and efficient Bayesian optimization for discrete and structured data.
acd4d6c8cfc9df063e303cdc6746817f8496c659.proposed_method: A new Bayesian optimization framework, Correlated latent space Bayesian Optimization (CoBO), is developed to address the misalignment between latent space and objective function values. The method introduces two regularizations: Lipschitz regularization, which penalizes latent space mappings that violate a learned Lipschitz constant to encourage smoothness and high correlation between latent distances and objective value differences, and a latent distance regularization that constrains the average pairwise latent distance to match the expected value under the VAE prior. Additionally, a loss weighting scheme is employed, assigning higher weights to reconstruction and regularization losses for samples with high objective values, focusing learning on promising regions. The approach also incorporates trust region recoordination, dynamically adjusting the search region in latent space based on updated optimal latent vectors, and utilizes a joint training scheme for the VAE encoder/decoder and the surrogate model, followed by sparse Gaussian Process-based surrogate modeling and Thompson sampling for acquisition.
acd4d6c8cfc9df063e303cdc6746817f8496c659.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on nine optimization tasks spanning three benchmark datasets: arithmetic expression fitting, molecule design (Guacamol benchmark with seven tasks), and the DRD3 task from Therapeutics Data Commons. Each task involves optimizing black-box objective functions over discrete or structured input spaces, with varying initialization points and oracle call budgets (e.g., 40k initializations/500 calls for arithmetic, 10k/70k for Guacamol, 100/3k for DRD3). Baselines include LOL-BO, W-LBO, TuRBO-L, and standard latent space BO (LS-BO). Evaluation metrics focus on the mean and standard deviation of achieved objective values over multiple runs, and ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of each proposed component. The surrogate model is implemented using sparse GP with RBF kernel and deep kernel learning, and candidate selection is performed via Thompson sampling within dynamically updated trust regions.
acd4d6c8cfc9df063e303cdc6746817f8496c659.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces explicit regularizations to maximize the correlation between latent space distances and objective value differences, a loss weighting scheme that focuses learning on high-value regions, and a novel trust region recoordination mechanism. These innovations collectively bridge the gap between latent and input spaces in latent space Bayesian optimization, resulting in smoother latent landscapes and improved optimization performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art results across all benchmark tasks, and detailed ablations validate the effectiveness of each component.

ad113d8b6f8f6dace7abd12dc88af520aaaf3fc7.title: LISA: Reasoning Segmentation via Large Language Model
ad113d8b6f8f6dace7abd12dc88af520aaaf3fc7.research_question: How can intelligent perception systems be enabled to perform image segmentation based on complex, implicit, and reasoning-intensive natural language instructions, rather than relying solely on explicit object references or predefined categories?
ad113d8b6f8f6dace7abd12dc88af520aaaf3fc7.hypothesis: Multimodal large language models (LLMs) can be endowed with the capability to generate accurate segmentation masks in response to implicit, reasoning-based textual queries by integrating a novel embedding-as-mask paradigm and end-to-end training, even with limited reasoning-specific data.
ad113d8b6f8f6dace7abd12dc88af520aaaf3fc7.proposed_method: A new framework, termed Language Instructed Segmentation Assistant (LISA), is proposed to enable multimodal LLMs to output segmentation masks in response to complex and implicit text queries. The method expands the LLM's vocabulary with a special <SEG> token, whose last-layer embedding is projected and decoded into a segmentation mask using a vision backbone (e.g., SAM or Mask2Former) and a dedicated decoder. The model is trained end-to-end with both text generation and segmentation mask losses, allowing it to learn to respond to both explicit and implicit instructions. Training leverages a combination of semantic segmentation datasets, referring segmentation datasets, and visual question answering data, with efficient fine-tuning achieved via LoRA to preserve the LLM's original capabilities. The embedding-as-mask paradigm allows the model to directly generate fine-grained segmentation outputs, bypassing the need for intermediate text-based object identification.
ad113d8b6f8f6dace7abd12dc88af520aaaf3fc7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a newly established benchmark, ReasonSeg, which contains over 1,000 image-instruction-mask samples annotated with implicit, reasoning-based queries derived from OpenImages and ScanNetv2. The model will be trained on standard semantic segmentation datasets (ADE20K, COCO-Stuff, LVIS-PACO, PartImageNet, PASCAL-Part), referring segmentation datasets (refCOCO, refCOCO+, refCOCOg, refCLEF), and VQA datasets (LLaVA-Instruct-150k, LLaVA-v1.5-mix665k), with careful exclusion of test images to prevent data leakage. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art referring and open-vocabulary segmentation models (e.g., OVSeg, GRES, X-Decoder, SEEM), as well as two-stage pipelines combining LLMs and segmentation models. Evaluation metrics will include global IoU (gIoU) and cumulative IoU (cIoU), with both quantitative and qualitative analyses. Ablation studies will assess the impact of vision backbone choice, training data composition, fine-tuning strategies, and data augmentation via instruction rephrasing.
ad113d8b6f8f6dace7abd12dc88af520aaaf3fc7.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the reasoning segmentation task, which requires models to segment objects based on implicit, reasoning-rich natural language queries—a capability not addressed by existing segmentation or multimodal LLM systems. The embedding-as-mask paradigm is novel in enabling direct mask generation from LLM embeddings, supporting end-to-end training and flexible integration with different vision backbones. The ReasonSeg benchmark provides the first large-scale evaluation suite for reasoning segmentation. The approach demonstrates robust zero-shot performance on reasoning segmentation without explicit reasoning data and achieves further improvements with minimal fine-tuning, unlocking new segmentation capabilities for multimodal LLMs.

ad113e1fbad65c2c38f71c76460280302375f8c4.title: MoH: Multi-Head Attention as Mixture-of-Head Attention
ad113e1fbad65c2c38f71c76460280302375f8c4.research_question: How can the efficiency and performance of attention mechanisms in Transformer-based models be improved without increasing the number of parameters, particularly by reducing redundant attention head activations across various domains such as vision, diffusion, and language modeling?
ad113e1fbad65c2c38f71c76460280302375f8c4.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that treating attention heads as experts within a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) framework, combined with dynamic routing and weighted summation, will enable each token to select the most relevant attention heads, thereby reducing computational costs and redundancy while maintaining or improving model accuracy.
ad113e1fbad65c2c38f71c76460280302375f8c4.proposed_method: A novel Mixture-of-Head Attention (MoH) architecture will be developed, which conceptualizes attention heads as experts in an MoE-like mechanism. Each token will dynamically select a subset of attention heads via a routing network, activating only the top-K heads per token. The standard summation in multi-head attention will be replaced with a weighted summation, where routing scores determine the contribution of each activated head. A subset of heads will be designated as shared heads, always activated to capture common knowledge, while the remaining heads are dynamically routed. A two-stage routing strategy will be employed to balance the contributions between shared and routed heads, and a load-balance loss will be incorporated to ensure even utilization of heads. The framework will be designed to be compatible with both training from scratch and continue-tuning of pre-trained multi-head attention models.
ad113e1fbad65c2c38f71c76460280302375f8c4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across multiple domains: Vision Transformers (ViT) for image classification using the ImageNet-1K dataset, Diffusion Transformers (DiT) for class-conditional image generation on ImageNet-1K at 256x256 resolution, and large language models (LLMs) including continue-tuning of pre-trained models such as LLaMA3-8B. Baselines will include standard multi-head attention models with identical training settings. Evaluation metrics for vision tasks will include Top-1 accuracy, FID, sFID, Inception Score, Precision, and Recall. Language models will be evaluated on benchmarks such as SciQ, PIQA, WinoGrande, OpenbookQA, LogiQA, TruthfulQA, MMLU, CEVAL, CMMLU, GSM8K, HellaSwag, BoolQ, LAMBADA, NQ, and ARC-C, using 0-shot and few-shot accuracy as appropriate. Ablation studies will assess the impact of shared heads, routing strategies, and the ratio of shared to routed heads. Inference efficiency will be measured by comparing computational time across varying sequence lengths and head activation ratios.
ad113e1fbad65c2c38f71c76460280302375f8c4.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a dynamic attention-head routing mechanism that allows each token to adaptively select the most relevant attention heads, improving inference efficiency and model performance without increasing the number of parameters. The integration of shared heads and a two-stage routing strategy enhances the flexibility and expressiveness of the attention mechanism. The approach is generalizable across vision, diffusion, and language modeling tasks, and uniquely enables continue-tuning of pre-trained multi-head attention models into the MoH framework. Experimental results are expected to demonstrate that MoH achieves competitive or superior performance to standard multi-head attention while utilizing only 50%–90% of the attention heads, establishing a new paradigm for efficient attention-based models.

ad13b213681b6f634bc83a264df246e83dd9a9d9.title: mPLUG-OwI2: Revolutionizing Multi-modal Large Language Model with Modality Collaboration
ad13b213681b6f634bc83a264df246e83dd9a9d9.research_question: How can a multi-modal large language model be designed to effectively leverage collaboration between different modalities, such as vision and language, to improve performance on both text-only and multi-modal tasks, while mitigating modality interference and preserving modality-specific features?
ad13b213681b6f634bc83a264df246e83dd9a9d9.hypothesis: Introducing a modularized network architecture with shared functional modules for modality collaboration and a modality-adaptive module for preserving modality-specific features will enable a multi-modal large language model to achieve superior performance on both text and multi-modal tasks, compared to existing approaches that do not explicitly address modality collaboration and interference.
ad13b213681b6f634bc83a264df246e83dd9a9d9.proposed_method: A novel multi-modal large language model will be developed with a modularized architecture consisting of a vision encoder (e.g., ViT-L/14), a visual abstractor, a text embedding layer, and a language decoder (e.g., LLaMA-2-7B). The model will incorporate shared functional modules to promote modality collaboration and introduce a modality-adaptive module (MAM) that projects visual and language features into a shared semantic space while preserving their unique characteristics. The visual abstractor will use a fixed set of learnable queries to extract high-level semantic features from images, reducing redundancy and computational cost. The modality-adaptive module will decouple the representations of vision and language using separate normalization and projection layers, mitigating granularity mismatches and modality interference. A two-stage training paradigm will be employed: initial pre-training on large-scale image-text pairs to align vision and language representations, followed by joint instruction tuning using both mono-modal and multi-modal instruction data, with the vision encoder and modality-adaptive modules remaining trainable throughout.
ad13b213681b6f634bc83a264df246e83dd9a9d9.experiment_details: Experiments will involve pre-training on approximately 400 million image-text pairs from public datasets such as Conceptual Captions (CC3M/CC12M), COCO, Laion-en, COYO, and DataComp. Instruction tuning will use a diverse set of datasets, including image captioning (TextCaps, COCO), image question answering (VQAv2, OKVQA, OCR-VQA, GQA, A-OKVQA), region-aware QA (RefCOCO, VisualGenome), multi-modal instruction data (LLaVA-instruct-150K), and text-only instruction data (ShareGPT-80K, SlimOrca). Evaluation will be conducted on classic vision-language benchmarks (e.g., Flickr30K, COCO, VQAv2, OKVQA, GQA, VizWizQA, TextVQA, SciQA), recent zero-shot multi-modal benchmarks (MME, MMBench, MM-Vet, SEED-Bench, Q-Bench), and pure-text benchmarks (MMLU, BBH, AGIEval, ARC). Baselines will include state-of-the-art MLLMs such as BLIP-2, MiniGPT-4, LLaVA, Qwen-VL-Chat, and others. Metrics will include CIDEr for image captioning, accuracy for VQA, and benchmark-specific scores for multi-modal and text tasks. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the modality-adaptive module, joint instruction tuning, trainable vision encoder, number of learnable queries, and image resolution.
ad13b213681b6f634bc83a264df246e83dd9a9d9.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first multi-modal large language model architecture that explicitly demonstrates and leverages modality collaboration in both pure-text and multi-modal scenarios. The modality-adaptive module enables effective decoupling and interaction of modality-specific features, overcoming granularity mismatches and modality interference present in prior methods. The two-stage training paradigm, with a trainable vision encoder throughout, further enhances the model's ability to capture both low-level and high-level semantic information. Comprehensive experiments are expected to show state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of vision-language and text benchmarks, as well as improved generalization and robustness compared to existing MLLMs.

ad23e2117ec30e588116583de9e98b5e94f336a8.title: Diffusion-Classifier Synergy: Reward-Aligned Learning via Mutual Boosting Loop for FSCIL
ad23e2117ec30e588116583de9e98b5e94f336a8.research_question: How can continual learning systems effectively learn new classes from limited examples in a sequential manner without forgetting previously acquired knowledge, particularly under data-scarce conditions?
ad23e2117ec30e588116583de9e98b5e94f336a8.hypothesis: A mutual boosting loop between a diffusion-based generative model and a classifier, guided by a dynamic, multi-faceted reward function, will enhance both knowledge retention and new class learning in few-shot class-incremental learning scenarios.
ad23e2117ec30e588116583de9e98b5e94f336a8.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that establishes a mutual boosting loop between a diffusion model and a few-shot class-incremental learning (FSCIL) classifier. The approach leverages Diffusion Alignment as Sampling (DAS) to guide the diffusion model using a dynamic reward function derived from the evolving state of the classifier. The reward system operates at two levels: (1) the feature level, where prototype-anchored maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) and dimension-wise variance matching rewards ensure semantic coherence and intra-class diversity of generated images; and (2) the logits level, where recalibrated confidence and cross-session confusion-aware rewards promote the generation of exploratory samples and enhance inter-class discriminability. Generated images are used to augment the classifier’s training, and improvements in classifier performance yield more informative reward signals for the diffusion model, resulting in a synergistic co-evolutionary process.
ad23e2117ec30e588116583de9e98b5e94f336a8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard FSCIL benchmarks, including miniImageNet, CUB-200, and CIFAR-100. Each dataset will be partitioned into a base session with ample data and several incremental sessions with few-shot (e.g., 5-shot) learning tasks. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art FSCIL methods such as TOPIC, CEC, FACT, TEEN, SAVC, DyCR, ALFSCIL, OrCo, and ADBS. Evaluation metrics will include session-wise and average classification accuracy across all sessions. The experimental setup will use the Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium model as the generative backbone, with images generated at 512x512 resolution and resized as needed. For each class, a limited number of images (e.g., 10-30 per class per session) will be generated, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the contribution of each reward component.
ad23e2117ec30e588116583de9e98b5e94f336a8.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a mutual boosting loop between a diffusion model and a classifier for FSCIL, enabling co-evolution through reward-aligned generation. A multi-faceted reward function is designed, operating at both feature and logits levels, to ensure semantic coherence, intra-class diversity, and robust inter-class discrimination. The approach strategically tailors generated images to the classifier's evolving needs, achieving state-of-the-art performance on FSCIL benchmarks without modifying the baseline classification network. The method demonstrates that aligning generative processes with classifier feedback is critical for overcoming stability-plasticity and data scarcity challenges in continual learning.

ad346966b7863a8bb783e0c41f6d4f98ad971698.title: WILDCHAT-50M: A Deep Dive Into the Role of Synthetic Data in Post-Training
ad346966b7863a8bb783e0c41f6d4f98ad971698.research_question: How does the choice and diversity of synthetic data sources impact the effectiveness of post-training large language models (LLMs), and what are the key factors influencing synthetic data quality for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) in open-source settings?
ad346966b7863a8bb783e0c41f6d4f98ad971698.hypothesis: The quality and diversity of synthetic data, particularly the choice of data-generating model (DGM), significantly influence the downstream performance of LLMs during post-training. Certain DGMs produce higher-quality synthetic data that leads to better generalist chat and instruction-following capabilities, even with smaller datasets.
ad346966b7863a8bb783e0c41f6d4f98ad971698.proposed_method: A large-scale synthetic chat dataset, WILDCHAT-50M, will be constructed by collecting multi-turn conversation responses from over 50 open-weight LLMs, ranging from 0.5B to 104B parameters, using a standardized inference framework (VLLM) across a high-performance GPU cluster. The dataset will be curated to maximize diversity in model architectures, parameter sizes, and context window lengths, with each model contributing over 1 million conversations. A new supervised fine-tuning (SFT) data mixture, RE-WILD, will be created by heuristically blending high-quality synthetic responses with auxiliary datasets targeting complementary skillsets (e.g., math, world knowledge, chat/instruction following). Fine-tuning will be performed on a strong base model (Llama-3.1-8B) using advanced training optimizations (gradient checkpointing, flash attention, FSDP) and standardized hyperparameters (AdamW optimizer, cosine scheduler, bf16 precision). Comparative analyses will be conducted to assess the impact of DGM choice, data scaling, context window length, and DGM blending on downstream model performance and response characteristics.
ad346966b7863a8bb783e0c41f6d4f98ad971698.experiment_details: Experiments will involve fine-tuning Llama-3.1-8B base models on various SFT mixtures, including RE-WILD and established baselines such as Tulu-3 SFT, MagpieAlignSFT, and Ultrachat. Each SFT run will use 250,000 conversation samples (with ablations at 100k and 500k) and be trained on 4xH100 nodes for approximately 5.5 hours. Evaluation will be conducted using a suite of standardized benchmarks (MixEval, AlpacaEval2-LC, MTBench with GPT-4o-mini as judge, OpenLLM Leaderboard, IFEval, MMLUPro, BBH, GPQA, MATH, MUSR) and the Evalchemy framework, ensuring reproducibility and comparability. Baseline models from diverse families (Qwen, Llama, Cohere Command-R, AI21 Jamba) will be compared, with detailed analysis of throughput efficiency, response similarity, and stylistic inheritance. Additional experiments will ablate the effects of dataset scaling, DGM blending, and context window truncation, and will analyze the heritability of stylistic and factual qualities from DGMs to SFT models.
ad346966b7863a8bb783e0c41f6d4f98ad971698.novelty_claims: The proposed dataset, WILDCHAT-50M, will be the largest and most diverse publicly available synthetic chat dataset to date, enabling unprecedented large-scale comparative analysis of synthetic data quality and DGM selection. The RE-WILD SFT mixture is designed to outperform existing SFT baselines with fewer samples by leveraging high-quality synthetic responses and targeted auxiliary data. The methodology provides novel empirical insights into the heritability of stylistic and factual qualities in SFT, the impact of DGM choice on downstream performance, and the (non-)benefit of DGM blending. The work will provide open-source resources, code, and standardized evaluation protocols to support the broader research community in advancing LLM post-training with synthetic data.

ad3daf7e5935b0d7ff576dfff57dd7a14d921d57.title: Two Effects, One Trigger: On the Modality Gap, Object Bias, and Information Imbalance in Contrastive Vision-Language Models
ad3daf7e5935b0d7ff576dfff57dd7a14d921d57.research_question: What are the underlying causes of the modality gap and object bias in contrastive vision-language models, and how do these phenomena affect downstream performance and representation learning? Can these effects be mitigated by addressing information imbalance between image and text modalities?
ad3daf7e5935b0d7ff576dfff57dd7a14d921d57.hypothesis: An information imbalance between image and text modalities is the primary trigger for both the modality gap and object bias in contrastive vision-language models. Reducing this imbalance will decrease both the modality gap and object bias, leading to improved downstream performance.
ad3daf7e5935b0d7ff576dfff57dd7a14d921d57.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical and analytical investigation will be conducted to study the emergence and impact of the modality gap and object bias in contrastive vision-language models. The approach includes: (1) evaluating a large suite of pre-trained contrastive VLMs on standard benchmarks to quantify the modality gap using both existing (L2M) and newly proposed (Relative Modality Gap, RMG) metrics; (2) introducing and applying a novel metric, Matching Object Attribute Distance (MOAD), to formally measure object bias; (3) performing controlled interventions on both synthetic and real datasets to manipulate the degree of information imbalance between modalities, such as varying the number of attributes in captions or omitting parts of captions; (4) analyzing the embedding space to identify which dimensions contribute to the modality gap and how local neighborhood structures differ between modalities; and (5) conducting ablation studies and post-hoc embedding manipulations to assess the feasibility of closing the modality gap and its effect on performance.
ad3daf7e5935b0d7ff576dfff57dd7a14d921d57.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both real-world and synthetic datasets. For real data, 98 pre-trained contrastive VLMs (e.g., CLIP, SigLIP) will be evaluated on MSCOCO, ImageNet, MIT-States, and UT-Zappos using standard protocols (e.g., R@1 for retrieval, top-1 accuracy for classification). Synthetic data will be generated using a fully-controllable Multi-modal Attributes and Digits (MAD) dataset based on Morpho-MNIST, where captions are systematically varied to control information imbalance. Baselines will include models trained on datasets of varying scale and with different caption manipulations. Evaluation metrics will include the proposed RMG and MOAD, as well as downstream task performance. Additional analyses will involve ablation of embedding dimensions, neighborhood similarity via normalized Kendall-τ distance, and fine-tuning experiments with controlled temperature parameters to study the relationship between modality gap and logit entropy.
ad3daf7e5935b0d7ff576dfff57dd7a14d921d57.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new formal metric (MOAD) for quantifying object bias, enabling precise measurement and comparison across models and tasks. It proposes the Relative Modality Gap (RMG) as an improved measure of the modality gap that accounts for intra-modality distances. The research uniquely identifies information imbalance as the common root cause of both the modality gap and object bias, and demonstrates through controlled experiments that mitigating this imbalance directly reduces both effects. Further, the work provides new insights into the structure of the embedding space, showing that only a few dimensions drive the modality gap and that local neighborhoods differ significantly between modalities. The connection between the modality gap and logit entropy is also established, offering a new perspective on the flexibility and limitations of contrastive VLM training.

ad4a0938c48e61b7827869e4ac3baffd0aefab35.title: Emerging Properties in Self-Supervised Vision Transformers
ad4a0938c48e61b7827869e4ac3baffd0aefab35.research_question: Do self-supervised learning strategies confer unique representational properties and performance advantages to Vision Transformers (ViTs) compared to convolutional neural networks (convnets), and what architectural or training components are critical for these effects?
ad4a0938c48e61b7827869e4ac3baffd0aefab35.hypothesis: Self-supervised pretraining of Vision Transformers, particularly with a knowledge distillation framework and specific architectural/training choices, leads to emergent semantic properties in learned features and superior performance on downstream tasks compared to both supervised ViTs and self-supervised convnets.
ad4a0938c48e61b7827869e4ac3baffd0aefab35.proposed_method: A novel self-supervised learning framework, DINO, will be developed for Vision Transformers and convolutional networks. The method employs a student-teacher paradigm where both networks share the same architecture, and the teacher is updated as an exponential moving average (EMA) of the student. Training is performed by minimizing a cross-entropy loss between the outputs of the student and teacher networks on multiple augmented views of the same image, with centering and sharpening applied to the teacher output to avoid collapse. Multi-crop augmentation is used to encourage local-to-global correspondences, and the projection head consists of a 3-layer MLP with normalization. The framework is designed to be flexible, requiring no architecture changes or batch normalization, and can be stabilized without contrastive losses or predictors.
ad4a0938c48e61b7827869e4ac3baffd0aefab35.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale image datasets such as ImageNet and Google Landmarks v2, using both ViT and ResNet architectures. Models will be evaluated on linear classification, k-NN classification, image retrieval (Oxford, Paris), copy detection (INRIA Copydays), video object segmentation (DAVIS-2017), and transfer learning to various downstream tasks (e.g., CIFAR, iNaturalist, Flowers, Cars). Baselines will include supervised models, as well as state-of-the-art self-supervised methods like BYOL, MoCo-v2, SwAV, and Barlow Twins. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy, mean average precision (mAP), region similarity (J), and contour accuracy (F). Ablation studies will systematically vary components such as momentum encoder, multi-crop, loss function, and patch size, and computational requirements will be measured in terms of training time and GPU memory usage.
ad4a0938c48e61b7827869e4ac3baffd0aefab35.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a self-supervised knowledge distillation framework that enables Vision Transformers to learn features with explicit semantic segmentation information and strong k-NN classification performance, properties not observed in supervised ViTs or convnets. The method demonstrates that simple architectural and training modifications, such as momentum teacher updates and multi-crop augmentation, are critical for these emergent properties. DINO achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks, transfers better than supervised pretraining, and is computationally efficient. The framework is robust to small batch sizes and does not require architectural changes or batch normalization, making it broadly applicable.

ad4b365630f1c13d74d78f0f5d8cee87ef356d41.title: Fine-Tuning Language Models with Just Forward Passes
ad4b365630f1c13d74d78f0f5d8cee87ef356d41.research_question: How can large language models be fine-tuned for downstream tasks using methods that significantly reduce memory requirements compared to traditional backpropagation-based approaches, while maintaining competitive performance and enabling optimization of non-differentiable objectives?
ad4b365630f1c13d74d78f0f5d8cee87ef356d41.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a memory-efficient zeroth-order optimization method, which estimates gradients using only forward passes and operates in-place, can fine-tune large language models with a memory footprint comparable to inference, achieving performance on par with standard backpropagation-based fine-tuning and enabling optimization of non-differentiable objectives.
ad4b365630f1c13d74d78f0f5d8cee87ef356d41.proposed_method: A memory-efficient zeroth-order optimizer (MeZO) will be developed, adapting the classical ZO-SGD algorithm to operate in-place and require only the memory needed for inference. The method will use the Simultaneous Perturbation Stochastic Approximation (SPSA) gradient estimator, which perturbs model parameters with Gaussian noise and estimates gradients based on the difference in loss values from two forward passes. By resetting the random number generator with stored seeds, the method avoids storing large perturbation vectors, further reducing memory usage. MeZO will be implemented to support both full-parameter and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (e.g., LoRA, prefix tuning), and will be extended to handle non-differentiable objectives such as accuracy or F1 score. Additionally, MeZO will be compatible with adaptive optimizers like Adam and will include variants inspired by layerwise adaptive optimization.
ad4b365630f1c13d74d78f0f5d8cee87ef356d41.experiment_details: Comprehensive experiments will be conducted on both masked language models (e.g., RoBERTa-large, 350M parameters) and large autoregressive models (e.g., OPT-13B, 30B, 66B parameters) across a range of downstream tasks, including classification, multiple-choice, and generation. The evaluation will compare MeZO against baselines such as zero-shot inference, in-context learning, linear probing, and standard fine-tuning with Adam, using metrics like accuracy and F1 score. Experiments will be performed in both few-shot and many-shot settings, with prompt-based inputs, and will assess memory consumption, wall-clock time, and storage efficiency. Additional studies will explore MeZO's ability to optimize non-differentiable objectives and its scalability to models with up to 66 billion parameters.
ad4b365630f1c13d74d78f0f5d8cee87ef356d41.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a memory-efficient zeroth-order optimizer that enables fine-tuning of extremely large language models using only forward passes, with a memory footprint equivalent to inference. Unlike previous zeroth-order methods, MeZO operates in-place and is compatible with both full-parameter and parameter-efficient tuning methods. The method is capable of optimizing non-differentiable objectives, which are challenging for backpropagation-based approaches. Theoretical analysis suggests that, under certain conditions, the convergence rate of MeZO depends on the local effective rank of the loss landscape rather than the number of parameters, challenging classical lower bounds for zeroth-order optimization. MeZO also offers significant reductions in storage requirements for fine-tuned models and demonstrates strong empirical performance across diverse tasks and model scales.

ad4beeecbdfc7dd238eb55e2b19113f62096d95b.title: Habitat 3.0: A Co-Habitat for Humans, Avatars and Robots
ad4beeecbdfc7dd238eb55e2b19113f62096d95b.research_question: How can a simulation platform be developed to enable comprehensive study and benchmarking of collaborative human-robot tasks in realistic home environments, supporting both high-fidelity humanoid avatars and real human interaction, and what are the effects of such a platform on the development and evaluation of social embodied AI agents?
ad4beeecbdfc7dd238eb55e2b19113f62096d95b.hypothesis: A simulation platform that supports accurate, efficient, and diverse humanoid and robot simulation, along with human-in-the-loop capabilities, will facilitate the development of more effective and generalizable collaborative human-robot policies, leading to improved task efficiency and emergent social behaviors in both automated and real human evaluation settings.
ad4beeecbdfc7dd238eb55e2b19113f62096d95b.proposed_method: A simulation platform will be developed that integrates articulated humanoid avatars and robotic agents within diverse, realistic 3D home environments. Humanoid avatars will be modeled using articulated skeletons with skinned meshes for visual fidelity, leveraging SMPL-X body models to generate diverse shapes and poses. Motion and behavior will be controlled via hierarchical policies combining high-level planners or learned policies with low-level skills for navigation and object manipulation, utilizing precomputed motion clips and pose interpolation for efficiency. The platform will feature a human-in-the-loop infrastructure, enabling real humans to control avatars via mouse/keyboard or VR, and supporting interactive data collection and evaluation. Collaborative tasks such as social navigation (robot follows humanoid at safe distance) and social rearrangement (robot and humanoid jointly move objects) will be implemented, with both scripted and learned policies for agents.
ad4beeecbdfc7dd238eb55e2b19113f62096d95b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two main tasks: social navigation and social rearrangement. The Habitat Synthetic Scenes Dataset (HSSD) will be used, with Boston Dynamics Spot as the robot embodiment, across 37 training, 12 validation, and 10 test scenes. Baselines will include heuristic experts with privileged information, end-to-end RL policies trained with DDPPO, and population-based approaches for multi-agent coordination. Evaluation metrics will include success rates, path efficiency, following rates, collision rates, and relative efficiency compared to solo performance. Automated evaluations will be performed with both learned and scripted humanoid collaborators, while human-in-the-loop studies will involve 30 real human participants interacting with the robot in the rearrangement task, measuring task completion, efficiency, and division of labor.
ad4beeecbdfc7dd238eb55e2b19113f62096d95b.novelty_claims: The proposed platform introduces a fast, high-fidelity simulation of articulated humanoid avatars with diverse appearances and behaviors, optimized for efficient training and evaluation of embodied AI agents. It uniquely combines humanoid and robot simulation with real-time human-in-the-loop interaction, supporting both automated and interactive evaluation in complex, realistic environments. The framework enables the study of emergent collaborative behaviors, generalization to unseen partners and environments, and provides standardized benchmarks for social navigation and rearrangement tasks. The platform's speed, flexibility, and realism are claimed to exceed prior simulators, unlocking new research directions in embodied human-AI collaboration.

ad720ec891fd143090de390a2e800eb8e9e6eb4d.title: Line Graph Neural Networks for Link Prediction
ad720ec891fd143090de390a2e800eb8e9e6eb4d.research_question: How can the link prediction task in graphs be improved by reducing information loss and increasing training efficiency, especially in the context of deep learning-based approaches?
ad720ec891fd143090de390a2e800eb8e9e6eb4d.hypothesis: Transforming the link prediction problem from a graph classification task in the original graph to a node classification task in the corresponding line graph will reduce information loss, require fewer parameters, and improve both predictive performance and training efficiency compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.
ad720ec891fd143090de390a2e800eb8e9e6eb4d.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a novel framework that reformulates the link prediction task as a node classification problem in the line graph of the original network. First, for each candidate link, an h-hop enclosing subgraph centered on the two target nodes is extracted. A node labeling function is applied to assign structural importance labels to all nodes in the subgraph. The subgraph is then transformed into its corresponding line graph, where each node represents an edge in the original subgraph. Node attributes in the line graph are generated by combining the labels and, if available, the original node attributes from the subgraph using an order-invariant transformation. Graph convolutional neural networks (GCNs) are then applied to the line graph to learn node embeddings, which directly represent the features of the candidate link. The existence of the link is predicted by classifying the corresponding node in the line graph using these learned embeddings.
