The approach seamlessly integrates PAC-Bayesian analysis with the standard VAE framework, avoiding the need for additional stochasticity or modification of the VAE objective. The theoretical results are applicable under both bounded and manifold-structured data assumptions, and the derived bounds are explicitly linked to the VAE's empirical optimization objective.

aee09f1215295ad7149706f0995560d88effdabd.title: $C^*$-algebra Net: A New Approach Generalizing Neural Network Parameters to $C^*$-algebra
aee09f1215295ad7149706f0995560d88effdabd.research_question: How can neural network models be generalized by extending their parameters from real or complex numbers to elements of a C*-algebra, and what are the practical and theoretical benefits of such a generalization for tasks such as density estimation and few-shot learning?
aee09f1215295ad7149706f0995560d88effdabd.hypothesis: Generalizing neural network parameters to C*-algebra-valued elements will enable continuous aggregation and interaction among multiple models, leading to improved learning efficiency, adaptability to new tasks, and better performance in data-scarce regimes compared to conventional real-valued or ensemble approaches.
aee09f1215295ad7149706f0995560d88effdabd.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed in which each parameter of a neural network is generalized from a real (or complex) value to a value in a commutative unital C*-algebra, specifically focusing on the algebra of continuous functions on a compact space. The neural network is reformulated so that its weights, biases, and activations are C*-algebra-valued, and the model operates on inputs and outputs that are also elements or functions in this algebra. Learning is performed via a gradient descent method adapted to the Hilbert C*-module structure, with an A-valued (C*-algebra-valued) loss function and gradients computed accordingly. To enable practical computation, parameters are projected onto a finite-dimensional subspace (e.g., via kernel ridge regression using a set of basis functions), and regularization terms are introduced to encourage smoothness and interaction among models indexed by the underlying compact space. The method supports both pointwise and interactive learning across the parameter space, allowing for continuous interpolation and aggregation of multiple models.
aee09f1215295ad7149706f0995560d88effdabd.experiment_details: Experiments are proposed on practical problems such as density estimation using normalizing flows and few-shot learning for classification. For density estimation, toy datasets (e.g., swissroll and circles) are used, with limited training samples to test the framework's ability to learn distributions efficiently. The model is compared against standard real-valued approaches and discrete ensemble methods, using negative log-likelihood as the evaluation metric. For few-shot learning, the miniImageNet dataset is employed, focusing on 5-way 1-shot classification tasks, with the proposed method compared to meta-learning baselines. The C*-algebra-valued parameters are implemented using kernel-based function approximation, and Adam optimizer is used for training. Hyperparameters such as the number of basis functions, regularization strength, and learning rates are varied to assess their impact on performance. Additional experiments are suggested for ensemble learning, time-series/spatial data generation, and learning distributions over parameters.
aee09f1215295ad7149706f0995560d88effdabd.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first general framework for neural networks with C*-algebra-valued parameters, enabling continuous aggregation and interaction among multiple models within a unified mathematical structure. The approach leverages tools from functional analysis, such as regression and integration over function spaces, to enhance learning efficiency and adaptability. The method generalizes and subsumes existing real-valued, complex-valued, and ensemble learning approaches, and provides a principled way to learn and interpolate between multiple models interactively. Theoretical and practical advances are claimed in terms of representational power, learning efficiency in data-scarce regimes, and the potential for new applications in meta-learning, density estimation, and generative modeling.

af1562eb85e7929d46881b8b725df24e32f8fade.title: TFG: Unified Training-Free Guidance for Diffusion Models
af1562eb85e7929d46881b8b725df24e32f8fade.research_question: How can a unified, theoretically grounded, and efficient framework be developed for training-free guidance in diffusion models, enabling conditional generation across diverse tasks and modalities without the need for additional model training?
af1562eb85e7929d46881b8b725df24e32f8fade.hypothesis: A unified algorithmic framework that generalizes and extends existing training-free guidance methods through a comprehensive hyper-parameterized design space, combined with an effective hyper-parameter search strategy, will consistently outperform individual prior methods in conditional generation tasks across vision, audio, and molecular domains.
af1562eb85e7929d46881b8b725df24e32f8fade.proposed_method: A unified framework, termed Training-Free Guidance (TFG), is proposed to encompass and generalize existing training-free guidance algorithms for diffusion models. The method introduces a hyper-parameterized design space, where each point corresponds to a specific guidance strategy, including mean guidance, variance guidance, implicit dynamic (Gaussian smoothing), and recurrence. At each denoising step, TFG computes gradients of a target predictor (e.g., classifier, energy function) with respect to either the predicted clean sample or the noisy sample, modulated by hyper-parameters controlling guidance strength, smoothing, and recurrence. An efficient hyper-parameter search strategy is developed, leveraging structure analysis (e.g., increasing, decreasing, constant schedules) and beam search to identify optimal scalar and vector parameters for any downstream task. The framework is theoretically analyzed to show that existing methods are special cases within this space, and empirical studies are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the unified approach.
af1562eb85e7929d46881b8b725df24e32f8fade.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted across 7 diffusion models and 16 tasks with 40 individual targets, spanning images (CIFAR10, ImageNet, CelebA, Cat), molecules (QM9), and audio (mel spectrograms). Baselines include five prominent training-free guidance methods (DPS, LGD, FreeDoM, MPGD, UGD), each instantiated as a subspace of the TFG framework. Evaluation metrics are task-specific and include label accuracy, Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Kernel Inception Distance (KID), LPIPS, CLIP score, MAE, valid ratio, and DTW/FAD for audio. Hyper-parameters for all methods are selected via grid or beam search, and experiments are run with consistent settings (e.g., T=100, DDIM η=1, fixed recurrence/iteration counts) for fair comparison. Large-scale benchmarking is performed, requiring over 2,000 GPU hours, and ablation studies analyze the effect of hyper-parameters and recurrence.
af1562eb85e7929d46881b8b725df24e32f8fade.novelty_claims: The proposed framework unifies all major existing training-free guidance algorithms as special cases within a single, theoretically grounded design space, enabling systematic comparison and principled extension. A novel hyper-parameter search strategy is introduced, allowing efficient adaptation to new tasks and modalities. The approach is benchmarked more extensively than prior work, covering a broad spectrum of tasks and domains, and demonstrates consistent performance improvements (average 8.5% gain in guidance validity) over existing methods. The work establishes a comprehensive foundation and benchmark for future research in training-free conditional generation with diffusion models.

af1c871282ec122869d03f5420ef5d9143358a91.title: Visual Programming: Compositional visual reasoning without training
af1c871282ec122869d03f5420ef5d9143358a91.research_question: How can complex and compositional visual tasks described in natural language be solved without task-specific training, by leveraging modular neuro-symbolic systems that combine large language models and off-the-shelf vision modules?
af1c871282ec122869d03f5420ef5d9143358a91.hypothesis: A neuro-symbolic system that uses in-context learning with large language models to generate executable modular programs from natural language instructions can flexibly and accurately solve a wide range of compositional visual reasoning tasks without any task-specific training, while providing interpretable rationales.
af1c871282ec122869d03f5420ef5d9143358a91.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a modular neuro-symbolic framework that takes as input visual data (images or image sets) and a natural language instruction. Using in-context learning, a large language model (such as GPT-3) is prompted with a few example instruction-program pairs to generate a high-level, Python-like program for the new instruction. Each line of the generated program invokes a specific module, which may be an off-the-shelf neural vision model (e.g., object detectors, VQA models, segmentation models), a language model, or a symbolic Python subroutine (e.g., image processing, arithmetic, logical operations). The program is executed step-by-step by an interpreter, which maintains a program state and passes intermediate outputs between modules. Each module also provides a visual HTML summary of its computation, enabling the system to generate an interpretable visual rationale for the entire reasoning process. Adding new capabilities is straightforward by implementing and registering new modules.
af1c871282ec122869d03f5420ef5d9143358a91.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four diverse tasks: compositional visual question answering (using the GQA dataset), zero-shot reasoning on image pairs (using NLVRV2), factual knowledge object tagging (custom instructions and images), and language-guided image editing (custom instructions and images). For each task, a small set of in-context examples (instruction-program pairs) will be manually annotated and provided to the language model. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art end-to-end models such as VILT-VQA and VILT-NLVR (finetuned where appropriate). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy for question answering and reasoning tasks, F1 score for object localization and tagging (precision and recall of bounding boxes and class labels), and manual correctness scoring for image editing. The effect of prompt size and prompt engineering strategies (random, curated, majority voting) will be systematically studied. Visual rationales will be used for error analysis and to guide instruction tuning for performance improvement.
af1c871282ec122869d03f5420ef5d9143358a91.novelty_claims: The proposed approach eliminates the need for any task-specific or gradient-based training by leveraging in-context learning with large language models to generate modular programs for visual reasoning. The system is highly flexible, supporting a wide range of tasks by composing diverse modules, and is easily extensible to new capabilities. The method provides strong interpretability through visual rationales that summarize intermediate reasoning steps, enabling error analysis and user-driven instruction tuning. Experiments demonstrate strong zero-shot and few-shot performance on complex compositional tasks that are challenging for end-to-end models, and show that prompt engineering and visual rationales can further improve accuracy.

af3b20fd7690f8305a16f4d0a19583693c14354a.title: Density Ratio-Free Doubly Robust Proxy Causal Learning
af3b20fd7690f8305a16f4d0a19583693c14354a.research_question: How can causal effects be accurately estimated in observational settings where confounders are unobserved but proxy variables for both treatment and outcome are available, particularly in the presence of continuous or high-dimensional treatments and proxies?
af3b20fd7690f8305a16f4d0a19583693c14354a.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a doubly robust estimation framework, which combines outcome bridge and treatment bridge function approaches using kernel-based methods and conditional mean embeddings, will yield consistent and accurate causal effect estimates in proxy causal learning settings, even when one of the bridge functions is misspecified and without requiring explicit density ratio estimation.
af3b20fd7690f8305a16f4d0a19583693c14354a.proposed_method: A novel doubly robust estimation framework is developed for proxy causal learning (PCL), leveraging two kernel-based algorithms: Doubly Robust Kernel Proxy Variable (DRKPV) and Doubly Robust Proxy Maximum Moment Restriction (DRPMMR). The approach integrates outcome bridge function estimation (via Kernel Proxy Variable or Proxy Maximum Moment Restriction) with a density ratio-free treatment bridge function estimator (Kernel Alternative Proxy), both formulated in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHS). Conditional mean embeddings are used to estimate conditional expectations, enabling closed-form solutions and scalability to continuous and high-dimensional treatments and proxies. The doubly robust estimator is constructed such that consistency is achieved if either the outcome or treatment bridge function is correctly specified, and the method avoids the need for indicator functions or kernel smoothing over the treatment variable.
af3b20fd7690f8305a16f4d0a19583693c14354a.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets, including a synthetic low-dimensional confounded data generation process, the high-dimensional dSprite image dataset, the Legalized Abortion and Crime dataset, and the ECLS-K Grade Retention dataset. Baselines for comparison include state-of-the-art PCL methods: Proximal Kernel Doubly Robust (PKDR), Kernel Negative Control (KNC), Kernel Proxy Variable (KPV), Proximal Maximum Moment Restriction (PMMR), and Kernel Alternative Proxy (KAP). Evaluation is based on mean squared error (MSE) of dose-response curve estimation, with results averaged over multiple independent runs and data splits. Hyperparameters such as kernel bandwidth and regularization are selected via median heuristic and cross-validation. Additional robustness experiments are performed by perturbing bridge function coefficients to simulate model misspecification, and the impact on estimation accuracy is assessed.
af3b20fd7690f8305a16f4d0a19583693c14354a.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the first kernel-based doubly robust estimators for PCL that are density ratio-free and applicable to continuous and high-dimensional treatments and proxies. The methodology unifies and extends prior outcome and treatment bridge approaches, providing closed-form, scalable, and provably consistent estimators. The approach achieves double robustness, remaining consistent if either bridge function is correctly specified, and demonstrates superior empirical performance and robustness to model misspecification compared to existing baselines.

af5c7848417882012203ac21399977ebda695a2b.title: RepoCoder: Repository-Level Code Completion Through Iterative Retrieval and Generation
af5c7848417882012203ac21399977ebda695a2b.research_question: How can repository-level information be effectively leveraged to improve automated code completion, enabling accurate code generation across varying granularities and repository structures?
af5c7848417882012203ac21399977ebda695a2b.hypothesis: Incorporating repository-level information through an iterative retrieval and generation framework will significantly improve the performance of code completion systems compared to in-file and single-step retrieval-augmented approaches.
af5c7848417882012203ac21399977ebda695a2b.proposed_method: A novel framework, RepoCoder, will be developed to address repository-level code completion by integrating a similarity-based retriever and a pre-trained code language model within an iterative retrieval-generation pipeline. The process begins by partitioning repository files into code snippets using a sliding window, which are indexed for retrieval. For each code completion request, the unfinished code serves as the initial query to retrieve relevant code snippets from the repository. The retrieved snippets are concatenated with the unfinished code to form a prompt for the language model, which generates a code completion. In subsequent iterations, the generated code from the previous step is incorporated into the retrieval query, allowing the system to refine its context and retrieve more targeted information. This iterative process continues for a fixed number of steps or until convergence, with all model parameters kept frozen and no reliance on static code analysis or heuristic rules.
af5c7848417882012203ac21399977ebda695a2b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a newly constructed benchmark, RepoEval, which consists of high-quality, recent real-world Python repositories from GitHub. RepoEval includes datasets for line completion, API invocation completion, and function body completion, with evaluation at multiple granularities. The experimental setup will compare RepoCoder against strong baselines, including in-file completion and vanilla retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), as well as an oracle retrieval method. Multiple pre-trained language models of varying sizes (e.g., GPT-3.5-Turbo, CODEGEN-6B/2B/350M) will be used. Evaluation metrics will include Exact Match (EM), Edit Similarity (ES), and execution-based pass rates using unit tests. Hyperparameters such as prompt length, retrieval window size, and number of retrieved snippets will be empirically set, and ablation studies will be performed to analyze the impact of retrieval quality and code snippet locations.
af5c7848417882012203ac21399977ebda695a2b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first iterative retrieval-generation framework specifically designed for repository-level code completion, enabling effective use of scattered repository information without static analysis or fine-tuning. RepoCoder is capable of handling various completion granularities and demonstrates significant improvements over in-file and vanilla retrieval-augmented baselines. The introduction of the RepoEval benchmark provides the first comprehensive, multi-granularity evaluation suite for repository-level code completion, leveraging real-world repositories and unit-test-based evaluation. The iterative use of model predictions to enhance retrieval is a key innovation, bridging the gap between retrieval context and intended completion targets.

af66cfb7290366491044d1c7e43ee4c0021fc878.title: Intriguing properties of generative classifiers
af66cfb7290366491044d1c7e43ee4c0021fc878.research_question: How do generative classifiers, particularly those based on text-to-image models, compare to discriminative models and human observers in terms of object recognition, especially under challenging out-of-distribution conditions and perceptual illusions?
af66cfb7290366491044d1c7e43ee4c0021fc878.hypothesis: Generative classifiers based on modern text-to-image models will exhibit human-like shape bias, near-human out-of-distribution accuracy, state-of-the-art alignment with human classification errors, and an ability to understand certain perceptual illusions, surpassing or matching discriminative models in these aspects.
af66cfb7290366491044d1c7e43ee4c0021fc878.proposed_method: The proposed method will adapt state-of-the-art text-to-image generative models (such as diffusion models and autoregressive models) to function as zero-shot classifiers. For each test image, the method will generate reconstructed images conditioned on class-specific text prompts (e.g., 'A bad photo of a <class>') for all possible classes. The class whose reconstruction is closest to the test image, measured by L2 distance or conditional likelihood, will be selected as the predicted label. For diffusion models, the diffusion variational lower bound will be used to approximate the conditional log-likelihood, while for autoregressive models, the exact conditional likelihood will be computed. The approach will be applied to multiple generative models, including Imagen, Stable Diffusion, and Parti, with appropriate preprocessing and prompt engineering for each model.
af66cfb7290366491044d1c7e43ee4c0021fc878.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 17 challenging out-of-distribution datasets from the model-vs-human toolbox, which include both parametric distortions (e.g., noise, blur, rotation) and non-parametric manipulations (e.g., sketches, silhouettes, texture-shape cue conflicts). The performance of generative classifiers will be compared against 52 discriminative models (including ConvNets, vision transformers, and CLIP) and human psychophysical data collected from 90 observers. Evaluation metrics will include shape bias (fraction of shape-based decisions), out-of-distribution accuracy (fraction of correct decisions on OOD data), and error consistency (Cohen’s kappa measuring alignment of error patterns with humans). Models will be evaluated at their native resolutions and with standardized prompts. Additional qualitative experiments will assess the models' understanding of visual illusions by reconstructing ambiguous images based on different prompts.
af66cfb7290366491044d1c7e43ee4c0021fc878.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a comprehensive evaluation framework for generative classifiers as zero-shot object recognizers, leveraging recent advances in text-to-image generative modeling. It claims to be the first to systematically demonstrate that generative classifiers can achieve human-level shape bias, near-human OOD accuracy, and state-of-the-art error consistency with human observers, as well as an ability to understand perceptual illusions. The research also investigates the origins of increased shape bias in generative models, linking it to diffusion-style training and low-frequency emphasis, and provides evidence for the potential of generative pre-training as an alternative to traditional discriminative or contrastive approaches in computer vision.

af68f10ab5078bfc519caae377c90ee6d9c504e9.title: Flow Matching for Generative Modeling
af68f10ab5078bfc519caae377c90ee6d9c504e9.research_question: How can continuous normalizing flows (CNFs) be trained efficiently and scalably for generative modeling, and can alternative probability paths beyond diffusion processes improve generative performance and sampling efficiency?
af68f10ab5078bfc519caae377c90ee6d9c504e9.hypothesis: Training CNFs using a simulation-free flow matching objective based on regressing vector fields of fixed conditional probability paths, including those defined by optimal transport, will enable more scalable, robust, and efficient generative modeling compared to existing diffusion-based approaches.
af68f10ab5078bfc519caae377c90ee6d9c504e9.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed for generative modeling that leverages Flow Matching (FM), a simulation-free approach for training CNFs by regressing neural vector fields to match target vector fields that generate prescribed probability paths between noise and data distributions. The method introduces the Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) objective, which enables unbiased and tractable training by decomposing the intractable marginal vector field into per-sample conditional vector fields and aggregating them. The approach supports a general family of Gaussian conditional probability paths, including both diffusion-based and optimal transport (OT) paths, by parameterizing the mean and standard deviation as differentiable functions of time. The vector field is constructed in closed form for these paths, and the CNF is trained to minimize the CFM loss using stochastic gradient descent, allowing direct control over the probability path and enabling efficient ODE-based sampling.
af68f10ab5078bfc519caae377c90ee6d9c504e9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image generation benchmarks, including CIFAR-10 and ImageNet at various resolutions (32×32, 64×64, 128×128). The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art diffusion-based baselines such as DDPM, Score Matching, and ScoreFlow, using identical U-Net architectures and hyperparameters where possible. Evaluation metrics will include negative log-likelihood (NLL, in bits per dimension), Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for sample quality, and the number of function evaluations (NFE) required for ODE-based sampling. Both unconditional and conditional (super-resolution) generation tasks will be considered, and ablation studies will compare the effects of different probability paths (diffusion vs. OT) on training speed, sample quality, and sampling efficiency. Standard ODE solvers (e.g., dopri5, Euler, midpoint, RK4) will be used to assess numerical stability and computational cost.
af68f10ab5078bfc519caae377c90ee6d9c504e9.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a simulation-free, scalable training paradigm for CNFs via the Flow Matching objective, which generalizes beyond diffusion-based probability paths to include optimal transport and other paths. This enables efficient, unbiased training and fast, reliable sampling using standard ODE solvers. The method claims improved robustness, stability, and generalization compared to score matching and diffusion-based methods, as well as state-of-the-art likelihood and sample quality on large-scale image datasets. The framework also provides a unified perspective on generative modeling with CNFs, allowing direct specification of probability paths and opening new directions for designing generative models with tailored properties.

af705d648b5b16daa3dcc593bc593f2574d76c07.title: Grammar Prompting for Domain-Specific Language Generation with Large Language Models
af705d648b5b16daa3dcc593bc593f2574d76c07.research_question: How can large language models be enabled to effectively generate outputs in highly structured, domain-specific languages, especially in few-shot settings where only limited exemplars are available?
af705d648b5b16daa3dcc593bc593f2574d76c07.hypothesis: Incorporating explicit, specialized grammar representations into the prompting and decoding process will improve the ability of large language models to generate syntactically valid and semantically accurate outputs in domain-specific languages, compared to standard prompting approaches.
af705d648b5b16daa3dcc593bc593f2574d76c07.proposed_method: A novel approach, termed grammar prompting, will be developed to enhance large language model (LLM) performance on domain-specific language (DSL) generation tasks. This method augments each in-context demonstration with a specialized Backus–Naur Form (BNF) grammar that is minimally sufficient for generating the specific output example. At inference, the LLM first predicts a specialized BNF grammar given the input, then generates the output conditioned on this grammar, ensuring that generated outputs conform to domain-specific syntactic constraints. A constrained decoding algorithm based on Earley parsing will be implemented to enforce grammatical correctness during autoregressive generation, correcting invalid outputs by extracting the longest valid prefix and selecting valid continuations. The approach will be evaluated both with and without constrained decoding, and compared to baselines such as standard prompting and derivation tree prompting.
af705d648b5b16daa3dcc593bc593f2574d76c07.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of DSL generation tasks, including semantic parsing (SMCalFlow, Overnight, GeoQuery), AI planning (PDDL), and molecule generation (SMILES). For semantic parsing, few-shot settings will be used with 16–32 in-context examples, and baselines will include standard prompting, constrained decoding with the full grammar, and derivation tree prompting. Evaluation metrics will include program accuracy (exact match of predicted and reference programs) and execution accuracy (equivalence of execution results). For molecule generation, the task will be to generate class-specific molecules from a small set of exemplars, with metrics such as validity, diversity, retrosynthesis score, and class membership. In PDDL planning, the efficiency of plan generation will be measured in terms of search nodes created/expanded and success rate, comparing grammar-prompted LLM guidance to standard LLM prompting and domain-specific baselines. Multiple LLMs (e.g., Codex, GPT-3.5, GPT-4, PaLM2-L) will be evaluated to assess generality.
af705d648b5b16daa3dcc593bc593f2574d76c07.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the use of explicit, specialized BNF grammars as intermediate reasoning steps in LLM prompting for DSL generation, enabling the model to leverage external knowledge and domain-specific constraints. The approach operationalizes grammar-constrained decoding with a practical Earley parser-based algorithm, balancing syntactic validity and API efficiency. This framework is demonstrated across a variety of DSL tasks, showing improved performance over standard prompting and derivation tree-based methods, and enabling compositional generalization and zero-shot adaptation to unseen functions. The method is also shown to enhance molecule generation and AI planning efficiency, illustrating its broad applicability.

af70c7cdf8f2e599782f740dac544ffd48b2f40c.title: Optimizing Adaptive Attacks against Watermarks for Language Models
af70c7cdf8f2e599782f740dac544ffd48b2f40c.research_question: How robust are current watermarking methods for large language models against adaptive attacks, and can adaptively optimized paraphrasing attacks reliably evade watermark detection while preserving text quality, even under constrained attacker resources?
af70c7cdf8f2e599782f740dac544ffd48b2f40c.hypothesis: Adaptively optimized paraphrasing attacks, even when performed by resource-constrained attackers with no access to the provider's watermarking key or watermarked samples, can reliably evade detection from state-of-the-art LLM watermarking methods with negligible impact on text quality.
af70c7cdf8f2e599782f740dac544ffd48b2f40c.proposed_method: A framework will be developed to optimize paraphrasing attacks against known watermarking algorithms by formulating watermark robustness as an objective function. The attacker will use open-weight surrogate language models to generate watermarked text using surrogate keys, and then fine-tune a paraphraser via reinforcement learning (e.g., Direct Preference Optimization) to maximize the expected evasion rate while maintaining high text quality. Preference datasets will be curated by generating paraphrased samples, labeling them as positive (watermark removed, high quality) or negative (watermark retained), and using these for RL-based fine-tuning. The optimization will be performed over multiple random seeds, surrogate models, and watermarking methods, simulating a no-box, offline attacker who knows the watermarking algorithms but not the secret key or watermarked samples.
af70c7cdf8f2e599782f740dac544ffd48b2f40c.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate the effectiveness of adaptive attacks against four state-of-the-art watermarking methods (Exp, Dist-Shift, Binary, Inverse) using open-weight LLMs (e.g., Llama2-7b, Qwen2.5-7b) as both surrogate and paraphrasing models. The provider's models will include Llama2-13b and Llama3.1-70b. Baseline non-adaptive attacks (e.g., DIPPER, translation, synonym replacement, vanilla paraphrasing with Llama2-7b or GPT3.5) will be compared to the proposed adaptive attacks. Evaluation metrics will include evasion rate (fraction of watermarked text undetected after attack) and multiple text quality metrics (LLM-Judge, Mauve, Perplexity). Ablation studies will be conducted over model sizes, watermarking methods, hyperparameters, and false positive rate thresholds. Computational cost and runtime will be measured, with experiments run on NVIDIA A100 GPUs.
af70c7cdf8f2e599782f740dac544ffd48b2f40c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces an adaptive, optimization-based attack framework that tunes paraphrasers specifically against known watermarking algorithms, rather than relying on non-adaptive or handcrafted attacks. The method demonstrates that even resource-constrained attackers can efficiently and reliably evade watermark detection from state-of-the-art methods with minimal impact on text quality. The approach is shown to be Pareto-optimal in the evasion-quality tradeoff, and remains effective even in non-adaptive settings against unseen watermarks. The proposal highlights the necessity of evaluating watermark robustness against adaptive, optimizable attacks and provides a reproducible methodology for future benchmarking.

af81d2ccfc0a88af6ed619080ef6ff67662b9d0f.title: DETRs with Hybrid Matching
af81d2ccfc0a88af6ed619080ef6ff67662b9d0f.research_question: How can the training efficacy and accuracy of DETR-based object detection and vision models be improved without sacrificing their end-to-end inference efficiency and NMS-free design?
af81d2ccfc0a88af6ed619080ef6ff67662b9d0f.hypothesis: Introducing a hybrid matching scheme that combines one-to-one and one-to-many set matching during training will increase the number of positive samples, thereby improving training efficacy and overall model accuracy, while retaining the inference efficiency and end-to-end properties of DETR-based models.
af81d2ccfc0a88af6ed619080ef6ff67662b9d0f.proposed_method: A hybrid matching strategy is proposed for DETR-based models, where two parallel branches are maintained during training: a one-to-one matching branch (using standard Hungarian matching) and an auxiliary one-to-many matching branch. The one-to-many branch assigns multiple queries to each ground truth by repeating the ground truth annotations and performing bipartite matching, thereby increasing the number of positive samples. Both branches share most network parameters, and their losses are combined during training. At inference time, only the original one-to-one matching branch is used, ensuring no additional computational overhead or loss of the end-to-end, NMS-free property. Variants of the hybrid matching scheme include hybrid epoch and hybrid layer strategies, which alternate or split the matching strategies across training epochs or decoder layers, respectively.
af81d2ccfc0a88af6ed619080ef6ff67662b9d0f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a diverse set of vision tasks and DETR-based architectures, including 2D object detection (COCO, LVIS), panoptic segmentation (COCO), 3D object detection (nuScenes with PETRv2), multi-person pose estimation (COCO with PETR), and multi-object tracking (MOT17 with TransTrack). Baseline models will include Deformable-DETR, PETRv2, PETR, and TransTrack, with backbones such as ResNet-50, Swin-T, Swin-L, and VoVNet-99. Evaluation metrics will include mAP, NDS, AP, MOTA, and oLRP, among others. The experimental setup will control for training epochs, number of queries, and backbone architectures to ensure fair comparison. Ablation studies will investigate the impact of the number of auxiliary queries, parameter sharing, and matching scheme variants on accuracy, training time, and memory consumption.
af81d2ccfc0a88af6ed619080ef6ff67662b9d0f.novelty_claims: The hybrid matching scheme introduces a simple yet effective way to increase the number of positive samples during DETR training, addressing the inefficiency of one-to-one matching without compromising inference speed or the end-to-end design. The approach is general and can be applied to a wide range of DETR-based models and vision tasks with minimal tuning. Consistent accuracy improvements are demonstrated across multiple benchmarks and tasks, with no additional inference cost. The method also provides insights into the importance of positive sample optimization in transformer-based detection frameworks.

af8399746bf7025b680d0eb9a84e5df3af8b1c27.title: A Stronger Mixture of Low-Rank Experts for Fine-Tuning Foundation Models
af8399746bf7025b680d0eb9a84e5df3af8b1c27.research_question: How can the fine-tuning of foundation models using low-rank adaptation methods be improved to better approximate full fine-tuning, while addressing both limited representation capacity and gradient sub-optimality in mixture-of-expert (MoE) architectures?
af8399746bf7025b680d0eb9a84e5df3af8b1c27.hypothesis: Integrating Riemannian gradient preconditioners with a gate-value-rescaled gradient updating strategy in MoE-LoRA architectures will enhance both the stability and effectiveness of feature learning, leading to improved performance and convergence speed across diverse downstream tasks.
af8399746bf7025b680d0eb9a84e5df3af8b1c27.proposed_method: A novel training strategy is proposed for mixture-of-expert low-rank adapters (MoE-LoRA) in foundation models, combining Riemannian gradient preconditioning with a gate-based rescaling of expert gradients. Each LoRA expert's gradient is refined using a Riemannian preconditioner, but the method further adjusts for the curvature distortion introduced by the gating mechanism by rescaling gradients according to the respective gate values. An engineering approximation is introduced, replacing each gate value with its square root during forward propagation, and decomposing the forward computation into optimizable and non-optimizable components to ensure correct gradient flow. This approach is implemented for both SGD and AdamW optimizers, and can be integrated with existing MoE-LoRA architectural variants. The method is designed to be lightweight and compatible with standard training pipelines.
af8399746bf7025b680d0eb9a84e5df3af8b1c27.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a variety of downstream tasks, including question answering (ScienceQA, CommonsenseQA, OpenBookQA, SIQA), the GLUE Benchmark (nine tasks), and vision-language tasks (Visual7W, VMCBench) using foundation models such as Llama-3.2-3B, GLM-4-9B, and LLaVA-v1.5-7B. Comparative baselines include independently Riemannian-preconditioned MoE-LoRA, conventional MoE-LoRA, and state-of-the-art MoE-LoRA variants such as MoELoRA and MoLA. Evaluation metrics include accuracy and average performance across tasks, with careful control of experimental variables such as learning rates, number of experts, per-expert rank, and top-k routing. Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of the gate-based rescaling both with and without Riemannian preconditioning, and across various MoE architectures.
af8399746bf7025b680d0eb9a84e5df3af8b1c27.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a theoretically grounded and practically efficient gate-value-rescaled Riemannian preconditioning strategy for MoE-LoRA, addressing both limited representation and gradient sub-optimality. It provides the first solution that explicitly accounts for the curvature distortion induced by gating in MoE architectures, and offers an engineering approximation that is compatible with standard optimizers and existing MoE-LoRA variants. Experimental results demonstrate consistent improvements in both performance and convergence speed across a wide range of tasks and model sizes, establishing the method as a new state-of-the-art for parameter-efficient fine-tuning of foundation models.

af9676f9beaeca214bfbf7f2897828820d48abdc.title: LLaVA-MoLE: Sparse Mixture of LoRA Experts for Mitigating Data Conflicts in Instruction Finetuning MLLMs
af9676f9beaeca214bfbf7f2897828820d48abdc.research_question: How can data conflicts arising from mixing instruction datasets from distinct domains be mitigated during instruction finetuning of multimodal large language models (MLLMs), without significantly increasing computational or memory costs?
af9676f9beaeca214bfbf7f2897828820d48abdc.hypothesis: A sparse mixture of Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) experts, where each token is routed to a single expert based on its embedding, can effectively resolve data conflicts in instruction finetuning of MLLMs, maintaining or improving performance across multiple domains without increasing training or inference costs.
af9676f9beaeca214bfbf7f2897828820d48abdc.proposed_method: A novel architecture is proposed that extends the standard LoRA finetuning paradigm by introducing a sparse mixture of LoRA experts (MoLE) into the MLP layers of the Transformer blocks within an MLLM. For each token, a router conditioned on the token embedding selects the top-1 expert from a set of LoRA experts, activating only that expert for computation and leaving others idle. This approach allows tokens from different domains to be adaptively routed to different experts, expanding the model's capacity to handle diverse data while keeping computational and memory costs similar to plain-LoRA. The method incorporates a load-balancing loss to ensure uniform expert utilization and supports flexible adjustment of dataset sampling ratios during training, enabling targeted performance improvements on specific domains.
af9676f9beaeca214bfbf7f2897828820d48abdc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a base MLLM architecture with a CLIP ViT-L vision encoder and Vicuna-7B LLM, with all vision and language model weights frozen except for LoRA parameters. The pretraining dataset is ShareGPT4V (1.3M samples), and instruction finetuning uses three domains: general multi-task (M3IT, ShareGPT4V Instruct), document-oriented (UReader collection), and biomedicine (PathVQA). Models will be evaluated on TinyLVLM-eHub (42 visual-language benchmarks), UReader (ChartQA, DocVQA), and PathVQA (open/closed-ended). Baselines include plain-LoRA models trained on individual and mixed datasets, as well as dense MoE variants. Evaluation metrics include overall and category scores on each benchmark. Experiments will vary the number of experts, LoRA rank, dataset sampling ratios, and compare sparse vs. dense MoE strategies, with ablation studies on routing and expert utilization.
af9676f9beaeca214bfbf7f2897828820d48abdc.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a sparse mixture of LoRA experts for instruction finetuning MLLMs, enabling token-level expert routing without increasing computational or memory costs compared to plain-LoRA. This approach is claimed to effectively resolve data conflicts when mixing instruction datasets from distinct domains, achieving consistent or superior performance across benchmarks relative to strong baselines, including those trained with more data or higher LoRA rank. The method also demonstrates superior scalability and efficiency over dense MoE approaches, particularly for long-context inputs, and allows for flexible domain-specific performance tuning via dataset sampling adjustments.

af9f365ed86614c800f082bd8eb14be76072ad16.title: Classifier-Free Diffusion Guidance
af9f365ed86614c800f082bd8eb14be76072ad16.research_question: Can guidance in conditional diffusion models be performed without relying on a separately trained classifier, and can such a method effectively trade off sample quality and diversity in generative modeling tasks?
af9f365ed86614c800f082bd8eb14be76072ad16.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a classifier-free guidance method, which combines conditional and unconditional diffusion model score estimates, can achieve a similar or better trade-off between sample fidelity and diversity as classifier-based guidance, without the need for an auxiliary classifier.
af9f365ed86614c800f082bd8eb14be76072ad16.proposed_method: A novel classifier-free guidance approach will be developed for conditional diffusion models. This method involves jointly training a single neural network to perform both conditional and unconditional denoising diffusion modeling by randomly dropping the conditioning information during training with a specified probability. During sampling, the method linearly combines the conditional and unconditional score estimates using a tunable guidance strength parameter, effectively interpolating between the two. The resulting guided score is used in the reverse diffusion process to generate samples, allowing explicit control over the trade-off between sample quality and diversity. The approach eliminates the need for a separate classifier and its associated gradient computations, simplifying the training and sampling pipeline.
af9f365ed86614c800f082bd8eb14be76072ad16.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on class-conditional ImageNet datasets at 64x64 and 128x128 resolutions, using standard architectures and hyperparameters from prior guided diffusion models. The method will be evaluated by varying the guidance strength parameter and the probability of unconditional training, as well as the number of sampling steps. Baselines will include classifier-guided diffusion models (such as ADM-G) and leading generative models like BigGAN-deep and CDM. Evaluation metrics will be Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and Inception Score (IS), computed on 50,000 generated samples per setting. The impact of guidance strength, unconditional training probability, and sampling steps on sample quality and diversity will be systematically analyzed.
af9f365ed86614c800f082bd8eb14be76072ad16.novelty_claims: The proposed classifier-free guidance method introduces a simple and effective alternative to classifier-based guidance for diffusion models, requiring only minor modifications to the training and sampling procedures. It avoids the need for an auxiliary classifier and its associated complications, enabling pure generative models to achieve state-of-the-art trade-offs between sample fidelity and diversity. The approach demonstrates that high-quality, diverse samples can be generated without adversarial classifier gradients, and provides a new perspective on guidance in generative modeling.

afba7beaa7c66cfc72972eb2a569f13c7554bfef.title: FITS: Modeling Time Series with 10k Parameters
afba7beaa7c66cfc72972eb2a569f13c7554bfef.research_question: How can time series analysis tasks such as forecasting and anomaly detection be performed efficiently and accurately with extremely lightweight models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained edge devices?
afba7beaa7c66cfc72972eb2a569f13c7554bfef.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by reinterpreting time series analysis as interpolation in the complex frequency domain, and by leveraging a compact complex-valued neural network architecture, it is possible to achieve state-of-the-art performance on time series forecasting and anomaly detection tasks using models with orders of magnitude fewer parameters than existing approaches.
afba7beaa7c66cfc72972eb2a569f13c7554bfef.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that models time series data by projecting input segments into the complex frequency domain using the real Fast Fourier Transform (rFFT). The method will employ a single complex-valued linear layer to learn both amplitude scaling and phase shifting, enabling interpolation in the frequency domain. A low-pass filter (LPF) will be integrated to retain only essential frequency components, reducing model size while preserving critical information. After frequency domain manipulation, the interpolated representation will be mapped back to the time domain via the inverse rFFT, and reversible instance-wise normalization (RIN) will be used to ensure zero-mean input and output. The model will be supervised in the time domain using standard loss functions, and the interpolation rate will be controlled to match the desired output length for forecasting or reconstruction tasks.
afba7beaa7c66cfc72972eb2a569f13c7554bfef.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on widely-used real-world time series datasets, including Traffic, Electricity, Weather, ETT, and M4 for forecasting, and SMD, PSM, SWaT, MSL, and SMAP for anomaly detection. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as PatchTST, TimesNet, FEDFormer, DLinear, Anomaly Transformer, THOC, OmniAnomaly, and others. Evaluation metrics will include Mean Squared Error (MSE) and symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error (SMAPE) for forecasting, and Precision, Recall, and F1-score for anomaly detection. Hyperparameters such as look-back window size and cutoff frequency will be tuned via grid search, and results will be reported as the mean and standard deviation over multiple runs. Ablation studies will examine the effects of look-back window length and cutoff frequency on performance and model size.
afba7beaa7c66cfc72972eb2a569f13c7554bfef.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a highly compact complex-valued neural network for time series analysis, achieving top-tier performance with as few as 5k–10k parameters—orders of magnitude smaller than existing models. The method pioneers the use of complex frequency domain interpolation for both forecasting and reconstruction, capturing both amplitude and phase information efficiently. Integration of a low-pass filter and weight-sharing across channels further enhances compactness and efficiency. The framework is specifically designed for edge deployment, enabling real-time inference and training on devices with limited computational resources, while maintaining or surpassing the accuracy of much larger models.

afdf04289e384e9750cc9a3dc901c5606738804f.title: Unsupervised 3D Perception with 2D Vision-Language Distillation for Autonomous Driving
afdf04289e384e9750cc9a3dc901c5606738804f.research_question: How can unsupervised 3D perception systems for autonomous driving be developed to detect, track, and semantically label both static and moving objects in open-set scenarios, without relying on 3D human annotations?
afdf04289e384e9750cc9a3dc901c5606738804f.hypothesis: Incorporating vision-language knowledge distillation from pre-trained 2D image-text models into a multi-modal unsupervised 3D auto-labeling pipeline will enable high-quality open-vocabulary 3D object detection and tracking for both static and moving objects, surpassing prior class-agnostic and motion-only approaches.
afdf04289e384e9750cc9a3dc901c5606738804f.proposed_method: A multi-modal unsupervised auto-labeling pipeline will be developed that leverages LiDAR point cloud sequences, camera images, and pre-trained 2D vision-language models. The method will extract motion cues from LiDAR data using scene flow estimation and semantic features from images via a vision-language encoder. These features will be projected onto 3D points using sensor calibration, and a spatio-temporal clustering algorithm will generate initial bounding box proposals, filtering out background categories using text-based embeddings. Amodal 3D bounding boxes and tracklets will be created by aggregating object observations over time, with non-maximum suppression applied to refine labels. The resulting auto labels (amodal boxes, tracklets, and per-point semantic features) will be used to supervise a 3D object detector, which is further enhanced by a feature distillation branch that aligns 3D point features with the vision-language embedding space. At inference, the detector will output class-agnostic boxes and per-point features, enabling open-vocabulary semantic assignment via text queries mapped to the shared embedding space.
afdf04289e384e9750cc9a3dc901c5606738804f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Waymo Open Dataset, utilizing multi-modal sensor data (LiDAR and camera) in diverse driving scenarios. The detection backbone will be based on PointPillars, with Huber loss for box regression and Focal Loss for objectness classification. Baselines will include prior class-agnostic auto-labeling methods, geometric clustering, and variants using only motion or vision-language features. Evaluation will cover both class-agnostic and class-aware (open-vocabulary) 3D detection for moving-only and all-motion-state objects, using metrics such as 3D Average Precision (3DAP) at various IoU thresholds, as well as tracking metrics (MOTA, MOTP). The impact of feature distillation and semantic assignment via text queries will be ablated, and qualitative results will be presented for open-vocabulary queries at inference.
afdf04289e384e9750cc9a3dc901c5606738804f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable unsupervised open-vocabulary 3D perception in autonomous driving, capable of detecting and semantically labeling both static and moving objects without 3D human labels. It introduces a multi-modal auto-labeling pipeline that combines motion cues and vision-language semantics, and distills 2D vision-language knowledge into 3D detectors, allowing flexible text-based querying at inference. The method claims significant improvements over prior unsupervised 3D perception approaches, particularly in handling static objects and providing semantic labels, and demonstrates state-of-the-art results on challenging benchmarks.

afe0998d191f3ea8490c7df100a3ffc5dcc62c5e.title: LiveCodeBench: Holistic and Contamination Free Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code
afe0998d191f3ea8490c7df100a3ffc5dcc62c5e.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) for code be evaluated in a comprehensive and contamination-free manner, capturing a broad spectrum of code-related capabilities beyond standard code generation, and enabling fair, up-to-date comparisons across diverse models and training cutoffs?
afe0998d191f3ea8490c7df100a3ffc5dcc62c5e.hypothesis: A continuously updated, contamination-free benchmark that evaluates LLMs across multiple code-related tasks and problem difficulties will provide a more accurate, holistic, and fair assessment of model capabilities than existing static benchmarks, and will reveal differences in model performance and overfitting not captured by current evaluation methods.
afe0998d191f3ea8490c7df100a3ffc5dcc62c5e.proposed_method: A new benchmark, LiveCodeBench, will be developed to evaluate LLMs for code using problems collected in real-time from competitive programming platforms (LeetCode, AtCoder, CodeForces), each tagged with release dates to enable time-segmented, contamination-free evaluation. The benchmark will encompass four distinct scenarios: code generation from natural language, self-repair of buggy code using error feedback, code execution (predicting output for given code and input), and test output prediction (generating expected outputs for given inputs and problem statements). Problems will be curated for quality, clarity, and balanced difficulty, with extensive test cases per problem and automated or platform-sourced ground truth. The framework will support extensibility for new evaluation scenarios and will include tools for dataset curation, prompt generation, and model evaluation.
afe0998d191f3ea8490c7df100a3ffc5dcc62c5e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of 511 problems collected from May 2023 to May 2024 across the three platforms, with subsets filtered by problem release date to match model training cutoffs and avoid contamination. A total of 52 models, including 18 base and 34 instruction-tuned models, both open and closed access, will be evaluated. Evaluation metrics will include Pass@1 for code generation and self-repair (fraction of problems solved correctly on the first attempt), execution-based correctness for code execution, and equivalence-based grading for test output prediction. Baselines will include existing benchmarks such as HumanEval and MBPP, and comparisons will be made across model types, sizes, and instruction-tuning status. Experiments will also analyze performance by problem difficulty and across the four evaluation scenarios.
afe0998d191f3ea8490c7df100a3ffc5dcc62c5e.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces live, time-segmented evaluation to eliminate contamination from training data, enabling fair comparison of models released at different times. It expands evaluation beyond code generation to include self-repair, code execution, and test output prediction, providing a holistic view of code-related capabilities. The benchmark ensures high-quality, balanced, and diverse problems with robust test cases, and supports extensibility for future scenarios. It enables the detection of overfitting to existing benchmarks and reveals nuanced differences in model performance not captured by prior work.

afe42e22585597fe9b490646d8b8446cc1c82c28.title: BlackJAX: Composable Bayesian inference in JAX
afe42e22585597fe9b490646d8b8446cc1c82c28.research_question: How can a composable, modular, and high-performance library for Bayesian inference be designed to facilitate the development, experimentation, and deployment of advanced sampling and variational inference algorithms across modern computational architectures?
afe42e22585597fe9b490646d8b8446cc1c82c28.hypothesis: A functionally pure, compositional library built on JAX can enable efficient, flexible, and extensible Bayesian inference by providing low-level algorithmic components that can be combined to create both standard and novel inference methods, while maintaining compatibility with probabilistic programming languages and supporting execution on CPUs, GPUs, and TPUs.
afe42e22585597fe9b490646d8b8446cc1c82c28.proposed_method: A new library will be developed that implements a wide range of Bayesian inference algorithms, including Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), sequential Monte Carlo (SMC), stochastic gradient MCMC, and variational inference (VI). The library will adopt a functional programming paradigm, ensuring that all algorithms are Markovian and side-effect free, which simplifies parallelization and reproducibility. Core algorithmic components—such as Metropolis-Hastings accept/reject steps, Hamiltonian and Langevin dynamics, stochastic gradient utilities, resampling, and tempering mechanisms—will be exposed as modular, composable functions. Both high-level and low-level APIs will be provided, allowing users to instantiate standard algorithms or construct custom inference procedures by composing basic building blocks. The library will be written in Python and leverage JAX for automatic differentiation and compilation to accelerate computations on diverse hardware.
afe42e22585597fe9b490646d8b8446cc1c82c28.experiment_details: The proposed library will be evaluated by implementing state-of-the-art sampling algorithms, such as vanilla HMC, NUTS, and generalized HMC, along with adaptation schemes for hyperparameters. Experiments will include benchmarking against existing libraries in terms of speed, flexibility, and extensibility, using a variety of probabilistic models and datasets representative of real-world Bayesian inference tasks. Integration with popular probabilistic programming languages will be tested, and performance will be assessed on CPUs, GPUs, and TPUs. Evaluation metrics will include sampling efficiency, convergence diagnostics, and ease of algorithmic customization. Additional experiments will demonstrate the construction and effectiveness of novel algorithms created via the compositional API.
afe42e22585597fe9b490646d8b8446cc1c82c28.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first Python library specifically designed for both users and developers of Bayesian inference methods, emphasizing functional purity and composability. By exposing low-level algorithmic components, the library enables the creation of custom and hybrid inference algorithms not possible with existing monolithic solutions. The use of JAX ensures high performance and seamless hardware acceleration, while the modular design supports integration with probabilistic programming languages and modern scientific computing ecosystems. Planned features such as an inference database and enhanced diagnostics further advance transparency, reproducibility, and educational utility in Bayesian computation.

afea234e64326aa5ceebf296304e00babcce764d.title: Computational-Statistical Gaps in Gaussian Single-Index Models
afea234e64326aa5ceebf296304e00babcce764d.research_question: What are the fundamental computational and statistical limits for recovering the hidden direction in high-dimensional Gaussian single-index models, and under what conditions do computational-to-statistical gaps emerge for efficient algorithms in these models?
afea234e64326aa5ceebf296304e00babcce764d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that for a broad class of Gaussian single-index models, there exists a sharp computational-to-statistical gap in sample complexity for recovering the hidden direction, with efficient algorithms requiring significantly more samples than information-theoretic limits, and that this gap can be precisely characterized by a generative exponent associated with the model.
afea234e64326aa5ceebf296304e00babcce764d.proposed_method: A rigorous theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the sample complexity required for recovering the hidden direction in Gaussian single-index models. The approach will characterize the model using a generative exponent, derived from the Hermite polynomial expansion of the joint distribution of the projected input and the label. Lower bounds on sample complexity for computationally efficient algorithms will be established within both the Statistical Query (SQ) and Low-Degree Polynomial (LDP) frameworks, leveraging mutual information decompositions and moment-based arguments. Matching upper bounds will be demonstrated by constructing and analyzing a polynomial-time partial-trace estimator, which exploits the structure of the generative exponent to efficiently recover the hidden direction when sufficient samples are available. Additionally, the existence of smooth and Lipschitz deterministic target functions with arbitrarily large generative exponents will be constructed to show the generality of the results.
afea234e64326aa5ceebf296304e00babcce764d.experiment_details: Theoretical experiments will be conducted by analyzing the recovery problem under various instantiations of the joint distribution P, including additive and multiplicative noise, mixtures, and deterministic link functions. The sample complexity of brute-force search (information-theoretic optimum) will be compared to that of efficient algorithms constrained to the SQ and LDP frameworks. Evaluation will be based on the number of samples required to recover the hidden direction up to a specified accuracy, with complexity measured as a function of the input dimension d and the generative exponent k*. Theoretical baselines will include existing results for monotonic and quadratic link functions, as well as known computational lower bounds for related inference problems. The tightness of lower and upper bounds will be validated by constructing explicit examples and proving the existence of models with prescribed generative exponents.
afea234e64326aa5ceebf296304e00babcce764d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a precise characterization of computational-to-statistical gaps in Gaussian single-index models via the generative exponent, extending beyond prior results based on the information exponent. It establishes tight lower and upper bounds on sample complexity for efficient algorithms in both the SQ and LDP frameworks, and demonstrates that these bounds can differ polynomially from information-theoretic limits. The construction of smooth target functions with arbitrarily large generative exponents further shows the generality and sharpness of the proposed framework. The partial-trace estimator provides a new, efficient recovery algorithm that matches the lower bounds, thus fully characterizing the computational landscape of these models.

afea54c7f17f4fac0f71bebed6bc782ed69d8bd0.title: Depth Anything: Unleashing the Power of Large-Scale Unlabeled Data
afea54c7f17f4fac0f71bebed6bc782ed69d8bd0.research_question: How can monocular depth estimation models be improved to robustly generalize across diverse, unseen scenes and conditions using large-scale unlabeled data?
afea54c7f17f4fac0f71bebed6bc782ed69d8bd0.hypothesis: Scaling up monocular depth estimation training with massive, diverse unlabeled images—annotated via self-training—and equipping the model with challenging optimization targets and semantic priors will significantly enhance generalization and zero-shot performance compared to models trained solely on labeled data.
afea54c7f17f4fac0f71bebed6bc782ed69d8bd0.proposed_method: A foundation model for monocular depth estimation will be developed by leveraging both labeled and a vast amount of unlabeled images. First, a teacher model is trained on 1.5 million labeled images from six public datasets using an affine-invariant loss for multi-dataset joint training. This teacher is then used to generate pseudo-depth labels for 62 million unlabeled images collected from eight large-scale public datasets. A student model is trained on the union of labeled and pseudo-labeled images, but with strong perturbations (color jitter, Gaussian blur, and CutMix) applied to the unlabeled data to create a more challenging optimization target, compelling the model to learn robust, invariant representations. Additionally, a feature alignment loss is introduced to transfer rich semantic priors from a frozen DINOv2 encoder to the depth model, enhancing both depth estimation and high-level semantic understanding. The overall loss combines depth regression and semantic alignment, with a tolerance margin to avoid over-constraining the feature space.
afea54c7f17f4fac0f71bebed6bc782ed69d8bd0.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate zero-shot depth estimation on six public datasets (KITTI, NYUv2, Sintel, DDAD, ETH3D, DIODE) and on randomly captured photos, comparing against strong baselines such as MiDaS v3.1 and ZoeDepth. Fine-tuning experiments will be conducted on NYUv2 and KITTI for metric depth estimation, and the model will also be transferred to semantic segmentation tasks on Cityscapes and ADE20K. Evaluation metrics include Absolute Relative Error (AbsRel), delta accuracy thresholds (δ1, δ2, δ3), RMSE, and mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) for segmentation. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of data scaling, perturbation strategies, and semantic alignment. The experimental setup uses DINOv2-based ViT encoders (S, B, L), DPT decoders, and standard data augmentation, with careful control of batch sizes, learning rates, and training schedules.
afea54c7f17f4fac0f71bebed6bc782ed69d8bd0.novelty_claims: The proposal highlights the value of scaling up with massive, diverse unlabeled monocular images for monocular depth estimation, which is both practical and previously underexplored. It introduces a simple yet effective data engine for automatic pseudo-labeling at scale, a novel use of strong perturbations to maximize the benefit of unlabeled data, and a semantic feature alignment loss leveraging DINOv2 to endow the model with high-level scene understanding. The approach claims to achieve superior zero-shot generalization, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines, and to produce a multi-task encoder effective for both depth estimation and semantic segmentation.

afeeb8f5018eebb1a1d334b94dbbfc48d167efef.title: iTransformer: Inverted Transformers Are Effective for Time Series Forecasting
afeeb8f5018eebb1a1d334b94dbbfc48d167efef.research_question: How can the Transformer architecture be adapted to improve the effectiveness, efficiency, and generalization ability of models for multivariate time series forecasting, particularly in scenarios with large lookback windows and diverse variates?
afeeb8f5018eebb1a1d334b94dbbfc48d167efef.hypothesis: Applying the attention and feed-forward network components of the Transformer architecture along inverted dimensions—specifically, using attention over variate tokens and feed-forward networks over temporal dimensions—will yield more effective, interpretable, and generalizable representations for multivariate time series forecasting than conventional Transformer architectures.
afeeb8f5018eebb1a1d334b94dbbfc48d167efef.proposed_method: A novel framework, termed iTransformer, is proposed in which the standard Transformer architecture is repurposed without modifying its native components. Instead of embedding multiple variates at a single timestamp as a temporal token, each entire time series (i.e., each variate) is independently embedded as a variate token. Self-attention is then applied across these variate tokens to capture multivariate correlations, while a shared feed-forward network is used along the temporal dimension of each variate token to learn nonlinear series representations. Layer normalization is applied to the series representation of each variate to reduce discrepancies caused by inconsistent measurements. The model uses an encoder-only Transformer structure, omitting position embeddings, and leverages efficient attention mechanisms as plugins to handle large numbers of variates. Prediction of future time series is accomplished using a linear projection layer applied to the learned representations.
afeeb8f5018eebb1a1d334b94dbbfc48d167efef.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on seven real-world multivariate time series datasets, including ECL, ETT (4 subsets), Exchange, Traffic, Weather, Solar-Energy, and PEMS (4 subsets), with additional results on a large-scale Market dataset. The proposed method is compared against ten strong baselines, including Transformer-based (Autoformer, FEDformer, Crossformer, PatchTST, Stationary), linear-based (DLinear, TiDE, RLinear), and TCN-based (SCINet, TimesNet) models. Evaluation metrics include Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE), with experiments covering various prediction lengths and fixed lookback windows. Additional analyses include ablation studies, generalization to unseen variates, scalability with lookback window size, and efficiency assessments using partial variate sampling during training.
afeeb8f5018eebb1a1d334b94dbbfc48d167efef.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces an inverted application of Transformer components, applying attention to variate tokens and feed-forward networks to temporal dimensions, which is claimed to be a fundamental architectural shift without modifying native Transformer modules. This inversion enables more interpretable multivariate correlations, improved generalization to unseen variates, and better scalability with lookback window size. The method demonstrates state-of-the-art performance across diverse real-world benchmarks and is shown to enhance a variety of Transformer variants. Additionally, a novel efficient training strategy for high-dimensional multivariate series is proposed, leveraging the model's flexibility to reduce memory footprint without sacrificing accuracy.

b000d6865db824af1563708fb7a545ddd65c6b3a.title: Plug-and-Play Diffusion Features for Text-Driven Image-to-Image Translation
b000d6865db824af1563708fb7a545ddd65c6b3a.research_question: How can controllable, high-fidelity text-driven image-to-image translation be achieved using pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models, such that the structure and layout of a guidance image are preserved while allowing significant semantic and appearance changes as specified by a target text prompt?
b000d6865db824af1563708fb7a545ddd65c6b3a.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that fine-grained control over generated image structure and semantic layout can be achieved by manipulating and injecting internal spatial features and self-attention maps from a guidance image into the generation process of a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model, without requiring any additional training or fine-tuning.
b000d6865db824af1563708fb7a545ddd65c6b3a.proposed_method: A novel plug-and-play framework will be developed that leverages the internal spatial features and self-attention maps of a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model (e.g., Stable Diffusion) for text-guided image-to-image translation. The method will begin by inverting a real or generated guidance image into the model's latent space using DDIM inversion. During the denoising process, spatial features and self-attention matrices will be extracted from intermediate decoder layers of the U-Net architecture at each timestep. These features and attention maps will then be injected into the generation process of a new image, guided by a target text prompt, at selected layers and timesteps. The injection strategy will be carefully controlled to balance structure preservation and appearance transformation, with ablations on which layers and timesteps to inject features and attention. The approach will require no additional training or fine-tuning of the diffusion model.
b000d6865db824af1563708fb7a545ddd65c6b3a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two newly curated benchmarks: Wild-TI2I, consisting of 148 diverse text-image pairs (including both real and generated guidance images), and ImageNet-R-TI2I, derived from ImageNet-R renditions with manually aligned source-target text prompts. The method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines, including SDEdit (at multiple noise levels), Prompt-to-Prompt (P2P), DiffuseIT, VQGAN+CLIP, Text2LIVE, FlexIT, and DiffusionCLIP. Evaluation metrics will include CLIP cosine similarity for text-image alignment and DINO-ViT self-similarity distance for structure preservation. Both quantitative and qualitative analyses will be performed, including ablations on the injection of features and attention, and tests on a range of guidance image domains (real, generated, artistic, and textureless).
b000d6865db824af1563708fb7a545ddd65c6b3a.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a zero-shot, training-free framework for text-driven image-to-image translation that leverages internal representations of pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models. It provides new empirical insights into the spatial feature encoding of such models and demonstrates that direct manipulation of these features and self-attention maps enables fine-grained control over structure and semantic layout. The approach achieves a superior balance between structure preservation and semantic transformation compared to existing baselines, and is applicable to a wide variety of guidance image types without the need for domain-specific training or prompt alignment.

b02281dbd4b39da338311c7e3cc496c46e2b288a.title: Deep Neural Networks pruning via the Structured Perspective Regularization
b02281dbd4b39da338311c7e3cc496c46e2b288a.research_question: How can structured pruning of deep neural networks be performed in a principled and efficient manner to significantly reduce model size and computational cost while maintaining or improving predictive accuracy across various architectures and datasets?
b02281dbd4b39da338311c7e3cc496c46e2b288a.hypothesis: A regularization method derived from the perspective reformulation of a mixed-integer programming model can induce structured sparsity in neural networks, enabling effective pruning of entire entities (such as filters or channels) during training, resulting in compressed models that retain or improve accuracy compared to state-of-the-art pruning techniques.
b02281dbd4b39da338311c7e3cc496c46e2b288a.proposed_method: A new structured pruning approach will be developed by formulating the pruning problem as a mixed-integer programming (MIP) model, where the objective combines the standard loss, an ℓ2 regularization term, and a structured ℓ0 norm over prunable entities (e.g., filters, channels). The perspective reformulation technique will be applied to strengthen the continuous relaxation of the MIP, leading to a regularization term called Structured Perspective Regularization (SPR). This term will be incorporated into the training objective, promoting the simultaneous pruning of all weights within specified entities. The method will include a projection step to eliminate indicator variables, yielding a closed-form regularizer that can be efficiently optimized with standard training algorithms. Additional refinements will be made by adapting regularization strength per layer and accounting for the size of each prunable entity, followed by a fine-tuning phase after pruning.
b02281dbd4b39da338311c7e3cc496c46e2b288a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification benchmarks including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet, using popular architectures such as ResNet-18, ResNet-20, ResNet-50, ResNet-56, and Vgg-16. The method will be implemented in PyTorch with SGD optimization and cross-entropy loss, with hyperparameters tuned via grid search. Training will involve initial training with the SPR term, pruning based on a threshold for entity sparsity, and fine-tuning the pruned network. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art structured pruning methods such as SSS, EPFS, L2PF, PFFEC, HRANK, PFC, CHIP, DNR, OTO, and HFP. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 and top-5 accuracy, percentage of parameters pruned, and computational efficiency. Experiments will be performed on both moderate (single GPU) and large-scale (multi-GPU) setups, with ablation studies to assess the impact of key hyperparameters and design choices.
b02281dbd4b39da338311c7e3cc496c46e2b288a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a mathematically principled regularization term for structured pruning, derived from the perspective reformulation of an exact MIP model, rather than relying on heuristic importance scores. The method enables flexible, architecture-agnostic pruning of arbitrary structures within neural networks and allows for efficient optimization using standard training routines. By projecting away indicator variables, the approach yields a closed-form regularizer that directly promotes structured sparsity. Experimental results are expected to demonstrate competitive or superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art structured pruning methods, with the additional benefit of theoretical justification and adaptability to various architectures and pruning granularities.

b02d8250bf26701f0e300bb6d6c3cff7558b2754.title: ScaleCrafter: Tuning-free Higher-Resolution Visual Generation with Diffusion Models
b02d8250bf26701f0e300bb6d6c3cff7558b2754.research_question: How can pre-trained diffusion models be adapted to generate high-resolution images with arbitrary aspect ratios, without additional training or fine-tuning, while avoiding common issues such as object repetition and structural artifacts?
b02d8250bf26701f0e300bb6d6c3cff7558b2754.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the primary limitation in high-resolution image generation with pre-trained diffusion models arises from the restricted convolutional receptive field rather than the number of attention tokens, and that dynamically adjusting the convolutional perception field during inference can enable high-quality, tuning-free image synthesis at resolutions far exceeding the original training size.
b02d8250bf26701f0e300bb6d6c3cff7558b2754.proposed_method: A novel, training-free framework is proposed that enables pre-trained diffusion models to generate images at much higher resolutions and arbitrary aspect ratios. The core technique is a dynamic re-dilation strategy, which adjusts the dilation factor of convolutional kernels during inference to expand the receptive field proportionally to the target resolution.
