This includes both integer and fractional dilation via feature map stretching and bilinear interpolation, as well as layer- and timestep-aware dilation schedules. To address periodic downsampling artifacts at extreme resolutions, a convolution dispersion technique is introduced, enlarging the kernel size through a linear transformation and structure- and pixel-level calibration to maintain fidelity. Additionally, a noise-damped classifier-free guidance mechanism is incorporated, linearly combining outputs from the original and modified models to preserve denoising ability while improving structural correctness. The approach requires no additional training or optimization and operates entirely at inference time.
b02d8250bf26701f0e300bb6d6c3cff7558b2754.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple versions of Stable Diffusion (SD 1.5, SD 2.1, SDXL 1.0) and a text-to-video model (LVDM), evaluating image generation at resolutions up to 16× the training size (e.g., 4096×4096 from a 512×512 model). The Laion-5B dataset will be used for text prompts, with 30,000 samples generated at 1024×1024 and 10,000 samples at higher resolutions. Baselines will include direct inference, attention scaling factor adaptation, and super-resolution models such as SD-SR. Evaluation metrics will include Frechet Inception Distance (FID), Kernel Inception Distance (KID), and for video, Frechet Video Distance (FVD) and Kernel Video Distance (KVD). User studies will assess texture definition at extreme resolutions. Ablation studies will isolate the effects of re-dilation progression, convolution dispersion, and noise-damped guidance.
b02d8250bf26701f0e300bb6d6c3cff7558b2754.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a tuning-free, inference-only method for high-resolution image generation with pre-trained diffusion models, fundamentally addressing the object repetition issue by expanding the convolutional receptive field. The dynamic re-dilation and convolution dispersion techniques are novel in their ability to adapt pre-trained kernels to arbitrary resolutions without retraining. The noise-damped classifier-free guidance further enhances denoising and structure fidelity in ultra-high-resolution synthesis. This framework enables direct use of low-resolution-trained diffusion models for high-resolution and arbitrary aspect ratio generation, representing a significant advance over prior attention-based or window-fusion methods.

b04df44b550caa4bb2c247bbf3e7d32907c549b9.title: Gaussian in the Wild: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Unconstrained Image Collections
b04df44b550caa4bb2c247bbf3e7d32907c549b9.research_question: How can novel view synthesis from unconstrained, in-the-wild image collections be improved to achieve high-quality, flexible scene reconstruction and faster rendering, particularly in the presence of photometric variations and transient occluders?
b04df44b550caa4bb2c247bbf3e7d32907c549b9.hypothesis: Separating intrinsic and dynamic appearance features for each 3D Gaussian point, combined with adaptive feature sampling and visibility-aware loss, enables more accurate and efficient scene reconstruction from unconstrained image collections compared to global appearance modeling approaches.
b04df44b550caa4bb2c247bbf3e7d32907c549b9.proposed_method: A new framework is introduced that represents a scene using explicit 3D Gaussian points, where each point is endowed with independent intrinsic and dynamic appearance features. Intrinsic appearance is modeled as a learnable attribute per point, while dynamic appearance is adaptively sampled from multiple feature maps extracted from reference images using a Unet with a ResNet backbone. Each Gaussian point learns its own sampling coordinates for these feature maps, enabling it to focus on local, high-frequency details and environmental variations. The intrinsic and dynamic features are fused via a dedicated MLP-based fusion network, and the resulting appearance features are decoded into color values for rendering. A 2D visibility map, also predicted by a Unet, is used to modulate the loss during training, reducing the impact of transient occluders and improving robustness.
b04df44b550caa4bb2c247bbf3e7d32907c549b9.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on three scenes from the PhotoTourism dataset: Brandenburg Gate, Sacre Coeur, and Trevi Fountain, which feature varying appearances and transient objects. The proposed method is quantitatively evaluated using PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS metrics, and is compared against baselines including 3DGS, NeRF-W, Ha-NeRF, and CR-NeRF. Rendering speed is measured in frames per second (FPS) on an RTX 3090 GPU at 800x800 resolution, with both feature extraction and rendering time included. The model is trained for 70,000 steps using the Adam optimizer, with images downsampled by a factor of two, and adaptive control of 3D Gaussians is performed as in 3DGS.
b04df44b550caa4bb2c247bbf3e7d32907c549b9.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel per-point appearance modeling approach that separates intrinsic and dynamic features, enabling fine-grained control over local appearance variations. Adaptive sampling from multiple feature maps allows each Gaussian point to capture detailed, high-frequency environmental effects. The use of a visibility map for loss weighting effectively mitigates the influence of transient occluders. The framework achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction quality and surpasses previous NeRF-based methods in rendering speed by over 1000×, while maintaining high fidelity in novel view synthesis from unconstrained image collections.

b059d640377740dbd65daa866412f03916765c70.title: Do Bayesian Neural Networks Need To Be Fully Stochastic?
b059d640377740dbd65daa866412f03916765c70.research_question: Is it necessary for Bayesian neural networks to treat all parameters stochastically to achieve expressive and practically useful predictive distributions, or can partially stochastic networks suffice across various inference modalities and datasets?
b059d640377740dbd65daa866412f03916765c70.hypothesis: Partially stochastic Bayesian neural networks, in which only a subset of parameters are treated stochastically, can match or outperform fully stochastic Bayesian neural networks in terms of predictive expressivity and practical performance, while offering reduced computational and memory costs.
b059d640377740dbd65daa866412f03916765c70.proposed_method: The proposed research will systematically investigate the expressivity and practical performance of partially stochastic Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) compared to fully stochastic BNNs. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to establish whether partially stochastic architectures can serve as universal conditional distribution approximators, leveraging results such as the Noise Outsourcing Lemma and the Universal Approximation Theorem. Multiple neural network architectures will be constructed with varying numbers and locations of stochastic parameters, including configurations with stochasticity limited to the first hidden layer, output layer, or other subsets. Both joint and two-stage training procedures will be explored, where deterministic parameters are learned via maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation and stochastic parameters are inferred using Bayesian techniques such as Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC), Laplace approximation, SWAG, and mean-field variational inference (MFVI). The methodology will also include the development and evaluation of inference pipelines tailored for partially stochastic networks.
b059d640377740dbd65daa866412f03916765c70.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across four inference modalities: HMC, Laplace approximation, SWAG, and MFVI. Empirical evaluations will span eight datasets, including UCI regression datasets (e.g., Yacht, Boston, Energy), and image classification benchmarks such as CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, including corrupted versions (CIFAR-10-C). Baseline comparisons will include fully stochastic BNNs, deterministic networks, and partially stochastic networks with varying stochastic subsets (e.g., input layer, output layer, first hidden layer, and combinations thereof). Evaluation metrics will include negative log-likelihood, accuracy, and calibration measures, with additional focus on out-of-distribution (OOD) robustness using gap splits and corrupted datasets. Experimental setups will control for posterior approximation fidelity and computational resources, and will report results over multiple random seeds and train-test splits to ensure statistical robustness.
b059d640377740dbd65daa866412f03916765c70.novelty_claims: The proposal claims that partially stochastic Bayesian neural networks can serve as universal conditional distribution approximators, challenging the prevailing assumption that full stochasticity is required for expressivity. It further asserts that, across a range of inference methods and datasets, partially stochastic networks can match or even outperform fully stochastic networks in predictive performance, despite using fewer stochastic parameters and incurring lower computational and memory costs. The research also highlights the lack of practical benefit from full stochasticity under current Bayesian inference methods, and provides both theoretical and empirical evidence to support a shift toward partially stochastic model constructions in Bayesian deep learning.

b066bab42d963daf4d8831695d2ef7787f2473c9.title: Principled Probabilistic Imaging using Diffusion Models as Plug-and-Play Priors
b066bab42d963daf4d8831695d2ef7787f2473c9.research_question: How can expressive diffusion models be leveraged as principled priors for accurate Bayesian posterior sampling in general linear and nonlinear imaging inverse problems, avoiding the common approximations that lead to inaccurate sample distributions?
b066bab42d963daf4d8831695d2ef7787f2473c9.hypothesis: Integrating diffusion models as plug-and-play priors within a rigorous Markov chain Monte Carlo framework, specifically using a split Gibbs sampler and the EDM formulation, will enable accurate posterior sampling for a wide range of imaging inverse problems, including highly ill-posed and nonlinear cases, outperforming existing DM-based and optimization-based methods in reconstruction accuracy and posterior estimation.
b066bab42d963daf4d8831695d2ef7787f2473c9.proposed_method: A new Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm, Plug-and-Play Diffusion Models (PnP-DM), is developed to perform posterior sampling for imaging inverse problems by alternating between a likelihood step and a prior step within the split Gibbs sampler framework. The likelihood step enforces data consistency, sampling from the conditional distribution given the current image estimate and measurements, using either closed-form Gaussian sampling for linear problems or Langevin dynamics for general nonlinear cases. The prior step is formulated as a Gaussian denoising posterior sampling problem, which is solved by leveraging the EDM (Elucidated Diffusion Models) framework to unify and rigorously apply a variety of state-of-the-art diffusion models as image priors. An annealing schedule for the coupling parameter is introduced to facilitate efficient mixing and avoid local minima. The method is modular, allowing seamless integration of different pretrained diffusion models without additional customization or retraining.
b066bab42d963daf4d8831695d2ef7787f2473c9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six imaging inverse problems: three linear (Gaussian deblurring, motion deblurring, and super-resolution) and three nonlinear (coded diffraction pattern reconstruction, Fourier phase retrieval, and real-world black hole imaging). The FFHQ dataset will be used for synthetic problems, and real interferometric data from the M87 black hole will be used for the real-world test. Baselines will include optimization-based methods (PnP-ADMM, DPIR), conditional DM-based methods (DDRM, DPS), and SGS-based methods (PnP-SGS, DPnP). Evaluation metrics will include PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS for quantitative assessment, and posterior mean and standard deviation images will be compared to ground truth where available. Each method will use the same pretrained diffusion model checkpoints, converted to the EDM formulation as needed, and 20 random samples will be drawn per test case for statistical evaluation.
b066bab42d963daf4d8831695d2ef7787f2473c9.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled Bayesian framework for posterior sampling in imaging inverse problems using diffusion models as plug-and-play priors, avoiding the heuristic or approximate updates common in prior DM-based methods. By connecting the prior step to the EDM formulation, the method provides a unified interface for rigorously incorporating a wide range of state-of-the-art diffusion models without additional customization. The approach is demonstrated on both linear and nonlinear problems, including challenging real-world scenarios, and is supported by theoretical analysis establishing convergence guarantees in terms of average Fisher information. Empirical results show improved accuracy in both reconstruction and posterior estimation compared to existing methods.

b085968c4362fb286ad6c5ef71a5db9630da0498.title: KVQuant: Towards 10 Million Context Length LLM Inference with KV Cache Quantization
b085968c4362fb286ad6c5ef71a5db9630da0498.research_question: How can memory and computational efficiency be improved for large language model (LLM) inference with extremely long context windows, specifically by reducing the memory footprint of Key-Value (KV) cache activations without significant degradation in model accuracy?
b085968c4362fb286ad6c5ef71a5db9630da0498.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a combination of novel quantization techniques—including per-channel key quantization, pre-RoPE key quantization, sensitivity-weighted non-uniform quantization, and per-vector dense-and-sparse quantization—can enable ultra-low precision (sub-4-bit) KV cache quantization for LLMs, achieving substantial memory savings and faster inference while maintaining minimal accuracy loss.
b085968c4362fb286ad6c5ef71a5db9630da0498.proposed_method: The proposed method develops a comprehensive quantization framework for KV cache activations in LLMs, integrating several innovations. First, per-channel key quantization is applied to better align quantization with the distribution of key activations, sharing scaling factors and zero-points along the channel dimension. Second, pre-RoPE key quantization is introduced, quantizing keys before applying rotary positional embeddings (RoPE) and then performing RoPE post-dequantization via a fused kernel, thereby mitigating the distributional mixing caused by RoPE. Third, a sensitivity-weighted non-uniform quantization (NUQ) scheme is derived offline using calibration data, leveraging diagonal Fisher information to optimize quantization signposts for each layer. Fourth, per-vector dense-and-sparse quantization is used to isolate and separately store outlier values at the granularity of channels or tokens, allowing the main quantization range to focus on the bulk of the data. Custom CUDA kernels are implemented to efficiently compress, dequantize, and process quantized activations during inference, supporting both dense and sparse representations.
b085968c4362fb286ad6c5ef71a5db9630da0498.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of LLMs, including LLaMA (7B/13B/30B/65B), Llama-2 (7B/13B/70B), Llama-3 (8B/70B), and Mistral-7B. Evaluation will use standard language modeling benchmarks such as Wikitext-2 and C4, as well as long-context benchmarks like LongBench and RULER. Baseline comparisons will include uniform and non-uniform quantization (intX, nfX), and state-of-the-art methods such as Atom and FlexGen, as well as KIVI for passkey retrieval. Metrics will include perplexity, passkey retrieval accuracy, and task-specific scores on LongBench and RULER. The experimental setup will involve both offline calibration (using 16 calibration samples from Wikitext-2) and online quantization for certain components, with memory usage, latency (benchmarked on A6000 and A100 GPUs), and maximum context length supported as key evaluation criteria.
b085968c4362fb286ad6c5ef71a5db9630da0498.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces several novel contributions: (1) per-channel key quantization prior to RoPE to better match activation distributions and reduce quantization error; (2) efficient pre-RoPE quantization with custom fused kernels for on-the-fly RoPE application; (3) offline-calibrated, sensitivity-weighted non-uniform quantization tailored for KV cache activations; (4) per-vector dense-and-sparse quantization for outlier handling at fine granularity; and (5) a complete, efficient CUDA kernel implementation for real-time quantized inference. These innovations collectively enable accurate 3-bit quantization of KV cache activations with less than 0.1 perplexity degradation, 4.8x memory savings, and support for up to 10 million token context lengths on multi-GPU systems, outperforming existing baselines in both accuracy and efficiency.

b096dc25eeacb00ca35293131230e6234bac9a59.title: Understanding Warmup-Stable-Decay Learning Rates: A River Valley Loss Landscape Perspective
b096dc25eeacb00ca35293131230e6234bac9a59.research_question: How can learning rate schedules be designed to enable flexible, efficient, and high-performing pretraining of large language models without requiring a pre-specified compute budget, and what theoretical principles underlie the effectiveness of such schedules in complex loss landscapes?
b096dc25eeacb00ca35293131230e6234bac9a59.hypothesis: The pretraining loss landscape of language models exhibits a 'river valley' structure, where progress along the primary direction (the 'river') is best achieved with a sustained high learning rate, while oscillations in orthogonal 'mountain' directions can be effectively minimized by a rapid learning rate decay. Therefore, a learning rate schedule that combines a long stable high-rate phase with a sharp decay phase will yield superior optimization and model performance across varying compute budgets.
b096dc25eeacb00ca35293131230e6234bac9a59.proposed_method: A novel learning rate schedule, Warmup-Stable-Decay (WSD), is proposed, which consists of an initial warmup, followed by a long stable phase with a constant high learning rate, and finally a rapid decay phase. This approach allows indefinite training during the stable phase, enabling branching at any point for compute budget flexibility. The method is theoretically motivated by modeling the loss landscape as a 'river valley', where the stable phase enables fast progress along the river direction despite high oscillations, and the decay phase reduces oscillations to reveal true optimization progress. An improved variant, WSD-S, is also introduced for continual learning, which reuses previous checkpoints’ decay phases and resumes training from decayed checkpoints without rolling back, thereby maintaining only a single main branch and reducing complexity.
b096dc25eeacb00ca35293131230e6234bac9a59.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large language models with parameter sizes ranging from 0.1B to 1.2B. Pretraining will be performed on real-world datasets such as OpenWebText, as well as synthetic bi-gram datasets to validate theoretical predictions. The proposed WSD and WSD-S schedules will be compared against standard cosine and cyclic-cosine learning rate schedules. Evaluation metrics will include training and validation loss curves, final model performance, and the ability to efficiently generate strong checkpoints for multiple compute budgets in a single run. Ablation studies will examine the sensitivity of performance to the duration and timing of the decay phase.
b096dc25eeacb00ca35293131230e6234bac9a59.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretically grounded learning rate schedule that decouples training progress from a fixed compute budget, enabling flexible checkpointing and continual pretraining. The river valley loss landscape framework provides new insights into the dynamics of stochastic optimization in language model pretraining. The WSD-S variant further simplifies continual learning by eliminating the need for checkpoint rollbacks. Empirical and theoretical analyses demonstrate that the proposed schedules outperform or match optimally tuned baselines across a range of model sizes and compute budgets, while providing a principled explanation for observed non-traditional loss curves.

b0a120b9304b362d0183b779f27f0e837d90926c.title: Closing the Computational-Query Depth Gap in Parallel Stochastic Convex Optimization
b0a120b9304b362d0183b779f27f0e837d90926c.research_question: Can the gap between computational depth and query depth in parallel stochastic convex optimization be closed, achieving optimal parallel performance for minimizing Lipschitz, convex functions with access to a stochastic subgradient oracle?
b0a120b9304b362d0183b779f27f0e837d90926c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a new parallel algorithm can be developed that matches the best-known query depth and query complexity for parallel stochastic convex optimization, while simultaneously reducing the computational depth to match the query depth up to logarithmic factors, even for small accuracy regimes.
b0a120b9304b362d0183b779f27f0e837d90926c.proposed_method: A novel parallel algorithm will be designed for stochastic convex optimization by leveraging a ball acceleration framework that operates on the Gaussian convolution of the target convex function. The approach involves reducing the original optimization problem to a sequence of regularized, ball-constrained subproblems, each formulated as minimizing a Gaussian-convolved version of the function over a small Euclidean ball. The key technical innovation is the development and exploitation of new stability properties of the Hessian of the Gaussian convolution, enabling the reduction of these subproblems to stochastic unconstrained quadratic minimization problems. Efficient parallel algorithms will be constructed for solving these quadratic problems, circumventing the need for strong concentration bounds on Hessian approximations by using asymmetric stochastic estimators. Fast matrix multiplication techniques will be integrated to further reduce computational complexity and depth, especially when the matrix multiplication exponent approaches 2.
b0a120b9304b362d0183b779f27f0e837d90926c.experiment_details: The proposed algorithm will be evaluated on the standard stochastic convex optimization problem with access to a stochastic subgradient oracle, considering both the classic Lipschitz convex optimization setting and more general settings with bounded stochastic gradients. Experiments will compare the new method against state-of-the-art baselines, including subgradient descent, cutting plane methods, and recent parallel algorithms such as those by [CJJ+23] and [BJL+19]. Evaluation metrics will include query depth (number of parallel rounds), query complexity (total oracle queries), computational depth (sequential computation rounds), and computational complexity (total computational work). Theoretical and empirical performance will be measured across varying problem dimensions and accuracy parameters, with particular focus on the intermediate regime where nontrivial parallel speedups are possible.
b0a120b9304b362d0183b779f27f0e837d90926c.novelty_claims: The proposed research closes a previously open gap between computational depth and query depth for parallel stochastic convex optimization, achieving for the first time a parallel algorithm whose computational depth matches the best-known query depth up to logarithmic factors. The method introduces new structural results on the stability of the Hessian of Gaussian convolutions of convex functions, enabling efficient reduction to quadratic subproblems solvable in parallel. The approach circumvents the need for concentration bounds on asymmetric Hessian approximations and leverages fast matrix multiplication to achieve nearly-linear work under favorable conditions. Additional contributions include new tools for boosting expected optimality bounds to high probability and efficient parallel handling of hard constraints, with potential broader impact in optimization and learning theory.

b0d791cd8e9a87f37258832beaa321037048da26.title: Improved Techniques for Training Consistency Models
b0d791cd8e9a87f37258832beaa321037048da26.research_question: How can the training of consistency models for generative modeling be improved to achieve higher sample quality and efficiency, without relying on distillation from pre-trained diffusion models or learned perceptual metrics such as LPIPS?
b0d791cd8e9a87f37258832beaa321037048da26.hypothesis: Directly training consistency models from data, using improved objective functions, noise schedules, and training curricula, can surpass the sample quality of models trained via distillation from diffusion models and eliminate the need for learned perceptual metrics, while maintaining or improving efficiency.
b0d791cd8e9a87f37258832beaa321037048da26.proposed_method: The proposed method develops an improved consistency training (iCT) framework for generative models that eliminates the need for distillation from pre-trained diffusion models and reliance on learned metrics like LPIPS. Key components include: (1) removing the Exponential Moving Average (EMA) from the teacher network to ensure theoretical consistency and improved learning dynamics; (2) replacing LPIPS with the Pseudo-Huber loss, a robust, twice-differentiable metric that bridges the gap between L1 and L2 losses and is less sensitive to outliers; (3) introducing a lognormal noise schedule for sampling noise levels, which emphasizes lower noise levels and better aligns with the inductive biases of the model; (4) implementing an exponentially increasing curriculum for the number of discretization steps (N), doubling N after a set number of training iterations to balance bias and variance; and (5) optimizing hyperparameters such as weighting functions, noise embedding sensitivity, and dropout rates to further improve training stability and sample quality. The approach is designed to allow consistency models to learn directly from data, facilitating both one-step and multi-step sample generation.
b0d791cd8e9a87f37258832beaa321037048da26.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image generation benchmarks, including CIFAR-10 and ImageNet 64x64. The ScoreSDE architecture will be used for CIFAR-10, and the ADM architecture for ImageNet, with both standard and deeper variants evaluated. Models will be trained for 400,000 iterations, using the improved training techniques described above. Evaluation metrics will include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Inception Score (IS), and Precision/Recall. Baselines for comparison will include previous consistency training (CT) and consistency distillation (CD) methods, as well as state-of-the-art diffusion models, GANs, and other fast sampling approaches. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of each proposed modification, and both one-step and two-step sampling procedures will be evaluated.
b0d791cd8e9a87f37258832beaa321037048da26.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces several innovations: (1) a theoretically justified removal of EMA from the teacher network in consistency training, leading to improved convergence and sample quality; (2) the first use of the Pseudo-Huber loss as a robust, non-learned metric for consistency models, enabling high sample quality without reliance on learned perceptual features; (3) a lognormal noise schedule that more effectively balances training across noise levels; (4) an exponentially increasing curriculum for discretization steps that empirically optimizes the bias-variance tradeoff; and (5) a comprehensive set of hyperparameter and architectural improvements tailored for direct consistency training. Collectively, these advances enable consistency models to achieve or surpass the sample quality of models trained via distillation, rivaling state-of-the-art diffusion models and GANs in both one-step and multi-step generation settings.

b0f9feb42ddcda481bd0c950202410a64285342b.title: RoME: Domain-Robust Mixture-of-Experts for MILP Solution Prediction across Domains
b0f9feb42ddcda481bd0c950202410a64285342b.research_question: How can a learning-based framework be developed to robustly predict high-quality solutions for Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) problems that generalize effectively across diverse problem domains and unseen distributions?
b0f9feb42ddcda481bd0c950202410a64285342b.hypothesis: A mixture-of-experts architecture, combined with a two-level distributionally robust optimization training strategy, will enable a single model to generalize across multiple MILP domains and achieve strong performance on both seen and unseen problem distributions, including zero-shot settings.
b0f9feb42ddcda481bd0c950202410a64285342b.proposed_method: A domain-robust mixture-of-experts (MoE) framework will be constructed for MILP solution prediction. The method will represent each MILP instance as a bipartite graph, which is processed by a shared graph neural network (GNN) encoder to extract structural embeddings. Multiple expert networks will be defined, each specializing in different structural regularities, and a dynamic gating mechanism will route instances to experts based on learned task embeddings. A multi-head decoder will further aggregate expert outputs for final solution prediction. The model will be trained using a composite loss that includes binary cross-entropy, expert diversity regularization to prevent mode collapse, and a fuzzy membership consistency loss that enforces output stability under isotropic perturbations of the task embedding. At the domain level, a group-wise distributionally robust optimization (DRO) objective will be used to minimize the worst-case expected loss across domains, with domain weights updated via exponential gradient ascent to focus learning on harder or underrepresented domains.
b0f9feb42ddcda481bd0c950202410a64285342b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five MILP problem families: Independent Set (IS), Set Covering (SC), Item Placement (IP), Combinatorial Auctions (CA), and Workload Appointment (WA), covering a range of combinatorial structures and constraints. The model will be trained on three domains (IS, IP, SC) and evaluated on all five, with WA and CA serving as zero-shot test domains. Baselines will include Predict-and-Search (PS), Contrastive Predict-and-Search (ConPS), and conventional solvers (Gurobi, SCIP), with all methods evaluated using the best objective value within a 1,000-second time limit and absolute primal gap relative to the best-known solution. Further evaluation will be performed on curated subsets of the MIPLIB benchmark to assess zero-shot generalization to real-world, out-of-distribution MILP instances. Ablation studies and interpretability analyses will be conducted to assess the contributions of architectural and training components, such as DRO, MoE, embedding perturbation, and expert diversity.
b0f9feb42ddcda481bd0c950202410a64285342b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified mixture-of-experts architecture for MILP solution prediction that dynamically routes instances to specialized experts based on learned task embeddings. It incorporates a two-level distributionally robust optimization strategy, including both inter-domain group DRO and intra-domain embedding perturbation, to enhance robustness and generalization across diverse MILP domains. The framework enables a single model to achieve strong cross-domain and zero-shot performance, outperforming existing learning-based and conventional solvers, and provides interpretability into expert specialization and task embedding structure.

b0fe8ecda139c94bd1fc94ab2723605512dd446e.title: Wider or Deeper? Scaling LLM Inference-Time Compute with Adaptive Branching Tree Search
b0fe8ecda139c94bd1fc94ab2723605512dd446e.research_question: How can inference-time computation for large language models (LLMs) be more effectively scaled to improve performance on complex reasoning and coding tasks, particularly by balancing exploration (diversity of outputs) and exploitation (solution refinement) using external feedback?
b0fe8ecda139c94bd1fc94ab2723605512dd446e.hypothesis: Adaptive search strategies that dynamically balance exploration and exploitation, guided by external feedback, will outperform fixed-width or purely exploratory/exploitative approaches in inference-time scaling for LLMs on complex tasks.
b0fe8ecda139c94bd1fc94ab2723605512dd446e.proposed_method: A novel inference-time framework, Adaptive Branching Monte Carlo Tree Search (AB-MCTS), is proposed to generalize repeated sampling by integrating principled multi-turn exploration and exploitation. At each node in the search tree, AB-MCTS adaptively decides whether to 'go wider' by generating new candidate responses or 'go deeper' by refining existing ones, leveraging external feedback signals such as test case results or validation scores. The method formalizes this decision process via Bayesian posterior updates, enabling Thompson sampling to balance exploration and exploitation at each step. Two variants are developed: AB-MCTS-M, which uses a node-specific mixed Bayesian model to share statistical strength across subtrees, and AB-MCTS-A, which aggregates child nodes under a CONT node and uses independent Bayesian models for each action. Both variants allow for unbounded branching, enabling the search to dynamically allocate computational resources based on the evolving search landscape.
b0fe8ecda139c94bd1fc94ab2723605512dd446e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four diverse benchmarks requiring complex problem-solving: LiveCodeBench, CodeContest, ARC-AGI, and MLE-Bench. These benchmarks encompass competitive programming, abstract reasoning, and machine learning engineering tasks, with LLMs generating Python code as solutions. External feedback, such as test case results or validation scores, will be used to guide the search. The proposed AB-MCTS methods will be compared against three baselines: repeated sampling (best-of-n), sequential refinement, and standard MCTS (with fixed branching factor). Evaluation metrics include Pass@1 and Pass@2 success rates, as well as average rank across tasks. Experiments will use frontier LLMs such as GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3, with a fixed generation budget (e.g., 128 API calls), and temperatures set according to best practices for each model. Performance will be analyzed across varying computational budgets and search tree shapes (depth vs. width).
b0fe8ecda139c94bd1fc94ab2723605512dd446e.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces unbounded, adaptive branching into MCTS for LLM inference, allowing principled, feedback-driven decisions between generating new candidates and refining existing solutions. This approach unifies the strengths of repeated sampling (exploration) and sequential refinement (exploitation), overcoming the limitations of fixed-width or purely exploratory/exploitative methods. The Bayesian decision process and Thompson sampling enable efficient balancing of search strategies, and the method is demonstrated to outperform both repeated sampling and standard MCTS on challenging real-world benchmarks. The framework is extensible and can be combined with other inference-time scaling techniques, providing a robust mechanism for leveraging the diverse output space of LLMs in multi-turn solution refinement.

b115c1e1e9e51f8ad7d47b745bc04e29a654b84d.title: Faithful Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
b115c1e1e9e51f8ad7d47b745bc04e29a654b84d.research_question: How can reasoning by large language models be made more faithful and interpretable, ensuring that the generated reasoning chains accurately reflect the process by which final answers are derived across a variety of complex reasoning tasks?
b115c1e1e9e51f8ad7d47b745bc04e29a654b84d.hypothesis: Decomposing complex reasoning into a two-stage process—Translation (natural language to interleaved natural and symbolic reasoning chains) and Problem Solving (deterministic execution of symbolic reasoning chains)—will guarantee faithfulness of explanations and improve both interpretability and empirical performance over standard chain-of-thought prompting.
b115c1e1e9e51f8ad7d47b745bc04e29a654b84d.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that decomposes complex reasoning tasks into two explicit stages. In the Translation stage, a language model is prompted to translate a natural language query into a structured reasoning chain that interleaves natural language (NL) comments and symbolic language (SL) programs (such as Python, Datalog, or PDDL). The NL component breaks down the query into subquestions, dependencies, and rationales, while the SL component encodes executable steps for each subproblem. In the Problem Solving stage, an external deterministic solver (e.g., Python interpreter, Datalog executor, or PDDL planner) is used to execute the symbolic reasoning chain and derive the final answer. This approach ensures that the final answer is causally and faithfully derived from the reasoning chain, making the explanation both interpretable and verifiable.
b115c1e1e9e51f8ad7d47b745bc04e29a654b84d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on ten reasoning datasets spanning four domains: Math Word Problems (GSM8K, SVAMP, MultiArith, ASDiv, AQuA), Planning (SayCan), Multi-hop Question Answering (StrategyQA, Date Understanding, Sports Understanding), and Relational Inference (CLUTRR). Few-shot prompting will be used, with 6-10 exemplars per dataset, and both greedy decoding and self-consistency decoding strategies will be evaluated. Baselines will include standard prompting, standard chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting, and Least-to-Most (LtM) prompting. Evaluation metrics will focus on final answer accuracy, with additional human evaluation of reasoning chain plausibility. The experiments will utilize large language models such as OpenAI Codex and GPT-4 as the Translator, and appropriate deterministic solvers for each symbolic language.
b115c1e1e9e51f8ad7d47b745bc04e29a654b84d.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a general and interpretable framework that guarantees faithfulness by ensuring the final answer is deterministically derived from an explicitly generated reasoning chain. Unlike prior work, the approach interleaves natural language and symbolic language within the reasoning chain, making it accessible to non-programmers and generalizable across diverse domains and symbolic languages. The method sets new state-of-the-art few-shot performance on multiple benchmarks, demonstrates strong synergy between faithfulness and accuracy, and provides the first systematic human evaluation of reasoning chain plausibility in chain-of-thought prompting.

b1234cfbd428f093d1b83abd0ffd424c51b7f4f6.title: Balancing Multimodal Training Through Game-Theoretic Regularization
b1234cfbd428f093d1b83abd0ffd424c51b7f4f6.research_question: How can training imbalances and modality competition in multimodal learning be addressed to ensure balanced optimization across all modalities and achieve consistent performance improvements when integrating multiple data sources?
b1234cfbd428f093d1b83abd0ffd424c51b7f4f6.hypothesis: Introducing a game-theoretic regularization framework that decomposes and balances task-relevant unique and shared information across modalities will mitigate modality competition, leading to more effective multimodal learning and improved performance compared to existing training strategies.
b1234cfbd428f093d1b83abd0ffd424c51b7f4f6.proposed_method: A novel regularization approach, termed the Multimodal Competition Regularizer (MCR), is proposed to address modality competition in multimodal learning. The method decomposes the joint mutual information between modalities and the target into task-relevant unique and shared components, using refined lower and upper bounds to promote informative signals and suppress noise. The framework incorporates three key loss components: (1) a Mutual Information Perturbed Difference (MIPD) loss that estimates each modality's unique contribution via output variations under latent-space perturbations; (2) a supervised contrastive loss to maximize shared task-relevant information between modalities; and (3) a Conditional Entropy Bottleneck (CEB) loss to penalize task-irrelevant shared information by reconstructing latent representations from the output. A game-theoretic training strategy is employed, where each modality's encoder can adopt collaborative, independent, or greedy strategies to balance its influence, with the greedy strategy (each modality maximizing its own contribution while minimizing others') serving as the default for robust performance. Latent-space permutations are used for efficient conditional mutual information estimation, reducing computational overhead compared to input-space perturbations.
b1234cfbd428f093d1b83abd0ffd424c51b7f4f6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic datasets designed to induce modality competition and a suite of established real-world multimodal benchmarks. Real-world datasets include AVE and UCF for action recognition, CREMA-D for emotion recognition, CMU-MOSI and CMU-MOSEI for sentiment analysis, and Something-Something V2 for egocentric action recognition. A variety of model architectures will be employed, ranging from smaller models trained from scratch (e.g., ResNet-18, small-scale Transformers) to large, self-supervised pretrained models (e.g., Swin-TF, Conformer, Wav2Vec2, HuBERT, ViViT). Baselines for comparison will include unimodal models (frozen and finetuned), ensembles, joint training, Multi-Loss, MMCosine, MSLR, OGM, AGM, MLB, ReconBoost, MMPareto, and D&R, among others. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy for classification tasks and binary accuracy for regression tasks. Experiments will analyze performance under varying degrees of modality informativeness imbalance, and post-hoc error analysis will be performed to assess the routing and synergy capabilities of the proposed method.
b1234cfbd428f093d1b83abd0ffd424c51b7f4f6.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a game-theoretic regularization framework that adaptively balances modality contributions during training, preventing the adverse effects of modality competition. It refines mutual information decomposition with improved lower and upper bounds for both unique and shared task-relevant information, and introduces efficient latent-space permutation techniques for conditional mutual information estimation. The method is claimed to consistently outperform all prior multimodal training strategies and simple baselines across diverse datasets, architectures, and task types, demonstrating robust and generalizable improvements in multimodal supervised learning.

b12488cf6cf9c630ab2d344964bf2233bbd9dee8.title: Transformers Meet Directed Graphs
b12488cf6cf9c630ab2d344964bf2233bbd9dee8.research_question: How can transformers be extended to effectively model directed graphs, enabling improved performance and robustness in tasks where directionality is essential, such as program analysis and correctness prediction?
b12488cf6cf9c630ab2d344964bf2233bbd9dee8.hypothesis: Incorporating direction- and structure-aware positional encodings into transformer architectures will significantly enhance their ability to model directed graphs, leading to improved predictive performance and robustness on tasks where edge directionality is crucial.
b12488cf6cf9c630ab2d344964bf2233bbd9dee8.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that introduces two types of direction- and structure-aware positional encodings for directed graphs: (1) the eigenvectors of the Magnetic Laplacian, which generalize the combinatorial Laplacian to encode edge directionality using complex-valued spectral information, and (2) directional random walk encodings, which extend random walk-based node embeddings to account for both forward and reverse transitions in directed graphs. The Magnetic Laplacian encodings are normalized to resolve scale, sign, and rotation ambiguities, and are processed with a dedicated neural network module (e.g., SignNet or MLP) before integration into the transformer. Directional random walk encodings aggregate multi-step landing probabilities from both forward and reverse walks, including personalized PageRank for global context, and are similarly processed for use as node positional encodings. Both encoding types are designed to be permutation equivariant and to capture critical directionality information lost by traditional undirected encodings.
b12488cf6cf9c630ab2d344964bf2233bbd9dee8.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a range of tasks requiring directed graph understanding, including a custom correctness prediction task for sorting networks (where directionality is essential), and the Open Graph Benchmark Code2 dataset for function name prediction from source code graphs. Baselines include transformers with sinusoidal and Laplacian positional encodings, random walk encodings, SVD-based spectral encodings, and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) with and without directionality. Evaluation metrics include F1 score for classification and RMSE for regression tasks. Experimental setups involve ablation studies on positional encoding types, analysis of generalization to longer sequences, and robustness to semantics-preserving permutations in source code. The proposed methods are tested on synthetic and real-world datasets, with careful control of graph construction and class balance.
b12488cf6cf9c630ab2d344964bf2233bbd9dee8.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first comprehensive direction-aware positional encodings for transformers on directed graphs, leveraging the Magnetic Laplacian and directional random walks. It claims to bridge the gap between sequence-based and graph-based modeling by enabling transformers to natively handle directed graph structures, which are ubiquitous in domains such as program analysis and logic circuits. The method is claimed to outperform prior state-of-the-art approaches on challenging benchmarks, provide robustness to input permutations that preserve semantics, and enable significant reductions in effective input dimensionality by exploiting graph invariances. Additionally, the approach is designed to be complementary to existing GNN architectures and is applicable to both weighted and unweighted graphs.

b12541867632737e826b7b01c7fbe1c4222d8655.title: Compressing Context to Enhance Inference Efficiency of Large Language Models
b12541867632737e826b7b01c7fbe1c4222d8655.research_question: How can the inference efficiency of large language models (LLMs) be improved when processing long contexts, such as extended documents or conversations, without significantly compromising task performance?
b12541867632737e826b7b01c7fbe1c4222d8655.hypothesis: Redundant or non-essential content in input contexts can be systematically identified and pruned using information-theoretic measures, resulting in more compact inputs that reduce computational costs while maintaining comparable performance on downstream tasks.
b12541867632737e826b7b01c7fbe1c4222d8655.proposed_method: A model-agnostic framework, Selective Context, is proposed to optimize LLM inference by filtering out redundant or non-essential content from input contexts. The method computes the self-information (surprisal) of lexical units (tokens, phrases, or sentences) using a base causal language model. Tokens are merged into larger lexical units, and a percentile-based filtering approach is used to retain only the most informative units, adaptively selecting content based on the distribution of self-information values. The process can be applied at different granularities (token, phrase, sentence), with phrase-level found to be optimal. This filtered, compacted context is then fed to the target LLM for downstream tasks, reducing memory and computation requirements.
b12541867632737e826b7b01c7fbe1c4222d8655.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three datasets requiring long-context processing: arXiv papers (first two sections per paper), BBC News articles, and real conversations from ShareGPT.com. Four tasks will be evaluated: summarization, question answering, conversation response generation, and original context reconstruction. Multiple LLMs will be used as backbones, including GPT-3.5, GPT-4, LLaMA (7B, 13B, 30B), and Vicuna (7B, 13B), with smaller models (LLaMA-7B or GPT-3-curie) used for self-information computation. Baselines will include full-context inference and random deletion at matched compression ratios. Evaluation metrics will include BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE, and BERTScore for output similarity, as well as faithfulness checks via manual and automated methods. Experiments will systematically vary compression ratios and lexical unit granularity, and measure both performance and resource usage (memory, inference time).
b12541867632737e826b7b01c7fbe1c4222d8655.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a complementary, model-agnostic method for enhancing LLM inference efficiency by targeting redundancy in the input context itself, rather than modifying model architectures or relying on distillation. The use of self-information to quantify and prune redundancy at multiple lexical granularities is novel, and the percentile-based adaptive filtering allows for flexible trade-offs between efficiency and performance. The method is shown to significantly reduce memory and inference time (up to 36% and 32%, respectively) with only minor drops in output quality, and can be combined with other efficiency techniques.

b1362b8a11b1984378b91162195e10e369f6b012.title: Human-in-the-loop: Provably Efficient Preference-based Reinforcement Learning with General Function Approximation
b1362b8a11b1984378b91162195e10e369f6b012.research_question: How can reinforcement learning agents efficiently learn optimal policies based solely on human trajectory preference feedback, particularly when both the transition dynamics and preference functions are represented by general (potentially non-linear or nonparametric) function approximators, and how can this be extended to settings with n-wise comparisons?
b1362b8a11b1984378b91162195e10e369f6b012.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a model-based reinforcement learning algorithm, leveraging value-targeted regression and optimistic planning, can achieve provably efficient (sublinear) regret bounds in preference-based RL with general function approximation. Furthermore, extending this framework to n-wise comparison settings will yield similarly efficient algorithms with improved sample complexity.
b1362b8a11b1984378b91162195e10e369f6b012.proposed_method: A novel optimistic model-based reinforcement learning algorithm, termed Preference-based Optimistic Planning (PbOP), will be developed for the setting where agents receive only trajectory preference feedback from a human overseer, rather than numeric rewards. The algorithm will estimate both the transition model and the preference function using least-squares regression, constructing high-confidence sets for each via Eluder dimension and covering number-based concentration bounds. At each episode, the agent will compute confidence bonuses for both transition and preference estimations, and define a set of near-optimal policies by solving an optimistic planning problem over these confidence sets. The most exploratory policy pairs will be selected by maximizing the uncertainty (bonus) in the preference feedback, encouraging efficient exploration. This framework will be further extended to a new setting, RL with n-wise comparisons, where multiple trajectories are compared per episode, and the algorithm will be adapted to exploit the additional information for improved sample efficiency.
b1362b8a11b1984378b91162195e10e369f6b012.experiment_details: Experiments will be designed to evaluate the proposed PbOP algorithm and its extension to n-wise comparisons. Synthetic and/or benchmark RL environments with large or continuous state spaces will be used, where the true reward function is hidden and only preference feedback is available. Baselines will include existing preference-based RL algorithms limited to tabular or linear settings, as well as standard RL algorithms adapted to preference feedback. Evaluation metrics will focus on cumulative regret, sample efficiency, and scalability with respect to the Eluder dimension and function class complexity. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to establish upper and lower bounds on regret, and empirical results will demonstrate the algorithm's performance relative to baselines.
b1362b8a11b1984378b91162195e10e369f6b012.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first provably efficient model-based RL algorithm for preference-based settings with general function approximation, achieving regret bounds that scale with the Eluder dimension and covering numbers rather than the cardinality of the state-action space. It establishes near-optimal regret rates in both linear and general function classes, and provides the first theoretical and algorithmic results for RL with n-wise trajectory comparisons. The approach also demonstrates a reduction from RL with once-per-episode feedback to preference-based RL, unifying and extending previous theoretical frameworks.

b154dd79d04782680801acf8d80f54f0939e9d31.title: Explicit Regularization in Overparametrized Models via Noise Injection
b154dd79d04782680801acf8d80f54f0939e9d31.research_question: How does injecting noise into model parameters during training affect explicit regularization and generalization in both simple and overparameterized machine learning models, including deep neural networks?
b154dd79d04782680801acf8d80f54f0939e9d31.hypothesis: Injecting small, independent, layer-wise noise into model parameters during training induces explicit regularization that improves generalization performance, and avoids the variance explosion that occurs with simultaneous noise injection in all parameters, especially in overparameterized neural networks.
b154dd79d04782680801acf8d80f54f0939e9d31.proposed_method: A novel training procedure is proposed where, at each gradient descent step, independent Gaussian noise is injected into the parameters of a single randomly selected layer (layer-wise perturbation), rather than all layers simultaneously. The method is analyzed theoretically for both finite-dimensional models (e.g., linear regression, Lasso, nuclear norm problems) and overparameterized neural networks, including those with infinite width. Taylor expansions and asymptotic analysis are used to derive the explicit form of the regularizer induced by noise injection, showing that for simple models, the regularizer corresponds to well-known norms (e.g., L1, group Lasso, nuclear norm), and for deep networks, it is related to the trace of the Hessian of the loss with respect to the model output. The approach is further extended to deep architectures by scaling the noise variance appropriately with the number of layers, ensuring that the regularization effect remains stable as model width increases.
b154dd79d04782680801acf8d80f54f0939e9d31.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of models, including shallow and deep multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs), convolutional neural networks (CNNs), and ResNet architectures, using datasets such as synthetic regression data, FashionMNIST, and CIFAR-10. Both full-batch and stochastic gradient descent will be used, with comparisons made between standard gradient descent, simultaneous noise injection in all parameters, and the proposed layer-wise noise injection. Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy and the trace of the Hessian (as a measure of flatness/regularization). The effect of varying the noise scale will be systematically explored, and the experimental setup will include both underparameterized and highly overparameterized regimes to assess the robustness and scalability of the proposed method.
b154dd79d04782680801acf8d80f54f0939e9d31.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces an explicit regularization technique for overparameterized models via independent layer-wise noise injection, which provably avoids the variance explosion associated with simultaneous perturbation of all parameters. The method provides a unified theoretical framework connecting noise injection to explicit regularization for a variety of models and loss functions, including deep neural networks with large widths. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate improved generalization performance and more stable training dynamics compared to existing noise injection approaches. The approach is simple to implement and can be easily integrated into existing training pipelines for modern neural architectures.

b15769e20f2a07a0f53a4a4b877e38e9c57eb96e.title: Robotic Offline RL from Internet Videos via Value-Function Pre-Training
b15769e20f2a07a0f53a4a4b877e38e9c57eb96e.research_question: How can large-scale, unlabeled internet video data be leveraged to improve the generalization and robustness of robotic offline reinforcement learning for manipulation tasks?
b15769e20f2a07a0f53a4a4b877e38e9c57eb96e.hypothesis: Pre-training value functions directly on large-scale, action-free human video datasets using temporal-difference learning will produce visual representations that, when further refined with multi-task robotic data, enable downstream offline RL policies to generalize more broadly and robustly to novel tasks, objects, and distractors compared to existing video pre-training or representation learning approaches.
b15769e20f2a07a0f53a4a4b877e38e9c57eb96e.proposed_method: A three-phase framework is proposed. In Phase 1, an intent-conditioned value function (ICVF) is pre-trained on large-scale human video data (e.g., Ego4D) using temporal-difference (TD) learning, despite the absence of action and reward annotations. The ICVF models the value of reaching various goal observations conditioned on intended goals, with representations learned via a shared visual encoder and specialized MLP heads. In Phase 2, the learned visual representation is refined using a multi-task robotic dataset (e.g., Bridge), where a Q-function and policy are trained via multi-task conservative Q-learning (CQL), conditioning on both the robot's observation and a task identifier (either one-hot or language-based). In Phase 3, the system is fine-tuned on a small, task-specific robot dataset using offline CQL, with stratified sampling to mitigate overfitting. The entire pipeline is designed to bridge the domain gap between human video and robot data, and to align learned representations with the robot's action space.
b15769e20f2a07a0f53a4a4b877e38e9c57eb96e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a real WidowX robot platform, targeting several challenging manipulation tasks such as pick-and-place, tool use, and multi-phase actions in a toy kitchen environment. Pre-training will utilize the Ego4D dataset (4M transitions) for video data and the Bridge dataset (150K transitions) for multi-task robot data. For each downstream task, 10 teleoperated demonstrations will be collected, including variations in objects and distractors. Baselines will include methods that do not use video data (PTR, BC), as well as state-of-the-art video pre-training approaches (R3M, MVP, VIP). Evaluation metrics will focus on task success rates under varying initial conditions, presence of distractors, and novel objects, with additional diagnostic experiments such as value estimation error and Grad-CAM visualizations to probe representation quality. Simulation experiments will also be performed to assess generalization in controlled settings.
b15769e20f2a07a0f53a4a4b877e38e9c57eb96e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to demonstrate that temporal-difference value learning alone can effectively pre-train representations from large-scale, action-free video data for robotic offline RL. Unlike prior methods that rely on self-supervised or contrastive objectives, this method directly optimizes value functions aligned with downstream RL objectives. The framework bridges the domain gap between human video and robot data via multi-task Q-learning, and supports both discrete and language-based task specifications. Experimental results indicate significant improvements in generalization and robustness over prior video pre-training and imitation learning methods, especially in scenarios with novel objects, distractors, and workspace variations.

b15d92ff28b2cf1fd13bf6187844df1e073054a3.title: Improved Training Technique for Shortcut Models
b15d92ff28b2cf1fd13bf6187844df1e073054a3.research_question: How can the core limitations of shortcut models for generative modeling—such as compounding guidance artifacts, inflexible guidance, frequency bias, self-consistency divergence, and unstable generative trajectories—be systematically addressed to enable high-quality, efficient, and flexible sample generation across one-step, few-step, and multi-step regimes?
b15d92ff28b2cf1fd13bf6187844df1e073054a3.hypothesis: Introducing a unified training framework that integrates dynamic guidance control, frequency-aware losses, scalable optimal transport, and improved self-consistency stabilization will resolve the key bottlenecks of shortcut models, resulting in substantial improvements in generative quality, flexibility, and efficiency.
b15d92ff28b2cf1fd13bf6187844df1e073054a3.proposed_method: A new training framework, termed Improved Shortcut Model (iSM), will be developed to address the five major limitations of existing shortcut models. The method will incorporate four main components: (1) Intrinsic Guidance, which makes the guidance scale an explicit input to the model, enabling dynamic, inference-time control and resolving the compounding guidance flaw; (2) Multi-Level Wavelet Loss, which replaces standard pixel-wise objectives with a frequency-aware loss based on multi-level discrete wavelet transforms to mitigate low-frequency bias and enhance high-frequency detail reconstruction; (3) Scaling Optimal Transport (sOT), which pools samples from multiple mini-batches to compute large-scale optimal transport plans, decoupling OT batch size from training batch size and yielding straighter, more stable generative paths; and (4) a Twin EMA strategy, maintaining two separate exponential moving average networks—one for stable inference and another for up-to-date self-consistency targets—thereby reconciling training stability with self-consistency. The training objective will be a weighted sum of velocity, guidance, and self-consistency losses, with interval-based guidance applied to avoid diversity collapse in high-noise regimes.
b15d92ff28b2cf1fd13bf6187844df1e073054a3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ImageNet 256×256 dataset, using the XL/2 variant of the SiT architecture for the main model. The evaluation will compare the proposed iSM framework against a broad range of baselines, including GANs (BigGAN-deep, GigaGAN, StyleGAN-XL), masked/auto-regressive models (VQGAN, MaskGIT, VAR, MAR), and diffusion/flow-based models (ADM, CDM, SimDiff, LDM-4-G, U-DiT-L, U-ViT-H, DiT-XL/2, SiT-XL/2, REPA-XL/2, FlowDCN), as well as previous shortcut and variable-step models (SM, IMM). Metrics used will include FID-50k, FD-DINOv2, and Inception Score (IS), with evaluations performed at various numbers of function evaluations (NFE) to test one-step, few-step, and multi-step generation. Ablation studies will systematically vary key hyperparameters for each proposed component, and additional experiments will test scalability to higher resolutions (ImageNet 512×512) and alternative architectures (FlowDCN).
b15d92ff28b2cf1fd13bf6187844df1e073054a3.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to formalize and resolve the flaw of compounding guidance in shortcut models, introduces dynamic, inference-time controllable guidance via Intrinsic Guidance, and pioneers the use of multi-level wavelet losses to address frequency bias in shortcut generative models. The Scaling Optimal Transport approach enables large-scale OT matching without increasing training memory requirements, resulting in straighter and more stable generative trajectories. The Twin EMA strategy uniquely decouples inference and target stabilization, improving self-consistency without sacrificing sample quality. Collectively, these innovations establish shortcut models as a flexible, efficient, and highly competitive class of generative models, closing the performance gap with leading GANs and diffusion-based methods.

b15e6e2b1d81bc110f8fc98c3caf2e25e2512539.title: Autoregressive Model Beats Diffusion: Llama for Scalable Image Generation
b15e6e2b1d81bc110f8fc98c3caf2e25e2512539.research_question: Can vanilla autoregressive models, using the original next-token prediction paradigm from large language models and without vision-specific inductive biases, achieve state-of-the-art performance in scalable image generation when properly scaled and equipped with advanced image tokenizers and high-quality training data?
b15e6e2b1d81bc110f8fc98c3caf2e25e2512539.hypothesis: Vanilla autoregressive models, when scaled appropriately and combined with optimized image tokenizers and high-quality training data, can match or surpass the image generation performance of diffusion models and other state-of-the-art approaches, both in class-conditional and text-conditional settings.
b15e6e2b1d81bc110f8fc98c3caf2e25e2512539.proposed_method: A novel image generation framework is proposed that leverages the Llama architecture, applying the next-token prediction paradigm directly to visual data. Images are first quantized into discrete tokens using a quantized autoencoder-based tokenizer with a downsample ratio of 16 and a codebook optimized for high reconstruction quality and codebook usage. The resulting token sequences are modeled using transformer-based autoregressive models of varying sizes (from 111M to 3.1B parameters), with class or text conditioning incorporated via learnable embeddings or pre-trained text encoders (e.g., FLAN-T5XL). Classifier-free guidance, advanced sampling techniques (top-k, top-p, temperature), and LLM community optimizations (such as vLLM for inference speed) are integrated to further enhance generation quality and efficiency.
b15e6e2b1d81bc110f8fc98c3caf2e25e2512539.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard benchmarks, primarily the 256x256 ImageNet dataset for class-conditional generation and LAION-COCO plus an internal high-aesthetics dataset for text-conditional generation. The image tokenizer will be evaluated using rFID, PSNR, SSIM, and codebook usage on ImageNet and COCO validation sets. Image generation models will be compared against GANs, diffusion models, and other autoregressive baselines using metrics such as FID, Inception Score, Precision, and Recall. Ablation studies will examine the effects of codebook design, number of tokens, model size, classifier-free guidance, and sampling configurations. Inference speed improvements will be quantified using the vLLM serving framework, measuring speedup ratios across model sizes.
b15e6e2b1d81bc110f8fc98c3caf2e25e2512539.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a scalable image generation framework that applies the original next-token prediction paradigm of language models to visual data without vision-specific architectural modifications. It demonstrates that, with proper scaling and advanced tokenizer design, vanilla autoregressive models can outperform popular diffusion models on standard image generation benchmarks. The work also claims significant improvements in inference speed by leveraging LLM serving frameworks, and provides a generalizable, high-quality image tokenizer that closes the gap with continuous representations. The approach facilitates open-source development and lays the groundwork for unified multimodal foundation models.

b16c7d45183b9d595ab64301be019741b1528860.title: Llemma: An Open Language Model For Mathematics
b16c7d45183b9d595ab64301be019741b1528860.research_question: How can a large language model be effectively adapted and specialized for mathematical reasoning and problem solving, including tool use and formal theorem proving, while remaining open access and reproducible?
b16c7d45183b9d595ab64301be019741b1528860.hypothesis: Continued pretraining of a strong code-focused language model on a diverse, large-scale corpus of mathematics-related text and code will yield a base model with substantially improved mathematical reasoning, tool use, and formal theorem proving capabilities, outperforming existing open models.
b16c7d45183b9d595ab64301be019741b1528860.proposed_method: A new approach is developed that continues pretraining an existing code-specialized language model (CodeLlama) on a curated, large-scale dataset called Proof-Pile-2. Proof-Pile-2 is constructed as a 55B-token mixture of scientific papers, high-quality web data filtered for mathematics, and mathematical code, including a new 11B-token AlgebraicStack dataset of math-related code from 17 languages. The pretraining mixture consists of 95% Proof-Pile-2, 2% general domain data (from The Pile, excluding overlapping sources), and 3% GitHub code. Two model sizes (7B and 34B parameters) are initialized from CodeLlama and trained further using standard autoregressive language modeling objectives, with careful engineering for large-batch, mixed-precision distributed training. Hyperparameters such as learning rate schedules, batch sizes, and context lengths are tuned for stability and efficiency, and a RoPE base period contraction is applied to the 7B model to enable future long-context finetuning.
b16c7d45183b9d595ab64301be019741b1528860.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate the resulting models on a suite of mathematical reasoning benchmarks, including MATH (high-school competition problems), GSM8k (middle-school word problems), OCW Courses (undergraduate STEM problems), MMLU-STEM (STEM subset of MMLU), and SAT math questions. Both chain-of-thought and majority voting evaluation protocols are used, with few-shot prompts and greedy or nucleus sampling. Tool-use capabilities are assessed by prompting the model to solve problems with access to a Python interpreter and symbolic computation tools (SymPy), and formal mathematics abilities are evaluated on informal-to-formal and formal-to-formal theorem proving tasks using the miniF2F benchmark in Isabelle and Lean proof assistants. Baselines include CodeLlama, Llama2, and the proprietary Minerva models, with performance measured by exact match accuracy, pass@k, and theorem closure rates. Additional analyses include data mixture ablation, memorization checks via n-gram overlap, and manual inspection of corpus overlap.
b16c7d45183b9d595ab64301be019741b1528860.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first openly released large language models specialized for mathematics that outperform all known open base models and even proprietary models of similar scale on key benchmarks. The methodology includes the creation and release of Proof-Pile-2 and AlgebraicStack, the largest open math-focused code dataset to date. The approach demonstrates, for the first time, few-shot formal theorem proving and autoformalization by an open model, as well as robust tool-use capabilities without additional finetuning. All models, datasets, and code are made fully open, establishing a new platform for research in mathematical reasoning and language model adaptation.

b16cbdacf53ab4870ce7645d899c7e9e6f41c51e.title: Is DPO Superior to PPO for LLM Alignment? A Comprehensive Study
b16cbdacf53ab4870ce7645d899c7e9e6f41c51e.research_question: Are reward-free methods, such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), fundamentally superior to reward-based methods like Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) for aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences across diverse RLHF tasks? What are the key factors that influence the effectiveness of these alignment approaches?
b16cbdacf53ab4870ce7645d899c7e9e6f41c51e.hypothesis: DPO may have fundamental limitations in certain alignment scenarios, particularly due to sensitivity to distribution shifts between model outputs and preference data, while PPO's performance can be substantially improved through specific algorithmic enhancements.
b16cbdacf53ab4870ce7645d899c7e9e6f41c51e.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted to compare DPO and PPO for LLM alignment. The methodology will include (1) formal analysis of the algorithmic properties and limitations of DPO, particularly its susceptibility to out-of-distribution responses and biased solutions; (2) ablation studies to identify and validate critical factors that enhance PPO's performance, such as advantage normalization, large batch size, and exponential moving average updates for the reference model; and (3) iterative approaches for DPO, where model-generated samples are re-annotated and used for further training to mitigate distribution shift. Both static and iterative training paradigms will be explored for DPO, and PPO will be tuned with best practices identified in reinforcement learning literature.
b16cbdacf53ab4870ce7645d899c7e9e6f41c51e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a suite of RLHF testbeds, including dialogue generation (e.g., HH-RLHF, SafeRLHF) and challenging code generation tasks (e.g., APPS, CodeContest). Models such as Llama2-7B and CodeLlama-34B will be fine-tuned using both PPO and DPO (including iterative DPO). Evaluation metrics will include win rates against human-preferred responses, helpfulness and harmlessness scores (using official reward models), safety rates, and code correctness (pass@k). Baselines will include SFT, RRHF, PRO, and previously published models (e.g., AlphaCode). Ablation studies will systematically vary PPO components (batch size, advantage normalization, reference model update) to isolate their effects. Both preference-based and direct reward feedback will be utilized, and the impact of data distribution, preference annotation quality, and iterative data collection will be analyzed.
b16cbdacf53ab4870ce7645d899c7e9e6f41c51e.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a rigorous theoretical and empirical comparison of reward-free (DPO) and reward-based (PPO) RLHF methods for LLM alignment, revealing fundamental limitations of DPO related to distribution shift and out-of-distribution exploitation. It identifies and validates key algorithmic factors that enable PPO to achieve state-of-the-art results, particularly in challenging code generation tasks. The study also proposes and evaluates iterative DPO as a mitigation strategy for distribution mismatch, providing practical guidelines for robust RLHF training. The work aims to set new benchmarks and establish best practices for LLM alignment across diverse domains.

b18e880d09c27c3e7026e21a8bca8b29f40f1cf5.title: Solving Inverse Problems with Score-Based Generative Priors learned from Noisy Data
b18e880d09c27c3e7026e21a8bca8b29f40f1cf5.research_question: How can inverse problems be effectively solved using score-based generative priors when only noisy training data is available, particularly in scenarios where acquiring large, clean datasets is impractical?
b18e880d09c27c3e7026e21a8bca8b29f40f1cf5.hypothesis: It is possible to jointly learn a denoiser and a score-based generative model from only noisy training data by leveraging a unified loss function that combines Stein's unbiased risk estimate (SURE), denoising score matching (DSM), and Tweedie's formula, thereby enabling effective posterior sampling and reconstruction in inverse problems even at low signal-to-noise ratios.
b18e880d09c27c3e7026e21a8bca8b29f40f1cf5.proposed_method: A novel framework, SURE-Score, is developed to jointly learn a denoiser and a score-based generative model using a single deep neural network trained exclusively on noisy samples. The method formulates a unified loss function that integrates SURE for self-supervised denoising, DSM for learning the score function, and Tweedie's rule to ensure consistency between denoising and score estimation at a specific noise level. The loss consists of two main terms: one for denoising (SURE) and one for score matching (DSM), weighted by a scalar hyperparameter, and both are computed using the same network via a recurrent call. The approach is compatible with additive Gaussian noise but is extendable to other exponential family noise models. During inference, posterior sampling is performed using an annealed Langevin dynamics algorithm, which incorporates the learned score function and data consistency with respect to the forward operator.
b18e880d09c27c3e7026e21a8bca8b29f40f1cf5.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on two linear inverse problems: compressive MIMO wireless channel estimation and accelerated 2D multi-coil MRI reconstruction. For MIMO, clustered delay line (CDL) channels are simulated with varying SNR levels (0 dB and 10 dB), and the score-based model is compared against baselines such as supervised DSM, naive DSM on noisy data, BM3D, Noise2Self, and Noise2Score. For MRI, the FastMRI dataset is used, with multi-coil T2-weighted brain scans, and experiments are performed at an acceleration factor of 5×. Evaluation metrics include normalized mean squared error (NMSE) for channel estimation and normalized root mean squared error (NRMSE) for MRI, with both qualitative and quantitative analyses of prior and posterior sampling. The experimental setup includes training with 10,000 noisy samples, use of the NCSNv2/RefineNet architecture, and hyperparameter selection based on mini-batch statistics.
b18e880d09c27c3e7026e21a8bca8b29f40f1cf5.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a unified framework that enables joint learning of denoising and score-based generative modeling from only noisy data, eliminating the need for clean training samples. The approach leverages a novel loss function that couples SURE, DSM, and Tweedie's rule within a single deep neural network, ensuring consistency and efficiency. SURE-Score is demonstrated to be effective across different domains (wireless MIMO and MRI) and at extremely low SNRs (as low as 0 dB), achieving performance close to supervised methods. The method is generalizable to other noise models and provides a practical solution for real-world scenarios where clean data is unavailable.

b190697d8106a555f525acec33c6a91c67b88483.title: The Clever Hans Mirage: A Comprehensive Survey on Spurious Correlations in Machine Learning
b190697d8106a555f525acec33c6a91c67b88483.research_question: How can spurious correlations in machine learning models be systematically identified, characterized, and mitigated to improve robustness and generalization across diverse domains and distribution shifts?
