b190697d8106a555f525acec33c6a91c67b88483.hypothesis: Spurious correlations in machine learning models can be effectively addressed through a comprehensive taxonomy of data-centric, representation learning, post-hoc, and specialized methods, leading to improved model robustness, fairness, and generalization under distribution shifts.
b190697d8106a555f525acec33c6a91c67b88483.proposed_method: A comprehensive research plan will be developed to systematically investigate spurious correlations in machine learning. The approach will begin by formally defining spurious correlations and constructing a fine-grained taxonomy of existing mitigation strategies, categorized into data-centric methods (such as data augmentation, balancing, and pseudo-label discovery), representation learning approaches (including causal intervention, invariant learning, feature disentanglement, and contrastive learning), post-hoc correction techniques (identification then mitigation, finetuning, optimization-based, ensemble, and adversarial methods), and specialized approaches for non-standard settings. For each category, representative algorithms will be implemented and analyzed, with technical emphasis on how they disrupt the association between spurious attributes and target labels. The methodology will also include the creation or curation of benchmark datasets and evaluation metrics specifically designed to expose and measure the impact of spurious correlations, as well as the development of diagnostic tools to visualize and quantify model reliance on spurious features.
b190697d8106a555f525acec33c6a91c67b88483.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of benchmark datasets known for spurious correlation challenges, such as Waterbirds, CelebA, CivilComments, and tasks from the WILDS benchmark. Baseline models will include standard Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM), Group DRO, and other state-of-the-art robust learning algorithms. Evaluation metrics will focus on worst-group accuracy, group-wise error rates, and out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization performance. Experimental setups will involve controlled environment shifts to test model robustness, ablation studies to isolate the effect of each mitigation strategy, and stress-testing with counterfactual or adversarially perturbed data. Comparative analyses will be performed to assess the effectiveness, scalability, and limitations of each method within the taxonomy.
b190697d8106a555f525acec33c6a91c67b88483.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first comprehensive, fine-grained taxonomy of methods for addressing spurious correlations in machine learning, spanning the entire model development pipeline. It provides a unified framework for formalizing, diagnosing, and mitigating spurious correlations, along with curated benchmarks and evaluation metrics tailored to this challenge. The work aims to bridge gaps between disparate research areas—such as domain generalization, group robustness, shortcut learning, and simplicity bias—by systematically mapping their connections to spurious correlations. The proposal also identifies open challenges and future research directions, particularly in the context of foundation models and generative AI, offering actionable insights for advancing robust and fair machine learning.

b19ff8bb7f7934e46d7f87ee8f0ec6c9bd3676c5.title: Privacy Amplification Through Synthetic Data: Insights from Linear Regression
b19ff8bb7f7934e46d7f87ee8f0ec6c9bd3676c5.research_question: How can the release of synthetic data generated from differentially private linear regression models amplify privacy guarantees, and under what conditions does this amplification occur or fail, particularly in relation to the adversary's knowledge of the generative process?
b19ff8bb7f7934e46d7f87ee8f0ec6c9bd3676c5.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that releasing a limited number of synthetic data points generated from random inputs to a differentially private linear regression model can provide stronger privacy guarantees (privacy amplification) than those directly inherited from the model, whereas adversarial control over the generative seed negates this amplification.
b19ff8bb7f7934e46d7f87ee8f0ec6c9bd3676c5.proposed_method: A theoretical and empirical framework will be developed to analyze privacy amplification in synthetic data release, focusing on the linear regression setting. Differentially private models will be trained using output perturbation and noisy gradient descent, and the privacy guarantees of synthetic data generated from these models will be quantified using the f-Differential Privacy (f-DP) and Rényi Differential Privacy (RDP) frameworks. The analysis will consider two scenarios: (1) adversarial control of the generative seed, and (2) generation from random inputs. For the latter, the convergence of the distribution of synthetic outputs to Gaussian distributions will be leveraged to derive non-asymptotic and asymptotic privacy bounds, including closed-form expressions for trade-off functions and Rényi divergences. The methodology will also extend to the release of multiple synthetic data points and higher-dimensional settings, employing central limit theorems and matrix product convergence results.
b19ff8bb7f7934e46d7f87ee8f0ec6c9bd3676c5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic datasets in high-dimensional linear regression settings, where models are privatized via output perturbation or noisy gradient descent. The privacy leakage will be evaluated by comparing the trade-off functions and Rényi divergences between the distributions of synthetic data generated from adjacent datasets. Monte Carlo simulations will be used to estimate privacy loss for varying numbers of synthetic data points, input dimensions, and levels of adversarial knowledge. Baseline comparisons will include the post-processing upper bound on privacy loss and direct model release. Evaluation metrics will focus on the tightness of privacy amplification bounds, the rate of convergence to Gaussian approximations, and the scaling of privacy loss with respect to the number of released synthetic samples and model complexity.
b19ff8bb7f7934e46d7f87ee8f0ec6c9bd3676c5.novelty_claims: The proposed research will provide the first rigorous theoretical quantification of privacy amplification in synthetic data release for linear regression, establishing both negative and positive results depending on adversarial control. It will introduce new analytical tools for bounding privacy loss using f-DP and RDP in the context of synthetic data, and derive explicit, non-asymptotic bounds for privacy amplification when synthetic data is generated from random inputs. The work will also demonstrate that, under certain conditions, releasing a small number of synthetic samples can yield stronger privacy guarantees than those implied by the post-processing theorem, and will offer insights into the limitations of privacy amplification when adversarial seed control is possible. These findings will lay the groundwork for extending privacy amplification analysis to more complex models and real-world synthetic data generation scenarios.

b1d77c7921bcd79f520d252473225ac19d6b6289.title: Guided Flows for Generative Modeling and Decision Making
b1d77c7921bcd79f520d252473225ac19d6b6289.research_question: Can conditional guidance techniques be effectively integrated into flow-based generative models to improve sample quality and computational efficiency across a variety of conditional generative modeling and decision-making tasks, including image synthesis, text-to-speech, and offline reinforcement learning?
b1d77c7921bcd79f520d252473225ac19d6b6289.hypothesis: Integrating classifier-free guidance into flow-based generative models will significantly enhance conditional sample quality and planning performance, while also providing substantial computational efficiency gains compared to diffusion-based approaches.
b1d77c7921bcd79f520d252473225ac19d6b6289.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed that adapts classifier-free guidance (CFG) to flow matching models, specifically continuous normalizing flows (CNFs) trained via vector field regression. The method introduces 'Guided Flows', where the conditional velocity field is constructed as a convex combination of unconditional and conditional velocity fields, parameterized by a guidance weight. The velocity field is trained using a Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) loss, where with a certain probability, the model is trained on either the true condition or a null condition. Sampling is performed by numerically integrating the guided velocity field ODE using an ODE solver, with the guidance weight controlling the emphasis on conditional information. The approach is instantiated for both optimal transport and cosine-scheduled Gaussian paths, and is applied to a variety of data modalities and tasks.
b1d77c7921bcd79f520d252473225ac19d6b6289.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on three main tasks: conditional image generation (using downsampled 64x64 ImageNet), zero-shot text-to-speech synthesis (using 60K hours of ASR-transcribed English audiobooks), and return-conditioned plan generation in offline reinforcement learning (using D4RL benchmark datasets for Hopper, Walker, and HalfCheetah). Baselines include diffusion models (DDPM and DDIM) with classifier-free guidance, and Decision Diffuser for RL. Evaluation metrics include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for image generation, word error rate (WER) for TTS, and normalized return for RL tasks. The same U-Net architecture and comparable hyperparameters are used across models for fair comparison. Ablations are performed on guidance weights and number of ODE/diffusion steps to assess sample quality and computational efficiency. Multiple random seeds and evaluation episodes are used for statistical robustness.
b1d77c7921bcd79f520d252473225ac19d6b6289.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to integrate classifier-free guidance into flow matching models for conditional generative modeling. It extends the applicability of flow-based models to conditional tasks previously dominated by diffusion models, including plan generation in offline RL. The approach demonstrates state-of-the-art sample quality in image and speech generation, and achieves a 10x speedup over diffusion models in offline RL while maintaining comparable performance. Theoretical justification is provided for the guided velocity field, and empirical results highlight both the efficacy and efficiency of the method across diverse domains.

b1fbbf3b4017575fd2ff46430770b266a90fc4b7.title: Tree-Sliced Wasserstein Distance: A Geometric Perspective
b1fbbf3b4017575fd2ff46430770b266a90fc4b7.research_question: How can the geometric and topological limitations of Sliced Wasserstein (SW) distance, which relies on one-dimensional projections, be addressed to enable more expressive and efficient comparison of probability measures in high-dimensional spaces?
b1fbbf3b4017575fd2ff46430770b266a90fc4b7.hypothesis: Replacing one-dimensional projection lines in the SW framework with more intricate, metrizable tree systems will enable the definition of a new metric—Tree-Sliced Wasserstein distance on Systems of Lines (TSW-SL)—that better captures topological and geometric properties of distributions, while maintaining computational efficiency comparable to SW.
b1fbbf3b4017575fd2ff46430770b266a90fc4b7.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that generalizes the projection mechanism in SW by introducing tree systems—collections of lines in high-dimensional space equipped with a tree structure, metrizable by a tree metric. The method will define a Radon Transform on Systems of Lines, parameterized by splitting maps that distribute mass across the tree system, ensuring injectivity and well-posedness. Probability measures will be pushed forward onto these tree systems, and the closed-form solution for optimal transport on tree metrics will be leveraged to compute the Tree-Sliced Wasserstein distance (TSW-SL) between the transformed measures. The approach will use a Monte Carlo sampling scheme to approximate the integral over the space of tree systems, with efficient computation enabled by parallelizable operations such as matrix multiplication and sorting.
b1fbbf3b4017575fd2ff46430770b266a90fc4b7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of tasks where SW is commonly applied, including gradient flows, generative adversarial networks (GANs), and denoising diffusion models. Datasets will include synthetic distributions such as Swiss Roll and 25 Gaussians, as well as high-dimensional Gaussian mixtures, and real-world image datasets like CelebA, STL-10, and CIFAR-10. Baseline comparisons will involve SW and its variants (MaxSW, SWGG, LCVSW), using consistent numbers of projection directions for fairness. Evaluation metrics will include Wasserstein distance reduction over optimization iterations, Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), and Inception Score (IS) for generative models. Experimental setups will control for the number of lines per tree system and the number of sampled tree systems, and ablation studies will assess the impact of these parameters on performance.
b1fbbf3b4017575fd2ff46430770b266a90fc4b7.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the concept of tree systems as a generalization of one-dimensional projection lines, enabling the definition of a new metric space with tree metrics that admit closed-form optimal transport solutions. A novel Radon Transform on Systems of Lines is defined, with proven injectivity, allowing for meaningful and efficient projection of high-dimensional measures onto tree systems. The resulting Tree-Sliced Wasserstein distance (TSW-SL) captures richer topological and geometric information than SW, while retaining similar computational complexity. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior performance in tasks involving complex or high-dimensional distributions, establishing TSW-SL as a more expressive and scalable alternative to traditional SW and its variants.

b2092ea6163c06136b807ce4fc13781d94de1510.title: VideoTree: Adaptive Tree-based Video Representation for LLM Reasoning on Long Videos
b2092ea6163c06136b807ce4fc13781d94de1510.research_question: How can long-form video data be efficiently and effectively represented for large language model (LLM) reasoning, such that query-relevant information is extracted while minimizing redundancy and accommodating the hierarchical structure of video content?
b2092ea6163c06136b807ce4fc13781d94de1510.hypothesis: A training-free, query-adaptive, hierarchical tree-based video representation can significantly improve both the accuracy and efficiency of LLM-based reasoning over long videos by dynamically extracting and organizing query-relevant information in a coarse-to-fine manner.
b2092ea6163c06136b807ce4fc13781d94de1510.proposed_method: The proposed approach constructs a query-adaptive, hierarchical tree structure (VIDEOTREE) to represent long videos for LLM reasoning. The method begins with adaptive breadth expansion, where visual features are extracted from video frames using a pre-trained visual encoder and clustered via K-Means to group semantically similar frames. The centroid of each cluster is selected as a keyframe, which is then captioned using a vision-language model-based captioner. Relevance scores for each caption are assigned by prompting an LLM with the captions and the query, iterating clustering and scoring until sufficient query-relevant clusters are identified. Next, relevance-guided depth expansion is performed, where clusters with high or moderate relevance are recursively sub-clustered to capture finer-grained, query-specific details, forming a hierarchical tree structure. The final tree is traversed to generate a temporally ordered, text-based video description, which is then provided to the LLM for reasoning and answering the input query.
b2092ea6163c06136b807ce4fc13781d94de1510.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three long-form video question answering benchmarks: EgoSchema (5K QA pairs, 250 hours of video), NExT-QA (5,440 videos, ~52K questions, average 44s per video), and the long split of Video-MME (average 44 minutes per video). The evaluation will use standard multiple-choice QA accuracy as the primary metric. Baselines will include training-free methods (e.g., LLoVi, VideoAgent), open-source and proprietary multimodal LLMs (e.g., GPT-4V, LVNet, InternVL2), and methods using various visual encoders and captioners. The experimental setup will control for captioner and LLM choice, and efficiency will be measured via inference time and number of LLM calls. Ablation studies will examine the impact of tree components, number of captions, and open-source LLMs.
b2092ea6163c06136b807ce4fc13781d94de1510.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a training-free, query-adaptive, hierarchical tree-based video representation that dynamically allocates more keyframes to query-relevant regions and fewer to irrelevant ones, leveraging both coarse and fine-grained video structure. Unlike prior approaches that treat videos as unstructured lists of captions, this method explicitly models the hierarchical and semantic structure of video content, enabling efficient and effective extraction of query-relevant details. The approach improves both reasoning accuracy and inference efficiency, outperforms existing training-free methods and several proprietary/open-source MLLMs on multiple benchmarks, and enhances interpretability by providing human-readable tree structures highlighting key visual cues for LLM reasoning.

b24e899ec0f77eef2fc87a9b8e50516367aa1f97.title: VMamba: Visual State Space Model
b24e899ec0f77eef2fc87a9b8e50516367aa1f97.research_question: How can a vision backbone be designed to achieve computational efficiency and scalability for visual representation learning, while maintaining or improving performance across a variety of visual perception tasks such as image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation?
b24e899ec0f77eef2fc87a9b8e50516367aa1f97.hypothesis: Integrating state space models with a novel two-dimensional selective scan mechanism into a vision backbone will enable linear time complexity, improved scalability with input size, and superior performance on visual tasks compared to existing convolutional, transformer, and SSM-based architectures.
b24e899ec0f77eef2fc87a9b8e50516367aa1f97.proposed_method: A new family of vision backbone architectures, termed VMamba, will be developed by adapting state space models (SSMs) for visual data. The core innovation is the Visual State-Space (VSS) block, which incorporates a 2D-Selective-Scan (SS2D) module. SS2D unfolds input image patches along four distinct spatial traversal paths (cross-scan), processes each sequence in parallel using selective SSM (S6) blocks, and merges the results to form a 2D feature map (cross-merge). The architecture eliminates the need for additional positional embeddings and employs hierarchical representations with down-sampling stages. Architectural and implementation optimizations, such as efficient kernel implementations, removal of redundant branches, and parameter tuning, will be applied to maximize inference speed and memory efficiency.
b24e899ec0f77eef2fc87a9b8e50516367aa1f97.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard benchmarks including ImageNet-1K for image classification, MS COCO for object detection and instance segmentation, and ADE20K for semantic segmentation. The VMamba models (Tiny, Small, Base) will be compared against state-of-the-art CNNs (e.g., ConvNeXt), Vision Transformers (e.g., Swin, HiViT), and SSM-based models (e.g., S4ND, Vim). Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy for classification, mean Average Precision (mAP) for detection and segmentation, mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) for semantic segmentation, throughput (images/sec), FLOPs, and memory usage. Experiments will also analyze scalability with input resolution, effective receptive fields, and ablations on scanning patterns and architectural components. All experiments will be run on high-performance GPU servers, following established protocols for fair comparison.
b24e899ec0f77eef2fc87a9b8e50516367aa1f97.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first vision backbone that adapts selective state space models with a novel 2D-Selective-Scan mechanism, enabling linear computational complexity for 2D visual data. The SS2D module bridges the gap between 1D sequential scanning and 2D spatial traversal, allowing efficient global context aggregation without quadratic complexity. The VMamba family demonstrates superior input scaling efficiency, high throughput, and state-of-the-art performance across multiple visual tasks. Architectural and implementation refinements further enhance practical deployment, and the approach generalizes well to various downstream tasks and input resolutions.

b256751e6abcc595f7500f3cc0e8c1f225af7837.title: Programming Every Example: Lifting Pre-training Data Quality like Experts at Scale
b256751e6abcc595f7500f3cc0e8c1f225af7837.research_question: How can the quality of large-scale pre-training corpora for language models be improved efficiently and flexibly, at the level of individual examples, to enhance downstream model performance and training efficiency across general and domain-specific tasks?
b256751e6abcc595f7500f3cc0e8c1f225af7837.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that treating data refinement as a programmable task, executed by language models generating fine-grained operations for each example, will yield higher-quality pre-training corpora than traditional rule-based or selection methods, resulting in improved downstream task performance and greater pre-training efficiency.
b256751e6abcc595f7500f3cc0e8c1f225af7837.proposed_method: A novel framework, Programming Every Example (PROX), will be developed to automate data refinement for pre-training corpora using small language models. The approach involves two main stages: (1) document-level programming, where the model decides whether to keep or drop entire documents, and (2) chunk-level programming, where the model generates fine-grained operations such as line removal and string normalization for document segments. The method leverages a small, fine-tuned language model to generate Pythonic function calls representing these operations for each example. These generated programs are then executed by a dedicated executor to produce a refined, high-quality corpus. The model adaptation process involves supervised fine-tuning on seed data annotated by a strong LLM, enabling the refining model to learn to generate appropriate operations for a wide range of noisy patterns and content types.
b256751e6abcc595f7500f3cc0e8c1f225af7837.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of large-scale pre-training corpora, including RedPajama-V2, C4, FineWeb, FineWeb-Edu, DCLM, and the domain-specific OpenWebMath dataset. Multiple model sizes (from 0.3B to 1.7B parameters) will be evaluated, both as refining models and as base models for pre-training on the curated data. Baselines will include standard rule-based filtering pipelines (such as Gopher, C4, and FineWeb rules), as well as state-of-the-art data selection methods (e.g., DSIR, DsDm, MATES, QuRating). Evaluation will be performed on a suite of downstream benchmarks (e.g., ARC, MMLU, HellaSwag, PIQA, SIQA, WinoGrande, SciQ) using zero-shot and few-shot accuracy, as well as on mathematical reasoning tasks for domain-specific continual pre-training. The experimental setup will control for training steps and batch size across methods, and will analyze both downstream performance and computational efficiency (FLOPs) required for data refinement and pre-training.
b256751e6abcc595f7500f3cc0e8c1f225af7837.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the concept of treating data refinement as a programmable task at the example level, leveraging small language models to autonomously generate and execute fine-grained operations for corpus cleaning. This approach unifies and generalizes rule-based heuristics into a flexible, scalable program space, enabling systematic and individualized data quality improvements at scale. The method is claimed to outperform both rule-based and model-based data selection baselines in downstream tasks, while also significantly reducing the computational cost of pre-training by enabling similar or better performance with far fewer training tokens and FLOPs. The framework is broadly applicable across model sizes, corpora, and domains, and is designed for reproducibility and extensibility.

b272513916b45c8517d289d7abee4a53e6832187.title: ToRA: A Tool-Integrated Reasoning Agent for Mathematical Problem Solving
b272513916b45c8517d289d7abee4a53e6832187.research_question: How can mathematical problem-solving performance be improved in large language models by integrating natural language reasoning with external computational tools, and what are the benefits and challenges of such integration across diverse mathematical domains?
b272513916b45c8517d289d7abee4a53e6832187.hypothesis: Integrating natural language reasoning with program-based external tool usage in large language models will significantly enhance mathematical problem-solving accuracy and generalization, surpassing both rationale-only and program-only approaches.
b272513916b45c8517d289d7abee4a53e6832187.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that interleaves natural language rationales with program-based external tool usage for mathematical reasoning. The approach involves designing an interactive reasoning format where the model alternates between generating step-by-step rationales and invoking external tools (such as computation libraries and symbolic solvers) via code execution. To train the model, a corpus of tool-integrated reasoning trajectories will be curated using high-quality synthetic annotations generated by prompting advanced language models on established mathematical datasets. Imitation learning will be applied to this corpus to fine-tune large language models, followed by output space shaping, which augments training with diverse valid and corrected trajectories to encourage flexible and robust reasoning. The final system will be capable of multi-round interaction, dynamically deciding when to use natural language or external tools until the problem is solved.
b272513916b45c8517d289d7abee4a53e6832187.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 10 mathematical reasoning datasets, including GSM8k, MATH, GSM-Hard, SVAMP, ASDIV, TabMWP, SingleEQ, SingleOP, AddSub, and MultiArith, covering a range of mathematical domains and difficulty levels. The proposed models will be evaluated against both proprietary (e.g., GPT-4, ChatGPT, PaLM-2, Claude-2) and open-source baselines (e.g., LLaMA-2, WizardMath, CodeLLaMA, Platypus-2, Toolformer), using accuracy of predicted answers as the primary metric. Training will utilize the TORA-CORPUS dataset (curated tool-integrated trajectories) and additional augmented samples generated via output space shaping. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the interleaved reasoning format and output space shaping strategies. Implementation will involve fine-tuning LLaMA-2 and CodeLLaMA models (7B-70B parameters) with a consistent training pipeline, and evaluation will use greedy decoding with a maximum of three tool executions per problem.
b272513916b45c8517d289d7abee4a53e6832187.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first open-source framework that synergistically interleaves natural language rationales with program-based tool usage for mathematical reasoning, enabling models to dynamically leverage both semantic analysis and precise computation. The curated TORA-CORPUS dataset uniquely combines natural language and code-based tool interactions, providing high-quality training data for this paradigm. Output space shaping is proposed as a novel training strategy to enhance reasoning diversity and correct tool-use errors, resulting in significant performance gains. The approach achieves substantial improvements over prior state-of-the-art open-source models across all tested mathematical benchmarks, and for the first time, enables open-source models to exceed 50% accuracy on competition-level MATH tasks, rivaling proprietary systems like GPT-4.

b27861ed8189cda048b7f48e00430b4059098ece.title: Sampling-Based Accuracy Testing of Posterior Estimators for General Inference
b27861ed8189cda048b7f48e00430b4059098ece.research_question: How can the accuracy of posterior estimators, particularly those based on generative models or simulation-based inference, be effectively and reliably tested using only samples, especially in high-dimensional or likelihood-free settings where explicit posterior evaluations are unavailable?
b27861ed8189cda048b7f48e00430b4059098ece.hypothesis: A sampling-based coverage testing method that leverages random reference points and credible regions can provide a necessary and sufficient diagnostic for the accuracy of posterior estimators, outperforming existing coverage-based methods in generality and applicability.
b27861ed8189cda048b7f48e00430b4059098ece.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed for accuracy testing of posterior estimators using only samples from the true joint distribution and the estimated posterior. The method, named Tests of Accuracy with Random Points (TARP), constructs credible regions around randomly chosen reference points in parameter space, using a specified distance metric. For each simulation, posterior samples are generated, and the fraction of samples within a ball centered at the reference point and extending to the true parameter value is computed. This statistic is aggregated across simulations and reference points to estimate the expected coverage probability. The approach is proven to be both necessary and sufficient for verifying posterior accuracy, as it tests coverage for all possible ways of positioning credible regions, and does not require explicit posterior density evaluations.
b27861ed8189cda048b7f48e00430b4059098ece.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a variety of synthetic and realistic inference tasks. Synthetic experiments include a Gaussian toy model with various cases (correct, overconfident, underconfident, and biased estimators), where true posteriors are known and both HPD and TARP coverage are compared. The method is also tested on high-dimensional gravitational lensing source reconstruction, where posterior samples are generated via diffusion models and explicit posterior evaluation is intractable. Datasets consist of simulated parameter-observation pairs, and evaluation metrics include expected coverage probability versus credibility level. Baselines include standard HPD coverage tests and other coverage-based diagnostics, with careful analysis of the impact of reference point distributions and distance metrics.
b27861ed8189cda048b7f48e00430b4059098ece.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a sampling-based coverage test that is both necessary and sufficient for verifying the accuracy of posterior estimators, even when explicit posterior evaluations are unavailable. Unlike existing coverage-based methods, TARP applies to high-dimensional spaces, generative models (e.g., GANs, diffusion models), and simulation-based inference scenarios. The approach can detect biases and inaccuracies that standard HPD coverage tests may miss, and is robust to the choice of reference point distribution and distance metric. This represents a significant advance in the validation of posterior inference methods, particularly for modern machine learning-based estimators.

b27d4a4b6795f80886c436fdaec4fa0d9415707c.title: Automatic differentiation of nonsmooth iterative algorithms
b27d4a4b6795f80886c436fdaec4fa0d9415707c.research_question: How can automatic differentiation be rigorously and effectively applied to nonsmooth iterative algorithms, and what are the theoretical and practical implications for differentiable programming and machine learning?
b27d4a4b6795f80886c436fdaec4fa0d9415707c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, under appropriate nonexpansivity or contraction conditions, a well-defined limiting object exists for nonsmooth automatic differentiation of iterative algorithms, which can be characterized within the framework of conservative derivatives and can provide meaningful and convergent derivatives for the fixed points of such algorithms.
b27d4a4b6795f80886c436fdaec4fa0d9415707c.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed for the automatic differentiation (AD) of nonsmooth iterative algorithms by leveraging the concept of conservative Jacobians, which generalize classical derivatives to nonsmooth settings. The approach will analyze the asymptotic behavior of 'piggyback' derivative recursions—where derivatives are propagated alongside iterates—when the underlying mapping is locally Lipschitz and path-differentiable, but possibly nonsmooth. The method will rigorously characterize the attractor set of these nonsmooth piggyback iterations as a set-valued fixed point, using tools from variational analysis and fixed-point theory. The framework will also establish conditions for almost everywhere convergence of classical derivatives and provide quantitative convergence rates for a broad class of functions, such as those with Lipschitz gradient selection structures. The methodology will be instantiated for several classes of iterative solvers, including proximal splitting algorithms (forward-backward, Douglas-Rachford, ADMM) and momentum methods (e.g., Heavy-Ball), with explicit construction of the required conservative Jacobians.
b27d4a4b6795f80886c436fdaec4fa0d9415707c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of parametric convex optimization problems, including Ridge regression, Lasso, sparse inverse covariance selection, and trend filtering. For each scenario, iterative solvers such as forward-backward splitting, Douglas-Rachford, and ADMM will be implemented, and both the convergence of iterates and the convergence of their piggyback derivatives (Jacobian sequences) will be empirically evaluated. The experiments will utilize synthetic datasets with random initialization, repeated multiple times (e.g., 100 repetitions) to assess robustness, and will report statistics such as medians and deciles. Evaluation metrics will include the distance of iterates to the fixed point and the distance of piggyback Jacobians to the Jacobian of the fixed point, measured over iterations. Comparisons will be made between different algorithms and between smooth and nonsmooth cases, with additional investigation of failure modes (e.g., divergence of derivatives in the Heavy-Ball method) to validate theoretical predictions.
b27d4a4b6795f80886c436fdaec4fa0d9415707c.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a rigorous, general framework for automatic differentiation of nonsmooth iterative algorithms, providing a set-valued fixed-point characterization of limiting derivatives via conservative Jacobians. It establishes, for the first time, convergence guarantees and linear convergence rates for piggyback derivatives in a broad class of nonsmooth settings, including semialgebraic and piecewise smooth functions. The approach unifies and extends prior results by connecting nonsmooth AD to variational analysis and fixed-point theory, and demonstrates applicability to widely used optimization algorithms in machine learning. Additionally, the research identifies and explains failure modes of AD in certain momentum methods, highlighting the boundaries of the proposed theory.

b2961394ecb6051ffe1847fcc9e5eb7685d3ec6d.title: Inverse Reinforcement Learning without Reinforcement Learning
b2961394ecb6051ffe1847fcc9e5eb7685d3ec6d.research_question: How can the sample and computational efficiency of inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) be improved by leveraging expert state visitation distributions, and what are the theoretical and practical implications of such approaches for imitation learning tasks?
b2961394ecb6051ffe1847fcc9e5eb7685d3ec6d.hypothesis: Access to the expert's state visitation distribution can be used to design IRL algorithms that avoid the global exploration problem inherent in traditional RL-based IRL, leading to exponential improvements in sample and computational efficiency while maintaining or improving policy performance relative to the expert.
b2961394ecb6051ffe1847fcc9e5eb7685d3ec6d.proposed_method: A novel framework for IRL is proposed that utilizes expert resets, i.e., resetting the learner to states sampled from the expert's visitation distribution, to alleviate the global exploration burden in policy optimization. Two main algorithms are introduced: MMDP (Moment Matching by Dynamic Programming), which computes a sequence of policies backwards in time using dynamic programming and moment-matching games at each timestep; and NRMM (No-Regret Moment Matching), which learns a single stationary policy by sampling random timesteps and states from the expert distribution and performing no-regret policy improvement. Both methods are formulated in primal and dual variants, and can be combined in a meta-algorithm called FILTER (Fast Inverted Loop Training via Expert Resets), which interpolates between traditional IRL and the proposed expert-reset methods by mixing expert resets with standard environment resets. The methodology is general and can be applied to a variety of IRL algorithms, including those based on adversarial training or moment matching.
b2961394ecb6051ffe1847fcc9e5eb7685d3ec6d.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on continuous control tasks from the PyBullet suite (e.g., HopperBulletEnv-v0, Walker2DBulletEnv-v0, HalfCheetahBulletEnv-v0) and the antmaze-large tasks from the D4RL benchmark. Expert policies are trained using RL and provide 25 demonstration trajectories. To increase task difficulty, a 'tremble' probability is introduced, causing random actions during learner rollouts. Baseline comparisons include behavioral cloning (BC) and a strong moment-matching (MM) IRL baseline with improved GAIL-like architecture, integral probability metric-based discriminators, and advanced policy optimizers (e.g., Soft Actor Critic, TD3+BC). Evaluation metrics focus on policy performance (e.g., interquartile mean of returns) as a function of environment interactions, with results averaged over 10 seeds. The FILTER algorithm is evaluated with different expert reset probabilities (alpha), and performance is compared in terms of both sample efficiency and final policy quality.
b2961394ecb6051ffe1847fcc9e5eb7685d3ec6d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the use of expert resets in IRL, enabling exponential improvements in sample and computational efficiency compared to traditional IRL methods that require repeated RL subroutines. The MMDP and NRMM algorithms are the first to theoretically and empirically demonstrate polynomial-time IRL with strong performance guarantees, avoiding the global exploration problem. The FILTER meta-algorithm provides a principled way to interpolate between quadratic and linear compounding of errors, combining the strengths of both traditional and expert-reset-based IRL. The methods are general, applicable to a broad class of IRL algorithms, and achieve state-of-the-art performance on challenging continuous control and navigation benchmarks without access to reward information.

b298f65455dd4acbbc96e8aa43bd3673af480bcb.title: Object-Centric Slot Diffusion
b298f65455dd4acbbc96e8aa43bd3673af480bcb.research_question: Can diffusion models be effectively integrated into unsupervised object-centric learning frameworks to improve the discovery and compositional generation of objects in complex naturalistic images, without relying on supervised annotations?
b298f65455dd4acbbc96e8aa43bd3673af480bcb.hypothesis: Integrating diffusion models as slot-conditioned decoders within object-centric learning frameworks will significantly enhance object decomposition, compositional image generation, and editing capabilities, especially in complex scenes, compared to existing transformer-based approaches.
b298f65455dd4acbbc96e8aa43bd3673af480bcb.proposed_method: A novel framework, Latent Slot Diffusion (LSD), will be developed that replaces conventional slot decoders with a latent diffusion model conditioned on object-centric slots derived from Slot Attention. The method begins by encoding an input image into a set of slots using a Slot Attention encoder, which partitions the image into compositional entities. A pre-trained auto-encoder compresses the image into a low-dimensional latent space, reducing computational cost while preserving fidelity. The LSD decoder, a slot-conditioned latent diffusion model, reconstructs the image latent by iteratively denoising a noisy latent vector conditioned on the slot representations. The denoising network is implemented as a UNet architecture augmented with slot-conditioned transformers at each layer, allowing the slots to guide the denoising process and thus the image generation. The entire system is trained end-to-end in an unsupervised manner, with the diffusion model maximizing the likelihood of the latent given the slots, and the Slot Attention encoder jointly optimized.
b298f65455dd4acbbc96e8aa43bd3673af480bcb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on five datasets: CLEVR, CLEVRTex, MOVi-C, MOVi-E (synthetic multi-object scenes of increasing complexity), and FFHQ (high-resolution face images). Evaluation tasks include unsupervised object segmentation (using metrics such as mean Best Overlap (mBO), mean Intersection over Union (mIoU), and Foreground Adjusted Rand Index (FG-ARI)), downstream property prediction (accuracy for discrete properties, MSE for continuous properties), compositional image generation (measured by FID scores), and slot-based image editing. Baselines for comparison are SLATE (state-of-the-art transformer-based object-centric model) and SLATE+ (a variant using a pre-trained VQGAN auto-encoder). All models utilize the same pre-trained auto-encoder for fair comparison. Additional experiments will investigate the use of pre-trained diffusion models (e.g., Stable Diffusion) for real-world object-centric learning and conditional generation.
b298f65455dd4acbbc96e8aa43bd3673af480bcb.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to integrate diffusion models as slot-conditioned decoders in unsupervised object-centric learning, enabling compositional conditional generation without supervised annotations such as text. It introduces a new framework for unsupervised compositional diffusion modeling based solely on visual concepts extracted from images. The method demonstrates superior performance over transformer-based decoders, particularly as scene complexity increases, and enables, for the first time, object-centric modeling and editing on challenging datasets like FFHQ. The approach also pioneers the use of pre-trained diffusion models for scalable, real-world object-centric learning and conditional generation.

b29b6315506a0db2cd39cb9faee82c2e8cc0105b.title: Approximating Full Conformal Prediction at Scale via Influence Functions
b29b6315506a0db2cd39cb9faee82c2e8cc0105b.research_question: How can the computational efficiency of full conformal prediction for classification be improved to enable its application to large-scale datasets and complex machine learning models, while retaining its strong statistical guarantees and predictive power?
b29b6315506a0db2cd39cb9faee82c2e8cc0105b.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that influence functions can be used to efficiently approximate the leave-one-out retraining procedure required by full conformal prediction, resulting in a method that is both computationally scalable and statistically consistent with full CP as the training set size increases.
b29b6315506a0db2cd39cb9faee82c2e8cc0105b.proposed_method: A new approach, Approximate full Conformal Prediction (ACP), will be developed to approximate the full conformal prediction (CP) objective for classification tasks. The method will leverage first-order influence functions to efficiently estimate the effect of adding and removing points from the training set, thereby avoiding the need to retrain the underlying machine learning model for each test point and candidate label. Two strategies will be explored: an indirect approach that approximates the model parameters after data perturbation and a direct approach that estimates the change in loss at a point due to data perturbation. The direct approach is conjectured and empirically validated to provide a better approximation. The method will be implemented for models trained via empirical risk minimization (e.g., logistic regression, neural networks), with convex and twice differentiable loss functions, and will include a single training phase to compute the Hessian and gradients, followed by efficient prediction using influence scores.
b29b6315506a0db2cd39cb9faee82c2e8cc0105b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on real-world datasets including MNIST, CIFAR-10, and the US Census dataset, using various underlying models such as logistic regression, multilayer perceptrons (with different architectures), and convolutional neural networks. The proposed ACP method will be compared against mainstream conformal prediction alternatives: Split CP (SCP), Regularized Adaptive Prediction Sets (RAPS), and Cross-validation+ (CV+). Evaluation metrics will include prediction set size (efficiency), area under the curve (AUC) of prediction set size versus significance level, empirical error rate (validity), and fuzziness of p-values. Statistical significance of results will be assessed using appropriate tests. Computational efficiency and scalability will be measured by comparing running times and resource usage between ACP and full CP. Synthetic data experiments will also be performed to analyze approximation error, the effect of regularization, and consistency as the training set size increases.
b29b6315506a0db2cd39cb9faee82c2e8cc0105b.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to efficiently approximate full conformal prediction for complex models such as neural networks using influence functions, providing finite-sample error guarantees and consistency as the training set grows. Unlike prior scalable alternatives, ACP retains the statistical power and validity of full CP while being computationally feasible for large datasets. The direct influence-based approximation is novel and empirically shown to outperform indirect approaches. Theoretical analysis establishes finite-sample bounds and the impact of regularization on approximation quality. The method enables practical application of full CP to real-world, large-scale machine learning problems where previous methods were computationally prohibitive.

b29bebc4e0316e63d37410bdde2718b560030bae.title: C-Mixup: Improving Generalization in Regression
b29bebc4e0316e63d37410bdde2718b560030bae.research_question: How can generalization in regression tasks, including in-distribution, task generalization, and out-of-distribution robustness, be improved through data augmentation techniques that interpolate between training examples?
b29bebc4e0316e63d37410bdde2718b560030bae.hypothesis: Adjusting the sampling probability for mixup data augmentation in regression tasks based on label similarity, rather than uniform or feature-based selection, will improve generalization performance and robustness to distribution shifts.
b29bebc4e0316e63d37410bdde2718b560030bae.proposed_method: A novel data augmentation technique, C-Mixup, will be developed for regression tasks. This method modifies the standard mixup approach by assigning higher probability to mixing pairs of training examples that have more similar continuous labels, rather than sampling pairs uniformly or based on input feature similarity. The sampling probability for each pair is computed using a Gaussian kernel over label distances, ensuring that pairs with closer labels are more likely to be chosen. During training, for each example in a batch, another example is sampled according to this probability distribution, and the two are linearly interpolated in both input and label space using a mixing coefficient drawn from a Beta distribution. The resulting synthetic examples are then used to update the model parameters via standard optimization. This approach is designed to be computationally efficient due to the typically low dimensionality of the label space and is compatible with both standard supervised regression and meta-learning settings.
b29bebc4e0316e63d37410bdde2718b560030bae.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on eleven datasets spanning tabular, time-series, image, and video data, including Airfoil Self-Noise, NO2, Exchange-Rate, Electricity, Echocardiogram Videos, ShapeNet1D, Pascal1D, RCF-MNIST, PovertyMap, Communities and Crime, SkillCraft, and Drug-Target Interaction datasets. Baselines will include empirical risk minimization (ERM), vanilla mixup, manifold mixup, k-Mixup, LocalMixup, MixRL, and several domain generalization methods such as IRM, IB-IRM, V-REx, CORAL, GroupDRO, and Fish. Evaluation metrics will include Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), and Pearson correlation (R), with both average and worst-domain performance reported for domain shift scenarios. Experimental setups will use appropriate neural architectures for each dataset (e.g., fully connected networks, LST-Attn, EchoNet-Dynamic, ResNet-50, DeepDTA) and hyperparameters will be tuned via cross-validation. Additional analyses will examine compatibility with other mixup variants, alternative distance metrics, and sensitivity to the Gaussian kernel bandwidth.
b29bebc4e0316e63d37410bdde2718b560030bae.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a label-similarity-based sampling strategy for mixup in regression, addressing the problem of generating unrealistic or noisy virtual labels when mixing pairs with dissimilar targets. The approach is theoretically justified to improve generalization in supervised and meta-learning regression settings and is empirically validated to outperform existing mixup variants and domain generalization methods on a wide range of datasets. C-Mixup is computationally efficient, compatible with existing mixup variants, and does not require domain annotations, making it broadly applicable for improving both in-distribution and out-of-distribution performance in regression tasks.

b2c68b708a9f98996b18c8d21b53a815a2c46a8b.title: ProPILE: Probing Privacy Leakage in Large Language Models
b2c68b708a9f98996b18c8d21b53a815a2c46a8b.research_question: How can the risk and extent of personally identifiable information (PII) leakage in large language models (LLMs) be effectively probed and quantified by both data subjects and LLM service providers, considering both black-box and white-box access scenarios?
b2c68b708a9f98996b18c8d21b53a815a2c46a8b.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that effective probing techniques, leveraging both black-box and white-box access, can reveal significant risks of PII leakage in LLMs, and that prompt engineering (including soft prompt tuning) can amplify the ability to detect such leakage.
b2c68b708a9f98996b18c8d21b53a815a2c46a8b.proposed_method: A comprehensive probing framework, ProPILE, will be developed to assess PII leakage in LLMs. The framework will include two main probing strategies: (1) Black-box probing, where data subjects use hand-crafted prompts based on their own PII to query LLMs and evaluate the likelihood of PII leakage, and (2) White-box probing, where LLM service providers leverage access to training data and model parameters to optimize prompts via soft prompt tuning, maximizing the likelihood of PII reconstruction. The methodology will formalize the concepts of 'linkability' (the association of PII with its owner in context) and 'structurality' (the degree to which PII follows recognizable patterns), and will quantify leakage using both string match and likelihood-based metrics. The approach will support both structured (e.g., phone numbers, addresses) and unstructured (e.g., affiliations, family relationships) PII types.
b2c68b708a9f98996b18c8d21b53a815a2c46a8b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the OPT-1.3B language model, trained on the publicly available Pile dataset. The evaluation dataset will consist of structured PII quadruplets (name, phone number, email, address) for 10,000 data subjects, name-family relationship pairs for 10,000 subjects, and name-university pairs for 2,000 subjects, extracted using regular expressions, named entity recognition, and QA models. Black-box probing will utilize multiple prompt templates and beam search decoding, comparing the likelihood and exact match rates of target PII against randomly selected PII. White-box probing will involve soft prompt tuning using subsets of the training data, varying the number of soft tokens and initialization methods, and measuring the impact on leakage likelihood and exact match rates. Transferability of soft prompts across different model sizes will also be evaluated. Baselines will include random PII likelihoods and standard prompt-based querying. Evaluation metrics will include reconstruction likelihood, exact string match rates, and the γ<k metric indicating the fraction of subjects whose PII can be reconstructed within k queries.
b2c68b708a9f98996b18c8d21b53a815a2c46a8b.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a dual-access probing tool that empowers both data subjects and LLM service providers to assess PII leakage risks in deployed LLMs. The approach is novel in its formalization of linkability and structurality for PII leakage analysis, its support for both structured and unstructured PII, and its integration of black-box and white-box probing strategies, including the use of soft prompt tuning to amplify leakage detection. The methodology enables practical, scalable, and transferable probing of privacy risks in real-world LLM deployments, representing a pioneering step toward user empowerment and proactive privacy evaluation.

b2c92011a6f2b49183eb532b99b65e9a7761e0a3.title: PO3AD: Predicting Point Offsets toward Better 3D Point Cloud Anomaly Detection
b2c92011a6f2b49183eb532b99b65e9a7761e0a3.research_question: How can the detection and localization of anomalies in 3D point cloud data be improved under the anomaly-free training setting, given the challenges posed by the disordered and sparse nature of point clouds?
b2c92011a6f2b49183eb532b99b65e9a7761e0a3.hypothesis: Learning to predict point-wise offsets between normal and pseudo-anomalous point clouds, especially when pseudo anomalies are generated in a geometry-aware manner, enables more effective extraction of normal representations and enhances anomaly detection performance compared to traditional reconstruction-based or memory bank methods.
b2c92011a6f2b49183eb532b99b65e9a7761e0a3.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that focuses on predicting point-wise offsets between normal and pseudo-anomalous 3D point clouds to facilitate anomaly detection. The approach utilizes a backbone network (MinkUNet, a voxel-based sparse convolutional neural network) to extract latent features from voxelized point clouds. An offset predictor, implemented as a multi-layer perceptron (MLP), estimates the displacement vectors (offsets) for each point, supervised by a combined L1 loss on offset magnitude and a negative cosine loss on offset direction. Pseudo anomalies are generated using a new augmentation technique, Norm-AS, which moves points in randomly selected patches along or against their surface normal vectors, creating bulge or concavity anomalies that better mimic real-world defects. During inference, the predicted offset magnitudes serve as direct anomaly scores for each point.
b2c92011a6f2b49183eb532b99b65e9a7761e0a3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two benchmark datasets for 3D point cloud anomaly detection: Anomaly-ShapeNet (synthetic, multi-category, with 1,600 samples across 40 categories) and Real3D-AD (real scans, 12 categories, with significant train-test domain gap). The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines including memory bank-based, reconstruction-based, and hybrid methods such as BTF, PatchCore, Reg3D-AD, IMRNet, and R3D-AD. Evaluation will use both object-level and point-level AUC-ROC metrics for detection and localization. The implementation will employ MinkUNet34C as the backbone, a three-layer MLP for offset prediction, and training will use Adam optimizer with cosine annealing. Ablation studies will investigate the impact of loss components and the pseudo anomaly generation strategy. Robustness to noise and sensitivity to patch size will also be evaluated.
b2c92011a6f2b49183eb532b99b65e9a7761e0a3.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first application of point offset prediction for 3D point cloud anomaly detection, shifting the focus from traditional reconstruction to offset learning. A new pseudo anomaly generation technique, Norm-AS, is developed that leverages surface normal vectors to create more realistic and informative pseudo anomalies, improving the training process. The approach enables the model to concentrate on pseudo-abnormal regions, leading to superior extraction of normal representations. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods in both detection and localization tasks, with notable robustness to noise and reduced sensitivity to augmentation hyperparameters.

b3086fbbc678a7616ac390a41945f45e0d0ab001.title: Dataset Inference: Ownership Resolution in Machine Learning
b3086fbbc678a7616ac390a41945f45e0d0ab001.research_question: How can ownership of machine learning models be reliably resolved in the presence of model stealing attacks, by determining whether a suspect model contains private knowledge from an original training dataset?
b3086fbbc678a7616ac390a41945f45e0d0ab001.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that models which have incorporated private knowledge from a victim's training set, either directly or indirectly, will exhibit statistically distinguishable behaviors on that data compared to models trained independently, enabling reliable ownership resolution via dataset inference.
b3086fbbc678a7616ac390a41945f45e0d0ab001.proposed_method: A novel framework for ownership resolution, termed dataset inference (DI), is proposed. This approach leverages the information asymmetry between model owners (who possess the private training data) and adversaries (who may have stolen the model or data). The method involves generating feature embeddings that characterize the 'prediction margin' or confidence of a model's predictions on input data, using either white-box (MinGD) or black-box (Blind Walk) techniques to estimate the distance of data points to the model's decision boundary. These embeddings are used to train a confidence regressor that predicts the likelihood a sample was part of the private training set. Ownership claims are then resolved via statistical hypothesis testing that aggregates confidence scores over multiple samples, ensuring low false positive rates.
b3086fbbc678a7616ac390a41945f45e0d0ab001.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on standard image classification benchmarks including CIFAR10, CIFAR100, SVHN, and ImageNet. The victim model architecture is WideResNet (WRN-28-10), while adversarial models use smaller or varied architectures. Multiple model stealing scenarios are evaluated: model extraction via API queries (logit and label), fine-tuning, data-free distillation, and training from scratch with stolen data. Both white-box and black-box settings are tested, using as few as 10-50 private samples for ownership testing. Evaluation metrics include p-values from hypothesis tests, effect size (difference in mean confidence scores), and false positive rates, with statistical tests repeated 100 times for robustness. Baselines include independent models trained on separate datasets to ensure specificity.
b3086fbbc678a7616ac390a41945f45e0d0ab001.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces dataset inference as a general and robust framework for model ownership resolution that does not require retraining, overfitting, or watermarking of the defended model. It is the first to leverage statistical testing over multiple private samples for ownership claims, and to propose black-box (Blind Walk) and white-box (MinGD) embedding generation methods for this purpose. The method is shown to be effective against state-of-the-art and adaptive model stealing attacks, requiring only a small number of private samples and achieving high confidence in ownership claims. Unlike prior work, it applies post-hoc to any deployed model and is robust to adversarial adaptation.

b30ce57128b672945b3e24f98aee63b2b3881ee0.title: Generative Flows on Discrete State-Spaces: Enabling Multimodal Flows with Applications to Protein Co-Design
b30ce57128b672945b3e24f98aee63b2b3881ee0.research_question: How can generative models be extended to jointly model and generate data across discrete and continuous modalities, with a focus on enabling flexible, high-quality multimodal generation for complex scientific domains such as protein structure and sequence co-design?
b30ce57128b672945b3e24f98aee63b2b3881ee0.hypothesis: A flow-based generative modeling framework can be constructed for discrete state spaces using continuous-time Markov chains, and when combined with continuous flow models, will enable flexible, high-performance multimodal generation that surpasses existing diffusion-based and unimodal approaches, particularly for protein structure-sequence co-design.
b30ce57128b672945b3e24f98aee63b2b3881ee0.proposed_method: A novel generative modeling framework, Discrete Flow Models (DFMs), will be developed for discrete data by leveraging continuous-time Markov chains (CTMCs) to realize the discrete analogue of continuous flow matching. The method will define a probability flow that linearly interpolates from noise to data, parameterized by a rate matrix derived from the Kolmogorov equation, and will train a denoising neural network using cross-entropy to predict clean data from noisy inputs. DFMs will be integrated with continuous flow-based models to construct a unified multimodal generative model capable of jointly modeling discrete (e.g., amino acid sequence) and continuous (e.g., 3D protein structure) modalities. The multimodal model, termed Multiflow, will factorize conditional flows for each modality and allow for flexible sampling, including conditioning on any subset of modalities, by decoupling the noise schedules and enabling control over CTMC stochasticity at inference time.
b30ce57128b672945b3e24f98aee63b2b3881ee0.experiment_details: Experiments will first validate the discrete generative modeling capabilities of DFMs on character-level text modeling using the text8 dataset, comparing performance against discrete diffusion models (D3PM), Score Entropy Discrete Diffusion (SEDD), and autoregressive baselines, with evaluation metrics including negative log-likelihood (NLL) as measured by a large language model (GPT-J-6B) and sample entropy. The primary application will be protein co-design, where the model will be trained on curated Protein Data Bank (PDB) datasets of protein structures and sequences, with lengths ranging from 60 to 384 residues. Evaluation will use self-consistency metrics such as scRMSD (structure consistency root mean squared deviation) between generated and predicted structures (using ESMFold or AlphaFold2), designability (percentage of samples with scRMSD < 2Å), diversity (number of unique structure clusters via FoldSeek), and novelty (average TM-score to closest PDB protein). Baselines for protein co-design will include RFdiffusion, ProteinGenerator, and Protpardelle, with additional comparisons to ProteinMPNN for sequence design. Experiments will also assess the effects of varying CTMC stochasticity on structural properties and test the model's ability to perform forward/inverse folding and conditional generation tasks.
b30ce57128b672945b3e24f98aee63b2b3881ee0.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the first flow-based generative model for discrete data that is compatible with continuous flow models, enabling true multimodal generation across discrete and continuous state spaces. DFMs generalize and improve upon existing discrete diffusion models by allowing flexible, inference-time control over sample properties and stochasticity, and by decoupling the choice of rate matrix from training. The integration of DFMs with continuous flows in the Multiflow model enables joint, flexible, and state-of-the-art co-generation of protein structure and sequence, surpassing previous methods that rely on separate or sequential models for each modality. The approach also provides a simple, extensible recipe for constructing generative flows on discrete spaces, facilitating new applications in scientific domains requiring multimodal modeling.

b31a5884a8ebe96b6300839b28608b97f8f8ef76.title: LongBench: A Bilingual, Multitask Benchmark for Long Context Understanding
b31a5884a8ebe96b6300839b28608b97f8f8ef76.research_question: How can a comprehensive, bilingual, and multi-task benchmark be developed to rigorously evaluate the long context understanding abilities of large language models (LLMs) across a diverse set of real-world and synthetic tasks in both English and Chinese?
b31a5884a8ebe96b6300839b28608b97f8f8ef76.hypothesis: A standardized, large-scale, multi-task benchmark covering a wide range of long-context tasks and languages will enable more rigorous and holistic evaluation of LLMs' capabilities in long context understanding, revealing strengths, weaknesses, and areas for improvement across models and techniques.
b31a5884a8ebe96b6300839b28608b97f8f8ef76.proposed_method: A novel benchmark, LongBench, will be constructed to evaluate long context understanding in LLMs. The benchmark will include 21 datasets spanning six major task categories: single-document QA, multi-document QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion, with data in both English and Chinese. Each dataset will be standardized into a unified input-output format (input, context, answer), with context lengths averaging thousands of tokens or characters to ensure realistic long-context scenarios. Data will be sourced from existing public datasets, adapted or newly annotated as needed, and will include both naturally occurring and synthetic long-context challenges. Automatic evaluation metrics such as F1, ROUGE-L, classification accuracy, exact match accuracy, and edit similarity will be used for consistent, scalable assessment. Additionally, a variant, LongBench-E, will be created to ensure even distribution of context lengths for fine-grained analysis of model performance as context length increases.
b31a5884a8ebe96b6300839b28608b97f8f8ef76.experiment_details: Experiments will involve evaluating a diverse set of state-of-the-art LLMs with long context capabilities, including both commercial (e.g., GPT-3.5-Turbo-16k) and open-source models (e.g., Llama2-7B-chat-4k, LongChat-v1.5-7B-32k, XGen-7B-8k, InternLM-7B-8k, ChatGLM2-6B, ChatGLM2-6B-32k, Vicuna-v1.5-7B-16k). Each model will be assessed in a zero-shot setting (except for few-shot tasks) using the standardized input format, with truncation strategies applied when context exceeds model limits. Baseline comparisons will include both models with and without specialized long-context training or architectures. Evaluation will use the specified automatic metrics per dataset, and results will be analyzed for overall performance, robustness to increasing context length (using LongBench-E), and the impact of context compression techniques such as retrieval-based and summarization-based compression. Additional experiments will assess the degree to which models rely on memorization versus true context understanding by withholding context and comparing performance.
b31a5884a8ebe96b6300839b28608b97f8f8ef76.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark is the first to provide a bilingual, multi-task, and large-scale evaluation suite specifically tailored for long context understanding in LLMs, covering a broad spectrum of real-world and synthetic tasks in both English and Chinese. LongBench introduces standardized formats and automatic evaluation for scalable, reproducible assessment, and includes both natural and synthetic datasets to test a wide range of long-context reasoning patterns. The benchmark enables nuanced analysis of model capabilities across context lengths and task types, and supports evaluation of context compression techniques. This comprehensive approach fills a critical gap in current LLM evaluation resources, which have previously lacked diversity in task types, languages, and context lengths for long-context scenarios.

b31c2967451722780e92604532e19cdd3f0f49fb.title: MobileNeRF: Exploiting the Polygon Rasterization Pipeline for Efficient Neural Field Rendering on Mobile Architectures
b31c2967451722780e92604532e19cdd3f0f49fb.research_question: How can neural radiance field (NeRF) representations be adapted to enable efficient, high-quality, real-time novel view synthesis on a wide range of mobile and low-power devices using standard graphics hardware?
b31c2967451722780e92604532e19cdd3f0f49fb.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that representing NeRFs as textured polygonal meshes with binary opacities and feature textures, rendered via the standard polygon rasterization pipeline and a lightweight neural shader, will enable interactive frame rates and high-quality view synthesis on mobile and integrated GPU platforms, while significantly reducing memory and computational requirements compared to volumetric NeRF methods.
b31c2967451722780e92604532e19cdd3f0f49fb.proposed_method: A novel approach will be developed that represents a NeRF as a set of textured polygons, where each polygon approximates the scene surface and is associated with a texture atlas storing binary opacity and deep feature vectors. Rendering is performed in two stages: first, the polygonal mesh is rasterized using the classic GPU rasterization pipeline with z-buffering to produce a feature image; second, a small, view-dependent multilayer perceptron (MLP), implemented as a GLSL fragment shader, interprets the per-pixel features and view direction to produce the final RGB color. The method involves a three-stage training pipeline: (1) continuous training of a NeRF-like model with optimizable mesh vertices and MLPs for opacity and features, (2) binarization of opacities using a straight-through estimator and anti-aliasing via feature super-sampling, and (3) discretization into an explicit polygonal mesh with baked textures and a compact neural shader. The approach leverages standard polygon rendering pipelines, enabling compatibility with a broad range of devices and efficient parallelism.
b31c2967451722780e92604532e19cdd3f0f49fb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three benchmark datasets: Synthetic 360° scenes (NeRF), forward-facing scenes (LLFF), and unbounded 360° outdoor scenes (Mip-NeRF360). The method will be evaluated on a variety of devices, including mobile phones, tablets, Chromebooks, and desktop GPUs, using web-based viewers to ensure broad compatibility. Baselines will include SNeRG (the only prior NeRF variant shown to run on low-power devices), as well as comparisons to original NeRF and JAXNeRF where applicable. Evaluation metrics will include rendering speed (frames per second), GPU memory consumption, disk storage requirements, and image quality metrics such as PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS. Ablation studies will assess the impact of mesh optimization, texture resolution, anti-aliasing, and the neural shader. The rendering resolution will match the training images for each dataset, and both qualitative and quantitative results will be reported.
b31c2967451722780e92604532e19cdd3f0f49fb.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new NeRF representation based on textured polygons with binary opacities and feature textures, enabling efficient rendering via standard polygon rasterization pipelines. This approach achieves an order of magnitude speedup over the state-of-the-art (SNeRG) while maintaining comparable image quality, and reduces memory usage by storing surface textures instead of volumetric textures. The method is compatible with a wide range of devices, including mobile phones and web browsers, and supports real-time manipulation and editing of reconstructed scenes. The framework does not require reconstructed 3D geometry as input and is the first to demonstrate interactive NeRF rendering on commodity mobile hardware using only standard graphics APIs.

b32a6f6ef7dd775e0f876b4713ceccebc56e651e.title: A systematic evaluation of large language models of code
b32a6f6ef7dd775e0f876b4713ceccebc56e651e.research_question: How do large language models trained on code perform across various programming languages, and what are the effects of model architecture, training data composition, and scale on their ability to model and generate code? Additionally, can a large open-source language model trained exclusively on a multilingual code corpus match or surpass the performance of proprietary models in specific programming languages?
b32a6f6ef7dd775e0f876b4713ceccebc56e651e.hypothesis: Large language models trained exclusively on a diverse, multilingual corpus of code will achieve competitive or superior performance compared to existing open-source and proprietary models, particularly in programming languages that are well-represented in the training data. Furthermore, training on a mixture of programming languages may enable better generalization and transfer across languages.
b32a6f6ef7dd775e0f876b4713ceccebc56e651e.proposed_method: A systematic evaluation will be conducted by training a family of large-scale language models, termed PolyCoder, using the GPT-2 architecture with varying parameter sizes (160M, 400M, 2.7B). The models will be trained from scratch on a curated and deduplicated dataset comprising 249GB of code from 12 programming languages, sourced from popular GitHub repositories. Data preprocessing will include filtering out files that are too large or too small, deduplication via content hashing, and training a custom GPT-2 tokenizer on a representative subset of the multilingual corpus. The training will be performed using the GPT-NeoX toolkit, optimizing hyperparameters such as learning rate, batch size, and context window size to balance computational constraints and model capacity. The approach will also include a comparative analysis of existing open-source models (GPT-Neo, GPT-J, GPT-NeoX, CodeParrot) and the proprietary Codex model, focusing on differences in training data, architecture, and scale.
b32a6f6ef7dd775e0f876b4713ceccebc56e651e.experiment_details: Experiments will include both extrinsic and intrinsic evaluations. For extrinsic evaluation, all models will be assessed on the HumanEval benchmark, which requires code generation from natural language prompts and tests functional correctness using pass@k metrics (pass@1, pass@10, pass@100). Sampling strategies will include varying softmax temperatures and nucleus sampling (top-p=0.95), with 100 samples per prompt. For intrinsic evaluation, model perplexity will be measured on an unseen set of 100 randomly sampled files per language from 12 programming languages, ensuring no overlap with training data for open-source models. Baselines will include Codex (via API), GPT-Neo, GPT-J, GPT-NeoX, and CodeParrot, with evaluation metrics normalized for tokenization differences using Pygments. Key experimental setup details include training PolyCoder models on a single machine with 8 Nvidia RTX 8000 GPUs, training up to 150K steps, and comparing results across model sizes and training regimes.
b32a6f6ef7dd775e0f876b4713ceccebc56e651e.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first large-scale, open-source language model trained exclusively on a multilingual corpus of code spanning 12 programming languages. It provides a comprehensive, systematic evaluation of both proprietary and open-source code language models across multiple languages and tasks. The research aims to fill a critical gap by releasing models and datasets that democratize access to large code language models, enabling further research and application. Notably, the approach investigates the effects of multilingual code pretraining and model scaling, and demonstrates that the proposed PolyCoder model can outperform proprietary models such as Codex in specific languages (e.g., C), offering new insights into cross-language transfer and training data design.

b333bfd817d1eca166bc8c07568cf0f8f1c93cc3.title: COLA: Consistent Learning with Opponent-Learning Awareness
b333bfd817d1eca166bc8c07568cf0f8f1c93cc3.research_question: How can multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithms achieve stable and socially desirable outcomes in general-sum games, particularly by addressing the limitations of opponent-shaping methods such as Learning with Opponent-Learning Awareness (LOLA)?
b333bfd817d1eca166bc8c07568cf0f8f1c93cc3.hypothesis: Consistent update functions under mutual opponent shaping can be learned efficiently and robustly, leading to improved convergence and more prosocial solutions in general-sum games, even when higher-order LOLA fails to converge.
b333bfd817d1eca166bc8c07568cf0f8f1c93cc3.proposed_method: A new approach, Consistent LOLA (COLA), is proposed to learn a pair of update functions for agents in differentiable games by explicitly minimizing a differentiable consistency loss inspired by a formal definition of mutual opponent-shaping consistency. The method parameterizes the agents' update functions as neural networks and uses gradient-based optimization to minimize the difference between the left- and right-hand sides of the consistency equations over a region of interest in the parameter space. This reframing requires at most second-order derivatives and avoids the need for recursive computation of higher-order LOLA updates. The consistency loss is computed as the norm of the difference between the proposed update and the ideal consistent update, and the neural network parameters are optimized to minimize this loss across sampled parameter pairs.
b333bfd817d1eca166bc8c07568cf0f8f1c93cc3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of general-sum games, including polynomial games such as the Tandem game, Hamiltonian game, and Balduzzi game, as well as non-polynomial games like Matching Pennies, the Ultimatum game, and the Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma (IPD). The experimental setup involves training COLA update functions and comparing their performance to baselines including LOLA, higher-order LOLA (HOLA), Stable Opponent Shaping (SOS), and Competitive Gradient Descent (CGD). Evaluation metrics include consistency loss, convergence behavior, cosine similarity between update functions, and the quality of the learned solutions (e.g., whether they are prosocial or Pareto-optimal).
