b47507f12a8b7d26f78a484e32a08d61d3f87358.research_question: How can the reasoning abilities of large language models (LLMs) be rigorously evaluated when facts required for reasoning are distributed across extremely long natural language contexts, and what are the limitations of current models in utilizing extended context lengths for complex reasoning tasks?
b47507f12a8b7d26f78a484e32a08d61d3f87358.hypothesis: Current large language models are limited in their ability to effectively utilize long input contexts for complex reasoning tasks, and their performance degrades as context length and reasoning complexity increase. Fine-tuned recurrent memory architectures may overcome these limitations and enable efficient reasoning over extremely long sequences.
b47507f12a8b7d26f78a484e32a08d61d3f87358.proposed_method: A scalable and extensible benchmark, BABILong, will be developed to evaluate LLMs on their ability to reason over facts distributed within arbitrarily long natural language documents. The benchmark will comprise 20 diverse reasoning tasks, such as fact chaining, induction, deduction, counting, and list/set handling, with relevant facts 'hidden' among distractor sentences sampled from large corpora like PG19. Tasks will be generated by interleaving task-relevant facts with background text to create samples of varying and unprecedented lengths, up to tens of millions of tokens. The evaluation framework will allow for the assessment of both pre-trained and fine-tuned models, including retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) approaches and recurrent memory transformer architectures, under controlled and reproducible conditions.
b47507f12a8b7d26f78a484e32a08d61d3f87358.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the BABILong benchmark, with datasets constructed by embedding task-relevant facts from the bAbI suite into background text from the PG19 corpus, creating evaluation splits up to 10 million tokens and testing up to 50 million tokens for select models. Over 30 recent LLMs of various sizes and architectures will be evaluated, including open-source models (e.g., LLama-3.1, Qwen-2.5, Mistral, Phi-3), proprietary models (e.g., GPT-4, Gemini 1.5 Pro), RAG pipelines, and recurrent memory models (RMT, ARMT, Mamba). Baselines will include both zero-shot and fine-tuned models, as well as RAG with chunk and sentence retrieval. Evaluation metrics will focus on accuracy for each reasoning task, with detailed analysis of context utilization, performance degradation with context length, and comparison to other benchmarks such as MMLU and RULER. Fine-tuning experiments will be performed on select models using curriculum learning strategies and task-specific data.
b47507f12a8b7d26f78a484e32a08d61d3f87358.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces a scalable, generative, and multi-task evaluation framework for long-context reasoning, supporting document lengths up to and beyond 10 million tokens. BABILong provides a more challenging and representative assessment of LLMs' abilities than prior 'needle-in-a-haystack' or synthetic benchmarks by embedding diverse reasoning tasks within natural, distractor-rich contexts. The benchmark is designed to be immune to data leakage and adaptable to future models with even larger context windows. Experiments will demonstrate, for the first time, that recurrent memory transformer architectures can process and reason over input sequences up to 50 million tokens, setting a new record for sequence length handled by a single model. The work will also provide comprehensive insights into the limitations of current LLMs and RAG methods in long-context reasoning, establishing BABILong as a critical resource for the development and evaluation of next-generation language models.

b47812325fd9493eb8d5dbf1deb7ad4a763ebe65.title: Looking Inward: Language Models Can Learn About Themselves by Introspection
b47812325fd9493eb8d5dbf1deb7ad4a763ebe65.research_question: Can large language models (LLMs) acquire knowledge about their own internal states or behavioral tendencies that is not contained in or derivable from their training data, and can this introspective capability be systematically measured and enhanced?
b47812325fd9493eb8d5dbf1deb7ad4a763ebe65.hypothesis: LLMs can develop introspective abilities that allow them to predict properties of their own behavior in hypothetical scenarios more accurately than other models, even when those other models are trained on the same behavioral data.
b47812325fd9493eb8d5dbf1deb7ad4a763ebe65.proposed_method: A framework will be developed to measure introspection in LLMs by finetuning models to answer hypothetical questions about properties of their own outputs (self-prediction), such as predicting whether their response to a prompt would be even or odd, or identifying the ethical stance of their likely answer. The approach involves generating ground-truth object-level behaviors for a set of prompts, extracting properties from these outputs, and then training the model to answer hypothetical questions about these properties. To rigorously test introspective access, a second, distinct model will be trained (cross-prediction) on the same behavioral data to predict the first model’s responses. Further, the introspective model will be subjected to behavioral modification via additional finetuning, and its ability to update its self-predictions in line with its changed behavior will be evaluated. Chain-of-thought reasoning will be excluded to focus on basic introspective capabilities.
b47812325fd9493eb8d5dbf1deb7ad4a763ebe65.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize a variety of LLMs, including GPT-4, GPT-4o, Llama-3-70B, and GPT-3.5, with finetuning performed using APIs such as Fireworks and OpenAI’s finetuning API. Diverse datasets will be constructed for both training and evaluation, including tasks like Wikipedia completions, animal sequences, and MMLU questions, with behavioral properties such as output character position, ethical stance, and wealth-seeking tendencies. Six datasets will be used for training and six held out for testing to ensure generalization. Baselines will include always predicting the most common behavior. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on held-out datasets, mean absolute deviation (MAD) for calibration, and comparison of self-prediction versus cross-prediction performance. Additional experiments will test the robustness of introspective ability after behavioral modification and examine limitations on tasks requiring longer or more complex outputs.
b47812325fd9493eb8d5dbf1deb7ad4a763ebe65.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a systematic framework for measuring and eliciting introspection in LLMs, including new datasets, finetuning protocols, and evaluation methods. It claims to provide the first direct evidence that LLMs can access privileged information about their own behavioral tendencies not inferable from training data, challenging the view that LLMs merely imitate their training distributions. The approach also demonstrates that introspective ability is robust to behavioral changes induced by finetuning and that self-prediction-trained models are better calibrated than cross-prediction models. Limitations and failure cases are identified, providing a roadmap for future research on model honesty, explainability, and self-awareness.

b488223a9422d43ed8c0e0da04c9c0592eb07829.title: Stochastic collapse: how gradient noise attracts SGD dynamics towards simpler subnetworks
b488223a9422d43ed8c0e0da04c9c0592eb07829.research_question: What are the underlying mechanisms by which stochastic gradient descent (SGD) biases the training dynamics of over-parameterized neural networks towards simpler subnetworks, and how does this implicit bias affect generalization performance and the role of learning rate schedules?
b488223a9422d43ed8c0e0da04c9c0592eb07829.hypothesis: Stochastic gradient noise in SGD induces an implicit bias that attracts the dynamics towards invariant sets in parameter space corresponding to simpler (sparse or low-rank) subnetworks, and this stochastic collapse improves generalization, particularly when large learning rates are maintained for extended periods during early training.
b488223a9422d43ed8c0e0da04c9c0592eb07829.proposed_method: The proposed research will develop a theoretical framework to identify and characterize invariant sets in neural network parameter space, particularly those arising from architectural symmetries such as vanishing and identical neurons. The dynamics of SGD will be analyzed using a stochastic differential equation (SDE) approximation, enabling the derivation of sufficient conditions for stochastic attractivity towards these invariant sets based on the interplay between loss landscape curvature and gradient noise. Analytical results will be extended from one-dimensional to high-dimensional settings, and the theoretical predictions will be empirically validated in deep neural networks. Furthermore, the impact of stochastic collapse on generalization will be studied in both linear teacher-student models and modern deep architectures, with a focus on the effects of learning rate and batch size.
b488223a9422d43ed8c0e0da04c9c0592eb07829.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training deep neural networks such as VGG-16 and ResNet-18 on standard image classification datasets including CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. The presence and strength of stochastic collapse will be quantified by measuring the number of independent neurons per layer, using hierarchical clustering of neuron parameters to detect vanishing and identical neurons. The effects of varying learning rates and batch sizes on the degree of collapse will be systematically explored. Additionally, a linear teacher-student framework will be employed to analytically and empirically assess the relationship between stochastic collapse and generalization, with evaluation metrics including training loss, test loss, and test accuracy. Baselines will include networks trained with different noise levels and learning rate schedules.
b488223a9422d43ed8c0e0da04c9c0592eb07829.novelty_claims: This research introduces a mechanistic and quantitative theory explaining how stochastic gradient noise drives SGD dynamics towards invariant sets representing simpler subnetworks, providing a new perspective on the implicit bias of SGD beyond traditional regularization views. The work establishes sufficient conditions for stochastic attractivity in both low- and high-dimensional settings, connects these dynamics to generalization improvements, and offers a theoretical explanation for the empirical success of prolonged large learning rates in deep learning. The approach unifies symmetry-based invariant set analysis with stochastic process theory, and provides new empirical evidence of stochastic collapse in widely used deep architectures.

b4ae3a820a29b3dd18d66d021f709be9e66dc9d7.title: The Plug-in Approach for Average-Reward and Discounted MDPs: Optimal Sample Complexity Analysis
b4ae3a820a29b3dd18d66d021f709be9e66dc9d7.research_question: What is the optimal sample complexity required to learn near-optimal policies in average-reward and discounted Markov decision processes (MDPs) using a plug-in approach, and how can this be achieved without prior knowledge of key problem parameters such as the diameter or mixing time?
b4ae3a820a29b3dd18d66d021f709be9e66dc9d7.hypothesis: The plug-in approach, when combined with anchoring and optional reward perturbation, achieves minimax-optimal sample complexity for learning near-optimal policies in both average-reward and discounted MDPs, without requiring prior knowledge of complexity parameters such as the diameter or uniform mixing time.
b4ae3a820a29b3dd18d66d021f709be9e66dc9d7.proposed_method: The proposed method develops a plug-in framework for learning policies in MDPs by first estimating the transition model using samples from a generative model, then solving the estimated MDP to obtain a policy. Key enhancements include (1) anchoring, which modifies the empirical transition matrix by introducing a small probability of transitioning to a fixed anchor state, ensuring the estimated model is weakly communicating and facilitating stable policy computation; and (2) optional random perturbation of the reward vector to guarantee uniqueness and computational tractability of the optimal policy. The approach is instantiated for both average-reward and discounted MDPs, with the ability to use any suitable MDP solver for the estimated model. Theoretical analysis is conducted to derive high-probability bounds on the suboptimality of the learned policy in terms of problem-dependent complexity measures such as the diameter, mixing time, and bias span, without requiring these parameters to be known a priori.
b4ae3a820a29b3dd18d66d021f709be9e66dc9d7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a generative model setting, where independent samples are drawn from the unknown transition kernel for each state-action pair. The method will be evaluated on synthetic and/or benchmark MDPs with varying properties (e.g., different diameters, mixing times, and state-action space sizes). Baseline comparisons will include existing sample-optimal methods based on discounted MDP reduction, dynamic horizon Q-learning, and stochastic saddle-point optimization, as well as explicit diameter estimation approaches. Evaluation metrics will focus on the number of samples required to achieve an ε-optimal policy (sample complexity), as well as the empirical suboptimality gap. Experimental setups will vary the amount of prior knowledge available and assess robustness to unknown parameters.
b4ae3a820a29b3dd18d66d021f709be9e66dc9d7.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to provide a comprehensive and optimal sample complexity analysis for the plug-in method in average-reward MDPs, matching minimax lower bounds in several settings without requiring prior knowledge of complexity parameters such as the diameter or mixing time. The method unifies and improves upon prior approaches by achieving optimal diameter- and mixing-based sample complexities with a simple, generic algorithm. Novel analysis techniques are introduced to handle long-horizon problems and span-based complexity measures, and these techniques also yield improved results for discounted MDPs, removing previous sample size restrictions and eliminating the need for reward perturbation in some cases. The approach demonstrates that the plug-in method is not only simple and natural but also theoretically optimal and broadly applicable.

b4e2592ffea484d28a6b121641aa6a9d1a81ce98.title: Generative Modeling of Regular and Irregular Time Series Data via Koopman VAEs
b4e2592ffea484d28a6b121641aa6a9d1a81ce98.research_question: How can generative modeling of both regular and irregular time series data be improved to better capture underlying dynamics, enable incorporation of domain knowledge, and support robust and interpretable generation across diverse scientific and engineering applications?
b4e2592ffea484d28a6b121641aa6a9d1a81ce98.hypothesis: Introducing a variational autoencoder framework with a novel linear latent prior inspired by Koopman theory will enable more robust, interpretable, and accurate generative modeling of time series data—both regular and irregular—compared to existing GAN- and VAE-based methods, while also facilitating the integration of domain-specific constraints.
b4e2592ffea484d28a6b121641aa6a9d1a81ce98.proposed_method: A new generative modeling framework, Koopman Variational Autoencoder (KoVAE), is proposed, which integrates a linear latent prior based on Koopman operator theory within a sequential VAE architecture. The method models the latent dynamics as governed by a learnable linear operator, estimated in a manner similar to Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD), enabling the latent space to reflect the underlying system's dynamics. The posterior is constructed using an embedding layer (NCDE for irregular data), a GRU-based encoder, linear layers for mean and variance estimation, and a GRU-based decoder. The prior is realized by mapping inputs to a latent space where the evolution is linear, with the Koopman operator learned via least-squares fitting between consecutive latent states. The training objective combines reconstruction, prediction (to enforce linearity in the latent space), and regularization terms, and supports the addition of spectral constraints on the Koopman operator to encode domain knowledge such as stability or oscillatory behavior.
b4e2592ffea484d28a6b121641aa6a9d1a81ce98.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world time series datasets, including Sines, Stocks, Energy, and MuJoCo, as well as a nonlinear pendulum system for physics-constrained evaluation. Both regular and irregular sampling regimes will be tested, with irregularity simulated by randomly omitting 30%, 50%, or 70% of observations. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art GAN-based methods (TimeGAN, GT-GAN, RCGAN, C-RNN-GAN, WaveGAN), VAE-based methods (TimeVAE, CR-VAE), and autoregressive models (T-Forcing, P-Forcing, WaveNet). Evaluation metrics will include discriminative scores (ability of a classifier to distinguish real from generated samples), predictive scores (mean absolute error when training on synthetic and testing on real data), and qualitative assessments via t-SNE and kernel density estimation. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the linear prior and recurrent components.
b4e2592ffea484d28a6b121641aa6a9d1a81ce98.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel linear Koopman-inspired prior into the VAE framework for time series generation, enabling explicit modeling of latent dynamics and seamless integration of domain knowledge via spectral constraints. It is the first to combine VAEs and Koopman-based methods for both regular and irregular time series generation. The method supports physics-constrained generation and stability analysis through spectral properties of the learned operator. Empirical results are expected to show substantial improvements over state-of-the-art GAN and VAE baselines on both quantitative and qualitative metrics, and the framework is designed to be flexible, interpretable, and easy to implement.

b4f0b446c833d3096119163b60436c5f9699e95d.title: Optimal Rates for Regularized Conditional Mean Embedding Learning
b4f0b446c833d3096119163b60436c5f9699e95d.research_question: What are the optimal statistical learning rates for regularized kernel-based estimation of conditional mean embeddings (CME) in potentially misspecified settings, particularly when the target CME lies outside the standard Hilbert-Schmidt operator space, and how can these rates be characterized without restrictive assumptions on the dimensionality or smoothness of the underlying spaces?
b4f0b446c833d3096119163b60436c5f9699e95d.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, by leveraging a novel vector-valued interpolation space construction and associated operator-theoretic techniques, it is possible to derive minimax optimal and adaptive learning rates for empirical CME estimators in both well-specified and misspecified settings, matching known upper bounds without requiring finite-dimensionality or strong smoothness assumptions, and to establish corresponding lower bounds demonstrating the optimality of these rates.
b4f0b446c833d3096119163b60436c5f9699e95d.proposed_method: The proposed method develops a rigorous framework for CME estimation using kernel ridge regression within a newly defined vector-valued interpolation space. This space is constructed via a tensor product of Hilbert spaces and isometrically isomorphic to a space of Hilbert-Schmidt operators acting from an interpolation space between the input RKHS and L2, to the output RKHS. The approach generalizes beyond the well-specified case by embedding the target CME in this larger interpolation space, thus accommodating misspecification. The method involves deriving closed-form solutions for the regularized empirical CME estimator and analyzing its convergence properties under general eigenvalue decay and embedding assumptions, without requiring the output RKHS to be finite-dimensional or the kernel eigenvalues to decay rapidly.
b4f0b446c833d3096119163b60436c5f9699e95d.experiment_details: Theoretical analysis will be supplemented by empirical evaluations using synthetic and real-world datasets where the conditional distributions and kernel properties can be controlled or estimated. Standard kernel choices such as Gaussian, Laplacian, and Matérn will be considered, with datasets sampled from joint distributions over input and output spaces. Baseline comparisons will include existing CME estimation methods under both well-specified and misspecified settings. Evaluation metrics will focus on the convergence rate of the empirical CME estimator in various interpolation norms (including L2 and operator norms), and the tightness of upper and lower bounds will be assessed. Experimental setups will also vary the smoothness and dimensionality conditions to test the robustness of the proposed rates.
b4f0b446c833d3096119163b60436c5f9699e95d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel vector-valued interpolation space framework for CME estimation, enabling the analysis of learning rates in misspecified settings without restrictive assumptions on kernel eigenvalue decay or output space dimensionality. The method establishes, for the first time, matching upper and lower bounds for the learning rate of CME estimators in infinite-dimensional settings, demonstrating minimax optimality. Unlike prior work, the approach does not require explicit continuity or injectivity conditions on the embedding operators, and it applies to a broader class of kernels and distributions. The results extend the theoretical understanding of CME learning and provide practical guidelines for regularization and kernel selection in nonparametric inference tasks.

b4f9e9130b29754c526c454ab54043b49bdd387d.title: Tensor Product Attention Is All You Need
b4f9e9130b29754c526c454ab54043b49bdd387d.research_question: How can attention mechanisms in large language models be improved to significantly reduce memory and computational overhead for long input sequences, while maintaining or improving model quality and compatibility with existing positional encoding schemes?
b4f9e9130b29754c526c454ab54043b49bdd387d.hypothesis: A contextual, low-rank tensor factorization of queries, keys, and values within the attention mechanism will enable substantial reductions in key-value cache memory and computational requirements during inference, without sacrificing—and potentially improving—model performance on language modeling and downstream tasks.
b4f9e9130b29754c526c454ab54043b49bdd387d.proposed_method: A novel attention mechanism, Tensor Product Attention (TPA), will be developed by factorizing the query, key, and value activations into contextual low-rank tensor products. For each token, the hidden state will be projected into factor matrices for each attention head, and queries, keys, and values will be constructed as sums of tensor products of these factors. Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) and other positional encodings will be integrated directly into the factorization, allowing for efficient pre-rotation and seamless compatibility. The TPA mechanism will be incorporated into a new Transformer architecture, the Tensor ProducT ATTenTion Transformer (T6), which replaces standard multi-head attention layers with TPA modules. Additionally, an efficient inference algorithm, FlashTPA Decoding, will be designed to exploit the factorized representations and accelerate autoregressive decoding by avoiding materialization of full attention tensors.
b4f9e9130b29754c526c454ab54043b49bdd387d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale language modeling tasks using the FineWeb-Edu100B dataset, which contains 100 billion training tokens and 0.1 billion validation tokens. Models will be trained at multiple scales (124M, 353M, 773M, and 1.5B parameters) for 50 billion tokens. Baselines will include standard Multi-Head Attention (MHA), Multi-Query Attention (MQA), Grouped-Query Attention (GQA), and Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA), with all models parameter-matched for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics will include validation loss, perplexity, and accuracy on a suite of downstream benchmarks (ARC, BoolQ, HellaSwag, OBQA, PIQA, WinoGrande, MMLU, SciQ) in both zero-shot and two-shot settings. Decoding speed and memory usage will be benchmarked for FlashTPA against optimized implementations of FlashMHA, FlashMQA, FlashGQA, and FlashMLA across varying batch sizes, embedding dimensions, and sequence lengths.
b4f9e9130b29754c526c454ab54043b49bdd387d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a fundamentally new attention mechanism based on contextual tensor factorization, enabling an order-of-magnitude reduction in key-value cache memory during inference. The method provides native compatibility with rotary and other positional embeddings, allowing for straightforward integration into existing Transformer architectures. The approach generalizes and subsumes standard attention mechanisms (MHA, MQA, GQA) as special cases within the TPA framework. An efficient decoding algorithm, FlashTPA, is proposed to further accelerate inference by leveraging the factorized structure. The combined innovations are expected to address critical scalability challenges for long-context language models without compromising, and often improving, model quality.

b501df63ce56e1f62ed7c99ca1301a28de83bc4f.title: CAT: Circular-Convolutional Attention for Sub-Quadratic Transformers
b501df63ce56e1f62ed7c99ca1301a28de83bc4f.research_question: How can the computational complexity of Transformer attention mechanisms be reduced below quadratic time while fully preserving the global softmax-based weighting structure and maintaining or improving empirical performance on large-scale vision and language tasks?
b501df63ce56e1f62ed7c99ca1301a28de83bc4f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a Fourier-based circular-convolutional attention mechanism, which preserves the global softmax structure and leverages the properties of circulant matrices, can achieve sub-quadratic (O(NlogN)) computational complexity without sacrificing representational power or empirical accuracy, and may even improve efficiency and stability compared to standard self-attention.
b501df63ce56e1f62ed7c99ca1301a28de83bc4f.proposed_method: A novel attention mechanism, Circular-convolutional Attention (CAT), is proposed that interprets attention weights as a circulant matrix derived from a softmax-normalized projection of the input sequence. Specifically, the input X is projected via a learnable matrix to produce a vector Z, which is then softmax-normalized to Z*. This vector serves as the first row of a circulant matrix, representing global pairwise interactions. The attention output is computed by convolving this circulant matrix with the value projections, which is efficiently implemented in the frequency domain using the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and its inverse (IFFT), combined with a Hadamard product. This approach maintains exact global softmax normalization, reduces the number of learnable parameters by merging query and key projections, and achieves O(NlogN) complexity. The method naturally extends to multi-head attention and can be integrated as a drop-in replacement for standard attention layers.
b501df63ce56e1f62ed7c99ca1301a28de83bc4f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two major benchmarks: ImageNet-1k for image classification and WikiText-103 for language modeling. The proposed CAT mechanism will be evaluated in both full and hybrid (CAT-Alter) configurations, replacing all or half of the attention layers in standard ViT (CLIP-B/L) and Transformer-XL/GPT-2 small architectures. Baselines will include standard self-attention and, where feasible, linear and sparse attention variants. Evaluation metrics will include validation accuracy for image classification and word-level perplexity for language modeling. Training will use consistent hyperparameters and hardware (e.g., 4 NVIDIA V100 GPUs, AdamW optimizer, standard learning rates and batch sizes) across all variants. Additional ablation studies will compare different parameterizations (qkv, qv, q-only, v-only) to assess the trade-offs between parameter efficiency and accuracy.
b501df63ce56e1f62ed7c99ca1301a28de83bc4f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the concept of Engineering-Isomorphic Transformers (EITs), a new class of attention mechanisms that strictly preserve the global softmax weighting while achieving sub-quadratic complexity. CAT is the first attention mechanism to realize this principle using FFT-based circular convolutions, enabling O(NlogN) runtime and reducing parameter count without introducing sequence-length-dependent hyperparameters. The method provides a theoretically grounded and practically efficient alternative to existing kernel-based or sparse approximations, demonstrating consistent empirical improvements or parity with standard attention on large-scale tasks. The work also reveals that merging query and key projections can yield a strong balance of efficiency and accuracy, and that hybrid architectures combining CAT with standard attention can further enhance robustness and performance.

b50d19c5c298f6562c3b3c6c3822a351bdc89260.title: MMMU: A Massive Multi-Discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
b50d19c5c298f6562c3b3c6c3822a351bdc89260.research_question: How can the evaluation of large multimodal models (LMMs) be advanced to rigorously assess expert-level understanding and reasoning across a broad range of college-level disciplines using highly heterogeneous multimodal data?
b50d19c5c298f6562c3b3c6c3822a351bdc89260.hypothesis: A multimodal benchmark that incorporates expert-level, college-grade questions spanning diverse subjects and image types will reveal significant gaps in current LMM capabilities and drive progress toward models with expert-level reasoning and perception.
b50d19c5c298f6562c3b3c6c3822a351bdc89260.proposed_method: A new benchmark, named MMMU, will be developed to evaluate LMMs on expert-level multimodal understanding and reasoning. The benchmark will consist of 11,550 carefully curated questions sourced from college exams, textbooks, and quizzes, covering 30 subjects and 183 subfields across six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering. Each question will feature interleaved text and images, with 30 highly heterogeneous image types including diagrams, charts, medical scans, music sheets, and more. The benchmark will be divided into development, validation, and test sets, with questions categorized by difficulty and annotated for quality. The evaluation will focus on perception, knowledge recall, and deliberate reasoning, requiring models to jointly interpret text and images and apply domain-specific knowledge.
b50d19c5c298f6562c3b3c6c3822a351bdc89260.experiment_details: Experiments will involve evaluating a wide array of LMMs and text-only LLMs, both open-source and proprietary, under a zero-shot setting. Models will be assessed using micro-averaged accuracy on both multiple-choice and open-ended questions, with systematic, rule-based answer extraction to handle long-form outputs. Baselines will include random and frequent choice, as well as human expert performance for comparison. The benchmark will analyze performance across disciplines, image types, and question difficulties, and will include error analysis to categorize model failures (e.g., perceptual, knowledge, reasoning errors). The leaderboard will be updated live to track progress, and experiments will be conducted on high-performance GPUs.
b50d19c5c298f6562c3b3c6c3822a351bdc89260.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces unprecedented breadth and depth by covering 30 college-level subjects and 30 heterogeneous image types, far exceeding the scope of existing multimodal benchmarks. It uniquely emphasizes expert-level reasoning and domain-specific knowledge, rather than commonsense or daily knowledge. The benchmark’s design challenges models with interleaved text-image inputs and requires advanced perceptual and reasoning skills, making it a necessary test for progress toward Expert AGI. The data curation process ensures high-quality, diverse, and challenging questions, and the benchmark provides detailed error analysis to guide future model improvements.

b50e850a58b6fc41bbbbf05d199aa43dc581c163.title: Inductive Moment Matching
b50e850a58b6fc41bbbbf05d199aa43dc581c163.research_question: How can generative models for continuous domains achieve high-fidelity outputs, efficient inference, and stable training in a single-stage process, particularly enabling one- or few-step sampling without the instability and complexity of existing distillation or consistency-based approaches?
b50e850a58b6fc41bbbbf05d199aa43dc581c163.hypothesis: A generative modeling framework based on inductive moment matching, which leverages self-consistent, marginal-preserving interpolants and a moment-matching objective, will enable stable, single-stage training of one- or few-step generative models that achieve state-of-the-art sample quality and inference efficiency, outperforming existing diffusion and consistency models.
b50e850a58b6fc41bbbbf05d199aa43dc581c163.proposed_method: A new class of generative models, termed Inductive Moment Matching (IMM), is proposed to enable one- or few-step sampling with a single-stage training procedure. IMM operates on time-dependent marginal distributions of stochastic interpolants, constructing mappings from any marginal at time t to any marginal at time s < t, thereby supporting direct and recursive multi-step generation. The method employs marginal-preserving, self-consistent interpolants (such as DDIM) to ensure that the distribution at each step is independent of the starting time, guaranteeing convergence to the data distribution. Training is performed by minimizing a sample-based divergence, specifically the Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD), between the model's and data's marginal distributions, using multiple particles to match all moments. The model is parameterized as a deterministic mapping, and practical algorithmic choices include the use of transformer architectures, time and noise embeddings, and specific weighting and kernel functions to enhance stability and performance.
b50e850a58b6fc41bbbbf05d199aa43dc581c163.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image generation benchmarks, including CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-256×256, using both unconditional and class-conditional settings. The proposed IMM models will be trained from scratch and compared against a wide range of baselines: diffusion models, flow matching models, distillation-based few-step models, and other few-step-from-scratch models. Evaluation metrics will include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for sample quality, with ablations on model architectures (e.g., DiT, DDPM++), embedding types, number of MMD particles, flow schedules, and mapping functions. The experimental setup will also investigate training stability, scalability with model and compute size, and the effect of different sampling strategies (pushforward, restart, multi-step). Hyperparameter choices such as kernel type, weighting functions, and noise embedding scales will be systematically explored.
b50e850a58b6fc41bbbbf05d199aa43dc581c163.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a stable, single-stage training procedure for few-step generative models, eliminating the need for pre-training, distillation, or dual-network optimization. IMM guarantees distribution-level convergence and remains robust across a wide range of hyperparameters and architectures. The method generalizes and unifies prior approaches, including diffusion, flow matching, and consistency models, and theoretically explains the instability of existing consistency models as a special case of first-moment matching. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art FID scores on standard benchmarks with significantly fewer inference steps, and the approach is claimed to scale efficiently with both model size and compute.

b54efb1ef315ecb68571b99ae7489d1834da02ba.title: SC-GS: Sparse-Controlled Gaussian Splatting for Editable Dynamic Scenes
b54efb1ef315ecb68571b99ae7489d1834da02ba.research_question: How can dynamic scenes be efficiently and accurately represented for high-fidelity novel view synthesis and user-controllable motion editing, using a compact and editable motion representation from monocular video input?
b54efb1ef315ecb68571b99ae7489d1834da02ba.hypothesis: Explicitly decomposing the motion and appearance of dynamic scenes into a sparse set of control points and dense 3D Gaussians, respectively, will enable efficient, high-quality dynamic view synthesis and intuitive motion editing, outperforming existing methods in both rendering speed and visual fidelity.
b54efb1ef315ecb68571b99ae7489d1834da02ba.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed that represents dynamic scenes by separating motion and appearance: sparse control points are used to model scene motion, while dense 3D Gaussians capture appearance and geometry. Each control point is associated with time-varying 6-DoF transformations, parameterized via a deformation MLP conditioned on control point location and time. The motion of each Gaussian is determined by interpolating the transformations of its k-nearest control points using a Gaussian-kernel RBF, effectively creating a locally rigid, compact motion field. An ARAP (As-Rigid-As-Possible) loss is introduced to enforce spatial continuity and local rigidity among control points, and an adaptive density adjustment strategy dynamically prunes or adds control points to accommodate varying motion complexities. The entire system, including Gaussians, control points, and the deformation MLP, is jointly optimized using a combination of rendering loss and ARAP loss.
b54efb1ef315ecb68571b99ae7489d1834da02ba.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on benchmark dynamic scene datasets, including D-NeRF and NeRF-DS, which feature a variety of rigid and non-rigid object motions. The proposed method will be quantitatively evaluated using metrics such as PSNR, SSIM, MS-SSIM, and LPIPS, and compared against state-of-the-art baselines including D-NeRF, TiNeuVox, Tensor4D, K-Planes, FF-NVS, and 4D-GS. Ablation studies will assess the impact of control points and ARAP loss on performance. Rendering speed and qualitative results, including motion editing capabilities, will also be evaluated to demonstrate efficiency and flexibility.
b54efb1ef315ecb68571b99ae7489d1834da02ba.novelty_claims: The approach introduces a sparse, explicit motion representation using control points, significantly reducing the parameter space for modeling scene dynamics compared to per-Gaussian motion models. The integration of an ARAP loss for local rigidity and adaptive control point density adjustment enables robust learning of complex motions from monocular video. The method uniquely supports user-controllable motion editing by manipulating the learned control points, while maintaining high-fidelity appearance. Extensive experiments are expected to show state-of-the-art performance in both rendering quality and speed, as well as novel capabilities for motion editing not present in existing methods.

b562ce4b85a97de5a9e909c7dcd090d0fa5f19ec.title: A Systematic Study of Bias Amplification
b562ce4b85a97de5a9e909c7dcd090d0fa5f19ec.research_question: When and how does bias amplification occur in machine learning models, and what are the key factors influencing its magnitude in image classification tasks?
b562ce4b85a97de5a9e909c7dcd090d0fa5f19ec.hypothesis: Bias amplification in machine learning models is systematically influenced by factors such as the degree of bias in training data, model capacity, training set size, model overconfidence, training dynamics, and the relative difficulty of class versus group membership recognition.
b562ce4b85a97de5a9e909c7dcd090d0fa5f19ec.proposed_method: A systematic and controlled study will be conducted using synthetic image classification tasks where biases can be tightly controlled. Binary classification problems will be constructed from standard image datasets by randomly assigning half the classes as positive and half as negative. Synthetic groups will be created by inverting images, allowing precise manipulation of the correlation between group and class labels without introducing causal relationships. The degree of bias will be parameterized by varying the probability of inversion for positive and negative samples, enabling a range of bias strengths. Residual networks (ResNets) of varying depths, widths, and regularization strengths will be trained using standard procedures, and bias amplification will be measured using the directional bias amplification metric. Experiments will systematically vary dataset bias, model capacity, training set size, and training duration, and will also swap the difficulty of group versus class recognition to probe underlying mechanisms.
b562ce4b85a97de5a9e909c7dcd090d0fa5f19ec.experiment_details: Experiments will use the FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 datasets, with standard train/test splits. Binary classification tasks will be generated by random class assignment, and synthetic group membership will be induced by image inversion. Bias in the dataset will be controlled by adjusting inversion probabilities for positive and negative samples. Models will be trained using mini-batch SGD with Nesterov momentum, weight decay, and data augmentation as appropriate. The primary evaluation metric for bias amplification will be the BiasAmp directional measure, with model accuracy and expected calibration error (ECE) also reported. Experiments will include systematic sweeps over model depth, width, regularization, training set size, and training epochs, with results averaged over multiple random seeds and confidence intervals reported.
b562ce4b85a97de5a9e909c7dcd090d0fa5f19ec.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first systematic, controlled study of bias amplification in machine learning, leveraging synthetic group construction to precisely manipulate and measure bias. The approach enables disentanglement of causal and correlational effects between group and class labels. The study will provide comprehensive insights into how bias amplification depends on model and data factors, reveal dynamic changes during training, and identify best practices for reducing bias amplification. The findings are expected to inform the development of more effective mitigation strategies for bias in machine learning models.

b565273208fd6bb197db695115e8a74356b246af.title: Pretraining a Shared Q-Network for Data-Efficient Offline Reinforcement Learning
b565273208fd6bb197db695115e8a74356b246af.research_question: How can offline reinforcement learning agents be enabled to learn effective policies from minimal amounts of pre-collected data, across diverse domains and data distributions, without requiring additional environment interaction?
b565273208fd6bb197db695115e8a74356b246af.hypothesis: Pretraining a shared Q-network using a transition prediction task to initialize the feature representation will improve the data efficiency and performance of offline RL agents, enabling them to learn more accurate value functions and achieve higher returns with less data compared to standard approaches.
b565273208fd6bb197db695115e8a74356b246af.proposed_method: A plug-and-play pretraining framework is developed for offline RL, utilizing a shared Q-network architecture composed of a backbone feature extractor and two shallow heads: one for next-state prediction (transition head) and one for Q-value estimation (Q-value head). The method proceeds in two stages: (1) Pretraining, where the backbone and transition head are trained jointly via self-supervised regression to predict the next state from state-action pairs, minimizing mean squared prediction error; (2) RL training, where the backbone is fine-tuned (or optionally frozen) alongside the Q-value head using any standard offline RL objective. This modular design allows seamless integration with existing offline RL algorithms and enhances the quality of learned representations for value estimation. The approach is theoretically analyzed under the projected Bellman equation, showing that pretraining increases the feature matrix rank and tightens the upper bound on Q-value estimation error.
b565273208fd6bb197db695115e8a74356b246af.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of offline RL benchmarks, including D4RL (locomotion tasks with HalfCheetah, Hopper, Walker2d across random, medium, medium-replay, medium-expert, and expert datasets), Robomimic (robotic manipulation tasks), V-D4RL (image-based environments), and ExoRL (datasets with diverse collection strategies and state coverage). The method will be evaluated as an augmentation to multiple baseline offline RL algorithms such as AWAC, CQL, IQL, TD3+BC, DrQ+BC, MOPO, MOBILE, ACL, IRIS, and BCQ. Performance will be measured using normalized scores, average episode returns, and success rates, with results averaged over multiple random seeds. Data efficiency will be assessed by training on reduced dataset fractions (1%, 3%, 10%, 30%, 100%) and across varying data qualities and collection strategies. Proxy Q-error and feature matrix rank will be used to analyze representation quality and value estimation accuracy.
b565273208fd6bb197db695115e8a74356b246af.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a simple yet effective pretraining framework for offline RL that is architecture-agnostic and easily integrates with existing algorithms. By leveraging a shared Q-network and transition prediction pretraining, the method significantly improves data efficiency and performance, even with severely reduced datasets and across diverse data distributions. Theoretical analysis provides new insights into how pretraining enhances feature expressiveness and reduces Q-value estimation error. Extensive empirical results demonstrate that the method outperforms both model-based and representation learning baselines under data-limited conditions, establishing a new standard for data-efficient offline RL.

b58d5388fd408af2437ac173cb457e8ff01598a7.title: How Mask Matters: Towards Theoretical Understandings of Masked Autoencoders
b58d5388fd408af2437ac173cb457e8ff01598a7.research_question: What is the theoretical role of masking in masked autoencoder (MAE) frameworks for self-supervised learning, and how does the choice of mask ratio affect downstream performance and feature representations?
b58d5388fd408af2437ac173cb457e8ff01598a7.hypothesis: Masking in MAE implicitly aligns positive pairs in a manner analogous to contrastive learning, and incorporating an explicit feature uniformity regularization will mitigate dimensional collapse and improve downstream performance.
b58d5388fd408af2437ac173cb457e8ff01598a7.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed to formally connect the reconstruction loss of masked autoencoders to an alignment loss over mask-induced positive pairs, drawing parallels to contrastive learning. The methodology includes constructing a bipartite mask graph and an augmentation graph to model the relationships induced by masking, and mathematically analyzing the lower bounds of the MAE loss in terms of alignment and uniformity losses. To address the observed dimensional collapse, a Uniformity-enhanced MAE (U-MAE) loss will be introduced by augmenting the standard MAE objective with an explicit spectral uniformity regularization term on the encoder's output features. The coefficient of the uniformity term will be tuned to balance reconstruction and feature diversity, and theoretical guarantees on downstream classification error will be established based on this new loss formulation.
b58d5388fd408af2437ac173cb457e8ff01598a7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification benchmarks including CIFAR-10, ImageNet-100, and ImageNet-1K. Various Vision Transformer (ViT) backbones (ViT-Tiny, ViT-Base, ViT-Large) will be used as encoders, with a default mask ratio of 0.75 and a flexible decoder architecture. Both linear probing (training a linear classifier on frozen features) and full fine-tuning (training both encoder and classifier) will be evaluated. Baselines will include the original MAE loss and other masked image modeling methods such as SimMIM, with and without the proposed uniformity regularization. Evaluation metrics will include linear probing accuracy, fine-tuning accuracy, and analysis of feature singular values and effective rank to assess dimensional collapse. Additional ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of the uniformity coefficient and mask ratio.
b58d5388fd408af2437ac173cb457e8ff01598a7.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first formal theoretical connection between masked autoencoders and contrastive learning, showing that MAE implicitly aligns mask-induced positive pairs. It provides the first theoretical downstream guarantees for MAE methods, including an analysis of the effect of mask ratio on representation learning. The Uniformity-enhanced MAE (U-MAE) loss is proposed as a novel regularization technique to explicitly address dimensional feature collapse, resulting in significant empirical improvements in linear probing accuracy across multiple datasets and architectures. The theoretical insights also offer principled guidance for selecting optimal mask ratios in MAE frameworks.

b5bda12b16209d77a0ede563fc1fb81422471820.title: An Efficient Doubly-Robust Test for the Kernel Treatment Effect
b5bda12b16209d77a0ede563fc1fb81422471820.research_question: Can an efficient, doubly-robust, kernel-based statistical test be developed to detect distributional treatment effects in observational studies, providing valid type-I error control and computational efficiency without relying on permutation procedures?
b5bda12b16209d77a0ede563fc1fb81422471820.hypothesis: A kernel-based, doubly-robust test for distributional treatment effects can achieve valid type-I error control and high power in detecting differences in outcome distributions between treated and control groups, while being computationally efficient and applicable to observational data.
b5bda12b16209d77a0ede563fc1fb81422471820.proposed_method: A novel statistical test, termed AIPW-xKTE (Augmented Inverse Propensity Weighted cross Kernel Treatment Effect), will be developed to assess distributional treatment effects using kernel mean embeddings and doubly-robust estimation. The method leverages the maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) between the kernel mean embeddings of the counterfactual outcome distributions, estimated via augmented inverse propensity weighting (AIPW) to ensure double robustness. To address computational inefficiency and the lack of analytic null distributions in traditional kernel tests, the approach employs cross U-statistics and sample splitting, yielding a permutation-free test statistic with asymptotic normality under the null. The procedure involves splitting the data, fitting nuisance estimators (propensity scores and conditional mean embeddings) on separate folds, and computing an inner product-based test statistic whose distribution is analytically tractable. The test is designed to be valid under standard causal inference assumptions (consistency, no unmeasured confounding, overlap) and is applicable to both experimental and observational settings.
b5bda12b16209d77a0ede563fc1fb81422471820.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic data will be generated under four scenarios: (I) no treatment effect, (II) mean shift only, (III) higher-moment differences only, and (IV) alternative higher-moment differences, with unknown propensity scores estimated from the data. The proposed AIPW-xKTE test will be compared to baseline methods including Causal Forests, Bayesian Additive Regression Trees (BART), and a linear regression-based AIPW estimator, focusing on empirical size (type-I error) and power across scenarios. Evaluation metrics include rejection rates under the null and alternative, and calibration of the test statistic's distribution. Real data experiments will use the Infant Health and Development Program (IHDP) dataset, with multiple scenarios constructed to test for both mean and higher-moment distributional effects. Bootstrapped subsets will be used to estimate rejection rates, and the propensity score model will be intentionally misspecified to assess robustness. The computational efficiency of the proposed test will be benchmarked against permutation-based kernel tests.
b5bda12b16209d77a0ede563fc1fb81422471820.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first kernel-based, doubly-robust test for distributional treatment effects with provably valid type-I error control in observational studies. It introduces a permutation-free, computationally efficient framework based on cross U-statistics and sample splitting, enabling analytic p-values and avoiding the high computational cost of permutation-based approaches. The test is capable of detecting distributional changes beyond mean shifts, such as differences in variance or higher moments, and is robust to misspecification of either the propensity score or outcome regression models. The framework generalizes existing kernel treatment effect tests to the doubly-robust setting and extends their applicability to observational data.

b5bffe41155052a43010ec7197f832e81c546268.title: Quiet-STaR: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Think Before Speaking
b5bffe41155052a43010ec7197f832e81c546268.research_question: Can language models be trained to autonomously generate and leverage internal rationales or 'thoughts' during language modeling, thereby improving their reasoning abilities and performance on tasks that require implicit or explicit reasoning, without relying on curated reasoning datasets or explicit task supervision?
b5bffe41155052a43010ec7197f832e81c546268.hypothesis: Training language models to generate internal rationales at each token position in arbitrary text, and optimizing these rationales to improve future token prediction, will enhance the model's ability to reason and improve performance on downstream reasoning tasks, even in zero-shot settings without task-specific fine-tuning.
b5bffe41155052a43010ec7197f832e81c546268.proposed_method: A new framework, Quiet-STaR, is introduced to enable language models to generate internal rationales (thoughts) after each token in a sequence, using learnable meta-tokens to mark the start and end of each rationale. A parallel sampling algorithm is developed to efficiently generate rationales for all token positions in a sequence, leveraging custom attention masks to allow for scalable training. The model is trained to mix predictions made with and without these rationales using a learned mixing head, which interpolates between the base and rationale-augmented predictions. The generation of rationales is optimized using a REINFORCE-based objective, rewarding rationales that improve the likelihood of future tokens (using a non-myopic, multi-token-ahead loss), and teacher-forcing is applied to stabilize training and provide a richer learning signal.
b5bffe41155052a43010ec7197f832e81c546268.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted by continuing pretraining of the Mistral 7B language model on large-scale web text corpora, specifically OpenWebMath (a technical web crawl) and the Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus (C4). The model is evaluated in zero-shot settings on downstream reasoning benchmarks, including CommonsenseQA and GSM8K, without any task-specific fine-tuning. Baselines include the same model trained without thought tokens, as well as comparisons to pause token approaches. Evaluation metrics include zero-shot accuracy on the reasoning tasks and perplexity improvements, with additional analysis on the distribution of improvements across token types and the impact of rationale length. The experimental setup explores different numbers of thought tokens and looks ahead multiple tokens to assess the effect of deeper reasoning.
b5bffe41155052a43010ec7197f832e81c546268.novelty_claims: The proposed approach generalizes reasoning-focused language model training from curated, task-specific datasets to arbitrary, unstructured text, enabling models to learn reasoning skills from the full diversity of language. A scalable, parallel rationale generation algorithm is introduced, along with learnable meta-tokens for marking and optimizing rationale boundaries. The framework incorporates a novel mixing head for interpolating rationale-augmented and base predictions, and applies a non-myopic, multi-token-ahead objective to better capture the utility of reasoning. The method demonstrates significant zero-shot improvements on challenging reasoning benchmarks without fine-tuning, and shows that longer, internally generated rationales lead to greater performance gains, particularly on difficult tokens.

b611c501269224702d1a9942c8600a31ec66ab28.title: ChartQA: A Benchmark for Question Answering about Charts with Visual and Logical Reasoning
b611c501269224702d1a9942c8600a31ec66ab28.research_question: How can question answering systems be developed to accurately answer complex, open-vocabulary questions about real-world charts, requiring both visual and logical reasoning, and how can a large-scale benchmark be constructed to evaluate such systems effectively?
b611c501269224702d1a9942c8600a31ec66ab28.hypothesis: Integrating visual features from chart images with automatically extracted data tables in transformer-based models will enable more accurate and robust question answering on complex, real-world chart data, especially for questions requiring visual and logical reasoning.
b611c501269224702d1a9942c8600a31ec66ab28.proposed_method: A large-scale benchmark will be constructed, consisting of over 20,000 real-world chart images sourced from diverse platforms and annotated with both human-authored and machine-generated question-answer pairs. The methodology involves extracting structured data tables from chart images using an enhanced ChartOCR pipeline, which combines key-point detection, OCR, and alignment of data values with textual labels. Two transformer-based models will be developed: an extension of TAPAS (VisionTaPas) that incorporates both tabular and visual features via a cross-modal encoder, and a vision-language variant of T5 (VL-T5) that conditions text generation on both flattened tables and visual features extracted from chart elements using Mask R-CNN and Vision Transformers. The models will be further extended to support arithmetic operations such as difference and ratio, and trained using a combination of weak supervision and heuristically generated operation-specific labels.
b611c501269224702d1a9942c8600a31ec66ab28.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the newly created ChartQA benchmark as well as on existing datasets (FigureQA, DVQA, PlotQA) for comprehensive evaluation. The datasets will be split into training, validation, and test sets, with careful manual cleaning and quality assurance for machine-generated questions. Baseline models such as PReFIL and PlotQA* will be implemented for comparison. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, with relaxed matching for numerical answers (within 5% of gold value) and exact match for non-numerical answers. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of supporting additional operations and the inclusion of visual features. Transfer learning experiments will pretrain models on synthetic datasets and fine-tune on ChartQA to assess generalization.
b611c501269224702d1a9942c8600a31ec66ab28.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first large-scale benchmark for chart question answering with real-world charts and human-authored, open-vocabulary questions focused on visual and logical reasoning. It presents a unified pipeline that combines advanced data extraction from chart images with transformer-based QA models capable of integrating both visual and tabular information. The approach extends existing models to support new arithmetic operations and demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on multiple datasets, while revealing new challenges in handling complex, compositional, and visually grounded questions.

b612fc6af23cccf2133c2ea40597453ab40dc2c3.title: AdaLoRA: Adaptive Budget Allocation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
b612fc6af23cccf2133c2ea40597453ab40dc2c3.research_question: How can parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large pre-trained language models be improved by adaptively allocating the parameter budget among weight matrices according to their importance, rather than distributing it evenly across all modules and layers?
b612fc6af23cccf2133c2ea40597453ab40dc2c3.hypothesis: Adaptive allocation of the parameter budget to weight matrices based on their importance will improve the performance and parameter efficiency of fine-tuning large pre-trained language models, especially under low-budget constraints, compared to existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods.
b612fc6af23cccf2133c2ea40597453ab40dc2c3.proposed_method: A novel fine-tuning framework, AdaLoRA, is developed to adaptively allocate the parameter budget among the weight matrices of a pre-trained language model based on their estimated importance. The method parameterizes incremental updates to each weight matrix using a singular value decomposition (SVD) form, where the update is represented as PΛQ, with P and Q as orthogonal matrices and Λ as a diagonal matrix of singular values. The importance of each triplet (singular value and corresponding vectors) is quantified using a new metric that combines sensitivity (gradient-weight product) and uncertainty (smoothed by exponential moving average). During training, singular values corresponding to less important triplets are pruned, dynamically adjusting the rank and thus the parameter budget allocated to each matrix. A global budget scheduler is introduced to gradually reduce the total parameter budget during training, starting from a higher initial value and converging to a target budget, which helps stabilize training and improve performance.
b612fc6af23cccf2133c2ea40597453ab40dc2c3.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a range of NLP tasks, including natural language understanding (GLUE benchmark), question answering (SQuAD v1.1 and v2.0), and natural language generation (XSum and CNN/DailyMail), using DeBERTaV3-base and BART-large as the base models. AdaLoRA is compared against baselines such as full fine-tuning, BitFit, adapter tuning (Houlsby and Pfeiffer adapters), and LoRA, under various parameter budget constraints (e.g., 0.08% to 2.2% of full model parameters). Evaluation metrics include accuracy, F1, exact match, and ROUGE scores, depending on the task. The experimental setup involves matching the number of trainable parameters across methods, tuning hyperparameters such as learning rate and regularization, and reporting results averaged over multiple runs with different random seeds.
b612fc6af23cccf2133c2ea40597453ab40dc2c3.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces an adaptive, importance-aware budget allocation mechanism for parameter-efficient fine-tuning, which dynamically adjusts the rank of incremental updates to each weight matrix using an SVD-based parameterization. A new importance metric is designed to guide the pruning of singular values, and a global budget scheduler is implemented for stable and effective training. This method enables more effective use of limited parameter budgets, leading to consistent improvements over existing baselines, especially in low-budget settings, and demonstrates superior parameter efficiency and performance across multiple NLP tasks and models.

b61a64b24ddaf5fb83f8c0cd0c48dd9c4e96d47f.title: Self-Adapting Language Models
b61a64b24ddaf5fb83f8c0cd0c48dd9c4e96d47f.research_question: Can large language models be endowed with the ability to autonomously adapt their own parameters in response to new tasks, knowledge, or examples by generating and utilizing their own training data and update strategies?
b61a64b24ddaf5fb83f8c0cd0c48dd9c4e96d47f.hypothesis: Large language models can achieve more effective and lasting adaptation to new tasks and knowledge if they are trained to generate their own synthetic finetuning data and optimization directives, using reinforcement learning to maximize downstream performance.
b61a64b24ddaf5fb83f8c0cd0c48dd9c4e96d47f.proposed_method: A novel framework, Self-Adapting Language Models (SEAL), will be developed to enable language models to self-adapt by generating 'self-edits'—natural language instructions that specify both synthetic training data and, optionally, optimization hyperparameters or data augmentation strategies. The adaptation process will be structured as a two-level loop: an outer reinforcement learning (RL) loop that optimizes the policy for generating effective self-edits, and an inner loop that applies the generated self-edit via supervised finetuning (using LoRA adapters for efficiency) to update the model's weights. The RL reward signal will be derived from the downstream performance of the updated model on a target task, such as question answering or few-shot generalization. The self-edit generation policy will be trained using a filtered behavior cloning approach (ReSTEM), where only self-edits that lead to improved task performance are reinforced. The framework will be instantiated for both knowledge incorporation (by generating implications or restatements of new passages) and few-shot learning (by specifying data augmentations and training hyperparameters for novel tasks).
b61a64b24ddaf5fb83f8c0cd0c48dd9c4e96d47f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in two domains: (1) knowledge incorporation, using the SQuAD dataset, where the model must integrate new factual passages into its parameters and answer questions without access to the original text; and (2) few-shot abstract reasoning, using a curated subset of the ARC-AGI benchmark, where the model must generalize from limited demonstrations. For knowledge incorporation, models such as Qwen2.5-7B will be evaluated on no-context SQuAD accuracy after adaptation via self-edits, and compared against baselines including direct passage finetuning, passage plus synthetic data (from the base model or GPT-4.1), and the unadapted base model. For few-shot learning, Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct will be used, with success rates measured as the percentage of self-edits leading to correct outputs on held-out ARC tasks. Baselines will include in-context learning, test-time training with and without RL-optimized self-edits, and an oracle with optimal human-crafted configurations. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on downstream tasks and adaptation success rate, with careful tracking of performance across RL training iterations and in continual learning scenarios.
b61a64b24ddaf5fb83f8c0cd0c48dd9c4e96d47f.novelty_claims: The proposed framework enables language models to autonomously generate and apply their own synthetic finetuning data and update directives, directly leveraging their generative capabilities for self-adaptation. Unlike prior methods that rely on external adaptation modules, auxiliary networks, or static data generation heuristics, this approach meta-learns the adaptation strategy via reinforcement learning, optimizing for downstream utility of self-edits. The method supports flexible adaptation across domains, including knowledge integration and few-shot generalization, and demonstrates that self-generated synthetic data can outperform data produced by much larger models (e.g., GPT-4.1). Additionally, the framework is general with respect to the format of self-edits and can be extended to continual learning and agentic settings.

b6256ffe592d6032c98bd2867a8c9b1c61886821.title: seq-JEPA: Autoregressive Predictive Learning of Invariant-Equivariant World Models
b6256ffe592d6032c98bd2867a8c9b1c61886821.research_question: How can a self-supervised learning framework be developed to simultaneously learn representations that are both invariant and equivariant to transformations, thereby supporting a wide range of downstream tasks including those requiring sequential integration of observations?
b6256ffe592d6032c98bd2867a8c9b1c61886821.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by introducing architectural inductive biases and action-conditioned sequential processing into a joint-embedding predictive architecture, it is possible to naturally disentangle and learn both invariant and equivariant representations without the need for explicit equivariance losses or dual predictors, thus resolving the trade-off between invariance and equivariance in self-supervised learning.
b6256ffe592d6032c98bd2867a8c9b1c61886821.proposed_method: A novel self-supervised world modeling framework, termed seq-JEPA, will be developed to process sequences of transformed views (observations) of inputs. Each view will be encoded and concatenated with an embedding of the relative transformation (action) that produces the next observation. These view-action pairs will be passed through a transformer encoder, which acts as a learned working memory to aggregate the sequence into a global representation. A predictor head will then condition this aggregate representation on the upcoming action to predict the representation of the next observation, with training driven by maximizing cosine similarity between predicted and target representations. The target representations will be computed using an exponential moving average of the encoder, and no additional equivariance-specific losses or predictors will be employed. The architecture is designed such that individual encoded views become equivariant, while the aggregate representation becomes invariant, supporting both types of downstream tasks.
b6256ffe592d6032c98bd2867a8c9b1c61886821.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of datasets and transformation regimes. The 3DIEBench dataset will be used to evaluate both invariance (via object classification) and equivariance (via rotation prediction) with 3D object renderings under varying rotations, floor hues, and lighting. Additional experiments will use CIFAR100 and Tiny ImageNet with hand-crafted augmentations (crop, color jitter, blur), and STL-10 for predictive learning across simulated eye movements (saccades) using patch sequences sampled via saliency and inhibition-of-return strategies. Baselines will include state-of-the-art invariant (SimCLR, BYOL, VICReg, VICRegTraj) and equivariant (SEN, EquiMod, SIE, ContextSSL) SSL methods, as well as hybrid variants such as ConditionalBYOL and Conv-JEPA. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 linear classification accuracy for invariance, R2 score for transformation/action prediction (equivariance), and retrieval-based metrics (MRR, Hit@1, Hit@5). Probes will be trained on frozen representations, and extensive ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of action conditioning, sequence length, and architectural choices.
b6256ffe592d6032c98bd2867a8c9b1c61886821.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new architectural framework that enables the simultaneous learning of invariant and equivariant representations through sequential action-conditioned prediction, without requiring explicit equivariance losses, dual predictors, or hand-crafted objectives. The method leverages transformer-based sequence aggregation to naturally disentangle invariance and equivariance in the learned representations. It is also claimed to excel in tasks requiring the integration of sequential observations, such as path integration and predictive learning across saccades, and to scale gracefully with longer sequence lengths. This framework is positioned as a general, non-generative world model that supports efficient representation learning from partial observations and is adaptable to a wide range of transformation types and downstream tasks.

b6261ab0a8ee31fcab0e2675280aa95521586894.title: How to Select Which Active Learning Strategy is Best Suited for Your Specific Problem and Budget
b6261ab0a8ee31fcab0e2675280aa95521586894.research_question: How can the most suitable active learning strategy be automatically selected for a given machine learning problem and labeling budget, without prior knowledge of which strategy will perform best under the specific conditions?
b6261ab0a8ee31fcab0e2675280aa95521586894.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a derivative-based test, which analyzes the model's error response to small perturbations in the labeled dataset, can effectively determine whether a low-budget or high-budget active learning strategy is optimal for the current scenario. This enables dynamic and robust selection of the most appropriate active learning strategy across varying budget regimes.
b6261ab0a8ee31fcab0e2675280aa95521586894.proposed_method: The proposed method, SelectAL, introduces a two-step framework for dynamic active learning strategy selection. First, a derivative-based surrogate test is performed by removing small, class-balanced subsets of labeled data according to candidate low-budget, high-budget, and random strategies, and measuring the impact on model generalization error via cross-validation. The strategy whose removal most degrades performance is inferred to be most critical for the current budget regime, thus identifying whether a low-budget or high-budget strategy is appropriate. In the second step, SelectAL selects the most competitive active learning strategy from the identified regime (low or high budget) to query new unlabeled examples for labeling. The approach is designed to be flexible, allowing for the incorporation of any state-of-the-art active learning strategies and is robust to a wide range of budget sizes.
b6261ab0a8ee31fcab0e2675280aa95521586894.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using deep neural networks, specifically ResNet-18, on standard computer vision datasets including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet-50. The evaluation will involve multiple active learning rounds, with SelectAL dynamically choosing between low-budget (e.g., ProbCover, TypiClust) and high-budget (e.g., BADGE, inverse-TypiClust) strategies, as well as random selection, depending on the current labeled set size. Baselines will include a variety of established active learning methods such as Min margin, Max entropy, Least confidence, DBAL, CoreSet, BALD, and random sampling. Performance will be assessed using mean test accuracy and standard error over multiple runs, with comparisons made across different labeling budgets (low, medium, high). The experimental setup will ensure fair comparisons by using a common codebase and consistent hyperparameters.
b6261ab0a8ee31fcab0e2675280aa95521586894.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to introduce a budget-aware, automatic selection mechanism for active learning strategies that does not require prior knowledge of the optimal strategy for a given problem and budget. SelectAL leverages a novel derivative-based test to dynamically identify the most effective strategy for any budget regime, providing a practical and theoretically motivated solution to a longstanding open problem in active learning. The approach is versatile, robust across diverse datasets and budget sizes, and can readily incorporate future advances in active learning algorithms.

b63c9235347c1a40c5bc02b19786276be7ccd23e.title: Revisiting Bi-Linear State Transitions in Recurrent Neural Networks
b63c9235347c1a40c5bc02b19786276be7ccd23e.research_question: How can recurrent neural networks be designed to effectively learn and generalize state tracking tasks, including simulating finite state machines and modular arithmetic, and what architectural principles enable or impede such capabilities?
b63c9235347c1a40c5bc02b19786276be7ccd23e.hypothesis: Purely bilinear (multiplicative, non-affine) hidden-to-hidden state transitions in recurrent neural networks provide a natural and sufficient inductive bias for learning and generalizing state tracking tasks, outperforming both linear and non-linear RNNs with additive terms, as well as Transformer-based models.
b63c9235347c1a40c5bc02b19786276be7ccd23e.proposed_method: A family of recurrent neural network architectures will be developed in which the hidden state at each time step is updated via a bilinear function of the previous hidden state and the current input, parameterized by a three-way tensor. Several variants will be explored, including full bilinear models, low-rank factorizations (using Canonical Polyadic decomposition), and block-diagonal structures to control parameter count and model expressivity. Special attention will be given to enforcing the absence of additive terms in the recurrence, ensuring scale-invariance and stability. Additional variants will include models with real or complex diagonal transition matrices, as well as block-diagonal matrices parameterized as input-dependent rotations. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to characterize the class of state tracking tasks each architecture can represent, and practical techniques for stabilizing training and inference (such as normalization exploiting scale-invariance) will be employed.
b63c9235347c1a40c5bc02b19786276be7ccd23e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three core state tracking tasks: modular addition (predicting the sum of a sequence modulo m), simulating random finite state machines, and modular arithmetic (sequences of integers and arithmetic operators with results computed modulo m). Datasets will consist of sequences of varying lengths, with training on short sequences (length 2-10) and evaluation on much longer sequences (length up to 500) to assess length generalization. Baseline models will include LSTM, simple RNN, Mamba, and Transformer architectures, all matched for hidden and input dimensionality (e.g., 256). Evaluation metrics will be accuracy normalized such that 0 indicates random chance and 1 indicates perfect accuracy. Additional experiments will assess data efficiency by varying training set size, and ablation studies will compare the effect of additive versus purely bilinear interactions. Further, experiments will test the ability to learn parity with frozen random bilinear networks and only a trained readout layer.
b63c9235347c1a40c5bc02b19786276be7ccd23e.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a comprehensive taxonomy and empirical evaluation of bilinear recurrent neural network architectures for state tracking, demonstrating that pure bilinear (non-affine) updates are both necessary and sufficient for strong generalization in these tasks. The work establishes a hierarchy of model expressivity, showing that block-diagonal and diagonal variants correspond to increasingly restricted classes of regular languages and group structures.
