It is claimed that, unlike prior linear and Transformer-based models, the proposed bilinear RNNs can simulate arbitrary finite state machines and learn parity with minimal data, even with frozen recurrent weights. The scale-invariance property of the bilinear update is leveraged for stable training and inference. The research also provides negative results for models with only additive or positive diagonal transitions, clarifying the limitations of popular architectures such as Mamba.

b64537bdf7a103aa01972ba06ea24a9c08f7cd74.title: Analog Bits: Generating Discrete Data using Diffusion Models with Self-Conditioning
b64537bdf7a103aa01972ba06ea24a9c08f7cd74.research_question: How can continuous-state diffusion models be adapted to efficiently and effectively generate discrete or categorical data, such as images and text, while overcoming the limitations of autoregressive and existing discrete diffusion approaches?
b64537bdf7a103aa01972ba06ea24a9c08f7cd74.hypothesis: Continuous diffusion models, when combined with an analog bit representation of discrete data and enhanced by self-conditioning and asymmetric time interval techniques, can achieve or surpass state-of-the-art performance in discrete data generation tasks, both in terms of sample quality and efficiency.
b64537bdf7a103aa01972ba06ea24a9c08f7cd74.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a framework where discrete data is first encoded into binary bits, which are then cast as real-valued analog bits suitable for modeling with continuous-state diffusion models. During training, a continuous diffusion process is applied to these analog bits using a regression loss, and at sampling time, the generated analog bits are thresholded to recover the discrete variables. Two key enhancements are incorporated: Self-Conditioning, where the denoising network conditions on its own previous predictions during the iterative sampling process, and Asymmetric Time Intervals, where time scheduling during sampling is manipulated to use non-uniform intervals, improving denoising quality. The method is designed to be simple, generic, and compatible with both continuous and discrete time parameterizations, requiring minimal changes to standard diffusion model architectures.
b64537bdf7a103aa01972ba06ea24a9c08f7cd74.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on discrete image generation tasks using CIFAR-10 and ImageNet 64x64 datasets, as well as image captioning on the MS-COCO 2017 dataset. For image generation, various binary encoding schemes (UINT8, GRAYCODE, UINT8(RAND)) will be evaluated, and sample quality will be measured using the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) metric, computed between 50,000 generated samples and the training set. For captioning, captions will be tokenized and encoded as analog bits, with evaluation using BLEU-4, CIDEr, and ROUGE-L metrics. Baselines will include state-of-the-art autoregressive models and existing discrete diffusion models. Model architectures will be based on U-Net for images and Transformer decoders for captions, with extensive ablations on self-conditioning and time interval strategies.
b64537bdf7a103aa01972ba06ea24a9c08f7cd74.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the concept of analog bits, enabling continuous diffusion models to natively generate discrete data without reformulating the state space. The approach is further enhanced by novel self-conditioning and asymmetric time interval techniques, both of which significantly improve sample quality and efficiency. The method achieves state-of-the-art results in discrete image generation, outperforming leading autoregressive and discrete diffusion models, and demonstrates competitive performance in image captioning. The framework is simple, generic, and extensible, requiring minimal modifications to existing diffusion models.

b64fb9eb7a9f523ee15e9a1fe4170cc1d8189fc3.title: Knowledge Graph Reasoning with Relational Digraph
b64fb9eb7a9f523ee15e9a1fe4170cc1d8189fc3.research_question: How can knowledge graph reasoning be improved by leveraging richer relational structures that capture both semantic and local evidence, while maintaining efficiency and interpretability in both inductive and transductive settings?
b64fb9eb7a9f523ee15e9a1fe4170cc1d8189fc3.hypothesis: Introducing a novel relational structure, the relational directed graph (r-digraph), and developing an efficient, query-dependent graph neural network (RED-GNN) will enable more effective and interpretable reasoning over knowledge graphs by capturing complex local evidence and overlapping relational paths, outperforming existing path-based and subgraph-based methods.
b64fb9eb7a9f523ee15e9a1fe4170cc1d8189fc3.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed that generalizes relational paths into r-digraphs, which are subgraphs composed of overlapping relational paths between query and answer entities. To efficiently construct and learn from these r-digraphs, a variant of graph neural network, RED-GNN, will be designed. RED-GNN will recursively encode multiple r-digraphs with shared edges using dynamic programming, significantly reducing redundant computation. A query-dependent attention mechanism will be integrated to select strongly correlated edges within the r-digraph, allowing the model to focus on the most relevant local evidence for each query. The model will be trained end-to-end using a multi-class log-loss, and the learned attention weights will provide interpretable evidence for the reasoning process.
b64fb9eb7a9f523ee15e9a1fe4170cc1d8189fc3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard knowledge graph reasoning benchmarks, including both inductive and transductive settings. Datasets such as WN18RR, FB15k-237, NELL-995, Family, and UMLS will be used, with appropriate splits for training, validation, and testing. Baselines will include rule-based methods (RuleN, NeuralLP, DRUM), path-based methods (MINERVA, PathCon, RNNLogic), and GNN-based methods (CompGCN, DPMPN, GraIL). Evaluation metrics will include mean reciprocal rank (MRR), Hit@1, and Hit@10, using filtered ranking and tie-aware policies. Hyperparameters will be tuned via grid search, and computational efficiency will be assessed by measuring training and inference time, as well as model parameter size. Ablation studies and case studies on interpretability will further validate the approach.
b64fb9eb7a9f523ee15e9a1fe4170cc1d8189fc3.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the r-digraph as a new relational structure that unifies the strengths of relational paths and subgraphs, enabling the capture of complex local evidence in knowledge graphs. The RED-GNN model leverages dynamic programming for efficient recursive encoding of overlapping r-digraphs and incorporates a query-dependent attention mechanism for interpretable and adaptive reasoning. This approach is claimed to achieve state-of-the-art performance in both inductive and transductive reasoning tasks, with significant improvements in efficiency and interpretability over existing methods.

b66e5f0b5a8835e62fc3f31ad515e9861c71510c.title: Erwin: A Tree-based Hierarchical Transformer for Large-scale Physical Systems
b66e5f0b5a8835e62fc3f31ad515e9861c71510c.research_question: How can deep learning architectures be scaled efficiently and effectively to model large-scale physical systems defined on irregular grids, particularly in the presence of long-range interactions and multi-scale coupling?
b66e5f0b5a8835e62fc3f31ad515e9861c71510c.hypothesis: A hierarchical transformer architecture that leverages tree-based partitioning can achieve linear computational complexity while maintaining or improving prediction accuracy for large-scale physical systems with irregular geometries and long-range dependencies.
b66e5f0b5a8835e62fc3f31ad515e9861c71510c.proposed_method: A new hierarchical transformer framework is developed that organizes computation over irregular point clouds using ball tree partitioning. The method constructs a perfect binary ball tree over the input data, recursively partitioning points into nested sets (balls) of equal size, each represented by a center and radius. Self-attention is computed independently within each ball at fixed hierarchy levels, enabling localized computation with linear complexity in the number of nodes. To capture both local and global features, the architecture alternates between progressive coarsening (aggregating features at coarser tree levels) and refinement (distributing coarse features back to finer scales), and introduces a novel cross-ball interaction mechanism by rotating the point cloud and recomputing the ball tree, allowing information flow between otherwise separated regions. The model incorporates positional encodings and distance-based attention biases to enhance geometric awareness, and is structured in a UNet-like encoder-decoder with skip connections for multi-scale feature integration.
b66e5f0b5a8835e62fc3f31ad515e9861c71510c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a diverse set of large-scale physical domains, including cosmological simulations (N-body point clouds with 5,000 nodes), molecular dynamics (coarse-grained polymers with up to thousands of atoms), partial differential equation (PDE) benchmarks (on both point clouds and structured/unstructured meshes), and turbulent fluid dynamics (EAGLE dataset with 1.1 million 2D meshes, averaging 3,388 nodes each). Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art graph neural networks (MPNN, SEGNN, NequIP), transformer-based models (PointTransformer v3, OctFormer, Transolver, UPT), and other relevant architectures (PointNet++, MeshGraphNet, GAT, DilResNet). Evaluation metrics will include mean squared error (MSE), root mean squared error (RMSE), negative log-likelihood (NLL), and relative L2 error, depending on the task. The experimental setup will systematically vary training set sizes, window/ball sizes, and architectural ablations (e.g., with/without cross-ball connections, coarsening, and different embedding modules) to assess scalability, computational efficiency (runtime, memory), and predictive accuracy.
b66e5f0b5a8835e62fc3f31ad515e9861c71510c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the use of ball tree partitioning to enable linear-time self-attention for irregular point clouds, overcoming the quadratic scaling bottleneck of traditional attention mechanisms. The hierarchical transformer design combines progressive coarsening and refinement of the ball tree with a novel cross-ball interaction mechanism, allowing simultaneous capture of fine-grained local details and global features. The method achieves state-of-the-art performance in both computational efficiency and prediction accuracy across multiple large-scale physical domains, and demonstrates superior scalability compared to existing graph-based and transformer-based models. The architecture is hardware-efficient, generalizes to a variety of scientific learning tasks, and provides a flexible framework for modeling complex, multi-scale, and long-range interactions in physical systems.

b686dfbb55d541562e7a56d0cac21df48e979be6.title: Faster Algorithms for Computing the Stationary Distribution, Simulating Random Walks, and More
b686dfbb55d541562e7a56d0cac21df48e979be6.research_question: How can fundamental quantities associated with random walks on directed graphs, such as the stationary distribution, personalized PageRank vectors, hitting times, and escape probabilities, be computed more efficiently than with existing general-purpose linear algebra methods?
b686dfbb55d541562e7a56d0cac21df48e979be6.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by developing specialized algorithms for solving directed Laplacian systems and leveraging reductions to Eulerian Laplacians and RCDD Z-matrices, it is possible to asymptotically improve the running time for computing key random walk quantities on directed graphs, surpassing the performance of general linear system solvers and fast matrix multiplication, especially for sparse graphs.
b686dfbb55d541562e7a56d0cac21df48e979be6.proposed_method: The proposed approach centers on designing faster algorithms for solving linear systems in directed Laplacians, which are natural asymmetric analogs of undirected Laplacians. The method involves reducing a variety of random walk-related problems to the solution of a small number of directed Laplacian systems, particularly on Eulerian graphs. To solve Eulerian Laplacian systems, the method preconditions the system using the symmetrized Laplacian (U = 1/2(L + L^T)), applies the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse, and leverages nearly-linear-time Laplacian solvers. The approach further employs preconditioning and subsampling, using low-rank updates and the Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury identity, to efficiently solve systems in matrices of the form L^T U^+ L + αU. For more general classes of matrices (RCDD Z-matrices), the method reduces their solution to Eulerian Laplacian systems by embedding them into larger Eulerian systems. The stationary distribution is computed by iteratively scaling and updating the Laplacian to obtain an Eulerian form, then solving the resulting system, and similar techniques are applied to compute personalized PageRank, hitting times, escape probabilities, and commute times.
b686dfbb55d541562e7a56d0cac21df48e979be6.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate the proposed algorithms on directed graphs with n vertices and m edges, including both synthetic and real-world datasets. The algorithms will be benchmarked against existing state-of-the-art methods, such as iterative solvers and approaches based on fast matrix multiplication. Evaluation metrics will include running time (asymptotic and empirical), accuracy of computed quantities (e.g., ℓ2 distance to the true stationary distribution or personalized PageRank vector), and scalability with respect to graph size and sparsity. The experimental setup will also assess the impact of graph condition numbers (e.g., mixing time, restart probability) on performance, and will include tests on sparse graphs to demonstrate breaking the O(n^2) barrier. Additional experiments will validate the stability and numerical precision of the algorithms in the standard RAM computational model.
b686dfbb55d541562e7a56d0cac21df48e979be6.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first algorithms that asymptotically improve the running time for solving directed Laplacian systems and computing associated random walk quantities on directed graphs, surpassing the performance of general linear system solvers and fast matrix multiplication, especially for sparse graphs. The method breaks the O(n^2) barrier for sparse instances and provides a unified framework for efficiently computing stationary distributions, personalized PageRank vectors, hitting times, escape probabilities, and all-pairs commute times. The approach also extends sketching techniques for commute times from undirected to directed graphs and provides new reductions and algorithmic primitives for directed spectral graph theory.

b6948a9e8b3eec5a56a80c69727154fcd7ececce.title: AgentPoison: Red-teaming LLM Agents via Poisoning Memory or Knowledge Bases
b6948a9e8b3eec5a56a80c69727154fcd7ececce.research_question: How vulnerable are large language model (LLM) agents that utilize retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) or memory modules to backdoor attacks via poisoning their knowledge bases or long-term memory, and what methodologies can be developed to systematically red-team and assess these vulnerabilities?
b6948a9e8b3eec5a56a80c69727154fcd7ececce.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that LLM agents relying on RAG or memory modules can be effectively compromised by injecting a small number of malicious, stealthy demonstrations into their knowledge bases or memories, such that the agent will reliably retrieve these demonstrations and execute adversarial actions when presented with optimized trigger queries, while maintaining normal performance on benign queries.
b6948a9e8b3eec5a56a80c69727154fcd7ececce.proposed_method: A novel red-teaming framework, AGENTPOISON, will be developed to conduct backdoor attacks on RAG-based LLM agents by poisoning their memory or knowledge base with a minimal set of optimized malicious demonstrations. The approach formulates trigger generation as a constrained optimization problem, aiming to map triggered queries into a unique and compact region of the embedding space, maximizing retrieval of poisoned instances while preserving agent utility for benign inputs. The optimization objective jointly minimizes uniqueness loss (to separate triggered from benign queries), compactness loss (to cluster triggered queries), target generation loss (to induce the adversarial action), and coherence loss (to ensure the trigger is stealthy and contextually appropriate). A gradient-guided beam search algorithm will be employed to search for discrete trigger tokens that satisfy these constraints, requiring no additional model training or fine-tuning.
b6948a9e8b3eec5a56a80c69727154fcd7ececce.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three real-world LLM agent types: an autonomous driving agent (Agent-Driver), a knowledge-intensive QA agent (ReAct-StrategyQA), and a healthcare record management agent (EHRAgent). The corresponding datasets include a driving experience memory set (23k entries), a curated Wikipedia-based QA knowledge base (10k passages), and an augmented healthcare memory set (700+ entries). The attack will be benchmarked against four baselines (GCG, AutoDAN, CPA, BadChain), using metrics such as retrieval attack success rate (ASR-r), target action attack success rate (ASR-a), end-to-end attack success rate (ASR-t), and benign accuracy (ACC). The setup will test various LLM backbones (GPT-3.5, LLaMA3) and retriever types (end-to-end and contrastive), with poison rates below 0.1%. Additional studies will assess trigger transferability across retrievers, resilience to perturbations, and robustness against perplexity-based and rephrasing defenses.
b6948a9e8b3eec5a56a80c69727154fcd7ececce.novelty_claims: The proposed approach constitutes the first systematic red-teaming and backdoor attack framework targeting generic RAG-based LLM agents via memory or knowledge base poisoning. AGENTPOISON introduces a novel constrained optimization for trigger generation that ensures high retrieval and attack success rates with minimal poisoned instances and negligible impact on benign performance. The method demonstrates high transferability of triggers across different embedding models, resilience to various input perturbations, and stealthiness against standard defenses. Unlike prior attacks, AGENTPOISON requires no model retraining or fine-tuning, and achieves state-of-the-art attack efficacy and stealth.

b69882cb6c7367ea91224c27982277c5e643862e.title: VeriGen: A Large Language Model for Verilog Code Generation
b69882cb6c7367ea91224c27982277c5e643862e.research_question: Can large language models be effectively adapted to automate the generation of high-quality Verilog code for digital hardware design, and how does their performance compare to existing commercial and open-source solutions across a range of hardware design tasks?
b69882cb6c7367ea91224c27982277c5e643862e.hypothesis: Fine-tuning large language models on a curated and diverse corpus of Verilog code will significantly improve their ability to generate syntactically and functionally correct Verilog code, potentially outperforming or matching commercial state-of-the-art models, especially in scenarios requiring domain-specific knowledge.
b69882cb6c7367ea91224c27982277c5e643862e.proposed_method: A comprehensive Verilog training corpus will be constructed by aggregating and cleaning open-source Verilog code from public GitHub repositories and extracting relevant content from Verilog textbooks using OCR and regular expressions. Multiple pre-trained large language models (LLMs) of varying sizes and architectures, including CodeGen (2B, 6B, 16B), MegatronLM, and J1-Large, will be fine-tuned on this corpus using high-performance computing resources and advanced parallelization strategies (e.g., ZeRO, DeepSpeed). Fine-tuning will be performed with default hyperparameters, and models will be trained for one or more epochs depending on hardware constraints. The resulting models will be evaluated using a two-pronged approach: a hand-designed problem set with exhaustive and unit testbenches, and a large-scale benchmark derived from the HDLBits platform, with prompts varying in detail and structure to assess robustness.
b69882cb6c7367ea91224c27982277c5e643862e.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize two main evaluation sets: (1) a hand-crafted set of 17 Verilog design problems with varying difficulty, each accompanied by custom testbenches for functional validation, and (2) an extended set of 181 problems sourced from HDLBits, covering a broad spectrum of hardware design categories and difficulty levels. For each problem, prompts will be generated at multiple detail levels, and models will be queried with varying sampling temperatures and numbers of completions per prompt. Baseline comparisons will include both the fine-tuned open-source models and leading commercial LLMs such as GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4, and PALM2. Evaluation metrics will focus on syntactic correctness (successful compilation) and functional correctness (passing all testbench cases), with additional analysis of the impact of model size, prompt detail, and dataset augmentation. Simulation and synthesis tools such as Icarus Verilog and the HDLBits online judge will be used to automate correctness checks.
b69882cb6c7367ea91224c27982277c5e643862e.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the largest known open-source Verilog training corpus for LLM fine-tuning, along with a systematic methodology for evaluating Verilog code generation at scale. It pioneers the comprehensive benchmarking of both open-source and commercial LLMs on hardware design tasks, demonstrating that smaller, fine-tuned, in-house models can achieve or surpass the performance of much larger commercial models in Verilog code generation. The approach also provides open-source training and evaluation scripts, as well as model checkpoints, to facilitate further research in hardware design automation using LLMs.

b698dbfaf9b961502062cbfcbe05d319047d8495.title: Towards Understanding Sharpness-Aware Minimization
b698dbfaf9b961502062cbfcbe05d319047d8495.research_question: What are the underlying mechanisms and theoretical explanations for the generalization improvements observed with Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) and its variants, particularly m-SAM, in deep neural network training?
b698dbfaf9b961502062cbfcbe05d319047d8495.hypothesis: The generalization benefits of SAM, especially with low-m sharpness, are not fully explained by existing PAC-Bayes generalization bounds or by convergence to flat minima; instead, these benefits arise from a distinct implicit bias in the optimization trajectory that can be theoretically characterized and empirically observed.
b698dbfaf9b961502062cbfcbe05d319047d8495.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted to analyze the implicit bias induced by SAM and its m-SAM variant. The approach will include: (1) theoretical analysis of the implicit bias for diagonal linear networks, showing how SAM selects solutions with better generalization properties compared to standard gradient descent, and quantifying the effect of m-sharpness; (2) empirical studies on non-linear and deep networks to characterize the properties of the implicit bias, including experiments on fine-tuning standard models with SAM; (3) development of convergence results for SAM in non-convex objectives under stochastic gradient settings, including proofs of convergence to stationary points and analysis of step size requirements; and (4) systematic evaluation of the role of worst-case weight perturbations and batch size in the effectiveness of SAM.
b698dbfaf9b961502062cbfcbe05d319047d8495.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard deep learning benchmarks such as CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 using architectures like ResNet-18 and ResNet-34. Training will be performed with standard data augmentation and varying batch sizes (e.g., 128 and 1024). The study will compare different weight perturbation methods: empirical risk minimization (ERM), random perturbations, n-SAM, and m-SAM with various values of m. Evaluation metrics will include test error, training error, m-sharpness, and suboptimality factors. Additional experiments will analyze the effect of switching between ERM and SAM at different training stages, the impact of label noise, and the role of batch normalization versus group normalization. Hyperparameters such as perturbation radius and number of projected gradient ascent steps will be systematically varied and ablated.
b698dbfaf9b961502062cbfcbe05d319047d8495.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new theoretical framework for understanding the implicit bias of SAM and its variants, demonstrating that the generalization improvements are due to a bias toward solutions with favorable complexity measures (e.g., lower l1-norm in linear settings) rather than previously hypothesized mechanisms. It provides the first convergence guarantees for SAM under non-convex stochastic settings and empirically shows that fine-tuning with SAM can substantially improve generalization even when starting from standard ERM solutions. The work also clarifies the essential role of low-m, worst-case perturbations and challenges the sufficiency of existing generalization bounds and flatness-based explanations.

b6aefb73267f3ab95522b560d46a086a22883d1a.title: Learning Rule-Induced Subgraph Representations for Inductive Relation Prediction
b6aefb73267f3ab95522b560d46a086a22883d1a.research_question: How can inductive relation prediction in evolving knowledge graphs be improved by learning subgraph representations that more effectively capture relevant logical rules while eliminating irrelevant ones, thereby enhancing reasoning performance and scalability?
b6aefb73267f3ab95522b560d46a086a22883d1a.hypothesis: A single-source edge-wise graph neural network (GNN) that initializes edge features only for the target link and employs RNN-based edge-wise message passing can learn rule-induced subgraph representations that encode only relevant logical rules, leading to improved inductive relation prediction accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods.
b6aefb73267f3ab95522b560d46a086a22883d1a.proposed_method: A novel single-source edge-wise GNN framework, termed REST, is proposed to learn rule-induced subgraph representations for inductive relation prediction. The approach begins by extracting a local subgraph around each query triple, omitting node labeling to accelerate preprocessing. Single-source initialization is applied, where only the target link receives a nonzero embedding based on its relation, while all other links are initialized to zero. Edge-wise message passing is then performed using RNN-based functions (GRU for message computation and LSTM for edge updates), allowing the model to capture the sequential properties of logical rules and to aggregate information only along cycles that include the target link. The final representation of the target link is used for scoring its plausibility, ensuring that only relevant rules are encoded in the subgraph representation.
b6aefb73267f3ab95522b560d46a086a22883d1a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three standard inductive relation prediction benchmark datasets derived from WN18RR, FB15k-237, and NELL-995, ensuring no entity overlap between training and test splits. The proposed REST method will be compared against both rule-based baselines (NeuralLP, DRUM, RuleN) and subgraph-based baselines (GraIL, CoMPILE, TACT, SNRI, ConGLR), using the Hits@10 metric under a filtered setting with 50 randomly sampled negative triples per test query. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of single-source initialization and various message/update functions, and subgraph extraction efficiency will be evaluated by comparing preprocessing times with existing methods. All experiments will be repeated with multiple random seeds and implemented using PyTorch and DGL.
b6aefb73267f3ab95522b560d46a086a22883d1a.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a single-source initialization strategy that assigns nonzero embeddings exclusively to the target link, ensuring that only relevant logical rules are captured during message passing. The edge-wise message passing framework, utilizing RNN-based functions, models the sequential nature of logical rules, which is not addressed by previous subgraph-based approaches. REST eliminates the need for node labeling in subgraph extraction, significantly improving preprocessing efficiency (up to 11.66× faster). The approach is theoretically proven to learn rule-induced subgraph representations, providing both improved reasoning accuracy and practical interpretability. REST achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple inductive relation prediction benchmarks, demonstrating its effectiveness and scalability.

b6bb3b09d6b77d008adc4788c9212a90040f2376.title: CLIPSelf: Vision Transformer Distills Itself for Open-Vocabulary Dense Prediction
b6bb3b09d6b77d008adc4788c9212a90040f2376.research_question: How can the dense region representations of vision transformer-based vision-language models be enhanced to improve open-vocabulary dense prediction tasks such as object detection and segmentation, without relying on region-text pair annotations?
b6bb3b09d6b77d008adc4788c9212a90040f2376.hypothesis: Self-distillation of vision transformer-based vision-language models, by aligning region representations from dense feature maps with image-level representations of corresponding image crops, will significantly improve region-language alignment and downstream open-vocabulary dense prediction performance, even in the absence of region-text pair supervision.
b6bb3b09d6b77d008adc4788c9212a90040f2376.proposed_method: A self-distillation framework, termed CLIPSelf, is proposed to fine-tune vision transformer-based vision-language models (specifically CLIP ViTs) for improved dense region representation. The method partitions each input image into a grid of randomly sized patches, then aligns the region representation pooled from the student's dense feature map (via RoIAlign or mask pooling) with the image-level representation of the same patch obtained from a frozen teacher model. The cosine similarity between the student region embedding and the teacher image embedding is maximized as the self-distillation loss. The student model is initialized from the teacher's weights and is fine-tuned using only image data, without any region-text pairs. The approach is flexible to use either grid patches or region proposals, and can be applied to various downstream tasks by replacing the backbone in existing dense prediction frameworks with the fine-tuned model.
b6bb3b09d6b77d008adc4788c9212a90040f2376.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on open-vocabulary object detection, semantic segmentation, and panoptic segmentation tasks. For detection, two-stage detectors are built on frozen and fine-tuned CLIP ViTs, evaluated on OV-COCO and OV-LVIS benchmarks using AP metrics. For segmentation, the fine-tuned models are integrated into Cat-Seg and ODISE frameworks, with evaluation on ADE20K, PASCAL Context, and COCO Panoptic datasets using mIoU, mAcc, PQ, and mAP metrics. Ablation studies investigate the effects of patch split size, number of trainable layers, and input resolution. Baselines include methods using region-text pairs, frozen CLIP CNNs, and other state-of-the-art open-vocabulary models. Additional experiments explore the use of local window attention and out-of-domain datasets (e.g., CC3M) for self-distillation.
b6bb3b09d6b77d008adc4788c9212a90040f2376.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to explicitly inject strong region-language alignment into vision transformer-based vision-language models through self-distillation, without requiring region-text pair annotations. It bridges the gap between global image-level and local region representations in CLIP ViTs, enabling their effective use in open-vocabulary dense prediction tasks. The method is annotation-free, generalizable across tasks, and applicable to various model architectures, including those with local window attention. Experimental results demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on multiple open-vocabulary benchmarks, surpassing both region-text pair-based and prior self-supervised approaches.

b6bd1c1028cd2f24470aacac1b6d590c35ff51ef.title: Perceive Anything: Recognize, Explain, Caption, and Segment Anything in Images and Videos
b6bd1c1028cd2f24470aacac1b6d590c35ff51ef.research_question: How can a unified and efficient framework be developed to enable comprehensive region-level visual understanding—including recognition, explanation, captioning, and segmentation—across both images and videos, supporting multi-granular and streaming semantic outputs?
b6bd1c1028cd2f24470aacac1b6d590c35ff51ef.hypothesis: Integrating a powerful segmentation model with large language models, and leveraging a dedicated semantic perceiver to bridge visual and language modalities, will enable simultaneous and efficient region-level segmentation and generation of diverse, context-aware semantic outputs for images and videos, including streaming video captioning.
b6bd1c1028cd2f24470aacac1b6d590c35ff51ef.proposed_method: A novel framework will be designed that extends a robust segmentation backbone (such as SAM2) with a large language model (LLM) semantic decoder, connected via a lightweight Semantic Perceiver module. The Semantic Perceiver will transform rich intermediate visual features—including mask tokens, IoU, and prompt tokens—into multi-modal tokens suitable for LLM comprehension. The model will feature parallel mask and semantic decoders, enabling simultaneous generation of segmentation masks and diverse semantic outputs (category, definition, function, detailed captions) for specified regions in both images and videos. For streaming video captioning, a memory module and pixel shuffle operations will be employed to propagate historical visual and textual context across video clips, ensuring temporally consistent and contextually rich region-level descriptions. Training will follow a three-stage curriculum: image pretraining, video-enhanced pretraining, and multimodal supervised fine-tuning, with the segmentation backbone frozen throughout.
b6bd1c1028cd2f24470aacac1b6d590c35ff51ef.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a wide range of region-level recognition and captioning benchmarks for both images and videos. Image datasets will include LVIS, PACO, COCO-Text, and Total-Text for recognition and explanation tasks, and RefCOCOg, Visual Genome, Ref-L4, Ferret-Bench, and MDVP-Bench for region-level captioning, evaluated using metrics such as Semantic Similarity, Semantic IoU, accuracy, ROUGE-L, METEOR, and CIDEr. Video benchmarks will include Elysium, BensMOT, HC-STVG, and VideoRefer-Bench-D for regional video captioning, and ActivityNet for streaming region-level captioning, using CIDEr, METEOR, and a custom GPT-4o-evaluated Spatio-Temporal Description Continuity Score (G-STDC). Baselines will include state-of-the-art region-level vision-language models and streaming video captioning models. All evaluations will be performed in a zero-shot setting without dataset-specific fine-tuning. The training dataset will be constructed via an advanced data refinement and augmentation pipeline, resulting in 1.5M image and 0.6M video region-semantic annotations, including bilingual (English/Chinese) and streaming video captions.
b6bd1c1028cd2f24470aacac1b6d590c35ff51ef.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to enable comprehensive, multi-granular region-level visual understanding—including recognition, explanation, captioning, and segmentation—across both images and videos within a single, efficient model. It introduces a Semantic Perceiver module that efficiently bridges segmentation features and language models for region-level semantic decoding. The method supports streaming video region captioning with temporally consistent outputs, enabled by novel data augmentation and memory mechanisms. A new high-quality, large-scale dataset with multi-level semantic annotations and streaming video captions is constructed, including bilingual support. The approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks while being significantly faster and more memory-efficient than prior methods.

b6e773e8a69ae6c13c5fab08a6d97b554318ea19.title: Multiple Physics Pretraining for Physical Surrogate Models
b6e773e8a69ae6c13c5fab08a6d97b554318ea19.research_question: How can large-scale, task-agnostic pretraining be leveraged to develop spatiotemporal surrogate models that generalize across multiple heterogeneous physical systems, and does such pretraining facilitate improved transfer learning to new or low-data physical regimes, including higher-dimensional systems?
b6e773e8a69ae6c13c5fab08a6d97b554318ea19.hypothesis: 1. A single model can learn the dynamics for multiple classes of physical behavior. 2. Learning partially overlapping physics is beneficial for transfer learning.
b6e773e8a69ae6c13c5fab08a6d97b554318ea19.proposed_method: A novel pretraining strategy, Multiple Physics Pretraining (MPP), will be developed for spatiotemporal surrogate modeling using transformer architectures. The approach will embed fields from diverse physical systems into a shared embedding space via per-sample Reversible Instance Normalization (RevIN) and system-specific learned field embeddings. An Axial Vision Transformer (AViT) backbone will be employed, utilizing scalable axial attention to process high-dimensional spatiotemporal data efficiently. The model will be trained autoregressively to predict the next state of the system, with a normalized mean squared error (NMSE) loss to balance contributions from systems with varying scales. Task sampling during training will ensure efficient hardware utilization and diverse batches by randomly sampling systems and accumulating gradients over micro-batches. The architecture will be designed to allow for inflation to higher-dimensional systems (e.g., from 2D to 3D) via kernel inflation techniques.
b6e773e8a69ae6c13c5fab08a6d97b554318ea19.experiment_details: Experiments will use the PDEBench benchmark suite, which contains two-dimensional time-dependent simulations from four nonlinear PDEs (compressible/incompressible Navier-Stokes, shallow water equations, and 2D diffusion-reaction) with varied state variables, resolutions, initial/boundary conditions, and simulation parameters. The proposed MPP models will be compared against dedicated baselines such as UNet, FNO (Fourier Neural Operator), and ORCA-SWIN, as well as task-specific AViT models and pretrained video transformer models (VideoMAE). Evaluation metrics will include Normalized Root Mean Squared Error (NRMSE) averaged over fields and examples. Experiments will assess: (1) multi-task learning performance without finetuning, (2) transfer learning to previously unseen physics (including low-data regimes and new parameter regimes), and (3) transfer to higher-dimensional (3D) systems via model inflation. Ablation studies will examine the impact of normalization and balanced loss objectives.
b6e773e8a69ae6c13c5fab08a6d97b554318ea19.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a scalable, autoregressive, task-agnostic pretraining framework for physical surrogate modeling that enables a single transformer model to learn and predict the dynamics of multiple heterogeneous physical systems simultaneously. A novel shared embedding and normalization strategy is developed to unify fields from different systems, facilitating transfer learning across diverse physics. The approach demonstrates, for the first time, successful large-scale pretraining across multiple nonlinear physics for spatiotemporal systems, outperforming or matching task-specific baselines without finetuning and enabling superior transfer to new physical regimes and higher-dimensional systems. The method also provides an efficient pathway for model inflation from 2D to 3D, addressing the computational challenges of high-dimensional physical simulation.

b6f6263a206c18e4fb9e01ed26af532a9bd44b3a.title: OSVI-WM: One-Shot Visual Imitation for Unseen Tasks using World-Model-Guided Trajectory Generation
b6f6263a206c18e4fb9e01ed26af532a9bd44b3a.research_question: How can a robotic agent perform one-shot visual imitation of unseen tasks, given only a single expert demonstration video and the agent's initial observation, especially when the agent and expert may have different embodiments and there is no direct alignment between their states or actions?
b6f6263a206c18e4fb9e01ed26af532a9bd44b3a.hypothesis: A world-model-guided trajectory generation framework that predicts future latent states and actions from a single expert demonstration and the agent's initial observation will enable robust one-shot visual imitation, improving generalization to unseen tasks and outperforming existing methods, even under embodiment mismatch and without large-scale pretraining.
b6f6263a206c18e4fb9e01ed26af532a9bd44b3a.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces an end-to-end framework for one-shot visual imitation learning, leveraging a world-model-guided trajectory generation approach. Expert demonstration frames and the agent's initial observation are encoded into a shared latent space using a ResNet-18 encoder. A recursive module, comprising an action model and a world model, predicts a sequence of future latent states and actions in this latent space, modeling environment dynamics and enabling future-aware planning. The predicted latent trajectory is then decoded into physical waypoints using spatial and temporal pooling, followed by an MLP-based waypoint predictor, which outputs a sequence of attributed waypoints (3D position and gripper state) for robotic control. An auxiliary loss is applied to the predicted latent trajectory to enhance the world model's ability to capture environment dynamics, and a re-planning mechanism is incorporated to improve robustness by allowing the agent to re-plan waypoints based on updated observations if the task is not completed.
b6f6263a206c18e4fb9e01ed26af532a9bd44b3a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both simulated and real-world robotic benchmarks. Simulated environments include Meta-World (50 manipulation tasks, with 46 for training and 4 for testing, where test tasks differ semantically and structurally from training) and Pick-and-Place (16 tasks, with different expert and agent embodiments). Real-world setups involve Two-Franka-PP (two Franka arms at different locations), Human-Franka-PP (human expert and Franka agent), and Human-Franka-Push (human expert and Franka agent, pushing tasks). Each method will be evaluated over multiple rollouts per task, using success rate as the primary metric, with additional breakdowns for sub-tasks like reaching and grasping. Baselines will include DAML, T-OSVI, and AWDA, with and without additional training data. Ablation studies will assess the impact of key architectural components, such as the world-model-guided trajectory generation, auxiliary losses, and re-planning. Training will use in-domain data only, with demonstration image mixup regularization and early stopping to prevent overfitting.
b6f6263a206c18e4fb9e01ed26af532a9bd44b3a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel world-model-guided trajectory generation module tailored for one-shot visual imitation on unseen tasks, enabling future-aware planning in a latent space. Unlike prior methods, the framework is trained entirely on in-domain data without large-scale pretraining, supports embodiment mismatch between expert and agent, and incorporates a robust waypoint controller with re-planning. The method achieves substantial improvements in success rates over state-of-the-art baselines, particularly on tasks that require generalization to new semantics or structures, and demonstrates strong applicability to real-world robotic platforms.

b7016f306bb22ed98036c218c30f1c4d301d034c.title: Transformer-based Planning for Symbolic Regression
b7016f306bb22ed98036c218c30f1c4d301d034c.research_question: How can symbolic regression models be improved to generate mathematical expressions that optimally balance fitting accuracy and complexity, while also enhancing extrapolation and robustness to noise?
b7016f306bb22ed98036c218c30f1c4d301d034c.hypothesis: Incorporating a planning-based decoding strategy that leverages non-differentiable feedback, such as fitting accuracy and equation complexity, into transformer-based symbolic regression models will result in generated equations with superior fitting-complexity trade-offs, improved extrapolation, and greater robustness to noise compared to existing decoding strategies.
b7016f306bb22ed98036c218c30f1c4d301d034c.proposed_method: A novel decoding framework, Transformer-based Planning for Symbolic Regression (TPSR), will be developed by integrating Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) into the inference process of pre-trained transformer-based symbolic regression models. The method frames equation generation as a Markov Decision Process, where each state represents a partially generated equation and actions correspond to selecting the next token. MCTS is used to guide the sequence generation by incorporating both the model's next-token probabilities and external, non-differentiable feedback such as fitting accuracy and equation complexity. The reward function is designed to balance normalized mean squared error (NMSE) and equation complexity, with a tunable parameter to control the trade-off. To enhance efficiency, top-k and sequence caching mechanisms are implemented, reducing redundant computations during tree search and beam search expansions.
b7016f306bb22ed98036c218c30f1c4d301d034c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard symbolic regression benchmark datasets, including SRBench (with Feynman, Strogatz, and Black-box datasets) and In-domain Synthetic datasets. The proposed TPSR method will be evaluated using pre-trained transformer backbones, such as the E2E model, and compared against baselines utilizing beam search and sampling decoding strategies, as well as state-of-the-art genetic programming and regression models. Evaluation metrics will include R2 score, accuracy at various tolerance thresholds, and equation complexity (measured by expression tree size). Experimental setups will systematically vary the trade-off parameter in the reward function, as well as MCTS parameters (number of rollouts, beam size, top-k expansions), and include ablation studies on caching mechanisms and search parameters. Extrapolation and robustness to noise will be assessed by testing on out-of-distribution data and datasets with varying noise levels.
b7016f306bb22ed98036c218c30f1c4d301d034c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a model-agnostic, planning-based decoding strategy for symbolic regression that directly incorporates non-differentiable feedback into the sequence generation process via MCTS. Unlike conventional transformer decoding methods, this framework enables optimization for objectives beyond token-level accuracy, such as fitting and complexity. The method also features efficient caching mechanisms for scalable inference. The approach is claimed to achieve superior fitting-complexity trade-offs, enhanced extrapolation, and improved robustness to noise compared to existing state-of-the-art baselines.

b71e0b8be745eae27825315a26a3cc3b723cf729.title: Haste Makes Waste: A Simple Approach for Scaling Graph Neural Networks
b71e0b8be745eae27825315a26a3cc3b723cf729.research_question: How can the performance and scalability of graph neural networks (GNNs) be improved on large-scale graphs, particularly in the presence of neighborhood explosion and feature staleness, while maintaining efficiency and compatibility with existing GNN frameworks?
b71e0b8be745eae27825315a26a3cc3b723cf729.hypothesis: Decoupling the forward and backward propagation phases in GNN training and dynamically increasing the frequency of memory table updates for historical embeddings will significantly reduce feature staleness, leading to improved model performance, faster convergence, and better scalability on large-scale graph datasets.
b71e0b8be745eae27825315a26a3cc3b723cf729.proposed_method: A novel training algorithm, REST (REducing STaleness), is proposed to address the staleness of historical embeddings in scalable GNNs. The method decouples the forward and backward propagation phases, allowing the memory table containing node embeddings to be updated more frequently than the model parameters. Specifically, for each mini-batch, multiple forward passes are executed without gradient computation to refresh the memory table, followed by a forward and backward pass to update model parameters. This approach is highly flexible, orthogonal to existing sampling and memory-based methods, and can be integrated with various GNN backbones. An advanced variant, REST-IS, incorporates importance sampling by prioritizing the update of embeddings for nodes that are frequently sampled as neighbors, further mitigating the impact of staleness for high-importance nodes.
b71e0b8be745eae27825315a26a3cc3b723cf729.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several large-scale benchmark datasets, including ogbn-arxiv, ogbn-products, REDDIT, ogbn-papers100M, and MAG240M. The proposed methods will be evaluated using standard node classification tasks, with accuracy as the primary metric. Baselines will include state-of-the-art GNNs (GCN, GraphSAGE, FastGCN, Cluster-GCN, GraphSAINT, SGC), as well as historical embedding methods (GAS, VR-GCN, MVS-GCN, GraphFM) and recent staleness-mitigation techniques (ReFresh, LMC). The experimental setup will involve varying batch sizes, different GNN backbones (GCN, APPNP, GCNII), and ablation studies on the frequency of memory updates and batch sizes for memory refresh. Memory usage and training time will be measured to assess efficiency, and convergence speed will be analyzed by plotting accuracy versus time and epochs.
b71e0b8be745eae27825315a26a3cc3b723cf729.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple yet highly effective framework for reducing feature staleness in historical embedding-based GNNs by decoupling forward and backward propagation and increasing memory update frequency. This approach directly addresses the root cause of staleness, leading to significant improvements in prediction accuracy and convergence speed, especially on large-scale graphs and with small batch sizes. REST is highly general, compatible with any sampling strategy or GNN backbone, and can be seamlessly integrated with existing methods. The importance sampling variant, REST-IS, further enhances robustness by prioritizing updates for high-importance nodes. Experimental results demonstrate substantial performance gains over all major baselines, with up to 3.6% improvement on ogbn-products and accelerated convergence, all without increasing memory costs.

b732e65c2d5c0bbe868430873ad7f1a682cf2232.title: Algorithm Selection for Deep Active Learning with Imbalanced Datasets
b732e65c2d5c0bbe868430873ad7f1a682cf2232.research_question: How can an adaptive algorithm selection strategy be developed to automatically choose effective deep active learning algorithms for novel, unlabeled, and potentially class-imbalanced datasets, in both multi-class and multi-label classification settings?
b732e65c2d5c0bbe868430873ad7f1a682cf2232.hypothesis: An adaptive meta-algorithm that models the algorithm selection process as a multi-armed bandit problem and incorporates class-balance-aware reward functions will outperform or match the best available deep active learning algorithms in terms of label efficiency, classification accuracy, and class diversity across a variety of imbalanced datasets.
b732e65c2d5c0bbe868430873ad7f1a682cf2232.proposed_method: A meta-algorithm, TAILOR (Thompson Active Learning Algorithm Selection), will be developed to iteratively and adaptively select among a pool of candidate deep active learning algorithms. At each round, TAILOR will use Thompson Sampling to maintain and update posterior distributions over the expected reward (e.g., class diversity or positive label discovery) for each candidate algorithm, drawing samples from Beta or Dirichlet distributions depending on the classification setting (multi-label or multi-class). The reward function will be designed to encourage class-balanced selection by inversely weighting classes based on their current representation in the labeled set, or to prioritize positive label discovery in multi-label search tasks. In each batch, TAILOR will select a set of algorithms, run each to select examples, annotate the batch, update posteriors, and retrain the neural network model on the expanded labeled set. A discounting factor may be applied to handle non-stationarity in reward distributions.
b732e65c2d5c0bbe868430873ad7f1a682cf2232.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on ten datasets exhibiting various degrees of class imbalance, including four multi-label datasets (CelebA, COCO, VOC, Stanford Cars) and six multi-class datasets (ImageNet, Kuzushiji-49, Caltech256, imbalanced CIFAR-10, imbalanced CIFAR-100, imbalanced SVHN). The candidate pool will include a wide range of state-of-the-art deep active learning algorithms and per-class decomposed strategies, with the number of candidates ranging from tens to over a hundred. Baseline comparisons will include individual active learning algorithms, random meta-selection, and prior meta-algorithmic approaches (e.g., ALBL). Evaluation metrics will include mean average precision (multi-label), balanced accuracy (multi-class), class diversity (size of the smallest class in labeled set), and total number of positive labels collected. Experiments will be performed under limited annotation budgets (10-20 rounds, batch sizes from 500 to 10,000), and results will be averaged over multiple trials with standard error reported.
b732e65c2d5c0bbe868430873ad7f1a682cf2232.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first adaptive algorithm selection strategy for deep active learning, particularly effective in class-imbalanced settings. The method generalizes to both multi-label and multi-class tasks and can efficiently select among large pools of candidate algorithms under limited annotation budgets. The reward functions are specifically designed for class balance and positive label discovery, and the bandit reduction leverages full label observations for improved regret bounds over standard contextual bandit reductions. Extensive experiments are planned to demonstrate that the proposed method achieves accuracy and class diversity comparable to or better than the best candidate algorithm across diverse datasets.

b745b041e0d9410d7f49afaaff8c36bc838384b5.title: Regret Bounds for Markov Decision Processes with Recursive Optimized Certainty Equivalents
b745b041e0d9410d7f49afaaff8c36bc838384b5.research_question: How can reinforcement learning algorithms be designed to efficiently solve episodic, finite-horizon Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) under general risk-sensitive objectives, specifically those characterized by recursive optimized certainty equivalents (OCEs), and what are the fundamental regret limits in this setting?
b745b041e0d9410d7f49afaaff8c36bc838384b5.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a model-based reinforcement learning algorithm leveraging recursive OCEs and tailored exploration bonuses can achieve provably optimal regret bounds in risk-sensitive tabular MDPs, with regret scaling optimally in the number of episodes and actions, and that minimax lower bounds can be established for this general class of risk measures.
b745b041e0d9410d7f49afaaff8c36bc838384b5.proposed_method: A new model-based reinforcement learning algorithm, termed OCE-VI, will be developed for episodic, finite-horizon tabular MDPs with unknown transition probabilities and known reward functions. The algorithm will use recursive optimized certainty equivalents (OCEs) to define risk-sensitive value functions, replacing the expectation in standard Bellman updates with the OCE operator parameterized by a concave utility function. Exploration will be encouraged through an upper confidence bound (UCB) style bonus, which is explicitly dependent on the chosen utility function, thus adapting the degree of exploration to the agent's risk aversion. The OCE-VI algorithm will iteratively update empirical transition models, compute risk-sensitive Q-values via value iteration, and solve a one-dimensional concave optimization problem at each step to evaluate the OCE for the next-state value distribution. Theoretical analysis will employ concentration inequalities and a novel change-of-measure technique to handle the nonlinearity of the OCE and to derive regret bounds.
b745b041e0d9410d7f49afaaff8c36bc838384b5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on finite-horizon, tabular MDPs with finite state and action spaces, using a variety of utility functions to instantiate different OCEs, including mean, entropic risk, CVaR, and mean-variance. The OCE-VI algorithm will be compared against established baselines such as UCBVI for risk-neutral RL and specialized algorithms for entropic risk and CVaR. Evaluation metrics will include cumulative regret over K episodes, with particular attention to the dependence on the number of states, actions, horizon, and the specific risk measure. The experimental setup will involve repeated episodes with fixed or randomly initialized states, and the performance will be assessed both empirically and through theoretical regret upper and lower bounds. Computational tractability and scalability of the OCE-VI algorithm will also be evaluated, especially in terms of the efficiency of solving the OCE optimization at each step.
b745b041e0d9410d7f49afaaff8c36bc838384b5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to provide regret bounds for reinforcement learning in tabular MDPs with a broad family of recursive risk measures unified under the OCE framework, encompassing entropic risk, CVaR, and mean-variance as special cases. The exploration bonus is adaptively designed based on the agent's risk aversion, a novel feature not present in prior work. Theoretical contributions include new concentration bounds for OCEs of value functions and a general change-of-measure technique for regret analysis under nonlinear risk objectives. The minimax lower bounds established are tight up to logarithmic factors and generalize previous results for risk-neutral and specific risk-sensitive settings.

b768011c1dd42b13ae8a1c34b99ac4228304dabd.title: Fourier Neural Operator with Learned Deformations for PDEs on General Geometries
b768011c1dd42b13ae8a1c34b99ac4228304dabd.research_question: How can partial differential equations (PDEs) on arbitrary, potentially irregular geometries be efficiently and accurately solved using deep learning-based surrogate models, while maintaining computational efficiency and flexibility in input formats?
b768011c1dd42b13ae8a1c34b99ac4228304dabd.hypothesis: A neural operator framework that learns to deform irregular physical domains into uniform latent spaces, enabling the application of fast Fourier transforms (FFT) in the latent space, will achieve higher accuracy and computational efficiency for solving PDEs on general geometries compared to existing methods.
b768011c1dd42b13ae8a1c34b99ac4228304dabd.proposed_method: A geometry-aware Fourier Neural Operator (Geo-FNO) framework is developed to address PDEs on arbitrary geometries. The method introduces a learnable or fixed deformation map that transforms the irregular input domain into a uniform latent computational space, where the standard FNO architecture with FFT can be applied. The deformation is parameterized as a neural network and trained end-to-end alongside the solution operator, allowing the model to adaptively learn optimal mappings for various domain shapes and input formats (e.g., point clouds, meshes, design parameters). The architecture includes lifting and projection networks for encoding and decoding, geometric Fourier transforms for spectral operations, and supports both structured and unstructured meshes. For domains with complex topology, domain decomposition and Fourier continuation techniques are incorporated to ensure general applicability.
b768011c1dd42b13ae8a1c34b99ac4228304dabd.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a range of PDEs, including Elasticity, Plasticity, Advection, Euler’s, and Navier-Stokes equations, across both forward modeling and inverse design tasks. The method is evaluated on various geometries and input formats, such as point clouds and non-uniform meshes. Baselines include standard numerical solvers and interpolation-based machine learning PDE solvers like the original FNO. Evaluation metrics focus on computational speedup (cost-accuracy trade-off) and solution accuracy, with discretization-convergence properties assessed by training on low-resolution datasets and evaluating on high-resolution cases. Additional experiments explore the impact of learned versus fixed deformations and the effectiveness of domain decomposition for complex topologies.
b768011c1dd42b13ae8a1c34b99ac4228304dabd.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a neural operator framework that learns domain deformations, enabling FFT-based neural operators to handle arbitrary geometries and input formats. This results in a method that combines the computational efficiency of FFT with the flexibility of adaptive meshes and learned deformations. The framework supports end-to-end training of both the deformation and solution operator, generalizes to a wide variety of PDEs and geometries, and achieves significant speedup and accuracy improvements over existing methods. The approach also extends to complex topologies via domain decomposition and supports various input parameterizations, making it broadly applicable in engineering and scientific computing.

b778fd5f23b91499e4186539e66596a0ac67a13b.title: A Survey on Mixture of Experts in Large Language Models
b778fd5f23b91499e4186539e66596a0ac67a13b.research_question: How can mixture of experts (MoE) architectures be systematically advanced and optimized for large language models (LLMs) across algorithmic, system, and application domains, and what are the key design choices and challenges in scaling, training, and deploying MoE-based LLMs?
b778fd5f23b91499e4186539e66596a0ac67a13b.hypothesis: The integration of advanced mixture of experts (MoE) frameworks, including novel gating functions, expert architectures, and system-level optimizations, will enable large language models to achieve greater scalability, efficiency, and performance with reduced computational overhead compared to traditional dense models.
b778fd5f23b91499e4186539e66596a0ac67a13b.proposed_method: A comprehensive research program is proposed to develop and evaluate new MoE architectures for LLMs. This includes the design of novel gating mechanisms (such as adaptive, sparse, dense, and soft gating), exploration of expert network types (e.g., FFN, attention, parameter-efficient experts), and systematic investigation of hyperparameter configurations (expert count, size, placement frequency). The methodology will also encompass the development of system-level enhancements for computation, communication, and storage efficiency tailored to the dynamic and sparse workload of MoE models. Furthermore, the proposal includes the creation of a new taxonomy for MoE advancements, empirical evaluation of auxiliary loss functions for load balancing, and the integration of parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques. The research will extend to both algorithmic innovations and practical system deployments, ensuring that proposed methods are evaluated for real-world applicability and scalability.
b778fd5f23b91499e4186539e66596a0ac67a13b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a diverse set of open-source and proprietary LLMs equipped with MoE layers, such as Mixtral-8x7B, DeepSeekMoE, Qwen1.5-MoE, and others spanning NLP, vision, multimodal, and recommender system domains. Benchmark datasets will include standard language modeling corpora, image classification datasets (e.g., DomainNet), and multilingual translation benchmarks (e.g., NLLB). Baselines will consist of dense transformer models, classic sparse MoE models (e.g., GShard, Switch Transformer), and recent parameter-efficient fine-tuning approaches. Evaluation metrics will cover model perplexity, accuracy, throughput, computational cost, and load balancing efficiency. Experimental setups will systematically vary MoE hyperparameters, gating strategies, and expert architectures to assess their impact on model performance and resource utilization.
b778fd5f23b91499e4186539e66596a0ac67a13b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new, comprehensive taxonomy for MoE in LLMs, encompassing algorithmic, system, and application perspectives. It advances the state of the art by systematically exploring and integrating novel gating functions (including adaptive, non-trainable, and soft expert merging), expert network designs, and hyperparameter strategies. The research uniquely addresses both algorithmic and system-level challenges, including load balancing, expert specialization, and efficient deployment at scale. Additionally, the work aims to bridge the gap between academic research and practical deployment, providing open-source resources and empirical guidelines for the broader community.

b783168c885ecbae0fccdb46ec8e9afd0ef99b7f.title: Avalon's Game of Thoughts: Battle Against Deception through Recursive Contemplation
b783168c885ecbae0fccdb46ec8e9afd0ef99b7f.research_question: How can large language model (LLM) agents be equipped to effectively identify and counteract deceptive or misleading information in complex multi-agent environments that involve hidden roles and misinformation, such as the Avalon game?
b783168c885ecbae0fccdb46ec8e9afd0ef99b7f.hypothesis: Integrating recursive contemplation mechanisms, including formulation and refinement contemplation with first-order and second-order perspective transitions, will significantly enhance LLM agents' ability to detect, resist, and strategically respond to deception in multi-agent environments, without requiring additional fine-tuning or game-specific data.
b783168c885ecbae0fccdb46ec8e9afd0ef99b7f.proposed_method: A novel framework, Recursive Contemplation (ReCon), will be developed to enhance LLM agents' reasoning and deception-handling abilities in multi-agent games characterized by hidden roles and misinformation. The method consists of two main cognitive processes: formulation contemplation and refinement contemplation. Formulation contemplation enables the agent to generate initial internal thoughts and spoken content, incorporating a first-order perspective transition to infer the mental states of other players based on observed history. Refinement contemplation allows the agent to further polish its thoughts and speech by simulating how other players might perceive its statements, utilizing a second-order perspective transition. The process is implemented through structured prompting, where the agent alternates between private contemplation and public speech, updating its assumptions and strategies at each stage. This approach is designed to prevent exposure of private information, improve logical consistency, and enable nuanced, context-aware deception detection and response.
b783168c885ecbae0fccdb46ec8e9afd0ef99b7f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Avalon game as a testbed, leveraging its inherent complexity, hidden roles, and reliance on deception. The evaluation will involve end-to-end gameplay with LLM agents (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude) equipped with the ReCon framework, compared against a baseline Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting method. Both quantitative and qualitative analyses will be performed, including ablation studies to assess the contribution of each component (formulation/refinement contemplation, first/second-order perspective transitions). Multi-dimensional evaluation metrics, such as concealment, logic, contribution, persuasiveness, information, and creativity, will be used, with GPT-4 serving as an automatic evaluator for preference judgments. The setup includes 20 full Avalon games per method, generating over 2300 responses, and response format adherence will be monitored. No additional fine-tuning or game-specific data will be used.
b783168c885ecbae0fccdb46ec8e9afd0ef99b7f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a recursive contemplation framework that systematically integrates human-inspired recursive thinking and perspective-taking into LLM agents for the first time in deceptive multi-agent environments. Unlike prior methods, ReCon enables robust deception detection and response without requiring extra fine-tuning or domain-specific data. The method provides a generalizable, plug-and-play mechanism for enhancing LLM agents' reasoning, information concealment, and strategic communication in adversarial settings. Extensive ablation and multi-dimensional analyses demonstrate the effectiveness and necessity of each component, establishing new benchmarks for LLM performance in deception-rich environments.

b7864b0e76f402ab668247ed20438374b6be8e3b.title: Scalable Model Merging with Progressive Layer-wise Distillation
b7864b0e76f402ab668247ed20438374b6be8e3b.research_question: How can the capabilities of multiple fine-tuned models be effectively integrated into a single, scalable model, especially when only limited domain-specific data is available for merging?
b7864b0e76f402ab668247ed20438374b6be8e3b.hypothesis: Access to even a small amount of domain-specific data enables significantly more effective model merging than data-agnostic approaches, and a progressive, layer-wise distillation strategy can improve both the scalability and performance of merged models.
b7864b0e76f402ab668247ed20438374b6be8e3b.proposed_method: A novel model merging algorithm, ProDistill (Progressive Layer-wise Distillation), will be developed to integrate multiple fine-tuned models into a single unified model. The method frames model merging as a teacher-student distillation problem, where the merged model (student) progressively aligns its internal activations with those of the fine-tuned models (teachers) at each layer. The approach optimizes element-wise merging coefficients for each layer by minimizing the mean squared error between the merged model's activations and those of the fine-tuned models, using a few-shot, domain-specific validation set. To address memory and computational constraints, the algorithm operates in a layer-wise fashion, updating only the current layer's coefficients and activations at each step, and employs dual-inputs to better approximate global feature alignment. This progressive strategy is designed to be scalable to models with billions of parameters.
b7864b0e76f402ab668247ed20438374b6be8e3b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of tasks and architectures, including vision (e.g., ViT models on image classification datasets such as SUN397, Cars, RESISC45, EuroSAT, SVHN, GTSRB, MNIST, DTD), natural language understanding (e.g., BERT and RoBERTa on GLUE benchmark tasks), and large language models (e.g., LLAMA2, WizardMath-13B, Llama-2-13B-Code-Alpaca on code and math generation tasks). Baselines will include Task Arithmetic, Fisher merging, RegMean, AdaMerging, Localize-and-Stitch, TIES-Merging, and WIDEN, among others. Evaluation metrics will include task-specific accuracy, average performance across tasks, and normalized average scores. Experimental setups will vary the number of validation samples (few-shot regime), training epochs, and memory usage to assess data, computation, and memory efficiency. Visualization techniques such as t-SNE will be used to analyze feature separation in the merged models.
b7864b0e76f402ab668247ed20438374b6be8e3b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to provide a theoretical analysis demonstrating the necessity of domain-specific data for effective model merging, showing that data-agnostic methods can have arbitrarily poor worst-case performance. ProDistill introduces a progressive, layer-wise distillation framework that enables efficient and scalable merging of large models, including those with over 10 billion parameters. The method leverages element-wise merging coefficients and dual-input activation alignment, resulting in state-of-the-art performance with significant improvements over existing few-shot merging methods in both vision and language tasks. Additionally, ProDistill achieves superior data, computation, and memory efficiency, making it practical for large-scale deployment.

b78b5ce5f21f46d8149824463f8eebd6103d49aa.title: FigStep: Jailbreaking Large Vision-language Models via Typographic Visual Prompts
b78b5ce5f21f46d8149824463f8eebd6103d49aa.research_question: How can the safety alignment of large vision-language models (LVLMs) be robustly evaluated and potentially circumvented using cross-modal attacks, and what are the limitations of current safety mechanisms in protecting against multimodal jailbreaks?
b78b5ce5f21f46d8149824463f8eebd6103d49aa.hypothesis: LVLMs, despite inheriting safety-aligned large language models (LLMs), remain vulnerable to cross-modal jailbreak attacks that exploit typographic visual prompts, due to insufficient safety alignment between visual and textual modalities.
b78b5ce5f21f46d8149824463f8eebd6103d49aa.proposed_method: A novel black-box jailbreak algorithm, termed FigStep, will be developed to evaluate and exploit vulnerabilities in LVLMs. The method will transform prohibited textual queries into typographic images and pair them with benign incitement text prompts, leveraging the LVLM's ability to read and follow visual instructions while bypassing textual safety filters. The pipeline consists of three steps: (1) paraphrasing the harmful question into a declarative form, (2) rendering this as a numbered typographic image, and (3) crafting a neutral text prompt to encourage step-by-step completion. The approach requires only API-level access to the LVLM, assumes no internal knowledge or parameter manipulation, and is fully automatable.
b78b5ce5f21f46d8149824463f8eebd6103d49aa.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a newly constructed safety benchmark, SafeBench, containing 500 manually verified harmful questions across 10 forbidden topics. Six open-source LVLMs (including LLaVA, MiniGPT4, and CogVLM) and two closed-source models (GPT-4V, GPT-4o) will be evaluated. Baselines will include vanilla text-only queries, state-of-the-art text-based jailbreaks (e.g., GCG, DeepInception, ICA, CipherChat, MultiLingual), and image-based attacks (e.g., Visual-RolePlay, Query-Relevant Images, JP OCR, VAE). Attack success rate (ASR) and response perplexity (PPL) will be measured, with manual annotation for accuracy. Ablation studies will assess the necessity of each pipeline component, and the impact of hyperparameters (e.g., temperature, repetition) and prompt variations will be analyzed. Defense strategies such as OCR detection, system prompt modification, and adversarial noise will also be evaluated.
b78b5ce5f21f46d8149824463f8eebd6103d49aa.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first comprehensive, fully automated, black-box typographic visual jailbreak for LVLMs, requiring no model internals or adversarial optimization. It demonstrates that current LVLMs can be reliably and efficiently jailbroken via cross-modal attacks, surpassing both text-based and prior image-based methods in attack success and cost. The work provides new insights into the semantic but not safety alignment of visual embeddings, proposes SafeBench as a novel safety evaluation benchmark, and highlights the urgent need for cross-modal safety alignment techniques. Additionally, the research systematically evaluates and exposes the limitations of existing defense mechanisms.

b7a4be5a703f251b2d341d30ccec5e201881981b.title: Gradient Matching for Domain Generalization
b7a4be5a703f251b2d341d30ccec5e201881981b.research_question: How can machine learning models be trained to generalize effectively to unseen domains, particularly under distribution shifts, by leveraging invariances across multiple source domains?
b7a4be5a703f251b2d341d30ccec5e201881981b.hypothesis: Maximizing the alignment of gradient directions across different training domains will encourage models to learn invariant features, thereby improving generalization to unseen domains compared to empirical risk minimization and other domain generalization methods.
b7a4be5a703f251b2d341d30ccec5e201881981b.proposed_method: A novel training objective, termed Inter-Domain Gradient Matching (IDGM), is introduced to encourage the alignment of gradient directions across domains by maximizing the inner product between gradients computed from different domains. The IDGM objective augments the standard empirical risk minimization loss with an auxiliary term that penalizes misalignment of gradients, thus promoting learning of invariant features. To address the computational inefficiency of directly optimizing the gradient inner product (which requires second-order derivatives), a first-order approximation algorithm called Fish is developed. Fish performs multiple inner-loop updates on cloned model parameters using mini-batches from different domains, then updates the original parameters based on the difference between the cloned and original models, effectively approximating the IDGM objective without second-order computations.
b7a4be5a703f251b2d341d30ccec5e201881981b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of domain generalization benchmarks, including the WILDS benchmark (real-world distribution shifts across vision and language tasks) and DOMAINBED (synthetic-to-real transfer and diverse domain generalization datasets such as ColoredMNIST, RotatedMNIST, VLCS, PACS, OfficeHome, Terra Incognita, and DomainNet). The proposed method will be compared against strong baselines including ERM, IRM, GroupDRO, Mixup, MLDG, Coral, MMD, DANN, and CDANN. Evaluation metrics will be dataset-specific, such as accuracy, worst-group accuracy, macro F1, and Pearson correlation, following the protocols of each benchmark. Model architectures will include ResNet, DenseNet, and BERT, with hyperparameters and model selection strategies aligned with benchmark standards. Additional ablation studies will assess the impact of hyperparameters, domain grouping strategies, and computational efficiency.
b7a4be5a703f251b2d341d30ccec5e201881981b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new objective for domain generalization based on maximizing inter-domain gradient alignment, which directly targets the learning of invariant features across domains.
