The Fish algorithm provides a computationally efficient, first-order approximation to the otherwise costly second-order optimization required by the IDGM objective. This approach is claimed to be both simple to implement and broadly applicable, achieving competitive or state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of challenging domain generalization tasks and modalities. The method is also demonstrated to be robust to different architectures and types of distribution shift, and its effectiveness is supported by both theoretical analysis and empirical results.

b7b7a549629bbe7fa325572339938980e77d155c.title: AnyText: Multilingual Visual Text Generation And Editing
b7b7a549629bbe7fa325572339938980e77d155c.research_question: How can accurate, coherent, and multilingual visual text be generated and edited within images using diffusion models, overcoming the challenges of legibility, language diversity, and seamless integration with image backgrounds?
b7b7a549629bbe7fa325572339938980e77d155c.hypothesis: Integrating auxiliary latent information (glyph, position, and masked image) with OCR-based text embeddings into a diffusion-based generative framework will significantly improve the accuracy, legibility, and multilingual capability of visual text generation and editing in images.
b7b7a549629bbe7fa325572339938980e77d155c.proposed_method: A novel diffusion-based framework will be developed for multilingual visual text generation and editing. The method will incorporate an auxiliary latent module that encodes glyph images, positional information, and masked images into a latent feature map, enabling precise control over text placement and region preservation. A text embedding module will be designed that leverages a pre-trained OCR model to extract glyph-level features from rendered text lines, which are then fused with semantic caption embeddings via a transformer-based encoder. The resulting embeddings will be mapped into the diffusion model using cross-attention. Training will employ both a text-control diffusion loss, which guides the model to generate accurate text in the latent space, and a text perceptual loss, which uses OCR feature similarity in the image space to further supervise writing correctness at the pixel level. The architecture will be modular, allowing plug-and-play integration with existing diffusion models.
b7b7a549629bbe7fa325572339938980e77d155c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the newly constructed AnyWord-3M dataset, which contains over 3 million image-text pairs with OCR annotations across multiple languages, including Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, and others. Evaluation will be performed on the AnyText-benchmark, comprising separate test sets for Chinese and English, using metrics such as Sentence Accuracy (Sen. ACC), Normalized Edit Distance (NED), and Frechet Inception Distance (FID) to assess text correctness and image realism. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art text-to-image and text-in-image editing models such as ControlNet, TextDiffuser, and GlyphControl, with all methods evaluated under consistent sampling and prompt conditions. Ablation studies will be performed to validate the contribution of each module (editing, position, text embedding, perceptual loss) using subsets of the training data and the benchmark.
b7b7a549629bbe7fa325572339938980e77d155c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first diffusion-based framework capable of accurate, coherent, and editable multilingual visual text generation. Key innovations include the integration of an OCR-based text embedding module for robust glyph and semantic representation, a modular auxiliary latent module for flexible text control, and the use of a dedicated text perceptual loss for pixel-level supervision. The method supports multi-line, deformed, and irregular text regions, as well as plug-and-play compatibility with existing diffusion models. Additionally, the work contributes the first large-scale multilingual visual text dataset (AnyWord-3M) and a comprehensive benchmark (AnyText-benchmark) for evaluating visual text generation quality and accuracy.

b7c408dc2764269a8ae1bde4fd48f5bead185f9f.title: Statistical guarantees for sparse deep learning
b7c408dc2764269a8ae1bde4fd48f5bead185f9f.research_question: What are the statistical guarantees for deep neural networks with various types of sparsity, such as connection sparsity and node sparsity, particularly in high-dimensional regression settings with multiple outputs and unbounded loss functions? How do these guarantees depend on network architecture parameters such as width, depth, and output dimensionality, and how can regularization-based approaches be theoretically justified in this context?
b7c408dc2764269a8ae1bde4fd48f5bead185f9f.hypothesis: Sparse deep neural networks, when regularized appropriately, can achieve accurate prediction and generalization performance even in high-dimensional settings with wide and deep architectures, and these guarantees can be established for a broad class of sparsity types and loss functions.
b7c408dc2764269a8ae1bde4fd48f5bead185f9f.proposed_method: A new statistical framework will be developed for analyzing deep feedforward neural networks under various sparsity-inducing regularization schemes, including both connection sparsity (via elementwise ℓ1 regularization) and node sparsity (via group-lasso or ℓ2,1 regularization). The approach will focus on regression-type problems with multiple outputs, unbounded data, and subgaussian noise, and will employ regularization rather than hard constraints to induce sparsity. The methodology will leverage advanced tools from high-dimensional statistics and empirical process theory, including oracle inequalities, effective noise analysis, and chaining-based concentration inequalities, to derive prediction and generalization error bounds. The framework will be designed to accommodate different activation functions (beyond ReLU), multiple outputs, and norm-based sparsity, and will avoid auxiliary parameters or reparametrizations that are not commonly used in practice.
b7c408dc2764269a8ae1bde4fd48f5bead185f9f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using both synthetic and real-world datasets, such as MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, to evaluate the prediction and generalization performance of sparse deep neural networks under connection and node sparsity regularization. The experimental setup will include varying the network width, depth, and output dimensionality to test the scalability and robustness of the proposed statistical guarantees. Baseline comparisons will be made against existing theoretical bounds and practical implementations of sparsity in deep learning, including constraint-based and regularization-based approaches. Evaluation metrics will include prediction error (mean squared error) and generalization error, with particular attention to the dependence of these errors on network architecture parameters and sparsity levels.
b7c408dc2764269a8ae1bde4fd48f5bead185f9f.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces statistical guarantees for deep neural networks with both connection and node sparsity, covering multiple outputs and unbounded loss functions, which have not been addressed simultaneously in previous work. The framework provides oracle inequalities and error bounds with only mild (logarithmic or sublinear) dependence on network width and depth, supporting the use of very wide and deep sparse networks. Unlike prior approaches, the method relies on regularization rather than constraints, aligns closely with practical implementations, and avoids unnatural auxiliary parameters. The theoretical analysis employs advanced empirical process techniques and effective noise concepts that are uncommon in deep learning theory, and the results are the first to provide statistical guarantees for node-sparse networks with multiple outputs.

b7cbf03974511d7855b4c01e3005f3e38bd1a136.title: Rapid locomotion via reinforcement learning
b7cbf03974511d7855b4c01e3005f3e38bd1a136.research_question: How can legged robots achieve agile, high-speed, and robust locomotion—including rapid running and turning—across diverse and challenging natural terrains without relying on hand-designed models or extensive sensing suites?
b7cbf03974511d7855b4c01e3005f3e38bd1a136.hypothesis: End-to-end reinforcement learning, combined with adaptive curriculum learning and online system identification, enables legged robots to learn robust, high-speed locomotion policies that generalize across terrains and transfer effectively from simulation to real-world deployment.
b7cbf03974511d7855b4c01e3005f3e38bd1a136.proposed_method: A neural network-based controller will be trained in simulation to map sensory observations and velocity commands to joint position commands for a quadruped robot. The method employs a teacher-student framework: the teacher policy has access to privileged simulation parameters (such as robot and terrain dynamics) and is trained using reinforcement learning with domain randomization, while the student policy learns to infer these parameters implicitly from a history of sensor data via an online system identification module. An adaptive curriculum strategy will be implemented to progressively expand the range and complexity of velocity commands, using reward-based updates to focus learning on feasible and incrementally challenging tasks. The neural network architecture will consist of separate modules for encoding domain parameters, policy body, and adaptation, optimized using PPO and supervised learning for the identification module.
b7cbf03974511d7855b4c01e3005f3e38bd1a136.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the MIT Mini Cheetah robot, both in simulation (IsaacGym) and in real-world environments including indoor flat ground, outdoor grass, ice, and gravel. The policy will be trained on 400 million simulated timesteps with extensive domain randomization over robot and terrain parameters. Baselines will include policies trained without curriculum, with box and grid adaptive curricula, and with/without online system identification. Evaluation metrics will focus on velocity tracking error, command area (the range of velocities tracked within an error threshold), maximum sustained speed, and qualitative robustness to disturbances and terrain changes. Real-world performance will be measured using motion capture and video analysis, and ablation studies will assess the impact of curriculum and system identification.
b7cbf03974511d7855b4c01e3005f3e38bd1a136.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a fully end-to-end learned locomotion controller that achieves record agility for a quadruped robot, including the highest reported speeds for the MIT Mini Cheetah. Key innovations include an adaptive curriculum learning strategy that models the joint difficulty of linear and angular velocity commands, and an online system identification module that enables robust sim-to-real transfer at high speeds. The method demonstrates that reinforcement learning can produce a single policy capable of rapid, robust locomotion and recovery behaviors across a wide range of natural terrains, using only minimal onboard sensing.

b7dc9589304180d7bc60b695847b5dba25847ecc.title: A Comprehensive Study on Quantization Techniques for Large Language Models
b7dc9589304180d7bc60b695847b5dba25847ecc.research_question: How can quantization techniques be systematically analyzed and optimized for large language models (LLMs) to reduce computational and memory requirements while maintaining high model accuracy across diverse tasks and hardware environments?
b7dc9589304180d7bc60b695847b5dba25847ecc.hypothesis: Advanced quantization techniques, including both post-training quantization (PTQ) and quantization-aware training (QAT), can significantly reduce the size and computational demands of LLMs without substantial loss of accuracy, especially when tailored calibration, granularity, and data-free training strategies are employed.
b7dc9589304180d7bc60b695847b5dba25847ecc.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed to systematically study, implement, and compare a wide range of quantization techniques for LLMs. The methodology will include both mathematical analysis and empirical evaluation of affine and scale quantization, various calibration strategies (global, max, KL divergence, percentile), and granularity settings (per-layer, per-channel). The study will focus on two main quantization paradigms: PTQ (including methods like GPTQ and SmoothQuant) and QAT (including data-free approaches such as LLM-QAT for key-value caches). For PTQ, block-wise and layer-wise quantization algorithms will be implemented, leveraging Hessian-based optimization for error minimization. For QAT, knowledge distillation and synthetic data generation will be used to enable effective quantization in the absence of original training data, with special attention to activation and KV cache quantization. Mixed-precision and attention-aware strategies will also be explored to further optimize the trade-off between efficiency and accuracy.
b7dc9589304180d7bc60b695847b5dba25847ecc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of LLMs, including but not limited to OPT, BLOOM, and LLaMA, covering model sizes from hundreds of millions to over 175 billion parameters. Evaluation will use standard language modeling benchmarks such as WikiText2, as well as downstream tasks from datasets like BoolQ, PIQA, SIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, and ARC-e. Baseline comparisons will include full-precision models and existing quantization methods such as RTN and SmoothQuant. Evaluation metrics will include perplexity, accuracy on downstream tasks, model size, inference speed, and memory consumption. Both 3-bit and 4-bit quantization regimes will be tested, along with mixed-precision configurations for weights, activations, and KV caches. The impact of calibration methods and quantization granularity will be systematically assessed.
b7dc9589304180d7bc60b695847b5dba25847ecc.novelty_claims: The proposed study will deliver a unified and systematic comparison of quantization techniques tailored for LLMs, including the first comprehensive analysis of data-free QAT for key-value cache quantization. The research will introduce and benchmark advanced calibration and granularity strategies, as well as mixed-precision and attention-aware quantization methods, across a wide spectrum of model sizes and tasks. The project aims to establish best practices for deploying highly compressed LLMs on resource-constrained hardware, providing actionable insights into precision configuration and quantization-aware training without access to original datasets.

b7dfa8acfa5776e22e7c8f6cc0c05b060515e6d6.title: Convergence of Adam Under Relaxed Assumptions
b7dfa8acfa5776e22e7c8f6cc0c05b060515e6d6.research_question: Can the Adam optimization algorithm be theoretically proven to converge to stationary points under more realistic and relaxed assumptions than previously considered, particularly without requiring globally bounded gradients or global Lipschitz smoothness? Furthermore, can the convergence rate of Adam be accelerated using variance reduction techniques under these relaxed conditions?
b7dfa8acfa5776e22e7c8f6cc0c05b060515e6d6.hypothesis: Adam converges to stationary points under a generalized, non-uniform smoothness condition where the local smoothness (Hessian norm) is bounded by a sub-quadratic function of the gradient norm, even without assuming globally bounded gradients or global Lipschitz continuity. Additionally, a variance-reduced version of Adam can achieve accelerated convergence rates under similar relaxed assumptions.
b7dfa8acfa5776e22e7c8f6cc0c05b060515e6d6.proposed_method: A rigorous convergence analysis of the Adam algorithm will be developed under a generalized smoothness condition, specifically where the local Hessian norm is bounded by a sub-quadratic function of the gradient norm (the (ρ, L0, Lρ) smoothness condition with 0 ≤ ρ < 2). The analysis will avoid the standard bounded gradient or global Lipschitz assumptions by introducing a new technique to directly prove the boundedness of gradients along the optimization trajectory. This will involve constructing a Lyapunov function and employing a contradiction argument to show that, with high probability, the gradients remain bounded throughout the optimization process. Furthermore, a variance-reduced version of Adam (VRAdam) will be proposed, inspired by the STORM algorithm, which modifies the momentum update rule to reduce variance and accelerate convergence. Theoretical guarantees for both standard and variance-reduced Adam will be established under both almost surely bounded and sub-Gaussian gradient noise assumptions.
b7dfa8acfa5776e22e7c8f6cc0c05b060515e6d6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard deep learning tasks using datasets such as CIFAR-10, employing various neural network architectures including shallow CNNs and deep ResNets (e.g., ResNet-Small, ResNet110). The Adam optimizer will be evaluated with different hyperparameter settings, particularly varying the λ parameter, to empirically validate the theoretical claims regarding insensitivity to λ and dimension-free convergence rates. Baselines will include standard Adam and potentially other adaptive optimizers or variance-reduced algorithms. Evaluation metrics will focus on convergence to stationary points (measured by gradient norm) and test error rates. The experimental setup will ensure that the theoretical assumptions (e.g., batch size, noise characteristics) are reasonably approximated in practice.
b7dfa8acfa5776e22e7c8f6cc0c05b060515e6d6.novelty_claims: The proposed analysis removes the need for strong and often unrealistic assumptions such as globally bounded gradients or global Lipschitz smoothness, instead relying on a more general and practically relevant smoothness condition. A new proof technique is introduced to establish boundedness of gradients along the optimization trajectory, which can be applied to Adam and potentially other optimization algorithms. The variance-reduced Adam variant achieves an accelerated convergence rate of O(ε⁻³) under relaxed assumptions, improving upon existing results. The convergence guarantees are dimension-free and hold under both almost surely bounded and sub-Gaussian gradient noise, broadening the applicability of the results to practical deep learning scenarios.

b7e531104c95eb67ce6c20d6dc1318e8bf837bf8.title: Conflict-Averse Gradient Descent for Multi-task Learning
b7e531104c95eb67ce6c20d6dc1318e8bf837bf8.research_question: How can the optimization of multi-task learning models be improved to mitigate the detrimental effects of conflicting gradients, thereby achieving better performance across all tasks compared to existing approaches?
b7e531104c95eb67ce6c20d6dc1318e8bf837bf8.hypothesis: A gradient-based optimization method that explicitly minimizes the worst-case local improvement among all task objectives, while regularizing updates within a neighborhood of the average gradient, will provably converge to an optimum of the average loss and outperform existing multi-task learning optimization techniques in both supervised and reinforcement learning settings.
b7e531104c95eb67ce6c20d6dc1318e8bf837bf8.proposed_method: A novel optimization algorithm, Conflict-Averse Gradient Descent (CAGrad), is proposed for multi-task learning. This method formulates the update direction as the solution to a constrained optimization problem: at each step, it seeks an update vector within a ball around the average gradient that maximizes the minimum inner product with any task-specific gradient, thereby minimizing the worst-case local improvement across all tasks. The approach introduces a hyperparameter c ∈ [0,1) to control the trade-off between following the average gradient and reducing gradient conflict. The optimization is efficiently solved in the dual space, reducing the computational burden to a function of the number of tasks rather than the number of model parameters. The method generalizes both standard gradient descent and the multiple gradient descent algorithm (MGDA) as special cases, depending on the value of c, and is model-agnostic, applicable to deep neural networks and reinforcement learning policies.
b7e531104c95eb67ce6c20d6dc1318e8bf837bf8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of multi-task learning benchmarks, including toy optimization problems, the Multi-Fashion+MNIST classification dataset, NYU-v2 and CityScapes for multi-task supervised vision tasks, Meta-World MT10 and MT50 for multi-task reinforcement learning, and CIFAR10 for semi-supervised learning with auxiliary tasks. Baseline methods for comparison will include standard gradient descent, MGDA, PCGrad, GradNorm, Cross-Stitch, MTAN, SoftModularization, and CARE, among others. Evaluation metrics will include average and per-task loss, accuracy, mean intersection-over-union (mIoU), pixel accuracy, absolute and relative errors, and RL task success rates. Experiments will use consistent training setups, multiple random seeds, and statistical significance testing. Computational efficiency and scalability will also be assessed, including a variant (CAGrad-Fast) that subsamples task gradients for speedup.
b7e531104c95eb67ce6c20d6dc1318e8bf837bf8.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a principled, theoretically grounded approach to mitigating gradient conflict in multi-task learning by optimizing for the worst-case local improvement of any task, while maintaining convergence guarantees to the optimum of the average loss. Unlike prior gradient manipulation methods, CAGrad provides explicit control over the optimization trajectory and provable convergence to a specific solution, rather than an arbitrary Pareto-stationary point. The approach is computationally efficient via dual optimization, generalizes existing methods, and demonstrates improved empirical performance and efficiency across a range of challenging multi-task supervised, semi-supervised, and reinforcement learning benchmarks.

b83079322b10772b121d43277c1e3bc96e28623a.title: Compress then Serve: Serving Thousands of LoRA Adapters with Little Overhead
b83079322b10772b121d43277c1e3bc96e28623a.research_question: How can collections of thousands of LoRA adapters for large language models be compressed and served efficiently, while preserving their individual task performance and maximizing inference throughput under limited GPU memory constraints?
b83079322b10772b121d43277c1e3bc96e28623a.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that joint compression of LoRA adapters into shared bases with adapter-specific scaling matrices, potentially combined with clustering of similar adapters, can significantly reduce memory and computational overhead while maintaining the performance of the original adapters during inference.
b83079322b10772b121d43277c1e3bc96e28623a.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces a joint compression framework for LoRA adapters, formulating the problem as a reconstruction task where the goal is to approximate each adapter's parameter matrices via a shared low-rank basis and adapter-specific scaling matrices. The approach utilizes a joint diagonalization (JD) algorithm to learn shared matrices (U, V) and adapter-specific matrices (Σ_i), minimizing the Frobenius norm of the reconstruction error across all adapters. To address scalability for large collections, a clustering algorithm is incorporated, grouping similar LoRAs and applying joint compression within each cluster to further reduce reconstruction error and parameter count. The optimization alternates between updating cluster assignments and minimizing per-cluster reconstruction error, with theoretical guarantees provided for the reconstruction loss. Hyperparameter selection for rank and cluster count is guided by empirical reconstruction error, and the compressed adapters are integrated into an LLM serving system for efficient multi-adapter inference.
b83079322b10772b121d43277c1e3bc96e28623a.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training over 1000 LoRA adapters on the Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 model using 1000 diverse natural instruction tasks. The compressed adapters will be evaluated against their uncompressed counterparts using metrics such as Rouge-L, cross-entropy loss, exact match, and agreement, with a primary focus on Rouge-L due to its strong correlation with downstream utility. Baseline comparisons will include uncompressed LoRAs, individually SVD-compressed LoRAs, and state-of-the-art multi-LoRA serving systems (e.g., vLLM with and without Punica kernel optimizations). Throughput will be measured as requests per second under realistic asynchronous serving scenarios, with varying numbers of concurrent LoRAs and GPU memory constraints. Additional experiments will analyze the relationship between reconstruction error and downstream performance, as well as the impact of clustering and compression rank on both accuracy and throughput.
b83079322b10772b121d43277c1e3bc96e28623a.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a joint diagonalization-based compression scheme for LoRA adapters, enabling the serving of thousands of adapters with a fraction of the memory and computational overhead. The method extends to scalable clustering for large collections, providing a principled trade-off between compression and reconstruction error. Theoretical analysis establishes guarantees on reconstruction loss and its empirical relationship to downstream performance. Integration with state-of-the-art LLM serving systems demonstrates that the approach can maintain up to 99% of original LoRA performance while achieving major throughput gains. The release of a large-scale, high-quality LoRA collection and open-source code further facilitates future research and adoption.

b835345c6168d7b179516700aa4460912a8857e9.title: HomoDistil: Homotopic Task-Agnostic Distillation of Pre-trained Transformers
b835345c6168d7b179516700aa4460912a8857e9.research_question: How can task-agnostic knowledge distillation be improved to produce compact, general-purpose pre-trained language models that maintain high performance across a variety of downstream tasks, while addressing the challenge of prediction discrepancy between large teacher models and smaller student models?
b835345c6168d7b179516700aa4460912a8857e9.hypothesis: Iteratively pruning a student model initialized from a large pre-trained teacher, while jointly optimizing both distillation and training losses at each step, will maintain a small prediction discrepancy and result in a more effective and generalizable compact model for downstream tasks compared to existing task-agnostic distillation methods.
b835345c6168d7b179516700aa4460912a8857e9.proposed_method: A novel task-agnostic distillation framework, termed Homotopic Distillation (HomoDistil), will be developed. The student model is initialized as an exact copy of the teacher model and, during training, is iteratively pruned at the neuron level based on a sensitivity-based importance score. At each iteration, the least important neurons are pruned using a cubically decreasing sparsity schedule, and the student is further trained to minimize a weighted sum of losses: masked language modeling loss, KL-divergence between teacher and student outputs, mean squared error between hidden representations and attention scores at both embedding and intermediate layers. Dimension-matching linear projections are used where necessary. The pruning is structured at the neuron level to ensure hardware efficiency and maintain architectural compatibility.
b835345c6168d7b179516700aa4460912a8857e9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using BERT-base as the teacher and initial student model, with continual pre-training performed on the English Wikipedia and Toronto BookCorpus datasets. The student will be pruned to various target sizes and fine-tuned on the GLUE benchmark (covering nine NLU tasks) and SQuAD v1.1/v2.0 for question answering. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art task-agnostic distillation approaches such as DistilBERT, TinyBERT-GD, MiniLM, and MiniLMv2, all using BERT-base as the teacher for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics will include task-specific accuracy, F1, and EM scores, with results averaged over multiple random seeds. Hyperparameters such as learning rate, batch size, and pruning schedule will be tuned, and ablation studies will be conducted to assess the impact of different importance metrics and loss objectives.
b835345c6168d7b179516700aa4460912a8857e9.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first task-agnostic distillation method that combines iterative neuron-level pruning with continual distillation, maintaining a small prediction discrepancy throughout training. Unlike prior methods that fix student size or require extensive tuning for initialization, this method dynamically prunes the student while leveraging both output and intermediate-layer knowledge. The approach ensures hardware-friendly structured sparsity and demonstrates superior generalization and downstream task performance, especially at extreme compression ratios, compared to existing task-agnostic distillation baselines.

b83a9e35c3aeeb37708e362473c7617d59b815b5.title: The FineWeb Datasets: Decanting the Web for the Finest Text Data at Scale
b83a9e35c3aeeb37708e362473c7617d59b815b5.research_question: How can large-scale, high-quality web-based pretraining datasets be systematically curated to optimize the performance of large language models (LLMs), and what are the most effective strategies for filtering, deduplication, and educational content selection at scale?
b83a9e35c3aeeb37708e362473c7617d59b815b5.hypothesis: Systematic empirical evaluation and ablation of filtering and deduplication strategies, combined with targeted educational content selection using LLM-based classifiers, will yield web-scale pretraining datasets that enable LLMs to outperform those trained on existing open datasets, particularly on knowledge- and reasoning-intensive benchmarks.
b83a9e35c3aeeb37708e362473c7617d59b815b5.proposed_method: A multi-stage data curation pipeline will be developed to construct a large-scale pretraining dataset from multiple Common Crawl snapshots. The pipeline will begin with custom text extraction from WARC files using the trafilatura library to minimize boilerplate and improve text quality. Base filtering will be applied using a combination of URL blocklists, fastText language identification (with a threshold for English content), and quality/repetition filters inspired by MassiveText. Deduplication will be performed independently for each crawl using MinHash-based fuzzy deduplication on 5-grams, with transitive clustering to remove near-duplicate documents. Additional heuristic filters will be systematically designed by analyzing statistical differences between high- and low-quality data, selecting thresholds for metrics such as fraction of lines ending with punctuation, proportion of duplicated lines, and proportion of short lines. Selected C4-inspired filters will be incorporated, excluding those that excessively reduce data volume. For an educational subset, a classifier trained on LLM-generated synthetic annotations will be used to filter for high-quality educational content.
b83a9e35c3aeeb37708e362473c7617d59b815b5.experiment_details: Ablation experiments will be conducted at each pipeline stage by training 1.71B parameter Llama-architecture models on equal-sized random samples (typically 28B or 350B tokens) from each dataset variant, ensuring consistent architecture and training hyperparameters. Evaluation will be performed using a suite of academic benchmarks, including CommonSense QA, HellaSwag, OpenBook QA, PIQA, SIQA, WinoGrande, ARC, and MMLU, with large benchmarks truncated to 1000 samples for efficiency. Each experiment will be repeated with different random seeds and data splits to ensure robustness, and aggregate benchmark scores will be used to assess the impact of each curation step. For the educational subset, the classifier will be validated using F1 score on a held-out set of LLM-annotated samples, and the resulting dataset's impact will be measured on knowledge- and reasoning-intensive benchmarks. All models and evaluation setups will be made publicly available for reproducibility.
b83a9e35c3aeeb37708e362473c7617d59b815b5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a fully documented, reproducible, and empirically optimized pipeline for large-scale web dataset curation, including systematic ablation of filtering and deduplication strategies. It advances the state of the art by releasing the largest open web-based pretraining dataset (15T tokens) and a novel educational subset (1.3T tokens) filtered using LLM-based synthetic annotations. The methodology provides detailed empirical guidance on the impact of each curation step and demonstrates that the resulting datasets enable LLMs to outperform all prior open datasets on a range of academic benchmarks, particularly those requiring knowledge and reasoning. The public release of the datasets, codebase, and ablation models further enhances transparency and reproducibility in LLM pretraining data curation.

b842b83a7ff5dff8e3b83915d8c15423b6085728.title: Gemma: Open Models Based on Gemini Research and Technology
b842b83a7ff5dff8e3b83915d8c15423b6085728.research_question: How can a family of lightweight, open large language models be developed to achieve strong performance in language understanding, reasoning, coding, and safety across a range of academic benchmarks, while supporting responsible and safe deployment for diverse applications?
b842b83a7ff5dff8e3b83915d8c15423b6085728.hypothesis: Openly released, instruction-tuned large language models built on advanced transformer architectures and robust data filtering can outperform similarly sized open models on a wide variety of language, reasoning, and safety benchmarks, while maintaining low rates of memorization and supporting responsible AI development.
b842b83a7ff5dff8e3b83915d8c15423b6085728.proposed_method: A family of transformer decoder-based language models will be developed in two parameter sizes (2B and 7B), utilizing rotary positional embeddings, multi-query or multi-head attention (depending on model size), GeGLU activations, and RMSNorm for stability. Models will be pretrained on up to 6T tokens of primarily English web, math, and code data using large-scale distributed TPUv5e infrastructure, with careful data filtering to remove unsafe, low-quality, and personal information. Fine-tuning will be conducted via supervised learning on synthetic and human-generated prompt-response pairs, followed by reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) using a reward model trained on preference data. Special formatting control tokens will annotate conversational roles and turns during instruction tuning. Extensive safety filtering and contamination analysis will be applied throughout data collection and evaluation.
b842b83a7ff5dff8e3b83915d8c15423b6085728.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate both pretrained and instruction-tuned models on a comprehensive suite of academic benchmarks, including MMLU, HellaSwag, PIQA, SIQA, BoolQ, Winogrande, CommonsenseQA, OBQA, ARC-e, ARC-c, TriviaQA, NQ, HumanEval, MBPP, GSM8K, MATH, AGIEval, and BBH, using standard evaluation protocols and metrics such as accuracy, pass@1, and majority voting. Baseline comparisons will include similarly sized open models such as LLaMA-2 (7B/13B) and Mistral (7B), with additional human preference evaluations conducted on held-out prompt sets for instruction following and safety. Memorization rates will be measured using both exact and approximate matching on held-out data, and personal data leakage will be assessed with automated sensitive data detection tools. Safety and bias will be evaluated using benchmarks such as RealToxicity, BOLD, CrowS-Pairs, BBQ, Winogender, TruthfulQA, Winobias, and Toxigen.
b842b83a7ff5dff8e3b83915d8c15423b6085728.novelty_claims: The proposed models introduce a new family of open, instruction-tuned LLMs that achieve state-of-the-art performance among similarly sized open models across a wide range of academic and safety benchmarks. The approach combines advanced transformer techniques, large-scale distributed training, rigorous data filtering, and comprehensive safety and memorization evaluations. The release includes both pretrained and fine-tuned checkpoints, open-source inference code, and detailed safety assessments, supporting responsible research and deployment. The models demonstrate particularly strong results in mathematics and coding, and set new standards for responsible openness and safety in LLM development.

b879450f50a6113f44a5baf0bcd5b4331eeb7bbc.title: Conditional Prompt Learning for Vision-Language Models
b879450f50a6113f44a5baf0bcd5b4331eeb7bbc.research_question: How can prompt learning methods for vision-language models be improved to enhance generalization and transferability to unseen classes and domains, while maintaining parameter efficiency and adaptability to new tasks?
b879450f50a6113f44a5baf0bcd5b4331eeb7bbc.hypothesis: Instance-conditional prompt learning, where prompts are dynamically generated for each input image via a lightweight neural network, will yield more generalizable and transferable representations for vision-language models compared to static, class-specific prompt learning.
b879450f50a6113f44a5baf0bcd5b4331eeb7bbc.proposed_method: A novel framework, Conditional Context Optimization (CoCoOp), will be developed to address the limitations of static prompt learning in vision-language models. The method will extend existing prompt learning approaches by introducing a lightweight neural network (Meta-Net) that generates an input-conditional token for each image. This token will be combined with a set of learnable context vectors to form dynamic prompts, which are then processed by a frozen pre-trained vision-language model (such as CLIP). The approach will optimize the context vectors and Meta-Net parameters using a small number of labeled images from downstream datasets, ensuring parameter efficiency and adaptability. The overall architecture will allow gradients to flow through both the context vectors and the Meta-Net, enabling end-to-end optimization of the prompt generation process.
b879450f50a6113f44a5baf0bcd5b4331eeb7bbc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 11 diverse visual recognition datasets, including challenging scene recognition benchmarks such as SUN397. The evaluation protocol will include a base-to-new generalization setting, where models are trained on base classes and tested on completely novel, unseen classes. Additional experiments will assess cross-dataset transfer and domain generalization capabilities. Baselines will include manual prompt engineering, zero-shot CLIP, and static prompt learning approaches such as CoOp. Performance will be measured using standard accuracy metrics on both base and novel classes, as well as transfer and domain generalization tasks. The experimental setup will ensure that the vision-language backbone remains frozen to isolate the effect of prompt learning strategies.
b879450f50a6113f44a5baf0bcd5b4331eeb7bbc.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the concept of instance-conditional prompt learning for vision-language models, a paradigm shift from static, class-specific prompt optimization. By leveraging a parameter-efficient neural network to generate dynamic prompts conditioned on each input image, the method addresses the overfitting and poor generalization issues of prior prompt learning approaches. This framework is claimed to be the first to systematically tackle the generalizability problem in prompt learning for vision-language models, demonstrating substantial improvements in transferability to unseen classes and domains. The method also provides a simple yet effective solution that is orthogonal to advances in vision-language model architectures and is broadly applicable to CLIP-like models.

b88ba0959975d1aba56b182735c3abb5cc344023.title: Score as Action: Fine-Tuning Diffusion Generative Models by Continuous-time Reinforcement Learning
b88ba0959975d1aba56b182735c3abb5cc344023.research_question: How can diffusion generative models be fine-tuned to better align with human preferences or feedback, while preserving their continuous-time structure and improving robustness to time discretization and solver choices?
b88ba0959975d1aba56b182735c3abb5cc344023.hypothesis: Fine-tuning diffusion models via a continuous-time reinforcement learning (RL) framework, formulated as a stochastic control problem where score functions are treated as actions, will yield improved alignment with human preferences, enhanced robustness to time discretization, and superior sample quality compared to discrete-time RL and other baseline methods.
b88ba0959975d1aba56b182735c3abb5cc344023.proposed_method: A unified continuous-time RL framework will be developed for fine-tuning diffusion models, treating the score function as a control variable within the backward stochastic differential equation (SDE) that governs the generative process. The fine-tuning objective will combine a terminal reward, reflecting alignment with human feedback (e.g., via a reward model like ImageReward), and a regularization term based on the KL divergence between the fine-tuned and pretrained model distributions. Policy optimization will be performed using a scalable algorithm that leverages the structural properties of diffusion models, including a novel value network design that incorporates both denoised sample prediction and residual correction. Policy gradients will be estimated directly in continuous time, avoiding discretization-induced errors, and the algorithm will accommodate both discrete and continuous-time solvers.
b88ba0959975d1aba56b182735c3abb5cc344023.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both small-scale and large-scale diffusion models. For small-scale evaluation, the CIFAR-10 dataset will be used to fine-tune a DDPM-based diffusion model with a reduced number of generation steps (e.g., T=10), and performance will be measured using the Frechet Inception Distance (FID). The method will be compared against DxMI (an inverse RL-based diffusion training method) under matched settings. For large-scale evaluation, Stable Diffusion v1.5 will be fine-tuned on text-to-image tasks, using the pretrained ImageReward model as the reward signal. The value network will be based on a BLIP backbone with an MLP header, and LoRA will be used for efficient U-Net adaptation. Comparisons will include discrete-time RL baselines and other non-RL fine-tuning methods. Evaluation metrics will include reward model scores and qualitative sample quality, with robustness to time discretization assessed by varying the number of inference steps.
b88ba0959975d1aba56b182735c3abb5cc344023.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first scalable policy optimization algorithm for continuous-time RL tailored to diffusion models, leveraging their intrinsic continuous-time structure. It formulates fine-tuning as a stochastic control problem with score functions as actions, enabling direct optimization in continuous time and overcoming limitations of discrete-time RL methods. The method also presents a novel value network architecture that exploits the denoised sample prediction property of diffusion models, leading to more effective value estimation. Theoretical contributions include new policy gradient and policy improvement results for KL-regularized rewards with state-independent diffusion coefficients, as well as explicit bounds on the performance gap due to discretization. Experimental results demonstrate improved sample quality, faster convergence, and greater robustness to inference-time discretization compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

b8c236dc5963dac36b0d8e419beb5876e3a18f96.title: Deep Transformers without Shortcuts: Modifying Self-attention for Faithful Signal Propagation
b8c236dc5963dac36b0d8e419beb5876e3a18f96.research_question: Is it possible to successfully train deep transformers without relying on skip connections or normalization layers, and if so, what modifications to the self-attention mechanism are required to ensure faithful signal propagation and prevent rank collapse in such architectures?
b8c236dc5963dac36b0d8e419beb5876e3a18f96.hypothesis: Deep transformers without skip connections or normalization layers can be made trainable and achieve competitive performance with standard transformers by appropriately modifying the self-attention mechanism to ensure faithful signal propagation and avoid rank collapse.
b8c236dc5963dac36b0d8e419beb5876e3a18f96.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves designing new variants of the self-attention mechanism that enable faithful signal propagation in deep, skipless, and normalization-free transformers. Three approaches are introduced: Value-SkipInit, Uniform Signal Preserving Attention (U-SPA), and Exponential Signal Preserving Attention (E-SPA). Value-SkipInit modifies the attention operation to interpolate between the identity and standard attention at initialization, using trainable parameters. U-SPA and E-SPA construct attention matrices that preserve the kernel structure across layers, using Cholesky factors of well-behaved kernel families (uniform and exponentially decaying, respectively), ensuring diagonals remain stable and off-diagonals avoid rank collapse. These methods require careful parameter initialization, the use of bias matrices, and location-dependent rescaling to realize the desired attention matrices at initialization. The approach is compatible with causal masking and positional encodings, and can be extended to models with MLP blocks and optional skip connections.
b8c236dc5963dac36b0d8e419beb5876e3a18f96.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on WikiText-103 and C4 datasets using deep transformer models (up to 36 or more layers), focusing on next-token prediction tasks. Baselines include standard transformers with and without skip connections and normalization, as well as models using Deep Kernel Shaping (DKS) and other initialization schemes. Evaluation metrics include training loss, validation loss (perplexity), and downstream task performance. The Adam optimizer is used, and ablations are performed for different activation functions, normalization settings, and skip connection weights. The experimental setup also explores the impact of training duration and model depth, with results averaged over multiple random seeds.
b8c236dc5963dac36b0d8e419beb5876e3a18f96.novelty_claims: The proposed research claims the first demonstration that deep transformers can be successfully trained without skip connections or normalization layers by directly addressing signal propagation in self-attention. The introduction of E-SPA and U-SPA methods provides a principled way to construct attention matrices that avoid rank collapse and maintain stable signal propagation at large depths. The approach enables deep vanilla transformers to achieve performance parity with standard architectures, albeit with longer training, and allows normalization-free transformers with skip connections to match standard training speeds. These innovations offer new insights into transformer trainability and open avenues for more efficient and theoretically grounded architectures.

b8d0e4988790fcf2c769e607e0c94cfd03ae1aac.title: Lossy Compression with Pretrained Diffusion Models
b8d0e4988790fcf2c769e607e0c94cfd03ae1aac.research_question: Can pretrained diffusion models be effectively leveraged for lossy image compression, achieving competitive rate-distortion performance compared to state-of-the-art generative compression methods, without requiring additional training?
b8d0e4988790fcf2c769e607e0c94cfd03ae1aac.hypothesis: Pretrained diffusion models, when combined with a practical implementation of the DiffC algorithm and efficient reverse-channel coding, can serve as powerful and competitive lossy image compressors at ultra-low bitrates, without the need for retraining or specialized architectures.
b8d0e4988790fcf2c769e607e0c94cfd03ae1aac.proposed_method: The proposed method implements a practical, end-to-end lossy image compression protocol based on the DiffC algorithm, utilizing pretrained diffusion models such as Stable Diffusion 1.5, 2.1, XL, and Flux-dev. The approach operates in two main stages: first, a noisy sample of the target image is communicated using a sequence of reverse-channel coding steps, each transmitting minimal information to steer the denoising process. Second, the noisy sample is denoised using probability-flow-based DDPM denoising, specifically employing a probability flow ODE followed by a DDIM scheduler for efficient and high-fidelity reconstruction. Key technical innovations include a CUDA-based implementation of reverse-channel coding for speed, greedy optimization of denoising timestep schedules to minimize bitrate, and adaptation of the protocol to both DDPM and OT flow-based diffusion models. The method is zero-shot, requiring no additional training, and supports progressive encoding to arbitrary bitrates.
b8d0e4988790fcf2c769e607e0c94cfd03ae1aac.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image compression benchmarks, including the Kodak and DIV2K datasets. The method will be evaluated using various pretrained diffusion models (Stable Diffusion 1.5, 2.1, XL, and Flux-dev), and compared against state-of-the-art generative compression baselines such as HiFiC, MS-ILLM, DiffEIC, and PerCo. Evaluation metrics will include PSNR, LPIPS, CLIP score, and Q-Align for perceptual quality. Encoding and decoding times, as well as model parameter counts, will be measured on an A40 GPU. The experimental setup will systematically vary the number of denoising steps and bitrate, and will include ablation studies on prompt conditioning and denoising strategies. Visual comparisons and rate-distortion curves will be reported to assess both quantitative and qualitative performance.
b8d0e4988790fcf2c769e607e0c94cfd03ae1aac.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first complete and practical implementation of the DiffC algorithm for lossy image compression using large, pretrained diffusion models. Key innovations include overcoming the reverse-channel coding bottleneck with a fast CUDA-based implementation, a principled greedy optimization of denoising schedules, and zero-shot compression capability without retraining. The method demonstrates competitive or superior rate-distortion and perceptual quality compared to specialized generative compression methods, and is naturally progressive and flexible across bitrates and model architectures.

b8e71ca3603cfd24bdf98fa34f2664d9b99a444b.title: Spontaneous symmetry breaking in generative diffusion models
b8e71ca3603cfd24bdf98fa34f2664d9b99a444b.research_question: How can the underlying dynamics of generative diffusion models, particularly the phenomenon of spontaneous symmetry breaking, be leveraged to improve sample quality, diversity, and efficiency in generative modeling?
b8e71ca3603cfd24bdf98fa34f2664d9b99a444b.hypothesis: The generative dynamics of diffusion models exhibit a spontaneous symmetry breaking phenomenon that divides the process into distinct phases, and exploiting this bifurcation through optimized initialization schemes can significantly improve the performance and diversity of fast samplers.
b8e71ca3603cfd24bdf98fa34f2664d9b99a444b.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted to characterize the spontaneous symmetry breaking in the generative dynamics of diffusion models. The methodology involves analyzing the fixed points and stability of the potential function governing the generative stochastic differential equation (SDE), both in low-dimensional toy models and high-dimensional real datasets. Building on these insights, a Gaussian late initialization scheme will be developed, wherein the generative process is initialized at an empirically determined critical time point just before the onset of instability, using a Gaussian distribution fitted to the noise-corrupted dataset at that time. This approach aims to bypass the early mean-reverting phase, focusing computational resources on the critical window that determines sample diversity and quality. The method will be implemented for various fast samplers, including DDIM and PNDM, and compared with standard initialization strategies.
b8e71ca3603cfd24bdf98fa34f2664d9b99a444b.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed on a range of image datasets, including MNIST, CIFAR-10, CelebA (32x32 and 64x64), and Imagenet64x64. Diffusion models will be trained using both discrete-time (DDPM) and continuous-time (variance-preserving SDE) frameworks. Fast samplers such as DDIM and PNDM will be evaluated with both standard and proposed Gaussian late initialization schemes, using a fixed number of denoising steps (e.g., 3, 5, 10). Evaluation metrics will include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for sample quality and entropy-based measures for diversity, with additional analysis of demographic attributes (e.g., race, age, gender) using facial attribute classifiers on generated CelebA samples. The critical time for initialization will be determined empirically by maximizing FID performance across different starting times. Direct analysis of the potential function along interpolating paths between generated samples will be conducted to provide evidence of bifurcation and symmetry breaking.
b8e71ca3603cfd24bdf98fa34f2664d9b99a444b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel theoretical framework that identifies and characterizes spontaneous symmetry breaking in the generative dynamics of diffusion models, a phenomenon not previously explored in this context. The Gaussian late initialization scheme leverages this insight to optimize fast sampling, resulting in substantial improvements in both sample quality and diversity, with up to 3x better FID scores on certain datasets. The approach also provides a systematic, theoretically motivated method for selecting initialization points in fast samplers, addressing limitations of prior empirical heuristics. Additionally, the work offers new perspectives on the role of symmetry and phase transitions in deep generative modeling, with implications for fairness and bias reduction.

b8ebcf6f5330dce753b4ac462ca9e4ed06900e73.title: A Unified Theory of Diversity in Ensemble Learning
b8ebcf6f5330dce753b4ac462ca9e4ed06900e73.research_question: What is the formal role and definition of diversity in ensemble learning, and how does it relate to ensemble performance across a wide range of supervised learning scenarios and loss functions?
b8ebcf6f5330dce753b4ac462ca9e4ed06900e73.hypothesis: Diversity in ensemble learning can be rigorously defined as a quantifiable component within the bias-variance decomposition of ensemble loss, and managing a bias/variance/diversity trade-off—rather than simply maximizing diversity—leads to improved ensemble performance across various loss functions.
b8ebcf6f5330dce753b4ac462ca9e4ed06900e73.proposed_method: A unified theoretical framework will be developed that decomposes ensemble loss functions into bias, variance, and diversity components for a broad class of losses, including both regression and classification settings. The approach will generalize the bias-variance decomposition by introducing a 'diversity' term, derived from first principles, and will formalize the centroid combiner rule for ensemble aggregation as a function of the loss. The methodology will extend existing decompositions for squared loss to other losses such as cross-entropy and Poisson, and will provide alternative formulations for losses where additive decompositions are not available (e.g., 0/1 loss), quantifying diversity effects conditional on label distributions. The framework will leverage properties of Bregman divergences to derive analytic forms for both the centroid combiner and the diversity term, enabling a consistent treatment across different learning scenarios.
b8ebcf6f5330dce753b4ac462ca9e4ed06900e73.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets spanning regression and classification tasks, utilizing a variety of loss functions (e.g., squared, cross-entropy, Poisson, and 0/1 loss). Ensembles will be constructed using standard methods such as Bagging, Random Forests, and Boosting, with different ensemble sizes and member generation strategies (parallel and sequential). Baselines will include classical bias-variance decompositions and existing diversity measures from the literature. Evaluation metrics will include ensemble risk, average individual risk, empirical bias, variance, and the newly defined diversity term, as well as overall predictive performance. The experimental setup will systematically vary model capacity and ensemble member similarity to empirically validate the theoretical trade-offs and the impact of diversity on ensemble performance.
b8ebcf6f5330dce753b4ac462ca9e4ed06900e73.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a unified, loss-dependent theory of ensemble diversity that generalizes and subsumes prior results, providing exact bias-variance-diversity decompositions for a wide range of loss functions. The approach formalizes diversity as a hidden dimension in the bias-variance decomposition, applicable to both regression and classification, and establishes the centroid combiner as a principled aggregation rule. For loss functions lacking additive decompositions, the method offers alternative, label-dependent quantifications of diversity. The research challenges the prevailing heuristic of maximizing diversity, instead advocating for explicit management of a bias/variance/diversity trade-off, fundamentally advancing the theoretical understanding of ensemble learning.

b8f280d8bf685f8da7c83068e73f000528072d6b.title: Sparse Feature Circuits: Discovering and Editing Interpretable Causal Graphs in Language Models
b8f280d8bf685f8da7c83068e73f000528072d6b.research_question: How can interpretable, fine-grained causal circuits within language models be scalably discovered and edited to explain and modify model behaviors, and how can these circuits be leveraged to improve model generalization and robustness to spurious correlations without requiring disambiguating labeled data?
b8f280d8bf685f8da7c83068e73f000528072d6b.hypothesis: Sparse feature circuits, constructed from human-interpretable features identified via sparse autoencoders, can provide faithful and complete causal explanations of language model behaviors. Editing these circuits by ablating task-irrelevant features, as judged by humans, will improve model generalization and reduce reliance on spurious signals, even in the absence of disambiguating labeled data.
b8f280d8bf685f8da7c83068e73f000528072d6b.proposed_method: A scalable framework will be developed for discovering sparse feature circuits in language models by leveraging sparse autoencoders (SAEs) trained on model submodules (such as attention layers, MLPs, and residual streams). The method will decompose model activations into sparse, interpretable features and error terms, treating these as nodes in a computation graph. Causal effects of each node and edge on a chosen model metric (e.g., output probability difference) will be estimated using efficient linear approximations (attribution patching and integrated gradients) to compute indirect effects. Nodes and edges with significant causal influence will be aggregated into sparse feature circuits that explain specific model behaviors. The approach will support both supervised (contrastive pairs, classification data) and unsupervised (clustering behaviors from large corpora) discovery of circuits.
b8f280d8bf685f8da7c83068e73f000528072d6b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on language models such as Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B, using both custom-trained and open-source SAEs. Evaluation will include subject-verb agreement tasks (with datasets adapted from prior work) using contrastive input pairs, as well as a classifier debiasing task on the Bias in Bios dataset, where profession and gender labels are used to test generalization and robustness to spurious correlations. Baselines will include neuron-based circuits, random feature ablations, concept bottleneck probing, and oracle classifiers. Metrics will include interpretability (via human annotation), faithfulness and completeness (proportion of model behavior explained or eliminated by the circuit), accuracy on intended and unintended labels, and worst-group accuracy. Additionally, an unsupervised pipeline will be applied to a large text corpus (The Pile) to discover thousands of circuits for automatically clustered behaviors.
b8f280d8bf685f8da7c83068e73f000528072d6b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a scalable method for discovering and editing sparse, human-interpretable causal circuits in language models, overcoming the limitations of polysemantic and hard-to-interpret units like neurons or attention heads. The method enables detailed mechanistic understanding and practical editing of model behaviors, including the removal of spurious signals without access to disambiguating labeled data. A fully unsupervised pipeline is developed for large-scale circuit discovery, and the SHIFT technique is introduced for classifier debiasing via human-guided feature ablation. The approach demonstrates superior interpretability and effectiveness compared to neuron-based and other baseline methods.

b9180d372eb2d3232e7124ac1b6ef98550ec99f2.title: Understanding Oversquashing in GNNs through the Lens of Effective Resistance
b9180d372eb2d3232e7124ac1b6ef98550ec99f2.research_question: How can the phenomenon of oversquashing in graph neural networks (GNNs) be better understood and mitigated by leveraging global graph connectivity measures, and what is the relationship between effective resistance and the ability of GNNs to transmit information between distant nodes?
b9180d372eb2d3232e7124ac1b6ef98550ec99f2.hypothesis: Reducing the total effective resistance in a graph will alleviate oversquashing in GNNs, thereby improving the ability of GNNs to transmit information between distant nodes and enhancing overall model performance on graph-based tasks.
b9180d372eb2d3232e7124ac1b6ef98550ec99f2.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that analyzes oversquashing in GNNs through the lens of effective resistance, a well-established graph-theoretic measure of connectivity. The method will introduce total effective resistance as a global quantification of oversquashing and provide theoretical justification for its use as an upper bound on information contraction in GNNs. An algorithm will be designed to identify and add edges to the input graph that minimize total effective resistance, using a greedy heuristic based on the biharmonic distance and effective resistance between node pairs. This rewiring strategy will be implemented as a preprocessing step before GNN training, and relational GNN architectures will be employed to accommodate both original and newly added edges, leveraging edge-type information for improved message passing.
b9180d372eb2d3232e7124ac1b6ef98550ec99f2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard graph classification benchmarks from the TUDataset collection, including datasets such as Mutag, Proteins, Enzymes, Reddit-Binary, IMDB-Binary, and Collab. The proposed rewiring method (GTR) will be compared against multiple baselines, including no rewiring, curvature-based rewiring (SDRF), spectral gap-based rewiring (FoSR), and fully connected augmentation strategies. Multiple GNN architectures, such as GCN, GIN, and their relational variants, will be evaluated. The number of edges added by the rewiring algorithm will be treated as a hyperparameter. Performance will be measured using classification accuracy, and additional analyses will include ablation studies on the number of edges added and the effect of hidden dimension size. Evaluation will also consider the impact of rewiring on spectral properties and total effective resistance of the graphs.
b9180d372eb2d3232e7124ac1b6ef98550ec99f2.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretically grounded approach to quantifying and mitigating oversquashing in GNNs using effective resistance, providing the first direct theoretical link between total effective resistance and oversquashing. The rewiring algorithm leverages global graph connectivity rather than local or purely spectral criteria, and is shown to outperform or match state-of-the-art rewiring strategies in empirical benchmarks. Theoretical analysis extends previous work by bounding oversquashing between arbitrary node pairs and across arbitrary GNN depths, rather than being limited to local neighborhoods or shallow layers. The method also offers a practical, scalable heuristic for graph rewiring with provable impact on global information flow in GNNs.

b923138069cdec59b976424cd0fbb41702a56239.title: Koopa: Learning Non-stationary Time Series Dynamics with Koopman Predictors
b923138069cdec59b976424cd0fbb41702a56239.research_question: How can non-stationary time series with complex, time-varying dynamics be effectively forecasted by leveraging modern dynamical systems theory, particularly in the presence of both time-invariant and time-variant components?
b923138069cdec59b976424cd0fbb41702a56239.hypothesis: Decomposing non-stationary time series into time-invariant and time-variant components using frequency-domain analysis, and modeling each with specialized, hierarchically organized Koopman predictors, will improve forecasting accuracy and efficiency compared to existing deep learning-based and Koopman-based methods.
b923138069cdec59b976424cd0fbb41702a56239.proposed_method: A novel forecasting framework, Koopa, will be developed to address non-stationary time series by disentangling time-invariant and time-variant dynamics using a Fourier Filter at each layer. The architecture will consist of stackable Koopa Blocks, each responsible for learning hierarchical dynamics by taking the residual of the previous block's fitted system as input. Within each block, the Fourier Filter separates the input into time-invariant and time-variant components. Time-invariant Koopman Predictors will learn globally shared Koopman embeddings and operators from all lookback-forecast windows, while time-variant Koopman Predictors will compute localized, context-aware operators within each lookback window using dynamic mode decomposition. The outputs of all blocks will be aggregated to form the final forecast, and the model will be trained end-to-end without the reconstruction loss typical of canonical Koopman autoencoders.
b923138069cdec59b976424cd0fbb41702a56239.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six real-world time series forecasting benchmarks, covering a range of domains and exhibiting various degrees of non-stationarity. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines, including Transformer-based models, MLP-based models, and previous Koopman-based approaches. Evaluation metrics will include forecasting accuracy (such as MAE, RMSE), training time, and memory consumption. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by using consistent lookback and forecast window sizes, and by reporting averaged results across multiple runs.
b923138069cdec59b976424cd0fbb41702a56239.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a modular, hierarchical Koopman forecasting framework that explicitly disentangles and models time-invariant and time-variant dynamics in non-stationary series. The use of Fourier-based disentanglement and localized Koopman operator learning within a residual deep architecture is novel. The method supports context-aware adaptation to incoming data, enabling scalable forecast horizons. Additionally, the architecture achieves competitive or superior performance to state-of-the-art baselines while significantly reducing training time and memory usage.

b92985bc6723edaf7c450b970751602552a67a0d.title: Neural network learns low-dimensional polynomials with SGD near the information-theoretic limit
b92985bc6723edaf7c450b970751602552a67a0d.research_question: Can gradient-based training of neural networks efficiently learn single-index models with low-dimensional polynomial link functions, achieving sample and computational complexity near the information-theoretic limit, even when prior correlational statistical query lower bounds suggest higher complexity?
b92985bc6723edaf7c450b970751602552a67a0d.hypothesis: Gradient-based optimization of two-layer neural networks using stochastic gradient descent (SGD) with minibatch reuse can learn single-index models with polynomial link functions at a sample complexity that matches the information-theoretic lower bound up to polylogarithmic factors, regardless of the information exponent of the link function.
b92985bc6723edaf7c450b970751602552a67a0d.proposed_method: A two-layer neural network with N neurons will be trained using SGD to minimize the squared loss on data drawn from an isotropic Gaussian distribution in high dimensions. The network will use polynomial activation functions constructed as sums of Hermite polynomials up to a degree determined by the target link function's degree. Training will proceed in two phases: first, the first-layer weights are optimized using normalized SGD with a key feature of reusing the same minibatch for consecutive gradient steps, enabling the extraction of higher-order (non-correlational) information from the gradient updates. An interpolation (negative momentum) step is introduced to stabilize training and enhance signal-to-noise ratio. After sufficient alignment with the target direction is achieved, the second-layer parameters are trained (e.g., via ridge regression) to fit the unknown link function, leveraging random bias units for universal approximation.
b92985bc6723edaf7c450b970751602552a67a0d.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training the proposed two-layer neural network on synthetic datasets generated according to the single-index model y = σ*(⟨x, θ⟩) + noise, where x is drawn from a standard Gaussian in d dimensions and σ* is a polynomial of degree q. The sample complexity n and runtime T will be varied as functions of d and compared to theoretical predictions. Baseline comparisons will include online SGD (one-pass, no batch reuse), kernel methods, and existing statistical query (SQ) and correlational statistical query (CSQ) algorithms. Evaluation metrics will include population squared loss (generalization error) and alignment between learned and true index directions. Key experimental setups will test the effect of minibatch reuse, activation function choice, and the impact of information versus generative exponent on learnability.
b92985bc6723edaf7c450b970751602552a67a0d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach demonstrates that SGD with minibatch reuse can implement non-correlational label transformations, enabling learning of single-index polynomials at near-optimal sample complexity, independent of the information exponent. This challenges prior conjectures and lower bounds based on the CSQ model, showing that neural networks can match the efficiency of tailored SQ algorithms for low-dimensional polynomial regression. The method provides the first general statistical guarantees for SGD-trained neural networks learning arbitrary polynomial single-index models near the information-theoretic limit, and introduces a practical algorithmic framework that leverages higher-order information via minibatch reuse.

b945115f175231d7fafefbdeacdc40edc391273f.title: Inference Scaling Laws: An Empirical Analysis of Compute-Optimal Inference for LLM Problem-Solving
b945115f175231d7fafefbdeacdc40edc391273f.research_question: How does the allocation of inference-time compute between model size and inference strategy affect the problem-solving performance of large language models (LLMs), and what are the empirical scaling laws governing compute-optimal inference configurations across different tasks and model families?
b945115f175231d7fafefbdeacdc40edc391273f.hypothesis: Smaller language models, when paired with advanced inference strategies, can achieve equal or superior problem-solving performance compared to larger models under the same inference compute budget. Furthermore, novel tree search algorithms can yield more favorable cost-performance trade-offs than conventional sampling or existing tree search methods.
b945115f175231d7fafefbdeacdc40edc391273f.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical investigation will be conducted to characterize inference scaling laws for LLMs by systematically varying model sizes and inference strategies under fixed inference compute budgets. The methodology will include the implementation and evaluation of several inference strategies: greedy search, best-of-n, majority voting, weighted majority voting, and tree search algorithms such as Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) and a newly proposed Reward Balanced Search (REBASE). The REBASE algorithm will be designed to use a process reward model for node expansion, leveraging softmax-normalized reward scores to allocate expansion budgets at each tree depth, thus eliminating the need for explicit rollouts and improving computational efficiency. Theoretical analysis will be performed to establish convergence properties and upper bounds for sampling-based voting strategies, highlighting their limitations and motivating the use of more sophisticated search-based inference methods.
b945115f175231d7fafefbdeacdc40edc391273f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on mathematical reasoning benchmarks, specifically GSM8K (grade-school math) and MATH (high school competition-level math), with the MATH500 subset used for detailed evaluation. Multiple model families and sizes will be tested, including general-purpose LLMs (such as Pythia and Mistral) and math-specialized models (such as Llemma-7B and Llemma-34B), all fine-tuned on the MetaMath dataset. A consistent reward model (Llemma-34B fine-tuned on Math-Shepherd) will be used for candidate scoring across all inference strategies. Each inference configuration will be evaluated across a range of compute budgets (measured in FLOPs per question), and performance will be assessed using error rates on the test sets. Baselines will include standard sampling-based methods and MCTS, with all methods compared in terms of both accuracy and computational cost.
b945115f175231d7fafefbdeacdc40edc391273f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first systematic empirical study of inference scaling laws for LLMs, focusing on the trade-offs between model size and inference strategy under fixed compute budgets. It formulates the compute-optimal inference problem and provides new theoretical analysis of convergence properties for voting-based inference. The proposed REBASE tree search algorithm is claimed to be Pareto-optimal, achieving superior cost-performance trade-offs compared to both sampling-based and existing tree search methods such as MCTS. The findings are expected to demonstrate that smaller models with advanced inference algorithms can outperform larger models in compute-constrained settings, offering new insights and practical guidelines for deploying LLMs efficiently.

b95ca121a606da32180ab8bb0c0c58bf19b1499b.title: Guiding LLMs The Right Way: Fast, Non-Invasive Constrained Generation
b95ca121a606da32180ab8bb0c0c58bf19b1499b.research_question: How can constrained decoding for large language models be made both highly efficient and minimally invasive, ensuring that generated outputs strictly adhere to complex syntactic constraints (such as context-free grammars or regular expressions) without incurring significant computational overhead or loss in task accuracy?
b95ca121a606da32180ab8bb0c0c58bf19b1499b.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a decoding algorithm leveraging pre-computation, subword-aligned constraint enforcement, and speculative decoding can achieve minimally invasive constrained generation for LLMs, resulting in strict syntactic adherence, negligible or even negative performance overhead, and no loss in downstream task accuracy compared to unconstrained decoding.
b95ca121a606da32180ab8bb0c0c58bf19b1499b.proposed_method: A novel decoding algorithm, DOMINO, will be developed to enforce syntactic constraints (such as context-free grammars and regular expressions) in a fully subword-aligned manner during LLM generation. The method will pre-compute scanner and parser states, constructing subterminal prefix trees that align the model's token vocabulary with grammar terminals. During inference, the algorithm will efficiently traverse these pre-computed trees to generate token masks, ensuring only valid continuations are allowed at each step. DOMINO will further incorporate speculative decoding and opportunistic masking, allowing the model to propose multiple tokens in parallel and validate them efficiently, thus reducing the number of model forward passes. The approach will be designed to be minimally invasive, intervening only when necessary to enforce constraints, and will support both offline and online grammar enforcement scenarios.
b95ca121a606da32180ab8bb0c0c58bf19b1499b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on benchmark tasks requiring structured output, including GSM8K (math reasoning) and CoNLL-2003 (named entity recognition), using models such as Mistral-7B and Llama-2 13B. The evaluation will compare DOMINO against unconstrained decoding and several baseline constrained decoding methods (e.g., GUIDANCE, LLAMA.CPP, template-based approaches) in terms of downstream task accuracy, output validity, perplexity, and throughput. Datasets will be formatted to require outputs in JSON or other structured formats, and prompts will use few-shot demonstrations. Metrics will include accuracy of the generated structured outputs, well-formedness, perplexity, and relative generation speed (tokens per second) under various constraint types (e.g., JSON with/without schema, C code, XML). Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of lookahead parameters and speculative decoding settings.
b95ca121a606da32180ab8bb0c0c58bf19b1499b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a minimally invasive, subword-aligned constrained decoding algorithm that leverages pre-computation and speculative decoding to enforce complex syntactic constraints with negligible or negative overhead. Unlike prior methods, DOMINO achieves strict constraint adherence without sacrificing task accuracy or throughput, and in many cases, surpasses unconstrained generation speed. The method is general, supporting regex, context-free grammars, and template-based constraints, and is the first to demonstrate that constrained decoding can be both highly efficient and non-invasive for LLMs.

b9830d64bb2cf35197b2597b030da05f0fe66dea.title: Deep Learning for Time Series Anomaly Detection: A Survey
