b9830d64bb2cf35197b2597b030da05f0fe66dea.research_question: How can deep learning techniques be systematically categorized, advanced, and evaluated for effective anomaly detection in time series data across diverse domains and anomaly types?
b9830d64bb2cf35197b2597b030da05f0fe66dea.hypothesis: Deep learning models, when systematically categorized by detection strategy and neural architecture, can outperform traditional methods in time series anomaly detection by effectively capturing complex temporal and spatial dependencies, and can be tailored to address a wide variety of anomaly types and application domains.
b9830d64bb2cf35197b2597b030da05f0fe66dea.proposed_method: A comprehensive taxonomy will be developed to classify deep learning models for time series anomaly detection into forecasting-based, reconstruction-based, representation-based, and hybrid methods. Each category will be further subdivided according to the underlying neural network architectures, such as RNNs, CNNs, Transformers, GANs, AEs, VAEs, GNNs, and HTMs. The methodology will include a detailed analysis of learning schemes (supervised, unsupervised, semi-supervised, self-supervised), input formats (point vs. window), and anomaly types (point, contextual, seasonal, trend, shapelet, intermetric, and temporal-intermetric). Practical guidelines will be formulated for model selection, dataset choice, and interpretability, and a structured framework for evaluating models using appropriate metrics and thresholding techniques will be established. The approach will also address model interpretability and incremental learning capabilities, ensuring applicability to real-world streaming and high-dimensional settings.
b9830d64bb2cf35197b2597b030da05f0fe66dea.experiment_details: Experiments will involve benchmarking state-of-the-art deep learning anomaly detection models on a curated set of publicly available time series datasets spanning domains such as finance, healthcare, manufacturing, and urban management. Datasets will be categorized by domain and made accessible via hyperlinks for reproducibility. Baseline comparisons will include both traditional statistical, clustering, distance, and density-based methods, as well as recent deep learning models. Evaluation will utilize metrics such as precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC, and domain-specific interpretability measures. Experimental setups will consider both univariate and multivariate time series, with attention to the detection of both point and subsequence anomalies, and will include ablation studies on model components and learning schemes.
b9830d64bb2cf35197b2597b030da05f0fe66dea.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a novel, fine-grained taxonomy of deep learning models for time series anomaly detection, encompassing recent advances and emerging architectures not covered in prior surveys. It provides an integrated framework for model selection, interpretability, and metric evaluation, along with practical guidelines for practitioners. The work compiles and categorizes benchmarks and datasets, addresses open challenges, and identifies future research directions, thereby offering a comprehensive resource for advancing the field of time series anomaly detection with deep learning.

b9b220b485d2add79118ffdc2aaa148b67fa53ef.title: Pre-Trained Language Models for Interactive Decision-Making
b9b220b485d2add79118ffdc2aaa148b67fa53ef.research_question: Can pre-trained language models be leveraged as a general framework for interactive sequential decision-making across diverse environments, including those without explicit language inputs or outputs? How does the use of sequential input representations and LM-based weight initialization affect generalization and policy learning in such tasks?
b9b220b485d2add79118ffdc2aaa148b67fa53ef.hypothesis: Pre-trained language models, when used to initialize policy networks and provided with sequential input representations of goals, observations, and histories, will enable more effective learning and combinatorial generalization in interactive decision-making tasks than traditional policy learning methods, regardless of whether the input encoding is natural language or an arbitrary sequence.
b9b220b485d2add79118ffdc2aaa148b67fa53ef.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed in which all policy inputs—goals, observations, and action histories—are converted into sequential data (e.g., sequences of tokens, which may be natural language, indices, or arbitrary strings). These sequences are embedded and passed into a transformer-based policy network initialized with the weights of a pre-trained language model (such as GPT-2). The policy network is fine-tuned via imitation learning to predict the next action, maximizing the likelihood of expert or high-reward trajectories. In addition to imitation learning on expert data, an active data gathering procedure is integrated, where the agent explores the environment, relabels failed trajectories with new goals using hindsight relabeling, and updates the policy in a self-supervised loop. The approach is designed to be broadly applicable, supporting various input modalities and encoding schemes.
b9b220b485d2add79118ffdc2aaa148b67fa53ef.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in two embodied environments: VirtualHome (a 3D partially observable environment with complex goals and large action spaces) and BabyAI (a 2D grid world for instruction following). The method will be evaluated on in-distribution tasks, novel scenes (randomized object placements), and novel tasks (unseen combinations of goals and objects). Baselines will include recurrent networks (LSTM), multilayer perceptrons (MLP), online RL methods (PPO), Hindsight Experience Replay (DQN+HER), and the original BabyAI method. Evaluation metrics will primarily be task success rates, measured over hundreds of episodes and multiple random seeds. Ablation studies will analyze the effects of input encoding schemes, sequential vs. non-sequential representations, and pre-trained vs. randomly initialized weights. Both imitation learning (with expert data) and active data gathering (without expert data) setups will be explored.
b9b220b485d2add79118ffdc2aaa148b67fa53ef.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the use of pre-trained language models as a general-purpose scaffold for interactive decision-making by converting all policy inputs into sequential data, regardless of their original modality. It demonstrates that LM-based policy initialization and sequential input representations substantially improve combinatorial generalization to novel tasks and environments. The integration of an active data gathering procedure enables policy learning without pre-collected expert data, outperforming standard RL and HER methods in complex embodied environments. Analyses reveal that the benefits of LM pre-training extend beyond natural language inputs to arbitrary sequential encodings, and that both sequential processing and weight initialization are critical for generalization. This approach positions pre-trained LMs as a computational backbone for structured generalization in decision-making tasks beyond language processing.

b9bbebe9f719e33229dd0801275f984c8f4f21ae.title: Enhanced gradient-based MCMC in discrete spaces
b9bbebe9f719e33229dd0801275f984c8f4f21ae.research_question: How can gradient-based Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods be effectively extended to discrete spaces to improve sampling efficiency, especially in the presence of high-dimensional and strongly correlated discrete distributions?
b9bbebe9f719e33229dd0801275f984c8f4f21ae.hypothesis: Discrete analogues of continuous gradient-based MCMC methods, such as MALA, equipped with mechanisms for multi-dimensional updates and preconditioning, will yield more efficient and effective sampling in discrete spaces compared to existing baselines.
b9bbebe9f719e33229dd0801275f984c8f4f21ae.proposed_method: The proposal is to develop several new discrete gradient-based MCMC samplers inspired by the Metropolis-Adjusted Langevin Algorithm (MALA). The first method, the Norm-Constrained Gradient (NCG) sampler, uses a soft norm constraint to enable multi-dimensional updates in the proposal distribution, addressing the limitation of single-dimension updates in prior methods. The second method, Auxiliary Variable Gradient (AVG) sampler, employs auxiliary Gaussian variables and a Taylor expansion to construct a tractable, fully-factorised proposal distribution in an extended state-space. The third method, Preconditioned AVG (PAVG), extends AVG by incorporating a global quadratic approximation and a preconditioning matrix, estimated adaptively, to capture second-order interactions. All methods are implemented within a Metropolis-Hastings framework, with efficient sampling and evaluation enabled by the factorised structure of the proposals.
b9bbebe9f719e33229dd0801275f984c8f4f21ae.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of challenging discrete sampling problems, including high-dimensional correlated ordinal mixture distributions, sparse Bayesian variable selection in linear regression, Ising models, and deep energy-based models parameterized by convolutional neural networks. Baselines for comparison include Gibbs-with-Gradients (GWG), standard Gibbs sampling, Metropolis-Hastings with uniform proposals, and ordinal-GWG. Evaluation metrics will include marginal and pairwise estimation errors (using KL divergence and Frobenius norm), effective sample size (ESS), and parameter estimation error for identifiable models. Each experiment will use either exact or approximate ground-truth distributions to enable quantitative comparison, and step-size and preconditioning parameters will be tuned or adaptively estimated as appropriate.
b9bbebe9f719e33229dd0801275f984c8f4f21ae.novelty_claims: The proposed methods introduce the first discrete analogues of MALA that allow for multi-dimensional updates and tractable preconditioning in discrete spaces. The use of auxiliary variables and the 'Gaussian integral trick' enables a new form of preconditioning that was previously intractable for general discrete distributions. The framework extends prior auxiliary-variable schemes to more general target distributions and demonstrates, for the first time, how discrete gradient-based samplers can be derived from both locally-informed and auxiliary-variable frameworks. Empirical results are expected to show superior sampling efficiency and estimation accuracy compared to existing baselines, particularly in high-dimensional and strongly correlated settings.

b9c289f141c54ab465a885fb7be7936d98e8c853.title: Better & Faster Large Language Models via Multi-token Prediction
b9c289f141c54ab465a885fb7be7936d98e8c853.research_question: Can training large language models to predict multiple future tokens at each position, rather than just the next token, improve sample efficiency, downstream capabilities, and inference speed for both code and natural language tasks?
b9c289f141c54ab465a885fb7be7936d98e8c853.hypothesis: Training language models with a multi-token prediction objective, where the model predicts several future tokens in parallel at each position, will result in higher sample efficiency, improved downstream performance (especially on generative and reasoning tasks), and faster inference compared to standard next-token prediction approaches.
b9c289f141c54ab465a885fb7be7936d98e8c853.proposed_method: A novel multi-token prediction framework will be developed for large language models, where at each position in the training corpus, the model is tasked with predicting the next n tokens using n independent output heads, all operating on top of a shared transformer trunk. The architecture will be designed to minimize memory and compute overhead by sequentially computing the forward and backward passes for each output head, accumulating gradients at the trunk and freeing memory before moving to the next head. During inference, only the next-token head will be used for standard autoregressive generation, but the additional heads will be leveraged for self-speculative decoding to accelerate inference. The method will also include ablations to determine the optimal number of tokens to predict and adaptations for different vocabulary sizes and tokenization schemes.
b9c289f141c54ab465a885fb7be7936d98e8c853.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by training models of various sizes (from 300M to 13B parameters) on large-scale code and natural language datasets, including up to 1T tokens. Evaluation will be performed on established benchmarks such as MBPP, HumanEval, APPS/Intro for code, and ROUGE-based summarization, GSM8K for mathematics, and multiple-choice NLP tasks for natural language. Baselines will include compute-matched next-token prediction models. Metrics will include pass@k for code tasks, ROUGE-L for summarization, accuracy for mathematics and reasoning, and inference speedup via speculative decoding. Experiments will also include ablations on the number of predicted tokens, training with different tokenization schemes (byte-level vs. subword), and fine-tuning on downstream tasks such as CodeContests.
b9c289f141c54ab465a885fb7be7936d98e8c853.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a simple yet effective multi-token prediction architecture for large language models that incurs no additional training time or memory overhead. It claims significant improvements in sample efficiency and downstream performance, particularly for larger models and generative tasks such as code synthesis. The approach enables self-speculative decoding for up to 3x faster inference, and demonstrates that multi-token prediction fosters the development of induction heads and algorithmic reasoning capabilities. The method is shown to be especially beneficial at scale and when training for multiple epochs, and offers a memory-efficient implementation suitable for large-scale training.

b9d2c40f1fc33d5bc80d66d0553f8703cd3e9e94.title: Slot-VAE: Object-Centric Scene Generation with Slot Attention
b9d2c40f1fc33d5bc80d66d0553f8703cd3e9e94.research_question: How can object-centric scene generation be improved to enable coherent, high-quality, and controllable generation of novel scenes, while supporting unsupervised object decomposition and attribute-level disentanglement?
b9d2c40f1fc33d5bc80d66d0553f8703cd3e9e94.hypothesis: Integrating slot attention with a hierarchical variational autoencoder (VAE) framework, and employing independent priors on slot representations, will enable effective joint inference of global scene and object-centric representations, leading to improved sample quality, scene structure accuracy, and disentanglement compared to existing slot-based generative models.
b9d2c40f1fc33d5bc80d66d0553f8703cd3e9e94.proposed_method: A novel generative model, Slot-VAE, will be developed by embedding the slot attention mechanism within a hierarchical VAE architecture. The model will infer a global scene latent vector to capture high-level scene structure and a set of object-centric slot representations to encode individual object components. During generation, slot representations will be produced from the global scene vector using a shared slot attention module, ensuring coherence in scene structure. The inference process will use a convolutional neural network (CNN) for feature extraction, followed by slot attention and a shared multilayer perceptron (MLP) to infer Gaussian parameters for each slot. Training will employ a variational objective with an auxiliary loss to enforce independence among slots, and architectural strategies such as weight and initialization sharing between slot attention modules will be used to address slot order matching and enable effective KL divergence calculation.
b9d2c40f1fc33d5bc80d66d0553f8703cd3e9e94.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three multi-object synthetic datasets: ObjectRoom, ShapeStacks, and ArrowRoom, each presenting varying complexity in object shapes and scene structure. The proposed model will be compared against state-of-the-art object-centric generative baselines including GENESIS, GENESIS-V2, SRI, and GNM. Evaluation metrics will include Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) for segmentation quality, Frechet Inception Distance (FID) for sample quality, and Scene Structure Accuracy (S-Acc) for the correctness of generated scene relationships. Both qualitative and quantitative analyses will be performed, including ablation studies to assess the importance of slot attention, weight sharing, and initialization strategies. Baseline models will be evaluated using either publicly available pre-trained weights or by training with official code, ensuring fair comparison.
b9d2c40f1fc33d5bc80d66d0553f8703cd3e9e94.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first integration of slot attention within a hierarchical VAE framework for object-centric scene generation, enabling the simultaneous learning of global scene and object-centric representations. The method provides a principled probabilistic approach to object and attribute-level disentanglement, and introduces architectural innovations such as shared slot attention modules with weight and initialization sharing to address the slot order matching problem. Extensive experiments are expected to demonstrate superior sample quality, scene structure learning, and disentanglement compared to existing slot-based generative models.

b9dc7f44768dcb18c4a3ad8dafa727defbb280ba.title: Domain Generalization by Mutual-Information Regularization with Pre-trained Models
b9dc7f44768dcb18c4a3ad8dafa727defbb280ba.research_question: How can domain generalization be improved by leveraging information from pre-trained models, particularly in the presence of significant distribution shifts between source and unseen target domains?
b9dc7f44768dcb18c4a3ad8dafa727defbb280ba.hypothesis: Maximizing the mutual information between the representations of a target model and those of a large pre-trained model (used as an oracle approximation) during training will lead to more robust, domain-generalized features, thereby improving out-of-distribution performance compared to standard empirical risk minimization or existing domain generalization methods.
b9dc7f44768dcb18c4a3ad8dafa727defbb280ba.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that regularizes the training of a target model by maximizing the mutual information (MI) between its feature representations and those of a large pre-trained model, which serves as an approximation to an unattainable oracle model. The method, termed Mutual Information Regularization with Oracle (MIRO), formulates the objective as a combination of the standard empirical risk minimization (ERM) loss and a mutual information regularization term. The MI term is made tractable by deriving a variational lower bound, where the variational distribution is modeled as a Gaussian with learned mean and diagonal covariance encoders. Multi-scale features from intermediate and final layers of both the target and pre-trained models are used for regularization, with simple architectures for the encoders to control computational cost. The final loss is optimized via stochastic gradient descent, and the approach is compatible with various backbone architectures and can be combined with parameter space ensemble methods.
b9dc7f44768dcb18c4a3ad8dafa727defbb280ba.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on five standard domain generalization benchmarks: PACS, VLCS, OfficeHome, TerraIncognita, and DomainNet, following the DomainBed protocol with leave-one-out cross-validation and three random trials per setting. The primary backbone is ResNet-50 pre-trained on ImageNet, but larger pre-trained models such as CLIP (ViT, 400M image-text pairs) and SWAG (RegNetY-16GF, 3.6B Instagram images) are also evaluated. Baselines include ERM and a wide range of state-of-the-art DG methods (e.g., CORAL, IRM, Mixstyle, SWAD). Evaluation metrics are out-of-domain classification accuracy averaged across all target domains. Hyperparameters are tuned on source-domain validation splits, and implementation details (e.g., batch size, optimizer, regularization coefficient) are carefully specified. Additional experiments analyze the effect of pre-training scale and the combination with SWAD.
b9dc7f44768dcb18c4a3ad8dafa727defbb280ba.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new domain generalization framework that leverages mutual information regularization with a pre-trained model as an oracle approximation, rather than relying solely on domain-invariant feature learning. The method provides a tractable variational lower bound for MI-based regularization, is compatible with multi-scale feature regularization, and demonstrates that larger and more diverse pre-trained models further enhance domain generalization. The approach is plug-and-play with existing architectures and optimizers, and empirical results show consistent and significant improvements over state-of-the-art DG methods, especially when scaling up the pre-trained backbone.

b9e4ea7ff34a304cc0e7bfaa638eaa850391b676.title: Accelerating Reinforcement Learning with Value-Conditional State Entropy Exploration
b9e4ea7ff34a304cc0e7bfaa638eaa850391b676.research_question: How can exploration in reinforcement learning be improved to address the imbalance between high-value and low-value state distributions, particularly in supervised settings where task rewards are present?
b9e4ea7ff34a304cc0e7bfaa638eaa850391b676.hypothesis: Maximizing value-conditional state entropy, by conditioning exploration bonuses on state value estimates, will lead to more effective and balanced exploration, thereby accelerating reinforcement learning across a variety of tasks compared to standard state entropy maximization.
b9e4ea7ff34a304cc0e7bfaa638eaa850391b676.proposed_method: A novel exploration technique is proposed that maximizes value-conditional state entropy (VCSE). The method partitions the state space according to value estimates and computes the entropy of visited states within each value partition. The Kraskov-Stögbauer-Grassberger (KSG) estimator is used to estimate conditional entropy, and an intrinsic reward proportional to the value-conditional state entropy is defined. During training, only states with similar value estimates are considered when computing the intrinsic bonus, preventing low-value state distributions from biasing exploration in high-value regions and vice versa. The agent is trained to maximize the sum of extrinsic (task) reward and the VCSE-based intrinsic reward, with value normalization applied to ensure consistency throughout training.
b9e4ea7ff34a304cc0e7bfaa638eaa850391b676.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a diverse set of benchmarks, including MiniGrid (navigation tasks with sparse rewards and partial observability), DeepMind Control Suite (pixel-based locomotion tasks), and Meta-World (pixel-based manipulation tasks). The approach is integrated into state-of-the-art RL algorithms such as Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C) and DrQv2. Baselines include standard state entropy (SE) exploration and reward-conditional state entropy (RCSE), with careful control of intrinsic reward scaling (beta) and ablation studies on value conditioning and batch size. Evaluation metrics include success rate and episode return, with results averaged over multiple runs and compared across baselines. Additional implementation details include the use of replay buffers, value normalization, and feature extraction via random encoders or intrinsic curiosity modules, depending on the environment.
b9e4ea7ff34a304cc0e7bfaa638eaa850391b676.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the concept of value-conditional state entropy for exploration in reinforcement learning, addressing the known issue of imbalanced exploration in supervised settings. By conditioning entropy estimation on value estimates, the method prevents low-value states from dominating the exploration process in high-value regions. The approach is claimed to be simple, intuitive, and stable, and is shown to consistently improve the sample-efficiency of RL algorithms across a wide range of challenging tasks and domains. The use of the KSG estimator for conditional entropy in this context and the integration with modern RL pipelines are also novel aspects.

ba1ce9f45b5a84d8c8609c1db23aebc887c0ae4d.title: Multi-step Problem Solving Through a Verifier: An Empirical Analysis on Model-induced Process Supervision
ba1ce9f45b5a84d8c8609c1db23aebc887c0ae4d.research_question: How can process supervision for multi-step problem solving be automated to improve the performance of verifier models on math and coding tasks, without relying on expensive human annotations?
ba1ce9f45b5a84d8c8609c1db23aebc887c0ae4d.hypothesis: Automatically constructed process supervision data, generated by sampling completions of intermediate solutions using a reasoning model, can effectively train process-supervised verifiers that outperform output-supervised verifiers and self-consistency baselines, and generalize across different reasoning models.
ba1ce9f45b5a84d8c8609c1db23aebc887c0ae4d.proposed_method: A novel data curation method, Model-induced Process Supervision (MiPS), is developed to automate the annotation of intermediate steps in multi-step problem solving tasks. For each intermediate solution (i.e., a prefix of steps), the reasoning model is used to generate multiple completions via Monte Carlo sampling, and the proportion of correct completions is computed as the correctness score for that step. These step-wise correctness scores are then used to train a process-supervised verifier (PSV) that predicts the likelihood of correctness at each step. The verifier is trained either to predict the exact correctness probabilities (soft objective) or a binarized version (hard objective). During inference, various aggregation functions (such as max, sum_logit, or mean_odd) are explored to combine the step-wise predictions into a final score for solution selection.
ba1ce9f45b5a84d8c8609c1db23aebc887c0ae4d.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on two math datasets (GSM8K and MATH) and one coding dataset (MBPP), using large language models such as PaLM 2-S and PaLM 2-L as both reasoners and verifiers. For each dataset, a fixed number of problems are used to generate verifier training data, with separate splits for fine-tuning, verification training, and testing. Baselines include output-supervised verifiers (OSV), process-supervised verifiers trained on human or algorithmic labels, and self-consistency. Evaluation metrics focus on accuracy of solution selection, with additional analysis on aggregation functions, the effect of step position, training objectives, and transferability of verifiers to solutions generated by different reasoning models (including gpt-turbo-3.5). The number of sampled completions and aggregation strategies are systematically varied to assess robustness and generalization.
ba1ce9f45b5a84d8c8609c1db23aebc887c0ae4d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces an automatic and scalable method (MiPS) for constructing process supervision data for verifier training, eliminating the need for costly human annotation. The empirical analysis demonstrates that verifiers trained on MiPS data outperform output-supervised verifiers and self-consistency on multiple datasets and tasks. The study provides new insights into the choice of aggregation functions for noisy, model-generated supervision, and shows that MiPS-trained verifiers generalize well across different reasoning models. The approach is also validated on both math and coding domains, extending the applicability of process supervision beyond previous work.

ba2b6a94d4fb018c9eab252a34d80787ae962f46.title: Differentially Private Optimization on Large Model at Small Cost
ba2b6a94d4fb018c9eab252a34d80787ae962f46.research_question: How can differentially private optimization for large neural network models be made as efficient in terms of time and memory as standard (non-private) training, without sacrificing accuracy or privacy guarantees?
ba2b6a94d4fb018c9eab252a34d80787ae962f46.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a novel implementation technique can enable differentially private (DP) optimization of large neural networks to achieve comparable computational efficiency (in both time and memory) to standard training, while maintaining state-of-the-art accuracy and strong privacy guarantees.
ba2b6a94d4fb018c9eab252a34d80787ae962f46.proposed_method: A new implementation framework, termed Book-Keeping (BK), will be developed to enable efficient differentially private optimization for large neural networks. The method will leverage three key algorithmic innovations: (1) the ghost norm trick, which computes per-sample gradient norms without instantiating full per-sample gradients, (2) a book-keeping strategy to reuse intermediate computations and avoid redundant back-propagation passes, and (3) ghost differentiation, which further reduces unnecessary gradient computations. The BK algorithm will be designed to require only a single back-propagation per mini-batch, avoid storing per-sample gradients, and minimize additional memory overhead. For high-dimensional data or large models, a hybrid approach will be introduced, making layer-wise decisions to combine the most efficient strategies for each layer. The implementation will be compatible with standard optimizers (e.g., SGD, Adam), parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques (e.g., LoRA, Adapters), and large-scale distributed training.
ba2b6a94d4fb018c9eab252a34d80787ae962f46.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of vision and language tasks using large-scale models, including GPT2-large (774M parameters), RoBERTa-large (355M), BEiT-large (304M), ResNet, and ViT architectures. Datasets will include E2E (text generation), GLUE (language understanding), and CIFAR10/100 and ImageNet (image classification). The proposed BK method will be compared against existing state-of-the-art DP implementations such as Opacus, GhostClip, and FastGradClip, as well as standard non-private training. Evaluation metrics will include training time (wall-clock and theoretical complexity), memory usage, and task-specific accuracy (e.g., BLEU for text, classification accuracy for images). Experiments will be run on modern hardware (e.g., A100 GPUs), and ablation studies will analyze the impact of model size, input dimension, and hybridization strategies.
ba2b6a94d4fb018c9eab252a34d80787ae962f46.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel, general-purpose implementation technique (Book-Keeping) that enables DP training of large neural networks with time and memory complexity nearly matching that of standard training. The method is the first to achieve state-of-the-art accuracy with less than 1% memory overhead and only 1.03× the time complexity of non-private training, significantly outperforming prior DP implementations. Additional innovations include a hybrid layer-wise strategy for high-dimensional data, compatibility with parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and an automatic, user-friendly codebase that can convert any standard training script into its DP counterpart with minimal code changes.

ba3e9e45f91257c9af6dfe74ed91a03c53086f07.title: Parallel Sampling of Diffusion Models
ba3e9e45f91257c9af6dfe74ed91a03c53086f07.research_question: Can the sampling process of diffusion models be accelerated by parallelizing the denoising steps, thereby reducing sample latency without sacrificing sample quality, and how does this approach compare to existing sequential and reduced-step sampling methods across diverse domains such as robotics and image generation?
ba3e9e45f91257c9af6dfe74ed91a03c53086f07.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that denoising steps in diffusion model sampling, traditionally performed sequentially, can be parallelized using iterative refinement (e.g., Picard iterations), enabling significant reductions in sampling latency without measurable degradation in sample quality, and that this approach is compatible with existing fast sampling techniques.
ba3e9e45f91257c9af6dfe74ed91a03c53086f07.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that leverages Picard iterations to parallelize the denoising steps of pretrained diffusion models. The method, termed ParaDiGMS, will iteratively guess and refine the entire denoising trajectory, updating all timesteps in parallel within a sliding window to fit within memory constraints. The approach will incorporate up-front noise sampling for SDE-based models and employ a convergence tolerance to ensure the resulting samples remain close in distribution to those from the original sequential process. The algorithm will be designed to be compatible with existing fast sampling techniques such as DDIM and DPM-Solver by swapping out the discretization method, and will include practical optimizations for GPU memory and compute efficiency.
ba3e9e45f91257c9af6dfe74ed91a03c53086f07.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of robotic control tasks (Robosuite Square, PushT, Franka Kitchen) using the DiffusionPolicy framework, as well as on high-dimensional image generation models (Stable Diffusion-v2, LSUN Church, and LSUN Bedroom). The evaluation will compare ParaDiGMS-augmented samplers (ParaDDPM, ParaDDIM, ParaDPMSolver) against their sequential counterparts in terms of sampling speed (wall-clock time), number of model evaluations, and sample quality metrics (task reward for robotics, FID and CLIP scores for images). Experiments will be run on single and multi-GPU setups, varying batch window sizes and convergence tolerances to assess trade-offs between compute, speed, and quality. Baselines will include standard DDPM, DDIM, and DPM-Solver samplers.
ba3e9e45f91257c9af6dfe74ed91a03c53086f07.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to enable parallelization of denoising steps in diffusion model sampling, introducing a new axis of trading compute for speed without sacrificing sample quality. ParaDiGMS is claimed to be fully compatible with existing fast sampling methods, allowing for combined improvements in both speed and quality. The approach provides consistent 2-4x speedups across a range of domains and models, and is expected to yield even greater gains as hardware parallelism improves. This work opens up new possibilities for real-time and interactive applications of diffusion models.

ba5a133fbdcd1cf0f5195da48515691683a8f774.title: PRDP: Progressively Refined Differentiable Physics
ba5a133fbdcd1cf0f5195da48515691683a8f774.research_question: How can the computational cost of training neural networks with differentiable physics solvers be significantly reduced without sacrificing model accuracy, particularly when these solvers are iterative and embedded within the training loop?
ba5a133fbdcd1cf0f5195da48515691683a8f774.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that full training accuracy of neural networks can be achieved using physics solvers at a significantly coarser level of refinement than full convergence, and that adaptively refining solver accuracy only as needed during training will yield substantial computational savings without loss of accuracy.
ba5a133fbdcd1cf0f5195da48515691683a8f774.proposed_method: A novel algorithm, Progressively Refined Differentiable Physics (PRDP), will be developed to adaptively control the refinement level of iterative physics solvers during neural network training. The method begins with a coarse physics solver (few iterations) and monitors a validation metric throughout training. If the validation metric plateaus, the algorithm incrementally increases the number of solver iterations, refining the physics only as necessary. This refinement is stopped once further increases do not yield validation improvements, thus identifying the minimal sufficient level of physics accuracy for training. The approach is designed to be agnostic to the choice of iterative linear solver and differentiation method (unrolled or implicit), and it maintains consistent refinement levels for both the primal and adjoint computations in the training loop.
ba5a133fbdcd1cf0f5195da48515691683a8f774.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of differentiable physics learning scenarios, including convex inverse problems (e.g., Poisson equation), autoregressive neural emulators for diffusion and Burgers equations, and neural-hybrid solvers for the Navier-Stokes equations. Both 1D, 2D, and 3D problems will be used, with datasets generated from discretized partial differential equations and reference solutions. Baselines will include training with fully converged physics solvers and manually scheduled refinement. Evaluation metrics will focus on normalized mean squared error (nMSE) on validation datasets, as well as total cumulative solver iterations and wall-clock training time. The effectiveness of PRDP will be assessed by comparing accuracy and computational savings (iteration and time reduction) against these baselines, with results aggregated over multiple random seeds.
ba5a133fbdcd1cf0f5195da48515691683a8f774.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces an adaptive, validation-driven refinement schedule for differentiable physics solvers within neural network training, enabling significant reductions in computational cost by combining savings from both progressive refinement and incomplete convergence. Unlike prior work, this method is broadly applicable to sparse iterative linear systems arising from PDE discretizations, supports both unrolled and implicit differentiation, and automatically determines the optimal refinement schedule and stopping criterion during training. The method is demonstrated to achieve up to 86% fewer cumulative solver iterations and up to 78% reduction in training time, while maintaining state-of-the-art accuracy across a variety of differentiable physics learning tasks.

ba8293be338f4bed4a6e44e7ce78510d74c1e048.title: Benchmarking Constraint Inference in Inverse Reinforcement Learning
ba8293be338f4bed4a6e44e7ce78510d74c1e048.research_question: How can the evaluation and benchmarking of constraint inference algorithms in inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) be systematically advanced, particularly in realistic domains such as robot control and autonomous driving, and how can the robustness and effectiveness of these algorithms be measured under various practical challenges?
ba8293be338f4bed4a6e44e7ce78510d74c1e048.hypothesis: Modeling the posterior distribution over constraints, rather than relying on point estimates, will improve the robustness and accuracy of constraint inference in inverse constrained reinforcement learning, particularly in high-dimensional and continuous environments.
ba8293be338f4bed4a6e44e7ce78510d74c1e048.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark will be developed for evaluating inverse constrained reinforcement learning (ICRL) algorithms across a diverse set of environments, including both virtual (robotic control via MuJoCo) and realistic (autonomous driving via the HighD dataset) domains. For each environment, relevant constraints will be designed and expert agents will be trained using constrained reinforcement learning methods (such as PPO-Lagrange and Policy Iteration Lagrange) to generate demonstration datasets that respect these constraints. In addition to standard baselines, a novel Variational Inverse Constrained Reinforcement Learning (VICRL) algorithm will be proposed, which models the posterior distribution over constraint functions using a Beta distribution parameterized by a neural network. VICRL will optimize an evidence lower bound (ELBo) objective, incorporating a KL-divergence regularizer to capture both the mean and variance of constraint uncertainty. The method will iteratively update both the policy and the constraint distribution until convergence, enabling robust constraint inference even in high-dimensional, continuous, and stochastic environments.
ba8293be338f4bed4a6e44e7ce78510d74c1e048.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of environments, including five MuJoCo-based robotic control tasks with added location constraints, and realistic highway driving scenarios constructed from the HighD dataset, with constraints on vehicle speed and inter-vehicle distance. Expert demonstration datasets will be generated using agents trained with ground-truth constraints. Baseline methods for comparison will include Binary Classifier Constraint Learning (BC2L), Generative Adversarial Constraint Learning (GACL), and Maximum Entropy Constraint Learning (MECL). Evaluation metrics will include constraint violation rate (the frequency of constraint breaches in trajectories) and feasible cumulative rewards (total rewards collected before any constraint violation). Additional experiments will examine robustness to noisy or violating demonstrations, stochastic environment dynamics (by injecting Gaussian noise), and the challenge of recovering multiple simultaneous constraints. All experiments will be repeated with multiple random seeds, and statistical significance will be assessed using appropriate tests.
ba8293be338f4bed4a6e44e7ce78510d74c1e048.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark provides the first systematic and diverse testbed for evaluating ICRL algorithms in both virtual and realistic domains, addressing the lack of standardized evaluation in the field. The VICRL algorithm introduces a Bayesian approach to constraint inference by modeling the full posterior distribution over constraints, enabling explicit handling of epistemic uncertainty and improved robustness compared to point-estimate methods. The benchmark and methodology facilitate the study of critical research questions, such as robustness to noisy demonstrations, performance under stochasticity, and the recovery of multiple constraints, which have not been systematically addressed in prior work.

ba8325ac0fea03fa171a0e46153e48bf797bd780.title: Fast Private Kernel Density Estimation via Locality Sensitive Quantization
ba8325ac0fea03fa171a0e46153e48bf797bd780.research_question: How can kernel density estimation (KDE) be performed efficiently and accurately under differential privacy constraints, especially for high-dimensional and large-scale datasets?
ba8325ac0fea03fa171a0e46153e48bf797bd780.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a general framework leveraging locality sensitive quantization (LSQ) can enable the construction of differentially private KDE mechanisms that are computationally efficient, scalable to high dimensions, and maintain strong privacy and utility guarantees.
ba8325ac0fea03fa171a0e46153e48bf797bd780.proposed_method: A novel framework called Locality Sensitive Quantization (LSQ) will be developed to construct private KDE mechanisms by 'privatizing' existing efficient non-private KDE approximation techniques in a black-box manner. The LSQ framework abstracts key properties such as quantization, bounded range, and sparsity, allowing the use of methods like Random Fourier Features (RFF), Fast Gauss Transform (FGT), and Locality Sensitive Hashing (LSH) within a differentially private context. The method involves representing the kernel as an expected inner product between sparse, bounded vectors, adding Laplace noise to a compact quantized summary of the dataset, and releasing a differentially private function that can be queried arbitrarily often. The mechanism is parameterized to balance computational efficiency, privacy, and accuracy, and is designed to scale linearly in the data dimension for high-dimensional settings.
ba8325ac0fea03fa171a0e46153e48bf797bd780.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on public benchmark datasets covering both high- and low-dimensional regimes, including Covertype (n=581,012, d=55), GloVe (n=1,000,000, d=100), Diabetes (n=101,766, d=2), and NYCTaxi (n=100,000, d=2). The proposed LSQ-based mechanisms will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as the Bernstein mechanism and a vanilla noisy sampling approach. Evaluation metrics will include KDE approximation error as a function of privacy parameter (epsilon), computational budget (e.g., number of features or expansion terms), and curator running time. Each experiment will use held-out random query points and results will be averaged over multiple queries and trials. Parameter selection will be analyzed to optimize the trade-off between privacy, accuracy, and computational cost.
ba8325ac0fea03fa171a0e46153e48bf797bd780.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to break the exponential dependence on data dimension in differentially private Gaussian KDE, achieving linear time in the dimension and making private KDE feasible for high-dimensional data. The LSQ framework generalizes and unifies several existing KDE approximation techniques, enabling their direct use in private settings. It also provides improved sample complexity and computational efficiency for low-dimensional data. The method supports a wider class of kernels than previous LSH-based approaches and is the first to provide nearly linear dependence on the error parameter in both sample complexity and running time for low-dimensional Gaussian KDE. Empirical results demonstrate significant improvements in speed and accuracy over prior private KDE methods.

ba98e89eb2afea1155c65d2ae26903d593c2fe22.title: Conformal prediction beyond exchangeability
ba98e89eb2afea1155c65d2ae26903d593c2fe22.research_question: How can conformal prediction methods be generalized to provide valid predictive inference when the assumptions of data exchangeability and algorithmic symmetry are violated, such as in the presence of distribution drift or when using nonsymmetric model fitting algorithms?
ba98e89eb2afea1155c65d2ae26903d593c2fe22.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by employing weighted quantiles and a new randomization technique, conformal prediction methods can maintain robust predictive coverage even when data are nonexchangeable and algorithms are nonsymmetric, with coverage guarantees that degrade gracefully as exchangeability is violated.
ba98e89eb2afea1155c65d2ae26903d593c2fe22.proposed_method: A new framework for conformal prediction will be developed that relaxes the traditional requirements of data exchangeability and symmetric model fitting. The method will introduce fixed, prespecified weights to each data point, reflecting their relevance or similarity to the test instance, and will use weighted quantiles for constructing prediction intervals. Additionally, a novel randomization technique will be designed to enable the use of nonsymmetric algorithms that may prioritize recent or spatially proximate observations. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to derive explicit upper bounds on the coverage gap as a function of the total variation distance between distributions of data points, weighted accordingly. The approach will be formulated for both split and full conformal prediction settings, and will be extensible to general nonconformity scores.
ba98e89eb2afea1155c65d2ae26903d593c2fe22.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both simulated and real-world datasets to evaluate the robustness and practical utility of the proposed nonexchangeable conformal prediction methods. Real-data experiments will include applications to electricity usage forecasting (e.g., the ELEC2 dataset) and election forecasting, where distribution drift and nonexchangeability are present. Baseline comparisons will be made against standard conformal prediction methods that assume exchangeability. Evaluation metrics will focus on empirical coverage rates (e.g., proportion of true values contained within prediction intervals) and interval width, with particular attention to coverage degradation under distribution drift. Experimental setups will include scenarios with varying degrees and types of nonexchangeability to assess the method's adaptability and robustness.
ba98e89eb2afea1155c65d2ae26903d593c2fe22.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a generalization of conformal prediction that accommodates both nonexchangeable data and nonsymmetric algorithms, a setting not addressed by prior methods. The use of fixed, prespecified weights and weighted quantiles enables robustness to distribution drift and other real-world violations of exchangeability, while theoretical results provide explicit, quantifiable bounds on coverage loss. The method retains exact coverage guarantees when data are exchangeable, and degrades gracefully otherwise. This approach is broadly applicable and can be extended to various nonconformity scores and predictive tasks.

baa188151055496872282379f193ba405052febb.title: Scaling Law with Learning Rate Annealing
baa188151055496872282379f193ba405052febb.research_question: How can the full validation loss curve of neural language models during training be accurately modeled and predicted, taking into account both data scaling and the effects of learning rate scheduling and annealing?
baa188151055496872282379f193ba405052febb.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the validation loss at any training step can be quantitatively described by a scaling law that incorporates both a power-law term over the area under the learning rate curve and an additional term accounting for the cumulative effects of learning rate annealing, enabling accurate prediction of loss dynamics across various learning rate schedules and model sizes.
baa188151055496872282379f193ba405052febb.proposed_method: A new scaling law framework will be developed to model the entire validation loss curve of language models during training. The proposed formulation expresses the loss at each training step as L(s) = L0 + A·S1^(-α) - C·S2, where S1 is the cumulative area under the learning rate curve (summed learning rate), and S2 is a novel annealing area term that captures the momentum and cumulative effect of learning rate reductions. The S2 term is defined recursively to account for the historical decay of learning rate changes, parameterized by a decay factor λ (typically between 0.99 and 0.999). The method requires fitting only a small number of training curves to estimate the parameters (L0, A, C, α), after which it can predict the full loss trajectory for arbitrary learning rate schedules, including unseen ones. The approach is further extended to include model size scaling by introducing an additional multiplicative factor N^γ to the annealing term, allowing the law to generalize across different model architectures and sizes.
baa188151055496872282379f193ba405052febb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using large language models with LLAMA-like architectures, trained from scratch on the Fineweb dataset and validated on RedPajama-CC. The main model will have 594M non-embedding parameters, with additional experiments on models up to 1.7B parameters and open-sourced models such as BLOOM-176B and OLMo-1B. The AdamW optimizer will be used with standard hyperparameters, and various learning rate schedules (constant, cosine, multi-step, WSDLRS, cyclic) will be evaluated. The proposed scaling law will be fitted to loss curves from a subset of training runs, and its predictive accuracy will be assessed on unseen schedules and model sizes. Evaluation metrics will include mean prediction error and R^2 coefficient of determination, with fitting performed via Huber loss minimization using the L-BFGS algorithm. Robustness will be tested across different batch sizes, decay factors, and architectural variants.
baa188151055496872282379f193ba405052febb.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a quantitative scaling law that models the entire loss curve, rather than just the final loss, by explicitly incorporating the effects of learning rate annealing through a novel momentum-based term. This formulation enables accurate prediction of loss dynamics across arbitrary learning rate schedules and model sizes using minimal computational resources, requiring only a small number of training runs for parameter fitting. The method generalizes traditional scaling laws, provides theoretical explanations for empirical phenomena observed in language model training, and offers practical guidance for optimizing learning rate schedules. The approach is claimed to significantly reduce the computational cost of scaling law formulation while increasing accuracy and expressiveness in modeling training dynamics.

baa4f95081e9663fb045d145acc70049ace16ac9.title: DPM-Solver++: Fast Solver for Guided Sampling of Diffusion Probabilistic Models
baa4f95081e9663fb045d145acc70049ace16ac9.research_question: How can the efficiency and stability of guided sampling in diffusion probabilistic models (DPMs) be improved, especially for high guidance scales and across both pixel-space and latent-space applications?
baa4f95081e9663fb045d145acc70049ace16ac9.hypothesis: A high-order ODE solver tailored to the data prediction parameterization, combined with thresholding methods and a multistep approach, will enable significantly faster and more stable guided sampling in DPMs, outperforming existing first- and high-order solvers in terms of sample quality and convergence speed, particularly at large guidance scales.
baa4f95081e9663fb045d145acc70049ace16ac9.proposed_method: A novel high-order ODE solver, DPM-Solver++, will be developed specifically for guided sampling in DPMs. The method will solve the diffusion ODE using the data prediction model parameterization, which predicts clean data from noisy observations, rather than the traditional noise prediction model. To address the instability observed in previous high-order solvers at large guidance scales, a multistep variant will be introduced, leveraging previous step information to reduce effective step size and improve convergence. Dynamic thresholding techniques will be incorporated to mitigate train-test mismatch by ensuring generated samples remain within the data bounds. The approach will be implemented for both single-step and multistep second-order solvers, with theoretical guarantees on convergence order.
baa4f95081e9663fb045d145acc70049ace16ac9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on high-resolution image synthesis tasks using pretrained DPMs on the ImageNet 256x256 dataset with classifier guidance, as well as on latent-space DPMs such as Stable Diffusion evaluated on the MS-COCO 2014 validation set. The proposed method will be compared to state-of-the-art fast samplers, including DDIM, DPM-Solver, DEIS, and PNDM, across a range of guidance scales (e.g., 2.0, 4.0, 7.5, 8.0) and varying numbers of function evaluations (NFE), from 10 to 250. Evaluation metrics will include FID (Fréchet Inception Distance) for sample quality and L2-norm error relative to high-step DDIM baselines for convergence analysis. Ablation studies will assess the impact of parameterization, solver order, step size schedule, and thresholding.
baa4f95081e9663fb045d145acc70049ace16ac9.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first high-order ODE solver for guided sampling in DPMs based on the data prediction model, rather than the noise prediction model, enabling the use of thresholding to address train-test mismatch. The multistep solver variant is specifically designed to mitigate instability at large guidance scales, a limitation of previous high-order solvers. The approach is training-free, generalizes DDIM to higher orders for the data prediction parameterization, and achieves state-of-the-art speed and sample quality for guided sampling, converging in as few as 15-20 steps across both pixel-space and latent-space DPMs.

bac09a590f8f13a65409d41184a550001130e31f.title: Fast Sparse Decision Tree Optimization via Reference Ensembles
bac09a590f8f13a65409d41184a550001130e31f.research_question: Can sparse decision trees be optimized efficiently to achieve predictive performance competitive with black-box machine learning models, while maintaining interpretability and practical runtimes, especially for datasets with continuous-valued features?
bac09a590f8f13a65409d41184a550001130e31f.hypothesis: Incorporating smart guessing strategies derived from reference black-box ensemble models into branch-and-bound-based optimal decision tree algorithms will significantly reduce computational time and memory requirements, while enabling the construction of sparse decision trees with predictive accuracy comparable to or better than the reference black-box models.
bac09a590f8f13a65409d41184a550001130e31f.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that augments any branch-and-bound-based optimal decision tree algorithm with three smart guessing strategies informed by a reference ensemble model (such as a gradient-boosted decision tree). First, thresholds for binarizing continuous features will be guessed by extracting only those split points used in the reference ensemble, drastically reducing the search space. Second, the maximum tree depth required for a sparse, accurate model will be estimated by relating the complexity of the reference ensemble to the VC-dimension and depth of a single tree, providing a principled upper bound for depth constraints. Third, tighter lower bounds for subproblems in the branch-and-bound search will be guessed by leveraging the reference model’s predictions on data subsets, allowing early pruning of suboptimal branches. These strategies will be integrated into existing solvers (such as GOSDT and DL8.5) with minimal modification, and theoretical guarantees will be established to bound the loss relative to the reference ensemble.
bac09a590f8f13a65409d41184a550001130e31f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on seven datasets, including real-world and simulated data: a 2D spiral pattern, the FICO credit risk dataset, three recidivism datasets (COMPAS, Broward, Netherlands), and two Amazon Mechanical Turk coupon datasets (Takeaway and Restaurant). The proposed method will be evaluated using cross-validation, with reference models trained as gradient-boosted decision trees (GBDT) with dataset-specific hyperparameters. Baselines will include state-of-the-art optimal decision tree solvers (GOSDT, DL8.5) without guessing, CART, and born-again tree ensembles. Evaluation metrics will include training and test accuracy, tree sparsity (number of leaves), and computational runtime. Experiments will assess the impact of each guessing strategy individually and in combination, with additional analysis of robustness to incorrect guesses and qualitative comparison of resulting tree structures.
bac09a590f8f13a65409d41184a550001130e31f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a general-purpose, reference-model-informed guessing framework that can be applied to any branch-and-bound-based optimal decision tree algorithm, enabling orders-of-magnitude speedup in training while preserving or improving predictive accuracy and sparsity. The method provides theoretical guarantees on the closeness of the resulting tree's performance to that of the reference ensemble, and uniquely leverages ensemble-derived knowledge to guide threshold selection, depth constraints, and lower bound estimation. This approach allows for practical, interpretable, and near-optimal decision tree construction on datasets previously intractable for existing optimal solvers.

bacdf9671fb872287201b53d768df89b4d6630a3.title: SWIFT: On-the-Fly Self-Speculative Decoding for LLM Inference Acceleration
bacdf9671fb872287201b53d768df89b4d6630a3.research_question: How can large language model (LLM) inference be accelerated in a plug-and-play manner without requiring auxiliary models or additional training, while maintaining the original output distribution and adapting efficiently to diverse and dynamic input data streams?
bacdf9671fb872287201b53d768df89b4d6630a3.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging inherent layer sparsity within LLMs, through adaptive on-the-fly layer skipping during inference, can enable lossless acceleration of LLM inference across a variety of tasks and input domains, without the need for additional training or auxiliary models.
bacdf9671fb872287201b53d768df89b4d6630a3.proposed_method: A novel self-speculative decoding framework, SWIFT, is developed to accelerate LLM inference by dynamically skipping intermediate layers of the target LLM during the drafting phase. The approach consists of two main phases: (1) context-based layer set optimization, where an adaptive mechanism uses LLM-generated context to efficiently identify the optimal set of layers to skip for the current input stream, and (2) confidence-aware inference acceleration, which utilizes the optimized layer configuration to maximize draft token acceptance and verification efficiency. The optimization phase alternates between random search and interval Bayesian optimization to propose candidate layer sets, using matchness scores (exact match ratios between draft and true tokens) as the objective. During inference, early-stopping drafting and dynamic verification strategies are applied based on confidence scores, ensuring efficient and accurate speculative decoding. The method is fully plug-and-play, requiring no additional training or model modifications, and is designed to adapt to task-specific and input-specific sparsity patterns in real time.
bacdf9671fb872287201b53d768df89b4d6630a3.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on LLaMA-2 and CodeLLaMA models across multiple tasks, including summarization (CNN/DailyMail), mathematical reasoning (GSM8K), storytelling (TinyStories), translation (WMT16 DE-EN), instruction following (Alpaca), question answering (NatureQuestions), and code generation (HumanEval). The evaluation includes both greedy and sampling-based decoding, with metrics such as mean generated length, token acceptance rate, wall-clock decoding speed (tokens/s), and speedup ratios relative to vanilla autoregressive decoding. Baselines include prior plug-and-play speculative decoding methods such as Parallel Decoding and Lookahead Decoding, which use Jacobi-based drafting. The experimental setup involves 1-shot or 5-shot evaluation, random sampling of test instances, and systematic measurement of both efficiency and output distribution preservation. Additional analyses examine latency breakdown, adaptation to dynamic input streams, optimization overhead, and scalability across model sizes and backbones (including Yi-34B and DeepSeek-Coder-33B).
bacdf9671fb872287201b53d768df89b4d6630a3.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first plug-and-play self-speculative decoding algorithm that adaptively optimizes layer skipping on-the-fly, enabling lossless LLM acceleration without auxiliary models or additional training. Key innovations include a context-based layer set optimization mechanism leveraging LLM-generated context for real-time adaptation, and confidence-aware inference strategies for efficient speculative drafting and verification. The approach demonstrates consistent 1.3× to 1.6× speedups across diverse models and tasks, maintains high token acceptance rates, and preserves the original output distribution. The method is shown to be robust to domain shifts and dynamic input streams, and is compatible with various LLM backbones, highlighting its generalizability and practical applicability.

badf5d00486111d936b056e52f13c26c1bbbd573.title: DINO-WM: World Models on Pre-trained Visual Features enable Zero-shot Planning
badf5d00486111d936b056e52f13c26c1bbbd573.research_question: How can task-agnostic world models be trained from offline, pre-collected visual trajectories to enable zero-shot planning and generalization across diverse environments and tasks without relying on task-specific supervision, expert demonstrations, or reward modeling?
badf5d00486111d936b056e52f13c26c1bbbd573.hypothesis: World models trained on pre-trained visual patch features can achieve robust, task-agnostic predictive modeling of environment dynamics, enabling effective zero-shot planning and generalization to novel tasks and configurations without the need for explicit reward signals or expert demonstrations.
badf5d00486111d936b056e52f13c26c1bbbd573.proposed_method: A novel world modeling framework will be developed that operates entirely in the latent space of pre-trained visual patch embeddings, specifically leveraging DINOv2 Vision Transformer (ViT) features. The method will encode each observation into a set of patch embeddings using a frozen DINOv2 encoder, and model environment dynamics via a decoder-only ViT-based transition model that predicts future latent states conditioned on a history of past latents and actions. The transition model will incorporate causal attention and will concatenate action and proprioceptive information to each patch vector, allowing for autoregressive prediction at the frame level. Training will be conducted using a latent consistency loss between predicted and actual future patch embeddings, with an optional independent decoder for interpretability. At test time, planning will be performed in latent space using model predictive control (MPC) with the cross-entropy method (CEM) to optimize action sequences that minimize the distance between predicted and goal latent states.
badf5d00486111d936b056e52f13c26c1bbbd573.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six diverse environment suites, including maze navigation, sliding and robotic arm manipulation, and deformable object manipulation, using RGB observations of size 224x224. The method will be evaluated using pre-collected offline datasets, with planning tasks defined as reaching visually specified goal states from arbitrary initial conditions. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art world models such as IRIS, DreamerV3, TD-MPC2, and generative video models like AVDC, as well as ablations with different pre-trained encoders (R3M, ResNet, DINOCLS). Evaluation metrics will include planning success rate, Chamfer Distance for deformable environments, and perceptual similarity (LPIPS) for predicted visual reconstructions. Additional experiments will test generalization to unseen environment configurations and analyze the impact of encoder choice and data scale.
badf5d00486111d936b056e52f13c26c1bbbd573.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a task-agnostic world modeling framework that operates directly on pre-trained visual patch embeddings, eliminating the need for pixel-space reconstruction, reward modeling, or expert demonstrations. The method enables zero-shot planning through latent space trajectory optimization and demonstrates superior generalization to novel tasks and environment configurations. Key innovations include the use of frozen DINOv2 patch features for observation encoding, a ViT-based transition model with causal attention for latent dynamics, and planning entirely in latent space, resulting in improved computational efficiency and interpretability. The approach achieves state-of-the-art performance across a range of challenging control and manipulation tasks, outperforming prior world models and generative video baselines.

bb0b86bad44dac2b7c049855771c0eb61578983a.title: Robust Multimodal Large Language Models Against Modality Conflict
bb0b86bad44dac2b7c049855771c0eb61578983a.research_question: How can multimodal large language models (MLLMs) be made more robust against hallucinations arising from conflicts between information in different input modalities, such as vision and language, in real-world scenarios?
bb0b86bad44dac2b7c049855771c0eb61578983a.hypothesis: Hallucinations in MLLMs can be significantly reduced by explicitly addressing modality conflict through targeted dataset construction and the application of prompt engineering, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning methods.
bb0b86bad44dac2b7c049855771c0eb61578983a.proposed_method: A formal definition of modality conflict will be established, encompassing object, attribute, and relationship inconsistencies between visual and textual inputs. A new dataset, Multimodal Modality Conflict (MMMC), will be constructed by systematically introducing conflicts into vision-language tasks using a substitution framework, large language models for component detection and substitution, and human verification for quality control. Three mitigation strategies will be developed: (1) prompt engineering, which augments model prompts to explicitly instruct the model to check for the presence of queried information; (2) supervised fine-tuning, where MLLMs are trained on the MMMC dataset to align predictions with conflict-aware ground-truth answers; and (3) reinforcement learning, where models are optimized via a reward function that encourages semantically consistent, non-hallucinated responses, using a reward model to judge answer consistency. Each method will be implemented with detailed technical steps, including the use of LoRA for efficient parameter updates and advanced RL algorithms such as REINFORCE++.
bb0b86bad44dac2b7c049855771c0eb61578983a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the MMMC dataset, which contains 20,000 image-question-answer triples simulating object, attribute, and relationship conflicts, split into training and testing sets. Multiple state-of-the-art MLLMs (e.g., InstructBLIP, LLaVA-v1.5, LLaVA-NeXT, Qwen2-VL-Instruct, and GPT-4o) will be evaluated as baselines. Evaluation metrics will include hallucination rate (Hallu-Rate), ROUGE-L for response overlap, and LLM-as-a-Judge scores for overall response quality, with both closed-source (GPT-4o) and open-source (Llama-3.3-70B) models used as judges. The impact of each mitigation method will be compared, and additional analyses will be performed on alignment tax (performance loss on standard benchmarks) and training stability. Training details such as optimizer settings, batch sizes, and number of epochs/episodes will be systematically varied and reported.
bb0b86bad44dac2b7c049855771c0eb61578983a.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first formalization of modality conflict in MLLMs at the levels of objects, attributes, and relationships, and constructs a dedicated benchmark dataset (MMMC) specifically for this phenomenon. It systematically investigates and compares three mitigation strategies—prompt engineering, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning—providing a comprehensive analysis of their effectiveness. The approach provides new insights into the robustness of MLLMs and highlights previously overlooked sources of hallucination, offering practical methods and evaluation protocols for future research in robust multimodal AI.

bb27bf8856d0edaaa7554d0bf2751071f6556a97.title: I Think, Therefore I Diffuse: Enabling Multimodal In-Context Reasoning in Diffusion Models
bb27bf8856d0edaaa7554d0bf2751071f6556a97.research_question: How can diffusion models be enabled to perform advanced multimodal in-context reasoning, such as interpreting interleaved image and text prompts and generating logically coherent outputs, without relying on complex reasoning-based datasets or extensive retraining?
bb27bf8856d0edaaa7554d0bf2751071f6556a97.hypothesis: Aligning vision-language models (VLMs) with diffusion decoders via a shared feature space, using vision-language training as a proxy task, will effectively transfer multimodal reasoning capabilities to diffusion models, enabling them to perform in-context reasoning and composition tasks with high accuracy and efficiency.
bb27bf8856d0edaaa7554d0bf2751071f6556a97.proposed_method: A novel alignment paradigm, ThinkDiff, will be developed to transfer multimodal in-context reasoning capabilities from VLMs to text-to-image diffusion models. The method introduces a lightweight aligner network that maps VLM output features into the shared input feature space of both a large language model (LLM) decoder and a diffusion decoder. Vision-language training will be used as a proxy task, aligning the VLM with the LLM decoder using cross-entropy loss on image-caption datasets. Two variants will be implemented: ThinkDiff-LVLM, which uses a large vision-language model and random masked training to avoid shortcut mappings, and ThinkDiff-CLIP, which leverages a CLIP vision encoder for semantic image understanding. During inference, the LLM decoder is replaced by the diffusion decoder, enabling the model to generate images based on interleaved multimodal context.
bb27bf8856d0edaaa7554d0bf2751071f6556a97.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate the proposed method on the CoBSAT benchmark, which tests multimodal in-context reasoning across ten tasks with 2-shot and 4-shot settings. ThinkDiff-LVLM will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as SEED-LLaMA, Emu, and GILL, using prediction accuracy as the primary metric. ThinkDiff-CLIP will be assessed on its ability to compose images and texts using prompts and datasets from DreamBooth, IP-Adapter, and other public sources. Ablation studies will examine the impact of the aligner network design, random masked training, and the use of generated versus input tokens. Training efficiency will be measured in terms of GPU usage and time, and qualitative results will be provided to demonstrate logical coherence and compositional ability.
bb27bf8856d0edaaa7554d0bf2751071f6556a97.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new alignment paradigm that enables diffusion models to inherit advanced multimodal reasoning capabilities from VLMs without requiring complex reasoning-based datasets or extensive retraining. The use of vision-language training as a proxy task for feature alignment is novel and allows efficient and robust transfer of reasoning abilities. The approach is lightweight, requiring only a small aligner network and minimal training resources, and demonstrates substantial improvements in reasoning accuracy and compositionality over existing methods. Additionally, the method is broadly applicable to various diffusion decoders and modalities, including potential extensions to video generation.

bb2f00760ad3eb2d8b82a2ededb5f709b80327b0.title: Machine learning in solar physics
bb2f00760ad3eb2d8b82a2ededb5f709b80327b0.research_question: How can advanced machine learning techniques be systematically applied to analyze large-scale solar physics data in order to improve understanding, prediction, and automation of solar phenomena and related hazardous events?
bb2f00760ad3eb2d8b82a2ededb5f709b80327b0.hypothesis: The application of modern machine learning methods, including supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning, will enable the extraction of previously inaccessible insights from high-dimensional solar physics datasets, leading to improved prediction, classification, and understanding of solar phenomena.
bb2f00760ad3eb2d8b82a2ededb5f709b80327b0.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed that leverages a range of machine learning algorithms—including deep neural networks (DNNs), convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), autoencoders, and clustering techniques—to process and analyze large-scale solar observational datasets. The methodology will include supervised learning for regression and classification tasks (e.g., flare prediction, image segmentation), unsupervised learning for dimensionality reduction and pattern discovery (e.g., principal component analysis, k-means, spectral clustering), and reinforcement learning for optimizing observational strategies and adaptive optics. Data partitioning strategies will be carefully designed to avoid overfitting and ensure generalization, and both encoder-decoder architectures and autoencoders will be explored for tasks such as data denoising and inversion. The framework will also incorporate explainable AI techniques for model interpretability and uncertainty quantification.
bb2f00760ad3eb2d8b82a2ededb5f709b80327b0.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize large, curated solar datasets such as those from the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO), Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope (DKIST), and European Solar Telescope (EST), encompassing terabyte- to petabyte-scale image and spectropolarimetric data. Baseline comparisons will be made against traditional physics-based inversion methods and simpler machine learning models. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, mean squared error, area under the ROC curve (AUC), and skill scores relevant to flare prediction and classification tasks. Data will be partitioned into training, validation, and test sets with careful consideration of temporal and spatial correlations to ensure robust assessment of model performance. Experiments will also investigate the impact of data augmentation, regularization, and hardware acceleration on scalability and efficiency.
bb2f00760ad3eb2d8b82a2ededb5f709b80327b0.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified, systematic application of state-of-the-art machine learning techniques to the domain of solar physics, addressing the challenges posed by high-dimensional, large-scale observational data. Novel contributions include the integration of deep learning architectures with physical models for improved inversion and prediction, the use of unsupervised methods for automated dimensionality reduction and feature extraction, and the exploration of reinforcement learning for observational planning. The framework aims to automate and accelerate data analysis, enhance predictive capabilities for hazardous solar events, and provide interpretable models that bridge data-driven and physics-based approaches.

bb47823ccdaca2c69f6a3fa77b6072b829ba001b.title: InternVideo2: Scaling Foundation Models for Multimodal Video Understanding
bb47823ccdaca2c69f6a3fa77b6072b829ba001b.research_question: How can large-scale, multimodal foundation models be developed to achieve robust, transferable video and video-text representations that generalize across a wide range of video understanding tasks, including long-form video reasoning, video-centric dialogue, and multimodal perception?
bb47823ccdaca2c69f6a3fa77b6072b829ba001b.hypothesis: A progressively trained, large-scale video foundation model that unifies masked video modeling, crossmodal contrastive learning, and next-token prediction, combined with high-quality, temporally consistent multimodal data, will yield state-of-the-art performance across diverse video, audio, and video-language tasks, including long-context and reasoning scenarios.
bb47823ccdaca2c69f6a3fa77b6072b829ba001b.proposed_method: A new family of video foundation models will be developed using a three-stage progressive training scheme. In the first stage, a Vision Transformer-based video encoder will be trained to reconstruct unmasked video tokens, guided by expert models (InternViT and VideoMAE) via projection layers and token-level mean squared error alignment. The second stage will introduce crossmodal contrastive and matching objectives, aligning video, audio, speech, and text representations using lightweight encoders for audio (BEATs) and text (BERT-Large), with multimodal caption fusion and masked language modeling. The third stage will connect the video encoder to a large language model (LLM) using a QFormer design, enabling next-token prediction and instruction tuning for open-ended video-centric dialogue. High-definition post-training will further enhance fine-grained and long-context spatiotemporal capabilities. The entire training pipeline will leverage a large, curated multimodal dataset with temporally segmented clips and fused video-audio-speech captions.
