bb47823ccdaca2c69f6a3fa77b6072b829ba001b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across more than 70 video, audio, and video-language tasks, including action recognition (Kinetics-400/600/700, Something-Something V2, Moments in Time, UCF101, HMDB51, Charades, ActivityNet, HACS), temporal action localization (THUMOS14, ActivityNet, HACS Segment, FineAction), video instance segmentation (YouTube-VIS2019), video retrieval (MSR-VTT, LSMDC, DiDeMo, MSVD, ActivityNet, VATEX), video temporal grounding (QVHighlight, Charade-STA), and audio-related tasks (AudioCaps, ClothoV1/V2, ClothoAQA, AMAVQA, ESC-50). Baselines will include state-of-the-art models such as CLIP, VideoMAE, VideoPrism, UMT, and others. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy, mean Average Precision (mAP), Recall@K, and task-specific measures (e.g., mIoU for segmentation, HiT@1 for highlight detection). Both zero-shot and finetuning settings will be explored, and ablations will assess the impact of model scaling, multimodal data, and training stages.
bb47823ccdaca2c69f6a3fa77b6072b829ba001b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified, scalable progressive training framework that integrates masked video modeling, crossmodal contrastive learning, and next-token prediction for multimodal video understanding. The method leverages a newly curated, large-scale multimodal dataset with temporally consistent segmentation and fused video-audio-speech captions, enhancing semantic alignment and generalization. The model architecture scales up to 6B parameters and incorporates efficient training strategies (e.g., DeepSpeed, FlashAttention). The resulting models demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across a broad spectrum of video, audio, and video-language benchmarks, particularly excelling in long-form video reasoning and open-ended video-centric dialogue.

bb857c72e7c75fc3d4b44b1dcaa66c62ea10a2e1.title: Analyzing and Improving the Training Dynamics of Diffusion Models
bb857c72e7c75fc3d4b44b1dcaa66c62ea10a2e1.research_question: How can the training dynamics of diffusion models for image synthesis be better understood and improved to achieve more stable, efficient, and high-quality generative performance without increasing computational complexity?
bb857c72e7c75fc3d4b44b1dcaa66c62ea10a2e1.hypothesis: Systematically standardizing the magnitudes of activations, weights, and updates throughout the diffusion model architecture and training process will eliminate imbalances and drifts, resulting in more effective training and improved image synthesis quality at equal or lower computational cost. Additionally, enabling post-hoc adjustment of exponential moving average (EMA) parameters will provide new opportunities for optimizing and analyzing model performance.
bb857c72e7c75fc3d4b44b1dcaa66c62ea10a2e1.proposed_method: A comprehensive redesign of the diffusion model training procedure is proposed, focusing on the ADM U-Net architecture. The method involves a sequence of modifications: (1) standardizing activation magnitudes by dividing layer outputs by their expected scaling, using a weight normalization approach without learned output scales; (2) explicitly normalizing weights to unit variance before each training step to control effective learning rates and prevent weight drift; (3) removing data-dependent group normalization layers and replacing them with lighter pixel normalization where beneficial; (4) ensuring all fixed-function and nonlinear layers (e.g., Fourier features, SiLU activations) are magnitude-preserving by analytically scaling their outputs; (5) introducing learned gain parameters at critical points to allow the network to adapt output variance as needed. Additionally, a novel post-hoc EMA method is developed, allowing arbitrary EMA profiles to be synthesized after training by storing multiple averaged parameter vectors and reconstructing desired averages via least-squares fitting.
bb857c72e7c75fc3d4b44b1dcaa66c62ea10a2e1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ImageNet-512 dataset, using class-conditional latent diffusion with a pre-trained decoder for 8x upsampling. The evaluation will focus on Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) as the primary metric, comparing results with and without classifier-free guidance. Several model sizes (XS to XXL) will be tested to assess scalability, and results will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as ADM, DiT, VDM++, RIN, and StyleGAN-XL. Deterministic sampling with 63 steps will be used for efficiency, and the impact of each architectural and training modification will be measured incrementally. Additional experiments will analyze the effect of EMA length, both globally and per-tensor, and explore the interactions between EMA, guidance strength, model size, and training time. The method will also be validated on ImageNet-64 in RGB space to demonstrate generality.
bb857c72e7c75fc3d4b44b1dcaa66c62ea10a2e1.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified, magnitude-preserving redesign of the diffusion model architecture and training procedure, eliminating uncontrolled drifts in activations, weights, and updates. It claims significant improvements in image synthesis quality (FID) at fixed or reduced computational cost, surpassing previous state-of-the-art results. The post-hoc EMA method is presented as a novel tool for efficient, flexible model averaging and analysis, enabling new types of studies and optimizations that were previously computationally infeasible. The overall approach simplifies the architecture, reduces reliance on normalization layers, and provides principled control over training dynamics, potentially benefiting a wide range of diffusion-based generative models.

bb927c2cacf7e19a762ca0135f7dce60a4d236cc.title: Understanding Nonlinear Implicit Bias via Region Counts in Input Space
bb927c2cacf7e19a762ca0135f7dce60a4d236cc.research_question: How can the implicit bias that governs generalization in nonlinear, overparameterized neural networks be characterized using geometric properties of the input space, and what factors influence this bias?
bb927c2cacf7e19a762ca0135f7dce60a4d236cc.hypothesis: Implicit bias in nonlinear neural networks can be effectively characterized by the count of connected decision regions in the input space, and training with larger learning rates or smaller batch sizes induces solutions with fewer regions, leading to better generalization.
bb927c2cacf7e19a762ca0135f7dce60a4d236cc.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed to quantify implicit bias in neural networks by measuring the number of connected regions in the input space where the network predicts the same label, referred to as the region count. This metric will be computed by projecting the input space onto low-dimensional subspaces (e.g., 1D to 5D) spanned by randomly selected training points, and then counting the maximally connected regions within these subspaces using the trained network's predictions. The approach is invariant to network parameterization and reflects the geometric complexity of the classifier. Theoretical analysis will be conducted, particularly for two-layer ReLU networks, to establish connections between region count and training hyperparameters such as learning rate and batch size, and to prove that larger learning rates induce fewer regions. Empirical procedures will be designed to estimate region counts efficiently, and the method will be extended to a variety of architectures and datasets.
bb927c2cacf7e19a762ca0135f7dce60a4d236cc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification datasets such as CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet, using a range of neural network architectures including ResNet18, ResNet34, VGG19, MobileNetV2, ShuffleNetV2, EfficientNetB0, RegNetX 200MF, SENet18, and SimpleDLA. The impact of training hyperparameters (learning rate, batch size, weight decay) and data augmentation techniques (mixup, random crop, random flip) on region count and generalization gap will be systematically evaluated. Region counts will be estimated by sampling low-dimensional subspaces and computing the number of connected decision regions. Baseline metrics such as norm-based and margin-based measures will be compared to region count in terms of their correlation with generalization gap. Evaluation metrics will include the correlation coefficient between region count and generalization gap, as well as test accuracy. Ablation studies will be performed to assess robustness across architectures, datasets, optimizers, and subspace dimensions.
bb927c2cacf7e19a762ca0135f7dce60a4d236cc.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel, parameterization-invariant metric—region count—for characterizing implicit bias in nonlinear neural networks, extending previous work limited to linear models or low-dimensional subspaces. The approach provides a comprehensive geometric perspective on generalization, supported by both empirical and theoretical analysis. It systematically demonstrates that region count correlates strongly with generalization gap across a wide range of architectures, datasets, and training regimes, and establishes, for the first time, a theoretical link between training hyperparameters and region count in nonlinear settings. The method also offers practical tools for diagnosing and potentially improving generalization in deep learning models.

bb9864391fb1c69f8b3240205a8a8ac65b2b6d07.title: Methods of improving LLM training stability
bb9864391fb1c69f8b3240205a8a8ac65b2b6d07.research_question: How can the training stability of large language models (LLMs) be improved, particularly under high learning rates, by controlling the magnitude of outputs in transformer linear layers?
bb9864391fb1c69f8b3240205a8a8ac65b2b6d07.hypothesis: Applying targeted normalization and softmax control techniques to specific linear layers in the transformer block will improve training stability and allow for higher learning rates without model divergence, while also improving model perplexity.
bb9864391fb1c69f8b3240205a8a8ac65b2b6d07.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves a systematic investigation and development of normalization and softmax control strategies for transformer-based LLMs. Several approaches will be implemented and compared: (1) applying layer normalization not only after QK layers but also after Proj and FC2 layers (QK FC norm); (2) applying layer normalization after the QKV layer and removing pre-normalization (QKV norm); (3) combining QK layer normalization with softmax capping (QK norm cap); and (4) evaluating baseline methods such as σReparam, softmax temperature adjustment, softmax capping, softmax clipping, and LayerScale. Each method will be integrated into a transformer model architecture, with careful placement of normalization layers and softmax modifications as described. The technical implementation will use bfloat16 for linear layer computations, float32 for optimizer weights, and rotary positional embeddings. Regularization will be applied via weight decay, and no dropout will be used.
bb9864391fb1c69f8b3240205a8a8ac65b2b6d07.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a small LLM with 830M parameters, 24 transformer blocks, and a hidden size of 1024, trained on a diverse dataset comprising 1T tokens from 53 human languages and 37 programming languages. The model will be trained using the Adam optimizer with specified β1 and β2 parameters, gradient clipping, and a learning rate schedule (linear warmup followed by cosine decay). Multiple learning rates (6e-3, 8e-3, 20e-3, 40e-3, 60e-3, 80e-3) will be tested to assess model convergence and divergence. Baseline methods and proposed normalization/softmax strategies will be compared. Evaluation metrics will include model convergence (based on validation loss) and perplexity, with experiments run on 32 H100 GPUs. Additional experiments will train selected models on 0.2T tokens with a standard learning rate (3e-4) to assess final perplexity improvements.
bb9864391fb1c69f8b3240205a8a8ac65b2b6d07.novelty_claims: The proposal extends prior work by analyzing not only the magnitude of attention logits but also all outputs of linear layers within the transformer block, identifying QKV, Proj, and FC2 as critical points for magnitude growth leading to instability. Novel contributions include the application of layer normalization after QKV (without pre-normalization), the combination of QK layer normalization with softmax capping, and a comprehensive comparison of multiple normalization and softmax control strategies. The proposed methods are claimed to allow a 1.5x increase in learning rate without model divergence compared to previous approaches, and to yield significant improvements in perplexity over baseline models.

bb9a44c94a89dbe00f0061d05c70a45064ff6ea6.title: CMMLU: Measuring massive multitask language understanding in Chinese
bb9a44c94a89dbe00f0061d05c70a45064ff6ea6.research_question: How can the knowledge and reasoning abilities of large language models (LLMs) be comprehensively evaluated in the context of Mandarin Chinese, across a wide range of subjects and task types, including both general and China-specific knowledge domains?
bb9a44c94a89dbe00f0061d05c70a45064ff6ea6.hypothesis: A benchmark specifically designed for Mandarin Chinese, covering diverse subjects and including region- and culture-specific content, will reveal significant gaps in current LLM performance and provide actionable insights for improving Chinese language understanding in LLMs.
bb9a44c94a89dbe00f0061d05c70a45064ff6ea6.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark suite, CMMLU, will be developed to evaluate LLMs on massive multitask language understanding in Mandarin Chinese. The benchmark will consist of 11,528 manually curated multiple-choice questions spanning 67 subjects, including STEM, humanities, social sciences, and China-specific topics. Each question will have four answer choices, with only one correct answer, and will be formatted to include both fill-in-the-blank and direct-answer types, with mathematical and chemical expressions presented in both LaTeX and plaintext as appropriate. Data collection will involve expert annotators sourcing questions from non-public materials, mock exams, and quiz shows to minimize overlap with LLM training data. Rigorous quality control will be implemented through random sampling and verification, and the dataset will be split into a few-shot development set and a test set for each subject.
bb9a44c94a89dbe00f0061d05c70a45064ff6ea6.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate over 20 contemporary multilingual and Chinese LLMs, including commercial models (e.g., GPT-4, ChatGPT) and open-source models (e.g., LLaMA, Baichuan, ChatGLM, Falcon, BLOOMZ). Evaluation will be conducted in both zero-shot and few-shot settings, using standardized prompts and two main answer extraction strategies: free generation (for commercial models) and next-token prediction (for open-source models). Performance will be measured by accuracy, with macro-averaging across subjects and breakdowns by subject type (STEM, humanities, social sciences, China-specific, other). Additional analyses will examine the impact of chain-of-thought prompting, the number of in-context examples, model size, negation in questions, and sub-option question formats. Baselines will include random choice accuracy, and detailed comparisons will be made between models and across subject categories.
bb9a44c94a89dbe00f0061d05c70a45064ff6ea6.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces the first large-scale, publicly available multitask evaluation suite specifically tailored for Mandarin Chinese, covering both general and region-specific knowledge areas not found in existing benchmarks. It addresses the limitations of English-centric and translation-based benchmarks by including questions that are culturally and linguistically unique to China. The methodology ensures minimal data leakage into LLM training sets and provides a robust framework for analyzing LLM weaknesses, such as handling negation and complex sub-option questions. The benchmark enables fair, reproducible, and comprehensive assessment of LLMs for Chinese language understanding and reasoning, and offers actionable insights for future model development.

bba58099a13b59f8272dc2c0129057670e252fa1.title: Neural Feature Fusion Fields: 3D Distillation of Self-Supervised 2D Image Representations
bba58099a13b59f8272dc2c0129057670e252fa1.research_question: How can dense 2D image feature extractors be extended to enable consistent, semantically meaningful 3D scene representations that support tasks such as object retrieval, segmentation, and editing, particularly in both static and dynamic real-world scenarios?
bba58099a13b59f8272dc2c0129057670e252fa1.hypothesis: Distilling features from self-supervised 2D image feature extractors into a 3D neural field via neural rendering will result in a 3D representation that is more consistent across viewpoints, more robust to occlusions, and more semantically meaningful than the original 2D features, thereby improving performance on downstream tasks such as object retrieval, segmentation, and scene editing.
bba58099a13b59f8272dc2c0129057670e252fa1.proposed_method: A novel framework, Neural Feature Fusion Fields (N3F), is proposed to distill features from a 2D image feature extractor (e.g., DINO, MoCo-v3, DeiT) into a 3D neural field using a student-teacher paradigm. The teacher network, pre-trained on large-scale datasets, provides dense 2D features for each image, while the student network learns a 3D feature field parameterized as a neural radiance field (NeRF) or its dynamic variants. Training is performed by minimizing a combined loss that includes both image reconstruction and feature reconstruction, using differentiable volumetric rendering to project 3D features into 2D image space for supervision. The approach is compatible with both static and dynamic neural rendering architectures, such as vanilla NeRF for static scenes and NeuralDiff for dynamic, egocentric video, by adding feature prediction heads to each component of the neural field. The resulting 3D feature field enables both 2D and 3D queries, supporting multi-view consistent feature extraction, object segmentation in 3D, and scene editing through manipulation of the learned 3D features.
bba58099a13b59f8272dc2c0129057670e252fa1.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the LLFF dataset (static scenes) and a subset of the EPIC-KITCHENS dataset (dynamic, egocentric videos). The method is implemented on top of NeRF for static scenes and NeuralDiff for dynamic scenes, with additional feature prediction heads for each neural field component. Pre-trained transformer-based feature extractors (DINO, MoCo-v3, DeiT) serve as teachers, and their features are distilled into the 3D student network. Evaluation is performed on multiple downstream tasks: 2D and 3D object retrieval, 3D segmentation, scene editing, and amodal segmentation. For quantitative evaluation, annotated object regions are used to measure mean average precision (mAP) for object retrieval across multiple scenes and queries. Baselines include the original 2D teacher features, and performance is compared to the N3F-distilled 3D features. Additional qualitative experiments demonstrate the ability to segment and edit objects in 3D, including through occlusions.
bba58099a13b59f8272dc2c0129057670e252fa1.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a general framework for distilling 2D image features into a 3D neural field, enabling multi-view consistent, semantically meaningful 3D scene representations without requiring manual 3D labels. Unlike prior work, this approach is applicable to both static and dynamic scenes, leverages self-supervised features for open-world applicability, and supports a broad range of downstream tasks including 3D object segmentation, scene editing, and amodal segmentation. The method demonstrates significant improvements over 2D feature baselines in both quantitative and qualitative evaluations, and enables capabilities (such as 3D segmentation and editing) not possible with 2D-only representations.

bbc57e1b3cf90e09b64377f13de455793bc81ad5.title: Mixture-of-Experts with Expert Choice Routing
bbc57e1b3cf90e09b64377f13de455793bc81ad5.research_question: How can routing strategies in sparsely-activated Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models be improved to enhance training efficiency, load balancing, and downstream task performance, while maintaining or reducing computational cost?
bbc57e1b3cf90e09b64377f13de455793bc81ad5.hypothesis: Allowing experts to select top-k tokens (expert choice routing) instead of tokens selecting top-k experts will result in better load balancing, improved training efficiency, and superior downstream performance compared to conventional token-choice routing in MoE models.
bbc57e1b3cf90e09b64377f13de455793bc81ad5.proposed_method: A heterogeneous Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model is developed, employing an expert choice routing strategy. In this approach, each expert independently selects the top-k tokens it will process, where k is determined by the batch size, number of experts, and a tunable capacity factor. The gating function computes token-to-expert affinity scores using a softmax over learned expert embeddings, and each expert selects its top-k tokens based on these scores. The selected tokens are routed to experts using permutation and gating matrices, and the outputs are aggregated back to the original token order. Additional constraints can be imposed to limit the maximum number of experts per token, formulated as an entropy-regularized linear programming problem. The method is implemented within a Transformer architecture, replacing the feed-forward component of every other layer with a MoE layer, and includes modifications such as per-layer relative positional bias and Gated Linear Units.
bbc57e1b3cf90e09b64377f13de455793bc81ad5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a high-quality dataset of 1.6 trillion tokens, representative of diverse natural language use cases. Models will be pre-trained with various numbers of experts (16 to 128) and expert sizes (100M to 8B parameters), with both MoE and dense baselines for comparison. The evaluation will focus on fine-tuning performance across 11 tasks from the GLUE and SuperGLUE benchmarks, using accuracy as the primary metric. Baselines will include Switch Transformer (top-1 gating), GShard (top-2 gating), and HashLayer routing methods. Training efficiency will be measured by convergence speed and perplexity, with experiments run on large-scale TPU clusters. Ablation studies will explore the effects of varying the capacity factor and capping the number of experts per token.
bbc57e1b3cf90e09b64377f13de455793bc81ad5.novelty_claims: The proposed expert choice routing method guarantees perfect load balancing by design, eliminates the need for auxiliary load balancing losses, and enables a variable number of experts per token based on learned importance. This approach allows for more flexible and efficient allocation of computational resources, leading to over 2x faster training convergence compared to state-of-the-art MoE routing methods, and consistent improvements in downstream task performance. The method also demonstrates strong scaling properties with increased numbers of experts and outperforms both dense models and alternative sparse routing strategies on large-scale natural language benchmarks.

bbc6531afdfe41fe8664002a80d9d73a07a080d2.title: GaussianEditor: Swift and Controllable 3D Editing with Gaussian Splatting
bbc6531afdfe41fe8664002a80d9d73a07a080d2.research_question: How can 3D scene editing be made more precise, controllable, and efficient, particularly for complex scenes, using explicit 3D representations while overcoming the limitations of existing mesh, point cloud, and implicit neural field-based methods?
bbc6531afdfe41fe8664002a80d9d73a07a080d2.hypothesis: Incorporating semantic tracing and hierarchical organization into Gaussian Splatting representations will enable faster, more precise, and more controllable 3D editing, outperforming both traditional and implicit approaches in terms of editability, fidelity, and speed.
bbc6531afdfe41fe8664002a80d9d73a07a080d2.proposed_method: A novel 3D editing framework will be developed based on Gaussian Splatting (GS), leveraging explicit point cloud-like representations for real-time rendering and direct manipulation. The method will introduce Gaussian semantic tracing, which dynamically assigns and tracks semantic labels to individual Gaussians throughout the training process, enabling precise targeting of edit regions as the scene evolves. Hierarchical Gaussian Splatting (HGS) will be implemented, organizing Gaussians into generations based on their densification stage and applying progressively stronger anchor constraints to older generations to stabilize geometry and prevent excessive fluidity under stochastic generative guidance. Specialized 3D inpainting algorithms will be designed for both object removal and addition, utilizing 2D inpainting diffusion models, image-to-3D conversion, and coordinate alignment to efficiently update the GS representation. The approach will support both text-based and explicit (e.g., bounding box) editing controls.
bbc6531afdfe41fe8664002a80d9d73a07a080d2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of complex 3D scenes, including large-scale environments and detailed facial regions, using datasets reconstructed via multi-view images and Structure-from-Motion (SFM). The method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as Instruct-Nerf2Nerf, Instruct-Pix2Pix, and other NeRF/GS-based editing techniques. Evaluation metrics will include qualitative visual comparisons, user studies, and quantitative measures such as CLIP Directional Similarity to assess edit fidelity and alignment with prompts. Editing speed (total runtime per session) and controllability (degree of unintended changes outside target regions) will also be measured. Ablation studies will be performed to isolate the contributions of semantic tracing and hierarchical constraints.
bbc6531afdfe41fe8664002a80d9d73a07a080d2.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces dynamic Gaussian semantic tracing for continuous, fine-grained control of editing regions, overcoming the limitations of static masks in evolving 3D scenes. Hierarchical Gaussian Splatting is developed to stabilize generative editing by regulating the flexibility of Gaussians based on their generation, enabling convergence to high-fidelity results under stochastic guidance. A dedicated 3D inpainting pipeline is designed for GS, enabling rapid object removal and addition with minimal artifacts. The method claims significant improvements in edit precision, speed (5-10 minutes per session), and controllability compared to prior 3D editing frameworks.

bbf218fd97d3c18801eb6eb09345bb38e7bcc871.title: Improving Dictionary Learning with Gated Sparse Autoencoders
bbf218fd97d3c18801eb6eb09345bb38e7bcc871.research_question: How can the quality of unsupervised dictionary learning for neural network activations be improved, particularly in terms of achieving sparser and more interpretable representations without sacrificing reconstruction fidelity?
bbf218fd97d3c18801eb6eb09345bb38e7bcc871.hypothesis: Separating the detection of active features from the estimation of their magnitudes within a sparse autoencoder, and applying the sparsity penalty only to the detection pathway, will reduce reconstruction biases such as shrinkage and yield sparser, equally or more interpretable decompositions at comparable or improved reconstruction fidelity.
bbf218fd97d3c18801eb6eb09345bb38e7bcc871.proposed_method: A novel Gated Sparse Autoencoder (Gated SAE) architecture will be developed, which replaces the standard single-layer ReLU encoder with a gated encoder consisting of two separate affine transformations: one for detecting which dictionary elements are active (the gating path), and another for estimating the magnitudes of these activations (the magnitude path). The L1 sparsity penalty will be applied exclusively to the gating path, minimizing its impact on magnitude estimation and thus reducing shrinkage bias. Weight sharing will be implemented between the gating and magnitude paths to control parameter growth, specifically by tying projection directions but allowing separate scaling and bias parameters. The loss function will include a reconstruction term, a sparsity term on the gating preactivations, and an auxiliary reconstruction term to ensure the gating path supports accurate reconstructions. Training will require two decoder passes per update to compute both the main and auxiliary reconstruction losses.
bbf218fd97d3c18801eb6eb09345bb38e7bcc871.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on activations from several language models, including GELU-1L, Pythia-2.8B, and Gemma-7B, across multiple sites such as MLP outputs, attention outputs, and residual streams. Gated SAEs will be compared against baseline SAEs, with compute matched by increasing the baseline's feature count by 50% to account for the additional training cost of Gated SAEs. Evaluation metrics will include the L0 norm (average number of active features) for sparsity, 'loss recovered' for reconstruction fidelity (measured by the change in language model cross-entropy loss when SAE reconstructions are spliced in), and a relative reconstruction bias metric to quantify shrinkage. Manual interpretability will be assessed via blinded human rater studies on randomly sampled features, using a standardized interface and statistical analysis to compare interpretability scores. Ablation studies will further dissect the contributions of architectural and training modifications.
bbf218fd97d3c18801eb6eb09345bb38e7bcc871.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new Gated SAE architecture that decouples feature detection from magnitude estimation, enabling targeted application of the sparsity penalty and thus mitigating shrinkage bias inherent in standard sparse autoencoders. This approach is claimed to achieve a Pareto improvement in the trade-off between sparsity and reconstruction fidelity, requiring fewer active features for comparable fidelity and producing features that are at least as interpretable as those from baseline methods. The method also provides a systematic framework for evaluating and improving the interpretability and faithfulness of learned dictionary features in neural network activations.

bc2ac51104e3a477938aa664e20527a7178fd418.title: Bench2Drive: Towards Multi-Ability Benchmarking of Closed-Loop End-To-End Autonomous Driving
bc2ac51104e3a477938aa664e20527a7178fd418.research_question: How can end-to-end autonomous driving (E2E-AD) systems be comprehensively, fairly, and realistically evaluated across multiple driving abilities in a closed-loop environment, overcoming the limitations of current open-loop and closed-loop benchmarks?
bc2ac51104e3a477938aa664e20527a7178fd418.hypothesis: A benchmark that provides a large-scale, diverse, and fully-annotated official training dataset, combined with a granular closed-loop evaluation protocol across a wide range of interactive driving scenarios, will enable more comprehensive, fair, and meaningful assessment of E2E-AD systems’ capabilities compared to existing benchmarks.
bc2ac51104e3a477938aa664e20527a7178fd418.proposed_method: A new benchmarking framework, Bench2Drive, will be developed to evaluate E2E-AD systems in a closed-loop simulation environment. The framework will include an official training dataset of 2 million fully-annotated frames collected from 13,638 short clips, covering 44 interactive driving scenarios, 23 weather conditions, and 12 towns within the CARLA simulator. Each scenario will be isolated in short routes (~150 meters), enabling granular skill assessment and minimizing the confounding effects of long, multi-scenario routes. The evaluation protocol will require models to complete 220 short routes, each focusing on a specific driving skill under varying conditions, and will employ a set of metrics including Success Rate, Driving Score, Efficiency, and Comfortness. The dataset will be collected using a world-model-based reinforcement learning expert agent, and will include comprehensive sensor data and annotations to ensure fair algorithm-level comparisons.
bc2ac51104e3a477938aa664e20527a7178fd418.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training and evaluating several state-of-the-art E2E-AD baseline models (such as UniAD, VAD, AD-MLP, TCP, ThinkTwice, and DriveAdapter) using the official Bench2Drive dataset. The base subset (1,000 clips) will be used for training, with 950 clips for training and 50 for open-loop validation, ensuring balanced scenario and weather representation. Closed-loop evaluation will be conducted in CARLA across the 220 test routes, with metrics including Success Rate, Driving Score, Efficiency, and Comfortness, as well as multi-ability breakdowns for skills such as Merging, Overtaking, Emergency Brake, Give Way, and Traffic Sign handling. Baseline models will be compared both in open-loop (L2 error) and closed-loop settings, and the impact of expert feature distillation will be assessed. All experimental code, data, and checkpoints will be made publicly available.
bc2ac51104e3a477938aa664e20527a7178fd418.novelty_claims: Bench2Drive is the first benchmark to provide multi-ability, closed-loop evaluation of E2E-AD systems with a large-scale, standardized, and diverse official training dataset. It enables granular skill assessment by isolating scenarios in short routes, supports fair algorithm-level comparison by using a unified dataset, and introduces comprehensive metrics that go beyond traditional driving scores to include efficiency and comfortness. The benchmark addresses key limitations of existing open-loop and closed-loop evaluations, such as high variance, lack of scenario diversity, and inability to disentangle specific driving skills.

bc2ddba47a9d6b378abd8a8584849f3e4c410f24.title: WorldSimBench: Towards Video Generation Models as World Simulators
bc2ddba47a9d6b378abd8a8584849f3e4c410f24.research_question: How can the capabilities of advanced video generation models, particularly those functioning as world simulators, be systematically evaluated from both perceptual and embodied perspectives across diverse real-world scenarios?
bc2ddba47a9d6b378abd8a8584849f3e4c410f24.hypothesis: A dual evaluation framework that combines explicit perceptual assessment with implicit manipulative evaluation will provide a more comprehensive and actionable measure of the capabilities and limitations of video generation models as world simulators, especially in embodied tasks.
bc2ddba47a9d6b378abd8a8584849f3e4c410f24.proposed_method: A dual evaluation framework, WorldSimBench, will be developed to assess video generation models acting as world simulators. The first component, Explicit Perceptual Evaluation, will utilize a large, fine-grained human-annotated dataset (HF-Embodied Dataset) covering three representative embodied scenarios: Open-Ended Embodied Environment (OE), Autonomous Driving (AD), and Robot Manipulation (RM). This dataset will be constructed by generating scenario-specific videos using various models, followed by detailed human feedback along hierarchical evaluation dimensions such as visual quality, condition consistency, and embodiment. A Human Preference Evaluator, based on a fine-tuned VideoLLM (e.g., Flash-VStream with LoRA), will be trained to align with human perceptual judgments. The second component, Implicit Manipulative Evaluation, will assess the actionability and situational awareness of generated videos by integrating them into closed-loop simulation environments. Pre-trained video-to-action models will translate generated videos into control signals, enabling evaluation of the models' effectiveness in real-time embodied tasks.
bc2ddba47a9d6b378abd8a8584849f3e4c410f24.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across three simulation platforms: MineRL for OE (Minecraft), CARLA for AD (autonomous driving), and CALVIN for RM (robot manipulation), each with scenario-specific observation and action spaces. Multiple state-of-the-art video generation models will be fine-tuned and evaluated using both the Explicit Perceptual Evaluation (via the Human Preference Evaluator and HF-Embodied Dataset) and Implicit Manipulative Evaluation (via closed-loop task performance using video-to-action models). Evaluation metrics will include multi-dimensional human-aligned scores for perceptual quality, as well as task-specific success rates, route completion, infraction scores, and other scenario-relevant quantitative measures. Baselines will include both traditional feature similarity metrics and large language model-based evaluators (e.g., GPT-4o), with comprehensive comparisons across all models and scenarios.
bc2ddba47a9d6b378abd8a8584849f3e4c410f24.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a hierarchical categorization of predictive models based on embodiment and output modality, culminating in the definition and evaluation of world simulators. The dual evaluation framework, WorldSimBench, is novel in its integration of explicit human-aligned perceptual assessment and implicit manipulative evaluation within embodied simulation environments. The creation of the HF-Embodied Dataset, featuring fine-grained human feedback across 20 dimensions and three scenarios, represents a significant resource for both evaluation and future model alignment. The Human Preference Evaluator, trained to align with nuanced human judgments, offers improved generalization and alignment over existing LLM-based evaluators. This comprehensive approach enables actionable insights into the strengths and limitations of current video generation models, guiding future research toward more robust and physically consistent world simulators.

bc8428e270a5474cabfaff578d44955f757ccacd.title: LoSparse: Structured Compression of Large Language Models based on Low-Rank and Sparse Approximation
bc8428e270a5474cabfaff578d44955f757ccacd.research_question: How can large language models be compressed in a way that significantly reduces memory and computational requirements while maintaining high performance across diverse natural language tasks?
bc8428e270a5474cabfaff578d44955f757ccacd.hypothesis: A model compression technique that approximates each weight matrix as the sum of a low-rank matrix and a structured sparse matrix will outperform existing pruning and low-rank methods in terms of efficiency and accuracy, especially at high compression rates.
bc8428e270a5474cabfaff578d44955f757ccacd.proposed_method: The proposed method, LoSparse, compresses large language models by representing each weight matrix as the sum of a low-rank matrix and a structured sparse matrix. The low-rank component is initialized using singular value decomposition (SVD) to capture the coherent, expressive parts of the weight matrix, while the sparse component captures the incoherent, less expressive parts. An iterative structured pruning algorithm is applied to the sparse matrix, using neuron importance scores derived from gradient-weight products and smoothed by exponential moving averages. During training, the low-rank and sparse matrices are updated via stochastic gradient descent, and the sparse matrix is pruned progressively according to a cubic decay schedule on the proportion of retained neurons. This decomposition and pruning are applied to all weight matrices except LayerNorm and the final prediction head, and the forward pass is restructured to utilize the decomposed matrices for computational efficiency.
bc8428e270a5474cabfaff578d44955f757ccacd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on natural language understanding (GLUE benchmark), question answering (SQuAD v1.1), and natural language generation (XSum) tasks. The method will be evaluated on popular transformer models such as DeBERTaV3-base, BERT-base, and BART-large. Baselines will include full fine-tuning, movement pruning, and iterative pruning (ITP). Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, F1 score, Rouge-1, and other task-specific metrics. The proportion of retained parameters (remaining ratio) will be varied to assess performance at different compression levels, and all experiments will be run on NVIDIA V100 GPUs using the Huggingface Transformers codebase.
bc8428e270a5474cabfaff578d44955f757ccacd.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a structured compression technique that combines low-rank approximation and structured pruning in a unified framework, effectively decoupling coherent and incoherent components of weight matrices. This method leverages the strengths of both low-rank and sparse approximations, addressing the limitations of each when used independently. The algorithm is designed to be orthogonal and complementary to knowledge distillation methods, and can be readily integrated with them. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate significant improvements over existing compression methods in both efficiency and model performance, particularly at high compression rates.

bc8611c27c2676aa1c593f2986e24d2e813e9a63.title: Efficient and Context-Aware Label Propagation for Zero-/Few-Shot Training-Free Adaptation of Vision-Language Model
bc8611c27c2676aa1c593f2986e24d2e813e9a63.research_question: How can vision-language models be adapted to downstream tasks in a zero-shot or few-shot, training-free manner, improving label efficiency, computational efficiency, and generalization without requiring task-specific hyperparameter tuning or additional unlabeled support sets?
bc8611c27c2676aa1c593f2986e24d2e813e9a63.hypothesis: A graph-based, context-aware label propagation framework that dynamically incorporates text prompts, few-shot examples, and test samples, with feature re-weighting and efficient graph expansion, will enable accurate, training-free adaptation of vision-language models to diverse downstream tasks, outperforming existing methods in both efficiency and accuracy.
bc8611c27c2676aa1c593f2986e24d2e813e9a63.proposed_method: A unified, training-free adaptation framework for vision-language models is developed based on iterative label propagation over a dynamically constructed graph. The graph includes nodes for text prompt prototypes, few-shot labeled samples (if available), and test samples, with edges determined by context-aware, feature-dimension re-weighted similarities. Graph construction is performed using K-nearest neighbor search within and across modalities, and the graph is dynamically expanded to support inductive inference as new test samples arrive, reducing computational complexity. The label propagation process is iterative, with label resets for prototypes and labeled nodes at each step, and pseudo-labels for test samples are incrementally updated to accelerate convergence. Feature re-weighting is performed using the variance statistics of text embeddings and few-shot features to emphasize discriminative dimensions and suppress irrelevant intra-class variance, further sparsifying the graph for robustness.
bc8611c27c2676aa1c593f2986e24d2e813e9a63.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a wide range of downstream tasks, including fine-grained categorization (e.g., ImageNet, Flowers102, DTD, OxfordPets, StanfordCars, UCF101, Caltech101, Food101, SUN397, FGVCAircraft, EuroSAT), style-transfer datasets (ImageNet-V2, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-Sketch), and out-of-distribution benchmarks (15 corruption types from ImageNet-C). Both zero-shot and few-shot scenarios will be evaluated using pre-trained CLIP models (ResNet50 and ViT-B/16 architectures), with consistent hyperparameters across all experiments. Baselines will include prompt-tuning methods (TPT, DiffTPT, CoOp, CoCoOp) and adapter-based methods (CLIP-Adapter, TIP-Adapter, DMN, TDA, ZLaP, among others). Evaluation metrics will focus on classification accuracy, and computational efficiency will be measured by wall-clock inference time. Ablation studies will assess the impact of individual components, such as label propagation, graph substructures, and feature re-weighting strategies.
bc8611c27c2676aa1c593f2986e24d2e813e9a63.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a holistic, training-free, and context-aware label propagation framework for vision-language model adaptation that eliminates the need for task-specific hyperparameter tuning and additional unlabeled support sets. It features a novel dynamic graph expansion mechanism for efficient inductive inference, context-aware feature re-weighting based on downstream task statistics, and an iterative label propagation process with incremental pseudo-label updates. The method achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and computational efficiency across a diverse set of downstream tasks, outperforming both training-based and training-free baselines.

bc8eee373bf96e508a0848cdafbc7b76fbff5859.title: Information-theoretic Generalization Analysis for VQ-VAEs: A Role of Latent Variables
bc8eee373bf96e508a0848cdafbc7b76fbff5859.research_question: What are the fundamental information-theoretic factors governing the generalization and data generation performance of vector-quantized variational autoencoders (VQ-VAEs), and how do latent variables contribute to these properties in unsupervised learning settings?
bc8eee373bf96e508a0848cdafbc7b76fbff5859.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the generalization and data generation capabilities of VQ-VAEs are governed primarily by the complexity of the encoder and latent variables, and not by the complexity of the decoder. Furthermore, introducing a novel data-dependent prior that leverages permutation symmetry will yield a generalization error bound that converges asymptotically and is independent of the decoder.
bc8eee373bf96e508a0848cdafbc7b76fbff5859.proposed_method: A rigorous information-theoretic analysis will be developed to characterize the relationship between latent variables, generalization, and data generation in VQ-VAEs. The approach introduces a novel data-dependent prior over latent variables, constructed using a permutation-symmetric supersample setting, to enable a decoder-independent generalization error bound. The methodology involves deriving upper bounds on the generalization gap based on Kullback–Leibler divergences between the posterior and the proposed prior over latent variables, as well as analyzing the 2-Wasserstein distance between the true data distribution and the generated data distribution. The analysis will be extended to both deterministic and stochastic encoder settings, and will include metric entropy-based uniform convergence bounds for softmax-based posteriors. Key steps include formalizing the permutation-symmetric prior, deriving the corresponding generalization bounds, and establishing the asymptotic convergence of these bounds under regularized encoder complexity.
bc8eee373bf96e508a0848cdafbc7b76fbff5859.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on benchmark datasets such as MNIST, with VQ-VAE models trained using varying encoder and decoder complexities (e.g., by altering the number of residual blocks in the decoder and the dimensionality of the latent space). The generalization gap will be measured as the difference between test and training reconstruction losses. Baselines will include models with standard uniform priors and alternative prior choices, as well as comparisons across different decoder architectures. Evaluation metrics will include the empirical generalization gap, KL divergence terms from the theoretical bounds, and the 2-Wasserstein distance between generated and true data distributions. Additional experiments will assess the effect of the proposed data-dependent prior on both generalization and data generation performance, with results analyzed for asymptotic behavior as sample size increases.
bc8eee373bf96e508a0848cdafbc7b76fbff5859.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first rigorous information-theoretic generalization analysis for VQ-VAEs with discrete latent spaces, yielding decoder-independent generalization error bounds. A novel permutation-symmetric, data-dependent prior is developed, enabling an asymptotically convergent generalization bound that isolates the contribution of latent variables. The analysis also provides the first formal justification for KL-based regularization on latent variables in VQ-VAEs and establishes a theoretical upper bound on the data generation quality via the 2-Wasserstein distance. The framework highlights the critical role of encoder and latent variable complexity, rather than decoder complexity, in governing generalization and generation performance. These contributions offer actionable insights for model design and prior selection in unsupervised generative modeling.

bc8f65e37416af8bbbf87d6af88b1267d4c7321f.title: Multi-Token Prediction Needs Registers
bc8f65e37416af8bbbf87d6af88b1267d4c7321f.research_question: How can multi-token prediction objectives be improved to enhance the training and fine-tuning of autoregressive transformer models for both language and vision generative tasks, while maintaining compatibility with existing model architectures and minimizing additional parameter overhead?
bc8f65e37416af8bbbf87d6af88b1267d4c7321f.hypothesis: Introducing interleaved, trainable register tokens into the input sequence during training, each tasked with predicting future tokens at varying offsets, will provide richer supervisory signals and improve model performance on generative tasks compared to standard next-token prediction and existing multi-token prediction methods, without requiring architectural changes or significant parameter increases.
bc8f65e37416af8bbbf87d6af88b1267d4c7321f.proposed_method: A novel multi-token prediction framework, MuToR, will be developed by interleaving learnable register tokens within the input sequence during training. Each register token is assigned a randomly sampled offset and is trained to predict the token at that offset ahead in the sequence, while standard tokens retain the next-token prediction objective. Attention masking will be carefully designed so that register tokens attend only to preceding regular tokens, and regular tokens remain blind to register tokens, ensuring that the inference procedure remains unchanged and efficient. All register tokens will share a single learnable embedding, and their prediction offsets will be encoded via positional embeddings, requiring no architectural modifications. The overall training loss will be a weighted sum of the standard next-token loss and the auxiliary register loss, with the relative contribution controlled by a tunable coefficient.
bc8f65e37416af8bbbf87d6af88b1267d4c7321f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both language and vision domains. For language modeling, the method will be evaluated on mathematical reasoning (GSM8K, MATH500, AQUA-RAT) and abstractive summarization (SAMSum, DialogSum) benchmarks, using pretrained models such as Gemma 2B and Llama 3 8B. Fine-tuning and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT, e.g., with LoRA) scenarios will be tested. Baselines will include standard next-token prediction and an adapted multi-token prediction method with additional output heads. Evaluation metrics will include exact-match accuracy for reasoning tasks and ROUGE scores for summarization. For vision, the approach will be applied to autoregressive image generation on ImageNet 256x256 using LlamaGen-B, with evaluation via FID, IS, Precision, and Recall. Additional ablations will examine the effects of prediction horizon, number and placement of register tokens, and embedding sharing. Synthetic tasks such as star-graph path-finding will further probe the method's ability to overcome shortcut learning.
bc8f65e37416af8bbbf87d6af88b1267d4c7321f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a register-based multi-token prediction objective that enables scalable prediction horizons with minimal parameter overhead and no architectural changes, ensuring seamless integration with off-the-shelf pretrained models. Unlike prior methods that require additional transformer heads or layers, this method leverages a single shared embedding for all register tokens and encodes prediction offsets via positional embeddings. The attention masking strategy preserves standard inference efficiency and compatibility. The approach is demonstrated to be effective across both language and vision domains, in both full and parameter-efficient fine-tuning settings, and offers unique flexibility for long-range and structured prediction tasks.

bc8fb1f72493ad39f2970b99863fe5fcac78c1fc.title: Neural Algorithmic Reasoning with Causal Regularisation
bc8fb1f72493ad39f2970b99863fe5fcac78c1fc.research_question: How can neural networks be improved to generalize algorithmic reasoning to out-of-distribution (OOD) data, particularly when input sizes are larger or structurally different from those seen during training?
bc8fb1f72493ad39f2970b99863fe5fcac78c1fc.hypothesis: Learning representations of intermediate algorithmic computations (hints) that are invariant to specific input changes—those that do not affect the current computational step—will improve the out-of-distribution generalization of neural algorithmic reasoners.
bc8fb1f72493ad39f2970b99863fe5fcac78c1fc.proposed_method: A new framework, Hint-ReLIC, is proposed to enhance neural algorithmic reasoning by leveraging a causality-inspired self-supervised learning objective. The approach begins by constructing a causal graph that models the execution trajectory of an algorithm, identifying subsets of the input (Xs) that determine the outcome of each computational step, and subsets (Xc) that can vary without affecting the step. Data augmentation procedures are designed to generate new inputs that, despite being larger or structurally altered, lead to identical intermediate computations. A self-supervised contrastive loss, based on the ReLIC objective, is employed to enforce that representations of hints are invariant across such augmented inputs. Additionally, a KL divergence penalty ensures invariance in the probability distributions across augmentations. The model is implemented by replacing the standard hint prediction loss in a graph neural network (GNN) with this regularization objective, and includes the reversal of pointer-type hints to further enrich the learning signal.
bc8fb1f72493ad39f2970b99863fe5fcac78c1fc.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a diverse subset of the CLRS-30 algorithmic reasoning benchmark, which includes a variety of graph-based and sorting/searching algorithms known to exhibit OOD generalization challenges. The proposed Hint-ReLIC model is compared against a strong Triplet-GMPNN baseline, as well as ablations that include or exclude pointer reversals and hint usage. Evaluation is performed using the micro-F1 score on OOD test data, where input sizes are larger than those seen during training. Data augmentations are carefully constructed to simulate valid interventions on the input, ensuring that the computational step remains unchanged. Multiple random seeds and standard error reporting are used to ensure robust comparisons.
bc8fb1f72493ad39f2970b99863fe5fcac78c1fc.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel self-supervised regularization objective for neural algorithmic reasoning, grounded in a formal causal model of algorithm execution. Unlike prior work, the method enforces invariance of intermediate computation representations across input augmentations that do not affect the current step, provably improving causal invariance and OOD generalization. The approach leverages hints not just as auxiliary targets, but as anchors for constructing meaningful data augmentations and self-supervised objectives, leading to significant improvements—up to 3×—in OOD performance on challenging algorithmic tasks.

bc8fcde10b35b89962d72969e29ab7c638552546.title: FasterCache: Training-Free Video Diffusion Model Acceleration with High Quality
bc8fcde10b35b89962d72969e29ab7c638552546.research_question: How can the inference speed of video diffusion models be substantially accelerated without requiring additional training, while maintaining high-quality video generation across diverse architectures and settings?
bc8fcde10b35b89962d72969e29ab7c638552546.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a training-free approach leveraging dynamic feature reuse in attention modules, along with optimized reuse of conditional and unconditional outputs in classifier-free guidance, can significantly accelerate video diffusion model inference without degrading video quality.
bc8fcde10b35b89962d72969e29ab7c638552546.proposed_method: A novel training-free acceleration framework, FasterCache, will be developed for video diffusion models. The approach introduces a Dynamic Feature Reuse Strategy, where attention module outputs are computed at alternate timesteps and their differences are used as bias terms to approximate feature evolution, with a weighting function w(t) modulating the contribution of these differences over the sampling process. This preserves both feature distinction and temporal continuity, mitigating the loss of subtle details. Additionally, a CFG-Cache mechanism will be implemented, which analyzes the frequency-domain differences between conditional and unconditional outputs at each timestep. High- and low-frequency biases are cached and adaptively enhanced during reuse, allowing the unconditional branch to be approximated from the conditional branch in subsequent steps, with adaptive weighting based on the sampling phase. The method is designed to be plug-and-play, requiring no retraining or modification of the base diffusion models.
bc8fcde10b35b89962d72969e29ab7c638552546.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of state-of-the-art video diffusion models, including Open-Sora 1.2, Open-Sora-Plan, Latte, CogVideoX, and Vchitect-2.0. The proposed method will be compared against recent acceleration baselines such as PAB and ∆-DiT, with adaptations as necessary for video synthesis. Evaluation will focus on both inference efficiency (MACs, latency) and visual quality (VBench, LPIPS, PSNR, SSIM), using standard benchmarks such as VBench and prompt sets. Ablation studies will assess the contributions of each component (dynamic feature reuse, CFG-Cache, frequency enhancement), and scalability will be tested on multi-GPU setups and across varying video lengths and resolutions. Implementation will use PyTorch with FlashAttention on NVIDIA A100 GPUs, and hyperparameters will be tuned for optimal performance.
bc8fcde10b35b89962d72969e29ab7c638552546.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the first dynamic, training-free feature reuse strategy for attention modules in video diffusion transformers, preserving both subtle inter-step variations and temporal consistency. It pioneers the exploitation of redundancy in classifier-free guidance, introducing a frequency-aware caching mechanism (CFG-Cache) that adaptively enhances high- and low-frequency components to maintain detail quality. The approach is generalizable across diverse video diffusion models and does not require model retraining, offering significant acceleration with minimal quality loss. Extensive evaluation demonstrates superior speedup and visual fidelity compared to existing cache-based and acceleration methods.

bcd160f7f33472700e24c981509e4d3a2a7e9308.title: A General Framework for Auditing Differentially Private Machine Learning
bcd160f7f33472700e24c981509e4d3a2a7e9308.research_question: How can the privacy guarantees of differentially private machine learning models be empirically audited in a general and statistically rigorous manner, across a variety of model types and datasets, to detect potential privacy violations or implementation errors?
bcd160f7f33472700e24c981509e4d3a2a7e9308.hypothesis: A general auditing framework that combines improved privacy search and verification methods with a toolkit of influence-based poisoning attacks will enable more powerful and effective empirical evaluation of privacy guarantees in differentially private machine learning models, outperforming existing model-specific or low-power approaches.
bcd160f7f33472700e24c981509e4d3a2a7e9308.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework, ML-Audit, will be developed to empirically audit the privacy of arbitrary differentially private machine learning models. The method begins by generating neighboring datasets through a set of optimized poisoning attacks, tailored for each model type (e.g., logistic regression, Naive Bayes, random forest, DP-SGD), which perturb a single data point to maximize the influence on the model's output. For each pair of original and perturbed datasets, the framework repeatedly trains the model to sample from the randomized output distribution, then applies a likelihood ratio-based optimization to determine the most distinguishing output set (S) for privacy risk estimation. The approach employs a classifier to learn the posterior probability of dataset membership given model outputs, enabling the construction of optimal rejection regions for hypothesis testing. Statistical confidence intervals are calculated using improved estimation bounds (e.g., Katz-log confidence interval), and group privacy is leveraged by inserting multiple copies of the perturbed point to increase statistical distinguishability. The framework is designed to be model-agnostic, scalable to various ML algorithms, and robust to practical implementation constraints.
bcd160f7f33472700e24c981509e4d3a2a7e9308.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of common machine learning datasets, including adult, credit, iris, breast-cancer, banknote, thoracic, FMNIST, and CIFAR10. The framework will be applied to differentially private implementations of logistic regression (objective and output perturbation), Naive Bayes, random forest, and DP-SGD. For each model and dataset, privacy parameters (epsilon) will be varied across a wide range, and the auditing procedure will be repeated multiple times to assess statistical power and confidence. Baseline methods for comparison will include the ClipBKD attack, row-swap (random point swap), and existing membership inference or loss-threshold attacks. Evaluation metrics will focus on the detected lower bound of privacy loss (epsilon), statistical confidence intervals, and the ability to detect privacy violations or implementation errors. The experimental setup will use thousands of Monte Carlo samples for each mechanism, with careful separation of search and verification samples to avoid bias.
bcd160f7f33472700e24c981509e4d3a2a7e9308.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to provide a general, model-agnostic procedure for auditing the differential privacy of arbitrary machine learning models, overcoming limitations of previous approaches that were either model-specific or lacked statistical power. The method introduces a novel combination of influence-based poisoning attacks, likelihood ratio-based optimization for output set selection, and improved statistical estimation techniques, resulting in orders-of-magnitude improvements in auditing efficacy. The approach enables detection of privacy violations due to implementation errors or misuse, and provides insights into dataset- and algorithm-dependent privacy leakage. The framework is compatible with prior model-specific approaches but achieves similar or improved results across a broader range of models and datasets.

bcd7572f83cb27b11202c4d06ffb88d08d264c02.title: Exact Convergence Rate of the Last Iterate in Subgradient Methods
bcd7572f83cb27b11202c4d06ffb88d08d264c02.research_question: What are the exact worst-case convergence rates for the last iterate in subgradient methods when minimizing nonsmooth convex functions with bounded subgradients, and how can optimal step size or step length strategies be designed to achieve these rates?
bcd7572f83cb27b11202c4d06ffb88d08d264c02.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the last iterate of subgradient methods can achieve exact, tight worst-case convergence rates under appropriate choices of constant step size or constant step length, and that a new optimal subgradient method can be constructed to match the lower bound for last-iterate accuracy in nonsmooth convex optimization.
bcd7572f83cb27b11202c4d06ffb88d08d264c02.proposed_method: A generalized proof technique will be developed that tracks the distance between the current iterate and a dynamically chosen reference point at each iteration, extending the standard analysis of subgradient methods. The convergence of the last iterate will be analyzed for projected subgradient methods using either constant step sizes or constant step lengths, with explicit formulas derived for the worst-case rates. The method will include the derivation of the optimal constant step size for a given number of iterations, and a new optimal subgradient method will be constructed to achieve the best possible last-iterate accuracy. The approach will rigorously establish lower bounds and demonstrate the tightness of the rates by constructing matching worst-case instances.
bcd7572f83cb27b11202c4d06ffb88d08d264c02.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted primarily through theoretical analysis and the construction of explicit worst-case problem instances. For validation, synthetic convex optimization problems will be designed, such as unconstrained univariate cases and high-dimensional examples with specified subgradient norms and initial distances. The performance of the proposed methods will be compared against standard subgradient methods with various step size rules. Evaluation metrics will include the objective accuracy of the last iterate after N iterations, with particular attention to matching the derived theoretical rates. Baselines will include best-iterate and average-iterate convergence rates, as well as previously known lower bounds for black-box nonsmooth convex optimization.
bcd7572f83cb27b11202c4d06ffb88d08d264c02.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a generalized proof technique for last-iterate convergence analysis, establishes the exact worst-case convergence rates for the last iterate under constant step size and step length regimes, and derives the optimal step size for minimizing last-iterate error. A new optimal subgradient method is proposed that achieves the theoretical lower bound for last-iterate accuracy, demonstrating that this rate is tight and cannot be improved by any black-box method. The work also proves that no universal step size sequence can achieve the optimal rate at every iteration, highlighting the necessity of N-dependent step size schedules.

bcdaf6c98ddbd6809cf6241aa77200d7394db163.title: CRITIC: Large Language Models Can Self-Correct with Tool-Interactive Critiquing
bcdaf6c98ddbd6809cf6241aa77200d7394db163.research_question: How can large language models be enabled to autonomously verify and improve their outputs across diverse tasks using external tools, in a manner that does not require additional supervised training or large-scale human annotation?
bcdaf6c98ddbd6809cf6241aa77200d7394db163.hypothesis: Integrating external tool-based feedback into the output generation process of large language models will enable more effective self-correction and output improvement than relying solely on the models' intrinsic self-verification capabilities.
bcdaf6c98ddbd6809cf6241aa77200d7394db163.proposed_method: A unified framework, termed CRITIC, will be developed to empower large language models (LLMs) to iteratively verify and correct their outputs by interacting with external tools such as search engines, code interpreters, and toxicity assessment APIs. The process begins with the LLM generating an initial output for a given input. The output is then verified by querying appropriate external tools, which provide critiques regarding specific aspects such as truthfulness, correctness, or toxicity. These critiques are concatenated with the original input and output, and the LLM is prompted to generate a revised output conditioned on this feedback. This verify-then-correct cycle is repeated iteratively until a stopping criterion is met, such as the output passing all verification checks or reaching a maximum number of iterations. The framework leverages in-context learning and few-shot prompting to guide the LLM in both tool interaction and self-correction, without requiring any additional model fine-tuning.
bcdaf6c98ddbd6809cf6241aa77200d7394db163.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three representative tasks: free-form question answering (focusing on factual correctness), mathematical program synthesis (emphasizing code correctness and executability), and toxicity reduction (ensuring safe and fluent text generation). For question answering, datasets such as AmbigNQ, TriviaQA, and HotpotQA will be used, with evaluation based on EM and F1 scores. Mathematical program synthesis will utilize GSM8k, SVAMP, and TabMWP datasets, reporting exact match rates after program execution. Toxicity reduction will be evaluated using 1,000 prompts from the RealToxicityPrompts dataset, with toxicity measured by the PERSPECTIVE API, alongside fluency and diversity metrics. Baselines will include vanilla prompting, chain-of-thought, self-consistency, retrieval-augmented methods, and state-of-the-art supervised approaches. Both proprietary (ChatGPT, text-davinci-003) and open-source (LLaMA-2 7B/13B/70B) LLMs will be tested, and ablations will assess the impact of tool interaction.
bcdaf6c98ddbd6809cf6241aa77200d7394db163.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a general, plug-and-play method for enabling black-box LLMs to self-correct via external tool interaction, without any additional supervised training or data annotation. It unifies verification and correction across diverse tasks and tools, leveraging in-context learning for both tool use and critique incorporation. The approach demonstrates that external feedback is critical for consistent self-improvement of LLMs, outperforming both intrinsic self-correction and prior retrieval-augmented or supervised baselines. The method is model-agnostic, scalable, and applicable to a wide range of LLMs and tasks, highlighting the inadequacy of LLMs' self-verification and the necessity of external tool feedback for trustworthy AI.

bce29cc829fab288c41ae5678e1bb5b95bf218d4.title: Aligning Bag of Regions for Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
bce29cc829fab288c41ae5678e1bb5b95bf218d4.research_question: How can open-vocabulary object detection be improved by leveraging the compositional structure of multiple semantic concepts in a scene, as implicitly learned by large-scale vision-language models?
bce29cc829fab288c41ae5678e1bb5b95bf218d4.hypothesis: Explicitly aligning embeddings of contextually interrelated groups of regions (bags of regions), rather than only individual regions, with vision-language model representations will better capture compositional semantics and improve open-vocabulary object detection performance.
bce29cc829fab288c41ae5678e1bb5b95bf218d4.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that groups contextually related region proposals from an image into 'bags of regions.' Each region's features are projected into a word embedding space to create pseudo words, which are then concatenated and fed into the text encoder of a frozen vision-language model (VLM), such as CLIP. Spatial information, including box shape and center position, is encoded as positional embeddings and added to the pseudo words before encoding. The resulting bag-of-regions embedding is aligned, via contrastive learning, to the corresponding image feature extracted by the VLM's image encoder from a crop enclosing the bag. A neighborhood sampling strategy is employed to select nearby regions, ensuring semantic continuity and balanced region sizes within each bag. The approach is instantiated on Faster R-CNN by replacing its classifier with a linear layer mapping region features to pseudo words, and training is performed using both bag-level and individual region-level contrastive losses.
bce29cc829fab288c41ae5678e1bb5b95bf218d4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the OV-COCO and OV-LVIS open-vocabulary detection benchmarks, using standard splits for base and novel categories. The proposed method will be evaluated using box AP at IoU 0.5 (AP50) for COCO and both mask and box mAP (averaged over IoUs from 0.5 to 0.95) for LVIS, with a focus on novel and rare categories. Baselines will include state-of-the-art distillation-based open-vocabulary detectors such as ViLD, OV-DETR, DetPro, and caption-supervised methods like RegionCLIP and PB-OVD. The backbone will be ResNet50-FPN, and the VLM teacher will be CLIP ViT-B/32. Ablation studies will examine the effects of sampling strategies, overlap thresholds, number of pseudo words, and the inclusion of spatial information. Transferability will be assessed by evaluating models trained on OV-LVIS on Pascal VOC, COCO, and Objects365 datasets.
bce29cc829fab288c41ae5678e1bb5b95bf218d4.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to explicitly align bag-of-regions embeddings, rather than only individual region embeddings, with vision-language model features for open-vocabulary object detection. The method introduces a neighborhood sampling strategy to form semantically coherent bags of regions and encodes spatial relationships as positional embeddings, enabling the text encoder to capture scene-level compositional semantics. This framework is general, supporting both image and caption supervision, and achieves new state-of-the-art results on multiple open-vocabulary detection benchmarks. The approach demonstrates improved generalization and transferability to novel categories and datasets.

bcf905de68f78ad1e21ec488eed643e2cfe747dc.title: Prediction via Shapley Value Regression
bcf905de68f78ad1e21ec488eed643e2cfe747dc.research_question: How can predictive models be designed to simultaneously generate accurate predictions and provide real-time, theoretically sound Shapley value explanations, thereby eliminating the computational overhead of post-hoc explanation methods?
bcf905de68f78ad1e21ec488eed643e2cfe747dc.hypothesis: Integrating Shapley value computation directly into the predictive model training process enables simultaneous generation of accurate predictions and faithful feature attributions, achieving performance comparable to state-of-the-art models while providing more accurate explanations than existing Shapley approximators.
bcf905de68f78ad1e21ec488eed643e2cfe747dc.proposed_method: A novel framework, ViaSHAP, will be developed to learn a function that outputs Shapley values for each input instance, with predictions derived as the sum of these values. Two architectural approaches will be explored: one based on the universal approximation theorem (using multi-layer perceptrons) and another leveraging the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem (using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks, KANs). The model will be trained using a dual-objective loss: a weighted least squares loss to align predicted Shapley values with their theoretical properties, and a standard prediction loss (e.g., cross-entropy or mean squared error) to ensure predictive accuracy. Sampling of feature coalitions will be used during training to enforce Shapley properties such as local accuracy and missingness. The model will be designed to accommodate various output types, including regression and classification, with optional link functions for output normalization.
bcf905de68f78ad1e21ec488eed643e2cfe747dc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 25 publicly available tabular datasets, each split into training, validation, and test sets. Four implementations of ViaSHAP (KAN-based with splines, KAN-based with RBFs, and two MLP-based variants) will be compared against established baselines including XGBoost, Random Forests, and TabNet, all trained with default hyperparameters. Predictive performance will be evaluated using the area under the ROC curve (AUC), with statistical significance assessed via Friedman and Nemenyi tests. For explainability evaluation, ground truth Shapley values will be computed using unbiased KernelSHAP, and the similarity between model-generated and ground truth attributions will be measured using cosine similarity, Spearman rank correlation, and R^2. Additional experiments will be performed on the CIFAR-10 image dataset using ResNet and U-Net based ViaSHAP models, with explanation accuracy assessed by the effect of feature inclusion/exclusion on predictions. Ablation studies will investigate the impact of key hyperparameters, coalition sampling, and loss weighting.
bcf905de68f78ad1e21ec488eed643e2cfe747dc.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to integrate Shapley value computation directly into the predictive modeling process, enabling real-time, theoretically grounded explanations without post-hoc computation. The method is architecture-agnostic, supporting both universal approximators and Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks, and is shown to produce more accurate Shapley value explanations than popular approximators like FastSHAP. ViaSHAP achieves predictive performance on par with state-of-the-art algorithms for tabular data while providing explanations that closely align with ground truth Shapley values. The framework also demonstrates applicability to image data, offering a unified solution for interpretable machine learning across domains.

bcfa73aedf1b2d1ee4f168e21298a37ac55a37f7.title: Bias and Fairness in Large Language Models: A Survey
bcfa73aedf1b2d1ee4f168e21298a37ac55a37f7.research_question: How can social bias and fairness in large language models (LLMs) be systematically defined, evaluated, and mitigated across diverse natural language processing tasks and applications?
bcfa73aedf1b2d1ee4f168e21298a37ac55a37f7.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed to formalize and categorize social bias and fairness in LLMs, consolidating definitions and taxonomies from machine learning, NLP, and sociolinguistics. The approach will introduce distinct facets of harm and operationalize fairness through a set of desiderata tailored for LLMs. Three intuitive taxonomies will be constructed: (1) metrics for bias evaluation, organized by the level of model operation (embeddings, probabilities, generated text), (2) datasets for bias evaluation, categorized by structure (counterfactual inputs or prompts) and targeted harms/social groups, and (3) bias mitigation techniques, classified by intervention stage (pre-processing, in-training, intra-processing, post-processing) with granular subcategories. Mathematical formalization and unified notation will be used to enhance comparability and clarity across metrics and mitigation techniques.
bcfa73aedf1b2d1ee4f168e21298a37ac55a37f7.experiment_details: The proposed research will involve a systematic survey and classification of existing metrics, datasets, and mitigation methods for bias in LLMs. Publicly available datasets will be consolidated and annotated for improved access and comparability, with a focus on identifying the types of harm and social groups targeted.
