Evaluation will include analysis of metric-dataset compatibility and limitations in capturing downstream application biases. The study will also highlight challenges in dataset consistency, reliability, and validity, and provide representative examples and mathematical formalizations for each class of method. No new empirical experiments are proposed, but the framework will be validated through comprehensive literature synthesis and taxonomy construction.
bcfa73aedf1b2d1ee4f168e21298a37ac55a37f7.novelty_claims: The proposed work introduces a unified and formalized set of definitions for social bias and fairness specific to LLMs, expanding on prior frameworks by integrating sociolinguistic perspectives. It presents the first comprehensive taxonomies that disambiguate metrics, datasets, and mitigation techniques, organizing them by their underlying structure and intervention stage. The research provides a consolidated benchmark of publicly available datasets, mathematical formalization for improved metric comparison, and granular classification of mitigation methods. By synthesizing diverse bodies of work and identifying open challenges, the framework aims to guide future research and practice in bias evaluation and mitigation for LLMs.

bd0431d8a5ec2ef9f66c26f3fa7b14ebd01435b3.title: SG-I2V: Self-Guided Trajectory Control in Image-to-Video Generation
bd0431d8a5ec2ef9f66c26f3fa7b14ebd01435b3.research_question: How can controllable image-to-video generation be achieved with precise trajectory control over object and camera motion, without requiring fine-tuning or external supervision, by leveraging only the knowledge present in pre-trained image-to-video diffusion models?
bd0431d8a5ec2ef9f66c26f3fa7b14ebd01435b3.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that semantically aligning feature maps within a pre-trained image-to-video diffusion model and optimizing the latent representations with respect to user-specified bounding box trajectories will enable zero-shot, fine-grained control over object and camera motion in generated videos, achieving high visual quality and motion fidelity without the need for fine-tuning or external annotated data.
bd0431d8a5ec2ef9f66c26f3fa7b14ebd01435b3.proposed_method: A novel zero-shot, self-guided framework for controllable image-to-video generation will be developed. The method will accept an input image and a set of user-specified bounding box trajectories, representing desired object or camera motions. During the early denoising steps of a pre-trained image-to-video diffusion model (e.g., Stable Video Diffusion), feature maps will be extracted from specific self-attention layers and semantically aligned across frames by modifying the attention mechanism to use key and value tokens from the first frame. The noisy latent input to the denoising network will then be optimized with a loss that enforces similarity of aligned features within each bounding box along the specified trajectory, using a Gaussian heatmap to focus the optimization. To preserve visual quality and avoid out-of-distribution artifacts, a frequency-based post-processing step will replace the high-frequency components of the optimized latent with those from the original latent, using a low-pass filter in the Fourier domain.
bd0431d8a5ec2ef9f66c26f3fa7b14ebd01435b3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the image-to-video variant of Stable Video Diffusion to generate 14-frame videos at 576×1024 resolution. The validation set of the VIPSeg dataset will be used, with control regions and trajectories matching those in prior work. The proposed method will be compared against supervised baselines (DragNUWA, DragAnything, ImageConductor) and adapted zero-shot baselines (FreeTraj, MOFT, DragDiffusion), with all videos resized to 320×576 for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics will include Frechet Inception Distance (FID) and Frechet Video Distance (FVD) for visual quality, and ObjMC for motion fidelity, where ObjMC measures the average distance between generated and target trajectories using Co-Tracker. Ablation studies will examine the effects of feature map selection, U-Net layer choice, learning rate, denoising timestep, and post-processing cut-off frequency.
bd0431d8a5ec2ef9f66c26f3fa7b14ebd01435b3.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the first zero-shot, self-guided approach for trajectory control in image-to-video generation, requiring no fine-tuning or external annotated data. Key innovations include a novel feature alignment procedure for self-attention layers in video diffusion models, enabling precise motion control via latent optimization, and a frequency-based post-processing technique to maintain visual fidelity. The method supports arbitrary input images and multiple objects or regions, unifying object and camera motion control. Extensive analysis and experiments demonstrate superior performance over zero-shot baselines and competitive results with supervised methods, while maintaining high-resolution output and general applicability.

bd04e8b6d726bdfa51f4d10b9c6693075c99afee.title: Rosetta Neurons: Mining the Common Units in a Model Zoo
bd04e8b6d726bdfa51f4d10b9c6693075c99afee.research_question: Do different neural network models trained for various vision tasks and with different architectures share common internal representations, and can these shared units be systematically identified and utilized for cross-model translation and manipulation without supervision or manual annotation?
bd04e8b6d726bdfa51f4d10b9c6693075c99afee.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that certain visual concepts and structures are inherently embedded in the natural world and can be learned by different neural network models, regardless of their specific task, architecture, or type of supervision, resulting in the existence of common units—termed 'Rosetta Neurons'—across diverse models.
bd04e8b6d726bdfa51f4d10b9c6693075c99afee.proposed_method: A comprehensive algorithm will be developed to mine a dictionary of 'Rosetta Neurons' across a diverse set of vision models, including both generative and discriminative architectures. The method involves extracting activation maps from multiple models using a shared dataset, normalizing these activations, and computing pairwise correlations to identify units with highly correlated responses across models. Mutual nearest neighbor filtering ('best buddies') is applied to ensure reliable matches, and clustering is used to group synonymous units expressing the same concept. The approach is designed to be annotation-free, leveraging only the natural emergence of shared concepts in the data, and includes a novel inversion technique to visualize and manipulate these shared units within generative models.
bd04e8b6d726bdfa51f4d10b9c6693075c99afee.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a model zoo consisting of eight popular vision models: StyleGAN2, StyleGAN-XL, BigGAN (generative), and ResNet50, DINO-ResNet50, DINO-ViT, MAE, CLIP-ResNet50 (discriminative/self-supervised/text-supervised). All models will be evaluated on the same datasets, primarily ImageNet and LSUN, to ensure comparability. Baselines will include standard inversion techniques and perceptual loss-based methods. Evaluation metrics will include PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS for image inversion quality, as well as qualitative assessments of concept emergence and manipulation capability. The experimental setup will also include cross-model translation tasks, out-of-distribution inversions, and fine-grained editing to demonstrate the utility and robustness of the mined Rosetta Neurons.
bd04e8b6d726bdfa51f4d10b9c6693075c99afee.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a novel, annotation-free framework for mining and visualizing common units—Rosetta Neurons—across a wide range of vision models with different architectures and training regimes. Unlike previous approaches, this method does not require semantic labels or specialized training, and it enables direct model-to-model translation, bridging generative and discriminative representations. The approach allows for a lightweight, flexible inversion and editing process that can perform cross-domain and out-of-distribution manipulations, offering new insights into the shared structure of deep neural networks and facilitating advanced generative tasks.

bd0fae435b93819d407f36d9d52565d5dfb5f87c.title: MiniCPM-V: A GPT-4V Level MLLM on Your Phone
bd0fae435b93819d407f36d9d52565d5dfb5f87c.research_question: How can a multimodal large language model (MLLM) be designed to achieve state-of-the-art performance comparable to leading models like GPT-4V, while being efficiently deployable on resource-constrained end-side devices such as mobile phones, and supporting high-resolution visual understanding, trustworthy behavior, and multilingual capabilities?
bd0fae435b93819d407f36d9d52565d5dfb5f87c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by integrating advanced architectural innovations, adaptive visual encoding, efficient training and alignment strategies, and specialized deployment optimizations, it is possible to develop an MLLM that matches or surpasses GPT-4V-level performance, supports high-resolution and multilingual tasks, and can be deployed efficiently on mobile and other end-side devices.
bd0fae435b93819d407f36d9d52565d5dfb5f87c.proposed_method: The proposed approach involves constructing an MLLM with a modular architecture consisting of a visual encoder (SigLIP-SoViT-400m/14), a shared compression layer using a perceiver resampler with cross-attention, and a large language model (LLM) backbone. Adaptive visual encoding is employed to partition high-resolution images into slices that match the visual encoder’s pre-training distribution, with 2D positional embedding interpolation to maintain spatial fidelity. Token compression reduces the number of visual tokens for efficiency, and a spatial schema is introduced to encode slice positions. The training pipeline includes a three-stage pre-training process (warming up the compression layer, extending input resolution, and adaptive high-res training with OCR data), followed by supervised fine-tuning on high-quality multimodal datasets, and hallucination reduction via RLAIF-V, which uses scalable AI feedback and direct preference optimization. Multilingual generalization is achieved by leveraging a strong multilingual LLM pivot and lightweight instruction tuning.
bd0fae435b93819d407f36d9d52565d5dfb5f87c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a comprehensive suite of 11 popular multimodal benchmarks aggregated under the OpenCompass evaluation, including tasks for visual question answering, OCR, reasoning, grounding, and multilingual interaction. Pre-training utilizes large-scale image-text pairs from datasets such as COCO, VG, CC3M, CC12M, LAION-2B, and specialized OCR datasets in English and Chinese. Supervised fine-tuning leverages high-quality datasets like VQAv2, DocVQA, TextVQA, and others, with additional multilingual data spanning over 30 languages. Baseline comparisons will include leading MLLMs such as GPT-4V-1106, Gemini Pro, Claude 3, Qwen-VL, and others. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on VQA/OCR tasks, hallucination rates (e.g., on ObjectHalBench), multilingual performance, and deployment efficiency metrics such as memory usage, inference speed, and latency on various mobile devices using quantized models.
bd0fae435b93819d407f36d9d52565d5dfb5f87c.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a novel MLLM framework that achieves GPT-4V-level performance with significantly reduced model size, enabling efficient deployment on mobile phones and other end-side devices. Key innovations include adaptive high-resolution visual encoding for arbitrary aspect ratios, a highly efficient token compression strategy, scalable hallucination reduction via RLAIF-V with open-source AI feedback, and a multilingual generalization strategy that minimizes reliance on multimodal data in low-resource languages. The approach demonstrates state-of-the-art results on comprehensive multimodal benchmarks and sets a new standard for practical, trustworthy, and multilingual MLLMs on resource-constrained devices.

bd1331b233e84bab7eba503abc60b31ac08e7881.title: Beyond the Imitation Game: Quantifying and extrapolating the capabilities of language models
bd1331b233e84bab7eba503abc60b31ac08e7881.research_question: How can the capabilities and limitations of large language models be comprehensively evaluated and extrapolated, particularly as models increase in scale, across a diverse set of challenging tasks that go beyond current benchmarks?
bd1331b233e84bab7eba503abc60b31ac08e7881.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a large-scale, diverse benchmark containing tasks beyond the reach of current language models will reveal both quantitative improvements and qualitative breakthroughs as model scale increases, and that such a benchmark will enable more accurate characterization and prediction of language model capabilities and limitations.
bd1331b233e84bab7eba503abc60b31ac08e7881.proposed_method: A comprehensive benchmark, named Beyond the Imitation Game benchmark (BIG-bench), will be constructed to include over 200 tasks spanning diverse domains such as linguistics, mathematics, reasoning, science, social bias, software development, and more. Tasks will be designed to be unsolvable by current models and will include both JSON-based and programmatic formats, allowing for zero- and few-shot evaluation. The benchmark will be openly developed, with contributions from a wide range of experts, and will include a lightweight subset (BIG-bench Lite) for efficient evaluation. A standardized API will facilitate model interaction and performance measurement, supporting a variety of metrics including accuracy, calibration, and custom task-specific scores.
bd1331b233e84bab7eba503abc60b31ac08e7881.experiment_details: Experiments will involve evaluating multiple large language models, including dense and sparse transformer architectures (such as OpenAI's GPT-3 series, Google's BIG-G, and Switch-style sparse transformers), across a range of parameter scales from millions to hundreds of billions. Each model will be tested on all BIG-bench tasks using consistent inference settings (e.g., greedy decoding, zero temperature), and results will be compared to a strong human expert baseline, where raters are allowed to use all available resources. Evaluation metrics will include exact string match, multiple choice accuracy, calibration error, and others as appropriate for each task. Aggregate and per-task performance will be analyzed, with particular attention to scaling trends, breakthrough behaviors, and areas where models lag behind human performance.
bd1331b233e84bab7eba503abc60b31ac08e7881.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces an unprecedented breadth and difficulty of evaluation for language models, targeting tasks believed to be beyond current model capabilities and enabling the detection of both gradual and breakthrough improvements as models scale. The methodology includes a novel open contribution process, expert human baselines, and a focus on extrapolating future model capabilities. The benchmark is designed to remain relevant as models improve, overcoming the short lifespans and narrow focus of existing benchmarks. Additionally, the inclusion of both JSON and programmatic tasks allows for flexible and comprehensive assessment of model abilities, including multi-step reasoning and dialog.

bd1aef9b9c1a96d110659c154cf942ecb5f77a8c.title: Optimal error bounds for non-expansive fixed-point iterations in normed spaces
bd1aef9b9c1a96d110659c154cf942ecb5f77a8c.research_question: What are the optimal error bounds and convergence rates achievable by general Mann iterations for computing fixed points of non-expansive maps in normed spaces, and how can the choice of averaging parameters be optimized to minimize the worst-case fixed-point residual after a finite number of iterations?
bd1aef9b9c1a96d110659c154cf942ecb5f77a8c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, by formulating and solving an optimization problem over the averaging parameters of Mann iterations, it is possible to attain the smallest possible worst-case fixed-point residual, and that the optimal convergence rate for such iterations is O(1/n), which is tight and cannot be improved for general non-expansive maps.
bd1aef9b9c1a96d110659c154cf942ecb5f77a8c.proposed_method: A general framework will be developed for optimizing the averaging parameters in Mann fixed-point iterations applied to non-expansive maps on normed spaces. The approach formulates the minimization of the worst-case fixed-point residual as a nested sequence of optimal transport problems, allowing the derivation of universal, tight error bounds that depend only on the choice of averaging coefficients. Both fixed-horizon and sequential optimization strategies will be explored: the former solves a global non-convex optimization problem for a pre-specified number of iterations, while the latter incrementally optimizes each new averaging parameter based on previous choices and computed distances. Additional structural constraints, such as monotonicity of the averaging sequence, will be incorporated to simplify computation and enable explicit greedy algorithms for special cases like Halpern and Krasnosel’skiı-Mann iterations. Analytical and numerical techniques will be used to identify optimal or near-optimal parameter sequences and to establish the tightness of the resulting error bounds.
bd1aef9b9c1a96d110659c154cf942ecb5f77a8c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of non-expansive maps defined on normed spaces, with the diameter of the domain normalized to one. The performance of the proposed optimized Mann iterations will be evaluated in terms of the fixed-point residual norm after n steps, compared to classical iterations such as Halpern and Krasnosel’skiı-Mann with standard and optimized stepsizes. Numerical optimization of the averaging coefficients will be performed using state-of-the-art solvers (e.g., Knitro, Baron, CPLEX, Gurobi), and the resulting rates and residuals will be benchmarked against known theoretical lower bounds and previous best-known results. Both synthetic linear and affine non-expansive maps and more general cases will be considered. Evaluation metrics include the worst-case residual norm, convergence rate (as a function of n), and tightness of the derived bounds.
bd1aef9b9c1a96d110659c154cf942ecb5f77a8c.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a universal and tight optimal transport-based framework for deriving error bounds for general Mann iterations, applicable to all non-expansive maps in normed spaces. The methodology enables the explicit optimization of averaging parameters to achieve the best possible convergence rates, establishing that O(1/n) is the optimal rate for such iterations. Analytical characterization of optimal stepsizes for Halpern iterations and the demonstration that classical and certain parameterized variants attain these optimal rates are provided. The work also proves that for Krasnosel’skiı-Mann iterations, the best achievable rate is O(1/sqrt(n)), and shows that even extended variants cannot surpass this rate. The approach unifies and generalizes previous results, offering both theoretical guarantees and practical algorithms for optimal fixed-point iteration design.

bd206d206e78b90c9d4b7ccc0d3b57e051075e9a.title: Compositional Abilities Emerge Multiplicatively: Exploring Diffusion Models on a Synthetic Task
bd206d206e78b90c9d4b7ccc0d3b57e051075e9a.research_question: How do conditional diffusion models acquire compositional generalization abilities, and what are the data-centric factors and learning dynamics that govern the emergence and failure of these capabilities in generative models?
bd206d206e78b90c9d4b7ccc0d3b57e051075e9a.hypothesis: Compositional generalization abilities in conditional diffusion models emerge multiplicatively, such that the ability to generate novel combinations of concepts depends on the concurrent acquisition of all underlying atomic capabilities. The emergence of these abilities is governed by the structure of the data-generating process, the frequency of concept occurrence in the training data, and the concept distance from the training set. Furthermore, there exists a critical threshold of data frequency required for a model to learn and compose certain concepts, and fine-tuning alone is insufficient to remedy misgeneralizations arising from adversarial data configurations.
bd206d206e78b90c9d4b7ccc0d3b57e051075e9a.proposed_method: A minimalistic and interpretable synthetic framework, termed 'concept graphs,' will be developed to systematically study compositional generalization in conditional diffusion models. The method involves defining concept variables (e.g., shape, color, size) and constructing datasets where images are paired with tuples denoting specific combinations of these variables. The diffusion models will be conditioned on these tuples, and the training data will be carefully controlled to include or exclude certain concept combinations, as well as to vary the frequency of specific concepts. The learning dynamics of the models will be analyzed by monitoring their ability to generate images corresponding to both seen and novel (out-of-distribution) concept combinations. The framework will also allow for adversarial setups and fine-tuning experiments to probe failure modes and the limits of compositional generalization.
bd206d206e78b90c9d4b7ccc0d3b57e051075e9a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using synthetic datasets constructed from three concept variables (shape, color, size), each with two possible values, resulting in a set of concept classes organized as nodes in a concept graph. The diffusion models will be trained on subsets of these nodes, with systematic variation in the frequency of certain concept classes to study the impact on generalization. Evaluation will be performed using linear classifier probes trained to predict each concept variable from generated images, with compositional accuracy defined as the product of probe accuracies. Baselines will include random classifiers and additive versus multiplicative accuracy measures. Additional experiments will be conducted on the CelebA dataset, using real-world attributes (gender, smiling, hair color) to validate findings at larger scale. Fine-tuning experiments will be performed to assess whether downstream adaptation can recover from misgeneralizations induced by adversarial data splits.
bd206d206e78b90c9d4b7ccc0d3b57e051075e9a.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a minimalistic, interpretable synthetic framework ('concept graphs') for systematically studying compositional generalization in diffusion models, enabling controlled interventions and mechanistic hypothesis testing. It claims to be the first to demonstrate perfect compositional generalization on a synthetic vision problem and to characterize the multiplicative emergence of compositional abilities, providing a data-centric explanation for emergent phenomena in generative models. The work also identifies critical data frequency thresholds for learning specific capabilities and demonstrates that fine-tuning is generally insufficient to address misgeneralizations, thus uncovering novel failure modes and providing actionable insights for dataset design and model reliability.

bd38cbbb346a347cb5b60ac4a133b3d73cb44e07.title: Efficient Online Reinforcement Learning with Offline Data
bd38cbbb346a347cb5b60ac4a133b3d73cb44e07.research_question: How can online reinforcement learning algorithms effectively leverage offline data, such as expert demonstrations or sub-optimal trajectories, to improve sample efficiency and exploration without requiring extensive modifications, pre-training, or explicit behavioral constraints?
bd38cbbb346a347cb5b60ac4a133b3d73cb44e07.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a minimal set of targeted modifications to existing off-policy RL algorithms—specifically, balanced sampling of offline and online data, critic regularization via Layer Normalization, and large ensemble critics—enables reliable and efficient use of offline data during online RL, leading to improved performance across diverse environments without additional computational overhead.
bd38cbbb346a347cb5b60ac4a133b3d73cb44e07.proposed_method: A new framework, RLPD (Reinforcement Learning with Prior Data), is developed to integrate offline data directly into online off-policy RL training. The method employs 'symmetric sampling', where each training batch consists of 50% samples from the online replay buffer and 50% from the offline dataset, ensuring balanced exposure to both data sources. To prevent catastrophic value overestimation and stabilize training, Layer Normalization is applied to the critic networks, effectively bounding Q-value extrapolation for out-of-distribution actions. Additionally, large ensembles of critic networks are used to improve sample efficiency and regularization, with target Q-values computed via random ensemble distillation or by subsetting critics as appropriate for the environment. The approach is designed to be agnostic to the quality and quantity of offline data, requires no offline pre-training, and maintains the computational simplicity of standard off-policy RL algorithms.
bd38cbbb346a347cb5b60ac4a133b3d73cb44e07.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of 30 benchmark tasks, including D4RL AntMaze (sparse-reward navigation with sub-optimal trajectories), D4RL Locomotion (dense-reward tasks with varying data quality), and Adroit Sparse (dexterous manipulation with limited expert demonstrations). Additional experiments will target vision-based domains using V-D4RL, where only pixel observations are available. Baselines for comparison include canonical off-policy methods using offline data (e.g., SACfD), state-of-the-art offline-to-online RL approaches (e.g., IQL+Finetuning, Off2On), and behavior cloning. Evaluation metrics include normalized return, sample efficiency (performance vs. environment steps), and variance across multiple seeds (typically 10). Ablation studies will assess the impact of each design choice (sampling ratio, LayerNorm, ensemble size, critic regularization) and provide a workflow for adapting the method to new environments.
bd38cbbb346a347cb5b60ac4a133b3d73cb44e07.novelty_claims: The proposed approach claims to achieve state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of online RL tasks with offline data, surpassing prior methods by up to 2.5× in normalized return, while introducing only minimal and easily adoptable modifications to standard off-policy RL algorithms. The method is notable for its simplicity, lack of additional computational overhead, and generality across both sparse and dense reward settings, as well as pixel-based and proprioceptive tasks. Key innovations include the symmetric sampling strategy, the use of Layer Normalization in critics as a minimal yet effective regularizer against value overestimation, and the demonstration that large critic ensembles substantially improve sample efficiency. The proposal also provides a practical workflow for practitioners to tune environment-specific design choices, facilitating robust deployment across diverse domains.

bd3a0bbabae3260098e06bfb615147fb6d34e55a.title: Latent Plans for Task-Agnostic Offline Reinforcement Learning
bd3a0bbabae3260098e06bfb615147fb6d34e55a.research_question: How can task-agnostic, long-horizon robot control policies be learned from high-dimensional, unstructured, and offline datasets, enabling robots to solve complex sequential tasks without access to predefined task labels or expert demonstrations?
bd3a0bbabae3260098e06bfb615147fb6d34e55a.hypothesis: A hierarchical approach that combines imitation learning for low-level skill acquisition with offline reinforcement learning for high-level skill chaining can enable the learning of general-purpose, task-agnostic policies from unstructured play data, resulting in improved performance on long-horizon, multi-tier tasks compared to existing imitation learning and offline RL methods.
bd3a0bbabae3260098e06bfb615147fb6d34e55a.proposed_method: A hierarchical framework will be developed in which a low-level policy learns a continuous latent skill space via self-supervised imitation learning from unstructured play data, using a sequence-to-sequence conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) to encode and decode latent plans into motor actions. The high-level policy will operate in this latent plan space, learning to chain latent skills to achieve long-horizon goals through offline, goal-conditioned reinforcement learning. Hindsight relabeling will be used to augment transitions with sparse rewards, sampling both positive and hard negative goals to improve the informativeness of the reward signal. The high-level policy will be trained using Conservative Q-Learning (CQL), initialized from the prior learned by the low-level policy, and will leverage dynamic programming to sequence latent skills for complex tasks.
bd3a0bbabae3260098e06bfb615147fb6d34e55a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in both simulated and real-world environments, primarily using the CALVIN environment for simulation, which provides 6 hours of unstructured teleoperated play data with a 7-DoF Franka Emika Panda robot arm. Real-world experiments will use 9 hours of play data collected with the same robot and a VR controller, with additional gripper camera input to avoid occlusions. The proposed method will be compared against baselines including Play-supervised Latent Motor Plan (LMP) for imitation learning, Conservative Q-Learning with Hindsight Experience Replay (CQL+HER) for offline RL, and Relay Imitation Learning (RIL) for hierarchical learning. Evaluation metrics will include success rates on long-horizon multitask visual goal chains (LH-MTVis), sequential task completion, and generalization to unseen goal images, with both quantitative rollouts and qualitative demonstrations across 25 distinct manipulation tasks in the real world.
bd3a0bbabae3260098e06bfb615147fb6d34e55a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to explicitly target long-horizon, multi-tier, task-agnostic control from purely offline, unstructured play data without access to a model or predefined skills. By combining imitation learning for latent skill acquisition with offline RL for skill chaining in a unified, self-supervised hierarchical framework, the method enables general-purpose visuomotor agents to solve previously unseen combinations of skills and temporally extended goals. The approach demonstrates an order-of-magnitude improvement in performance over state-of-the-art baselines in both simulated and real-world settings, and is scalable to a single multi-task policy capable of 25 real-world manipulation tasks.

bd5deadc58ee45b5e004378ba1d54a96bc947b4a.title: FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation
bd5deadc58ee45b5e004378ba1d54a96bc947b4a.research_question: How can the factual precision of long-form text generated by large language models be evaluated in a fine-grained, scalable, and reliable manner, particularly when each generation may contain a mixture of true and false information?
bd5deadc58ee45b5e004378ba1d54a96bc947b4a.hypothesis: A fine-grained, atomic fact-based evaluation framework, combined with automated estimation using retrieval-augmented language models, can provide accurate and scalable assessment of factual precision in long-form text generation, closely approximating human evaluation.
bd5deadc58ee45b5e004378ba1d54a96bc947b4a.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces a novel evaluation metric, FACTSCORE, which decomposes long-form model-generated text into atomic facts—each representing a single, verifiable piece of information. For each atomic fact, a binary label is assigned based on whether it is supported by a trusted knowledge source (e.g., Wikipedia). The overall FACTSCORE is computed as the percentage of atomic facts in a generation that are supported by the knowledge source. To address the high cost and time of human annotation, an automated estimator is developed that first retrieves relevant passages from the knowledge source, then uses a strong language model to validate each atomic fact via zero-shot prompting or nonparametric probability methods. Ensemble approaches combine retrieval-based and nonparametric methods to further improve accuracy. The system is designed to be modular, allowing evaluation of any language model's generations at scale without manual effort.
bd5deadc58ee45b5e004378ba1d54a96bc947b4a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the task of generating people biographies, as these are objective and well-covered in Wikipedia. Three state-of-the-art commercial language models (InstructGPT, ChatGPT, and PerplexityAI) will be evaluated using extensive human annotation to establish ground-truth FACTSCOREs. The automated estimator will then be validated against this human-annotated dataset, measuring error rates and ranking consistency. Subsequently, the automated FACTSCORE estimator will be applied to a large-scale evaluation of 6,500 generations from 13 recent language models, including both closed and open-source systems. Evaluation metrics will include the FACTSCORE itself, error rate compared to human annotation, and preservation of model ranking. Additional analyses will assess the impact of entity rarity, position of facts within generations, and model size on factual precision.
bd5deadc58ee45b5e004378ba1d54a96bc947b4a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a fine-grained, atomic fact-based metric for factual precision that overcomes the limitations of sentence-level or binary evaluations. It provides the first scalable, automated estimator for this metric, achieving less than 2% error compared to human annotation. The methodology enables large-scale, cost-effective evaluation of long-form factuality across a diverse set of language models, and reveals new insights into the factual performance of both commercial and public models. The FACTSCORE framework and annotated data will be open-sourced for community use, facilitating further research and benchmarking.

bd5f550743126c050fb7d891c8b2b0b6aba266bc.title: FedADMM: A federated primal-dual algorithm allowing partial participation
bd5f550743126c050fb7d891c8b2b0b6aba266bc.research_question: How can federated learning algorithms be designed to efficiently solve non-convex composite optimization problems with non-smooth regularizers, while allowing for partial client participation and accommodating both statistical and system heterogeneity?
bd5f550743126c050fb7d891c8b2b0b6aba266bc.hypothesis: A federated primal-dual algorithm based on the ADMM framework, when applied to the dual of the composite optimization problem, will enable partial client participation, provide convergence guarantees for non-convex and non-smooth objectives, and handle heterogeneity in federated learning settings.
bd5f550743126c050fb7d891c8b2b0b6aba266bc.proposed_method: A new federated optimization algorithm, FedADMM, will be developed by applying a primal-dual approach using the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) to the dual formulation of the federated composite optimization problem. The method will allow only a subset of clients to participate in each communication round, selected via a proper random sampling scheme, ensuring that every client has a nonzero probability of selection. Each participating client will perform local updates by approximately minimizing an augmented Lagrangian involving its local objective and a global consensus variable, followed by a dual variable update. The server will aggregate updates from participating clients, apply a proximal mapping for the global model, and broadcast the updated global variable back to the selected clients. The algorithm will support inexact computation of proximal steps to accommodate limited client resources.
bd5f550743126c050fb7d891c8b2b0b6aba266bc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on federated learning benchmarks involving non-convex and non-smooth objectives, with heterogeneous and non-i.i.d. data distributions across clients. The evaluation will compare FedADMM against state-of-the-art federated optimization baselines such as FedAvg, FedProx, FedDR, and FedPD. Metrics will include convergence rate, communication efficiency, and final model accuracy. The experimental setup will vary the degree of client participation, the level of data heterogeneity, and the presence of non-smooth regularizers to assess robustness and scalability.
bd5f550743126c050fb7d891c8b2b0b6aba266bc.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a federated primal-dual algorithm that enables partial client participation for non-convex composite optimization with non-smooth regularizers, a capability not present in existing primal-dual federated methods. The approach establishes a theoretical equivalence between the proposed FedADMM and existing Douglas-Rachford-based algorithms, extending convergence guarantees to a broader class of problems and participation models. The method supports inexact local computations and generalizes to constrained and non-smooth settings, thereby broadening the applicability of federated optimization in practical, heterogeneous environments.

bd7237ad2db9786beffbe59bdfb06432da2adc1d.title: Moral Alignment for LLM Agents
bd7237ad2db9786beffbe59bdfb06432da2adc1d.research_question: How can decision-making agents based on large language models (LLMs) be aligned with explicit human moral values in a transparent and effective manner, and to what extent can such alignment generalize across different environments and tasks?
bd7237ad2db9786beffbe59bdfb06432da2adc1d.hypothesis: Explicitly encoding core human moral values as intrinsic rewards during reinforcement learning-based fine-tuning will enable LLM agents to reliably adopt and generalize moral strategies, outperforming or complementing existing alignment approaches that rely on implicit human preference data.
bd7237ad2db9786beffbe59bdfb06432da2adc1d.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed for aligning LLM agents to human moral values by designing and implementing intrinsic reward functions that explicitly encode deontological and utilitarian moral principles. The approach will involve fine-tuning instruction-tuned LLMs (specifically, Gemma2-2b-it) using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) in repeated social dilemma environments such as the Iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma (IPD). The reward functions will be carefully crafted to represent (1) selfish/game-theoretic payoffs, (2) deontological penalties for violating moral norms (e.g., defecting against a cooperator), (3) utilitarian collective welfare, and (4) multi-objective combinations. Fine-tuning will be conducted via structured prompts that abstract away explicit references to the IPD, using unique action tokens to avoid memorization and encourage generalization. The methodology will also include mechanisms for penalizing illegal actions and for testing the ability of agents to 'unlearn' previously acquired selfish strategies through subsequent moral fine-tuning.
bd7237ad2db9786beffbe59bdfb06432da2adc1d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Gemma2-2b-it LLM, fine-tuned with PPO on the IPD environment against both fixed-strategy (Tit-for-Tat, Always Cooperate, Always Defect, Random) and learning (LLM-based) opponents. Training will be performed for 1000 episodes with batch sizes of 3–5, leveraging 4-bit quantization and LoRA for computational efficiency. Evaluation will focus on the learning dynamics of moral strategies, the ability to unlearn selfish behavior, and the generalization of learned moral policies to other matrix games (Iterated Stag Hunt, Chicken, Bach-or-Stravinsky, Defective Coordination) using novel action tokens. Baselines will include models fine-tuned with standard game rewards and without fine-tuning. Performance will be assessed using metrics such as action choice distributions, moral regret (difference between optimal and actual moral reward), and the consistency of moral behavior across environments. Additional analyses will test the impact of fine-tuning on unrelated prompts and prompt variations.
bd7237ad2db9786beffbe59bdfb06432da2adc1d.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a transparent, explicit, and generalizable method for moral alignment of LLM agents by leveraging intrinsic reward functions grounded in moral philosophy, rather than relying on implicit human preference data. The approach enables both the learning and unlearning of moral strategies, demonstrates generalization across diverse environments, and provides a cost-effective and interpretable alternative to prevailing alignment techniques such as RLHF and DPO. The methodology also supports multi-objective and pluralistic alignment, paving the way for more robust and adaptable AI agents.

bdb68c5e2369633b20e733774ac66eb4600c34d1.title: LLM-Adapters: An Adapter Family for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models
bdb68c5e2369633b20e733774ac66eb4600c34d1.research_question: How can parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods, specifically adapter-based approaches, be optimally integrated into large language models (LLMs) to maximize performance across diverse reasoning tasks, and what are the effects of adapter type, placement, and configuration on downstream task performance in both in-distribution and out-of-distribution scenarios?
bdb68c5e2369633b20e733774ac66eb4600c34d1.hypothesis: Adapter-based parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods, when optimally configured and placed within open-access LLMs, can enable smaller models to achieve comparable or even superior performance to much larger models on specific reasoning tasks, while requiring significantly fewer trainable parameters.
bdb68c5e2369633b20e733774ac66eb4600c34d1.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical study will be conducted on a suite of adapter-based PEFT methods, including Series Adapters, Parallel Adapters, LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation), and Prefix-Tuning, integrated into representative open-source LLMs such as LLaMA, BLOOM, and GPT-J. The study will systematically evaluate the impact of adapter type, placement (e.g., after MLP layers, after Attention layers, or both), and key hyperparameters (e.g., bottleneck size, LoRA rank, number of virtual tokens) on performance. A unified, user-friendly framework called LLM-Adapter will be developed to facilitate seamless integration and experimentation with these adapters. The methodology will include constructing high-quality, task-specific fine-tuning datasets for arithmetic and commonsense reasoning, leveraging both existing datasets and synthetic data generated via teacher models (e.g., ChatGPT with chain-of-thought prompting). Fine-tuning will be performed on these datasets, followed by extensive evaluation across multiple benchmarks.
bdb68c5e2369633b20e733774ac66eb4600c34d1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on fourteen benchmark datasets spanning arithmetic reasoning (e.g., GSM8K, SVAMP, MultiArith, AddSub, AQuA, SingleEq) and commonsense reasoning (e.g., BoolQ, PIQA, SIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-e, ARC-c, OBQA). For each adapter type and configuration, models will be fine-tuned on curated training sets (Math10K for arithmetic, Commonsense170K for commonsense) and evaluated on all relevant datasets. Baselines will include zero-shot chain-of-thought prompting with large proprietary models such as GPT-3.5 and ChatGPT. Evaluation metrics will primarily be accuracy on each dataset. Experimental setup will control for batch size, learning rate, and number of epochs, with systematic variation of adapter-specific hyperparameters. Both in-distribution (ID) and out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios will be analyzed to assess generalization.
bdb68c5e2369633b20e733774ac66eb4600c34d1.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a unified, extensible framework (LLM-Adapter) for integrating and benchmarking a wide range of adapter-based PEFT methods in open-source LLMs. It provides the first comprehensive empirical comparison of adapter types, placements, and configurations across multiple LLMs and reasoning tasks. The study will generate and release high-quality, task-specific fine-tuning datasets for both arithmetic and commonsense reasoning, enabling reproducible research. The work aims to demonstrate that, with optimal PEFT strategies, smaller LLMs can match or exceed the performance of much larger models on targeted tasks, thus democratizing access to high-performing language models.

bdba3bd30a49ea4c5b20b43dbd8f0eb59e9d80e2.title: Diffusion policy: Visuomotor policy learning via action diffusion
bdba3bd30a49ea4c5b20b43dbd8f0eb59e9d80e2.research_question: How can robot visuomotor policy learning be improved to handle multimodal action distributions, high-dimensional action spaces, and achieve stable, high-performance behavior across a wide range of complex manipulation tasks?
bdba3bd30a49ea4c5b20b43dbd8f0eb59e9d80e2.hypothesis: Representing robot visuomotor policies as conditional denoising diffusion processes will enable more expressive, robust, and stable policy learning, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods, especially in scenarios requiring multimodal action distributions and high-dimensional action sequences.
bdba3bd30a49ea4c5b20b43dbd8f0eb59e9d80e2.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that formulates visuomotor robot policies as Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPMs), where the policy generates action sequences via a conditional denoising process conditioned on visual observations. The method will incorporate receding-horizon control to enable closed-loop, temporally consistent action sequences, and will utilize a vision-conditioned diffusion process to efficiently extract and use visual features for real-time inference. Two neural architectures will be explored: a CNN-based backbone with FiLM conditioning for most tasks, and a transformer-based time-series diffusion model to address tasks requiring high-frequency action changes. The visual encoder will be trained end-to-end, with architectural ablations including ResNet and ViT variants, and the noise schedule will be tuned for optimal performance in control tasks. Inference acceleration techniques such as DDIM will be employed to ensure real-time control capability.
bdba3bd30a49ea4c5b20b43dbd8f0eb59e9d80e2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across 15 tasks from 4 major robot manipulation benchmarks, including both simulated and real-world environments, with tasks spanning 2DoF to 6DoF actions, single- and multi-task settings, and both rigid and fluid objects. Datasets will include human and multi-human demonstrations, with both state-based and vision-based observations. Baselines for comparison will include LSTM-GMM (BC-RNN), BET, and IBC, each evaluated with their optimal action space (typically velocity control), while the proposed method will leverage position control where advantageous. Evaluation metrics will primarily be task success rate and target coverage (e.g., IoU for manipulation tasks), with extensive ablation studies on network architecture, visual encoder design, action horizon, and robustness to latency and perturbations. Real-world experiments will cover multi-stage tasks, 6DoF manipulation, and non-rigid object handling, with performance measured against human-level benchmarks.
bdba3bd30a49ea4c5b20b43dbd8f0eb59e9d80e2.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first application of conditional denoising diffusion models to robot visuomotor policy learning, enabling expressive modeling of multimodal action distributions and stable training without the need for negative sampling or intractable normalization. Key innovations include the integration of receding-horizon control with diffusion-based action sequence generation, a vision-conditioned diffusion process for efficient and real-time inference, and a novel time-series diffusion transformer architecture for high-frequency action tasks. The method claims significant empirical improvements over state-of-the-art baselines, with an average success-rate improvement of 46.9% across benchmarks, and demonstrates robustness to latency, perturbations, and complex real-world scenarios.

bdbaf59d78a17db9bca840958f865f680aab0447.title: Randomized Dimensionality Reduction for Facility Location and Single-Linkage Clustering
bdbaf59d78a17db9bca840958f865f680aab0447.research_question: How can randomized dimensionality reduction be leveraged to accelerate and improve the scalability of clustering algorithms, specifically for facility location and single-linkage hierarchical clustering (minimum spanning tree), in high-dimensional spaces without sacrificing solution quality? What are the theoretical and empirical trade-offs between projected dimension, intrinsic data dimensionality, and clustering accuracy for these problems?
bdbaf59d78a17db9bca840958f865f680aab0447.hypothesis: Random projections into a subspace whose dimension depends primarily on the intrinsic (doubling) dimension of the data, rather than the ambient dimension or the number of clusters, can preserve the cost and solution quality of facility location and minimum spanning tree clustering problems up to a constant or arbitrarily small factor, while significantly reducing computational requirements.
bdbaf59d78a17db9bca840958f865f680aab0447.proposed_method: A framework is developed that applies random projections to reduce the dimensionality of input datasets prior to solving facility location and single-linkage clustering problems. The projection dimension is set proportional to the doubling dimension of the data, ensuring that the intrinsic structure is preserved. For facility location, both the cost of the optimal solution and the quality of locally optimal solutions are analyzed after projection, using geometric properties and concentration inequalities. For minimum spanning tree clustering, the method ensures that the cost and structure of the MST are preserved within a (1+ε) factor for any ε > 0, with the required projection dimension depending logarithmically on the inverse of ε and the doubling dimension. The approach also extends to facility location with squared distance costs. Theoretical guarantees are established for both cost preservation and solution quality, and lower bounds are provided to show the necessity of the chosen projection dimensions and optimality conditions.
bdbaf59d78a17db9bca840958f865f680aab0447.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on real-world high-dimensional datasets, including a Faces dataset (4096 dimensions) and a subset of the MNIST dataset (784 dimensions, digit '2'), as well as synthetic datasets with varying doubling dimensions. For facility location, random projections are applied to reduce the dimension, and clustering is performed using the Mettu-Plaxton algorithm with varying numbers of facilities opened. The cost of solutions found in the projected space is compared to those found in the original space, and runtime improvements are measured. For minimum spanning tree clustering, the cost of the MST found in the projected space (evaluated in the original space) is compared to the true MST, and the computational speedup is recorded. Additional experiments compare the effect of low versus high doubling dimension on the required projection dimension for accurate MST recovery. All results are averaged over multiple trials, and the evaluation metrics include cost ratios and runtime.
bdbaf59d78a17db9bca840958f865f680aab0447.novelty_claims: The proposed approach establishes that the dimension required for accurate clustering via random projection depends only on the intrinsic doubling dimension of the data, not on the number of clusters, which contrasts with previous results for k-means and k-medians. The method provides both theoretical and empirical guarantees for preserving the cost and solution quality of facility location and MST clustering under dimensionality reduction, including for locally optimal solutions. It introduces new lower bounds demonstrating the necessity of the projection dimension and optimality assumptions, and shows that these results do not extend to k-means or k-medians even for low doubling dimension. The approach yields significant computational speedups with minimal loss in clustering accuracy, validated on real and synthetic datasets.

bdc779d003c0ba0d0425a4b9d8b475da2705b11d.title: PARM: Multi-Objective Test-Time Alignment via Preference-Aware Autoregressive Reward Model
bdc779d003c0ba0d0425a4b9d8b475da2705b11d.research_question: How can large language models (LLMs) be efficiently and effectively aligned at test-time to diverse, multi-dimensional user preferences without retraining or fine-tuning the base model, and how can trade-offs between conflicting objectives be dynamically managed during inference?
bdc779d003c0ba0d0425a4b9d8b475da2705b11d.hypothesis: A single, unified autoregressive reward model (ARM) conditioned on user preference vectors and trained using a preference-aware bilinear low-rank adaptation (PBLoRA) can achieve efficient, precise, and scalable multi-objective test-time alignment for frozen LLMs, outperforming existing methods in terms of alignment quality, inference efficiency, and flexibility.
bdc779d003c0ba0d0425a4b9d8b475da2705b11d.proposed_method: A unified autoregressive reward model (ARM), termed Preference-Aware ARM (PARM), will be jointly trained across all preference dimensions, enabling dynamic adjustment to user-specified trade-offs at inference. The ARM will be conditioned on low-dimensional user preference vectors using a novel Preference-Aware Bilinear Low-Rank Adaptation (PBLoRA), which introduces a bilinear form where a preference-conditioned weight matrix modulates low-rank adaptation matrices. PBLoRA splits adaptation into preference-agnostic and preference-aware components, allowing shared and objective-specific features to be learned efficiently. During training, preference vectors are sampled from a simplex, and the ARM is optimized using a linear scalarization of multi-objective losses, ensuring coverage of the Pareto front. At inference, the trained PARM guides the frozen LLM's generation by providing token-level rewards aligned with the specified preference vector, enabling precise and computationally efficient alignment.
bdc779d003c0ba0d0425a4b9d8b475da2705b11d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multi-objective alignment tasks, including safety alignment (balancing helpfulness and harmlessness) using the PKU-SafeRLHF-10K dataset and helpful assistant tasks (helpfulness, harmlessness, humor) using the HH-RLHF dataset. Baselines will include Rewarded Soups, MOD, and GenARM, with all methods evaluated under frozen LLM settings. Evaluation metrics will include Hypervolume (HV) for Pareto front quality, Mean Inner Product (MIP) for preference alignment, and inference efficiency (time and parameter count). Models such as Alpaca-7B, Alpaca-65B, TinyLLaMA-1.1B-Chat, and LLaMA-2-7B-Chat will be used as base and reward models, with experiments including both standard and weak-to-strong (small-to-large model) guidance scenarios. Ablation studies will assess the impact of PBLoRA components and parameter configurations.
bdc779d003c0ba0d0425a4b9d8b475da2705b11d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a single, unified ARM for multi-objective test-time alignment, eliminating the need for multiple reward models and reducing inference cost. The Preference-Aware Bilinear Low-Rank Adaptation (PBLoRA) enables efficient and expressive conditioning on user preference vectors, surpassing the representational capacity of prior low-rank adaptation methods. The method allows for weak-to-strong guidance, where a small reward model can guide much larger frozen LLMs without retraining, making multi-objective alignment accessible under limited computational resources. Experiments are expected to demonstrate superior alignment quality, finer-grained preference control, and significant improvements in inference efficiency over existing methods.

bdeecc39d47eeb59f997b687af1b1a9347e14523.title: SurvSHAP(t): Time-dependent explanations of machine learning survival models
bdeecc39d47eeb59f997b687af1b1a9347e14523.research_question: How can time-dependent, model-agnostic explanations be developed for machine learning survival models to improve interpretability and variable importance assessment across the entire survival function?
bdeecc39d47eeb59f997b687af1b1a9347e14523.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a time-dependent extension of Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP), when applied to survival models, will provide accurate, interpretable, and locally faithful explanations of survival function predictions, outperforming existing methods such as SurvLIME in detecting time-dependent variable effects and ranking variable importance.
bdeecc39d47eeb59f997b687af1b1a9347e14523.proposed_method: A novel explanation framework, SurvSHAP(t), is proposed to generalize SHAP to survival models with functional outputs. For each observation and time point, SurvSHAP(t) computes Shapley value-based attributions for each predictor, quantifying their contribution to the predicted survival function at that time. Two estimation strategies are developed: (1) permutation-based Shapley sampling, where the marginal contribution of each variable is averaged over all possible orderings, and (2) a kernel-based approach using weighted linear regression with functional responses and Shapley kernel weights for computational efficiency. The method ensures local accuracy, missingness, and consistency properties, and allows aggregation of time-dependent attributions to yield variable importance scores. The approach is model-agnostic and can be applied to any survival model outputting a survival function.
bdeecc39d47eeb59f997b687af1b1a9347e14523.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world medical datasets. Synthetic datasets will be generated with known time-dependent and constant variable effects, enabling ground-truth validation. Models such as Cox Proportional Hazards (CPH) and Random Survival Forests (RSF) will be trained and explained. Evaluation metrics will include Brier score for model performance, local accuracy (normalized standard deviation of the difference between model output and explanation), Changing Sign Proportion (CSP) for detecting time-dependent effects, GT-Shapley (correlation with ground-truth Shapley values), and normalized RMSE for explanation fidelity. Comparisons will be made against SurvLIME and SurvLIME-KS baselines, using variable importance ranking correlation (additive hyperbolic Kendall’s tau) to assess ranking accuracy. Real-world validation will include use cases such as heart failure prediction, with all methods implemented in Python and code made publicly available.
bdeecc39d47eeb59f997b687af1b1a9347e14523.novelty_claims: SurvSHAP(t) is the first explanation method to provide time-dependent, model-agnostic variable attributions for survival models, directly explaining the survival function at each time point. The method preserves SHAP properties in the functional output setting, enables detection of variables with time-dependent effects, and offers superior aggregation for variable importance compared to existing approaches like SurvLIME. The framework is broadly applicable to all models with functional outputs and is accompanied by accessible, open-source implementation.

bdff213f0cb1d51d1e68b8e7ef75d74124ef124a.title: FreqPrior: Improving Video Diffusion Models with Frequency Filtering Gaussian Noise
bdff213f0cb1d51d1e68b8e7ef75d74124ef124a.research_question: How can the initialization of noise in video diffusion models be improved to enhance the quality and semantic fidelity of text-driven video generation, while maintaining computational efficiency?
bdff213f0cb1d51d1e68b8e7ef75d74124ef124a.hypothesis: A noise initialization strategy that refines Gaussian noise in the frequency domain using a tailored frequency filtering method will yield a noise prior that closely approximates a standard Gaussian distribution, thereby improving video generation quality and semantic consistency, and reducing inference time compared to existing approaches.
bdff213f0cb1d51d1e68b8e7ef75d74124ef124a.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a new noise prior, termed FreqPrior, for text-to-video diffusion models. The approach consists of three main stages: a partial sampling process, a diffusion process, and a noise refinement stage. Initially, Gaussian noise is sampled and partially diffused to an intermediate timestep, rather than the full diffusion trajectory, to save computation. In the noise refinement stage, two sets of noise are prepared to separately encode low-frequency and high-frequency information. A novel frequency filtering technique is applied in the frequency domain, where a low-pass filter is used for the low-frequency component and a modified high-pass filter (using the square root of the complement of the squared low-pass mask) is used for the high-frequency component, ensuring the resulting noise remains Gaussian. Both real and imaginary parts of the inverse Fourier transformed noise are retained in a symmetric formulation to preserve variance and information. This process is iterated to obtain a refined noise prior, which is then used as the initial latent for video generation.
bdff213f0cb1d51d1e68b8e7ef75d74124ef124a.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on three open-source text-to-video diffusion models: VideoCrafter, ModelScope, and AnimateDiff. The evaluation uses the VBench benchmark, which provides hierarchical and disentangled metrics closely aligned with human perception, including quality score, semantic score, and a weighted total score (all ranging from 0 to 100). Baselines include standard Gaussian noise, mixed noise, progressive noise, and FreeInit, with all methods evaluated under consistent settings (e.g., DDIM sampler, Butterworth low-pass filter with a normalized cutoff of 0.25, and two additional sampling iterations for prior-finding where applicable). For each noise prior, 4730 videos are generated for evaluation. Inference time, including both prior-finding and generation, is reported for all methods. Ablation studies are performed on key hyperparameters such as the ratio cosθ (controlling low-frequency retention) and the intermediate timestep t.
bdff213f0cb1d51d1e68b8e7ef75d74124ef124a.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel frequency filtering method specifically designed for Gaussian noise, rather than traditional signals, enabling the refined noise prior to maintain a distribution extremely close to standard Gaussian. The approach theoretically and empirically achieves negligible covariance error relative to standard Gaussian noise, addressing the variance decay issue found in prior frequency-based methods. The partial sampling process at an intermediate timestep significantly reduces inference time without compromising generation quality. The method is robust to hyperparameter choices and demonstrates superior performance across multiple state-of-the-art video diffusion models, achieving the highest scores on VBench and outperforming all baselines in both quality and efficiency.

be24ab597deeb00f9ee36a1434b36c3747483c28.title: No "Zero-Shot" Without Exponential Data: Pretraining Concept Frequency Determines Multimodal Model Performance
be24ab597deeb00f9ee36a1434b36c3747483c28.research_question: How does the frequency of downstream concepts in pretraining datasets influence the zero-shot performance of large-scale multimodal models across classification, retrieval, and generation tasks?
be24ab597deeb00f9ee36a1434b36c3747483c28.hypothesis: Zero-shot performance of multimodal models on downstream concepts is strongly determined by the frequency of those concepts in the pretraining data, such that linear improvements in performance require exponentially more pretraining samples for each concept.
be24ab597deeb00f9ee36a1434b36c3747483c28.proposed_method: A comprehensive analysis will be conducted to quantify the relationship between pretraining concept frequency and downstream zero-shot performance in multimodal models. First, a set of over 4,000 concepts will be compiled from 27 downstream evaluation datasets spanning classification, retrieval, and image generation tasks. For each concept, its frequency in several large-scale pretraining datasets (e.g., CC-3M, CC-12M, YFCC-15M, LAION-400M, LAION-Aesthetics) will be estimated using scalable text indexing and open-vocabulary image tagging (RAM++), followed by intersection to determine image-text matched frequencies. Multiple multimodal models, including both discriminative (CLIP variants) and generative (various T2I diffusion models), will be evaluated on downstream tasks, and their performance will be correlated with the log-scaled pretraining frequency of each concept. Additional analyses will control for sample-level similarity between pretraining and test data, and synthetic datasets with controlled concept distributions will be used to further test the robustness of the observed trends.
be24ab597deeb00f9ee36a1434b36c3747483c28.experiment_details: Experiments will involve 10 CLIP models and 24 text-to-image models, evaluated on 17 classification, 2 retrieval, and 8 generation downstream datasets. Pretraining datasets will include CC-3M, CC-12M, YFCC-15M, LAION-400M, and LAION-Aesthetics, with additional experiments on synthetic datasets such as SynthCI-30M. Evaluation metrics will include mean accuracy for classification, Recall@1/5/10 for retrieval, and both automated (CLIP-score, aesthetic score) and human-rated metrics for image generation. Prompting strategies will be varied, including class name, templated prompts, and prompt ensembles. The robustness of the frequency-performance relationship will be tested by removing pretraining samples similar to test data and by evaluating on a newly constructed long-tailed benchmark, 'Let It Wag!', which focuses on rare concepts. All experimental artifacts, including frequency indices and misalignment annotations, will be released publicly.
be24ab597deeb00f9ee36a1434b36c3747483c28.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a systematic, large-scale quantification of how pretraining concept frequency governs zero-shot performance in multimodal models, revealing a consistent log-linear scaling law across diverse architectures, tasks, and datasets. The methodology includes precise frequency estimation in both image and text modalities, quantification of image-text misalignment, and stress-testing with synthetic data and controlled similarity. A new long-tailed benchmark, 'Let It Wag!', is proposed to evaluate model generalization on rare concepts. The findings are expected to challenge prevailing assumptions about zero-shot generalization and highlight fundamental sample inefficiency in current multimodal foundation models.

be4156b6c5b804af6a20e5f723e521df6981b6fc.title: Antidote: Post-fine-tuning Safety Alignment for Large Language Models against Harmful Fine-tuning
be4156b6c5b804af6a20e5f723e521df6981b6fc.research_question: Can a post-fine-tuning defense mechanism be developed for large language models (LLMs) that is robust to harmful fine-tuning attacks and insensitive to fine-tuning hyper-parameters, while maintaining high performance on downstream tasks?
be4156b6c5b804af6a20e5f723e521df6981b6fc.hypothesis: A post-fine-tuning realignment method that identifies and prunes harmful parameters from a fine-tuned LLM can effectively reduce harmful outputs caused by malicious fine-tuning, regardless of the hyper-parameters used during fine-tuning, and can do so without significantly degrading performance on benign downstream tasks.
be4156b6c5b804af6a20e5f723e521df6981b6fc.proposed_method: A novel post-fine-tuning safety alignment framework, named Antidote, will be developed to mitigate harmful behaviors in LLMs induced by harmful fine-tuning attacks. The approach consists of a three-stage pipeline: (1) initial safety alignment using a curated alignment dataset, (2) user fine-tuning which may include harmful data, and (3) a post-fine-tuning one-shot pruning stage. In the pruning stage, the method will compute an importance score for each model parameter using the Wanda score, which combines parameter magnitude and activation statistics over a re-alignment dataset containing harmful prompts and responses. The top-k most important (i.e., harmful) parameters will be identified and pruned from the model by applying a binary mask, effectively deactivating their contribution. This process is designed to be agnostic to the fine-tuning hyper-parameters, such as learning rate and number of epochs, and aims to recover the model's safety alignment without retraining.
be4156b6c5b804af6a20e5f723e521df6981b6fc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple open-weight LLMs, including Llama2-7B, Mistral-7B, Gemma-7B, and Llama3-8B. The evaluation will use several downstream tasks (SST2, AGNEWS, GSM8K, AlpacaEval) and datasets for alignment, fine-tuning (with varying proportions of harmful data), and re-alignment (harmful-only data, e.g., BeaverTails). Baselines will include supervised fine-tuning (SFT), alignment-stage defenses (Vaccine, RepNoise), and fine-tuning-stage defenses (Lisa, LDIFS). Evaluation metrics will be Harmful Score (the proportion of unsafe outputs flagged by a moderation model) and Fine-tune Accuracy (Top-1 accuracy on downstream tasks). Experiments will systematically vary fine-tuning hyper-parameters (learning rate, epochs, sample size, harmful data ratio) to assess robustness. Additional analyses will include ablation studies on pruning mask ratio, size and composition of the re-alignment dataset, and system resource overhead.
be4156b6c5b804af6a20e5f723e521df6981b6fc.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a post-fine-tuning defense that is agnostic to fine-tuning hyper-parameters, addressing the hyper-parameter sensitivity issue found in prior alignment and fine-tuning-stage defenses. By leveraging a one-shot pruning mechanism based on importance scoring over a re-alignment dataset, the method can recover safety alignment even after strong harmful fine-tuning attacks. The approach is simple, efficient, and compatible with various LLM architectures and alignment datasets, and it demonstrates robust performance across a wide range of experimental conditions. This represents a significant advancement over existing defenses, which often fail under practical fine-tuning settings required for high downstream accuracy.

be431d20e27bafc584858bb76ba41b483cfd514b.title: Identifying Linear Relational Concepts in Large Language Models
be431d20e27bafc584858bb76ba41b483cfd514b.research_question: How can human-interpretable relational concepts be systematically identified as directions in the latent activation space of large language models, and how effective are these directions for classification and causal intervention tasks compared to standard probing methods?
be431d20e27bafc584858bb76ba41b483cfd514b.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that inverting a linear relational embedding (LRE) trained to map subject activations to object activations will yield concept directions—termed linear relational concepts (LRCs)—that more accurately correspond to human-interpretable concepts in model activations and outperform traditional probing classifiers in both classification accuracy and causal influence over model outputs.
be431d20e27bafc584858bb76ba41b483cfd514b.proposed_method: A novel approach is proposed to identify concept directions in the latent space of transformer language models by leveraging linear relational embeddings (LREs). First, for a given relation (e.g., 'located in'), a linear transformation is trained to map subject activations to object activations using a set of prompts and their corresponding model activations. Unlike prior work, the method averages all object token activations (not just the first token) and allows for the use of non-terminal model layers, improving performance on multi-token objects. The LRE is then inverted using a low-rank pseudo-inverse of the weight matrix, mapping object activations back to the subject space. The resulting vectors, termed linear relational concepts (LRCs), are normalized to unit length and represent concept directions in the subject activation space. These LRCs are used both as classifiers (via dot product with subject activations) and as intervention vectors to causally edit model outputs by adding or subtracting LRCs from subject activations at multiple layers.
be431d20e27bafc584858bb76ba41b483cfd514b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the LRE relations dataset, which contains over 10,000 instances across 47 relation types, categorized into factual, linguistic, commonsense, and bias relations. Two language models, Llama2-7b and GPT-J, will be evaluated. For each relation, a 50%/50% train/test split will be used, ensuring balanced representation of objects. Evaluation metrics include multi-class classification accuracy (using the LRC as a classifier) and causality (the ability of LRC-based interventions to shift model predictions to a counterfactual object). Baselines include a linear support vector machine (SVM) classifier and input averaging, as well as ablations using only the final object layer or first object token. Hyperparameters such as the rank of the pseudo-inverse and intervention scaling will be tuned, and results will be averaged over multiple random seeds. Performance will be analyzed for both single-token and multi-token objects, and the effect of object and subject layer selection will be systematically explored.
be431d20e27bafc584858bb76ba41b483cfd514b.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces several innovations: (1) the use of inverted LREs to derive concept directions (LRCs) that function as both classifiers and causal intervention vectors; (2) the extension of LREs to handle multi-token objects and non-terminal object layers, significantly improving performance over prior approaches; (3) empirical demonstration that LRCs outperform standard probing classifiers such as SVMs in both classification accuracy and causality across a broad set of relational concepts; and (4) systematic analysis of the impact of pseudo-inverse rank, layer selection, and training sample choice on the effectiveness of concept direction identification.

be48a321a638149a7f45297ccb1cf31eb6cf0263.title: TransRAC: Encoding Multi-scale Temporal Correlation with Transformers for Repetitive Action Counting
be48a321a638149a7f45297ccb1cf31eb6cf0263.research_question: How can repetitive action counting in videos be improved to handle long, realistic video scenarios with interruptions and inconsistencies, and how can model interpretability and generalization be enhanced through better data and algorithmic design?
be48a321a638149a7f45297ccb1cf31eb6cf0263.hypothesis: Encoding multi-scale temporal correlations with transformer-based architectures, combined with fine-grained period annotations and density map regression, will significantly improve the accuracy, interpretability, and generalization of repetitive action counting in long and realistic video scenarios.
be48a321a638149a7f45297ccb1cf31eb6cf0263.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that encodes multi-scale temporal correlations using transformer-based architectures. Video sequences will be processed at multiple temporal scales (e.g., single-frame, 4-frame, and 8-frame subsequences) using a Video Swin Transformer backbone to extract spatio-temporal features. These features will be further processed with 3D convolution and global pooling to capture rich temporal context. A self-attention mechanism will compute correlation matrices at each scale, which are then concatenated and passed through a period predictor that outputs a density map representing the distribution of action cycles. The density map regression approach leverages fine-grained temporal annotations, enabling both accurate counting and interpretable predictions. The model will be trained using mean squared error loss between predicted and ground truth density maps, which are generated by Gaussianizing the annotated action cycle positions.
be48a321a638149a7f45297ccb1cf31eb6cf0263.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a newly collected large-scale dataset, RepCount, which contains 1,451 videos and approximately 20,000 fine-grained annotations, covering a wide range of video lengths (4-88 seconds) and including realistic anomalies such as action interruptions and inconsistencies. The method will be evaluated on RepCount (both Part-A and Part-B subsets), as well as on existing benchmarks such as UCFRep and Countix, to assess generalization. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art repetition counting methods (e.g., RepNet, Zhang et al.), action recognition models (e.g., X3D, Video Swin Transformer), and action segmentation models. Evaluation metrics will include Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Off-By-One (OBO) accuracy. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of multi-scale processing, self-attention correlation matrices, and density map regression versus classification-based predictors.
be48a321a638149a7f45297ccb1cf31eb6cf0263.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new large-scale, fine-grained annotated dataset (RepCount) for repetitive action counting in realistic scenarios, addressing the limitations of existing datasets in terms of video length, annotation granularity, and anomaly coverage. The proposed method is the first to encode multi-scale temporal correlations with transformers specifically for this task, and to leverage density map regression for interpretable and accurate period prediction. The approach is claimed to outperform state-of-the-art methods on all tested datasets and demonstrates superior generalization to unseen data without fine-tuning. The combination of multi-scale transformer encoding and fine-grained density map regression provides both performance and interpretability advances over prior work.

be55e8ec4213868db08f2c3168ae666001bea4b8.title: Pythia: A Suite for Analyzing Large Language Models Across Training and Scaling
be55e8ec4213868db08f2c3168ae666001bea4b8.research_question: How do large language models develop and evolve over the course of training, and how do these patterns change as models scale? What is the impact of training data properties, such as term frequency and gendered language, on model behavior, memorization, and bias across different model sizes and training stages?
