be55e8ec4213868db08f2c3168ae666001bea4b8.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that (1) the frequency and ordering of terms in pretraining data influence downstream model performance and bias; (2) interventions in training data, such as modifying gendered pronoun frequencies, can mitigate bias in large language models; (3) the memorization of training data by models is not significantly affected by the order in which data is presented, but rather follows a predictable statistical process; and (4) scaling up model size leads to emergent behaviors and correlations between pretraining statistics and few-shot performance.
be55e8ec4213868db08f2c3168ae666001bea4b8.proposed_method: A comprehensive suite of 16 autoregressive, decoder-only language models, ranging from 70M to 12B parameters, will be trained on the Pile dataset and a deduplicated version of the Pile, ensuring all models see data in the exact same order. Each model will be checkpointed 154 times during training, providing fine-grained access to intermediate states. The architecture will follow best practices for large-scale transformer models, including dense attention layers, rotary embeddings, parallelized attention and feedforward sublayers, and untied embedding matrices. Training will use large batch sizes and consistent hyperparameters across scales, leveraging distributed training techniques and hardware optimizations such as FlashAttention. Tools will be developed to reconstruct the exact training dataloader state for any checkpoint, enabling precise analysis of data exposure.
be55e8ec4213868db08f2c3168ae666001bea4b8.experiment_details: Experiments will include (1) interventions in the training data to alter the frequency of gendered pronouns in the final stages of training, followed by evaluation on gender bias benchmarks such as WinoBias and CrowS-Pairs; (2) analysis of memorization dynamics by tracking the recall of specific sequences throughout training, using the (k, l)-memorization metric and comparing the distribution of memorized sequences to a Poisson process; (3) investigation of the relationship between pretraining term frequencies and few-shot performance on arithmetic and QA tasks, using the LM Evaluation Harness and calculating correlations across checkpoints and model sizes; and (4) comparison of models trained on deduplicated versus non-deduplicated data. Baselines will include comparable public models such as OPT and BLOOM, and evaluation metrics will include perplexity, accuracy, bias scores, and memorization rates.
be55e8ec4213868db08f2c3168ae666001bea4b8.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first publicly available suite of large language models that span multiple orders of magnitude in scale, are trained on public data in a fully controlled and reproducible manner, and provide extensive intermediate checkpoints and dataloader state reconstruction. This enables, for the first time, fine-grained studies of training dynamics, scaling effects, and the causal impact of data interventions on model behavior and bias. The suite facilitates novel experimental designs, such as counterfactual retraining and precise memorization analysis, that were previously infeasible due to lack of suitable model resources.

be79d0ef6dec980140bf3dc940a80a23183acf91.title: HyperDAS: Towards Automating Mechanistic Interpretability with Hypernetworks
be79d0ef6dec980140bf3dc940a80a23183acf91.research_question: How can the process of mechanistic interpretability—specifically, the identification and disentanglement of neural network features that mediate high-level concepts—be automated in large language models without relying on brute-force search over hidden representations?
be79d0ef6dec980140bf3dc940a80a23183acf91.hypothesis: A transformer-based hypernetwork can be trained to automatically localize concept-relevant token positions and construct feature subspaces in the hidden states of a target language model, enabling effective and faithful mechanistic interpretability through causal interventions.
be79d0ef6dec980140bf3dc940a80a23183acf91.proposed_method: A novel framework, HyperDAS, will be developed using a transformer-based hypernetwork to automate the localization and feature construction process for mechanistic interpretability. The method encodes a natural language description of the target concept and attends to both base and counterfactual runs of a fixed target language model layer. It dynamically selects token positions in both the base and counterfactual prompts using a cross-attention mechanism, and constructs an orthogonal feature subspace via a Householder transformation conditioned on the concept encoding. Interventions are performed by patching the selected subspace of the base token's hidden vector with that of the aligned counterfactual token, allowing for causal testing of concept mediation. The model is trained end-to-end with a combination of a causal intervention loss and a sparsity loss to enforce one-to-one token alignments and prevent trivial or uninterpretable solutions.
be79d0ef6dec980140bf3dc940a80a23183acf91.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the RAVEL benchmark, which evaluates the ability to localize and disentangle entity attributes through causal interventions in large language models. The target model will be Llama3-8B, and both single-domain and multi-domain variants of HyperDAS will be trained and evaluated. Baseline comparisons will include the current state-of-the-art Multi-task DAS (MDAS) method, which relies on manually selected token positions. Evaluation metrics will include the RAVEL Cause, Iso, and Disentangle scores, which measure the effectiveness and specificity of interventions. Key experimental setups will involve varying the intervention layer, analyzing intervention locations, and tuning the sparsity loss to assess its impact on interpretability and alignment.
be79d0ef6dec980140bf3dc940a80a23183acf91.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a hypernetwork-based approach that automates both the localization of concept-relevant token positions and the construction of feature subspaces for causal interventions, eliminating the need for brute-force search. HyperDAS is claimed to achieve state-of-the-art performance on the RAVEL benchmark, outperforming previous methods by enabling dynamic, end-to-end differentiable selection of intervention sites and subspaces. The approach also incorporates architectural and training constraints to mitigate the risk of inadvertently steering or editing the target model, aiming for faithful mechanistic interpretability. Additionally, the method provides insights into the geometry of learned feature subspaces and their alignment with specific attributes.

be7a88babf78512b545f585517704cb597388cbc.title: ReEvo: Large Language Models as Hyper-Heuristics with Reflective Evolution
be7a88babf78512b545f585517704cb597388cbc.research_question: How can large language models be leveraged to automate the design of heuristics for combinatorial optimization problems, enabling efficient exploration of open-ended heuristic spaces with minimal human intervention across diverse problem types and settings?
be7a88babf78512b545f585517704cb597388cbc.hypothesis: Integrating evolutionary search with reflective capabilities in large language models will enable the automated generation of high-quality heuristics for combinatorial optimization problems, achieving superior sample efficiency and performance compared to existing language model-based hyper-heuristics and expert-designed approaches.
be7a88babf78512b545f585517704cb597388cbc.proposed_method: A novel framework, Reflective Evolution (ReEvo), will be developed to serve as a Language Hyper-Heuristic (LHH) that uses large language models (LLMs) to generate, evolve, and improve heuristics for combinatorial optimization problems (COPs). The method encodes each candidate heuristic as a code snippet and initializes a population of such heuristics using LLMs prompted with problem specifications. The evolutionary process iteratively applies five steps: (1) selection of parent heuristics based on performance, (2) short-term reflection where an LLM analyzes relative performance of parent heuristics and provides verbal feedback, (3) crossover to generate offspring heuristics using both parents and reflection insights, (4) long-term reflection where accumulated knowledge and insights are distilled and summarized to guide future generations, and (5) elitist mutation to refine the best heuristics based on long-term reflections. The framework supports both white-box and black-box problem settings, and incorporates fitness landscape analysis to assess and smooth the search space, with LLMs acting as both generators and reflectors throughout the evolutionary process.
be7a88babf78512b545f585517704cb597388cbc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across six representative combinatorial optimization problems: Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP), Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP), Orienteering Problem (OP), Multiple Knapsack Problem (MKP), Bin Packing Problem (BPP), and Decap Placement Problem (DPP) for electronic design automation. The proposed method will be applied to evolve various heuristic types, including penalty heuristics for Guided Local Search, heuristic measures for Ant Colony Optimization, genetic operators for Genetic Algorithms, constructive heuristics for TSP, and attention-reshaping heuristics for neural combinatorial optimization solvers. Baseline comparisons will include expert-designed heuristics, state-of-the-art neural and LLM-based hyper-heuristics (such as EoH and DeepACO), and classic hyper-heuristics. Evaluation metrics will include optimality gap, execution time, objective value, and sample efficiency (number of heuristic evaluations). Both white-box and black-box prompting scenarios will be tested, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the contribution of each component of the ReEvo framework. Multiple large language models (e.g., GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4 Turbo, Llama3-70B) will be used to demonstrate robustness.
be7a88babf78512b545f585517704cb597388cbc.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces Language Hyper-Heuristics (LHHs) as a new paradigm that leverages large language models to generate heuristics in open-ended spaces, eliminating the need for manually predefined heuristic spaces. Reflective Evolution (ReEvo) innovatively integrates evolutionary search with LLM-based short-term and long-term reflections, enabling verbal gradient-based guidance and smoother fitness landscapes. The approach demonstrates superior sample efficiency and generalization across multiple combinatorial optimization domains and algorithmic types, outperforming both expert-designed and state-of-the-art LLM-based hyper-heuristics. The framework also supports reliable evaluation in black-box settings and provides interpretable, rule-based heuristics that can enhance or surpass neural combinatorial optimization solvers without additional model training.

be8db99310602d66bba64bcf41a572c45816fbfc.title: Let's Verify Step by Step
be8db99310602d66bba64bcf41a572c45816fbfc.research_question: How can the reliability of reward models for multi-step reasoning tasks be improved, and what is the comparative effectiveness of process supervision versus outcome supervision in training such models, especially when considering the cost and scalability of human feedback?
be8db99310602d66bba64bcf41a572c45816fbfc.hypothesis: Process supervision, which provides step-level feedback, will result in more reliable reward models for multi-step reasoning tasks than outcome supervision, which only provides feedback on the final outcome. Additionally, active learning strategies will increase the data efficiency of process supervision.
be8db99310602d66bba64bcf41a572c45816fbfc.proposed_method: A comprehensive comparison will be conducted between process supervision and outcome supervision for training reward models used in multi-step reasoning tasks. The approach will involve training large-scale and small-scale reward models, with all models finetuned from a capable base language model (e.g., GPT-4 or a similar architecture). For process supervision, human data-labelers will annotate the correctness of each step in model-generated solutions, while outcome supervision will use final-answer correctness, either from automatic grading or model-based supervision. The process supervision dataset (PRM800K) will be constructed with step-level human feedback, and active learning will be employed to prioritize labeling of convincing wrong-answer solutions. The reward models will be evaluated by their ability to select correct solutions from a pool of generated candidates, using best-of-N search strategies.
be8db99310602d66bba64bcf41a572c45816fbfc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the challenging MATH dataset, with both large-scale and small-scale regimes. Large-scale models will be finetuned from a base GPT-4 model, while small-scale models will use a similar architecture with less pretraining compute. The process-supervised reward model (PRM) and outcome-supervised reward model (ORM) will be compared using a representative subset of the MATH test set, with evaluation based on the fraction of correctly solved problems via best-of-N search. Baselines will include majority voting and ORM trained on uniform samples. Additional experiments will investigate the effect of active learning on data efficiency and will assess out-of-distribution generalization using recent STEM exam problems (AP Calculus, AP Chemistry, AP Physics, AMC10/12). Evaluation metrics will include percentage of problems solved, data efficiency, and generalization performance.
be8db99310602d66bba64bcf41a572c45816fbfc.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a large-scale, step-level human feedback dataset (PRM800K) for process supervision in mathematical reasoning. It systematically compares process and outcome supervision at scale, demonstrating the superior reliability of process-supervised reward models. The research also innovates by applying active learning to improve data efficiency in collecting human feedback for process supervision. Furthermore, the approach evaluates out-of-distribution generalization to recent STEM exams, providing evidence of robustness beyond the training domain.

bea3593ba91fda7c9ae2ee07ad3b9465cd45ffff.title: Dichotomy of Early and Late Phase Implicit Biases Can Provably Induce Grokking
bea3593ba91fda7c9ae2ee07ad3b9465cd45ffff.research_question: What mechanisms underlie the sharp transition from memorization to generalization (grokking) in over-parameterized neural networks, and how can the interplay of implicit biases during different training phases explain this phenomenon across classification and regression tasks?
bea3593ba91fda7c9ae2ee07ad3b9465cd45ffff.hypothesis: A dichotomy of early and late phase implicit biases, induced by large initialization and small weight decay during training, can provably induce grokking—characterized by a sharp transition from overfitting to generalization—in homogeneous neural networks.
bea3593ba91fda7c9ae2ee07ad3b9465cd45ffff.proposed_method: The proposed approach involves a rigorous theoretical and empirical investigation of training dynamics in homogeneous neural networks, such as MLPs and CNNs with homogeneous activations, under regimes of large initialization and small weight decay. The method models training as gradient flow with regularized loss, starting from a zero-output initialization to avoid loss explosion. Theoretical analysis distinguishes between an early 'kernel regime'—where the network behaves like a kernel predictor due to strong early-phase implicit bias—and a late 'rich regime'—where a max-margin or min-norm predictor emerges as weight decay becomes influential. The transition between these regimes is characterized mathematically, and the timing of the sharp transition is linked to the scale of initialization and weight decay. The framework is instantiated in both classification (e.g., sparse linear classification with diagonal linear nets) and regression (e.g., over-parameterized matrix completion) settings, with proofs provided for convergence to kernel and max-margin/min-norm solutions.
bea3593ba91fda7c9ae2ee07ad3b9465cd45ffff.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on modular addition tasks, sparse linear classification, and over-parameterized matrix completion (e.g., multiplication table completion). For modular addition, two-layer ReLU networks will be trained with varying initialization scales and weight decay values, using full-batch gradient descent, to observe the timing and sharpness of grokking transitions. In the sparse linear classification setting, diagonal linear nets will be trained on synthetic datasets with k-sparse ground-truth weights, comparing early-phase (kernel/NTK) and late-phase (max L1-margin) generalization. For matrix completion, low-rank matrices will be reconstructed from partial observations using matrix factorization parameterizations, and the test loss on unobserved entries will be tracked. Baselines include standard kernel predictors and max-margin/min-norm solutions, and evaluation metrics include training/test accuracy or loss, as well as the timing and sharpness of the transition from memorization to generalization.
bea3593ba91fda7c9ae2ee07ad3b9465cd45ffff.novelty_claims: The proposal aims to provide the first rigorous theoretical proof of grokking in neural network settings, demonstrating that a sharp transition from memorization to generalization can be induced by the dichotomy of early and late phase implicit biases. The analysis establishes a provably sharp transition point, rather than a gradual change, and explains how initialization scale and weight decay control the timing of grokking. The framework is general for homogeneous neural networks and is instantiated in both classification and regression tasks, including new phenomena such as 'misgrokking' where generalization degrades after initial success. Theoretical results connect the kernel regime to NTK predictors and the rich regime to max-margin/min-norm solutions, with empirical validation across multiple tasks.

bec89199faf9a7aa6b1605f1d506c8d215f036f1.title: Learning Soft Constraints From Constrained Expert Demonstrations
bec89199faf9a7aa6b1605f1d506c8d215f036f1.research_question: How can cumulative soft constraints that govern expert behavior be learned from demonstrations when the reward function is known, particularly in stochastic domains and with arbitrary state-action spaces?
bec89199faf9a7aa6b1605f1d506c8d215f036f1.hypothesis: It is possible to recover cumulative soft constraint functions from expert demonstrations by iteratively optimizing a constraint function such that the resulting constrained policy matches expert behavior, even in the presence of noise and in continuous or stochastic environments.
bec89199faf9a7aa6b1605f1d506c8d215f036f1.proposed_method: A novel inverse constraint learning (ICL) framework is proposed to recover cumulative soft constraints from expert demonstrations, assuming the reward function is given. The method alternates between two main phases: (1) a constrained reinforcement learning (RL) phase, where a policy is optimized to maximize expected reward subject to the current constraint function, and (2) a constraint adjustment phase, where the constraint function is updated to make the expert policy feasible while increasing the constraint values for non-expert-like policies. The constraint function is parameterized by a flexible neural network with a sigmoid output, and the optimization is performed using the penalty method, which converts constrained optimization into an unconstrained problem with a ReLU penalty term. To improve convergence, a normalizing flow density estimator is used to reweight policies and trajectories, favoring those dissimilar to the expert, thus sharpening the distinction between expert and agent behaviors during constraint adjustment.
bec89199faf9a7aa6b1605f1d506c8d215f036f1.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a diverse set of environments, including synthetic gridworlds, CartPole variants, highway driving scenarios based on the HighD and ExiD datasets, and Mujoco robotics environments such as Ant-Constrained and HalfCheetah-Constrained. The proposed method is compared against two baselines: GAIL-Constraint (an adaptation of Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning) and ICRL (Inverse Constrained Reinforcement Learning), both capable of learning neural network-based constraints. Evaluation metrics include Constraint Mean Squared Error (CMSE) between the true and recovered constraints, and Normalized Accrual Dissimilarity (NAD) measuring the similarity between expert and agent state-action visitation distributions. The experimental setup includes multiple random seeds, detailed hyperparameter tuning, and ablation studies on optimization methods and reweighting strategies.
bec89199faf9a7aa6b1605f1d506c8d215f036f1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to recover cumulative soft constraints bounded in expectation, as defined in constrained Markov Decision Processes, from expert demonstrations in stochastic domains with arbitrary (including continuous) state-action spaces. Unlike prior work that focuses on hard or probabilistic constraints in discrete settings, this method enables learning of soft, cumulative constraints using neural networks and is empirically shown to outperform existing baselines in both accuracy and policy similarity to experts. The use of the penalty method for optimization and the integration of normalizing flow-based reweighting for improved convergence further distinguish the approach.

bed75393db4c3216470f93d7ec21803ec40b3c72.title: Implicit regularization in Heavy-ball momentum accelerated stochastic gradient descent
bed75393db4c3216470f93d7ec21803ec40b3c72.research_question: Does the momentum parameter in Heavy-ball momentum accelerated stochastic gradient descent play a role in implicit regularization, and how does it affect the generalization performance of deep neural networks compared to standard gradient descent and stochastic gradient descent?
bed75393db4c3216470f93d7ec21803ec40b3c72.hypothesis: The momentum parameter in Heavy-ball momentum accelerated (stochastic) gradient descent amplifies the strength of implicit regularization, leading to improved generalization performance and flatter minima compared to methods without momentum.
bed75393db4c3216470f93d7ec21803ec40b3c72.proposed_method: A theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted to characterize the implicit regularization induced by the momentum parameter in Heavy-ball momentum accelerated gradient descent (GD+M) and its stochastic variant (SGD+M). The approach involves deriving a continuous-time trajectory for the discrete momentum update, showing that it follows a modified loss function consisting of the original loss and an amplified implicit regularizer. The analysis will extend to both full-batch and mini-batch (stochastic) settings, providing explicit mathematical formulations for the implicit regularization term as a function of the momentum parameter. Theoretical results will be complemented by numerical experiments to validate the impact of momentum on regularization strength and generalization.
bed75393db4c3216470f93d7ec21803ec40b3c72.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification benchmarks including MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100, using popular deep network architectures such as ResNet-18, ResNet-50, DenseNet-121, and WideResNet-16-8. Both full-batch and mini-batch training regimes will be explored, with systematic variation of the momentum parameter and learning rate to isolate their effects. Baseline comparisons will include standard gradient descent (GD), stochastic gradient descent (SGD), and their momentum-accelerated counterparts (GD+M, SGD+M), with all external regularization (e.g., weight decay, dropout, label smoothing) disabled except for batch normalization. Evaluation metrics will focus on test accuracy, sharpness, and the variance of test accuracy across runs, with results averaged over multiple random seeds and epochs.
bed75393db4c3216470f93d7ec21803ec40b3c72.novelty_claims: The proposal aims to provide the first explicit and general mathematical characterization of implicit regularization for Heavy-ball momentum accelerated stochastic gradient descent in non-linear neural networks. It claims to demonstrate that the momentum parameter amplifies the implicit regularization effect by a quantifiable factor, leading to stronger preference for flatter minima and improved generalization. The work also explores the interaction between implicit gradient regularization and noise injection, suggesting that these two forms of regularization can reinforce each other. Theoretical findings are supported by comprehensive empirical validation across multiple architectures and datasets.

bf14244669d5505f63343d4365d99d24aa6c5e82.title: Monkey: Image Resolution and Text Label are Important Things for Large Multi-Modal Models
bf14244669d5505f63343d4365d99d24aa6c5e82.research_question: How can large multimodal models (LMMs) be enhanced to better handle high-resolution images and provide more detailed, contextually rich text descriptions for improved performance on complex vision-language tasks such as image captioning and visual question answering?
bf14244669d5505f63343d4365d99d24aa6c5e82.hypothesis: Increasing the input image resolution to match or exceed the original training size of the vision encoder, combined with the generation of multi-level, contextually enriched text descriptions, will significantly improve the ability of LMMs to capture fine-grained visual details and complex scene-object associations, resulting in superior performance across a wide range of vision-language tasks.
bf14244669d5505f63343d4365d99d24aa6c5e82.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a framework that divides high-resolution input images into uniform patches using a sliding window approach, with each patch resized to the resolution supported by the original vision encoder (e.g., 448×448). Each patch is processed independently through a shared static Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder, augmented with LoRA-based adapters and a trainable visual resampler to enhance detail sensitivity without extensive pretraining. Both global and local features are extracted: the original image is also resized and processed to preserve holistic context. A cross-attention-based visual resampler summarizes visual information into a language-compatible feature space. Additionally, a multi-level description generation pipeline is developed, which synthesizes detailed and contextually rich captions by integrating outputs from advanced systems such as BLIP2, PPOCR, GRIT, SAM, and ChatGPT, capturing both global and local visual-textual relationships. These descriptions are used to augment training data, enabling the model to learn nuanced associations between image regions and textual semantics.
bf14244669d5505f63343d4365d99d24aa6c5e82.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a comprehensive suite of public datasets spanning image captioning (COCO Caption, TextCaps), general visual question answering (VQAv2, OKVQA, GQA, ScienceQA, VizWiz), scene text-centric VQA (TextVQA, OCRVQA, AI2D), and document-oriented VQA (DocVQA, ChartQA, InfoVQA, DeepForm, KLC, WTQ, TabFact, VisualMRC), totaling approximately 1.44 million examples. Baselines will include state-of-the-art LMMs such as Flamingo, BLIP-2, InstructBLIP, Shikra, mPLUG-Owl2, LLaVA1.5, and Qwen-VL. Evaluation metrics will cover standard task-specific scores such as accuracy, BLEU, CIDEr, and perception scores on benchmarks like MME. Ablation studies will systematically vary input resolutions, the number of trainable adapters, and the use of multi-level descriptions to isolate their contributions. Implementation will utilize pretrained ViT-BigG and Qwen-VL LLMs, with instruction tuning and consistent resampling across patches, and training will be performed with AdamW optimizer and large batch sizes on high-performance GPUs.
bf14244669d5505f63343d4365d99d24aa6c5e82.novelty_claims: The proposed approach enables high-resolution input processing (up to 1344×896) in LMMs without the need for costly pretraining from scratch, by leveraging patch-based division and adapter-based fine-tuning. The multi-level description generation method automatically produces rich, layered, and contextually diverse captions by integrating multiple advanced vision and language systems, bridging the gap between simple text labels and complex visual scenes. This synergy between high-resolution visual input and comprehensive textual supervision is claimed to result in significant performance gains across diverse multimodal benchmarks, particularly in tasks requiring fine-grained detail recognition and dense text understanding. The method is also resource-efficient, scalable, and demonstrates superior results compared to existing LMMs, including in qualitative comparisons with models like GPT4V.

bf36a0b5cf9d59c92b7480618cfec3f9faa5d03c.title: Distributionally Robust Optimization with Bias and Variance Reduction
bf36a0b5cf9d59c92b7480618cfec3f9faa5d03c.research_question: How can distributionally robust optimization (DRO) problems, particularly those involving spectral risk-based uncertainty sets and f-divergence penalties, be efficiently and reliably solved using stochastic optimization methods, with improved convergence and stability under distribution shift and fairness constraints?
bf36a0b5cf9d59c92b7480618cfec3f9faa5d03c.hypothesis: A stochastic gradient-based optimization algorithm that incorporates both bias and variance reduction techniques, and requires tuning only a single learning rate hyperparameter, will achieve linear convergence for smooth regularized losses in spectral risk-based DRO problems, outperforming existing methods in terms of convergence speed, stability, and robustness to distribution shift and fairness metrics.
bf36a0b5cf9d59c92b7480618cfec3f9faa5d03c.proposed_method: A new stochastic optimization algorithm, called Prospect, is proposed for minimizing spectral risk measures in distributionally robust optimization. The method constructs an unbiased gradient estimator for the DRO objective by maintaining a running table of loss values and leveraging the structure of the spectral risk measure, which involves solving an inner maximization problem over a convex polytope defined by the spectrum. Bias reduction is achieved by updating the loss table incrementally and using the most adversarial distribution weights for gradient estimation. Variance reduction is incorporated via a control variate scheme, where additional running tables of gradients and weights are maintained and updated at each iteration, allowing the use of a constant learning rate. The algorithm efficiently updates these tables using only a small number of function and gradient oracle calls per iteration, and solves the inner maximization using isotonic regression (Pool Adjacent Violators algorithm) after sorting the loss table.
bf36a0b5cf9d59c92b7480618cfec3f9faa5d03c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of supervised learning tasks, including tabular regression (yacht, energy, concrete, kin8nm, power), fairness benchmarks (diabetes130-hospitals, acsincome), and distribution shift benchmarks from the WILDS suite (amazon reviews, iwildcam). The proposed method will be compared against baselines such as minibatch stochastic gradient descent (SGD), stochastic regularized dual averaging (SRDA), Saddle-SAGA, and LSVRG. Evaluation metrics will include training suboptimality (relative to the optimal objective value), fairness metrics such as statistical parity, and robustness metrics such as worst-group and median-group misclassification error under distribution shift. Hyperparameters such as shift cost and regularization will be fixed or tuned as appropriate, and the number of oracle calls per epoch will be tracked to compare convergence rates.
bf36a0b5cf9d59c92b7480618cfec3f9faa5d03c.novelty_claims: The proposed algorithm achieves linear convergence for any positive shift cost with only a single hyperparameter (learning rate), contrasting with previous methods that require multiple hyperparameters or fail to converge due to bias or inadequate regularization. The bias and variance reduction techniques are specifically tailored for spectral risk measures and allow for efficient, scalable updates. The method is empirically shown to converge 2-3× faster than state-of-the-art baselines on a range of benchmarks, and demonstrates improved stability and fairness under distribution shift. The approach generalizes to non-smooth losses via the Moreau envelope and can be extended to other uncertainty sets and fairness contexts.

bf3cd8a979617ef0021e88e8c1844bfb513beee9.title: Dissecting Fine-Tuning Unlearning in Large Language Models
bf3cd8a979617ef0021e88e8c1844bfb513beee9.research_question: How effective are fine-tuning-based unlearning methods at removing targeted knowledge from large language models, and what are the underlying mechanisms and limitations of these approaches?
bf3cd8a979617ef0021e88e8c1844bfb513beee9.hypothesis: Fine-tuning-based unlearning methods do not truly erase targeted knowledge from large language models but instead alter the retrieval mechanisms, primarily by modifying the coefficients in the MLP components and attention states, leading to apparent but incomplete unlearning effects.
bf3cd8a979617ef0021e88e8c1844bfb513beee9.proposed_method: A comprehensive investigation will be conducted into the mechanisms of fine-tuning-based unlearning in large language models through a series of activation patching and parameter restoration experiments. The approach will involve isolating and manipulating specific model components—namely, the coefficients (mℓ) and value vectors (Wℓ) in the MLPs, as well as the attention components (Aℓ)—to determine their roles in knowledge recall and unlearning. Experiments will be performed in three settings: restoring only the coefficients, restoring only the value vectors, and restoring only the attention states, each layer by layer, to assess their individual and combined effects on knowledge recovery. The methodology will also include simultaneous restoration of coefficients and attention states to evaluate their joint impact. The study will use causal mediation techniques to observe the effects of patching over windows of consecutive layers, enabling precise attribution of unlearning effects to specific model components.
bf3cd8a979617ef0021e88e8c1844bfb513beee9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two recent large language models: LLaMA2-7B-chat and OLMo-7B. For each model, 10 well-known concepts will be selected from the ConceptVectors Benchmark, and corresponding training data will be extracted from the models' pre-training datasets (RedPajama for LLaMA, Dolma for OLMo). Fine-tuning-based unlearning methods, including DPO, NPO, NPO+KL, and GradientDifference, will be applied to erase knowledge of these concepts. The effectiveness of unlearning will be evaluated using Knowledge Recovery Score (KRS), which measures the restoration of model outputs after patching specific components. Behavioral tests will be performed using QA pairs related to both target and unrelated concepts, with BLEU scores used to quantify changes in output. The experimental setup will also monitor the global impact of unlearning on unrelated knowledge and capabilities, and include rigorous controls to isolate the effects of each component.
bf3cd8a979617ef0021e88e8c1844bfb513beee9.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a detailed mechanistic dissection of fine-tuning-based unlearning in large language models, revealing that apparent unlearning is primarily achieved by altering the coefficients in the MLPs and attention states rather than erasing knowledge from value vectors. The study provides the first comprehensive evidence that such methods do not truly remove embedded knowledge, but instead change the way it is retrieved, making them vulnerable to recovery attacks and causing unintended degradation of unrelated model capabilities. The methodology offers a novel framework for evaluating unlearning at both the component and behavioral levels, and highlights the need for more precise metrics and approaches for true knowledge erasure in large language models.

bf7025a2e5dbb3c09deae02a1aa98a256ca559e2.title: Video-ChatGPT: Towards Detailed Video Understanding via Large Vision and Language Models
bf7025a2e5dbb3c09deae02a1aa98a256ca559e2.research_question: How can large vision and language models be leveraged to enable detailed, coherent, and contextually rich open-ended conversations about video content, capturing both spatial and temporal dynamics in videos?
bf7025a2e5dbb3c09deae02a1aa98a256ca559e2.hypothesis: Integrating a video-adapted visual encoder with a large language model and fine-tuning on a large, diverse set of video-instruction pairs will enable the resulting multimodal model to generate accurate, detailed, and contextually appropriate conversations about videos, outperforming existing video conversation models.
bf7025a2e5dbb3c09deae02a1aa98a256ca559e2.proposed_method: A novel multimodal framework will be developed by merging a pretrained visual encoder (CLIP ViT-L/14) adapted for spatiotemporal video representation with a large language model (Vicuna, initialized with LLaVA weights). The visual encoder will process video frames independently to extract frame-level embeddings, which are then average-pooled along spatial and temporal dimensions to obtain both temporal and spatial representations. These features are concatenated and projected via a trainable linear adapter into the language model's input space. Instruction tuning will be performed using a curated dataset of 100,000 video-instruction pairs, generated through a combination of human-assisted and semi-automatic annotation pipelines. During fine-tuning, only the adapter layer is updated, aligning video features with the language model's embedding space to enable natural and reliable video-grounded responses.
bf7025a2e5dbb3c09deae02a1aa98a256ca559e2.experiment_details: Experiments will involve fine-tuning the proposed model on a dataset of 100,000 video-instruction pairs, with both human and semi-automatically generated annotations. Evaluation will be conducted using a newly designed quantitative benchmarking framework, assessing correctness, detail orientation, contextual understanding, temporal understanding, and consistency. The model's performance will be compared against strong baselines such as VideoChat, LLaMAAdapter, Video-LLaMA, and FrozenBiLM, using standard datasets including ActivityNet-200, MSVD-QA, MSRVTT-QA, TGIF-QA, and ActivityNet-QA. Both zero-shot and open-ended question-answering tasks will be evaluated, with metrics including accuracy and human/GPT-3.5/Vicuna-based scoring on a 1-5 scale. Ablation studies will assess the impact of annotation sources and evaluation consistency.
bf7025a2e5dbb3c09deae02a1aa98a256ca559e2.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first large-scale, instruction-tuned video conversation model that combines a video-adapted visual encoder with a large language model for detailed video understanding. A new, scalable annotation framework is developed to generate a diverse and high-quality dataset of 100,000 video-instruction pairs. Additionally, a comprehensive quantitative evaluation framework for video conversation models is proposed, enabling objective benchmarking across multiple conversational and understanding dimensions. The approach is claimed to achieve state-of-the-art performance on several video question-answering and conversation benchmarks, demonstrating superior temporal, spatial, and contextual comprehension compared to existing models.

bf7468c9ef85c4bb764e08e7b5380129e707cf59.title: LoViT: Long Video Transformer for surgical phase recognition
bf7468c9ef85c4bb764e08e7b5380129e707cf59.research_question: How can surgical phase recognition in long, complex surgical videos be improved by effectively modeling both local fine-grained and global temporal dependencies, while addressing the challenges of similar visual scenes across different phases and computational constraints?
bf7468c9ef85c4bb764e08e7b5380129e707cf59.hypothesis: A two-stage deep learning framework that combines a temporally-rich spatial feature extractor with a multi-scale temporal aggregator—incorporating both local (short-term) and global (long-term) temporal attention mechanisms—will outperform existing methods in surgical phase recognition, particularly on long and complex surgical videos.
bf7468c9ef85c4bb764e08e7b5380129e707cf59.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a two-stage framework for online surgical phase recognition in long surgical videos. First, a temporally-rich spatial feature extractor is trained using video clips, rather than single frames, to embed temporal context directly into spatial features; this extractor is based on a Vision Transformer (ViT) backbone. After training, the spatial extractor's weights are frozen, and each frame is embedded for subsequent temporal modeling. The temporal aggregator consists of two cascaded modules: (1) a local Transformer-based module (L-Trans) that captures fine-grained, short-term temporal dependencies using self-attention and cross-attention mechanisms over local windows, and (2) a global Informer-based module (G-Informer) that employs ProbSparse self-attention to efficiently model long-range dependencies across the entire video sequence. A multi-scale temporal fusion head then integrates local and global features, followed by linear layers for phase classification and phase transition-aware supervision. Phase transition areas are emphasized using a 1D asymmetric Gaussian kernel to generate a transition map, which is used as an auxiliary supervision signal during training.
bf7468c9ef85c4bb764e08e7b5380129e707cf59.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two publicly available surgical video datasets: Cholec80 (80 videos, 7 phases, ~39 minutes per video) and AutoLaparo (21 videos, 7 phases, ~66 minutes per video). Both datasets will be sampled at 1 fps and resized to 250x250 pixels for input. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines, including EndoNet, MTRCNet-CL, PhaseNet, SV-RCNet, OHFM, TeCNO, TMRNet, Trans-SVNet, and AVT. Evaluation metrics will include video-level accuracy, phase-level precision, recall, and Jaccard index, with both strict and relaxed (10-second boundary) metrics reported for fair comparison. Implementation will use PyTorch, with training on an NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU, and hyperparameters such as learning rate, warmup, and cosine annealing specified. Ablation studies will assess the contributions of the temporally-rich spatial extractor, local/global temporal modules, and phase transition-aware supervision.
bf7468c9ef85c4bb764e08e7b5380129e707cf59.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a temporally-rich spatial feature extractor trained with video clips, enabling more discriminative spatial representations by leveraging temporal context. It is the first to combine multi-scale temporal aggregation using both vanilla self-attention for local dependencies and ProbSparse self-attention for global dependencies in surgical phase recognition. The approach also introduces a simple yet effective phase transition-aware supervision mechanism via a transition map, improving the model's ability to detect phase boundaries. This framework is designed to efficiently handle long surgical videos, overcoming the computational and representational limitations of prior CNN, RNN, and TCN-based methods. The method achieves state-of-the-art results on two challenging datasets, demonstrating improved accuracy and stability over existing approaches.

bf7abedaa95c680d3b29c32127a42bef0003bf81.title: LTX-Video: Realtime Video Latent Diffusion
bf7abedaa95c680d3b29c32127a42bef0003bf81.research_question: How can a unified, efficient, and high-quality video generation model be developed that supports both text-to-video and image-to-video tasks, while achieving real-time or faster-than-real-time performance and maintaining high visual fidelity and temporal consistency?
bf7abedaa95c680d3b29c32127a42bef0003bf81.hypothesis: Integrating the Video-VAE and denoising transformer into a holistic latent diffusion framework, with high spatiotemporal compression and novel loss functions, will enable faster-than-real-time video generation without sacrificing video quality or fine detail, outperforming existing models of similar scale.
bf7abedaa95c680d3b29c32127a42bef0003bf81.proposed_method: A transformer-based latent diffusion model will be developed that tightly integrates a high-compression Video-VAE and a denoising transformer. The Video-VAE will employ spatiotemporal downscaling (32×32×8 per token) and a high latent channel depth (128 channels), achieving a 1:192 compression ratio. The patchifying operation will be relocated from the transformer input to the VAE input, enabling the transformer to operate efficiently in a highly compressed latent space and perform full spatiotemporal self-attention. The VAE decoder will be tasked with both latent-to-pixel conversion and the final denoising step, producing clean results directly in pixel space and eliminating the need for a separate upsampling module. Additional architectural innovations include the use of rotary positional embeddings with normalized fractional coordinates, QK-normalization for attention stability, and a suite of novel loss functions (including a ReconstructionGAN and a spatiotemporal DWT loss) to enhance reconstruction quality and detail.
bf7abedaa95c680d3b29c32127a42bef0003bf81.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale video datasets for both text-to-video and image-to-video generation tasks. The model will be benchmarked against state-of-the-art baselines such as MovieGen, HunyuanVideo, PyramidFlow, and CogVideoX, with comparisons made on metrics including visual quality, prompt adherence, motion fidelity, and generation speed. Evaluation will include generating 5-second videos at 24fps and 768×512 resolution, measuring both qualitative and quantitative results (e.g., FVD, CLIP score, runtime). The model will be trained with a combination of pixel reconstruction (MSE), Video-DWT (L1), perceptual (LPIPS), and ReconstructionGAN losses, and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of architectural and training choices.
bf7abedaa95c680d3b29c32127a42bef0003bf81.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a holistic integration of Video-VAE and transformer-based latent diffusion, optimizing their interaction for efficiency and quality. A novel high-compression Video-VAE architecture is developed, leveraging unique loss functions and multi-layer noise injection to enable unprecedented compression rates while maintaining video fidelity. The method eliminates the need for a separate upsampler by assigning the final denoising step to the VAE decoder, directly generating fine details in pixel space. Additional innovations include the use of ReconstructionGAN for improved adversarial training in reconstruction tasks and the application of advanced positional embeddings and attention normalization for robust spatiotemporal modeling. The resulting model achieves faster-than-real-time generation and sets a new benchmark for accessible, scalable video generation.

bf9e3b31e6207293213caa60b7563e989d8cd9a3.title: Test-Time Model Adaptation with Only Forward Passes
bf9e3b31e6207293213caa60b7563e989d8cd9a3.research_question: How can test-time adaptation be achieved for deep neural networks deployed on resource-limited and non-modifiable hardware, such as quantized models on edge devices, without relying on backpropagation or model weight updates, in order to improve robustness to distribution shifts?
bf9e3b31e6207293213caa60b7563e989d8cd9a3.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a derivative-free, forward-only optimization strategy—specifically, learning input prompts and shifting activations using a covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES) guided by an unsupervised fitness function—can enable effective test-time adaptation on both full-precision and quantized models, outperforming existing gradient-based and gradient-free methods in terms of accuracy, calibration, and memory efficiency.
bf9e3b31e6207293213caa60b7563e989d8cd9a3.proposed_method: A novel test-time Forward-Optimization Adaptation (FOA) framework will be developed that avoids backpropagation and model weight modification. The method introduces learnable input prompts, inserted before the first layer of the model (e.g., Vision Transformer), which are adapted online using a derivative-free optimizer—specifically, the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES). A custom unsupervised fitness function will be designed, combining prediction entropy and the discrepancy between activation statistics of out-of-distribution (OOD) test samples and source in-distribution (ID) samples. To further enhance adaptation, a back-to-source activation shifting mechanism will be implemented, directly adjusting the final layer activations of test samples toward the source domain statistics using an online-updated shifting direction. The approach is designed to be compatible with quantized and hard-coded models, requiring only forward passes and minimal memory overhead.
bf9e3b31e6207293213caa60b7563e989d8cd9a3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four standard OOD generalization benchmarks: ImageNet-C, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-V2, and ImageNet-Sketch. Both full-precision (32-bit) and quantized (8-bit, 6-bit) Vision Transformer (ViT-Base) models will be evaluated, with models trained on ImageNet-1K. Baselines will include gradient-free TTA methods (e.g., LAME, T3A) and gradient-based methods (e.g., TENT, SAR, CoTTA), as well as no adaptation. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy and expected calibration error (ECE). Experimental setups will systematically vary batch size, population size in CMA-ES, number of prompt embeddings, and number of ID samples used for statistics. Additional ablation studies will assess the impact of each method component, and memory usage and computational efficiency will be benchmarked for deployment scenarios on resource-constrained devices.
bf9e3b31e6207293213caa60b7563e989d8cd9a3.novelty_claims: The proposed FOA framework introduces the first test-time adaptation paradigm that is fully forward-only and does not require any model weight updates or backpropagation, making it suitable for quantized and hard-coded models on edge devices. The method leverages a derivative-free evolutionary strategy (CMA-ES) for prompt adaptation, guided by a novel unsupervised fitness function that incorporates both entropy and activation distribution alignment. A new activation shifting mechanism is proposed to align OOD test activations with source domain statistics in a forward-only manner. The approach achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and calibration on both full-precision and quantized models, with up to 24-fold memory reduction compared to gradient-based methods, thus greatly expanding the practical applicability of test-time adaptation.

bfc07ed6e6d4aef2674d0e412215b3253b95336c.title: SSDA3D: Semi-supervised Domain Adaptation for 3D Object Detection from Point Cloud
bfc07ed6e6d4aef2674d0e412215b3253b95336c.research_question: How can semi-supervised domain adaptation be effectively achieved for 3D object detection in point clouds, particularly under significant domain shifts such as different LiDAR configurations, cities, and weather conditions, when only a small amount of labeled target data is available?
bfc07ed6e6d4aef2674d0e412215b3253b95336c.hypothesis: Integrating both inter-domain adaptation and intra-domain generalization within a unified semi-supervised framework will significantly improve 3D object detection performance under domain shift, even with limited labeled target data, potentially surpassing fully-supervised models trained on the target domain alone.
bfc07ed6e6d4aef2674d0e412215b3253b95336c.proposed_method: A novel two-stage semi-supervised domain adaptation framework for 3D object detection, termed SSDA3D, will be developed. The first stage, Inter-domain Adaptation, introduces an Inter-domain Point-CutMix module that generates region-wise mixed point cloud samples from both labeled source and labeled target domains, acting as intermediate domain data to encourage the learning of domain-invariant representations. The second stage, Intra-domain Generalization, employs an Intra-domain Point-MixUp module that globally mixes labeled and pseudo-labeled target samples to regularize the pseudo label distribution and enhance generalization on the unlabeled target set. The framework leverages a teacher-student paradigm, where the teacher model, trained in the first stage, generates pseudo labels for the unlabeled target data, and the student model is trained on the mixed data. Key technical components include region-level point cloud mixing constrained by geometric range, pseudo-label filtering, collision detection for label merging, and probabilistic application of mixing strategies during training.
bfc07ed6e6d4aef2674d0e412215b3253b95336c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the challenging cross-domain setting of Waymo (64-beam LiDAR) to nuScenes (32-beam LiDAR), using the CenterPoint 3D object detector as the backbone. The labeled target data will be subsampled at varying proportions (1%, 5%, 10%, 20%, 100%) to simulate different annotation budgets, with the remainder treated as unlabeled. Baselines for comparison include Source Only, ST3D-UDA (unsupervised domain adaptation), Labeled Target (fully-supervised on partial target data), Co-training (joint training on labeled source and target), ST3D-SSDA (semi-supervised extension of ST3D), and Oracle (fully-supervised on 100% target labels). Evaluation metrics will include Average Precision (AP) and nuScenes Detection Score (NDS) on the car category, following official protocols, and the Closed Gap metric to quantify the proportion of the domain gap closed relative to Oracle. Ablation studies will assess the contribution of each module and the impact of mixing probabilities.
bfc07ed6e6d4aef2674d0e412215b3253b95336c.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to address semi-supervised domain adaptation for 3D object detection in point clouds, jointly tackling inter-domain adaptation and intra-domain generalization. The Inter-domain Point-CutMix module introduces region-level mixing of point clouds to create intermediate domain samples, effectively reducing domain discrepancy. The Intra-domain Point-MixUp module regularizes pseudo label distributions by mixing labeled and pseudo-labeled target data, improving robustness and generalization. The method demonstrates that with as little as 10% labeled target data, it can surpass the performance of fully-supervised models trained on 100% target labels, thus achieving state-of-the-art results while significantly reducing annotation costs.

c01c7c1f903dfaa78812fb20a6cb2db25e4712e3.title: Quantifying Uncertainty in Answers from any Language Model and Enhancing their Trustworthiness
c01c7c1f903dfaa78812fb20a6cb2db25e4712e3.research_question: How can uncertainty in the answers generated by large language models (LLMs), especially those accessible only via black-box APIs, be quantified in a way that enables users to assess the trustworthiness of any given output and enhance the reliability of LLM-based applications?
c01c7c1f903dfaa78812fb20a6cb2db25e4712e3.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a combination of extrinsic and intrinsic confidence assessments, derived from multiple sampled outputs and self-reflection prompts, can provide accurate and generalizable uncertainty estimates for LLM responses, even when only black-box access is available.
c01c7c1f903dfaa78812fb20a6cb2db25e4712e3.proposed_method: A novel uncertainty quantification framework, BSDETECTOR, will be developed to estimate numeric confidence scores for any output generated by an LLM. The method will combine two complementary components: Observed Consistency and Self-reflection Certainty. Observed Consistency will be computed by sampling multiple responses from the LLM using varied prompts and temperature settings, then measuring the semantic similarity and contradiction between the original answer and these samples using a natural language inference (NLI) model and an indicator function. Self-reflection Certainty will be obtained by prompting the LLM to assess its own answer through follow-up questions, rating its confidence in a discrete, interpretable manner. The final confidence score will be a weighted aggregation of these two components, with hyperparameters tuned based on empirical performance. This approach will not require access to LLM training data or token-level probabilities, making it broadly applicable to any LLM accessible via API.
c01c7c1f903dfaa78812fb20a6cb2db25e4712e3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of question-answering benchmarks, including GSM8K (grade-school math word problems), SVAMP (math word problems), CommonsenseQA (commonsense reasoning), and TriviaQA (open-domain trivia). The method will be evaluated using OpenAI's Text-Davinci-003 and GPT-3.5 Turbo models. For each dataset, the true answers will be used to assess the accuracy of LLM responses. The quality of uncertainty estimates will be measured using the Area Under the Receiver Operator Characteristic Curve (AUROC), comparing the ability of the proposed method to distinguish correct from incorrect answers. Baseline methods will include likelihood-based uncertainty (where available), temperature sampling, and self-reflection certainty alone. Additional experiments will assess the impact of selecting the most confident answer from multiple samples and the use of confidence scores to guide human-in-the-loop and fully automated LLM-based evaluation, including on the Summarize-from-feedback dataset for open-ended evaluation tasks.
c01c7c1f903dfaa78812fb20a6cb2db25e4712e3.novelty_claims: The proposed method is claimed to be the first to provide accurate, generalizable uncertainty estimates for any LLM output using only black-box API access, without requiring access to training data, token-level probabilities, or additional model training. The approach uniquely combines extrinsic (Observed Consistency) and intrinsic (Self-reflection Certainty) confidence assessments in a unified framework. It is also claimed that the method enables more reliable answer selection and LLM-based evaluation, outperforming existing baselines and improving both the accuracy of LLM responses and the trustworthiness of automated evaluations in high-stakes applications.

c01dd96803eb95ffd3bb4472d6dcf313fe4d675d.title: The Structure of Relation Decoding Linear Operators in Large Language Models
c01dd96803eb95ffd3bb4472d6dcf313fe4d675d.research_question: How is relational knowledge structured and organized within large transformer-based language models, and can collections of linear relation decoding operators be efficiently compressed without significant loss in decoding accuracy?
c01dd96803eb95ffd3bb4472d6dcf313fe4d675d.hypothesis: Collections of linear relation decoding operators in large language models exhibit significant redundancy due to shared, coarse-grained semantic properties, enabling their effective compression via order-3 tensor network architectures without substantial loss in relational decoding performance.
c01dd96803eb95ffd3bb4472d6dcf313fe4d675d.proposed_method: A comprehensive methodology will be developed to analyze and compress collections of linear relational decoding operators extracted from large transformer-based language models. The approach will involve representing each relation's decoder as an affine transformation and organizing all such decoders into a third-order tensor. Two principal tensor network architectures will be explored: a Simple Order-3 Tensor Network and a Triangle Tensor Network, both equipped with projection matrices to align with the embedding spaces of the models. Optional relation embedding networks will be incorporated to relax linearity assumptions. The tensor networks will be trained end-to-end, with the language model parameters fixed, using cross-entropy loss on the predicted object tokens. Compression effectiveness will be evaluated by varying the inner dimensions of the tensor networks and comparing parameter efficiency and faithfulness.
c01dd96803eb95ffd3bb4472d6dcf313fe4d675d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using several large language models, including GPT-J, Llama3-18B, and GPT-NeoX-20B. Three datasets will be utilized: the Hernandez et al. (2023) dataset of 47 mostly orthogonal relations, an extended dataset with 79 relations designed to introduce semantic overlap, and a mathematical relations dataset for controlled structure analysis. Baselines will include independently trained low-rank LRE matrices and canonical linear decoders estimated via Jacobian-based procedures. Evaluation will focus on faithfulness (top-1 accuracy of object prediction), parameter count, and generalization to unseen samples. A cross-evaluation protocol will be implemented to measure semantic similarity between relations by applying each decoder to all other relations' subject-object pairs, producing a faithfulness matrix for structural analysis.
c01dd96803eb95ffd3bb4472d6dcf313fe4d675d.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a novel property-centric perspective on the organization of relational decoders in large language models, demonstrating that these operators are highly compressible due to shared semantic properties rather than being strictly relation-specific. The use of order-3 tensor networks for compressing entire collections of relational decoders is innovative, providing both interpretability and parameter efficiency. The cross-evaluation protocol offers a new empirical measure of semantic similarity among relations, revealing block structures and property-level encoding. The work advances understanding of how relational knowledge is encoded and generalizes in large language models, with implications for both interpretability and model compression.

c021f6928f92582585fc758db20d11a5ad756fca.title: B2T Connection: Serving Stability and Performance in Deep Transformers
c021f6928f92582585fc758db20d11a5ad756fca.research_question: How can the stability and performance of deep Transformer architectures be improved, particularly with respect to the placement of layer normalization and the vanishing gradient problem, across a range of text generation and sequence modeling tasks?
c021f6928f92582585fc758db20d11a5ad756fca.hypothesis: Introducing an additional residual connection that bypasses layer normalization in Post-LN Transformers will mitigate the vanishing gradient problem, enable stable training of deep architectures, and preserve or enhance the performance advantages of Post-LN over Pre-LN configurations.
c021f6928f92582585fc758db20d11a5ad756fca.proposed_method: A novel modification to the Post-LN Transformer architecture is proposed, termed the Bottom-to-Top (B2T) connection. This method introduces an additional residual connection that skips over all layer normalization operations within each layer except the final one, directly connecting the input of a layer to the output of its feed-forward network. This design is intended to retain gradient flow during backpropagation, similar to Pre-LN, while preserving the transformation effectiveness of higher layers characteristic of Post-LN. The B2T connection is formalized as adding the input and the feed-forward output before the final layer normalization, ensuring that gradients are less affected by the normalization layers and thus mitigating the vanishing gradient problem. The modification is lightweight, does not require additional computational overhead, and is compatible with existing Transformer implementations.
c021f6928f92582585fc758db20d11a5ad756fca.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a wide range of text generation and sequence modeling tasks, including machine translation (using the WMT English-to-German dataset with 4.5M sentence pairs), abstractive summarization (using the Gigaword headline generation dataset and additional news corpora), language modeling (WikiText-103), and automatic speech recognition (LibriSpeech). Both shallow (6-layer) and deep (18-layer, 100-layer) encoder-decoder configurations will be evaluated. Baselines will include standard Post-LN and Pre-LN Transformers, as well as recent stabilization and initialization methods such as DLCL, Admin, T-Fixup, RealFormer, and DeepNet. Evaluation metrics will include BLEU scores for translation, ROUGE for summarization, perplexity for language modeling, and word error rate for ASR. All models will be implemented in fairseq or official repositories, with hyperparameters matched to prior work for comparability. Experiments will assess both training stability (e.g., convergence, gradient norms) and final task performance.
c021f6928f92582585fc758db20d11a5ad756fca.novelty_claims: The proposed B2T connection is a simple yet effective architectural modification that enables stable training of deep Post-LN Transformers without incurring additional computational costs. Unlike prior methods, it directly addresses the vanishing gradient problem associated with layer normalization in deep stacks, while preserving the superior performance of Post-LN in shallow models. The approach is broadly applicable across diverse sequence modeling tasks and outperforms or matches recent state-of-the-art stabilization techniques. This work provides new empirical and theoretical insights into the interplay between layer normalization, residual connections, and gradient flow in deep Transformer architectures.

c022f75b00d795c6297d6a9ea948856ea4d365a1.title: DeepSpeed- Inference: Enabling Efficient Inference of Transformer Models at Unprecedented Scale
c022f75b00d795c6297d6a9ea948856ea4d365a1.research_question: How can transformer model inference be made highly efficient and scalable across a wide range of model sizes, architectures (dense and sparse), application scenarios (latency-critical and throughput-oriented), and hardware configurations, including resource-constrained environments?
c022f75b00d795c6297d6a9ea948856ea4d365a1.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a comprehensive inference system combining optimized single-GPU kernels, advanced parallelism strategies (tensor, pipeline, expert, and data parallelism), and heterogeneous memory utilization (GPU, CPU, NVMe) can dramatically improve the efficiency, scalability, and accessibility of transformer model inference for both dense and sparse models at unprecedented scales.
c022f75b00d795c6297d6a9ea948856ea4d365a1.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a multi-component inference system for transformer models. First, highly optimized single-GPU transformer kernels are developed, leveraging advanced operator fusion (Deep-Fusion) and custom GeMM implementations to maximize memory bandwidth utilization and reduce kernel launch overheads, especially at small batch sizes. Second, the system applies a layered parallelism strategy: tensor parallelism for intra-node scaling, pipeline parallelism with hybrid scheduling and activation offloading for inter-node scaling, and a coordinated combination of tensor, data, and expert parallelism for sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, including novel communication optimizations (Parallelism Coordinated Communication). Third, a heterogeneous inference mode (ZeRO-Inference) is proposed, which enables inference of massive models by streaming weights from CPU or NVMe storage and optimizing memory usage to allow large batch sizes on limited GPU resources. All components are designed to support both latency-sensitive and throughput-oriented scenarios, and to be compatible with various data types (FP32, FP16, INT8).
c022f75b00d795c6297d6a9ea948856ea4d365a1.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate the system on a diverse set of transformer models, including dense models ranging from 1.5B to 530B parameters (e.g., GPT-2, GPT-Neo, GPT-J, GPT-NeoX, LM-175B, LM-530B) and sparse MoE models up to 2 trillion parameters. The evaluation will cover both latency-critical and throughput-oriented scenarios, using metrics such as end-to-end latency, token throughput (tokens/sec), and hardware utilization (TFLOPS, memory bandwidth). Baselines will include state-of-the-art inference systems (e.g., FasterTransformer, ONNXRuntime, TensorRT, FastTransformer) and GPU-only solutions. Experiments will be conducted on single-GPU, multi-GPU (up to hundreds of GPUs), and heterogeneous memory configurations, with detailed breakdowns of performance contributions from each optimization. The system will also be tested on resource-constrained setups to demonstrate accessibility improvements.
c022f75b00d795c6297d6a9ea948856ea4d365a1.novelty_claims: The proposal claims several innovations: (1) introduction of memory-bandwidth-centric kernel fusion and custom GeMM kernels for transformer inference at small batch sizes; (2) a comprehensive, layered parallelism strategy that unifies tensor, pipeline, expert, and data parallelism for both dense and sparse models; (3) novel communication optimizations (Parallelism Coordinated Communication) that reduce all-to-all latency and enable scaling sparse MoE inference to hundreds of GPUs; (4) ZeRO-Inference, a heterogeneous memory solution that enables inference of models up to 25× larger than GPU-only approaches with high throughput on limited GPU resources; and (5) extensive empirical validation demonstrating unprecedented scale (trillion-parameter inference), state-of-the-art latency and throughput, and democratization of large-model inference.

c05d18f89932196b907813f3a107792632afda79.title: Federated Learning Via Inexact ADMM
c05d18f89932196b907813f3a107792632afda79.research_question: How can federated learning optimization algorithms be designed to improve both communication and computational efficiency, while ensuring robust convergence and mitigating the impact of straggler devices in practical, large-scale, and heterogeneous environments?
c05d18f89932196b907813f3a107792632afda79.hypothesis: An inexact alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) framework, with partial device participation and periodic global averaging, will achieve superior communication and computational efficiency, robust convergence under mild conditions, and effective mitigation of the straggler effect compared to existing federated learning algorithms.
c05d18f89932196b907813f3a107792632afda79.proposed_method: A novel federated learning framework based on inexact ADMM will be developed, where the global averaging of model parameters occurs only at specific periodic intervals, reducing the number of communication rounds (CR) required for convergence. At each communication round, the server selects a subset of clients (partial device participation) to update their local parameters, while the remaining clients retain their previous states, thus mitigating the impact of stragglers. Each selected client solves its local subproblem approximately (inexactly), allowing for flexible accuracy and reduced computational burden. The local subproblem is formulated as an augmented Lagrangian minimization, and clients use efficient iterative solvers with controllable accuracy to update their local models. The server aggregates the updated parameters from the selected subset and broadcasts the new global model, ensuring convergence through a carefully designed selection scheme and mild assumptions (gradient Lipschitz continuity and coerciveness of the objective).
c05d18f89932196b907813f3a107792632afda79.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets, including linear regression with non-i.i.d. data and logistic regression tasks. Real datasets such as Qsar oral toxicity (UCI) and real-sim (Libsvm) will be used, with varying numbers of clients, feature dimensions, and participation rates. The proposed method will be compared against several state-of-the-art federated learning baselines, including FedAvg, FedProx, FedAlt, and FedSim. Evaluation metrics will include objective function value, communication rounds (CR), and computational time. Experimental setups will systematically vary key parameters such as the number of clients, participation rate, and frequency of global averaging to assess the impact on efficiency and scalability. All algorithms will be initialized identically, and stopping criteria will be based on gradient norm thresholds or objective value proximity.
c05d18f89932196b907813f3a107792632afda79.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces an inexact ADMM-based federated learning framework that uniquely combines periodic global averaging, partial device participation, and inexact local updates to achieve both communication and computational efficiency. The approach is robust to straggler effects by allowing the server to exclude slow or unresponsive clients from updates without compromising convergence. Convergence to stationary points is guaranteed under only gradient Lipschitz continuity and coerciveness, which are milder conditions than those required by most existing algorithms. Empirical results demonstrate superior numerical performance, achieving faster convergence (in terms of both CR and computational time) compared to several state-of-the-art federated learning algorithms.

c05fddaa0451cf5cfe2e09e7631005f350f49b13.title: What Matters in Data for DPO?
c05fddaa0451cf5cfe2e09e7631005f350f49b13.research_question: What characteristics of preference data are most critical for the performance of Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) in aligning large language models with human preferences?
c05fddaa0451cf5cfe2e09e7631005f350f49b13.hypothesis: The quality of the chosen responses in preference datasets is the primary determinant of DPO performance, while the quality of rejected responses and the preference gap between responses have a comparatively limited impact.
c05fddaa0451cf5cfe2e09e7631005f350f49b13.proposed_method: A systematic investigation will be conducted into how the distributional properties of preference data influence DPO training. Theoretical analysis will be developed to characterize the optimal response distribution under DPO and to formalize the impact of chosen and rejected response quality on the DPO objective and its gradients. Empirical studies will be designed to manipulate the quality of chosen and rejected responses independently, as well as to control the preference gap and the mixture of on-policy versus off-policy data. The methodology will include constructing datasets with controlled response quality tiers, implementing both standard and online DPO training regimes, and analyzing the resulting model behaviors through both loss landscape and performance metrics.
c05fddaa0451cf5cfe2e09e7631005f350f49b13.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize the Allen-AI Llama-3.1-Tulu-3-8B-SFT checkpoint as the base model, with DPO training performed on curated subsets of the Open Assistant 2 and UltraFeedback datasets. Data will be processed to ensure no overlap with SFT training and to provide multiple responses per prompt, each labeled with quality scores from a reward model. DPO datasets will be synthesized to systematically vary the quality of chosen and rejected responses, as well as the preference gap. Evaluation will be conducted using benchmarks such as AlpacaEval-2, MMLU, IFEval, TruthfulQA, and GSM8K, with performance averaged over multiple random seeds. Baselines will include supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and continual SFT on high-quality responses, and comparisons will be made to online DPO with on-policy data generation.
c05fddaa0451cf5cfe2e09e7631005f350f49b13.novelty_claims: The proposed research provides the first comprehensive theoretical and empirical analysis of how preference data characteristics—particularly the quality of chosen responses—affect DPO training and performance. It challenges prevailing assumptions about the importance of preference gap and exposure bias, demonstrating that DPO effectiveness is overwhelmingly anchored in the quality of chosen responses. The findings offer actionable guidance for constructing high-impact preference datasets and inform best practices for LLM alignment strategies.

c07fe613ee8a5ef234c6bc4278ed335f181a964c.title: Standard Gaussian Process is All You Need for High-Dimensional Bayesian Optimization
c07fe613ee8a5ef234c6bc4278ed335f181a964c.research_question: Can standard Bayesian Optimization with Gaussian Processes be effectively applied to high-dimensional optimization problems, and what modifications or insights are necessary to ensure robust performance in such settings?
c07fe613ee8a5ef234c6bc4278ed335f181a964c.hypothesis: Standard Bayesian Optimization with Gaussian Processes, when equipped with appropriate kernel choices and robust length-scale initialization strategies, can achieve state-of-the-art performance in high-dimensional optimization tasks, overcoming previously assumed limitations.
c07fe613ee8a5ef234c6bc4278ed335f181a964c.proposed_method: The proposed approach systematically investigates the use of standard Gaussian Processes (GP) in Bayesian Optimization (BO) for high-dimensional problems. The methodology involves evaluating the impact of different kernel functions, specifically comparing the Square Exponential (SE) kernel and the Matérn-5/2 kernel, on optimization performance. A theoretical analysis is conducted to identify and characterize the gradient vanishing issue that arises with improper length-scale initialization in high dimensions, particularly with the SE kernel. Based on this analysis, a robust length-scale initialization strategy is introduced, where the initial length-scale grows with the square root of the input dimension, mitigating the risk of gradient vanishing and enabling effective GP training. The method is implemented within a standard BO framework, utilizing acquisition functions such as UCB, and is designed to require no additional priors or regularization.
c07fe613ee8a5ef234c6bc4278ed335f181a964c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on twelve benchmark optimization problems, including six synthetic functions (e.g., Ackley, Rosenbrock, Hartmann6, Stybtang) and six real-world tasks (e.g., vehicle design, SVM hyperparameter tuning, rover trajectory planning, DNA regression, neural architecture search, and humanoid trajectory optimization), with input dimensions ranging from 30 to 1,003. The proposed method will be compared against nine state-of-the-art high-dimensional BO baselines, including TreeUCB, RDUCB, HESBO, ALEBO, SaasBO, TURBO, VBO, and two Bayesian neural network-based BO methods. Evaluation metrics will include the maximum function value achieved (optimization performance), mean squared error for GP training, and runtime performance.
