Each method will be run multiple times with shared initial datasets to ensure fair comparison, and both standard and robust initialization strategies will be tested for SE and Matérn kernels.
c07fe613ee8a5ef234c6bc4278ed335f181a964c.novelty_claims: The proposal challenges the prevailing belief that standard BO with Gaussian Processes is unsuitable for high-dimensional optimization, providing both empirical evidence and theoretical justification. A novel theoretical analysis identifies improper length-scale initialization as the primary cause of failure in high dimensions and introduces a simple, robust initialization strategy that fundamentally mitigates gradient vanishing. The approach demonstrates that, with this adjustment, standard BO can match or surpass specialized high-dimensional BO methods without requiring additional structural assumptions, priors, or regularization. The findings advocate for a re-evaluation of standard BO's potential in high-dimensional settings.

c08823c1e2ac64cea04bb3faec280b90245f1ec2.title: Exploring Channel Distinguishability in Local Neighborhoods of the Model Space in Quantum Neural Networks
c08823c1e2ac64cea04bb3faec280b90245f1ec2.research_question: How can quantum neural network (QNN) architectures, specifically their ansatzes, be characterized in terms of their ability to distinguish between quantum channels in the local neighborhood of the model space, and how does this relate to trainability and optimization dynamics in QNNs?
c08823c1e2ac64cea04bb3faec280b90245f1ec2.hypothesis: The distinguishability of quantum channels induced by small parameter updates in QNN ansatzes is limited, especially for hardware-efficient ansatzes (HEAs) with few parameters, which may contribute to the observed trainability issues in QNNs.
c08823c1e2ac64cea04bb3faec280b90245f1ec2.proposed_method: A comprehensive analysis will be conducted on QNN ansatzes by first evaluating the limitations of current expressivity measures, such as closeness to a 2-design, and arguing their inadequacy for capturing the full model space. An alternative, data-agnostic approach will be developed by introducing a measure of channel distinguishability using the diamond norm, quantifying how much a QNN's quantum channel changes under small parameter perturbations. An upper bound on this channel sensitivity will be derived via Taylor expansion, relating the distinguishability directly to the number of parameters and the magnitude of parameter updates. The method will focus on hardware-efficient ansatzes, employing layered architectures with parameterized single-qubit rotations and fixed entangling gates, and will systematically analyze the impact of circuit depth, number of qubits, and parameter count on channel sensitivity.
c08823c1e2ac64cea04bb3faec280b90245f1ec2.experiment_details: Experiments will be performed on QNNs with 1 to 4 qubits and 1 to 5 layers, using combinations of rotation gates (Rx, Ry, Rz) and entangling gates (CNOT, CZ) to construct various HEA architectures. Random perturbation experiments will uniformly sample parameters in [0, 2π], perturbing 95% of them by small percentages (0.1%, 0.5%, 1%) to assess channel sensitivity distributions via the diamond norm. Additionally, training-based experiments will be conducted using binary classification tasks on the wine and breast cancer datasets, with features reduced via PCA and encoded into quantum states. Each architecture will be trained 50 times for 150 iterations using the Adam optimizer, and channel sensitivity will be monitored at each step. Baselines will include both random perturbation and training-based updates, and evaluation metrics will focus on the diamond norm as a measure of distinguishability, with results aggregated using confidence intervals.
c08823c1e2ac64cea04bb3faec280b90245f1ec2.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel, data-agnostic framework for characterizing QNN ansatzes based on local channel distinguishability, moving beyond traditional expressivity measures such as 2-design closeness. It derives and empirically validates an upper bound on channel sensitivity, directly connecting ansatz architecture to trainability. The approach provides new insights into the limitations of small-scale, hardware-efficient QNNs, suggesting that iterative training may be fundamentally ineffective due to minimal distinguishability in the model space. This work pioneers the systematic study of local model space neighborhoods in QNNs and highlights the need for improved initialization and ansatz design strategies.

c0aca900e823edcffd1b9f8b3d12398a76d3a898.title: Direct Motion Models for Assessing Generated Videos
c0aca900e823edcffd1b9f8b3d12398a76d3a898.research_question: How can the temporal consistency and realism of motion in generated videos be automatically and effectively assessed, particularly in ways that align with human judgment and are robust to appearance-based confounds?
c0aca900e823edcffd1b9f8b3d12398a76d3a898.hypothesis: A metric based on learned latent representations of point tracks, rather than pixel-level or appearance-based features, will more accurately and sensitively capture temporal distortions and motion inconsistencies in generated videos, and will better predict human evaluations of motion realism and consistency.
c0aca900e823edcffd1b9f8b3d12398a76d3a898.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed for evaluating generated video quality by focusing on the motion of objects, independent of appearance. The approach will leverage point tracks extracted from videos using a state-of-the-art point tracking model (e.g., BootsTAPIR), which are then encoded into a dense, fixed-size latent representation using a custom trajectory autoencoder architecture (TRAJAN) based on Perceiver-style transformers. The encoder processes variable-sized sets of point trajectories, handling occlusions via attention masks, and produces a compressed motion latent. A decoder reconstructs held-out tracks from random query points, ensuring the latent encodes a dense motion field. The resulting latent representations can be used to compute distances between video distributions (via Fréchet distance), between pairs of videos (via L2 distance), or to assess individual videos (via reconstruction error or Average Jaccard score). This method is designed to be invariant to appearance and sensitive to temporal distortions.
c0aca900e823edcffd1b9f8b3d12398a76d3a898.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world video datasets. Synthetic distortions will be applied to the UCF101 dataset to evaluate metric sensitivity to temporal corruptions, following established protocols. Distribution-level, pairwise, and per-video evaluations will be performed, comparing the proposed method to baselines including FVD, I3D, VideoMAE, optical flow-based metrics (RAFT), and motion histograms. Human studies will be conducted on generated videos from open-source models (e.g., EvalCrafter, VideoPhy) to collect fine-grained ratings on motion quality, realism, consistency, and speed. Evaluation metrics will include Spearman's rank correlation with human judgments, sensitivity to synthetic temporal distortions, and ability to localize motion inconsistencies. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by controlling for overall motion magnitude and using z-scored rater responses.
c0aca900e823edcffd1b9f8b3d12398a76d3a898.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a unified, interpretable metric for video generation quality that is based on learned latent representations of point tracks, rather than appearance or pixel-level features. This approach enables sensitive detection of temporal distortions, provides per-video and distribution-level assessments, and allows for spatiotemporal localization of motion errors. The method is claimed to outperform existing metrics in predicting human ratings of motion realism and consistency, and to offer greater interpretability and robustness to appearance confounds than prior work.

c0ae5848ba0141dd3f827321f46110f52946764b.title: Knowledge Distillation from A Stronger Teacher
c0ae5848ba0141dd3f827321f46110f52946764b.research_question: How can knowledge distillation be improved to enable effective transfer from significantly stronger teacher models to student models, especially when there is a large discrepancy in model capacity or training strategies, across a variety of computer vision tasks?
c0ae5848ba0141dd3f827321f46110f52946764b.hypothesis: Relaxing the requirement for exact prediction matching between teacher and student by instead preserving the inter-class and intra-class relational structure of the teacher's outputs will enable more effective knowledge transfer from stronger teachers, leading to improved student performance compared to traditional knowledge distillation methods.
c0ae5848ba0141dd3f827321f46110f52946764b.proposed_method: A novel knowledge distillation framework is proposed that replaces the conventional Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence loss with a correlation-based loss, specifically leveraging the Pearson correlation coefficient to measure and maximize the alignment between teacher and student outputs. The method introduces two types of relational knowledge: inter-class relations, which capture the correlation between the predicted probability distributions for each instance, and intra-class relations, which capture the correlation of predicted probabilities across all instances for each class. The overall training objective combines the standard classification loss with both inter-class and intra-class relational distillation losses, weighted by tunable hyperparameters. This approach allows the student model to focus on preserving the teacher's preference structure and semantic relationships, rather than matching absolute prediction values, thus mitigating issues arising from large teacher-student discrepancies.
c0ae5848ba0141dd3f827321f46110f52946764b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard image classification datasets (CIFAR-100, ImageNet), object detection (MS COCO), and semantic segmentation (Cityscapes). Student models of varying sizes and architectures (e.g., ResNet-18, MobileNetV2, EfficientNet-B0, Swin-T) will be distilled from stronger teachers (e.g., ResNet-34/50/101/152, Swin-L) trained with both baseline and advanced strategies (including label smoothing, data augmentation, and regularization). Baseline methods for comparison will include vanilla KD, OFD, CRD, SRRL, RKD, and other state-of-the-art distillation approaches. Evaluation metrics will include top-1 and top-5 accuracy for classification, average precision (AP) for detection, and mean Intersection-over-Union (mIoU) for segmentation. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the contributions of inter-class and intra-class relations, and experiments will be run with and without ground-truth supervision to isolate the effect of the proposed relational losses.
c0ae5848ba0141dd3f827321f46110f52946764b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a simple yet effective correlation-based loss for knowledge distillation that explicitly models both inter-class and intra-class relational structures, enabling robust distillation from much stronger teachers. Unlike prior methods, this framework does not require additional intermediate feature alignment or memory banks, and incurs minimal computational overhead. The method is shown to consistently outperform both vanilla KD and more sophisticated feature-based distillation methods across diverse tasks and architectures, particularly when the teacher is significantly stronger due to size or advanced training strategies.

c0b2f6e956bf40a59c766f6da5947cb14e7d1d26.title: Zero-Shot Goal-Directed Dialogue via RL on Imagined Conversations
c0b2f6e956bf40a59c766f6da5947cb14e7d1d26.research_question: How can agents be trained to effectively conduct goal-directed, multi-turn dialogues with humans, optimizing for overall conversational outcomes, without relying on curated human-human dialogue datasets or direct supervised fine-tuning of large language models?
c0b2f6e956bf40a59c766f6da5947cb14e7d1d26.hypothesis: Leveraging large language models to generate diverse, task-relevant synthetic dialogues, followed by offline reinforcement learning on this imagined data, will produce agents that outperform both directly-prompted LLMs and imitation learning approaches on goal-directed dialogue tasks, especially in scenarios requiring information gathering and adaptation to latent user factors.
c0b2f6e956bf40a59c766f6da5947cb14e7d1d26.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that first employs an 'imagination engine' to generate a synthetic dataset of diverse, task-relevant dialogues using a large language model (LLM) conditioned on task descriptions and sampled human personas. The process involves three steps: (1) reasoning to synthesize textual persona descriptions relevant to the task, (2) generating synthetic dialogues between simulated agents and humans with varying personas and success outcomes, and (3) critiquing and refining these dialogues using task-specific criteria to ensure gradual information revelation and realistic conversational flow. The resulting dataset is then post-processed into RL training examples, and a downstream agent (potentially a smaller language model) is trained using offline value-based reinforcement learning (e.g., Implicit Language Q-Learning), optimizing for multi-turn, goal-directed objectives.
c0b2f6e956bf40a59c766f6da5947cb14e7d1d26.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two goal-directed dialogue tasks: personalized instruction (where the agent must teach a concept tailored to the user's background knowledge) and preference elicitation (where the agent must recommend activities based on latent user preferences). The synthetic dialogue datasets will be generated using GPT-3.5 as the LLM, while downstream agents will be trained using a smaller GPT-2 model. Baselines will include directly-prompted GPT-3.5 agents and agents trained via behavioral cloning (BC) and filtered BC on the same synthetic data. Evaluation will involve both user studies (with 12 participants rating agents on task success, naturalness, information-gathering, and satisfaction) and large-scale simulated evaluations with GPT-generated users. Metrics will include Likert-scale ratings, success rates (e.g., correct recommendation within a fixed number of turns), utterance conciseness, and robustness in challenging or out-of-distribution scenarios.
c0b2f6e956bf40a59c766f6da5947cb14e7d1d26.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a zero-shot RL algorithm for goal-directed dialogue that requires only a task description as input, eliminating the need for curated human-human datasets. The imagination engine is a novel mechanism for generating diverse, instructive synthetic dialogues tailored to any task, leveraging LLMs' strengths in emulating realistic but suboptimal conversations. This is the first instance of using synthetic dialogue generation for reinforcement learning rather than supervised learning. The method enables the training of effective, smaller dialogue agents by distilling knowledge from large LLMs, and demonstrates superior performance and robustness compared to both direct LLM prompting and imitation learning baselines.

c0c5c078d7f229ff028093f6dd4ba512e2f33fdc.title: PoLAR: Polar-Decomposed Low-Rank Adapter Representation
c0c5c078d7f229ff028093f6dd4ba512e2f33fdc.research_question: How can the expressiveness and convergence speed of parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods for large-scale language models be improved by better utilizing the allocated low-rank subspace?
c0c5c078d7f229ff028093f6dd4ba512e2f33fdc.hypothesis: Parameterizing low-rank updates using polar decomposition, with direction matrices constrained to Stiefel manifolds and an unconstrained scale matrix, will increase the stable rank of updates, mitigate directional diversity collapse, and lead to improved fine-tuning performance and faster convergence compared to classical low-rank adapter parameterizations.
c0c5c078d7f229ff028093f6dd4ba512e2f33fdc.proposed_method: A novel low-rank adapter parameterization, termed PoLAR, will be developed by factorizing the low-rank update as the product of two column-orthogonal direction matrices (constrained to Stiefel manifolds) and an unconstrained scale matrix. This approach enforces orthogonality in the update directions, thereby increasing the stable rank and promoting diversity in the learned updates. The optimization will be performed using Riemannian optimization techniques, specifically leveraging a landing field method that avoids costly retraction operations, making the approach scalable to large models and compatible with GPU hardware. The method will be implemented as a drop-in replacement for existing low-rank adaptation pipelines, requiring only matrix multiplications for efficiency.
c0c5c078d7f229ff028093f6dd4ba512e2f33fdc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of large language models, including DeBERTa-v3, Llama-2-7B, Gemma-3-12B, and Gemma-3-27B, covering both masked and autoregressive architectures. Evaluation will span three benchmark domains: general language understanding (GLUE), commonsense reasoning (BoolQ, PIQA, SIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-e, ARC-c, OBQA), and mathematical problem solving (MetaMathQA, GSM8K, MATH). Baselines will include classical LoRA and DoRA parameterizations, as well as other recent low-rank adaptation variants. Metrics such as accuracy and stable rank will be used to assess performance, and runtime efficiency will be measured on GPU hardware, comparing the proposed landing method to traditional retraction-based Riemannian optimization. Hyperparameters such as adapter rank and regularization strength will be systematically varied to analyze their effects.
c0c5c078d7f229ff028093f6dd4ba512e2f33fdc.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a polar decomposition-based parameterization for low-rank adapters that enforces orthogonality in update directions, directly addressing the issue of low stable rank and diversity collapse in classical approaches. The co-design of architecture and optimizer, specifically the use of a landing field for Riemannian optimization, enables scalable and efficient training on large models. Theoretical analysis demonstrates exponentially faster convergence rates compared to standard low-rank parameterizations, and empirical results show consistent improvements in both stable rank and downstream task performance across multiple benchmarks and model sizes.

c0d8e5ee66c279299012cc3b8d0519011b3f4998.title: KTO: Model Alignment as Prospect Theoretic Optimization
c0d8e5ee66c279299012cc3b8d0519011b3f4998.research_question: How can model alignment objectives for large language models be designed to more closely reflect human decision-making biases, and does directly optimizing for human utility (as described by prospect theory) improve alignment performance compared to existing preference-based methods?
c0d8e5ee66c279299012cc3b8d0519011b3f4998.hypothesis: Directly optimizing large language models using a loss function grounded in prospect theory, which models human utility and biases such as loss aversion, will match or exceed the performance of existing preference-based alignment methods, even when trained on weaker but more abundant binary feedback signals.
c0d8e5ee66c279299012cc3b8d0519011b3f4998.proposed_method: A novel alignment framework, Kahneman-Tversky Optimization (KTO), will be developed that formulates model alignment as an optimization problem grounded in prospect theory. The method will define a human-aware loss (HALO) based on a value function inspired by the Kahneman-Tversky model, incorporating key properties such as loss aversion and risk sensitivity. The loss will directly maximize the utility of model generations, using a logistic function to ensure numerical stability and explicit hyperparameters to control risk and loss aversion. The approach will require only a binary signal indicating whether an output is desirable or undesirable, and will estimate a reference point (e.g., a KL divergence-based baseline) for each microbatch to reflect the relative utility of outputs. Hyperparameters such as learning rate, batch size, and risk/loss aversion coefficients will be tuned to optimize performance across different data imbalances and model scales.
c0d8e5ee66c279299012cc3b8d0519011b3f4998.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple large language model families (e.g., Llama, Pythia, Mistral, Qwen) ranging from 1B to 30B parameters. Models will be aligned using KTO and compared to baselines including Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), offline PPO variants, Conditional SFT, and Sequence Likelihood Calibration. Datasets will include preference-based datasets such as Anthropic-HH, OpenAssistant, SHP, and UltraFeedback, as well as binary feedback settings (e.g., one output per input). Evaluation will use both closed-ended tasks (e.g., GSM8K for mathematical reasoning, MMLU, BigBench-Hard, HumanEval) and open-ended judgments from humans and GPT-4, with metrics such as win rate against SFT targets and standard accuracy measures. Experiments will also explore the effects of data imbalance, absence of SFT, and the use of reference-free variants. Hyperparameter sweeps and ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of different value function designs and training configurations.
c0d8e5ee66c279299012cc3b8d0519011b3f4998.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new class of human-aware loss functions (HALOs) for model alignment, explicitly grounded in prospect theory and human utility modeling. KTO is the first alignment method to directly maximize prospect-theoretic utility rather than preference likelihood, enabling effective use of abundant binary feedback. The method demonstrates that preference data is not strictly necessary for high-quality alignment, and that inductive biases in the loss function are critical for performance. Theoretical analysis provides new insights into the limitations of preference-based objectives and the robustness of KTO to noisy or intransitive feedback. The proposal also establishes that there is no universally superior alignment loss; instead, the optimal loss depends on the inductive biases appropriate for the specific setting.

c0ebf1852b82d4ca52ab8429003be4bff884bc5b.title: LiNeS: Post-training Layer Scaling Prevents Forgetting and Enhances Model Merging
c0ebf1852b82d4ca52ab8429003be4bff884bc5b.research_question: How can post-training interventions be designed to mitigate catastrophic forgetting and enhance generalization in fine-tuned and merged models, particularly in both single-task and multi-task scenarios across vision and NLP domains?
c0ebf1852b82d4ca52ab8429003be4bff884bc5b.hypothesis: Scaling parameter updates in neural networks based on layer depth after fine-tuning—specifically, downscaling updates in shallow layers—will preserve generalization abilities of pre-trained models while retaining fine-tuned task performance, and will reduce negative task interference when merging models.
c0ebf1852b82d4ca52ab8429003be4bff884bc5b.proposed_method: A post-training editing technique, termed Layer-increasing Network Scaling (LiNeS), will be developed to linearly scale the parameter updates (residuals) of a neural network according to layer depth. The method computes the difference between the fine-tuned and pre-trained weights (the task vector), and applies a scaling factor that increases from shallow to deep layers. Specifically, for each layer ℓ, the update is scaled by λ(ℓ) = α + β*(ℓ-1)/(L-1), where L is the total number of layers and α, β are hyperparameters. This approach preserves general features in shallow layers (by keeping updates small) while allowing deeper layers to encode task-specific information. The method is applicable both to single-task fine-tuning and to the merging of multiple task-specific models, where the merged residual is similarly scaled before being added back to the pre-trained weights.
c0ebf1852b82d4ca52ab8429003be4bff884bc5b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of benchmarks in computer vision and natural language processing. In vision, CLIP ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16, and ViT-L/14 models will be fine-tuned on 8, 14, and 20-task classification benchmarks, with performance measured on both target (fine-tuned) and control (zero-shot) tasks. In NLP, T5-large models will be evaluated on 7-task, 8-task QA, and 11-task benchmarks. Baseline comparisons will include standard fine-tuning, weight interpolation (WiSE-FT), and state-of-the-art model merging methods such as Task Arithmetic, Ties-merging, and Consensus Merging. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on target and control tasks, out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization, and Pareto fronts for multi-objective scenarios. Additional experiments will assess the method's impact on merging LLM policies trained with different reward functions (e.g., RLHF on RedditSummary), using both in-domain and OOD datasets. Hyperparameters (α, β) will be tuned per scenario to optimize the trade-off between task performance and generalization.
c0ebf1852b82d4ca52ab8429003be4bff884bc5b.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple, computationally efficient, and post-training approach to mitigate catastrophic forgetting and task interference by leveraging the inductive bias that shallow layers encode general features. Unlike prior methods that require modifying the fine-tuning process or training additional parameters, LiNeS operates directly in weight space and is orthogonal to existing merging and interpolation techniques. The method is shown to consistently improve both single-task and multi-task performance, enhance out-of-distribution generalization, and Pareto-dominate baselines in merging scenarios, including LLM policy alignment. Its plug-and-play nature and minimal computational overhead make it broadly applicable across architectures and domains.

c0f75f38d928a40dc1bd0e74e06a7b4a6913ee4c.title: Self-Repellent Random Walks on General Graphs - Achieving Minimal Sampling Variance via Nonlinear Markov Chains
c0f75f38d928a40dc1bd0e74e06a7b4a6913ee4c.research_question: How can random walk-based sampling methods on general graphs be improved to achieve lower sampling variance, particularly in the context of Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) procedures, while maintaining scalability and robustness over large, complex network topologies?
c0f75f38d928a40dc1bd0e74e06a7b4a6913ee4c.hypothesis: Introducing a self-repellent mechanism into random walks, parameterized by a tunable parameter, will lead to a reduction in asymptotic sampling variance compared to classical Markov chain-based random walks, with the variance decreasing as the strength of the self-repellence increases.
c0f75f38d928a40dc1bd0e74e06a7b4a6913ee4c.proposed_method: A nonlinear Markov chain framework will be developed, termed Self-Repellent Random Walks (SRRW), in which the transition probability to a node is inversely related to the number of times that node has been visited in the past. The transition kernel is parameterized by a positive real parameter α, controlling the strength of self-repellence: higher α makes the walk less likely to revisit frequently visited nodes. The transition probability from node i to node j is proportional to the base Markov chain transition probability, multiplied by a factor that decreases as the empirical occupation measure of node j increases, specifically using a polynomial form (x_j / μ_j)^(-α), where x_j is the empirical occupation of node j and μ_j is the target stationary distribution. The method is designed to require only local information (neighboring nodes' statistics) and is scale-invariant, making it suitable for large graphs. Theoretical analysis will establish almost sure convergence of the empirical distribution to the target distribution, derive a central limit theorem for the empirical measure, and provide an explicit form for the asymptotic covariance matrix as a function of α.
c0f75f38d928a40dc1bd0e74e06a7b4a6913ee4c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on general undirected graphs, including real-world networks such as the wiki-Vote graph (889 nodes, 2914 edges), using the Metropolis-Hastings random walk as the base Markov chain for unbiased graph sampling. The SRRW will be compared against standard MCMC methods (α = 0) and non-backtracking random walks. Evaluation metrics will include total variation distance (TVD) between the empirical and target distributions, mean squared error (MSE) of estimators for graph statistics (e.g., average degree), and the asymptotic variance of MCMC estimators. Multiple values of α, including time-varying α schedules, will be tested to assess both transient and asymptotic performance. Results will be averaged over multiple simulation runs (e.g., 500) to ensure statistical significance.
c0f75f38d928a40dc1bd0e74e06a7b4a6913ee4c.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a general class of self-repellent random walks on arbitrary graphs that interact with the entire past history of the process, rather than just the most recent steps. It provides a theoretically grounded approach that guarantees convergence to any prescribed target distribution while achieving strictly lower asymptotic sampling variance than classical Markov chains, with the variance provably decreasing as the self-repellence parameter increases. The method is robust, scalable, and requires only local information, making it practical for large networks. Theoretical contributions include explicit characterization of the asymptotic covariance matrix, proof of monotonic variance reduction (in Loewner ordering), and demonstration that the variance can be made arbitrarily small, outperforming even i.i.d. samplers for sufficiently large α. Empirical results further validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the advantage of time-varying self-repellence schedules.

c11983c44f5c149454ea54d45c7a6abd15cedc9d.title: The Generative Leap: Sharp Sample Complexity for Efficiently Learning Gaussian Multi-Index Models
c11983c44f5c149454ea54d45c7a6abd15cedc9d.research_question: What is the optimal sample complexity for efficiently learning the hidden subspace in high-dimensional Gaussian multi-index models using polynomial-time algorithms, and how can this complexity be characterized in terms of intrinsic properties of the data distribution?
c11983c44f5c149454ea54d45c7a6abd15cedc9d.hypothesis: The sample complexity required for efficient agnostic estimation of the hidden subspace in Gaussian multi-index models is governed by a generative leap exponent, and a sequential spectral estimation procedure based on Hermite kernel U-statistics can achieve this optimal complexity without prior knowledge of the model.
c11983c44f5c149454ea54d45c7a6abd15cedc9d.proposed_method: A new sequential estimation framework is developed for learning the hidden subspace in generic Gaussian multi-index models. The approach introduces the generative leap exponent, a generalization of the generative exponent for single-index models, which quantifies the minimal Hermite polynomial degree needed at each step to reveal new directions in the subspace. The method constructs a leap decomposition of the index space and iteratively estimates directions using spectral analysis of Hermite kernel U-statistics, which aggregate information from pairwise sample interactions via positive definite kernels. At each iteration, the estimator recovers the relevant subspace by computing the top eigenvectors of a matrix formed from the U-statistic, and then augments the label with projections onto the recovered subspace for the next step. This procedure is repeated until the full index space is recovered, with each leap governed by the corresponding Hermite degree.
c11983c44f5c149454ea54d45c7a6abd15cedc9d.experiment_details: Experiments are proposed on a range of synthetic and real datasets that instantiate various Gaussian multi-index models, including deep ReLU networks with bias, general deep neural networks with r-dimensional first hidden layers, Gaussian parity functions, and intersections of half-spaces. The proposed algorithm will be evaluated against state-of-the-art baselines such as iterated filtered PCA, moment-based methods, and gradient-based learning algorithms. Evaluation metrics will include subspace recovery error (e.g., principal angle or projection distance), sample complexity required for accurate recovery, and computational efficiency. The experimental setup will systematically vary the ambient dimension d, intrinsic dimension r, and generative leap exponent k⋆ to empirically validate the theoretical sample complexity bounds and demonstrate the computational-statistical gap.
c11983c44f5c149454ea54d45c7a6abd15cedc9d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the generative leap exponent as a sharp, distribution-dependent characterization of sample complexity for multi-index models, extending prior results from single-index settings. The sequential Hermite kernel U-statistic estimator is novel in its ability to recover the hidden subspace optimally without prior knowledge of the model, matching computational lower bounds in the low-degree polynomial framework. The approach provides the first general, agnostic, and efficient algorithm for subspace recovery in Gaussian multi-index models with provably optimal sample complexity, and establishes a computational-to-statistical gap for cases where the generative leap exponent exceeds two. The method also generalizes and improves upon previous results for specific function classes, such as deep neural networks and polynomial multi-index models.

c11ea9618aab887b4feaf07b306d07425a9f1bdc.title: Weakly Supervised Regression with Interval Targets
c11ea9618aab887b4feaf07b306d07425a9f1bdc.research_question: How can regression models be effectively learned from weakly supervised data where only interval targets, rather than exact real-valued targets, are available for each instance?
c11ea9618aab887b4feaf07b306d07425a9f1bdc.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a statistically consistent regression model can be learned from interval target data by appropriately modeling the data generation process and employing loss functions or constraints that leverage the interval information, resulting in performance comparable to fully supervised regression.
c11ea9618aab887b4feaf07b306d07425a9f1bdc.proposed_method: A novel statistical model will be developed to describe the data generation process for regression with interval targets (RIT), ensuring that the true target value always lies within the provided interval. Two main approaches will be explored: (1) a simple selection method that chooses a representative value (such as the middlemost value) within the interval as the training target, and (2) a statistically consistent limiting method that constrains model predictions to fall within the interval, using a convex surrogate loss based on the maximum deviation from the interval bounds. The limiting method will be theoretically analyzed for consistency and estimation error bounds, and will be implemented using empirical risk minimization with the surrogate loss. The approach will be compatible with both linear and neural network models.
c11ea9618aab887b4feaf07b306d07425a9f1bdc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of datasets, including computer vision datasets (AgeDB, IMDB-WIKI), a natural language processing dataset (STS-B), and several UCI Machine Learning Repository datasets (Abalone, Airfoil, Auto-mpg, Housing, Concrete, Power-plant). For each dataset, interval targets will be generated by randomly sampling intervals of specified maximum size q around the true target. Baseline methods will include leftmost, rightmost, and middlemost value selection strategies, as well as established interval-valued data prediction methods (CRM, SINN, RANN, IN). Evaluation metrics will include mean squared error (MSE), mean absolute error (MAE), Pearson correlation, and geometric mean. Both linear and multilayer perceptron models will be used for tabular data, ResNet-50 for image data, and BiLSTM-based models for text data. The performance of the proposed method will be compared to baselines under varying interval sizes and training set sizes, with repeated sampling and training to assess robustness.
c11ea9618aab887b4feaf07b306d07425a9f1bdc.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a statistically consistent framework for regression with interval targets, including a new data generation model and a limiting method with theoretical guarantees of consistency and estimation error bounds. Unlike prior approaches, the method explicitly models the interval annotation process and leverages the full interval information rather than reducing it to a point estimate. The approach is shown to be robust to increasing interval sizes and outperforms both simple selection strategies and existing interval-valued regression methods across diverse domains. Theoretical analysis and empirical results demonstrate that the method can recover the optimal fully supervised regression model as the amount of interval-labeled data increases.

c12b39fa51eb2155e4592be3dc9586853b178ba4.title: Information-theoretic generalization bounds for learning from quantum data
c12b39fa51eb2155e4592be3dc9586853b178ba4.research_question: How can a unified information-theoretic framework be developed to provide generalization error bounds for a wide range of quantum learning tasks, including those involving classical-quantum data, and what are the implications of such bounds for the design and analysis of quantum learning algorithms?
c12b39fa51eb2155e4592be3dc9586853b178ba4.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that generalization error in quantum learning can be effectively bounded using classical and quantum information-theoretic quantities, such as mutual information and Holevo information, under appropriate concentration conditions on the loss observables and data distributions.
c12b39fa51eb2155e4592be3dc9586853b178ba4.proposed_method: A general mathematical formalism will be constructed to model quantum learning procedures as channels acting on classical-quantum (CQ) data, producing hypotheses that may be classical or quantum. The framework will define risk and generalization error in terms of quantum observables and extend classical notions such as empirical and true risk to the quantum setting by introducing separate test and training subsystems, which may be entangled or correlated. Information-theoretic tools, including quantum mutual information, Holevo information, and quantum concentration inequalities, will be employed to derive upper bounds on the expected generalization error. The methodology will leverage quantum analogues of classical decoupling lemmas, and employ sub-gaussian moment generating function (MGF) bounds for both classical and quantum observables to control the concentration of the loss around its expectation.
c12b39fa51eb2155e4592be3dc9586853b178ba4.experiment_details: The proposed framework will be instantiated and validated through theoretical analysis and application to several canonical quantum learning scenarios, such as PAC learning of quantum states, quantum parameter estimation, learning classical functions from entangled quantum data, and variational quantum machine learning. For each scenario, the framework will be specialized to the relevant data structure (e.g., i.i.d. samples, entangled states), and the generalization bounds will be computed in terms of the information-theoretic quantities and sub-gaussian parameters. Comparisons will be made to existing sample complexity results and classical bounds, with particular attention to how the quantum information measures influence the scaling with data size and Hilbert space dimension. Evaluation metrics will include the tightness of the generalization error bounds and their dependence on the mutual information between data and hypothesis.
c12b39fa51eb2155e4592be3dc9586853b178ba4.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified and general information-theoretic framework for quantum learning, capable of capturing a broad spectrum of quantum learning tasks within a single formalism. It establishes the first generalization error bounds for quantum learners in terms of both classical and quantum information measures, including quantum mutual information and Holevo information, under sub-gaussian concentration assumptions. The approach provides a new perspective on the bias-variance tradeoff in quantum learning, clarifies the interplay between classical and quantum sample complexity, and extends classical information-theoretic generalization analysis to the fully quantum domain. The framework is versatile, encompassing scenarios such as learning from entangled data, quantum differential privacy, and variational quantum machine learning, thus laying the groundwork for a unified theory of generalization in quantum learning.

c12c87607371d095cb3e149fe20fef5acd9d116f.title: A Practical Method for Constructing Equivariant Multilayer Perceptrons for Arbitrary Matrix Groups
c12c87607371d095cb3e149fe20fef5acd9d116f.research_question: How can a general and efficient method be developed for constructing multilayer perceptrons that are equivariant to arbitrary matrix groups, enabling neural networks to exploit symmetries present in diverse data domains such as images, graphs, point clouds, and physical systems?
c12c87607371d095cb3e149fe20fef5acd9d116f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a polynomial-time algorithm can be formulated to construct all linear layers equivariant to arbitrary matrix groups, and that neural network architectures built using these layers will generalize better and outperform non-equivariant baselines on tasks with underlying symmetries.
c12c87607371d095cb3e149fe20fef5acd9d116f.proposed_method: A general framework will be developed to characterize and construct all linear layers that are equivariant to arbitrary matrix groups, given finite-dimensional representations of the group acting on input and output spaces. The method reduces the equivariance constraints to a finite set of linear constraints, specifically M + D constraints where M is the number of discrete group generators and D is the dimension of the group. These constraints are solved using a polynomial-time algorithm based on singular value decomposition (SVD) or an efficient Krylov subspace method, which exploits the Kronecker and block structure of the group representations. The resulting equivariant linear layers are combined with gated nonlinearities and a novel bilinear layer to form an Equivariant Multilayer Perceptron (EMLP) architecture, which can be instantiated for any matrix group by specifying its generators and representations. The approach is designed to be scalable to high-dimensional representations and supports arbitrary tensor representations, enabling application to a wide range of symmetry groups.
c12c87607371d095cb3e149fe20fef5acd9d116f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic and real-world tasks requiring equivariance to various matrix groups, including previously unexplored groups such as O(5), SO(1,3), Sp(n), and the Rubik’s cube group. Datasets will include synthetic invariant and equivariant regression tasks (e.g., O(5)-invariant regression, SO(3)-equivariant moment of inertia prediction), Lorentz-invariant particle scattering problems, and dynamical systems with known symmetries (e.g., double pendulum with O(2) symmetry). Baselines will include standard multilayer perceptrons (MLPs), MLPs trained with data augmentation to enforce symmetry, and other equivariant architectures where applicable. Evaluation metrics will include prediction accuracy, data efficiency (performance as a function of training set size), and conservation of physical quantities (e.g., angular momentum) in dynamical systems. Experimental setups will ensure fair comparison by matching model capacity and training procedures across methods.
c12c87607371d095cb3e149fe20fef5acd9d116f.novelty_claims: The proposed method provides the first completely general and efficient algorithm for constructing equivariant linear layers for arbitrary matrix groups and representations, subsuming prior specialized approaches for specific groups as special cases. It enables the construction of equivariant neural networks for groups and representations that were previously infeasible, including high-dimensional and non-compact groups. The approach introduces a scalable constraint-solving algorithm that leverages group structure for computational efficiency, and a flexible neural network architecture (EMLP) that can be instantiated for any symmetry group. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior generalization and data efficiency compared to both non-equivariant and data-augmented baselines, as well as the ability to model complex physical systems with exact or approximate conservation laws.

c12dd3380cd6bb46d033aef2624467871adbd6e2.title: FedTGP: Trainable Global Prototypes with Adaptive-Margin-Enhanced Contrastive Learning for Data and Model Heterogeneity in Federated Learning
c12dd3380cd6bb46d033aef2624467871adbd6e2.research_question: How can federated learning be improved to effectively handle both data and model heterogeneity, while minimizing communication costs and preserving privacy, especially in scenarios where clients possess diverse model architectures and non-identically distributed data?
c12dd3380cd6bb46d033aef2624467871adbd6e2.hypothesis: Introducing trainable global prototypes, optimized with adaptive-margin-enhanced contrastive learning, will improve the separability and semantic quality of shared knowledge in heterogeneous federated learning, resulting in superior client performance compared to naive prototype aggregation and existing state-of-the-art methods.
c12dd3380cd6bb46d033aef2624467871adbd6e2.proposed_method: A novel federated learning framework is proposed in which the server maintains a set of trainable global prototypes (TGP) for each class. These prototypes are optimized using an adaptive-margin-enhanced contrastive learning (ACL) objective that encourages large inter-class separability and semantic alignment with client prototypes. The margin in the contrastive loss is adaptively set in each communication round to match the maximum margin among client prototypes, avoiding overlarge margins in early training and ensuring robust prototype separation. The server-side prototype optimization is decoupled from client model architectures, requiring only prototype vectors from clients, and does not require access to client model parameters or private data distributions. The server sends the optimized global prototypes to clients, who then use them to guide local training by minimizing a supervised loss combined with a prototype alignment term, thereby improving local feature separability.
c12dd3380cd6bb46d033aef2624467871adbd6e2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four popular image classification datasets (Cifar10, Cifar100, Flowers102, Tiny-ImageNet) under both pathological and practical non-IID data settings. Twelve heterogeneous model architectures, including various CNNs and ResNets, will be used to simulate model heterogeneity. The proposed method will be compared against six state-of-the-art baselines: LG-FedAvg, FedGen, FML, FedKD, FedDistill, and FedProto. Evaluation metrics will include test accuracy, communication cost per iteration, and robustness to increasing model heterogeneity, number of clients, and feature dimensionality. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the adaptive margin, the trainable processing network, and other key components. Hyperparameter sensitivity will be evaluated for the margin threshold and server training epochs.
c12dd3380cd6bb46d033aef2624467871adbd6e2.novelty_claims: The approach introduces the concept of trainable global prototypes for federated learning, optimized with an adaptive-margin-enhanced contrastive loss that dynamically adjusts inter-class separation based on client prototype statistics. This method eliminates the need to share model parameters or private class distribution information, reducing privacy risks and communication overhead. The framework is robust to both data and model heterogeneity, and achieves superior accuracy compared to existing prototype-based and knowledge distillation methods, as demonstrated by extensive experiments. The adaptive margin mechanism and decoupled server-side prototype optimization are claimed as key innovations.

c13fe83e88cd30149ab1f264e93d26817e192b0d.title: Generalized Polyak Step Size for First Order Optimization with Momentum
c13fe83e88cd30149ab1f264e93d26817e192b0d.research_question: How can adaptive step size policies be generalized and effectively applied to first-order optimization algorithms with momentum, particularly in settings where the condition number of the problem is unknown or difficult to estimate, and how do these adaptive methods compare to existing approaches in terms of stability, convergence, and performance on large-scale machine learning tasks?
c13fe83e88cd30149ab1f264e93d26817e192b0d.hypothesis: Adaptive step size frameworks, inspired by the Polyak step size, can be generalized to momentum-based first-order optimization methods, resulting in algorithms that are less sensitive to hyperparameter choices, more stable on ill-conditioned problems, and capable of achieving superior or comparable performance to state-of-the-art adaptive and fixed step size methods in both deterministic and stochastic settings.
c13fe83e88cd30149ab1f264e93d26817e192b0d.proposed_method: A generic Adaptive Learning Rate (ALR) framework will be developed for momentum-based first-order optimization algorithms, specifically targeting heavy-ball (HB) and moving averaged gradient (MAG) methods. The adaptive step size will be derived by minimizing the upper bound of the distance to the optimum, using available function values and gradients, and incorporating momentum terms. Two main variants, ALR-HB and ALR-MAG, will be formulated, with step size rules that adaptively combine current loss, gradient norms, and momentum directions. The framework will be extended to stochastic settings (ALR-SHB and ALR-SMAG) by using mini-batch estimates and introducing scaling and upper-bound hyperparameters to ensure practical stability and convergence. The approach will also be adapted for use with Nesterov accelerated gradient and will allow for the incorporation of weight decay for improved generalization in deep learning.
c13fe83e88cd30149ab1f264e93d26817e192b0d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. For deterministic settings, ill-conditioned least-squares problems will be generated with known condition numbers to evaluate convergence and sensitivity to hyperparameters, comparing ALR-HB and ALR-MAG against baselines such as gradient descent with Polyak step size, heavy-ball with optimal and tuned parameters, L4Mom, AGM, AHB, and AdGD-accel. For stochastic settings, large-scale machine learning tasks will be addressed, including training deep neural networks on CIFAR10, CIFAR100, and Tiny-ImageNet datasets using architectures like WRN-28-10 and DenseNet121. Baselines will include SGD with momentum (constant, step-decay, cosine), Adam, SPS max, SLS-acc, L4Mom, and AdSGD. Evaluation metrics will include convergence rate, training loss, and test accuracy. Additional experiments will assess the effect of warmup heuristics and weight decay on generalization. Hyperparameters will be tuned via grid search or set according to theoretical guidance, and results will be averaged over multiple runs to account for randomness.
c13fe83e88cd30149ab1f264e93d26817e192b0d.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces the first principled and general adaptive step size policy for momentum-based first-order optimization methods, extending the Polyak step size to heavy-ball, MAG, and Nesterov accelerated algorithms. The approach provides theoretical guarantees, including global linear convergence under semi-strong convexity and smoothness, and demonstrates reduced sensitivity to hyperparameter choices compared to existing methods. The stochastic extensions (ALR-SHB and ALR-SMAG) offer the first linear convergence guarantees for SGD with momentum under adaptive Polyak-inspired step sizes, and the methods outperform or match state-of-the-art adaptive and fixed step size algorithms in both convex and deep learning settings. The framework also enables efficient integration of weight decay and warmup techniques, further improving generalization and practical performance.

c14572cbcca22f4257ea9fb9f85b1eac8cb6ab88.title: FairWASP: Fast and Optimal Fair Wasserstein Pre-processing
c14572cbcca22f4257ea9fb9f85b1eac8cb6ab88.research_question: How can disparities in machine learning model outputs across different subgroups be reduced through pre-processing of training data, while maintaining compatibility with any downstream classification algorithm and preserving data utility?
c14572cbcca22f4257ea9fb9f85b1eac8cb6ab88.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a pre-processing approach based on optimal sample reweighting, which minimizes the Wasserstein distance to the original dataset while satisfying demographic parity constraints, can effectively reduce disparities across subgroups without significantly altering the data distribution or harming downstream model accuracy.
c14572cbcca22f4257ea9fb9f85b1eac8cb6ab88.proposed_method: A novel pre-processing framework, FairWASP, is developed to assign integer-valued sample weights to training data such that the reweighted dataset minimizes the Wasserstein distance to the original data distribution, subject to empirical demographic parity constraints. The approach reformulates the pre-processing task as a large-scale mixed-integer program (MIP), which is then relaxed to a linear program (LP) for tractability. A highly efficient algorithm based on the cutting plane method is proposed to solve the dual of the LP, leveraging the structure of the fairness constraints and the sparsity of the problem. The method returns integer weights, allowing the reweighted dataset to be constructed by duplicating or eliminating samples, ensuring compatibility with any classification algorithm. An extension, FairWASP-PW, is also proposed to handle pairwise demographic parity constraints by optimizing over both the sample weights and the target marginal distributions using zero-th order optimization.
c14572cbcca22f4257ea9fb9f85b1eac8cb6ab88.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. The synthetic dataset is designed to induce dependency between features and protected variables, allowing for controlled evaluation of fairness interventions. Real datasets include Adult, Drug, Communities and Crime, and German Credit, all commonly used in fairness research. The proposed method is compared against state-of-the-art pre-processing baselines such as Disparate Impact Remover, Learning Fair Representations, Reweighing, and Optimized Pre-processing. Evaluation metrics include demographic parity (measured as the absolute difference in mean classifier outcomes between groups) and downstream classifier accuracy (AUC). Experimental setup involves training a multi-layer perceptron classifier on the pre-processed datasets, with results averaged over multiple train/test splits. Computational efficiency is benchmarked against commercial solvers (Gurobi, Mosek), with runtime and scalability evaluated for increasing dataset sizes.
c14572cbcca22f4257ea9fb9f85b1eac8cb6ab88.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first pre-processing approach to minimize the overall distributional distance (Wasserstein distance) from the original data while enforcing fairness via sample reweighting. Theoretical results show that integer weights are optimal, enabling the method to be interpreted as sample duplication or elimination, thus ensuring compatibility with any downstream classifier. The cutting plane algorithm for solving the reformulated LP is highly efficient, vastly outperforming state-of-the-art commercial solvers in both speed and scalability. The extension to pairwise demographic parity constraints further broadens the applicability of the framework. Empirical results demonstrate that the method achieves competitive or superior fairness-utility tradeoffs compared to existing approaches.

c1522fcc9ad365c79910a30352dcbe5e567a262b.title: Bagging is an Optimal PAC Learner
c1522fcc9ad365c79910a30352dcbe5e567a262b.research_question: What is the optimal sample complexity for PAC (Probably Approximately Correct) learning in the realizable setting, and can a practical and widely used ensemble method achieve this optimality?
c1522fcc9ad365c79910a30352dcbe5e567a262b.hypothesis: The classic bagging (bootstrap aggregation) algorithm is an optimal PAC learner in the realizable setting, achieving the theoretically minimal sample complexity for learning any concept class of fixed VC-dimension.
c1522fcc9ad365c79910a30352dcbe5e567a262b.proposed_method: The proposed method systematically analyzes the bagging (bootstrap aggregation) algorithm in the context of PAC learning. Bagging is implemented by repeatedly sampling t bootstrap samples (with replacement) of size n from a training set S of m i.i.d. examples, where each sample is used to train a hypothesis using empirical risk minimization (ERM) over the concept class C. The final output is a majority vote (or equivalently, a voting classifier) over the t hypotheses. Theoretical analysis is conducted to show that, for appropriately chosen t = O(log(m/δ)) and n in [0.02m, m], the majority vote hypothesis achieves the optimal PAC sample complexity. The proof leverages margin-based analysis and constructs structured groupings of bootstrap samples to relate the performance of bagging to that of an idealized voting classifier averaging over all possible bootstrap samples.
c1522fcc9ad365c79910a30352dcbe5e567a262b.experiment_details: Theoretical results are established for all distributions D over an input domain X, for any concept class C of VC-dimension d, and for all target concepts c in C. The analysis does not rely on empirical datasets but instead provides PAC guarantees with high probability over random training samples S ~ D^m and random bootstrap samples. Theoretical baselines include empirical risk minimization (ERM) and previously proposed optimal PAC learners, such as Hanneke's algorithm. Evaluation metrics are the probability of misclassification (generalization error) and the sample complexity required to achieve error at most ε with confidence at least 1-δ. Key experimental setup details include the use of t = O(log(m/δ)) bootstrap samples, each of size n = Θ(m), and the majority vote aggregation.
c1522fcc9ad365c79910a30352dcbe5e567a262b.novelty_claims: The proposal claims that bagging, a widely used and practical ensemble method, is not only effective in practice but also achieves the theoretically optimal sample complexity for PAC learning in the realizable setting. This result bridges a longstanding gap between practical heuristics and theoretical optimality, providing a simpler and more efficient alternative to previous optimal PAC learners. The analysis further demonstrates that only a logarithmic number of bootstrap samples are required for optimality, in contrast to prior algorithms that require a polynomial number of sub-samples. Additionally, the work provides new theoretical justification for the empirical success of bagging and establishes connections between bagging, boosting, and optimal weak-to-strong learning.

c16c05ca0a3d24519405849fd24604fc1ce47751.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
c16c05ca0a3d24519405849fd24604fc1ce47751.research_question: How do methodological choices in activation patching—specifically, the selection of corruption methods, evaluation metrics, and patching strategies—impact the reliability and interpretability of localization and circuit discovery in language models?
c16c05ca0a3d24519405849fd24604fc1ce47751.hypothesis: Variations in corruption methods, evaluation metrics, and patching strategies significantly influence the outcomes of activation patching, potentially leading to inconsistent or unreliable interpretability results. In-distribution corruption methods and logit-based metrics are hypothesized to yield more robust and accurate localization of model components.
c16c05ca0a3d24519405849fd24604fc1ce47751.proposed_method: A systematic investigation will be conducted into the methodological choices underlying activation patching in language models. The approach will involve comparing two primary corruption methods—Gaussian noising (GN) and symmetric token replacement (STR)—to assess their impact on model interpretability. Several evaluation metrics, including probability, logit difference, and KL divergence, will be analyzed for their effectiveness in detecting both positive and negative contributions of model components. Additionally, the study will contrast sliding window patching (jointly restoring activations across multiple layers) with single-layer patching and summation, to evaluate their respective abilities to localize computation. Each methodological variant will be applied across multiple interpretability tasks and settings to determine their influence on localization and circuit discovery outcomes.
c16c05ca0a3d24519405849fd24604fc1ce47751.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on decoder-only language models such as GPT-2 small, GPT-2 XL, and GPT-J 6B. Datasets will include factual recall prompts (e.g., PAIREDFACTS, derived from Meng et al. 2022), IOI (indirect object identification) sentences, Python docstring completion, greater-than comparison tasks, and basic arithmetic tasks. For each task, both GN and STR corruption methods will be applied, and patching effects will be measured using probability, logit difference, and KL divergence metrics. Baselines will include results from prior studies using default methodological choices. The experimental setup will involve patching activations at specific tokens or layers, iterating over model components (e.g., attention heads, MLP layers), and evaluating the restoration of model performance. Detection criteria (e.g., 2 standard deviations from the mean effect) will be used to identify important components. Results will be averaged over hundreds of prompts to ensure statistical robustness.
c16c05ca0a3d24519405849fd24604fc1ce47751.novelty_claims: The proposed research will provide the first systematic and empirical evaluation of methodological choices in activation patching for language model interpretability. It will identify and quantify the sensitivity of interpretability outcomes to corruption methods, evaluation metrics, and patching strategies. The study will offer conceptual and empirical evidence regarding the risks of out-of-distribution corruption (e.g., GN) and the limitations of probability-based metrics in detecting negative model components. Recommendations for best practices in activation patching—including the use of in-distribution corruption (STR) and logit difference metrics—will be established, contributing to more reliable and standardized interpretability analyses in the field.

c170b8763cb9f53810fbf44717fb78d8c04bb023.title: Parallelizing non-linear sequential models over the sequence length
c170b8763cb9f53810fbf44717fb78d8c04bb023.research_question: How can the evaluation and training of inherently sequential, non-linear models such as Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (Neural ODEs) be parallelized over sequence length to overcome the traditional bottleneck of sequential computation, thereby enabling efficient learning on long sequences without sacrificing output accuracy?
c170b8763cb9f53810fbf44717fb78d8c04bb023.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by reformulating the evaluation of non-linear sequential models as fixed-point iteration problems with quadratic convergence, it is possible to parallelize their computation over sequence length, resulting in significant speedups on modern hardware without compromising model accuracy or requiring changes to model architecture.
c170b8763cb9f53810fbf44717fb78d8c04bb023.proposed_method: A general framework, termed DEER (Differential Equation as fixed point itERation), will be developed to restate non-linear differential or difference equations as fixed-point iteration problems. This approach leverages Newton's method in Banach space to achieve quadratic convergence. The method involves iteratively applying a parallelizable fixed-point update that requires evaluating the model's non-linear function, its Jacobian, and solving a linear system, all of which can be efficiently implemented on GPUs or TPUs. The framework is applicable to both continuous (ODEs) and discrete (RNNs) sequential models, and does not require any special architectural modifications. Forward and backward derivatives for training are derived to allow efficient parallel gradient computation, and practical implementation details such as shifter functions and parallel prefix scan algorithms are specified for efficient execution.
c170b8763cb9f53810fbf44717fb78d8c04bb023.experiment_details: Experiments will benchmark the proposed method against standard sequential evaluation on tasks including untrained GRU forward and backward passes, Hamiltonian Neural Network (HNN) training on a two-body physics dataset (with 10,000 time points), and time-series classification using GRUs on the EigenWorms dataset (17,984 time samples per entry). Baselines will include standard sequential RNN/ODE solvers (e.g., RK45 for ODEs) and state-of-the-art models such as ODE-RNN, NCDE, NRDE, UnICORNN, and LEM. Evaluation metrics will include speedup (wall-clock time), output accuracy (classification accuracy or validation loss), and numerical precision differences between sequential and parallel methods. Experiments will be conducted using JAX and related libraries to leverage efficient parallel scan operations, with additional tests on multi-head GRU architectures for sequential CIFAR-10 classification. Multiple random seeds and batch sizes will be used to ensure robustness and generalizability of results.
c170b8763cb9f53810fbf44717fb78d8c04bb023.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to enable parallelization of non-linear sequential models over sequence length without requiring architectural changes or special structure, achieving up to three orders of magnitude speedup in evaluation and over tenfold acceleration in training. The approach generalizes to a wide range of sequential models, including both ODEs and RNNs, and provides a unified fixed-point iteration framework with quadratic convergence. The method facilitates rapid experimentation and exploration of classical and novel non-linear sequential models for long sequence problems, overcoming a longstanding computational bottleneck in the field.

c1799bf28d1ae93e1631be5b59196ee1e568f538.title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
c1799bf28d1ae93e1631be5b59196ee1e568f538.research_question: How can query-focused summarization be effectively performed over large, private, or previously unseen text corpora, enabling large language models to answer both local and global sensemaking queries at scale?
c1799bf28d1ae93e1631be5b59196ee1e568f538.hypothesis: A graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (GraphRAG) approach that constructs a knowledge graph from source documents, partitions it into communities, and generates hierarchical community summaries will enable large language models to answer global, sensemaking queries with greater comprehensiveness and diversity than conventional vector-based RAG methods, while maintaining scalability to large datasets.
c1799bf28d1ae93e1631be5b59196ee1e568f538.proposed_method: The proposed method begins by splitting the source document corpus into manageable text chunks. An LLM is then prompted to extract entities, relationships, and factual claims from each chunk, with prompts tailored to the domain as needed. These extracted elements are aggregated into a knowledge graph, where nodes represent entities and edges represent relationships, with edge weights reflecting the frequency of relationships. Hierarchical community detection (e.g., Leiden algorithm) is applied to partition the graph into nested communities, enabling divide-and-conquer summarization. For each community at each level of the hierarchy, the LLM generates summaries by prioritizing prominent nodes and edges, and recursively incorporating lower-level summaries into higher-level ones. At query time, community summaries are used in a map-reduce fashion: partial answers are generated for each community summary, scored for helpfulness, and then the most relevant are combined and summarized to produce a final global answer to the user query.
c1799bf28d1ae93e1631be5b59196ee1e568f538.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two large-scale datasets: a podcast transcript corpus (~1 million tokens) and a news article corpus (~1.7 million tokens), both divided into overlapping 600-token chunks. The proposed GraphRAG method will be evaluated at multiple levels of the community hierarchy (C0–C3) and compared against a vector-based RAG baseline (semantic search) and a global text summarization baseline using a map-reduce approach. Evaluation will use LLM-as-a-judge adaptive benchmarking, with corpus-specific global sensemaking questions generated via LLM personas and tasks. Metrics will include comprehensiveness, diversity, empowerment, and directness, assessed through head-to-head LLM comparisons and claim-based quantitative measures (number and diversity of extracted factual claims). All methods will use consistent context window sizes and prompts, and statistical significance will be established through multiple replicates.
c1799bf28d1ae93e1631be5b59196ee1e568f538.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a scalable, graph-based RAG framework that enables global sensemaking over large text corpora by leveraging hierarchical community detection and community-level summarization. Unlike conventional RAG, which is limited to localized retrieval, this method supports query-focused summarization for broad, corpus-level questions. The pipeline integrates LLM-driven entity and relationship extraction, modular graph partitioning, and a map-reduce answering mechanism, offering both improved answer quality (comprehensiveness and diversity) and efficiency (reduced context token requirements). Additionally, the proposal includes an adaptive benchmarking methodology for generating and evaluating global sensemaking queries tailored to real-world use cases.

c193011099906126fe7b6cfcb04062cf4591ccf9.title: Specformer: Spectral Graph Neural Networks Meet Transformers
c193011099906126fe7b6cfcb04062cf4591ccf9.research_question: How can more expressive and flexible spectral filters be developed for graph neural networks to effectively leverage the full spectrum of the graph Laplacian, capturing both global and local structural information for improved graph representation learning?
c193011099906126fe7b6cfcb04062cf4591ccf9.hypothesis: A Transformer-based set-to-set spectral filter with learnable bases can more effectively capture both the magnitudes and relative dependencies of all eigenvalues in the graph Laplacian, leading to improved performance and flexibility over traditional scalar-to-scalar polynomial spectral filters and spatial GNNs.
c193011099906126fe7b6cfcb04062cf4591ccf9.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a novel spectral graph neural network architecture, Specformer, which encodes the entire set of graph Laplacian eigenvalues using a positional encoding scheme tailored for the spectral domain. These encoded eigenvalues are processed through a multi-layer Transformer encoder to capture both their magnitudes and relative dependencies via self-attention. A decoder with a bank of learnable bases is then employed to generate new, expressive spectral filters by combining the learned representations, enabling the construction of permutation-equivariant and non-local graph convolutions. Each feature dimension is assigned a separate graph Laplacian matrix based on these learned bases, and node representations are updated through stacked graph convolutional layers with optional residual connections. The model supports different parameter sharing schemes (Small, Medium, Large) to balance expressiveness and efficiency.
c193011099906126fe7b6cfcb04062cf4591ccf9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic experiments will use 2D grid graphs constructed from images, with node features corresponding to pixel values and ground-truth signals generated by applying predefined spectral filters (e.g., low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, band-rejection, comb) to the graph signals. Real-world node classification tasks will be evaluated on homophilic (Cora, Citeseer, Amazon-Photo, ogbn-arXiv) and heterophilic (Chameleon, Squirrel, Actor, Penn94) datasets, using standardized splits and comparing against spatial GNNs, spectral GNNs, and graph Transformer baselines. Graph-level tasks will be assessed on ZINC, MolHIV, and MolPCBA datasets, with evaluation metrics including mean squared error, R2 score, and classification accuracy or ROC-AUC as appropriate. Model sizes will be controlled for fair comparison, and truncated spectral decomposition will be used for scalability on large graphs.
c193011099906126fe7b6cfcb04062cf4591ccf9.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a Transformer-based set-to-set spectral filter that, unlike traditional scalar-to-scalar polynomial filters, can capture both the magnitude and relative differences of all eigenvalues in the graph spectrum. The use of learnable bases in the decoder allows for flexible, non-local, and permutation-equivariant graph convolutions, generalizing and extending the capabilities of existing spectral GNNs and spatial GNNs. The approach is theoretically shown to be permutation equivariant and universal in approximating both univariate and multivariate continuous functions over the spectrum. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior performance on both node-level and graph-level tasks, especially in challenging settings where traditional polynomial filters are less expressive.

c1966d66a92214f245ddf1209830095063a4d11a.title: Latent Refinement via Flow Matching for Training-free Linear Inverse Problem Solving
c1966d66a92214f245ddf1209830095063a4d11a.research_question: How can linear inverse problems in image processing be solved more efficiently and effectively, particularly for high-resolution data, by leveraging generative models in latent space without requiring additional task-specific training?
c1966d66a92214f245ddf1209830095063a4d11a.hypothesis: Utilizing pretrained latent flow priors and a theoretically grounded, time-dependent posterior covariance within a flow-matching ODE framework in latent space will enable training-free, scalable, and high-quality solutions to linear inverse problems, outperforming existing latent diffusion-based and pixel-space flow-based methods.
c1966d66a92214f245ddf1209830095063a4d11a.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed that solves linear inverse problems by performing conditional ODE sampling in the latent space of a pretrained autoencoder, guided by a pretrained latent flow-matching vector field. The method represents the prior implicitly via a latent prior and decoder, and samples from the posterior by integrating a reverse-time ODE whose velocity field is corrected using a likelihood-based guidance term. The posterior covariance is analytically derived using Tweedie’s formula and the optimal vector field, resulting in a time-dependent, theoretically justified covariance that is informed by the pretrained flow. The approach includes an initialization scheme that starts the reverse ODE from a partially corrupted latent encoding of the observation, improving stability and convergence. Efficient computation of the required Jacobian-vector products and covariance matrices is achieved via automatic differentiation and, when necessary, conjugate gradient solvers.
c1966d66a92214f245ddf1209830095063a4d11a.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on FFHQ, ImageNet, and CelebA-HQ datasets at 256×256 resolution, evaluating tasks such as Gaussian deblurring, motion deblurring, super-resolution (×4), and box inpainting. The measurement operators and noise levels are set to reflect realistic inverse problem settings. The proposed method is compared against state-of-the-art latent diffusion solvers (PSLD, MPGD, Resample, DMplug, DAPS, SITCOM) and pixel-based flow/diffusion baselines (ΠGDM, OT-ODE, C-ΠGFM), using metrics including LPIPS, PSNR, SSIM, and FID. The architecture is based on the LFM-VAE framework with DiT transformer backbones, and pre-trained models are used for all datasets. Adaptive ODE solvers are employed for inference, and ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of posterior covariance modeling and initialization strategies. All experiments are run on a single NVIDIA 3090 GPU.
c1966d66a92214f245ddf1209830095063a4d11a.novelty_claims: The proposed framework is the first to enable training-free linear inverse problem solving via latent flow matching, operating entirely in latent space for enhanced scalability and efficiency. A key innovation is the introduction of a theoretically justified, time-dependent posterior covariance that leverages information from the pretrained vector field, leading to improved guidance and reconstruction quality. The method achieves state-of-the-art results across multiple tasks and datasets, surpassing existing latent diffusion and pixel-space flow-based approaches in both perceptual and quantitative metrics, while also offering faster inference. The approach requires no additional training or substantial hyperparameter tuning for new inverse problems.

c1caa303549764d220ff17dc1785985dd1ba6047.title: AnimateDiff: Animate Your Personalized Text-to-Image Diffusion Models without Specific Tuning
c1caa303549764d220ff17dc1785985dd1ba6047.research_question: How can personalized text-to-image diffusion models be extended to generate high-quality, temporally coherent animations without requiring model-specific fine-tuning or extensive computational resources?
c1caa303549764d220ff17dc1785985dd1ba6047.hypothesis: A plug-and-play motion module, trained on real-world video data and integrated with a domain adapter and lightweight fine-tuning techniques, can effectively enable animation generation in personalized text-to-image diffusion models while preserving visual quality and domain-specific features.
c1caa303549764d220ff17dc1785985dd1ba6047.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a modular framework that augments existing personalized text-to-image diffusion models with animation capabilities.
