Additional ablation studies will examine the impact of planning depth, model accuracy, and sample efficiency.
c39fb7a46335c23f7529dd6f9f980462fd38653a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a planning algorithm that does not require any prior knowledge of environment dynamics or game rules, instead learning a model that predicts only the most planning-relevant quantities. This enables the agent to achieve superhuman performance in board games and state-of-the-art results in visually complex domains like Atari, surpassing both model-free and previous model-based methods. The method unifies model-based planning and model-free learning, extends planning algorithms to domains with unknown dynamics, and demonstrates scalability and sample efficiency across a diverse set of challenging environments.

c3bd20c5794efdde989a7dfbbc29946a9550878d.title: Reasoning-as-Logic-Units: Scaling Test-Time Reasoning in Large Language Models Through Logic Unit Alignment
c3bd20c5794efdde989a7dfbbc29946a9550878d.research_question: How can the reliability and logical consistency of large language models' (LLMs) reasoning processes be improved, particularly in tasks requiring mathematical and algorithmic reasoning, by addressing inconsistencies between natural language reasoning steps and programmatic logic?
c3bd20c5794efdde989a7dfbbc29946a9550878d.hypothesis: Aligning natural language reasoning steps with programmatic logic units via an iterative, unit-level validation and correction process will reduce reasoning hallucinations and improve both the accuracy and interpretability of LLM-generated solutions.
c3bd20c5794efdde989a7dfbbc29946a9550878d.proposed_method: A novel test-time scaling framework, Reasoning-as-Logic-Units (RaLU), will be developed to enforce alignment between natural language (NL) explanations and program logic. The approach begins by prompting the LLM to generate an initial program for the reasoning task, which is then decomposed into discrete logic units using static code analysis and control flow graph (CFG) construction. Each logic unit, representing a coherent computational intent (e.g., a loop or conditional block), is iteratively validated through dialogue with the LLM: the model explains, judges, and, if necessary, corrects each unit, with a rewind-and-correct mechanism ensuring local and global consistency. Explanations are generated to map code operations to task requirements, and the process continues until all units are validated or a confidence threshold is reached. The final solution is synthesized from the verified logic units and their aligned NL explanations, ensuring both computational rigor and interpretability.
c3bd20c5794efdde989a7dfbbc29946a9550878d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on four established benchmarks: GSM8K and MATH for mathematical reasoning, and HumanEval and MBPP (including their extended versions) for code reasoning. The evaluation will use three open-source LLM backbones: Deepseek-V3, Llama3.3-70B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct. Baselines will include direct prompting, Chain-of-Thought (CoT), Program-of-Thought (PoT), Self-Consistency, Self-Calibration, Self-Refine, Self-Check, and rubber-duck debugging methods. Metrics will include answer accuracy for math tasks and pass@1 for code tasks. The experimental setup will control for the number of correction turns and candidate solutions, and ablation studies will assess the impact of logic unit granularity and the use of NL steps versus program-guided units.
c3bd20c5794efdde989a7dfbbc29946a9550878d.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a structured, test-time reasoning process that decomposes generated programs into logic units, aligning each with natural language explanations through iterative validation and correction. This dual anchoring of code and NL reasoning is claimed to significantly mitigate reasoning hallucinations, improve both accuracy and interpretability, and outperform existing single-path and multi-path reasoning baselines. The method provides granular traceability, enabling precise error localization and correction, and demonstrates generalizability across multiple LLM architectures and both mathematical and algorithmic reasoning domains.

c3c7464acb90049c5f520b0732dc7435ba3690bd.title: Attend-and-Excite: Attention-Based Semantic Guidance for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
c3c7464acb90049c5f520b0732dc7435ba3690bd.research_question: How can the semantic faithfulness of text-to-image diffusion models be improved, particularly in generating all subjects and correctly binding attributes as specified in the input text prompt?
c3c7464acb90049c5f520b0732dc7435ba3690bd.hypothesis: Guiding the cross-attention mechanisms of pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models during inference can mitigate semantic failures such as catastrophic neglect and incorrect attribute binding, resulting in images that more faithfully represent the input text prompts.
c3c7464acb90049c5f520b0732dc7435ba3690bd.proposed_method: A novel framework, Attend-and-Excite, will be developed to intervene in the generative process of pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models (such as Stable Diffusion) at inference time. The method will extract subject tokens from the input prompt and monitor their corresponding cross-attention maps at each denoising timestep. A loss objective will be defined to maximize the attention values for each subject token, ensuring that every subject is attended to by at least one image patch. The latent code will be iteratively refined via gradient-based updates to increase the maximal activation for neglected subject tokens, with Gaussian smoothing applied to attention maps to avoid adversarial solutions and encourage spatial coherence. This optimization will be performed on-the-fly, without additional training or fine-tuning of the generative model.
c3c7464acb90049c5f520b0732dc7435ba3690bd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a newly constructed benchmark dataset consisting of prompts with multiple subjects and varied attribute bindings, including combinations of animals, objects, and colors. For each prompt, 64 images will be generated using random seeds across all evaluated methods. Baselines will include Stable Diffusion, Composable Diffusion, and Structure Diffusion. Evaluation metrics will comprise CLIP-based image-text similarity (both for full prompts and minimum similarity for the most neglected subject), text-text similarity using BLIP-generated captions, and user studies to assess semantic fidelity. Additional qualitative analysis will be performed on complex prompts involving multiple subjects and attributes.
c3c7464acb90049c5f520b0732dc7435ba3690bd.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the concept of Generative Semantic Nursing (GSN), specifically instantiated as Attend-and-Excite, which provides inference-time semantic guidance by directly manipulating the latent space of pre-trained diffusion models through attention-based objectives. Unlike prior methods, this framework does not require retraining or fine-tuning and can be applied to any prompt structure. The method not only addresses catastrophic neglect but also implicitly improves attribute binding, and enables more explainable image generation by producing faithful cross-attention maps. The approach is demonstrated to outperform existing baselines both quantitatively and qualitatively.

c3e5a20b844c042d2174263d2fd5b30d8cc8f0b0.title: Grounding DINO: Marrying DINO with Grounded Pre-Training for Open-Set Object Detection
c3e5a20b844c042d2174263d2fd5b30d8cc8f0b0.research_question: How can object detection models be designed to effectively detect arbitrary objects specified by human language inputs in open-set scenarios, achieving strong generalization to novel categories and supporting tasks such as referring expression comprehension?
c3e5a20b844c042d2174263d2fd5b30d8cc8f0b0.hypothesis: A tightly fused multi-modal architecture, combining visual and linguistic features at multiple stages of the detection pipeline and pre-trained on large-scale grounded datasets, will significantly improve open-set object detection performance and generalization to novel categories and referring expression tasks.
c3e5a20b844c042d2174263d2fd5b30d8cc8f0b0.proposed_method: A novel open-set object detection framework is proposed that integrates a Transformer-based detector backbone with multi-phase cross-modal fusion. The architecture consists of an image backbone (e.g., Swin Transformer) and a text backbone (e.g., BERT) for feature extraction, followed by a feature enhancer module that performs self-attention and cross-attention between image and text features. A language-guided query selection mechanism identifies image regions most relevant to the input text, initializing decoder queries for object detection. The detection head employs a cross-modality decoder with alternating self-attention, image cross-attention, and text cross-attention layers to tightly align and refine multi-modal representations. Sub-sentence level text features are used to avoid unwanted interactions between unrelated category names, improving fine-grained understanding. The model is trained using a combination of contrastive loss for classification and L1/GIoU losses for bounding box regression, with auxiliary losses after each decoder layer.
c3e5a20b844c042d2174263d2fd5b30d8cc8f0b0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple benchmarks, including COCO (closed-set and zero-shot), LVIS (long-tail open-set), ODinW (open-domain), and referring expression comprehension datasets such as RefCOCO/+/g. The model will be pre-trained on large-scale datasets including Object365, Open Images, GoldG, Cap4M, COCO, and RefCOCO, without using the test set training splits for zero-shot evaluation. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art open-set detectors such as GLIP, DetCLIP, OV-DETR, and DINO. Evaluation metrics will include Average Precision (AP) and its variants (APr, APc, APf) for object detection and referring tasks. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of each architectural component, and both zero-shot transfer and fine-tuning scenarios will be evaluated. Models will be trained on large-scale GPU clusters with detailed hyperparameter settings (e.g., number of queries, feature scales, batch sizes) specified.
c3e5a20b844c042d2174263d2fd5b30d8cc8f0b0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a tightly fused multi-modal detection framework that performs cross-modal feature fusion at multiple stages (feature enhancement, query selection, and decoding), surpassing previous methods that only fuse modalities at a single stage. The use of sub-sentence level text features with attention masking for category name separation is a novel technique for improving fine-grained language-vision alignment. The framework achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot object detection performance on COCO and ODinW benchmarks, and demonstrates superior scalability and generalization to novel categories and referring expression tasks compared to existing methods.

c3eed6435ae609ee800c6e9daee038535af2ef22.title: Bridging State and History Representations: Understanding Self-Predictive RL
c3eed6435ae609ee800c6e9daee038535af2ef22.research_question: What are the essential characteristics of effective state and history representations in reinforcement learning, and how can a unified, theoretically grounded approach be developed to learn such representations efficiently in both Markov decision processes (MDPs) and partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs)?
c3eed6435ae609ee800c6e9daee038535af2ef22.hypothesis: 1) Self-predictive and observation-predictive auxiliary signals improve sample efficiency over standard value-based representations, especially in sparse-reward and distracting environments. 2) End-to-end learning of self-predictive representations is as effective as phased training. 3) Stop-gradient techniques in auxiliary losses prevent representational collapse and stabilize learning. 4) In deterministic tasks, simple deterministic objectives suffice, while in stochastic settings, probabilistic objectives are preferable. 5) Self-predictive representations are more robust to irrelevant distractors than observation-predictive representations.
c3eed6435ae609ee800c6e9daee038535af2ef22.proposed_method: A minimalist reinforcement learning algorithm will be developed that learns self-predictive representations end-to-end by integrating a single auxiliary loss into any model-free RL framework. The method employs an encoder to map histories (or states) to latent representations, and a latent transition model to predict the next latent state given the current latent and action. The auxiliary loss enforces a self-predictive condition by minimizing the distance (e.g., ℓ2 or KL divergence) between the predicted and actual next latent state, using a stop-gradient target to prevent representational collapse. The approach does not require reward model learning, planning, multi-step predictions, or metric learning, thus isolating the effect of representation learning from policy optimization. The algorithm is compatible with both deterministic and probabilistic encoders and can be instantiated with recurrent networks for POMDPs.
c3eed6435ae609ee800c6e9daee038535af2ef22.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three types of benchmarks: standard MDPs (MuJoCo locomotion tasks), MDPs with high-dimensional distracting observations (by adding Gaussian noise features), and sparse-reward POMDPs (MiniGrid suite). Baselines will include standard model-free RL (e.g., TD3, R2D2), state-of-the-art self-predictive and observation-predictive methods (e.g., ALM(3)), and phased training variants. Evaluation metrics will include episodic return, sample efficiency, and the rank of learned representations to assess representational collapse. The effect of different auxiliary losses (ℓ2, forward/reverse KL), ZP target types (online, detached, EMA), and the presence of distractors will be systematically compared. Multiple random seeds and confidence intervals will be used for statistical robustness.
c3eed6435ae609ee800c6e9daee038535af2ef22.novelty_claims: The proposed research establishes a unified theoretical framework connecting state and history representations in RL, revealing that many prior methods are special cases of self-predictive abstraction. It provides new theoretical insights into the optimization dynamics of self-predictive learning, particularly the role of stop-gradient techniques in preventing collapse. The minimalist algorithm is novel in its simplicity, requiring only a single auxiliary loss and no reward or planning models, and is the first to learn self-predictive representations end-to-end in POMDPs. The approach enables disentanglement of representation learning from policy optimization, allowing for fair and isolated evaluation of representation methods. Empirical results are expected to yield actionable guidelines for RL practitioners regarding representation learning choices.

c3eee48481b3b8f4be18026e389fadf9a53ad192.title: Content-based Unrestricted Adversarial Attack
c3eee48481b3b8f4be18026e389fadf9a53ad192.research_question: How can unrestricted adversarial attacks be designed to generate photorealistic, highly transferable adversarial examples by adaptively modifying diverse image content, while maintaining semantic consistency and overcoming the limitations of current attack methods?
c3eee48481b3b8f4be18026e389fadf9a53ad192.hypothesis: Mapping images onto a well-trained, low-dimensional manifold of natural images and optimizing them along adversarial directions within this space will enable the generation of photorealistic, semantically consistent, and highly transferable unrestricted adversarial examples that outperform existing methods in both attack success and visual quality.
c3eee48481b3b8f4be18026e389fadf9a53ad192.proposed_method: A novel unrestricted adversarial attack framework is developed by leveraging a low-dimensional manifold of natural images, represented by a diffusion generative model (specifically, Stable Diffusion). The approach first maps input images onto the manifold's latent space using an Image Latent Mapping (ILM) process, which inverts the DDIM sampling procedure and optimizes null text embeddings for each timestamp to minimize reconstruction errors. Adversarial Latent Optimization (ALO) is then performed by introducing perturbations in the latent space, maximizing the classifier's loss while constraining the perturbation magnitude to preserve semantic consistency and photorealism. The optimization employs skip gradients to efficiently approximate the gradient of the denoising process and incorporates differentiable boundary processing to ensure valid image ranges. The method iteratively updates latent representations to generate adversarial examples that combine changes in shape, texture, and color, while maintaining natural appearance.
c3eee48481b3b8f4be18026e389fadf9a53ad192.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the ImageNet-compatible dataset, consisting of 1,000 images from the ImageNet validation set. The proposed method is evaluated against state-of-the-art unrestricted adversarial attacks, including SAE, ADer, ReColorAdv, cAdv, tAdv, ACE, ColorFool, and NCF, using their default parameters. Attack success rate (ASR) is the primary evaluation metric, measuring the percentage of misclassified images. Both convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision transformers (ViTs) are used as target models, including MobileNet-V2, Inception-v3, ResNet-50/152, DenseNet-161, EfficientNet-b7, MobileViT-s, ViT-B, Swin-B, and PVT-v2. Additional experiments test robustness against adversarial defense methods, such as input pre-processing defenses (HGD, R&P, NIPS-r3, JPEG, Bit-Red, DiffPure) and adversarially trained models (Inc-v3ens3, Inc-v3ens4, IncRes-v2ens, ResNet50-Debaised, Shape-ResNet). Image quality is assessed with non-reference metrics (NIMA, HyperIQA, MUSIQ, TReS), and ablation studies are performed to analyze the impact of momentum and differentiable boundary processing. All experiments are run on an NVIDIA Tesla A100 GPU, with Stable Diffusion v1.4 and prompts generated by BLIPv2.
c3eee48481b3b8f4be18026e389fadf9a53ad192.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a new paradigm for unrestricted adversarial attacks by adaptively generating adversarial examples along a low-dimensional manifold of natural images, ensuring both photorealism and diversity in adversarial content. The method leverages diffusion models for manifold representation, employs a novel combination of image latent mapping and adversarial latent optimization, and integrates efficient gradient approximation and boundary processing. The approach achieves significantly higher attack success rates and transferability compared to state-of-the-art methods, while maintaining or surpassing image quality. The method also demonstrates the ability to break through a wide range of adversarial defenses, highlighting the limitations of current robustness strategies.

c3f1fae241a3c2449e675ab750873d800f95513c.title: SimPO: Simple Preference Optimization with a Reference-Free Reward
c3f1fae241a3c2449e675ab750873d800f95513c.research_question: How can preference optimization for large language models be improved to achieve better alignment with human preferences, increased training efficiency, and reduced reliance on reference models, while avoiding length bias and maintaining or improving performance on standard conversational benchmarks?
c3f1fae241a3c2449e675ab750873d800f95513c.hypothesis: A preference optimization algorithm that employs a reference-free, length-normalized reward based on the average log probability of generated sequences, combined with a target reward margin in the Bradley-Terry objective, will outperform existing reference-based and reference-free methods in both efficiency and alignment with human preferences, without inducing length bias.
c3f1fae241a3c2449e675ab750873d800f95513c.proposed_method: A new offline preference optimization algorithm, SimPO, will be developed to directly align the reward function with the generation metric by using the average log probability of all tokens in a response as the implicit reward. This reward will be length-normalized to prevent the model from exploiting response length, addressing a key limitation in previous approaches. The method will eliminate the need for a reference model, thereby reducing computational and memory overhead. Additionally, a target reward margin will be incorporated into the Bradley-Terry objective, ensuring that the reward for the preferred (winning) response exceeds that of the non-preferred (losing) response by at least a specified margin. The algorithm will be trained using preference pairs (prompt, winning response, losing response) and optimized to maximize the probability that the model assigns higher reward to the preferred response, with hyperparameters for reward scaling and margin tuned for optimal performance.
c3f1fae241a3c2449e675ab750873d800f95513c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large language models such as Llama-3-8B, Mistral-7B, and Gemma-2-9B, under both base and instruction-tuned (Instruct) setups. Training will utilize open-source datasets including UltraChat-200k for supervised fine-tuning and UltraFeedback for preference optimization. Evaluation will be performed on widely adopted benchmarks: AlpacaEval2 (805 examples), Arena-Hard (500 examples), and MT-Bench (80 examples), using metrics such as length-controlled win rate, raw win rate, and single-answer grading by GPT-4-based judge models. Baselines will include state-of-the-art preference optimization methods such as DPO, IPO, CPO, KTO, ORPO, R-DPO, RRHF, and SLiC-HF. Hyperparameters (reward scaling β and margin γ) will be tuned, and ablation studies will be conducted to assess the impact of length normalization and reward margin. Efficiency will be measured in terms of runtime and GPU memory usage.
c3f1fae241a3c2449e675ab750873d800f95513c.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a reference-free, length-normalized reward formulation for preference optimization that directly aligns with the generation likelihood, eliminating the need for a reference model and reducing computational and memory requirements. The incorporation of a target reward margin into the Bradley-Terry objective is claimed to further improve generalization and model performance. The approach is expected to outperform existing reference-based and reference-free methods across multiple benchmarks, while avoiding length bias and maintaining high-quality, concise responses. Additionally, the method demonstrates improved reward accuracy and efficiency compared to prior algorithms.

c40cf4dd911d60635fb3f46e6c031c3ffa9453b6.title: Slot-Guided Adaptation of Pre-trained Diffusion Models for Object-Centric Learning and Compositional Generation
c40cf4dd911d60635fb3f46e6c031c3ffa9453b6.research_question: How can object-centric learning be advanced to enable robust unsupervised object discovery, segmentation, and compositional image generation in complex real-world images using generative models, while avoiding biases inherent in text-conditioned diffusion models?
c40cf4dd911d60635fb3f46e6c031c3ffa9453b6.hypothesis: Integrating slot attention with pretrained diffusion models through slot-based adapter conditioning and self-supervised attention alignment will enable more accurate object-centric representations and compositional image generation in real-world scenarios, outperforming existing slot-based and diffusion-based methods without requiring external supervision.
c40cf4dd911d60635fb3f46e6c031c3ffa9453b6.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a framework that combines slot attention with pretrained diffusion models by incorporating adapter layers for slot-based conditioning. An input image is first encoded using a visual backbone (DINOv2 for real-world datasets, CNN for synthetic), followed by slot attention to extract object-centric slot representations. The pretrained Stable Diffusion UNet serves as the decoder, where additional adapter cross-attention layers are inserted after each original cross-attention layer in all downsampling and upsampling blocks. These adapters condition the diffusion process on the slot representations, while a 'register' token, computed by pooling slots or features, is used to capture global context through the original text-conditioning modules. The pretrained diffusion model remains frozen; only the adapter layers and slot attention are trained. A self-supervised guidance loss is introduced to align the slot attention masks with the adapter cross-attention masks, encouraging the model to produce slot representations that correspond closely to actual objects, and vice versa, without external supervision.
c40cf4dd911d60635fb3f46e6c031c3ffa9453b6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic (MOVi-E) and real-world (VOC, COCO) datasets, covering challenging multi-object scenes. The evaluation will use standard metrics for unsupervised object segmentation and discovery, including foreground adjusted rand index (FG-ARI), mean intersection over union (mIoU), and mean best overlap (mBO), with both instance-level and class-level variants. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art unsupervised object-centric methods such as SLATE, SLATE+, Latent Slot Diffusion (LSD), SlotDiffusion, DINOSAUR, and SlotAttention. For image generation and compositional editing, fidelity will be assessed using FID and KID scores. Ablation studies will examine the effects of different architectural choices (e.g., conditioning blocks, register token strategies) and guidance loss variants. All models will use a frozen DINOv2 encoder for real-world datasets and a frozen Stable Diffusion model (v1.5 or v2.1) as the decoder, with training focused on the slot attention and adapter layers.
c40cf4dd911d60635fb3f46e6c031c3ffa9453b6.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces slot-based adapter conditioning into pretrained diffusion models, eliminating text-conditioning bias while retaining generative power. It is the first to demonstrate successful compositional image generation and editing on the COCO dataset without external supervision. The approach also presents a novel self-supervised guidance loss to align slot attention and diffusion cross-attention, improving object-slot correspondence and segmentation quality. The method achieves state-of-the-art performance in unsupervised object discovery, segmentation, and compositional generation, with reduced computational requirements compared to competing approaches.

c41864045d7326f4f69de2cf9ca44beaac476c53.title: Object-Centric Learning for Real-World Videos by Predicting Temporal Feature Similarities
c41864045d7326f4f69de2cf9ca44beaac476c53.research_question: Can unsupervised object-centric learning methods be scaled to learn structured object representations from unconstrained, real-world video datasets, and what approaches can improve object discovery in such challenging settings?
c41864045d7326f4f69de2cf9ca44beaac476c53.hypothesis: Incorporating a self-supervised temporal feature similarity loss, which leverages both semantic and motion information from pre-trained vision transformer features, will enable object-centric video models to effectively discover and track objects in unconstrained real-world videos, outperforming existing baselines.
c41864045d7326f4f69de2cf9ca44beaac476c53.proposed_method: A novel object-centric video learning framework is proposed that combines a pre-trained self-supervised Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder, a recurrent slot attention grouping module, and an efficient SlotMixer decoder. The ViT encoder extracts dense patch-level features from each video frame, which are then grouped into object-centric slots using recurrent slot attention, initialized with slots from the previous frame. The SlotMixer decoder efficiently decodes these slots to produce predictions for both current frame feature reconstruction and future patch similarity distributions. The core innovation is a self-supervised temporal similarity loss: for each patch, the model predicts a probability distribution over where semantically similar patches move in future frames, computed via a softmax over the cosine similarity (affinity) matrix between patch features across frames. The final training objective combines this temporal similarity loss with a feature reconstruction loss, promoting both semantic grouping and motion consistency.
c41864045d7326f4f69de2cf9ca44beaac476c53.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three synthetic datasets (MOVi-C, MOVi-D, MOVi-E) and several real-world datasets, including YouTube-VIS 2021, YouTube-VIS 2019, and DAVIS. The model's performance will be evaluated using video foreground Adjusted Rand Index (FG-ARI) and mean Best Overlap (mBO), which assess the quality and consistency of discovered object masks. Baselines for comparison include SAVi (mixture-based decoder with image reconstruction loss), STEVE (transformer decoder with discrete code reconstruction), and trivial block pattern masks, as well as recent image-based methods such as DINOSAUR, LSD, and SlotDiffusion. Ablation studies will examine the effects of the temporal similarity loss, feature reconstruction loss, decoder choice, hyperparameters (such as time shift and softmax temperature), and the type of self-supervised features. Zero-shot transfer experiments will test generalization to unseen datasets, and memory efficiency will be compared between the SlotMixer and MLP broadcast decoders.
c41864045d7326f4f69de2cf9ca44beaac476c53.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel self-supervised temporal feature similarity loss for object-centric video learning, which integrates both semantic and motion cues without requiring explicit motion labels or optical flow. The method is the first to demonstrate scalable, unsupervised object-centric learning on unconstrained real-world video datasets such as YouTube-VIS. The use of the SlotMixer decoder enables efficient video processing with reduced memory overhead, and the combination of temporal similarity and feature reconstruction losses synergistically improves object grouping and tracking. The approach is robust to camera motion and generalizes well to new datasets, representing a significant advancement in unsupervised object-centric video representation learning.

c42eb51e5cc4662521134c9291696848c7a88c98.title: Coalescing Random Walks and Voting on Connected Graphs
c42eb51e5cc4662521134c9291696848c7a88c98.research_question: What are general upper bounds on the coalescence time of coalescing random walks and the completion time of the voter model on arbitrary connected graphs, and how do these bounds depend on structural graph parameters such as the eigenvalue gap and degree variability?
c42eb51e5cc4662521134c9291696848c7a88c98.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the expected coalescence time for coalescing random walks, and equivalently the expected completion time for the voter model, can be tightly bounded in terms of the graph's second eigenvalue and a parameter capturing degree variability, leading to improved or sublinear bounds for certain classes of graphs.
c42eb51e5cc4662521134c9291696848c7a88c98.proposed_method: A detailed probabilistic and spectral analysis will be conducted to derive upper bounds on the coalescence time for general connected graphs. The approach will involve modeling the coalescence process as a sequence of phases, analyzing the reduction in particle count from n to a threshold k*, and then from k* to 1, using mixing times and hitting times of random walks. The method will leverage the equivalence between coalescing random walks and the voter model, and will express bounds in terms of the second eigenvalue of the transition matrix (λ2) and a degree-variability parameter ν, defined as the ratio of the average squared degree to the square of the average degree. The analysis will utilize contraction techniques on product graphs to reduce the problem of multiple random walks to a single walk on a higher-dimensional graph, allowing the use of spectral gap and mixing time results.
c42eb51e5cc4662521134c9291696848c7a88c98.experiment_details: Theoretical results will be validated through analysis on various classes of graphs, including regular graphs, expanders, bipartite graphs (with lazy walks), star graphs, and graphs with power-law degree distributions. Key parameters such as the eigenvalue gap (1−λ2), maximum degree, and ν will be computed for each graph class. The derived bounds will be compared to known results and lower bounds, and the tightness of the proposed bounds will be discussed in extremal cases. Evaluation metrics will include the order of the derived upper bounds relative to n and other graph parameters, and whether the bounds are sublinear or linear for specific graph families.
c42eb51e5cc4662521134c9291696848c7a88c98.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified and explicit upper bound on coalescence and voting times for arbitrary connected graphs, parameterized by both the spectral gap and a degree-variability measure. The method generalizes and refines previous bounds by making the influence of graph structure explicit, and demonstrates sublinear coalescence times for certain heavy-tailed degree distributions. The approach provides a framework that can improve upon classical hitting-time-based bounds and reveals new insights into the interplay between spectral properties and degree heterogeneity in random walk-based processes.

c431b1a922385830d4c934a5679edfb9cedc600b.title: Spike No More: Stabilizing the Pre-training of Large Language Models
c431b1a922385830d4c934a5679edfb9cedc600b.research_question: What are the underlying causes of instability, specifically loss spikes, during the pre-training of large language models, and how can the pre-training process be theoretically and empirically stabilized across different model scales and training configurations?
c431b1a922385830d4c934a5679edfb9cedc600b.hypothesis: Loss spikes during large language model pre-training are primarily caused by sudden growth in gradient norms, which can be controlled by ensuring small sub-layer parameter initialization and maintaining a large standard deviation in shortcut (embedding) connections. Satisfying these two conditions will prevent loss spikes and enable stable, efficient pre-training.
c431b1a922385830d4c934a5679edfb9cedc600b.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed to analyze the upper bound of gradient norms in Transformer-based large language models by examining the spectral norms of the Jacobian matrices for sub-layers, including feed-forward and attention components. The analysis will identify the relationship between parameter initialization, embedding scaling, and gradient norm stability. Two stabilization conditions will be imposed: (1) initializing sub-layer parameters with sufficiently small values using established initialization schemes, and (2) ensuring the standard deviation of each embedding (shortcut connection) is close to one, achieved either by scaling embeddings or applying layer normalization to the embedding layer. Empirical verification will be conducted by implementing these modifications in large-scale pre-training setups and comparing their effect on loss and gradient spike occurrence.
c431b1a922385830d4c934a5679edfb9cedc600b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the C4 dataset for pre-training, with validation on separated C4 data. Evaluation will include perplexity measurements on WikiText and LAMBADA datasets, as well as accuracy on standard benchmarks such as PIQA, OpenBookQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-easy, and ARC-challenge. Model configurations will include Pre-LN Transformer architectures with parameter sizes of 350M, 1.7B, and 13B, using the GPT-2 BPE vocabulary. Methods compared will include the standard (Vanilla) configuration, embedding gradient detachment, embedding layer normalization, and scaled embedding approaches. Key metrics will be loss curves, gradient norms, and perplexity, with experiments run at multiple learning rates to assess stability and performance under different training regimes.
c431b1a922385830d4c934a5679edfb9cedc600b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretically grounded analysis linking loss spikes to the spectral norms of sub-layer Jacobians in Transformers, providing explicit upper bounds on gradient norms. It establishes two concrete, generalizable conditions—small sub-layer initialization and large embedding shortcut variance—for stabilizing pre-training, and demonstrates that these conditions are not always satisfied in current standard LLM implementations. The approach unifies and explains the effectiveness of several previously empirical stabilization techniques, enabling stable training at larger learning rates and model scales, and systematically prevents catastrophic divergence during LLM pre-training.

c435ecd0321dcec1f25e458bf930311f9e1d04b6.title: Winoground: Probing Vision and Language Models for Visio-Linguistic Compositionality
c435ecd0321dcec1f25e458bf930311f9e1d04b6.research_question: How effectively can current vision and language models perform visio-linguistic compositional reasoning, particularly when required to distinguish between images and captions that contain identical sets of words in different orders?
c435ecd0321dcec1f25e458bf930311f9e1d04b6.hypothesis: State-of-the-art vision and language models will struggle to perform visio-linguistic compositional reasoning when tested on tasks that require sensitivity to word order and compositional structure, performing at or near chance levels.
c435ecd0321dcec1f25e458bf930311f9e1d04b6.proposed_method: A novel evaluation task and dataset, Winoground, will be developed to probe visio-linguistic compositionality in multimodal models. Each example in the dataset will consist of two images and two captions, where both captions contain exactly the same set of words but in different orders, such that each caption matches only one image. The dataset will be carefully hand-curated by expert annotators, who will also provide a rich set of fine-grained linguistic and visual tags to facilitate detailed analysis. The evaluation protocol will include three metrics: text score (matching captions to images), image score (matching images to captions), and group score (requiring correct matching of all combinations in a set). Human performance will be established via crowdsourcing for baseline comparison.
c435ecd0321dcec1f25e458bf930311f9e1d04b6.experiment_details: Experiments will involve evaluating a diverse set of state-of-the-art vision and language models, including both transformer-based (e.g., UNITER, ViLLA, VinVL, VisualBERT, ViLT, LXMERT, ViLBERT, UniT, FLAVA, CLIP) and RNN-based (VSE++, VSRN) architectures. Models will be tested on the Winoground dataset, which contains 400 examples (1600 image-caption pairs) with 800 unique images and captions. Baselines will include random chance and human performance (measured via Amazon Mechanical Turk). Evaluation metrics will be computed for overall performance as well as for specific linguistic and visual tags. Additional analyses will assess the impact of model architecture, pretraining dataset size, caption length, and caption perplexity on performance.
c435ecd0321dcec1f25e458bf930311f9e1d04b6.novelty_claims: The proposed task and dataset introduce a new, rigorous benchmark for visio-linguistic compositional reasoning that cannot be solved by bag-of-words or unimodal priors, as both captions in each example use the same words in different orders. The dataset is expertly curated and richly annotated with fine-grained linguistic and visual tags, enabling detailed error analysis and probing of model capabilities. This approach provides a more precise and challenging evaluation of compositional reasoning than existing multimodal benchmarks, and is designed to drive progress in the development of more robust vision and language models.

c458cec389a2ed3bbe5e35bc9a5b0a85ca073d15.title: Human Control: Definitions and Algorithms
c458cec389a2ed3bbe5e35bc9a5b0a85ca073d15.research_question: How can artificial intelligence systems be designed to ensure robust human control, particularly in scenarios involving shutdown or corrective instruction, while avoiding undesirable incentives such as resisting shutdown or manipulating human overseers?
c458cec389a2ed3bbe5e35bc9a5b0a85ca073d15.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that formalizing and incentivizing specific behavioral properties—such as shutdown instructability, vigilance, obedience, and caution—will enable the design of AI agents that reliably accept and follow human corrective instructions, preserve human autonomy, and avoid causing harm, even in the presence of advanced capabilities and potential incentive misalignments.
c458cec389a2ed3bbe5e35bc9a5b0a85ca073d15.proposed_method: A formal framework will be developed for modeling human control over AI systems using structural causal influence models (SCIMs), with a focus on the shutdown problem as a canonical scenario. The methodology will define and analyze behavioral properties such as shutdown instructability (requiring obedience to shutdown commands, ensuring human vigilance, and agent caution), shutdown alignment (acting in accordance with human values, even without explicit instruction), and non-obstruction (ensuring the agent does not interfere with human control). Several algorithms will be rigorously specified and compared within this framework, including utility indifference, causal indifference, cooperative inverse reinforcement learning (CIRL), and a new constrained optimization approach that explicitly enforces the desired behavioral constraints. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to prove the relationships between these properties and to establish under what conditions each algorithm achieves the desired safety guarantees.
c458cec389a2ed3bbe5e35bc9a5b0a85ca073d15.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using formal, toy shutdown scenarios modeled as SCIMs, where agents interact with human overseers who may issue shutdown commands based on latent values. Each algorithm will be instantiated within these models and evaluated for its ability to achieve shutdown instructability, shutdown alignment, and non-obstruction. Baseline comparisons will include previously proposed methods such as utility indifference, causal indifference, and CIRL. Evaluation metrics will include expected human utility, the frequency and correctness of shutdown behavior, preservation of human autonomy, and robustness to changes in human preferences or behavior. Additional analysis will assess the algorithms' performance under varying assumptions about agent knowledge, human rationality, and the availability of utility information.
c458cec389a2ed3bbe5e35bc9a5b0a85ca073d15.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a formal definition of shutdown instructability as a behavioral variant of corrigibility, providing rigorous guarantees for human control in AI systems. It establishes, for the first time, a unified causal framework for comparing and analyzing different approaches to human control, including both existing and novel algorithms. The constrained optimization algorithm is proposed as a sound method for achieving shutdown instructability, contingent on the agent's ability to model vigilance, obedience, and caution. The analysis clarifies the limitations of prior approaches and demonstrates that shutdown instructability is more closely coupled to non-obstruction (true human control) than alternative properties such as shutdown alignment. This work aims to set a new standard for the formal study and practical achievement of corrigibility and safe human oversight in advanced AI systems.

c464ad1d4ec99c3ed8da02217df61dace3075f67.title: Long-Sequence Recommendation Models Need Decoupled Embeddings
c464ad1d4ec99c3ed8da02217df61dace3075f67.research_question: How can the interference between attention and representation learning in long-sequence recommendation models be mitigated to improve both retrieval accuracy and representation discriminability, while maintaining or improving efficiency for large-scale online recommendation systems?
c464ad1d4ec99c3ed8da02217df61dace3075f67.hypothesis: Decoupling the embedding spaces used for attention calculation and representation aggregation in long-sequence recommendation models will resolve gradient conflict and domination, leading to improved attention accuracy, better representation discriminability, and enhanced efficiency without significant loss in predictive performance.
c464ad1d4ec99c3ed8da02217df61dace3075f67.proposed_method: A novel recommendation framework is proposed that employs two fully decoupled embedding tables: one dedicated to attention calculation (correlation between target and user behaviors) and another dedicated to representation learning (discriminative feature aggregation for prediction). During the search stage, the attention embedding table is used to compute scaled dot-product attention scores between the target item and each behavior in the user's history, retrieving the top-k most relevant behaviors. In the sequence modeling stage, the representation embedding table is used to generate target-aware representations (e.g., via element-wise product between behavior and target embeddings), which are aggregated (weighted by attention scores) and passed to a predictor (such as an MLP) for click-through rate prediction. The decoupling allows independent optimization of each embedding space, resolving gradient conflicts and enabling flexible dimensionality choices for attention and representation. Additionally, the attention embedding dimension can be reduced to accelerate retrieval without degrading overall model performance.
c464ad1d4ec99c3ed8da02217df61dace3075f67.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on public long-sequence recommendation datasets such as Taobao and Tmall, where user click sequences and item/category IDs are available. The proposed method will be compared against a range of baselines, including ETA, SDIM, DIN, TWIN, TWIN-V2, and various projection-based or hard-search variants. Evaluation metrics will include AUC, NDCG for retrieval quality, mutual information for representation discriminability, GAUC, and Logloss. Both offline and large-scale online A/B testing will be performed, including deployment on a major advertising platform with billions of daily samples. The impact of embedding dimension, retrieval number, and sequence length will be systematically studied, and training/inference efficiency will be measured by convergence speed and search acceleration.
c464ad1d4ec99c3ed8da02217df61dace3075f67.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to identify and address the interference between attention and representation learning in long-sequence recommendation models from a multi-task learning perspective. The method introduces a fully decoupled embedding architecture, which resolves gradient domination and conflict, leading to significant improvements in both attention accuracy and representation discriminability. The approach enables substantial acceleration of the search stage (up to 50% faster) by reducing attention embedding size, without significant performance loss. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art results on public datasets and substantial online gains in a real-world production environment.

c4695ca6ace3f184b67d3561c418f20b124d067e.title: "What do you want from theory alone?" Experimenting with Tight Auditing of Differentially Private Synthetic Data Generation
c4695ca6ace3f184b67d3561c418f20b124d067e.research_question: How tightly can empirical privacy leakage be estimated in differentially private synthetic data generation (DP-SDG) algorithms, and how do different threat models and dataset configurations affect the accuracy and reliability of these privacy audits?
c4695ca6ace3f184b67d3561c418f20b124d067e.hypothesis: Empirical privacy leakage from DP-SDG implementations can be tightly estimated by employing rigorous auditing procedures, including strong adversarial threat models and carefully crafted worst-case datasets, and that current black-box auditing methods are insufficient to reveal all privacy violations or to match theoretical differential privacy guarantees.
c4695ca6ace3f184b67d3561c418f20b124d067e.proposed_method: A comprehensive auditing framework will be developed to empirically estimate privacy leakage in state-of-the-art DP-SDG implementations. The approach will employ membership inference attacks (MIAs) under a range of adversarial threat models, including black-box, passive white-box, and active white-box settings. The methodology will involve constructing both average-case and implementation-specific worst-case neighboring datasets, as well as identifying worst-case target records using vulnerability analysis. Multiple types of MIAs will be instantiated, such as distance-to-closest-record (DCR), query-based attacks, shadow modeling, and gradient canary attacks (for models with learnable parameters). The empirical privacy leakage will be quantified by comparing the adversary's success rates in distinguishing between outputs generated from neighboring datasets, and these results will be mapped to lower bounds on the differential privacy parameter (ε) using established statistical methods.
c4695ca6ace3f184b67d3561c418f20b124d067e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on widely used tabular datasets, such as the Adult and San Francisco Fire Department Calls for Service datasets, focusing on categorical attributes to ensure compatibility with various DP-SDG algorithms. The study will audit multiple implementations of three prominent DP-SDG algorithms (PrivBayes, MST, and DPWGAN), including both original and re-implemented versions from public and industry sources. Each implementation will be evaluated under different privacy budgets (ε values) and with both average-case and worst-case dataset configurations (e.g., small, narrow, and repeated-record datasets). Baseline comparisons will include standard black-box MIAs (DCR, query-based) and advanced white-box and active white-box attacks. Evaluation metrics will include empirical lower bounds on ε (ε_emp), false positive and negative rates, and the area under the ROC curve (AUC) for attack success. The experimental setup will involve training thousands of synthetic data models per configuration, with cross-validation and statistical confidence intervals reported for all results.
c4695ca6ace3f184b67d3561c418f20b124d067e.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first large-scale, systematic audit of DP-SDG algorithms and their implementations across multiple threat models and dataset configurations. It develops novel white-box MIAs for statistical generative models (PrivBayes, MST) and adapts active white-box auditing to generative adversarial networks (DPWGAN). The framework identifies both known and previously undiscovered differential privacy violations, including implementation-specific issues such as metadata leakage and random seed reuse. The research demonstrates that black-box MIAs are often insufficient for tight privacy estimation, and establishes the necessity of white-box and worst-case dataset audits for reliable empirical privacy guarantees.

c490f23a7f1bac63bab6eb7f83be9644e72dd986.title: Communication-Efficient Collaborative Perception via Information Filling with Codebook
c490f23a7f1bac63bab6eb7f83be9644e72dd986.research_question: How can collaborative perception systems for multi-agent 3D object detection be made more communication-efficient while maintaining or improving perception performance, especially in both homogeneous and heterogeneous sensor settings?
c490f23a7f1bac63bab6eb7f83be9644e72dd986.hypothesis: By optimizing both the representation and selection of collaborative messages—specifically through codebook-based message representation and information-filling-driven message selection—it is possible to significantly reduce communication costs without sacrificing, and potentially improving, collaborative perception performance across diverse agent and sensor configurations.
c490f23a7f1bac63bab6eb7f83be9644e72dd986.proposed_method: A novel collaborative perception framework, CodeFilling, will be developed to optimize the trade-off between perception ability and communication cost. The method consists of four main modules: (1) a single-agent detector that processes multi-modal sensor data (LiDAR, camera) and projects features into a unified bird’s-eye view (BEV) space; (2) an information-filling-driven message selection module that generates spatial information score maps and solves a constrained optimization problem to select non-redundant, informative spatial regions for message sharing; (3) a codebook-based message representation module that approximates selected feature vectors with learned task-driven codebooks, enabling agents to transmit compact integer code indices instead of high-dimensional floating-point feature maps; and (4) a message decoding and fusion module that reconstructs and aggregates supportive features from received code indices using the shared codebook, followed by detection decoding. The codebook is learned jointly with the detection task to ensure that the compressed representation retains essential information for 3D object detection. The overall system is trained end-to-end with losses for detection, information score map generation, and codebook learning.
c490f23a7f1bac63bab6eb7f83be9644e72dd986.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both a real-world dataset (DAIR-V2X) and a large-scale simulation dataset (OPV2VH+), covering homogeneous (LiDAR-only, camera-only) and heterogeneous (mixed sensor) agent settings. The evaluation will focus on 3D object detection performance, using Average Precision (AP) at IoU thresholds of 0.30 and 0.50 as the primary metrics. Communication cost will be measured as the total message size in bytes (log-scaled), following standard protocols. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art collaborative perception methods such as Where2comm, HMViT, V2VNet, DiscoNet, V2X-ViT, AttFuse, and late fusion. Additional robustness experiments will assess the impact of pose errors (using Gaussian noise) and communication latency. Ablation studies will examine the contributions of the message selection and codebook representation modules, as well as the effects of varying codebook size, code quantity, and information demand parameters.
c490f23a7f1bac63bab6eb7f83be9644e72dd986.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces two key innovations: (1) a codebook-based message representation that enables efficient transmission of perceptual information via compact integer indices, significantly reducing communication overhead compared to floating-point feature maps; and (2) an information-filling-driven message selection strategy that collectively optimizes the selection of non-redundant, informative spatial regions to fulfill each agent’s information demand, further minimizing redundant communication. The framework is designed to be inclusive of both homogeneous and heterogeneous agent settings, providing a standardized feature space for diverse sensor modalities. The method claims to achieve state-of-the-art perception-communication trade-offs, outperforming prior work by orders of magnitude in communication efficiency while maintaining or improving detection accuracy, and demonstrates robustness to real-world challenges such as pose errors and communication latency.

c49ac1f916d6d2edeb187e6619c8d23acd95eb21.title: cosFormer: Rethinking Softmax in Attention
c49ac1f916d6d2edeb187e6619c8d23acd95eb21.research_question: Can the softmax operator in transformer attention mechanisms be replaced with a linear function that maintains key properties of softmax, thereby enabling efficient and scalable attention for long sequences without sacrificing accuracy across a broad range of tasks?
c49ac1f916d6d2edeb187e6619c8d23acd95eb21.hypothesis: A linear attention mechanism that enforces non-negativity and incorporates a decomposable, cosine-based re-weighting scheme can match or surpass the accuracy of traditional softmax-based attention while reducing computational complexity to linear time and space.
c49ac1f916d6d2edeb187e6619c8d23acd95eb21.proposed_method: A new linear transformer architecture, COSFORMER, will be developed to replace the softmax operation in self-attention with a linear operator that satisfies two crucial properties: non-negativity of the attention matrix and a non-linear re-weighting mechanism. Non-negativity will be enforced by applying a ReLU activation to the query and key projections, ensuring that only positively correlated information is aggregated. To introduce a non-linear re-weighting effect similar to softmax, a cosine-based distance re-weighting mechanism will be incorporated, which amplifies local correlations and introduces a recency bias, leveraging Ptolemy’s theorem for efficient decomposition. The resulting attention computation will be fully decomposable and exhibit linear time and space complexity with respect to sequence length, making it suitable for both causal and cross-attention scenarios.
c49ac1f916d6d2edeb187e6619c8d23acd95eb21.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of language modeling and text understanding tasks, including autoregressive and bidirectional setups. Pre-training will be performed on the WikiText-103 dataset for both types of language models, and downstream fine-tuning will be evaluated on GLUE (QQP, SST-2, MNLI), IMDB, and AMAZON datasets. The method will also be benchmarked on the Long-Range Arena (LRA) suite, which includes tasks like ListOps, byte-level text classification, document retrieval, image classification on CIFAR-10, and Pathfinder, to assess long-range dependency modeling. Baselines will include vanilla Transformer, Performer, Reformer, Linear Transformer, Longformer, and other efficient transformer variants. Evaluation metrics will include perplexity for language modeling, accuracy for classification tasks, and average scores across LRA tasks. Efficiency will be measured in terms of training and inference speed as well as memory footprint, with experiments run on GPUs and sequence lengths ranging up to 4,000 tokens.
c49ac1f916d6d2edeb187e6619c8d23acd95eb21.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel linear attention mechanism that does not approximate softmax but instead replaces it with a fully decomposable linear operation combined with a cosine-based re-weighting scheme. This method uniquely enforces non-negativity and locality bias, resulting in linear time and space complexity without the approximation errors or instability of prior kernel-based or sparse attention methods. COSFORMER is claimed to achieve state-of-the-art performance on long-sequence benchmarks, match or exceed the accuracy of vanilla transformers on a wide range of tasks, and provide significant improvements in speed and memory efficiency over all existing efficient transformer architectures.

c4adc81a41aa1f3dd8c835d22a8f3c34da10711d.title: The Bias Amplification Paradox in Text-to-Image Generation
c4adc81a41aa1f3dd8c835d22a8f3c34da10711d.research_question: How can bias amplification in text-to-image generation models be accurately measured, and what are the underlying factors that contribute to apparent amplification of gender-occupation biases when comparing generated images to training data?
c4adc81a41aa1f3dd8c835d22a8f3c34da10711d.hypothesis: Apparent bias amplification in text-to-image generation models is significantly influenced by distributional discrepancies between training captions and generation prompts, and accounting for these differences will substantially reduce measured amplification.
c4adc81a41aa1f3dd8c835d22a8f3c34da10711d.proposed_method: The proposed research will systematically investigate bias amplification in text-to-image generation by comparing gender distributions in training data and generated images for a set of occupations. The methodology involves generating images using a suite of prompts that do not specify gender, then classifying the gender of generated and training images using automated face and gender detection methods. To address confounding factors, the approach will include (1) filtering training captions to exclude those with explicit gender indicators, (2) using nearest neighbor retrieval in text embedding space to select training captions that closely match the structure and semantics of prompts, and (3) directly aligning prompts with training captions to establish a lower bound for amplification. Bias amplification will be quantified as the difference in deviation from gender parity between generated and training images for each occupation.
c4adc81a41aa1f3dd8c835d22a8f3c34da10711d.experiment_details: Experiments will use Stable Diffusion (versions 1.4 and 1.5) as the text-to-image model, with LAION-5B as the training dataset. Sixty-two occupations will be selected, and for each, 500 images will be generated per prompt using four distinct, gender-neutral prompts. Gender classification will be performed using a combination of face detection and CLIP-based zero-shot gender prediction, filtering for high-confidence cases. Baseline comparisons will include naive keyword-based selection of training captions, exclusion of captions with gender indicators, and nearest neighbor matching in embedding space. Evaluation metrics will include average bias amplification across occupations and prompts, with statistical tests to assess significance. Additional analyses will compare the effects of prompt variation and the impact of aligning prompts with training captions.
c4adc81a41aa1f3dd8c835d22a8f3c34da10711d.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a critical re-examination of bias amplification measurement in text-to-image generation, highlighting and addressing the confounding impact of distributional differences between training and generation inputs. The research proposes novel methodological controls, including explicit filtering of gender indicators and embedding-based nearest neighbor selection, to more accurately isolate model-induced amplification from artifacts of data mismatch. The approach establishes a lower bound for bias amplification by directly aligning prompts with training captions, providing new insights into the true extent of model bias. The findings are expected to inform best practices for bias evaluation and encourage more nuanced analyses in future studies.

c4c317d8e718500fe694c27bce0869db503e711c.title: Data re-uploading with a single qudit
c4c317d8e718500fe694c27bce0869db503e711c.research_question: Can multi-level quantum systems (qudits) be effectively utilized in quantum machine learning, specifically for classification and regression tasks, and how do their capabilities compare to traditional qubit-based approaches?
c4c317d8e718500fe694c27bce0869db503e711c.hypothesis: Qudit-based quantum circuits, when used in data re-uploading architectures, can achieve equal or superior performance to qubit-based circuits in certain machine learning tasks, particularly when the structure of the data and label encoding is well-aligned with the qudit Hilbert space. The inclusion of specific quantum operators, such as squeezing, is hypothesized to be necessary for optimal performance.
c4c317d8e718500fe694c27bce0869db503e711c.proposed_method: A data re-uploading quantum circuit architecture will be developed using a single d-level qudit, where each class label is encoded as an orthogonal basis state of the qudit. The circuit will be constructed from multiple layers, each comprising data-dependent and data-independent unitary operations generated by exponentiating angular momentum operators (Lx, Lz) and a squeezing operator (Lz^2). Two main circuit structures will be explored: one inspired by Euler rotations with alternating x and z rotations, and another simplified form that generalizes the data encoding and includes squeezing in each layer. The model will be trained using supervised learning, optimizing circuit parameters via classical optimization algorithms (e.g., ADAM, L-BFGS-B, Powell) to minimize loss functions such as mean squared error (MSE) or overlap loss. For comparison, equivalent circuits will be implemented using qubits, with multi-class labels represented by maximally orthogonal single-qubit states, and qudit circuits will be mapped to multi-qubit systems for hardware execution.
c4c317d8e718500fe694c27bce0869db503e711c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Synthetic datasets will include 1D regression tasks and 2D multi-class classification problems (e.g., horizontal stripes, rotated stripes, concentric rings), while real-world evaluation will use the MNIST handwritten digits dataset (with dimensionality reduction via PCA). Baseline comparisons will be made against classical machine learning algorithms such as random forest, k-nearest neighbors, and support vector classifiers. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy and mean squared error, with performance assessed over multiple random splits of training and test sets (e.g., 750 training and 250 test samples, repeated 50-60 times for statistical robustness). Both numerically exact simulations and implementations on IBM quantum hardware (using mapped multi-qubit representations and 512 measurement shots per circuit) will be performed to assess the impact of hardware noise and finite sampling.
c4c317d8e718500fe694c27bce0869db503e711c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach investigates the fundamental capabilities of single-qudit data re-uploading circuits for machine learning, demonstrating that qudits can efficiently encode multi-class labels and learn highly non-linear decision boundaries. The research claims that the alignment between qudit state encoding and data structure introduces an inductive bias that can substantially improve performance over qubit-based circuits in certain scenarios. The necessity of the squeezing operator for achieving full expressivity in qudit circuits is elucidated. Additionally, a systematic comparison between qudit and qubit data re-uploading circuits is provided, including practical considerations for mapping qudits to multi-qubit hardware and the effects of measurement noise and operator choices on learning performance.

c4e0c4a6e82ed58ca57ec36a8ec275db38473ba2.title: Structure Invariant Transformation for better Adversarial Transferability
c4e0c4a6e82ed58ca57ec36a8ec275db38473ba2.research_question: How can the transferability of adversarial examples across different deep neural network architectures be improved, particularly in black-box settings, without sacrificing semantic integrity or recognition by humans?
c4e0c4a6e82ed58ca57ec36a8ec275db38473ba2.hypothesis: Increasing the diversity of input transformations, especially by applying localized and varied transformations to image blocks while preserving the global structure, will significantly enhance the transferability of adversarial examples across both convolutional and transformer-based neural networks.
c4e0c4a6e82ed58ca57ec36a8ec275db38473ba2.proposed_method: A novel input transformation-based attack, termed Structure Invariant Attack (SIA), will be developed to boost adversarial transferability. The method will partition each input image into multiple blocks (e.g., a 3x3 grid) and apply a randomly selected transformation (such as shifting, flipping, rotation, scaling, noise addition, resizing, DCT, or dropout) independently to each block, thereby generating highly diverse but structurally consistent images. For each attack iteration, a set of N such transformed images will be created, and the average gradient across these images will be computed to update the adversarial perturbation using a momentum-based iterative scheme. Constraints will be imposed on certain transformations (e.g., only 180-degree rotations) to avoid information loss and ensure semantic content is preserved. This approach is designed to be compatible with existing gradient-based attacks and can be integrated with model-specific or ensemble-based attack strategies.
c4e0c4a6e82ed58ca57ec36a8ec275db38473ba2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the ImageNet ILSVRC 2012 validation set, using 1,000 images from 1,000 categories that are correctly classified by the baseline models. The proposed SIA will be compared against state-of-the-art input transformation-based attacks (DIM, TIM, DEM, Admix, SSA) and integrated into momentum-based (MI-FGSM), model-specific (SGM, LinBP), and ensemble attack frameworks. Both convolutional (ResNet-18, ResNet-101, ResNext-50, DenseNet-121, MobileNet) and transformer-based (ViT, Swin Transformer) architectures will serve as surrogate and victim models. Evaluation metrics will include attack success rate (misclassification rate) in both white-box and black-box settings, as well as transferability across architectures. Additional experiments will assess attack performance against a suite of defense mechanisms (e.g., adversarial training, denoisers, certified defenses, input preprocessing). Ablation studies will examine the contribution of individual transformations, block partitioning, and parameter sensitivity (number of blocks, number of transformed images per gradient step).
c4e0c4a6e82ed58ca57ec36a8ec275db38473ba2.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a structure-invariant transformation framework that applies diverse, localized transformations to image blocks, rather than global transformations, to maximize diversity while preserving semantic structure. This fine-grained approach is claimed to significantly enhance adversarial transferability across both CNN and transformer architectures, outperforming existing state-of-the-art input transformation-based attacks. The method is generalizable, compatible with a variety of attack and defense strategies, and provides new insights into the relationship between transformation diversity and adversarial robustness.

c4e251fe9574036a1de4eef5152bfb4507ee16c2.title: Learnable Filters for Geometric Scattering Modules
c4e251fe9574036a1de4eef5152bfb4507ee16c2.research_question: How can graph neural networks be enhanced to more effectively capture multi-scale and long-range dependencies in graph-structured data, while maintaining mathematical guarantees and improving performance on graph classification and regression tasks?
c4e251fe9574036a1de4eef5152bfb4507ee16c2.hypothesis: Introducing a learnable geometric scattering module into graph neural networks will enable adaptive, multi-frequency feature extraction, leading to improved expressiveness, robustness, and predictive performance, particularly on graphs with complex connectivity and large diameters.
c4e251fe9574036a1de4eef5152bfb4507ee16c2.proposed_method: A novel learnable geometric scattering (LEGS) module will be developed and integrated into graph neural network architectures. The LEGS module will generalize the geometric scattering transform by allowing the diffusion wavelet scales to be learned from data via backpropagation, rather than being fixed a priori. The method will construct a bank of graph wavelet filters parameterized by trainable diffusion scales, implemented through a differentiable module that cascades diffusion operators and pointwise nonlinearities. Node-level features will be aggregated using statistical moments to form permutation-invariant graph-level representations. The module will be incorporated into larger neural networks, with options for fully connected or radial basis function output layers, and will support hybrid or ensemble architectures with other GNN modules.
c4e251fe9574036a1de4eef5152bfb4507ee16c2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of graph classification and regression benchmarks, including biochemical datasets (e.g., NCI1, NCI109, ENZYMES, PROTEINS, PTC, DD, MUTAG), social network datasets (e.g., COLLAB, IMDB-BINARY, IMDB-MULTI, REDDIT-BINARY, REDDIT-MULTI-12K, REDDIT-MULTI-5K), and molecular property prediction tasks (e.g., QM9, ZINC15, BindingDB, CASP12). Baselines will include standard GNNs such as GCN, GraphSAGE, GAT, GIN, as well as fixed geometric scattering with SVM and simple neural network baselines. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy for graph classification tasks and mean squared error for regression tasks. Experimental setups will involve 10-fold cross-validation, ablation studies on training set size, and ensemble models combining LEGS with other GNN features. Additional analyses will assess the descriptive quality of learned embeddings and robustness to reduced training data.
c4e251fe9574036a1de4eef5152bfb4507ee16c2.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first fully differentiable, learnable geometric scattering module for graph neural networks, enabling adaptive selection of multi-scale diffusion wavelet filters. This method retains the mathematical guarantees of geometric scattering (such as stability, energy preservation, and permutation invariance) while allowing end-to-end task-driven learning. The approach achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on a range of graph classification and regression benchmarks, particularly excelling on biochemical graphs with large diameters and complex connectivity. The method also demonstrates robustness to small training sets and provides descriptive embeddings that preserve global graph relationships, supporting its use in both predictive and exploratory graph analysis.

c4e9f6433ba328212958c4dedba589b45f13d052.title: Bayesian Federated Learning: A Survey
c4e9f6433ba328212958c4dedba589b45f13d052.research_question: How can federated learning be enhanced to better address challenges such as limited and dynamic data, client heterogeneity, uncertainty, and the need for analytical explainability in decentralized, privacy-preserving environments?
c4e9f6433ba328212958c4dedba589b45f13d052.hypothesis: Integrating Bayesian learning principles into federated learning frameworks will enable more robust, well-calibrated, and dynamic predictions, particularly in the presence of uncertainty, heterogeneity, and limited data.
c4e9f6433ba328212958c4dedba589b45f13d052.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework for Bayesian Federated Learning (BFL) will be developed, systematically incorporating Bayesian inference into both client-side and server-side federated learning processes. On the client side, methods such as Bayesian neural networks, Bayesian optimization, and Bayesian nonparametric models will be used to enable local models to quantify uncertainty and leverage prior knowledge, improving robustness and performance on small or non-IID datasets. On the server side, aggregation and decomposition techniques such as Bayesian model ensembles, Bayesian posterior decomposition, and Bayesian continual learning will be employed to aggregate local updates into global models while maintaining uncertainty quantification and interpretability. The framework will also explore hybrid, hierarchical, and dynamic BFL methods to address evolving, heterogeneous, and complex real-world scenarios. Optimization strategies, including variational inference and expectation propagation, will be utilized to approximate posterior distributions efficiently and manage computational and communication costs.
c4e9f6433ba328212958c4dedba589b45f13d052.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of real-world and benchmark datasets relevant to federated learning, including domains such as healthcare, finance, autonomous driving, and smart devices. Both IID and non-IID data distributions will be considered to evaluate robustness. Baseline comparisons will include classic federated learning algorithms (e.g., FedAvg), privacy-preserving FL, and state-of-the-art Bayesian and non-Bayesian FL methods. Evaluation metrics will encompass accuracy, robustness to data heterogeneity, uncertainty calibration (e.g., expected calibration error), communication and computational efficiency, and privacy guarantees. Experimental setups will involve varying the number of clients, degree of data heterogeneity, and communication rounds to assess scalability and adaptability.
c4e9f6433ba328212958c4dedba589b45f13d052.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified taxonomy and comprehensive framework for Bayesian Federated Learning that systematically integrates Bayesian inference into federated learning at both client and server levels. It advances the state of the art by addressing limitations of existing FL methods in handling uncertainty, limited data, and heterogeneity, and by providing mechanisms for robust, explainable, and dynamically adaptive learning. The proposal also identifies and aims to fill key gaps in current BFL research, such as handling complex non-IIDness, hierarchical and hybrid structures, dynamic and evolving client conditions, and actionable requirements for real-world applications.

c4fb74b5f69e5c0f3822b82e1bd082d5d95fc8d0.title: Tractable Control for Autoregressive Language Generation
c4fb74b5f69e5c0f3822b82e1bd082d5d95fc8d0.research_question: How can complex lexical constraints be efficiently and reliably imposed on autoregressive language generation models, such that generated text satisfies arbitrary constraints without sacrificing generation quality?
c4fb74b5f69e5c0f3822b82e1bd082d5d95fc8d0.hypothesis: Tractable probabilistic models (TPMs), when trained to approximate large language models, can be used to guide autoregressive generation to efficiently satisfy arbitrary lexical constraints while maintaining or improving generation quality.
c4fb74b5f69e5c0f3822b82e1bd082d5d95fc8d0.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that leverages tractable probabilistic models (TPMs), specifically hidden Markov models (HMMs), to guide autoregressive language generation under arbitrary lexical constraints. The approach involves first distilling a TPM to approximate the distribution of a pre-trained language model (e.g., GPT2-large) via maximum likelihood estimation on samples from the language model, minimizing KL-divergence between the two. At inference time, the TPM is used to efficiently compute the probability of satisfying a given lexical constraint, formulated as a conjunctive normal form (CNF), for any sequence prefix. This probability is combined with the language model's next-token distribution to produce a new conditional distribution for constrained generation. An efficient dynamic programming algorithm is developed to compute the required conditional probabilities for HMMs, enabling fast and exact enforcement of constraints during generation. The method supports both unsupervised (domain-adapted) and supervised (seq2seq fine-tuned) settings, with a hyperparameter controlling the influence of the TPM and language model in the supervised case.
c4fb74b5f69e5c0f3822b82e1bd082d5d95fc8d0.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on challenging constrained text generation benchmarks, including CommonGen, Yelp!Review, and News datasets.
