The base language model is GPT2-large, fine-tuned either for domain adaptation (unsupervised) or in a sequence-to-sequence manner (supervised). HMMs with 4096 hidden states are trained as TPMs using the expectation-maximization algorithm on samples from the fine-tuned language model. Lexical constraints are encoded as CNFs, capturing required keywords and their inflections. Generation is performed using beam search with various beam sizes, and outputs are re-ranked by the base language model's log-likelihood. Evaluation metrics include BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, SPICE, constraint coverage, and success rate, with both automatic and human evaluations. Baselines include insertion-based models (InsNet), search-based decoding (NeuroLogic, A*esque), and auxiliary neural models (NADO). Ablation studies analyze the impact of TPM approximation quality, hyperparameter robustness, and beam size. Run-time comparisons are performed on GPU hardware.
c4fb74b5f69e5c0f3822b82e1bd082d5d95fc8d0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to use tractable probabilistic models to impose arbitrary lexical constraints in autoregressive language generation, guaranteeing 100% constraint satisfaction while achieving state-of-the-art generation quality. The method decouples constraint enforcement from TPM training, allowing any constraint to be imposed at inference without retraining. An efficient dynamic programming algorithm is introduced for conditioning HMMs on complex lexical constraints. The framework demonstrates scalability and effectiveness across multiple datasets and constraint types, motivating further development of more expressive TPMs for language modeling.

c4ff8bc44d88cd267baf18ac5d3a3a1fe86d08eb.title: Training Language Models to Self-Correct via Reinforcement Learning
c4ff8bc44d88cd267baf18ac5d3a3a1fe86d08eb.research_question: How can large language models be trained to effectively self-correct their own mistakes in multi-turn reasoning tasks, using only self-generated data and without reliance on external supervision or multiple models?
c4ff8bc44d88cd267baf18ac5d3a3a1fe86d08eb.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a multi-turn, on-policy reinforcement learning approach, with explicit regularization and reward shaping, can significantly improve the intrinsic self-correction ability of large language models compared to supervised fine-tuning or standard RL approaches.
c4ff8bc44d88cd267baf18ac5d3a3a1fe86d08eb.proposed_method: A novel two-stage multi-turn reinforcement learning framework, SCoRe, will be developed to train large language models for self-correction. In Stage I, the model is initialized by optimizing for high-reward second-attempt responses while constraining the first attempt to remain close to the base model via a KL-divergence penalty, thus decoupling the two attempts and preventing behavior collapse. In Stage II, the model is jointly trained on both attempts using a reward shaping mechanism that provides a bonus for transitions that demonstrate genuine self-correction progress—specifically, correcting previously incorrect answers and penalizing changes that degrade correctness. The approach operates entirely on self-generated data, leveraging on-policy rollouts to avoid distribution shift and ensure that the learned policy generalizes to the model's own mistakes. Adaptive regularization and optional augmentation with base model samples are incorporated to further enhance learning stability and coverage.
c4ff8bc44d88cd267baf18ac5d3a3a1fe86d08eb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Gemini 1.0 Pro and Gemini 1.5 Flash language models. The primary evaluation datasets will be MATH (Hendrycks et al., 2021) for mathematical reasoning and HumanEval (Chen et al., 2021) for code generation tasks. Baselines will include supervised fine-tuning approaches such as STaR and Pair-SFT, as well as standard multi-turn RL. Evaluation metrics will comprise accuracy at the first and second attempts, net improvement in accuracy (Δ(t1, t2)), the fraction of incorrect-to-correct transitions (Δi→c), and the fraction of correct-to-incorrect transitions (Δc→i). The experimental setup will involve multi-turn (two-turn) self-correction traces, and ablation studies will be performed to analyze the impact of each stage and the reward shaping mechanism.
c4ff8bc44d88cd267baf18ac5d3a3a1fe86d08eb.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first multi-turn RL framework that achieves substantial intrinsic self-correction in LLMs using only self-generated data, without external supervision, teacher models, or majority voting. The two-stage training process with explicit decoupling and reward shaping directly addresses the failure modes of distribution shift and behavior collapse found in prior methods. The approach demonstrates significant improvements in self-correction ability, setting new state-of-the-art results on established reasoning and coding benchmarks.

c501897288fa5c84047f6292ac88be76e0e7d1d9.title: On the Effective Number of Linear Regions in Shallow Univariate ReLU Networks: Convergence Guarantees and Implicit Bias
c501897288fa5c84047f6292ac88be76e0e7d1d9.research_question: What are the convergence properties and implicit bias of gradient flow when training shallow univariate ReLU neural networks for binary classification, and how does network width affect generalization and the effective number of linear regions in the learned function?
c501897288fa5c84047f6292ac88be76e0e7d1d9.hypothesis: Gradient flow on sufficiently wide univariate ReLU networks, when trained on data labeled by a target network of width r, will converge to solutions that achieve perfect training accuracy and possess at most O(r) linear regions, even under mild over-parameterization, thereby providing generalization guarantees.
c501897288fa5c84047f6292ac88be76e0e7d1d9.proposed_method: The proposed approach involves analyzing the dynamics of gradient flow (GF) on depth-2 (single hidden layer) univariate ReLU neural networks in a binary classification setting. The method assumes that the data labels are generated by the sign of a target network with r neurons. The analysis is conducted under the assumption of i.i.d. normally distributed initialization of weights and biases, and a compactly supported data distribution. Theoretical results are derived to show that, with high probability, GF converges in direction to a network achieving zero training error and having at most O(r) linear regions. The methodology includes a two-stage proof: first, establishing that sufficient over-parameterization ensures the empirical loss can be driven arbitrarily low; second, characterizing the implicit bias of GF to demonstrate convergence to a solution with a minimal number of linear regions, independent of the initial width, once the loss is sufficiently small.
c501897288fa5c84047f6292ac88be76e0e7d1d9.experiment_details: The experimental validation will be primarily theoretical, relying on rigorous proofs and probabilistic arguments. Theoretical results will be stated under explicit assumptions about the initialization (e.g., Gaussian with specified variance) and the data distribution (e.g., compact support, minimum interval length with constant label). The analysis will consider varying the network width k relative to the target width r, and will derive sample complexity and generalization bounds. Comparisons will be made to existing results in the literature, particularly those based on norm minimization and NTK/lazy training regimes, to highlight differences in width requirements and generalization behavior. Evaluation metrics include the number of linear regions in the learned function, empirical and population loss, and the probability of achieving perfect classification.
c501897288fa5c84047f6292ac88be76e0e7d1d9.novelty_claims: The proposal claims to provide the first end-to-end convergence and generalization guarantees for gradient flow on univariate ReLU networks in the binary classification setting, under mild over-parameterization. The analysis demonstrates that over-parameterization is both necessary and sufficient for successful optimization, and that the implicit bias of gradient flow leads to solutions with an effective number of linear regions matching the target network up to a constant factor. This geometric characterization of implicit bias enables intuitive generalization bounds and goes beyond norm-based and NTK-based analyses by operating in the rich (feature-learning) regime. The results also establish that the required network width depends only on the complexity of the target function, not on the sample size, and provide lower bounds showing that insufficient width prevents successful learning.

c5274ab0368de03859793840945dc865bcef1044.title: Robust Multi-Task Learning with Excess Risks
c5274ab0368de03859793840945dc865bcef1044.research_question: How can multi-task learning be made robust to label noise, particularly in scenarios where tasks are drawn from heterogeneous sources with varying data quality?
c5274ab0368de03859793840945dc865bcef1044.hypothesis: A task balancing method that dynamically updates task weights based on excess risks—defined as the gap between current and optimal model performance—will yield more robust multi-task learning outcomes in the presence of label noise than existing loss-based or gradient-based weighting methods.
c5274ab0368de03859793840945dc865bcef1044.proposed_method: A novel multi-task learning framework, ExcessMTL, is proposed that assigns task weights according to the excess risk of each task, which measures the distance to convergence rather than the raw loss. Excess risks are estimated efficiently using a Taylor approximation, with the Hessian matrix approximated via the diagonal of the empirical Fisher information matrix, computed from historical gradients. Task weights are updated using a multiplicative (exponentiated gradient) scheme, ensuring stability and convergence, and are normalized at each iteration. The method includes scale processing to normalize excess risks across tasks, addressing issues arising from heterogeneous loss scales or data magnitudes. The optimization proceeds iteratively: excess risks are estimated, weights are updated, and a gradient update is performed using the weighted sum of task losses.
c5274ab0368de03859793840945dc865bcef1044.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several multi-task learning benchmarks, including MultiMNIST, Office-Home, and NYUv2. Label noise will be injected into one or more tasks by flipping labels (for classification) or adding Gaussian noise (for regression), with the noise level varied systematically. Baselines for comparison will include adaptive weighting methods such as GradNorm, MGDA, GroupDRO, IMTL, and uniform scalarization, as well as validation-based weighting (MOML). Evaluation metrics will include overall accuracy, accuracy on clean tasks, and task-specific metrics (e.g., pixel accuracy, relative error, angle accuracy) depending on the dataset. The experimental setup will measure the impact of increasing noise on both noisy and clean tasks, with a focus on the robustness of the proposed method compared to baselines.
c5274ab0368de03859793840945dc865bcef1044.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the use of excess risk as a robust criterion for task weighting in multi-task learning, providing resilience to label noise by focusing on the improvable portion of risk. The approach offers an efficient and accurate excess risk estimation via Taylor approximation and a stable multiplicative weight update mechanism. Theoretical analysis establishes convergence guarantees and Pareto stationarity, matching or exceeding the properties of existing multi-objective optimization methods. Empirical results demonstrate superior robustness and performance on clean tasks under high label noise, outperforming both adaptive and static baselines. The insights on excess risk and convergence distance have potential applicability beyond multi-task learning, suggesting broader impact for robust algorithmic design in machine learning.

c536c7a33452298937a093ea65e87462bb95bedd.title: Learning to Refactor Action and Co-occurrence Features for Temporal Action Localization
c536c7a33452298937a093ea65e87462bb95bedd.research_question: How can temporal action localization in untrimmed videos be improved by addressing the challenge of co-occurring features, such as context and background, that often dominate subtle human action signals within video snippets?
c536c7a33452298937a093ea65e87462bb95bedd.hypothesis: Explicitly decoupling and recombining action and co-occurrence features within video snippets will yield more salient action representations, leading to improved accuracy in temporal action localization tasks.
c536c7a33452298937a093ea65e87462bb95bedd.proposed_method: A novel framework, termed RefactorNet, will be developed to refactor snippet-level video features for temporal action localization. The method consists of three main stages: (1) feature embedding using a two-stream network to extract snippet features, (2) a feature refactoring network that decouples each snippet representation into an action component and a co-occurrence component using two separate encoders trained with pairs of action samples and coupling samples, and (3) recombination of these components into a new snippet representation. The decoupling is supervised by minimizing and maximizing cosine similarities between action and co-occurrence components of action and coupling samples, respectively. A KL-divergence regularization is applied to the co-occurrence component to prevent it from overwhelming the action signal. The refactored features are then used by a boundary-based action detector for proposal generation, classification, and temporal boundary regression.
c536c7a33452298937a093ea65e87462bb95bedd.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the THUMOS14 and ActivityNet v1.3 benchmark datasets for temporal action localization. The feature extraction will use a two-stream I3D network pretrained on Kinetics, with video divided into 16-frame snippets. The action detector will utilize BSN for proposal generation, and features for each proposal will be pooled using RoIPooling. Multiple baselines will be compared, including a baseline without feature refactoring and a deep baseline with additional convolutional layers. Evaluation metrics will include mean Average Precision (mAP) at various tIoU thresholds, with standard splits and protocols followed for each dataset. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the contributions of the decoupling losses, KL regularization, and the impact of using only action or co-occurrence components.
c536c7a33452298937a093ea65e87462bb95bedd.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to explicitly refactor snippet-level features by decoupling and recombining action and co-occurrence components for temporal action localization. The method introduces a novel auxiliary task for feature decoupling using action and coupling samples derived from standard annotations, without requiring additional supervision for co-occurrence features. The recombination strategy and KL regularization ensure a balanced and salient action representation, leading to significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods on standard benchmarks. The approach is complementary to existing context modeling techniques and provides new insights into disentangled representation learning for video understanding.

c566041d4667dff6d5528e8fd76d362a33b8d0b2.title: The Price of Freedom: Exploring Expressivity and Runtime Tradeoffs in Equivariant Tensor Products
c566041d4667dff6d5528e8fd76d362a33b8d0b2.research_question: What are the tradeoffs between expressivity and computational efficiency in different tensor product operations for E(3)-equivariant neural networks, and how do these tradeoffs impact practical performance and applicability in 3D geometric deep learning tasks?
c566041d4667dff6d5528e8fd76d362a33b8d0b2.hypothesis: Reducing the computational complexity of tensor product operations in E(3)-equivariant neural networks leads to a corresponding reduction in expressivity, and this tradeoff can be systematically characterized and measured. Furthermore, alternative implementations of these operations can provide practical speedups without sacrificing asymptotic complexity, but may limit the types of geometric interactions that can be modeled.
c566041d4667dff6d5528e8fd76d362a33b8d0b2.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed to analyze and compare various tensor product operations (TPOs) used in E(3)-equivariant neural networks, including the Clebsch-Gordan Tensor Product (CGTP), Gaunt Tensor Product (GTP), and Matrix Tensor Product (MTP). The approach will introduce formal measures of expressivity and interactability, quantifying the space of equivariant bilinearities each TPO can represent and which irreducible representation (irrep) interactions are possible. The method will also include the design and implementation of a novel, simplified GTP using a spherical grid, which maintains the same asymptotic runtime as the original but is more efficient in practice. Theoretical analysis will be complemented by detailed runtime and expressivity comparisons, leveraging both asymptotic analysis and empirical microbenchmarking. Selection rules for each TPO will be derived to formalize the types of interactions permitted, and the impact of these rules on downstream tasks will be investigated.
c566041d4667dff6d5528e8fd76d362a33b8d0b2.experiment_details: Experiments will involve systematic microbenchmarking of CGTP, GTP (both Fourier and spherical grid implementations), and MTP on both CPU and GPU hardware (e.g., NVIDIA RTX A5500, A100). Metrics such as wall-clock time, FLOPs, and GPU utilization will be collected using tools like NVIDIA Nsight Compute. The benchmarks will be normalized for expressivity to enable fair comparison. Downstream experiments will include training and evaluating E(3)-equivariant neural networks on tasks such as force and energy prediction for molecular systems (using datasets like 3BPA and revised MD17) and classification of 3D chiral structures (e.g., 3D Tetris pieces). Baselines will include existing implementations of each TPO, and evaluation metrics will cover both computational performance and task accuracy. Additional analysis will investigate the ability of each TPO to model antisymmetric interactions and chiral structures.
c566041d4667dff6d5528e8fd76d362a33b8d0b2.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first systematic framework for quantifying and benchmarking the expressivity and interactability of tensor product operations in E(3)-equivariant neural networks. A novel, simplified implementation of the Gaunt Tensor Product using a spherical grid is developed, achieving the same asymptotic complexity as the original but with up to 30% practical speedup. The work provides the first comprehensive microbenchmarks of TPOs, revealing that theoretical runtime improvements often come at the cost of expressivity and that empirical performance may diverge from asymptotic predictions. The analysis formalizes the loss of antisymmetric interactions in certain fast TPOs and demonstrates the practical impact of these limitations on real-world tasks, such as chiral structure classification.

c57293882b2561e1ba03017902df9fc2f289dea2.title: Hierarchical Text-Conditional Image Generation with CLIP Latents
c57293882b2561e1ba03017902df9fc2f289dea2.research_question: How can robust joint text-image representations be leveraged to improve the diversity, photorealism, and controllability of text-conditional image generation systems?
c57293882b2561e1ba03017902df9fc2f289dea2.hypothesis: Explicitly generating and conditioning on learned image representations in a joint text-image embedding space will improve image diversity and enable more powerful semantic and style manipulations, while maintaining high photorealism and caption similarity.
c57293882b2561e1ba03017902df9fc2f289dea2.proposed_method: A hierarchical two-stage generative model is proposed for text-conditional image generation. The first stage is a prior model that generates CLIP image embeddings from a given text caption, using either an autoregressive (AR) or diffusion-based approach. The second stage is a diffusion-based decoder that generates images conditioned on the CLIP image embedding (and optionally the text caption). The decoder architecture is modified to incorporate CLIP embeddings into the timestep embedding and as context tokens, and classifier-free guidance is used by randomly dropping conditioning information during training. High-resolution images are produced via a cascade of two diffusion upsampler models, each trained with appropriate image degradations and spatial convolutions. The prior is trained either by quantizing PCA-reduced CLIP embeddings for AR modeling or directly modeling the continuous embedding with a diffusion process, with both approaches supporting classifier-free guidance.
c57293882b2561e1ba03017902df9fc2f289dea2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale datasets of image-caption pairs, such as those used for training CLIP and other text-to-image models. The proposed method will be compared against strong baselines including DALL-E and GLIDE, evaluating both AR and diffusion priors. Evaluation metrics will include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for sample quality, as well as systematic human evaluations for photorealism, caption similarity, and sample diversity. Additional experiments will probe the structure of the CLIP latent space, test image variation and interpolation capabilities, and assess zero-shot language-guided image manipulation. The impact of different prior architectures, guidance scales, and conditioning signals will be systematically analyzed.
c57293882b2561e1ba03017902df9fc2f289dea2.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a hierarchical text-to-image generation framework that explicitly models and inverts robust CLIP image embeddings, enabling improved image diversity with minimal loss in photorealism and caption similarity. The approach allows for powerful semantic and style-preserving image variations, interpolation between images, and zero-shot language-guided image manipulations, all within a unified joint embedding space. The use of diffusion models for both the prior and decoder stages is claimed to be more computationally efficient and to produce higher-quality samples than autoregressive approaches. The method also provides new tools for probing and visualizing the semantic structure of learned image representations.

c5859754c1f6c099199d42b488415b04a7bfd527.title: TWIN V2: Scaling Ultra-Long User Behavior Sequence Modeling for Enhanced CTR Prediction at Kuaishou
c5859754c1f6c099199d42b488415b04a7bfd527.research_question: How can ultra-long user behavior sequences, spanning the full lifecycle of user interactions, be efficiently and accurately modeled to enhance click-through rate (CTR) prediction in large-scale recommendation systems?
c5859754c1f6c099199d42b488415b04a7bfd527.hypothesis: Hierarchical clustering of life-cycle user behaviors, combined with cluster-aware attention mechanisms, enables efficient compression and modeling of ultra-long behavior sequences, resulting in more accurate and diverse CTR predictions compared to existing methods.
c5859754c1f6c099199d42b488415b04a7bfd527.proposed_method: A hierarchical clustering approach will be developed to aggregate similar items within a user's life-cycle behavior sequence into clusters during an offline phase. This compression reduces the sequence length from up to one million behaviors to a manageable number of clusters by recursively applying k-means clustering with adaptive cluster sizes, guided by collaborative filtering item embeddings. Each cluster will be represented by a virtual item, constructed by averaging numerical features and selecting representative categorical features. In the online phase, a two-stage retrieval and scoring process will be used: the General Search Unit (GSU) retrieves the top relevant clusters for a target item using cluster-aware target attention, which reweights attention scores based on cluster size, and the Exact Search Unit (ESU) further extracts long-term user interests from these clusters using multi-head attention. The resulting user interest representation is then used as input to the CTR prediction model.
c5859754c1f6c099199d42b488415b04a7bfd527.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a large-scale industrial dataset from Kuaishou, containing over 345 million users, 45 million videos, and 46 billion samples, with user histories reaching up to 100,000 behaviors. The dataset will be split by time, using 23 hours per day for training and 1 hour for testing, over five consecutive days. Baselines will include state-of-the-art models such as Avg-Pooling, DIN, SIMHard, SIMSoft, ETA, SDIM, SIMCluster, SIMCluster+, and TWIN, with all models using consistent user and item features. Evaluation metrics will be AUC and GAUC, with mean and standard deviation reported over five days. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of hierarchical clustering variants and cluster-aware attention, and online A/B tests will measure improvements in watch time and recommendation diversity across multiple app scenarios.
c5859754c1f6c099199d42b488415b04a7bfd527.novelty_claims: The proposed method enables modeling of user behavior sequences at the full life-cycle scale, far exceeding the length limitations of prior approaches. The hierarchical clustering technique adaptively compresses ultra-long sequences, reducing storage and computational costs by 90% while preserving user interest diversity. The cluster-aware target attention mechanism introduces a principled way to reweight attention based on cluster size, capturing comprehensive and multi-faceted user interests. The approach is validated at billion-user scale and demonstrates significant improvements in both offline metrics and online business outcomes, supporting its practical deployment in large-scale recommendation systems.

c58e1bba9ec91b908c57390230fc9432bf23796e.title: Projecting Assumptions: The Duality Between Sparse Autoencoders and Concept Geometry
c58e1bba9ec91b908c57390230fc9432bf23796e.research_question: How do the architectural assumptions of sparse autoencoders (SAEs) influence their ability to recover and represent the underlying concepts in neural network representations, particularly when these concepts exhibit heterogeneous intrinsic dimensionality and nonlinear separability?
c58e1bba9ec91b908c57390230fc9432bf23796e.hypothesis: Different SAE architectures impose implicit structural assumptions on the data, which in turn bias the types of concepts they can recover; explicitly incorporating data properties such as nonlinear separability and concept heterogeneity into SAE design will enable more faithful and comprehensive concept discovery.
c58e1bba9ec91b908c57390230fc9432bf23796e.proposed_method: A unified framework will be developed to analyze SAE architectures as solutions to a bilevel optimization problem, revealing the duality between encoder constraints and concept geometry in data. The investigation will systematically characterize the implicit assumptions of popular SAE variants (ReLU, TopK, JumpReLU) regarding concept separability and dimensionality. To address the limitations identified, a novel geometry-driven SAE, SpaDE (Sparsemax Distance Encoder), will be designed. SpaDE will employ a competitive projection nonlinearity onto the probability simplex, enabling adaptive sparsity and nonlinear separability by computing Euclidean distances to learned prototypes and applying the sparsemax function. The method will ensure that the encoder can flexibly match the true structure of concepts in the data, supporting both low- and high-dimensional, as well as nonlinearly separable, concepts.
c58e1bba9ec91b908c57390230fc9432bf23796e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a progression of datasets: (1) controlled synthetic datasets with Gaussian clusters to isolate nonlinear separability and heterogeneity, (2) semi-synthetic datasets using formal language model activations (e.g., English PCFG with part-of-speech concepts), and (3) large-scale, naturalistic datasets such as Imagenette with representations from DINOv2 vision models. Baseline comparisons will include ReLU, JumpReLU, and TopK SAE architectures. Evaluation metrics will include F1 scores for monosemanticity, mean squared error (MSE) for reconstruction quality, cosine similarity matrices for latent co-occurrence, and spectral clustering for concept delineation. Experiments will systematically vary sparsity levels and measure per-concept performance, with detailed analysis of receptive fields and latent specialization.
c58e1bba9ec91b908c57390230fc9432bf23796e.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretical framework establishing the duality between SAE architecture and concept geometry, demonstrating that no single SAE is universally optimal for concept discovery. It provides the first systematic empirical analysis of how implicit architectural assumptions limit concept recovery, particularly for heterogeneous and nonlinearly separable concepts. The SpaDE architecture is proposed as a novel SAE that explicitly incorporates both nonlinear separability and adaptive sparsity, enabling the discovery of previously hidden concepts and outperforming existing SAEs in structured concept recovery. The work challenges the prevailing notion of universal SAEs and advocates for data-aware, geometry-driven interpretability methods.

c5a9f7919ab213aa8ef1653e480ca0f7e385ac0e.title: Finite-Sample Convergence Bounds for Trust Region Policy Optimization in Mean-Field Games
c5a9f7919ab213aa8ef1653e480ca0f7e385ac0e.research_question: How can scalable and theoretically grounded algorithms be developed to compute approximate Nash equilibria in ergodic mean-field games with finite state-action spaces, and what are their finite-sample convergence properties?
c5a9f7919ab213aa8ef1653e480ca0f7e385ac0e.hypothesis: Trust-region-based policy optimization methods, when extended to the mean-field game framework and equipped with appropriate regularization and population update mechanisms, will yield efficient, stable, and provably convergent algorithms for finding approximate Nash equilibria, even in the presence of sampling noise and without full knowledge of environment dynamics.
c5a9f7919ab213aa8ef1653e480ca0f7e385ac0e.proposed_method: A novel algorithm, Mean-Field Trust Region Policy Optimization (MF-TRPO), is proposed to compute approximate Nash equilibria for ergodic mean-field games in finite state-action spaces. The method extends trust region policy optimization (TRPO) to the mean-field game setting by leveraging the stability and robustness of trust-region updates and incorporating entropy regularization for solution stability. Two variants are developed: Exact MF-TRPO, which assumes access to the model and performs deterministic policy and population updates, and Sample-Based MF-TRPO, which operates in a model-free setting using sampled trajectories and a restart distribution to estimate policy gradients and population distributions. The algorithms iteratively alternate between policy optimization (using trust-region updates with closed-form softmax solutions) and mean-field population updates, with theoretical guarantees on convergence and sample complexity under standard assumptions such as Lipschitz continuity, ergodicity, and monotonicity of the mean-field updates.
c5a9f7919ab213aa8ef1653e480ca0f7e385ac0e.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a grid-based crowd modeling environment, where agents navigate a 5x5 grid with obstacles and a designated point of interest, receiving rewards based on movement, crowding, and proximity to the target. The Sample-Based MF-TRPO algorithm is evaluated, with results averaged over multiple random seeds. The main evaluation metric is exploitability, measuring the potential improvement an agent could achieve by deviating unilaterally from the learned policy. The progression of the mean-field distribution is visualized over time to demonstrate learning dynamics. Baselines from the literature are referenced for comparison, and the experimental setup includes varying the entropy regularization parameter to assess its impact on convergence and stability.
c5a9f7919ab213aa8ef1653e480ca0f7e385ac0e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first trust-region-based algorithm for mean-field games with explicit finite-sample convergence guarantees. It extends TRPO to the mean-field setting, providing both exact and sample-based variants with rigorous theoretical analysis, including high-probability bounds and sample complexity scaling as O~(1/ε^6) for reaching ε-approximate Nash equilibria. The method relaxes restrictive assumptions from prior work, incorporates monotonicity for stabilizing population dynamics, and achieves improved convergence rates and sample efficiency. The sample-based variant is model-free and applicable to real-world settings, bridging reinforcement learning techniques with mean-field game optimization.

c5abe36e801ba0b53dab135af631c65f03ad00df.title: Momentum Provably Improves Error Feedback!
c5abe36e801ba0b53dab135af631c65f03ad00df.research_question: Can distributed stochastic optimization algorithms using contractive communication compression (such as Top-K) be designed to achieve efficient convergence without requiring large batch sizes or restrictive bounded gradient assumptions, and can their sample and communication complexity be improved under standard smoothness and bounded variance assumptions?
c5abe36e801ba0b53dab135af631c65f03ad00df.hypothesis: Incorporating Polyak's momentum into error feedback-based distributed stochastic optimization algorithms will provably improve their stability and sample complexity, enabling efficient convergence with small batch sizes and without requiring restrictive assumptions such as bounded gradients or gradient similarity.
c5abe36e801ba0b53dab135af631c65f03ad00df.proposed_method: A new distributed stochastic optimization algorithm, EF21-SGDM, is proposed, which enhances the EF21 error feedback mechanism by integrating Polyak's momentum at each client node. Each client maintains local state vectors for momentum and error feedback, updating them using stochastic gradients and contractive compression operators (e.g., Top-K). The method uses a Lyapunov-based analysis to ensure monotonic progress and stability, even with small batch sizes. Additionally, a double-momentum variant (EF21-SGD2M) is developed, where a second momentum estimator is maintained to further reduce variance and improve sample complexity. Both algorithms are designed to operate under standard smoothness and bounded variance assumptions, without requiring bounded gradient or gradient similarity conditions.
c5abe36e801ba0b53dab135af631c65f03ad00df.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets, including stochastic quadratic optimization and neural network training tasks. The proposed EF21-SGDM and EF21-SGD2M methods will be compared against baselines such as EF14-SGD, EF21-SGD, BEER, and other state-of-the-art distributed optimization algorithms using contractive compressors. Evaluation metrics will include convergence rate to stationary points (measured by expected gradient norm), sample complexity, and communication complexity (number of bits transmitted). Experiments will systematically vary batch sizes, number of clients, and compression parameters to assess stability, scalability, and efficiency. Additional ablation studies will investigate the impact of momentum and double-momentum components.
c5abe36e801ba0b53dab135af631c65f03ad00df.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to provably demonstrate that momentum can eliminate the need for large batch sizes in error feedback-based distributed optimization with contractive compressors, achieving stable convergence under standard smoothness and bounded variance assumptions. The method achieves improved sample and communication complexity compared to previous error feedback algorithms, without requiring restrictive bounded gradient or gradient similarity assumptions. The double-momentum variant further tightens sample complexity bounds in non-asymptotic regimes. Theoretical analysis introduces new Lyapunov function constructions and proof techniques that are of independent interest for nonconvex stochastic optimization with momentum.

c5d18dbb92d0cd5393baa1e69de33d6922ac3e57.title: RoCo: Dialectic Multi-Robot Collaboration with Large Language Models
c5d18dbb92d0cd5393baa1e69de33d6922ac3e57.research_question: How can large language models be leveraged to enable flexible, generalizable, and interpretable multi-robot collaboration for complex manipulation tasks, including both high-level coordination and low-level motion planning, without requiring task-specific engineering?
c5d18dbb92d0cd5393baa1e69de33d6922ac3e57.hypothesis: Equipping each robot with a large language model agent that engages in dialog-based communication, jointly reasons about task strategies, and incorporates environment feedback will enable effective multi-robot collaboration and motion planning across a diverse set of tasks, achieving high adaptability and generalization without task-specific training.
c5d18dbb92d0cd5393baa1e69de33d6922ac3e57.proposed_method: A unified framework is proposed in which each robot is represented by an LLM agent that participates in structured dialog to exchange information, reason about task strategies, and coordinate sub-task allocations. The dialog protocol ensures that agents share their observations, capabilities, and intentions, and collectively agree on sub-task plans, which may include 3D task-space waypoints. After a dialog round, the proposed sub-task plan undergoes a series of validations, including text parsing, task and agent constraint checks, inverse kinematics feasibility, and collision checking. If any validation fails, detailed feedback is provided to the agents, prompting iterative refinement of the plan. Once validated, the sub-task plan is translated into goal configurations for each robot, and a centralized RRT-based multi-arm motion planner computes joint-space trajectories, optionally leveraging LLM-generated waypoints to accelerate planning and reduce sample complexity.
c5d18dbb92d0cd5393baa1e69de33d6922ac3e57.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on RoCoBench, a newly introduced benchmark comprising six multi-robot tabletop manipulation tasks that vary in task decomposition (sequential vs. parallel), observation sharing (asymmetric vs. shared), and workspace overlap (low to high). The method is evaluated using GPT-4 as the LLM, and compared against an oracle central planner (CentralPlan) with full environment access, as well as ablations removing dialog history and environment feedback. Evaluation metrics include task success rate within a finite number of rounds, number of environment steps to completion, and number of re-plan attempts per round. Additional experiments assess the impact of LLM-proposed waypoints on planning efficiency, zero-shot adaptation to task variations, and real-world human-robot collaboration using a pre-trained object detector for perception.
c5d18dbb92d0cd5393baa1e69de33d6922ac3e57.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a dialectic, dialog-based multi-robot collaboration framework that leverages LLMs for both high-level task coordination and low-level motion planning, enabling flexible, interpretable, and generalizable multi-robot systems. The method demonstrates the use of LLMs for 3D spatial reasoning and waypoint generation, significantly reducing motion planning complexity. RoCoBench, a diverse benchmark for multi-robot manipulation, is introduced to systematically evaluate these capabilities. The framework supports zero-shot adaptation to new task semantics and human-in-the-loop collaboration, representing a significant departure from traditional task-specific multi-robot systems.

c5d82b27897633d6c3b2e452a0dc6c019d4a1565.title: Towards Principled Evaluations of Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretability and Control
c5d82b27897633d6c3b2e452a0dc6c019d4a1565.research_question: How can the evaluation of sparse autoencoders for interpretability and control in large language models be made more principled and objective, particularly in the absence of ground-truth features for realistic tasks?
c5d82b27897633d6c3b2e452a0dc6c019d4a1565.hypothesis: Supervised feature dictionaries constructed from task-relevant attributes can serve as an effective benchmark for evaluating the approximation, controllability, and interpretability of sparse autoencoders, and can reveal both strengths and limitations of unsupervised feature learning methods.
c5d82b27897633d6c3b2e452a0dc6c019d4a1565.proposed_method: A new evaluation framework will be developed for assessing sparse feature dictionaries in the context of specific language model tasks. The methodology begins by selecting task-relevant attributes that describe the prompts and computing high-quality supervised feature dictionaries using these attributes, typically by averaging activations corresponding to each attribute value. These supervised dictionaries are then used as a reference to evaluate unsupervised dictionaries (such as those learned by sparse autoencoders) along three axes: (1) sufficiency and necessity of dictionary reconstructions for the task, (2) sparse controllability of model behavior via feature editing, and (3) interpretability of features with respect to their causal role in the model's computation. The approach includes both interpretation-agnostic and interpretation-aware evaluations, and employs combinatorial optimization for sparse control interventions.
c5d82b27897633d6c3b2e452a0dc6c019d4a1565.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Indirect Object Identification (IOI) task using GPT-2 Small, with activations extracted from key components of the IOI circuit. Datasets will include both the IOI dataset (task-specific) and the OpenWebText corpus (full pretraining distribution). Baselines will consist of supervised feature dictionaries and mean ablation baselines. Evaluation metrics will include logit difference (measuring the model's preference for correct completions), accuracy of attribute editing, and F1 scores for feature interpretability. Experimental setups will compare supervised dictionaries, task-specific sparse autoencoders, and full-distribution sparse autoencoders across sufficiency/necessity, sparse controllability, and interpretability tests, including both quantitative and qualitative analyses of feature phenomena such as occlusion and over-splitting.
c5d82b27897633d6c3b2e452a0dc6c019d4a1565.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a principled, task-grounded methodology for evaluating sparse autoencoders by leveraging supervised feature dictionaries as a reference. This approach enables objective, interpretable, and causally meaningful assessments of feature quality in the absence of ground-truth, and is the first to demonstrate such disentanglement in a realistic LLM task. The framework also uncovers and contextualizes qualitative phenomena in sparse autoencoder training, such as feature occlusion and over-splitting, and provides tools for both interpretation-agnostic and interpretation-aware evaluation of feature dictionaries.

c5e9fd131cde68c218d0ea69cd617a67c7f35d42.title: ProlificDreamer: High-Fidelity and Diverse Text-to-3D Generation with Variational Score Distillation
c5e9fd131cde68c218d0ea69cd617a67c7f35d42.research_question: How can high-fidelity and diverse 3D content be automatically generated from textual descriptions using only pretrained text-to-image diffusion models, while overcoming issues of over-saturation, over-smoothing, and low diversity in existing methods?
c5e9fd131cde68c218d0ea69cd617a67c7f35d42.hypothesis: Modeling the 3D parameter as a random variable and optimizing a distribution over 3D scenes, rather than a single point estimate, will enable the generation of higher-fidelity, more diverse, and semantically accurate 3D representations from text prompts. Additionally, improvements in rendering resolution, time scheduling, and scene initialization will further enhance the quality and diversity of generated 3D content.
c5e9fd131cde68c218d0ea69cd617a67c7f35d42.proposed_method: A novel framework, Variational Score Distillation (VSD), is proposed to treat the 3D representation parameters as random variables, optimizing a distribution over possible 3D scenes conditioned on a text prompt. The method maintains a set of 3D parameter particles to represent this distribution and updates them using a gradient-based rule derived from the Wasserstein gradient flow, aligning the distribution of rendered images with that of a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model via KL divergence minimization. The score function for noisy rendered images is estimated using a low-rank adaptation (LoRA) of the pretrained diffusion model, enabling efficient and effective learning. The training alternates between updating the 3D particles and fine-tuning the score function, and incorporates improvements such as high-resolution rendering (up to 512x512), an annealed distillation time schedule, and a carefully designed scene initialization strategy to support complex scene generation.
c5e9fd131cde68c218d0ea69cd617a67c7f35d42.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the Stable Diffusion model as the base text-to-image diffusion model. The approach will be evaluated on both object-centric and complex scene generation tasks, using NeRF (Neural Radiance Fields) and mesh representations. Comparisons will be made against state-of-the-art baselines including DreamFusion, Magic3D, and Fantasia3D, with all baselines using Score Distillation Sampling (SDS). Evaluation metrics will include visual fidelity, diversity, and the ability to generate complex scenes, assessed through qualitative comparisons, user studies, and quantitative metrics where applicable. Ablation studies will be performed to isolate the effects of rendering resolution, time schedule, VSD versus SDS, and scene initialization. The number of particles in the VSD framework will be varied (typically 1-4) to assess diversity, and classifier-free guidance (CFG) weights will be systematically explored.
c5e9fd131cde68c218d0ea69cd617a67c7f35d42.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled variational inference framework for text-to-3D generation, generalizing and improving upon existing score distillation methods by optimizing a distribution over 3D scenes rather than a single representation. The method enables high-fidelity and diverse 3D generation at high rendering resolutions, supports complex multi-object scenes with 360-degree views, and achieves superior performance with standard classifier-free guidance weights. Additional innovations include a two-stage annealed time schedule for distillation, a new scene initialization strategy for complex scenes, and the use of LoRA for efficient score function estimation. The framework is demonstrated to outperform previous methods in both fidelity and diversity, and is the first to systematically address and explain the limitations of SDS in the context of text-to-3D generation.

c5ef0f8e8a4aac22d157865db0db19bc6c6ee704.title: Deep Linear Probe Generators for Weight Space Learning
c5ef0f8e8a4aac22d157865db0db19bc6c6ee704.research_question: How can information about neural networks, such as their training dataset or generalization error, be accurately and efficiently extracted from model weights, especially in the absence of access to the original data or extensive computational resources?
c5ef0f8e8a4aac22d157865db0db19bc6c6ee704.hypothesis: Probing methods, when enhanced with structured probe generation and appropriate inductive biases, can outperform existing mechanistic and graph-based approaches for weight space learning, providing more accurate predictions of model attributes while reducing overfitting and computational cost.
c5ef0f8e8a4aac22d157865db0db19bc6c6ee704.proposed_method: A novel framework, Deep Linear Probe Generators (ProbeGen), will be developed to improve probing-based weight space learning. ProbeGen factorizes each probe into a per-probe latent code and a shared deep linear generator network, which consists of stacked linear layers without non-linear activations. This design encourages sharing of information across probes and introduces an implicit regularization effect, reducing overfitting compared to traditional latent optimization of probes. For structured data modalities such as images, the generator can incorporate domain-specific inductive biases, such as convolutional layers, to further enhance probe quality. The model responses to these probes are then used to train a classifier (e.g., an MLP) to predict the desired attribute of the neural network.
c5ef0f8e8a4aac22d157865db0db19bc6c6ee704.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on established benchmarks for weight space learning, including MNIST and FMNIST implicit neural representation (INR) datasets for training data prediction, and CIFAR10-GS and CIFAR10-WildPark for generalization error prediction. A new large-scale Model Zoo of over 6,000 ResNet18 models trained on Tiny-Imagenet subsets will also be used to test scalability. ProbeGen will be compared against baselines such as StatNN, DWS, NFN, ScaleGMN, NeuralGraphs, and vanilla probing. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy for INR tasks and Kendall’s τ for generalization error prediction. Computational efficiency will be assessed in terms of floating point operations (FLOPs), and ablation studies will examine the effects of generator architecture, probe number, and inductive bias.
c5ef0f8e8a4aac22d157865db0db19bc6c6ee704.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a deep linear probe generator architecture that provides implicit regularization and enables structured, efficient probe learning. This approach significantly reduces overfitting compared to existing probing strategies and achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks, often with 30 to 1000 times fewer FLOPs than leading graph-based methods. The method also demonstrates scalability to large model populations and adaptability to different data modalities through the incorporation of domain-specific inductive biases.

c5f0a00e39b9b6bcbafa53f2560d057174ae3ca4.title: BundleSDF: Neural 6-DoF Tracking and 3D Reconstruction of Unknown Objects
c5f0a00e39b9b6bcbafa53f2560d057174ae3ca4.research_question: How can 6-DoF pose tracking and 3D reconstruction of unknown, rigid objects be achieved from monocular RGBD video sequences, without prior knowledge of the object or interaction agent, and in the presence of challenging conditions such as occlusion, lack of texture, and dynamic interactions?
c5f0a00e39b9b6bcbafa53f2560d057174ae3ca4.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a co-designed framework combining online pose graph optimization with a neural object field representation, supported by a dynamic memory pool and hybrid SDF modeling, will enable robust, causal 6-DoF tracking and high-quality 3D reconstruction of unknown objects from monocular RGBD video, even under severe occlusions, lack of texture, and varied interaction agents.
c5f0a00e39b9b6bcbafa53f2560d057174ae3ca4.proposed_method: The proposed method develops a near real-time system that jointly performs 6-DoF pose tracking and 3D reconstruction of unknown rigid objects from monocular RGBD video. The approach requires only a 2D object mask in the first frame and no prior knowledge of the object or interaction agent. A neural implicit object field (Neural Object Field) is learned per video, modeling both geometry (as a signed distance field) and appearance, while a concurrent online pose graph optimization thread refines object poses across selected memory frames. A dynamic memory pool is maintained to store the most informative historical frames, facilitating multi-view consistency and reducing tracking drift. Hybrid SDF modeling is introduced to handle uncertain free space due to noisy segmentation and occlusions, and efficient hierarchical ray sampling with an octree structure accelerates neural field training and rendering. The system operates causally, updating both the neural object field and pose estimates online as new frames are processed.
c5f0a00e39b9b6bcbafa53f2560d057174ae3ca4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three public benchmarks: HO3D (human hand-object interaction), YCBInEOAT (robotic arm-object interaction), and BEHAVE (human body-object interaction), covering a wide range of dynamic and challenging scenarios. The evaluation will use monocular RGBD video sequences, with only the first frame's object mask provided. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art methods such as DROID-SLAM, NICE-SLAM, KinectFusion, BundleTrack, SDF-2-SDF, and others, with appropriate adaptations to ensure fairness (e.g., using the same segmentation masks). Performance will be measured using 6-DoF pose estimation metrics (ADD, ADD-S AUC) and 3D reconstruction quality (chamfer distance between reconstructed and ground-truth meshes). The experimental setup will test robustness to occlusion, lack of texture, and long-term tracking drift, with no re-initialization allowed after tracking failures.
c5f0a00e39b9b6bcbafa53f2560d057174ae3ca4.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a novel co-design of concurrent 6-DoF tracking and neural 3D reconstruction processes that operate online and in near real-time. Key innovations include a hybrid SDF representation for handling uncertain free space, a dynamic memory pool for robust multi-view pose optimization, and a neural object field learned per video without pre-training or object priors. The method operates causally and generalizes to arbitrary rigid objects and interaction agents, handling severe occlusions, specular highlights, and untextured surfaces. Experimental results are expected to demonstrate significant improvements over existing methods in both pose tracking accuracy and 3D reconstruction quality across diverse and challenging datasets.

c60bbdfd53783008e864344161ce79f1a780fe71.title: Does Generation Require Memorization? Creative Diffusion Models using Ambient Diffusion
c60bbdfd53783008e864344161ce79f1a780fe71.research_question: Can diffusion models be trained to achieve high-quality and creative image generation while significantly reducing memorization of the training set, particularly in low-data regimes and across both unconditional and text-conditional settings?
c60bbdfd53783008e864344161ce79f1a780fe71.hypothesis: It is possible to train diffusion models that maintain strong generation fidelity and creativity while reducing memorization by leveraging a principled training procedure that focuses on high-noise regimes, thus mitigating information leakage from the training set.
c60bbdfd53783008e864344161ce79f1a780fe71.proposed_method: A novel training framework is introduced that splits the diffusion process into two regimes based on a noise threshold parameter t_n. For noise levels t ≤ t_n, the standard denoising score matching objective is used, while for t > t_n, the model is trained exclusively on noisy versions of the training data using an Ambient Score Matching loss. This approach involves constructing a noisy dataset S_{t_n} by corrupting each training image at noise level t_n, and then alternating between clean and noisy samples during training. The method ensures that, in the high-noise regime, the model learns to denoise without direct exposure to the original data, thereby reducing the risk of memorization. Theoretical analysis is provided to demonstrate that information leakage from the training set is significantly reduced in the high-noise regime, and the method is compatible with both unconditional and text-conditional diffusion models.
c60bbdfd53783008e864344161ce79f1a780fe71.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of datasets, including FFHQ with both limited (e.g., 300 images) and larger training sets. Both unconditional and text-conditional diffusion models will be evaluated. Baselines will include standard DDPM training and recent memorization-reduction techniques such as sampling adaptations and data corruption methods. Evaluation metrics will include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for image quality and explicit memorization metrics, such as the percentage of generated images that are duplicates of the training set. The experimental setup will systematically vary the noise threshold parameter t_n to analyze the trade-off between image quality and memorization, and qualitative results will be reported for both unconditional and text-conditional prompts.
c60bbdfd53783008e864344161ce79f1a780fe71.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a principled framework for reducing memorization in diffusion models by leveraging high-noise training regimes and Ambient Score Matching, which has not been previously applied in this context. The approach is theoretically grounded, providing new insights into the relationship between noise scale, memorization, and information leakage. The method achieves a favorable trade-off between fidelity and memorization, outperforming existing baselines in both image quality and reduction of memorization, especially in low-data settings. Additionally, the framework is general and can be combined with other anti-memorization techniques, further enhancing its practical utility.

c62831f819d0e93ffb13804158af1d0148d706ee.title: Elucidating the Exposure Bias in Diffusion Models
c62831f819d0e93ffb13804158af1d0148d706ee.research_question: What are the underlying causes and effects of exposure bias in diffusion models, how can this bias be quantitatively measured, and can a practical, training-free method be developed to mitigate its impact on generative performance?
c62831f819d0e93ffb13804158af1d0148d706ee.hypothesis: Exposure bias in diffusion models arises from prediction errors that cause a mismatch between training and sampling distributions, leading to error accumulation and degraded sample quality. It is hypothesized that a training-free adjustment of the sampling process can reduce exposure bias and improve generative performance.
c62831f819d0e93ffb13804158af1d0148d706ee.proposed_method: A systematic analytical investigation will be conducted to model the sampling distribution in diffusion models, explicitly incorporating prediction errors at each sampling step. A novel metric, based on the variance difference between training and sampling distributions, will be introduced to quantify exposure bias throughout the sampling chain. Building on this analysis, a training-free, plug-in method called Epsilon Scaling will be developed, which rescales the network's output during sampling to move the sampling trajectory closer to the vector field learned during training. The scaling schedule will be determined either by simulation or by a simple parameter search, and the method will be designed for compatibility with a wide range of diffusion model architectures and samplers.
c62831f819d0e93ffb13804158af1d0148d706ee.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple diffusion model frameworks, including ADM, DDIM, EDM, LDM, DiT, and PFGM++, covering both deterministic and stochastic sampling, as well as conditional and unconditional generation tasks. Standard image generation benchmarks such as CIFAR-10, LSUN Tower, FFHQ, CelebA-HQ, and ImageNet (at various resolutions) will be used. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art samplers and previously proposed methods for mitigating exposure bias. Evaluation metrics will primarily include Frechet Inception Distance (FID), as well as precision and recall, with results reported over 50,000 generated samples and full training sets as reference. The impact of Epsilon Scaling on exposure bias will be assessed using the proposed variance-based metric, and ablation studies will explore the effect of different scaling schedules.
c62831f819d0e93ffb13804158af1d0148d706ee.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a rigorous analytical framework for understanding exposure bias in diffusion models, including the derivation of a new metric to quantify this bias. The Epsilon Scaling method offers a simple, training-free, and plug-in solution that is broadly applicable across diffusion architectures and samplers. The approach is claimed to significantly improve generative sample quality, as measured by FID, without retraining or additional computational overhead, and to provide new insights into the relationship between prediction error, sampling drift, and exposure bias.

c6478decdfff11ccbd085967c2f83aea11927a46.title: Preference Transformer: Modeling Human Preferences using Transformers for RL
c6478decdfff11ccbd085967c2f83aea11927a46.research_question: How can human preferences be effectively modeled to improve reward learning and policy optimization in reinforcement learning, particularly in settings where reward functions are difficult to specify and human feedback is limited?
c6478decdfff11ccbd085967c2f83aea11927a46.hypothesis: Modeling human preferences using a transformer-based architecture that captures non-Markovian reward dependencies and assigns importance weights to trajectory events will enable more efficient and accurate reward learning from human feedback, resulting in improved agent performance on complex control and manipulation tasks.
c6478decdfff11ccbd085967c2f83aea11927a46.proposed_method: A novel preference modeling framework is proposed in which the probability of preferring a trajectory segment is determined by a weighted sum of non-Markovian rewards, rather than the conventional Markovian sum with equal weights. The core of the approach is the Preference Transformer, a neural architecture that stacks causal (unidirectional) and bidirectional self-attention layers to process trajectory segments. The model first encodes state-action sequences using a causal transformer to produce context-aware embeddings, then applies a preference attention layer that computes both non-Markovian rewards and their associated importance weights via bidirectional self-attention. The preference predictor aggregates these outputs to model the weighted sum of rewards, allowing for credit assignment to critical events within trajectories. Training is performed by minimizing cross-entropy loss between the model's preference predictions and actual human preference labels.
c6478decdfff11ccbd085967c2f83aea11927a46.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a range of complex control and manipulation tasks using offline RL benchmarks, specifically D4RL (including AntMaze and Gym-Mujoco locomotion tasks) and Robomimic (robotic manipulation tasks). Human preference data is collected by querying pairs of trajectory segments from these datasets and recording expert feedback. The learned reward functions are used to train RL agents with Implicit Q-Learning (IQL), and performance is evaluated using expert-normalized scores (D4RL) and success rates (Robomimic). Baselines include MLP-based Markovian reward models and LSTM-based non-Markovian reward models, both trained with the same human preference data. Additional experiments compare performance with synthetic (scripted) preference teachers and analyze the alignment of learned rewards and importance weights with human intent. Human evaluations are conducted to assess the qualitative alignment of agent behaviors with human preferences.
c6478decdfff11ccbd085967c2f83aea11927a46.novelty_claims: The proposed framework generalizes preference modeling by introducing a weighted sum of non-Markovian rewards, enabling the capture of temporal dependencies and credit assignment within trajectories. The Preference Transformer architecture incorporates a novel preference attention layer for learning both non-Markovian rewards and their importance weights from human feedback. This approach demonstrates superior performance over existing Markovian and non-Markovian baselines, particularly in tasks requiring long-term context understanding and critical event detection. The method is shown to induce well-aligned reward functions and enables agents to learn complex, novel behaviors that are difficult to specify with traditional reward engineering.

c64a99ec780d5e1c6ba242a82e72e96eb0c3ef8a.title: An Information-Theoretic Perspective on Intrinsic Motivation in Reinforcement Learning: A Survey
c64a99ec780d5e1c6ba242a82e72e96eb0c3ef8a.research_question: How can intrinsic motivation, grounded in information-theoretic principles, be systematically leveraged to address key challenges in deep reinforcement learning, such as sparse reward exploration and skill abstraction?
c64a99ec780d5e1c6ba242a82e72e96eb0c3ef8a.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that intrinsic motivation mechanisms, formalized through information-theoretic objectives such as surprise, novelty, and skill learning, can significantly enhance exploration efficiency and skill transfer in deep reinforcement learning environments, particularly under sparse reward conditions.
c64a99ec780d5e1c6ba242a82e72e96eb0c3ef8a.proposed_method: A comprehensive framework will be developed that unifies intrinsic motivation mechanisms in reinforcement learning under an information-theoretic taxonomy. The approach will formalize and computationally implement intrinsic rewards based on measures such as entropy, mutual information, and model uncertainty, corresponding to the notions of surprise, novelty, and skill learning. The methodology will include the integration of intrinsic and extrinsic rewards via weighted combinations, hierarchical reinforcement learning architectures for temporal abstraction, and goal-parameterized policies to facilitate multi-task and skill-based learning. Efficient learning techniques such as goal relabeling and hindsight experience replay will be incorporated to improve sample efficiency and generalization across tasks.
c64a99ec780d5e1c6ba242a82e72e96eb0c3ef8a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard deep reinforcement learning benchmarks, including environments with sparse rewards such as Montezuma's Revenge and continuous control tasks in simulators like MuJoCo. The proposed methods will be compared against established baselines such as Deep Q-Networks (DQN), hierarchical RL methods, and exploration strategies like epsilon-greedy and parameter-space noise. Evaluation metrics will include cumulative reward, exploration coverage, skill transferability, and sample efficiency. Ablation studies will be performed to isolate the contributions of different intrinsic motivation objectives and their combinations.
c64a99ec780d5e1c6ba242a82e72e96eb0c3ef8a.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified, information-theoretic taxonomy for intrinsic motivation in reinforcement learning, systematically categorizing and formalizing surprise, novelty, and skill learning as computational objectives. The framework enables a principled integration of intrinsic rewards into deep RL algorithms, supports hierarchical skill abstraction, and provides generalizable mechanisms for exploration in sparse-reward settings. The approach aims to bridge gaps between psychological theory, information theory, and practical RL algorithm design, offering new insights and tools for robust, transferable skill acquisition and efficient exploration.

c64e878be5705fafb200c6bfa0c8f1764c49608f.title: On Over-Squashing in Message Passing Neural Networks: The Impact of Width, Depth, and Topology
c64e878be5705fafb200c6bfa0c8f1764c49608f.research_question: What are the fundamental causes of over-squashing in Message Passing Neural Networks (MPNNs), and how do the architectural parameters (width, depth) and graph topology influence this phenomenon? Can a unified theoretical framework be developed to explain and predict over-squashing, and how do existing mitigation strategies, such as graph rewiring, relate to these factors?
c64e878be5705fafb200c6bfa0c8f1764c49608f.hypothesis: Over-squashing in MPNNs is primarily determined by the graph topology, specifically by commute and access times between nodes, and cannot be effectively mitigated by simply increasing network width or depth. Spatial and spectral graph rewiring approaches alleviate over-squashing by reducing these topological obstructions.
c64e878be5705fafb200c6bfa0c8f1764c49608f.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical analysis will be conducted to characterize over-squashing in MPNNs as a function of network width, depth, and graph topology. Sensitivity bounds will be derived for the propagation of information in MPNNs, relating the Jacobian of node features to architectural parameters and topological quantities such as commute and access times. The analysis will be extended to both shallow and deep regimes, identifying the transition from over-squashing to vanishing gradients as depth increases. Theoretical results will be further connected to spectral properties of the graph, such as the Cheeger constant and effective resistance, providing a unified explanation for the efficacy of spatial and spectral rewiring methods. Empirical validation will be performed using synthetic tasks designed to stress long-range dependencies, confirming theoretical predictions.
c64e878be5705fafb200c6bfa0c8f1764c49608f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic graph transfer tasks, where source and target nodes are placed at varying distances on different graph topologies (e.g., CrossedRing, Ring, CliquePath). Models such as GCN, GIN, SAGE, and GAT will be evaluated by varying hidden dimension (width) and number of layers (depth), with performance measured as the ability to transfer information from source to target. The impact of graph rewiring (both spatial and spectral) will be assessed by comparing performance before and after rewiring, using metrics such as accuracy and sensitivity of node features. Evaluation will focus on how performance degrades with distance and how it correlates with topological metrics like commute time and effective resistance. Theoretical predictions will be validated by observing the onset of over-squashing and vanishing gradients in relation to model and graph parameters.
c64e878be5705fafb200c6bfa0c8f1764c49608f.novelty_claims: The proposed research provides the first unified theoretical framework that rigorously connects over-squashing in MPNNs to graph-theoretic quantities such as commute time, access time, and the Cheeger constant. It analytically demonstrates the limitations of width and depth in mitigating over-squashing and characterizes the transition to vanishing gradients. The framework explains why both spatial and spectral graph rewiring methods are effective, offering precise conditions under which they alleviate over-squashing. The work also generalizes prior analyses to higher-dimensional node features, arbitrary depth, and a broader class of MPNN architectures, and introduces new sensitivity-based metrics for quantifying information propagation in graph neural networks.

c655668193bb8b067fb539ae6d5760f8cff6e056.title: Systematic Outliers in Large Language Models
c655668193bb8b067fb539ae6d5760f8cff6e056.research_question: What are the underlying mechanisms, distributions, and functional roles of systematic outliers in large language models, and how can understanding these phenomena inform improvements in model training, convergence, and compression?
c655668193bb8b067fb539ae6d5760f8cff6e056.hypothesis: Systematic outliers in large language models emerge as a result of the self-attention mechanism's softmax operation and function as implicit, context-aware scaling factors within the attention mechanism. Explicitly introducing context-aware scaling factors can eliminate these outliers, thereby accelerating convergence and improving model compression without degrading performance.
c655668193bb8b067fb539ae6d5760f8cff6e056.proposed_method: A systematic framework will be developed to define, categorize, and analyze three types of outliers in large language models: activation outliers, weight outliers, and attention outliers. The methodology involves mathematical formalization of outlier detection based on deviations from mean values, followed by empirical analysis of their distributions across layers, feature dimensions, and token positions in various Transformer-based LLMs. The interconnections and lifecycle of outliers will be investigated through correlation studies and visualization of propagation paths from weights to activations to attention scores. To test functional hypotheses, several variants of the attention mechanism will be implemented, including explicit fixed and context-aware biases and scaling factors, to isolate the effects of each on outlier formation. Theoretical derivations will be provided to link the emergence of outliers to architectural constraints, particularly the softmax normalization in attention.
c655668193bb8b067fb539ae6d5760f8cff6e056.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on models such as LLaMA2-7B and GPT-2, covering both pretrained and fine-tuned settings. Outlier distributions will be analyzed layer-wise, across feature and sequence dimensions, and in relation to specific tokens (e.g., start and weak semantic tokens). Multiple attention mechanism variants will be trained and evaluated, including default attention, explicit fixed/context-aware bias, attention bias, and explicit context-aware scaling factors. Evaluation will include the presence and magnitude of outliers, convergence speed, and robustness to model compression techniques such as quantization (e.g., FP16, AbsMaxW8) and pruning (e.g., 50% sparsity). Metrics such as perplexity (PPL) on datasets like WikiText2 and training/validation loss curves will be used to compare performance and efficiency across variants.
c655668193bb8b067fb539ae6d5760f8cff6e056.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a unified and systematic categorization of outliers in large language models, revealing their interconnectedness and lifecycle across model components. It hypothesizes and empirically validates that systematic outliers are a direct consequence of the softmax operation in self-attention and function as implicit, context-aware scaling factors. The research claims that explicitly introducing context-aware scaling factors into the attention mechanism can eliminate outliers, leading to faster convergence and significantly improved robustness to compression, with negligible parameter overhead. These findings offer new theoretical insights into the internal dynamics of Transformer-based LLMs and practical strategies for optimizing model efficiency and stability.

c65a64ea1be8dd654e2685f9bfea4c5118a98804.title: Evaluating Instruction-Tuned Large Language Models on Code Comprehension and Generation
c65a64ea1be8dd654e2685f9bfea4c5118a98804.research_question: How do recent open-source instruction-tuned large language models (LLMs) perform on a diverse set of code comprehension and generation tasks across different evaluation settings (zero-shot, few-shot, and fine-tuning), and what are the practical implications regarding their performance, cost, and usage strategies?
c65a64ea1be8dd654e2685f9bfea4c5118a98804.hypothesis: Instruction-tuned LLMs exhibit strong generalization and in-context learning capabilities on code-related tasks, outperforming both small task-specific models and similar-sized models without instruction tuning, and their performance can be further enhanced through fine-tuning and optimal prompt strategies.
c65a64ea1be8dd654e2685f9bfea4c5118a98804.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation framework will be developed to assess the capabilities of 10 recent open-source instruction-tuned LLMs on four representative code comprehension and generation tasks: defect detection, clone detection, assertion generation, and code summarization. The evaluation will be conducted in three settings: zero-shot (direct prompt-based inference), few-shot (with demonstration examples and various shot-selection strategies, including BM25-based retrieval), and fine-tuning (using parameter-efficient methods such as LoRA). The framework will include detailed prompt engineering tailored to each model and task, and will compare instruction-tuned LLMs against both small state-of-the-art (SOTA) models and large models without instruction tuning. Technical implementation will ensure reproducibility by using open-source models, standardized datasets, and consistent hyperparameters.
c65a64ea1be8dd654e2685f9bfea4c5118a98804.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize widely-adopted datasets for each task: Devign for defect detection, BigCloneBench for clone detection, ATLAS for assertion generation, and CodeSearchNet for code summarization. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy for defect detection, F1 score for clone detection, exact match for assertion generation, and a preference rate judged by ChatGPT for code summarization. Baselines will consist of four small SOTA models (CodeGPT-adapted, CoText, PLBART, CodeT5) and one large non-instructed model (CodeGen-6B). Each LLM will be assessed in zero-shot, few-shot (with fixed, random, and BM25-based shot selection), and fine-tuned settings. Resource usage (GPU hours, memory, and inference time) will also be recorded. Statistical significance of shot selection strategies will be tested using paired t-tests.
c65a64ea1be8dd654e2685f9bfea4c5118a98804.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first large-scale, systematic evaluation of open-source instruction-tuned LLMs on a broad spectrum of code comprehension and generation tasks, covering multiple model architectures, instruction domains, and evaluation settings. The study will provide new insights into the generalization, in-context learning, and fine-tuning capabilities of instruction-tuned LLMs in software engineering, and will empirically identify optimal strategies for prompt design and shot selection. Additionally, the work will offer practical guidance on the trade-offs between model performance, resource consumption, and cost, thereby informing both researchers and practitioners in the field.

c65c4b68ac153176354a4c33c37f0ba1d86772c0.title: DiGress: Discrete Denoising diffusion for graph generation
c65c4b68ac153176354a4c33c37f0ba1d86772c0.research_question: How can discrete denoising diffusion models be leveraged to generate graphs with categorical node and edge attributes, while preserving structural properties and scaling to large and diverse graph datasets?
c65c4b68ac153176354a4c33c37f0ba1d86772c0.hypothesis: Utilizing a discrete Markovian diffusion process that operates directly on graph node and edge categories, combined with a permutation-equivariant graph transformer denoising network, will enable the generation of realistic, diverse, and valid graphs that better preserve structural properties compared to continuous diffusion approaches. Further, incorporating marginal-preserving noise models and auxiliary structural features will improve sample quality and scalability.
