c65c4b68ac153176354a4c33c37f0ba1d86772c0.proposed_method: A novel discrete denoising diffusion model, DiGress, will be developed for graph generation. The approach will define a Markov noise process that progressively corrupts graphs by independently adding/removing edges and altering node or edge categories, using transition matrices tailored to preserve the marginal distributions of node and edge types. A permutation-equivariant graph transformer network will be trained to invert this process, predicting the clean graph from noisy inputs via node and edge classification tasks. The architecture will be augmented with auxiliary structural and spectral features computed from noisy graphs at each diffusion step, enhancing the network's representational power. Additionally, a discrete guidance procedure will be introduced to enable conditional generation on graph-level properties, using a regressor to steer the denoising process toward desired targets.
c65c4b68ac153176354a4c33c37f0ba1d86772c0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both molecular and non-molecular graph generation benchmarks, including datasets such as QM9, MOSES, GuacaMol, stochastic block models, and planar graphs. The method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines, including Set2GraphVAE, SPECTRE, GraphNVP, GDSS, GraphRNN, GRAN, JT-VAE, NAGVAE, and GraphINVENT. Evaluation metrics will include validity, uniqueness, novelty, negative log-likelihood, and graph property statistics (e.g., degree, clustering, orbit counts), as well as conditional generation accuracy for graph-level properties. The setup will involve ablation studies on noise models and feature augmentations, and scalability will be assessed on large datasets with over a million molecules.
c65c4b68ac153176354a4c33c37f0ba1d86772c0.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first discrete denoising diffusion model for attributed graph generation, operating directly on categorical node and edge types. It preserves graph sparsity and structural properties throughout the diffusion process, overcoming limitations of continuous noise models. The approach incorporates a marginal-preserving noise model and auxiliary graph-theoretic features, enabling improved sample quality and scalability. A novel discrete guidance scheme for conditional graph generation is also developed. The method achieves state-of-the-art results on challenging graph generation tasks and is the first one-shot model to scale to large molecular datasets without relying on molecule-specific representations.

c689d1f3ae2447fd5b2f108b5b4436276e4d3761.title: LayoutLMv3: Pre-training for Document AI with Unified Text and Image Masking
c689d1f3ae2447fd5b2f108b5b4436276e4d3761.research_question: How can a unified pre-training framework be developed to effectively learn multimodal representations for Document AI tasks, leveraging both text and image modalities for improved performance on both text-centric and image-centric document understanding tasks?
c689d1f3ae2447fd5b2f108b5b4436276e4d3761.hypothesis: A unified multimodal Transformer model, pre-trained with integrated text and image masking objectives along with a cross-modal alignment objective, will yield superior and more generalizable representations for Document AI tasks compared to models with separate or non-unified pre-training objectives.
c689d1f3ae2447fd5b2f108b5b4436276e4d3761.proposed_method: A new multimodal Transformer architecture will be designed to jointly encode text and image information from document images. The model will accept as input a concatenation of word embeddings (augmented with 1D and 2D positional/layout embeddings) and linear-projected image patch embeddings, without relying on CNN-based feature extractors. Pre-training will employ three objectives: (1) Masked Language Modeling (MLM) for reconstructing masked text tokens, (2) Masked Image Modeling (MIM) for reconstructing discrete image patch tokens derived from a visual tokenizer, and (3) a Word-Patch Alignment (WPA) objective that predicts whether a text token and its corresponding image patch are jointly masked, thus facilitating fine-grained cross-modal alignment. The model will be trained on large-scale document image datasets using self-supervised learning, with all objectives optimized jointly.
c689d1f3ae2447fd5b2f108b5b4436276e4d3761.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several public benchmarks spanning both text-centric and image-centric Document AI tasks. Datasets will include FUNSD (form understanding), CORD (receipt understanding), DocVQA (document visual question answering), RVL-CDIP (document image classification), and PubLayNet (document layout analysis). Baseline comparisons will include text-only models (BERT, RoBERTa), text+layout models (LayoutLM, StructuralLM), and multimodal models using CNN-based image embeddings (LayoutLMv2, DocFormer, UDoc, TILT). Evaluation metrics will include F1 score for entity extraction, accuracy for classification, ANLS for question answering, and mean average precision (mAP) for layout analysis. The model will be pre-trained on the IIT-CDIP dataset (11 million document images) and fine-tuned on each downstream task with task-specific heads and hyperparameters. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of each pre-training objective and the choice of image embedding.
c689d1f3ae2447fd5b2f108b5b4436276e4d3761.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first multimodal Document AI pre-training framework that eliminates the need for CNN or region-based visual feature extractors, using simple linear patch embeddings for images. It unifies text and image pre-training objectives (MLM and MIM) and introduces a novel Word-Patch Alignment objective for explicit cross-modal alignment. The framework is general-purpose, supporting both text-centric and image-centric tasks, and demonstrates state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks with improved parameter efficiency and architectural simplicity.

c68cc84ec7808d7bbd5686a6bd1393752a9d8e8d.title: Agent Workflow Memory
c68cc84ec7808d7bbd5686a6bd1393752a9d8e8d.research_question: How can language model-based agents be enabled to effectively solve long-horizon, complex web navigation tasks by learning and reusing abstract, generalizable task workflows from past experiences, in both online and offline scenarios?
c68cc84ec7808d7bbd5686a6bd1393752a9d8e8d.hypothesis: Equipping language model-based agents with a workflow memory that induces, stores, and reuses abstract, reusable task workflows from prior experiences will significantly improve their performance, efficiency, and generalization on complex, long-horizon web navigation tasks compared to agents relying solely on fixed examples or in-context learning.
c68cc84ec7808d7bbd5686a6bd1393752a9d8e8d.proposed_method: A novel Agent Workflow Memory (AWM) framework is proposed, which induces reusable task workflows from agent experiences and integrates them into the agent's memory to guide future actions. Workflows are represented as a combination of a high-level natural language description and a sequence of steps, each including the environment state, reasoning, and executable actions. Workflow induction is performed using a language model-based module that abstracts common sub-routines from one or more input experiences, replacing example-specific contexts with generalized placeholders to enhance reusability. The framework supports both offline induction from annotated or synthesized examples and online, supervision-free induction from self-generated successful trajectories, with workflows continuously integrated into agent memory as new tasks are solved. The agent utilizes these workflows as auxiliary memory during inference, and an optional extension allows workflows to be added as high-level actions in the agent's action space.
c68cc84ec7808d7bbd5686a6bd1393752a9d8e8d.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on two major web navigation benchmarks: WebArena (812 tasks across five websites and four domains) and Mind2Web (over 1000 tasks from 200+ domains). In WebArena, only test examples are available, so AWM is evaluated in the online setting, using GPT-4 for both workflow induction and agent action generation, and compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as BrowserGym and SteP (which uses human-written workflows). In Mind2Web, both offline (using training data for workflow induction) and online (inducing workflows from test queries) settings are explored, with comparisons to MindAct and Synapse baselines. Evaluation metrics include task success rate, step-wise success rate, element accuracy, action accuracy, and average number of steps per task. Additional experiments assess generalization to cross-task, cross-website, and cross-domain splits, as well as ablations on workflow representation and utilization.
c68cc84ec7808d7bbd5686a6bd1393752a9d8e8d.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a general and flexible workflow memory mechanism that enables agents to induce and reuse abstract, reusable workflows from past experiences, supporting both offline and online learning scenarios. Unlike prior approaches that rely on fixed examples or human-written workflows, this framework abstracts workflows at the sub-routine level and integrates them into agent memory, allowing for continual adaptation and efficient learning from small amounts of data. The method demonstrates substantial improvements in task success and efficiency, robust generalization across tasks, websites, and domains, and operates effectively even when no annotated examples are available. Additional innovations include the exploration of workflow representation formats and the extension of workflows as callable high-level actions within the agent's action space.

c695c4e68561347564ea0daa50dc339dff73d8c5.title: Ghost in the Minecraft: Generally Capable Agents for Open-World Environments via Large Language Models with Text-based Knowledge and Memory
c695c4e68561347564ea0daa50dc339dff73d8c5.research_question: How can generally capable agents be developed to efficiently and robustly solve a wide range of long-horizon, open-world tasks in complex environments such as Minecraft, surpassing the limitations of traditional reinforcement learning approaches?
c695c4e68561347564ea0daa50dc339dff73d8c5.hypothesis: Integrating large language models with hierarchical goal decomposition, text-based knowledge, and memory will enable agents to achieve superior generalization, efficiency, and robustness in open-world environments compared to reinforcement learning-based controllers.
c695c4e68561347564ea0daa50dc339dff73d8c5.proposed_method: A novel agent framework will be developed that leverages large language models (LLMs) for hierarchical goal decomposition, planning, and interaction within the Minecraft environment. The architecture consists of three main components: an LLM Decomposer that recursively breaks down high-level goals into sub-goals using structured formats and external text-based knowledge; an LLM Planner that generates sequences of structured, semantically meaningful actions for each sub-goal, incorporates feedback from the environment, and maintains a text-based memory of successful action plans for future reference; and an LLM Interface that implements these structured actions as keyboard and mouse operations in the Minecraft environment, providing feedback on execution success or failure. The system utilizes a comprehensive knowledge base extracted from the Minecraft Wiki and crafting/smelting recipes, and employs memory mechanisms to summarize and retrieve effective strategies for recurring tasks.
c695c4e68561347564ea0daa50dc339dff73d8c5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the full set of 262 item-collection tasks in the Minecraft Overworld, excluding items only obtainable via trading, treasure chests, or special map structures. The proposed agent will be evaluated on 'Coverage of the Overworld Technology Tree' and 'Success Rate' metrics, comparing its performance to state-of-the-art baselines such as VPT, DreamerV3, and DEPS. The ObtainDiamond task will serve as a key benchmark for direct comparison, with strict time and step limits for fair evaluation. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of goal decomposition, feedback, external knowledge, and memory components. The experimental setup will utilize the MineDojo environment, and the agent will be trained and executed on a single CPU node with 32 CPU cores, without GPU requirements.
c695c4e68561347564ea0daa50dc339dff73d8c5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first agent capable of unlocking the entire Minecraft Overworld technology tree, demonstrating broad generalization and open-world competence. The framework departs from traditional RL-based methods by employing LLMs for hierarchical planning, structured action abstraction, and explicit text-based knowledge and memory, resulting in significantly higher success rates and learning efficiency. The method achieves a +47.5% improvement in success rate on the ObtainDiamond task compared to prior work, and demonstrates robust performance across all item-collection tasks. The approach does not require GPU resources for training, marking a substantial advance in computational efficiency and scalability for generally capable agents in open-world environments.

c6ae2bb8c912bb757acedb9b72ab988800368b6c.title: Chebyshev Polynomial-Based Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks: An Efficient Architecture for Nonlinear Function Approximation
c6ae2bb8c912bb757acedb9b72ab988800368b6c.research_question: How can neural network architectures be improved to achieve more efficient, accurate, and interpretable nonlinear function approximation, particularly for high-dimensional and complex functions?
c6ae2bb8c912bb757acedb9b72ab988800368b6c.hypothesis: Incorporating learnable activation functions parametrized by Chebyshev polynomials on the edges of neural network architectures, inspired by the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem, will result in improved parameter efficiency, flexibility, and interpretability for nonlinear function approximation tasks compared to traditional Multi-Layer Perceptrons.
c6ae2bb8c912bb757acedb9b72ab988800368b6c.proposed_method: A novel neural network architecture, termed the Chebyshev Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (Chebyshev KAN), will be developed. This architecture will represent each edge in the network with a learnable univariate function parameterized as a Chebyshev polynomial of a specified degree, rather than using fixed activation functions at the nodes. Input data will be normalized and expanded into Chebyshev polynomial bases, and learnable coefficients will be associated with each basis function. The network output will be computed by an Einstein summation operation that combines the polynomial bases with the learned coefficients, enabling dynamic, data-adaptive nonlinear transformations. The architecture will support both first and second kind Chebyshev polynomials, and allow for systematic exploration of polynomial degree, initialization methods, and normalization techniques.
c6ae2bb8c912bb757acedb9b72ab988800368b6c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of tasks: (1) digit classification using the MNIST dataset, where images will be preprocessed and passed through several Chebyshev KAN layers followed by fully connected layers, with performance compared to traditional MLPs; (2) synthetic function approximation tasks involving polynomial, trigonometric, and discontinuous functions, where input-output pairs will be generated and mean squared error (MSE) will be used as the evaluation metric; (3) fractal function generation, where the model will be trained to approximate fractal-like functions and assessed by MSE and qualitative comparison of predicted versus true outputs. Ablation studies will systematically vary initialization methods (e.g., Xavier, He, Lecun), normalization strategies (tanh, Min-Max, standardization), polynomial degree, and Chebyshev polynomial type to assess their impact on accuracy, parameter efficiency, and stability. Baseline comparisons will include traditional MLPs and original KAN implementations.
c6ae2bb8c912bb757acedb9b72ab988800368b6c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a neural network architecture that leverages the Kolmogorov-Arnold theorem and Chebyshev polynomial parametrization for learnable edge functions, resulting in superior parameter efficiency, dynamic activation flexibility, and enhanced interpretability compared to traditional MLPs. The method enables compact and stable representations of complex, high-dimensional functions, and demonstrates improved accuracy and efficiency on both standard benchmarks and challenging synthetic tasks. The architecture also offers a transparent framework for analyzing learned transformations, and provides systematic insights through comprehensive ablation studies.

c6bb2c03f14faeadfdab7821619488c62ce6f263.title: Particle algorithms for maximum likelihood training of latent variable models
c6bb2c03f14faeadfdab7821619488c62ce6f263.research_question: How can scalable and practical algorithms be developed for maximum likelihood estimation in broad classes of latent variable models, particularly when traditional EM or MCMC-based approaches are computationally infeasible or intractable?
c6bb2c03f14faeadfdab7821619488c62ce6f263.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that particle-based algorithms, derived from discretized gradient flows of the free energy functional associated with latent variable models, can efficiently and accurately approximate maximum likelihood estimators and corresponding posteriors, even in high-dimensional and complex models.
c6bb2c03f14faeadfdab7821619488c62ce6f263.proposed_method: The proposed approach formulates maximum likelihood estimation for latent variable models as the minimization of a free energy functional F(θ, q), where θ are model parameters and q is a distribution over latent variables. By identifying and discretizing various gradient flows associated with F, practical particle-based algorithms are constructed. These include particle gradient descent (PGD), a particle-based quasi-Newton (PQN) method, and a particle marginal gradient descent (PMGD) approach. Each method evolves a cloud of particles representing the latent variable distribution, updating both θ and the particle cloud via discretized mean-field Fokker-Planck or Langevin dynamics, with parameter updates informed by empirical averages over the particle cloud. Technical adaptations such as adaptive step sizes, stochastic gradient estimates, and vectorized computation are incorporated to ensure scalability and stability in high-dimensional settings.
c6bb2c03f14faeadfdab7821619488c62ce6f263.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of models and datasets, including a toy hierarchical Gaussian model, Bayesian logistic regression (using a breast cancer dataset with 683 data points and 9 regression weights), a Bayesian neural network for MNIST digit classification (subsampled to 1000 data points), and a deep generator network for image reconstruction and synthesis on MNIST and CelebA datasets. Baselines for comparison will include traditional EM, variational inference (mean-field Gaussian VI), stochastic optimization via unadjusted Langevin (SOUL), variational autoencoders (VAE), alternating backpropagation (ABP), and short-run MCMC (SR). Evaluation metrics will include test error rates, mean squared error for inpainting, Fréchet Inception Distance for image synthesis, and log pointwise predictive density. Key experimental details include varying the number of particles, step sizes, and using both time-averaged and final particle clouds for posterior approximation.
c6bb2c03f14faeadfdab7821619488c62ce6f263.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a new class of particle-based algorithms for maximum likelihood training of latent variable models, derived from discretized gradient flows of the free energy functional. These methods are claimed to be broadly applicable, scalable to high-dimensional settings, and simple to implement. The approach unifies and generalizes existing methods such as EM, ULA, and variational inference under a common optimization framework, and demonstrates improved performance and scalability over traditional MCMC-EM and coordinate-wise Monte Carlo methods. The research also paves the way for further algorithmic innovations by considering joint optimization over parameters and latent distributions, and by leveraging alternative geometries and optimization routines.

c6db7e8f83ae54a3634d4dcb17db03c0c55ec2b5.title: VILA-U: a Unified Foundation Model Integrating Visual Understanding and Generation
c6db7e8f83ae54a3634d4dcb17db03c0c55ec2b5.research_question: How can a unified foundation model be developed to effectively integrate visual understanding and generation across images, videos, and language, using a single, streamlined architecture?
c6db7e8f83ae54a3634d4dcb17db03c0c55ec2b5.hypothesis: A unified autoregressive next-token prediction framework, equipped with a vision tower that aligns discrete visual tokens with textual inputs during pretraining, can achieve competitive performance in both visual-language understanding and generation tasks without the need for external components such as diffusion models.
c6db7e8f83ae54a3634d4dcb17db03c0c55ec2b5.proposed_method: A unified multi-modal framework will be constructed, featuring a foundation vision tower that converts visual inputs into discrete tokens via residual vector quantization. This vision tower will be pretrained using a combination of text-image contrastive loss and VQ-based image reconstruction loss, ensuring both semantic alignment with text and high-fidelity visual reconstruction. The multi-modal model will concatenate visual and text tokens, inserting special tokens to distinguish modalities, and train the entire system with a unified next-token prediction objective. Residual quantization will be employed to balance feature capacity and token efficiency, and a depth transformer will be used to autoregressively predict residual codes for visual tokens. The approach will leverage pretrained CLIP weights for initialization and apply a staged training recipe to first establish alignment and then enhance reconstruction.
c6db7e8f83ae54a3634d4dcb17db03c0c55ec2b5.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize the LLaMA-2-7B language model and SigLIP-based vision encoders, with residual quantization and depth transformer modules. The vision tower will be trained on COYO-700M and evaluated for zero-shot classification and reconstruction on ImageNet. Multi-modal pretraining will use 1M [image, text] pairs from ShareGPT4V, 6M interleaved text-image pairs from MMC4, 15M [text, image] pairs from an internal dataset, and 1M [text, video] pairs from OpenVid. Visual understanding will be evaluated on benchmarks such as VQAv2, GQA, TextVQA, POPE, MME, SEED, MM-Vet, ActivityNet, MSVD, MSRVTT, and TGIF. Visual generation will be assessed using MJHQ-30K (FID), GenAI-Bench (image-to-text generation), and VBench (video generation), with classifier-free guidance applied during generation. Comparisons will be made against both autoregressive and diffusion-based baselines.
c6db7e8f83ae54a3634d4dcb17db03c0c55ec2b5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a unified autoregressive framework that eliminates the need for separate modules or diffusion models for visual generation, simplifying the architecture. The vision tower uniquely combines text-image contrastive alignment and residual quantization, enabling discrete visual tokens to be semantically meaningful and reconstructable. The method demonstrates that autoregressive models can achieve near state-of-the-art performance in both visual understanding and generation, with competitive results to diffusion-based models despite using less training data. The unified training recipe and staged alignment-reconstruction strategy further enhance the model's effectiveness for multi-modal tasks.

c6dd31c40836d616b50feab17aff569591c4262e.title: VideoLLaMA 2: Advancing Spatial-Temporal Modeling and Audio Understanding in Video-LLMs
c6dd31c40836d616b50feab17aff569591c4262e.research_question: How can spatial-temporal modeling and audio understanding be advanced in large video-language models to improve performance on multimodal video and audio tasks such as video question answering and captioning?
c6dd31c40836d616b50feab17aff569591c4262e.hypothesis: Integrating a specialized spatial-temporal convolution connector for video features and a joint-trained audio branch into a dual-branch video-language model will significantly enhance the model's ability to capture complex spatial, temporal, and auditory dynamics, resulting in improved performance on multimodal video and audio understanding tasks.
c6dd31c40836d616b50feab17aff569591c4262e.proposed_method: A dual-branch architecture is proposed, consisting of a Vision-Language Branch and an Audio-Language Branch, each independently encoding their respective modalities before fusing information in a large language model (LLM) decoder. The Vision-Language Branch utilizes a frame-based image encoder (e.g., CLIP ViT-L/14), followed by a novel Spatial-Temporal Convolution (STC) connector that employs RegStage convolutional blocks and 3D convolution for spatial-temporal aggregation and token compression, preserving order and minimizing information loss. The Audio-Language Branch processes audio as log-mel spectrograms using a state-of-the-art audio encoder (BEATs), followed by a multilayer perceptron for modality alignment. Joint training is performed to integrate both branches, enabling the model to learn cross-modal representations and instruction-following capabilities. The LLM backbone (e.g., Mistral-Instruct, Mixtral-Instruct, Qwen2-Instruct) is fine-tuned for multimodal tasks, with modality-specific encoders frozen or optimized depending on the training stage.
c6dd31c40836d616b50feab17aff569591c4262e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a wide range of video, audio, and audio-visual datasets. Pre-training utilizes large-scale web-crawled video-text and image-text datasets (e.g., Panda-70M, WebVid-10M, VIDAL-10M, InternVid-10M, CC-3M, DCI) and audio-text datasets (e.g., WavCaps, AudioCaps, Clotho, MusicCaps, VGGSound, UrbanSound8K, ESC50, TUT2017/2016, VocalSound). Multi-task fine-tuning incorporates high-quality, fine-grained annotations for tasks such as video captioning, video QA, audio captioning, sound event classification, and instruction-following using datasets like VideoChat, Kinetics-710, SthSthv2, NExTQA, CLEVRER, EgoQA, Tgif, AVQA, AVSD, AVInstruct, and more. Evaluation is performed on multiple-choice video QA (EgoSchema, Perception-Test, MV-Bench, VideoMME), open-ended video QA (MSVD-QA, ActivityNet-QA, Video-ChatGPT), and video captioning (MSVC) benchmarks. Baselines include both proprietary (e.g., Gemini, GPT-4V, Reka) and open-source models (e.g., LLaMA-VID, Video-LLaVA, VideoChat2, LLaVA-NeXT-Video, PLLaVA, VILA1.5, LLaVA-OneVision). Metrics include top-1 accuracy for QA and GPT-assisted correctness/detailedness scores for captioning. Training details specify batch sizes, learning rates, and epoch counts for each stage.
c6dd31c40836d616b50feab17aff569591c4262e.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel Spatial-Temporal Convolution (STC) connector for video feature aggregation, which preserves spatial-temporal order and reduces token count while minimizing information loss. The dual-branch architecture with independent vision and audio encoders, jointly trained for multimodal integration, enables advanced audio-visual understanding. The approach systematically addresses limitations in temporal modeling and audio integration seen in prior video-LLMs. Comprehensive multi-stage training and evaluation across diverse multimodal datasets and tasks further distinguish the proposed method, setting a new standard for open-source video-language models.

c6ee979c2da4b55a8486abae4cd720422ab09b26.title: When Not to Trust Language Models: Investigating Effectiveness of Parametric and Non-Parametric Memories
c6ee979c2da4b55a8486abae4cd720422ab09b26.research_question: How can the strengths and limitations of large language models (LMs) in memorizing factual knowledge be systematically characterized, and under what conditions should parametric (model-internal) versus non-parametric (retrieval-based) memories be relied upon for open-domain question answering? Can a system be developed to adaptively combine these memory types to optimize both performance and efficiency?
c6ee979c2da4b55a8486abae4cd720422ab09b26.hypothesis: Factual knowledge that is frequently discussed on the web is more likely to be memorized by language models, while less popular knowledge is not well captured and thus requires retrieval of external non-parametric memories. Adaptive use of retrieval, based on question characteristics such as entity popularity and relationship type, can improve both accuracy and efficiency over always using retrieval or parametric memory alone.
c6ee979c2da4b55a8486abae4cd720422ab09b26.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical study will be conducted to probe the factual knowledge memorization capabilities of large language models across a spectrum of model sizes and architectures. The approach will involve evaluating models on open-domain question answering tasks using both existing and newly constructed datasets (e.g., POPQA) that systematically vary entity popularity and relationship type. The methodology will include (1) closed-book QA to assess parametric memorization, (2) retrieval-augmented QA using both sparse (BM25) and dense (Contriever) retrieval systems, and (3) a novel Adaptive Retrieval framework that dynamically decides, per question, whether to augment the input with retrieved evidence based on a heuristic (e.g., entity popularity threshold) tuned on a development set. The Adaptive Retrieval system will select between parametric-only and retrieval-augmented predictions to maximize accuracy and minimize inference cost.
c6ee979c2da4b55a8486abae4cd720422ab09b26.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using ten large language models from three families (GPT-Neo, OPT, GPT-3) with varying parameter counts. Evaluation will be performed on two open-domain QA datasets: the newly constructed POPQA (14k questions with controlled entity popularity and relationship types) and EntityQuestions (long-tail entity distribution). Accuracy will be used as the primary evaluation metric, with a prediction marked correct if any substring matches a gold answer. Baselines will include vanilla (parametric-only) LMs, always-retrieval-augmented LMs (BM25, Contriever, GenRead), and the proposed Adaptive Retrieval method. Additional analyses will examine the effect of scaling, entity popularity, and relationship type on memorization, as well as the efficiency gains (inference time and API cost) of adaptive retrieval. The effectiveness of retrieval augmentation will be further dissected by analyzing cases where retrieval helps or harms performance, using recall@1 of retrieved documents.
c6ee979c2da4b55a8486abae4cd720422ab09b26.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new large-scale, entity-centric QA dataset (POPQA) specifically designed to probe long-tail factual knowledge and control for entity popularity and relationship type. It presents a novel Adaptive Retrieval framework that, for the first time, adaptively decides when to use non-parametric retrieval based on input features, rather than always retrieving or relying solely on parametric memory. This approach is claimed to improve both accuracy and efficiency, especially for large LMs, and provides new insights into the interplay between model scale, memorization, and retrieval augmentation. The work also offers a fine-grained analysis of when retrieval helps or hurts, and demonstrates significant inference cost reductions with adaptive strategies.

c6f9e20f574c37e2ef12fa41a5729df8e0499f6f.title: Sample-Efficient Optimization in the Latent Space of Deep Generative Models via Weighted Retraining
c6f9e20f574c37e2ef12fa41a5729df8e0499f6f.research_question: How can sample-efficient black-box optimization be improved for high-dimensional and structured input spaces, such as those encountered in scientific and engineering applications, by leveraging deep generative models and adaptive latent space methods?
c6f9e20f574c37e2ef12fa41a5729df8e0499f6f.hypothesis: Weighted retraining of deep generative models, where data points are assigned weights according to their objective function values and the generative model is periodically retrained on these weighted datasets, will lead to a latent space that is more amenable to efficient optimization, resulting in improved sample efficiency and optimization performance compared to existing latent space optimization methods.
c6f9e20f574c37e2ef12fa41a5729df8e0499f6f.proposed_method: A novel optimization framework is proposed that operates in the latent space of a deep generative model (DGM), such as a variational autoencoder (VAE) or a generative adversarial network (GAN). The method introduces a weighted retraining procedure, where data points collected during the optimization trajectory are assigned explicit, positive weights based on their objective function values using a rank-based weighting function. The generative model is periodically retrained or fine-tuned on the weighted dataset, ensuring that the latent manifold increasingly models high-performing regions of the input space. Optimization is performed in the latent space using a surrogate model, such as a Gaussian process, which is fit to the latent representations of the weighted dataset and used to propose new query points. This approach actively adapts the generative model to focus on promising regions, overcoming the limitations of static, pre-trained generative models.
c6f9e20f574c37e2ef12fa41a5729df8e0499f6f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three representative optimization tasks: (1) a 2D shape area maximization task using binary images, (2) an arithmetic expression fitting task using a formal grammar, and (3) a chemical design task optimizing penalized logP using the ZINC250k molecule dataset. For each task, an appropriate deep generative model (e.g., convolutional VAE, grammar VAE, or junction tree VAE) will be employed, and latent space optimization will be performed using Bayesian optimization with a Gaussian process surrogate. Baselines will include standard latent space optimization (LSO) without retraining, cross-entropy method variants (CEM-PI, DbAS, FBVAE, RWR), and state-of-the-art domain-specific methods such as ChemBO. Evaluation metrics will focus on sample efficiency, specifically the TopK score (the Kth best novel evaluated point as a function of the number of objective function evaluations), and experiments will be repeated with multiple random seeds to assess robustness. Hyperparameters such as weighting strength and retraining frequency will be systematically varied and analyzed.
c6f9e20f574c37e2ef12fa41a5729df8e0499f6f.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a principled combination of data weighting and periodic retraining for deep generative models in the context of latent space optimization, transforming the generative model into an active participant in the optimization process. This approach enables the latent space to adaptively focus on high-performing regions, significantly improving sample efficiency and optimization performance over both standard LSO and existing weighted retraining methods, which typically use binary weights and lack an explicit optimization component. The method is general, easy to implement on top of existing models, and applicable to a wide range of high-dimensional, structured optimization problems without requiring domain-specific knowledge.

c7215ab4589ce3590910c597e86b1aba8e460d49.title: e3nn: Euclidean Neural Networks
c7215ab4589ce3590910c597e86b1aba8e460d49.research_question: How can a generalized, flexible, and mathematically rigorous framework be developed for constructing E(3)-equivariant trainable functions, enabling neural networks to operate directly on 3D geometric data and geometric tensors with predictable transformation properties under rotations, translations, and inversion?
c7215ab4589ce3590910c597e86b1aba8e460d49.hypothesis: A unified and extensible framework based on provably general equivariant operations, such as tensor products and spherical harmonics, will enable the efficient construction of E(3)-equivariant neural networks that can generalize better, require less data, and support a broad range of scientific and engineering applications involving 3D data.
c7215ab4589ce3590910c597e86b1aba8e460d49.proposed_method: A comprehensive Python-based software framework will be developed to facilitate the construction of E(3)-equivariant neural networks. The core of the framework will include mathematically rigorous and composable equivariant operations, such as a general TensorProduct class for trainable bi-linear operations between irreducible representations (irreps) of the orthogonal group O(3), and efficient implementations of spherical harmonics for representing functions on the sphere. Additional components will include parity-equivariant operations, fast conversion between irreps and signals on the sphere, and modules for decomposing tensors of arbitrary rank into direct sums of irreps. The framework will provide all base operations needed to build complex equivariant modules, such as convolutions and attention mechanisms, ensuring that all network components preserve the desired transformation properties under the Euclidean group.
c7215ab4589ce3590910c597e86b1aba8e460d49.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a diverse set of scientific and engineering tasks involving 3D data, such as molecular property prediction, phonon density of states prediction, interatomic potential modeling, diffusion MRI analysis, and fluid flow approximation. Datasets will include molecular structures, micro-CT images, and simulated physical systems. Baselines will comprise both invariant models (operating only on scalars) and restricted equivariant models (limited to scalar and vector operations), as well as existing state-of-the-art equivariant architectures. Evaluation metrics will include prediction accuracy, generalization error (learning curves), and data efficiency. The experimental setup will leverage the modularity of the proposed framework to articulate various E(3)-equivariant architectures, such as Tensor Field Networks, 3D Steerable CNNs, and SE(3) Transformers, enabling systematic comparison and ablation studies.
c7215ab4589ce3590910c597e86b1aba8e460d49.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a unified, extensible, and mathematically rigorous set of primitives for constructing E(3)-equivariant neural networks, including full support for parity-equivariance (O(3)), a general and parameterizable TensorProduct operation, and efficient conversion between irreps and spherical signals. The approach enables the articulation of a wide variety of equivariant architectures within a single software ecosystem, supporting arbitrary complexity and facilitating research across multiple scientific domains. The framework's generality, composability, and focus on geometric tensor algebra represent significant innovations over previous invariant or restricted equivariant models.

c73f7edb0b7453e65e8838aa1f1cdd54f535e25d.title: SVGD as a kernelized Wasserstein gradient flow of the chi-squared divergence
c73f7edb0b7453e65e8838aa1f1cdd54f535e25d.research_question: Can a new perspective on Stein Variational Gradient Descent (SVGD) as a kernelized Wasserstein gradient flow of the chi-squared divergence lead to improved theoretical understanding and new sampling algorithms with strong convergence guarantees?
c73f7edb0b7453e65e8838aa1f1cdd54f535e25d.hypothesis: Viewing SVGD as a kernelized gradient flow of the chi-squared divergence, rather than the KL divergence, will provide stronger theoretical convergence guarantees under weaker conditions (such as the Poincaré inequality), and enable the development of new algorithms—such as Laplacian Adjusted Wasserstein Gradient Descent (LAWGD)—with scale-invariant, exponential convergence properties.
c73f7edb0b7453e65e8838aa1f1cdd54f535e25d.proposed_method: The proposed method develops a novel theoretical framework that interprets SVGD as a kernelized Wasserstein gradient flow of the chi-squared divergence, rather than the traditional KL divergence. This perspective motivates the design of a new algorithm, Laplacian Adjusted Wasserstein Gradient Descent (LAWGD), which leverages the spectral decomposition of the Laplacian operator associated with the target density. In LAWGD, the kernel is chosen as the inverse of the Langevin diffusion generator, ensuring that the kernel operator matches the spectral properties required for strong convergence. The algorithm evolves a set of particles according to a discretized version of the gradient flow, where the update direction for each particle is computed using the spectral kernel, which is approximated numerically via finite differences or explicit eigendecomposition when available. This approach is designed to ensure exponential convergence in KL divergence under the relatively weak assumption that the target distribution satisfies a Poincaré inequality.
c73f7edb0b7453e65e8838aa1f1cdd54f535e25d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on low-dimensional sampling tasks, including the standard Gaussian distribution and mixtures of Gaussians in one and two dimensions. For the standard Gaussian, the spectral kernel is constructed using Hermite polynomials, while for more general target distributions, the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of the associated differential operator are approximated using finite difference methods on a discretized grid. LAWGD will be compared to SVGD with standard RBF kernels, using matched step sizes and initialization schemes. Evaluation metrics will include the convergence of the empirical particle distribution to the target density, assessed via kernel density estimation and direct comparison to the true density. The experimental setup will involve tuning step sizes for both algorithms and running them for a fixed number of iterations, with visual and quantitative assessments of sample quality.
c73f7edb0b7453e65e8838aa1f1cdd54f535e25d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a fundamentally new interpretation of SVGD as a kernelized Wasserstein gradient flow of the chi-squared divergence, leading to the first finite-time theoretical guarantees for SVGD under a Poincaré inequality. The development of LAWGD represents a novel algorithmic contribution, providing scale-invariant exponential convergence without requiring log-concavity of the target distribution. The use of the spectral decomposition of the Langevin generator to construct the kernel is a new methodological innovation, and the resulting algorithm demonstrates strong uniform ergodicity and practical feasibility in low-dimensional settings.

c742d3228e08c2c7b7775861e432511b54410b27.title: Dynamic-Resolution Model Learning for Object Pile Manipulation
c742d3228e08c2c7b7775861e432511b54410b27.research_question: How can dynamic and adaptive scene representations at varying levels of abstraction be learned and leveraged to optimize efficiency and effectiveness in robotic manipulation of object piles across diverse tasks and environments?
c742d3228e08c2c7b7775861e432511b54410b27.hypothesis: Dynamic selection of scene representation resolution, conditioned on current observations and task goals, enables a unified dynamics model to achieve superior efficiency and effectiveness in object pile manipulation compared to fixed-resolution approaches.
c742d3228e08c2c7b7775861e432511b54410b27.proposed_method: A unified framework is developed that constructs dynamic-resolution particle-based representations of the environment from RGBD visual observations. A resolution regressor, trained in a self-supervised manner using Bayesian optimization, predicts the optimal abstraction level (i.e., number of particles) at each planning step based on the current observation and task goal. The perception module samples particles from the visual input at the predicted resolution, and a graph neural network (GNN)-based dynamics model, instantiated with node and edge encoders/decoders, predicts the evolution of the particle-based scene representation under external actions. This model is integrated into a model-predictive control (MPC) loop, where at each step, the optimal resolution is adaptively selected, the scene is encoded, future states are predicted, and actions are optimized via trajectory optimization (combining sampling and gradient descent) to minimize a task-specific objective.
c742d3228e08c2c7b7775861e432511b54410b27.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted both in simulation (using NVIDIA FleX) and in the real world with a robotic manipulator equipped with a pusher and an overhead RGBD camera. The evaluation covers three object pile manipulation tasks: gathering, redistributing into complex shapes, and sorting multiple piles, using various granular materials (e.g., almonds, coffee beans, rice, candy). The method is compared against fixed-resolution dynamics models and a CNN-based baseline. Evaluation metrics include task success rate (fraction of trials achieving a distribution distance below a threshold), task loss reduction over MPC steps, and qualitative assessment of goal achievement. The experimental setup includes diverse initial and goal configurations to assess adaptability and generalization.
c742d3228e08c2c7b7775861e432511b54410b27.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a dynamic-resolution scene representation framework for robotic manipulation, enabling continuous and adaptive selection of abstraction level during task execution. A unified GNN-based dynamics model generalizes across varying particle set sizes and densities, supporting flexible planning. The method leverages a self-supervised resolution regressor trained via Bayesian optimization to automatically determine the most effective representation for each task stage. This results in improved efficiency and effectiveness over state-of-the-art fixed-resolution baselines, as demonstrated across multiple real-world and simulated object pile manipulation tasks.

c74b5d298cd5fe735f2c8bc18a94f28010a2ccfc.title: Cut and Learn for Unsupervised Object Detection and Instance Segmentation
c74b5d298cd5fe735f2c8bc18a94f28010a2ccfc.research_question: How can unsupervised object detection and instance segmentation models be developed to discover and localize multiple objects in diverse image domains without relying on human-annotated labels?
c74b5d298cd5fe735f2c8bc18a94f28010a2ccfc.hypothesis: Self-supervised visual representations contain sufficient information to enable the discovery and localization of multiple objects per image, and this capability can be amplified through a combination of mask generation, robust loss strategies, and iterative self-training, resulting in state-of-the-art unsupervised object detection and segmentation performance across diverse domains.
c74b5d298cd5fe735f2c8bc18a94f28010a2ccfc.proposed_method: A novel unsupervised object detection and instance segmentation framework, Cut-and-LEaRn (CutLER), will be developed. The approach begins by extracting self-supervised features from a Vision Transformer (ViT) model pretrained with DINO on unlabeled data. A new mask generation algorithm, MaskCut, will be introduced to iteratively apply Normalized Cuts to the patch-wise similarity matrix derived from DINO features, producing multiple coarse binary masks per image. These masks serve as pseudo-labels for training a detection model using a robust loss dropping strategy (DropLoss), which ignores loss for predicted regions with low overlap to pseudo-labels, encouraging exploration of unlabeled objects. The detection model is further refined through multiple rounds of self-training, where high-confidence predictions are used as additional pseudo-labels in subsequent training rounds.
c74b5d298cd5fe735f2c8bc18a94f28010a2ccfc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using only unlabeled ImageNet data for training, with no access to target domain images or labels during model development. The method will be evaluated in a zero-shot manner on 11 diverse benchmarks, including COCO, LVIS, VOC, OpenImages, Objects365, UVO, KITTI, Watercolor, Comic, and Clipart, covering a wide range of domains such as natural images, paintings, sketches, videos, and traffic scenes. Standard detection and segmentation architectures (e.g., Mask R-CNN, Cascade Mask R-CNN) will be used as backbones. Baselines will include state-of-the-art unsupervised and zero-shot methods such as FreeSOLO, TokenCut, LOST, and DETReg. Evaluation metrics will include class-agnostic Average Precision (AP) and Average Recall (AR) for both bounding boxes and masks. Additional experiments will assess the impact of fine-tuning with varying amounts of labeled data and the generalization of the approach to different detection architectures and pretraining datasets.
c74b5d298cd5fe735f2c8bc18a94f28010a2ccfc.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces MaskCut, a simple yet effective extension of Normalized Cuts for discovering multiple object masks per image using self-supervised features. The approach is architecture- and data-agnostic, compatible with various detection models, and requires only unlabeled data for training. The robust DropLoss strategy enables the model to explore and detect objects missed by initial pseudo-labels. Multiple rounds of self-training further refine the model, leading to significant improvements in both detection and segmentation performance. The method achieves state-of-the-art results in zero-shot unsupervised object detection and segmentation, more than doubling the performance of previous approaches on most benchmarks, and demonstrates strong robustness to domain shifts. Additionally, the framework can serve as a superior pretraining strategy for label-efficient and fully supervised detection and segmentation tasks.

c78350e81298ca87bc1d59b466fa40081232caaa.title: Teaching Large Language Models to Reason with Reinforcement Learning
c78350e81298ca87bc1d59b466fa40081232caaa.research_question: How can reinforcement learning techniques be leveraged to improve the reasoning capabilities of large language models across various reward schemes, model initializations, and training regimes?
c78350e81298ca87bc1d59b466fa40081232caaa.hypothesis: Reinforcement learning algorithms, particularly Expert Iteration, can enhance the reasoning abilities of large language models more effectively and efficiently than traditional supervised fine-tuning, and may overcome limitations in output diversity and overfitting associated with static datasets.
c78350e81298ca87bc1d59b466fa40081232caaa.proposed_method: A comprehensive comparative study will be conducted using several reinforcement learning algorithms—Expert Iteration (EI), Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), and Return-Conditioned RL (RCRL)—to fine-tune large language models on reasoning tasks. The approach will involve both sparse and dense reward signals, provided either heuristically or via a learned reward model, and will evaluate models initialized from both pre-trained and supervised fine-tuned checkpoints. For EI, rejection sampling and distillation will be used to iteratively improve the policy, while PPO will be implemented with on-policy rollouts and gradient updates, incorporating architectural optimizations such as LoRA and value head detachment for stability. RCRL will be trained offline using step-wise labeled trajectories derived from EI-generated data. Outcome-Based Reward Models (ORMs) will be trained as verifiers to rerank candidate solutions and further guide policy improvement.
c78350e81298ca87bc1d59b466fa40081232caaa.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on math word problem benchmarks GSM8K and SVAMP, using Llama-2 models of 7B and 13B parameters. Both supervised fine-tuned (SFT) and pre-trained initializations will be tested. Evaluation metrics will include maj@1 (greedy sampling accuracy), maj@96 (majority vote over 96 samples), rerank@96 (ORM-based reranking), and pass@96 (best-of-96 accuracy). Baselines will include SFT, prompted models, and results from other state-of-the-art models such as GPT-3, GPT-4, and WizardMath. Ablations will be performed on reward density, ORM guidance, sampling parameters, and model size. Sample complexity, convergence speed, and the impact of exploration diversity will be systematically analyzed.
c78350e81298ca87bc1d59b466fa40081232caaa.novelty_claims: The proposed research offers a systematic, head-to-head comparison of multiple RL algorithms for LLM reasoning, revealing that Expert Iteration achieves superior performance and competitive sample efficiency compared to PPO and RCRL. The study will demonstrate that RL fine-tuning can simultaneously improve both greedy and best-of-N accuracy metrics, in contrast to supervised fine-tuning which often trades off diversity for accuracy. It will also identify that the primary bottleneck for further improvements is limited exploration during RL training, rather than reward signal quality or algorithmic sophistication. These findings will provide new insights into the role of RL in LLM fine-tuning and highlight the importance of exploration and synthetic data generation for robust reasoning capabilities.

c7a7104df3db13737a865ede2be8146990fa4026.title: Mitigating Hallucination in Large Multi-Modal Models via Robust Instruction Tuning
c7a7104df3db13737a865ede2be8146990fa4026.research_question: How can hallucination in large multi-modal models (LMMs) be effectively mitigated, particularly when models are required to generate image-grounded responses to diverse and open-ended visual instructions?
c7a7104df3db13737a865ede2be8146990fa4026.hypothesis: Incorporating a large-scale, diverse visual instruction tuning dataset containing both positive and negative instructions at multiple semantic levels will significantly reduce hallucination in LMMs and improve their robustness and faithfulness to image content.
c7a7104df3db13737a865ede2be8146990fa4026.proposed_method: A large-scale visual instruction tuning dataset, LRV-Instruction, will be constructed using GPT-4 to generate 400,000 visual instructions spanning 16 vision-and-language tasks. This dataset will include both positive and negative instructions, with negative instructions systematically designed at three semantic levels: Nonexistent Object Manipulation, Existent Object Manipulation, and Knowledge Manipulation, in both declarative and interrogative formats. The method will involve fine-tuning state-of-the-art LMMs (e.g., MiniGPT4 and mPLUG-Owl) on this dataset, using only the necessary modules (e.g., linear projection layer or LoRA-based text encoder adaptation) to maximize efficiency. To evaluate hallucination and instruction-following ability, a novel automated evaluation framework, GPT4-Assisted Visual Instruction Evaluation (GAVIE), will be developed, leveraging GPT-4 to score model outputs on relevancy and accuracy without requiring human-annotated ground truth.
c7a7104df3db13737a865ede2be8146990fa4026.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by fine-tuning MiniGPT4-7B and mPLUG-Owl-7B on the LRV-Instruction dataset, with comparisons to baseline models including MiniGPT4, LLaVA, InstructBLIP, MMGPT, and others. Evaluation will be performed on the proposed LRV-Instruction evaluation set as well as public benchmarks such as MME (measuring perception and cognition), POPE and AMBER (object hallucination), and GQA (visual question answering). The GAVIE framework will be used to provide quantitative scores for hallucination and instruction-following, and human expert evaluations will be collected for alignment analysis. The impact of varying the ratio of positive to negative instructions in training will also be systematically studied.
c7a7104df3db13737a865ede2be8146990fa4026.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first large-scale and diverse visual instruction tuning dataset (LRV-Instruction) with both positive and negative instructions at multiple semantic levels, enabling robust instruction tuning for LMMs. It also proposes GAVIE, a novel, automated, and flexible evaluation framework for hallucination and instruction-following that does not require human-annotated ground truth and can adapt to diverse instruction formats. The approach is claimed to significantly reduce hallucination in LMMs, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods and providing empirical evidence on the importance of balanced positive and negative instruction data.

c7af46b35061e856aa3332ac2eec6a7ccee0cb35.title: Watermark Stealing in Large Language Models
c7af46b35061e856aa3332ac2eec6a7ccee0cb35.research_question: Are current large language model (LLM) watermarking schemes robust against adversarial attacks that attempt to reverse-engineer or bypass the watermark, and what are the fundamental vulnerabilities in their deployment?
c7af46b35061e856aa3332ac2eec6a7ccee0cb35.hypothesis: Current state-of-the-art LLM watermarking schemes are vulnerable to practical attacks that can reverse-engineer the watermarking rules through black-box API access, enabling both spoofing (imprinting a watermark without the secret key) and scrubbing (removing a watermark) with high success rates and low cost.
c7af46b35061e856aa3332ac2eec6a7ccee0cb35.proposed_method: A novel automated watermark stealing algorithm will be developed to approximate the secret watermarking rules used by LLMs. The method involves querying the API of a watermarked LLM with a diverse set of prompts, collecting the generated responses, and constructing empirical conditional distributions over token sequences. These distributions are used to compute scoring functions that estimate the likelihood of a token being classified as 'green' (i.e., contributing to the watermark) in a given context. The attacker then leverages these scores to guide an auxiliary language model during text generation, either to imprint the watermark (spoofing) or to avoid it (scrubbing), by modifying the model's logits in proportion to the estimated scores. The approach is designed to work in realistic black-box settings, without access to the secret key or the internal watermarking parameters, and is applicable to a range of state-of-the-art watermarking schemes.
c7af46b35061e856aa3332ac2eec6a7ccee0cb35.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple state-of-the-art watermarking schemes, including KGW2-SELFHASH, KGW2-SUM, KGW-HARD, KGW-SOFT, and UNIGRAM, using a variety of LLMs (e.g., LLAMA-7B, LLAMA-13B, MISTRAL-7B, GEMMA-7B) as both the target and attacker models. The evaluation will cover both spoofing (generating watermarked text without the key) and scrubbing (removing the watermark from text) attacks. Datasets such as Dolly-CW, HarmfulQ+AdvBench, MMWBookReports, MMWFakeNews, and RedditWritingPrompts will be used to ensure diversity and realism. Baselines will include standard paraphrasers (DIPPER, PEGASUS, ChatGPT) and recursive paraphrasing. Evaluation metrics will include the fraction of successful attacks at very low false positive rates (FPR), text quality as judged by GPT-4 or P-SP scores, and perplexity. The cost-effectiveness of the attack will be analyzed by varying the number of API queries, with a focus on achieving high attack success rates for less than $50 in API costs.
c7af46b35061e856aa3332ac2eec6a7ccee0cb35.novelty_claims: The proposed research formalizes and thoroughly studies the threat model of LLM watermark stealing, introducing the first automated algorithm for reverse-engineering watermarking rules through black-box API access. It provides the first comprehensive evaluation of both spoofing and scrubbing attacks on state-of-the-art watermarking schemes in realistic, low-FPR, high-quality text settings. The research demonstrates that vulnerabilities to spoofing directly enable highly effective scrubbing attacks, challenging the previously held belief that robustness to spoofing and scrubbing are at odds. The findings reveal that current watermarking schemes, including those previously considered robust, are susceptible to practical attacks, emphasizing the urgent need for more robust watermarking designs and evaluation protocols.

c7be406d6e144d260724dcbadc75252228bb3d99.title: Rethinking Circuit Completeness in Language Models: AND, OR, and ADDER Gates
c7be406d6e144d260724dcbadc75252228bb3d99.research_question: How can the logical structure of circuits within language models be systematically characterized and fully discovered to ensure both faithfulness and completeness, and what are the implications of such logical decompositions for mechanistic interpretability?
c7be406d6e144d260724dcbadc75252228bb3d99.hypothesis: Decomposing circuits in language models into AND, OR, and ADDER gates, and employing a combined noising-based and denoising-based intervention framework, will enable the complete and faithful identification of all logical gate types within circuits, thereby improving both interpretability and completeness compared to existing methods.
c7be406d6e144d260724dcbadc75252228bb3d99.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed that systematically decomposes circuits in language models into three fundamental logical gate types: AND, OR, and ADDER gates. The approach will employ both noising-based (Ns) and denoising-based (Dn) intervention strategies in parallel, allowing for the identification and separation of all three gate types by analyzing the intersections and differences between the circuits discovered by each strategy. The method will be designed to be compatible with existing circuit discovery algorithms, such as greedy search, linear estimation, and differentiable mask approaches, and will introduce minimal computational overhead. To ensure accurate separation of gate types, a granularity alignment procedure will be implemented, using a misalignment score to match the scale of Ns and Dn interventions. The overall optimization objective will combine the faithfulness and completeness losses from both intervention strategies, subject to a sparsity constraint.
c7be406d6e144d260724dcbadc75252228bb3d99.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the GPT-2 small language model as the computational graph, and will focus on three benchmark tasks: Indirect Object Inference (IOI), Greater Than (GT), and Syntactic Agreement (SA). Baseline comparisons will include representative methods from greedy search (e.g., ACDC), linear estimation (e.g., EAP), and differentiable mask (e.g., Edge Pruning). Evaluation metrics will include KL divergence and task accuracy for faithfulness, the change in output after circuit removal for completeness, and the ratio of circuit edges to total graph edges for sparsity. Randomness and reproducibility of discovered circuits will be assessed via Hamming distance across multiple random seeds. The experiments will also analyze the distribution, contribution, and functional roles of each logical gate type within the recovered circuits.
c7be406d6e144d260724dcbadc75252228bb3d99.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a systematic logical decomposition of circuits in language models into AND, OR, and ADDER gates, providing a principled framework for analyzing faithfulness and completeness. The combined noising-based and denoising-based intervention strategy enables full recovery and separation of all logical gate types, overcoming the limitations of existing methods that fail to fully identify OR gates or ensure completeness. The framework is designed for compatibility with a wide range of existing circuit discovery algorithms and introduces a novel granularity alignment procedure to ensure accurate gate classification. The research will also provide new insights into the functional distribution and output contributions of different logical gate types, advancing the interpretability and controllability of language models.

c7d7ad1eb52247c9c54a97fa83087d49070156a1.title: DAGMA: Learning DAGs via M-matrices and a Log-Determinant Acyclicity Characterization
c7d7ad1eb52247c9c54a97fa83087d49070156a1.research_question: How can the process of learning directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) from observational data be improved in terms of computational efficiency, accuracy, and scalability, particularly for both linear and nonlinear structural equation models, by developing new continuous optimization characterizations of acyclicity?
c7d7ad1eb52247c9c54a97fa83087d49070156a1.hypothesis: A novel acyclicity characterization based on the log-determinant function over M-matrices will enable more efficient, accurate, and scalable learning of DAG structures from data compared to existing trace-based acyclicity regularizers.
c7d7ad1eb52247c9c54a97fa83087d49070156a1.proposed_method: A new acyclicity characterization will be developed using the log-determinant (log-det) function, defined over the set of M-matrices, which leverages the nilpotency property of DAGs. This characterization, denoted as h_l det, is exact and differentiable, and is shown to be invex, ensuring all stationary points correspond to DAGs. The proposed learning algorithm, DAGMA (Directed Acyclic Graphs via M-matrices for Acyclicity), will optimize a score-based objective regularized by the log-det acyclicity function, following a central path approach reminiscent of barrier methods. The optimization proceeds by solving a sequence of unconstrained problems with decreasing regularization strength, guaranteeing convergence to a DAG without requiring post-processing. The method supports both linear and nonlinear SEMs, with model parameters (e.g., neural networks) optimized via first-order methods such as ADAM, and initialization within the feasible region ensured by starting from the zero matrix.
c7d7ad1eb52247c9c54a97fa83087d49070156a1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real datasets, covering a range of linear and nonlinear structural equation models (SEMs) with various noise types (Gaussian, Gumbel, exponential) and both binary and continuous data. Graph structures will include Erdős-Rényi (ER4) and scale-free (SF4) models, with node counts ranging from small (20) to large (1000). The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines such as GES, PC, NOTEARS, and GOLEM, using least squares and log-likelihood as score functions. Evaluation metrics will include structural Hamming distance (SHD) for accuracy and wall-clock runtime for computational efficiency. The experimental setup will use consistent hyperparameters across methods, and optimization will be performed using first-order solvers with a fixed wall-time limit for fairness.
c7d7ad1eb52247c9c54a97fa83087d49070156a1.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first acyclicity characterization for DAG learning based on the log-determinant function over M-matrices, providing an exact, differentiable, and invex regularizer. The method offers improved detection of large cycles, better-behaved gradients, and significantly faster computation compared to existing trace-based acyclicity functions. The central path optimization approach ensures that the final solution is always a DAG, eliminating the need for post-processing. Extensive experiments are expected to demonstrate superior accuracy (lower SHD) and substantial speedups over state-of-the-art methods for both linear and nonlinear SEMs.

c80d353af4d078d386e4e3b8d310b5d85e0c940b.title: Minimal Exploration in Structured Stochastic Bandits
c80d353af4d078d386e4e3b8d310b5d85e0c940b.research_question: How can minimal exploration strategies be designed for a broad class of structured stochastic multi-armed bandit (MAB) problems, where the mapping from arms to rewards exhibits known structural properties, in order to achieve optimal regret performance?
c80d353af4d078d386e4e3b8d310b5d85e0c940b.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by explicitly characterizing and matching the minimal exploration rates of sub-optimal arms, as dictated by the structure of the reward function, it is possible to design an algorithm that achieves asymptotically optimal regret for any structured stochastic bandit problem.
c80d353af4d078d386e4e3b8d310b5d85e0c940b.proposed_method: A new algorithm, OSSB (Optimal Sampling for Structured Bandits), will be developed to address structured stochastic bandit problems with arbitrary known structure in the arm-reward mapping. The method alternates between three phases: exploitation (selecting the empirically best arm), exploration (sampling sub-optimal arms at rates determined by the solution to a semi-infinite linear program that encodes the minimal exploration rates), and estimation (improving the estimate of the unknown reward parameters). In each round, OSSB computes empirical averages for each arm, solves an optimization problem to determine the minimal required exploration for each arm given the current estimates, and selects arms to ensure that the empirical sampling frequencies match these rates. The algorithm is designed to ensure that the number of times each sub-optimal arm is sampled converges to the theoretically minimal rate required to distinguish the optimal arm, as dictated by the structure of the problem. This approach does not rely on optimism-based or Thompson sampling principles, but instead directly targets the lower bound on regret.
c80d353af4d078d386e4e3b8d310b5d85e0c940b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on linear bandit problems with Gaussian rewards, using a finite set of arms (e.g., 81 arms in a 3-dimensional space) and multiple randomly generated parameter settings. OSSB will be compared against established baselines, including Thompson Sampling, GLM-UCB, and other asymptotically optimal algorithms. Evaluation will focus on cumulative regret over a range of time horizons, with results averaged across multiple random seeds and parameter instances. Performance will be assessed using average regret and confidence intervals, demonstrating the efficiency and practical superiority of OSSB relative to existing methods.
c80d353af4d078d386e4e3b8d310b5d85e0c940b.novelty_claims: The proposed approach provides the first unified solution and finite-time analysis for a wide class of structured stochastic bandit problems, encompassing linear, Lipschitz, unimodal, combinatorial, and dueling bandits. OSSB is the first algorithm to achieve asymptotically optimal regret for any structure by explicitly matching the minimal exploration rates derived from a general semi-infinite linear program. The method departs from classical optimism-based and Thompson sampling approaches, offering a new paradigm for exploration in structured bandits. Additionally, the work establishes new instance-specific regret lower bounds and demonstrates that OSSB can outperform existing state-of-the-art algorithms in practice.

c811bedbe8f4c21d0cba9f9175f7c2eb203284a7.title: Gemini 1.5: Unlocking multimodal understanding across millions of tokens of context
c811bedbe8f4c21d0cba9f9175f7c2eb203284a7.research_question: How can large-scale multimodal models be designed to efficiently process, recall, and reason over extremely long contexts—spanning millions of tokens and multiple modalities such as text, audio, and video—while maintaining or improving state-of-the-art performance across a broad range of tasks?
c811bedbe8f4c21d0cba9f9175f7c2eb203284a7.hypothesis: A sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) Transformer architecture, combined with advanced training, distillation, and serving infrastructure, will enable efficient and effective multimodal understanding and reasoning over contexts of up to 10 million tokens, surpassing existing models in both long-context and core multimodal benchmarks.
c811bedbe8f4c21d0cba9f9175f7c2eb203284a7.proposed_method: A new family of multimodal models will be developed using a sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) Transformer architecture, allowing conditional computation and efficient scaling to billions of parameters. The models will be natively multimodal, supporting interleaved inputs of text, audio, video, and code, and will be trained on massive, diverse datasets using TPUv4 accelerators. The approach will include architectural innovations to support context windows of up to 10 million tokens without degradation in performance, and will incorporate both dense and sparse scaling strategies. Two model variants will be constructed: a high-capacity model (Gemini 1.5 Pro) and a lightweight, latency-optimized model (Gemini 1.5 Flash), with the latter distilled online from the former and optimized for fast inference and efficient serving.
c811bedbe8f4c21d0cba9f9175f7c2eb203284a7.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate the models' long-context capabilities using both synthetic and real-world tasks across modalities. Synthetic 'needle-in-a-haystack' retrieval tasks will probe recall accuracy up to 10 million tokens for text, audio, and video. Real-world benchmarks will include long-document QA, long-video QA, and long-context automatic speech recognition (ASR), as well as in-context learning tasks such as translating a low-resource language from a single grammar manual. Core capabilities will be assessed on established benchmarks spanning math, science, reasoning, multilinguality, code, image, chart/document understanding, and multimodal reasoning. Baselines will include state-of-the-art models such as Claude 3.0, GPT-4 Turbo, and Gemini 1.0 Ultra, with evaluation metrics including recall, accuracy, word error rate, and benchmark-specific scores. Latency and serving efficiency will be measured across multiple languages using standardized API queries.
c811bedbe8f4c21d0cba9f9175f7c2eb203284a7.novelty_claims: The proposed models introduce a generational leap in context window size, enabling near-perfect recall and reasoning over up to 10 million tokens across multiple modalities—an order of magnitude beyond current state-of-the-art models. The architecture combines sparse MoE Transformers with advanced training and distillation techniques for unprecedented efficiency and scalability. The models demonstrate state-of-the-art or superior performance on a wide range of multimodal and long-context benchmarks, including novel in-context learning capabilities such as learning new languages from raw documentation. The lightweight variant achieves comparable quality with significantly reduced latency and serving costs, making large-scale multimodal reasoning practical for real-world applications.

c82ed4d78d9c1ee68039607ad8800482564284bd.title: Is Temperature Sample Efficient for Softmax Gaussian Mixture of Experts?
c82ed4d78d9c1ee68039607ad8800482564284bd.research_question: How does the temperature parameter in softmax-based gating functions affect sample efficiency and parameter estimation rates in Gaussian Mixture of Experts (MoE) models, and can a modified gating mechanism improve these rates?
c82ed4d78d9c1ee68039607ad8800482564284bd.hypothesis: The introduction of an activation function prior to the softmax gating in dense-to-sparse MoE models will mitigate detrimental interactions between temperature and model parameters, thereby improving parameter estimation rates from sub-polynomial to polynomial rates.
c82ed4d78d9c1ee68039607ad8800482564284bd.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted on the sample efficiency of temperature in softmax-based gating for Gaussian MoE models. The methodology involves formalizing the dense-to-sparse gating mechanism, analyzing its convergence rates for maximum likelihood estimation, and identifying the partial differential equation-based interactions between temperature and other model parameters that slow convergence. To address these issues, a novel activation dense-to-sparse gating function will be developed, where the output of a linear layer is passed through a non-linear activation (e.g., sigmoid or GELU) before entering the softmax. Theoretical conditions (first- and second-order independence) will be imposed on the activation function to ensure the elimination of problematic parameter interactions. Rigorous mathematical analysis will be performed to derive the improved estimation rates under both exact-specified and over-specified settings.
c82ed4d78d9c1ee68039607ad8800482564284bd.experiment_details: Empirical validation will be carried out using synthetic datasets generated from both standard and activation dense-to-sparse Gaussian MoE models. The Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm will be used for parameter estimation. Experiments will be conducted across a range of sample sizes (n = 10^4 to 10^5), with both exact-specified (number of experts known) and over-specified (number of experts overestimated) scenarios. Evaluation metrics will include convergence rates of the maximum likelihood estimator to the true mixing measure, measured using various Voronoi loss functions and Total Variation distance. Baseline comparisons will be made between standard dense-to-sparse gating and the proposed activation dense-to-sparse gating, with multiple runs to assess empirical convergence rates and variability.
c82ed4d78d9c1ee68039607ad8800482564284bd.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a new class of gating functions—activation dense-to-sparse gates—for Gaussian MoE models, providing the first theoretical analysis showing that standard temperature-based softmax gating leads to sub-polynomial parameter estimation rates due to intrinsic parameter interactions. By imposing linear independence conditions on the activation function, the proposed method rigorously demonstrates that parameter estimation rates can be improved to polynomial rates. The work also establishes new minimax lower bounds and provides practical guidelines for expert selection and estimation in MoE models, with implications for both well-specified and misspecified settings.

c848ef8d5cb5a04a7074d180f2bf937dce3388d9.title: Benign Overfitting in Two-layer Convolutional Neural Networks
c848ef8d5cb5a04a7074d180f2bf937dce3388d9.research_question: Under what conditions does benign overfitting occur in over-parameterized two-layer convolutional neural networks trained by gradient descent, and how does the signal-to-noise ratio influence the transition between benign and harmful overfitting?
c848ef8d5cb5a04a7074d180f2bf937dce3388d9.hypothesis: Benign overfitting in two-layer convolutional neural networks occurs when the signal-to-noise ratio and sample size satisfy a specific quantitative condition, enabling the network to achieve both low training and test loss; otherwise, overfitting becomes harmful and test loss remains high.
c848ef8d5cb5a04a7074d180f2bf937dce3388d9.proposed_method: A theoretical and algorithmic framework will be developed to analyze the training dynamics of two-layer convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with polynomial ReLU activation functions, where the second layer parameters are fixed.
