The input data will be modeled as consisting of label-dependent signal patches and label-independent noise patches, with a precise signal-noise decomposition of the CNN filters. Gradient descent will be used to train the CNN, and the evolution of the filter coefficients will be tracked via a discrete dynamical system that separates signal learning from noise memorization. A two-stage analysis will be conducted: the first stage examines the initial regime where loss derivatives are approximately constant, and the second stage analyzes the convergence of training and test loss as the network parameters evolve. Key technical steps include establishing monotonicity properties of the signal and noise coefficients, and leveraging homogeneity of the network to bound population loss.
c848ef8d5cb5a04a7074d180f2bf937dce3388d9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in a theoretical setting, where the data distribution is explicitly defined: each input consists of two patches, one containing a signal vector correlated with the label, and the other containing Gaussian noise orthogonal to the signal. The primary evaluation will be based on population (test) loss and training loss, with rigorous bounds derived for both. Theoretical baselines include prior results for linear models, kernel methods, and neural tangent kernel (NTK) regimes. The main experimental variable is the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and the analysis will characterize the phase transition in generalization behavior as SNR and sample size vary. No empirical datasets are specified; all results are derived analytically.
c848ef8d5cb5a04a7074d180f2bf937dce3388d9.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first precise theoretical characterization of benign overfitting in convolutional neural networks beyond the neural tangent kernel regime. A novel signal-noise decomposition technique is developed, enabling the reduction of the non-convex neural network training process to a tractable dynamical system of coefficients. The work establishes sharp phase transition conditions, driven by the signal-to-noise ratio, that delineate when benign overfitting is possible. The proof techniques and analytical tools presented are generalizable and may be applicable to broader classes of deep neural networks.

c84d3c9b9b191001c586c5ca9d2b6570bfe9d65d.title: Progressive Compositionality In Text-to-Image Generative Models
c84d3c9b9b191001c586c5ca9d2b6570bfe9d65d.research_question: How can text-to-image generative models be equipped with a deeper and more generalizable understanding of compositional relationships between objects and attributes, especially in complex scenarios?
c84d3c9b9b191001c586c5ca9d2b6570bfe9d65d.hypothesis: A curriculum-based contrastive learning approach, supported by a high-quality, automatically curated dataset of contrastive image pairs, will significantly improve the compositional understanding and generation capabilities of diffusion-based text-to-image models.
c84d3c9b9b191001c586c5ca9d2b6570bfe9d65d.proposed_method: A novel multi-stage curriculum contrastive learning framework, named EVOGEN, will be developed for fine-tuning diffusion-based text-to-image generative models. The approach will leverage a new contrastive dataset, CONPAIR, consisting of 15,000 high-quality image pairs with minimal visual differences but distinct compositional semantics. The data generation pipeline will use large language models (LLMs) to create complex compositional prompts and Visual Question Answering (VQA) models to automatically assess and curate image-text alignment, including a reverse-alignment strategy to revise prompts when image generation fails. The curriculum will be structured in three stages: (1) learning single object-attribute compositions, (2) mastering attribute binding and spatial/non-spatial relationships between two objects, and (3) handling complex scenes with multiple objects and intricate relationships. A contrastive loss based on InfoNCE will be applied to maximize the similarity between positive image-text pairs and minimize it for negative pairs, with a projection head mapping image representations to the contrastive space.
c84d3c9b9b191001c586c5ca9d2b6570bfe9d65d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using Stable Diffusion v2 as the base model, with fine-tuning performed on the CONPAIR dataset. The evaluation will utilize compositional text-to-image benchmarks such as T2I-CompBench and color-object compositionality prompts, measuring alignment with metrics like CLIPScore and VQA-guided image-text similarity. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art models such as SDXL, DALL-E 2, PixArt-α, Composable Diffusion, StructureDiffusion, Attn-Exct, GORs, and MARS. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the CONPAIR dataset, contrastive loss, and multi-stage curriculum. Qualitative and user studies will further evaluate compositional accuracy and user preference across a spectrum of compositional complexity.
c84d3c9b9b191001c586c5ca9d2b6570bfe9d65d.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a fully automated pipeline for generating high-quality, minimally-different contrastive image pairs for compositional learning, leveraging both LLMs and VQA models. The CONPAIR dataset offers a unique progression from simple to complex compositional scenarios, covering a broad range of attributes and relationships. The EVOGEN framework pioneers a curriculum-based contrastive fine-tuning strategy for diffusion models, enabling progressive learning of compositionality. The reverse-alignment technique for prompt revision based on VQA feedback is an innovative solution to improve image-text alignment in challenging cases. Overall, the approach aims to set a new standard for compositional understanding in text-to-image generation.

c85662dcd17eed4452019b640a30a323970472ef.title: Learning Transferable Motor Skills with Hierarchical Latent Mixture Policies
c85662dcd17eed4452019b640a30a323970472ef.research_question: How can reusable and transferable motor skills be learned from offline data in a way that enables efficient adaptation to new tasks, objects, and modalities, particularly in challenging and sparse-reward environments?
c85662dcd17eed4452019b640a30a323970472ef.hypothesis: A hierarchical latent mixture policy model that combines discrete and continuous latent variables across three levels of abstraction will enable the learning of distinct, interpretable, and transferable motor skills from offline data, resulting in improved sample efficiency and performance when adapting to new tasks, objects, and sensory modalities, especially in sparse-reward settings.
c85662dcd17eed4452019b640a30a323970472ef.proposed_method: A hierarchical latent mixture policy framework will be developed, consisting of three levels: a high-level discrete latent variable representing abstract skill selection, a mid-level continuous latent variable capturing variation within each skill, and a low-level latent-conditioned controller that executes motor primitives. The model will be trained on offline datasets of state-action trajectories using a variational inference approach, optimizing the evidence lower bound (ELBO) with KL-regularization terms to encourage structured latent representations. Information asymmetry will be employed by providing different subsets of state information to each hierarchy level, ensuring that higher levels focus on abstract behaviors while lower levels handle detailed motor control. After offline training, the learned skill hierarchy will be transferred to reinforcement learning agents by freezing lower levels and learning new high-level controllers, either over discrete skills or continuous latent mixtures, with KL-regularization to maintain proximity to the offline-learned skill priors.
c85662dcd17eed4452019b640a30a323970472ef.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in MuJoCo-based robotic manipulation environments using a Sawyer arm and multiple object sets of varying geometric complexity, following established stacking benchmarks. Two offline datasets will be used: one for simple stacking tasks and another covering all pairwise stacking combinations across diverse object sets. The method will be compared against several baselines, including learning from scratch, Neural Probabilistic Motor Primitives (NPMP) with KL-regularization, behavior cloning (BC) with and without hierarchical structure, and asymmetric actor-critic approaches for vision-based transfer. Evaluation metrics will include sample efficiency, asymptotic performance, and state space coverage, with additional analysis of skill interpretability, directed exploration, and performance in dense, staged sparse, and fully sparse reward settings. Ablation studies will assess the contributions of discrete and continuous latent components, as well as the impact of KL-regularization.
c85662dcd17eed4452019b640a30a323970472ef.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel three-level hierarchical latent mixture policy that explicitly models both discrete and continuous behavioral structure, enabling the decomposition of offline data into distinct, reusable skills. Unlike prior two-level or purely discrete/continuous methods, this framework captures complementary advantages of both representations and supports flexible transfer to new tasks, objects, and sensory modalities. The method demonstrates superior sample efficiency and performance, particularly in sparse-reward scenarios, by facilitating directed exploration through abstract skill reuse. Extensive analysis and ablations provide new insights into the benefits of hierarchical skill structure and the conditions under which such skills are most effective.

c86fd4e03954f6ed32a37bff08bdb8148ecedd01.title: Multi-Mode Online Knowledge Distillation for Self-Supervised Visual Representation Learning
c86fd4e03954f6ed32a37bff08bdb8148ecedd01.research_question: How can self-supervised visual representation learning be improved for both small and large models by enabling collaborative, bidirectional knowledge transfer between heterogeneous or homogeneous models, rather than relying on traditional unidirectional knowledge distillation from a static teacher to a student?
c86fd4e03954f6ed32a37bff08bdb8148ecedd01.hypothesis: Collaborative, online knowledge distillation between two models—incorporating both self-distillation and cross-distillation with a cross-attention feature search strategy—will enable mutual knowledge transfer, leading to improved self-supervised visual representation learning for both models, regardless of their architecture or size.
c86fd4e03954f6ed32a37bff08bdb8148ecedd01.proposed_method: A novel Multi-Mode Online Knowledge Distillation (MOKD) framework is proposed, wherein two different models are trained collaboratively in a self-supervised manner. The approach incorporates two distinct distillation modes: self-distillation, where each model independently learns representations using a contrastive self-supervised objective (based on DINO), and cross-distillation, where knowledge is exchanged between the two models. Cross-distillation leverages both MLP-based and Transformer-based (T-Head) projection heads, with the T-Head employing a cross-attention feature search strategy to enhance semantic alignment and adaptively transfer relevant features between models. The overall loss for each model is a weighted sum of self-distillation and cross-distillation losses, with hyperparameters controlling the contribution of each. Training is performed online, with both models and their momentum (EMA) versions updated simultaneously, and the method is applicable to both heterogeneous (e.g., CNN and ViT) and homogeneous model pairs.
c86fd4e03954f6ed32a37bff08bdb8148ecedd01.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale image datasets such as ImageNet and its subsets, as well as transfer learning benchmarks like CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. Both heterogeneous (e.g., ResNet50/101 with ViT-Small/Base) and homogeneous (e.g., ResNet-ResNet, ViT-ViT) model pairs will be evaluated. Baselines will include independently trained models using DINO, as well as state-of-the-art self-supervised learning (SSL) and self-supervised knowledge distillation (SSL-KD) methods such as SEED, DisCo, MCL, and ReKD. Evaluation metrics will include k-NN and linear probing accuracy for representation quality, as well as downstream task performance on object detection and instance segmentation (using COCO with Mask R-CNN), and semi-supervised learning protocols (1% and 10% ImageNet subsets). Ablation studies will analyze the impact of each loss component and hyperparameter, and additional analyses will include feature visualization and attention distance metrics.
c86fd4e03954f6ed32a37bff08bdb8148ecedd01.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a multi-mode, online knowledge distillation framework that enables bidirectional, collaborative self-supervised learning between two models, rather than the traditional unidirectional, static-teacher paradigm. A novel cross-attention feature search strategy within the Transformer-based projection head is developed to enhance semantic feature alignment and adaptively transfer relevant knowledge. The approach is generalizable to both heterogeneous and homogeneous model pairs and demonstrates state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of tasks and architectures. Extensive experiments show that both models in the pair benefit from mutual knowledge transfer, outperforming independently trained baselines and existing SSL-KD methods.

c871377b208814713c18e25633866323a2982136.title: Proving Test Set Contamination in Black Box Language Models
c871377b208814713c18e25633866323a2982136.research_question: How can test set contamination in black-box language models be provably detected without access to pretraining data or model weights, and what are the statistical guarantees and practical limitations of such detection methods?
c871377b208814713c18e25633866323a2982136.hypothesis: It is possible to provably identify test set contamination in black-box language models by exploiting statistical properties of exchangeable datasets, specifically by detecting violations in permutation invariance of log-likelihoods assigned to different orderings of a benchmark dataset.
c871377b208814713c18e25633866323a2982136.proposed_method: A novel statistical test will be developed to detect test set contamination in language models accessible only via log-likelihood queries. The method leverages the property of exchangeability in benchmark datasets, where all permutations of the dataset should be equally likely under non-contaminated models. The approach involves comparing the log-likelihood assigned by the model to the canonical (public) ordering of a dataset with the log-likelihoods assigned to multiple randomly shuffled orderings. A sharded likelihood comparison test will be implemented, partitioning the dataset into contiguous shards, permuting within each shard, and aggregating the differences in log-likelihoods using a t-test to assess statistical significance. This approach is computationally efficient, allows parallelization, and provides asymptotic false positive rate guarantees under the null hypothesis of no contamination.
c871377b208814713c18e25633866323a2982136.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by training a 1.4 billion parameter GPT-2 style language model on a mixture of Wikipedia and intentionally injected benchmark test sets (e.g., BoolQ, HellaSwag, OpenbookQA, MNLI, NaturalQuestions, TruthfulQA, PIQA, MMLU). Each test set will be subsampled to around 1000 examples and duplicated at varying rates to simulate different contamination scenarios. The sharded likelihood comparison test will be evaluated for sensitivity to duplication rate, number of shards, and number of permutations per shard. Further, the method will be applied to audit several public language models (LLaMA2-7B, Mistral-7B, Pythia-1.4B, GPT-2 XL, BioMedLM) for contamination on eight public benchmarks, using 50 shards and up to 250 permutations per shard. Evaluation metrics include p-values from the statistical test, with significance assessed at standard thresholds (e.g., 0.05), and negative controls (such as BioMedLM) will be used to validate the specificity of the test.
c871377b208814713c18e25633866323a2982136.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a provable, statistically grounded method for detecting test set contamination in black-box language models using only log-likelihood queries, without requiring access to training data or model weights. By exploiting the exchangeability property of datasets, the method provides rigorous false positive rate guarantees. The sharded likelihood comparison test improves both computational efficiency and statistical power over naive permutation tests, enabling detection of contamination even in small datasets and at low duplication rates. The release of pre-trained models with known contamination and a public benchmark supports further research and development of contamination detection methods.

c896257eea2cb25dc36dfc4d0d1f8812e68c8ce3.title: Repurposing Diffusion-Based Image Generators for Monocular Depth Estimation
c896257eea2cb25dc36dfc4d0d1f8812e68c8ce3.research_question: Can the rich visual priors encoded in large-scale diffusion-based image generators be effectively repurposed to enable robust, generalizable monocular depth estimation from a single image, especially in zero-shot and cross-domain scenarios?
c896257eea2cb25dc36dfc4d0d1f8812e68c8ce3.hypothesis: A pretrained diffusion-based image generator, when fine-tuned with a carefully designed protocol and synthetic RGB-D data, can serve as a highly generalizable and state-of-the-art monocular depth estimator, leveraging its extensive visual knowledge to outperform existing methods even without exposure to real-world depth data.
c896257eea2cb25dc36dfc4d0d1f8812e68c8ce3.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that adapts a pretrained latent diffusion model (LDM), specifically Stable Diffusion v2, for monocular depth estimation. The approach involves freezing the original VAE encoder and decoder, and fine-tuning only the denoising U-Net to predict affine-invariant depth maps conditioned on an input image. Both the RGB image and its corresponding depth map are encoded into the latent space, with the depth map replicated across channels to match the VAE input requirements. The U-Net is modified to accept concatenated latent codes, and fine-tuning is performed using a standard diffusion noise objective with a combination of multi-resolution and annealed noise schedules. Depth normalization ensures affine invariance, and training is conducted exclusively on high-quality, dense synthetic datasets to avoid the pitfalls of noisy or incomplete real-world depth data.
c896257eea2cb25dc36dfc4d0d1f8812e68c8ce3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by fine-tuning the model on synthetic datasets such as Hypersim (indoor scenes) and Virtual KITTI (outdoor scenes), totaling approximately 74,000 samples. Evaluation will be performed on five real-world datasets (NYUv2, KITTI, ETH3D, ScanNet, DIODE) that are not seen during training, covering both indoor and outdoor environments. The method will be benchmarked against state-of-the-art baselines including MiDaS, LeReS, Omnidata, HDN, DPT, and DiverseDepth, using affine-invariant evaluation metrics such as Absolute Mean Relative Error (AbsRel) and delta1 accuracy. The experimental setup includes zero-shot transfer testing, ablations on training noise and data domains, and test-time ensembling to assess robustness and performance gains.
c896257eea2cb25dc36dfc4d0d1f8812e68c8ce3.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple and resource-efficient fine-tuning protocol that transforms a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model into a state-of-the-art monocular depth estimator using only synthetic data. It achieves excellent zero-shot generalization to real-world datasets without ever seeing real depth maps, outperforming prior methods in both indoor and outdoor scenarios. The approach leverages the comprehensive visual priors of foundation diffusion models, and demonstrates that such models can be efficiently adapted for dense prediction tasks like depth estimation with minimal computational resources and data requirements. Additional innovations include the use of multi-resolution and annealed noise during training, affine-invariant depth normalization, and a robust test-time ensembling scheme.

c8d78956db5c1efd83fa890fd1aafbc16aa2364b.title: Quantum variational algorithms are swamped with traps
c8d78956db5c1efd83fa890fd1aafbc16aa2364b.research_question: Are variational quantum algorithms (VQAs), particularly shallow and local models, generally trainable, and what are the fundamental obstacles to their optimization and learning performance?
c8d78956db5c1efd83fa890fd1aafbc16aa2364b.hypothesis: Shallow, local variational quantum algorithms are generally untrainable due to the prevalence of poor local minima in their loss landscapes, and noisy optimization of a wide variety of quantum models is infeasible with a sub-exponential number of queries.
c8d78956db5c1efd83fa890fd1aafbc16aa2364b.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical and empirical investigation will be conducted into the trainability of variational quantum algorithms. The approach will involve two main components: (1) analytical study of the optimization landscape of shallow, local VQAs using tools from random matrix theory and statistical query (SQ) learning frameworks, with particular focus on the distribution and concentration of local minima relative to the global minimum; (2) derivation of lower bounds on the number of statistical queries required for learning in the presence of noise, by analyzing the SQ dimension of function classes generated by shallow variational circuits. Additionally, the convergence of variational loss landscapes to Wishart hypertoroidal random fields (WHRFs) under local scrambling assumptions will be established, allowing inference about the critical point structure. Numerical simulations will be performed to validate theoretical predictions, including teacher-student setups and VQE tasks, using parameterized quantum circuits and gradient-based optimization.
c8d78956db5c1efd83fa890fd1aafbc16aa2364b.experiment_details: Experiments will include numerical simulations of quantum convolutional neural networks (QCNNs) and checkerboard ansatzes in teacher-student learning tasks, as well as variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) problems for finding ground states of local Hamiltonians. Simulations will be conducted for varying numbers of qubits (e.g., 4 to 24), with parameterized 2-qubit gates and analytic gradients, using optimizers such as Adam and vanilla gradient descent. The datasets will consist of randomly generated quantum circuits and Hamiltonians, with training and evaluation based on classification accuracy (for QCNNs) and loss/trace distance to the ground state (for VQE). Baselines will include varying circuit depths and parameter counts to assess the impact of overparameterization. Evaluation metrics will focus on convergence to global minima, distribution of final losses, and the fraction of runs achieving high accuracy or low energy.
c8d78956db5c1efd83fa890fd1aafbc16aa2364b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a rigorous analysis of the trainability of shallow, local variational quantum algorithms, extending beyond the well-studied barren plateau phenomenon to demonstrate the prevalence of poor local minima even in regimes with large gradients. It establishes, for the first time, that a superpolynomially small fraction of local minima are within any constant energy of the global minimum for a wide class of shallow VQAs, rendering them untrainable without good initialization. The work also provides new lower bounds on the statistical query complexity for learning quantum models under noise, showing that noisy optimization is infeasible with sub-exponential queries. The convergence of local VQA loss landscapes to Wishart hypertoroidal random fields is proven, connecting quantum optimization landscapes to random field theory. These results are validated by extensive numerical simulations, offering a comprehensive and previously unexplored perspective on the fundamental limitations of VQA trainability.

c8dc4af5c61f95cc79b7f83e8339efa62af8f811.title: Animate Anyone: Consistent and Controllable Image-to-Video Synthesis for Character Animation
c8dc4af5c61f95cc79b7f83e8339efa62af8f811.research_question: How can consistent and controllable character animation videos be synthesized from a single reference image and a sequence of driving poses, while maintaining high fidelity to the character's appearance and ensuring temporal stability across frames?
c8dc4af5c61f95cc79b7f83e8339efa62af8f811.hypothesis: Integrating a dedicated reference feature extraction network, spatial attention mechanisms, lightweight pose guidance, and temporal modeling into a diffusion-based image-to-video synthesis framework will enable the generation of temporally consistent, high-fidelity, and controllable character animation videos from arbitrary reference images and pose sequences.
c8dc4af5c61f95cc79b7f83e8339efa62af8f811.proposed_method: A novel diffusion-based framework is developed for pose-guided image-to-video synthesis, targeting character animation. The method extends the Stable Diffusion architecture by introducing a ReferenceNet, an asymmetrical UNet structure that extracts detailed spatial features from the reference image and injects them into the denoising UNet via spatial attention. A lightweight Pose Guider encodes pose skeleton images and aligns them with the noise latent, enabling precise and efficient pose control. Temporal consistency is achieved by integrating a temporal attention layer within the denoising UNet, allowing the model to capture inter-frame dependencies. The overall architecture leverages pretrained weights from Stable Diffusion and employs a two-stage training strategy: first training on individual frames to learn appearance and pose conditioning, then fine-tuning temporal layers on multi-frame video clips for smooth motion.
c8dc4af5c61f95cc79b7f83e8339efa62af8f811.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using a proprietary dataset of 5,000 character video clips for generalization, as well as three public benchmarks: UBC Fashion Video, TikTok Dance, and Ted-talk datasets. The model is trained in two stages: single-frame training for 30,000 steps with a batch size of 64 at 768x768 resolution, followed by temporal layer training on 24-frame sequences for 10,000 steps with a batch size of 4. Baselines include state-of-the-art image animation and image-to-video methods such as DreamPose, DisCo, AnimateDiff, Gen-2, MRAA, TPSMM, BDMM, FOMM, and SD-I2V (a combination of Stable Diffusion, ControlNet, IP-Adapter, and AnimateDiff). Evaluation metrics comprise image-level SSIM, PSNR, LPIPS, and video-level FVD. Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of ReferenceNet, temporal modeling, and training strategies.
c8dc4af5c61f95cc79b7f83e8339efa62af8f811.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces ReferenceNet, a dedicated feature extractor for reference images that preserves fine-grained appearance details through spatial attention integration with the denoising UNet. The method achieves controllable and temporally stable character animation via a lightweight pose guider and a temporal attention mechanism, all within a diffusion-based framework. Unlike prior methods, this approach enables generalizable, high-fidelity animation of arbitrary characters without domain constraints, and demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks. Ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of the architectural innovations in detail preservation, temporal consistency, and training efficiency.

c8e59a9d0acd91d0cf68b63d7c84127dd63d1cec.title: One-step differentiation of iterative algorithms
c8e59a9d0acd91d0cf68b63d7c84127dd63d1cec.research_question: How can the differentiation of iterative algorithms be made both computationally efficient and easy to implement, particularly in the context of machine learning and bilevel optimization problems?
c8e59a9d0acd91d0cf68b63d7c84127dd63d1cec.hypothesis: One-step differentiation, which only differentiates the last iteration of an iterative process, provides a computationally efficient and sufficiently accurate approximation of the true Jacobian for fast-converging algorithms, and can be implemented as easily as automatic differentiation within standard frameworks.
c8e59a9d0acd91d0cf68b63d7c84127dd63d1cec.proposed_method: A novel one-step differentiation approach is proposed, in which only the final iteration of an iterative algorithm is differentiated, while all previous iterations are treated as constants using a stop_gradient primitive. This method leverages native automatic differentiation tools, requiring no custom Jacobian-vector or vector-Jacobian product implementations, and is compatible with any framework supporting stop_gradient. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to derive approximation bounds for the one-step Jacobian estimator, with particular attention to linearly, superlinearly, and quadratically convergent algorithms. The method will also be extended to hypergradient computation in bilevel optimization, and its complexity will be compared to automatic and implicit differentiation both analytically and empirically.
c8e59a9d0acd91d0cf68b63d7c84127dd63d1cec.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several optimization problems, including Newton's method for regularized logistic regression, an interior point solver for quadratic programming, and weighted ridge regression solved by gradient descent. Synthetic datasets with varying sizes and condition numbers will be generated, and the cpusmall dataset from LibSVM will be used for benchmarking. The proposed one-step differentiation method will be compared against full automatic differentiation and implicit differentiation baselines. Evaluation metrics will include computational time, memory usage, and the accuracy of the estimated Jacobian or hypergradient, as well as the optimality gap for both iterates and Jacobians. Implementation will utilize differentiable programming frameworks such as JAX, leveraging their automatic differentiation and stop_gradient capabilities.
c8e59a9d0acd91d0cf68b63d7c84127dd63d1cec.novelty_claims: The proposed method offers a general, easy-to-implement, and computationally efficient alternative to both automatic and implicit differentiation for iterative algorithms. It provides a unified theoretical approximation analysis for the one-step Jacobian estimator, including explicit error bounds and convergence results for a broad class of algorithms. The approach achieves accuracy comparable to implicit differentiation for fast (superlinear or quadratic) algorithms, but with the simplicity and transparency of automatic differentiation. The method is demonstrated to be effective for hypergradient computation in bilevel optimization and is validated on a diverse set of numerical experiments, showing significant computational advantages and practical accuracy.

c8e7303cfc13217d8daadbce8818a24cdb1d8073.title: Parallel MCMC algorithms: theoretical foundations, algorithm design, case studies
c8e7303cfc13217d8daadbce8818a24cdb1d8073.research_question: How can a unified theoretical and algorithmic framework for parallel (multiproposal) Markov Chain Monte Carlo (pMCMC) algorithms be developed to enable efficient, unbiased, and reversible sampling from complex, high- and infinite-dimensional probability distributions, while leveraging modern high-performance computing architectures?
c8e7303cfc13217d8daadbce8818a24cdb1d8073.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a measure-theoretic, extended phase space formalism can be constructed to rigorously characterize and generalize pMCMC algorithms, enabling the derivation of new, efficient, and theoretically justified multiproposal MCMC methods—including those suitable for high- and infinite-dimensional targets—while maintaining ergodicity, reversibility, and computational scalability.
c8e7303cfc13217d8daadbce8818a24cdb1d8073.proposed_method: A rigorous, measure-theoretic framework will be established for pMCMC algorithms, situating multiproposal Markov transition kernels within an extended phase space. The approach will define general criteria for proposal mechanisms and acceptance probabilities that guarantee ergodicity and reversibility with respect to a target measure. The framework will encompass both random walk and Hamiltonian-type proposals, as well as structured proposal clouds and resampling strategies. Special attention will be given to 'conditionally independent' proposal kernels, enabling the derivation of Barker-type and Metropolis-Hastings-type acceptance rules that are unbiased for a broad class of target measures. The methodology will further extend to allow for multiple jumps between proposals within each iteration, and will be instantiated in concrete algorithms such as multiproposal preconditioned Crank-Nicolson (mpCN) samplers suitable for high- and infinite-dimensional settings.
c8e7303cfc13217d8daadbce8818a24cdb1d8073.experiment_details: Numerical case studies will be conducted to evaluate the efficacy and scalability of the proposed pMCMC algorithms. Experiments will include parallelization studies using TensorFlow and GPU hardware, scaling up to 100,000 proposals per iteration, and measuring wall time and sampling efficiency across increasing target dimensionality and multimodal distributions. The mpCN algorithm will be applied to Bayesian statistical inversion problems for partial differential equations, including both finite- and infinite-dimensional parameter spaces motivated by fluid measurement. Datasets will comprise synthetic inverse problems such as estimation of antisymmetric matrix coefficients, divergence-free fluid flow fields, and fluid domain shape estimation, each presenting complex, non-Gaussian, and high-dimensional posteriors. Baselines will include standard, single-proposal MCMC methods, and evaluation metrics will focus on sampling efficiency, mixing rates, computational speedup, and accuracy of posterior estimation.
c8e7303cfc13217d8daadbce8818a24cdb1d8073.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified, measure-theoretic foundation for pMCMC algorithms, generalizing and rigorously justifying multiproposal acceptance mechanisms—including Barker-type rules—across general state spaces. The framework enables the principled design of new algorithms, such as multiproposal versions of the preconditioned Crank-Nicolson sampler, that are provably reversible and unbiased for high- and infinite-dimensional targets. The approach also systematically incorporates structured proposal clouds, resampling, and multiple inter-proposal jumps, and demonstrates natural compatibility with modern parallel and high-performance computing architectures. These innovations provide both theoretical and practical advances over existing single-proposal and ad hoc multiproposal MCMC methods.

c8f88063357e270fef070c6f19ff142ccc5cd10c.title: Towards Efficient and Scalable Sharpness-Aware Minimization
c8f88063357e270fef070c6f19ff142ccc5cd10c.research_question: How can the computational efficiency and scalability of sharpness-aware minimization techniques be improved for large-scale deep learning, particularly in large-batch training scenarios such as Vision Transformers, without sacrificing generalization performance?
c8f88063357e270fef070c6f19ff142ccc5cd10c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by decomposing the update direction of sharpness-aware minimization into components and reusing the direction that biases towards flatter regions across multiple iterations, the computational overhead can be significantly reduced while maintaining similar generalization and accuracy gains as the original method. Furthermore, incorporating a layer-wise scaling rule for weight perturbations will enable effective large-batch training and further enhance scalability.
c8f88063357e270fef070c6f19ff142ccc5cd10c.proposed_method: A novel optimizer, LookSAM, will be developed to accelerate sharpness-aware minimization by periodically computing the adversarial perturbation (inner gradient ascent) and reusing the component of the update direction that biases learning towards flatter regions. The method decomposes the SAM gradient into two parts: one parallel to the standard gradient descent direction and another orthogonal component that encourages flat minima. The orthogonal component, which changes slowly across iterations, will be reused in intermediate steps, while the full SAM computation is performed only every k steps. Additionally, a layer-wise extension (Look-LayerSAM) will be proposed, where the perturbation is adaptively scaled for each layer using a norm-based scaling matrix, addressing instability in large-batch training. The approach will be implemented with adaptive hyperparameters controlling the reuse frequency and scaling intensity.
c8f88063357e270fef070c6f19ff142ccc5cd10c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-1k datasets, using models such as ResNet-18, ResNet-50, WideResNet-28-10, and various Vision Transformer (ViT) architectures. The proposed methods will be compared against baselines including standard SGD/AdamW, vanilla SAM, and a naive periodic-SAM (SAM-k). Evaluation metrics will include top-1 accuracy and training time per epoch, with a particular focus on large-batch settings (up to 64k batch size) and distributed training using TPUs. Additional experiments will incorporate data augmentation techniques such as RandAug and Mixup. Hyperparameter sensitivity analyses will be performed for the reuse weight and perturbation intensity. Layer-wise scaling will be evaluated for its impact on stability and scalability in large-batch regimes.
c8f88063357e270fef070c6f19ff142ccc5cd10c.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a novel framework for efficient sharpness-aware minimization by reusing the direction that biases towards flatter regions, reducing the need for costly inner maximization at every step. The method achieves computational complexity comparable to first-order optimizers while maintaining the accuracy and generalization benefits of SAM. The layer-wise extension enables, for the first time, successful scaling of Vision Transformer training to batch sizes as large as 64k, with significant speedup (up to 8×) over previous methods and state-of-the-art training times. The approach provides a principled solution to large-batch training challenges, outperforming heuristic tuning and existing adaptive optimizers.

c90a99eeb57019732a6cc996bb9eaf13faedf00f.title: In-context Learning and Induction Heads
c90a99eeb57019732a6cc996bb9eaf13faedf00f.research_question: What are the underlying mechanisms responsible for in-context learning in transformer language models, and to what extent do specific attention head circuits contribute to this phenomenon across model scales and architectures?
c90a99eeb57019732a6cc996bb9eaf13faedf00f.hypothesis: Induction heads, defined as specific attention head circuits that perform pattern completion via sequence copying, constitute the primary mechanism for the majority of in-context learning in transformer models of varying sizes.
c90a99eeb57019732a6cc996bb9eaf13faedf00f.proposed_method: The proposed research will systematically investigate the role of induction heads in in-context learning by combining mechanistic analysis, empirical observation, and targeted interventions across transformer models of different sizes and architectures. The approach involves training multiple transformer models (including attention-only and models with MLPs) and saving snapshots throughout training. Per-token loss analysis will be conducted using principal component analysis (PCA) on log-likelihood vectors across tokens to visualize and quantify training dynamics. Induction heads will be identified based on their empirical behavior in sequence copying tasks, specifically through prefix matching and copying metrics on random token sequences. The research will further employ architectural perturbations and direct ablations of attention heads to assess causal relationships between induction head formation and in-context learning.
c90a99eeb57019732a6cc996bb9eaf13faedf00f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of 34 transformer models varying in depth, width, and inclusion of MLP layers, trained on diverse language modeling datasets. Each model will be analyzed at multiple training checkpoints, with more than 50,000 attention head ablations performed to isolate the contribution of individual heads. In-context learning will be quantified by the difference in loss between the 500th and 50th token in a 512-token context, averaged over 10,000 random sequences. Baselines will include models with and without induction head ablations, as well as models with architectural modifications that inhibit induction head formation. Evaluation metrics will focus on in-context learning scores, induction head presence (via prefix matching and copying), and the correlation between these metrics across training and model scales.
c90a99eeb57019732a6cc996bb9eaf13faedf00f.novelty_claims: This research proposes a comprehensive, multi-pronged empirical and mechanistic investigation into the origins of in-context learning in transformer models, introducing the concept of induction heads as a unifying mechanistic explanation. The approach combines direct ablation, architectural perturbation, and large-scale per-token loss analysis to provide both causal and correlational evidence across model sizes. The work bridges microscopic circuit-level interpretability with macroscopic learning dynamics, offering new insights into phase transitions during training and their implications for model safety and generalization.

c92c1f35cf9dbe8ea30b2eb7e3ed2d99b202cb50.title: Right Time to Learn:Promoting Generalization via Bio-inspired Spacing Effect in Knowledge Distillation
c92c1f35cf9dbe8ea30b2eb7e3ed2d99b202cb50.research_question: How can the generalization ability of deep neural networks be improved through novel knowledge distillation paradigms inspired by biological learning mechanisms?
c92c1f35cf9dbe8ea30b2eb7e3ed2d99b202cb50.hypothesis: Incorporating a bio-inspired spacing effect—introducing controlled intervals between teacher and student learning steps—into knowledge distillation will promote convergence to flatter minima in the loss landscape, thereby enhancing the generalization performance of student models across various architectures and datasets.
c92c1f35cf9dbe8ea30b2eb7e3ed2d99b202cb50.proposed_method: A new knowledge distillation strategy, termed SpacedKD, will be developed by introducing a temporal spacing effect inspired by biological learning. In this approach, the teacher network is updated several steps ahead of the student, after which its parameters are frozen and used to guide the student over the same set of training batches. The interval between teacher and student updates is controlled by a hyperparameter (SpaceInterval), which can be tuned based on the dataset and model size. This method will be implemented for both online KD (where teacher and student are separate networks trained simultaneously) and self KD (where different layers of the same network act as teacher and student). Theoretical analysis will be conducted to connect the spacing effect with convergence to flatter minima, using the Hessian trace as a measure of loss landscape flatness.
c92c1f35cf9dbe8ea30b2eb7e3ed2d99b202cb50.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple image classification benchmarks, including CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, ImageNet-100, and ImageNet-1K, using both ResNet-based (ResNet-18, ResNet-50, ResNet-101) and transformer-based (DeiT-Tiny, PiT-Tiny) architectures. Baseline comparisons will include traditional online KD, self KD, and advanced KD methods such as TSB, CTKD, and LSKD. Evaluation metrics will primarily be top-1 classification accuracy, with additional robustness tests using image corruption (e.g., impulse noise, zoom blur) and adversarial attacks (e.g., BIM). The impact of different space intervals, loss functions, and training hyperparameters (learning rate, batch size) will be systematically analyzed. All experiments will be repeated three times for statistical reliability.
c92c1f35cf9dbe8ea30b2eb7e3ed2d99b202cb50.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a temporally spaced knowledge distillation paradigm inspired by the biological spacing effect, which is architecture- and algorithm-agnostic and can be plugged into existing KD frameworks. The approach is theoretically motivated by its connection to flatter loss landscapes and empirically validated to yield consistent improvements in generalization and robustness across diverse datasets, architectures, and KD methods. The method also identifies a critical period for applying the spacing effect, offering new insights into the temporal dynamics of effective knowledge transfer.

c935ad16b132f526b289e16e84d73c5821bfc100.title: Algorithms to estimate Shapley value feature attributions
c935ad16b132f526b289e16e84d73c5821bfc100.research_question: How can the estimation of Shapley value-based feature attributions for machine learning models be systematically analyzed, categorized, and improved in terms of theoretical soundness, computational efficiency, and practical utility?
c935ad16b132f526b289e16e84d73c5821bfc100.hypothesis: By disentangling the complexity of Shapley value estimation into the feature removal approach and the tractable estimation strategy, it is possible to develop a comprehensive framework that clarifies, compares, and improves existing and novel algorithms for feature attribution in machine learning models.
c935ad16b132f526b289e16e84d73c5821bfc100.proposed_method: A systematic framework will be developed to analyze and categorize algorithms for estimating Shapley value feature attributions based on two primary axes: (1) the method for removing feature information (e.g., baseline replacement, marginal sampling, conditional sampling), and (2) the estimation strategy for tractably approximating the Shapley value (e.g., model-agnostic sampling, model-specific analytic solutions). The approach will involve formalizing the coalitional game for each feature removal method, detailing the mathematical assumptions and implications, and mapping 24+ algorithms into this taxonomy. Both model-agnostic (e.g., KernelSHAP, IME, permutation, multilinear extension) and model-specific (e.g., LinearSHAP, TreeSHAP, DeepSHAP) strategies will be characterized, with explicit attention to their theoretical guarantees, computational complexity, and practical tradeoffs. Empirical benchmarking will be conducted to compare convergence properties, bias, and variance of estimation strategies under different removal approaches.
c935ad16b132f526b289e16e84d73c5821bfc100.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using a diverse set of machine learning models, including linear models, tree ensembles, and deep neural networks, trained on standard benchmark datasets such as tabular census data and image datasets. For each model type, multiple Shapley value estimation algorithms will be implemented, covering both model-agnostic and model-specific approaches. Baselines will include popular methods such as LIME, KernelSHAP, TreeSHAP, and DeepSHAP. Evaluation metrics will focus on computational efficiency (runtime, number of model evaluations), estimation accuracy (bias and variance relative to ground-truth or analytic solutions), and robustness to feature correlations. Special attention will be given to the impact of feature removal strategies (baseline, marginal, conditional) on attribution outcomes. The experimental setup will include systematic variation of parameters such as the number of baseline samples, similarity metrics for empirical estimation, and the use of synthetic data to control feature dependencies.
c935ad16b132f526b289e16e84d73c5821bfc100.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a unified, two-factor framework for analyzing and categorizing Shapley value feature attribution algorithms, enabling a principled comparison of 24+ distinct methods. It clarifies the theoretical and practical implications of different feature removal and estimation strategies, identifies gaps and inconsistencies in the literature, and provides empirical benchmarks that highlight tradeoffs in bias, variance, and computational efficiency. The work aims to guide both practitioners and researchers in selecting, implementing, and developing improved algorithms for interpretable machine learning.

c948e2d00ac2628ed4098a009c67c81ea4cc00a2.title: ColPali: Efficient Document Retrieval with Vision Language Models
c948e2d00ac2628ed4098a009c67c81ea4cc00a2.research_question: How can document retrieval systems be improved to efficiently and accurately retrieve visually rich documents by leveraging both visual and textual information, while maintaining low latency and high throughput suitable for industrial-scale applications?
c948e2d00ac2628ed4098a009c67c81ea4cc00a2.hypothesis: Directly embedding document pages as images using vision-language models, combined with a late interaction matching mechanism, will enable more efficient and accurate retrieval of visually rich documents compared to traditional text-centric or multimodal retrieval pipelines.
c948e2d00ac2628ed4098a009c67c81ea4cc00a2.proposed_method: A novel document retrieval framework will be developed that utilizes a vision-language model (VLM) to generate high-quality, multi-vector embeddings directly from images of document pages. The model architecture will extend a compact VLM (such as PaliGemma-3B) by adding a projection layer to map output token embeddings (from both text and image tokens) into a lower-dimensional space suitable for late interaction. The retrieval process will employ a late interaction operator, summing the maximum dot products between query and document embeddings, allowing fine-grained matching between query terms and image patches. The entire system will be trained end-to-end with a contrastive loss, using both real and synthetic query-page pairs, and will support efficient offline indexing and fast online querying. Techniques such as token pooling and query augmentation will be explored to optimize memory and performance trade-offs.
c948e2d00ac2628ed4098a009c67c81ea4cc00a2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the newly introduced ViDoRe benchmark, which covers a wide range of page-level document retrieval tasks across multiple domains (medical, business, scientific, administrative), modalities (text, figures, tables, infographics), and languages (English, French). The proposed method will be compared against strong baselines, including text-only retrieval (BM25, BGE-M3), multimodal pipelines with OCR and captioning, and state-of-the-art contrastive VLMs (JinaCLIP, NomicEmbedVision, SigLIP). Evaluation metrics will include nDCG@5, Recall@K, and MRR for retrieval performance, as well as latency and indexing throughput to assess practical efficiency. Ablation studies will investigate the impact of model size, number of image patches, query augmentation, and training data composition. Additional experiments will assess generalization to out-of-domain and multilingual tasks.
c948e2d00ac2628ed4098a009c67c81ea4cc00a2.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new paradigm for document retrieval by embedding entire document pages as images using vision-language models, bypassing complex and brittle text extraction pipelines. It pioneers the use of late interaction mechanisms for vision-based retrieval, enabling fine-grained matching between query tokens and image patches. The method achieves state-of-the-art retrieval performance on visually complex document benchmarks while drastically reducing indexing latency and simplifying the retrieval pipeline. The open release of the ViDoRe benchmark, models, and codebase further establishes a new standard for evaluating and developing visually rich document retrieval systems.

c94e49617f569204f989643e5462691b9b3a482b.title: Estimating Training Data Influence by Tracking Gradient Descent
c94e49617f569204f989643e5462691b9b3a482b.research_question: How can the influence of individual training examples on specific model predictions be efficiently and accurately estimated in machine learning models trained with stochastic gradient descent, regardless of architecture, domain, or task?
c94e49617f569204f989643e5462691b9b3a482b.hypothesis: A method that traces the evolution of the loss on a test point throughout the training process, by leveraging gradients, checkpoints, and loss functions, can provide a scalable, accurate, and generalizable estimate of the influence of training examples on model predictions.
c94e49617f569204f989643e5462691b9b3a482b.proposed_method: A novel framework, TracIn, is proposed to estimate the influence of a training example on a specific prediction by tracing how the loss on a test point changes during training whenever the example is used. The method is grounded in the fundamental theorem of calculus, decomposing the loss difference on a test point between the start and end of training via gradients along the optimization trajectory. A first-order gradient approximation is used to make the computation tractable, and practical scalability is achieved by leveraging saved checkpoints from standard training procedures, rather than requiring access to every training step. The method attributes influence by computing the dot product of gradients of the loss with respect to model parameters for both the training and test examples at various checkpoints, and summing these contributions across checkpoints and minibatches. The approach is agnostic to model architecture and can be applied to any model trained with stochastic gradient descent or its variants.
c94e49617f569204f989643e5462691b9b3a482b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple datasets and tasks, including image classification (CIFAR-10 with ResNet-56, MNIST with a three-layer neural network, and ImageNet with ResNet-50), text classification (DBPedia with a Simple Word-Embedding Model), and regression (California Housing Prices with a three-layer neural network). Baselines for comparison will include influence functions and representer point selection methods. Evaluation will focus on the identification of mislabeled training examples by measuring the fraction of mislabeled data recovered at various ranks, using metrics such as the fraction of mislabeled examples identified in the top-k ranked training points by self-influence. Additional analyses will examine the effect of different checkpoint selection strategies, the accuracy of first-order approximations, and the interpretability of influential examples. Experimental setups will include introducing controlled label noise, varying checkpoint intervals, and comparing influence estimates across model layers.
c94e49617f569204f989643e5462691b9b3a482b.novelty_claims: The proposed method offers a simple, scalable, and general approach to estimating training data influence that requires only access to gradients, checkpoints, and loss functions, without reliance on second-order optimality conditions or complex matrix inversions. It is architecture- and domain-agnostic, applicable to any model trained with stochastic gradient descent or its variants. The method provides practical advantages over prior approaches, including ease of implementation, computational efficiency, and the ability to attribute influence at any model layer. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior performance in identifying mislabeled data and providing interpretable insights into model behavior, with broad applicability across tasks and datasets.

c95244ea3ec82de5adc96fd3b96c0f59f5d1b1b2.title: Diffusion Models for Reinforcement Learning: A Survey
c95244ea3ec82de5adc96fd3b96c0f59f5d1b1b2.research_question: How can diffusion models be leveraged to address key challenges in reinforcement learning, such as restricted expressiveness, data scarcity, compounding error in model-based planning, and generalization in multitask learning, and what roles can diffusion models play across various RL-related tasks?
c95244ea3ec82de5adc96fd3b96c0f59f5d1b1b2.hypothesis: Diffusion models, due to their powerful and flexible distributional modeling capabilities, can enhance reinforcement learning by improving sample quality, training stability, expressiveness of policies, data augmentation, planning consistency, and generalization across tasks.
c95244ea3ec82de5adc96fd3b96c0f59f5d1b1b2.proposed_method: A comprehensive research program is proposed to systematically investigate the integration of diffusion models into reinforcement learning pipelines. The approach will involve developing and evaluating diffusion models as planners (for trajectory-level planning), as policy models (for action distribution modeling), and as data synthesizers (for dataset augmentation). Technical components will include implementing denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPM) and score-based generative models, employing guided sampling techniques (classifier-guided and classifier-free), and exploring fast sampling methods to ensure practical inference times. The methodology will also explore hierarchical and multitask extensions, safety-constrained sampling, and retrieval-augmented generation. Key steps will involve training diffusion models on RL datasets, conditioning on relevant state, action, and reward variables, and integrating learned models into RL algorithms for both offline and online settings.
c95244ea3ec82de5adc96fd3b96c0f59f5d1b1b2.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard RL benchmarks, including high-dimensional control tasks and multitask environments. Datasets such as D4RL and custom multitask offline RL datasets will be used. Baseline comparisons will include conventional RL algorithms (e.g., Q-learning, policy gradients), model-based RL with autoregressive planners, and generative models such as VAEs and GANs. Evaluation metrics will include cumulative reward, sample efficiency, policy expressiveness (e.g., multimodality of action distributions), planning consistency (temporal coherence), and generalization to new tasks. Additional experiments will assess the impact of diffusion-based data augmentation and the ability to handle safety constraints and rare events. Ablation studies will examine the effects of different sampling strategies, guidance mechanisms, and model architectures.
c95244ea3ec82de5adc96fd3b96c0f59f5d1b1b2.novelty_claims: The proposed research claims novelty in systematically exploring and categorizing the diverse roles of diffusion models within reinforcement learning, including as planners, policies, and data synthesizers. It introduces the application of advanced diffusion modeling techniques—such as guided sampling, hierarchical structures, and retrieval-augmented generation—to RL contexts. The approach aims to address longstanding RL challenges (expressiveness, data scarcity, compounding error, multitask generalization) with a unified generative modeling framework, and to pioneer new directions such as generative simulation, safety-constrained RL via conditional sampling, and skill composition through multimodal diffusion models.

c97b287498b16a332aeca2f80e739a436b3175e0.title: Guided Search Strategies in Non-Serializable Environments with Applications to Software Engineering Agents
c97b287498b16a332aeca2f80e739a436b3175e0.research_question: How can guided search strategies be designed and applied to improve the reliability and performance of autonomous agents operating in non-serializable environments, particularly for complex multi-step tasks in software engineering?
c97b287498b16a332aeca2f80e739a436b3175e0.hypothesis: Guided search strategies that leverage learned action-value functions—specifically, 1-step lookahead and trajectory selection—can significantly improve the average-case performance of agentic systems in non-serializable environments, narrowing the gap between average and best-case outcomes, even under constraints that preclude traditional search techniques.
c97b287498b16a332aeca2f80e739a436b3175e0.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves developing and evaluating two complementary guided search strategies suitable for non-serializable environments: (1) 1-step lookahead, where at each decision point, a set of candidate actions is sampled from a base policy, and the action with the highest predicted action-value (as estimated by a learned critic model) is selected; and (2) trajectory selection, where multiple complete trajectories are generated using the base policy, and the trajectory with the highest terminal action-value is chosen for execution. Both strategies rely on a critic model trained to estimate action-values, using a bootstrapped dataset of agent trajectories and temporal-difference learning (TD(λ)) to balance bias and variance in value estimation. The approach is designed to operate strictly forward in time, without the ability to rollback or branch, thus adhering to the constraints of non-serializable environments.
c97b287498b16a332aeca2f80e739a436b3175e0.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using the SWE-agent framework in the SWE-bench Verified benchmark, a challenging non-serializable environment based on Docker containers for automated software engineering tasks. The main evaluation metric is Success Rate (SR), defined as the percentage of problems solved. The base policy is a fine-tuned Qwen2.5-72B language model, and the critic is initialized from LLaMA3.1-70B and trained on 80,000 positive and negative trajectories collected via bootstrapping. Baselines include the base policy without guided search, as well as state-of-the-art open-weight and proprietary models. Experiments systematically vary the number of action candidates (K), the number of trajectories (N), and other hyperparameters such as sampling temperature and TD(λ) parameters. Statistical significance is assessed by running each configuration multiple times with different random seeds and reporting mean SR and standard error. Additional experiments test the transferability of the approach to proprietary models like GPT-4o.
c97b287498b16a332aeca2f80e739a436b3175e0.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces and formalizes the concept of non-serializable reinforcement learning environments and systematically studies guided search strategies that are feasible under such constraints. It claims the development of two practical and effective guided search operators—1-step lookahead and trajectory selection—guided by learned action-value functions, which are shown to significantly improve agent performance in non-serializable settings. The approach achieves state-of-the-art results for open-weight models on SWE-bench Verified and demonstrates transferability to closed-source models. The work also provides insights into training robust critic models and offers practical guidelines for balancing computational cost with performance gains.

c983653841b6987d9959318f074a595783838576.title: On the Convergence of Adam and Beyond
c983653841b6987d9959318f074a595783838576.research_question: How can the convergence issues observed in popular adaptive stochastic optimization algorithms, such as ADAM and RMSPROP, be addressed to ensure reliable optimization performance in both convex and nonconvex settings, particularly in high-dimensional and deep learning applications?
c983653841b6987d9959318f074a595783838576.hypothesis: Adaptive optimization algorithms that incorporate long-term memory of past gradients, rather than relying solely on exponential moving averages over a fixed window, will achieve guaranteed convergence and improved empirical performance compared to existing methods like ADAM and RMSPROP.
c983653841b6987d9959318f074a595783838576.proposed_method: A novel adaptive optimization algorithm, AMSGRAD, will be developed to address the convergence failures of exponential moving average-based methods. AMSGRAD modifies the update rule by maintaining the maximum of all past squared gradient estimates (v_t) and using this maximum for normalization, ensuring a non-increasing step size and preventing the learning rate from increasing unexpectedly. The algorithm will be implemented with the same computational and memory efficiency as ADAM, and will include theoretical convergence analysis in the convex setting, providing data-dependent regret bounds. Additionally, an alternative approach, ADAMNC, will be explored, which employs a non-constant schedule for the exponential averaging parameters to guarantee convergence without altering the algorithm's structure.
c983653841b6987d9959318f074a595783838576.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets to evaluate the proposed methods. Synthetic experiments will use carefully constructed convex and stochastic optimization problems designed to expose the non-convergence behavior of ADAM, with performance measured by average regret and parameter convergence. Real-world experiments will include multiclass classification tasks using logistic regression (convex) and neural networks (nonconvex) on the MNIST dataset, as well as training a convolutional neural network (CIFARNET) on the CIFAR-10 dataset. Baselines will include ADAM and, where appropriate, other adaptive methods. Evaluation metrics will include training and test loss, accuracy, and convergence speed, with hyperparameters selected via grid search and consistent minibatch sizes across methods.
c983653841b6987d9959318f074a595783838576.novelty_claims: The proposed approach identifies and rigorously analyzes a fundamental flaw in the convergence behavior of popular adaptive methods such as ADAM and RMSPROP, providing explicit examples and theoretical proofs of non-convergence. AMSGRAD introduces a principled modification that guarantees convergence while retaining the practical benefits of adaptive methods, and is accompanied by theoretical regret bounds. The work also explores alternative parameter scheduling strategies (ADAMNC) for further robustness. Empirical results demonstrate that the proposed methods not only fix convergence issues but also often yield improved or more robust performance compared to existing algorithms.

c98ab919b0d76e080df50e0e718cd43f7547b683.title: An Optimal Discriminator Weighted Imitation Perspective for Reinforcement Learning
c98ab919b0d76e080df50e0e718cd43f7547b683.research_question: How can reinforcement learning algorithms be improved to more effectively learn optimal policies from offline datasets, particularly in the presence of suboptimal or corrupted data, by leveraging visitation distribution ratios and imitation learning perspectives?
c98ab919b0d76e080df50e0e718cd43f7547b683.hypothesis: Iteratively refining the offline dataset using corrected visitation distribution ratios and applying discriminator-weighted imitation learning will enable reinforcement learning algorithms to break the regularization barrier, resulting in improved policy performance and stability compared to existing Primal-RL and Dual-RL methods, especially on challenging or corrupted datasets.
c98ab919b0d76e080df50e0e718cd43f7547b683.proposed_method: A new algorithm, Iterative Dual Reinforcement Learning (IDRL), is proposed to address limitations in current Dual-RL methods regarding accurate estimation of the state-action visitation distribution ratio. The approach begins by using a semi-gradient Dual-RL method to estimate the action distribution ratio, then applies an off-policy evaluation-based correction to recover the true visitation distribution ratio. This corrected ratio is used to filter the offline dataset, removing suboptimal transitions with zero weights. The process is repeated iteratively: after each iteration, Dual-RL is rerun on the refined dataset, progressively moving the visitation distribution closer to the optimal. The final policy is extracted via weighted behavior cloning using the optimal visitation distribution ratio obtained from the last iteration. The method is theoretically justified with performance bounds and guarantees monotonic improvement with each iteration.
c98ab919b0d76e080df50e0e718cd43f7547b683.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of offline RL benchmarks, including D4RL Mujoco locomotion tasks, Antmaze navigation tasks, and Kitchen manipulation tasks, as well as on more realistic corrupted demonstration datasets where expert and random trajectories are mixed. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art Primal-RL methods (e.g., TD3+BC, CQL, ReBRAC, Diffusion-QL) and Dual-RL methods (e.g., IQL, SQL, O-DICE), as well as filtered behavior cloning baselines (X%-BC). Evaluation metrics will primarily be normalized return scores, with results averaged over multiple random seeds to assess stability. Ablation studies will be performed to isolate the effects of the iterative procedure and the use of visitation versus action distribution ratios. Additional experiments will test robustness on datasets with high proportions of suboptimal or noisy data.
c98ab919b0d76e080df50e0e718cd43f7547b683.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a principled iterative self-distillation framework that corrects the visitation distribution ratio in Dual-RL and uses it to refine the offline dataset, enabling the learning of near-optimal policies even from corrupted or suboptimal data. Unlike previous approaches, this method provides a theoretically justified curriculum of dataset filtering, guarantees monotonic policy improvement, and does not require additional hyperparameters for regularization. The approach is lightweight compared to generative model-based methods and demonstrates superior stability and robustness across diverse offline RL tasks.

c994e32622c0b888769ca904b64eb27f902d5a7c.title: Compositional Score Modeling for Simulation-Based Inference
c994e32622c0b888769ca904b64eb27f902d5a7c.research_question: How can simulation-based inference be improved to efficiently and accurately estimate posterior distributions conditioned on multiple observations, while minimizing simulator calls and avoiding the limitations of standard inference methods?
c994e32622c0b888769ca904b64eb27f902d5a7c.hypothesis: A compositional score modeling approach that factorizes the posterior over individual or small subsets of observations, and aggregates learned score functions, will enable efficient and robust simulation-based inference for arbitrary numbers of observations, outperforming existing neural posterior and likelihood estimation methods, especially in sample efficiency and handling multimodality.
c994e32622c0b888769ca904b64eb27f902d5a7c.proposed_method: The proposed approach introduces a framework based on conditional score modeling, specifically leveraging diffusion models to approximate the gradients (scores) of diffused posterior distributions. The method constructs a sequence of bridging densities that factorize over individual (or small subsets of) observations, enabling the training of a single score network on samples from the simulator with only one observation per parameter setting. At inference time, the method aggregates the outputs of the score network for each observation and uses an annealed Langevin dynamics sampler to generate approximate samples from the target posterior. The framework is generalized to a family of methods (PF-NPSE) that interpolate between fully factorized (one observation per score) and non-factorized (all observations jointly) approaches, allowing a trade-off between sample efficiency and error accumulation. The approach is compatible with permutation-invariant architectures to handle varying numbers of observations and can be adapted to models with constrained priors via reparameterization.
c994e32622c0b888769ca904b64eb27f902d5a7c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of benchmark tasks commonly used in simulation-based inference, including Gaussian/Gaussian, Gaussian/Mixture of Gaussians, Susceptible-Infected-Recovered (SIR), Lotka–Volterra, and the Weinberg simulator. Each method will be evaluated under varying simulator call budgets (e.g., 1,000 to 30,000) and with different numbers of conditioning observations at inference time. Baseline comparisons will include Neural Posterior Estimation (NPE), Neural Likelihood Estimation (NLE), and Neural Ratio Estimation (NRE), using consistent architectures and training budgets. Evaluation metrics will include squared Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) between true and approximate posteriors, as well as classifier two-sample tests. Robustness will be assessed with respect to score network parameterization, Langevin sampler hyperparameters, and the value of the subset size parameter m for PF-NPSE.
c994e32622c0b888769ca904b64eb27f902d5a7c.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel compositional score modeling framework for simulation-based inference that enables efficient aggregation of arbitrary numbers of observations at inference time with minimal simulation cost. Unlike prior approaches, it avoids the limitations of standard inference algorithms (such as MCMC or variational inference) by using score-based generative modeling and annealed Langevin dynamics for sampling. The factorized construction of bridging densities allows for sample-efficient training and robust handling of multimodal posteriors. The generalization to partially factorized methods provides a tunable trade-off between sample efficiency and error accumulation, and empirical results demonstrate superior or competitive performance compared to existing neural inference baselines.

c99da279368dffea1513351b027054edcddb7ebc.title: Mirror, Mirror of the Flow: How Does Regularization Shape Implicit Bias?
c99da279368dffea1513351b027054edcddb7ebc.research_question: How does explicit regularization interact with and shape the implicit bias in overparameterized models during training, and how can this interplay be leveraged to improve generalization and control the geometry of training dynamics?
c99da279368dffea1513351b027054edcddb7ebc.hypothesis: Explicit regularization, when integrated into the mirror flow framework, can systematically modulate the type, position, and range of implicit bias in overparameterized models, and dynamic schedules of regularization (such as switching off weight decay during training) can lead to improved generalization by exploiting the lasting effects of past regularization.
c99da279368dffea1513351b027054edcddb7ebc.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed that integrates explicit regularization into the mirror flow dynamics of optimization, allowing for both constant and dynamic regularization schedules. The approach will characterize the effects of explicit regularization on the geometry of the training dynamics by analyzing the time-dependent Legendre (Bregman) function associated with the mirror flow. Sufficient conditions for the reparameterization and regularizer will be established to ensure convergence and optimality, and a systematic procedure will be provided for identifying appropriate explicit regularizers for a given model architecture. The framework will be applied to a broad class of problems, including sparse coding, matrix sensing, single-layer attention, and LoRA, with a focus on three key effects: positional bias, type of bias, and range shrinking. Theoretical results will be complemented by a geometric interpretation, and dynamic regularization strategies such as turning off weight decay at specific training stages will be explored.
c99da279368dffea1513351b027054edcddb7ebc.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several representative tasks: (1) matrix sensing with a sparse ground truth, using quadratic reparameterization and comparing the effects of constant versus dynamic weight decay (including switching off regularization mid-training) on recovery accuracy and sparsity; (2) fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) with LoRA on the tiny_shakespeare dataset, tracking the evolution of the nuclear-to-Frobenius norm ratio under different weight decay schedules; (3) fine-tuning of a pretrained Vision Transformer (ViT) on ImageNet, with dynamic weight decay schedules, measuring validation accuracy and sparsity metrics. Baselines will include linear reparameterizations with L1 regularization and constant weight decay. Evaluation metrics will include reconstruction error, sparsity (nuclear/Frobenius norm ratio), and test/validation accuracy. The experimental setup will be designed to demonstrate the lasting effect of dynamic regularization on the geometry of the solution and generalization performance.
c99da279368dffea1513351b027054edcddb7ebc.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a unified theoretical framework that explicitly characterizes the interplay between explicit regularization and implicit bias within the mirror flow paradigm, extending prior work by allowing for time-dependent (dynamic) regularization. It provides new geometric insights into how explicit regularization shapes the implicit bias, including positional bias, type of bias, and range shrinking. The approach establishes sufficient conditions for convergence and optimality in the presence of dynamic regularization, and offers a systematic method for designing regularizers for a wide range of architectures. The proposal also claims practical innovation by demonstrating that dynamic regularization schedules, such as switching off weight decay during training, can leverage the accumulated effects of regularization to improve generalization, a strategy validated across diverse tasks including sparse coding, matrix sensing, attention mechanisms, and LoRA-based fine-tuning.

c9b6d0db6c2bebe0bcf593d95bea0e62b2443ef3.title: The Effect of Sampling Temperature on Problem Solving in Large Language Models
c9b6d0db6c2bebe0bcf593d95bea0e62b2443ef3.research_question: How does the sampling temperature hyperparameter affect the problem-solving performance of large language models on multiple-choice question-and-answer (MCQA) tasks across different models, prompt-engineering techniques, and problem domains?
c9b6d0db6c2bebe0bcf593d95bea0e62b2443ef3.hypothesis: Changes in sampling temperature within a typical operational range (e.g., 0.0 to 1.0) do not have a statistically significant impact on the problem-solving accuracy of large language models on MCQA tasks.
c9b6d0db6c2bebe0bcf593d95bea0e62b2443ef3.proposed_method: A systematic empirical evaluation will be conducted by administering MCQA exams to a diverse set of large language models (LLMs) using a range of sampling temperatures. The study will utilize nine widely-used LLMs and five distinct prompt-engineering techniques, including baseline, domain expertise, self-recitation, chain-of-thought, and a composite prompt. For each model and prompt combination, MCQA problems will be drawn from standardized benchmarks spanning various domains and difficulty levels.
