Each LLM will be prompted to answer each question multiple times at each temperature setting, with all other sampling parameters held constant to isolate the effect of temperature. The primary outcome will be the correct-answer accuracy, with additional analysis of text variability using multiple similarity metrics.
c9b6d0db6c2bebe0bcf593d95bea0e62b2443ef3.experiment_details: Experiments will use two MCQA exam sets: a large 1,000-question set for detailed domain analysis and a smaller 100-question set for high-level comparisons across all models and prompts. Problems will be randomly sampled from ten established LLM benchmarks covering domains such as math, science, law, medicine, and language. Each combination of LLM, prompt, exam, and temperature will be tested with ten repeated attempts per question to compute average accuracy. Sampling temperature will be varied from 0.0 to 1.6 (with most experiments focusing on 0.0 to 1.0), and all other sampling parameters (e.g., top-k, top-p) will be fixed. Baseline comparisons will include different LLMs and prompt-engineering techniques, with evaluation metrics including mean accuracy and a suite of text similarity measures (Jaccard, BoW, TF-IDF, Levenshtein, BLEU, SBERT). Statistical significance of accuracy differences will be assessed using the Kruskal-Wallis test.
c9b6d0db6c2bebe0bcf593d95bea0e62b2443ef3.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a comprehensive and systematic investigation of the effect of sampling temperature on LLM problem-solving performance, addressing a gap in empirical evidence for best practices in prompt engineering and hyperparameter tuning. The study is novel in its breadth, covering multiple LLMs, prompt-engineering strategies, and problem domains, and in its use of rigorous statistical analysis. The findings are expected to inform practical guidelines for AI engineers and contribute to theoretical understanding of solution-space search and model hallucination in LLMs.

c9bdc9ad2c3cf3230ba9aac7b5783ab411f0d204.title: R3M: A Universal Visual Representation for Robot Manipulation
c9bdc9ad2c3cf3230ba9aac7b5783ab411f0d204.research_question: Can visual representations pre-trained on diverse human video data enable efficient and generalizable learning of downstream robotic manipulation tasks, particularly in low-data regimes and previously unseen environments?
c9bdc9ad2c3cf3230ba9aac7b5783ab411f0d204.hypothesis: A visual representation pre-trained on large-scale, diverse human video datasets using objectives that capture temporal dynamics, semantic relevance, and compactness will enable more data-efficient and generalizable policy learning for robotic manipulation tasks than existing visual representations or training from scratch.
c9bdc9ad2c3cf3230ba9aac7b5783ab411f0d204.proposed_method: A novel visual representation learning framework will be developed by pre-training an image encoder on the Ego4D human video dataset, which contains diverse egocentric videos annotated with natural language descriptions. The training objective will combine three components: (1) time-contrastive learning to ensure the embedding captures temporal dynamics relevant for physical interaction, (2) video-language alignment to encourage semantic relevance by aligning visual features with paired language annotations, and (3) L1 (and optionally L2) regularization to promote sparse and compact representations. The encoder will be based on a ResNet architecture and trained with Adam optimization, using random cropping as data augmentation. Once trained, the encoder will be used as a frozen perception module for downstream robot policy learning, where the learned embeddings are concatenated with robot proprioceptive data and fed into a policy network.
c9bdc9ad2c3cf3230ba9aac7b5783ab411f0d204.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across 12 simulated robot manipulation tasks in three benchmark environments: MetaWorld, Franka Kitchen, and Adroit. Each environment will provide multiple viewpoints and varying task parameters to test generalization. The evaluation will focus on data-efficient imitation learning using behavior cloning, with the pre-trained visual representation kept frozen and compared against baselines including CLIP, supervised ImageNet features, MoCo (345) (PVR), and learning from scratch. Metrics will include average task success rates over multiple seeds, viewpoints, and demonstration set sizes. Additional real-world experiments will be performed using a Franka Emika Panda robot in a cluttered apartment, where the robot will learn five household manipulation tasks from just 20 demonstrations each. Ablation studies will assess the impact of each training objective component, and comparisons will be made to alternative pre-training strategies and datasets.
c9bdc9ad2c3cf3230ba9aac7b5783ab411f0d204.novelty_claims: The proposed approach leverages large-scale, diverse human video data with paired language annotations to pre-train a universal visual representation for robot manipulation, a departure from prior methods that rely on static images or limited in-domain robot data. The method uniquely combines time-contrastive learning, video-language alignment, and sparsity regularization to create embeddings that are both semantically meaningful and compact. The resulting representation demonstrates superior data efficiency and generalization across a wide range of simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, outperforming state-of-the-art visual representations such as CLIP and MoCo. This framework has the potential to establish a new standard for off-the-shelf visual models in robotic manipulation.

c9c0324fcdc92cf7e24f9c4230864851a552f953.title: JailbreakBench: An Open Robustness Benchmark for Jailbreaking Large Language Models
c9c0324fcdc92cf7e24f9c4230864851a552f953.research_question: How can the robustness of large language models (LLMs) against jailbreaking attacks be systematically and reproducibly evaluated, and what standardized benchmarks, datasets, and evaluation frameworks are necessary to facilitate progress in developing and comparing both attacks and defenses?
c9c0324fcdc92cf7e24f9c4230864851a552f953.hypothesis: A comprehensive, open, and standardized benchmark that includes a curated dataset of harmful and benign behaviors, an evolving repository of adversarial prompts (jailbreak artifacts), and a reproducible evaluation pipeline will enable more effective, reproducible, and community-driven research on jailbreaking attacks and defenses for LLMs.
c9c0324fcdc92cf7e24f9c4230864851a552f953.proposed_method: A robust benchmarking platform, JailbreakBench, will be developed to evaluate the susceptibility of LLMs to jailbreaking attacks and the effectiveness of corresponding defenses. The benchmark will include: (1) a curated dataset (JBB-Behaviors) of 100 unique harmful behaviors and matched benign behaviors, sourced from prior work and original contributions, covering a range of misuse categories; (2) an open repository of adversarial prompts, responses, and metadata for reproducibility and extensibility; (3) a standardized red-teaming pipeline supporting both local and cloud-based models, enabling streamlined generation and evaluation of jailbreaks; (4) a modular framework for implementing and evaluating both baseline and novel defenses, with support for adaptive attacks; and (5) a rigorous classifier selection process for automated evaluation of jailbreak success, utilizing open-weight LLMs as judges with custom prompts. The benchmark will be community-driven, allowing researchers to submit new attacks, defenses, and models, and will maintain a public leaderboard to track progress.
c9c0324fcdc92cf7e24f9c4230864851a552f953.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of open-source (e.g., Vicuna-13B-v1.5, Llama-2-7B-chat-hf) and closed-source (e.g., GPT-3.5-Turbo-1106, GPT-4-0125-Preview) LLMs. Baseline attacks such as Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG), Prompt Automatic Iterative Refinement (PAIR), hand-crafted jailbreaks (JB-Chat), and prompt+random search (RS) will be evaluated. Baseline defenses including SmoothLLM, PerplexityFilter, Erase-and-Check, synonym substitution, and removal of non-dictionary items will be implemented and tested. Attack success rates (ASR), average number of queries, and tokens used will be reported, with evaluation performed using a selected LLM-based judge (Llama-3-70B with a custom prompt). Refusal rates on benign behaviors will be measured to assess over-conservatism of models and defenses. The evaluation framework will ensure deterministic sampling and fixed token generation for reproducibility, and all results will be tracked on a public leaderboard.
c9c0324fcdc92cf7e24f9c4230864851a552f953.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark introduces the first fully open, extensible, and reproducible platform for evaluating both jailbreaking attacks and defenses on LLMs. Key innovations include an evolving repository of state-of-the-art adversarial prompts (jailbreak artifacts), a unique dataset of harmful and matched benign behaviors, a standardized and modular evaluation pipeline, rigorous and transparent judge selection based on human agreement, and a public leaderboard for tracking progress. The benchmark prioritizes community-driven extensibility, reproducibility, and accessibility, addressing critical gaps in prior work such as lack of open artifacts, inconsistent evaluation metrics, and irreproducibility. The platform is designed to facilitate adaptive research and accelerate the development of robust LLMs.

c9df2e5d2afd86a5df9cb78130f7589048b2a8b7.title: Low-Dimension-to-High-Dimension Generalization And Its Implications for Length Generalization
c9df2e5d2afd86a5df9cb78130f7589048b2a8b7.research_question: How can models achieve robust generalization when trained on low-dimensional instances and evaluated on high-dimensional instances, particularly in reasoning tasks where the problem scale increases? What are the theoretical and practical limitations of current model architectures in achieving such length generalization, and how can inductive biases and position embedding designs be leveraged to address these challenges?
c9df2e5d2afd86a5df9cb78130f7589048b2a8b7.hypothesis: LDHD (Low-Dimension-to-High-Dimension) generalization is unattainable without appropriate inductive bias; models equipped with suitable inductive biases and principled position embeddings can achieve robust length generalization even in the presence of data format nuisances.
c9df2e5d2afd86a5df9cb78130f7589048b2a8b7.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed to formalize LDHD generalization, disentangling the inherent scaling challenge from data format nuisances in reasoning tasks. The approach will analyze the inductive biases of various model architectures, such as random feature models (RFMs), random feature models with projection (RFMP), and position-only linear attention with advice (PLAA), particularly under stochastic gradient descent (SGD) training. Theoretical results will be established to characterize the conditions under which these models converge to min-degree interpolators with respect to different linearly independent sets, thereby achieving or failing LDHD generalization. Building on these insights, a new principle for designing position embeddings will be proposed, leading to the development of RPE-Square, a novel embedding that combines relative position encoding with mechanisms to handle unaligned data formats.
c9df2e5d2afd86a5df9cb78130f7589048b2a8b7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on tasks such as unaligned copy and URF (Unaligned and Reverse Format) addition, where models are trained on small-scale (short-length) instances and tested on larger-scale (long-length) instances. Datasets will include synthetic arithmetic and symbolic reasoning problems with varying input formats. Baseline models will include Transformers with standard Relative Position Embedding (RPE) and other conventional position embedding schemes. Evaluation metrics will focus on accuracy across both in-distribution and out-of-distribution (length-extrapolated) test sets, with digit-wise accuracy reported for addition tasks. Experimental setups will ensure that models are exposed only to low-dimensional training data, and their ability to generalize to higher-dimensional test data will be rigorously assessed.
c9df2e5d2afd86a5df9cb78130f7589048b2a8b7.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a formal LDHD generalization perspective that separates problem scale from data format, providing a more precise theoretical foundation for length generalization. It establishes a No-Free-Lunch theorem for LDHD generalization, demonstrating the necessity of inductive bias. The analysis reveals how different model architectures induce distinct inductive biases, influencing their ability to generalize from low- to high-dimensional spaces. A principled approach to position embedding design is proposed, culminating in the RPE-Square embedding, which is shown to enhance length generalization and handle data format nuisances more effectively than existing methods. These contributions advance both the theoretical understanding and practical capabilities of models in scalable reasoning tasks.

c9e4efa58fd42a07da27ae70254981715cc257d5.title: Mitigating Reward Over-Optimization in RLHF via Behavior-Supported Regularization
c9e4efa58fd42a07da27ae70254981715cc257d5.research_question: How can reward over-optimization in reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) for large language models be effectively mitigated, particularly by addressing the extrapolation errors that arise when reward models evaluate out-of-distribution (OOD) responses?
c9e4efa58fd42a07da27ae70254981715cc257d5.hypothesis: Regularizing the value function using a behavior-supported Bellman operator, which penalizes OOD actions based on the next-token distribution from the reward training dataset, will reduce OOD response generation during RLHF, thereby mitigating reward over-optimization and enabling convergence to the optimal in-distribution policy.
c9e4efa58fd42a07da27ae70254981715cc257d5.proposed_method: A novel Behavior-Supported Policy Optimization (BSPO) algorithm is developed to address reward over-optimization in RLHF. The method defines the behavior policy as the next-token distribution derived from the reward model's training data, characterizing the in-distribution (ID) region. A behavior-supported Bellman operator is introduced to regularize the value function, penalizing all OOD values without affecting ID ones. The ScoreLM model is implemented to jointly predict both the reward and the behavior distribution, using a combined loss function that balances preference modeling and supervised next-token prediction. Policy optimization is performed by iteratively updating the policy within the ID region, guided by the regularized value estimates, and leveraging PPO with advantage estimates derived from the behavior-supported value function.
c9e4efa58fd42a07da27ae70254981715cc257d5.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted in a synthetic RLHF setup, using a gold-standard reward model (Llama3-8B) and three proxy reward models of varying sizes (GPT-2-large 774M, TinyLlama 1.1B, ShearedLlama 2.7B), all trained on preference data from the UltraFeedback dataset. The initial policy is Alpaca-7B, and all algorithms are evaluated using the same proxy and gold models. Baselines include Standard PPO, PPO with KL penalty, Constrained PPO (CPPO), and two ensemble-based methods (ENS-UWO and ENS-WCO). Evaluation metrics include proxy reward, gold reward, win rate against the initial model, and the average number of behavior-unsupported (OOD) actions per response. The experimental setup tracks OOD generation, policy performance, and robustness to KL divergence constraints.
c9e4efa58fd42a07da27ae70254981715cc257d5.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to use value regularization, via a behavior-supported Bellman operator, to address reward over-optimization in RLHF by penalizing only OOD actions while preserving ID policy evaluation. The method introduces a principled way to detect and control OOD responses using the next-token distribution, enabling explicit modeling of the ID region and ensuring monotonic policy improvement until convergence to the optimal behavior-supported policy. The ScoreLM architecture provides a lightweight and effective implementation for joint reward and behavior distribution prediction. Empirical results demonstrate superior mitigation of reward over-optimization and improved policy performance compared to existing baselines, especially at larger KL divergences.

ca00f4056f9039d3c1a4c3a113f5ee0527149b66.title: Eyes Wide Shut? Exploring the Visual Shortcomings of Multimodal LLMs
ca00f4056f9039d3c1a4c3a113f5ee0527149b66.research_question: What are the underlying causes of visual shortcomings in state-of-the-art multimodal large language models (MLLMs), and how can visual grounding in these models be systematically evaluated and improved?
ca00f4056f9039d3c1a4c3a113f5ee0527149b66.hypothesis: The visual limitations of current MLLMs stem from deficiencies in their vision encoders, particularly those based on CLIP, and integrating features from vision-only self-supervised learning models can enhance visual grounding without sacrificing instruction-following capabilities.
ca00f4056f9039d3c1a4c3a113f5ee0527149b66.proposed_method: A systematic investigation will be conducted to identify and analyze failure cases in MLLMs by constructing a benchmark based on 'CLIP-blind pairs'—image pairs that are encoded similarly by CLIP but are visually distinct according to a vision-only self-supervised model (e.g., DINOv2). The Multimodal Visual Patterns (MMVP) benchmark will be created by manually formulating straightforward visual questions targeting the differences in these pairs. The proposed methodology will further explore the integration of vision-only self-supervised features (such as DINOv2) into MLLMs through two strategies: Additive Mixture-of-Features (A-MoF), which linearly combines CLIP and DINOv2 features, and Interleaved Mixture-of-Features (I-MoF), which spatially interleaves visual tokens from both encoders. These approaches will be implemented within a standard MLLM framework (e.g., LLaVA) to assess their impact on visual grounding and instruction-following.
ca00f4056f9039d3c1a4c3a113f5ee0527149b66.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize the MMVP benchmark, constructed from 150 CLIP-blind image pairs (300 questions), sourced from ImageNet-1K and LAION-Aesthetic datasets. Evaluation will be performed on a range of open-source and closed-source MLLMs, including LLaVA-1.5, InstructBLIP, Mini-GPT4, GPT-4V, Gemini, and Bard, with human performance measured via user studies for comparison. Additional benchmarks such as MMVP-VLM, MM-Bench, GQA, and POPE will be used to assess visual pattern recognition, generalization, and hallucination. Baselines will include models using only CLIP or only DINOv2 as vision encoders, as well as models with varying proportions of mixed features. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy on MMVP and MMVP-VLM (visual grounding), LLaVA benchmark (instruction-following), and POPE (hallucination resistance). Ablation studies will be conducted to isolate the effects of feature mixing ratios and spatial interleaving.
ca00f4056f9039d3c1a4c3a113f5ee0527149b66.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel diagnostic benchmark (MMVP) specifically targeting systematic visual failures in MLLMs by leveraging CLIP-blind pairs and straightforward visual questions. It systematically categorizes visual shortcomings into nine patterns and demonstrates that scaling data or model size in CLIP-based encoders does not resolve most visual grounding issues. The Mixture-of-Features (MoF) approach, including both additive and interleaved strategies, is proposed as a new method to combine complementary strengths of CLIP and vision-only self-supervised models, achieving improved visual grounding without compromising language instruction-following. The work provides new insights into the bottlenecks of current multimodal systems and offers a principled path forward for enhancing visual representation learning in MLLMs.

ca26023c4dbde9a54145b68e1a6a40533fcc1a4a.title: CALIP: Zero-Shot Enhancement of CLIP with Parameter-free Attention
ca26023c4dbde9a54145b68e1a6a40533fcc1a4a.research_question: How can the zero-shot performance of large-scale vision-language models, such as CLIP, be efficiently enhanced for downstream tasks without requiring additional training or labeled data, and can such improvements generalize across both 2D and 3D domains?
ca26023c4dbde9a54145b68e1a6a40533fcc1a4a.hypothesis: Introducing a parameter-free, bidirectional cross-modal attention mechanism to interact visual and textual representations within CLIP will improve zero-shot classification accuracy on diverse downstream tasks, without the need for additional training or learnable parameters. Furthermore, extending this mechanism with lightweight learnable layers will further boost performance under few-shot settings.
ca26023c4dbde9a54145b68e1a6a40533fcc1a4a.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that augments CLIP with a parameter-free cross-modal attention module designed to facilitate bidirectional interactions between intermediate spatial visual features and category-level textual features. This attention mechanism omits all learnable parameters, directly computing attention maps via matrix multiplication between L2-normalized visual and textual features, followed by softmax normalization and bidirectional feature updates. The updated features are then pooled and combined with the original CLIP logits for final prediction, using a weighted sum of the original, visual-guided, and textual-blended logits. For few-shot scenarios, a parametric extension (CALIP-FS) is introduced by inserting lightweight, modality-shared linear projection layers before and after the attention calculation, which are fine-tuned while keeping the CLIP encoders frozen. This approach is designed to be universally applicable to both 2D images and 3D point clouds (via multi-view projections), and requires no additional data or training for zero-shot enhancement.
ca26023c4dbde9a54145b68e1a6a40533fcc1a4a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 14 benchmark datasets, including 11 diverse 2D image classification datasets (e.g., ImageNet, Caltech101, OxfordPets, Flowers102, Food101, FGVCAircraft, DTD, EuroSAT, SUN397, StanfordCars, UCF101) and 3 3D point cloud datasets (ModelNet10, ModelNet40, ScanObjectNN), as well as two medical imaging datasets (ISIC, BCCD). The proposed method will be evaluated in zero-shot settings (no downstream training) and few-shot settings (1, 2, 4, 8, 16 shots per class), using standard accuracy as the primary evaluation metric. Baselines will include zero-shot CLIP, CoOp, CLIP-Adapter, Tip-Adapter, and Linear-probe CLIP. For 3D tasks, point clouds will be projected to multi-view depth maps and processed using PointCLIP. Out-of-distribution robustness will be assessed using ImageNet-V2, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R, and ImageNet-Sketch. Ablation studies will investigate the effect of different logits combinations, attention magnitudes, projection layer placements, and hyperparameter sensitivity. Visualizations of attention maps and feature updates will be provided to analyze the interpretability and effectiveness of the cross-modal interactions.
ca26023c4dbde9a54145b68e1a6a40533fcc1a4a.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first parameter-free, training-free cross-modal attention module for zero-shot enhancement of CLIP, enabling efficient and universal improvement of downstream performance without requiring any additional data or fine-tuning. The method achieves consistent and significant accuracy gains across a wide range of 2D and 3D benchmarks, and even surpasses some few-shot fine-tuned baselines in zero-shot settings. The parametric extension (CALIP-FS) further demonstrates state-of-the-art results under few-shot training, with superior generalization and robustness to distribution shifts. The framework is simple, efficient, and broadly applicable, offering new insights for zero-shot adaptation of large-scale multi-modal models.

ca2cb722ec9780e4575e8bfb216d8f6c9e3a99ac.title: Regret Minimization with Performative Feedback
ca2cb722ec9780e4575e8bfb216d8f6c9e3a99ac.research_question: How can near-optimal predictive models be found and regret minimized in online learning environments where model deployment induces unknown shifts in the data distribution, and feedback consists of samples from these shifted distributions rather than simple bandit feedback?
ca2cb722ec9780e4575e8bfb216d8f6c9e3a99ac.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that leveraging the richer performative feedback—specifically, access to samples from the induced distribution after each model deployment—enables the design of algorithms that achieve regret bounds scaling primarily with the complexity of the distribution shifts, rather than the complexity of the reward (risk) function, even without convexity assumptions.
ca2cb722ec9780e4575e8bfb216d8f6c9e3a99ac.proposed_method: A novel algorithm, termed the performative confidence bounds algorithm, will be developed to minimize regret in performative prediction settings. The algorithm will iteratively deploy models, collecting samples from the induced distributions, and use these samples to construct tight confidence bounds on the performative risk of both explored and unexplored models. By leveraging the structure of performative feedback, the method will estimate the risk of unexplored models using decoupled performative risk calculations and Lipschitz continuity of the distribution map. The algorithm will proceed in phases, maintaining and refining an active set of candidate models, sequentially eliminating suboptimal regions of the parameter space based on confidence bounds, and adaptively discretizing the space to focus exploration. The approach does not require convexity of the performative risk and only assumes Lipschitz continuity of the distribution map and the loss function in the relevant arguments.
ca2cb722ec9780e4575e8bfb216d8f6c9e3a99ac.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in simulated performative prediction environments, where the learner interacts with an environment by deploying models and receiving samples from the resulting distribution. The experimental setup will include varying the sensitivity (Lipschitz constant) of the distribution map, the complexity of the parameter space, and the number of samples collected per deployment. Baseline comparisons will be made against classical Lipschitz bandit algorithms, such as the adaptive zooming algorithm, which only utilize zeroth-order feedback. Evaluation metrics will include cumulative performative regret, convergence to performative optima, and the tightness of confidence bounds. Additional experiments may consider special cases such as location family distribution maps and adaptations of algorithms like LinUCB.
ca2cb722ec9780e4575e8bfb216d8f6c9e3a99ac.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a new algorithmic framework for regret minimization in performative prediction that exploits the richer feedback structure inherent in these settings. The method achieves regret bounds that scale with the complexity of the distribution map rather than the performative risk, allowing for highly irregular or nonconvex risk landscapes. The algorithm provides finite-sample guarantees and converges to near-optimal models without requiring strong structural assumptions such as convexity. The work also establishes a conceptual and technical connection between performative prediction and continuum-armed bandit literature, leveraging and extending bandit tools for a fundamentally richer feedback model.

ca42de76952541d66e75d2b77ba90380471f5f07.title: Sharpness-Aware Training for Free
ca42de76952541d66e75d2b77ba90380471f5f07.research_question: How can sharpness-aware training be achieved for deep neural networks without incurring significant additional computational or memory overhead, while maintaining or improving generalization performance?
ca42de76952541d66e75d2b77ba90380471f5f07.hypothesis: Minimizing a novel trajectory loss, based on the Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence between the outputs of a neural network at current and past weights, can serve as an effective proxy for sharpness minimization, leading to flatter minima and improved generalization with negligible computational overhead compared to standard optimizers.
ca42de76952541d66e75d2b77ba90380471f5f07.proposed_method: A new sharpness-aware training algorithm, Sharpness-Aware Training for Free (SAF), will be developed by introducing a trajectory loss that quantifies the KL-divergence between the outputs of the current model and those from previous epochs for the same data instances. This trajectory loss will be added to the standard training loss after an initial warm-up period, with targets for the KL-divergence obtained by recording model outputs from a fixed number of epochs in the past. To address memory concerns on extremely large datasets, a memory-efficient variant, MESA, will be implemented, which uses an exponential moving average (EMA) of model weights to generate targets for the trajectory loss. Both SAF and MESA will be integrated into standard stochastic gradient descent or AdamW training pipelines, requiring minimal changes to the optimization process.
ca42de76952541d66e75d2b77ba90380471f5f07.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on benchmark image classification datasets including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet. A range of deep neural network architectures, such as ResNet-18, ResNet-50, ResNet-101, ResNet-152, WideResNet-28-10, PyramidNet-110, and Vision Transformer (ViT), will be used for evaluation. Baseline methods will include standard optimizers (SGD, AdamW), Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM), Efficient SAM (ESAM), GSAM, and LookSAM. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy, training speed (images per second), memory usage, and sharpness measures as defined by the SAM methodology. Hyperparameters will be kept consistent across methods for fair comparison, and experiments will be run multiple times with different random seeds. Loss landscape visualizations and sharpness evolution over epochs will also be analyzed.
ca42de76952541d66e75d2b77ba90380471f5f07.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a trajectory loss as a computationally efficient proxy for sharpness, enabling sharpness-aware training at nearly zero additional computational cost compared to standard optimizers. SAF achieves state-of-the-art generalization performance and training speed, outperforming SAM and its variants on large-scale datasets and models. The memory-efficient MESA variant further enables deployment on extremely large datasets with minimal memory overhead. The method provides a new direction for sharpness-aware training by leveraging the natural trajectory of weight updates, rather than explicit sharpness maximization steps.

ca444821352a4bd91884413d8070446e2960715a.title: On the Parameterization and Initialization of Diagonal State Space Models
ca444821352a4bd91884413d8070446e2960715a.research_question: How can diagonal state space models be effectively parameterized and initialized to achieve strong performance on sequence modeling tasks, and what are the theoretical and empirical implications of different design choices in these models?
ca444821352a4bd91884413d8070446e2960715a.hypothesis: Careful parameterization and initialization of diagonal state space models, particularly through principled choices of the state matrix and kernel computation, will enable these models to match or exceed the performance of more complex state space models such as those using diagonal plus low-rank (DPLR) parameterizations, while offering greater simplicity and efficiency.
ca444821352a4bd91884413d8070446e2960715a.proposed_method: A new framework for diagonal state space models (SSMs), termed S4D, will be developed by systematically exploring and consolidating design choices in parameterization, initialization, and kernel computation. The method will use a diagonal state matrix A, initialized using principled schemes such as the diagonalization of the HiPPO-LegS matrix (HiPPO-D), inverse-law scaling, or damped Fourier frequencies, ensuring the real part is negative for stability. The convolution kernel will be computed efficiently via Vandermonde matrix multiplication, leveraging the structure of diagonal matrices for computational simplicity. Parameterization will allow for independent or joint training of input/output matrices (B, C), and both bilinear and zero-order hold discretization schemes will be supported. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to explain the effectiveness of diagonal initializations and to establish conditions under which diagonal SSMs recover the dynamics of more expressive models in the infinite state limit.
ca444821352a4bd91884413d8070446e2960715a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a diverse set of sequence modeling benchmarks, including Sequential CIFAR-10 (image classification with flattened pixel sequences), BIDMC Vital Signs (biosignal time series regression), and Speech Commands (audio waveform classification), covering a range of modalities, sequence lengths (1K, 4K, 16K), and both bidirectional and causal settings. The proposed S4D variants will be systematically compared to DPLR-based S4 models and other baselines such as RNNs, CNNs, and Transformers. Ablation studies will isolate the effects of different parameterizations, initializations, and discretization methods. Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy and regression error, with results averaged over multiple seeds for robustness. The Long Range Arena (LRA) benchmark will also be used to assess performance on tasks requiring long-range dependency modeling.
ca444821352a4bd91884413d8070446e2960715a.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a systematic and theoretically grounded framework for parameterizing and initializing diagonal state space models, resulting in models that are dramatically simpler to implement and understand compared to existing approaches. The work provides new mathematical analysis explaining why certain diagonal initializations recover the dynamics of more complex models in the infinite state limit. The S4D method achieves state-of-the-art or competitive results across multiple domains while requiring only minimal code for kernel computation. The research disentangles and clarifies the effects of various design choices, enabling fair and controlled comparisons between diagonal and DPLR-based SSMs, and demonstrates that diagonal SSMs can achieve high performance with appropriate initialization and parameterization.

ca6096142016a2ba8133f6cb2c04ad30f5eae730.title: Learning to Walk in Minutes Using Massively Parallel Deep Reinforcement Learning
ca6096142016a2ba8133f6cb2c04ad30f5eae730.research_question: How can training times for real-world robotic locomotion tasks be drastically reduced while maintaining policy performance and robustness, particularly for complex terrains and sim-to-real transfer scenarios?
ca6096142016a2ba8133f6cb2c04ad30f5eae730.hypothesis: Massively parallel deep reinforcement learning, leveraging thousands of simulated robots on a single GPU and a novel automatic curriculum, will enable the training of robust locomotion policies for legged robots in minutes rather than hours or days, without sacrificing policy effectiveness or sim-to-real transferability.
ca6096142016a2ba8133f6cb2c04ad30f5eae730.proposed_method: A massively parallel reinforcement learning framework will be developed, utilizing the Isaac Gym simulation environment to run thousands of robot instances simultaneously on a single workstation GPU. The approach will employ a custom implementation of the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm, with all data collection and policy updates performed directly on the GPU to minimize data transfer overhead. Key modifications will include tuning batch sizes, mini-batch sizes, and the number of steps per robot to optimize learning dynamics in the high-parallelism regime, as well as a careful handling of episode resets to maintain critic performance. An automatic, game-inspired curriculum will be integrated, dynamically adjusting terrain difficulty for each robot based on its performance, thereby enabling efficient progression from simple to complex tasks without manual tuning.
ca6096142016a2ba8133f6cb2c04ad30f5eae730.experiment_details: Experiments will involve training quadrupedal robots (primarily ANYmal C, but also ANYmal B, ANYmal C with an arm, Unitree A1, and Cassie) to traverse a variety of procedurally generated terrains, including flat, sloped, rough, stairs, and obstacles. Training will be conducted with up to 4096 robots in parallel and batch sizes up to 196,608, with policies trained in under 20 minutes. Evaluation will include robustness and traversability tests in simulation, measuring success rates for each terrain type under high-velocity commands, and sim-to-real transfer experiments on physical robots, using real sensor data and elevation maps. Baselines will include varying numbers of parallel robots and batch sizes to analyze the trade-off between training speed and policy performance. Metrics will include total episode reward, training time, and success rates across different terrain complexities.
ca6096142016a2ba8133f6cb2c04ad30f5eae730.novelty_claims: The proposed framework enables end-to-end training of complex locomotion policies for real-world robots in minutes, representing a speedup of multiple orders of magnitude over prior methods. Innovations include the use of massive parallelism on a single GPU for both simulation and learning, a novel automatic curriculum that adapts task difficulty per robot without external tuning, and algorithmic modifications for effective learning in the high-parallelism regime. The approach demonstrates generalizability across multiple robot platforms and terrains, and achieves robust sim-to-real transfer without requiring complex reward shaping or action space engineering.

ca66912298f2e5c739ac0f6f0b5932422551b608.title: Graph Mixup with Soft Alignments
ca66912298f2e5c739ac0f6f0b5932422551b608.research_question: How can data augmentation techniques for graph classification be improved by addressing the challenge of node-level correspondence between graphs, in order to enhance the generalization, robustness, and performance of graph neural networks (GNNs)?
ca66912298f2e5c739ac0f6f0b5932422551b608.hypothesis: Explicitly modeling node-level correspondences between pairs of graphs through soft alignments will enable more effective mixup-based data augmentation, resulting in improved generalization, robustness to label noise, and classification performance of GNNs compared to existing graph augmentation and mixup methods.
ca66912298f2e5c739ac0f6f0b5932422551b608.proposed_method: A novel graph mixup framework, termed S-Mixup, will be developed to generate augmented graphs for classification tasks. The method will compute a soft assignment matrix between pairs of graphs, leveraging node features and graph topology to establish node-level correspondences via a graph matching network with attention-based cross-graph message passing. One graph in the pair will be transformed using the soft assignment matrix so that its adjacency and node feature matrices are aligned with the other graph, resulting in matched node orders and sizes. The aligned graphs will then be mixed by performing convex combinations (linear interpolation) of their adjacency matrices, node feature matrices, and labels, with the mixup ratio sampled from a Beta distribution. The resulting synthetic graphs and labels will be used as augmented training data for GNNs.
ca66912298f2e5c739ac0f6f0b5932422551b608.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple graph classification benchmarks, including six datasets from the TUDatasets collection (such as PROTEINS, NCI1, IMDB-BINARY, IMDB-MULTI, REDDIT-BINARY, REDDIT-MULTI-5K) and the large-scale ogbg-molhiv dataset from the OGB benchmark. The proposed method will be evaluated using GCN and GIN as backbone models. Baselines will include standard data augmentation methods (DropEdge, DropNode, Subgraph) and existing graph mixup methods (M-Mixup, SubMix, G-Mixup). Evaluation metrics will be classification accuracy and ROC-AUC, with results averaged over 10 runs using consistent train/validation/test splits. Additional experiments will assess robustness to noisy labels by introducing varying levels of label corruption. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of mixup strategies, mixup ratio ranges, normalization functions for the assignment matrix, and alternative graph matching algorithms.
ca66912298f2e5c739ac0f6f0b5932422551b608.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a principled approach to graph mixup by explicitly modeling node-level correspondences between arbitrary pairs of graphs using soft alignments, overcoming limitations of prior methods that ignore node matching or rely on random or class-level interpolations. This framework enables direct and meaningful interpolation of both node features and graph structures, preserving critical substructures (such as motifs) and avoiding the generation of noisy or unrealistic graphs. The approach is compatible with various graph matching algorithms and normalization schemes, and demonstrates superior performance and robustness compared to existing graph augmentation and mixup techniques.

ca6a2bc279be5a3349a22bfd6866ed633d18734b.title: MiniGPT-4: Enhancing Vision-Language Understanding with Advanced Large Language Models
ca6a2bc279be5a3349a22bfd6866ed633d18734b.research_question: How can vision-language understanding and generation capabilities be enhanced by aligning visual features with advanced large language models, and what are the key factors and training strategies required to achieve advanced multi-modal abilities in such systems?
ca6a2bc279be5a3349a22bfd6866ed633d18734b.hypothesis: Properly aligning visual features from a pre-trained vision encoder with an advanced large language model through a minimal projection mechanism will enable the emergence of advanced vision-language capabilities, comparable to those demonstrated by state-of-the-art multimodal models such as GPT-4.
ca6a2bc279be5a3349a22bfd6866ed633d18734b.proposed_method: A novel vision-language model will be developed by integrating a frozen, pre-trained vision encoder (ViT-G/14 from EVA-CLIP with Q-Former) and a frozen advanced large language model (Vicuna, based on LLaMA), connected via a single trainable linear projection layer. The training will proceed in two stages: first, the projection layer will be trained on a large-scale collection of aligned image-caption pairs to acquire general vision-language knowledge, keeping all other components frozen. In the second stage, the model will be fine-tuned using a curated, high-quality dataset of detailed image descriptions formatted in a conversational template, enhancing the naturalness and reliability of generated outputs. Data post-processing will be employed to ensure the quality of fine-tuning data, including automated and manual correction of generated captions.
ca6a2bc279be5a3349a22bfd6866ed633d18734b.experiment_details: Experiments will include both qualitative and quantitative evaluations. The model will be pretrained for 20,000 steps with a batch size of 256 on 4 A100 GPUs using a combined dataset from LAION, Conceptual Captions, and SBU, totaling approximately 5 million image-text pairs. Fine-tuning will use around 3,500 high-quality image-description pairs, requiring only 400 steps with a batch size of 12 on a single A100 GPU. Evaluation will be performed on advanced vision-language tasks (meme interpretation, recipe generation, advertisement creation, and poem composition) using a custom set of 100 images, with human evaluators assessing task fulfillment. Standard image captioning benchmarks such as COCO will be used, with correctness judged by coverage of ground-truth objects and relations. Baseline comparisons will include BLIP-2 (using Flan-T5 XXL) and ablation studies will explore architectural variants (e.g., removing Q-Former, using multiple projection layers, or fine-tuning Q-Former). Additional analysis will assess hallucination rates and spatial understanding using metrics like CHAIR and datasets such as AOK-VQA and GQA.
ca6a2bc279be5a3349a22bfd6866ed633d18734b.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a minimal and efficient alignment mechanism—training only a single projection layer—to bridge pre-trained vision encoders and advanced large language models, enabling the emergence of advanced multi-modal abilities. It is claimed that this approach allows for rapid training (approximately 10 hours on 4 GPUs) and demonstrates that advanced vision-language capabilities, such as detailed image description, meme interpretation, and website generation from hand-drawn drafts, can be achieved without end-to-end training or large-scale architectural modifications. The work also presents a new high-quality dataset for fine-tuning conversational vision-language alignment and provides systematic ablation studies to validate the sufficiency of the proposed alignment strategy. The approach is positioned as a significant step toward understanding and replicating the advanced capabilities of closed-source models like GPT-4.

ca724adee2c54c66db260885217a5d62f478130d.title: Probabilistic Generating Circuits - Demystified
ca724adee2c54c66db260885217a5d62f478130d.research_question: What are the fundamental relationships and computational properties between probabilistic generating circuits (PGCs), probabilistic circuits (PCs) with negative weights, and determinantal point processes (DPPs), particularly regarding tractable inference and model expressiveness for discrete random variables of varying arity?
ca724adee2c54c66db260885217a5d62f478130d.hypothesis: The power of PGCs arises primarily from the allowance of negative weights rather than the use of probability generating polynomials, and nonmonotone PCs (with negative weights) computing set-multilinear polynomials can strictly subsume PGCs in terms of tractable inference and expressiveness.
ca724adee2c54c66db260885217a5d62f478130d.proposed_method: A comprehensive theoretical analysis will be conducted to formally relate PGCs and nonmonotone PCs, including explicit constructions that transform any PGC into an equivalent nonmonotone PC with only polynomial overhead. Complexity-theoretic arguments will be used to establish the (in)tractability of marginalization for PGCs over categorical variables with more than two categories, leveraging reductions from #P-hard problems such as counting perfect matchings in bipartite graphs. Further, the properties of nonmonotone PCs computing set-multilinear polynomials will be analyzed to show their support for tractable marginalization across arbitrary categorical domains. Additional compositional operations will be designed to preserve the semantic properties of probability distributions and set-multilinearity in nonmonotone PCs. Theoretical connections between DPPs, PGCs, and nonmonotone PCs will be explored, including the use of affine projections and algebraic complexity arguments.
ca724adee2c54c66db260885217a5d62f478130d.experiment_details: The investigation will primarily involve formal proofs and complexity-theoretic reductions rather than empirical experiments. Key constructions will include explicit circuit transformations, hardness reductions from #P-complete problems (e.g., perfect matching counting), and randomized polynomial-time algorithms for property testing (such as set-multilinearity). Baselines for comparison will include standard PCs (with nonnegative weights), DPPs, and PGCs restricted to binary variables. Evaluation will focus on tractability of marginalization, expressiveness, and circuit size overhead, with complexity classes (e.g., #P, FP, NP) serving as the primary evaluation metrics.
ca724adee2c54c66db260885217a5d62f478130d.novelty_claims: The proposed research claims that the allowance of negative weights, rather than the use of generating polynomials, is the key to the expressiveness and tractability of PGCs. It is demonstrated that every PGC over binary variables can be efficiently simulated by a nonmonotone PC, and that nonmonotone PCs computing set-multilinear polynomials support tractable marginalization for arbitrary categorical variables, strictly subsuming PGCs. The research also establishes new hardness results for marginalization in PGCs beyond binary variables and provides constructive algorithms for property testing in nonmonotone PCs. Furthermore, it explores deep connections between algebraic complexity theory and probabilistic modeling by relating affine projections of DPPs to arithmetic formulas, indicating foundational barriers to separating the expressive power of these models.

ca9f5b3bf0f54ad97513e6175b30497873670fed.title: Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality
ca9f5b3bf0f54ad97513e6175b30497873670fed.research_question: How can the theoretical and algorithmic connections between structured state space models (SSMs) and attention mechanisms be leveraged to design more efficient and scalable sequence modeling architectures for language modeling and related tasks?
ca9f5b3bf0f54ad97513e6175b30497873670fed.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by formalizing and exploiting the duality between SSMs and attention mechanisms through the lens of structured semiseparable matrices, it is possible to develop new architectures and algorithms that achieve superior efficiency and competitive or improved performance compared to existing Transformer-based and SSM-based models.
ca9f5b3bf0f54ad97513e6175b30497873670fed.proposed_method: A unified framework, termed Structured State Space Duality (SSD), will be developed to connect SSMs and variants of attention via the mathematical abstraction of structured semiseparable matrices. The approach involves representing sequence models both as matrix transformations and tensor contractions, revealing dual linear (recurrent) and quadratic (attention-like) forms. The core of the method is the design of a new architecture, Mamba-2, whose main layer refines the selective SSM by imposing a scalar-times-identity structure on the recurrence matrix and expanding the head dimension to match modern Transformer conventions. A novel SSD algorithm will be implemented using block decompositions of semiseparable matrices, enabling optimal trade-offs in training and inference compute, memory usage, and hardware utilization. The architecture will also incorporate parallelism strategies, such as tensor and sequence parallelism, and introduce head structures analogous to multi-head attention for SSMs.
ca9f5b3bf0f54ad97513e6175b30497873670fed.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on large-scale language modeling tasks using datasets such as the Pile, with models trained at varying parameter scales (e.g., 2.7B parameters trained on 300B tokens). Baselines will include previous SSM models (e.g., Mamba), open-source Transformers (e.g., Pythia-2.8B, Pythia-6.9B), and optimized Transformer implementations (e.g., FlashAttention-2). Evaluation metrics will include perplexity, wall-clock training time, and performance on standard downstream tasks, as well as challenging multi-query associative recall tasks. The experimental setup will assess both training efficiency and inference speed, with particular attention to performance at long sequence lengths and scalability with respect to state size and hardware parallelism.
ca9f5b3bf0f54ad97513e6175b30497873670fed.novelty_claims: The proposal claims several innovations: (1) a comprehensive theoretical framework unifying SSMs and attention via structured semiseparable matrices; (2) the introduction of the SSD algorithm, enabling efficient computation of SSMs with optimal hardware utilization; (3) the design of the Mamba-2 architecture, which Pareto-dominates prior SSMs and Transformers in both efficiency and performance; (4) the extension of architectural concepts such as multi-head attention to SSMs; and (5) the demonstration that any kernel attention method with a fast recurrent form must be an SSM, establishing a new class of dual sequence models with both linear and quadratic forms.

cab3d65b3f4d0a4169d0fdaaed15af6be1d6bb84.title: Magpie: Alignment Data Synthesis from Scratch by Prompting Aligned LLMs with Nothing
cab3d65b3f4d0a4169d0fdaaed15af6be1d6bb84.research_question: Can high-quality, diverse instruction alignment data for large language models (LLMs) be synthesized at scale directly from aligned LLMs, without relying on human-generated seed prompts or prompt engineering, and can such data rival or surpass existing public and proprietary alignment datasets in downstream model performance?
cab3d65b3f4d0a4169d0fdaaed15af6be1d6bb84.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that prompting aligned LLMs with only the pre-query template, leveraging their auto-regressive nature, enables the scalable synthesis of diverse and high-quality instruction-response pairs. This synthetic data, when used for supervised fine-tuning and preference optimization, will yield models that match or outperform those trained on existing public or proprietary alignment datasets.
cab3d65b3f4d0a4169d0fdaaed15af6be1d6bb84.proposed_method: A fully automated self-synthesis pipeline, named MAGPIE, will be developed to generate large-scale instruction alignment data from aligned LLMs. The method consists of two main steps: (1) Instruction Generation, where only the pre-query template (as defined by the chat format of the LLM) is input to the model, prompting it to autonomously generate a user instruction; and (2) Response Generation, where the generated instruction is paired with the appropriate post-query template and input back to the LLM to produce a corresponding response. The pipeline will be extended to support multi-turn conversations, preference optimization (by sampling multiple responses and ranking them with a reward model), and domain-specific or multilingual data generation via tailored system prompts. Filtering mechanisms based on various quality, diversity, and safety metrics will be incorporated to curate the final dataset.
cab3d65b3f4d0a4169d0fdaaed15af6be1d6bb84.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted by applying the MAGPIE pipeline to open-weight aligned LLMs such as Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Llama-3-70B-Instruct, generating datasets of several million instruction-response pairs. The resulting datasets will be used to fine-tune base LLMs (e.g., Llama-3-8B, Qwen1.5, Qwen2) via supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and direct preference optimization (DPO). Baseline comparisons will include models fine-tuned on leading public instruction datasets such as ShareGPT, WildChat, EvolInstruct, UltraChat, OpenHermes, GenQA, and TuluV2Mix. Evaluation will be performed on established alignment and instruction-following benchmarks including AlpacaEval2, Arena-Hard, WildBench, and a suite of Huggingface OpenLLM Leaderboard tasks (e.g., MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag, TruthfulQA, WinoGrande, GSM8K). Metrics will include win rate (WR), length-controlled win rate (LC), and standard deviation (SD), with GPT-4-Turbo and official instruct models serving as reference evaluators. Additional analyses will address data coverage, diversity, quality, safety (using Llama-Guard-2), and cost efficiency.
cab3d65b3f4d0a4169d0fdaaed15af6be1d6bb84.novelty_claims: The proposed approach eliminates the need for human-written seed prompts or prompt engineering by leveraging the auto-regressive properties of aligned LLMs to self-synthesize instructions from scratch. The method is fully automated, scalable, and model-agnostic, supporting multi-turn, preference-optimized, domain-specific, and multilingual dataset generation. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate that models fine-tuned solely on MAGPIE-generated data can outperform those trained on existing public datasets and even rival official proprietary instruct models, despite using significantly fewer data points. The framework's extensibility and filtering capabilities further enhance its adaptability and practical utility for open-source LLM alignment.

cab58a0263d454604896dce6b8fbf4df1dd99ff0.title: EAGLE-2: Faster Inference of Language Models with Dynamic Draft Trees
cab58a0263d454604896dce6b8fbf4df1dd99ff0.research_question: How can the inference speed of large language models be improved without altering the output distribution or requiring additional model training, particularly by leveraging context-dependent properties of draft token acceptance?
cab58a0263d454604896dce6b8fbf4df1dd99ff0.hypothesis: Dynamically adjusting the draft tree structure during speculative sampling, based on context-aware estimates of draft token acceptance rates derived from the draft model's confidence scores, will significantly increase the number of accepted tokens per cycle and yield greater inference speedup while preserving the original output distribution.
cab58a0263d454604896dce6b8fbf4df1dd99ff0.proposed_method: A novel context-aware dynamic draft tree framework will be developed for speculative sampling in large language model inference. The method will utilize the draft model's confidence scores as proxies for token acceptance rates, enabling dynamic adjustment of the draft tree structure in response to the context of each generation step. During the expansion phase, the top-k tokens with the highest estimated global acceptance probabilities (computed as the product of confidence scores along the path from the root) will be selected for further expansion. In the reranking phase, all draft tokens will be globally reranked by their acceptance probabilities, and the top-m will be selected to form a connected, flattened sequence for verification by the original LLM. The approach will ensure that the attention mask is adjusted according to the draft tree structure so that each token only attends to its ancestors, maintaining consistency with vanilla autoregressive decoding.
cab58a0263d454604896dce6b8fbf4df1dd99ff0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of LLMs, including Vicuna 7B/13B, LLaMA2-Chat 7B/13B/70B, and LLaMA3-Instruct 8B/70B. Six diverse tasks will be evaluated: multi-turn conversation (MT-bench), code generation (HumanEval), mathematical reasoning (GSM8K), instruction following (Alpaca), summarization (CNN/DailyMail), and question answering (NaturalQuestions). Baselines will include vanilla autoregressive decoding, standard speculative sampling, PLD, Medusa, Lookahead, Hydra, and EAGLE. Evaluation metrics will focus on speedup ratio (relative to vanilla decoding) and average acceptance length per draft-verification cycle, with all methods tested on the same hardware for fairness. Zero-shot and few-shot settings will be used, and no additional model training will be required for the proposed method.
cab58a0263d454604896dce6b8fbf4df1dd99ff0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a fully context-aware dynamic draft tree for speculative sampling, leveraging the draft model's confidence scores to approximate acceptance rates without additional overhead or model training. This enables dynamic, context-sensitive adjustment of the draft tree structure, resulting in significantly higher acceptance lengths and speedup ratios compared to static-tree or position-only methods. The method is lossless, ensuring the output distribution remains identical to that of the original LLM, and requires no fine-tuning or modification of the LLM or draft model. Out-of-the-box usability and provable distributional consistency are key innovations.

caf6ca4ccfabf903003cdf927fb7e883342fdcad.title: Exposing flaws of generative model evaluation metrics and their unfair treatment of diffusion models
caf6ca4ccfabf903003cdf927fb7e883342fdcad.research_question: How can evaluation metrics for generative models, particularly those used for image synthesis, be improved to better align with human perception of image realism and to more accurately assess fidelity, diversity, and memorization across diverse generative model architectures and datasets?
caf6ca4ccfabf903003cdf927fb7e883342fdcad.hypothesis: Current evaluation metrics for generative models, especially those relying on Inception-V3-based feature spaces such as FID, do not strongly correlate with human perception of image realism and may unfairly penalize certain model classes, such as diffusion models. Replacing Inception-V3 with self-supervised encoders like DINOv2-ViT-L/14 will yield evaluation metrics that better align with human judgments. Furthermore, existing memorization metrics are insufficient for reliably detecting memorization in generative models.
caf6ca4ccfabf903003cdf927fb7e883342fdcad.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation framework will be developed to systematically assess generative models using a wide array of metrics and feature extractors. The approach involves generating large-scale synthetic image datasets from state-of-the-art generative models spanning multiple architectures (diffusion, GAN, VAE, normalizing flow, transformer-based, consistency models) and training them on diverse image datasets (CIFAR10, ImageNet1k, FFHQ, LSUN-Bedroom). Human subject experiments, designed according to psychophysics best practices, will be conducted to establish a robust baseline for image realism by measuring human error rates in distinguishing real from generated images. Multiple evaluation metrics—covering fidelity, diversity, rarity, and memorization—will be computed using both traditional (Inception-V3) and alternative (self-supervised and supervised) feature extractors, including DINOv2-ViT-L/14, CLIP, SwAV, MAE, data2vec, and ConvNeXt. Qualitative and quantitative analyses will be performed to investigate the alignment between metric scores and human perception, as well as to examine the sensitivity of memorization metrics.
caf6ca4ccfabf903003cdf927fb7e883342fdcad.experiment_details: Experiments will involve generating 100,000 images per model across 41 generative models and four datasets, resulting in over 4 million images. Human evaluation will be conducted via large-scale two-alternative forced choice tasks, with over 1,000 paid participants and more than 200,000 individual responses, to measure the human error rate as a ground truth for image realism. The evaluation will include 17 metrics (e.g., FID, KID, IS, precision, recall, density, coverage, rarity, Vendi score, memorization ratio, AuthPct, C_T, FLS-POG) computed using nine different encoders. Baseline comparisons will be made across model types and metrics, with statistical analyses (e.g., ANOVA) to assess significance. Memorization will be directly checked using calibrated l2 distance between generated and training images, and the effectiveness of automated memorization metrics will be benchmarked against this ground truth.
caf6ca4ccfabf903003cdf927fb7e883342fdcad.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the largest and most comprehensive evaluation of generative model metrics to date, combining large-scale human subject experiments with a systematic analysis of 17 metrics across nine encoders and multiple model architectures. It claims to expose fundamental flaws in widely used metrics such as FID, particularly their misalignment with human perception and their unfair penalization of diffusion models. The study will demonstrate that self-supervised encoders, especially DINOv2-ViT-L/14, provide a more perceptually relevant feature space for generative evaluation, enabling metrics that better reflect human judgments. Additionally, it will provide new insights into the limitations of current memorization metrics and advocate for direct measurement of memorization using calibrated l2 distance. The release of all generated datasets, human evaluation data, and a modular library for metric computation is intended to facilitate further research and establish new standards for generative model evaluation.

caf9c793b5ad3036ed1d7d6b2e66d23892ff04ce.title: Tight Auditing of Differentially Private Machine Learning
caf9c793b5ad3036ed1d7d6b2e66d23892ff04ce.research_question: How can empirical auditing of differentially private machine learning algorithms be made both tight and computationally efficient, especially for large models and natural (non-adversarial) datasets, and what are the implications for validating privacy guarantees and detecting implementation bugs?
caf9c793b5ad3036ed1d7d6b2e66d23892ff04ce.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by tailoring auditing schemes to the specific privacy mechanisms used in DP-SGD and leveraging advanced composition theorems (such as functional DP and Gaussian DP), it is possible to obtain tight empirical privacy estimates with significantly fewer training runs, even for natural datasets, and that such schemes can surface subtle implementation bugs missed by prior methods.
caf9c793b5ad3036ed1d7d6b2e66d23892ff04ce.proposed_method: A new auditing framework will be developed that directly leverages the trade-off functions of specific differential privacy mechanisms (e.g., Gaussian DP, functional DP) rather than relying solely on (ε,δ)-DP bounds. The approach will use hypothesis testing interpretations of DP, employing both Clopper-Pearson and Bayesian estimation methods to compute tight lower bounds on privacy leakage from empirical false positive and false negative rates. The method will adapt recent advances in privacy loss distribution (PLD) accounting and tight composition theorems to reduce the number of required training runs from thousands to as few as two. The framework will support multiple threat models, including white-box access with gradient or input canaries and black-box access, and will be designed to be computationally efficient and applicable to both adversarial and natural datasets.
caf9c793b5ad3036ed1d7d6b2e66d23892ff04ce.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of standard machine learning datasets and models, including settings with both adversarially crafted and natural training data. The evaluation will compare the proposed auditing scheme against existing baselines such as traditional (ε,δ)-DP auditing with Clopper-Pearson and Bayesian methods, as well as prior empirical auditing techniques. Metrics will include the tightness of empirical privacy estimates (i.e., how closely they match theoretical guarantees), the number of training runs required for non-trivial estimates, and the ability to detect privacy implementation bugs. The setup will also explore the impact of model and training hyperparameters, model architecture, and attacker assumptions on empirical privacy leakage.
caf9c793b5ad3036ed1d7d6b2e66d23892ff04ce.novelty_claims: The proposed approach claims several innovations: (1) the first empirical auditing scheme for DP-SGD that provides tight privacy estimates for natural datasets, not just worst-case adversarial settings; (2) a dramatic reduction in computational overhead, requiring only two training runs instead of thousands or millions; (3) adaptation of functional DP and Gaussian DP trade-off functions for direct empirical auditing, avoiding looseness from (ε,δ)-DP conversions; (4) demonstration that the method can surface subtle implementation bugs in differentially private ML code that elude prior auditing tools; and (5) a practical framework that can be integrated into the testing pipelines of DP-ML systems for both validation and debugging.

cafe794035266eaef5d53e5d37aa486c71db9703.title: Rho-1: Not All Tokens Are What You Need
cafe794035266eaef5d53e5d37aa486c71db9703.research_question: How can language model pre-training be made more efficient and effective by focusing on the most useful tokens, rather than uniformly applying next-token prediction loss to all tokens in the training corpus?
cafe794035266eaef5d53e5d37aa486c71db9703.hypothesis: Selective training on a subset of tokens that are more aligned with the desired data distribution and exhibit high excess loss will improve language model performance and data efficiency compared to conventional training on all tokens.
cafe794035266eaef5d53e5d37aa486c71db9703.proposed_method: A new framework, Selective Language Modeling (SLM), will be developed to enhance language model pre-training by focusing loss computation on a subset of tokens deemed most beneficial. The approach consists of three main steps: (1) training a reference model on a curated, high-quality dataset to represent the desired data distribution, (2) using this reference model to score each token in the larger pretraining corpus based on its loss, and (3) during pre-training, selecting only the top k% of tokens with the highest excess loss (the difference between the current model's loss and the reference model's loss) for loss computation and gradient updates. This selective process is designed to filter out noisy, irrelevant, or already-learned tokens, thereby concentrating learning on tokens that are more informative and aligned with downstream tasks. The token selection ratio (k%) is treated as a hyperparameter and can be adjusted based on empirical results.
cafe794035266eaef5d53e5d37aa486c71db9703.experiment_details: Experiments will involve continual pre-training of language models such as Tinyllama-1.1B and Mistral-7B on both mathematical (OpenWebMath, ~14B tokens) and general domain corpora (SlimPajama, StarCoderData, OpenWebMath, totaling 80B tokens). Reference models will be trained on high-quality subsets (0.5B math tokens, 1.9B general tokens) for three epochs. Baselines will include models trained with standard causal language modeling (CLM) and leading models such as Gemma, Qwen1.5, Phi-1.5, DeepSeekLLM, DeepSeekMath, CodeLlama, Minerva, LLemma, and InternLM2-Math. Evaluation will use few-shot and fine-tuned performance on benchmarks including MATH, GSM8k, SVAMP, ASDiv, MAWPS, MQA, STEM, SAT, MMLU, BBH, MBPP, HumEval, AGIEval, ARC, BoolQ, PIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, OBQA, and TydiQA, with metrics such as accuracy and perplexity. Token selection ratios (e.g., 60% for 1B models, 70% for 7B models) will be explored, and ablation studies will analyze the impact of different scoring functions and selection ratios.
cafe794035266eaef5d53e5d37aa486c71db9703.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel token-level selection mechanism for language model pre-training, moving beyond document-level filtering and uniform loss application. By leveraging a reference model to score and select tokens based on excess loss, the approach enables efficient use of training data, significantly reduces the number of tokens needed for state-of-the-art performance, and improves downstream task accuracy. The methodology is generalizable across domains and can be applied even in the absence of high-quality reference data through self-referencing. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate substantial gains in both data efficiency and model performance, with the method achieving baseline or superior results using a fraction of the pretraining tokens required by leading models.

cb0c5d1f195122c6da8d8dd939b51b9597d948df.title: Latent Safety-Constrained Policy Approach for Safe Offline Reinforcement Learning
cb0c5d1f195122c6da8d8dd939b51b9597d948df.research_question: How can offline reinforcement learning policies be learned to maximize cumulative rewards while strictly adhering to safety constraints, using only pre-collected static datasets, and without incurring the risks of unsafe exploration?
cb0c5d1f195122c6da8d8dd939b51b9597d948df.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that modeling safety constraints in a latent space using conditional generative models, and optimizing policy learning within this space, will enable the derivation of policies that both maximize reward and maintain strict safety compliance in offline reinforcement learning scenarios.
cb0c5d1f195122c6da8d8dd939b51b9597d948df.proposed_method: A novel framework, Latent Safety-Prioritized Constraints (LSPC), will be developed to address safe offline reinforcement learning. The approach begins by modeling the distribution of safety constraints in a latent space using a Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE), which encodes state-action pairs and reconstructs safe actions, thereby implicitly enforcing policy support within the dataset and prioritizing safety. The learned latent space serves as a tractable embedding of safety constraints derived from cost-labeled offline data. Policy optimization is then formulated as a constrained reward-return maximization problem, where an additional encoder is trained to find latent embeddings that maximize expected reward while remaining within the learned safety-prioritized latent boundary. Advantage-weighted regression (AWR) is used both for extracting a conservatively safe policy and for optimizing reward within the latent constraint space. The training process alternates between critic updates (using Implicit Q-Learning for both reward and cost) and policy extraction steps, ensuring that the final policy adheres to safety constraints while achieving high reward.
cb0c5d1f195122c6da8d8dd939b51b9597d948df.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the DSRL benchmark, which includes tasks from MetaDrive, SafetyGymnasium, and BulletSafetyGym, covering a variety of autonomous driving and robotic control scenarios. Performance will be evaluated using normalized return (reward) and normalized cost, with safety defined as achieving a normalized cost below a specified threshold. The proposed method will be compared against several baselines, including BC-Safe, CDT, CPQ, and FISOR, across multiple cost thresholds and random seeds. Evaluation will follow standard protocols, measuring both safety compliance and reward optimization, and visualizations of action distributions and training progress will be provided to analyze policy behavior in the latent constraint space.
cb0c5d1f195122c6da8d8dd939b51b9597d948df.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a principled method for modeling and enforcing safety constraints in offline RL via a latent space learned from static datasets, using CVAEs. Unlike existing methods, it disentangles safety and reward optimization, enabling flexible and tractable safety enforcement without requiring explicit divergence constraints with the behavior policy. The framework provides theoretical guarantees on policy performance and constraint violation, with bounds that depend on the learned latent safety policy rather than the unknown behavior policy. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate superior safety and reward trade-offs compared to state-of-the-art baselines, and the method allows for adjustable conservativeness in safety prioritization.

cb100f740cb52abad66028526ba532d60b012949.title: Level constrained first order methods for function constrained optimization
cb100f740cb52abad66028526ba532d60b012949.research_question: How can first-order methods be developed for solving constrained optimization problems where both the objective and constraint functions are composite (i.e., sums of smooth, possibly nonconvex, and simple convex functions), and what are the complexity guarantees for such methods under various settings including stochastic, finite-sum, and nonsmooth cases?
cb100f740cb52abad66028526ba532d60b012949.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by transforming the original function-constrained optimization problem into a sequence of convex subproblems with carefully controlled constraint levels, a feasible proximal gradient method can be developed that achieves complexity bounds comparable to unconstrained gradient descent, while maintaining strict feasibility and bounded Lagrange multipliers under standard constraint qualifications.
cb100f740cb52abad66028526ba532d60b012949.proposed_method: A novel Level Constrained Proximal Gradient (LCPG) method is proposed for function-constrained optimization. The approach reformulates the original problem into a sequence of convex subproblems by partially linearizing the composite objective and constraint functions at each iteration and adding a proximal term. Each subproblem is solved exactly or approximately, requiring at most one gradient and function value computation per iteration. The feasibility of iterates is maintained by incrementally updating the constraint levels, ensuring that the iterates follow a strictly feasible path. The method is extended to handle stochastic objectives (LCSPG), finite-sum objectives (LCSVRG), and structured nonsmooth constraints using smoothing techniques. Complexity analysis is provided for both exact and inexact solutions of subproblems, leveraging a gradient descent-type framework.
cb100f740cb52abad66028526ba532d60b012949.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of constrained optimization problems, including both convex and nonconvex settings. Datasets will include synthetic and real-world instances where the objective and constraint functions are composite, and may include stochastic or finite-sum structures. Baseline methods for comparison will include penalty methods, augmented Lagrangian methods, sequential quadratic programming (SQP), and existing proximal point algorithms. Evaluation metrics will focus on the number of gradient and function evaluations required to reach approximate KKT points or specified optimality gaps, as well as feasibility and convergence properties. Both exact and inexact solution regimes for subproblems will be evaluated, and the impact of constraint qualification assumptions will be analyzed.
cb100f740cb52abad66028526ba532d60b012949.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a new feasible proximal gradient framework for function-constrained optimization that converts the problem into a sequence of efficiently solvable convex subproblems. The approach uniquely maintains strict feasibility and bounded Lagrange multipliers via a level-control mechanism, enabling convergence to stationary points under standard constraint qualifications. The complexity bounds achieved match those of unconstrained gradient descent for a broad class of problems, including nonconvex, stochastic, and nonsmooth settings, which is claimed to be new in the literature. Extensions to stochastic and variance-reduced variants, as well as structured nonsmooth constraints, further broaden the applicability and novelty of the approach.

cb1b5d949a1d711b1bd3a2924e045ad3f893252c.title: Finding Alignments Between Interpretable Causal Variables and Distributed Neural Representations
cb1b5d949a1d711b1bd3a2924e045ad3f893252c.research_question: How can interpretable high-level causal models be faithfully aligned with distributed representations in deep neural networks, overcoming the limitations of brute-force search and localist variable alignment assumptions?
