cb1b5d949a1d711b1bd3a2924e045ad3f893252c.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that distributed alignment search (DAS), which leverages gradient-based optimization and distributed (non-localist) interventions, will enable the discovery of more faithful and interpretable alignments between high-level causal variables and low-level neural representations than existing brute-force or localist methods.
cb1b5d949a1d711b1bd3a2924e045ad3f893252c.proposed_method: The proposed methodology introduces Distributed Alignment Search (DAS), a framework for aligning high-level causal variables with distributed subspaces of neural representations. Instead of brute-force enumeration, DAS uses gradient descent to optimize an orthogonal rotation matrix that maps neural activations into alternative bases, enabling soft, distributed interventions. Distributed interchange interventions are defined by rotating neural activations, intervening on specific subspaces, and rotating back, allowing individual neurons to participate in multiple conceptual roles. The alignment is learned by minimizing a differentiable loss (e.g., cross-entropy) between the counterfactual outputs of the high-level causal model and the neural network under distributed interventions, with the rotation matrix as the optimization parameter. The method is applicable to both linear and nonlinear neural networks, provided the transformation is invertible and differentiable.
cb1b5d949a1d711b1bd3a2924e045ad3f893252c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two tasks: (1) a hierarchical equality task using a three-layer feed-forward network with ReLU activations, and (2) a natural language inference (NLI) task using pretrained Transformer-based language models fine-tuned for the specific task. For each task, neural networks will be trained to perfect accuracy, and distributed alignment will be learned using DAS. Evaluation will be performed using interchange intervention accuracy (IIA), quantifying the proportion of interventions where high-level and low-level models yield equivalent effects. Baselines will include brute-force search over localist alignments (aligning high-level variables with disjoint neuron groups) and the closest localist alignment to the learned distributed alignment. Additional analyses will test the decomposability of learned distributed representations. Datasets will include synthetic data for the hierarchical equality task and a controlled NLI dataset for the language model experiments.
cb1b5d949a1d711b1bd3a2924e045ad3f893252c.novelty_claims: The proposed approach eliminates the need for computationally expensive brute-force search by introducing a gradient-based method for alignment discovery. It further removes the restrictive assumption that high-level variables must align with disjoint neuron sets, enabling the identification of distributed, overlapping representations. DAS is claimed to reveal internal conceptual structures in neural networks that are missed by prior localist or brute-force approaches, providing more faithful and interpretable causal abstractions. The method is general, theoretically grounded, and empirically shown to achieve higher or perfect interchange intervention accuracy compared to existing baselines.

cb3968152f7d93f53d24b00279a90d5071ddc85a.title: Understanding the Effects of RLHF on LLM Generalisation and Diversity
cb3968152f7d93f53d24b00279a90d5071ddc85a.research_question: How do different stages of reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) fine-tuning pipelines affect the out-of-distribution (OOD) generalisation and output diversity of large language models (LLMs) across summarisation and instruction-following tasks?
cb3968152f7d93f53d24b00279a90d5071ddc85a.hypothesis: It is hypothesised that RLHF fine-tuning improves out-of-distribution generalisation performance of LLMs compared to supervised fine-tuning, but may reduce output diversity, indicating a trade-off between these two desirable properties.
cb3968152f7d93f53d24b00279a90d5071ddc85a.proposed_method: The proposed research will systematically evaluate the effects of each stage in the RLHF pipeline—supervised fine-tuning (SFT), reward modelling (RM), and reinforcement learning (RL)—on LLMs. The methodology involves training models using SFT on demonstration data, training reward models to predict human preferences between output pairs, and fine-tuning models with RL (using Proximal Policy Optimization) to maximise the reward model output while regularising with a KL-divergence penalty to remain close to the SFT policy. Additionally, Best-of-N (BoN) sampling will be used, where multiple outputs are generated and the reward model selects the best one, to disentangle the effects of reward modelling from RL optimisation. The approach will be applied to two tasks: text summarisation and instruction following, using established datasets and evaluation protocols.
cb3968152f7d93f53d24b00279a90d5071ddc85a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the LLaMa 7B model as the base LLM, with additional experiments on OPT models of varying sizes for robustness. For summarisation, models will be trained on the TL;DR Reddit dataset and evaluated both in-distribution (TL;DR test set) and out-of-distribution (CNN/DailyMail test set). For instruction following, models will be trained and evaluated using AlpacaFarm's Self-Instruct dataset, AlpacaEval, and a newly generated Sequential Instructions OOD dataset. Evaluation will use GPT-4 as a simulated human annotator to measure preference win rates against reference outputs and head-to-head model comparisons. Output diversity will be assessed using multiple metrics: expectation-adjusted distinct N-grams (EAD), Sentence-BERT embedding cosine similarity, and NLI-based diversity, both per-input and across-inputs, with outputs sampled at temperature 1 and K=16 samples per input. Baselines will include SFT, RLHF, and BoN approaches.
cb3968152f7d93f53d24b00279a90d5071ddc85a.novelty_claims: This research provides a rigorous, multifaceted empirical analysis of how each stage of the RLHF pipeline impacts both OOD generalisation and output diversity in LLMs, across multiple tasks and datasets. It introduces a comprehensive diversity evaluation using syntactic, semantic, and logical metrics, and demonstrates an inherent trade-off between generalisation and diversity in current fine-tuning methods. The work also presents the first empirical evidence of mode collapse across inputs in RLHF-trained models and offers actionable guidance for selecting fine-tuning strategies based on application requirements. The proposed analysis framework and open-sourced codebase enable reproducible research and future investigation into methods that could improve the trade-off between generalisation and diversity.

cb40d6ed111ebe2a9620b3b65fe60597065fc183.title: Teaching Language Models to Critique via Reinforcement Learning
cb40d6ed111ebe2a9620b3b65fe60597065fc183.research_question: How can large language models be trained to effectively critique and refine their own outputs, particularly in code generation tasks, in order to improve iterative self-improvement without relying on human supervision?
cb40d6ed111ebe2a9620b3b65fe60597065fc183.hypothesis: Training a decoupled critic language model via a two-stage process—first using execution-guided critique synthesis for supervised finetuning, followed by reinforcement learning with variance reduction—will enable the critic to generate feedback that significantly improves the correction performance of a fixed generator model, leading to enhanced solution quality and reduced compounding errors during iterative critique-revision cycles.
cb40d6ed111ebe2a9620b3b65fe60597065fc183.proposed_method: A novel framework, Critic Training via Reinforcement Learning (CTRL), is developed to train a specialized critic language model that is decoupled from the task-performing generator model. The methodology consists of two main stages: (1) Execution-guided critique synthesis, where high-quality critiques are generated by reasoning over execution feedback from code solutions, and these are used for supervised finetuning of the critic. (2) Reinforced critique generation, where the critic is further optimized using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), a reinforcement learning approach that reduces training variance by leveraging group-based relative advantages instead of value networks. The critic is trained to provide structured feedback, including analysis of strengths and weaknesses, actionable suggestions, and a correctness judgment. At test time, the trained critic can be paired with any generator model to iteratively refine solutions through multiple rounds of critique and revision.
cb40d6ed111ebe2a9620b3b65fe60597065fc183.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on several code generation benchmarks, including CodeContests, LiveCodeBench, MBPP+, and JudgeBench. The training data is sourced from the TACO dataset, filtered to 18,820 programming problems with associated test cases. The critic model is based on Qwen2.5-Coder-Ins, and during training, the generator is fixed to the same model; evaluations pair the critic with both the base generator and stronger models such as GPT-4o. Baselines include zero-shot generation, self-critique, and critique-revision using other LLMs (e.g., GPT-4o). Evaluation metrics include Pass@1 (success rate), the fraction of incorrect solutions corrected (Δ↑), the fraction of correct solutions regressed (Δ↓), and F1 score for discrimination ability. The experimental setup includes multi-turn critique-revision iterations, and the effectiveness of the critic is assessed in both single-turn and multi-turn settings, as well as its ability to generalize across domains and model scales.
cb40d6ed111ebe2a9620b3b65fe60597065fc183.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a decoupled critic LLM trained via a two-stage process that combines execution-guided critique synthesis with reinforcement learning using GRPO, enabling effective and stable training without human supervision. The approach demonstrates that relatively weaker critic models can guide stronger generator models, exhibiting a weak-to-strong generalization phenomenon. The critic provides structured, actionable feedback that significantly improves solution quality and mitigates compounding errors across multiple iterations. The method enables efficient test-time scaling through iterative critique-revision and achieves substantial improvements over existing baselines on challenging code generation benchmarks. Additionally, the critic generalizes as a generative reward model, providing accurate judgments beyond its training domain.

cb5b71a622aff47014d4f28a958679629a8b6363.title: A Watermark for Large Language Models
cb5b71a622aff47014d4f28a958679629a8b6363.research_question: How can outputs from large language models be watermarked in a way that is imperceptible to humans but easily and efficiently detectable by algorithms, without requiring access to the model's parameters or API, and with minimal degradation of text quality?
cb5b71a622aff47014d4f28a958679629a8b6363.hypothesis: It is possible to embed a statistical watermark into the outputs of large language models such that the watermark is robust, efficiently detectable from short text spans, does not require model access for detection, and minimally impacts output quality.
cb5b71a622aff47014d4f28a958679629a8b6363.proposed_method: A watermarking framework will be developed that operates during the text generation process of large language models. The method involves, for each generated token, selecting a randomized subset of the vocabulary (the 'green list') using a hash seeded by prior tokens, and softly promoting the selection of green list tokens by boosting their logits by a constant delta during sampling. This approach is designed to be imperceptible to humans and does not require model retraining. Detection is performed using a statistical test (one-proportion z-test) that compares the observed frequency of green list tokens in a text segment to the expected frequency under the null hypothesis of natural text, yielding interpretable p-values. The method is further extended to support private watermarks using pseudorandom functions and secret keys, as well as robust variants that resist brute-force attacks and downstream amplification.
cb5b71a622aff47014d4f28a958679629a8b6363.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using multi-billion parameter models from the OPT family, with text prompts drawn from the RealNews-like subset of the C4 dataset. Both multinomial sampling and beam search decoding strategies will be evaluated. Baselines will include non-watermarked model outputs and human-written text. Evaluation metrics will include detection accuracy (type-I and type-II error rates), z-score statistics, area under the ROC curve (AUC), and perplexity (PPL) of generated text. Experiments will systematically vary watermark parameters (green list size gamma, logit boost delta) and analyze detection sensitivity as a function of text length and entropy. Attack robustness will be assessed against paraphrasing, tokenization, and insertion attacks.
cb5b71a622aff47014d4f28a958679629a8b6363.novelty_claims: The proposed framework enables efficient, open-source watermark detection without access to model parameters or APIs, and embeds watermarks that are statistically detectable from short text spans (as few as 25 tokens) while maintaining high text quality. The method introduces a rigorous statistical detection test with interpretable p-values, an information-theoretic analysis of watermark sensitivity, and robust private watermarking schemes. The approach is designed to be resistant to a range of adversarial attacks, including paraphrasing and tokenization manipulations, and can be tuned for public or private watermarking scenarios.

cb5e3f085caefd1f3d5e08637ab55d39e61234fc.title: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances
cb5e3f085caefd1f3d5e08637ab55d39e61234fc.research_question: How can semantic knowledge from large language models be effectively grounded in the real-world affordances of robotic agents to enable robots to follow high-level, abstract, and ambiguous natural language instructions in complex environments?
cb5e3f085caefd1f3d5e08637ab55d39e61234fc.hypothesis: Grounding large language models with affordance functions derived from pretrained robotic skills will enable robots to interpret and execute high-level natural language instructions more accurately and robustly, compared to approaches that use ungrounded language models or lack affordance grounding.
cb5e3f085caefd1f3d5e08637ab55d39e61234fc.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that integrates large language models (LLMs) with value functions representing affordances of pretrained low-level robotic skills. The method operates by first receiving a high-level natural language instruction and a set of available skills, each with a language description and a learned affordance function (value function). The LLM is used to score the likelihood that each skill's description is a valid next step for the instruction, while the affordance function estimates the probability that the skill can be successfully executed in the current state. The two probabilities are multiplied to select the most appropriate skill at each step, forming an interpretable, stepwise plan. This process is repeated iteratively, appending each selected skill to the instruction context, until the task is completed. Skills and their value functions are trained using behavioral cloning and reinforcement learning, with language-conditioned policies and value functions leveraging pretrained sentence encoders.
cb5e3f085caefd1f3d5e08637ab55d39e61234fc.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using a mobile manipulator robot in both a real office kitchen and a mock kitchen environment. The robot is equipped with a diverse set of 55+ manipulation and navigation skills, each trained with either behavioral cloning or reinforcement learning. A total of 101 natural language instructions spanning various complexities, time horizons, and embodiment conditions are evaluated. Baselines include variants without affordance grounding, without LLM grounding, and with alternative language models or skill selection strategies. Evaluation metrics include planning success rate (whether the generated skill sequence is correct) and execution success rate (whether the robot successfully completes the instruction), both assessed by human raters. Additional ablations test the impact of LLM size, skill set extensibility, chain-of-thought prompting, and multilingual queries.
cb5e3f085caefd1f3d5e08637ab55d39e61234fc.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a probabilistic framework that grounds language model outputs in real-world robotic affordances, enabling robots to decompose and execute high-level, abstract instructions using only feasible skills. The method provides interpretable, stepwise plans and demonstrates improved performance over ungrounded or less integrated baselines. The framework is shown to be scalable with improvements in language models, easily extensible to new skills, and capable of handling complex reasoning and multilingual instructions. This represents a significant advance in bridging the gap between language understanding and embodied robotic action.

cb6b0f26496a5fba104f544a5273b4bb917ac958.title: SECA: Semantically Equivalent and Coherent Attacks for Eliciting LLM Hallucinations
cb6b0f26496a5fba104f544a5273b4bb917ac958.research_question: How can realistic adversarial prompts that preserve semantic equivalence and coherence be generated to elicit hallucinations in large language models (LLMs), and what does this reveal about LLM robustness in high-stakes domains?
cb6b0f26496a5fba104f544a5273b4bb917ac958.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that adversarial prompts which are both semantically equivalent and linguistically coherent to the original input can be systematically generated and will be effective at eliciting hallucinations from state-of-the-art LLMs, thereby exposing vulnerabilities that are not revealed by existing attack methods.
cb6b0f26496a5fba104f544a5273b4bb917ac958.proposed_method: A novel framework is developed that formulates the generation of realistic adversarial attacks for hallucination elicitation as a constrained optimization problem over the prompt space, subject to semantic equivalence and coherence constraints. The approach employs a constraint-preserving zeroth-order method, leveraging a proposer LLM to generate diverse candidate prompts that are semantically equivalent to the original, guided by sampled instructions to encourage lexical and structural diversity. Each candidate prompt is then filtered by a feasibility checker LLM, which enforces strict semantic equivalence based on mutual entailment, preservation of information, and answer consistency. The most adversarial prompt is selected by maximizing the log-probability of eliciting a predefined hallucinated response from the target LLM, and the process iterates until a stopping criterion is met. This pipeline ensures that only prompts satisfying both semantic equivalence and coherence are considered, while efficiently searching the discrete prompt space.
cb6b0f26496a5fba104f544a5273b4bb917ac958.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on a filtered subset of the MMLU dataset, focusing on multiple-choice question answering tasks where the target LLMs initially answer correctly. Both open-source (e.g., Llama-3-3B/8B, Qwen-2.5-7B/14B, Llama-2-13B) and commercial (e.g., GPT-4.1-Nano, GPT-4o-Mini) models are evaluated as targets. Baselines include the use of original prompts and the Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG) method, with attack success rates (ASR@K), semantic equivalence error (SEE), and semantic coherence error (SCE) as primary metrics. Additional evaluation involves LLM-based and human annotation of hallucination types, and analysis of prompt lexical diversity and verbosity. The experimental setup includes the use of lightweight LLMs for proposing candidates and more powerful LLMs for feasibility checking, as well as automated and human-in-the-loop evaluations for robustness and reliability.
cb6b0f26496a5fba104f544a5273b4bb917ac958.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first systematic approach for generating adversarial prompts that are both semantically equivalent and coherent, addressing a key gap in realistic hallucination elicitation for LLMs. The framework formulates the problem as a constrained optimization and employs a constraint-preserving zeroth-order search, leveraging LLMs both as proposers and as feasibility checkers. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach achieves significantly higher attack success rates with minimal semantic errors compared to state-of-the-art baselines, revealing new insights into LLM brittleness under realistic prompt variations. The method also provides a scalable and automated tool for evaluating LLM robustness in practical, high-stakes applications.

cb6cc7d28d06a0d7c0d3f0d7ee551bbc86dbc3aa.title: AlpacaFarm: A Simulation Framework for Methods that Learn from Human Feedback
cb6cc7d28d06a0d7c0d3f0d7ee551bbc86dbc3aa.research_question: How can research and development of instruction-following large language models that learn from human feedback be accelerated and made more accessible, given the high cost of data collection, lack of trustworthy evaluation protocols, and absence of validated reference implementations?
cb6cc7d28d06a0d7c0d3f0d7ee551bbc86dbc3aa.hypothesis: A simulation framework that uses large language models to simulate human feedback, provides automated evaluation protocols, and includes validated reference implementations of learning-from-feedback methods can enable rapid, low-cost, and reliable development of instruction-following models, with insights transferable to real-world human feedback scenarios.
cb6cc7d28d06a0d7c0d3f0d7ee551bbc86dbc3aa.proposed_method: A simulation framework, AlpacaFarm, will be developed to address the challenges of learning from human feedback in large language models. The framework will simulate human pairwise feedback by designing prompts for oracle API LLMs (e.g., GPT-4), capturing both quality judgments and annotator variability through a pool of simulated annotators and injected noise to mimic human inconsistencies. Automated evaluation protocols will be established by measuring win-rates of candidate models against a reference model (e.g., Davinci003) using simulated annotators across a diverse set of realistic instructions, constructed by combining multiple open-source evaluation datasets. The framework will also provide validated, open-source implementations of several learning-from-pairwise-feedback (LPF) methods, including PPO, best-of-n sampling, expert iteration, DPO, Quark, and binary reward conditioning, all starting from a supervised fine-tuned base model. The end-to-end workflow will enable researchers to train, evaluate, and compare LPF algorithms in simulation before transferring insights to real human feedback settings.
cb6cc7d28d06a0d7c0d3f0d7ee551bbc86dbc3aa.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the LLaMA 7B model as the base, initially fine-tuned on a 10k instruction SFT split from the Alpaca dataset. Simulated pairwise preference data will be collected using a pool of 13 LLM-based annotators with prompt variation and injected noise, and human preference data will be collected via crowdworkers for validation. Six LPF methods and several baselines (including GPT-4, ChatGPT, Davinci001, and Alpaca7B) will be trained and evaluated both in simulation and with human feedback. Evaluation will be performed by computing win-rates against Davinci003 on a composite evaluation set of 805 instructions drawn from public datasets (Self-Instruct, OpenAssistant, Anthropic, Vicuna, Koala) and a set of real-world demo instructions. Agreement between simulated and human annotators, as well as the correlation between simulated and human-based method rankings, will be quantitatively assessed. Computational costs and qualitative changes in model outputs will also be analyzed.
cb6cc7d28d06a0d7c0d3f0d7ee551bbc86dbc3aa.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a low-cost, high-fidelity simulation environment for learning from human feedback in LLMs, enabling rapid iteration and reproducible research. It provides a novel methodology for simulating human pairwise feedback that captures both agreement and variability, validated against real human annotations. The framework offers the first open-source, validated reference implementations of multiple LPF methods in a unified setting. Automated evaluation protocols and realistic instruction datasets are designed to closely match real-world human interactions, with demonstrated high correlation between simulated and human-based method rankings. This approach significantly reduces the cost and time required for developing and benchmarking instruction-following models that learn from feedback.

cb754310302086dfbbcd098263200e2a03f65874.title: Membership Inference Attacks against Language Models via Neighbourhood Comparison
cb754310302086dfbbcd098263200e2a03f65874.research_question: How can membership inference attacks against language models be made more effective and realistic in scenarios where adversaries do not have access to in-domain reference data, and what are the privacy risks posed by such attacks under practical threat models?
cb754310302086dfbbcd098263200e2a03f65874.hypothesis: A membership inference attack that calibrates model loss scores using synthetically generated neighboring text samples—rather than reference models trained on in-domain data—will outperform existing reference-free attacks and be competitive with reference-based attacks, even when adversaries lack perfect knowledge of the training data distribution.
cb754310302086dfbbcd098263200e2a03f65874.proposed_method: A novel membership inference attack is proposed that leverages neighborhood comparison instead of relying on reference models. For a given target text sample, a set of highly similar neighbor sentences is generated through minimal word replacements using a pretrained masked language model (such as BERT), ensuring that semantics, structure, and syntax are preserved. The attack computes the difference between the loss of the target sample and the average loss of its neighbors under the target language model (e.g., GPT-2). If the target sample's loss is substantially lower than its neighbors, it is inferred to be a member of the training set, indicating potential overfitting. This approach eliminates the need for additional data or knowledge about the training data distribution and uses only grey-box access to the target model (i.e., access to loss or confidence scores). Key technical steps include neighbor generation via masked language modeling with dropout to preserve context, and a decision rule based on calibrated loss differences.
cb754310302086dfbbcd098263200e2a03f65874.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three datasets: AG News (news article summaries), Twitter (tweets from the Sentiment140 dataset), and Wikipedia (Wikitext-103 excerpts). Each dataset is split into disjoint subsets for training the target model, negative examples, and reference model training. The base GPT-2 model is fine-tuned as the target model. Baselines include the LOSS attack (reference-free) and Likelihood Ratio Attacks (LiRA) with various reference models: a base reference (pretrained GPT-2), candidate references (trained on similar but not identical data), and an oracle reference (trained on a different subset of the same data as the target). Evaluation metrics include true positive rates (TPR) at low false positive rates (FPR: 1%, 0.1%, 0.01%) and AUC. Ablation studies will vary the number of neighbors and word replacements. Additional experiments will assess robustness against differentially private training (DP-SGD) and the impact of reference model quality on attack success.
cb754310302086dfbbcd098263200e2a03f65874.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first neighborhood-based membership inference attack for language models that does not require access to in-domain reference data. It demonstrates that synthetically generated neighbor samples can serve as effective proxies for difficulty calibration, outperforming existing reference-free attacks and even matching or surpassing reference-based attacks under realistic threat models. The approach highlights the fragility of reference-based attacks when adversaries lack perfect data, and provides a more practical and broadly applicable threat model for privacy assessment in language models.

cb756ff5513facdd3f1a3798e6d1bfe846d69b59.title: Towards Tight Convex Relaxations for Contact-Rich Manipulation
cb756ff5513facdd3f1a3798e6d1bfe846d69b59.research_question: How can globally optimal motion plans for robotic systems performing contact-rich manipulation tasks be efficiently computed, while simultaneously reasoning about both discrete contact mode switches and continuous dynamics, without relying on initial guesses or suffering from poor scalability?
cb756ff5513facdd3f1a3798e6d1bfe846d69b59.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that formulating the global motion planning problem for contact-rich manipulation as a shortest-path problem in a graph of convex sets, combined with tight semidefinite convex relaxations of the underlying nonconvex dynamics, will enable efficient computation of near-globally optimal, feasible trajectories, outperforming existing local and mixed-integer optimization methods in both quality and reliability.
cb756ff5513facdd3f1a3798e6d1bfe846d69b59.proposed_method: The proposed method develops a framework that models the motion planning problem for contact-rich manipulation as a shortest-path problem in a graph of convex sets (GCS). Each vertex in this graph represents a feasible set of trajectories within a fixed contact mode, where the hybrid dynamics (including discrete contact mode switches and continuous system evolution) are captured. For each contact mode, the nonconvex, bilinear quasi-static dynamics arising from simultaneous optimization over object pose, contact locations, and contact forces are approximated using a semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxation, yielding a tight convex relaxation of the original problem. The global planning problem is then encoded as a GCS, where paths correspond to contact sequences and transitions between modes are handled via non-contact motion segments. The overall convex relaxation is solved efficiently as a single SDP, and the resulting solution is rounded to obtain a feasible, executable trajectory, with the optimality gap bounded by comparing the costs of the relaxed and rounded solutions.
cb756ff5513facdd3f1a3798e6d1bfe846d69b59.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on planar pushing tasks using both simple (box-shaped) and complex (T-shaped) slider geometries. For each geometry, 100 random initial and target configurations will be sampled uniformly, and the proposed planner will generate motion plans without requiring initial guesses. The performance will be evaluated in terms of success rate, planning time, and optimality gap (the difference between the convex relaxation and the rounded feasible solution). Baseline comparisons will be made against state-of-the-art contact-implicit trajectory optimization methods, which rely on local optimization and initial guesses. Evaluation metrics will include solution feasibility, optimality gap, and computational efficiency. Additionally, the generated plans will be executed on a real robotic system (Kuka LBR iiwa 7 R800) to demonstrate hardware feasibility, with friction parameters tuned empirically.
cb756ff5513facdd3f1a3798e6d1bfe846d69b59.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel integration of tight semidefinite convex relaxations with the graph of convex sets framework for global motion planning in contact-rich manipulation. Unlike prior methods, this framework enables simultaneous reasoning over discrete mode switches and continuous dynamics, provides near-global optimality guarantees, and does not require initial guesses. The method avoids the scalability issues of mixed-integer programming and the locality of contact-implicit optimization, achieving high reliability and solution quality even in complex, high-dimensional hybrid systems. The approach is claimed to be the first to solve the global planning-through-contact problem as a single convex program with tight relaxations, and is generalizable to more complex multi-contact manipulation tasks.

cb84e762cdffbd3dd25f865474f384bb032960b1.title: A Spectral Condition for Feature Learning
cb84e762cdffbd3dd25f865474f384bb032960b1.research_question: How can neural network training be scaled to ensure nontrivial feature learning at all widths, and what principled scaling rules should govern the initialization and update of weight matrices to achieve this goal?
cb84e762cdffbd3dd25f865474f384bb032960b1.hypothesis: Scaling the spectral norm of weight matrices and their updates according to the square root of the fan-out divided by the fan-in at each layer is sufficient and necessary to induce nontrivial feature learning in deep neural networks, even at large widths.
cb84e762cdffbd3dd25f865474f384bb032960b1.proposed_method: A new framework is proposed in which the spectral norm of each weight matrix and its corresponding gradient update in a neural network is scaled as the square root of the ratio of fan-out to fan-in at each layer. This 'spectral scaling condition' is implemented either via direct spectral normalization or by choosing layerwise initialization scales and learning rates that enforce the desired spectral norm. The approach is formalized for both linear and nonlinear multilayer perceptrons (MLPs), and generalizes to arbitrary architectures and optimizers by focusing on the operator structure of neural networks. The method provides explicit prescriptions for initialization and learning rate scaling, ensuring that both the features and their updates at each layer remain of order one with respect to width, thereby maintaining nontrivial feature evolution throughout training.
cb84e762cdffbd3dd25f865474f384bb032960b1.experiment_details: Experiments are proposed using deep MLPs of varying width and depth, trained on standard datasets such as CIFAR-10. The spectral scaling condition will be compared against popular parameterizations, including standard (Kaiming/Xavier/LeCun) initialization, neural tangent parameterization, and Frobenius-normalized update schemes. Evaluation metrics will include the norm and evolution of hidden features, spectral and Frobenius norms of weights and updates, effective rank of updates, and alignment between updates and incoming features. Empirical verification will be conducted for both small and large batch sizes, and across different activation functions (e.g., ReLU, tanh), with statistical analysis over multiple random initializations and training runs.
cb84e762cdffbd3dd25f865474f384bb032960b1.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a principled, spectral-norm-based scaling rule for both initialization and gradient updates that guarantees nontrivial feature learning at all widths, unifying and generalizing previous approaches such as maximal update parametrization. The spectral scaling condition is shown to be both necessary and sufficient for feature evolution, and is applicable to any architecture or optimizer. The method provides a conceptual advance by focusing on operator norms rather than heuristics based on entry size or Frobenius norm, and offers practical implementation strategies that streamline hyperparameter selection for large-scale deep learning.

cb8db7a6e7d5dd09fff6a3094c3c2e479f3d72d7.title: DataEnvGym: Data Generation Agents in Teacher Environments with Student Feedback
cb8db7a6e7d5dd09fff6a3094c3c2e479f3d72d7.research_question: How can the process of generating targeted training data for improving machine learning models be automated through the development of autonomous data generation agents, and what types of simulated environments best support the iterative, feedback-driven nature of this process across diverse tasks and modalities?
cb8db7a6e7d5dd09fff6a3094c3c2e479f3d72d7.hypothesis: Automated data generation agents, when placed in appropriately structured teacher environments that provide iterative feedback from student models, can effectively generate targeted training data that improves student model performance across a range of tasks. Furthermore, increasing the structure and interpretability of the environment's state and action spaces will enhance the controllability, effectiveness, and interpretability of the data generation process.
cb8db7a6e7d5dd09fff6a3094c3c2e479f3d72d7.proposed_method: A modular testbed, termed DATAENVGYM, will be developed to simulate teacher environments for data generation agents. The framework will formalize data generation as a sequential decision-making process, where an agent, composed of a data generation policy and a data generation engine, interacts with a student model. The agent receives feedback on student performance, plans new training data generation, and iteratively updates the student model. Three environment variants will be implemented: (1) an open-ended environment with unstructured state and action spaces, (2) a skill-list environment with automatically inferred, human-interpretable skill-based state representations, and (3) a skill-tree environment with hierarchical skill representations and structured actions (explore/exploit) for curriculum control. Skill discovery and organization modules will be integrated to automatically extract and hierarchically organize skills from data using large language models. The system will support plug-and-play modules for skill discovery, organization, and data generation, facilitating extensibility and benchmarking.
cb8db7a6e7d5dd09fff6a3094c3c2e479f3d72d7.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across four domains: mathematics (MATH), visual question answering (GQA, NaturalBench), programming (LiveCodeBench), and tool-use (MnMs). For each domain, instruction-tuned student models (e.g., PaliGemma-3B, Gemma-2-2B, Llama-3-8B) will be used, and teacher agents will be instantiated with LLM-based policies (e.g., GPT-4o) and, for multimodal tasks, text-to-image models (e.g., SDXL-Turbo). Baseline agents will be evaluated in each environment variant, comparing policies that condition on student feedback ('WithState') to those that do not ('NoState'). Evaluation metrics will include task-specific accuracy, skill-level performance, and other fine-grained measures (e.g., plan accuracy, tool precision/recall/F1). Training will proceed for a fixed number of iterations, with validation accuracy used to select the best model checkpoints. Additional analyses will examine the impact of skill rarity, question difficulty, and training dynamics over iterations.
cb8db7a6e7d5dd09fff6a3094c3c2e479f3d72d7.novelty_claims: The proposed testbed introduces the first general-purpose, modular environment for developing and benchmarking autonomous data generation agents in a closed-loop, feedback-driven setting. It supports multiple levels of structure in state and action spaces, including novel skill-list and hierarchical skill-tree representations, enabling interpretable and controllable curriculum design. The framework facilitates rapid prototyping and evaluation of data generation policies, engines, and skill discovery methods across diverse tasks and modalities. By enabling systematic comparison of agent architectures and feedback mechanisms, the testbed lays the groundwork for future advances in automated model improvement and curriculum learning.

cb9750d21838f59c4281f7ea456ebad394265549.title: Missing Data Imputation and Acquisition with Deep Hierarchical Models and Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
cb9750d21838f59c4281f7ea456ebad394265549.research_question: How can missing data imputation and active feature acquisition be improved for heterogeneous, mixed-type, and incomplete datasets using deep generative models?
cb9750d21838f59c4281f7ea456ebad394265549.hypothesis: Employing a hierarchical variational autoencoder with Hamiltonian Monte Carlo-based inference and automatic hyperparameter tuning will yield more accurate missing data imputation and active feature acquisition than existing single-layer, Gaussian-based VAE approaches.
cb9750d21838f59c4281f7ea456ebad394265549.proposed_method: A novel deep hierarchical variational autoencoder (HH-VAEM) will be developed to handle mixed-type, incomplete data. The approach consists of a two-stage modeling process: first, independent marginal VAEs are trained for each feature to encode mixed-type data into marginal Gaussian posteriors; second, a hierarchical dependency VAE captures inter-feature dependencies using a hierarchical latent space. Inference over the hierarchical latent variables is performed using Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) with automatic hyperparameter tuning, and a hierarchical reparameterization technique is introduced to stabilize HMC sampling in deep latent hierarchies. The method also incorporates a sampling-based strategy for active feature acquisition, estimating mutual information via histogram-based estimators for efficient and accurate sequential information gain computation.
cb9750d21838f59c4281f7ea456ebad394265549.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on ten UCI datasets with mixed-type data, as well as high-dimensional image datasets such as MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CelebA. Missing data will be introduced at varying rates in both training and testing phases to simulate real-world incomplete data scenarios. The proposed HH-VAEM will be compared against several baselines, including single-layer Gaussian VAEM, importance-weighted MIWAEM, hierarchical Gaussian H-VAEM, and one-layer HMC-VAEM. Evaluation metrics will include negative log-likelihood (NLL) for imputation and prediction tasks, root mean squared error (RMSE) for sequential active information acquisition (SAIA), and qualitative assessments via image inpainting. Both quantitative and qualitative results will be reported, with ablation studies to assess the contribution of hierarchical modeling and HMC inference.
cb9750d21838f59c4281f7ea456ebad394265549.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first hierarchical VAE for mixed-type incomplete data that leverages HMC with automatic hyperparameter tuning for improved approximate inference. A hierarchical reparameterization technique is proposed to address pathological behavior in HMC sampling over deep latent hierarchies. Additionally, a novel sampling-based mutual information estimator for active feature acquisition is developed, offering lower bias and greater efficiency than Gaussian-based alternatives. The combined framework is claimed to achieve superior performance in missing data imputation, supervised learning with missing features, and active feature acquisition compared to existing baselines.

cba618cef4844f37f3ab8ee7dd34633672848eed.title: Breaking Neural Network Scaling Laws with Modularity
cba618cef4844f37f3ab8ee7dd34633672848eed.research_question: How can modular neural network architectures be leveraged to improve generalization in high-dimensional tasks, and what theoretical and practical mechanisms enable modular networks to break the exponential sample complexity scaling laws observed in nonmodular neural networks?
cba618cef4844f37f3ab8ee7dd34633672848eed.hypothesis: Modular neural networks, when appropriately aligned with the modular structure of tasks, can achieve generalization with sample complexity that is independent of the input dimensionality, thereby breaking the exponential scaling law that constrains nonmodular networks.
cba618cef4844f37f3ab8ee7dd34633672848eed.proposed_method: A theoretical framework will be developed to model neural network generalization, synthesizing existing results and extending them to both monolithic and modular architectures. The approach will involve constructing a regression model where the task output is a sum of module outputs, each processing a low-dimensional projection of the input. Explicit, non-asymptotic expressions for generalization error will be derived for both monolithic and modular networks, demonstrating the dependence (or independence) of sample complexity on input dimensionality. Building on these insights, a novel learning rule will be proposed to align neural network modules with the underlying modular structure of the task. This learning rule will use a kernel-based objective to optimize module input projections, minimizing the norm of module parameters required to fit the training data, and will be applicable to both linear and nonlinear module projections. After initialization, all module parameters, including projections, will be further optimized via gradient descent on the task loss.
cba618cef4844f37f3ab8ee7dd34633672848eed.experiment_details: Empirical validation will be conducted on parametrically controllable, high-dimensional tasks, including a modular sine wave regression task and a new Compositional CIFAR-10 benchmark. Neural networks of varying depth, width, and modularity will be trained and evaluated, with key variables including input dimensionality, number of modules, model size, and training set size. Baseline comparisons will include monolithic (nonmodular) networks, randomly initialized modular networks, and the proposed modular network with the new learning rule. Evaluation metrics will include test loss (for regression) and accuracy (for classification), as well as sample complexity required to achieve a fixed generalization error. Additional experiments will test out-of-distribution generalization, robustness to distribution shifts, and the ability to recover true module directions. Ablation studies will assess the impact of using ground-truth module directions and the adaptability of learned module projections.
cba618cef4844f37f3ab8ee7dd34633672848eed.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first explicit, non-asymptotic theoretical expressions for generalization error in modular neural networks, demonstrating that modular architectures can achieve sample complexity independent of task dimensionality. A novel, practical learning rule is developed to align neural network modules with the modular structure of tasks, overcoming known optimization difficulties in modular architectures. The proposed method is validated on both linear and nonlinear modular tasks, showing improved generalization both in- and out-of-distribution compared to existing baselines. The approach is broadly applicable to a range of modular architectures and provides new theoretical and empirical insights into breaking neural network scaling laws through modularity.

cbad2da88a77bffaa237496c15c85518575bfb59.title: Referring Multi-Object Tracking
cbad2da88a77bffaa237496c15c85518575bfb59.research_question: How can multi-object tracking in videos be guided by natural language expressions to flexibly and accurately ground and track an arbitrary number of semantically referred objects, including those with dynamic temporal status, in complex real-world scenarios?
cbad2da88a77bffaa237496c15c85518575bfb59.hypothesis: Integrating cross-modal reasoning between visual and linguistic features within a transformer-based, end-to-end online tracking framework will enable accurate, flexible, and temporally-aware multi-object tracking guided by natural language expressions, outperforming existing single-object and image-based referring understanding methods.
cbad2da88a77bffaa237496c15c85518575bfb59.proposed_method: A novel end-to-end transformer-based architecture, termed TransRMOT, will be developed to address referring multi-object tracking (RMOT). The method will employ a cross-modal early-fusion module to densely integrate visual features from video frames and linguistic features from a language query, followed by a stack of deformable attention layers for refined cross-modal representation. The decoder will utilize two types of queries: track queries, which propagate instance embeddings across frames for temporal association, and detect queries, which identify new-born objects in the current frame. A referent head will output class, bounding box, and referring scores for each object instance, enabling the model to flexibly predict and track all objects matching the given language expression throughout the video. The model will be trained using a combination of detection, association, and referring losses, and optimized for both frame-level detection and temporal association.
cbad2da88a77bffaa237496c15c85518575bfb59.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a newly constructed benchmark, Refer-KITTI, derived from the KITTI dataset and annotated with 818 language expressions across 18 videos, each expression referring to an average of 10.7 objects with high temporal dynamics. The proposed method will be compared against both CNN-based and transformer-based multi-object tracking baselines, each enhanced with cross-modal fusion modules for fair comparison. Evaluation will use the HOTA metric, which balances detection and association accuracy, as well as additional metrics such as DetA, AssA, DetRe, DetPr, AssRe, AssPr, and LocA. Ablation studies will assess the impact of cross-modal fusion, linguistic extractor choice, association strategy, and referring threshold. Generalization will be evaluated by varying the ratios of expressions and videos used for training, and by testing on out-of-distribution datasets such as BDD100K.
cbad2da88a77bffaa237496c15c85518575bfb59.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first general framework and benchmark for referring multi-object tracking (RMOT), enabling language-guided tracking of an arbitrary number of objects with dynamic temporal status in videos. Key innovations include the design of a cross-modal early-fusion module within a transformer architecture, the decoupling of object queries into track and detect queries for robust temporal association, and the creation of the Refer-KITTI benchmark with high flexibility and low annotation cost. The approach is claimed to substantially outperform existing single-object and image-based referring understanding methods, as well as state-of-the-art multi-object trackers adapted for cross-modal input.

cbaf689fd9ea9bc939510019d90535d6249b3367.title: Jamba: A Hybrid Transformer-Mamba Language Model
cbaf689fd9ea9bc939510019d90535d6249b3367.research_question: How can a hybrid architecture combining Transformer, state-space (Mamba), and mixture-of-experts (MoE) layers be designed to achieve high performance, efficient long-context processing, and manageable memory footprint in large language models?
cbaf689fd9ea9bc939510019d90535d6249b3367.hypothesis: A hybrid architecture that interleaves Transformer and Mamba layers, augmented with mixture-of-experts modules, will provide state-of-the-art language modeling capabilities, support efficient processing of very long contexts, and maintain a smaller memory and compute footprint compared to vanilla Transformer-based models of similar or larger size.
cbaf689fd9ea9bc939510019d90535d6249b3367.proposed_method: A novel large language model architecture will be developed by interleaving blocks of Transformer and Mamba layers in a specified ratio, forming a hybrid stack. Within these blocks, mixture-of-experts (MoE) modules will be integrated into selected multi-layer perceptron (MLP) layers, with a configurable number of experts per layer and top-K expert selection per token. The architecture will be parameterized by the number of layers, the ratio of attention to Mamba layers, the frequency of MoE application, and the number of experts and active experts per token. RMSNorm normalization will be applied in Mamba layers to stabilize training, and explicit positional encodings will be omitted for Mamba layers. Additional architectural features will include grouped-query attention, SwiGLU activations, and load balancing for MoE. The model will be designed to fit within the memory constraints of a single 80GB GPU, supporting context lengths up to 256K tokens, with flexibility for other configurations.
cbaf689fd9ea9bc939510019d90535d6249b3367.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a wide range of standard academic language model benchmarks, including commonsense reasoning (HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-E, ARC-Challenge, PIQA), reading comprehension (BoolQ, QuAC), mathematical and code reasoning (GSM8K, HumanEval), aggregate benchmarks (MMLU, BBH), and others (NaturalQuestions, TruthfulQA). Long-context capabilities will be evaluated using synthetic 'needle-in-a-haystack' retrieval and naturalistic few-shot classification and QA tasks (Trec-Fine, NLUIntent, Banking77, CLINC150, NarrativeQA, LongFQA, CUAD, SFiction) with context lengths up to 256K tokens. Baseline comparisons will include Llama-2 (13B, 70B), Mixtral-8x7B, and Gemma. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, F1, and throughput (tokens/second), with experiments run on NVIDIA H100/A100 GPUs using both quantized and non-quantized weights. Ablation studies will explore the impact of varying the ratio of attention to Mamba layers, MoE configuration, and normalization strategies.
cbaf689fd9ea9bc939510019d90535d6249b3367.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first production-grade hybrid architecture that interleaves Transformer and state-space (Mamba) layers at scale, combined with mixture-of-experts modules for increased capacity and efficiency. The architecture achieves a substantial reduction in key-value cache memory requirements (up to 8x smaller than vanilla Transformers), supports unprecedented long-context processing (up to 256K tokens in production-grade models), and delivers state-of-the-art performance with significantly improved throughput and memory efficiency. The design space offers flexibility for resource- and objective-specific configurations, and the model demonstrates that hybrid attention-SSM architectures can match or surpass the performance of leading Transformer-only models while enabling efficient scaling.

cbcc0a5c647c671354688a503e4bce58fbda6d7a.title: Exploring the Whole Rashomon Set of Sparse Decision Trees
cbcc0a5c647c671354688a503e4bce58fbda6d7a.research_question: How can the complete set of nearly-optimal sparse decision trees (the Rashomon set) be efficiently enumerated, represented, and analyzed to provide practitioners with a comprehensive view of model choices and their properties for a given dataset?
cbcc0a5c647c671354688a503e4bce58fbda6d7a.hypothesis: It is possible to develop an efficient algorithm that can fully enumerate and represent the Rashomon set of sparse decision trees for real-world datasets, enabling practical exploration of all nearly-optimal models and supporting advanced analyses such as variable importance, robustness to data shifts, and evaluation under alternative metrics.
cbcc0a5c647c671354688a503e4bce58fbda6d7a.proposed_method: A novel algorithm, TreeFARMS, is proposed to enumerate the complete Rashomon set of sparse decision trees for a given dataset. The method leverages dynamic programming with customized analytical bounds to prune the search space, ensuring only trees within a specified objective threshold are considered. The Rashomon set is stored in a specialized hierarchical data structure (ModelSet), which groups together trees and subtrees sharing the same objective value to maximize memory and computational efficiency. The approach includes algorithms for extracting the Rashomon set from the dependency graph and for uniform sampling when the set is too large to store in memory. The method also supports the construction of Rashomon sets for alternative metrics (e.g., balanced accuracy, F1-score) and enables analysis of the set's sensitivity to data perturbations.
cbcc0a5c647c671354688a503e4bce58fbda6d7a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of real-world datasets, including those from the UCI Machine Learning Repository (e.g., Car Evaluation, Congressional Voting Records, Monk2, Iris), the COMPAS criminal recidivism dataset, the FICO credit risk dataset, and several coupon-related survey datasets. The performance and completeness of TreeFARMS will be compared against baselines such as Bayesian Additive Regression Trees (BART), Random Forests, CART, and GOSDT on subsets of data. Evaluation metrics will include the number of distinct trees found, runtime, and the ability to recover the full Rashomon set. Additional analyses will examine variable importance across the Rashomon set using model class reliance (MCR), the relationship between Rashomon sets for different metrics, and the robustness of the Rashomon set to removal of data subsets.
cbcc0a5c647c671354688a503e4bce58fbda6d7a.novelty_claims: The proposed method provides the first complete enumeration of the Rashomon set for a highly nonlinear, discrete function class (sparse decision trees) on real-world problems. The specialized ModelSet data structure enables efficient storage, querying, and sampling of exponentially large sets of models. The approach supports new analyses, such as exact computation of variable importance ranges (MCR) for all well-performing trees, direct construction of Rashomon sets for alternative metrics from the accuracy Rashomon set, and robust analysis of model stability under data perturbations. This work shifts the paradigm from selecting a single optimal model to enabling user-driven exploration of all nearly-optimal, interpretable models.

cbd81507197e2d32b6f6c8ac99039f3a607ee8f1.title: VerilogEval: Evaluating Large Language Models for Verilog Code Generation
cbd81507197e2d32b6f6c8ac99039f3a607ee8f1.research_question: How can large language models be systematically evaluated and improved for the task of Verilog code generation, and what benchmarking framework and datasets are required to enable robust, automated, and comprehensive assessment of LLM performance in hardware design and verification?
cbd81507197e2d32b6f6c8ac99039f3a607ee8f1.hypothesis: Supervised fine-tuning of large language models using synthetic problem-code pairs generated by LLMs will significantly improve the models' ability to generate functionally correct Verilog code, as measured by automated simulation-based benchmarks. Furthermore, a diverse and well-curated evaluation dataset will provide a more accurate and robust assessment of LLM capabilities in Verilog code generation.
cbd81507197e2d32b6f6c8ac99039f3a607ee8f1.proposed_method: A benchmarking framework will be developed to evaluate large language models on Verilog code generation tasks. The framework will include a comprehensive evaluation dataset of 156 problems sourced from the HDLBits platform, covering a wide range of Verilog coding challenges such as combinational circuits, finite state machines, debugging, and testbench construction. Two types of problem descriptions will be created: manually curated (human) and LLM-generated (machine), both converted to text-only formats suitable for LLM input. Automated functional correctness testing will be implemented by comparing the simulation outputs of generated Verilog code to golden reference solutions using the ICARUS Verilog simulator in a sandboxed Docker environment. Additionally, a synthetic supervised fine-tuning dataset will be constructed by leveraging LLMs to generate problem descriptions paired with Verilog code, filtered for quality and self-containment. Models will be fine-tuned on this dataset to align them more closely with the Verilog code generation task.
cbd81507197e2d32b6f6c8ac99039f3a607ee8f1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using several large language models, including the CodeGen series (with model sizes ranging from 350M to 16B parameters) and OpenAI's gpt-3.5-turbo and gpt-4. Models will be evaluated on the VerilogEval benchmark, which consists of both human- and machine-generated problem descriptions. The primary evaluation metric will be pass@k (for k = 1, 5, 10), which measures the proportion of problems for which at least one of k generated code samples passes all functional tests. Each model will generate multiple code completions per problem, and results will be compared against baselines and across different model sizes and fine-tuning strategies. Fine-tuning experiments will use synthetic SFT data generated from open-source Verilog code, filtered for self-containment and quality, with hyperparameters such as learning rate, batch size, and sampling strategies specified. Additional experiments will assess the impact of SFT data quality by introducing mismatched problem-code pairs and measuring performance degradation.
cbd81507197e2d32b6f6c8ac99039f3a607ee8f1.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first open-source, large-scale, and diverse benchmark specifically designed for evaluating LLMs on Verilog code generation, addressing limitations in the scope, diversity, and automation of prior benchmarks. The framework enables fully automated, simulation-based functional correctness evaluation, overcoming the inadequacies of text-based metrics such as BLEU. The approach also demonstrates that LLMs can be effectively bootstrapped to generate high-quality synthetic supervised fine-tuning data, leading to substantial improvements in Verilog code generation performance. The methodology provides a reproducible and extensible foundation for future research in LLM-based hardware design automation.

cbeca8850c37cb3cca794091c888b00a193c2b59.title: Fine-Tuning of Continuous-Time Diffusion Models as Entropy-Regularized Control
cbeca8850c37cb3cca794091c888b00a193c2b59.research_question: How can diffusion models be fine-tuned to optimize a user-specified reward function while maintaining sample diversity and staying close to the original data distribution, thereby mitigating issues such as reward collapse and overoptimization?
cbeca8850c37cb3cca794091c888b00a193c2b59.hypothesis: Fine-tuning diffusion models via an entropy-regularized control framework, which incorporates both reward maximization and KL-divergence regularization against the pre-trained model, will enable the generation of diverse, high-reward samples that remain close to the original data distribution and avoid reward collapse.
cbeca8850c37cb3cca794091c888b00a193c2b59.proposed_method: A novel fine-tuning framework is proposed that formulates the problem as an entropy-regularized stochastic control task over continuous-time diffusion models. The approach introduces a loss function combining a terminal reward (reflecting the user-specified objective) and an entropy regularization term (KL divergence) with respect to the pre-trained diffusion model, applied to both the drift term and the initial distribution. The optimal control is derived using neural stochastic differential equations (SDEs), where the drift and initial distribution are learned to maximize the expected reward while penalizing deviations from the original data distribution. The method leverages a value function estimated via empirical risk minimization and solves the resulting control problems using neural SDE solvers, enabling tractable optimization and sampling from the target distribution. The framework is instantiated in an algorithm (ELEGANT) that alternately learns the value function, the optimal initial distribution, and the optimal drift, resulting in a fine-tuned sampler that preserves diversity and sample quality.
cbeca8850c37cb3cca794091c888b00a193c2b59.experiment_details: Experiments are proposed across multiple domains, including image generation (using Stable Diffusion v1.5 and the LAION Aesthetics Predictor V2 as the reward function) and biological sequence generation (using GFP and TFBind datasets with reward models trained on fluorescence and binding activity, respectively). Baselines for comparison include guidance-based sampling, PPO with KL-penalized reinforcement learning, and existing direct reward backpropagation methods without KL regularization. Evaluation metrics include the mean reward of generated samples, KL divergence from the original data distribution, and diversity measures such as Levenshtein distance or sample variance. The experimental setup involves pre-training diffusion models on standard datasets, then fine-tuning them using the proposed method and baselines, with performance assessed via quantitative metrics and qualitative sample analysis.
cbeca8850c37cb3cca794091c888b00a193c2b59.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a theoretically principled and computationally efficient entropy-regularized control approach for fine-tuning continuous-time diffusion models. Unlike prior methods, it jointly learns both the drift and initial distribution using neural SDEs, incorporates a double entropy regularization to maintain proximity to the pre-trained model, and provides formal guarantees on the preservation of diversity and avoidance of reward collapse. The method is empirically validated across both image and biological sequence domains, demonstrating superior performance in reward maximization, sample diversity, and mitigation of overoptimization compared to existing baselines.

cc34cf5019b9886885e543bbca1030979a99a6c6.title: Running Markov Chain Monte Carlo on Modern Hardware and Software
cc34cf5019b9886885e543bbca1030979a99a6c6.research_question: How can Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods be efficiently accelerated using modern parallel hardware (such as GPUs and TPUs) and deep learning software frameworks (such as JAX and PyTorch), and what are the practical benefits and challenges of such acceleration for statistical inference workloads?
cc34cf5019b9886885e543bbca1030979a99a6c6.hypothesis: MCMC workloads can be significantly accelerated by leveraging modern parallel hardware and deep learning-oriented software frameworks, resulting in substantial improvements in sampling efficiency and throughput compared to traditional CPU-based workflows.
cc34cf5019b9886885e543bbca1030979a99a6c6.proposed_method: A framework will be developed for executing MCMC algorithms, specifically Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) and No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS), on modern parallel hardware such as GPUs. The approach involves implementing probabilistic models and their log-densities using JAX, taking advantage of its automatic differentiation and vectorized operations to enable efficient computation of gradients and parallel execution of multiple chains. The method will utilize program transformations such as automatic vectorization (via jax.vmap) to parallelize MCMC chains, and will reparameterize constrained parameters using bijective transformations to allow unconstrained optimization in R^d. The implementation will avoid Python-native control flow in favor of JAX's functional control flow primitives to ensure compatibility with hardware acceleration and compiler optimizations.
cc34cf5019b9886885e543bbca1030979a99a6c6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a sparse Bayesian logistic regression model using the German Credit dataset (N=1000 observations, 24 features). Both HMC and NUTS will be implemented using the BlackJAX library, with diagnostics computed via ArviZ. Performance will be benchmarked on an Nvidia P100 GPU and a 28-core Intel Xeon Platinum 8273CL CPU, using 64 parallel chains and 1000 MCMC steps per chain. Pre-tuned hyperparameters (step size, mass matrix, leapfrog steps) will be used for fair comparison. Evaluation metrics will include wall-clock time, effective sample size (ESS), and ESS per second, with a focus on the global scale parameter τ. Additional experiments will vary the number of parallel chains to assess scalability and hardware utilization.
cc34cf5019b9886885e543bbca1030979a99a6c6.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a systematic approach for adapting MCMC workflows to modern parallel hardware using deep learning software frameworks, demonstrating dramatic speedups over traditional CPU-based methods. The approach leverages automatic differentiation, vectorized computation, and functional control flow to enable efficient, scalable, and hardware-agnostic MCMC sampling. The research also provides practical insights and patterns for practitioners, highlighting both the benefits and potential pitfalls of running MCMC on accelerators.

cc3d6dd74dbd162d1f9e2ebc6282ef16d59c4d3c.title: Are Language Models Efficient Reasoners? A Perspective from Logic Programming
cc3d6dd74dbd162d1f9e2ebc6282ef16d59c4d3c.research_question: How efficiently can language models perform deductive reasoning in the presence of irrelevant information, as assessed through a formal logic programming framework applied to natural language proofs?
cc3d6dd74dbd162d1f9e2ebc6282ef16d59c4d3c.hypothesis: Language models, when presented with reasoning tasks containing irrelevant information, will exhibit reduced efficiency in deductive inference, generating proofs that include unnecessary inference steps and detours through irrelevant theorems, even when final answer accuracy remains high.
cc3d6dd74dbd162d1f9e2ebc6282ef16d59c4d3c.proposed_method: A novel framework will be developed to evaluate the efficiency of language model reasoning by aligning natural language proofs generated by the model with shortest possible proofs derived from formal logic programs. This framework will utilize verbalized logic programs, where each theorem in the logic program is associated with a set of natural language strings, enabling mapping between model outputs and formal deductions. Efficiency will be quantified by comparing the size of the model-generated proof to the size of the shortest proof, penalizing unnecessary inference steps. The methodology will disentangle inefficiency due to unnecessary deductive steps from verbosity in natural language, focusing primarily on the former.
cc3d6dd74dbd162d1f9e2ebc6282ef16d59c4d3c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a dataset of grade school math word problems (GSM), systematically augmented with varying numbers and types of irrelevant axioms that differ in semantic overlap with the goal theorem. Multiple language models, including both general-purpose and reasoning-specialized models, will be evaluated. Baselines will include problems with only relevant axioms (control) and problems matched for input length but without irrelevant content. Evaluation metrics will include answer accuracy, proof efficiency (ratio of shortest proof size to model proof size), and the proportion of irrelevant theorems generated. The experimental setup will control for agent and entity overlap between relevant and irrelevant axioms, and both non-ground and ground queries will be tested.
cc3d6dd74dbd162d1f9e2ebc6282ef16d59c4d3c.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a formal, logic programming-based framework for evaluating the efficiency of language model reasoning, moving beyond correctness to assess the ability to avoid unnecessary inference. The approach enables automatic, fine-grained mapping of natural language proofs to formal deductive steps, and systematically manipulates the presence and nature of irrelevant information in reasoning tasks. This framework generalizes previous approaches by allowing for multiple, arbitrarily placed irrelevant axioms and provides new insights into the search heuristics and inefficiencies of language models in deductive reasoning.

cc435dddfb8042b518444502507bbc1e62c1a3ff.title: Strategic Classification with Graph Neural Networks
cc435dddfb8042b518444502507bbc1e62c1a3ff.research_question: How can graph-based classifiers, specifically Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), be learned in environments where users may strategically modify their features in response to the classifier, and what are the implications of interdependent user responses induced by graph structures on the robustness and performance of such classifiers?
cc435dddfb8042b518444502507bbc1e62c1a3ff.hypothesis: Learning algorithms that explicitly model and anticipate strategic, interdependent user responses in graph-based classification settings can achieve greater robustness and potentially improved predictive performance compared to methods that assume independent or non-strategic user behavior.
cc435dddfb8042b518444502507bbc1e62c1a3ff.proposed_method: A differentiable framework will be developed for learning graph-based classifiers that are robust to strategic user behavior. The method will focus on linear GNN architectures, such as Simplified Graph Convolution (SGC), where node embeddings are computed as weighted combinations of a node's features and those of its neighbors. Strategic user responses will be modeled as myopic best-responses over multiple rounds, where each user iteratively updates their features to maximize their own utility, accounting for both the classifier and the influence of their neighbors. This response process will be implemented as a stack of differentiable neural layers, each corresponding to a round of strategic adjustment, with a closed-form, projection-like operator used to compute optimal feature modifications. The entire process will be made differentiable by smoothing non-differentiable operations (e.g., hard thresholds) with sigmoidal approximations, enabling end-to-end training via gradient-based optimization.
cc435dddfb8042b518444502507bbc1e62c1a3ff.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world networked datasets. Synthetic data will be generated with controlled feature distributions and graph structures to systematically vary the degree of graph influence and strategic behavior. Real data experiments will use standard GNN benchmarks such as Cora, CiteSeer, and PubMed, adapted to binary classification and inductive settings. Baselines will include naïve graph-based classifiers that do not account for strategic behavior, as well as non-strategic benchmarks. Evaluation metrics will primarily be classification accuracy, with additional analysis of robustness to varying levels of user movement (modification cost), number of strategic response rounds (depth), and sensitivity to hyperparameters. The experimental setup will include ablations on the number of response layers and the maximum allowed feature modification distance.
cc435dddfb8042b518444502507bbc1e62c1a3ff.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a practical, differentiable framework for learning graph-based classifiers that are robust to strategic, interdependent user responses—a setting largely unexplored in prior strategic classification literature, which has focused on independent responses and linear models. The method provides a closed-form, differentiable operator for modeling multi-round, graph-dependent strategic behavior, enabling efficient end-to-end training. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate that explicitly accounting for strategic behavior not only mitigates the vulnerability of graph-based models to gaming but, in some cases, can harness user incentives to improve system performance. This work bridges the gap between strategic classification and graph-based learning, offering new insights into the interplay between social structure, user incentives, and robust predictive modeling.

cc57a02307b77585f69779cca2937dedc69006d6.title: Detecting Edit Failures In Large Language Models: An Improved Specificity Benchmark
cc57a02307b77585f69779cca2937dedc69006d6.research_question: How can the specificity of model editing techniques for large language models be more accurately measured, and what are the limitations of current specificity benchmarks in detecting unwanted side effects of model edits?
cc57a02307b77585f69779cca2937dedc69006d6.hypothesis: Current specificity benchmarks for model editing in large language models fail to detect significant unwanted side effects, and introducing a dynamic benchmark along with a KL divergence-based metric will provide a more sensitive and comprehensive evaluation of specificity.
cc57a02307b77585f69779cca2937dedc69006d6.proposed_method: A dynamic specificity benchmark, named COUNTERFACT+, will be developed by modifying existing neighborhood prompts from the COUNTERFACT dataset to include the context of the model edit, thereby increasing the likelihood of surfacing unintended side effects. In addition to existing metrics such as Neighborhood Score (NS) and Neighborhood Magnitude (NM), a new metric—Neighborhood KL Divergence (NKL)—will be introduced, which measures the KL divergence between the next-token probability distributions of the edited and unedited models over the full vocabulary. This approach will be used to systematically evaluate the specificity of recent model editing techniques, including ROME, MEMIT, and fine-tuning with L-infinity norm constraints (FT-L), across multiple model sizes (GPT-2-medium, GPT-2-XL, GPT-J). The methodology involves performing targeted model edits, generating dynamic neighborhood prompts, and computing all three specificity metrics to assess the presence and extent of unintended side effects.
cc57a02307b77585f69779cca2937dedc69006d6.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize the COUNTERFACT dataset, which contains 21,919 non-factual statements, and its dynamic extension COUNTERFACT+, where neighborhood prompts are prepended with the model edit statement. The evaluation will be conducted on GPT-2-medium, GPT-2-XL, and GPT-J (6B) models, applying three model editing methods: ROME, MEMIT, and FT-L. For each edit, specificity will be assessed using NS, NM, and the newly proposed NKL metric. Baseline comparisons will include the unedited models and FT-L, while ROME and MEMIT serve as state-of-the-art model editing techniques. Evaluation metrics will be reported with 99% confidence intervals, and performance will be analyzed across both the original and dynamic benchmarks to determine the sensitivity of each metric to unwanted side effects.
cc57a02307b77585f69779cca2937dedc69006d6.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces COUNTERFACT+, a dynamic specificity benchmark that adapts to the tested model edit and is more sensitive than previous benchmarks. It also proposes Neighborhood KL Divergence (NKL), a principled metric that evaluates specificity based on the full probability distribution rather than only directly implicated tokens. This approach is expected to reveal previously undetected specificity failures in existing model editing techniques and provide a more robust framework for evaluating and developing safe and effective model edits in large language models.

cc5b6a71b2598cb147c757caf84ac9f26354305b.title: Trajectory Bellman Residual Minimization: A Simple Value-Based Method for LLM Reasoning
cc5b6a71b2598cb147c757caf84ac9f26354305b.research_question: Can value-based reinforcement learning methods, specifically trajectory-level Bellman residual minimization, provide an efficient and principled alternative to policy-based methods for enhancing reasoning capabilities in large language models (LLMs), particularly in mathematical reasoning tasks?
