cc5b6a71b2598cb147c757caf84ac9f26354305b.hypothesis: Trajectory-level Bellman residual minimization, when adapted for LLMs using model logits as Q-values, will achieve comparable or superior performance to policy-based RL methods (such as PPO and GRPO) on mathematical reasoning benchmarks, while reducing computational and memory overhead and maintaining theoretical guarantees of convergence.
cc5b6a71b2598cb147c757caf84ac9f26354305b.proposed_method: A novel value-based reinforcement learning algorithm, Trajectory Bellman Residual Minimization (TBRM), will be developed for LLM reasoning tasks. The method minimizes the squared Bellman residual at the trajectory level, using the model's own logits to parameterize Q-values, and operates under the KL-regularized RL framework. TBRM eliminates the need for critics, advantage estimation, importance sampling, or clipping, and can function with only one rollout per prompt, though it scales to multiple rollouts. The optimization objective regresses the model's logits onto a single trajectory-level Bellman residual, leveraging only the outcome reward for each trajectory, and updates model parameters via gradient descent. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to prove convergence to the near-optimal KL-regularized policy from arbitrary off-policy data, utilizing recent advances in trajectory-level change-of-measure analysis.
cc5b6a71b2598cb147c757caf84ac9f26354305b.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on six standard mathematical reasoning benchmarks: AIME24, AIME25, AMC23, MATH500, Minerva Math, and OlympiadBench. The DAPO prompt set (17.4k math problems) will be used for training, with models Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B and Qwen2.5-Math-7B evaluated. Baselines will include Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), with comparable hyperparameters and training steps. Evaluation metrics will be accuracy (Avg@1 for single response, Avg@32 for multiple responses per prompt), using Math-Verify for automated correctness verification. Both single and multiple rollout settings will be tested for TBRM and baselines, and computational efficiency (training time, GPU memory) will be measured.
cc5b6a71b2598cb147c757caf84ac9f26354305b.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first trajectory-level Bellman residual minimization algorithm tailored for LLMs, enabling fully off-policy, value-based RL without critics or importance sampling. It leverages model logits as Q-values under the KL-regularized framework and requires only one rollout per prompt, reducing computational and memory demands. Theoretical contributions include a new convergence analysis based on trajectory-level change-of-measure, improving prior bounds and simplifying proofs. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate that value-based RL can match or surpass state-of-the-art policy-based methods for LLM reasoning, while being more efficient and scalable.

cc5dd7ed24abfa24fdc48aeb5f3fe7e5e7677521.title: State Entropy Regularization for Robust Reinforcement Learning
cc5dd7ed24abfa24fdc48aeb5f3fe7e5e7677521.research_question: Can state entropy regularization improve the robustness of reinforcement learning policies to structured and spatially correlated perturbations, and how do its robustness guarantees compare to those of policy entropy regularization?
cc5dd7ed24abfa24fdc48aeb5f3fe7e5e7677521.hypothesis: State entropy regularization provides stronger robustness to structured and spatially correlated perturbations than policy entropy regularization, particularly in transfer learning and environments with global changes, while maintaining or improving performance under reward and transition uncertainty.
cc5dd7ed24abfa24fdc48aeb5f3fe7e5e7677521.proposed_method: A reinforcement learning framework will be developed that augments the standard RL objective with a state entropy regularization term. The method will maximize the expected return plus a weighted entropy of the induced state distribution, where the entropy is estimated using a k-nearest neighbor estimator for both discrete and continuous state spaces. Theoretical analysis will be conducted to characterize the robustness properties of this regularization, including formal guarantees under reward and transition uncertainty, and to compare these guarantees to those of policy entropy regularization. The approach will also analyze the sensitivity of robustness gains to the number of rollouts used for policy evaluation and investigate the limitations of entropy regularization in fully solving kernel-robust RL problems and in risk-averse settings.
cc5dd7ed24abfa24fdc48aeb5f3fe7e5e7677521.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both discrete (MiniGrid) and continuous (Mujoco Pusher and Ant) RL environments. Policies will be trained with no regularization, policy entropy regularization, and state entropy regularization, using A2C for MiniGrid and PPO for Mujoco, with hyperparameters tuned to ensure nominal performance degradation is less than 5%. Robustness will be evaluated under spatially correlated perturbations (e.g., large walls or obstacles blocking optimal paths), uniformly distributed small-scale perturbations (e.g., scattered obstacles), and reward uncertainty (e.g., randomized goal locations). Baselines will include standard RL, policy entropy regularization, and robust RL methods such as PRMDP and NRMDP. Evaluation metrics will include average return, success rate, and performance under perturbations, with results averaged over multiple seeds and reported with confidence intervals. Ablation studies will examine the effect of rollout budget and regularization strength on robustness.
cc5dd7ed24abfa24fdc48aeb5f3fe7e5e7677521.novelty_claims: The proposed research provides the first comprehensive theoretical characterization of the robustness properties of state entropy regularization in RL, including formal guarantees under both reward and transition uncertainty. It demonstrates that state entropy regularization induces robustness to globally structured perturbations, outperforming policy entropy regularization in such settings. The work also establishes fundamental limitations of entropy regularization for kernel-robust RL and risk-averse objectives, and empirically shows the sensitivity of robustness gains to the number of rollouts used for policy evaluation. The approach clarifies the conditions under which state entropy regularization enhances robustness and delineates its boundaries.

cc6fc3c546b354abf6a0aa3b553f28a6b812489f.title: Improved Distribution Matching Distillation for Fast Image Synthesis
cc6fc3c546b354abf6a0aa3b553f28a6b812489f.research_question: How can the distillation of large, multi-step diffusion models into efficient one-step or few-step image generators be improved to achieve high-quality, fast image synthesis without the need for costly paired data or regression losses, while maintaining or surpassing the quality of the original teacher models?
cc6fc3c546b354abf6a0aa3b553f28a6b812489f.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that removing the regression loss from distribution matching distillation, stabilizing training with a two time-scale update rule, integrating a GAN loss with real data, and simulating inference-time generator samples during training will enable the distilled student generator to achieve or surpass the image quality and diversity of the teacher diffusion model while significantly reducing computational cost.
cc6fc3c546b354abf6a0aa3b553f28a6b812489f.proposed_method: The proposed method eliminates the need for a regression loss in distribution matching distillation by directly optimizing a distribution matching objective between the student generator and the teacher diffusion model. Training stability is achieved by employing a two time-scale update rule, where the fake score estimator is updated more frequently than the generator to accurately track the generator's output distribution. A GAN loss is incorporated into the distillation process, with a discriminator trained to distinguish between real images and generator outputs, thereby providing additional supervision from real data and mitigating errors in the teacher's score estimation. The approach supports both one-step and multi-step student generators, with a novel backward simulation procedure during training that aligns the training and inference domains by using noisy synthetic images generated by the student as intermediate inputs. This unified framework enables efficient and scalable distillation for high-resolution and text-to-image synthesis tasks.
cc6fc3c546b354abf6a0aa3b553f28a6b812489f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on class-conditional image generation using ImageNet-64x64 and text-to-image synthesis on COCO2014, with teacher models including SDXL and SDv1.5. Evaluation metrics include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) for image quality and diversity, CLIP Score for text-image alignment, and PatchFID for high-resolution detail assessment. Baselines for comparison will include prior distillation methods such as DMD, GAN-based approaches, and consistency models, as well as the original teacher models using standard ODE or SDE samplers. Human evaluations will be performed via user studies to assess visual appeal and prompt alignment. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of removing the regression loss, the two time-scale update rule, the GAN loss, and the backward simulation procedure.
cc6fc3c546b354abf6a0aa3b553f28a6b812489f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a regression-free distribution matching distillation framework that eliminates the need for costly paired data, significantly reducing computational overhead. Training stability is ensured by a novel two time-scale update rule. The integration of a GAN loss enables the student generator to leverage real data, surpassing the teacher model's quality. The method extends distribution matching to multi-step generators and resolves the training-inference domain mismatch through backward simulation. Together, these innovations establish new benchmarks in one-step and few-step image generation, achieving state-of-the-art results in both speed and quality.

cc9826c222ac1e81b4b374dd9e0df130f298b1e8.title: Language-driven Semantic Segmentation
cc9826c222ac1e81b4b374dd9e0df130f298b1e8.research_question: How can semantic segmentation models be designed to flexibly support arbitrary and previously unseen label sets at test time, leveraging language-based representations to enable zero-shot generalization without requiring additional training data?
cc9826c222ac1e81b4b374dd9e0df130f298b1e8.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that embedding both image pixels and descriptive text labels into a shared embedding space using pretrained language and vision models, and training the image encoder with a contrastive objective to align pixel and label embeddings, will enable semantic segmentation models to generalize to unseen categories and arbitrary label sets at inference time, achieving competitive or superior performance compared to existing zero- and few-shot methods.
cc9826c222ac1e81b4b374dd9e0df130f298b1e8.proposed_method: A new framework for language-driven semantic segmentation will be developed, in which a pretrained text encoder (such as CLIP) computes embeddings for arbitrary sets of descriptive input labels, while a transformer-based image encoder (e.g., DPT with a ViT backbone) produces dense per-pixel embeddings for the input image. The image encoder will be trained with a per-pixel contrastive objective to maximize the similarity between the embedding of each pixel and the embedding of its corresponding ground-truth label, using a softmax cross-entropy loss with temperature scaling. After correlating pixel and label embeddings via inner product, a spatial regularization module—composed of depthwise or bottleneck convolutional blocks—will be applied to refine and upsample the segmentation predictions to the original image resolution. The method will support dynamic label sets of arbitrary length and order at inference, enabling zero-shot segmentation by simply changing the input label set to the text encoder.
cc9826c222ac1e81b4b374dd9e0df130f298b1e8.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard semantic segmentation benchmarks, including PASCAL-5i, COCO-20i, and FSS-1000, following established few-shot and zero-shot evaluation protocols. The proposed method will be compared to state-of-the-art few-shot segmentation models (e.g., OSLSM, co-FCN, AMP-2, PANet, PGNet, FWB, PPNet, DAN, PFENet, RePRI, HSNet) as well as zero-shot baselines (e.g., ZS3Net, SPNet). Evaluation metrics will include mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) and Foreground-Background IoU (FB-IoU). Additional ablation studies will be performed on ADE20K to assess the impact of different spatial regularization blocks and text encoders, and to compare performance on fixed-label segmentation tasks. The training will use SGD with momentum, a polynomial learning rate scheduler, and batch sizes appropriate for multi-GPU setups. The model will also be tested on a mixture of multiple datasets to demonstrate generalization and label flexibility.
cc9826c222ac1e81b4b374dd9e0df130f298b1e8.novelty_claims: The proposed approach enables on-the-fly synthesis of zero-shot semantic segmentation models that can handle arbitrary, user-defined label sets at test time without retraining or additional labeled samples. By leveraging high-capacity, pretrained language models for label embedding and aligning them with visual features, the method generalizes to unseen categories and supports hierarchical and semantically related labels. The framework achieves highly competitive zero-shot performance, rivaling few-shot and fixed-label segmentation methods, and introduces a flexible architecture for dynamic label handling in dense prediction tasks.

cc9f2fd320a279741403c4bfbeb91179803c428c.title: Reward Uncertainty for Exploration in Preference-based Reinforcement Learning
cc9f2fd320a279741403c4bfbeb91179803c428c.research_question: How can exploration strategies be designed to improve the sample- and feedback-efficiency of preference-based reinforcement learning algorithms, particularly in complex tasks where human feedback is expensive and reward engineering is challenging?
cc9f2fd320a279741403c4bfbeb91179803c428c.hypothesis: Incorporating an intrinsic reward based on the uncertainty (disagreement) among an ensemble of learned reward models will drive exploration in preference-based reinforcement learning, leading to improved sample- and feedback-efficiency compared to existing exploration methods that do not leverage human preference uncertainty.
cc9f2fd320a279741403c4bfbeb91179803c428c.proposed_method: A novel exploration framework will be developed for preference-based reinforcement learning (RL), in which an ensemble of reward models is trained using human (or oracle) preferences between trajectory segments. At each timestep, the intrinsic reward is computed as the standard deviation (disagreement) of the predicted rewards across the ensemble for the current state-action pair, reflecting the uncertainty in the learned reward function. The total reward used for policy optimization will be a weighted sum of the extrinsic reward (mean prediction of the ensemble) and the intrinsic reward (ensemble standard deviation), with a decaying coefficient to gradually shift focus from exploration to exploitation as training progresses. The ensemble is initialized with diverse random parameters to ensure initial diversity, and each reward model is independently updated using cross-entropy loss based on preference feedback. This approach is designed to encourage the agent to explore state-action pairs where the reward function is most uncertain, thereby targeting areas where additional human feedback is most informative.
cc9f2fd320a279741403c4bfbeb91179803c428c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of complex robotic manipulation tasks from the Meta-World benchmark, using both off-policy (PEBBLE) and on-policy (PrefPPO) preference-based RL algorithms. The agent will receive preferences from a scripted teacher based on ground-truth reward sums for trajectory segments, and the true average return will be used as the primary evaluation metric. The proposed method will be compared against several exploration baselines, including state entropy maximization, forward dynamics model disagreement, and intrinsic curiosity module (ICM), with careful hyperparameter tuning for each. Evaluation will focus on both sample-efficiency (success rate versus environment steps) and feedback-efficiency (success rate under varying budgets of human feedback queries), with results averaged over multiple runs and statistical significance assessed via mean and standard deviation. Additional ablation studies will assess the impact of ensemble size, feedback session size, and the quality of learned reward functions (measured by EPIC distance to ground truth).
cc9f2fd320a279741403c4bfbeb91179803c428c.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first exploration strategy for preference-based RL that leverages uncertainty in learned reward functions as an intrinsic reward, directly aligning exploration with areas of high uncertainty in human preferences. This approach is claimed to improve both sample- and feedback-efficiency over existing exploration methods, while maintaining simplicity and computational efficiency by reusing the reward model ensemble already present in preference-based RL. The method is also robust to different ensemble sizes and feedback budgets, and leads to learned reward functions that more closely approximate ground truth rewards.

cca9a148b5078106587bdf6f1dd791a375410d90.title: Rethinking the Bias of Foundation Model under Long-tailed Distribution
cca9a148b5078106587bdf6f1dd791a375410d90.research_question: How does the bias inherent in foundation models, particularly under long-tailed data distributions, affect downstream learning tasks, and what strategies can effectively mitigate both parameter and data imbalance to improve generalization in such settings?
cca9a148b5078106587bdf6f1dd791a375410d90.hypothesis: Parameter imbalance inherited from foundation model pre-training exerts a more significant negative impact on downstream long-tailed tasks than data imbalance alone, and existing re-balancing methods are insufficient to address this; a causal learning-based backdoor adjustment can more effectively mitigate both types of imbalance and improve performance.
cca9a148b5078106587bdf6f1dd791a375410d90.proposed_method: A novel methodology is proposed that models the long-tailed learning problem from a causal perspective, identifying the incomplete semantic factor—arising from parameter imbalance in the foundation model—as a confounder that induces spurious correlations between input samples and labels. To address this, a causal structure graph is constructed, and a backdoor adjustment method is introduced to estimate the true causal effect between input samples and labels, rather than simply fitting observed correlations. The approach operationalizes this by fusing predictions from multiple foundation models (e.g., CLIP, OpenCLIP, MetaCLIP), each representing different incomplete semantic factors, and applies re-balancing techniques such as Logit Adjustment (LA) to obtain balanced outputs. These outputs are then merged using fusion weights according to the backdoor criterion, providing an unbiased estimation that simultaneously mitigates parameter and data imbalance. The method is designed to be compatible with Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) techniques and does not require access to pre-training data.
cca9a148b5078106587bdf6f1dd791a375410d90.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard long-tailed benchmarks, including ImageNet-LT, Places365-LT, and iNaturalist2018, utilizing ViT-B/16 as the backbone and employing PEFT methods such as AdaptFormer and Visual Prompt Tuning (VPT). Multiple foundation models (CLIP, OpenCLIP, MetaCLIP) will serve as sources of incomplete semantic factors. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art methods such as LiVT, LPT, VL-LTR, RAC, LIFT, Decoder, GML, and BALLAD, with and without external data. Evaluation metrics will focus on average accuracy across head (D-Many), medium (D-Medium), and tail (D-Few) classes, as well as overall accuracy. Additional analyses will include K-Nearest-Neighbor (KNN) accuracy for feature representation quality and ablation studies on the number of semantic factors used in the backdoor adjustment. Experimental setups will ensure fair comparisons by standardizing epochs, parameter counts, and training protocols.
cca9a148b5078106587bdf6f1dd791a375410d90.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to formally distinguish and jointly address parameter imbalance (inherited from foundation model pre-training) and data imbalance (in downstream tasks) in long-tailed learning. It introduces a causal learning framework that models the incomplete semantic factor as a confounder and applies a backdoor adjustment to eliminate its negative impact. The method demonstrates that parameter imbalance is fundamentally different from data imbalance and cannot be mitigated by existing re-balancing techniques alone. By leveraging multiple foundation models as proxies for incomplete semantic factors and fusing their outputs, the approach achieves more balanced and robust performance, particularly improving accuracy for underrepresented tail classes. Empirical results show consistent and significant gains over prior state-of-the-art methods on multiple large-scale long-tailed datasets, without requiring access to pre-training data or additional external data.

ccaff61e0c1e629d91d78f82a64b3cbc8f3f7023.title: Robust Distortion-free Watermarks for Language Models
ccaff61e0c1e629d91d78f82a64b3cbc8f3f7023.research_question: How can robust, distortion-free watermarks be embedded in the outputs of autoregressive language models such that the provenance of generated text can be reliably detected, even after substantial editing or paraphrasing, without altering the original text distribution or requiring access to the language model or prompt at detection time?
ccaff61e0c1e629d91d78f82a64b3cbc8f3f7023.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a watermarking methodology based on deterministic mapping from a randomized key sequence to language model outputs, combined with robust alignment-based detection, can achieve distortion-free, agnostic, and robust watermarking of language model text, enabling reliable detection even after significant text perturbation.
ccaff61e0c1e629d91d78f82a64b3cbc8f3f7023.proposed_method: A novel watermarking protocol will be developed in which a language model provider embeds a watermark by deterministically mapping a sequence of random numbers (the watermark key) to a sample from the language model using a distortion-free decoder. Two instantiations of this approach will be explored: one using inverse transform sampling and another using exponential minimum sampling, both ensuring that the marginal distribution over generated text remains unchanged. Detection will be performed by any party with access to the watermark key, using a robust sequence alignment algorithm to correlate the observed text with the key sequence, yielding a p-value quantifying the likelihood that the text is watermarked. The detection method will be model-agnostic and prompt-agnostic, relying on alignment costs tailored to the specific watermarking strategy, and will include dynamic programming techniques to ensure robustness to token-level edits (insertions, deletions, substitutions). To support multiple queries and avoid key reuse, a randomized wrapper will be implemented that shifts the key sequence for each generation, maintaining statistical indistinguishability from standard language model outputs.
ccaff61e0c1e629d91d78f82a64b3cbc8f3f7023.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three large language models: OPT-1.3B, LLaMA-7B, and Alpaca-7B. Watermarked text will be generated and subjected to a variety of adversarial perturbations, including random token substitutions, insertions, deletions, and automated paraphrasing (e.g., translation to other languages and back). Detection performance will be evaluated using statistical power (p-values) as the primary metric, with detection considered successful at p ≤ 0.01. Baseline comparisons will include existing watermarking methods that introduce distributional bias or lack robustness. The evaluation will focus on the minimum text length required for reliable detection, the proportion of detectable responses under different entropy conditions, and the resilience of the watermark to various attack scenarios. Additional case studies will be performed on instruction-following tasks to assess feasibility in low-entropy response settings.
ccaff61e0c1e629d91d78f82a64b3cbc8f3f7023.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first watermarking methodology for language models that simultaneously achieves distortion-freeness, agnosticism (model and prompt independence), and robustness to substantial text corruption. Unlike prior methods, the technique does not alter the language model's output distribution and remains detectable even after significant paraphrasing or editing. The use of robust sequence alignment for detection and the theoretical analysis of statistical power and lower bounds based on watermark potential are novel contributions. The methodology is generalizable, supports multiple queries without key reuse, and is validated on state-of-the-art language models with comprehensive empirical and theoretical support.

ccb14568bf097c85ae03fc3ca79ce08ddf2943d2.title: An Online Learning Theory of Brokerage
ccb14568bf097c85ae03fc3ca79ce08ddf2943d2.research_question: How can brokerage in two-sided markets, where traders are not assigned fixed buyer or seller roles and valuations are private and drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution, be addressed from an online learning and regret minimization perspective under different feedback models?
ccb14568bf097c85ae03fc3ca79ce08ddf2943d2.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that, under the assumption of a bounded density for the distribution of traders' valuations, it is possible to design online learning algorithms for brokerage that achieve optimal regret rates (up to constant factors) in both full feedback and limited (two-bit) feedback settings. Furthermore, the optimal regret rate will degrade or learning will become impossible if the bounded density assumption is dropped.
ccb14568bf097c85ae03fc3ca79ce08ddf2943d2.proposed_method: A novel online learning framework is developed for brokerage in two-sided markets, where at each round, two traders with private valuations arrive and a broker proposes a price. The framework considers two feedback models: (1) full feedback, where both traders' valuations are revealed after each round, and (2) two-bit feedback, where only the traders' willingness to buy or sell at the proposed price is revealed. For the full feedback case, a Follow-the-Mean (FTM) algorithm is proposed, which posts the empirical mean of observed valuations as the trading price. For the two-bit feedback case, an Explore-then-Commit (ETC) algorithm is designed, where an initial exploration phase estimates the expected valuation using only binary feedback, followed by committing to the estimated value. Theoretical analysis leverages new approximation and representation lemmas to establish regret bounds and the optimality of the proposed algorithms under the bounded density assumption.
ccb14568bf097c85ae03fc3ca79ce08ddf2943d2.experiment_details: Theoretical experiments are conducted by analyzing the regret performance of the proposed algorithms under various assumptions about the distribution of traders' valuations. Hard instances are constructed using carefully designed distributions with bounded density to demonstrate matching upper and lower regret bounds. The regret is evaluated as a function of the time horizon T and the density bound M. Comparisons are made to existing baselines from the online learning literature on bilateral trade, particularly in settings with fixed buyer/seller roles and different feedback models. The evaluation metrics focus on the regret rate (e.g., O(M log T), O(√MT)), and the analysis includes both upper and lower bounds to establish optimality.
ccb14568bf097c85ae03fc3ca79ce08ddf2943d2.novelty_claims: The proposed research is the first to address online learning for brokerage in bilateral trade without fixed buyer/seller roles, capturing the flexibility of real-world OTC markets. It introduces the first algorithms and lower bounds with the correct dependence on both the time horizon T and the density bound M, improving exponentially over previous regret rates in the full feedback setting. The work also establishes the first learnability results and matching lower bounds for the two-bit feedback model in this context, and provides algorithms that are robust to the validity of the bounded density assumption, achieving optimal regret in both bounded and unbounded cases.

ccb1ccc4deacc4fb18000f0e1ce24329548963ae.title: Describe, Explain, Plan and Select: Interactive Planning with Large Language Models Enables Open-World Multi-Task Agents
ccb1ccc4deacc4fb18000f0e1ce24329548963ae.research_question: How can interactive planning methods be developed to enable multi-task embodied agents to robustly accomplish complex, long-horizon tasks in open-world environments, where both accurate multi-step reasoning and state-dependent task feasibility present significant challenges?
ccb1ccc4deacc4fb18000f0e1ce24329548963ae.hypothesis: Integrating iterative plan refinement through plan execution description, self-explanation of failures, and a horizon-predictive goal selection mechanism into a large language model-based planning framework will significantly improve the robustness and efficiency of multi-task agents in open-world environments compared to existing LLM-based planners.
ccb1ccc4deacc4fb18000f0e1ce24329548963ae.proposed_method: A novel interactive planning framework, termed 'Describe, Explain, Plan and Select' (DEPS), is proposed for embodied agents operating in open-world environments. The method begins by using a large language model (LLM) to decompose high-level natural language tasks into a sequence of sub-goals, which are executed by a goal-conditioned controller. Upon execution failure, an event-triggered descriptor summarizes the current state and outcome, which is then fed back to the LLM. The LLM, acting as both explainer and planner, analyzes the feedback to identify errors and re-plans the task with explicit explanations, iteratively refining the plan. To address the challenge of state-dependent task feasibility, a trainable horizon-predictive selector module ranks parallel candidate sub-goals based on estimated completion steps, dynamically choosing the most efficient path forward. The selector is implemented as a neural network trained to predict the horizon (remaining steps) for each candidate goal, using an ImpalaCNN backbone and sharing parameters with the controller when applicable.
ccb1ccc4deacc4fb18000f0e1ce24329548963ae.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 71 diverse tasks from the Minecraft Universe Benchmark SkillForgeChain, covering a range of complexities and grouped into eight meta-task categories. The method will be evaluated in multiple Minecraft environments (MineDojo, MineRL, MC-TextWorld) with varying versions and controllers (e.g., MC-Controller, Steve-1), as well as in non-open-ended domains such as ALFWorld and Tabletop Manipulation. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art LLM-based planners such as GPT Zero-shot Planner, ProgPrompt, Chain-of-Thought, InnerMonologue, and Code-as-Policies, all using the same controller and prompt templates for fairness. Success rate will be the primary evaluation metric, with each task executed 30 times and results averaged. Ablation studies will analyze the impact of the selector and the number of re-planning rounds, and additional experiments will focus on the challenging ObtainDiamond task to assess performance on long-horizon, complex planning.
ccb1ccc4deacc4fb18000f0e1ce24329548963ae.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces an interactive, iterative planning loop that combines plan execution description, self-explanation, and re-planning within an LLM framework, which is not present in prior LLM-based planners. The integration of a horizon-predictive selector that dynamically ranks and selects parallel sub-goals based on state-dependent feasibility is a novel contribution, enabling more efficient and robust planning in open-world settings. The method demonstrates, for the first time, robust zero-shot multi-task performance across 70+ open-world tasks in Minecraft, nearly doubling the overall success rate compared to existing baselines and achieving notable results on the long-standing ObtainDiamond challenge. The framework is generalizable to other domains and does not require environment-specific planning training.

ccc2b6b8b5c0b8d33433dfbfe5ae8b8045b5173a.title: Fast Video Generation with Sliding Tile Attention
ccc2b6b8b5c0b8d33433dfbfe5ae8b8045b5173a.research_question: How can the computational bottleneck of attention in high-resolution, long-duration video generation using Diffusion Transformers be alleviated without sacrificing video quality?
ccc2b6b8b5c0b8d33433dfbfe5ae8b8045b5173a.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that the strong spatial-temporal locality and redundancy present in the attention patterns of pretrained video diffusion models can be exploited to design a hardware-efficient, sparse attention mechanism that significantly accelerates inference while maintaining or minimally impacting video generation quality.
ccc2b6b8b5c0b8d33433dfbfe5ae8b8045b5173a.proposed_method: A novel attention mechanism, Sliding Tile Attention (STA), will be developed to replace full 3D attention in video Diffusion Transformers. STA operates by partitioning the video latent space into spatial-temporal tiles, with each tile attending only to a local window of neighboring tiles, thus leveraging the observed locality in attention scores. The method will employ a hardware-aware, tile-by-tile sliding window design that eliminates irregular, GPU-unfriendly mixed attention blocks, instead producing only dense and empty blocks for optimal compute efficiency. Kernel-level optimizations will be implemented, including asynchronous data loading and inter-block mask management, to maximize memory throughput and parallelism on modern GPUs. The approach will support both training-free deployment, by profiling and configuring optimal window sizes per attention head, and fine-tuning, allowing for even higher sparsity and efficiency gains.
ccc2b6b8b5c0b8d33433dfbfe5ae8b8045b5173a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the HunyuanVideo model, a state-of-the-art open video Diffusion Transformer, generating 5-second 720P videos. The evaluation will compare STA against several baselines, including FlashAttention-2/3, CLEAR, NATTEN, TiledNATTEN, Swin, and ∆-DiT, using both training-free and fine-tuned settings. Metrics will include kernel-level efficiency (MFU, FLOPs, latency), end-to-end inference time, and video quality assessed by human preference (MovieGen Bench), as well as automated metrics such as VBench, SSIM, PSNR, and CD-FVD. The experimental setup will ensure comparable sparsity levels across methods, and ablation studies will be conducted to analyze the impact of window size, head specialization, and kernel optimizations. Additional experiments will test the method on image super-resolution tasks with the FLUX model.
ccc2b6b8b5c0b8d33433dfbfe5ae8b8045b5173a.novelty_claims: The proposed method claims the first hardware-efficient, higher-order (2D/3D) sliding-window-like attention implementation that achieves wall-clock speedups proportional to attention sparsity in video Diffusion Transformers. It introduces a tile-based sliding window design that eliminates inefficient mixed attention blocks, enabling dense computation patterns highly suitable for modern GPUs. STA supports both plug-and-play acceleration (requiring no retraining) and further efficiency via fine-tuning, with minimal or no loss in video generation quality. The method also provides an automatic, head-specialized window configuration strategy and demonstrates superior quality-efficiency tradeoffs compared to existing sparse attention and caching-based acceleration techniques.

ccd6f8b6544f112de632e49bfbe592a0a654537d.title: DriveGPT4: Interpretable End-to-End Autonomous Driving Via Large Language Model
ccd6f8b6544f112de632e49bfbe592a0a654537d.research_question: How can large multimodal language models be leveraged to develop interpretable, end-to-end autonomous driving systems that can both predict vehicle control signals and provide human-understandable explanations for their actions?
ccd6f8b6544f112de632e49bfbe592a0a654537d.hypothesis: Integrating large multimodal language models with domain-specific visual instruction tuning data will enable the development of autonomous driving systems that are both interpretable and capable of state-of-the-art end-to-end control, outperforming existing baselines in both control prediction and natural language explanation tasks.
ccd6f8b6544f112de632e49bfbe592a0a654537d.proposed_method: A novel multimodal large language model, DriveGPT4, will be developed to process multi-frame video inputs and textual queries for autonomous driving. The system will utilize a video tokenizer based on Valley to convert video frames into text domain tokens, which are then concatenated and input into a large language model (LLaMA2). Both temporal and spatial features will be extracted from video data using a CLIP-based visual encoder, and projected into the text domain via a learned projector. Control signals (such as speed and turning angle) will be embedded within the text outputs, allowing the model to simultaneously generate natural language explanations and low-level vehicle control predictions. Training will proceed in two stages: pretraining for video-text alignment on large-scale general datasets, followed by mix-finetuning using a bespoke visual instruction tuning dataset created from BDD-X and ChatGPT-generated QAs to enhance domain-specific reasoning and flexibility.
ccd6f8b6544f112de632e49bfbe592a0a654537d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the BDD-X dataset, which contains approximately 20,000 annotated video clips with vehicle action descriptions, justifications, and control signals. The testing set will be split into 'Easy', 'Medium', and 'Hard' subsets based on scene complexity. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art interpretable autonomous driving models (e.g., ADAPT) and recent multimodal video understanding LLMs (e.g., Video-LLaMA, Valley). Evaluation metrics will include CIDEr, BLEU4, and ROUGE-L for text generation tasks, as well as RMSE and threshold accuracy for control signal prediction. Additional evaluation will use ChatGPT-based scoring for flexible, open-ended question answering. Ablation studies will assess the impact of different training data components and mix-finetuning strategies.
ccd6f8b6544f112de632e49bfbe592a0a654537d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first interpretable end-to-end autonomous driving system based on large multimodal language models capable of both control prediction and natural language explanation. A new visual instruction tuning dataset tailored for autonomous driving is created using ChatGPT, enabling the model to answer a diverse range of user queries beyond fixed QA formats. The mix-finetuning strategy combining general and domain-specific instruction-following data is claimed to significantly enhance both visual understanding and reasoning abilities. The method demonstrates superior performance over existing baselines in both interpretability and control tasks, and shows strong generalization to new domains and question types.

ccec08f900d70a52d38c2b910d81183e0de5d80d.title: Evaluating Open-Source Sparse Autoencoders on Disentangling Factual Knowledge in GPT-2 Small
ccec08f900d70a52d38c2b910d81183e0de5d80d.research_question: Can open-source sparse autoencoders (SAEs) provide a feature space for language model hidden representations that enables disentanglement of related factual knowledge, such as the country and continent a city is in, more effectively than neurons or supervised linear feature learning methods?
ccec08f900d70a52d38c2b910d81183e0de5d80d.hypothesis: Sparse autoencoders trained on hidden representations of language models can produce feature spaces where distinct factual concepts (e.g., country and continent) are more disentangled and causally manipulable than in the original neuron space, and can approach or exceed the performance of supervised linear feature learning (DAS) in this regard.
ccec08f900d70a52d38c2b910d81183e0de5d80d.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves evaluating several open-source sparse autoencoders (SAEs) trained on the hidden representations of GPT-2 small, focusing on their ability to disentangle and mediate factual knowledge about cities' countries and continents. The RAVEL benchmark will be used to assess the separability of these concepts by learning binary masks that select features for targeted interventions: changing the country of a city without altering its continent, and vice versa. Interchange interventions will be performed in the feature spaces of four SAEs (OpenAI SAE, two Apollo SAEs, Bloom SAE), with neurons serving as a baseline and distributed alignment search (DAS) learned linear features as a supervised skyline. For each feature space, differentiable binary masking (DBM) will be applied to select relevant features, and interventions will be evaluated by fixing feature values to those corresponding to different inputs and observing the model's output changes.
ccec08f900d70a52d38c2b910d81183e0de5d80d.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize the RAVEL dataset, filtered to 40 cities known by GPT-2 small, generating 1600 interchange interventions each for 'country' and 'continent' (3200 total). The dataset will be split into 70% training, 10% validation, and 20% test sets. For each SAE and baseline, binary masks will be trained to select features mediating 'country' or 'continent' knowledge, and interventions will be evaluated using accuracy on whether the model output reflects the intended factual change. Evaluation metrics include intervention accuracy (for both 'country' and 'continent'), disentangle score (average of the two accuracies), reconstruction loss, and sparsity statistics. Baselines include the original neuron space and DAS-learned linear subspaces. Experiments will be conducted across multiple layers of GPT-2 small, with detailed results reported for layers 1 and 5. Training uses a batch size of 16, temperature annealed from 10 to 0.1, 20 epochs, and a learning rate of 0.001.
ccec08f900d70a52d38c2b910d81183e0de5d80d.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces a rigorous comparative evaluation of open-source SAEs for their ability to disentangle and causally mediate factual knowledge in language model representations, using the RAVEL benchmark and interchange interventions. It systematically benchmarks multiple SAE architectures against both unsupervised (neurons) and supervised (DAS) baselines, providing new evidence on the effectiveness and limitations of SAEs for mechanistic interpretability. The approach leverages differentiable binary masking for feature selection and offers detailed analysis of reconstruction loss, knowledge degradation, and feature sparsity, contributing to the principled evaluation of feature spaces for causal analysis in deep learning models.

ccf6d9d7cec0d4aa9b50c99659765668d6e7c6c2.title: From Explicit CoT to Implicit CoT: Learning to Internalize CoT Step by Step
ccf6d9d7cec0d4aa9b50c99659765668d6e7c6c2.research_question: Can language models be trained to internalize chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning steps, thereby enabling them to perform complex reasoning tasks without generating explicit intermediate steps, while maintaining high accuracy and improving inference speed?
ccf6d9d7cec0d4aa9b50c99659765668d6e7c6c2.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a gradual, curriculum-based removal of explicit CoT steps during training will enable language models to internalize the reasoning process within their hidden states, allowing for implicit CoT reasoning that achieves accuracy comparable to explicit CoT methods but with significantly faster inference.
ccf6d9d7cec0d4aa9b50c99659765668d6e7c6c2.proposed_method: A curriculum learning approach, termed Stepwise Internalization, is proposed to enable implicit chain-of-thought reasoning in language models. The method begins with a model trained using explicit CoT supervision, where both intermediate reasoning steps and the final answer are predicted. In successive training stages, a fixed number of CoT tokens are removed from the output sequence, and the model is finetuned to predict the remaining steps and the final answer. This process continues until all CoT tokens are removed, forcing the model to internalize the reasoning process and directly predict the answer from the input. To stabilize training, two key techniques are introduced: (1) resetting the optimizer state whenever additional CoT tokens are removed to avoid abrupt changes in gradient statistics, and (2) 'Removal Smoothing', where a small random offset is added to the number of tokens removed at each step, smoothing the transition between stages and preventing sudden loss spikes.
ccf6d9d7cec0d4aa9b50c99659765668d6e7c6c2.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on multi-digit multiplication tasks (4x4, 5x5, 7x7, 9x9) using synthetic data generated following BIG-bench protocols, as well as on the GSM8K grade-school math word problem dataset. The method is evaluated on various pretrained language models, including GPT-2 Small, Phi-3 3.8B, and Mistral-7B, and compared against several baselines: NoCoT (no chain-of-thought supervision), Explicit CoT (full chain-of-thought supervision), and ICoT-KD (implicit CoT via knowledge distillation). Evaluation metrics include exact match accuracy for final answer prediction and inference speed (examples per second), with speed measured relative to NoCoT baselines on standardized hardware. Ablation studies are performed to assess the impact of removal smoothing, optimizer resets, removal direction, and the number of tokens removed per epoch.
ccf6d9d7cec0d4aa9b50c99659765668d6e7c6c2.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a simple yet effective curriculum learning framework for internalizing chain-of-thought reasoning, eliminating the need for teacher-student knowledge distillation or specially mixed training data. Stepwise Internalization enables language models to achieve implicit CoT reasoning, matching or surpassing the accuracy of prior implicit CoT methods while significantly improving inference speed. The approach is generalizable across tasks and model sizes, and demonstrates state-of-the-art performance for implicit CoT on challenging arithmetic and math reasoning benchmarks, outperforming much larger models that do not use explicit CoT.

ccff488946e5dbaee3bf07277000753fd07ef48b.title: DeciMamba: Exploring the Length Extrapolation Potential of Mamba
ccff488946e5dbaee3bf07277000753fd07ef48b.research_question: How can the length extrapolation and context extension capabilities of state-space models, specifically Mamba, be improved to effectively process sequences significantly longer than those seen during training, while maintaining computational efficiency and strong performance on long-range NLP tasks?
ccff488946e5dbaee3bf07277000753fd07ef48b.hypothesis: Embedding a dynamic, data-dependent token filtering and pooling mechanism within pre-trained Mamba models will enable effective extrapolation to much longer sequence lengths than those seen during training, without requiring additional training or significant computational overhead.
ccff488946e5dbaee3bf07277000753fd07ef48b.proposed_method: A new context-extension method, DeciMamba, will be developed for Mamba-based models. The approach introduces a decimation mechanism that leverages the hidden filtering behavior inherent in the S6 layer's selective recurrent gate (parameterized by per-token delta values, ∆_t). For each layer selected for decimation, tokens are assigned importance scores based on the mean ∆_t across channels. Only the top-P most important tokens are retained for further processing by the S6 layer, with P decreasing in deeper layers according to a decay schedule. The decimation scope (i.e., which layers perform pooling) is determined by measuring each layer's effective receptive field using a novel MambaMeanDistance metric, targeting layers responsible for long-range dependencies. The decimation is applied only during the inference pre-fill phase, ensuring efficient parallel computation and minimal interference with the model's autoregressive decoding.
ccff488946e5dbaee3bf07277000753fd07ef48b.experiment_details: Experiments will evaluate DeciMamba on a suite of long-context NLP tasks, including zero-shot and fine-tuned settings. Benchmarks such as LongBench (covering multi-document QA, summarization, coding, and synthetic tasks), document retrieval (using SQuAD v2), multi-document QA, Passkey Retrieval (on WikiText-103), and language modeling (on PG-19) will be used. Models of various sizes (e.g., 130M, 1.4B, 2.8B parameters) will be tested, with all models trained on relatively short context lengths (e.g., 2K tokens) and evaluated on much longer sequences (up to 128K tokens). Baselines will include standard Mamba and equivalent Transformer models (e.g., Pythia suite), with evaluation metrics such as F1, Rouge-L, accuracy, and perplexity (measured on the farthest context positions). Inference efficiency will be benchmarked on GPU hardware, and ablation studies will examine the impact of decimation layer selection and pooling strategies.
ccff488946e5dbaee3bf07277000753fd07ef48b.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first context-extension technique specifically designed for Mamba and S6-based models, introducing a data-driven decimation mechanism that expands the effective receptive field by dynamically filtering unimportant tokens. The approach enables substantial extrapolation to longer contexts without retraining or increased computational cost, and introduces new metrics (MambaMeanDistance) for quantifying context utilization. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate significant improvements in long-context generalization and inference speed over existing baselines, with detailed ablations supporting the effectiveness of the decimation strategy.

cd1c724ad7a01186711add767cea2811af720dd1.title: SpikingBERT: Distilling BERT to Train Spiking Language Models Using Implicit Differentiation
cd1c724ad7a01186711add767cea2811af720dd1.research_question: Can the computational and energy costs of large language models (LLMs) be significantly reduced by developing a biologically inspired spiking neural network (SNN) language model, and can such a model achieve competitive performance on natural language processing tasks compared to conventional transformer-based architectures?
cd1c724ad7a01186711add767cea2811af720dd1.hypothesis: A spiking language model, trained using implicit differentiation and knowledge distillation from a pre-trained transformer-based model, can achieve comparable accuracy to efficient LLMs on NLP tasks while offering substantial reductions in computational and energy requirements.
cd1c724ad7a01186711add767cea2811af720dd1.proposed_method: A novel spiking language model architecture inspired by BERT will be developed, featuring spiking encoder layers composed of leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neurons and a spiking attention mechanism. The model will be trained using an implicit differentiation technique that leverages the convergence of average spiking rates (ASR) at equilibrium, thus overcoming the non-differentiability of spiking neurons and reducing memory usage during training. Knowledge distillation (KD) will be employed by mapping the equilibrium ASR of the spiking 'student' model's intermediate layers to the activations of a larger pre-trained BERT 'teacher' model, using mean squared error loss for internal representations and cross-entropy loss for output logits. The training process will involve both general-domain and task-specific KD, with additional architectural features such as optional feedback connections for enhanced bio-plausibility and energy efficiency.
cd1c724ad7a01186711add767cea2811af720dd1.experiment_details: The proposed spiking language model will be evaluated on seven tasks from the GLUE benchmark, covering classification and regression tasks such as QQP, MNLI, SST-2, QNLI, RTE, MRPC, and STS-B. The model will be compared against standard NLP baselines (e.g., CBoW, BiLSTM, GenSen), efficient BERT variants (TinyBERT, NAS-BERT), and recent spiking language models (e.g., SpikeGPT) where applicable. Evaluation metrics will include accuracy, F1 score, and Pearson/Spearman correlation as appropriate for each task. The experimental setup will include hyperparameter sweeps for convergence time steps, threshold voltage, leak term, and batch size, with energy and power efficiency measured using normalized operation counts and spike rates. Ablation studies will assess the impact of architectural choices such as normalization, feedback connections, and number of encoder layers.
cd1c724ad7a01186711add767cea2811af720dd1.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first operational spiking language model evaluated on multiple GLUE benchmark tasks, leveraging a novel spiking attention mechanism and an ANN-SNN knowledge distillation framework based on equilibrium states. The use of implicit differentiation for SNN training in NLP enables scalable, deep spiking models without surrogate gradients or backpropagation through time. The approach claims substantial improvements in energy and memory efficiency, and demonstrates that spiking LMs can achieve competitive accuracy with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost compared to conventional and efficient transformer-based models.

cd245068a71294b7ff6feadb27257e59532eff0d.title: Octopus: Alleviating Hallucination via Dynamic Contrastive Decoding
cd245068a71294b7ff6feadb27257e59532eff0d.research_question: How can hallucination in large vision-language models (LVLMs) be effectively alleviated, considering that different inputs and generative steps may require different mitigation strategies?
cd245068a71294b7ff6feadb27257e59532eff0d.hypothesis: A dynamic, adaptive framework that identifies the type of hallucination at each generative step and selects the most appropriate contrastive decoding strategy will outperform static, one-size-fits-all approaches in reducing hallucinations in LVLMs.
cd245068a71294b7ff6feadb27257e59532eff0d.proposed_method: A novel framework, termed Octopus, will be developed to dynamically mitigate hallucinations in LVLMs by adaptively selecting among multiple contrastive decoding (CD) strategies at each generative step. The method introduces a transformer-based decision module ('eye') that, at each step of generation, analyzes the hidden states of the model to recognize the specific type of hallucination present. Based on this recognition, an action vector ('tentacle') is produced, which selects from a pool of candidate CD strategies (e.g., addressing language priors, visual information loss, or attention bias, as exemplified by VCD, M3ID, and AVISC). The selected strategy is then applied to perform a contrastive operation at that step. The entire workflow is optimized using Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) or reinforcement learning, relying on preference data constructed from human or automatic metrics, while keeping the LVLM weights frozen for deployability.
cd245068a71294b7ff6feadb27257e59532eff0d.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both generative and discriminative tasks using benchmarks such as AMBER, Object-HalBench, MMHalBench, and POPE, with LVLMs like LLaVA-1.5-7B and InstructBLIP as backbones. Evaluation metrics will include CHAIR, Cover, Hal, Cog, GPT-4V scores for generative tasks, and Accuracy/F1 for discriminative tasks. Baselines will comprise both retraining-based and post-hoc CD methods (e.g., VCD, M3ID, AVISC, LCD, ICD, OPERA), as well as random and ablation variants of the proposed method. The experimental setup will involve constructing preference datasets for DPO optimization, using both human and automatic metrics to label positive and negative samples, and extensive ablation studies to assess the impact of different numbers and types of CD strategies, model architectures, and optimization algorithms.
cd245068a71294b7ff6feadb27257e59532eff0d.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a dynamic, token-level selection mechanism for contrastive decoding strategies, enabling fine-grained and adaptive hallucination mitigation in LVLMs. Unlike prior methods that apply a single CD strategy uniformly, this framework recognizes the hybrid and step-dependent nature of hallucination causes and organizes a tailored workflow at each generative step. The method is designed for high deployability, requiring no retraining of the LVLM backbone, and demonstrates extensibility by allowing seamless integration of additional CD strategies. Experimental results are expected to show state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks for both generative and discriminative tasks.

cd27f45bc760447fb4de3209e2381ea3493bbd57.title: ReST-MCTS*: LLM Self-Training via Process Reward Guided Tree Search
cd27f45bc760447fb4de3209e2381ea3493bbd57.research_question: How can high-quality reasoning traces for large language model (LLM) self-training be automatically acquired, and how can process reward signals be effectively leveraged to improve verification and self-improvement of LLMs without relying on dense human annotation?
cd27f45bc760447fb4de3209e2381ea3493bbd57.hypothesis: Automatically inferring per-step process rewards via a process-reward-guided Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) enables the collection of higher-quality reasoning traces, which, when used for mutual self-training of policy and reward models, leads to superior LLM reasoning capabilities compared to existing self-training paradigms.
cd27f45bc760447fb4de3209e2381ea3493bbd57.proposed_method: A novel self-training framework is proposed that integrates a process reward model (PRM) with a modified Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS*) to guide the exploration and selection of high-quality reasoning traces. The process reward model estimates the quality value of each partial solution step, reflecting its likelihood of contributing to a correct final answer. MCTS* uses these per-step quality values to guide node selection, expansion, rollout, and backpropagation in the search tree, enabling efficient pruning and prioritization of promising reasoning paths. The framework iteratively self-trains both the policy model (LLM) and the process reward model: MCTS* generates reasoning traces, correct traces are selected and used to fine-tune the policy, while all generated traces are used to further refine the reward model. This mutual self-training loop continues for multiple iterations, with inferred per-step rewards serving as both value targets for the reward model and as filters for high-quality policy training data.
cd27f45bc760447fb4de3209e2381ea3493bbd57.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on multiple reasoning benchmarks, including MATH, GSM8K, TheoremQA, SciBench, and CEval-Hard, using various LLM backbones such as LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B:MetaMATH, SciGLM-6B, GLM4, GPT-3.5-turbo, and LLaMA2-13B-Chat. Baselines include Self-Consistency (SC), Best-of-N, Tree-of-Thought (ToT), ReSTEM, Self-RewardingLM, and MATH-SHEPHERD. Evaluation metrics primarily focus on solution accuracy, with experiments repeated for multiple self-training iterations to assess continuous improvement. Search budget (token usage) is controlled to ensure fair comparison across methods. Both in-distribution and out-of-distribution generalization are tested, and ablation studies compare different reward model training strategies and reasoning policies.
cd27f45bc760447fb4de3209e2381ea3493bbd57.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first mutual self-training paradigm for both policy and process reward models in LLMs, using a process-reward-guided tree search (MCTS*) that automatically infers per-step rewards without human annotation. The method enables efficient, scalable acquisition of high-quality reasoning traces, surpassing prior methods in both trace quality and downstream LLM performance. The framework demonstrates superior accuracy and self-improvement capability over state-of-the-art self-training and reasoning baselines under equivalent search budgets, and establishes a new standard for process reward model training and utilization in LLM self-training.

cd467136e3dc283defd70d17197049b8e792e60e.title: Learning Strategic Language Agents in the Werewolf Game with Iterative Latent Space Policy Optimization
cd467136e3dc283defd70d17197049b8e792e60e.research_question: How can intelligent agents be developed to effectively play free-form strategic language games, such as Werewolf, which require both strategic decision-making and natural language interaction?
cd467136e3dc283defd70d17197049b8e792e60e.hypothesis: Iteratively combining game-theoretic policy optimization in a discrete latent strategy space with large language model (LLM) fine-tuning will enable agents to overcome intrinsic bias and limited exploration in free-form language games, resulting in improved strategic reasoning and communication abilities.
cd467136e3dc283defd70d17197049b8e792e60e.proposed_method: A novel iterative framework, Latent Space Policy Optimization (LSPO), will be developed to train strategic language agents for free-form games. The approach begins by mapping free-form language actions into a discrete latent strategy space using LLM-generated utterances and semantic clustering, thus abstracting the original game into a tractable extensive-form game. Game-theoretic methods, such as Counterfactual Regret Minimization (CFR), are then applied to optimize policies within this latent space, addressing intrinsic bias in action distributions. The LLM is subsequently fine-tuned using Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) to align its language generation with the learned latent-space policy, enabling the agent to generate novel strategies and expand the latent space. This process is iteratively repeated, allowing the agent to progressively enhance both its strategic reasoning and language communication capabilities.
cd467136e3dc283defd70d17197049b8e792e60e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted in a seven-player text-based Werewolf game environment, with roles including Werewolves, Seer, Doctor, and Villagers. The base language model will be Llama-3-8B-Instruct. The agent's performance will be evaluated over multiple LSPO iterations, measuring prediction accuracy of hidden roles and win rates for both the Werewolf and Village sides. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art agents such as ReAct, ReCon, Cicero-like, and SLA, with each agent playing both sides in head-to-head matches. Evaluation metrics will include win rate, prediction accuracy, and exploitability. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of key components, such as policy optimization and fine-tuning, as well as sensitivity to clustering and fine-tuning hyperparameters.
cd467136e3dc283defd70d17197049b8e792e60e.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces an iterative combination of game-theoretic optimization and LLM fine-tuning in a dynamically expanding latent strategy space, addressing both intrinsic bias and limited exploration in free-form language games. By abstracting natural language actions into a discrete latent space, the method enables tractable application of game-theoretic solvers to environments with unbounded action spaces. The iterative alignment of LLM outputs with evolving latent-space policies leads to agents that progressively acquire more complex and robust strategic behaviors, outperforming existing state-of-the-art approaches in social deduction games.

cd6496bc404e18a24f634e3dded2ed1cdca03e0f.title: Learning to Learn with Generative Models of Neural Network Checkpoints
cd6496bc404e18a24f634e3dded2ed1cdca03e0f.research_question: Can a generative model trained on large datasets of neural network checkpoints learn to rapidly optimize neural network parameters for a variety of downstream tasks, including both supervised and reinforcement learning, by directly generating parameter updates conditioned on desired performance metrics?
cd6496bc404e18a24f634e3dded2ed1cdca03e0f.hypothesis: A generative model pre-trained on a large, diverse dataset of neural network checkpoints can learn to produce parameter updates that achieve user-specified performance metrics (such as loss, error, or return) in a single step, outperforming traditional hand-designed optimizers in rapid adaptation and generalization to new tasks and initializations.
cd6496bc404e18a24f634e3dded2ed1cdca03e0f.proposed_method: A large-scale dataset of neural network checkpoints will be constructed by saving parameters and associated task-level metrics (e.g., losses, errors, returns) from numerous training runs across different tasks (such as MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Cartpole) and architectures (MLPs, CNNs). A conditional diffusion-based generative model, implemented as a transformer operating on tokenized parameter vectors and metric prompts, will be trained to predict the distribution over updated parameters that achieve a desired target metric, given an initial parameter vector and its associated metric. The model will use a diffusion process to gradually denoise future parameter vectors, and will be trained with a simplified variational lower bound loss that encourages accurate prediction of denoised parameters. Architectural innovations include per-layer tokenization, chunking for large layers, scalar metric tokenization, and a global residual connection to facilitate learning parameter updates.
cd6496bc404e18a24f634e3dded2ed1cdca03e0f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on supervised learning tasks (MNIST and CIFAR-10) and a reinforcement learning task (Cartpole), using datasets comprising millions of checkpoints generated from thousands of training runs with varied random initializations. Baselines will include standard gradient-based optimizers such as SGD, Adam, AdamW, Momentum, and NAGRMSprop, with hyperparameters tuned via grid search. Evaluation metrics will include performance after a single parameter update (loss, error, return), prompt alignment (R^2 between prompted and achieved metrics), and the ability to optimize non-differentiable objectives. Additional experiments will assess generalization to out-of-distribution initializations, scaling with model and dataset size, and the diversity of generated parameter solutions. Recursive prompting will be used to test iterative optimization capabilities.
cd6496bc404e18a24f634e3dded2ed1cdca03e0f.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces generative pre-training directly in neural network parameter space, leveraging a large dataset of checkpoints rather than traditional data modalities. It enables rapid, one-step optimization of unseen neural network parameters to user-specified performance levels, including for non-differentiable objectives. The method supports multimodal sampling of parameter solutions, generalizes to out-of-distribution initializations, and demonstrates favorable scaling properties. Unlike prior meta-learning and learned optimizer approaches, this method does not require unrolled optimization or reinforcement learning for training, making it more scalable and stable.

cd7427ba511c126ed0cf32ba9404b6aa53da0153.title: Stochastic Interpolants: A Unifying Framework for Flows and Diffusions
cd7427ba511c126ed0cf32ba9404b6aa53da0153.research_question: How can a unified generative modeling framework be developed that bridges arbitrary probability densities in finite time, encompassing both flow-based and diffusion-based approaches, and what are the implications for sample quality, likelihood control, and algorithmic efficiency in deterministic and stochastic generative models?
cd7427ba511c126ed0cf32ba9404b6aa53da0153.hypothesis: A general framework based on stochastic interpolants, which flexibly bridges any two probability densities via continuous-time stochastic processes with tunable noise, will enable exact finite-time transport, unify flow and diffusion models, and provide improved or comparable generative modeling performance with tractable likelihood estimation and efficient sampling.
cd7427ba511c126ed0cf32ba9404b6aa53da0153.proposed_method: The proposed method constructs a class of generative models using stochastic interpolants, defined as continuous-time stochastic processes that interpolate between two arbitrary probability densities by combining samples from both densities with a latent Gaussian variable modulated by a time-dependent function. The interpolant's time-dependent density is shown to satisfy both a first-order transport equation and a family of forward and backward Fokker-Planck equations with tunable diffusion coefficients. Drift coefficients for the associated ODEs and SDEs are characterized as unique minimizers of quadratic objective functions, which can be estimated empirically from data. The framework allows for both deterministic (ODE-based) and stochastic (SDE-based) generative models, with the flexibility to optimize the diffusion coefficient to maximize likelihood. Additionally, likelihood and cross-entropy estimators are derived for these models, and the approach is shown to recover the Schrödinger bridge in the optimal transport setting when optimizing over the interpolant.
cd7427ba511c126ed0cf32ba9404b6aa53da0153.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on synthetic datasets such as 2D and 128D Gaussian mixtures, as well as real-world image generation tasks. The proposed stochastic interpolant models will be compared against standard baselines including score-based diffusion models, normalizing flows, and other recent flow-matching and bridge-based generative models. Evaluation metrics will include sample quality (e.g., FID for images), likelihood estimates, and cross-entropy calculations. The experimental setup will explore both deterministic and stochastic variants of the framework, analyze the impact of the latent variable and diffusion coefficient, and assess the tractability and efficiency of likelihood estimation and sampling procedures.
cd7427ba511c126ed0cf32ba9404b6aa53da0153.novelty_claims: The proposed framework unifies flow-based and diffusion-based generative models by introducing a general class of stochastic interpolants capable of bridging arbitrary densities exactly in finite time. It provides a principled way to control and estimate likelihoods for both deterministic and stochastic models, introduces new quadratic objectives for learning drift and score functions, and offers unbiased incorporation of noise via latent variables and tunable diffusion. The approach generalizes and extends existing methods, recovers the Schrödinger bridge as a special case, and decouples the design of the bridging density from the sampling process, enabling flexible algorithmic implementations and theoretical insights.

cdcc2c6e465d7c3a64915d0b33deb00c794840a9.title: LICO: Large Language Models for In-Context Molecular Optimization
cdcc2c6e465d7c3a64915d0b33deb00c794840a9.research_question: Can large language models be effectively adapted for black-box optimization tasks in scientific domains, such as molecular optimization, where domain-specific data is scarce and natural language interfaces are insufficient?
cdcc2c6e465d7c3a64915d0b33deb00c794840a9.hypothesis: Equipping large language models with domain-specific embedding and prediction layers, and training them on a mixture of intrinsic and synthetic functions, will enable efficient in-context surrogate modeling and optimization in non-language scientific domains, outperforming traditional and existing LLM-based approaches.
cdcc2c6e465d7c3a64915d0b33deb00c794840a9.proposed_method: A general-purpose framework, LICO, will be developed to extend arbitrary base large language models for black-box optimization. The approach introduces three new layers to the LLM: an embedding layer for inputs (e.g., molecular fingerprints), an embedding layer for function values (scores), and a prediction layer for outputting the estimated property of unseen candidates. Training will use a semi-synthetic objective, where the model is conditioned on sequences of (input, score) pairs from a mixture of intrinsic (domain-knowledge-based) and synthetic (Gaussian Process-generated) functions, and tasked to autoregressively predict scores for new inputs. Special tokens and a task prompt in natural language will be prepended to guide the model in associating inputs and outputs, leveraging the LLM's pretraining for efficient in-context learning. After training, optimization will proceed by iteratively generating candidate molecules, predicting their scores and uncertainties, and selecting the most promising candidates for evaluation using an acquisition function that balances exploration and exploitation.
cdcc2c6e465d7c3a64915d0b33deb00c794840a9.experiment_details: Experiments will focus on molecular optimization using the Practical Molecular Optimization (PMO) benchmark, which comprises 23 diverse objective functions relevant to drug discovery. Two settings will be considered: the original PMO with a budget of 10,000 function calls, and a low-budget PMO-1K setting with 1,000 calls. The ZINC 250K dataset will provide unlabeled molecules for training, with molecular fingerprints as input features. Baselines will include state-of-the-art methods such as GeneticGFN, REINVENT, AugmentedMemory, GraphGA, GPBO, and MOLLEO. Evaluation will use the area under the curve (AUC) of the top-10 average objective value versus number of function calls, min-max scaled to [0,1], and results will be averaged over multiple random seeds. Ablation studies will assess the impact of language instructions, the ratio of synthetic to intrinsic functions, model pretraining, and LLM size.
cdcc2c6e465d7c3a64915d0b33deb00c794840a9.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a novel architecture that extends LLMs to non-language scientific domains using domain-specific embedding and prediction layers, enabling in-context surrogate modeling without reliance on natural language descriptions. The semi-synthetic training strategy, combining intrinsic and synthetic functions, is claimed to be critical for generalization to unseen objectives. The approach allows conditioning on more historical data by reducing sequence length, and demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on challenging molecular optimization tasks, outperforming both traditional surrogate models and prior LLM-based methods. The work also provides new insights into the scaling properties of LLMs for scientific optimization tasks.

cdcf3f36866ef1e16eba26d57c2324362247ba84.title: Zephyr: Direct Distillation of LM Alignment
cdcf3f36866ef1e16eba26d57c2324362247ba84.research_question: How can a smaller open-source language model be effectively aligned to user intent, achieving performance comparable to much larger models, without relying on costly human feedback or sampling-based reinforcement learning methods?
cdcf3f36866ef1e16eba26d57c2324362247ba84.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that direct distillation of alignment from larger teacher models using AI-generated preference data, combined with distilled direct preference optimization (dDPO), can produce a small language model that is highly aligned to user intent and competitive with much larger models trained with human feedback.
cdcf3f36866ef1e16eba26d57c2324362247ba84.proposed_method: The proposed methodology involves a three-stage process. First, distilled supervised fine-tuning (dSFT) is performed on a base language model (e.g., Mistral-7B) using a large, high-quality, self-instructed dataset (UltraChat), where instructions and responses are generated and refined iteratively by a teacher model. Second, AI Feedback (AIF) is collected by prompting multiple models for responses to the same inputs and using a powerful teacher model (e.g., GPT-4) to score and rank these outputs, forming preference pairs. Third, distilled direct preference optimization (dDPO) is applied, where the student model is optimized to prefer higher-ranked responses over lower-ranked ones using a static dataset of preference pairs, without any additional sampling or reinforcement learning. Training is performed using standard optimization techniques, with careful data preprocessing and hyperparameter selection to maximize alignment and generalization.
cdcf3f36866ef1e16eba26d57c2324362247ba84.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted using the Mistral-7B model as the base, with fine-tuning performed on the UltraChat dataset (approximately 200k examples after filtering) for dSFT, and the UltraFeedback dataset (64k prompts, each with four model responses scored by GPT-4) for dDPO. Training utilizes the TRL library, DeepSpeed ZeRO-3, and FlashAttention-2 on 16 A100 GPUs, with models trained for 1-3 epochs depending on the stage. Evaluation is carried out on MT-Bench (multi-turn, GPT-4 scored), AlpacaEval (single-turn, GPT-4 scored, win-rate vs. baseline), and the HuggingFace OpenLLM Leaderboard (ARC, HellaSwag, MMLU, TruthfulQA). Baselines include a range of open and proprietary models at various parameter scales (7B to 70B), including models trained with dSFT, dPPO, RLHF, and SFT. Key metrics include MT-Bench score, AlpacaEval win-rate, and performance on academic benchmarks.
cdcf3f36866ef1e16eba26d57c2324362247ba84.novelty_claims: The approach introduces a fully distillation-based alignment pipeline for small language models that eliminates the need for human annotation and sampling-based RL methods. By leveraging AI-generated preference data and direct preference optimization, the method achieves state-of-the-art results for 7B parameter chat models, surpassing even some 70B parameter models aligned with human feedback. The process is efficient, requiring only a few hours of training, and demonstrates that high-quality intent alignment can be distilled into small, open models using only AI feedback.

cdcfeb447fa8554c131c0a13a7ffcba30c0381e1.title: High Fidelity Neural Audio Compression
cdcfeb447fa8554c131c0a13a7ffcba30c0381e1.research_question: How can high-fidelity, real-time audio compression be achieved at low bitrates across diverse audio domains, while maintaining low latency and computational efficiency suitable for practical deployment?
