cdcfeb447fa8554c131c0a13a7ffcba30c0381e1.hypothesis: A neural audio codec utilizing a streaming encoder-decoder architecture with quantized latent space, trained end-to-end with a multi-scale spectrogram adversarial loss and stabilized by a novel loss balancer, will outperform traditional and neural baselines in both subjective and objective audio quality metrics at low bitrates and across multiple audio domains. Further, lightweight Transformer-based entropy coding can significantly reduce bandwidth without compromising quality or real-time performance.
cdcfeb447fa8554c131c0a13a7ffcba30c0381e1.proposed_method: A neural audio codec will be developed based on a streaming convolutional encoder-decoder architecture, with sequence modeling via LSTMs and residual connections. The encoder produces a latent representation, which is quantized using Residual Vector Quantization (RVQ) with multiple codebooks, allowing variable bitrate support. The decoder reconstructs the audio from the quantized latent space. Training will be end-to-end, combining time-domain and multi-scale frequency-domain (mel-spectrogram) reconstruction losses, a multi-scale STFT-based adversarial discriminator loss, and a commitment loss for quantization. A novel loss balancer will be introduced to stabilize training by ensuring each loss contributes a specified fraction of the overall gradient, decoupling hyperparameter selection from loss scale. Additionally, a small Transformer-based language model will be trained for entropy coding over the quantized units, enabling further bandwidth reduction while preserving real-time constraints.
cdcfeb447fa8554c131c0a13a7ffcba30c0381e1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on diverse datasets, including DNS Challenge and CommonVoice for speech, AudioSet and FSD50K for general audio, and Jamendo plus a proprietary dataset for music. Both monophonic (24 kHz) and stereophonic (48 kHz) audio will be evaluated. Baselines will include traditional codecs (Opus, EVS, MP3) and neural codecs (Lyra-v2, SoundStream). Evaluation will use both subjective (MUSHRA listening tests with at least 10 annotators per sample, following strict filtering protocols) and objective metrics (ViSQOL, SI-SNR). Ablation studies will assess the impact of discriminator architectures, streaming vs. non-streaming setups, multi-bandwidth training, and the loss balancer. Real-time performance and latency will be measured on standard CPU hardware. Training will use the Adam optimizer, multi-GPU setups, and a variety of bandwidth targets via variable codebook selection.
cdcfeb447fa8554c131c0a13a7ffcba30c0381e1.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a state-of-the-art neural audio codec that achieves real-time, high-fidelity compression at low bitrates across multiple audio domains and sampling rates. Key innovations include: (1) a simplified and efficient training regime using a single multi-scale spectrogram adversarial discriminator, (2) a novel loss balancer mechanism that stabilizes training and decouples loss weighting from scale, and (3) the integration of a lightweight Transformer-based entropy coder for further bandwidth reduction without sacrificing real-time performance. The approach is claimed to outperform both traditional and neural baselines in subjective and objective evaluations, and to support both streaming and non-streaming use cases with low latency.

cddb552f6c3464a54a02b0b64b2d1af56c086606.title: MathCoder: Seamless Code Integration in LLMs for Enhanced Mathematical Reasoning
cddb552f6c3464a54a02b0b64b2d1af56c086606.research_question: How can open-source large language models be enhanced to achieve advanced mathematical reasoning and problem-solving capabilities, particularly by integrating code execution and natural language reasoning in a seamless manner?
cddb552f6c3464a54a02b0b64b2d1af56c086606.hypothesis: Integrating interleaved natural language, code generation, and code execution feedback into the training and inference processes of open-source language models will significantly improve their mathematical reasoning abilities, enabling them to outperform existing open-source models and potentially rival closed-source solutions.
cddb552f6c3464a54a02b0b64b2d1af56c086606.proposed_method: A new framework will be developed to fine-tune open-source language models using a specially constructed instruction-following dataset, MathCodeInstruct, which contains math problems paired with solutions that interleave natural language reasoning, code, and execution results. The dataset will be created in two stages: first, by collecting GPT-4 Code Interpreter-style solutions for existing datasets (GSM8K and MATH), and second, by generating intermediate-difficulty problems through a novel problem interpolation prompting strategy, with solutions generated by an initial fine-tuned model. Special tokens will be used to demarcate natural language, code, and execution results, enabling the model to learn to produce and utilize these components during both training and inference. During inference, code blocks will be executed in real time (e.g., via Jupyter Notebooks), and the resulting outputs will be fed back into the model to guide subsequent reasoning steps.
cddb552f6c3464a54a02b0b64b2d1af56c086606.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both in-domain (GSM8K, MATH) and out-of-domain (SVAMP, Mathematics, SimulEq) datasets, covering a wide range of mathematical topics and difficulty levels. The proposed models will be based on Llama-2 and CodeLlama architectures of varying sizes (7B, 13B, 34B, 70B), and will be compared against strong open-source baselines (WizardMath, Llama-1 RFT, Galactica) as well as closed-source models (ChatGPT-3.5, GPT-4, PaLM-2, GPT-4 Code Interpreter). Evaluation will use accuracy on final answers as the primary metric, with zero-shot settings for the proposed models and few-shot or chain-of-thought prompting for baselines. Ablation studies will examine the impact of problem interpolation, code execution during inference, and loss computation strategies. Training will utilize large-scale GPU clusters, standard cross-entropy loss (excluding execution result tokens), and efficient optimization techniques (DeepSpeed, flash attention).
cddb552f6c3464a54a02b0b64b2d1af56c086606.novelty_claims: This proposal introduces the first systematic integration of natural language reasoning, code generation, and execution feedback into open-source LLMs for mathematical reasoning. It presents a novel dataset construction method combining GPT-4-style solutions and problem interpolation to bridge gaps in problem difficulty. The approach leverages special tokenization and real-time code execution during inference, enabling models to dynamically reason with both generated code and its outputs. The resulting models are expected to set new state-of-the-art performance among open-source LLMs on multiple math benchmarks, demonstrating substantial gains over prior instruction-tuned and code-augmented approaches.

cde48b24264e44355abb0e548a2cf7c70bb072b4.title: NV-Embed: Improved Techniques for Training LLMs as Generalist Embedding Models
cde48b24264e44355abb0e548a2cf7c70bb072b4.research_question: How can decoder-only large language models be improved to serve as generalist embedding models for a wide range of text embedding tasks, including retrieval, classification, clustering, and semantic similarity, while maintaining simplicity and reproducibility?
cde48b24264e44355abb0e548a2cf7c70bb072b4.hypothesis: Removing the causal attention mask during contrastive training, introducing a latent attention pooling layer, and employing a two-stage contrastive instruction-tuning approach with curated training data will significantly enhance the performance of decoder-only LLMs as general-purpose embedding models, surpassing existing bidirectional and decoder-only embedding models.
cde48b24264e44355abb0e548a2cf7c70bb072b4.proposed_method: A new model architecture will be developed based on a decoder-only LLM (e.g., Mistral-7B), augmented with a latent attention layer for pooling token representations into expressive sequence embeddings. The causal attention mask will be removed during contrastive training to enable bidirectional context modeling, enhancing representation learning. Training will follow a two-stage contrastive instruction-tuning procedure: the first stage focuses on retrieval datasets using in-batch negatives and curated hard-negative examples, while the second stage blends in non-retrieval tasks (classification, clustering, semantic similarity) and disables in-batch negatives to avoid misleading signals. Training data will be curated using positive-aware hard-negative mining, synthetic data generation via LLMs, and example-based multi-class labeling to maximize generalization and task coverage.
cde48b24264e44355abb0e548a2cf7c70bb072b4.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB), covering 56 tasks across retrieval, reranking, clustering, classification, semantic similarity, and summarization. Additional evaluation will be performed on the AIR-Benchmark to assess out-of-domain retrieval capabilities. Baselines will include leading bidirectional and decoder-only embedding models such as BGE, Stella, SFR-Embedding, GTE-Qwen2, and OpenAI's text-embed-3-large. Evaluation metrics will include nDCG@10, MAP, V-Measure, accuracy, Spearman correlation, and average scores across tasks. Ablation studies will examine the impact of pooling methods, attention mask types, training strategies, hard-negative mining, and synthetic data augmentation. Model compression techniques, including pruning, quantization, and knowledge distillation, will also be analyzed for accuracy and robustness.
cde48b24264e44355abb0e548a2cf7c70bb072b4.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a latent attention pooling layer for decoder-only LLMs, enabling more expressive sequence embeddings than mean pooling or last-token pooling. Removing the causal attention mask during contrastive training allows for bidirectional context modeling within a decoder-only architecture. The two-stage contrastive instruction-tuning method is tailored to optimize both retrieval and non-retrieval tasks, with careful handling of in-batch negatives. The training data curation pipeline leverages positive-aware hard-negative mining, synthetic data generation, and example-based multi-class labeling, facilitating reproducibility and state-of-the-art performance. The resulting model achieves and maintains the top position on the MTEB leaderboard and demonstrates superior out-of-domain retrieval performance on AIR-Benchmark.

cdf2397e3b90dab5e60ef28405187b79a68b48f1.title: A Stitch in Time Saves Nine: A Train-Time Regularizing Loss for Improved Neural Network Calibration
cdf2397e3b90dab5e60ef28405187b79a68b48f1.research_question: How can neural network models be trained to produce well-calibrated confidence estimates for all classes, including non-predicted ones, across diverse tasks and under challenging conditions such as domain shift, class imbalance, and dense prediction settings?
cdf2397e3b90dab5e60ef28405187b79a68b48f1.hypothesis: Incorporating a differentiable, multi-class calibration loss function during training, which penalizes discrepancies between predicted confidence and empirical accuracy for all classes, will yield neural network models with improved calibration across predicted and non-predicted classes, outperforming both post-hoc and existing train-time calibration methods, without sacrificing accuracy.
cdf2397e3b90dab5e60ef28405187b79a68b48f1.proposed_method: A novel auxiliary loss function, Multi-class Difference in Confidence and Accuracy (MDCA), will be developed and integrated into the training objective of deep neural networks. This loss computes, for each mini-batch, the average absolute difference between the predicted confidence and the empirical frequency for every class, ensuring calibration across the entire output vector rather than only the predicted class. The MDCA loss is fully differentiable, allowing seamless integration with standard or application-specific loss functions such as cross-entropy, label smoothing, or focal loss. A hyperparameter will be introduced to control the trade-off between the primary loss and the MDCA term, and the method will be compatible with existing architectures and training pipelines.
cdf2397e3b90dab5e60ef28405187b79a68b48f1.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, Tiny-ImageNet, Mendeley V2, PACS (for domain shift), Rotated MNIST (for synthetic domain shift), PASCAL VOC 2012 (semantic segmentation), and 20 Newsgroups (NLP). Models such as ResNet-20/32/50/56/34, Xception65 (for segmentation), and Global-Pool CNN (for NLP) will be used. The proposed method will be compared against baselines including cross-entropy, label smoothing, focal loss, Brier score, MMCE, DCA, and FLSD, as well as post-hoc calibration methods like temperature scaling and Dirichlet calibration. Evaluation metrics will include Expected Calibration Error (ECE), Static Calibration Error (SCE), class-wise ECE, and test error. Experiments will also assess robustness under domain shift, class imbalance, and dense prediction tasks, with ablation studies on batch size and hyperparameter settings.
cdf2397e3b90dab5e60ef28405187b79a68b48f1.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a differentiable, train-time calibration loss that regularizes the entire confidence vector, not just the predicted class, enabling class-wise calibration in multi-class settings. Unlike post-hoc methods, it does not require a hold-out set and leverages the full capacity of the neural network for calibration. The method is general, compatible with various loss functions and tasks, and demonstrates superior calibration performance under domain shift, class imbalance, and in dense prediction scenarios. Additionally, the approach improves calibration for minority classes and non-predicted labels, and outperforms both train-time and post-hoc state-of-the-art calibration techniques without compromising accuracy.

ce06533ecc98ba221a4db427738884c6a6af6eee.title: FreeDoM: Training-Free Energy-Guided Conditional Diffusion Model
ce06533ecc98ba221a4db427738884c6a6af6eee.research_question: How can conditional diffusion models be made more flexible, efficient, and broadly applicable across diverse conditions and data domains without requiring additional training for each new condition?
ce06533ecc98ba221a4db427738884c6a6af6eee.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that training-free conditional diffusion models guided by energy functions constructed from off-the-shelf, pre-trained, time-independent networks can achieve effective and versatile conditional generation across a wide range of conditions and data domains, matching or surpassing the controllability and quality of training-required methods.
ce06533ecc98ba221a4db427738884c6a6af6eee.proposed_method: A training-free, energy-guided conditional diffusion framework is proposed that leverages pre-trained, time-independent neural networks (such as classifiers, segmentation networks, or encoders) to construct flexible energy functions for various conditions (e.g., text, segmentation maps, sketches, landmarks, face IDs, style images). These energy functions are used to guide the sampling process of pre-trained unconditional diffusion models by inserting a gradient step of the energy function into each sampling iteration. The method approximates the time-dependent energy function for noisy intermediate samples using the output of these pre-trained networks on denoised estimates, enabling guidance without retraining any components. An efficient time-travel strategy is integrated, applying additional resampling steps selectively during the semantic stage of diffusion to improve controllability in large data domains while minimizing computational overhead. The approach supports both image and latent diffusion models, and can combine multiple conditions by summing their respective energy gradients.
ce06533ecc98ba221a4db427738884c6a6af6eee.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on multiple open-source pre-trained diffusion models, including unconditional human face diffusion models (trained on CelebA-HQ), unconditional and classifier-based ImageNet diffusion models, and latent diffusion models such as Stable Diffusion and ControlNet. The method will be evaluated on a variety of conditional generation tasks, including text-to-image, segmentation map guidance, sketch-to-image, landmark and face ID guidance, and style transfer, as well as multi-condition scenarios. Baselines for comparison will include training-required methods such as TediGAN and Universal Guidance Diffusion (UGD). Evaluation metrics will include FID for image quality, condition-matching distances (e.g., Euclidean distance in feature space), and qualitative visual inspection. The DDIM sampler with 100 steps will be used, and detailed ablations will be performed to assess the impact of the time-travel strategy and learning rate scaling.
ce06533ecc98ba221a4db427738884c6a6af6eee.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a general, training-free framework for conditional diffusion that supports a wide range of conditions and data domains without retraining or fine-tuning. The method flexibly constructs energy functions from off-the-shelf networks, enabling rapid adaptation to new conditions. The efficient time-travel strategy selectively applies additional sampling only where needed, improving controllability in large data domains with minimal computational cost. The framework is compatible with both image and latent diffusion models and can be combined with existing training-required conditional interfaces for enhanced control. Extensive experiments demonstrate superior or comparable controllability and image quality to state-of-the-art training-required and training-free baselines, with significant improvements in flexibility, simplicity, and cost.

ce435482acc0e195be8d8f002b2655b4c7b08be6.title: DivideMix: Learning with Noisy Labels as Semi-supervised Learning
ce435482acc0e195be8d8f002b2655b4c7b08be6.research_question: How can robust deep neural network training be achieved in the presence of noisy labels by leveraging techniques from semi-supervised learning?
ce435482acc0e195be8d8f002b2655b4c7b08be6.hypothesis: A framework that dynamically separates clean and noisy samples using probabilistic modeling of per-sample loss, and then applies semi-supervised learning strategies to utilize both sets, will significantly improve robustness and generalization of deep neural networks trained with noisy labels.
ce435482acc0e195be8d8f002b2655b4c7b08be6.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a dual-network framework, where two neural networks are trained simultaneously to mitigate confirmation bias. At each epoch, each network fits a two-component Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) to its per-sample loss distribution to estimate the probability of each sample being clean or noisy. Based on a threshold, the dataset is divided into a labeled set (presumed clean) and an unlabeled set (presumed noisy), and each network uses the division generated by the other network for training. During mini-batch training, an improved MixMatch semi-supervised learning strategy is applied, incorporating label co-refinement for labeled data (combining ground-truth labels and network predictions weighted by clean probability) and label co-guessing for unlabeled data (using ensemble predictions from both networks). The method also includes a confidence penalty during warmup to prevent overfitting to asymmetric noise and regularization to prevent class collapse.
ce435482acc0e195be8d8f002b2655b4c7b08be6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on benchmark datasets including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Clothing1M, and WebVision, covering both synthetic (symmetric and asymmetric) and real-world label noise scenarios. The primary architecture used will be PreAct ResNet-18 for CIFAR datasets, ResNet-50 for Clothing1M, and Inception-ResNet-v2 for WebVision, with standard data augmentation and hyperparameter settings. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art noisy label learning methods such as Meta-Learning, Joint-Optim, M-correction, Co-teaching, and MixMatch, among others. Evaluation metrics will focus on test accuracy (both best and last epoch), and ablation studies will be performed to assess the contribution of each component (co-divide, label refinement, augmentation, and ensemble inference).
ce435482acc0e195be8d8f002b2655b4c7b08be6.novelty_claims: The proposed framework uniquely integrates noisy label learning with semi-supervised learning by treating noisy samples as unlabeled data, rather than attempting to correct or reweight their labels. The co-divide strategy, where two diverged networks divide data for each other using GMM-based loss modeling, is designed to avoid confirmation bias and filter different types of errors. The method further innovates by enhancing MixMatch with label co-refinement and co-guessing, enabling robust utilization of both clean and noisy data. Extensive experiments are expected to demonstrate substantial improvements over existing methods across multiple datasets and noise regimes.

ce6633b40f8e9658709041dca5135561fdbe4714.title: DMPlug: A Plug-in Method for Solving Inverse Problems with Diffusion Models
ce6633b40f8e9658709041dca5135561fdbe4714.research_question: How can inverse problems be solved using pretrained diffusion models in a way that ensures both manifold feasibility and measurement feasibility, while also achieving robustness to unknown types and levels of measurement noise?
ce6633b40f8e9658709041dca5135561fdbe4714.hypothesis: A plug-in optimization framework that parameterizes the solution space via the reverse process of a pretrained diffusion model, and integrates early stopping based on the early-learning-then-overfitting (ELTO) phenomenon, will yield solutions that are both on the data manifold and measurement-feasible, and will be robust to unknown noise types and levels, outperforming existing interleaving approaches.
ce6633b40f8e9658709041dca5135561fdbe4714.proposed_method: The proposed method, DMPlug, treats the entire reverse diffusion process of a pretrained diffusion model as a deterministic function R(z) mapping a seed z to the data manifold. The inverse problem is reformulated by reparameterizing the solution as x = R(z) and optimizing a regularized data-fitting objective with respect to z: min_z ℓ(y, A(R(z))) + Ω(R(z)), where ℓ is the data-fitting loss and Ω is a regularizer. The optimization is performed using gradient-based solvers such as ADAM or L-BFGS, and the reverse process R is implemented using fast samplers (e.g., DDIM) with a small number of reverse steps to ensure computational efficiency. For problems with multiple unknowns (e.g., blind deblurring), multiple pretrained priors can be integrated by extending the parameterization to multiple seeds. To address robustness to unknown noise, the method leverages the ELTO property: early stopping is employed using the ES-WMV strategy, which detects the performance peak without ground truth by monitoring the running variance of intermediate reconstructions.
ce6633b40f8e9658709041dca5135561fdbe4714.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a range of linear and nonlinear inverse problems, including super-resolution, inpainting, nonlinear deblurring, blind image deblurring (BID), and BID with turbulence. Evaluation datasets include CelebA, FFHQ, and LSUN-bedroom, each resized to 256×256 and sampled with 100 images per task. Recovery quality will be measured using PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS. Baselines for comparison include state-of-the-art diffusion-based methods (DPS, ReSample, BlindDPS, ILVR), GAN-based methods (BKS-styleGAN), classical MAP-based methods, and supervised deep learning models (DeBlurGANv2, Stripformer, MPRNet, TSR-WGAN). Robustness experiments will introduce various noise types (Gaussian, impulse, shot, speckle) at different levels, and the same code and formulation will be used regardless of noise type or level. Early stopping performance will be quantified by the PSNR gap between the detected early stopping point and the true peak. Ablation studies will explore the use of different priors (e.g., LDMs, Denoising Networks), multiple priors for multi-object problems, and alternative optimizers.
ce6633b40f8e9658709041dca5135561fdbe4714.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a fundamentally different plug-in approach for solving inverse problems with pretrained diffusion models, replacing the dominant interleaving paradigm with a unified optimization over the seed space. This method ensures both manifold and measurement feasibility by design, and is the first to demonstrate robustness to unknown noise types and levels in diffusion-based inverse problem solvers, enabled by the integration of the ELTO phenomenon and an unsupervised early stopping strategy. The approach is flexible, supporting multiple priors and optimizers, and achieves significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods, especially for challenging nonlinear inverse problems.

ce806f8d32f6fb1eaa821248a1bc4fa2cd949fbb.title: Discrete Diffusion Modeling by Estimating the Ratios of the Data Distribution
ce806f8d32f6fb1eaa821248a1bc4fa2cd949fbb.research_question: Can a new probabilistic modeling technique for discrete data enable diffusion models to achieve competitive or superior performance to autoregressive models in language modeling and generation tasks, while also supporting efficient, controllable, and flexible sampling strategies?
ce806f8d32f6fb1eaa821248a1bc4fa2cd949fbb.hypothesis: A discrete diffusion modeling framework based on learning the ratios of the data distribution via a novel score entropy loss will enable diffusion models to outperform existing discrete diffusion approaches and rival autoregressive models in both likelihood-based evaluation and generation quality, while providing additional benefits such as efficient sampling and controllable generation.
ce806f8d32f6fb1eaa821248a1bc4fa2cd949fbb.proposed_method: A discrete diffusion modeling approach is proposed that parameterizes the reverse diffusion process using the ratios of the data distribution, learned through a novel score entropy loss function. The score entropy loss is designed to extend score matching principles to discrete spaces, ensuring positivity and scalability, and is implemented in a denoising variant for computational tractability. The method introduces structured transition matrices (e.g., absorbing or uniform) to efficiently model token-level transitions, and employs a transformer-based architecture with time conditioning to learn the score network. Sampling strategies leverage the learned ratios for both unconditional and conditional generation, including arbitrary prompting and infilling, and employ efficient simulation algorithms such as τ-leaping and Tweedie denoisers to trade off compute and quality.
ce806f8d32f6fb1eaa821248a1bc4fa2cd949fbb.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on standard language modeling benchmarks including Text8 (character-level), WikiText2, Penn Treebank (PTB), WikiText103, LAMBADA, and One Billion Words, using established data splits and tokenizers to ensure comparability. The proposed method will be evaluated against both autoregressive baselines (e.g., GPT-2) and existing discrete diffusion models (such as D3PM and PLAID), with model sizes matched as closely as possible. Evaluation metrics will include perplexity (for likelihood estimation), bits per character (BPC), and MAUVE score (for generation quality), as well as generative perplexity for sampled sequences. Both unconditional and conditional generation (including infilling) will be tested, and the impact of different sampling strategies and numbers of network evaluations will be systematically assessed.
ce806f8d32f6fb1eaa821248a1bc4fa2cd949fbb.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a principled and scalable score entropy loss that extends score matching to discrete spaces, enabling efficient and effective training of discrete diffusion models. By directly parameterizing probability ratios, the approach allows for highly controllable generation, including arbitrary prompting and infilling, without requiring specialized training or distribution annealing techniques. The method achieves substantial improvements over prior discrete diffusion models in both perplexity and generation quality, and is competitive with, or outperforms, autoregressive models of similar size. Additionally, the framework provides a predictable trade-off between compute and quality, supports efficient sampling with fewer network evaluations, and offers a flexible foundation for further advances in discrete generative modeling.

ce8b811df85717836d1c522a77ee69e4eab77254.title: Progressive Compression with Universally Quantized Diffusion Models
ce8b811df85717836d1c522a77ee69e4eab77254.research_question: Can diffusion probabilistic models be adapted to enable efficient, progressive data compression that supports both lossy and lossless reconstruction, while achieving high fidelity and realism across a range of bit-rates with a single model?
ce8b811df85717836d1c522a77ee69e4eab77254.hypothesis: A diffusion model with a forward process based on uniform noise (rather than Gaussian noise), combined with universal quantization and a suitably designed reverse process, can enable computationally efficient, end-to-end progressive compression that matches or exceeds the performance of existing traditional and neural codecs in terms of rate-distortion and rate-realism trade-offs.
ce8b811df85717836d1c522a77ee69e4eab77254.proposed_method: A new framework, termed Universally Quantized Diffusion Model (UQDM), will be developed for progressive data compression. The forward process will replace Gaussian noise with uniform noise channels, enabling compatibility with universal quantization (UQ) for efficient simulation and entropy coding. The reverse process will be parameterized using a learnable denoising network that predicts both the mean and per-coordinate variance, inspired by recent advances in diffusion modeling. The model will be trained end-to-end by minimizing the negative evidence lower bound (NELBO), which corresponds to the operational coding cost of progressive compression. During encoding and decoding, universal quantization will be used to transmit latent variables at each step, allowing for incremental transmission and progressive reconstruction quality improvements.
ce8b811df85717836d1c522a77ee69e4eab77254.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic (e.g., swirl toy data) and real-world image datasets, including CIFAR-10 (32x32 images) and ImageNet64 (64x64 images). The UQDM will be compared against traditional codecs (JPEG, JPEG2000, BPG) and recent neural codecs (CTC, CDC), with particular attention to progressive coding capabilities. Baselines will include both non-progressive and progressive codecs. Evaluation metrics will include bits-per-dimension (BPD) for lossless compression, peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) for fidelity, and Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and sliced Wasserstein distance for realism. The same U-net denoising architecture will be used for both UQDM and baseline diffusion models to ensure fair comparison, and experiments will assess both denoised and ancestral sampling strategies for progressive reconstruction.
ce8b811df85717836d1c522a77ee69e4eab77254.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel diffusion-based progressive codec that replaces Gaussian noise with uniform noise in the forward process, enabling the use of universal quantization for efficient and tractable entropy coding. Unlike prior diffusion-based codecs, the method supports progressive decoding with a single unconditional model across all bit-rates, eliminating the need for separate models per rate. The approach achieves competitive or superior rate-distortion and rate-realism performance compared to both classic and state-of-the-art neural codecs, including in the high bit-rate regime. Theoretical connections to variational diffusion models are established, and the method demonstrates, for the first time, the practical viability of unconditional diffusion models for progressive compression.

ce992f68e5936940881de6fe2814ed0df72dfceb.title: How Do Large Language Monkeys Get Their Power (Laws)?
ce992f68e5936940881de6fe2814ed0df72dfceb.research_question: What underlying mechanisms govern the scaling behavior of aggregate success rates in large (multimodal) language models as the number of independent inference attempts per task increases, and how can these mechanisms be mathematically characterized and predicted?
ce992f68e5936940881de6fe2814ed0df72dfceb.hypothesis: Aggregate power law scaling in the negative log of average success rates with respect to the number of inference attempts emerges from the distributional properties of single-attempt success probabilities across tasks, specifically when this distribution exhibits a heavy left tail (power-law behavior near zero).
ce992f68e5936940881de6fe2814ed0df72dfceb.proposed_method: A mathematical and empirical investigation will be conducted to analyze the scaling behavior of large language models' performance as a function of repeated independent inference attempts per task. The approach involves deriving theoretical results connecting per-task exponential scaling with aggregate power law scaling, contingent on the distribution of single-attempt success probabilities. The methodology includes fitting parametric distributions (such as scaled Beta-Binomial or Kumaraswamy distributions) to the empirical distribution of single-attempt success rates across tasks, and then simulating or analytically deriving the aggregate scaling law. Additionally, a new distributional estimator will be developed to predict the power law exponent and intercept by leveraging the fitted distribution, enabling more sample-efficient and accurate forecasting of scaling behavior.
ce992f68e5936940881de6fe2814ed0df72dfceb.experiment_details: Experiments will utilize benchmark datasets such as MATH (for mathematical problem solving) and HarmBench (for multimodal jailbreaking) to evaluate a range of large language models, including the Pythia family, Claude, Gemini, GPT-4o, and Llama38B. For each model and benchmark, multiple independent attempts per task will be sampled, and both per-task and aggregate success rates will be measured. Baseline comparisons will include standard least-squares regression estimators for power law exponents versus the proposed distributional estimator. Evaluation metrics will focus on the accuracy of predicted scaling exponents, relative error in exponent estimation, and sample efficiency under varying numbers of problems and samples per problem. Synthetic data with known ground-truth exponents will also be generated to backtest estimator performance.
ce992f68e5936940881de6fe2814ed0df72dfceb.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a rigorous theoretical framework that reconciles per-task exponential scaling with aggregate power law scaling via the distribution of single-attempt success probabilities. It provides necessary and sufficient conditions for the emergence of power law scaling in aggregate success rates, grounded in the heavy-tailed nature of the underlying distribution. A novel distributional estimator is proposed for predicting power law scaling parameters, offering significantly improved sample efficiency and accuracy compared to standard regression-based methods. The approach also explains previously observed deviations from power law scaling and enables more reliable forecasting of model performance as inference compute is scaled.

ce9f672df0da5cf91e1551513f04c2fba756eeaf.title: Prune 'n Predict: Optimizing LLM Decision-making with Conformal Prediction
ce9f672df0da5cf91e1551513f04c2fba756eeaf.research_question: How can decision-making accuracy and uncertainty quantification of large language models (LLMs) be improved in multiple-choice and tool selection tasks, particularly in high-stakes domains where incorrect outputs are risky?
ce9f672df0da5cf91e1551513f04c2fba756eeaf.hypothesis: 1. Reducing the number of distractor options in multiple-choice questions using principled uncertainty quantification will improve LLM accuracy. 2. Optimizing the score function used in conformal prediction to minimize prediction set sizes, while maintaining coverage guarantees, will further enhance the effectiveness of this approach.
ce9f672df0da5cf91e1551513f04c2fba756eeaf.proposed_method: A two-stage framework is developed for optimizing LLM decision-making. First, conformal prediction (CP) is used to generate a prediction set of answer choices for each question, ensuring with high probability (e.g., 95%) that the correct answer is retained. The original question is then revised to include only the choices in this prediction set, and the LLM is re-prompted with this reduced set—a procedure termed Conformal Revision of Questions (CROQ). To maximize the benefit of CROQ, a score function optimization framework (CP-OPT) is introduced, which learns a scoring function (using a neural network over LLM logits and penultimate layer representations) that minimizes the average size of the prediction set while preserving the desired coverage. The optimization is performed using differentiable surrogates for set size and coverage, with regularization and cross-entropy terms, and solved via stochastic gradient descent. The final threshold for the prediction set is calibrated on a separate dataset to ensure valid coverage.
ce9f672df0da5cf91e1551513f04c2fba756eeaf.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on three benchmark datasets: MMLU (covering 57 domains), TruthfulQA (focusing on truthful answering), and ToolAlpaca (tool-use instances reformatted as MCQs). Multiple instruction-tuned, open-weight LLMs are evaluated, including Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Phi-3-4k-mini-Instruct, and Gemma-2-9b-it-SimPO. The methodology is compared against standard LLM inference and conformal prediction using raw logits as scores. Evaluation metrics include average prediction set size, coverage rate (the probability the correct answer is in the set), and accuracy before and after applying CROQ. Statistical significance of improvements is assessed using paired t-tests. Calibration and test splits are used as per standard practice, and hyperparameters for the score optimization are tuned as described in the appendices.
ce9f672df0da5cf91e1551513f04c2fba756eeaf.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel two-stage decision-making framework for LLMs that leverages conformal prediction to prune distractor answers and then re-prompts the LLM, a process not previously used to improve LLM accuracy in MCQ tasks. Additionally, a new optimization framework (CP-OPT) is developed to learn score functions that minimize prediction set size while maintaining rigorous coverage guarantees, outperforming both raw logits and heuristic scores. The approach is model-agnostic, can be applied post-hoc to any LLM, and is empirically shown to yield significant accuracy improvements and more efficient uncertainty quantification.

cee75e291d693e3ee4087f1aa74f0f7e223b3b6f.title: PDE-Refiner: Achieving Accurate Long Rollouts with Neural PDE Solvers
cee75e291d693e3ee4087f1aa74f0f7e223b3b6f.research_question: How can neural PDE solvers be improved to achieve accurate, stable, and uncertainty-aware long-term rollouts for time-dependent partial differential equations across a wide range of spatial frequency spectra?
cee75e291d693e3ee4087f1aa74f0f7e223b3b6f.hypothesis: An iterative refinement process inspired by diffusion models, which explicitly denoises predictions at multiple amplitude levels, will enable neural PDE solvers to accurately model both dominant and non-dominant spatial frequency components, resulting in significantly improved long-term rollout accuracy, stability, data efficiency, and uncertainty quantification compared to existing neural, numerical, and hybrid approaches.
cee75e291d693e3ee4087f1aa74f0f7e223b3b6f.proposed_method: A novel neural PDE solver, termed PDE-Refiner, is proposed that employs an iterative multistep refinement process. At each refinement step, the model receives as input the previous timestep(s), the current prediction, and the refinement step index. Gaussian noise of decreasing variance is added to the prediction at each step, and the model is trained to denoise this input by predicting the added noise, thereby focusing on different amplitude levels of the solution spectrum. The noise schedule is exponentially decreased, ensuring that early steps capture high-amplitude (dominant) frequencies, while later steps focus on low-amplitude (non-dominant) frequencies. The approach is implemented as a diffusion model with a small number of denoising steps and a very low minimum noise variance, tailored for deterministic PDE solutions. During inference, the model autoregressively generates long rollouts by sequentially applying the refinement process at each timestep, and predictive uncertainty is quantified by sampling multiple noise realizations.
cee75e291d693e3ee4087f1aa74f0f7e223b3b6f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on challenging PDE benchmarks, including the 1D Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation and the 2D Kolmogorov flow (a variant of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations). For the 1D case, data will be generated on a mesh of 256 points with periodic boundaries, with initial conditions sampled from truncated Fourier series; training and test sets will consist of thousands of trajectories. For the 2D case, direct numerical simulation (DNS) data will be downsampled to 64x64 resolution, and standard datasets from prior work will be used. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines including U-Net and Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) architectures trained with mean squared error (MSE), alternative loss functions (e.g., Sobolev norm), hybrid neural-numerical methods, and classical numerical solvers. Evaluation metrics will include high-correlation rollout time (Pearson correlation threshold), mean squared error, and uncertainty calibration. Ablation studies will assess the impact of the number of refinement steps, noise schedules, spatial resolution, and dataset size.
cee75e291d693e3ee4087f1aa74f0f7e223b3b6f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a new class of neural PDE solvers that iteratively refine predictions using a denoising process inspired by diffusion models, enabling accurate modeling of all spatial frequency components. The method provides a principled approach to spectral data augmentation, improving data efficiency and generalization. It also enables efficient and accurate uncertainty quantification for long rollouts, a feature lacking in most existing neural PDE solvers. The approach is broadly applicable to various PDEs and is shown to outperform state-of-the-art neural, numerical, and hybrid methods in terms of rollout accuracy, stability, and data efficiency.

cef330bacf014d60daabbd489647b2006af130ca.title: Discovering Language Model Behaviors with Model-Written Evaluations
cef330bacf014d60daabbd489647b2006af130ca.research_question: How can the process of evaluating language model behaviors be scaled and diversified using automated methods, and what novel behaviors or risks can be uncovered through such large-scale, model-driven evaluation frameworks?
cef330bacf014d60daabbd489647b2006af130ca.hypothesis: Automated generation of evaluation datasets using language models, with minimal human oversight, can produce high-quality, diverse, and relevant tests for a wide range of model behaviors, enabling the discovery of novel and potentially concerning behaviors as models scale and undergo reinforcement learning from human feedback.
cef330bacf014d60daabbd489647b2006af130ca.proposed_method: A multi-stage, automated framework will be developed for generating evaluation datasets using language models (LMs). The process begins by instructing an LM to generate candidate evaluation examples conditioned on desired output classes (e.g., 'yes'/'no', multiple-choice options) and specific behavioral attributes or personas. Generated examples are then filtered using a secondary model (such as a preference model or classifier) to ensure label correctness and adherence to additional constraints (e.g., grammaticality, relevance, diversity). For more complex evaluations, iterative sampling and filtering stages will be implemented, allowing for the incorporation of human-in-the-loop feedback and the enforcement of sophisticated schema constraints (such as those found in Winogender-style tests). The resulting datasets are label-balanced and formatted for direct use in model evaluation, with prompts designed to elicit clear behavioral responses from target models.
cef330bacf014d60daabbd489647b2006af130ca.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of language models varying in size (from 810M to 52B parameters) and degree of RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) training (0 to 1000 RL steps). The generated evaluation datasets will cover 154 distinct behavioral categories, including personality traits, political and ethical views, social biases, and advanced AI risk factors. Baseline comparisons will include human-written datasets and existing evaluation benchmarks. Evaluation metrics will include label correctness (as determined by crowdworker consensus), relevance ratings, label ambiguity, and inter-rater agreement (e.g., Fleiss’s Kappa). Additional analyses will examine model performance trends, such as inverse scaling and sycophancy, across model sizes and RLHF stages. Data quality will be validated through large-scale crowdworker annotation, and interactive visualizations will be used to assess dataset diversity and coverage.
cef330bacf014d60daabbd489647b2006af130ca.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a scalable, automated framework for generating high-quality evaluation datasets using language models themselves, significantly reducing the human effort and cost associated with manual dataset creation. The method enables rapid iteration, large-scale behavioral testing, and the discovery of previously unobserved behaviors, including inverse scaling effects and sycophancy. The proposal also claims to produce some of the earliest and largest datasets for advanced AI risk evaluation, and to demonstrate that automated, model-written evaluations can match or exceed the quality of human-written benchmarks in terms of relevance and label correctness.

cf60a639add75cdea4273697269ee463024b7926.title: RichDreamer: A Generalizable Normal-Depth Diffusion Model for Detail Richness in Text-to-3D
cf60a639add75cdea4273697269ee463024b7926.research_question: How can a generalizable and robust text-to-3D generation pipeline be developed to produce highly detailed and diverse 3D content from free-form user prompts, overcoming the limitations of current methods in geometric fidelity, appearance modeling, and generalization to novel categories?
cf60a639add75cdea4273697269ee463024b7926.hypothesis: A diffusion model trained jointly on normal and depth maps derived from large-scale real-world image-text datasets, combined with an albedo diffusion model for appearance disentanglement, will provide strong geometric priors and effective appearance regularization, resulting in improved detail richness, generalization, and state-of-the-art performance in text-to-3D generation.
cf60a639add75cdea4273697269ee463024b7926.proposed_method: A novel Normal-Depth diffusion model will be developed by extending a text-to-image diffusion architecture (such as Stable Diffusion) to jointly model the distribution of surface normals and depth maps. The model will be pre-trained on the LAION-2B dataset, where normal and depth maps are estimated using state-of-the-art monocular predictors, and then fine-tuned on synthetic 3D datasets (e.g., Objaverse) with ground-truth geometry. The architecture will modify the VAE to output four channels (three for normals, one for depth) and adapt the UNet denoiser for the new input. For geometry generation, the diffusion model will guide the optimization of 3D representations (DMTet or NeRF) via Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) losses on rendered normal and depth maps. To address appearance modeling, an albedo diffusion model conditioned on depth will be introduced, regularizing the albedo component and promoting disentanglement from lighting effects. The pipeline will support both DMTet and NeRF representations, with geometry and appearance optimization performed in a decoupled, coarse-to-fine manner.
cf60a639add75cdea4273697269ee463024b7926.experiment_details: Experiments will involve pre-training the Normal-Depth diffusion model on the LAION-2B dataset, using predicted normal and depth maps, followed by fine-tuning on the Objaverse dataset with rendered ground-truth maps. Geometry generation will be evaluated by rendering uniform-albedo images and computing CLIP scores against text prompts, while appearance modeling will be assessed via CLIP scores on textured renders. Baselines for comparison will include state-of-the-art text-to-3D methods such as Fantasia3D, DreamFusion-IF, Magic3D-IF, TextMesh-IF, ProlificDreamer, MVDream, and SweetDreamer, using both DMTet and NeRF backbones. User studies will be conducted to assess perceptual quality of geometry and appearance. Ablation studies will evaluate the impact of the Normal-Depth model, pre-training on LAION, and the albedo diffusion model. Optimization details include using 24 rendered views per object, batch sizes of 512, and evaluation on over 100 prompts with 16 rendered views per object.
cf60a639add75cdea4273697269ee463024b7926.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a generalizable Normal-Depth diffusion model that jointly learns the distribution of surface normals and depth from large-scale real-world data, providing a robust geometric prior for text-to-3D generation. An albedo diffusion model is proposed to regularize appearance modeling and disentangle reflectance from illumination. The method enables improved generalization to diverse prompts and categories, achieves state-of-the-art results in both geometry and appearance, and is compatible with both DMTet and NeRF representations. The approach also demonstrates effective integration into existing text-to-3D pipelines and provides a scalable solution for high-fidelity 3D content creation from text.

cf694df964caa156ec306b45d3a3127533cb458f.title: Pick-a-Pic: An Open Dataset of User Preferences for Text-to-Image Generation
cf694df964caa156ec306b45d3a3127533cb458f.research_question: How can large-scale, publicly available datasets of real user preferences for text-to-image generation be collected and leveraged to improve the evaluation and alignment of text-to-image models with human preferences?
cf694df964caa156ec306b45d3a3127533cb458f.hypothesis: A dataset of real user preferences, collected through an open web application, will enable the training of a scoring function that predicts human preferences more accurately than existing automatic metrics and can be used to improve both model evaluation and image selection in text-to-image generation.
cf694df964caa156ec306b45d3a3127533cb458f.proposed_method: A web application will be developed to allow users to generate images from text prompts using state-of-the-art text-to-image models and to express their preferences between pairs of generated images. Data consisting of prompts, image pairs, and user preference labels (including ties) will be collected and curated, with quality control measures such as user authentication, NSFW filtering, and activity monitoring. A CLIP-based model will be fine-tuned using this dataset, employing a reward modeling objective analogous to that used in InstructGPT, where the model minimizes the KL-divergence between predicted and actual user preference distributions for image pairs. The scoring function will compute a real-valued score for each prompt-image pair using transformer-based text and image encoders, and will be trained with prompt-frequency-based loss weighting to avoid overfitting.
cf694df964caa156ec306b45d3a3127533cb458f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the collected Pick-a-Pic dataset, which contains over 500,000 examples and 35,000+ distinct prompts, with images generated by models such as Stable Diffusion 2.1, Dreamlike Photoreal 2.0, and Stable Diffusion XL. The scoring function's performance will be evaluated on held-out validation and test splits, using accuracy metrics that account for ties, and compared against baselines including CLIP-H, an aesthetics predictor, ImageReward, HPS, and human experts. Additional experiments will assess the correlation of the scoring function with human rankings on both Pick-a-Pic and MS-COCO prompts, using metrics such as Spearman correlation and Elo ratings. The impact of using the scoring function for image selection (ranking) will be tested by generating multiple images per prompt and comparing the preferred images selected by different scoring functions via human raters.
cf694df964caa156ec306b45d3a3127533cb458f.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first large-scale, open dataset of real user preferences for text-to-image generation, collected from intrinsically motivated users rather than crowdworkers. The proposed scoring function, trained on this dataset, is claimed to achieve superhuman performance in predicting user preferences and to correlate more strongly with human judgments than existing automatic metrics such as FID, CLIP-H, and aesthetics predictors. The dataset and scoring function are positioned as new standards for evaluating and improving text-to-image models, enabling more relevant and human-aligned model development and assessment.

cf719230aea682499c43580a40f8fbb6c4181d97.title: Gap-Dependent Bounds for Q-Learning using Reference-Advantage Decomposition
cf719230aea682499c43580a40f8fbb6c4181d97.research_question: Can gap-dependent regret bounds and policy switching cost bounds be established for on-policy Q-learning algorithms in finite-horizon episodic tabular Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) that utilize variance estimators and reference-advantage decomposition, and do these bounds improve upon existing worst-case and gap-dependent results?
cf719230aea682499c43580a40f8fbb6c4181d97.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by leveraging variance estimators in exploration bonuses and reference-advantage decomposition for variance reduction, Q-learning algorithms can achieve improved gap-dependent regret bounds and policy switching cost bounds that are logarithmic in the total number of steps and outperform prior Hoeffding-type and worst-case results.
cf719230aea682499c43580a40f8fbb6c4181d97.proposed_method: A novel error decomposition framework will be developed to analyze the regret and policy switching cost of two optimism-based, on-policy Q-learning algorithms—UCB-Advantage and Q-EarlySettled-Advantage—that utilize variance estimators in their exploration bonuses and reference-advantage decomposition for variance reduction. The methodology involves constructing surrogate reference functions that enable the decomposition of estimation errors into martingale components, allowing for the application of concentration inequalities. The analysis will separate errors into reference estimation, advantage estimation, and reference settling, and will relate empirical errors and bonuses to the maximum conditional variance Q* rather than loose upper bounds. The approach will also address the non-martingale issues arising from settled reference functions by introducing surrogate reference functions, ensuring that error terms can be tightly controlled throughout the learning process.
cf719230aea682499c43580a40f8fbb6c4181d97.experiment_details: Theoretical analysis will be conducted on finite-horizon episodic tabular MDPs characterized by S states, A actions, and H steps per episode. The proposed regret and policy switching cost bounds will be compared against existing baselines, including Q-learning algorithms with Hoeffding-type bonuses (e.g., UCB-Hoeffding) and previous worst-case and gap-dependent results. Evaluation metrics will include expected regret as a function of the suboptimality gap and the total number of policy switches, with explicit dependence on the minimum suboptimality gap, maximum conditional variance, and other problem parameters. Theoretical results will be validated by deriving explicit upper bounds and comparing their scaling with respect to S, A, H, T, and the suboptimality gap against prior works.
cf719230aea682499c43580a40f8fbb6c4181d97.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first gap-dependent regret analysis for Q-learning algorithms that use variance estimators and reference-advantage decomposition, as well as the first gap-dependent analysis of policy switching cost for Q-learning. The error decomposition framework and the construction of surrogate reference functions represent technical innovations that enable the control of weighted estimation error sums in the presence of variance-based bonuses. The approach yields regret and switching cost bounds that are logarithmic in the total number of steps and demonstrate improved dependence on the suboptimality gap and other problem parameters compared to previous results. These techniques are of independent interest and may be applicable to other settings such as offline Q-learning and stochastic learning with reference-advantage decompositions.

cf8fced1f446c554ca0c5608ae0a1131184212f6.title: High-Fidelity Audio Compression with Improved RVQGAN
cf8fced1f446c554ca0c5608ae0a1131184212f6.research_question: How can high-fidelity, universal neural audio compression be achieved for diverse audio domains (speech, music, environmental sounds, etc.) at extremely high compression rates, while minimizing artifacts and maximizing reconstruction quality and bitrate efficiency?
cf8fced1f446c554ca0c5608ae0a1131184212f6.hypothesis: A neural audio compression model that combines improved residual vector quantization, periodic inductive biases, advanced adversarial and reconstruction losses, and balanced data sampling can achieve significantly higher compression rates and audio fidelity across all audio domains compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.
cf8fced1f446c554ca0c5608ae0a1131184212f6.proposed_method: A universal neural audio compression model will be developed based on a fully convolutional encoder-decoder architecture, employing residual vector quantization (RVQ) to discretize audio representations. The encoder will downsample audio using strided convolutions, and the decoder will upsample using corresponding layers, with non-linear Snake activations introducing a periodic inductive bias to improve waveform generation and reduce artifacts. Codebook learning will be enhanced by projecting encodings into a low-dimensional space and applying L2 normalization, improving codebook utilization and bitrate efficiency. The model will be trained with a combination of multi-scale mel-spectrogram reconstruction losses, adversarial losses using multi-period and complex multi-scale STFT discriminators (with sub-band splitting), and codebook/commitment losses. Quantizer dropout will be applied probabilistically to enable variable bitrate support without degrading full-bandwidth quality. Balanced data sampling will ensure full-bandwidth and domain diversity during training.
cf8fced1f446c554ca0c5608ae0a1131184212f6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a large-scale dataset comprising speech (DAPS, DNS Challenge, Common Voice, VCTK), music (MUSDB, Jamendo), and environmental sounds (AudioSet), all resampled to 44.1kHz. The model will be evaluated on held-out test splits from each domain, using 3000 ten-second segments. Objective evaluation metrics will include ViSQOL (perceptual quality), mel-spectrogram distance, STFT distance, SI-SDR (scale-invariant source-to-distortion ratio), and bitrate efficiency (entropy-based). Subjective evaluation will be performed using a MUSHRA-inspired listening test with expert listeners. Comparisons will be made against state-of-the-art baselines such as EnCodec, Lyra, and Opus at various bitrates. Thorough ablation studies will be performed to assess the impact of architectural choices, loss functions, quantization strategies, and data sampling techniques.
cf8fced1f446c554ca0c5608ae0a1131184212f6.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a universal neural audio codec capable of handling all audio domains and sampling rates with a single model, achieving up to 90x compression at 8kbps with minimal quality loss. Key innovations include improved codebook learning for maximal bitrate utilization, the use of periodic Snake activations for enhanced audio fidelity, a multi-band multi-scale STFT discriminator for superior phase and high-frequency modeling, and a balanced data sampling strategy to ensure full-bandwidth reconstruction. The model demonstrates superior performance to existing codecs across objective and subjective metrics, and provides a practical, open-source foundation for future generative audio modeling.

cfb0a89ce5295ddc6ea568295611f8baf17d8c25.title: CO2: Efficient Distributed Training with Full Communication-Computation Overlap
cfb0a89ce5295ddc6ea568295611f8baf17d8c25.research_question: How can large-scale distributed training of deep neural networks be made highly efficient and scalable on clusters with limited communication bandwidth, while maintaining strong convergence and generalization performance across diverse tasks?
cfb0a89ce5295ddc6ea568295611f8baf17d8c25.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a distributed training framework employing local updating, asynchronous parameter synchronization, and specialized stabilization techniques can achieve full overlap of communication and computation, thereby enabling near-ideal scalability and robust model performance even on bandwidth-constrained clusters.
cfb0a89ce5295ddc6ea568295611f8baf17d8c25.proposed_method: A novel distributed training framework, CO2, is proposed to enable full overlap of communication and computation in data-parallel deep learning. The method employs a local updating strategy, where each worker independently performs multiple local updates without synchronization, followed by an asynchronous all-reduce operation on model parameters after every τ local steps. This asynchronous communication is decoupled from computation, allowing subsequent training steps to proceed without waiting for synchronization, thus maximizing resource utilization. To address potential instability from asynchrony, a staleness gap penalty is introduced to quantify and penalize discrepancies between parameter versions during outer momentum updates, and an outer momentum clipping mechanism is applied to prevent extreme parameter values and enhance training stability. The framework is designed to be compatible with memory-efficient optimizers such as ZeRO-series, and theoretical convergence guarantees are established under standard assumptions.
cfb0a89ce5295ddc6ea568295611f8baf17d8c25.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted across a wide range of tasks in computer vision and natural language processing, including image classification (ResNet-50, ViT, VVT on ImageNet-1K), semantic segmentation (VVT+SemanticFPN on ADE20K), 3D point cloud reconstruction (Point-MAE on ShapeNet), autoregressive language modeling (GPT-2 variants and TransNormer-LLM on OpenWebText and WikiText-103), and bidirectional language modeling (RoBERTa on Wikipedia+BookCorpus). The proposed method will be compared against baselines such as SGD, Adamw, Local-SGD/Adamw, Overlap-Local-SGD/Adamw, and SlowMo, with careful hyperparameter tuning for each. Evaluation metrics include Top-1 validation accuracy for vision tasks and validation perplexity for language tasks. Scalability will be assessed on clusters up to 128 A100 GPUs under both high-bandwidth (800Gbps RDMA) and low-bandwidth (80Gbps TCP/IP) inter-node connections, with throughput and scalability ratios reported. Ablation studies will be performed to isolate the effects of staleness gap penalty and outer momentum clipping.
cfb0a89ce5295ddc6ea568295611f8baf17d8c25.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a fully asynchronous parameter synchronization mechanism that achieves complete overlap of communication and computation, enabling 100% scalability even on clusters with severely limited bandwidth. The integration of staleness gap penalty and outer momentum clipping is novel for stabilizing asynchronous distributed training. The method is theoretically grounded with proven convergence guarantees and is compatible with established memory-efficient optimizers. Extensive empirical validation across diverse tasks and cluster configurations demonstrates superior scalability and competitive or improved convergence and generalization compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

cfb5ef050cad787196d60a55a9583107d02e58e3.title: BlackVIP: Black-Box Visual Prompting for Robust Transfer Learning
cfb5ef050cad787196d60a55a9583107d02e58e3.research_question: How can parameter-efficient transfer learning be achieved for large-scale pre-trained vision models in scenarios where model parameters are inaccessible (black-box setting) and memory resources are limited, while maintaining robust adaptation to diverse downstream tasks?
cfb5ef050cad787196d60a55a9583107d02e58e3.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that reparameterizing visual prompts as input-dependent, image-shaped perturbations generated by a lightweight neural network, and optimizing them via a zeroth-order optimization algorithm with gradient correction, will enable robust and efficient adaptation of black-box pre-trained vision models to new tasks with minimal memory and parameter requirements.
cfb5ef050cad787196d60a55a9583107d02e58e3.proposed_method: The proposed method introduces a black-box visual prompting framework, BlackVIP, which adapts large pre-trained vision models to downstream tasks without requiring access to model parameters or architecture. BlackVIP consists of two main components: (1) a Coordinator, which is a lightweight autoencoder-style neural network that generates input-dependent, image-shaped visual prompts for each input image, and (2) a Simultaneous Perturbation Stochastic Approximation with Gradient Correction (SPSA-GC) optimizer, which estimates gradients for prompt optimization using only model output queries. The Coordinator leverages a frozen, self-supervised pre-trained encoder to extract semantic features, which are combined with a learnable task-specific trigger vector and decoded into a prompt that is added to the input image. SPSA-GC efficiently updates the Coordinator's parameters by querying the black-box model with perturbed inputs and applying a momentum-based correction to the estimated gradients, improving convergence and robustness to noise.
cfb5ef050cad787196d60a55a9583107d02e58e3.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on 16 datasets covering a wide range of visual domains, including natural images, fine-grained categories, textures, satellite imagery, and synthetic datasets designed to test robustness to distribution and object location shifts (e.g., Biased MNIST and Loc-MNIST). The target model is a CLIP ViT-B/16 vision transformer, treated as a black-box API. Baselines include zero-shot CLIP, black-box adversarial reprogramming (BAR), and visual prompting (VP) with both white-box and black-box (SPSA-GC) optimization. Evaluation metrics are primarily classification accuracy, with additional analysis using t-SNE and normalized mutual information (NMI) for embedding quality, as well as memory usage, parameter count, and query efficiency. Few-shot learning settings (e.g., 16-shot) are used for training, and all methods are compared under identical resource constraints.
cfb5ef050cad787196d60a55a9583107d02e58e3.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to enable input-dependent, image-shaped visual prompting for black-box vision models using a neural prompt generator and zeroth-order optimization. BlackVIP eliminates the need for model parameter access and large memory allocation, making it suitable for real-world, resource-limited scenarios. The integration of SPSA-GC provides more accurate and stable gradient estimation than prior black-box optimization methods, leading to improved adaptation performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that BlackVIP achieves robust transfer learning across diverse tasks, outperforming existing black-box and input-space prompting baselines, and achieving high efficiency in terms of learnable parameters, memory usage, and API query cost.

cfdaf06f93d53e045006a087d8cac70ad142c631.title: Mixture of In-Context Prompters for Tabular PFNs
cfdaf06f93d53e045006a087d8cac70ad142c631.research_question: How can in-context learning methods for tabular data be scaled to handle large datasets efficiently, while maintaining or improving predictive performance compared to state-of-the-art deep learning and tree-based algorithms?
cfdaf06f93d53e045006a087d8cac70ad142c631.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that combining a scalable routing-based prompt construction mechanism with context-aware finetuning will enable transformer-based in-context learning models for tabular data to achieve state-of-the-art performance on large and diverse tabular datasets, overcoming existing scalability and alignment limitations.
cfdaf06f93d53e045006a087d8cac70ad142c631.proposed_method: A new framework, MIXTUREPFN, is developed to enable scalable and effective in-context learning for tabular data. The approach introduces a Sparse Mixture of In-Context Prompters (MICP), where test samples are routed to one of K specialized prompters, each associated with a local cluster of the training data, using a routing module initialized via K-Means clustering. Each prompter constructs a prompt by concatenating incoming test samples with a precomputed support set of bounded size, enabling efficient batch inference with fixed memory and logarithmic time complexity relative to the training set size. To address misalignment between the pretraining data prior and the inference-time data distribution, a Context-Aware Prior-Fitted Network (CAPFN) is proposed, which finetunes the pretrained model on bootstrapped samples from the downstream dataset using adapter layers. The finetuning process simulates the inference-time prompt construction mechanism, ensuring the model is well-adapted to the actual data distribution encountered during deployment.
cfdaf06f93d53e045006a087d8cac70ad142c631.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on the TABZILLA benchmark, which comprises 36 challenging tabular classification datasets with diverse properties and 19 strong baseline algorithms, including both deep learning models and gradient-boosted decision trees. The evaluation protocol uses Condorcet voting and mean rank comparisons, with statistical significance assessed via the Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test across 10 cross-validation splits. Baselines include XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, various neural networks, and prior PFN-based models. Metrics such as log-likelihood and accuracy are reported, and ablation studies are performed to assess the contribution of each component (MICP, CAPFN, KNN-prompting variants, and adapter-based finetuning). The experimental setup ensures fair comparison by considering only datasets on which all algorithms successfully run within a fixed runtime budget.
cfdaf06f93d53e045006a087d8cac70ad142c631.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the first scalable mixture-of-experts style routing mechanism for in-context learning on tabular data, reducing inference complexity from quadratic to logarithmic time and constant memory with respect to dataset size. It further innovates by aligning the pretrained model to the inference-time data distribution using a novel bootstrapped finetuning policy with adapters, enabling robust performance across dataset sizes and irregularities. The framework achieves statistically significant state-of-the-art results on a large and diverse benchmark, outperforming both deep learning and tree-based baselines, and demonstrates robustness to dataset irregularities and scalability to large datasets where previous PFN-based approaches fail.

cfec1e2e670bc5de1a0621f66eaed7abb56387f3.title: Revisiting Classifier Two-Sample Tests
cfec1e2e670bc5de1a0621f66eaed7abb56387f3.research_question: How can two-sample testing be improved to work effectively on high-dimensional data, provide interpretable results, and be applicable to tasks such as evaluating generative models and causal discovery?
cfec1e2e670bc5de1a0621f66eaed7abb56387f3.hypothesis: Classifier-based two-sample tests (C2ST), which leverage modern binary classifiers, can provide powerful, interpretable, and flexible alternatives to traditional two-sample tests, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods in various settings including high-dimensional data, generative model evaluation, and causal inference.
cfec1e2e670bc5de1a0621f66eaed7abb56387f3.proposed_method: The proposed approach constructs a two-sample test by labeling examples from one sample as positive and the other as negative, then training a binary classifier to distinguish between them. The test statistic is the classification accuracy on a held-out test set; if the samples are from the same distribution, accuracy should be near chance. The method is instantiated with different classifiers, such as neural networks (C2ST-NN) and k-nearest neighbors (C2ST-KNN), and is theoretically analyzed for its asymptotic distribution and testing power. The approach is extended to interpretability by analyzing classifier outputs and learned features, and is further adapted for evaluating generative models (e.g., GANs) by comparing real and generated samples in feature space, as well as for causal discovery by training conditional GANs in both causal directions and selecting the direction with the lower two-sample test statistic.
cfec1e2e670bc5de1a0621f66eaed7abb56387f3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real datasets. Synthetic experiments include distinguishing between Gaussian and Student-t distributions, as well as independence testing on sinusoidal data with varying noise and frequency. Real data experiments involve distinguishing between categories of NIPS conference papers and facial expressions from the Karolinska Directed Emotional Faces dataset. For generative model evaluation, DCGANs will be trained on LSUN and LFW datasets, and samples will be compared using C2ST and baseline tests (MMD, ME, SCF) in both pixel and deep feature (ResNet) spaces. For causal discovery, the method will be evaluated on the Tübingen cause-effect pairs dataset, comparing against established baselines (ANM-HSIC, IGCI, RCC). Evaluation metrics include type-I and type-II errors, test power, and interpretability of the learned features. All experiments use a significance level of α = 0.05 or 0.01, and results are averaged over multiple trials.
cfec1e2e670bc5de1a0621f66eaed7abb56387f3.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a flexible and scalable framework for two-sample testing that leverages modern binary classifiers, enabling automatic representation learning and interpretable test statistics. It provides simple null distributions and allows for direct interpretability of where and how distributions differ. The approach is shown to outperform or match state-of-the-art alternatives in both synthetic and real-world settings, and uniquely enables the evaluation of generative models with intractable likelihoods as well as novel applications in causal discovery using conditional generative models.

cffcfc8d317448d902a98f703f2ef56433c4aa0d.title: EIA: Environmental Injection Attack on Generalist Web Agents for Privacy Leakage
cffcfc8d317448d902a98f703f2ef56433c4aa0d.research_question: What are the privacy risks posed by generalist web agents when interacting with potentially compromised websites, and how can adversarial manipulations in the web environment lead to unauthorized leakage of users' personally identifiable information (PII) or entire user requests?
cffcfc8d317448d902a98f703f2ef56433c4aa0d.hypothesis: Generalist web agents are vulnerable to environmental injection attacks that can be stealthily embedded within compromised websites, leading to significant privacy leakage of users' PII and full task requests, even in the absence of prior knowledge of user tasks and without disrupting normal agent functionality.
cffcfc8d317448d902a98f703f2ef56433c4aa0d.proposed_method: A novel attack methodology, Environmental Injection Attack (EIA), will be developed to manipulate the web environment by injecting malicious but stealthy HTML elements and persuasive instructions into benign webpages. Two injection strategies will be explored: Form Injection (FI), which creates new HTML forms with embedded instructions, and Mirror Injection (MI), which replicates target elements and attaches malicious instructions via auxiliary attributes such as aria-label. The attack will leverage CSS opacity settings to render injected elements invisible or barely perceptible, and utilize JavaScript-based auto-submission mechanisms to exfiltrate sensitive information without disrupting the agent's workflow. The approach will be parameterized by injection position relative to target elements and by the visibility of injected content, enabling adaptation to diverse web environments and maximizing attack stealthiness and efficacy.
cffcfc8d317448d902a98f703f2ef56433c4aa0d.experiment_details: Experiments will target the SeeAct generalist web agent framework, powered by multiple large multimodal models (GPT-4V, Llava-1.6-Mistral-7B, Llava-1.6-Qwen-72B). The evaluation will use 177 action steps involving diverse PII categories, curated from the Mind2Web dataset, with realistic websites manually adapted from dataset snapshots. Attack performance will be measured using Attack Success Rate (ASR) for both specific PII leakage and full user request leakage, across different injection strategies, positions, and opacity settings. Baseline success rates without attack will be reported, and additional experiments will assess detectability using traditional web security tools (e.g., VirusTotal), agent functional integrity post-attack, and the effectiveness of defensive system prompts. The impact of human supervision and various defense strategies will also be analyzed.
cffcfc8d317448d902a98f703f2ef56433c4aa0d.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first comprehensive threat model and attack methodology specifically targeting privacy leakage in generalist web agents via environmental manipulations. EIA advances beyond traditional prompt injection and web attacks by adapting malicious content to the web environment, enabling the leakage of both specific PII and entire user requests—information not accessible through conventional attacks. The method demonstrates high attack success rates while maintaining agent functionality and evading detection by standard tools and defensive prompts.
