The research also provides new insights into the trade-offs between agent autonomy and security, and highlights the need for advanced, context-aware defense mechanisms for LLM-powered web agents.

d0086b86103a620a86bc918746df0aa642e2a8a3.title: Language Models as Knowledge Bases?
d0086b86103a620a86bc918746df0aa642e2a8a3.research_question: To what extent do large pretrained language models store and recall relational, factual, and commonsense knowledge, and how does their performance as knowledge bases compare to traditional symbolic knowledge bases and supervised extraction systems?
d0086b86103a620a86bc918746df0aa642e2a8a3.hypothesis: Large pretrained language models, such as BERT, encode substantial amounts of relational and factual knowledge in their parameters, enabling them to answer cloze-style queries competitively with or better than traditional knowledge base construction methods, even without fine-tuning.
d0086b86103a620a86bc918746df0aa642e2a8a3.proposed_method: A comprehensive evaluation framework will be developed to probe the factual and commonsense knowledge present in pretrained language models. The approach involves constructing the LAMA (LAnguage Model Analysis) probe, which consists of multiple knowledge sources (e.g., Wikidata, ConceptNet, SQuAD) represented as subject-relation-object triples or question-answer pairs. Each fact is converted into a manually crafted cloze-style template, which is then used to query the language model by masking the object and ranking candidate tokens. The methodology ensures fair comparison across models by restricting predictions to a unified vocabulary and focusing on single-token answers. Multiple state-of-the-art pretrained language models (e.g., BERT-base, BERT-large, ELMo, Transformer-XL) will be evaluated without any fine-tuning, and their output probabilities will be used to rank candidate answers.
d0086b86103a620a86bc918746df0aa642e2a8a3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on several curated datasets: Google-RE (manually aligned Wikipedia facts), T-REx (automatically aligned Wikidata triples), ConceptNet (commonsense triples), and SQuAD (cloze-style questions with single-token answers). For each dataset, a set of cloze templates will be defined per relation, and models will be evaluated on their ability to predict the correct object. Baselines will include frequency-based prediction, a supervised relation extraction system (with both naive and oracle entity linking), and an open-domain QA system (DrQA). Evaluation metrics will focus on mean precision at k (P@k), with special attention to P@1 and P@10, and analyses will include breakdowns by relation type (e.g., 1-to-1, N-to-M) and sensitivity to template phrasing. Additional analyses will correlate model performance with factors such as training data frequency and semantic similarity.
d0086b86103a620a86bc918746df0aa642e2a8a3.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a systematic, large-scale probing framework (LAMA) for quantifying the factual and commonsense knowledge encoded in pretrained language models. It provides the first detailed comparison of language models as unsupervised knowledge bases against both traditional symbolic extraction pipelines and supervised QA systems, using a unified evaluation methodology. The approach reveals the surprising ability of models like BERT-large to recall factual knowledge at levels competitive with or surpassing supervised extraction systems, and offers new insights into the types of knowledge most readily captured by language model pretraining. The framework is extensible and can be used to evaluate future models and multi-token answer scenarios.

d078b6e88bc4749f4eb83f289537a88b4aaf54e6.title: On the Expressivity Role of LayerNorm in Transformers' Attention
d078b6e88bc4749f4eb83f289537a88b4aaf54e6.research_question: What is the role of LayerNorm in the expressivity and functionality of the multi-head attention mechanism in Transformer models, and how do its geometric components affect model performance in language modeling and related tasks?
d078b6e88bc4749f4eb83f289537a88b4aaf54e6.hypothesis: Decomposing LayerNorm into its geometric components—projection onto a subspace orthogonal to the all-ones vector and scaling to a fixed norm—enhances the expressivity and effectiveness of the attention mechanism in Transformers by enabling equal attention across keys when needed and preventing the existence of unselectable keys.
d078b6e88bc4749f4eb83f289537a88b4aaf54e6.proposed_method: A detailed investigation will be conducted into the geometric effects of LayerNorm within Transformer architectures, specifically focusing on its decomposition into two components: (a) projection of input vectors onto a hyperplane orthogonal to the all-ones vector, and (b) scaling of these projected vectors to a fixed L2 norm. The method involves both theoretical analysis and empirical ablation studies, where variants of LayerNorm (with and without projection and scaling) are implemented in Transformer models. The impact of each component on the attention mechanism will be analyzed by examining the ability to create queries that attend equally to all keys and by assessing the presence of unselectable key vectors. Theoretical proofs will be provided to formalize the relationship between these geometric operations and the selection properties of the attention mechanism.
d078b6e88bc4749f4eb83f289537a88b4aaf54e6.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. For the synthetic task, a 'majority' function dataset will be constructed, where the model must identify the most frequent token in a sequence of categorical tokens. A single-layer Transformer encoder with a small hidden dimension (d=8) and a single attention head will be trained with and without the projection component of LayerNorm, and convergence speed, alignment of queries, and test accuracy will be measured across multiple random seeds. For language modeling, a 4-layer GPT2-based Transformer with a hidden size of 8 will be trained on the Wikipedia dataset (6.5M examples) for 50K steps, and the fraction of unselectable keys will be measured in each layer using validation sequences from SQuAD. Additionally, sentiment analysis experiments will be performed on the Stanford TreeBank dataset using a BERT-based encoder with and without LayerNorm, and the impact on token selectability and model performance will be assessed. Baselines will include models with standard LayerNorm, models with ablated projection or scaling, and comparisons will be made using metrics such as training loss, test loss, accuracy, and the fraction of unselectable keys.
d078b6e88bc4749f4eb83f289537a88b4aaf54e6.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a novel geometric interpretation of LayerNorm, decomposing it into projection and scaling components and rigorously analyzing their separate contributions to the expressivity of attention in Transformers. It is claimed that projection enables the attention mechanism to attend equally to all keys, facilitating tasks such as majority computation, while scaling eliminates the problem of unselectable keys, ensuring that any key can be selected by the attention mechanism. Theoretical proofs and empirical evidence are provided to support these claims, and the findings challenge the prevailing assumption that LayerNorm's primary role is normalization for optimization, instead highlighting its critical role in model expressivity. The work also provides practical recommendations for the placement and design of normalization layers in small Transformer models.

d07f9392045c5c44bd64ddc6fa951be40e31edbf.title: Dynamic View Synthesis as an Inverse Problem
d07f9392045c5c44bd64ddc6fa951be40e31edbf.research_question: Can high-fidelity dynamic view synthesis from monocular videos be achieved in a training-free setting, without any weight updates, auxiliary modules, or synthetic pre-training, by manipulating only the noise initialization phase of a pre-trained video diffusion model?
d07f9392045c5c44bd64ddc6fa951be40e31edbf.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that structured manipulation of the noise initialization phase in a pre-trained video diffusion model enables high-fidelity, physically consistent dynamic view synthesis from monocular videos, eliminating the need for model fine-tuning, auxiliary modules, or synthetic data.
d07f9392045c5c44bd64ddc6fa951be40e31edbf.proposed_method: The proposed method formulates dynamic view synthesis as an inverse problem and introduces a novel noise initialization mechanism for pre-trained video diffusion models. The approach centers on the K-order Recursive Noise Representation (K-RNR), which recursively refines the initial noise to align VAE-encoded latents with DDIM-inverted latents, enabling stable and faithful scene reconstruction even under zero-terminal SNR schedules. To address the synthesis of newly visible regions due to camera motion, Stochastic Latent Modulation (SLM) is introduced, which performs visibility-aware sampling and contextually permutes latent features to plausibly complete occluded regions directly in latent space. Adaptive scaling is incorporated into K-RNR to prevent scale explosion and maintain visual fidelity. Camera conditioning is achieved by lifting monocular video frames into dynamic 3D point clouds using monocular depth prediction, rendering novel views under target camera trajectories, and generating corresponding visibility masks for occlusion handling.
d07f9392045c5c44bd64ddc6fa951be40e31edbf.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using the pre-trained CogVideoX-5B-I2V model, with inference performed in a training-free manner. The evaluation dataset will comprise 1000 videos from OpenVid-1M, 50 from DAVIS, and 50 AI-generated videos, each rendered under 10 canonical camera trajectories to test robustness to diverse viewpoint shifts. Baselines for comparison include GCD, TrajectoryAttention, DaS, TrajectoryCrafter, and ReCamMaster, covering both attention-sharing and LoRA-based approaches. Evaluation metrics will include FID, FVD, CLIP-T, CLIP-F, rotation and translation errors (RotErr, TransErr), matched pixels (Mat. Pix.), FVD-V, CLIP-V, PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS, assessing visual quality, camera pose accuracy, view synchronization, and per-frame fidelity. Ablation studies will be performed to isolate the effects of K-RNR, adaptive scaling, and SLM.
d07f9392045c5c44bd64ddc6fa951be40e31edbf.novelty_claims: The proposal claims the first training-free framework for dynamic view synthesis from monocular videos by manipulating only the noise initialization phase of a pre-trained video diffusion model. Key innovations include the identification and formalization of the Zero-Terminal SNR Collapse Problem, the development of the K-order Recursive Noise Representation for stable and high-fidelity inversion under challenging noise schedules, and the introduction of Stochastic Latent Modulation for occlusion-aware scene completion in latent space. The method eliminates the need for weight updates, auxiliary modules, or synthetic pre-training, and achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple quantitative and qualitative metrics.

d081584960c42f7793502bb496e46f682e3e43b3.title: Long Context Transfer from Language to Vision
d081584960c42f7793502bb496e46f682e3e43b3.research_question: How can large multimodal models be enabled to effectively process and understand extremely long video sequences, overcoming current limitations in visual context length and dataset availability?
d081584960c42f7793502bb496e46f682e3e43b3.hypothesis: If the context length of a language model backbone is significantly extended through long-context language training and then aligned with vision modalities using short image data, the ability to handle long contexts will transfer from language to vision, allowing large multimodal models to process orders of magnitude more visual tokens without explicit long video training.
d081584960c42f7793502bb496e46f682e3e43b3.proposed_method: The proposed method involves first extending the context length of a large language model (LLM), specifically Qwen2-7B-Instruct, through continued pretraining on long text sequences up to 224K tokens using optimized memory-efficient training strategies such as FlashAttention-2, RingAttention, activation checkpointing, and parameter offload. The long-context LLM is then modality-aligned with vision by training solely on short image-text pairs, employing a unified encoding scheme called UniRes. UniRes divides images (and by extension, videos) into grids, encodes each grid with CLIP-ViT-L-336px, projects features through a multi-layer perceptron, and applies 2x2 average pooling to produce visual tokens. During inference, videos are represented as extended images, allowing the model to process thousands of frames as a single sequence of visual tokens. The approach strictly follows a train-short, test-long protocol to isolate and ablate the phenomenon of long context transfer from language to vision.
d081584960c42f7793502bb496e46f682e3e43b3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world benchmarks. The V-NIAH (Visual Needle-In-A-Haystack) benchmark, inspired by the language NIAH test, is developed to evaluate the model's ability to locate and retrieve visual information across extremely long video contexts. V-NIAH consists of hours-long videos with a single 'needle' frame and a corresponding question, sampled at 1 FPS, with evaluation based on perplexity and answer correctness. Additional evaluation will be performed on Video-MME, a comprehensive suite for video LMMs with diverse data types and qualitative annotations, as well as on MLVU and several short video and image benchmarks (e.g., NeXTQA, ActivityNetQA, InfoVQA, AI2D). Baselines include state-of-the-art LMMs such as LLaVA-NeXT-Video, Video-LLaVA, and others, with comparisons focusing on context length, number of frames processed, and performance metrics such as accuracy, consistency, and qualitative correctness. The impact of the UniRes encoding scheme versus AnyRes and the effect of denser frame sampling will also be ablated.
d081584960c42f7793502bb496e46f682e3e43b3.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the concept of long context transfer, demonstrating that extending the language model's context length enables multimodal models to process significantly longer visual sequences without explicit video training. A unified encoding scheme (UniRes) is developed to represent both images and videos consistently, facilitating effective alignment and transfer. The V-NIAH benchmark is proposed as the first synthetic evaluation suite to rigorously measure visual context length in LMMs. The resulting LongVideoAssistant (LongVA) model is claimed to achieve state-of-the-art performance among 7B-parameter models on long video understanding tasks, processing over 2000 frames or 200K visual tokens in a single pass, and outperforming baselines that rely on visual token reduction or heuristic pruning.

d082a02baab9ec980a7cea3576f3249639875759.title: Contextual Bandits with Packing and Covering Constraints: A Modular Lagrangian Approach via Regression
d082a02baab9ec980a7cea3576f3249639875759.research_question: How can contextual bandit algorithms be designed to efficiently handle both packing and covering linear resource constraints, including settings with positive and negative resource consumption, while achieving optimal regret and constraint violation guarantees in stochastic and switching environments?
d082a02baab9ec980a7cea3576f3249639875759.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a modular Lagrangian framework, leveraging regression oracles for contextual learning and primal-dual optimization, can achieve statistically optimal vanishing-regret guarantees for contextual bandits with general linear constraints, even in the presence of both packing and covering constraints and under stochastic or switching environments.
d082a02baab9ec980a7cea3576f3249639875759.proposed_method: A new modular algorithmic framework, LagrangeCBwLC, will be developed for contextual bandits with linear constraints (CBwLC). The method will combine a Lagrangian-based primal-dual approach for handling resource constraints with regression-oracle-based contextual bandit learning. Specifically, the algorithm will set up a repeated zero-sum game between a primal algorithm (selecting arms based on observed contexts) and a dual algorithm (adjusting resource multipliers), where the primal algorithm uses a regression oracle to estimate expected rewards and consumptions for context-arm pairs. The Lagrangian payoff will be carefully reweighted to accommodate both packing and covering constraints, as well as positive and negative resource consumption. The modularity of the framework will allow for plug-in primal algorithms, provided they satisfy suitable regret guarantees, and will support extensions to switching environments where the underlying data distribution changes a bounded number of times.
d082a02baab9ec980a7cea3576f3249639875759.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets that simulate contextual bandit environments with multiple arms, contexts, and resources subject to linear packing and covering constraints. The proposed algorithm will be compared against established baselines, including prior methods for contextual bandits with knapsacks (CBwK) and bandits with linear constraints (BwLC), as well as oracle-based and optimistic approaches. Evaluation metrics will include cumulative regret, maximum constraint violation, and outcome-regret (the maximum of regret and constraint violation) over a fixed time horizon. The experimental setup will also include scenarios with switching environments to test robustness and adaptability.
d082a02baab9ec980a7cea3576f3249639875759.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first regression-oracle-based algorithm for contextual bandits with general linear constraints, supporting both packing and covering constraints and allowing for negative resource consumption. It provides the first vanishing-regret guarantees for this setting beyond purely stochastic environments, including switching environments. The modular Lagrangian framework enables plug-and-play integration of any primal bandit algorithm with suitable regret bounds, and achieves statistically optimal outcome-regret under mild assumptions. The approach also sidesteps strong impossibility results in adversarial settings by introducing a weaker, fairer benchmark for comparison.

d0905b74f84e8865ab8bd362aef23b5ddab1588a.title: Policy Mirror Ascent for Efficient and Independent Learning in Mean Field Games
d0905b74f84e8865ab8bd362aef23b5ddab1588a.research_question: How can efficient and independent learning be achieved in mean-field games without relying on population generative models or centralized controllers, and what are the sample complexity guarantees for such approaches in large N-player settings?
d0905b74f84e8865ab8bd362aef23b5ddab1588a.hypothesis: Policy mirror ascent, combined with single-path temporal difference learning, enables N agents to independently and efficiently converge to an approximate Nash equilibrium in stationary mean-field games using only their own local observations, without requiring population generative models or centralized coordination.
d0905b74f84e8865ab8bd362aef23b5ddab1588a.proposed_method: A novel algorithmic framework is proposed that leverages policy mirror ascent (PMA) operators to iteratively update agent policies in stationary mean-field games. The method departs from traditional best-response-based approaches by constructing a contractive PMA operator whose fixed point corresponds to the Nash equilibrium. Value function estimation is performed using single-path temporal difference (TD) learning, where each agent learns from its own trajectory without the need for a population generative model or the ability to manipulate the population distribution. The approach supports both centralized (synchronized policy updates) and fully independent learning (each agent updates its policy using only local information), and provides explicit sample complexity guarantees. Strongly concave regularization is incorporated to ensure contraction properties and enable efficient learning.
d0905b74f84e8865ab8bd362aef23b5ddab1588a.experiment_details: Experiments are designed to evaluate the proposed algorithms in simulated stationary mean-field game environments with finite state and action spaces. The experimental setup includes both centralized and independent learning regimes, where N agents interact with the environment using only their own state, action, and reward observations. The algorithms are compared against existing baselines that require population generative models or centralized controllers. Evaluation metrics include convergence to Nash equilibrium (measured by policy distance and reward gap), sample complexity (number of environment steps required to reach a specified accuracy), and scalability with respect to the number of agents. Theoretical analysis is provided to establish sample complexity bounds of O(ε^{-2}) for centralized learning and O(ε^{-2} - a) for independent learning, with explicit consideration of population bias and mixing conditions.
d0905b74f84e8865ab8bd362aef23b5ddab1588a.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to establish finite-sample guarantees for independent learning in stationary mean-field games without requiring population generative models or centralized controllers. The approach introduces a contractive policy mirror ascent operator, enabling efficient computation of approximate Nash equilibria using only single-path simulations. Unlike prior work, the method does not require manipulation of the population distribution, and supports both centralized and fully independent learning with explicit sample complexity bounds. Theoretical contributions include new contraction and mixing analyses, as well as the extension of single-agent conditional TD learning to the multi-agent mean-field setting.

d0a1dd918288d445d3e8146a186d5256a2fc5ca3.title: DPM-Solver-v3: Improved Diffusion ODE Solver with Empirical Model Statistics
d0a1dd918288d445d3e8146a186d5256a2fc5ca3.research_question: How can the sampling efficiency and quality of diffusion probabilistic models (DPMs) be improved by optimizing the ODE solver parameterization and discretization, particularly for scenarios with limited function evaluations or large guidance scales?
d0a1dd918288d445d3e8146a186d5256a2fc5ca3.hypothesis: Introducing a novel ODE formulation for DPM sampling that leverages empirically estimated model statistics to minimize first-order discretization error, combined with advanced multistep predictor-corrector schemes and practical techniques, will yield faster and higher-quality sampling than existing training-free solvers.
d0a1dd918288d445d3e8146a186d5256a2fc5ca3.proposed_method: A new ODE solver for diffusion probabilistic models will be developed by formulating the diffusion ODE with three types of empirically estimated coefficients (empirical model statistics: linear, scaling, and bias coefficients) derived from the pretrained model. The method will minimize the first-order discretization error by solving for optimal coefficients via Monte Carlo estimation over sample trajectories, leading to a generalized parameterization that subsumes previous approaches. The solver will employ a high-order multistep predictor-corrector framework, where local Taylor expansions of the parameterized function are used for accurate transitions between time steps, and global convergence is ensured by reusing cached function values. Practical enhancements, such as pseudo-order solvers for very small step counts and half-corrector strategies for large guidance scales, will be incorporated to further improve stability and sample quality in challenging regimes.
d0a1dd918288d445d3e8146a186d5256a2fc5ca3.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on both pixel-space and latent-space DPMs, covering unconditional and conditional sampling tasks. Datasets will include CIFAR10, LSUN-Bedroom, ImageNet-256, and MS-COCO2014, with model architectures such as ScoreSDE, EDM, Guided-Diffusion, and Stable-Diffusion. The proposed method will be compared against state-of-the-art training-free ODE solvers including DPM-Solver++, UniPC, DEIS, and Heun’s method, using evaluation metrics such as Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and mean squared error (MSE) on generated samples. Experiments will systematically vary the number of function evaluations (NFE) from 5 to 20, and ablations will be performed to assess the impact of empirical model statistics and practical solver variants. All methods will be evaluated on large sample sizes (e.g., 10k–50k samples) to ensure statistical significance.
d0a1dd918288d445d3e8146a186d5256a2fc5ca3.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a novel ODE formulation for DPM sampling that leverages empirically estimated model statistics to achieve near-optimal parameterization, reducing discretization error beyond previous noise/data prediction schemes. The solver generalizes and unifies prior exponential integrator-based methods, providing a flexible high-order predictor-corrector framework with provable local and global accuracy guarantees. Practical innovations such as pseudo-order solvers and half-corrector techniques address key challenges in low-step or high-guidance regimes, enabling significant improvements in sample quality and speed, particularly at very low numbers of function evaluations.

d0a5a6a5b5540967d6f12651aebd446e4c0dc807.title: GeoChat:Grounded Large Vision-Language Model for Remote Sensing
d0a5a6a5b5540967d6f12651aebd446e4c0dc807.research_question: How can a unified large vision-language model be developed to enable multitask conversational capabilities, including visual grounding, for high-resolution remote sensing imagery, given the unique challenges and lack of domain-specific multimodal instruction data in the remote sensing domain?
d0a5a6a5b5540967d6f12651aebd446e4c0dc807.hypothesis: A large vision-language model, instruction-tuned on a comprehensive, remote sensing-specific multimodal dataset and equipped with spatial reasoning and task-specific prompts, will outperform general-domain VLMs in multitask conversational understanding and visual grounding tasks on remote sensing imagery.
d0a5a6a5b5540967d6f12651aebd446e4c0dc807.proposed_method: A novel vision-language model, GeoChat, will be developed by instruction-tuning a large language model (Vicuna-v1.5) and a visual backbone (CLIP-ViT-L/14) using a newly constructed remote sensing multimodal instruction-following dataset. The model architecture will include a high-resolution image encoder, an MLP adaptor to project visual features into the language model space, and task-specific prompt tokens to direct the model's behavior for various tasks such as image/region captioning, visual question answering, scene classification, and visually grounded conversations. Spatial location representations will be incorporated into both inputs and outputs, allowing the model to reason about and ground responses to specific regions or objects within images. Training will utilize LoRA-based fine-tuning for efficient adaptation of the language model, while keeping the visual backbone and adaptor frozen to preserve general visual-linguistic knowledge.
d0a5a6a5b5540967d6f12651aebd446e4c0dc807.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a suite of remote sensing benchmarks, including scene classification (AID, UCMerced), visual question answering (RSVQA-LRBEN, RSVQA-HRBEN, Floodnet), and visual grounding tasks using a newly proposed benchmark based on the SAMRS dataset. The training dataset will comprise approximately 318,000 instruction pairs generated from diverse remote sensing datasets covering object detection, scene classification, and VQA, with detailed attribute and relationship annotations for referring expressions and grounding. Baseline comparisons will include state-of-the-art general-domain VLMs (e.g., LLaVA-1.5, MiniGPT-v2, Qwen-VL) and remote sensing-specific models (e.g., RSGPT, Bi-Modal, SHRNet, EasyToHard). Evaluation metrics will include classification accuracy, accuracy@0.5 IoU for grounding, ROUGE and METEOR scores for captioning, and average accuracy for VQA. The experimental setup will ensure both zero-shot and supervised evaluations to assess generalization and robustness.
d0a5a6a5b5540967d6f12651aebd446e4c0dc807.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces the first unified large vision-language model for remote sensing that supports multitask conversational capabilities, including region-specific dialogue and visually grounded responses with spatial coordinates. A novel multimodal instruction-following dataset for remote sensing will be constructed, enabling instruction-tuning for diverse tasks. The approach integrates task-specific prompting and spatial location representations to enable seamless switching between image-level and region-level reasoning. The resulting model is expected to establish a new benchmark for multitask conversational VLMs in remote sensing, outperforming both general-domain and existing remote sensing-specific models, particularly in zero-shot settings.

d0a6fb583971a5b3ffc89780ff914d8beae02a9c.title: SINDER: Repairing the Singular Defects of DINOv2
d0a6fb583971a5b3ffc89780ff914d8beae02a9c.research_question: How can structural defects in patch tokens extracted by large-scale Vision Transformer models, such as DINOv2, be theoretically understood and efficiently repaired to improve performance in dense downstream tasks without requiring full model retraining or access to large-scale proprietary datasets?
d0a6fb583971a5b3ffc89780ff914d8beae02a9c.hypothesis: Singular defects in patch tokens of pre-trained Vision Transformers originate from the leading left singular vectors of the network's weights, and these defects can be mitigated by fine-tuning a small subset of parameters using a smoothness regularization on a limited dataset, thereby improving downstream dense prediction performance while preserving classification accuracy.
d0a6fb583971a5b3ffc89780ff914d8beae02a9c.proposed_method: A novel fine-tuning algorithm, SINDER, is proposed to repair singular defects in pre-trained Vision Transformer models. The method begins by theoretically identifying the direction of defective tokens in each layer via the leading left singular vector of the linearized network operations. During fine-tuning, defective tokens are detected by measuring their alignment with these singular defect directions. A spatial smoothness regularization is imposed on the defective tokens, encouraging them to resemble a weighted average of their spatial neighbors. Only a small subset of parameters—specifically, the singular values of the linear layers in up to 10 layers preceding the first defective layer—are updated, with the rest of the network frozen. This approach allows the model to be fine-tuned using only a small, unlabeled dataset, preserving the original feature quality and minimizing the risk of overfitting.
d0a6fb583971a5b3ffc89780ff914d8beae02a9c.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted by fine-tuning the DINOv2 giant model on 30,000 randomly selected images from the ImageNet-1K training set for one epoch, using SGD with momentum and a small learning rate. The effectiveness of the proposed method is evaluated on a range of downstream tasks: unsupervised segmentation (using STEGO and CAUSE) on Cityscapes, Potsdam-3, and VOC2012; supervised segmentation on ADE20k and VOC2012; depth estimation on NYUd; and classification on ImageNet-1K. Baselines include the original DINOv2 model and a DINOv2 variant retrained with register tokens. Evaluation metrics include mean Intersection over Union (mIoU), accuracy, mean average precision (mAP) for segmentation, and top-1/top-5 accuracy for classification. The experimental setup ensures that only a small fraction of parameters are updated, and all backbones are frozen during downstream evaluation.
d0a6fb583971a5b3ffc89780ff914d8beae02a9c.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretical framework linking singular defects in Vision Transformer patch tokens to the leading left singular vectors of network weights, enabling input-agnostic prediction of defect directions. A data-efficient, parameter-sparse fine-tuning method is developed that repairs these defects using only a small, unlabeled dataset, avoiding the need for full retraining or proprietary data. The approach demonstrates superior or comparable performance to retraining-based baselines in dense prediction tasks, with reduced computational and data requirements, and offers a practical solution for deploying large-scale pre-trained models in real-world scenarios.

d0b51b21e84026a369d6482d30fbfa935a98e3ac.title: Learning Perturbations to Explain Time Series Predictions
d0b51b21e84026a369d6482d30fbfa935a98e3ac.research_question: How can the interpretability of neural network predictions for multivariate time series data be improved, particularly in identifying which features at which times are most influential for a given prediction?
d0b51b21e84026a369d6482d30fbfa935a98e3ac.hypothesis: Learning both the perturbation and the mask, rather than using fixed perturbations, will yield more accurate and informative explanations for time series predictions by better capturing temporal dependencies and feature importance.
d0b51b21e84026a369d6482d30fbfa935a98e3ac.proposed_method: A novel perturbation-based explanation framework is proposed for multivariate time series predictions. The approach involves learning both a trainable mask and a data-driven perturbation operator, where the perturbation is generated by a neural network (such as a GRU or bidirectional GRU) conditioned on the input time series. The perturbation operator is defined as a convex combination of the original input and the neural network-generated perturbation, weighted by the learned mask. The objective function encourages the model to mask as much data as possible while keeping the perturbed prediction close to the original, and simultaneously regularizes the perturbation network to produce minimal, uninformative outputs unless necessary. The framework supports both preservation and deletion game objectives, but emphasizes the preservation mode for stability and interpretability.
d0b51b21e84026a369d6482d30fbfa935a98e3ac.experiment_details: Experiments are conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. The synthetic dataset is generated using a two-state Hidden Markov Model (HMM) with three features, where only two features are relevant for the label, allowing for quantitative evaluation against ground-truth saliency. The real-world dataset is MIMIC-III, consisting of multivariate ICU patient time series, with the task of predicting in-hospital mortality from 48 hours of data. Baselines include DeepLift, DynaMask, Integrated Gradients, GradientShap, FIT, Lime, Occlusion, Augmented Occlusion, and RETAIN. Evaluation metrics for the synthetic data include area under recall (AUR), area under precision (AUP), information content, and entropy of the mask. For MIMIC-III, metrics include accuracy drop, cross-entropy change, comprehensiveness, and sufficiency, measured by masking salient features and comparing prediction changes. Ablation studies are performed on regularization hyperparameters and perturbation network architectures.
d0b51b21e84026a369d6482d30fbfa935a98e3ac.novelty_claims: The proposed method is the first to jointly learn both the perturbation and the mask for explaining time series predictions, generalizing and extending prior fixed-perturbation approaches such as DynaMask. By leveraging a neural network to generate perturbations, the method adapts to complex temporal dependencies and repetitive patterns in time series data, overcoming limitations of local or fixed perturbations. Empirical results demonstrate significant improvements in explanation quality and informativeness over existing baselines, and the approach provides more stable and interpretable feature attributions for temporal models.

d0c5fea7fa6d98e026583450c01ec745673ba230.title: Torsional Diffusion for Molecular Conformer Generation
d0c5fea7fa6d98e026583450c01ec745673ba230.research_question: How can molecular conformer generation be improved by leveraging the structure of torsional degrees of freedom, and can a generative model be developed that outperforms both machine learning and traditional cheminformatics methods in terms of accuracy, speed, and chemical fidelity?
d0c5fea7fa6d98e026583450c01ec745673ba230.hypothesis: A diffusion-based generative model that operates specifically on the space of torsion angles, rather than full Euclidean coordinates, will enable more accurate, efficient, and chemically meaningful molecular conformer generation. Furthermore, such a model can provide exact likelihoods, enabling the construction of generalizable Boltzmann generators for molecular systems.
d0c5fea7fa6d98e026583450c01ec745673ba230.proposed_method: A novel generative framework is proposed that models the diffusion process over the space of molecular torsion angles, representing conformers as points on a hypertorus. The method leverages an extrinsic-to-intrinsic score model: a neural network receives a 3D point cloud of a molecular conformer (extrinsic coordinates) and predicts the score on the molecule-specific torsional space (intrinsic coordinates). The score network is designed to be SE(3)-invariant and parity-equivariant, using tensor field networks and a specialized 'pseudotorque' layer to output pseudoscalar quantities for each rotatable bond. The forward diffusion process is formulated as Brownian motion on the torus, and the reverse process is solved via a geodesic random walk, with training performed using denoising score matching. The model is further extended to enable exact likelihood computation, allowing for energy-based training and the development of torsional Boltzmann generators that can sample from the Boltzmann distribution of unseen molecules.
d0c5fea7fa6d98e026583450c01ec745673ba230.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on the GEOM-DRUGS dataset, which contains gold-standard conformer ensembles for drug-like molecules, as well as on additional datasets such as GEOM-XL and GEOM-QM9 to test scalability and generalization. The proposed method will be compared against leading baselines, including RDKit ETKDG, OMEGA (a commercial software), GeoMol, and GeoDiff (the previous state-of-the-art diffusion model). Evaluation metrics will include Average Minimum RMSD (AMR), Coverage (recall and precision), and chemical property errors (energy, dipole moment, HOMO-LUMO gap, and minimum energy) computed with xTB after relaxation. The number of denoising steps, runtime, and effective sample size for Boltzmann sampling will also be measured. A conformer matching preprocessing step will be used to align training and test distributions for conditional modeling.
d0c5fea7fa6d98e026583450c01ec745673ba230.novelty_claims: The proposed approach is the first to formulate molecular conformer generation as diffusion modeling on the hypertorus, enabling non-Euclidean diffusion on complex molecular datasets. The extrinsic-to-intrinsic score model satisfies key physical symmetries and allows for efficient, accurate prediction of torsional updates. The method achieves state-of-the-art results, outperforming both machine learning and cheminformatics baselines in accuracy and speed, and is the first to consistently surpass the established OMEGA software. Additionally, the framework enables the first generalizable Boltzmann generator based on diffusion models, capable of sampling from the Boltzmann distribution for classes of molecules rather than individual systems.

d0cd5ede6535f617e40b58517fe593b648b737b0.title: Are High-Degree Representations Really Unnecessary in Equivariant Graph Neural Networks?
d0cd5ede6535f617e40b58517fe593b648b737b0.research_question: Are higher-degree representations necessary to achieve full expressivity in equivariant Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), particularly when modeling symmetric geometric structures, and can a more expressive yet efficient equivariant GNN be developed by incorporating such representations?
d0cd5ede6535f617e40b58517fe593b648b737b0.hypothesis: Equivariant GNNs constrained to first-degree (vector) representations will suffer from expressivity degeneration on symmetric graphs, and incorporating higher-degree steerable representations will restore and enhance their expressive power without incurring prohibitive computational costs.
d0cd5ede6535f617e40b58517fe593b648b737b0.proposed_method: A new equivariant GNN framework, termed HEGNN, is proposed to enhance the expressivity of existing scalarization-based models (such as EGNN) by incorporating high-degree steerable features. The method initializes node features with spherical harmonics up to a user-specified maximal degree, thus capturing higher-order geometric information. Cross-degree invariant messages are computed by taking inner products between steerable features of the same degree from neighboring nodes, followed by scalarization and aggregation via multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs). The update rules for node features, coordinates, and steerable features are performed using these invariant messages, and the architecture avoids the computational overhead of Clebsch-Gordan tensor products by leveraging the scalarization trick for cross-degree interactions. The final node and graph-level predictions are obtained through invariant and equivariant readouts, respectively.
d0cd5ede6535f617e40b58517fe593b648b737b0.experiment_details: Experiments are designed to evaluate the expressivity and practical performance of HEGNN on both synthetic and real-world datasets. For expressivity, symmetric graphs such as k-fold rotations and regular polyhedra are used, with arbitrary 3D rotations applied to test the ability of different models to distinguish between rotated instances. Baselines include EGNN, GVP-GNN (vector-only), TFN, and MACE (high-degree steerable models), with HEGNN tested under varying maximal degrees. Evaluation is performed using classification accuracy for distinguishing symmetric structures. For physical dynamics, the N-body system (with varying numbers of particles) and the MD17 molecular dynamics dataset are used, with MSE as the primary metric and inference time also reported. Baselines for these tasks include invariant, equivariant, and high-degree models. Additional perturbation experiments introduce noise to test robustness. All experiments use standardized data splits and are run on high-performance GPUs.
d0cd5ede6535f617e40b58517fe593b648b737b0.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces a theoretically grounded analysis demonstrating that equivariant GNNs limited to first-degree representations degenerate to zero functions on symmetric graphs, thus necessitating higher-degree features for full expressivity. HEGNN is claimed to be the first model to combine the efficiency of scalarization-based message passing with the expressivity of high-degree steerable representations, avoiding the computational cost of traditional Clebsch-Gordan-based models. The method is shown to outperform both vector-only and conventional high-degree models on tasks involving both symmetric and general geometric graphs, and to provide improved robustness to symmetry-breaking perturbations.

d1006b6233f86e67ed2283c084e1dacfbdc3e71b.title: STAMP Your Content: Proving Dataset Membership via Watermarked Rephrasings
d1006b6233f86e67ed2283c084e1dacfbdc3e71b.research_question: How can dataset creators reliably prove whether their proprietary content has been included in the pretraining data of large language models, especially in settings where access to the model's training data or weights is unavailable and the content must retain its utility (e.g., as evaluation benchmarks)?
d1006b6233f86e67ed2283c084e1dacfbdc3e71b.hypothesis: Embedding distinct watermarks into multiple semantically equivalent rephrasings of a dataset, and subsequently comparing model likelihoods between public and private watermarked versions using paired statistical tests, enables statistically significant and robust detection of dataset membership in LLM pretraining corpora, even when the contaminated data constitutes a minuscule fraction of the training set.
d1006b6233f86e67ed2283c084e1dacfbdc3e71b.proposed_method: A novel framework is proposed that enables dataset owners to generate multiple rephrased versions of their content, each embedding a unique, cryptographically controlled watermark using a hash-based watermarking scheme (e.g., KGW). One watermarked version, using a public key, is released online, while several others, each with a private key, are kept confidential. To detect dataset membership, the method computes the model's perplexity (or likelihood) for both the public and private versions of each document using the target LLM. A paired t-test is then performed on the perplexity differences between public and private versions across the dataset. If the model was trained on the public version, it is expected to assign systematically lower perplexity to those samples, resulting in statistically significant test results. The approach is robustified by averaging across multiple private rephrasings per document, mitigating document-level biases, and is designed to preserve semantic meaning and utility of the original content.
d1006b6233f86e67ed2283c084e1dacfbdc3e71b.experiment_details: Experiments involve continual pretraining of the Pythia 1B language model on a corpus deliberately contaminated with watermarked versions of four standard benchmarks (TriviaQA, ARC-C, MMLU, GSM8K), each comprising less than 0.001% of the total training tokens. The method is compared against recent statistical baselines (PaCoST, LLMDI) and state-of-the-art membership inference attacks (MIAs), using p-values and AUROC as evaluation metrics. Additional experiments assess false positive rates by testing on uncontaminated models and on held-out, non-member subsets watermarked with the same keys. Utility and semantic preservation are evaluated using the lm-evaluation-harness for LLM performance on original versus watermarked benchmarks, and with the P-SP semantic similarity metric. Real-world case studies are conducted on EMNLP paper abstracts and blog posts, with both automated (GPT-4) and human evaluations to assess content quality.
d1006b6233f86e67ed2283c084e1dacfbdc3e71b.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces a practical, statistically rigorous framework for proving dataset membership in LLM pretraining data using watermarked rephrasings and paired statistical testing, without requiring access to the model's training data or weights. It leverages cryptographically controlled watermarking to enhance detection sensitivity while preserving content utility, outperforming existing contamination detection and membership inference baselines by orders of magnitude. The approach is robust to false positives, generalizes across datasets and model families, and is validated in real-world scenarios with both automatic and human evaluations. Furthermore, it systematically analyzes the trade-offs between watermarking strength, statistical power, dataset size, and pretraining corpus size.

d10e3ef7fa49e13915d0e93c0877f2f2a26cd97a.title: Robust Algorithms on Adaptive Inputs from Bounded Adversaries
d10e3ef7fa49e13915d0e93c0877f2f2a26cd97a.research_question: How can dynamic and centralized algorithms be designed to maintain robustness against adaptive inputs generated by adversaries with bounded capabilities, such as sparsity constraints or limited interaction, across a range of linear algebraic and data analysis problems?
d10e3ef7fa49e13915d0e93c0877f2f2a26cd97a.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that by leveraging advanced sketching techniques, leverage score sampling, and differential privacy mechanisms, it is possible to design algorithms that maintain robust, accurate outputs against adaptively chosen, bounded adversarial inputs, while achieving significant improvements in computational and space efficiency over naïve or non-robust approaches.
d10e3ef7fa49e13915d0e93c0877f2f2a26cd97a.proposed_method: The proposed research will develop a unified algorithmic framework for robust dynamic and centralized algorithms under bounded adversarial adaptivity. For dynamic regression, the method will utilize leverage score sampling to construct subspace embeddings of the design matrix, followed by Johnson-Lindenstrauss (JL) dimensionality reduction to efficiently maintain and update the least-squares objective as the label vector undergoes sparse, adversarial updates. The solution will dynamically maintain a sketched solution vector and efficiently update it using the sparsity of the changes, amortizing pre-processing and update costs. For centralized settings, the approach will instantiate multiple randomized data structures, using differential privacy (DP) mechanisms—such as private median aggregation and advanced composition—to hide internal randomness and ensure robustness to adaptive queries. The framework will be further tailored for specific problems, such as adaptive distance estimation and kernel density estimation, by leveraging problem-specific sampling and privacy amplification techniques to improve pre-processing time and support unlimited adaptive queries.
d10e3ef7fa49e13915d0e93c0877f2f2a26cd97a.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a variety of tasks, including dynamic least-squares regression, adaptive distance estimation, and kernel density estimation. Datasets will include synthetic and real-world data matrices for regression and point sets in high-dimensional spaces for density and distance queries. Baseline comparisons will include naïve non-robust algorithms (e.g., recomputing solutions from scratch or using standard sketching without adaptivity protection) and state-of-the-art robust algorithms where available. Evaluation metrics will include approximation accuracy (e.g., (1+ε)-approximation), update/query time, space complexity, and robustness to adversarially adaptive input sequences. The experimental setup will systematically vary adversarial strategies (e.g., different sparsity levels, number of adaptive queries) and measure empirical performance and failure rates.
d10e3ef7fa49e13915d0e93c0877f2f2a26cd97a.novelty_claims: The proposed framework introduces a unified, theoretically grounded approach for robust dynamic and centralized algorithms under bounded adversarial adaptivity, achieving near-optimal space and time complexity. Key innovations include the use of leverage score sampling and JL sketching for efficient dynamic regression under sparse adaptive updates, the application of differential privacy mechanisms to protect against adaptive adversaries in both dynamic and centralized settings, and specific algorithmic improvements for adaptive distance and kernel density estimation that surpass prior frameworks in pre-processing time and query support. The approach generalizes to a broad class of problems, providing robust solutions with provable guarantees and practical efficiency.

d1101476c85ae324142440e9f568ecbf41625be5.title: Analyzing Leakage of Personally Identifiable Information in Language Models
d1101476c85ae324142440e9f568ecbf41625be5.research_question: To what extent do language models trained on sensitive data leak personally identifiable information (PII) through black-box access, and how effective are existing privacy defenses such as PII scrubbing and differential privacy in mitigating this leakage across different domains?
d1101476c85ae324142440e9f568ecbf41625be5.hypothesis: Existing privacy defenses, including PII scrubbing and differential privacy, reduce but do not eliminate the risk of PII leakage from language models, and novel attack strategies can quantitatively reveal residual leakage even under these defenses.
d1101476c85ae324142440e9f568ecbf41625be5.proposed_method: A comprehensive empirical framework will be developed to rigorously assess PII leakage from language models via black-box extraction, reconstruction, and inference attacks. The approach will formalize three threat models—extraction (uninformed attacker), reconstruction (partially informed attacker with masked context), and inference (attacker with candidate PII knowledge)—using game-based definitions. Concrete attack algorithms will be designed to approximate the ideal leakage for each threat model, leveraging NER-based PII tagging, sampling-based generation, and constrained decoding techniques. The methodology will include the use of public masked language models to fill residual masks, top-k sampling to generate candidate PII, and perplexity-based ranking to identify likely PII completions. Additionally, a lazy estimation technique will be implemented to efficiently estimate PII extractability without exhaustive sampling.
d1101476c85ae324142440e9f568ecbf41625be5.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on three real-world datasets from distinct domains: law cases (ECHR), corporate emails (Enron), and healthcare reviews (Yelp-Health). Multiple variants of GPT-2 (Small, Medium, Large, XL) will be fine-tuned on these datasets under four privacy regimes: undefended, PII-scrubbed, differentially private (DP-SGD, ε=8), and combined scrubbing+DP. PII tagging will utilize state-of-the-art NER models (Flair and spaCy/Presidio) across 21 entity classes. Evaluation metrics will include PII extraction precision/recall, reconstruction/inference accuracy, and model utility (perplexity), with baseline leakage controlled by comparing to pre-trained models. Attacks will be compared to prior methods (e.g., TAB attack), and ablation studies will analyze the impact of model size, PII duplication, token length, and context length on leakage.
d1101476c85ae324142440e9f568ecbf41625be5.novelty_claims: The proposed research introduces a novel taxonomy and rigorous game-based definitions for three distinct PII leakage threat models, enabling fine-grained quantitative assessment of privacy risks in language models. The attack algorithms are designed to be more effective than existing approaches, achieving up to 10× higher PII extraction rates by leveraging context and public masked LMs. The study is the first to empirically measure the interplay between PII scrubbing and differential privacy in mitigating PII leakage, revealing that even with strong DP guarantees, a non-trivial fraction of PII remains vulnerable. Additional contributions include a sample-efficient estimation method for PII extractability, new insights into the relationship between membership inference and PII reconstruction, and comprehensive evaluation across multiple domains and model sizes.

d123a153790442bc7d2fe39baa7621b795b7f6d0.title: Beyond Reward: Offline Preference-guided Policy Optimization
d123a153790442bc7d2fe39baa7621b795b7f6d0.research_question: How can reinforcement learning agents be trained in fully offline settings using only human preferences between trajectories, without access to reward functions or online environment interaction?
d123a153790442bc7d2fe39baa7621b795b7f6d0.hypothesis: It is hypothesized that a one-step offline preference-guided policy optimization paradigm, which directly models both offline trajectories and human preferences in a joint embedding space, can learn effective decision policies without the need for separate reward function learning, and can outperform or match existing offline RL and preference-based RL baselines.
d123a153790442bc7d2fe39baa7621b795b7f6d0.proposed_method: A novel offline preference-guided policy optimization (OPPO) framework is proposed, which eliminates the need for separate reward function learning by jointly modeling offline trajectories and human preferences in a single step. The method introduces two key objectives: an offline hindsight information matching (HIM) objective to optimize a contextual policy π(a|s,z) and a preference modeling objective, implemented as a triplet loss, to identify the optimal context z* that aligns with human preferences. The HIM objective ensures the policy can reconstruct trajectory statistics in a learned latent space, while the preference modeling objective iteratively updates both the context encoder and the optimal context embedding to maximize alignment with preferred trajectories. The policy and context encoder are trained alternately, using transformer-based architectures (e.g., BERT for the encoder and GPT for the policy), to ensure stability and effective preference alignment in the latent space.
d123a153790442bc7d2fe39baa7621b795b7f6d0.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on continuous control tasks from the D4RL benchmark, including Hopper, Walker, and Halfcheetah environments, across various dataset types (medium, medium-replay, medium-expert). The method will be compared against several baselines: Decision Transformer (DT) with true and learned rewards, CQL and IQL with true rewards, and Behavior Cloning (BC). Evaluation metrics include normalized return scores, and ablation studies will assess the impact of the one-step paradigm, the amount of preference feedback, and the use of real human-labeled preferences (including tests on Robomimic datasets with human teleoperator data). Visualization techniques such as t-SNE will be used to analyze the learned latent space and preference alignment. Experiments will also investigate the robustness of the method to varying quantities of preference feedback and the transferability of the learned context embeddings.
d123a153790442bc7d2fe39baa7621b795b7f6d0.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces a one-step offline preference-guided policy optimization paradigm that directly optimizes the policy in a high-level embedding space, eliminating the need for separate reward function learning. The method leverages a novel combination of hindsight information matching and preference modeling objectives to jointly learn a contextual policy and optimal context embedding. This framework addresses the information bottleneck of scalar rewards and enables effective policy learning from sub-optimal or diverse offline trajectories using only binary preference signals. Empirical results demonstrate that the method achieves competitive or superior performance compared to existing offline RL and preference-based RL baselines, and the learned latent space is interpretable and robust to varying feedback quantities.

d12dbe90e767b299de644de41ae47a5733634e58.title: TWIN: TWo-stage Interest Network for Lifelong User Behavior Modeling in CTR Prediction at Kuaishou
d12dbe90e767b299de644de41ae47a5733634e58.research_question: How can lifelong user behavior modeling be improved for click-through rate (CTR) prediction in large-scale recommender systems by addressing the inconsistency between coarse and fine-grained behavior retrieval stages?
d12dbe90e767b299de644de41ae47a5733634e58.hypothesis: Aligning the target-behavior relevance metrics and network parameters between the general search and exact search stages in lifelong user behavior modeling will yield more accurate user interest extraction and improve CTR prediction performance, while maintaining computational efficiency at industrial scale.
d12dbe90e767b299de644de41ae47a5733634e58.proposed_method: A two-stage interest network (TWIN) is proposed for lifelong user behavior modeling in CTR prediction. The first stage, Consistency-Preserved General Search Unit (CP-GSU), retrieves the most relevant behaviors from tens of thousands of a user's historical actions using an attention-based relevance metric identical to that of the second stage, the Exact Search Unit (ESU). To overcome the computational bottleneck of applying target attention (TA) over long sequences, behavior features are split into item-inherent and user-item cross features. Item-inherent features are projected via pre-computing and caching, while user-item cross features are compressed into bias terms for efficient attention score calculation. The architecture ensures end-to-end parameter sharing and consistency between both stages, and is optimized for low-latency online deployment.
d12dbe90e767b299de644de41ae47a5733634e58.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on a large-scale real-world production dataset from Kuaishou, comprising 46 billion samples. The proposed TWIN method will be compared against state-of-the-art baselines including SIMHard, SIMSoft, ETA, SDIM, DIN, DIEN, and others, with sequence lengths up to 10^5 behaviors. Evaluation metrics will include offline CTR prediction accuracy and online A/B testing for business impact. Ablation studies will be performed to assess the contribution of each component, and computational efficiency will be measured, including latency and resource consumption in the online serving system.
d12dbe90e767b299de644de41ae47a5733634e58.novelty_claims: The proposal introduces the first two-stage lifelong user behavior modeling framework that achieves full consistency in both network architecture and parameterization between the general and exact search stages. It extends the applicability of target attention mechanisms from hundreds to up to 100,000 behaviors through novel feature splitting, projection, and caching strategies. The method claims significant improvements in CTR prediction accuracy and computational efficiency, enabling deployment at industrial scale with a 99.3% reduction in the main computational bottleneck, and demonstrates successful real-world impact by serving hundreds of millions of users.

d13b6f2067565943f1f2f8319f8f6c120704e75c.title: LongGenBench: Benchmarking Long-Form Generation in Long Context LLMs
d13b6f2067565943f1f2f8319f8f6c120704e75c.research_question: How can the ability of large language models (LLMs) to generate coherent, high-quality, and instruction-compliant long-form text outputs be rigorously evaluated, particularly in scenarios that require adherence to complex instructions over extended sequences?
d13b6f2067565943f1f2f8319f8f6c120704e75c.hypothesis: Current large language models, despite their proficiency in long-context input retrieval, are not yet capable of reliably generating high-quality, instruction-following long-form text outputs, especially as output length increases.
d13b6f2067565943f1f2f8319f8f6c120704e75c.proposed_method: A novel benchmark, LongGenBench, will be developed to systematically evaluate the long-form text generation capabilities of long-context LLMs. The benchmark will comprise four distinct scenarios—Diary Writing, Menu Design, Skyscraper Design, and Urban Planning—spanning both temporal and spatial domains, each with short (16K tokens) and long (32K tokens) versions. Each scenario will be instantiated with three types of instruction templates: Single Instruction (SI), Range Instruction (RI), and Periodic Instruction (PI), which require the model to inject, distribute, or repeat specific content at designated points, ranges, or intervals within the generated text. Over 20 templates per instruction type will be used to ensure diversity and control, and each task will be paired with a check set for systematic evaluation. The evaluation pipeline will automatically parse generated outputs into subtasks and assess adherence to instructions using custom metrics.
d13b6f2067565943f1f2f8319f8f6c120704e75c.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on ten long-context LLMs, including both open-source and closed-source models, with parameter sizes ranging from 7B to 72B and context windows up to 128K tokens. For each scenario, 800 examples will be generated at both 16K and 32K token lengths, using carefully curated prompts to ensure relevance and prevent off-topic responses. Inference will be performed using the vLLM system with BFloat16 precision on 8×NVIDIA A800 GPUs, employing greedy decoding. Model performance will be evaluated using three metrics: Main Task Completion (overall subtask completion rate), Specific Task Instruction Completion-1 (STIC-1, adherence to individual instruction types), and Specific Task Instruction Completion-2 (STIC-2, overall instruction adherence and execution quality). Baseline comparisons will include existing long-context benchmarks such as Ruler and Needle-in-a-Haystack, with performance trends analyzed as a function of output length and instruction complexity.
d13b6f2067565943f1f2f8319f8f6c120704e75c.novelty_claims: The proposed benchmark is the first to systematically evaluate super-long-form text generation (16K–32K+ tokens) in LLMs with a focus on instruction-following and coherence over extended outputs. LongGenBench introduces a diverse set of creative and technical scenarios, each with rigorously controlled instruction types and positions, enabling granular assessment of model capabilities. The evaluation framework includes novel metrics for instruction adherence and subtask completion, and the benchmark is designed to reveal failure modes and performance degradation unique to long-form generation. By open-sourcing the benchmark, the proposal aims to catalyze further research and improvement in long-form generation for real-world applications.

d1461167c9fef8fe3ba129c514acfd14bbe7a51e.title: Fine-Tuning Discrete Diffusion Models via Reward Optimization with Applications to DNA and Protein Design
d1461167c9fef8fe3ba129c514acfd14bbe7a51e.research_question: How can discrete diffusion models be fine-tuned to generate sequences that not only resemble natural data but also optimize specific task-related reward functions, with applications in domains such as DNA and protein design?
d1461167c9fef8fe3ba129c514acfd14bbe7a51e.hypothesis: Fine-tuning discrete diffusion models using a reward optimization framework that incorporates both a reward function and a regularization term preserving naturalness will enable the generation of sequences that are both natural-like and optimized for desired properties.
d1461167c9fef8fe3ba129c514acfd14bbe7a51e.proposed_method: A novel fine-tuning algorithm, DRAKES (Direct Reward bAcKpropagation with gumbEl Softmax trick), will be developed for discrete diffusion models. The method formulates the fine-tuning process as a reinforcement learning problem, maximizing the expected reward of generated sequences while penalizing divergence from a pretrained diffusion model via a KL regularization term. To enable end-to-end differentiability through the discrete sampling process, the Gumbel-Softmax trick will be employed, allowing gradients to flow through entire diffusion trajectories. The algorithm iteratively samples differentiable trajectories using the relaxed Gumbel-Softmax, computes the empirical objective combining reward and KL terms, and updates model parameters using stochastic gradient descent. Theoretical analysis will establish that the optimized model generates samples proportional to the product of the pretrained model likelihood and the exponentiated reward, ensuring both naturalness and high reward.
d1461167c9fef8fe3ba129c514acfd14bbe7a51e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on two primary tasks: regulatory DNA sequence design for enhancer activity and protein sequence design for stability in the inverse folding setting. For DNA design, a large-scale enhancer dataset (∼700k sequences, 200 bp each) with measured activity in human cell lines will be used, with pretrained masked discrete diffusion models and reward oracles based on the Enformer architecture. Evaluation metrics will include predicted activity, chromatin accessibility classification, 3-mer and motif correlations, and log-likelihood under the pretrained model. For protein design, the ProteinMPNN-based diffusion model will be pretrained on PDB data, and reward oracles trained on the Megascale stability dataset (∼1.8M variants). Evaluation will use predicted stability, structure RMSD (scRMSD), and overall success rate (combining stability and folding accuracy). Baselines will include guidance-based methods (classifier guidance, SMC, TDS), classifier-free guidance, pretrained models, and ablations without KL regularization. Additional validation will involve in silico physics-based simulations (e.g., PyRosetta) for protein stability.
d1461167c9fef8fe3ba129c514acfd14bbe7a51e.novelty_claims: The proposed approach introduces the first RL-based fine-tuning algorithm for discrete diffusion models that enables direct backpropagation of rewards through discrete trajectories using the Gumbel-Softmax trick. The method addresses unique algorithmic and theoretical challenges specific to discrete diffusion models formulated as continuous-time Markov chains, rather than Brownian motion as in continuous domains. Theoretical guarantees are provided, establishing a principled connection between reward maximization and classifier guidance in discrete diffusion models. Empirical results are expected to demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in generating DNA and protein sequences that are both natural-like and optimized for task-specific objectives, outperforming existing guidance-based and classifier-free approaches.

d151ced8700d84a2efe411a234a4cb2c595e8ca9.title: Language model compression with weighted low-rank factorization
d151ced8700d84a2efe411a234a4cb2c595e8ca9.research_question: How can language models be compressed more effectively to reduce parameter count while maintaining task-specific performance, particularly in resource-constrained environments?
d151ced8700d84a2efe411a234a4cb2c595e8ca9.hypothesis: Incorporating parameter importance, as measured by Fisher information, into the low-rank factorization process will enable more effective compression of language models, resulting in smaller models that better preserve task-specific accuracy compared to traditional SVD-based compression.
d151ced8700d84a2efe411a234a4cb2c595e8ca9.proposed_method: A novel compression framework will be developed that integrates Fisher information into the low-rank factorization of neural network weight matrices. The method modifies the standard singular value decomposition (SVD) objective by weighting the reconstruction error for each parameter according to its estimated Fisher information, which is computed as the accumulated squared gradient of the parameter over the training dataset. To ensure computational tractability, the importance weights are aggregated at the row level, allowing the use of standard SVD solvers on a reweighted matrix. The factorized matrices are then reconstructed by removing the Fisher information scaling, and the resulting compressed model is optionally fine-tuned on the target task to further recover or improve performance. This approach is designed to directly compress task-specific models without requiring expensive generic pre-training or knowledge distillation.
d151ced8700d84a2efe411a234a4cb2c595e8ca9.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on transformer-based language models using a variety of natural language understanding tasks from the GLUE benchmark (including CoLA, SST-2, MRPC, STS-B, QQP, MNLI, QNLI) and a named entity recognition task on the CoNLL-2003 dataset. The proposed method will be compared against standard SVD-based compression, as well as state-of-the-art compact models such as DistilBERT, MiniLM, MobileBERT, TinyBERT, and ALBERT, both with and without additional fine-tuning. Evaluation metrics will include task-specific accuracy, F1 score, correlation coefficients, and average performance across tasks. The experimental setup will ensure fair comparison by using consistent training configurations, compressing only the linear layers in transformer blocks, and reporting results without hyperparameter tuning. Further experiments will assess the method's ability to compress already compact models and its compatibility with parameter-sharing strategies.
d151ced8700d84a2efe411a234a4cb2c595e8ca9.novelty_claims: The proposed method introduces the use of Fisher information as a principled importance weighting in the low-rank factorization objective for model compression, aligning the compression process with task-specific objectives rather than mere matrix reconstruction. This approach enables direct compression of task-specific models, often outperforming or matching methods that require costly pre-training and distillation. Additionally, the method demonstrates the ability to further compress already compact models with minimal or no loss in accuracy, and is compatible with parameter-sharing architectures such as ALBERT. The framework is simple to implement, leveraging existing SVD solvers, and provides a new perspective on aligning compression objectives with downstream task performance.

d1659541a88868b0dc191afae77efd6c049f6b3e.title: Minimax Instrumental Variable Regression and $L_2$ Convergence Guarantees without Identification or Closedness
d1659541a88868b0dc191afae77efd6c049f6b3e.research_question: How can nonparametric instrumental variable (IV) regression be estimated using general function approximation methods, while avoiding the limitations of requiring uniqueness of the IV solution, reliance on pseudometric error rates, and the closedness condition on the conditional expectation operator?
d1659541a88868b0dc191afae77efd6c049f6b3e.hypothesis: A penalized minimax estimator, formulated as a constrained optimization problem and leveraging Lagrange multipliers, can achieve convergence to the least norm IV solution with strong L2 error guarantees under only the source condition and realizability assumptions, without requiring uniqueness or the closedness condition.
d1659541a88868b0dc191afae77efd6c049f6b3e.proposed_method: A new penalized minimax estimator is developed for nonparametric IV regression by reformulating the estimation problem as a constrained optimization in a Hilbert space. The objective is to find the least norm solution to the IV equation by solving a minimax problem involving a Lagrangian, where the primal variable corresponds to the regression function and the dual variable serves as a Lagrange multiplier. The empirical version of the objective replaces population expectations with empirical averages and restricts the function classes for both the regression and multiplier functions to manageable hypothesis spaces. The estimator is defined as the minimizer (over the regression function class) and maximizer (over the multiplier class) of a penalized empirical objective, which includes a regularization term on the regression function. Theoretical analysis is conducted to show that, under source condition and realizability assumptions, this minimax formulation identifies the least norm solution and admits finite-sample L2 convergence guarantees.
d1659541a88868b0dc191afae77efd6c049f6b3e.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted using both synthetic and real-world datasets relevant to instrumental variable regression, such as those used in causal inference, missing data, and asset pricing contexts. The penalized minimax estimator will be compared against existing minimax IV regression methods, including those based on projected mean squared error and those requiring the closedness condition. Baselines will include sieve- and kernel-based estimators as well as recent machine learning-based minimax estimators. Evaluation metrics will focus on L2 error rates between the estimated and true regression functions, as well as projected mean squared error where appropriate. Statistical learning theory tools, such as Rademacher complexity, will be used to analyze and bound empirical process terms, and experiments will systematically vary function class complexity and sample size to study convergence rates.
d1659541a88868b0dc191afae77efd6c049f6b3e.novelty_claims: The proposed estimator is the first to provide strong L2 convergence guarantees for nonparametric IV regression with general function approximation, without requiring uniqueness of the solution or the closedness condition. The method leverages a novel minimax formulation based on Lagrange multipliers, which allows targeting the least norm solution even in the presence of multiple solutions. The theoretical analysis demonstrates that only the source condition and realizability assumptions are needed, which are strictly weaker than the closedness condition imposed by previous works. This significantly broadens the applicability of minimax IV regression estimators and enables the integration of modern machine learning methods such as neural networks and tree-based models.

d171c920f0a0ce69396ea4b61c8f466dd1f1cb2f.title: Change is Hard: A Closer Look at Subpopulation Shift
d171c920f0a0ce69396ea4b61c8f466dd1f1cb2f.research_question: How can machine learning models be systematically evaluated and improved for robustness to subpopulation shifts across diverse real-world domains, and what are the underlying mechanisms and trade-offs that govern generalization under such shifts?
d171c920f0a0ce69396ea4b61c8f466dd1f1cb2f.hypothesis: Current state-of-the-art algorithms improve robustness only for certain types of subpopulation shifts (such as spurious correlations and class imbalance), but not for others (such as attribute imbalance and attribute generalization), and that simple model selection criteria can be surprisingly effective even without group-annotated validation data.
d171c920f0a0ce69396ea4b61c8f466dd1f1cb2f.proposed_method: A unified and generic framework will be developed to formalize and dissect subpopulation shift, decomposing it into basic types such as spurious correlations, attribute imbalance, class imbalance, and attribute generalization. This framework will enable fine-grained analysis by modeling data as generated from core features and attributes, and quantifying the degree and type of shift present in each dataset. A comprehensive benchmark will be established, evaluating 20 state-of-the-art algorithms spanning various learning strategies across 12 real-world datasets from vision, language, and healthcare domains. The methodology will include systematic evaluation of model selection strategies, attribute availability scenarios, and a broad set of evaluation metrics beyond worst-group accuracy. Additionally, the roles of representation learning and classifier learning will be decoupled and analyzed to understand their impact under different shift scenarios.
d171c920f0a0ce69396ea4b61c8f466dd1f1cb2f.experiment_details: Experiments will be conducted on 12 real-world datasets, including Waterbirds, CelebA, MetaShift, ImageNetBG, NICO++, Living17, MultiNLI, CivilComments, MIMICNotes, MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert, and CXRMultisite, covering image, text, and medical data. Over 10,000 models will be trained using 20 algorithms, such as ERM, GroupDRO, JTT, LISA, DFR, Mixup, IRM, ReSample, ReWeight, CBLoss, Focal, LDAM, BSoftmax, CRT, and others. Baselines will include vanilla empirical risk minimization and various balanced or re-weighted training approaches. Evaluation metrics will encompass worst-group accuracy, average accuracy, worst-case precision, F1-score, balanced accuracy, adjusted accuracy, and expected calibration error. Experiments will systematically vary the availability of attribute information in training and validation, and compare model selection strategies using both group-annotated and group-agnostic criteria.
